title: A Coq Formalization of a Simple Register-Allocation Pass for a Subset of C
abstract: Register allocation is a well-known compiler phase that maps an unbounded set of virtual registers to a fixed set of machine registers. Despite its apparent simplicity in textbooks, correctness proofs are subtle because they require showing that the mapping preserves the semantics of every program under every possible execution path. This paper presents a mechanically verified register-allocation pass for a fragment of C covering expressions, assignments, and structured control flow, formalized entirely in Coq 8.4. The source and target languages are given operational semantics as small-step relations, and the allocator is proved to be a forward simulation. The allocator handles linear-scan allocation over a fixed set of four general-purpose registers and a spill region in memory. A fully extracted OCaml executable is benchmarked on 37 synthetic programs and produces output equivalent to GCC's -O0 tier on all test cases. The proof comprises approximately 4 200 lines of Coq vernacular.
venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Certified Programs and Proofs (CPP 2013)

title: Intrinsically Typed Syntax for a Core Functional Language in Agda
abstract: When formalizing programming languages in a proof assistant, one common approach is to define raw syntax and then impose well-typing as a separate predicate. An alternative is to use intrinsically typed syntax, where every syntactic constructor carries a proof of its own type. This paper develops such an encoding for a core call-by-value functional language with sums, products, and general recursion, formalized in Agda 2.5. We define terms as inhabitants of a family indexed by a typing context and a type, making ill-typed terms syntactically inexpressible. A big-step evaluator is defined by structural recursion over the typed syntax and shown to be total for well-typed closed terms. The formalization amounts to 1 800 lines of Agda. We compare the proof burden with an equivalent untyped-syntax formalization of the same language and find that intrinsic typing eliminates roughly 30 % of the lemmas concerning type preservation.
venue: Journal of Logical and Algebraic Methods in Programming

title: Verified Translation Validation for Constant Folding in the Presence of Integer Overflow
abstract: Constant folding is a standard optimization that replaces constant subexpressions with their computed values at compile time. Its correctness is straightforward under mathematical integers but becomes subtle under fixed-width machine integers because intermediate expressions may overflow. This paper studies translation validation for a constant-folding pass applied to an intermediate representation with 32-bit two's-complement arithmetic, using a semantics that precisely models wrapping overflow. We define a validator that, given a source IR program and its optimized image, either certifies that the two programs are semantically equivalent or produces a counterexample trace. The validator itself is implemented and verified in Coq 8.7; the verified property is that every trace accepted by the validator implies contextual equivalence under our integer semantics. Experiments on 120 programs drawn from open benchmarks show that the validator accepts all outputs produced by a reference constant-folding implementation and rejects 100 % of artificially injected incorrect optimizations in a suite of 50 mutation tests.
venue: Formal Aspects of Computing

title: A Modular Proof of Correctness for a Stack-Based Bytecode Verifier
abstract: Bytecode verification ensures that programs loaded into a virtual machine satisfy basic safety properties such as stack balance and type safety before execution. Proofs of bytecode verifier correctness often become monolithic because the verifier's dataflow analysis and the machine's operational semantics are tightly coupled. We present a modular proof methodology in which the dataflow analysis is separated from the machine semantics by a precise abstract interpretation interface. Both components are verified independently in Coq, and the final correctness theorem is assembled by combining the two modules through the interface. The target machine is a simple stack machine with arithmetic, branching, heap allocation, and method invocation. The abstract domain tracks integer and reference types. The entire proof is 6 500 lines of Coq and was completed under Coq 8.8. The modular structure allowed us to swap the abstract domain without modifying the machine-semantics module.
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP 2018)

title: Formalizing the Hindley–Milner Type Inference Algorithm in Coq with a Completeness Proof
abstract: Hindley–Milner type inference is the basis of type systems in languages such as ML and Haskell. While the soundness of the algorithm is discussed in most textbooks, completeness—the fact that the algorithm finds the most general type—is harder to prove and is often omitted from mechanized treatments. This paper presents a full Coq formalization of Algorithm W including both soundness and completeness. The formalization uses a constraint-based presentation in which unification is factored out and verified separately as a rewriting system on finite trees. Completeness is stated as: if a term has any type in the Damas–Milner type system, then Algorithm W returns a substitution that is at least as general. The proof involves a detailed induction over the derivation structure and requires 38 auxiliary lemmas. The total proof is 5 100 lines of Coq 8.9. A worked example traces type inference for a small polymorphic program through every step of the formalization.
venue: Journal of Automated Reasoning

title: Dependent Types as a Specification Language for Numeric Algorithms: A Case Study in Matrix Multiplication
abstract: Dependent type systems can express fine-grained correctness conditions directly in types, making it possible to state and prove algorithmic properties without writing separate logical specifications. We use this capability to specify and verify a straightforward matrix-multiplication algorithm in Agda, where matrix dimensions are carried as type indices and the result type statically enforces dimensional compatibility. Beyond dimensional correctness, we encode the algebraic property that the result equals the mathematical matrix product over a commutative ring, and prove this property for both a naive cubic algorithm and a block-decomposed variant. The block-decomposed proof reuses the naive algorithm's correctness lemma recursively. We measure proof effort in terms of lines and proof steps and compare the approach with a standalone Coq proof using a separate specification predicate. The Agda intrinsic approach requires 22 % fewer lines for the equivalent theorems at the cost of more constrained type signatures.
venue: Electronic Notes in Theoretical Informatics and Computer Science

title: Towards a Certified Compiler for a Subset of Rust: Ownership Types in Coq
abstract: Rust's ownership and borrowing model prevents data races and use-after-free errors by construction but is complex enough that certified-compilation work has largely avoided it. This paper reports on an initial formalization of a small Rust-like language, called MicroRust, in Coq 8.13. MicroRust supports mutable and immutable borrows, move semantics, and basic lifetimes but excludes closures and traits. We define a type system for MicroRust that enforces single ownership and borrow exclusivity, prove type soundness via progress and preservation, and define a translation to a low-level language without ownership annotations. The translation is proved to be a backward simulation: every behavior of the target is a behavior of the source. The current formalization is 7 800 lines and covers programs up to 200 lines of MicroRust. We discuss the main obstacles encountered when encoding lifetime constraints as de Bruijn-indexed region variables.
venue: Proceedings of the European Symposium on Programming (ESOP 2022)

title: A Survey of Mechanized Semantics for Intermediate Representations Used in Production Compilers
abstract: Several production compilers—including GCC, LLVM, and CompCert—rely on one or more intermediate representations (IRs) as the backbone of their optimization pipelines. Formalizing the semantics of these IRs in a proof assistant is a prerequisite for certified compilation work, but the landscape of existing formalizations is fragmented and difficult to navigate. This chapter surveys mechanized semantics for six IRs drawn from the literature: three register-transfer-level IRs, an SSA-form IR, a continuation-passing-style IR, and a typed bytecode IR. For each, we summarize the semantic model used (operational, denotational, or axiomatic), the proof assistant and its version, the scope of verified properties, and the known limitations. We identify five recurring technical challenges and discuss how different formalizations address or sidestep them. The survey covers 24 papers published between 2005 and 2023 and is intended as an entry point for researchers beginning work on certified compilation.
venue: Advances in Formal Verification — A Handbook for Practitioners, Springer

title: Certifying Dataflow Analyses for a Static Analyzer: From Coq Proofs to Extracted C Code
abstract: Static analyzers that detect runtime errors in C programs rely on dataflow analyses whose correctness is critical but rarely formally verified. This paper describes the verification of three dataflow analyses—reaching definitions, live variables, and interval analysis—for a small but realistic subset of C, including pointers and loops. All three analyses are formalized as instances of a generic Galois-connection-based abstract interpretation framework in Coq 8.18. The generic framework is proved sound once; each analysis instantiates it and proves that its transfer functions are monotone with respect to the relevant abstract lattice. The verified analyses are then extracted to OCaml and linked against a hand-written parser to form a prototype analyzer. On a benchmark of 80 programs drawn from embedded-systems code, the extracted analyzer reproduces all 214 warnings produced by a reference implementation and raises no false negatives relative to the reference. Extraction and compilation take under 3 seconds.
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Static Analysis (SAS 2026)

title: Sensitivity Bounds for Linear Queries on Partitioned Statistical Databases
abstract: This paper examines global and local sensitivity of linear aggregate queries executed over horizontally partitioned relational databases. We derive closed-form upper bounds for query sensitivity as a function of partition cardinality and attribute domain width, and show that these bounds are tight for a class of sum and count queries. The analysis uses elementary combinatorial arguments and applies to both exact and approximate differential privacy formulations. We validate the bounds empirically using a synthetic population dataset of 500,000 records partitioned across eight virtual nodes. Results show that our bounds reduce required Laplace noise by 12–18% compared to the standard global sensitivity baseline in all tested query families. The work provides a foundation for calibrating noise mechanisms in distributed query systems without requiring full database access at a central point.
venue: Journal of Mathematical Foundations of Computing

title: Supercritical CO₂ extraction of β-caryophyllene from Origanum vulgare: effect of pressure and temperature on yield and selectivity
abstract: The extraction of β-caryophyllene from dried oregano (Origanum vulgare L.) was studied using supercritical CO₂ in a 0.5 L vessel over a pressure range of 10–40 MPa and temperatures from 40 to 80 °C. Extraction curves were recorded gravimetrically at each condition, and individual terpenoid fractions were quantified by GC-MS. Maximum β-caryophyllene yield of 3.1 mg/g dry herb was obtained at 25 MPa and 60 °C. A Sovová-type broken-and-intact cell model was fitted to the extraction curves, yielding internal and external mass-transfer coefficients in good agreement with published literature values for similar matrices. Selectivity relative to thymol and carvacrol decreased with increasing pressure, consistent with reduced CO₂ density dependence at high pressure. The results provide a working operating window for sesquiterpene-selective extraction without the need for additional fractionation steps. A simple single-parameter correction to the broken-and-intact cell model improved the fit at early extraction times (R² = 0.985).
venue: Journal of Supercritical Fluids and Process Engineering

title: Равнотежа течност–течност у системима CO₂ + етанол + монотерпени: мерења и моделовање Пенг-Робинсоновом ЈС
abstract: Фазна равнотежа у бинарним и троструким системима CO₂ + етанол и CO₂ + лимонен + етанол испитана је у опсегу притисака 8–30 МПа на температурама 40, 50 и 60 °С у статичкој ћелији са визуелним прозором. Добијени подаци за притиске растварања пружили су основу за прилагођавање бинарних параметара интеракције у Пенг-Робинсоновој једначини стања са Van der Waals-овим правилима мешања. Средња апсолутна релативна одступања за притисак у бинарним системима износила су 2,4 и 3,1% за CO₂ + лимонен и CO₂ + етанол, редом. У троструком систему са 5 масених % етанола запажено је значајно повећање растворљивости лимонена у поређењу са бинарним системом, нарочито на притисцима испод 15 МПа. Добијени параметри интеракције унети су у базу података за накнадна инжењерска прорачуна и могу се директно применити у дизајну процеса са ко-растварачима на бази алкохола.

title: Co-solvent effects of propylene glycol on the supercritical CO₂ solubility of selected diterpene acids from Rosmarinus officinalis
abstract: The influence of propylene glycol (PG) as a co-solvent on the solubility of carnosic acid and ursolic acid in supercritical CO₂ was investigated at 15–35 MPa and 50–70 °C using a dynamic flow apparatus. PG concentrations of 1, 3, and 5 mol% were tested. At 20 MPa and 60 °C, addition of 3 mol% PG increased the apparent solubility of carnosic acid by a factor of 4.8 compared to pure CO₂, while ursolic acid showed a more moderate enhancement factor of 2.1. The Mendez-Santiago–Teja model was applied to represent the solubility data with satisfactory accuracy (AARD < 7%). Infrared spectra of fractions collected downstream confirmed that PG did not cause chemical alteration of the target compounds. The practical implication is that relatively modest PG additions can shift the operating pressure for economically relevant yields of diterpene acids downward by approximately 8 MPa.
venue: Separation and Purification Technology Letters

title: Optimisation of supercritical CO₂ extraction of thymol-rich fractions from Thymus serpyllum using response surface methodology
abstract: A Box-Behnken experimental design with three factors — pressure (12–28 MPa), temperature (40–70 °C), and CO₂ flow rate (2–8 g/min) — was applied to optimise the recovery of thymol from dried wild thyme (Thymus serpyllum). Responses recorded were thymol mass yield and purity relative to total extract mass. Quadratic response surface models for both responses achieved R² values of 0.971 and 0.944. The desirability-function optimisation indicated 22 MPa, 55 °C, and 5 g/min as the preferred combination, giving a predicted thymol yield of 8.4 mg/g dry material with 61% purity. Five validation experiments at these conditions yielded a mean thymol content of 8.1 ± 0.3 mg/g, confirming the model. Gas chromatography with flame ionisation detection (GC-FID) was used throughout. The study also identified a saddle region in the pressure–temperature response surface where phenolic monoterpene and carvacrol co-extraction increased substantially.

title: Terpenoid fingerprinting of supercritical CO₂ extracts from ten Lamiaceae species cultivated in Vojvodina
abstract: Supercritical CO₂ extracts of ten species from the Lamiaceae family grown under uniform agronomic conditions in Vojvodina were prepared at a standard condition of 18 MPa and 50 °C and analysed by GC-MS and HPLC-DAD. The study aimed to establish baseline terpenoid profiles for species including lavender, sage, basil, marjoram, and lemon balm, among others. Monoterpene hydrocarbons dominated extracts of Salvia officinalis and Lavandula angustifolia, while oxygenated sesquiterpenes were more abundant in Melissa officinalis and Ocimum basilicum. Principal component analysis of 38 identified compounds separated the ten species into three clusters, broadly corresponding to the chemical diversity reported in hydrodistillation-based literature. Systematic differences between supercritical and steam-distilled composition are discussed with reference to the polarity window accessible to neat CO₂ at the test conditions. The dataset provides reference values for future optimisation studies targeting individual compounds.

title: Solubility of α-bisabolol in supercritical CO₂: experimental data and correlation with four equations of state
abstract: The solubility of α-bisabolol, a sesquiterpene alcohol of pharmaceutical interest, in supercritical CO₂ was measured over the pressure range 10–40 MPa at 40, 50, and 60 °C using a gravimetric-dynamic method. Solubility values ranged from 0.18 × 10⁻³ to 6.74 × 10⁻³ mole fraction, showing a strong pressure dependence and a crossover pressure near 17 MPa where the temperature dependence reverses sign. Four equations of state — Peng-Robinson, Soave-Redlich-Kwong, PC-SAFT, and Patel-Teja — were fitted to the data. PC-SAFT with one binary interaction parameter per isotherm gave the lowest overall AARD of 3.8%, versus 6.2–9.1% for the cubic equations. The crossover pressure was reproduced accurately by PC-SAFT. Physical property estimates for α-bisabolol required for the EOS fitting were obtained using group contribution methods, and their uncertainty was propagated to the fitted parameters. Recommendations for process-scale solubility estimation are given.

title: Pressure-fractionated supercritical CO₂ extraction of sage (Salvia officinalis): mass balance and terpenoid distribution across three pressure stages
abstract: A three-stage pressure-reduction fractionation system was used to separate supercritical CO₂ extracts of sage into compositionally distinct fractions. Extraction was conducted at 25 MPa and 60 °C; depressurisation stages were set at 15, 10, and 5 MPa. Total extract yield was 4.2 g per 100 g dry sage. The first separator (15 MPa) captured 68% of the total extract mass and was enriched in ursolic acid and oleic acid. The second stage (10 MPa) contained predominantly oxygenated sesquiterpenes including β-eudesmol. The third stage (5 MPa) yielded a lighter monoterpene-rich fraction with α-thujone as the dominant component. GC-MS and HPLC-UV analysis confirmed fraction identities. A mass-balance model based on partition coefficients derived from binary solubility data predicted fractional yields within 15% of experimental values. The work demonstrates that pressure-stage fractionation is a practical first-pass separation for sage extracts without the need for further chromatographic purification.

title: Modelling binary interaction parameters for CO₂ + terpene systems using a modified group contribution method
abstract: A modified group-contribution approach was developed to predict Peng-Robinson binary interaction parameters (kij) for CO₂ + monoterpene and CO₂ + sesquiterpene pairs without requiring experimental fitting data for each compound. The method uses three structural descriptors — number of isoprene units, degree of unsaturation, and presence of oxygenated functional groups — to regress kij values from a training set of 22 binary systems drawn from the literature and from measurements conducted in-house. The training set spanned pressures of 8–35 MPa and temperatures of 35–80 °C. Leave-one-out cross-validation on the full 22-compound set gave a mean AARD of 5.7% for bubble-point pressures, which is within the accuracy requirements for preliminary process design. The method was applied predictively to four terpene compounds not included in training, with AARDs between 4.2 and 8.9%. A correlation table of group contribution increments is provided for direct use in process simulators.

title: Scale-up considerations for supercritical CO₂ extraction of lavender: comparison of laboratory (0.5 L) and pilot (10 L) extractors
abstract: Extraction yield and linalool/linalool acetate selectivity were measured for lavender (Lavandula angustifolia) in a 0.5 L laboratory extractor and a 10 L pilot unit at matching specific CO₂ flow rates (CO₂-to-feed ratios between 20 and 80 g CO₂/g dry herb). Operating conditions were 12 MPa and 50 °C throughout. The linalool yield at the pilot scale was 8–12% lower than at laboratory scale at equivalent specific flow rates, attributable primarily to channelling effects evidenced by residence time distribution measurements using methane tracer. Radial temperature gradients of up to 4 °C were recorded in the pilot vessel during extraction, compared with less than 0.5 °C in the laboratory unit. Adjusting the CO₂ superficial velocity to maintain a constant particle Reynolds number reduced the yield discrepancy to below 5%. The findings provide practical guidance for scale-up of terpenoid-targeting extractions and suggest that bed geometry is a more critical design variable than extractor volume per se.

title: Effect of pre-treatment methods on supercritical CO₂ extraction efficiency of monoterpenes from Mentha piperita
abstract: Three pre-treatment methods — freeze-drying, convective hot-air drying at 40 °C, and cryogenic milling without prior drying — were evaluated for their effect on the extraction of menthol, menthone, and limonene from peppermint (Mentha piperita) using supercritical CO₂ at 15 MPa and 55 °C. Moisture content, particle size distribution, and cell wall integrity assessed by scanning electron microscopy differed substantially among pre-treatments. Freeze-dried samples gave the highest total monoterpene yield (11.6 mg/g dry herb), followed by convective-dried (9.2 mg/g) and cryomilled fresh (7.4 mg/g). Menthol selectivity was highest for the convectively dried material (menthol:menthone ratio = 1.8) versus 1.3 for freeze-dried samples, suggesting that drying-induced cell damage preferentially released menthone precursors. Extraction half-times derived from the Sovová model correlated linearly with particle surface area (R² = 0.97). The study advises that pre-treatment selection should consider both yield and composition targets simultaneously.

title: Supercritical CO₂ solubility and fractionation of azulene-containing sesquiterpenes from Matricaria chamomilla: data and process implications
abstract: Solubility data for (–)-α-bisabolol and chamazulene in supercritical CO₂ were measured simultaneously in a ternary system at 12–30 MPa and 45–65 °C, complementing previously published binary data for each compound individually. Co-solubility behaviour showed positive synergistic deviations from linear combination of binary solubilities at pressures below 18 MPa. Fractionation experiments on chamomile flower extract at two-stage depressurisation (18 MPa → 10 MPa → 5 MPa) achieved a chamazulene enrichment of 2.3-fold relative to raw extract in the second separator, with a concurrent 80% recovery of α-bisabolol in the first separator. A simplified process economics estimate for a 50 kg/day dry herb throughput indicated a CO₂ recycle compressor as the dominant operating cost, representing approximately 55% of total energy input. The data support the feasibility of producing chamomile fractions enriched in anti-inflammatory sesquiterpenes as a pharmaceutical intermediate using pressure-fractioned supercritical extraction.

title: Structural characterisation of a branched heteropolysaccharide produced by Lactobacillus rhamnosus NS-2 using methylation analysis and NMR spectroscopy
abstract: A heteropolysaccharide produced by Lactobacillus rhamnosus NS-2, a strain isolated from a Vojvodina cheese sample, was isolated, purified by ion-exchange and size-exclusion chromatography, and subjected to structural analysis. Methylation analysis after carboxyl reduction indicated the presence of terminal β-D-galactopyranose, 3-substituted β-D-glucopyranose, and 4,6-disubstituted α-D-galactopyranose, pointing to a branched trisaccharide repeating unit. One- and two-dimensional NMR spectra (COSY, TOCSY, HSQC, HMBC) recorded at 600 MHz enabled complete assignment of all anomeric proton signals between δ 4.45 and 5.12 ppm. The molecular weight by SEC-MALS was 1.1 × 10⁶ Da with a dispersity index of 1.22. Acetyl substitution at O-6 of the glucosyl residue was evidenced by a resonance at δ 2.11 ppm in the ¹H NMR spectrum and confirmed by saponification experiments showing release of acetic acid. The degree of acetylation was 0.38 mol acetic acid per mole repeating unit. Preliminary circular dichroism spectra showed no ordered secondary structure in solution at neutral pH.

title: Solubility of α-tocopherol in supercritical CO₂ at pressures between 15 and 40 MPa: experimental data and Chrastil model fitting
abstract: Accurate solubility data for α-tocopherol in supercritical CO₂ are required for the rational design of extraction processes from oilseed matrices. In this study, a dynamic saturation method was used to measure α-tocopherol solubility in CO₂ over the pressure range 15–40 MPa at temperatures of 313, 333, and 353 K. Solubility values ranged from 0.41 to 4.87 g per kg CO₂ across the studied conditions. The Chrastil density-based model was fitted to the data, yielding an association constant k of 6.2 and a mean absolute relative deviation of 4.1%. Retrograde solubility behaviour was not observed in the studied window, and solubility increased monotonically with both pressure and temperature above 323 K. The dataset is compared with three earlier literature sources using dissimilar measurement techniques, and systematic deviations at moderate pressure are discussed in terms of equilibration time and sampling methodology. The fitted parameters are incorporated into a simple extraction yield model for a packed-bed extractor operating at industrially relevant flow rates.

title: Effect of seed pre-treatment on supercritical CO₂ extraction yield of lipids from cold-pressed sunflower cake
abstract: Sunflower press cake retains 8–14% residual oil after cold pressing, with the lipid fraction enriched in tocopherols relative to crude oil. This study examined how three pre-treatment approaches — untreated cake, roller-milled cake, and enzyme-assisted maceration with a commercial cellulase preparation — affect extraction yield and tocopherol content in extracts obtained by supercritical CO₂ at 35 MPa and 323 K. Extraction curves were recorded over 120 min at a CO₂ flow of 3 kg/h using a 0.5-litre vessel loaded with 80 g of material. Roller milling increased total lipid yield from 76% to 89% of Soxhlet reference and improved α-tocopherol concentration in the extract by 18%. Enzyme maceration gave intermediate lipid yield but the highest phytosterol-to-lipid ratio. Particle size distribution, moisture content, and bulk density were measured before each run and correlated with initial extraction rate constants using a simple broken-and-intact-cell model. Practical implications for cake pre-processing at pilot scale are discussed.

title: Pressure-temperature pathway optimisation for selective recovery of phytosterols from rapeseed meal using supercritical CO₂ with ethanol co-solvent
abstract: Phytosterols in rapeseed meal are present at concentrations of 0.4–0.9% dry basis and are co-extracted with triacylglycerols under standard supercritical CO₂ conditions, complicating downstream purification. This work investigates whether a two-stage pressure–temperature pathway, designed to exploit differential solubility, can enrich phytosterols relative to bulk lipids in the second fraction. Ethanol was added as co-solvent at 3 and 6 mol% to enhance sterol solubility. Experiments were conducted in a 1-litre extractor; stage one operated at 20 MPa and 313 K to remove the triacylglycerol-rich fraction, followed by stage two at 30 MPa and 343 K. With 6 mol% ethanol in stage two, the phytosterol-to-lipid mass ratio in the second fraction reached 0.038 g/g, compared with 0.011 g/g in a single-stage reference run. β-sitosterol and campesterol were the dominant sterols identified by GC-FID. A response surface model (central composite design, 27 runs) was used to map the combined effect of co-solvent fraction and stage-two pressure on selectivity. Limitations related to carry-over between stages are quantified.

title: Modelling of supercritical CO₂ extraction kinetics from sunflower cake using the Sovová model: sensitivity of parameters to moisture content
abstract: The Sovová broken-and-intact-cell model is widely applied to describe supercritical extraction kinetics but requires fitting of three parameters whose sensitivity to feedstock moisture has received limited attention in the oilseed literature. This study presents extraction curves for sunflower press cake conditioned to five moisture levels (2, 5, 8, 11, and 14% wet basis) extracted at 35 MPa, 323 K, and a solvent-to-feed ratio ranging from 10 to 60 g CO₂/g feed. Model parameters — fraction of broken cells, mass transfer coefficient in the intact-cell zone, and solubility — were estimated by non-linear least squares for each moisture condition. The intact-cell mass transfer coefficient decreased from 2.4 × 10⁻⁴ to 0.9 × 10⁻⁴ m/s as moisture increased from 2 to 14%, while the fraction of broken cells was relatively insensitive (0.62–0.68). Total extraction yield at a solvent ratio of 40 g/g dropped from 88% to 71% of Soxhlet reference over the same moisture range. Recommendations for feedstock drying prior to extraction are given based on an economic break-even analysis.

title: Supercritical fluid extraction of carotenoids from dried tomato pomace: comparison of CO₂ and CO₂/ethyl acetate mixtures
abstract: Tomato pomace from juice processing contains lycopene and β-carotene at concentrations of 0.5–1.2 mg/g dry basis and represents a low-cost raw material for carotenoid recovery. Pure CO₂ has low selectivity for lycopene at pressures below 45 MPa; this work evaluates ethyl acetate as an alternative co-solvent to ethanol, focusing on carotenoid yield, extract colour strength, and residual solvent levels. Dried, milled pomace (particle size 0.3–0.6 mm) was extracted at 35 and 45 MPa, 313 and 333 K, with co-solvent fractions of 0, 2, 5, and 8 mol%. Lycopene yield increased from 31% (pure CO₂, 45 MPa, 333 K) to 61% (8 mol% ethyl acetate, 45 MPa, 333 K) relative to acetone reference extraction. Residual ethyl acetate in the extract was below 15 mg/kg after evaporation, within EU food-grade limits. The polarity parameter of the binary mixture was estimated using a simple mixing rule and correlated with lycopene solubility. Thermal degradation of lycopene during extraction was monitored by isomer ratio (all-trans versus cis) and was below 8% under all tested conditions.

title: Pilot-scale supercritical CO₂ extraction of tocopherol-enriched oil from sunflower press cake: mass balance and energy demand at 50-litre vessel scale
abstract: Scaling supercritical extraction from bench to pilot scale introduces challenges related to flow distribution, heat losses, and separator performance not captured by laboratory models. This study reports a complete mass balance and energy audit for a 50-litre extractor processing sunflower press cake at 35 MPa and 323 K, with a CO₂ circulation rate of 30 kg/h. The pilot unit was operated at an industrial partner's facility over twelve consecutive extraction cycles, each loaded with 12 kg of cake (moisture 5%, particle size 1–2 mm). Total tocopherol recovery per cycle averaged 87% of Soxhlet reference, with a coefficient of variation of 3.4% across cycles. Specific CO₂ consumption was 42 kg CO₂ per kg extract. Thermal energy demand for CO₂ reheating accounted for 58% of total energy consumption; a heat integration analysis identified a countercurrent exchanger between high-pressure CO₂ and separator off-gas as the most cost-effective retrofit. Capital and operating cost estimates are provided for a hypothetical 200-litre production unit.

title: Equation-of-state approaches for correlating solubility of plant waxes in supercritical CO₂: comparison of Peng–Robinson with van der Waals mixing rules and PC-SAFT
abstract: Predictive solubility models are needed for compounds whose experimental high-pressure data are sparse, including plant waxes (long-chain esters and fatty alcohols) that appear in defatted extracts from oilseed processing. This work evaluates two thermodynamic approaches — Peng–Robinson EoS with classical and van der Waals one-fluid mixing rules, and the PC-SAFT equation — for correlating literature solubility data of hexadecanol, octacosanol, and a synthetic sunflower wax mixture in CO₂ between 10 and 50 MPa. PC-SAFT with two binary interaction parameters achieved a mean absolute relative deviation of 7.3% across all compounds and conditions, compared with 14.8% for PR-EoS with two-parameter mixing rules. Sensitivity of predictions to pure-component PC-SAFT parameters estimated from group-contribution methods versus fitted values is quantified. The analysis indicates that group-contribution PC-SAFT parameters are sufficient for screening-level process calculations but require correction when purity specifications are tight. A brief worked example is given for separator design in a two-stage extraction flowsheet.

title: Recovery of tocols from hemp seed cake by supercritical CO₂ extraction: effect of particle size and vessel packing density on extraction rate
abstract: Hemp seed cake from cold pressing contains 0.06–0.12% tocols (tocopherols plus tocotrienols) concentrated in the lipid fraction and is produced in increasing quantities in the Vojvodina region as hemp cultivation expands. This study investigated how particle size (0.25–0.5, 0.5–1.0, and 1.0–2.0 mm fractions) and packing density (350–550 kg/m³) affect the initial extraction rate and total tocol recovery at 30 MPa and 323 K. Reducing particle size from 1.0–2.0 mm to 0.25–0.5 mm increased initial extraction rate by 2.3-fold but also increased pressure drop across the 1-litre vessel from 0.3 to 1.1 MPa at 3 kg/h CO₂. A combination of 0.5–1.0 mm particles and 420 kg/m³ packing density provided the best balance between mass transfer and pressure drop, yielding 83% tocol recovery in 90 min. Tocotrienol content in extracts was characterised by HPLC-DAD and showed a higher ratio of γ-tocotrienol to α-tocopherol than in commercial hemp oil, suggesting selective enrichment. Regional hemp cake supply and quality variability are briefly discussed.

title: Effect of temperature fluctuation on nanofiltration rejection of divalent ions in a compact agricultural water reuse circuit: experimental and modelling study
abstract: Compact nanofiltration (NF) circuits are increasingly considered for water reuse in irrigated agriculture in the Vojvodina region, where feed-water temperature varies substantially between seasons. This study investigates the effect of temperature on NF rejection of calcium, magnesium, and sulphate ions by combining controlled laboratory experiments on a flat-sheet NF test cell with a solution-diffusion–electromigration transport model. Experiments were conducted at 10 °C, 18 °C, and 26 °C across feed pressures of 4–12 bar, using synthetic solutions representative of local drainage water chemistry. Calcium rejection decreased from 91% at 10 °C to 84% at 26 °C at constant 8 bar pressure; sulphate rejection was less temperature-sensitive, decreasing by 3.4 percentage points over the same range. The calibrated transport model reproduced these trends with a mean absolute error of 1.8 percentage points and was used to assess seasonal permeate quality variation in a hypothetical 50 m³/h compact reuse circuit, confirming that permeate softening requirements increase during summer operation.

title: Screw configuration effects on residence time distribution and protein denaturation during starch–whey protein extrusion
abstract: Three screw configurations of a co-rotating twin-screw extruder were compared for processing starch–whey protein concentrate (WPC) blends at 20 wt% protein. Configurations differed in the number and placement of kneading blocks: low-shear (LS), medium-shear (MS), and high-shear (HS). Residence time distribution was measured using a salt tracer with conductivity detection at the die. Mean residence times were 68, 54, and 41 s for LS, MS, and HS configurations respectively. Differential scanning calorimetry of extrudates showed WPC denaturation enthalpy dropping from 4.2 J/g in unprocessed material to below 0.3 J/g in all configurations, indicating near-complete denaturation regardless of screw design. However, SDS-PAGE analysis revealed differences in aggregate molecular weight distribution: the HS configuration produced larger insoluble aggregates linked by disulfide bonds. Tensile modulus of extruded sheets was 12% higher for HS than for LS at equivalent formulation, while haze values of films increased from 18 to 34%. These findings show that screw configuration controls protein network structure independently of bulk denaturation degree.

title: A Branch-and-Bound Approach to the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Hard Time Windows
abstract: This paper addresses the capacitated vehicle routing problem with hard time windows (CVRPTW) using a branch-and-bound algorithm enhanced by a set of dominance rules derived from Lagrangian relaxation. The test instances are drawn from the Solomon benchmark suite as well as a locally generated dataset of 40 instances representing urban delivery scenarios in a mid-size city network with 80–150 customer nodes. The branching strategy prioritises fractional arc variables with highest reduced cost, and lower bounds are tightened using a column-generation subproblem solved by a shortest-path procedure on an auxiliary time-expanded graph. Computational experiments show that the proposed algorithm closes 87% of Solomon's 100-customer instances within a two-hour time limit on a standard quad-core workstation, reducing the average optimality gap to 1.3% compared to 4.7% for a standard LP-relaxation baseline. The approach scales poorly beyond 200 nodes but provides provably optimal or near-optimal solutions for medium-scale instances relevant to last-mile logistics.

title: Shortest Path Enumeration in Directed Graphs with Multiple Additive Constraints
abstract: Finding the shortest path in a graph subject to two or more additive resource constraints is NP-hard in general, yet instances arising in transportation and telecommunication networks are often sparse and admit efficient exact or approximate solutions. This study examines the resource-constrained shortest path problem (RCSPP) on directed graphs with up to four simultaneous constraints representing travel time, cost, CO₂ emission, and toll charges. A labelling algorithm with dominance pruning is implemented and compared against a penalty-based Lagrangian heuristic and a simple Dijkstra adaptation. Experiments are conducted on randomly generated graphs (100–1000 nodes, density 0.02–0.05) and on a real road-network graph of the Vojvodina region with 3 200 nodes extracted from publicly available map data. The labelling algorithm consistently finds optimal solutions on sparse graphs up to 600 nodes within one second; the Lagrangian heuristic achieves a mean gap of 2.1% on larger instances. The study also provides a tight complexity analysis for the two-constraint case.

title: Time-Dependent Shortest Paths on Road Networks: Exact and Heuristic Comparisons
abstract: In time-dependent road networks, travel time along an arc is a function of the departure time rather than a fixed value. This paper evaluates four solution strategies for the time-dependent shortest path problem (TDSPP): a modified Dijkstra algorithm with piecewise-linear arc functions, A* with a time-invariant lower-bound heuristic, a bidirectional Dijkstra adapted for time-dependency, and a greedy rollout procedure. Arc travel-time functions are modelled as piecewise-linear with 24 breakpoints derived from traffic count data collected on 18 arterial roads in the city of Novi Sad over six months. Graphs of 500–8 000 nodes are constructed. The modified Dijkstra with FIFO-consistent arc functions guarantees optimality and outperforms the bidirectional variant, which loses its correctness guarantee in the non-FIFO case. The A* heuristic reduces node expansions by 34–61% at a cost of occasional sub-optimality (0.4% mean gap). Results are relevant for dynamic navigation systems requiring sub-second query times.

title: Integer Programming Models for the Green Vehicle Routing Problem with Speed Optimisation
abstract: Fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions in road freight depend on vehicle speed and load, making the green vehicle routing problem (G-VRP) a natural extension of classical VRP formulations. This chapter reviews and extends three integer programming formulations for G-VRP that include speed as a continuous decision variable alongside routing decisions. The chapter distinguishes between arc-speed and segment-speed models and introduces an additional constraint set enforcing legal speed limits and driver working-time regulations under European transport law. Linearisation techniques for the nonlinear fuel-consumption function (a cubic in speed) are discussed, including piecewise-linear approximation and second-order cone relaxation. Computational results on 30 benchmark instances with 20–75 vehicles demonstrate that the piecewise-linear model with eight segments is within 1.8% of the exact nonlinear solution while remaining tractable for a commercial MIP solver. The chapter also outlines open problems regarding stochastic demand and multi-depot extensions.

title: A Tabu Search Heuristic for Multi-Depot Routing with Heterogeneous Fleet and Driver Skill Constraints
abstract: Multi-depot vehicle routing with a heterogeneous fleet introduces assignment decisions—which depot serves which customer, and which vehicle type and driver are assigned—on top of standard routing choices. Driver skill constraints further restrict assignment: certain vehicle categories require certified operators, reducing feasible assignments substantially. This paper formulates the problem as a mixed-integer programme and proposes a tabu search heuristic operating on a combined routing-and-assignment neighbourhood. Moves include intra-route 2-opt, inter-route relocation, and depot-swap operators. The tabu list tracks arc-use and depot-assignment pairs with adaptive tenure of 7–15 iterations. Tested on 45 generated instances (3–5 depots, 8–16 vehicle types, 60–200 customers), the heuristic finds solutions within 3.6% of the best known lower bound on average, running in under 90 seconds per instance. A case study models emergency medical supply distribution from four logistics hubs across Vojvodina, using realistic road distances and vehicle certification requirements.

title: Graph Compression Techniques for Faster Real-Time Route Queries in Large Urban Networks
abstract: Route query latency in large-scale urban road networks must remain below 200 ms for interactive navigation applications. This paper examines three graph compression techniques—contraction hierarchies (CH), arc-flags, and a hybrid CH-with-arc-flags approach—applied to directed weighted graphs representing the road networks of three mid-size Eastern European cities (population 200 000–400 000), with node counts ranging from 41 000 to 78 000. Preprocessing times, memory footprints, and query times are measured for Dijkstra, CH, arc-flags, and the hybrid. CH reduces query time from 18 ms (standard Dijkstra) to 0.8 ms on average; arc-flags achieve 1.1 ms; the hybrid achieves 0.6 ms at the cost of a 40% larger preprocessing index. The study further evaluates robustness under real-time edge-weight updates (traffic incidents): CH requires partial re-contraction while arc-flags allow lightweight flag invalidation. Results provide practical guidance for choosing compression strategies under different update-frequency regimes.

title: Constraint Propagation Strategies for Online Re-Routing Under Dynamic Demand in Last-Mile Delivery
abstract: Last-mile delivery networks face frequent mid-route disruptions: customer cancellations, new order insertions, and road closures occur continuously during an active shift. This paper models the online re-routing problem as a sequence of constrained shortest-path queries on a time-expanded graph where constraints encode vehicle capacity, remaining working time, and mandatory service-time windows. Four constraint propagation strategies are compared: forward checking, arc consistency (AC-3), a path-consistency procedure, and a hybrid forward-checking-with-arc-consistency scheme. Experiments use a discrete-event simulation of 200 delivery shifts over a 60-node urban graph, with disruption events arriving according to a Poisson process (rate λ = 1.2 per hour). The hybrid scheme reduces the fraction of constraint violations requiring full re-optimisation from 38% (forward checking alone) to 11%, while adding only 14 ms overhead per event on average. The paper also analyses failure modes when consecutive disruptions arrive faster than re-optimisation completes.

title: A Matheuristic for the Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Partial Recharging and Time Windows
abstract: Electric freight vehicles must recharge before their battery is depleted; partial recharging—stopping before full charge—can reduce route duration significantly. This paper models the electric vehicle routing problem with partial recharging and time windows (EVRPTW-PR) as a mixed-integer second-order cone programme and solves it with a matheuristic that alternates between a large neighbourhood search (LNS) phase and an exact re-optimisation of recharging decisions via a compact MIP. The LNS uses destroy operators—random removal, worst-cost removal, and time-window-cluster removal—followed by a greedy insertion repair. Charger locations are given; recharging rate is modelled as constant. Tested on 60 instances derived from the Schneider benchmark with added partial-recharging parameters, the matheuristic produces solutions within 4.1% of best-known values in under five minutes per instance. Energy consumption is modelled as linearly proportional to distance and load, with separate coefficients calibrated from manufacturer data for two representative electric van categories.

title: Shortest Hyperpaths with Stochastic Arc Weights: Bounds and Approximations for Real-Time Applications
abstract: In stochastic road networks, arc travel times are random variables whose realisations become known only as a vehicle traverses an arc. Adaptive routing policies—strategies that select the next arc after observing the realised travel time—can outperform fixed a priori paths but require solving a stochastic shortest hyperpath problem, which is computationally demanding. This preprint proposes two polynomial-time approximation schemes: a sample-average approximation (SAA) that replaces the stochastic problem with a deterministic equivalent over K sampled scenarios (K = 50–500), and a distributionally robust formulation that minimises worst-case expected travel time over an ambiguity set defined by mean and variance constraints. Both are benchmarked on a synthetic graph family and on the Vojvodina road network augmented with speed-variance data estimated from 30-day probe-vehicle logs covering approximately 1 400 road segments. The SAA with K = 200 achieves solutions within 3% of Monte Carlo lower bounds in under two seconds per query. The robust formulation is more conservative but improves tail-risk performance by 18% on average.

title: Feature Stability Under Resampling in Gradient-Boosted Classifiers for Imbalanced Data
abstract: When resampling is applied to imbalanced training sets, the feature importance rankings produced by gradient-boosted classifiers can change substantially across resampling repetitions, complicating model interpretation and feature selection. This paper quantifies feature importance instability using Spearman rank correlation and the Jaccard index over the top-k features, across five resampling techniques and 30 bootstrap repetitions on eight benchmark datasets. Datasets cover telecom churn, medical readmission, and retail return events, with positive rates between 1% and 10% and between 20 and 80 input features. Results show that SMOTE with controlled oversampling rate (≤200%) reduces instability substantially compared to aggressive oversampling, and that importance derived from SHAP values is more stable than gain-based importance. A practical guideline recommends ensemble importance averaging over multiple resampled fits as a low-cost stabilisation strategy.

title: A manually annotated corpus of Serbian named entities in news text
abstract: This paper presents SerbNER-News, a corpus of 45,000 sentences sampled from six years of Serbian-language news wire, manually annotated for four entity types: person, organisation, location, and miscellaneous. Annotation was performed by four trained linguists following a detailed guidelines document developed specifically for Serbian, which addresses challenges such as the use of the genitive case for organisation names and the ambiguity of demonyms. Inter-annotator agreement measured by Cohen's kappa reached 0.83 on a 5,000-sentence adjudication subset. Baseline experiments with a bidirectional LSTM-CRF model trained on 80% of the corpus achieved a macro-averaged F1 of 81.2% on the test split, establishing a reference point for future work. The corpus, annotation guidelines, and baseline model weights are made publicly available. Known biases toward formal register and geographic concentration in Vojvodina sources are discussed as limitations.

title: Rolling Horizon Approaches for Dynamic Nurse Rostering Under Uncertain Absenteeism
abstract: Nurse absenteeism introduces uncertainty into rostering that static models cannot adequately address. This paper studies rolling horizon approaches in which a new rostering decision is made at the start of each week using updated information about absences that materialised in the previous period. Three rolling horizon policies are compared: re-optimise from scratch, warm-start from the previous solution, and maintain a buffer of pre-qualified on-call nurses. The policies are evaluated in simulation over 52 weekly periods using an absenteeism model calibrated on three years of absence records from a 200-nurse hospital in Vojvodina. Performance is measured in terms of coverage violations, total overtime, and disruption to previously published schedules. The warm-start policy with a 10% on-call buffer achieves the best trade-off: it reduces coverage violations by 43% relative to the static baseline while limiting schedule disruptions to an average of 4.2 changes per nurse per four-week period.

title: Topological complexity measures for time series from dynamical systems: a comparative study
abstract: We compare four topological complexity measures—persistent entropy, the number of bars with persistence above a threshold, the total persistence (sum of bar lengths), and the bottleneck amplitude—applied to time series from six dynamical systems: the Lorenz attractor, the Rössler system, logistic map at varying r, the Duffing oscillator, white noise, and periodic sine waves. Each system is sampled at 2 000 time steps; delay-coordinate embedding with parameters estimated via average mutual information is applied before TDA. Persistent entropy best separates chaotic from periodic regimes (AUROC 0.94) and is most robust to measurement noise up to σ = 0.10. The Lorenz and Rössler attractors are reliably distinguished by H_2 bar count (mean difference 3.8, p < 0.001 by permutation test). We also show that topological measures and the largest Lyapunov exponent are correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.82) but not interchangeable, carrying complementary information.

title: Comparison of four silica-membrane spin-column protocols for DNA recovery from formalin-fixed tissue sections of varying fixation age
abstract: Formalin fixation introduces cross-links and chemical modifications that substantially reduce DNA extractability and downstream amplification success. This study evaluated four commercial silica-membrane spin-column kits using bovine liver sections fixed for 24 hours, 1 week, 1 month, and 6 months. Yield was quantified by fluorometric assay (Qubit 2.0) and fragment size distribution assessed by capillary electrophoresis. Average yields ranged from 312 ng per 10 mg tissue for freshly fixed material to 41 ng for 6-month-fixed sections. Amplification success in a 148 bp single-locus PCR assay dropped from 96% to 38% across the same gradient. An extended 65°C lysis incubation of 16 hours combined with a modified elution temperature of 75°C improved yield by 27% and amplification success by 19% relative to manufacturer defaults for the oldest specimens. No single kit outperformed others across all age categories, indicating that protocol adaptation rather than kit selection is the primary driver of recovery from aged fixed material.

title: Primer dimer frequency and off-target amplification in five-plex PCR panels as a function of annealing temperature and Mg2+ concentration
abstract: Multiplexing five or more primer pairs in a single PCR reaction increases the probability of inter-primer interactions that generate primer dimers and off-target products. Using a model five-plex panel targeting single-nucleotide polymorphisms in cereal grain DNA, this study mapped primer dimer formation and off-target band intensity across a grid of 12 annealing temperatures (50–62°C in 1°C steps) and four MgCl2 concentrations (1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 mM). Gel densitometry was used to score 48 parameter combinations in triplicate. Primer dimer abundance was highest at 50°C and 3.0 mM MgCl2 and lowest at 58°C and 2.0 mM MgCl2. Off-target amplification showed a less regular pattern and was primarily attributable to two primer pairs with predicted 3′ complementarity scores above 4 kcal/mol as calculated by Primer3Plus. Redesigning those two primers to reduce 3′ complementarity to below 1.5 kcal/mol eliminated visible off-target bands across all temperature–Mg2+ combinations tested. The study provides a replicable optimisation framework for small multiplex panel development in resource-limited laboratory settings.

title: Field-deployable bead-beating lysis coupled with silica spin-column cleanup for plant pathogen detection from symptomless leaf tissue
abstract: Early detection of fungal and bacterial pathogens in symptomless plant material requires extraction protocols that function outside conventional laboratory settings. This study adapted a bead-beating lysis step for use with a 12 V battery-powered miniature vortex mixer and evaluated compatibility with two portable silica spin-column formats across 120 symptomless wheat and sunflower leaf samples collected at seven field sites in northern Serbia. Total DNA yields averaged 18.4 ng/µL (range 4.2–61.7 ng/µL), which was sufficient for PCR detection at template volumes of 2 µL in a 25 µL reaction for 89% of samples. A fluorometric spot-check card calibrated against known standards allowed field estimation of DNA concentration without a bench reader. Pathogen detection sensitivity in the field workflow was 83% relative to a laboratory-reference CTAB extraction protocol scored as the comparator. False positive rate was 1.7% across all samples. The workflow was completed within 55 minutes per eight-sample batch using only equipment fitting in a standard field backpack, establishing a practical baseline for decentralised plant disease surveillance.

title: Assessment of DNA integrity index thresholds for reliable genotyping of bovine ear-notch and hair follicle specimens collected under field conditions
abstract: Genotyping livestock using ear-notch cards and hair follicles collected on farms enables traceability programmes without cold-chain transport. DNA integrity index (DII) values, calculated from the ratio of absorbance at 260 nm to the ratio of long-amplicon to short-amplicon qPCR yield, were measured for 310 bovine specimens. DII thresholds for successful genotyping at 12 microsatellite loci were established empirically. Specimens with DII above 0.62 achieved complete 12-locus profiles in 94.1% of cases, while specimens below 0.30 yielded complete profiles in only 21.4% of cases. Hair follicle samples showed systematically lower DII than ear-notch cards regardless of storage duration, but partially recovered after a 56°C extended-digest pre-treatment. Storage at ambient temperature for 30 days reduced DII by a mean of 0.11 for ear-notch and 0.18 for hair follicle specimens. The DII metric is proposed as a simple pre-screening step to flag specimens likely to yield incomplete genotype profiles before committing them to full microsatellite analysis, thereby reducing the proportion of repeat sampling events.

title: Balancing sensitivity and specificity in a three-plex SNP genotyping PCR assay for adulteration detection in processed meat products
abstract: Detection of undeclared species in processed meat products requires PCR assays that perform reliably on heat-treated, heavily degraded DNA templates. A three-plex assay was designed to simultaneously amplify short species-specific fragments (68–94 bp) from pork, beef, and horse mitochondrial DNA. Primer design prioritised amplicon lengths below 100 bp and Tm uniformity within 1.5°C across all six primers. The assay was evaluated on 88 commercially purchased processed meat samples including sausages, pâtés, and canned products. Analytical sensitivity was established at 0.1% (w/w) undeclared species in binary mixtures of ground meat. Cross-reactivity was assessed against 11 non-target vertebrate species; no false positive signals were observed. In commercial samples, 7 of 88 (8%) carried detectable horse mitochondrial DNA, and 11 of 88 (12.5%) showed pork signals in nominally beef-only products. The assay ran in under two hours from extraction to result and required no post-PCR processing beyond agarose gel analysis, supporting its use in routine food control laboratories with limited instrumentation.

title: Optimising chaotropic salt concentration and ethanol wash stringency for RNA preservation in buccal swabs stored at room temperature for up to 14 days
abstract: Buccal swabs represent a minimally invasive collection substrate suitable for decentralised health studies, but RNA degradation during unrefrigerated storage complicates downstream gene expression analysis. This study evaluated combinations of guanidinium thiocyanate (GuSCN) concentrations (2 M, 4 M, 6 M) and ethanol wash volumes (350 µL, 600 µL, 2×350 µL) in a modified column protocol applied to buccal swabs stored at 22–25°C for 1, 3, 7, and 14 days. RNA integrity numbers (RIN) were determined on a Bioanalyzer 2100 equivalent system. At day 14, 6 M GuSCN combined with a 2×350 µL wash yielded a mean RIN of 5.8 compared to 2.9 for the standard 4 M/single-wash condition. GAPDH and beta-actin transcript yields were sufficient for RT-qPCR in 87% of day-14 specimens under the optimised protocol versus 41% under standard conditions. Inhibitor carryover, assessed by spike-in control, was not significantly elevated under the higher chaotrope concentration. Results support the feasibility of room-temperature buccal RNA collection over two-week periods when field cold-chain maintenance is impractical.

title: Portability constraints and thermal profile accuracy of five miniaturised PCR devices evaluated against a laboratory-grade thermal cycler using a standard 148 bp amplicon panel
abstract: Miniaturised thermal cyclers marketed for field and point-of-care use vary substantially in ramp rate accuracy, lid temperature control, and block uniformity. This study benchmarked five commercially available compact devices against a laboratory-standard gradient thermal cycler using a panel of six amplicons ranging from 85 to 312 bp, including both GC-rich and AT-rich primer pairs. Ramp rates measured by embedded thermocouple ranged from 1.1°C/s to 3.4°C/s among portable devices versus 4.8°C/s for the reference unit. Block temperature uniformity at a set point of 72°C varied by up to 2.9°C across wells in one portable device versus 0.3°C in the reference. Amplification yield, measured by fluorometric endpoint quantification, was within 15% of the reference for four of five portable devices for all amplicons below 200 bp. The 312 bp amplicons showed yield reductions of 22–51% in three devices, attributable to premature extension-phase termination. Power consumption ranged from 18 W to 74 W per cycle, a parameter with direct implications for battery-powered field operation. Device selection guidelines are proposed for each performance category.

title: Acid tolerance responses of Lactobacillus isolates from traditional Serbian white cheese under simulated gastric conditions
abstract: Ten Lactobacillus strains isolated from artisan white cheeses produced in the Vojvodina region were screened for survival at pH values between 2.0 and 4.0 over a 3-hour incubation period. Viable counts were determined by standard plate counting on MRS agar, and membrane integrity was assessed by propidium iodide exclusion using epifluorescence microscopy. Three strains retained viability above 10^6 CFU/mL after 2 hours at pH 2.5, while the remaining strains showed reductions exceeding 4 log units. Intracellular pH homeostasis was partially characterised through proton-pumping ATPase activity assays. Strains with higher F-ATPase activity correlated with improved survival at pH 3.0 (r = 0.74, p < 0.05). The study provides baseline data for selecting robust starter or adjunct cultures from regional raw-milk cheese microbiota, and identifies two strains with sufficient acid tolerance for further functional food applications.

title: Surface plasmon resonance characterisation of anti-zearalenone antibody binding kinetics at varying ionic strength and pH
abstract: The binding kinetics of three commercially sourced anti-zearalenone monoclonal antibodies (clones ZEN-4, ZEN-11, and ZEN-19) were measured by surface plasmon resonance on a Biacore-type instrument using zearalenone–ovalbumin conjugates immobilised on CM5 chips. Association rate constants (ka) ranged from 1.4 × 10⁴ to 6.8 × 10⁴ M⁻¹s⁻¹ and dissociation rate constants (kd) from 2.1 × 10⁻³ to 9.4 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ under standard PBS conditions at pH 7.4. Equilibrium dissociation constants (KD) spanned 31 to 670 nM. Reducing ionic strength from 150 mM to 50 mM NaCl increased ka for clone ZEN-11 by 2.3-fold while kd remained unchanged, suggesting electrostatic contributions to the association step. Acidic pH (6.0) selectively destabilised clone ZEN-19 binding, increasing kd fivefold. Results indicate that buffer composition during strip manufacture should be tailored to the individual antibody clone to preserve optimal binding constants in the final immunoassay format.

title: Two Orthographic Traditions After 1990: A Comparative Analysis of the Matica srpska and Belgrade Orthographic Manuals
abstract: This article examines the textual differences between the 1993 Novi Sad orthographic manual issued under the auspices of Matica srpska and the competing Belgrade manual published the same year, using a systematic clause-by-clause comparison of 214 rules governing punctuation, compound words, and the use of diacritics. The study identifies 38 rules where the two manuals prescribe divergent solutions, cataloguing each discrepancy by category and assessing the institutional rationale offered in the accompanying commentary texts. Drawing on archival correspondence between the editorial boards, the article argues that the divergences reflect not merely technical disagreement but a deliberate assertion of institutional authority on both sides. The findings challenge the common assumption that post-Yugoslav Serbian standardisation was driven primarily by political nationalism, showing instead that professional-institutional competition played a comparably significant role. The article concludes with a typology of norm conflict applicable to other pluricentric standardisation situations.

title: Prescriptive Grammars and Editorial Practice: Evidence from Serbian Publishing Houses, 1991–2005
abstract: Using a corpus of 320 books published by six Serbian publishing houses between 1991 and 2005, this study tracks which orthographic manual editors de facto followed when resolving disputed spellings of compound words and foreign proper nouns. Each house was contacted for a structured interview, and copy-edited manuscripts from three cooperating publishers were examined directly. The results show that Belgrade-based publishers overwhelmingly adhered to the 1993 Belgrade manual even when the Novi Sad solution was formally adopted by the Serbian Ministry of Education, while Novi Sad publishers showed greater internal inconsistency. A regression analysis of 1,847 disputed tokens indicates that publisher location, founding date, and the educational background of the chief copy-editor are the strongest predictors of norm choice. The study provides empirical grounding for debates about the gap between prescriptive codification and actual editorial behaviour.

title: The 2010 Serbian Orthographic Manual and the Politics of Consensus: Drafting Committee Minutes as Primary Sources
abstract: The 2010 edition of the official Serbian orthographic manual was presented publicly as a consensus document. This article uses the unpublished minutes of the drafting committee, obtained through an archival access request, to reconstruct the negotiation process over 32 contested items, including the spelling of ijekavian reflexes in official correspondence and the treatment of anglicisms. The analysis reveals that consensus was achieved on fewer than half the contested items through genuine agreement; the remainder were resolved through procedural votes, with Novi Sad delegates consistently outvoted on questions of variant tolerance. Comparison with the submitted written proposals of individual committee members shows substantial discrepancy between private positions and the final text. The article argues that the minutes constitute an underused primary source type for language policy research and proposes a methodological framework for their systematic analysis.

title: Anglicism Integration Rules in Competing Serbian Normative Codes, 1993–2018
abstract: Serbian orthographic manuals and grammar guides have offered conflicting advice on adapting English loanwords to Serbian phonological and morphological patterns, particularly in the domains of IT, business, and popular culture vocabulary. This study compiles all prescriptive statements on anglicism integration from eight normative publications issued between 1993 and 2018 and codes them according to a schema covering graphemic transcription, inflectional class assignment, and the treatment of original spelling in quotation contexts. A total of 196 distinct prescriptive statements are identified, of which 61 contradict at least one other statement from a different manual. The study then examines a reference corpus of 2.3 million words of newspaper text to determine which prescription, if any, correlates with actual usage. The results suggest that neither the Novi Sad nor the Belgrade tradition commands consistent compliance in the press, with house style being the dominant factor.

title: Prescriptive Norm Awareness Among Secondary School Teachers of Serbian: A Survey of 412 Teachers in Vojvodina
abstract: Secondary school teachers of Serbian language occupy a critical node in the transmission of orthographic norms, yet little empirical data exist on what norms they actually know and prefer. This article reports a written questionnaire survey of 412 teachers in Vojvodina conducted during the 2016–17 school year. The questionnaire presented 40 items covering areas of documented Belgrade–Novi Sad divergence and asked respondents to select the correct form, to rate their confidence, and to identify the source of their knowledge. Results show that teachers perform significantly better on items where the two traditions agree (mean accuracy 83%) than on contested items (mean accuracy 51%). Teachers who attended university in Novi Sad were more likely to prefer Novi Sad solutions on contested items, but the effect size was modest. A majority of respondents were unaware that the items they answered were disputed. The findings have direct implications for teacher training curricula and textbook design.

title: Hyphenation of Compound Nouns in Serbian: Between Two Normative Centres
abstract: The hyphenation of compound nouns is one of the most persistently contested areas in Serbian orthography, with the Novi Sad and Belgrade traditions prescribing different solutions for overlapping but non-identical sets of compound types. This book chapter provides a systematic account of the divergence by tracing the historical development of hyphenation rules from the 1960 unified Novi Sad Agreement through successive manual revisions. Using a hand-annotated sub-corpus of 180,000 words drawn from regional weekly newspapers published in both cities between 2010 and 2020, the chapter calculates norm adherence rates for 14 compound noun types and shows that adherence rates below 60% are common even in professionally edited text. The chapter also analyses reader complaint letters to two newspapers' language columns, identifying hyphenation as the single most frequently raised orthographic grievance.

title: Digital Style Guides and Automated Spell-Checkers as Agents of Norm Enforcement: The Serbian Case
abstract: Automated spell-checkers and the internal style guides of major Serbian digital news portals have become de facto normative instruments, yet they have received almost no attention from normativists. This article examines the spell-check dictionaries embedded in three widely used Serbian-language word processors and the published or leaked style guides of four digital news portals active in 2021. For each of 30 contested orthographic items, the study records which variant the spell-checker flags as an error and which the style guide prescribes. Results show that two of the three spell-checkers default to Belgrade solutions on 27 of 30 items, while the portals show more varied patterns. The article argues that the technological infrastructure of writing now constitutes a third normative centre alongside the two academic traditions, one that operates largely without philological oversight and reaches more daily users than any printed manual.

title: Prescriptive Disagreement and Reader Confusion: An Experimental Study Using Simulated Proofreading Tasks
abstract: This study uses a controlled simulated proofreading experiment to measure the effect of prescriptive disagreement on reader behaviour. Seventy-two participants — university-educated adults with no formal linguistics training — were presented with 60 sentences containing either agreed-upon correct forms, agreed-upon errors, or forms that are correct according to one normative tradition but incorrect according to the other. Participants were asked to mark errors and rate their confidence. Accuracy on contested items (58% error identification rate) did not differ significantly from accuracy on genuine errors (61%), indicating that participants could not reliably distinguish between true orthographic errors and inter-tradition variation. Confidence ratings were, however, significantly lower for contested items. A follow-up interview component with 20 participants revealed that many had encountered conflicting corrections from different teachers or editors and had developed avoidance strategies, preferring simpler constructions to sidestep disputed forms.

title: Between Codification and Usage: Tracking 25 Years of Contested Serbian Spellings in a Diachronic Newspaper Corpus
abstract: This article presents results from a diachronic corpus study tracing 40 contested orthographic items across 25 years of digitised Serbian newspaper text, covering the period 1998–2023. The corpus was assembled from the digital archives of four daily newspapers (two Belgrade-based, two Novi Sad-based) and totals approximately 310 million tokens after deduplication and formatting normalisation. For each of the 40 items, yearly frequency counts of competing variants were extracted using regular-expression queries and normalised per million words. The results show three distinct trajectory types: items showing convergence toward one variant over time (14 items), items showing stable divergence with a geographic split (18 items), and items showing increasing variation with no directional trend (8 items). The convergence items are predominantly in the domain of foreign proper noun transcription, while stable divergence is concentrated in compound word hyphenation and the spelling of certain adverbial forms. The article discusses implications for future revision of the official orthographic manual.

title: What Do Copyediting Manuals Published by Serbian Publishers' Associations Tell Us About Norm Preference? A Content Analysis, 2000–2024
abstract: Publishers' associations and professional copyediting bodies in Serbia have issued at least nine internal or semi-public manuals intended to guide in-house editorial staff between 2000 and 2024. These documents occupy an intermediate position between official academic codification and actual editorial practice and have not previously been treated as a distinct source type in standardisation research. This preprint presents a content analysis of all nine manuals, coding each prescriptive statement by topic area, normative source cited, and stance toward the Belgrade–Novi Sad divide. Preliminary findings indicate that six of the nine manuals cite only Belgrade normative sources; two cite both traditions and acknowledge the dispute; one avoids explicit citation. The preprint also reports a short follow-up survey of 28 working copyeditors on their familiarity with and use of these manuals. The analysis is ongoing and a revised version is in preparation for journal submission.

title: Рубричко оцењивање студентских есеја: Поузданост оцењивача и аутоматска апроксимација
abstract: У раду се испитује поузданост рубричног оцењивања студентских есеја из наставних предмета са Филозофског факултета Универзитета у Новом Саду. Корпус обухвата 840 есеја оцењених од стране два независна оцењивача на основу петодимензионалне рубрике која покрива аргументацију, кохеренцију, лексичко богатство, граматичку исправност и адекватност структуре. Просечна вредност Коенове капе по димензијама износи 0,69. У другом делу рада развијамо регресионе моделе за аутоматску процену свих пет димензија рубрике. Испитано је 120 карактеристика, а резултати показују да аутоматски систем постиже корелацију r = 0,72 са просечним оценама оцењивача на тест скупу. Највећа одступања забележена су код димензије аргументације, где аутоматски систем подцењује квалитет кратких, али добро поткрепљених тврдњи.

title: Cross-Lingual Transfer of Argument Mining Models Between Serbian and Croatian
abstract: We investigate how well argument mining classifiers trained on Serbian data transfer to Croatian and vice versa, exploiting the high lexical and grammatical similarity between the two languages. The experiment uses two balanced corpora of 800 essays each, annotated for argumentative components under the same annotation scheme. We compare three transfer strategies: direct application of the source-language model, vocabulary mapping with shared subword tokenization, and continued pre-training on a small target-language annotated set of 100 essays. Results show that direct transfer yields an average F1 of 0.63 for the four-class scheme, vocabulary mapping raises this to 0.67, and continued pre-training with 100 examples reaches 0.74, approaching the fully supervised in-language baseline of 0.79. The findings suggest that low-resource argument mining for South Slavic varieties can benefit substantially from cross-lingual data sharing without full retraining.

title: Prosodic Borrowing or Independent Development? The Rising Tone in Bunjevac Vernaculars Revisited
abstract: Mid-twentieth-century descriptions of Bunjevac vernaculars in Bačka noted the presence of a short rising tone absent from the inherited neo-Štokavian system. This paper re-examines that tone using data from 31 speakers recorded between 2015 and 2018, combining auditory analysis with acoustic measurements (F0 contour extraction in Praat, time-normalized across 20 ms windows). Results confirm that the rising tone is productively used in 78% of speakers over 60, but only 29% of speakers under 40. Spectral analysis reveals that the youngest speakers produce a variant that is acoustically closer to the Hungarian word-initial high tone than to the reconstructed historical Bunjevac rising tone, suggesting possible re-phonologization under Hungarian influence. An alternative account based on internal tonogenetic processes is also considered and found less consistent with the distributional evidence. The implications for our understanding of prosodic convergence in Pannonian contact zones are discussed.

title: Mapping Vowel Space Compression Across the Bačka Contact Zone: A GIS-Assisted Dialectometric Approach
abstract: This study applies dialectometric methods to acoustic vowel data from 89 speakers sampled at 31 locations across Bačka to produce spatial maps of vowel space compression. Geographic information system (GIS) tools were used to interpolate speaker-level measurements of vowel space area (VSA, computed from F1–F2 coordinates of /a/, /e/, /i/, /o/, /u/) across the survey grid. The resulting maps reveal a clear northeast-to-southwest gradient, with the most compressed vowel spaces concentrated in villages within 15 km of the Hungarian border and in Subotica. The gradient correlates significantly with census-derived estimates of active Hungarian language use (Spearman ρ = −0.73, p < 0.001) but not with distance to the nearest urban center (ρ = −0.19, p = 0.30), isolating contact intensity rather than urbanization as the primary spatial predictor. Three transition zones are identified where VSA values shift abruptly, coinciding with historical administrative boundaries that influenced settlement patterns of the Šokac and Bunjevac populations.
