title: Textbook Representations of Academic Writing in Serbia: A Critical Review of Seven University-Level Manuals
abstract: This article critically examines how academic writing is described and taught in seven university-level Serbian-language writing manuals published between 1998 and 2013. The review assesses how each manual treats genre, metadiscourse, citation conventions, and disciplinary variation. Analysis reveals that the manuals predominantly prescribe a single, discipline-neutral model of academic prose and devote little attention to the rhetorical functions of hedging or the role of metadiscourse in positioning the writer relative to claims and readers. Descriptions of citation practice are largely mechanical and do not address the rhetorical dimension of source use. Three of the seven manuals were found to reproduce, without attribution, definitions and examples from earlier Eastern European writing pedagogy literature. The paper calls for revised instructional frameworks informed by current genre theory and corpus-based descriptions of authentic Serbian academic prose.

title: Bounds on the h*-Vector Coefficients of Lattice Simplices with One Interior Lattice Point
abstract: This paper investigates upper and lower bounds on the coefficients of the h*-vector (Ehrhart h-vector) for lattice simplices of dimension three and four that contain exactly one interior lattice point. Using a combination of direct enumeration via Polymake and analytic arguments based on Ehrhart–Macdonald reciprocity, we classify all such simplices up to unimodular equivalence in dimension three and provide partial results in dimension four. A total of 214 equivalence classes in dimension three are identified and tabulated. For the fourth-dimensional case, we establish that the second coefficient of the h*-vector is bounded above by 11 under the given interior-point constraint, improving a previously known bound of 14 due to general results in the literature. Proof techniques rely on the interplay between the volume of the simplex, the Smith normal form of its vertex matrix, and properties of the associated generating function. All computational results are cross-verified using SageMath scripts made available as supplementary material.

title: Counting Lattice Points in Dilations of Centrally Symmetric Lattice Polytopes
abstract: We study the Ehrhart polynomial of centrally symmetric lattice polytopes in dimensions two through five, with emphasis on the relationship between symmetry constraints and the palindromic property of the h*-vector. For each dimension we enumerate all combinatorial types of centrally symmetric lattice polytopes with vertex coordinates bounded in absolute value by 3, yielding a database of 1 047 distinct polytopes after unimodular equivalence reduction. The palindromic condition on the h*-vector is verified computationally for all entries of the database, consistent with the theoretical prediction for reflexive polytopes in this family. We additionally derive a closed-form expression for the Ehrhart polynomial in the two-dimensional case as a function of the area and the number of boundary lattice points, recovering Pick's theorem as a special case. The paper includes worked examples and a discussion of how the leading coefficient relates to normalised volume computations performed in Polymake.

title: Face Numbers of Three-Dimensional Lattice Polytopes with Bounded Vertex Coordinates
abstract: This work examines the face numbers (f-vectors) of three-dimensional convex lattice polytopes whose vertices have integer coordinates in the box {0,1,...,k}^3 for k ranging from 1 to 5. We generate the full set of combinatorial types in each box using a systematic vertex-set enumeration approach combined with convex hull computation. For k = 4 we find 3 872 distinct combinatorial types, significantly extending earlier tabulations limited to k ≤ 3. The distribution of f-vectors is analysed statistically: the modal polytope type is a triangulated polytope with 8 vertices, 18 edges, and 12 faces. We prove that for lattice polytopes in the k = 2 box, the maximum number of vertices is 18 and the maximum number of faces is 32, both achieved by specific configurations described explicitly. A brief comparison with the continuous (non-lattice) version of the problem via the Upper Bound Theorem highlights differences arising from the integrality constraint.

title: Unimodular Triangulations of Lattice Polygons: An Algorithmic Perspective
abstract: A lattice polygon is said to admit a unimodular triangulation if it can be subdivided into triangles each of unit normalised area using only lattice points on or inside the polygon. We present an algorithmic study of which lattice polygons with at most 12 boundary lattice points and at most 5 interior lattice points admit such triangulations. The algorithm proceeds by iterative stellar subdivision and checks unimodularity via the absolute value of the determinant of each triangle's vertex matrix. Out of 6 214 tested polygons (up to unimodular equivalence), 94.7% admit at least one unimodular triangulation. The remaining 5.3% are catalogued and their obstructions characterised in terms of the position of interior points relative to the boundary. We also provide an integer linear programming formulation of the triangulation existence problem and discuss its practical performance. The polygon database and triangulation scripts are released under an open licence.

title: On the Reflexivity of Lattice Polytopes Arising from 0/1 Matrices
abstract: We investigate convex lattice polytopes defined as the convex hull of the rows of 0/1 matrices of fixed dimensions and examine when such polytopes are reflexive. A polytope is reflexive if its dual is also a lattice polytope; reflexive polytopes appear in mirror symmetry and toric geometry. For m×n matrices with m ≤ n ≤ 5, we enumerate all combinatorial types of the resulting polytopes and test reflexivity by computing the dual polytope in Polymake and checking whether all dual vertices are lattice points. Among the 2 101 distinct polytopes arising from 4×4 matrices, 38 are reflexive. We classify these 38 cases and describe the corresponding matrix structures. The paper also establishes a sufficient condition on the row sum vector of a 0/1 matrix that forces non-reflexivity of the associated polytope, proved by a direct volume argument.

title: A Bayesian sequential test for the two-sample binomial problem with early stopping
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of comparing two binomial proportions in a sequential setting where observations arrive one at a time and early stopping is desirable. We derive a Bayes factor stopping rule based on Beta-Binomial conjugate models and study its operating characteristics through simulation. Experiments with 10,000 replicated trials show that the proposed rule achieves average sample sizes 30–45% smaller than the fixed-sample likelihood ratio test at the same frequentist error rates when the true effect size is moderate (odds ratio 1.5–2.5). We also examine sensitivity to prior hyperparameter choice and propose a straightforward empirical Bayes calibration procedure. The method is illustrated on a web clickthrough dataset with daily traffic of approximately 200 sessions per variant, demonstrating practical applicability in low-traffic digital experiments. Code and simulation scripts are provided as supplementary material.

title: Adaptive allocation in clinical micro-pilots: a Bayesian bandit approach for rare-condition feasibility studies
abstract: Feasibility studies for rare medical conditions often enrol fewer than 50 patients, making standard randomised controlled trial designs inefficient. We propose a Bayesian adaptive allocation scheme based on Thompson sampling with informative priors derived from published meta-analyses. The scheme is evaluated through a simulation study calibrated to three real-world rare-condition contexts (sample sizes 20, 35, and 50) and across a range of true treatment effect magnitudes. Compared to equal randomisation, the adaptive scheme allocates on average 12–19 more patients to the superior arm while maintaining type I error below 0.05. We formalise the stopping criterion using a posterior predictive probability threshold and analyse its sensitivity to prior-data conflict. The paper discusses regulatory considerations for adaptive designs and provides worked examples using conjugate Normal-Normal and Beta-Binomial models. Simulation code is available on a public repository.

title: Numerical verification of the Crooks fluctuation theorem for an overdamped colloidal particle in a time-dependent double-well potential
abstract: We present a detailed numerical study of the Crooks fluctuation theorem (CFT) applied to an overdamped Brownian particle moving in a double-well potential whose barrier height is varied according to a prescribed protocol. The Langevin equation is integrated with an Euler–Maruyama scheme at time steps of 10^−4 dimensionless units over ensembles of 10^5 forward and reverse trajectories. Free-energy differences computed via the CFT are compared against those obtained from thermodynamic integration and Bennett acceptance ratio estimates, showing agreement within 0.3% across a range of switching rates spanning two decades. We document systematic deviations at the fastest switching rates and relate them to the finite relaxation time of the particle relative to the protocol duration. The work distribution is measured to exhibit clear non-Gaussian tails during fast driving. Results confirm that the CFT remains valid even when the work distribution has substantial weight below zero, and we quantify the effective irreversibility as a function of protocol speed.

title: Experimental test of fluctuation-dissipation breakdown in a driven granular gas using a tracer particle
abstract: We report measurements of the effective temperature and the violation of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) in a quasi-two-dimensional driven granular gas. A heavy tracer disk (diameter 15 mm, mass 4.2 g) is immersed in a monolayer of 1200 lighter steel spheres (diameter 3 mm) agitated by a vertically oscillating plate. The velocity autocorrelation function and the linear response to a weak horizontal magnetic force are measured simultaneously. The ratio of the response to the correlation defines the frequency-dependent effective temperature Teff(ω), which exceeds the kinetic temperature by 30–60% across the frequency range 1–50 Hz, demonstrating clear FDT breakdown. The coefficient of restitution is estimated at e = 0.87 ± 0.02 from binary collision videos. Results are compared with predictions from an inelastic Boltzmann–Lorentz equation, showing qualitative agreement but systematic 15% over-prediction of Teff at low frequencies. This constitutes one of the first direct FDT tests in a driven granular system at the single-tracer level.

title: Persistent Betti Numbers as Descriptors of Lorenz-Type Attractors Under Parameter Variation
abstract: We compute zero- and one-dimensional persistent Betti numbers for point clouds sampled from numerically integrated Lorenz-type attractors across a grid of 480 parameter pairs (ρ, σ) with β fixed. Point clouds of 5 000 points each are obtained by fourth-order Runge–Kutta integration with step size 0.001, after discarding a transient of 10 000 steps. Vietoris–Rips filtrations are constructed up to scale ε = 4.0 in increments of 0.05. The resulting persistence diagrams show a sharp increase in the first Betti number β₁ as ρ passes through the classical chaos onset near ρ ≈ 24.7, recovering known bifurcation structure without any prior knowledge of the vector field. Inter-diagram distances measured by the Wasserstein W₂ metric provide a one-dimensional summary curve that tracks bifurcations with a resolution comparable to the largest Lyapunov exponent. Computational cost per diagram averages 14 seconds on a single core. The study establishes a baseline for using persistence diagrams as parameter-space fingerprints of three-dimensional autonomous flows.

title: Classification of Electrochemical Oscillation Modes Using Persistence Landscape Features
abstract: Electrochemical oscillations in platinum-electrolyte systems display several distinct modes—simple periodic, mixed-mode, and chaotic—whose classification from raw current time series is non-trivial. We record current time series at 2 kHz sampling rate during potentiostatic experiments at 17 distinct applied potentials, with 30 replicates per potential, yielding 510 time series of length 60 000 points each. Reconstructed attractors are obtained by time-delay embedding with m = 5 and τ selected by mutual information. Persistence landscapes in dimension one are computed on Vietoris–Rips filtrations and discretised on a common grid of 200 points to produce feature vectors. A linear support vector machine trained on 70% of the data achieves 91.4% classification accuracy on the held-out 30%, outperforming both recurrence-quantification-analysis features (84.2%) and raw power-spectrum features (79.6%). The study demonstrates that persistence landscapes are informative even when oscillation amplitudes differ by less than 3% between classes.

title: Road traffic noise levels along the main arterials of Novi Sad: a baseline measurement campaign
abstract: This study presents results from a systematic noise measurement campaign conducted at 38 roadside locations along six major arterials in Novi Sad during 2009–2010. Equivalent continuous sound pressure levels (LAeq) were recorded over 48-hour periods using calibrated Class 1 sound level meters at 4 m height. Measured Lday and Lnight values ranged from 62 to 79 dB(A) and 54 to 71 dB(A), respectively. Traffic volume and composition data were collected simultaneously using manual counts and a pneumatic tube counter at six cross-sections. The results revealed that heavy goods vehicles contributed disproportionately to night-time levels despite representing only 14% of total flow. Measured values were compared against the default predictions of the NMPB-Routes method, and systematic overestimation of up to 3.2 dB(A) was found in street-canyon geometries. The dataset established a reference baseline for subsequent modelling studies in the city.
venue: Journal of Road and Transport Research

title: Calibration of COPERT IV emission factors for the Serbian passenger car fleet under urban driving conditions
abstract: National average COPERT IV emission factors are derived from European fleet compositions that differ substantially from those in Serbia. This paper reports a calibration exercise based on real-world fuel consumption records and instantaneous speed profiles collected from 62 instrumented vehicles representing the five most common engine-size categories in the Serbian fleet. Remote sensing measurements at two urban checkpoints provided additional CO and NOₓ concentration data for cross-validation. Corrected emission factors for CO, NOₓ, PM₁₀, and hydrocarbons were derived by minimising residuals between modelled and tunnel-measured concentrations in a 310 m urban tunnel section. The adjusted factors differed from standard COPERT IV values by between −8% and +31% depending on pollutant and speed bin. The resulting calibrated set is intended for use in Serbian urban dispersion modelling studies and is provided as a supplementary dataset.

title: Strategic noise mapping for Novi Sad: application of the END directive methodology to a mid-sized Pannonian city
abstract: The European Environmental Noise Directive requires agglomerations above 100 000 inhabitants to produce strategic noise maps at five-year intervals. This paper describes the production of the first research-grade strategic noise map for Novi Sad using SoundPlan 7.4, a digital terrain model at 1 m resolution, and hourly traffic volumes disaggregated by vehicle class for the morning, afternoon, and night periods. Road centreline geometry was derived from a municipal GIS database and supplemented with building footprint data. The resulting Lden map shows that approximately 38 000 residents are exposed to levels above 65 dB(A) Lden, with the highest values concentrated along the Futoška and Bulevar Oslobođenja corridors. Uncertainty was estimated through a Monte Carlo propagation of input variability, yielding a 95% confidence interval of ±1.8 dB(A) for grid cells adjacent to the road. The maps were made available to the city planning authority.

title: Influence of road surface texture on tyre–road noise emission at low speeds in urban areas
abstract: Tyre–road interaction noise dominates above approximately 50 km/h but remains significant at lower urban speeds on coarse aggregate surfaces. This study compared noise emissions on four pavement types—dense bituminous macadam, stone mastic asphalt, porous asphalt, and concrete—at a standardised test section on the Novi Sad ring road. Close-proximity measurements were carried out for four representative vehicle categories at speeds of 30, 50, and 70 km/h following ISO 11819-2 procedures. Porous asphalt yielded reductions of 3.1–4.7 dB(A) relative to dense macadam depending on vehicle category and speed. Temperature correction using the CPX reference method was applied to normalise all results to 20 °C. Statistical analysis showed that surface type explained 61% of the variance in measured noise levels when controlling for speed and vehicle category. The findings are discussed in the context of the cost-effectiveness of pavement renewal as a noise mitigation measure.

title: Roadside PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅ concentrations near a signalised intersection: measurements and AERMOD simulation
abstract: Traffic-generated particulate matter concentrations vary considerably at short distances from intersections owing to stop-and-go acceleration patterns. This study reports a six-week roadside monitoring campaign at a high-flow signalised intersection in central Novi Sad, using two co-located optical particle counters and one reference gravimetric sampler. Simultaneous video-based traffic counts provided vehicle flow and composition at one-minute resolution. Measured PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅ 24-hour average concentrations exceeded the Serbian threshold on 9 and 4 days respectively during the campaign period. AERMOD was run with a line-source geometry and the calibrated emission factors from a previous study; modelled-to-measured ratios averaged 0.91 for PM₁₀ and 0.87 for PM₂.₅. A sensitivity analysis showed that emission factor uncertainty dominated total prediction uncertainty, contributing roughly 55% of the variance. The paper discusses implications for siting of regulatory monitoring stations.

title: Population-weighted noise exposure indicators for Serbian cities: a comparative analysis of Novi Sad, Niš, and Kragujevac
abstract: Existing noise assessments in Serbia are typically reported as grid-averaged levels without weighting by actual residential population density. This paper introduces population-weighted exposure indicators (PWEL) derived by overlaying strategic noise maps with the 2011 census grid for three Serbian cities with populations between 170 000 and 290 000. The GIS overlay procedure linked 250 m × 250 m population grid cells to modelled Lden values from SoundPlan runs conducted independently for each city. Results show that PWEL_Lden values were 1.4 to 3.1 dB(A) lower than simple area-averaged levels owing to the concentration of population away from the busiest arterials. Kragujevac showed the highest PWEL despite having the lowest total road network length, attributable to a denser residential layout adjacent to industrial access routes. The indicator is proposed as a candidate metric for national reporting under the Environmental Noise Directive.

title: Dispersion modelling of NOₓ along a 4 km urban corridor under different traffic management scenarios
abstract: This study evaluates the effect of three traffic management interventions—a 40 km/h speed limit, adaptive signal coordination, and a freight delivery time window—on roadside NOₓ concentrations along a 4 km arterial corridor in Novi Sad. Hourly vehicle flows and speed profiles were generated with a microsimulation model calibrated to observed counts, and NOₓ emission rates were computed using calibrated COPERT-derived factors. Dispersion was simulated with AERMOD using a 50 m receptor grid at 1.5 m height over a full calendar year of meteorological data from Rimski Šančevi station. The 40 km/h scenario reduced annual mean NOₓ at the nearest receptor row by 9%, whereas adaptive signal coordination achieved 14% and the freight time window 7%. Combining all three measures yielded a 21% reduction. The paper discusses the trade-off between NOₓ reductions and predicted increases in CO₂ from slower speeds.

title: Annoyance and sleep disturbance from road traffic noise in residential areas of Novi Sad: a social survey
abstract: A cross-sectional social survey was conducted in four residential neighbourhoods of Novi Sad in autumn 2019, collecting responses from 612 adults on self-reported noise annoyance and sleep disturbance attributable to road traffic. Questionnaire design followed the ISO/TS 15666 standard. Respondents' addresses were geocoded and matched to modelled Lden and Lnight values from the city's strategic noise map. Logistic regression showed that the probability of high annoyance (score ≥ 72 on the ICBEN scale) increased significantly above Lden = 60 dB(A), with an odds ratio of 2.4 per 5 dB(A) increment. Sleep disturbance showed a steeper dose–response above Lnight = 50 dB(A). Socioeconomic status and window orientation were significant confounders. The derived dose–response curves are compared with WHO 2018 reference curves and are broadly consistent but shifted by approximately 2 dB(A) toward higher tolerance.

title: Combined noise and air pollution exposure index for urban traffic corridors: methodology and application
abstract: Noise and air pollution are typically assessed in isolation despite sharing common sources and jointly affecting human health. This book chapter presents a combined exposure index (CEI) that merges normalised noise (Lden) and PM₂.₅ annual mean concentration into a single dimensionless score using equal-weight linear combination after normalisation to WHO guideline levels. The method is applied to a 22 km network of primary arterials in Novi Sad, producing a corridor-level ranking of environmental burden. Results show that seven corridor segments exceed the CEI threshold of 1.0 set at simultaneous exceedance of both WHO guidelines. The index is computed in a GIS environment and is designed to support prioritisation of mitigation investments. Sensitivity of corridor rankings to the relative weighting of the two components is tested, showing that rank order is stable for weight ratios between 0.3 and 0.7. Limitations related to spatial resolution mismatch between noise grids and dispersion model outputs are discussed.
venue: Urban Environmental Burden Assessment: Methods and Case Studies (Springer Transport Series)

title: Low-cost sensor networks for traffic-related air pollution monitoring: performance evaluation under Pannonian climate conditions
abstract: Low-cost electrochemical and optical sensors offer spatially dense monitoring at a fraction of the cost of reference instruments but require rigorous field characterisation. This study evaluated five sensor platforms—measuring NO₂, O₃, PM₁₀, and PM₂.₅—deployed at six roadside and two urban-background sites in Novi Sad over a 12-month period spanning all four seasons. Sensor readings were collocated with a reference TEOM for particulate matter and a chemiluminescence analyser for NO₂ at one site. Correction factors derived from linear regression with reference instruments reduced PM₂.₅ root-mean-square error from 18.4 to 6.1 µg/m³. Performance degraded significantly during summer fog events, with sensor-to-reference ratios reaching 2.3 for PM₁₀. Temperature and relative humidity explained 34% of residual variance after primary correction. Practical guidance on maintenance intervals and correction model transferability is provided for transport research groups considering similar deployments.

title: Effect of electric bus introduction on corridor-level PM and noise exposure: a scenario analysis for two Novi Sad bus lines
abstract: The replacement of diesel buses with battery-electric buses (BEBs) is expected to reduce both exhaust emissions and, to a lesser degree, traffic noise. This paper models the impact of converting two high-frequency bus lines in Novi Sad—lines 4 and 11A—to BEBs under three fleet replacement scenarios: 25%, 50%, and 100% BEB share. Emission factors for diesel buses follow calibrated COPERT values; BEB emission factors account for tyre and brake wear only. Dispersion of PM₁₀ along the 6.2 km shared corridor was simulated with AERMOD; noise was modelled in SoundPlan using measured BEB drive-by levels from a comparable deployment in Subotica. Full replacement reduced annual mean roadside PM₁₀ by 17% and Lden by 1.1 dB(A) at the nearest facades. The noise benefit is modest because diesel buses account for only 8% of total traffic flow on the corridor, while the PM reduction is more pronounced owing to the high linear density of bus stops.

title: Mapping cumulative health burden from traffic noise and PM₂.₅ using disability-adjusted life years: a pilot study for Novi Sad
abstract: Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) provide a common currency for comparing health burdens from different environmental stressors. This preprint presents a DALY-based health impact assessment for road-traffic-related noise and PM₂.₅ exposure in Novi Sad using 2021 population census data and updated dispersion and noise maps. Noise-attributable DALYs were estimated following the WHO QALY-to-DALY conversion approach for ischaemic heart disease and cognitive impairment in children; PM₂.₅-attributable DALYs followed the GBD concentration-response functions for cardiopulmonary disease and lung cancer. Total estimated annual burden was 1 840 DALYs (95% CI: 1 210–2 630), of which PM₂.₅ contributed approximately 58% and noise 42%. Spatial analysis identified three hotspot census tracts in the northern industrial buffer zone and along the Futog road where combined per-capita burden exceeded the 95th percentile. The methodology and input data are shared openly to support replication.

title: Rolling-Horizon Replanning Intervals in Urban Parcel Delivery: Effect on Solution Quality and Driver Workload
abstract: This study examines how the choice of replanning interval—ranging from two to thirty minutes—affects route quality and operational disruption in a rolling-horizon framework for urban parcel delivery. A simulation experiment is conducted on a synthetic city network with 40 vehicles and up to 350 dynamically arriving requests per shift, calibrated using data from a Novi Sad courier operator. Solution quality is measured by total travelled distance and number of late deliveries; driver workload is approximated by the frequency of route modification events. Results indicate that intervals between eight and twelve minutes offer a practical compromise: late deliveries drop by 22 % relative to static planning, while drivers receive on average 3.1 route revisions per shift. Shorter intervals below four minutes yield marginal quality improvements at the cost of significantly higher dispatch overhead.

title: Fleet Assignment Under Stochastic Travel Times: A Chance-Constrained Formulation for the Multi-Depot Case
abstract: The paper formulates the multi-depot fleet assignment problem under stochastic travel times as a chance-constrained mixed-integer programme. Travel time distributions on each arc are estimated from six months of GPS data and approximated as log-normal. The chance constraint requires that the probability of a vehicle violating its depot return time does not exceed 5 %. Two solution strategies are compared: sample average approximation with 200 scenarios and a deterministic equivalent obtained by replacing stochastic arcs with their 95th-percentile values. On a test bed of 48 instances derived from a regional food distribution network with three depots and 12 to 24 vehicles, sample average approximation yields solutions 4.1 % less conservative in total fleet cost than the deterministic equivalent, at the expense of roughly four times longer computation. The model is implemented in Python using an open-source MILP solver.

title: Time-of-Day Variation in Public Transport Accessibility: Evidence from Continuous Isochrone Sampling
abstract: Most accessibility studies use one or two representative departure times, potentially masking large intra-day variation. This paper samples 30-minute isochrone areas from a fixed set of 50 residential origin points in Novi Sad at every 10-minute interval between 05:00 and 23:00 on weekdays, Saturdays, and Sundays, using a GTFS feed validated against on-board passenger counts from autumn 2017. The resulting dataset contains 8,280 isochrone polygons. Results show that the coefficient of variation in reachable area across departure times exceeds 0.45 for origins in outer districts, compared with 0.18 for origins near the main corridor. Sunday midday accessibility in peripheral zones is on average 41% lower than weekday peak accessibility. The paper provides a methodological template and openly releases the sampling scripts and aggregated isochrone dataset under a CC-BY licence.

title: Macroscopic Traffic Simulation Models for Corridor Planning: Calibration Principles and Practice
abstract: This book chapter provides a practitioner-oriented account of calibration workflows for LWR and cell-transmission models applied to inter-urban corridor planning. It covers data requirements, including minimum counting station density (recommended: one station per 8–12 km for rural motorways), acceptable loop detector fault rates, and floating car sample-size rules of thumb. The chapter reviews objective functions used in calibration—GEH, RMSPE, and mean absolute error—and discusses their respective sensitivities to peak and off-peak conditions. Two worked examples using anonymised Vojvodina corridor datasets illustrate iterative parameter adjustment. Common failure modes—including overfitting to a single day's data and neglecting the effect of incident-induced capacity drops—are discussed with reference to published validation studies. The chapter is aimed at transport engineers in regional planning agencies who use commercial packages but need to understand the underlying model behaviour.

title: Freight Mode Choice Between Road and Inland Waterway in the Middle Danube Region: A Review of Empirical Evidence
abstract: Research on freight mode choice along the Middle Danube has been conducted intermittently since the mid-1990s, but findings are fragmented across national reports, grey literature, and conference papers not easily accessible to an international audience. This chapter synthesises 34 empirical studies published or circulated between 1995 and 2020, covering Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Serbia, and Romania. The review distinguishes between aggregate models fitted to traffic count data, disaggregate models using shipper surveys, and simulation-based approaches. Key findings include a persistent underestimation of road haulage competitiveness in aggregate models relative to survey-based disaggregate estimates, and near-universal identification of reliability and transit time as the two attributes with the largest shipper willingness-to-pay values. Methodological issues including endogeneity of price in revealed preference data and the absence of cross-country comparable datasets are discussed. Directions for coordinated survey efforts are proposed.

title: Uticaj geometrije prozorskog otvora na godišnje pokazatelje dnevnog osvetljenja u kancelarijama u Novom Sadu
abstract: Rad ispituje kako se promenom odnosa površine prozora i spoljašnjeg zida (WWR) u rasponu 20–60% menjaju vrednosti sDA300/50% i ASE1000,250h u tipičnoj kancelarijskoj osnovi dubine 9 m, orijentisanoj ka jugu i severu, u klimatskim uslovima Novog Sada. Simulacije su izvršene u Daysim-u korišćenjem lokalne EnergyPlus meteorološke datoteke za period 2000–2010. Definisano je šest scenarija sa fiksnim unutrašnjim roletama (refleksija 0,55) i bez zaštite od sunca. Rezultati pokazuju da se pri WWR od 40% postiže sDA iznad 55% korisne površine za južnu orijentaciju, ali istovremeno ASE premašuje preporučenu granicu od 10% površine pri WWR ≥ 50%. Za severnu orijentaciju ASE ostaje ispod praga u svim scenarijima, dok sDA ne prelazi 48% ni pri najvećem WWR. Rad zaključuje da optimalni WWR za južnu fasadu u datoj klimi iznosi oko 35–38%, uz obaveznu primenu spoljnih ili međuprostornih senila.

title: Validation of a Simplified Radiance Model Against Physical Scale-Model Measurements Under Overcast Sky Conditions in Novi Sad
abstract: Accurate climate-based daylight simulation requires validated models calibrated for local sky conditions. This paper compares illuminance predictions from a Radiance-based simulation model against physical measurements taken inside a 1:20 scale model of a generic open-plan office placed under a calibrated artificial sky dome at the Faculty of Technical Sciences laboratory in Novi Sad. Measurements were recorded at 15 sensor points across the floor plane under CIE overcast sky with a horizontal illuminance of 10,000 lux. The simulation used Perez sky model parameters derived from the same diffuse and global radiation input. Across all sensor positions, the mean absolute percentage error was 8.3%, with the largest deviations (up to 14%) occurring within 0.5 m of the window wall. Sensors in the rear third of the 8 m deep plan showed errors below 6%. The results confirm that the simplified model is adequate for annual daylight metric calculations beyond the immediate perimeter zone, and a correction factor of 0.92 is proposed for the first 1 m band.

title: Poređenje algoritama za upravljanje pokretnim lamelama u kancelarijama prema kriterijumima sDA i vizuelnog komfora
abstract: Rad poredi tri algoritma za automatsko upravljanje horizontalnim lamelama zastakljene fasade u kancelarijskom prostoru dubine 10 m u Novom Sadu: algoritam baziran na praćenju sunčevog ugla (sun-tracking), algoritam zasnovan na merenju unutrašnje rasvetljenosti na radnoj površini (closed-loop illuminance) i statički godišnji profil ugla nagiba određen optimizacijom. Simulacije su sprovedene u Daysim-u za 8 760 vremenskih koraka, koristeći TMY datoteku dobijenu iz meteoroloških podataka IMGW instituta za centralnoevropski region. Analizirano je 12 fasadnih scenarija kombinovanjem tri orijentacije (jug, jugoistok, istok) i četiri geometrije lamela (dubina 25–80 mm, razmak 60–120 mm). Sun-tracking algoritam postiže najviše vrednosti sDA (do 68%) na južnoj fasadi, ali generiše i najveći ASE (do 17%). Statički profil pokazuje uravnoteženije rezultate: sDA 58%, ASE 9% za južnu orijentaciju. Closed-loop pristup daje konzistentno niske ASE vrednosti (ispod 8%) uz sDA od 54–61% u zavisnosti od orijentacije.

title: Annual Daylight Performance of Electrochromic Glazing in Deep-Plan Offices: A Parametric Study for the Pannonian Climate Zone
abstract: Electrochromic glazing offers stepless or multi-state visible transmittance modulation without movable parts. This study evaluates the annual daylight performance of a four-state electrochromic glazing system (Tvis: 0.06, 0.18, 0.42, 0.60) applied to the south and west façades of a 12 m deep open-plan office in Novi Sad, Serbia (45.3° N). A parametric matrix of 48 configurations was generated by varying sill height (0.8–1.1 m), head height (2.4–2.9 m), and glazing width (3–6 m). Simulations were run in Daysim 4.0 using a TMY weather file derived from the Serbian Hydrometeorological Institute dataset for 1990–2015. A rule-based control logic switched glazing states at 15-minute intervals based on exterior vertical solar irradiance thresholds. Results show that the four-state system achieves sDA300/50% above 60% for 71% of the parametric configurations on the south façade while keeping ASE1000,250h below 10% in 88% of cases. On the west façade, ASE compliance drops to 61% of configurations due to low-angle afternoon sun. The study identifies head height as the dominant geometric variable for sDA performance (Pearson r = 0.71).

title: Uticaj unutrašnje refleksivnosti površina na distribuciju dnevnog svetla u dubokim kancelarijskim osnovama — parametarska studija za klimu Vojvodine
abstract: Distribucija dnevnog osvetljenja u dubokim kancelarijskim prostorima značajno zavisi od sposobnosti unutrašnjih površina da reflektuju i redistribuiraju svetlost. Ovaj rad kvantifikuje uticaj kombinacija refleksivnosti stropa (0,70–0,90), zidova (0,40–0,70) i poda (0,15–0,35) na vrednosti sDA300/50% i uniformnost rasvetljenosti (u50/u10 odnos) u kancelarijama dubine 10 i 14 m u Novom Sadu. Parametarska matrica od 108 slučajeva simulirana je u Radiance/Daysim okruženju. Rezultati pokazuju da povećanje refleksivnosti stropa sa 0,70 na 0,90 povećava sDA za 4,5–7,2 procentnih poena u zadnjoj trećini prostora (zona 7–10 m od fasade), dok uticaj refleksivnosti poda ne prelazi 2 procentna poena ni u jednoj zoni. Visoka refleksivnost zidova (0,70) doprinosi ujednačenijoj distribuciji, ali kod južnih fasada može pogoršati ASE za 1,5–3 procentna poena u perimeternoj zoni. Rad predlaže preporučene opsege refleksivnosti za projektovanje kancelarija u klimatskim uslovima Vojvodine.

title: Occupant Satisfaction and Measured Illuminance in Offices with Automated Blind Systems: A Post-Occupancy Study in Three Buildings in Novi Sad
abstract: Simulation-based daylight metrics do not always align with occupant experience. This paper reports a post-occupancy study conducted in three office buildings in Novi Sad equipped with automated horizontal venetian blind systems, covering a total of 214 workstations. Point-in-time illuminance measurements were taken at 08:00, 11:00, and 15:00 on clear, intermediate, and overcast sky days over four representative weeks across two seasons (March–April and September–October 2022). An anonymous questionnaire on glare discomfort, visual satisfaction, and perceived productivity was administered to 178 occupants. Median measured illuminance at the task plane ranged from 310 to 720 lux depending on position and sky condition. Reported glare discomfort was highest (42% of respondents) on clear-sky afternoons at west-facing workstations despite the automated blind being active, suggesting the control setpoint of 50 W/m² vertical solar irradiance was insufficient for low-angle incidence. Correlation between measured sDA compliance (evaluated retroactively from annual simulation) and occupant satisfaction scores was moderate (Spearman ρ = 0.54), indicating that sDA alone is not a complete predictor of subjective visual comfort in these buildings.

title: Coupled Thermal–Daylight Optimisation of External Shading Fins on South Façades: Trade-offs Between sDA, ASE, and Cooling Energy Demand in Novi Sad
abstract: External vertical and horizontal fins affect both solar heat gain and daylight availability, creating trade-offs that are rarely quantified together. This paper presents a coupled simulation approach linking EnergyPlus for thermal calculations and Daysim for annual daylight metrics, applied to a reference south-facing office module (6 × 10 m, 2.8 m floor-to-ceiling) in Novi Sad. A genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) explored 1,200 combinations of fin depth (0.2–0.8 m), fin spacing (0.6–1.8 m), and fin angle (vertical to 30° tilted). Pareto-optimal solutions were identified for three objective pairs: maximising sDA while minimising ASE; minimising cooling energy while maintaining sDA above 55%; and a three-objective case. Results show that horizontal fins of 0.5 m depth at 1.2 m spacing reduce cooling demand by 18% relative to no shading while achieving sDA of 57% and ASE of 8.2%. Adding a 10° southward tilt to the same geometry improves sDA by 3.1 percentage points at the cost of a 1.8% cooling energy increase. The dataset and Grasshopper definition are available in the supplementary materials.

title: Primena LEED v4.1 i EN 17037 metrika u kontekstu srpskog klimatskog prostora: komparativna analiza zahteva i diskrepancije u vrednovanju dnevnog osvetljenja
abstract: LEED v4.1 i evropski standard EN 17037 uvode različite pristupe vrednovanju dnevnog osvetljenja: LEED koristi sDA i ASE kao godišnje klimatski zasnovane pokazatelje, dok EN 17037 propisuje minimalnu i ciljnu rasvetljenost (300/500 lux) za izabrane reprezentativne datume. Ovaj rad poredi rezultate primene oba sistema na identičan skup od šest kancelarijskih prostora u Novom Sadu koji variraju po dubini (8, 10, 12 m), orijentaciji (jug, sever) i tipu fasade (fiksne lamele, pokretne lamele, bez zaštite). Simulacije za LEED kriterijume sprovedene su u Daysim-u (godišnja TMY analiza), a za EN 17037 u Radiance-u za dva reprezentativna dana (21. mart, 21. jun). Rezultati pokazuju da prostori koji zadovoljavaju EN 17037 minimum ne zadovoljavaju LEED sDA kriterijum u 3 od 6 slučajeva za severnu orijentaciju, dok svi prostori koji zadovoljavaju LEED sDA istovremeno zadovoljavaju EN 17037 cilj. Diskrepancija je najveća u prostorijama sa pokretnim lamelama, gde EN 17037 pretpostavlja otvorenu poziciju lamela na reprezentativne datume. Rad predlaže smernice za usaglašenu primenu oba standarda u srpskoj regulativi.

title: Spatial Organisation of Šokac Farmsteads in the Bačka Region: A Typological Survey Based on Late Nineteenth-Century Cadastral Records
abstract: This study examines the spatial layout of 214 farmsteads attributed to the Šokac population in four cadastral municipalities in the central Bačka region, using digitised cadastral plans from the 1880–1895 survey held in the Vojvodina Archive. Plot dimensions, building footprints, courtyard arrangements, and the positioning of ancillary structures were recorded and classified into five recurring layout types. Field verification visits to 38 surviving properties confirmed the persistence of two dominant typological patterns characterised by a linear sequence of dwelling, storage, and stable along the plot axis. Measurements showed median plot widths of 14–18 metres and depths reaching 60–90 metres, consistent with the strip-lot system of planned colonisation settlements. The study identifies a correlation between plot depth and the number of ancillary buildings, suggesting incremental densification over successive generations. Results are compared with contemporaneous survey data from the Baranya and Slavonia regions, highlighting both shared Pannonian characteristics and local variations attributable to soil type and market-town proximity.

title: Segment Angular Analysis as a Predictor of Pedestrian Route Choice in a Historic Urban Core
abstract: Segment-level analysis with angular weighting has been shown to outperform classic axial integration in predicting vehicular movement in some European cities. This paper tests whether the same advantage holds for pedestrian route choice in the Novi Sad historic core. Using GPS traces from 124 volunteer participants recruited over four weeks in spring 2015, observed routes were compared to shortest-path and least-angle predictions generated from a segment model of 1,087 segments. The least-angle model correctly predicted more than 60 percent of observed route segments, compared to 51 percent for the topological shortest-path model. The improvement was strongest on routes longer than 400 metres. However, for trips originating from the central market, the route choice was dominated by the direct visibility to the destination rather than angular minimisation, suggesting a context dependency that aggregate models do not capture. Practical implications for pedestrian signage placement are discussed.

title: Effect of mortar joint geometry and composition on measured vapour diffusion resistance of historic brick masonry: specimen-scale study
abstract: Mortar joints in historic brick masonry differ in geometry and composition from modern jointwork, and their vapour transport properties are rarely measured independently. Thirty-six masonry specimens (240 mm × 240 mm × 115 mm) were assembled using replicated nineteenth-century Vojvodina bricks and three mortar formulations—hydraulic lime, natural cement, and gypsum-lime—with joint thicknesses of 10, 14, and 18 mm. Equivalent vapour diffusion resistance factors (μeq) were determined using the wet-cup and dry-cup methods at 23 °C. μeq values ranged from 5.2 to 9.7 across the full specimen set. Joint composition had a larger effect on μeq than joint thickness: gypsum-lime mortars produced values 31 % higher than hydraulic lime at equivalent thickness. A simple mixture rule using area fractions of brick and mortar predicted μeq with a mean absolute error of 9 % across all specimens, which is considered acceptable for HAM simulation input preparation. The results are incorporated into the material property database used by the research group.

title: Locating leaks from pressure sensors and a calibrated hydraulic model
abstract: Unaccounted-for water remains a critical challenge for utilities across Central and Eastern Europe. This paper presents a methodology for pinpointing leak locations in water distribution networks by combining pressure measurements from a sparse sensor network with a calibrated steady-state hydraulic model. A sensitivity matrix is constructed by simulating hypothetical leaks at candidate nodes and computing the resulting pressure deviations across the sensor array. Observed pressure residuals from field measurements are then matched against the matrix columns using a least-squares minimisation procedure, yielding a ranked shortlist of probable leak locations. The method is validated on a real distribution network in a Vojvodina town with approximately 12,000 service connections. Results from seven controlled leak trials demonstrate a mean localisation error of less than 180 metres in 85 % of cases, using only nine permanently installed pressure loggers. Sensitivity to model parameter uncertainty is assessed through Monte Carlo perturbation, showing that calibration quality is the dominant factor controlling localisation accuracy. The proposed approach is computationally lightweight and suitable for real-time deployment on utility SCADA platforms, making it attractive for small and medium-sized water companies with limited budgets for physical inspection campaigns.

title: Pressure management cuts losses in a mid-size town
abstract: Excessive water losses from leakage and pressure-related bursts impose significant financial and environmental costs on urban water utilities. This conference paper reports field results from a pressure management intervention carried out in a mid-size town of roughly 35,000 inhabitants in northern Serbia. Three pressure-reducing valve stations were installed at strategic entry points of pre-defined district metered areas, and target night-time pressures were determined through a minimum night flow analysis combined with hydraulic model simulations. Monitoring over an eighteen-month period following valve commissioning revealed an average reduction in minimum night flow of 28 %, corresponding to an estimated saving of approximately 190,000 cubic metres of treated water per year. Burst frequency also fell by 34 % relative to the two-year pre-intervention baseline. The paper discusses the importance of accurate boundary meter data for isolating genuine leakage savings from apparent losses caused by meter inaccuracies. Lessons learned regarding stakeholder engagement with the local utility are presented, and key performance indicators suitable for regulatory reporting are proposed.

title: District metered area design for a flat-terrain distribution network in Vojvodina
abstract: The flat topography and radially branched pipe layouts typical of Vojvodina towns pose specific challenges for district metered area delineation that are not adequately addressed by methods developed for hilly or grid-based networks. This paper proposes a graph-partitioning procedure adapted to low-relief conditions, in which a weighted undirected pipe network graph is partitioned using a spectral clustering algorithm. Weighting accounts for pipe diameter, hydraulic head loss per unit length, and proximity to existing boundary meter infrastructure. The procedure is applied to the distribution network of a Vojvodina municipality with approximately 8,500 connections, yielding six district metered areas with balanced demand loads and hydraulically isolated boundaries. Hydraulic model simulations confirm that the proposed zoning maintains minimum nodal pressures above the regulatory threshold of 2.5 bar at peak demand, while reducing average zone pressure by 0.6 bar compared to the undivided network. Metering costs for the proposed layout are estimated and compared with two alternative configurations generated by manual engineering judgment. The paper concludes with a sensitivity analysis examining how demand growth projections over a ten-year horizon affect zone hydraulic performance and recommends a phased implementation strategy for cash-constrained utilities.

title: Calibration of hydraulic models using automated meter infrastructure data
abstract: Hydraulic model calibration traditionally relies on dedicated field measurement campaigns that are expensive and logistically demanding. The widespread deployment of automated meter infrastructure in Serbian water utilities creates a new opportunity to harvest demand data at fine temporal resolution for continuous model updating. This paper presents a calibration workflow in which hourly consumption data from smart meters are aggregated to district metered area level and used alongside pressure logger readings to estimate nodal demand multipliers and pipe roughness coefficients via a gradient-based optimisation algorithm. The procedure is implemented for a network of 6,200 connections and tested against an independent dataset of fire-flow hydrant tests not used during calibration. Calibrated model predictions of static pressure match observed values with a mean absolute error of 0.08 bar, compared with 0.31 bar for the uncalibrated base model. The paper also evaluates model performance degradation over time as infrastructure ages, finding that re-calibration every six to nine months is sufficient to maintain acceptable accuracy for operational decision-making. Practical guidance is offered on handling common data quality issues including meter drop-outs, reverse-flow readings, and clock synchronisation errors.

title: Minimum night flow analysis under varying diurnal demand patterns in small Serbian towns
abstract: Minimum night flow analysis is widely used to estimate background leakage in water distribution networks, yet standard reference values for legitimate night-time consumption per connection were derived predominantly from Western European cities. This paper investigates whether those reference values are transferable to small Serbian towns, which exhibit distinct household water use patterns driven by differences in building stock, garden irrigation practices, and commercial activity profiles. Continuous flow data from nineteen district metered areas across seven municipalities in Vojvodina, covering a combined total of 47,000 service connections, were collected over twelve-month monitoring periods. Statistical analysis reveals that legitimate night-time consumption per connection in this context averages 0.47 litres per connection per hour, approximately 15 % lower than the commonly cited UK reference figure. Seasonal variation is also more pronounced, with summer irrigation creating secondary night-time demand peaks that can mask leakage signals if analysis is confined to winter months only. Revised reference values and a practical protocol for selecting suitable analysis nights are proposed. Application of the revised values to the monitored areas reduces estimated leakage by an average of 11 % compared with calculations using unadjusted international benchmarks, with implications for prioritisation of network rehabilitation investments.

title: Step-testing protocol for sequential leak localisation in district metered areas
abstract: Step testing is a well-established operational technique for narrowing the search zone for leaks in water distribution networks, yet the sequence in which isolation valves are closed has a large effect on the information gained per test and the disruption caused to consumers. This paper formulates valve closure sequencing as a binary integer programme that maximises the expected reduction in suspect pipe length per step while constraining the number of properties affected by pressure drops below a service standard threshold. The optimised sequences are compared against conventional heuristic ordering on five test networks drawn from Vojvodina municipalities of varying size and topology. On average, the optimised protocol reaches a leak localisation accuracy of ±150 metres in 40 % fewer valve operations than the heuristic approach. A simplified greedy heuristic that approximates the integer programme solution is also presented for use by field teams without access to optimisation software. The paper provides guidance on integrating step-testing results with model-based localisation estimates to further reduce the pipe length requiring physical inspection. Safety considerations relating to transient pressure surges during rapid sequential valve closures are discussed, along with mitigation measures.

title: Pressure transient analysis for leak detection: applicability in low-velocity rural mains
abstract: Transient-based leak detection exploits the reflection of pressure waves from discontinuities, including leaks, in pipe systems. Most published work on this technique addresses high-velocity transmission mains, whereas rural distribution networks in Vojvodina operate at characteristically low flow velocities and contain numerous small-diameter lateral branches that can scatter and attenuate transient signals. This paper reports laboratory experiments on a 120-metre pipe rig assembled to replicate the hydraulic characteristics of a rural main, including T-junctions and diameter transitions representative of Vojvodina infrastructure. Controlled leaks of 0.1 to 1.5 litres per second were introduced at known locations, and pressure transients were generated by rapid valve actuation. Wavelet decomposition was applied to the recorded pressure traces to isolate leak-reflected signals from junction-reflected noise. For straight pipe segments exceeding 60 metres in length, leak reflection signals were identifiable for leak rates as low as 0.3 litres per second with signal-to-noise ratios above 4 dB. Accuracy of localisation within identified segments was within ±8 metres. Limitations arising from air entrainment and plastic pipe viscoelasticity are characterised, and practical recommendations for field application in rural Vojvodina mains are provided.

title: Water loss reduction in Vojvodina: a comparative review of utility performance over two decades
abstract: This book chapter surveys published data and utility annual reports covering water loss indicators across Vojvodina municipalities from 2002 to 2022, offering the most comprehensive longitudinal analysis of the region to date. The chapter traces the adoption of the International Water Association water balance methodology by Serbian utilities and evaluates the reliability of reported non-revenue water figures, noting that inconsistent accounting practices complicate direct inter-utility comparisons in the early part of the study period. Normalised performance indicators including infrastructure leakage index and litres per service connection per day are reconstructed where sufficient data exist, allowing more meaningful benchmarking. A clear improvement trend is observed from approximately 2012 onwards, coinciding with increased EU pre-accession funding for infrastructure rehabilitation. However, median infrastructure leakage index values in 2022 remain above 3.0, indicating substantial remaining potential for loss reduction. Case studies of three utilities that achieved notable performance improvements are examined in depth, revealing common success factors including sustained pressure management, systematic active leakage control, and investment in automated meter infrastructure. The chapter closes with a policy discussion directed at the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry.

title: Sensor placement optimisation for leak detection in branched rural networks
abstract: The cost-effectiveness of pressure-based leak detection is strongly influenced by the number and placement of permanently installed pressure sensors. Existing sensor placement methods typically assume looped network topologies and may perform poorly when applied to the predominantly branched pipe layouts found in rural Vojvodina. This paper proposes a sensor placement optimisation framework tailored to branched networks, using a modified maximum coverage model in which each candidate sensor location is evaluated by the number of distinct leak scenarios it can distinguish given a specified pressure measurement resolution. A simulated annealing metaheuristic is employed to explore the combinatorial solution space for networks with up to 400 candidate nodes. The framework is applied to three real branched networks in Vojvodina villages, and the resulting optimal placements are compared against placements generated by hydraulic sensitivity analysis and by uniform spatial distribution. The proposed method achieves equivalent leak detectability to the hydraulic sensitivity approach while using on average 22 % fewer sensors, representing a meaningful capital cost saving for small rural utilities. The paper also quantifies how the optimal number of sensors scales with network size and branching density, providing practitioners with a simple sizing rule for preliminary budgeting.

title: Effect of moisture content and barrel temperature on expansion ratio and texture of extruded triticale flour
abstract: Twin-screw extrusion of whole-meal triticale flour was conducted at three moisture levels (14, 17, and 20 g/100 g) and barrel temperature profiles ranging from 120 °C to 180 °C in the metering zone. Expansion ratio, bulk density, hardness, and specific mechanical energy (SME) were measured for each combination. Expansion ratio peaked at 17% moisture and 160 °C, reaching a value of 4.8, while hardness followed an inverse trend (minimum 18 N at the same condition). SME decreased monotonically with increasing moisture, from 312 kJ/kg at 14% to 187 kJ/kg at 20%. X-ray microtomography revealed a closed-cell foam structure at intermediate moisture that became open and irregular at 20% moisture. Results suggest that a narrow moisture–temperature window exists for triticale that differs substantially from wheat-based benchmarks reported in the literature, primarily because of the lower gluten network strength in triticale endosperm.

title: In vitro starch digestibility of extruded sorghum snacks: influence of amylose-to-amylopectin ratio and processing temperature
abstract: Two sorghum varieties differing in amylose content (22% and 34%) were extruded at barrel temperatures of 140, 160, and 180 °C using a co-rotating twin-screw extruder. In vitro starch digestibility was assessed using a modified Englyst method, quantifying rapidly digestible starch (RDS), slowly digestible starch (SDS), and resistant starch (RS) fractions. The high-amylose variety extruded at 140 °C retained the highest RS fraction (8.3 g/100 g dry matter), whereas the low-amylose variety at 180 °C showed the highest RDS (71.2 g/100 g). Scanning electron microscopy of cross-sections confirmed more uniform granule disruption in the low-amylose extrudates. These data indicate that variety selection interacts substantially with temperature programming in determining the glycaemic character of the final product, a factor relevant for product positioning in functional food markets. Sorghum-specific protein matrix effects on starch digestibility are discussed.

title: Die geometry as a determinant of cell wall thickness in extruded triticale-sorghum blends
abstract: A set of five circular die inserts with capillary diameters from 2.0 mm to 4.5 mm and length-to-diameter (L/D) ratios of 1, 2, and 3 were tested during extrusion of a 60:40 triticale–sorghum flour blend at a fixed screw speed of 250 rpm and constant barrel temperature profile. Cell structure was characterised by X-ray microtomography (voxel size 18 µm), from which mean cell wall thickness, cell diameter distribution, and open-cell fraction were extracted. Decreasing die diameter from 4.5 to 2.0 mm increased mean cell wall thickness from 0.31 mm to 0.54 mm and reduced open-cell fraction from 41% to 18%. L/D ratio showed a secondary effect: higher L/D increased wall thickness by approximately 0.05 mm across all diameters tested. Pressure drop measurements at the die confirmed that L/D effects operate through residence time and pressure build-up rather than shear rate alone. Implications for snack crunchiness and structural uniformity are discussed.

title: Specific mechanical energy mapping across screw speed and feed rate combinations in triticale extrusion
abstract: A factorial experiment varying screw speed (150, 200, 250, 300 rpm) and dry feed rate (3, 5, 7 kg/h) was conducted on a pilot-scale co-rotating twin-screw extruder processing triticale wholemeal at 17% feed moisture. In-line torque and die pressure were logged continuously at 10 Hz to compute instantaneous SME. Mean SME ranged from 142 kJ/kg (300 rpm, 7 kg/h) to 389 kJ/kg (150 rpm, 3 kg/h). Response surface modelling explained 91% of SME variance. Correlation of SME with product water absorption index (WAI), water solubility index (WSI), and degree of starch gelatinisation showed that gelatinisation exceeded 85% above 260 kJ/kg regardless of how that SME was achieved, suggesting that SME is a reliable process signature for gelatinisation but not sufficient alone to predict expansion ratio, which also depended on the ratio of screw speed to feed rate. Practical guidance for process scale-up is provided.

title: Physicochemical and sensory properties of extruded breakfast cereal bases from triticale enriched with inulin
abstract: Triticale flour was blended with chicory inulin at substitution levels of 0, 5, 10, and 15 g/100 g before extrusion at 155 °C metering zone temperature and a die diameter of 3 mm. The resulting extrudates were characterised for expansion ratio, water absorption and solubility indices, total dietary fibre, colour (CIE L*a*b*), and textural properties (three-point bending). A trained panel of nine assessors evaluated crunchiness, colour, and overall acceptability. Expansion ratio declined from 4.5 to 3.1 as inulin level increased, attributable to dilution of the starch matrix and reduced melt viscosity. Total dietary fibre increased proportionally. Sensory crunchiness scores were not significantly different between 0 and 10% substitution levels (p > 0.05), suggesting that moderate inulin addition is feasible without major textural penalty. Colour became slightly darker (ΔE* ≈ 2.1) at 15% inulin, likely due to Maillard reactions involving inulin degradation products.

title: Comparative barrel temperature profiling strategies for sorghum extrusion: flat, ascending, and descending profiles
abstract: Three barrel temperature profiles—flat (160 °C across all zones), ascending (130–160–180 °C), and descending (180–160–130 °C)—were applied during extrusion of white sorghum flour at constant moisture (16%) and screw speed (220 rpm). SME, die pressure, melt temperature, expansion ratio, and in vitro starch digestibility were measured. The descending profile produced the lowest SME (198 kJ/kg) and highest resistant starch fraction (6.9 g/100 g), whereas the ascending profile yielded the highest expansion ratio (4.7) and the lowest RS (3.2 g/100 g). The flat profile gave intermediate results in all parameters. Differential scanning calorimetry of raw and extruded samples confirmed that descending profiles allowed partial retrogradation of amylose in the cooled metering zone. The study provides a practical basis for tailoring sorghum extrudates towards either high-expansion snack or higher-RS functional cereal applications by choice of profile alone, without equipment modification.

title: Influence of particle size of triticale wholemeal on extrudate microstructure and starch availability
abstract: Triticale wholemeal was fractionated into three particle size classes: coarse (>500 µm), medium (250–500 µm), and fine (<250 µm) by air classification. Each fraction and the original unseparated flour were extruded under identical conditions (160 °C metering zone, 17% moisture, 250 rpm, 3 mm die). Cell structure was characterised by image analysis of SEM cross-sections, computing mean cell area, cell circularity, and wall-to-cell ratio. Starch availability was assessed by the Megazyme total starch and resistant starch assay kits. Fine wholemeal gave significantly smaller mean cell area (0.34 mm²) and higher RDS (64 g/100 g) compared to coarse wholemeal (0.71 mm², RDS 51 g/100 g). The coarser bran particles in the coarse fraction appeared to interrupt cell wall formation and impede gelatinisation, an effect visible in SEM as discontinuous walls. Results suggest that milling intensity prior to extrusion is a cost-effective lever for cell structure control.

title: Optimisation of screw configuration elements for uniform SME distribution during co-extrusion of sorghum-based snack cores
abstract: Four screw configurations, varying the number, pitch, and stagger angle of kneading blocks in the transition zone, were evaluated during co-extrusion of a sorghum-based core with a potato starch outer sheath at a pilot scale. In-line pressure sensors at three axial positions and continuous torque logging allowed reconstruction of local specific energy dissipation profiles. Configuration C, with two sets of three 45°-stagger kneading blocks separated by a right-handed conveying element, gave the most uniform energy dissipation (coefficient of variation 11% across zones versus 28–34% for other configurations) and produced extrudates with the most consistent cell diameter distribution (D90–D10 range of 0.42 mm versus 0.61–0.79 mm). Die pressure was also most stable under configuration C (standard deviation 0.8 bar over 30 min). Starch gelatinisation degree and expansion ratio were statistically equivalent across configurations at p = 0.05, indicating that homogeneity of structure rather than average property values is the primary benefit of optimised screw design for co-extrusion.

title: Characterisation of wheat flour fractions from roller-milled and stone-milled streams: comparative rheological and enzyme activity profiles
abstract: Mill streams from a commercial roller mill and a stone mill processing the same Renan wheat batch were collected (12 streams per mill type) and characterised for protein content, ash, damaged starch (AACC 76-33), α-amylase activity (Ceralpha), endo-xylanase activity (Xylazyme AX), farinograph stability, and Mixolab C3 and C5 torques. Stone-milled streams showed 18–34 % higher damaged starch and 22–41 % higher α-amylase activity than corresponding roller-milled fractions, associated with lower Mixolab C3 torques (mean difference 0.21 Nm). Farinograph stability was statistically equivalent between mill types for matched protein content, but development time was shorter for stone-milled streams. Endo-xylanase activity was detectable in all stone-milled streams but below the assay limit of detection in seven of twelve roller-milled streams. These differences have practical implications for targeted substitution of stone-milled streams in specialty bread and artisan biscuit formulations.

title: Serum IgG concentrations and passive transfer failure rates in neonatal piglets on smallholder farms in the Vojvodina region
abstract: Failure of passive transfer (FPT) in neonatal piglets is associated with increased pre-weaning mortality and reduced growth performance, yet its prevalence on small and semi-subsistence pig farms in southeastern Europe remains poorly characterised. This cross-sectional study sampled 186 piglets from 24 smallholder farms in Vojvodina between March and September 2022. Blood was collected at 48–72 hours of life; serum IgG was quantified by ELISA and serum total protein by refractometry. FPT was defined as serum IgG below 10 mg/mL. Mean serum IgG was 18.4 ± 6.7 mg/mL; FPT was recorded in 22.6% of piglets. Litter size above 13 piglets, parity one sows, and ambient temperature below 8 °C at farrowing were significantly associated with FPT in multivariable logistic regression (p < 0.05). Farm management factors, including supervised suckling in the first two hours of life, were protective. The results indicate that FPT rates on Vojvodina smallholder farms are comparable to those reported for intensive systems in Western Europe, and that simple on-farm interventions may reduce their frequency.

title: Accuracy of Brix refractometry for estimating serum IgG in piglets under field conditions: a comparison with ELISA
abstract: Brix refractometry has been proposed as a rapid, affordable proxy for serum immunoglobulin concentration in neonatal calves and foals, but validation data for piglets under practical farm conditions are limited. This method-comparison study enrolled 142 piglets from 18 farms in Serbia and Croatia sampled at 48 hours post-partum. Serum total solids were measured with a temperature-compensated digital Brix refractometer; IgG was quantified by indirect ELISA using a commercially available porcine-specific kit. Pearson correlation between Brix percentage and IgG was r = 0.71 (p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis for the detection of FPT (IgG < 10 mg/mL) indicated an optimal Brix cut-off of 8.5%, yielding sensitivity of 78% and specificity of 84%. Agreement assessed by Bland-Altman analysis showed acceptable limits for screening purposes but systematic underestimation at higher IgG concentrations. Refractometry is suitable as a rapid herd-level screening tool on farms without laboratory access, provided that samples with borderline Brix values are confirmed by ELISA.

title: Colostrum IgG concentration in sows of different parities and breeds on family farms: seasonal and management effects
abstract: The immunoglobulin G content of sow colostrum is a primary determinant of passive immunity in neonatal piglets, yet data from non-commercial farm settings are scarce. Colostrum samples were collected from 97 sows on 15 family farms in Vojvodina over two farrowing seasons (autumn–winter 2023 and spring–summer 2024). Farms kept a mix of Swedish Landrace crosses and domestic Mangalica-cross genotypes. Colostrum IgG was determined by ELISA from samples taken within one hour of the first piglet's birth. Mean IgG concentration was 63.2 ± 21.4 mg/mL, with a range of 18.9 to 118.6 mg/mL. Parity significantly influenced IgG content: parities 3–5 sows had the highest concentrations (mean 72.1 mg/mL), while parity-one gilts averaged 48.3 mg/mL (p < 0.001). Autumn–winter farrowings were associated with lower colostrum IgG compared with spring–summer farrowings. Mangalica-cross sows showed numerically higher IgG than Landrace crosses, though the difference did not reach significance after adjustment for parity and season. These data provide baseline reference values for colostrum quality assessment in non-intensive Vojvodina pig production.

title: Pre-weaning mortality and its relationship with passive transfer status in smallholder pig production: findings from a longitudinal cohort in Serbia
abstract: Understanding whether failure of passive transfer (FPT) independently predicts pre-weaning mortality under smallholder conditions in Serbia provides practical information for extension services and veterinary practitioners. A prospective cohort of 311 piglets from 21 farms was followed from birth to weaning (day 28). FPT status was determined by Brix refractometry at 48 hours, with FPT defined as Brix below 8.5%. Farm-level data on hygiene scoring, teat access management, and ambient temperature were recorded. Pre-weaning mortality was 14.1% overall. Piglets classified as FPT had 2.7-fold higher odds of death before weaning compared with adequately transferred animals after adjustment for litter size and birth weight (95% CI: 1.4–5.3; p = 0.003). Mortality was concentrated in the first seven days of life. The association held across both seasons of recruitment. These findings support the use of early colostrum management protocols as a practical mortality-reduction measure on smallholder farms in the region.

title: Heritability estimates for total number born and number born alive in Vojvodina Mangalica purebreds using an animal model
abstract: This study estimated heritability for total number born (TNB) and number born alive (NBA) in a Vojvodina Mangalica population maintained at four registered farms in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina. Records from 1,142 litters collected between 2003 and 2012 were analysed using a single-trait animal model with REML implemented in the ASReml software package. Fixed effects included parity, herd-year-season of farrowing, and mating type. Heritability estimates for TNB and NBA were 0.09 ± 0.03 and 0.08 ± 0.03, respectively, consistent with values reported for other indigenous European pig breeds characterised by limited selection history. Posterior standard errors indicated low precision due to the relatively small and unbalanced pedigree structure spanning three generations. The results confirm that litter size traits in Mangalica carry low additive genetic variance, suggesting that selection response will be slow and that management of inbreeding within this numerically restricted population warrants attention.

title: Phenotypic and genetic variation in farrowing interval and its relationship with litter size in Mangalica × Landrace sows under extensive housing conditions
abstract: Farrowing interval (FI), defined as the number of days between consecutive farrowings, affects annual productivity but has received little attention in indigenous crossbred pig populations. Using 2,756 complete sow records from four Vojvodina farms with outdoor or deep-litter housing systems, this study estimated heritability of FI and its genetic and phenotypic correlations with TNB and NBA. Data spanned parities 1–6 over the period 2014–2024. A bivariate animal model was fitted with REML. Heritability of FI was 0.07 ± 0.03. Genetic correlation between FI and TNB was −0.21 ± 0.18, not significantly different from zero, suggesting that selection for shorter farrowing interval would not substantially compromise litter size at birth. Phenotypic correlations between FI and litter size traits were near zero. Season of farrowing accounted for the largest portion of fixed-effect variance in FI, consistent with the outdoor management context. Results provide a baseline for designing selection indexes in Vojvodina Mangalica crossbred production systems.

title: Interaction between dietary zearalenone and soy isoflavones on LH pulsatility in ovariectomized cows: a dose-response study
abstract: Diets for dairy cows frequently combine maize-derived ZEN with soy meal isoflavones, yet their combined effects on gonadotropin secretion are poorly characterised. Eighteen ovariectomized Holstein cows were assigned to one of six treatment groups (n = 3) in a 6 × 6 Latin square design with 21-day periods, receiving factorial combinations of ZEN (0, 0.8, 1.6 mg/day) and soy isoflavone load (low: 80 mg/day; high: 320 mg/day). Pulsatile LH secretion was characterised by 6-hour blood sampling profiles (every 10 min) analysed by the PULSAR algorithm. High ZEN reduced mean LH pulse frequency by 38% relative to control (p < 0.001); high isoflavone load independently reduced pulse amplitude by 19% (p < 0.05). The combination of high ZEN and high isoflavone produced an additive reduction in pulse frequency (–52%; p < 0.001) with no statistically significant interaction term, indicating independent mechanisms acting on the hypothalamo-pituitary axis. These findings suggest that cumulative estrogenic load, rather than source identity, determines suppression magnitude.

title: Urinary multi-mycotoxin profiling in Vojvodina dairy herds using dilute-and-shoot LC-MS/MS: first occurrence data for enniatins and beauvericin alongside classical Fusarium toxins
abstract: Surveillance of cattle exposure to mycotoxins has historically focused on ZEN, aflatoxin B1, and fumonisins, but emerging Fusarium toxins such as enniatins (ENNs) and beauvericin (BEA) are increasingly detected in European cereals. A dilute-and-shoot LC-MS/MS method was developed and validated for the simultaneous quantification of 14 mycotoxins and metabolites in bovine urine. Method performance: recovery 72–109%, CV < 12%, LODs 0.05–0.8 ng/mL across analytes. Urine samples from 84 cows on 7 farms (12 cows per farm) were analysed. ENN B was the most frequently detected emerging toxin (76% prevalence; median 1.8 ng/mL), followed by ENN B1 (58%) and BEA (29%). Co-occurrence of ENN B with α-ZOL occurred in 68% of samples. No significant correlations between ENN/BEA concentrations and reproductive hormone outcomes were observed at current exposure levels, though statistical power was limited by sample size. The method and baseline data support future monitoring programmes.

title: Buffer pH method calibration for lime requirement estimation on Vojvodina chernozem soils
abstract: Reliable lime requirement prediction depends on the choice of buffer pH method and its local calibration. This study compared three buffer solutions—modified Shoemaker–McLean–Pratt (SMP), Adams–Evans, and a phosphate-acetate buffer—against incubation lime requirement values obtained from 48 chernozem soil samples collected across five municipalities in northern Vojvodina. Soil pH ranged from 5.4 to 6.8, organic carbon from 1.9 to 3.6 percent, and clay content from 22 to 41 percent. The SMP buffer showed the strongest linear relationship with incubation lime requirement (r² = 0.87, RMSE = 0.31 t CaCO₃ ha⁻¹), while the Adams–Evans method systematically underestimated requirements by 12–18 percent in soils with high smectite content. Regression equations specific to chernozem texture classes are presented, and practical correction factors are proposed for laboratory use. The results suggest that regional recalibration is necessary before any single buffer method is adopted in routine advisory services across the Pannonian Basin.
