title: Cation exchange capacity fractionation in seasonally waterlogged soils of the Sava–Danube interfluve
abstract: Hydromorphic soils subject to seasonal waterlogging exhibit dynamic shifts in cation exchange capacity (CEC) due to redox-driven changes in organic matter and iron-oxyhydroxide surfaces. Sixty-two soil profiles from the Sava–Danube interfluve were sampled at three depths (0–20, 20–40, and 40–60 cm) in dry and wet seasons over two consecutive years. CEC was measured by the ammonium acetate method at pH 7.0, and exchangeable cation composition was determined by AAS. CEC values in the surface horizon ranged from 14.2 to 31.7 cmol(+) kg⁻¹ and declined by an average of 28 percent at 40–60 cm in waterlogged profiles, with calcium saturation dropping from 78 to 51 percent. The seasonal difference in surface CEC was statistically significant (paired t-test, p < 0.01) and correlated with loss-on-ignition fluctuation. Implications for amelioration planning and lime timing are discussed.

title: Spatial variability of soil reaction and base saturation across a toposequence in the Fruška Gora footzone
abstract: A transect-based study was conducted along a 4.2 km toposequence descending from Fruška Gora ridgeline to alluvial terrace to characterise spatial trends in pH, exchangeable acidity, and base saturation. Ninety-six composite samples were collected on a 200 m grid and analysed for pH (water and KCl), exchangeable Al³⁺, H⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, K⁺, and Na⁺. Kriging-interpolated maps showed a clear acidification gradient from ridge (mean pHKCl 4.6) to upper terrace (pHKCl 5.9), with exchangeable Al³⁺ reaching 3.8 cmol(+) kg⁻¹ in Cambisol-dominated ridge soils. Base saturation increased from 42 to 89 percent along the toposequence. The study identified two distinct liming priority zones and estimated an aggregate lime requirement of 5 800 t CaCO₃ for the surveyed 480 ha catchment. Results are discussed in the context of precision amelioration scheduling.

title: Modelling lime requirement from readily available soil parameters: a comparison of regression and random forest approaches
abstract: Laboratory determination of lime requirement through incubation or buffer methods is time-consuming and not universally available. This study assessed whether lime requirement can be predicted sufficiently accurately from routinely measured soil variables—pH (KCl), organic carbon, clay content, and electrical conductivity—using multiple linear regression and random forest models. A dataset of 310 topsoil samples from Vojvodina representing three soil associations (chernozem, eutric Fluvisol, and gleyic Phaeozem) was split 70:30 for training and testing. The random forest model outperformed linear regression (test RMSE 0.41 vs. 0.68 t CaCO₃ ha⁻¹; R² 0.81 vs. 0.64), with clay content and organic carbon identified as the most influential predictors by permutation importance. Cross-validation across soil associations revealed that the model trained on chernozem alone performed poorly on Fluvisol samples (RMSE increased to 1.12), indicating that association-specific training sets are necessary for practical deployment.

title: Soil buffering curves under long-term calcium carbonate application: evidence from a 12-year field experiment
abstract: Long-term effects of repeated liming on soil acid–base buffering behaviour are rarely quantified. This paper presents data from a 12-year field experiment on a slightly acid chernozem at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station where CaCO₃ was applied at 0, 2, 4, and 6 t ha⁻¹ every four years. Soil was sampled in years 0, 4, 8, and 12 at two depths. Acid–base titration buffer curves were constructed from each sample by incremental HCl and NaOH additions. The highest application rate elevated pHKCl from 5.7 to 6.5 after 12 years and shifted the inflection point of the buffer curve by 0.4 pH units. Buffer capacity, calculated as the slope of the linear portion of the titration curve, increased proportionally with cumulative CaCO₃ input (r = 0.77). Exchangeable Mg²⁺ declined slightly at 40–60 cm under the highest treatment, a finding with practical implications for maintaining cation balance.

title: Exchangeable sodium percentage dynamics following gypsum amendment in solonetz soils of the Banat plain
abstract: Solonetz soils in the Banat plain suffer from high exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP) that restricts permeability and root development. A two-year micro-plot experiment tested four gypsum doses (0, 5, 10, and 15 t ha⁻¹) combined with two irrigation water qualities on solonetz soils with initial ESP values of 21–36 percent. ESP, hydraulic conductivity, and exchangeable cation composition were measured at six-month intervals. The 10 t ha⁻¹ dose reduced ESP below the 15 percent threshold within 18 months across all water quality treatments, whereas 5 t ha⁻¹ achieved this only when irrigation EC was below 0.8 dS m⁻¹. Hydraulic conductivity improved from 0.03 to 0.19 cm h⁻¹ at the highest dose after 24 months. A simple first-order kinetic model fitted ESP decline well (R² = 0.84), and dose-specific rate constants are tabulated.

title: Sensitivity analysis of lime requirement models to measurement uncertainty in soil pH and CEC inputs
abstract: This conference paper presents a Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis applied to four lime requirement models (Shoemaker–McLean–Pratt, Mehlich, Nair–Graetz, and a locally calibrated Vojvodina model) to quantify how analytical uncertainty in input variables propagates to uncertainty in lime dose recommendation. Input uncertainties were defined from interlaboratory comparison data for 15 Serbian soil testing laboratories: coefficient of variation was 2.1 percent for pH(KCl), 8.4 percent for CEC, and 11.7 percent for organic carbon. Ten thousand Monte Carlo iterations per model were run for three reference soils representing light, medium, and heavy texture classes. Resulting lime dose uncertainty expressed as 95 percent prediction intervals ranged from ±0.6 to ±2.3 t CaCO₃ ha⁻¹ depending on model and texture, with organic carbon uncertainty being the dominant driver in two of the four models. The results support stricter interlaboratory harmonisation for organic carbon determination.

title: Relationship between soil organic matter fractions and pH buffering intensity in degraded Vojvodina chernozem
abstract: Organic matter contributes substantially to soil acid–base buffering through carboxylate and phenolic functional groups, yet its fractions differ in buffering effectiveness. This study isolated humic acids, fulvic acids, and humin fractions from 36 degraded chernozem samples spanning a gradient of organic carbon from 0.9 to 3.1 percent. Potentiometric titration of isolated fractions was conducted from pH 3 to 10. Humic acid fractions showed the highest specific buffering capacity (mean 420 mmol H⁺ kg⁻¹ per pH unit), followed by humin (310) and fulvic acid (185). In a multiple regression including clay CEC, the organic matter fractions together explained 71 percent of variance in whole-soil buffering intensity. Degraded soils with organic carbon below 1.5 percent had buffering capacities 38 percent lower than undegraded counterparts at equivalent clay content, suggesting that organic matter loss significantly reduces resilience to acidification inputs.

title: A GIS-assisted framework for catchment-scale lime requirement mapping integrating soil association boundaries and topographic wetness index
abstract: Existing lime requirement maps for Vojvodina are typically produced at the field level and do not account for lateral redistribution of bases through surface and subsurface flow. This study developed a catchment-scale mapping framework combining conventional soil survey data with topographic wetness index (TWI) derived from a 5 m resolution digital elevation model. Lime requirement was first estimated at 214 sample points using the calibrated SMP buffer method, then modelled as a function of soil association membership, TWI, and depth-to-groundwater using a generalised additive model (GAM). The framework was applied to three 200–600 ha catchments in south Bačka. Cross-validation RMSE was 0.55 t CaCO₃ ha⁻¹, comparable to within-field variability. Maps highlighted systematically higher lime needs in concave footslope positions within otherwise uniformly classified chernozem zones, with practical consequences for variable-rate lime application planning.

title: Leaching risk assessment of acetochlor in Vojvodina soils using column experiments and the PELMO model
abstract: Undisturbed soil columns (50 cm length, 10 cm diameter) representing three Vojvodina soil series (chernozem, solonetz, and alluvial meadow soil) were used in laboratory leaching experiments. Acetochlor was applied at the soil surface at 2.0 kg a.i. ha⁻¹ and columns were irrigated at 5 mm day⁻¹ for 60 days. Leachate fractions (every 5 days) and soil layers (0–10, 10–25, 25–50 cm) were analysed by GC-ECD. Acetochlor was detected in leachate from the solonetz columns starting at day 20, reaching a maximum concentration of 0.82 µg L⁻¹ at day 35, exceeding the EU drinking water limit of 0.1 µg L⁻¹. Chernozem columns showed no leachate detections above 0.05 µg L⁻¹. PELMO 3.3 model predictions agreed reasonably with observed chernozem data (normalised root mean squared error 18%) but underestimated leaching from solonetz by a factor of 2.4, attributed to preferential flow. Results indicate a site-specific leaching risk for solonetz soils common in southern Vojvodina.

title: Baseline Pupil Diameter Variability as a Predictor of Attentional Demand in a Lane-Keeping Task
abstract: This study examined whether resting-state pupil diameter fluctuations measured before a driving session could predict participants' subsequent cognitive load responses during a standardised lane-keeping task. Thirty-two healthy adult volunteers completed a 20-minute simulated drive on a monotonous highway segment while pupil diameter was recorded at 250 Hz using an infrared remote eye tracker mounted on the dashboard. Baseline recordings of five minutes were obtained in a dim cabin before each session. Linear mixed-effects models revealed that individuals with higher baseline pupil variability (coefficient of variation > 6.1 %) showed significantly attenuated task-evoked pupil dilation (p < 0.01), suggesting a ceiling effect consistent with elevated tonic arousal. Secondary regression against self-reported NASA-TLX scores confirmed a moderate negative correlation (r = −0.44). The finding has practical implications for personalising cognitive load thresholds in driver state monitoring systems, since a single pre-drive calibration window may be sufficient to stratify drivers into low- and high-sensitivity groups without requiring lengthy baseline protocols.

title: Frequency-Domain Features of the Electrooculogram for Discriminating Alert and Drowsy Driving States
abstract: Electrooculography (EOG) captures corneoretinal potential differences arising from saccades and slow eye movements; however, its frequency-domain properties under prolonged driving are underexplored relative to time-domain blink metrics. This paper presents an analysis of EOG recordings from 24 subjects during a 90-minute monotonous driving simulation, with drowsiness confirmed by simultaneous EEG alpha-band power increase and self-report. Short-time Fourier transform applied to 10-second EOG windows produced spectral features in the 0.05–2 Hz band. A linear discriminant classifier trained on six spectral features achieved 82.4 % accuracy (leave-one-subject-out cross-validation) in distinguishing alert from drowsy epochs, outperforming blink-rate alone by 11 percentage points. Delta-band (0.05–0.5 Hz) power explained the largest variance. The results suggest that frequency-domain EOG analysis can serve as a lightweight drowsiness indicator suitable for low-power wearable headsets, requiring only two periocular electrodes.

title: Sensor Fusion of ECG and Eye-Tracking Signals for Continuous Cognitive Load Estimation: A Kalman Filter Approach
abstract: Estimating cognitive load continuously from a single physiological channel is unreliable due to inter-individual variability and signal artefacts common in vehicle environments. This work proposes a Kalman filter framework that fuses heart-rate variability (HRV) features derived from ECG with task-evoked pupil dilation measured by a remote infrared eye tracker. Data were collected from 18 participants performing a secondary auditory n-back task at three difficulty levels (0-back, 1-back, 2-back) superimposed on a simulated urban driving scenario. The fused estimate tracked ground-truth load level transitions 340 ms faster on average than either channel alone, and mean absolute error against NASA-TLX ratings decreased from 14.2 % (ECG only) and 17.8 % (eye-tracking only) to 9.6 % with fusion. The Kalman gain adaptation handled blink-induced dropout in pupil data effectively, reducing missing-data artefacts by 63 %. The paper provides a practical formulation amenable to real-time implementation on a microcontroller-class processor at 100 Hz update rate.

title: Influence of Road Geometry Complexity on Fixation Duration Distributions in Experienced vs. Novice Drivers
abstract: Eye fixation behaviour changes with driving expertise, but the quantitative effect of road geometry—curve radius, junction density—on fixation duration distributions has not been systematically characterised. Forty-four licensed drivers (22 with fewer than two years of experience, 22 with more than ten) completed four 15-minute scenarios of varying road complexity in a fixed-base driving simulator. Eye fixations were extracted from remote eye-tracker data at 120 Hz using a velocity-threshold algorithm. Hierarchical Bayesian modelling of fixation durations revealed that novice drivers showed significantly longer mean fixation durations (245 ± 38 ms vs. 196 ± 29 ms) and narrower spatial dispersion of gaze in high-complexity segments, consistent with focused attentional tunnelling. Expert drivers maintained a wider and more uniform gaze distribution irrespective of geometry. Blink frequency dropped by 18 % in high-complexity segments for novices but only 5 % for experts. These distributions provide empirically grounded thresholds for adaptive warning systems that account for driver experience level.

title: Real-Time Driver Drowsiness Detection on an ARM Cortex-M7 Platform Using Compressed EEG Features
abstract: Translating EEG-based drowsiness detectors from offline research to embedded automotive platforms requires significant computational reduction without sacrificing classification performance. This paper describes the design and validation of a drowsiness detector running on a 400 MHz ARM Cortex-M7 microcontroller with 1 MB of on-chip SRAM. A four-channel EEG montage covering frontal and parietal sites was used; features were restricted to alpha-to-theta ratio and spectral edge frequency computed over 4-second non-overlapping windows. A support vector machine with a linear kernel was trained on a 30-subject dataset and then quantised to 16-bit fixed-point arithmetic. On the embedded target, the complete detection pipeline ran in 18.2 ms per window—well within the 4-second budget—and consumed 62 mW from a 3.3 V supply. Classification accuracy on a held-out test set of eight subjects was 79.1 %, compared with 81.4 % for the floating-point desktop version, indicating negligible degradation from quantisation. The implementation is suitable for integration into a vehicle ECU with standard CAN-bus output.

title: Galvanic Skin Response Artefact Rejection in Automotive Environments Using Adaptive Notch Filtering
abstract: Galvanic skin response (GSR) measured through steering-wheel electrodes is contaminated by motion artefacts caused by grip pressure changes and road vibration, limiting its usefulness in driver monitoring. This paper evaluates three adaptive artefact rejection strategies—least-mean-squares adaptive notch filtering, empirical mode decomposition, and a reference-channel subtraction scheme—applied to GSR recorded from 15 subjects during real on-road driving over a standardised 25 km urban–rural route. Motion was measured simultaneously with a triaxial accelerometer on the steering wheel column. Signal quality was assessed as the ratio of event-related skin conductance response amplitude to residual noise floor. The adaptive notch filter achieved the highest signal-to-noise improvement (8.3 dB average) while maintaining the lowest computational cost (12 µs per sample at 512 Hz on a Cortex-M4). Empirical mode decomposition performed comparably in noise reduction (7.9 dB) but required 10× more computation. Practical guidance is given for selecting filter parameters based on vehicle speed profile.

title: Physiological Signal Processing for Driver State Monitoring: Methods and Challenges
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of physiological sensing modalities used in driver state monitoring, with particular emphasis on the signal processing pipeline from raw acquisition to decision-level output. Covered modalities include ECG, EEG, electrooculography, GSR, and remote photoplethysmography. For each, the chapter discusses relevant physiological mechanisms, sensor placement constraints in automotive settings, typical signal-to-noise characteristics, and appropriate preprocessing steps. Feature extraction methods are categorised as time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-frequency, with worked examples drawn from publicly available and in-house datasets. The chapter also addresses multi-modal fusion architectures, including feature-level, decision-level, and hybrid fusion, and evaluates their trade-offs in terms of latency, robustness, and computational cost. A concluding section outlines open challenges: personalisation of thresholds, non-stationarity of physiological signals over drive duration, and regulatory considerations for deployment in production vehicles. Intended as a reference for graduate students and practitioners entering the field.

title: Cross-Subject Generalisation of a Pupil-Based Cognitive Load Classifier Using Domain Adaptation
abstract: Pupil-based cognitive load classifiers trained on one group of subjects typically perform poorly on new individuals due to inter-subject differences in baseline diameter and light reflex gain. This study applies a covariate-shift domain adaptation technique—specifically, importance-weighted cross-validation—to a pupillometry dataset from 40 subjects performing a variable-difficulty visual search task. Subjects were split into a source domain (25 subjects used for classifier training) and a target domain (15 unseen subjects). Without adaptation, a random forest classifier achieved 61.3 % accuracy on target subjects; with importance-weighted training, accuracy rose to 74.6 %. The adaptation required only two minutes of unlabelled target-subject data collected during a warm-up trial, making it practical for deployment. Confusion matrices show that misclassification was most common between adjacent load levels rather than extremes. The results suggest that lightweight domain adaptation can substantially close the generalisation gap in pupil-based systems without full subject-specific retraining.

title: Detection of Secondary Task Engagement During Driving Using Combined EEG Theta Power and Saccade Velocity Features
abstract: Secondary task engagement (e.g. phone-based interaction) raises cognitive load and alters both neural and oculomotor dynamics. This study investigated whether the combination of frontal EEG theta power and peak saccade velocity could reliably detect secondary task onset and offset during driving. Twenty-six participants drove a simulated suburban route while performing intermittent phone-number recall tasks of 10-second duration. EEG was recorded from Fz, F3, and F4; eye-tracking provided saccade kinematics at 250 Hz. A gradient boosting classifier using four features (frontal theta power, theta asymmetry, peak saccade velocity, saccade duration) achieved 85.7 % binary detection accuracy in a leave-one-session-out evaluation, with mean detection latency of 2.1 seconds from task onset. Saccade velocity alone accounted for 68 % of the classifier's feature importance score. EEG theta contributed most during tasks with high verbal working memory load. The combination improves robustness compared with single-modality approaches in naturalistic driving conditions.

title: Estimation of Time-on-Task Fatigue from Remote Photoplethysmography in a Fixed-Base Driving Simulator
abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) extracts heart rate and its variability from subtle skin colour changes captured by a standard RGB camera, offering a fully contactless physiological monitoring approach. This paper assesses whether rPPG-derived HRV features are sensitive enough to track time-on-task fatigue in a 75-minute monotonous highway simulation. Twenty subjects were recorded with an 1080p camera at 30 fps under controlled cabin illumination. A plane-orthogonal-to-skin (POS) algorithm extracted the pulse signal; interbeat intervals were estimated and low-frequency HRV features computed in 60-second windows. Compared with reference contact ECG, mean interbeat interval error was 6.3 ms (RMSE) and SDNN correlation was r = 0.87. HRV indices showed the expected fatigue progression—decreasing RMSSD and LF/HF ratio—with trajectories comparable to contact ECG. False-alarm rate for a threshold-based fatigue alert was 14.2 % versus 11.8 % for contact ECG. These results support rPPG as a viable contactless alternative for passive fatigue monitoring in simulator and near-production settings.

title: Multimodal Dataset for Driver Cognitive State Monitoring: Recording Protocol and Baseline Benchmarks
abstract: Publicly available datasets combining synchronised EEG, eye-tracking, ECG, and GSR in a driving simulator context remain scarce, hindering reproducibility and comparative evaluation. This paper describes the design, recording protocol, and initial benchmark results of an open dataset collected at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. Fifty-two participants completed four driving scenarios—monotonous highway, urban traffic, secondary cognitive task, and unexpected hazard—yielding approximately 140 hours of synchronised physiological and video data. All signals were timestamped to a common hardware clock with drift below 0.5 ms over a 90-minute session. Metadata include subjective ratings (NASA-TLX, Karolinska Sleepiness Scale), demographic information, and driving experience. Baseline classification benchmarks for drowsiness and cognitive load are reported using logistic regression, SVM, and a shallow convolutional network. The dataset is deposited on an open institutional repository under a CC-BY 4.0 licence. The paper details inclusion criteria, ethical approval reference, and step-by-step preprocessing scripts.

title: Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Retinal OCT Layer Segmentation When Source Data Are Inaccessible
abstract: Source-free domain adaptation addresses the practical constraint that source training data cannot be shared due to patient privacy agreements or institutional policies. We adapted a retinal layer segmentation network trained on 780 OCT volumes from one clinical device to three target devices, each with a distinct speckle noise profile and axial resolution, using only 15 unlabelled target volumes per device and the pre-trained source model. Adaptation was achieved by iterative pseudo-labelling combined with test-time batch normalisation statistics computed on the target domain. On the three target devices, mean absolute layer thickness error decreased by 12.4, 9.8, and 14.1 µm relative to direct source-model application. Performance matched supervised fine-tuning with 30 labelled volumes, despite using zero target labels. The framework requires no retraining from scratch and converges within 25 adaptation steps.

title: Haemodynamic response of the tibialis anterior during a stepwise incremental plantar flexion protocol measured by continuous-wave NIRS
abstract: Graded exercise protocols allow the relationship between workload and muscle oxygen delivery and utilisation to be characterised non-invasively. Sixteen recreationally active men performed a five-stage plantar flexion protocol on a custom ergometer (20, 40, 60, 80, 100% of maximal voluntary contraction in 3-minute stages) while CW-NIRS monitored the tibialis anterior. OHb rose progressively from rest to 60% MVC (mean increase 18 µM) before plateauing, while DHb increased monotonically across all stages (mean increase 31 µM at 100% MVC). The oxygenation index (OHb − DHb) turned negative above 70% MVC, indicating that oxygen consumption exceeded delivery at moderate-to-high intensities. Arterial occlusion cuff manoeuvres bracketing each stage confirmed the calibration of the desaturation slope. Repeated measures ANOVA revealed significant stage effects for all chromophores (p < 0.001) and significant linear DHb trends. Inter-session reliability assessed over two sessions one week apart yielded intraclass correlation coefficients of 0.88–0.93 for peak chromophore responses.

title: Power-Quality Disturbances in Industrial Electroplating Baths: Field Measurements and Source Identification
abstract: Chromium and nickel electroplating rectifiers generate significant harmonic currents that propagate into the medium-voltage supply network and distort voltage waveforms across neighbouring loads. This study presents field measurements taken at three electroplating facilities in the Vojvodina region over a six-month period using calibrated power analysers at the point of common coupling and at individual rectifier cabinets. Total harmonic distortion of current (THDi) reached 28–41% at the rectifier terminals, with dominant fifth and seventh harmonics accounting for 70–75% of harmonic content. Voltage THD at the busbar exceeded the EN 50160 limit of 8% during peak-production shifts at two of the three sites. Passive LC filters tuned to the fifth harmonic were evaluated through simulation and on-site trials; measured THDi dropped to 9–12% post-installation. The paper discusses the correlation between production scheduling patterns and harmonic injection levels, and proposes a simplified screening method for rapid site classification based on installed rectifier capacity and shift timing.

title: Energy-Flow Mapping Methodology for Batch Electrochemical Processing Lines
abstract: Batch electrochemical lines — including anodising, electroforming, and electrolytic degreasing — follow cyclical current and thermal profiles that complicate standard metering-based energy accounting. This paper develops a systematic energy-flow mapping methodology adapted for batch processes, combining continuous submetering of rectifier DC output, bath heating elements, ventilation, and effluent treatment units with material-balance cross-checks. The methodology was applied to two aluminium anodising lines at an automotive component supplier in Novi Sad. Sankey diagrams constructed from twelve weeks of logged data show that electrolytic heating accounted for 52–58% of total site electricity, while ventilation contributed 18–22%, figures substantially different from operator estimates. The procedure identifies a set of standardised measurement points sufficient to reconstruct full-site energy flows without permanently installed instrumentation on every sub-circuit, reducing audit preparation time by approximately 35% compared to a conventional audit protocol tested at the same facility.

title: Load Profile Analysis of Variable-Speed Drive Systems in HVAC and Conveyor Applications: Implications for Demand-Side Management
abstract: Variable-speed drives (VSDs) are widely cited as energy-saving devices, yet their aggregated effect on plant load profiles and peak-demand charges is undercharacterised. This conference paper presents measured half-hourly load profiles from eleven manufacturing sites in Serbia and Hungary, each operating between four and twenty-three VSDs on HVAC and conveyor duty. Data were collected over one full calendar year to capture seasonal variation. The analysis shows that VSD penetration above 40% of installed motor capacity correlates with a flattening of the daily load curve and a 9–17% reduction in peak-to-average ratio, which translates to measurable savings under Serbian red-zone tariff rules. However, three sites showed increased reactive power demand due to unfiltered VSD front-end rectifiers, partially offsetting the active-power savings. The paper discusses a simple pre-audit screening index for estimating whether VSD-related load-flattening will produce net tariff benefits at a given site.

title: Thermal Imaging as a Supplementary Tool in Industrial Energy Audits of Electromechanical Equipment
abstract: Infrared thermography is routinely used for predictive maintenance but is less commonly integrated into energy audits. This study examines how thermal imaging of motors, switchgear, and bus ducts can improve loss quantification during audits. At a Vojvodina-based electric motor rewinding and testing facility, thermographic surveys were conducted in parallel with power-quality logging at forty-two measurement points across two production shifts. Temperature anomalies on motor housings and cable terminations were correlated with measured copper and iron losses calculated from current and voltage waveforms. The combined approach identified six motors with winding insulation degradation whose measured electrical losses were 11–23% above nameplate expectations; replacing these with IEC IE3-class units was estimated to save 47 MWh per year. The paper presents a reproducible integration protocol and discusses the minimum qualification requirements for thermographers participating in energy audits at sites with live electrical equipment.

title: Peak-Demand Tariff Exposure in Serbian Manufacturing: A Cross-Sector Benchmarking Study
abstract: Serbian electricity tariff regulation imposes a significant penalty on peak active and reactive power demand during defined red-zone hours. Despite this, few published studies quantify tariff exposure across manufacturing sectors or compare reduction potentials. This paper reports findings from energy audits carried out at twenty-seven manufacturing sites in Serbia between 2012 and 2015, covering food processing, metal forming, plastic injection moulding, and electrochemical surface treatment. For each site, peak-demand tariff costs were extracted from twelve months of bills and crosschecked against metered half-hourly interval data. Electrochemical surface-treatment sites showed the highest tariff-to-total-bill ratio (31–38%), compared with 12–19% for food processing. Achievable reductions through load shifting alone — without capital investment — were estimated at 14–22% of the tariff component across sectors. The paper provides sector-specific load-shifting windows derived from production-schedule analysis and discusses constraints imposed by process chemistry and quality requirements.

title: Automated Submetering Architecture for Continuous Energy Monitoring in Electroplating Facilities
abstract: Continuous energy monitoring in electroplating plants is complicated by the co-existence of high-current DC rectifier circuits, three-phase AC motor drives, and resistive heating loads on shared busbars. This paper describes a submetering architecture deployed at a zinc–nickel plating facility in Subotica, Serbia, consisting of twenty-four current-transformer-based sensors, a Modbus RTU data concentrator, and a cloud-accessible time-series database sampled at ten-second intervals. The system was validated against utility interval meters over a three-month commissioning period; discrepancy was below 1.2%. After twelve months of operation, the continuous data stream enabled identification of two systematic energy anomalies — a heating-bath thermostat hunting pattern adding 6.8 MWh per month, and an idle-run pattern on the rinsing-tank agitation motors consuming 3.1 MWh per month — neither of which had been visible in periodic audit snapshots. The paper discusses sensor selection criteria, installation challenges in corrosive environments, and data-management requirements for long-term monitoring.

title: Demand-Side Management for Induction Furnace Operations: Scheduling Model and Industrial Trial
abstract: Induction furnaces for aluminium scrap remelting draw power in distinct melt-and-hold cycles that produce sharp demand spikes. This study develops a mixed-integer scheduling model for a foundry operating three medium-frequency induction furnaces, with the objective of minimising monthly peak demand while satisfying production volume and delivery-deadline constraints. The model was parameterised using two months of measured power profiles and production logs from a Novi Sad foundry. Trial implementation of the derived schedule over a subsequent four-month period reduced measured monthly peak demand by 18.3% on average, compared with the operator's prior heuristic scheduling. The reduction corresponded to a verified tariff saving of approximately 4,200 EUR per month. The paper discusses the sensitivity of the schedule to scrap-charge variability and furnace downtime, and identifies the minimum telemetry needed to run the model in near-real-time using current meter readings as input.

title: Reactive Power Compensation Planning for a Multi-Process Manufacturing Site with Dominant Rectifier and VSD Loads
abstract: Manufacturing sites combining large rectifier installations and variable-speed drives present a reactive power compensation problem that static capacitor banks alone cannot solve reliably, owing to harmonic resonance risk. This paper reports a compensation planning study for a Vojvodina-based manufacturer of electric motors, where measured power-factor values ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 across shifts and monthly reactive energy penalties represented 8.3% of the total electricity bill. A combination of passive detuned capacitor banks and a 200 kVAr active filter was evaluated through simulation calibrated against six months of power-quality measurements. The selected solution — two detuned banks at 7% tuned to 189 Hz, plus the active filter on the rectifier feeder — achieved a simulated power factor of 0.968 under peak-load conditions. Post-installation measurements over three months confirmed a power factor of 0.952–0.971 and a 91% reduction in harmonic voltage distortion at the point of common coupling. Reactive energy penalty costs dropped by 87% relative to the pre-installation baseline.

title: Baseline Setting and Measurement and Verification for Load-Shifting Interventions in Electrochemical Plants
abstract: Measurement and verification (M&V) of demand-side management interventions in electrochemical manufacturing is complicated by process variability: bath temperature, electrolyte concentration, and substrate geometry all influence electrical load independently of scheduling decisions. This paper proposes an M&V protocol for load-shifting projects at electrochemical plants, adapted from the IPMVP Option B framework, with explicit correction procedures for three primary non-routine adjustment variables: production volume, bath-electrolyte conductivity, and ambient temperature. The protocol was applied retrospectively to data from load-shifting trials at five plating and anodising facilities. Corrected savings estimates differed from uncorrected estimates by between −11% and +19%, illustrating the importance of adjustment. The paper provides worked examples of the correction calculations and discusses the minimum monitoring requirements needed to apply the protocol at a new site, including which variables can be proxied from process-control logs rather than dedicated instrumentation.

title: Impact of Time-of-Use Tariff Reform on Optimal Load-Scheduling in Serbian Metal Finishing SMEs
abstract: A revision to Serbian distribution tariff regulation in 2021 changed the red-zone window definitions and increased the demand charge coefficient, altering the economics of load-shifting for small and medium manufacturing enterprises. This paper analyses the impact of the tariff change on fourteen metal-finishing SMEs that had previously implemented schedule-based load-shifting recommendations. For each site, the pre-reform load schedules were re-optimised under the new tariff structure using a linear programming model driven by fifteen-minute interval meter data. In eleven of fourteen cases the optimal schedule window shifted by 60–90 minutes, and the achievable tariff saving increased by 4–14 percentage points relative to the pre-reform potential, because the new red-zone windows align better with natural gaps in surface-treatment process cycles. Three sites showed diminished benefit due to customer-driven delivery constraints that prevented schedule modification. The paper discusses implications for policy design and for the timing of investment in smart-metering infrastructure at SME level.

title: On-Site Renewable Integration and Its Effect on Peak-Demand Management at an Electromechanical Assembly Plant: A Measured Case Study
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic systems are increasingly installed at manufacturing sites in Serbia under net-metering arrangements, but their interaction with active peak-demand management programmes has received limited attention. This paper presents measured data from a 480 kWp rooftop PV installation at an electromechanical assembly plant in Novi Sad, combining twelve months of fifteen-minute PV generation and site demand data with tariff modelling. The analysis shows that PV generation reduces peak demand during summer afternoon hours by 60–130 kW on clear days, but introduces scheduling conflicts on overcast winter days when the coincidence of PV generation with the red-zone window is low. An adjusted load-shifting schedule that explicitly accounts for PV generation forecast uncertainty was developed and back-tested against the measured year; it reduced monthly peak demand by a further 8.3% on average compared with a schedule that ignores PV variability. The paper discusses practical forecasting approaches suitable for plant-level implementation without specialist meteorological expertise.

title: Energy Intensity Indicators for Electrochemical Surface Treatment: Definition, Measurement Protocol, and Sector Benchmarks for the Western Balkans
abstract: Energy intensity metrics for electrochemical surface-treatment processes are not standardised, making it difficult to compare audit findings across facilities or to set evidence-based improvement targets. This paper proposes a set of process-level energy intensity indicators (EIIs) for five common surface-treatment technologies — zinc electroplating, chromium hard-plating, nickel plating, aluminium anodising, and electrolytic phosphating — each expressed per unit of treated surface area and per unit of coating thickness where applicable. The indicators were derived from measurements at twenty-two facilities across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia collected between 2019 and 2023. Sector benchmark distributions are reported as 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile values for each technology. The paper also describes a simplified measurement protocol for calculating site-level EIIs using only production records and monthly energy bills, enabling rapid self-assessment without a full instrument-based audit. Comparison of self-assessed EIIs against instrument-verified values at eight sites showed agreement within ±9%.

title: Data-Driven Detection of Abnormal Energy Consumption Patterns in Continuous Electroforming Lines Using Statistical Process Control Charts
abstract: Continuous electroforming lines for copper foil and nickel mesh production run at near-constant current density for days or weeks at a time, making gradual efficiency degradation difficult to detect from periodic audits. This preprint describes the application of statistical process control (SPC) methods — specifically CUSUM and EWMA charts — to time-series energy data from two continuous electroforming lines in Serbia and one in Romania, logged at one-minute resolution over eight and eleven months respectively. Chart parameters were tuned using three months of baseline data collected immediately after a confirmed maintenance overhaul. The charts correctly flagged three anode degradation events and one electrolyte-temperature drift event across the monitoring periods, each confirmed retrospectively by maintenance logs. Average detection lag was 4.2 hours, compared with an estimated 60–180 hours for detection by operator observation alone. The preprint discusses the sensitivity-specificity trade-off under different chart parameterisations and provides guidance on adapting the approach to other constant-rate electrochemical processes.

title: Effect of rack loading density on airflow uniformity and drying rate consistency in batch chambers: a combined experimental and simulation study
abstract: Three trolley loading configurations—sparse (40 % volumetric fill), medium (65 %), and dense (85 %)—were tested in a 7.2 m³ industrial batch drying chamber used for fermented sausages. For each configuration, airflow velocity was measured at 96 points using a hot-wire anemometer and product weight loss was recorded at 16 sample positions over 96-hour drying cycles. Uniformity index values for airflow dropped from 0.79 at sparse loading to 0.52 at dense loading. Corresponding coefficients of variation for weight loss at cycle end were 7.2, 12.4, and 21.6 %. A validated CFD model was used to simulate 15 additional loading geometries. Regression analysis of simulation results showed that uniformity index decreased approximately linearly with fill fraction above 55 % and that horizontal inter-rack spacing below 60 mm was the primary geometric factor causing local stagnation. A simple loading guideline is proposed that maintains uniformity index above 0.68 for the chamber geometry tested.

title: Life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions of a biomass-supplemented district heating network: a case study from Vojvodina
abstract: This study presents a cradle-to-grave LCA of a district heating network in a mid-sized Vojvodina municipality that covers approximately 18 000 residential units. The network is supplied by a natural-gas boiler plant (70% of annual heat output) supplemented by a wood-chip combustion unit (30%). Inventory data were collected directly from the operator for a one-year reference period and cross-checked against national emission factor databases. The functional unit was defined as the delivery of 1 GJ of heat to the building envelope. Results indicate a carbon footprint of 68 kg CO₂-eq per GJ under the base-case allocation, falling to 41 kg CO₂-eq per GJ when biomass is credited with avoided landfill emissions. Sensitivity analysis showed that the moisture content of wood chips and the transmission loss rate in the pipe network together explain over 60% of output variance. The study used SimaPro 9.3 with the ecoinvent 3.8 database and the ReCiPe 2016 midpoint method. Findings suggest that even a modest biomass share substantially reduces global warming potential relative to a fully gas-fired reference system, though the magnitude depends heavily on fuel sourcing assumptions.

title: Heat exchanger fouling effects on ORC system dynamics: a simulation study for a food-processing application
abstract: Fouling accumulation on evaporator surfaces was integrated into a dynamic ORC model to assess its influence on system output over a simulated six-month operating period relevant to a vegetable-oil processing plant producing 180–220 °C exhaust gas. Fouling resistance was modelled using an exponential asymptotic growth function with parameters taken from published food-industry heat exchanger data. The simulation predicts a gradual reduction in evaporating pressure of approximately 0.4 bar over the period, corresponding to a 6.1% drop in net electrical output if the pump-speed controller is not re-tuned. A simple re-tuning procedure based on measured superheat deviation was tested in simulation: it recovers 4.3 percentage points of the lost output without hardware intervention. The study highlights that fouling is a meaningful disturbance in food-sector ORC installations and that periodic controller re-tuning, rather than continuous cleaning, may be a cost-effective management approach. Sensitivity to fouling-rate parameter uncertainty was assessed with a Monte Carlo run of 500 samples.

title: Effect of dynamic load cycling on diaphragm impedance in alkaline electrolysers: bench-scale experiments and model calibration
abstract: Repeated start–stop and load-ramping cycles representative of wind-coupled operation were imposed on two commercial Zirfon diaphragm samples mounted in a single-cell test fixture over 1 200 hours. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy was recorded every 100 hours to track diaphragm ionic resistance. Scanning electron microscopy images were taken at 400-hour intervals to observe pore structure evolution. Ionic resistance increased by 31% over the test period under aggressive cycling (four ramp events per hour) compared to 14% under steady-state operation. A modified empirical degradation model with a cycling-frequency term was calibrated against the impedance data; the model fits observed resistance with a mean absolute error of 1.9 mΩ cm². The calibrated model was integrated into the system-level simulation tool developed in earlier work to assess the additional cost penalty imposed by high-frequency curtailment signals.

title: Two-tissue compartment modelling of 18F-FDG kinetics in primary bone sarcomas: reproducibility of microparameters across two scan sessions
abstract: Dynamic 18F-FDG PET acquisition was performed in 22 patients with histologically confirmed primary bone sarcomas before the start of chemotherapy. Two 60-minute dynamic scans were obtained seven days apart to assess test–retest reproducibility of the influx rate constant Ki, the phosphorylation rate k3, and the dephosphorylation rate k4. Arterial blood sampling was used as the gold-standard input function, and results were compared with image-derived input functions from the descending aorta. The two-tissue irreversible compartment model provided the best fit in 18 of 22 cases based on Akaike information criterion. Ki showed intraclass correlation coefficients above 0.88 for both input function methods. k3 was more variable, with ICC of 0.72 using image-derived input functions. Tumour volume of interest delineation using a 40 percent SUV threshold was the dominant source of variability. Findings suggest that Ki derived from image-based input functions is sufficiently reproducible for use as a response biomarker in multicentre studies, whereas k3 requires standardised arterial sampling.

title: Patlak graphical analysis versus full compartmental modelling for response assessment after induction chemotherapy in osteosarcoma: a comparison in 34 patients
abstract: This retrospective study compared Patlak graphical analysis and full two-tissue compartmental modelling for quantifying 18F-FDG uptake changes after two cycles of induction chemotherapy in 34 patients with osteosarcoma of the femur or tibia. Dynamic PET data were acquired before treatment and after the second chemotherapy cycle. Tumour-to-background ratios, Ki from Patlak analysis, and the microparameters K1 through k4 from compartmental fitting were correlated with histopathological tumour necrosis graded at surgery using the Huvos scale. Patlak-derived Ki showed a statistically significant negative correlation with Huvos grade (r = −0.71, p < 0.001). Full compartmental modelling added marginal predictive value for Huvos grades I and II but was superior in identifying grade IV responders, reaching sensitivity of 91 percent versus 76 percent for Patlak analysis. Scan time could be reduced to 40 minutes without significant loss of precision for Patlak analysis. Patlak Ki is recommended as a practical primary endpoint for response monitoring in clinical trials.

title: Parametric Ki maps in soft-tissue sarcoma: generation using basis function method and correlation with histological grade
abstract: Parametric imaging of the net influx rate Ki was performed voxel-wise in 27 patients with soft-tissue sarcoma (nine high-grade, eleven intermediate-grade, seven low-grade by FNCLCC grading). Dynamic 18F-FDG PET data spanning 60 minutes were processed with a basis function implementation of the Patlak model to generate whole-tumour Ki maps. Mean Ki, 75th percentile Ki, and the heterogeneity index defined as the coefficient of variation across tumour voxels were extracted. High-grade tumours showed significantly higher mean Ki (mean 0.038 mL/min/g, SD 0.009) than low-grade tumours (mean 0.014 mL/min/g, SD 0.005). The heterogeneity index did not differ significantly between grade groups but showed potential for distinguishing necrotic from viable tumour subregions. Comparison with standard SUVmax indicated that Ki outperformed SUVmax in separating high from intermediate grade (AUC 0.84 versus 0.73). The basis function method converged in all voxels with acceptable noise amplification, supporting clinical feasibility.

title: Effect of blood glucose level on 18F-FDG kinetic parameters in musculoskeletal tumours: a prospective study
abstract: Elevated blood glucose competes with 18F-FDG for cellular uptake and may distort kinetic parameters if not corrected. Forty-one patients with musculoskeletal tumours (23 bone, 18 soft-tissue) underwent dynamic 18F-FDG PET with simultaneous blood glucose measurement. Scans were repeated under normo- and hyperglycaemic conditions induced by glucose loading in a subset of 14 patients. Ki, k3, and SUVmax were compared between conditions. Ki decreased by a mean of 18 percent under hyperglycaemia (blood glucose 8.4–12.1 mmol/L) when no glucose correction was applied. After applying the Lúdvigsen correction formula, residual difference between conditions dropped to 4 percent and was non-significant. k3 was less sensitive to hyperglycaemia than Ki. SUVmax correction using the blood glucose multiplier performed equivalently to the kinetic-based correction for Ki. Protocols requiring fasting glucose below 7.0 mmol/L remain appropriate, but glucose-corrected Ki provides a reliable alternative when borderline hyperglycaemia cannot be avoided.

title: Image-derived input functions from different arterial territories for dynamic PET in pelvic sarcomas: accuracy and practical considerations
abstract: Arterial input function (AIF) derivation from image regions avoids invasive arterial cannulation but requires a sufficiently large arterial cross-section within the PET field of view. In patients with pelvic sarcomas, the descending aorta and common iliac arteries are both accessible. This study evaluated AIFs from four candidate regions in 18 patients undergoing dynamic 18F-FDG PET for pelvic or proximal femoral sarcomas, comparing them with direct radial artery sampling. The aortic AIF showed the lowest mean bias relative to arterial sampling (4.2 percent), while the common iliac artery showed 9.1 percent bias owing to partial volume effects at smaller vessel diameters. Partial volume correction using a recovery coefficient approach reduced iliac bias to 5.4 percent. Ki estimates derived from aortic image-derived AIFs were within 6 percent of gold-standard values in 15 of 18 patients. Iliac artery AIFs required correction to achieve comparable accuracy. Practical recommendations for field-of-view positioning are provided.

title: Kinetic modelling of 18F-NaF PET in osteoblastic lesions of bone sarcoma: a pilot study in 15 patients
abstract: 18F-sodium fluoride (18F-NaF) PET allows quantification of bone mineralisation turnover through a three-compartment model incorporating plasma fluoride kinetics. This pilot study applied two-tissue compartmental modelling to dynamic 18F-NaF PET data in 15 patients with osteosarcoma, nine of whom had predominantly osteoblastic lesions. Model-derived parameters K1 (fluoride delivery), k3 (incorporation into hydroxyapatite), and Ki (net fluoride uptake) were compared before and after induction chemotherapy. k3 decreased significantly after treatment in histological responders (Huvos III/IV), with a mean reduction of 42 percent (range 31–61 percent). SUVmax showed a mean reduction of 31 percent in the same group. In non-responders, k3 increased by a mean of 12 percent, possibly reflecting reactive osteoblastic activity. The three-compartment model was identifiable in 13 of 15 tumours. These preliminary results indicate that 18F-NaF kinetics may provide a complementary view of bone sarcoma response to 18F-FDG, meriting a larger prospective study.

title: Shortened dynamic acquisition windows for Patlak analysis in osteosarcoma: validation of a 20-minute late-phase protocol
abstract: Standard dynamic 18F-FDG PET protocols require 60-minute acquisitions, limiting patient throughput. This study validated a shortened late-phase protocol consisting of a 10-minute early dynamic frame (0–10 min) followed by a 10-minute static frame at 50–60 minutes post-injection, enabling Patlak analysis with only 20 minutes of scanner time. Forty patients with confirmed osteosarcoma were scanned using both full 60-minute and shortened protocols. Ki estimates from the shortened protocol showed strong agreement with full-protocol Ki (Bland–Altman mean difference −0.0012 mL/min/g, 95 percent limits of agreement −0.0051 to 0.0027). Sensitivity and specificity for predicting Huvos III/IV response were 85 and 82 percent for the shortened protocol versus 88 and 84 percent for the full protocol. The shortened protocol was accepted by all patients and allowed scheduling of two additional static whole-body scans per day. Clinical implementation guidance and suggested patient scheduling are provided.

title: Interobserver variability in tumour volume of interest delineation and its impact on kinetic parameters in 18F-FDG PET of soft-tissue sarcomas
abstract: Kinetic parameter extraction from dynamic PET data depends critically on the tumour volume of interest (VOI). This study quantified interobserver variability in VOI delineation among five readers with varying experience levels and assessed its propagation into kinetic parameters in 30 soft-tissue sarcoma patients. Readers delineated tumour VOIs using three methods: manual contouring, 40 percent SUVmax thresholding, and a gradient-based edge detection algorithm. Intraclass correlation for VOI volume across all readers was 0.76 for manual, 0.89 for threshold-based, and 0.91 for gradient-based delineation. Ki showed ICC of 0.83 with threshold-based delineation compared with 0.68 for manual. The gradient-based method yielded the highest ICC for Ki (0.87) and was least sensitive to reader experience. k3 variability exceeded Ki variability under all delineation strategies, with ICCs between 0.58 and 0.72. Automated gradient-based delineation is recommended for multicentre kinetic studies. A standardised delineation protocol and training requirements are proposed.

title: Tumour blood flow derived from early 18F-FDG PET frames as an independent predictor of histological response in Ewing sarcoma
abstract: Early-phase 18F-FDG PET frames (0–2 minutes post-injection) provide a surrogate measure of tumour perfusion reflecting the tracer delivery parameter K1. This study examined whether K1 extracted from two-tissue compartmental modelling independently predicted histological response in 28 patients with Ewing sarcoma. Patients underwent dynamic 18F-FDG PET before and after three cycles of VIDE chemotherapy. K1, Ki, and SUVmax were extracted from baseline and mid-treatment scans. In a logistic regression model predicting Huvos III/IV response, baseline K1 (OR 4.1, 95% CI 1.3–12.9) and relative change in Ki after treatment (OR 6.7, 95% CI 2.1–21.4) were independent predictors; baseline SUVmax was not significant when K1 was included. The combination of baseline K1 and relative Ki change reached AUC of 0.87. These results suggest that perfusion-related kinetics contain prognostic information beyond static uptake measures, and early frames should not be discarded in dynamic acquisition protocols.

title: Radiomics features extracted from parametric Ki maps versus static SUV maps in soft-tissue sarcoma: a comparative analysis
abstract: Radiomics applied to static SUV PET images captures tumour heterogeneity but conflates metabolic activity with perfusion and partial volume effects. This study tested whether first- and second-order radiomic features extracted from voxel-wise Patlak Ki maps offered different or superior information to SUVmax maps in 44 soft-tissue sarcoma patients. Ki maps were generated voxel-by-voxel using the basis function implementation. Thirty-eight radiomic features were extracted from both map types. Using cross-validated LASSO-penalised logistic regression, a four-feature Ki-map signature predicted high-grade tumours with AUC 0.83, compared with AUC 0.77 for the best SUV-map signature. Texture features from Ki maps (GLCM energy and GLRLM run-length non-uniformity) were selected by the model, while SUV maps favoured intensity-based features. Agreement between Ki-map and SUV-map radiomics predictions was moderate (Cohen's κ 0.54), indicating partially independent information. Ki-map radiomics may add value but requires prospective validation.

title: Multicentre reference values for 18F-FDG kinetic parameters in musculoskeletal tumours: a harmonisation study across four Balkan centres
abstract: Quantitative kinetic parameters can vary across centres due to differences in scanner models, reconstruction algorithms, and acquisition protocols. This study harmonised dynamic 18F-FDG PET protocols across four centres in Serbia, Slovenia, Croatia, and Hungary, collecting data from 91 patients with musculoskeletal tumours. All centres applied the same Patlak protocol with image-derived aortic input functions. A scanner-specific calibration phantom was scanned at each site and used to derive harmonisation factors. Before harmonisation, between-centre coefficient of variation for Ki was 19 percent; after applying harmonisation factors, it fell to 7 percent. Reference ranges for Ki stratified by tumour type (osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, synovial sarcoma, undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma) and anatomical location are reported. These reference values are intended to support multicentre clinical trials and provide a benchmark for interpreting single-centre results. The harmonisation pipeline is described in sufficient detail for other centres to adopt it.

title: Spectral analysis as a model-free alternative to compartmental fitting in dynamic 18F-FDG PET of bone sarcomas
abstract: Spectral analysis (SA) provides a model-free characterisation of tracer kinetics by decomposing the tissue time–activity curve into a sum of exponential components without a priori assumptions about compartmental structure. This study applied SA to dynamic 18F-FDG PET data from 35 bone sarcoma patients and compared results with two-tissue compartmental modelling regarding treatment response classification. SA-derived impulse response function integrals at early (0–10 min) and late (10–60 min) time intervals, the SA-derived irreversible uptake component (SA-Ki), and standard Patlak Ki were all evaluated against histopathological Huvos grade at surgery. SA-Ki showed comparable discrimination to Patlak Ki (AUC 0.82 versus 0.84, p = 0.61). The early SA component correlated with K1 from compartmental modelling (r = 0.79), confirming its perfusion sensitivity. SA was more robust when the model order was set between 30 and 60 components. SA may be preferred when model selection between reversible and irreversible compartmental structures is uncertain.

title: Deep learning-based automated delineation of bone sarcoma on dynamic 18F-FDG PET: impact on downstream kinetic parameter estimation
abstract: Manual or threshold-based VOI delineation is time-consuming and user-dependent. This study evaluated a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained to segment bone sarcoma lesions on dynamic 18F-FDG PET image series and assessed whether CNN-derived VOIs produced kinetic parameters equivalent to expert manual delineation. The CNN was trained on 210 annotated dynamic PET studies from three centres and tested on 47 independent cases from the Novi Sad centre. Dice overlap between CNN and expert VOIs was 0.79 (IQR 0.71–0.86). Ki derived from CNN VOIs agreed with expert-VOI Ki within 8 percent in 41 of 47 cases (Bland–Altman 95% limits of agreement −0.0044 to 0.0039 mL/min/g). Cases with Dice below 0.65 were predominantly small or flat cortical lesions. CNN delineation time was under 12 seconds per case versus 14 minutes for manual contouring. Integration with the clinical PET workstation is in progress. The pretrained model weights are available upon request.

title: First-order texture features of T2-weighted liver MRI for discrimination of early versus advanced hepatic fibrosis
abstract: Texture analysis extracts statistical descriptors from image intensity distributions without requiring segmentation of individual lesions. In this study, first-order texture features—mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis, and entropy—were computed from T2-weighted fast spin-echo images of 110 patients with biopsy-confirmed fibrosis grades F0 to F4 (METAVIR). A liver parenchyma region of interest was manually delineated in three axial slices per patient by a single radiologist. Entropy and kurtosis showed the strongest univariate association with fibrosis grade (Spearman ρ = 0.67 and −0.58, respectively). A logistic regression model combining five texture features achieved AUC 0.84 for binary classification of F0–F1 versus F2–F4. Bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals were 0.77–0.90. Feature extraction was performed using in-house MATLAB routines. The study demonstrates that simple intensity statistics carry diagnostically relevant information about hepatic microstructural change.

title: Compressed sensing reconstruction of undersampled paediatric chest CT: simulation on clinical data
abstract: Compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction allows image recovery from fewer measurements than classical sampling theory requires, provided the signal is sparse in some transform domain. We retrospectively selected 28 paediatric chest CT acquisitions (ages 2–16 years) and simulated sinogram undersampling at ratios of 2×, 3×, and 4× by zeroing Poisson-noisy projection views in the raw data domain. Total variation (TV) minimisation and wavelet sparsity constraints were applied in an iterative CS framework implemented in MATLAB. Structural similarity index (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) were computed against full-data FBP references. TV-based CS at 2× undersampling yielded mean SSIM 0.91 ± 0.03; wavelet sparsity performed comparably at 2× but degraded faster at higher ratios. Streak artefacts near the mediastinum were the primary failure mode at 4×. The simulation suggests 2× undersampling is achievable with acceptable quality, motivating future prospective scan protocol design.

title: Segment-specific variation of Ktrans across white matter tracts in cerebral small vessel disease: a DTI-guided DCE-MRI analysis
abstract: White matter tracts differ in their vulnerability to microvascular injury in cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). Thirty-one patients with MRI-confirmed CSVD and 18 controls underwent combined diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and DCE-MRI at 3T. Probabilistic tractography defined seven bilateral white matter tract segments including the corticospinal tract, forceps major, and superior longitudinal fasciculus. Ktrans was sampled within each tract mask. Fractional anisotropy (FA) was inversely correlated with Ktrans across all tracts (Spearman r = −0.61, p < 0.001). The highest Ktrans elevation in CSVD patients was observed in the anterior thalamic radiation (0.0071 ± 0.0019 min⁻¹) compared with controls (0.0029 ± 0.0008 min⁻¹). Mean diffusivity showed a weaker association with Ktrans than FA. These findings indicate that BBB leakage and microstructural damage co-localise within specific vulnerable tracts, providing a rationale for targeted tract-based biomarkers in CSVD monitoring.

title: Machine learning classification of thyroid nodules using elastographic and B-mode ultrasound features
abstract: This study explored whether combining quantitative ultrasound features with machine learning could improve malignancy classification beyond single-threshold approaches. A dataset of 312 nodules (89 malignant) was assembled retrospectively from two centres. Input features included SWE mean and maximum stiffness, strain ratio, nodule diameter, echogenicity grade, margin regularity, calcification type, and Doppler vascularity score. Four classifiers were compared: logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and a gradient-boosted tree. Five-fold cross-validation was used; test performance was evaluated on a held-out 20% split. The gradient-boosted tree achieved the best AUC of 0.94 (95% CI 0.91–0.97), sensitivity 87.6%, specificity 91.3%. SWE maximum stiffness and calcification type were the two most important features by permutation importance. Logistic regression performed nearly as well (AUC 0.91), suggesting that a simple weighted score could approximate the ensemble model in routine practice.

title: Poverenje u obavezni penzijski sistem i sklonost dobrovoljnoj štednji: empirijska analiza na uzorku zaposlenih u Vojvodini
abstract: Rad ispituje vezu između stepena poverenja u državni penzijski sistem i participacije u dobrovoljnoj štednji za penziju na uzorku od 487 zaposlenih lica starosti između 25 i 55 godina iz Vojvodine, anketiranih u periodu oktobar–decembar 2023. godine. Podaci su prikupljeni strukturiranim upitnikom koji uključuje adaptirane skale poverenja razvijene za posttanzicioni kontekst, kao i sociodemografske i ekonomske kontrolne varijable. Logistička regresija pokazuje da zaposleni koji izražavaju nizak nivo poverenja u solventnost penzijskog sistema imaju 2,3 puta veće izglede da štede dobrovoljno, ali je veličina ušteđevine statistički ne razlikuje od grupe s visokim poverenjem. Moderatorski efekat finansijske pismenosti je značajan samo za ispitanike sa višim obrazovanjem. Nalaz upućuje na to da nedostatak poverenja podstiče participaciju, ali ne i dovoljnu akumulaciju kapitala, što ima direktne implikacije za dizajn podsticajnih mera penzijske politike u Srbiji.

title: Present Bias and Emergency Savings Buffers: Evidence from a Laboratory Experiment with Serbian University Students
abstract: This study uses a controlled laboratory experiment to measure present bias and its relationship to emergency savings behaviour among 214 undergraduate and graduate students at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica. Participants completed a series of binary intertemporal choice tasks implemented in z-Tree, from which individual quasi-hyperbolic discounting parameters (β, δ) were estimated. A follow-up survey measured self-reported emergency fund adequacy and recent savings behaviour. The estimated mean β of 0.71 (SD = 0.18) confirms substantial present bias in the sample. Regression analysis shows that each 0.10-unit decrease in β is associated with a 14.3 percentage-point reduction in the probability of holding savings equivalent to one month of expenses. The effect persists after controlling for income, parental wealth, and financial literacy scores. The results suggest that present bias, rather than income constraints alone, is a meaningful predictor of inadequate precautionary savings among young adults in Serbia, pointing to the potential relevance of commitment savings products in this market.

title: Bihejvioralni obrasci štednje domaćinstava u posttanzicionim ekonomijama: pregled literature i istraživački okvir
abstract: Rad sistematizuje empirijsku literaturu o bihejvioralnim odrednicama štednje domaćinstava objavljenu u periodu od 2005. do 2022. godine, s fokusom na zemlje Centralne i Istočne Evrope i Zapadnog Balkana. Pregledom 74 studije identifikovana su tri dominantna teorijska okvira: prospektna teorija i averzija prema gubitku, hiperbolično diskontovanje i pristranost ka sadašnjosti, te institucionalno poverenje. Analiza ukazuje na metodološku heterogenost – 41% studija oslanja se isključivo na anketne podatke, dok eksperimentalni i neuroekomski pristupi ostaju marginalni u regionalnom kontekstu. Poseban doprinos rada jeste identifikacija istraživačke praznine u pogledu interakcije između poverenja u penzijski sistem i bihejvioralnih pristranosti, naročito u kontekstu Srbije gde su raspoloživi longitudinalni podaci o štednji domaćinstava ograničeni. Na osnovu pregleda predlaže se integrisani istraživački okvir za buduća empirijska istraživanja u regionu.

title: Loss Aversion Asymmetry in Household Saving Decisions: A Cross-Country Comparison Between Serbia and Slovakia
abstract: Using matched survey data collected in 2024 from 612 households in Serbia (Novi Sad and Subotica metropolitan areas) and 589 households in Slovakia (Bratislava and Košice), this study tests whether the degree of loss aversion predicts the household gross saving rate and the composition of financial assets. Loss aversion coefficients were elicited through a standardised mixed-gamble task administered online. Ordinary least squares and quantile regression models are estimated separately for each country and for the pooled sample. In Serbia, a one-unit increase in the loss aversion coefficient (λ) is associated with a 1.8 percentage-point increase in the gross saving rate (p < 0.01), conditional on income, household size, and employment status. In Slovakia the coefficient is positive but smaller (0.9 pp) and less precisely estimated. Serbian respondents allocate a significantly higher share of savings to cash and bank deposits compared to Slovak households, consistent with loss aversion theory. Cross-country differences in the λ–saving relationship are partially explained by differences in pension system trust and macroeconomic volatility experience.

title: Cyber Insurance Pricing for SMEs Using Credibility Theory: Evidence from Vojvodina
abstract: This paper applies Bühlmann–Straub credibility theory to cyber insurance pricing for small and medium enterprises, using a dataset of 127 SMEs in the Vojvodina region that participated in a voluntary risk disclosure programme between 2019 and 2022. Each firm reports annual cyber incident counts and aggregate losses; the dataset yields 381 firm–year observations. Credibility weights are computed per firm size class (micro, small, medium) and per industry sector. The resulting credibility-weighted frequency and severity parameters are compared to class-mean priors; the average credibility weight across firms is 0.41, reflecting the limited length of individual histories. Simulated insurance premiums based on the credibility model differ from those based on class-mean parameters by up to 23% for individual firms. The paper discusses how technology parks and business incubators could facilitate the data pooling arrangements needed to expand such credibility datasets.

title: Determinants of Sovereign Yield Spreads in Western Balkan Economies: A Panel Data Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the macroeconomic and institutional determinants of sovereign yield spreads for five Western Balkan economies—Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Albania, and Montenegro—over the period 2005–2010. Using a fixed-effects panel model with quarterly data drawn from IMF Article IV reports and national central banks, the study tests whether fiscal balance, external debt ratios, GDP growth, and institutional quality indices significantly predict the spread over German Bunds. Results indicate that the fiscal balance-to-GDP ratio carries the largest coefficient in absolute terms, with a one-percentage-point deterioration associated with an average spread widening of 38 basis points. Institutional quality proxies based on World Bank governance indicators are statistically significant only when interacted with debt levels above 45 percent of GDP. The findings suggest that markets assign a nonlinear penalty to fiscal deterioration in structurally weak institutional environments, a pattern not observed in comparable Central and Eastern European EU members during the same period.

title: Currency Board Arrangements and Sovereign Risk Perception: Evidence from Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: Bosnia and Herzegovina has operated a currency board pegged to the euro since 1997. This study asks whether the arrangement has reduced sovereign risk premia relative to comparable economies with managed floats over the period 2000–2011. The empirical strategy employs a synthetic control method, constructing a counterfactual borrowing cost trajectory from a donor pool of seven small European economies with similar income levels and openness ratios. Quarterly data on domestic bond yields and external commercial borrowing spreads are sourced from the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the World Bank's Quarterly External Debt Statistics. The synthetic control closely tracks observed spreads before 2008 and diverges afterward, with the currency board associated with spreads roughly 55–80 basis points lower than the counterfactual during the 2008–2009 crisis. The discipline imposed on monetary financing appears to have provided a credibility buffer when global risk appetite collapsed, though the mechanism operates differently depending on whether the sovereign borrows primarily in domestic or foreign currency.

title: Contagion or Fundamentals? Decomposing Western Balkan Spread Movements During the 2011–2012 European Debt Crisis
abstract: This study decomposes quarterly changes in sovereign yield spreads for Serbia, Montenegro, and North Macedonia during the 2011–2012 European sovereign debt crisis into a component attributable to domestic fundamentals and a component reflecting contagion from Eurozone periphery countries. The decomposition uses a two-step procedure: first, a fundamentals-predicted spread is constructed from a long-run FMOLS model estimated on pre-crisis data; second, residuals from this model during the crisis window are regressed on measures of Eurozone periphery stress (Italian–German spread, VIX, and a CDS index for Greece, Portugal, and Spain). Contagion accounts for 41–58 percent of the observed spread widening across the three countries, with Serbia displaying the highest contagion loading. The result has practical implications for policymakers, as spread pressures driven by external contagion cannot be offset through domestic fiscal adjustment alone and may call for pre-arranged credit lines or reserve buffers.

title: Collateral Demands and Female-Owned Businesses: Evidence from Serbian Commercial Bank Records, 2005–2010
abstract: This paper examines whether Serbian commercial banks imposed systematically higher collateral requirements on female-owned SMEs compared to otherwise comparable male-owned firms between 2005 and 2010. Using a matched sample of 1,240 loan applications drawn from branch-level credit files at four mid-sized Serbian banks, we estimate logistic and OLS models controlling for firm age, sector, loan size, and creditworthiness proxies derived from audited financial statements. Female sole proprietors faced collateral-to-loan ratios approximately 14 percentage points higher than their male counterparts after controlling for observable firm characteristics. The gap was largest in manufacturing and construction and smallest in retail trade. We find no significant interaction between loan officer gender and the collateral differential, suggesting that the disparity reflects institutional policies rather than individual discretion alone. The results are robust to alternative collateral definitions and to the exclusion of micro-firms with fewer than five employees. Implications for supervisory guidance and credit policy in transition banking markets are discussed.

title: Supervisory Attention to Gender Equity in SME Lending: A Survey of Banking Regulators in Central and Eastern Europe
abstract: This paper reports findings from a structured online survey of senior supervisory officials at twelve central banks and financial regulatory authorities in Central and Eastern Europe, conducted in late 2023. Respondents answered 34 questions covering whether gender-disaggregated data is collected in credit registries, whether gender equity in SME lending is an explicit supervisory objective, what enforcement tools exist, and what obstacles impede reform. Eight of twelve authorities collect no gender-disaggregated data in their credit registries. Only three have issued guidance specifically addressing gender in SME loan assessment. Supervisory capacity, legal mandate, and political prioritisation are cited as the main barriers. The survey also identifies three jurisdictions—Poland, Romania, and Slovakia—that have taken incremental steps toward disaggregated reporting. The paper proposes a minimum data standard and a tiered supervisory checklist that could be adopted without primary legislation in most surveyed jurisdictions.

title: Retail Sukuk for Infrastructure Financing in Serbia: Fiscal, Legal, and Structural Feasibility
abstract: This working paper assesses the feasibility of the Republic of Serbia issuing retail sukuk to finance infrastructure projects, drawing on the precedents of the UK's Al-Rayan sukuk programme and Indonesia's retail sovereign sukuk series. The analysis covers three dimensions: fiscal (whether sukuk issuance costs are competitive with conventional bond issuance given Serbia's current sovereign rating of BB+ and prevailing yields), legal (the amendments to the Law on Public Debt and Law on Securities required to enable asset-lease sukuk), and structural (the selection of state-owned assets suitable for the underlying lease arrangement without triggering constitutional restrictions on disposal of public property). The paper estimates that a five-year, EUR 200 million ijara sukuk linked to transport infrastructure could be priced within 20–35 basis points of an equivalent eurobond, making it viable if the government values the diversification of the investor base. The paper was prepared as a policy background document for a faculty roundtable held in November 2025.
