title: Delta-of-Delta Encoding for Monotonic Sensor Counters in Relational Column Stores
abstract: Monotonic counter sequences produced by industrial pulse sensors exhibit strong first-order and second-order differences that standard LZ-family compressors exploit poorly when applied at the row level. This paper evaluates a purely arithmetic delta-of-delta scheme applied within a columnar storage engine on sequences of 32-bit unsigned integers sampled at 1 kHz. Experiments use 14 days of vibration counter data from a water-treatment facility logging 48 sensor channels, yielding roughly 58 billion raw values. The scheme is compared against Snappy, LZ4, and a Gorilla-style float codec adapted for integers. Delta-of-delta achieves a compression ratio of 18.3:1 against raw binary, outperforming LZ4 (11.1:1) with 40 % lower decompression CPU time. Encoding throughput on a single core reaches 920 MB/s. The paper also derives a closed-form bound on the representable range for a fixed bit-width delta register and proposes a lightweight overflow-detection branch that adds under 2 % latency overhead.

title: Bitmap Index Compression Trade-offs for Low-Cardinality Attributes in Time-Series Tables
abstract: Bitmap indexes over low-cardinality categorical attributes are common in data-warehouse workloads, but their behaviour on append-only time-series tables with frequent partial scans has received less attention. We compare uncompressed bitmaps, WAH (Word-Aligned Hybrid), CONCISE, and Roaring Bitmaps on synthetic and real sensor-classification workloads where cardinality ranges from 4 to 256 distinct values and table sizes range from 10 million to 2 billion rows. Real data come from a Serbian environmental monitoring network logging air-quality sensor states at 10-second intervals over 18 months across 31 stations. Roaring Bitmaps reduce index size by 55–72 % relative to WAH while maintaining AND/OR operation throughput within 8 % of uncompressed bitmaps for selective queries. We identify a crossover point at cardinality 64 above which WAH outperforms Roaring in sequential full-scan aggregation. Query plans that choose index type adaptively based on observed cardinality at load time reduce total query time by 23 % in the mixed workload benchmark.

title: Columnar Storage Layout for Mixed-Rate Sensor Streams: Alignment, Padding, and Scan Cost
abstract: Industrial sensor networks rarely emit all channels at a uniform rate. A pressure transducer may log at 100 Hz while a thermal sensor logs at 1 Hz, creating mixed-rate column groups within a single logical schema. Storing such streams in a uniform columnar layout either wastes space through padding or requires indirection structures that slow scans. This chapter surveys three physical layout strategies—uniform-stride padding, epoch-grouped variable-stride, and separate per-rate column families—and analyses their scan cost analytically and experimentally. Experiments use a 90-day dataset of 112 sensor channels from a pilot manufacturing line at 14 distinct sampling rates, totalling 430 GB uncompressed. Epoch-grouped variable-stride achieves the best compromise: 31 % less storage than uniform-stride padding with scan overhead under 6 % compared to single-rate baselines. Practical guidelines for schema designers are derived, including a heuristic for grouping channels into rate classes.

title: Efficient SUM and AVG Aggregation Over Compressed Integer Columns Without Full Decompression
abstract: Computing SUM and AVG over delta-compressed integer columns typically requires full decompression before the arithmetic pass. We present a method that accumulates partial sums directly over delta-coded blocks by exploiting the algebraic structure of prefix-sum reconstruction, reducing decompression to the final carry-propagation step. The technique is implemented inside a fork of an open-source columnar engine (DuckDB-compatible file format) and evaluated on six months of electricity sub-metering data at 1-second resolution across 200 household circuits, approximately 31 billion rows. End-to-end SUM throughput increases by 1.8× on a single core and 2.1× on four cores compared to decompress-then-aggregate. The method generalises to COUNT DISTINCT with HyperLogLog sketches embedded in compressed blocks, yielding a 1.4× speedup there. Memory bandwidth measurements confirm that savings come primarily from reduced cache pressure rather than reduced arithmetic.

title: Adaptive Bit-Packing Width Selection for High-Frequency Accelerometer Streams
abstract: Fixed-width bit-packing assigns the same bit-width to every value in a block, wasting bits when the dynamic range is temporarily narrow. We propose a lightweight adaptive scheme that re-estimates the required bit-width every 512 values using a running maximum register and encodes the width in a 6-bit block header. The scheme targets 16-bit signed accelerometer samples recorded at 4 kHz. A corpus of 22 hours of vibration data from rotating machinery in a Serbian food-processing plant (seven machine types, 63 sensors) is used for evaluation. Adaptive bit-packing reduces storage by 19–34 % relative to fixed 16-bit packing and by 9–17 % relative to fixed optimal-width packing computed offline. Decompression speed on SSE4.2 SIMD instructions remains within 4 % of fixed-width scalar decompression. We also report failure modes when the running maximum underestimates abrupt transients and propose a saturating-rollback mechanism.

title: Zone Maps vs. Min-Max Indexes in Columnar Engines: Behaviour Under Skewed Sensor Value Distributions
abstract: Zone maps (per-block min-max metadata) are a standard pruning mechanism in columnar databases, but their effectiveness degrades when value distributions within blocks are highly skewed or multi-modal, which is common in sensor streams that include fault and alarm states. We characterise the pruning rate of zone maps analytically as a function of block size and intra-block value variance and validate the model on four real sensor datasets: river-level gauges, photovoltaic panel voltage logs, industrial pressure manifolds, and HVAC temperature arrays. Block sizes of 512 to 65536 values are tested. For multi-modal distributions the pruning rate drops below 30 % even at block size 512. We evaluate two lightweight alternatives—quantile sketches and learned min-max predictors trained on preceding blocks—and find that a 7-quantile sketch stored in 28 bytes per block restores pruning rates to above 70 % at a metadata overhead of 0.03 % of raw data size. Implementation notes for integration into an open-source columnar engine are provided.

title: Compression-Aware Query Planning for Time-Bounded Window Aggregations
abstract: Time-bounded window aggregations (e.g., SUM over the last 15 minutes) on append-only sensor tables require accessing a suffix of one or more compressed blocks. The query planner must decide whether to decompress an entire boundary block or to seek within it, a choice that depends on block size, compression codec, and selectivity. We formalise this as a cost model parameterised by measured decompression throughput, seek latency, and block fill factor, and integrate it into a rule-based planner for a columnar storage engine. Evaluation uses six months of power-grid sensor data at 500 Hz from a regional substation, with window widths ranging from 1 second to 24 hours. The cost-model-guided planner reduces query latency by 28–41 % over a baseline that always decompresses full boundary blocks, and by 12–18 % over a simpler heuristic that always seeks. The model's calibration requires a 90-second profiling pass run once at database initialisation.

title: On-Disk Representation of Irregular-Timestamp Sensor Logs: Separating Time and Value Columns
abstract: Most time-series storage literature assumes uniform sampling intervals, so timestamp columns are stored implicitly as a start time plus stride. Environmental and IoT sensors with event-driven reporting produce irregular timestamps that must be stored explicitly. We study the compression and scan-performance implications of separating timestamp columns from value columns on disk versus interleaving them. Three physical layouts are compared on a 14-month dataset of soil-moisture readings from 180 field sensors distributed across Vojvodina, Serbia, with inter-arrival times varying from 30 seconds to 45 minutes. Separating columns allows timestamp and value codecs to be chosen independently; Gorilla-style XOR encoding for floating-point values combined with FOR (Frame of Reference) encoding for microsecond-resolution timestamps reduces combined storage by 26 % relative to interleaved LZ4. Random-access latency increases by 11 % due to two separate seeks, which is acceptable for analytical workloads but warrants consideration for point-lookup-heavy use cases.

title: Benchmarking In-Database Compression Codecs for Sub-Second Rollup Queries on a Single-Node Commodity Server
abstract: Sub-second rollup latency over billion-row sensor tables is achievable on a single commodity server if the codec, block size, and aggregation strategy are matched to the query workload. We construct a reproducible benchmark using publicly available hardware (AMD EPYC 7003, 128 GB DDR4, NVMe SSD) and four synthetic workloads derived from real sensor patterns: smooth analogue signals, step-change switching signals, random noise, and mixed. Eight codecs are tested: LZ4, Zstandard-3, Zstandard-9, Gorilla float, delta-varint, bit-packing, PFOR, and a cascade of delta followed by bit-packing. Rollup query latency, compression ratio, and encode/decode throughput are reported for block sizes of 256, 1024, and 4096 values. Delta+bit-packing on smooth signals achieves 0.38-second rollup over 2 billion rows with a 21:1 ratio. No single codec dominates across all workloads; a decision table mapping signal type to codec is provided. All benchmark code and datasets are released under an open licence.

title: Predicting Compressibility of Sensor Blocks from Lightweight Signal Statistics
abstract: Choosing a compression codec at write time without compressing the data first requires a proxy metric that correlates with compression ratio. We evaluate seven lightweight statistics—range, variance, zero-crossing rate, run-length entropy estimate, lag-1 autocorrelation, approximate quantile spread, and bit-reversal entropy—as predictors of final compression ratio for LZ4, Zstandard, delta+PFOR, and Gorilla across a corpus of 4.1 million 1024-value blocks drawn from 11 sensor deployments spanning energy, agriculture, and manufacturing domains. Lag-1 autocorrelation alone achieves a Spearman rank correlation of 0.81 with the delta+PFOR ratio and can be computed in a single pass over a block in under 0.2 µs on the target hardware. A two-feature classifier (autocorrelation + range) correctly routes blocks to the best codec in 73 % of cases, reducing mean storage size by 14 % compared to a fixed-codec policy with no runtime overhead above 1.1 %.

title: Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata
abstract: Srpski jezik je morfološki bogat, što znači da ista leksema može imati nekoliko desetina flektivnih oblika. U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa. Koristimo tri stemera dostupna za srpski jezik — dva pravilo-zasnovana i jedan statistički — i kombinujemo ih s fonemskim kanonizacionim korakom opisanim u prethodnim radovima. Evaluacija je sprovedena na podskupu CLEF 2012 kolekcije koji sadrži dokumente u oba pisma. Rezultati pokazuju da redosled operacija (stemovanje pre ili posle normalizacije skripte) utiče na odziv, pri čemu stemovanje posle normalizacije daje konzistentno bolje rezultate za sve tri kombinacije (poboljšanje od 4 do 9 procentnih poena u MAP). Rad daje i analizu grešaka za 50 ručno pregledanih upita.

title: Fairness Metrics in Automated Roster Generation: A Survey and Comparative Study
abstract: Personnel scheduling systems that minimise cost or maximise coverage often produce rosters that are perceived as unfair by employees, leading to low adoption rates. This chapter surveys fairness criteria used in the scheduling literature, classifying them into four categories: load equity, preference satisfaction, distribution of undesirable shifts, and seniority-based entitlements. For each category, we describe representative mathematical formulations and discuss their computational implications. A comparative experiment on a common dataset of 12 nurse scheduling instances illustrates the trade-offs between cost-oriented and fairness-oriented objective functions. Results confirm that including fairness penalties increases objective function values by 8–31% relative to cost-only optima, but that most of this increase occurs at small fairness weight values, suggesting that modest fairness investments yield proportionally large equity gains. The chapter concludes with a discussion of participatory design methods for eliciting employee-specific fairness weights.

title: Zaštita manjinskih poverilaca pri potvrdi plana reorganizacije: analiza srpskog Zakona o stečaju
abstract: Rad analizira mehanizme zaštite manjinskih poverilaca u postupku potvrde plana reorganizacije prema Zakonu o stečaju Republike Srbije iz 2009. godine, s izmenama do 2017. U fokusu su materijalni i proceduralni standardi koje sud mora primeniti pre potvrde plana, uključujući test najboljeg interesa poverilaca i pravila o glasanju po klasama. Istraživanje se zasniva na pregledu 74 predmeta iz baze Privrednog apelacionog suda u periodu 2012–2017, uz kvalitativnu analizu obrazloženja sudskih odluka. Rezultati ukazuju da srpski sudovi dosledno primenjuju formalni test potvrde, ali retko vrše samostalnu ekonomsku procenu vrednosti imovine dužnika, oslanjajući se gotovo isključivo na nalaze stečajnih upravnika. Identifikovane su tri kategorije sudske prakse: pasivna potvrda, ograničena provjera i aktivna kontrola. Zaključak je da su zakonske odredbe o zaštiti poverilaca nepotpune u delu koji se tiče cross-class cramdown scenarija.

Metodom strukturirane komparativne analize obrađeni su zakonski tekstovi, podzakonski akti i reprezentativni sudski predmeti iz perioda 2010–2020. Posebna pažnja posvećena je načinu na koji svaki sistem definiše klase poverilaca, kvorum za glasanje i uslove pod kojima sud može potvrditi plan uprkos protivljenju jedne ili više klasa. Nalazi pokazuju da sve četiri jurisdikcije zadržavaju visok prag zahteva za glasanje (75–80% prema vrednosti potraživanja), dok su standardi ekonomske procene vrednosti dužnika manje precizno razrađeni. Identifikuju se i sistemske razlike između jurisdikcija common law orijentacije i kontinentalnopravnih obrazaca koji su dominirali u procesu posttranzicijskog zakonodavnog transfera.

title: Transposition of the EU Preventive Restructuring Directive in Western Balkan Candidate States: A Gap Analysis
abstract: This article examines the extent to which the legal frameworks of four Western Balkan EU candidate states—Serbia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, and Albania—align with the requirements of Directive (EU) 2019/1023 on preventive restructuring frameworks. The analysis focuses specifically on provisions relevant to micro and small enterprises (MSEs), including early warning mechanisms, debtor-in-possession management, and plan confirmation standards. The study draws on a combination of statutory comparison, legislative history review, and semi-structured interviews conducted with twelve insolvency practitioners in Belgrade, Skopje, and Podgorica during 2021–2022. Findings indicate that existing frameworks in all four states contain partial functional equivalents to Directive requirements, but diverge significantly on cross-class cramdown thresholds and the treatment of equity holders under reorganisation plans. The article proposes a set of minimum legislative adjustments that would enable candidate states to align their systems without wholesale statutory replacement, emphasising the constraints imposed by limited judicial capacity at the commercial court level.

title: The Best-Interest-of-Creditors Test in Micro-Enterprise Insolvency: Valuation Problems and Judicial Practice in Serbia and Croatia
abstract: The best-interest-of-creditors test requires that no dissenting creditor receive less under a confirmed reorganisation plan than they would in liquidation. While the standard is well-established in doctrine, its practical application in proceedings involving micro-enterprises raises acute valuation problems: asset values are often illiquid, accounting records are unreliable, and courts lack in-house financial expertise. This study examines 49 confirmed and 21 rejected reorganisation plans drawn from the commercial courts of Serbia (2015–2022) and Croatia (2017–2022), coding judicial reasoning against a structured analytical rubric. The data reveal that courts in both jurisdictions apply the test in a largely formalistic manner, accepting plan-proponent valuations without independent scrutiny in approximately 68% of the Serbian and 54% of the Croatian cases reviewed. The article identifies the structural conditions under which independent judicial valuation is most likely to occur and proposes procedural amendments—including mandatory appointment of independent valuers in contested micro-enterprise proceedings—drawing on the German InsO model.

title: Cross-Class Cramdown Under the 2019 EU Restructuring Directive: Doctrinal Limits and Interpretive Options for Small-State Implementers
abstract: The cross-class cramdown mechanism introduced by Directive 2019/1023 represents the most significant shift in European insolvency law in a generation, yet its implementation in smaller EU member states and candidate countries remains poorly studied. This article examines the doctrinal ambiguities of Articles 11 and 12 of the Directive—particularly the absolute priority rule and its permitted derogations—as they bear on reorganisation plans involving micro and small enterprises. The analysis employs a doctrinal method supplemented by comparative review of implementing legislation in Romania, Bulgaria, and Slovenia as of mid-2023. The article argues that the Directive's optional absolute priority rule derogation for SMEs creates a risk of forum-shopping in jurisdictions with open borders and integrated credit markets. Three interpretive options available to implementing legislators are assessed against the competing objectives of creditor protection, enterprise rescue, and procedural economy. The article concludes that the most coherent approach for small-state implementers is a conditional absolute priority rule with an explicit judicial override power calibrated to the size of the enterprise.

title: Reorganizacijski plan kao instrument očuvanja radnih mesta u malim preduzećima: pravni okvir i sudska praksa

Polazeći od normativne analize Zakona o stečaju i Zakona o radu, autor ispituje da li postojeći standardi potvrde plana pružaju sudu dovoljno diskrecionog prostora da vrednost radnih mesta eksplicitno ugradi u ocenu ekonomske opravdanosti plana. Analiza obuhvata 22 sudska predmeta u kojima su planovi reorganizacije malih preduzeća sadržali odredbe o zadržavanju zaposlenih, prikupljenih iz baza Privrednog apelacionog suda za period 2013–2023. Ustanovljeno je da srpski sudovi gotovo nikada ne pominju radna mesta kao faktor pri potvrdi plana, čak ni u slučajevima kada plan eksplicitno sadrži garantiju zapošljavanja. Rad zaključuje da bi izmena člana 157. Zakona o stečaju mogla ovlastiti sudove da u ograničenim okolnostima uzmu u obzir socijalne efekte plana, po uzoru na slovenački Zakon o finančnem poslovanju.

title: Procedural Barriers to Reorganisation Plan Confirmation for Micro-Enterprises: Evidence from Three Post-Transition Jurisdictions
abstract: This article investigates procedural—as opposed to substantive—barriers that prevent micro-enterprises from successfully completing reorganisation plan confirmation proceedings in Serbia, Bulgaria, and North Macedonia. The research is based on a mixed-methods design combining documentary analysis of 91 court files (Serbia n=38, Bulgaria n=29, North Macedonia n=24) from the period 2018–2024 and semi-structured interviews with 18 insolvency practitioners. Procedural barriers identified include: mandatory creditor committee formation requirements disproportionate to the number of creditors in micro-enterprise cases; rigid voting period deadlines that do not account for creditor notification delays in rural commercial registries; and fee structures that deter plan filings by sole-trader enterprises. Regression analysis of the file-level data indicates that each additional mandatory procedural step between plan submission and confirmation hearing is associated with a 9.4-day increase in total proceeding duration (p<0.01). The article proposes a simplified fast-track confirmation procedure for enterprises below €250,000 in total liabilities, drawing on the streamlined micro-enterprise track introduced in the Austrian Insolvenzordnung reform of 2021.

title: Algorithmic Hiring Tools and the Right Not to Be Subject to Automated Decisions: Lessons from Three Supervisory Authority Investigations in the EU
abstract: This paper analyses three supervisory authority investigations completed between 2019 and 2021 involving automated candidate screening or ranking tools used by large employers in France, the Netherlands, and Germany. The paper reconstructs each case from publicly available decisions, press releases, and guidance documents, and applies a common analytical framework organised around four questions: Was the decision 'solely' automated? Did a meaningful human review occur? Was the data subject informed in a legally adequate manner? Were the grounds for objection effectively communicated? The analysis finds that 'meaningful human review' is the most contested element across all three cases and that supervisory authorities apply the concept inconsistently. The paper discusses the implications for employers in Serbia and other EU candidate countries that import workforce management software developed and configured in EU member states, and argues that technology importers may inherit compliance risks embedded in tool design.

title: Out-of-Court Dispute Resolution for Cross-Border Consumer Complaints in the Western Balkans: Capacity Assessment and DSA Implications
abstract: The DSA imposes new out-of-court dispute-settlement obligations on online platforms (Art. 21) that presuppose functioning certified ADR bodies. This paper assesses the current state of consumer ADR infrastructure in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina through a combination of desk research and 12 semi-structured interviews with ADR administrators and consumer organisation representatives conducted in 2022–2023. The study finds that none of the three jurisdictions has a certified body meeting the EU ADR Directive's quality criteria in the cross-border e-commerce context, and that case volumes handled by existing consumer conciliation bodies are too low to sustain specialist expertise. The paper models three policy pathways—national ADR development, a regional joint body, and reliance on EU-based ODR platform referral—and evaluates each against feasibility, cost, and consumer-access criteria. It concludes that a regional joint mechanism, modelled loosely on the Nordic Consumer Ombudsman network, is the most proportionate medium-term solution.

title: Enforceability of Automated Settlement Triggers in Energy Commodity Contracts: A Comparative Study of Austrian and Serbian Law
abstract: This article presents a systematic doctrinal comparison of how automated settlement triggers embedded in energy commodity contracts would be treated under Austrian and Serbian contract law. The study analyses hypothetical gas and electricity forward contracts with code-based payment release mechanisms, testing enforceability against good faith requirements, prohibition of unfair contract terms, and the mandatory rules governing payment obligations in both jurisdictions. In Austria, the primary constraint is the general clause on abuse of rights under §1295 ABGB; in Serbia, the equivalent constraint arises under Articles 12 and 13 of the Law on Obligations. The article finds that both systems would uphold automated settlement triggers in business-to-business contracts provided the trigger conditions are sufficiently determinate and the counterparty retained meaningful opportunity to review the code before signing. A checklist of minimum drafting requirements is proposed.

title: Statička krutost slobodno lebdećeg planarnog stola sa trajnim magnetima u konfiguraciji Halbachove rešetke
abstract: Rad analizira statičku krutost planarnog levitacionog stola koji koristi Halbachovu permanentno-magnetnu rešetku u sprezi sa ravnim zavojnicama. Izrađen je analitički model koji uzima u obzir harmonike magnetnog polja do petog reda, a verifikacija je sprovedena trodimenzionalnom simulacijom metodom konačnih elemenata u paketu Magneto-3D v4.2. Eksperimentalni uzorci od dva prototipa pokazali su da vertikalna krutost iznosi 18,4 N/mm uz standardnu devijaciju od 0,3 N/mm u opsegu levitacione visine 0,4–1,2 mm. Horizontalna krutost u oba planarnih smera bila je negativna (destabilizujuća), vrednosti oko −2,1 N/mm, što zahteva aktivnu povratnu spregu. Rezultati su primenjeni na dimenzionisanje pojačivača struje i određivanje zahteva za krutost nosača u litografskim fiksturama. Rad daje tabele krutosti u funkciji geometrijskih parametara rešetke koje mogu poslužiti kao projektni alat.

title: Decentralised current-force linearisation for a six-degree-of-freedom magnetic levitation stage
abstract: Magnetic levitation stages used in semiconductor lithography exhibit strongly coupled, position-dependent force-to-current relationships that complicate controller design. This paper presents a decentralised linearisation scheme in which the force matrix is recomputed at each sampling interval using a pre-identified polynomial model of the coil-magnet geometry. The method avoids the full matrix inversion required by centralised approaches and reduces the real-time computation load by 34% on a fixed-point DSP running at 20 kHz. Experiments on a laboratory prototype with a 200 mm × 200 mm travel range demonstrated that the residual cross-coupling force after linearisation was below 8 mN over 95% of the workspace, compared with 47 mN for a fixed nominal matrix. Position noise spectral density at 1 Hz was 12 nm/√Hz in the horizontal axes and 6 nm/√Hz in the vertical axis. The linearisation scheme was validated at stage velocities up to 0.5 m/s and accelerations up to 4 m/s².

title: Thermal modelling of planar coil arrays under continuous scanning duty cycles
abstract: Heat generated in planar coil arrays of magnetically levitated stages is a principal source of thermally induced positioning error in lithography applications. A lumped-parameter thermal network was constructed for a four-phase coil array with 64 individual coils arranged on an aluminium baseplate with an internal water-cooling channel. Thermal resistance parameters were identified from step-response experiments using 32 embedded NTC sensors. Under a representative 60-second scanning duty cycle producing a mean coil current of 2.8 A RMS, the model predicted peak coil temperatures within 1.4°C of measured values. Simulations showed that increasing channel flow rate beyond 1.5 L/min yielded diminishing returns, reducing the peak temperature by less than 0.3°C per additional 0.5 L/min increment. A feedforward current-redistribution strategy based on the model reduced peak temperature rise by 18% without degrading positioning performance. The validated model has been integrated into the group's stage design tool.

title: Iterative learning control for repetitive scanning trajectories on a magnetically levitated stage
abstract: Semiconductor wafer scanning involves highly repetitive step-and-scan trajectories, making iterative learning control (ILC) a natural fit for reducing systematic tracking errors. This paper applies a norm-optimal ILC algorithm to the horizontal axes of a six-DOF magnetic levitation stage, using measured position error from the previous scan to update the feedforward input for the next. Convergence conditions are derived for the system's identified frequency-response model between 0 and 500 Hz. After 12 learning iterations over a 150 mm scan stroke at 0.3 m/s, the RMS tracking error dropped from 310 nm to 31 nm, a reduction factor of ten. The controller was robust to payload changes of ±150 g without relearning, provided the mass was distributed symmetrically. Stability in the presence of measurement noise was analysed and a noise-weighting matrix was tuned empirically. The practical implementation on the existing DSP hardware required no additional processing overhead beyond 7% of the available cycle budget.

title: Uticaj vibracija temelja na submikrometarsku pozicionu tačnost magnetno levitiranog stola
abstract: Magnetno levitiran pozicioni sto u principu nema mehaničku vezu sa okolnom konstrukcijom, ali vibracije temelja ipak utiču na performanse sistema kroz senzorski lanac i elektromagnetnu spregu sa nepokretnim delovima uređaja. U ovom radu merene su vibracije temelja u tipičnoj laboratorijskoj sredini u frekventnom opsegu 1–200 Hz koristeći tronožni seizmometar sa rezolucijom 0,1 nm/√Hz. Utvrđeno je da su dominantni izvori poremećaja u opsegu 8–25 Hz sa amplitudama do 180 nm. Izmerene vibracije ubrizgane su kao poremećaj u petlju upravljanja stola metodom signalnih injekcija, a ustanovljeno je da uzrokuju degradaciju pozicione nesigurnosti za faktor 2,3 u poređenju sa uslovima niskih vibracija. Predložen je aktivni kompenzator poremećaja zasnovan na akcelero-metarskim povratnim signalima koji smanjuje prenesene vibracije za 14 dB u kritičnom frekventnom opsegu. Eksperimentalna verifikacija sprovedena je na prototipu stola u laboratorijskim uslovima bez posebno izolovanog postamenta.

title: Coil geometry optimisation for force ripple reduction in planar Lorentz actuator arrays
abstract: Force ripple in planar Lorentz actuator arrays arises from spatial harmonics in the magnetic flux density distribution and from manufacturing tolerances in coil winding geometry. The paper quantifies these contributions separately for a 4 × 4 coil array using a combination of finite element simulations and measurements on individual coil specimens. Monte Carlo analysis with measured winding tolerance data (mean pitch deviation 38 µm, standard deviation 12 µm) shows that manufacturing variability accounts for approximately 40% of the total force ripple at the fundamental spatial frequency. A parametric study of coil aspect ratio, conductor cross-section, and end-turn geometry identified a configuration that reduced simulated force ripple from 1.8% to 0.7% of peak force while maintaining the same copper fill factor and total coil resistance. The optimised geometry was prototyped and tested; measured force ripple was 0.9%, the difference from simulation attributed to residual winding irregularities. The optimisation workflow is described in sufficient detail to be reproduced with standard FEA tools.

title: Real-time payload mass and centre-of-mass estimation for adaptive gravity compensation on a levitated stage
abstract: When a lithography fixture carries workpieces of varying mass and centroid position, a fixed gravity-compensation current profile introduces static tilt and z-axis offset errors. This paper presents a recursive least-squares estimator that identifies the payload mass and two-dimensional centre-of-mass location in real time from the six force and torque setpoints demanded by the position controller, without any additional sensors. Simulations using the identified plant model show convergence to within 2% of the true mass after 0.8 s for payloads ranging from 0.2 kg to 1.4 kg. On the physical stage, the estimator reduced static tilt error from up to 18 µrad to below 3 µrad across the tested payload range. The algorithm runs within a 50 µs sample interval on the existing control hardware with 11% processor utilisation. An analysis of estimator sensitivity to coil resistance drift with temperature is included, showing that a 5% resistance change causes less than 0.5% error in mass estimation.

title: A convolutional classifier for packaging defect detection deployed on a Zynq-7000 SoC
abstract: Deploying a trained convolutional neural network for surface defect classification directly onto an FPGA-based system-on-chip avoids the latency associated with PCIe-attached GPU cards and allows integration into existing programmable logic control architectures. This paper describes the quantisation, pruning and HLS synthesis workflow used to map a six-layer network, originally trained on 18 000 labelled images of pharmaceutical blister packs, onto a Xilinx Zynq-7000 device. The network identifies four defect classes—missing tablet, cracked seal, mislabelled pocket and correct—at a sustained throughput of 120 classifications per second per camera lane. Compared with a floating-point GPU baseline, the FPGA implementation achieved within 2.1 percentage points of classification accuracy (92.6% vs 94.7%) while reducing power consumption from 85 W to 6.3 W. Latency from image capture to classification output was 8.2 ms. The paper includes a discussion of fixed-point precision trade-offs at 8-bit and 12-bit configurations.

title: Integrating a vision-guided pick-and-place cell with an MES via OPC-UA: implementation and latency characterisation
abstract: Manufacturing execution systems increasingly demand real-time telemetry from autonomous robotic cells, yet most published work addresses the vision and motion layers in isolation from the factory IT layer. This paper describes the integration of a vision-guided pick-and-place cell—comprising a conveyor, two cameras, an embedded classifier and a six-axis arm—with a pilot MES instance using the OPC-UA publish-subscribe protocol. The integration covers object classification events, arm cycle timestamps, reject counts and camera health diagnostics. End-to-end message latency from classification event to MES database commit was measured at 14.2 ms median and 31.8 ms at the 99th percentile under continuous production load. The paper identifies the OPC-UA encoding step as the dominant latency contributor (38% of median) and evaluates binary vs JSON encoding options. A reference architecture diagram and sample information model are provided as supplementary material.

title: Sliding mode control for active vibration damping in hydraulic boom cranes subject to wind and payload swing
abstract: Hydraulic boom cranes on offshore supply vessels experience coupled boom vibration and payload swing induced by wave motion and wind gusts. This paper applies sliding mode control to the hydraulic luffing and slewing cylinders with the objective of reducing tip displacement and payload pendulum angle simultaneously. The sliding surface is defined on a linear combination of tip velocity error and payload angle, with weighting derived from a two-degree-of-freedom crane model linearised at three operating points. Wind disturbance is modelled as a Dryden turbulence spectrum with a standard deviation of 8 m/s. Hardware-in-the-loop tests using a scaled 1:10 physical crane model driven by electrohydraulic actuators show a 54% reduction in tip displacement RMS and a 47% reduction in peak payload swing compared to an uncontrolled baseline during a simulated Beaufort 5 sea state.

title: Spectral Subtraction with Adaptive Oversubtraction Factors for Wind-Noise Reduction in Outdoor Dialogue Recording
abstract: Wind noise represents one of the most persistent problems in location audio, characterised by a non-stationary low-frequency spectrum that changes with gusting patterns. This paper evaluates a spectral subtraction approach in which the oversubtraction factor is updated frame-by-frame using a running estimate of spectral flatness. Twenty recordings of scripted dialogue were made outdoors in three wind-speed conditions (2–4 m/s, 5–7 m/s, 8–11 m/s) using a directional shotgun microphone mounted on a standard furry windshield. Noise estimates were initialised during pre-roll silence and refreshed using a minimum statistics tracker. The adaptive scheme reduced residual wind energy by an average of 6.4 dB relative to a fixed-factor baseline across all conditions, measured via perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) and short-time objective intelligibility (STOI). Musical noise artefacts, assessed by informal listening panels of twelve audio engineers, were rated as less obtrusive than those produced by the fixed baseline at medium and high wind speeds. The method is implemented as a real-time plug-in prototype and tested within a standard post-production timeline.

title: Perceptual Evaluation of Residual Artefacts in Single-Channel Noise Reduction for Film Dialogue
abstract: Noise reduction processing applied to film dialogue commonly introduces tonal residuals and spectral smearing that are perceptible even when objective scores improve. This study conducted a series of MUSHRA listening tests with 24 participants drawn from two groups: trained audio post-production engineers and non-specialist film viewers. Seven noise reduction algorithms—four spectral domain methods and three Wiener filter variants—were applied to 30 clips extracted from independently produced Serbian short films, each contaminated with one of four background noise types: traffic, air conditioning, crowd ambience, and electrical hum. Ratings were collected for overall quality, dialogue clarity, and background acceptability. Results showed that engineers penalised tonal residuals significantly more than non-specialists, and that Wiener smoothing reduced residual tones at the cost of temporal smearing perceived negatively by both groups. The findings suggest that optimising for PESQ alone is insufficient for editorial acceptance in fiction post-production contexts.

title: Minimum Statistics Noise Estimation Under Rapidly Varying Acoustic Conditions: A Comparative Study
abstract: Minimum statistics noise estimation is widely used in speech enhancement but its tracking speed and bias correction are typically calibrated for stationary or slowly varying environments. This paper compares six configurations of the minimum statistics estimator—varying window length (0.5 s to 3 s), subwindow count (4 to 16), and bias compensation factor—across recordings gathered in twelve distinct acoustic environments ranging from indoor studios to open-air markets in Novi Sad and Subotica. Ground truth noise floors were obtained by recording environmental noise without speech under matched conditions. Tracking error, over-estimation probability, and resulting STOI scores after spectral subtraction are reported. Shorter windows with higher subwindow counts performed best in rapidly changing conditions (outdoor markets, busy corridors) while longer windows remained superior in stationary environments (HVAC-dominated interiors). An adaptive window-length selection heuristic based on spectral variance is proposed and validated on a held-out set of 40 recordings.

title: A Dataset of Annotated Location-Audio Recordings for Dialogue Restoration Research
abstract: Progress in dialogue restoration is partly hampered by the absence of publicly annotated corpora reflecting real production conditions. This paper describes the construction and release of the NovSAD-Loc corpus, comprising 4.2 hours of dialogue recordings collected during the production of eight short fiction films shot on location in Vojvodina between 2015 and 2017. Each clip is annotated for noise type (eleven categories), signal-to-noise ratio range, microphone type, shooting distance, and editorial acceptability rating provided by the supervising sound editors. The corpus is segmented into 2,118 clips averaging 7.1 seconds. Baseline results for four published spectral reduction algorithms are reported using PESQ, STOI, and a subjective rating scale. Inter-rater agreement on acceptability labels reached a Cohen's kappa of 0.61 across three annotators. The dataset and annotation guidelines are made available under a Creative Commons licence to support reproducible research in post-production audio processing.

title: Frequency-Dependent Gain Smoothing to Reduce Musical Noise in Spectral Attenuation of HVAC Interference
abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems produce interference with a characteristic harmonic structure superimposed on broadband turbulence noise, making flat spectral attenuation prone to visible and audible residual tones. This study applies frequency-dependent temporal smoothing of gain functions, calibrated separately for the harmonic and broadband components of HVAC noise, to 62 dialogue recordings made in office and institutional interiors. The harmonic component is identified via a comb filter bank aligned to the dominant fundamental estimated from the noise-only pre-roll. Smoothing time constants in harmonic frequency bins are extended by a factor of 1.8 relative to broadband bins, reducing tonal residuals by a mean of 4.1 dB (A-weighted) without measurable degradation of STOI scores. A small listening test with 16 post-production practitioners confirmed that the modified approach was preferred over unsmoothed attenuation in 73% of trials involving HVAC-contaminated clips.

title: Comparison of STFT and MDCT Domains for Spectral Noise Reduction of Location Dialogue
abstract: The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) dominates implementations of spectral noise reduction, yet the modified discrete cosine transform (MDCT) is the analysis basis of several broadcast audio codecs and offers different time-frequency resolution trade-offs. This paper implements matched spectral subtraction and Wiener filter processing in both domains and applies them to 90 clips from the NovSAD-Loc corpus spanning three noise categories. Frame length, overlap, and window function are held constant across domains where possible. MDCT-domain processing produced marginally lower musical noise ratings in informal listening (mean difference 0.3 on a five-point scale, not statistically significant), while STFT processing showed slightly better STOI preservation (mean difference 0.012). Processing latency and computational cost per frame are also compared. The results suggest that domain choice alone is unlikely to account for substantial quality differences; the noise estimation and gain computation strategies are more consequential.

title: Editorial Acceptability of Noise-Reduced Dialogue: Threshold Estimation Across Production Formats
abstract: Broadcast, streaming, and theatrical exhibition formats impose different perceptual contexts for dialogue noise, yet acceptability thresholds are rarely quantified in format-specific terms. This study recruited 30 participants—ten each from broadcast post-production, film post-production, and online video editing—and presented stimuli from three noise categories at five SNR levels processed by a standard spectral subtraction algorithm. Participants rated acceptability for their usual delivery format. A logistic regression model estimated the SNR threshold at which each group reached 50% acceptability. Broadcast editors showed a stricter threshold (estimated at 22.4 dB SNR) compared to online video editors (17.8 dB), with film editors occupying an intermediate position (20.1 dB). Residual artefact type interacted with format preference: tonal residuals were disproportionately penalised by broadcast editors. Findings are discussed in the context of loudness normalisation standards and codec transparency expectations.

title: Adaptive Spectral Noise Reduction for Multi-Microphone Location Sets: Handling Inter-Channel Coherence
abstract: Location sound recording for drama productions frequently employs multiple simultaneous channels—boom microphone, radio microphone, and plant microphones—each capturing different noise characteristics and speech levels. Applying single-channel noise reduction independently to each track can produce inter-channel incoherence artefacts when tracks are combined in the mix. This study proposes a workflow in which noise estimates from the boom channel, assumed to have the highest noise exposure, inform gain curves applied coherently across all simultaneously active channels after appropriate level normalisation. Tests were conducted on 24 two- and three-channel location sets recorded during a television drama production. Coherent processing reduced inter-channel comb filtering artefacts rated in a 20-person listening test at 0.9 points lower severity (five-point scale) than independent processing, with no statistically significant degradation of per-channel STOI. A reference implementation is described as a session template for a major DAW platform.

title: Noise Reduction Artefact Perception in Hearing-Aid Users Watching Subtitled Drama: A Pilot Study
abstract: People using hearing aids represent a significant portion of the broadcast drama audience, yet noise reduction processing designed for normative hearing may interact unpredictably with hearing-aid signal processing chains. This pilot study recruited 14 adults with mild-to-moderate sensorineural hearing loss wearing their own hearing aids and 14 age-matched normal-hearing controls. Both groups watched four short drama excerpts with dialogue processed at two noise reduction intensities (light and heavy spectral subtraction) and one unprocessed control, with subtitles present. Subjective ratings of dialogue clarity, background disturbance, and overall experience were collected via questionnaire. Hearing-aid users showed greater sensitivity to temporal smearing artefacts than controls, rating heavily processed conditions 0.7 points lower on a ten-point clarity scale. Light processing was rated acceptable by both groups. Results suggest that post-production engineers may need to apply more conservative noise reduction when producing content targeting hearing-impaired audiences.

title: Noise Floor Estimation Using Parabolic Spectral Interpolation in Reverberant Interiors
abstract: Standard minimum statistics noise estimators assume that the noise floor is observable during low-energy frames, but in reverberant interiors the decaying reverb tail occupies these frames and biases the estimate upward. This paper proposes a correction in which the noise floor estimate in each frequency bin is refined via parabolic interpolation of the local minimum spectral trajectory, exploiting the smooth spectral shape of diffuse-field reverberation. Validation used 55 recordings made in five reverberant spaces (T60 ranging from 0.6 s to 2.1 s) in buildings at the University of Novi Sad campus. The correction reduced noise overestimation by a mean of 2.8 dB in the 500 Hz–2 kHz range and improved PESQ scores by 0.14 MOS-LQO points on average compared to uncorrected minimum statistics. The method adds negligible computational overhead and is compatible with existing single-channel spectral subtraction pipelines.

title: Timbral memory and category formation for abstract electroacoustic textures across repeated exposure
abstract: Repeated exposure to unfamiliar abstract sounds is known to facilitate category formation, but the mechanisms by which timbral features support category boundaries remain unclear. This study used a 5-day repeated-exposure paradigm in which 24 participants heard 60 synthesised electroacoustic textures drawn from three covertly defined spectral-roughness clusters (low, medium, high roughness). On day 1 and day 5, participants performed a free-sorting task and provided verbal labels for spontaneously formed groups. By day 5, sorting consistency (measured by adjusted Rand index) increased significantly for the high-roughness cluster (mean ARI 0.38 to 0.62, p < 0.01) but not for the medium-roughness cluster. Verbal labels collected on day 5 showed that spectral descriptors (e.g., 'grating', 'rough', 'metallic') were used more frequently than temporal descriptors, suggesting that spectral roughness functions as a stable timbral anchor in long-term timbral memory. Findings contribute to understanding how listeners develop timbral categories for non-referential sounds.

title: Magnetic Tape Degradation and the Audibility of Archival Loss in Yugoslav Pop Recordings
abstract: This article investigates the physical degradation of magnetic tape stocks used in Yugoslav commercial and broadcast recording, focusing on shedding and sticky-shed syndrome in reels held at three institutional archives in Serbia and Croatia. Forty-two reels dating from 1966 to 1984 were assessed using visual inspection, playback testing, and baking trials conducted at 52°C for periods between four and eight hours. Successful transfers were obtained from 29 reels; 13 showed irreversible loss of signal in some passages. Spectral comparison between degraded and stable sections of the same reels shows consistent high-frequency loss above 8 kHz as the most common degradation signature, alongside intermittent dropout events averaging 12 milliseconds in duration on the most affected material. The paper discusses the methodological challenges of treating archival degradation simultaneously as a conservation problem and as an acoustic phenomenon carrying historical information about storage conditions. A proposed workflow for condition assessment and transfer prioritisation is outlined, drawing on procedures adapted from practices at two Western European sound archives.

title: Characterisation of Axial Mode Resonances in Asymmetric Rectangular Control Rooms Below 120 Hz
abstract: Axial room modes in rectangular enclosures are well described analytically, but real control rooms deviate substantially from ideal geometry due to asymmetric wall absorption, equipment placement, and diffuse boundaries. This study characterised modal behaviour in eleven small mixing rooms (volumes 28–64 m³) at a music academy and three associated private studios in Novi Sad. Impulse response measurements were taken at 27 listening positions per room using a dodecahedral loudspeaker and a B&K 4190 microphone. Frequency resolution was 0.5 Hz up to 200 Hz. Results showed that asymmetry consistently displaced pressure maxima by 0.3–1.1 m from analytically predicted positions, and that the Q factor of dominant modes averaged 24.3 across the sample, compared with a theoretical prediction of 31.1 for equivalent rectangular rooms. The deviations had measurable consequences for equaliser placement efficacy: filters centred on analytically derived modal frequencies missed energy peaks by up to 4.1 dB at the primary listening position. The paper argues for measurement-driven modal identification as a precondition for any parametric correction procedure in asymmetric spaces.

title: Retrospective Assessment of Parametric Equalisation Effectiveness in 18 Studio Rooms Treated Between 2000 and 2015
abstract: This paper revisits 18 small studio and control rooms in Serbia and Hungary that were treated with parametric equalisation procedures developed and applied by the authors' group between 2000 and 2015. The rooms were remeasured in 2021–2022 using identical equipment and protocols to the original sessions. The objective was to determine how well the original corrections held over time as rooms aged, equipment changed, and occupancy patterns shifted. In 11 of 18 rooms, the spectral standard deviation at the primary listening position had increased by more than 2 dB relative to the post-correction baseline. The dominant causes were equipment relocation (7 rooms), acoustic panel degradation (3 rooms), and changes in speaker model (4 rooms). In 7 rooms the correction remained within 1 dB of the original result. The paper provides a maintenance protocol and discusses how often recalibration is warranted under different room usage scenarios. Findings suggest that corrections based on optimised parametric filters have a median useful life of approximately 4–6 years before recalibration is needed.

title: Friction and wear behaviour of CrN coatings deposited at varying nitrogen partial pressures by reactive magnetron sputtering
abstract: CrN coatings were deposited on AISI H11 tool steel substrates by direct-current reactive magnetron sputtering at nitrogen partial pressures ranging from 0.15 Pa to 0.55 Pa in steps of 0.10 Pa. Coating thickness was held constant at approximately 3 µm, verified by ball-crater cross-section measurements. Phase composition was assessed by X-ray diffraction; coatings deposited above 0.35 Pa showed a dominant CrN phase with a minor Cr2N contribution, while those at 0.15 Pa were predominantly Cr2N. Nanoindentation hardness ranged from 16.2 GPa to 21.8 GPa across the series, with the highest value recorded at 0.25 Pa. Tribological testing was performed on a pin-on-disc tribometer using alumina balls (6 mm diameter) at 1 N, 3 N, and 5 N normal loads and a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s over 500 m. Specific wear rates at 1 N ranged from 1.4 × 10⁻⁶ to 3.8 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/N·m depending on composition. The coefficient of friction stabilised between 0.45 and 0.62 in the steady-state regime. Wear track morphology examined by scanning electron microscopy indicated abrasive groove formation at low loads transitioning to adhesive delamination patches at 5 N for the softer compositions. Results suggest that nitrogen partial pressure is a first-order control variable for both mechanical and tribological performance of CrN in this deposition window.

title: Adhesion strength and scratch response of CrN and TiAlN coatings on differently pre-treated H11 steel substrates
abstract: Scratch testing and Rockwell C adhesion assessment were used to compare interfacial behaviour of CrN and TiAlN coatings deposited on AISI H11 substrates subjected to three surface pre-treatment conditions: ground only, ground and polished (Ra ≈ 0.05 µm), and ground, polished, and plasma-etched in-situ prior to deposition. Coatings were 3.5 µm thick for both compositions. Progressive-load scratch tests were performed from 1 N to 70 N at a loading rate of 100 N/min with a Rockwell diamond indenter (200 µm tip radius). Critical loads Lc2 (cohesive failure) and Lc3 (adhesive failure) were extracted from acoustic emission and optical microscopy. For CrN, Lc3 values increased from 38 N on ground substrates to 56 N after plasma etching. TiAlN showed a comparatively smaller sensitivity to substrate preparation, with Lc3 values ranging from 44 N to 51 N. Rockwell C indentation at HF1–HF6 classification confirmed that plasma-etched samples fell in the HF1–HF2 category for both coating types. Cross-sectional focused ion beam milling revealed a continuous interface without voids for plasma-etched samples, whereas ground-only samples exhibited localised micro-delamination at the interface. Findings point to plasma etching as a reliable pre-treatment step for improving adhesion of both coating systems.

title: Correlation between accelerated ageing results (ISO 5630-3 and ISO 5630-5) and natural ageing over two years for coated food-grade paperboard
abstract: A two-year natural ageing study was conducted on food-grade folding boxboard (FBB, 360 g/m²) samples coated with five coating systems (LDPE, PVA, polyethylene–wax blend, shellac, and a bio-based polylactic acid dispersion), stored under controlled conditions (23 °C, 50 % RH). At six-month intervals and at the end of two years, WVTR, bending stiffness, brightness (ISO 2470), and grease resistance (kit test) were measured. The same samples were compared with material artificially aged under ISO 5630-3 (90 °C, 50 % RH) and ISO 5630-5 (80 °C, 65 % RH) at the start of the study. ISO 5630-5 gave a better statistical correspondence with two-year natural ageing for WVTR (R² = 0.83) than ISO 5630-3 (R² = 0.61). For mechanical properties, neither protocol correlated well (R² < 0.50), suggesting that standardised thermal ageing is insufficient for predicting long-term stiffness behaviour. Practical conversion factors are proposed for each coating system.

title: Recyclability and barrier retention of all-polyethylene multilayer films after mechanical reprocessing
abstract: All-PE multilayer films (HDPE core/LLDPE inner/mLLDPE seal, total 120 µm) were granulated and reprocessed up to five times on a twin-screw extruder at 200 °C. Cast films were remade from regranulate after each reprocessing cycle. OTR increased from 380 cm³/(m²·day·bar) in the virgin film to 610 cm³/(m²·day·bar) after five cycles; WVTR increased by 28 %. Melt flow index rose from 1.1 to 2.4 g/10 min (190 °C, 2.16 kg) over five cycles, indicating chain scission. GPC analysis showed Mw decrease from 168 000 to 121 000 g/mol and broadening of the dispersity index from 4.2 to 6.1. Tensile strength at break fell by 19 %. DSC crystallinity was largely unchanged (65 ± 2 %) across cycles, suggesting that the barrier increase is attributable primarily to microstructural defects rather than crystallinity change. A compatibiliser addition at 1 % by mass partially recovered tensile properties but did not significantly recover OTR.

title: Accelerated bainitic transformation in medium-Mn TRIP steel by prior cold deformation of austenite
abstract: A 0.18C–0.8Si–4.5Mn (wt%) medium-manganese steel was deformed in compression by 10%, 20%, and 30% reduction at 600 °C prior to isothermal bainite holding at 350 °C and 400 °C. Dilatometric length-change curves were recorded continuously and the transformation kinetics were compared with an undeformed reference. Prior deformation of 20% reduced the time to 50% transformation completion from 840 s to 190 s at 350 °C, attributed to the increased dislocation density providing additional bainite nucleation sites. However, the maximum retained austenite fraction dropped from 16.1 vol% in the reference to 9.8 vol% in the 30%-deformed condition, as the accelerated transformation exhausted the austenite volume before carbon enrichment could stabilise sufficient fractions. EBSD phase mapping confirmed a finer bainite packet size in deformed specimens. Tensile tests showed that the 20%-deformed condition offered the best balance, with ultimate tensile strength of 1050 MPa and total elongation of 24%.

title: Skin temperature distribution patterns in healthy adults during graded ambient cooling: a baseline thermographic study
abstract: Establishing reliable baseline data is a prerequisite for any deviation-based clinical monitoring scheme. This study recruited 38 healthy adult volunteers (19 female, 19 male, aged 21–34) and recorded full-body infrared thermograms under controlled ambient conditions ranging from 18 °C to 28 °C in 2 °C increments. Images were acquired with a calibrated FLIR T650sc camera at 15-minute intervals following a 20-minute acclimatisation period. Seventeen anatomical regions of interest were defined and mean skin temperatures extracted using a semi-automated segmentation routine. Results showed a statistically significant linear relationship between ambient temperature and distal extremity temperatures (R² = 0.81–0.89), while trunk temperatures remained within a 0.9 °C band across the full ambient range. Sex-related differences were most pronounced at the hands and feet. The dataset and region-of-interest definitions established here were used in subsequent modelling work targeting populations with impaired thermoregulation.

title: Predicting rectal temperature from infrared facial and neck thermograms: a regression approach in resting subjects
abstract: Non-invasive surrogate measures of core body temperature are clinically attractive but technically demanding. This study assessed whether a multivariate linear regression model trained on infrared thermogram features from the face and anterior neck could predict simultaneously measured rectal temperature with clinically acceptable accuracy. Forty-two resting healthy participants underwent simultaneous infrared imaging (FLIR A655sc) and continuous rectal temperature monitoring over 90-minute sessions at two ambient temperatures (22 °C and 27 °C). Forty-one thermographic predictors were extracted, and a leave-one-subject-out cross-validation scheme was employed. The best-performing model used five predictors and achieved a mean absolute error of 0.21 °C and a 95% limits-of-agreement interval of ±0.38 °C against rectal temperature. These margins fall within the ±0.5 °C threshold commonly cited in clinical thermometry standards. The study supports feasibility but highlights the sensitivity of predictions to perspiration and hair coverage artefacts.

title: Thermoregulatory impairment in cervical spinal cord injury: quantifying autonomic dysfunction through infrared thermography
abstract: Individuals with cervical spinal cord injury (SCI) lose supraspinal autonomic control below the lesion level, substantially impairing thermoregulation. This observational study enrolled 24 participants with chronic cervical SCI (AIS A–B, injury duration 2–11 years) and 24 able-bodied controls, measuring full-body thermograms and ambient-corrected skin temperature indices across three standardised ambient conditions (20 °C, 24 °C, 28 °C). The SCI group demonstrated significantly reduced thermal responsiveness below the lesion: mean temperature change per 4 °C ambient increment was 0.41 °C in the SCI lower limbs versus 1.03 °C in controls (p < 0.001). Inter-individual variability was markedly higher in the SCI group (coefficient of variation 34% vs. 11%). Lesion completeness and level were the strongest predictors of thermographic response magnitude. Findings provide quantitative targets for personalised thermal comfort management in rehabilitation ward settings.

title: A two-compartment thermal model parameterised for cervical spinal cord injury: validation against skin thermometry data
abstract: Computational thermoregulatory models developed for healthy adults do not adequately represent the physiology of spinal cord injury, where peripheral vasomotor and sudomotor responses are absent below the lesion. This paper proposes a two-compartment lumped-parameter thermal model in which the sub-lesion compartment is governed by passive heat exchange only, while the supra-lesion compartment retains standard autonomic control equations. Model parameters were estimated by fitting to the longitudinal thermographic and core temperature dataset collected from 24 cervical SCI participants in a previous study. Validation used a held-out subset covering two additional ambient conditions. The model reproduced mean skin temperatures in the lower limb compartment with a root mean square error of 0.29 °C and captured the blunted dynamic response observed experimentally. Sensitivity analysis identified metabolic heat production and ambient air velocity as the parameters with the greatest influence on sub-lesion temperatures under resting conditions.

title: Infrared thermography as a screening tool for pressure injury risk in wheelchair users with spinal cord injury: a pilot clinical study
abstract: Prolonged sitting in wheelchair users with SCI creates ischemic microenvironments at bony prominences, increasing pressure injury risk. This pilot study tested whether contact-free infrared thermography of the seated ischial and sacral regions could discriminate between low- and high-risk tissue states, as classified by a standardised clinical pressure injury risk scale (Braden scale). Twenty wheelchair-dependent SCI participants were imaged in a standardised seated position before and after a 60-minute sitting trial using a FLIR A655sc camera mounted below a custom transparent seat plate. Thermal asymmetry indices and rate of temperature rise during loading were extracted. High-risk participants (Braden score ≤ 14) showed a significantly faster post-loading temperature rebound (mean 0.8 °C/min vs. 0.3 °C/min, p = 0.003). Sensitivity was 75% and specificity 80% at an optimised threshold, suggesting practical utility as a supplementary monitoring tool pending larger trials.

title: Thermal comfort assessment methods in clinical rehabilitation wards: a structured literature review and gap analysis
abstract: Thermal comfort is known to affect recovery outcomes, pain perception, and autonomic stability in inpatient rehabilitation populations, yet systematic approaches to its assessment and control in clinical wards remain rare. This chapter reviews the available methods for measuring and modelling thermal comfort, with particular attention to their applicability in populations with impaired thermoregulation. The PMV–PPD framework, its physiological extensions, and adaptive models are discussed in terms of their underlying assumptions and the degree to which those assumptions are violated by SCI, stroke, or traumatic brain injury populations. Wearable sensor approaches, infrared-based methods, and questionnaire instruments are compared across 63 primary studies published between 2000 and 2021. The chapter concludes with a gap analysis identifying the absence of validated adaptive feedback protocols for clinical ward environments as the most critical unresolved problem in the field.

title: Continuous non-contact core temperature estimation during occupational therapy sessions in SCI patients using a ceiling-mounted infrared array
abstract: Monitoring core temperature continuously during active rehabilitation sessions is practically constrained by wiring and infection control requirements of invasive or semi-invasive probes. This study evaluated a ceiling-mounted 32×32 infrared sensor array (operating at 8–14 µm) as a means of tracking estimated core temperature during 45-minute upper-limb occupational therapy sessions in 18 cervical SCI inpatients. Estimated core temperature was derived from a previously validated two-compartment model fed with supra-lesion skin temperatures extracted from the array. Ground truth was provided by zero-heat-flux forehead thermometry. Mean absolute error across 162 session-observations was 0.33 °C, with 89% of estimates within ±0.5 °C of the forehead reference. Temperature excursions above 37.8 °C occurred in four participants and were associated with high ambient temperature and inadequate hydration. The results support further development of room-integrated thermal monitoring for rehabilitation wards.

title: Adaptive room temperature control in a rehabilitation ward bay: a crossover trial comparing fixed and model-driven setpoint schedules
abstract: Fixed heating, ventilation, and air conditioning setpoints in rehabilitation wards are typically calibrated for healthy adults and may not provide adequate thermal comfort for patients with thermoregulatory impairment. This crossover trial assigned 30 inpatients with cervical or thoracic SCI to two one-week conditions in a single rehabilitation bay: standard ward protocol (23 ± 1 °C fixed setpoint) and model-driven adaptive control using individualised thermoregulatory model predictions updated hourly from ceiling-mounted infrared estimates. Primary outcomes were thermal comfort votes (7-point scale) and estimated core temperature stability. The adaptive protocol improved mean comfort vote scores from 3.1 to 4.6 (5 = comfortable) and reduced core temperature variance by 31%. Energy consumption of the HVAC system increased by 8% under adaptive control. No adverse events attributable to the protocol were recorded. The trial was conducted in the rehabilitation ward at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina.

title: Inter-session reproducibility of infrared thermographic skin temperature indices in cervical SCI: implications for longitudinal monitoring
abstract: Clinical use of infrared thermography as a longitudinal monitoring tool requires knowledge of measurement reproducibility over time. This study assessed test–retest reliability of 17 regional skin temperature indices derived from full-body thermograms in 20 chronic cervical SCI participants imaged at three sessions separated by one week each, under standardised protocol conditions. Intraclass correlation coefficients for trunk and upper limb indices ranged from 0.82 to 0.94, indicating good to excellent reproducibility. Lower limb indices showed lower reproducibility (ICC 0.61–0.78), likely reflecting the greater sensitivity of denervated vasculature to minor ambient fluctuations. Bland–Altman plots identified a small but consistent session-order drift of 0.12 °C per week in the lower extremity indices, possibly attributable to seasonal ambient humidity changes. The findings recommend ambient humidity monitoring as a covariate in longitudinal thermographic protocols and suggest that clinical decisions should be based on within-session relative patterns rather than absolute temperature values.

title: Unsupervised cluster tracking for long-term multi-electrode recordings: a comparison of three drift-compensation strategies
abstract: Long-duration multi-electrode recordings produce spike-cluster configurations that evolve continuously, making it difficult to maintain consistent unit identity without operator intervention. This study compares three unsupervised strategies for tracking cluster identity across sessions: (1) nearest-centroid assignment in PCA space, (2) Hungarian-algorithm matching on Mahalanobis distance matrices, and (3) a hidden Markov model that treats unit identity as a latent state. A benchmark corpus of 14 publicly shared datasets (total 2,847 recording hours, ranging from rodent somatosensory to primate motor cortex) was used for evaluation. The HMM-based approach reduced identity-swap errors by 34% relative to nearest-centroid matching across the full corpus, but required three times the processing time. The Hungarian method offered a practical compromise with 22% error reduction and modest computational cost. Sensitivity analyses show that the relative ranking of methods is preserved across electrode types (tetrode vs. linear probe) but that absolute performance drops markedly when firing rates fall below 1.2 spikes per second.

title: Spatially adaptive directional filtering for shear-wave field separation in heterogeneous tissue: a simulation and phantom study
abstract: Directional filters are routinely used to separate right-travelling from left-travelling shear waves before local SWS estimation, reducing the bias introduced by reflections. Standard implementations use fixed filter directions and bandwidths selected for homogeneous tissue. In heterogeneous media—relevant to fibrotic nodules and steatotic patches—wave direction and dominant frequency shift spatially, causing fixed filters to suppress useful signal energy or pass reflected energy. This paper describes a spatially adaptive directional filter whose orientation and bandwidth are updated at each image pixel using a local radon-transform-based direction estimator operating on a 7 × 7 spatial neighbourhood. Evaluation was performed on FDTD-simulated wave fields for five heterogeneous geometries and on six agar-polyacrylamide multi-layer phantoms. The adaptive filter reduced inclusion SWS bias from 0.19 m/s to 0.06 m/s and improved inclusion contrast by a factor of 1.7 relative to a fixed-direction filter. Computation cost was 0.8 s per frame, compatible with offline clinical workflow.

title: Coherence Modelling in Serbian Expository Texts Using Centering Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the applicability of Centering Theory to Serbian expository prose, a language with relatively free word order and rich morphological agreement. We manually annotated 320 paragraphs drawn from undergraduate essays collected at the University of Novi Sad for forward-looking and backward-looking centers, then trained a log-linear classifier to predict coherence transitions. The model achieved an F1 score of 0.71 on a held-out test set of 80 paragraphs, outperforming a unigram language model baseline by 9 percentage points. Error analysis revealed that null subjects and clitic clusters posed the greatest challenge for automatic center identification. Results suggest that morphosyntactic features specific to Serbian, particularly case marking and verbal agreement, can partially substitute for word-order cues exploited in English-language systems. We release the annotated dataset and evaluation scripts under a Creative Commons licence.

title: A Treebank-Based Study of Discourse Connectives in Serbian Journalistic Texts
abstract: We present a corpus study of discourse connectives in a 150,000-token sample of Serbian newspaper text drawn from the SrpKor2012 corpus. Each connective token was manually labelled according to a simplified version of the Penn Discourse Treebank annotation scheme adapted to Serbian morphosyntax. Across 2,341 annotated instances, causal and contrastive relations together account for 54% of all explicit connective uses, with temporal connectives comprising 18%. We compare the distribution against similar studies for Croatian and Slovene and find cross-linguistic alignment in high-frequency categories but notable divergence in concessive marking. A conditional random field tagger trained on the annotated portion reaches 83.4% token-level accuracy in a ten-fold cross-validation setting. The annotated data and the tagger are made available to the research community through the CLARIN.SI infrastructure.

title: Argument Structure in Secondary-School Persuasive Writing: A Corpus-Based Framework for South Slavic
abstract: This book chapter outlines a theoretical and methodological framework for annotating argument structure in persuasive essays written by secondary-school students in Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian. Drawing on Toulmin's model of argumentation and adapting it to agglutinative morphological patterns common to South Slavic, we propose a six-label annotation scheme covering claims, evidence, warrants, rebuttals, and two types of background statements. We applied the scheme to a pilot corpus of 500 student essays collected from three national school systems and report inter-annotator agreement of κ = 0.74 for the major claim/evidence distinction. The chapter discusses sources of disagreement, particularly for implicit warrants, and compares annotation decisions across the three language varieties. We argue that a shared tagset can facilitate comparative studies of argumentation pedagogy across the region.

title: Automated Essay Scoring for Serbian: Baseline Models and Feature Analysis
abstract: We describe the first systematic study of automated essay scoring (AES) for Serbian-language student writing. The dataset consists of 1,200 argumentative essays written by first-year university students, each scored holistically by two trained raters on a six-point scale; the quadratic weighted kappa between raters was 0.81. We extracted 87 features spanning lexical richness, syntactic complexity, discourse coherence, and spelling error rate, then trained support vector regression and random forest models. The best configuration (random forest with all feature groups) achieved r = 0.76 with human scores in five-fold cross-validation. Ablation experiments showed that discourse-level features—specifically entity grid coherence scores and connective density—contributed 6 percentage points of explained variance beyond surface features alone. We discuss implications for formative feedback tools in Serbian higher education.

title: Entity Grids for South Slavic: Adapting the Barzilay–Lapata Model to Pro-Drop Languages
abstract: The entity grid model of Barzilay and Lapata (2008) represents local coherence as transition probabilities over grammatical roles across sentences. Its original design assumes English word order and frequent overt subject realization. In this paper we adapt the model for pro-drop South Slavic languages by augmenting the standard entity extraction pipeline with a null-subject recovery module trained on the SETimes.HR parallel corpus. We evaluate the adapted model on Serbian and Croatian text discrimination tasks using 600 document pairs (300 per language). The adapted model achieves 79.2% accuracy on Serbian and 81.1% on Croatian, compared to 71.4% and 72.9% respectively for the unmodified English pipeline. We analyze the contribution of recovered null subjects and find that they account for roughly one quarter of all subject-role transitions in the data.

title: A Discourse-Annotated Corpus of Serbian Administrative Texts
abstract: Administrative and legal language in Serbian has received little attention from computational discourse researchers despite its societal importance and high text volume. This paper presents SrpAdmin-Disc, a corpus of 420 documents (approximately 280,000 tokens) drawn from municipal decisions, regulatory notices, and public procurement announcements, annotated at three levels: sentence boundaries, discourse segments, and coherence relation labels from a 14-category taxonomy adapted from Rhetorical Structure Theory. Inter-annotator agreement on relation labelling was κ = 0.66, which is comparable to RST annotation studies for other languages. We provide baseline results for automatic discourse segmentation (F1 = 0.88) and relation classification (F1 = 0.58) using a BiLSTM-CRF architecture with pre-trained Serbian word embeddings. The corpus is deposited in the CLARIN.SI repository under a CC-BY-NC licence and is intended to support research in automated document summarization and compliance checking.

title: Comparing Neural and Feature-Based Approaches to Coherence Assessment in Student Writing
abstract: We conduct a direct comparison of three coherence assessment approaches on a corpus of 1,600 Serbian student essays: (1) a feature-engineered system based on entity grids and discourse connective counts, (2) a sentence-pair neural model using averaged GloVe vectors, and (3) a fine-tuned multilingual BERT model (mBERT) evaluated under both in-language and zero-shot cross-lingual conditions. The task is to rank essay pairs by coherence quality as judged by human raters; we report pairwise accuracy. mBERT fine-tuned on Serbian essays achieves 77.3% pairwise accuracy, outperforming the feature-based system (69.1%) and the GloVe model (72.8%). In the zero-shot condition, where mBERT is fine-tuned only on Czech and Polish essays, accuracy drops to 64.2%, pointing to the importance of at least some Serbian training signal. We discuss the interpretability gap between the neural and feature-based systems and its implications for pedagogical feedback generation.
