title: Towards Rubric-Aligned Feedback Generation for Serbian University Essays
abstract: Automated feedback systems typically produce holistic scores without explaining which rubric criteria are met or unmet. This paper describes an approach that maps essay segments to five rubric dimensions—argumentation, coherence, vocabulary, grammar, and structure—and generates short explanatory feedback strings by filling dimension-specific templates populated with extracted text evidence. We evaluate the system on 200 essays scored by human instructors and use a sentence-level human judgment protocol to assess feedback quality across four criteria: accuracy, specificity, relevance, and usefulness. Raters judged 68% of automatically generated feedback instances as accurate and 54% as useful. The argumentation and coherence dimensions performed best, while vocabulary feedback was rated least useful, often because the templates failed to capture idiomatic misuse. We discuss the bottleneck of template design and outline plans for a data-driven template induction approach.

title: Аргументациона структура у уџбеничким текстовима за основну школу: анотациона студија
abstract: Рад истражује аргументациону структуру у текстовима из четири уџбеника за шести разред основне школе (историја, биологија, грађанско васпитање и српски језик) укупног обима 62.000 токена. Примењена је упрошћена верзија шеме за анотацију аргумената намењена нестручним анотаторима и ученицима старијег узраста. Три анотатора обрадила су исти узорак од 2.400 реченица; просечна капа износила је 0,61. Резултати показују да уџбеници природних наука садрже знатно мање експлицитних тврдњи и доказа него уџбеници друштвених наука. Такође, анализа је указала на честу употребу имплицитних налогâ у уџбеницима грађанског васпитања, где аутор претпоставља да ученик самостално изводи закључак. Налазе доводимо у везу са препорукама за наставу критичког мишљења на основношколском нивоу.

title: Discourse Coherence Benchmarks for Serbian: Design, Collection, and Evaluation
abstract: Reliable benchmark datasets are a prerequisite for systematic progress in coherence modelling. This paper reports on the construction of SrpCohBench, a benchmark suite comprising four tasks: sentence ordering, sentence insertion, incoherent sentence detection, and discourse coherence rating. The dataset draws on three source genres—news articles, academic abstracts, and student essays—with a total of 9,600 instances distributed across the four tasks. We generated negative examples through controlled permutation and deletion strategies rather than random shuffling, which pilot studies showed produces more realistic and challenging test cases. We evaluate six existing models on the benchmark, including adapted versions of two English coherence systems, and report that no model exceeds 71% accuracy on the hardest sentence-insertion task. We make SrpCohBench publicly available as a permanent evaluation resource.

title: Argument Span Detection in Serbian Using Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-trained Models
abstract: Argument mining typically decomposes into two subtasks: detecting argumentative spans and classifying their roles. In this paper we focus on span detection in Serbian using three pre-trained encoder-decoder architectures: mBART-50, mT5-base, and BERTić, a language model pre-trained specifically on Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian data. Experiments are conducted on the SrpArgEss corpus of 1,400 annotated student essays. We treat span detection as a token-level sequence labelling problem and fine-tune each model for 10 epochs with grid-searched learning rates. BERTić achieves the best token F1 of 0.81, followed by mT5-base at 0.79 and mBART-50 at 0.77. We also evaluate on a 200-essay out-of-domain test set drawn from online opinion columns and observe a drop of 7–9 F1 points across all models, suggesting sensitivity to genre. Error analysis identifies nested and embedded argumentative spans as the primary source of remaining errors.

title: Scoring Argumentative Quality in Serbian Business Reports: A Rubric-Based Corpus Study
abstract: Business reports present a genre largely overlooked in South Slavic argument mining research. This preprint describes a corpus of 620 annual and sustainability reports produced by companies registered in Serbia between 2018 and 2024, totalling approximately 4.2 million tokens. We developed a three-dimension rubric covering claim explicitness, evidence grounding, and logical consistency, and annotated a 200-report stratified sample with trained annotators (κ = 0.68 average). Preliminary modelling experiments using the annotated sample show that a fine-tuned BERTić classifier reaches macro F1 = 0.72 for a three-class claim-explicitness rating task. We also report corpus statistics on discourse connective use, sentence length, and nominalization density, comparing the business genre against the student essay corpora used in earlier work. The full annotated subset and feature extraction scripts are included in the supplementary materials.

title: Clause Length and Syntactic Complexity in Early Serbian Modernist Prose: A Comparative Corpus Study
abstract: This paper compares syntactic complexity measures in two corpora: 22 short-story collections published between 1900 and 1910 (390,000 tokens) and a set of 18 collections from 1920 to 1930 (360,000 tokens). Mean clause length in words, subordination depth, and the ratio of finite to non-finite clauses were computed using a custom rule-based parser adapted for pre-standardisation Serbian orthography. The later corpus shows a statistically significant reduction in mean clause length (from 9.4 to 7.8 words per clause) and an increase in coordinate rather than subordinate linkage, consistent with a broader European modernist move toward shorter syntactic units. The paper also isolates dialogue passages and shows that the trend is stronger in narrator text than in dialogue, which exhibits more conservative syntactic patterns throughout both periods. Limitations of automatic parsing on historical texts are discussed.

title: Cross-Lingual Transfer for Named-Entity Recognition Across South Slavic Languages: A Feature-Based Study
abstract: Named-entity recognition systems trained on one South Slavic language can achieve moderate performance on related languages without any target-language training data, but the degree of transferability varies considerably by entity type and script. This study evaluates zero-shot cross-lingual transfer among Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Macedonian, and Slovenian using a shared feature representation built from romanised transliteration, language-independent character embeddings, and shared morphological clusters derived from multilingual Wiktionary. Transfer was evaluated on five NER test sets each containing between 15,000 and 40,000 tokens. Serbian-to-Croatian transfer attained an entity-level F1 of 72.1 %, the highest pair, while Serbian-to-Macedonian reached only 58.4 %, largely due to script and suffix divergence. Adding 1,000 target-language annotated tokens in a few-shot setting raised Macedonian F1 to 69.7 %. Results confirm that shared inflectional morphology, rather than lexical overlap alone, predicts transferability across this language group.

title: Parental Language Ideologies and Intergenerational Romani Transmission in Novi Sad Peri-Urban Households
abstract: This paper reports on a qualitative study of language ideologies held by 22 parents in Serbian–Romani bilingual households in three peri-urban settlements adjacent to Novi Sad. Semi-structured interviews explored parental beliefs about the utility, prestige, and emotional value of Romani versus Serbian in the context of their children's schooling and future employment prospects. Thematic analysis identified two dominant ideological orientations: an instrumental orientation prioritising Serbian acquisition for social mobility, held by 15 of 22 parents, and a heritage orientation emphasising Romani as a carrier of familial and ethnic identity, held by the remaining seven. Parents with the instrumental orientation more frequently reported discouraging children from using Romani outside the home. The paper situates these findings within language shift literature on minority languages in Central and Eastern European urban contexts and argues that economic precarity mediates ideological stance, with parents experiencing greater employment instability more consistently endorsing Serbian monolingual norms.

title: The Role of Lexical Aspect (Aktionsart) in Early L2 Aspect Marking in Serbian
abstract: Drawing on the Aspect Hypothesis proposed for Romance and Germanic L2 learners, this paper investigates whether Serbian L2 learners' early verb morphology clusters around inherent lexical aspectual classes. Sixty-one intermediate learners of Serbian completed an elicited written narrative task based on a picture sequence; 1,047 past-tense verb tokens were coded for both grammatical aspect and Aktionsart class following a four-way vendlerian classification. Chi-square analysis revealed a significant association between achievement and accomplishment predicates and perfective marking (p < .001), while activity and state verbs showed predominantly imperfective marking. The pattern mirrors predictions of the Aspect Hypothesis, though the effect was weaker than reported for Romance contexts, likely due to the overt morphological salience of Serbian prefixation. The paper argues that Aktionsart bootstrapping interacts with the transparency of Serbian verbal morphology in ways not fully captured by current versions of the hypothesis.

title: Fault Propagation Modelling in Pneumatic Control Loops Using Coloured Petri Nets
abstract: This paper presents a structured approach to modelling fault propagation in pneumatic process control loops using coloured Petri nets (CPNs). Pneumatic actuators and positioners exhibit failure modes that differ substantially from their electronic counterparts, yet most formal safety tools treat them as generic components. The study constructed CPN models of four representative loop configurations drawn from a natural gas distribution station, covering pressure, flow, and level control. Fault injection experiments were conducted on a laboratory-scale rig equipped with a Fisher pneumatic positioner and a Foxboro pressure transmitter. Simulation results showed that undetected positioner hysteresis faults propagate to process variable deviations exceeding 15% of setpoint within 8 minutes under typical disturbance conditions. The CPN approach allowed quantification of diagnostic coverage for each loop, with values ranging from 0.71 to 0.84, consistent with IEC 61508 partial stroke requirements. The work provides a basis for deriving cause-consequence diagrams directly from the CPN state space, reducing manual HAZOP worksheet effort.

title: Comparative Evaluation of HAZOP and FMEA for Safety Instrumented Systems in Batch Chemical Processes
abstract: HAZOP and failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) are both required at different lifecycle stages under IEC 61511, yet their results are rarely compared systematically for the same system. This study applied both methods to a batch reactor safety instrumented system at a Serbian pharmaceutical intermediate manufacturer, covering 23 cause-consequence pairs identified during the process hazard analysis phase. HAZOP sessions involved six domain experts over three days and produced 47 action items. Parallel FMEA on the same logic solver and field device inventory generated 31 failure modes, of which 9 had no direct counterpart in the HAZOP output. Analysis of the discrepancies showed that common-cause failures in shared instrument supply lines were systematically underrepresented in the HAZOP worksheets. Quantitative risk reduction factors were recalculated after incorporating the missing failure modes, reducing the estimated safety integrity level adequacy from SIL 2 to SIL 1 for two protection layers. Recommendations for a combined worksheet format are provided.

title: Safety Integrity Level Assignment for Hybrid Electro-Pneumatic Loops: A Reliability Data Gap Analysis
abstract: Hybrid control loops that combine electronic sensors with pneumatic final elements present a data gap problem when applying the IEC 61511 probabilistic demand rate framework: generic failure rate databases such as OREDA and EXIDA cover electronic field devices comprehensively but contain sparse entries for pneumatic positioners, boosters, and volume tanks used in process industries. This paper quantifies the gap by comparing failure rate estimates from four industry databases against in-service failure records collected from two refinery units in the Vojvodina region over a seven-year period, covering 148 pneumatic final control elements. Observed dangerous undetected failure rates for spring-and-diaphragm actuators were 1.8 to 3.4 times higher than database medians, while solenoid valve failure rates agreed within 20%. The paper derives posterior failure rate distributions using a Bayesian updating procedure and assesses the impact on SIL verification calculations, showing that the SIL 2 claim for six representative loops would downgrade to SIL 1 when plant-specific data replace generic entries.

title: Formal Specification of Cause-Effect Logic for Safety Instrumented Functions Using Structured Text and Timed Automata
abstract: Safety instrumented functions (SIFs) in process plants are typically specified informally through cause-and-effect matrices, which are prone to ambiguity during PLC programming and verification. This paper proposes a translation procedure from cause-and-effect matrix representations to timed automata in the UPPAAL model checker, with a parallel structured text implementation for a Siemens S7-class safety PLC. The procedure is demonstrated on a fired heater protection system comprising 12 SIFs, 34 initiators, and 19 final elements. Model checking against IEC 61511-1 functional requirements identified two state reachability errors and one timing constraint violation that had not been detected during the conventional design review. The timed automata representation was also used to verify the correct inhibit and bypass logic for manual override scenarios. Round-trip consistency between the UPPAAL model and the structured text code was maintained using a Python-based code generation script, reducing manual transcription effort by approximately 60%.
venue: Control Engineering Practice

title: Layer of Protection Analysis Under Epistemic Uncertainty: A Fuzzy Set Approach for Small-Scale Petrochemical Plants
abstract: Layer of protection analysis (LOPA) requires initiating event frequency and independent protection layer (IPL) probability of failure on demand (PFD) data that are often poorly characterised for small-scale plants lacking incident history. This paper applies fuzzy triangular numbers to represent epistemic uncertainty in LOPA input parameters for four accident scenarios at a propylene storage facility in Serbia. Expert elicitation was structured using a modified Delphi procedure with seven process safety engineers, yielding trapezoidal membership functions for each uncertain parameter. Defuzzification via centre of gravity produced risk estimates between 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ and 6.7 × 10⁻⁵ dangerous events per year for the highest-consequence scenario, compared with a point estimate of 3.1 × 10⁻⁵ from the conventional LOPA. The fuzzy approach revealed that LOPA conclusions were most sensitive to uncertainty in the demand rate of the pressure relief valve IPL rather than to initiating event frequency, which has implications for inspection and testing prioritisation.

title: Quantitative Assessment of Proof Test Coverage for Pneumatic Control Valves Using Partial Stroke Testing Data
abstract: Proof test coverage (PTC) is a key parameter in IEC 61511 PFD calculations, yet empirical data on PTC for pneumatic control valves subjected to partial stroke testing (PST) remain limited. This paper presents results from a three-year data collection programme at two process plants in Vojvodina, covering 94 pneumatic on-off valves equipped with PST devices. Valve diagnostic signals were logged continuously and correlated with subsequent full stroke test outcomes to establish which failure modes PST detected or missed. PTC values derived from the data ranged from 0.55 to 0.76 depending on valve size and service fluid, substantially lower than the 0.9 value commonly assumed in vendor documentation. A multivariate logistic regression model was fitted to predict PTC from valve seat diameter, differential pressure class, and service hours since last full stroke test, yielding an area under the ROC curve of 0.81. The results support more conservative PTC input to SIL verification.

title: Modelling Instrument Air System Failures as Common Cause Events in Multi-Loop Safety Analysis
abstract: Instrument air supply is a shared utility that can simultaneously impair multiple pneumatic final elements, making it a potential common cause failure source in safety instrumented systems. Despite its significance, IEC 61511 provides limited guidance on how to incorporate instrument air failure into the quantitative safety lifecycle. This paper develops a fault tree model of a representative instrument air distribution system comprising compressors, dryers, receivers, and distribution headers, and integrates it with the SIL verification calculations of six dependent safety instrumented functions in a refinery distillation unit. Beta factors for common cause between pneumatically actuated loops sharing the same distribution header were estimated at 0.08 to 0.13 using the PDS method, approximately twice the value assumed in the original safety case. Sensitivity analysis showed that for loops with a PFD target below 0.01, the instrument air common cause contribution alone can consume more than 40% of the overall PFD budget.

title: Systematic Identification of Human Action Initiating Events in HAZOP Studies for Automated Process Plants
abstract: Automated process plants retain a significant number of manual operations — sampling, bypass switching, filter cleaning — that can initiate hazardous process deviations not captured by standard HAZOP guide words applied to piping and instrumentation diagrams. This book chapter reviews procedures for supplementing conventional HAZOP with human reliability analysis (HRA) to ensure completeness of the initiating event inventory. The chapter draws on three case studies from Serbian and Hungarian process industries covering a solvent recovery unit, a gas compression station, and a polymer blending facility. For each case, task analysis was used to enumerate manual operations, and the THERP method was used to estimate human error probabilities, which were then incorporated as additional initiating events in the HAZOP worksheets. The integrated approach increased the number of identified initiating events by 18 to 27% across the three cases and led to additional independent protection layer requirements in two of the three LOPA studies that followed.

title: Functional Safety Assessment of a Retrofit PLC-Based Safety Instrumented System Replacing a Relay Logic Panel
abstract: Relay logic panels in older process plants are increasingly being replaced by programmable logic controller-based safety instrumented systems to reduce maintenance burden and extend plant life. This paper documents the full IEC 61511 safety lifecycle assessment for such a retrofit at a Vojvodina sugar production facility, where a 42-relay panel controlling steam drum protection was replaced by a two-channel IEC 61508-compliant safety PLC. The assessment covers hazard identification, SIL determination by risk graph, SIL verification by simplified equations, functional logic review, and factory acceptance testing. PFD for the final SIS configuration was calculated at 4.3 × 10⁻³, confirming SIL 1 compliance with margin. The paper also documents lessons learned regarding the management of change process, specifically the challenge of re-validating cause-and-effect logic when the original relay panel documentation was incomplete. A structured documentation recovery procedure involving loop testing and tracing is described.

title: Automated HAZOP Node Decomposition from P&ID Graph Representations Using a Rule-Based Parser
abstract: Manual HAZOP preparation — extracting nodes, process parameters, and design intentions from piping and instrumentation diagrams — is time-consuming and depends on facilitator experience. This paper describes a rule-based parser that ingests vectorised P&ID data in ISO 10628-2 symbol format and automatically decomposes the diagram into HAZOP nodes together with candidate process parameters and control loop references. The parser was implemented in Python and tested against four P&IDs from an ammonia refrigeration system, ranging in complexity from 18 to 61 instrument tags. Automatic node proposals agreed with expert-defined nodes in 83% of cases; disagreements arose primarily at interfaces between heat exchanger circuits and their associated control loops. The tool also generates a preliminary cause-consequence seed list derived from propagation rules encoded from IEC 61882 Annex D. Integration with a commercial HAZOP worksheet software package is described. The paper does not claim to replace experienced HAZOP facilitators but characterises the workload reduction achievable in the preparation phase.

title: Diagnostic Coverage Estimation for Smart Positioners on Pneumatic Rotary Valves: Field Data from Five Years of Operation
abstract: Smart positioners equipped with valve signature diagnostics are marketed as providing diagnostic coverage sufficient to support SIL 2 claims for pneumatic rotary valve assemblies, but independent field assessments of the actual diagnostic coverage achieved in service are scarce. This paper analyses five years of diagnostic alarm and maintenance records from 67 butterfly and ball valves fitted with smart positioners at two process plants in the Pannonian region. Maintenance records were cross-referenced with positioner diagnostic outputs to classify each corrective maintenance event as detected or undetected by the positioner diagnostics prior to the maintenance trigger. Observed diagnostic coverage ranged from 0.61 to 0.88 across valve types and service conditions, with lower values associated with high-cycle services and abrasive media. For seven valves in high-pressure gas service, the positioner failed to detect developing seat leakage until process measurements indicated a deviation. The paper provides a disaggregated coverage dataset by failure mode category that can be used directly in IEC 61511 PFD calculations.

title: Aerodynamic Disturbance Compensation in Multirotor UAVs: Methods, Limitations, and Open Problems
abstract: This chapter reviews approaches for compensating aerodynamic disturbances in multirotor UAV control systems, covering the period from the emergence of commercial autopilots around 2010 to the early 2020s. The chapter is organised around four disturbance categories: steady crosswind, low-frequency gusts, high-frequency turbulence, and rotor-induced aerodynamic coupling. For each category, representative compensation strategies are described—feedforward from onboard anemometry, model-based disturbance observers, adaptive and robust controllers, and learning-based methods—with attention to the implementation constraints imposed by onboard computational resources. A recurring theme is the conflict between disturbance rejection bandwidth and actuator authority limits, especially in payload-carrying UAVs. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems, including the absence of standardised outdoor wind disturbance test protocols, the difficulty of validating rotor wake models above 12 m/s, and the gap between laboratory controller performance and in-field reliability. Approximately 140 references are synthesised.

title: Embedded implementation of a kinematic recalibration algorithm on a real-time robot controller platform
abstract: Moving kinematic recalibration algorithms from an external PC to the embedded controller of an industrial robot reduces latency, eliminates communication overhead, and simplifies integration into existing cells. This paper describes the porting of a previously published extended Kalman filter recalibration algorithm to a real-time Linux platform running on the controller hardware of a six-axis robot. The implementation uses fixed-point arithmetic for the filter prediction step and floating-point only for the infrequent update step triggered by laser tracker measurements. Execution time per filter cycle was reduced from 18 ms on a desktop PC to 6 ms on the embedded platform, comfortably within the 10 ms control loop period. Numerical equivalence between the embedded and desktop implementations was verified to within 1×10⁻⁵ mm over 10,000 test epochs. Integration into the robot's existing joint offset update mechanism required modification of 340 lines of controller firmware. Field validation over 30 eight-hour shifts confirmed that embedded and external implementations produced statistically indistinguishable TCP error distributions.

title: Gear diagnostics in planetary drives: signal processing and simulation methods
abstract: This book chapter reviews the signal processing and computational simulation approaches used for diagnostics in planetary gearboxes, covering synchronous averaging, cepstrum analysis, time-frequency methods, and multi-body torsional dynamics modelling. The chapter discusses the practical challenges of sensor placement on rotating carriers, reference signal acquisition for order tracking, and the selection of appropriate diagnostic indices for different failure modes including pitting, spalling, and tooth fracture. Example results from laboratory gearbox experiments at two test facilities are used to illustrate each method. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current limitations, including the difficulty of separating overlapping mesh harmonics when the number of planet gears changes the sideband spacing, and directions for combining physics-based models with data-driven approaches.

title: Naming the Condition: Diagnostic Disclosure and Self-Perception Among Type 2 Diabetes Patients in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper draws on 34 semi-structured interviews conducted with patients newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at three primary healthcare centres in Vojvodina between 2011 and 2012. Participants were interviewed twice—once within one month of diagnosis and again six months later—to track shifts in self-description and health behaviour. Analysis followed a grounded theory approach. Findings show that the label 'diabetic' was adopted rapidly as a master identity by roughly two-thirds of respondents, overriding prior occupational and familial self-descriptions in everyday talk. Patients who framed diabetes as a lifestyle failure rather than a physiological condition were significantly less likely to maintain medication adherence at the six-month follow-up. The paper argues that the diagnostic moment functions as a biographical disruption that Serbian primary care providers are structurally unprepared to address, given consultation times averaging under eight minutes. Implications for patient education design are discussed.

title: Contested Labels: Fibromyalgia Recognition and Help-Seeking Trajectories in Serbia
abstract: Fibromyalgia occupies an ambiguous position in Serbian clinical practice: it is recognised by rheumatologists but frequently dismissed by general practitioners. This qualitative study analysed in-depth interviews with 28 women diagnosed with fibromyalgia recruited through two patient associations in Belgrade and Novi Sad. Interviews were conducted in 2013 and coded thematically using NVivo 10. Three recurrent trajectories were identified: early acceptance of the diagnosis as relief, prolonged diagnostic odyssey lasting on average 4.3 years before receiving the fibromyalgia label, and persistent rejection of the label in favour of alternative explanatory frameworks. Women on longer diagnostic odysseys reported higher rates of simultaneous use of informal healers and private specialist clinics. The paper situates these trajectories within the structural fragmentation of the Serbian healthcare system following 1990s austerity reforms, arguing that diagnostic ambiguity is partially a product of underfunded specialist referral chains.

title: Between Diagnosis and Disbelief: Doctor–Patient Communicative Asymmetry in Serbian Endocrinology Consultations
abstract: This study applies conversation analysis to 61 audio-recorded outpatient consultations at two endocrinology departments in Serbia, collected between 2014 and 2015. Recordings were transcribed using Jefferson notation. The analysis focuses on sequences in which physicians communicate a new or revised chronic illness diagnosis. Results show that physicians dominated diagnostic explanation sequences in 89 percent of recorded encounters, with patients producing fewer than two substantive questions per consultation on average. Interruptions of patient narrative by physicians occurred at a mean rate of 3.4 per ten-minute consultation. The paper identifies a recurrent interactional pattern labelled 'pre-emptive closure', in which physicians issue follow-up appointment instructions before patients have completed their accounts of symptoms. The study discusses how these micro-level communicative practices reproduce broader social hierarchies and may contribute to poor patient comprehension of treatment regimens.

title: Chronic Fatigue and the Limits of Legitimacy: Online Forum Discourse Among Serbian Patients
abstract: This paper analyses 1,240 posts from three Serbian-language online patient forums dedicated to chronic fatigue syndrome, collected by systematic web scraping between January and June 2016. Posts were coded inductively, with a secondary deductive pass using Kleinman's explanatory models framework. Four dominant discursive strategies were identified through which forum participants sought to establish the legitimacy of their condition: citation of international diagnostic criteria, comparison with more institutionally recognised illnesses, documentation of failed medical encounters, and mutual validation of symptom lists. Notably, 38 percent of posts included references to foreign medical sources not available in Serbian translation, suggesting that internet access creates asymmetric diagnostic literacy among patients. The paper contributes to the sociology of e-health by arguing that online communities do not merely support patients but actively participate in the social construction of diagnostic categories that lack firm clinical consensus.

title: Diagnostic Categories as Institutional Filters: Gatekeeping in Serbian Primary Care for Patients Presenting with Medically Unexplained Symptoms
abstract: Using a mixed-method design, this study combined analysis of administrative data from 6 primary healthcare centres in Vojvodina (covering 14,500 patient episodes in 2016–2017) with 19 interviews with general practitioners. Administrative records were coded for diagnostic category, referral outcome, and number of prior visits. Interviews were analysed thematically. Quantitative findings indicate that patients presenting with symptoms later classified as medically unexplained had on average 5.7 visits to a GP before receiving any specialist referral, compared to 1.9 visits for patients presenting with immediately classifiable conditions. GP interview data reveal considerable uncertainty about referral pathways for ambiguous presentations and a preference for watchful waiting that physicians explicitly linked to resource constraints. The paper theorises GPs as institutional gatekeepers whose diagnostic decisions are shaped not only by clinical reasoning but by administrative pressure to limit specialist caseloads.

title: Sick Role Renegotiated: Chronic Illness, Work Disability Certification, and Social Stigma in Post-Industrial Vojvodina
abstract: This book chapter examines how the formalisation of chronic illness through state disability certification affects occupational identity and social standing among working-age adults in Vojvodina. Drawing on 42 interviews conducted in 2018–2019 with individuals holding official disability status due to chronic musculoskeletal or metabolic conditions, the chapter traces how certification simultaneously enables access to social transfers and triggers stigmatising attributions from employers, family members, and peers. Interviewees described a persistent pressure to perform sufficient sickness to justify certification while maintaining enough normality to avoid social exclusion. The analysis extends Parsons' sick-role model to account for the specific pressures of post-industrial labour markets where formal employment has contracted and informal work arrangements are widespread. The chapter argues that disability certification in Serbia operates less as a welfare instrument than as a labelling mechanism that reorganises social relationships around the certified individual.

title: Migration, Return, and Diagnostic Discontinuity: Chronic Illness Management Among Serbian Labour Migrants Returning from Germany and Austria
abstract: Labour migration creates gaps and discontinuities in chronic illness management when migrants return to Serbia after years of treatment abroad. This qualitative study recruited 26 returnees with chronic conditions (predominantly type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) through diaspora associations and general practice registers in Novi Sad and Subotica. Interviews conducted in 2021 focused on experiences re-entering the Serbian healthcare system after periods of two to fifteen years abroad. Participants consistently described incompatibilities between their acquired health literacy—shaped by German or Austrian patient education materials—and the communication styles and information provision practices they encountered in Serbian outpatient settings. Several respondents had brought medication brand names no longer available in Serbia, creating additional confusion. The paper argues that diagnostic discontinuity for returnees constitutes a structural gap in Serbian health policy, which currently lacks any standardised re-integration protocol for returning migrants with pre-existing chronic conditions.

title: Institutional Trust and Chronic Disease Self-Management: A Survey Study of 1,100 Adults with Diagnosed Chronic Conditions in Serbia
abstract: Qualitative research on chronic illness in Serbia has consistently found low institutional trust as a background factor shaping healthcare-seeking behaviour, but quantitative data remain scarce. This paper reports findings from a cross-sectional survey administered to 1,100 adults with at least one diagnosed chronic condition, recruited via general practices across four Serbian regions in 2023. The questionnaire combined validated items from the Trust in Physicians Scale and the Partners in Health scale with Serbia-specific items on informal payment practices and perceived healthcare quality. Multilevel regression analyses showed that reported experience of informal payment was the strongest predictor of reduced institutional trust (β=−0.38, p<0.001), outperforming disease severity and socioeconomic status. Lower institutional trust was in turn associated with reduced adherence to prescribed medication regimens and higher use of informal therapeutic networks. Regional variation was modest after controlling for individual-level factors. The findings strengthen the case for addressing informal payment as a structural determinant of self-management outcomes.

title: Diagnosis as Boundary Work: How Serbian General Practitioners Distinguish 'Real' from 'Functional' Illness
abstract: Drawing on 46 interviews with general practitioners in Serbia conducted between 2024 and 2025, this paper examines the cognitive and rhetorical work through which GPs draw distinctions between conditions they regard as biomedically legitimate and those they classify informally as 'functional', 'psychological', or 'invented'. Thematic analysis identified a cluster of boundary-marking practices: reliance on laboratory results as proof of legitimacy, attribution of ambiguous presentations to patient personality types, and reference to workload pressure as justification for brief consultations. Female patients and patients with lower educational attainment were disproportionately assigned to the 'functional' category, as reported in GPs' own accounts. The paper situates these practices within the sociology of boundary work as developed by Gieryn and extended by Star and Griesemer to clinical settings, arguing that diagnostic boundary drawing in primary care reproduces existing social inequalities by assigning less diagnostic effort to patients already marginalised in other social domains.

title: Leaving or Staying? Migration Intentions and Precarious Employment Among Youth in Vojvodina
abstract: Emigration from Serbia has accelerated since 2010, with young people and the educated among the most mobile. This conference paper examines the relationship between subjective experience of labour market precarity and stated migration intentions, using data from a cross-sectional survey of 508 respondents aged 18–34 in Vojvodina, collected in 2018. Logistic regression models show that experiencing two or more episodes of informal employment in the preceding three years significantly increases the probability of expressing definite migration intentions (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.47–3.11), net of education, ethnicity, and parental socioeconomic status. The relationship is stronger for respondents in municipalities with above-average unemployment rates. Qualitative interviews with 15 respondents illustrate how uncertainty about future employment stability is narrated as the primary driver of migration planning, with destination countries including Germany, Austria, and Canada cited most frequently.

title: Measuring Sunday: Self-Reported Versus Counted Church Attendance Among Roman Catholics in Vojvodina, 2007–2009
abstract: This study compares self-reported attendance figures drawn from a representative household survey of 812 Roman Catholic respondents in Vojvodina with headcounts conducted by trained observers in 34 parishes during the same period. Self-reported weekly attendance exceeded observer-counted figures by an average of 18 percentage points, consistent with patterns documented in Western European contexts. The discrepancy was largest among respondents aged 35–55 and in municipalities with higher unemployment rates. The paper discusses possible mechanisms, including social desirability bias and definitional ambiguity regarding what constitutes an 'attendance'. Logistic regression models show that educational level and frequency of private religious practice partially predict the size of the individual discrepancy. The findings have implications for survey-based estimates of religiosity in the region and call for mixed-method approaches that combine observational and self-report data in future studies.

title: Comparison of Buffer-Based and Rate-Based Adaptation Algorithms for HTTP Adaptive Streaming over Emulated Mobile Networks
abstract: This paper evaluates three representative HTTP adaptive streaming adaptation algorithms—a pure buffer-based approach, a throughput-estimation approach, and a hybrid variant—using a controlled network emulation testbed built on Linux Traffic Control. Experiments simulate LTE traces collected from a publicly available dataset of 120 drive-test recordings across urban and suburban environments. Each algorithm was exercised across 40 video sequences encoded at seven quality levels from 200 kbps to 4 Mbps using H.264. Performance is measured using rebuffering ratio, average bitrate, and number of quality switches per session. Results show that the buffer-based algorithm reduces rebuffering events by 34% compared to the throughput-estimation approach on highly variable traces, but increases the number of quality switches by 18%. The hybrid algorithm achieves the best trade-off on sequences where bandwidth variability is moderate. All experiment scripts and trace files are released as supplementary material.
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Broadband Communications and Information Technology (BCIT)

title: Measuring Segment Fetch Time Estimation Accuracy in DASH Players Under Bursty Packet Loss
abstract: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP clients rely on accurate throughput estimation to make bitrate decisions. This work examines how bursty packet loss—modelled using a Gilbert–Elliott two-state Markov chain—distorts segment fetch time estimates in four open-source DASH players. A repeatable experiment harness was built around a local MPEG-DASH server and a kernel-level packet loss injector. Twelve loss patterns covering burst lengths from 2 to 50 packets and mean loss rates from 0.5% to 8% were applied. Results reveal that all tested players systematically underestimate available throughput when burst length exceeds 20 packets, leading to unnecessarily conservative bitrate selection. The degree of underestimation ranges from 12% to 41% depending on player and loss pattern. A corrective exponential smoothing scheme with a burst-detection gate is proposed and shown to reduce estimation error by an average of 22 percentage points across the tested conditions.

title: Latency Characterisation of WebRTC Signalling Paths in Peer-to-Peer and Selective Forwarding Unit Configurations
abstract: WebRTC deployments differ substantially in their signalling and media-plane topology. This study measures end-to-end signalling latency for peer-to-peer (P2P) and Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) configurations across three geographic scenarios: local-area, national, and cross-border (Serbia–Austria). A custom WebRTC test harness built on a headless Chromium driver records ICE candidate gathering time, DTLS handshake duration, and first-frame latency for 500 session-establishment attempts per scenario per topology. Median signalling latency in the SFU configuration exceeds P2P by 38 ms on LAN and by 74 ms on the cross-border path, while P2P ICE candidate gathering takes disproportionately longer under symmetric NAT. The paper also examines the effect of TURN server placement on gathering time, finding that co-locating the TURN server with the SFU reduces total latency by up to 19% in the cross-border scenario. Practical guidelines for server placement are derived from the measurements.

title: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming in Practice: Deployment Challenges and Protocol Trade-offs
abstract: This book chapter surveys practical considerations in deploying adaptive bitrate streaming at scale, covering the MPEG-DASH and HLS protocol families, content delivery network integration, and segment duration selection. The chapter discusses trade-offs between segment length (2 s versus 6 s) and their effect on startup latency, zapping time, and storage overhead, drawing on published measurement studies and the authors' own testbed experiments. A section is devoted to low-latency extensions (LL-DASH and LL-HLS), examining their chunked transfer encoding mechanisms and the additional demands they place on origin server configuration. The chapter concludes with a discussion of common pitfalls in manifest generation and CDN cache interaction that lead to avoidable rebuffering in production deployments. Aimed at graduate students and practitioners, the text includes annotated configuration examples and references to open-source toolchains.

title: Container-Based Deployment of Open-Source SFU Media Servers: Resource Consumption and Scaling Behaviour Under Synthetic Load
abstract: Selective Forwarding Unit media servers are increasingly deployed inside container orchestration platforms. This paper measures CPU, memory, and network I/O consumption of two widely used open-source SFU implementations under synthetic WebRTC load generated by a headless browser farm. Tests scale from 10 to 400 concurrent video participants in increments of 10, with each participant sending a 720p30 stream at 1.5 Mbps. Measurements are taken on a single physical host and on a three-node Kubernetes cluster. The single-host experiments reveal that both servers reach CPU saturation at approximately 280 concurrent senders, though memory profiles differ substantially: one server allocates memory proportionally to participant count while the other shows stepwise growth correlated with internal thread pool boundaries. In the Kubernetes configuration, automatic horizontal pod autoscaling with a CPU threshold of 70% correctly provisions additional replicas in all but two of 30 scaling events, where a 4-second detection lag causes brief packet loss spikes averaging 1.2%.

title: Coordinated Bitrate Adaptation Across Multiple SFU Nodes Using a Shared Network State Cache
abstract: When a WebRTC session spans more than one Selective Forwarding Unit node, individual per-node congestion control decisions can conflict, causing bitrate oscillations visible to end users. This paper proposes a coordination mechanism in which each SFU node periodically writes per-stream bandwidth estimates and packet loss statistics to a shared Redis cache, and a lightweight arbitration process resolves conflicting instructions before they are forwarded to sending clients. The mechanism is implemented as an extension to an open-source SFU and evaluated in a three-node testbed using network emulation to introduce 5–25% asymmetric packet loss. Without coordination, competing REMB messages cause 1.8 quality switches per minute on average in the tested scenarios; with the cache-based coordination layer, this falls to 0.4 switches per minute. Mean video bitrate delivered to receivers increases by 11% under high-loss conditions. The Redis round-trip overhead adds a median of 3.2 ms to the control loop.

title: Effect of ICE Restart Frequency on Perceived Quality in Mobile WebRTC Sessions During Handover Events
abstract: Handover between Wi-Fi and cellular access in mobile devices triggers ICE restarts in WebRTC sessions, temporarily interrupting media flow. This study quantifies how restart frequency and duration affect perceived audiovisual quality using a combination of objective metrics (VMAF, PESQ) and a small subjective test with 28 participants recruited from university staff and students. A mobile test client running on Android was used to force handover events at controlled intervals of 30 s, 60 s, and 120 s during 5-minute video call sessions. VMAF scores drop by an average of 18 points during a restart event of 900 ms duration. Subjective ratings show a statistically significant decline in overall quality scores when restart events occur more frequently than once per 60 seconds (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.01). Increasing the ICE candidate pre-gathering timeout from 500 ms to 1500 ms reduces median restart duration by 310 ms without measurably affecting session setup time.

title: Overhead Analysis of Encryption and Authentication in Large-Scale WebRTC Deployments
abstract: DTLS-SRTP is mandatory in WebRTC, yet its computational overhead is rarely quantified in the context of high-density media servers. This paper measures CPU cycles consumed by DTLS handshake and SRTP encryption on commodity x86-64 server hardware across three cipher suites (AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305) at participant counts from 50 to 600. Profiling is performed using hardware performance counters via the perf subsystem. AES-256-GCM consumes 9% more CPU than AES-128-GCM at 600 participants; CHACHA20-POLY1305 outperforms both AES variants on processors without AES-NI acceleration by 23%, but trails AES-128-GCM by 7% when AES-NI is present. The paper also evaluates the overhead of DTLS session resumption, finding that it reduces per-connection handshake CPU cost by 61% and is therefore worth enabling in deployments where clients reconnect frequently. Findings are contextualised against projected server capacity costs for a hypothetical deployment of 10,000 concurrent users.
venue: Journal of Network and Communication Security

title: Signal Attenuation Through Reinforced Concrete Walls at Sub-GHz Frequencies: A Controlled Laboratory Study
abstract: Penetration loss through reinforced concrete walls is a critical parameter for indoor and sub-surface LoRa deployments but is rarely characterised under controlled conditions. This study measured insertion loss at 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz through six concrete slab samples with varying aggregate composition and rebar density, obtained from a demolition site in Novi Sad. A vector network analyser with calibrated horn antennas was used in a shielded measurement cell. Median penetration loss at 868 MHz ranged from 14.3 dB for a 15 cm unreinforced slab to 31.7 dB for a 30 cm slab with 12 mm rebar at 10 cm spacing. Frequency dependence followed an approximately linear relationship with slab thickness in the 868–915 MHz band. The results provide material-specific correction factors for use in link budget tools targeting basement and underground infrastructure sensor deployments.

title: Quantisation Effects on Convolutional Neural Networks for Vibration-Based Fault Detection Deployed on Cortex-M7
abstract: Post-training quantisation (PTQ) of floating-point convolutional neural networks to 8-bit fixed-point is a standard step for microcontroller deployment, but its effect on detection sensitivity for subtle bearing faults is not well characterised. This paper trains a small five-layer 1-D CNN on 30000 vibration segments (2048 samples each, 25.6 kHz) covering five fault categories and a healthy class, then applies symmetric and asymmetric per-layer and per-channel PTQ schemes. Accuracy degradation from float32 to int8 ranged from 0.4% (per-channel asymmetric) to 3.8% (per-layer symmetric) on the test set. Flash footprint dropped from 187 kB to 51 kB, and inference on an STM32H743 at 480 MHz required 4.1 ms, fitting comfortably within a 10 ms real-time budget. An ablation study shows that quantisation of the first convolutional layer accounts for 60–70% of total accuracy loss, suggesting a mixed-precision strategy where only that layer remains in float16.

title: Low-Cost dSPACE-Based Hardware-in-the-Loop Test Bench for Hybrid Energy Storage Controllers
abstract: This paper describes the construction and validation of a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test bench designed for rapid prototyping of hybrid energy storage control algorithms. The plant model, representing a supercapacitor–battery DC bus with a bidirectional half-bridge converter, runs on a dSPACE DS1104 card at a 10 μs integration step. The physical part of the bench includes a programmable DC electronic load and a 10 A bidirectional power supply that receive setpoint commands via analogue outputs. Validation against a purely physical bench with identical storage components showed agreement in current waveforms within ±2.1% over a 3-hour test cycle. The described setup reduces test time compared with repeated physical charging cycles and allows safe evaluation of fault scenarios such as sudden load disconnection and converter switch failure. Component cost is detailed, and the bench has been made available to graduate students in the laboratory at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

title: Voltage Over-Scaling in Custom CMOS Arithmetic Circuits: Timing Error Rates and Image Quality Correlation
abstract: Reducing the supply voltage below the guardband threshold of a synchronous digital circuit introduces timing violations that manifest as bit-level errors at flip-flop outputs. This paper characterises the relationship between supply voltage reduction, timing error rate, and perceptual image quality degradation for three arithmetic building blocks—a 16-bit carry-lookahead adder, an 8×8 Wallace tree multiplier, and a 16-bit barrel shifter—implemented in a 180 nm standard cell process. Circuits are fabricated as part of a multi-project wafer run and tested at supply voltages from 1.8 V down to 1.1 V. Timing error rates are measured using a scan-based capture scheme. The resulting error patterns are injected into a software model of a JPEG 2000 wavelet transform stage, and SSIM is measured on a 300-image corpus. Results show that adder and shifter error rates remain below 0.1% down to 1.35 V, while the multiplier degrades more steeply, dropping below acceptable SSIM thresholds at 1.45 V.

title: Bearing current measurement methodology for inverter-driven induction motors under supply voltage imbalance
abstract: This paper presents a systematic measurement methodology for quantifying bearing currents in induction motors fed by voltage-source inverters operating under supply voltage imbalance. Three current paths are distinguished: circulating bearing currents, rotor ground currents, and electric discharge machining (EDM) currents. Shielded Rogowski coils with a bandwidth of 50 MHz were used to capture fast transients on the shaft and bearing outer races of a 15 kW four-pole induction motor. Measurements were conducted at switching frequencies of 4, 8, and 12 kHz under balanced conditions and under 2%, 4%, and 6% voltage imbalance defined according to NEMA MG1 methodology. Results show that EDM current pulse repetition rate increases by approximately 23% when imbalance rises from 0% to 6% at 8 kHz switching frequency. The circulating current component, by contrast, is largely insensitive to supply imbalance within this range. The methodology and uncertainty analysis presented here are intended to support reproducible comparisons across laboratories.

title: Land Fragmentation and Rental Market Activity in Vojvodina: Evidence from Cadastral Records, 2010–2020
abstract: Land fragmentation remains a persistent structural feature of agriculture in the Pannonian Plain. This paper uses parcel-level cadastral data from three municipalities in Vojvodina, covering approximately 48,000 parcels, to document trends in average parcel size, ownership dispersion, and the incidence of rental agreements over the 2010–2020 period. Descriptive statistics are combined with a probit model to identify farm and plot characteristics associated with the likelihood of a parcel entering the rental market. Results indicate that parcels smaller than 0.5 hectares and those with absentee owners located more than 50 km from the farm have a statistically significant higher probability of remaining outside active cultivation or being rented informally. The share of formally registered rental contracts increased from 31 percent to 47 percent over the study period, though substantial heterogeneity exists across municipalities. The findings suggest that incomplete land market institutions, rather than price signals alone, drive fragmentation persistence in this region.

title: Anticipated Decoupling Effects on Farm Exit Intentions in Serbia: A Survey-Based Analysis
abstract: Using a structured farm survey conducted in 2023 across four districts of Vojvodina (n = 312 farms), this study investigates how expectations about future subsidy decoupling under Serbia's EU accession-aligned agricultural policy affect stated intentions to exit farming, rent out land, or expand holdings. The questionnaire captured farm size, tenure structure, operator age, off-farm income, and respondents' awareness of CAP reform trajectories. Binary logistic regression is used to model exit and expansion intentions separately. Farms operated by individuals over 55 years with more than 40 percent of household income from off-farm sources show the highest probability of stating exit intentions conditional on decoupling. Smaller farms below 5 hectares are more likely to indicate plans to rent out rather than sell. Awareness of policy reform details is low across the sample, with fewer than 28 percent of respondents able to correctly characterise the difference between coupled and decoupled payment schemes. The results point to information gaps as a potential policy leverage point in the pre-accession context.

title: Land Consolidation Programmes in EU Candidate States: A Comparative Review of Implementation Barriers in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro
abstract: This book chapter reviews the administrative, legal, and financial barriers to state-led land consolidation programmes in three Western Balkan EU candidate countries between 2015 and 2023. Drawing on programme documents, national legislation, semi-structured interviews with 14 officials from land administration agencies, and published evaluation reports, the chapter maps the gap between consolidation targets set in National Rural Development Programmes and actual consolidation area achieved. In all three countries, fewer than 15 percent of planned consolidation area had been processed by end-2022. Common barriers include incomplete land registration, multi-year inheritance disputes that block parcel transfers, and insufficient co-financing capacity at the municipal level. The chapter also notes that subsidy design in each country continues to decouple payment entitlements from consolidation participation, reducing the policy coherence between income support and structural adjustment objectives. Recommendations focus on sequencing land registration completion ahead of consolidation targeting and aligning payment eligibility rules with consolidation programme incentives.

title: Buyer power, slaughterhouse concentration, and farm-gate price suppression in the Serbian pig sector
abstract: This chapter reviews the industrial structure of the Serbian pig slaughtering sector and links it to empirical evidence on farm-gate price formation. Using plant-level slaughterhouse throughput data obtained under a data access agreement with the Veterinary Directorate of Serbia for 2010–2018, we calculate regional CR4 ratios at the NUTS-3 level. In the majority of Serbian districts, the top four slaughterhouses account for over 70 percent of certified throughput. We then estimate farm-gate price equations for each region and find a significant negative relationship between regional buyer concentration and farm-gate price levels, after controlling for feed costs and live-weight inventory. The estimated buyer power discount ranges from 3 to 9 percent of the market price. The chapter also surveys non-price mechanisms through which concentrated buyers exert influence, including delayed payment terms and quality grade manipulation, drawing on a structured survey of 124 pig farmers conducted in 2017.

title: Comparing Autoencoder Architectures for Anomaly Scoring in Web Server Access Logs
abstract: We evaluate four autoencoder designs—shallow, deep, variational, and denoising—for scoring anomalies in Apache access logs gathered from three production web services over 90 days. Input features include request method, status code, payload size, inter-arrival time, and URI path hash. Each architecture is trained on a 70-day clean baseline and tested on 20 days containing 1,247 manually labelled anomalies spanning DDoS precursors, crawler bursts, and authentication brute-force sequences. The denoising autoencoder achieves the highest AUROC of 0.91, while the variational model offers better calibration of reconstruction-error thresholds. We find that log volume spikes caused by legitimate marketing campaigns substantially raise false-positive rates unless a session-level normalisation step is applied. Processing latency for the best model is 18 ms per 10,000 requests on a single GPU, making online deployment feasible. Code and anonymised dataset excerpts are released.

title: Temporal Pattern Mining in Multi-Source Event Logs Using Frequent Episode Discovery
abstract: Frequent episode discovery is applied to correlated event sequences drawn simultaneously from OS syslogs, application logs, and SNMP traps in a mid-sized enterprise network. The study covers a 14-month trace comprising events from 120 devices. Episodes are mined at three temporal granularities (1 s, 10 s, 60 s) and ranked by a lift-based interestingness measure. Results show that 83% of confirmed incidents correspond to at least one high-lift episode identified at the 10-second granularity, while per-source mining misses 41% of the same incidents. A post-processing step uses agglomerative hierarchical clustering to group structurally similar episodes, reducing the analyst's review set from ~9,000 raw episodes to 214 episode families. The paper also discusses the computational cost of episode mining as event rates grow, reporting quadratic scaling behaviour beyond roughly 50,000 events per second on commodity hardware.

title: Benchmarking Stream Processing Engines for Real-Time Log Anomaly Detection Pipelines
abstract: This study compares Apache Flink, Apache Storm, and a custom lightweight engine for deploying log anomaly detection models in a streaming context. Three detection algorithms—isolation forest, one-class SVM, and a sliding-window statistical method—are embedded into each engine and evaluated on synthetic log streams injected at rates from 10,000 to 500,000 events per second. Metrics collected include end-to-end latency, throughput, CPU and memory footprint, and detection recall under backpressure conditions. Flink exhibits the most stable latency (median 7 ms at 200 k events/s) and the lowest performance degradation when detection model inference time increases. The one-class SVM degrades most severely under high throughput, dropping recall from 0.88 to 0.61 at 400 k events/s due to feature computation bottlenecks. Recommendations for practitioners on engine and algorithm pairing are provided.

title: Log Parsing at Scale: Evaluating Drain, Spell, and AEL on Industrial SCADA Event Logs
abstract: Log parsing is a prerequisite for machine learning on unstructured log data, yet most parsing benchmarks use IT rather than operational technology (OT) logs. This paper evaluates three representative parsers—Drain, Spell, and Abstracting Event Log (AEL)—on logs collected from two SCADA systems in a regional water treatment facility and a district heating network, totalling 22 million lines across eight months. Evaluation uses grouping accuracy against a manually annotated ground truth of 310 distinct event templates. Drain achieves 94.1% grouping accuracy on water-treatment logs but drops to 81.7% on heating-network logs, where message formats are less regular. A hybrid pre-processing step combining domain-specific token masking with Drain raises accuracy to 97.4% on both corpora. Parser throughput, sensitivity to depth and similarity-threshold hyperparameters, and degradation under firmware update events are also analysed in detail.

title: Correlated Anomaly Detection Across Microservice Traces and Infrastructure Logs Using Graph-Based Clustering
abstract: Modern applications generate interleaved traces from dozens of microservices alongside infrastructure logs from the underlying Kubernetes nodes. This paper proposes representing concurrent events as nodes in a time-attributed multigraph, where edges encode causal or temporal co-occurrence within a configurable window. Community detection via the Louvain algorithm is then applied to identify correlated anomaly clusters. Experiments are conducted on a synthetic microservice benchmark (8 services, 14 days, 4.3 billion events) with injected faults covering latency spikes, pod crashes, and network partitions. The graph-based approach achieves a macro-averaged F1 of 0.84 for fault-type classification, compared to 0.71 for an independent per-log isolation forest baseline. Memory consumption grows linearly with the number of active trace IDs, reaching 6.2 GB at peak load in the test environment. A pruning strategy based on trace-completion events reduces memory usage by 38%.

title: Self-Tuning Threshold Selection for Streaming Anomaly Detectors Under Non-Stationary Log Distributions
abstract: Fixed reconstruction-error thresholds for autoencoder-based anomaly detectors become unreliable when log distributions shift due to application updates, workload changes, or seasonal traffic patterns. This paper introduces a threshold adaptation scheme based on extreme value theory (EVT), specifically fitting a generalised Pareto distribution to the tail of recent reconstruction errors in a sliding window of configurable width. The scheme is evaluated on four real-world log datasets with documented distribution shifts: a university web portal (50 days), an e-commerce backend (90 days), a CI/CD pipeline (120 days), and a virtualised telecom switching platform (60 days). Compared to static thresholds and a simple percentile-based method, the EVT approach reduces false-positive rates by between 22% and 47% depending on dataset, while maintaining recall above 0.87 in all four cases. Computational overhead of threshold updates is under 2 ms per window step.
venue: Journal of Network and Systems Management

title: Unsupervised Detection of Lateral Movement in Enterprise Networks via Windows Event Log Correlation
abstract: Lateral movement by adversaries typically produces subtle, distributed signals across Windows Security Event Logs on multiple hosts. This study constructs user-host access graphs from Security Event IDs 4624, 4648, 4768, and 4769 collected over 30 days from a 600-host enterprise test environment, with synthetic lateral movement sequences injected following MITRE ATT&CK patterns. Node embeddings derived from a graph autoencoder are clustered with k-means; cluster membership deviation is used as an anomaly score. The method detects 19 of 24 injected lateral movement chains with a false-positive rate of 3.2 per day—substantially below the 11.7 per day produced by a signature-based SIEM rule set. A user-facing triage interface ranks suspicious chains by graph anomaly score. Limitations around encrypted Kerberos traffic and pass-the-hash variants that bypass standard logging are discussed.
venue: Proceedings of the 18th European Symposium on Research in Cybersecurity (ESRC)

title: Log-Based Predictive Maintenance for Conveyor Belt Controllers: A Case Study from a Food-Processing Plant
abstract: Predictive maintenance using log data from industrial programmable logic controllers (PLCs) is explored in a food-processing facility in Vojvodina operating 14 conveyor belt lines. PLC diagnostic logs recording motor current deviations, sensor timeouts, and safety interlock triggers were collected over 18 months, yielding approximately 9.4 million log entries and 38 confirmed maintenance events. A combination of sliding-window frequency features and an isolation forest classifier trained on normal operating periods is used to flag degradation precursors. Leave-one-out cross-validation across the 38 events yields a mean warning lead time of 4.3 hours before failure with a precision of 0.79 and recall of 0.87. The paper describes practical challenges including irregular maintenance windows that contaminate normal-operation labels and proprietary log formats that required manual template construction.

title: Dimension Reduction Strategies for Log Embeddings in High-Throughput Anomaly Detection: UMAP, PCA, and Random Projections Compared
abstract: Log embedding vectors derived from transformer-based language models are high-dimensional (768–1024 dimensions) and expensive to process at stream-processing speeds. This paper systematically compares three dimension-reduction strategies—PCA, random projections, and UMAP—for use in downstream anomaly detection on log streams, evaluating trade-offs between compression ratio, anomaly detection accuracy, and reduction latency. Experiments use four publicly available log datasets augmented with two proprietary datasets from partners, covering syslog, HDFS, BGL supercomputer logs, and application logs from a regional ISP. At a 32-dimensional target, UMAP preserves anomaly structure best (AUROC 0.89 averaged across datasets) but requires 14× more time to fit than PCA. Random projections at 64 dimensions achieve AUROC 0.84 with negligible fitting overhead, making them preferable in continuously retraining deployments. Interaction effects between reduction method and downstream detector type are analysed with a factorial experimental design.

title: Federated Anomaly Detection on Distributed Log Streams Without Raw Data Sharing
abstract: Many organisations are willing to participate in shared anomaly detection initiatives but cannot transfer raw logs off-premises due to regulatory or competitive concerns. This paper proposes a federated learning framework in which each participant trains a local autoencoder on its own log streams and shares only model parameter gradients with a central aggregator. Experiments involve five simulated organisations with heterogeneous log formats (web, database, VPN, mail, and DNS servers) and deliberately asynchronous update schedules. Federated averaging and two robust aggregation strategies (coordinate-wise median and trimmed mean) are compared. The federated model achieves AUROC within 0.04 of a centrally trained oracle model on anomalies present across multiple participants, though performance degrades for organisation-specific anomaly types unique to a single participant. Communication overhead per round is under 12 MB per participant.

title: Temporal Causality Inference Between Correlated Log Events Using Granger-Inspired Tests on Count Time Series
abstract: Distinguishing genuine causal relationships between event types from spurious temporal correlations is a persistent challenge in multi-source log analysis. This paper adapts Granger causality testing to discrete-valued count time series formed by bucketing log event occurrences at 1-second resolution. A negative binomial regression model accounts for overdispersion common in log count data. The approach is validated on a synthetic dataset of 50 known causal pairs injected into background traffic and on a real 90-day production log corpus from a cloud-hosted ERP system. On the synthetic data, the method recovers 46 of 50 causal pairs at a 5% false-discovery-rate threshold; on the production corpus, six previously unknown causal pairs are identified that collectively explain a recurring five-minute service degradation whose root cause had been unresolved for over a year. Sensitivity to bucket width and minimum event frequency is characterised.
venue: Knowledge and Information Systems

title: A Structured Dataset of Serbian Bank Statement Scans for Financial OCR Research
abstract: Progress in financial document OCR is hampered by the lack of publicly available, annotated datasets that reflect real-world scan quality variation. This paper describes the construction and release of SerbBankScan-2018, a corpus of 2,400 bank statement page images sourced from three Serbian commercial banks (anonymised), spanning the years 2005–2015. Images were digitised at 200 and 300 dpi under three scanner types and include instances of ink smearing, paper yellowing, and duplex bleed-through. Ground-truth transcriptions were produced by two independent annotators and reconciled, covering approximately 1.1 million character instances. Inter-annotator agreement on ambiguous tokens reached 94.3%. The paper describes annotation guidelines, class distribution statistics, and baseline OCR results obtained with Tesseract 4.0 and a fine-tuned CRNN model, reporting character error rates of 7.2% and 3.8% respectively.

title: Segmentation of Multi-Page Laboratory Reports into Logical Sections Using Hierarchical Clustering of Visual Features
abstract: Multi-page laboratory reports often bundle a cover page, summary tables, appendices with raw measurement data, and signature blocks into a single PDF. Downstream extraction systems benefit from first segmenting the document into these logical sections. This paper applies agglomerative clustering over a feature vector that combines text density, estimated line spacing, font-height distribution, and the presence of ruling lines per page. No labelled training data are used; the number of clusters is selected by the silhouette criterion. Evaluated on 620 multi-page reports from five laboratories, covering water analysis, soil testing, and food microbiology, the method correctly assigns 91.2 % of pages to their ground-truth section class when the section count is known and 87.4 % when it is estimated automatically. The paper includes an ablation study showing that ruling-line features provide the largest marginal contribution to clustering quality.

title: Stability of Feature Importance Rankings Under Bootstrap Resampling in Random Forests
abstract: Feature importance scores derived from tree-based models are widely used to explain predictions, but their stability under data perturbation is rarely quantified. This study applies bootstrap resampling (B=500) to four tabular datasets ranging from 2,000 to 80,000 instances, computing mean decrease in impurity and permutation-based importance at each resample. Rank correlation (Spearman ρ) between importance vectors from different bootstrap draws is used as a stability metric. The analysis finds that for datasets with fewer than 5,000 instances, the top-ranked feature changes in approximately 22% of resample pairs, rising to 38% when correlated features are present. A simple ranking stabilisation procedure based on averaging importance across 50 sub-models reduces rank volatility by roughly half with less than 2% increase in training time. The findings suggest that single-run importance scores should be treated with caution in regulatory reporting contexts.

title: Resilience-Aware Joint VNF Placement and Migration Scheduling in Backbone SD-WANs: A Survey and Taxonomy
abstract: The joint problem of placing VNFs and scheduling their migrations to maintain service resilience in backbone SD-WANs has attracted significant research attention since 2014. This survey collects and classifies 87 papers published between 2014 and 2025, organising them along four axes: problem formulation (static, dynamic, stochastic), optimisation method (exact, heuristic, learning-based), failure model (single link, multi-link, node, correlated), and evaluation methodology (analytical, simulated, emulated, deployed). The survey identifies that fewer than 20% of papers combine placement and migration scheduling jointly, and fewer than 10% validate on real deployed infrastructure. Key open challenges include handling correlated failures from shared-risk link groups, integrating placement with BGP convergence timescales, and building public benchmarks with realistic failure traces. The paper proposes a reference architecture and a checklist for experimental reproducibility.

title: Comparison of OWAS and REBA observational methods applied to automotive sub-assembly workstations in a Serbian manufacturing plant
abstract: This study evaluated the agreement between the Ovako Working posture Analysis System (OWAS) and the Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) method when applied to 14 workstations in a mid-size automotive components plant near Novi Sad. Two trained observers independently coded 40-minute video recordings of each workstation, yielding 1,120 posture-sampling intervals per method. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Cohen's kappa and intraclass correlation coefficients. OWAS and REBA produced concordant risk-category classifications for 68% of workstations; the largest discrepancies occurred at tasks involving sustained wrist deviation combined with moderate trunk flexion, where REBA consistently assigned higher action categories. Weighted kappa between the two methods was 0.54 (95% CI: 0.44–0.64), indicating moderate agreement. The findings suggest that method selection substantially affects the priority ranking of workstations for intervention, and that neither tool alone adequately captures combined shoulder–wrist loading in precision assembly. Recommendations for method pairing in plant-level ergonomic programmes are provided.

title: Prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal symptoms among manual assembly workers in the Vojvodina region: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was administered to 412 manual assembly workers across six manufacturing facilities in Vojvodina, Serbia. The Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire was used to record 12-month and 7-day symptom prevalence for nine body regions. Overall 12-month prevalence of any musculoskeletal symptom was 74.3%. The lower back (52.2%), neck (41.0%), and right shoulder (37.4%) were the most frequently affected regions. Logistic regression identified prolonged static standing (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.5–3.0), repetitive hand–wrist movements (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.9–4.1), and years of tenure exceeding ten years (OR 1.9, 95% CI 1.3–2.7) as significant predictors of lower-back complaints. Female workers reported higher neck and upper-limb symptom rates than male workers. The results establish a regional baseline for longitudinal monitoring and provide occupational physicians with site-specific risk estimates.

title: Validation of a simplified observational checklist for overhead assembly tasks against electromyographic shoulder muscle activity
abstract: This study tested the validity of a six-item observational checklist developed for rapid assessment of overhead assembly tasks by comparing checklist scores with simultaneously recorded surface electromyography (sEMG) of the upper trapezius, anterior deltoid, and infraspinatus muscles in a laboratory setting. Eighteen male participants performed standardised overhead fastening tasks at three height configurations (15°, 30°, and 60° above shoulder level) with varying tool weights (0.3 kg and 1.2 kg). The checklist assigned a risk score of 1–4 to each task combination. Pearson correlations between checklist scores and normalised mean sEMG amplitude (%MVE) were 0.73 for upper trapezius, 0.81 for anterior deltoid, and 0.61 for infraspinatus. Sensitivity for detecting tasks exceeding 20% MVE was 79% and specificity was 72%. The checklist showed acceptable validity for anterior deltoid loading but underestimated infraspinatus demands at moderate height. Revised scoring weights are proposed.
