title: IMU-based continuous trunk posture monitoring during a full production shift: feasibility and data quality in an industrial setting
abstract: Wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) offer the potential to monitor worker posture over full shifts, but their practical deployment in industrial environments raises questions about data completeness, sensor drift, and worker acceptance. This paper reports a feasibility study in which seven assembly workers wore a two-sensor IMU system (lumbar and thoracic placement) for entire eight-hour shifts across three consecutive working days. Trunk flexion angle was computed at 50 Hz. Data completeness averaged 94.2% across all sessions; the main causes of data loss were electromagnetic interference near welding stations and two instances of sensor detachment. Drift correction using periodic static reference postures reduced root-mean-square angle error from 4.8° to 1.9° when compared with simultaneous video-coded reference frames. Workers rated comfort at 3.9/5 and reported no interference with task performance. The study identifies placement protocols and drift correction procedures suitable for longitudinal field deployment.

title: Effect of a workstation redesign intervention on trunk and neck posture exposure in a printed-circuit-board assembly line
abstract: A before–after field study assessed the impact of a participatory workstation redesign on biomechanical exposure at a printed-circuit-board (PCB) assembly line in a Serbian electronics manufacturer. Prior to the intervention, 11 female assemblers wore IMUs on the thorax and upper arm for two full shifts each. The intervention, developed through four workshops with workers and production engineers, included adjustable work-surface height, tilted component trays, and repositioned magnifying lamp supports. Post-intervention measurements were conducted six weeks later under identical conditions. Mean daily time spent in trunk flexion exceeding 30° decreased from 38.4% to 19.7% of shift time (p < 0.001). Neck flexion greater than 20° fell from 54.1% to 31.8% (p < 0.001). Workers' self-reported neck and shoulder discomfort on a visual analogue scale dropped from 5.8 to 3.4 (scale 0–10) after eight weeks. Production throughput was unchanged. The study provides quantified evidence for workstation adjustment effectiveness in light-electronics assembly.

title: Cumulative lumbar loading indices derived from full-shift IMU recordings: sensitivity to task cycle variation in packaging operations
abstract: Cumulative loading metrics attempt to integrate exposure over time, but their sensitivity to natural variation in task cycles has received limited study in field conditions. This paper analysed IMU recordings from 22 workers in a food-packaging facility over two production shifts each, totalling 352 hours of continuous trunk kinematics data. Three cumulative loading indices were computed: time-weighted angle exposure (TWAE), L4–L5 compression dose estimated via a simplified biomechanical model, and the 90th-percentile flexion angle per hour. Workers were classified by task assignment (manual stacking, case sealing, and quality inspection). Within-worker day-to-day variability expressed as coefficient of variation ranged from 12% to 31% across indices and tasks. Between-task differences were statistically significant for all three indices (ANOVA, p < 0.01). The compression dose showed the highest discriminative power between task groups. Results suggest that single-shift measurements may be insufficient to characterise habitual exposure, and that at least three measurement days are needed for stable estimates.

title: Musculoskeletal disorder risk in small and medium enterprises: barriers to ergonomic assessment adoption in the Western Balkans
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in manufacturing represent a disproportionate share of occupational musculoskeletal disorder cases in the Western Balkans, yet structured ergonomic assessments are rarely conducted in this sector. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 34 occupational safety officers and production managers across SMEs in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. Thematic analysis identified four main barriers: limited financial resources for consultancy and equipment, absence of internal ergonomics expertise, perception that regulatory compliance through documentation is sufficient, and lack of accessible, low-cost assessment tools adapted to local languages. Facilitating factors included proximity to academic institutions, participation in supplier audit programmes by large OEMs, and previous experience with occupational injury compensation claims. The paper discusses policy implications and proposes a tiered assessment framework that matches tool complexity to available organisational capacity.

title: Upper-limb exposure assessment using the OCRA checklist and strain index in repetitive screwdriving tasks: a comparative analysis
abstract: The Occupational Repetitive Actions (OCRA) checklist and the Strain Index (SI) are both used for repetitive upper-limb task assessment, but their scores do not always agree, creating uncertainty in intervention prioritisation. This study applied both methods to 18 screwdriving task variants differing in screw size (M3–M8), driver type (manual, electric, pneumatic), and cycle time (8–24 s). Task parameters were measured via video analysis and force gauges. OCRA checklist scores ranged from 3.5 to 18.2 and SI scores from 1.8 to 21.6 across task variants. Spearman rank correlation between the two instruments was 0.69. Disagreements exceeding one risk category occurred in six task variants and were associated with tasks where force demands were high but frequency was low. Sensitivity analyses showed that force factor weighting in SI most strongly drives divergence. A decision guide for selecting instruments according to predominant exposure dimension is presented.

title: Postural load classification using machine learning applied to multi-sensor IMU data from manual assembly workers
abstract: This study investigated whether postural risk categories derived from RULA could be reliably predicted from IMU sensor data using supervised machine learning, reducing reliance on manual observer coding. A labelled dataset was constructed by having two observers code 2,840 five-second posture epochs from video recordings of 30 assembly workers, while simultaneous IMU data from seven body segments were collected. Four classifiers were trained and cross-validated: decision tree, random forest, support vector machine, and gradient boosting. Gradient boosting achieved the highest macro-averaged F1 score of 0.78 across four RULA action-level classes, outperforming the others. Precision was highest for Action Levels 1 and 4 (0.88 and 0.85 respectively) and lowest for Level 2 (0.67), which overlaps biomechanically with adjacent classes. Feature importance analysis identified trunk and upper-arm inclination angles and their derivatives as the most discriminative variables. The trained model is being evaluated in an ongoing field deployment.

title: Reliability of RULA scores obtained from markerless depth-camera pose estimation versus manual video coding in an electronics assembly context
abstract: Markerless depth cameras and human-pose estimation algorithms offer an accessible alternative to marker-based motion capture for ergonomic assessments, but their RULA scoring reliability relative to manual coding has not been established for fine assembly tasks. Forty-eight task clips from an electronics assembly laboratory were coded by three trained observers and simultaneously processed by a depth-camera pose-estimation pipeline using a publicly available skeletal model. Joint angles were extracted and converted to RULA scores using standardised angle thresholds. Intraclass correlation coefficients between manual and automated RULA scores were 0.71 for upper-arm, 0.66 for wrist, and 0.52 for neck segments. Action-level agreement at the four-category level was 61%. Systematic underestimation of wrist ulnar deviation by the algorithm was the primary source of error, attributed to limited depth resolution at the distal hand. Targeted correction of wrist-segment estimation is needed before automated scoring can replace observer coding.

title: Six-month follow-up of a resistance exercise programme on upper-limb musculoskeletal symptom severity in automotive cable-harness assemblers
abstract: A randomised controlled trial examined whether a workplace-based resistance exercise programme reduced musculoskeletal symptom severity in cable-harness assemblers performing highly repetitive hand–wrist operations. Sixty-four female workers at one production site were randomised to intervention (n=32) or control (n=32) groups. The intervention consisted of 15-minute guided resistance exercises targeting forearm flexors, extensors, and shoulder external rotators, performed three times per week for 24 weeks. Primary outcome was change in the QuickDASH score at 12 and 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included grip strength, pinch strength, and symptom frequency. At 24 weeks, the intervention group showed a mean QuickDASH reduction of 8.3 points (95% CI: 5.1–11.5) compared with 2.1 points (95% CI: −0.4–4.6) in the control group. Grip strength increased by 9.4% in the intervention group. Attendance at exercise sessions averaged 71%. The study supports targeted exercise as a feasible secondary prevention measure in highly repetitive manual assembly.

title: Ergonomic risk profiling of collaborative robot-assisted assembly cells: do human postural demands change when a cobot handles heavy sub-components?
abstract: Collaborative robots (cobots) are increasingly introduced to assembly lines to reduce physical loading, but systematic measurements of the resulting changes in human postural exposure are scarce. This study compared ergonomic risk profiles at two matched assembly cells in a domestic appliance manufacturer: one fully manual and one with a cobot performing part positioning and transfer of sub-components weighing 4–9 kg. IMU measurements were collected from 12 workers in each cell across two full shifts. RULA-equivalent scores were computed from IMU-derived joint angles. Contrary to expectations, mean trunk flexion time and shoulder abduction exposure were not significantly reduced in the cobot cell (p = 0.12 and p = 0.21 respectively). However, wrist deviation exposure was significantly lower (p = 0.003), and perceived exertion ratings (Borg CR-10) dropped from 4.2 to 2.8 for arm fatigue. Time–motion analysis revealed that workers adopted new postures to interface with the cobot's handover point that partially substituted for the reduced heavy-handling demands. The findings suggest that cobot integration requires concurrent workstation layout optimisation to realise postural benefits.

title: Comparative LCA of solvent-based and aqueous two-phase extraction for enzyme recovery in downstream bioprocessing
abstract: Downstream processing frequently dominates the environmental burden of enzyme-based biotechnology products, yet comparative LCA data for alternative separation technologies are limited. This study assessed global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, and water depletion for two enzyme recovery routes—ethyl acetate solvent extraction and polyethylene glycol–phosphate aqueous two-phase extraction—applied to a model lipase product at laboratory scale. Inventory data were measured experimentally in the Faculty laboratory using a validated gravimetric protocol. The functional unit was defined as 1 kg of lipase with a specific activity of 500 U/g dry weight. Aqueous two-phase extraction showed 34% lower global warming potential (2.1 vs. 3.2 kg CO2-eq) but 2.7 times higher water consumption. Solvent production and incineration dominated the burden of the organic-solvent route. The paper discusses upscaling assumptions and argues that water depletion should be included as a mandatory impact category in downstream process comparisons.
venue: Green Process and Product Assessment

title: Adapting the ecoinvent Background Database to Serbian Electricity Grid Conditions for Construction Product LCA
abstract: Life-cycle assessment studies of construction products in Serbia routinely use European background datasets without adjustment, potentially introducing systematic errors in electricity-related impact categories. This paper presents a procedure for constructing a Serbian electricity grid mix dataset for use in SimaPro and openLCA, based on official generation statistics from 2013 to 2015 published by the national transmission system operator. The adapted mix comprised 70% lignite, 14% hydropower, 9% natural gas, and 7% oil and other sources. The procedure was applied to four construction product case studies: fired clay brick, gypsum board, mineral wool insulation, and ceramic floor tile. Differences in GWP100 compared to the ENTSO-E Central European average ranged from +18% for mineral wool to +31% for gypsum board, driven by higher lignite share. Climate change impacts were most sensitive to grid substitution; land use and water depletion impacts were largely unaffected. A documented dataset file in EcoSpold2 format is made available as supplementary material for regional LCA practitioners.

title: Simultaneous determination of fourteen VOCs in workplace air using a single thermal desorption GC-MS method: validation and application in a flexographic printing plant
abstract: A single-run thermal desorption GC-MS method for the simultaneous quantification of 14 volatile organic compounds (toluene, ethylbenzene, xylene isomers, styrene, ethyl acetate, n-butyl acetate, 2-butanone, 4-methyl-2-pentanone, isopropanol, n-propanol, n-butanol, isobutanol, and acetone) was developed and validated. Method validation followed EN 13936 guidance. Detection limits ranged from 0.3 µg/m³ (ethylbenzene) to 2.1 µg/m³ (acetone). Within-laboratory reproducibility expressed as relative standard deviation was below 8% for all compounds at three concentration levels. The method was applied to 124 personal samples collected over four weeks in a flexographic printing facility. Acetone and ethyl acetate dominated the exposure profile, with geometric means of 312 and 187 mg/m³ respectively. Cluster analysis of individual exposure profiles identified three distinct exposure groups corresponding to ink-mixing, press-operating, and cleaning roles within the facility.

title: Explosion protection measures in small-scale pellet production facilities: a gap analysis against ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU in Vojvodina SMEs
abstract: Seventeen small and medium pellet production enterprises in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina were audited against requirements of ATEX Directives 2014/34/EU and 1999/92/EC. Audits included document review, walkthroughs, and measurement of local dust concentrations. Thirteen facilities lacked an explosion protection document. Zone classification was absent in eleven cases. Only four facilities had conducted any systematic ignition source analysis. Equipment in ATEX Zone 21 that bore no ATEX certification was identified in twelve facilities. Common deficiencies included ungrounded metallic conveyor frames, missing vent panels on bucket elevators, and no housekeeping schedule for dust accumulations. A prioritised compliance checklist was developed from the findings and submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Environment. The paper quantifies the compliance gap and estimates cost ranges for remediation categories, providing a practical basis for a sector-level improvement programme.

title: Sequential extraction of phosphorus fractions in surface sediments of Ludoš Lake, Serbia: baseline characterisation
abstract: Surface sediment samples (0–5 cm, n = 18) were collected from Ludoš Lake, a shallow eutrophic lake in Vojvodina, during summer low-water conditions. A five-step sequential extraction procedure was applied to quantify loosely sorbed P, iron-bound P, aluminium-bound P, calcium-bound P, and residual organic P. Total phosphorus concentrations ranged from 820 to 1 540 mg kg⁻¹ dry weight. Iron-bound P was the dominant fraction (38–52 % of total P), with concentrations peaking in the central basin. Loosely sorbed P showed strong spatial correlation with overlying water dissolved oxygen, suggesting active exchange at the sediment–water interface. Calcium-bound P accounted for 15–22 % of total P and was attributed to carbonate-associated minerals typical of Pannonian lacustrine sediments. The results provide the first systematic fractionation dataset for Ludoš Lake and highlight the large reservoir of potentially mobile P.

title: Pore water phosphate profiles and diffusive flux estimates across the sediment–water interface in three Vojvodina shallow lakes
abstract: Undisturbed sediment cores were retrieved from Palić, Ludoš, and Okanj lakes in late spring and early autumn of 2010. Pore water was extracted by centrifugation at 2 cm depth intervals down to 20 cm. Phosphate concentrations in pore water exceeded overlying water values by factors of 8 to 47 at all sites, indicating a consistent upward concentration gradient. Diffusive fluxes were estimated using Fick's first law with tortuosity-corrected diffusion coefficients, yielding seasonal flux ranges of 0.4–3.2 mg P m⁻² d⁻¹. Autumn values were consistently higher, coinciding with thermally driven bottom-water oxygen depletion. The Palić site showed the highest flux (3.2 mg P m⁻² d⁻¹), consistent with its long history of organic enrichment. These flux estimates are compared with published whole-lake phosphorus budgets for each site and used to assess the relative contribution of internal loading.

title: Effect of nitrate addition on phosphorus retention capacity of eutrophic lake sediments under laboratory-controlled redox conditions
abstract: Intact sediment cores from Ludoš Lake were incubated under four controlled redox treatments: oxic (dissolved oxygen 8–9 mg L⁻¹), sub-oxic with nitrate addition (10 mg NO₃⁻-N L⁻¹), anoxic without nitrate, and anoxic with sulfate reduction allowed. Temperature was maintained at 20 °C. Dissolved phosphate, iron, manganese, and nitrate were monitored in overlying water every 48 hours over a 28-day period. Nitrate addition suppressed phosphate release by 61 % compared with the anoxic control, most plausibly through maintenance of iron-oxide surface binding capacity facilitated by nitrate-reducing bacteria. However, sulfate-reducing conditions led to complete collapse of iron-bound P retention and dissolved phosphate concentrations reached 1.8 mg L⁻¹. Results suggest that nitrate-based management interventions may be effective in sediments dominated by iron-bound P but are insufficient when sulfate reduction becomes prevalent in organic-rich hypolimnetic zones.

title: Seasonal variability in iron-bound phosphorus and its relationship to dissolved oxygen in shallow Pannonian lakes
abstract: Monthly sediment sampling (0–10 cm) was conducted across four sites in Palić Lake over twelve months (2014–2015). Iron-bound P, measured by the modified Hedley procedure, ranged from 210 mg kg⁻¹ in February to 87 mg kg⁻¹ in August at the deepest sampling point (maximum depth 1.8 m). Concurrent measurements of dissolved oxygen and redox potential at 2 cm above the sediment showed that redox potentials below −80 mV preceded significant decreases in iron-bound P by 10–14 days. Total dissolved iron in pore water showed a corresponding increase. Regression analysis across all sites and months yielded a significant inverse relationship between iron-bound P fraction size and cumulative anoxic hours per month (r² = 0.74, p < 0.001). The data suggest that even brief nocturnal anoxia, common in macrophyte-dense shallow lakes, is sufficient to mobilise measurable quantities of iron-bound P on a monthly timescale.

title: Phosphorus internal loading model for shallow polymictic lakes: calibration on Pannonian case studies
abstract: A steady-state phosphorus mass-balance model incorporating an internal loading term was calibrated and validated using a three-year dataset from Ludoš and Okanj lakes. Internal loading rates were estimated from sediment core incubations and pore water flux calculations. The model treats the lake as a single well-mixed compartment and parameterises internal loading as a function of water-column anoxic fraction, derived from continuous oxygen monitoring. Calibration was performed by minimising root-mean-square error between modelled and observed monthly mean total phosphorus in the water column. Root-mean-square error after calibration was 18 µg L⁻¹ for Ludoš and 24 µg L⁻¹ for Okanj, representing acceptable performance for shallow polymictic systems with high short-term variability. Sensitivity analysis identified the internal loading coefficient and the sedimentation rate as the most influential parameters. The model was used to evaluate scenarios of external load reduction and indicates that load reduction alone will not achieve mesotrophic conditions within a decade without simultaneous management of internal loading.

title: Organic phosphorus mineralisation rates in anoxic incubations of Vojvodina lake sediments
abstract: Organic phosphorus (org-P) dynamics were studied in anoxic laboratory incubations of sediments from five lakes in Vojvodina over 42 days at 20 °C. Sediment total organic carbon ranged from 28 to 91 g kg⁻¹. Organic P was operationally defined as the NaOH-extractable P after ignition minus the NaOH-extractable P in unignited samples. Release of phosphate to overlying water during anoxic incubations exceeded calculated inorganic P pools from iron reduction at three of five sites, implying mineralisation of labile org-P contributed 15–38 % of total P release. First-order mineralisation rate constants ranged from 0.003 to 0.011 d⁻¹ and were positively correlated with sediment total organic carbon. These findings suggest that in highly organic sediments, eutrophication models that attribute all anoxic P release to iron reduction may underestimate the long-term internal loading by a substantial margin.

title: Sediment core stratigraphy and historical reconstruction of phosphorus accumulation in Palić Lake over the past 150 years
abstract: Two 60 cm sediment cores from Palić Lake were sectioned at 1 cm resolution and dated by ²¹⁰Pb using the CRS model. Phosphorus fractions, organic carbon, and biogenic silica were measured at 2 cm intervals. Phosphorus accumulation rates increased from approximately 0.12 g P m⁻² yr⁻¹ in pre-1900 sediments to 0.94 g P m⁻² yr⁻¹ in post-1960 layers, coinciding with agricultural intensification in the catchment. The iron-bound P fraction remained proportionally stable (35–45 %) throughout the core, while calcium-bound P declined from 28 % to 18 % and organic P increased from 17 % to 32 % in recent decades. Total P concentrations in the uppermost 2 cm reached 1 870 mg kg⁻¹. The historical reconstruction suggests that the contemporary sediment P pool represents decades of catchment loading and that recovery timescales will likely be multi-decadal even under improved external load conditions.

title: Phosphorus geochemistry in interconnected wetland–lake systems: a case study from the Carska Bara wetland complex, Vojvodina
abstract: The Carska Bara wetland complex consists of a network of oxbow lakes, channels, and reed beds hydrologically connected to the Tisa River floodplain. Sediment samples were collected from eight sub-basins during spring high water and late summer low water. Total phosphorus concentrations ranged from 420 to 1 210 mg kg⁻¹, with lower values in reed-bed sediments and higher values in the central lake basins. Iron-bound P was positively correlated with the proportion of mineral sediment fraction (r = 0.68), while organic P dominated in organogenic reed-bed deposits. Flood pulse events in spring redistributed loosely sorbed P laterally, estimated at 14–37 kg P per flood event based on average suspended sediment concentration and measured loosely sorbed P content. The study characterises the wetland complex as a seasonal P transformer rather than a simple P sink, with net P retention during low water and net P export during flood conditions.

title: Calcium-bound phosphorus in hard-water shallow lakes of the Pannonian Plain: controls and implications for internal loading
abstract: Pannonian shallow lakes typically have high alkalinity and calcium concentrations due to loess-derived catchment geology. Calcium-bound P (Ca-P) is often regarded as geochemically inert over management-relevant timescales, but its formation and dissolution under varying pH and CO₂ conditions may be significant in hard-water systems. Batch experiments were conducted at pH values of 7.5, 8.5, and 9.5 (achieved by CO₂ manipulation) using sediment slurries from six Vojvodina lakes. Ca-P increased by 12–28 % under pH 9.5 conditions, consistent with co-precipitation with calcite driven by algal photosynthesis during summer. Dissolution was observed at pH 7.5 in night incubations, with phosphate release of 0.08–0.21 mg L⁻¹. These diurnal pH oscillations, which commonly exceed 1.5 pH units in macrophyte-dense shallow lakes, suggest that Ca-P participates in short-term P cycling more actively than assumed and should be included in internal loading assessments for hard-water systems.

title: Redox-driven coupling of phosphorus and sulfur cycling in organic-rich sediments of a small endorheic lake, eastern Vojvodina
abstract: An unnamed endorheic saline lake in eastern Vojvodina, with no surface outflow and high organic sediment content (TOC up to 118 g kg⁻¹), was selected to study the interaction of phosphorus and sulfur cycles under persistently reducing conditions. Pore water was sampled monthly over one year using Rhizon samplers at 1, 3, 5, 10, and 15 cm depth. Dissolved sulfide reached 4.2 mM at 15 cm depth in summer. Iron sulfide formation, inferred from AVS (acid volatile sulfide) measurements (up to 38 µmol g⁻¹), reduced the capacity of sediments to retain iron-bound P. Solid-phase iron declined from 8.2 to 2.1 mg g⁻¹ between winter and summer, while loosely sorbed P increased from 12 to 87 mg kg⁻¹ over the same period. A molar Fe:S ratio below 1.5 throughout summer coincided with maximal phosphate concentrations in pore water (up to 6.8 mg L⁻¹). These data indicate that sulfate-mediated iron scavenging is a primary control on P mobility in saline organic-rich sediments and represents a feedback that is difficult to reverse through external load management alone.

title: Assessment of lanthanum-modified bentonite as a phosphorus capping agent in Pannonian shallow lake sediments: a laboratory mesocosm evaluation
abstract: Lanthanum-modified bentonite (LMB) is used in lake restoration to bind mobile phosphorus fractions at the sediment surface. Its effectiveness depends on sediment chemistry and water alkalinity. This study evaluated LMB performance in mesocosms (150 L tanks) filled with sediment and water from Palić Lake. Four dosing rates (10, 20, 40, and 80 g m⁻²) were tested under three redox regimes over 60 days. At 40 g m⁻², overlying water total phosphorus decreased from 390 µg L⁻¹ to 62 µg L⁻¹ within 14 days under oxic conditions, but efficiency dropped to 54 % reduction under anoxic conditions. High alkalinity (mean 4.8 mEq L⁻¹) reduced lanthanum binding capacity relative to published results from softer-water systems. The 80 g m⁻² treatment maintained effective phosphorus suppression even under anoxia. Ecotoxicological parameters (zooplankton mortality, phytoplankton diversity) were unaffected at all dosing rates tested. The results suggest LMB can be effective in Pannonian lakes but requires higher dosing rates than those used in Scandinavian applications due to elevated alkalinity.

title: Interannual variability of internal phosphorus loading in Okanj Lake (2016–2024): trends under changing precipitation and temperature
abstract: A nine-year monitoring dataset from Okanj Lake (2016–2024) was analysed to identify trends in water-column total phosphorus and estimated internal loading under varying climatic conditions. Internal loading was estimated monthly using a mass-balance approach accounting for measured external inputs from the main inflow channel, atmospheric deposition, and outflow. Internal loading was the dominant phosphorus source in six of nine years, accounting for 52–79 % of total annual P input. Years with prolonged drought (lower inflow volume) and higher mean summer water temperatures showed significantly elevated internal loading estimates (mean 1.9 g P m⁻² yr⁻¹) compared with wetter, cooler years (mean 1.1 g P m⁻² yr⁻¹). Linear trend analysis showed a statistically significant increase in summer water temperature of 0.18 °C yr⁻¹ over the study period (p = 0.03). The dataset suggests that climate-driven warming and reduced dilution during dry periods are amplifying internal loading in this system and that eutrophication pressure may worsen even if external loads remain constant.

title: Surface carbonation of commercial soap bars: a comparative field study of five bar formulations over 18 months
abstract: Five commercially formulated soap bars with varying total fatty matter (TFM 72–80%), glycerol content, and declared free alkali were stored under ambient indoor conditions at a standardised location in Novi Sad (mean RH 58%, mean temperature 18 °C). Surface scrapings of approximately 0.1 mm depth were collected at months 0, 3, 6, 12, and 18. Carbonate content was determined by acid digestion and titrimetry, and confirmed by FTIR. All formulations showed measurable carbonate accumulation within three months. The highest TFM bar accumulated 0.38 wt% carbonate after 18 months compared with 1.12 wt% for the lowest TFM bar. Free alkali content at month 0 correlated positively with carbonate accumulation rate (r = 0.89). Hardness loss measured by Shore A durometry correlated with carbonate concentration. The study provides baseline field data linking standard quality parameters to actual carbonation progression under temperate continental climate conditions.

title: Influence of electronic descriptors derived from DFT calculations on QSAR models for imidazole antifungals
abstract: Thirty-one imidazole-based antifungal compounds were subjected to geometry optimisation at the B3LYP/6-31G* level using Gaussian 09. Frontier molecular orbital energies (HOMO, LUMO), chemical hardness, electronic chemical potential, and Fukui condensed indices were extracted and combined with topological descriptors. Principal component regression and partial least squares (PLS) regression were applied separately to the full descriptor matrix. The PLS model with two latent variables (R² = 0.85, Q²LOO = 0.80) outperformed the PCR counterpart by approximately 0.05 in explained variance. Inclusion of the HOMO–LUMO gap and the electrophilicity index ω as predictors substantially reduced cross-validated error relative to models relying on topological indices alone. The applicability domain was defined via the leverage-based Williams plot; three compounds fell outside the domain and were excluded from the predictive statistics. Results suggest that electronic parameters capture sterol biosynthesis inhibition mechanisms that graph-theoretical indices cannot encode.

title: Multi-residue LC-MS/MS screening of antibiotics in irrigation water and adjacent agricultural soil: method development and field application
abstract: This study presents a dual-matrix method for the simultaneous screening of 18 antibiotic residues (9 sulphonamides, 6 tetracyclines, 3 macrolides) in irrigation water and topsoil samples collected from five irrigation canals in the Danube-Tisa-Danube (DTD) hydrosystem, Vojvodina. Water samples (500 mL) were processed by Oasis HLB SPE, while soil (5 g) was extracted by the EDTA-QuEChERS protocol. Both extracts were analysed by the same LC-MS/MS method (HSS T3 column, 10 mM ammonium formate/acetonitrile gradient, ESI+). For soil analysis, matrix-matched calibration prepared in procedural blank extracts of three representative soil types achieved acceptable recoveries (73–109 %). Among 36 paired samples, 10 irrigation water samples contained detectable sulphamethoxazole (0.03–0.8 µg L⁻¹), and the corresponding adjacent soils showed higher sulphonamide concentrations (up to 31 µg kg⁻¹) than canal-distal soils, suggesting cumulative loading via irrigation. The unified analytical platform reduces instrument time per sample batch by approximately 40 % compared to separate method applications.

title: Top-View Human Body Segmentation Using a Single Ceiling-Mounted Camera and Floor-Plane Homography
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of detecting and segmenting standing and crouching humans viewed from a ceiling-mounted monocular RGB camera in a laboratory mock-up of a warehouse aisle. The floor-plane homography is estimated once from a calibration checkerboard and used to warp candidate foreground blobs into a normalised bird's-eye representation before classification. A background-subtraction baseline is compared against a shallow convolutional classifier trained on 4,200 labelled frames collected over three sessions with six volunteers. The homography-normalised pipeline raises detection F1 from 0.71 to 0.83 relative to direct classification in the original image plane. Failure cases concentrate around workers bending below the 90-degree trunk-angle threshold and under heavy shelf occlusion. The dataset and annotation tool are released publicly. Results suggest that even simple geometric normalisation substantially reduces the variation a classifier must handle when the camera viewpoint is fixed and the floor is planar.

title: Estimating Inter-Person Distances in Crowded Indoor Scenes from a Single Fixed Camera Using Ground-Plane Projection
abstract: Accurate distance estimation between pedestrians in shared indoor workspaces is relevant for safety monitoring but difficult with a single camera when the scene is crowded. This work formulates distance estimation as a ground-plane projection problem: detected head centroids from a top-mounted camera are back-projected onto the calibrated floor plane, and Euclidean distances are computed in world coordinates. Detections are obtained with a histogram-of-oriented-gradients detector fine-tuned on an in-house overhead dataset of 1,850 annotated frames. Projection errors are analysed as a function of subject height variation (1.55–1.95 m) and camera height (2.8 m and 3.5 m fixtures). At 3.5 m height, median distance error is 8.1 cm for pairs separated by more than 0.5 m. The method requires no stereo rig and no depth sensor, making it suitable for retrofitting existing ceiling camera infrastructure. Limitations in scenes with more than eight simultaneous occupants are documented.

title: Occlusion-Robust 2D Pose Estimation for Workers Partially Hidden by Industrial Shelving Units
abstract: Standard 2D pose estimators degrade sharply when applied to workers whose lower body is hidden behind shelving structures in warehouses or manufacturing cells. This paper proposes a two-branch architecture: one branch processes the visible torso region and predicts a partial keypoint set, while a second branch uses shelf bounding-box annotations to hallucinate plausible lower-limb configurations conditioned on posture context. Training uses a combination of the publicly available MPII Human Pose dataset and 2,100 newly collected frames from a factory-floor test site in Novi Sad with manually annotated partial poses. On the test split, the two-branch model reduces mean per-joint position error for occluded joints by 18.4 mm compared to a single-branch baseline, while adding only 12% to inference time. Experiments vary occlusion fraction from 30% to 80% of the body. The method is intended as a preprocessing step for downstream depth lifting.

title: A Benchmark Dataset for Overhead-View Human Pose Estimation in Cluttered Indoor Scenes (OVPose-Cluttered)
abstract: Benchmarking overhead-view pose estimators has been hampered by the scarcity of annotated datasets that combine realistic clutter with significant inter-person occlusion. This paper describes OVPose-Cluttered, a dataset of 18,400 annotated frames recorded in three indoor environments: a simulated warehouse, a university canteen, and an assembly workshop. Cameras were mounted at heights between 2.6 m and 4.1 m. Annotations include 17-joint 2D skeletons, per-joint occlusion flags, and approximate depth values obtained by cross-referencing a co-located RGB-D sensor during capture (the depth sensor is not provided to methods under evaluation). Inter-annotator agreement measured by percentage of correct keypoints at 0.05 normalised distance is 93.7%. Baseline results for five published overhead and standard-view pose estimators are reported. The dataset is distributed under a non-commercial research licence and is hosted on the university repository. Known limitations include limited ethnic and body-size diversity among participants.

title: Depth-Consistent Temporal Smoothing for Overhead Monocular 3D Skeleton Sequences
abstract: Frame-by-frame 3D pose estimation from an overhead monocular camera produces skeleton sequences that exhibit temporal jitter, particularly in depth estimates for joints near the camera's optical axis (i.e., the top of the head and shoulders). This paper presents a recurrent smoothing module that appends to any static 3D pose estimator and is trained with a depth-consistency loss penalising physically implausible bone-length variation across consecutive frames. Evaluation is performed on OVPose-Cluttered and on a second sequence dataset of 22 activities recorded in the university's indoor laboratory. The module reduces mean temporal jitter (measured as frame-to-frame joint displacement normalised by bone length) by 34% while increasing per-frame mean per-joint position error by only 1.9 mm. Processing adds 3 ms per frame. Qualitative results show smoother limb trajectories during walking and shelf-retrieval actions. The module is architecture-agnostic and was tested atop three different backbone estimators.

title: Scene-Geometry Prior Estimation from Uncalibrated Ceiling Images Using Structural Line Clustering
abstract: Applying depth-aware human detection in buildings where camera calibration records are unavailable requires recovering geometric priors on-the-fly. This paper proposes a method that clusters line segments extracted from a single ceiling-mounted frame into structural groups corresponding to walls, shelving edges, and floor junctions. From these clusters, camera height and tilt are estimated via a constrained optimisation that assumes a Manhattan-world environment. Tested on 46 ceiling camera installations across three buildings in Novi Sad, the method estimates camera height with a median absolute error of 6.8 cm against laser-measured ground truth. Tilt estimation error is below 1.2 degrees in 80% of test cases. Run-time for geometry estimation is 0.9 s on a standard CPU, making one-time on-deployment calibration practical. The method degrades in rooms with curved or heavily decorated ceilings; a manual override interface is provided.

title: Multi-Person 3D Tracking Under Heavy Mutual Occlusion Using Skeletal Pose Graphs and Temporal Association
abstract: Tracking multiple people in overhead monocular video when individuals frequently pass behind each other or shelving structures requires linking detections across identity-loss intervals. This paper represents each detected person at each frame as a node in a pose graph whose edges encode skeletal similarity, spatial proximity, and estimated depth trajectory. A Hungarian-algorithm assignment with a learned affinity score handles frame-to-frame linking, while a re-identification module based on gait cycle features resolves tracks after occlusion gaps up to 2.1 seconds. On OVPose-Cluttered extended with tracking annotations for 14 sequences, the system achieves a multi-object tracking accuracy of 68.4% and an identity switch rate of 0.09 switches per person per minute, improving over a nearest-neighbour baseline (MOTA 54.1%, 0.31 switches). Experiments range from two to eight simultaneous occupants. Processing runs at 17 fps on a single GPU.

title: Evaluating Monocular Depth Cues for Human Detection in Overhead Views: Focus, Defocus, and Texture Gradient
abstract: Monocular depth estimation in overhead views can exploit cues that are less prominent in frontal views: defocus blur increases sharply as objects approach the lens axis, and texture gradient on clothing and floor surfaces provides scale information. This study systematically evaluates three monocular cue types—defocus map, texture gradient, and apparent body-segment scaling—as standalone and combined depth signals for ranking detected humans by distance from the camera. A controlled experiment captured 30 volunteers at five known heights (floor to camera distances 2.2–4.0 m) under four lighting conditions. Defocus-based depth ranking achieves 84% rank accuracy in isolation; texture gradient achieves 71%; combined ranking via a small fusion network reaches 91%. Cue reliability varies with clothing texture density and ambient illumination. The results inform which cues merit integration into overhead pose-lifting pipelines operating without LiDAR or structured light.

title: Transferring Overhead Pose Estimators Across Indoor Environments Using Domain Adaptation with Style-Transferred Floor Textures
abstract: Overhead pose estimators trained in one indoor facility typically degrade when deployed in a different facility due to variations in floor texture, lighting colour temperature, and ceiling height. This paper investigates a domain-adaptation strategy in which floor-region style transfer—using a fast neural texture synthesis model—is applied to source-domain training images to simulate target-domain appearances, with ceiling-height rescaling applied to match target deployment geometry. The approach requires only 120 unlabelled frames from the target facility. Evaluated on transfers between three facility pairs (warehouse-to-canteen, warehouse-to-assembly-hall, canteen-to-assembly-hall), mean per-joint position error after adaptation is on average 11.3 mm lower than without adaptation and 4.1 mm above a fully supervised target-domain model. The method has no inference-time overhead. Floor texture style transfer is shown to outperform whole-image style transfer for this task because it leaves skeleton-relevant regions largely unaltered.

title: Skeleton-Based Fall Detection From Ceiling Cameras in Geriatric Ward Mock-Ups: Effect of Bed and Furniture Occlusion
abstract: Fall detection in hospital wards using ceiling-mounted monocular cameras is complicated by beds, curtains, and medical equipment that occlude large portions of patient bodies. This paper applies a 3D skeletal pose estimator adapted for overhead views to 14 hours of footage recorded in a geriatric ward mock-up with eight instrumented falls and 220 simulated activities of daily living performed by six healthy adult volunteers. The detector flags a fall event when the estimated hip-joint height drops below 40 cm from the floor and a trunk-angle threshold is exceeded for at least three consecutive frames. With bed and furniture occlusion present, sensitivity is 82.1% and specificity is 94.6% at the chosen thresholds. Without occlusion, sensitivity rises to 93.8%. Sources of missed detections are analysed: rolling out of bed accounts for 61% of false negatives. The work is conducted in collaboration with a medical device development group and is intended as a feasibility study.

title: Depth-Aware Human Detection Without Depth Sensors: A Survey of Methods for Overhead Industrial Camera Systems
abstract: This survey covers methods published between 2010 and 2025 for detecting and localising humans in three-dimensional space using only RGB images from ceiling-mounted or high-angle cameras, with no active depth sensing. The scope includes monocular depth estimation, scene-geometry prior incorporation, top-view pose estimation, and their application to industrial safety monitoring, warehouse logistics, and service robotics. Seventy-one papers are reviewed and categorised along four axes: geometric prior type (none, floor-plane, full room model, learned), depth cue type (appearance, defocus, shadow, combined), occlusion handling strategy, and evaluation protocol. Quantitative comparison tables are provided for seven datasets. Key open problems identified include reliable performance under changing illumination, scalability to multi-storey shelving above 3 m, and the lack of standardised benchmarks combining depth ground truth with heavy occlusion. Practical considerations for deployment in existing facilities are discussed in a dedicated section.

title: Firmware Architecture for Bridging CANopen DS401 and ISO 11783 in Retrofit Sensor Modules
abstract: Many older agricultural implements carry CANopen-based sensors that cannot communicate directly with ISOBUS task controllers. This work describes a firmware architecture for a compact gateway ECU that translates CANopen DS401 digital and analogue I/O process-data objects (PDOs) into ISO 11783 process data messages, enabling legacy sensors to participate in precision-farming data flows without hardware replacement. The gateway is built around an STM32F4 microcontroller and uses two independent CAN controllers operating at 250 kbit/s and 500 kbit/s. Mapping tables are stored in flash and configurable through an ISOBUS virtual terminal menu. Field trials on a 120-hectare test plot with a John Agro tractor (fictional) and a three-section sprayer boom demonstrated 99.6% message delivery over six-hour continuous sessions. Object dictionary alignment issues introduced by vendor-specific CANopen profiles are discussed and a resolution strategy using sub-index remapping is presented.

title: Comparison of Machine-Learning Approaches for Automated Defect Classification in Flying-Probe ICT Data
abstract: This paper compares five supervised classification algorithms—logistic regression, random forest, gradient-boosted trees, a shallow multilayer perceptron, and a support vector machine with RBF kernel—for classifying PCB assembly defects from flying-probe in-circuit test measurement vectors. The dataset comprised 11,340 test records from 18 months of production, annotated with nine defect categories confirmed by automated optical inspection and manual rework records. Feature sets included 28 electrical measurements per record: impedance magnitude, phase, DC resistance, and transient current slope at multiple test points. Random forest and gradient-boosted trees achieved the highest macro-averaged F1 scores of 0.913 and 0.908 respectively on a stratified held-out test set. The MLP performed comparably at 0.901 but required substantially longer training time. A practical deployment scheme is described in which the classifier runs as a post-processing module on the tester host PC, adding less than 200 ms per board. Class imbalance handling via SMOTE is evaluated, showing consistent benefit for rare defect categories.

title: Calibration of a Battery Cell Emulator for BMS ECU Validation on a Low-Cost HiL Platform
abstract: Battery management system (BMS) ECUs require accurate emulation of cell voltages, temperatures, and internal impedances during validation testing. This paper describes the design and calibration of a 12-cell emulator board built from precision voltage references, operational amplifier buffers, and a digitally programmable resistor network to model ohmic and diffusion impedances. The board interfaces to a Zynq-7020 SoC running the simulation host and updates cell parameters at 10 ms intervals via SPI. Calibration was performed against a reference Keithley source-measure unit across the 2.5–4.2 V operating range; voltage accuracy after calibration was ±2.1 mV at 25 °C and ±4.8 mV over the −20 °C to 60 °C range. A lithium iron phosphate cell model with 18 parameters was validated against 12 published drive-cycle datasets. A commercial BMS ECU was tested using 88 scripted test cases including cell balancing activation, state-of-charge estimation accuracy, and over-voltage protection response time. The total bill of materials for the emulator board was 280 EUR.

title: Effect of ferrite tile arrangement on leakage flux and shielding efficiency in inductive charging pads for wheeled industrial robots
abstract: Ferrite shielding is widely used in IPT pads to improve coupling and reduce electromagnetic interference. This study systematically varied the arrangement of N87-grade ferrite tiles beneath a 300 mm × 300 mm rectangular primary coil to identify configurations that maximise shielding efficiency while remaining cost-effective. Six tile layouts were fabricated and measured for field distribution at 150 kHz using a 2D scanning probe at heights of 5, 10, and 20 mm above the coil surface. The best-performing configuration, consisting of a full-coverage layer with 5 mm inter-tile gaps, reduced stray magnetic flux density at 200 mm lateral distance from 18.3 µT to 4.7 µT relative to the unshielded baseline, exceeding the ICNIRP 2010 reference level compliance margin. An analytical reluctance model was fitted to experimental data and showed root-mean-square error of 1.2 µT across all probe positions. Coil quality factor improved from 187 to 224 when full-coverage ferrite was applied. Practical assembly guidance is provided for integration into AGV floor pads.

title: Water sorption isotherms of whey protein concentrate–maltodextrin blends: fitting GAB and BET models across a range of blend ratios
abstract: Equilibrium moisture content was determined for nine binary blends of whey protein concentrate (WPC-80) and maltodextrin (DE 12 and DE 18) over water activity values from 0.11 to 0.85 at 25 °C using a static gravimetric method. Monolayer moisture content estimated by the BET model ranged from 3.1 g/100 g dry matter for pure maltodextrin DE 12 to 6.8 g/100 g for pure WPC-80, with blend values following an approximately linear mixing rule below 0.6 water activity. The GAB model provided better fit across the full range (mean relative deviation below 6% for all blends), while the BET model underestimated uptake above aw 0.65. Critical water activity for the onset of caking was identified between 0.55 and 0.62 depending on blend composition, confirmed visually by scanning electron microscopy of partially sintered particles. The dataset provides baseline thermodynamic parameters for drying and packaging design of whey–carbohydrate powder mixes.

title: Effect of outlet geometry and hopper half-angle on the discharge rate of hygroscopic whey–sugar powder blends
abstract: Discharge behaviour of four whey–sucrose powder blends (20, 40, 60 and 80 wt% whey protein concentrate) was studied using a flat-bottomed and a wedge-shaped hopper with outlet diameters of 10, 15 and 20 mm at two ambient relative humidity levels (40% and 65%). Mass flow rate was measured by weighing at 0.5 s intervals over ten replicate runs per condition. Flow index values derived from Jenike shear cell testing at 65% RH exceeded 4 for all blends with whey content below 60 wt%, indicating cohesive to very cohesive behaviour. Arch formation frequency increased markedly above 60% RH, particularly for high-whey blends, consistent with elevated surface stickiness measured by texture analyser probe. The 15 mm outlet eliminated arching only for blends with 40 wt% whey or less under dry conditions. Empirical regression equations relating blend composition, humidity and hopper geometry to arch probability are proposed.

title: Caking kinetics of spray-dried whey–lactose powder under isothermal humid storage: a structural characterisation study
abstract: Spray-dried whey–lactose powder (70:30 by mass, moisture content 3.2 g/100 g) was stored at 33%, 53% and 65% relative humidity and 25 °C for up to 28 days. Caking degree was quantified as the fraction retained on a 1 mm sieve after standardised mechanical agitation at intervals of 1, 3, 7, 14 and 28 days. Powders stored at 33% RH showed no measurable caking over the study period, while samples at 53% RH reached 42% caking degree by day 14. At 65% RH, caking degree exceeded 85% within 7 days. X-ray powder diffraction confirmed that lactose crystallisation proceeded concurrently with aggregation at 53% and 65% RH, with the degree of crystallinity rising from below 5% initially to 62% at 53% RH after 28 days. Particle contact angle between adjacent aggregated particles, estimated from SEM images using geometric approximation, correlated linearly with caking degree (R² = 0.91). Results were used to parameterise a first-order kinetic model of caking progression.

title: Surface energy components of food-grade anti-caking agents determined by inverse gas chromatography at infinite dilution
abstract: Dispersive and specific components of surface free energy were measured by inverse gas chromatography (iGC) at infinite dilution for six food-grade anti-caking agents: silicon dioxide (E 551), tricalcium phosphate (E 341iii), microcrystalline cellulose (E 460), magnesium stearate (E 572), rice starch and a commercial hydrophobised silica. Measurements were carried out at 30, 40 and 50 °C using a series of n-alkane probes and polar probes (ethyl acetate, acetone, dichloromethane, chloroform). Dispersive surface energy ranged from 29.4 mJ/m² for hydrophobised silica to 61.2 mJ/m² for tricalcium phosphate at 30 °C. The Lewis acid–base parameters Ka and Kb indicated that fumed silicon dioxide had the highest acid character, consistent with its well-documented hydrogen-bond accepting behaviour toward hydroxyl-rich surfaces. These parameters were subsequently correlated with experimentally measured adhesion of each agent to a model whey–maltodextrin particle surface, providing a rational basis for anti-caking agent selection.

title: Comparison of shear cell and avalanche index methods for ranking flowability of protein–carbohydrate powder blends
abstract: Flowability of twelve commercial and laboratory-prepared protein–carbohydrate blends (protein content 10–80 wt%; carbohydrate components: lactose, sucrose, maltodextrin DE 6 and DE 18) was characterised in parallel using a Hosokawa powder rheometer (avalanche energy and time indices) and a rotational powder flow tester (basic flowability energy, compressibility, permeability). Samples were conditioned at 11%, 33% and 53% relative humidity before testing. The two methods produced concordant rankings at 11% and 33% RH (Spearman ρ > 0.88) but diverged significantly at 53% RH for blends with high lactose content, where crystallisation artefacts affected shear cell measurements but not the dynamic avalanche test. Compressibility index increased from below 12% at 11% RH to above 35% for six blends at 53% RH. The avalanche method was more repeatable (coefficient of variation below 4% across all samples) but less sensitive to differences among freely flowing powders. Practical guidance for method selection depending on humidity condition and blend composition is provided.

title: Anti-caking efficacy of silicon dioxide and tricalcium phosphate in a whey protein isolate–trehalose blend at elevated water activity
abstract: The ability of silicon dioxide (E 551, fumed, specific surface area 200 m²/g) and tricalcium phosphate (E 341iii) to suppress caking in a whey protein isolate–trehalose blend (60:40 w/w) was evaluated at dosages of 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 wt% following storage at 65% RH and 25 °C for 21 days. Caking degree, flowability energy and cohesion index were measured at 0, 7, 14 and 21 days. At 1.0 wt% silicon dioxide, caking degree after 21 days was reduced from 78% (control) to 31%, and basic flowability energy remained measurable throughout the study. Tricalcium phosphate at the same dosage reduced caking to 51%. At 2.0 wt%, both agents performed similarly (caking degree 26–29%). Surface energy analysis by iGC showed that silicon dioxide adhesion energy toward the blend surface was 1.8-fold higher than that of tricalcium phosphate, consistent with the observed efficacy difference. An additive model combining dosage and surface adhesion energy predicted caking degree with a mean absolute error of 4.3 percentage points.

title: Particle size distribution changes in blended pea protein–maltodextrin powders during humid storage and their relationship to flowability
abstract: Spray-dried pea protein isolate–maltodextrin DE 12 blends at three protein-to-carbohydrate ratios (30:70, 50:50, 70:30) were stored at 33% and 53% RH for up to 21 days. Particle size distributions were measured by laser diffraction (wet dispersion, refractive index 1.46) at days 0, 7 and 21, and volume mean diameter D[4,3] and span were extracted. At 53% RH, the 70:30 blend showed a bimodal distribution by day 7 with a secondary peak centred at 310 µm, indicating aggregate formation; the D[4,3] increased from 82 µm to 198 µm by day 21. Flowability energy (FE) measured in the powder flow tester increased from 148 mJ to over 600 mJ in the same sample, and the correlation between D[4,3] and FE across all samples and time points was strong (Pearson r = 0.87, p < 0.001). At 33% RH, size distributions were stable for all three blends. FESEM images confirmed that aggregate growth was driven by liquid-bridge formation at particle contact points at the higher humidity.

title: Sorption isotherm modelling for plant-based protein–carbohydrate powder blends: evaluation of four two-parameter models
abstract: Equilibrium moisture content was measured for binary blends of pea protein isolate, rice protein concentrate and faba bean flour with maltodextrin DE 6 across seven water activity levels (0.11–0.85) at 20 °C and 30 °C using a dynamic vapour sorption analyser. The Guggenheim–Anderson–de Boer (GAB), BET, Henderson and Oswin models were fitted to each isotherm by nonlinear least squares. GAB provided the best overall fit with mean relative percent deviation below 7% across all samples; BET was adequate only below aw 0.65. Isosteric heats of sorption, calculated from the Clausius–Clapeyron equation using the 20 °C and 30 °C datasets, ranged from 44 to 61 kJ/mol at monolayer moisture content and decreased monotonically toward the bulk water condensation enthalpy above aw 0.7. Faba bean blends showed consistently higher monolayer moisture values (5.8–7.1 g/100 g dm) than pea or rice blends at equivalent maltodextrin content, attributed to their higher lysine and arginine content providing additional polar sorption sites.
venue: Food Biophysics and Powder Engineering

title: Effect of pre-crystallisation of lactose on the caking resistance of whey–lactose powder at elevated humidity
abstract: Spray-dried whey–lactose powder (72:28 w/w) was subjected to controlled pre-crystallisation by exposure to 68% RH at 25 °C for 1, 2 and 4 hours before final drying to 3.0 g/100 g moisture content. X-ray powder diffraction and differential scanning calorimetry confirmed that lactose crystallinity increased from below 3% (untreated) to 41%, 67% and 89% respectively. All powders were then stored at 53% and 65% RH for 14 days and evaluated for caking degree, flowability energy and compressibility. At 65% RH, the 4-hour pre-crystallised powder retained a caking degree of 19% after 14 days versus 82% for untreated material. Flowability energy remained above 200 mJ only for the 4-hour pre-crystallised sample at 65% RH, indicating that the crystalline lactose matrix resisted liquid-bridge formation. Particle morphology characterised by SEM showed that crystalline protrusions on the particle surface impeded close contact between particles. The study provides quantitative targets for pre-crystallisation extent required to achieve stable powder flow under humid warehouse conditions.

title: Flowability and compressibility of mixed legume–cereal protein powders intended for sports nutrition applications
abstract: Six binary and ternary blends of pea protein isolate, hemp protein concentrate and oat protein flour (in total protein content range 50–80 wt%) were characterised for flow properties relevant to industrial handling and canister filling. Bulk and tapped densities, Carr index, Hausner ratio, angle of repose and shear cell parameters (unconfined yield strength, major principal stress, effective angle of internal friction) were measured at 11%, 33% and 53% RH. All blends were cohesive at 53% RH (flow factor ff < 4) and either easy-flowing or cohesive at 33% RH depending on composition. At 11% RH, the oat-dominant ternary blend had the lowest compressibility (Carr index 14%) and the highest permeability, attributed to its fibrous particle morphology. Powder segregation tendency was assessed by a rotating drum method and found to be significant only for blends with particle size span above 2.1. A simple scoring matrix for blend suitability in auger-fill operations is proposed based on the measured parameters.

title: Antioxidant activity of melanoidin fractions isolated from extruded corn-wheat blend snacks
abstract: Melanoidins were isolated from extruded snacks produced from 70:30 corn–wheat blends at 160 and 180 °C by sequential dialysis and ultrafiltration, yielding high-molecular-weight (HMW, >10 kDa) and low-molecular-weight (LMW, 1–10 kDa) fractions. Antioxidant capacity was assessed by DPPH radical scavenging, FRAP and ABTS assays. HMW fractions consistently showed higher DPPH inhibition (IC₅₀ 3.8–5.1 mg/mL) compared with LMW fractions (IC₅₀ 8.2–11.4 mg/mL). FRAP values for HMW fractions ranged from 1.8 to 2.6 mmol Fe²⁺ equivalent per gram of dry melanoidin. Total nitrogen content, measured by Dumas combustion, was positively correlated with antioxidant capacity (r = 0.84). Fluorescence spectroscopy confirmed characteristic melanoidin emission at 440 nm. These findings indicate that the HMW melanoidin pool formed during extrusion cooking contributes meaningfully to the overall antioxidant capacity of the finished snack product.

title: Exopolysaccharide production by heterofermentative lactobacilli in wheat sourdough: quantification and effect on crumb structure
abstract: Four heterofermentative Lactobacillus strains, including Limosilactobacillus fermentum NS-SD-03 and Levilactobacillus brevis NS-SD-11 isolated from spontaneous wheat sourdoughs from Bačka, were compared for EPS accumulation during a two-stage sourdough process (Type I, 20 h, 30 °C). EPS was extracted from dough using aqueous ethanol precipitation and quantified by the phenol–sulphuric acid assay. Yields ranged from 0.18 to 0.62 g per 100 g flour. Bread samples baked from EPS-enriched sourdoughs exhibited specific volume increases of 4–9% compared to controls as measured by rapeseed displacement. Crumb firmness at day 1 and day 5 post-baking was assessed by texture analyser (TPA, 40% compression). Firmness at day 5 was 18–31% lower in EPS-producing sourdough breads. Water activity did not differ significantly between treatments. These results suggest EPS contributes to both initial softness and retardation of staling in wheat sourdough bread.

title: Noise Exposure Levels in Small Metalworking Workshops in Vojvodina: A Baseline Survey
abstract: This study presents octave-band noise measurements conducted in 14 small metalworking workshops in the Vojvodina region of Serbia, employing a Brüel & Kjær Type 2250 analyser and personal dosimeters worn over full eight-hour shifts. A total of 61 worker-shift measurements were collected across operations including turning, milling, grinding, and sheet metal cutting. Daily personal noise exposure levels (LEX,8h) ranged from 79 dB(A) to 96 dB(A), with grinding and sheet metal cutting consistently exceeding the 85 dB(A) upper action value set by EU Directive 2003/10/EC. Octave-band spectra showed dominant energy in the 1–4 kHz range for grinding operations. The paper establishes a regional baseline and identifies the process types requiring priority engineering controls. Measurement uncertainty was estimated following ISO 9612:2009, with combined standard uncertainty values between 1.1 and 2.3 dB(A). Recommendations for initial engineering control sequencing are discussed in the context of resource constraints typical of SMEs.

title: Comparison of Point Measurement and Personal Dosimetry Methods for Estimating LEX,8h in Lathe Operations
abstract: The study compares two measurement strategies prescribed in ISO 9612:2009 — task-based point measurements and full-shift personal dosimetry — for estimating daily noise exposure of lathe operators in five Vojvodina metalworking enterprises. Thirty paired measurement sessions were conducted over six months. Point-measurement estimates exceeded dosimeter readings by a mean of 1.4 dB(A) with a standard deviation of 0.9 dB(A), a difference attributable largely to operator movement away from the noise source during non-cutting intervals. The agreement was closer for operators assigned to dedicated CNC lathes with limited mobility. Bland-Altman analysis confirmed acceptable limits of agreement for compliance purposes in most task configurations. The findings suggest that point-measurement strategies may conservatively overestimate exposure in tasks with intermittent machine contact, and practical guidance is offered on selecting the most appropriate strategy based on task structure and available instrumentation in SME contexts.

title: Octave-Band Spectral Characterisation of Angle Grinder Noise and Its Relation to High-Frequency Hearing Threshold Shifts in Exposed Workers
abstract: Angle grinders are among the highest noise-generating hand tools in metalworking, yet spectral characterisation studies in real workshop environments remain sparse. This paper reports octave-band measurements taken at the operator ear position during five standard grinding tasks performed on mild steel, stainless steel, and cast iron in a controlled workshop at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Sound pressure levels at 2 kHz and 4 kHz exceeded 95 dB by 3–8 dB relative to A-weighted totals. Audiometric data from 38 workers with five or more years of regular angle grinder use were compared against an unexposed reference group of 22 workers from the same enterprises. The exposed group showed statistically significant threshold shifts at 4 kHz (mean 12.3 dB HL, p < 0.01) and 6 kHz (mean 9.7 dB HL, p < 0.05) relative to the reference group after controlling for age. The results support targeted audiometric monitoring at high frequencies and argue for prioritising engineering controls at the grinder–workpiece interface.

title: Engineering Noise Control Options for Sheet Metal Stamping Presses in SMEs: A Cost-Ranked Assessment
abstract: Stamping presses represent a persistent noise problem in small metal-parts manufacturers, with A-weighted levels at operator positions often exceeding 94 dB(A). This paper documents a structured engineering control assessment carried out at four enterprises in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin operating mechanical eccentric presses with nominal forces between 100 and 400 kN. For each press, candidate controls were identified — including damped die sets, press enclosures, vibration isolation mounts, and acoustic screens — and their expected insertion loss was estimated from published third-party data and verified by before/after measurements at two sites where controls were implemented during the study period. Controls were ranked by noise reduction achieved per euro invested, using quotations obtained from regional suppliers. Damped die sets provided the best cost-effectiveness ratio (0.8–1.9 dB(A) per 100 EUR) when combined with partial enclosures. Full enclosures achieved the largest absolute reduction (up to 11 dB(A)) but were cost-effective only for presses running single-product campaigns exceeding eight hours per day.

title: Design and Pilot Testing of a Simplified Audiometric Surveillance Protocol for Metalworking SMEs Without In-House Occupational Health Staff
abstract: Small and medium-sized metalworking enterprises in Serbia frequently lack direct access to occupational physicians, creating practical barriers to conducting periodic audiometric surveillance as required under national Regulation on Occupational Noise (Official Gazette RS 50/2010) and the underlying EU Directive. This paper describes the design and twelve-month pilot testing of a simplified surveillance protocol developed in collaboration with three Novi Sad SMEs and a contracted occupational health clinic. The protocol specifies screening audiometry intervals based on measured LEX,8h bands, defines referral criteria for threshold shift confirmation, and assigns record-keeping responsibilities to the employer's safety coordinator. In the pilot, 74 workers received initial and twelve-month follow-up audiograms. Protocol adherence was 89% at follow-up. Eleven workers (14.9%) met referral criteria for confirmatory audiometry; of these, three received modified job assignments. Protocol documentation requirements were calibrated to be completable in under two hours per worker per year by non-specialist staff.

title: Noise Mapping of a Medium-Sized Metalworking Facility Using a Grid-Based Measurement Approach: Validation Against Worker Dosimetry
abstract: Spatial noise maps of industrial facilities are used to identify high-exposure zones and support engineering control planning, but their accuracy relative to personal dosimetry is rarely validated in practice. This paper reports a grid-based noise mapping exercise conducted in a 2 400 m² metalworking facility producing agricultural machinery components near Novi Sad. Measurements were taken at 104 grid nodes on a 4 × 4 m grid during production, from which contour maps were constructed using kriging interpolation in MATLAB. Predicted LEX,8h values for 17 job positions were compared with dosimeter measurements from the same workers over the same production week. Mean absolute deviation between map predictions and dosimetry was 1.7 dB(A). Deviations exceeded 3 dB(A) for four mobile workers whose movement patterns were not adequately captured by a static grid. The paper proposes a supplementary mobile-worker correction procedure and discusses the minimum grid resolution needed to achieve 2 dB(A) accuracy for fixed-station operators.

title: Hearing Conservation Programme Compliance in Vojvodina Metalworking SMEs: A Questionnaire-Based Assessment
abstract: EU Directive 2003/10/EC and its Serbian transposition impose specific obligations on employers once noise exposure exceeds action values, including information provision, hearing protection supply, audiometric surveillance, and training. This paper reports findings from a structured questionnaire administered to safety officers and employers at 41 metalworking SMEs in Vojvodina during 2020–2021. Respondents self-reported compliance across 14 directive obligations. Hearing protection supply was reported as compliant by 88% of enterprises; audiometric surveillance at the prescribed intervals was reported by only 31%. Noise risk assessment documentation was present in 73% of enterprises but had been updated within three years in only 44% of those. Multivariate logistic regression showed that enterprises with a dedicated safety coordinator and more than 25 employees were significantly more likely to comply with audiometric surveillance requirements (OR 4.2, 95% CI 1.6–11.1). The results identify surveillance continuity as the weakest compliance link and inform targeted intervention design.

title: Combined Noise and Vibration Exposure Among Hand-Tool Operators in Metalworking: Concurrent Assessment and Interaction Effects on Self-Reported Symptoms
abstract: Hand-arm vibration and noise frequently co-occur in metalworking hand-tool tasks, yet occupational exposure assessments typically address each hazard independently. This paper reports concurrent measurements of noise exposure (ISO 9612:2009) and hand-arm vibration (ISO 5349-1:2001) for four common hand-tool tasks — angle grinding, chiselling, filing with a pneumatic file, and riveting — conducted across six SMEs in Novi Sad and Subotica. For 52 exposed workers, self-reported symptom questionnaires covering hearing difficulty, tinnitus, tingling, and grip weakness were completed. Prevalence of tinnitus was 46% in workers with both LEX,8h > 85 dB(A) and A(8) > 2.5 m/s², compared with 22% in those with only elevated noise exposure and 19% in those with only elevated vibration. The association between combined high exposure and tinnitus remained significant after adjusting for age and exposure duration (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.2–6.6). Limitations related to cross-sectional design and self-report bias are discussed.

title: Accuracy of Low-Cost Sound Level Meter Applications for Occupational Noise Screening in Metalworking Workshops
abstract: The proliferation of smartphone-based sound level meter applications raises questions about their suitability for regulatory noise screening in SMEs where access to calibrated Class 1 instrumentation is limited. This study compared seven Android and iOS applications against a Class 1 Brüel & Kjær Type 2250 analyser under controlled conditions using pink noise, a 1 kHz pure tone, and pre-recorded metalworking noise signals played through a loudspeaker in a semi-anechoic chamber, and subsequently in three live metalworking workshops. At levels between 80 and 95 dB(A), mean deviations of applications from the reference ranged from −0.4 to +6.8 dB(A). Two applications equipped with MEMS microphone calibration routines achieved deviations within ±2 dB(A) across all test conditions; the remaining five showed larger deviations above 90 dB(A). Workshop tests broadly confirmed laboratory rankings. The paper proposes a simple screening criterion: applications are appropriate for identifying locations likely to require full Class 1 assessment, but not for compliance determination.

title: Effectiveness of Acoustic Enclosures Retrofitted to Existing CNC Machining Centres: Measurements at Four SMEs
abstract: CNC machining centres are increasingly common in Vojvodina metalworking SMEs but are rarely purchased with full acoustic enclosures due to cost. This paper reports the results of partial and full acoustic enclosure retrofits applied to eight CNC machining centres at four enterprises over a 14-month period. Insertion loss was measured before and after installation using third-octave band analysis at operator station and room-average positions. Full enclosures with door interlocks achieved mean insertion losses of 9.3–13.1 dB(A) at the operator position; partial enclosures covering three sides and the top achieved 4.2–6.8 dB(A). Post-retrofit LEX,8h values fell below the 85 dB(A) upper action value at six of eight machines. Production time losses attributable to enclosure door opening cycles averaged 2.1 minutes per hour, a figure used in post-hoc cost-benefit calculations. All retrofits were designed in-house using locally sourced mineral-wool-faced panels and were costed between 1 800 and 6 400 EUR per machine.

title: Audiometric Data Trends Over Ten Years in a Longitudinal Cohort of Metalworking Workers in Vojvodina
abstract: Long-term audiometric surveillance data from occupational cohorts in the Western Balkans are rarely published systematically. This paper presents ten-year longitudinal audiometric records for a cohort of 89 metalworking workers enrolled between 2013 and 2014 at enterprises participating in the simplified surveillance protocol described in earlier work by the same group. Annual pure-tone audiograms at 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 kHz were collected; workers with less than six valid annual records were excluded, leaving 67 in the analysis. Mean threshold deterioration over ten years at 4 kHz was 7.4 dB HL (SD 4.1) in workers consistently exposed above 85 dB(A), compared with 2.9 dB HL (SD 2.8) in those who received effective noise control or job reassignment before year three. Age-corrected progression rates derived from ISO 1999:2013 slightly underestimated observed deterioration in the highest-exposure subgroup. The dataset is made available as a supplementary file to support regional audiometric norm development.

title: Effect of Workstation Height Adjustment on Upper Trapezius Muscle Activity During Electronic Component Inspection
abstract: Sustained low-level muscle activity in the upper trapezius is associated with work-related neck and shoulder disorders in inspection workers. This controlled laboratory study examined the effect of three workstation heights (elbow height minus 10 cm, elbow height, elbow height plus 10 cm) on normalised upper trapezius EMG amplitude in 16 female and 12 male participants performing a simulated electronic component inspection task at a rate of 25 components per minute. Height was varied using an electrically adjustable table; task duration per condition was 20 minutes with 10-minute rest intervals. Normalised EMG (as percentage of maximum voluntary contraction) was lowest at elbow height for both sexes, with mean values of 6.2% MVC for women and 5.4% MVC for men. The minus-10 cm condition produced the highest trapezius activity (9.8% and 8.1% MVC respectively), consistent with increased shoulder abduction demands. A carryover effect between conditions was observed and controlled via a Latin-square counterbalanced design. Results provide quantitative support for existing ergonomic guidelines on inspection workstation sizing and indicate that individual height adjustment reduces exposure by approximately 35% compared to a fixed low surface.

title: Stochastic task time models in assembly line balancing: a scenario-based formulation
abstract: Task processing times in real assembly environments are subject to operator variability, material inconsistency, and tool wear. This paper proposes a scenario-based two-stage stochastic programming model for the ALBP-1 where task durations follow empirically fitted distributions. Scenarios are generated using Latin hypercube sampling calibrated against time-study data collected over eight weeks in a small-series pneumatic valve assembly facility. The expected number of workstations is minimised in the first stage; recourse costs for cycle time violations are penalised in the second stage. A sample average approximation scheme with 200 scenarios is solved via CPLEX 12.5. On a 35-task, 5-model instance the stochastic model yields solutions with 9% fewer cycle time violations in out-of-sample validation compared to a deterministic baseline using mean task times. Sensitivity analysis shows that the recourse penalty coefficient has the strongest influence on first-stage station assignments.
