title: Comparison of Degree-Day and Regression-Based Heating Adjustments in Commercial Building EPCs
abstract: Heating degree-day (HDD) adjustments are widely used in simplified IPMVP Option C applications for commercial buildings, but their accuracy relative to regression-based adjustments has not been systematically evaluated in continental climates. This study compares HDD adjustment, simple linear regression on outdoor temperature, and multiple regression on temperature and occupancy for a sample of 20 commercial buildings in Novi Sad over five years. Adjusted savings estimates using the three methods diverge by up to 17% in years with atypical temperature distributions. Regression on temperature alone outperforms HDD adjustment in 16 of 20 buildings by root mean square prediction error criteria. Adding occupancy as a second variable provides additional improvement only in buildings with variable occupancy schedules. The paper recommends phasing out standalone HDD adjustments in favour of regression approaches even for simpler commercial applications.

title: Cost Estimation Accuracy and Its Consequences for Project Financial Performance in Serbian ETO Manufacturers
abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between pre-order cost estimation accuracy and project-level financial outcomes in a sample of 18 Serbian engineer-to-order manufacturers. Data were collected through a structured survey and supplemented with archival project cost data where companies permitted access. Estimation error was defined as the percentage deviation of final actual cost from the estimate used for pricing. The sample median absolute estimation error was 18.4%, with a directional bias towards underestimation in 61% of projects. A correlation analysis shows a statistically significant negative association between estimation error magnitude and project gross margin. Qualitative interviews with project managers at six companies identified four recurring causes of systematic underestimation: optimistic scope assumptions, inadequate treatment of rework allowances, neglect of engineering change order costs, and lump-sum subcontract pricing risk. The paper proposes a simple risk-loading framework based on historical error distributions to calibrate contingency allowances at bid stage.

title: Estimating TRL Transition Probabilities from Historical Project Data: A Markov Chain Model
abstract: This paper constructs a discrete-time Markov chain model of TRL progression for manufacturing R&D projects, calibrated on a dataset of 148 projects funded across three consecutive national innovation calls in Serbia between 2009 and 2015. Projects were assessed at funding entry and at 12-month intervals; TRL was recorded by an independent assessor at each observation point. Estimated transition matrices differ by sector: metal-working projects show higher probabilities of advancing two TRL levels per period (mean 0.22) than electronic-systems projects (mean 0.14), but also higher probabilities of stagnation at TRL 4 (0.31 vs. 0.19). Absorbing states at TRL 8 and TRL 9 are reached by 41 % of metal-working projects within 24 months and by 29 % of electronic-systems projects within 36 months. The model is used to derive expected time-to-market estimates and to simulate the portfolio-level TRL distribution under different funding allocation strategies. Limitations arising from non-stationarity of transition probabilities across programme cycles are discussed.

title: OEE trend decomposition using seasonal-trend decomposition via LOESS: detecting gradual performance drift on sugar-beet processing lines
abstract: Gradual performance drift on continuous-process equipment is difficult to detect using conventional statistical process control charts calibrated to detect step-change shifts. This paper applies seasonal-trend decomposition via LOESS (STL) to 30 months of shift-level OEE time series from two sugar-beet slicing and diffusion lines at a refinery in Vojvodina, separating campaign-seasonal variation, slow trend, and residual noise components. Trend components revealed a monotonic decline in performance rate of approximately 0.4 percentage points per month on one line, attributable to progressive wear on diffusion drum scrapers—a finding invisible in standard monthly OEE reports. Residual components were used to calibrate a CUSUM chart for early detection of acute failure events. The approach correctly identified the onset of a bearing degradation event on the diffusion drum 11 shifts before the event triggered an unplanned stoppage in the validation period. The paper provides R code for the full analysis pipeline as supplementary material.
venue: Journal of Production Engineering

title: Objectively Measured Sitting Time and Fasting Triglycerides in Administrative Employees: A Cross-Sectional Study in Novi Sad
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined associations between accelerometry-derived sedentary time and fasting triglyceride concentrations in 118 administrative employees (mean age 41.3 ± 8.7 years; 63% women) recruited from four municipal institutions in Novi Sad. Participants wore a hip-fixed ActiGraph-equivalent triaxial accelerometer for seven consecutive days during waking hours. Valid wear time criteria required ≥10 hours per day on ≥4 days. Sedentary time was extracted using a 100 counts-per-minute cut-point. Fasting venous blood samples were collected on a single morning visit. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, each additional hour of daily sedentary time was associated with a 4.1% higher triglyceride concentration (95% CI: 1.2–7.1%). Participants in the highest tertile of sitting time (>9.4 h/day) showed mean triglycerides 0.38 mmol/L above the lowest tertile. No significant interaction by sex was detected. These findings suggest that total accumulated sitting, independent of physical activity level, is meaningfully associated with one established cardiometabolic risk marker in white-collar populations.

title: Feasibility of Using Wrist-Worn Accelerometers for Sedentary Behaviour Classification in Occupational Settings: Agreement with Hip Placement
abstract: Wrist placement of accelerometers improves compliance in free-living monitoring but may produce different sedentary time estimates compared to the reference hip placement. This methodological study assessed agreement between simultaneously worn wrist and hip accelerometers in 47 office workers over three consecutive weekdays. Intraclass correlation coefficients, Bland–Altman plots, and mean absolute percentage error were computed for total sedentary time and bout-based metrics. Total sedentary time showed moderate-to-good agreement (ICC = 0.74; 95% CI: 0.61–0.84), with the wrist device producing on average 22.3 minutes more sedentary time per day than the hip device. Agreement for prolonged bout duration (≥30 min) was weaker (ICC = 0.58). These discrepancies were larger among participants with more frequent hand movements at work, assessed via self-report job task inventory. Findings indicate that placement-specific calibration or machine-learning classifiers trained on occupational contexts may be necessary before wrist accelerometry can replace hip accelerometry in white-collar sedentary behaviour research.

title: Agreement between IMU-derived and force-plate-derived vertical loading rate estimates during football cutting manoeuvres: a concurrent validity study
abstract: Vertical loading rate (VLR) during change-of-direction tasks is linked to bone stress and soft-tissue injury risk, but portable alternatives to force plates are needed for field deployment. Thirty healthy male footballers performed standardised 45° and 90° cuts over an instrumented force plate while wearing a shank-mounted IMU. VLR was estimated from the IMU using a published regression equation and compared with force plate values across 480 cutting trials. Mean bias was −0.12 body weights per second (95% limits of agreement: −1.84 to 1.60 BW/s). The proportion of trials classified correctly into high versus low VLR tertiles by the IMU method was 71%. Bias was heteroscedastic, increasing at higher VLR values, which limits the method's precision precisely when risk-identification is most important. The study quantifies the current accuracy ceiling of single-sensor IMU estimation of VLR and identifies the conditions under which practitioner interpretations should be made cautiously.

title: Kinematic description of the barbell trajectory in the clean across three competitive weight categories
abstract: Barbell displacement trajectories during the clean were compared across three competitive weight categories (≤69 kg, 77 kg, ≥85 kg) using a six-camera Qualisys motion capture system operating at 200 Hz. Forty-two male lifters performed three maximal-effort cleans; barbell markers were used to reconstruct mediolateral, anterior–posterior, and vertical displacement throughout the lift. Mediolateral barbell deviation during the pull under was significantly greater in the ≥85 kg category (mean peak deviation 3.8 ± 1.1 cm) compared to ≤69 kg (2.4 ± 0.8 cm, p = 0.003). Vertical barbell velocity at the end of the second pull correlated negatively with mediolateral deviation (r = −0.48, p = 0.001), suggesting that lateral drift is associated with suboptimal vertical momentum. Weight-category-specific trajectory norms are proposed as reference benchmarks for coaching feedback.

title: Antioxidant enzyme activity and lipid peroxidation in the digestive gland of Unio pictorum following acute copper exposure
abstract: Laboratory-exposed specimens of Unio pictorum were subjected to copper concentrations of 10, 50, and 200 µg/L for 96 hours under controlled conditions (18 °C, pH 7.6). Activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) were measured spectrophotometrically in digestive gland homogenates, alongside malondialdehyde (MDA) levels as an index of lipid peroxidation. SOD activity increased significantly at 50 and 200 µg/L (p < 0.01), while CAT was elevated only at the highest concentration. GPx showed a biphasic pattern, rising at 50 µg/L and declining at 200 µg/L, suggesting saturation of the glutathione-dependent defence. MDA concentrations were dose-dependent and reached 3.8-fold above control values at 200 µg/L. The results indicate oxidative damage at copper concentrations routinely detected in moderately polluted Danubian tributaries and support the utility of these endpoints in environmental risk assessment.

title: Metallothionein induction in Dreissena polymorpha as a biomarker of cadmium exposure in the Tisa River
abstract: Field-collected specimens of Dreissena polymorpha from six sites along the Tisa River (Serbia) and one reference site were analysed for metallothionein (MT) protein concentrations using a cadmium saturation assay, alongside tissue cadmium burdens determined by flame atomic absorption spectrometry (FAAS). MT levels ranged from 0.31 µg/g wet weight at the reference site to 2.74 µg/g at the most contaminated downstream location near an agricultural drainage channel. A significant positive linear relationship was found between tissue cadmium and MT concentration (r² = 0.81, p < 0.001, n = 72). Condition index and gonadal stage were recorded to account for physiological variability. Seasonal sampling (spring and autumn) revealed higher MT induction in spring, coinciding with elevated river cadmium loads following snowmelt. The data suggest that D. polymorpha MT is a sensitive and interpretable indicator for low-level cadmium contamination in large lowland rivers.

title: Combined copper and cadmium exposure in Unio tumidus: interactive effects on glutathione status and MT expression
abstract: Binary mixture experiments were conducted to evaluate whether copper and cadmium act additively, synergistically, or antagonistically on glutathione-related defences and metallothionein expression in Unio tumidus. Mussels were exposed for 14 days to nominal concentrations of 20 µg/L Cu, 5 µg/L Cd, and their combination at the same concentrations, with a solvent control. Total glutathione (GSH+GSSG), glutathione reductase activity, and MT mRNA levels measured by quantitative RT-PCR were recorded in gill and digestive gland tissue. In combined exposures, gill GSH depletion (−47%) exceeded the sum of individual treatments (−21% and −18%, respectively), indicating synergism in oxidative glutathione consumption. MT mRNA induction showed a predominantly additive pattern in the digestive gland. These findings complicate the interpretation of MT as a single-metal biomarker in rivers where mixed contamination is common.

title: Sublethal cadmium effects on lysosomal membrane stability and neutral red retention in haemocytes of Unio pictorum
abstract: Haemocytes were isolated from Unio pictorum specimens exposed for 7 days to cadmium at 2, 10, and 40 µg/L. Lysosomal membrane stability was evaluated by the neutral red retention (NRR) assay, a cytological endpoint recommended in OSPAR biological effects guidelines. NRR time decreased from a control mean of 68 min to 29 min at 40 µg/L (p < 0.001). Histological sections of digestive gland tubules stained with Nile Blue A showed concentration-dependent lipofuscin accumulation and dilatation of lysosomal compartments. Metal accumulation in soft tissue was confirmed by graphite furnace AAS: tissue cadmium reached 18.3 µg/g dry weight at the highest exposure. The NRR endpoint showed a lower effect concentration (LOEC = 2 µg/L) than classical biochemical biomarkers measured in the same experiment, supporting its sensitivity for detecting early-stage cadmium stress in field bivalve populations.

title: Spatial variation in oxidative stress biomarkers of Dreissena polymorpha across a pollution gradient on the Sava River
abstract: A biomonitoring survey was conducted at nine sites along a 340 km stretch of the Sava River between Šabac and its confluence with the Danube, encompassing an urban-industrial gradient. Dreissena polymorpha was collected in autumn and spring from two consecutive years. A battery of eight biomarkers was measured: SOD, CAT, GPx, glutathione S-transferase (GST), total reduced glutathione, MDA, protein carbonyl content, and MT. Water and sediment metal concentrations (Cu, Cd, Zn, Pb, Ni) were measured by ICP-MS. Integrated biomarker response index version 2 (IBRv2) was calculated to rank site contamination. IBRv2 correlated with dissolved copper (r = 0.74) more strongly than with cadmium (r = 0.52), while protein carbonyls were most strongly associated with Pb. Upstream reference sites showed significantly lower IBRv2 scores in both seasons. The survey provides a multi-biomarker baseline for regulatory monitoring of the Serbian section of the Sava.

title: Biomarker responses in freshwater mussels as tools for Danubian water quality assessment: a methodological overview
abstract: This book chapter reviews the application of biochemical biomarkers in Unio and Dreissena species for monitoring trace metal pollution in the Danube basin, synthesising published data from the period 1998–2016. Methodological considerations for enzyme extraction, MT quantification, and lipid peroxidation assays are discussed, with emphasis on inter-laboratory comparability and the influence of biological variables (season, sex, age class, reproductive stage) on baseline biomarker levels. Recommendations are made for standardised sampling protocols, tissue preparation, and quality control measures. The chapter also addresses the integration of biomarker data with chemical analysis and ecological assessment frameworks under the EU Water Framework Directive. Case studies from the Tisa, Sava, and Morava rivers are presented. Specific attention is paid to the statistical approaches appropriate for multi-site, multi-season data sets with moderate sample sizes.

title: Copper accumulation and oxidative response kinetics in Unio pictorum: a time-course study at environmentally relevant concentrations
abstract: Unio pictorum were exposed to 15 µg/L Cu (close to the EU EQS annual average for freshwater) over 28 days, with sampling at days 1, 3, 7, 14, and 28. Copper content in gill, digestive gland, and mantle was quantified by ICP-OES at each time point, alongside MDA, protein carbonyls, SOD, and CAT activity. Gill copper reached plateau at day 7 (42.8 µg/g dry weight), whereas digestive gland copper continued to accumulate to day 28 (61.3 µg/g dry weight). SOD activity was significantly elevated from day 3 onwards in both tissues. MDA showed a delayed peak at day 14 in the digestive gland, declining slightly by day 28, possibly reflecting adaptive upregulation of CAT. A depuration phase of 14 days reduced tissue copper by 64% in gill but only 38% in digestive gland, indicating differential detoxification kinetics. These time-resolved data are relevant for designing passive biomonitoring deployments.

title: Seasonal baseline variability of metallothionein and antioxidant enzymes in wild Unio crassus from an unpolluted Pannonian stream
abstract: Accurate interpretation of field biomarker data requires knowledge of natural physiological variation. Unio crassus was sampled monthly for 12 months from a reference site on the Zlatica stream (Vojvodina, Serbia), where dissolved copper and cadmium were consistently below 2 µg/L and 0.1 µg/L, respectively. MT, SOD, CAT, GPx, and MDA were quantified in digestive gland and gills. MT showed a clear seasonal pattern with a minimum in winter (0.18 µg/g ww) and a peak in early June (0.61 µg/g ww), correlating with gonadic activity assessed by histology. SOD activity was highest in early spring and lowest in summer. Multiple regression analysis indicated that condition index, reproductive stage, and water temperature together explained 67% of MT variance. These reference data serve as season-adjusted control values for field biomonitoring studies in the Pannonian lowland region.

title: Characterisation of a copper-inducible metallothionein isoform in Dreissena polymorpha gill tissue by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis and LC-MS/MS
abstract: Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis followed by LC-MS/MS was used to characterise metallothionein isoforms in Dreissena polymorpha gill protein extracts from laboratory specimens exposed to 0, 20, and 80 µg/L Cu for 7 days. Three distinct spots with the expected low molecular weight (6–8 kDa) and acidic pI (4.2–4.8) were resolved. Spot intensity of one isoform, tentatively designated DpMT-2, increased 4.3-fold at 80 µg/L relative to control. Tryptic peptides matched a partial sequence in the Dreissena transcriptome database with 94% coverage. The cysteine content of the deduced protein (20 Cys in 71 amino acids) is consistent with metal-binding capacity. DpMT-2 induction was also confirmed by western blot using a polyclonal antibody raised against purified U. tumidus MT. The data provide protein-level evidence for a copper-responsive MT isoform that may be targeted in future immunochemical field assays.

title: Active versus passive biomonitoring with transplanted Dreissena polymorpha cages: copper and cadmium uptake and biomarker responses in three Danubian tributaries
abstract: Dreissena polymorpha from a reference population were enclosed in standardised mesh cages and transplanted for 21 days at nine field stations on the Tisa, Tamiš, and Begej rivers (Serbia), alongside resident mussel populations where present. Metal accumulation, MT, MDA, and GST were measured in transplanted and resident animals at each site. Transplanted mussels showed faster metal uptake rates and steeper biomarker gradients between clean and impacted sites than resident populations, which displayed signs of physiological adaptation. GST activity in transplanted animals discriminated low-exposure from high-exposure sites with greater statistical power (one-way ANOVA, p < 0.001) than the same endpoint in residents. Dissolved metal concentrations monitored by DGT passive samplers ran parallel to cage exposure estimates. The caging approach provided reproducible, spatially resolved biomarker data suitable for ranking tributary contamination under the WFD chemical status framework.

title: Cadmium-induced changes in mitochondrial membrane potential and cytochrome c release in digestive gland cells of Unio tumidus
abstract: Primary cell cultures derived from digestive gland of Unio tumidus were established and exposed to cadmium chloride at 1, 5, and 25 µM for 24 and 48 hours. Mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) was assessed using the fluorescent probe JC-1 on a microplate reader, and cytochrome c release to cytosol was quantified by ELISA. At 5 µM Cd, ΔΨm decreased by 31% after 24 h (p < 0.01), and cytochrome c in the cytosolic fraction increased 2.6-fold. At 25 µM, a further decline in ΔΨm and 6.8-fold cytochrome c release were observed, accompanied by a 5.2-fold elevation of cellular MDA, suggesting concurrent lipid peroxidation. Co-treatment with 1 mM N-acetylcysteine partially reversed ΔΨm loss, implicating oxidative stress as a mediator of cadmium-induced mitochondrial dysfunction. These in vitro findings complement whole-organism biomarker data and indicate mechanistic pathways for cadmium toxicity in bivalve digestive cells.

title: Low-dose cadmium and copper co-exposure in Unio pictorum over 60 days: bioaccumulation, histopathology, and biochemical biomarker integration
abstract: A 60-day chronic co-exposure experiment tested the effects of environmentally realistic binary metal mixtures (5 µg/L Cu + 1 µg/L Cd; 10 µg/L Cu + 2 µg/L Cd) on Unio pictorum. Tissue metal loads, histopathological scoring of digestive gland tubules and gills, and a nine-biomarker panel (including SOD, CAT, GPx, GST, total GSH, MT, MDA, protein carbonyls, and neutral red retention) were assessed at days 15, 30, and 60. Principal component analysis of biomarker data separated all treatment groups from controls from day 30 onwards, with the first principal component explaining 44% of variance and loading most strongly on MT and protein carbonyls. Histopathological lesion scores (haemocytic infiltration, tubule atrophy, lysosomal enlargement) increased progressively with exposure duration and metal concentration. Integrated biomarker response scores correlated well with histopathological index values (Spearman r = 0.82). The 60-day low-dose design better reflects real tributary exposure scenarios than acute tests.

title: Metallothionein gene expression patterns across tissues of Dreissena polymorpha under differential copper and cadmium exposure: a quantitative RT-PCR survey
abstract: Tissue-specific MT gene expression was quantified by RT-PCR in gill, digestive gland, mantle, and foot of Dreissena polymorpha exposed to Cu (20 µg/L), Cd (5 µg/L), or both for 7 and 21 days. Three MT isoform transcripts (DpMT-1, DpMT-2, DpMT-3) previously identified in the species were targeted using isoform-specific primers. DpMT-2 showed the highest induction ratio in digestive gland under copper exposure (11.4-fold at day 21), while DpMT-3 responded preferentially to cadmium in gill tissue (8.7-fold at day 7). DpMT-1 expression was relatively stable across treatments and tissues, suggesting a constitutive housekeeping role. Co-exposure resulted in additive transcript accumulation for DpMT-2 but supra-additive responses for DpMT-3 in mantle. These isoform-specific patterns have implications for designing targeted molecular biomarker panels that distinguish Cu- from Cd-dominated contamination in field populations.

title: Biogenic H2S in ion exchange water treatment – operational risks, mechanisms and mitigation: a review
abstract: This chapter provides a structured overview of the processes leading to biogenic hydrogen sulphide formation in cation exchange resins used for water softening and demineralisation. Mechanisms of SRB colonisation, the role of sulphonate functional groups as sulphur sources, electron donor availability, and hydraulic conditions favouring anaerobic microsites are discussed with reference to published literature and the authors' own experimental data from studies carried out between 2010 and 2021. The chapter covers analytical methods for H2S and sulphide detection in resin systems, discusses regulatory contexts relevant to the Western Balkans, and evaluates mitigation strategies including sanitisation chemistry, flow management and pre-treatment for organic carbon removal. Case studies from field installations in Serbia, Hungary and Croatia are summarised. The chapter is intended as a reference for water utilities, equipment manufacturers and regulators.

title: Inorganic carbon balance in pilot-scale continuous saponification: CO2 input, alkali consumption, and precipitate distribution
abstract: A 50 L pilot saponifier operating in continuous mode at a fatty acid feed rate of 2.4 kg h⁻¹ was instrumented with inline pH, conductivity, and CO2 partial pressure sensors. Sodium hydroxide feed concentration was varied between 28 and 38 wt%. Mass balance calculations over 8 h production runs showed that between 0.8 and 1.4 g CO2 per kg soap was incorporated as carbonate under ambient air contact conditions. Precipitate sampling at five points along the process line demonstrated that 60–70% of carbonate formation occurred in the crutcher zone where temperature dropped below 80 °C. Raising NaOH inlet temperature from 60 to 80 °C reduced carbonate incorporation by 22%. The pilot study translates laboratory carbonate kinetics to process-relevant conditions and identifies the crutcher cooling stage as the critical control point for managing inorganic carbon in soap manufacturing.

title: Copper(II) Complexes of Tridentate ONS Hydrazone Ligands: Synthesis, Solution Equilibria, and Redox Properties
abstract: Four tridentate hydrazone ligands bearing oxygen, nitrogen, and sulphur donor atoms were synthesised and reacted with CuCl₂·2H₂O in a 1:1 molar ratio. Crystal structures of three complexes showed square-planar geometry with Cu–O distances of 1.91–1.95 Å, Cu–N 1.95–2.01 Å, and Cu–S 2.26–2.31 Å. UV–visible pH titrations (I = 0.1 M KCl, 298 K) yielded stepwise stability constants log K₁ = 11.3–13.6 for the ML species, decreasing with electron-withdrawing substituents. Cyclic voltammetry in acetonitrile showed quasi-reversible Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox couples at E₁/₂ = −0.31 to −0.44 V vs. Fc/Fc⁺, shifted cathodically relative to [Cu(bipy)₂]²⁺. Solution ¹H NMR in DMSO-d₆ was used to confirm coordination mode and detect free ligand fractions at substoichiometric metal loading.

title: PM10 source apportionment in the Vojvodina plain using positive matrix factorisation: a two-site comparison
abstract: Simultaneous PM10 sampling was conducted at two sites in Vojvodina—an urban location in Novi Sad and a rural background site near Zrenjanin—over 12 months in 2021–2022. A total of 186 valid 24-hour filter samples per site were analysed for nine water-soluble ions by ion chromatography, and gravimetric PM10 mass was determined. Positive matrix factorisation (EPA PMF 5.0) resolved five factors at the urban site: secondary sulfate, secondary nitrate, road dust/soil resuspension, biomass burning, and a mixed industrial/traffic factor. At the rural site, four factors were resolved, with secondary sulfate accounting for 34% of PM10 mass, notably higher than the urban proportion of 26%. Seasonal analysis revealed that nitrate-rich episodes were concentrated in autumn and early spring, consistent with lower temperatures favouring particulate NH4NO3 stability. The cross-site comparison suggests regional-scale transport of sulfate aerosol from industrial emitters to the south-southeast. Factor profiles are provided and compared with published European receptor modelling datasets.

title: Comparison of variable selection algorithms for small azole QSAR datasets: stepwise regression, genetic algorithms, and LASSO
abstract: Small datasets are common in antifungal QSAR research because experimental MIC determinations are labour-intensive. This study compares three variable selection algorithms—forward stepwise multiple linear regression, a standard genetic algorithm, and LASSO penalised regression—applied to three published azole datasets (n = 38, 47, and 62). Evaluation criteria were R²ext on a 20 % hold-out set, the ratio of training observations to selected descriptors, and computation time. LASSO consistently achieved the best compromise, yielding R²ext values of 0.80, 0.84, and 0.79 and descriptor-to-observation ratios above 5 in all three cases. The genetic algorithm produced models of comparable accuracy but required 15–40 times longer computation. Stepwise regression was fastest but generated models with poor descriptor-to-observation ratios in two out of three datasets, raising overfitting concerns. Tuning the LASSO regularisation parameter λ by nested cross-validation was essential; a single CV loop underestimated λ by approximately 30 %.

title: Viromes of drinking water distribution biofilms: phage predation on nitrifying bacteria under chloramine selection
abstract: Despite the ecological importance of phage–host dynamics in shaping nitrifier populations, virome data from drinking water distribution biofilms remain scarce. We isolated the viral fraction from 18 biofilm samples collected across three Vojvodina networks by sequential filtration (0.45 µm then 0.1 µm) and ultracentrifugation, and sequenced DNA with Illumina NextSeq (2 × 150 bp). After assembly with VIBRANT and taxonomy assignment using vConTACT2, we identified 1,247 viral operational taxonomic units. Phages with predicted Nitrospira and Nitrosomonas hosts constituted 4.1 and 2.7% of viral OTUs respectively. Comparative analysis between high-chloramine (> 1.5 mg/L) and low-chloramine (< 0.5 mg/L) sites showed significantly higher nitrifier-phage richness at low-residual sites (Mann–Whitney U, p = 0.003), consistent with higher host abundance enabling phage propagation. Two phage contigs encoding auxiliary metabolic genes homologous to nxrB were identified, suggesting potential for metabolic manipulation of the Nitrospira host. These results indicate that phage predation may contribute to regulating nitrifier guild dynamics in chloramine-maintained biofilms.

title: Overlapping decomposition events in Ca–Sr carbonate solid solutions: deconvolution by Gaussian fitting of DTG data
abstract: Synthetic Ca1−xSrxCO3 solid solutions (x = 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0) were prepared by co-precipitation from aqueous nitrate solutions and characterised by XRD (Vegard's law verification), TG-DSC at 5–20 K min−1, and coupled FTIR. The DTG profiles of intermediate compositions (x = 0.1–0.8) exhibited asymmetric peaks indicating overlapping events. Three-component Gaussian fitting resolved contributions from Ca-rich, intermediate, and Sr-rich domains in the solid solution, with peak positions shifting monotonically from 830 °C (pure calcite) to 960 °C (pure strontianite) at 10 K min−1 in nitrogen. DSC enthalpies scaled linearly with x (176 to 234 kJ mol−1). Activation energies by isoconversional analysis rose from 198 to 247 kJ mol−1 with increasing Sr content. The Gaussian deconvolution method was validated against physical mixtures of the pure end members, showing correct recovery of component fractions to within ±5 mol%.

title: Galvanostatic deposition of polypyrrole films on stainless steel substrates from aqueous oxalic acid electrolytes
abstract: Polypyrrole (PPy) thin films were deposited on type-316 stainless steel substrates using galvanostatic electrolysis at current densities ranging from 0.5 to 4 mA cm⁻². Oxalic acid was selected as the supporting electrolyte to investigate how counter-ion incorporation affects film morphology and conductivity. Films deposited at 1.5 mA cm⁻² showed the most uniform nodular structure according to SEM analysis, with average nodule diameters of 180 ± 25 nm. Four-point probe measurements yielded conductivities between 12 and 47 S cm⁻¹ depending on deposition conditions. Cyclic voltammetry in 0.5 M Na₂SO₄ revealed specific capacitance values of 210 F g⁻¹ at 5 mV s⁻¹ for optimally deposited films. FTIR spectra confirmed characteristic PPy ring stretching and C–H deformation bands. The study established baseline deposition conditions for subsequent composite work and demonstrated that oxalic acid counter-ions measurably increase film porosity compared to perchlorate-doped counterparts prepared under identical conditions.

title: Influence of TiO₂ nanoparticle loading on the electroactivity of electrodeposited polyaniline composite films
abstract: Polyaniline–TiO₂ composite films were prepared by electropolymerisation of aniline in 1 M H₂SO₄ suspensions containing anatase TiO₂ nanoparticles at concentrations of 0, 1, 3, and 5 g L⁻¹. The resulting films were characterised by SEM-EDX, XRD, and cyclic voltammetry. Titanium incorporation into the polymer matrix increased with suspension loading up to 3 g L⁻¹, beyond which agglomeration was observed by SEM. Composite films prepared at 3 g L⁻¹ TiO₂ exhibited a specific capacitance of 485 F g⁻¹ at 10 mV s⁻¹, compared with 320 F g⁻¹ for pure PANI films prepared identically. XRD confirmed retention of the anatase crystal phase within the composite. UV-vis spectroelectrochemistry showed that the TiO₂ inclusion shifted the polaron absorption band by approximately 15 nm, suggesting a degree of electronic interaction between phases. The results indicate that moderate TiO₂ loading substantially improves charge storage without compromising film adhesion to the substrate.

title: Electrochemical impedance modelling of polyaniline–MnO₂ composite electrodes in neutral sulfate electrolyte
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was applied to polyaniline–MnO₂ composite electrodes prepared by sequential deposition on graphite substrates. Impedance spectra were recorded over the frequency range 10 mHz to 100 kHz at five potentials within the capacitive window of the electrode. A three-element equivalent circuit comprising a solution resistance, a constant phase element representing the double layer, and a Warburg-type diffusion element for proton insertion into MnO₂ was fitted to the data using a nonlinear least-squares algorithm. The fit residuals remained below 3% across all spectra. The interfacial capacitance derived from the CPE exponent (n = 0.87 ± 0.02) indicated a moderately rough electrode surface consistent with SEM observations. At 0.2 V vs. Ag/AgCl, the low-frequency capacitance reached 520 F g⁻¹. The study demonstrated that the EIS model can reliably distinguish the PANI pseudocapacitive contribution from the MnO₂ intercalation capacitance, providing a framework for separating charge-storage mechanisms in composite electrodes.

title: Cycle-stability degradation mechanisms in polypyrrole–RuO₂ supercapacitor electrodes: a combined SEM and EIS study
abstract: Long-term galvanostatic charge–discharge cycling (5000 cycles at 2 A g⁻¹) was performed on polypyrrole–RuO₂ composite electrodes prepared on titanium current collectors. Capacitance retention dropped from an initial 610 F g⁻¹ to 430 F g⁻¹ after 5000 cycles, corresponding to a 29.5% loss. SEM imaging at intervals of 500, 1000, 2000, and 5000 cycles revealed progressive delamination at the polymer–oxide interface beginning after approximately 1500 cycles, concurrent with a measurable increase in charge-transfer resistance derived from EIS spectra. A semi-empirical degradation model based on a stretched exponential function was fitted to the capacitance–cycle data, yielding a characteristic decay constant of τ = 2800 cycles. The model was validated against a second independently prepared electrode set, reproducing the measured retention within ±4%. Dissolution of RuO₂ into the electrolyte was quantified by ICP-OES and accounted for approximately 8% of the total capacity loss, with structural swelling of the PPy matrix identified as the dominant mechanism.

title: Supercapacitor electrode materials based on conducting polymers: synthesis strategies and performance metrics
abstract: This chapter reviews literature published between 2005 and 2018 covering the preparation of polyaniline, polypyrrole, and polythiophene-based composite electrodes for supercapacitor applications. Synthesis methods discussed include chemical oxidative polymerisation, in situ electrodeposition, and template-directed growth, with emphasis on how each method influences film morphology, conductivity, and interfacial contact resistance. Performance metrics including specific capacitance, energy density, power density, and cycle-life retention are tabulated for over 120 reported electrode systems, allowing direct comparison across electrolyte types and current collector materials. Special attention is given to the role of metal oxide supports—particularly TiO₂, MnO₂, and RuO₂—in stabilising the polymer matrix during extended cycling. The chapter also discusses the use of equivalent circuit modelling in impedance spectroscopy as a diagnostic tool for identifying capacity fade mechanisms. Practical considerations for electrode upscaling and testing protocol standardisation are addressed in a closing section.

title: Self-limiting electrodeposition of a polyaniline–TiO₂ bilayer architecture and its impedance response across the 200 K–330 K temperature range
abstract: A two-step electrodeposition procedure was developed to produce PANI–TiO₂ bilayer electrodes on carbon-fibre paper substrates. In the first step, a compact TiO₂ seed layer was deposited cathodically from a TiCl₄ precursor solution; in the second step, aniline was polymerised anodically atop the TiO₂ layer. The self-limiting character of TiO₂ deposition was verified by quartz crystal microbalance measurements, showing mass saturation at 18 µg cm⁻² after 300 s. EIS measurements were conducted in a custom-built temperature-controlled cell from 200 K to 330 K in 10 K increments. The charge-transfer resistance followed Arrhenius behaviour with an activation energy of 0.38 eV, consistent with a thermally activated polaron hopping mechanism in the PANI layer. At 300 K, the composite bilayer exhibited a specific capacitance of 510 F g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹, outperforming electrodes without the TiO₂ interlayer by 22%. Temperature dependence data were used to parameterise an extended equivalent circuit valid across the full temperature range investigated.

title: Polypyrrole–MnO₂ composite electrodes deposited on laser-perforated stainless-steel mesh: capacitance and rate performance
abstract: Laser perforation was used to introduce a regular array of 120 µm diameter holes in type-316 stainless-steel mesh current collectors, increasing the geometric surface area by 34% as verified by profilometry. Polypyrrole–MnO₂ composites were then deposited on both perforated and unperforated meshes under identical potentiostatic conditions. Mass loading was controlled gravimetrically and held constant at 1.8 mg cm⁻² for all samples. Cyclic voltammetry in 0.5 M Na₂SO₄ at scan rates from 2 to 100 mV s⁻¹ showed that perforated-mesh electrodes retained 71% of their 5 mV s⁻¹ capacitance (440 F g⁻¹) at 100 mV s⁻¹, compared with 52% retention for unperforated counterparts. EIS-derived ion diffusion coefficients were 1.8× higher for perforated electrodes, consistent with improved electrolyte access through the holes. After 3000 charge–discharge cycles at 3 A g⁻¹, the perforated electrodes retained 83% of initial capacitance versus 74% for the reference. The laser-perforation approach is simple, scalable, and compatible with existing roll-to-roll processing.

title: Data-driven modelling of capacitance fade in conducting polymer supercapacitor electrodes using accelerated aging protocols
abstract: An accelerated aging protocol was designed for conducting polymer supercapacitor electrodes by combining elevated temperature (50 °C) with high-rate galvanostatic cycling (5 A g⁻¹) to compress the time-equivalent of 10 000 standard cycles into approximately 1200 accelerated cycles. Four electrode chemistries were tested: pure PANI, pure PPy, PANI–TiO₂, and PPy–MnO₂. Capacitance, ESR, and mid-frequency phase angle were recorded every 100 cycles. A multiple linear regression model using three EIS-derived features as predictors reproduced the measured capacitance with R² = 0.94 across all electrode types on a held-out validation set. Feature importance analysis identified the phase angle at 1 Hz as the single most predictive variable, explaining 61% of variance. The time–temperature superposition principle was validated for PPy–MnO₂ with a shift factor of 4.2 between 25 °C and 50 °C. The model provides a basis for condition monitoring of polymer supercapacitor cells without requiring full cycling tests.

title: Multi-element profiling of phycobiliprotein preparations by ICP-MS: trace metal transfer from biomass feedstock to purified product
abstract: Transfer of 18 trace elements (including As, Cd, Pb, Hg, Se, Fe, Zn, Cu, Mn, Co, Ni, Cr, Mo, Ba, Sr, V, Al, and Ti) through the purification chain from raw Arthrospira platensis biomass to final food-grade C-phycocyanin was quantified by ICP-MS after microwave digestion (HNO3/H2O2 system). Paired samples from five independent production batches were analysed at four stages: raw biomass, clarified extract, DEAE eluate, and SEC-polished final product. Decontamination factors (DF) were calculated for each element at each step. Iron showed a DF of 8.2 after SEC polishing, consistent with removal of ferredoxin-associated iron. Cadmium DF across the full protocol was 31, reducing concentrations from 0.18 mg/kg in biomass to 0.006 mg/kg in the final product. Lead and mercury were at or below LOQ (0.002 mg/kg) in all final products. Arsenic, predominantly as arsenobetaine, was partially retained, with DF of only 4.1, warranting monitoring. The data provide a mass-balance basis for regulatory dossiers concerning heavy metal safety of phycocyanin food colourants.

title: Phycobiliprotein purification at small and medium scale: chromatographic strategies and quality criteria for food applications
abstract: This chapter reviews chromatographic methods used for preparative isolation of C-phycocyanin, B-phycoerythrin, and allophycocyanin from microalgal and cyanobacterial biomass, with emphasis on protocols suitable for small and medium production scales (grams to low kilogram per batch). Ion-exchange materials discussed include DEAE-cellulose, DEAE-Sepharose, and Q-Sepharose, with a comparative analysis of binding capacity, selectivity, and regenerability. Hydroxyapatite and size-exclusion polishing steps are covered, including practical column sizing and operating conditions. The chapter addresses analytical quality criteria relevant to food-grade classification, specifically the A620/A280 purity ratio, fluorescence retention, SDS-PAGE profile, and trace element compliance with EU maximum levels. A section on method validation requirements for food additive applications draws on EU Commission guidance and ISO 17025 principles. Economic factors including resin cost, buffer consumption, and cleaning-in-place procedures are discussed qualitatively. The chapter is directed at researchers and process chemists beginning scale-up of phycobiliprotein purification.

title: Manganese oxidation states in drinking water treatment plant sludges: implications for sludge dewatering and disposal
abstract: Sludges from four drinking water treatment plants in Vojvodina relying on oxidation–filtration for Mn removal were characterised for Mn oxidation state distribution using X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy and chemical extraction. Total Mn in dried sludges ranged from 1.2 to 6.8 % by weight. XANES analysis revealed that Mn(IV) as birnessite-type phases constituted 60–80 % of total Mn, with the remainder distributed between Mn(III) (predominantly as manganite) and residual Mn(II) co-precipitated with Fe-hydroxide. Sludge dewatering performance (assessed by specific resistance to filtration, SRF) worsened significantly when Mn(II) fractions exceeded 25 %, attributed to lower density and higher surface charge of amorphous Mn(OH)₂ particles. Disposal scenarios under Serbian and EU hazardous waste thresholds are evaluated; none of the tested sludges exceeded the Mn leachate limit at neutral pH, but two exceeded the limit under acidic leachate conditions. Recommendations for conditioning prior to landfill disposal are provided.

title: Co-crystal formation between furosemide and three pyridine derivatives: structural inference from PXRD and Raman spectroscopy in the absence of single-crystal data
abstract: Three co-crystals of furosemide (a poorly soluble loop diuretic) with 2-aminopyridine, 3-hydroxypyridine, and 4,4′-bipyridine were prepared by LAG with acetonitrile and characterised entirely in polycrystalline form. Single crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction could not be grown from any of the nine solvent systems attempted. Structural inference relied on indexing of PXRD patterns (DICVOL06 and TREOR90 algorithms), lattice parameter comparison with Cambridge Structural Database entries, and Raman band shifts. The carbonyl stretch of furosemide at 1678 cm⁻¹ shifted to 1663 cm⁻¹ in the 2-aminopyridine co-crystal, consistent with N–H···O hydrogen bonding. Quantitative phase analysis of DSC data confirmed 1:1 stoichiometry for all three co-crystals by molar enthalpy comparison. Dissolution experiments in simulated intestinal fluid (FaSSIF) at 37 °C showed 1.5-, 1.9-, and 1.3-fold increases in maximum dissolved concentration for the three co-crystals, respectively. The 3-hydroxypyridine co-crystal showed a spring-and-parachute effect with maximum concentration maintained for 120 minutes.

title: Regularised Non-Negative Matrix Factorisation for Sparse Implicit Feedback in Movie Recommendation
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of learning latent user and item representations from implicit feedback signals—click counts and view durations—where observed interactions constitute less than 0.1% of the full user-item matrix. We apply non-negative matrix factorisation with L2 regularisation and a confidence-weighted loss that treats unobserved entries as negative evidence with down-weighted certainty. Experiments are conducted on two datasets: a crawled Serbian film portal log containing 340,000 users and 12,000 titles, and the publicly available MovieLens-10M benchmark. Factorisation rank is varied from 10 to 200; optimal rank of 50 achieves an NDCG@10 of 0.314 on the portal dataset versus 0.289 for a popularity baseline. We analyse how regularisation strength interacts with dataset sparsity and show that confidence scaling on unobserved entries consistently outperforms uniform negative weighting. Runtime on a single 16-core server scales approximately linearly with the number of observed interactions up to 5 million events.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Neighbourhood-Based and Model-Based Collaborative Filtering on E-Commerce Data from the Western Balkans
abstract: We compare user-based k-nearest-neighbour collaborative filtering, item-based kNN, and singular value decomposition-based matrix factorisation on a proprietary dataset provided by a mid-size Novi Sad online retailer, comprising 91,000 users and 6,400 products over 18 months of purchase history. Similarity metrics tested include cosine, adjusted cosine, and Pearson correlation. SVD with rank-40 decomposition achieves Precision@5 of 0.187 and Recall@5 of 0.143, outperforming item-based kNN (0.161 / 0.129) and user-based kNN (0.148 / 0.118) at the same cut-off. We document practical challenges specific to the dataset: extreme popularity skew, infrequent rebuying behaviour, and seasonal drift. The paper provides a replication guide so that practitioners with similarly sized datasets can reproduce the evaluation pipeline using open-source tools. All experiments run on commodity hardware within two hours.
venue: Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information and Intelligent Systems (CECIIS)

title: Temporal Dynamics in Matrix Factorisation: Modelling User Preference Drift with Time-Decayed Interaction Weights
abstract: User tastes evolve over time, yet most matrix factorisation models treat all historical interactions as equally informative. We propose a straightforward extension to standard alternating least squares factorisation in which each interaction is multiplied by an exponential decay factor parametrised by its age relative to the query timestamp. The decay rate is treated as a per-user hyperparameter estimated from a held-out validation window. We evaluate on three datasets—a news portal clickstream (2.1 million events), the Movielens-20M benchmark, and a music streaming log from a regional provider—using a temporal train/test split that simulates online recommendation. Time-decay factorisation improves NDCG@10 by 4–7% over a static model across all three datasets, with the largest gains on the news dataset where interest shifts rapidly. We also show that a single global decay rate recovers about 80% of the gain from per-user rates at substantially lower tuning cost.

title: Autoencoders for Collaborative Filtering: A Study of Denoising and Variational Variants
abstract: We systematically compare denoising autoencoders (DAE) and variational autoencoders (VAE) as alternatives to matrix factorisation for top-N recommendation from implicit feedback. Both architectures take a user's full interaction history as input and are trained to reconstruct it under random masking noise at drop rates of 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. We test four hidden-layer configurations (one to three layers, width 128 to 512) on the Netflix Prize subset and on an internal dataset from a Serbian IPTV operator (480,000 users, 3,200 titles). The VAE variant with a single 256-unit hidden layer and KL-annealing achieves the best NDCG@10 on both datasets, outperforming our baseline SVD by 11.3% and 9.8% respectively. We analyse the latent space geometry and find that the variational bottleneck produces more uniformly distributed user representations, which correlates with reduced popularity bias in the top-10 lists. Compute requirements and sensitivity to hyperparameter choices are documented in detail.

title: Knowledge Graph Embeddings as Side Information for Item Cold-Start Recommendation
abstract: When new items enter a catalogue they have no interaction history, and pure collaborative filtering fails. We use knowledge graph (KG) embeddings—specifically TransE and RotatE trained on a product attribute graph—to initialise item latent vectors before any interactions are observed. The KG is constructed from product metadata (category hierarchy, brand relations, material attributes) for a fashion retail domain, containing 41,000 entities and 210,000 triples. These embeddings are injected into a standard matrix factorisation model as a regularisation prior on the item factor matrix. On a cold-start evaluation protocol where test items have zero training interactions, our method achieves Recall@20 of 0.073 versus 0.031 for a content-based baseline and near-zero for pure CF. For warm items the KG prior adds a small but consistent improvement of 1–2% on NDCG@10. We provide ablations over embedding dimensionality and the weighting of the KG regularisation term.

title: Recommender Systems in Practice: Methods, Architectures, and Evaluation
abstract: This book chapter surveys the landscape of recommender system methods from neighbourhood-based approaches through matrix factorisation to deep learning models, with emphasis on practical deployment considerations. We cover data preprocessing for implicit versus explicit feedback, offline evaluation pitfalls including popularity bias in ranking metrics, and the gap between offline and online A/B test outcomes. A section on serving architectures discusses two-stage retrieval-ranking pipelines and approximate nearest-neighbour indexes for embedding-based retrieval. The chapter includes worked examples using synthetic data and references to open-source implementations. It is aimed at graduate students and practitioners who wish to implement and evaluate recommender systems without requiring prior exposure to the research literature. The treatment is self-contained with respect to linear algebra and basic probability.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Session-Based Recommendation: An Empirical Comparison of GCN, GAT, and SR-GNN on Short-Session Data
abstract: Session-based recommendation models the next-click prediction problem using only the items observed within the current anonymous session, without access to long-term user history. We re-implement and evaluate three graph neural network approaches—Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), Graph Attention Network (GAT), and the gated SR-GNN model—on two public benchmarks (Diginetica, RetailRocket) and a proprietary dataset of supermarket browsing sessions collected by a Novi Sad-based grocery chain, containing 820,000 sessions with median length 4. We use a strict temporal split and report MRR@20 and HR@20. SR-GNN outperforms the others on Diginetica (MRR@20: 0.502) but all three models perform within noise on the grocery dataset, likely due to very short session lengths. We identify session length as a critical moderator of GNN advantage over simpler GRU baselines and provide guidance on when the added complexity is justified.

title: Fairness Metrics in Recommender Systems: Measuring and Mitigating Popularity Bias in Top-N Lists
abstract: Popular items dominate top-N recommendation lists produced by most collaborative filtering models due to their over-representation in training data. We define and operationalise four group-fairness metrics for items: coverage, aggregate diversity, long-tail coverage, and Gini coefficient of recommendation frequency. We then compare three post-processing debiasing strategies—reranking by inverse popularity, calibration to target genre distributions, and maximum marginal relevance—against an unmodified VAE-based recommender on two datasets: a music streaming log and a book recommendation dataset scraped from a regional literary portal. Reranking by inverse popularity improves long-tail coverage from 12% to 34% with only a 3.1% reduction in NDCG@10 on the music dataset. We discuss trade-offs between accuracy and diversity metrics and provide a decision guide for practitioners choosing among the three strategies.

title: Contrastive Self-Supervised Pre-Training of User Embeddings for Cross-Domain Recommendation
abstract: We investigate whether user embeddings pre-trained on a source domain (music streaming) using a contrastive self-supervised objective can improve recommendation quality in a sparse target domain (podcast listening) when only a fraction of users overlap. The pre-training task constructs positive pairs by splitting a user's interaction sequence at a random cut and treating both halves as views of the same user; negatives are drawn from other users in the same mini-batch. Pre-trained embeddings are then fine-tuned with a matrix factorisation objective on the target domain. On a dataset of 210,000 overlapping users shared by a regional media platform, fine-tuned embeddings improve NDCG@10 by 8.4% over training from scratch and by 5.1% over a transfer approach using direct embedding copying. Gains are concentrated in users with fewer than 15 target-domain interactions, confirming that the benefit is primarily in the sparse-data regime.

title: Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbour Retrieval for Embedding-Based Recommenders: A Benchmark on Commodity Hardware
abstract: Two-stage recommenders use approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search to retrieve candidate items from a learned embedding space before a more expensive ranking model re-scores them. We benchmark five ANN index structures—HNSW, IVF-Flat, IVF-PQ, ScaNN, and a flat exact baseline—on three embedding spaces of different dimensionalities (64, 128, 256) and catalogue sizes (50K, 500K, 5M items) using recall@100 and query latency at fixed memory budgets on a single server with 64 GB RAM and no GPU. HNSW achieves the best recall–latency trade-off for catalogues up to 500K items; IVF-PQ becomes competitive at 5M items under 16 GB memory constraints. We also measure how ANN retrieval recall translates to end-to-end NDCG@10 degradation and find that recall@100 above 0.92 causes less than 1% NDCG loss relative to exact retrieval. A practical configuration guide is included.

title: Large Language Model Representations as Item Features in Hybrid Recommender Systems
abstract: We examine whether dense text representations extracted from a frozen large language model (a 7-billion-parameter decoder-only model) can serve as item feature vectors in a hybrid collaborative filtering framework, replacing or complementing manually engineered metadata features. Item descriptions from a job advertisement portal (340,000 postings) are encoded with mean pooling over final-layer token embeddings to produce 4096-dimensional vectors, then projected to lower-dimensional spaces (64, 128) via a learned linear layer jointly trained with the CF objective. On a held-out evaluation set, the LLM-feature hybrid achieves NDCG@10 of 0.381 versus 0.354 for a metadata-feature hybrid and 0.369 for pure CF, with the largest gain for items posted within the last 7 days (effectively cold-start). We also test freezing versus fine-tuning the projection layer and find that even the frozen projection recovers most of the benefit. Inference latency for encoding new items is 140 ms per item on a single A4000 GPU.

title: Automated Adapter Generation from Mismatched Interface Specifications
abstract: When two systems must be integrated but their interface specifications describe incompatible message structures or interaction protocols, a protocol adapter is required. Manual adapter coding is error-prone and difficult to maintain. This paper presents a model-driven method in which both interfaces are described as finite-state machines annotated with typed message vocabularies; the mismatch is characterised as a set of transformation rules derived automatically by a constraint solver, and ATL templates then generate executable Apache Camel routes that implement the adapter. The method was applied to 22 real interface pairs collected from three companies in the manufacturing sector in Vojvodina. Fully automated generation succeeded in 16 cases; the remaining six required on average 2.3 hours of manual refinement. Generated adapters passed all supplied regression tests.

title: Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams
abstract: This paper proposes an incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic without the need for periodic full retraining. The algorithm maintains a fixed number of Gaussian components (K = 5 to 20 evaluated) and uses a Bayesian update rule to adjust component means, covariances, and weights with each arriving window of observations. Feature vectors are 32-dimensional, derived from 10-second traffic windows. The method was evaluated on a 180-day Modbus/TCP capture from a district heating control network and compared with a static GMM retrained every 24 hours. The iGMM maintained an F1 score within 0.03 of the periodically retrained model while reducing retraining compute cost by 94%. Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested. Memory footprint per detector instance was under 120 KB.

title: Out-of-Distribution Detection for Legal Document Classifiers: A Study on Serbian Administrative Text
abstract: Classifiers deployed in production legal systems regularly encounter documents that belong to no category in the training taxonomy—newly enacted law types, atypical procedural forms, or documents from adjacent domains. This paper studies out-of-distribution (OOD) detection as a complement to standard closed-set classification in the context of Serbian administrative law. Seven OOD detection methods are evaluated: maximum softmax probability, ODIN, Mahalanobis distance, energy-based scoring, a Monte Carlo dropout ensemble, a deep ensemble, and a one-class neural baseline. Evaluation uses an in-distribution set of 6,400 administrative decisions across 16 categories and four OOD sets of increasing distance from the in-distribution. At a 95% true-positive rate threshold, energy-based scoring and the Mahalanobis method perform best, achieving AUROC values of 0.91 and 0.89 respectively. The paper discusses calibration of classifier confidence scores as a prerequisite for reliable OOD thresholding in production deployments.

title: Overhead Characterisation of Label-Propagation Mechanisms Across Five Microservice Frameworks
abstract: Label propagation for information-flow monitoring can be implemented at multiple abstraction levels in modern microservice frameworks. This paper compares five implementation strategies across five popular frameworks: context propagation via W3C TraceContext headers (Spring Boot, Quarkus), middleware interception (gRPC interceptors), service mesh header injection (Istio/Envoy), a shared sidecar IPC channel, and kernel-level socket tagging via eBPF. Each strategy is benchmarked on a chain of ten services with varying payload sizes (1 KB–1 MB) and request rates (10–5,000 req/s). Metrics collected are end-to-end latency, CPU overhead on the service host, and label accuracy (fraction of requests carrying a correct label). The eBPF approach and TraceContext header approach tie on accuracy (99.7% and 99.4% respectively) while differing substantially on CPU overhead (0.8% vs. 0.2% at 1,000 req/s). The paper provides selection guidance based on framework constraints and accuracy requirements.

title: Prevalence of footpad dermatitis in broiler flocks on Vojvodina farms: a cross-sectional survey across 18 production cycles
abstract: Footpad dermatitis (FPD) is a widely used welfare indicator in broiler production, yet baseline prevalence data for the Pannonian Plain region of Serbia were lacking. This study surveyed 18 consecutive production cycles across six commercial farms in Vojvodina during 2012–2013, scoring 5 400 birds at slaughter using a four-point scale. Mean FPD prevalence at score 2 or higher was 38.4%, with significant seasonal variation: cycles ending in July–August showed prevalence 22 percentage points higher than winter cycles. Litter moisture content, measured every ten days, explained 54% of the variance in FPD score in a mixed-effects model controlling for stocking density and breed. Stocking density above 34 kg/m² was associated with a 1.8-fold increase in odds of high-severity FPD. The results provide a regional reference dataset and indicate that summer litter management is the primary modifiable risk factor in the local continental climate.

title: Adaptation of the Welfare Quality broiler protocol to high-temperature summer conditions in the Pannonian climate zone
abstract: The Welfare Quality (WQ) broiler protocol was developed primarily in northern and western European settings and its scoring thresholds have not been validated for the warm continental summers typical of the Pannonian Plain. This study applied the full WQ protocol to 12 commercial farms in Serbia and Hungary over two consecutive summers (2014 and 2015), comparing protocol outcomes with independent physiological stress markers including heterophil-to-lymphocyte ratios and breast blister prevalence. WQ scores for thermal comfort were assigned as 'acceptable' in 9 of 24 visits despite ambient house temperatures exceeding 32°C for more than six hours per day, a condition associated in this dataset with H/L ratios indicative of moderate heat stress. Logistic regression showed that the current WQ thermal threshold misclassified approximately 29% of visits relative to the physiological criterion. Proposed revised thresholds are presented for three climate-zone subgroups, along with a decision flowchart for assessors working in warm continental regions.

title: Inter-observer reliability of a simplified five-criterion on-farm welfare index for broilers applied by farm personnel
abstract: Standardised welfare assessment is of limited practical use if it cannot be reliably performed by farm staff without specialist training. This study developed a simplified five-criterion welfare index (WI-5) covering footpad dermatitis, hock burn, breast blister, dustbathing behaviour frequency, and water drinker cleanliness, and tested its inter-observer reliability in a training trial involving 24 assessors (12 trained researchers and 12 farm workers) across eight farms in Serbia. Each assessor independently scored the same 60 birds per visit, and agreement was quantified with Cohen's kappa and intraclass correlation coefficients. Kappa values for trained researchers ranged from 0.71 to 0.86; farm-worker kappa values after a two-hour training session ranged from 0.61 to 0.79, indicating substantial agreement. The criterion with lowest agreement was dustbathing frequency (kappa 0.61 for farm workers), suggesting that behavioural criteria require longer training. WI-5 scores correlated strongly with the full Welfare Quality outcome score (r = 0.83, p < 0.001), supporting its use as a rapid screening tool.

title: Gait scoring in commercial broilers: comparison of a visual six-point scale and a pressure-mat-based locomotion index
abstract: Lameness is a principal welfare concern in fast-growing broiler breeds. Two scoring methods were compared: a conventional observer-assigned six-point gait scale (GS-6) applied to 120 birds per farm and a pressure-mat locomotion index (PLI) derived from peak force asymmetry and step-length ratio measured on a 1.2-metre portable mat. Data were collected from ten farms in Serbia during winter 2018 over three visits each, generating 360 farm-visit observations and 43 200 individual gait assessments. GS-6 and PLI agreed in classifying birds as lame (score ≥ 3 or PLI > 0.28) in 81.4% of cases. Discordant cases were disproportionately birds in the GS-6 score-2 category. PLI identified clinically relevant asymmetry in 14.2% of score-2 birds classified as non-lame by visual scoring. Intraclass correlation for repeated PLI measurements on the same bird within a single session was 0.91. The portable pressure mat required 40 minutes more per farm visit than visual scoring, representing a practical trade-off for commercial adoption.

title: Environmental monitoring as a component of welfare assessment: temperature-humidity index thresholds and their association with behaviour in broiler houses during Vojvodina summers
abstract: Hot summer periods in Vojvodina regularly produce temperature-humidity index (THI) values above 28, a threshold not explicitly referenced in current EU welfare legislation for poultry. This study installed continuous dataloggers at three heights (0.1, 0.5, and 1.5 m) in 14 broiler houses across nine farms and recorded indoor THI at five-minute intervals across the full 2020 summer growing season. Simultaneously, focal-animal scan sampling was conducted during six visits per house, recording panting, water intake frequency, activity, and mortality. THI at bird level (0.1 m) exceeded 28 for a cumulative mean of 312 hours per cycle in uninsulated houses versus 94 hours in insulated houses with evaporative cooling. Panting incidence exceeded 40% of birds when THI surpassed 29.5, and daily mortality spiked above 0.12%/day when THI at bird level exceeded 31 for more than two consecutive hours. Insulation and evaporative cooling together reduced cumulative high-THI exposure by 70%. Results are presented as lookup tables usable by welfare assessors without dataloggers.

title: Scoring schemes for litter quality in broiler houses: a comparison of four methods under field conditions in Serbia and Romania
abstract: Litter quality scoring is embedded in most broiler welfare protocols, but at least four distinct scoring schemes circulate in regional use across Southeast Europe, with no published comparison of their agreement or practical burden. This study applied four schemes—a two-point binary scheme, a four-point ordinal scheme, a visual wetness-caking composite, and a dry-matter percentage measured gravimetrically—concurrently on litter samples from 22 farms in Serbia and Romania across two production seasons (2020 and 2021), yielding 528 sampling occasions. Gravimetric dry-matter percentage served as the reference criterion. Ordinal scheme scores correlated most strongly with dry matter (Spearman ρ = −0.79), while binary scores showed the weakest correlation (ρ = −0.51). The composite scheme performed comparably to the ordinal scheme (ρ = −0.77) and was preferred by assessors for speed. Agreement between Serbian and Romanian assessors applying the same scheme was moderate to good (kappa 0.63–0.74). A harmonised three-point descriptive scoring guide for regional use is proposed.

title: Welfare outcomes across three fast-growing broiler genotypes reared under identical commercial conditions in Vojvodina
abstract: Breed selection is a primary driver of welfare outcomes in commercial broilers, but comparative data for the genotypes predominant in Southeast European markets are limited. Three Ross-type and two Cobb-type genotypes widely distributed in Serbia were reared in identical experimental pens (1 000 birds per pen, three replicate pens per genotype, stocking density 32 kg/m²) under commercial management conditions at a partner farm in Vojvodina. Welfare assessments at day 35 included gait scoring, footpad dermatitis scoring, breast blister prevalence, mortality records, and ocular discharge scoring. Significant genotype differences were found for gait score distribution (χ² = 41.2, p < 0.001): one Ross-type genotype showed 31% of birds at GS ≥ 3 versus 18% in the best-performing genotype. Footpad dermatitis prevalence ranged from 22% to 44% across genotypes under identical litter management. Cumulative seven-week mortality ranged from 2.1% to 4.7%. Results indicate that genotype selection alone can shift welfare outcomes by margins comparable to management interventions.

title: Welfare assessment scoring systems for broiler chickens in Southeast Europe: methods, limitations, and adaptation to regional conditions
abstract: This chapter reviews published and grey-literature welfare assessment protocols applied to commercial broiler production, with particular attention to their suitability for the continental climate conditions, farm structures, and regulatory context of Southeast Europe. The chapter covers the origins and structure of major scoring systems, including the Welfare Quality broiler protocol, the European Chicken Commitment monitoring requirements, and national schemes from Serbia, Romania, Hungary, and Croatia. For each system, the chapter summarises the evidence base for individual indicators, documented performance in warm continental settings, and practical constraints for adoption on small and medium farms typical of the Vojvodina and Banat regions. Climate-specific modifications discussed include revised thermal thresholds, adjusted litter moisture scoring windows for summer cycles, and alternative behavioural indicators applicable when pen access is restricted. The chapter concludes with a structured comparison table of 11 systems across 14 criteria and identifies gaps where field validation studies are absent.
venue: Poultry Production in Southeast Europe: Systems, Welfare, and Policy (Edited volume, University of Novi Sad Press)

title: Dustbathing behaviour frequency as a welfare indicator in commercial broiler flocks: feasibility of inclusion in routine on-farm assessments
abstract: Dustbathing is a recognised behavioural need in domestic fowl, but its inclusion in commercial broiler welfare protocols remains inconsistent, partly due to uncertainty about reliable observation methods under farm conditions. This study recorded dustbathing frequency in 16 commercial broiler houses in Serbia during two production cycles (2024 and 2025) using instantaneous scan sampling at 30-minute intervals between 09:00 and 15:00, validated against continuous video recording on a subset of four houses. Dustbathing was observed in 9 of 16 houses in at least one scan session. Frequency was positively associated with litter dry matter content above 75% (OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.8–6.5) and negatively associated with stocking density above 36 kg/m² (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22–0.77). Inter-observer agreement for presence-absence of dustbathing at flock level was good (kappa 0.73). The study supports including a presence-absence dustbathing criterion in rapid welfare screens, while a frequency count requires a minimum 45-minute observation window that may not be feasible in all commercial visits.

title: Linking welfare assessment scores at farm level to slaughter-line indicator data: a two-year pilot across four Serbian broiler integrators
abstract: Slaughter-line data on footpad dermatitis, hock burn, breast blister, and condemnation rates are routinely collected in EU-regulated abattoirs and offer a retrospective welfare signal, but their correspondence with on-farm welfare scores in the Serbian regulatory context has not been quantified. This pilot study matched slaughter-line records from four broiler integrators in Serbia with on-farm welfare assessments conducted within seven days of slaughter across 78 flocks between 2024 and 2025. Correlation between on-farm FPD score distribution and slaughter-line FPD prevalence at severity ≥ 2 was moderate (Spearman ρ = 0.62). Slaughter-line hock burn prevalence showed weaker on-farm correspondence (ρ = 0.44), possibly reflecting changes in litter contact patterns during transport. Condemnation rates were not significantly correlated with any single on-farm welfare score but were associated with composite welfare index scores below the threshold for 'acceptable' classification (Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.007). The findings support using slaughter-line data as a cross-check for on-farm assessment programmes but indicate that it cannot substitute for direct farm evaluation.

title: Predicting cumulative estrogenic burden in dairy cow diets: a scoring model validated against urinary biomarkers in Vojvodina farms
abstract: No practical on-farm tool currently integrates multiple estrogenic feed inputs into a unified risk score. Using data collected from 22 farms over two years, we developed a cumulative estrogenic burden (CEB) score that combines standardised contributions from dietary ZEN, formononetin, daidzein, coumestrol, and cypermethrin, weighted by their relative binding affinities to the bovine estrogen receptor-α derived from published Ki values. The CEB score was validated against urinary α-ZOL and estradiol-17β in 220 cows. Linear regression of urinary α-ZOL on CEB score yielded R² = 0.54 (p < 0.001); inclusion of herd random effects improved fit (marginal R² = 0.49, conditional R² = 0.68). CEB score quartile membership was significantly associated with FSCR in a secondary analysis (Q4 vs. Q1: OR 0.44; p = 0.003). A simplified spreadsheet implementation of the model, requiring only routine feed analysis data, was tested by three Vojvodina veterinary practitioners and rated as feasible in field conditions. The model requires prospective validation in wider farm populations.

title: Digestibility of soybean meal and sunflower protein concentrate as partial fishmeal replacers in European catfish diets: effect of feed processing method
abstract: Replacement of fishmeal with plant protein sources was tested in European catfish diets processed either by cold pelleting or steam extrusion. Three inclusion levels of soybean meal (0, 15, 30%) and two inclusion levels of sunflower protein concentrate (0 and 12%) were combined with the two processing methods, yielding 12 dietary treatments. Fish averaging 120 g were held in indoor recirculating tanks (n = 15 per tank, three replicates per treatment) for 49 days. Faeces were collected by settling column. Crude protein ADC declined from 86.4% to 79.1% as soybean meal inclusion increased from 0 to 30% in pelleted diets, but only from 87.2% to 83.6% in extruded diets, suggesting that extrusion partially mitigates anti-nutritional factor activity. Sunflower protein concentrate did not significantly interact with processing method. Specific growth rate and protein efficiency ratio paralleled digestibility patterns. Histological examination of mid-intestinal sections showed no signs of enteritis at any treatment level.

title: Vitamin E and selenium supplementation during summer: effects on oxidative status and milk fat composition in Holstein-Friesian cows
abstract: A randomised block trial was conducted with 48 Holstein-Friesian cows divided into four groups receiving: (1) control diet, (2) additional vitamin E (1,000 IU/day), (3) organic selenium (0.3 mg/kg DM as selenised yeast), and (4) combined vitamin E and selenium supplementation. The trial ran for 60 days during summer (THI mean 76.2). Blood was sampled on days 0, 30, and 60 for superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione peroxidase (GPx), and malondialdehyde (MDA) assays. Milk fatty acid profiles were obtained by GC-FID. The combined supplement group showed the highest GPx activity and lowest MDA concentration throughout the trial. CLA content was 22% higher in the combined group compared to control at day 60 (p < 0.05). Polyunsaturated fatty acid proportion also increased modestly in groups 3 and 4. Milk yield and composition parameters other than fat showed no significant treatment effects. These results suggest that antioxidant supplementation partially counteracts heat-stress-induced degradation of milk fat quality.

title: Legibility thresholds of directional arrows in hospital corridor signage: a controlled viewing-distance study
abstract: This study measured the critical viewing distance at which 42 adult participants could correctly identify seven directional arrow variants used in Serbian public hospital signage. Stimuli were printed on matte substrates and presented under three illuminance levels (50 lx, 150 lx, and 500 lx) in a light-tight chamber. Arrow width-to-height ratio, stroke width, and arrowhead angle were varied systematically across 21 design conditions. Participants identified the direction of travel indicated by each arrow from distances ranging from 1 m to 18 m in 0.5 m increments. Results showed that reducing stroke width below 12% of symbol height caused identification accuracy to drop below 90% at distances exceeding 8 m even at 500 lx. Arrowhead angles between 40° and 55° yielded the highest identification rates across all illuminance levels. Recommendations for minimum stroke width and arrowhead geometry are proposed for standardisation within hospital wayfinding guidelines in Serbia.
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Information Design
