title: Pictogram comprehension across age groups in a tertiary care hospital in Vojvodina
abstract: The study assessed comprehension rates of 30 ISO 7001 transport and healthcare-related pictograms among three age groups (18–35, 36–59, 60–79 years; n = 180 total, 60 per group) recruited in the waiting areas of a large regional hospital. Participants were shown each pictogram individually on a calibrated tablet display at a standardised ambient luminance of 200 cd/m² and asked to state its meaning without any contextual cues. A second session introduced a bilingual Serbian–Hungarian text label beneath the symbol. Comprehension scores without labels averaged 58% for the 60–79 age group compared to 79% for the 18–35 group. Adding text labels raised overall comprehension to 91% but reduced the benefit specifically for pictograms with ambiguous spatial relationships. Sixteen pictograms fell below the ISO-recommended 67% comprehension threshold when tested without labels in the oldest group. The findings support mandatory text pairing in wayfinding applications targeting mixed-age hospital populations.

title: Colour contrast ratios in existing hospital wayfinding systems: an audit of twelve facilities in Serbia and Croatia
abstract: An observational audit was conducted across twelve hospital facilities in Serbia (eight) and Croatia (four), recording foreground–background colour contrast ratios of 684 installed wayfinding signs. Measurements were taken using a calibrated spectrophotometer under prevailing ambient conditions, and contrast ratios were computed according to the WCAG 2.1 relative luminance formula adapted for reflective surfaces. Fifty-three percent of measured signs fell below a contrast ratio of 3:1, and 31% below 2:1. Facilities built before 1985 had a significantly higher proportion of non-conforming signs than those built after 2000. Common failure modes included yellow text on cream backgrounds, dark-grey symbols on mid-grey substrate panels, and colour-coded zone maps with insufficient inter-zone differentiation. The audit instrument and scoring rubric developed for this study are described in detail and are available for replication in other Central and Eastern European healthcare facility audits.

title: Contrast sensitivity and sign character recognition in adults aged 65 and older: implications for minimum type size in healthcare wayfinding
abstract: Contrast sensitivity functions (CSFs) were measured for 68 adults aged 65–84 using a sinusoidal grating test under photopic (300 lx) and mesopic (5 lx) conditions. The same participants then completed a character recognition task with uppercase sans-serif text (Helvetica Neue LT Pro 55 Roman and 75 Bold weights) at sizes ranging from 12 mm to 80 mm cap height, presented on matte white signage-grade substrate at contrast ratios of 4.5:1 and 8:1. CSF peak sensitivity at mesopic luminance was on average 0.41 log units lower than at photopic luminance across the group. A type size of 40 mm cap height at 8:1 contrast achieved 95% correct identification at a 5 m viewing distance under mesopic conditions. Below 25 mm at 4.5:1 contrast, accuracy dropped below 80% even at 3 m. Recommendations are formulated for minimum type sizes in hospital corridor and lift-lobby signage where night-time lighting is reduced.

title: Wayfinding strategy differences between first-time and repeat visitors in a multi-building hospital campus: an observational study
abstract: Forty-eight participants (24 first-time visitors, 24 repeat visitors) were recruited at the entrance of a multi-building regional hospital campus in Vojvodina and asked to navigate to four pre-specified destinations. Participants wore a chest-mounted camera and a GPS tracker; post-task interviews were conducted using a think-aloud recall protocol. First-time visitors spent on average 4.2 minutes longer per route and consulted printed directory signs 3.1 times more frequently than repeat visitors. Errors were categorised as wrong-turn, backtracking, and sign-missed; wrong-turn errors clustered at two T-junction nodes where sign placement was blocked by a temporary construction screen. Repeat visitors relied primarily on landmark cues rather than directional signs, suggesting that sign systems must remain functional for orientation even when environmental landmarks are temporarily altered. The study identifies five specific sign locations that account for 67% of all navigational errors.

title: Symbol–text spatial arrangement and reading order in bilingual hospital signage: Serbian and Hungarian side-by-side layouts
abstract: Healthcare facilities in the Vojvodina region of Serbia are legally required to provide bilingual signage in Serbian and Hungarian in municipalities where the Hungarian community exceeds 15% of the population. This study examined how the spatial arrangement of a pictogram relative to bilingual text blocks affects reading speed and comprehension. Forty subjects with Serbian as their first language and 40 with Hungarian as their first language completed timed reading tasks for six layout configurations varying the symbol position (left, right, above text) and the ordering of the two language text blocks. Eye-tracking data were collected using a remote eye tracker at 60 Hz. Symbol-left placement with Serbian text on top produced the fastest mean fixation-to-decision time (1.8 s) for Serbian-dominant readers, while Hungarian-dominant readers showed no statistically significant preference for language ordering. Results inform a bilingual signage template for healthcare facilities in the region.

title: Retroreflective materials for emergency egress signage: luminance uniformity measurements in reduced-power lighting scenarios
abstract: Emergency egress signs in hospitals are required to remain readable during power failures when only battery-backed emergency lighting operates, typically reducing corridor illuminance to 1–5 lx. This study evaluated four commercially available retroreflective substrate materials (two glass-bead and two microprismatic types) as potential replacements for internally illuminated plastic sign panels. Luminance uniformity and minimum–maximum luminance ratios were measured across each substrate at five incidence angles (0°, 10°, 20°, 30°, 45°) under a 2 lx emergency lighting simulation using a standardised LED emergency luminaire. Microprismatic materials maintained luminance uniformity ratios above 0.65 at incidence angles up to 20°, while glass-bead materials dropped below 0.40 beyond 10°. A practical assessment protocol using portable luminance meters is described, enabling facilities managers to evaluate installed retroreflective signs without laboratory equipment. Limitations related to specular reflections from polished floor surfaces are discussed.

title: Information hierarchy and sign density at decision points in hospital wayfinding: a subjective workload study
abstract: Excessive sign density at navigational decision points has been identified anecdotally as a source of confusion, but empirical data on information load thresholds remain sparse. Sixty participants navigated a hospital corridor simulation rendered in a 3-D virtual environment displayed on a large-format monitor. Sign panels at simulated T-junctions contained between 2 and 10 destination entries, with sub-experiments varying font size, colour-coding, and arrow orientation. NASA-TLX subscale scores for mental demand and frustration increased significantly when entry count exceeded six (p < 0.01) regardless of colour-coding condition. Response time to select the correct destination increased by an average of 0.32 s per additional entry beyond six. A hierarchical categorisation of destinations into three display tiers (immediate clinical areas, support services, building exits) is proposed as a practical method for managing information density within the six-entry threshold.

title: A field evaluation of redesigned wayfinding signs in an oncology centre: before-and-after navigation performance and user satisfaction
abstract: A complete wayfinding sign system was redesigned and installed in a 380-bed oncology centre following a structured design process that incorporated legibility testing and staff consultation. Pre-installation data were collected over three weeks (n = 94 unassisted navigation observations) and post-installation data over three weeks six months after installation (n = 98 observations). The primary outcome was successful unassisted navigation, defined as reaching the stated destination without asking staff for directions or making more than one corrective backtrack. Successful navigation increased from 61% pre-installation to 84% post-installation. Staff reported a 43% reduction in wayfinding-related questions from patients and visitors based on a structured log kept by reception personnel. Patient satisfaction survey scores related to ease of finding one's way increased by 1.4 points on a 7-point Likert scale. The study describes the design process, testing methodology, and implementation logistics.

title: Floor-level and ceiling-level wayfinding cues: visibility from wheelchair and walking-frame user eye heights
abstract: Standard-height wall-mounted signage is designed for standing adult eye heights (approximately 1.55–1.70 m) and may be partially or fully outside the useful visual field of wheelchair users (eye height approximately 1.20 m) and walking-frame users who adopt a forward-inclined posture (functional eye height approximately 0.95–1.10 m). This study measured detection and identification distances for wall-mounted signs at three installation heights (1.0 m, 1.5 m, 2.1 m) for 22 wheelchair users and 18 walking-frame users recruited at rehabilitation and geriatric wards. Detection distance for signs at 1.0 m was significantly greater for wheelchair users than for walking-frame users (p = 0.008). Floor-applied vinyl wayfinding strips were also tested; identification of the destination label was not possible beyond 2.5 m for any participant group due to perspective distortion. Dual-height mounting at 1.0 m and 1.5 m is recommended for facilities serving high proportions of mobility-impaired users.

title: Typeface weight and stroke modulation effects on character recognition under simulated cataract contrast reduction
abstract: Cataract-related vision impairment reduces contrast sensitivity rather than acuity, making it a useful model for testing signage under age-related conditions. Using a cataract simulation filter (Neuro-Vision CatSim 2 goggles, calibrated to approximately 0.3 log unit loss at 3 cycles/degree), 55 participants aged 22–40 with normal acuity completed character identification tasks for eight typefaces varying in stroke weight (thin, regular, medium, bold, extrabold) and modulation (low-modulation grotesks versus high-modulation humanist sans-serifs). Text was presented at a fixed cap height of 35 mm at 5 m on matte-white signage substrate at 180 lx. Bold and extrabold weight variants of low-modulation grotesks achieved identification accuracy above 93% under the cataract filter; thin and regular weights of high-modulation humanist faces fell below 75%. The results suggest that stroke modulation is a more critical parameter than weight alone for users with contrast sensitivity deficits.

title: Standardisation gaps in hospital wayfinding sign systems in the Western Balkans: a comparative policy review
abstract: This paper reviews existing technical standards, building regulations, and national guidelines governing hospital wayfinding signage in six Western Balkan countries (Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania). Regulatory documents were collected through national standards institutes and ministry of health websites; interviews were conducted with eight hospital facility managers across the region. No country in the survey has a dedicated national standard for healthcare wayfinding; applicable requirements are scattered across fire safety codes, accessibility legislation, and voluntary quality frameworks. The ISO 7001 pictogram standard has been formally adopted in Serbia and Croatia but not in the remaining four countries. Significant variation exists in minimum contrast, type size, and symbol size requirements across the jurisdictions that do specify such values. The paper identifies the most consequential gaps and discusses pathways toward a regional harmonised guideline, drawing on comparisons with German DIN and UK NHS wayfinding standards.

title: Dynamic digital wayfinding displays in hospital entrance lobbies: update frequency and motion effects on older adult legibility
abstract: Digital display panels are increasingly used as directory boards in hospital lobbies, with content cycling through multiple screens or using scrolling text. This study examined how content update frequency (static, 5 s cycle, 3 s cycle, continuous scroll at 40 px/s) affected legibility and task completion for 44 adults aged 65–80 and 44 adults aged 25–40. Participants were asked to locate a named destination on a digital directory panel at a standardised distance of 3.5 m. Task completion rate for older adults fell from 91% on static displays to 54% on 3-second cycled displays and to 29% on continuously scrolled content. Younger adults showed no significant difference across cycle frequencies but performed below 80% on continuous scroll. Fixation duration data from remote eye tracking showed that older adults required at least 4.2 s of stable display time to complete a single read. Recommendations for minimum dwell times and motion-free zones in digital hospital directory design are proposed.

title: Colour-zone coding systems in hospital wayfinding: memorability and navigation efficiency in a multi-storey building simulation
abstract: Colour-zone coding assigns a distinct colour to each functional zone or floor of a hospital, aiming to reduce cognitive load during navigation. This study tested whether participants could correctly associate six colour codes with their corresponding zones after a single briefing exposure, and whether this association aided navigation in a multi-storey virtual building simulation. Seventy-two participants were divided into a colour-coded sign condition and a text-only sign condition. In the virtual building, navigation to six targets was timed and error-counted over three consecutive trials. After three trials, colour-coded condition participants committed fewer wrong-floor errors (mean 0.8 vs. 2.1 per participant) and showed steeper learning curves. However, 18 participants reported colour vision deficiency or difficulty; post-hoc analysis showed their error rates were equivalent across conditions, indicating that colour coding without secondary coding (shape or pattern) provides no benefit for this group. Revised guidelines integrating redundant coding are discussed.

title: Template Inheritance Architectures for Multi-Brand Document Systems
abstract: Large organisations that operate multiple brands simultaneously need document template systems in which brand-specific rules override shared structural defaults without duplicating entire template trees. This paper proposes an inheritance model adapted from object-oriented programming, applied to a document template language based on XML stylesheets. Brands are encoded as override layers that modify colour tokens, typeface assignments, spacing scales, and logo-placement rules. A case study examined a fictional fast-moving consumer goods company operating seven sub-brands with a combined annual output exceeding 14 000 distinct document instances. Template tree depth ranged from two to four levels. Compared to a flat template approach used previously, the inheritance model reduced total template file count by 71 percent and cut mean time-to-update after brand refresh from 11 days to 2.5 days, as measured by version-control commit histories provided for the experiment.

title: Evaluation of Open-Format Colour Standards for Cross-Site Variable-Data Campaign Print Production
abstract: Marketing campaigns distributed across multiple print sites require that all sites reproduce brand colours within agreed tolerances from a single variable-data master file. This paper examines the practical effectiveness of three open colour communication formats—CGATS21 CRPC conditions, ISO 15339 reference print conditions, and a customer-supplied ISO 12647-2 deviation specification—as alignment frameworks for a variable-data campaign produced at five print sites in Serbia, Slovenia, and the Czech Republic. Spot colour simulations and key brand colour patches were measured from each site's output on common coated and uncoated substrates. Inter-site ΔE2000 for the primary brand colour ranged from 0.8 to 4.9 depending on the standard used. The ISO 15339 CRPC conditions provided the tightest clustering (maximum inter-site ΔE2000 of 2.3) because they specify spectral targets rather than printing conditions. Recommended minimum requirements for distributed variable-data campaign production are stated.

title: Device Link Profile Construction for Ink Saving in Toner-Based Digital Printing on Coated Substrates
abstract: Device link profiles that substitute composite black for CMY overprint regions can reduce toner consumption while maintaining colour appearance, but their construction and deployment in variable-data workflows introduces colour management complexity. This study constructs device link profiles using three GCR strategies (light, medium, skeleton) for a CMYK toner press profiled to ISO 12647-2 coated paper conditions and evaluates them against a reference rendering without GCR on 768-patch and photographic test targets. Total area coverage reduction achieved by skeleton GCR was 28% on the photographic test image. Neutral stability across the grey balance scale improved measurably with skeleton GCR, reducing grey balance ΔE2000 from 1.8 to 0.9 on average. A practical integration procedure for embedding device link profiles within JDF job tickets for automated application at the RIP is described, and compatibility across three RIP platforms is assessed.

title: Illumination Geometry and Spectral Bandwidth Effects on Contrast Ratio Measurements of Printed QR Codes
abstract: ISO/IEC 15416 and 15415 define contrast ratio measurement conditions that were calibrated for laser-based scanners and do not fully represent the CCD-based imagers increasingly used in logistics. This study compared contrast ratio values for 90 printed QR code symbols measured under four illumination geometries (45°/0°, diffuse/8°, 30°/normal, and dark-field ring) combined with three spectral bandwidths (broadband white, 660 nm ± 10 nm bandpass, and 870 nm ± 15 nm bandpass). Symbols spanned four print quality grades and were printed flexographically on white BOPP film, uncoated kraft paper, and thermal-transfer label stock. Contrast ratio ranged from 0.44 to 0.91 across conditions for the same physical symbol, with dark-field ring illumination systematically inflating values on embossed substrates by 0.08–0.14 units relative to 45°/0°. Correlations between measurement geometry and actual first-read-rate on three industrial imager models are reported, supporting geometry selection recommendations for in-line verification systems.

title: Optimizacija parametara plazma predtretmana atmosferskim pritiskom za štampu na polietilenskim folijama niiske površinske energije
abstract: Ispitan je uticaj parametara DBD (dielektrično barijernog pražnjenja) plazma tretmana atmosferskim pritiskom — frekvencije (5–25 kHz), brzine transporta folije (2–20 m/min) i razmaka elektroda (1–3 mm) — na kvašljivost i površinsku energiju LDPE folije debljine 80 µm. Eksperimentalni plan je postavljen prema Box–Behnken dizajnu sa 15 eksperimenata. Odzivna veličina bila je totalna površinska energija izračunata OWRK metodom. Optimalni uslovi (18 kHz, 5 m/min, razmak 1,5 mm) dali su površinsku energiju od 46,2 mN/m u poređenju sa netretiranom vrednošću od 31,4 mN/m. Uz optimalne uslove plazma tretmana, adhezija vodene fleksografske boje na bazi akrilata poboljšana je sa ocene 4 na ocenu 0 po ISO 2409. ATR-FTIR spektri potvrdili su povećanje koncentracije karbonilnih i hidroksilnih grupa na površini.

title: Effect of nip pressure on toner penetration depth in uncoated papers of varying formation
abstract: Nip pressure was varied between 1.5 and 4.5 bar in 0.5 bar steps on a laboratory fuser rig to investigate toner penetration depth in uncoated papers characterised by three distinct formation levels (assessed by transmitted-light image analysis with a formation tester). Penetration depth was determined from cross-sectional SEM images of cryo-fractured samples; at least 25 measurement sites per sample were evaluated. Results showed that penetration depth increased with pressure on all substrates, reaching 8.3 µm at 4.5 bar for the most openly formed paper compared with 3.1 µm for the most uniform formation at the same pressure. Papers with irregular formation showed significantly higher variance in penetration depth (standard deviation up to 2.9 µm) compared with uniform formation papers (0.8 µm), implying localised adhesion variability. Pearson correlation between formation coefficient and penetration variance was r = 0.91. The data suggest that formation uniformity should be included as a substrate specification parameter for electrophotographic specialty applications.

title: Effect of aluminium layer thickness on the retroreflective brightness of hot-embossed holographic security labels
abstract: Hot-embossed holographic labels intended for document authentication are commonly metallised with aluminium by physical vapour deposition. This study investigates how aluminium layer thickness—varied from 20 nm to 120 nm in 20 nm steps—affects zero-order reflectance, first-order diffraction efficiency, and perceptible colour shift as measured by a calibrated spectrophotometer under D65 illumination. Samples were prepared on polyester film with a 1200 lines/mm sinusoidal grating master. Reflectance at 550 nm increased monotonically from 28 % to 71 % as thickness grew from 20 to 80 nm, plateauing thereafter. First-order efficiency peaked at 60 nm aluminium (23.4 %) and declined above 80 nm owing to increased specular reflection. SEM cross-sections confirmed conformal coverage at all thicknesses above 40 nm. Colour gamut area in CIELAB for the rainbow-shift zone was maximised at 60 nm. Results suggest that the common industrial practice of depositing 80–100 nm aluminium for brightness optimisation sacrifices diffraction colour performance by up to 18 % relative to the optimal thickness.
venue: Surface and Coatings Technology

title: Degradation of diffraction grating security features under accelerated UV and humidity cycling: a quantitative study
abstract: Long-term stability of diffraction grating security features is critical for their reliable machine verification throughout a product's shelf life. Samples from three commercial label constructions—uncoated aluminium-on-PET, overcoated aluminium-on-PET, and demetallised silver-on-BOPP—were subjected to accelerated ageing: 500 hours UV exposure at 0.89 W/m² per ISO 4892-2, and 20 cycles of 85 % RH / 10 % RH at 40 °C per IEC 60068-2-38. First-order diffraction efficiency, colour coordinates, and peel adhesion were measured at 0, 100, 250, and 500 hours. Uncoated aluminium samples lost 28 % efficiency after 500 UV hours while overcoated samples lost only 6 %. Humidity cycling caused adhesion reduction of 19–35 % in all constructions but no measurable grating groove degradation by AFM. A linear degradation model fitted to efficiency versus dose predicted service life at 10 % efficiency loss threshold of 3.2 years for uncoated and 14.7 years for overcoated constructions under Central European outdoor ambient conditions.

title: Mitochondrial calcium accumulation during simulated ischaemia in isolated rat ventricular cardiomyocytes
abstract: We examined the kinetics of mitochondrial calcium ([Ca2+]m) accumulation during simulated ischaemia using the fluorescent indicator Rhod-2 AM in freshly isolated adult rat ventricular cardiomyocytes. Cells were subjected to 30 minutes of metabolic inhibition (2-deoxyglucose plus sodium azide) followed by 20 minutes of washout. [Ca2+]m rose progressively during metabolic inhibition, reaching approximately 3.4-fold above baseline by minute 25, and increased further by 1.8-fold during the first 10 minutes of washout before partial recovery. Cytosolic calcium ([Ca2+]c) measured simultaneously with Fluo-4 AM showed an earlier and steeper rise. Pharmacological inhibition of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter with ruthenium red (10 µM) attenuated [Ca2+]m accumulation by 61% and reduced cell death assessed by propidium iodide exclusion from 54% to 29%. These findings establish a temporal dissociation between cytosolic and mitochondrial calcium loading and confirm the uniporter as a significant route of mitochondrial calcium entry under these conditions.

title: Cyclosporin A reduces infarct size in the Langendorff rat heart by delaying mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening at reperfusion
abstract: The mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opens at the onset of reperfusion and is a key determinant of cell death. We tested whether cyclosporin A (CsA), an mPTP inhibitor acting through cyclophilin D, reduces infarct size in an ex vivo rat heart model. Isolated Sprague-Dawley rat hearts were perfused in Langendorff mode, subjected to 35 minutes of regional ischaemia by left anterior descending artery ligation, and reperfused for 120 minutes. CsA (0.2 µM) or vehicle was administered for 5 minutes before reperfusion. Infarct size, measured by triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining, was reduced from 42 ± 5% of the area at risk in controls to 24 ± 4% in CsA-treated hearts (p < 0.01, n = 8 per group). Mitochondrial swelling assay on isolated cardiac mitochondria confirmed that CsA delayed calcium-induced swelling onset by approximately 90 seconds at equivalent calcium loads. Haemodynamic recovery, assessed by left ventricular developed pressure, was also improved in treated hearts.

title: Superoxide production at complex I and complex III during cardiac reperfusion: contribution to mPTP activation
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated at the onset of reperfusion are thought to promote mPTP opening, but the relative contributions of mitochondrial electron transport chain complexes I and III remain debated. We used MitoSOX Red fluorescence to measure superoxide production in permeabilised rat cardiomyocytes following reoxygenation after 20 minutes of anoxia. Selective inhibition of complex I with rotenone (1 µM) reduced superoxide signal by 48% compared with vehicle-treated reoxygenated cells, while the complex III inhibitor stigmatellin (1 µM) reduced it by 31%. Combined inhibition reduced the signal by 67%. mPTP opening, monitored by calcein-cobalt quench, was delayed by 38% with rotenone and by 22% with stigmatellin alone. These data suggest complex I is a quantitatively larger source of reperfusion ROS in this model. Antioxidant treatment with MitoTEMPO (10 µM) recapitulated the combined inhibitor effect on mPTP opening and reduced cell death to a similar extent.

title: Expression of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex subunits in rat myocardium following repeated ischaemic preconditioning
abstract: Ischaemic preconditioning (IPC) is a powerful cardioprotective intervention, but its effects on the molecular machinery of mitochondrial calcium uptake are not fully characterised. We applied three cycles of 5-minute ischaemia and 5-minute reperfusion to isolated rat hearts and then assessed expression of MCU, MICU1, MICU2, and EMRE by western blotting and quantitative real-time PCR in ventricular tissue harvested at 30 minutes after the preconditioning protocol. MCU protein expression was unchanged (0.98-fold, p = 0.78), while MICU1 protein increased 1.6-fold (p = 0.03) and MICU2 increased 1.4-fold (p = 0.04) relative to non-preconditioned controls. EMRE expression was unaltered. At the mRNA level, MICU1 transcript was elevated 2.1-fold. These findings suggest that IPC acutely upregulates the gatekeeping subunits MICU1 and MICU2, potentially raising the calcium threshold for uniporter activation and thereby reducing mitochondrial calcium overload during subsequent index ischaemia.

title: Mitochondrial permeability transition in ageing rat cardiomyocytes: calcium threshold and matrix swelling kinetics
abstract: Ageing is associated with increased susceptibility to ischaemia-reperfusion injury, but whether this reflects intrinsic changes in mPTP properties is unclear. We compared mPTP characteristics in cardiac mitochondria isolated from young (3-month) and aged (24-month) male Wistar rats. Calcium retention capacity, measured fluorimetrically with Calcium Green-5N, was 37% lower in aged mitochondria (198 ± 18 nmol Ca2+/mg protein vs. 315 ± 22 nmol Ca2+/mg protein, p < 0.001, n = 9 per group). Swelling amplitude at equivalent calcium challenge was 1.5-fold greater in aged preparations. Cyclophilin D content, assessed by western blot, was elevated 1.9-fold in aged hearts. Partial knockdown of cyclophilin D with siRNA in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes rescued the low-calcium threshold phenotype, confirming that cyclophilin D upregulation contributes mechanistically. These data provide a cellular basis for the age-dependent increase in infarct size observed in our Langendorff model.

title: Mitochondrial calcium handling and cardioprotection: mechanisms and open questions
abstract: This chapter reviews the current understanding of mitochondrial calcium uptake and release pathways in the heart, with emphasis on their roles in ischaemia-reperfusion injury and cardioprotective interventions. The mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex, the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchanger, and the mPTP are discussed as an integrated system. Key experimental findings from cell, isolated organ, and in vivo models are summarised, including the effects of genetic manipulation of MCU and cyclophilin D. The chapter also discusses unresolved questions: the structural identity of the mPTP pore-forming unit, species differences in uniporter kinetics, and the translation of laboratory cardioprotection to clinical settings. Evidence from human myocardial biopsy studies and clinical trials of CsA in acute myocardial infarction is critically assessed. The chapter is intended for graduate students and researchers entering the field.

title: Real-time imaging of mitochondrial permeability transition in single living cardiomyocytes using a dual calcein-TMRM protocol
abstract: Simultaneous monitoring of mPTP opening and mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) in the same cardiomyocyte enables direct correlation between these two events during ischaemia-reperfusion. We describe and validate a protocol using calcein-AM (retained in mitochondria until pore opening) combined with tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester (TMRM, a ΔΨm indicator) in isolated adult rat cardiomyocytes imaged by confocal microscopy during simulated ischaemia-reperfusion. In 74% of cells (n = 112), calcein loss from mitochondria coincided within one imaging frame (30 s) with collapse of TMRM fluorescence at reperfusion. In 21% of cells, ΔΨm collapsed before detectable calcein release, and in 5%, calcein release preceded ΔΨm collapse. CsA treatment (0.2 µM) delayed the coincident event by a median of 4.5 minutes and reduced the fraction of cells undergoing transition within 20 minutes of reperfusion from 68% to 31%. The protocol provides a reproducible tool for pharmacological screening in single cardiomyocytes.

title: Effect of diabetes mellitus on mitochondrial calcium uptake and mPTP sensitivity in rat ventricular myocytes
abstract: Diabetic hearts are more vulnerable to ischaemia-reperfusion injury, and impaired mitochondrial calcium handling may contribute. We used streptozotocin-induced type 1 diabetic rats (8 weeks post-injection, fasting glucose > 20 mmol/L) to assess [Ca2+]m uptake kinetics and mPTP sensitivity. Mitochondrial calcium uptake rate, measured in permeabilised cardiomyocytes with Rhod-2, was reduced by 34% in diabetic animals compared with controls, consistent with reduced MCU expression (western blot: 0.67-fold, p = 0.01). Paradoxically, calcium retention capacity was also reduced (234 ± 21 vs. 312 ± 19 nmol/mg protein, p < 0.001), indicating increased mPTP sensitivity despite slower uniporter-mediated uptake. Cyclophilin D was elevated 1.7-fold. Under simulated ischaemia-reperfusion in Langendorff hearts, infarct size was 55 ± 6% in diabetic vs. 40 ± 5% in controls (p = 0.002). CsA partially reversed the increased vulnerability, reducing diabetic infarct size to 38 ± 5%.

title: Influence of magnesium supplementation on mitochondrial calcium overload and cell survival during cardiac ischaemia-reperfusion
abstract: Magnesium competes with calcium for uptake through the mitochondrial calcium uniporter and may limit mitochondrial calcium overload during ischaemia-reperfusion. We supplemented male Wistar rats with magnesium orotate (380 mg/kg/day orally) for four weeks before Langendorff ischaemia-reperfusion experiments. Infarct size was reduced from 44 ± 6% in controls to 31 ± 4% in supplemented animals (p = 0.004, n = 10 per group). Cardiomyocytes isolated from supplemented hearts showed 27% lower peak [Ca2+]m during simulated ischaemia-reperfusion and delayed calcein loss by approximately 6 minutes. Tissue magnesium content, measured by atomic absorption spectrometry, was elevated 1.3-fold in supplemented hearts. In an in vitro competition assay using isolated mitochondria, raising free Mg2+ from 0.3 to 1.0 mM reduced calcium uptake rate through the uniporter by 40% at sub-saturating calcium concentrations (200 nM), consistent with competitive inhibition. These findings support a mechanistic basis for magnesium-mediated cardioprotection.

title: Transcriptomic profiling of cardiac mitochondrial calcium handling genes following acute myocardial infarction in rats: a time-course study
abstract: We characterised the temporal gene expression response of components of the mitochondrial calcium handling system in rat hearts after acute myocardial infarction induced by permanent left anterior descending artery ligation. Left ventricular tissue from the infarct border zone was collected at 2, 6, 24, and 72 hours post-ligation and profiled by RNA sequencing (n = 5 per time point). MCU transcript levels were reduced by 52% at 24 hours and remained suppressed at 72 hours. MICU1 was transiently elevated at 6 hours (1.8-fold) before returning to baseline. NCLX (mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchanger) was upregulated 2.3-fold at 72 hours. Cyclophilin D mRNA increased progressively, reaching 2.7-fold at 72 hours. Pathway enrichment analysis linked the 24-hour time point to oxidative stress and mitochondrial fission gene clusters. These patterns suggest a coordinated transcriptional remodelling of mitochondrial calcium machinery beginning within hours of infarction.

title: Mitochondrial dynamics and mPTP: interaction between fission/fusion balance and pore opening in ischaemia-reperfused cardiomyocytes
abstract: Mitochondrial fission is promoted at reperfusion and has been associated with mPTP opening, but the causal direction of this relationship remains contested. We used Mdivi-1 (50 µM), a DRP1 inhibitor that reduces mitochondrial fission, in isolated adult rat cardiomyocytes subjected to 25 minutes of simulated ischaemia followed by 30 minutes of reperfusion. Mitochondrial morphology was quantified by confocal imaging of MitoTracker-labelled organelles using an automated aspect-ratio analysis. Mdivi-1 maintained elongated morphology in 61% of mitochondria vs. 23% in vehicle-treated cells. Calcein-cobalt quench assay showed that mPTP opening was delayed by a median of 8 minutes in Mdivi-1 treated cells and the fraction of cells completing transition within the 30-minute reperfusion window fell from 72% to 41%. CsA and Mdivi-1 together did not show additive protection beyond CsA alone (44% transition rate), suggesting convergent rather than independent mechanisms.

title: Differences in mitochondrial permeability transition pore susceptibility between male and female rat cardiomyocytes during simulated ischaemia-reperfusion
abstract: Female sex is associated with better recovery from myocardial ischaemia in experimental models, but the mitochondrial basis of this difference is not fully resolved. We compared mPTP opening characteristics in cardiomyocytes isolated from adult male and female Wistar rats using the calcein-TMRM dual-label confocal protocol. Calcium retention capacity in isolated mitochondria was 28% higher in females (n = 11) than in males (n = 11, p = 0.003). During simulated ischaemia-reperfusion, the fraction of cells completing mPTP opening within 20 minutes of reperfusion was 69% in males vs. 44% in females. Ovariectomy reduced female calcium retention capacity to male levels and abolished the difference in mPTP opening fraction. Oestradiol replacement in ovariectomised animals (subcutaneous 17β-oestradiol, 25 µg/kg/day for 2 weeks) restored calcium retention capacity and pore-opening latency to intact-female values. Cyclophilin D levels did not differ between sexes, suggesting that oestradiol acts through a pathway independent of cyclophilin D.

title: Selective inhibition of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter with a synthetic ruthenium compound reduces reperfusion injury without affecting baseline cardiac function
abstract: We evaluated Ru405, a synthetic mononuclear ruthenium complex synthesised at the University of Belgrade, as a selective MCU inhibitor with improved membrane permeability compared with classical ruthenium red. Binding selectivity was confirmed by surface plasmon resonance against recombinant MCU protein (KD = 38 nM) and by patch-clamp recordings in HEK293 cells overexpressing MCU. In isolated adult rat cardiomyocytes, Ru405 (500 nM) reduced [Ca2+]m peak during simulated ischaemia-reperfusion by 41% without altering resting cytosolic calcium or contractile amplitude under normal pacing. In Langendorff rat hearts, infarct size with Ru405 administered at reperfusion was 26 ± 4% vs. 43 ± 5% in vehicle controls (p < 0.001, n = 9 per group). Haemodynamic parameters at baseline were indistinguishable between treated and control hearts. These results support selective MCU inhibition as a strategy for limiting reperfusion injury with a favourable functional safety profile.

title: Preprint: MCU complex remodelling in human right atrial appendage correlates with susceptibility to post-cardiac surgery ischaemia-reperfusion: a pilot biopsy study
abstract: Translation of experimental mPTP and MCU findings to human cardiac tissue is limited by access to myocardial samples. We obtained right atrial appendage biopsies from 24 patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting at the Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases of Vojvodina. Biopsies were taken at the start of surgery before cross-clamp and processed for western blotting of MCU, MICU1, MICU2, and cyclophilin D, and for calcium retention capacity assay. Patients were stratified retrospectively by troponin I release at 12 hours post-surgery as a proxy for intraoperative ischaemia-reperfusion injury (high release: n = 11; low release: n = 13). High-release patients had lower pre-surgical MICU1 expression (0.71-fold, p = 0.04), lower calcium retention capacity (−31%, p = 0.009), and higher cyclophilin D (1.5-fold, p = 0.02). MCU expression did not differ. These preliminary data suggest pre-existing variation in mitochondrial calcium handling may predict vulnerability. Validation in a larger cohort is required.

abstract: Binarization of archival documents is complicated by ink fading, paper yellowing, and non-uniform lighting introduced during digitization. This paper evaluates five locally adaptive thresholding algorithms—Sauvola, Bernsen, Niblack, Wolf–Jolion, and a newly proposed gradient-weighted variant—on a corpus of 340 scanned pages from nineteenth-century municipal records held at the Archive of Vojvodina. The pages include both Latin and Cyrillic handwriting at resolutions of 300 and 600 dpi. Evaluation uses pixel-level F-measure and the DIBCO pseudo-F metric. The gradient-weighted approach achieves an average F-measure of 88.4 on the 600 dpi subset, outperforming Sauvola by 3.1 points on heavily foxed pages while remaining within 0.4 points on clean pages. Processing time per A4 page is approximately 1.2 seconds on a single CPU core. The annotated dataset and code are released publicly.
venue: Journal of Document Engineering and Archiving

title: A Comparative Study of Feature Extraction Approaches for Isolated Handwritten Character Recognition in Serbian Cyrillic
abstract: Recognizing isolated handwritten Cyrillic characters from forms scanned in municipal offices presents challenges due to wide writer variability and partial character touching. This study compares gradient histogram descriptors (HOG), Zernike moment features, and raw pixel intensity patches as inputs to an SVM classifier with an RBF kernel. A dataset of 18,400 isolated character images contributed by 92 writers is constructed and partitioned into 80/20 train–test splits. HOG at a cell size of 8×8 pixels combined with a one-vs-one SVM yields 94.7% accuracy across 30 Cyrillic character classes, compared with 91.2% for Zernike moments and 88.9% for raw patches. Error analysis shows that confusion is concentrated among visually similar pairs such as З/З and Н/И. The dataset is deposited with the Serbian Language Resources Consortium.

title: Text Line Segmentation in Mixed-Script Handwritten Documents Using Projection Profiles and Seam Carving
abstract: Documents from the multilingual administrative tradition of the former Austro-Hungarian territories in Vojvodina often contain pages with text alternating between Latin, Cyrillic, and Hungarian scripts written by different hands. Text line segmentation in such documents is complicated because standard horizontal projection profiles fail when lines are skewed or when inter-line spacing is irregular. This work combines coarse segmentation via Hough-transform-based skew correction with a seam carving step guided by a trained pixel-level classifier that distinguishes text pixels from background. Experiments are performed on 120 double-column pages from three different collections. The proposed pipeline achieves a line detection rate of 91.3% at an IoU threshold of 0.5, compared with 84.7% for projection-only baselines. Failure cases are concentrated at page boundaries and around large decorative initials.

title: Script Identification in Bilingual Vojvodina Administrative Documents: Latin vs. Cyrillic
abstract: Automatic script identification is a prerequisite for routing document images to script-specific OCR engines. This paper addresses Latin–Cyrillic discrimination in word images extracted from scanned Vojvodina government documents spanning 1919–1990. Thirty-two texture and morphological features are computed per word image and fed to a random forest classifier trained on 9,600 word samples. The classifier achieves 97.1% accuracy on a held-out test set of 2,400 samples. Performance degrades to 93.4% on words shorter than four characters and on words containing numerals. A post-processing step using a language model trained on a trigram corpus of Serbian and Hungarian text raises overall accuracy to 97.9% by resolving ambiguous short words through their contextual neighbours. The system is integrated into the document processing workflow of a regional archive.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Word-Level OCR Confidence Estimation in Degraded Document Images
abstract: OCR engines typically output a confidence score per character, but word-level confidence is often inaccurate for degraded scans where ink bleed-through and partial occlusion affect multiple adjacent characters simultaneously. This paper trains a small convolutional network (five layers, approximately 420K parameters) to predict word-level OCR accuracy directly from the word image patch, independent of the OCR engine's internal score. Training uses 44,000 word patches derived from documents where ground truth transcriptions are available, with the binary cross-entropy loss between predicted and actual character error rate at word level. On a held-out test set of 8,800 patches, the CNN confidence correlates with actual word accuracy at Spearman ρ = 0.71, compared with ρ = 0.58 for the Tesseract 4 built-in confidence. The model is useful for selective human post-correction workflows where only low-confidence words are flagged for review.

title: End-to-End Handwritten Word Recognition for Low-Resource Scripts Using Transfer Learning from Latin Pre-Trained Models
abstract: Training sequence-to-sequence handwritten text recognition models from scratch requires large annotated corpora that do not exist for many scripts used in Serbian and Macedonian historical records. This paper investigates transfer learning from an LSTM-CTC model pre-trained on 800,000 Latin handwritten word images (drawn from the IAM and RIMES datasets) to target tasks in Serbian Cyrillic and Macedonian Cyrillic with training sets of only 3,200 and 1,800 word images respectively. Systematic ablation over which network layers to freeze shows that freezing the first two convolutional layers and fine-tuning the remaining layers gives the best trade-off: character error rates of 8.3% and 11.7% on the two target scripts, compared with 14.1% and 18.9% for models trained from scratch. Results confirm that visual feature representations transfer across scripts with distinct grapheme inventories.

title: Document Layout Analysis for Multi-Column Historical Newspapers Using Region-Based Convolutional Networks
abstract: Digitized newspapers from the Vojvodina region printed between 1900 and 1950 contain variable numbers of columns, embedded advertisements, photographs, and ruled separators, making automated layout analysis difficult. This paper trains a Mask R-CNN model on 620 manually annotated newspaper pages to detect and classify six region types: article text, headline, advertisement, photograph, caption, and separator. The model achieves mean average precision (mAP) at IoU 0.5 of 81.4% across all region types on a test set of 155 pages. Article text and headline classes reach mAP above 88%, while advertisement regions, which vary most in shape, reach only 71.2%. An ablation study shows that augmenting the training set with artificially degraded copies (Gaussian noise, synthetic stains) improves mAP by 2.8 points on the most degraded test pages. The annotated dataset of 775 pages is publicly released.

title: Synthetic Degradation Augmentation for Training OCR Models on Real-World Scanned Forms
abstract: Government and banking forms digitized from physical archives frequently exhibit degradation artefacts—coffee stains, fold lines, rubber stamp over-printing, and partial ink fade—that reduce OCR accuracy significantly. This paper proposes a parametric degradation pipeline that generates synthetic copies of clean form images with controllable artefact injection. Fourteen degradation operators are defined, each with a documented parameter space calibrated by matching second-order statistics of real degraded scans using a held-out calibration set of 200 pages. A ResNet-based OCR model trained on synthetically degraded data and evaluated on 1,100 real degraded form images achieves a word accuracy of 83.6%, compared with 71.4% for the same model trained on clean data only. Mixing 30% real degraded samples into training raises word accuracy to 86.9%. The pipeline source code and calibration data are released.

title: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Overlapping Stamps and Seals in Scanned Identity Documents
abstract: Official stamps and seals in identity and travel documents frequently overlap with printed or handwritten text, complicating both human and automated reading. This paper frames stamp detection and segmentation as an instance segmentation problem and trains a YOLOv5-seg model on a dataset of 3,400 document image crops annotated with 7,800 stamp instances across four shape categories: circular, rectangular, oval, and free-form. A separate inpainting network (U-Net architecture) is subsequently applied to restore the text occluded by detected stamps. The combined pipeline reduces character error rate of OCR on stamp-occluded text regions from 31.7% to 14.3% on a test set of 680 crops. The privacy-sensitive identity document images used in training were obtained under a data processing agreement with a national printing authority and are not publicly released; only model weights are shared.

title: Benchmarking Transformer-Based OCR Architectures on a Multilingual Vojvodina Corpus
abstract: Transformer encoder–decoder architectures have become dominant in many sequence recognition tasks, yet their performance on multilingual document corpora mixing Latin, Cyrillic, and Hungarian text within a single page has not been systematically assessed. This paper introduces VojDoc-ML, a benchmark corpus of 4,200 annotated page images drawn from five archival collections representing the period 1880–1980. Four architectures are evaluated: TrOCR-base, TrOCR-large, a character-level Vision Transformer, and a hybrid CNN–Transformer baseline. Character error rates at page level range from 6.1% (TrOCR-large, clean pages) to 28.4% (CNN–Transformer baseline, severely degraded pages). Mixed-script pages consistently yield 4–7 percentage points higher CER than single-script pages across all models. The paper analyses failure modes and provides per-collection breakdowns. The VojDoc-ML corpus and evaluation scripts are publicly available.

title: Active Learning for Ground Truth Annotation of Historical Handwritten Text: A Cost-Benefit Analysis
abstract: Constructing ground truth transcription datasets for historical handwritten documents is expensive because it requires expert palaeographers. This paper evaluates four active learning query strategies—least confidence, margin sampling, entropy sampling, and core-set selection—for selecting which word images to send for human annotation within a fixed budget of 5,000 annotation units per iteration across five iterations. Experiments are conducted using a base HTR model trained on the VojDoc-ML corpus. Core-set selection reduces the annotation budget needed to reach a target CER of 12% by 34% relative to random sampling. Least confidence sampling performs similarly to random sampling, contradicting some prior findings, which the authors attribute to the high visual homogeneity within each archival collection. Palaeographer annotation time and cost per 1,000 words are also reported, providing a basis for project budgeting.

title: Printed Text Recognition on Business Documents with Inconsistent Typography: A Study Across Eight Fonts and Four Degradation Levels
abstract: Business documents such as invoices, delivery notes, and purchase orders produced by small enterprises in Serbia are frequently digitized on low-cost flatbed scanners and exhibit typography inconsistencies arising from dot-matrix and inkjet printers. This paper constructs a synthetic corpus of 22,000 business document images combining eight typeface families (four serif, four sans-serif) with four programmatically induced degradation levels (clean, light, moderate, heavy). A fine-tuned TrOCR-base model trained on this corpus reaches 97.3% word accuracy on clean text and 89.6% on heavily degraded text. An ablation removing typeface diversity from training causes a drop of 5.1 points on unseen fonts. The study also reports key–value pair extraction accuracy for six standard invoice fields, finding that extraction errors are dominated by OCR errors on numeric fields rather than by structural parsing failures.

title: Zero-Shot Script Identification Using Vision–Language Models: Experiments on a Four-Script Corpus
abstract: Vision–language models pre-trained on large web-scale datasets encode visual and textual representations that may generalize to script identification without script-specific fine-tuning. This paper evaluates three publicly available vision–language models—CLIP ViT-B/32, CLIP ViT-L/14, and a multimodal model based on LLaVA-1.5—on a four-script corpus containing Latin, Cyrillic, Hungarian Latin, and Arabic word images extracted from mixed-provenance documents. Under zero-shot prompting with script-name text anchors, CLIP ViT-L/14 achieves 84.2% word-level classification accuracy averaged across scripts, while LLaVA-1.5 with a short description prompt reaches 79.6%. Both lag behind a fine-tuned ResNet-50 baseline (96.1%) but require no annotated training data. Performance on Arabic drops to 71.3% for CLIP ViT-L/14, attributed to underrepresentation of Arabic document images in assumed pre-training data. Practical implications for rapid deployment in archival digitization projects are discussed.

title: Structured Information Extraction from Degraded Serbian Land Registry Documents Using a Multi-Stage Pipeline
abstract: Serbian land registry books (zemljišne knjige) from the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries are handwritten in a mixture of German and Serbian, use a specialized tabular layout with handwritten column entries, and survive in varying states of physical degradation. This paper presents a complete pipeline for structured extraction covering deskewing, binarization, table structure recovery, line segmentation, HTR transcription, and named entity parsing for parcel numbers, owner names, and surface areas. Each stage is evaluated independently and in cascade on a test set of 310 pages from three cadastral districts. End-to-end field-level extraction F1 reaches 73.8% for parcel numbers, 68.4% for owner names, and 81.2% for surface areas. Cascade error analysis shows that 61% of final extraction errors originate in the HTR stage, while table structure recovery accounts for 22%. The system is deployed in a pilot at a regional cadastral office.

title: Keyword-based categorisation of fault descriptions in low-voltage network maintenance logs
abstract: Maintenance logs generated by field technicians in electrical distribution networks are typically written in informal, abbreviated natural language and contain frequent domain-specific jargon. This study presents a rule-based keyword extraction pipeline applied to a corpus of 14,200 maintenance records collected over five years from a Serbian regional distribution operator. Records were pre-processed using a custom tokeniser that handles Serbian Latin transliteration and common abbreviations. A manually curated lexicon of 340 fault-related terms was compiled with input from three senior network engineers. The pipeline assigned each record to one of twelve fault categories, achieving a precision of 0.81 and recall of 0.76 on a held-out test set of 1,400 records annotated by two independent reviewers. Inter-annotator agreement reached a Cohen's kappa of 0.74. The analysis revealed that cable insulation degradation and connector corrosion together accounted for 38 percent of all categorised faults. The lexicon and annotation guidelines are made publicly available to support reproducibility.

title: Interrupt Response Time Characterisation of the Zephyr RTOS on Zynq-7000 SoC Across ARM and MicroBlaze Processing Elements
abstract: The Xilinx Zynq-7000 SoC integrates a dual Cortex-A9 processing system and a Xilinx MicroBlaze soft-processor instantiated in programmable logic. This study characterises interrupt response time for the Zephyr RTOS running natively on the Cortex-A9 and for a cross-compiled Zephyr image running on the MicroBlaze at 100 MHz. Both targets used identical application tasks and the same interrupt source—a hardware timer in PL—to ensure comparability. On the Cortex-A9, median interrupt latency was 1.2 µs with a 99th-percentile value of 3.8 µs. On MicroBlaze the corresponding values were 0.9 µs and 1.4 µs, reflecting the simpler pipeline and absence of speculative execution. Cache warm-up effects, GIC configuration on the A9 side, and the Zephyr device-tree binding for MicroBlaze interrupts are discussed in detail. The paper also documents the cross-compilation configuration required to produce a MicroBlaze ELF binary from the mainline Zephyr source tree.

title: Typological Survey of Earthen-Wall Dwellings in the Southern Fruška Gora Foothills
abstract: This study presents a systematic typological inventory of 214 surviving earthen-wall (nabijača and čerpič) dwellings recorded across 18 foothill settlements on the southern slopes of Fruška Gora. Fieldwork conducted in 2009 combined measured drawings, photographic documentation, and structured interviews with 47 elderly residents. Buildings were classified into five morphological subtypes based on wall construction technique, roof pitch, and courtyard arrangement. Analysis showed that 61 percent of surveyed structures had undergone partial modernisation incompatible with original fabric, while only 14 percent retained intact original features. The study established a baseline condition index used in subsequent monitoring campaigns and proposed a preliminary heritage significance ranking applicable to municipal spatial plans. Findings were cross-referenced with cadastral records dating to the interwar period. The paper argues that this building stock, largely absent from official heritage registers, constitutes a culturally significant but rapidly disappearing layer of regional identity.

title: Visitor Motivation and Heritage Perception at Three Restored Foothill Farmsteads: A Pilot Study
abstract: A questionnaire-based exit survey administered to 312 visitors at three municipally restored farmstead complexes near Irig and Beočin examined motivations for visiting, levels of perceived authenticity, and willingness to pay for guided interpretation. Data were collected over two summer seasons (2009–2010). Cluster analysis identified four visitor segments: culturally motivated day-trippers (38%), recreational visitors with incidental heritage interest (27%), diaspora returnees (19%), and school group participants (16%). Perceived authenticity scores were significantly higher at the site that had retained original construction materials than at the two sites that used concrete infill repairs, despite the latter receiving higher aesthetic ratings. Willingness to pay for interpretation services correlated with educational level and prior heritage tourism experience rather than with segment membership. The paper discusses implications for site presentation strategies at small-scale rural heritage attractions with limited operating budgets.

title: Land-Use Change and the Erosion of Traditional Settlement Morphology in the Srem Foothills, 1980–2010
abstract: Using historical aerial photographs, contemporary orthophoto imagery, and cadastral data, this paper quantifies land-use change in eight Srem foothill settlements over three decades. Total built-up area increased by an average of 34 percent across the study villages, driven primarily by new residential construction on former orchard plots. The proportion of plot footprints retaining traditional courtyard orientation decreased from 72 to 49 percent over the study period. Kernel density mapping revealed that heritage-significant vernacular structures are concentrated in a contracting inner core of each settlement, increasingly surrounded by incompatible construction. A spatial regression model identified plot size, proximity to a main road, and household income level as significant predictors of modernisation pressure. The paper recommends the delineation of morphologically sensitive zones in local spatial plans as a first-order conservation measure prior to heritage tourism development.

title: Heritage Routes as Frameworks for Dispersed Vernacular Architecture: Lessons from the Syrmian Wine-Road Corridor
abstract: This paper evaluates the Syrmian Wine-Road cultural route as a structuring mechanism for dispersed vernacular heritage sites that individually lack the critical mass to sustain independent visitor flows. The analysis draws on visitor counts, accommodation occupancy data, and interviews with 22 site managers and local tourism officers collected in 2012–2013. The route connected 31 points of interest across 90 kilometres, of which 11 involved vernacular farm or cellar complexes. Sites embedded in the route achieved an average of 2.8 times more annual visitors than comparable standalone sites, and 43 percent of visitors reported that the route itinerary had introduced them to sites they had not previously been aware of. Challenges identified include inconsistent signage, uneven site readiness, and a lack of coordinated interpretation. The paper proposes a readiness-assessment checklist for incorporating vernacular architecture sites into itinerary-based tourism products.

title: Adaptive Reuse of Vernacular Farmsteads for Rural Accommodation: Regulatory and Economic Barriers in Vojvodina
abstract: Based on 34 semi-structured interviews with farmstead owners, local government officers, and tourism entrepreneurs conducted in 2014, this paper examines the practical barriers preventing the conversion of heritage-significant vernacular structures into registered rural accommodation units in Vojvodina. Three categories of barrier were identified: regulatory (incompatibility between fire-safety requirements and earthen or timber construction), economic (high upfront restoration costs relative to projected revenues from a thin domestic market), and institutional (absence of advisory support for small owners navigating planning procedures). A cost-benefit model constructed for a representative 250-square-metre farmstead indicated that renovation to meet current standards would cost approximately 2.5 times the market value of the structure as agricultural property. The paper discusses subsidy mechanisms used in comparable Central European contexts and evaluates their transferability to the Serbian policy environment.

title: Intangible Heritage Associated with Vernacular Building Practices in Fruška Gora Villages: Documentation and Tourism Potential
abstract: This paper reports on the documentation of intangible heritage associated with earthen and timber vernacular construction in ten Fruška Gora foothill villages, based on oral history interviews with 29 informants aged 68–94 conducted in 2014–2015. Recorded material included seasonal construction calendars, names of specialist craftsmen and their tools, communal labour (moba) arrangements, and ritual practices marking the completion of a new house. Analysis identified 17 distinct craft knowledge elements, of which fewer than four are still actively practised. The paper discusses the tourism interpretation potential of craft demonstration programmes and assesses precedents from comparable initiatives in Slovenia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. It argues that intangible and tangible dimensions of vernacular heritage must be presented jointly to provide visitors with a coherent cultural narrative, and that recording oral testimony is urgent given the advanced age of remaining knowledge holders.

title: Condition Monitoring of Earthen-Wall Structures Over a Decade: Repeat Survey of the 2009 Baseline Cohort
abstract: A repeat structural condition assessment of 102 earthen-wall dwellings first surveyed in 2009 was carried out in 2017 using the same condition index protocol. Over the eight-year interval, 23 structures (22.5%) had been demolished, 19 had undergone partial or full cladding with cement render, and 11 had been abandoned without maintenance. Only 6 structures showed evidence of sympathetic repair using compatible earthen materials. The overall condition index for the surviving unaltered cohort declined by a mean of 1.4 points on the 10-point scale, with roof deterioration and rising damp identified as the primary drivers of decline. Statistical comparison of 2009 and 2017 scores using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirmed a significant deterioration trend. The paper updates loss-rate estimates and argues that the window for meaningful heritage tourism development based on authentic fabric is narrowing significantly, with roughly two decades of meaningful survival probable for the majority of the cohort under current conditions.

title: Community Attitudes toward Heritage Tourism Development in Three Foothill Villages: A Comparative Survey
abstract: A household survey of 286 permanent residents across three Fruška Gora foothill villages examined attitudes toward heritage tourism development, perceived benefits and costs, and willingness to participate in tourism-related activities. Questionnaires were administered door-to-door in 2017. Attitudes were predominantly positive but conditional: 74 percent of respondents supported tourism development in principle, yet 61 percent expressed concern about seasonal crowding and 48 percent about loss of residential character. Factor analysis of attitude items produced three interpretable dimensions: economic optimism, privacy concern, and cultural pride. Regression analysis showed that length of residence and ownership of a heritage-significant property were the strongest positive predictors of willingness to engage in bed-and-breakfast or craft demonstration activities. The comparative dimension revealed that the village with an existing, if small-scale, tourism presence displayed more differentiated and pragmatic attitudes than the two villages without prior tourism exposure.

title: Vernacular Architecture as a Component of Slow Tourism Products in the Fruška Gora National Park Buffer Zone
abstract: This book chapter examines the compatibility of vernacular architecture heritage with slow tourism principles in the buffer settlements of the Fruška Gora National Park, drawing on earlier fieldwork data and semi-structured interviews with six tour operators conducted in 2019. The chapter first characterises the surviving heritage stock in terms of spatial distribution, accessibility, and interpretation readiness. It then evaluates how three commercial slow-tourism itineraries marketed in 2018–2019 incorporated or ignored vernacular architecture sites, finding that while all three itineraries passed through relevant settlements, only one included any explicit reference to the built heritage. The chapter argues that the low visibility of vernacular architecture in packaged products reflects a deficit of interpretation materials and trained local guides rather than a lack of visitor interest. It concludes with a framework for embedding vernacular sites into multi-day slow-tourism programmes that combine walking, cycling, gastronomy, and craft encounters.

title: Photogrammetric Documentation of Endangered Vernacular Structures: A Low-Cost Protocol for Small Research Groups
abstract: This paper presents and evaluates a low-cost close-range photogrammetry protocol developed for the documentation of earthen and timber vernacular buildings in field conditions typical of foothill Vojvodina: uneven terrain, partially collapsed structures, and limited access for scaffolding. Sixteen buildings in four settlements were documented using a consumer-grade mirrorless camera and freely available structure-from-motion software. Point cloud densities, orthophoto resolutions, and processing times were recorded for each building. Mean facade orthophoto resolution of 4.2 mm/pixel was achieved at an average field time of 3.5 hours per structure and processing time of 6 hours on a mid-range desktop workstation. Results were compared against a subset of three structures documented simultaneously by a professional survey team using terrestrial laser scanning; geometric deviations were below 15 mm for 94 percent of check points. The protocol is presented as a practical baseline for research groups operating without large equipment budgets, with documented limitations regarding deeply shadowed surfaces and glossy renders.

title: Cross-Border Comparison of Heritage Tourism Valorisation Approaches for Traditional Rural Architecture: Vojvodina, Baranja, and Slavonia
abstract: This paper compares policy frameworks, funding instruments, and on-ground outcomes for the heritage tourism valorisation of traditional rural architecture across three administratively distinct regions sharing a common vernacular building tradition: Vojvodina (Serbia), Baranja (Hungary and Croatia), and Slavonia (Croatia). Data were gathered through document analysis of spatial plans and heritage registers, interviews with 18 heritage and tourism officials, and site visits to 24 identified best-practice or counter-factual cases in 2021–2022. The comparison reveals that Croatian Slavonia has advanced furthest in terms of formal listing and subsidy access, while Vojvodina has a more extensive surviving stock but weaker institutional support. The Hungarian Baranya/Baranja area presents a hybrid picture with stronger EU funding absorption but significant authenticity losses from inappropriate restoration. The paper draws on the comparison to formulate five transferable policy recommendations for accelerating valorisation in the Serbian context.

title: Tourists' Photographic Representation of Vernacular Architecture on Social Media: Content Analysis of Geotagged Images from Fruška Gora
abstract: This paper analyses 2,840 publicly accessible geotagged photographs posted to a major image-sharing platform between January 2019 and December 2022 by visitors to 14 Fruška Gora foothill settlements. Images were coded for subject matter, compositional framing, and textual tags using a coding scheme developed and tested by two independent coders (inter-rater reliability κ = 0.78). Vernacular architecture appeared as the primary subject in 18.3 percent of images and as a background element in a further 31.6 percent, making the built environment the most frequently photographed non-natural element in the dataset. Earthen-wall houses, wine cellars, and wooden gate structures were the three most frequently depicted building types. Semantic network analysis of user-generated tags revealed that vernacular buildings were most commonly associated with terms relating to autumn, tranquility, and authenticity rather than historical or architectural terminology. The paper discusses implications for destination communication and the design of on-site interpretation materials targeting social-media-active visitor segments.

title: Mapping Thermal Comfort Conditions in Earthen-Wall Vernacular Interiors: Implications for Heritage Interpretation and Visitor Experience
abstract: Earthen-wall vernacular structures in the Fruška Gora foothill zone are frequently described by residents and visitors as thermally comfortable, yet quantitative data on indoor climate conditions are scarce. This paper reports measurements of air temperature, relative humidity, and mean radiant temperature recorded at 15-minute intervals over one full year (2023–2024) in three unoccupied but structurally intact earthen-wall houses open to visitor access. Thermal comfort indices (PMV, PET) were calculated for each measurement point and compared against outdoor reference stations. Results confirmed a significant thermal buffering effect: interior temperatures remained within the 18–26 °C band for 78 percent of the year compared with 41 percent outdoors. Relative humidity fluctuations were strongly attenuated. The paper discusses how these measurable thermal qualities can be incorporated into heritage interpretation narratives as a tangible demonstration of the environmental intelligence embedded in vernacular construction, and considers visitor-comfort implications for scheduling guided visits.

title: Seasonal variation in GPS-tracked visitor behaviour across trail difficulty classes in a Serbian mountain park
abstract: Trails classified as easy, moderate, and difficult attract visitors with different physical activity profiles and respond differently to seasonal weather conditions. This study draws on GPS data collected in four seasons from 318 individual hikers in Kopaonik area managed recreation zones, complemented by simultaneous meteorological records. For each track, movement speed, elevation gain rate, pause frequency, and total horizontal range were calculated. Mixed-effects regression models tested the influence of trail class, season, group size, and daily temperature on each metric. Difficult trails showed the largest seasonal variation in use frequency, with summer use 4.6 times higher than winter use, whereas easy trails remained comparatively stable year-round. Speed on moderate trails dropped by an average of 0.4 km/h on days with air temperature above 28 °C. Pause frequency peaked in autumn across all trail classes, likely associated with foraging and photography behaviour. These patterns inform seasonal staffing and maintenance scheduling for park management bodies.

title: Outdoor thermal comfort and visitor behaviour in urban parks of Vojvodina: a multi-city study
abstract: Visitor behaviour and concurrent thermal comfort conditions were surveyed in five urban parks across Vojvodina (Novi Sad, Subotica, Zrenjanin, Sombor, Vršac) during summer 2018. Behavioural mapping recorded the number of park visitors, their activity level, and chosen microspot (sun, partial shade, full shade) every 30 minutes between 09:00 and 19:00 on 10 measurement days per city. Simultaneous microclimate measurements provided UTCI values at matched measurement points. Visitor counts declined sharply when UTCI exceeded 38 °C, with an average reduction of 42% compared to counts at UTCI 28–32 °C. Shaded benches near water features retained the highest visitor densities across all UTCI levels. Vršac park, which had the highest tree canopy density (61%), showed the smallest visitor decline under high UTCI. Results suggest that park design emphasising canopy closure and proximity to water significantly sustains outdoor recreation viability during heat periods.

title: Digital wayfinding tools and their uptake among cycling tourists in low-connectivity rural areas: a field experiment in Vojvodina
abstract: This study tested the usability and adoption of an offline-capable mobile wayfinding application on a 90 km cycling route in the Bačka region under conditions of intermittent mobile network coverage. A convenience sample of 94 volunteer cyclists was divided into a group using the application and a control group using printed maps. Route completion rates, deviation events recorded by GPS tracks, time spent at points of interest, and post-route satisfaction scores were compared between groups. Application users completed the route with 40% fewer unintended deviations and spent on average 22 minutes longer at heritage stops flagged in the app. Satisfaction scores for orientation were significantly higher in the application group (mean 4.3 vs. 3.6 on a 5-point scale; p < 0.01). However, battery consumption and unfamiliarity with smartphone operation were reported as practical barriers by approximately 15% of application group participants. The results are relevant for tourism technology providers and route managers considering digital tools for rural deployments.

title: Landscape sensitivity to wind erosion in the Deliblato Sands under current and projected climate conditions
abstract: A spatially distributed wind erosion sensitivity index was computed for the Deliblato Sands by combining four input layers: mean annual wind speed at 10 m from the ERA5 reanalysis downscaled to 1 km, fraction of bare sand derived from 2018 Sentinel-2 classification, topographic exposure computed from a 5 m lidar-derived DEM, and vegetation cover index from NDVI time series. Index values were aggregated to a 100 m grid and validated against a set of 38 field-identified sites of known activity status. Under the 2018 baseline, 8.3% of the reserve area showed high or very high sensitivity. The analysis was then repeated using bias-corrected temperature and precipitation projections from three regional climate model runs under the RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios for the 2041–2060 window. Under RCP8.5, the area of high sensitivity expanded by approximately 3.4 percentage points, driven largely by projected summer precipitation deficits reducing vegetation cover rather than by changes in wind speed. The index is operationally simple enough to be updated annually as new satellite data become available.

title: Sand dune forms and their geomorphic evolution at the Deliblato Sands: an educational field guide for undergraduate geomorphology courses
abstract: This book chapter presents a structured field guide for teaching aeolian geomorphology at the Deliblato Sands, designed for single-day undergraduate excursions. Seven stops are described, each linked to a specific landform type: barchanoid ridge, parabolic dune, deflation hollow, sand sheet, blowout, leeward sand apron, and stabilised dune with soil profile. For each stop the chapter provides a landscape photograph, annotated sketch map, set of observation tasks, and background text situating the form within the broader stabilisation history of the field. GPS coordinates are given for access points and viewpoints. The guide also includes a simplified chronology of afforestation interventions from 1895 to 2010, drawn from forestry district records. The chapter is intended as a companion to lecture materials on process geomorphology and can be adapted for secondary school groups with minor simplification. Field safety considerations specific to soft sand substrates and seasonal flooding in interdune corridors are addressed.

title: Cross-Border Comparison of Food-Tourism Integration in Spa Destinations: Serbia and Romania
abstract: This study compares how small spa towns in Serbia and Romania embed locally produced food into their destination offers, drawing on a mixed-method design applied during 2020 and 2021. On the Serbian side, Prolom Banja, Banja Koviljača, and Sijarinska Banja were selected; on the Romanian side, Băile Herculane, Covasna, and Vatra Dornei. Data collection combined tourist exit surveys (n = 614 total), food provision mapping, and interviews with 18 tourism operators. Romanian destinations showed significantly higher rates of formal inclusion of regional food products in accommodation menus (61 percent versus 38 percent in Serbia), which is attributed in part to EU rural development funding available to Romanian producers before 2021. Serbian destinations demonstrated stronger informal street-food culture around public park areas. The paper identifies three shared structural barriers: fragmented supply chains, seasonal workforce instability, and lack of cross-sector certification schemes.
