title: Envelope spectrum analysis for early-stage outer-race bearing defect detection under variable speed conditions
abstract: This paper investigates the application of envelope spectrum analysis to detect incipient outer-race defects in deep-groove ball bearings operating under variable shaft speeds between 600 and 2400 RPM. Experiments were conducted on a custom-built test rig with seeded defects of three severity levels introduced by electrical discharge machining. Vibration signals were acquired at 51.2 kHz using a piezoelectric accelerometer mounted on the bearing housing. A Hilbert transform-based envelope was computed after bandpass filtering in the resonance frequency band identified through spectral kurtosis. Fault characteristic frequencies were tracked using angular resampling to compensate for speed variation. Detection was evaluated on 240 test runs; the outer-race defect frequency was reliably identified at severity level 2 and above, with a false-alarm rate below 4%. The results confirm the viability of envelope analysis without order tracking hardware when angular resampling is applied post-hoc from a tachometer signal.

title: Comparison of empirical mode decomposition and wavelet packet transform for gearbox fault feature extraction
abstract: Gearbox tooth-surface fatigue and chipping faults produce non-stationary vibration signatures that challenge classical Fourier-based methods. This study compares empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and wavelet packet transform (WPT) for extracting fault-sensitive features from a two-stage helical gearbox test rig running at 1450 RPM under three load levels. Fourteen statistical features — including kurtosis, RMS, and energy ratio per sub-band — were computed from the intrinsic mode functions and wavelet packet nodes, respectively. A k-nearest neighbour classifier was trained and tested using stratified five-fold cross-validation on a dataset of 600 labelled acquisitions spanning healthy, pitting, and chipped-tooth conditions. WPT with a Daubechies-8 mother wavelet achieved 93.5% overall accuracy versus 87.2% for EMD-derived features, with the energy ratio from the third-level WPT nodes providing the most discriminative single feature. Misclassification was concentrated at low-load conditions for both methods.

title: Vibration-based bearing fault classification using support vector machines with RBF kernels on a low-cost MEMS accelerometer platform
abstract: Industrial deployment of bearing diagnostics requires sensor and computation costs compatible with high-volume machinery. This paper evaluates a MEMS accelerometer (±16 g, 12-bit ADC, 10 kHz bandwidth) as an alternative to laboratory-grade piezoelectric sensors for classifying four bearing conditions: healthy, inner-race fault, outer-race fault, and rolling-element fault. A support vector machine with radial basis function kernel was trained on time-domain and frequency-domain features extracted from 1024-sample windows. Training data were collected at 1200 and 1800 RPM; test data included a 900 RPM speed not seen during training. Classification accuracy on the MEMS sensor reached 89.1% overall, compared with 95.4% for a co-located piezoelectric reference sensor. The accuracy gap was largest for rolling-element faults (−9.3 pp) due to the MEMS unit's higher noise floor above 4 kHz. Practical thresholds for minimum defect size detectable by the MEMS sensor are quantified.

title: On-edge bearing fault detection with a convolutional neural network quantised for ARM Cortex-M4 deployment
abstract: Running inference for bearing diagnostics directly on a microcontroller eliminates the need for continuous data streaming to a central server, reducing latency and communication overhead. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) was designed to classify five bearing conditions from raw vibration windows of 2048 samples acquired at 25.6 kHz. The network was trained on 4800 labelled windows collected on a laboratory test rig, then quantised from 32-bit float to 8-bit integer using post-training quantisation. The resulting model (63 kB) was deployed on an STM32F4-based board. Inference time was 14.7 ms per window, and classification accuracy dropped by 1.8 percentage points compared with the floating-point baseline (94.6% versus 96.4%). Power draw during inference was measured at 38 mW. The study also reports sensitivity of accuracy to quantisation bit-width, showing that 8-bit suffices while 4-bit degrades performance by more than 6 pp.

title: Fault detection in permanent-magnet synchronous motor bearings using combined vibration and stator current signals
abstract: Vibration and stator current signals carry complementary information about bearing health in permanent-magnet synchronous motors. This study investigates sensor fusion of these two modalities for detecting outer-race and inner-race bearing faults at incipient and developed stages in a 2.2 kW PMSM under 25%, 50%, and 75% rated load. Features were extracted separately from each modality — RMS, kurtosis, and characteristic frequency amplitudes from vibration; sideband amplitudes around the supply frequency from current — and fused at the feature level before input to a random forest classifier. Fusion improved overall accuracy to 91.8% compared with 84.3% for vibration alone and 79.6% for current alone on a 480-sample test set. Gain was most pronounced at 25% load where vibration signal-to-noise ratio is lowest. The approach requires only a single additional current sensor if a vibration sensor is already present.

title: Dataset and benchmark for multi-speed bearing fault classification under realistic industrial noise conditions
abstract: Publicly available bearing fault datasets are typically acquired under controlled laboratory conditions with low ambient noise, limiting their representativeness. This paper presents a dataset of 14 400 vibration recordings collected on a test rig enclosed in a sheet-metal housing with a running air compressor as background noise source, representing a noise floor 12–18 dB higher than comparable open-bench datasets. Shaft speed was varied across nine levels from 500 to 2900 RPM; five fault classes were included. A benchmark evaluation of seven classifiers — Naïve Bayes, k-NN, SVM-RBF, decision tree, random forest, 1D-CNN, and a shallow LSTM — is reported. 1D-CNN achieved the highest accuracy at 91.2%, but the random forest reached 89.7% with significantly lower inference time. The dataset is made available for download under a CC-BY 4.0 licence. Baseline code is provided in Python.

title: Transfer learning for bearing fault detection across different machine configurations using domain adaptation
abstract: Machine learning models trained on one rotating machine configuration frequently perform poorly when applied to a different machine with different nominal vibration characteristics. This paper evaluates maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) domain adaptation for transferring a bearing fault classifier trained on a 4-pole induction motor test rig to two target machines: a 6-pole motor and a belt-driven spindle, both with different bearing types. Source-domain training used 3200 labelled samples; target domains provided 0, 10, and 50 labelled samples in three adaptation scenarios. With zero target labels, MMD adaptation improved accuracy from 61.4% (no adaptation) to 76.9% on the 6-pole target and from 54.1% to 70.3% on the spindle. With 50 target labels, accuracy reached 88.2% and 83.7% respectively. Results suggest that moderate unlabelled target data is sufficient for useful transfer when vibration frequency bands are partially overlapping.

title: Wireless sensor node with adaptive sampling for continuous bearing condition monitoring in multi-machine installations
abstract: Continuous high-rate vibration sampling across many machines is energetically and bandwidth-intensive. This paper presents a wireless sensor node design in which the sampling rate adapts between a low-power survey mode (1 kHz, 5 s per minute) and a full-rate diagnostic mode (25.6 kHz, triggered) based on a lightweight RMS threshold computed on-chip. The node uses a sub-GHz radio and a primary lithium battery. Field deployment covered eight conveyor-drive bearings in a food processing facility over 14 months. Battery life exceeded 18 months at the observed trigger rate. Three developing bearing faults were flagged by the node and confirmed by scheduled inspection, with lead times of 19, 31, and 44 days before audible symptoms appeared. One false positive occurred, attributable to a temporary increase in ambient floor vibration during facility maintenance.

title: Explainability of CNN-based bearing fault classifiers through gradient-weighted activation mapping on time-frequency inputs
abstract: Black-box neural network classifiers are difficult to validate for safety-relevant maintenance decisions. This study applies gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) to a 2D-CNN trained on short-time Fourier transform spectrograms to identify which time-frequency regions drive fault-class predictions for inner-race, outer-race, and cage faults in angular-contact bearings. The model was trained on 5600 spectrograms and achieved 94.1% five-fold cross-validated accuracy. Grad-CAM heat maps were generated for 200 correctly and 18 incorrectly classified test samples. For inner-race faults, activation concentrated consistently at the ball-pass inner-race frequency harmonic band, in agreement with analytical fault-frequency predictions. Outer-race activations were more distributed, correlating with sidebands rather than the carrier frequency. Misclassified samples showed activation in noise-dominated low-frequency regions, providing a diagnostic indicator for uncertain predictions. The results support Grad-CAM as a practical sanity-check tool for maintenance engineers.

title: Compact Snapshot Hyperspectral Sensor for On-Robot Plastic Waste Grasping in Unstructured Bins
abstract: Fixed conveyor-based NIR sorting systems cannot directly address bin-picking scenarios where objects are piled and stationary. This paper integrates a snapshot mosaic-filter hyperspectral sensor (16 spectral bands, 470–950 nm) with a collaborative robot arm for material-type-aware grasping of mixed plastic waste in a 400 × 400 mm bin. The sensor, mounted at the robot wrist, captures a full hyperspectral image in a single 8 ms exposure. A lightweight random forest classifier trained on 12 000 patch samples from 8 polymer classes achieved 88.6% per-patch accuracy; aggregated object-level predictions reached 94.1%. Grasp planning used a depth map from a co-registered structured-light sensor. In 200 pick-and-sort trials on a bin with 15–25 randomly placed objects, the system achieved 91.5% material-correct sorting with a cycle time of 4.2 s per object. Failure analysis identified gloss saturation and very small fragments below 15 mm as the main error sources.

title: Effect of ambient temperature variation on the long-term stability of robot kinematic calibration in uncontrolled workshop environments
abstract: Calibration of industrial robots is routinely performed in temperature-controlled metrology rooms, yet robots operate in workshops where ambient temperature may vary by 15°C or more across a day. This study quantifies the degradation in calibration validity caused by ambient temperature swings using field measurements from two robot installations in an automotive component workshop in Novi Sad over a 90-day monitoring period. A laser tracker and a network of 24 ambient and structural temperature sensors logged data at 15-minute intervals. Calibration accuracy, expressed as the deviation of measured TCP positions from commanded positions, degraded from an initial 0.15 mm RMS to 0.38 mm RMS on days with ambient swings exceeding 12°C. A correction lookup table indexed by ambient temperature reduced this drift to 0.17 mm without requiring a full recalibration pass. The study quantifies the recalibration interval as a function of allowable accuracy budget and expected ambient temperature range, providing practitioners with a dimensioning tool.
venue: International Journal of Machine Tools and Manufacture

title: Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Rolling Bearings: Training Data Requirements and Generalisation Across Operating Conditions
abstract: Recurrent neural networks with long short-term memory (LSTM) cells have been proposed for RUL prediction, but their practical data requirements are rarely quantified rigorously. This paper examines how many run-to-failure sequences are needed to train a reliable LSTM model, and how well a model trained at one operating condition generalises to others, using a dataset of 68 bearing run-to-failure sequences recorded at two speeds (1,200 and 1,800 rpm) and two radial loads (4 kN and 6 kN). Networks were trained on subsets ranging from 5 to 50 sequences. With 20 or more training sequences, mean absolute percentage error in RUL prediction stabilised near 14.3% at the 50% consumed-life mark. Cross-condition generalisation degraded performance to 22–28% MAPE when the training and test operating conditions differed, but a simple linear scaling of the health index by rated load and speed partially recovered accuracy to 17.1%. The study provides practical guidance for maintenance engineers considering LSTM-based prognosis tools.
venue: Journal of Intelligent Maintenance Systems

title: Comparison of time-domain AE features for estimating remaining useful tool life in intermittent milling
abstract: Intermittent milling introduces periodic AE bursts that complicate continuous wear tracking methods designed for steady-state cutting. This work evaluates seven time-domain features — RMS, variance, peak-to-peak amplitude, crest factor, kurtosis, skewness, and signal entropy — for their ability to estimate remaining useful tool life (RUL) during slot milling of X40CrMoV5-1 steel (50 HRC). Experiments were conducted on a Haas VF-2 at three feed-per-tooth levels (0.04, 0.07, 0.10 mm/tooth). Each of 18 tool runs was continued until VB exceeded 300 µm. Features were computed from 20 ms gating windows aligned to the cutting interval. A support vector regression model trained on six runs at each feed level achieved median RUL errors of 12.4% (0.04 mm/tooth) and 17.1% (0.10 mm/tooth), with entropy and kurtosis providing the highest individual predictive power. The study provides quantitative guidance for selecting time-domain features when frequency-domain analysis is computationally prohibitive.
venue: Journal of Manufacturing Processes and Systems

title: Spin-dependent conductance in Co/Cu multilayers measured by a modified van der Pauw technique
abstract: We report magnetoresistance measurements on Co/Cu multilayers grown by dc magnetron sputtering on thermally oxidised silicon substrates. Samples with Co layer thicknesses between 0.5 nm and 4 nm and Cu spacer thicknesses between 0.8 nm and 3.5 nm were characterised at temperatures from 10 K to 300 K. The van der Pauw method was adapted to account for the anisotropic in-plane resistivity arising from shape anisotropy in narrow rectangular mesas patterned by photolithography. Giant magnetoresistance ratios up to 18% were measured at 10 K, decreasing to 11% at room temperature for optimally spaced structures. Interlayer exchange coupling oscillation periods of approximately 1.1 nm in the Cu spacer were extracted from the field dependence of the magnetisation reversal. Temperature-dependent resistivity data were fitted to a two-current model incorporating magnon scattering, yielding spin-asymmetry coefficients consistent with earlier bulk scattering estimates for cobalt. The results establish a baseline for subsequent studies substituting heavy-metal underlayers beneath the ferromagnetic stack.

title: Ferromagnetic resonance linewidth and damping in Py/Pt bilayers as a function of Pt thickness
abstract: Gilbert damping enhancement due to spin pumping was investigated in Ni80Fe20 (Py)/Pt bilayers using broadband ferromagnetic resonance spectroscopy in the frequency range 4–18 GHz. Py thickness was held fixed at 8 nm while Pt thickness was varied from 0 to 10 nm. The frequency-dependent linewidth data were fitted to extract the effective Gilbert damping parameter α, which rose from 0.0075 for bare Py to 0.018 for Py(8 nm)/Pt(5 nm) before saturating, consistent with a spin-diffusion length in Pt of approximately 1.4 nm at room temperature. The spin-mixing conductance g↑↓ was determined to be 4.1 × 10^19 m−2. Control samples with a 2 nm Ta spacer between Py and Pt showed negligible damping enhancement, confirming that direct interfacial spin transmission drives the effect. These measurements provide interfacial parameters needed to model spin-orbit torque efficiencies in the same material stack.

title: Anomalous Hall effect as a probe of magnetisation state in Ta/CoFeB/MgO stacks
abstract: We characterise the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in Ta(5 nm)/Co40Fe40B20(1.2 nm)/MgO(2 nm)/Ta(2 nm) stacks deposited by magnetron sputtering, with the aim of using AHE resistance as an in-situ magnetisation state indicator during current-pulse switching experiments. Films were annealed at temperatures between 280 °C and 380 °C for 1 hour under a perpendicular field of 1.5 T; optimal perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was achieved after annealing at 320 °C, yielding a Hall angle of 0.21% and a coercive field of 48 mT. The AHE loop squareness exceeded 0.98, confirming homogeneous switching. Current-induced switching was tested in Hall bar devices of dimensions 10 × 2 µm2 patterned by electron-beam lithography. At a nominal current density of 7.5 × 10^11 A m−2, complete magnetisation reversal was observed under a 10 mT in-plane bias field. The critical switching current showed no significant dependence on pulse duration over the range 10 ns to 1 µs at room temperature.

title: Spin Hall angle determination in W and Ta underlayers by harmonic Hall voltage analysis
abstract: Second-harmonic Hall voltage measurements were used to separate field-like and damping-like spin-orbit torque components in W(t)/Co20Fe60B20(1.5 nm)/MgO heterostructures, where the W thickness t ranged from 2 to 8 nm. Both β-W and α-W phases were obtained by controlling the argon sputtering pressure; X-ray diffraction confirmed the phase composition. The effective spin Hall angle θ_SH was extracted following the standard harmonic analysis with careful correction for the planar Hall admixture. β-W layers yielded θ_SH values between −0.28 and −0.33, roughly three times larger in magnitude than those obtained from α-W reference samples. The anomalous Nernst contribution to the second-harmonic signal was estimated and found to be below 8% of the spin-torque contribution across all samples. Separate harmonic measurements on corresponding Ta underlayer devices gave θ_SH = −0.11 ± 0.02, consistent with published values. The results support β-W as the preferred underlayer for maximising torque efficiency in this geometry.

title: Interface oxidation effects on perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in Pt/Co/AlOx trilayers
abstract: The role of controlled over-oxidation at the Co/AlOx interface in determining perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) was studied in Pt(4 nm)/Co(0.6–1.6 nm)/Al(1.5 nm) stacks, where the Al layer was oxidised by exposure to a radio-frequency oxygen plasma for durations between 5 s and 120 s. Magnetic properties were assessed by vibrating sample magnetometry and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements. The interface anisotropy energy K_s peaked at an oxygen plasma exposure of approximately 25 s, reaching 1.35 mJ m−2 for Co thickness of 0.9 nm, before declining with prolonged oxidation due to cobalt oxide formation confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Spin-orbit torque switching experiments in Hall bar devices showed that PMA-optimised samples required 40% lower critical current densities compared with reference samples produced without plasma treatment. The findings point to the Co/oxide interface anisotropy as the dominant energy scale governing the switching threshold in this underlayer system.
venue: Journal of Magnetism and Magnetic Structures

title: Temperature dependence of spin-orbit torque efficiency in Pt/CoFeB/MgO from 50 K to 400 K
abstract: Spin-orbit torque efficiencies in Pt(5 nm)/Co40Fe40B20(1.2 nm)/MgO(2 nm) Hall bars were characterised between 50 K and 400 K using second-harmonic voltage analysis at 13.7 Hz with AC current densities of 5 × 10^10 A m−2. The damping-like torque efficiency ξ_DL increased monotonically from 0.09 at 400 K to 0.16 at 50 K, tracking the temperature dependence of the longitudinal conductivity of Pt. Field-like torque efficiency ξ_FL remained nearly temperature-independent at 0.03–0.04 across the full range. Magnetisation determined from anomalous Hall hysteresis loops showed a 12% reduction between 50 K and 400 K, with coercivity varying from 82 mT at 50 K to 31 mT at 400 K. A side-jump and skew-scattering decomposition suggested that intrinsic Berry-phase contributions dominate the damping-like component at low temperature while extrinsic scattering becomes increasingly relevant above 300 K. These results constrain device operating windows for memory applications at elevated temperatures.

title: Propagation of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-stabilised domain walls in Ta/CoFeB/MgO wires measured by Kerr microscopy
abstract: Domain wall velocities and creep exponents were measured in 500 nm-wide Ta(5 nm)/Co32Fe48B20(0.95 nm)/MgO(2 nm)/Ta(2 nm) wires as a function of applied in-plane longitudinal field and current density using time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy with 5 µs temporal resolution. In the creep regime, domain wall velocity followed a stretched-exponential field dependence with creep exponent µ = 0.25 ± 0.03, consistent with a one-dimensional disorder universality class. The effective Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) constant D was extracted by measuring the asymmetry of domain wall velocities driven by positive and negative out-of-plane fields combined with an in-plane bias, yielding D = 0.18 mJ m−2. Current-assisted depinning was demonstrated: a current density of 2 × 10^11 A m−2 reduced the effective depinning field by 14 mT. The measured DMI is sufficient to stabilise Néel walls but insufficient to nucleate isolated skyrmions under the present conditions, providing a boundary condition for stack engineering aimed at skyrmion-based storage.

title: Magnetic tunnel junctions integrated with spin-orbit torque write lines: switching voltage and retention trade-off
abstract: Three-terminal devices consisting of CoFeB(1.0 nm)/MgO(1.6 nm)/CoFeB(3 nm) magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJ) coupled to a Pt(5 nm) spin-orbit torque write channel were fabricated by combining magnetron sputtering, electron-beam lithography, and argon ion-beam milling. Tunnel magnetoresistance ratios of 130–145% were measured at room temperature following annealing at 330 °C for 1 h. Switching current densities in the Pt channel averaged 6.2 × 10^11 A m−2 under a 15 mT in-plane bias field. Retention was tested by measuring the thermal stability factor ∆ at 85 °C for 200 devices; the median ∆ was 42 ± 5, falling at the lower edge of the 10-year retention requirement. Increasing the free-layer CoFeB thickness to 1.3 nm raised ∆ to 57 but increased the switching current density to 8.1 × 10^11 A m−2, illustrating the retention–write-current trade-off. A simple macrospin model incorporating the torque asymmetry between parallel and antiparallel configurations accounted for the observed write-error-rate asymmetry within experimental uncertainty.
venue: Solid-State Electronics and Devices

title: Spintronics: principles and applications in memory and logic
abstract: This book chapter provides an account of the physical mechanisms underlying spintronic device operation, structured for advanced undergraduate and postgraduate students with a background in solid-state physics. It covers the origins of spin-dependent transport, the spin Hall effect and its relationship to band-structure topology, ferromagnetic resonance as a characterisation tool, and the transition from domain-wall-based to uniform-mode switching in scaled devices. Quantitative treatment is given to the macrospin Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation augmented by spin-transfer and spin-orbit torque terms, with worked examples drawn from Ta/CoFeB/MgO and Pt/Co/AlOx material systems. A final section surveys the state of integration of spin-orbit torque cells with standard back-end-of-line complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor processes, highlighting the constraints imposed by thermal budget, contamination control, and contact resistance. Illustrative data are drawn partly from the authors' own experimental work and partly from the open literature, with an emphasis on reproducible results verified across multiple laboratories.

title: Field-free spin-orbit torque switching driven by exchange bias in IrMn/CoFeB/MgO heterostructures
abstract: Elimination of the in-plane bias field required for deterministic spin-orbit torque switching was pursued by exchange-biasing the CoFeB free layer with an IrMn antiferromagnetic layer. Stacks of Pt(4 nm)/IrMn(8 nm)/Co32Fe48B20(1.1 nm)/MgO(2 nm)/Ta(2 nm) were deposited and field-cooled through the IrMn Néel temperature (~250 °C for this composition) under a 500 mT longitudinal field. Exchange bias fields H_EB between 18 mT and 34 mT were obtained depending on the IrMn deposition temperature. Hall bar devices demonstrated field-free switching at current densities of 7.8 × 10^11 A m−2, with switching probability exceeding 95% for pulse widths above 50 ns. Thermal stability of the exchange bias was tested by cycling devices between 25 °C and 100 °C; a 20% reduction in H_EB after 500 thermal cycles was observed, attributed to partial reorientation of antiferromagnetic grains below the blocking temperature distribution. The blocking temperature distribution was characterised by torque magnetometry, and strategies for improving thermal stability through IrMn grain size control are discussed.

title: Thickness-dependent spin-orbit torque and anomalous Hall effect in sputtered Pd/Co bilayers
abstract: Palladium is investigated as an alternative heavy-metal underlayer to Pt and W for spin-orbit torque applications. A series of Pd(t)/Co(1.0 nm)/MgO(2 nm) stacks with Pd thickness t from 1 nm to 12 nm was deposited by dc magnetron sputtering. The effective spin Hall angle extracted by harmonic Hall voltage analysis reached a saturation value of 0.07 ± 0.01 for t ≥ 6 nm, smaller than Pt but accompanied by a lower longitudinal resistivity (45 µΩ cm versus 110 µΩ cm for Pt), resulting in comparable charge-to-spin conversion efficiencies in absolute terms. Perpendicular magnetic anisotropy was confirmed for Co thicknesses up to 1.3 nm, with K_eff = 2.8 × 10^5 J m−3 at the optimum Pd thickness of 4 nm. First-principles estimates of the spin Hall conductivity for fcc Pd retrieved from an independent collaborator suggested a dominant intrinsic contribution. Anomalous Hall angle measurements as a function of longitudinal conductivity placed Pd/Co in the moderately clean regime of the scaling diagram. The results confirm that Pd is a viable, lower-resistivity alternative for applications where Joule heating is a concern.

title: Pulse-duration scaling of switching current density in Pt/CoFeB/MgO Hall bar devices
abstract: The dependence of switching current density J_sw on pulse duration τ was measured in Pt(5 nm)/Co40Fe40B20(1.2 nm)/MgO(2 nm) Hall bar devices for τ spanning five orders of magnitude from 1 ns to 100 µs. Measurements were performed at 300 K in the presence of a 12 mT in-plane bias field. For τ < 10 ns, the data followed a power-law relation J_sw ∝ τ^(−0.5), consistent with thermally assisted macrospin reversal governed by a single energy barrier. For longer pulses, J_sw approached a thermodynamic threshold current density of 2.9 × 10^11 A m−2. Pulse-width jitter introduced by the arbitrary waveform generator was characterised separately and deconvolved from the switching statistics. Write-error rates were mapped as a function of (J, τ) across a 5 × 5 grid of operating points; contours of constant write-error rate at 10^−3 and 10^−5 are reported. Comparison with a stochastic macrospin model including the Oersted field correction showed agreement within 15% across the full τ range, with the largest deviations occurring in the sub-nanosecond regime where ringing on the voltage pulse was most significant.

title: Orbital Hall effect contribution to torque in Cr/CoFeB heterostructures probed by vector network analyser ferromagnetic resonance
abstract: Recent theoretical predictions suggest that the orbital Hall effect in 3d transition metals can produce torques comparable to or exceeding those from the spin Hall effect. We investigate Cr(t)/Co40Fe40B20(1.2 nm)/MgO(2 nm) heterostructures with Cr thickness from 2 to 10 nm as a candidate system. Vector network analyser ferromagnetic resonance measurements in the range 3–20 GHz were used to extract the real and imaginary parts of the spin-mixing conductance as a function of Cr thickness. The effective damping-like torque efficiency derived from harmonic Hall measurements reached 0.05 ± 0.01, smaller than Pt but notable given the weak intrinsic spin Hall conductivity of Cr. A comparison between samples with and without a 0.5 nm Al spacer inserted to suppress direct spin transmission suggests that approximately 60% of the observed torque can be attributed to orbital-to-spin conversion at the Cr/CoFeB interface. The frequency shift of the ferromagnetic resonance with current also indicates a field-like orbital torque contribution with efficiency 0.03 ± 0.01. These results motivate further investigation of 3d-metal underlayers as low-resistivity torque sources.

title: Joule-heating-induced magnetisation dynamics during nanosecond current pulses in Pt/CoFeB/MgO
abstract: Self-heating during spin-orbit torque switching pulses is known to modify effective anisotropy and coercivity, yet the magnitude of the effect on nanosecond timescales remains poorly quantified experimentally. We use the temperature dependence of the anomalous Hall resistance as an in-situ thermometer to track the mean device temperature during and after current pulses of duration 1–100 ns in Pt(5 nm)/Co40Fe40B20(1.2 nm)/MgO(2 nm) Hall bars. Estimated peak temperatures for a current density of 10^12 A m−2 reached 380 K in 100 ns pulses but only 315 K in 5 ns pulses, indicating that the ferromagnetic layer is in substantial thermal non-equilibrium with the substrate during short pulses. Finite-element thermal modelling with independently measured thermal boundary resistances at the Pt/SiO2 interface reproduced the measured temperature transients to within 8%. The thermally modified anisotropy field reduced the effective switching current density by 12% in long pulses compared with short pulses, an effect that a purely athermal macrospin model overestimates the required current for 100 ns pulses. Recommendations for derating device current specifications to account for self-heating are provided.

title: Temperature-dependent Mössbauer study of synthetic Al-substituted goethite as a reference for palaeosol studies
abstract: Synthetic goethite samples with Al/(Al+Fe) molar ratios of 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 were prepared by co-precipitation and characterised by X-ray diffraction, BET surface area measurements, and ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy at temperatures between 4.2 K and 295 K. The Néel temperature decreased from 395 K for pure goethite to 318 K for the 20 mol% Al-substituted sample, tracking the linear trend reported in earlier literature. Hyperfine field distributions extracted by Voigt-based fitting at 4.2 K showed increasing asymmetry with Al content, with the peak field dropping from 50.1 T to 46.7 T across the series. Unit-cell parameters from Rietveld refinement contracted along the b-axis by 0.021 Å across the substitution range. A calibration table linking peak hyperfine field at 4.2 K to Al substitution was compiled and is intended to improve quantitative interpretation of Mössbauer spectra from natural palaeosol goethites. Uncertainty estimates account for particle-size effects on magnetic relaxation.

title: Iron oxide speciation across MIS 5–7 in a Romanian loess section: Mössbauer and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy comparison
abstract: A 12-metre section from a quarry exposure near Turnu Măgurele, southern Romania, spanning marine isotope stages 5 to 7 was sampled at 10 cm intervals, yielding 120 specimens. Transmission ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectra at 300 K and 130 K were acquired and fitted; results were compared with Fe-oxide estimates derived independently from diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) using the second-derivative method. Mössbauer-derived haematite proportions correlated with DRS haematite (r = 0.83, n = 120, p < 0.001), while goethite agreement was weaker (r = 0.61), likely because fine-grained superparamagnetic goethite contributes to the DRS signal but is not fully resolved as a sextet at 130 K. Combined use of both methods reduced misclassification of ferrihydrite-rich horizons near palaeosol bases. The MIS 6 glacial shows a distinctly low Gt/Hm ratio (0.6 ± 0.15) relative to MIS 7 (2.4 ± 0.3), correlating with a documented arid episode in central-eastern Europe and consistent with regional pollen records.

title: Electrowetting manipulation of droplets generated on-chip: integration of co-flow generation with a downstream EWOD transport rail
abstract: This paper describes the integration of a glass co-flow droplet generator with a downstream planar EWOD transport section on a single chip. Droplets of 0.5–2 µL aqueous dye solution were produced at the co-flow junction at rates of 2–15 Hz and transferred without external handling to the EWOD section, where they were transported, split, and directed to designated reservoirs. Transfer success rate exceeded 94 % at generation frequencies below 8 Hz but decreased to 78 % at 12 Hz due to timing jitter between the generator and the electrode control logic. A custom timing circuit reduced this jitter to less than 5 ms, restoring the success rate to 91 % at 12 Hz. Droplet volume was conserved through transport and splitting to within 4 %. Dead volume at the junction between the two sections was reduced from 3.2 µL to 0.6 µL by redesigning the channel-to-electrode transition geometry.

title: Positron annihilation characterisation of thermally aged versus neutron-irradiated 15Kh2MFA chromium–molybdenum–vanadium steel
abstract: 15Kh2MFA Cr–Mo–V steel, used in VVER-440 reactor pressure vessels, was studied in three conditions: (i) reference as-received, (ii) thermally aged at 350 °C for 10,000 hours under no irradiation, and (iii) neutron-irradiated to 2×10^19 n/cm² at 270 °C. Positron lifetime spectra were fitted with three components for irradiated and aged specimens. The as-received material showed a single lifetime of 113 ps. Thermal ageing produced a weak second component at 155 ps with an intensity of 6%, attributed to small dislocation-associated vacancy clusters. Irradiation produced a stronger second component at 195 ps (intensity 22%) and a third at 385 ps (intensity 4%), consistent with mono-to-di vacancy complexes and vacancy clusters of size 8–12 vacancies respectively. The chromium–vanadium carbide precipitate network, confirmed by TEM in the aged samples, apparently acts as a competing positron trap distinct from radiation-induced vacancy clusters. Comparison between the two ageing mechanisms is relevant to lifetime extension assessments for operating VVER reactors.
venue: Journal of Nuclear Engineering and Radiation Science

title: Permeability prediction from NMR T2 distributions in Neogene aquifer sands of northern Vojvodina
abstract: Hydraulic permeability of twelve unconsolidated to weakly consolidated Neogene sand samples from water-supply boreholes in northern Vojvodina was estimated using three NMR-based models: Timur–Coates, SDR (Schlumberger–Doll Research), and a locally calibrated power-law model linking geometric mean T2 to permeability. Grain-size analysis and constant-head permeameter measurements provided reference data. The locally calibrated model (k = 0.043·T2gm^2.1·φ^4.2, k in mD, T2gm in ms, φ dimensionless) outperformed both Timur–Coates and SDR, reducing root-mean-square log error from 0.68 and 0.54 to 0.31 log-cycle units respectively. Disagreement was largest for samples containing more than 8% silt, where T2 distributions showed a significant fast-relaxing shoulder. The calibrated model was applied to continuous NMR logs from two exploration boreholes, producing permeability profiles consistent with step-drawdown pumping test intervals.

title: NMR relaxometry as a proxy for specific surface area in geothermal reservoir rocks: a case study from southern Pannonian Basin
abstract: Five drill-core samples from a geothermal exploration well in southern Vojvodina (measured bottom-hole temperature 87 °C) were characterised by NMR T2 relaxometry, BET nitrogen adsorption, and mercury injection capillary pressure. Specific surface area derived from NMR using a fixed surface relaxivity of 5 µm/s agreed with BET values within 25% for quartz-dominated samples but overestimated BET area by a factor of 2.3 in a zeolite-altered tuffaceous sample. Recalibrating ρ₂ individually for each lithology reduced the NMR–BET discrepancy to below 15% across all samples. Pore-size distributions from NMR and mercury injection showed consistent modal radii for pores larger than 0.1 µm; NMR missed pore throat information below this size accessible to mercury at pressures above 100 MPa. The study suggests NMR is adequate for macro- and mesopore characterisation in geothermal reservoirs of the region but requires lithology-specific ρ₂ calibration.

title: Time-resolved OES of pulsed DC glow discharges in N2–H2: species evolution during and after the voltage pulse
abstract: Time-resolved optical emission spectroscopy with 5 μs gate width was applied to a pulsed DC glow discharge in 70% N2 / 30% H2 at 4 mbar. Pulse repetition frequency was varied from 5 to 100 kHz and duty cycle from 25% to 75% at a peak voltage of 550 V. Emission intensities of N2 (C→B, 337 nm), N2+ (B→X, 391 nm), NH (A→X, 336 nm), and Hα (656 nm) were recorded as functions of time within the pulse period. During the on-phase, N2+ emission reached a maximum within 15 μs and then declined, while NH emission peaked later at approximately 35 μs, consistent with a two-step formation mechanism via N atoms and H radicals. In the off-phase, N2+ emission collapsed within 10 μs, whereas NH persisted for up to 80 μs, indicating a neutral radical reservoir. At 50 kHz and 50% duty cycle the time-averaged nitrogen uptake rate was 14% higher than for equivalent DC operation at the same mean power, attributed to enhanced atomic nitrogen availability during afterglow periods.
venue: Plasma Chemistry and Plasma Processing

title: Comparison of continuous and intermittent negative pressure wound therapy in Wagner grade 2 and 3 diabetic foot ulcers: a pilot randomised controlled trial
abstract: Negative pressure wound therapy is widely used in diabetic foot ulcer management, but the optimal delivery mode—continuous versus intermittent—remains debated, and evidence from Central and Eastern European clinical settings is limited. This single-centre pilot randomised controlled trial allocated 44 patients with Wagner grade 2 or 3 ulcers to continuous NPWT at −125 mmHg or intermittent NPWT cycling between −125 mmHg and 0 mmHg at five-minute intervals, both applied for a maximum of 28 days. Primary outcomes were wound surface area reduction and granulation tissue coverage at day 14 and day 28, assessed by standardised digital planimetry. At day 28, the intermittent group showed a mean wound area reduction of 58% compared with 44% in the continuous group (95% CI for difference: 4–24%, p = 0.04). Granulation tissue coverage was likewise higher in the intermittent arm (72% vs 61%, p = 0.06). Adverse events, predominantly peri-wound maceration, occurred at similar rates in both groups (18% vs 20%). The results support a larger confirmatory trial and provide preliminary data on pressure cycling parameters suitable for future protocol standardisation.

title: Effect of negative pressure wound therapy on biofilm disruption in diabetic foot ulcers: ex vivo flow-cell model results and early clinical correlation
abstract: Although NPWT is thought to reduce bacterial burden in chronic wounds, the direct mechanical effect on established biofilm structure has not been systematically characterised under controlled conditions. This study used an ex vivo flow-cell model seeded with P. aeruginosa biofilm grown on porcine skin explants to quantify biofilm disruption at four NPWT pressures (−75, −100, −125, and −150 mmHg) applied for 30-minute sessions. Biofilm biomass was quantified by crystal violet extraction and confocal z-stack volume measurement before and after treatment. Pressures of −125 mmHg and above produced statistically significant reductions in biofilm volume (35% and 41% respectively, p < 0.05), whereas −75 mmHg showed no significant effect. In a secondary observational component, swab cultures from 22 clinical NPWT patients were collected on days 0, 7, and 14; patients whose wounds were managed at −125 mmHg showed a greater decline in semi-quantitative bacterial load scores compared with those at −75 mmHg. Limitations include the simplified single-species model and the small clinical cohort. The data suggest that pressure selection may influence biofilm management outcomes and warrant prospective clinical investigation.

title: Transcystic versus transcholedochal approach for laparoscopic common bile duct exploration: a comparative study of 94 patients
abstract: This prospective observational study compared outcomes of transcystic and transcholedochal laparoscopic common bile duct exploration (LCBDE) performed between 2011 and 2015 at two referral centres in Vojvodina. Ninety-four patients with confirmed choledocholithiasis were included: 57 underwent transcystic LCBDE and 37 underwent transcholedochal LCBDE with primary duct closure in 22 cases and T-tube drainage in 15. Stone clearance was achieved in 89.5% of transcystic and 91.9% of transcholedochal cases (p = 0.71). Postoperative bile leak occurred in 3 transcholedochal patients (8.1%), all managed conservatively or with endoscopic stenting. Median hospital stay was significantly shorter in the transcystic group (2.4 vs. 4.1 days, p = 0.003). Transcholedochal exploration was more frequently required for stones larger than 10 mm and multiple stones. The results suggest transcystic exploration as the preferred first-line approach when anatomically feasible.

title: Fluoroscopy-guided versus choledochoscopy-guided stone retrieval during laparoscopic transcystic common bile duct exploration: a prospective randomised pilot trial
abstract: This single-centre pilot randomised controlled trial compared fluoroscopy-guided basket retrieval (FG) with direct choledochoscopy-guided retrieval (CG) in 60 patients undergoing transcystic laparoscopic CBD exploration between 2019 and 2022. Patients were randomised 1:1. Primary endpoint was complete stone clearance confirmed by completion cholangiography or choledochoscopy. Complete clearance was achieved in 24 of 30 FG patients (80.0%) and 27 of 30 CG patients (90.0%; p = 0.29). Procedure time was shorter in the FG group (mean 34 vs. 52 minutes, p = 0.001). Radiation dose was a mean of 8.4 mGy in the FG group; zero in the CG group. No bile leaks or CBD injuries occurred in either group. Conversion to transcholedochal exploration was required in 4 FG and 2 CG patients. The trial was underpowered to establish equivalence; a larger multicentre trial is warranted. The protocol is registered at the Serbian Clinical Trials Registry.

title: Mechanical failure modes of tackers under repetitive loading: an in vitro fatigue analysis
abstract: Tacker devices secure mesh to the abdominal wall, but their fatigue behaviour under cyclic physiological loads is rarely studied. We tested three commercially available helical tacker designs (designated T1, T2, T3) inserted into porcine peritoneum and posterior rectus sheath. Specimens (n = 10 per group) were subjected to sinusoidal loading at 1 Hz, amplitude 5–30 N, replicating cough and Valsalva manoeuvre cycles, to a maximum of 100,000 cycles or failure. Median cycles to failure were 12,400 for T1, 38,700 for T2, and >100,000 for T3 (no failures). Failure analysis by scanning electron microscopy revealed helical wire fracture at the point of maximal curvature in T1 and T2. Pullout force measured after cyclic testing was reduced by 34% in T1 and 19% in T2 compared with non-cycled controls. T3's thicker wire gauge appeared protective against fatigue fracture.
venue: Hernia and Abdominal Wall Surgery

title: Standardisation of IONM protocols in thyroid surgery across four Balkan university hospitals: a feasibility report
abstract: Lack of protocol standardisation limits multicentre comparison of IONM outcomes. This feasibility study brought together surgical teams from four university hospitals in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia to assess current IONM practice variation and develop a shared minimum dataset. A structured survey of IONM equipment, stimulation parameters, electrode types, and documentation practices was completed by 18 surgeons. Major heterogeneity was found in stimulation current (0.5–3 mA), electrode type (tube surface vs. interarytenoid needle), and criteria for signal loss (threshold ranging from 10% to 75% amplitude decrease). A consensus protocol was drafted adopting 1 mA stimulation, 50% amplitude decrease as signal loss threshold, and mandatory post-dissection V2 signal documentation. Piloting of the shared protocol is planned across 120 cases in 2022–2023.

title: Multicentre validation of a shared IONM protocol across four Balkan university hospitals: interim results
abstract: Following the 2021 feasibility study, a shared IONM protocol was implemented across surgical units in Novi Sad, Osijek, Sarajevo, and Skopje. This paper reports interim results from the first 118 cases accrued under the protocol (target n=240). Standardised data collection included stimulation parameters, baseline and post-dissection V2 amplitude, signal loss events, and 6-week laryngoscopy. Protocol adherence was 91% across sites. Pooled transient RLN palsy rate was 4.2% (5/118) and permanent palsy 0.8% (1/118). Intracentre amplitude variability was reduced compared to pre-standardisation historical data (coefficient of variation 29% vs 44%). Two signal loss events were detected enabling operative pause; in one case, full signal recovery was achieved after repositioning the retractor. The dataset, once complete, will be submitted for publication in a peer-reviewed journal. These interim findings support the feasibility of shared IONM data standards in a resource-heterogeneous multicentre setting.

title: Performance of CUSUM charts under Weibull-distributed measurement error in plastic part dimensions
abstract: Dimensional measurements of injection-moulded parts frequently exhibit right-skewed distributions attributable to tool wear and material shrinkage variability. This study examines the average run length (ARL) behaviour of one-sided CUSUM charts when the underlying quality characteristic follows a two-parameter Weibull distribution rather than the normal distribution assumed at design stage. Monte Carlo simulation was conducted for shape parameters β ranging from 0.8 to 3.5 and reference values k set at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 standard deviations. Results show that for β below 1.5 the in-control ARL is inflated by up to 34% relative to the nominal ARL₀ of 370, leading to excessive false-alarm rates once out-of-control conditions arise. A corrected control limit derived from the empirical percentile of the Weibull distribution is proposed and evaluated against the standard Gaussian design. The corrected chart restores the nominal in-control ARL within ±5% across all simulated scenarios and improves out-of-control detection speed by 18–27% for mean shifts of one standard deviation.
venue: Journal of Quality and Reliability in Manufacturing

title: Process capability indices for skewed dimensional tolerances: a comparative study on polypropylene housing components
abstract: Standard process capability indices Cp and Cpk assume normality and are known to be unreliable for skewed distributions. This paper compares four non-normal capability estimators — Clements' method, the Burr distribution approach, a Johnson transformation estimator, and a kernel density estimator — applied to wall-thickness data collected from 1,240 polypropylene housing components produced on a 120-tonne injection moulding machine. Data were gathered over 31 production shifts, yielding individual measurements at four locations per part. The skewness of the pooled distribution was 1.42 and kurtosis 5.87. The kernel density estimator and the Johnson transformation produced the closest agreement with empirically determined yield rates, with absolute errors below 0.4 percentage points. The Clements method systematically overestimated capability by 0.12–0.19 index units. Practical recommendations for selecting among these methods based on sample size constraints are provided, together with bootstrap confidence intervals for each estimator.

title: Adaptive EWMA schemes with variable sampling intervals for monitoring short-run injection moulding processes
abstract: Short production runs in injection moulding present difficulties for conventional fixed-interval EWMA charts because insufficient data are available for reliable parameter estimation. This paper proposes a variable sampling interval (VSI) EWMA scheme calibrated using a maximum likelihood estimator updated sequentially as production proceeds. The chart operates with two sampling intervals: a short interval triggered when the EWMA statistic exceeds a warning limit, and a standard interval otherwise. Performance is evaluated through Markov chain analysis supplemented by 50,000-run simulation for shift magnitudes of 0.5σ, 1.0σ, and 1.5σ. The target product is a connector housing produced in batches of 200 units. Results show a reduction in the expected time to signal of 22% relative to the fixed-interval EWMA at a 1.0σ shift, with only a 3% increase in average sample number. A sensitivity analysis examines robustness to mis-specified in-control means, showing acceptable performance for estimation errors below 0.2σ.

title: Gamma-distributed CUSUM charts: exact versus approximate control limit computation for surface roughness in moulded optical parts
abstract: Surface roughness measurements on injection-moulded optical components, specifically lens holders produced in PMMA, follow a gamma distribution owing to the deterministic contribution of mould surface finish superimposed on stochastic processing variability. This study derives exact control limits for one-sided upper CUSUM charts under a gamma process model using the integral equation approach of Page (1954) extended to non-Gaussian families, and compares results with two approximation methods: a normalising transformation and a Wilson–Hilferty cube-root approximation. Exact limits were computed numerically for shape parameters α from 2 to 20 and scale parameters estimated from 18 months of production data comprising 4,600 subgroup observations. The approximation error of the Wilson–Hilferty method remained below 1.8% for α ≥ 5, making it practical for implementation on production floor systems. For α < 5, the exact approach is recommended, as the approximation underestimates the required decision interval h by up to 9.3%, inflating the false alarm rate. Implementation guidelines are provided in tabular form.

title: Economic design of EWMA control charts for non-normal processes: a cost model with imperfect repair
abstract: Economic design of control charts selects chart parameters — sample size n, sampling interval h, and control limit k — by minimising an expected cost function per unit time. Most published models assume normally distributed process outputs and perfect corrective action. This paper extends the Lorenzen–Vance cost model to accommodate non-normal output using a generalised lambda distribution (GLD) fit and incorporates imperfect repair, in which a restoration action reduces but does not eliminate the assignable cause with a fixed probability. The model is applied to flash height data from a family of automotive clip components produced by a Tier-2 Serbian supplier. Input cost parameters were gathered through structured interviews with quality and maintenance personnel. Optimal chart parameters differ substantially from those obtained under normality: the economic optimum shifts toward smaller n and shorter h when the GLD tail heaviness parameter exceeds a threshold identified in sensitivity analysis. The expected hourly quality-related cost under the GLD-based design was 11.4% lower than under the normal-based design.

title: Run-length distribution properties of CUSUM charts for Burr Type XII quality characteristics
abstract: The Burr Type XII distribution is flexible enough to approximate many skewed and heavy-tailed distributions encountered in manufacturing and has been proposed as a universal model for non-normal quality data. This paper derives the run-length distribution for CUSUM charts designed under the Burr XII assumption, evaluating the standard deviation of the run length (SDRL) and the fifth percentile of the run-length distribution alongside the customary ARL. Numerical integration and simulation were combined for a grid of Burr XII parameters (c, k) spanning distributions from near-normal to strongly skewed. A key finding is that heavy-tailed Burr XII distributions produce SDRL values 40–65% larger than their ARL, implying that ARL alone is an inadequate performance summary. Charts designed to achieve ARL₀ = 370 may have a 5th-percentile run length below 12 for c < 2. Corrected design tables are presented for practitioners and an R package implementation is described.

title: Monitoring warpage in thin-walled injection moulded parts using a multivariate EWMA chart with Box-Cox transformed responses
abstract: Warpage in thin-walled injection-moulded parts depends jointly on mould temperature, cooling time, and packing pressure, producing a multivariate response vector whose marginal distributions are skewed. This paper applies a multivariate EWMA (MEWMA) chart to simultaneously monitor four warpage measurements taken at prescribed locations on an automotive instrument panel trim strip. Because the MEWMA chart assumes multivariate normality, the marginal responses are first transformed using individually estimated Box-Cox parameters. The transformed data were tested for multivariate normality using the Henze–Zirkler statistic. A historical dataset of 620 subgroups of size 3, gathered over six months of serial production, served as Phase I reference data. Out-of-control scenarios involving a shift in one or two response means were simulated to assess detection performance. The MEWMA on Box-Cox-transformed data detected a 1.5σ shift in a single response 31% faster on average than the chart applied to untransformed data, while maintaining the nominal false-alarm rate.

title: Phase I estimation effects on CUSUM chart performance under log-normal process distributions
abstract: Control chart performance studies often assume that in-control process parameters are known precisely, whereas in practice they are estimated from a Phase I reference sample. This study quantifies the effect of Phase I sample size on the conditional and unconditional ARL of CUSUM charts when the monitored quality characteristic follows a log-normal distribution. Simulation experiments were conducted for Phase I sample sizes m = 20, 50, 100, and 200, with subgroup sizes n = 1 and 5. For the log-normal distribution with σ = 0.3 on the log scale, the unconditional in-control ARL reached 90% of its known-parameter value only when m exceeded 150 for n = 1. The practitioner-to-practitioner variability, summarised by the standard deviation of the conditional ARL, remained substantial even at m = 200. Recommendations are provided for Phase I sample size selection as a function of the log-normal shape parameter, and an adjusted control limit procedure is proposed that reduces the variability by approximately 40% relative to unadjusted charts.

title: Adaptive sampling interval CUSUM charts for detecting small mean shifts in non-normal injection moulding data
abstract: Adaptive sampling interval (ASI) CUSUM charts adjust the time between samples based on the current value of the CUSUM statistic, sampling more frequently when a process shift is suspected. Previous ASI CUSUM studies have largely assumed normality. This paper evaluates ASI CUSUM performance under gamma, log-normal, and inverse Gaussian distributions, motivated by gate-flash and sink-mark severity data collected from a high-volume closure component produced in HDPE. The three-zone ASI scheme, in which the sampling interval takes values from the set {0.1h, 0.5h, h}, is compared with fixed-interval CUSUM using the expected weighted run length (EWRL) criterion. Under all three non-normal models, the ASI scheme achieved EWRL reductions of 19–38% for small shifts (δ = 0.5σ) relative to the fixed-interval chart at equal in-control ARL. The improvement was largest under the inverse Gaussian model, where tail asymmetry interacts favourably with the adaptive mechanism. An approximation formula for the optimal zone boundaries as a function of distribution skewness is derived and validated.

title: Copula-based multivariate SPC for correlated non-normal quality characteristics in multi-cavity injection moulding
abstract: In multi-cavity injection moulding, quality characteristics measured across cavities are correlated and individually non-normal, violating both independence and normality assumptions of standard multivariate charts. This paper proposes a copula-based monitoring framework in which marginal distributions are fitted separately for each cavity using maximum likelihood estimation, and their joint distribution is modelled through a Clayton or Gumbel copula selected by the AIC. A T²-type statistic is then computed from the copula-transformed uniform marginals and compared with control limits derived by simulation. The method is applied to shrinkage measurements from an eight-cavity mould producing polyamide connector bodies, with 540 production subgroups of size 2 per cavity serving as Phase I data. Compared with the standard Hotelling T² chart applied to raw data, the copula-based chart reduced the false-alarm rate from 7.1% to 1.8% under the true in-control distribution and improved out-of-control ARL for a shift in one cavity by 24%.

title: Distribution-free CUSUM charts based on sequential ranks for injection moulding process monitoring
abstract: Distribution-free (nonparametric) control charts avoid distributional assumptions entirely and are therefore attractive when process output distributions are uncertain or change over time. This paper investigates a sequential-rank CUSUM chart for individual observations, applying it to cycle-time deviations and part-weight data recorded during production of polyethylene film clips. The reference sample comprised 300 Phase I observations; Phase II performance was evaluated by simulation for four distributional models: normal, gamma, Weibull, and a mixture distribution representing start-up transients. The nonparametric chart maintained in-control ARL within 5% of the nominal 370 across all models, whereas a parametric CUSUM designed under normality showed in-control ARL degradation of up to 41% under the mixture model. Out-of-control detection speed of the nonparametric chart was 8–15% slower than the correctly specified parametric chart but 10–22% faster than the mis-specified parametric chart, confirming the robustness advantage. Computational implementation details suitable for programmable logic controllers are included.

title: Economic-statistical design of variable parameter EWMA charts for skewed processes in medical device injection moulding
abstract: Medical device components produced by injection moulding are subject to tight dimensional tolerances and regulatory requirements that limit the acceptable false-alarm rate. This study addresses economic-statistical design of variable parameter (VP) EWMA charts — in which both the sample size n and sampling interval h switch between two values depending on the current EWMA statistic — for processes with skewed output described by a three-parameter lognormal model. The objective function combines the Lorenzen–Vance expected cost with constraints on in-control ARL (≥ 200) and out-of-control ARL (≤ 8 at δ = 1.5σ), calibrated to requirements from a medical plastics manufacturer. Optimisation was performed using a hybrid genetic algorithm with local Nelder–Mead refinement over 5,000 iterations. Results show that the VP-EWMA satisfying both constraints achieves a 14.2% reduction in expected hourly cost compared with a fixed-parameter EWMA meeting the same statistical requirements. Sensitivity of the optimal design to cost parameter estimation error is characterised through a structured perturbation analysis.

title: Monitoring melt viscosity indices in recycled polymer injection moulding using EWMA charts with estimated parameters under non-normality
abstract: The growing use of recycled polymers in injection moulding introduces additional variability in melt viscosity, which is an in-process quality indicator correlated with final part properties. Melt flow index (MFI) measurements of recycled polypropylene batches exhibit pronounced right skewness (skewness coefficient 1.8–2.4) and batch-to-batch parameter drift. This study applies an EWMA chart with parameters estimated from a rolling Phase I window of the 60 most recent subgroups to monitor MFI in real time. The chart is designed to achieve a steady-state ARL of 150 at the target MFI, with control limits adjusted for parameter estimation uncertainty using a bootstrap correction derived from 10,000 resamples of the Phase I data. Data were collected from a production line processing post-consumer PP flake over 22 weeks, producing 1,840 subgroup observations of size 3. The rolling-estimation EWMA detected seven assignable causes confirmed by operator inspection, with two false alarms, against four detections and six false alarms for a fixed-parameter chart designed under normality.

title: Comparison of CUSUM and EWMA adaptive-interval schemes for detecting process mean and variance shifts simultaneously in non-normal bivariate data
abstract: Simultaneous shifts in process mean and variance occur in injection moulding when a machine parameter drifts, and detecting both types of shift with a single chart is practically desirable. This paper compares adaptive-interval CUSUM and EWMA schemes designed to monitor both the mean and variance of a bivariate quality vector whose marginals follow gamma distributions with shape parameters estimated from production data. The comparison criterion is the expected integrated run length (EIRL) over a range of shift combinations (δ_mean ∈ {0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5}, δ_variance ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} in ratio units). Simulation was based on 100,000 replications per scenario. The EWMA scheme with smoothing parameter λ = 0.15 outperformed CUSUM at small simultaneous shifts, while CUSUM was superior for large variance-only shifts. Neither scheme dominated uniformly, and a switching rule triggered by the ratio of the two statistics' recent increments reduced the EIRL by 9–16% relative to each single scheme across all scenarios. Practical guidance for scheme selection based on the anticipated shift profile is provided.

title: Incorporating Manufacturing Readiness Level Criteria into TRL-Based Stage-Gate Frameworks: A Comparative Case Study
abstract: Manufacturing readiness levels (MRL) and technology readiness levels (TRL) address complementary but distinct dimensions of R&D project maturity, yet most publicly funded programmes conflate them or apply TRL criteria alone. This paper presents a comparative case study of two Serbian manufacturing firms—a hydraulic components producer and a food-packaging machinery firm—that participated in a regional innovation support scheme and had their projects assessed under both TRL-only and integrated TRL-MRL frameworks. Assessment data were collected at project entry, mid-term, and closure (18-month projects, 2014–2016). Under TRL-only assessment, both projects reached gate-approval thresholds at mid-term; under the integrated framework, the hydraulic components project would have been flagged for a corrective action plan due to low MRL scores in process control and tooling. Post-project production ramp-up data show that the hydraulic components firm took 11 months longer than forecast to reach target output volume, consistent with the MRL gap identified retrospectively. The paper proposes an integration protocol specifying which MRL sub-criteria are most predictive of post-project production performance for discrete-parts manufacturers.

title: An Agent-Based Model of Knowledge Diffusion in Newly Merged Manufacturing Firms
abstract: This paper presents an agent-based model (ABM) designed to simulate the diffusion of tacit and explicit knowledge between employees following a merger of two manufacturing firms. The model, implemented in AnyLogic 7.2, represents individual workers as agents with heterogeneous knowledge stocks, learning rates, and social network positions. Firms are modelled as two initially distinct knowledge communities that are progressively merged under four integration speed scenarios. Simulation experiments across 500 runs per scenario show that rapid integration strategies (full structural merger within six months) consistently reduce aggregate knowledge stocks by 18–23% compared to phased approaches, primarily due to the disruption of informal knowledge-sharing ties. The model is calibrated against survey data from 47 employees at a Vojvodina-based metal-processing company. Results suggest that preserving informal cross-unit communication channels during the early integration phase significantly mitigates knowledge loss.

title: Blocking Strategies for Privacy-Preserving Record Linkage in Distributed Patient Registries
abstract: Record linkage across health registries maintained by separate institutions requires blocking to reduce the quadratic comparison space while preserving privacy. This paper evaluates three blocking approaches—sorted neighbourhood, canopy clustering, and phonetic key indexing—applied to a synthetic patient dataset of 120,000 records distributed across four simulated hospital nodes. Privacy is maintained through Bloom filter encoding of quasi-identifiers before any cross-site transmission. Linkage quality is measured using precision, recall, and F-measure against a ground-truth identifier. Sorted neighbourhood achieved the best recall (0.91) at acceptable computational cost, while canopy clustering reduced comparison pairs by 73% with only a 4% drop in recall. The paper also quantifies information leakage from Bloom filter collisions under a frequency attack and proposes a salting scheme that reduces attack success rate from 38% to under 3% on the tested configurations. Results are reproducible using the released synthetic data generator.

title: Enforcing k-Anonymity on Longitudinal Electronic Health Records: A Generalization Lattice Approach
abstract: Longitudinal electronic health records contain temporal quasi-identifiers—sequences of diagnosis codes and visit dates—that standard k-anonymity algorithms do not handle well. This work extends the classic Datafly generalization lattice to accommodate ordered temporal attributes. The algorithm operates on a dataset of 45,000 de-identified discharge records from a regional hospital system in Vojvodina, Serbia, provided under a data sharing agreement. For k=5, the method achieves an average information loss of 18.4% measured by the normalized certainty penalty, compared to 27.1% for the baseline Datafly. The paper reports runtimes on datasets scaled from 10,000 to 200,000 records and discusses the trade-off between temporal granularity and anonymity level. Limitations include sensitivity to rare disease codes that form near-unique quasi-identifiers even after generalization.

title: Comparing l-Diversity and t-Closeness for Sensitive Attribute Protection in Serbian Hospital Discharge Data
abstract: Both l-diversity and t-closeness were proposed to address attribute disclosure risks that k-anonymity alone cannot prevent, but comparative empirical studies on real-world health data remain sparse in Central and Eastern European contexts. This paper applies both models to a dataset of 32,000 anonymized hospital discharge records containing ICD-10 diagnosis codes as sensitive attributes. Attribute distributions in the dataset are skewed, with cardiovascular conditions comprising 41% of records, which creates challenges for entropy l-diversity. Experiments show that t-closeness with t=0.15 provides better protection against skewness-based attacks than 3-diverse partitions while incurring only a 6% higher suppression rate. The paper also documents the effect of quasi-identifier selection on equivalence class size distribution and discusses practical recommendations for registry administrators.

title: A Secure Multi-Party Protocol for Computing Linkage Frequencies Across Federated Cancer Registries
abstract: Computing aggregate linkage statistics across cancer registries operated by different national institutions requires exchanging frequency information without disclosing individual records. This paper presents a two-party protocol based on additively homomorphic encryption (Paillier scheme) that allows two registry operators to compute joint frequency tables of encoded quasi-identifiers. The protocol is implemented in Python and evaluated on synthetic datasets of 20,000 records per site, modelling cervical cancer registries. Communication overhead is measured as a function of the number of distinct quasi-identifier combinations, ranging from 1.2 MB to 14.7 MB for 500 to 5,000 distinct values. Correctness is verified against plaintext computations; no frequency leakage beyond the intended aggregate is demonstrated under a semi-honest adversary model. The paper discusses extensions to the malicious adversary setting.

title: Re-identification Risk Assessment for Aggregated Health Statistics Published by Public Health Institutes
abstract: Public health institutes regularly publish aggregated tables of disease incidence, mortality, and treatment outcomes. When cell counts are small, individuals may be re-identified by combining publicly available sociodemographic data. This paper systematically assesses re-identification risk for 14 published statistical tables from three Serbian public health institutes, using a prosecutor model and a background knowledge dataset drawn from the 2011 census microdata. For 6 of the 14 tables, at least one cell contained a unique combination of age group, municipality, and diagnosis category. Applying cell suppression reduced unique cells to zero in all tables but removed 9–23% of published data. The paper proposes a hierarchical suppression ordering that minimises total information loss and discusses alignment with the EU General Data Protection Regulation requirements for anonymized statistical outputs.

title: Privacy-Preserving Record Linkage Without a Trusted Third Party: A Hash-Based Protocol for Cross-Border Patient Matching
abstract: Cross-border patient matching in Europe is required for continuity of care and epidemiological research but cannot rely on a single trusted third party due to regulatory constraints across jurisdictions. This paper presents a protocol in which each site independently hashes patient quasi-identifiers using a site-specific secret key before transmitting encoded values to a coordination server, which computes candidate pairs without ever seeing plaintext data. The protocol is evaluated on a synthetic dataset of 60,000 patient records split across sites representing Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, with deliberately introduced name transliteration variants and recording errors. Linkage F-measure reaches 0.87 under a Jaro-Winkler similarity threshold of 0.88, and the protocol adds a median overhead of 340 ms per 1,000 record pairs compared to plaintext linkage. Privacy properties are analysed under an honest-but-curious coordination server assumption.

title: Data Masking Techniques for Clinical Trial Datasets: A Structured Review and Classification
abstract: Clinical trial datasets contain combinations of demographic, pharmacological, and outcome variables that make standard anonymization challenging. This book chapter provides a structured review of data masking techniques applicable to clinical trial data, covering generalization, suppression, data swapping, synthetic data generation, and noise addition. Techniques are classified along three axes: utility preservation, re-identification risk reduction, and implementation complexity. For each technique, the chapter summarises empirical results from the published literature (2005–2017), noting dataset sizes, quasi-identifier sets, and reported information loss metrics. Special attention is given to the interaction between masking and statistical analysis validity: simulated clinical outcomes show that noise addition at standard deviation levels above 0.15 times the variable range leads to statistically significant distortion of treatment effect estimates in 7 of 12 reviewed studies. The chapter concludes with a decision framework for trial data custodians selecting among techniques.

title: Differential Privacy for Federated Query Processing in Distributed Health Registries
abstract: Federated query processing allows analysts to pose aggregate queries across health registries without centralising data. Adding differential privacy (DP) noise to query results at each node prevents inference about individual records, but the composition of DP mechanisms across nodes and across multiple queries degrades privacy guarantees rapidly. This paper implements and evaluates three noise addition strategies—Laplace mechanism, Gaussian mechanism, and the sparse vector technique—in a four-node federated registry testbed built on PostgreSQL. Queries involve COUNT and SUM aggregates over diagnosis and medication attributes for 90,000 synthetic patient records. With a global privacy budget of ε=1.0, the Laplace mechanism yields relative error of 3.1% for COUNT queries at a table size of 10,000 rows, while the sparse vector technique extends the usable budget across 40 sequential queries with a 12% accuracy penalty compared to non-private baselines.

title: Quasi-Identifier Discovery in Semi-Structured Health Data Using Mutual Information Screening
abstract: Identifying which attributes or attribute combinations constitute quasi-identifiers in semi-structured health data—such as HL7 FHIR resources—is a prerequisite for applying anonymization correctly, yet it is often done manually. This paper proposes an automated screening procedure based on pairwise and higher-order mutual information estimates to rank candidate quasi-identifier sets by their discriminative power. The procedure is applied to a synthetic FHIR R4 dataset of 25,000 patient resources generated by the MedSynth generator, with 34 candidate attributes. The method correctly identifies all manually annotated quasi-identifiers at a threshold that retains 89% precision and 95% recall, running in under 4 minutes on a standard server. A false positive analysis shows that ICD code prefixes at the chapter level are consistently flagged despite low individual discriminative power due to correlation with age and region.

title: Privacy Risk in the Integration of Birth Registry and School Health Records: A Case Study in Vojvodina
abstract: Linking birth registry records with school health assessment records enables longitudinal child health research but creates substantial privacy risk because the combined dataset contains rare attribute combinations. This paper reports a case study conducted with anonymized records from the Vojvodina birth registry (2005–2015, n=138,000) and school health screening data (n=112,000 children aged 6–10), integrated under a research protocol approved by the relevant ethics committee. The linkage uses Bloom filter-encoded identifiers; the resulting linked dataset is evaluated for k-anonymity with k=5 across seven quasi-identifiers. Before anonymization, 14.2% of records fall in equivalence classes of size one. A tailored suppression and generalisation procedure reduces this to 0% while retaining 91% of records. Attribute utility for four target research variables is assessed using logistic regression AUC comparisons between original and anonymized datasets, with AUC differences below 0.03 in all cases.

title: Measuring Utility Loss Under Sequential Anonymization Operations on Federated Datasets
abstract: When health datasets pass through multiple anonymization steps—first locally at each site, then again after federation—utility loss compounds in ways that are difficult to predict from individual step metrics. This paper formalises a framework for tracking utility loss through a pipeline of k-anonymity, l-diversity, and suppression operations applied sequentially. Six pipeline configurations are evaluated on a federated synthetic dataset with three sites, each contributing 30,000 records with partially overlapping attribute schemas. Utility is measured using the discernibility penalty, normalized certainty penalty, and downstream classification accuracy on a simulated readmission prediction task. Results show that applying k-anonymity locally before federation increases total discernibility penalty by 34% compared to a single global anonymization pass, but reduces maximum information exposure at any single site by 61%. The framework is implemented as a Python library with documented APIs.
