title: Sensitivity of Textile LCA Results to Background Database Choice: ecoinvent 3.3 versus 3.6
abstract: Database updates in ecoinvent between versions 3.3 and 3.6 altered electricity supply mixes, chemical production datasets, and water treatment processes in ways that are consequential for textile LCA studies. This paper presents a structured comparison using a fixed cradle-to-gate model for a woven cotton twill fabric, holding all foreground inventory data constant while switching background databases. Climate change impact scores differed by up to 12% between database versions, mainly attributable to revised European electricity grid mixes. Freshwater eutrophication changed by 31% owing to updated phosphorus removal efficiency coefficients in wastewater treatment datasets. Characterisation was performed under ReCiPe 2016 (H) for eight midpoint categories. Monte Carlo analysis (n = 1,000 runs) was used to distinguish genuine parameter uncertainty from database-driven variability. The paper recommends that textile LCA practitioners report the database version explicitly and conduct at least a one-way sensitivity check when comparing studies published across major ecoinvent release boundaries.

title: Life Cycle Assessment of Hemp Fibre Production in Serbia: From Sowing to Hackling
abstract: Hemp cultivation is expanding in Serbia following regulatory changes in 2018, and the crop is proposed as a low-input alternative to cotton for domestic textile production. This study presents a gate-to-gate LCA covering field cultivation, water retting, mechanical breaking, and hackling of hemp fibre for ten-hectare trial plots in two Vojvodina locations. Inventory data were collected through on-site measurements and farmer interviews over the 2019 growing season. Climate change impact was 0.61 kg CO2 eq per kg of hackled long fibre, substantially below published values for conventionally irrigated cotton (range 2.1–4.8 kg CO2 eq/kg). Fossil resource use was 6.2 MJ/kg, dominated by diesel combustion in field machinery. Human carcinogenic toxicity was elevated relative to cotton due to particulate matter emissions during dry mechanical processing, suggesting that occupational exposure controls warrant attention. The study supplies the first Serbian foreground inventory dataset for hemp fibre and discusses its integration into product-level garment LCA.

title: Occupational Inhalation Exposure to Cotton Dust and Its Inclusion in LCA-Based Human Health Impact Assessment
abstract: Occupational health burdens from cotton dust inhalation in spinning mills are rarely incorporated into product-level textile LCA, yet they represent a significant fraction of human health impact in countries with limited dust control regulation. This study combines workplace air sampling data from two ring-spinning facilities in Serbia with USEtox occupational exposure factors and DALY-based characterisation to estimate the human health midpoint contribution of inhalable cotton dust. Gravimetric measurements at 24 workstations showed total inhalable dust concentrations between 1.8 and 6.4 mg/m³, with endotoxin concentrations positively correlated (r = 0.71). The derived DALY contribution per kilogram of ring-spun yarn was 1.3 × 10⁻⁶, comparable in magnitude to the climate change contribution when expressed in the same endpoint metric. Integration of this occupational pathway into a full garment LCA shifted the dominant impact category from climate change to human health at the endpoint level. The paper outlines a practical inventory template for including occupational cotton dust exposure in SimaPro-based models.

title: Carbon Footprint Labelling Schemes for Textiles: A Review of Methodological Requirements and Compliance Gaps
abstract: Several voluntary and emerging mandatory carbon footprint labelling schemes for textile products have been introduced in Europe between 2015 and 2023, each with distinct requirements for system boundaries, allocation procedures, and characterisation factors. This chapter reviews six schemes—including the Product Environmental Footprint Category Rules for apparel and footwear—against a consistent analytical framework drawn from ISO 14067 and EN 15804. Key methodological divergences are identified in the treatment of land use change for natural fibres, the inclusion or exclusion of the use phase, and the handling of recycled content. The chapter draws on empirical results from earlier LCA studies of cotton and linen garments conducted by the authors to illustrate how the same underlying inventory data can yield carbon footprint values differing by up to 28% depending on scheme-specific rules. Recommendations are made for harmonisation, with particular attention to requirements that are disproportionately burdensome for small and medium textile enterprises in southeastern Europe.

title: Inventory Modelling of Enzymatic Scouring as a Substitute for Alkaline Scouring in Cotton Pre-treatment: Mass Balance and Toxicity Implications
abstract: Alkaline scouring of greige cotton fabric consumes substantial quantities of sodium hydroxide and generates high-pH effluent requiring intensive neutralisation. Enzymatic scouring with pectinase preparations has been proposed as a lower-impact alternative, but quantified inventory data for industrial-scale enzymatic processes remain scarce in public LCA databases. This study presents a mass balance for both processes based on measurements at a pilot dyehouse in Novi Sad over 42 production batches totalling 8.6 tonnes of fabric. Sodium hydroxide consumption was eliminated in the enzymatic route but replaced by an enzyme preparation at 1.2 kg per 100 kg fabric; liquid enzyme production was modelled using a proxy dataset for submerged fermentation. Climate change impact decreased by 38% in the enzymatic route. Freshwater ecotoxicity increased by 9% due to the nitrogen-rich fermentation effluent. Human carcinogenic toxicity decreased by 61%, mainly because alkaline scouring wastewater contains residual surfactant loads. The paper supplies updated SimaPro unit process templates for both routes as supplementary material.

title: Towards Dynamic LCA for Textile Systems: Incorporating Time-Differentiated Emission Characterisation for Short-Rotation Fibre Crops
abstract: Standard attributional LCA uses static characterisation factors that treat all greenhouse gas emissions as temporally equivalent regardless of when they occur during the product life cycle. For natural-fibre textile systems with meaningful carbon uptake and release cycles—hemp, flax, and fast-growing bast crops—this static approach may misrepresent actual radiative forcing contributions. This paper adapts the dynamic LCA framework of Levasseur et al. to a cradle-to-gate model of hemp twill fabric produced in Serbia, using annual time-step emission profiles for field cultivation (carbon uptake), retting (methane and N₂O), and yarn formation. Dynamic characterisation was performed with time-horizon-specific GWP values at 20, 50, and 100 years. The 20-year dynamic GWP was 18% lower than the static 100-year GWP for the hemp system, while the difference was less than 4% for a comparable cotton scenario. The study argues that time-differentiated LCA is most relevant for comparative decisions between biogenic-fibre and synthetic alternatives at short policy time horizons and provides open-access Python scripts for dynamic emission profiling.

title: Psychoacoustic Metrics as Predictors of Annoyance in Combined Road and Rail Traffic Environments
abstract: Standard A-weighted level descriptors may not fully capture the annoyance arising from combined road and rail traffic, where spectral and temporal characteristics differ substantially. This laboratory listening test exposed 96 participants to 72 synthesised soundscape stimuli representing combinations of road traffic and freight train pass-bys at controlled signal-to-background ratios. Stimuli were characterised by Zwicker loudness (N5), sharpness (S), roughness (R), and fluctuation strength (F) alongside LAeq. Multiple regression and structural equation modelling were used to predict annoyance ratings. N5 and fluctuation strength jointly accounted for 61% of annoyance variance, compared to 48% for LAeq alone. The incremental contribution of rail pass-by events was best captured by a peak-weighted fluctuation strength metric. Results suggest that psychoacoustic composite indices could supplement A-weighted indicators in action plan priority setting for mixed traffic corridors, particularly where freight rail frequency exceeds six events per hour.

title: Influence of electrode material on chromium(VI) reduction during electrocoagulation of tanning and plating wastewaters
abstract: This study compared aluminium, iron, and stainless-steel electrodes for Cr(VI) removal from two industrial effluent matrices: a simulated tannery wastewater (Cr(VI) 20–80 mg/L) and a simulated electroplating rinsewater (Cr(VI) 50–200 mg/L). Experiments were conducted in a 5-litre batch EC cell at current densities of 10 and 25 mA/cm². Iron electrodes achieved complete Cr(VI) reduction to Cr(III) and subsequent co-precipitation within 30 min at 25 mA/cm² and pH 6, yielding final effluent concentrations below 0.05 mg/L. Aluminium electrodes were less effective for reduction but produced lower sludge volumes. Stainless-steel electrodes showed minimal Cr(VI) reduction. Operating cost analysis indicated that iron electrodes offered the lowest combined electrode and energy cost per cubic metre treated. Results suggest iron EC is preferable for plating SMEs already handling iron-rich process streams.

title: Seasonal and spatial patterns of PAH wet deposition fluxes in the Novi Sad metropolitan area during 2014–2015
abstract: Event-based wet deposition samples were collected using an automated wet-only collector at three stations representing urban core, suburban, and peri-industrial land-use categories. Over 78 precipitation events totalling 532 mm were sampled across two complete seasons. Solid-phase extraction on Oasis HLB cartridges followed by GC-MS/MS analysis quantified 15 PAHs. Flux-weighted mean concentrations of fluoranthene and pyrene were significantly higher (Mann–Whitney U, p < 0.05) at the peri-industrial station (1.8 and 1.4 µg L⁻¹, respectively) than at the urban core. Annual wet deposition flux for Σ15PAH ranged from 1,340 ng m⁻² yr⁻¹ at the background suburban site to 4,870 ng m⁻² yr⁻¹ downwind of an oil refinery buffer zone. First-flush effects were observed in 60% of events with initial intensities above 5 mm h⁻¹. Results indicate that wet deposition represents a non-negligible pathway for PAH input to urban soils and surface waters in the region.

title: Prevalence of tetracycline and erythromycin resistance among Enterococcus faecalis isolates from finishing pigs in Vojvodina
abstract: A cross-sectional survey was conducted on 14 commercial pig-finishing farms in Vojvodina province, Serbia, between 2009 and 2010. Rectal swabs from 280 animals were processed on selective Slanetz–Bartley agar, yielding 312 confirmed Enterococcus faecalis isolates. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined by broth microdilution in Mueller–Hinton broth supplemented with 2% lysed horse blood, and results were interpreted using EUCAST epidemiological cut-off values. Resistance to tetracycline was detected in 78.5% of isolates and to erythromycin in 64.1%. PCR screening identified the tet(M) gene in 87.6% of tetracycline-resistant strains and erm(B) in 93.5% of erythromycin-resistant strains. Co-resistance to both antimicrobial classes was found in 59.6% of all isolates. Multivariable logistic regression indicated that farms with documented in-feed tetracycline prophylaxis had significantly higher odds of carrying tet(M)-positive isolates (OR 4.2, 95% CI 1.9–9.4). The findings suggest that routine antimicrobial use in pig production in this region selects for resistance gene accumulation in commensal enterococci.

title: First description of vanA-carrying Enterococcus faecium in a broiler production chain in Serbia
abstract: Between March and September 2012, cloacal samples were collected from 180 broiler chickens at three integrated poultry production sites in central Serbia, together with environmental swabs from litter, feeders, and slaughter-line surfaces. All samples were plated on bile-aesculin azide agar with 6 mg/L vancomycin. Nineteen Enterococcus faecium isolates were recovered, of which five showed high-level vancomycin resistance (MIC ≥ 256 mg/L) and four carried the vanA gene cluster confirmed by multiplex PCR and Sanger sequencing. Pulsed-field gel electrophoresis revealed three distinct clonal types, with one type present at two separate production sites, suggesting either common source contamination or horizontal gene transfer along the production chain. Transfer of vancomycin resistance to a recipient E. faecalis JH2-2 strain was demonstrated in broth mating experiments at frequencies of 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻⁷ per donor cell. These findings represent the first documented occurrence of vanA-positive E. faecium in Serbian poultry production and highlight a potential food-safety risk requiring surveillance.

title: Comparison of disk diffusion and broth microdilution for susceptibility testing of Enterococcus spp. from cattle: agreement with EUCAST interpretive criteria
abstract: Disk diffusion (DD) and broth microdilution (BMD) were compared for nine antimicrobial agents commonly used in bovine medicine across 198 Enterococcus isolates recovered from mastitic milk and faecal samples at twelve dairy farms in Vojvodina. Species composition was 62% E. faecalis, 29% E. faecium, and 9% other Enterococcus spp. All MICs were determined in cation-adjusted Mueller–Hinton broth with lysed horse blood additive, and DD inhibition zones were read after 18–20 hours on Mueller–Hinton fastidious agar. Categorical agreement between methods, applying EUCAST v12.0 breakpoints, ranged from 88.4% for linezolid to 97.9% for ampicillin. Essential agreement (±1 dilution) was ≥90% for all agents tested. Very major error rates exceeded 10% for DD with nitrofurantoin, leading to a recommendation to use BMD as the primary method for this drug–pathogen combination. The study provides practical guidance for regional veterinary diagnostic laboratories where both methods are in routine use.

title: Genotypic characterisation of high-level aminoglycoside resistance in enterococci from swine farms in three Danubian countries
abstract: High-level aminoglycoside resistance (HLAR) determinants were investigated in 427 Enterococcus isolates collected from pig farms in Serbia, Romania, and Croatia during a coordinated sampling campaign in 2014–2015. Isolates with high-level gentamicin resistance (MIC ≥ 512 mg/L) and high-level streptomycin resistance (MIC ≥ 2048 mg/L) were screened by PCR for aac(6′)-Ie-aph(2′′)-Ia, ant(4′)-Ia, ant(6′)-Ia, and aph(3′)-IIIa genes. HLAR was detected in 38.2% of isolates; aac(6′)-Ie-aph(2′′)-Ia was the most prevalent determinant (71.9% of HLAR strains). Multi-locus sequence typing of 60 representative isolates identified four sequence types previously associated with hospital-adapted E. faecium lineages, occurring at all three country sites. Although no direct zoonotic transfer was established, the shared sequence type distribution across borders suggests that livestock may serve as a reservoir for clinically relevant enterococcal clones in the region. Results were interpreted alongside country-level antimicrobial sales data for veterinary use.

title: Antimicrobial resistance profiles of Enterococcus spp. in organic versus conventional pig production systems in Vojvodina
abstract: Resistance patterns were compared between enterococcal populations recovered from 6 certified organic and 8 conventional pig farms in Vojvodina, sampled twice during 2016. Faecal swabs from 10 animals per farm per visit yielded 364 enterococcal isolates (E. faecalis 55%, E. faecium 36%, other spp. 9%). MICs for nine antimicrobials were determined by broth microdilution and categorised using EUCAST epidemiological cut-off values. Resistance prevalence was lower on organic farms for all agents tested; the largest difference was observed for tetracycline (38% vs. 81%, p < 0.001) and erythromycin (29% vs. 67%, p < 0.001). Multidrug resistance (resistance to ≥3 antimicrobial classes) was present in 14.7% of isolates from organic farms versus 43.9% from conventional farms. Despite reduced resistance levels, organic farm isolates were not resistance-free, suggesting persistence of resistance genes in the absence of selection pressure or possible introduction through purchased animals. These results support the value of organic management practices in reducing AMR burden in commensal bacteria.

title: Whole-genome sequencing of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium from a Serbian swine farm: resistome and mobile genetic element characterisation
abstract: Four vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) isolates previously identified in a Vojvodina swine cohort were subjected to short-read whole-genome sequencing on an Illumina MiSeq platform (2 × 250 bp paired-end). Genome assemblies ranged from 2.74 to 2.91 Mb with 2,680–2,790 predicted coding sequences. ResFinder 4.0 analysis identified vanA, erm(B), tet(M), ant(6′)-Ia, and aph(3′)-IIIa across the four genomes; all carried at least four resistance determinants. The vanA gene cluster was located on a plasmid (pVRE-NS01, 54.3 kb) identified by Plasmid Finder and carrying sequence homology to Tn1546 transposons. PlasmidFinder additionally predicted two other plasmid replicons per isolate associated with erm(B) carriage. MLST assigned all four isolates to ST117 and ST78, lineages previously reported in European clinical settings. Comparative genomics against publicly available livestock and clinical VREfm genomes indicated that the pVRE-NS01 plasmid backbone shares >97% nucleotide identity with plasmids from clinical isolates in Hungary and Germany, raising questions about veterinary–clinical linkage.

title: Temporal trends in antimicrobial resistance among enterococci from Vojvodina pig farms, 2010–2019
abstract: Longitudinal MIC data collected from five sentinel pig farms in Vojvodina over ten years (2010–2019) were analysed to detect temporal trends in Enterococcus spp. resistance. A total of 1,048 isolates (E. faecalis 58%, E. faecium 42%) were tested annually for ampicillin, vancomycin, teicoplanin, linezolid, gentamicin (high-level), streptomycin (high-level), tetracycline, erythromycin, and chloramphenicol. Joinpoint regression was used to identify inflection points in annual resistance prevalence. Tetracycline resistance decreased significantly from 79% in 2010 to 54% in 2019 (average annual percent change −2.5%, p = 0.003), coinciding with national restrictions on prophylactic in-feed tetracyclines introduced in 2013. Erythromycin resistance remained stable at 60–68% throughout. High-level gentamicin resistance showed a modest increase from 21% to 34% (p = 0.04). No linezolid-resistant isolates were detected in any year, and vancomycin resistance prevalence remained below 3% throughout the study period. The analysis highlights the partial effectiveness of national policy interventions on resistance trends at farm level.

title: AMR phenotyping in livestock enterococci: methodological considerations and regional challenges
abstract: This chapter discusses practical and interpretive challenges in applying EUCAST clinical breakpoints and epidemiological cut-off values to Enterococcus spp. isolated from food-producing animals. Key topics include the choice between broth microdilution and gradient strip methods for MIC determination, the impact of inoculum density variation on MIC endpoints for high-level aminoglycoside resistance screening, and the limited availability of veterinary-specific breakpoints for certain antimicrobial–species combinations. The chapter draws on experience from surveillance work in Serbia, Romania, and Hungary to illustrate how interlaboratory MIC differences arise from media batch variation and incubation time inconsistencies. Recommendations for quality control using EUCAST-designated reference strains are provided. A section addresses the interpretation of resistance rates obtained under EUCAST criteria versus CLSI criteria, a common source of confusion when comparing published surveillance datasets from different European and non-European countries. The chapter is intended for diagnostic microbiologists, veterinary epidemiologists, and students entering the field.

title: Resistance gene carriage and conjugative transfer capacity among Enterococcus faecalis isolates from cattle with clinical mastitis in Vojvodina
abstract: Thirty-eight Enterococcus faecalis isolates from clinical bovine mastitis cases on 11 farms were characterised for antimicrobial resistance and conjugative transfer capacity. MICs were determined by broth microdilution for 10 antimicrobials. All isolates carried at least one resistance gene; tet(M) was detected in 82%, erm(B) in 61%, and aph(3′)-IIIa in 39%. Conjugative mating experiments with E. faecalis JH2-2 as recipient were performed in filter mating assays at 37°C for 18 hours. Transfer of tet(M) was demonstrated at frequencies of 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁷, and erm(B) transfer occurred at 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻⁸. In transconjugant isolates, PFGE confirmed transfer rather than spontaneous mutation. Fourteen of 38 donor isolates transferred two or more resistance genes simultaneously. The co-transfer of resistance determinants on conjugative elements from a primary bovine pathogen increases the potential for resistance dissemination both within the udder microenvironment and beyond, warranting attention in mastitis management protocols.

title: Comparison of EUCAST epidemiological cut-off values between 2016 and 2024 versions and their effect on resistance categorisation of archived swine Enterococcus isolates
abstract: Successive revisions to EUCAST epidemiological cut-off (ECOFF) values can alter how archived bacterial populations are categorised, complicating longitudinal AMR surveillance. This study applied EUCAST ECOFF versions 2016, 2019, 2021, and 2024 retrospectively to MIC distributions from 628 Enterococcus isolates (E. faecalis 54%, E. faecium 46%) collected between 2014 and 2018 from Vojvodina swine farms. For E. faecalis, ECOFF revisions caused a net 7.2 percentage point increase in the proportion categorised as wild-type for linezolid, and a 4.5 percentage point decrease for teicoplanin across the four versions. For E. faecium, the largest shift was for erythromycin (ECOFF tightened from 1 to 0.5 mg/L in 2021), reclassifying an additional 11.3% of isolates as non-wild-type. These reclassifications, while scientifically justified by updated MIC distribution data, pose practical challenges for national AMR trend reports that use frozen datasets. The article proposes a transparent versioning notation for published surveillance tables.

title: Occurrence and diversity of linezolid resistance determinants in Enterococcus faecium from poultry and swine in Serbia: a pilot genomic survey
abstract: Linezolid resistance in enterococci is rare but clinically critical. Twenty-three Enterococcus faecium isolates with reduced linezolid susceptibility (MIC 4–16 mg/L) were identified from a collection of approximately 1,200 isolates gathered in Vojvodina farms between 2020 and 2024. All 23 underwent short-read Illumina sequencing. The optrA gene was identified in 18 isolates, cfr(D) in 3 isolates, and mutations in domain V of 23S rRNA (G2576T) in 4 isolates (with two isolates carrying both optrA and 23S rRNA mutations). optrA was chromosomally located in 11 of 18 optrA-positive isolates and plasmid-borne in 7, as inferred from read-mapping to reference plasmids and confirmed in three cases by conjugation experiments. MLST revealed that 14 of 23 isolates belonged to ST18 and ST80. The predominance of optrA in livestock isolates, combined with its demonstrated transferability, is relevant for antimicrobial stewardship policy, given that linezolid is a last-resort agent in human medicine.

title: Risk factor analysis for Toxoplasma gondii seropositivity in rural pig-keeping households in Vojvodina: a questionnaire-based epidemiological study
abstract: A structured questionnaire was administered to 94 farm operators accompanying blood sampling of 487 pigs across five municipalities in Vojvodina in 2013. Variables covered farm management, cat ownership and feeding practices, rodent control, water source, and slaughter habits. Serology was performed by MAT. Overall porcine seroprevalence was 26.8%. Mixed-effects logistic regression treating farm as a random effect identified feeding kitchen waste including raw offal (OR 5.2, p < 0.001), absence of any rodent control measure (OR 2.8, p = 0.003), and more than two resident cats (OR 3.1, p = 0.004) as significant predictors. A substantial proportion of operators (62%) reported consuming home-produced pork as raw or lightly cured products, pointing to a direct exposure pathway. Stratification by municipality revealed spatial heterogeneity in farm-level seroprevalence ranging from 18% to 37%, warranting geographically targeted interventions.

title: Urine protein electrophoresis patterns in cats with chronic kidney disease across IRIS stages 1–4
abstract: Characterising urinary protein fractions can help localise the site and severity of renal damage. Sodium dodecyl sulphate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) was performed on urine samples from 62 cats grouped by IRIS CKD stage (stage 1: n = 12; stage 2: n = 18; stage 3: n = 17; stage 4: n = 15) and 20 healthy controls. Samples were concentrated by ultrafiltration and loaded at equal protein concentrations. Albumin, immunoglobulin light chains, and low-molecular-weight proteins (< 30 kDa) consistent with tubular origin were identified by molecular weight comparison against standard ladders. The proportion of low-molecular-weight protein bands increased progressively with IRIS stage (stage 1: 18% of total protein, stage 4: 52%). Albumin predominance was more pronounced in stage 3 and 4 cats, consistent with glomerular involvement. Between-cat variability was high, particularly in stage 2. Inter-assay coefficient of variation was 8.3%. Results confirm that SDS-PAGE can complement urine protein:creatinine ratio by distinguishing glomerular from tubular proteinuria patterns, but standardisation of sample handling remains a practical challenge for routine clinical use.

title: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling of enrofloxacin tissue residues in cattle: parameterisation and sensitivity analysis
abstract: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model was developed for enrofloxacin and its active metabolite ciprofloxacin in beef cattle to support mechanistic withdrawal period prediction. The model incorporated 10 tissue compartments (muscle, liver, kidney, fat, gut wall, lung, skin, injection site, blood, and rest of body), with tissue:plasma partition coefficients estimated from in vitro binding data and literature values. Tissue blood flows and organ volumes were taken from published bovine physiological datasets. The model was calibrated against data from two independent depletion studies (n = 48 total animals) and validated against a third study (n = 24). Predicted tissue concentrations were within 1.5-fold of observed values for muscle and kidney across all time points. A variance-based global sensitivity analysis (Sobol indices) identified renal clearance and muscle partition coefficient as the dominant parameters determining muscle residue uncertainty. The model is suitable for extrapolation to other dosing regimens and for assessing the effect of body weight on depletion kinetics.

title: Detection and genotyping of Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato in Ixodes ricinus ticks removed from roe deer in Vojvodina
abstract: Ticks removed from 54 roe deer carcasses during 2013–2014 were tested for Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato by nested PCR targeting the 5S–23S intergenic spacer region. Of 318 I. ricinus adults and nymphs screened, 47 (14.8%) were Borrelia-positive. Sequence analysis of 38 confirmed amplicons identified five genospecies: B. afzelii (44.7%), B. garinii (26.3%), B. valaisiana (18.4%), B. lusitaniae (7.9%), and B. burgdorferi sensu stricto (2.6%). Mixed infections were detected in 6 ticks (15.8% of positives). Borrelia prevalence did not differ significantly between adult and nymphal stages (χ² test, p = 0.17). Phylogenetic analysis placed the B. garinii sequences in a cluster with central European strains. The results confirm that roe deer in Vojvodina support Borrelia-infected I. ricinus at prevalences consistent with adjacent countries and that multiple genospecies circulate within a single host population.

title: Piecewise-Linear Approximation of ECG Signals Using Adaptive Breakpoint Selection
abstract: This paper examines piecewise-linear approximation as a preprocessing stage for ECG compression. A dynamic-programming algorithm selects breakpoints by minimising the sum of squared residuals subject to a maximum reconstruction error bound of 10 µV. Experiments were conducted on 30 records from the PhysioNet MIT-BIH arrhythmia database resampled to 360 Hz. The method achieves an average compression ratio of 4.1:1 at a per-sample root-mean-square error below 8 µV, outperforming fixed-window linear interpolation by approximately 18% in bit rate under identical distortion constraints. Computational cost is O(N log N) per record, making the approach suitable for microcontroller deployment in wearable monitors. The study also evaluates how premature ventricular contractions, which deviate from normal quasi-periodic morphology, affect the breakpoint density and proposes a beat-classification pre-filter that reduces the density penalty for irregular beats by 23%.

title: Beat-Synchronous DCT Coding of Long-Term ECG Recordings
abstract: Long-term (Holter) ECG recordings present compression challenges because gradual heart-rate drift shifts beat boundaries relative to fixed analysis windows. This work proposes a beat-synchronous discrete cosine transform (DCT) coder in which each beat is individually segmented using a Pan-Tompkins R-peak detector, zero-padded or truncated to a uniform 512-sample frame, and transformed to the DCT domain. Coefficient quantisation thresholds are derived per lead from a short training segment of the same recording, adapting to inter-patient variability. Tested on 18 two-lead 24-hour recordings at 250 Hz sampled at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, the coder achieves a mean compression ratio of 9.3:1 at a percentage root-mean-square difference (PRD) of 1.8%, with diagnostic quality preserved as assessed by two cardiologists. The encoding latency per beat averages 0.4 ms on a standard laptop CPU, confirming real-time feasibility.

title: Wavelet Packet Decomposition for Compression of Neonatal EEG with Burst-Suppression Patterns
abstract: Neonatal EEG with burst-suppression (BS) patterns has highly non-stationary quasi-periodicity that challenges standard EEG compressors tuned to adult signals. This study applies wavelet packet decomposition with adaptive basis selection via the best-basis algorithm, followed by run-length and Huffman coding of thresholded coefficients. The degree of non-stationarity is quantified by a burst-ratio metric computed over 10-second epochs, and the decomposition depth is adjusted accordingly. A dataset of 22 neonatal eight-channel recordings (duration 2–4 hours each, sampled at 256 Hz) was provided by the Institute for Child and Youth Health Care of Vojvodina. At a reconstruction SNR of 30 dB, the adaptive scheme achieves a compression ratio of 6.8:1 compared to 4.9:1 for a fixed-depth packet transform, a gain attributed primarily to more efficient representation of suppression epochs. No statistically significant difference in burst detection sensitivity was found between original and reconstructed signals using an automated BS detector.

title: Exploiting Inter-Beat Redundancy in ECG Compression via Differential Pulse-Code Modulation of DCT Coefficients
abstract: Consecutive cardiac beats in sinus rhythm show high morphological similarity, so their DCT coefficient sequences are strongly correlated across time. This paper models each lead's DCT coefficient track as a first-order autoregressive process and applies differential pulse-code modulation (DPCM) along the beat index rather than within a single beat. A predictor is trained on the first 30 seconds of each record and updated every 60 seconds to track slow morphological drift. Arithmetic coding is applied to the residual with a Laplacian model for the dominant low-frequency coefficients and a Cauchy model for higher-frequency ones. On a corpus of 48 single-lead records at 500 Hz, mean PRD is 1.4% at a compression ratio of 12.7:1, compared to 9.3:1 for independent per-beat DCT coding at matched PRD. The improvement degrades gracefully to 10.1:1 in the presence of atrial fibrillation, where inter-beat morphology is less predictable.

title: Sparse Coding of PPG Signals Using a Learned Overcomplete Dictionary
abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals share quasi-periodic pulse structure but exhibit waveform variation due to respiratory modulation and motion artefact. This work trains a 256-atom overcomplete dictionary on a 10,000-pulse corpus using the K-SVD algorithm, then encodes each 200-sample pulse segment as a sparse combination of at most eight atoms, with atom indices and coefficients quantised to 8 and 16 bits respectively. A greedy matching pursuit selects atoms sequentially. On a held-out test set of 3,200 pulses from 16 subjects collected with a finger oximeter at 100 Hz, the method achieves a mean reconstruction error of 0.6% PRD at 3.2 bits per sample, compared to 4.1 bits per sample for a 12-coefficient per-pulse DCT coder at the same PRD. Dictionary generalisation across subjects is evaluated; inter-subject PRD increase is 0.3 percentage points on average, suggesting moderate portability without per-subject retraining.

title: Rate-Distortion Analysis of Beat-Aligned Versus Free-Running Frames for ECG Entropy Coding
abstract: A systematic rate-distortion (R-D) comparison is made between two framing strategies for ECG entropy coding: beat-aligned frames that follow R-peak detection and free-running fixed-length frames of equivalent average duration. For each strategy, DCT coefficients are entropy coded with a context-adaptive arithmetic coder using three coefficient-magnitude context classes. R-D curves are computed at PRD values of 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 4%, and 8% across 60 single-lead records spanning normal sinus rhythm, sinus tachycardia, and first-degree AV block. Beat-aligned framing provides lower bit rates at PRD below 2%—a mean advantage of 0.4 bits per sample—while free-running framing is competitive at higher distortion where the frame-synchronisation overhead of beat detection is not amortised. The crossover PRD and its dependence on heart rate are characterised analytically. The results inform codec design choices in constrained implantable device scenarios.

title: Learned Entropy Models for ECG Compression Using Recurrent Context Prediction
abstract: Recent learned image compression methods use neural networks to model the entropy of quantised latent representations. This paper adapts that paradigm to single-lead ECG by replacing the standard spatial entropy model with a small gated recurrent unit (GRU) that predicts the probability distribution of each DCT coefficient from the previous 16 coefficients in the same beat and from the corresponding coefficient in the preceding beat, capturing both intra-beat spectral structure and inter-beat temporal redundancy. The GRU has 64 hidden units and is trained jointly with a scalar quantiser on 120 hours of ECG drawn from publicly available databases. At a target PRD of 1.5%, the learned model uses 1.6 bits per sample compared to 2.1 bits per sample for a hand-designed Laplacian arithmetic coder, a 24% reduction. Model size is 48 kB, and decoding runs at 180× real time on a laptop CPU. The paper also analyses failure modes on arrhythmic beats.

title: Embedded Coding of Physiological Signals: A Survey of Transform, Sparse, and Learned Approaches
abstract: This chapter surveys compression techniques for ECG, EEG, and PPG signals with emphasis on methods that exploit quasi-periodic structure. The first part covers classical transform-based approaches—DCT, wavelet, and wavelet packet—and their adaptation to beat-aligned or epoch-aligned frames. The second part reviews sparse representation methods, including structured dictionaries and joint multi-channel sparsity. The third part covers learned approaches: variational autoencoders, recurrent entropy models, and hybrid transform-neural architectures published up to early 2024. For each family, representative methods are compared on standardised datasets where available, and compression ratio, PRD, and encoder complexity are tabulated. The chapter also discusses application constraints: energy budgets in implantable devices, latency in real-time telemetry, and regulatory considerations for diagnostic-grade reconstruction. Open problems, including compression under non-stationary arrhythmic conditions and the lack of unified evaluation benchmarks, are identified.

title: Variable-Rate Learned ECG Compression with a Single Model via Conditional Quantisation Noise
abstract: Most learned compression models are trained at a fixed rate-distortion tradeoff, requiring separate models per operating point. This preprint proposes a single-model variable-rate ECG codec in which the quantisation noise level is fed as a scalar condition to both the GRU entropy model and a lightweight convolutional synthesis network. The condition scalar is drawn from a uniform grid of 16 values covering PRD targets from 0.5% to 8%. Training uses a weighted sum of rate and distortion losses with the condition scalar randomised each mini-batch. On a held-out test set of 48 single-lead records, the single conditioned model matches or slightly exceeds per-target trained models at all 16 operating points, with a maximum PRD deviation of 0.12 percentage points. Total model footprint is 61 kB, only 27% larger than a single fixed-rate model. Ablations confirm that conditioning the synthesis network is necessary; conditioning only the entropy model reduces the gain by roughly half.

title: Warm-Starting ALNS with Machine-Learning Initialisation for Real-Time Rescheduling
abstract: In real-time vehicle rescheduling, the quality of the initial solution fed to a metaheuristic strongly affects final solution quality when computation time is capped at 30–60 seconds. This paper investigates whether a graph neural network (GNN) trained on historical rescheduling instances can produce initial assignments that reduce the number of ALNS iterations needed to reach a target solution quality. The GNN is trained on 4 200 solved instances derived from a regional transport operator's incident log spanning three years. Experiments on a held-out test set of 600 instances show that GNN-initialised ALNS reaches solutions within 1% of a 5-minute ALNS run using only 18 seconds of computation on average, compared to 41 seconds when initialised with a greedy heuristic. The approach is sensitive to distribution shift: performance degrades when incident types in the test set differ substantially from those in training data, which limits transferability without retraining.

title: Scheduling Night-Shift Sequences Under Ergonomic Constraints: A CP and LNS Hybrid Approach
abstract: Night-shift sequencing rules derived from ergonomic guidelines impose complex restrictions that are difficult to encode efficiently in standard scheduling models. This paper investigates a hybrid approach combining constraint programming with large neighbourhood search (LNS) to handle sequences of night shifts for 60 nurses in a surgical department. Ergonomic constraints include prohibitions on more than three consecutive nights, mandatory recovery days following any night block, and limitations on forward versus backward rotation patterns. The CP component handles feasibility and propagation; the LNS component iteratively destroys and repairs a portion of the schedule using a random destroy operator calibrated on a 25% destruction rate. Compared to a pure CP approach with restarts, the hybrid reduces average solution time by 58% and improves average soft constraint satisfaction by 14% across 20 test instances derived from real scheduling data. Experiments were conducted on instances from a single tertiary hospital with four wards over a six-week horizon.

title: Existence and regularity of minimizers for a capillary energy functional with contact angle constraints
abstract: We study a variational problem for liquid drops resting on a planar solid substrate, where the energy consists of a surface tension term, a gravitational potential term, and a wetting energy along the contact line. The admissible class is taken within the space of sets of finite perimeter, and we impose a fixed contact angle condition in a weak, measure-theoretic sense. Using the direct method of the calculus of variations together with a compactness argument in BV, we establish existence of minimizers for contact angles in the range (0°, 180°). Regularity is then addressed via an excess-decay iteration adapted to the boundary, yielding C^{1,α} smoothness of the free surface away from the contact line for α < 1/2. A counter-example shows that the contact line itself need not be rectifiable without additional assumptions on the substrate. The results are illustrated with numerical profiles computed via Surface Evolver for Bond numbers between 0.1 and 5, showing good agreement with the analytical predictions.

title: Representation-Theoretic Methods in Graph Neural Networks: A Survey of Mathematical Foundations
abstract: This book chapter surveys the mathematical connections between harmonic analysis on groups, classical representation theory, and the design of equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs). The first part reviews Peter–Weyl theory for compact groups, Mackey's imprimitivity theorem, and their role in characterising equivariant linear maps between feature spaces. The second part traces how these structures appear implicitly in message-passing GNNs and explicitly in architectures based on group convolution. The third part discusses open questions, particularly for non-compact and non-unimodular groups, where the absence of a finite Haar measure or the failure of square-integrability complicates the definition of equivariant convolution. Mathematical prerequisites are kept at the graduate level; proofs are provided for the key equivalence theorems, while implementation details are referenced rather than reproduced.

title: Persistent Homology Features as Descriptors for Single-Cell Trajectory Topology
abstract: Topological data analysis via persistent homology offers a framework for characterising the shape of point clouds without committing to a specific embedding. We extract persistence diagrams from Vietoris–Rips filtrations built on k-NN graphs of single-cell RNA-seq data and use the resulting Betti number sequences to classify trajectory topologies — linear, bifurcating, trifurcating, and cyclic — across 28 real and simulated datasets. A linear SVM trained on vectorised persistence diagrams using the persistence image representation achieves 86 percent cross-validated accuracy on topology classification, compared to 71 percent for a baseline using only the first two PCA components. We also demonstrate that H1 persistence features correlate with the number of real lineage branches in five experimentally validated datasets. Computational cost scales approximately as O(n^2) in cell count, which is feasible for datasets up to 20 000 cells on a standard workstation.

title: Comparison of Aisle Configuration Policies in a Single-Command Order-Picking System: A Simulation Study
abstract: This study compares three aisle configuration policies—straight perpendicular aisles, fish-bone layout, and flying-V layout—in a single-command order-picking warehouse using discrete-event simulation. A reference facility of 3 600 m² with 8 picking aisles and 2 400 storage locations was modelled in FlexSim 7.2. Order inter-arrival times were sampled from a non-homogeneous Poisson process calibrated on six months of historical shipment data from a regional grocery distributor. Throughput, mean travel time per pick, and picker utilisation were recorded across 30 replications per configuration under three daily demand intensities. The fish-bone layout reduced mean travel time by 12.4% relative to the perpendicular baseline at high demand, but increased congestion at the I/O point by 18%. The perpendicular configuration remained preferable at low to medium demand intensities. Results suggest that layout choice interacts strongly with arrival rate profile, and that evaluation under a single static demand level may be misleading.

title: Slot Assignment for Perishable Goods in a Refrigerated Distribution Centre Under Fluctuating Throughput Requirements
abstract: Slotting optimisation in refrigerated warehouses must account for both travel-time minimisation and temperature-zone compliance, creating constraints not present in ambient storage. This paper formulates the slot assignment problem as a mixed-integer programme with zone capacity constraints and a weighted travel-distance objective. Instances were constructed from demand data of a 1 200-SKU cold-chain operator in the Vojvodina region, covering a 90-day planning horizon. A greedy constructive heuristic followed by a variable neighbourhood search produced solutions within 3.1% of the LP relaxation bound on average for 20-test instances, with computation times under 90 seconds. Simulation experiments in AnyLogic confirmed that the heuristic-generated assignments reduced forklift travel distance by 9.8% and average order fulfilment time by 7.3% relative to a turnover-based slotting baseline. The approach handles weekly reassignment cycles without prohibitive rehandling costs.

title: Layout Optimisation of a Constrained Cross-Docking Terminal Using a Simulated Annealing–Simulation Hybrid
abstract: Cross-docking terminals with irregular footprints present layout problems that standard analytical models handle poorly. This paper applies a simulated annealing metaheuristic coupled with a discrete-event simulation oracle to optimise the placement of inbound and outbound dock doors, staging lanes, and transfer equipment in an irregularly shaped terminal of 2 100 m². The hybrid iterates by proposing layout perturbations, evaluating each via a short simulation run of 480 simulated minutes, and accepting or rejecting changes according to the SA acceptance criterion. Tested on a real terminal operated by a regional freight forwarder, the hybrid found a configuration that reduced average truck dwell time from 47.3 minutes to 38.8 minutes (18% reduction) over a 10-hour operating window. Computational experiments show that embedding even short simulation runs (20 replications, 5 minutes each) within the metaheuristic loop yields substantially better solutions than analytical distance-based objectives alone, particularly when sorting conveyor speeds are heterogeneous.

title: Throughput Analysis of an Automated Storage and Retrieval System Under Non-Stationary Demand: A Case Study
abstract: This book chapter examines throughput characteristics of a single-aisle unit-load AS/RS installed in a pharmaceutical distribution centre in Serbia, focusing on the degradation of system performance during demand surges that occur at predictable intervals—end-of-month replenishment orders and pre-holiday peaks. Empirical arrival data spanning 18 months were decomposed into trend, periodic, and residual components; the periodic component was used to parameterise a non-homogeneous Poisson arrival process in the simulation model. Sensitivity analyses varied crane acceleration profiles (0.3–0.6 m/s²), dwell-point strategies (lower left corner vs. mid-point), and I/O point configurations (single vs. dual). Results indicate that dual I/O configuration combined with a mid-point dwell strategy sustained throughput within 5% of rated capacity up to 1.8× the baseline arrival rate, whereas the standard single I/O lower-left configuration experienced queue build-up beyond 1.4× baseline. The chapter also discusses a simplified queuing-network approximation that reproduces simulation results within 8% for planning purposes.

title: Forklift Fleet Sizing in a Shared-Resource Warehouse: Balancing Utilisation Against Order Cycle Time
abstract: Determining the appropriate number of forklifts in a warehouse where the same fleet serves both inbound putaway and outbound picking is a classical sizing problem, but one that existing closed-form models address poorly when arrival processes are bursty. This paper develops a simulation-based procedure for fleet sizing using a combination of steady-state performance metrics and transient response analysis. Data from a consumer goods warehouse operating two overlapping shifts were used to validate the model; the facility handles approximately 3 200 pallet movements per day across 11 600 storage locations. Experiments explored fleets of 4–10 forklifts under observed inter-arrival distributions for receiving and dispatch processes. A fleet of seven forklifts minimised the sum of forklift idle cost and order delay penalty under the base scenario; sensitivity to arrival rate uncertainty favoured eight forklifts when variance in inbound truck arrival was high. The study also documents the effect of shift-handover periods, which account for up to 14% of daily delay.

title: Impact of Storage Zone Reconfiguration on Travel Time Distribution in a Manual Pick-and-Pass System
abstract: Pick-and-pass systems divide a warehouse into sequential zones, each served by a dedicated picker, and are sensitive to workload imbalances that cause blocking between zones. This paper studies how reconfiguring zone boundaries and reassigning SKUs affects the distribution—not just the mean—of order travel time across a 10-zone manual pick-and-pass system in a spare parts distributor. Empirical order data consisting of 62 000 lines collected over four months were used to fit per-SKU demand distributions. A simulation model with 10 zone agents reproduced observed throughput (mean absolute error 2.1%) before testing 48 reconfiguration scenarios defined by zone width and ABC-class boundary parameters. Quantile regression on simulation output showed that configurations that equalised mean zone workloads reduced the 90th percentile of order travel time by up to 31%, while mean reduction was only 11%, indicating that variance effects dominate tail performance. Practitioners relying on mean travel time alone would under-invest in workload balancing.

title: Simulation-Based Evaluation of Dynamic Re-Slotting Triggers in an E-Commerce Fulfilment Centre
abstract: E-commerce fulfilment centres experience rapid seasonal shifts in SKU demand profiles that static slotting policies cannot accommodate efficiently. This paper evaluates three trigger strategies for initiating slot reassignment—calendar-based (weekly), threshold-based (triggered when a SKU's observed demand rank deviates by more than k positions from its assigned slot rank), and hybrid—using discrete-event simulation of a 5 400-location split-case fulfilment centre. Demand data were synthesised from publicly reported e-commerce seasonal patterns augmented with promotional event spikes. Over a 90-day simulated horizon, the threshold-based trigger with k = 15 reduced mean pick travel time by 14.6% relative to no re-slotting, while incurring 38% fewer slot moves than weekly re-slotting. The hybrid strategy achieved comparable travel-time reduction with 22% fewer moves than threshold-only. Re-slotting labour cost was modelled explicitly; under the labour cost assumptions tested, the hybrid approach yielded positive net benefit only when pick volume exceeded approximately 8 500 lines per day.

title: Low-Cost Wireless Sensor Network for Real-Time Energy Monitoring on a Pilot Welding Line
abstract: Purpose-built energy monitoring systems for small manufacturing companies are often prohibitively expensive. This paper describes the design, calibration, and field validation of a wireless sensor network (WSN) built from commodity current transformer modules, ESP32 microcontrollers, and an MQTT broker running on a local server. The system was deployed on a six-station MIG welding line at an engineering SME in Novi Sad. Accuracy was assessed against a certified three-phase power analyser over a 10-day concurrent measurement campaign; the mean absolute error in cumulative energy was 1.9 % per station. Data latency averaged 340 ms end-to-end. The paper reports the full bill of materials (total hardware cost EUR 480 for six channels), calibration procedure, firmware architecture, and lessons learned regarding interference from welding inverter switching. A simple web dashboard presenting real-time and historical load profiles is described. The hardware design files are released under an open licence.

title: Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimisation with Correlated Demand Across Retail Nodes: A Copula-Based Approach
abstract: Standard multi-echelon inventory models assume independent demand across retail nodes, but cross-sectional demand correlation—driven by shared promotions, regional weather events, or economic shocks—can cause simultaneous stockouts that conventional safety stock calculations underestimate. This paper models joint demand across 24 retail nodes using a Gaussian copula with marginal distributions fitted separately for each node. A two-echelon network is then optimised by numerical integration of the copula-based joint distribution to obtain warehouse-level safety stocks that meet per-node service level requirements. The approach is compared against an independence-assumption benchmark on data from a regional clothing retailer covering 18 months of daily sales. Under high correlation (Kendall τ > 0.4, observed during seasonal peaks), the copula model reduces observed stockout frequency at the warehouse by 31% while adding only 7% to warehouse safety stock. Computational tractability for networks with up to 30 nodes is demonstrated.

title: Benchmarking Balanced Scorecard Adoption Rates and Practices Among Manufacturing SMEs in the Western Balkans: A Survey of 210 Companies
abstract: Large-scale survey data on balanced scorecard adoption in the Western Balkans have been absent from the literature, limiting comparative analysis and policy relevance. This paper reports findings from a structured survey of 210 manufacturing SMEs (50–499 employees) across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, conducted in 2021–2022. The questionnaire covered BSC adoption status, number of KPIs monitored, review frequency, software tools used, and the relationship between BSC use and ISO certification status. Adoption rates were 34% in Serbia, 21% in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and 17% in North Macedonia. Among adopters, the average number of tracked KPIs was 18 (SD = 7.4), and financial perspective indicators dominated. Only 38% of adopters reviewed their BSC on a monthly or more frequent basis. Chi-square tests confirm a significant association between BSC adoption and ISO 9001 certification across all three countries. The dataset is publicly available through the Faculty of Technical Sciences repository.

title: Gradient-corrected mechanical work estimation during road cycling: a field validation against indirect calorimetry
abstract: Accurate estimation of external mechanical work in road cycling requires accounting for terrain gradient, yet most commercial devices apply flat-ground assumptions. This study compared gradient-corrected mechanical work estimates—derived from a digital elevation model fused with GPS positional data—against breath-by-breath indirect calorimetry in 14 trained male cyclists completing three standardised hill-repeat protocols (average grade 4.2 %, 7.8 %, and 11.3 %). Mechanical efficiency was computed at each gradient condition. The gradient-corrected model reduced mean absolute error in energy expenditure estimation from 18.4 % (flat-ground model) to 6.1 % relative to calorimetry. Bland–Altman analysis indicated acceptable limits of agreement (±38 kcal per 60-minute stage). Efficiency values declined significantly with increasing grade (p < 0.01), consistent with previously reported physiological constraints. Findings support the use of terrain-adjusted power-based models for field monitoring in hilly terrain and highlight the inadequacy of ignoring elevation data in training load calculations.

title: Session RPE as a proxy for internal load in amateur endurance cyclists: agreement with heart rate–based TRIMP across 8 weeks of base training
abstract: Session rating of perceived exertion (sRPE) is widely used to quantify internal training load due to its low cost and ease of administration. This study examined the agreement between sRPE-derived load scores and heart rate–based training impulse (TRIMP, Banister method) across an 8-week base-training mesocycle in 22 amateur male road cyclists. Participants recorded sRPE within 30 minutes of each session; simultaneously, Polar heart rate monitors logged beat-by-beat data throughout. A total of 347 paired observations were collected. Intraclass correlation between weekly sRPE load and weekly TRIMP was 0.74 (95 % CI: 0.68–0.79). Agreement was stronger during low-intensity sessions (ICC = 0.81) than during high-intensity intervals (ICC = 0.59). Linear mixed models indicated that session duration and perceived effort interacted significantly (p = 0.003). The results suggest sRPE is a reasonable but imperfect proxy, particularly for interval-heavy training weeks, and recommend pairing it with at least partial heart rate monitoring.

title: Power output profiling across varying road gradients in domestic-category road cyclists using on-bike SRM crankset measurement
abstract: Power output distribution is known to vary with terrain, but detailed gradient-stratified profiles are rarely reported for domestic-category cyclists. Fourteen male domestic-category road cyclists wore SRM crankset power meters during 12 competition stages over one regional season (total distance 2,840 km). GPS tracks were matched to a 10 m resolution digital elevation model to assign each pedal stroke a terrain gradient band (< −4 %, −4 to 0 %, 0 to 4 %, 4 to 8 %, > 8 %). Mean power output, normalised power, and variability index were computed per band. Mean power on ascents > 8 % was 312 ± 41 W, compared with 198 ± 28 W on flat terrain. Normalised power–to-body-mass ratio peaked at the 4–8 % gradient band. Variability index was highest on descents, reflecting braking and coasting. These gradient-stratified profiles can inform pacing strategy design and training target selection for this competitive category.

title: Perceived exertion calibration across training phases in competitive cyclists: longitudinal tracking of the Borg CR10 anchoring effect
abstract: The Borg CR10 scale requires individual anchoring to remain meaningful over time, yet longitudinal drift in anchor perception is poorly documented in competitive endurance athletes. This study tracked 18 competitive male road cyclists across a full annual training plan (44 weeks, four mesocycles). At the start of each mesocycle, anchoring sessions were performed at standardised intensities (ventilatory threshold 1, threshold 2, and peak aerobic power). sRPE responses to standardised submaximal efforts were then monitored weekly. Anchor drift—defined as change in CR10 score for the same absolute power output—averaged 0.9 CR10 units across the year, with the largest drift observed between the base and competition phases (0.6 units, p = 0.02). Re-anchoring at mesocycle transitions significantly stabilised scores. Practical implications include recommending re-anchoring procedures after extended low-intensity phases and around major physiological fitness changes.

title: A terrain energy expenditure model for mass-start cycling events: construction and sensitivity analysis
abstract: This paper describes the construction and sensitivity analysis of a terrain-based energy expenditure model applicable to mass-start road cycling events. The model integrates rider mass, bicycle mass, rolling resistance coefficients, aerodynamic drag, road gradient (derived from 5 m resolution lidar), and mean power output measured via hub-based power meters. Model equations follow a mechanical energy balance framework. Sensitivity analysis identified rider frontal area and rolling resistance as the parameters with the highest influence on total predicted energy expenditure (partial variance contributions of 31 % and 24 % respectively). A Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 runs was used to propagate measurement uncertainty. Validation against metabolic cart measurements in six participants on an instrumented 12 km test loop yielded a mean prediction error of 5.3 % (SD 2.1 %). The model and Python implementation are described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Heart rate variability indices as real-time internal load indicators during multi-day cycling stage races
abstract: Monitoring cumulative fatigue during multi-day stage races is practically difficult. This study examined whether morning resting heart rate variability (HRV), specifically the root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), could track accumulated internal load across a simulated five-day stage race in 16 trained male cyclists. External load was quantified daily using gradient-corrected normalised power (GcNP), developed in earlier work by the same group. RMSSD declined progressively across race days (Day 1: 68 ± 12 ms; Day 5: 44 ± 9 ms; p < 0.001 for linear trend). The daily decrement in RMSSD correlated negatively with the previous day's GcNP (r = −0.61, p < 0.001). RMSSD recovered partially after the built-in rest day. These findings support morning RMSSD measurement as a practical, non-invasive cumulative-load indicator and suggest thresholds for rest-day insertion that warrant further investigation in real race conditions.

title: Comparing GPS-derived and power-meter-derived external load metrics in mountain bike cross-country racing
abstract: Mountain bike cross-country (XCO) racing presents highly variable terrain that challenges standard external load quantification methods. This study compared GPS-derived speed and distance metrics with crank-based power meter outputs in 11 competitive XCO riders completing three race-format efforts on a standardised World Cup–style course. GPS-derived mechanical work estimates exceeded power-meter estimates by a mean of 14.2 % (range 9–21 %), with larger discrepancies on steep technical ascents where GPS velocity was underestimated due to canopy interference. Normalised power was more consistent between methods (mean difference 3.1 %). Gradient correction applied to GPS data reduced the overestimation to 6.4 %. The data suggest that in forested or heavily broken terrain, GPS-only external load metrics should be treated with caution, and power meter data should be considered the reference method where feasible.

title: Borg scale response to terrain steepness: an experimental study with recreational cyclists on instrumented climbs
abstract: This conference paper reports a controlled experiment investigating how road gradient influences the relationship between objectively measured intensity and perceived effort on the Borg 6–20 scale. Twenty recreational cyclists (10 men, 10 women; mean age 34 ± 6 years) completed identical relative intensity efforts (65 % and 80 % of peak power output) on flat, 5 %, and 10 % gradient segments of a 4 km instrumented course. Despite matched relative power outputs, RPE scores were significantly higher on the 10 % gradient compared with flat terrain at both intensities (p < 0.05 for both). Biomechanical posture changes and increased lower-limb muscular strain at steep gradients are proposed as contributing factors beyond cardiovascular loading. These findings have practical implications for RPE-based intensity prescriptions used in hilly training contexts.

title: Load quantification in ultra-endurance cycling: a case study across a 600 km unsupported randonneuring event
abstract: Ultra-endurance cycling events lasting 40+ hours impose physiological demands that are poorly characterised in the scientific literature. This paper presents a detailed single-case study of one male trained randonneur completing a 600 km unsupported brevêt. External load was monitored with a crank power meter and a barometric altimeter-equipped GPS unit; internal load was tracked via continuous heart rate recording, daily morning RMSSD, and sRPE collected at each checkpoint (nine in total). Total elevation gain was 7,840 m. Mean power output was 142 W over 43.5 hours of riding; normalised power was 178 W. Heart rate drift of approximately 11 bpm was observed at equivalent power outputs between hours 8 and 36, consistent with cardiovascular drift. RMSSD fell from 71 ms pre-event to 28 ms at the 36-hour checkpoint before stabilising. The findings illustrate method feasibility in extreme field conditions and highlight cardiovascular drift as a major complication for internal–external load coupling models.

title: Validation of a low-cost barometric altimeter pipeline for gradient-corrected energy expenditure estimation in field cycling
abstract: High-resolution elevation data substantially improve energy expenditure estimates in road cycling, but consumer-grade GPS units often have insufficient vertical accuracy. This study validated a pipeline that fuses barometric altimeter data with a post-processed GPS trace and a 5 m lidar digital elevation model to reconstruct per-second terrain gradient. Twelve cyclists completed 18 sessions on three instrumented courses (flat, rolling, and hilly) while wearing both a research-grade barometric logger and a consumer GPS unit. The fused pipeline reduced mean gradient estimation error from 1.8 % (GPS-only) to 0.4 % relative to static reference gradients measured by total station surveying. Corresponding energy expenditure estimates improved from 11.2 % to 4.7 % mean absolute percentage error versus metabolic cart reference. The pipeline is implemented in open-source Python and tested on data from three consumer device brands available at under 350 EUR retail price.

title: Coping Strategy Profiles in Adolescent Athletes Across Different Competitive Sports: A Cross-Sectional Analysis
abstract: This cross-sectional study compared coping strategy profiles among adolescent athletes competing in individual and team sports using the Athletic Coping Skills Inventory-28 (ACSI-28). Participants were 112 athletes (58 individual sport, 54 team sport; aged 14–18 years; 49 female, 63 male) recruited from sports clubs affiliated with the Vojvodina regional sport association. Individual sport athletes scored significantly higher on the coachability subscale (p < 0.05) and concentration subscale (p < 0.01) than team sport athletes. Team sport athletes reported higher scores on the peaking under pressure subscale (p < 0.05). No significant sex differences were found in total ACSI-28 scores, though females scored higher on the goal setting and mental preparation subscale (p < 0.05). Cluster analysis identified three distinct coping profiles across the sample: problem-focused copers, avoidance-prone copers, and balanced copers, with avoidance-prone profiles more prevalent among athletes with self-reported high competitive anxiety. Findings suggest that coping style is partly associated with sport type and competitive anxiety level, and that profiling may assist practitioners in targeting psychological skills training.

title: Parental Involvement Profiles and Their Association with Sustained Participation in Youth Basketball: Evidence from Serbia
abstract: Parents of 278 youth basketball players (aged 10–15, 54% male) in Serbian clubs completed a validated parental involvement scale covering three dimensions: facilitative support, directive involvement, and pressure. Latent profile analysis identified four parental involvement profiles: supportive-low pressure (34%), disengaged (21%), directive-high pressure (27%), and balanced (18%). Children with parents in the directive-high pressure profile had a 3.1-fold greater odds of discontinuing participation within 18 months compared with the supportive-low pressure group (OR = 3.12, 95% CI [1.84, 5.28]). The balanced profile was associated with the highest self-determined motivation scores at follow-up. Findings align with self-determination theory predictions and suggest that parental education programmes embedded in club structures may help sustain participation rates.

title: Between School Sport and Club Pathways: Transition Points and Dropout Risk in Early Adolescence Across Vojvodina
abstract: This mixed-methods study examined the transition from school physical education–based sport to club-based competition as a structural dropout risk point for adolescents in Vojvodina. Survey data were collected from 508 pupils aged 11–13 in 22 primary schools and matched with club registration records over a 24-month follow-up. Of those expressing intent to join a club, 41% did not register within 12 months, and 29% of registrants discontinued within the following 12 months. Qualitative interviews with 18 physical education teachers and 12 parents identified distance to club facilities, registration costs, and perceived selectivity of clubs as key structural barriers. Girls and children from rural municipalities faced compound disadvantage. The study maps specific transition touchpoints where municipalities and clubs could intervene with low-cost measures to reduce early exit.

title: Relationship between maximal isometric grip force and barbell acceleration during the snatch second pull
abstract: Pearson and Spearman correlations were used to examine relationships between maximal isometric grip force (bilateral and unilateral) and peak barbell acceleration during the snatch second pull in 28 competitive male weightlifters from clubs in Serbia and Croatia. Grip force was assessed using a Jamar Plus digital dynamometer; barbell acceleration was derived from a calibrated linear position transducer attached to the barbell. Non-dominant hand grip force showed a moderate positive correlation with peak barbell acceleration (r = 0.51, p = 0.006), while dominant hand grip force showed a weaker correlation (r = 0.38, p = 0.045). The ratio of dominant to non-dominant grip force (asymmetry ratio) was negatively correlated with peak barbell acceleration (r = −0.44, p = 0.019), suggesting that more symmetric grip strength is associated with greater second-pull acceleration. These observational data do not establish causality but support targeted grip-symmetry training as a potentially useful adjunct to technical coaching.

title: Finite-element estimation of solder joint fatigue life in a dual-axis MEMS accelerometer under thermal cycling between −40 °C and 125 °C
abstract: This paper presents a three-dimensional finite-element model of a dual-axis MEMS accelerometer assembled on an FR-4 substrate, developed to estimate solder joint fatigue life under repeated thermal excursions from −40 °C to 125 °C. Material properties for SAC305 solder alloy, silicon die, and FR-4 laminate were obtained through a combination of literature values and in-house laser flash diffusivity measurements. Cyclic plasticity was modelled using an Anand viscoplastic constitutive law calibrated against published strain-rate data. The model predicted fatigue life at the outermost solder balls using the Coffin–Manson approach, yielding a characteristic life of approximately 1 840 cycles for a ramp rate of 10 °C/min with 15-minute dwell times. Results were compared against accelerated thermal cycling experiments conducted on ten identical assemblies, showing agreement within 12%. A mesh sensitivity study and the influence of underfill coverage on predicted stress concentration factors are discussed. The work confirms that underfill extending beneath 60% of the die perimeter reduces the peak accumulated inelastic strain per cycle by roughly 35%.

title: Effect of die-attach void fraction on transient temperature rise in a stacked three-die MEMS pressure sensor assembly
abstract: Voiding in die-attach adhesive layers is a common manufacturing defect that alters the local thermal resistance and can generate hot spots during device operation. This paper quantifies the relationship between void fraction and peak transient temperature in a stacked three-die assembly housing separate pressure, humidity, and temperature sensing elements. Finite-element models with randomly distributed circular voids at void area fractions of 0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, and 30% were generated using a parametric meshing script. Each configuration was subjected to a 50-ms power pulse of 120 mW representative of simultaneous read-out of all three dies. At 30% void fraction, the peak temperature at the bottom die exceeded the void-free case by 18.4 K, while the temperature at the top die increased by only 3.1 K, highlighting the asymmetric sensitivity of stacked architectures. Void location was found to matter more than void fraction alone: a single 15%-equivalent void positioned directly beneath the active region raised temperatures comparably to a uniformly distributed 25% void fraction. Implications for X-ray inspection acceptance thresholds are discussed.

title: Thermomechanical reliability of a quad-sensor MEMS environmental module: comparison of glob-top and moulded compound encapsulation
abstract: Multi-sensor MEMS modules for precision agriculture are increasingly integrated into single housings combining gas, humidity, temperature, and particulate sensing. The choice of encapsulant material significantly affects both the thermal resistance of the assembly and the thermo-mechanical stress experienced by the sensor dies. This study compares glob-top epoxy encapsulation against transfer-moulded epoxy compound in a quad-sensor module through a combined experimental and simulation approach. Finite-element models of both configurations were validated against infrared thermography at three steady-state power levels (50, 100, and 150 mW total). Under a −20 °C to 85 °C thermal cycle, the moulded variant exhibited 28% higher von Mises stress at the silicon–encapsulant interface but provided 15% lower thermal resistance from die to ambient. Delamination risk was assessed using the critical energy release rate criterion; glob-top encapsulation showed margin factors above 2.0 at all interfaces, while the moulded variant showed a margin of 1.4 at the gas sensor die edge. Recommendations for geometric modifications to the mould cavity are provided.

title: Thermal modelling of MEMS-based gas sensor arrays in precision agriculture: chapter on packaging reliability
abstract: This book chapter addresses the reliability challenges arising from the packaging of gas sensor arrays deployed in open-field agricultural monitoring stations, where devices undergo daily and seasonal thermal excursions that span 60–80 K. The chapter begins with a review of relevant failure mechanisms—solder fatigue, delamination, and die cracking—before presenting a hierarchy of modelling approaches ranging from analytical compact models to full three-dimensional finite-element simulations. A case study is presented for a four-element metal-oxide gas sensor array encapsulated in a DIP-16 ceramic package, for which the finite-element model was correlated to thermocouple measurements at six internal locations. The chapter discusses how accelerated thermal cycling test standards developed for automotive electronics (IEC 60068-2-14) translate to field conditions using a damage accumulation framework, and proposes a simplified cycle-counting method suited to data obtained from low-cost on-board temperature loggers. Guidance on selecting conservative safety factors for rural deployment environments with intermittent power supply is also given.

title: Influence of printed circuit board copper fill ratio on junction temperature distribution in a six-die MEMS inertial measurement unit
abstract: Copper fill ratio in the ground and power planes of a PCB is a design parameter that strongly affects the effective in-plane thermal conductivity of the substrate and consequently the temperature distribution across co-located sensor dies. This study investigates the effect of copper fill ratios ranging from 20% to 80% on the steady-state junction temperatures of a six-die MEMS inertial measurement unit using a homogenised anisotropic thermal conductivity model embedded in a finite-element board-level simulation. Material homogenisation was validated against a fully-detailed copper-trace model on a 20 mm × 20 mm coupon, with a maximum temperature deviation of 1.8 K. At 40-mW total dissipation, increasing copper fill from 20% to 80% reduced the hottest die junction temperature by 6.2 K and improved inter-die temperature uniformity by a factor of 1.9. The influence of via density beneath each die was examined as a secondary variable; adding a 4 × 4 thermal via array beneath the hottest die provided an additional 3.4 K reduction independent of copper fill. Results are presented as lookup tables intended for use by layout engineers without access to simulation tools.

title: Cyclic creep accumulation in lead-free solder interconnects of a dual-mode soil moisture MEMS sensor under diurnal temperature profiles from a field measurement campaign
abstract: Standard thermal cycling tests use trapezoidal temperature–time profiles that may not represent the gradual diurnal variations experienced by sensors installed in agricultural fields. This paper uses 14 months of temperature data logged at 15-minute intervals from a soil moisture sensor deployment in Vojvodina to construct statistically representative diurnal load spectra. Rainflow counting identified five dominant cycle classes ranging in amplitude from 8 K to 41 K. A finite-element creep model of the sensor's BGA interconnect layer was driven by each cycle class, and damage fractions were accumulated using Miner's rule. The total predicted fatigue life under the field spectrum was 2.3 times longer than a life prediction based on the IPC-9701 standard test condition, suggesting that standard test profiles are conservative for this deployment environment. Sensitivity of the prediction to dwell time was found to be higher than sensitivity to ramp rate for cycles below 20 K amplitude. The modelling procedure is described in sufficient detail to be applicable to other field-deployed sensor types with minimal modification.
