title: A reduced-order thermal network model for real-time reliability monitoring of a packaged multi-sensor MEMS node in the field
abstract: Full finite-element thermal simulations are computationally impractical for real-time monitoring applications. This paper describes a systematic procedure for extracting a compact thermal network model from a calibrated FE model of a six-sensor environmental MEMS node and embedding it in firmware running on a low-power microcontroller. The network topology was determined by a structured condensation approach retaining 12 nodes, compared to 480 000 elements in the reference FE model. Calibration used 24 steady-state and 8 transient operating conditions; the maximum temperature prediction error of the compact model relative to the FE reference was 2.1 K across all validation cases. Deployed on a Cortex-M4 microcontroller at 48 MHz, the model executes in under 3 ms, enabling a 1-Hz update rate for accumulated damage estimation using an on-chip Palmgren–Miner counter. Over a six-week outdoor pilot in summer 2025, the firmware-resident damage accumulation estimate differed by 7% from a post-hoc FE-based calculation using logged temperature data. The approach enables on-device end-of-life estimation without cloud connectivity.

title: Integrating Sentinel-2 derived nitrogen maps with ground-based active optical sensor readings: a data assimilation approach for within-season management
abstract: Satellite-derived nitrogen status maps provide broad spatial coverage but are limited by revisit frequency and cloud cover; proximal AOS measurements provide high temporal density but cover only the tractor's path. This study developed a data assimilation framework combining Sentinel-2 red-edge band composites (cloud-free acquisitions available on average every 8.4 days during the study period) with tractor-mounted AOS readings collected along pre-planned sampling transects covering roughly 20% of field area. A kriging-based spatial interpolator was used to propagate AOS-corrected nitrogen estimates across the full field, weighting satellite pixels by their agreement with concurrent AOS readings within a 30-m buffer. Applied across three fields (total 210 ha) over two seasons, the fused maps reduced RMS prediction error by 22% relative to satellite-only maps and by 31% relative to kriging from AOS transects alone. The framework was implemented as an open-source QGIS plugin distributed under a BSD licence.

title: Kalman-filter-based plausibility checking for soil temperature sensor arrays with heterogeneous failure modes
abstract: Soil temperature arrays deployed at multiple depths are subject to at least four distinct failure modes: complete open-circuit failure, partial short inducing constant-low readings, slow drift from burial-induced mechanical stress on thermistor leads, and intermittent noise injection from nearby electric fence controllers. This paper applies an ensemble Kalman filter to a seven-sensor vertical array, using a one-dimensional heat diffusion model as the process model parameterised with local soil thermal diffusivity estimates. The filter's innovation sequence is monitored with a chi-squared test to isolate faulty sensors without discarding the ensemble. In a 14-month field deployment at two sites in the Banat region, the method identified all 9 sensor faults confirmed by physical inspection, correctly attributed failure mode in 7 of those cases, and continued providing usable profile estimates from the remaining functional sensors throughout each fault episode. The paper also examines computational feasibility on a Cortex-M4 at 80 MHz, where the 7-state filter update completes in 3.8 ms, making edge execution practical with 30-minute sampling.

title: Functionalised gold nanoparticle amplification of QCM responses in MIP-based sensors for metformin in urine-affected water matrices
abstract: Metformin, a widely prescribed antidiabetic pharmaceutical, is detected at µg L⁻¹ concentrations in municipal wastewater effluents but presents challenges for gravimetric sensing due to its low molecular mass (129 Da). A signal amplification strategy using 15 nm gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) functionalised with metformin-imprinted polymer shells was investigated. AuNP–MIP conjugates were prepared by surface-initiated polymerisation after MAPTMS priming of citrate-stabilised AuNPs. Hydrodynamic diameter of conjugates was 54 ± 6 nm (DLS). In a sandwich-type QCM assay, initial metformin binding to the surface MIP layer was followed by injection of AuNP–MIP conjugate suspension. The amplified signal at 1 µM metformin was –185 Hz compared to –22 Hz without amplification (8.4-fold). The linear range extended from 50 nM to 5 µM (R² = 0.991) and LOD was 18 nM. In synthetic urine-spiked tap water (10% v/v), mean recovery was 96 ± 8% across 12 replicates. Non-specific adsorption of urea and creatinine on AuNP–MIP conjugates was assessed and found to contribute less than 4% to total signal.

title: Metal-oxide chemiresistive sensors for agri-food quality monitoring: materials, mechanisms, and deployment challenges
abstract: This chapter reviews chemiresistive metal-oxide sensor platforms relevant to monitoring fruit ripening indicators (ethylene, ethanol, acetaldehyde) and mycotoxin-related markers (certain aldehydes and terpenes) in food storage and logistics settings. The discussion covers the correlation between microstructural parameters (grain size, porosity, doping) and sensitivity, selectivity, and drift in humid atmospheres representative of real storage environments. Operating strategies including temperature modulation and principal component analysis of multi-sensor arrays are reviewed with reference to published datasets. The chapter also addresses practical constraints: power consumption in mobile deployments, sensor-to-sensor variability in batch production, and calibration stability over 12-month field use. Materials covered include SnO₂, ZnO, WO₃, and TiO₂, with attention to recently reported doped variants. Challenges around interference from ethylene and humidity covariance are discussed in the context of cold-chain monitoring for the regional agri-food sector.

title: Experimental measurement of friction coefficients in steel wire rope contacts under low-velocity sliding
abstract: Static and kinetic friction coefficients between individual wire strands and smooth steel capstan surfaces were measured using a purpose-built sliding rig capable of imposing wrap angles from 30° to 270° and normal loads up to 2 kN. Tests were conducted at sliding velocities between 0.5 and 50 mm/s at room temperature without lubrication. Results for five commercial rope constructions (6×7, 6×19, 6×37, 8×19, and spiral strand) are reported. The classical capstan equation underpredicted the exit tension by 6–18% depending on construction, a discrepancy attributed to interwire contact contributions not captured by the belt-friction model. Kinetic friction coefficients ranged from 0.14 to 0.31 across constructions. Variance between repeat tests was below 4% for all configurations. The dataset provides baseline values for subsequent analytical modelling of bending-stiffness corrections.

title: A corrected capstan model accounting for rope bending stiffness at small wrap angles
abstract: The classical capstan (belt-friction) equation assumes a perfectly flexible, inextensible rope. For steel wire ropes with outer diameters above approximately 8 mm, bending stiffness introduces a non-negligible distributed moment that alters the normal pressure distribution and hence the friction-limited tension ratio. A one-dimensional analytical model was derived by treating the rope as a Timoshenko beam on a circular rigid surface and incorporating Coulomb friction as a distributed tangential traction. The model predicts tension ratio as a function of wrap angle, bending stiffness, and rope tension level. Closed-form expressions were obtained for the limiting cases of very stiff and very flexible ropes. Predictions were validated against experimental data from six rope samples spanning EI values from 1.2 to 47 N·m². Discrepancy between measured and predicted tension ratios was within ±3.5% for wrap angles between 45° and 180°.

title: Stick-slip onset conditions in cable-pulley systems: an energy-based criterion
abstract: Stick-slip motion in cable-driven mechanical systems generates oscillatory forces that cause fatigue damage and positioning errors. This paper develops an energy-based criterion for the onset of stick-slip in a single cable looped over a rigid cylindrical pulley, incorporating bending energy storage during the stuck phase and elastic wave propagation during slip release. The criterion yields a critical ratio of applied velocity to the product of system stiffness and contact compliance. Numerical integration of the governing equations was performed for 120 parameter combinations; in all cases the analytical criterion predicted onset within 8% of the simulated transition velocity. Experiments on a laboratory cable rig using a 10 mm 6×19 rope confirmed the predicted trend. The results suggest that increasing cable tension by 25% or reducing wrap angle by 30° eliminates stick-slip in the tested configuration.

title: Influence of helical lay angle on the apparent friction coefficient in wire rope capstan tests
abstract: Lay angle in helically stranded ropes introduces a systematic geometric effect on the contact angle between outer wires and the capstan surface. This paper reports an experimental and analytical study of the lay-angle influence for rope samples with lay angles ranging from 11° to 24°. Tests were conducted on a motorised capstan rig at a wrap angle of 180° and three rope tension levels (0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 kN). For each sample, the effective friction coefficient inferred from the classical capstan equation was computed and compared with the value obtained from a geometry-corrected model that accounts for the projected contact area modification. The geometry correction reduced the apparent friction coefficient by 9–17%, depending on lay angle. A regression equation relating lay angle to the correction factor is provided. The results have direct implications for the design of drum hoists where multiple rope layers are wound at varying effective lay angles.

title: Tension distribution in a multi-pass capstan drive: combined effect of friction and bending stiffness
abstract: Multi-pass capstan drives, used in cable transport and industrial hoisting, involve the rope contacting the drum or sheave at several successive wrap zones. Tension distribution in these systems is governed by cumulative friction and by elastic bending energy stored and released at each contact zone. A recursive analytical model was developed for an n-pass configuration, extending the single-pass corrected capstan model to account for tension-level-dependent bending stiffness. The model was applied to a two-pass and three-pass laboratory arrangement and compared with strain-gauge measurements at four positions along the cable. Mean prediction error was 2.1% for the two-pass and 4.8% for the three-pass case. A parametric study showed that ignoring bending stiffness overestimates the available friction force by up to 22% in stiff ropes at low tension, which is relevant for safety calculations in overhead crane design.

title: Vibration signatures of stick-slip transitions measured by accelerometry on crane hoist ropes
abstract: Field measurements were performed on four overhead travelling cranes in a metal fabrication facility to record vibration signatures during low-speed lifting operations. Triaxial accelerometers were attached to rope anchor brackets and to the drum housing. Data were acquired at 10 kHz for 45 lifting cycles across loads from 0.5 to 8 t. Stick-slip events were identified as peaks in the lateral rope acceleration exceeding 0.8 m/s² coinciding with a velocity dip in the drive encoder signal. The frequency of such events increased with load and was highest at rope speeds between 0.02 and 0.12 m/s. Dominant frequencies in the stick-slip spectra ranged from 4 to 19 Hz depending on rope length and tension. The data are compared with predictions from a lumped-parameter model, and guidelines for hoist speed control to avoid the critical velocity range are proposed.

title: Temperature rise at rope-sheave contacts under sustained sliding: measurement and simple thermal model
abstract: Frictional heat at rope–sheave contacts is of practical concern because elevated temperature accelerates lubrication degradation and surface oxidation. A laboratory sheave rig was instrumented with thermocouples embedded in the sheave groove at depths of 0.5, 1.5, and 3 mm below the contact surface. Tests were conducted at sliding speeds of 0.05–0.5 m/s, normal loads of 0.3–1.5 kN, and wrap angles of 90° and 180°. Temperature rise at the groove surface reached 38°C above ambient at the highest load and speed combination after 300 s of continuous sliding. A one-dimensional transient thermal model with a moving heat source was fitted to the data; the effective thermal contact conductance was found to be 4 200–6 800 W/m²K depending on load. The model provides a practical tool for estimating contact temperatures in crane and elevator sheave design without recourse to full finite-element analysis.

title: Effect of rope surface roughness and wear state on capstan friction: a controlled abrasion study
abstract: As wire ropes age in service, outer wire surfaces become progressively smoother through running-in wear and then rougher as fatigue pitting develops. To isolate the effect of surface condition, rope samples were abraded in a controlled manner on a rotary tribometer to achieve six surface roughness levels (Ra from 0.3 to 4.1 µm) and tested on the capstan rig at standardised conditions. Friction coefficient increased monotonically from 0.16 to 0.29 over the tested roughness range when all other parameters were held constant. The relationship was well approximated by a power law with exponent 0.31. Additional tests on naturally worn rope segments from two lifting installations confirmed the trend. The findings suggest that friction-based tension calculations should account for rope age and roughness state, and that inspection intervals may need to be shortened when friction coefficient exceeds 0.27 in safety-critical applications.

title: Analytical treatment of rope bending stiffness variation along a curved contact arc
abstract: In real rope–sheave contacts the bending stiffness of the rope is not constant along the contact arc because curvature varies as the rope enters and exits the groove. This paper extends previous corrected capstan models by allowing the bending stiffness to vary as a prescribed function of arc position, derived from the measured moment–curvature relation of five rope constructions. The resulting boundary-value problem is solved numerically using a fourth-order Runge–Kutta scheme with shooting; convergence to within 0.1% relative error is achieved in fewer than 20 iterations. For the softest rope tested, the variable-stiffness model reduced prediction error from 4.8% to 1.9% compared with the constant-stiffness model. For stiffer ropes the improvement was smaller (0.6%). The computational overhead is modest and the method is suitable for integration into design calculation sheets.

title: Rope mechanics in cable-driven rehabilitation devices: friction and compliance considerations
abstract: Cable-driven exoskeletons and rehabilitation robots rely on low-friction, low-compliance rope transmission, yet most mechanical analyses of these devices use the classical capstan equation without correction for the stiff, small-diameter Dyneema and stainless steel cables commonly employed. This book chapter reviews the relevant friction and compliance effects, surveys measurement data from the literature and from the authors' own experiments on cables with diameters from 1.5 to 6 mm, and provides corrected design equations for tension estimation in cable-driven assistive devices. Particular attention is given to stick-slip thresholds at the low actuator velocities typical of rehabilitation tasks (0.005–0.05 m/s). Worked design examples for a wrist exoskeleton and a finger rehabilitation device are included. The chapter also discusses the dependence of stick-slip threshold on cable pre-tension and the implications for control system design.

title: Dynamic tension measurement in hoisting ropes using a fibre-optic strain approach: calibration and field trial
abstract: Accurate real-time measurement of rope tension in operating hoists is required for both condition monitoring and safety enforcement. This study describes the calibration and a six-week field trial of a fibre-optic Bragg grating (FBG) sensor system clamped to the rope anchor bracket of a 12.5 t overhead crane. The calibration procedure uses the capstan-corrected tension model to back-calculate rope tension from measured bracket strain, avoiding the need for an in-line load cell. Calibration was performed against a reference load cell over the full load range; root-mean-square calibration error was 1.4% of full scale. During the field trial, 1 840 lifting cycles were logged. The system correctly identified three overload events exceeding 110% of rated load and captured the characteristic stick-slip oscillation pattern at low hoist speeds, consistent with earlier laboratory findings. System reliability was 99.2% over the trial period.

title: Hygrothermal behaviour of sealed electrical cabinets installed in unheated substations: field measurements and modelling
abstract: Twelve steel electrical cabinets installed in four unheated substations in Vojvodina were instrumented with internal and external temperature–humidity loggers over a 14-month period spanning two winters. Internal relative humidity exceeded 85 % for more than 480 hours per year in cabinets without anti-condensation heaters, with the longest continuous exceedance episode lasting 61 hours. A lumped-parameter hygrothermal model driven by measured exterior boundary conditions reproduced the measured internal humidity with a root-mean-square error of 3.2 percentage points. Model calibration identified the dominant vapour pathway as the cable entry glands rather than the door gasket, accounting for approximately 68 % of total vapour ingress. Anti-condensation heater power requirements derived from the model range from 6 W to 22 W depending on cabinet volume. Recommendations for gland specification and heater sizing are given.

title: Bearing and Gear Fault Signatures in a Combined Drivetrain Assembly: Mutual Interference and Separation Strategies
abstract: In practical drivetrains, bearings and gears are mechanically coupled, and their fault signatures co-exist in a single vibration channel. This study characterises the interference patterns between simultaneously active bearing and gear faults using a modular drivetrain test rig. Eleven fault combination scenarios were tested, including healthy baseline, isolated bearing fault, isolated gear fault, and eight bearing–gear fault combinations of varying severity. Blind source separation using independent component analysis (ICA) is applied to a four-accelerometer array, and the separated components are individually analysed with SES and CS2. For bearing-dominated combinations, ICA recovers bearing signature SNR within 2 dB of the isolated fault case in 9 of 11 scenarios. Gear-dominated combinations are harder to separate, with residual bearing energy leaking into the gear component at levels up to −14 dB. A decision-level fusion rule combining component-level probabilities is proposed and yields 89.7% correct joint diagnosis across all 11 scenarios and 60 repeated runs.
venue: Journal of Mechanical Diagnostics and Reliability

title: Conformal versus straight-drilled cooling channels in injection moulds: a comparative thermal analysis for a thin-walled polypropylene component
abstract: The thermal performance of conformal cooling channels, produced by selective laser sintering of H13 tool steel, was compared with conventional straight-drilled channels in a mould for a thin-walled polypropylene lid (projected area 180 cm²). Steady-state and transient thermal simulations were performed using a boundary-element heat-transfer solver. Conformal channels with a 6 mm diameter and constant 10 mm distance to the cavity surface reduced average cycle time from 18.4 s to 13.1 s (29%) and reduced the maximum temperature difference across the cavity face from 22.4 °C to 8.7 °C. Warpage in the ejected part was predicted using a decoupled shrinkage model and validated against CMM measurements on 30 production parts. Conformal channels reduced peak warpage from 0.54 mm to 0.28 mm. Material costs and manufacturing complexity of the conformal insert are discussed quantitatively, with a break-even analysis indicating viability above 80 000 parts.

title: Fatigue Life Estimation of Thin-Web Flexure Hinges Under Variable-Amplitude Cyclic Bending
abstract: Flexure hinges in precision mechanisms are routinely subjected to cyclic loading over millions of cycles, yet most published life estimates rely on constant-amplitude S–N data without accounting for variable-amplitude spectra. This paper applies the rainflow cycle-counting method together with Miner's linear damage rule to estimate the fatigue life of thin-web circular flexure hinges made from two spring steels (X10CrNi18-8 and 42CrMo4) under three representative variable-amplitude bending spectra derived from experimental measurements on a laboratory micro-positioning stage. Finite-element-based stress analysis provides local stress amplitudes at the hinge throat for each counted cycle. Predicted lives ranged from 1.2 × 10⁶ to 8.7 × 10⁷ cycles depending on material and spectrum, with 42CrMo4 outperforming X10CrNi18-8 under the high-mean-stress spectrum by a factor of approximately 3.4. Experimental fatigue tests were conducted on twelve specimens; predicted lives agreed with measured lives within a factor of 2.1 in all cases, consistent with standard engineering fatigue scatter. The study provides a practical workflow for life estimation in the early design stage without requiring dedicated component-level fatigue testing.

title: Steady-state thermal load model for a class C refrigerated semi-trailer under Central European summer conditions
abstract: A lumped-parameter steady-state model was developed to predict the thermal load on a 13.6 m class C refrigerated semi-trailer travelling on a representative route between Novi Sad and Vienna. Panel thermal conductance was measured on six insulated wall samples using a calibrated hot-box apparatus, yielding effective U-values between 0.38 and 0.44 W/m²K. Solar radiation on the roof surface was accounted for using an equivalent ambient temperature correction derived from six months of measured road-side irradiance data. The model predicted internal air temperature with a mean absolute error of 0.6 °C compared with data from 22 instrumented commercial runs. Sensitivity analysis showed that door-opening frequency during multi-stop delivery contributes between 11 and 18 % of the total daily thermal load, a factor often underestimated in standard certification procedures. Results were compared against ATP-equivalent steady-state calculations, and deviations of up to 9 % were identified at ambient temperatures above 35 °C.

title: Measurement of effective thermal transmittance of polyurethane-foam insulated panels after accelerated ageing
abstract: Fifteen polyurethane-foam sandwich panels identical in specification to those used in commercial refrigerated body construction were subjected to controlled ageing cycles replicating five years of service exposure: repeated thermal cycling between −20 °C and +40 °C, mechanical vibration at 5–50 Hz, and periodic humidity exposure. Hot-box measurements were performed before ageing and after 500, 1000, 2000 and 3000 hours of exposure. Mean effective thermal conductivity of the foam core increased from 0.023 W/mK at baseline to 0.029 W/mK after 3000 hours, a rise of approximately 26 %. The outer glass-fibre-reinforced polyester skins showed delamination beginning at roughly 1500 hours, which correlated with a step increase in measured transmittance. The study provides experimentally derived ageing correction factors that can be applied in thermal load models using panel age as an input parameter. Findings suggest that ATP re-certification intervals may need adjustment for high-humidity operational environments.

title: Parameter estimation for a reciprocating compressor model from limited manufacturer data
abstract: Transport refrigeration unit compressors are typically characterised by manufacturer performance maps that cover only a subset of the operating envelope encountered in transient route simulations. This paper presents a parameter estimation procedure for a semi-empirical reciprocating compressor model using a constrained least-squares approach applied to 48 data points from published performance tables and 12 additional measurements from a laboratory test rig. The model, based on a modified Winandy–Saavedra–Lebrun formulation, achieved a root-mean-square error of 1.8 % for cooling capacity and 2.3 % for shaft power across the extrapolated operating range. A Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis quantified the effect of measurement noise on estimated parameters. The resulting model was integrated into a full TRU simulation and showed improved temperature prediction accuracy compared with simple polynomial fits, particularly at evaporating temperatures below −10 °C relevant for frozen cargo applications.

title: Influence of refrigerant charge level on the energy performance of a small transport refrigeration unit
abstract: Refrigerant charge level in transport refrigeration units drifts over service life due to minor leaks at shaft seals and fittings. An experimental study was conducted on a 3.5 t van-mounted TRU operating with R-452A refrigerant at four charge levels: 90 %, 100 %, 110 % and 120 % of the nominal charge. Measurements were taken at steady state in a climate-controlled chamber at 25 °C and 35 °C ambient, with the cargo box loaded to 50 % of its rated thermal mass. Coefficient of performance degraded by 8.3 % at 90 % charge and by 6.1 % at 120 % charge relative to nominal, consistent with increased subcooling at overcharge reducing suction superheat. Pull-down time from +20 °C to +4 °C cargo air temperature increased by 14 % at 90 % charge. The results are intended to support maintenance interval recommendations for fleet operators.

title: Modelica-based object-oriented modelling of a vapour-compression refrigeration cycle for transport applications
abstract: A component library for vapour-compression refrigeration cycles tailored to transport refrigeration units was developed within the Modelica/Dymola environment. Components include a variable-speed scroll compressor, a fin-and-tube condenser with air-side fan, a thermostatic expansion valve, and a plate evaporator, each described by physics-based equations with parameters identified from published data or laboratory measurements. The library supports continuous thermal boundary conditions derived from interpolated ambient temperature profiles and variable cargo thermal mass. Validation was carried out against a 48-hour instrumented road test of a refrigerated trailer hauling frozen fish from Novi Sad to Thessaloniki. Simulated cargo air temperature matched measured values with a maximum deviation of 1.1 °C; compressor cycling frequency agreed within 7 %. The library is modular and allows component substitution for alternative refrigerants without structural model changes.

title: Assessment of phase-change material integration in refrigerated van bodies for short urban delivery routes
abstract: Phase-change material (PCM) panels with a melting point of +2 °C were integrated into the ceiling and side walls of a standard 3.5 t refrigerated van body to provide thermal buffering during compressor-off periods. Three configurations were tested: ceiling only (20 kg PCM), ceiling and sides (38 kg PCM), and sides only (18 kg PCM). Experiments were conducted in a temperature-controlled hall at 28 °C ambient with the van loaded with 200 kg of fresh produce. The ceiling-and-sides configuration extended the compressor-off tolerable period by 47 minutes compared with the baseline before cargo temperature exceeded +6 °C, at the cost of a 38 kg payload penalty. A simple cost–benefit analysis based on fuel price, payload loss and TRU maintenance cost per operating hour was performed for a representative 200-day delivery season in Vojvodina. The ceiling-only configuration showed a positive net present value over five years for operators running more than 7 stops per day.

title: Effect of ambient humidity on condenser performance and compressor discharge temperature in refrigerated transport units
abstract: High relative humidity reduces the effective temperature difference available for heat rejection at the air-cooled condenser of a TRU, particularly when partial condensation of moisture on the fins occurs. This study presents measurements from a controlled outdoor test facility at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad, where a production TRU was operated over 90 test days spanning spring and summer with ambient temperatures between 18 °C and 39 °C and relative humidity between 28 % and 87 %. Compressor discharge temperature increased by an average of 4.2 °C per 10 percentage points of relative humidity increase when ambient temperature exceeded 32 °C, compared with 1.8 °C at 22 °C ambient. Condenser fan power increased by up to 12 % at maximum humidity conditions to maintain acceptable discharge pressure. An empirical correction to condenser heat-transfer coefficient as a function of humidity is proposed and validated against the collected dataset.

title: Energy mapping of a chilled food distribution fleet in Vojvodina: fuel consumption, idle time, and route-temperature correlation
abstract: Telematics and on-board diagnostic data from a fleet of 24 refrigerated vehicles operated by a regional chilled food distributor in Vojvodina were analysed over a 12-month period comprising approximately 340 000 km of operation. TRU fuel consumption was separated from traction fuel using calibrated secondary fuel meters installed during a four-week instrumented sub-study on six representative vehicles. Mean TRU fuel consumption across the fleet was 1.14 L/100 km, with a standard deviation of 0.31 L/100 km attributable primarily to ambient temperature, delivery stop frequency, and cargo loading pattern. Idle time (engine running, vehicle stationary, TRU operating) accounted for 31 % of total TRU operating hours. Route ambient temperature explained 42 % of variance in daily TRU fuel consumption in a multivariate regression model. The dataset provides a baseline for evaluating technology interventions such as electric standby, PCM buffering, and route optimisation.

title: Simulation-based comparison of R-404A, R-452A and R-454C in a transport refrigeration cycle under variable ambient conditions
abstract: The phase-down of HFCs under the Kigali Amendment and EU F-gas regulations is driving refrigerant transitions in transport refrigeration. This paper compares R-404A (the incumbent), R-452A (a widely adopted interim blend) and R-454C (a low-GWP HFO/HFC blend) in the validated Modelica TRU model, using three ambient temperature profiles representing a typical Danube region summer day, a hot spell day (peak 41 °C), and a mild day (peak 22 °C). Across the summer-day profile, R-454C achieved a COP 3.1 % higher than R-452A and 6.8 % higher than R-404A, with pull-down time from +20 °C to +4 °C 4.2 minutes shorter than R-404A. Compressor discharge temperature for R-454C was 7 °C lower than R-404A on the hot spell day, reducing thermal stress. Mild flammability (A2L classification) implications for van-body sealing requirements are discussed qualitatively.

title: Thermal load modelling for mixed fresh and frozen compartments in a dual-temperature refrigerated trailer
abstract: Dual-temperature trailers that carry both chilled (+2 °C to +4 °C) and frozen (−18 °C to −20 °C) compartments present modelling challenges because the partition wall between compartments is a significant internal heat source for the frozen zone. A two-zone dynamic model was developed and validated against 11 instrumented commercial runs of a dual-temperature semi-trailer operated on routes from Novi Sad to destinations in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia. The partition wall thermal resistance was characterised independently in laboratory conditions. Simulations showed that heat flux through the partition wall accounted for 18–24 % of the total thermal load on the frozen compartment under the operating conditions studied, a larger fraction than estimated in design calculations that neglect transient cargo loading states. Compressor scheduling was analysed and a load-priority switching algorithm that reduced total TRU energy consumption by 5.4 % per trip was proposed and tested in simulation.

title: Electric standby operation of transport refrigeration units at urban loading docks: measured energy consumption and thermal performance
abstract: Electric standby (shore-power) connections allow refrigerated vehicle TRUs to operate from the grid during loading-dock dwell, replacing diesel consumption. This study reports measured energy and thermal data from eight refrigerated vehicles equipped with electric standby capability at two distribution centres in Novi Sad over a nine-month monitoring period covering 1 240 individual dock visits. Mean dock dwell time was 38 minutes. Electric energy consumed per dock visit averaged 0.74 kWh for chilled vehicles and 1.31 kWh for frozen vehicles. Grid-side power demand peaked at 3.8 kW per vehicle during initial pull-down after hot-unload events. Temperature recovery curves were parameterised and used to update boundary conditions in the dynamic simulation model for subsequent route segments. Infrastructure cost calculations suggest payback periods of 3.2 to 5.8 years depending on diesel price and annual dock call frequency, without accounting for emission zone compliance incentives.

title: Empirical Characterisation of Residential Electricity Load Variability in Central Serbia Using Clustering Techniques
abstract: Accurate load profile models are a prerequisite for storage sizing studies, yet data from Serbian distribution networks remain scarce in the open literature. This paper presents analysis of smart meter records collected from 214 residential customers connected to a low-voltage feeder in the Šumadija region over 18 months. Data gaps of up to 6% were imputed using a k-nearest-neighbour approach. Hierarchical agglomerative clustering with Ward linkage identified six representative daily load archetypes, distinguished primarily by morning peak timing, evening ramp steepness, and weekend flattening. Seasonal modulation coefficients are provided for each archetype. The resulting synthetic profile library was validated against an independent set of 40 metered households achieving a mean absolute percentage error below 9% on daily energy totals. The dataset and clustering code are made available as supplementary material for use in sizing and simulation studies.

title: Benchmark of rule-based and model-predictive control strategies for a PV–compressor–chiller utility cluster under Serbian TOU tariffs
abstract: Three control strategies—a rule-based heuristic, a receding-horizon model-predictive controller with a 24-hour lookahead, and a hybrid combining both—are compared on a simulated utility cluster consisting of a 30 kWp PV array, a 75 kW screw compressor, and a 40 kW scroll chiller serving a light-manufacturing building. The cluster model was calibrated against measurement data from a partner company in the Novi Sad industrial zone. Each strategy was evaluated over 365 simulated days using 2022 measured irradiation and load data, with energy cost computed against the current Serbian three-period TOU tariff for industrial consumers. The model-predictive controller achieved 14.2% lower annual energy cost than the baseline rule-based strategy; the hybrid reached 13.7%. Computational demand of the MPC was 6–9 seconds per optimisation cycle on a standard embedded controller, which is compatible with 15-minute tariff intervals. The rule-based strategy outperformed MPC on days with cloud-induced forecast error exceeding 25% of daily yield.

title: Ground thermal recharge potential of hybrid ground-source heat pump systems using air-side heat rejection: a parametric study for the Pannonian climate
abstract: Hybrid ground-source heat pump systems combine a borehole field with an auxiliary air-cooled heat rejecter to reduce ground thermal imbalance in heating-dominated climates. However, the efficiency benefit depends on the frequency and duration of periods when ambient air temperature is low enough to make air-side heat rejection thermodynamically and economically justified. This parametric study uses 30 years of measured meteorological data from Novi Sad (1990–2020) to establish the recharge potential and quantifies it for three building archetypes: a detached house, a multi-family block, and an office building. For the detached house with a thermal imbalance ratio of 2.9, the hybrid strategy reduces the 20-year borehole field temperature depression from 3.8 K to 1.9 K and improves the lifecycle SCOP by 9 %. For the office building, where cooling loads are more significant, the benefit is smaller (4 % SCOP improvement). A dimensionless recharge index is proposed to characterise the local climatic suitability for hybrid operation.

title: Working-fluid charge management in small ORC systems: modelling and experimental study of charge-sensitive performance
abstract: The total working-fluid charge significantly affects performance in small hermetically sealed ORC systems where no external fluid reservoir is used. This paper develops a charge-sensitive model that tracks fluid inventory across component volumes, allowing the simulation of performance changes caused by charge depletion due to slow leakage or deliberate adjustment. The model was implemented for the laboratory rig charged with R1234ze(E) and validated at five charge levels between 80% and 115% of nominal. At 85% charge, measured net power fell by 9.3% relative to nominal due to reduced evaporating pressure and increased superheat; at 115% charge, measured condenser subcooling increased to 8.1 °C, reducing pump cavitation risk but lowering efficiency by 2.1%. An explicit charge-sensitive expander inlet quality indicator was derived that correlates with net output within ±1.8% across the tested range. The model is useful for condition monitoring and for optimising charge in field installations where heat-source temperature deviates from the design value.

title: Experimental validation of a CO₂ transcritical refrigeration test rig at the University of Novi Sad: instrumentation, steady-state protocol, and uncertainty analysis
abstract: This paper documents the small-scale CO₂ transcritical test rig commissioned at the Thermal Systems Laboratory, Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad. The rig has a nominal cooling capacity of 3.2 kW (MT circuit) with adjustable high-side pressure between 70 bar and 120 bar, controlled via an electronic expansion valve and a back-pressure regulator. Instrumentation consists of eight T-type thermocouples (±0.3 K), four pressure transducers (±0.15 % FS), and a Coriolis mass-flow meter (±0.1 % reading). A GUM-compliant uncertainty analysis gives expanded COP uncertainty of ±4.2 % at a 95 % confidence level. Steady-state validation runs were conducted at ambient temperatures of 25 °C, 30 °C, 35 °C, and 38 °C, with measured COP values of 3.41, 3.08, 2.71, and 2.44 respectively. Simulated values from the EES model deviate by no more than 3.8 % across all conditions. The dataset is made available as supplementary material to support further validation work in the region.

title: Incorporating stack voltage degradation into electrolyser sizing optimisation for curtailed solar photovoltaic electricity
abstract: Stack voltage increases over operating lifetime as electrodes and diaphragms age, reducing hydrogen output per unit energy input. This work embeds a linear degradation rate (expressed in mV per full-load equivalent hour) into a mixed-integer linear programme that sizes the electrolyser stack, rectifier, and buffer storage for a solar PV plant in northern Serbia with measured hourly curtailment profiles over three years. The model selects stack rated current and a planned replacement schedule simultaneously with storage volume. Results show that ignoring degradation underestimates optimum stack capacity by 12–18% and overestimates 20-year net present value by up to 9%. Sensitivity to degradation rate uncertainty (±40%) was assessed; stack oversizing of 8–11% relative to the deterministic optimum provides near-optimal robustness across the tested range. Case studies at three curtailment levels (5%, 15%, and 25% of annual generation) are presented.

title: Shear Strength Variability of Weathered Marl from the Fruška Gora Southern Slopes: A Statistical Characterisation
abstract: Weathered marl outcrops along the southern piedmont of Fruška Gora exhibit pronounced spatial variability in cohesion and friction angle, complicating deterministic stability analyses. This study reports triaxial and direct shear test results from 87 samples collected at six cut-slope sites along the Novi Sad–Irig road corridor. Coefficients of variation for effective cohesion ranged from 28 % to 44 %, while those for friction angle ranged from 9 % to 16 %. Probability distributions were fitted using maximum-likelihood estimation; a lognormal model provided the best fit for cohesion at five of six sites. The compiled dataset provides a regional baseline for probabilistic geotechnical design in marl formations and is compared with published data from geologically similar terrains in Hungary and Croatia. Implications for characteristic-value selection under Eurocode 7 are discussed.

title: One-Dimensional Infiltration Modelling in Collapsible Loess Under Simulated Rainfall: Comparison of Green–Ampt and Richards Equation Approaches
abstract: Loess deposits on the Fruška Gora foothills are susceptible to wetting-induced collapse and slope failure triggered by prolonged rainfall events. This paper applies both the Green–Ampt model and the full Richards equation to rainfall-infiltration scenarios derived from 30-year rainfall records at Sremski Karlovci station. Column experiments using undisturbed loess samples (dry density 1.41–1.52 Mg/m³) provided soil water characteristic curves and hydraulic conductivity functions used to parameterise the models. The Richards equation reproduced observed wetting-front depths to within 8 % on average, whereas Green–Ampt errors reached 22 % during low-intensity prolonged events. Sensitivity analysis identified saturated hydraulic conductivity as the dominant parameter controlling infiltration depth. Results support the use of the Richards equation in site-specific slope stability assessments despite its higher parameterisation demand.

title: Limit Equilibrium Versus Finite Element Limit Analysis for Cut Slopes in Layered Loess–Marl Profiles
abstract: Stability assessments of cut slopes often rely on limit equilibrium methods despite their inability to capture progressive failure and kinematic constraints. This study compares factors of safety obtained from Spencer's limit equilibrium method, strength reduction finite element analysis (SRFEA), and finite element limit analysis (FELA) using upper- and lower-bound theorems for twelve cross-sections from three road cuts in Vojvodina. Stratigraphy at each site included alternating loess and weathered marl layers with total depths of 8–14 m. FELA upper- and lower-bound solutions bracketed SRFEA results within 4 % in ten of twelve cases, providing confidence in all three approaches for simple geometries. For cross-sections with inclined marl interbeds dipping toward the cut face, FELA lower bounds fell up to 11 % below Spencer results, suggesting non-conservative outcomes from limit equilibrium in those configurations. The findings recommend FELA for final design checks at such sites.

title: Probabilistic Slope Stability Assessment Using First-Order Reliability Method and Monte Carlo Simulation: Application to a Loess Cut Slope Near Beočin
abstract: Deterministic factors of safety mask the influence of parameter uncertainty on slope performance. This paper applies both the first-order reliability method (FORM) and Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) with 10,000 realisations to a 9.5 m high loess cut slope near the Beočin cement quarry access road. Input random variables are effective cohesion, friction angle, saturated hydraulic conductivity, and initial suction, characterised from 64 laboratory tests. FORM and MCS probabilities of failure agreed to within one order of magnitude for target probability levels above 10⁻³ but diverged for smaller probabilities, where FORM underestimated risk. Sensitivity indices from both methods consistently identified friction angle and hydraulic conductivity as the two most influential variables. A reliability-based design chart is produced for slope angles between 45° and 70° and rainfall return periods of 10, 25, and 100 years, providing a practical design aid for highway planners in the region.

title: Soil Water Characteristic Curves of Loess–Marl Transition Zones and Their Influence on Transient Pore Pressure Development
abstract: The interface between loess and underlying marl creates hydraulic contrasts that trap perched water during rainfall and elevate pore pressures at depths critical for slope stability. This study measures soil water characteristic curves (SWCCs) for both materials and their transition zone using the filter paper method and a pressure plate apparatus for suctions from 0.1 to 1500 kPa. Seventeen field piezometer records from three instrumented slopes over two years are compared with transient seepage simulations using OpenGeoSys. The simulated pore pressure build-up at the loess–marl contact reproduced observed peaks within 15 % for six of eight monitored rainfall events. Events with antecedent rainfall indices above 40 mm/14 days showed the strongest pore pressure response, supporting event-based early-warning thresholds. The SWCC dataset is provided as supplementary material to facilitate regional comparisons.

title: Spatial Correlation of Geotechnical Parameters in Loess Deposits: Autocorrelation Length Estimation from CPTu Soundings
abstract: Random field models for slope reliability analyses require autocorrelation length estimates that are rarely available for Vojvodina loess. This study analyses 22 cone penetration tests with pore pressure measurement (CPTu) performed at seven sites across the Fruška Gora piedmont and Srem plateau. Vertical autocorrelation lengths for normalised cone resistance (Qtn) were estimated by fitting exponential and squared-exponential correlation models using method-of-moments and maximum-likelihood estimators. Vertical scales of fluctuation ranged from 0.35 m to 1.10 m, consistent with typical loess lamination thicknesses observed in nearby exposures. Horizontal autocorrelation lengths were estimated from cross-sounding correlation at two sites with closely spaced profiles (5–20 m spacing) and ranged from 12 to 31 m. The derived correlation structure parameters are incorporated into a random field slope stability example using the local average subdivision method, demonstrating that ignoring spatial correlation overestimates failure probability by factors of 2–5 for shallow failure modes.

title: Effect of Vegetation Root Reinforcement on the Stability of Shallow Slopes in Weathered Loess: A Finite Element Parametric Study
abstract: Shallow failures in loess slopes during intense summer storms frequently involve root-reinforced topsoil layers. This paper implements the Wu root reinforcement model within a 2D plane-strain finite element framework to investigate how root tensile strength, density, and depth distribution affect factors of safety and failure mechanisms for slopes with heights of 1.5–4.5 m and angles of 40°–65°. Root reinforcement was treated as an anisotropic cohesion increment parameterised from pull-out tests on three grass and shrub species commonly found on Fruška Gora slopes. Simulations show that even low root reinforcement values (5–10 kPa additional cohesion) increase factors of safety by 15–30 % for shallow planar failures while having negligible influence on deeper rotational modes. A simplified design chart is derived to guide vegetation-based slope protection decisions. Results are broadly consistent with field failure inventories collected after two heavy-rain episodes in 2017 and 2020.

title: Finite Element Limit Analysis of Rainfall-Triggered Slope Failures: Coupling Transient Seepage with Bound Theorems
abstract: Coupling transient seepage analysis with limit analysis allows time-varying safety factors to be computed during a rainfall event without iterative strength-reduction procedures. This paper describes an implementation in which pore pressure fields from a Richards-equation seepage model are passed at successive time steps into upper- and lower-bound FELA, using linear programming with 6-noded triangular elements and discontinuous stress and velocity fields. The procedure is applied to a 12 m cut slope in Fruška Gora marl subjected to a 72-hour design storm derived from frequency analysis of Novi Sad meteorological records (1961–2019). Factors of safety drop from 1.63 (dry antecedent conditions) to 1.08 at 61 hours, with the lower bound trailing the upper bound by less than 6 % throughout the event. The time to critical safety factor is sensitive to initial suction distribution; a 20 % reduction in initial suction advances the critical time by 9 hours. The method is computationally tractable on a standard workstation, completing a 72-step analysis in under 40 minutes.

title: Early Warning Thresholds for Rainfall-Induced Slope Failures on the Fruška Gora Piedmont: A Reliability-Based Approach
abstract: Rainfall thresholds for slope failure are commonly derived empirically from landslide inventories, but reliability-based thresholds explicitly account for geotechnical parameter uncertainty. This study defines critical rainfall intensity–duration (I–D) thresholds for three slope typologies in the Fruška Gora piedmont (loess-only, loess-over-marl, and incised valley flanks in marl) by setting a target failure probability of 10⁻³ per event. For each typology, 500 Monte Carlo realisations of the coupled seepage–FELA model are run for a grid of I–D combinations. The resulting I–D threshold curves lie 15–30 % below empirically derived thresholds from regional landslide records compiled over 1980–2021, suggesting that purely empirical thresholds may underestimate risk for lower-frequency, high-intensity events. Integration with the Vojvodina Meteorological Agency's nowcast data is discussed as a pathway toward operational slope warning. Limitations related to spatial homogeneity assumptions are acknowledged.

title: Geotechnical Characterisation of Road Cut Failures Along the Fruška Gora Corridor: Post-Failure Back-Analysis Using FELA
abstract: Three slope failures that occurred during the autumn 2021 rainfall season on access roads to Fruška Gora National Park were investigated through field mapping, borehole drilling, and laboratory testing. Post-failure geometries were surveyed by UAV-based photogrammetry, yielding digital terrain models with ±3 cm vertical accuracy. Back-analysis using FELA with pore pressures estimated from the nearest recording piezometer at the time of failure produced back-calculated friction angles of 17°–21° for the marl layers, consistent with residual strength values from ring shear tests performed on remoulded samples. Cohesion back-calculated to near-zero values in all three cases, corroborating the hypothesis of progressive strength loss along pre-existing fissures. The back-analysed strength parameters fall within the lower quartile of the regional database compiled in earlier work, and the implications for conservative parameter selection in new design are discussed.

title: Reliability of Retaining Structures Supporting Cut Slopes in Loess: Influence of Hydraulic Boundary Conditions on Design Outcomes
abstract: Retaining walls in loess terrain perform very differently depending on whether drainage provisions behind the wall are maintained. This paper conducts a parametric reliability study for three retaining wall configurations (cantilever, anchored sheet pile, and gravity wall) supporting 6 m cuts in loess under transient infiltration. Pore pressure histories are generated from the Richards-equation seepage model for 20-, 50-, and 100-year return-period storms. For each storm and wall type, 2000 Monte Carlo realisations are performed with random shear strength, hydraulic conductivity, and wall geometry tolerance as input variables. The probability of exceeding limiting active earth pressure increases by a factor of 3–8 for blocked drainage compared to functioning drainage under the 100-year storm. Failure to maintain drainage is identified as a more influential factor than parameter variability for all wall types. Design recommendations for drainage inspection intervals are proposed based on the reliability results.

title: Probabilistic Assessment of Climate-Change Effects on Slope Stability in the Fruška Gora Region Using Downscaled Rainfall Projections
abstract: Regional climate projections for Serbia indicate increases in short-duration rainfall intensity under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios by mid-century, with potential implications for slope failure frequencies in susceptible terrain. This study takes downscaled daily precipitation projections from the CORDEX-EUR-11 ensemble (five models) for the 2041–2060 horizon and derives design storm intensities through extreme-value frequency analysis. The updated storm inputs feed into the coupled transient seepage–FELA reliability framework for the three Fruška Gora slope typologies characterised in earlier work. Results indicate that median failure probabilities increase by 18–42 % under RCP4.5 and 31–67 % under RCP8.5 relative to the 1981–2010 baseline, with loess-over-marl slopes showing the largest sensitivity. Uncertainty from climate model spread dominates over geotechnical parameter uncertainty for longer return periods. The analysis provides a quantitative basis for prioritising slope maintenance budgets on regional road networks under projected climate change, though limitations of the downscaling approach are discussed in detail.

title: Harmonising land parcel data across administrative boundaries: a comparison of procedural approaches under the INSPIRE Land Cover and Cadastral Parcels themes
abstract: Cross-border harmonisation of cadastral parcel datasets is required by the INSPIRE directive but remains challenging in practice due to differing national data models, geometry encodings, and attribute semantics. This paper compares three procedural approaches—direct attribute mapping, intermediate conceptual schema mediation, and instance-level transformation using feature manipulation—applied to a paired dataset of 28 000 parcels along a section of the Croatian-Serbian boundary. Data were obtained from the Croatian State Geodetic Administration and the Serbian Real Estate Cadastre for a 15 km stretch of the Danube floodplain. Attribute alignment covered parcel identifier structures, tenure type classifications, and area measurement methods. Geometric discrepancies at the boundary line reached up to 4.2 m, attributable to independent densification of the state border base. The paper quantifies attribute mapping completeness (87–94% depending on approach), geometry reconciliation rate, and processing time, and recommends a hybrid schema-mediation approach for routine operational use.

title: Accuracy Assessment of Seven-Parameter Helmert Transformation Between the Serbian National Datum and ETRS89
abstract: This study evaluates the positional accuracy achievable when converting coordinates from the Serbian national reference frame D96/TM to ETRS89 using a classical seven-parameter Helmert transformation. A set of 84 geodetic control points distributed across Vojvodina and central Serbia, with coordinates determined by static GNSS observations processed with Bernese 5.2, was used to estimate transformation parameters by least-squares adjustment. Root-mean-square residuals were computed separately for the northern lowland region and the southern hilly terrain. Results indicate RMS values of 3.1 cm and 7.8 cm respectively, confirming that a single rigid-body transformation is insufficient for cadastral-grade work across the full national territory. Parameter correlation analysis shows strong coupling between the Z-translation and the rotation around the X-axis. The study recommends partitioning the national network into at least three transformation zones before applying seven-parameter models for applications requiring sub-decimetre accuracy.

title: Semi-automated generation of Level of Detail 3 IFC models from airborne LiDAR and oblique imagery for urban infrastructure asset management
abstract: Municipal asset management systems increasingly require georeferenced 3D models of road networks, retaining walls, and drainage structures at LOD 3 detail. This paper describes a semi-automated pipeline combining airborne LiDAR point clouds (8 pts/m²) with oblique photogrammetric imagery for a 2.4 km² test area in a medium-sized Serbian town. LiDAR provides accurate geometric primitives while oblique imagery supplies surface material classification. The pipeline segments ground and above-ground infrastructure classes, fits parametric IFC objects to segments, and assigns material attributes from image-derived classifications. Manual operator time was 11 hours for the test area versus an estimated 140 hours for conventional survey-based modelling. Geometric accuracy of generated objects was assessed against 210 check measurements; 82 % met a 10 cm tolerance threshold. The paper discusses integration with an existing GIS-based asset management system used by the municipality and identifies drainage structures as the class with lowest automation reliability.

title: Effect of sodium sulphate concentration on the durability index of alkali-activated fly ash mortars: an accelerated immersion study
abstract: Mortars based on Class F fly ash activated with NaOH + sodium silicate (Ms = 1.0, Na2O = 6 wt%) were immersed in Na2SO4 solutions of 1, 3, 5 and 10 wt% concentration for 365 days. A durability index (DI) was constructed from normalised values of compressive strength retention, mass change and linear expansion measured at 90, 180 and 365 days. At 1 wt% solution, DI remained above 0.85 throughout the test. At 5 wt%, DI dropped to 0.71 at 365 days; at 10 wt%, to 0.54. SEM cross-sections showed progressive gypsum precipitation in surface layers at concentrations above 3 wt%. Chloride diffusion coefficients measured by the rapid chloride migration test on reference specimens not exposed to sulphate were 4.1 × 10−12 m2 s−1, indicating low permeability in the undamaged material. The DI framework is proposed as a straightforward comparative tool for screening binder compositions before full-scale testing.

title: A Practical Workflow for Integrating Hydrostatic Levelling Sensor Drift Correction into Periodic Network Adjustment
abstract: Long-term hydrostatic levelling installations suffer from sensor drift caused by sediment accumulation, membrane ageing, and temperature creep in the connecting fluid. This paper describes a calibration and correction workflow developed and tested on a six-sensor HLS installed in the inspection gallery of a concrete weir structure operated by a Vojvodina water management authority since 2021. Sensor drift was characterised through periodic zero-point checks against co-located precise levelling observations at approximately 90-day intervals. A linear drift model per sensor was estimated within a combined adjustment that treats both HLS readings and spirit levelling height differences as observations. Over 30 months, individual sensor drift rates ranged from 0.04 mm per month to 0.19 mm per month. Application of drift corrections reduced the residual discrepancy between adjusted HLS and spirit levelling heights from 1.3 mm RMS to 0.4 mm RMS. The workflow is described in sufficient detail to be reproducible with standard geodetic adjustment software.

title: Change Readiness as a Predictor of ERP Implementation Outcome in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
abstract: This paper examines the relationship between pre-implementation change readiness scores and project outcome in a sample of 47 manufacturing SMEs in the Vojvodina region that adopted ERP systems between 2005 and 2009. Change readiness was operationalised through a 24-item questionnaire adapted from Armenakis's readiness model, administered to top and middle management six months prior to go-live. Implementation outcome was assessed using a composite index combining schedule adherence, budget deviation, and user satisfaction measured twelve months post-go-live. Ordinal logistic regression revealed that change readiness scores explained 31% of the variance in outcome, with the subscale capturing management commitment showing the strongest individual effect. Firms with readiness scores in the lowest quartile were 4.2 times more likely to report failed or severely delayed implementations. The findings suggest that readiness diagnostic tools should be embedded in vendor pre-sales processes rather than treated as optional consulting add-ons.

title: Mapping Employee Resistance Factors During ERP Go-Live: Evidence from Five Case Studies in the Food Processing Sector
abstract: Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 68 employees across five food-processing companies in Serbia and Hungary that went live with integrated ERP systems between 2007 and 2010, this study identifies and categorises the resistance factors most frequently cited by end users. Thematic analysis produced seven distinct resistance categories, with perceived loss of task autonomy and distrust of data accuracy being the two most prevalent. Cases were compared using cross-case synthesis. Three of the five companies employed change agents; in those cases, active resistance behaviours such as data sabotage and system workarounds were reported at roughly half the rate found in the remaining two companies. The paper proposes a resistance typology distinguishing attitudinal, behavioural, and structural resistance, and discusses implications for project team composition. Limitations include self-selection of participating companies and potential social desirability bias in interview responses.

title: Post-Go-Live Knowledge Erosion in Small Enterprises: A Longitudinal Perspective
abstract: This study tracks documented system knowledge among key users and IT staff at eleven small enterprises in Serbia's wholesale trade sector at three time points: immediately after go-live, twelve months later, and twenty-four months later. Knowledge was assessed through structured competency tests covering module-specific functionality and through analysis of internal support ticket logs. Mean competency test scores declined by 18% at month twelve and by 34% at month twenty-four relative to the post-training baseline. Support ticket volume increased correspondingly, peaking at month eighteen. Semi-structured interviews with general managers revealed that only two of the eleven firms maintained a formal knowledge retention plan; neither had experienced statistically significant test score declines. The paper discusses the role of staff turnover, vendor disengagement, and absence of internal documentation standards in accelerating knowledge loss. A simple retention index is proposed for SME use without specialist HR infrastructure.

title: Measuring ERP Implementation Failure: Towards a Consistent Definition and Taxonomy for SME Research
abstract: The ERP implementation literature applies the term 'failure' inconsistently, making cross-study comparison unreliable. This conceptual paper reviews 94 empirical studies published between 1995 and 2013 and identifies six distinct operationalisations of failure ranging from project abandonment to long-term underutilisation. A taxonomy is proposed that separates project-level failure (budget, schedule) from adoption-level failure (utilisation, benefit realisation) and organisational failure (strategic misalignment). The taxonomy is applied retrospectively to the reviewed studies, and it is shown that 38% of results reported as contradictory become consistent when the failure type is held constant. The paper concludes with a minimum reporting standard recommended for researchers studying SME ERP outcomes, including required variables and suggested measurement intervals. The framework is intended to be practically applicable without requiring large-scale survey infrastructure.

title: The Role of Middle Management in ERP Resistance Diffusion: Insights from the Serbian Retail Sector
abstract: Middle managers occupy a structurally ambiguous position during ERP implementations: they are expected to champion change while often feeling their own roles are threatened by system transparency. This mixed-methods study surveyed 112 middle managers at 29 retail companies in Serbia and conducted follow-up interviews with 18 of them. Quantitative analysis using structural equation modelling found that perceived role threat fully mediated the relationship between ERP transparency features and resistance behaviour, explaining 44% of the variance in resistance scores. The qualitative component revealed four distinct coping strategies: constructive engagement, passive compliance, covert obstruction, and overt refusal. Companies that involved middle managers in module configuration decisions reported lower resistance diffusion to their subordinates. Findings underscore that implementation success depends on explicitly addressing the middle-management layer rather than focusing change communication solely on executive sponsors and frontline users.

title: Vendor Lock-In Perceptions and Their Effect on Post-Implementation System Utilisation in Serbian SMEs
abstract: Using a cross-sectional survey of 83 SMEs that had been operating an ERP system for at least three years, this study examines how managers' perceptions of vendor lock-in influence their willingness to invest in training, customisation, and integration with additional modules. A seven-item lock-in perception scale was developed and validated (Cronbach's alpha 0.81). Hierarchical regression showed that lock-in perception negatively predicted post-implementation investment intention (β = –0.39, p < 0.001) after controlling for firm size, industry, and system age. Companies expressing high lock-in concern were also 2.8 times more likely to report using the ERP system for fewer than half of the functional areas originally contracted. The paper discusses implications for vendors regarding transparent pricing and migration assistance as tools for increasing customer engagement, and for policymakers considering SME digitalisation support programmes.

title: Organisational Change Readiness Assessment Tools for ERP Projects: A Comparative Evaluation
abstract: This book chapter reviews and comparatively evaluates six readiness assessment instruments available to organisations planning ERP implementations, including both commercially available diagnostic surveys and instruments proposed in academic literature. Each instrument is assessed against eight criteria: theoretical grounding, psychometric validation evidence, applicability to SMEs, coverage of structural versus attitudinal readiness, administration burden, cost, availability of normative benchmarks, and track record in published studies. Instruments developed primarily in North American large-enterprise contexts showed systematic weaknesses when applied to the SME setting: they underweighted resource scarcity and overweighted IT governance maturity. A composite checklist is provided that practitioners can adapt for organisations with fewer than 250 employees. The chapter also identifies gaps in instrument design, particularly the absence of tools that assess readiness dynamically across the implementation lifecycle rather than at a single pre-project snapshot.

title: ERP Implementation Failure Rates in the Western Balkans: A Structured Survey of 140 SMEs
abstract: Despite the importance of SME digitalisation to regional economic development, systematic data on ERP implementation outcomes in the Western Balkans are lacking. This paper reports results from a structured questionnaire survey administered to 140 SMEs in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia that completed an ERP implementation between 2014 and 2019. Failure was operationalised using the taxonomy proposed in the author's 2015 work, allowing separate analysis of project-level and adoption-level failure. Project-level failure rates were 29% in Serbia, 34% in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and 31% in North Macedonia. Adoption-level failure rates were substantially higher: 52%, 58%, and 55% respectively. Logistic regression identified absence of a dedicated internal project manager, implementation duration exceeding eighteen months, and use of heavily customised deployments as the strongest predictors of both failure types. The data are made available as a supplementary dataset to encourage replication.

title: Knowledge Transfer Mechanisms in ERP Transitions Between Incumbent and Successor Systems: Evidence from SME Upgrades
abstract: When an SME replaces one ERP system with another, it faces a compound knowledge transfer challenge: institutional knowledge embedded in the old system must be surfaced and re-contextualised for the new platform while new functionality is simultaneously introduced. This study examines twelve such system replacement projects in Serbian and Hungarian SMEs using a retrospective interview and document analysis approach. Data sources included project documentation, training records, and interviews with key users and managers conducted six months after go-live on the successor system. Analysis identified three knowledge transfer modes: tacit-to-tacit (mentoring), explicit-to-explicit (document migration), and mixed (facilitated workshops). Companies relying primarily on the tacit-to-tacit mode reported significantly higher user satisfaction but were more vulnerable to knowledge loss when key informants departed. The paper proposes a sequencing model for ERP replacement projects that prioritises explicit documentation of business-critical workarounds before decommissioning the incumbent system.

title: Benchmarking Post-Go-Live Support Structures in Serbian SMEs: Findings from a Mixed-Methods Study
abstract: This preprint reports preliminary findings from an ongoing study examining the formal and informal support structures that SMEs maintain after ERP go-live, and their relationship to long-term adoption quality. Survey data were collected from 96 SMEs in Serbia across manufacturing, retail, and logistics sectors in 2024 and 2025. Support structures were categorised along three dimensions: contractual vendor support, internal first-line support capacity, and peer or community-based support. Only 21% of firms maintained all three categories; 38% relied exclusively on vendor contracts, which were typically activated reactively. Adoption quality, measured via a utilisation coverage index and a reported benefit realisation score, was significantly higher in firms with internal first-line support capacity than in those without (mean utilisation coverage 74% vs 51%). Qualitative interviews with 24 managers from the sample are ongoing; preliminary themes suggest that cost sensitivity and lack of awareness of alternatives rather than disinterest in training drive low internal support investment.

title: Adsorpcija polimernih lanaca na ravnoj površini: Monte Karlo studija skalirnih eksponenata
abstract: U ovom radu ispitujemo adsorpciju samoizbjegavajućih lanaca na atraktivnoj ravnoj površini primenom pivot Monte Karlo algoritma na kubnoj rešetki. Simulirali smo lance dužine N = 32 do N = 2048 segmenata pri različitim vrednostima energije površinske interakcije ε/kT u opsegu od 0,1 do 1,5. Određeni su skalirni eksponenti za srednji kvadrat rastojanja krajeva lanca i broj kontakata sa površinom. Naši rezultati daju kritični eksponent ukrštanja φ = 0,484 ± 0,009, što je u dobroj saglasnosti sa predikcijama teorije polja do jedne petlje. Analiza konačnih veličina primenjena je radi procene tačke adsorpcionog prelaza pri βεc = 0,293 ± 0,004. Diskutuje se uticaj geometrije rešetke na vrednosti eksponenata i poređenje sa kontinualnim modelima.

title: Renormalization group treatment of polymer chains grafted to a flat wall
abstract: We apply the field-theoretic renormalization group at two-loop order to the problem of a single polymer chain grafted by one end to an inert flat wall in a good solvent. Starting from the O(n→0) field theory in d = 4 − ε dimensions, we derive the scaling exponents governing the size of the grafted chain and the distribution of segment density normal to the wall. The exponent ν_surface is obtained as 0.588 ± 0.003 to second order in ε, consistent with independent Monte Carlo data. We further compute the cross-over scaling function describing the transition from mushroom to brush regime as a function of surface grafting density σ. The free energy per chain as a function of σ is calculated and compared with self-consistent field theory predictions. Discrepancies at high grafting density are attributed to higher-order loop contributions not captured at the two-loop level.

title: Skaliranje polimernih lanaca na nehomogenim površinama sa periodičnim hemijskim šarama
abstract: Razmatramo statističku mehaniku polimernih lanaca u blizini površine sa periodičnom šarom atraktivnih i repulzivnih traka. Korišćenjem prilagođene verzije pivot algoritma ispitali smo kako prostorna periodičnost šare utiče na efektivni adsorpcioni prag i na vrednost eksponenta ukrštanja. Za lance dužine N do 512 i za periode šare λ od 2 do 32 rešetačke jedinice dobijamo da efektivni prag linearno raste sa frakcionim udelom repulzivnih traka p sve do p ≈ 0,6, nakon čega dolazi do nagle promene ponašanja. Diskutujemo relevantnost ovih nalaza za razumevanje adsorpcije biopolimera na heterogenim biomembranama. Poređenjem sa analitičkim aproksimacijama zasnovanim na modelu efektivnog medija dobija se kvalitativna, ali ne i kvantitativna saglasnost.

title: Crossover scaling in polymer adsorption: a systematic comparison of lattice models
abstract: We perform a systematic comparison of three lattice models — simple cubic, face-centred cubic, and hexagonal close-packed — for the adsorption transition of self-avoiding walks onto a flat surface. For each lattice we simulate chains of length N = 64 to N = 4096 using the pivot algorithm with Metropolis acceptance, accumulating at least 10^8 accepted moves per state point. The adsorption transition temperatures, expressed as reduced couplings βε_c, differ by up to 18% across lattice types, while the universal exponents φ and γ_1 agree within statistical uncertainty of ±0.005 across all three. The effective exponents obtained from finite-chain data exhibit a slow crossover governed by corrections to scaling with Wegner exponent Δ ≈ 0.53. We conclude that lattice-specific corrections to scaling are the dominant source of apparent discrepancies reported in the earlier literature. Implications for the interpretation of experimental adsorption isotherms are discussed.

title: Višelančana adsorpcija na strukturiranim supstratima: efekat lančane gustine
abstract: Proučavamo sistem više samoizbjegavajućih lanaca koji se istovremeno adsorpuju na strukturisanom supstratu sa periodičnim nizom atraktivnih tačaka. Simulacije su izvedene metodom grandkanonskog Monte Karla za gustine lanaca ρ od 0,001 do 0,08 po rešetačkoj jedinici površine. Pri niskim gustinama ponašanje sistema odgovara adsorpciji jednog lanca, dok pri ρ > 0,04 dolazi do kolektivnih efekata koji pomeraju efektivni adsorpcioni prag za oko 12% ka nižim vrednostima energije. Merimo i prostornu korelacionu funkciju segmenata duž površine i pokazujemo da ona u kritičnom režimu poštuje skalirni oblik sa eksponentom η_‖ = 0,22 ± 0,03. title: Field-theoretic description of polymer chains near a repulsive wall: one-loop corrections to the depletion layer
abstract: We compute one-loop corrections to the segment density profile of a dilute polymer solution near a hard repulsive wall using the O(n→0) field theory. The depletion length ξ_dep is expressed as a function of the bulk correlation length ξ_bulk and the bare interaction parameter u, and renormalized at the fixed point of Wilson and Fisher. Our result for the amplitude ratio A = ξ_dep/ξ_bulk is A = 1.07 ± 0.02 at one loop in d = 3, compared with the Gaussian-chain value of 1.00 and the de Gennes blob estimate of 1.10. We also calculate the depletion-induced interaction between two parallel repulsive walls separated by distance D, obtaining an exponentially decaying force with decay length equal to ξ_dep. The osmotic pressure contribution is computed and found to deviate from the Derjaguin approximation by roughly 8% at separations D ≈ 2ξ_dep. These findings are relevant for colloidal stabilization by depletion forces.

title: Uticaj zakrivljenosti površine na adsorpcioni prelaz polimernih lanaca: cilindrična i sferična geometrija
abstract: Sistemom pivot Monte Karlo simulacija ispitujemo adsorpciju samoizbjegavajućih lanaca na cilindričnim i sferičnim površinama atraktivnog karaktera u poređenju sa ravnom površinom. Poluprečnik zakrivljenosti R variran je od 5 do 80 rešetačkih jedinica za lance dužine N od 64 do 1024. Za sfernu geometriju korekturni koeficijent je veći za faktor 1,7 u odnosu na cilindrični slučaj, što je konzistentno sa geometrijskim razmatranjima baziranim na broju površinskih kontakata. title: Scaling of loop and tail length distributions at the adsorption transition
abstract: Using a transfer-matrix method combined with exact enumeration up to N = 36 steps and Monte Carlo data up to N = 2048, we determine the scaling functions governing the distribution of loop lengths l and tail lengths t in a polymer chain adsorbed at a flat surface exactly at the critical adsorption point. The loop-length distribution P(l) follows a power law P(l) ~ l^{−(1+α)} with exponent α = 0.67 ± 0.02 obtained from our Monte Carlo data, consistent with earlier field-theory predictions. The tail distribution P(t) shows a different exponent α_t = 0.44 ± 0.03. We further compute the mean loop length ⟨l⟩ and mean tail length ⟨t⟩ as functions of chain length N and surface interaction strength ε, and determine the scaling crossover between the adsorbed and desorbed phases. The ratio ⟨l⟩/⟨t⟩ at criticality is found to be 0.31 ± 0.02, independent of N for N > 200.
