Obrađuju se modeli samoizbjegavajuće šetnje, teorija skaliranja po de Ženu i Vičentiju, kao i savremene višepetljene računske sheme. Posebno se razmatraju fenomeni adsorpcijskog prelaza, formiranja četkica i deplecijskog sloja. title: Two-loop renormalization group analysis of the adsorption transition in polymer solutions with excluded-volume interactions
abstract: We extend the field-theoretic renormalization group treatment of the polymer adsorption transition to two-loop order within the O(n→0) framework, incorporating both bulk and surface coupling constants. The surface critical exponent φ is computed as a double expansion in ε = 4 − d and the surface enhancement variable c. We obtain φ = 0.500 − 0.048ε − 0.017ε² at the special transition fixed point, yielding φ ≈ 0.484 in d = 3 after Padé resummation, in excellent agreement with our earlier Monte Carlo result of 0.484 ± 0.009. The anomalous dimension of the surface field, η_⊥, is determined to be 0.192 ± 0.008. We also evaluate the correction-to-scaling amplitude ratio at two-loop order and find it to be negative, which explains the systematic downward curvature observed in finite-chain Monte Carlo data. The results confirm the universality of the adsorption transition across different chain models.

title: Finite-size scaling analysis of polymer adsorption on nanopatterned surfaces using Wang–Landau sampling
abstract: We apply the Wang–Landau flat-histogram Monte Carlo method to compute the density of states of self-avoiding walks on a cubic lattice with a nanopatterned attractive surface consisting of square patches of size s × s separated by repulsive gaps. Simulations are performed for patch sizes s = 2, 4, 8, 16 lattice units and chain lengths N = 128 to 512. From the density of states we extract the full free energy landscape as a function of the number of surface contacts and identify adsorption transition temperatures with precision better than 0.3%. For small patch sizes (s < 8) the transition temperature is suppressed relative to the uniform surface by up to 22%, while the transition remains continuous with the same crossover exponent φ = 0.484 within uncertainty. For s ≥ 8 the behaviour approaches that of the uniform surface within 3%. We provide a simple scaling argument relating the suppression of T_c to the ratio s/⟨R_g⟩.

title: Conformational properties of ring polymers adsorbed at a flat surface
abstract: Ring polymers differ topologically from linear chains: the absence of free ends suppresses the tail contribution to adsorbed configurations, modifying the universality class of the adsorption transition. We study this problem using Monte Carlo simulations of self-avoiding rings of length N = 32 to 1024 on a cubic lattice with an attractive flat surface. The adsorption transition temperature for rings is found to be shifted downward by 9.5 ± 0.5% relative to linear chains of the same N. The crossover exponent for rings is φ_ring = 0.500 ± 0.006, statistically indistinguishable from the linear-chain value, suggesting that the bulk topology does not alter the universality class. However, the density profile of adsorbed ring segments normal to the surface decays with a different power-law amplitude than for linear chains. We quantify this difference and discuss its connection to the entropic cost of ring closure near a surface.

Primenom renormalizacione grupe za površinsku teoriju polja u geometriji klina pokazujemo da kritični eksponenti zavise od ugla θ na način koji se može izraziti jednačinom φ(θ) = φ_0 + a₁(π−θ) + a₂(π−θ)² gde smo analitički odredili koeficijente a₁ i a₂ u prvom redu u ε = 4−d. title: Uticaj gustine dislokacija na akustičnu vodljivost u epitaksijalnim slojevima galijum nitrida
abstract: U ovom radu ispitivali smo kako gustina dislokacija u epitaksijalnim slojevima GaN utiče na transport akustičnih fonona i merenu toplotnu provodnost. Korišćenjem Ramanovske termometrije u 3ω konfiguraciji izmerena je toplotna provodnost serije uzoraka pripremljenih metaloorganskom hemijskom depozicijom iz parne faze (MOCVD), sa gustinom dislokacija između 5 × 10⁸ cm⁻² i 8 × 10⁹ cm⁻². Toplotna provodnost pri sobnoj temperaturi opala je sa 185 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ na 112 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ u navedenom opsegu gustine dislokacija. Numerički model zasnovan na Callawayevoj aproksimaciji primenjen je kako bi se razdvojili doprinosi rasejanja na dislokacijama, granicama zrna i Umklapovim procesima. Utvrđeno je da su dislokacije primarni mehanizam rasejanja fonona ispod gustine od oko 2 × 10⁹ cm⁻², dok iznad te vrednosti dominiraju kolektivni efekti deformacionih polja. Rezultati su relevantni za projektovanje toplotnog menadžmenta u RF pojačavačima zasnovanim na GaN platformi.

title: Modelling bursting behaviour in calcium-activated potassium channels: a hierarchical Markov chain approach
abstract: Calcium-activated potassium channels exhibit bursting gating, characterised by clusters of rapid openings separated by long silent intervals. We model this behaviour using a hierarchical Markov chain in which a slow process (calcium binding) modulates a faster gating process (voltage-dependent transitions). The slow and fast subsystems each have two states, yielding a four-state model overall. Rate constants are estimated from 28 single-channel recordings obtained in inside-out patches from rat cortical neurons at two intracellular calcium concentrations (1 μM and 10 μM). The model reproduces the bimodal distribution of closed times, the mean burst duration (18.4 ms at 10 μM Ca²⁺), and the dependence of burst frequency on voltage. The coupling between calcium-binding rate and voltage is quantified through a cross-sensitivity coefficient, which takes a value of 0.31 mV⁻¹ at physiological calcium levels. Simulated power spectra of the channel current match measured spectra within 15% across the 1 Hz–2 kHz range.

title: Dissolved oxygen gradients in Danube-connected floodplain lakes of northern Serbia: seasonal patterns and fish habitat implications
abstract: This study characterised dissolved oxygen dynamics in seven floodplain lakes of the Vojvodina region over two consecutive years (2010–2011) using continuous data loggers deployed at three depths. Mean daily minimum oxygen concentrations fell below 2 mg/L in five of the seven lakes during summer stratification, with hypoxic periods lasting between 18 and 63 days. Shallow lakes with high macrophyte biomass showed pronounced diel fluctuations, while deeper, turbid lakes exhibited persistent nocturnal hypoxia. Fish community surveys using electrofishing revealed that common carp (Cyprinus carpio) and crucian carp (Carassius carassius) were disproportionately abundant in the most hypoxia-prone sites relative to reference oxic reaches. The data provide a baseline for understanding selective pressures acting on cyprinid populations in this landscape and identify priority sites for subsequent physiological and genetic sampling. Seasonal temperature co-variation with oxygen is described and its confounding effects discussed.

title: Gill lamellar surface area and blood haemoglobin concentration in common carp from hypoxic and normoxic floodplain sites
abstract: Morphological and haematological traits were compared between common carp populations sampled from three chronically hypoxic and three normoxic floodplain lakes in the Pannonian Basin. Fish from hypoxic sites had, on average, 23% greater total gill lamellar surface area when adjusted for body mass (ANCOVA, F = 18.4, p < 0.001, n = 120), with shorter inter-lamellar cell masses measured in scanning electron micrographs. Mean haemoglobin concentration was 11.6 g/dL in hypoxic-site fish versus 9.8 g/dL at normoxic sites (t-test, p = 0.003). Haematocrit values followed the same trend but with greater variance. Differences persisted after a six-week laboratory acclimation at standardised oxygen levels, suggesting a heritable component to at least part of the variation. Common garden designs and reciprocal transplant experiments are proposed as next steps. Results are discussed in the context of well-documented variation in European wild carp populations.

title: Critical oxygen threshold (Pcrit) variation in wild common carp: a multi-population respirometry study
abstract: Critical oxygen tension (Pcrit) was measured in 148 adult common carp from eight Vojvodina floodplain lakes spanning a gradient of summer hypoxia severity. Closed-chamber intermittent respirometry was used to determine standard metabolic rate and Pcrit for each individual. Population mean Pcrit ranged from 1.4 mg O₂/L to 2.6 mg O₂/L across sites. Mixed-effects models showed that mean summer minimum dissolved oxygen concentration at the source lake explained 41% of among-population variance in Pcrit after controlling for fish body mass and condition factor. Within-population variance was also higher at normoxic sites, consistent with relaxed selection on this trait. No significant association was found between Pcrit and individual body mass within populations. The study provides quantitative evidence for population-level differentiation in a key hypoxia-tolerance trait and establishes a respirometry protocol suitable for field-collected cyprinids.

title: Phenotypic plasticity in metabolic rate of juvenile common carp under chronic moderate hypoxia: acclimation dynamics and reversibility
abstract: Juvenile common carp (mean body mass 12.4 g) originating from a single normoxic-site population were exposed to chronic moderate hypoxia (3 mg O₂/L) or normoxia (8 mg O₂/L) for 10 weeks in flow-through tanks, followed by a six-week recovery period at normoxia. Standard metabolic rate was measured every two weeks using intermittent respirometry. Hypoxia-exposed fish reduced standard metabolic rate by 31% relative to controls by week four, with rates stabilising thereafter. Haematocrit and gill lamellar surface area increased significantly in hypoxia fish by week six. Upon return to normoxia, metabolic rate recovered to control levels within three weeks, but gill morphology showed only partial reversal by week six of recovery. Growth rate was reduced in hypoxia-exposed fish by 18% over the treatment period. Results indicate that gill structural changes are more persistent plastic responses than metabolic rate adjustments, which has implications for interpreting field population data.

title: Population genetic structure of common carp in Vojvodina floodplain lakes inferred from microsatellite markers
abstract: Genetic diversity and population structure were assessed in 210 common carp sampled from nine floodplain lakes and two river reference sites in Vojvodina using 14 microsatellite loci. STRUCTURE analysis indicated three genetic clusters broadly corresponding to lake isolation history: permanently isolated lakes, seasonally connected lakes, and river-associated populations. FST values among permanently isolated lake populations ranged from 0.04 to 0.11, indicating moderate differentiation. Lakes with the longest estimated hydrological isolation showed the lowest allelic richness, consistent with founder effects and drift. Outlier locus tests (BayeScan) identified two microsatellite loci with signatures potentially consistent with directional selection, both located in genomic regions associated with oxygen transport in previous mapping studies. The results provide a population genetic framework for interpreting phenotypic differences and for designing future common garden experiments. Commercial stocking history, where documented, is discussed as a confounding factor.

title: Local adaptation in common carp: evidence from a reciprocal transplant experiment across contrasting floodplain sites
abstract: A reciprocal transplant experiment was conducted using carp from one chronically hypoxic and one normoxic Vojvodina floodplain lake, with 40 fish per origin-environment combination held for 12 weeks in semi-natural mesocosms approximating source-site conditions. Survival, growth, Pcrit, and gill surface area were measured. In the hypoxic treatment, fish of hypoxic origin had 14% higher survival, 9% greater Pcrit by week 12 under acute challenge tests, and larger gill lamellar surface areas than fish of normoxic origin. Normoxic-origin fish showed partial acclimation in gill morphology but did not fully match hypoxic-origin values. In the normoxic treatment, no significant differences in survival or growth were detected between origins. A genotype-by-environment interaction for Pcrit was statistically supported (mixed model, interaction term p = 0.018). The pattern is consistent with local adaptation to hypoxia rather than pure phenotypic plasticity, though the two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive.

title: Transcriptomic response to acute hypoxia in common carp from populations with contrasting hypoxia exposure histories
abstract: RNA-seq was used to compare transcriptomic responses to a standardised two-hour acute hypoxia challenge (1.5 mg O₂/L) in gill tissue of common carp from a chronically hypoxic lake population and a normoxic lake population (n = 8 per group). After quality filtering and mapping to the Cyprinus carpio reference genome, 312 genes were differentially expressed in the normoxic-origin fish but not in the hypoxic-origin fish, while 87 genes unique to the hypoxic-origin fish showed acute up-regulation. Pathway analysis indicated that normoxic-origin fish mounted a broader HIF-1α signalling response, consistent with a less constitutively active hypoxia pathway at baseline. Hypoxic-origin fish showed higher baseline expression of genes encoding haemoglobin subunits and carbonic anhydrase IV. These differences suggest that prior adaptation has partially buffered the acute transcriptional stress response. Raw count data and differential expression tables are deposited in a public repository.
venue: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology – Part D: Genomics and Proteomics

title: Inter-generational effects of parental hypoxia exposure on offspring Pcrit and gill morphology in common carp
abstract: Whether plastic responses to hypoxia in common carp can be transmitted to unexposed offspring (transgenerational plasticity) was investigated using F1 offspring of parents held under hypoxic or normoxic conditions for six months prior to spawning. F1 fry were raised in identical normoxic conditions for 16 weeks, then assessed for Pcrit, gill lamellar surface area, and HIF-1α pathway gene expression. Offspring of hypoxia-exposed parents had Pcrit values 0.22 mg O₂/L lower on average than offspring of normoxic parents (p = 0.04, n = 96), and gill lamellar surface area was 8% greater after adjustment for body length. Expression of two carbonic anhydrase genes was elevated in offspring of hypoxic parents. Effect sizes were smaller than those observed in direct parental acclimation studies but were statistically detectable. DNA methylation profiling of selected gill gene promoters is ongoing and preliminary results are discussed. These findings suggest that transgenerational plasticity may contribute to rapid phenotypic adjustment of carp populations to habitat hypoxia.

title: RADseq-based demographic history inference for three amphipod species from Vojvodina wetlands
abstract: We generated reduced-representation genomic data (2b-RAD protocol, mean coverage 21×) for Gammarus fossarum, G. balcanicus, and Echinogammarus trichiatus sampled from 15 Vojvodina wetland and canal sites (n = 246 individuals). After SNP filtering (minor allele frequency > 0.05, maximum 10% missingness), we retained 8,412 SNPs for downstream analyses. ADMIXTURE clustering resolved five genetic units across the three species roughly corresponding to large hydrological sub-basins. PSMC demographic reconstructions for G. fossarum indicated a moderate population size reduction coinciding with the Last Glacial Maximum, followed by a 3.5-fold expansion in the early Holocene. Outlier locus detection (pcadapt) identified 53 putatively adaptive SNPs for G. fossarum; GO enrichment pointed to ion transport and osmotic stress response pathways. These results are the first genome-wide assessment of Pannonian amphipod demographic history.

title: Allelopathic interactions between Fallopia japonica and riparian sedge communities: a mesocosm study
abstract: Mesocosms (120 L, n = 40) were established with riparian soil and planted with Carex acutiformis, Carex riparia, and Scirpus sylvaticus, individually and in three-species mixtures. Half received additions of freeze-dried Fallopia japonica root material at 10 g m⁻² at 30-day intervals over six months, simulating decomposing rhizome input. Shoot biomass, rhizome production, and photosynthetic efficiency (Fv/Fm) were measured at 60-day intervals. Rhizome additions reduced total sedge biomass by 28% in monocultures and 34% in mixtures after 180 days. Fv/Fm decreased significantly in Carex riparia (from 0.79 to 0.71) but not in C. acutiformis. Soil phenolic acid concentrations increased monotonically with rhizome additions and were negatively correlated with sedge biomass (r = −0.68, p < 0.001). Results demonstrate that decomposing F. japonica rhizome material can exert measurable phytotoxic effects under near-field conditions in wetland mesocosms.

title: Preliminary assessment of airborne Betula-type pollen concentrations at three monitoring points along an urban–rural gradient in northern Vojvodina
abstract: Three Burkard volumetric spore traps were deployed simultaneously during the birch pollen season (late March to early May 2025) at sites representing central urban Novi Sad, the peri-urban belt, and an agricultural village 40 km north near Sombor. Daily pollen concentrations were estimated following standard European Aeroallergen Network protocols. Peak daily concentrations at the urban site reached 412 grains m⁻³ on 14 April, compared to 298 grains m⁻³ at the peri-urban site and 187 grains m⁻³ at the rural site. The urban site showed a 2–3 day earlier season onset compared to the rural site, consistent with the urban heat island effect. Total seasonal pollen integral (SPIn) was 1,840, 1,210, and 870 grains m⁻³ day at urban, peri-urban, and rural stations, respectively. These preliminary data indicate a need for multi-point monitoring networks rather than single-station extrapolation when informing allergy warning systems in Vojvodina.

title: Uloga hidroperioda u oblikovanju beta diverziteta zooplanktona privremenih slatinskih jezera
abstract: Proučavan je uticaj hidroperioda na beta diverzitet zajednica zooplanktona u 19 privremenih slatinskih jezera u Vojvodini tokom sušne 2015. i vlažne 2016. godine. Hidroperiod je kvantifikovan na osnovu satelitskih snimaka (Sentinel-2) i merenja nivoa vode na terenu. Zajednice zooplanktona uzorkovane su u tri navrata po godini. Nestingovost i zamena vrsta (species replacement) dekomponovane su iz ukupnog beta diverziteta korišćenjem Baselgine metode. U vlažnoj godini, zamena vrsta bila je dominantna komponenta beta diverziteta (68%), dok je u sušnoj godini nestingovost porasla na 51%, što ukazuje na filtriranje zajednica putem izumiranja. Duži hidroperiod bio je pozitivno povezan sa alfa diverzitetom (r² = 0,47). Rezultati naglašavaju ranjivost ovih zajednica na klimatske ekstrema.

title: Transfer factors between substrate bark, epiphytic lichen thallus, and ambient particulate matter for selected trace elements: a comparative field study in Serbia and Hungary
abstract: Transfer factors (TFs) between bark substrate, lichen thallus, and colocated PM10 filter samples were determined for Zn, Cu, Ni, Cd, Pb, and Fe at 18 paired sites across a cross-border transect spanning southern Hungary and northern Serbia. Lichen species sampled included Hypogymnia physodes and Parmelia sulcata. PM10 filters were collected over 30-day passive exposure periods using standard diffusion samplers. ICP-MS was used for trace element quantification in all matrices following microwave-assisted acid digestion. TFs from bark to thallus ranged from 0.8 to 4.6 depending on element and species, with Cd consistently showing the highest values. Correlation analysis indicated that lichen Pb and Cd concentrations were more strongly associated with PM10 loadings than with bark substrate concentrations (r² = 0.71 and 0.68 respectively), reinforcing the aerial uptake pathway as dominant. Inter-species differences in TF were statistically significant for Ni and Fe but not for Cd or Pb.

title: Skeletonisation and Graph Extraction from Retinal Vessel Segmentation Maps: A Comparative Pipeline Study
abstract: Accurate graph representations of the retinal vasculature depend critically on the quality of the skeletonisation step applied after binary vessel segmentation. This study evaluated four skeletonisation algorithms—Zhang–Suen thinning, morphological erosion, medial-axis transform, and a pruned distance-transform approach—on 120 fundus images drawn from a local diabetic screening archive. Each skeleton was converted to a weighted graph whose nodes represent vessel bifurcations and crossings and whose edges carry length, tortuosity, and estimated calibre. Quantitative agreement between graph topology derived from manual tracings and each automated pipeline was measured using Jaccard similarity for edges and node-count deviation. The medial-axis method coupled with iterative spur removal produced the lowest node-count error (mean 4.2 %) and highest edge Jaccard (0.81). Runtime on a standard CPU was under 3 seconds per image. Findings inform later studies on descriptor extraction from graph representations of the retinal microvasculature.

title: Estimation of Arteriole-to-Venule Ratio in Fundus Images Using Colour-Channel Thresholding and Graph Labelling
abstract: The arteriole-to-venule ratio (AVR) is a clinically relevant index of retinal vascular narrowing. Automated AVR estimation requires reliable separation of arterioles from venules before calibre can be measured. This paper presents a pipeline that combines opponent-colour thresholding in the green and red channels with a minimum-cut graph labelling scheme applied to the extracted vascular network graph. The method was tested on 230 fundus images from 115 patients with type 2 diabetes and 115 normoglycaemic controls recruited at a diabetes outpatient clinic in Novi Sad. Calibre was estimated at standardised distances from the optic disc using a parabolic model. Mean absolute error against manual AVR measurement was 0.041. Diabetic subjects showed a statistically significant reduction in AVR compared with controls (0.63 ± 0.07 vs. 0.69 ± 0.06, p < 0.001). The pipeline runs without manual initialisation and processes a full image pair in under 8 seconds.

title: Graph-Theoretic Complexity Indices of the Retinal Vascular Tree in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Early retinal vascular changes in type 2 diabetes may precede clinically visible retinopathy by years. This study characterised the retinal vascular network in 88 patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes (duration less than 18 months, no visible retinopathy on standard grading) and 88 age- and sex-matched controls using graph-theoretic complexity indices derived from the vessel graph. Indices included cyclomatic number, mean branching order, vascular density, graph diameter, and average clustering coefficient estimated over local neighbourhood windows. Graphs were constructed from semi-automated vessel segmentations verified by a trained grader. Patients showed significantly lower cyclomatic number (p = 0.003), reduced average branching order (p = 0.011), and higher graph diameter (p = 0.007) compared with controls after adjustment for age, sex, and blood pressure. Fractal dimension estimated from box-counting on the binary segmentation corroborated the graph-based findings (p = 0.018). These results suggest measurable topological rarefaction of the retinal network at diabetes onset.

title: Reproducibility of Retinal Vascular Network Graph Descriptors Across Three Fundus Camera Models
abstract: Graph-theoretic descriptors of the retinal vasculature may vary with imaging hardware due to differences in resolution, field of view, and colour rendering. Reproducibility across devices is necessary before descriptors can be used in multi-centre studies. Forty-two participants were imaged on the same day with three fundus camera models operating at 45-degree field of view and resolutions ranging from 2.0 to 3.5 megapixels. Vessel segmentation was performed with a fixed trained U-Net model and graphs were constructed using the pipeline described in earlier work. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were computed for twelve graph descriptors. Seven descriptors—including cyclomatic number, vascular density, mean edge length, and bifurcation angle statistics—showed ICC above 0.80 across all camera pairs. Graph diameter and clustering coefficient showed moderate reproducibility (ICC 0.61–0.74). Calibre-based descriptors were most sensitive to resolution differences. Results indicate that topological descriptors are substantially more robust to camera variation than metric descriptors.

title: Retinal Vascular Morphology as a Chapter in Computational Ophthalmology: Methods and Clinical Context
abstract: This book chapter reviews quantitative methods for characterising retinal vascular morphology from fundus photographs, with emphasis on graph-theoretic approaches developed over the previous decade. The chapter covers vessel segmentation strategies, skeletonisation, graph construction conventions, and the derivation of descriptors including fractal dimension, vessel calibre indices, branching angles, and topological complexity measures. Clinical context is provided for each descriptor class, discussing associations with hypertension, diabetes, and ageing established in population-based studies. Limitations of current automated pipelines—including sensitivity to image quality, optic disc segmentation errors, and lack of standardisation across research groups—are discussed in detail. The chapter concludes with an assessment of what is needed for clinical translation, including prospective validation cohorts, standardised software, and integration with electronic health records. The intended audience includes biomedical engineering researchers and clinicians with a quantitative background.

title: Bifurcation Angle Distribution in the Retinal Vascular Network as a Discriminator Between Diabetic and Hypertensive Microangiopathy
abstract: Diabetic and hypertensive retinopathy share overlapping fundus features, complicating differential assessment in patients with co-morbid conditions. This study examined whether the distribution of bifurcation angles in the retinal vascular graph differs between the two conditions. Fundus images from 74 patients with type 2 diabetes without hypertension, 68 patients with essential hypertension without diabetes, and 70 controls were analysed. Bifurcation angles at each branching node were measured using the tangent directions of the two daughter vessels estimated over a 30-pixel arc from the branch point. Circular statistical descriptors—mean angle, angular variance, and skewness—were derived for arteriole and venule subtrees separately. Diabetic patients showed a significantly wider mean arteriolar bifurcation angle (72.4° ± 11.3°) compared with hypertensive patients (65.1° ± 10.7°, p = 0.002) and controls (68.8° ± 9.9°). Venular angles did not differ significantly across groups. A logistic regression model using arteriolar angular descriptors alone achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.76 for discriminating diabetic from hypertensive microangiopathy.

title: Longitudinal Change in Retinal Vascular Graph Topology Over 36 Months in Patients with Controlled Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Cross-sectional studies of retinal vascular morphology in diabetes cannot determine whether observed differences precede glycaemic dysregulation or develop concurrently. This prospective study followed 61 patients with type 2 diabetes under standard pharmacological management for 36 months with annual fundus imaging. Graph-theoretic descriptors were extracted at each time point and mixed-effects linear models were fitted to assess within-subject change. Cyclomatic number showed a statistically significant decline over the observation period (mean annual change −0.8 %, 95 % CI −1.3 to −0.3, p = 0.004), while vascular density declined at a rate of −0.6 % per year (p = 0.019). Neither HbA1c trajectories nor antihypertensive use fully explained the observed topological changes in multivariate models. Eleven patients progressed to mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy at month 36; these subjects showed significantly faster decline in cyclomatic number from the first annual visit onwards. The findings support topological graph descriptors as candidate biomarkers for progressive microvascular deterioration.

title: Spatial Heterogeneity of Vascular Graph Density Across Retinal Quadrants in Type 2 Diabetes
abstract: Microvascular dropout in diabetic retinopathy is known to be spatially non-uniform, yet most automated analyses summarise graph descriptors globally over the visible retinal area. This study partitioned the retinal vascular graph into superior, inferior, nasal, and temporal quadrants relative to the fovea and computed vascular density, mean edge length, and local clustering coefficient separately for each quadrant in 104 diabetic patients and 95 controls. Diabetic patients showed preferential density reduction in the temporal quadrant (mean difference −9.3 %, p < 0.001) relative to the nasal quadrant (−4.1 %, p = 0.031), with the superior–inferior asymmetry index significantly elevated compared with controls (p = 0.007). Quadrant-stratified descriptors improved classification accuracy over global descriptors when used as features in a support vector machine (AUC 0.84 vs. 0.77). Spatial stratification of graph analysis may provide more sensitive markers of early diabetic microvascular damage than whole-image summaries.

title: Automated Optic Disc Centring for Consistent Graph Coordinate Normalisation in Retinal Fundus Analysis
abstract: Consistent placement of the coordinate origin at the optic disc centre is essential for reproducible quadrant-stratified vascular graph analysis and for computing descriptors at standardised distances from the disc margin. Manual disc centring is time-consuming; automated methods vary in accuracy across image quality levels. This paper evaluates a two-stage approach: a coarse localisation using the brightest-region heuristic followed by a fine refinement using a circular Hough transform applied to the disc boundary probability map from a lightweight convolutional detector. On a test set of 312 images spanning a range of quality scores, the method achieved a mean disc-centre localisation error of 11.4 pixels (0.09 disc diameters) compared with manual reference points, outperforming the brightest-region heuristic alone (32.1 pixels) and a Haar-cascade detector (18.7 pixels). Failure rate (error exceeding 0.5 disc diameters) was 1.9 %. Integration into the existing graph analysis pipeline added 0.4 seconds mean processing time per image.

title: Retinal Vascular Graph Descriptors Combined with HbA1c Trajectories for Predicting 5-Year Retinopathy Onset in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Predicting which patients with type 2 diabetes will develop retinopathy within five years would allow targeted surveillance. This retrospective cohort study linked fundus images at diabetes diagnosis with electronic health record data for 189 patients followed for at least five years. Thirty-seven patients developed mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy within the follow-up period. At-diagnosis graph descriptors (cyclomatic number, arteriolar AVR, temporal-quadrant vascular density, mean bifurcation angle) were combined with HbA1c area-under-curve over the first 12 months in a Cox proportional-hazards model. The combined model showed a concordance index of 0.81 (95 % CI 0.74–0.87), compared with 0.71 for HbA1c trajectory alone and 0.74 for graph descriptors alone. Temporal-quadrant vascular density was the single strongest graph predictor (hazard ratio 0.61 per 10 % increase, p = 0.002). The results support adding baseline graph descriptors to metabolic risk models for retinopathy surveillance stratification, though prospective validation is required.

title: Site-Effect Estimation in Diffusion Tensor Imaging Metrics Across Four Eastern European Scanning Centres
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics such as fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) are sensitive to acquisition parameters and scanner hardware. We collected DTI data from 74 healthy adults scanned at four centres in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, each using a distinct scanner model and b-value scheme. Linear mixed-effects models were fitted to FA and MD values extracted from 20 white-matter tracts defined by the JHU atlas, with site treated as a random effect. Site explained 11–29% of variance in FA depending on tract, even after controlling for age and sex. A retrospective harmonisation step based on ComBat reduced this unexplained variance by 64% on average without attenuating biologically meaningful age effects. The results quantify the extent to which between-site variability would confound group-difference studies conducted without harmonisation and provide a reference dataset for methodological benchmarking.

title: Personalised Threshold Adaptation for Acoustic Fall Detection Using Short Calibration Sequences
abstract: Population-level thresholds for acoustic fall detection generalise poorly across individuals due to differences in gait, body mass, footwear, and floor type. This paper proposes a simple online threshold adaptation scheme that updates the detection threshold using a two-minute calibration walk at the start of each monitoring session. Data from 54 community-dwelling older adults (mean age 73, range 65–84) were collected in their homes; each participant performed 10 scripted near-falls (controlled lowering to a mat) and 10 actual daily living sessions with continuous wear. The calibration walk yields per-person energy and spectral centroid statistics used to shift a Gaussian discriminant boundary. Adapted thresholds reduced false positive rate from 4.1 per hour to 1.7 per hour, with sensitivity maintained above 0.90 across 88% of participants. The adaptation algorithm requires 1.1 kB RAM and 2 ms computation on a Cortex-M4 at 80 MHz. The paper discusses the minimum calibration duration (below 90 s adaptation quality degrades substantially) and the effect of floor covering on detection reliability.

title: Benchmarking edge inference of biosignal classifiers on ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V microcontrollers
abstract: Deploying trained machine learning classifiers on wearable microcontrollers requires careful trade-offs between model accuracy, latency, and energy consumption. This study benchmarked five classifiers—linear discriminant analysis, decision tree, random forest (50 trees), a quantised multilayer perceptron, and a quantised 1-D convolutional network—compiled for two target platforms: an ARM Cortex-M4 at 168 MHz and a RISC-V core at 200 MHz, both with 256 kB SRAM. Models were trained on a 40-feature physiological stress dataset and converted to fixed-point arithmetic using an 8-bit quantisation scheme. The quantised MLP achieved 80.1% balanced accuracy with 1.8 ms inference time and 0.9 µJ per inference on the Cortex-M4, representing the best accuracy-energy trade-off. The RISC-V platform consumed 18% less energy per inference but required additional manual optimisation of memory layout. Quantisation reduced accuracy by at most 2.3 percentage points across all models.

title: Inter-day reliability of wrist-derived autonomic indices across menstrual cycle phases in young women
abstract: Autonomic nervous system tone varies with hormonal fluctuations across the menstrual cycle, yet most wearable validation studies treat female participants as a homogeneous group. This study recruited 34 eumenorrhoeic women aged 20–30 and measured wrist PPG-derived HRV and EDA tonic level on four sessions timed to the menstrual, follicular, ovulatory, and luteal phases, confirmed by basal body temperature and urinary LH tests. Intraclass correlation coefficients for same-phase repeated measures were high for RMSSD (ICC = 0.81) and LF power (ICC = 0.77) but poor for LF/HF (ICC = 0.44). Significant differences between cycle phases were found for RMSSD (highest in the follicular phase, 56.2 ± 14.1 ms) and tonic EDA (highest in the luteal phase). These findings imply that phase should be recorded as a covariate in studies using female participants, and that LF/HF should be interpreted with caution from short wrist-PPG windows.

title: Population-level stability of motor cortex tuning during chronic recording: a longitudinal dataset and descriptive analysis
abstract: We present a longitudinal dataset and accompanying analysis characterising how directional tuning of motor cortex neurons evolves over twelve consecutive weeks in two rhesus macaques performing an eight-target centre-out task. Recordings were obtained daily using 96-channel Utah arrays. A total of 4,312 single-unit and multi-unit recordings were analysed. Preferred directions of well-isolated single units showed median angular drift of 11° per week, with high variance across units and animals. Units with initially high signal-to-noise ratios (greater than 4.0) drifted less and were more likely to remain isolable at week twelve. Population-level decoding performance, measured by offline velocity reconstruction R², declined by a mean of 0.04 per week for a fixed decoder but only 0.01 per week when a weekly recalibration step was applied. The dataset is deposited in an open repository and is intended as a benchmark for future decoder stability studies.

title: Seasonal NDVI trajectories from Landsat-8 for distinguishing winter wheat and sunflower parcels in the Vojvodina plain
abstract: This study examined the separability of winter wheat and sunflower cultivation units in the Vojvodina lowland using dense NDVI time series derived from Landsat-8 surface reflectance imagery acquired during the 2015 and 2016 growing seasons. A total of 412 reference parcels were digitised from cadastral data and verified by field survey. Temporal profiles were constructed at 16-day intervals and smoothed using a Savitzky–Golay filter before being fed into a random forest classifier. Overall classification accuracy reached 91.4% for winter wheat and 87.9% for sunflower across both years. The main source of confusion was between sunflower and maize in parcels smaller than 1.5 hectares, where mixed pixels reduced time-series coherence. Results suggest that the phenological window between day-of-year 160 and 220 provides the greatest discriminative power for separating these two summer crops. The dataset and code are made available through the BioSense Institute repository.

title: Effect of cloud gap-filling strategy on Sentinel-2 derived LAI estimates in humid continental climates
abstract: Frequent cloud cover in temperate agricultural regions causes substantial data gaps in optical satellite time series, potentially biasing derived biophysical variables such as leaf area index (LAI). This paper compares four gap-filling approaches—linear interpolation, Whittaker smoother, harmonic regression, and a radial basis function network—applied to Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument Level-2A imagery over a 180 000-hectare study area in northern Serbia. LAI was estimated using a lookup-table inversion of the PROSAIL radiative transfer model. Reference LAI measurements were collected at 38 field plots across three crop types during the 2018 season. The harmonic regression and Whittaker smoother produced the lowest root mean square errors against field data (0.41 and 0.44 m² m⁻² respectively), while linear interpolation performed worst in years with extended cloud sequences exceeding 25 consecutive days. The study recommends harmonic regression as the default for LAI products intended for yield modelling in the region.

title: Integrating ERA5-Land meteorological variables with satellite vegetation indices for in-season winter wheat yield forecasting at the field level
abstract: Accurate in-season yield forecasting at individual field level remains difficult because satellite observations alone do not capture agronomic stress caused by temperature extremes or moisture deficits. This paper presents a regression framework that combines seven Sentinel-2 derived spectral indices sampled at weekly intervals with ERA5-Land reanalysis variables including daily maximum temperature, precipitation sum, and reference evapotranspiration. Training data were compiled from 1 247 winter wheat parcels in the Srem district spanning the 2017–2020 growing seasons, with yield ground truth from cooperative combine-harvester records. A gradient boosting regressor outperformed a simple LAI-based benchmark, reducing mean absolute error from 0.71 t ha⁻¹ to 0.49 t ha⁻¹ when the model was applied to the 2021 holdout season. Feature importance analysis identified the red-edge chlorophyll index acquired between Zadoks stage 37 and 55 as the strongest single predictor. Spatial autocorrelation of residuals was moderate (Moran's I = 0.18), indicating that local soil variability not captured by weather reanalysis remains a limiting factor.

title: Parcel boundary delineation from Sentinel-2 imagery using a watershed segmentation approach adapted for fragmented agricultural landscapes
abstract: Automatic delineation of agricultural parcel boundaries is a prerequisite for scalable field-level monitoring but is complicated by the small, irregular parcel structure typical of post-socialist land fragmentation in the western Balkans. This conference paper describes an adaptation of marker-controlled watershed segmentation applied to a composite of three Sentinel-2 bands (B4, B8, B11) and a gradient magnitude image generated from a spring-season mosaic. Markers were seeded using local minima of the gradient after Gaussian smoothing at two spatial scales. Accuracy was evaluated against 630 manually digitised parcels in a 5 000-hectare test region in the South Bačka district. The method achieved an average boundary displacement error of 8.3 m and an over-segmentation rate of 14%, comparable to published results on larger, more regular field systems in Western Europe. The approach is computationally light and runs within Google Earth Engine without requiring additional training data.

title: A transferability assessment of yield prediction models trained in the Pannonian Plain when applied to Romanian agricultural regions
abstract: Machine learning models trained on local yield and satellite data often degrade when transferred to neighbouring regions with different climate regimes, soil types, and crop varieties. This study evaluates the transferability of three yield prediction models—random forest, support vector regression, and a convolutional recurrent network operating on image time series—trained on Serbian Pannonian Plain data and tested on 890 winter wheat parcels distributed across four counties in south-west Romania. Models were trained on 2017–2021 Serbian data and applied without retraining, with partial retraining on 20% of Romanian parcels, and with full retraining. Partial retraining using as few as 180 Romanian parcels recovered 78% of the performance attainable with full local training. The convolutional recurrent network showed the largest absolute performance drop under zero-shot transfer but also the greatest benefit from partial retraining. The study concludes that a small locally collected calibration dataset is sufficient for practical deployment across the Pannonian–Wallachian agroclimatic gradient.

title: Combining Sentinel-1 SAR coherence and Sentinel-2 optical indices for sunflower yield estimation under variable cloud cover
abstract: Optical satellite data for yield modelling become unreliable during cloudy periods that coincide with critical crop growth stages. This study investigates whether Sentinel-1 C-band SAR coherence, which is unaffected by cloud cover, can supplement or replace optical indices during such periods for sunflower yield estimation. A dataset of 534 sunflower parcels in the Banat region monitored from 2019 to 2022 was used. Repeat-pass interferometric coherence was computed from 6-day Sentinel-1 pairs on ascending and descending orbits. Coherence values between day-of-year 190 and 230 correlated negatively with canopy biomass (r = −0.61) and showed predictive value for final yield independent of optical data. A fusion model combining coherence time series with cloud-gapfilled NDVI achieved a mean absolute error of 0.44 t ha⁻¹, compared with 0.61 t ha⁻¹ for an optical-only baseline in years with high cloud frequency. The benefit of SAR fusion was largest in the 2021 season, which experienced 34 cloudy days during the critical growth window.

title: Temporal resolution requirements for Sentinel-2 based yield modelling: a sensitivity analysis across five crop types
abstract: The operational cadence of Sentinel-2 is five days at the equator but is reduced by cloud cover and orbital geometry at mid-latitudes. It remains unclear how large the resulting temporal gaps can be before yield prediction accuracy degrades significantly. This paper presents a systematic sensitivity analysis in which synthetic temporal gaps of 5, 10, 15, 20, and 30 days are introduced into complete Sentinel-2 time series for five crop types—winter wheat, maize, sunflower, soybean, and sugar beet—across 2 300 parcels observed in Vojvodina from 2018 to 2023. Yield prediction models were retrained and evaluated for each gap scenario. Winter wheat and sugar beet showed the steepest accuracy decline beyond 15-day gaps, linked to the narrow phenological windows of booting and canopy closure respectively. Maize and sunflower were more tolerant of sparse observations due to longer plateau phases in their spectral trajectories. Results provide quantitative guidance for data acquisition planning and for identifying crop types most in need of SAR data supplementation.

title: Parcel-level crop yield prediction in heterogeneous agricultural landscapes: methods, data requirements, and operational constraints
abstract: This book chapter reviews quantitative approaches to predicting crop yields at the individual parcel level using satellite time series and ancillary data, with emphasis on conditions typical of Central and South-East European agricultural regions. The chapter covers radiative transfer model inversion, statistical regression, and machine learning approaches, discussing their data requirements, computational demands, and performance under limited ground truth availability. A practical section addresses the challenge of obtaining parcel boundaries from heterogeneous national LPIS databases and the trade-offs involved in selecting temporal compositing windows. The chapter draws on published literature and on experiments conducted by the authors over parcels in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania between 2017 and 2024. An operational workflow suitable for deployment by regional agricultural advisory services is outlined, including a checklist of minimum data requirements and common failure modes encountered in practice.

title: Seismic Vulnerability Index of Pre-War Masonry Housing Blocks in Vojvodina: A Field Calibration Study
abstract: This paper presents the calibration of the vulnerability index method (Vj) for a sample of 138 pre-1945 unreinforced brick masonry residential buildings surveyed across four municipalities in Vojvodina. Field data were collected using a modified rapid visual screening form adapted from the EMS-98 classification, augmented by flatjack tests at 22 buildings to establish in-situ mortar strength. The resulting vulnerability curves were compared against synthetic ground motion scenarios derived from the seismic hazard map of Serbia (PGA 0.10–0.16 g, 475-year return period). Mean damage grades for the stock ranged from D1 to D2 at the design hazard level, with approximately 14% of buildings showing pre-existing structural irregularities that elevated their index by more than 0.12. The study concludes that the standard Italian vulnerability index requires regional recalibration to avoid underestimating risk in flat, low-seismicity agricultural plains where soil amplification on Holocene alluvial deposits is the dominant modifier.

title: Damage Patterns in Rubble-Stone Masonry Churches Following the 2010 Kruševo Aftershock Sequence
abstract: Fourteen Orthodox and Catholic churches built from rubble limestone masonry in the Kruševo micro-region of North Macedonia were inspected within three weeks of a Mw 4.7 main shock and its aftershock sequence. Damage was catalogued using a structured form including crack mapping, out-of-plane displacement measurements with a handheld distometer, and photogrammetric documentation at six sites. Nine of the fourteen structures showed newly initiated diagonal shear cracks at gable walls; two exhibited partial collapse of apse vaults. Mortar samples were analysed for compressive strength at the laboratory of the Faculty of Civil Engineering in Skopje, yielding values between 0.4 and 1.1 MPa, consistent with lime-based historic mortars. The paper discusses recurrent failure mechanisms—tympanum separation, bell-tower–nave disconnection, and lintel rotation—and maps them against construction typology and plan geometry. A simplified fragility proxy based on tower height-to-base ratio is proposed and benchmarked against the observed damage grades.

title: Shove Test Variability in Solid Brick Masonry: Influence of Bed Joint Depth and Measurement Protocol
abstract: The shove test is widely used to estimate shear strength at masonry bed joints in existing buildings, yet its reproducibility across operators and equipment configurations is poorly documented in European practice. This study reports 186 individual shove tests conducted at 31 buildings in Novi Sad and Sremska Mitrovica, controlling for joint depth (15–30 mm), measurement frame stiffness, and precompression level. Results show a coefficient of variation of 31% across tests within the same wall, and a systematic positive bias of 18% when joint depth is less than 20 mm compared with the standard 25 mm condition. A correction factor table is derived by regression for the depth and precompression parameters. The study also compares shove test shear strength estimates with those from diagonal compression tests on extracted wall panels at four sites, finding reasonable agreement (within 15%) when the proposed corrections are applied. Guidance is provided for practitioners performing assessments under Serbian technical regulations (Pravilnik o tehničkim normativima za izgradnju objekata visokogradnje u seizmičkim područjima).

title: GIS-Based Exposure Model for Unreinforced Masonry Urban Fabric: A Case Study of the Stari Grad Quarter, Sremska Mitrovica
abstract: A building-by-building exposure database was constructed for the historic core of Sremska Mitrovica, comprising 624 structures. Data acquisition combined cadastral records, on-site visual screening, and archive drawings from the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments of Vojvodina. Each building was assigned attributes for construction period, number of storeys, floor system type, façade condition, and a qualitative index of structural regularity. The dataset was integrated into a QGIS environment and linked to a probabilistic seismic hazard grid at 0.05° resolution derived from a regional attenuation model. Loss estimation using mean damage grade curves produced an expected 23% of the stock reaching damage grade D3 or higher at a 475-year return period scenario. The paper discusses the sensitivity of the aggregate loss estimate to floor system classification uncertainty, which proved to be the dominant epistemic variable, accounting for 40% of the variance in the output. The database structure is made available for replication in similar Pannonian-zone towns.

title: Thermal and Structural Performance of Externally Applied GFRP Mesh Reinforced Render as a Retrofit Strategy for Brick Masonry Load-Bearing Walls
abstract: External reinforced render systems offer the dual benefit of improving both seismic in-plane shear capacity and thermal insulation when combined with mineral wool boards. This paper reports cyclic in-plane tests on eight full-scale brick masonry wall specimens (1.2 m × 2.4 m) with and without a glass-fibre-reinforced polymer mesh embedded in 30 mm cement-lime render at both faces. Applied pre-compression levels were 0.15 and 0.30 MPa. Retrofitted specimens showed a mean 2.4-fold increase in lateral force capacity and a 3.1-fold increase in displacement ductility compared to unretrofitted controls. Thermal transmittance of the wall assembly was measured in a hot-box apparatus before and after cyclic loading; no detectable degradation of the insulation board bond was observed at drift levels up to 0.8%. The paper provides design guidance compatible with Eurocode 6 and discusses compatibility constraints when applying the system to protected masonry in heritage contexts, recommending reversibility provisions and minimum mortar strength thresholds.

title: Flat-Jack Testing in Pre-1945 Masonry Buildings: Observations from 54 Buildings in Three Serbian Cities
abstract: This paper consolidates results from flat-jack testing campaigns carried out between 2013 and 2018 at 54 pre-1945 solid-brick masonry buildings in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin. Single flat-jack tests provided local stress estimates at 136 positions; double flat-jack tests at 48 positions yielded elastic modulus values. Compressive stress in load-bearing walls ranged from 0.11 to 0.54 MPa, with a mean of 0.26 MPa, consistent with tributary-area estimates for two- to four-storey buildings with timber floor systems. Elastic modulus values ranged from 880 to 3,100 MPa, with a median of 1,540 MPa. A Weibull distribution provided a better fit to the modulus data than a normal distribution. Building age, mortar type (identified by visual inspection and spot carbonation tests), and storey count were examined as predictors; only mortar type showed a statistically significant association with modulus at the 5% level. The results are tabulated as reference ranges for use in assessment calculations under Eurocode 6 when direct testing is not feasible.

title: Influence of Irregular Plan Geometry on Seismic Response of Single-Storey Masonry Rural Structures in the Mačva Plain
abstract: Single-storey rural residential structures with L-shaped and T-shaped plan geometries are common across the Mačva Plain in northwestern Serbia, yet their seismic behaviour under low-magnitude events is largely uncharacterised. Nonlinear pushover analyses were conducted on simplified equivalent-frame models of 16 representative plan configurations, parameterised by aspect ratio, re-entrant corner depth, and position of openings. Material properties were assigned from in-situ test data collected at twelve rural structures during a 2019 field campaign. Torsional irregularity amplified peak displacement demand at re-entrant corners by 1.3 to 1.8 times relative to regular box-shaped comparators under the same base shear level. Corner tensile cracking initiated at drift levels as low as 0.05% for configurations where the re-entrant corner depth exceeded 40% of the façade length. The study suggests that current simplified assessment procedures, which treat single-storey masonry as inherently low-risk, underestimate damage potential at plan irregularity concentrations. Simple geometric screening criteria are proposed to flag irregular rural buildings for more detailed assessment.

title: Photogrammetric Crack Mapping for Sequential Damage Assessment: Precision and Workflow Evaluation at Three Masonry Pilot Buildings
abstract: Repeated close-range photogrammetric surveys were carried out at three masonry buildings in Novi Sad at six-month intervals over two years to evaluate the precision of automated crack detection and its suitability for tracking progressive structural deterioration. Image acquisition used a mirrorless camera with a 24 mm fixed lens; point clouds were processed in Agisoft Metashape with a mean ground sampling distance of 1.2 mm. Crack width measurements derived from the photogrammetric model were compared against manual calliper measurements at 240 reference points; the root mean square error was 0.18 mm, acceptable for the classification thresholds used in EMS-98. Between-epoch change detection correctly identified 91% of new crack propagation events larger than 0.5 mm, with a false-positive rate of 8%. The main workflow bottleneck was control-point placement on textured historic façades, addressed by a target-free optimisation procedure. The paper discusses integration of the workflow into periodic inspection protocols and its cost relative to manual survey, estimating a 35% time saving per inspection after the initial model is established.

title: Compatibility Assessment of Hydraulic Lime Injection Grouts with Historic Brick Masonry: Mechanical and Durability Criteria
abstract: Injection grouting with hydraulic lime-based suspensions is commonly used to consolidate deteriorated multi-leaf masonry walls. This study evaluates the compatibility of six commercially formulated natural hydraulic lime (NHL) grouts with historic solid brick specimens sourced from three 19th-century buildings in Novi Sad. Grout injectability was measured in a sand-column test; workability retention at 30 and 60 minutes was recorded. After 90-day curing, compressive strength of grout prisms ranged from 2.3 to 7.8 MPa and bond tensile strength to brick ranged from 0.14 to 0.41 MPa. Freeze-thaw durability was evaluated through 25 cycles; two grouts with water-cement ratio above 1.0 showed microcracking visible in thin-section petrography. Thermogravimetric analysis confirmed residual portlandite contents consistent with pozzolanic activity levels. The study identifies an NHL grout formulation range (compressive strength 3–5 MPa; bond strength ≥ 0.25 MPa; no freeze-thaw degradation) as compatible with the target brick type, providing specification guidance for practitioners undertaking seismic consolidation under heritage protection constraints.

title: Seismic Risk Perception Among Residents of Unreinforced Masonry Housing in Vojvodina: A Survey of 480 Households
abstract: Understanding residents' risk perception is a prerequisite for designing effective retrofitting incentive programmes. A structured questionnaire was administered to 480 households living in pre-1964 unreinforced masonry apartment buildings across six municipalities in Vojvodina. The questionnaire measured awareness of seismic hazard, trust in building safety, knowledge of retrofitting options, and willingness to contribute financially to collective structural improvements. Only 34% of respondents correctly identified their municipality as lying in a seismically active zone; 61% considered their building safe without qualification. Logistic regression showed that prior experience of felt shaking (even at intensity III–IV) was the strongest predictor of elevated risk awareness (OR = 3.4, 95% CI 2.1–5.5), followed by tertiary education (OR = 2.1). Willingness to pay for retrofitting was expressed by 41% of respondents but conditioned predominantly on co-financing by the state. The results indicate that awareness-raising campaigns tied to post-earthquake periods are more effective than baseline information programmes, and that subsidy structures are a more powerful lever than technical information provision.

title: Towards a Regional Fragility Function Set for Pannonian-Zone URM Buildings: Integration of Observational and Analytical Data
abstract: This preprint presents work in progress towards empirical-analytical fragility functions for four construction typology classes identified in the PUVZ (Pannonian URM Vojvodina–Zsitva) dataset assembled by the authors over a decade of fieldwork. The dataset currently includes 1,247 buildings in 12 municipalities across northern Serbia and southern Hungary with full attribute coding and, for 304 buildings, matched macroseismic intensity observations from seven historical and instrumental seismic events (Mw 3.9 to 5.1). Analytical fragility is derived from nonlinear static analyses of archetype models calibrated against the flat-jack testing database reported in earlier publications. Observed and analytical fragility are combined using a Bayesian updating scheme. Preliminary median damage thresholds at damage state DS2 (moderate damage) are 0.11 g PGA for the most vulnerable typology class (pre-1918, one storey, rubble infill) and 0.19 g for the least vulnerable (1930–1963, three storeys, ring-beam present). Uncertainty bounds remain wide; additional strong-motion records from the expanding Serbian national network are expected to reduce epistemic variance before journal submission.

title: Street Network Modifications and Predicted Pedestrian Redistribution: Evaluating Three Regeneration Scenarios for the Novi Sad Waterfront
abstract: The Novi Sad municipal authority has proposed three alternative street network configurations for the redevelopment of the Štrand-adjacent waterfront zone, which is expected to accommodate mixed-use development on approximately 11 hectares. This paper uses space syntax scenario modelling to evaluate the pedestrian distribution implications of each proposal. Full axial and segment models were built for each scenario by integrating the proposed network into the existing city-wide model. Radius-3 and radius-5 integration, NACH, and step depth from the existing city centre were computed for all three variants. Scenario B, which extends two existing pedestrian-priority streets directly to the waterfront edge, produces the highest integration uplift for adjacent city-centre streets (mean increase 0.18 in R3 integration) while also distributing flow more evenly across the waterfront frontage. The paper provides a method for presenting syntax-based scenario comparisons in a format accessible to non-specialist planning committees.

title: Acoustic retrofit of a 1960s primary school in Subotica: design process, implementation, and post-occupancy evaluation
abstract: This paper documents the full design-to-evaluation cycle of an acoustic retrofit project at a primary school in Subotica, Serbia, carried out in 2016–2017. Six classrooms were treated with wall-mounted perforated gypsum panels backed by 50 mm glass-wool batts and fabric-wrapped corner bass traps. Pre- and post-retrofit measurements followed ISO 3382-1 for reverberation and ISO 16283-1 for sound insulation; STI was measured at 12 positions per room. Mean T20 at 500 Hz dropped from 1.08 s to 0.58 s. Mean STI improved from 0.55 to 0.71. A post-occupancy survey administered to 14 teachers six months after completion recorded significant reductions in reported vocal fatigue and perceived noise disturbance. Total material cost per classroom was approximately 2 200 EUR, making the solution viable within standard municipal renovation budgets. Simulated predictions using ODEON 16 are compared against measured values.

title: Tactile and Wayfinding Accessibility in Historic Urban Cores: Conflicts Between Conservation Requirements and Inclusive Design Standards
abstract: Installing tactile ground surface indicators and kerb modifications in protected historic zones raises conflicts between heritage conservation rules and accessibility obligations that Serbian legislation does not clearly resolve. This book chapter reviews 14 documented case studies from Serbian and Croatian cities where conflicts arose during public realm works in protected zones, drawing on planning decision records and interviews with six municipal architects and two heritage inspectors. Cases are categorised by conflict type: surface material substitution, level change treatment, and insertion of street furniture with accessibility functions. The chapter proposes a decision framework that identifies conditions under which full-specification TGSI provision is achievable without heritage impact, partial provision is achievable, and a documented derogation should be sought. The framework was trialled retrospectively against five of the 14 cases and found to match the outcome actually reached in three.

title: Creatinine clearance estimation in ICU patients: comparison of four equations against measured 24-hour urinary creatinine
abstract: Accurate estimation of renal function is essential for antibiotic dosing in intensive care, yet the performance of standard equations in critically ill patients remains inconsistent. This prospective observational study enrolled 87 adult patients admitted to a mixed ICU at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina over 14 months. The Cockcroft-Gault, MDRD, CKD-EPI, and Jelliffe equations were each compared against 24-hour measured urinary creatinine clearance (mCrCL). Augmented renal clearance (ARC), defined as mCrCL above 130 mL/min/1.73 m², was identified in 31 patients (35.6%). Cockcroft-Gault showed the smallest bias (mean prediction error −4.1 mL/min) and the narrowest limits of agreement by Bland-Altman analysis, yet still misclassified ARC status in 14 of 31 affected patients. CKD-EPI systematically underestimated clearance in ARC patients (mean error −22.4 mL/min). Findings suggest that none of the tested equations reliably identifies ARC, reinforcing the value of direct urine collection or alternative biomarkers in this population.

title: Population pharmacokinetics of piperacillin-tazobactam in critically ill patients with and without augmented renal clearance
abstract: Piperacillin-tazobactam is a first-line agent in ICU empirical therapy, but its pharmacokinetics are markedly altered in patients with augmented renal clearance (ARC). This study developed a population pharmacokinetic model using NONMEM 7.4 in 64 adult ICU patients receiving piperacillin-tazobactam as a standard 30-minute infusion. A two-compartment model with first-order elimination best described the data. Measured creatinine clearance (mCrCL) and body weight were identified as significant covariates for clearance and volume of distribution, respectively. In the 23 patients with ARC (mCrCL > 130 mL/min), total piperacillin clearance was 64% higher than in non-ARC patients (15.3 vs. 9.3 L/h). Monte Carlo simulations (10,000 iterations) demonstrated that standard dosing (4.5 g every 6 hours) achieved the 50% fT > MIC target in only 61% of simulations against Pseudomonas aeruginosa at MIC 16 mg/L in ARC patients. Extended infusion strategies (over 3 or 4 hours) improved target attainment to 84–91%. Findings support routine TDM and extended infusion in ARC patients.

title: Augmented renal clearance in trauma versus sepsis ICU patients: a prospective comparative cohort study
abstract: The prevalence and determinants of augmented renal clearance (ARC) may differ between ICU admission diagnoses. This study prospectively enrolled 112 adult patients over 18 months, stratified by primary admission diagnosis: trauma (n = 55) and sepsis (n = 57). ARC, defined as 8-hour urinary creatinine clearance above 130 mL/min/1.73 m², was assessed on ICU days 1, 3, and 7. Prevalence of ARC on day 1 was significantly higher in trauma patients (52.7%) compared to sepsis patients (28.1%, p = 0.009). In multivariate logistic regression, younger age (OR 0.96 per year, 95% CI 0.93–0.99), male sex (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.1–5.3), and lower APACHE II score (OR 0.91 per point) were independent predictors of ARC across both groups. ARC resolved by day 7 in 71% of sepsis patients but persisted in 61% of trauma patients still in the ICU at that time point. These findings have direct implications for antibiotic dosing protocol stratification.

title: PK/PD target attainment of meropenem in ICU patients: impact of renal function and infusion duration
abstract: Meropenem is a carbapenem widely used in severe infections, yet its pharmacokinetic variability in critical illness complicates dosing. A prospective observational study collected 312 plasma samples from 48 adult ICU patients receiving meropenem 1 g or 2 g every 8 hours. A one-compartment linear model was fitted in Monolix 2019R2. Measured creatinine clearance was the strongest covariate for drug clearance (p < 0.001). Monte Carlo simulation (n = 5,000) evaluated PK/PD target attainment (%fT > MIC ≥ 40%) across three dosing regimens and two infusion durations (30 min vs. 3 h) at MIC breakpoints from 0.5 to 8 mg/L. For MIC = 2 mg/L, prolonged infusion of 2 g every 8 h achieved 91% target attainment compared to 74% for standard 30-minute infusion. In patients with mCrCL > 150 mL/min, even prolonged infusion of 2 g failed to achieve ≥ 90% target attainment at MIC = 4 mg/L, suggesting dose escalation may be warranted in this subgroup.

title: Pharmacokinetic modelling approaches for antibiotic optimisation in the ICU: a methodological review
abstract: Population pharmacokinetic modelling, Bayesian forecasting, and Monte Carlo simulation have become central tools for antibiotic dosing decisions in intensive care. This book chapter reviews the theoretical foundations and practical application of these methods, focusing on software platforms in common clinical use: NONMEM, Monolix, and Pmetrics. The chapter addresses model-building steps including structural model selection, covariate analysis, and internal and external validation, illustrated with examples drawn from studies of beta-lactam and aminoglycoside antibiotics. Special attention is given to augmented renal clearance as a pharmacokinetic driver, biomarkers for renal function estimation, and the translation of model outputs into actionable dosing recommendations at the bedside. Limitations of current approaches are discussed, including sparse sampling in critically ill patients, time-varying covariates, and the gap between population-level predictions and individual patient management. The chapter is aimed at clinical pharmacists and pharmacologists entering this research area.

title: External validation of a published population pharmacokinetic model for ceftazidime in ICU patients using a Serbian cohort
abstract: External validation of published population pharmacokinetic (popPK) models before local implementation is rarely performed but is critical for patient safety. This study externally validated a ceftazidime popPK model originally developed in a French ICU cohort against prospectively collected data from 41 adult ICU patients at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Plasma samples (n = 193) were collected at steady state; measured creatinine clearance ranged from 42 to 218 mL/min, with ARC present in 39% of patients. Predictive performance was assessed using mean prediction error (bias), root mean squared prediction error (imprecision), and normalised prediction distribution errors (NPDE). The original model showed acceptable bias (MPE −6.8%) but poor imprecision (RMSE 38.2%) and non-normal NPDE distribution in patients with ARC. A re-estimation step in NONMEM, adjusting the clearance-creatinine clearance relationship, substantially improved RMSE to 22.4% and normalised the NPDE distribution. Results underscore the importance of local validation before adopting external models for Bayesian-guided TDM.

title: Continuous versus intermittent infusion of beta-lactams in ICU patients with augmented renal clearance: a prospective randomised pilot study
abstract: Continuous infusion (CI) of beta-lactam antibiotics has theoretical advantages over intermittent bolus dosing for time-dependent killing, particularly in patients with augmented renal clearance (ARC) in whom intermittent dosing frequently fails pharmacodynamic targets. This pilot randomised controlled trial enrolled 60 adult ICU patients with confirmed or suspected gram-negative infection and mCrCL > 130 mL/min, allocated to CI (n = 30) or intermittent infusion (n = 30) of either piperacillin-tazobactam or meropenem, with antibiotic selection at clinician discretion. PK/PD target attainment (100% fT > 4× MIC) at 48 hours was the primary pharmacodynamic endpoint, assessed by population PK modelling on collected trough and steady-state samples. CI achieved the pharmacodynamic target in 83.3% of patients versus 56.7% in the intermittent group (p = 0.022). Clinical cure at day 7 was numerically higher in the CI group (63% vs. 47%, p = 0.18). No significant difference in adverse events was observed. The study was powered for the pharmacodynamic endpoint only; clinical outcomes require confirmation in a larger trial.

title: Development of a Bayesian dosing tool for piperacillin in ICU patients with highly variable renal clearance: model building and internal validation
abstract: Bedside Bayesian dosing tools can facilitate real-time individualisation of antibiotic therapy, but their development requires robust underlying population pharmacokinetic models and careful validation. This study developed and internally validated a population PK model for piperacillin intended as the engine of a prototype clinical decision support module. Data comprised 504 plasma samples from 82 adult ICU patients at two Serbian sites. A two-compartment model with first-order elimination and a proportional residual error model was selected based on objective function value and visual predictive checks. Measured creatinine clearance (mCrCL), total body weight, and vasopressor use were retained as significant covariates. Internal validation by bootstrapping (n = 1,000 runs) and prediction-corrected visual predictive checks confirmed model stability. Simulation scenarios modelled dosing adjustments at mCrCL intervals of 50 mL/min from 60 to 250 mL/min. The tool prototype was implemented in a web-based interface using R Shiny, enabling target concentration input and posterior PK parameter estimation from one to three concentration measurements.

title: Differential fermentation kinetics of inulin-type fructans and their effect on luteolin aglycone release in a pH-controlled in vitro digestion system
abstract: Inulin-type fructans differ in degree of polymerisation and consequently in fermentation rate and site within the colon, which may affect the local availability of co-ingested flavonoids. We compared short-chain fructooligosaccharides (scFOS, DP 2–8), long-chain inulin (lcInulin, DP 10–60), and Agave-derived inulin (DP 22–34) using a three-stage continuous in vitro colon model (pH 5.5, 6.2, and 6.8 in proximal, transverse, and distal compartments, respectively). Microbial inocula were prepared from pooled faecal samples of eight healthy volunteers. Luteolin (30 µM) was introduced at the proximal stage. scFOS supported faster fermentation (maximum gas production at 8 h) and earlier luteolin ring-fission, producing resorcinol derivatives predominantly in the proximal compartment. lcInulin deferred peak catabolism to the distal compartment (20–24 h), yielding higher concentrations of phloroglucinol. Total flavonoid recovery across compartments varied between 12 and 27% depending on fibre source. Results suggest that fibre chain length can be exploited to spatially target flavonoid catabolism along the colon.

title: Encapsulation of rutin in pectin-alginate microbeads: fibre matrix effects on simulated gastrointestinal release and subsequent colonic catabolism
abstract: Combining prebiotic fibres as both encapsulant and colon-targeting matrix could simultaneously deliver a bioactive flavonoid and modulate the microenvironment responsible for its catabolism. We prepared rutin-loaded microbeads using high-methoxyl pectin (2%), sodium alginate (1%), and CaCl₂ gelation, achieving encapsulation efficiencies of 78–84%. Beads (mean diameter 1.1 ± 0.2 mm) were subjected to a sequential in vitro digestion protocol (gastric: pH 1.8, 2 h; intestinal: pH 6.8, 3 h; colonic: batch fermentation with faecal slurry, 24 h). HPLC analysis showed less than 8% rutin release through the intestinal phase; colonic fermentation produced a catabolite profile dominated by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylpropionic acid (22.3 µM) and phloroglucinol (11.7 µM). Unencapsulated rutin produced significantly less 3,4-dihydroxyphenylpropionic acid (14.1 µM) under identical fermentation conditions, suggesting that the pectin matrix promoted metabolically active microbial communities. Microbead preparation is scalable and compatible with food-grade processing conditions.

title: Comparative immunogenicity reporting in biosimilar mAb registration dossiers: gaps between ICH S6(R1) requirements and submitted data
abstract: ICH S6(R1) and the corresponding EMA guideline on similar biological medicinal products require characterisation of immunogenic potential as part of the non-clinical and clinical comparability exercise. This paper systematically reviewed the immunogenicity sections of 24 biosimilar monoclonal antibody registration dossiers submitted to EMA between 2015 and 2021, using redacted dossier summaries obtained through freedom-of-information requests and published EPARs. Extraction focused on assay formats used, cut-point validation approaches, reporting of neutralising antibody prevalence, and duration of immunogenicity follow-up. Results showed that 10 of 24 dossiers reported neutralising antibody data only as a secondary endpoint with no pre-specified equivalence margin. Follow-up periods ranged from 24 to 52 weeks, with no dossier providing data beyond one year. A gap analysis against current ICH Q5E and EMA biosimilar guidelines identified seven discrete areas of inconsistent compliance. The findings were communicated to the Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee secretariat as a background briefing note.

title: Threshold Selection Strategies for Binary Classifiers Trained on Severely Imbalanced Sensor Data
abstract: Operational sensor logs from industrial machinery frequently exhibit class imbalance ratios exceeding 1:500 between fault and normal states. Standard classifiers trained on such data learn to minimise overall loss by almost entirely ignoring the minority class. This paper evaluates seven threshold-moving strategies—including cost-sensitive calibration, F-beta optimisation, and precision-recall break-even—on four publicly available and two proprietary vibration datasets with imbalance ratios between 1:200 and 1:1200. Experiments use three base classifiers: logistic regression, a gradient-boosted tree, and a one-dimensional convolutional network. Results show that threshold strategies interacting with the base classifier type produce large performance variation: no single strategy dominates across all settings. For the convolutional model, precision-recall break-even consistently achieves the best G-mean scores, while cost-sensitive calibration favours recall at an unacceptable precision cost on the most extreme imbalance cases. Recommendations are given as a decision guide indexed by imbalance ratio and acceptable false-positive rate.
