title: Comparative Evaluation of Oversampling Techniques for Multivariate Time-Series Fault Classification
abstract: Synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) and its variants were originally designed for tabular data and do not respect temporal dependencies present in multivariate sensor streams. This paper compares six oversampling methods—SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, TimeGAN-based synthesis, DTW-barycentric averaging, and a simple window-jitter baseline—on three industrial datasets: hydraulic pump telemetry, CNC spindle vibration, and electrical substation load measurements. Each dataset is split chronologically to avoid leakage, and ten-fold cross-validation is applied within the training segment. Evaluation uses area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) and macro F1. DTW-barycentric averaging achieves the highest AUPRC on the two vibration datasets (0.84 and 0.79 respectively) but underperforms TimeGAN on the load dataset. Window jitter, despite its simplicity, ranks third overall and substantially outperforms standard SMOTE in all tested settings, suggesting that temporal coherence is more important than interpolation sophistication for most fault types.

title: A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information
abstract: In many industrial monitoring scenarios, operators can label a small fraction of anomalous events while the majority of the data stream remains unlabelled. Standard one-class SVM (OC-SVM) ignores partial labels entirely; this paper proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation. The method is evaluated on four datasets: bearing degradation signals, network intrusion logs, medical ECG records with annotated arrhythmia bursts, and a synthetic benchmark with controlled sparsity of positive labels (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). At 5% label density, the constrained OC-SVM reduces false-negative rate by 18 percentage points relative to the unconstrained baseline without statistically significant change in false-positive rate. The framework adds a single hyperparameter controlling constraint weight and remains tractable for datasets up to 500,000 samples with an RBF kernel. Ablation studies confirm that gains diminish beyond 15% label density, at which point a supervised SVM becomes preferable.

title: Detecting Concept Drift in Streaming Fault Data Using Adaptive Windowing and Classifier Ensemble Voting
abstract: Industrial processes evolve over time due to wear, seasonal variation, and deliberate operational changes, causing the statistical properties of sensor streams to shift. Classifiers trained on historical data degrade silently when such drift occurs. This work applies ADWIN-based adaptive windowing to trigger retraining of a rotating ensemble of gradient-boosted classifiers on a gas compressor monitoring stream collected over 26 months. Three types of artificial concept drift—sudden, gradual, and recurrent—are injected into a held-out test segment and detection latency is measured. ADWIN combined with ensemble voting detects sudden drift with a median latency of 47 samples and gradual drift with a latency of 190 samples, compared to 620 samples for a non-adaptive baseline. Memory overhead is bounded by retaining at most five ensemble members. The study also documents four naturally occurring drifts identified in the real 26-month log, correlating two of them with documented maintenance events.

title: Self-Training with Uncertainty Filtering for Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection in High-Dimensional Process Data
abstract: Self-training iteratively assigns pseudo-labels to unlabelled samples and retrains a classifier, but in highly imbalanced settings pseudo-label noise disproportionately corrupts the minority class. This paper introduces an uncertainty filter based on prediction entropy estimated through Monte Carlo dropout: only samples whose entropy falls below a calibrated threshold enter the pseudo-labelled pool. The method is tested on three high-dimensional datasets (128 to 512 features) derived from chemical reactor sensors, semiconductor fabrication metrology, and server performance counters, all with imbalance ratios above 1:300. Starting from 2% labelled data, the filtered self-training approach reaches 91% of fully supervised F1 performance on the chemical reactor dataset, compared to 74% for standard self-training. Runtime scales linearly in dataset size and does not require architectural changes beyond enabling dropout at inference time. A sensitivity analysis over the entropy threshold is provided.

title: Benchmarking Real-Time Anomaly Detection Pipelines on Edge Hardware Under Memory and Latency Constraints
abstract: Deploying anomaly detection at the network edge requires balancing model accuracy against strict memory budgets and latency targets. This paper profiles eight detection pipelines—including isolation forest, lightweight autoencoder, quantised convolutional network, and random forest with feature hashing—on three edge boards (an ARM Cortex-A72 single-board computer, a microcontroller-class device with 256 KB RAM, and an FPGA soft-processor). Workloads are drawn from wind turbine SCADA signals and smart meter load profiles sampled at 10 Hz and 1 Hz respectively. The quantised convolutional network fits within 200 KB and achieves 97% of its full-precision AUPRC while meeting a 5 ms per-window latency budget on the ARM board. On the microcontroller, only isolation forest and feature-hashed random forest are deployable; the latter achieves the better AUPRC (0.71 vs. 0.63). All profiling code and configuration files are released under an open licence.

title: Imbalanced Learning for Industrial Time-Series: A Structured Review of Methods and Evaluation Practices
abstract: This chapter surveys the literature on learning from imbalanced industrial time-series data published between 2010 and 2022, covering approximately 160 papers. The chapter is organised around five methodological families: resampling, cost-sensitive training, anomaly-detection-based approaches, threshold adjustment, and ensemble methods. For each family, representative algorithms are described, and reported evaluation metrics are tabulated. A recurring finding is that many papers report only accuracy or AUC-ROC despite these being insensitive to minority-class performance at high imbalance ratios; the chapter argues for systematic reporting of AUPRC and G-mean alongside domain-relevant cost measures. A taxonomy of evaluation pitfalls specific to temporal data—including label leakage across temporal folds and inappropriate use of stratified k-fold on non-stationary streams—is presented. The chapter concludes with a structured list of open problems, including the combination of concept drift adaptation with imbalanced learning and the lack of standardised public benchmarks for industrial fault streams.

title: Active Learning with Query-by-Committee for Labelling Efficiency in Imbalanced Fault Streams
abstract: Obtaining labelled fault examples is expensive in industrial settings because it requires expert inspection. Active learning selects the most informative unlabelled samples for expert annotation, potentially reducing labelling cost. This paper applies query-by-committee (QBC) using a committee of five classifiers—two gradient-boosted trees, two SVMs with different kernels, and a shallow neural network—to three simulated fault streams with imbalance ratios of 1:100, 1:500, and 1:2000. A disagreement-weighted sampling strategy biased toward minority-class candidates is introduced to counteract the tendency of standard QBC to query near the decision boundary in the majority class region. The biased strategy reaches 90% of fully labelled F1 using only 12% of available labels at 1:500 imbalance, compared to 21% for unbiased QBC and 31% for random sampling. Latency until the first useful model (F1 > 0.5) is reduced from 840 queries to 310 queries under the biased strategy.

title: Embedded Predictive Coding for Inertial Measurement Unit Streams in Vehicle Telematics
abstract: Fleet telematics units generate high-volume 6-axis IMU data at 100 Hz used for driver behaviour scoring and road surface classification. This paper describes a predictive coder for IMU streams that uses second-order linear prediction with coefficients updated per frame via a recursive least-squares routine fitting within 2 kB of working memory on a Cortex-M7 at 216 MHz. Residuals are quantised with a non-uniform scalar quantiser whose levels are adapted to a Laplacian residual distribution. Across 480 km of mixed urban, motorway, and rural driving logged with an instrumented vehicle, the coder achieves a mean compression ratio of 5.2:1 at 3.1% root-mean-square normalised distortion. Hard braking and pothole events, identified by a reference classifier, were preserved with 96.4% event retention versus 78.1% for a non-adaptive arithmetic coder at the same bit rate. Computational load was 1.4% of CPU capacity, leaving ample headroom for concurrent GNSS and CAN processing.

title: Static Analysis of Notebook Smells
abstract: The software-engineering concept of code smells has been adapted for Jupyter notebooks, where additional structural issues such as non-linear execution order, long chains of imports split across cells, and oversized cells with mixed concerns are common. This book chapter reviews the state of the art in notebook smell detection tools and taxonomies as of 2020, categorises fourteen proposed smell types from the literature, and evaluates four open-source detectors against a common benchmark of 400 annotated notebooks. Detection rates range from 41 % to 67 % for the smell types each tool targets. The chapter also presents guidelines for incorporating smell detection into continuous-integration workflows and discusses how certain smells, particularly those involving hidden execution state, overlap with reproducibility and correctness failures. Original contributions include a unified smell ontology and a mapping between smell types and the defect categories from earlier empirical studies by the authors. Intended audience includes practitioners designing data-science toolchains and researchers building analysis tools.

title: Weibull Parameter Estimation for Hydraulic Cylinder Seals Under Variable Load Cycles
abstract: This paper addresses the estimation of two-parameter Weibull shape and scale parameters for hydraulic cylinder rod seals operating under variable cyclic loads in industrial assembly lines. Failure time data were collected from 214 seal specimens tested on a purpose-built hydraulic fatigue bench at pressures ranging from 120 to 280 bar and cycle frequencies of 0.5 to 4 Hz. Maximum likelihood estimation and median-rank regression were compared using Anderson–Darling goodness-of-fit statistics. Results indicate that the shape parameter varies between 1.8 and 2.4 depending on load profile, implying wear-out behaviour across all conditions. The scale parameter was found to decrease nonlinearly with increasing pressure amplitude, and an empirical correction factor is proposed to adjust standard catalogue life predictions. Confidence intervals on the B10 life differed by up to 18% between the two estimation methods for small samples, a finding with direct implications for maintenance interval setting in low-volume production environments.

title: Joint Optimisation of Maintenance Intervals and Spare-Parts Stock Levels for Hydraulic Pump Units
abstract: This study formulates a joint optimisation model that simultaneously determines the preventive replacement interval and the reorder point and order quantity for spare hydraulic pump units in a flexible manufacturing system. The pump lifetime is modelled with a three-parameter Weibull distribution fitted to 19 years of field records from a press-forming plant. Demand for spares is treated as an intermittent Poisson process driven by the replacement intensity. Total expected cost per unit time, comprising holding, ordering, replacement labour, and production-loss costs, is minimised using a grid-search procedure over a two-dimensional decision space. The optimal policy reduces total cost by 22% relative to the current practice of using independent fixed-interval maintenance and (s, Q) inventory rules. Sensitivity analysis shows that the cost function is relatively flat near the optimum with respect to replacement interval, but steep with respect to reorder point, suggesting that inventory decisions deserve priority attention in practice.

title: Reliability-Centred Maintenance Planning for Automated Assembly Lines: A Case Study in the Automotive Supply Sector
abstract: This chapter describes the application of a reliability-centred maintenance methodology to a six-station automated assembly line for gearbox sub-assemblies at a Tier-2 automotive supplier in central Serbia. Functional failure analysis identified 48 failure modes across hydraulic clamping, pneumatic transfer, and electric drive subsystems. Criticality was ranked using a modified risk priority matrix that incorporates Weibull-based probability of failure within the maintenance window alongside severity and detectability scores. Maintenance tasks were selected from inspection, time-based replacement, and condition monitoring, and intervals were set by minimising expected total downtime cost. Implementation over an 18-month pilot period reduced unplanned stoppages by 31% and decreased annual spare-parts expenditure by approximately 8%. The chapter also discusses practical barriers encountered during data collection and workforce engagement, and provides a template for applying the procedure in similar environments.

title: Effect of Contamination Level on the Failure Rate of Hydraulic Directional Valves: A Competing-Risks Analysis
abstract: Hydraulic directional control valves in automated assembly systems are subject to multiple competing failure causes, primarily spool wear, solenoid coil burnout, and seal extrusion. This paper applies a competing-risks framework combining cause-specific Weibull sub-distributions to field failure data from 104 valves monitored over 36 months across three production facilities. Particle contamination level, quantified as ISO 4406 cleanliness class, was recorded at monthly intervals and included as a time-varying covariate in a cause-specific proportional hazard model. Spool wear failure rate increased sharply above ISO cleanliness class 18/16/13, while the other two causes were not significantly associated with contamination. The overall component reliability under contamination class 18/16/13 is estimated to be 34% lower at 10 000 operating hours than under class 16/14/11. Implications for filtration specification and maintenance interval adjustment are presented alongside a practical contamination monitoring protocol.

title: Spare-Parts Demand Forecasting for Low-Turnover Pneumatic Actuators Using Reliability-Based Simulation
abstract: Spare-parts demand for slow-moving pneumatic actuators is difficult to forecast using classical time-series methods due to infrequent and irregular consumption. This paper proposes a Monte Carlo simulation approach in which individual actuator lifetimes are sampled from fitted Weibull distributions and aggregated over a fleet of 280 actuators in a battery module assembly plant. The simulation generates empirical demand distributions at weekly resolution, which are then used to set stock levels meeting a 95% part-availability service level. Comparison with historical consumption data over a 24-month validation period shows that the simulation-based stock levels reduce average inventory holding by 17% while maintaining the target service level, outperforming both exponential smoothing and Croston's method. The approach is straightforward to implement in spreadsheet tools commonly used in Serbian manufacturing SMEs and does not require dedicated forecasting software.

title: Maintenance Cost Modelling for Pneumatic Grippers Subject to Wear-Out: Comparison of Age-Replacement and Opportunistic Policies
abstract: This paper compares age-replacement and opportunistic maintenance policies for pneumatic parallel grippers in a multi-station assembly line. Gripper lifetime data from six production lines over five years were pooled and a Weibull distribution with shape parameter 2.1 and scale 14 200 operating cycles was fitted. Under opportunistic maintenance, replacements are triggered when a gripper reaches a specified threshold fraction of its B50 life while another component in the same station is being replaced. Total expected cost per production cycle, incorporating gripper unit cost, labour, and line-stoppage penalties, was evaluated analytically for age-replacement and by discrete-event simulation for the opportunistic policy. Opportunistic maintenance reduces expected cost by 11 to 19% depending on the stoppage penalty assumed, with the greatest benefit at stations with three or more concurrent components nearing their replacement thresholds. A decision chart is provided to guide practitioners in selecting between the two policies.

title: Incorporating Covariate-Based Hazard Models into SCADA-Driven Maintenance Scheduling for Hydraulic Presses
abstract: Modern hydraulic presses in sheet-metal forming lines generate continuous SCADA data streams including pressure peaks, cycle time, and temperature. This paper describes a framework for integrating time-varying covariate data from SCADA into a Cox proportional hazard model to produce dynamic replacement schedules for hydraulic cylinder assemblies. Data from 18 press units over 30 months were used, yielding 94 observed cylinder failures. Covariates extracted at 10-minute intervals were aggregated into daily summary statistics; peak pressure exceedances above 310 bar and temperature cycles above 65 °C emerged as the strongest predictors. The hazard model was updated daily and used to compute the next-day replacement probability; a threshold probability of 0.12 per day triggered a work order. Compared to a fixed 4 500-cycle replacement interval, the policy reduced emergency replacements from 38 to 11 over the 12-month prospective validation period, with a modest 6% increase in planned replacement cost.

title: Sensitivity of Optimal Maintenance Intervals to Weibull Parameter Uncertainty: A Bootstrap-Based Assessment for Small Fleet Sizes
abstract: In many industrial settings, lifetime datasets for hydraulic and pneumatic components contain fewer than 30 complete failure observations, making Weibull parameter estimates highly uncertain. This paper quantifies how this uncertainty propagates into optimal preventive replacement intervals derived from an age-replacement cost model. A parametric bootstrap procedure is applied to eight empirical datasets with sample sizes ranging from 12 to 48 complete failures, covering hydraulic seals, pneumatic cylinders, and directional valves. For each bootstrap sample, optimal intervals are recomputed and their distribution characterised. Results show that the coefficient of variation of the optimal interval exceeds 25% for samples smaller than 20, rising above 40% for samples of 12. A conservative interval selection strategy using the 75th-percentile bootstrap estimate is proposed and evaluated against an expected-cost criterion; it reduces the probability of selecting an interval that increases realised cost by more than 10% from 31% to 9% across the datasets studied.

title: Regression Model Selection Criteria for IPMVP Option C: An Empirical Comparison Across 30 Industrial Sites
abstract: Multiple candidate regression models can satisfy ASHRAE Guideline 14 acceptance thresholds for the same facility, leaving practitioners without clear guidance on selection. This paper applies six model selection criteria—adjusted R², AIC, BIC, CVRMSE, mean bias error, and fractional bias—to datasets from 30 industrial sites across Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. Criteria disagree on best model in 43% of cases when three or more candidate models are evaluated. A scoring approach combining adjusted R², CVRMSE, and MBE simultaneously selects models that produce lower out-of-sample savings estimation error than any single-criterion approach, as validated by withheld test periods. The paper also documents that including more than four independent variables rarely improves out-of-sample performance despite improving in-sample fit, consistent with overfitting concerns. Recommendations are provided for practitioners specifying baseline modelling procedures in EPC contracts.

title: Benchmarking OEE in the Western Balkans food and beverage sector: cross-industry survey findings
abstract: Benchmarking studies of OEE in the food and beverage sector from developing economies in Southeast Europe are scarce, making target-setting for regional plants difficult. This paper reports findings from a structured survey of 61 food and beverage production sites across Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, administered between 2023 and 2024. Plant maintenance managers provided 12-month retrospective OEE figures, loss category breakdowns, and descriptive data on maintenance organisation. Usable responses were obtained from 48 sites covering dairy, beverage, bakery, and edible oils sub-sectors. Median OEE across all sites was 64.1 % (IQR 54–72 %). Dairy and edible-oil plants reported significantly lower availability rates than beverage plants (p < 0.05, Mann-Whitney U test). Plants with a dedicated maintenance planner role reported 7.2 percentage-point higher OEE than those without, after controlling for plant size and equipment age. These findings provide the first regional OEE benchmarks for food manufacturing in the Western Balkans and are intended to support maintenance managers in setting improvement targets grounded in comparable industry data.

title: Influence of annealing temperature on crystallinity and piezoelectric response of spin-coated PVDF thin films on flexible polyimide substrates
abstract: PVDF thin films were deposited by spin coating from dimethylformamide solutions onto 25 µm polyimide substrates and annealed at temperatures between 60 °C and 140 °C in steps of 20 °C. X-ray diffraction confirmed that the β-phase fraction increased from 38% to 61% as annealing temperature rose from 60 °C to 120 °C, declining above that threshold due to partial α-phase recrystallisation. The piezoelectric charge coefficient d33 was measured by a Berlincourt-type meter and reached a maximum of 24 pC/N at 120 °C. Impedance spectroscopy across 100 Hz–1 MHz revealed that the electromechanical coupling factor kt peaked at 0.18 for the same condition. Film thickness ranged from 1.1 µm to 2.4 µm as confirmed by contact profilometry. The results provide a process window for fabricating flexible PVDF sensors compatible with standard printed circuit board assembly, without requiring additional poling steps beyond the annealing treatment.

title: Electromechanical characterisation of PVDF-TrFE cantilever harvesters under controlled base excitation at frequencies below 50 Hz
abstract: Cantilever beams of PVDF-TrFE (77:23 mol%) were fabricated on stainless-steel shims and characterised under sinusoidal base excitation at amplitudes of 0.05 g to 0.5 g and frequencies from 5 Hz to 50 Hz, representative of ambient structural vibrations. Each beam was 30 mm × 8 mm with a 0.8 g proof mass at the tip. Open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current, and output power were recorded across a resistive load sweep from 10 kΩ to 10 MΩ. Peak output power of 18.4 µW was obtained at 22 Hz, 0.3 g excitation, and an optimal load of 680 kΩ. The frequency response showed a half-power bandwidth of 3.1 Hz. Tip displacement was monitored by laser vibrometry, and the electromechanical coupling coefficient k² was derived as 0.021. Fatigue testing over 10⁷ cycles at 0.3 g showed no measurable change in d33 or resonance frequency, indicating mechanical durability suitable for embedded sensor nodes.

title: Screen-printed silver electrodes on PVDF membranes: contact resistance, adhesion and effect on harvested power
abstract: The integration of flexible piezoelectric films with compliant electrodes is a recognised bottleneck in harvester fabrication. This study evaluates screen-printed silver paste electrodes on 28 µm PVDF membranes, comparing three commercially available conductive inks with different binder systems cured at 80 °C and 120 °C. Contact resistance was measured by four-point probe and ranged from 0.4 Ω/sq to 3.1 Ω/sq depending on ink formulation and curing temperature. Adhesion was assessed by cross-cut tape tests following repeated bending cycles (bending radius 5 mm, 5000 cycles); two of three inks showed visible delamination above 2000 cycles. For the best-performing ink, output power density at 25 Hz, 0.2 g excitation was 8.7 µW/cm², compared with 9.1 µW/cm² for sputtered gold electrodes under identical conditions, representing a 4.4% penalty. The findings support screen printing as a low-cost electrode route for prototyping flexible harvesters where moderate efficiency loss is acceptable.

title: Comparison of poling protocols for solution-cast PVDF-TrFE films: corona discharge versus contact poling under variable temperature
abstract: PVDF-TrFE (75:25 mol%) films cast from methyl ethyl ketone solutions were poled using two protocols: corona discharge at a needle-to-plate gap of 30 mm, applied voltage 15 kV, and contact poling at electric fields of 40–80 MV/m combined with simultaneous heating to 50–100 °C. Remnant polarisation (Pr) was extracted from P–E hysteresis loops measured at 100 Hz. Corona-poled samples achieved Pr of 68 mC/m² compared with 74 mC/m² for the best contact-poled condition (70 MV/m, 80 °C). The d33 values followed the same trend, reaching 29 pC/N and 32 pC/N respectively. Thermal stability was evaluated by holding samples at 60 °C for 500 hours; both sets showed less than 8% decrease in Pr, with no statistically significant difference between protocols. Corona poling produced more spatially uniform polarisation as mapped by piezoelectric force microscopy across 50 µm × 50 µm areas, making it preferable for large-area flexible substrates.

title: Flexible PVDF-based vibration sensor patches for structural health monitoring of grain storage silos
abstract: Grain storage structures in agricultural settings generate low-frequency, low-amplitude vibrations (5–40 Hz, 0.02–0.15 g) during filling and discharge operations. This paper describes fabrication and field testing of adhesive sensor patches incorporating 52 µm PVDF-TrFE films encapsulated between polyurethane layers and attached to steel silo walls at three facilities in Vojvodina, Serbia. Patches measured 60 mm × 40 mm and included an on-patch charge amplifier circuit. Vibration signatures were recorded over 30-day periods and compared against reference accelerometer data (Pearson r = 0.93). Output voltages ranged from 12 mV to 340 mV depending on wall position and load state. Patch-to-patch sensitivity variation across 12 units was ±6.3%, attributed primarily to electrode printing tolerances. Durability under temperature cycling (−10 °C to +45 °C, 50 cycles) showed no performance degradation beyond measurement uncertainty. The approach is proposed as a low-cost complement to wired accelerometer networks for condition monitoring in rural infrastructure.

title: Effect of ZnO nanoparticle doping on the piezoelectric and dielectric properties of PVDF-TrFE thin films
abstract: ZnO nanoparticles (mean diameter 35 nm, confirmed by TEM) were dispersed in PVDF-TrFE solutions at concentrations of 0, 1, 3, 5, and 10 wt% and the resulting composite films were spin-coated onto ITO-coated PET substrates. FTIR confirmed that β-phase content increased from 58% to 67% at 3 wt% ZnO before declining at higher loadings due to particle agglomeration observed by SEM. d33 measured by the Berlincourt method rose from 26 pC/N to 35 pC/N at 3 wt%, then fell to 21 pC/N at 10 wt%. Relative permittivity at 1 kHz increased monotonically from 9.4 to 16.2 across the doping range, while dielectric loss remained below 0.05 for concentrations up to 5 wt%. Harvested power from a 25 mm × 10 mm cantilever at 30 Hz, 0.25 g was 11.3 µW for the 3 wt% composite versus 8.8 µW for the undoped film. Leakage current density at 50 MV/m increased from 2.1 nA/cm² to 18.7 nA/cm² at 10 wt%, imposing a practical upper limit on doping.

title: Integration of flexible PVDF harvesters with ultra-low-power wireless sensor nodes: end-to-end energy budget analysis
abstract: Autonomous wireless sensor nodes require a complete understanding of the energy budget from mechanical excitation to data transmission. This paper presents measurements and modelling for a system comprising a PVDF-TrFE cantilever harvester (active area 12 cm²), a rectifier–storage circuit using a 1 mF supercapacitor, and a custom 2.4 GHz transceiver operating at a 60-second beacon interval. Under floor vibration excitation typical of a light industrial workshop (18 Hz, 0.08 g), the harvester delivered 4.2 µW average power, which charged the supercapacitor from 0 V to operational threshold (1.8 V) in 94 seconds. The transceiver consumed 3.1 µW average power at the chosen duty cycle, yielding a net positive energy balance of 1.1 µW. Temperature sensitivity of the harvester output (−0.22 µW/°C between 15 °C and 45 °C) was characterised and incorporated into the model. Packet reception rate over a 48-hour continuous test was 97.4%. The study identifies rectifier diode forward voltage drop as the dominant loss mechanism, accounting for 31% of total losses.

title: Wearable PVDF-TrFE patches for gait-induced energy harvesting: placement optimisation and mechanical loading analysis
abstract: Placement of flexible piezoelectric harvesters on the human body determines both the available strain amplitude and the usability of the device. This study compares four body locations — heel insole, ankle strap, knee brace, and lower-back belt — using thin (80 µm total stack) PVDF-TrFE patches instrumented simultaneously on five participants walking at 4 km/h and 6 km/h on a treadmill. Finite element modelling with measured gait kinematics predicted maximum principal strains of 920 µε (heel), 450 µε (ankle), 210 µε (knee), and 130 µε (lower back). Measured open-circuit voltages over 10-step averages were 2.1 V, 0.9 V, 0.5 V, and 0.3 V respectively, consistent with FEM predictions within 14%. Harvested power per step at the heel location averaged 38 µJ through a matched 500 kΩ load. Participant comfort ratings on a seven-point scale were lowest for the heel insole (4.2/7) due to thickness, suggesting a design trade-off. Accelerated wear testing at 10⁶ simulated steps showed no cracking of the encapsulation layer.

title: Printed PVDF-TrFE sensors embedded in agricultural drone landing skids for vibration monitoring during crop inspection missions
abstract: Multirotor agricultural drones generate characteristic vibration profiles during takeoff, hovering, and landing that can indicate mechanical degradation or payload imbalance. Flexible PVDF-TrFE sensors were embedded within 3D-printed polylactic acid landing skid segments of a commercially available six-rotor drone platform. Sensors were fabricated by aerosol-jet printing of PVDF-TrFE ink followed by corona poling, yielding d33 of 21 pC/N on curved surfaces with radii as small as 15 mm. Sensitivity to vibration in the 10–200 Hz range was calibrated against a MEMS reference accelerometer. During 42 field missions over three months covering vineyards in Fruška Gora, the embedded sensors logged vibration data at 2 kHz sampling. Principal component analysis of the frequency spectra correctly distinguished normal operation from artificially induced motor imbalance in 89% of test cases. Sensor mass was 1.4 g per skid, representing a negligible payload impact. The paper discusses aerosol-jet parameter optimisation and ink rheology constraints.

title: A decision-support architecture for real-time AOS-guided top-dressing: sensor data ingestion, zone assignment, and machine actuation
abstract: This book chapter describes the end-to-end architecture of a real-time variable-rate fertiliser application system developed and tested at BioSense Institute. The system couples a tractor-mounted active optical sensor array with an onboard edge-computing unit that streams reflectance data, applies field-specific calibration coefficients, and communicates rate commands to a pneumatic spreader controller at 2 Hz. The chapter covers the data pipeline from raw detector voltages through NREDI computation, lookup-table-based nitrogen rate assignment, and ISOBUS messaging to the spreader. Integration with pre-existing prescription map layers is handled via a zone-override logic: if AOS-derived nitrogen status deviates from the prescription zone mean by more than one standard deviation, the AOS reading overrides the map layer; otherwise, a weighted average is used. System latency from sensor detection to actuator response averaged 480 ms during field tests on a 150-ha farm. Limitations related to GPS positioning accuracy at headlands are discussed.

title: Characterising packet loss patterns in NB-IoT deployments across mixed urban and agricultural terrain in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper reports an empirical measurement campaign assessing NB-IoT link behaviour at 29 fixed sites across a 2,400 km² area in the Vojvodina region, covering densely built township centres, sparse rural roads, and open crop fields. Uplink and downlink packets were transmitted at 5-minute intervals over 60 consecutive days using commercial SIM7020 modules attached to custom data loggers. The dataset comprises approximately 1.2 million transmission attempts per direction. Results show that packet loss rate is strongly bimodal: median loss of 1.3 percent at sites within 4 km of a base station versus 18.7 percent at sites beyond 12 km. Burst loss episodes lasting more than 30 minutes were observed predominantly between 05:00 and 08:00 local time, correlated with agricultural machinery interference signatures identified via received signal strength indicators. A Markov chain model fitted to the burst statistics achieves a Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance of 0.04 against the measured distribution. The characterisation informs retransmission and local buffering policies discussed in a companion study.

title: A comparison of sensor placement strategies for microclimate reconstruction in vineyard rows
abstract: Vineyard canopy microclimate strongly influences disease pressure and berry quality. This study evaluated four sensor placement strategies—uniform grid, terrain-adaptive, canopy-edge-biased, and random—using data collected across a 12-hectare vineyard in the Fruška Gora foothills during the 2017 growing season. Fifteen roving sensors and five permanently installed reference nodes measured temperature and relative humidity at 10-minute intervals. Reconstruction accuracy for temperature was assessed by treating each fixed node in turn as a withheld target and interpolating from the remaining observations. Terrain-adaptive placement achieved the lowest mean absolute error (0.44 °C) compared to the uniform grid (0.63 °C). Humidity reconstruction was less sensitive to placement strategy, with all configurations performing similarly. Results suggest that even modest topographic relief justifies departing from a regular grid in favour of targeted placement at ecologically distinct positions.

title: Comparative evaluation of drop-casting, spin-coating, and electropolymerisation for MIP layer deposition on QCM transducers
abstract: Three common deposition techniques for molecularly imprinted polymer layers on quartz crystal microbalance gold surfaces were compared with respect to film uniformity, reproducibility between sensors fabricated in the same batch, limit of detection, and operational stability under continuous flow conditions. Ibuprofen was selected as target analyte. Drop-casting produced the thickest films (mean 110 nm, CV = 24% across seven sensors), spin-coating intermediate films (mean 28 nm, CV = 9%), and electropolymerisation produced films of 19 nm (CV = 6%). LODs in 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) were 2.1 µM, 0.4 µM, and 0.6 µM for drop-cast, spin-coated, and electropolymerised sensors respectively. Under continuous flow (0.2 mL min⁻¹) for 48 h, frequency baselines drifted by 12 Hz, 4 Hz, and 3 Hz respectively. Scanning electron microscopy images of cross-sections stained by Pt ion beam deposition confirmed thickness measurements. The results indicate that both spin-coating and electropolymerisation are acceptable for quantitative analysis, while drop-casting is unsuitable for high-precision work without additional planarisation steps.

title: Gravimetric and viscoelastic characterisation of swelling behaviour of cross-linked MIP films in aqueous buffer using QCM-D
abstract: The mechanical and swelling properties of molecularly imprinted polymer films in aqueous environments are often neglected in sensor development despite their direct influence on mass sensitivity calibration. QCM-D measurements in liquid phase were performed on spin-coated MIP films (template: sulfamethoxazole) with three crosslinker densities: 10, 20, and 40 mol% ethylene glycol dimethacrylate relative to total monomer. Voigt-model fitting of ΔF and ΔD overtones (3rd, 5th, 7th) yielded storage moduli of 1.8, 4.5, and 9.2 MPa and loss moduli of 0.4, 0.8, and 1.1 MPa for increasing crosslinker content in buffer. Swelling ratios determined by dry-wet frequency shift comparison were 38%, 22%, and 11% respectively. Use of the Sauerbrey equation without viscoelastic correction overestimated bound analyte mass by 28% for the lowest crosslinker density film but by only 6% for the highest. Sulfamethoxazole rebinding kinetics showed that equilibrium was reached in 8, 12, and 24 min for increasing crosslinker densities, indicating a trade-off between mechanical rigidity and mass transport within the polymer network.

title: Temperature-modulated operation of SnO₂ sensors for discrimination of acetone, ethanol, and toluene below 1 ppm using linear discriminant analysis
abstract: A single SnO₂ thin-film sensor was operated under a sinusoidal temperature modulation profile (250–400 °C, 0.1 Hz) and the resulting dynamic resistance waveform was decomposed into 20 harmonic features per measurement cycle. Linear discriminant analysis was applied to datasets of 360 exposure cycles covering three VOCs (acetone, ethanol, toluene) each at four concentration levels (0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 ppm) in backgrounds of 30–60% RH synthetic air. Classification accuracy was 91.3% for a three-class problem using a leave-one-out cross-validation scheme. Confusion was highest between ethanol and acetone at 0.2 ppm, where accuracy dropped to 79%. The method requires no sensor array and reduces hardware complexity relative to multi-sensor electronic nose approaches. Harmonic feature weights indicated that the 3rd and 5th harmonics carried the greatest discriminatory information, consistent with differences in adsorption/desorption activation energies for the three analytes on grain boundary surface sites.

title: Aspect and action completion: Serbian speakers' mental segmentation of video events
abstract: This study examined whether habitual use of perfective versus imperfective aspect in Serbian influences how native speakers perceive natural action boundaries in silent video clips. Forty-two monolingual Serbian adults watched 60 short video clips of everyday activities and pressed a button whenever they judged one action unit to have ended and another begun. Segmentation rates were compared with those of a matched group of English speakers. Serbian participants produced significantly more fine-grained segmentation at action climax points—events canonically encoded by perfective verbs—than English speakers (mean difference 0.31 segments per 10-s clip, p < .01). A follow-up priming task showed faster recognition of completion-implying images after perfective sentence frames. Results are interpreted as evidence that grammatical aspect shapes online event parsing even when the stimuli are entirely non-linguistic, consistent with weak Whorfian claims. Implications for theories of event segmentation are discussed.

title: Grammatical gender assignment and colour-word associations in Serbian: a replication and extension
abstract: Previous research in several Indo-European languages suggested that the grammatical gender of an object noun correlates with speakers' tendencies to attribute stereotypically gendered colours to the referent. This study attempted a direct replication and extension with Serbian, which has a three-gender system (masculine, feminine, neuter). One hundred and twelve Serbian undergraduates completed a forced-choice colour attribution task for 80 common object images. Objects whose nouns were grammatically feminine were selected as 'pinkish' or 'reddish' significantly more often than masculine or neuter objects (Cohen's d = 0.44). The neuter condition showed no consistent directional bias. A second experiment using reaction times found facilitation when colour probes were congruent with the grammatical gender of the preceding object noun. Effect sizes were modest but reliable across both tasks. The study provides Serbian-language data for a cross-linguistic comparison database and highlights the specificity of gender effects to the feminine–masculine contrast.

title: Does speaking two gender languages double the effect? Object categorisation in Serbian–Hungarian bilinguals
abstract: Serbian and Hungarian differ fundamentally in grammatical gender: Serbian marks gender morphologically on nouns and agreeing words, while Hungarian lacks grammatical gender entirely. This between-language contrast offers a natural test of linguistic relativity in bilinguals. Thirty-two early Serbian–Hungarian bilinguals and 32 Serbian monolinguals performed a free-sorting task with 120 object images. Objects were sorted more often by conceptual category and less often by shape in the monolingual Serbian group than in bilinguals, suggesting that regular exposure to a genderless language attenuated gender-congruence grouping. Additionally, bilinguals' sorting patterns shifted depending on which language was primed immediately before the task (Serbian or Hungarian prime condition), indicating a context-sensitive rather than a fused representation. Response times and sorting consistency across two sessions are reported. The data support a weak, context-modulated version of the Sapir–Whorf hypothesis for gender effects in adulthood.

title: Language priming and similarity judgements for tool and vessel nouns across grammatical genders
abstract: This conference paper reports a preregistered experiment testing whether the grammatical gender of Serbian nouns for common tools (mostly masculine) and vessels (mostly feminine) affects similarity judgements between object pairs that share functional but not perceptual features. Sixty Serbian monolinguals rated the similarity of 90 object pairs on a 7-point scale, with half the pairs sharing grammatical gender and half mismatching. Same-gender pairs received marginally higher similarity ratings overall (mean difference 0.19 scale points), but the effect was significant only for feminine-feminine pairs (p = .03) and not for masculine-masculine pairs (p = .21). This asymmetry had not been predicted and is discussed in relation to frequency and prototypicality of the feminine gender class in Serbian. Limitations regarding the confound between semantic domain and gender class are noted, and a follow-up design with matched noun frequencies is proposed.

title: Aspect-based prediction during sentence processing: eye-tracking evidence from Serbian
abstract: This study used the visual-world eye-tracking paradigm to ask whether Serbian verbal aspect cues allow listeners to anticipate whether an upcoming event will be depicted as completed or ongoing. Forty native Serbian adults heard sentences containing perfective or imperfective verbs while viewing scenes showing an agent, a partially completed action, and a fully completed action. Eye gaze to the target image (completed scene for perfective, ongoing scene for imperfective) was recorded from verb onset through 2,000 ms. Participants showed reliable anticipatory looks to the aspect-congruent image beginning 450 ms after verb onset, well before the sentence-final noun was heard. The anticipatory effect was larger for perfective than imperfective verbs, consistent with the directional asymmetry in aspectual semantics. Individual differences in self-reported mental imagery vividness (VVIQ) did not reliably moderate the anticipation effect. Data are discussed in terms of incremental processing models and the role of grammatical information in predictive coding.

title: Cross-linguistic influence in late bilinguals: grammatical gender congruence effects in L2 German learners with Serbian L1
abstract: German and Serbian share grammatical gender but assign gender to many overlapping nouns differently (e.g., Serbian sunce 'sun' is neuter while German Sonne is feminine). This creates a population of bilinguals for whom the same concept has conflicting gender labels across their two languages. Forty-two Serbian university students learning German at intermediate level (B1–B2) completed a colour attribution task and a metaphor appreciation task in both languages. In the German session, participants showed gender attribution patterns intermediate between German monolinguals and Serbian monolinguals, with the direction of bias predicting the dominant-language index from a language history questionnaire. Metaphor appreciation scores were consistently higher for metaphors gender-congruent with Serbian even in the German session, suggesting a persistent L1 effect at the semantic level. The study offers evidence that late-onset L2 acquisition does not fully override the L1 grammatical gender system in non-linguistic cognition.

title: Linguistic relativity in psychological research: a methodological overview for Slavic-language contexts
abstract: This book chapter surveys methodological approaches used in linguistic-relativity research and evaluates their suitability for studying Slavic languages, which possess elaborate morphological gender and aspect systems rarely addressed together in a single research programme. The chapter first reviews the main paradigms—forced-choice categorisation, similarity judgement, priming, eye-tracking, and interference tasks—and discusses how each controls or fails to control for verbal mediation. A second section addresses the particular challenges posed by Serbian and other South Slavic languages: high case syncretism, free word order, and the interaction of aspect with tense in creating referential ambiguity. Recommendations for stimulus construction, counterbalancing, and the treatment of individual differences in metalinguistic awareness are offered. The chapter ends with a summary of open questions regarding the development of gender and aspect effects across the lifespan and their attenuation or amplification in bilingual populations.

title: Serbian–Hungarian bilinguals show attenuated aspectual framing effects in event memory
abstract: Event memory studies in monolingual populations have shown that perfective framing of a described event leads to better recall of the endpoint and less recall of intermediate steps compared with imperfective framing. This study tested whether the same framing effect appears in Serbian–Hungarian bilinguals (N = 44) relative to Serbian monolinguals (N = 44). Participants read 32 short event descriptions framed with perfective or imperfective verbs, then completed a surprise recognition test 20 minutes later. Serbian monolinguals showed the standard endpoint-advantage for perfective descriptions (d = 0.61). Bilinguals showed a significantly reduced endpoint advantage (d = 0.28), and this reduction was correlated with self-rated Hungarian proficiency (r = .39, p = .009). Additionally, bilinguals showed faster response times on fillers in the Hungarian prime condition, suggesting reduced depth of aspectual processing. The findings extend earlier sorting-task work and suggest that memory-level aspectual framing effects are sensitive to bilingual language experience.

title: Children's acquisition of gender-congruence categorisation biases in Serbian: a longitudinal study from ages 5 to 8
abstract: Adult Serbian speakers show reliable gender-congruence effects in object categorisation tasks, but the developmental trajectory of these effects has not been tracked longitudinally. This preregistered study followed 68 monolingual Serbian-speaking children at ages 5, 6, 7, and 8, administering an age-adapted picture-sorting task and a forced-choice similarity task at each wave. No gender-congruence sorting bias was detectable at age 5. A small but significant bias first emerged at age 6 for feminine nouns (d = 0.31) and at age 7 for masculine nouns (d = 0.27). By age 8 effect sizes were comparable to those typically reported in adult samples. The emergence of the bias correlated with accurate production of gender agreement morphology on adjectives, assessed via a picture-naming elicitation task, suggesting a link between productive morphological command and the onset of the cognitive bias. Neuter-noun objects showed no consistent pattern across any wave.

title: Aspect and tense interaction in simultaneous interpreters: response-time evidence for reduced aspectual priming
abstract: Professional simultaneous interpreters who regularly work between Serbian and Hungarian must rapidly re-encode aspectually marked Serbian verb forms into a language lacking grammatical aspect. If interpreting experience weakens the cognitive grip of aspect on event representation, this population should show smaller aspectual priming effects than both Serbian monolinguals and non-interpreting bilinguals. We recruited 22 certified conference interpreters (Serbian–Hungarian working direction), 22 Serbian–Hungarian bilinguals without interpreting experience, and 22 Serbian monolinguals. All completed a response-time task in which aspect-congruent or aspect-incongruent photographs followed Serbian sentences. Monolinguals showed the largest congruency effect (mean RT advantage 68 ms), non-interpreting bilinguals an intermediate effect (41 ms), and interpreters the smallest (19 ms, non-significant). Between-group differences survived correction for working memory span, language proficiency, and years of Serbian education. The results are the first to implicate professional bilingual practice as a moderator of aspectual framing effects in cognition.

title: Eye-Tracking Evidence for Cognitive Overload During Complex Multi-Screen Induction Tasks
abstract: Twenty-eight participants with no prior experience in a target administrative task completed a simulated induction exercise across either a single-screen or dual-screen workstation setup. Eye-tracking data were recorded throughout using a desktop-mounted Tobii TX300 system. Dependent measures included fixation duration, saccade length, dwell time on instructional versus task areas, and a secondary task reaction time used as an online cognitive load indicator. Participants in the single-screen condition showed longer average fixation durations on instructional text (391 ms vs. 312 ms) and more frequent regressions, suggesting greater processing difficulty despite—or because of—the reduced spatial separation of information sources. Dual-screen participants completed the task 18% faster on average but scored 11% lower on a subsequent unannounced retention test. The results partially support a distinction between performance efficiency and learning efficiency and have direct implications for workstation design during early-tenure onboarding.

title: Cross-cultural measurement invariance of a digital cognitive flexibility task across Serbian, Romanian, and Hungarian adolescent samples
abstract: A computer-administered task battery measuring cognitive flexibility via task-switching and set-shifting paradigms was administered to adolescent samples in Serbia (n = 487), Romania (n = 413), and Hungary (n = 398), ages 15–17. Confirmatory factor analyses with a bifactor structure distinguished a general cognitive flexibility factor and two specific factors (rule updating, interference suppression). Multi-group confirmatory factor analysis tested configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Full metric invariance held across all three groups (ΔCFI = 0.007); scalar invariance was partial, with two intercepts non-invariant in the Hungarian sample, attributable to differential familiarity with the task interface. Latent mean comparisons adjusting for partial invariance showed no significant group differences on the general factor (p = 0.17), but the Romanian group scored lower on interference suppression (d = 0.29). Response-time parameters were more variable across groups than accuracy parameters.

title: Motor tremor and target acquisition on resistive touchscreens: an empirical study with adults aged 65–80
abstract: This study examined how age-associated hand tremor affects the accuracy and completion time of target-acquisition tasks on resistive touchscreen devices. Forty-two adults aged 65–80 (mean age 71.4, SD 4.6) and 38 younger controls (mean age 24.1) performed a standardised Fitts's Law tapping protocol across four target sizes (8, 14, 20, and 28 mm diameter) and two tremor-severity groups classified by the Fahn–Tolosa–Marín scale. Older participants showed error rates 3.1 to 4.8 times higher than controls on the two smallest target sizes, with disproportionate increases at target diameters below 14 mm. Movement time in older participants did not scale with the index of difficulty in the same way predicted by the classic Fitts model, suggesting a need for age-adjusted modelling. Qualitative observation revealed compensatory two-finger stabilisation strategies in approximately 34 % of older participants. The findings support minimum target size recommendations of at least 20 mm for applications targeting this age group.

title: Adaptation and Initial Validation of the Maslach Burnout Inventory – General Survey for the Serbian Working Population
abstract: This study reports the translation, cross-cultural adaptation, and initial psychometric evaluation of the Maslach Burnout Inventory – General Survey (MBI-GS) in Serbian. A convenience sample of 312 employed adults from the Vojvodina region completed the Serbian version alongside measures of job demands and general health. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the original three-factor structure (exhaustion, cynicism, professional efficacy) with acceptable fit indices (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.061). Internal consistency coefficients ranged from 0.74 to 0.88 across subscales. Convergent validity was established through significant correlations with the Perceived Stress Scale (r = 0.51) and the General Health Questionnaire-12 (r = −0.44). Differential item functioning analyses by gender and occupational sector revealed no substantial measurement bias. The Serbian MBI-GS is recommended as a sufficiently reliable and valid screening instrument for research and occupational health practice in the region, though further norm development on stratified samples is needed.

title: Actigraphy-based sleep estimation versus polysomnography in young adults: agreement and limits in a laboratory setting
abstract: Actigraphy is widely used in sleep research as a low-cost alternative to polysomnography (PSG), yet its accuracy for staging sleep in laboratory conditions remains debated. This study compared wrist actigraphy (ActiGraph GT9X) with concurrent PSG in 29 healthy young adults across two consecutive laboratory nights. Epoch-by-epoch agreement for wake versus sleep was 84.3% (κ = 0.61). Actigraphy systematically overestimated total sleep time by a mean of 23 minutes (95% CI: 14–32 min) and showed poor sensitivity for detecting brief awakenings shorter than 5 minutes. Slow-wave sleep duration as estimated by actigraphy correlated only modestly with PSG-derived values (r = 0.47, p = .010). These findings caution against using actigraphy as a direct proxy for SWS measurement in studies where slow-wave activity is the primary variable of interest. Recommendations for hybrid designs combining both methods are discussed.

title: Does attachment style predict help-seeking attitudes for psychological distress? Evidence from a regional Serbian community survey
abstract: Using data from a regional community survey conducted in the South Bačka district of Vojvodina (n = 541, ages 18–65, 53% women), this study tested whether adult attachment style predicted attitudes toward seeking professional psychological help after controlling for gender, age, education, prior therapy experience, and psychological distress level. Attachment anxiety was positively associated with more favourable help-seeking attitudes (β = .18, p < .001), while attachment avoidance was negatively associated (β = −.27, p < .001). These effects remained significant after controlling for all covariates. Moderation analyses indicated that the negative effect of avoidance was stronger among men than women (interaction β = −.14, p = .03). The findings have practical implications for the design of outreach campaigns targeting help-seeking reluctance in the Serbian general population, particularly among avoidantly attached men in rural and peri-urban communities where stigma toward psychological services remains elevated.

title: Strategic Noise Mapping of a Mid-Sized Serbian City: Methodology and Compliance Assessment Under END 2002/49/EC
abstract: This study presents the development of a strategic noise map for Zrenjanin, Serbia, following the requirements of the EU Environmental Noise Directive. Road traffic volumes from 72-hour counts at 34 measurement points were combined with digital terrain models and building stock data to feed a CadnaA propagation model using the NMPB-Routes-96 method. Lden and Lnight indicators were calculated across a 5 m resolution grid covering 48 km² of the urban area. Results showed that approximately 22% of residents were exposed to Lden values exceeding 55 dB(A), with the highest levels concentrated along two national road corridors passing through residential zones. The study identifies a systematic underestimation of façade reflections in densely built blocks and proposes a corrected building absorption coefficient for local construction typologies. Noise action plan priorities are ranked by a cost-per-exposed-person metric. The work was conducted as part of the municipality's first END reporting cycle and provides a baseline dataset for longitudinal monitoring.

title: Measured versus Modelled Road Traffic Noise Levels in a Radial Street Network: A Validation Study
abstract: Validation of propagation models is essential before their use in regulatory mapping. This paper compares predicted noise levels from SoundPLAN 7.3, using the RLS-90 emission model, against simultaneous 30-minute Leq measurements at 58 receiver positions distributed across a radial street network in Novi Sad. Traffic composition, speed, and flow were logged concurrently. The mean absolute difference between modelled and measured Leq values was 1.9 dB(A), with a standard deviation of 2.6 dB(A). Discrepancies exceeding 4 dB(A) occurred predominantly at intersections with irregular stop-and-go patterns not captured by steady-state emission models. A correction factor derived from observed idling fractions at signalised junctions reduced the mean error to 1.1 dB(A). The study also examines the sensitivity of predictions to input uncertainty in vehicle speed, finding that a ±5 km/h speed error propagates to a ±1.4 dB(A) prediction error. Recommendations for measurement campaign design in the Serbian urban context are provided.

title: Annoyance Response to Road Traffic Noise in Mixed Residential–Commercial Zones: A Field Survey in Two Serbian Cities
abstract: A structured questionnaire survey was administered to 487 residents in mixed-use zones of Novi Sad and Niš, Serbia, to examine the relationship between objectively measured noise exposure and self-reported annoyance. Outdoor Lden was determined from validated noise maps calibrated with spot measurements at each participant's façade. Annoyance was rated on an ICBEN-standard 11-point numerical scale. The dose–response relationship was fitted using ordinal logistic regression, controlling for socio-demographic variables, noise sensitivity, and window orientation. At Lden = 65 dB(A), the percentage of highly annoyed residents (%HA) was 28.4%, which is approximately 6 percentage points lower than the EU reference curve, suggesting contextual factors specific to post-socialist urban morphology. Noise sensitivity and perceived traffic increase over the past year were significant independent predictors of annoyance beyond the acoustic dose. The survey instrument and raw anonymised dataset are archived and available upon request.

title: Insertion Loss of Thin Concrete and Recycled-Rubber Composite Noise Barriers: Laboratory and In-Situ Comparison
abstract: This study evaluates the acoustic performance of three barrier configurations: a 200 mm solid concrete panel, a 120 mm recycled-rubber crumb composite panel, and a hybrid two-layer system combining both materials. Laboratory measurements in a semi-anechoic chamber determined the sound reduction index (Rw) according to ISO 10140-2, yielding Rw values of 38, 31, and 36 dB respectively. In-situ insertion loss was subsequently measured at a 400 m segment of a bypass road in Sremska Mitrovica using the substitution method with a controlled loudspeaker source at 15 positions. The hybrid panel achieved a mean insertion loss of 11.2 dB(A) for road traffic, compared to 12.1 dB(A) for concrete, while offering a 34% mass reduction per unit area. Wind-induced vibration at frequencies below 200 Hz was higher for the rubber composite and is flagged as a potential durability concern. Results are discussed in the context of barrier selection criteria under Serbian technical regulation SRPS U.J6.202.

title: Characterisation of Wheel–Rail Noise Sources on Urban Tram Lines Using Wayside Pass-By Measurements
abstract: Urban tram networks generate distinctive noise spectra that differ substantially from road traffic, yet Serbian noise mapping practice often applies road traffic emission models to tram lines due to a lack of local source data. This paper reports wayside pass-by measurements at seven sites on the Novi Sad tram network, covering three tram car types and three track configurations including jointed rail, continuously welded rail, and a curved section with a 35 m radius. Sound exposure level (SEL) and maximum A-weighted level (LAFmax) were recorded for 312 individual pass-by events. Spectral analysis identified a dominant wheel squeal component at 1250–2000 Hz on the curved section reaching LAFmax up to 84 dB(A) at 7.5 m. Source emission spectra were compared against the harmonised CNOSSOS-EU tramway model, revealing a 3–7 dB underestimation in the 630–2000 Hz octave bands for jointed track. A locally calibrated emission dataset is proposed for future mapping cycles in cities with legacy tram infrastructure.

title: Temporal Variability of Traffic Noise Indicators and Its Implications for Long-Term Exposure Assessment
abstract: The EU Environmental Noise Directive requires calculation of annual average noise indicators, yet measurements are typically taken over short periods. This study examines the temporal variability of Lden and Lnight at four permanent monitoring stations installed in Novi Sad over a 14-month period, with 15-minute logging intervals. Traffic volume and composition data from inductive loop detectors at co-located road sections were also analysed. Day-to-day variability in Lday was found to follow a near-normal distribution with a standard deviation of 1.8–2.7 dB(A) depending on site type, while seasonal variation contributed an additional 1.1–1.6 dB(A) difference between summer and winter averages, partly attributable to changes in heavy vehicle fraction and tyre type. Monte Carlo simulation was used to estimate the uncertainty in annual Lden derived from 7-day measurement campaigns, showing a 90th percentile error of ±2.3 dB(A). Practical guidance is provided for selecting measurement periods that minimise bias in compliance assessments.

title: Green Noise Barriers in Urban Settings: Acoustic Performance and Maintenance Constraints
abstract: Vegetated or 'green' noise barriers are increasingly proposed in urban renewal projects, but their acoustic performance is inconsistently reported in the literature. This review and field study examines three installed green barrier systems in Novi Sad: a gabion wall with ivy cover, a modular planter panel system filled with mineral wool substrate, and a dense hedgerow of 2.8 m height. Insertion loss was measured according to the ISO 10847 in-situ method over two seasons. The gabion–ivy system achieved a mean insertion loss of 6.4 dB(A) in summer and 5.1 dB(A) in winter, consistent with the substrate being the primary acoustic element rather than vegetation. The mineral wool planter panel reached 9.8 dB(A) but showed visible moisture damage after 18 months. The hedgerow provided only 2.1 dB(A) insertion loss despite its density, confirming that biological barriers alone are acoustically insufficient at standard urban heights. Maintenance cost data collected from the city public services department are included and compared against concrete barrier lifecycle costs.

title: Noise Exposure Modelling for a New Residential District Alongside a Freight Railway Corridor: Pre-Construction Assessment
abstract: This conference paper describes a pre-construction noise assessment for a planned mixed residential and retail development of approximately 1 200 dwellings alongside an active freight railway corridor in the Vojvodina region. Rail traffic data including train category, speed, and daily frequency were obtained from the national infrastructure manager for a reference year. The CNOSSOS-EU rail noise emission model was applied within SoundPLAN 8.1 using a 2 m receiver height grid. Two barrier layout scenarios were tested: a single 3 m concrete barrier at 8 m from the nearest track centreline, and a staggered dual-barrier configuration. The dual-barrier reduced the area with Lnight > 50 dB(A) by 38% compared to the single barrier, though diffraction over the inner barrier remained significant for low-frequency components below 125 Hz. Sensitivity analyses for future traffic growth of 15% and 30% show that the dual configuration remains compliant with Serbian residential limits under both scenarios. Recommendations for final barrier placement and dwelling layout are provided.

title: Occupational Noise Exposure of Tram Drivers in Novi Sad: Personal Dosimetry and Hearing Threshold Shifts
abstract: While environmental noise from tram networks is well studied, occupational exposure of tram operators receives less attention. This study conducted personal dosimetry measurements on 28 tram drivers over full working shifts using calibrated Svantek SV 104 dosimeters. Results showed a mean daily noise exposure level LEX,8h of 79.4 dB(A), with five drivers exceeding the 85 dB(A) upper action value. Audiometric screening of the same cohort revealed notched hearing loss patterns at 4 kHz in 11 of 28 drivers, with a statistically significant association between years of service and threshold shift magnitude (r = 0.61, p < 0.01). Interior cabin noise was dominated by traction motor harmonics and wheel squeal transmission through the floor. Three cost-effective cab modification options are evaluated: floor damping pads, cab door sealing, and driver seat vibration isolation. Implementation of floor damping and door sealing together was estimated to reduce LEX,8h by approximately 3.2 dB based on source path contribution analysis.

title: Effect of Urban Canyon Geometry on Road Traffic Noise Distribution: Systematic Variation of H/W Ratio Using Scale Models
abstract: Urban canyon geometry is known to influence multiple sound reflections and shadow zones, yet the quantitative relationship between height-to-width ratio and noise distribution at upper floors remains insufficiently documented for Central European building stock. This study constructed seven 1:20 scale models of street canyons with H/W ratios ranging from 0.4 to 2.2, tested with a calibrated loudspeaker source simulating a uniform traffic line source. Sound pressure level distributions were mapped at 48 receiver positions per model at five equivalent floor heights. Results show that increasing H/W above 1.5 raises noise levels at the third floor and above by 2.1–3.8 dB(A) relative to open terrain, due to reinforced lateral reflections, while ground-floor levels remain largely unaffected. The effect is most pronounced for façades facing the source directly and diminishes for rear-facing façades where multiple reflections increase attenuation variability. A simple empirical correction formula for H/W-dependent façade level adjustment is proposed for use in rapid assessment tools.

title: Integrating Noise Exposure Data into Urban Health Risk Maps: A GIS-Based Approach for Vojvodina Municipalities
abstract: Noise-induced health risk quantification requires combining exposure maps with population data in a spatial framework. This study develops a GIS workflow that integrates strategic noise maps (Lden, Lnight) from five Vojvodina municipalities with census block population grids and WHO dose–response functions for ischaemic heart disease and sleep disturbance attributable to road traffic noise. Exposure–response functions from the WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines for the European Region (2018) were applied to estimate attributable cases per municipality. Across the five study municipalities, an estimated 4 200 persons are highly sleep-disturbed and 310 attributable cases of ischaemic heart disease events per year are associated with road traffic noise exposure above threshold. Spatial hotspot analysis using Getis-Ord Gi* statistics identifies three priority intervention zones where health burden density exceeds the 90th percentile. The resulting composite risk index map is designed to be interpretable by non-specialist municipal planners and is being piloted in the Sremska Mitrovica action plan revision.

title: Environmental Product Declarations for Software-as-a-Service: Feasibility and Methodology
abstract: Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) are well established for physical products but remain largely absent for software-delivered services. This preprint explores the feasibility of issuing EPDs for SaaS products under EN 15804 and ISO 14025 frameworks, discussing the particular challenges of defining functional units, establishing representative system boundaries, and handling multi-tenancy. A worked example is developed for a hypothetical project management SaaS platform with 50,000 active users, drawing on published emission factor datasets and operational telemetry assumptions from published cloud provider disclosures. The resulting EPD template quantifies global warming potential at 0.31 kgCO₂e per active user per month under a median usage scenario, with hardware manufacturing accounting for 55% of that figure. The paper identifies three unresolved methodological questions—software update cycles, dormant account treatment, and third-party API calls—and proposes provisional solutions pending formal standardisation work.

title: Dust Exposure Levels Among Workers in Small-Scale Sunflower Seed Processing Plants in Northern Serbia
abstract: Small-scale sunflower seed processing facilities operate under informal conditions in the Vojvodina region and are largely absent from published occupational hygiene literature. This cross-sectional field study measured inhalable and respirable dust fractions at 14 facilities over two crop seasons (2015–2016), covering 62 worker-shifts. Personal sampling was conducted using IOM samplers and cyclone-type respirable dust heads, with gravimetric analysis at an accredited laboratory. Geometric mean inhalable dust concentrations across all tasks were 6.8 mg/m³, with dehulling operators recording the highest values (up to 18.4 mg/m³), consistently above the 10 mg/m³ OEL set by Serbian regulation. Respirable fractions at those workstations reached 3.1 mg/m³ on average. Natural ventilation through open wall panels was the sole air management strategy at 11 of the 14 facilities. The study documents a previously unquantified exposure burden and provides baseline data for regulatory enforcement and engineering control prioritisation.

title: Life cycle assessment of recombinant protein production in Escherichia coli: effect of fermentation medium composition on environmental burdens
abstract: The environmental performance of recombinant protein production in E. coli is influenced substantially by fermentation medium formulation choices, particularly the selection between defined mineral media and complex yeast-extract-based media. This study compared four medium compositions for production of a model industrial protease at laboratory scale (2 L bioreactor). All experiments were conducted under identical induction and temperature shift protocols. Primary inventory data included substrate quantities, electricity, sterilisation steam, and downstream processing reagents measured per batch. The functional unit was 1 g of purified protease at ≥95% SDS-PAGE purity. Global warming potential ranged from 18.4 to 41.7 kg CO2-eq/g across the four media, with yeast extract synthesis and transport dominating the high end. Defined media with glucose and ammonium sulfate showed the lowest burden but required longer cultivation time, increasing electricity consumption by 34%. The study highlights that medium selection is an environmental design variable and proposes a medium-optimisation criterion that balances titre, cost, and global warming potential simultaneously.

title: ISO 14064-3 Third-Party Verification of a Distribution Utility's GHG Statement: Lessons from a Pilot Audit
abstract: Third-party verification of corporate GHG statements under ISO 14064-3 is uncommon among Southeast European utilities. This paper documents a pilot verification exercise conducted for a mid-size Serbian distribution utility covering reporting year 2015. The verification team reviewed inventory documentation, sampled metered energy loss data, checked SF6 top-up records, and assessed the treatment of Scope 3 categories including business travel and contractor vehicle fuel. Material misstatements were found in two areas: the utility had used an outdated national emission factor (0.721 kg CO2/kWh instead of the current 0.689 kg CO2/kWh), causing a 4.7% overstatement of Scope 2 emissions, and had omitted employee commuting from Scope 3. The paper discusses verification sampling strategies appropriate to utility data structures, defines reasonable assurance thresholds for loss metering uncertainty, and proposes a standardised data collection template to reduce verifier effort in future cycles.

title: Comparing carbon footprint calculation methods for package tour operators: GHG Protocol versus ISO 14064-1
abstract: Package tour operators in Central and Eastern Europe are increasingly required by international buyers to report their carbon footprints, yet no single calculation standard dominates the market. This paper applies both the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard and ISO 14064-1 to emissions data from three Serbian package tour operators with annual client volumes between 4,200 and 18,000 passengers. Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions were estimated using a combination of supplier invoices, fuel purchase records, and spend-based proxy factors. Results showed that the two frameworks produced GWP estimates differing by 12–34% for the same operator, driven chiefly by boundary rules for downstream transport and accommodation. The ISO 14064-1 approach yielded higher totals in all three cases owing to its broader value-chain inclusion criteria. Sensitivity analysis using Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) identified emission factors for coach transport as the dominant source of variance. The study recommends harmonisation of Scope 3 category treatment before mandatory reporting is introduced in the Western Balkans accession process.

title: Towards a regional carbon accounting registry for tourism destinations in the Western Balkans: institutional requirements and data infrastructure
abstract: Several national tourism strategies in the Western Balkans reference carbon neutrality targets for the sector, but none has established a functioning emissions registry capable of tracking progress. This preprint outlines the institutional and data infrastructure requirements for a regional tourism carbon accounting registry covering Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and North Macedonia. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 22 national tourism organisation representatives, environmental ministry officials, and private sector operators, the paper identifies five prerequisite conditions: a shared functional unit convention, a harmonised emission factor library, a minimum mandatory reporting scope for registered accommodation providers, a governance mechanism for disputed allocations, and a publicly accessible data portal. Comparison with the EU Tourism Dashboard initiative suggests that Western Balkans countries could adopt a compatible architecture at substantially lower cost by leveraging existing national statistical office infrastructure. A phased implementation roadmap spanning 2026–2031 is proposed, with pilot testing recommended in Serbia and Montenegro during the first phase.

title: Desiccation-induced changes in chlorophyll fluorescence and membrane integrity in three Tortula species from the Pannonian lowlands
abstract: We compared desiccation responses in Tortula ruralis, T. muralis, and T. caninervis collected from loess walls and steppe soils near Fruška Gora. Plants were dried at 25 °C and 30 % relative humidity for 24, 48, and 96 hours, then rehydrated for 2 hours. Fv/Fm was measured at each time point using a PAM-2100 fluorometer. All three species showed rapid decline in Fv/Fm after 24 h desiccation (mean drop from 0.76 to 0.31), but T. ruralis recovered to 0.72 within 90 minutes of rehydration, while T. muralis recovered only to 0.53 after 2 hours. Electrolyte leakage assays confirmed greater membrane damage in T. muralis. Antioxidant enzyme activity (SOD, CAT, APX) was elevated 2–4-fold in T. ruralis during the first 6 hours of rehydration, suggesting reactive oxygen species scavenging as a primary protective mechanism. Results indicate species-specific variation in desiccation tolerance capacity within a single genus under continental steppe conditions.
