title: Carotenoid and anthocyanin profiles of biological soil crusts along a moisture gradient in the Deliblato Sands
abstract: Biological soil crust (BSC) communities were sampled at 12 sites in the Deliblato Sands (southern Vojvodina) along a gradient from seasonally wet interdune depressions to exposed dune crests. Crust biomass, chlorophyll a/b ratios, and carotenoid composition (including β-carotene, lutein, zeaxanthin, and violaxanthin) were quantified by HPLC. Anthocyanin content was determined spectrophotometrically. Zeaxanthin to total xanthophyll ratio increased from 0.12 at wet sites to 0.41 at the driest crest sites, consistent with sustained photoprotective de-epoxidation. Total anthocyanin content correlated negatively with soil moisture (r = −0.74, p < 0.001, n = 36 samples). Crust thickness and biomass declined significantly above 30 m elevation within the dune system. The data suggest that xanthophyll cycle activity and anthocyanin accumulation are key photoprotective strategies in BSC-forming organisms under combined water and radiation stress in this continental sand habitat.

title: Recovery kinetics of net photosynthesis in desiccated Syntrichia ruralis under simulated Pannonian summer conditions
abstract: Syntrichia ruralis gametophytes collected from three steppe sites in Vojvodina were subjected to a 14-day desiccation protocol in a programmable climate chamber set to replicate July temperature and humidity cycles recorded at Pančevo meteorological station (daily maxima 35–39 °C, relative humidity minima 18–24 %). Net photosynthesis was measured with an infrared gas analyser (LI-COR 6400) immediately after rehydration and at 15-minute intervals for 3 hours. Full recovery (≥90 % of pre-desiccation rates) was achieved within 60–75 minutes across all three populations. No significant difference was found between populations (one-way ANOVA, F = 1.3, p = 0.28). Respiration recovered faster than photosynthesis, resulting in negative net carbon balance during the first 20 minutes post-rehydration. Photoinhibition was absent when desiccation was performed in darkness, whereas light-desiccated plants showed 18 % lower maximum photosynthetic rates on day 1 of recovery. Findings highlight the interaction between light and water stress in field-relevant conditions.

title: Ultrastructural responses of moss chloroplasts to repeated desiccation–rehydration cycles
abstract: Transmission electron microscopy was used to examine chloroplast and cell wall ultrastructure in Abietinella abietina and Rhytidium rugosum after one, three, and five desiccation–rehydration cycles (DRC). Plants were dried to equilibrium at 15 % RH and rehydrated by immersion for 1 hour. Thylakoid stacking was quantified from micrograph measurements on at least 40 chloroplasts per treatment. After one DRC, thylakoid grana retained normal stacking (mean granal lamellae per stack: 6.2 ± 1.1). After five DRCs, A. abietina showed significant unstacking in 38 % of observed chloroplasts and a 22 % increase in plastoglobule number per chloroplast section. R. rugosum showed less pronounced changes (12 % chloroplasts affected after five DRCs). Cell walls remained intact in both species throughout all treatments. Results suggest cumulative oxidative stress on thylakoid membranes with repeated cycling, and differential resilience between the two steppe-adapted species.

title: Desiccation tolerance of biological soil crust communities on loess banks in the Pannonian region: a comparative field and laboratory study
abstract: BSC communities from loess banks at eight sites across Vojvodina and northern Serbia were characterised for species composition (dominated by Syntrichia ruralis, Ceratodon purpureus, Nostoc commune, and Microcoleus vaginatus) and subjected to standardised desiccation assays in the laboratory. In the field, chlorophyll fluorescence loggers recorded Fv/Fm continuously at two sites over one growing season. Field Fv/Fm fell below 0.2 during 14 % of daylight hours in July, always recovering above 0.6 after morning dew events. Lab assays showed that crust photosynthetic recovery was strongly correlated with rewetting speed: rapid immersion produced full recovery in 85 % of samples, whereas slow vapour-phase rewetting produced full recovery in only 54 %. Species richness was higher on north-facing than south-facing loess sections (mean 11.3 vs. 7.6 species per 0.25 m² quadrat, t-test p = 0.009). These results provide baseline ecophysiological data for loess conservation management.

title: Effects of simulated nitrogen deposition on desiccation tolerance and pigment content in Syntrichia ruralis
abstract: Nitrogen deposition is increasing in Central European steppe systems. To test its effect on moss stress physiology, Syntrichia ruralis turfs were irrigated weekly with NH4NO3 solutions at 0, 10, 25, and 50 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ equivalent concentrations for 12 weeks in outdoor mesocosms. Desiccation tolerance (Fv/Fm recovery after 72 h at 20 % RH) declined significantly at the 50 kg N treatment (recovery to 0.58 vs. 0.74 in controls, p = 0.003, n = 8 per treatment). Chlorophyll a/b ratio increased at high N, suggesting impaired xanthophyll cycle activity. SOD activity was significantly lower in high-N plants during rehydration. Total nitrogen content of moss tissue confirmed uptake. No significant growth response was detected over the experiment duration. These results suggest that even moderate increases in atmospheric N deposition may reduce the stress resilience of steppe moss species without producing visible morphological changes.

title: Bryophyte and biological soil crust diversity as indicators of loess habitat integrity: methods and preliminary assessment
abstract: This book chapter reviews methodological approaches for using BSC and bryophyte communities as integrity indicators for loess bank and steppe habitats in the Pannonian region. We discuss species composition surveys, remote sensing of crust cover, and ecophysiological benchmarks (including Fv/Fm thresholds and chlorophyll content indices) as complementary assessment tools. A case study from 22 loess wall sites in Vojvodina illustrates how a combined score based on species richness, crust continuity, and mean summer Fv/Fm correlates with independently assessed habitat quality scores (Spearman r = 0.71, p < 0.001). We argue that rapid ecophysiological screening with portable fluorometers can substitute partial laboratory assays for routine monitoring. Practical recommendations for conservation managers are provided, including protocols adaptable to non-specialist field teams. Limitations of current methods related to seasonal variation and observer calibration are discussed.

title: Seasonal dynamics of antioxidant capacity in biological soil crusts on south-facing steppe slopes in Vojvodina
abstract: Biological soil crusts were sampled monthly from March to October at a permanent plot on a south-facing steppe slope at Stara Pazova over two consecutive years (2019–2020). Total antioxidant capacity (DPPH and FRAP assays), ascorbate peroxidase activity, and malondialdehyde content were measured in crust material separated into phototrophic crust (upper 1 mm) and bulk crust (1–5 mm) fractions. DPPH-radical scavenging capacity in the phototrophic fraction peaked in July (mean 142 µmol TE g⁻¹ DW) and was lowest in March (61 µmol TE g⁻¹ DW). MDA content followed the same pattern, peaking in July–August. APX activity was highest in April–May, coinciding with the period of rapid rehydration–desiccation cycling after spring rainfall. Interannual variability was pronounced: the drier year 2020 produced 28 % higher peak DPPH values. Depth fractionation revealed consistently lower antioxidant capacity in the bulk crust layer.

title: Transcriptomic response to desiccation in Syntrichia ruralis from a continental steppe population: comparison with an Atlantic reference dataset
abstract: RNA was extracted from Syntrichia ruralis plants collected at a Vojvodina loess steppe site and subjected to controlled desiccation (48 h at 25 % RH, 25 °C) and 2 h rehydration. Transcriptome libraries were prepared using TruSeq and sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq 550 (paired-end, 2 × 75 bp). De novo assembly produced 38,412 unigenes. Differential expression analysis (DESeq2) identified 2,104 significantly upregulated and 1,387 downregulated unigenes during desiccation (FDR < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1.5). Comparison with a published Atlantic-climate S. ruralis transcriptome dataset showed 71 % overlap in desiccation-upregulated gene clusters, but the continental population showed stronger upregulation of late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) protein transcripts and lower induction of aquaporin-related transcripts. GO enrichment analysis highlighted protein folding, ROS detoxification, and membrane stabilisation as primary biological processes. These differences may reflect population-level adaptation to more severe desiccation regimes.

title: Drought frequency modulates recovery capacity of cyanobacterial crusts: evidence from a multi-year rewetting experiment
abstract: We conducted a three-year outdoor mesocosm experiment at the University of Novi Sad experimental garden, exposing intact BSC cores (n = 60, 15 cm diameter) from the Deliblato Sands to three rewetting frequency treatments: ambient rainfall, reduced frequency (50 % of ambient events), and increased frequency (150 % via supplemental irrigation). After each growing season, crust photosynthetic recovery rates (Fv/Fm after 2 h rehydration), biomass, and community composition were assessed. By year 3, reduced-frequency treatment crusts showed significantly slower initial Fv/Fm recovery (0.42 at 30 min vs. 0.61 in controls, p = 0.01) and 23 % lower total crust biomass. Moss component richness declined in reduced-frequency treatments (from mean 4.2 to 2.7 species per core), while cyanobacterial dominance increased. Increased-frequency treatment produced modest biomass gains but no significant change in recovery rates. Results suggest that projected drying trends in the Pannonian region may gradually shift BSC communities toward cyanobacterial dominance.

title: Mapping biological soil crust cover on Vojvodina loess banks using UAV multispectral imagery and field spectroradiometry
abstract: We evaluated whether UAV-mounted multispectral sensors can reliably detect and map BSC cover on loess bank habitats at eight sites in Vojvodina. A DJI Matrice 300 drone carrying a MicaSense RedEdge-MX sensor was flown at 30 m altitude. Ground truth was provided by field spectroradiometry (ASD FieldSpec 4) and 128 quadrat-based BSC cover estimates. A random forest classifier trained on five spectral bands plus NDVI and NDWI indices achieved an overall accuracy of 79 % and a kappa coefficient of 0.71 for distinguishing crust-covered, bare, and vascular-plant-covered surfaces. Confusion was highest between sparse BSC and bare loess (17 % misclassification rate). Crust cover mapped at one intensively managed agricultural border site was 4 % compared with 38 % at a protected steppe reference site. The method provides a scalable tool for monitoring crust recovery after disturbance and is discussed in the context of habitat restoration assessment.

title: Grandmothers as Educational Brokers: Observations from Roma Settlements in Southern Vojvodina
abstract: This study examines the role of grandmothers in mediating children's preparation for formal schooling in three rural Roma settlements in southern Vojvodina, Serbia. Drawing on six months of ethnographic fieldwork conducted between September 2022 and February 2023, the research involved 34 semi-structured interviews with grandmothers, mothers, and primary school teachers, supplemented by 48 hours of participant observation in household and community settings. Analysis using thematic coding revealed that grandmothers functioned as primary organisers of pre-literacy routines, story-telling practices, and the transmission of behavioural norms aligned with school expectations, often compensating for parents' limited formal education. In 21 out of 34 households interviewed, grandmothers reported being the sole adult consistently engaging children in school-preparatory activities. The findings suggest that school-outreach programmes targeting only nuclear-family parents systematically miss a central node in actual learning support networks. The paper argues for a broader, kinship-inclusive definition of parental involvement when designing family engagement policies for rural Roma communities.

title: Between Home and Classroom: How Roma Parents in Rural Serbia Interpret School Demands
abstract: This paper investigates how Roma parents in four villages in the Srem and Bačka districts of Vojvodina construct and communicate meaning around their children's schooling obligations. Data were gathered through 29 narrative interviews conducted in 2023, with parents and extended family members who had at least one child enrolled in grades one through four of primary school. Interviews were conducted in Serbian and Romani, with a community interpreter present in twelve sessions. Analysis focused on the language parents used to describe homework, teacher contact, and attendance, revealing a consistent pattern in which school obligations were reframed as collective family responsibilities rather than individual parental duties. Participants frequently cited older siblings, aunts, and uncles rather than themselves when asked who helps children with schoolwork. The study also documents recurring tensions between school scheduling and seasonal agricultural labour, which shaped attendance patterns for 17 of the 29 families. Findings contribute to debates about the structural conditions of low parental involvement scores reported in Roma community assessments.

title: Mapping Informal Learning Networks in Marginalised Rural Communities: A Methodological Note on Sociogram Use in Ethnopedagogical Research
abstract: This methodological paper reports on the use of sociograms as a supplementary mapping tool during ethnographic fieldwork in rural Roma communities in Vojvodina. The procedure was piloted across two field sites during autumn 2023, involving 18 adult participants who were asked to identify all household and extended-family members they considered relevant to a child's learning at home. Participants drew or verbally described relational maps which were then rendered as network diagrams by the researchers. The exercise surfaced 11 distinct recurring structural configurations, including hub-and-spoke patterns centred on a single elder, and more distributed chain structures spanning households in different hamlets. The paper evaluates the practical challenges encountered, including participant unfamiliarity with abstract mapping tasks and the ethical complexities of recording named interpersonal relationships in small, identifiable communities. It concludes that adapted sociogram techniques, when introduced gradually and explained in concrete relational terms, can usefully complement interview and observation data in ethnopedagogical work with non-literate or semi-literate adult participants.

title: Parental Involvement Through Kin: A Comparative Look at Roma and Non-Roma Rural Households in Serbia and Romania
abstract: This conference paper presents preliminary comparative findings from parallel fieldwork conducted in rural communities in southern Vojvodina, Serbia, and western Oltenia, Romania, focusing on the extent to which parental involvement in schooling is delegated to extended kin in Roma and non-Roma low-income households. Data collection took place between January and June 2025 and included 41 semi-structured household interviews across four field sites, two per country. Participants were sampled using purposive snowball referral based on school-age children's enrolment records obtained in cooperation with local primary schools. Preliminary coding indicates that delegation of schooling support to extended kin is substantially more frequent in Roma households (present in 28 of 33 Roma households) than in matched non-Roma rural households (9 of 20), though the character of that delegation differs across sites. Romanian field sites showed a higher incidence of older siblings as primary helpers, while Serbian sites showed a stronger grandmother-centred pattern. The paper discusses limitations of cross-national comparison given differences in school systems, data access, and fieldwork conditions.

title: What Schools Miss When They Call Home: Teacher Perceptions of Roma Family Structures in Rural Vojvodina
abstract: This study examines how primary school teachers in rural Vojvodina conceptualise Roma family structures when attempting to engage parents in school activities, and how those conceptualisations affect contact strategies. Between February and May 2026, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 22 classroom teachers across seven village primary schools in three municipalities with significant Roma populations. Teachers were asked to describe their typical methods for reaching parents, their assessments of parental responsiveness, and their understanding of who constitutes a child's relevant adult caregivers. Analysis identified a persistent assumption among 18 of the 22 teachers that the mother is the appropriate and sole contact point for school communication, regardless of actual household composition. Teachers who had received any form of intercultural education training during initial teacher preparation showed more varied contact strategies, though the sample is too small to generalise this finding. The paper discusses implications for in-service teacher training and for the design of school-family liaison roles in rural multiethnic contexts.

title: Longitudinal Stability of Narrative Tone in Adolescent Diaries: A Two-Year Follow-Up
abstract: Narrative tone — the overarching affective orientation of a personal narrative — has been identified in adult studies as a relatively stable individual characteristic. This paper reports two-year follow-up data from 53 adolescents who had participated in an earlier diary study beginning at ages 11–12. Participants completed monthly diary entries over 24 months spanning their first two years of secondary school. Narrative tone was rated on a redemption–contamination dimension using an established scheme. Results showed moderate rank-order stability (r = 0.52) across the two years, with a statistically significant overall shift towards more redemptive framing in the second year. Stability was higher among participants who reported having at least one stable close friendship throughout the period. The paper discusses how these patterns compare with adult longitudinal findings and considers developmental explanations for lower stability in adolescent samples.

title: Cross-National Patterns in Transition Narratives: A Comparative Study in Serbia and Hungary
abstract: This comparative study examined narrative accounts of the primary-to-secondary school transition produced by 112 adolescents in Serbia and 98 in Hungary, all aged 12–13 and sampled within two months of starting secondary school. Participants completed a semi-structured written narrative task and a brief questionnaire on transition experiences. Narrative texts were analysed using cross-national coding protocols developed collaboratively by the research teams to ensure conceptual equivalence. Serbian participants more frequently used relational references (mentions of peers, teachers) when describing identity-relevant change, while Hungarian participants more frequently cited institutional or structural features of the new school. Both groups showed similar rates of temporal orientation towards the future. The study discusses how schooling culture and family socialisation patterns may shape the content rather than the structure of transition narratives. Limitations related to sampling and translation equivalence are acknowledged.

title: Longitudinal Stability of Moral Reasoning Levels in Preschool Children: A One-Year Follow-Up
abstract: A cohort of 61 children first assessed at age four was re-assessed approximately twelve months later using the same battery of three dilemma story tasks. The battery had shown acceptable test-retest reliability in prior work (r = 0.67). The aim was to determine whether individual differences in moral reasoning level at age four predicted level at age five, and to examine whether children attending preschool groups using more structured peer discussion activities showed greater gains. Teachers at participating institutions completed a brief activity log over the year. Results showed moderate rank-order stability (r = 0.52) and a mean upward shift of 0.38 scale points. Children in classrooms where structured discussion was reported at least twice per week showed gains 0.19 points larger than peers in low-discussion classrooms, a difference that was statistically significant after controlling for age and sex. Attrition over the follow-up period was 14%, which is discussed as a limitation.

title: How Preschool Practitioners Use Storytelling for Moral Guidance: A Survey of Attitudes and Reported Practices in Vojvodina
abstract: This study surveyed 184 preschool practitioners employed in state-funded preschool institutions across Vojvodina on their attitudes toward storytelling as a moral education tool and their reported frequency and methods of use. A purpose-built questionnaire with 28 items was validated on a pilot sample of 32 practitioners and showed acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.77). Findings indicated that 91% of respondents reported using stories for moral purposes at least weekly, but only 23% reported routinely posing open-ended questions to prompt children's reasoning, with most instead providing direct moral commentary after the story. Attitudes toward child-led discussion were generally positive but respondents cited time pressure and large group sizes as primary barriers. Practitioners who had received structured training in dialogic reading or Socratic questioning methods reported significantly more discussion-oriented practices. The survey provides baseline data for designing continuing professional development programmes.

title: T2 relaxation time distributions in Banatite limestone samples: comparison of CPMG acquisition parameters
abstract: Carr–Purcell–Meiboom–Gill (CPMG) measurements were performed on twelve limestone core plugs from the Banat region at 2 MHz proton frequency. Echo spacing was varied between 0.1 ms and 1.0 ms to evaluate the sensitivity of T2 distributions to acquisition settings. Laplace inversion using a regularised least-squares algorithm produced T2 spectra with geometric mean values ranging from 8 ms to 340 ms across the sample set. Shorter echo spacings resolved fast-relaxing components associated with clay-bound water, contributing a mean 12% signal fraction not detected at longer spacings. Mercury injection capillary pressure measurements on the same plugs confirmed pore-throat radii consistent with the NMR-derived pore-size proxy. The study provides practical guidance for selecting CPMG parameters when characterising heterogeneous carbonates and establishes a local calibration dataset linking T2 geometric mean to median pore radius through a surface relaxivity of 6.1 µm/s.

title: Low-field NMR characterisation of sandstone porosity in the Pannonian Basin: comparison with helium porosimetry
abstract: Twelve Pannonian Basin sandstone plug samples of varying grain size and cement content were characterised by low-field NMR at 2 MHz and by helium porosimetry. Total NMR porosity, calculated from the initial amplitude of CPMG decays, agreed with helium porosity to within ±1.5 porosity units for nine of the twelve samples; three clay-rich samples showed a systematic NMR underestimate of about 3 porosity units, attributed to fast-relaxing clay-bound proton populations with T2 below the first echo. T2 distributions showed bimodal character in medium-grained quartz-cemented specimens, with peaks near 20 ms and 180 ms interpreted as micro- and macroporosity respectively. Permeability estimates using the Timur–Coates model correlated with air permeability measurements (R² = 0.81, n = 12) after sample-specific calibration of the free-fluid cut-off. The results support routine use of bench-top NMR in core analysis workflows for regional aquifer characterisation.

title: Surface relaxivity estimation in heterogeneous carbonates using combined NMR and scanning electron microscopy
abstract: Accurate NMR-to-pore-size conversion requires knowledge of the surface relaxivity ρ₂, which is difficult to determine independently in mineralogically complex carbonates. Ten plug samples from a Cretaceous limestone outcrop in western Serbia were characterised by CPMG NMR, nitrogen adsorption BET analysis, and backscattered electron scanning electron microscopy. A calibration procedure was developed in which BET-derived specific surface area and NMR logarithmic mean T2 jointly constrain ρ₂, yielding values between 3.8 and 9.2 µm/s depending on calcite versus dolomite content. SEM image analysis confirmed that dolomitised zones had smaller average crystal sizes and correspondingly faster surface relaxation. The calibrated ρ₂ values improved agreement between NMR pore-size distributions and image-derived chord-length distributions. The approach requires no mercury injection and is applicable to water-sensitive or fragile samples, which is relevant for shallow aquifer core material.

title: Two-dimensional T1–T2 correlation NMR for fluid typing in water-saturated and partially oil-saturated sandstone
abstract: Two-dimensional inversion of T1–T2 magnetisation data was applied to sandstone plugs saturated with brine, crude oil, and mixed-fluid states at controlled water saturations of 100%, 70%, 50%, and 30%. Measurements were carried out at 2 MHz on six samples drawn from the same formation. In fully brine-saturated samples, T1/T2 ratios clustered near 1.5–2.0, consistent with fast surface relaxation in water-wet pores. Oil-bearing samples showed a second population with T1/T2 ratios of 4–7 and T2 values in the 100–600 ms range. Partial saturation experiments revealed continuous redistribution of the two populations as water saturation decreased, with brine increasingly confined to smaller pores. The 2D maps allowed unambiguous fluid identification that was not possible from T2 distributions alone. Echo spacing sensitivity and regularisation parameter selection are discussed in detail.

title: Effect of drying temperature on NMR-measured porosity in clay-bearing sandstones
abstract: Sample preparation protocol, particularly drying conditions, can substantially alter measured porosity and T2 distributions in clay-bearing sedimentary rocks. Eighteen sandstone plugs with clay content ranging from 2% to 18% (determined by X-ray diffraction) were dried at 40 °C, 80 °C, and 105 °C under vacuum and re-saturated with deionised water before NMR measurement. Drying at 105 °C caused irreversible collapse of smectite interlayers in four samples, reducing re-saturation porosity by 1.8–4.2 porosity units compared to 40 °C drying. T2 distributions for 105 °C-dried samples lost the short-T2 clay-bound component, while the macroporosity peak was unaffected. No significant differences were observed among low-clay samples. The findings recommend drying at 40 °C or below for NMR porosity measurements intended for comparison with downhole logging, where formation temperature rarely exceeds 60 °C in shallow Pannonian Basin wells.

title: NMR relaxometry
abstract: This chapter provides a self-contained introduction to NMR relaxometry as applied to fluid-filled porous media. Starting from the Bloch equations, the text derives the relationship between transverse relaxation and pore geometry through the fast-diffusion and intermediate-diffusion regimes, with explicit treatment of surface-to-volume ratio, surface relaxivity, and bulk fluid relaxation. Pulse sequences for T1 (inversion recovery, saturation recovery) and T2 (CPMG) measurements are described, with practical guidance on echo spacing, number of echoes, and signal averaging. The chapter covers Laplace inversion methods including Tikhonov regularisation and the Butler–Reeds–Dawson algorithm, discussing regularisation parameter selection and resolution limits. Worked examples use data from limestone and sandstone samples. The chapter closes with a discussion of multi-dimensional relaxation experiments and their use for fluid typing. Suitable for graduate students in physics, geophysics, and reservoir engineering.

title: Pore connectivity assessment in tight carbonates using diffusion–relaxation D–T2 NMR maps
abstract: Diffusion–T2 correlation experiments were performed on six tight carbonate samples with helium porosities between 3.2% and 9.7% and air permeabilities below 0.1 mD. The stimulated echo sequence with variable diffusion encoding time allowed separation of restricted from unrestricted diffusion regimes. At short diffusion times (Δ = 5 ms), effective diffusion coefficients lay within 15% of the bulk water value, indicating that pore-surface effects dominated over geometrical restriction at the probed length scale. At longer diffusion times (Δ = 100 ms), restricted diffusion coefficients decreased by 30–60%, with the largest reductions in samples where SEM imaging showed isolated vugs. D–T2 maps showed two populations: a fast-diffusing, long-T2 group attributed to vuggy macroporosity, and a slow-diffusing, short-T2 group attributed to microporosity within the micritic matrix. The ratio of population amplitudes correlated inversely with measured permeability, suggesting that isolated macroporosity increases porosity but not connectivity.

title: Repeatability of low-field NMR porosity and T2 distributions across four European laboratories: an interlaboratory study
abstract: Six sandstone and three carbonate core plugs, prepared from a common set of half-cores and shipped to four university laboratories in Serbia, Slovenia, Hungary, and Italy, were measured independently by CPMG NMR at 2 MHz proton frequency. Each laboratory used its own instrument, calibration, and inversion software but followed a shared measurement protocol specifying saturation fluid, echo spacing (0.2 ms), number of echoes (8000), and number of averages. Total NMR porosity showed interlaboratory reproducibility of ±1.1 porosity units (one standard deviation, n = 9 samples × 4 labs). Geometric mean T2 reproducibility was ±9% relative. Larger discrepancies in T2 distribution shape were traced to differences in regularisation parameter selection rather than hardware. A simple consensus procedure based on L-curve analysis reduced T2 shape disagreement by approximately half. The results support pooling of NMR datasets across regional research consortia if porosity is the primary target.

title: Cryoporometry by NMR versus relaxometry for pore-size characterisation in chalk: do the two methods probe the same pore population?
abstract: NMR cryoporometry and T2 relaxometry were applied to the same set of eight chalk samples with BET-measured specific surface areas between 2.1 and 6.8 m²/g and helium porosities of 28–42%. Cryoporometry, using water as the probe liquid and the Gibbs–Thomson relation with calibration constant k = 48.5 nm·K, yielded unimodal pore-radius distributions centred at 50–110 nm. Relaxometry-derived pore-size distributions using ρ₂ = 4.5 µm/s showed broader distributions with an additional population below 30 nm not visible in cryoporometry. Comparison with nitrogen desorption pore-size distributions (BJH method) confirmed that the sub-30 nm population was real and attributed to inter-crystalline microporosity in coccolith fragments. Cryoporometry selectively resolves the dominant meso- and macropore system, while relaxometry captures the full pore network including sub-30 nm pores when a short enough echo spacing is used (0.1 ms). The two methods are complementary rather than interchangeable.

title: Estimating irreducible water saturation in sandstone core plugs from T2 cut-off calibration: sensitivity to mineralogy and pore geometry
abstract: The T2 cut-off value separating free-fluid from capillary-bound and clay-bound water is conventionally set at 33 ms for sandstones, but its validity varies with mineralogy and pore structure. Twenty-two sandstone plugs from four formations in the Pannonian Basin were centrifuged at a capillary pressure equivalent to 50 psi air–water drainage and measured by NMR before and after centrifugation. Sample-specific T2 cut-off values, determined as the T2 value minimising error between NMR-predicted and gravimetric irreducible water saturation, ranged from 14 ms to 68 ms. XRD clay content above 10% correlated with lower optimal cut-off values; samples with coarse, well-sorted grains had higher cut-offs. Applying the 33 ms universal cut-off produced irreducible water saturation errors of up to 12 saturation units. A simple regression model using clay content and median grain size from image analysis as predictors reduced mean absolute error from 6.1 to 2.8 saturation units. Implications for local water-bearing formation evaluation are discussed.

title: Prostorna raspodela aktivnosti Ra-226 u dunavskom aluvijalnom nanosnom tlu između Bezdana i Apatina
abstract: U cilju procene geohemijskog fona radijuma u aluvijalnom delu Dunava između Bezdana i Apatina, uzorkovani su sedimenti sa 47 tačaka u mreži 2 × 2 km. Uzorci su uzimani na tri dubine: 0–10, 20–30 i 50–60 cm. Aktivnost Ra-226 merena je direktnom gama-spektrometrijom i metodom ekstrakcije radonom u zatvorenom sistemu, uz međulaboratorijsku verifikaciju sa Institutom za nuklearne nauke u Vinči. Prosečna aktivnost Ra-226 iznosila je 24,8 ± 3,2 Bq/kg na površini, bez statistički značajnog vertikalnog gradijenta (F-test, p = 0,12). Vrednosti su niže od panevropskog medijana, što se dovodi u vezu sa razređivanjem karbonatnim rečnim nanosima alpskog porekla. Geoestatistička analiza variograma ukazuje na korelacionu dužinu od oko 4,5 km, konzistentnu sa heterogenošću rečnih meandara. Karta interpolovanih vrednosti prikazana je u GIS okruženju i biće integrisana u regionalni atlas radioaktivnosti tla.

title: Jamming phase diagram of a bidisperse granular mixture under combined shear and vertical vibration
abstract: We mapped the jamming phase diagram of a bidisperse glass-bead mixture (diameter ratio 1.4, small-sphere volume fraction x_s = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6) in a cylindrical Couette cell (inner radius 40 mm, gap 30 mm) with simultaneous vertical vibration. Solid fraction was varied from φ = 0.55 to φ = 0.64. The jamming boundary was identified as a sharp increase in torque variance exceeding a threshold of five times the baseline. The phase diagram shows that vibration at Γ = 1.5 extends the flowing regime to φ values 0.025 higher than in the unvibrated case. The x_s = 0.4 mixture has the highest jamming φ at fixed Γ, consistent with random-close-packing arguments for binary mixtures. We provide parametric equations for the jamming boundary as a function of (φ, Γ, x_s) valid within the tested range.

title: Inter-comparison of two lightning location networks over the Carpathian–Pannonian region: a three-month campaign
abstract: A coordinated three-month inter-comparison campaign (June–August 2021) is presented between the locally operated Vojvodina VLF network and a recently installed broadband magnetic field antenna array operated by a partner institution in Timișoara, Romania. Stroke-level data from both networks are matched using a 1 ms coincidence window; 8 413 matched stroke pairs form the analysis dataset. Median location discrepancy is 4.7 km with a 90th-percentile value of 11.3 km. Systematic eastward bias in the Serbian network is traced to inaccurate site correction factors and is reduced from 3.1 km to 0.8 km after recalibration. Peak current estimates from the two networks agree within 12 % for negative strokes but diverge by up to 28 % for positive strokes, suggesting waveform model differences. Detection efficiency above 10 kA estimated from cross-detection rates is 81 % for the Serbian network and 78 % for the Romanian one. The study supports ongoing efforts to build a regional joint lightning data product.

title: Corrosion behaviour of plasma-nitrided AISI H13 in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution: role of compound layer phase composition
abstract: AISI H13 specimens plasma-nitrided under three sets of conditions chosen to produce γ'-dominant, mixed γ'/ε, and ε-dominant compound layers were exposed to 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Electrochemical characterisation included open-circuit potential monitoring (72 h), potentiodynamic polarisation (−0.5 to +0.5 V vs. Ag/AgCl, 1 mV s−1), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy at OCP (10 mHz–100 kHz). The γ'-dominant layer showed the most noble OCP (−0.31 V) and the lowest passive current density (8 μA cm−2). The ε-dominant layer corroded at a rate approximately three times higher in the passive region despite displaying higher surface hardness. Equivalent circuit modelling of the EIS data using a two-time-constant model indicated that the γ'-layer had a pore resistance of 38 kΩ cm² compared with 9 kΩ cm² for the ε-dominant layer, consistent with the denser structure observed in TEM cross-sections. Untreated AISI H13 had a pore resistance of only 1.2 kΩ cm², confirming that all nitrided conditions substantially improved corrosion resistance.
venue: Corrosion Science

title: Occupational dose distribution among cardiology staff during diagnostic coronary angiography in a regional hospital
abstract: This study characterised the distribution of occupational radiation doses received by cardiologists, scrub nurses, and anaesthesiology staff during 312 consecutive diagnostic coronary angiography procedures performed at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina over a 14-month period. Thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLD-100) were placed at the collar, chest, and wrist positions on all personnel present in the fluoroscopy suite. Dose area product (DAP) values were recorded for each procedure using a built-in ionisation chamber. The mean collar dose per procedure was 0.41 mSv for the primary operator and 0.09 mSv for the assisting nurse. A statistically significant correlation was found between DAP and operator collar dose (r = 0.73, p < 0.001). Procedures involving complex vessel anatomy required on average 38% more fluoroscopy time and produced collar doses approximately 1.6 times higher than straightforward cases. The paper recommends minimum shielding configurations and fluoroscopy time reduction strategies tailored to the observed workload pattern.

title: Evaluation of lead apron attenuation efficiency under realistic fluoroscopy scatter conditions
abstract: Lead aprons are the primary protective garment used by interventional staff, yet their attenuation efficiency under realistic scatter field conditions is seldom measured directly. This study evaluated seven commercially available apron models (0.25 mm, 0.35 mm, and 0.50 mm lead equivalent) using a Rando phantom as a scatter source at tube voltages of 70, 80, and 100 kVp. Dosimeters were placed beneath and above the apron surface at eleven anatomical points. At 80 kVp, the 0.35 mm equivalent aprons provided a mean attenuation factor of 93.4% at the thorax but only 74.1% at the lateral lumbar region, where apron overlap seams were present. The study found that no tested model provided uniform protection across all measurement points, and that declared lead equivalence systematically overestimated lateral flank protection by 8–15%. Recommendations are provided for apron selection and positioning protocols applicable to single-plane and biplane fluoroscopy suites.

title: Fluoroscopy time and DAP as predictors of staff dose in peripheral vascular interventions
abstract: Peripheral vascular interventions (PVI) are among the longer fluoroscopy procedures in an interventional suite, yet occupational dose data specific to this procedure class remain sparse in the regional literature. This prospective study enrolled 198 PVI cases at two institutions in Vojvodina and recorded fluoroscopy time, DAP, number of cine runs, and the personal dose equivalent Hp(10) for the primary operator, assistant, and circulating nurse. Median DAP was 42 Gy·cm² and median fluoroscopy time 18.4 minutes per procedure. Multivariate regression showed that fluoroscopy time was the single strongest predictor of operator dose, explaining 61% of variance after controlling for DAP and cine run count. For each additional minute of fluoroscopy, the operator collar dose increased by a mean of 19 μSv. Based on these findings, a set of fluoroscopy time reduction techniques was drafted and piloted over a subsequent six-month period, resulting in a mean reduction of 22% in fluoroscopy time without change in procedural success rate.

title: Implementation of a structured radiation dose optimisation protocol in an interventional cardiology unit: a before-and-after study
abstract: This paper describes the design and evaluation of a structured dose optimisation protocol introduced at the interventional cardiology unit of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina in 2005. The protocol addressed frame rate selection, collimation practice, last-image-hold utilisation, and table height adjustment. Before-period data covered 420 procedures in 2004; after-period data covered 418 procedures in 2006. Primary operator collar doses were estimated from TLD measurements and DAP-to-dose conversion factors validated in the same suite. Mean DAP decreased from 58.3 Gy·cm² to 44.1 Gy·cm² (24% reduction; 95% CI: 19–29%). Estimated operator effective dose per procedure fell from 0.28 mSv to 0.19 mSv. Compliance with the protocol, assessed through observation checklists, reached 81% by the end of the after period. The study also found that frame rate reduction from 15 to 7.5 frames per second for standard diagnostic runs was achievable without reported loss of diagnostic confidence by attending cardiologists.

title: Eye lens dose to interventional cardiologists: measurements and comparison with the revised ICRP dose limit
abstract: Following the 2011 International Commission on Radiological Protection recommendation to lower the occupational eye lens dose limit to 20 mSv per year, this study measured eye lens doses for nine interventional cardiologists at two Vojvodina institutions over a 12-month period. HP(3) dosimeters were placed on custom headbands worn just above the lateral canthus. Eye lens dose was also estimated from collar TLD readings using a conversion factor derived from a Rando phantom experiment conducted in the same suite geometry. Directly measured HP(3) values ranged from 7.2 to 31.4 mSv over the study year; two operators exceeded the new 20 mSv annual limit. There was a systematic underestimation of eye lens dose when collar TLD readings were used with the conversion factor (mean ratio measured/estimated: 1.41). The paper argues for direct eye lens monitoring as standard practice rather than collar-based estimation for high-workload operators, and evaluates the feasibility of wearing protective eyewear.

title: Radiation dose optimisation in fluoroscopy-guided biliary drainage procedures: staff dose and patient dose considerations
abstract: Fluoroscopy-guided percutaneous biliary drainage (PBD) is performed predominantly by radiologists rather than cardiologists and involves prolonged intermittent fluoroscopy with varied angulation. This study examined both patient and operator doses in 87 PBD procedures at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Patient entrance skin dose was estimated from DAP and backscatter factors; operator doses were measured with TLD at collar and hand positions. Mean patient entrance skin dose was 312 mGy per procedure (range 84–890 mGy). Operator collar doses ranged from 0.08 to 0.62 mSv per procedure; hand doses for the primary operator averaged 1.14 mSv per procedure. The highest hand doses occurred during needle placement and guide-wire manipulation. Use of remote wire manipulation tools reduced mean hand dose by 34% in a subset of 22 procedures. Shielding audit identified that the available ceiling-suspended shield was used in only 47% of cases; compliance improved to 78% following a targeted training session.

title: A multicentre survey of radiation protection practices in interventional fluoroscopy units across Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina
abstract: This paper reports on a structured survey of radiation protection practices conducted at 14 interventional fluoroscopy units in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina during 2012–2013. Unit physicists and lead radiologists at each site completed a standardised questionnaire covering equipment age, dose monitoring procedures, staff training records, shielding inventory, and protocol documentation. On-site measurements of scatter dose at standard positions were performed at eight of the 14 units using a calibrated ionisation chamber. Results showed that only five units had written dose optimisation protocols; staff personal dosimetry was conducted at all units but collar doses were routinely read at quarterly intervals rather than monthly at 10 of the 14 sites, delaying dose feedback. Equipment age ranged from 2 to 19 years; units with equipment older than 12 years produced scatter dose rates at the operator position 1.8 to 2.7 times higher than newer units for equivalent procedures. The paper provides a set of minimum practice standards derived from the survey findings.

title: Radiation protection in interventional fluoroscopy: a practical guide for clinical staff
abstract: This book chapter provides a practical, procedure-oriented overview of radiation protection measures applicable to fluoroscopy-guided interventional procedures. Topics covered include the physical basis of scatter radiation, occupational dose limits under Serbian and European regulatory frameworks, selection and correct use of personal protective equipment, optimisation of fluoroscopy technique parameters, monitoring of occupational doses, and special considerations for pregnant workers. Worked examples use dose data collected from clinical practice at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. The chapter is intended for cardiologists, radiologists, and nurses who work in interventional suites and who may not have formal radiation physics training. Emphasis is placed on practical decision points encountered during procedures rather than theoretical derivations. A checklist for radiation protection audits and a template for local written protocols are included as appendices.

title: Long-term occupational dose trends in an interventional radiology department: a 20-year retrospective analysis
abstract: This retrospective analysis used personal dosimetry records held by the Serbian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency to track annual occupational doses received by staff in the interventional radiology department of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina from 1996 to 2016. Records covered 34 individuals across three professional categories: radiologists (n=11), radiographers (n=14), and nursing staff (n=9). Annual effective dose estimates were derived from collar dosimeter readings using standard conversion factors. Mean annual dose for radiologists declined from 4.8 mSv in 1997 to 1.2 mSv in 2016, coinciding with two equipment replacement cycles and the formal introduction of dose optimisation protocols. No individual exceeded the 20 mSv annual limit in any year; however, three radiologists showed cumulative 5-year doses exceeding 40 mSv in the period 1998–2005. The analysis highlights the measurable impact of protocol-driven dose management and equipment modernisation on long-term occupational dose.

title: Geodesic Approximation on Empirical Manifolds for High-Dimensional Data Embeddings
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of estimating geodesic distances on manifolds reconstructed from noisy finite-sample data. We analyse the convergence of graph-based shortest-path estimates to true geodesic distances as sample size increases, under Riemannian manifold assumptions with bounded curvature. Two graph construction strategies are compared: k-nearest-neighbour graphs and epsilon-ball graphs. Experiments on synthetic manifolds embedded in dimensions 50 through 500 show that k-NN graphs with k scaling as O(log n) consistently outperform fixed-epsilon constructions in low-curvature regions. We also derive a corrected distance estimator that compensates for sampling density gradients, reducing mean absolute geodesic error by 18–34 percent across six benchmark manifolds. The results are relevant for any downstream task relying on geodesic distances, including Isomap-type embeddings and pseudotime estimation in biological data. Code and benchmark manifold generators are released as an open-source Python library.

title: Diffusion Maps with Adaptive Bandwidth Selection for Biological Expression Data
abstract: Diffusion maps embed data by constructing a Markov chain on a neighbourhood graph, with embedding coordinates derived from the eigenvectors of the diffusion operator. A key practical difficulty is choosing the kernel bandwidth parameter, which strongly affects the geometry of the resulting embedding. We propose a data-adaptive bandwidth selection criterion based on the estimated local intrinsic dimensionality at each data point, computed using the two-nearest-neighbour estimator. The method is evaluated on seven publicly available microarray gene-expression datasets ranging from 200 to 4 800 samples and 6 000 to 22 000 features. Compared to fixed-bandwidth diffusion maps and bandwidth selected by median-heuristic, the adaptive scheme improves cluster separation as measured by silhouette coefficient in six of seven datasets, with gains between 0.04 and 0.21. Runtime overhead relative to standard diffusion maps is under 5 percent. An R implementation is provided.

title: A Riemannian Gradient Descent Algorithm for Structured Low-Rank Matrix Approximation
abstract: We formulate the problem of fitting a structured low-rank matrix model as an optimisation problem on the Grassmann manifold and derive a Riemannian gradient descent algorithm with an Armijo-type line search. The algorithm is applied to the problem of imputing dropout zeros in single-cell RNA-seq count matrices, where the true expression matrix is assumed to lie near a low-dimensional manifold in log-space. On three simulated datasets with known ground-truth dropout patterns, the Riemannian approach recovers missing entries with lower mean squared error than two standard nuclear-norm relaxation methods, with differences statistically significant at the 1 percent level by paired Wilcoxon test. We analyse convergence to a first-order critical point and discuss the effect of rank misspecification. Limitations include quadratic memory scaling with cell count and sensitivity to the initial rank estimate.

title: Pseudotime Ordering of Hematopoietic Progenitor Cells Using Elastic Principal Graphs
abstract: Trajectory inference from single-cell RNA-seq data requires assigning each cell a pseudotime coordinate reflecting its position along a differentiation path. We apply the elastic principal graph framework, which fits a branching curve skeleton to data in PCA-reduced space by minimising a sum of data-to-graph distances and a smoothness penalty on graph topology. Using a dataset of 2 730 bone-marrow progenitor cells profiled across six developmental stages, we infer a trajectory with three branches corresponding to myeloid, erythroid, and lymphoid lineages. Branch assignment accuracy, evaluated against known surface-marker labels, reaches 89 percent. Comparison with three competing trajectory methods on the same data shows that elastic graphs recover the known branching topology more consistently when the branching point occurs late in pseudotime. We discuss sensitivity to PCA dimensionality choices and propose a cross-validation heuristic for selecting the number of principal components.

title: Benchmarking Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction Methods on Simulated Single-Cell RNA-Seq Datasets
abstract: We present a systematic evaluation of six nonlinear dimensionality reduction methods — diffusion maps, UMAP, t-SNE, LLE, PHATE, and a graph-autoencoder baseline — on single-cell RNA-seq data generated with the Splatter simulation framework under twelve parameter settings. Evaluation metrics include preservation of global structure (Spearman correlation of pairwise distances), cluster separability (Davies–Bouldin index), and trajectory recovery (Kendall tau between inferred and ground-truth pseudotime). Across 144 simulation conditions, PHATE and diffusion maps score highest on trajectory recovery, while UMAP excels at cluster separability. No single method dominates across all metrics. We also examine how the choice of highly variable gene selection affects results: restricting to the top 500 versus top 2 000 variable genes changes method rankings for trajectory recovery in 31 of 144 conditions. The benchmark suite is released as a reproducible Snakemake workflow.

title: Manifold Learning for Single-Cell Data: Methods and Biological Applications
abstract: This book chapter reviews the mathematical foundations and practical use of manifold learning techniques in the context of single-cell transcriptomics. We cover the spectral graph theory underpinning diffusion-based methods, the optimisation objectives behind UMAP and its variants, and the assumptions shared across principal-curve-based trajectory methods. A section on validation discusses the difficulty of ground-truth availability in real biological experiments and advocates for the use of synthetic benchmarks with known topology alongside partially-labelled real datasets. Case studies include neural differentiation, T-cell activation, and erythropoiesis. The chapter also addresses common practical pitfalls such as overinterpretation of two-dimensional projections, the effect of sequencing depth normalisation on embedding quality, and the choice of distance metric. Worked examples are provided using publicly available datasets and Python code.

title: Velocity-Augmented Diffusion Maps for Developmental Trajectory Inference
abstract: RNA velocity provides an estimate of the future transcriptional state of each cell by comparing unspliced and spliced mRNA abundances. We incorporate velocity vectors as directional constraints into the diffusion map framework by replacing the symmetric kernel with an asymmetric kernel that upweights transitions aligned with the velocity direction. The resulting directed diffusion operator is non-reversible, and its singular vectors rather than eigenvectors define the pseudotime embedding. We validate the method on a neurogenesis dataset containing 3 580 cells with expert-annotated cell-type labels, finding that directed diffusion maps recover the correct developmental ordering in 94 percent of pairwise cell comparisons, compared to 81 percent for undirected diffusion maps and 88 percent for a published RNA velocity-based ordering method. We also show reduced sensitivity to dropout noise when velocity estimates are smoothed over the k-NN graph before kernel construction.

title: Scalable Landmark-Based PHATE for Atlas-Scale Single-Cell Datasets
abstract: The PHATE algorithm constructs a multiscale geometry of cellular state space using potential distances derived from a diffusion operator, but its O(n^2) memory requirement becomes prohibitive for datasets exceeding 100 000 cells. We introduce LM-PHATE, a landmark-based approximation in which potential distances are computed exactly for a set of L landmarks selected by k-means++ and then extended to all cells by distance-weighted interpolation. On four datasets ranging from 80 000 to 1.3 million cells, LM-PHATE with L = 2 000 landmarks recovers trajectory structures visually and quantitatively indistinguishable from full PHATE on a 50 000-cell subsample, while reducing peak memory usage by a factor of 12 to 18 and wall-clock time by a factor of 8 to 14. We provide an implementation compatible with the AnnData ecosystem and benchmark against existing scalable trajectory tools on a standardised set of metrics.

title: Assessing the Effect of Feature Selection on Manifold Geometry in scRNA-seq Embeddings
abstract: Highly variable gene (HVG) selection is a standard preprocessing step in single-cell analysis pipelines, yet its effect on the geometry of downstream manifold embeddings is rarely quantified. We systematically vary the number of HVGs from 200 to 5 000 in steps of 200 and measure changes in three embedding geometry descriptors: the distribution of local intrinsic dimensionality estimates, the persistence diagram of the Rips filtration, and the Spearman correlation between embedding distances and full-transcriptome distances. Experiments across nine datasets spanning three tissue types show that embeddings stabilise geometrically above approximately 1 500 HVGs for datasets with fewer than 10 000 cells, but require up to 3 000 HVGs for larger datasets. We also find that Seurat-style dispersion-based HVG selection and scran-style modelling of mean–variance trend yield embeddings with indistinguishable geometric properties at matched HVG counts. Results suggest that the common default of 2 000 HVGs is reasonable but should be validated per dataset.

title: Integrating Spatial Transcriptomics and Single-Cell Trajectories via Graph-Coupled Manifold Alignment
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics platforms measure gene expression while retaining physical tissue coordinates, whereas single-cell RNA-seq captures high-resolution transcriptional states without spatial context. Combining both data types for trajectory inference requires aligning two manifolds that share latent biological variables but differ in feature space and measurement noise characteristics. We propose a graph-coupled manifold alignment approach that constructs a joint graph by connecting cells across modalities using a correspondence set derived from nearest-neighbour matching in a common low-dimensional projection, then jointly embeds both graphs using a generalised eigenvalue formulation. Evaluated on a developing mouse embryo dataset with 8 200 spatially resolved spots and 12 400 single-cell RNA-seq profiles, the method recovers spatial gradients of pseudotime consistent with known anteroposterior patterning, with 91 percent of spatial spots assigned to pseudotime intervals matching immunofluorescence marker annotations. Runtime on a 32-core server is under 20 minutes.

title: Curvature Estimation on Data Manifolds and Its Effect on Pseudotime Variance
abstract: Pseudotime variance — the spread of pseudotime assignments around a trajectory curve — is often treated as a nuisance, but we argue it carries information about local transcriptional heterogeneity. We formalise this by relating pseudotime variance to the sectional curvature of the estimated data manifold at each point along the trajectory. Using a kernel-based curvature estimator applied to diffusion map embeddings, we compute curvature profiles for 14 published scRNA-seq datasets and find that high-curvature regions coincide with known cell-fate decision points in nine cases. We propose a curvature-weighted pseudotime smoother that reduces pseudotime variance at high-curvature points while preserving global ordering, improving Kendall tau trajectory correlation by 0.05–0.12 across datasets with annotated branching points. The method is implemented in Python and integrated into the DiffMap-tools package maintained by our group.

title: Bayesian Estimation of Structural Breaks in Corporate Cash Flows Using Reversible Jump MCMC
abstract: Identifying the number and timing of structural breaks in a financial time series is a model selection problem with a variable-dimensional parameter space. This paper applies reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (RJMCMC) to simultaneously estimate break locations, the number of breaks, and segment-specific regression parameters in a piecewise linear cash-flow model. Convergence diagnostics are based on the potential scale reduction factor across five independent chains. The method is applied to annual and quarterly cash-flow data from a panel of 35 publicly listed regional companies covering 2008–2021, a span that encompasses the 2008 financial crisis, the 2012 sovereign debt period, and the 2020 pandemic shock. The posterior mode number of breaks is 2 for most firms, with break locations concentrating around Q3 2009 and Q2 2020. Segment-level volatility estimates differ by a factor of 2.3 on average across break periods, consistent with external macroeconomic evidence.

title: Decomposition Methods for Large-Scale Multi-Period AC Optimal Power Flow
abstract: Multi-period AC optimal power flow couples time steps through storage and ramp constraints, making the resulting nonlinear program substantially larger than single-period formulations. This chapter reviews decomposition approaches applicable to such problems, covering Lagrangian relaxation, alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and temporal decomposition with overlapping windows. For each method the convergence guarantees, practical stopping criteria, and communication overhead in a parallel implementation are described. Numerical illustrations use a 300-bus network with 12 storage units over a 48-period horizon. ADMM with a penalty parameter schedule converges to within 0.5% of a monolithic solve in 14 iterations on 8 parallel workers. The chapter also discusses how SOCP relaxations can replace AC subproblems to improve convexity properties and speed up each decomposition step, at the cost of a small feasibility gap that must be corrected in post-processing.

title: Formal Verification of a Constant-Time NTT Implementation Using the Frama-C Framework
abstract: Number Theoretic Transform implementations are at the heart of lattice-based KEM performance, but verifying their constant-time property formally remains challenging. This paper presents a Frama-C/WP-based verification of a complete constant-time NTT implementation for the ring Z_q[x]/(x^{256}+1) with q = 3329, corresponding to the ML-KEM-512 parameter set. We annotate the C source with ACSL contracts specifying absence of secret-dependent branches and memory accesses, and discharge 1,847 verification conditions automatically using the Alt-Ergo and CVC5 SMT solvers. Of the conditions, 43 required manual lemma assistance. The verified implementation matches cycle counts of the unverified reference to within 0.4%, confirming that verification annotations do not degrade performance. We also identify one latent timing leak in a subtraction-based modular reduction present in three widely used open-source libraries, report it to maintainers, and provide a verified replacement.

title: Mechanism Design for Congestion-Aware Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
abstract: Network congestion limits how much energy prosumers can exchange across constrained distribution lines, yet most peer-to-peer trading mechanisms ignore grid topology. This paper proposes a congestion-aware Vickrey–Clarke–Groves (VCG) mechanism that incorporates nodal capacity constraints into the allocation rule and payment scheme. The mechanism is proved to be dominant-strategy incentive compatible and budget-balanced in expectation. A 34-node radial distribution test network is used to benchmark the approach against a topology-blind double auction. Across 500 simulated trading intervals, the VCG mechanism reduces congestion violations by 78% and improves aggregate surplus by 11% relative to the baseline. Computational complexity scales quadratically with the number of agents, which limits applicability to markets with fewer than approximately 200 participants without additional decomposition. Extensions to multi-period trading windows are outlined in the concluding section.
venue: European Journal of Operational Research in Energy

title: Marginal fit of pressed lithium disilicate crowns before and after glaze firing: a stereomicroscopic assessment
abstract: Marginal discrepancy of pressed lithium disilicate (LS2) crowns was measured on standardised typodont premolar preparations at four anatomical sites (mesial, distal, buccal, lingual) before and after glaze firing. Forty crowns from two pressing batches were seated on epoxy resin dies and cross-sectioned for stereomicroscopic measurement at 40× magnification. Mean marginal gap before glazing was 68 ± 12 µm; after glazing the gap increased to 89 ± 15 µm, a statistically significant difference (paired t-test, p < 0.001). Buccal margins showed the largest post-glaze increase. No batch-to-batch differences were detected. The results suggest that glaze firing at 770 °C causes a measurable but clinically acceptable dimensional change. These baseline data informed subsequent masticatory loading studies by confirming pre-test marginal quality within a 120 µm threshold. The study underscores the need to measure marginal fit at multiple time-points during fabrication.

title: Surface roughness of 3Y-TZP zirconia after different chairside adjusting and polishing protocols
abstract: Monolithic 3Y-TZP zirconia discs (n = 60, diameter 15 mm, sintered to final density) were subjected to four surface finishing protocols: (A) no adjustment, (B) diamond bur adjustment only, (C) diamond bur followed by rubber polishing, and (D) diamond bur followed by rubber polishing and re-glaze firing. Surface roughness Ra was measured by contact profilometry at baseline and after each step. Protocol B produced the highest Ra values (1.82 ± 0.34 µm), significantly higher than protocol D (0.31 ± 0.09 µm, p < 0.001). Scanning electron microscopy revealed surface crack propagation up to 4 µm depth following adjustment without subsequent polishing. Phase composition by X-ray diffraction showed minimal monoclinic content increase (< 2%) for all protocols, indicating that the adjustments did not trigger significant transformation toughening at the surface. Clinically, re-glazing after polishing remains preferable for restoring surface integrity after intraoral adjustment.

title: Two-body wear of monolithic zirconia and lithium disilicate against human enamel under simulated masticatory loading
abstract: Wear of monolithic 3Y-TZP zirconia and lithium disilicate (LS2) occlusal surfaces against natural human enamel antagonists was compared using a four-station masticatory simulator. Specimens (n = 15 per group) were loaded at 49 N, 1.7 Hz, through 100,000 cycles in artificial saliva at 37 °C. Volumetric wear was quantified by optical profilometry and micro-CT before and after simulation. LS2 crowns showed significantly greater self-wear (mean volume loss 0.89 ± 0.21 mm³) than zirconia crowns (0.14 ± 0.06 mm³, p < 0.001). Conversely, enamel antagonists opposing zirconia lost 0.72 ± 0.18 mm³ compared with 0.31 ± 0.12 mm³ opposing LS2 (p < 0.001). Scanning electron microscopy of zirconia surfaces revealed minimal grain pull-out; LS2 surfaces showed microfracture and ploughing. The trade-off between material self-wear and antagonist wear is relevant to material selection for patients with parafunctional habits.

title: Effect of cement film thickness on marginal integrity of monolithic zirconia molar crowns after thermocycling and mechanical loading
abstract: This study examined how resin cement film thickness affects the marginal integrity of monolithic 3Y-TZP crowns after combined thermocycling and cyclic loading. Sixty molar crowns were cemented on stainless steel dies under three seating loads (5 N, 15 N, 30 N), yielding three cement film groups (mean thicknesses 82, 54, and 31 µm). Specimens were thermocycled (5–55 °C, 5,000 cycles) and then subjected to 50,000 compressive cycles at 200 N. Marginal gap measurements were performed by cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy before and after each ageing stage. Pre-ageing gaps ranged from 58 to 103 µm across groups. After combined ageing, the 31 µm group showed the smallest gap increase (Δ = 9 µm) and lowest incidence of cement washout (8%), while the 82 µm group had a Δ of 31 µm and 33% washout rate. Thinner cement films correlate with better marginal stability under simulated clinical conditions.

title: Long-term marginal stability of monolithic zirconia crowns under fatigue loading: a micro-CT longitudinal study
abstract: Marginal gap evolution in monolithic 3Y-TZP posterior crowns was tracked longitudinally using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) at four fatigue intervals (0, 250,000, 500,000, and 1,000,000 cycles). Twenty crowns were cemented on extracted human premolar stumps with self-adhesive resin cement and loaded at 120 N in a masticatory simulator. Micro-CT scans (voxel size 9 µm) at each interval allowed volumetric reconstruction of the cement space. Mean marginal gap increased from 62 ± 8 µm at baseline to 75 ± 11 µm at 1,000,000 cycles. The increment between 500,000 and 1,000,000 cycles was not statistically significant (p = 0.12), suggesting stabilisation of marginal gap change after the initial seating adjustment phase. No catastrophic marginal fractures were recorded. These findings support the clinical durability of monolithic zirconia crowns over a loading range equivalent to approximately four years of normal function.

title: Wear of polished versus glazed monolithic zirconia occlusal surfaces: profilometric and SEM analysis after 500,000 masticatory cycles
abstract: The influence of occlusal surface finishing—polishing versus glazing—on wear behaviour of monolithic 3Y-TZP zirconia crowns and on opposing enamel antagonists was evaluated after 500,000 simulated masticatory cycles. Thirty molar crowns were divided equally into polished and glazed groups. Wear testing used a chewing simulator with 49 N vertical load and 0.7 mm lateral movement in artificial saliva. Profilometric scanning before and after testing quantified Ra changes and wear depth. Polished zirconia showed lower self-wear depth (mean 6.2 ± 1.4 µm) compared with glazed zirconia (8.9 ± 2.1 µm, p < 0.05). Enamel antagonist wear was not significantly different between groups (p = 0.18), contrary to earlier reports using higher loads. SEM images of polished surfaces revealed fewer surface irregularities post-test than glazed surfaces, which showed glaze layer delamination in four specimens. Polishing is recommended over glazing for final surface preparation of zirconia occlusal surfaces.

title: Comparative three-body wear of monolithic zirconia and lithium disilicate in a food-slurry masticatory simulation using a PMMA abrasive medium
abstract: Three-body wear, mediated by food-particle abrasives, was assessed for monolithic 3Y-TZP zirconia and lithium disilicate (LS2) posterior crowns using a modified chewing simulator incorporating a polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) bead slurry as abrasive medium. Specimens (n = 20 per material) were loaded at 49 N, 1.5 Hz, for 200,000 cycles. Wear facet depth and volume loss were determined by optical coherence profilometry. Three-body wear volumes were substantially higher than two-body wear values from an earlier study under comparable conditions: LS2 lost 2.14 ± 0.38 mm³ and zirconia 1.07 ± 0.22 mm³. The ratio of LS2 to zirconia wear was approximately 2:1, consistent with two-body data. Surface analysis showed prominent pull-out craters on LS2 but smoother tribological wear tracks on zirconia. Enamel antagonist wear was also measured; zirconia caused 1.31 ± 0.29 mm³ enamel loss versus 0.87 ± 0.19 mm³ for LS2. Abrasive food particles amplify the material-dependent differences already observed in two-body testing.

title: Marginal gap and ceramic surface degradation after autoclave sterilisation cycles in monolithic posterior crowns: a preliminary investigation
abstract: Repeated autoclave sterilisation is not routinely applied to cemented crowns but may occur to try-in or provisional restorations. This preliminary study investigated whether five autoclave cycles (134 °C, 2.1 bar, 18 min each) alter marginal gap dimensions and surface integrity of unseated monolithic 3Y-TZP and LS2 crowns. Twenty crowns (10 per material) were scanned by micro-CT and by profilometry before and after sterilisation. No statistically significant marginal gap changes were found for either material (p > 0.05). Profilometric Ra values were unchanged for zirconia but showed a marginal increase for LS2 (from 0.22 to 0.31 µm, p = 0.04), which SEM imaging attributed to superficial glaze micro-dissolution. XRD confirmed no monoclinic phase increase in zirconia. The results suggest that standard autoclave sterilisation does not compromise the dimensional integrity of either ceramic system, though repeated sterilisation of LS2 may warrant monitoring of surface quality.

title: Remineralisation potential of CPP-ACP under different salivary flow conditions simulated in vitro
abstract: Artificial saliva flow rate has been proposed as a confounding variable in studies assessing CPP-ACP efficacy. In this study, a custom-built flow cell maintained three steady-state flow rates (0.1, 0.5, and 1.5 mL/min) over standardised bovine enamel specimens during pH cycling. CPP-ACP gel was applied for 3 minutes at the start of each remineralisation phase. Mineral change was assessed by TMR after 10 days. At 0.1 mL/min, mineral gain was 14% of initial loss; at 0.5 mL/min, 24%; at 1.5 mL/min, 29%. Calcium and phosphate ion concentrations in the effluent were measured by ICP-OES and showed elevated release under low-flow conditions, suggesting reduced delivery efficiency. SEM-EDX mapping confirmed calcium-rich surface deposits were thickest at 1.5 mL/min. These results indicate that salivary flow rate significantly modulates CPP-ACP remineralisation outcomes and should be controlled or reported in in vitro protocols.
venue: Journal of Hard Tissue Biology and Biomineralization

title: Micro-CT assessment of subsurface porosity changes in early enamel lesions following repeated CPP-ACP and fluoride treatment cycles
abstract: Micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) was used to image the three-dimensional internal porosity structure of standardised artificial lesions in human enamel (n = 30 blocks) before and after 10-day treatment with CPP-ACP, 1 450 ppm F dentifrice slurry, a combination, or deionised water. Voxel size was 2 μm. Total lesion porosity, maximum pore diameter, and mineral density distribution histograms were extracted using Dragonfly software. Combination treatment reduced total lesion porosity from 19.4% to 12.7%, corresponding to the greatest subsurface mineral gain. The fluoride-alone group showed the greatest surface mineral density increase but less subsurface pore closure. CPP-ACP alone produced more uniform subsurface pore reduction with less surface hypermineralisation. Deionised water controls showed no significant change. These three-dimensional data are consistent with the complementary mechanisms proposed from two-dimensional TMR studies and provide spatial detail about where within the lesion body mineral is deposited preferentially.

title: Remineralisation outcomes in early childhood caries-affected enamel compared with sound enamel: differences in CPP-ACP and fluoride response
abstract: Enamel from teeth extracted due to severe early childhood caries (ECC, n = 22 teeth) was compared with enamel from premolars extracted for orthodontic reasons (n = 22) as a reference population. Artificial surface lesions were created under identical pH cycling conditions and then treated with CPP-ACP paste, 900 ppm F rinse, combined treatment, or negative control over seven days. TMR measured baseline mineral loss and subsequent recovery. ECC enamel showed 23% lower initial mineral density by micro-CT, greater initial lesion depth after the standardised demineralisation, and lower percentage mineral recovery under all treatment conditions (overall mean 15% recovery versus 28% in reference enamel, p < 0.001). SEM-EDX revealed disrupted prism boundaries and reduced magnesium content in ECC enamel. These structural differences may partly explain the clinical observation that lesions in young children with ECC are more resistant to standard remineralisation regimens and may require modified treatment protocols or extended application times.

title: Salivary interleukin-1β and interleukin-6 levels in patients with chronic periodontitis: a cross-sectional study
abstract: This cross-sectional study measured unstimulated whole saliva concentrations of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in 62 adults with chronic periodontitis and 40 periodontally healthy controls recruited at the Dental Clinic of Novi Sad. Saliva was collected by the spitting method and cytokine concentrations were determined by sandwich ELISA. Patients with periodontitis showed significantly elevated IL-1β (median 312 pg/mL versus 89 pg/mL in controls, p < 0.001) and IL-6 (median 47 pg/mL versus 18 pg/mL, p < 0.001). Periodontal indices — probing pocket depth, clinical attachment loss, and bleeding on probing — correlated positively with both cytokines (Spearman ρ 0.61–0.72). Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that IL-1β remained an independent predictor of periodontitis after adjustment for age, sex, and smoking status. These findings support the use of salivary cytokines as accessible, non-invasive indicators of periodontal inflammation, though prospective longitudinal data are needed to establish predictive utility.

title: Salivary adiponectin and resistin in the context of periodontal-metabolic comorbidity: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Adipokines such as adiponectin and resistin are secreted by adipose tissue and modulate inflammatory responses; their presence in saliva has been reported but their association with periodontal-metabolic comorbidity has not been systematically evaluated. Databases PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to December 2022. Studies comparing salivary adiponectin or resistin in adult patients with any combination of periodontitis and type 2 diabetes versus controls were eligible. Twelve studies met inclusion criteria (total n = 1,247). Meta-analysis using a random-effects model found salivary adiponectin significantly lower in patients with both conditions compared to diabetes alone (standardised mean difference −0.61, 95 % CI −0.91 to −0.31; I² = 58 %). Resistin data were insufficient for pooled analysis. Heterogeneity was partly explained by differences in diabetes duration (meta-regression p = 0.04). Publication bias was moderate (Egger's test p = 0.09). The review highlights gaps in standardised saliva collection protocols and the need for longitudinal designs.
