title: Collective Guilt or Identity Threat? Serbian Majority Participants' Responses to Framed Descriptions of Wartime Atrocities
abstract: This study investigated whether majority-group members' emotional reactions to descriptions of in-group wartime atrocities are better characterised as collective guilt or as identity-protective defensiveness. Ninety-four Serbian undergraduate participants read one of three vignettes: a neutral historical description, a responsibility-attributing description, or a victim-centred description of a fictional inter-ethnic conflict. Dependent measures included self-reported collective guilt, shame, anger, and a brief behavioural willingness-to-compensate scale. Results indicated that the responsibility-attributing vignette produced significantly higher identity-threat scores (d = 0.61, p = .004) compared to the victim-centred condition, while collective guilt scores did not differ significantly between experimental conditions. Shame scores were elevated across both experimental vignettes relative to the neutral control. Mediation analyses suggested that perceived threat to national identity partially suppressed the relationship between vignette condition and compensatory intentions. The findings replicate and partially extend prior work from German and Dutch samples to a South-East European post-conflict context, while raising questions about the cross-cultural portability of the collective guilt construct.

title: Measuring Implicit Associations Between National In-group and Moral Wrongdoing: An IAT Study with Serbian and Croatian Student Samples
abstract: Using a standard Implicit Association Test procedure, this study examined the strength of automatic associations between national in-group category labels and concepts related to moral wrongdoing (e.g., atrocity, guilt, perpetrator) versus moral virtue (e.g., heroism, defender, justice) in two student samples: 78 Serbian participants recruited at the University of Novi Sad and 81 Croatian participants recruited at a partner university in Zagreb. IAT D-scores indicated that both samples showed a reliable implicit preference for associating their national in-group with virtue-related rather than wrongdoing-related concepts (Serbian sample: D = 0.52, SE = 0.08; Croatian sample: D = 0.47, SE = 0.09). Importantly, D-score magnitude was not significantly correlated with explicit national identification in either sample, nor with self-reported collective guilt. Post-test explicit measures revealed moderate collective guilt and low shame scores in both groups. The dissociation between implicit and explicit indicators suggests that studies relying solely on self-report may underestimate automatic defensiveness in post-conflict majority populations. Limitations regarding student convenience sampling and the fictional conflict framing are discussed.

title: The Role of Moral Disengagement Mechanisms in Minimising Perceived In-group Responsibility for Historical Violence
abstract: This pre-registered study tested whether Bandura's moral disengagement mechanisms — specifically displacement of responsibility, diffusion of responsibility, and dehumanisation of victims — could predict the degree to which majority-group members minimise their in-group's causal responsibility for a described historical atrocity. Participants were 142 Serbian adults recruited via online convenience sampling. They completed Bandura's Moral Disengagement Scale, read a detailed vignette describing a fictional 1990s-era conflict-related massacre attributed to a majority ethnic group in an unnamed Balkan country, and then completed scales assessing attributed in-group responsibility, counterfactual distancing, and collective guilt. Displacement and diffusion of responsibility each significantly predicted lower in-group responsibility attribution (β = −0.29 and β = −0.22 respectively, both p < .01), while dehumanisation of victims did not reach significance in this sample. Collective guilt showed a moderate negative correlation with moral disengagement total score (r = −0.38). The study contributes empirical data on the psychological architecture of historical denial processes in a population with direct cultural proximity to the described events.

title: Apology Framing and Its Effect on Perceived Sincerity and Willingness to Forgive: A Vignette Experiment Across Three Balkan Samples
abstract: Inter-group apologies issued by political leaders are a common feature of post-conflict reconciliation processes, yet little research has examined how the framing of such apologies affects their reception among majority-group members in the Western Balkans. This conference paper reports data from an experimental vignette study conducted with samples from Serbia (n = 89), Bosnia and Herzegovina (n = 76), and North Macedonia (n = 64). Participants read a fictional political apology for wartime violence that varied on two dimensions: source of apology (head of state vs. parliament) and explicitness of responsibility attribution (explicit vs. hedged). Perceived sincerity was rated on a five-item scale adapted from prior work in the German transitional justice literature. Results indicated a significant main effect of explicitness on perceived sincerity in the Serbian sample (F(1, 87) = 6.14, p = .015), but not in the other two samples. Willingness-to-forgive scores were uniformly low across conditions and samples, suggesting a ceiling effect in resistance. Cross-national differences in response patterns are discussed with reference to differences in conflict proximity and dominant national narratives.

title: Historical Shame and Educational Exposure: Do Secondary School Curricula Affect Majority-Group Adolescents' Collective Emotions About Past Violence?
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined whether the degree of exposure to factual historical content about inter-ethnic violence in secondary school is associated with collective shame, collective guilt, and national identification in young adults. Participants were 211 first-year psychology and history students at three universities in Serbia and Vojvodina who completed retrospective self-report measures of history curriculum exposure, a modified Collective Guilt Questionnaire, the Collective Shame Scale, and a standard measure of national identification. Greater recalled exposure to atrocity-related historical content was associated with modestly higher collective shame (r = 0.24, p = .001) but showed no significant relationship with collective guilt or national identification after controlling for parental education. Regression analyses including political orientation and family narrative variables explained 18% of the variance in collective shame. The results are discussed in terms of educational policy implications and the partial decoupling of shame from guilt in pedagogical contexts. Methodological limitations of retrospective curriculum exposure measurement are acknowledged.

title: Area-of-interest dwell time profiles differentiate adaptive from maladaptive error-correction strategies in novice programmers
abstract: When novice programmers encounter syntax errors, their gaze allocation patterns during error correction vary considerably and may indicate whether correction strategies are systematic or haphazard. This study tracked eye movements of 38 first-year computer science students as they debugged short code snippets containing one to three planted errors. Area-of-interest dwell times were computed for five screen regions: error-flagged lines, surrounding context, console output, documentation panel, and unrelated code. Students who resolved errors successfully showed higher proportional dwell time on console output and context regions (combined 54% of total dwell) compared with unsuccessful students (38%). Dwell time entropy—a measure of distribution uniformity—was higher in unsuccessful students (M = 2.31 bits vs. M = 1.87 bits, p < .01). Findings suggest that structured gaze protocols reflecting systematic information search characterise effective debugging and that dwell-time entropy may serve as a formative monitoring index in programming education.

title: Measurement invariance of the Hexagonal Personality Inventory across age groups in a Serbian employed sample
abstract: This study tested measurement invariance of the revised Serbian Hexagonal Personality Inventory (HPI-S) across younger (18–35 years, n = 387) and older (36–60 years, n = 341) employed adults drawn from manufacturing, healthcare, and administrative sectors. Multi-group CFA was conducted using a sequence of progressively constrained models: configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Configural and metric invariance were supported across all six scales. However, scalar invariance tests revealed non-invariant intercepts for seven items on the Conscientiousness and Agreeableness scales (ΔCFI > 0.010, ΔRMSEA > 0.015). Partial scalar invariance was established after freeing these intercepts. Latent mean comparisons indicated a statistically significant difference favouring the older group on Conscientiousness (d = 0.31) and a non-significant trend on Emotional Stability. The findings caution against direct raw-score comparisons across age groups in multi-cohort personnel selection contexts without accounting for partial non-invariance.

title: Construction and initial validation of the Occupational Wellbeing Inventory for Serbian white-collar workers
abstract: This paper reports the construction and validation of the Occupational Wellbeing Inventory (OWI-SR), a 32-item instrument developed to assess four dimensions of occupational wellbeing—emotional exhaustion, job satisfaction, sense of meaning, and colleague support—in Serbian white-collar contexts. Item generation drew on focus groups with 24 employees and a literature review of existing scales. An exploratory factor analysis on a calibration sample (n = 302) was followed by confirmatory factor analysis on a separate validation sample (n = 341). The four-factor correlated model fit was acceptable (CFI = 0.92, RMSEA = 0.061, SRMR = 0.062). Convergent validity was assessed against established measures of burnout and work engagement; discriminant validity was examined using the average variance extracted criterion. All four subscales met the AVE threshold of 0.50. Test–retest reliability over four weeks was r = 0.77–0.84. The OWI-SR shows promise as a concise assessment tool adapted to local labour market conditions.

title: Psychometric properties of the Fear of Intimacy Scale in a Serbian student sample
abstract: This study evaluated the psychometric properties of a 35-item self-report measure of fear of intimacy in a sample of 489 Serbian university students (mean age 21.1, 72% women). Exploratory factor analysis suggested a single-factor solution accounting for 31% of total variance, consistent with the original instrument's unidimensional design. Internal consistency was α = .93. Test-retest reliability over a four-week interval in a subsample (n = 74) was r = .81. Convergent validity was supported by positive correlations with attachment avoidance (r = .62) and anxiety (r = .38), and negative correlations with self-disclosure (r = −.54). Discriminant validity was evidenced by a near-zero correlation with social desirability (r = −.07). Women scored significantly lower on fear of intimacy than men (d = −0.29, p < .01), consistent with Western samples. The scale is considered suitable for use with Serbian student populations, and normative data stratified by gender are provided.

title: Eye-tracking indices of attention control during a rule-based card-sorting task in 4- and 5-year-old children
abstract: Gaze behaviour was recorded with a Tobii Spectrum eye-tracker during a researcher-developed card-sorting task in 56 children aged 48–60 months to examine whether fixation patterns differentiated successful from unsuccessful rule application. Children sorted cards by shape or colour according to a rule cue presented at trial onset. Dwell time on the rule cue, number of fixations before card selection, and total saccade count were extracted as oculomotor indices. Children who sorted correctly on switch trials had longer dwell times on the rule cue (M = 1,340 ms vs. M = 890 ms; d = 0.71) and fewer saccades before responding (M = 4.1 vs. M = 6.7; d = 0.64). Age in months moderated the relationship between dwell time and switching accuracy. Findings provide oculomotor process evidence for the role of directed attention in early cognitive flexibility and suggest eye-tracking as a useful complement to accuracy-based scoring.

title: Primena video-kodiranja u istraživanjima psihodinamske formulacije: metodološka razmatranja i etički izazovi
abstract: Rad raspravlja o metodološkim i etičkim aspektima primene video-zapisa kliničkih intervjua u istraživanjima pouzdanosti psihodinamskih formulacija. Na osnovu iskustva stečenog u tri istraživačka projekta realizovana na Filozofskom fakultetu u Novom Sadu u periodu 2014–2020, autori razmatraju pitanja informisanog pristanka, anonimizacije materijala i čuvanja podataka u skladu sa GDPR regulativom. Takođe se analiziraju prednosti video-kodiranja u poređenju sa transkriptima: mogućnost kodiranja neverbalne komunikacije, paralingvističkih signala i afekata procenjivača. Preliminarni podaci iz tekuće studije (N = 28 intervjua, tri procenjivača) pokazuju da video-kodiranje poboljšava ICC vrednosti za odbrambene mehanizme prosečno za 0.11 u poređenju sa isključivim oslanjanjem na transkripciju. Predlažu se praktične smernice za uspostavljanje video-kodirnih laboratorija u kliničkim istraživačkim centrima.

title: Noise-robust Serbian speech recognition for telephone audio
abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems deployed in telephone call centres routinely encounter background noise, channel distortions, and codec artefacts that degrade recognition accuracy. This paper presents a noise-robust ASR framework specifically designed for Serbian telephone audio. We compile a new evaluation benchmark drawn from real call-centre recordings and augment an existing Serbian speech corpus with synthetically degraded samples covering eight noise categories at signal-to-noise ratios between 0 dB and 20 dB. Acoustic models based on a hybrid TDNN-HMM architecture are trained with multi-condition augmentation, and we further investigate the effectiveness of spectral mapping and feature normalisation as front-end compensations. Results show that our best system achieves a 17.3% relative word-error-rate reduction over a clean-trained baseline on the noisy telephone benchmark while retaining competitive performance on clean read speech. We additionally evaluate domain adaptation using a small set of in-domain transcribed calls, demonstrating that even 30 minutes of labelled telephone data yields measurable gains. The released models and benchmark encourage reproducible research on under-resourced Slavic languages in noisy telephony conditions.

title: A Serbian text-to-speech voice built from 20 hours of audio
abstract: High-quality text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis for low-resource languages typically demands hundreds of hours of professionally recorded audio, an impractical requirement for Serbian. This paper describes the construction of a natural-sounding Serbian TTS voice trained from only 20 hours of studio-quality recordings produced by a single female speaker. We adopt a Tacotron-2-style sequence-to-sequence acoustic model combined with a flow-based neural vocoder and investigate several data-efficiency techniques including transfer learning from a related Slavic language, phoneme-level duration modelling, and prosody embedding. Objective evaluations using mel-cepstral distortion and voiced/unvoiced decision rates confirm the viability of the approach, while a listening test with 42 native Serbian speakers yields a mean opinion score of 4.01, competitive with systems trained on substantially larger corpora. We publicly release the trained model weights and the pronunciation lexicon developed during the project. The work establishes a reproducible pipeline for building decent-quality TTS voices for other South Slavic languages that currently lack such resources.

title: Building a telephone speech corpus for Serbian: collection, annotation, and baseline ASR results
abstract: Scarcity of annotated telephone-quality speech data is a primary obstacle to advancing automatic speech recognition for Serbian. This paper describes the design and construction of TeleSrp-300, a 300-hour corpus of simulated and real telephone conversations in Serbian, collected from 180 speakers across three dialect regions. Recordings were captured over both VoIP and PSTN channels, then manually transcribed and annotated for speaker identity, channel type, and background noise level. We describe the annotation workflow, quality-control procedures, and the resulting inter-annotator agreement scores. Baseline ASR experiments using a Kaldi-based recipe establish word error rates that serve as reproducible reference points for the community. Comparative analysis across dialect sub-sets reveals that non-standard dialectal pronunciations account for approximately 34% of substitution errors in the baseline model. The corpus and associated tools are made freely available for academic use, and we outline a roadmap for extending coverage to spontaneous conversational speech and code-switching scenarios common in Serbian urban environments.

title: End-to-end speech recognition for Serbian using transformer architectures with limited training data
abstract: End-to-end models have largely supplanted hybrid systems in high-resource speech recognition, yet their appetite for labelled data makes direct application to low-resource languages such as Serbian challenging. This paper investigates how transformer-based end-to-end architectures—specifically Conformer CTC/Attention and Whisper fine-tuning—perform when training data is limited to under 100 hours of Serbian speech. We systematically compare three data augmentation regimes (SpecAugment, speed perturbation, and room-impulse-response simulation) and two cross-lingual initialisation strategies (from Croatian and from a massively multilingual model). Experiments on three test sets of varying acoustic conditions show that fine-tuning a multilingual pre-trained checkpoint with aggressive augmentation outperforms all from-scratch baselines, achieving a word error rate of 9.4% on read speech and 22.1% on spontaneous telephone conversations. We also quantify the effect of vocabulary size and subword unit type for Serbian's inflectional morphology, finding that character-level models are surprisingly competitive with byte-pair-encoding variants when training data is scarce.

title: Pronunciation lexicon construction for Serbian TTS: a rule-based and data-driven hybrid approach
abstract: A high-coverage pronunciation lexicon is a fundamental component of both speech synthesis and recognition systems, yet no publicly available standardised lexicon exists for Serbian. This paper presents a methodology for constructing such a lexicon by combining hand-crafted grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions with a sequence-to-sequence neural model trained on 28,000 manually verified word–phoneme pairs. We introduce a novel hybrid decoding strategy that applies the rule-based system as a constraint over the neural model's beam search, reducing the phoneme error rate on a held-out test set to 2.1%, compared with 4.7% for the neural-only baseline. The resulting lexicon covers 210,000 headwords including inflected forms, proper nouns, and foreign loanwords common in contemporary Serbian media. Integration experiments within the TTS pipeline described in our earlier work confirm that the improved lexicon raises the mean opinion score by 0.13 points. The lexicon is released under an open licence to facilitate reproducibility.

title: Speaker adaptation for call-centre ASR: few-shot techniques for Serbian conversational speech
abstract: In deployed call-centre environments, ASR systems routinely encounter a wide diversity of speakers whose vocal characteristics differ substantially from the training population. This paper examines speaker adaptation strategies for a Serbian call-centre ASR system, focusing on the practically important scenario where only a small amount of unlabelled or weakly labelled speech from a new speaker is available at inference time. We compare i-vector and x-vector speaker representations as conditioning inputs, test model-agnostic meta-learning initialisation for rapid fine-tuning, and evaluate unsupervised hypothesis-driven adaptation using N-best list rescoring. Experiments conducted on 50 held-out speaker profiles from a real call-centre deployment show that x-vector conditioning combined with two-pass decoding reduces word error rate by 11.8% relative compared with the unadapted baseline using only 60 seconds of unlabelled target-speaker audio. We discuss practical deployment constraints—latency, memory footprint, and privacy—that influence the choice of adaptation method in production systems.

title: Noise robustness benchmarks for South Slavic speech recognition: a comparative study
abstract: Despite the linguistic proximity of the South Slavic language cluster, automatic speech recognition systems for these languages have been evaluated on inconsistent benchmarks, making cross-language comparison difficult. This paper introduces a unified noise robustness benchmark suite covering Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian, comprising read speech, spontaneous speech, and telephone-channel recordings, each degraded with eight standardised noise types at five SNR levels. We evaluate five published ASR systems for each language under identical conditions and report word error rates alongside a newly proposed noise-robustness index (NRI) that summarises performance across conditions in a single comparable scalar. Results reveal that Serbian models lag Croatian counterparts by 4–7 absolute WER points on noisy telephone conditions, largely attributable to corpus size differences. The benchmark suite and evaluation scripts are released openly, and we propose a shared task at the next relevant workshop to stimulate community participation in improving robustness for all three languages.

title: Prosody modelling for expressive Serbian speech synthesis
abstract: Monotone prosody is a well-documented limitation of neural text-to-speech systems trained on neutral read speech, and Serbian is no exception. This paper investigates explicit prosody modelling techniques aimed at producing more natural-sounding Serbian synthesis. We propose a hierarchical prosody encoder that operates at word, phrase, and utterance level, extracting latent pitch and energy representations from reference audio at training time and predicting them from text alone at inference. The model is trained on the same 20-hour corpus used in our prior TTS work, supplemented with 3 hours of expressive radio-broadcast speech to enrich prosodic variety. Subjective evaluation via a 5-point naturalness test with 55 Serbian listeners shows a mean opinion score of 4.18, an improvement of 0.17 over the baseline flat-prosody system. Acoustic analysis confirms that the proposed model reproduces interrogative and emphatic intonation patterns with significantly higher fidelity. We release model checkpoints and audio samples alongside the paper.

title: Speech technology for interactive voice response systems: lessons from deploying Serbian ASR and TTS in a call-centre environment
abstract: Interactive voice response (IVR) systems are among the most commercially significant applications of speech technology, yet practical accounts of deploying such systems for morphologically complex languages like Serbian remain scarce in the academic literature. This book chapter describes the architectural and linguistic engineering decisions made during the 2018–2021 deployment of a Serbian-language speech pipeline within a commercial call-centre product. We discuss corpus collection under operational constraints, the iterative design of the pronunciation lexicon and language model for the telephony domain, acoustic model training and re-training schedules triggered by production feedback, and the integration of a neural TTS component for dynamic prompt generation. Key challenges including dialectal variation, spontaneous disfluencies, and DTMF interference are examined alongside the practical solutions adopted. The chapter concludes with a retrospective analysis of performance metrics tracked over three years of live deployment and identifies open research problems that motivated subsequent academic work by the authors.

title: Moisture Uptake Kinetics and Dimensional Change in Polyamide 6 and Polyamide 66 Under Saturated Humidity Conditions
abstract: This study characterises the moisture absorption behaviour of injection-moulded polyamide 6 (PA6) and polyamide 66 (PA66) specimens exposed to 95% relative humidity at 37 °C over a 12-week period. Mass gain and linear dimensional change were measured at weekly intervals using a precision balance (resolution 0.01 mg) and a coordinate measuring machine (CMM) with 1 µm repeatability. PA6 reached equilibrium moisture content of 8.4 wt% by week 8, while PA66 equilibrated at 6.9 wt% by week 10. Dimensional swelling in the transverse direction reached 0.71% for PA6 and 0.54% for PA66; longitudinal swelling was approximately 40% lower in both grades, reflecting the anisotropy introduced by the injection moulding flow direction. A Fickian diffusion model provided a satisfactory fit for the early uptake phase (R² > 0.97), though deviation at long times indicated a two-stage absorption mechanism. Results provide baseline data relevant to tolerance stack-up analysis in close-fitting biomedical connector assemblies.

title: Effect of Pre-Conditioning Humidity on the Tensile Properties of Acetal Copolymer Used in Surgical Instrument Housings
abstract: Acetal copolymer (POM-C) specimens were conditioned at four relative humidity levels (30%, 50%, 75%, and 95%) at 23 °C for six weeks prior to tensile testing according to ISO 527-2. Moisture uptake in POM-C is known to be low (below 0.3 wt% at saturation), yet the study aimed to determine whether even modest humidity shifts produce statistically significant changes in tensile modulus, yield stress, and elongation at break. Results showed no significant change in modulus (variation within ±1.2%) across the humidity range. Yield stress declined by 3.1% from the dry state to the 95% RH condition. Elongation at break increased from 28% in dry specimens to 34% in the 95% RH group. These findings suggest that POM-C is a dimensionally stable alternative to polyamides for precision-fit surgical housings, though its brittleness at sub-zero temperatures remains a limitation discussed in context.

title: Fatigue Life Reduction in Conditioned Polyamide 12 Under Cyclic Tensile Loading at Physiological Temperature
abstract: Polyamide 12 (PA12) dumbbell specimens were pre-conditioned to four moisture states (dry-as-moulded, 2%, 4%, and 6% moisture content by mass) and subjected to uniaxial cyclic tensile fatigue at 37 °C, load ratio R = 0.1, and frequencies of 1 Hz and 5 Hz. S–N curves were generated for each moisture state using a minimum of 12 specimens per condition. At a peak stress of 35 MPa, fatigue life fell from 2.1 × 10⁵ cycles in the dry state to 6.4 × 10⁴ cycles at 6% moisture content, a reduction of approximately 70%. Frequency had a secondary effect; specimens tested at 5 Hz showed 8–12% shorter lives, attributed to hysteretic heating confirmed by infrared surface temperature measurements. Fracture surfaces examined by scanning electron microscopy revealed a transition from crazing-dominated failure in dry specimens to shear band-dominated failure in conditioned specimens. A two-parameter Weibull analysis of the fatigue data is presented for each condition.

title: Accelerated Ageing of PEEK in Simulated Body Fluid: Mechanical and Structural Changes Over 24 Months Equivalent
abstract: Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) specimens were aged in simulated body fluid (SBF, Kokubo formulation) at 70 °C to approximate 24 months of in-service exposure using an Arrhenius acceleration factor of 8. Tensile modulus, flexural strength, and Charpy impact energy were measured at equivalent intervals of 0, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Tensile modulus showed no statistically significant change across the ageing period (mean 3.61 GPa, standard deviation 0.09 GPa). Flexural strength declined by 6.3% at the 24-month equivalent time point. FTIR analysis indicated no new absorption bands attributable to chain scission or oxidation. Water uptake reached a plateau of 0.12 wt% after three months equivalent ageing. X-ray diffraction showed a marginal increase in crystallinity index from 32% to 35%, consistent with physical ageing of the amorphous phase. The results support the suitability of PEEK for load-bearing spinal implant components in terms of bulk mechanical stability, while flagging the surface mineralisation observed in SBF as a topic for further study.

title: Dimensional Stability of Polysulfone Connectors After Sterilisation Cycles: Steam, Ethylene Oxide, and Gamma Irradiation Compared
abstract: This paper compares the dimensional and mechanical consequences of three sterilisation methods on injection-moulded polysulfone (PSU) connector components representative of those used in extracorporeal blood circuits. Specimens were subjected to 1, 5, and 25 sterilisation cycles of each type: steam autoclave (134 °C, 3 min), ethylene oxide (EtO, 55 °C, 12 h), and gamma irradiation (25 kGy). Critical dimensions (bore diameter and wall thickness) were measured by CMM before and after each cycle set. Steam autoclaving produced the largest dimensional changes, with bore diameter increasing by 0.08 mm after 25 cycles. EtO caused negligible dimensional change but introduced measurable yellowing (ΔE* = 4.1 after 25 cycles) and a 9% reduction in Charpy notched impact strength. Gamma irradiation at 25 kGy caused a 14% reduction in elongation at break per cycle set but had minimal dimensional effect. Findings are presented as a decision matrix for sterilisation method selection.

title: Hygrothermal Stress Distribution in Polyamide 66 Snap-Fit Joints Predicted by Finite Element Analysis and Validated Experimentally
abstract: Snap-fit joints manufactured from polyamide 66 are widely used in disposable diagnostic device housings. This work develops a finite element model that incorporates moisture-dependent elastic modulus and swelling strain fields to predict the stress state in a cantilever snap-fit beam after hygroscopic loading to three moisture levels (2%, 4%, and 6% wt%). Moisture-dependent material properties were taken from a database of experimental results generated in the authors' laboratory. FEA predictions were validated against strain gauge measurements on conditioned specimens at the root of the cantilever beam. Predicted root strains agreed with measured values within 9% across all moisture conditions. The model shows that hygroscopic swelling introduces a compressive prestress at the beam root that partially offsets the tensile stress induced by snap engagement, effectively increasing the insertion force by 6–11% but reducing the risk of root cracking under repeated engagement cycles. Design charts relating moisture level to safe deflection angle are provided.

title: Creep Behaviour of Moisture-Saturated Ultrahigh-Molecular-Weight Polyethylene for Orthopaedic Bearing Applications
abstract: Compressive creep tests were performed on dry and moisture-saturated (8-week immersion in 0.9% NaCl at 37 °C) compression-moulded UHMWPE discs at stresses of 5, 10, and 15 MPa sustained for 1000 h at 37 °C. The Findley power law and a Burgers viscoelastic model were fitted to the creep compliance data. Moisture saturation increased equilibrium creep compliance at 1000 h by 18% at 10 MPa. The Findley exponent n was 0.17 for dry specimens and 0.22 for saturated specimens, indicating that moisture accelerates the time-dependent deformation response. Cross-sectional hardness (Shore D) measured on recovered specimens after creep was 3–5 units lower in saturated samples. Crystallinity measured by DSC showed no significant change after the creep test, ruling out stress-induced crystallisation as a dominant mechanism. The results are discussed in terms of acceptable dimensional tolerance loss for tibial plateau liner components under intermittent ambulatory loading.

title: Fatigue Crack Growth in Polyamide 6 Under Variable Amplitude Loading After Moisture Pre-Conditioning
abstract: Compact tension (CT) specimens machined from injection-moulded polyamide 6 plates were pre-conditioned to dry and moisture-equilibrated (8.4 wt%) states and tested under variable amplitude loading using a standardised block programme derived from ISO 12107 guidelines adapted for polymer specimens. Crack length was monitored using a direct current potential drop (DCPD) method with resolution of approximately 0.05 mm, validated against optical surface crack measurements. Fatigue crack growth rate da/dN was modelled using a modified Paris relation. The Paris coefficient C was 1.8 times higher in moisture-conditioned specimens compared with dry specimens at equivalent ΔK levels. The Paris exponent m increased from 4.1 (dry) to 5.3 (conditioned), indicating a steeper crack propagation response in the wet state. Fractographic examination showed a more diffuse damage zone in conditioned specimens, attributed to plasticisation of the polymer matrix by absorbed water. Implications for inspection interval design in reusable medical device components are discussed.

title: Influence of Glass Fibre Reinforcement on Hygroscopic Dimensional Change and Fatigue Performance of Polyamide 66 in Humid Environments
abstract: Short-glass-fibre-reinforced PA66 (30 wt% GF) is compared with unfilled PA66 with respect to moisture absorption, dimensional swelling, and fatigue life under uniaxial tension–tension cycling at R = 0.1 and 37 °C/85% RH. Moisture uptake of the reinforced grade plateaued at 3.9 wt%, compared with 7.1 wt% for unfilled PA66, under identical conditioning. Linear dimensional swelling at saturation was reduced by approximately 55% in the reinforced grade. S–N data collected at four stress levels (25, 35, 45, and 55 MPa) showed that reinforcement increased the number of cycles to failure by a factor of 2.3–4.1, depending on stress level and moisture state. Fibre–matrix debonding observed by SEM in conditioned reinforced specimens confirmed that moisture degrades the interface, partially offsetting the bulk mechanical benefit of reinforcement. An interaction factor quantifying the combined effect of humidity and fibre content on fatigue limit is proposed based on linear regression of the full dataset.

title: Comparison of Accelerated Ageing Protocols for Assessing Fatigue Life of Thermoplastic Polyurethane in Catheter Tubing
abstract: Three accelerated ageing protocols for thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) catheter tubing segments are compared: elevated temperature immersion (70 °C in phosphate-buffered saline), combined UV/humidity exposure (UVA, 0.76 W/m², 50% RH), and real-time ageing at 23 °C/50% RH over 52 weeks. Fatigue life under cyclic bending (displacement-controlled, 1 Hz, 180° bend radius) was measured for each protocol at nominal ageing equivalents of 6, 12, 24, and 52 weeks. The elevated temperature protocol was the most aggressive: fatigue life after 24-week equivalent ageing dropped to 42% of the initial value. Molecular weight (GPC), hardness (Shore A), and elongation at break were measured alongside fatigue data. Arrhenius correlation between the 70 °C and 23 °C datasets yielded an activation energy of 84 kJ/mol, within the range expected for hydrolytic degradation of polyester-based TPU. The UV/humidity protocol produced divergent results not predictable from the thermal model, suggesting a different degradation mechanism relevant only to external device surfaces.

title: Dimensional Tolerance Loss in Polyetherimide Components During Long-Term Storage in Humidity-Controlled Packaging
abstract: Polyetherimide (PEI) is used in precision-fit diagnostic device components where dimensional tolerances of ±0.02 mm or tighter are required. This work tracks dimensional changes in injection-moulded PEI discs and pins stored in sealed packaging at three relative humidity levels (30%, 60%, and 90%) over 18 months. CMM measurements at six-month intervals show that at 90% RH, average diameter growth reached 0.015 mm after 18 months, representing 75% of the maximum allowable tolerance. Moisture uptake at 90% RH reached 1.2 wt%, consistent with literature values for unfilled PEI. Specimens stored at 30% RH showed negligible dimensional change (<0.003 mm). A linear predictive model relating absorbed moisture to dimensional deviation, validated against independent specimens, is presented with 95% confidence intervals. The study provides evidence to support the use of desiccant packaging with a humidity indicator below 40% RH for long shelf-life storage of PEI diagnostic components.

title: Multiaxial Fatigue of Moisture-Conditioned Polypropylene Copolymer Used in Infusion Pump Housings
abstract: Impact-modified polypropylene copolymer specimens were conditioned to two moisture states (dry-as-moulded and 0.25 wt% equilibrium moisture at 85% RH, 23 °C) and subjected to multiaxial fatigue loading using a biaxial test fixture applying simultaneous axial and torsional cyclic loads at R = 0.1 and 1 Hz. Tests were conducted at 23 °C and 37 °C. The von Mises equivalent stress criterion was evaluated against fatigue data from uniaxial reference tests. At 23 °C, the criterion predicted biaxial fatigue life within ±15% for dry specimens. At 37 °C and wet conditions, predictions were non-conservative by up to 35%, indicating that the combined effect of temperature and moisture on multiaxial damage accumulation is not captured by a simple equivalent stress approach. A modified criterion incorporating a moisture reduction factor fitted empirically from the dataset is proposed. Fractographic analysis showed corner crack initiation at surface injection gate marks in all specimens.

title: Characterisation of Fatigue Behaviour of Additively Manufactured Polyamide 12 Components After Cyclic Moisture Exposure
abstract: Selective laser sintered (SLS) polyamide 12 specimens were subjected to 10 repeated cycles of moisture absorption (95% RH, 37 °C, 7 days) and desorption (23 °C, 50% RH, 7 days) prior to fatigue testing. A control group was tested in the dry-as-built condition. Tension–tension fatigue tests (R = 0.1, 1 Hz, 37 °C) were performed. The cyclic hygroscopic treatment reduced fatigue life at 40 MPa by 38% compared with the dry control group. Micro-CT imaging performed before and after the hygroscopic cycling revealed enlargement of interlayer porosity, with mean pore diameter increasing from 48 µm to 67 µm. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) showed a reduction in storage modulus of 12% and an increase in the loss tangent peak area of 18% after hygroscopic cycling, indicating increased viscoelastic energy dissipation per cycle. The findings are relevant to the growing use of SLS-printed PA12 in patient-specific surgical guides and low-load orthopaedic ancillaries.

title: Combined Effect of Sterilisation and Cyclic Humid Loading on the Dimensional Fidelity of PEEK Cranial Implant Prototypes
abstract: Milled and injection-moulded PEEK cranial implant prototypes of standardised test geometry were subjected to up to 50 steam sterilisation cycles (134 °C) combined with intermediate storage at 23 °C/80% RH representing the intracycle period. Dimensional measurements by industrial CT scanning (resolution 0.05 mm) were taken every 10 sterilisation cycles. Wall thickness deviation from the nominal CAD geometry remained below 0.04 mm throughout testing for both manufacturing routes. Surface roughness Ra increased by 0.18 µm per 10 cycles for milled specimens and 0.31 µm for moulded specimens, attributed to differential surface crystallisation. No statistically significant change in flexural strength was observed up to 50 cycles for either group. Moisture uptake stabilised at 0.14 wt% after the first five sterilisation cycles. The results indicate that dimensional integrity is maintained over a clinically relevant sterilisation lifetime, though the surface roughness increase in moulded specimens warrants monitoring in implants where osseointegration surface texture is a design parameter.

title: Prediction of Residual Fatigue Life in Humidity-Aged Engineering Polymers Using Dynamic Mechanical Analysis Signatures: A Screening Approach
abstract: This paper investigates whether DMA measurements—specifically storage modulus E′, loss modulus E″, and the loss tangent tan δ recorded at 1, 10, and 100 Hz—can serve as rapid non-destructive predictors of residual fatigue life in humidity-aged polymer specimens without performing full fatigue tests. Four materials were studied: PA6, PA66-GF30, POM-C, and PEEK, each aged at 85% RH and 37 °C for 0, 4, 8, 16, and 32 weeks. DMA signatures were correlated with fatigue lives measured at a fixed stress amplitude of 40% of the tensile strength for each material–ageing combination (n = 8 per data point). For PA6 and PA66-GF30, tan δ at 1 Hz showed the strongest correlation with residual fatigue life (Pearson r = −0.91 and −0.87 respectively). POM-C and PEEK showed weaker correlations (r = −0.61 and −0.54), consistent with their low moisture uptake limiting the DMA-detectable change. A simple regression-based screening criterion using tan δ thresholds is proposed and its applicability limits are discussed.

title: Hydrogen permeation through AISI 316L in the presence of SRB biofilm: implications for hydrogen embrittlement
abstract: The hydrogen permeation flux through AISI 316L membranes (thickness 0.5 mm) was measured using a modified Devanathan–Stachurski cell under SRB biofilm conditions. Membranes were exposed on the charging side to actively growing Desulfovibrio desulfuricans cultures in synthetic water at 150 mg/L Cl⁻ and 100 mg/L SO₄²⁻. Steady-state hydrogen permeation current density reached 0.18 µA/cm² in biofilm-covered membranes, compared to 0.04 µA/cm² in sterile controls under identical ionic conditions. Diffusion coefficients calculated from the time-lag method were 1.9 × 10⁻¹² m²/s and 2.3 × 10⁻¹² m²/s for biofilm and sterile conditions respectively, suggesting that the passive film rather than bulk diffusion limits hydrogen entry. Slow strain rate tests on pre-charged specimens showed a 12% reduction in reduction of area relative to uncharged controls. The data indicate that hydrogen embrittlement risk, though generally low for 316L, is measurably elevated in chronic MIC exposure scenarios.

title: Moisture sorption isotherms of hemp shiv at temperatures between 10 °C and 40 °C
abstract: Hemp shiv is widely used as the aggregate phase in bio-based building composites, yet its equilibrium moisture content across a broad temperature range is rarely reported with sufficient resolution. This study measured adsorption and desorption isotherms of industrial hemp shiv at 10, 23, and 40 °C using a gravimetric dynamic vapour sorption analyser over the relative humidity range 5–95 %. Samples were conditioned at each step until mass drift fell below 0.002 % per minute. The resulting datasets were fitted with the Guggenheim–Anderson–de Boer (GAB) model; the monolayer moisture content decreased from 6.1 % at 10 °C to 4.7 % at 40 °C, while the sorption hysteresis loop narrowed with increasing temperature. The temperature dependence of the GAB parameters was expressed through Arrhenius-type relations, enabling interpolation for intermediate conditions. These data are intended as material-level inputs for whole-building hygrothermal simulation tools such as WUFI and DELPHIN. The study also quantified the influence of particle size fraction (2–4 mm versus 4–8 mm) and found no statistically significant effect on equilibrium moisture content, though the rate of approach to equilibrium was faster for finer particles.

title: Activation energy of zeta-phase growth in batch hot-dip galvanizing of low-silicon structural steel
abstract: The growth kinetics of the Fe–Zn zeta (FeZn13) phase were investigated for low-silicon structural steels (Si < 0.04 wt.%) galvanized at bath temperatures between 440 °C and 480 °C with immersion times of 1 to 12 minutes. Coating thickness was measured by cross-sectional metallography on polished specimens and quantified using image analysis software. The activation energy for zeta-phase thickening was determined by fitting thickness-versus-time data to a parabolic growth law, yielding a value of 48 ± 3 kJ/mol, consistent with diffusion-controlled growth. Phase identification was confirmed by X-ray diffraction on separated layer fragments. Bath temperature had a stronger effect on total coating thickness than immersion time in the ranges studied. Results provide a baseline dataset for comparison with reactive silicon steels and for validation of thermodynamic diffusion simulations performed using the CALPHAD approach.

title: Friction Behaviour of Phosphate-Coated Steel Surfaces in Mineral Oil Containing Quartz Microparticles
abstract: This study examined the friction and wear characteristics of phosphate-coated low-alloy steel discs sliding against hardened steel pins in a mineral oil lubricant deliberately contaminated with quartz particles of 10–50 µm diameter at concentrations of 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 g/L. Pin-on-disc tests were conducted at sliding speeds of 0.05–0.3 m/s and normal loads of 5–30 N. Friction coefficients were measured continuously and worn surfaces were examined by scanning electron microscopy and profilometry. Phosphate coatings with a layer thickness of approximately 8 µm reduced the running-in friction coefficient by 22% compared with uncoated specimens at 0.5 g/L particle concentration, but this advantage diminished at concentrations above 0.8 g/L, where abrasive cutting became the dominant wear mechanism. Mass loss rates followed a power-law dependence on particle concentration with an exponent of 1.34. The results suggest that phosphate treatments are suitable for moderate contamination levels but require supplementary surface hardening for heavily loaded circuits.

title: Effect of Surface Roughness Parameters on Slurry Erosion Rate in Stainless Steel Nozzle Inserts
abstract: Slurry erosion tests were performed on AISI 316L stainless steel nozzle insert specimens with five distinct surface finish conditions, ranging from Ra 0.1 µm (mirror-polished) to Ra 1.8 µm (ground), using a recirculating slurry rig with 150-µm alumina particles at 3 m/s impingement velocity and 2 wt% solid concentration. Erosion rates were determined gravimetrically after 4, 8, and 12 h of exposure. White-light interferometry was used to track surface evolution at three measurement intervals. Smoother surfaces showed lower initial erosion rates but reached a steady-state mass loss 18% higher than mid-range roughness specimens (Ra 0.4–0.6 µm), suggesting that a moderate surface microtexture retains a thin lubricant film that attenuates particle impact. SEM cross-sections revealed that the dominant erosion mode on polished surfaces shifted from plastic indentation to micro-cutting after 8 h. Implications for the selection of finishing parameters in precision valve seats are discussed.

title: Wettability Modification of Hardened Tool Steel by Femtosecond Laser Surface Texturing
abstract: Femtosecond laser pulses (800 nm wavelength, 120 fs pulse duration, 1 kHz repetition rate) were applied to H13 tool steel substrates to produce four regular texture geometries: parallel grooves, crossed grooves, dimple arrays, and pillar arrays, each at two spatial periods (50 µm and 100 µm). Static and dynamic contact angles with distilled water and with ISO VG 46 hydraulic oil were measured before and after texturing. All textures reduced the water contact angle relative to the polished reference, except the pillar array at 50-µm period, which yielded a superhydrophobic response (contact angle 152°) due to air entrapment in re-entrant cavities. Oil spreading was accelerated on all textured surfaces. Subsequent ageing tests in a humid chamber for 30 days showed that pillar arrays retained hydrophobicity within ±4° of the initial value, while grooved geometries degraded by up to 28°. The study provides geometry selection criteria for valve-spool surfaces intended to resist water ingress in hydraulic systems.

title: Comparative Wear Performance of DLC and CrN PVD Coatings on Hydraulic Pump Pistons Operating in Contaminated Bio-Oil
abstract: Diamond-like carbon (DLC, a-C:H type, 2.8 µm thick) and chromium nitride (CrN, 3.1 µm thick) coatings deposited by magnetron sputtering were evaluated on axial-piston pump slipper pads running against a hardened steel swashplate in a fully formulated bio-based ester lubricant (ISO VG 46 equivalent) contaminated with 20-µm steel particles at 500 mg/L. Tests ran for 200 h at 250 bar and 1450 rpm. DLC-coated pads lost 31% less volume than CrN pads over the full test duration, but DLC adhesion failure was observed on three of six specimens after 150 h in the presence of water contamination (0.1 vol%). Friction coefficients for DLC averaged 0.06 versus 0.11 for CrN during steady-state operation. The findings indicate that adhesion of DLC to steel substrates must be improved via an interlayer before deployment in bio-oils that may absorb moisture.

title: Tribological Properties of PTFE-Based Composite Coatings on Aluminium Alloy Valve Bodies
abstract: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) composite coatings reinforced with 5, 10, and 15 vol% micro-scale MoS2 filler were sprayed onto AA6061-T6 aluminium substrates and cured at 380 °C. Dry sliding tests on a ball-on-flat tribometer (6-mm Si3N4 ball, 10 N load, 50 mm/s, 10 000 cycles) and boundary-lubricated tests using kerosene with 100 mg/L calcium carbonate particles (2–8 µm) were conducted. Coating hardness ranged from 0.28 GPa (0 vol% MoS2) to 0.41 GPa (15 vol%), measured by nanoindentation. In dry sliding, the 10 vol% composition gave the lowest specific wear rate (1.4 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/N·m). In particle-laden kerosene, all PTFE composites outperformed an uncoated aluminium reference by a factor of 4–7 in volume loss, with the 10 vol% formulation again optimal. Surface analysis by EDX confirmed MoS2 transfer to the counterface at all tested compositions.

title: Influence of Silane Coupling Agent Chain Length on the Hydrophobicity and Adhesion of Fluoropolymer Coatings on 316L Steel
abstract: Four perfluoroalkylsilane coupling agents with chain lengths of C4, C8, C12, and C18 were used as adhesion-promoting interlayers between AISI 316L stainless steel substrates and a spin-coated fluoropolymer topcoat (Dynoflex FP-22). Static water contact angles, roll-off angles, and peel adhesion (90° peel test) were measured before and after 500 h immersion in ISO VG 32 hydraulic oil at 60 °C and after 200 thermal cycles (−20 °C to 80 °C). The C12 silane gave the best balance: static contact angle 148°, roll-off angle 6°, and peel adhesion 4.2 N/mm, compared with the highest adhesion from C4 silane (5.9 N/mm) but at a static contact angle of only 118°. Immersion in hydraulic oil caused contact-angle reductions of 8–14° across all samples, while thermal cycling had a smaller effect (≤5°). The C12 interlayer is recommended for steel fluid-handling parts requiring persistent hydrophobicity in oil-immersed conditions.

title: Erosion-Resistant Hybrid Coatings for Micro-Dosing Pump Components: A Review of Physical and Chemical Deposition Routes
abstract: This chapter reviews experimental and applied literature from 2005 to 2020 on coatings used to extend the service life of micro-dosing pump heads and check valves operating in pharmaceutical and chemical process environments where dosing fluids carry fine precipitate particles. Deposition methods covered include magnetron sputtering, plasma-assisted CVD, sol-gel processing, and electrophoretic deposition. For each method, coating microstructure, typical thickness range, hardness, adhesion, and erosion resistance data reported in the literature are tabulated. Particular attention is paid to multi-layer architectures that combine a hard ceramic underlayer (TiN, CrN, or Al2O3) with a low-surface-energy topcoat (DLC or fluoropolymer). The chapter also discusses how wettability interacts with particle-impact erosion: surfaces with water contact angles above 130° show 15–40% lower erosion rates in aqueous slurries in several independent studies. Gaps in the literature, particularly the long-term stability of hybrid coatings under combined mechanical and chemical attack, are identified.

title: Wetting and Tribological Performance of Candle-Soot Templated Superhydrophobic Coatings on Steel Under Continuous Slurry Flow
abstract: A candle-soot templating method followed by TEOS vapour infiltration and fluorosilane functionalisation was used to produce superhydrophobic coatings (water contact angle 158 ± 2°, contact angle hysteresis 3°) on AISI 1045 steel coupons at essentially zero material cost. Coated and uncoated specimens were subjected to a continuous slurry jet (150 mg/L quartz, 40 µm median diameter, 4 m/s, 90° impingement) for 1, 3, 6, and 12 h. Gravimetric erosion measurements showed that the superhydrophobic coating reduced cumulative mass loss by 41% relative to the bare steel after 3 h, but the benefit fell to 12% after 12 h as the fractal soot structure was progressively destroyed. SEM imaging confirmed collapse of the re-entrant surface geometry after 6 h. A simple repair procedure—reapplication of fluorosilane without rebuilding the soot template—partially restored contact angle (to 141°) and reduced erosion by 24% over a subsequent 6-h test. The study sets practical durability limits for this coating class in industrial slurry environments.

title: Real-Time Monitoring of Coating Degradation in Hydraulic Metering Valves Using Embedded Thin-Film Sensors: A Feasibility Study
abstract: A feasibility study is presented for embedding piezoresistive thin-film strain gauges (NiCr, 200 nm thick, deposited by thermal evaporation) onto the outer wall of hydraulic metering valve cartridges to monitor coating integrity during service. The sensor signal is expected to shift as surface coatings wear through and the substrate modulus changes the local compliance. Finite element analysis of the cartridge under cyclic pressure (50–300 bar, 1 Hz) was used to identify four optimal sensor locations where the strain contrast between coated and uncoated states exceeded 40 µε. A laboratory prototype with DLC-coated cartridges was tested in a hydraulic circuit at 200 bar with 500 mg/L particle contamination. After 100 h, resistance drift in two of four sensors correlated with coating breakthrough confirmed by profilometry (r = 0.87). Sensor calibration drift, temperature compensation, and signal wiring in rotating or reciprocating components remain open challenges discussed in the paper.

title: Tribological Interaction Between Fluoropolymer-Coated Valve Seats and Ceramic Check-Valve Balls in Abrasive Pharmaceutical Slurries
abstract: Flat-on-ball tribological tests were conducted pairing alumina (Al2O3) ceramic balls (6 mm diameter, 1500 HV) against Dynoflex FP-22 fluoropolymer-coated AISI 316L steel seats in three model pharmaceutical slurries: microcrystalline cellulose suspension (d50 = 22 µm, 5 wt%), calcium phosphate suspension (d50 = 18 µm, 3 wt%), and kaolin suspension (d50 = 30 µm, 4 wt%). Testing parameters were 2 N normal load, 10 mm/s sliding speed, and stroke length 5 mm in reciprocating mode for 20 000 cycles. Coating wear volume was determined by white-light interferometry. The calcium phosphate slurry produced the highest coating wear rate (8.6 × 10⁻⁷ mm³/N·m), attributed to the angular particle morphology observed by SEM. The cellulose suspension gave the lowest wear rate (1.2 × 10⁻⁷ mm³/N·m). Friction coefficients remained in the range 0.04–0.09 for all three slurries throughout testing. A coating thickness of at least 18 µm is recommended to achieve a service life exceeding 5 × 10⁶ valve closure cycles under calcium phosphate conditions.

title: Effect of Substrate Pre-Treatment Temperature on the Adhesion and Microstructure of Magnetron-Sputtered TiN/DLC Bilayer Coatings for Micro-Pump Pistons
abstract: TiN interlayers (0.5 µm) followed by a-C:H DLC topcoats (2.0 µm) were deposited by unbalanced magnetron sputtering onto M2 tool steel micro-pump pistons pre-heated to 150, 250, and 350 °C prior to deposition. Cross-sectional TEM and XRD characterisation showed that substrates pre-treated at 250 °C produced a TiN columnar grain size of 12 nm and the lowest compressive residual stress in the DLC layer (−0.9 GPa versus −1.6 GPa at 150 °C). Rockwell-C indentation adhesion class was HF1 at 250 °C and HF3 at 150 °C. Micro-pump pistons coated at each pre-treatment condition were run for 500 h in a recirculating test circuit with ISO VG 22 oil and 200 mg/L of 15-µm alumina particles at 180 bar. Pistons pre-treated at 250 °C showed 28% lower diametral wear than those at 150 °C and maintained oil leakage below the manufacturer specification (≤ 0.3 mL/min) through the entire test. The 350 °C pre-treatment caused dimensional distortion of the piston geometry and is not recommended.

title: Effect of temperature and humidity conditioning on the shock absorption capacity of EPS packaging inserts
abstract: EPS pads (density 20 kg/m³, thickness 50 mm) were conditioned at four temperature–humidity combinations: 23°C/50% RH (control), 38°C/85% RH, −20°C/ambient, and 50°C/15% RH, each for 24 hours following ASTM D4169 pre-conditioning schedules. Drop testing with a 1.0 kg guided impactor from 600 mm was performed immediately after conditioning. Peak transmitted acceleration and cushion curve shifts were recorded across 20 replicate drops per condition. The 38°C/85% RH condition produced a 14% reduction in plateau stress and an 11% increase in peak transmitted acceleration relative to control. Low-temperature conditioning increased plateau stress by 9%, reducing energy absorption efficiency. A modified constitutive model incorporating temperature and moisture scaling factors is proposed and validated against the experimental data. The results suggest that distribution environment must be explicitly accounted for in cushioning qualification when routes pass through tropical or cold-chain segments.

title: Musculoskeletal disorder prevalence among electronics assembly workers in Vojvodina: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: A standardised Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire was administered to 312 assembly workers at four electronics manufacturing facilities in Vojvodina. Response rate was 84%. Twelve-month prevalence of neck/shoulder complaints was 62%, wrist/hand complaints 47%, and low-back complaints 54%. Logistic regression identified line-paced work (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.6–3.3), more than five years of tenure (OR 1.9, 95% CI 1.3–2.8), and working at a fixed-height bench (OR 1.6, 95% CI 1.1–2.3) as significant predictors of shoulder complaints. Workers using height-adjustable benches reported lower prevalence across all regions. The survey data were used to prioritise workstations for biomechanical assessment in a follow-up measurement campaign. Findings are consistent with European epidemiological literature on electronics manufacturing but provide a baseline specific to the Vojvodina manufacturing context, which differs from Western European facilities in terms of task mix and tooling age.

title: Participatory workstation redesign in a small metal-parts assembly enterprise: process, biomechanical outcomes, and lessons learned
abstract: This paper reports on a twelve-month participatory ergonomics programme conducted at a small enterprise (28 employees) producing precision metal sub-assemblies in the Novi Sad industrial zone. A joint worker–management–researcher team identified six priority workstations through a combination of Nordic Questionnaire results and direct observation. For each station, pre-intervention motion-capture sessions established baseline joint moment profiles, after which design changes were implemented through low-cost modifications: height-adjustable platforms, repositioned component containers, and angled presentation trays. Post-intervention measurements were conducted six months after implementation. Mean peak lumbar extension moments decreased by 17% across the six stations, and shoulder cumulative loading indices fell by 24%. Workers reported improvements in perceived exertion and general comfort on the NASA-TLX and Borg scales. Process documentation covers barriers encountered, including production schedule constraints and initial worker scepticism, and provides a step-by-step protocol adaptable to other small-to-medium manufacturers in the region.

title: Erosion pattern sensitivity to metering-edge radius in hydraulic proportional valves: a combined CFD and surface profilometry study
abstract: The influence of metering-edge rounding radius (0, 0.05, 0.10, and 0.20 mm) on cavitation-induced erosion patterns was examined using transient 3D simulations with the full cavitation model and subsequent surface profilometry measurements on specimens subjected to 500 hours of accelerated wear testing. CFD-derived bubble collapse energy density maps were compared with Ra and Rz roughness measurements on 12 spool specimens per edge radius. Smaller edge radii (0 and 0.05 mm) concentrated erosion within a 0.8 mm band on the downstream land face, whereas larger radii redistributed mass loss over a 2.5 mm zone with 40% lower peak roughness. Material removal rate estimates from the numerical erosion model agreed with gravimetric measurements within 12% for radii above 0.05 mm but underestimated wear for the sharp edge by 28%, suggesting that micro-jet impingement effects require sub-millimetre mesh resolution not achieved in the present study.

title: System boundary selection in LCA of batch fermentation processes: sensitivity to allocation rules and co-product handling
abstract: Life cycle assessment of fermentation-based products is sensitive to decisions made during system boundary definition and to the method chosen for handling co-products. This study examined three allocation approaches—mass-based, economic, and system expansion—applied to a hypothetical lactic acid fermentation process using glucose as feedstock. Inventory data were collected from published pilot-scale operation records and supplemented with ecoinvent 2.2 background data. The functional unit was defined as 1 kg of purified lactic acid at 90% purity. Results showed that global warming potential estimates ranged from 1.8 to 4.3 kg CO2-eq depending on the allocation method, a difference of nearly 140%. Acidification and eutrophication midpoint scores were similarly sensitive. The study provides a structured decision framework for practitioners selecting allocation procedures in ISO 14044-compliant studies, and recommends sensitivity analysis as a mandatory reporting element rather than an optional exercise.

title: Carbon footprint of citric acid production via submerged fermentation: an inventory study at industrial scale
abstract: Citric acid is one of the highest-volume fermentation chemicals globally, yet detailed cradle-to-gate LCA inventories at verified industrial scale remain sparse in the open literature. This paper reports a carbon footprint study of citric acid production using Aspergillus niger in 150 m³ stirred-tank reactors at a Central European facility. Inventory data were collected directly from plant records over a 12-month period and validated against mass balances. The functional unit was 1 tonne of anhydrous citric acid. Electricity for aeration and agitation accounted for 38% of the cradle-to-gate global warming potential of 1.62 t CO2-eq/t product. Glucose feedstock cultivation contributed a further 29%. Downstream processing, comprising filtration, ion exchange, and drying, contributed 21%. The remaining 12% arose from auxiliary chemicals. Uncertainty was quantified using Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations, yielding a 95% confidence interval of ±0.19 t CO2-eq. The results are compared with two previously published estimates and discrepancies are traced to differences in electricity grid mix assumptions.

title: LCA data quality assessment for industrial biotechnology: a review of inventory uncertainty sources
abstract: The reliability of LCA results for biotechnology products depends heavily on the quality of inventory data, which in industrial practice often combines primary plant data, literature estimates, and ecoinvent proxy data sets. This book chapter reviews and categorises uncertainty sources encountered in practice, drawing on case studies from fermentation, enzymatic synthesis, and microbial cell factory processes. The discussion covers temporal representativeness, geographic correlation of background data, technological spread between laboratory and industrial scale, and incomplete documentation of auxiliary material flows such as cleaning-in-place chemicals and filter aids. A semi-quantitative scoring procedure adapted from the Weidema and Wesnæs data quality indicator framework is proposed and demonstrated on three published industrial biotechnology LCAs. The chapter concludes with recommendations for minimum reporting standards that would facilitate meta-analysis and inter-study comparison.

title: System expansion versus substitution in LCA of biorefineries co-producing bioplastic monomers and animal feed: effects on climate and land use results
abstract: Biorefineries that simultaneously produce polyhydroxyalkanoate monomers and dried distillers' grains generate co-products requiring methodological decisions that substantially alter LCA outcomes. This study compared system expansion and two substitution variants for a model corn-based biorefinery producing 3-hydroxybutyric acid and animal feed co-product. Inventory data were compiled from three published pilot-plant datasets supplemented by ecoinvent 3.3 background data. The functional unit was 1 tonne of 3-hydroxybutyric acid monomer at 98% purity. Under system expansion, the global warming potential was –0.42 t CO2-eq/t product, indicating a net climate benefit due to animal feed credit. Under mass-based substitution the result was +0.91 t CO2-eq/t, and under economic substitution +0.55 t CO2-eq/t. Land use characterisation using the soil organic matter depletion method amplified differences further. The paper provides a structured reporting template for multi-output biorefinery LCA studies and recommends that all three approaches be disclosed in studies submitted for policy use.

title: Environmental profile of microbial biosurfactant production: LCA of a sophorolipid fermentation process at pilot scale
abstract: Sophorolipids produced by Starmerella bombicola are among the most commercially developed microbial biosurfactants, but their environmental advantages relative to petrochemical surfactants remain quantitatively uncertain. This study presents a cradle-to-gate LCA of sophorolipid production at pilot scale (500 L working volume) using rapeseed oil and glucose as co-substrates. Primary inventory data were collected over 18 experimental runs at the Faculty of Technical Sciences pilot plant. The functional unit was 1 kg sophorolipid at 85% purity with a defined hydrophilic–lipophilic balance. Global warming potential was 3.8 kg CO2-eq/kg product, dominated by rapeseed oil cultivation (51%) and electricity for aeration (28%). Comparison with a linear alkylbenzene sulfonate baseline showed a 22% reduction in global warming potential but a 3.1-fold increase in agricultural land use. The study applies EF 3.0 midpoint methodology and evaluates 16 impact categories. Sensitivity analysis revealed that the electricity grid decarbonisation trajectory to 2030 would reduce the climate advantage margin substantially.

title: Uncertainty propagation in life cycle inventory of fed-batch fermentation: a comparison of Monte Carlo and fuzzy arithmetic approaches
abstract: Quantifying uncertainty in LCA of fed-batch fermentation is complicated by the correlation structure of time-series inventory inputs such as substrate feed rates, dissolved oxygen control signals, and cooling water consumption. This methodological paper compared Monte Carlo simulation and fuzzy arithmetic as two approaches to uncertainty propagation for a gluconic acid fed-batch process. Inventory data were derived from 30 experimental runs at the Faculty pilot plant. Input distributions for Monte Carlo were fitted using maximum likelihood estimation; triangular fuzzy numbers were elicited from process engineers for the fuzzy arithmetic calculations. Global warming potential central estimates agreed within 3% between methods (2.14 vs. 2.19 kg CO2-eq/kg product), but 95% interval widths differed by a factor of 1.8, with Monte Carlo yielding narrower intervals. The paper discusses conditions under which correlation among fermentation inputs inflates Monte Carlo variance and proposes a partial rank correlation coefficient screening procedure to identify dominant uncertainty contributors prior to full simulation.

title: Hotspot identification in the LCA of a single-use bioreactor versus stainless steel system for vaccine antigen fermentation
abstract: Single-use bioreactor systems have been widely adopted in vaccine manufacturing because of reduced cleaning requirements, but their LCA profile relative to stainless steel reusable systems is context-dependent and disputed in the literature. This conference paper presents a hotspot analysis for a 200 L vaccine antigen fermentation process comparing single-use and stainless steel configurations, using primary data from a contract manufacturing collaboration and ecoinvent 3.7 background data. The functional unit was 1 batch of antigen at a specified immunogenic dose. In the single-use scenario, polypropylene bag manufacturing and incineration of contaminated plastic waste dominated, contributing 62% of global warming potential. In the stainless steel scenario, cleaning-in-place water heating and sodium hydroxide production were the largest contributors (47% combined). Under a low-carbon electricity grid, the gap between scenarios narrowed to less than 8%. The analysis identifies plastic waste end-of-life treatment and energy source as the two most actionable levers for environmental improvement.

title: Temporal dynamic LCA applied to a biogas-integrated lactic acid fermentation facility: accounting for biogenic carbon timing
abstract: Conventional attributional LCA treats biogenic carbon as climate-neutral at the point of photosynthesis, an assumption that introduces timing errors when biomass production and degradation are not synchronised within the study period. This paper applies a temporal dynamic LCA framework to a biogas-integrated lactic acid facility where corn stover is used for both fermentation feedstock and anaerobic digestion. The temporal inventory was constructed using a 100-year time horizon with annual resolution and characterised using time-differentiated global warming potential factors from the Levasseur dynamic characterisation approach. Primary data were collected from a regional biogas cooperative in Vojvodina and supplemented with fermentation inventory data from the preceding authors' studies. The dynamic global warming potential (100-year) was 0.71 kg CO2-eq/kg lactic acid compared to 0.58 kg CO2-eq/kg under static attributional LCA—a 22% underestimation in the static approach. The contribution of methane leakage from the biogas plant to the dynamic result was disproportionately large due to its short-term radiative forcing characteristics.

title: Benchmarking LCA software platforms for fermentation process modelling: a structured comparison of SimaPro, openLCA, and GaBi for industrial biotechnology applications
abstract: Practitioners in industrial biotechnology LCA frequently encounter software-specific differences in background database handling, co-product allocation routines, and uncertainty module implementations that are not fully documented in vendor literature. This paper presents a structured benchmark of three widely used LCA software platforms—SimaPro 9.4, openLCA 2.1, and GaBi 10—applied to an identical itaconic acid fermentation case study. The benchmark evaluated: background ecoinvent 3.9 data set matching, allocation module behaviour for multi-output unit processes, Monte Carlo sampling reproducibility across 5,000 iterations, and computation time for a process tree of 340 unit processes. Global warming potential results agreed within 2.1% across platforms when identical allocation settings were applied. Discrepancies up to 11.4% arose from differences in default electricity market dataset selection for Serbia and the Western Balkan region. The paper provides a decision checklist for practitioners selecting a platform for regulatory or policy-relevant LCA studies in the regional biotechnology sector.

title: Allocation Challenges in LCA of Multi-Tenant Cloud Computing Services
abstract: Multi-tenant cloud environments present significant methodological difficulties for life-cycle practitioners because physical resources are shared dynamically among clients whose workloads vary in intensity and duration. This paper systematically reviews allocation approaches—physical, economic, and system expansion—across 22 published LCA studies of cloud platforms, identifying inconsistencies that render cross-study comparisons unreliable. The authors propose a workload-hours allocation key calibrated against CPU utilisation logs, which was tested using operational telemetry from a mid-sized European cloud provider with three data centres. Applying the proposed key reduces variability in reported global warming potential per virtual machine hour by approximately 41% compared with simple physical allocation by server count. The paper further discusses how allocation choices affect ISO 14044 compliance and argues for standardised reporting requirements in forthcoming revisions of the GHG Protocol ICT Sector Guidance. Limitations include the absence of memory and storage disaggregation in the test dataset.

title: Allocation of Transmission and Distribution Losses to End-Use Categories: A Methodology for Consumer-Level Carbon Footprint Calculation
abstract: When calculating the carbon footprint of electricity consumption, distribution losses between the meter of the generating plant and the consumer meter must be allocated across consumer categories. This paper develops a loss-allocation methodology using load-profile data from four Serbian distribution areas, disaggregated into residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural categories. Hourly metered data for 2012 are combined with network impedance models to assign technical losses proportionally to instantaneous demand, while non-technical losses are allocated uniformly per kWh billed. The resulting consumer-class-specific loss coefficients range from 4.1% for large industrial consumers connected at 35 kV to 12.3% for rural low-voltage residential consumers. Multiplying these coefficients by the national attributional emission factor raises the effective Scope 2 factor for rural residential consumers by 0.089 kg CO2/kWh relative to the network-level average. The methodology is compatible with ISO 14064-1 and has been tested against metered balances for three distribution areas with a residual error below 2%.

title: Measurement and Reporting of Non-Technical Losses in GHG Inventories: Methodological Guidance
abstract: Non-technical losses (NTL) — electricity removed from the network without authorised metering — are rarely addressed in distribution utility GHG inventories, yet they affect both the accuracy of loss quantification and the question of which entity should account for the associated Scope 2 emissions. This paper reviews GHG Protocol and ISO 14064 guidance to clarify the treatment of NTL and proposes a reporting convention: the distribution company should include NTL-related losses in its own Scope 2 inventory, flagged separately, because it bears operational control over the network. A case study from a Serbian urban distribution zone quantifies NTL at 3.8% of distributed energy (2018–2020 average), contributing 2 940 t CO2e/year, which represents 6.1% of total company Scope 2 emissions. The paper also evaluates smart meter rollout as a means of NTL detection, showing that automated anomaly detection algorithms reduce NTL identification time from 18 months to under 6 weeks in a pilot zone of 4 200 meters.

title: Harmonising GHG Reporting Across Cross-Border Distribution Networks: A Methodological Framework for the Serbia–Hungary–Romania Tri-Border Region
abstract: Electricity distribution networks in the tri-border region of Serbia, Hungary, and Romania operate under three national regulatory frameworks with different mandatory emission factor definitions, different Scope 2 accounting conventions, and different requirements for SF6 leak reporting. This preprint proposes a harmonised reporting framework applicable to utilities operating cross-border interconnections or supplying loads in more than one jurisdiction. The framework adopts a dual-reporting structure: each national segment of a shared asset uses its host-country emission factor for regulatory compliance, while a consolidated group-level inventory uses market-based factors derived from a common regional dataset. The paper demonstrates the framework using a hypothetical 400 km cross-border high-voltage line with three ownership jurisdictions. Differences between jurisdictional and consolidated inventories reach up to 22% in Scope 2, primarily driven by the divergence between Hungarian (0.249 kg CO2/kWh in 2023), Romanian (0.312 kg CO2/kWh), and Serbian (0.581 kg CO2/kWh) average grid emission factors. The framework is intended as a discussion document ahead of a regional working group session.
