title: Dual isotope (δ¹³C, δ³⁷Cl) analysis of cis-1,2-dichloroethylene degradation under iron-reducing conditions
abstract: Dual-element isotope fractionation analysis combining carbon (δ¹³C) and chlorine (δ³⁷Cl) signatures was applied to trace the degradation of cis-1,2-dichloroethylene (cDCE) under iron-reducing conditions in batch microcosm experiments inoculated with sediment from a contaminated aquifer in northern Serbia. Incubations were run at 12°C for 150 days with lactate as an electron donor. Measurable cDCE degradation (>60% mass loss) was observed only after a 45-day lag phase. Carbon enrichment factors ε¹³C reached −4.1 ± 0.3‰, while chlorine enrichment factors ε³⁷Cl were −1.9 ± 0.2‰. The slope of the dual-isotope correlation (Λ = Δδ¹³C/Δδ³⁷Cl = 2.15 ± 0.12) was distinct from published values for aerobic oxidation (Λ ≈ 4.8), confirming reductive pathways. Hydrogen isotope measurements were precluded by low analyte concentrations. The results support the use of dual-isotope plots to discriminate degradation mechanisms at mixed-process sites where both reducing and oxidizing conditions coexist at different depths.
venue: Isotope Geochemistry and Environmental Tracing

title: Comparative evaluation of spatial indexing strategies for polygon-heavy cadastral datasets in PostgreSQL/PostGIS
abstract: Cadastral databases in Serbian municipalities routinely contain several million polygon features with highly irregular geometries. This paper benchmarks four spatial indexing approaches—standard GiST R-tree, BRIN spatial indexing, space-partitioning grids, and a hybrid block-clustered GiST—against a 4.2-million-parcel extract from the Republic Geodetic Authority. Query response times were measured across six spatial query types (bounding-box, point-in-polygon, distance, k-nearest-neighbour, clip, and overlay) at three database server configurations ranging from 32 GB to 128 GB RAM. The hybrid block-clustered GiST reduced median bounding-box query time by 38 % relative to default GiST on the largest configuration, while BRIN performed poorly for non-sequential polygon data. Results suggest that clustering geometry storage to match the dominant tile access pattern yields the most consistent gains across query types. The experimental dataset and SQL scripts are made publicly available.

title: Tile generation throughput for national-scale land-parcel vector data: a pipeline comparison
abstract: Delivering cadastral vector data over the web at scales from 1:500 000 down to 1:500 requires efficient pre-rendering or on-the-fly tile generation. This study compares three pipeline architectures—pre-rendered MVT tiles generated by Tippecanoe, on-the-fly GeoServer WMS with PNG delivery, and a hybrid partial-prerender approach—using a 6.8-million-feature land-parcel dataset covering the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina. Tile request latency, server CPU load, and storage footprint were logged over 72-hour simulated usage sessions with concurrent request loads of 10, 50, and 200 users. Pre-rendered MVT tiles achieved the lowest latency (median 42 ms at 200 concurrent users) but consumed 18 GB of storage per zoom level range, while the hybrid approach reduced storage by 61 % with a latency penalty of 120 ms at peak load. Recommendations for cache invalidation frequency are derived from the empirical data.

title: Geometry simplification thresholds for cadastral polygons across zoom levels in web map delivery
abstract: Automatic geometry simplification is central to multi-scale web map delivery, yet inappropriate tolerance settings introduce topological errors and visible artefacts in cadastral data where shared parcel boundaries must remain coincident after simplification. This paper tests five simplification algorithms—Douglas–Peucker, Visvalingam–Whyatt, topology-preserving Visvalingam, Rapson–Lang, and a custom skeleton-guided approach—applied to 340 000 parcels from two Vojvodina municipalities at zoom levels 10 through 18. Correctness metrics include sliver polygon count, T-intersection break count, and parcel area deviation. The topology-preserving Visvalingam algorithm produced the fewest sliver polygons (fewer than 0.3 % of features affected) across all tested zoom levels and is recommended as a baseline for cadastral tilesets. A lookup table of tolerance values per zoom level per algorithm is provided as supplementary data.

title: Partitioning strategies for distributed PostGIS clusters serving high-concurrency cadastral tile requests
abstract: As public cadastral web portals in the Western Balkans experience growing concurrent user loads, single-node PostGIS deployments reach performance ceilings. This work investigates three table partitioning strategies—range partitioning by municipality code, hash partitioning by parcel identifier, and spatial grid partitioning using a fixed 10 km × 10 km tile grid—on a Citus-managed distributed PostGIS cluster with four worker nodes. A synthetic workload of 500 concurrent tile requests, derived from real access logs of a Serbian cadastral portal, was replayed against each configuration. Spatial grid partitioning achieved the highest throughput (1 340 tiles/s) and lowest 95th-percentile latency (310 ms) under peak load, owing to colocation of spatially adjacent parcels on the same worker node. Range partitioning by municipality performed well for administrative boundary queries but poorly for cross-boundary tile fetches. Practical guidelines for re-partitioning live databases are discussed.

title: Encoding efficiency and decode performance of Mapbox Vector Tiles versus GeoJSON for large cadastral feature collections
abstract: The choice of vector tile encoding format affects both network payload size and client-side rendering speed in browser-based web GIS applications. This study compares Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT) protocol buffer encoding against GeoJSON for datasets of 10 000, 100 000, and 1 000 000 cadastral features at zoom levels 12–17. Payload sizes, client decode times on three hardware profiles, and frame rates during pan and zoom operations were recorded using instrumented Mapbox GL JS and Leaflet clients. MVT encoding reduced payload size by 74–81 % relative to GeoJSON across all dataset sizes. Decode time on a mid-range laptop CPU averaged 18 ms per tile for MVT versus 67 ms for GeoJSON at the 100 000-feature scale. The paper also analyses precision loss introduced by MVT's integer coordinate encoding at high zoom levels and its implications for sub-metre cadastral accuracy requirements.

title: Automated detection of topological inconsistencies in cadastral vector datasets prior to tile publication
abstract: Cadastral datasets exported from legacy land information systems frequently contain topological errors—gaps, overlaps, and duplicate geometries—that produce visible artefacts in rendered tiles and corrupt spatial query results. This paper presents a preprocessing workflow implemented in Python using Shapely and PostGIS that automatically detects and classifies four error types across an input dataset, then proposes deterministic repair operations for each class. The workflow was validated on datasets from three municipalities in Vojvodina totalling 1.1 million parcels. Detection recall reached 97.2 % for gaps wider than 0.05 m and 94.8 % for overlapping polygons, measured against a manually labelled ground truth of 4 800 known errors. Automated repair reduced residual error count by 88 % without manual intervention. Processing time scaled roughly linearly with feature count at 2.1 million features per hour on a 16-core server. Integration with a GeoServer publication pipeline is demonstrated.

title: Cache invalidation policies for dynamic cadastral tile servers: frequency, scope, and consistency trade-offs
abstract: Cadastral data changes continuously as parcels are split, merged, and reattributed. Tile caches that are not invalidated promptly deliver stale geometry to end users, while over-aggressive invalidation negates the performance benefit of caching. This paper analyses three cache invalidation strategies—time-to-live (TTL) expiry, event-driven invalidation triggered by database write operations, and a spatial-scope invalidation that purges only tiles intersecting the changed geometry—using a simulated change stream derived from six months of real update logs from a Vojvodina cadastral office. Spatial-scope invalidation reduced unnecessary tile regeneration by 64 % compared with full-cache TTL while maintaining geometric freshness within one hour of the triggering update for 98.4 % of changes. Implementation details for GeoWebCache and a custom NOTIFY-based PostgreSQL trigger mechanism are provided.

title: Spatial data infrastructures for cadastral web services in the Western Balkans: status, interoperability gaps, and alignment with INSPIRE
abstract: The INSPIRE directive mandates interoperable spatial data services across EU member states, yet Western Balkan countries preparing for accession maintain heterogeneous cadastral SDIs that vary widely in OGC compliance, coordinate reference system handling, and metadata completeness. This book chapter surveys the cadastral web service landscapes of Serbia, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro through structured questionnaires sent to national geodetic authorities and hands-on testing of published WMS and WFS endpoints against OGC compliance test suites. Nineteen of 31 tested endpoints failed at least one mandatory conformance class. Common issues include absent GetFeatureInfo implementations, inconsistent EPSG code declarations, and missing INSPIRE metadata elements. The chapter maps identified gaps to the INSPIRE Technical Guidance for Cadastral Parcels and outlines a prioritised remediation roadmap suitable for pre-accession technical assistance programmes.

title: Benchmarking vector tile rendering latency across three JavaScript mapping libraries for cadastral polygon layers
abstract: Browser-based rendering of dense cadastral polygon layers in MVT format places different demands on client-side JavaScript mapping libraries. This paper benchmarks Mapbox GL JS 2.x, MapLibre GL JS 3.x, and OpenLayers 7 for rendering cadastral tile layers at zoom levels 12–17 using a standardised test dataset of 50 000, 200 000, and 800 000 parcels, delivered from an identical GeoServer backend. Metrics include first-tile-render latency, time-to-full-tile-coverage, pan animation frame rate, and memory consumption, measured on four browser/OS combinations. MapLibre GL JS produced the highest sustained frame rate (58 fps median at 200 000 features on Chrome/Windows) and lowest memory usage. OpenLayers exhibited lower initial latency for small feature counts but degraded sharply beyond 200 000 simultaneous visible features. Practical styling considerations for cadastral label placement are also discussed.

title: Incremental tile pyramid update strategies for near-real-time cadastral change publication
abstract: Pre-rendered tile pyramids for cadastral datasets must be updated whenever parcel boundaries or attributes change, but full pyramid regeneration is computationally prohibitive for national-scale datasets updated multiple times daily. This paper presents and evaluates three incremental update strategies: bounding-box-scoped re-render, affected-tile-graph propagation, and a dirty-tile queue fed by PostGIS triggers. Experiments used a simulated change stream of 3 000 daily updates applied to a 5-million-feature Vojvodina cadastral dataset across zoom levels 10–18. The dirty-tile queue strategy processed 3 000 daily changes with a mean update latency of 4.2 minutes and a peak server load of 34 % on a four-core tile rendering worker, compared with 47 minutes and 91 % load for full regeneration. The paper also quantifies the trade-off between queue flush frequency and visual freshness.

title: Combining road-network constraints and parcel shape descriptors for zoom-adaptive label placement on cadastral web maps
abstract: Automatic label placement for cadastral parcel identifiers on web maps must adapt to changing parcel visibility, label density, and competing road-network annotations across zoom levels. This paper proposes a placement algorithm that uses parcel pole-of-inaccessibility positions, elongation ratio, and proximity to road centrelines to assign label anchors stored as pre-computed attributes in the PostGIS tile source. The algorithm was applied to 780 000 parcels in a three-municipality test area and evaluated against 14 000 manually assessed label placements by domain experts. Agreement rate reached 83 % at zoom level 15 and 76 % at zoom level 13 where parcel–road conflicts are most common. Label density management through cluster suppression at small scales is also detailed, with SVG rendering examples generated via MapLibre GL JS style specifications.

title: PostgreSQL 15 parallel query execution for spatial aggregate operations on cadastral datasets: measured gains and edge cases
abstract: PostgreSQL 15 expanded parallel query support for several spatial aggregate functions when used with PostGIS 3.3. This paper measures the performance impact of parallel execution on six spatial aggregate query types—area sum, unary union, convex hull, centroid array, spatial join count, and spatial clip aggregate—applied to a 6.1-million-parcel cadastral dataset at different parallelism degrees (1, 2, 4, and 8 workers). Area sum and centroid array showed near-linear scaling up to 8 workers (7.4× speedup). Unary union and spatial clip aggregate showed super-linear overhead beyond 4 workers due to geometry merge costs. Edge cases involving degenerate geometries that caused worker crashes in early test runs are documented along with mitigation patches. Recommendations for max_parallel_workers_per_gather settings specific to cadastral workloads are provided.

title: Serving cadastral vector tiles from columnar storage: DuckDB-spatial as a read-optimised tile backend
abstract: Traditional PostGIS deployments are row-oriented, which limits scan throughput for the full-table reads required during tile generation. This preprint investigates DuckDB with its spatial extension as a read-optimised backend for generating MVT tiles from cadastral datasets. A 7.2-million-feature Vojvodina cadastral table was loaded into DuckDB Parquet files partitioned by a spatial grid. Tile generation throughput was measured for cold and warm runs across zoom levels 10–17 and compared with equivalent PostGIS 3.4 pipelines. DuckDB achieved 2.1–3.8× higher throughput for full-zoom-level batch generation due to columnar projection pushdown, but showed 40 % higher latency for single-tile on-the-fly requests owing to Parquet file open overhead. The findings suggest DuckDB-spatial is well-suited for overnight full-pyramid rebuilds but not for interactive tile serving. A hybrid architecture using DuckDB for batch regeneration and PostGIS for on-the-fly requests is proposed.

title: First U-Th dated speleothem record from Risovača Cave, Serbia: oxygen and carbon isotope variability during MIS 5
abstract: Two stalagmites collected from Risovača Cave (central Serbia, 44.1°N, 20.6°E) were subjected to uranium-thorium (U-Th) thermal ionisation mass spectrometry dating and stable oxygen and carbon isotope analysis. Twelve U-Th age determinations constrain deposition to 128–71 ka, encompassing Marine Isotope Stage 5 (MIS 5). Stable isotope measurements (δ¹⁸O, δ¹³C) were performed at 0.5 mm resolution, generating approximately 900 data points per stalagmite. δ¹⁸O values range from −8.4‰ to −5.1‰ VPDB, with the most negative values recorded during MIS 5e (128–116 ka), interpreted as warmer and/or more humid conditions. A prominent δ¹³C excursion (+2.3‰) at approximately 107 ka correlates with a brief vegetation reduction possibly linked to a cooling episode. Initial henley tests suggest equilibrium deposition for the majority of the record. These results represent the first isotopically characterised speleothem record from this cave system and expand the spatial coverage of MIS 5 climate archives in the central Balkans.

title: Force-chain length distributions in a quasi-two-dimensional vibrated granular bed
abstract: We report measurements of force-chain length and orientation statistics in a quasi-2D granular bed of spherical glass beads (diameter 3 mm) subjected to sinusoidal vertical vibration over a frequency range of 10–40 Hz and dimensionless accelerations Γ = 1.0–4.5. A photoelastic disc technique was adapted for glass beads by embedding thin pressure-sensitive films between bead layers. Force chains were identified using a minimum-force threshold of 1.5 times the mean contact force. At Γ ≈ 2.2 we observe a crossover in the chain-length distribution from exponential to power-law tails with exponent −2.1 ± 0.1, consistent with proximity to a jamming-like transition. Chain orientation becomes increasingly anisotropic as Γ decreases below this value. Results are compared with soft-sphere discrete-element simulations performed by co-authors, showing quantitative agreement within 8% for the mean chain length. The data suggest that vibration amplitude, rather than frequency alone, controls the transition.

title: Clogging probability in a vibrated hopper as a function of outlet-to-particle diameter ratio
abstract: We systematically measured the probability of clog formation at circular hopper outlets as a function of the ratio R = D_outlet/d_particle over the range R = 2.5–6.0, for two particle types (glass spheres and irregular sand grains) and three vibration levels. Experiments used a vertical vibration table operating at 15 Hz with Γ varied from 0 to 3.0. Each (R, Γ) combination was sampled over 500 independent flow events. Clogging probability decreases monotonically with both R and Γ, but the relationship is non-monotonic in frequency: an optimal frequency near 18 Hz minimises clogging at fixed Γ. Sand grains cloak at systematically higher rates than spheres for the same R, attributed to interlocking of irregular facets. A simple logistic regression model with three parameters captures 91% of the variance in clogging probability across all conditions. Results have direct implications for the design of vibration-assisted discharge systems in powder processing.

title: Stress relaxation and creep in static granular columns subject to low-amplitude vibration
abstract: Tall granular columns confined in a cylindrical tube (diameter 60 mm, fill height 300–600 mm) were subjected to continuous low-amplitude vibration (Γ = 0.05–0.4, f = 5–25 Hz) while axial stress at the base was monitored with a load cell sampled at 1 kHz. Under quasi-static vibration, columns exhibit a logarithmic stress relaxation over timescales of 10–1000 s with a rate coefficient that depends linearly on Γ for Γ < 0.2. Above Γ ≈ 0.25, relaxation transitions to a faster power-law regime. Creep displacement measured with a linear potentiometer scales as t^0.18 in the logarithmic regime. The Janssen screening length is reduced by up to 22% relative to the static case for the highest Γ tested. These results constrain the conditions under which vibration can be used to consolidate or discharge stored granular materials without triggering bulk flow.

title: Rheological characterisation of vibrated dense granular flows in inclined channels
abstract: We measured the velocity profiles and solid-fraction distributions of granular flows in a 600 mm inclined rectangular channel (width 80 mm) while applying transverse vibration perpendicular to the flow direction. Particle image velocimetry (PIV) was applied to the transparent side wall at frame rates of 500 fps. Solid fractions were inferred from light transmission calibration. At inclination angles of 22°–32°, transverse vibration at Γ = 1.5 and f = 20 Hz increases the mean flow velocity by 35–60% compared with unvibrated controls, depending on inclination. The velocity profiles narrow and the peak shifts toward the free surface, indicating shear-band thinning. An empirical modification of the μ(I)-rheology model, incorporating a vibration-dependent effective inertial number I_vib, reproduces the measured profiles with root-mean-square errors below 4% of the channel-average velocity. The modified rheology also predicts an upper vibration amplitude beyond which fluidisation destabilises steady flow.

title: Contact force probability distributions in polydisperse granular packings near jamming
abstract: Using an instrumented force-sensor array (64 sensors on a 100 × 100 mm grid, sensitivity 0.05 N), we measured contact force distributions in static packings of binary glass-sphere mixtures (diameter ratio 1:1.5, 1:2, 1:3) over packing fractions φ = 0.58–0.64. Packings were prepared by rain deposition followed by slow compaction with a top plate, then gently tapped to approach the jamming point. The force distribution P(f) exhibits a plateau below the mean force and an exponential tail; the tail exponent β decreases from 1.8 at φ = 0.59 to 1.2 near φ_J ≈ 0.635. Polydispersity at ratio 1:2 yields the broadest distribution and the lowest β, suggesting that size heterogeneity shifts jamming. We also report the first two moments of the force distribution as functions of φ and find a power-law divergence of the variance with exponent 0.55 ± 0.04 as φ → φ_J.

title: Effect of particle shape on flow-rate fluctuations in a vibrated 2D silo
abstract: We constructed a quasi-two-dimensional silo (280 × 400 × 6 mm) to compare the flow-rate statistics of three particle shapes: circles, pentagons, and elongated ellipses (aspect ratio 1.8), all with equivalent cross-sectional area. Particles were 3D-printed from PLA. The silo was vibrated vertically at f = 10 Hz with Γ = 1.0–3.0. Flow rate was recorded by a photogate at the outlet every 0.5 s over 600 s runs. Circular particles exhibit coefficient of variation (CV) in flow rate of 9% at Γ = 2.0; pentagons show CV = 18%; ellipses show CV = 27%, with episodic clogging. Power spectral densities of flow-rate time series show a broad 1/f^α component (α = 0.8–1.4) for non-circular shapes, absent for circles. Vibration reduces CV for all shapes but does not equalise them. We conclude that shape-induced interlocking is a distinct mechanism from size-ratio clogging.

title: Vibration-induced unjamming in cohesive granular materials: role of surface moisture
abstract: Cohesive forces due to capillary bridges can promote jamming at low packing fractions in humid granular materials. We investigated unjamming by vertical vibration in glass-bead packings equilibrated at relative humidities of 20%, 50%, and 80%, using outlet diameter D = 4d_particle (a size ratio that produces frequent clogging for dry particles). At 20% RH, the critical Γ for unjamming is 1.8, consistent with dry results. At 50% RH, critical Γ rises to 2.6; at 80% RH, no sustained flow was achieved below Γ = 4.1. We measured the pull-off force between individual beads at each humidity using a micro-force tester and used these values to estimate bridge energy. A dimensionless ratio of vibration kinetic energy to bridge energy collapses the unjamming threshold data onto a single curve across all humidities. These results are relevant to pharmaceutical powder handling and food processing.

title: Granular flow under vibration: from fundamentals to industrial applications
abstract: This chapter reviews the physics of vibration-assisted granular flow with emphasis on mechanisms relevant to industrial powder handling. We cover the phenomenology of jamming and clogging in hoppers and silos, the role of force-chain statistics in mediating flow intermittency, and the experimental evidence for vibration-induced rheological transitions. Key dimensionless parameters—the vibration number Γ, the inertial number I, and the cohesion number Co—are discussed in a unified framework. We also summarise discrete-element modelling approaches and their validation against experiment. A section on industrial context reviews vibration-assisted discharge in the pharmaceutical, food, and mining sectors, identifying the gap between laboratory understanding and engineering practice. The chapter concludes with open questions: the effect of particle shape polydispersity, the coupling of thermal and mechanical fluctuations near jamming, and scale-up criteria for vibration systems.
venue: Advances in Granular Materials Science and Engineering, Vol. 4, Springer

title: High-speed imaging of arch formation and collapse in a vibrated narrow hopper
abstract: Arch formation is the microscopic precursor to macroscopic clogging. We used high-speed imaging at 5000 fps to record arch formation and spontaneous collapse events at the outlet of a quasi-2D hopper (gap width 8 mm, outlet diameter 3.5d_particle = 14 mm) during continuous vibration at 15 Hz, Γ = 0.5–2.5. From 2 400 arch events, we characterised arch morphology (number of particles, curvature, contact angle distribution) and the time-to-collapse distribution. Collapse time follows a stretched exponential distribution with shape parameter β_s ≈ 0.6, indicating a broad distribution of energy barriers. The mean collapse time decreases as exp(−αΓ) with α = 1.4 ± 0.1. Arches with four or fewer particles collapse faster than five-particle arches by a factor of 3. These observations constrain kinetic models of vibration-assisted unjamming and provide benchmark data for DEM validation.
venue: Journal of Granular Matter and Powder Technology

title: Frequency-dependent effective viscosity of vibrated granular slurries: measurements and scaling
abstract: Granular slurries—particles suspended in a viscous fluid—exhibit flow properties distinct from dry granular media. We measured the effective viscosity of glass-bead/glycerol slurries (particle volume fraction φ = 0.40–0.58, bead diameter 1.5 mm) in a parallel-plate rheometer modified with an external vibration stage applying vertical oscillation at f = 1–100 Hz, Γ = 0.2–2.0. Effective viscosity was extracted from steady-shear measurements at shear rate γ̇ = 0.1–10 s^{−1}. At φ = 0.55, vibration at f = 20 Hz and Γ = 1.0 reduces effective viscosity by 42% relative to the unvibrated case. The reduction is maximal near a characteristic frequency that scales as f* ∝ (η_fluid/ρ_particle d²)^{1/2}, consistent with a fluid-inertia mechanism. A scaling collapse of all data using a modified Stokes number is presented, with residuals below 8%. These results are relevant to concrete pumping and ceramic processing.

title: Preliminary statistics of lightning ground flash density over the Vojvodina region derived from a VLF receiver network
abstract: A two-year (2011–2012) record from a three-station VLF sferic network operated across Vojvodina is used to compile lightning ground flash density maps at 10 km × 10 km resolution. The network uses time-of-arrival and magnetic direction finding to locate return strokes; median location accuracy estimated from reference storms is 3.2 km. Annual ground flash density across the study area ranges from 0.4 to 1.9 flashes km⁻² yr⁻¹, with a maximum in the Fruška Gora orographic corridor. Monthly distributions show a June peak accounting for 28 % of annual activity. Diurnal frequency maxima occur between 14:00 and 17:00 local time. Flash multiplicity data indicate that 61 % of detected events are single-stroke. Comparison with the European EUCLID network for overlapping months yields a detection efficiency estimate of 74 %. The dataset constitutes the first locally operated flash density climatology for the province.

title: Entropy production landscape in systems of interacting active and passive particles
abstract: Mixtures of active and passive particles are increasingly used as models for cell-organelle interactions and for engineering responsive soft materials. We simulate binary mixtures of active Brownian particles and passive hard disks at total packing fractions between 0.2 and 0.6, with active fraction varied from 0.05 to 0.95. Using a path-weight estimator for steady-state entropy production, we construct a two-dimensional map of entropy production as a function of composition and Péclet number for the active species. A non-additive contribution is identified: the entropy production of the mixture exceeds the sum of single-component values by 5–35% depending on composition, and this excess peaks near equal mixture fractions. Pair correlation analysis shows that the excess coincides with maximally heterogeneous spatial arrangement. We also report that passive particles accumulate at regions of high local entropy production, a finding with potential relevance for passive sorting in active media.

title: Experimental determination of convective heat transfer coefficients in a narrow vertical air channel representative of ventilated façade cavities
abstract: Natural convection in vertical air channels is relevant to ventilated façade systems, where buoyancy-driven flow governs thermal resistance. This paper reports measurements carried out in a purpose-built channel apparatus with an aspect ratio of 20:1 and gap widths of 20, 40, and 80 mm. Air velocity profiles were recorded with hot-wire anemometry at five heights, and wall temperatures were logged with calibrated T-type thermocouples at a 50 mm pitch. Tests covered input heat fluxes from 20 to 120 W/m². Local Nusselt numbers were derived and compared with published correlations for parallel-plate channels. Results showed that existing correlations overestimated convective transfer by 8–15 % for the 20 mm gap, a discrepancy attributed to developing-flow conditions that persist over a larger fraction of channel height than assumed in those models. Revised coefficients for a modified Churchill–Usagi form are proposed and validated against an independent dataset from a second series of tests at different ambient temperatures.

title: Longwave radiation exchange between parallel surfaces of differing emissivity in a façade cavity: measurements and view-factor analysis
abstract: Although radiation is frequently treated as a secondary effect in façade cavity heat transfer, its share can exceed 40 % of total transfer at moderate temperature differences when cavity width is small. This study presents measurements from a two-surface test cell (0.6 m × 1.2 m) in which one surface emissivity was varied from 0.05 to 0.90 using interchangeable coated aluminium panels. A calibrated thermopile radiometer recorded net radiative flux between the surfaces under imposed temperature differences of 5, 10, 15, and 20 K. Measured fluxes agreed with view-factor calculations to within ±3 % for emissivity values above 0.3, but discrepancies reached 9 % for the low-emissivity case, likely because of edge reflections not accounted for in the planar model. A correction factor relating cavity aspect ratio to effective emissivity is derived and tabulated for practical use in building-energy simulation tools.

title: Thermal characterisation of a paraffin-based PCM panel intended for incorporation in lightweight external wall assemblies
abstract: Phase-change materials can reduce peak thermal loads in lightweight constructions, but their effective thermal properties under realistic boundary conditions differ from values obtained by differential scanning calorimetry alone. This paper reports the characterisation of a commercial paraffin-filled graphite matrix panel with a nominal melting range of 23–26 °C. Measurements were conducted using a custom guarded hot-box apparatus at the University of Novi Sad. Effective thermal conductivity was determined in both solid and liquid phases, yielding 0.82 W/(m·K) and 0.61 W/(m·K) respectively. Latent heat capacity measured by enthalpy-based cycling calorimetry was 162 kJ/kg. Dynamic response tests applied sinusoidal surface temperature oscillations with amplitudes of ±4 K and periods of 6, 12, and 24 hours, showing decrement factors of 0.31, 0.19, and 0.11. Results provide input data directly usable in one-dimensional transient wall models without further calibration.

title: Coupled natural convection and radiation in a roof-integrated air channel with PCM layer: an experimental parametric study
abstract: Roof assemblies that combine ventilated air channels with phase-change material layers represent a passive strategy for reducing summer cooling loads in continental climates. An experimental roof module (1.2 m × 2.4 m) was constructed on an outdoor test platform in Novi Sad and monitored over three consecutive summer months. The module included a 30 mm paraffin panel on the inner deck surface and a 60 mm ventilated channel above it. Air temperature, surface temperature at nine points, and air velocity at the channel inlet and outlet were sampled at 1-minute intervals. On peak days with outdoor air temperatures exceeding 36 °C, the PCM layer reduced the amplitude of heat flux entering the living space by 52 % compared with an identical reference module without PCM. The ventilation rate in the channel varied between 0.04 and 0.18 m/s under purely buoyancy-driven conditions. A grey-body radiation model accounted for 38 % of the total heat exchange within the channel during afternoon hours. Seasonal energy savings estimated from integrated flux measurements amounted to 14 kWh/m² over the monitoring period.

title: Infrared thermography for detection of convective plume structure in a full-scale wall cavity: method validation and sensitivity analysis
abstract: Infrared thermography has been used qualitatively to observe buoyancy-driven flows near surfaces, but rigorous quantitative validation against contact sensors remains sparse for building-envelope geometries. This paper documents a systematic comparison between calibrated thermographic imaging and embedded thermocouple measurements on a 2.4 m tall, 0.1 m wide vertical cavity under temperature differences ranging from 3 to 18 K. A cooled focal-plane-array camera operating in the 8–12 µm band was positioned at a fixed standoff distance. Sensitivity of surface temperature maps to emissivity uncertainty (±0.05) was evaluated through a Monte Carlo procedure with 500 realisations, yielding an average surface temperature uncertainty of ±0.4 K across the test range. Agreement with thermocouple readings was within ±0.6 K for 94 % of measurement points. The validated setup was subsequently used to map convective plume development at the leading edge of the heated surface, confirming a 120 mm hydrodynamic entry length not resolved in earlier contact-sensor studies.

title: Thermal mass and phase-change material strategies for peak load attenuation in residential buildings in the Pannonian climate zone: a review of measurement-based evidence
abstract: Continental climates in the Pannonian region are characterised by hot summers with afternoon peak temperatures frequently above 35 °C and cold winters, creating a dual thermal challenge for building envelopes. This book chapter reviews experimental and monitoring studies published between 2005 and 2021 that report measured data on peak load attenuation in residential construction using either conventional high-density masonry, concrete, or phase-change material inserts. Studies are classified by wall or roof assembly type, measurement instrumentation, and reported performance metric. Across 24 studies meeting inclusion criteria, PCM integrations in lightweight assemblies achieved peak flux reductions of 30–65 %, while high-density masonry reduced peaks by 20–45 % at the same U-value. The chapter identifies consistent gaps: most studies were conducted over short monitoring periods of less than one heating or cooling season, outdoor thermal boundary conditions were incompletely characterised in several cases, and inter-laboratory comparability of guarded hot-box setups remains limited. Recommendations for minimum reporting standards are formulated.

title: Radiation view-factor corrections for non-planar joint profiles in prefabricated timber-frame external wall elements
abstract: Prefabricated timber-frame panels often incorporate recessed joints and overlapping edge profiles that create small enclosed sub-cavities along their perimeter. These geometries complicate standard parallel-plane radiation estimates used in hygrothermal simulation tools. This study presents measured and analytically computed view factors for four representative joint cross-sections with cavity depths ranging from 8 to 35 mm and widths from 5 to 20 mm. A radiometric integrating sphere setup adapted for planar samples was used to measure effective emissivity of finished wood and painted surfaces. View factors were computed numerically using a ray-tracing method on meshed profiles. Comparison with the measurements showed that standard planar approximations underestimate effective radiative conductance by 12–27 % in the deepest joint geometries. Correction multipliers as a function of cavity aspect ratio are tabulated and have been incorporated into the hygrothermal simulation workflow used by a regional prefabrication manufacturer under a short-term consultancy arrangement.

title: Sequential Append Mechanisms in Relational Audit Logs: A Comparative Study of Four Yugoslav Banking Systems
abstract: This study examines the structural properties of audit log implementations across four Yugoslav savings banks operating under the 1990 Banking Act. Using direct inspection of database transaction journals maintained on IBM DB2 installations, the paper evaluates whether log records satisfy sequential append constraints and whether retroactive modification is detectable through record-count and checksum reconciliation. Data from approximately 1.4 million transaction log entries over a six-month period in 1994 were analysed. Results indicate that three of the four institutions lacked any cryptographic chaining between log entries, relying solely on sequential row identifiers that could be renumbered without detection. The fourth institution maintained a parallel paper shadow log that provided a practical tamper-evidence mechanism, albeit at significant operational cost. The paper proposes a minimal chaining schema using SHA-1 digests applied to concatenated prior-entry hashes and entry content, estimating a storage overhead of less than two percent for the observed transaction volumes. Recommendations are addressed to compliance officers and database administrators working within the regulatory framework then applicable in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

title: Immutable Record Retention Requirements and Database Log Architecture: Lessons from Early Serbian Banking Regulation
abstract: Following the introduction of the Law on Accounting and Auditing of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in 1996 and subsequent National Bank directives, commercial banks were required to retain complete transaction audit records for a minimum of ten years. This paper analyses the gap between that legal obligation and the physical log-rotation practices observed at eight Serbian commercial banks between 1997 and 1999. On-site assessments revealed that six institutions routinely purged log files after ninety days due to storage constraints, with no archival copy maintained in an integrity-verified format. The paper formalises a retention architecture built around write-once optical disc storage combined with a hash-tree index allowing point-in-time log completeness proofs. A prototype was implemented on an IBM AS/400 platform using a custom RPGIII module and tested against synthetic transaction streams of up to 50,000 records per day. Completeness verification queries ran within four seconds on a 500,000-record archive segment. The design is evaluated against both the regulatory requirements and the operational constraints typical of medium-sized Serbian banks at the time.

title: Append-Only Log Structures for Internal Audit in Insurance Companies: Design Considerations and a Field Evaluation
abstract: Insurance claim processing systems in Serbia and Hungary were surveyed to assess the practical use of append-only logging for internal compliance purposes. Structured interviews and log schema inspections were carried out at eleven companies between 2001 and 2003. The paper classifies observed logging strategies into four categories: no dedicated audit log, a mutable audit table within the operational database, a physically separate append-only file, and an externally managed archive. For each category, a set of tamper-detection tests is defined and applied, including gap analysis on sequence numbers, timestamp ordering violations, and hash-chain breaks. Only two of the eleven companies maintained logs that passed all four tests. The paper then specifies a reference architecture for append-only insurance audit logs compliant with both Serbian and Hungarian regulatory requirements as of 2003, detailing record schemas, chaining protocols, and a lightweight verification daemon implementable on standard UNIX systems. Estimated implementation cost for a mid-size insurer is calculated at approximately 45,000 DEM equivalent in staff and infrastructure.

title: Cryptographic Chaining in Database Audit Trails: Performance Trade-offs on OLTP Workloads
abstract: Adding per-record cryptographic chaining to a high-throughput OLTP database audit log introduces write latency that can affect transaction throughput. This paper reports controlled benchmark experiments conducted on a PostgreSQL 8.1 installation running on commodity server hardware, comparing four chaining strategies: no chaining, MD5 chaining in application middleware, SHA-256 chaining in a database trigger, and SHA-256 chaining in a dedicated log server receiving asynchronous replication. Workloads simulated a retail banking environment with between 200 and 1,800 transactions per second drawn from a parameterised synthetic generator calibrated against real workload traces provided by a partner institution. Results show that trigger-based chaining increases average transaction latency by 18–34 percent at 800 TPS, while the dedicated log server approach keeps latency overhead below 4 percent at the same throughput level, at the cost of a short consistency window of approximately 120 milliseconds. The paper recommends the asynchronous log server architecture for institutions processing more than 400 transactions per second, and provides configuration guidance for PostgreSQL streaming replication in this context.

title: Regulatory Drivers for Tamper-Evident Logging in the Serbian Healthcare Sector: A Policy and Technical Review
abstract: The 2005 Law on Health Records in the Republic of Serbia mandated the preservation of complete electronic patient and billing records for fifteen years, yet provided no technical specification for how immutability should be ensured. This paper reviews the regulatory text alongside implementing bylaws issued between 2005 and 2008 and compares them with equivalent provisions in EU member states including Germany, Hungary, and Austria. A gap analysis identifies six areas where the Serbian regulation is ambiguous or silent with respect to technical logging requirements. For each gap, a technically grounded recommendation is formulated drawing on the ISO 15489 records management standard and the IHE ATNA profile for audit trail and node authentication. The paper also surveys eighteen Serbian healthcare institutions through a structured questionnaire administered in 2008, finding that only three maintained logs in an append-only format and none performed routine integrity verification. A tiered compliance roadmap is proposed, prioritising changes by estimated implementation effort and regulatory risk exposure.

title: Hash-Chained Audit Logs as Legal Evidence: Admissibility and Verification Procedures in Serbian Civil Proceedings
abstract: Electronic audit logs are increasingly submitted as evidence in commercial disputes and regulatory proceedings in Serbia, yet no settled procedural standard exists for verifying their integrity before a court. This book chapter reviews twelve civil cases decided between 2004 and 2011 in which one or more parties relied on database audit logs, drawing on published court decisions and unpublished case files accessed with the consent of the parties. Three recurring evidentiary problems are identified: absence of an expert-accessible verification procedure, lack of documentation of the chaining algorithm used, and failure to preserve the verification keys or seed values needed to reproduce the chain. The chapter proposes a standardised log certification package that would accompany any hash-chained audit log intended for legal use, including algorithm documentation, a verification script, chain-head timestamps notarised at the time of production, and a chain of custody declaration. Procedural recommendations are addressed to notaries, court-appointed IT experts, and database administrators at regulated institutions. The proposals are aligned with the then-current Serbian Law on Electronic Documents.

title: Column-Store Implementations of Append-Only Audit Tables: Storage Efficiency and Query Performance for Compliance Reporting
abstract: Append-only audit tables in regulated financial institutions accumulate very large volumes of narrow, uniform records that are written once and subsequently read mainly for sequential range scans during compliance reporting and forensic investigations. This profile matches the characteristics that column-oriented storage engines are designed to exploit. The paper evaluates three open-source column-store systems—Vertica Community Edition, MonetDB, and an early release of Apache Parquet-based storage accessed through Impala—against a row-store baseline (PostgreSQL 9.2) using a synthetic audit log dataset of 800 million records derived from anonymised banking log structures. Metrics measured include bulk load time, storage footprint, sequential range scan latency, and integrity-verification scan throughput. Column stores achieved storage reductions of 61–74 percent relative to the row-store baseline due to run-length encoding on low-cardinality status and event-type columns. Range scan latency for twelve-month compliance report queries improved by factors of 4.2 to 7.8. Recommendations are made for institutions planning to migrate legacy audit log stores to column-oriented architectures.

title: Evaluating Merkle-Tree Integrity Proofs for Incremental Log Verification in Banking Audit Systems
abstract: Periodic integrity verification of large audit logs is operationally preferable to continuous per-record verification, but a gap between verification cycles creates a window during which undetected tampering could occur. Merkle-tree structures offer a mechanism for producing compact proofs of log segment integrity that allow an auditor to verify any individual record or contiguous segment without replaying the full log. This paper describes an implementation of a Merkle-tree audit log overlay applied to an existing row-store audit database at a fictional representative Serbian commercial bank modelled on parameters drawn from publicly available National Bank of Serbia reporting data. The implementation is evaluated for proof generation time, proof size, and verifier workload across log sizes from one million to one billion records. Proof size grew logarithmically as expected, reaching 1.4 kilobytes for a billion-record log. The paper also analyses a threat model covering four classes of insider attacker—DBA, system administrator, backup operator, and compliance officer—and assesses which attack classes the Merkle-tree scheme defeats versus which require additional controls such as external notarisation.

title: Blockchain-Anchored Audit Logs for Regulated Industries: A Critical Assessment of Practical Deployability
abstract: Distributed ledger technologies have been proposed as a mechanism for providing externally verifiable, tamper-evident anchoring of enterprise audit logs. This paper assesses the practical deployability of such approaches for small and medium-sized financial institutions in Serbia, drawing on a literature review of 34 published proposals and a structured evaluation against five criteria: regulatory acceptance, operational cost, latency impact on audited systems, recoverability in case of ledger disruption, and compatibility with existing log management infrastructure. The assessment finds that public blockchain anchoring introduces confirmation latency of minutes to hours that is acceptable for daily batch log sealing but incompatible with real-time compliance monitoring requirements. Permissioned ledger approaches using a consortium of Serbian banks and the National Bank as nodes are technically more suitable but face governance and procurement obstacles. The paper concludes that Merkle-tree anchoring combined with periodic notarisation through an accredited timestamping authority remains the most deployable option under current Serbian legal and infrastructure conditions, and sketches a practical migration path for institutions already operating hash-chained logs.

title: Retention and Integrity Requirements for Audit Logs under the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act: Implications for Serbian Financial Institutions Seeking EU Market Access
abstract: The EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), applicable from January 2025, imposes explicit requirements on ICT-related log retention, integrity assurance, and audit trail completeness for financial entities operating within the EU. Serbian financial institutions maintaining correspondent relationships with EU banks or seeking authorisation to operate in EU member states face indirect exposure to these requirements. This paper analyses DORA Articles 9, 10, and 17 alongside the associated regulatory technical standards published in draft form by the European Supervisory Authorities in 2023, mapping each log-related obligation to a corresponding technical control. A self-assessment checklist of 22 control items is derived and applied in a survey of eight Serbian banks conducted in late 2023. Results show that most institutions satisfy basic retention duration requirements but only two demonstrate compliance with integrity verification frequency and independent verifiability obligations. The paper identifies the four highest-priority gaps and maps them to existing technical solutions described in prior literature, including append-only architectures and Merkle-tree verification schemes previously evaluated by the authors.
venue: Acta Oeconomica Suboticiensis

title: Pseudospectral Instability of a One-Dimensional Schrödinger-Type Operator with Complex Potential
abstract: We examine the pseudospectrum of the operator $T = -d^2/dx^2 + V(x)$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, where $V$ is a complex-valued polynomial potential of degree two with non-zero imaginary part. Using resolvent norm estimates computed via a Galerkin discretisation with piecewise-linear basis functions on a uniform grid of 800 nodes, we show that the $\varepsilon$-pseudospectrum extends far from the numerical range for values of $\varepsilon$ as small as $10^{-4}$. Structured perturbations of rank one are constructed that shift an eigenvalue by a distance exceeding ten times $\varepsilon$ in the operator norm. We compare these numerical findings with asymptotic results for the resolvent norm along lines parallel to the imaginary axis, confirming that the operator exhibits strong spectral instability characteristic of non-self-adjoint operators with non-real spectra. All computations were validated against a second discretisation based on Chebyshev collocation on a truncated interval $[-15, 15]$.
venue: Journal of Spectral Analysis and Differential Equations

title: Resolvent Norm Estimates for Sturm–Liouville Operators with Dissipative Boundary Conditions
abstract: This paper studies a regular Sturm–Liouville operator on the interval $[0,\pi]$ with a real, smooth coefficient function and dissipative boundary conditions parametrised by a complex number $\alpha$ with $\text{Im}(\alpha) > 0$. We derive explicit upper and lower bounds for the resolvent norm $\|(T - \lambda I)^{-1}\|$ for $\lambda$ in a neighbourhood of the positive real axis, using a combination of Green's function estimates and contour integration. For a specific one-parameter family of boundary conditions, we show that the resolvent norm grows at least as fast as $\text{Im}(\lambda)^{-3/2}$ as $\lambda$ approaches the real axis from above, for a sequence of real parts accumulating at the eigenvalues. Numerical confirmation is provided via MATLAB computations on a grid of $10^4$ spectral parameter values. The results extend an earlier theorem of Marletta and Tretter to the dissipative boundary case.
venue: Proceedings of the Regional Workshop on Operator Theory and Applications, Novi Sad

title: Numerical Range and Pseudospectrum of a Discretised Transport Operator
abstract: Spectral properties of discretisations of the one-way transport operator $Tu = -u'$ on $[0,1]$ with an inflow boundary condition are studied as the mesh parameter $h \to 0$. We compute the numerical range and $\varepsilon$-pseudospectrum for upwind finite-difference matrices of sizes $N = 50, 100, 200, 500$, and $1000$, and track their behaviour relative to the continuous spectrum of the operator. The $\varepsilon$-pseudospectrum of the matrix sequence is shown numerically to converge, in the Hausdorff sense, to the $\varepsilon$-pseudospectrum of the differential operator for $\varepsilon > 0$ fixed, at a rate roughly proportional to $N^{-1/2}$. We observe that even for $N = 100$ and $\varepsilon = 10^{-3}$, the pseudospectrum fills a region substantially larger than the convex hull of the eigenvalues, illustrating the failure of spectral approximation for non-normal matrices. This preprint arose from a student project and is submitted to a refereed journal.

title: Reiterated homogenisation of a second-order elliptic operator with two separated microscopic scales
abstract: We study an elliptic boundary value problem with coefficients that oscillate at two well-separated microscopic scales ε and ε², modelling a hierarchically structured composite—for instance, a woven fabric in which fibres themselves contain smaller-scale porosity. Using the method of reiterated homogenisation, we derive a three-level asymptotic expansion and identify two nested cell problems. Existence and uniqueness of solutions to both cell problems are established in suitable Sobolev spaces. The effective coefficient tensor is computed for 8 representative hierarchical geometries by solving the cell problems sequentially on separate unit cells. Convergence rates are measured numerically using a manufactured-solution technique; the rate in the energy norm is O(ε) as expected. We also show that neglecting the second microscale leads to an error in the effective conductivity of 6–22% depending on the volume fractions at each level, a range large enough to matter in practical thermal design calculations.

title: Computational homogenisation of viscoelastic fibre composites: influence of fibre arrangement on the long-time effective relaxation modulus
abstract: We apply computational homogenisation to predict the long-time effective relaxation modulus of a unidirectional fibre-reinforced composite with a viscoelastic polymer matrix described by a three-parameter Maxwell model. The study examines four fibre arrangements—square, hexagonal, random, and clustered—at a fixed volume fraction of 0.40. For each arrangement, the time-domain cell problem is solved by finite element analysis using a time-stepping scheme with 200 equal steps spanning three decades of time. The effective relaxation modulus at long times varies by up to 9% between the square and random arrangements, a difference that exceeds typical measurement uncertainty and is therefore practically significant. Clustering of fibres systematically reduces the long-time modulus compared with uniform distributions. We also show that the standard square-array unit cell, widely used for its simplicity, overestimates the long-time relaxation modulus relative to statistically isotropic random microstructures. Recommendations for choosing representative unit cells in viscoelastic homogenisation are given.
venue: European Journal of Computational Mechanics

title: Multiscale Persistent Homology for Identifying Transient Chaos in Delay-Differential Equations
abstract: Delay-differential equations (DDEs) with a single constant delay τ_d can exhibit transient chaos before settling onto a periodic attractor. Standard Lyapunov-exponent methods require very long integration times to distinguish transient from sustained chaos. We show that a persistent homology computation on a point cloud of length 2 000, taken from the transient segment alone, reliably identifies the transient chaotic phase by the presence of at least two β₁ generators with persistence above an empirically set threshold of 0.15. The Mackey–Glass equation at delay τ_d = 23 and the Wright equation at τ_d = π/2 + 0.2 serve as test cases, with 200 randomly initialised trajectories each. The topological criterion correctly identifies the chaotic transient in 188/200 Mackey–Glass and 191/200 Wright trajectories, compared with 164/200 and 172/200 for a short-time Lyapunov exponent criterion evaluated over the same segment length. False positives (periodic segments flagged as chaotic) number 4 and 3 respectively. Computation per cloud averages 3.1 seconds.
venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation

title: Particle migration and concentration profiles in oscillatory pipe flow of dense suspensions
abstract: Particle migration across streamlines was investigated in dense suspensions of polystyrene spheres (d = 210 μm, φ = 0.40–0.52) flowing through a cylindrical tube of diameter 8 mm under a sinusoidally varying pressure gradient. Oscillation frequencies ranged from 0.05 to 2 Hz and peak pressure amplitudes from 50 to 400 Pa. Concentration profiles were measured non-invasively using optical coherence tomography adapted for turbid media. At frequencies below 0.2 Hz, particles migrated toward the tube axis, consistent with the Leighton–Acrivos mechanism, reaching a centreline concentration roughly 20 % above the bulk value within 200 oscillation cycles. At frequencies above 0.8 Hz, the migration direction reversed and particles accumulated near the wall. This reversal was reproducible across three independent sample preparations. A simplified diffusive flux model with a frequency-dependent effective diffusivity captures the trend qualitatively but underestimates the reversal frequency by approximately 30 %. The data provide a benchmark for diffuse-interface suspension models.

title: Variable-order fractional diffusion equation for modelling temperature-dependent transport in cartilage
abstract: Motivated by the temperature sensitivity observed in earlier EIS experiments on liver tissue, this study formulates a variable-order fractional diffusion equation in which α depends on temperature T as α(T) = α₀ − γ(T − T₀). The equation is discretised using a second-order Crank–Nicolson-type scheme on a 1D spatial grid. Gadolinium-enhanced MRI experiments on six ex vivo bovine cartilage plugs at temperatures of 10, 20, 30, and 37 °C were used to calibrate the model. The fitted parameters were α₀ = 0.83 ± 0.04 and γ = 3.8 × 10⁻³ K⁻¹. The variable-order model reproduced the measured signal decay curves with a root-mean-square error of 2.1%, compared to 5.4% for a fixed-order model. The study demonstrates that a single additional scalar parameter γ is sufficient to capture temperature-driven changes in diffusion behaviour in cartilage over the physiological range.

title: Barriers to Lean Implementation in Serbian Food Processing SMEs: An Exploratory Survey
abstract: This paper reports findings from a structured questionnaire survey administered to 67 food processing small and medium enterprises in Vojvodina, Serbia, conducted in 2011. The study aimed to identify and rank barriers to lean production adoption using a five-point Likert scale instrument covering managerial, financial, cultural, and supply chain dimensions. Factor analysis yielded four latent barrier clusters, with managerial commitment and employee knowledge gaps emerging as the dominant factors, accounting for 41% of total variance. Firms employing fewer than 50 workers reported significantly higher scores on financial constraint items compared to mid-sized firms. Only 18% of respondents reported any formal lean training programme, and fewer than 10% used value stream mapping. The results suggest that awareness campaigns and publicly funded training schemes directed at owner-managers could meaningfully lower entry barriers. Limitations include self-reported data and regional sampling.

title: Value Stream Mapping in a Fruit Juice Production Line: A Case Study from Central Serbia
abstract: The paper presents a detailed application of value stream mapping (VSM) to the packaging line of a mid-sized fruit juice producer with approximately 340 employees located near Čačak, Serbia. Current-state mapping identified 14 discrete process steps, of which 6 contained non-value-adding activities representing 38% of total lead time. Bottleneck analysis pinpointed a labelling sub-process as the primary source of work-in-progress accumulation. A future-state map was developed in collaboration with line supervisors and production managers over three workshop sessions. Proposed changes included one-piece flow in the filling station and introduction of a pull scheduling signal at the packaging entry point. The study does not report post-implementation data, as the company had not completed changes at the time of writing. Methodological challenges related to seasonal demand variability in food production are discussed, as standard VSM assumes relatively stable throughput.

title: Employee Resistance to Lean Change in Labour-Intensive Food Manufacturing: Qualitative Evidence from Vojvodina
abstract: Lean transformation programmes frequently stall due to workforce resistance, yet this phenomenon is underexplored in the context of food manufacturing in transition economies. This study used semi-structured interviews with 28 shop-floor employees and 11 middle managers across four meat and dairy processing plants in Vojvodina. Thematic analysis revealed three primary resistance patterns: scepticism about management intentions, fear of job loss linked to efficiency gains, and a perceived conflict between standardised work procedures and craft-based occupational identity among skilled butchers and cheesemakers. Middle managers reported feeling caught between top-down lean directives and the need to maintain workforce morale. Findings suggest that communication strategies and participatory kaizen events may be more effective than top-down mandates, but only if accompanied by explicit job security assurances. Theoretical implications for change management literature in post-socialist industrial settings are discussed.

title: Lean Readiness Assessment Tool for Agri-Food Processors: Development and Pilot Testing
abstract: A diagnostic instrument for assessing organisational readiness for lean adoption in agri-food processing companies was developed through a three-round Delphi procedure involving 19 academic and practitioner experts from Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary. The resulting tool contains 32 items grouped into six dimensions: leadership commitment, workforce capability, process stability, supplier relationships, measurement infrastructure, and safety culture. Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 across dimensions in a pilot sample of 22 companies. Exploratory factor analysis broadly confirmed the six-factor structure with minor cross-loadings on the measurement infrastructure subscale. Scores were found to correlate moderately (r = 0.47, p < 0.01) with managers' self-assessed lean maturity. The tool is intended for use by production managers and lean consultants prior to committing resources to lean programmes, and the full instrument is provided as an appendix. Limitations of the Delphi composition and pilot sample size are acknowledged.

title: Performance Outcomes of Lean Adoption in Serbian Food Companies: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Using a cross-sectional design, this study examined the relationship between lean practice adoption and operational and financial performance in 94 Serbian food processing companies. Lean adoption was measured with a 20-item scale derived from the readiness instrument developed in earlier work; performance indicators were collected from company financial reports for the year prior to surveying and included labour productivity, inventory turnover, and operating profit margin. Ordinary least squares regression showed that composite lean score significantly predicted inventory turnover (β = 0.38, p < 0.001) and labour productivity (β = 0.29, p < 0.01), but not operating profit margin after controlling for firm size and sector. Companies in the dairy sub-sector showed higher lean scores on average than those in grain milling. The study is cross-sectional and cannot establish causality. Industry concentration in the northern Serbia region may limit external validity.

title: Supply Chain Constraints as Lean Barriers in Serbian Food Processing: A Mixed-Methods Inquiry
abstract: Food processing firms in Serbia operate within supply chains characterised by fragmented agricultural suppliers, seasonal raw material availability, and limited cold-chain infrastructure. This paper examines how these upstream constraints impede lean production practices, combining 17 in-depth interviews with procurement and operations managers with quantitative data from 51 firms. Interview analysis identified three mechanisms: demand variability from irregular supplier deliveries undermining level scheduling; the practice of large-batch purchasing to hedge against supply uncertainty, directly contradicting just-in-time principles; and weak contractual relationships preventing collaborative waste reduction. Survey data showed that firms with contracts covering more than 60% of raw material procurement had significantly higher pull-scheduling adoption rates. The paper contributes a contextualised model of supply chain–lean interaction applicable to similar agri-food environments in the Western Balkans and Central-Eastern Europe.

title: Lean and Food Safety Management Systems: Compatibility or Conflict in Serbian Meat Processing Plants
abstract: A recurrent concern among practitioners is whether lean's drive to eliminate non-value-adding activities conflicts with the mandatory documentation and process controls required by HACCP and ISO 22000 food safety standards. This paper investigated this question through comparative case analysis of three meat processing companies in Vojvodina that had implemented both lean practices and certified food safety management systems. Data were collected through document analysis, process observations, and 23 interviews conducted over six months. Findings indicate that conflict arises primarily in the area of standardised work, where food safety procedures and lean work standards are developed by different departments and may contradict each other at the operator level. Conversely, visual management tools showed strong complementarity with HACCP monitoring requirements. A set of integration guidelines was developed collaboratively with plant management teams. The paper is descriptive and the guidelines await broader validation.

title: Lean Production in Transition Economies: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: This systematic review synthesised empirical studies on lean production implementation published between 2000 and 2021 in transition and post-socialist economies, with a focus on Central and Eastern Europe and the Western Balkans. A search across four databases yielded 1,247 records; after title, abstract, and full-text screening, 63 studies met inclusion criteria. Food manufacturing was the most studied sector (27%), followed by automotive components (22%) and electronics assembly (18%). The most consistently reported adoption barrier was managerial commitment, appearing in 74% of included studies, followed by workforce skills gaps (61%) and financial constraints (49%). Performance outcomes were heterogeneous: productivity improvements were reported in 58% of studies with quantitative outcomes, while quality improvements were less frequently measured. Publication bias toward positive outcomes is discussed. The review identifies methodological weaknesses including small sample sizes and short follow-up periods, and proposes a research agenda for the region.

title: Kaizen Event Outcomes in Small Vojvodina Food Firms: A Longitudinal Follow-Up
abstract: Kaizen events are short-duration improvement workshops often recommended as a low-cost lean entry point for small companies. This paper reports a longitudinal study tracking 19 kaizen events conducted in 11 small food processing companies in Vojvodina between 2019 and 2021. Outcomes were measured at three points: immediately post-event, at three months, and at twelve months. Immediate gains in targeted process metrics (cycle time, defect rate) averaged 22% and 17% respectively. At twelve months, however, 58% of improvements had partially or fully eroded, particularly in firms without a designated lean champion. Companies that integrated kaizen outcomes into their ISO 9001 documentation showed significantly better sustainability of gains at twelve months. Sample size limits statistical power, and the study relies partly on self-reported data collected by company coordinators. The findings reinforce arguments for structural embedding of improvement activities rather than isolated events.

title: Digitalisation and Lean in Food Processing SMEs: Early Evidence from Serbia and Hungary
abstract: Industry 4.0 technologies are increasingly discussed as enablers of lean production, yet evidence from food processing SMEs in lower-income European economies remains sparse. This paper presents preliminary findings from a joint Serbia–Hungary survey of 81 food processing firms conducted in 2022–2023. The questionnaire covered adoption of digital tools (ERP systems, IoT sensors on production lines, barcode-based traceability) alongside established lean practice scales. Correlation analysis showed moderate positive associations between ERP adoption and pull scheduling (r = 0.41) and between IoT sensor use and statistical process control (r = 0.35). Qualitative interviews with 12 managers in six purposively selected firms revealed that digital tools often coexist with lean practices without explicit integration; most managers viewed them as separate improvement streams. The paper proposes a simple integration framework and flags data infrastructure costs as the primary barrier for firms with fewer than 100 employees.

title: Lean Production Adoption in the Serbian Food Industry: Barriers, Enablers, and Outcomes
abstract: This book chapter synthesises approximately a decade of the authors' empirical work and relevant regional literature to provide a consolidated account of where Serbian food processors stand with respect to lean production. The chapter opens with a description of the sector—around 3,400 registered food companies, predominantly SMEs, contributing roughly 24% of Serbian manufacturing output—before organising findings around a barrier–enabler–outcome framework. Key barriers discussed include managerial awareness deficits, supply chain fragmentation, seasonal demand patterns, and the coexistence of food safety compliance requirements. Enablers identified across studies include external consultant support, participation in cluster organisations, and EU-funded modernisation programmes. Performance outcomes are reviewed with attention to methodological variation across studies. The chapter concludes with practical guidance for companies and policymakers and highlights gaps in longitudinal and sector-comparative research. It is aimed at a practitioner-academic readership.

title: Knowledge Management Maturity Across Post-Socialist Local Governments: A Comparative Survey in Serbia and Croatia
abstract: Using the six-dimension instrument developed in earlier work, this study compares knowledge management maturity levels across 28 local governments in Serbia and 19 in Croatia. Data were collected via self-administered questionnaires completed by department heads (N = 412) during 2014–2015. Descriptive statistics and Mann–Whitney U tests were applied to detect cross-country and size-related differences. Results show that average maturity scores in both countries fall in the second of five levels ('reactive'), with technology and measurement dimensions scoring consistently lowest. Croatian municipalities score marginally higher on the strategy dimension, a difference that is statistically significant (p < 0.05) but modest in effect size (r = 0.17). Institution size correlates positively with maturity on the process dimension (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001). The paper discusses how shared administrative legacies coexist with divergent post-1990 reform trajectories to produce partially overlapping maturity profiles.

title: Zrelost upravljanja znanjem i apsorpcioni kapacitet u regionalnim razvojnim agencijama: iskustva iz Srbije i Rumunije
abstract: Istraživanje ispituje odnos između zrelosti upravljanja znanjem i apsorpcionog kapaciteta (ACAP) u dvanaest regionalnih razvojnih agencija – šest u Srbiji i šest u Rumuniji. Podaci su prikupljeni kombinacijom upitnika (N = 96 rukovodilaca i analitičara) i analize projektnih izveštaja u periodu od 2020. do 2021. godine. Zrelost upravljanja znanjem merena je prilagođenim šestodimenzionalnim instrumentom, a ACAP Zahra–George skalom adaptiranom za javni sektor. Korelaciona i regresiona analiza pokazale su da su dimenzije kulture i strategije upravljanja znanjem najjači prediktori apsorpcionog kapaciteta (β = 0,38 i 0,31, p < 0,01). Agencije s višim nivoom zrelosti pokazale su statistički značajno veću iskorišćenost EU fondova u posmatranom periodu (t = 2,91, p < 0,01). Nalazi se razmatraju u svetlu različitih reformskih putanja decentralizacije u dve zemlje.

title: Procena zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u zdravstvenim ustanovama: prilagođavanje okvira za upotrebu u domovima zdravlja u Vojvodini
abstract: Istraživanje ispituje mogućnost primene šestodimenzionalnog okvira zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u primarnoj zdravstvenoj zaštiti, na uzorku od osam domova zdravlja u Vojvodini. Okvir je adaptiran uvođenjem zdravstveno-specifičnih indikatora u dimenzijama procesa i kulture, na osnovu kvalitativnih intervjua sa 27 koordinatora i šefova službi. Kvantitativan deo istraživanja uključivao je anketiranje 183 zaposlena. Analiza pouzdanosti i eksploratorska faktorska analiza ukazuju na potrebu za razdvajanjem dimenzije kulture na dve posebne podskale: kultura razmene znanja između stručnjaka i kultura organizacionog učenja. Prosečan nivo zrelosti u uzorku odgovara trećem stepenu petostepene skale, što je viši rezultat nego u opštinskim upravama iz ranijih studija. Identifikovani su i specifični izazovi vezani za čuvanje medicinskog znanja u uslovima visoke fluktuacije lekara.

title: Optimisation of extraction conditions for sulphonamide antibiotics from clay-loam agricultural soil using dispersive solid-phase extraction
abstract: A dispersive solid-phase extraction (dSPE) procedure was developed and evaluated for the simultaneous extraction of six sulphonamide antibiotics—sulphamethoxazole, sulphadiazine, sulphathiazole, sulphamethazine, sulphadimethoxine and sulphachloropyridazine—from a clay-loam agricultural soil collected near Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia. The influence of sorbent type (C18, PSA, Florisil), sorbent mass (25–200 mg), and sample moisture content (0–25 % w/w) on recovery was systematically evaluated. Maximum recoveries of 72–91 % were achieved using 100 mg C18 combined with 50 mg PSA per gram of dry soil, with acetonitrile/0.1 % formic acid (85:15, v/v) as the extraction solvent. Detection was performed by LC-MS/MS in positive electrospray ionisation mode. Limits of quantification ranged from 0.3 to 1.1 µg kg⁻¹ dry weight. Matrix effects were characterised as moderate to strong (signal suppression 18–54 %), underscoring the necessity of matrix-matched calibration for accurate quantification in field samples.

title: Matrix-matched versus solvent-based calibration for quantification of tetracyclines in manure-amended arable soil: a systematic comparison
abstract: This study provides a systematic comparison of solvent-based and matrix-matched calibration for the quantification of five tetracycline antibiotics—tetracycline, oxytetracycline, chlortetracycline, doxycycline and minocycline—in two arable soil types (sandy loam and silty clay) amended with pig manure at rates of 0, 10 and 20 t ha⁻¹. Soil extracts were prepared by pressurised liquid extraction at 80 °C and 1500 psi using McIlvaine–EDTA buffer, cleaned up by mixed-mode cation-exchange SPE cartridges, and analysed by LC-MS/MS. Signal suppression determined by post-column infusion ranged from 31 % to 67 % depending on soil type and amendment level. Recoveries obtained with matrix-matched calibration (83–102 %) were significantly higher than those corrected by solvent-based calibration (54–79 %), confirming that matrix-matched calibration is essential when soil organic matter and clay content vary between sample batches. Intra-day and inter-day precision were below 12 % RSD for all analytes.
venue: Chromatographia Analytica

title: Ion suppression mapping across soil organic matter gradients in multi-residue LC-MS/MS analysis of veterinary antibiotics
abstract: Ion suppression remains a principal source of quantification error in LC-MS/MS-based soil residue analysis. This work characterised the relationship between soil organic matter (SOM) content (ranging from 0.8 % to 6.4 % LOI) and the degree of electrospray ionisation suppression for twelve veterinary antibiotics spanning three classes: sulphonamides (n=5), tetracyclines (n=4) and fluoroquinolones (n=3). Forty-two soil samples collected from Vojvodina agricultural fields were extracted with acetonitrile/McIlvaine buffer, purified over Oasis HLB cartridges, and analysed under identical LC-MS/MS conditions. Post-column infusion experiments showed a linear increase in suppression with SOM for sulphonamides (R²=0.78) and tetracyclines (R²=0.84). Fluoroquinolone responses were consistently suppressed by more than 60 % regardless of SOM level. These findings suggest that single-point matrix-matched calibration is insufficient when SOM varies by more than 1.5 % across sample sets, and that bracketed calibration sets matched by SOM class are preferable.
venue: Analytical Methods in Environmental Science
