title: Isotope-labelled internal standards as a practical alternative to matrix-matched calibration for tetracycline quantification in soil: feasibility and cost assessment
abstract: Stable isotope-labelled (SIL) internal standards are widely recommended for correcting matrix effects in LC-MS/MS; however, their cost and limited commercial availability complicate routine environmental monitoring. This study assessed the performance of five commercially available SIL internal standards (tetracycline-d6, oxytetracycline-d3, chlortetracycline-d3, sulphamethoxazole-¹³C₆ and sulphadiazine-d4) against matrix-matched calibration across 30 agricultural soil samples from the South Bačka District. The SIL-corrected recoveries (79–106 %) were statistically equivalent to matrix-matched values (F-test, α=0.05) for all analytes except chlortetracycline in high-clay samples (>35 % clay), where the SIL approach overestimated concentration by up to 23 %. A cost model based on purchase prices from three Serbian analytical suppliers indicated that SIL correction becomes cost-competitive with matrix preparation only in batches exceeding 40 samples per week. Recommendations for selecting calibration strategy based on sample throughput and soil heterogeneity are provided.
venue: Journal of Analytical and Environmental Chemistry

title: Validation of a QuEChERS-based extraction procedure for simultaneous determination of sulphonamide and tetracycline antibiotics in agricultural soils according to SANTE/11813/2017 guidelines
abstract: A QuEChERS-type extraction was adapted and fully validated for the simultaneous determination of nine sulphonamide and six tetracycline antibiotics in agricultural soils, following the SANTE/11813/2017 document. The protocol used acetonitrile/0.1 M EDTA-McIlvaine buffer (1:1, v/v) as the extraction solvent, with dSPE clean-up employing 150 mg MgSO₄, 50 mg C18 and 50 mg PSA. Method performance was evaluated at three fortification levels (1, 5 and 20 µg kg⁻¹) in three soil types. Recoveries across analytes ranged from 68 % to 107 %, repeatability RSDs were below 9 %, and reproducibility RSDs below 15 %. Limits of detection were 0.1–0.6 µg kg⁻¹ and LOQs 0.3–1.8 µg kg⁻¹ for all analytes. Matrix-matched calibration using procedural blanks from each soil type was essential for achieving acceptable trueness. The validated method was applied to 18 field samples collected from a pig-farming region in Srem, detecting oxytetracycline and sulphamethoxazole in 11 of 18 samples at concentrations of 2–48 µg kg⁻¹.

title: Occurrence and spatial distribution of antibiotic residues in Vojvodina agricultural soils receiving repeated manure applications
abstract: A monitoring study was conducted across 62 agricultural fields in four Vojvodina districts (South Bačka, North Banat, Srem and South Banat) to characterise the occurrence and spatial distribution of 15 antibiotic residues (sulphonamides and tetracyclines) following repeated pig and poultry manure applications over three consecutive years (2017–2019). Soil samples (0–20 cm depth) were extracted by the validated QuEChERS-EDTA procedure and analysed by LC-MS/MS with matrix-matched calibration. Tetracyclines were detected in 73 % of samples, with oxytetracycline reaching a maximum of 312 µg kg⁻¹ in sandy loam under intensive pig manure application. Sulphonamides were detected in 54 % of samples, predominantly sulphamethazine (median 8.4 µg kg⁻¹). Concentrations were significantly higher in fields receiving more than 15 t ha⁻¹ y⁻¹ manure (Mann-Whitney U, p<0.01). Soil pH, organic matter and clay content explained 41 % of the spatial variance in tetracycline accumulation (multiple regression). These results provide baseline data for regulatory risk assessment of antibiotic accumulation in Serbian agricultural soils.
venue: Environmental Monitoring and Soil Research

title: Effect of freeze-drying versus air-drying pretreatment on recovery of tetracyclines and sulphonamides from fresh agricultural soil
abstract: Sample pretreatment prior to extraction significantly influences recoveries of polar antibiotics from soil. This study compared freeze-drying (−50 °C, 48 h) and air-drying (25 °C, 72 h) as preparatory steps before SPE-based extraction of tetracyclines and sulphonamides from freshly collected agricultural soil samples. Twelve soil samples spiked at 10 µg kg⁻¹ were processed by both methods. Freeze-dried samples yielded significantly higher mean recoveries for tetracyclines (88 ± 7 %) compared to air-dried counterparts (71 ± 9 %), a difference attributed to thermal degradation of the enol form under air-drying conditions, confirmed by UV-vis spectral comparison. For sulphonamides, recovery differences were within method uncertainty (p=0.18, paired t-test). Storage stability at −18 °C of freeze-dried soil spiked at 5 µg kg⁻¹ was confirmed for 90 days with less than 8 % analyte loss. Results indicate that freeze-drying is preferable for tetracycline-targeted studies, particularly when sample transport or batch scheduling delays extraction beyond 48 h.

title: Retention behaviour of sulphonamide antibiotics on mixed-mode cation-exchange versus reversed-phase SPE sorbents: a sorbent screening approach for soil matrices
abstract: This work systematically evaluated five solid-phase extraction sorbents—Oasis HLB, Oasis MCX, Strata X-CW, Bond Elut Plexa PCX (all reversed-phase or mixed-mode cation-exchange) and a zeolite-based experimental material from a domestic supplier—for their retention and elution behaviour toward nine sulphonamide antibiotics spiked into three agricultural soil extracts at 10 µg kg⁻¹. Breakthrough volumes, matrix co-extractant removal (assessed by UV absorbance at 254 nm and gravimetric residue) and analyte recoveries were determined across pH 2, 4, 6 and 7 loading conditions. Oasis MCX at pH 4 provided the best combination of recovery (82–97 % for all analytes) and co-extractant removal (reduction of UV-absorbing interferences by 68 %). The zeolite-based material showed selective retention of sulphadiazine and sulphathiazole (>95 %) but poor recovery of more hydrophilic sulphonamides. These data provide a basis for sorbent selection in routine monitoring laboratories operating under budget constraints.

title: Calibration strategy selection for antibiotic residue analysis in heterogeneous soil matrices: practical guidance and worked examples
abstract: This book chapter provides practical guidance on selecting calibration strategies—solvent-based, matrix-matched, stable isotope-dilution and standard addition—for quantification of sulphonamide and tetracycline antibiotics in agricultural soils by LC-MS/MS. Drawing on experimental data from Vojvodina field campaigns and published European monitoring studies, the chapter discusses how soil organic matter, clay content, pH and sample preparation protocol interact to determine the magnitude and variability of matrix effects. Decision trees are provided for laboratories at different levels of resources and throughput. Worked numerical examples using real calibration data illustrate the consequences of selecting an inappropriate strategy, including bias estimation and uncertainty propagation. A section addresses regulatory acceptance criteria under current EU guidance documents for veterinary medicine residue methods. The chapter is aimed at practising laboratory chemists and postgraduate students entering the field of environmental residue analysis.

title: Volatile profile of traditionally dried red pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) from Vojvodina: identification by SPME-GC-MS
abstract: Headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with GC-MS was used to characterise the volatile fraction of sun-dried red pepper fruits from three traditional growing regions in Vojvodina. A CAR/PDMS/DVB fibre was selected after fibre-type comparison. Sixty-one compounds were identified, including pyrazines, furans, aldehydes, and terpenoids. 2-Methoxyphenol and furfural were the dominant Maillard-derived components, accounting for 18.3% and 11.7% of total peak area, respectively. Principal component analysis separated samples by geographical origin and drying duration. Linalool and β-caryophyllene were present at concentrations consistent with sensory threshold literature values. The study provides baseline volatile data for further investigations into heat-induced off-flavour formation in processed Capsicum products from this region.

title: Impact of fermentation by selected Lactobacillus strains on volatile and polyphenol profiles of Capsicum annuum mash
abstract: Capsicum annuum mash was fermented by three Lactobacillus strains (L. plantarum NS-07, L. fermentum NS-12, and L. brevis NS-19, all isolated from traditional Serbian fermented pepper) at 25 °C for 21 days. Volatile compounds were monitored at days 0, 7, 14, and 21 by HS-SPME-GC-MS; polyphenols were quantified by HPLC-DAD. Fermentation induced a significant decrease in hexanal (−62% across all strains by day 21) and an increase in ethyl esters associated with fruity notes. L. plantarum NS-07 preferentially degraded chlorogenic acid, reducing it by 74% with concurrent accumulation of caffeic acid and 4-vinylcatechol. Total titratable acidity increased to 1.8–2.3% lactic acid equivalents. Sensory panel evaluation confirmed preference for the NS-07-fermented product over unfermented control in terms of freshness and reduced bitterness.

title: Effect of vanadium precursor on phase composition and photocatalytic activity of bismuth vanadate prepared by co-precipitation
abstract: BiVO₄ was prepared by co-precipitation using three vanadium precursors—ammonium metavanadate, sodium orthovanadate, and vanadyl sulphate—at room temperature and after calcination at 400 °C and 500 °C. XRD patterns showed that ammonium metavanadate yielded the highest fraction of monoclinic phase (93%) after calcination at 450 °C, while vanadyl sulphate produced mixed tetragonal-monoclinic phases. Raman spectroscopy confirmed monoclinic distortion through the characteristic ν₁ symmetric stretching mode at 826 cm⁻¹. Photocatalytic degradation of Reactive Red 195 (10 mg L⁻¹, pH 6) under visible light (λ > 420 nm, 100 mW cm⁻²) reached 71% in 180 minutes for the ammonium metavanadate sample. TOC measurements indicated 38% mineralisation under the same conditions. The study provides a practical guide for precursor selection in scalable co-precipitation routes.

title: Conformational Preferences of Bis-Hydrazone Ligands and Their Zinc(II) Chelates: NMR and DFT Investigation
abstract: Symmetric and unsymmetric bis-hydrazone ligands formed by condensation of dihydrazides with two equivalents of aromatic aldehyde were studied in solution and as Zn(II) complexes. ¹H NMR in DMSO-d₆ at 298 K revealed two sets of signals for the unsymmetric compounds, corresponding to head-to-head and head-to-tail arrangements of the two hydrazone units, in approximately 3:1 ratio. Variable-temperature experiments (253–363 K) showed no coalescence up to the highest accessible temperature, indicating a high barrier (ΔG‡ > 95 kJ mol⁻¹). Upon complexation with ZnCl₂, only a single set of ligand signals was observed, consistent with enforced head-to-tail geometry in the complex. DFT optimisation of the Zn complex at the B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP level gave a tetrahedral zinc coordination geometry with Zn–N bond lengths of 2.10–2.14 Å, in agreement with an X-ray structure of one derivative.

title: Phosphorus limitation as a biofilm control strategy in chloramine-treated systems: mesocosm experiments with amended source water
abstract: Phosphate concentrations in Vojvodina groundwater used for drinking supply range from 0.04 to 0.18 mg P/L. We conducted mesocosm experiments to evaluate whether reducing bioavailable phosphorus to < 0.01 mg P/L, achieved by dosing iron coagulant upstream of the distribution loop, suppresses nitrifying biofilm development. Four pipe-loop mesocosms were operated at ambient and reduced phosphorus under two chloramine residuals (1.0 and 2.0 mg/L as Cl₂) for 240 days. Biofilm ATP, 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and qPCR of nxrB were measured at 60-day intervals. Phosphorus limitation reduced total biofilm ATP by 55% and nxrB gene copy numbers by 1.8 orders of magnitude at 1.0 mg/L chloramine, but differences were attenuated at 2.0 mg/L. Community structure in phosphorus-limited biofilms shifted toward oligotrophic Alphaproteobacteria with reduced Nitrospira abundance. The combination of moderate phosphorus limitation and a maintained chloramine residual of 1.5 mg/L effectively prevented nitrification onset throughout the 240-day trial.

title: Handling Schema Evolution in Long-Running ETL Pipelines: A Pattern Catalogue
abstract: ETL pipelines deployed in production environments frequently encounter schema changes in source systems—added columns, renamed attributes, restructured tables—that cause pipeline failures or silent data quality degradation. This paper documents a catalogue of 12 schema evolution patterns identified through examination of incident logs from four industrial data warehouse projects spanning between two and seven years of operation. For each pattern, the paper describes its frequency, the typical impact on downstream data quality, and a recommended handling strategy ranging from automated adaptation to human escalation. The catalogue was compiled through a combination of log analysis and semi-structured interviews with data engineers at the participating organisations. A lightweight classification model trained on structural change descriptors was found to correctly identify the applicable handling strategy in 79% of cases on a held-out test set of 96 observed changes. The paper argues that pipeline robustness requires explicit change-handling logic rather than reliance on operational monitoring alone.

title: RDF-Based Intermediate Representation for Schema-Agnostic Data Integration Pipelines
abstract: This paper proposes using RDF as a universal intermediate representation within ETL pipelines, enabling data from relational, document-oriented, and flat-file sources to be processed through a common transformation layer before loading into a target system. The central claim is that expressing all intermediate records as RDF triples annotated with source provenance and ontology-level type information allows downstream transformations to operate on semantic content rather than syntactic structure. A prototype pipeline was implemented using Apache Jena and a custom NiFi processor set, and evaluated on three integration scenarios drawn from the agri-food sector involving PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and CSV sources. End-to-end throughput averaged 14,200 records per second on commodity hardware, with an overhead of approximately 22% compared to a direct-mapping baseline without semantic annotation. Data quality improvements measured by completeness and consistency metrics averaged 11 percentage points over the baseline. Limitations related to RDF verbosity and serialisation cost at high throughput are discussed.

title: Automated Data Type Conflict Resolution in Cross-Organisational Data Sharing: Methods and Limitations
abstract: Data type conflicts—where semantically equivalent attributes carry incompatible physical representations across systems—are among the most common obstacles in cross-organisational data exchange. This paper systematically classifies data type conflicts into seven categories based on analysis of 23 data exchange specifications from public sector and manufacturing domains in Serbia and Hungary. For each conflict category, automated resolution strategies are defined and implemented as configurable transformation components within a prototype integration framework. The resolution logic draws on both schema-level metadata and ontology-level type hierarchies. Resolution accuracy was evaluated against expert-curated ground truth on 412 conflict instances, achieving an overall accuracy of 84%, with the lowest performance on unit-of-measure conflicts involving domain-specific measurement systems. The paper also quantifies the residual error introduced into downstream aggregation queries when type conflicts are resolved incorrectly, finding that even low error rates in type conversion can produce significant query result distortion.

title: Domain Ontology Construction for Industrial Sensor Data Integration: A Semi-Automated Approach
abstract: Industrial sensor networks in manufacturing and utilities generate data described by vendor-specific taxonomies and proprietary data dictionaries that impede cross-system integration. This paper describes a semi-automated pipeline for constructing domain ontologies from three heterogeneous source artefacts: vendor data sheets, existing industry standards documents, and legacy database schemas. The pipeline applies natural language processing to extract candidate concepts and relations from text, structural analysis to infer taxonomic structure from database foreign key patterns, and an expert review step to validate and merge candidate ontology modules. The resulting ontology was validated in the context of integrating sensor streams from two distinct industrial automation systems at a Vojvodina-region production facility, covering 640 distinct sensor types. Ontology coverage—defined as the proportion of integration-relevant attributes resolvable to ontology concepts—reached 91% after two expert review rounds. The paper reports on the time investment required at each pipeline stage and identifies document quality as the primary bottleneck.

title: Dynamic Schema Matching in Streaming ETL: Adapting to Mid-Flight Source Changes
abstract: Batch-oriented ETL assumptions break down in streaming architectures where source schemas can change while the pipeline is actively processing data. This paper addresses the problem of detecting and responding to schema changes in streaming data sources without pipeline interruption. A detection mechanism monitors the statistical distribution of field occurrences in each micro-batch window, triggering a re-matching procedure when field-level statistics deviate beyond empirically set thresholds. Re-matching uses a lightweight incremental matcher that reuses prior alignment results where structural similarity is preserved, avoiding full recomputation. The system was prototyped on Apache Kafka Streams and evaluated using a synthetic workload generator that injected schema changes at controlled intervals across five change severity levels. Mean detection latency was 4.2 seconds at a micro-batch interval of two seconds. Pipeline throughput degraded by no more than 9% during re-matching events. False positive detection rate was 3.1% across 1,200 injected change events.

title: Data Integration Architectures for Industry 4.0 Information Systems: A Structured Review
abstract: This chapter surveys data integration architectures employed in the context of Industry 4.0 deployments, with particular attention to how ETL, ELT, data virtualisation, and event-driven integration patterns address the heterogeneity introduced by combining operational technology and information technology data sources. The chapter is organised around four recurring integration challenges: structural heterogeneity, semantic heterogeneity, temporal misalignment, and provenance management. For each challenge, representative architectural responses are described and compared on criteria including scalability, schema flexibility, and latency characteristics. The survey draws on 67 primary sources published between 2014 and 2021, selected through a systematic search across four academic databases. The chapter concludes with an assessment of gaps in current architectural practice, particularly the limited adoption of formal semantic representations outside research prototypes and the under-addressed problem of integration pipeline maintenance over multi-year deployment horizons.

title: Benchmark Design for Evaluating Schema-Agnostic ETL Pipelines Under Heterogeneous Industrial Workloads
abstract: Evaluating ETL pipeline systems that claim schema-agnostic operation is complicated by the absence of agreed benchmarks that reflect realistic industrial schema diversity and data volumes. This paper presents a benchmark suite comprising five workload profiles derived from anonymised data integration tasks in the food processing, logistics, and energy sectors. Each workload profile specifies a source schema corpus, a set of integration queries, data volume parameters, and a reference integration result for correctness evaluation. The benchmark also defines metrics for schema-agnosticism degree—quantifying how much manual schema-specific configuration each system under test requires. Three existing open-source integration frameworks were evaluated against the benchmark, revealing substantial performance variation across workload profiles and large differences in required manual effort. The benchmark artefacts and evaluation harness are made available for reuse. The paper discusses design decisions and known limitations, including the difficulty of obtaining sufficiently diverse schema corpora without breaching confidentiality obligations.

title: Ontology Alignment Confidence Propagation in Multi-Step Integration Pipelines
abstract: When multiple schema matching steps are chained in a multi-source integration pipeline, uncertainty in early alignments propagates and compounds into later transformation stages, potentially causing systematic errors that are difficult to trace. This paper formalises the propagation of alignment confidence scores through a directed acyclic pipeline graph, treating each transformation step as a conditional probability modifier. The formalisation enables a pipeline-level confidence score to be attached to each output record, indicating the aggregate reliability of the ontology alignments involved in its derivation. An implementation was evaluated on a three-source integration pipeline combining data from a SCADA system, a laboratory information management system, and a document management system at an energy utility, totalling approximately 2.1 million records. Records flagged as low-confidence by the propagation model showed a defect rate 4.7 times higher than unflagged records when validated against domain expert review. The model adds a processing overhead of under 4% over the baseline pipeline.

title: Mapping Reuse Across ETL Projects: Identifying Transferable Transformation Logic Using Schema Similarity Clustering
abstract: Organisations that operate multiple ETL pipelines often redevelop functionally equivalent transformation logic independently across projects, representing duplicated effort and inconsistent data semantics. This paper investigates the extent to which transformation mappings developed for one integration project can be reused in subsequent projects via schema similarity clustering. A corpus of 38 ETL projects from six organisations was analysed, yielding 1,140 individual transformation rules. Schema similarity between project pairs was computed using a weighted combination of structural, lexical, and ontological similarity features. Clustering identified 14 transferable mapping clusters covering 31% of all transformation rules in the corpus. A reuse recommendation tool was prototyped and evaluated in a user study with eight data engineers, who rated 73% of recommendations as directly applicable or applicable with minor modifications. The paper quantifies estimated effort savings and discusses conditions under which reuse is most likely to succeed, including schema naming conventions and ontology coverage depth.

title: Bayesian Naive Classification of Short Multivariate Time Series with Informative Priors Derived from Expert Knowledge
abstract: Classifying multivariate time series when fewer than 150 labelled instances are available presents well-known difficulties for discriminative models. This paper examines a generative Bayesian approach in which prior distributions over class-conditional emission parameters are elicited from domain experts through a structured interview protocol and encoded as Dirichlet and Normal-Inverse-Wishart priors. Experiments are conducted on four industrial monitoring datasets with between 42 and 147 labelled sequences. Classification accuracy under the proposed informative-prior model reaches 81.3% on average across datasets, compared with 71.8% for a maximum-likelihood hidden Markov model trained on the same data. The posterior predictive checks confirm well-calibrated class probability estimates. A sensitivity analysis shows that moderate misspecification of the prior location has little effect on accuracy when sample sizes exceed 80. The method is evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation throughout, and all code and anonymised data subsets are made publicly available.

title: Shrinkage Priors for Cox Proportional Hazards Models in High-Dimensional Industrial Failure Data
abstract: When failure event datasets contain many candidate covariates relative to the number of observed events, standard maximum partial likelihood estimation of the Cox model is unstable. This paper compares Lasso, Ridge, elastic-net, horseshoe, and spike-and-slab shrinkage approaches within a Bayesian Cox framework applied to a turbine bearing dataset comprising 312 failure events and 87 sensor-derived features. Posterior inference is performed via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with 4,000 post-warmup draws. Variable selection consistency is assessed by comparing the 90% credible interval coverage of known zero coefficients introduced through simulation. The horseshoe prior identifies a sparse set of 11 features with credible intervals excluding zero while maintaining predictive concordance (C-index 0.81) comparable to elastic-net penalised partial likelihood (C-index 0.79). Run times for HMC are 40 minutes on a standard workstation, which is acceptable for offline model fitting. An R package implementing the proposed workflow is made available under an open-source licence.
venue: Reliability Engineering and Statistical Modelling

title: Imbalanced learning for predictive maintenance: lessons from three years of sensor log data in a food-processing facility
abstract: This book chapter documents a multi-year applied study in which supervised classification models were developed to predict equipment failures at a food-processing plant in Vojvodina. Sensor readings were sampled at one-minute intervals across 14 production lines over a 36-month period; failure events constituted 0.8 % of labelled windows. The chapter describes the full pipeline: raw signal cleaning, window segmentation, feature extraction (statistical moments, zero-crossing rate, spectral energy ratios), resampling, model selection, and deployment. Gradient-boosted trees with cost-sensitive weighting achieved a recall of 0.87 on failure windows at a false-positive rate of 0.09 in the final held-out evaluation. The chapter also discusses practical constraints encountered during deployment, including label noise from incomplete maintenance records and the difficulty of obtaining timely ground-truth annotations. The study is intended as a reference for practitioners facing similar settings.

title: Unpaid Work and Gendered Expectations in Vojvodina Rural Households: A Qualitative Snapshot
abstract: This article examines how unpaid domestic and agricultural work is distributed along gender lines in twelve villages in northern Vojvodina. Drawing on 38 semi-structured interviews conducted in 2022 with residents aged 25–75, the study traces persistent expectations that women manage both indoor household tasks and significant portions of kitchen garden labour, regardless of their formal employment status. Men in the sample predominantly identified field-crop decisions and machinery operation as their domain, while describing childcare and food preservation as naturally female responsibilities. The analysis applies a social constructionist framework, treating gendered task allocation not as biologically determined but as continuously reproduced through daily interaction, community norms, and reference to tradition. Results indicate that younger women (25–40) articulate greater dissatisfaction with this division than their mothers or grandmothers did at comparable life stages, yet structural constraints—limited childcare infrastructure, seasonal income dependence—curtail behavioural change. The paper argues that attitudinal shifts are outpacing structural conditions in these communities.

title: Three Generations Under One Roof: Authority, Care, and Gender in Extended Rural Families in Šumadija
abstract: Multi-generational co-residence remains common in rural Šumadija, and this paper investigates how authority over household decisions is distributed by gender and generation within such arrangements. Data come from 24 in-depth interviews and four months of intermittent ethnographic observation across seven villages in Kragujevac municipality, carried out in 2022–2023. The study finds that older women (grandmothers) frequently hold de facto authority over food production, resource allocation within the kitchen economy, and child-rearing standards, even as formal household headship is attributed to the eldest male. Middle-generation women report negotiating between their own preferences and the expectations of mothers-in-law, describing this as a primary source of household tension. Younger men in the sample express more egalitarian stated values but their actual participation in care tasks remains low. The paper uses positional mapping to visualise these layered authority structures and discusses the implications for rural welfare policy targeting women's autonomy.

title: How Young Women Narrate Their Return to the Village: Gender, Migration, and Renegotiation of Roles
abstract: Rural-to-urban student migration followed by partial return to natal villages is a recognisable pattern in Serbia, and this conference paper explores how young women who have studied in Novi Sad or Belgrade narrate their reintegration into rural households. Based on 19 narrative interviews conducted in 2024 with women aged 22–35 who had returned to their home villages in Bačka and Banat after completing higher education, the study examines the tensions between urban gender norms acquired during study and the role expectations they encounter upon return. Participants frequently describe incremental, low-conflict strategies for shifting household arrangements rather than direct confrontation—negotiating to keep part-time remote employment, re-labelling certain tasks as shared, or citing economic necessity to justify visible changes. The analysis draws on Goffman's concept of role distance. The paper concludes that return migration constitutes a specific social moment in which gender norms become temporarily negotiable, but the window is narrow and closes quickly once stable patterns re-establish.

title: Measuring the Unmeasured: Methodological Challenges in Studying Domestic Labour in Rural Serbian Contexts
abstract: This book chapter reflects on methodological difficulties encountered when conducting qualitative research on gendered domestic labour in Serbian villages, drawing on fieldwork experience gathered between 2021 and 2024 across three research projects involving a total of 94 participants in Vojvodina and central Serbia. The authors discuss three main challenges: the normalisation of gendered tasks, which makes participants reluctant to describe them as labour at all; the social desirability effect that leads men to overreport participation in care tasks during interviews; and logistical barriers to sustained ethnographic presence in small communities where the researcher is perceived as an outsider. Practical solutions explored include time-diary supplements to interviews, pair interviews with couples, and iterative member-checking sessions. The chapter also addresses the ethical dimension of research that can implicitly challenge community norms, and proposes a reflective positionality framework adapted to the Serbian rural context. The discussion is intended to be useful for researchers working in similar post-socialist rural settings in South-East Europe.

title: Street Renaming and Symbolic Politics in Post-2000 Vojvodinian Towns
abstract: This article analyses 147 street renaming decisions made between 2000 and 2014 across eleven Vojvodinian municipalities with significant ethnic minority populations, using municipal gazette data and local newspaper coverage as primary sources. Renamings are categorised by the type of figure or event honoured, the ethnic valence of the new name, and the degree of public contestation recorded in council minutes and press archives. Quantitative content analysis shows that 38 per cent of renamings involved replacing a name of Yugoslav-era socialist origin with a pre-war or interwar figure, and that municipalities with higher proportions of Hungarian or Slovak residents carried out proportionally more bilingual street sign changes than municipalities with homogeneous Serbian majorities. Contestation, measured by the number of formal objections filed, was highest in medium-sized towns undergoing electoral competition between nationally and ethnically oriented parties. The findings suggest that street renaming in Vojvodina operates as a low-intensity symbolic arena where national and minority elites negotiate visibility without triggering open conflict.

title: Binding of ferulic acid to isolated wheat starch fractions: isothermal titration calorimetry and fluorescence quenching study
abstract: Non-covalent interactions between ferulic acid and three wheat starch fractions—amylose, amylopectin, and granule-bound starch synthase (GBSS)-enriched granules—were characterised using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and steady-state fluorescence quenching at pH 5.0, 6.5, and 7.4, mimicking different segments of the gastrointestinal tract. ITC thermograms indicated that ferulic acid binding to amylose was enthalpically driven (ΔH = −18.3 kJ/mol) with a stoichiometry of approximately one ferulic acid molecule per 14 glucose units. Binding affinity to amylopectin was roughly four-fold lower (Ka = 2.1 × 10³ M⁻¹ versus 8.7 × 10³ M⁻¹ for amylose) at pH 6.5. Fluorescence quenching of the GBSS-enriched fraction yielded a Stern–Volmer constant of 1.8 × 10⁴ M⁻¹, consistent with static quenching. Circular dichroism spectra suggested minor conformational changes in the helical amylose chain upon complexation. These thermodynamic parameters establish a quantitative baseline for understanding how wheat bran phenolics modulate starch structure in processed cereal products.

title: Effect of quercetin and rutin on the in vitro digestibility of maize starch and estimated glycaemic index
abstract: The effect of quercetin (aglycone) and rutin (quercetin-3-O-rutinoside) on the in vitro digestibility of native and gelatinised maize starch was evaluated using the Englyst method with pancreatic α-amylase and amyloglucosidase at flavonoid concentrations of 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 mg/mL. Rapidly digestible starch (RDS), slowly digestible starch (SDS), and resistant starch (RS) fractions were quantified. At 1.0 mg/mL quercetin, RDS decreased by 23% relative to the control (p < 0.01) in gelatinised starch, while rutin reduced RDS by 12% at the same concentration, consistent with lower protein–polyphenol affinity of the glycosylated form. RS increased from 8.1% to 14.6% with quercetin at the highest dose. Estimated glycaemic index values calculated from the hydrolysis kinetics fell from 72.3 (control) to 64.8 (quercetin, 1.0 mg/mL). Enzyme activity assays confirmed that quercetin partially inhibited α-amylase (IC₅₀ = 0.38 mg/mL) independently of starch binding, suggesting a dual mechanism for glycaemic modulation.

title: X-ray diffraction and DSC characterisation of V-type amylose complexes formed with chlorogenic acid
abstract: V-type inclusion complexes between high-amylose maize starch and chlorogenic acid were prepared by co-precipitation at 80 °C followed by controlled cooling. Wide-angle X-ray scattering (WAXS) patterns showed the characteristic V6-type diffraction peak at 2θ = 7.4° for all complexes, with crystallinity index increasing from 6.2% in native starch to 18.5% in the complex prepared at a 1:0.15 starch:chlorogenic acid mass ratio. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) melting endotherms of the complexes appeared between 102 and 108 °C, confirming thermally stable inclusion structures. Enthalpy of melting (ΔHm) rose from 1.8 to 4.3 J/g across the concentration series. Rapid visco analysis showed a marked reduction in peak viscosity (from 312 to 187 mPa·s) and breakdown viscosity, indicating that complexation restricts swelling. Complexation efficiency, estimated by the phenolic content remaining in supernatants, reached 74% at the highest ratio tested. These structural data suggest that chlorogenic acid is accommodated within the amylose helix cavity, altering both thermal and pasting properties relevant to baking applications.

title: Polyphenol–starch interactions in rye bread crumb: extraction, characterisation and digestibility consequences
abstract: Rye bread crumb was fractionated by sequential aqueous extraction to isolate polyphenol–starch complexes formed during baking. Total polyphenol content of the starch-rich fraction was quantified by Folin–Ciocalteu (12.4 ± 0.8 mg GAE/g dry starch fraction) and individual phenolics identified by HPLC-DAD, with ferulic acid (61% of total), caffeic acid (17%), and sinapic acid (9%) as the dominant species. In vitro digestibility assays on the extracted starch fractions showed a 17% lower rate constant k (first-order model) compared with a control wheat starch fraction devoid of phenolics (k = 0.042 versus 0.051 min⁻¹). DSC thermograms of the extracted fraction revealed a minor endotherm at 100–104 °C attributable to V-type complexes, though peak area was small (ΔH = 0.9 J/g). The data indicate that even modest polyphenol loads encountered in real bread systems can slow starch hydrolysis, warranting consideration in nutritional labelling methodologies.

title: Competitive binding of epigallocatechin gallate and palmitic acid to amylose: implications for lipid–polyphenol–starch ternary complexes
abstract: The formation of ternary complexes among amylose, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), and palmitic acid was investigated because native cereal starches contain endogenous surface lipids that may compete or cooperate with polyphenols for the helical cavity. Binary and ternary complexes were prepared at varying molar ratios and characterised by DSC, WAXS, and molecular fluorescence. In binary amylose–palmitic acid complexes, DSC gave ΔHm = 6.1 J/g at 2θ = 7.4°. Addition of EGCG at equimolar EGCG:palmitic acid ratio reduced ΔHm to 4.2 J/g and shifted the crystallinity index from 22.1% to 16.4%, suggesting partial displacement of palmitic acid from the helix by EGCG. At a 2:1 EGCG:palmitic acid ratio, no V-type signal was detected. Fluorescence quenching titrations confirmed EGCG binding to amylose (Ka = 1.1 × 10⁴ M⁻¹) with no significant change in the presence of palmitic acid at low concentrations. In vitro digestibility of ternary complexes was intermediate between amylose–lipid (slowest) and amylose–EGCG (faster) binary systems. The competition between endogenous lipids and dietary polyphenols for the amylose helix has practical relevance for predicting glycaemic index of fortified cereal products.

title: Starch digestibility and polyphenol profile of traditional Serbian flatbreads made with whole-grain emmer and einkorn wheat
abstract: Three traditional Serbian flatbread formulations (pogačice) prepared with whole-grain emmer (Triticum dicoccum), einkorn (Triticum monococcum), and common wheat (control) flour were evaluated for total polyphenol content, individual phenolic acid profile (HPLC-DAD/MS), and in vitro starch digestibility. Emmer flatbread contained 2.4-fold more total bound phenolics than the common wheat control (486 versus 202 µg FAE/g dry matter). Ferulic acid comprised 78% of bound phenolics in emmer. In vitro starch hydrolysis rate constants were 0.038, 0.043, and 0.058 min⁻¹ for emmer, einkorn, and common wheat flatbreads, respectively. Estimated glycaemic index was 55.4 (emmer), 59.8 (einkorn), and 69.1 (control). Regression analysis across all samples showed that bound ferulic acid content explained 81% of the variance in digestibility rate constant (p < 0.001). Starch crystallinity measured by WAXS was also lower in emmer flatbread (14.2% versus 9.6% after baking), consistent with partial V-complex retention post-gelatinisation. These findings support the inclusion of ancient wheat varieties in reformulated bakery products targeting lower glycaemic response.

title: Polyphenol–starch interactions in cereal-based foods: current understanding and research gaps
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of the literature on non-covalent interactions between dietary polyphenols and cereal starch fractions, organised around three main themes: (i) the physical chemistry of complex formation, including thermodynamic drivers and structural outcomes; (ii) consequences for starch digestibility and estimated glycaemic index; and (iii) processing factors (gelatinisation temperature, water activity, pH) that modulate complex stability. The chapter summarises data from over 120 published studies from 2005 to 2021 and compares results across polyphenol classes (hydroxycinnamic acids, flavonols, catechins, anthocyanins) and cereal species (wheat, rye, barley, oat, maize, sorghum). Gaps identified include the absence of in vivo validation for most in vitro glycaemic data, limited work on bioaccessibility of polyphenols following complexation, and scarcity of studies on whole-grain matrix effects beyond starch. Methodological inconsistencies in in vitro digestion protocols are also discussed. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and researchers entering the field and provides a methodological annex comparing Englyst, INFOGEST, and static in vitro digestion protocols.

title: Interaction kinetics of caffeic acid with retrograded wheat starch: influence of starch crystallinity and water content
abstract: Caffeic acid binding to retrograded wheat starch with varying degrees of retrogradation (induced by storage at 4 °C for 1, 3, and 7 days) was studied to determine whether increased crystallinity of retrograded starch affects polyphenol uptake. Crystallinity indices of retrograded samples, measured by WAXS, were 14.2%, 21.8%, and 31.4% for 1-, 3-, and 7-day storage, respectively. Caffeic acid uptake, quantified by spectrophotometry at 323 nm after incubation at 25 °C, decreased with increasing crystallinity: 82%, 61%, and 43% of added caffeic acid (0.5 mg/mL) was bound by 1-, 3-, and 7-day retrograded starch, respectively. Water content modulated binding: at 20% moisture, binding efficiency was 30–40% lower than at 50% moisture across all samples. ITC measurements at the two water activity extremes confirmed that binding remained enthalpically driven but that enthalpy magnitude decreased at lower moisture. Retrograded starch also showed reduced α-amylase accessibility (hydrolysis rate constant 0.022 min⁻¹ versus 0.045 min⁻¹ for native), and caffeic acid addition produced a further modest reduction (0.018 min⁻¹) only in samples with lower crystallinity. These data are relevant for understanding polyphenol–starch interaction in bread staling.

title: Comparison of static and dynamic in vitro digestion models for estimating the effect of ferulic acid on wheat starch hydrolysis
abstract: Four in vitro digestion protocols—the Englyst method, the standardised INFOGEST static model, a two-stage pH-stat model, and a dynamic TIM-1 simulator—were applied to wheat starch gels (5% w/v) containing 0 or 1.0 mg/mL ferulic acid to compare their ability to detect polyphenol-mediated reductions in starch hydrolysis. All protocols detected a statistically significant reduction in hydrolysis due to ferulic acid (p < 0.05), but the magnitude differed: Englyst reported a 21% reduction in the hydrolysis index, INFOGEST 16%, pH-stat 19%, and the dynamic model 11%. Correlations between ferulic acid dose and hydrolysis reduction were linear and significant in all models (R² range 0.88–0.96). The dynamic model showed the smallest effect, consistent with more physiological enzyme concentrations and transit times. Dialysis experiments within the INFOGEST model indicated that 63% of initial ferulic acid remained associated with the starch pellet post-digestion. The study suggests that protocol choice materially affects the estimated magnitude of polyphenol–starch interactions and recommends reporting the full digestion kinetics curve rather than single-point hydrolysis indices.

title: Resveratrol incorporation into high-amylose maize starch gels and its effect on gel texture, polyphenol bioaccessibility, and simulated glycaemic response
abstract: Resveratrol was incorporated into high-amylose maize starch (HAMS) gels (8% w/v) at 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 mg/mL by hot-dispersion and slow-cooling to form inclusion complexes prior to gelation. Gel firmness measured by texture profile analysis increased by 18% at 1.0 mg/mL resveratrol, consistent with complex-induced retardation of amylose chain rearrangement. Polyphenol bioaccessibility was determined after INFOGEST digestion as the fraction recovered in the dialysate; resveratrol bioaccessibility was 29% in the uncomplexed control and decreased to 14% in HAMS gels, indicating partial entrapment within the starch matrix. In vitro glycaemic response, assessed by the starch hydrolysis index from the same digestion experiments, fell from 68.4 (control HAMS gel) to 57.1 (1.0 mg/mL resveratrol gel). FTIR spectra showed a band shift at 1000–1050 cm⁻¹ diagnostic of altered starch chain conformation upon complexation. The trade-off between polyphenol bioaccessibility and glycaemic response modulation is discussed in the context of designing functional starch-based delivery systems.

title: Oat starch fractions as polyphenol carriers: comparative binding of avenanthramides and phenolic acids
abstract: Avenanthramides (AVNs; AVN-A, AVN-B, AVN-C) are phenolic alkaloids unique to oats and structurally distinct from the hydroxycinnamic acids found in other cereals. This study compared the binding affinity of AVN-A, AVN-B, AVN-C, and ferulic acid for oat amylose and amylopectin at physiological pH using ITC and molecular docking. ITC Ka values for AVN-B (4.9 × 10³ M⁻¹) and AVN-C (6.1 × 10³ M⁻¹) exceeded those of ferulic acid (3.7 × 10³ M⁻¹) for oat amylose, with docking scoring attributing the difference to an additional hydrogen bond formed by the anthranilic nitrogen. In vitro starch hydrolysis assays showed that AVN-C reduced the hydrolysis index of oat starch gels by 19%, compared with 14% for ferulic acid at equimolar concentrations (0.8 mM). The β-glucan content of the oat starch fraction used was below 0.4% (w/w), confirmed by mixed-linkage glucan assay, excluding β-glucan as a confounding factor. These findings suggest that oat-specific polyphenols contribute to the low glycaemic response associated with oat-based foods through direct starch complexation, in addition to the well-characterised β-glucan effect.

title: WGS-based source attribution of a recurring Listeria monocytogenes ST121 contamination event in a frankfurter production line
abstract: Following repeated detection of L. monocytogenes in finished frankfurter product lots over a seven-month period at a medium-sized Serbian meat processor, a WGS-based investigation was undertaken to identify the contamination source. Forty-one isolates were sequenced: 14 from product, 22 from environmental swabs, and 5 from raw material batches. Core-genome MLST analysis clustered 33 isolates into a single ST121 clone (cgMLST ≤ 6 allele differences). Temporal and spatial analysis of positive sampling results, combined with production scheduling records provided by the facility, implicated a water-cooled vacuum stuffer as the primary harborage site. The inner sealing surface of the stuffer hopper was inaccessible during routine cleaning-in-place procedures. Physical disassembly and targeted swabbing confirmed dense biofilm in this location. Following equipment replacement and updated cleaning standard operating procedures, no ST121 isolates were recovered over a subsequent 16-week monitoring period. This case illustrates the diagnostic value of integrating WGS with process-level facility data.

title: Discrimination of cold-pressed sunflower, pumpkin seed, and hemp seed oils by NIR spectroscopy combined with principal component analysis and linear discriminant analysis
abstract: Cold-pressed oils from sunflower, pumpkin seed, and hemp seed are frequently subject to mislabelling due to their similar appearance and price differences. This study evaluated the ability of diffuse-reflectance NIR spectroscopy (900–2500 nm) to discriminate 87 authentic oil samples obtained from twelve certified Serbian producers over two harvest seasons. Spectra were preprocessed using standard normal variate (SNV) transformation and first-derivative Savitzky-Golay smoothing. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied for exploratory visualisation, and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) was used for supervised classification. The first three principal components explained 91.4% of total spectral variance. LDA achieved a correct classification rate of 96.6% in cross-validation (leave-one-out) and 94.3% on an independent test set of 28 samples. Spectral regions around 1720 nm and 2300 nm, associated with C–H overtones from fatty acid chains, were identified as the most discriminative through loading plots. The results indicate that benchtop NIR combined with LDA is a reliable, reagent-free first-line screening tool for routine oil type verification.

title: Portable NIR spectroscopy for on-site screening of cold-pressed sesame oil adulteration: calibration transfer from benchtop instrumentation
abstract: Portable NIR spectrometers offer the prospect of on-site fraud screening during procurement, but calibrations developed on laboratory benchtop instruments do not transfer directly to handheld devices due to differences in optical geometry and detector sensitivity. This work addressed calibration transfer for a PLSR model predicting the content of refined soybean oil in cold-pressed sesame oil (adulteration range 5–50% w/w). Spectra from 96 mixture samples were acquired on both a benchtop and a portable NIR device. Three transfer approaches were compared: piecewise direct standardisation (PDS), slope-bias correction, and spectral space transformation (SST). PDS reduced RMSEP on the portable device from 6.4% w/w (no transfer) to 2.9% w/w, and SST gave a similar result (3.1% w/w), while slope-bias correction was least effective (4.5% w/w). Transferred portable models approached benchtop accuracy (RMSEP 2.3% w/w), making on-site deployment operationally feasible for lots above 5% adulteration. The study provides a practical protocol for analytical laboratories seeking to extend NIR authentication workflows to field settings.

title: Cross-contamination of coccidiostat-free feed lots with lasalocid during sequential production: a field study in three Serbian compound feed mills
abstract: Lasalocid carry-over through feed manufacturing equipment was monitored in three compound feed mills in Vojvodina over a six-month period. After production runs of lasalocid-containing broiler starter (75 mg/kg target), sequential non-medicated feed batches were sampled at positions corresponding to 0%, 25%, 50%, and 100% of the subsequent batch volume (n = 156 composite samples total). Lasalocid concentrations were determined by LC-MS/MS. Carry-over into the first non-medicated batch ranged from 1.2 to 4.8% of the preceding medicated batch concentration, depending on mixer and conveyor design. Concentration in the second sequential batch fell below the EU action threshold of 1.25 mg/kg for all mills. Moisture content of the carry-over feed and mixer flush mass were significant predictors of contamination level (p < 0.05). Results support practical guidance for sequencing and flushing protocols to reduce inadvertent coccidiostat exposure in non-target species.

title: Credit Risk Provisioning in Yugoslav Commercial Banks: A Pre-Transition Assessment
abstract: This study examines loan loss provisioning practices in twelve Yugoslav commercial banks over the period 1986–1991, using audited balance-sheet data collected through direct bank surveys. The analysis applies a descriptive cross-sectional framework to assess the gap between declared provisions and estimated true expected losses, drawing on an early adapted version of the Altman Z-score for socialist enterprise borrowers. Results indicate that median provisioning covered only 38 percent of impaired exposures, with the shortfall most pronounced in banks with concentrated exposure to social enterprises undergoing self-management restructuring. The paper argues that distorted incentives embedded in the self-management credit relationship systematically suppressed timely recognition of credit deterioration. The findings provide a baseline for understanding the scale of inherited bad-loan stocks that successor banking systems in the post-Yugoslav states had to absorb after 1991, and inform subsequent debates about provisioning adequacy under the National Bank of Yugoslavia regulatory framework.

title: Collateral Recovery Rates in Serbian Bank Liquidations, 1991–1998
abstract: Drawing on liquidation records from seven insolvent Serbian banks resolved by the Agency for Bank Rehabilitation between 1991 and 1998, this paper constructs a dataset of 1,140 individual collateral disposals and estimates gross and net recovery rates for four collateral classes: residential real estate, commercial real estate, movable equipment, and guarantees. Ordinary least squares and Tobit regressions identify legal duration of enforcement proceedings, collateral-to-loan ratio at origination, and local real estate market depth as the principal determinants of recovery. Net recoveries average 31 percent of face value across all classes, falling to 17 percent for movable equipment. Commercial real estate in Vojvodina municipalities with functioning cadastral records showed recovery rates 14 percentage points higher than the national mean, pointing to the importance of property registry infrastructure. Policy implications for the sequencing of legal reforms accompanying bank resolution are discussed.

title: Servicer Moral Hazard in Delegated Loan Workout: Theory and Evidence from Hungarian and Romanian Markets
abstract: This paper models the principal–agent relationship between a bank selling a distressed loan portfolio and an external servicer contracted to manage collections. The model predicts that fixed-fee servicer contracts produce under-investment in costly recovery actions, while pure contingent-fee contracts may encourage premature settlement. An empirical test uses proprietary performance data from three delegated workout programmes executed in Hungary and Romania between 1999 and 2002, covering 8,300 retail and SME loan accounts. Estimation of a two-stage Heckman selection model shows that contingent-fee servicers achieve recovery rates 9.2 percentage points higher than fixed-fee servicers on comparable portfolios, but also settle accounts on average 47 days earlier, consistent with theoretical predictions about time-horizon distortions. The findings suggest that hybrid contract structures with a base fee, a contingency component, and a long-stop quality audit reduce moral hazard without unduly compressing servicer liquidity.

title: Thin Markets and Price Discovery in Non-Performing Loan Portfolios: Evidence from the Western Balkans
abstract: Secondary markets for distressed bank debt in the Western Balkans remain shallow: over the period 1998–2005, recorded arm's-length NPL portfolio sales in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia totalled fewer than forty transactions. This paper examines whether the bid–ask spreads observed in those transactions are consistent with information asymmetry models of thin-market pricing or whether they reflect primarily regulatory barriers to foreign servicer entry. Using transaction-level data assembled from central bank disclosures and Freedom of Information requests to resolution agencies, the study estimates a hedonic price model for portfolio characteristics including vintage, collateral mix, borrower sector, and legal status. The results suggest that information asymmetry accounts for roughly 55 percent of the observed discount to face value, while regulatory entry barriers explain an additional 28 percent. The paper proposes a standardised data-room protocol to reduce information gaps in future transactions.

title: Restructuring vs. Disposal: Bank-Level Incentives and the Choice of NPL Resolution Strategy in Serbia, 2002–2008
abstract: Serbian banks resolving non-performing loans between 2002 and 2008 faced a strategic choice between in-house workout, outright portfolio sale, and referral to external servicers. This paper uses regulatory supervisory data on 23 banks to estimate a multinomial logit model of resolution strategy selection as a function of bank capitalisation, management quality ratings, NPL concentration, and the vintage and sectoral composition of the impaired portfolio. Banks with capital adequacy ratios above 15 percent and relatively diversified NPL books were more likely to pursue internal workout; weakly capitalised banks with concentrated agriculture-sector exposures showed a strong propensity to defer resolution entirely. The paper documents that deferral is associated with higher ultimate loss rates and longer resolution timelines, consistent with the forbearance hypothesis. National Bank of Serbia supervisory implications are discussed, including proposed triggers for mandatory resolution timelines.

title: Legal Infrastructure and NPL Recovery: A Cross-Country Comparison of Creditor Rights Regimes in South-Eastern Europe
abstract: This chapter reviews the creditor rights environment across seven South-Eastern European jurisdictions—Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Bulgaria, and Romania—as they relate to unsecured and secured NPL recovery. The analysis draws on World Bank Doing Business enforcement indicators, national bankruptcy law texts, and a structured interview survey of 34 insolvency practitioners conducted in 2009–2010. It finds substantial cross-country variation in the time to enforce a secured claim (ranging from 340 days in Slovenia to over 900 days in Bosnia-Herzegovina) and in the formal priority of secured creditors in insolvency proceedings. The chapter argues that legal infrastructure heterogeneity partly explains the divergent development of secondary NPL markets across the region and outlines minimum harmonisation measures relevant to EU accession candidate countries. The analysis covers both pre- and post-global-financial-crisis legal reforms.

title: Post-Crisis NPL Accumulation in Serbian Corporate Banking: Sectoral Patterns and Servicer Capacity Constraints, 2009–2013
abstract: The global financial crisis triggered a sharp rise in non-performing corporate loans in Serbia, with the aggregate NPL ratio peaking at 21.4 percent in late 2012. This paper analyses National Bank of Serbia supervisory panel data covering 18 banks and approximately 4,200 corporate loan accounts to identify sectoral concentrations of NPL accumulation and to assess whether domestic servicer capacity was adequate to absorb the resulting workout demand. Survival analysis of time-to-resolution estimates shows that construction and real estate sector loans had median resolution periods exceeding 38 months, nearly twice the duration for manufacturing sector exposures. A capacity utilisation survey of 11 licensed workout servicers indicates that average caseload per analyst rose from 95 accounts in 2009 to 214 accounts in 2012, with statistically significant negative effects on recovery rates at caseloads above 160. Policy recommendations focus on servicer licensing standards and on the use of portfolio data rooms to attract foreign servicer entry.

title: Recovery Rate Determinants for SME NPLs Sold to Third-Party Servicers: Micro-Evidence from Serbia
abstract: Using a hand-collected dataset of 627 SME non-performing loan accounts sold to third-party servicers by three Serbian banks between 2010 and 2014, this paper estimates recovery rate determinants via a fractional response regression model. Explanatory variables include loan size, time since last payment, availability and type of collateral, sector of borrower activity, servicer contract type, and legal resolution channel used. Key findings are that collateral availability raises the expected recovery rate by 18 to 24 percentage points depending on type, while each additional year of account dormancy prior to sale reduces recovery by approximately 6.3 percentage points. Servicer use of out-of-court debt settlement agreements outperforms litigation-based channels by 11 percentage points in net present value terms after adjusting for resolution duration. The dataset is among the first micro-level SME NPL samples made available for academic analysis in the Western Balkan context.

title: NPL Resolution Progress in the Western Balkans, 2015–2022: A Comparative Policy Assessment
abstract: This paper provides a comparative assessment of NPL resolution progress across six Western Balkan economies over 2015–2022, drawing on IMF Article IV consultation reports, central bank financial stability reports, and European Commission progress reports. Aggregate NPL ratios fell substantially in all six jurisdictions, from a regional mean of 17.8 percent in 2015 to 6.4 percent in 2022, but the mechanisms and sustainability of reduction varied considerably. In Serbia and North Macedonia, reductions were driven primarily by bank write-offs and portfolio sales to foreign-owned servicers; in Bosnia-Herzegovina, by a combination of forbearance reclassification and collateral revaluation. The paper assesses whether reductions represent genuine resolution or accounting-level reclassification, using proxies derived from servicer registration data and secondary-market transaction volumes. It concludes that secondary market depth remains insufficient in four of the six jurisdictions to support durable resolution at scale and identifies regulatory and infrastructure bottlenecks that persist despite a decade of reform.

title: Postural responses to unexpected platform translations in goalball players with acquired versus congenital visual impairment
abstract: Twenty-four elite goalball athletes (12 with congenital, 12 with acquired visual impairment) and 12 sighted controls underwent a series of 20 randomised horizontal platform translations (peak velocity 25 cm/s, displacement 5 cm) on a motorised balance platform. Recovery time to return within a 5 mm CoP stability threshold, peak CoP displacement, and electromyographic (EMG) onset latency of tibialis anterior and gastrocnemius medialis were recorded. Athletes with congenital impairment showed significantly shorter recovery times (mean 1.09 s vs. 1.47 s in acquired group; p = 0.003) and lower peak CoP displacement in the AP direction. EMG onset latencies did not differ significantly between athlete subgroups, suggesting the advantage operates at a postural strategy level rather than reflex arc speed. Sighted controls fell intermediate on recovery time, indicating sport-specific training contributes independently of the mode of vision loss.

title: Reliability of force-plate measures during a standardised perturbation battery in visually impaired athletes: a test–retest study
abstract: Measurement reliability is a prerequisite for longitudinal balance assessment in adapted sport. This paper reports intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and minimal detectable change (MDC) values for eight CoP-derived variables obtained during a six-condition perturbation battery in 22 visually impaired athletes tested one week apart. Conditions included quiet standing with and without auditory white noise, foam surface standing, and three vibration tendon perturbation intensities applied bilaterally to the Achilles tendon. ICC values ranged from 0.78 to 0.94 across variables and conditions. MDC95 was 3.2 mm for quiet-stance AP range and 4.7 mm for ML mean velocity under foam. Variables recorded during the highest vibration intensity showed the weakest reliability (ICC 0.78), suggesting larger trial counts are needed. The battery and associated normative table are offered as a practical monitoring tool for coaches and sports medicine practitioners working in goalball.

title: Effect of a six-week proprioceptive training programme on static balance in junior visually impaired goalball athletes
abstract: A randomised controlled trial allocated 28 junior goalball players (B2–B3 classification, age 14–18) to a proprioceptive training group (PTG, n=14) or training-as-usual control group (CG, n=14) for six weeks. The PTG performed 20-minute proprioceptive circuit sessions three times weekly using wobble boards, uneven textured mats, and rhythmic perturbation tasks. Pre- and post-test CoP measures were collected on a force plate during 60-second quiet stance and a modified Star Excursion Balance Test conducted on the force plate. The PTG showed significant reductions in AP CoP mean velocity (−18.4%, p = 0.007) and ellipse area (−22.1%, p = 0.011) post-training. No significant changes were observed in the CG. Between-group effect sizes (Cohen's d) ranged from 0.72 to 0.91. Findings support incorporating structured proprioceptive work into junior goalball preparation.

title: Sensory conflict and balance in goalball: the effect of hearing protectors on postural sway during vibratory perturbation
abstract: Goalball athletes wear opaque eyeshades during competition and rely on auditory information for spatial orientation. This study examined whether reducing auditory input via hearing protectors (SNR 28 dB) modifies postural responses to bilateral Achilles tendon vibration (75 Hz, 60 seconds) in 20 experienced goalball athletes. A 2 × 2 (hearing protector: present/absent × vibration: present/absent) within-subjects design was used. The primary outcome was total CoP path length over 60 seconds. Vibration alone increased path length by 41% over quiet-stance baseline (p < 0.001). Adding hearing protectors to the vibration condition produced a further 19% increase in path length (p = 0.018), indicating that goalball athletes partially substitute ambient auditory cues for proprioceptive information during stance. The size of this auditory-proprioceptive substitution effect was positively correlated with years of playing experience (r = 0.61, p = 0.004).

title: Balance characteristics of the Serbian national goalball team in the season before and after a Paralympic cycle: a longitudinal observational study
abstract: This longitudinal study tracked eight members of the Serbian national goalball team over a four-year Paralympic preparation cycle (2016–2020, delayed to 2021). Three annual assessment sessions measured CoP variables, ground reaction force impulse during reactive stepping, and self-reported balance confidence (Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale). Mean AP range decreased from 28.4 mm at baseline to 21.7 mm at final assessment, a reduction of 23.6%. ML mean velocity showed a non-linear pattern, initially decreasing then plateauing in the pre-Paralympic year. Reactive stepping impulse improved monotonically across all three time points (p = 0.002, Friedman test). Balance confidence scores increased by 11 points on average. The trajectory suggests that postural control adaptation saturates before competition intensity peaks, which has implications for periodisation planning in Paralympic goalball.

title: Postural control under dual-task conditions in athletes with and without visual impairment: a comparison across sport disciplines
abstract: Dual-task paradigms reveal postural control automaticity. This cross-sectional study compared CoP measures during a cognitive arithmetic secondary task between four groups: visually impaired goalball players (n=15), visually impaired swimmers (n=15), sighted basketball players (n=15), and sighted non-athletes (n=15). All participants stood on a force plate for 60 seconds in single-task (stance only) and dual-task (stance plus serial-3 subtraction) conditions. Goalball players showed the smallest dual-task cost in ML CoP velocity (mean increase 6.4%), significantly lower than sighted non-athletes (28.2%, p < 0.001) and visually impaired swimmers (19.5%, p = 0.008). AP direction showed no significant group-by-task interaction. The pattern is consistent with more automated lateral postural control in goalball athletes, plausibly driven by years of training under full visual occlusion that requires concurrent cognitive processing during play.

title: Wearable inertial sensor versus force plate for monitoring standing balance in goalball athletes: a concurrent validity study
abstract: Force plates are impractical in field settings. This study evaluated the concurrent validity of a triaxial inertial measurement unit (IMU) worn at the L4–L5 level against Kistler force plate data in 26 visually impaired goalball athletes performing six 30-second standing balance trials per condition (firm, foam, vibration). Pearson correlations between IMU-derived root mean square acceleration and force-plate CoP mean velocity were r = 0.87 (AP) and r = 0.83 (ML) across all conditions. Bland-Altman analysis revealed acceptable limits of agreement for mean velocity (bias < 0.3 cm/s) but wider limits during the vibration condition. IMU-derived sway area correlated more weakly with force-plate 95% ellipse area (r = 0.71). An IMU at the lumbar position provides acceptable estimates of CoP velocity in adapted sports field assessments but should be used cautiously during high-frequency perturbation.

title: Centre-of-pressure complexity measures as indicators of balance training status in visually impaired goalball athletes
abstract: Nonlinear measures of CoP time series may capture adaptive postural control changes that linear statistics miss. This study applied approximate entropy (ApEn) and sample entropy (SampEn) to CoP data from 30 visually impaired goalball athletes stratified as experienced (≥5 years) or novice (< 2 years). Data were collected during 60-second quiet stance and a 60-second Achilles tendon vibration condition. Experienced athletes showed higher SampEn values in the ML direction under vibration (mean 1.34 vs. 1.02, p = 0.004), indicating more complex and adaptable postural fluctuations. AP SampEn did not differ between groups in either condition. ApEn results were directionally consistent but reached significance only under vibration. Regression analysis indicated years of goalball experience predicted ML SampEn under vibration (β = 0.054, R² = 0.38) independently of age and body mass index. Nonlinear metrics warrant inclusion in longitudinal monitoring protocols for adapted sport.

title: Perturbation-evoked postural adjustments in goalball: a conference report on classification and measurement considerations
abstract: This conference communication summarises methodological discussions from a workshop on balance assessment in visually impaired sport held at the 2022 European Congress of Adapted Physical Activity in Bratislava. Topics covered include the challenge of functional classification (B1–B3) heterogeneity in research samples, the choice of perturbation magnitude that avoids compensatory stepping in B1 athletes, and the comparability of CoP measures across laboratory force-plate systems. Preliminary unpublished data from the presenter's laboratory are described: a pilot sample of six B1 goalball athletes showed substantially larger CoP ellipse areas under foam surface conditions than the existing literature on B2–B3 athletes, underscoring the need for separate normative data by classification. Recommendations for a minimal reporting standard are proposed.

title: Trunk muscle activation patterns during unexpected lateral perturbation in visually impaired goalball athletes: surface EMG analysis
abstract: Lateral falls represent a specific risk in goalball due to the sport's lateral dive demands. This study examined surface EMG activation of external oblique, internal oblique, and quadratus lumborum during unexpected lateral tilts (5° at 50°/s) delivered by a motorised platform in 20 visually impaired goalball athletes and 20 sighted recreationally active controls. Response onset latency, peak normalised amplitude (% maximal voluntary contraction), and co-contraction index were computed. Goalball athletes showed shorter ipsilateral external oblique onset latencies (mean 87 ms vs. 112 ms; p < 0.001) and higher co-contraction indices compared with controls (p = 0.003). No group difference was found for quadratus lumborum onset. Peak normalised amplitude did not differ significantly between groups. The results indicate goalball-specific trunk motor preparation that may reduce lateral instability during play and landings.

title: Does sport classification moderate balance adaptation in goalball? Comparing B1, B2, and B3 athletes on a standardised perturbation battery
abstract: Despite the central role of visual impairment classification in Paralympic sport governance, few studies have examined whether B1, B2, and B3 athletes differ on objectively measured balance variables. This study recruited 45 competitive goalball athletes (15 per classification group) and administered a six-condition perturbation battery comprising quiet stance, foam surface, bilateral Achilles tendon vibration, and combinations thereof. Eight CoP variables were computed per condition. B1 athletes had significantly larger CoP 95% ellipse areas across all conditions (p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction), but showed equivalent or superior AP SampEn values relative to B2 and B3 athletes. Moderate classification-by-condition interactions were found for ML mean velocity during combined foam-vibration, with B1 athletes showing the steepest increase. These results suggest that classification group moderates perturbation sensitivity but not necessarily postural complexity, and that aggregating B1–B3 athletes in research samples may obscure clinically relevant differences.

title: Reliability of a multi-segment rigid-body model for upper-limb joint moment estimation in weightlifting
abstract: Test–retest reliability of a six-segment rigid-body model applied to Olympic weightlifting was assessed in nine male lifters who completed three testing sessions separated by seven days. Session-to-session intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC3,1) were calculated for peak net joint moments at the wrist, elbow, and shoulder across the snatch pull. ICC values ranged from 0.84 to 0.94 for shoulder and elbow moments and from 0.71 to 0.88 for wrist moments, indicating moderate-to-good reliability. Standard error of measurement for wrist peak moment was 6.8 N·m, corresponding to a minimal detectable change of 18.8 N·m. Sources of variability included skin marker displacement during rapid barbell acceleration and variability in hand segment mass estimation from regression equations. An updated anthropometric regression for the hand segment is proposed based on measurements from 44 male weightlifters, yielding reduced bias compared to existing cadaver-based equations.

title: Sweat rate prediction equations for ultra-trail runners in humid continental climates: validation and practical applicability
abstract: Prediction of sweat rate from meteorological variables and individual characteristics could support pre-race hydration planning without requiring individual sweat testing. This study used data from 87 runners across four races held over three consecutive summer seasons on Fruška Gora and the Vršac mountains, covering a range of ambient temperatures (22–34 °C) and relative humidity values (58–82%). Multiple linear regression modelling identified running pace, ambient temperature, relative humidity, and body mass as significant independent predictors of sweat rate (adjusted R² = 0.61). A simplified equation using only temperature and body mass retained 88% of the predictive variance of the full model. Cross-validation on a holdout sample of 21 runners from a 2023 race yielded a mean absolute error of 0.14 L·h⁻¹. The model performed best in the moderate temperature range (24–28 °C) and was least accurate for runners below 60 kg body mass. Practical tables derived from the model are provided for race organisers and coaches.

title: Admission Control in Multi-Class Server Farms: A Queueing Network Approach
abstract: This paper analyses admission control policies for server farms handling multiple classes of jobs with heterogeneous service requirements. The system is modelled as a network of M/G/k queues with class-dependent priority disciplines. Using matrix-analytic methods, we derive closed-form approximations for mean sojourn time and rejection probability under static threshold policies. Experiments on a simulated cluster of 128 nodes with four job classes and workloads drawn from traces of a 2009 academic computing grid show that a threshold vector tuned by a gradient-descent procedure reduces mean sojourn time by 18% compared to a FCFS baseline while keeping rejection below 2%. The analysis also identifies a concavity property of the throughput function that enables efficient policy search. The results carry implications for admission control design in shared infrastructure where quality-of-service targets must be maintained per job class.

title: Online Scheduling of Batch Jobs on Heterogeneous Clusters with Release Dates
abstract: We study the online scheduling problem in which jobs arrive over time with release dates, processing times that are unknown until completion, and must be assigned to machines of differing speeds. The objective is to minimise weighted completion time. A Longest-Processing-Time-first (LPT) strategy is adapted for the online setting using a lazy migration rule that avoids excessive job movement between machines. The analysis proves a competitive ratio of O(log n) for the adapted algorithm when processing times follow a log-normal distribution with parameters estimated from a three-month trace of a bioinformatics cluster at the University of Pécs. Simulation experiments confirm that in practice the algorithm achieves within 7% of an offline lower bound. Runtime overhead introduced by the migration-check procedure is below 1% of total scheduling overhead at cluster sizes up to 512 nodes.
