title: Modelling Auto-Scaling Latency in Cloud Platforms as a Transient Queue
abstract: Auto-scaling services react to load changes with a non-negligible spin-up delay, typically between 30 and 180 seconds on public cloud platforms. This paper models the system as an M/M/c queue with a time-inhomogeneous arrival process and delayed capacity increments. Transient state probabilities are computed numerically using uniformisation, and the impact of spin-up delay on queue length distribution and mean waiting time is characterised for workloads with sinusoidal and burst-shaped arrival patterns. Using publicly released workload data from a European e-government portal (anonymised, 90-day window, peak arrival rate 320 requests/second), the model predicts 95th-percentile response times within 11% of measurements during load ramp-up events. The paper derives a practical rule relating acceptable delay to the coefficient of variation of the inter-arrival time, offering a design guide for platform operators.

title: Resource Fragmentation in Multi-Tenant Clouds: Measurement and Mitigation
abstract: Resource fragmentation occurs when allocated virtual machines leave portions of physical hosts unusable due to mismatched CPU-to-memory ratios. This chapter reviews fragmentation metrics proposed in the literature, proposes a unified fragmentation index based on vector packing residuals, and surveys mitigation strategies including defragmentation via live migration, skewed VM flavours, and admission shaping. A case study using a 60-day operational trace from a fictional regional cloud provider with 48 physical hosts and approximately 900 concurrent VMs illustrates how the fragmentation index evolves over time and how a weekly defragmentation schedule reduces index values by 34% with a mean migration cost of 1.2 seconds of service interruption per VM. The chapter concludes with an open problem formulation connecting fragmentation control to the online vector bin-packing literature.

title: A Fluid Model for Workload Burstiness and Its Effect on Scheduler Performance
abstract: Bursty workloads violate the Poisson assumption underlying classical queueing analysis. This paper replaces the Poisson arrival model with a Markov-modulated fluid process parameterised by burstiness ratio and burst duration, and derives steady-state buffer content distributions analytically for a single-server fluid queue. The derived distributions are validated against discrete-event simulation using synthetic traces with burstiness ratios between 1.1 and 4.0. The model is then used to predict the degradation of three scheduling policies—FIFO, Shortest Job First, and Least Laxity—under increasing burstiness. Results show that Shortest Job First degrades least rapidly but requires accurate job-size estimation, while Least Laxity suffers from instability at burstiness ratios above 2.5 unless a smoothing window is applied. Parametric guidance for selecting the smoothing window width as a function of burst duration is provided.

title: Deadline-Aware Scheduling for Mixed Batch and Interactive Workloads on Shared Clusters
abstract: Shared computing clusters serving both interactive and batch workloads must balance tight deadline requirements of interactive tasks against the throughput needs of long-running batch jobs. We formulate the problem as an online scheduling problem with two priority classes, hard deadlines for the interactive class, and a weighted sum of tardy batch jobs as secondary objective. A modified Earliest-Deadline-First algorithm with batch back-fill is proposed and evaluated on traces from a university computing centre comprising 11 months of mixed workloads (approximately 230,000 jobs). The algorithm reduces interactive task deadline violation rate from 6.1% under simple priority scheduling to 1.4%, while reducing batch job mean slowdown from 3.8 to 2.9. The trade-off between interactive reliability and batch throughput is characterised as a Pareto frontier parameterised by a single back-fill aggressiveness parameter.

title: Energy-Aware Server Consolidation Using Lyapunov Drift Optimisation
abstract: Server consolidation reduces energy consumption by concentrating workloads onto fewer active hosts, but aggressive consolidation increases queueing delays. This paper applies Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty optimisation to dynamically control consolidation level, trading off energy consumption against a penalty for exceeding per-class response time targets. The control policy requires no prior knowledge of arrival rates and adapts to load changes in O(1) computation per scheduling epoch. Experiments on an OpenStack testbed with 16 physical nodes and workloads replaying a 7-day e-commerce trace show that the Lyapunov policy achieves energy savings of 22% compared to no consolidation and 8% compared to a threshold-based policy, while keeping 98.3% of requests within their response time targets. The paper proves that the policy maintains queue stability under any feasible load.

title: Bin-Packing Approximations for Container Scheduling in Microservice Architectures
abstract: Container-based microservice deployments generate scheduling problems where each container specifies requests and limits for CPU, memory, and network bandwidth, resulting in a three-dimensional vector bin-packing instance. This paper studies the approximation guarantees of five algorithms—FFD, Best-Fit Decreasing, a randomised rounding LP relaxation, a greedy list-scheduling heuristic, and a simulated-annealing post-processor—on both synthetic instances and a Kubernetes scheduling trace from an internal platform of a fictional logistics company (52,000 container placement decisions over 14 days). Approximation ratios are measured as excess node count over a lower bound derived from fractional relaxation. The LP-rounding approach achieves the best theoretical guarantee (2 OPT+3) and performs within 4% of optimal on trace instances, at the cost of 120 ms average runtime versus under 5 ms for FFD.

title: Sensitivity of Queueing-Based SLA Models to Arrival Process Misspecification
abstract: Service-level agreements (SLAs) in cloud computing are often derived from M/M/c or M/G/c queueing models, which assume Poisson arrivals. This paper quantifies the error incurred when the true arrival process has heavier autocorrelation structure—specifically, when it follows a Markov-modulated Poisson process (MMPP)—but is fitted and evaluated as if Poisson. A systematic experiment varies the MMPP correlation coefficient from 0 to 0.85 and the coefficient of variation of service times from 1.0 to 3.0. Mean waiting time prediction error grows from under 5% at low correlation to over 60% at high correlation, with strong interaction with service time variability. Practical recommendations are made for operators: re-estimate arrival processes at intervals no longer than 10 minutes during peak periods, and apply a safety margin of at least 15% to SLA threshold parameters derived under Poisson assumptions.

title: Preprint: Regret Bounds for Online Vector Bin Packing with Stochastic Item Arrivals
abstract: Online bin-packing algorithms must assign items to bins without knowledge of future items. In the stochastic setting where item sizes are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution, learning algorithms can exploit observed history to improve decisions. This preprint formulates the problem in an adversarial-then-stochastic framework and analyses the regret—measured as excess bins opened—of a UCB-style algorithm that maintains empirical size distributions and uses them to bias item-to-bin assignment probabilities. For d-dimensional items and bins of unit capacity in each dimension, an upper regret bound of O(d · T^{2/3} log T) is derived for horizon T, and a lower bound of Ω(d · T^{1/2}) is conjectured. Numerical experiments on synthetic 3-dimensional instances with 10,000 items confirm that empirical regret grows roughly as T^{0.59}, between the two bounds. The preprint also discusses implications for cloud scheduling when job resource footprints can be partially predicted from job metadata.

title: Workload Trace Characterisation for Distributed Cloud Scheduling Benchmarks: A Multi-Site Study
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of cloud scheduling algorithms requires workload traces that reflect realistic job mix, resource heterogeneity, and temporal patterns. This paper collects and characterises traces from four academic computing sites in Serbia, Croatia, Hungary, and Romania, covering a combined 18-month window and approximately 2.1 million job submissions. Statistical properties analysed include inter-arrival time distributions, job size (CPU × memory × duration) distributions, diurnal and weekly periodicity, and user-level burstiness. Fitted distributions are compared against Pareto, log-normal, and phase-type families; the heavy-tailed Pareto fits job duration and memory request marginals best, while inter-arrival times are well-modelled by MMPP(2) processes. A synthetic trace generator calibrated to these parameters is released alongside the paper, enabling controlled benchmark generation. The characterisation reveals systematic differences between sites that caution against generalising results from single-site studies.

title: A Branch-and-Bound Approach to Freight Consolidation on Sparse Rail Networks
abstract: This paper considers the problem of consolidating less-than-truckload freight shipments on a sparse fixed-route rail network modelled as a directed graph with 42 nodes and 67 arcs. An integer programming formulation is presented in which binary variables encode assignment of shipment batches to departure slots, and capacity constraints are imposed at each arc. A branch-and-bound algorithm is implemented and compared against a greedy earliest-departure heuristic on 120 randomly generated instances with demand drawn from empirical distributions derived from a Central European regional operator. The branch-and-bound procedure finds provably optimal solutions for instances with up to 200 shipments within a two-hour time limit in 91% of cases. Average cost reduction relative to the greedy baseline is 14.3%. The formulation is extended to handle transshipment nodes and the resulting increase in integrality gap is analysed.

title: Wrapping-Effect Reduction in Interval Taylor Solvers for Stiff Initial-Value Problems
abstract: Stiff ordinary differential equations pose particular difficulties for interval Taylor solvers because error accumulation from the wrapping effect can cause enclosures to grow rapidly. This paper analyses the sources of wrapping-effect inflation in step-by-step Taylor integration and introduces a coordinate-transformation strategy based on a QR-factored Jacobian evaluated at each grid point. The method is implemented within a prototype solver written in MATLAB using INTLAB for directed rounding. Numerical experiments on five benchmark stiff systems, including the Robertson chemical kinetics model and a linearised van der Pol oscillator at large parameter values, demonstrate that enclosure diameters are reduced by factors between 3.1 and 11.7 compared with a plain interval Taylor solver of the same order. Convergence and termination criteria are discussed and step-size control is adapted to maintain both verified inclusion and computational efficiency. Runtime overhead relative to non-rigorous integration is measured and kept below 40% for the tested systems.

title: Conditional tail expectation for bivariate environmental risk under asymmetric dependence
abstract: The conditional tail expectation (CTE), also known as expected shortfall, is a coherent risk measure widely used in financial risk management but less frequently applied to environmental hazard quantification. This paper derives analytical expressions for the bivariate CTE when the dependence structure belongs to the class of Archimedean copulas with completely monotone generators, covering the Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard and Joe families. The expressions are used to compute the expected discharge at one gauging station given that discharge at a second station simultaneously exceeds its empirical 95th, 99th and 99.9th percentiles, using records from eleven paired stations in the Tisza basin. Clayton copula fits indicate substantial asymmetry in lower and upper tail dependence, and the resulting CTEs are 12 to 38 percent higher than those implied by the bivariate Gaussian model with matched Kendall τ. Simulation experiments confirm the accuracy of the analytical results for sample sizes as small as n = 200.

title: Seasonal Soundscape Variation in Agricultural Lowlands: A Pilot Survey of Three Villages in the Bačka Region
abstract: This paper reports on a twelve-month field recording campaign conducted between 2008 and 2009 across three villages in the Bačka subregion of Vojvodina. Using a pair of omnidirectional microphones mounted at fixed monitoring points, continuous 24-hour recordings were made during four seasonal windows, yielding approximately 288 hours of raw audio. Spectral analysis was performed using short-time Fourier transforms, and acoustic indices including the Acoustic Complexity Index and Bioacoustic Index were computed across all sessions. Results showed pronounced low-frequency anthropogenic intrusion in summer months correlated with combine harvester activity, peaking between 75 and 82 dB(A) in open field positions. Winter recordings revealed the lowest overall energy levels but the highest proportion of naturally occurring ambient sound. The study argues that even within a single agricultural landscape, seasonal variation substantially alters the perceptual character of a soundscape, and that a minimum of four seasonal recording windows is methodologically necessary for meaningful documentation. Recommendations for standardised monitoring protocols in lowland agricultural settings are outlined.
venue: Journal of Central European Sound Studies

title: Documenting the Auditory Memory of Flood-Plain Villages along the Tisa River: Methods and Preliminary Findings
abstract: Several settlements along the Tisa River in northern Serbia have experienced significant demographic decline and partial abandonment since the mid-1990s, making systematic acoustic documentation urgent before habitual community sounds are lost entirely. This paper describes the fieldwork methodology developed for a pilot documentation campaign in four villages between 2010 and 2011. The approach integrated fixed-position stereo recording, mobile walkthrough sessions, and structured listening interviews with residents aged over 60. A total of 114 hours of audio were collected alongside 31 recorded interviews. Interviews were transcribed and coded using thematic analysis, with recurring sonic categories including church bells, water mill remnants, seasonal bird populations, and agricultural machinery of Soviet-era manufacture. Cross-referencing archival audio held at Radio Novi Sad with fresh recordings exposed substantial changes in ambient biological sound over roughly four decades. The paper discusses ethical dimensions of recording in communities with declining populations and proposes a consent and archiving framework suitable for heritage sound work in rural Serbia.

title: Low-Frequency Noise Accumulation in Novi Sad's Inner-City Courtyards: A Comparative Study Across Four Neighbourhoods
abstract: Interior courtyards in the older residential quarters of Novi Sad present a distinctive acoustic condition: semi-enclosed geometries that selectively trap certain frequency bands while attenuating others. This study measured and characterised the low-frequency noise environment in 22 courtyards distributed across the Liman, Podbara, Adamovićevo Naselje, and Staro Sajmište neighbourhoods during 2012. Measurements were taken using a calibrated class-1 sound level meter with octave-band filtering, supplemented by impulse response captures using a dodecahedron loudspeaker. Mean equivalent continuous sound levels (LAeq) ranged from 48 to 67 dB(A) depending on proximity to arterial roads. Octave band analysis indicated persistent energy below 125 Hz in all courtyards bordering major streets, attributed primarily to diesel bus and heavy goods vehicle traffic. The study establishes a baseline dataset for four representative urban morphologies and discusses implications for future urban planning decisions and for the long-term acoustic monitoring of a city undergoing rapid construction activity.

title: The Soundscape Archive as Cultural Heritage Object: Theoretical Frameworks and Practical Constraints
abstract: This book chapter examines the status of sound archives produced through systematic acoustic ecology fieldwork and asks whether such archives can and should be considered cultural heritage objects in their own right, rather than merely documentary instruments. Drawing on archival theory, heritage studies, and the author's own fieldwork across Vojvodina, the chapter surveys existing frameworks for the preservation of intangible cultural heritage and assesses their adequacy for time-stamped environmental audio. The argument proceeds through three sections: first, a review of how UNESCO conventions address sonic heritage; second, a critique of current digitisation and metadata standards used by national sound archives in the Western Balkans; and third, a proposal for a minimum metadata schema tailored to acoustic ecology deposits, covering geolocation precision, recording equipment specifications, weather conditions, and observer annotations. The chapter concludes that without deliberate institutional frameworks treating soundscape recordings as primary heritage objects rather than supplementary data, the long-term accessibility and interpretability of such archives cannot be guaranteed.

title: Binaural Capture Protocols for Immersive Re-presentation of Vanishing Rural Soundscapes
abstract: As binaural playback over headphones becomes a standard delivery format for documentary audio, the field recording community requires evidence-based protocols for capturing rural soundscapes in ways that preserve perceptual spatial fidelity under headphone reproduction. This paper reports on a comparative evaluation of four binaural recording configurations—two in-ear microphone placements on human subjects and two dummy-head systems—conducted across eight rural sites in Vojvodina in 2015. Stimuli from each configuration were presented to 24 listeners in a controlled playback session and evaluated on scales of externalisation, front-back confusion, and naturalness. The dummy-head configuration with custom pinnae showed significantly higher externalisation ratings (mean 4.2 out of 5) compared to the in-ear placement mounted superficially above the pinna (mean 3.1). Front-back confusion rates were substantially lower for the dummy-head in open-field settings with diffuse sound sources. Practical recommendations are drawn for researchers undertaking heritage soundscape capture with limited budgets, including a ranking of commercially available binaural systems tested in the field.
venue: Journal of Applied Acoustics and Audio Technology

title: Tracing Industrial Sonic Residue: Former Factory Sites in Novi Sad and Their Acoustic Transformation After Deindustrialisation
abstract: Between 1989 and 2005, more than a dozen large industrial enterprises in Novi Sad ceased operations, transforming former factory sites into zones of redevelopment, dereliction, or informal use. This paper investigates the acoustic traces of this transformation by triangulating three types of evidence: 24-hour ambient recordings made at six former industrial sites in 2016–2017, oral history interviews with 18 former workers and residents, and archival documents including industrial noise impact assessments held at the City of Novi Sad archive. The ambient recordings were analysed for soundscape composition using the N-ATIS index battery and manual annotation of sound event categories. All sites showed dominance of low-amplitude biological and meteorological sound sources, a near-complete disappearance of impulsive mechanical transients characteristic of production environments, and gradual colonisation by passerine bird species. Oral history accounts foregrounded the affective dimension of sonic loss, with several informants describing the silence following closure as initially distressing. The paper frames deindustrialisation as a soundscape event and discusses methods for producing archival representations that hold both the acoustic and the testimonial record.

title: Long-Term Monitoring of a Peri-Urban Wetland Soundscape: Eight Years of Data from Koviljsko-Petrovaradinski Rit
abstract: This paper presents results from an eight-year continuous monitoring programme at Koviljsko-Petrovaradinski Rit, a protected wetland complex immediately east of Novi Sad. Monitoring equipment included weatherproofed remote recording units deployed at three positions within the reserve, programmed to capture one-hour recordings at dawn, midday, and dusk on the first and fifteenth of each month from 2010 to 2018. The resulting dataset totals approximately 1,440 recordings and 1,440 hours of audio. Acoustic index time series revealed a statistically significant decline in the Bioacoustic Index at all three stations between 2010 and 2015, followed by partial recovery correlating with a restriction on motorised recreational access introduced in 2016. Anthropogenic index scores showed a monotonic increase throughout the period, driven by growth in road traffic on the adjacent bypass route. Spectral analysis confirmed progressive encroachment of low-frequency traffic noise into previously quieter frequency windows during breeding season dawn choruses. The dataset is deposited in an open-access repository and the paper discusses the archival schema used.

title: Encoding Place in Sound: Metadata Standards for Geolocated Environmental Audio in Open Repository Systems
abstract: Open-access repositories for environmental audio are proliferating, but metadata standards remain inconsistent across platforms, limiting interoperability and long-term reuse. This paper proposes a structured metadata schema for geolocated environmental audio deposits, drawing on practical experience from ten years of fieldwork archiving across Vojvodina and comparative review of six existing repository systems in Europe. The proposed schema contains 34 mandatory and 21 optional fields grouped into five modules: geographic, temporal, technical, ecological context, and observer annotation. Geographic fields include coordinate precision class, altitude, land cover type derived from CORINE classification, and distance to nearest persistent noise source. Technical fields encode microphone type, polar pattern, recording device, gain settings, and post-processing applied. The paper reports on a pilot implementation of the schema using 312 recordings deposited in a locally hosted instance of an open-source repository platform, and evaluates completeness and retrieval performance against a reference query set. Recommendations are made for adoption by regional sound archives and for alignment with existing Dublin Core and PREMIS frameworks.

title: Soundscape Quality Assessment in Four Novi Sad Public Squares Before and After Pedestrianisation: A Repeated-Measures Study
abstract: The City of Novi Sad undertook pedestrianisation works in four central squares between 2019 and 2022. This study exploited that temporal sequence to conduct before-and-after acoustic measurements and perceptual assessments at each site, providing a quasi-experimental dataset on how removal of vehicular traffic reshapes urban soundscape quality. Ambient recordings and sound level measurements were taken at each site during morning and evening peak periods before construction began and again twelve months after completion. Forty-eight resident volunteers completed standardised ISO 12913 perceptual assessments on each occasion. LAeq reductions ranged from 4.2 to 9.7 dB(A) across sites. Perceptual pleasantness scores improved significantly at three of the four squares, while the fourth showed no significant change, attributable to increased outdoor café noise replacing traffic. Acoustic index analysis confirmed the addition of audible fountain and bird activity at two refurbished squares. The paper discusses the mismatch between objective level reduction and perceptual improvement and suggests that replacement sound sources need deliberate design attention rather than passive emergence.

title: Field Recording Practice as Ethnographic Method: Reflexive Accounts from Ten Years of Work in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper takes a reflexive methodological stance on the practice of environmental field recording when conducted within inhabited communities rather than uninhabited natural environments. Drawing on fieldwork notes, participant reactions, and recorded material gathered across approximately 40 sites in Vojvodina between 2010 and 2022, the paper examines how the presence of recording equipment affects community behaviour, how decisions about what to record and how long to linger implicitly produce an argument about sonic significance, and how the archival disposition of recordings shapes future interpretive possibilities. Three extended case studies are drawn upon: a Roma settlement undergoing forced relocation, a Hungarian-speaking agricultural village resisting consolidation into a larger municipality, and a fishing community on the Danube whose seasonal camps have become permanent. The paper resists prescriptive conclusions but argues that field recording in social contexts carries ethnographic obligations that purely technical protocols do not address, and that training programmes in acoustic ecology should include substantive engagement with social research ethics.

title: Comparative Acoustic Ecology of Market Squares in Five Pannonian Cities: Sonic Indicators of Urban Vitality
abstract: This paper reports on a coordinated comparative study of outdoor market soundscapes in five mid-sized cities of the Pannonian region: Novi Sad, Subotica, Sombor, Zrenjanin, and Kikinda. At each site, recordings were made on three consecutive market days during spring 2024 using identical equipment and placement protocols. Sound event annotation was performed by two trained listeners working independently, with inter-rater reliability measured by Cohen's kappa (mean 0.81 across categories). Dominant sound event categories across all sites included vendor calls, trolley and cart movement, crowd murmur, and live music performance. Significant site-to-site variation was observed in the proportion of human voice to mechanical sound, and in the frequency and character of vendor calls, which showed distinct regional accent patterns and calling conventions. Principal component analysis of acoustic index matrices clustered Novi Sad and Subotica together and separated Sombor and Kikinda as lower-intensity soundscapes. The paper proposes that systematic sound event composition can serve as a proxy indicator of market economic activity and social density, and that longitudinal monitoring of market soundscapes offers a non-invasive approach to tracking urban vitality.

title: Adaptive music and sound layering in a browser-based puzzle game: a design study
abstract: This paper reports the design, implementation, and informal evaluation of a fully procedural audio system for a browser-based puzzle game developed as a teaching project at the Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad. The system uses a state machine with seven game states (idle, exploration, puzzle active, near-solution, solved, failed, transition) to drive both musical layer selection and ambient sound density. Musical material was pre-composed in 4-bar loops at three energy levels; granular synthesis supplied background environmental textures. A group of 22 student players completed a structured play session followed by a semi-structured interview. Analysis of interviews identified that players noticed music-state mismatches more readily than ambience mismatches, and that abrupt transitions caused higher reported distraction than crossfades of 1.5 seconds or longer. The findings are discussed in terms of design guidelines for small-team game audio production.

title: Procedural audio for museum visitor flow simulation: integrating occupancy sensing with generative soundscape synthesis
abstract: This paper reports a deployment study in which a procedural audio system was integrated with a real-time visitor occupancy sensing installation in a temporary exhibition at the Museum of Contemporary Art Vojvodina, Novi Sad. Passive infrared sensors in five zones fed occupancy counts at 2-second intervals to a granular synthesis engine generating spatialised ambient sound on a 16-channel ring array. The system ran continuously for 19 days. Occupancy counts correlated positively with synthesised grain density (r = 0.81, p < 0.001 across 4,560 2-second intervals). Visitor exit surveys (n = 211) asked about perceived atmosphere; 68% indicated the sound environment felt appropriate to the space and visitor activity. Staff interviews noted that the system occasionally produced artefacts during rapid transitions caused by school group arrivals, interpreted as a boundary condition for the density model. Failure modes and recommended parameter bounds are documented.

title: Proprioceptive Feedback Loops in Interactive Stage Environments
abstract: This book chapter, drawn from the author's doctoral research, presents a theoretical and practical account of proprioceptive feedback loops constructed between a performer's body and a visually responsive stage environment. The chapter reviews relevant literature from somatic practice (Body-Mind Centering, Feldenkrais Method), ecological psychology (Gibson's affordance theory), and human-computer interaction (enactive computing). It then describes a series of four installation-performances in which performers wore IMU arrays on eight body segments, with orientation and acceleration data driving a spatial audio-visual environment built in Unity. The chapter discusses how performers reported qualitative shifts in body awareness after repeated sessions, and how the visual environment's responsiveness appeared to modulate movement quality as assessed through video analysis. Technical details of the IMU network, synchronisation protocol, and Unity integration are provided in an appendix. The chapter argues that the concept of the feedback loop must account for perceptual lag, calibration drift, and performer habituation as structurally significant rather than merely technical problems.

title: Sensor Dropout and Choreographic Adaptation: A Study of System Reliability in Live Biosensor Performances
abstract: Wearable biosensor systems used in live performance are subject to signal dropout events caused by electrode displacement, Bluetooth interference, and battery depletion. This paper presents a systematic study of dropout events across 18 performances at four venues in Serbia and Croatia over one festival season, using a logging middleware that timestamped and classified each dropout by modality (sEMG, IMU, HR) and duration. Across 18 performances totalling approximately 9 hours of stage time, 143 discrete dropout events were recorded, with a mean duration of 4.2 seconds and a maximum of 31 seconds. sEMG dropouts accounted for 58% of events. The paper analyses how two performers reported adapting choreographically in response to perceived visual system failures and compares these accounts with the timestamped log data. It proposes a set of design heuristics for graceful degradation—fallback visual states that remain aesthetically coherent—and evaluates three fallback strategies through a structured feedback process with the performers and a directing collaborator.

title: Comparative Assessment of Three Low-Cost IMU Platforms for Dance Research Applications
abstract: This paper compares three commercially available, low-cost IMU platforms—referred to as Platform A, B, and C to avoid brand endorsement—on criteria relevant to dance and performance research: orientation accuracy, wireless range, sampling rate stability, battery life, and ease of integration with common creative coding environments. Tests were conducted in a controlled motion-capture laboratory using a mechanical arm with known angular trajectories as ground truth. Orientation error was assessed using the root mean squared error of quaternion difference across 120-second continuous recordings. Platform A achieved the lowest mean orientation RMSE (2.1°) but exhibited the highest dropout rate over Bluetooth (11.3 dropouts per hour). Platform C showed the most stable wireless connection and longest battery life (6.2 hours) at the cost of a fixed 50 Hz sampling rate. The paper also includes practical notes from deployment in four rehearsal contexts, addressing issues such as costume integration, performer comfort, and warm-up time for sensor stabilisation. Recommendations are made for different use scenarios.

title: Designing Visual Feedback for Group Somatic Practices: A Pilot with Five Performers
abstract: Most biosensor-driven performance systems are designed for solo performers. This paper reports on a pilot study extending a multi-channel sEMG and HRV system to a group of five performers working collectively within a contact improvisation framework. Each performer wore a two-channel sEMG wrist band and a chest HR monitor. Individual physiological streams were merged into aggregate features (group mean HRV coherence, maximum sEMG activation across performers) and used to drive a shared projected visual field. Over six three-hour rehearsal sessions and one public sharing event, data were collected through video observation, structured post-session interviews, and a custom logging system. Analysis of interview transcripts identified three recurring themes: heightened awareness of group states, confusion about which performer was influencing which visual element, and an emergent tendency toward synchronisation of breath and stillness at high-coherence moments. The paper discusses design implications for shared physiological feedback displays and recommends explicit visual attribution strategies for multi-performer setups.

title: Skin Conductance Response as a Scenographic Element: Technical Constraints and Performer Perspectives
abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), often measured as skin conductance response (SCR), is frequently discussed in affective computing literature but rarely deployed in live performance contexts. This paper documents a performance research process in which SCR signals from two performers were used to modulate the density and colour temperature of programmable LED lighting rigs across a 22-minute piece. Technical challenges included the 1–3 second response latency inherent to EDA, high sensitivity to electrode pressure artefacts caused by movement, and the difficulty of distinguishing thermoregulatory from emotionally driven responses during physically demanding performance. Two electrode placements (fingertip and volar forearm) were compared across 14 rehearsal sessions; the volar forearm placement produced 34% fewer movement artefacts. Performers were interviewed using a phenomenological approach adapted from Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis. Both reported that lighting changes felt most connected to experienced emotional states in slower, more stationary passages of the work, and disconnected during high-movement sequences. The paper concludes with revised signal-processing recommendations for EDA in movement-rich performance.

title: Towards Standardised Reporting for Biosensor-Based Performance Research: A Methodological Proposal
abstract: The field of biosensor-driven performance research lacks shared reporting conventions, making it difficult to compare results across studies. This preprint proposes a minimum reporting standard comprising nine items: sensor type and placement, sampling rate, signal processing pipeline (with version numbers of software used), calibration procedure, number and experience level of performers, number and duration of sessions, data logging method, method of evaluating the perceptual or expressive outcome, and a description of system failure events. The proposal is grounded in a review of 41 published studies from 2008 to 2024 that the authors identified through database searches of performance studies, HCI, and biomedical engineering literature. Of these, only 7 reported all nine items. The preprint invites community response and provides an example reporting template formatted for both journal articles and conference proceedings. A companion spreadsheet of the 41 reviewed studies is included as supplementary material.

title: Breath-Driven Generative Visual Systems in Mindfulness-Based Performance: A Cross-Cultural Study
abstract: This paper examines the use of respiratory signals—captured via a custom elastic chest-band sensor with a resistive stretch element—as the primary driver of generative visual output in two parallel mindfulness-based performance works created independently in Novi Sad, Serbia, and Ljubljana, Slovenia, using an agreed common technical framework. Each work involved six performers, eight rehearsal sessions, and two public performances. Breath rate, inhalation-to-exhalation ratio, and breath depth were extracted and mapped to visual parameters (cloud particle count, opacity, and drift velocity) in a shared TouchDesigner template. Post-performance audience surveys (n=47 Novi Sad, n=51 Ljubljana) used a 7-point Likert scale to assess perceived calm, perceived connection between performer and image, and aesthetic satisfaction. Mean scores for perceived calm were 5.6 (Novi Sad) and 5.3 (Ljubljana); perceived connection scores were 4.9 and 5.1 respectively. The paper discusses minor mapping-parameter differences introduced by each creative team and their measurable effects on audience perception scores.

title: Spectral Layering as a Compositional Strategy in Interactive Audio Installations
abstract: This study documents the design and audience reception of an interactive sound installation, Sediment, exhibited at the Novi Sad Cultural Centre in 2012. The piece used real-time spectral layering controlled by visitor movement tracked through a grid of 16 infrared proximity sensors. Spectral layers were generated procedurally using SuperCollider, with each sensor zone mapped to a distinct frequency band between 80 Hz and 8 kHz. Visitor trajectories were logged over a four-week exhibition period totalling approximately 1,200 individual visits. Qualitative post-visit interviews with 38 visitors and structured observation sessions with 12 recruited participants informed the analysis. Findings indicate that visitors consistently modulated their movement speed in response to sonic feedback, suggesting bidirectional behavioural influence between body movement and sound output. The paper discusses implications for designing participatory installations that foreground sonic agency without requiring prior musical knowledge.

title: Algorithmic Accompaniment for Oral Storytelling Performances: A Field Study
abstract: This paper reports on a two-year collaboration with three professional oral storytellers in the Vojvodina region to develop and evaluate an algorithmic accompaniment system that responds to speech prosody in real time. The system used pitch detection and speech energy envelope analysis to select and crossfade between procedurally generated textural layers in SuperCollider. Performers wore a Bluetooth headset microphone feeding a latency-compensated audio interface; end-to-end system latency was measured at 22 ms, which performers described as imperceptible in post-session debriefs. Three public performances were documented through audio-visual recording and followed by audience questionnaires (n = 67, 74, and 52 per event). Audiences rated the perceived integration of voice and accompaniment at 4.1 out of 5 on average. Challenges included prosodic variability across languages (Serbian and Hungarian were both used) and performer adaptation to the system's response curve, which required a rehearsal period of roughly six hours per performer.

title: Tactical Media
abstract: This book chapter provides an overview of the tactical media concept from its emergence at the Next Five Minutes festivals (Amsterdam, 1993–2003) through to its dispersal into social media-era practice. The chapter traces the intellectual genealogy of the term through contributions by David Garcia, Geert Lovink, and Critical Art Ensemble, then maps how Eastern European practitioners adopted, translated, and contested the concept within their specific post-socialist contexts. The chapter draws on archival research in three institutional collections in the Netherlands, Hungary, and Serbia, and on secondary literature across media studies, art history, and political theory. A section on legacy considers how tactical media's insistence on temporality and ephemerality complicates retrospective canonisation, a process now underway in several European contemporary art museums. The chapter is addressed to advanced undergraduates and postgraduate researchers entering the field.

title: Participatory Web Projects as Collective Memory Practice: Three Cases from Serbia, 2005–2015
abstract: This article examines three long-duration participatory web projects initiated by Serbian artists and collectives between 2005 and 2015, each of which solicited user-contributed materials—photographs, personal testimonies, audio recordings—to construct crowd-sourced archives of recent traumatic history. The projects are analysed through the frameworks of collective memory studies (Assmann, Halbwachs) and participatory art theory (Bishop, Kester). The study draws on semi-structured interviews with the three project initiators, download statistics and contributor metadata from project servers, and ethnographic observation of two offline events connected to the projects. Contributor analysis shows that all three projects attracted predominantly urban, university-educated users under forty, raising questions about whose memories are assembled and whose are absent. The article also addresses how platform migration and link rot have affected the projects' ongoing accessibility and reflects on the implications for memory studies of ephemeral digital archives.

title: Teaching Tactical Media: Curriculum Challenges in a Post-Yugoslav Art Academy
abstract: This paper reports on a five-year curriculum development process at the Department of Digital Arts, Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad, where an undergraduate module on tactical media and net.art was introduced in 2014 and revised in 2016 and 2019. The paper describes the pedagogical rationale, the selection of historical case studies, and the structure of practical assignments in which students produced their own tactical media interventions under live conditions. It reflects on tensions between the anti-institutional ethos of tactical media and the institutional setting of a state university, and on challenges posed by students' unfamiliarity with pre-smartphone internet culture. Data are drawn from module evaluation surveys (n=287 students across five years), assessment outcomes, and the author's reflective teaching journal. The paper identifies three recurring difficulties: contextualising historical works for students with no lived memory of the 1990s, managing ethical risks in live interventions, and assessing ephemeral or deliberately undocumented work.

title: Tensiomyographic muscle contractile properties before and after a repeated-sprint protocol in trained football players
abstract: This study examined changes in contractile properties of the vastus lateralis and rectus femoris following a standardised repeated-sprint protocol (10 × 30 m, 30 s passive recovery) in 18 male university-level football players. Tensiomyography measurements—contraction time (Tc), radial displacement (Dm), and delay time (Td)—were recorded at baseline, immediately after, and at 5 and 15 minutes post-exercise. Sprint times were captured with photocell gates, and rating of perceived exertion was recorded after each effort. Dm of the vastus lateralis increased significantly from baseline (mean ± SD: 4.1 ± 0.8 mm) to immediately post-sprint (6.3 ± 1.1 mm; p < 0.001), indicating reduced muscle stiffness consistent with peripheral fatigue. Tc showed a smaller and non-significant change. Correlations between Dm change and sprint time decrement were moderate (r = 0.51, p = 0.03). Partial recovery of Dm was observed by 15 minutes but full return to baseline was not confirmed within the measurement window. These findings suggest that tensiomyography can track peripheral fatigue development during repeated sprinting and may offer a practical non-invasive monitoring approach in team sport settings.

title: Voluntary activation of the knee extensors declines across successive sprint bouts but recovers faster than contractile displacement: a twitch interpolation study
abstract: The relative contribution of central versus peripheral mechanisms to fatigue during repeated sprinting remains debated. Twenty trained track athletes (11 men, 9 women; age 21.4 ± 2.1 years) completed eight maximal 6-second cycle sprints separated by 24 seconds of passive rest. Voluntary activation (VA) of the knee extensors was estimated using the twitch interpolation technique applied during maximal isometric knee extension at baseline and after sprints 2, 4, 6, and 8. Peak torque and peak power output were also recorded. VA declined from 94.2 ± 2.8% at baseline to 87.5 ± 4.1% after sprint 8 (p < 0.001), while peak torque fell by 19.4%. A partial return of VA toward baseline values (90.8 ± 3.5%) was recorded at 10 minutes post-exercise, preceding recovery of peak torque (still 12.3% below baseline). Tensiomyographic Dm remained elevated at 10 minutes (p = 0.004), suggesting peripheral fatigue was slower to resolve. These results indicate that central and peripheral fatigue develop concurrently during high-intensity repeated sprinting but follow different recovery time courses, with implications for warm-up and re-entry decisions in competitive sport.

title: Sex differences in neuromuscular fatigue responses to a repeated-sprint test: evidence from tensiomyography and surface EMG
abstract: Sex-based differences in fatigue resistance during repeated sprinting have been reported, but underlying neuromuscular mechanisms are poorly characterised in field-sport populations. This cross-sectional study compared 14 trained women and 14 trained men matched for sport (handball, basketball) on a repeated-sprint test (6 × 40 m, 25 s recovery). Tensiomyography of the biceps femoris and vastus medialis, surface EMG amplitude normalised to maximal voluntary contraction, and sprint time decrement index were assessed. Women showed a smaller sprint decrement index than men (6.1 ± 2.3% vs. 9.8 ± 3.1%; p = 0.002). Dm increase in vastus medialis post-exercise was lower in women (2.1 ± 0.7 mm vs. 3.6 ± 1.0 mm; p < 0.001). EMG amplitude decline did not differ significantly between sexes (p = 0.21). Biceps femoris contractile properties changed minimally in both groups. Regression analysis indicated that Dm change accounted for 38% of variance in sprint decrement across the full sample. These data suggest that women's greater fatigue resistance in this context is partly explained by lower peripheral fatigue accumulation in the knee extensors rather than differences in central drive.

title: Photolysis of ciprofloxacin in buffered aqueous solution under simulated solar irradiation: kinetics and primary degradation pathways
abstract: This study examined the direct photolysis of ciprofloxacin (CIP) at environmentally relevant concentrations (0.5–5 mg/L) in phosphate-buffered aqueous solutions at pH 5, 7, and 9, using a xenon arc solar simulator (290–800 nm, 500 W/m²). Pseudo-first-order rate constants ranged from 0.018 min⁻¹ at pH 5 to 0.047 min⁻¹ at pH 9, indicating significant pH dependence. HPLC-DAD monitored compound disappearance, and seven transformation products (TPs) were tentatively identified by LC-ion trap MSⁿ. Principal fragmentation involved sequential loss of the piperazine side chain followed by defluorination and decarboxylation. Mass balance calculations showed approximately 62% of total organic carbon remained in solution after 180 min irradiation. Two TPs retained the fluoroquinolone core structure and were flagged for further toxicity assessment. This work established baseline photodegradation data for CIP under central European irradiation conditions.

title: Effect of dissolved natural organic matter on the phototransformation kinetics of trimethoprim in surface water models
abstract: Trimethoprim (TMP) phototransformation was investigated in ultrapure water and in model surface waters containing Suwannee River humic acid (SRHA) at 5, 10, and 20 mg/L dissolved organic carbon. Irradiation was performed with a solar simulator over 240 min. At 10 mg/L SRHA, the apparent first-order rate constant decreased by 38% compared to ultrapure water, attributed to light-screening and reactive oxygen species scavenging. Steady-state concentrations of hydroxyl radical (·OH) were estimated at 4.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ M using pCBA as a probe compound. Nitrate and bicarbonate were varied independently; bicarbonate at 2 mM reduced degradation by 22% via ·OH scavenging. Four TPs were detected by UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS, with proposed structures involving hydroxylation of the trimethoxybenzyl ring. Bioluminescence inhibition tests on Aliivibrio fischeri showed modest but measurable toxicity increases at intermediate irradiation times relative to parent compound.

title: Identification of azithromycin photodegradation products in chlorinated and unchlorinated water matrices by LC-HRMS
abstract: Azithromycin (AZT) at 2 mg/L was subjected to simulated solar photolysis alone and in combination with free chlorine (0.5 and 2 mg/L Cl₂) to model drinking water treatment conditions. A total of 14 transformation products were detected in the unchlorinated system and 19 in the chlorinated system using a Thermo Scientific Q Exactive Orbitrap (resolving power 70,000 FWHM). Accurate masses and isotope pattern analysis enabled tentative structural assignment for 11 TPs; characteristic fragmentation of the macrolide ring system confirmed retention of the cladinose and desosamine sugar units in early-stage products. Chlorination introduced two chlorinated TPs not observed during photolysis alone. Degradation of parent compound followed pseudo-first-order kinetics with k = 0.031 min⁻¹ under photolysis and k = 0.089 min⁻¹ under combined photolysis–chlorination. Quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) screening of identified TPs flagged three structures as potential inhibitors of bacterial protein synthesis.

title: Photostability and transformation product toxicity of sulfamethoxazole across simulated freshwater, estuarine, and marine ionic strengths
abstract: The photodegradation of sulfamethoxazole (SMX) was studied at three ionic strengths mimicking freshwater (I = 0.01 M), estuarine (I = 0.1 M), and marine (I = 0.5 M) conditions using NaCl as the dominant electrolyte. Pseudo-first-order rate constants for direct photolysis were statistically indistinguishable across ionic strengths (0.041–0.044 min⁻¹), but ·OH-mediated degradation rates differed by up to 19%, attributed to chloride-mediated scavenging forming reactive chlorine species. Ten TPs were identified by LC-HRMS; two TP structures unique to higher chloride conditions showed chloro-substitution on the aniline ring. Zebrafish embryo acute toxicity tests (Danio rerio, 96 h FET assay) were performed on irradiated solutions at equivalent total organic carbon; solutions collected at 60 min irradiation showed highest embryotoxicity relative to parent SMX and fully irradiated samples, indicating transient formation of toxic TPs. Results caution against assuming complete detoxification upon disappearance of the parent compound.

title: Photodegradation of the antiepileptic drug carbamazepine in the presence of TiO₂ and simulated solar light: reaction intermediates and mineralisation extent
abstract: Carbamazepine (CBZ) photocatalytic degradation was studied under TiO₂ Aeroxide P25 loading of 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 g/L at initial CBZ concentration of 1 mg/L in ultrapure water. Rate constants increased from 0.009 min⁻¹ (direct photolysis only) to 0.078 min⁻¹ at 1.0 g/L TiO₂. TOC removal after 360 min reached 74% at maximum catalyst loading. Twelve TPs were detected by LC-HRMS/MS; proposed structures included acridine, acridone, and various hydroxylated CBZ derivatives consistent with previously reported pathways. Reaction pathway diagrams were constructed from temporal TP appearance and disappearance profiles. Acute toxicity towards Aliivibrio fischeri showed inhibition exceeding that of parent CBZ at 90 min irradiation (EC₅₀ approximately 3.4 mg CBZ-equivalent/L) before declining at extended irradiation times. This work supports the use of solar photocatalysis for CBZ removal but highlights an intermediate toxic window that should be considered in process design.

title: Occurrence and seasonal variation of fluoroquinolone and sulfonamide antibiotics in the Danube and Tisa rivers within the Vojvodina region
abstract: Surface water samples were collected at eight sampling points along the Danube and Tisa rivers in Vojvodina (northern Serbia) over four seasons in 2020–2021. Targeted analysis by UHPLC-MS/MS quantified six fluoroquinolones and five sulfonamides. Ciprofloxacin was the most frequently detected compound (detection frequency 87.5%), with maximum concentrations of 142 ng/L recorded near a municipal wastewater discharge point on the Tisa in spring. Sulfamethoxazole was detected at all sites at concentrations up to 89 ng/L. Concentrations were significantly elevated in spring and autumn, corresponding to agricultural antibiotic use cycles and higher precipitation-driven runoff. Risk quotients calculated against PNEC values derived from standard ecotoxicological endpoints exceeded 1 for ciprofloxacin at three sites, indicating potential ecological concern. This dataset provides a regional baseline for ongoing monitoring and informs the selection of priority compounds for photodegradation studies.

title: Benchmarking LC-HRMS data processing workflows for pharmaceutical transformation product identification: a comparison of four software tools on a ciprofloxacin test dataset
abstract: Consistent identification of photodegradation transformation products by LC-HRMS depends heavily on data processing workflow choices. This study compared four freely available or commercially licensed software tools—MZmine 3, Compound Discoverer 3.3 (Thermo Scientific), MS-DIAL 4.9, and SIRIUS 5—applied to an identical ciprofloxacin photolysis LC-Orbitrap dataset (positive and negative ionisation, 35,000 FWHM). Ground-truth TPs previously confirmed by authentic standards or reference spectra (n = 7) served as benchmarks. Recall ranged from 57% (MS-DIAL) to 100% (Compound Discoverer), while false positive rates varied between 8 and 34% for the non-targeted feature lists prior to manual curation. SIRIUS in-silico fragmentation scoring reduced the false positive rate to 11% after filtering but missed one TP owing to absence of the required MS² spectrum. Practical guidance on parameter settings, processing time (ranging from 8 min to 2.5 h per dataset), and minimum data quality requirements is provided to assist environmental analytical chemists selecting or combining tools.

title: Photodegradation of the antidiabetic drug metformin and its transformation product guanylurea under UV-A and simulated solar irradiation
abstract: Metformin (MET) is among the most frequently detected pharmaceuticals in European wastewater effluents, yet its photochemical behaviour and that of its primary biotic metabolite guanylurea (GU) remain incompletely characterised. This study irradiated MET and GU individually and as a binary mixture at environmentally relevant concentrations (0.1–2 mg/L) under UV-A (365 nm) and simulated solar light. MET exhibited negligible direct photolysis under both irradiation conditions (k < 0.002 min⁻¹) but degraded measurably via ·OH-mediated oxidation when hydrogen peroxide (0.5 mM) was added (k = 0.021 min⁻¹). GU degraded approximately four times faster than MET under ·OH conditions. LC-HRMS identified six TPs from the combined system, with biguanide ring-opening products dominating at extended irradiation times. Algal growth inhibition tests (Raphidocelis subcapitata, 72 h) showed EC₅₀ values for irradiated MET solutions that were 1.8-fold lower than for the parent compound at equivalent TOC, suggesting phototransformation does not reduce toxicity towards primary producers.

title: Transformation product profiling of clarithromycin during UV/H₂O₂ treatment and direct photolysis: structural elucidation and in silico hazard estimation
abstract: Clarithromycin (CLR), a macrolide antibiotic resistant to conventional biological treatment, was subjected to UV/H₂O₂ advanced oxidation (0.1–1.0 mM H₂O₂, 254 nm low-pressure lamp) and direct simulated solar photolysis at 1 mg/L in ultrapure and river water matrices. Twenty-two TPs were detected across all conditions by LC-Orbitrap HRMS (full-scan and ddMS² acquisition). Structural assignments for 16 TPs were proposed based on accurate mass, diagnostic fragment ions, and comparison with the CLR MS² library. UV/H₂O₂ generated a distinct TP pattern relative to solar photolysis, with hydroxylation at C-8 and demethylation of the cladinose sugar moiety being predominant under oxidative conditions. In silico hazard estimation using the T.E.S.T. v5.1 software predicted developmental toxicity potential for three TPs. River water matrix suppressed CLR degradation by approximately 31% due to ·OH scavenging by background organic matter. These results are relevant to assessing CLR removal and residual risk in UV-based drinking water treatment.

title: Ionic Strength Correction Models for Portable Photometric Iron Analysis: Comparison of Pitzer, Davies, and Empirical Regression Approaches
abstract: Activity coefficient corrections are rarely applied in field analytical chemistry, yet theoretical frameworks such as the Pitzer and Davies equations predict non-trivial deviations in reaction equilibria at the ionic strengths common in mineral-rich groundwaters. This study applied the Pitzer and Davies models to the 1,10-phenanthroline iron(II) system and compared their predictive power against empirical polynomial regression models fitted to experimental absorbance data collected across ionic strengths from 0.01 to 0.15 mol/L. Synthetic matrices were prepared using NaCl, MgCl2, CaCl2, and NaHCO3 in proportions approximating four regional aquifer types. The Davies equation predicted trends correctly but underestimated corrections by 30–50% relative to observed data. The Pitzer model performed better (15–25% underestimate) but requires ion-specific interaction parameters not always available for complex mixtures. Empirical polynomial regression with ionic strength and dominant cation identity as inputs achieved residuals below 1.5% across the calibration dataset and 2.1% on an independent validation set of 28 real samples. A lookup-table implementation suitable for non-specialist field users is provided.

title: Polymorphic screening of sulfamethoxazole by slurry conversion and solvent-drop grinding: identification of two previously unreported forms
abstract: Sulfamethoxazole is a widely used sulfonamide antibiotic whose polymorphic landscape has been incompletely characterised. Slurry conversion experiments in twelve solvents at 25 °C and 40 °C, combined with solvent-drop grinding using seven solvent systems, were carried out and the resulting solid phases were analysed by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. Two previously unreported crystalline forms, designated Form IV and Form V, were identified. Form IV, obtained reproducibly from acetonitrile slurries at 40 °C, showed a characteristic PXRD peak at 2θ = 8.3° absent from all known forms. DSC showed a sharp endotherm at 164 °C for Form IV, compared with 170 °C for the stable Form I. Form V appeared transiently during solvent-drop grinding with dimethyl sulfoxide and converted to Form I within 48 hours at ambient conditions. Variable-temperature PXRD confirmed an irreversible solid–solid transition of Form IV to Form I at 152 °C. The results extend the known polymorph space of this compound and provide reproducible preparation protocols for both new forms.

title: Stability constants of calcium(II) and magnesium(II) complexes with citrate and malate in NaClO₄ media at I = 0.10 M
abstract: Conditional stability constants for 1:1 and 1:2 metal–ligand complexes of Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ with citrate and malate were determined by glass-electrode potentiometry at 25 °C and I = 0.10 M (NaClO₄). Both mono- and dinuclear species were tested; only mononuclear 1:1 species were statistically justified by HYPERQUAD2008 refinement. For Ca–citrate, log K₁₁ = 3.48 ± 0.03; for Mg–citrate, log K₁₁ = 3.71 ± 0.02. Malate gave systematically lower constants: Ca–malate log K₁₁ = 1.82 ± 0.04, Mg–malate log K₁₁ = 2.16 ± 0.03. Competition experiments using Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ mixtures confirmed individual constant values within combined uncertainty. Speciation diagrams computed over pH 6.5–8.5 show that at typical calcareous soil pore-water pH (7.8–8.2), 55–70% of dissolved citrate and 20–35% of dissolved malate are complexed with Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺, substantially reducing their availability as Zn²⁺ or Cu²⁺ complexing agents.

title: Constructing a Composite Performance Index for Small and Medium-Sized Manufacturers: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of aggregating heterogeneous key performance indicators into a single composite index for manufacturing SMEs that lack dedicated measurement infrastructure. Using data collected from 34 enterprises in Vojvodina in 2010–2011, the study applies a weighted linear aggregation method where weights are derived through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with input from twelve senior managers across the sample companies. Four performance dimensions — financial, customer, internal processes, and learning and growth — were operationalised through 22 individual KPIs. Cronbach's alpha was used to verify internal consistency within each dimension (ranging from 0.71 to 0.84). The resulting composite index was validated against external audit scores and profit margin data. Results indicate that process-related KPIs carry disproportionate weight when managers with ISO 9001 experience are included as raters. The paper concludes with a simplified instrument suitable for quarterly self-assessment, reducing measurement burden to six core indicators without significant loss of discriminant validity. Limitations related to sample size and regional specificity are discussed.

title: Adapting the Balanced Scorecard to ISO 9001 Transition Contexts: Conceptual Alignment and Practical Constraints
abstract: The balanced scorecard (BSC) and ISO 9001 quality management standard share process-oriented thinking but differ substantially in measurement philosophy, documentation requirements, and management commitment expectations. This conceptual paper maps the structural overlap between the four BSC perspectives and the ten clauses of ISO 9001:2015, identifying 14 areas of direct alignment and eight areas of potential conflict. The analysis draws on a review of 61 published implementation case studies from European manufacturing companies published between 2000 and 2012, supplemented by interviews with five quality managers in Serbian companies undergoing ISO 9001 certification at the time of the study. The paper argues that the BSC customer perspective is most easily absorbed into the ISO framework, while the learning and growth perspective requires the greatest adaptation due to ISO's weak treatment of human capital metrics. A mapping matrix is proposed as a practical tool for consultants guiding simultaneous BSC and ISO implementations. The paper does not present empirical validation but sets the foundation for subsequent quantitative research.

title: Measurement Invariance of Balanced Scorecard Scales Across Manufacturing Subsectors: Evidence from Serbia and Slovenia
abstract: Balanced scorecard instruments are frequently adapted informally when moved between industry contexts, raising questions about whether scale items retain the same meaning across manufacturing subsectors. This study tests measurement invariance of a 28-item BSC survey instrument across three subsectors — metal processing, food manufacturing, and textile production — using data from 187 respondents in Serbian and Slovenian companies with 50–500 employees. Confirmatory factor analysis and multigroup structural equation modelling (SEM) were conducted in R using the lavaan package. Configural and metric invariance were confirmed across all three groups; scalar invariance held for the financial and internal processes perspectives but failed for two items in the customer perspective, suggesting that customer satisfaction is conceptualised differently in food manufacturing relative to the other subsectors. Practical implications for cross-sector benchmarking are discussed. The validated instrument is included as an appendix and is made available for replication studies.

title: Weighting Methods for Balanced Scorecard KPIs: A Comparative Study of AHP, Entropy Weighting, and Equal Weighting in the Context of Medium-Sized Enterprises
abstract: The choice of KPI weighting method in balanced scorecard implementations is rarely subjected to empirical scrutiny. This study compares three weighting approaches — pairwise AHP, entropy-based objective weighting, and simple equal weighting — applied to the same dataset of 41 medium-sized manufacturing companies in Serbia and Hungary. For each company, a composite performance score was calculated using all three methods, and the resulting rankings were compared using Spearman rank correlation and Kendall's W. Entropy weighting and AHP produce highly correlated rankings (ρ = 0.91), while equal weighting diverges substantially when KPI variance is uneven across dimensions. Sensitivity analysis shows that AHP rankings are more stable under data perturbation than entropy rankings. Survey data from 163 managers indicate a strong preference for AHP outputs when presented alongside the rationale, despite higher procedural complexity. The paper recommends a hybrid approach combining AHP for strategic KPIs with entropy weighting for operational indicators. Data and R scripts are available in the supplementary materials.

title: Performance Measurement Maturity and ISO 9001 Readiness: Developing a Pre-Certification Assessment Tool
abstract: Companies approaching ISO 9001 certification for the first time vary considerably in the sophistication of their existing performance measurement practices. This paper presents the development and validation of a 20-item Performance Measurement Maturity Assessment (PMMA) tool designed to estimate ISO 9001 transition readiness. Item generation drew on a review of maturity model literature and on semi-structured interviews with 18 quality consultants active in the Western Balkans region. Content validity was assessed by a panel of seven experts. Pilot testing was conducted with 62 manufacturing SMEs; exploratory factor analysis in SPSS yielded four factors explaining 67% of variance: data collection infrastructure, managerial engagement, process documentation, and corrective action routines. Confirmatory factor analysis on a second sample of 88 companies confirmed the factor structure (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.058). PMMA scores correlate significantly with time-to-certification outcomes tracked over 18 months (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). The tool is intended for use by consultants and internal quality managers as a structured diagnostic prior to ISO implementation.

title: Integrating Risk-Based Thinking from ISO 9001:2015 into Balanced Scorecard Design: A Framework for Manufacturing SMEs
abstract: The 2015 revision of ISO 9001 introduced an explicit requirement for risk-based thinking, replacing the earlier concept of preventive action. This requirement has no direct counterpart in classical balanced scorecard design, creating a gap in integrated management systems. This book chapter proposes a framework for embedding risk indicators into each of the four BSC perspectives, drawing on ISO 31000 risk management terminology and on data from ten case companies that participated in a structured implementation pilot in 2017–2018. For each perspective, the chapter identifies two to four candidate risk KPIs, specifies data sources, and illustrates aggregation logic using the companies' own figures. A worked numerical example demonstrates how a composite risk-adjusted BSC score differs from an unadjusted score in companies with high process variability. The chapter also discusses barriers encountered during the pilot, including resistance from finance managers unfamiliar with non-financial risk quantification and inconsistency in how risk registers were maintained across companies.

title: Aggregation Bias in Multi-Perspective Performance Indices: Simulation Evidence and Practical Corrections
abstract: Composite performance indices that aggregate KPIs across multiple perspectives are susceptible to aggregation bias when individual indicators are correlated within perspectives or when perspectives differ in the number of constituent indicators. This paper quantifies aggregation bias through a Monte Carlo simulation study calibrated on empirical correlation structures estimated from a panel dataset of 74 Serbian and Croatian manufacturing companies observed over three years. Simulation results show that standard weighted arithmetic aggregation systematically overstates overall performance when within-perspective correlations exceed 0.5, with bias increasing with the number of indicators per perspective. Three correction procedures are compared: principal component score substitution, geometric aggregation, and within-perspective decorrelation prior to aggregation. Geometric aggregation provides the best bias-correction at minimal computational cost and is recommended as the default for practitioners. The paper provides worked examples and an Excel template implementing all three methods. Findings have direct implications for balanced scorecard implementations where perspectives contain redundant indicators.

title: Short-Form Balanced Scorecard Instruments for Operational Monitoring: Validity and Reliability in High-Turnover Manufacturing Environments
abstract: Full-length balanced scorecard instruments are burdensome to administer in manufacturing environments with high staff turnover and limited administrative capacity. This paper develops and validates a 10-item short-form BSC instrument designed for monthly operational monitoring. Items were selected from a longer 32-item pool using a three-stage procedure: item-response theory analysis, expert rating for practical measurability, and empirical validation across 56 Serbian manufacturing SMEs followed over six months. The short form retains adequate coverage of all four perspectives with two to three items each. Reliability coefficients (McDonald's ω) range from 0.72 to 0.79 per perspective. Convergent validity with the full instrument is confirmed (r = 0.87 for composite scores). Sensitivity to change was tested by comparing short-form scores before and after documented process improvement interventions in 14 of the 56 companies; the instrument detected improvement in 11 of 14 cases. The short-form instrument and scoring guide are provided as supplementary materials.

title: Linking Employee Competence Development Metrics to ISO 9001 Clause 7.2 Requirements: A Practical Measurement Approach for Mid-Sized Manufacturers
abstract: ISO 9001:2015 Clause 7.2 requires organisations to determine and maintain employee competence, yet offers no guidance on measurement. This creates a gap when companies attempt to incorporate competence development into the learning and growth perspective of a balanced scorecard. Drawing on data from 22 mid-sized Serbian manufacturers that had held ISO 9001 certification for at least five years, this study documents the measurement practices actually used, identifies the most common operationalisations of competence KPIs, and tests which measures predict training effectiveness as assessed by follow-up operational audits. A total of 31 distinct competence metrics were identified across the sample. Regression analysis on a subsample with sufficient longitudinal data (n = 15) shows that metrics combining task completion rates with a structured competence gap assessment score are stronger predictors of audit outcomes than training hours alone. The paper proposes a four-item measurement mini-framework that aligns with both Clause 7.2 and standard learning and growth BSC indicators.

title: Machine learning surrogates for workload-based pricing in high-mix job shops
abstract: Optimal pricing functions derived from queueing or simulation models are computationally expensive to evaluate in real time, limiting their use in shop-floor execution systems. This paper investigates whether gradient-boosted regression trees trained on offline simulation data can serve as fast surrogates for a six-machine, ten-job-class job shop pricing model. A training dataset of 120,000 state-action-reward triples is generated from AnyLogic simulations. The trained surrogate predicts the near-optimal price for a new arriving job within 2 milliseconds on standard hardware, compared with 40 seconds for direct simulation lookahead. In a rolling-horizon production test, the surrogate policy achieves 97.4% of the revenue attained by the full simulation-based policy. Feature importance analysis identifies current aggregate utilisation and job processing time as the two most influential inputs, with job class contributing less than expected. The paper discusses data requirements and retraining frequency for production deployment.

title: Characterisation of aluminium hydroxide sludge from a surface-finishing facility in Vojvodina: elemental composition, phase distribution, and leaching behaviour
abstract: Sludge samples collected over twelve months from the neutralisation basin of an anodising plant in Vojvodina were characterised by ICP-OES, XRD, FTIR, and toxicity characteristic leaching procedure (TCLP). Aluminium accounted for 28–34 wt% of the dry solid, with subordinate iron, silicon, and sulphate. XRD patterns confirmed a predominantly amorphous boehmite-like phase, with traces of gibbsite appearing in samples collected during winter when bath temperatures were lower. TCLP leachates for Zn, Cu, Ni, and Cr remained below regulatory thresholds, supporting a classification as non-hazardous waste. Seasonal variation in sulphate content (1.2–4.7 wt%) was attributed to changes in sulphuric acid bath loading. These baseline data informed subsequent valorisation studies and established the compositional envelope within which value-added products can reliably be manufactured from this waste stream.

title: Dissolution kinetics of aluminium hydroxide sludge in dilute sulphuric acid: effect of temperature, acid concentration, and particle size
abstract: Acid dissolution is the first step in most wet-chemical valorisation routes for aluminium sludge, yet systematic kinetic data for anodising-derived material are scarce. Dissolution experiments were conducted at 30–80 °C, H2SO4 concentrations of 0.5–3.0 mol/L, and two particle-size fractions (<63 µm and 63–125 µm) using a stirred batch reactor. Aluminium extraction exceeded 92% under optimised conditions (70 °C, 2.0 mol/L, <63 µm, 60 min). The rate data fitted the shrinking-core model with a surface-reaction-controlled mechanism; apparent activation energy was 42.3 kJ/mol. Sulphate co-dissolution increased proportionally with acid concentration and partially inhibited Al release above 2.5 mol/L. These results define the processing window for downstream production of polyaluminium sulphate coagulants and serve as a reference for scale-up calculations.

title: Preparation and coagulation performance of polyaluminium sulphate derived from anodising sludge for treatment of synthetic textile dye wastewater
abstract: Polyaluminium sulphate (PAS) was synthesised by controlled acid digestion of anodising sludge followed by basification to Al/OH molar ratios of 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5. The resulting coagulants were characterised by 27Al NMR, which confirmed a progressive increase in the Keggin-ion (Al13) fraction from 14 to 37% as basicity increased. Coagulation–flocculation jar tests were performed on a synthetic reactive-blue dye solution (100 mg/L) and on a settled municipal wastewater effluent. At a PAS dose of 40 mg Al/L and pH 7.0, colour removal reached 94% for the dye solution, comparable to a commercial polyaluminium chloride reference. COD reduction in the municipal effluent was 61% at the same dose. Residual aluminium in treated water stayed below 0.15 mg/L under all conditions tested. The results support sludge-derived PAS as a technically viable alternative to virgin-source coagulants.

title: Hydrothermal synthesis of zeolite NaA from aluminium hydroxide sludge and rice husk ash: optimisation of Si/Al ratio and crystallisation conditions
abstract: Zeolite NaA was synthesised hydrothermally by combining an aluminate solution prepared from anodising sludge with a silicate solution derived from rice husk ash. Si/Al molar ratios of 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, and 1.5 were tested at 80 °C and 100 °C for 4–24 h. Phase purity was assessed by XRD using reference diffractograms; BET surface areas and Langmuir micropore volumes were determined from N2 adsorption at −196 °C. Maximum crystallinity (89%) was obtained at Si/Al = 1.0, 100 °C, and 12 h, yielding a BET surface area of 14 m²/g and a micropore volume of 0.19 cm³/g consistent with literature values for zeolite NaA. SEM showed well-defined cubic crystals of 2–5 µm. Ion-exchange capacity for Ca²⁺ reached 185 mg CaCO3/g, indicating potential applicability in water softening and detergent formulations.
