title: Low-temperature calcination of aluminium hydroxide sludge to produce an amorphous alumina adsorbent: fluoride removal from drinking water
abstract: Aluminium hydroxide sludge was calcined at 300, 450, 600, and 750 °C for 2 h to produce a series of adsorbents whose surface chemistry and structure were tracked by TGA-DSC, FTIR, and XRD. The 450 °C sample exhibited the highest BET surface area (218 m²/g) and retained abundant surface hydroxyl groups as confirmed by FTIR. Batch adsorption experiments for fluoride in synthetic solutions (2–15 mg F⁻/L, pH 5–8) showed maximum uptake of 12.4 mg/g at pH 6.5, well-described by the Langmuir isotherm (R² = 0.994). Pseudo-second-order kinetics fitted the time-uptake data with a rate constant of 0.0031 g/(mg·min). Column tests at a bed volume of 200 demonstrated complete fluoride removal below the WHO guideline (1.5 mg/L) for the first 95 bed volumes. Regeneration with 0.1 mol/L NaOH restored more than 85% of initial capacity over three cycles.

title: Phosphate recovery from secondary wastewater treatment effluent using calcined aluminium sludge granules
abstract: Granular adsorbent pellets were prepared by mixing 450 °C-calcined aluminium sludge powder with 5 wt% bentonite binder, extruding, and drying at 105 °C. The granules (1.5–2.5 mm diameter) were tested for phosphate adsorption in batch and fixed-bed column experiments using real secondary effluent from a municipal wastewater treatment plant, with total phosphorus concentrations of 4.2–6.8 mg/L. The Freundlich exponent (1/n = 0.41) indicated favourable adsorption; column tests at an empty-bed contact time of 8 min achieved >90% phosphate removal for the first 120 bed volumes. Phosphate-loaded granules were regenerated with 0.5 mol/L NaOH; the resulting phosphate-rich eluate (220 mg P/L) was evaluated as a liquid fertiliser substitute in a pot-trial with spring wheat, where growth and phosphorus uptake were statistically indistinguishable from a commercial monoammonium phosphate treatment.

title: Valorisation of anodising sludge: from waste characterisation to product synthesis — a review of conversion pathways and downstream applications
abstract: Anodising operations generate aluminium hydroxide sludge in quantities estimated at 0.5–2.5 kg per m² of anodised surface, yet the material remains widely landfilled. This chapter surveys conversion pathways that have been reported in the academic and patent literature, organised around four product families: soluble aluminium salts and polyaluminium coagulants, zeolites and aluminosilicate frameworks, calcined alumina adsorbents, and composite construction materials. For each pathway, the chapter discusses the required pre-treatment steps (dissolution, silica addition, calcination, granulation), key process variables, characterisation evidence for product quality, and documented end-use performance. Attention is given to impurity management, particularly iron, sulphate, and trace metals, which can compromise product purity or regulatory compliance. Economic and life-cycle considerations are summarised where data are available. The chapter concludes by identifying knowledge gaps, notably the limited number of pilot-scale demonstrations and the absence of standardised product specifications for sludge-derived coagulants in European regulations.

title: Effect of iron impurities in aluminium sludge on the quality and coagulation efficiency of derived polyaluminium chloride
abstract: Commercial polyaluminium chloride (PACl) specifications limit iron content to below 0.5 wt%, yet anodising sludge commonly contains 1–6 wt% Fe. This study examined three iron removal strategies applied prior to PACl synthesis: selective precipitation at pH 3.8, oxidation with H2O2 followed by filtration, and magnetic separation after mild calcination. Iron removal efficiencies were 71, 84, and 58% respectively. PACl batches prepared from treated and untreated sludge digests were compared by 27Al NMR, UV-Vis basicity titration, and jar-test performance across a range of water matrices (river water, synthetic kaolin suspension, pre-treated textile effluent). Iron residuals above 1.2 wt% in the final product reduced Al13 fraction by roughly 12 percentage points and decreased turbidity removal by 8–11% in jar tests, confirming that a purification step is necessary for products intended for drinking water treatment but not necessarily for industrial process water applications.

title: Synthesis of sodalite from aluminium hydroxide sludge and sodium silicate: structural characterisation and performance as an adsorbent for lead and cadmium ions
abstract: Sodalite was synthesised by combining sludge-derived sodium aluminate with commercial sodium silicate at Si/Al = 0.5 and treating hydrothermally at 120 °C for 48 h under static conditions. XRD Rietveld refinement confirmed phase-pure sodalite (space group P4̄3n) with unit-cell parameter a = 8.882 Å. BET surface area was 28 m²/g. Adsorption of Pb²⁺ and Cd²⁺ from single- and binary-metal solutions (0.5–50 mg/L, pH 5.5) followed Langmuir behaviour with maximum capacities of 74.6 mg Pb²⁺/g and 51.3 mg Cd²⁺/g. In binary systems, Pb²⁺ was preferentially adsorbed (selectivity coefficient 2.3), attributed to its stronger affinity for aluminosilicate surface sites. FTIR and XPS analysis after adsorption confirmed inner-sphere surface complexation as the dominant mechanism. Desorption with 0.1 mol/L HNO3 exceeded 90% for both metals, suggesting potential for metal recovery and adsorbent reuse.

title: Pilot-scale production of polyaluminium sulphate from anodising sludge: process mass balance, product consistency, and preliminary cost estimate
abstract: A 50-litre stirred-tank pilot reactor was used to produce polyaluminium sulphate (PAS) from anodising sludge over ten consecutive batches, processing a total of 42 kg of dry sludge. Each batch involved acid dissolution (H2SO4, 1.8 mol/L, 65 °C, 90 min), filtration to remove inerts, and basification to Al/OH = 2.0. Yield consistency was evaluated by measuring Al content, basicity, density, and turbidity of the liquid product. Batch-to-batch coefficient of variation was below 5% for all parameters except iron (CV 11%), the latter reflecting natural sludge heterogeneity. A simplified mass balance showed a PAS yield of 6.2 kg product per kg of dry sludge (expressed as Al2O3 equivalent). A preliminary production cost estimate, based on reagent consumption, energy, and labour, was 0.18–0.22 €/kg Al2O3 equivalent, compared to approximately 0.31 €/kg for commercially sourced aluminium sulphate in the region. Regulatory compliance of the product with EN 883 for water treatment chemicals is discussed.

title: Geopolymer binders incorporating anodising sludge as partial aluminium source: mechanical and leaching properties
abstract: Geopolymer pastes were formulated by partially replacing metakaolin (0, 10, 20, and 30 wt%) with raw anodising sludge and activating with 8 mol/L NaOH/sodium silicate solution (modulus 1.2). Setting time, compressive strength at 3, 7, and 28 days, and toxicity leaching (EN 12457-2) were determined. At 20 wt% sludge substitution, 28-day compressive strength was 31.4 MPa, only marginally lower than the reference paste (34.1 MPa). XRD and FTIR confirmed the formation of an aluminosilicate geopolymer network with amorphous hump shift consistent with Al incorporation. Leachate concentrations of Al, Cr, Ni, and Cu remained below EN waste acceptance criteria for inert landfill, supporting the classification of the material as an encapsulation matrix for trace metals present in the sludge. Shrinkage over 28 days was 0.18% for the 20 wt% sludge paste, within acceptable limits for most non-structural applications.

title: Comparative life cycle assessment of three valorisation routes for anodising aluminium sludge: coagulant production, zeolite synthesis, and landfill disposal
abstract: A cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted for two valorisation scenarios — production of polyaluminium sulphate (PAS) and synthesis of zeolite NaA — and compared against the baseline of stabilisation and landfill disposal, using primary inventory data from laboratory and pilot experiments. The functional unit was 1 tonne of dry anodising sludge processed. Global warming potential (GWP100), cumulative energy demand, and three water-related impact categories were calculated using the ReCiPe 2016 midpoint method. PAS production showed a net avoided GWP of 142 kg CO2-eq per functional unit relative to landfill, primarily through substitution of virgin aluminium sulphate. Zeolite NaA synthesis showed a higher energy demand (+38%) than PAS production but a larger avoided impact in the eutrophication category. Data quality limitations and allocation choices are discussed in detail. The results are intended to guide process selection rather than provide definitive environmental benchmarks.

title: Quantitative determination of hydroxymethylfurfural and furfural in commercially available paprika powders from the Western Balkan market
abstract: Fifty-six commercially available paprika powder samples from Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia were analysed for hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) and furfural content by HPLC-UV as indicators of thermal processing intensity and potential adulteration. HMF ranged from 2.1 to 487 mg/kg dry weight; furfural ranged from 0.8 to 214 mg/kg. Nine samples exceeded the provisional 200 mg/kg HMF threshold proposed in regional food safety discussions. Cluster analysis grouped samples into three processing-intensity classes. Country-of-origin labelling was inconsistent in four cases identified by isotope ratio analysis conducted by a collaborating laboratory. The results suggest a need for updated regional regulatory guidance on heat-marker limits in paprika products.

title: Random forest classification of ¹H NMR spectral patterns for rapid functional-group assignment
abstract: Assignment of functional groups from ¹H NMR spectra before full structure elucidation reduces the candidate space and accelerates downstream interpretation. We trained a random forest classifier on spectral feature vectors—bin integrals at 0.05 ppm resolution combined with multiplicity-pattern descriptors—extracted from 2840 spectra of organic compounds covering 14 functional-group classes. The training data were drawn from a curated subset of an open spectral repository supplemented by in-house measurements. Ten-fold cross-validation gave macro-averaged F1 scores between 0.82 and 0.97 depending on class, with lower scores for compounds bearing overlapping carbonyl types. The model was evaluated on an independent external set of 310 spectra not used in training, giving an overall accuracy of 84%. Feature importance analysis confirmed that chemical shift region bins around 2.1, 3.4, and 9.7 ppm carried the highest discriminatory weight. The trained model and feature extraction code are provided as supplementary material.

title: Systematic comparison of open spectral repositories for NMR-based chemoinformatics: coverage, format consistency, and metadata quality
abstract: Machine-learning approaches in NMR chemoinformatics depend critically on the quality of training data sourced from public repositories. We systematically evaluated four open repositories containing a combined total of approximately 180 000 NMR records for small organic molecules, assessing coverage by compound class, format consistency, and completeness of key metadata fields including molecular formula, solvent, field strength, and temperature. Across repositories, 31–58% of records lacked at least one metadata field required for unambiguous interpretation. Duplicate detection based on InChI keys revealed an effective non-redundant corpus of roughly 94 000 unique structures with ¹H data and 61 000 with ¹³C data. Compound-class coverage was strongly biased toward aromatic and heteroaromatic structures, with aliphatic acyclic compounds underrepresented at roughly 8% of records. We propose a minimal metadata standard and describe a preprocessing pipeline that harmonises records across repositories, making a cleaned 73 000-compound dataset available for download.

title: Metagenomic survey of iron-cycling guilds in tuberculated main sections: a pilot 454-pyrosequencing study
abstract: DNA was extracted from corrosion tubercle material removed from three sections of a 60-year-old cast-iron main in Novi Sad and subjected to 454 pyrosequencing of the V3–V5 region of the 16S rRNA gene. A total of 47,320 quality-filtered reads were binned into OTUs at 97% identity. Taxonomic profiling indicated that iron-oxidising Betaproteobacteria related to Sideroxydans lithotrophicus (12.3–18.7% relative abundance across sites) and iron-reducing Geobacter-affiliated phylotypes (5.1–9.8%) co-dominated the tubercle communities, together with sulphate-reducing Deltaproteobacteria (3.2–6.4%). Alphaproteobacteria, Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes comprised the remaining diversity. Functional annotation of a 3.2 Mbp assembled metagenome fragment using the MG-RAST pipeline identified genes for cyc2 outer-membrane cytochrome, mtoA and mtr operons, consistent with extracellular electron transfer coupled to iron cycling. This represented the first metagenomic characterisation of Vojvodina distribution system tubercles.

title: Sensitivity of egress time estimates to incomplete floor-plan data in large assembly buildings
abstract: Evacuation simulations typically assume complete and accurate building topology data, yet in practice floor plans are often outdated or partially missing. This study examines how systematic omissions in corridor connectivity data affect egress time distributions in a 4 200-seat concert hall archetype. A social-force agent-based model was implemented in NetLogo with 500 replications per scenario. Six levels of topology degradation were tested, from full connectivity down to 40 % of exits removed from agent knowledge. Results show that median egress time increases sub-linearly with degradation up to 25 % missing data, but variance in egress time grows sharply beyond that threshold, doubling by the 35 % missing-data condition. The findings suggest that safety assessments based on nominal topology can underestimate worst-case evacuation durations by up to 38 %. Implications for certification standards in public buildings are discussed.

title: Calibrating pedestrian speed distributions for Serbian indoor environments using low-cost depth sensors
abstract: Reliable agent-based evacuation models require empirically grounded pedestrian motion parameters. Existing parameter sets are largely derived from studies conducted in Western European or North American buildings, raising questions about transferability. This paper reports a measurement campaign in three university buildings in Novi Sad using two Microsoft Kinect v1 sensors mounted at corridor intersections. Walking speed, body radius, and group-formation frequency were recorded for 1 847 pedestrian trajectories over four weeks. The data were fitted to lognormal distributions and compared against the widely used SFPE Handbook parameters. Mean free-flow speed was 1.31 m/s (SD 0.19), approximately 8 % lower than SFPE reference values. Group-formation frequency reached 34 % of observed trajectories. Calibrated parameters are provided in a reusable format compatible with the MassMotion and NetLogo simulation platforms.

title: An agent-based framework for evacuation planning under partially known building topology
abstract: This chapter presents a generalised computational framework for modelling pedestrian evacuation when agents possess incomplete knowledge of the navigable environment. The framework extends the standard social-force model by introducing a topology-belief layer: each agent maintains a probabilistic graph of reachable nodes, updated through local observation as the simulation proceeds. The chapter describes the formal model, its implementation in Java using the MASON toolkit, and three validation scenarios drawn from published drill data in secondary schools and a sports arena. Particular attention is given to the representation of blocked corridors discovered only at runtime—a condition common in fire events. The framework is made available as an open-source library and is discussed as a teaching resource for graduate-level simulation courses.

title: Effect of exit signage degradation on agent wayfinding efficiency in smoke-filled corridors: a simulation study
abstract: Emergency exit signs are assumed to be continuously visible in most evacuation models, but smoke or power failure can reduce sign visibility during real events. This study couples a simple smoke-diffusion cellular-automaton sub-model with a social-force pedestrian simulation to assess how progressive signage degradation affects mean time to exit in a multi-story office building layout. Three corridor configurations (linear, branched, atrium) and four sign-density levels were tested across 1 000 Monte Carlo runs each. In the branched configuration, reducing sign density by 50 % increased mean evacuation time by 22 % and the proportion of agents exiting through a secondary exit rose from 11 % to 41 %. The atrium layout showed less sensitivity, suggesting geometric visibility as a partial substitute for explicit signage.

title: GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo ensemble simulation of stadium evacuation with stochastic exit availability
abstract: Large-venue evacuation scenarios require thousands of replications to characterise outcome distributions adequately, placing heavy demands on sequential simulation infrastructure. This paper describes a port of a social-force evacuation model to the FLAMEGPU 1.5 framework to exploit data-parallel execution on consumer-grade GPU hardware. A 40 000-seat stadium geometry was used as the test case. Exit availability was modelled as a Bernoulli random variable with probability 0.85 per gate, reflecting historical obstruction rates from incident reports. Ensembles of 10 000 replications were completed in under 90 minutes on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 card, compared with approximately 62 hours on a single CPU core. The paper reports strong scaling results, validates outputs against two published drill datasets, and discusses memory-layout strategies for dense crowd geometries.

title: Integrating real-time occupancy sensor data into running evacuation simulations via a lightweight assimilation scheme
abstract: Conventional evacuation simulations are initialised with assumed occupancy distributions and run open-loop. This paper proposes a sequential data-assimilation scheme that ingests counts from passive infrared sensors installed at corridor junctions and updates agent position distributions in a running simulation using an ensemble Kalman filter approach adapted for discrete agent states. The method was tested on a four-floor administrative building instrumented with 28 PIR sensors. Eleven fire-drill datasets were used: five for parameter tuning and six for validation. The assimilated simulations reduced mean absolute error in zone-level occupancy prediction from 4.1 agents to 1.8 agents at the 3-minute mark after alarm activation. Computational overhead added by assimilation steps was below 4 % of total simulation wall-clock time.

title: Comparing reactive and pre-planned routing strategies for agents with uncertain map knowledge in metro station evacuation
abstract: Metro station evacuation presents particular topological uncertainty because passengers' mental maps of the network vary substantially with familiarity. This paper compares two routing strategies embedded in an agent-based model: a pre-planned strategy in which agents follow memorised paths and a reactive strategy in which agents update paths based on congestion signals from neighbouring agents. Four station archetypes (island platform, side platform, cross-platform interchange, deep-level with multiple escalators) were simulated. Agents were assigned knowledge-accuracy scores sampled from a distribution derived from a 312-participant survey conducted at Novi Sad central bus terminal as a proxy environment. Reactive routing outperformed pre-planned routing in all four archetypes, reducing mean clearance time by 9–17 %, but showed higher variance in the deep-level archetype when escalator failure was introduced.

title: A probabilistic topology model for historic building stock with incomplete or conflicting cadastral records
abstract: Urban heritage districts often contain buildings whose internal layouts are partially documented in cadastral records from different eras, leading to contradictory floor-plan data. This paper introduces a probabilistic topology representation in which wall segments and door openings are assigned existence probabilities derived from multi-source record fusion, including cadastral maps, LiDAR point clouds, and photographic evidence. The representation is propagated into an evacuation simulation through a sample-then-simulate procedure: 500 topology samples are drawn per building, each generating one simulation run. The approach was applied to a block of seven 19th-century courtyard buildings in a protected urban zone. Results show that median egress time estimates from the probabilistic model are 14 % longer than those produced using the most recent single cadastral source, and tail probabilities (95th percentile egress time) differ by up to 31 %.

title: Uncertainty propagation in agent-based evacuation models: a variance-based global sensitivity analysis across topology, behaviour, and demand parameters
abstract: Agent-based evacuation models contain parameters drawn from three distinct sources—building topology, pedestrian behaviour, and occupancy demand—each carrying different forms and magnitudes of uncertainty. This preprint presents a variance-based global sensitivity analysis (Sobol indices) applied to a configurable social-force model of a multi-purpose indoor arena seating 8 000. Forty-one input parameters were varied within empirically motivated ranges across a quasi-random Saltelli sample of 65 536 model runs executed on a university HPC cluster. The analysis identifies exit width and agent reaction-time delay as the dominant contributors to variance in mean egress time (first-order indices 0.31 and 0.22 respectively), while topology connectivity uncertainty contributes disproportionately to variance in worst-case egress time. Interaction effects between behaviour parameters and topology parameters account for approximately 19 % of total output variance. The dataset and analysis scripts are deposited in the Zenodo repository.

title: Synthesis and characterisation of benzimidazolium salts as precursors for NHC–palladium complexes
abstract: A series of six symmetrically and unsymmetrically N,N'-disubstituted benzimidazolium salts bearing alkyl, benzyl and aryl substituents were prepared in two to three synthetic steps from commercially available benzimidazole. Reaction conditions for quaternisation were optimised with respect to solvent, temperature and stoichiometry. All salts were characterised by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy, elemental analysis and ESI-MS. Melting points and thermal stability were assessed by DSC. The influence of the N-substituent on the acidity of the C2 proton was probed by 1H NMR titration experiments with the non-nucleophilic base 1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene in DMSO-d6. A linear correlation was observed between the Hammett σ parameter of para-aryl substituents and the C2 chemical shift, providing a useful predictive tool for subsequent deprotonation steps. These salts serve as the immediate precursors for (NHC)Pd complexes targeted at aqueous coupling chemistry.

title: Palladium(II) complexes with saturated NHC ligands: synthesis, X-ray structures and preliminary catalytic tests
abstract: Four (SIMes)Pd(II) and (SIPr)Pd(II) complexes with allyl, cinnamyl or acetate ancillary ligands were synthesised by transmetallation from the corresponding silver–NHC intermediates. X-ray quality crystals were grown by slow diffusion and the solid-state structures of three complexes were determined; Pd–C(NHC) bond lengths fell in the range 2.012–2.031 Å, consistent with literature benchmarks for saturated NHC donors. Catalytic activity was assessed in test Suzuki–Miyaura couplings of 4-bromoacetophenone with phenylboronic acid in ethanol/water (3:1) at 60 °C with K2CO3 as base. Turnover numbers ranged from 840 to 2 300 across the four complexes after 2 h, with the cinnamyl variant showing the highest activity. Catalyst loading was 0.5 mol%. These results established the baseline for subsequent work on reducing reaction temperatures and expanding the substrate scope to aryl chlorides.

title: Effect of N-substituent bulk on the activation of (NHC)Pd(allyl)Cl pre-catalysts in aqueous media
abstract: The activation pathways of six (NHC)Pd(allyl)Cl pre-catalysts bearing NHC ligands with varying N-substituent steric profiles (N-Me, N-Bn, N-iPr, N-Cy, N-Mes, N-DIPP) were studied in D2O/DMSO-d6 mixtures by time-resolved 1H NMR and ESI-MS. Induction periods before observation of catalytic turnover varied from less than 5 min for the N-Me complex to over 40 min for the N-DIPP analogue, consistent with slower protodemetalation of bulkier allyl groups by water. Arrhenius parameters were extracted from variable-temperature experiments between 25 and 60 °C; activation energies ranged from 58 to 89 kJ mol−1. The data support a mechanism involving allyl protodemetalation as the rate-determining activation step under these aqueous conditions. A linear free-energy relationship between the Tolman cone angle analogue (% buried volume Vbur from SambVca calculations) and activation energy was established across the series, allowing pre-catalyst selection criteria to be defined for low-temperature applications.

title: Comparative study of Pd leaching from NHC–Pd complexes during Suzuki–Miyaura coupling in water and water–ethanol mixtures
abstract: Palladium leaching into solution was quantified by ICP-OES for five (NHC)Pd pre-catalysts after Suzuki–Miyaura coupling runs in pure water, water–ethanol (4:1 and 1:1 v/v), and pure ethanol at 60 °C using Cs2CO3 as base. Pd concentrations in filtered post-reaction solutions ranged from 0.4 to 18.7 ppm depending on solvent composition and NHC ligand. Reactions performed in pure water consistently showed higher Pd leaching than those in mixed solvents, while yields were uniformly above 90% by GC-MS quantification using naphthalene as internal standard. Hot-filtration tests and Hg-poisoning experiments were consistent with a predominantly homogeneous catalytic cycle in ethanol-rich media but suggested partial heterogeneous contribution in aqueous conditions. These findings have practical implications for catalyst recycling and product purity in pharmaceutical synthesis contexts where residual Pd limits are tightly regulated.

title: Room-temperature Suzuki–Miyaura coupling of aryl bromides in water using an (NHC)Pd(1-methylallyl)Cl pre-catalyst
abstract: A palladium pre-catalyst bearing an unsymmetrical N-(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-N'-(n-butyl)imidazol-2-ylidene NHC ligand and a 1-methylallyl leaving group was synthesised in four steps and characterised by NMR, elemental analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. In Suzuki–Miyaura coupling of 24 aryl bromides with aryl- and vinylboronic acids in water at 25 °C with K3PO4 as base, isolated yields of 73–98% were obtained within 3 h at 0.2 mol% Pd loading. Electron-poor and electron-neutral aryl bromides reacted cleanly; electron-rich substrates required modest warming to 40 °C. Sterically hindered ortho-substituted substrates gave yields of 65–78%. Control experiments with pre-formed Pd(0) nanoparticles showed lower reproducibility, supporting the role of the defined molecular pre-catalyst. The methodology was applied to the synthesis of three biaryl fragments relevant to pharmaceutical intermediate structures.

title: Influence of water-solubilising substituents on NHC–Pd pre-catalyst performance in purely aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura reactions
abstract: Four NHC–Pd complexes were prepared in which the NHC N-substituents carried sulfonato, polyethylene glycol (PEG-350), hydroxy or quaternary ammonium groups intended to improve catalyst solubility and mass-transfer efficiency in water without added co-solvent or surfactant. Solubility in water at 25 °C ranged from 0.8 mM for the hydroxy variant to 34 mM for the sulfonato complex. Catalytic runs with 4-bromobenzaldehyde and 4-methoxyphenylboronic acid at 50 °C with K2CO3 showed turnover frequencies at 30 min of 120–680 h−1, with the sulfonato complex outperforming all others. The PEG-functionalised catalyst could be partially recovered by precipitation with diethyl ether and reused three times with less than 8% yield drop. The quaternary ammonium variant showed reduced activity attributable to partial catalyst deactivation through ion-pairing with the borate leaving group, as evidenced by 11B NMR spectroscopy.

title: NHC–Pd complexes on modified silica as heterogenised catalysts for Suzuki–Miyaura coupling: preparation, characterisation and recyclability
abstract: SBA-15 mesoporous silica was functionalised with 3-chloropropyltriethoxysilane and subsequently reacted with N-methylimidazole to graft imidazolium chloride groups at surface loadings of 0.42–0.61 mmol g−1, as determined by elemental analysis and solid-state 13C CP-MAS NMR. Palladium was incorporated by reaction with [Pd(OAc)2] followed by reduction with phenylsilane, yielding surface-bound NHC–Pd(II) species confirmed by XPS (Pd 3d5/2 at 337.8 eV) and TEM (no Pd nanoparticles detected above 1 nm). In aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura coupling of aryl bromides at 60 °C, the heterogenised system achieved yields comparable to the homogeneous analogue in the first run, but retained 88% activity after five consecutive runs with Pd leaching below 1.1 ppm per cycle by ICP-OES. BET surface area decreased from 724 to 601 m2 g−1 after five cycles, suggesting minor pore blockage without structural collapse.

title: Density functional theory study of oxidative addition of aryl chlorides to (NHC)Pd(0) complexes bearing sterically differentiated ligands
abstract: The oxidative addition of chlorobenzene and four para-substituted aryl chlorides to a set of (NHC)Pd(0) model complexes was investigated using DFT at the M06-L/def2-TZVP level with implicit solvation (SMD, water). Transition-state geometries, activation barriers and reaction free energies were computed for NHC ligands covering a Vbur range of 26–42%. Calculated barriers for chlorobenzene ranged from 19.2 to 28.7 kcal mol−1, decreasing with increasing electron donation as measured by the Tolman electronic parameter analogue derived from computed CO stretching frequencies. A moderate steric penalty was identified for Vbur above 37%, arising from increased distortion of the Pd coordination plane in the transition state. These computational results are in qualitative agreement with experimental rate data obtained by in situ 31P NMR monitoring with a triphenylphosphine competition probe and provide guidance for ligand selection in reactions targeting aryl chloride substrates.

title: Gram-scale aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura coupling for synthesis of fluorinated biphenyl building blocks at 0.05 mol% Pd loading
abstract: A scalability study of aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura coupling was conducted using an (NHC)Pd(cinnamyl)Cl pre-catalyst at 0.05 mol% loading in water/2-propanol (9:1) with K3PO4 as base at 50 °C. Target substrates were six fluorinated aryl bromides of interest as building blocks in medicinal chemistry and agrochemical applications, selected in consultation with a regional fine-chemicals supplier. Reactions were carried out at the 5–25 g scale; isolated yields after aqueous extraction and recrystallisation ranged from 81 to 95%. Residual Pd in isolated products was 1.2–4.8 ppm by ICP-OES, meeting ICH Q3D guideline limits for oral dosage forms without additional scavenging treatment. E-factor values calculated for each transformation ranged from 8.3 to 14.1, comparing favourably with literature precedent for Pd-catalysed couplings in organic solvents. Reaction telescoping with in situ-prepared boronic acids was demonstrated for one substrate pair.

title: Benchmarking fifteen (NHC)Pd pre-catalysts in aqueous Suzuki–Miyaura coupling: a systematic comparison across substrate classes
abstract: Fifteen commercially accessible or readily synthesised (NHC)Pd pre-catalysts were evaluated against a standardised 30-substrate test set comprising aryl bromides and chlorides with a range of electronic and steric properties, heteroaryl bromides, and vinylboronic acids. Reactions were performed under uniform conditions in water/ethanol (4:1) at 40 °C, 0.5 mol% Pd, K2CO3 base, 2 h. Yields were determined by quantitative GC-MS; the full dataset (450 data points) is deposited in the supplementary materials. Principal component analysis of the yield data, combined with the ligand descriptors %Vbur, natural bond orbital charge on Pd, and activation energy from the companion DFT study, identified two performance clusters. Cluster A catalysts (six complexes) achieved median yields above 88% across all substrate classes, while Cluster B showed selectivity for electron-poor aryl bromides only. The analysis provides a decision framework for catalyst selection based on substrate profile without extensive trial experimentation.

title: Transcriptomic response of Desulfovibrio desulfuricans to sulphonate-functionalised polymer surfaces under anaerobic conditions
abstract: RNA sequencing was used to characterise gene expression in Desulfovibrio desulfuricans strain NS-7, isolated from a conditioned cation exchange resin in Novi Sad, when grown on sulphonate-functionalised polystyrene beads compared with inert glass beads under identical anaerobic conditions. Differential expression analysis identified 312 genes upregulated and 189 downregulated (|log₂FC| > 1.5, adjusted p < 0.05) on sulphonate surfaces. The most strongly upregulated genes included those encoding dissimilatory sulphite reductase (dsrA, dsrB), adenylyl-sulphate reductase (aprA) and several genes of unknown function in a genomic island tentatively associated with surface adhesion. Downregulation of flagellar assembly genes suggests transition to a sessile mode. The dataset provides the first transcriptome-level evidence that sulphonate surface chemistry actively modulates SRB gene expression in a manner consistent with direct sulphonate utilisation, complementing isotope-tracing data from the same group.

title: Comparative assessment of four applicability domain methods for azole QSAR models predicting ergosterol biosynthesis inhibition
abstract: Four methods for defining the applicability domain (AD) of QSAR models—the bounding box, the leverage-based Williams plot, the Euclidean distance to the centroid, and the k-nearest neighbours approach—were compared on two external datasets of azole antifungals (n = 67 and n = 43 compounds) targeting lanosterol 14α-demethylase. Models were built on a training set of 89 structurally diverse azoles using multiple linear regression. The k-NN method (k = 5, threshold at the 90th percentile of training set distances) produced the best balance between coverage (78 %) and predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.31 log units) on the combined external sets. The leverage approach was most conservative, retaining only 61 % of external compounds within the domain. Bounding box performance was highly sensitive to the number of descriptors included. Practical recommendations are given for choosing an AD method depending on the intended regulatory or screening context.
venue: SAR and QSAR in Environmental Research

title: Primena AHP metode za rangiranje istraživačko-razvojnih projekata u malim i srednjim preduzećima
abstract: U radu se analizira primena analitičko-hijerarhijskog procesa (AHP) za rangiranje R&D projekata u 14 malih i srednjih tehnoloških preduzeća sa područja Vojvodine. Istraživanje je sprovedeno putem strukturiranih intervjua s menadžerima i rukovodiocima razvoja tokom 2009. i 2010. godine. Identifikovano je šest ključnih kriterijuma: strateška usklađenost, tržišni potencijal, tehnička izvodljivost, rok realizacije, budžetska ograničenja i raspoloživost kadra. Primenom AHP modela u softverskom okruženju Expert Choice, rangiranje predloženih projekata pokazalo je statistički značajno slaganje s naknadnim odlukama menadžmenta (Kendalov koeficijent korelacije τ = 0,74). Rezultati ukazuju da je AHP primenljiv čak i kada preduzeća nemaju formalizovane procese upravljanja portfoliom, ali da kvalitet izlaznih rangova zavisi od doslednosti procenjivača – u 4 od 14 slučajeva zabeležena je indeks nekonzistentnosti veći od 0,10, što je zahtevalo ponovljene sesije. Rad doprinosi razumevanju praktičnih ograničenja AHP-a u kontekstu ograničenih organizacionih kapaciteta.

title: Combining Data Envelopment Analysis and Scoring Models for R&D Project Selection in Technology Firms
abstract: This paper examines the use of Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) as a complement to weighted scoring models in selecting R&D projects within technology-oriented firms. A cross-sectional dataset was assembled from 27 Serbian manufacturing and ICT companies, covering 183 candidate projects evaluated between 2009 and 2012. DEA was applied in an input-oriented, variable returns-to-scale formulation, treating personnel costs and calendar time as inputs, and expected revenue and patent potential as outputs. Efficiency scores were then combined with a five-criterion scoring model using a convex combination rule. The integrated approach reduced the shortlist of fundable projects by 18 percent compared with scoring alone, while improving the average efficiency of selected projects by 0.12 DEA units. Sensitivity analysis showed that the weighting of the combination parameter significantly affected outcomes in highly constrained budgets but had negligible influence when slack exceeded 30 percent of total resources. The findings suggest a structured protocol for practitioners who wish to incorporate both strategic fit and technical efficiency into portfolio decisions.

title: Strateška usklađenost R&D portfolija: merenje i implikacije za srednja preduzeća u prerađivačkoj industriji Srbije
abstract: Rad se bavi operacionalizacijom koncepta strateške usklađenosti R&D portfolija u kontekstu srednje velikih prerađivačkih preduzeća u Srbiji. Na uzorku od 38 preduzeća sa 50 do 250 zaposlenih, primenom anketnog upitnika i analize interne dokumentacije, konstruisan je indeks strateške usklađenosti (ISU) koji obuhvata pet dimenzija: tehnološku orijentaciju, tržišni fokus, finansijsku konzistentnost, kadrovsku osnovu i vremenski horizont. Korelaciona analiza pokazala je statistički značajnu pozitivnu vezu između ISU i trogodišnjeg rasta prihoda od prodaje (r = 0,51, p < 0,01). Multipla regresija ukazuje da tehnološka orijentacija i tržišni fokus zajedno objašnjavaju 34% varijanse rasta prihoda, dok preostale dimenzije nisu postigle statističku značajnost na nivou 0,05. Rezultati potvrđuju da formalizacija procesa strateške usklađenosti donosi merljive prednosti, ali da njen doprinos slabi u preduzećima s visokim stepenom neizvesnosti tržišnih uslova.

title: Risk-Adjusted Prioritization of R&D Projects: A Monte Carlo Simulation Approach
abstract: Standard project prioritization models in R&D management typically rely on deterministic estimates of cost and benefit, which underrepresent real-world uncertainty. This study applies Monte Carlo simulation to adjust priority scores in a portfolio of 62 R&D projects drawn from eight technology companies in Serbia and Hungary. Input distributions for development cost, time-to-market, and expected net present value were elicited through expert workshops and calibrated against three years of historical project data. Simulated priority distributions were compared with deterministic rankings derived from a standard weighted scoring model. In 23 of the 62 projects, the rank position shifted by more than two places after risk adjustment, with high-cost, long-horizon projects being systematically downgraded. A threshold analysis revealed that below a budget slack of 15 percent, risk-adjusted rankings differed substantially from deterministic ones in 71 percent of portfolio configurations tested. The paper proposes a simplified two-phase procedure suitable for companies without dedicated risk management departments, requiring only basic spreadsheet tooling.

title: Uticaj organizacione strukture na efikasnost upravljanja R&D portfoliom: komparativna studija
abstract: Rad istražuje vezu između tipa organizacione strukture (funkcionalna, matrična, projektna) i efikasnosti upravljanja R&D portfoliom u 29 srednje velikih preduzeća tehnološkog sektora u Srbiji i Bosni i Hercegovini. Efikasnost je operacionalizovana kroz tri pokazatelja: stopu realizacije planiranih projekata, prosečno prekoračenje budžeta i vreme od inicijacije do primene rezultata. Podaci su prikupljeni kombinacijom polustrukturiranih intervjua i pregleda projektne dokumentacije. Analiza varijanse (ANOVA) pokazala je statistički značajne razlike između organizacionih tipova u svim trima pokazateljima (p < 0,05). Matrična organizacija beleži najniže prosečno prekoračenje budžeta (8,3%), dok projektna organizacija ostvaruje najkraće vreme primene (14,2 meseca). Funkcionalna organizacija, najzastupljenija u uzorku (55%), pokazuje najveće varijacije u svim pokazateljima. Rezultati sugerišu da prelaz ka matričnoj ili projektnoj organizaciji može biti opravdan čak i za preduzeća sa svega 5–10 istovremenih R&D projekata.

title: Portfolio Balancing Heuristics for Firms with Constrained R&D Budgets: Evidence from the Western Balkans
abstract: This paper investigates the practical use of portfolio balancing heuristics in R&D-active technology firms operating under tight budget constraints, a context common in the Western Balkans region. Using a survey of 44 firms from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, each with annual R&D budgets between 50,000 and 500,000 euros, the study maps the heuristics actually employed against a reference taxonomy of 12 documented heuristics from the operations research literature. The most frequently reported heuristics were budget-ratio rules (68% of firms) and stage-gate filtering (52%), whereas optimization-based approaches were used by only 9% of respondents. A regression analysis linking heuristic sophistication to self-reported portfolio performance (measured on a validated 7-item scale) found a significant positive effect for firms above 200,000 euros in annual R&D spend but no significant effect for smaller budgets. The paper concludes with a decision flowchart guiding practitioners in selecting appropriate heuristics based on budget size and organizational capacity.

title: Integracija Balanced Scorecard pristupa u prioritizaciju R&D portfolija: studija slučaja
abstract: Rad opisuje integraciju Balanced Scorecard (BSC) okvira s modelom prioritizacije R&D portfolija u jednom srednje velikom srpskom preduzeću iz sektora automatizacije industrijskih procesa, koje zapošljava oko 180 radnika. Studija slučaja zasnovana je na dvogodišnjoj saradnji (2017–2019) tokom koje je autorka učestvovala kao konsultant. Prikazano je kako su četiri BSC perspektive (finansijska, korisnička, interna, rast i učenje) prevedene u kvantitativne težine kriterijuma za AHP model prioritizacije. Inicijalni portfelj od 21 projektnog predloga sveden je na realizabilni skup od 12 projekata. Praćenjem realizacije tokom 18 meseci utvrđeno je da su projekti selektovani integrisanim BSC-AHP pristupom u proseku ostvarili 91% planiranih KPI vrednosti, u poređenju sa 74% kod projekata odobrenih ranije, bez formalnog modela. Rad ukazuje na vrednost iterativnih kalibracijskih sesija s menadžmentom kao ključnog faktora uspešne primene.

title: Assessing the Maturity of R&D Portfolio Management Practices in Serbian Technology SMEs: A Framework and Preliminary Survey
abstract: Despite extensive literature on R&D portfolio management in large multinational firms, little is known about the maturity levels of these practices in small and medium-sized technology enterprises in transition economies. This paper develops a five-level maturity model for R&D portfolio management (RPM-MM) tailored to firms with 20–250 employees, drawing on capability maturity concepts from software engineering and adapting them to the specificities of R&D governance. The model was validated through expert review involving 11 academics and practitioners from Serbia, Croatia, and Romania. A preliminary survey of 33 Serbian technology SMEs placed 67 percent at maturity level 1 or 2 (ad hoc or defined processes), 27 percent at level 3 (managed), and only two firms at levels 4 or 5. Maturity level correlated positively with firm age (r = 0.43) and negatively with reported project failure rate (r = –0.38). The paper provides a self-assessment questionnaire comprising 30 items across six process areas, suitable for use by firms without external consultants.

title: Višekriterijumska optimizacija R&D portfolija u uslovima budžetske neizvesnosti: hibridni pristup zasnovan na stohastičkom programiranju
abstract: Rad razmatra problem formiranja R&D portfolija u situacijama kada finansijska sredstva nisu u potpunosti poznata unapred, što je uobičajeno za preduzeća koja se oslanjaju na kombinaciju sopstvenih prihoda i povremenih grantova. Predložen je hibridni model koji kombinuje stohastičko programiranje s dva scenarija budžetnih realizacija i TOPSIS metodu za konačno rangiranje projekata. Model je testiran na sintetičkim podacima generisanim na osnovu agregiranih karakteristika 19 portfelja iz ranijih studija. Simulirana su 500 budžetnih scenarija pri čemu je varijansa alokacije između projekata smanjena za 28% u poređenju s determinističkim TOPSIS modelom, uz zadržavanje prosečnog ranga projekata unutar ±1,2 mesta. Osetljivostna analiza pokazuje da su rezultati robustni na promene verovatnoća scenarija dok god razlika između scenarija ne prelazi 40% ukupnog budžeta. Predloženi postupak zahteva Excel ili R okruženje i prilagođen je preduzećima bez specijalizovane OR podrške.

title: The Effect of EU Funding Dependency on R&D Portfolio Composition in Western Balkan SMEs
abstract: Technology SMEs in the Western Balkans increasingly depend on EU-funded programmes to finance R&D activities, which may distort their portfolio composition toward projects that are eligible for grants rather than strategically optimal. This paper tests that hypothesis using data from 57 technology SMEs in Serbia and North Macedonia collected between 2019 and 2022. Firms were classified into three groups by share of EU funding in total R&D expenditure: low (below 20%), medium (20–60%), and high (above 60%). Portfolio composition was assessed along four dimensions: time horizon distribution, technology readiness level spread, market segment concentration, and ratio of incremental to exploratory projects. MANOVA results indicate that high-dependency firms showed significantly shorter average project time horizons (mean 18.4 months vs. 28.1 months for low-dependency firms, p < 0.01) and a higher share of incremental projects (73% vs. 54%). The findings have implications for both firm-level strategy and the design of national and regional R&D support schemes.

title: Projektni portfelj i organizaciono učenje: istraživanje povratnih veza u srednje velikim tehnološkim preduzećima
abstract: Upravljanje R&D portfoliom uglavnom se posmatra kao jednokratan proces izbora projekata, zanemarujući povratne veze između ishoda projekata i budućih odluka o prioritizaciji. Ovaj rad istražuje mehanizme organizacionog učenja koji posreduju između evaluacije završenih projekata i unapređenja kriterijuma za naredne cikluse prioritizacije. Istraživanje je zasnovano na dubinskim intervjuima s 24 menadžera iz 12 preduzeća u Vojvodini, praćenim analizom internih izveštaja. Kvalitativna analiza primenom kodiranja na osnovu utemeljene teorije identifikovala je tri distinktivna obrasca: reaktivno učenje (post-projektna analiza bez sistemskog prenosa znanja), adaptivno učenje (modifikacija težina kriterijuma nakon ciklusa) i generativno učenje (redefinisanje same strukture portfolia). Reaktivni obrazac prisutan je u 9 od 12 preduzeća. Rad sugeriše da formalizacija 'lekcija naučenih' protokola može olakšati prelaz ka adaptivnom obrascu bez značajnih ulaganja u sisteme za upravljanje znanjem.

title: Calibrating Multi-Criteria R&D Portfolio Models with Historical Data: A Procedure for Mid-Sized Firms
abstract: Multi-criteria portfolio prioritization models are sensitive to the weights assigned to evaluation criteria, yet most firms set these weights through expert judgment alone, without calibrating against historical outcomes. This paper proposes a backward calibration procedure in which archived project records are used to infer implied criterion weights that would have produced rankings closest to actual managerial decisions. The procedure is formalized as a constrained least-squares optimization and applied to retrospective data from six technology firms in Serbia and Hungary, covering 148 completed projects over a period of five to eight years per firm. The calibrated models achieved a median rank-order correlation of 0.81 with historical decisions, compared with 0.62 for uncalibrated expert-elicited weights on the same data. Calibration also revealed systematic discrepancies between stated and revealed preferences in five of the six firms, particularly regarding the weight attributed to time-to-market. The paper provides open-source R code for the calibration routine and a recommended data collection template.

title: Grey Relational Analysis for Ranking Vegetable Oil Suppliers Under Incomplete Information
abstract: Supplier evaluation in the edible oil sector frequently involves incomplete or imprecise data, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises that lack formalised procurement systems. This study applies grey relational analysis (GRA) to rank five sunflower oil suppliers for a mid-sized processing company in southern Vojvodina. Data were gathered through structured interviews and a review of procurement records spanning three years. Eight evaluation attributes were included: cost per tonne, moisture content of raw material, contract fulfilment rate, lead time variability, traceability documentation, proximity to plant, pesticide residue compliance, and supplier financial health. Grey coefficients and relational grades were computed, and a final ranking was derived. Results indicated that traceability documentation and pesticide residue compliance emerged as the most discriminating attributes. The paper also discusses the practical conditions under which GRA offers advantages over classical weighted-sum methods when attribute data are partially missing.

title: Perceived vs. Measured Resilience: A Comparison of Manager Self-Assessments and Financial Ratio Proxies in Serbian SMEs
abstract: Organizational resilience is often captured through manager self-reports, yet it is unclear how well subjective assessments correspond to observable financial indicators. This study compares resilience scores from a structured questionnaire administered to 93 managers of Serbian manufacturing SMEs with three financial ratio proxies—current ratio, interest coverage ratio, and operating profit margin—drawn from the Business Registers Agency of Serbia database for the same firms. Spearman correlations between self-reported resilience dimensions and financial proxies were weak to moderate (ρ = 0.18–0.41), with the strongest alignment observed between resource redundancy perceptions and the current ratio. Firm age and industry sector moderated several relationships. The findings suggest that survey instruments and financial proxies capture distinct facets of resilience and should be treated as complementary rather than interchangeable. Implications for measurement practice in transitional economy contexts are discussed, including data availability constraints that limit purely objective approaches in the region.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Fieldbus-to-Ethernet Gateway Latency Under Variable Network Load
abstract: This paper reports a systematic measurement study of round-trip latency introduced by software-based gateways translating between Profibus DP and standard IEEE 802.3 Ethernet. Four open-source gateway implementations were deployed on a laboratory testbed comprising a Siemens S7-300 PLC, a Raspberry Pi 3 acting as gateway hardware, and a dedicated measurement workstation. Traffic load was varied from 10% to 90% of nominal Profibus bandwidth using a synthetic cyclic data generator. Results show that median latency ranged from 1.8 ms to 14.3 ms depending on gateway software architecture, with event-driven designs outperforming polling-based designs by a factor of 2.1 at high load. Jitter was measured at the 99th percentile and found to exceed 10 ms in two of the four implementations, which the authors argue disqualifies them for motion-control applications without additional buffering. The study also identifies a memory leak in one widely used open-source project and proposes a patch that reduces worst-case latency by 18%.

title: Modbus TCP to OPC UA Mapping: Addressing Data Type Mismatches in Legacy Device Integration
abstract: Integrating legacy Modbus TCP devices into OPC UA-based supervisory systems is complicated by fundamental differences in data type representation, addressing semantics, and discovery mechanisms. This paper describes a structured mapping procedure that converts Modbus register maps, expressed in the common EDS-like flat file format used by device vendors, into OPC UA NodeSet2 XML definitions. The procedure handles unsigned 16-bit Modbus registers mapped onto OPC UA structured types, resolves the absence of native floating-point support in older Modbus dialects through a configurable byte-order and scaling layer, and generates an OPC UA companion information model that preserves engineering unit metadata. The mapping was validated against eleven legacy sensor and actuator devices from three manufacturers on a water treatment pilot installation in Zrenjanin. All eleven devices were browsable and subscribable through a standard OPC UA client within 40 minutes of applying the procedure, compared with an average of 4.2 hours using purely manual approaches. Remaining limitations related to Modbus exception code propagation are discussed.

title: Middleware Design Patterns for Bridging OPC UA and MQTT in Industrial IoT Deployments
abstract: This chapter surveys and classifies middleware design patterns used to mediate between OPC UA server-client architectures and MQTT broker-based publish–subscribe systems in factory-floor IoT deployments. Starting from a taxonomy of eleven distinct integration scenarios drawn from publicly documented industrial installations in Central and Eastern Europe, the chapter identifies three recurring structural patterns: the stateful session bridge, the topic-mapped proxy, and the schema-aware translator. Each pattern is described using UML component diagrams and evaluated against criteria including message ordering guarantees, reconnection behaviour, and quality-of-service mapping between OPC UA MonitoredItems and MQTT QoS levels 0–2. A reference implementation of the schema-aware translator pattern, built on the Eclipse Milo OPC UA stack and the Mosquitto broker, is provided and benchmarked on a Raspberry Pi 4, achieving throughput of 1,200 tag updates per second with less than 3 ms median end-to-end delay. Security bridging between OPC UA certificates and MQTT TLS mutual authentication is also addressed.
venue: Advances in Industrial Communication Systems, Springer (edited volume)

title: An OPC UA Information Model for Condition Monitoring Data in Small-Scale CNC Machining Centres
abstract: The paper presents the design and validation of an OPC UA companion information model targeting condition monitoring on small-scale CNC machining centres with spindle power below 7.5 kW, a category not covered by existing companion specifications such as OPC UA for Machinery. The model was derived from a requirements analysis involving interviews with five machine tool operators and two maintenance engineers at a mechanical parts manufacturer in Novi Sad. It exposes spindle vibration RMS values, tool-change cycle counts, axis temperature readings, and alarm history as typed OPC UA nodes with standardised engineering units encoded per UNECE Recommendation 20. The model was implemented on a Beckhoff CX5130 industrial PC and validated by connecting it to three third-party OPC UA clients; all clients correctly interpreted node types and unit annotations without client-side customisation. An open-source NodeSet2 file and a Python validation script are provided. The paper also reports a six-week pilot in which predictive maintenance alerts derived from the model reduced unplanned downtime by 23% compared with the preceding period.

title: Semantic Interoperability Between OPC UA and Asset Administration Shell in a Mixed-Protocol Shopfloor Environment
abstract: The Asset Administration Shell (AAS) standardised under IEC 63278 and the OPC UA information model share goals of machine-readable asset description but differ substantially in metamodel structure, serialisation formats, and runtime access mechanisms. This paper analyses the structural differences between the two formalisms and proposes a bidirectional synchronisation service that maps AAS Submodel descriptors to OPC UA ObjectType hierarchies and vice versa, using a declarative YAML configuration file to specify correspondence rules. The service was prototyped in Java using the Eclipse BaSyx AAS SDK and the Prosys OPC UA Java SDK and deployed in a laboratory shopfloor emulation containing eight simulated production assets representing three protocol domains: OPC UA, EtherNet/IP via a gateway, and MQTT-connected sensors. Synchronisation round-trip latency averaged 67 ms for a 48-property AAS Submodel under idle conditions. Semantic fidelity was assessed by exporting the resulting OPC UA model to RDF using a previously published mapping and running twelve SPARQL competency queries; eleven queries returned correct results, with one failing due to an unresolved unit-of-measure alignment issue that is discussed in detail.

title: Evaluating OPC UA PubSub Over TSN for Real-Time Control Traffic in Brownfield Networks
abstract: OPC UA PubSub combined with IEEE 802.1 Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) is increasingly proposed as a unified transport for both real-time control and monitoring traffic in industrial Ethernet networks, but most studies use greenfield testbeds. This paper reports experiments on a brownfield emulation where TSN-capable switches were inserted into an existing EtherNet/IP segment carrying live cyclic I/O traffic from a conveyor belt controller. Three OPC UA PubSub configurations — UDP multicast without TSN, UDP multicast with 802.1Qbv scheduled traffic shaping, and raw Ethernet frames with 802.1Qav credit-based shaper — were evaluated for worst-case delivery latency and packet loss at co-existing traffic loads of 40% and 70% of link capacity. With 802.1Qbv, worst-case latency for a 200-byte PubSub message dropped from 4.7 ms to 0.9 ms at 70% load, and zero packet loss was observed across a 30-minute measurement window. Without TSN, packet loss reached 0.4% at 70% load. Coexistence with EtherNet/IP implicit messaging showed no measurable degradation of the existing control traffic.

title: A Configuration Language for Declarative Specification of Industrial Protocol Translation Rules
abstract: Configuring industrial protocol gateways today relies heavily on vendor-specific graphical tools that do not support version control, automated testing, or deployment pipelines. This paper introduces ProtoSpec, a domain-specific language (DSL) for declarative specification of translation rules between pairs of industrial protocols. The grammar, defined in ANTLR4, covers field-level type coercion, scaling, enumeration mapping, and conditional routing based on tag values. A compiler toolchain generates gateway configuration artefacts targeting three open-source gateway runtimes. The language was evaluated through a user study with twelve automation engineers, half of whom had prior experience with at least one scripting language. Participants using ProtoSpec completed a set of five translation specification tasks in a median of 18 minutes compared with 41 minutes using a representative graphical tool, with a lower error rate (8% vs. 23% of task steps containing at least one mistake). The paper also discusses how ProtoSpec specifications can be stored in a Git repository and validated in a CI pipeline using a provided Docker-based test harness.

title: Temporal Convolutional Networks for Player Action Sequence Classification
abstract: Recurrent architectures such as LSTM have been the default choice for sequential player telemetry modelling, but they scale poorly on streams sampled at 200–500 Hz due to vanishing gradients over long sequences. This paper evaluates temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) as an alternative for classifying action sequences as normal, macro-assisted, or fully automated. Three datasets are used: two from game studios in Novi Sad and one publicly shared by a research group in Warsaw. Sequence lengths range from 500 to 4,000 events. TCN models with dilation factors of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 are compared against LSTM and GRU baselines across all three datasets. TCN achieves the highest macro-F1 on two of three datasets (0.89 and 0.91) while requiring 40–60% less training time than LSTM equivalents on the same GPU hardware. The paper also examines the receptive field requirements for capturing multi-scale behavioural patterns and reports ablations over kernel size and dilation depth.

title: Compositional Verification of Embedded Software Stacks: Scalability Limits and Practical Workarounds
abstract: Compositional verification decomposes a global correctness proof into per-component proofs discharged against local assume-guarantee contracts, promising relief from state-space explosion. However, compositionality breaks down when shared global resources—interrupt controllers, DMA channels, non-preemptive schedulers—create implicit dependencies not captured in pairwise contracts. This chapter surveys three years of experience applying compositional verification to industrial embedded stacks of 5 to 23 components. We identify four recurring dependency patterns that defeat standard circular assume-guarantee reasoning and describe adaptations: dependency annotations, ordered discharge sequences and partial verification with residual simulation. Case studies are drawn from a body-control module and a motor-drive controller. The chapter concludes with a discussion of tool support and the current state of integration with commercial static analysers.

title: Forecasting intermittent demand in regional retail chains
abstract: This paper investigates the challenge of forecasting intermittent demand within regional retail chains operating in Southeastern Europe. Intermittent demand—characterized by sporadic, irregular sales interspersed with periods of zero activity—poses significant difficulties for standard time-series methods. The study evaluates a range of established intermittent demand forecasting methods, including Croston's method, the Syntetos–Boylan Approximation, and Teunter–Syntetos–Babai classification, alongside more recent machine-learning-based approaches. A comparative experiment is conducted using point-of-sale data collected from three mid-sized retail chains operating across the Vojvodina region of Serbia. The analysis considers multiple product categories with varying demand density and coefficient of variation. Results indicate that ensemble methods combining statistical and gradient-boosting components outperform classical methods in accuracy as measured by mean absolute scaled error and cycle service level. The paper further discusses the practical implications of model selection for inventory replenishment policies, emphasizing that forecast accuracy improvements translate meaningfully into reductions in both stockout frequency and excess inventory costs. Recommendations are provided for practitioners seeking to implement intermittent demand forecasting in resource-constrained retail environments.

title: Promotion effects on store-level demand
abstract: This paper examines how promotional activities—including temporary price reductions, in-store displays, and flyer advertising—affect demand at the individual store level within regional retail chains. Using scanner data from a panel of twelve stores over a thirty-month period, the study constructs a hierarchical regression framework that decomposes observed demand lifts into baseline sales, promotional uplift, and cannibalization effects. Special attention is given to the interaction between promotion type and product category, as well as to temporal dynamics such as pre-promotion dip and post-promotion trough effects. The results confirm that promotional response is highly heterogeneous across store formats and geographic locations, underscoring the limitation of chain-level aggregated models. An extended version of the model incorporating store-specific promotional elasticity parameters is proposed and shown to improve demand forecasts during promotional periods by a statistically significant margin. The paper concludes with a discussion of how improved promotional demand models can be integrated into existing inventory management systems to reduce waste and improve service levels.

title: Inventory positioning under promotional uncertainty in multi-echelon retail networks
abstract: Promotional events introduce substantial demand uncertainty that complicates inventory positioning decisions across multi-echelon retail supply chains. This paper develops a stochastic inventory model that explicitly accounts for promotional demand uplift and its associated variance at both the distribution center and store echelons. The model is parameterized using historical promotional scan data from a fictional retail operator, Meridian Maloprodaja d.o.o., covering a two-year horizon across four distribution centers and forty-seven stores. A simulation-optimization approach is employed to determine safety stock levels and replenishment triggers that minimize total inventory cost while meeting target service levels during and outside promotional windows. Sensitivity analyses reveal that ignoring promotional demand variance in safety stock calculations leads to service level shortfalls of up to eighteen percentage points during high-intensity promotion periods. The paper proposes a practical promotional-state inventory policy that dynamically adjusts reorder points based on a short-term promotional calendar input, and demonstrates its superiority over static policies in a rolling-horizon out-of-sample evaluation. Implications for retail supply chain practitioners and software vendors are discussed.

title: Gradient boosting for retail demand forecasting: a benchmarking study in the Western Balkans
abstract: Machine learning methods have demonstrated strong performance in demand forecasting competitions, yet their practical utility in the context of retail operations in emerging markets remains underexplored. This paper presents a systematic benchmarking study comparing gradient boosting algorithms—specifically LightGBM-inspired and XGBoost-type implementations—against a battery of classical time-series methods including ARIMA, exponential smoothing state space models, and Theta on retail sales data from three fictional retail chains operating in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The dataset comprises weekly store-SKU combinations spanning three years, covering grocery, personal care, and household categories. Feature engineering pipelines incorporating calendar effects, lagged sales, price indices, and promotional flags are constructed and evaluated. Results show that gradient boosting outperforms classical benchmarks across the majority of product categories and forecast horizons, with the performance gap widening for products exhibiting strong promotional sensitivity. However, classical methods remain competitive for slow-moving and intermittent items. The paper offers a practical decision framework guiding retail analysts in method selection based on demand regularity classification and available feature richness.

title: Incorporating external signals into short-term retail demand forecasts
abstract: External signals such as weather conditions, local events, and macroeconomic indicators carry predictive information for retail demand that is not captured by historical sales patterns alone. This paper investigates the incremental forecasting value of integrating publicly available external data sources into short-term store-level demand models. Using a dataset spanning two years of daily sales from Zelena Mreža Prodavnica, a fictional Vojvodinian grocery retailer, the study constructs forecast models augmented with temperature and precipitation data, regional consumer confidence indices, and a structured local events calendar. Model performance is assessed through a blocked cross-validation scheme to avoid data leakage. Findings indicate that weather variables significantly improve forecast accuracy for seasonal fresh produce categories, while consumer confidence indices contribute marginally but consistently across multiple categories. Local event indicators prove most valuable for stores situated near venues hosting large public gatherings. The paper concludes that systematic integration of external signals is feasible within existing retail forecasting infrastructure at modest additional cost, and proposes a lightweight data pipeline architecture suitable for mid-sized retail operators.

title: Demand sensing with high-frequency point-of-sale data: evidence from a Serbian regional retailer
abstract: Demand sensing refers to the practice of using near-real-time transaction data to update short-horizon demand forecasts, thereby enabling more responsive replenishment decisions. This paper applies demand sensing principles to a high-frequency point-of-sale dataset obtained from Vojvođanski Lanac Prodavnica, a fictional regional Serbian retailer operating forty-two stores. Daily transaction counts at the SKU-store level are used to update weekly demand forecasts using a Kalman filter-based state-space framework that assimilates early-week sales observations to revise week-remaining demand estimates. The approach is compared against a baseline that commits to a fixed weekly forecast at the start of the period. Results demonstrate that demand sensing reduces forecast error in the second half of the selling week by approximately twenty-two percent on average, with the largest gains observed for products with high day-of-week sales concentration. The paper discusses the operational requirements for implementing demand sensing, including data latency thresholds, integration with replenishment scheduling systems, and the organizational capabilities necessary to act on intra-week forecast revisions. Limitations related to data quality and system integration are also addressed.

title: Cross-item demand cannibalization in retail promotions: a structured estimation approach
abstract: When a promoted item draws purchases away from related non-promoted products, the resulting cannibalization effect distorts both promotional lift estimates and inventory planning for the broader assortment. This paper proposes a structured vector regression framework for estimating simultaneous cross-item cannibalization effects within product categories during promotional periods. The model is identified using a combination of promotional timing variation and assortment structure constraints, and estimated on scanner panel data from Suncokret Hipermarket, a fictional Serbian hypermarket chain. The paper examines three product categories—carbonated beverages, dairy spreads, and detergents—covering a combined pool of over two hundred SKUs across two years. Estimation results reveal that cannibalization rates vary substantially by category and by the promotional depth applied. Incorporating estimated cannibalization effects into a joint inventory optimization for the affected category is shown to reduce total category stockout rates by eleven percent compared to item-by-item planning. The methodology is designed to be applicable in practice with standard store-level scan data and commercially available computing resources.

title: Forecasting in retail supply chains: methods, challenges, and opportunities in Southeastern Europe
abstract: This book chapter provides a comprehensive review of demand forecasting methods as applied in retail supply chain contexts, with particular attention to the institutional and data environment of Southeastern European markets. The chapter begins by surveying the landscape of classical time-series approaches—including exponential smoothing families, ARIMA-type models, and intermittent demand methods—before transitioning to a review of machine learning and hybrid approaches that have gained traction in recent years. Unique challenges associated with the regional context are discussed, including shorter historical data series due to relatively recent retail modernization, higher promotional intensity relative to Western European benchmarks, and limited availability of high-quality auxiliary data. The chapter then examines specific forecasting scenarios of practical importance: new product introductions, seasonal demand, and promotional events. Case vignettes drawn from the author's research collaborations with fictional retail operators in Serbia and the wider Western Balkans region are used to illustrate methodological trade-offs in practice. The chapter concludes by identifying open research directions, including the integration of supply chain disruption signals and the use of causal inference frameworks for promotional evaluation.

title: Hierarchical forecasting for retail chains: reconciliation methods and their inventory implications
abstract: Retail chains generate demand data at multiple levels of hierarchy—national, regional, store, and SKU—and forecasts produced independently at each level are typically inconsistent with one another, creating coordination problems in supply chain planning. This paper applies hierarchical forecasting reconciliation techniques, including optimal combination and minimum trace reconciliation, to sales data from Dunavska Trgovina, a fictional Serbian retail chain with stores distributed across three regions. The study evaluates reconciliation approaches against unreconciled base forecasts generated by exponential smoothing models at each hierarchy level, using a rolling-origin evaluation over eighteen months. Forecast accuracy is measured at all hierarchical levels, and resulting inventory policies are simulated to assess fill rates and holding costs. Results demonstrate that reconciled forecasts yield modest but consistent accuracy improvements at lower hierarchy levels while substantially reducing inconsistencies that trigger unnecessary emergency replenishments. A sensitivity analysis explores how the benefit of reconciliation varies with the degree of cross-regional demand correlation. The paper provides guidance for retail supply chain planners on selecting and implementing reconciliation strategies within enterprise resource planning systems.

title: Voluntary Disclosure of Social Information in Annual Reports of Serbian Companies: A Longitudinal Analysis 2005–2009
abstract: This study examines the extent and determinants of voluntary social information disclosure in annual reports published by 47 companies listed on the Belgrade Stock Exchange between 2005 and 2009. Using a structured content-analysis instrument with 68 disclosure items drawn from GRI G3 guidelines, the paper scores each report on a 0–1 scale. Ordinary least squares regression models test whether firm size, profitability, leverage, and industry membership predict disclosure scores. Results show that average social disclosure scores increased from 12.4% in 2005 to 19.7% in 2009, but remained low in absolute terms. Firm size (measured by total assets) and membership in extractive or utility sectors are the only statistically significant predictors. The findings suggest that voluntary disclosure in Serbia is primarily driven by visibility pressures rather than genuine stakeholder engagement, and that regulatory intervention may be needed to raise disclosure levels toward European norms.

title: Environmental Reporting Quality Among Manufacturing Firms in Vojvodina: Evidence from 2008–2011
abstract: The paper investigates environmental reporting quality in a sample of 31 manufacturing companies headquartered in Vojvodina that were publicly traded or state-owned between 2008 and 2011. A disclosure quality index was constructed using 52 items covering pollution, resource use, and regulatory compliance, coded from annual reports and corporate websites. The index distinguishes between mere presence of information (quantity) and specificity, comparability, and verifiability (quality). Panel data regressions reveal that while quantity scores improved over the period, quality scores stagnated around 22–25%. Companies in the food processing and chemical sectors scored higher on environmental disclosures than metalworking firms, partly reflecting exposure to EU export markets. The paper argues that a disconnect exists between reporting quantity and actual disclosure quality and that external assurance is associated with marginally higher quality scores, though assurance uptake remains below 10% of the sample.

title: The Relationship Between Audit Committee Characteristics and Non-Financial Disclosure: Evidence from Serbian Listed Companies
abstract: This paper analyses whether audit committee independence, size, and meeting frequency are associated with the quality of non-financial disclosures in annual reports of 55 companies listed on the Prime and Standard segments of the Belgrade Stock Exchange over 2010–2012. Non-financial disclosure quality is operationalised through a 74-item index covering environmental, social, and governance dimensions. Tobit regression is used because the dependent variable is bounded between zero and one. The proportion of independent members on the audit committee is positively and significantly associated with disclosure quality (coefficient 0.18, p < 0.05), while committee size and meeting frequency show no significant effects. These results are consistent with agency theory predictions and suggest that audit committee reforms introduced by the 2011 amendments to the Serbian Company Law had some measurable effect on reporting quality within a relatively short period.
