title: Adoption of Integrated Reporting in Transition Economies: Conceptual Barriers and Institutional Context
abstract: This book chapter situates integrated reporting adoption within the institutional context of transition economies in the Western Balkans, drawing on North's institutional theory and DiMaggio and Powell's isomorphism framework. The chapter reviews documentary evidence from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, covering the period 2010–2015. It argues that weak capital market development, concentrated ownership structures, and limited investor activism reduce the mimetic and normative pressures that drive voluntary uptake of frameworks such as the IIRC International Integrated Reporting Framework. Coercive pressures from state ownership and banking creditors tend to favour traditional financial reporting rather than integrated thinking. The chapter proposes a typology of adoption barriers specific to transition settings and discusses policy implications for securities regulators and professional accounting bodies in the region. The analysis draws on annual reports, regulatory documents, and six semi-structured interviews with preparers and auditors.

title: Do Investors Price Non-Financial Disclosure Quality? Evidence from the Belgrade Stock Exchange 2013–2017
abstract: This paper tests whether higher non-financial disclosure quality is associated with lower cost of equity capital for companies listed on the Belgrade Stock Exchange over the period 2013–2017. Cost of equity is estimated using the implied cost of capital approach with analyst forecast data sourced from a regional financial data provider. Non-financial disclosure quality scores are derived from the instrument developed in earlier work. Fixed-effects panel regressions with robust standard errors are estimated on an unbalanced panel of 48 firms and 240 firm-year observations. The baseline coefficient on disclosure quality is negative and statistically significant (−0.0034, p < 0.01), implying that a one-standard-deviation increase in quality is associated with a reduction in implied cost of equity of approximately 34 basis points. The effect is concentrated among firms with dispersed ownership, consistent with information asymmetry reduction being the primary channel. Results are robust to the exclusion of financial sector companies.

title: Assurance of Non-Financial Statements in Serbia: Current State and Preparers' Perspectives
abstract: External assurance of non-financial statements remains uncommon in Serbia despite the transposition of the EU Non-Financial Reporting Directive (2014/95/EU) into national legislation in 2019. This paper combines a quantitative survey of 38 large public-interest entities subject to the Directive with 12 semi-structured interviews with finance directors, sustainability managers, and external auditors. Findings show that only 11 of the 38 entities obtained any form of external assurance in their first mandatory reporting cycle, and that most chose limited rather than reasonable assurance engagements. Preparers cite cost, lack of clear standards, and insufficient board-level commitment as the main barriers. Auditors note the absence of sector-specific assurance criteria and a shortage of practitioners trained in non-financial verification. The paper discusses implications for the profession and for regulators implementing the forthcoming European Sustainability Reporting Standards.

title: Capital Market Reactions to First-Time Mandatory Non-Financial Reporting: Evidence from Serbian Large Public-Interest Entities
abstract: Serbia's Law on Accounting (2019) introduced mandatory non-financial reporting for large public-interest entities starting with the 2020 financial year. This paper uses an event-study methodology to examine abnormal returns around the first disclosure dates of non-financial statements for 34 companies on the Belgrade Stock Exchange. Three event windows (±1, ±3, and ±5 trading days) are examined using market-adjusted returns. No statistically significant average abnormal returns are detected across the full sample, suggesting that mandatory disclosure alone did not alter investor expectations. Subsample analysis reveals a marginally significant positive reaction (CAR +0.82%, p < 0.10) for companies that voluntarily disclosed above the regulatory minimum. Volume analysis indicates increased trading activity around disclosure for smaller-capitalisation firms. The results suggest that the informational value of mandatory non-financial statements depends substantially on disclosure quality rather than mere compliance.
venue: Eastern European Financial Markets Journal

title: Alignment Between ESRS and Current Serbian Sustainability Reporting Practice: A Gap Analysis
abstract: The European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), mandatory for large EU-listed companies from 2024, are likely to affect Serbian exporters and subsidiaries of EU companies operating in Serbia. This paper conducts a structured gap analysis comparing the content requirements of the twelve cross-cutting and topical ESRS with actual disclosure practices observed in 45 Serbian large companies' 2021 non-financial statements. Gaps are scored at the disclosure requirement level using the 91-item quality instrument developed in prior work, adapted to ESRS terminology. Results show an average gap rate of 71%, meaning that roughly seven in ten ESRS disclosure requirements are unmet or only partially met by current Serbian practice. The largest gaps concern Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions, workforce value-chain due diligence, and biodiversity. Companies with Big Four auditors and with export revenues exceeding 30% of turnover show significantly smaller gaps, suggesting that external accountability pressures are already driving some convergence.

title: Disclosure of Climate-Related Financial Information in Serbia: A Review of TCFD Alignment in Banking and Insurance Sectors
abstract: The Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) framework has been adopted voluntarily by a growing number of financial institutions globally. This paper examines whether Serbian banks and insurance companies subject to mandatory non-financial reporting have incorporated TCFD recommendations into their 2021 and 2022 disclosures. The sample covers 14 banks and 8 insurance companies. Content analysis is conducted using a 44-item TCFD alignment checklist. Mean alignment scores are low: 18.6% for banks and 9.3% for insurers. Governance and strategy pillars show higher disclosure rates than risk management and metrics and targets. Interviews with three bank sustainability officers suggest that awareness of TCFD is improving but that quantitative scenario analysis remains absent from all reports examined. The paper benchmarks Serbian results against a parallel study of Hungarian and Romanian financial institutions conducted by co-authors, identifying convergent low-disclosure patterns across the three countries.

title: Integrated Thinking and Strategy Connectivity in Integrated Reports: Text-Mining Evidence from Central and Eastern European Listed Companies
abstract: Integrated thinking—the premise that organisations manage capitals interdependently—is the conceptual foundation of the IIRC framework but is rarely measured empirically. This paper applies latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) topic modelling and cosine-similarity analysis to the full text of 210 annual and integrated reports published by listed companies in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia between 2019 and 2023. The goal is to assess the degree to which strategy, risk, and capital discussions are textually coherent rather than siloed. Reports are segmented into regulatory sections and section-to-section cosine similarities are calculated. Serbian reports show significantly lower cross-section coherence (mean 0.31) than Slovenian reports (mean 0.47), with Croatian reports in between (mean 0.39). Coherence is positively associated with report length, Big Four assurance, and IIRC framework adoption. The paper demonstrates that text-mining tools can operationalise conceptually rich but hard-to-measure reporting constructs.

title: Readability of Non-Financial Statements in Serbian Public-Interest Entities: A Linguistic Analysis
abstract: Readability of corporate disclosures affects whether the information actually reaches non-expert stakeholders. This paper measures readability of the non-financial statements filed by 40 Serbian public-interest entities for the 2023 reporting year using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Gunning Fog Index, and SMOG formula applied to Serbian-language texts, with formulae recalibrated for a sample of reference Serbian texts. Average grade-level scores place most reports in the 'university graduate' difficulty range (FK grade 16.2), well above the recommended 'upper secondary' target. Longer sentences and a high density of technical and regulatory terminology are the main readability penalties. Reports prepared with the assistance of external consultants or structured on GRI or ESRS templates show marginally better readability scores. The paper recommends plain-language guidance from the Serbian Business Registers Agency and professional accounting bodies, and provides a publicly available Python script for automated readability scoring in Serbian.

title: Real Activity Manipulation Around Tax Thresholds: Evidence from Hungarian and Serbian SMEs
abstract: Small firms near statutory tax thresholds have incentives to manage real activities rather than accruals, because accrual reversals attract auditor scrutiny while operational decisions are harder to challenge. This paper tests that hypothesis using an unbalanced panel of 1,840 Hungarian and Serbian SMEs over 2008–2013. Following Roychowdhury's framework, we construct proxies for abnormal cash flows from operations, abnormal production costs, and abnormal discretionary expenses. Regression discontinuity design around the respective national VAT and corporate income tax thresholds reveals significant downward manipulation of reported revenues among firms immediately below the upper threshold, accompanied by elevated production costs consistent with overproduction. The effect is stronger in Serbia than in Hungary, possibly reflecting weaker enforcement capacity. Results are robust to alternative bandwidth choices and falsification tests using thresholds where no incentive is expected.

title: Auditor Tenure and Independence Impairment in Family-Owned Firms: Evidence from Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: This paper investigates whether long auditor-client relationships are associated with reduced audit quality in family-owned firms in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The sample comprises 178 firms audited continuously by the same auditor for at least five years between 2009 and 2016. Audit quality is proxied by the absolute value of discretionary accruals estimated via the modified Jones model. Auditor tenure is measured as the number of consecutive years of engagement. The main empirical specification is a random-effects panel regression controlling for firm size, leverage, return on assets, and auditor size. Contrary to arguments that familiarity impairs independence, results reveal no statistically significant relationship between tenure length and discretionary accruals in this setting. A possible explanation is that in family-dominated, relationship-based business environments, long auditor tenure may in fact facilitate better knowledge transfer and more effective scrutiny. Robustness checks using alternative accrual models and excluding micro-firms confirm the baseline finding.

title: Auditor Switching in Family Firms: Evidence on Motivations and Fee Consequences in the Western Balkans
abstract: Auditor switches can signal either improved governance or opinion shopping. This study examines the incidence and consequences of auditor switching among 892 family-owned firms in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia over 2014–2020, using data from national business registers supplemented by audit report filings. Logistic regression is used to identify determinants of voluntary switches, and a difference-in-differences estimator compares audit fees in the year before and after the switch for firms that changed auditor against a matched control group that did not. Family firms are about 40 percent less likely to switch auditors in any given year compared to non-family firms, consistent with long-term relationship preferences. Among firms that do switch, those moving from a smaller to a larger audit firm pay on average 31 percent higher fees in the first post-switch year. Switches following a qualified opinion are more common in second-generation firms, suggesting some degree of opinion shopping in succession contexts.

title: Comparing Constraint-Handling Strategies in NSGA-II for Hyperparameter Tuning of Convolutional Networks Under FLOPs Budgets
abstract: Automated hyperparameter optimisation frequently ignores computational cost, producing configurations that are accurate but impractical on restricted hardware. This paper evaluates four constraint-handling strategies—penalty functions, repair operators, feasibility-first dominance, and ε-constrained selection—embedded inside NSGA-II to jointly minimise validation error and floating-point operations per inference pass on a fixed FLOPs ceiling. Experiments use three image-classification benchmarks (CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, and a small histology dataset of 18 000 labelled patches) with search spaces covering learning rate, weight decay, batch size, dropout probability, and depth of two convolutional blocks. Each strategy is run 30 times with a budget of 120 function evaluations. Feasibility-first dominance reaches the closest Pareto front approximation in hypervolume terms on all three datasets, with an average hypervolume ratio of 0.91 relative to the unconstrained reference front. Penalty functions converge faster in early generations but stagnate and are dominated in final populations. Runtime on a single NVIDIA GPU averaged 4.7 hours per full 30-run trial. Results suggest that dominance-based feasibility handling should be the default choice when FLOPs ceilings are hard constraints rather than soft preferences.

title: A Surrogate-Assisted MOEA/D Approach to Cell-Level Neural Architecture Search with Latency Constraints
abstract: Neural architecture search at the cell level involves evaluating thousands of candidate graphs, each requiring full training to estimate accuracy. This work proposes embedding a Gaussian process surrogate model inside MOEA/D to predict validation accuracy and inference latency jointly, allowing expensive true evaluations to be reserved for the most promising decomposition subproblems. The search space follows the DARTS cell formulation with eight candidate operations and a fixed stack of six cells. Surrogate updates use a batch of ten true evaluations per generation, selected by expected hypervolume improvement. Experiments run on CIFAR-100 and a 10-class subset of a publicly available remote-sensing scene dataset, with a hard latency constraint of 15 ms on an ARM Cortex-A55 core measured with ONNX Runtime. Across 20 independent runs, the surrogate-assisted variant reaches equivalent hypervolume to a fully evaluated MOEA/D baseline using 38 percent fewer true evaluations. Discovered architectures with skip connections eliminated outperform hand-designed baselines by 1.2–2.4 percentage points in top-1 accuracy at matched latency. The approach is reproducible; all code and architecture logs are released publicly.

title: Budget-Aware Warm-Starting for Multi-Objective Hyperparameter Optimisation Across Related Tasks
abstract: When a team must tune a family of related models—such as the same architecture retrained on different regional subsets of sensor data—prior optimisation runs contain useful information that is typically discarded. This paper investigates warm-starting NSGA-III with Pareto fronts transferred from earlier runs on related tasks, measuring how transfer affects convergence speed and final solution quality under a fixed evaluation budget of 80 configurations per task. The testbed consists of six regression tasks derived from an industrial energy-consumption monitoring dataset with 14 input features and targets covering heating and cooling loads across building types. Search space includes learning rate schedule type, hidden layer widths (two layers), activation function, and batch normalisation placement. Transfer is implemented via population seeding combined with archive injection; three seeding ratios (25 %, 50 %, 75 % of initial population) are compared against cold-start NSGA-III and random search. At 50 % seeding the method reduces the number of evaluations needed to reach a reference hypervolume threshold by a median of 31 evaluations across tasks, without degrading diversity on tasks where source and target fronts differ substantially. A negative transfer case is identified when task correlation falls below 0.3 in a feature-based similarity metric.

title: Partitioning Strategies for Time-Series Transactional Data in Mixed OLTP/OLAP Workloads
abstract: Databases that serve both transactional and analytical queries on time-series data must choose partitioning strategies that satisfy conflicting access patterns. This paper examines range, hash, and composite partitioning applied to a synthetic financial transaction dataset of 800 million records hosted on a six-node cluster. Query sets representing OLTP (point lookups, short-range scans) and OLAP (monthly aggregations, cohort analysis) workloads are run concurrently at varying ratios from 90/10 OLTP-heavy to 10/90 OLAP-heavy. Range partitioning on the timestamp column reduces OLAP query time by 41% relative to hash partitioning but increases OLTP tail latency by 27% due to hotspot formation on recent partitions. A composite scheme pairing hash on account identifier with monthly range sub-partitioning achieves within 8% of the best OLAP time while keeping OLTP tail latency within 11% of the hash-only baseline. The paper provides a decision guide based on the OLTP/OLAP ratio and estimated hotspot fraction.

title: Primjena WF-mreža za formalno modelovanje administrativnih procedura u lokalnoj samoupravi
abstract: Rad istražuje mogućnosti primjene WF-mreža (workflow Petri mreža) za formalizaciju administrativnih procedura u jedinicama lokalne samouprave u Srbiji. Analizirane su tri tipične procedure: izdavanje građevinskih dozvola, upis u matičnu knjigu i obnova vozačke dozvole. Za svaku proceduru izgrađen je WF-net model koristeći alat PIPE2, a modeli su verifikovani na osobine ispravnosti: ograničenost, živost i ostvarivost. Rezultati pokazuju da sve tri procedure sadrže strukturalne greške – u dva slučaja detektovani su mrtvi prelazi koji odgovaraju neiskorišćenim procesnim koracima, a u jednom slučaju pronađena je potencijalna blokada. Formalizacija je obavljena na osnovu pisane dokumentacije i intervjua sa referentima. Rad diskutuje i ograničenja pristupa kada su procedure djelimično neformalizovane ili podložne diskrecionom odlučivanju referenata.

title: Mapping SpGEMM onto a Reconfigurable Dataflow Fabric with a Compiled Routing Layer
abstract: Sparse general matrix–matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) exhibits highly irregular data movement that challenges static compilation. This paper describes a compilation approach in which an intermediate dataflow graph for SpGEMM is partitioned into segments whose routing requirements can be resolved statically, while a thin runtime layer handles dynamic segment transitions. The target is a reconfigurable FPGA-based dataflow fabric with 64 processing elements and a configurable interconnect. Compilation proceeds in three phases: symbolic sparsity analysis, segment extraction and scheduling, and routing table generation. Evaluated on six matrix pairs from scientific simulation and machine-learning workloads, the compiled fabric achieves 1.4–2.1× higher throughput than a reference CPU implementation running eight threads and 1.1–1.6× over a hand-tuned GPU kernel. The paper reports configuration compilation time, routing table size, and sensitivity to input matrix density.

title: Observed pedestrian crossing behaviour at an uncontrolled mid-block location on a two-lane arterial in Novi Sad
abstract: This paper reports field observations of pedestrian crossing behaviour at a single uncontrolled mid-block crossing on Futoška Street in Novi Sad collected over five weekday periods in autumn 2013. A fixed-angle video camera recorded 1,840 crossing events. Gap acceptance was the primary behavioural measure: pedestrians accepted gaps as short as 2.1 s under low-flow conditions, with median accepted gap of 5.8 s. Age and group size were coded manually for a 600-event subsample. Older pedestrians (estimated over 60) accepted significantly shorter gaps than middle-aged pedestrians, a finding counter to typical assumptions in the regional literature. The paper discusses limitations of manual observation and motivates the use of automated tracking in follow-up work. No surrogate safety measures were computed in this study; the focus is descriptive.

title: Extraction of vehicle and pedestrian trajectories from fixed overhead video using background subtraction: accuracy evaluation on a controlled test track
abstract: Reliable trajectory data are a prerequisite for computing surrogate safety measures from video. This study evaluates three background-subtraction algorithms—Gaussian mixture model, ViBe, and a frame-differencing baseline—applied to overhead footage recorded at a controlled test track in Novi Sad. Forty-two staged pedestrian-vehicle interaction runs were performed at known positions and speeds, providing ground truth via differential GPS. Mean positional error for the Gaussian mixture approach was 0.31 m at 25 fps with moderate occlusion. ViBe achieved 0.27 m but showed more false positives under shadow conditions common in afternoon recordings. The paper quantifies how trajectory error propagates into post-encroachment time estimates, showing that a 0.3 m position error at typical urban speeds introduces a PET estimation error of approximately 0.15 s. Recommendations for camera height, frame rate, and calibration procedure are provided for practitioners planning roadside video studies.

title: Post-encroachment time distributions at mid-block pedestrian crossings: a comparison of three sites with different speed environments
abstract: Post-encroachment time (PET) is widely used as a proxy for collision risk at pedestrian crossings, yet its distributional properties across varying speed contexts are rarely compared systematically. This study collected video data at three unsignalised mid-block crossings in Novi Sad with 85th-percentile vehicle speeds of 38, 52, and 64 km/h respectively. Automated trajectory extraction yielded 2,314 usable pedestrian-vehicle interaction pairs across approximately 120 hours of footage. PET distributions were right-skewed at all sites; the proportion of interactions with PET below 1.5 s—a common critical threshold—was 3.1%, 7.8%, and 14.6% at the three sites. Weibull and log-normal fits are compared; the log-normal provided marginally better fit by AIC at all sites. The relationship between operating speed and conflict frequency is approximately linear over this range. Implications for speed limit policy at uncontrolled crossings are discussed.

title: Effect of a median refuge island on pedestrian-vehicle PET at a mid-block crossing: before-after study in Novi Sad
abstract: Median refuge islands are a common low-cost intervention at mid-block crossings, but empirical before-after evidence on their effect on surrogate safety measures in Central and Eastern European contexts is limited. This paper presents a before-after study at a single mid-block crossing on Bulevar Evrope in Novi Sad where a raised median island was installed in spring 2020. Video data were collected over four weeks before installation and four weeks after, yielding 1,180 before and 1,410 after pedestrian crossing events. The proportion of interactions with PET below 1.5 s decreased from 9.3% to 4.1% after installation. Mean vehicle yielding rate increased from 28% to 61%. Crossing time increased by 1.4 s on average, consistent with the two-stage crossing requirement. The analysis controls for seasonal differences in pedestrian volume using an adjacent reference site. Confidence intervals are reported throughout; effect sizes are moderate but statistically reliable.

title: Surrogate safety measures in pedestrian research: a structured review of threshold values and calibration approaches
abstract: The literature on surrogate safety measures for pedestrian crossings lacks consensus on critical threshold values for post-encroachment time, time-to-collision, and gap time. This chapter reviews 47 empirical studies published between 2001 and 2021, summarising the range of threshold values used, the calibration methods applied, and the contexts (country, crossing type, speed environment) in which they were developed. PET critical thresholds in reviewed studies range from 0.8 s to 2.5 s; only nine studies provide any calibration against observed crash frequencies. The chapter discusses the consequences of threshold choice for conflict rate estimates and argues for context-specific calibration wherever crash data permit. A simple sensitivity analysis shows that switching from a 1.5 s to a 2.0 s threshold can increase estimated conflict rates by 40–120% depending on site characteristics. The chapter also identifies geographic gaps in the literature, noting the scarcity of studies from Southeast Europe.

title: Automated conflict detection at urban mid-block crossings using a YOLO-based detector and a rule-based PET estimator: field validation in Novi Sad
abstract: Manual annotation of video footage for conflict extraction is time-consuming and limits sample sizes in safety studies. This paper describes and validates an automated pipeline combining a fine-tuned YOLO object detector with a rule-based module for computing post-encroachment time from detected bounding-box centroids. The detector was fine-tuned on 4,200 manually annotated frames from five Novi Sad crossing sites covering varied lighting and seasonal conditions. Validation against manual annotation on a held-out dataset of 1,600 frames gave pedestrian detection F1 of 0.91 and vehicle detection F1 of 0.96. PET estimates from the automated pipeline agreed with manually measured PET to within 0.2 s in 84% of cases on the test set. The system was then applied to 210 hours of continuous footage across three crossings, producing a conflict dataset approximately eight times larger than would be feasible by manual methods in the same analysis time. Known limitations—partial occlusion, night-time performance—are documented.

title: Seasonal and time-of-day variation in cyclist-vehicle conflict rates at mid-block crossings: evidence from 14 months of continuous video monitoring
abstract: Conflict rates at pedestrian and cyclist crossings are typically estimated from short observation campaigns, raising questions about temporal representativeness. This paper reports conflict rates derived from 14 consecutive months of video monitoring at two mid-block crossings in Novi Sad equipped with permanent cameras installed as part of a municipal traffic management project. Automated trajectory extraction produced 6,840 cyclist crossing events and 18,200 pedestrian crossing events. Cyclist-vehicle conflict rates (PET below 1.0 s) were highest in April–May and September, coinciding with peak cycling volumes, and showed a clear morning peak between 07:30 and 09:00. Pedestrian conflict rates peaked in the 16:00–18:00 interval and were more uniformly distributed across seasons. Multivariate regression shows that cyclist conflict rate is more strongly associated with motor vehicle flow than with cyclist volume, while for pedestrians the relationship is approximately symmetric. Findings suggest that short observation campaigns conducted outside peak periods may underestimate annual conflict exposure by 30–50%.

title: Dwell Time and Stop Capacity Under Off-Schedule Bus Arrivals: Implications for BRT Performance Guarantees
abstract: This preprint investigates how off-schedule arrivals—buses arriving earlier or later than their timetabled slot—affect stop-level dwell time and capacity at BRT stations. Using a dataset of 5,490 arrivals from two BRT-standard corridors collected in 2024–2025, stop events are classified by deviation category: early (>2 min), on-time (±2 min), and late (>2 min). Dwell time is on average 23% longer for early buses and 17% longer for late buses compared to on-time arrivals, primarily because early arrivals encounter passenger groups that have accumulated beyond the normal inter-departure interval, while late arrivals encounter higher door occupancy. A capacity derating function is fitted to the data and shown to reduce predicted stop throughput by 8–31% across observed deviation magnitudes. The paper is under review at the European Journal of Traffic and Transportation Engineering.

title: Tactile Paving Coverage and Condition in Pedestrian Zones of Novi Sad: A Systematic Field Survey
abstract: This study presents a systematic field survey of tactile ground surface indicators (TGSIs) across 14 designated pedestrian zones in Novi Sad, conducted in 2009–2010. A total of 38.4 km of pedestrian routes were assessed using a structured observation protocol adapted from European standard EN 1436 and the then-current Serbian rulebook on accessibility. Each TGSI segment was classified by surface type, colour contrast ratio (measured with a Konica Minolta CM-600d spectrophotometer), physical condition, and continuity of guidance path. Of 1,247 discrete TGSI installations recorded, 61% showed one or more compliance failures, most commonly interrupted guidance strips at intersections and faded colour contrast below the 0.3 LRV differential threshold. The paper discusses the discrepancy between installation rates and functional usability, and proposes a simple four-category compliance scoring rubric for municipal audit use. Findings were communicated to the City Urban Planning Institute of Novi Sad.

title: Wayfinding Route Legibility for Blind Pedestrians at Bus Terminals: Case Studies from Three Serbian Cities
abstract: Using structured mobility trials with 24 participants who are fully blind or have severe visual impairment, this study evaluates wayfinding legibility at bus terminal entrances in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin. Participants completed standardised navigation tasks while a researcher recorded errors, hesitations, and verbal commentary. Task completion rates ranged from 29% in Zrenjanin to 54% in Novi Sad. Qualitative analysis of verbal data identified three principal failure modes: absent tactile transition strips at kerb cuts, inconsistent surface texture between concourse and platform areas, and no auditory confirmation at fare barriers. The paper maps physical deficiencies to specific clauses of the Serbian Rulebook on Conditions for Planning and Design of Objects with Respect to the Needs of Persons with Disabilities (2015) and calculates a non-compliance rate per terminal zone. Recommendations are given for phased remediation that municipalities could implement without full reconstruction.

title: Regulatory Gap Analysis: Serbian Accessibility Standards for Public Spaces Compared with European Framework Standards
abstract: This paper performs a clause-by-clause comparison of the Serbian technical rulebooks governing accessibility of public spaces (2015 edition) against three European reference documents: BS 8300:2009+A1:2010 (UK), DIN 18040-3:2014 (Germany), and the European Concept for Accessibility (ECA) Technical Assistance Manual. The comparison covers 11 thematic domains including tactile guidance paths, kerb design, pedestrian signal equipment, and rest point provision. Of 94 specific measurable requirements identified in the European documents, 41 have a direct Serbian counterpart, 28 have a partial counterpart with weaker numeric thresholds, and 25 have no equivalent. The paper does not argue for uncritical adoption of foreign standards but identifies the domains where Serbian guidance is most likely to produce non-accessible outcomes in practice, and proposes a prioritised update schedule for the responsible ministry. The analysis draws on the author's field data from earlier surveys to illustrate practical consequences of specific gaps.

title: Audio Beacons and Tactile Maps at Tram Stops: A Comparative Usability Study in Two Central European Cities
abstract: Low-cost iBeacon-based audio navigation systems and raised tactile maps were installed experimentally at four tram stops in Novi Sad and four in Debrecen, Hungary, during a six-month pilot. Forty participants with visual impairment (20 per city) completed standardised boarding tasks under three conditions: audio beacon only, tactile map only, and both combined. Task completion times and error counts were recorded; participants also completed a short usability questionnaire. Combined provision reduced mean task time by 34% relative to audio beacon alone in Novi Sad and 28% in Debrecen; the difference between cities is attributed to differences in platform geometry. Tactile maps alone performed best for users with residual vision. The paper reports on installation cost per stop (€340–€610 range) and discusses maintenance obligations that municipalities would need to commit to for sustained benefit. Usability questionnaire data are provided as supplementary material.

title: Mapping Accessible Pedestrian Infrastructure Through Participatory Surveys with Users with Visual Impairment: Methodology and Pilot Results
abstract: Conventional accessibility audits are conducted by sighted professionals using checklists; this paper tests a participatory methodology in which trained volunteers with visual impairment collect data directly using a structured verbal reporting protocol paired with GPS tracking. Twelve volunteer surveyors mapped 22 km of routes in central Novi Sad over four weeks in autumn 2017. Their reports were compared against professional audits of the same routes conducted independently. Agreement on the presence of specific defects (missing TGSI, damaged kerb cut, obstructed path) was 74%, with the participatory method identifying 18% more obstruction events than the professional audit, most of them temporary (A-frames, parked scooters). The paper describes data collection forms, training materials, and a simple GIS workflow for aggregating results. It argues that participatory surveys can usefully complement but not replace professional audits, and discusses observer fatigue and consistency limitations.

title: Inclusive Design Provisions in Serbian Municipal Master Plans: Content Analysis of 12 Plans Adopted Between 2010 and 2018
abstract: Municipal master plans (generalni urbanistički planovi) in Serbia are legally required to address accessibility, but no systematic review of how they actually do so has been published. This paper presents a content analysis of 12 plans adopted across Vojvodina municipalities between 2010 and 2018, coding each plan for the presence, specificity, and measurability of accessibility-related provisions. Plans were coded against a 47-item framework derived from the Serbian accessibility rulebook and the authors' earlier regulatory gap analysis. On average, plans addressed 11 of 47 items; provisions were predominantly general statements rather than measurable requirements. Only 2 of 12 plans included a dedicated accessibility implementation schedule. The paper identifies the planning stages at which accessibility provisions are most commonly dropped or generalised and proposes model plan language for three high-priority domains that municipalities could adopt without legislative change.

title: Post-Occupancy Evaluation of a Newly Refurbished Accessible Pedestrian Zone in Subotica: User Satisfaction and Remaining Deficiencies
abstract: A major refurbishment of the central pedestrian zone in Subotica, completed in 2019, incorporated tactile guidance paths and kerb modifications intended to comply with the Serbian accessibility rulebook. This paper reports a post-occupancy evaluation conducted 18 months after completion. Methods included a structured questionnaire administered to 68 respondents with visual impairment or other mobility impairments recruited through two disability organisations, direct measurement of 312 TGSI segments, and photographic documentation. Questionnaire results indicate moderate satisfaction with tactile guidance continuity (mean 3.1/5) but low satisfaction with kerb cut positioning at three key intersections (mean 1.9/5). Physical measurements found 19% of TGSI segments already showing surface height loss exceeding 2 mm, attributed to mechanical cleaning equipment used by the municipal street-cleaning service. The paper discusses the gap between design intent and post-construction reality and the role of maintenance regimes in sustaining accessibility outcomes.

title: Colour Contrast Standards for Tactile Paving: How Different Measurement Methods Produce Different Compliance Verdicts
abstract: European and domestic guidance documents specify minimum luminance reflectance value (LRV) differentials between tactile paving and surrounding surfaces, but they do not uniformly specify measurement method, instrument geometry, or illuminant. This paper measures LRV differentials on 80 in-situ TGSI installations in Novi Sad using three methods: a handheld spectrophotometer (45/0 geometry), a glossmeter-corrected reflectance protocol, and visual assessment by four trained assessors. For the same installations, compliance rates under a 0.3 LRV differential threshold vary from 44% (spectrophotometer) to 61% (visual assessment). The paper analyses sources of divergence, including specular reflection from wet surfaces and directional effects of textured profiles, and recommends a standardised field measurement protocol suitable for Serbian municipal audits. Data tables and measurement protocol description are provided as supplementary material.

title: Standardisation of Municipal Accessibility Audit Procedures in Serbia: Towards a Common Protocol for Tactile and Wayfinding Infrastructure
abstract: Serbian municipalities conducting accessibility audits of public spaces currently apply heterogeneous procedures, making comparison across cities and over time unreliable. This paper describes the development and piloting of a common audit protocol for tactile and wayfinding infrastructure, produced through a three-round Delphi process with 19 experts including municipal architects, disability organisation representatives, and academics from five Serbian institutions. The protocol covers 58 measurable items across six infrastructure categories. A pilot application was conducted in two neighbourhoods in Novi Sad and one in Zrenjanin by three independent audit teams; intra-protocol inter-team agreement averaged κ = 0.77. The paper presents the finalised protocol, discusses items where expert consensus was weakest, and describes a short web-based data entry tool developed to support its use. The protocol is offered as an open resource for municipal use and has been shared with the Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure.

title: Flood-Risk Zoning as a Design Generator: Lessons from Three Danubian Riverfront Regeneration Plans
abstract: Flood-risk zoning is commonly treated in urban planning practice as a constraint that removes land from productive use. This paper examines three regeneration masterplans—for sites in Novi Sad, Smederevo, and Galați (Romania)—prepared between 1996 and 2003, and analyses how each plan handled the tension between flood-plain regulation and the commercial pressure to develop waterfront land. Document analysis of planning dossiers, zoning ordinances, and design competition briefs was combined with structured interviews with eleven planners and municipal officials involved in the three cases. The Novi Sad case demonstrated that integrating a 100-year flood envelope as a primary design parameter—rather than applying it as a post-hoc overlay—resulted in higher proportions of publicly accessible open space and reduced long-term infrastructure maintenance costs. The Galați case showed the opposite pattern, with repeated revision of flood limits under developer pressure producing stranded public investment. The paper proposes a procedural checklist for incorporating hydrological constraints early in brief-writing for waterfront competitions.

title: Integrating EU Water Framework Directive Requirements into Local Brownfield Remediation Plans: A Practitioner's Guide for Serbian Municipalities
abstract: Following Serbia's signing of the Stabilisation and Association Agreement in 2008, Serbian municipalities faced increasing pressure to align local environmental planning with EU Water Framework Directive (WFD) requirements, despite the absence of a direct transposition obligation. This guide, produced under a bilateral research exchange, examines how WFD river-basin management objectives—particularly those relating to ecological status of riparian zones, diffuse pollution reduction, and morphological restoration of riverbanks—can be operationalised within the Serbian planning and permitting system as it stood in 2011. The guide provides worked examples from four Vojvodina municipalities that had undertaken or were planning brownfield remediation on riverfront sites. Each example traces the decision pathway from site assessment through zoning amendment to construction permit, identifying the points at which WFD-aligned conditions can be inserted without requiring legislative change. A checklist and a set of model planning conditions are included as appendices. The guide was distributed to 24 municipal planning offices through the Urban Planning Institute of Vojvodina.

title: Effect of Non-Uniform Pollution Layers on Surface Field Enhancement of Medium-Voltage Silicone Rubber Insulators
abstract: Non-uniform deposition of pollution on insulator sheds creates local conductivity gradients that significantly alter the tangential electric field distribution. In this study, three pollution distribution patterns — uniform, band-type, and tip-concentrated — were implemented in a 2D axisymmetric FEM model of a 20 kV insulator string. Conductivity values between 0.05 and 1.2 S/m were assigned to thin pollution films of 0.1 mm thickness, derived from equivalent salt deposit density measurements on field-aged samples collected from a 35 kV overhead line in the Vojvodina region. Simulations were run at power frequency (50 Hz). Band-type pollution at the shed tips produced tangential field peaks up to 2.3 times higher than the uniform case. The results correlate with leakage current measurements performed under identical pollution configurations in the laboratory salt-fog chamber, with agreement within 8%.

title: Boundary Element Analysis of Electric Field Redistribution Caused by Hydrophobicity Loss in Composite Insulator Sheds
abstract: Silicone rubber insulators progressively lose surface hydrophobicity when exposed to prolonged electrical and environmental stress, resulting in the formation of continuous water films rather than discrete droplets. This paper uses a boundary element method formulation to compute the electric field for four hydrophobicity classes (HC1 through HC4 according to the STRI guide) modelled as thin conductive layers with increasing surface conductance. Geometries correspond to a 24 kV dead-end insulator. The BEM approach allowed a direct comparison with previously published FEM results for the same geometry with a 4% discrepancy in peak field values, validating both methods. The transition from HC2 to HC3 produced the most pronounced increase in field non-uniformity, with shed-edge tangential fields rising from 0.55 kV/mm to 0.91 kV/mm. Implications for maintenance scheduling based on periodic hydrophobicity classification are discussed.

title: Influence of Rain Intensity on Electric Field Distribution Along 20 kV Composite Insulators: A Parametric Numerical Study
abstract: Rainfall on insulator surfaces introduces a dynamic, non-uniform water film whose thickness and conductivity depend on rain intensity, shed geometry, and inclination angle. A parametric FEM study was conducted covering rain intensities from 1 mm/h to 25 mm/h, translated into equivalent water film conductivities between 0.08 and 0.45 S/m based on empirical relationships from the literature. Three inclination angles (0°, 30°, and 45° from vertical) were modelled for a standard 20 kV pin-type composite insulator. Results show that rain intensity has a moderate effect on field distribution compared with contamination, with maximum tangential field increases of 35% under the heaviest rain scenario. However, the combination of pre-existing dry-band contamination and heavy rain produced synergistic field enhancement up to 2.8 kV/mm at the lower shed edges, approaching partial discharge inception thresholds estimated from published streamer criteria.

title: Numerical Computation of Electric Field in the Vicinity of Metal End Fittings of Composite Insulators
abstract: Metal end fittings at the cap and pin of composite insulators are known to concentrate the electric field locally, yet most published models simplify or omit their geometry. This paper presents a three-dimensional FEM model that explicitly represents the forged steel end fitting geometry of a 20 kV suspension insulator, digitised using coordinate-measuring machine data. Both dry and uniformly polluted surface conditions were examined. In the 3D model, field maxima at the fitting–rubber interface reached 1.15 kV/mm under dry energisation at rated voltage, compared with 0.78 kV/mm in a 2D axisymmetric approximation — a difference of 47%. The study demonstrates that 2D models systematically underestimate field concentrations at fittings and recommends minimum mesh refinement criteria (element size ≤ 0.3 mm at the triple junction) for reliable 3D computation.

title: Correlation Between Computed Electric Field Peaks and Leakage Current Harmonics on Polluted Composite Insulators
abstract: Leakage current waveform distortion under pollution is widely used as a diagnostic indicator, but its relationship to computed electric field distribution is not well established. This study correlates results from a validated 2D FEM model with simultaneous leakage current measurements on six 20 kV composite insulator samples subjected to controlled saline fog pollution in a climate chamber. Pollution layers with ESDD values of 0.025, 0.05, and 0.1 mg/cm² were tested at 50 Hz. Third-harmonic leakage current content increased from 3% to 18% as ESDD rose, while simulated peak tangential fields grew from 0.6 to 1.4 kV/mm at the shed edges. A linear regression between third-harmonic amplitude and simulated field peak yielded R² = 0.91, suggesting that field computation could support interpretation of online leakage current monitoring data.

title: Comparative Numerical Study of Shed Profile Modifications for Reducing Electric Field Peaks on Medium-Voltage Composite Insulators
abstract: Several shed profile variants — standard alternate-shed, deep-rib, and aerodynamic-taper designs — were evaluated numerically to identify geometric features that reduce electric field peaks under contaminated conditions. A parametric 2D FEM model was constructed for each profile with identical overall leakage distance of 560 mm and the same pollution conductivity of 0.1 S/m. Peak tangential field values, integrated field non-uniformity indices, and dry-band formation risk scores derived from field gradients were computed for 21 geometric configurations obtained by varying shed pitch, shed diameter ratio, and rib depth. The aerodynamic-taper profile with a shed diameter ratio of 1.35 and a pitch of 38 mm produced the lowest field peak (0.72 kV/mm) and the most uniform field distribution. Results are presented as response surfaces to guide future insulator design within standard dimensional constraints.

title: Electric Field Distribution on Composite Insulators with Localised Shed Damage: A Finite Element Investigation
abstract: Mechanical damage to silicone rubber sheds — cuts, punctures, and erosion craters — alters local geometry and can expose the fibreglass core, changing the dielectric properties in the damaged zone. This paper models three representative damage scenarios observed in field inspections of 20 kV distribution lines: a 5 mm cut on the shed underside, a 3 mm puncture reaching the core, and a 10 mm erosion patch on the shed tip. FEM simulations at rated voltage and with 0.05 mg/cm² ESDD contamination show that core exposure increases the local electric field at the defect boundary by a factor of 1.8 to 3.1 compared with the intact insulator, depending on damage type and location. The puncture scenario produced the most severe field distortion, with peaks of 2.1 kV/mm at the core–rubber interface, which exceeds the estimated partial discharge inception field for silicone rubber at 50 Hz.

title: Modelling Electric Field Distribution for Composite Insulators in Mixed Industrial and Agricultural Pollution Environments
abstract: Vojvodina presents a specific pollution challenge where overhead distribution lines pass through agricultural zones adjacent to food processing facilities, resulting in mixed organic and ionic contamination with poorly defined conductivity. Field samples from eleven 20 kV line sections were collected and characterised for surface conductivity, ESDD, and non-soluble deposit density. The measured conductivity range (0.03–0.65 S/m) was wider than typically reported for purely maritime or industrial pollution. A stochastic FEM approach was applied in which surface conductivity was treated as a spatially correlated random field with statistics derived from the measurements; 500 Monte Carlo realisations were computed. The 95th-percentile peak tangential field under this pollution regime was 1.62 kV/mm, compared with 1.21 kV/mm for uniform ESDD at the mean measured value. The study provides probabilistic field exceedance curves applicable to insulator selection in mixed-pollution corridors.

title: Assessment of Grading Ring Geometry on Electric Field Relief at the High-Voltage End of 35 kV Composite Insulators
abstract: Grading rings are installed at the energised end of suspension insulators to limit field concentration, but their sizing is largely based on empirical rules. This paper presents a systematic 3D FEM study of grading ring diameter (80–160 mm) and tube diameter (12–22 mm) for a 35 kV composite suspension insulator under dry and polluted conditions. A total of 48 ring configurations were simulated at rated phase-to-ground voltage. The ring shifted the field maximum away from the end fitting in all configurations; however, under pollution, an optimally designed ring (ring diameter 130 mm, tube 18 mm) reduced the field peak at the shed–fitting junction from 1.38 kV/mm to 0.64 kV/mm. Suboptimal ring sizing increased field concentration at the ring surface itself, with implications for corona onset. Recommended sizing curves as a function of insulator leakage distance are provided.

title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Prediction of Electric Field Peaks on Contaminated Composite Insulators from Geometric and Pollution Parameters
abstract: Running a full FEM simulation for each combination of insulator geometry and pollution condition is computationally expensive for grid-scale insulator fleet assessments. This paper investigates whether a gradient-boosted regression model trained on an FEM-generated dataset can accurately predict peak tangential electric field values. The training dataset comprised 2 400 2D FEM simulations varying six parameters: shed diameter ratio, pitch, shed count, pollution conductivity, film thickness, and power frequency voltage. An 80/20 train–test split was used; hyperparameters were tuned by fivefold cross-validation. The trained model predicted peak field values with a mean absolute error of 0.031 kV/mm and R² = 0.97 on the held-out test set, with inference times under 2 ms. The approach was validated against an independent set of 60 FEM cases not used in training, confirming generalisability within the parameter ranges studied. Limitations at extrapolation boundaries are discussed.

title: Error-Resilient H.265/HEVC Encoding for Low-Latency Industrial Video Monitoring Over IEEE 802.11n Links
abstract: Industrial process monitoring requires continuous video streams over Wi-Fi links that are subject to co-channel interference, resulting in periodic packet loss events lasting 50–300 ms. H.265/HEVC offers superior compression efficiency but introduces complex inter-frame dependencies that amplify error propagation. This paper characterises the error-propagation patterns of HEVC reference software HM 15.0 under periodic loss events representative of factory-floor IEEE 802.11n environments and evaluates three encoder-side mitigation strategies: adaptive intra-refresh insertion, slice-segment partitioning, and constrained motion-vector range limiting. A test set of eight 1080p industrial scene sequences was encoded at 1–4 Mbit/s. The combination of periodic intra-refresh at 30-frame intervals and four-slice partitioning reduced mean recovery time from 2.8 s to 0.4 s with a bitrate overhead of 9%. Slice-based partitioning alone was found insufficient without intra-refresh when loss bursts exceeded 120 ms. The results inform encoder configuration guidelines for industrial deployment.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Broadcasting – Regional Workshop Supplement (Invited Paper)

title: Interaction between grid-following inverter current control bandwidth and conducted emission levels: a parametric study
abstract: The relationship between the current control loop bandwidth of grid-following single-phase inverters and their conducted emission characteristics in the 150 kHz to 2 MHz range is examined through a parametric simulation study validated by laboratory measurements. A full-cycle time-domain inverter model is implemented in PLECS and exercised across current controller bandwidths from 500 Hz to 8 kHz, LCL filter corner frequencies from 4 kHz to 20 kHz, and DC bus voltages of 200 V, 350 V and 600 V. Conducted emission spectra at the AC terminals are extracted via an embedded LISN model and compared with CISPR 11 Class B limits. Increasing controller bandwidth from 1 kHz to 5 kHz reduces low-frequency distortion but increases emissions in the 200 kHz to 600 kHz band by 3 to 11 dB depending on LCL corner frequency. A low-pass post-filter of 47 µH/10 nF placed after the LCL filter reduces peak emission levels by 8 dB with less than 0.3% increase in fundamental voltage drop. Laboratory validation on a 2 kW prototype confirms simulation trends with deviations below 4 dB across 90% of the measured frequency range.

title: A Pre-Compliance Workflow for Mixed-Signal PCBs Integrating Near-Field Scanning, FDTD Simulation, and Layout Rule Checking
abstract: This paper describes an integrated pre-compliance workflow for mixed-signal PCB development that combines three techniques used sequentially across the design cycle. In the early layout phase, an automated rule-checking tool flags geometric violations associated with known emission risks. At the prototype stage, near-field scanning at 3 mm standoff generates spatial emission maps that identify dominant radiating structures. Finally, FDTD simulation using geometry extracted from the identified hotspots provides frequency-resolved quantification and supports what-if analysis of corrective measures. The workflow was applied to four prototype boards developed in collaboration with two regional electronics companies. Across all four boards, the integrated workflow identified the dominant emission source correctly in each case; corrective measures applied on the basis of simulation results reduced the peak radiated emission at the pre-compliance test receiver by between 5.2 dB and 11.7 dB before formal OATS measurement. Time-to-compliance for the four designs averaged 2.1 fewer test-and-rework cycles compared to a historical baseline of designs developed without structured pre-compliance analysis. The workflow documentation and rule-checker code are deposited in an open repository.

title: Temperature dependence of threshold voltage instability in enhancement-mode GaN HEMTs under positive gate bias stress
abstract: Threshold voltage instability under positive gate bias stress is a reliability concern for enhancement-mode GaN HEMTs. This paper reports constant-voltage stress experiments at Vgs values of +5 V, +6 V, and +7 V for stress durations up to 10 000 s at three ambient temperatures (25 °C, 75 °C, and 125 °C). Threshold voltage shift ΔVth was extracted by the drain current method at Ids = 1 mA after each stress interval. At +7 V / 125 °C after 10 000 s, ΔVth reached −420 mV, while at +5 V / 25 °C it remained below −30 mV. A stretched-exponential relaxation model fitted the recovery transients with R² > 0.98 in all cases. The activation energy extracted from Arrhenius fitting was 0.38 eV, consistent with electron trapping in Al-GaN surface states. A derating curve for maximum gate drive voltage as a function of operating temperature is provided for gate-driver designers.

title: Bayesian Compressed Sensing with Laplace Priors for Multiband Cognitive Radio Spectrum Recovery
abstract: This chapter reviews and extends Bayesian formulations of compressed sensing as applied to multiband spectrum recovery in cognitive radio. A hierarchical Bayesian model is constructed in which each frequency bin's power level is assigned a Laplace prior, enforcing sparsity without requiring explicit knowledge of the sparsity level. Posterior inference is performed via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling using a Gibbs sampler with 5000 burn-in and 10000 retained samples. The approach is compared against LASSO, OMP, and iterative reweighted least squares (IRLS) on synthetic multiband signals with 1 to 8 simultaneously active bands, each 5 MHz wide, within a 200 MHz observation window. The Bayesian method outperforms LASSO by 2.1 dB in NMSE at SNR = 5 dB and provides calibrated posterior uncertainty intervals, which are relevant for secondary user access decisions. Computational cost remains the primary limitation for real-time deployment; strategies for approximate inference are outlined.

title: Position-Sensorless Current Profiling for Switched Reluctance Motors Using Flux-Linkage Estimation from Phase Voltage and Current Measurements
abstract: Position sensors add cost, mechanical fragility, and wiring complexity to switched reluctance motor drives. This paper describes a sensorless rotor-position estimator that integrates the phase voltage–drop equation to obtain flux linkage in real time, then uses the calibrated flux-linkage look-up table to infer position. The method requires no additional hardware beyond the current transducers already present in the asymmetric bridge converter. The estimator is combined with a cubic torque-sharing function controller and tested on the 7.5 kW 8/6 SRM bench at 600–1800 rpm under step load changes from 20 Nm to 50 Nm. Position estimation error stayed below ±1.2 electrical degrees in steady state and ±3.1 degrees during load transients. Torque-ripple coefficient under sensorless operation was 21–26%, compared with 18–22% with a physical resolver, representing an acceptable degradation for most industrial fan and pump applications. Sensitivity to winding resistance variation with temperature is analysed and a simple online resistance correction scheme is proposed.

title: A three-branch ladder model for leakage and redistribution phenomena in supercapacitors
abstract: A three-branch RC ladder model extended with fractional-order capacitors is proposed to account simultaneously for fast charge storage, slow pore diffusion, and long-term leakage in electrochemical double-layer capacitors. Model parameters were determined from impedance spectra and from constant-current charge–discharge experiments performed on eight cells (1 F to 50 F) over 200 cycle sequences. The fractional exponents in the first and second branches differed by up to 0.12, indicating distinct pore populations. Voltage redistribution curves measured after current interruption were reproduced by the model with a root-mean-square error below 3 mV across all cells. The leakage conductance extracted from very low frequency measurements (down to 0.5 mHz) agreed with 72-hour self-discharge data to within 15%. The model is intended for use in energy management algorithms that must account for charge redistribution losses.

title: Applying Local Differential Privacy to Aggregate Sales Reporting in a Food-Processing SME Cluster: A Simulation Study
abstract: This paper examines how local differential privacy (LDP) can be applied to aggregate sales figures shared among fifteen food-processing firms participating in a regional cluster in Vojvodina. The study uses synthetic transaction data calibrated against publicly available industry statistics from the Serbian Business Registers Agency for the period 2018–2021. Three LDP mechanisms are compared: randomised response, the Laplace mechanism, and the Piecewise mechanism. Privacy budgets ranging from ε = 0.5 to ε = 4.0 are tested against utility loss measured by mean absolute percentage error on cluster-level demand forecasts. At ε = 1.0, the Piecewise mechanism achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 6.8 percent on monthly demand aggregates, compared to 11.4 percent for randomised response at the same budget. The simulation covers 10,000 Monte Carlo runs per configuration. Results suggest that LDP is practically viable for cluster-level reporting tasks where individual firm figures need not be disclosed, but that tighter privacy budgets substantially degrade forecast accuracy for smaller sub-clusters of fewer than five firms. The paper concludes with a discussion of governance conditions under which cluster coordinators could administer the noise-injection step.

title: A Federated Logistic Regression Protocol for Churn Prediction Without Raw Data Centralisation: Evidence from Serbian Retail SMEs
abstract: Federated learning is increasingly proposed as a way for competing firms to build shared predictive models without pooling customer records. This paper implements a federated logistic regression protocol and evaluates it on a dataset assembled from four Serbian retail SMEs, comprising approximately 38,000 anonymised customer records collected between 2020 and 2022. The firms operate in adjacent market segments and agreed to participate under a data-sharing agreement reviewed by the Serbian Personal Data Protection Commissioner. The protocol uses secure aggregation via additive secret sharing so that the central aggregator sees only the sum of model updates. Experiments compare the federated model against a centralised baseline and three locally trained models. The federated model reaches an AUC of 0.79 on the held-out test set, within 0.04 points of the centralised baseline. Communication overhead is measured across five aggregation rounds, averaging 2.3 MB per round per participant. The paper also documents practical obstacles encountered during deployment, including heterogeneous data schemas and unequal class distributions across participants.

title: Data Governance Frameworks for Cross-Firm Analytics in Industry Clusters: A Comparative Review of Practice in the Western Balkans and Visegrád Countries
abstract: This chapter surveys data governance arrangements adopted by twelve industry cluster organisations in Serbia, North Macedonia, Hungary, and the Czech Republic that have attempted to implement shared analytics infrastructure. Information was gathered through semi-structured interviews with cluster managers and IT coordinators conducted between September 2022 and March 2023. The chapter categorises governance models along two dimensions: the locus of data custody (centralised coordinator, distributed nodes, or third-party trustee) and the technical mechanism used to protect firm-level confidentiality (pseudonymisation, aggregation rules, or cryptographic protocols). Findings indicate that most clusters rely on contractual pseudonymisation with no technical enforcement, and that only two of the twelve cases use any form of cryptographic privacy protection. Barriers cited most frequently are the cost of implementation, absence of standardised data schemas within clusters, and distrust among competing firms. The chapter draws implications for technology transfer programmes targeting SME clusters and identifies conditions under which more technically rigorous approaches are likely to be adopted.

title: Measuring Utility–Privacy Trade-offs in Federated Cluster Analytics Under Heterogeneous Participation: A Toy Economy Approach
abstract: Federated analytics protocols for industry clusters face a participation heterogeneity problem: firms differ in size, data volume, and willingness to contribute noise to shared computations. This preprint introduces a toy economy model in which firms are represented as utility-maximising agents that choose a privacy budget ε from a discrete set before each aggregation round. The model is parameterised using stylised facts about SME size distributions from Eurostat data for Serbia and Hungary. Simulation experiments with 8, 16, and 32 synthetic firms show that without incentive alignment, stable participation collapses to a subset of larger firms within four to six rounds, causing the aggregate model quality to degrade by between 15 and 30 percent relative to full participation. Two incentive mechanisms are compared: a contribution-weighted revenue-sharing rule and a reputation scoring system. The revenue-sharing rule sustains broader participation in 71 percent of simulation runs at 32 firms, whereas reputation scoring achieves 58 percent. Limitations include the simplified action space and the absence of real firm data. The authors intend to ground the model with data from an ongoing cluster analytics pilot before journal submission.

title: Comparing Embedding-Based and Rule-Based Field Extraction on a Multilingual Engineering Report Corpus
abstract: Engineering organisations in the Western Balkans often produce reports in Serbian, Hungarian, or a mixture of the two, creating challenges for extraction pipelines calibrated to a single language. This paper presents a controlled comparison of a rule-based extractor and a fine-tuned multilingual sentence-embedding approach (using a publicly available multilingual transformer base model) on a corpus of 390 reports in three language configurations: Serbian-only, Hungarian-only, and mixed. Fourteen field types are evaluated. The rule-based system was developed over two years and contains 112 rules; the embedding-based system was fine-tuned on 210 annotated documents over approximately eight hours of GPU time using a rented cloud instance. On Serbian-only documents the rule-based system achieves higher precision (0.88 vs. 0.83) but lower recall (0.76 vs. 0.85). On mixed-language documents the embedding approach is substantially better (F1 0.80 vs. 0.61). Error analysis shows the rule-based system degrades mainly on code-switched field labels, while the embedding approach degrades on fields with highly regular numeric formats where rules are trivially precise. A hybrid configuration combining rule-based extraction for numeric fields and embedding-based extraction for text fields achieves the best overall F1 of 0.87.

title: Contactless Card Usage After Infrastructure Rollout: A Natural Experiment in the Serbian Retail Sector
abstract: The mandatory rollout of contactless-capable point-of-sale terminals in Serbia between 2016 and 2017 created a near-natural experiment. This study exploits spatial variation in rollout timing across 22 municipalities to estimate the effect of terminal availability on contactless transaction frequency among adults aged 55 and over. Administrative transaction data from a regional cooperative bank (anonymised panel of 4,820 cardholders) were merged with municipality-level rollout dates. Difference-in-differences estimates show that terminal availability increased monthly contactless transaction count by 1.8 transactions on average for the 55–64 cohort but by only 0.6 for the 65+ cohort, with the gap widening in rural municipalities. Qualitative exit interviews with 24 cardholders suggest that physical card handling confidence and fear of unintended charges explain residual non-use among the oldest cohort.

title: The Effect of Mandatory Pre-Trade Transparency on Price Volatility in Thin Grain Markets: An ABM Study
abstract: Regulatory proposals to introduce mandatory pre-trade price transparency in Central and Eastern European commodity spot markets have been debated since 2016, yet empirical evidence is unavailable because no such regime currently exists. This paper uses an agent-based simulation to evaluate ex ante the effect of three transparency levels — no disclosure, best-bid-offer disclosure, and full order book disclosure — on price volatility and market depth in a thin grain market. The baseline market is calibrated to 2013–2018 sunflower transaction data from the Novi Sad commodity exchange, with 240 daily observations per year. Across 1,000 simulation runs per transparency condition, full order book disclosure reduces daily return volatility by 18 percent compared with the no-disclosure baseline but decreases market depth (measured by the Kyle lambda) by 12 percent, as informed traders reduce their order sizes to protect information rents. Best-bid-offer disclosure achieves 11 percent volatility reduction with only 4 percent depth loss, suggesting it as the more efficient regulatory option for thin markets.

title: Decomposition-Based Forecasting of Weekly Retail Sales Using Additive STL and Linear Regression Residuals
abstract: This paper examines a two-stage forecasting approach for weekly retail sales in a mid-sized Serbian supermarket chain covering 38 product categories over four years (2005–2008). The first stage applies Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) to extract trend and seasonal components, and the second stage fits a linear regression on the residuals using lagged sales, price index, and a binary promotion indicator as predictors. The combined model is evaluated against naïve seasonal baselines and an ARIMA benchmark on a hold-out set of 52 weeks. The decomposition-regression model reduces mean absolute percentage error by 11.4% relative to the seasonal naïve and by 6.8% relative to ARIMA on the full category set. The improvement is most pronounced for categories with irregular promotional activity, where MAPE drops by up to 19%. The paper argues that explicit residual modelling after decomposition captures promotion-driven variance that ARIMA cannot readily absorb without extensive order selection.

title: Promotional Lift Estimation in High-Frequency Grocery Data: A Regression Tree Approach
abstract: Promotional discounts introduce sharp, short-lived demand spikes that distort standard time-series forecasts. This study uses daily point-of-sale data from a grocery retailer operating 12 stores in Vojvodina, covering 180 stock-keeping units over 26 months, to build a regression tree model that estimates the multiplicative promotional lift factor as a function of discount depth, display type, day-of-week, and preceding baseline demand. The tree is grown with a minimum leaf size of 30 observations and pruned by five-fold cross-validation. Estimated lift factors range from 1.1 to 4.7 across SKUs, with the highest lifts observed for beverages during weekend promotions. Incorporating the estimated lift factors into a Holt-Winters baseline reduces forecast RMSE by 14.2% on a four-week evaluation window compared to the baseline alone. The approach avoids the need for a large promotion history at the SKU level by pooling across the category.

title: Handling Missing and Zero-Inflated Sales Records in Short-Term Forecasting Pipelines
abstract: Transactional retail and e-commerce datasets routinely contain zeros that arise from two distinct processes: genuine absence of demand and stockouts or listing gaps. Conflating these two sources inflates forecast error and biases inventory replenishment decisions. This paper proposes a classification-then-regression pipeline in which a logistic regression first separates structural zeros from demand zeros using store-level availability flags, lagged assortment data, and warehouse shipment records, and an ensemble regression forecaster is then applied only to non-structural observations. Experiments are conducted on an online grocery dataset of 4,200 SKUs over 18 months, with roughly 31% zero-sales days. The pipeline lowers mean absolute error by 9.3% over a zero-imputation baseline and by 5.1% over a simpler censoring correction. Practical implications for data preprocessing in production forecasting systems serving small to mid-sized e-commerce operators are discussed.

title: Calendar Feature Engineering for Day-of-Week and Holiday Effects in E-Commerce Order Volume Forecasting
abstract: Day-of-week patterns and public holidays create systematic but non-stationary demand cycles in e-commerce order volumes. This study systematically evaluates 14 calendar feature representations—ranging from binary holiday flags and cyclical sine-cosine encodings to learned embeddings from a small feed-forward network—across three datasets: a Serbian online electronics retailer (22 months), a Hungarian fashion e-tailer (18 months), and a Croatian home goods platform (15 months). Each representation is plugged into an otherwise identical gradient boosted trees framework trained on rolling four-week windows. Cyclical encodings combined with a holiday-type categorical feature consistently outperform binary flags in all three datasets, reducing Weighted Absolute Percentage Error by between 3.1% and 7.4% depending on the series. The learned embedding approach offers marginal additional gains only for the electronics retailer, which has the most irregular holiday purchasing pattern. The paper provides practical guidance for feature selection in production forecasting pipelines with limited labelled history.

title: A Comparative Study of SARIMA and Random Forest Regressors for Monthly Demand Forecasting in a Regional B2B Marketplace
abstract: Regional business-to-business marketplaces exhibit demand patterns shaped by procurement cycles, fiscal calendar effects, and sector-specific seasonality that differ substantially from consumer retail. This paper compares SARIMA and Random Forest regressors for 1-month-ahead and 3-month-ahead demand forecasting across 87 product lines traded on a Novi Sad-based B2B platform over 48 months. SARIMA models are identified individually per product line using AIC-guided order selection; Random Forest is trained on a pooled dataset with product-line indicators, time index features, and macroeconomic covariates including the Serbian industrial production index and EUR/RSD exchange rate. Random Forest achieves lower MAPE at the 1-month horizon for 61 of 87 lines, while SARIMA performs comparably or better for the 18 product lines with the most regular seasonal cycles and sparse promotional activity. The cross-horizon comparison highlights the conditions under which a pooled ML model is preferable to individually fitted statistical models.

title: Quantile Regression Forests for Probabilistic Demand Forecasting Under Promotional Uncertainty
abstract: Point forecasts are insufficient for inventory planning under high promotional uncertainty because they suppress information about forecast spread. This paper applies Quantile Regression Forests to generate distributional demand forecasts for a set of 310 fast-moving consumer goods across 24 months of daily e-commerce data, with special attention to periods surrounding promotional events. The model is trained with promotional type, discount depth, days-since-last-promotion, and standard calendar features as inputs. Prediction intervals at the 80% and 95% nominal levels are evaluated using coverage and average interval width. QRF achieves empirical 80% coverage of 79.3% and 95% coverage of 93.8% on non-promotional days, but coverage degrades to 71.2% and 88.1% on the first two promotional days, indicating residual systematic underestimation of promotional variance. A post-hoc recalibration step using conformal prediction restores nominal coverage at the cost of wider intervals. Results suggest that model-based probabilistic forecasting still requires recalibration for accurate safety stock calculations in promotional settings.

title: Short-Term Demand Forecasting with Gradient Boosting: Feature Importance and Model Interpretability in E-Commerce Contexts
abstract: Gradient boosted trees have become a standard tool in demand forecasting, yet practitioners often deploy them without systematic analysis of which features drive forecast accuracy. This paper trains an XGBoost model on daily order data from a Serbian e-commerce platform covering four product categories (electronics, clothing, household goods, sporting goods) over 36 months and analyses feature importance using permutation importance, SHAP values, and partial dependence plots. Across all categories, lagged demand at lags 1, 7, and 14 days accounts for the largest share of explained variance. Promotional discount depth ranks fourth overall but rises to second for electronics, where promotional events are larger and less frequent. Day-of-week encoding consistently matters more than month-of-year encoding except in clothing, where seasonal fashion cycles dominate. The paper provides a structured walkthrough of interpretability analysis as a model validation and communication tool for forecasting teams in small and medium enterprises.

title: Forecasting Demand for a Long-Tail Product Assortment: Clustering-Then-Forecasting on Sparse E-Commerce Data
abstract: E-commerce platforms with long-tail assortments face the challenge that a large fraction of SKUs have sparse, intermittent demand histories too short or irregular to support individual model training. This paper proposes a clustering-then-forecasting approach in which SKUs are grouped using k-means on feature vectors comprising mean demand, coefficient of variation, average inter-demand interval, and promotional responsiveness score. A single XGBoost model is then fitted per cluster rather than per SKU, using cluster membership as an additional input feature. The method is evaluated on a dataset of 9,400 SKUs from a multi-category online retailer, of which 64% have fewer than 90 non-zero sales days over a 12-month training window. Compared to a global single-model baseline and individual ARIMA fits where feasible, the clustering approach reduces overall MAE by 8.1% and improves accuracy most substantially for the two sparse-demand clusters. Cluster stability across time is examined and found to be acceptable for quarterly re-clustering.
