title: Incorporating Web Search Volume as an External Covariate in Short-Term E-Commerce Demand Forecasting
abstract: Search query volume from public web indices is a publicly available, high-frequency signal that may lead observed retail demand by one to several days. This paper investigates whether adding weekly search index data as an external covariate improves 1-week-ahead demand forecasts for 45 consumer electronics products sold through a Serbian online retailer over 24 months. Cross-correlation analysis confirms a statistically significant lead relationship at lag 1 week for 28 of 45 products. A LightGBM model augmented with the lagged search index is compared to an identical model without it; augmentation reduces MAPE by 4.3% on average across the 28 correlated products and by a statistically insignificant 0.6% across the remaining 17. The paper also discusses practical obstacles including changes in search index methodology, inconsistent geographic coverage, and category-level aggregation in public data sources, and recommends a correlation screening step before routinely incorporating such covariates.

title: Transfer Learning for Demand Forecasting: Adapting Pre-Trained Gradient Boosting Models Across E-Commerce Verticals
abstract: Training accurate demand forecasting models requires sufficient historical data, which new e-commerce verticals or recently launched product lines often lack. This paper investigates whether a model pre-trained on transaction data from an established vertical (consumer electronics, 36 months, 120 SKUs) can be adapted to a data-scarce target vertical (home appliances, 8 months, 64 SKUs) through fine-tuning. A LightGBM model is pre-trained on the source domain and then incrementally updated using target domain data via a warm-start procedure, with early stopping based on target-domain validation loss. The adapted model is compared to a model trained from scratch on target data only and to a global pooled model. The transfer approach outperforms training from scratch on 51 of 64 target SKUs and performs comparably to the pooled model on average, with a meaningful advantage on SKUs with fewer than 60 training observations. Limitations regarding domain shift in promotional patterns are discussed.

title: Evaluating Rolling-Window Retraining Frequencies for Demand Forecasting Models in Volatile E-Commerce Environments
abstract: Machine learning demand forecasting models are typically retrained periodically, but the optimal retraining frequency depends on the rate of concept drift and available computational resources. This study evaluates five retraining schedules—daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, and quarterly—for XGBoost and LightGBM models applied to daily order data from a fast-fashion e-commerce platform over 18 months, a period that includes two major promotional seasons and one supply disruption event. Performance is tracked via a rolling MAPE computed over successive four-week evaluation windows. Weekly retraining yields the best average MAPE for both models, with diminishing returns for daily retraining and measurable degradation at monthly and quarterly frequencies. During the supply disruption window, all schedules show elevated error, but the daily retrained model recovers three weeks earlier than the weekly one. The results support weekly retraining as a practical default for high-variance promotional categories, with event-triggered retraining as a complementary mechanism.

title: Machine Learning for Retail and E-Commerce Forecasting: Methods, Data Pipelines, and Business Integration
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of machine learning regression and ensemble methods to short-term demand forecasting in retail and e-commerce settings, with a focus on practitioners working with transactional data. The chapter covers data preprocessing pipelines for high-frequency POS and order data, feature construction for temporal, promotional, and external covariates, model selection and validation protocols appropriate for time-ordered data, and the integration of forecasting outputs into inventory and pricing decision systems. Emphasis is placed on recurring practical challenges: zero-inflated series, sparse SKU histories, promotional calendar alignment, and the mismatch between statistical forecast accuracy metrics and operational cost objectives. Case examples are drawn from Southeastern European e-commerce contexts. The chapter is intended as a methodological reference for graduate students and analysts rather than as a theoretical treatment.

title: Evaluating Explanation Strategies for Cold-Start Recommendations in a Small Retail Web Interface: A User Study
abstract: Algorithmic recommendation quality alone does not determine whether a small retailer's customers accept and act on suggestions. This paper reports a controlled user study examining how three explanation strategies—no explanation, attribute-based rationale, and social proof framing—affect click-through intention on cold-start recommendations shown in a prototype web shop interface. Participants were 94 adult consumers recruited through a regional consumer panel in Vojvodina. Each participant evaluated ten cold-start recommendation scenarios under one explanation condition. Click-through intention was measured on a five-point scale. Attribute-based rationale explanations produced a mean intention score of 3.71 compared to 3.12 for social proof and 2.84 for no explanation. A moderation analysis shows the attribute explanation advantage is stronger for participants who report higher product involvement. The study suggests that for small retailers with limited social proof data, investing in structured product metadata also supports explanation quality, creating a secondary motivation beyond algorithmic performance.

title: Transfer learning for demand forecasting across product categories with heterogeneous sales volumes
abstract: Transferring a forecasting model trained on high-volume product categories to low-volume categories in the same retail domain is a practically attractive strategy when the target categories lack sufficient training data. This paper formalises the transfer as a fine-tuning procedure for LSTM networks and tests it on a dataset of 890 weekly series spanning eight product supergroups from a Croatian online fashion retailer. Source models are trained on supergroups with at least 60 weeks of data; fine-tuning is performed on target supergroups with 10 to 25 weeks of data using between 5 and 20 labelled examples. Transferred models reduce MAE by 12–19 percent relative to models trained from scratch on target data alone, depending on the volume ratio between source and target. The paper examines which source–target combinations yield the largest accuracy gains and finds that volume similarity is a stronger predictor of transfer benefit than category semantic similarity. Negative transfer is observed in two of 16 tested combinations.

title: Cloud-Based Accounting Software Adoption in Vojvodina's Small Family Manufacturers: Perceived Quality Differences Versus On-Premise Systems
abstract: As cloud-based accounting solutions become commercially accessible to micro and small enterprises, questions arise about whether owner-managers perceive the information outputs of cloud systems differently from those of locally hosted on-premise alternatives. This paper compares AIS output quality perceptions using the refined 18-item instrument developed in prior work, administered to matched samples of 89 cloud adopters and 91 on-premise users in Vojvodina's small manufacturing sector. Independent-samples t-tests and follow-up Cohen's d calculations showed that cloud adopters rated timeliness significantly higher (d = 0.52) but rated data traceability lower (d = 0.38) compared to on-premise users. No significant difference emerged for accuracy or format clarity. Regression analysis indicated that timeliness perceptions partially mediated the relationship between deployment mode and decision confidence. The findings have practical implications for software vendors designing product positioning for the family SME segment and for advisors recommending system migration.

title: Sensitivity of Back-Calculated Subgrade Moduli to Measurement Spacing in FWD Testing on Low-Traffic Roads in Vojvodina
abstract: Falling weight deflectometer tests were performed on twelve rural road sections in Vojvodina with varying subgrade soil types, including loess and alluvial clay deposits. Deflection bowls were recorded at sensor spacings of 200, 300, and 450 mm, and back-calculation was carried out using an iterative least-squares algorithm calibrated against laboratory resilient modulus measurements from undisturbed core samples. Results showed that reducing sensor spacing from 450 to 200 mm improved subgrade modulus prediction accuracy by 11 to 18 percent depending on soil type, with the largest gains observed for silty clay profiles. Seasonal testing in April and October revealed modulus differences of up to 35 percent on sections with shallow water tables, underscoring the importance of measurement timing. The study recommends a minimum of two FWD campaigns per year for maintenance planning on roads with fine-grained subgrades in the Pannonian region.

title: Temperature Correction Procedures for Asphalt Layer Moduli Derived from FWD Data: A Comparison of Three Published Methods Applied to Serbian State Roads
abstract: Three temperature correction procedures for FWD-derived asphalt layer moduli—based respectively on ASTM D4695 guidelines, the Swedish Road Administration method, and a polynomial regression approach developed for central European climates—were applied to data collected on 28 sections of Serbian state roads during summer and spring testing campaigns. Reference temperature was set at 20 °C. Differences between methods reached up to 22 percent in corrected modulus values at asphalt surface temperatures above 40 °C, while agreement was within 8 percent at temperatures between 15 and 25 °C. The Swedish method systematically underestimated moduli for dense-graded asphalt concrete mixes common in Serbia when surface temperatures exceeded 38 °C. A regression correction factor derived from local binder grade data is proposed to reduce this bias. The findings have direct implications for overlay thickness design on high-traffic corridors.

title: Back-Calculation of Pavement Layer Moduli under Freeze-Thaw Transition Conditions Using a Modified Boussinesq Framework
abstract: The paper presents a modified Boussinesq-based back-calculation framework that incorporates pore pressure changes in unbound granular base layers during the freeze-thaw transition period. Field data were collected on a 4.2-km test section on a regional road near Sombor during three consecutive spring thaw periods (2010–2012). FWD deflection measurements were taken at weekly intervals from mid-February to late April, capturing the full thaw weakening cycle. A three-layer elastic model was fitted iteratively, with a temperature-dependent viscoelastic correction for the asphalt layer. Results showed that base course moduli dropped to as low as 42 MPa during peak thaw weakening, compared to 280 MPa in frozen state and 190 MPa in the summer reference condition. The framework reduced root-mean-square deflection errors by 14 percent compared to isothermal back-calculation. Load restriction periods calculated from the results are compared to current Serbian regulations.

title: Effect of Recycled Asphalt Pavement Content on Back-Calculated Layer Moduli at Varying Temperatures
abstract: Six test sections with recycled asphalt pavement (RAP) content ranging from 0 to 40 percent by mass were constructed on a secondary road in Srem and monitored with FWD testing over two years. Back-calculated surface layer moduli at 20 °C reference temperature increased monotonically with RAP content up to 30 percent, beyond which stiffness gains were marginal while low-temperature susceptibility increased. At −5 °C, sections with 40 percent RAP showed moduli 18 percent higher than virgin asphalt controls but also exhibited a 23 percent increase in transverse cracking density after the first winter. Subbase and subgrade moduli were unaffected by surface mix composition. The results suggest that 20 to 25 percent RAP incorporation offers the best balance between stiffness contribution and cracking resistance for the continental climate of northern Serbia, and this range is compatible with current Serbian technical specifications for recycled mixtures.

title: Seasonal Variation of Unbound Granular Base Moduli on Roads with and without Drainage Improvement: A Multi-Year FWD Study
abstract: Paired road sections—one with improved edge drainage and one without—were instrumented on five routes in Bačka and monitored with quarterly FWD testing from 2015 to 2019. Pavement cross-sections were characterised with ground-penetrating radar prior to testing to confirm layer thicknesses. Back-calculated granular base moduli on undrained sections fell to a seasonal minimum averaging 68 MPa in late March compared to 195 MPa in August, a reduction of 65 percent. Drained sections exhibited a narrower seasonal range of 110 to 210 MPa. The modulus ratio between spring minimum and summer maximum correlated strongly with annual precipitation and depth to water table. A simple lookup table relating seasonal modulus adjustment factors to drainage category and mean annual precipitation is proposed for use in regional overlay design without the need for repeated FWD campaigns. The table has been integrated into an internal design spreadsheet used by the Vojvodina roads authority.

title: Pavement Deterioration Modelling under Combined Heavy Traffic and Repeated Freeze-Thaw Cycles Using a Coupled Thermal-Mechanical Approach
abstract: A numerical model coupling one-dimensional heat transfer through the pavement cross-section with a mechanistic fatigue damage accumulation algorithm was developed and validated against field data from ten monitored sections on a national road corridor in Serbia. The thermal module used finite difference discretisation with 20 mm layer intervals and hourly air temperature inputs from the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia for the period 2013–2020. Damage was accumulated using a modified Paris law for crack propagation, with moduli updated after each simulated freeze-thaw cycle based on empirical relationships fitted to FWD data. Sections subjected to more than 45 freeze-thaw cycles per year showed pavement life reductions of 28 to 40 percent compared to sections with fewer than 20 cycles, even at identical traffic loading. Model predictions of remaining structural life agreed with visual distress surveys within one year for 8 of 10 validation sections.

title: Influence of Climate Projections on Predicted Residual Life of Asphalt Pavements in the Pannonian Basin: A Scenario-Based Study
abstract: Regional climate projections from the EURO-CORDEX ensemble (RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios) were downscaled to 12 km resolution and used to drive a mechanistic-empirical deterioration model for a representative asphalt pavement cross-section in the Pannonian Basin. Two design traffic levels (2 × 10⁶ and 8 × 10⁶ equivalent single-axle loads over 20 years) were considered. Under RCP8.5, mean summer air temperatures are projected to rise by 2.1 °C by 2050 relative to the 1990–2020 baseline, reducing asphalt surface layer moduli and increasing rutting susceptibility. Simultaneously, the number of freeze-thaw cycles per year is projected to decrease by 12 to 18 percent, marginally reducing frost-related damage. The net effect on pavement life was negative in both traffic scenarios, with residual life reductions of 11 to 17 percent by mid-century. The study suggests that binder grade selection should be revisited for roads designed with a 30-year service life horizon in the region.

title: GPR-Assisted Layer Thickness Determination and Its Effect on Back-Calculation Reliability for Heterogeneous Pavement Structures
abstract: Ground-penetrating radar surveys were conducted prior to FWD testing on 18 pavement sections with known construction histories showing significant thickness variability due to multiple overlay campaigns. Layer thickness inputs derived from GPR (mean absolute error 6 mm against cores) were compared with thickness inputs taken from construction records. Back-calculation using GPR-derived thicknesses reduced the coefficient of variation of the estimated base course modulus from 31 to 19 percent across sections, while subgrade modulus estimates improved marginally. On sections where overlay thickness varied by more than 30 mm along a 100-m segment, GPR-based back-calculation changed design overlay thickness recommendations by an average of 22 mm. The paper quantifies the economic benefit of adding a GPR pre-survey to routine FWD campaigns for rehabilitation planning, estimating a reduction in unnecessary overlay material of 8 to 14 percent on heterogeneous sections.

title: Calibration of a Simplified Freeze-Thaw Deterioration Index for Use in Network-Level Pavement Management Systems in Serbia
abstract: A freeze-thaw deterioration index (FTDI) was developed to support network-level pavement management without requiring full mechanistic-empirical analysis at each section. The index combines annual freeze-thaw cycle count derived from daily minimum and maximum air temperatures, mean annual precipitation, subgrade soil type category, and pavement age into a single weighted score. Weights were calibrated against 12 years of pavement condition index (PCI) monitoring data from 340 sections in the Serbian state road network, using multiple linear regression with cross-validation. The FTDI explained 62 percent of the variance in PCI decline rates on flexible pavement sections with unbound granular bases. Sections with FTDI above 65 showed median PCI deterioration rates 2.3 times higher than sections below 35. The index is implemented as a spreadsheet tool supplied to regional road management offices and was piloted during 2024 network condition surveys.

title: Benchmarking graph neural network architectures for large-scale airborne point cloud segmentation on heterogeneous hardware
abstract: Several graph neural network architectures have been proposed for 3-D point cloud segmentation, but systematic comparisons on airborne rather than terrestrial data and on heterogeneous computing environments are scarce. This study benchmarks five architectures—EdgeConv, PointGAT, SuperpointGraph, RandLA-Net, and KPConv—on a common airborne LiDAR dataset of 1.1 billion points covering mixed urban and agricultural land in Vojvodina. Experiments were run on three hardware configurations: a consumer-grade GPU workstation (24 GB VRAM), the Faculty GPU cluster (4 × 16 GB VRAM), and a cloud-rented A100 instance. Metrics reported include overall accuracy, class-wise F1-score, training time, inference throughput, and peak GPU memory. KPConv achieved the highest overall accuracy (93.1%) but required 4.8× more training time than RandLA-Net, which reached 91.4% accuracy. On the multi-GPU cluster, RandLA-Net showed the best parallelisation efficiency (91%) while KPConv exhibited significant load imbalance. The paper provides a decision guide for practitioners choosing architectures given hardware budget and accuracy requirements, and reports the full confusion matrices and hyperparameter configurations used.

title: Stress intensity factor solutions for weld root cracks in cruciform fillet-welded joints under combined bending and axial load
abstract: Weld root cracks in cruciform fillet-welded joints are a common failure mode in steel bridge cross-girder connections yet SIF solutions for combined loading remain limited in the literature. This paper presents parametric finite element results for mode I stress intensity factors at weld root crack tips in cruciform joints with leg ratio a/T from 0.1 to 0.7 and plate thickness T from 12 to 40 mm, under 19 combinations of axial and in-plane bending loads. Three-dimensional models were built in Abaqus with refined meshes at the crack front using collapsed quadratic elements. Interaction integrals were used to extract KI values. The results were fitted to a polynomial correction function F(a/T, ρ, λ) with a maximum fitting error of 2.1% over the parametric space. Validation against three published experimental datasets showed mean deviation below 5%. The proposed solutions are intended for direct use in Paris-law integration routines for bridge connection fatigue assessment.

title: Static deflection modelling of a three-link planar arm under gravitational loading using finite-element discretisation
abstract: Lightweight aluminium links in serial manipulators exhibit measurable elastic deformation under their own weight and tool payloads, causing systematic positioning errors that rigid-body kinematic models cannot explain. This paper presents a quasi-static finite-element deflection model for a three-link planar arm with hollow rectangular cross-sections. Link stiffness matrices were derived from beam-theory and validated against measurements taken with a Renishaw touch probe at 216 configurations spanning the full workspace. Modelled deflections agreed with measured values to within 0.31 mm RMS at the end-effector across all tested configurations and payload levels of 0–2.5 kg. The model was then embedded in a compensation routine that adjusts joint-angle commands before motion execution. In a 40-point positioning test, uncompensated error of 1.87 mm RMS was reduced to 0.28 mm RMS. The approach is computationally light enough to run at 200 Hz on a standard ARM Cortex-M7 controller. Results suggest that offline stiffness identification combined with real-time command correction is a practical alternative to more expensive force/torque sensors for agricultural manipulators.

title: Payload-dependent kinematic error identification in a 4-DOF pick-and-place arm using partial pose measurements
abstract: Standard Denavit-Hartenberg calibration assumes a rigid robot and cannot account for configuration-dependent deflections caused by varying payloads. This paper proposes a calibration procedure that identifies both geometric parameter errors and a set of lumped payload-dependent compliance coefficients from partial end-effector pose measurements obtained with a laser tracker. Measurements were collected at 96 configurations with three payload conditions (0 kg, 1.0 kg, and 1.8 kg). A least-squares identification problem was formulated and solved iteratively. Identified model parameters reduced mean position error from 2.1 mm to 0.41 mm and mean orientation error from 0.9° to 0.19° across the full test set. The number of required measurement poses was systematically studied; configurations that maximise the observability index of the identification Jacobian were selected using a greedy algorithm. The method requires only a lightweight laser tracker rather than specialised metrology equipment, making it applicable in field maintenance scenarios for agricultural arms.

title: Effect of row-structure proximity on achievable calibration accuracy: a simulation study
abstract: Orchard row structures restrict manipulator configuration diversity during in-situ calibration because the arm must avoid collisions with trellis wires and tree canopy. This paper examines, through simulation, how configuration-space restrictions imposed by a standardised apple-row geometry affect the identifiability of geometric and compliance parameters. A Monte Carlo study over 5000 random row geometries (inter-row spacing 2.8–4.2 m, trellis height 1.8–3.4 m) generated constrained configuration sets of varying size. Calibration was simulated by adding Gaussian measurement noise (σ = 0.3 mm) to synthetic pose data and solving the identification problem. Parameter estimation error increased by a median factor of 2.4 compared to unconstrained full-workspace calibration. A minimum of 48 reachable configurations yielded position accuracy below 0.6 mm in 90% of row geometries tested. Strategies for selecting maximally informative configurations within the constrained space are discussed. The simulation code is available under a BSD-2 licence.

title: Stiffness identification under cyclic fruit-thinning loads using on-board joint torque sensing
abstract: Repetitive contact forces during mechanical fruit thinning produce cyclic loading on manipulator links that differs from the quasi-static payload assumptions used in most compliance calibration methods. This paper presents a stiffness identification procedure that exploits joint torque data collected during actual thinning motions rather than dedicated calibration routines. A 5-DOF prototype arm equipped with strain-gauge torque sensors at each joint performed 3200 thinning strokes on an instrumented plum-tree mockup. Link compliance parameters were identified from a regression model relating measured joint torques to end-effector position residuals observed with the Qualisys optical tracking system. Identified stiffness values agreed with bench-test values to within 6.4% for three of five links; the proximal link showed 11.2% discrepancy attributed to joint bearing play. Compensation using identified parameters reduced mean position error during thinning from 1.9 mm to 0.55 mm. The in-operation identification approach eliminates dedicated downtime for recalibration in field deployments.

title: Temperature-induced geometric parameter drift in an outdoor manipulator arm over a seasonal measurement campaign
abstract: Kinematic calibration performed indoors may become invalid when the robot operates outdoors across seasons because thermal expansion shifts geometric parameters. This study tracked the DH parameters of a lightweight 4-DOF orchard arm through monthly outdoor calibration sessions from March to November using a total station. Ambient temperature ranged from 4 °C to 38 °C. Link lengths varied by up to 0.19 mm per 10 °C temperature change, consistent with the thermal expansion coefficient of the aluminium alloy (6082-T6). Joint offset angles drifted by up to 0.06° per 10 °C, attributed to bearing clearance changes. A linear thermal compensation model, requiring only an ambient temperature input, reduced seasonally induced position error from a peak of 1.1 mm to below 0.35 mm. The study recommends that agricultural manipulators installed in open-air conditions incorporate a temperature-compensation layer in their kinematic model, calibrated once in a controlled setting.

title: Towards standardised test procedures for evaluating kinematic accuracy of agricultural robot arms
abstract: There is no agreed test standard for measuring and reporting position accuracy of manipulator arms in agricultural robotics, making literature comparisons unreliable. This book chapter reviews existing ISO and ANSI standards for industrial robot performance testing and discusses their limitations when applied to lightweight, compliance-affected agricultural arms operating outdoors. The authors propose a draft test protocol specifying seven mandatory configuration families that span roll, pitch, and payload combinations typical of orchard tasks, measurement equipment requirements (minimum accuracy class), environmental recording obligations (temperature, wind), and reporting metrics beyond the ISO 9283 repeatability figure. The protocol was piloted on two manipulator prototypes; results show that ISO 9283 repeatability underestimates operational positioning error by a factor of 1.4–2.1 when applied to compliant arms under variable payloads. The chapter is intended as a starting point for a working-group discussion within the European agricultural robotics community.

title: Compensation of link flexibility during apple-harvesting motions using model predictive joint-angle correction
abstract: Apple-harvesting requires the end-effector to reach fruit with position errors below 5 mm under fruit-weight payloads that change at each pick. A model predictive compensation scheme is presented that updates joint-angle commands at 50 Hz based on a real-time estimate of current payload, obtained from the change in joint torque at the wrist. The compliance model underlying the prediction was identified in a one-time 30-minute calibration session. Hardware-in-the-loop experiments on the BioSense 5-DOF orchard arm with 340 simulated pick-and-retract cycles showed mean end-effector position error of 0.48 mm (σ = 0.21 mm) compared to 1.73 mm (σ = 0.55 mm) without compensation. Computation ran on an embedded NVIDIA Jetson Orin module with 4.1 ms mean cycle time. Field trials in a commercial apple orchard in Futog, Serbia, covering 80 real fruit picks demonstrated a 91% success rate (detachment without contact with neighbouring fruit), up from 74% without compensation.

title: Identifying manipulator inertial parameters from free-swinging motions for use in dynamic deflection models
abstract: Accurate dynamic deflection compensation requires reliable inertial parameters (mass, centre of mass, inertia tensor) for each link and the tool. Direct measurement requires link disassembly, which is impractical in field conditions. This paper applies a free-swinging identification method to the BioSense 5-DOF orchard arm: each link is swung freely about its proximal joint while recording joint encoder data, and an equation-of-motion regression is solved for the link's inertial parameters. Twenty-five identification trials per link were performed. Identified mass values agreed with CAD model values to within 2.8% and inertia tensor diagonal elements to within 7.1%. Inertial parameters fed into the dynamic deflection model reduced trajectory tracking error during fast sweeping motions by 38% compared to the model using CAD-only inertia data. The method requires only joint encoders and no additional sensing hardware, which suits resource-constrained field deployments.

title: Effect of soil vibration transmitted through a mobile platform on end-effector positioning accuracy of an orchard manipulator
abstract: Orchard robots typically mount their manipulators on wheeled or tracked platforms that traverse uneven ground, introducing base vibrations that superimpose on link deflections. This study quantifies the contribution of platform-transmitted vibration to end-effector position error using a platform vibration characterisation campaign across three orchard floor types (mown grass, compacted gravel, tilled soil) at three travel speeds (0.2, 0.5, 0.8 m/s). Base accelerations were measured with a six-axis IMU and were input to a rigid-body simulation of the mounted arm. Simulated end-effector disturbance reached 3.1 mm peak-to-peak on tilled soil at 0.5 m/s, exceeding the deflection-induced error at the same speed. A passive vibration isolation mount (four rubber dampers, natural frequency 11 Hz) reduced base-transmitted disturbance to the end-effector by 61%. The study concludes that for combined mobile-plus-manipulator systems, vibration isolation at the base is a higher-priority intervention than further refinement of link-deflection compensation models.

title: Online deflection estimation without additional sensors using a reduced flexible-link model and motor current feedback
abstract: Adding accelerometers or strain gauges to a manipulator increases cost and failure risk in outdoor environments. This paper investigates whether motor current measurements, available on most servo drives, contain sufficient information to estimate link deflection states online. A reduced-order flexible-link model with two assumed modes per link was fitted to the BioSense 4-DOF arm; deflection states were estimated with an extended Kalman filter using only joint encoder and motor current signals as inputs. Estimator performance was evaluated against Qualisys optical tracking ground truth across 180 test motions with payloads ranging from 0 to 2.0 kg. Mean deflection estimation error at the end-effector was 0.54 mm, compared to a direct sensor measurement baseline of 0.18 mm. Compensation using EKF-estimated deflections reduced position error from 1.81 mm to 0.71 mm. While slightly less accurate than direct sensing, the current-only approach requires no additional hardware and could extend the operational service life of field robots.

title: Calibration transfer between nominally identical orchard manipulator arms: feasibility and accuracy limits
abstract: Deploying multiple identical orchard robots raises the question of whether a full kinematic calibration performed on one unit can be transferred to sister units with only a short verification step, rather than repeating the full procedure on each arm. This study examined three pairs of nominally identical BioSense 5-DOF arms built from the same drawings and bill of materials. Full calibration was performed on one arm of each pair; the identified parameters were transferred to the second arm and residual position errors were measured. Direct transfer without any verification step left mean errors of 0.94–1.37 mm, primarily due to manufacturing tolerances in joint housing alignment (measured spread 0.08–0.14 mm across units). A short 16-pose verification calibration, taking under 12 minutes, corrected these residuals to below 0.45 mm on all three units. The study provides a practical protocol for fleet-scale deployment of calibrated agricultural manipulators.

title: Measurement of pull-out force profiles for carrot cultivars in cohesive soils under controlled moisture conditions
abstract: Accurate characterization of the axial extraction force required to dislodge intact carrot roots from soil is a prerequisite for designing robotic harvesting grippers with appropriate actuator sizing. This study presents a laboratory-based pull-out testing protocol in which 180 carrot specimens of three cultivars (Nantes, Chantenay, and Flakkee) were harvested from standardized soil columns at three volumetric moisture levels (15%, 22%, and 30%). A custom servo-driven linear stage recorded continuous force–displacement profiles at a pull rate of 12 mm s⁻¹. Peak extraction forces ranged from 18 N to 74 N across cultivar–moisture combinations, with the highest values observed for the Flakkee cultivar at 22% moisture. Force–displacement curves exhibited a consistent elastic phase followed by an abrupt slip event corresponding to soil cohesion failure at the root surface. Statistical analysis using a two-way ANOVA confirmed that both cultivar morphology and soil moisture had significant independent effects (p < 0.01) on peak force, while their interaction term was significant only for the two wider cultivars. These results provide a baseline force dataset suitable for parameterizing robotic end-effector control laws.

title: Do Loan Officers Discriminate? Experimental Survey Evidence from Hungarian and Serbian Bank Branches
abstract: We report results from a structured vignette experiment conducted with 218 loan officers at bank branches in northern Serbia and southern Hungary in 2013. Participants evaluated eight standardised loan application profiles identical in financial ratios, sector, and loan size but varying in applicant gender and firm ownership structure. Loan officers were recruited through branch manager cooperation and completed paper-based surveys during working hours. Multinomial logit models show that female-named sole proprietors received approval recommendations approximately 11 percentage points less often than male-named equivalents, and were more frequently directed toward collateral top-up or guarantee requirements. The effect was stronger among officers with fewer than five years of experience and in branches with no written gender-neutral assessment protocol. Hungarian officers showed a smaller but statistically significant gap compared to Serbian officers. The experiment cannot establish causation in real lending decisions but provides direct evidence of attitudinal bias that may translate into loan file outcomes. We discuss limitations arising from social desirability bias and self-selection into participation.

title: Audit Trail Completeness and Gender Outcomes in SME Loan Files: A Documentary Analysis
abstract: Credit audit trails—the accumulated paper and digital records justifying a lending decision—vary considerably in completeness across bank branches in Serbia. This study asks whether incomplete audit trails are associated with worse loan terms for female applicants, using a sample of 860 closed loan files obtained under a data-sharing agreement with two regional banks. We coded each file for 23 documentation items covering income verification, collateral appraisal, guarantor identity, and approval rationale. Incomplete files, defined as missing six or more items, were more common in rural branches and for loans below RSD 2 million. Regression analysis shows that female applicants whose files were incomplete received interest rate spreads 47 basis points higher than male applicants with equivalently incomplete files, while no significant gender gap appeared in complete-file loans. The finding suggests that discretionary judgement fills gaps left by missing documentation, and that this discretion operates in a gender-differentiated manner. Policy recommendations focus on minimum documentation standards for small business loans.

title: Access to Finance for Women Entrepreneurs in the Western Balkans: A Comparative Overview
abstract: This book chapter surveys the empirical literature and available administrative data on female entrepreneurs' access to bank credit across six Western Balkan economies from approximately 2000 to 2015. Drawing on World Bank Enterprise Survey rounds, national credit registry statistics, and eleven in-depth interviews with bank credit risk managers, we identify three recurring structural factors: collateral shortfalls linked to property inheritance patterns, weak personal credit histories reflecting shorter formal employment tenures, and limited awareness of guarantee schemes among female business owners. Serbia and North Macedonia show the largest documented gaps in loan approval rates, while Montenegro shows relatively smaller differences possibly attributable to tourism-sector lending norms. The chapter discusses methodological limitations in cross-country comparison arising from differing SME definitions and credit registry coverage. It concludes with a policy matrix identifying low-cost interventions available to national development banks and supervisory authorities.

title: Personal Guarantees as a Substitute for Collateral: Gender Differences in Serbian SME Lending
abstract: When tangible collateral is insufficient, Serbian banks may accept personal guarantees from third parties. This paper investigates whether female-owned SMEs are more frequently required to provide such guarantees and whether the identity of acceptable guarantors differs by applicant gender. We analyse 2,190 loan contracts signed between 2012 and 2016, obtained from the credit portfolio records of three Serbian banks. Probit models indicate that female applicants are 9.3 percentage points more likely to be required to provide a personal guarantee after controlling for firm financial indicators and loan characteristics. Female applicants are also more often required to name a male co-guarantor, most commonly a spouse or male family member, which we document through a content analysis of guarantee clauses. This pattern raises concerns about the effective transfer of financial control and liability within households. We discuss the legal framework governing guarantee obligations under Serbian civil law and its implications for gender equity in business finance.

title: Measuring Loan Officer Discretion: A Latent Variable Approach Using Credit File Metadata
abstract: Loan officer discretion in SME lending is difficult to measure directly because decisions are justified post hoc in loan files. We propose a latent variable approach that uses observable metadata—processing time, number of revision rounds, and departures from model-predicted credit scores—as indicators of discretionary decision-making. Applying confirmatory factor analysis to a dataset of 3,410 loan files from seven Serbian banks between 2013 and 2018, we estimate a discretion index and examine its relationship with applicant gender. Files involving female applicants score 0.31 standard deviations higher on the discretion index, implying greater deviation from algorithmic recommendations in those cases. High-discretion files are associated with longer processing times and less favourable final terms for female applicants but not for male applicants. The method provides a replicable tool for supervisory use and for future research in other banking markets. Robustness checks include alternative factor structures and subsample analysis by bank size.

title: The 2008 Crisis and Gender-Differentiated Credit Tightening: Evidence from Serbian Bank Panel Data
abstract: The global financial crisis of 2008–2009 prompted widespread tightening of SME lending standards in Serbia. This paper examines whether tightening was distributed equally across male- and female-owned businesses. Using a bank-level panel dataset covering fourteen Serbian banks over 2006–2014 and disaggregated by reported borrower gender where available, we find that the post-crisis contraction in new SME loan volumes was 18–23 percent sharper for female-classified borrowers compared to male-classified borrowers within the same bank and sector. The effect persisted through 2011, with partial convergence thereafter. Banks with higher pre-crisis non-performing loan ratios showed the largest gender divergence in credit tightening. We interpret these results as consistent with risk aversion leading to disproportionate withdrawal from borrower segments perceived as marginal, with female-owned firms occupying that position in the distribution of bank relationships. Fixed-effects panel regressions and an event-study design both support the main finding.

title: Does Digitalisation of Loan Applications Reduce Gender Gaps? Preliminary Evidence from Serbian Fintech Pilots
abstract: Several Serbian banks introduced fully digital SME loan application portals between 2019 and 2022, removing face-to-face loan officer contact for initial screening. This preprint reports preliminary findings from a difference-in-differences analysis comparing gender gaps in approval rates and collateral requirements before and after portal introduction at four banks, against a control group of six banks that retained in-person processing throughout the period. The sample covers 8,720 applications filed between January 2018 and June 2023. Early results suggest that digitalization reduced the gender gap in approval rates by approximately 7 percentage points and narrowed collateral differentials by 9 percentage points at treated banks, consistent with the hypothesis that removing discretionary face-to-face contact attenuates gender bias. However, digital applicants show positive selection on financial literacy, complicating interpretation. The analysis is ongoing and the current estimates should be treated as provisional pending full data cleaning and robustness checks.

title: Inheritance Law, Property Ownership, and Female Collateral Capacity in Serbia: A Legal-Economic Analysis
abstract: Collateral shortfalls among female SME loan applicants are frequently attributed to lower property ownership rates. This paper investigates the legal mechanisms linking inheritance practice to female property accumulation in Serbia, combining analysis of civil registry and cadastral data for three municipalities in Vojvodina with a review of succession case outcomes from 2010 to 2022. Despite formal legal equality in inheritance rights since 1955, daughters receive immovable property in only 34 percent of intestate successions in the sample compared to 61 percent for sons, even when both are present in the family. Multivariate analysis of cadastral records shows that this gap translates into a 22 percentage point difference in property ownership rates among business-age adults, which we link to a predicted 11 percentage point gap in collateral-eligible assets. The paper argues that legal-formal equality is insufficient to eliminate asset gaps relevant to bank financing and that credit policy must account for the slow pace of inheritance norm change.

title: Loan Officer Turnover, Relationship Banking, and Gender: Evidence from a Natural Experiment in Serbian Branch Reorganisation
abstract: When banks restructure branch networks, loan officers are reassigned, ending established lending relationships. We exploit a wave of branch reorganisations at two major Serbian banks in 2021–2022 as a natural experiment to examine whether the disruption of banking relationships affected female and male SME borrowers differently. Using matched loan-officer and borrower panel data covering 4,340 SME accounts observed over 2019–2025, we find that female-owned firms experienced a 16 percent greater reduction in credit limits following officer reassignment compared to male-owned firms with equivalent credit histories and financials. The effect is concentrated in firms that had a relationship of four or more years with the displaced officer. Re-establishment of credit limits takes 14 months on average for female firms versus 9 months for male firms. The results suggest that relationship lending advantages accrue more slowly to female borrowers and are more fragile to organisational disruption, compounding the structural disadvantages documented in earlier work.

title: Exchange Rate Regime Choice and Sovereign Borrowing Costs: Comparing Fixed, Managed, and Floating Arrangements in Small Open Economies
abstract: Using a dataset of 28 small open economies in Central, Eastern, and Southeastern Europe over 2000–2015, this paper estimates the spread premium or discount associated with different exchange rate regimes after conditioning on fiscal and macroeconomic fundamentals. Regime classification follows the IMF Annual Report on Exchange Arrangements and Exchange Restrictions de facto taxonomy. A random-effects panel model with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors is applied to address cross-sectional dependence. Hard pegs—including currency boards and euroisation—are associated with spreads 60–90 basis points lower than managed floats with comparable debt ratios, but the discount narrows substantially during global risk-off episodes. The result is robust to alternative classifications and subsamples excluding EU members. An interaction term between hard peg status and external imbalances (current account deficit above 6 percent of GDP) suggests the spread discount disappears when external vulnerabilities are high, pointing to limits of exchange rate credibility in signalling overall macroeconomic stability.

title: Anti-Money-Laundering Obligations and Islamic Finance: Correspondent Banking Challenges in the Western Balkans
abstract: Islamic financial institutions in the Western Balkans face particular difficulties in maintaining correspondent banking relationships because their fee-based and profit-sharing income structures do not map cleanly onto the transaction-monitoring algorithms used by major European correspondent banks, which are calibrated for interest-bearing products. This study draws on structured interviews with compliance officers at six Western Balkan banks that handle Islamic finance-related transactions and reviews thirty-six suspicious transaction reports filed between 2018 and 2022 that originated from misclassification of legitimate Islamic finance transactions. The paper finds that approximately 40% of flagged transactions were later cleared as compliant, suggesting a significant false-positive rate driven by monitoring system design rather than genuine risk. Recommendations include FATF typology guidance tailored to profit-sharing structures and bilateral regulatory cooperation between national financial intelligence units in the region.

title: Segetal weed richness along an urbanisation gradient in the Vojvodina plain: a baseline floristic survey
abstract: This paper reports results of a systematic floristic survey conducted in 2009–2010 along four rural-to-urban transects radiating from Novi Sad. Each transect comprised 12 plots (100 m²) distributed at 2 km intervals from the city boundary to surrounding arable land, yielding 48 plots in total. Standard Braun-Blanquet relevés were recorded in late spring and late summer. A total of 287 vascular plant taxa were identified, of which 112 were classified as segetal or ruderal according to the Pannonicum flora database. Species richness declined from 41 species per plot in peri-urban zones to 18 per plot in intensively cultivated areas 20 km from the city edge. Ellenberg N values increased toward the urban core, averaging 6.1 in central plots versus 4.8 in rural plots. Indicator taxa for high nitrogen conditions, including Urtica dioica and Chenopodium album, were significantly more abundant (p < 0.01) within 6 km of the city boundary. The dataset provides a reference baseline for long-term monitoring of nitrogen-driven floristic change in lowland Serbia.

title: Nitrogen foliar content as a proxy for atmospheric N load in ruderal Asteraceae: field validation in the Pannonian lowland
abstract: The study tested whether foliar nitrogen concentration in three common ruderal Asteraceae species—Artemisia vulgaris, Conyza canadensis, and Cirsium arvense—could serve as a low-cost biomonitoring proxy for atmospheric reactive nitrogen deposition. Leaf material was collected at 30 sites across the Novi Sad metropolitan area and its agricultural surroundings in July and August 2012. Total foliar nitrogen was determined by Kjeldahl digestion and ICP-OES analysis. Foliar N ranged from 1.8 % dry weight at rural reference sites to 3.4 % dry weight at high-deposition urban fringe sites. Spearman correlations between foliar N and co-located ALPHA sampler deposition values were strong for Artemisia vulgaris (ρ = 0.82) and moderate for Conyza canadensis (ρ = 0.61). Species-specific differences in root uptake of soil mineral nitrogen partly confounded the atmospheric signal, especially on abandoned industrial plots with residual soil contamination. The results support cautious use of Artemisia vulgaris as a sentinel species in monitoring schemes where atmospheric instrumentation is unavailable.

title: Changes in Ellenberg N values of urban weed communities in Novi Sad between 1985 and 2014: a re-survey approach
abstract: Historical relevé data from city surveys conducted by the Novi Sad Municipal Institute for Nature Protection in 1985 (n = 63 relevés) were compared with new surveys of the same or equivalent locations recorded in 2013–2014 (n = 61 relevés). A paired comparison of mean Ellenberg N indicator values and species richness was performed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Mean community Ellenberg N increased significantly from 5.1 in 1985 to 6.2 in 2014 (W = 1847, p < 0.001). Total species richness per relevé declined marginally (from 22.4 to 19.8 taxa on average) but the decline was concentrated among low-N indicator species, while high-N indicator taxa increased in frequency by a median of 18 percentage points. The most consistent gainers were Galium aparine, Sisymbrium altissimum, and Amaranthus retroflexus. Land-cover change, particularly the replacement of cobbled courtyards with sealed surfaces, contributed to local extinctions of stress-tolerant species independently of N effects. The findings indicate ongoing nitrophilisation of the urban flora consistent with persistent elevated atmospheric N loads.

title: Experimental nitrogen addition to mesocosm grassland plots: community composition responses after three growing seasons
abstract: A mesocosm nitrogen addition experiment was established in 2014 at the Faculty of Agriculture greenhouse facility in Novi Sad. Forty-eight standardised plots (1 m × 1 m) were seeded with a standardised mixture of 15 ruderal and semi-ruderal species characteristic of Vojvodina roadsides. Four nitrogen treatment levels (0, 20, 40, 80 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ as ammonium nitrate solution applied in six equal splits) were applied in fully randomised blocks. After three growing seasons, above-ground biomass, species richness, Shannon diversity, and cover by functional group were assessed. Species richness declined from 10.3 species per plot at zero N to 6.8 at 80 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ (ANOVA, F₃,₄₄ = 18.4, p < 0.001). Tall-growing nitrophytes (Urtica dioica, Sambucus ebulus seedlings) increased cover from below 5 % to 38 % at the highest dose. Low-growing annuals (Poa annua, Sagina procumbens) were competitively excluded by year three at doses ≥ 40 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. Results mirror field gradient patterns and support the hypothesis that deposition-driven competitive exclusion is a primary driver of diversity loss.

title: Spatial interpolation of atmospheric nitrogen deposition across Vojvodina using kriging: comparison of thin-plate spline and ordinary kriging methods
abstract: Passive ALPHA sampler data collected at 48 sites across Vojvodina province during 2015–2016 were used to compare two spatial interpolation approaches for mapping total inorganic nitrogen deposition. Ordinary kriging and thin-plate spline interpolation were applied using R packages gstat and fields. Cross-validation using leave-one-out procedure showed that thin-plate spline produced lower root mean square error (RMSE = 1.21 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹) compared with ordinary kriging (RMSE = 1.67 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹). The resulting deposition map showed a clear urban plume extending 8–12 km downwind of Novi Sad in the prevailing north-westerly wind direction, with a secondary hotspot around the Zrenjanin petrochemical complex. Total N deposition exceeded 15 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ over approximately 18 % of the province area, mostly peri-urban and downwind of large livestock operations. The map was overlaid with floristic survey data to identify areas where deposition likely exceeds critical loads for mesophilous grassland plant communities.

title: Roadside verge management and nitrogen deposition interact to shape segetal flora in the Bačka region
abstract: This observational study examined how mowing frequency and atmospheric nitrogen deposition jointly influenced plant species composition on 76 roadside verge segments in Bačka, sampled in 2018. Mowing regime (classified as high-frequency ≥ 4 cuts yr⁻¹, low-frequency 1–2 cuts yr⁻¹, or unmanaged) was recorded from municipal maintenance records and verified by field inspection. N deposition at each site was estimated from the interpolated provincial deposition surface produced in earlier work. Redundancy analysis explained 41 % of species composition variance, with N deposition (λ = 0.22) and mowing frequency (λ = 0.12) as the two strongest explanatory variables. High mowing frequency dampened but did not eliminate the positive relationship between N deposition and nitrophyte cover. Unmanaged verges under high deposition (> 18 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹) were dominated almost exclusively by Urtica dioica, Galium aparine, and Fallopia japonica. Low-frequency mowing under moderate deposition supported the greatest number of target grassland species per segment. Results suggest that combining reduced mowing with deposition abatement offers the most benefit to roadside biodiversity.

title: Nitrogen deposition and weed management in cereal fields of Vojvodina: implications for integrated crop protection
abstract: This book chapter reviews current knowledge on interactions between atmospheric reactive nitrogen enrichment and weed community dynamics in winter wheat and maize fields of the Vojvodina plain, drawing on a decade of field and mesocosm data from the authors' research group and from parallel studies in Hungary and Romania. The review covers three themes: (1) nitrogen-driven competitive release of grass weeds, particularly Apera spica-venti and Alopecurus myosuroides, in wheat crops under elevated atmospheric N loads; (2) changes in herbicide efficacy observed at elevated foliar N concentrations in target weed species; and (3) economic implications of weed biomass increases for yield penalties in high-N deposition zones. Data from 14 farm surveys conducted between 2014 and 2020 are synthesised alongside published dose-response models. The chapter concludes that current integrated weed management recommendations do not account for atmospheric N as an external fertility input, potentially leading to under-application of crop competition measures at field margins near urban zones.

title: Critical load exceedances for semi-natural grassland communities in northern Serbia: a receptor-based mapping exercise
abstract: Empirical critical loads for nitrogen were assigned to seven semi-natural plant community types mapped across northern Serbia using national phytosociological databases and remote sensing land cover data. Critical load values were taken from the European Modelling and Mapping Manual (EUNIS habitats) and cross-referenced with the interpolated Vojvodina N deposition surface updated through 2020. Exceedance was calculated as deposition minus critical load for each mapped community polygon. Of 4,820 mapped polygons covering 61,400 ha of semi-natural vegetation, 34 % showed exceedance exceeding 5 kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. The most vulnerable community type was Pannonian loess grassland (Salvio-Festucetum rupicolae), for which 61 % of remaining patches were in exceedance. Spatial clustering of exceedances around Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin was confirmed by Moran's I statistic (I = 0.63, p < 0.001). These results are intended to feed into forthcoming national air quality management plans under Serbia's alignment with EU Directive 2016/2284.

title: Temporal stability of plant community composition indices along the Novi Sad nitrogen gradient: revisiting 12 transect plots after five years
abstract: Twelve fixed plots established along the main Novi Sad rural-to-urban transect in 2018 were re-surveyed in 2023 using identical Braun-Blanquet methodology in the same phenological window. The five-year interval allowed assessment of short-term floristic change under continuing elevated N deposition. Mean community Ellenberg N increased at eight of twelve plots, with the largest increases (0.4–0.6 units) at plots in the 4–8 km peri-urban zone coinciding with new residential and logistics development. Community-weighted mean specific leaf area (CWM-SLA) increased significantly at these plots (t₁₁ = 3.1, p = 0.010), indicating a shift toward fast-growing, high-resource-acquisition strategies. Shannon diversity declined at seven plots and was unchanged at five. Beta diversity between years, quantified by Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, was highest at plots with the greatest increase in deposition rather than at plots with highest absolute deposition. The results suggest that floristic responses track deposition change rather than deposition level per se, a finding with implications for monitoring design.

title: Integrating atmospheric nitrogen deposition data into weed risk maps for precision agriculture in Vojvodina: a methodological framework
abstract: This preprint outlines a GIS-based framework for producing spatially explicit weed pressure risk layers by combining atmospheric nitrogen deposition maps (derived from ALPHA sampler networks), soil nitrogen surplus estimates from national agricultural statistics, and current floristic survey data on nitrophilous weed abundance. The framework was tested in a 180 km² pilot area in the Bačka district using 2024 field season data from 34 sampling points. Weed pressure indices were calculated by summing cover-weighted Ellenberg N values per site and then modelled spatially using random forest regression with deposition, soil N, and land cover as predictors. The random forest model explained 68 % of variance in the index (out-of-bag R² = 0.68). Preliminary outputs show that areas within 5 km of the Novi Sad industrial zone and downwind of three large poultry farms present elevated weed pressure independently of farm-level fertilisation. The framework is intended for discussion with agricultural advisory services and precision agriculture technology providers at the NTP Novi Sad innovation cluster.

title: Enzyme production profiles of Trichoderma isolates with biocontrol activity: chitinase, glucanase and protease as predictive markers
abstract: Twelve Trichoderma isolates pre-selected for in vitro antagonism against Fusarium crown and root rot pathogens were tested for extracellular enzyme production. Chitinase, β-1,3-glucanase and protease activities were quantified spectrophotometrically in liquid culture supplemented with colloidal chitin, laminarin or casein as sole carbon sources. Incubation was carried out at 25 °C for 48–120 h. All three enzyme activities varied substantially among isolates. T. atroviride isolates consistently produced the highest chitinase levels (0.38–0.52 U ml⁻¹), while T. harzianum isolates showed the broadest combined enzyme profile. Pearson correlation analysis indicated a moderate positive relationship between chitinase activity and greenhouse biocontrol efficacy previously recorded for the same isolates (r = 0.68, p < 0.05), whereas glucanase and protease activities were not significant predictors. These results suggest that chitinase screening may serve as a practical secondary filter in biocontrol agent selection pipelines.

title: Cell-wall composition of wheat internodes as influenced by silicon: lignin, cellulose and hemicellulose fractions
abstract: The study quantified lignin, alpha-cellulose and hemicellulose in the cell walls of the second and third internodes of winter wheat treated with 0, 150 and 300 kg ha⁻¹ calcium silicate applied to soil before sowing. Samples were harvested at anthesis (GS65) and analysed by the Van Soest sequential fibre detergent method supplemented by the Klason lignin protocol. Total silicon in dry straw was determined by alkali fusion followed by ICP-OES. Silicon amendment increased acid-detergent lignin by 8.1 % (p < 0.05) and cellulose by 6.4 % (p < 0.05) at 300 kg ha⁻¹ relative to control, while hemicellulose fraction showed no statistically significant response. A moderate positive correlation (r = 0.54) was found between straw silicon concentration and Klason lignin across all plots. These results suggest silicon and lignin deposition are partially co-regulated during rapid internode extension, with practical implications for the timing of growth regulator applications in silicon-amended crops.

title: Pollen germination capacity of six apricot cultivars after short-duration sub-zero temperature exposure
abstract: Pollen from six apricot cultivars grown in Vojvodina orchards was collected at full bloom and subjected to controlled freezing at −1, −2, −3, and −4 °C for durations of 30, 60, and 120 minutes in a programmable freeze chamber. Germination was assessed on agar-sucrose medium after 24 h at 25 °C. At −2 °C for 60 minutes, mean germination across cultivars dropped from a control value of 74.3 % to 41.8 %, with the cultivar 'Keckemetska ruža' showing the steepest decline (68.1 % to 28.4 %) and 'Novosadska rodna' the smallest (79.2 % to 62.7 %). Pollen tube length was reduced proportionally to temperature decrease and duration. Scanning electron microscopy revealed collapsed apertures in non-viable grains. Results indicate that cultivar selection alone can mitigate germination losses by up to 34 percentage points under mild frost events, providing a practical basis for variety replacement recommendations in the region.

title: Frost damage to apricot pistils at the balloon and full-bloom stages: field and laboratory assessment
abstract: Over three consecutive springs (2009–2011) at the Rimski Šančevi research station, air temperature fell below 0 °C on 11 occasions between BBCH stage 57 and 65. Pistil samples were collected immediately before and after each event from the cultivars 'Mađarska najbolja' and 'Goldrich'. Browning of the ovule and style was scored on a 0–4 scale; fertilisation capacity was evaluated by hand-pollinating frost-exposed flowers and counting fruit set. Ovule browning scores above 2.5 correlated with fruit set below 8 %. Balloon-stage flowers (BBCH 57–59) proved 1.4 times more susceptible than open flowers at full bloom, contrary to expectations derived from central European studies. Minimum temperature, rate of temperature drop, and duration below threshold together explained 81 % of variance in ovule browning score in a multiple regression model. The data suggest that forecasting systems should weight rate of cooling rather than minimum temperature alone.

title: Microclimate variation within a flat-terrain apricot orchard during radiative frost nights
abstract: Temperature and relative humidity were logged at 15 sensor positions within a 1.2-hectare apricot orchard in Vojvodina during 22 radiative frost nights between 2011 and 2013. Sensors were placed at three canopy heights (0.3, 1.0, and 1.8 m) and three row orientations relative to the prevailing wind direction. Temperature differences of up to 1.8 °C were measured horizontally across the orchard within a single night, and vertical gradients within the canopy reached 1.2 °C. Row orientation explained 38 % of horizontal temperature variance in a mixed-effects model. Edge rows facing north-northwest consistently registered the lowest minima. These spatial patterns were not captured by the nearest agrometeorological station located 2.1 km away, indicating that on-site sensing is necessary for accurate frost-risk assessment at the orchard scale. Practical recommendations for sensor placement and selective wind-break positioning are derived.

title: In vitro pollen viability as a predictor of in vivo fruit set following natural frost events: a two-year apricot study
abstract: This study examined whether in vitro germination tests conducted within 6 hours of a frost event predict subsequent fruit set reliably enough to support management decisions. Pollen was sampled from 120 marked shoots across four cultivars on the morning after each of eight frost events during 2014 and 2015. In vitro germination was run in parallel with open-pollination fruit set counts at 35 days after full bloom. Pearson correlation between same-day in vitro germination rate and fruit set reached r = 0.74 (p < 0.001) when events with minimum temperature below −3 °C were analysed separately from milder events. For milder frosts (−0.5 to −2 °C), the correlation dropped to r = 0.41, suggesting pistil and ovule injury—not pollen failure—dominates yield loss in that temperature range. A decision chart is proposed linking in vitro germination thresholds to supplementary pollination intervention timing.

title: Anti-frost protective covers in apricot orchards: effect on pollen viability and pistil integrity
abstract: Three protective cover types—agrotextile fleece (17 g m⁻²), perforated polyethylene film, and a dual-layer reflective foil—were evaluated over two frost seasons (2015–2016) at a commercial apricot orchard near Čenej, Serbia. Covers were applied at BBCH 55 and removed at petal fall. Air temperature under covers during frost nights averaged 1.1–1.9 °C higher than uncovered controls depending on cover type. Pollen viability assessed by fluorochromatic reaction (FCR) was 63.4 % in uncovered plots versus 71.8–77.3 % under covers after the most damaging event (−2.8 °C minimum). Pistil browning scores were reduced by 38–52 % under cover treatments. Fruit set in covered rows was 2.1–2.9 times higher than in uncovered rows in the spring with three frost events. Cover application and removal cost was estimated at €280 ha⁻¹ per season at local labour rates.

title: Temporal shifts in apricot bloom date and late frost coincidence in Vojvodina, 1985–2020
abstract: Full-bloom dates for apricot recorded at three long-term monitoring sites in Vojvodina were analysed together with daily minimum temperature records for the period 1985–2020. Linear regression revealed an advance in mean full-bloom date of 6.8 days per decade. Late frost events (minimum temperature ≤ −1.5 °C occurring after 1 March) showed no significant trend in frequency but a shift toward earlier calendar dates of 3.2 days per decade, meaning the overlap between bloom and frost-risk period has increased. The probability of at least one damaging frost event during bloom increased from an estimated 24 % in the 1985–1994 decade to 41 % in 2011–2020, based on 10-day window analysis. Cultivars with later bloom phenology did not consistently escape frost because the frost-date distribution widened. The findings support the case for frost-tolerant genotype screening rather than phenological evasion as the primary adaptation strategy.

title: Cryoprotective pretreatment with proline spray and its effect on apricot pollen membrane integrity after freezing
abstract: Detached apricot branches at balloon stage were sprayed with aqueous proline solutions at 0, 5, 10, and 20 mM concentrations 18 hours before controlled freezing at −2.5 °C for 90 minutes. Pollen membrane integrity was assessed by Evans blue exclusion, FCR viability, and malondialdehyde (MDA) content as a marker of lipid peroxidation. The 10 mM proline treatment reduced MDA accumulation by 29 % relative to the water-spray control and maintained FCR viability at 68.4 % versus 49.1 % in the control. Pollen tube germination in vitro was also significantly higher after 10 mM proline treatment (58.3 % vs. 38.6 %). The 20 mM concentration showed no additional benefit and slightly depressed germination relative to 10 mM, suggesting a threshold effect. Branch re-attachment and pot-plant experiments confirmed that the treatment was deliverable via standard orchard sprayers without phytotoxic effects on leaves or petals at concentrations up to 10 mM.

title: Pollen viability screening of 22 apricot genotypes from the Novi Sad breeding collection under simulated frost stress
abstract: Twenty-two apricot genotypes held in the Faculty of Agriculture breeding collection were subjected to standardised freeze testing at −2 °C and −3 °C (90-minute exposures) during the 2019 and 2020 bloom seasons. Pollen FCR viability, agar-germination rate, and pollen tube length were measured for each genotype and each treatment in three replicates. Variation among genotypes was substantial: FCR viability after −3 °C ranged from 17.2 % to 61.8 %. Four genotypes—coded NS-07, NS-14, NS-19, and a selection from Hungarian parentage coded HU-03—consistently showed above-median viability across both temperatures and both years. Hierarchical cluster analysis grouped genotypes into three frost-tolerance classes. Correlation between −2 °C and −3 °C responses was high (r = 0.88), indicating that a single −3 °C test may suffice for screening. Results have been shared with the Faculty's apricot breeding programme as selection criteria.

title: Heat accumulation models for predicting apricot full-bloom date in the Pannonian region: calibration and validation across three sites
abstract: Four phenological models—Growing Degree Hours (GDH), Modified GDH, Utah Chill Units, and the Dynamic Model—were calibrated against observed full-bloom dates at Rimski Šančevi, Sremska Mitrovica, and Subotica over 1998–2015 and validated on the independent period 2016–2022. The Dynamic Model produced the lowest root mean square error (RMSE = 3.1 days) across all three sites in validation, followed by Modified GDH (RMSE = 4.4 days). The Utah model overestimated bloom advancement under warm winters, consistent with findings from other temperate European regions. Model outputs were combined with daily temperature forecasts from the ECMWF ensemble to generate 14-day probabilistic bloom-date forecasts. Forecast accuracy sufficient for practical frost-risk planning (±4 days) was achieved up to 9 days ahead. The calibrated Dynamic Model parameters are provided as supplementary data for use in regional agrometeorological services.

title: Combining pollen viability testing with thermal imaging to assess frost injury heterogeneity within apricot canopies
abstract: During the spring of 2023, a UAV-mounted thermal infrared camera was used to map canopy surface temperatures in a 0.8-hectare apricot block at Rimski Šančevi immediately following two frost events (−1.9 °C and −2.6 °C). Pollen and pistil samples were then collected from 96 canopy positions georeferenced to the thermal map. Positions showing canopy surface temperatures at least 0.5 °C below the block mean during the frost event had mean pollen FCR viability of 38.2 % compared with 57.4 % in warmer zones. Pistil browning scores correlated negatively with canopy surface temperature (r = −0.63, p < 0.001). The approach allowed spatial mapping of within-orchard fertility risk at a resolution not achievable with ground-based sensors alone. Integration of thermal UAV data with existing orchard management software is discussed as a practical route toward variable-rate supplementary pollination application.

title: Effect of antitranspirant kaolin particle film on apricot pistil temperature and fertilisation success under late frost conditions
abstract: Kaolin-based particle film (5 % w/v suspension) was applied as a full-canopy spray to apricot trees cv. 'Novosadska rodna' at BBCH 54–55 over two seasons (2023–2024). Pistil surface temperature was measured with contact thermocouples during frost nights; treated pistils averaged 0.3–0.5 °C warmer than untreated controls during the lowest temperature phase of the night. FCR pollen viability, pistil browning score, and final fruit set were assessed after each of four frost events. Kaolin-treated trees showed significantly higher fruit set (mean 18.4 %) compared with untreated trees (mean 12.1 %) across all four events, though the effect was statistically significant only for events with minimum temperature between −1.5 and −2.5 °C. At −3 °C, the thermal benefit was insufficient to prevent heavy pistil damage in either treatment. Reflectance measurements indicated that kaolin increased daytime canopy albedo by 0.09, with no detectable effect on leaf photosynthesis rate.

title: Pollen cryopreservation protocols for apricot frost-tolerant genotypes: viability retention over 12 months of storage
abstract: Pollen from four frost-tolerant apricot genotypes identified in earlier screening (NS-07, NS-14, NS-19, HU-03) was cryopreserved using three protocols: direct immersion in liquid nitrogen, slow cooling to −80 °C followed by liquid nitrogen transfer, and vitrification in a PVS2 solution. FCR viability and agar-germination rates were measured at 0, 3, 6, and 12 months of storage. Slow-cooling-plus-transfer protocol retained the highest viability across all genotypes at 12 months (mean FCR 71.4 %, germination 54.8 %), compared with direct immersion (FCR 64.9 %, germination 47.1 %) and vitrification (FCR 57.3 %, germination 38.2 %). Pollen from NS-19 showed the best post-storage viability under all protocols. Hand-pollination trials in spring 2025 using 12-month-stored pollen yielded fruit set rates statistically indistinguishable from fresh-pollen controls for the two best-performing protocol–genotype combinations. The study supports building a pollen bank for supplementary pollination in commercial orchards following severe frost years.

title: Abscisic acid concentrations in sweet cherry buds during natural dormancy induction in the Vojvodina region
abstract: Dormancy induction in sweet cherry (Prunus avium L.) is associated with marked shifts in endogenous abscisic acid (ABA) levels, yet data from the Pannonian climatic zone remain sparse. In this study, terminal and lateral buds were sampled weekly from six sweet cherry cultivars grown at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station between September and December over three consecutive seasons (2008–2010). ABA was quantified by HPLC with UV detection. Peak ABA concentrations reached 380–510 ng g⁻¹ fresh weight in late October across cultivars, coinciding with the completion of leaf abscission. Earlier-ripening cultivars showed a steeper ABA accumulation curve and achieved peak concentrations approximately ten days earlier than late-ripening ones. Correlations between mean daily temperature and ABA accumulation rate were significant (r = 0.74, p < 0.01) in two of three seasons. Results suggest ABA dynamics during induction are cultivar-specific and trackable with standard HPLC protocols, providing a baseline for further hormonal studies in this climatic zone.

title: Comparative polyphenol profiles of six Sambucus nigra accessions selected from the Pannonian Plain under identical orchard conditions
abstract: Six elderberry accessions maintained in a common-garden trial at the Faculty of Agriculture experimental orchard in Rimski Šančevi were evaluated over three seasons (2003–2005) for total polyphenol content (TPC), total anthocyanin content (TAC), chlorogenic acid, and DPPH radical scavenging capacity. Accessions were designated SN-PAN-01 through SN-PAN-06. TPC ranged from 523 to 1,024 mg GAE per 100 g FW. Accession SN-PAN-04 consistently exhibited the highest TAC (8.3 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside equivalents per g FW) and the strongest DPPH scavenging activity (IC50 = 0.31 mg mL−1). Chlorogenic acid was most abundant in SN-PAN-02 (5.8 mg g−1 DW). Year-to-year variation within accessions was generally smaller than between-accession variation, suggesting genetic rather than environmental factors as the primary driver of polyphenol profile in a uniform environment. The data supported selecting SN-PAN-04 for further stress physiology trials.

title: Light and moisture gradients as predictors of invasive shrub dominance along lowland riparian greenways in Serbia
abstract: We analysed vegetation data from 210 phytosociological relevés collected along 14 riparian greenway segments in lowland Serbia (Sava, Tisa, Begej, Tamiš) between 2013 and 2016. Environmental variables measured at each relevé included canopy light transmittance (LAI-2200C plant canopy analyser), volumetric soil moisture (TDR probe), distance from the waterline, and flood duration index estimated from gauging station records. Generalised linear models were used to predict cover of three focal invasive species (Amorpha fruticosa, Fallopia japonica sensu lato, Ailanthus altissima) from environmental predictors. Amorpha fruticosa cover was best predicted by flood duration (positive) and LAI (negative), explaining 41% of deviance. Fallopia cover was most strongly associated with soil moisture and proximity to human infrastructure. Ailanthus altissima dominated drier, less frequently flooded margins. These distinct niche preferences imply that different management strategies are needed for each species along the same corridor.
