title: Cache-Oblivious Data Layouts for Short-Read Alignment on Shared-Memory Multicore Systems
abstract: Short-read alignment is a memory-bandwidth-limited operation, and cache behaviour strongly influences throughput on modern multicore CPUs. We reformulated the FM-index traversal used in a widely adopted aligner to use a cache-oblivious layout derived from a van Emde Boas tree arrangement of the Burrows–Wheeler transform array. Experiments on a 32-core Intel Xeon system using 150 bp paired-end reads from a 30× human whole-genome dataset showed a 1.8× reduction in last-level cache misses and a 22 % wall-clock speedup compared to the reference implementation at equivalent accuracy. The layout adds roughly 4 % to index construction time and approximately 6 % to peak memory usage. We also measured performance on a smaller 16-core ARM server-class machine, observing a 17 % speedup, indicating the approach transfers across architectures. Profiling data are provided for three additional organisms with genome sizes ranging from 135 Mb to 2.4 Gb. The reformulated index is available as a patch against the original tool's source repository.

title: Evaluating SLURM Scheduling Policies for Mixed-Priority Genomic Workloads on a University HPC Cluster
abstract: University HPC clusters frequently host both long-running genomic assembly jobs and short, interactive variant-calling tasks submitted by clinical collaborators. We ran a six-month measurement study on a 640-core cluster at the University of Novi Sad, logging 18 400 job submissions across three user groups. We then replayed the trace under five SLURM scheduling configurations—backfill-only, priority preemption, gang scheduling, fair-share with decay factor 0.5, and a hybrid policy—using a discrete-event simulator we built in Python. The hybrid policy combining fair-share weighting with selective preemption of low-priority assembly jobs reduced median wait time for clinical variant-calling tasks from 47 minutes to 11 minutes, at the cost of a 3 % increase in total cluster makespan over the trace period. We describe configuration parameters, discuss trade-offs for clusters with heterogeneous node types, and release the simulator and anonymised job trace under an open licence.

title: Parallelisation Strategies for GATK HaplotypeCaller in Clinical Whole-Exome Sequencing Cohorts
abstract: GATK HaplotypeCaller remains a bottleneck in clinical WES pipelines because its local de novo assembly step is largely single-threaded at the per-sample level. We systematically evaluated three strategies for throughput improvement on a cohort of 412 anonymised WES samples (mean coverage 85×, 38–62 Mb target): genomic-interval scatter–gather with 100 Mb shards, sample-level parallelism across nodes, and a combination of both. Job orchestration used Snakemake with a SLURM backend. The scatter–gather approach alone reduced mean per-sample runtime from 4.1 hours to 41 minutes on 32 cores. Combining it with sample-level parallelism across 8 nodes processed the full 412-sample cohort in 19 hours wall time compared to 70 hours in the sequential baseline. We measured concordance against the baseline using precision and recall on GIAB benchmark variants: SNP precision 99.91 %, recall 99.87 %; indel precision 99.34 %, recall 99.21 %. Configuration files and Snakemake rules are provided as supplementary material.

title: Cost Modelling for Spot-Instance-Based Genomic Pipelines on Commercial Cloud Platforms
abstract: Spot and preemptible instances offer substantial per-hour cost reductions for cloud compute but introduce job interruption risk that can increase total cost when checkpointing is not implemented. We built a cost model for WGS alignment and variant-calling pipelines that incorporates hourly spot price distributions sampled over 90 days from two cloud providers, mean time to interruption distributions per instance family, and checkpoint overhead for BWA-MEM2 and GATK stages. Simulations over 500 synthetic cohort scenarios (50–1000 samples, 10×–30× coverage) showed that naive use of spot instances without checkpointing increased effective cost by 18–34 % relative to on-demand pricing in high-volatility markets. A bidding and checkpoint strategy derived from the model reduced pipeline cost by 41 % on average relative to on-demand in stable price periods. We validated the model against actual billing records from a 200-sample pilot run. The model is implemented as a Python library with a command-line interface.

title: Lossless Compression of Aligned BAM Files Using Reference-Relative Encoding of Soft-Clipped Reads
abstract: Soft-clipped bases in BAM files are stored as raw sequence and contribute disproportionately to file size in samples with adapter contamination or structural-variant-rich regions. We characterised soft-clip content in 60 WGS BAM files (mean 30× coverage, 150 bp reads) and found that soft-clipped bases account for 9–23 % of stored bases but represent only 2–6 % of aligned bases. We designed a reference-relative encoding scheme that replaces soft-clipped sequences with a compact difference representation against a local reference window, embedded within a standard BAM extension tag so that existing downstream tools read the files without modification. Across the 60-file benchmark, the scheme reduced total BAM size by 7.4 % on average with a maximum of 14.1 % in the most clip-heavy sample. Encoding and decoding add 4 % and 2 % respectively to BAM I/O time. The codec is implemented as a standalone C utility compatible with htslib.

title: Benchmarking Short-Read Aligners on Clinically Relevant Structural Variant Loci
abstract: Alignment accuracy at structural variant breakpoints affects downstream SV calling quality, yet most aligner benchmarks focus on SNPs and small indels. We constructed a synthetic benchmark dataset of 2 200 breakpoint-spanning read pairs spanning 110 curated SV loci (deletions, tandem duplications, and inversions ranging from 50 bp to 50 kb) derived from a validated clinical variant database. Four short-read aligners were evaluated: two BWT-based and two graph-based tools. We measured mapping quality distribution, soft-clip rate within 200 bp of breakpoints, and downstream SV call concordance using two SV callers. Graph-based aligners achieved 12–18 percentage point higher recall at inversion breakpoints compared to BWT-based aligners, but produced 2.3× more multimapping reads genome-wide, increasing false-positive SV calls by 9 %. Runtime and memory differences between aligner classes were substantial: graph-based alignment required 3.1× more peak RAM and 2.4× more wall time per sample. Results are tabulated per SV class and size bin.

title: Dynamic Resource Allocation for Multi-Tenant Genomic Workflow Execution Using Kubernetes and Nextflow
abstract: Research institutes increasingly run multiple concurrent genomic projects sharing the same cloud-native infrastructure. Static resource quotas lead to either underutilisation during low-demand periods or job queuing during peaks. We describe and evaluate a dynamic allocation layer sitting between Nextflow and a Kubernetes cluster, which adjusts CPU and memory requests per workflow task based on rolling estimates of per-task resource consumption drawn from a historical job database. The system was deployed on a 96-vCPU Kubernetes cluster running up to eight simultaneous WGS projects over a four-month period. Compared to static quotas tuned by an experienced administrator, the dynamic allocator reduced mean cluster idle fraction from 31 % to 11 % and cut average pipeline makespan by 19 % across 34 production runs. Memory overcommit events dropped from 6.2 % to 1.4 % of tasks. We discuss failure-mode handling and the overhead of the allocation service itself, which consumed under 0.3 % of cluster CPU on average.

title: Quantifying the Effect of Reference Genome Version Mismatches on Clinical Variant Reporting in a Diagnostic Setting
abstract: Clinical laboratories sometimes receive sequencing data aligned to GRCh37 while their reporting databases reference GRCh38, or vice versa, and liftover coordinates introduce small but non-trivial error rates. We processed 180 WES samples from a regional diagnostic laboratory three times each: aligned natively to GRCh37, aligned natively to GRCh38, and lifted over from GRCh37 to GRCh38 using a standard chain-file tool. Variant concordance between native GRCh38 and lifted-over calls was 99.61 % for SNPs and 97.83 % for indels. Discordant calls were enriched in segmental duplication regions and near microsatellite tracts. We identified 14 variants in clinically annotated disease genes that were present in native calls but absent after liftover, and 9 that appeared only after liftover due to coordinate shifts at homopolymer runs. The findings quantify a practically relevant error source and inform a simple quality-control step we recommend be added to diagnostic pipelines that accept externally aligned data.

title: Change-point localisation under irregular sampling intervals in harvester grain elevator sensor data
abstract: CAN-bus message scheduling on agricultural machines is priority-driven rather than synchronous, resulting in irregular inter-sample intervals that violate the stationarity assumptions of most change-point detection methods. This paper characterises the sampling irregularity in grain elevator load-cell and speed encoder channels (median interval 210 ms, coefficient of variation 0.41) and proposes an adaptation of the PELT algorithm using a continuous-time Ornstein-Uhlenbeck cost function to handle non-uniform sampling. The method is compared with naive application of standard PELT (assuming uniform intervals), BOCPD with Gaussian predictive distribution, and a simple linear interpolation pre-processing followed by standard PELT. Data come from six harvesters across two seasons, with 44 annotated change-point events derived from video-synchronised field observations. The OU-PELT method achieved a mean absolute localisation error of 1.8 seconds, compared to 4.1 seconds for naive PELT and 2.7 seconds for BOCPD. Computational cost of OU-PELT was approximately 3× that of standard PELT but remained under 50 ms per 1000-observation segment on a laptop CPU.

title: Impact of Coding Quality Variability on Readmission Model Fairness Across Hospitals of Different Sizes
abstract: Hospital readmission prediction models trained on pooled multi-site data may encode systematic coding quality differences between large academic centres and smaller regional hospitals, producing models that perform well on average but poorly for patients from lower-resource institutions. Using a five-site harmonised cohort (n = 28 700), this study quantified coding completeness via a proposed completeness score derived from expected code density for given diagnoses, and stratified model performance metrics by site. AUC ranged from 0.79 at the largest academic site to 0.68 at the smallest district hospital. Post-hoc reweighting of training instances by inverse completeness score narrowed this gap to 0.79 versus 0.74 with no significant change in overall AUC. Fairness-aware calibration further reduced site-level calibration discrepancy measured by expected calibration error from 0.07 to 0.04. Implications for deployment of shared readmission models in heterogeneous health systems are discussed.

title: Incorporating Protein Domain Co-occurrence Features into Graph Neural Network Drug–Target Interaction Models
abstract: Standard drug–target interaction (DTI) models based on graph neural networks typically encode proteins through sequence-derived embeddings or raw amino acid k-mer features. Protein domain composition, however, captures functionally relevant structural units that are often conserved across distantly related proteins and can be shared between otherwise dissimilar targets. We propose a domain co-occurrence feature layer that augments existing protein node representations by embedding Pfam domain pair frequencies computed from a reference proteome of 20 318 reviewed human proteins. These enriched node features are fed into an attentional graph encoder operating on a bipartite drug–protein graph. Experiments on the BindingDB filtered benchmark (17 246 interactions, 1 340 unique drugs, 762 unique targets) show that adding domain co-occurrence features improves AUROC from 0.869 to 0.891 and reduces the performance gap on low-data target classes (fewer than 10 known ligands) by 6.3 percentage points. An ablation study confirms that the gain is attributable specifically to domain co-occurrence rather than increased parameter count.

title: Упоредна анализа метода избора обележја за предикцију клиничких исхода на малим скуповима података

Коришћени су Pearson-ов коефицијент корелације, LASSO регресија, Random Forest важност обележја, рекурзивна елиминација обележја и мутуална информација. Свака метода оцењена је кроз стабилност избора (Jaccard индекс преко 50 итерација bootstrap узорковања) и утицај на AUROC логистичке регресије на истим скуповима. title: Characterisation of shear viscosity and pressure–volume–temperature behaviour of a glass-filled polyamide 66 for injection moulding simulation
abstract: Accurate rheological input data are a prerequisite for reliable mould-filling simulations. This study reports systematic capillary rheometer measurements of a 30 wt% glass-fibre-reinforced PA66 across shear rates from 10 to 10 000 s⁻¹ at 270, 280, and 290 °C. A five-constant Cross–WLF model was fitted to the data, yielding a mean deviation of 2.8% against measurements. PVT curves were recorded with a piston-die dilatometer over pressures up to 180 MPa, and the modified Tait equation parameters were determined. Both datasets were incorporated into Moldex3D simulations of a stepped-wall test cavity. Predicted fill pressure at the gate matched injection press measurements within 6% across 27 combinations of melt temperature and injection speed. The fitted rheological and PVT coefficients are reported in tabular form to support reproducible simulation studies by other groups working with the same commercial compound.

title: Influence of packing pressure profile on sink-mark depth in thick polypropylene plaques: experiment and simulation
abstract: Sink marks on the visible surfaces of thick injection-moulded parts represent a recurrent quality problem in consumer-goods applications. Twelve polypropylene plaques of 12 mm nominal wall thickness were produced on a 120-tonne machine using a three-stage packing profile, with peak packing pressures ranging from 40 to 90 MPa and packing times from 8 to 20 s. Sink-mark depth was measured with a contact profilometer at five defined positions. Sigmasoft simulations replicating each set of process conditions predicted sink depths within 0.08 mm RMS error. A second-order response-surface model constructed from the simulation results identified packing pressure in the first stage as the dominant factor, reducing sink depth by approximately 0.35 mm per 10 MPa increase above 60 MPa. The study provides a validated simulation workflow for industrial tooling departments working with polypropylene grades of similar melt-flow index.

title: Comparative assessment of three generalised Newtonian models for describing flow of high-density polyethylene melts at industrially relevant shear rates
abstract: Three constitutive models—Cross–WLF, Carreau–Yasuda, and Ellis—were fitted to capillary rheometer data for a pipe-grade HDPE at 190, 210, and 230 °C, using data from 48 experimental runs. Fitting was performed via nonlinear least-squares minimisation; goodness-of-fit was evaluated using adjusted R² and root mean squared log-error. The Cross–WLF model achieved the best overall performance (mean RMSLE 0.031), followed by Carreau–Yasuda (0.039) and Ellis (0.051), particularly at shear rates above 3 000 s⁻¹. Each model was also used to drive a 3D mould-filling simulation of a ring-gate disc cavity with a 6 mm wall. Predicted melt-front arrival times at four pressure transducer positions were compared to measurements. Cross–WLF and Carreau–Yasuda gave equivalent predictive accuracy for the filling stage; differences became evident only during the packing stage when pressure gradients exceeded 80 MPa/m.

title: Gate location and number effects on warpage and fibre orientation in injection-moulded glass-filled polypropylene housings
abstract: Warpage in glass-filled thermoplastic housings is governed by anisotropic shrinkage linked to fibre orientation distributions that develop during filling. A 2.5 mm average wall-thickness housing part intended for an electrical junction box was modelled in Moldex3D. Seventeen gate configurations, varying in number (one to four gates) and location, were simulated under a fixed processing window (melt temperature 240 °C, mould temperature 40 °C, injection time 1.8 s). Fibre orientation tensors were extracted at 15 critical cross-sections. Maximum out-of-plane displacement ranged from 0.61 mm for a single edge gate to 0.19 mm for a balanced four-gate arrangement. Three configurations were manufactured and measured on a CMM; predicted versus measured maximum displacement agreed within 0.04 mm. The study demonstrates a structured simulation-first gate selection methodology reducing physical trials by an estimated factor of four.

title: Measurement and modelling of elongational viscosity of polystyrene melts using a converging-die capillary attachment
abstract: Elongational flow contributions are significant in regions of high contraction ratio near gates and runners, yet they are rarely incorporated into industrial simulation workflows. This work used a converging-die attachment (half-angle 45°) mounted on a Göttfert Rheograph 6000 to estimate apparent elongational viscosity of a general-purpose polystyrene at four temperatures between 200 and 230 °C. The Cogswell analysis was applied to pressure-drop data from dies with L/D ratios of 0, 10, and 30. Elongational viscosity at a Trouton ratio above 100 was observed over extension rates from 10 to 800 s⁻¹. Simulation runs using a Rolie–Poly constitutive model augmented with the measured elongational data reduced gate-pressure prediction error from 9.1% to 3.6% compared to a purely shear-based model for a fan-gate flat plate.

title: Weld-line strength in thick-section acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene parts: effect of melt temperature and injection speed
abstract: Weld lines in injection-moulded parts act as stress concentrators whose severity depends on the thermal and rheological state of the melt at the point of confluence. Tensile bars of 8 mm thickness were moulded from ABS in a two-gate tool designed to force weld-line formation at the bar centre. Melt temperature was varied from 220 to 260 °C in 10 °C steps; injection speed from 20 to 80 mm/s. Tensile strength and elongation at break were measured for 180 specimens. A 20 °C rise in melt temperature increased weld-line strength by an average of 11%, while injection speed showed a weaker and non-monotonic effect. Mould-filling simulations correctly ranked all 20 experimental conditions by predicted weld-line temperature, confirming that the melt temperature at confluence, rather than the speed, is the primary governing variable accessible to the moulder.

title: Optimisation of process parameters for a 15 mm wall-thickness polycarbonate optical block using Design of Experiments and CAE simulation
abstract: Optical-quality polycarbonate parts with walls thicker than 10 mm are prone to internal voids, residual stress birefringence, and surface sink marks that cannot all be minimised simultaneously. A three-level Box–Behnken design with five factors—melt temperature, mould temperature, injection speed, first-stage packing pressure, and packing time—was executed in simulation (Moldex3D) for a 15 mm rectangular block geometry. Responses were maximum sink depth, maximum principal residual stress, and predicted internal void volume fraction. Pareto-optimal solutions were identified via weighted desirability. Two candidate parameter sets were physically verified: defect measurements agreed with predictions within 7% for all three responses. The recommended conditions (melt 295 °C, mould 100 °C, packing 85 MPa, 22 s) reduced sink depth by 58% and residual stress by 31% relative to the manufacturer's nominal settings.

title: Thermal conductivity of semi-crystalline polymer melts under pressure: measurement protocol and implications for mould-cooling simulation accuracy
abstract: Mould-cooling simulations rely on thermal conductivity values that are typically taken from ambient-pressure, room-temperature tabulations and held constant throughout the simulation. This study measured the thermal conductivity of isotactic polypropylene and polyoxymethylene in the melt state at pressures from 0.1 to 150 MPa using a custom needle-probe cell mounted in a high-pressure autoclave. Thermal conductivity increased by 18% for PP and 22% for POM over this pressure range. Incorporation of pressure-dependent conductivity functions into Sigmasoft mould-cooling simulations reduced the discrepancy between predicted and measured part-ejection temperatures from 8.3 °C to 2.1 °C on average across 32 moulding trials. The paper provides fitted polynomial coefficients for both materials and discusses the relative importance of this correction compared to uncertainties in mould-steel conductivity and coolant flow rate.

title: Crystallisation kinetics of isotactic polypropylene under fast cooling and elevated pressure: a combined DSC and high-pressure dilatometry study
abstract: Injection moulding exposes polymer melts to cooling rates and pressures that are far removed from standard DSC conditions, yet crystallisation models embedded in simulation codes are frequently calibrated only on atmospheric-pressure DSC data. In this study, differential scanning calorimetry was performed at cooling rates from 5 to 80 °C/min, and high-pressure dilatometry captured specific volume changes at pressures of 20, 60, and 120 MPa for an isotactic PP homopolymer with MFI of 12 g/10 min. The Nakamura crystallisation model was extended with a pressure shift factor determined from the dilatometry data. When this extended model replaced the standard atmospheric model in Moldex3D, predicted crystallinity distributions across a 10 mm plaque cross-section matched micro-CT density maps within 3.5% at all three pressure levels tested, compared to 12% error with the unmodified model.

title: Residual stress measurement in injection-moulded thick polycarbonate discs by layer removal and comparison with simulation
abstract: Through-thickness residual stress profiles in thick injection-moulded optical components influence part performance during service, particularly in applications involving temperature cycling. Polycarbonate discs of 20 mm thickness were produced at three mould temperatures (80, 100, 120 °C) and two packing pressures (60 and 90 MPa). The layer-removal method was applied: successive layers of approximately 0.5 mm were machined from one face while surface curvature was recorded with a coordinate measuring arm, and the Bernoulli-beam inverse calculation was used to recover stress profiles. Compressive stresses up to −18 MPa were found near both surfaces, with a tensile core peak of +12 MPa at 100 °C mould temperature. Sigmasoft thermo-viscoelastic simulations reproduced the profile shape and the location of the compressive-to-tensile transition within 0.7 mm. Mould temperature increase from 80 to 120 °C reduced surface compressive stress magnitude by 38%.

title: Simulation-assisted troubleshooting of short-shot defects in a multi-cavity tool for a fibre-reinforced polyamide structural bracket
abstract: A four-cavity injection moulding tool producing 30% glass-fibre PA66 structural brackets for the automotive supply chain exhibited intermittent short shots in cavities 3 and 4 under production conditions. Dimensional inspection of the manifold system revealed runner diameter deviations of up to 0.4 mm from nominal, introduced during tool regrind. Moldex3D simulations with measured runner geometries predicted a 12% flow imbalance between cavity pairs, consistent with the observed defect pattern. A corrective runner balancing strategy was evaluated in simulation and subsequently implemented by a tool-making partner; post-correction production trials confirmed elimination of short shots over a 2 000-cycle verification run. The paper describes the measurement protocol, the simulation methodology, and the iterative correction procedure, providing a transferable template for multi-cavity tool diagnosis.

title: Sensitivity of mould-filling simulation predictions to melt-temperature measurement method: thermocouple position and air-shot protocol effects
abstract: The melt temperature specified in injection moulding simulation is typically the set temperature of the barrel, whereas the actual melt temperature entering the cavity can differ by 10–25 °C due to viscous dissipation in the screw and nozzle. This study compared five melt-temperature measurement strategies—barrel set-point, nozzle contact thermocouple, air-shot pyrometer at three distances, and an instrumented nozzle—for three materials (PP, ABS, PA6) across a combined 108 experimental conditions. Measured temperatures fed into Moldex3D; sensitivity of predicted filling pressure, melt-front arrival time, and weld-line temperature to input method was quantified. For thick-section parts (≥8 mm), a 15 °C error in input melt temperature propagated to a 9.4% error in predicted packing pressure requirement. Recommendations are given for choosing a measurement method depending on part thickness and available instrumentation.

title: Injection moulding of thick-section thermoplastic parts: process fundamentals, defect mechanisms, and simulation methods
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of the physical phenomena governing injection moulding of parts with wall thicknesses above 6 mm, a regime in which standard thin-wall assumptions embedded in most commercial simulation codes become inadequate. The chapter covers melt rheology and its characterisation, packing and holding stage mechanics, crystallisation and solidification in the core, and the origin of defects including sink marks, internal voids, warpage, and residual stress. Simulation approaches are reviewed with emphasis on the transition from 2.5D Hele–Shaw solvers to full 3D finite-volume methods. Case studies drawn from the authors' laboratory illustrate validation procedures and the quantitative accuracy that can be expected from current commercial tools. A section on process parameter selection strategies discusses how Design of Experiments and response-surface methods can be integrated with CAE workflows. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and practising engineers entering the field.

title: Effect of mould-wall temperature non-uniformity on warpage and sink-mark formation in thick polycarbonate lenses: simulation and infrared thermography study
abstract: Variations in mould-surface temperature caused by uneven coolant distribution are rarely accounted for in injection moulding simulation, where uniform wall temperature boundary conditions are standard. In this study, infrared thermography of an open mould recorded peak-to-peak temperature non-uniformities of up to 14 °C across the cavity face during a 60 mm thick polycarbonate lens trial. These measured temperature maps were imported as spatially distributed boundary conditions into Sigmasoft simulations. Compared to a uniform-temperature simulation, the non-uniform model reduced warpage prediction error from 0.31 mm to 0.09 mm and sink-depth prediction error from 0.12 mm to 0.04 mm when validated against three physical samples. Sensitivity analysis showed that non-uniformities above 8 °C have a statistically significant effect on warpage even for this highly symmetric geometry. The methodology requires only a commercial infrared camera and standard simulation post-processing and can be applied without hardware changes to existing tools.

title: Mapping process parameter windows to porosity in Ti-6Al-4V LPBF: implications for topology-optimised thin-wall features
abstract: A systematic variation of laser power (250–380 W) and scan speed (900–1400 mm/s) was conducted on 5 mm cubic coupons of Ti-6Al-4V to map volumetric energy density against relative density measured by Archimedes weighing and optical metallography. A total of 36 parameter combinations were evaluated in triplicate. Relative density above 99.5 % was achieved in a band of energy densities between 55 and 75 J/mm³. Single-wall specimens of thickness 0.6–1.2 mm were then produced at selected parameter sets to assess whether process windows derived from bulk coupons transfer to thin-wall geometries typical of topology-optimised brackets. Wall thickness below 0.8 mm showed a systematic 1.8 percentage-point reduction in relative density compared to bulk predictions, attributed to increased heat dissipation at free surfaces. Corrected parameter recommendations for thin-wall regions are provided and their effect on bracket mass and mechanical stiffness is quantified through three build experiments.

title: Informal Guarantee Networks as Substitutes for Credit Rating Agencies: Evidence from Small Enterprises in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper investigates how small enterprises in Vojvodina access bank credit in the absence of reliable credit-scoring intermediaries. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 34 firm owners and loan officers conducted in 2011–2012, and supplemented by loan file data from two regional cooperative banks, the study documents a recurring pattern in which personal guarantor networks—composed of family members, business acquaintances, and local notables—serve as de facto reputation-signalling devices. Logistic regression on 218 loan applications shows that the presence of at least two non-family guarantors increases approval probability by 31 percentage points, controlling for firm size, sector, and collateral value. The pattern is most pronounced among firms founded after 1995, suggesting that institutional legacies of socialist-era state banking weaken but do not eliminate the reliance on informal social structures. The findings contribute to the institutional voids literature by specifying a mechanism through which relationship-based substitutes emerge organically without organised intermediary industries.

title: Personal Brokers in Agricultural Commodity Trade: A Case Study of the Bačka Wheat Market
abstract: Formal commodity exchanges for grain in Serbia collapsed in the early 2000s, leaving producers and processors without price-discovery and contract-enforcement intermediaries. This case study traces how a stratum of individual brokers—locally called 'menadžeri žita'—emerged to fill this gap in the Bačka sub-region between 2003 and 2013. Using archival records from the Regional Chamber of Commerce, 22 broker interviews, and nine buyer–seller dyad interviews, the study reconstructs broker role sets: price negotiation, informal contract witnessing, dispute mediation, and reputation certification. Brokers charge margins of 1.5–3% per transaction and sustain their position through multi-year relationship investments rather than licensing or formal accreditation. The paper situates these actors within Khanna and Palepu's institutional voids framework and extends it by showing that personal brokers can remain stable over a decade without formalising, provided switching costs remain high. Implications for agricultural policy and market design are discussed.

title: When Chambers of Commerce Become Social Clubs: Associational Substitution for Regulatory Bodies in Post-Socialist Serbia
abstract: This paper examines whether business associations can substitute for weak regulatory bodies in product quality certification. The empirical focus is on the wood-processing sector in southern Serbia, where the state technical standards agency has been chronically under-resourced since 1995. Through 41 interviews with firm managers, association staff, and ministry officials, and content analysis of 120 association newsletters from 2000 to 2014, the study finds that three regional branch associations have developed informal certification routines—including peer audits, collective marks, and blacklisting—that partially replace state functions. However, these routines are unevenly applied: firms with tighter social ties to association leadership receive more lenient treatment. The study concludes that associational substitutes reduce average transaction costs but introduce systematic favouritism, producing a second-order institutional problem. This finding qualifies optimistic accounts of civil society organisations as neutral void-fillers in transition economies.

title: Network Closure and Opportunism in Markets Without Enforcement: Evidence from a Survey of 312 Serbian SMEs
abstract: This paper uses original survey data collected in 2015 from 312 SMEs across five Serbian industries to test competing predictions about network closure and opportunism. Standard social capital theory predicts that dense, closed networks reduce opportunism by making defection visible and costly. Institutional voids theory predicts that when state enforcement is absent, network density becomes a necessary but insufficient deterrent because it coexists with resource scarcity pressures. Structural equation modelling reveals that network closure is negatively associated with reported contract breach (β = −0.28, p < 0.01) but that this effect is moderated by firm financial distress: among distressed firms, closure loses significance, suggesting that desperation overrides reputational constraints. The survey achieved a 61% response rate after two follow-up rounds. The results have implications for understanding why informal enforcement mechanisms observed in stable times may break down during economic shocks.

title: Diaspora Networks as Market Information Intermediaries: Serbian Export SMEs and Their Western European Contacts
abstract: This conference paper presents preliminary findings from an ongoing interview study of 18 Serbian manufacturing SMEs that export to Germany and Austria. The firms in the sample consistently lack access to formal market research services, trade credit insurers, and foreign buyer certification agencies—classic institutional voids at the internationalisation interface. In their place, diaspora contacts—relatives and former colleagues living in Germany and Austria—provide market intelligence, buyer vetting, and informal warranty of payment. The paper maps these diaspora roles onto a typology of intermediary functions drawn from the marketing channels literature. Preliminary analysis suggests that diaspora contacts are more commonly used for buyer vetting than for logistics or after-sales, and that this concentration creates bottlenecks when the contact has limited sectoral expertise. The paper calls for comparative work across diaspora corridors with different density and professional composition.

title: Relational Contracting in Romanian and Serbian Food Processing: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: This book chapter compares relational contracting practices in the food processing sectors of Romania and Serbia, two post-socialist economies that underwent EU accession (Romania in 2007) and EU candidate status (Serbia since 2012) along different timelines. Using 56 firm interviews collected in 2017–2018 and matched archival data on sector association activities, the chapter shows that Romanian food processors have partially formalised their relational contracts through EU-harmonised standards, while Serbian counterparts rely more heavily on handshake agreements backed by personal reputation. Despite this divergence, both country samples exhibit similar patterns of long-term exclusive supplier relationships that substitute for commodity spot markets. The chapter argues that the speed and depth of formal institutional development—rather than the mere fact of EU orientation—determines whether informal relational structures persist or are absorbed into formal contracting. Methodological notes on cross-country qualitative comparison are included.

title: Community Reputation Systems in the Absence of Online Rating Platforms: Evidence from Serbian Provincial Service Markets
abstract: Online reputation platforms such as customer review aggregators are sparsely used among micro-service providers in smaller Serbian cities. This paper asks what functional equivalent operates in their absence. Drawing on 290 structured interviews with consumers and 48 provider interviews in three provincial cities (Subotica, Sombor, Zrenjanin) conducted in 2019–2020, it documents a community reputation system based on referral chains: satisfied customers actively refer others, embedding quality signals in social ties rather than on public digital platforms. Probit models show that receipt of a personal referral increases the probability of first-time service purchase by 44 percentage points and reduces post-purchase dissatisfaction complaints by 29% compared to spontaneous market entry. The paper also finds that referral chain length—number of intermediary nodes—weakens the quality signal: referred customers three steps from the original source show dissatisfaction rates indistinguishable from walk-in customers. These results point to the geographic and social limits of informal reputation systems.

title: Institutional Voids and Startup Ecosystem Intermediaries: Do Technology Parks Fill the Gap?
abstract: Technology parks and incubators have been proposed as deliberate solutions to institutional voids facing technology startups, but empirical assessments of this claim are limited in post-socialist contexts. This paper studies whether NTP-type science and technology park tenancy substantively substitutes for absent legal, financial, and market-development intermediaries. Survey data from 94 technology park tenants and 87 non-tenant startups in Serbia collected in 2021–2022 are used in propensity-score-matched comparisons across six intermediary functions: legal advice, investor matching, talent recruitment, customer referral, supplier vetting, and technology licensing. Park tenancy is significantly associated with better access to legal advice (p < 0.01) and investor matching (p < 0.05) but shows no significant effect on customer referral or supplier vetting, which tenants continue to handle through informal personal networks. The finding suggests that formalised intermediary organisations address some voids selectively, leaving others intact, and that informal network practices persist even among formally supported firms.

title: Do Informal Networks Crowd Out Formal Intermediary Development? A Longitudinal Perspective on Serbian Factor Markets, 2000–2024
abstract: A recurrent hypothesis in institutional economics holds that well-functioning informal substitutes reduce the political and economic pressure to develop formal market intermediaries, thereby locking economies into informal equilibria. This working paper tests this hypothesis using a longitudinal dataset assembled from three rounds of enterprise surveys (2005, 2013, 2022) covering 460 Serbian firms that could be tracked across at least two waves. Fixed-effects panel models show that firms with higher informal network scores in 2005 were not significantly less likely to use formal intermediary services—credit bureaus, certified auditors, licensed brokers—in 2013 or 2022, once firm growth and sector are controlled for. If anything, the coefficient is weakly positive, consistent with a complementarity rather than a substitution dynamic. The paper discusses methodological challenges in constructing a comparable informality measure across waves and outlines directions for causal identification.

title: Post-Pandemic Demand Recovery Trajectories and Repricing Strategies in Urban Hotels: Evidence from Four Serbian Cities
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic produced an unprecedented and heterogeneous demand shock in urban hotel markets. Using daily administrative revenue data from 31 hotels in Belgrade, Novi Sad, Kragujevac, and Niš for the period January 2019 to December 2022, this paper estimates city-specific demand recovery curves and evaluates whether hotels that adopted aggressive repricing during the trough phase recovered faster than those that maintained pre-pandemic rate levels. A synthetic control method is applied to construct counterfactual recovery paths for each property. Results show that hotels that cut average daily rates by more than 20% during the trough recovered to 90% of pre-pandemic RevPAR roughly 4.2 months earlier on average, but at a cost of sustained brand dilution measurable in online review scores 18 months later. The trade-off between short-run occupancy gains and longer-run reputation effects is quantified and discussed.

title: Managerial Cognition and Realised Absorptive Capacity: Micro-Level Evidence from Cross-Border Ventures in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper bridges managerial cognition theory and the absorptive capacity literature by investigating how the mental models of senior managers shape the degree to which cross-border joint ventures in Vojvodina actually exploit external knowledge. Semi-structured interviews with 31 managers across 18 ventures in the ICT, agri-food, and rubber-and-plastics sectors were conducted during 2018–2019. Grounded theory coding yielded four cognitive archetypes—'gatekeepers', 'translators', 'accumulators', and 'resistors'—which differ systematically in their tolerance for knowledge ambiguity and their strategic framing of the partner relationship. Ventures led by 'translator'-type managers showed the highest scores on a realised absorptive capacity scale developed for the study, while 'resistor' archetypes were disproportionately present in ventures that formally dissolved within three years. The findings suggest that managerial selection and training programmes targeting cognitive flexibility could have measurable effects on venture-level learning outcomes independent of firm size or sector.

title: Science–Industry Linkages at the NTP Novi Sad Ecosystem: Absorptive Capacity Bottlenecks among Resident SMEs
abstract: This working paper reports preliminary findings from a structured survey of 41 SMEs resident at the Science Technology Park Novi Sad, conducted in late 2024 and early 2025, aimed at diagnosing absorptive capacity constraints that limit their engagement with university R&D partners. The survey instrument covers five domains: R&D expenditure as a share of turnover, human capital qualification, internal knowledge management practices, prior collaboration history, and managerial awareness of available EU co-funding instruments. Descriptive statistics and cluster analysis identify three firm archetypes: 'capacity-ready' (22 percent of sample), 'structurally constrained' (41 percent), and 'awareness-limited' (37 percent). The 'awareness-limited' cluster scores above average on R&D expenditure and qualification metrics but reports very low familiarity with Horizon Europe partnership instruments and with existing university technology transfer services. Results suggest that targeted brokerage and awareness-raising activities, rather than further subsidy provision, would be the most cost-effective intervention for a substantial share of NTP resident firms.

title: Flat structures and the erosion of implicit promises: a qualitative study of agile software teams
abstract: Based on 34 semi-structured interviews with developers, Scrum masters, and product owners in five agile software companies in Novi Sad conducted in 2016, this study examines how the removal of formal managerial layers reshapes the psychological contract. Thematic analysis identified three recurring tensions: (1) ambiguity about who holds the employer role in the contract, (2) a shift from career-advancement promises to autonomy-and-learning promises, and (3) heightened sensitivity to peer behaviour as a proxy for organisational fairness. Participants frequently described the organisation as an abstract collective rather than a personified authority, complicating the attribution of breach. The findings extend psychological contract theory to flat, team-centric structures by proposing the concept of distributed contract agency, where obligations are perceived as distributed across multiple actors rather than concentrated in a single employer entity. Implications for HR design in self-managing organisations are discussed.

title: Psychological safety, contract breach, and voice behaviour in flat technology firms: a multi-source study
abstract: This multi-source study combines employee self-reports with team-leader ratings to examine whether psychological safety moderates the relationship between contract breach and voice behaviour in flat technology firms. Data were collected from 178 employee–leader dyads in fourteen technology companies at the NTP Novi Sad and the Belgrade Innovation Centre in early 2025. Team leaders independently rated each employee's voice behaviour using a five-item scale, reducing common method bias. SEM results indicated that breach reduced employee voice (β = −0.30, p < 0.001) and that psychological safety moderated this effect: at one standard deviation above the safety mean the breach–voice path was attenuated to β = −0.12 (p = 0.09). The interaction was significant (ΔR² = 0.04, p < 0.05). The paper contributes evidence that safety climates can partially preserve constructive employee behaviour even when contract breach has occurred, and offers guidance for team-level management practice in project-based organisations.

title: Design and Experimental Validation of a 3 kW LLC Resonant Converter for Lead-Acid Battery Charging
abstract: This paper presents the design procedure and experimental characterisation of a 3 kW half-bridge LLC resonant converter intended for stationary lead-acid battery charging. The resonant tank parameters were selected using a first-harmonic approximation (FHA) model, with the resonant frequency set at 120 kHz and the quality factor Q constrained to 0.35 to maintain soft switching across the full load range of 10–100 %. A custom planar transformer wound on an N87 ferrite core was used to minimise leakage inductance variability. Measured full-load efficiency at the nominal 48 V output was 95.1 %. Switching waveforms confirmed zero-voltage switching (ZVS) on primary MOSFETs across all test conditions. Temperature rise measurements under continuous operation at 25 °C ambient showed a maximum core temperature of 68 °C. The paper also quantifies the deviation between FHA predictions and measured voltage gain, which reaches up to 4.2 % near the boundaries of the operating range.

title: Frequency-Domain Modelling of Core Loss in Ferrite Inductors Under Non-Sinusoidal Excitation
abstract: Accurate core loss prediction in resonant converter magnetics requires moving beyond the classical Steinmetz equation, which assumes purely sinusoidal flux waveforms. This work applies the improved generalised Steinmetz equation (iGSE) and a recently proposed duty-cycle-corrected extension to N87 and 3C95 ferrite cores under trapezoidal and clipped-sinusoidal flux excitations representative of LLC operation. Loss measurements were performed calorimetrically on toroidal samples at frequencies from 80 kHz to 400 kHz and peak flux densities from 20 mT to 150 mT. The iGSE model overestimated losses by 11–17 % compared to calorimetric data when the flux waveform contained significant third-harmonic content; the duty-cycle-corrected variant reduced this error to below 5 % across 85 % of the tested operating points. Steinmetz coefficients extracted from sinusoidal measurements at 100 kHz were found to be inadequate for extrapolation above 250 kHz. The results provide a practical guideline for magnetic component selection in medium-power resonant stages.

title: Comparison of Half-Bridge and Full-Bridge LLC Topologies for a 5 kW Bidirectional Energy Storage Interface
abstract: Bidirectional isolated DC-DC converters for lithium-ion energy storage require the ability to operate in both charging and discharging modes while maintaining soft switching. This study compares half-bridge and full-bridge LLC implementations at a 5 kW power level with a 400 V high-voltage bus and a 48 V battery-side bus. The CLLC variant, which adds a secondary resonant capacitor to symmetrise the gain curve, is included as a third candidate. Each topology was prototyped using 600 V CoolMOS devices on the primary and synchronous rectification with 80 V MOSFETs on the secondary. Efficiency was measured across the full load range in both power flow directions. The full-bridge CLLC achieved the highest reverse-mode efficiency (94.6 % at rated load) but required more precise dead-time control to avoid loss of ZVS at light loads below 15 %. A normalised loss breakdown attributing contributions to switching, conduction, and magnetic losses is presented for each topology at three representative operating points.

title: Impact of GaN HEMT Output Capacitance Nonlinearity on ZVS Boundary Prediction in Resonant Converters
abstract: Zero-voltage switching boundary calculations in LLC converters conventionally treat MOSFET output capacitance Coss as a fixed value. Gallium nitride HEMTs exhibit a strongly voltage-dependent Coss that can vary by a factor of 8 between 0 V and 400 V. This paper quantifies the error introduced by the fixed-capacitance assumption when designing resonant tanks for GaN-based primary switches. A 650 V, 35 A GaN HEMT from a commercial supplier was characterised using a Keysight E4990A impedance analyser from 1 kHz to 10 MHz at drain-source voltages from 0 V to 600 V. The equivalent linear capacitance concept was applied to extract an energy-equivalent Coss for use in tank design equations. Simulations in LTspice XVII were validated against a 2 kW prototype operating at 200 kHz. Using the energy-equivalent Coss reduced the ZVS boundary prediction error from 18 % to 3.5 % compared to the datasheet value. Practical design guidelines for adjusting dead time as a function of load current are proposed.

title: Analytical Loss Model for the Transformer Winding of an LLC Converter Accounting for Proximity and Skin Effects
abstract: Winding losses in high-frequency transformers are underestimated when DC resistance alone is used. This paper develops an analytical model based on the Dowell method, extended to account for round-wire layers and interleaved winding arrangements, and applies it to the transformer of a 3.5 kW, 150 kHz LLC converter. Winding loss was measured calorimetrically by subtracting core losses (evaluated from separate ring-sample measurements) from total magnetic component losses. At full load, the Dowell-based model predicted winding loss within 6 % of the measured value; a simplified approach using only DC resistance underestimated losses by 31 %. An optimisation procedure minimising total winding loss by adjusting the number of layers and strand diameter is demonstrated, resulting in a 2.1 °C reduction in steady-state winding temperature at rated output. The model is implemented as a spreadsheet tool and is made available as supplementary material.

title: Resonant Converters for Isolated DC-DC Stages in Battery Systems
abstract: This book chapter surveys resonant converter topologies—series resonant, parallel resonant, LLC, CLLC, and LCC—with an emphasis on their applicability to isolated DC-DC stages in battery energy storage systems rated between 1 kW and 20 kW. The chapter covers the derivation of voltage gain characteristics using both FHA and exact time-domain methods, discusses the conditions under which FHA introduces unacceptable errors, and presents design trade-offs between switching frequency range, transformer turns ratio, and resonant tank component tolerances. Control strategies including frequency modulation, phase-shift modulation, and burst-mode operation at light loads are reviewed. Representative efficiency data from published prototypes are tabulated and discussed in the context of application requirements for grid-connected and off-grid battery interfaces. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and practising engineers entering the field.

title: Thermal Management of a 10 kW CLLC Converter for Grid-Coupled Battery Storage: Modelling and Measurements
abstract: A 10 kW CLLC converter prototype was built using 650 V GaN HEMTs on the primary side and 100 V SiC Schottky diodes on the secondary, targeting a 400 V / 96 V isolated interface for a lithium iron phosphate battery bank. Thermal modelling was performed using a lumped-element RC network calibrated against infrared camera measurements taken at five steady-state operating points. The thermal model correctly predicted junction temperatures within 4 °C across all operating conditions. Under continuous rated-load operation with forced-air cooling at 2 m/s, the hottest device (primary GaN HEMT) reached 94 °C junction temperature. An empirical correlation between switching loss, dead time, and junction temperature was established by varying dead time from 40 ns to 200 ns. Reducing dead time below 80 ns restored ZVS at 20 % load but increased turn-off losses, raising steady-state junction temperature by 7 °C. The paper concludes with a procedure for selecting dead time as a function of load to balance ZVS maintenance against thermal stress.

title: Effect of DC Bias on Resonant Inductance and Quality Factor in LLC Converters for Supercapacitor Interfaces
abstract: Supercapacitor terminal voltage varies continuously from near 0 V to full rated voltage during charge and discharge cycles. When an LLC converter is used at the supercapacitor interface, the secondary-side current can introduce a DC bias component into the resonant inductance under partial-resonance operating modes, shifting the resonant frequency by up to 9 % and degrading the quality factor. This study characterises this effect on three inductors wound on different core materials (N87 ferrite, amorphous ribbon, and nanocrystalline) using a combination of impedance analyser measurements and LTspice simulations incorporating a Jiles–Atherton permeability model. Measurements were taken at DC bias currents from 0 A to 12 A and small-signal AC frequencies from 80 kHz to 300 kHz. The nanocrystalline core showed the smallest resonant frequency shift (1.8 %) and the best retention of quality factor under bias. Practical guidelines for air-gap selection to limit frequency deviation below 3 % across the supercapacitor voltage range are provided.

title: Parameterisation of an Extended Describing Function Model for CLLC Converters Using Impedance Analyser Measurements
abstract: The extended describing function (EDF) is a widely used small-signal model for resonant converters, but its accuracy depends critically on the accuracy of the resonant tank parameters. This paper demonstrates a measurement-based parameterisation procedure in which the resonant capacitance, resonant inductance, and transformer magnetising inductance are extracted from impedance analyser scans performed on the fully assembled converter board, rather than relying on component datasheet values or separate bench measurements of individual components. Measurements were made on a 5 kW CLLC converter operating between 90 kHz and 180 kHz. The procedure accounts for PCB trace inductances, interconnect capacitances, and winding inter-winding capacitance, all of which become significant above 100 kHz. Using the measured parameters reduced the error in the predicted control-to-output frequency response from 9.6 dB to 1.8 dB at the gain crossover frequency. A step-by-step measurement protocol is presented that can be applied without circuit disassembly.

title: Loss Partitioning in a 7 kW Bidirectional CLLC Stage for a Second-Life Battery Pack
abstract: Second-life lithium-ion battery packs repurposed from electric vehicles exhibit a wider terminal voltage range and higher internal resistance spread than new cells, placing additional demands on the DC-DC interface converter. This paper reports a detailed loss partitioning study on a 7 kW bidirectional CLLC stage designed for a second-life pack with a nominal voltage of 72 V and an operating range of 55–88 V. Losses were separated into switching losses (measured via double-pulse test), conduction losses (derived from on-state resistance measurements at operating temperature), and magnetic losses (calorimetric method). At full load in forward mode, total converter loss was 218 W, with magnetic losses contributing 38 %, primary switching losses 29 %, secondary conduction losses 21 %, and gate drive and auxiliary supply 12 %. Across the battery voltage range, total loss varied by ±19 % relative to the nominal operating point. Frequency schedules that minimise total loss as a function of instantaneous battery voltage are computed and compared against constant-frequency and fixed-frequency-with-phase-shift strategies.

title: Sensitivity of LLC Converter Efficiency to Resonant Tank Component Tolerances: A Monte Carlo Study
abstract: Resonant tank components—capacitors and inductors—carry manufacturing tolerances that shift the resonant frequency and quality factor away from their designed values. This paper presents a Monte Carlo analysis of the impact of ±5 % and ±10 % tolerance bands on resonant capacitance and inductance on the efficiency and ZVS coverage of a 3 kW LLC converter operating at a nominal resonant frequency of 130 kHz. The FHA gain model was solved for 10,000 randomly sampled component combinations under three load conditions (20 %, 60 %, 100 % of rated power). The probability of losing ZVS on the primary switches at 20 % load exceeded 14 % when both components carried ±10 % tolerances simultaneously, compared to 3.1 % with ±5 % tolerances. Efficiency at rated load was degraded by more than 0.5 percentage points in 8 % of Monte Carlo draws for ±10 % tolerances. Component sorting and post-assembly impedance measurement are evaluated as mitigation strategies, with their cost–benefit trade-off discussed for a small-series production context.

title: Frequency-Domain Loss Budgeting for Isolated DC-DC Converters in Stationary Energy Storage: A Unified Methodology
abstract: This paper proposes a unified methodology for constructing a frequency-domain loss budget for isolated resonant DC-DC converters used in stationary energy storage applications. The methodology integrates harmonic decomposition of converter waveforms with component-level loss models: an extended Steinmetz approach for magnetic cores, a frequency-weighted resistance model for windings, a charge-based switching loss model for semiconductors, and a dielectric loss model for film resonant capacitors. Each sub-model is calibrated independently using standardised bench measurements before being assembled into a full converter loss prediction. The methodology is validated against calorimetric measurements on a 10 kW CLLC prototype at nine operating points spanning the converter's frequency and load range. Total loss prediction error remained below 4.8 % at all tested operating points. The paper discusses how the methodology can be used during the design phase to allocate loss budgets between subsystems and to identify the component most sensitive to operating point deviations.

title: Adaptive Impedance Matching for Wearable UHF RFID Reader Antennas Subject to Body Loading
abstract: Body loading significantly alters the input impedance of antennas integrated into wearable devices, degrading read range and increasing power reflected back to the transmitter. This study characterises impedance variation of a 915 MHz RFID reader patch antenna mounted on five tissue-simulating phantom configurations representing different body locations. Measured impedance loci at each location were mapped on the Smith chart, with reactance shifts up to 35 Ω and resistance shifts up to 22 Ω recorded compared to free-space values. A switched-capacitor tuning network with four binary-weighted capacitors was designed and integrated, enabling 16 discrete matching states. An iterative hill-climbing algorithm operating from reflected power measurements selected the optimum state in under 80 ms. Field tests with five human subjects showed that adaptive matching recovered a mean 2.1 dB improvement in effective isotropic radiated power compared to a fixed matching network optimised for free-space conditions. Current consumption of the tuning circuit remained below 3 mA during active tuning.

title: Bootstrapped high-side gate driver for 650 V GaN: bootstrap diode selection and charge budget under variable duty cycle
abstract: Bootstrap-supplied high-side gate drivers for 650 V GaN half-bridges require careful diode selection and charge budget analysis because the bootstrap voltage must not fall below the gate-driver under-voltage lockout threshold across the full duty-cycle range. This paper analyses three bootstrap diode types—silicon fast-recovery, SiC Schottky, and GaN-based—in terms of reverse leakage current, forward voltage, and dynamic charge loss. A charge budget model including gate charge, quiescent current, and bootstrap capacitor leakage was validated experimentally in a 400 V, 300 W converter sweeping duty cycles from 5 % to 95 % at frequencies from 100 kHz to 1 MHz. The silicon fast-recovery diode caused bootstrap dropout at duty cycles above 85 % and above 500 kHz due to reverse recovery charge injected back into the bootstrap node. The SiC Schottky diode maintained stable high-side supply voltage across the full range. Minimum bootstrap capacitance requirements are tabulated as a function of frequency and duty cycle.

title: Uticaj artefakata retiminga na formalnu verifikaciju pipeline DSP jezgara: analiza i smernice
abstract: Automatski retiming, dostupan u sintetizatorima kao što su Vivado i Quartus, premešta registre između kombinacionih stepena radi poboljšanja timinga, ali može da izmeni posmatrljive latencije i da pokvari prethodno napisana formalna svojstva. Ovaj rad kvantifikuje koliko često retiming, primenjen na pet DSP pipeline jezgara (FIR filter, IIR sekcija drugog reda, CORDIC, FFT butterfly, DFE ekvalizator), narušava SVA svojstva napisana pre sinteze. U 38 od 110 testiranih kombinacija alat-jezgro, bar jedno svojstvo prestalo je da važi nakon retiminga. Predložen je metodološki vodič u četiri koraka koji obuhvata: (1) automatsku ekstrakciju latencije iz post-implementacionog netlista, (2) parametrizaciju SVA iskaza latencijom, (3) resintez netlistem kao novim referentnim modelom i (4) automatsku reanalizaciju. Primena vodiča na isti skup primera smanjila je broj neispravnih svojstava s 38 na 3, od kojih su sva tri bila namerna kršenja uvedena radi validacije metode.

title: A Rule-Based Explanation Layer for Support Vector Machine Classifiers in Tabular Medical Data
abstract: This paper describes a post-hoc explanation method for support vector machine (SVM) classifiers applied to tabular clinical datasets. The approach extracts conjunctive rules from the SVM decision boundary by sampling the margin region and fitting a compact rule set using a covering algorithm. Experiments were conducted on three publicly available datasets from the UCI repository covering diabetes screening, heart disease risk, and hospital readmission, comprising between 768 and 14 440 instances. The extracted rule sets achieve fidelity scores of 0.87–0.92 relative to the original SVM predictions while using on average 4.3 conditions per rule. A user study with eleven clinicians assessed rule interpretability on a five-point Likert scale; median ratings ranged from 3.8 to 4.4. The method is compared against LIME and a decision tree surrogate baseline. Results indicate that the rule-based approach is more consistent across repeated runs and produces shorter explanations, at a modest cost in fidelity. Limitations include sensitivity to the sampling density near the decision boundary and reduced performance on highly imbalanced classes.

title: Monotonicity Constraints as an Interpretability Tool in Gradient Boosting for Credit Scoring
abstract: Gradient boosting ensembles are widely used in credit scoring but are difficult to audit for regulatory compliance. This work studies whether enforcing monotonicity constraints during training serves as a practical interpretability mechanism without substantially degrading predictive performance. We experiment on a proprietary dataset of 120 000 loan applications from a regional bank, preprocessed under differential privacy guarantees to allow publication of aggregate statistics. Models with monotonicity constraints imposed on twelve economically motivated features show an area under the ROC curve of 0.791 compared with 0.803 for unconstrained models, a difference within one standard deviation across five cross-validation folds. Shapley value distributions under the constrained regime are more stable across data subsets, and the number of Shapley sign reversals—a proposed diagnostic for non-monotone influence—drops by 63 percent. We also show that constraint violations detected in unconstrained models correlate with demographic subgroup shifts in the test set. The findings suggest monotonicity constraints are a low-cost intervention for producing models that are easier to audit under the EU's algorithmic accountability guidelines.

title: Evaluating Attention Weights as Explanations in Sequence Classification Tasks
abstract: Attention weights in transformer-based sequence classifiers are frequently presented as explanations, but their relationship to model predictions is contested. This paper systematically evaluates attention-based explanations against gradient-based saliency maps and integrated gradients on four text classification benchmarks: news topic labelling, sentiment analysis, scientific claim verification, and legal clause categorisation. For each task, 500 explanations per method are assessed using three proxy faithfulness metrics: sufficiency, comprehensiveness, and input reduction accuracy. Across benchmarks, attention weights score lower on sufficiency (mean 0.61) than integrated gradients (mean 0.74) and are inconsistent with gradient-based saliency in 38 percent of instances at the token level. The gap narrows for longer sequences. We additionally collect human judgements on 200 explanation pairs per task; annotators prefer gradient-based explanations for legal and scientific text but show no strong preference for sentiment. The paper does not claim that attention is categorically uninformative, but argues that the choice of explanation method should be task-specific and empirically validated rather than chosen by convention.

title: Benchmarking Counterfactual Explanation Methods for Tabular Classifiers: A Comparative Study
abstract: Counterfactual explanations describe the minimal feature changes needed to obtain a different classifier output. This chapter surveys and benchmarks eight counterfactual generation methods on six tabular datasets spanning finance, healthcare, and public administration. Evaluation covers proximity (mean feature distance to the original instance), sparsity (average number of changed features), validity (fraction of counterfactuals that achieve the target class), and actionability (fraction respecting domain-defined immutable features). Methods tested include DICE, a growing spheres approach, a prototype-based method, and five research implementations. No single method dominates across all criteria: prototype-based approaches score highest on actionability (0.84) but lowest on proximity. Growing spheres produce the sparsest counterfactuals (1.9 changed features on average) but have lower validity for nonlinear boundaries. The chapter provides a decision guide mapping application requirements to method recommendations and identifies persistent gaps, particularly in handling heterogeneous mixed-type feature spaces and in generating diverse yet realistic counterfactual sets.

title: A Dataset for Sentence-Level Faithfulness Annotation in Abstractive Summarisation
abstract: This paper introduces SerbFaith-1K, a dataset of 1 200 abstractive summaries in Serbian and English generated from news and scientific abstracts, annotated at the sentence level for factual faithfulness. Each summary sentence is labelled as fully faithful, partially faithful, or hallucinated, with sub-labels indicating the error type (entity substitution, relation inversion, event fabrication, numerical distortion). Two trained annotators labelled all instances; inter-annotator agreement reached Fleiss's kappa of 0.71. The paper describes the annotation guidelines, the adjudication process for disputed cases, and an analysis of error type distributions, finding that numerical distortions are the most frequent error in scientific abstract summaries (34 percent of hallucination instances) while entity substitution dominates in news summaries (52 percent). Baseline experiments using NLI-based and question-answering-based faithfulness detectors on the dataset show F1 scores of 0.63 and 0.67 respectively. The dataset is released under a CC BY 4.0 licence.

title: Natural Language Inference as a Proxy for Factual Consistency Checking in Generated Text
abstract: Factual consistency checking in automatically generated text is often framed as a natural language inference (NLI) task, treating the source document as premise and each generated sentence as hypothesis. This paper investigates how well off-the-shelf NLI models serve this purpose. We evaluate five multilingual NLI checkpoints on four existing faithfulness benchmarks and find that entailment scores correlate with human faithfulness ratings at Spearman ρ = 0.49–0.67, varying substantially across domains. Performance drops markedly on long source documents (over 800 tokens), where models tend to produce neutral labels even for clearly hallucinated sentences. We trace this degradation to attention saturation in the encoder and show that chunking the premise into paragraphs and aggregating with min-pooling raises ρ by 0.09 on average. We also construct a controlled adversarial subset by swapping named entities and reversing numerical values, finding that NLI models detect fewer than half of these manipulations. The analysis suggests NLI-based consistency checking is a useful but incomplete signal, and that domain-specific fine-tuning and length-handling strategies are necessary for reliable deployment.

title: Probing Intermediate Representations of Pre-Trained Language Models for Factual Knowledge
abstract: Pre-trained language models (PLMs) are known to encode factual knowledge in their parameters, but the distribution of this knowledge across layers is not well understood. This paper applies a probing classifier methodology to six PLMs of varying sizes, testing for subject–relation–object triples from a manually constructed knowledge base of 4 800 facts in four domains: geography, institutional history, scientific authorship, and legal norms. For each fact, linear probes are trained on the hidden states of every transformer layer. Probing accuracy peaks at middle layers for relational facts (mean 71 percent) and at upper layers for entity-centric facts (mean 68 percent). Larger models do not consistently outperform smaller ones on low-frequency facts. We further investigate whether facts that are poorly encoded by the probe are also more susceptible to hallucination at inference time, finding a moderate but consistent correlation (r = 0.44 across domains). The results have implications for strategies that selectively freeze or update layers during fine-tuning to reduce hallucination.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Transformer Outputs Using Monte Carlo Dropout: A Study on Question Answering
abstract: This paper investigates whether Monte Carlo (MC) dropout can serve as a practical uncertainty estimate for transformer-based question answering (QA) models, and whether high uncertainty correlates with hallucinated or incorrect answers. Experiments use three QA datasets: one in English, one in Serbian, and one bilingual domain-specific dataset covering regulatory documents. MC dropout is applied at inference time with 30 forward passes; variance across answer span predictions is used as an uncertainty proxy. Models with high predictive variance are shown to produce incorrect answers at a rate 2.3 times higher than low-variance instances (p < 0.001). Calibration curves indicate that raw MC dropout variance is poorly calibrated (expected calibration error 0.18) but becomes usable after temperature scaling (ECE 0.07). For open-domain questions, uncertainty correlates more strongly with answer correctness than for closed-domain regulatory QA, where models tend to be overconfident. We discuss practical thresholds for triggering human review based on uncertainty estimates and the trade-off between coverage and abstention rate.

title: Towards Automatic Citation Grounding: Linking Sentences in Generated Reports to Source Passages
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems retrieve source passages before generating text, but they do not reliably attribute each generated sentence to the passages that support it. This paper addresses citation grounding: the automatic identification of which retrieved passage, if any, provides evidence for a generated sentence. We formulate the task as a bi-encoder retrieval problem followed by a cross-encoder re-ranking step, and train on a newly constructed dataset of 9 400 (generated sentence, passage, label) triples drawn from generated financial and medical reports. Labels were produced by a two-stage annotation protocol combining automatic NLI pre-filtering with human adjudication. The bi-encoder alone achieves recall@3 of 0.79; adding the cross-encoder re-ranker raises it to 0.86. Grounding precision at rank 1 is 0.71. We find that sentences containing numerical claims are the most difficult to ground (precision 0.58), while definitional sentences are easiest (precision 0.83). The paper also introduces a simple attribution confidence score and shows it correlates with human judgements of citation quality (ρ = 0.61).

title: Detecting Hallucinations in Long-Form Language Model Outputs Using Decomposition and Atomic Claim Verification
abstract: Long-form text generated by large language models may contain a mixture of supported and unsupported claims within a single paragraph, making sentence-level faithfulness evaluation insufficient. This paper proposes a pipeline that decomposes generated paragraphs into atomic claims using a fine-tuned decomposition model, retrieves relevant evidence passages for each claim from a linked corpus, and classifies each claim as supported, contradicted, or unverifiable using a fine-tuned NLI model. The pipeline is evaluated on three long-form generation tasks: biographies, medical treatment summaries, and legal case descriptions. On a human-annotated test set of 480 generated documents, the pipeline achieves claim-level detection F1 of 0.74, compared with 0.61 for a sentence-level baseline. Error analysis shows that implicit presuppositions and vague quantifiers are the main sources of remaining false negatives. We further report that the fraction of unverifiable claims—those where no retrieved passage addresses the claim—is a useful document-level hallucination risk signal, correlating with human overall quality ratings at ρ = 0.58.

title: Retrieval Quality and Its Effect on Downstream Hallucination Rates in RAG Systems
abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the quality of retrieved context directly affects the faithfulness of generated outputs, yet the relationship is rarely studied in controlled settings. This paper designs a factorial experiment varying retrieval precision (high, medium, low, and adversarial) across three RAG configurations (BM25 only, dense retrieval only, and hybrid) and two generator sizes. Retrieval precision is operationalised by injecting passages with controlled relevance degradation into the retrieval pool. Hallucination rates are measured using the atomic claim verification pipeline from prior work. Moving from high to medium retrieval precision increases hallucination rate by an average of 11 percentage points; adversarial passages (containing plausible but incorrect facts) increase it by 28 percentage points relative to the high-precision baseline. Dense retrieval generators are more susceptible to adversarial passages than BM25 generators. Generator size moderates adversarial sensitivity: larger models (7B parameters) show smaller increases than smaller models (1.3B) under adversarial conditions. The results provide empirical grounding for retrieval quality requirements in production RAG deployments.

title: Post-Hoc Explanation Consistency Under Distribution Shift: An Empirical Study
abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods are typically evaluated on held-out data from the same distribution as the training set. This paper examines how LIME, SHAP, and integrated gradients behave when the test distribution shifts relative to training. We induce controlled distribution shifts in four classification tasks (text, tabular, image, and time-series) by progressively modifying covariate distributions. Explanation consistency is measured as the rank correlation between feature importance scores produced on original and shifted instances matched by prediction confidence. All three methods degrade under shift, but the rate and nature of degradation differ: SHAP explanations lose consistency faster on tabular data (rank correlation drops from 0.81 to 0.47 at moderate shift), while integrated gradients are relatively stable for text and image tasks. We also show that explanation inconsistency is a detectable signal for distribution shift itself, providing a potential monitoring use case. The study uses no proprietary data; all datasets and shift protocols are described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: GroundCheck: A Framework for Real-Time Citation Verification in RAG-Powered Document Assistants
abstract: Production document assistant systems built on retrieval-augmented generation need to verify that claims in their outputs are traceable to specific source passages before responses are shown to users. This paper describes GroundCheck, a modular verification framework that intercepts generation outputs, decomposes them into atomic claims, and runs lightweight verification against the retrieved context within a latency budget of 400 milliseconds per response on commodity hardware. The framework uses a distilled cross-encoder for claim–passage entailment checking (73M parameters) and a rule-based post-processing step to attach inline citation markers to verified claims. In an offline evaluation against manually annotated outputs from a legal document assistant, GroundCheck achieves precision 0.80 and recall 0.76 for correctly identified unsupported claims. A qualitative deployment study with 24 legal professionals found that citation markers increased perceived trustworthiness of the system on a seven-point scale by 1.4 points on average. Failure analysis highlights remaining difficulties with multi-hop reasoning chains and implicitly contradictory evidence.
