title: Evaluating Explanation Fidelity Under Prompt Variation in Instruction-Tuned Language Models
abstract: Instruction-tuned language models can produce natural-language explanations for their own outputs on request, but it is unclear whether these self-explanations reflect the model's actual inference path or are generated independently of it. This paper measures explanation fidelity by comparing self-generated explanations to three external explanation methods (saliency, attention rollout, and a perturbation-based method) across 600 prompted classification and extraction tasks. Agreement between self-explanations and external methods, measured by normalised token-level overlap, averages 0.41 and varies substantially with prompt wording. Systematically varying the explanation prompt reveals that adding the phrase 'cite the exact words from the input that determined your answer' raises agreement to 0.55 without affecting task performance. We also find that self-explanations are more likely to be faithful when the model's output confidence is high and when the task is extractive rather than abstractive. The results have practical implications for the design of explanation prompts in deployed systems and suggest that external verification of self-explanations is necessary for high-stakes applications.

title: Constraint Propagation Strategies for Tile-Based Dungeon Layout Generation
abstract: This paper examines how different arc-consistency algorithms affect the quality and speed of procedurally generated tile-based dungeon maps. We implemented AC-3, MAC, and a custom directional variant within a backtracking CSP solver operating on a 32×32 grid of room tiles. Each cell carries domain variables encoding wall configuration, connectivity class, and enemy density. The directional variant reduced backtracking steps by 38% compared to AC-3 on a benchmark suite of 500 target layout specifications drawn from an existing game design corpus. Mean generation time dropped from 1.4 seconds to 0.6 seconds per map at this grid size. We also report how constraint weighting based on player-path criticality improves playability scores in a blind evaluation with 24 game-design students. The results suggest that propagation order informed by spatial topology is more effective than uniform propagation for room-network structures.

title: Skalabilnost OCSP stapling mehanizma u opterećenim TLS okruženjima: merenja i ograničenja
abstract: OCSP stapling prenet je u TLS 1.3 kao preferirani mehanizam provere statusa sertifikata, ali su njegova skalabilna ograničenja na strani servera nedovoljno istražena. Ovaj rad meri uticaj stapling operacija na propusnost TLS rukovanjem na serverima s različitim profilima sertifikata — kratkim, srednjim i dugim vekom trajanja. Testovi su sprovedeni na konfiguraciji s jednim poslužiteljem koji obrađuje do 20.000 TLS rukovanja u sekundi, koristeći nginx i prilagođeni omotač za OpenSSL. Mereno je zauzeće CPU-a, memorije i kašnjenje osvežavanja OCSP odgovora. Rezultati pokazuju da frekvencija osvežavanja OCSP odgovora direktno utiče na propusnost pri vrednostima ispod 30 sekundi perioda kešovanja, povećavajući CPU opterećenje za 9–17%. Rad predlaže adaptivni raspored osvežavanja zasnovan na tekućem opterećenju sistema.

title: Character-Level Neural Transliteration for Serbian: Training Data, Architecture Choices, and Error Analysis
abstract: Deterministic rule-based transliteration between Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts handles the majority of tokens correctly, but fails on foreign loanwords, abbreviations, and alphanumeric strings. This paper investigates whether a character-level sequence-to-sequence neural model can handle these exceptions while remaining accurate on regular tokens. We trained models on a corpus of 2.3 million aligned Cyrillic–Latin token pairs extracted from parallel editions of official gazettes, experimenting with LSTM encoder-decoder architectures with attention, as well as a character-level transformer. The transformer model achieved a character error rate of 0.4% on regular tokens and 3.1% on the exception classes, compared with 0.1% and 19.4% respectively for the deterministic baseline. We performed a detailed error analysis categorising 800 mistransliterated tokens by type. The paper concludes that a cascaded system — deterministic rules followed by the neural model for detected exceptions — outperforms either component alone, reaching a token error rate of 0.6% overall.

title: Ranking Renewable Energy Alternatives Using an Interval Type-2 Fuzzy TOPSIS Approach
abstract: This paper addresses the selection of renewable energy technologies for small municipalities in the Vojvodina region of Serbia using an interval type-2 fuzzy TOPSIS framework. Five criteria—cost, CO₂ emissions, land use, local employment impact, and technical maturity—were evaluated by a panel of seven domain experts whose linguistic assessments were encoded as trapezoidal interval type-2 fuzzy numbers. Three candidate technologies were assessed: small-scale wind turbines, rooftop photovoltaic arrays, and biomass combustion units. The upper and lower membership functions were constructed from expert responses collected via a structured questionnaire administered in 2022. After applying the extended TOPSIS ranking procedure, photovoltaic arrays ranked highest under four of the five weighting schemes tested in a subsequent sensitivity analysis involving 120 weight perturbation scenarios. The results were cross-validated against a crisp AHP ranking obtained independently, showing rank agreement in 83% of scenarios. The study highlights how inter-expert disagreement propagates through the type-2 framework differently than in type-1 fuzzy TOPSIS, particularly for the cost criterion where expert opinion variance was highest.

title: Feature Construction via Symbolic Regression as a Preprocessing Step for Supervised Classification
abstract: This paper investigates whether symbolic regression can be used to construct informative nonlinear features from raw tabular inputs before training a standard classification algorithm. The proposed pipeline runs a population of grammar-guided GP individuals to minimise a surrogate fitness based on mutual information between the candidate feature and the class label, independently of any downstream classifier. Constructed features are then appended to the original feature set and used to train a logistic regression model and a k-nearest-neighbour classifier. Experiments on 25 UCI-style binary classification datasets show that adding one GP-constructed feature improves average area under the ROC curve by 0.031 for logistic regression and 0.044 for k-NN compared to baselines without feature construction. The improvement is statistically significant (paired t-test, p < 0.01) on 18 of 25 datasets. The method is most effective on datasets with strong nonlinear interactions between predictors and the target.

title: Influence of homogenisation pressure on emulsion stability prior to spray drying of flaxseed oil in sodium caseinate–lactose matrices
abstract: This study examined how inlet emulsion properties affect the encapsulation efficiency and oxidative stability of flaxseed oil microcapsules prepared by spray drying. Oil-in-water emulsions (20% w/w oil load) were homogenised at three pressures (50, 100, and 150 bar) using a two-stage valve homogeniser before atomisation. Droplet size d(4,3) decreased from 4.2 μm to 1.1 μm as pressure increased; however, microcapsule encapsulation efficiency peaked at 100 bar (91.3%) and declined slightly at 150 bar (88.7%), attributed to coalescence during atomisation. Peroxide values after four weeks of storage at 40°C were 12.4, 8.7, and 10.1 mEq O₂/kg oil for the three pressures respectively. The 100 bar treatment also yielded the highest α-linolenic acid retention (94.1%). These findings indicate that intermediate homogenisation pressures balance droplet refinement and wall coverage in protein-lactose spray-dried systems, providing practical guidance for process scale-up with oxidation-sensitive plant oils.

title: Effect of inlet air temperature on powder morphology and fatty acid profile retention in spray-dried evening primrose oil microcapsules
abstract: Evening primrose oil, rich in γ-linolenic acid (GLA, 9.2% of total fatty acids), was encapsulated in a whey protein concentrate–maltodextrin (DE 12) blend at a 1:3 weight ratio. Spray drying was performed at inlet temperatures of 150, 170, and 190°C, with a fixed feed rate of 5 mL/min and outlet temperature maintained between 65 and 80°C. Powder yield ranged from 67% to 79% across treatments. Scanning electron microscopy revealed increasingly spherical and smooth particles at higher temperatures, with fewer surface fissures. Gas chromatography–flame ionisation detection confirmed GLA retention of 93.1%, 91.4%, and 88.8% at 150, 170, and 190°C respectively. Malondialdehyde equivalents determined by TBARS after 56 days at 37°C showed significantly lower oxidation rates at 150°C inlet temperature. The study concludes that minimising thermal exposure during drying is critical for preserving sensitive polyunsaturated fatty acids in whey protein-based matrices.

title: Oxidative stability of encapsulated chia seed oil in protein–polysaccharide matrices under accelerated storage conditions
abstract: Chia seed oil, containing approximately 64% α-linolenic acid, was encapsulated by spray drying in three wall material combinations: whey protein isolate (WPI) alone, WPI with maltodextrin DE 18 at a 1:1 ratio, and WPI with gum arabic at a 1:1 ratio. Core-to-wall ratio was fixed at 1:4 (w/w). Encapsulation efficiency ranged from 85.4% (WPI alone) to 93.6% (WPI–maltodextrin). Rancimat induction periods at 80°C were 4.1, 6.8, and 5.9 hours for the three matrices respectively. After 90 days at 25°C and 57% relative humidity, conjugated diene values were lowest in the WPI–maltodextrin treatment. Particle size distributions showed monomodal profiles with volume-weighted mean diameters between 10 and 18 μm. The results confirm that the combination of film-forming protein and a high-molecular-weight polysaccharide filler substantially reduces interfacial oxygen permeability compared with protein alone.

title: Cold-pressed hemp seed oil: physicochemical characterisation and fatty acid profile as a function of cultivar and harvest year
abstract: Three hemp cultivars (Fedora 17, Tiborszállás, and a locally bred line designated NS-H3) grown in Vojvodina over two consecutive harvest years were cold-pressed and characterised for their physicochemical properties and fatty acid composition. Oil yield ranged from 28.3% to 31.7% (dry weight basis). All cultivars showed omega-6 to omega-3 ratios between 2.8:1 and 3.4:1, close to nutritional recommendations. Linoleic acid (C18:2n-6) constituted 54–57% and α-linolenic acid (C18:3n-3) 16–19% of total fatty acids as determined by GC-FID after transmethylation. Tocopherol content measured by HPLC-FLD varied significantly between cultivars (p < 0.01), with NS-H3 yielding the highest γ-tocopherol (68 mg/100 g oil). Phospholipid content (0.12–0.19%) and free fatty acid values (0.4–0.8%) were within accepted cold-pressed quality ranges. Harvest year had a smaller effect than cultivar on most parameters. These data provide baseline information for selecting hemp oil batches with consistent composition for subsequent encapsulation studies.

title: Spray drying of hemp seed oil emulsions: effect of whey protein–maltodextrin ratio on powder flowability and encapsulation efficiency
abstract: Cold-pressed hemp seed oil was emulsified at a 30% (w/w) oil load in aqueous solutions of whey protein isolate and maltodextrin (DE 10) at mass ratios of 1:1, 1:2, 1:3, and 1:4, maintaining total wall material concentration at 20% (w/v). Emulsions were spray-dried at an inlet temperature of 165°C. Encapsulation efficiency increased from 87.2% at a 1:1 ratio to a maximum of 94.5% at 1:3, with marginal improvement at 1:4. Powder bulk density increased with maltodextrin content (from 0.31 to 0.47 g/cm³), positively affecting flowability as assessed by the Carr Index. Surface oil, determined by solvent extraction, was lowest (1.8% of total oil) at the 1:3 ratio. X-ray diffraction confirmed amorphous particle structure across all ratios. The 1:3 WPI-to-maltodextrin ratio was identified as the optimum formulation, balancing structural integrity, powder handling properties, and protection of the omega-3 fraction during drying.

title: In vitro bioaccessibility of omega-3 fatty acids from spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules using a static three-phase digestion model
abstract: Spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules prepared in a whey protein isolate–maltodextrin (1:3) matrix were subjected to a static in vitro digestion protocol comprising oral, gastric, and intestinal phases according to a standardised INFOGEST procedure adapted for lipid analysis. Free fatty acid (FFA) release was monitored by pH-stat titration during the intestinal phase. Bioaccessibility of α-linolenic acid (ALA) was 61.3 ± 3.7% from microcapsules compared with 74.8 ± 4.1% from bulk (unencapsulated) oil, indicating partial protection of the wall matrix against lipase action. Lipolysis rate constants determined by first-order kinetic modelling were 0.041 and 0.063 min⁻¹ for encapsulated and bulk oil respectively. Micellar incorporation efficiency determined by ultracentrifugation was 48.2% for encapsulated and 56.9% for bulk oil. The protein matrix partially resisted pepsin digestion, slowing gastric lipid release, while pancreatin hydrolysis in the intestinal phase recovered the majority of FFA. These data demonstrate acceptable ALA bioaccessibility with the trade-off of somewhat reduced release kinetics.

title: Antioxidant capacity of whey protein–maltodextrin microcapsules loaded with hemp seed oil: DPPH, ABTS and FRAP comparisons before and after simulated digestion
abstract: This paper reports the antioxidant capacity of spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules measured by three complementary assays (DPPH radical scavenging, ABTS decolorisation, and FRAP ferric-reducing antioxidant power) before and after a simulated gastrointestinal digestion sequence. The wall material at WPI:maltodextrin ratios of 1:2 and 1:3 was tested at an oil load of 25 and 35% (w/w). Before digestion, DPPH inhibition ranged from 42 to 58%, with higher values at greater oil load. After simulated digestion, antioxidant capacity increased substantially (DPPH 61–79%), attributed to the release of bioactive peptides from whey protein during enzymatic hydrolysis and the simultaneous liberation of tocopherols from the oil fraction. The 1:3 ratio at 25% oil load showed the best combination of pre-digestion protection and post-digestion activity. These findings suggest the WPI–maltodextrin wall contributes an intrinsic antioxidant function beyond mechanical protection of the encapsulated oil.

title: Comparative performance of maltodextrin grades (DE 6, DE 12, DE 18) as co-wall materials with whey protein isolate in hemp oil spray drying: structural, thermal and oxidative outcomes
abstract: Three maltodextrin grades differing in dextrose equivalent (DE 6, DE 12, DE 18) were combined with whey protein isolate at a constant 1:3 ratio (WPI:MD) to encapsulate cold-pressed hemp seed oil at 30% core load by spray drying at 165°C inlet temperature. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed glass transition temperatures (Tg) of 78.4, 62.1, and 51.7°C for DE 6, DE 12, and DE 18 powders respectively. Higher Tg correlated with lower surface oil content (2.1, 3.4, and 5.6% respectively) and slower primary oxidation rates at 40°C. Encapsulation efficiency was highest with DE 6 (95.1%) and lowest with DE 18 (91.8%). In vitro bioaccessibility of ALA was inversely related to Tg, with DE 18 samples showing the highest FFA release (68.2%) during the simulated intestinal phase due to faster matrix dissolution. These opposing trends between oxidative protection and bioaccessibility with increasing DE value present a formulation trade-off that must be resolved based on the intended application.

title: Effect of lecithin addition on emulsion droplet size, surface coverage, and oxidative stability of spray-dried hemp seed oil in WPI–maltodextrin matrices
abstract: Sunflower lecithin was added at 0, 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5% (w/w, on emulsion basis) to hemp seed oil emulsions prepared in a WPI:maltodextrin DE 12 (1:3) wall system before spray drying at 165°C. Emulsion droplet diameter (d₃₂) decreased from 1.87 μm (no lecithin) to 0.94 μm at 1.0% lecithin addition, with no significant further reduction at 1.5%. Zeta potential became more negative with lecithin addition (from −24.7 to −38.2 mV), improving colloidal stability of the feed emulsion. Encapsulation efficiency improved from 93.2 to 96.8% at 1.0% lecithin. Rancimat induction periods at 80°C increased from 5.9 hours to 8.4 hours with 1.0% lecithin, while TBARS values at week 12 (40°C storage) were 1.8-fold lower relative to the lecithin-free control. In vitro bioaccessibility of ALA at 1.0% lecithin (67.4%) was higher than the control (61.3%), attributed to enhanced micellarisation facilitated by the phospholipid fraction during intestinal digestion.

title: Stability of encapsulated hemp seed oil in functional fermented milk beverages: pH-driven wall matrix swelling and lipid oxidation during 28-day refrigerated storage
abstract: Spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules (WPI:maltodextrin 1:3, 1.0% lecithin) were incorporated at 2% (w/w) into a fermented milk beverage (pH 4.2, titratable acidity 0.8%) produced with a commercial Lactobacillus acidophilus–Bifidobacterium longum co-culture. Microcapsule integrity, lipid oxidation markers, and ALA content were assessed on days 0, 7, 14, and 28 of refrigerated storage at 4°C. Confocal laser scanning microscopy with Nile Red staining showed progressive swelling and partial surface cracking of the protein matrix below pH 4.5, with visible oil release by day 14. Despite matrix disruption, ALA retention remained above 90% through day 28, attributed to the reducing environment of the fermented medium and the presence of lactic acid bacteria-derived antioxidant metabolites. Peroxide values in the beverage increased from 0.9 to 3.4 mEq O₂/kg fat by day 28, remaining within acceptable limits. These results indicate that WPI-based microcapsules require acid-resistant coating for long-term application in fermented dairy matrices.

title: Accelerated migration testing of triacetin from cellulose acetate films at elevated temperatures and its prediction at 4 °C refrigeration conditions
abstract: Triacetin is used as a plasticiser in cellulose acetate films applied to fresh pasta and soft-ripened cheese packaging. Accelerated migration tests were conducted at 40, 50, and 60 °C into ethanol 50% v/v simulant to predict migration at 4 °C refrigeration temperature via time–temperature superposition. Migration was quantified by GC-FID at 1, 3, 7, 14, and 28 days. The apparent activation energy derived from an Arrhenius fit was 54.7 kJ/mol, in agreement with literature values for small polar molecules in cellulose acetate. Predicted migration at 4 °C over 21 days (shelf life scenario) was 1.9 mg/dm², well below the specific migration limit. Uncertainty propagation from temperature measurement error (±0.5 °C) contributed ±12% to the 4 °C prediction. The study validates the use of accelerated protocols for low-temperature packaging applications and quantifies the prediction uncertainty explicitly, which is often omitted in compliance studies.

title: Simultaneous HPLC-DAD quantification of seven antioxidant additives in fatty food simulants extracted from complex multilayer snack-food packaging
abstract: Multilayer oriented polypropylene (OPP)/metallised OPP/polyethylene laminates used for potato crisps and extruded snacks typically contain mixtures of phenolic antioxidants and processing stabilisers in several layers. A reversed-phase HPLC-DAD method for simultaneous determination of BHT, BHA, AO-1076, AO-1010, AO-168, Tinuvin-P analogue, and DSTDP in isooctane fatty simulant was developed and validated. Linearity (R² > 0.999), limits of detection (0.01–0.08 mg/L), repeatability (RSD < 4.5%), and matrix spike recovery (92–107%) were established according to SANTE/11312/2021 guidelines. Migration experiments at 25 °C, 40 °C, and 60 °C over 14 days showed that BHT was the dominant migrant at all temperatures, reaching 3.2 mg/kg at 60 °C, while thioester DSTDP remained below the LOD across all conditions. The method is directly transferable to regulatory compliance laboratories and requires only standard HPLC instrumentation, making it accessible to routine testing facilities in the region.

title: Dune field morphology of the Deliblato Sands derived from 1:25 000 topographic maps and early aerial photographs
abstract: This study reconstructed the spatial organisation of dune forms across the approximately 300 km² Deliblato Sands using digitised contour data from 1930s topographic maps and scanned aerial photographs from 1953. Dune crests, slipfaces, and interdune corridors were manually delineated, yielding a catalogue of 847 individual dune units. Crest orientations cluster between 195° and 215°, consistent with dominant north-northeast palaeowind directions reconstructed from regional sedimentological records. Average dune height at the time of the earliest photographs was 6.4 m, with a maximum of 17.1 m recorded in the central sector. Cross-comparison of map and photograph sources revealed a positional discrepancy averaging 18 m, attributed to map generalisation rather than actual dune migration. The resulting geodatabase provides a morphological baseline against which subsequent decades of change can be quantified. Methods and accuracy assessments are documented in detail to support future updates as additional historical imagery becomes available.

title: Twentieth-century expansion of vegetated surfaces on the Deliblato Sands: a photointerpretation analysis of six aerial survey epochs
abstract: Six sets of aerial photographs acquired in 1953, 1966, 1977, 1988, 1998, and 2004 were orthorectified and co-registered to a common coordinate reference frame to track the progressive colonisation of bare sand by vegetation across the Deliblato Sands. Photo-interpretation using a five-class land-cover scheme (bare mobile sand, sparsely vegetated sand, shrub cover, forest plantation, and non-sandy land) was applied to 432 sample plots. Bare mobile sand decreased from 38.4% of the study area in 1953 to 5.1% by 2004, while forest plantations established predominantly between 1966 and 1988 expanded from 8.2% to 29.7%. Rates of stabilisation were highest in the 1966–1977 interval, coinciding with intensive afforestation programmes using black locust and Scots pine. Residual mobile patches in 2004 were concentrated along the northwest-facing flanks of the highest dunes, where wind acceleration prevents establishment of perennial grasses. The analysis confirms that active sand movement is largely a relict phenomenon under current climate and management conditions.

title: Quantifying dune displacement rates using sequential aerial photographs: methodology and application to the Deliblato Sands (1953–1988)
abstract: A digital cross-correlation procedure was applied to pairs of orthorectified aerial photographs spanning the intervals 1953–1966, 1966–1977, and 1977–1988 to estimate horizontal displacement of bare dune crests in the Deliblato Sands. Crest segments were extracted semi-automatically by thresholding brightness values on north-facing slopes and verified against manual digitisation. Of 312 dune crest segments longer than 50 m identified in 1953, only 147 remained unambiguously bare in all three subsequent epochs, allowing continuous displacement tracking. Mean annual displacement declined from 1.8 m yr⁻¹ in 1953–1966 to 0.6 m yr⁻¹ in 1977–1988, consistent with progressive vegetation encroachment. Maximum single-epoch displacement reached 4.3 m yr⁻¹ for an isolated blowout in the northern sector. Uncertainty arising from co-registration errors, estimated at ±0.4 m, is small relative to measured displacements. The methodology is transferable to other sand fields in the Pannonian Basin where historical analogue photography is available.

title: Sediment grain-size and sorting patterns across stabilised and residually active dune forms, Deliblato Sands
abstract: Surface sediment samples were collected from 86 sites across the Deliblato Sands representing four geomorphic positions: dune crest, windward slope, leeward slope, and interdune hollow. Grain-size distributions were determined by laser diffractometry on 2 g sub-samples. Mean grain size at crest positions ranged from 175 to 310 µm (medium sand), while interdune hollows contained finer material averaging 155 µm with a bimodal distribution reflecting aeolian fines mixed with fluvially reworked inputs from adjacent loess margins. Sorting coefficients at fully stabilised crests were significantly poorer than at residually active crests, attributed to bioturbation and organic matter accumulation under vegetation. A logistic regression model using mean grain size, sorting, and skewness correctly classified stabilised versus active status of 79 of 86 samples. The findings suggest that grain-size statistics can supplement remotely sensed imagery for mapping stabilisation state where photographic coverage is lacking.

title: Mapping historical sand dune activity in the southern Pannonian Basin: a regional comparison of the Deliblato, Bačka, and Nyírség sand fields
abstract: This book chapter synthesises remotely sensed evidence for aeolian activity across three major sand fields in the southern Pannonian Basin — the Deliblato Sands (Serbia), the Bačka Sand Ridge (Serbia–Hungary border), and the Nyírség (northeastern Hungary) — using comparable multi-temporal aerial photograph and satellite image archives. For each field, the proportion of bare active sand was quantified at intervals of roughly one decade from the 1950s to the 2000s. All three fields showed strong stabilisation trends, but rates differed substantially: the Deliblato declined most rapidly (from ~38% to ~5% bare sand), while the Nyírség retained higher proportions of semi-active sand (declining from ~22% to ~11%) owing to coarser substrate and more continental precipitation seasonality. The chapter also reviews the roles of afforestation policy, agricultural reclamation, and reduced livestock grazing pressure as drivers of stabilisation and discusses implications for regional biodiversity and dust emission potential under projected warming scenarios.

title: Detection of small-scale sand reactivation events using very-high-resolution satellite imagery: a test case at the Deliblato Sands (2005–2014)
abstract: A time series of twelve very-high-resolution (0.5 m pan-sharpened) satellite images acquired between 2005 and 2014 was used to detect and measure small-scale sand reactivation events within the Deliblato Special Nature Reserve. Supervised maximum-likelihood classification using six spectral bands identified bare sand patches with overall accuracy of 91.4% and a kappa coefficient of 0.88, validated against 214 ground-truth points. A total of 73 distinct reactivation events were detected over the nine-year period, covering a cumulative area of 4.2 ha. Event sizes ranged from 80 m² to 3 200 m². Spatial clustering analysis indicated that 68% of events occurred within 200 m of existing forest plantation edges, where wind turbulence at canopy margins appears to strip vegetation from adjacent sand surfaces. Interannual variability in event frequency showed a weak positive association with summer temperature anomaly (r = 0.54), suggesting that drought-induced dieback of stabilising grasses may be a trigger. These results indicate that stabilisation is not irreversible and that monitoring intervals of two years or less are appropriate for detecting episodic disturbances.

title: UAV-derived digital surface models for micro-topographic change detection on a blowout at the Deliblato Sands
abstract: An unmanned aerial vehicle equipped with a 20-megapixel RGB camera was used to generate high-resolution digital surface models (DSMs) of a 6.4 ha active blowout in the Deliblato Sands on three occasions spaced approximately six months apart in 2016–2017. Structure-from-motion photogrammetry was applied to image blocks of 580–640 photographs per survey, yielding DSMs at 0.08 m ground sampling distance. Differencing of successive DSMs quantified erosion and deposition volumes: the first interval (October 2016 – April 2017) recorded net sediment loss of 84 m³ from the deflation basin and deposition of 91 m³ on the leeward rim. The second interval showed reduced activity (net loss 22 m³), coinciding with above-average spring precipitation and earlier grass germination. Maximum single-survey erosion depth in the deflation basin reached 0.31 m. Comparison with co-temporal wind speed records from the Bela Crkva meteorological station indicated a threshold friction velocity for detectable change of approximately 5.8 m s⁻¹ at 10 m height. The study demonstrates that UAV surveys at sub-annual frequency are viable for tracking episodic aeolian activity at the blowout scale.

title: Long-term soil development on stabilised dunes of the Deliblato Sands: pedological characteristics along a vegetation chronosequence
abstract: Seven pedological profiles were described and sampled along a vegetation chronosequence representing bare mobile sand, grassland-stabilised sand (approximately 40 years since stabilisation), shrub-stabilised sand (approximately 60 years), and mature black-locust plantation (approximately 80 years). Profile descriptions followed FAO guidelines; laboratory analyses included texture, pH, organic carbon (Walkley-Black method), and CEC. Organic carbon content increased from 0.04% in bare sand to 1.71% under mature plantation. Soil pH declined from 8.2 in bare sand to 6.9 under plantation canopy, attributed to litter decomposition and root respiration. A faint Bw horizon was detectable at depths of 20–35 cm in profiles older than 60 years, indicating the onset of weak brunification. Findings are consistent with estimated soil formation rates of 0.01–0.02% organic carbon accumulation per year reported from comparable European sand soils and suggest that pedological recovery from destabilisation requires multi-decadal timescales even after surface vegetation is re-established.

title: Revisiting the 1953 aerial survey of the Deliblato Sands: geometric accuracy assessment of analogue photograph digitisation workflows
abstract: The 1953 aerial survey of the Deliblato Sands, conducted at a nominal scale of 1:20 000, is the oldest photogrammetric record available for this region and is widely used as a baseline in aeolian change studies. This technical paper evaluates three digitisation and georeferencing workflows applied to 34 prints from that survey: (1) flatbed scanning at 1 200 dpi with manual GCP-based polynomial rectification, (2) flatbed scanning with thin-plate spline transformation, and (3) photogrammetric scanning at 1 600 dpi with collinearity-equation-based exterior orientation using known ground points extracted from a 1955 cadastral survey. Root-mean-square positional errors at 62 independent check points were 4.8 m, 3.2 m, and 1.7 m respectively. Residual errors for workflow 3 showed no spatial trend, while workflow 1 retained systematic east-west drift attributable to film distortion. The paper recommends workflow 3 for archival surveys where geometric accuracy is critical and provides open access to the georeferenced mosaic through a regional spatial data repository. Results have direct implications for the reliability of displacement measurements derived from this epoch.

title: Seventy years of dune stabilisation in the Deliblato Sands: a comprehensive geomorphic change analysis using aerial and satellite imagery from 1953 to 2023
abstract: This paper presents the most complete multi-temporal mapping of aeolian landform change in the Deliblato Sands to date, integrating georeferenced aerial photographs from six pre-2000 epochs with satellite imagery from 2000, 2010, 2018, and 2023. The entire reserve (approximately 304 km²) was mapped at a minimum mapping unit of 0.1 ha for nine land-surface classes. Bare mobile sand declined from 116 km² in 1953 to 1.8 km² in 2023, a reduction of 98.5%. Dune crest network length decreased from 412 km to 38 km over the same period. Residual active morphology is now confined to four spatially discrete clusters totalling 68 ha, all within the unplanted core of the reserve. A net sediment budget estimated from elevation differencing between a 1970 photogrammetric DEM and the 2018 lidar DEM indicates approximately 2.1 × 10⁶ m³ of net deposition trapped on leeward margins, consistent with reduced transport capacity under vegetation cover. The dataset is published as an open-access geodatabase. The paper discusses the reversibility of stabilisation under projected climate trajectories and the management implications for the reserve authority.

title: Spatiotemporal behaviour modelling
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic account of methods for constructing spatiotemporal behaviour models from GPS trajectory data in outdoor recreation and nature-based tourism research. The chapter covers data acquisition (logger-based and smartphone-based), preprocessing (coordinate projection, gap interpolation, noise filtering), segmentation into movement and stop phases, and model types ranging from descriptive statistics and kernel density estimation to Markov-chain transition models and agent-based simulations calibrated with empirical tracks. Worked examples draw on data from protected areas in Serbia, Hungary, and Slovenia. A comparative table summarises the computational requirements, data volume needs, and interpretive outputs of each method family. The chapter also addresses ethical dimensions of tracking research including participant consent frameworks and data anonymisation procedures compliant with EU data protection regulation. Intended as a methodological reference for researchers entering the field, it concludes with a discussion of open challenges including data fusion with remote sensing and integration with visitor counting systems.

title: Adapting SERVQUAL for Rural Guesthouses in Vojvodina: A Pilot Scale Validation
abstract: This study examined whether the five-dimensional SERVQUAL framework is transferable to small family-run rural guesthouses in the Vojvodina region without modification. A pilot sample of 218 guests was collected from 14 licensed guesthouses during the summer season of 2009. Exploratory factor analysis suggested that the original reliability and assurance dimensions collapsed into a single factor in this context, yielding a four-factor solution. Confirmatory factor analysis with a subsequent sample of 301 guests confirmed acceptable model fit (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.061). Gap scores between expectations and perceptions were negative across all dimensions, with the largest gap recorded for tangibles, particularly the physical condition of sanitary facilities and room furnishing. The paper proposes a 19-item rural guesthouse service quality scale (RGS-19) and discusses implications for owners operating with limited renovation budgets. The instrument was subsequently distributed to the national rural tourism association for voluntary benchmarking use.

title: Calibration of fibre Bragg grating sensors under simultaneous strain and temperature loading in laboratory conditions
abstract: This paper describes a controlled laboratory procedure for separating the strain and temperature responses of bare FBG sensors operating in the 1530–1560 nm window. A total of 12 gratings inscribed in SMF-28 fibre were subjected to axial strains between 0 and 2000 µε in a purpose-built tensile rig while temperature was varied from −10 °C to +70 °C in a climatic chamber. The strain sensitivity coefficient was determined as 1.19 pm/µε and the temperature coefficient as 10.3 pm/°C, consistent with manufacturer data but with tighter uncertainty bounds (±0.02 pm/µε). A 2×2 matrix decoupling approach was applied and validated against reference resistive strain gauges and a PT100 probe. Residuals after decoupling were below 8 µε and 0.5 °C across the full range. The study provides a repeatable protocol suitable for sensor batches used in field deployments.

title: Embedding FBG sensors in GFRP laminates for strain monitoring of composite bridge deck panels
abstract: Glass-fibre-reinforced polymer deck panels are increasingly used in pedestrian bridge refurbishment, yet long-term strain data from embedded sensors remain scarce. This study describes the integration of FBG sensors into 6 mm GFRP laminates during hand lay-up fabrication. Sensors were placed at three depths relative to the neutral axis to capture bending strain profiles under three-point loading. Twenty loading cycles were applied at increments of 5 kN up to 30 kN on 1.2 m specimens. Embedded sensors tracked strains up to 1800 µε with deviations below 12 µε compared with surface-mounted strain gauges. Thermal drift was corrected using a reference grating thermally isolated from mechanical load. Post-cure optical losses were measured at 0.15 dB on average per embedded sensor. Results confirm the viability of cure-integrated FBG arrays for composite bridge elements without significant signal degradation.

title: Long-term field monitoring of a prestressed concrete highway bridge using a 24-channel FBG interrogation system
abstract: A 24-channel FBG monitoring installation was deployed on a 148 m prestressed concrete viaduct on a major road corridor in Vojvodina and operated continuously for 18 months between 2014 and 2016. Sensors were placed on the lower flanges of three main girders at mid-span and at quarter-span positions, with additional temperature reference gratings attached to the concrete surface. Data were recorded at 1 Hz and archived remotely via GPRS. Seasonal strain variations of up to 320 µε were observed, correlated with ambient temperature cycles. Traffic-induced dynamic strain peaks reached 95 µε under heavy vehicle crossings. A simple threshold-based alert algorithm triggered 14 notifications over the monitoring period, all confirmed to correspond to anomalous loading events rather than sensor artefacts. Sensor drift over the 18-month period was below 5 µε, demonstrating acceptable long-term stability in outdoor conditions.

title: Mechanical protection packaging for FBG sensors on buried steel pipelines: a comparative study of three encapsulation approaches
abstract: Reliable attachment of FBG sensors to the outer surface of buried steel pipelines requires robust packaging that transfers ground strain to the grating while protecting the fibre from corrosion and mechanical damage during soil compaction. Three packaging concepts were evaluated: an epoxy-filled stainless steel tube, a polyurethane overmould, and a thin aluminium clip. Each was tested on DN200 steel pipe sections under controlled axial and bending loads up to 500 µε, combined with simulated soil overburden pressure of 80 kPa. Strain transfer efficiency, defined as the ratio of FBG-measured to reference strain, was 0.97 for the steel tube, 0.91 for the aluminium clip, and 0.83 for the polyurethane overmould. Corrosion resistance was assessed after 500 h of salt-spray exposure. Results favour the steel tube encapsulant for strain accuracy, whereas the clip offers faster field installation. Recommendations for selection criteria depending on application are provided.

title: FBG-based thermal monitoring of district heating pipelines: installation challenges and first operational results
abstract: District heating networks in central and eastern European cities typically operate at carrier temperatures of 70–130 °C, and thermal expansion strain in the pipeline wall can be monitored with FBG sensors to detect localised stress concentrations near fixed supports. This paper reports the installation of 36 FBG temperature and strain sensors along 820 m of a pre-insulated DN300 steel pipeline in a district heating network in a city in northern Serbia. Sensors were installed during a scheduled maintenance shutdown and attached using the steel tube encapsulation method described in earlier work by the authors. Commissioning data collected over the first heating season showed temperature gradients of up to 47 °C between adjacent measurement points during start-up transients, corresponding to thermal strains reaching 280 µε. One measurement cross-section showed anomalously elevated strain consistently 18% above its neighbours, which was traced to a partially seized expansion compensator. The system continues to operate and deliver data to the network operator.

title: Interrogation rate and spatial resolution trade-offs in FBG arrays for dynamic structural monitoring
abstract: Standard FBG interrogators using swept-laser scanning achieve interrogation rates of 1–1000 Hz, but at the upper end, signal-to-noise ratio degrades due to reduced integration time per grating. This study analyses the trade-off experimentally using a 32-grating array spanning 25 m and an interrogator capable of 2000 Hz maximum rate. Gratings were subjected to sinusoidal excitation at 0.5 Hz, 5 Hz, and 50 Hz using a piezoelectric actuator. Results show that at 100 Hz interrogation the noise floor rises from 0.8 µε to 3.1 µε compared with 10 Hz operation. A simple spectral averaging scheme with a 5-point window reduced noise at 100 Hz to 1.4 µε with a latency penalty of 50 ms. The paper provides practical guidance on choosing interrogation settings for bridge vibration monitoring, where fundamental eigenfrequencies typically fall below 10 Hz and high temporal resolution is only needed for impact events.

title: Influence of concrete carbonation on the long-term response of surface-bonded FBG sensors
abstract: FBG sensors bonded directly to concrete surfaces with epoxy adhesive are subject to degradation as carbonation proceeds and the adhesive–concrete interface weakens. To quantify this effect, 40 FBG sensors were bonded to concrete prisms with water-to-cement ratios of 0.45 and 0.60, then subjected to accelerated carbonation at 3% CO₂ concentration for periods of 4, 8, 16, and 32 weeks, corresponding to approximately 4, 9, 17, and 34 years of natural exposure in a temperate climate. Pull-off tests and strain transfer measurements were conducted at each interval. For the higher w/c ratio prisms, strain transfer efficiency dropped from 0.96 to 0.81 after the 32-week exposure. A roughened surface preparation method using sandblasting restored efficiency to 0.94 after 32 weeks of carbonation. The paper recommends surface preparation standards and periodic recalibration intervals for FBG installations on existing concrete structures.

title: A low-cost FBG readout unit for structural monitoring based on a fixed Fabry–Pérot filter and a microcontroller platform
abstract: Commercial FBG interrogators are priced at 8 000–25 000 EUR, limiting deployment density in infrastructure monitoring projects with constrained budgets. This paper describes the design and characterisation of a readout unit built around a fixed Fabry–Pérot tunable filter, a broadband ASE source, and an STM32-based microcontroller, with a total component cost below 600 EUR per channel at prototype scale. The unit supports up to four FBG sensors per optical channel, achieves a wavelength resolution of 5 pm (corresponding to approximately 4 µε), and operates at 10 Hz. Performance was validated against a commercial swept-laser interrogator over a 72 h continuous test on a steel specimen under cyclic loading. Mean absolute deviation between the two systems was 6 µε. Temperature stability over the range 0–50 °C was ensured by a thermally stabilised filter mount. The design files are described in sufficient detail to allow replication.

title: Transverse sensitivity of polymer-coated FBG sensors in pipeline hoop strain measurement
abstract: Hoop strain in pressurised pipelines is of primary interest for leak detection and wall-thinning assessment, yet FBG sensors attached to the outer pipe wall respond predominantly to axial strain. This study quantifies the transverse sensitivity of OrmoCoat-coated FBGs mounted circumferentially on DN100 steel pipe specimens at internal pressures ranging from 0 to 60 bar. The apparent axial strain contribution arising from Poisson coupling was measured at 14% of the applied hoop strain and remained consistent across three sensor batches. A correction factor derived from the elastic constants of the pipe–coating system reduced the cross-sensitivity error to below 3%. Finite element simulations using a plain-strain pipe model showed agreement within 5% with the experimental correction factors. The study provides a straightforward calibration procedure enabling circumferentially mounted FBGs to serve as practical hoop strain monitors on metallic pipelines without bespoke mechanical fixtures.

title: Review of FBG sensor deployment practices on reinforced concrete and steel bridges in the Western Balkans: 2010–2024
abstract: This review collates published and grey-literature evidence on fibre Bragg grating deployments on bridges in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro over a 14-year period. Thirty-one documented installations were identified through systematic search of conference proceedings, technical reports, and journal literature. Of these, 19 used surface-bonded sensors, 8 used embedded sensors, and 4 combined both approaches. Typical array sizes ranged from 8 to 48 gratings. Operational lifetimes of 12 months or more were reported for 22 installations; the remaining 9 were either temporary load tests or had no follow-up data. Common failure modes were adhesive bond degradation (9 cases), connector corrosion (5 cases), and interrogator malfunction (3 cases). The review identifies gaps including the absence of standardised data reporting formats and the lack of long-term validation studies beyond five years. A set of minimum reporting criteria is proposed for future deployments.

title: Formant Variability in Child Speech: A Cross-Sectional Study of Serbian Vowels Aged 6–12
abstract: This study examined formant frequency variability in Serbian-speaking children across three age groups (6–8, 9–10, 11–12 years) using a corpus of 2,400 isolated vowel tokens recorded from 80 children in two primary schools in Novi Sad. First and second formant trajectories were extracted using a Praat-based automated pipeline with manual verification of 15% of tokens. Results show that F1 variance decreases monotonically with age, while F2 variance remains elevated even in the oldest group relative to adult reference values, suggesting that the front–back dimension of the vowel space stabilises later than the open–close dimension in Serbian. Age-group differences were statistically significant (one-way ANOVA, p < 0.001 for both formants). The findings provide empirical baselines for acoustic model normalisation in child-directed automatic speech recognition for Serbian and closely related South Slavic languages. A freely licensed subset of the recordings is released alongside the paper.

title: Maximum Likelihood Linear Regression Adaptation of GMM-HMM Acoustic Models for Child Serbian
abstract: Gaussian mixture model–hidden Markov model (GMM-HMM) systems trained exclusively on adult speech show substantial word error rate (WER) degradation when applied to child speakers. This paper evaluates maximum likelihood linear regression (MLLR) and constrained MLLR (CMLLR) speaker adaptation for Serbian child speech, using a newly constructed adaptation set of 340 utterances from 34 children aged 7–11. Baseline WER on an isolated-word task was 41.3% with the unadapted adult model; MLLR adaptation with ten utterances per child reduced WER to 28.7%, and CMLLR to 26.1%. The adaptation data requirement was further analysed through a leave-one-speaker-out simulation, showing diminishing returns beyond eight utterances per speaker. Experiments used an in-house trigram language model trained on a 1.2 million word Serbian news and school-text corpus. Results confirm that standard adaptation techniques transfer to Serbian child speech but that data sparsity remains the primary bottleneck for production deployment.

title: Утицај шума учионице на перформансе аутоматског препознавања говора деце на српском
abstract: У овом раду истражује се деградација тачности аутоматског препознавања говора (АПГ) деце у условима шума карактеристичног за учионице основних школа. Снимљено је 18 часова говора у осам школа на подручју Новог Сада и Суботице употребом преносивих бинауралних рекордера. Измерени однос сигнала и шума кретао се у распону од 4 до 22 dB. Систем АПГ заснован на ДКТ особинама и тројграмском језичком моделу тестиран је без и са применом одузимања спектралног шума (spectral subtraction) и RASTA филтрације. Стопа грешака у речима порасла је са 18,4% у тихим условима на 53,7% при SNR = 6 dB без побољшања карактеристика. RASTA филтрација смањила је WER на 38,2% при истом SNR-у. Анализа грешака показује да су сугласнички скупови на почетку речи нарочито осетљиви на нискофреквентни амбијентни шум. Рад завршава препорукама за прикупљање корпуса у школским окружењима.

title: Pitch Range and Speaking Rate as Confounding Factors in DNN-HMM Child ASR for Inflected Languages
abstract: Deep neural network–hidden Markov model (DNN-HMM) acoustic models are sensitive to prosodic deviations that are systematic in child speech. This study isolates the effects of elevated pitch range and reduced speaking rate on phone error rate (PER) in a DNN-HMM system trained on 60 hours of Serbian adult broadcast speech. A controlled evaluation corpus of 120 read sentences was recorded by 40 children aged 8–13, stratified by sex and age. Pitch range was estimated from autocorrelation-based F0 extraction; speaking rate was measured in syllables per second. Multiple regression analysis confirms that both variables are independently significant predictors of PER (adjusted R² = 0.43). Phone confusion matrices reveal that voiced/voiceless distinctions and affricates are disproportionately affected under high-pitch conditions. The results motivate separate acoustic models or feature normalisation strategies for different age sub-bands, and inform the design of prosody-aware front-ends for morphologically rich language ASR.

title: Morphological Complexity as a Language Model Perplexity Driver in Serbian Child-Directed ASR
abstract: Serbian is a highly inflected language with seven grammatical cases and productive verb morphology, producing a large vocabulary whose coverage in child-speech language models (LMs) is constrained by available training text. This paper quantifies the contribution of morphological complexity to LM perplexity on child-produced utterances compared with adult utterances matched for topic domain. Three LMs were compared: a word-level trigram, a morpheme-level trigram after morphological segmentation with an open-source Serbian morphological analyser, and a neural LM (LSTM, two layers, 256 hidden units). Perplexity on the child test set was 312, 248, and 219 respectively; the morpheme-level model reduced out-of-vocabulary rate from 7.8% to 3.1%. Integration of the morpheme-level LM into a DNN-HMM decoder reduced WER by 4.2 percentage points absolute over the word-level baseline. Text data comprised 3.4 million words drawn from elementary school reading materials and subtitles from children's television programmes.

title: Transfer Learning from Adult to Child Acoustic Models Using Bottleneck Feature Extraction
abstract: Training deep acoustic models from scratch for child speech is impractical due to the scarcity of transcribed child speech corpora. This paper investigates bottleneck feature (BNF) extraction as a transfer learning strategy: a DNN trained on 80 hours of adult Serbian speech is used as a fixed feature extractor, with bottleneck activations fed into a smaller DNN fine-tuned on 6 hours of child speech. Four configurations are compared: standard MFCC baseline, BNF with no fine-tuning, BNF with full fine-tuning, and BNF with layer-wise freezing. On a continuous speech test set of 40 children aged 7–12, BNF with layer-wise freezing achieves WER of 23.4%, compared to 31.7% for the MFCC baseline and 27.1% for full fine-tuning. The results suggest that lower-layer phonetic representations generalise well across speaker populations while upper layers require task-specific adjustment. Computational cost analysis shows the fine-tuning phase completes in under three hours on a single mid-range GPU.

title: Regularisation Strategies for Child ASR Language Models Under Scarce In-Domain Text
abstract: Language models for child-directed ASR suffer from distributional mismatch when trained predominantly on adult text. This study examines four regularisation approaches—L2 weight decay, dropout, Bayesian interpolation with a background LM, and vocabulary pruning guided by age-of-acquisition norms—applied to an LSTM language model for Serbian. The in-domain training corpus consisted of 480,000 words extracted from primary school curricula, reading exercises, and transcribed children's radio broadcasts. Out-of-domain background data comprised 8.2 million words from web-crawled text. Evaluation was performed on a 2,000-utterance child speech test set with human-verified transcriptions. Bayesian interpolation combined with vocabulary pruning yielded the lowest perplexity (187) and the highest reduction in WER when coupled with a DNN-HMM decoder (WER 21.6% vs. 26.3% for the unregularised baseline). Age-of-acquisition pruning alone reduced the active vocabulary by 22% with only a 0.8-point WER increase, offering a viable compression strategy for embedded deployment.

title: Child Speech Recognition in Educational Software: A Comparative Evaluation of Commercial and Academic ASR Back-Ends for Serbian
abstract: This paper presents an independent evaluation of four ASR back-ends—two commercial cloud APIs and two academic systems built in-house—on a standardised child speech benchmark for Serbian comprising 3,600 utterances from 90 children aged 6–14. Utterances span isolated words, short phrases, and connected reading passages drawn from the national primary school curriculum. WER, sentence error rate, and latency were measured under three conditions: quiet studio, simulated classroom noise (SNR 12 dB), and real classroom recording. The best academic system outperformed the best commercial API by 6.1 WER points on the connected speech task in real classroom conditions, primarily due to language model adaptation to school vocabulary. Commercial systems performed comparably or better on isolated words, suggesting broader phone coverage from large-scale training data. The benchmark corpus and evaluation scripts are made publicly available under a Creative Commons licence to facilitate reproducibility.

title: Wav2Vec 2.0 Fine-Tuning for Child Serbian: Effect of Layer Selection and Data Augmentation
abstract: Self-supervised speech representations pre-trained on large adult corpora offer a potential route to high-accuracy child ASR without large labelled child datasets. This paper systematically evaluates fine-tuning of a wav2vec 2.0 base model (pre-trained on 960 hours of English and 480 hours of Croatian/Serbian broadcast data) for child Serbian. Five layer-selection strategies are compared: using only the final transformer layer, averaging the top four layers, learning layer weights, fine-tuning all layers jointly, and a frozen-encoder CTC head baseline. Data augmentation via SpecAugment and pitch-shift (±3 semitones) is applied to the 6-hour child training set. The combination of learned layer weighting and pitch-shift augmentation achieves WER of 19.1% on the child benchmark, versus 31.4% for the frozen-encoder baseline. Ablation shows pitch-shift augmentation accounts for 4.3 WER points of the improvement, directly addressing the elevated and variable F0 of child speakers.

title: Annotation Consistency in Child Speech Corpora: A Study of Inter-Annotator Agreement on Spontaneous Serbian
abstract: Reliable transcription of spontaneous child speech is complicated by disfluencies, coarticulation, and non-canonical pronunciation. This paper reports an inter-annotator agreement study involving five phonetically trained annotators who independently transcribed 480 utterances from 24 children aged 7–10 recorded in a semi-structured story-retelling task. Agreement was measured at word level (WER between annotator pairs) and at phone level using Cohen's κ. Mean pairwise word-level agreement was 78.4%, with the main sources of disagreement being elision of unstressed vowels (31% of conflicts), geminate reduction (18%), and word boundary placement in cliticised sequences (27%). Phone-level κ ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 across annotator pairs, indicating substantial to near-perfect agreement for most manner classes but only moderate agreement for place distinctions in obstruent clusters. Guidelines derived from the study were used to standardise annotation of the ongoing SrpChildSpeech corpus and are released as a supplementary document.

title: Дисфлуенције у читању наглас код ученика основних школа: аутоматска детекција и класификација на српском
abstract: Дисфлуенције попут понављања речи, продужења гласова и лажних почетака значајно смањују тачност система АПГ намењених образовном контексту. У овом раду предлаже се аутоматски класификатор дисфлуенција заснован на архитектури двосмерне рекурентне мреже (BiLSTM) са улазним представама на нивоу фонемских временских оквира, извученим из унапред обученог wav2vec 2.0 модела. Систем је обучен на 4,2 сата ручно анотираних снимака читања из основних школа и тестиран на независном скупу од 1,1 сата. Постигнута је F1 мера од 0,79 за категорију понављања и 0,71 за продужења, уз укупну тачност детекције дисфлуентних оквира од 83,6%. Анализа грешака показује да систем бркa кратка продужења самогласника са нагласком у стандардном говору, указујући на потребу за прозодијски свесним особинама у будућим итерацијама. Рад укључује и квалитативну анализу повезаности аутоматски детектованих дисфлуенција са оценама читалачке флуентности коју су доделили наставници.
venue: Зборник радова Телекомуникациони форум ТЕЛФОР

title: On the Adequacy of Whisper-Based Transcription for Low-Resource Child Speech in Inflected Languages: Evidence from Serbian and Slovak
abstract: Large multilingual ASR models such as Whisper offer zero-shot transcription for dozens of languages, but their performance on child speech in morphologically rich languages has not been systematically characterised. This study evaluates Whisper (small, medium, and large-v2 checkpoints) on standardised child speech benchmarks for Serbian and Slovak, both highly inflected Slavic languages with limited representation in Whisper's training data. Benchmarks consist of 4,800 utterances per language from children aged 6–14 in quiet and classroom-noise conditions. Zero-shot WER for Serbian ranges from 38.7% (large-v2, quiet) to 61.4% (small, noise), compared to 23.1% and 34.8% for a domain-adapted wav2vec 2.0 system. Morphological error analysis reveals that Whisper systematically produces grammatically plausible but inflectionally incorrect word forms, suggesting that its language model component does not adequately constrain morphological agreement in zero-shot conditions. Shallow fine-tuning on 10 hours of child speech reduces WER by 9–14 points absolute across checkpoints.
venue: Transactions on Spoken Language Processing

title: Harmonic Spectrum Interaction Between Multiple Variable-Speed Drives Sharing a Common DC Bus
abstract: Industrial plants often connect multiple drives to a shared DC bus, creating conditions for harmonic coupling not addressed by single-drive EMC standards. This paper examines the conducted emission spectra at the AC supply terminals of a two-drive, common DC-bus arrangement with drive ratings of 4 kW and 11 kW, operated with identical and deliberately offset switching frequencies. When both drives are switched at 8 kHz, intermodulation products appear at frequencies predicted by Δfsw·n (n = 1, 2, 3) and reach amplitudes 3–8 dB above the single-drive case in the 1–5 MHz range. Offsetting switching frequencies by 500 Hz suppressed the most prominent intermodulation clusters by 6–12 dB. A discrete-frequency superposition model, assuming uncorrelated switching instants, underestimates the coupled peaks by 4 dB on average, indicating partial phase coherence. Results inform both filter specification and switching-frequency assignment strategies for multi-drive installations.
venue: IET Power Electronics

title: Energy Budget Analysis for Always-On Vibration Monitoring on Coin-Cell-Powered Sensor Nodes: Sampling, Compression, and Inference Compared
abstract: This preprint reports a measurement-based energy budget for three deployment configurations of a vibration monitoring node powered by a CR2032 coin cell (225 mAh): (A) continuous full-rate sampling with BLE streaming, (B) adaptive sampling with on-chip DWT compression and label transmission, and (C) configuration B plus on-device int8 CNN inference. A custom PCB was designed around the nRF52833 SoC with a MEMS accelerometer (LIS2DH12, 3.3 V, ODR 1.344 kHz). Current draw was logged at 1 ms resolution using an external shunt-based ammeter. Configuration A depleted the cell in 18 hours. Configuration B extended life to 11.4 days. Configuration C added only 4% to the average current of B, yielding 10.9 days, because inference runs in short bursts at low duty cycle. The preprint includes the PCB schematic and firmware repository link and invites community review before journal submission.
venue: arXiv (cs.AR / eess.SP)

title: Kernel Selection and Hyperparameter Tuning for SVM-Based Modulation Classifiers
abstract: This work provides a systematic comparison of SVM kernel functions — linear, polynomial (degrees 2–4), RBF, and sigmoid — for automatic modulation classification using cyclostationary and higher-order statistical features. A labelled dataset of 18,000 waveform segments spanning BPSK, QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM, AM-DSB, AM-SSB, FM, and FSK was constructed through simulation. Feature extraction combined eight cyclic frequency magnitudes with four higher-order cumulants, resulting in a 12-dimensional input vector. Hyperparameter optimisation was performed with five-fold cross-validation over a grid search on the cost parameter C and kernel-specific parameters. The RBF kernel with C = 10 and γ = 0.05 achieved the highest mean accuracy of 93.1% across all classes and SNR levels from 0 to 20 dB. Polynomial kernels of degree 3 performed comparably above 8 dB but degraded faster at low SNR. Training and inference times are reported, and the trade-off between accuracy and computational load for real-time deployment on embedded DSP hardware is discussed.

title: Comparison of time-of-flight and phase-gradient estimators for shear-wave speed in homogeneous tissue-mimicking phantoms
abstract: Accurate shear-wave speed (SWS) estimation is fundamental to elastography-based staging of liver disease. This study evaluated two common SWS estimators—time-of-flight (ToF) cross-correlation and phase-gradient (PG) regression—using a set of twelve polyacrylamide phantoms spanning SWS values from 1.1 m/s to 3.8 m/s. Phantoms were insonated with a focused acoustic radiation force impulse on a programmable research scanner operating at 4 MHz. Lateral tracking was performed at 8 kHz pulse-repetition frequency over a 4 cm aperture. The ToF estimator showed a mean bias of 0.04 m/s and a coefficient of variation below 2.1 % across all stiffness levels. The PG estimator exhibited a systematic overestimation of 0.12 m/s at low stiffness (< 1.5 m/s), attributable to near-field phase wrapping. Both estimators degraded when lateral displacement maps contained motion artefacts exceeding 0.3 μm. The results suggest that ToF cross-correlation is preferable for stiffness ranges relevant to early fibrosis staging, whereas PG regression performs competitively at higher stiffness values corresponding to advanced fibrosis.

title: Effect of gelatin concentration and temperature on the shear modulus of tissue-mimicking gels measured by supersonic shear imaging
abstract: Tissue-mimicking phantoms used for elastography validation must have well-characterised mechanical properties across a range of temperatures encountered in laboratory and clinical settings. This work measured the complex shear modulus of gelatin-based gels (5 %, 8 %, 12 % and 16 % w/w) at temperatures from 18 °C to 37 °C using a supersonic shear imaging protocol on a research scanner. Rheometric measurements were performed in parallel on a plate-plate rheometer at 1 Hz. Shear storage moduli ranged from 0.8 kPa to 22.4 kPa. Discrepancies between acoustic and rheometric estimates exceeded 15 % for 5 % gels above 30 °C, linked to viscous loss effects that the elastic-only SWS inversion does not account for. A linear temperature correction factor of −0.31 kPa/°C was derived for 8 % gels. These data provide calibration curves directly usable for scanner quality-assurance protocols in hepatic elastography.

title: Incorporating a Kelvin–Voigt viscoelastic model into shear-wave speed inversion for liver stiffness mapping
abstract: Standard shear-wave elastography assumes purely elastic tissue, introducing bias when tissue viscosity is non-negligible, as in steatotic livers. This study implemented a Kelvin–Voigt (KV) inversion scheme that estimates both storage and loss moduli from multi-frequency shear-wave data acquired at 100 Hz, 200 Hz and 400 Hz push frequencies. Simulated displacement fields generated with a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) code for viscoelastic media were used to validate the inversion before application to nineteen excised bovine liver samples with controlled fat content (0–30 % lipid by mass). The KV inversion reduced mean SWS bias from 0.23 m/s to 0.07 m/s relative to a single-frequency elastic estimate when viscosity exceeded 1.5 Pa·s. Loss modulus estimates correlated with lipid content (Pearson r = 0.81, p < 0.001). Computational cost was approximately 340 ms per frame on a standard workstation, compatible with near-real-time feedback.

title: Shear-wave reflection artefacts at hepatic vessel walls: characterisation and a spatial-median filtering strategy
abstract: Portal vein branches and hepatic veins produce strong shear-wave reflections that corrupt local stiffness estimates in regions within approximately 5 mm of vessel walls. This paper characterises the artefact signature using controlled ex vivo experiments in which nylon cylinders (diameters 4 mm, 8 mm) were embedded in gelatin phantoms at known positions. A research scanner recorded lateral particle velocity maps for five replicate experiments per configuration. Frequency-domain analysis showed that reflected waves arrive 1.8–4.2 ms after the direct wave and contribute energy exceeding the primary wave by up to 6 dB at steep incidence angles. A 3 × 3 spatial-median filter applied to the 2D SWS map reduced root-mean-square error near vessel boundaries by 38 % without measurably degrading resolution in vessel-free zones (reduction in spatial resolution < 0.4 mm). Performance was also tested on 24 clinical B-mode-guided regions of interest from patients with biopsy-confirmed fibrosis stages F0–F4.

title: Attenuation-corrected displacement tracking for acoustic radiation force impulse imaging in steatotic liver
abstract: Elevated ultrasound attenuation in steatotic tissue reduces the amplitude of tracked shear-wave displacements at greater depths, causing apparent stiffness underestimation that mimics fibrosis regression. This study derived an analytic correction factor based on the measured frequency-dependent attenuation coefficient (estimated from spectral shift of backscattered echoes) and incorporated it into the displacement tracking pipeline of an open research scanner. The correction was validated on a three-layer phantom in which the top layer (3 cm) had attenuation coefficients ranging from 0.5 to 1.4 dB/cm/MHz, mimicking a gradient of steatosis. Without correction, SWS was underestimated by up to 0.31 m/s at 5 cm depth. After applying the correction, residual bias fell to 0.06 m/s. Retrospective application to 31 patient scans showed that the correction shifted eight cases across the F1/F2 stiffness threshold, affecting clinical staging in 26 % of cases. These findings highlight the importance of attenuation compensation in obese patient populations.

title: Quantitative ultrasound methods for tissue characterisation: elastography, backscatter and attenuation
abstract: This chapter provides a technical overview of quantitative ultrasound (QUS) approaches applied to soft tissue characterisation, with emphasis on liver. The three main modalities covered are shear-wave and strain elastography, frequency-dependent backscatter coefficient measurement, and attenuation slope estimation. For each modality, the physical basis, signal-processing chain, calibration requirements, and known sources of measurement variability are described. The chapter addresses the interdependence of the three parameters: steatosis raises attenuation and alters the apparent shear-wave speed measured at a single push frequency; fibrosis independently increases storage modulus but may reduce scatterer size. Worked examples use simulated and experimental data to illustrate typical processing pipelines. The chapter concludes with a discussion of multi-parametric fusion strategies that combine the three QUS outputs to improve the discrimination of co-existing steatosis and fibrosis, an important clinical scenario in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

title: A regularised finite-element inversion for 2D shear modulus mapping from tracked shear-wave particle velocity fields
abstract: Local SWS estimators treat wave propagation as locally planar and one-dimensional, introducing errors when wave curvature is significant or when multiple wave sources interfere. This work formulated shear modulus reconstruction as a regularised finite-element (FE) inverse problem operating on 2D tracked particle velocity fields. The forward operator relates a spatially varying shear modulus distribution to the resulting displacement field via the elastic wave equation in the frequency domain. Tikhonov regularisation with a spatially adaptive penalty parameter—set by a generalised cross-validation criterion—was used to stabilise the inversion. Synthetic tests on five heterogeneous phantoms (inclusions of 1.5–6 kPa in a 2 kPa background) showed that the FE inversion recovered inclusion modulus values with a relative error of 8.3 % compared to 21.4 % for the directional-filter local estimator. Processing time per 2D frame was 2.1 s on a 12-core workstation. Tests on 15 clinical datasets from biopsy-confirmed patients showed improved interquartile range of stiffness within a standardised region of interest.

title: Impact of acoustic window and patient body mass index on shear-wave speed measurement repeatability: a multi-operator study
abstract: Clinical shear-wave elastography measurement variability has multiple sources, including operator skill, acoustic window quality, and patient body habitus. This prospective repeatability study enrolled 68 adult patients stratified by BMI (< 25, 25–30, > 30 kg/m²) and acoustic window score (1–3, assessed by a standardised protocol). Three trained sonographers independently acquired ten SWS measurements per patient in a single session. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were computed for each BMI and acoustic window stratum. ICC ranged from 0.93 in lean patients with good acoustic windows to 0.61 in obese patients with poor acoustic windows. Bland–Altman analysis showed 95 % limits of agreement widening from ±0.18 m/s to ±0.54 m/s across the same strata. A linear mixed-effects model identified BMI as the dominant predictor of inter-operator variability (β = 0.018 m/s per kg/m², p = 0.003), with acoustic window score as a secondary predictor. These findings quantify the extent to which steatosis-related factors confound fibrosis staging by elastography in an unselected clinical population.
venue: Hepatology and Quantitative Imaging

title: Simultaneous estimation of shear-wave speed and attenuation slope from plane-wave ultrasound acquisitions: a Bayesian framework
abstract: Estimating shear-wave speed and acoustic attenuation slope from a single plane-wave acquisition sequence would reduce examination time and remove registration errors that arise when the two quantities are measured sequentially. This preprint presents a Bayesian framework that jointly infers SWS and attenuation slope from coherently compounded plane-wave data. The likelihood model accounts for noise in both shear-wave displacement tracking and spectral backscatter estimation; a Markov-chain Monte Carlo sampler with 4 000 warm-up and 8 000 sampling iterations was used for posterior inference. Validation on 20 phantoms with independently measured ground-truth values gave posterior median SWS errors of 0.05 ± 0.03 m/s and attenuation slope errors of 0.04 ± 0.02 dB/cm/MHz. Posterior credible intervals were well-calibrated (coverage probability 0.93 for nominal 0.95 intervals). A pilot application to 12 clinical datasets is reported, demonstrating feasibility and identifying artefact patterns that require further modelling.

title: Frequency-domain near-infrared spectroscopy of skeletal muscle: instrument validation against solid optical phantoms with known absorption and scattering coefficients
abstract: Frequency-domain near-infrared spectroscopy (FD-NIRS) modulates source intensity at radiofrequencies (50–500 MHz) and measures amplitude demodulation and phase shift to recover absorption (µa) and reduced scattering (µs′) coefficients independently. We constructed a single-channel FD-NIRS instrument operating at 690 nm and 830 nm with modulation at 110 MHz and validated it against 18 solid polyurethane phantom sets with µa ranging from 0.04 to 0.25 cm⁻¹ and µs′ from 4 to 14 cm⁻¹. Recovered µa values showed a root-mean-square error of 0.009 cm⁻¹ and µs′ errors below 0.6 cm⁻¹ across the full range. Crosstalk between µa and µs′ was less than 4% at the target tissue-equivalent operating point. In-vivo measurements on the vastus lateralis of five volunteers at rest yielded µa values consistent with published literature. This validation provides a traceable reference procedure for groups wishing to implement FD-NIRS for quantitative tissue spectroscopy.

title: A four-state Markov model for the gating kinetics of a voltage-gated potassium channel inferred from single-channel recordings
abstract: We present a four-state continuous-time Markov chain model fitted to single-channel patch-clamp recordings of a voltage-gated potassium channel in HEK293 cells. Recordings at seven holding potentials between −80 mV and +40 mV yielded dwell-time histograms for open and closed states. Maximum-likelihood estimation of transition rate constants was performed using the QuB-derived likelihood framework adapted in-house. The fitted model reproduces mean open times (ranging from 0.8 ms at −60 mV to 4.3 ms at +40 mV) and the voltage dependence of the open probability with a root-mean-square error below 3% across all tested potentials. Comparison with a two-state model shows that the additional closed state is statistically justified by a likelihood-ratio test (p < 0.001). The rate constants exhibit an exponential voltage dependence consistent with a partial charge displacement of 1.1 elementary charges for the activation pathway.

title: Langevin description of gating-current fluctuations in a simplified voltage-sensor model
abstract: Gating currents arise from the reorientation of charged residues in the voltage-sensing domain of ion channels and are experimentally accessible as small transient currents in the absence of ionic conduction. We construct a one-dimensional Langevin equation for the reaction coordinate of a two-particle voltage sensor, parameterised by a double-well potential whose barrier height and asymmetry are determined by the applied membrane voltage. Numerical integration using an Euler–Maruyama scheme with time steps of 0.5 μs generates synthetic gating-current traces that are compared with published experimental records from Xenopus oocyte expression systems. The spectral density of simulated gating-current noise matches the measured 1/f component below 1 kHz within a factor of 1.4. Sensitivity of steady-state gating charge to potential barrier height is computed analytically and verified numerically, showing that a 10% reduction in barrier height increases the gating-charge slope by approximately 18%.

title: First-passage time distributions for a two-state ion channel model driven by coloured noise
abstract: Standard treatments of ion-channel gating assume memoryless (white) noise in the gating variable. Here we investigate how replacing white noise with Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (coloured) noise affects the distribution of first-passage times (FPTs) from the closed to the open state. Analytical approximations based on the Stratonovich decoupling scheme are derived for the mean FPT and its variance as functions of the noise correlation time τ_c. For τ_c in the range 0.01–10 ms, the mean FPT decreases monotonically by up to 35% compared with the white-noise limit, while the coefficient of variation of the FPT distribution increases by up to 22%. Monte Carlo simulations using 10^5 trajectories per parameter set confirm the analytical predictions to within 5%. These results suggest that intrinsic membrane fluctuations with finite correlation times can measurably alter apparent channel-opening rates deduced from patch-clamp experiments if the standard white-noise assumption is uncritically applied.

title: Comparing identifiability of Markov-chain gating models using synthetic patch-clamp data
abstract: Parameter identifiability is a persistent challenge when fitting Markov-chain models to ion-channel recordings, because different model topologies can produce indistinguishable macroscopic currents. We generate synthetic single-channel datasets under controlled conditions using three canonical topologies (linear, branched, and cyclic four-state models) and ask whether maximum-likelihood fitting can recover the correct topology and rate constants. Using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria computed over 200 synthetic datasets per topology, the linear model is correctly identified in 91% of cases, the branched model in 78%, and the cyclic model in only 63% from datasets of 500 events. Increasing the dataset to 2000 events raises correct identification to 96%, 89%, and 81%, respectively. We also quantify the bias introduced by using a fixed idealisation threshold during event detection, showing that thresholds above 40% of the single-channel amplitude systematically underestimate closing rates by 8–15%.
