title: Effect of temperature on gating kinetics of a mechanosensitive channel: a stochastic modelling perspective
abstract: Mechanosensitive channels open in response to membrane tension and are important in cellular osmoregulation. We analyse the temperature dependence of gating kinetics for a bacterial mechanosensitive channel reconstituted in lipid bilayers at five temperatures (15°C, 20°C, 25°C, 30°C, 37°C). A two-state stochastic model with thermally activated rate constants is fitted simultaneously to patch-clamp data at all temperatures. The activation enthalpy for channel opening is estimated at 42 ± 5 kJ/mol and for closing at 58 ± 6 kJ/mol, implying that higher temperatures shift the equilibrium toward the open state. Simulated open-probability curves reproduce measured values with a mean absolute deviation of 2.1 percentage points. A sensitivity analysis shows that uncertainty in the lipid bilayer tension contributes more than temperature uncertainty to the variance in the fitted enthalpy values, motivating tighter experimental control of bilayer preparation protocols.

title: Numerical methods for stiff stochastic differential equations arising in ion-channel gating models
abstract: Some parameterisations of multi-state gating models lead to stiff systems of coupled stochastic differential equations, where fast and slow time scales coexist. Standard explicit Euler–Maruyama integration becomes unstable unless extremely small time steps are used, making simulations computationally prohibitive. We implement and benchmark four integration schemes—implicit Euler–Maruyama, Milstein, stochastic Runge–Kutta of order 1.5, and a split-step method—applied to a six-state gating model with rate constants spanning four orders of magnitude. Accuracy is assessed against analytical solutions available for reduced two-state submodels. The split-step method achieves the lowest global error (relative L2 norm of 0.003 at step size 0.1 ms) while maintaining stability. Runtime comparisons on a 16-core workstation show a 7-fold speed advantage over the implicit Euler scheme for 10^6-step trajectories. Freely available Python code is provided as supplementary material.
venue: Journal of Computational Physics in the Life Sciences

title: Ion channel gating as a Kramers escape problem: analytical and simulation results for asymmetric potentials
abstract: Kramers' escape theory provides a physical framework for thermally activated barrier crossing and has been applied to ion-channel gating, where the channel transitions between closed and open conformations over an energy barrier. Most treatments assume symmetric potentials, but real gating processes are asymmetric. We extend Kramers' formula to asymmetric double-well potentials and derive closed-form expressions for mean opening and closing rates as functions of barrier height, asymmetry parameter, and friction coefficient. Analytical predictions are compared with Langevin simulation results across a grid of 144 parameter combinations. Agreement is within 8% for weak-to-moderate asymmetry (|Δ| < 3 kT) and degrades to 22% for strongly asymmetric cases where the approximation assumptions break down. The friction coefficient inferred from fitting published macroscopic conductance data for a voltage-gated sodium channel lies in the range 0.6–1.1 in dimensionless units, consistent with overdamped dynamics.

title: Bayesian inference of ion-channel gating parameters using Markov chain Monte Carlo
abstract: We present a Bayesian framework for estimating rate constants of Markov-chain ion-channel models directly from idealised single-channel event lists. The likelihood is computed using the matrix-exponential formalism, and prior distributions are chosen as log-normal with means derived from published biophysical measurements. Posterior distributions are sampled using an adaptive Metropolis–Hastings algorithm run for 2 × 10^5 iterations after a burn-in of 5 × 10^4. Applied to synthetic datasets of varying length (100–5000 events), the method yields 90% credible intervals that contain the true values in 88–94% of cases, depending on dataset size. For a real patch-clamp dataset from a ligand-gated chloride channel recorded in rat dorsal-root ganglion neurons, the posterior means of the four rate constants differ by 12–18% from maximum-likelihood point estimates, and the posterior standard deviations provide explicit uncertainty quantification absent from classical approaches. Convergence is assessed via Gelman–Rubin diagnostics.

title: Stochastic resonance in a voltage-gated sodium channel model: dependence on noise amplitude and stimulus frequency
abstract: Stochastic resonance (SR) is the phenomenon whereby the addition of an optimal amount of noise enhances the detection of a weak periodic signal. We investigate SR in a six-state Markov model of a voltage-gated sodium channel by injecting a subthreshold sinusoidal voltage stimulus at frequencies between 10 Hz and 1 kHz superimposed on Gaussian white noise of variable amplitude. Channel open probability is used as the output variable. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as a function of noise amplitude exhibits a clear maximum at each tested frequency, confirming SR. The optimal noise amplitude increases from 2.1 mV at 10 Hz to 5.8 mV at 1 kHz. The peak SNR decreases by a factor of 3.2 as frequency increases over the tested range. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that intrinsic membrane noise may play a constructive role in neural signal detection at physiological temperatures.

title: Parameter estimation for multi-state ion-channel models using continuous hidden Markov models and the Viterbi algorithm
abstract: Standard analysis of single-channel patch-clamp data requires an idealisation step in which the raw current trace is segmented into discrete open and closed intervals before fitting. Idealisation introduces errors, particularly for brief events near the filter bandwidth. We reformulate parameter estimation as a continuous hidden Markov model (HMM) problem in which the raw filtered current trace is the observed sequence and the discrete gating states are hidden. The Viterbi algorithm provides the most probable state sequence given the model parameters, which are in turn optimised by expectation–maximisation. Applied to synthetic traces with a Gaussian measurement noise of 0.4 pA rms, the HMM approach recovers rate constants with 30% lower bias than threshold-based idealisation for events shorter than twice the filter dead time. On experimental data from a two-state GABA-A receptor channel, the HMM-derived closing rate is 12% higher than the value obtained by standard idealisation, consistent with missed brief closures.

title: Coupling between gating and permeation in a model potassium channel: a Fokker–Planck treatment
abstract: In most models, ion channel gating and ion permeation are treated as independent processes. Experimental evidence suggests, however, that occupancy of the selectivity filter by permeating ions can influence gate stability. We construct a two-dimensional Fokker–Planck model in which the gating coordinate and the ion-occupancy coordinate are coupled through a cross-term in the diffusion tensor. The steady-state probability distribution over the two-dimensional state space is obtained numerically on a 100 × 100 grid using successive overrelaxation. At physiological ion concentrations (140 mM K⁺), coupling reduces the predicted mean open-channel lifetime by 18% compared with the uncoupled model, and shifts the voltage of half-maximal activation by −6 mV. The magnitude of both effects scales approximately linearly with the coupling coefficient over the range explored. These predictions are testable with high-time-resolution single-channel recordings combined with varied ionic conditions.

title: Approximate Bayesian computation for ion-channel model selection when likelihoods are intractable
abstract: Computing the likelihood of a Markov-chain gating model for long, continuous patch-clamp recordings is computationally expensive and sometimes numerically unstable for models with six or more states. We implement approximate Bayesian computation sequential Monte Carlo (ABC-SMC) as a likelihood-free alternative for model selection among competing topologies. Summary statistics used in the ABC acceptance criterion include mean open time, mean closed time, open probability, variance of open-interval duration, and the first three autocorrelation coefficients of the binarised current trace. Applied to synthetic data generated under five model topologies, ABC-SMC selects the correct topology in 79–92% of replications depending on dataset size (500–3000 events). Tolerance schedules are optimised by a pilot study, reducing the number of simulations required by 40% compared with a fixed-tolerance scheme. Runtime for a six-state model on a 16-core node is approximately 3 hours per dataset, compared with 0.5 hours for a four-state model.

title: Sensitivity of gating kinetics to lipid bilayer composition: a combined experimental and modelling study
abstract: Lipid bilayer composition influences the mechanical and electrostatic environment experienced by membrane proteins and can alter ion-channel gating. We recorded single-channel activity from a reconstituted voltage-gated chloride channel in planar bilayers formed from four different lipid mixtures: pure POPE, POPE/POPG (3:1), POPE/cholesterol (4:1), and a ternary mixture approximating mammalian inner leaflet composition. Opening and closing rate constants were estimated by maximum-likelihood fitting of a three-state Markov model at holding potentials of −60 mV, 0 mV, and +60 mV. The closing rate increases by a factor of 2.3 when cholesterol content rises from 0% to 20 mol%, while the opening rate is relatively insensitive (less than 15% change). Stochastic simulations using the fitted parameters reproduce the voltage-dependence of open probability in each lipid condition with a mean absolute deviation below 3.5 percentage points. A mechanistic interpretation in terms of bilayer lateral pressure is discussed.

title: Uticaj periodičnosti supermreže na koherentni i nekoherentni doprinos transportu fonona u GaN/AlN sistemima na povišenim temperaturama
abstract: Analizirali smo prelaz između koherentnog i nekoherentnog fonon transporta u GaN/AlN supermrežama sa periodima od 2 do 30 nm u temperaturnom opsegu 300–600 K, koji odgovara radnim uslovima snažnih elektronskih uređaja. Uzorci su deponovani MBE metodom u saradnji s Institutom za mikroelektroniku i elektroniku u Bukureštu. Merenja toplotne provodnosti vršena su TDTR metodom, a rezultati su upoređeni s računarskim simulacijama zasnovanim na normalnim modovima supermreže i modelu nekoherentnog rasejanja na neravnim granicama. Pri 300 K minimum toplotne provodnosti (1,4 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) zabeležen je za period oko 5 nm, dok se pri 600 K minimum pomera prema kraćim periodima (~3 nm), što ukazuje na suzbijanje koherentnih efekata pri povišenoj temperaturi. Fononi s frekvencijama ispod 2 THz zadržavaju koherentnost čak i na 600 K za periode veće od 10 nm. Rezultati pružaju kvantitativne smernice za izbor perioda supermreže u GaN baferima za visokotemperaturne primene.

title: Positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy of ion-irradiated high-entropy alloys as candidate structural materials: preliminary results
abstract: Four multi-principal-element alloys — FeCrMnNi, FeCrMnNiCo, FeCrNiAl, and FeCrMnNiCu — were irradiated with 1 MeV Kr²⁺ ions to 0.1, 0.5, and 2 dpa at 300 °C and characterised by PALS alongside conventional ferritic RPV steel for reference. Mean positron lifetimes in the unirradiated alloys ranged from 115 ps (FeCrNiAl) to 132 ps (FeCrMnNiCu), reflecting differences in electronic density and trapping at chemical heterogeneities. After 2 dpa irradiation, the vacancy cluster component intensities in FeCrMnNiCo and FeCrNiAl were 35–50% lower than in the RPV reference steel, tentatively attributed to enhanced point-defect recombination in the chemically complex lattice. The FeCrMnNiCu alloy showed the highest cluster intensities, possibly due to Cu-assisted vacancy trapping analogous to RPV embrittlement mechanisms. These preliminary data motivate further systematic PALS studies of high-entropy alloy compositions for advanced fission and fusion applications.

title: Nonequilibrium phase diagrams of active particles with alignment interactions under spatial confinement
abstract: We study a two-dimensional system of polar self-propelled particles with Vicsek-type alignment in circular and annular confinement using event-driven Langevin simulations with up to 8000 particles. The parameter space of noise strength and packing fraction is surveyed on a 20 × 20 grid for three confinement radii (20, 50, and 100 particle diameters). We identify five distinct steady states: disordered gas, polar band, circulating flock, density-segregated rim state, and jammed cluster. Boundaries between states are mapped and compared with the unconfined Vicsek phase diagram. Confinement stabilises the circulating flock phase for noise strengths 15–40% higher than in the bulk, and suppresses the polar band phase entirely for radii below 30 particle diameters. Entropy production is highest in the circulating flock phase and lowest in the jammed cluster. We provide order-parameter time series for all five states and discuss the effect of curvature on collective motion.

title: On the Second Moment of Gaps Between Consecutive Primes up to 10^12
abstract: This paper examines the second moment of the sequence of gaps g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n for all primes up to 10^12. Using a segmented sieve of Eratosthenes optimised for cache efficiency, we enumerated approximately 3.6 × 10^10 consecutive prime pairs and computed empirical moments of the gap distribution. The second moment grows logarithmically with the upper bound, consistent with Cramér's probabilistic model but with a discernible constant factor that differs from the naive prediction by roughly 4.7%. We tabulate the distribution of normalised gaps in 200 bins and compare the resulting histogram against the Poisson and GUE spacing distributions. The data support the Poisson model for small gaps but reveal systematic deviations for gaps exceeding 4 log p. All computational results were independently verified on two separate hardware configurations to rule out arithmetic overflow errors. Source code and gap tables are provided as supplementary material.

title: Comparative Performance of Segmented Sieve Variants for Prime Enumeration Beyond 10^13
abstract: We benchmark four variants of the segmented sieve of Eratosthenes—standard, bit-packed, wheel-factored with modulus 30, and wheel-factored with modulus 210—for prime enumeration in intervals of length 10^8 located near 10^13 and 10^14. Experiments were run on a dual-socket server with 256 GB RAM and 16 physical cores. The wheel-210 variant achieves the lowest wall-clock time per prime found, with a throughput of 1.42 × 10^9 primes per second per core at the 10^13 level, representing a factor of 2.8 improvement over the standard segmented sieve. Memory access patterns are analysed using hardware performance counters, and cache miss rates are correlated with throughput degradation at larger sieve limits. The paper includes a correctness proof for the wheel decomposition and provides open-source C++ implementations. Results are directly applicable to large-scale prime-gap studies.

title: Maximal Prime Gaps in the Range [10^14, 10^14 + 2×10^10] and Comparison with Cramér–Granville Bounds
abstract: We report a systematic search for maximal prime gaps—gaps that strictly exceed all previously observed gaps—within the interval from 10^14 to 10^14 + 2×10^10. The search identifies 14 new record gaps in this range, the largest being 1442. For each record gap we record the initiating prime, the gap length, and the value of (g_n / log^2 p_n), which serves as the empirical approximation to the Cramér–Granville constant. The largest normalised gap found is 0.863, well below the conjectured upper bound of 1 but meaningfully above the median 0.63 observed in our previous work. We compare our results against heuristic bounds derived from the Cramér model and the Granville refinement, noting that the Granville bound appears tighter in this range. Statistical tests for clustering of record gaps are performed, and no significant deviation from a Poisson process is detected.

title: Arithmetic Progressions in Prime Gaps: Density Estimates via Sieve Theory
abstract: This work investigates how frequently the sequence of prime gaps (g_n) contains arithmetic progressions of length at least three. Using a combination of the large sieve inequality and a variant of the Goldston–Pintz–Yıldırım method adapted for gap sequences rather than primes themselves, we derive an upper bound on the density of three-term arithmetic progressions among gaps in the range [N, 2N] that is O(N / log^3 N). We complement the theoretical bound with computational counts over the first 10^9 prime gaps, finding approximately 6.4 × 10^6 such progressions, in reasonable agreement with the predicted order of magnitude. We also consider four-term progressions and establish that their count up to 10^9 gaps does not exceed 1.1 × 10^4, consistent with a much faster decreasing density. The paper discusses connections to the Green–Tao theorem and poses refined quantitative questions.

title: A Computational Approach to the Hardy–Littlewood Conjecture B for Twin Primes Below 10^14
abstract: Hardy and Littlewood's Conjecture B predicts that the number of twin prime pairs (p, p+2) up to x is asymptotically C_2 x / log^2 x, where C_2 ≈ 0.6601618... is the twin-prime constant. We evaluate this conjecture computationally for x = 10^k with k ∈ {10, 11, 12, 13, 14} using a multi-threaded segmented sieve. The ratio of the empirical count to the conjectured asymptotic ranges from 0.9981 at x = 10^10 to 0.9993 at x = 10^14, with the relative error decreasing roughly as 0.3 / log x, consistent with expectations from the secondary term analysis. We also test the analogous conjecture for cousin primes (gap 4) and sexy primes (gap 6), finding similar agreement. Detailed tables of counts and ratios are provided for all three prime-pair types at each scale.

title: A Distributed Sieve for Prime Gaps up to 10^15 Using MPI on a University Cluster
abstract: We describe the design, implementation, and validation of a distributed prime-gap sieve that scales across 48 compute nodes connected by an InfiniBand fabric. The algorithm partitions the sieve range into segments of length 2^32 assigned to individual MPI ranks, with a pre-sieving step using primes up to 10^8 broadcast to all ranks at startup. Load balancing is achieved through a dynamic task queue managed by a dedicated master process. The system processes the entire range from 2 to 10^15 in approximately 19 hours of wall time using 384 cores. We report gap counts, maximal gaps, and empirical moments of the gap sequence for this full range. The paper includes a formal verification that the distributed implementation produces results identical to a sequential reference implementation on the range up to 10^10.

title: Empirical Tests of Selberg's Central Limit Theorem for log|ζ(1/2+it)| via Prime Gap Statistics
abstract: Selberg's central limit theorem states that log|ζ(1/2+it)| / sqrt(log log T) converges in distribution to a standard normal as T → ∞. We explore a heuristic connection between this result and the fluctuations of prime gap sums over short ranges, using the explicit formula linking ζ to prime counting. Concretely, we compute weighted sums of prime gaps in intervals of varying length near 10^14 and track the normalised fluctuations of these sums. Comparing the empirical distribution of these normalised quantities to a standard normal via Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests at five scales (10^10 through 10^14), we find that convergence to normality is slow: at 10^14 the KS statistic is 0.031, statistically significant at the 1% level. The paper discusses what this suggests about the rate of convergence in Selberg's theorem and poses a quantitative conjecture on the rate.

title: Gaps Between Primes in Arithmetic Progressions: Verification of Generalised Elliott–Halberstam Beyond the Classical Range
abstract: The Elliott–Halberstam conjecture (EH) concerns the distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions and underpins many results about small prime gaps. We perform computational tests of the generalised EH conjecture at the level θ = 0.6 (beyond the classical Bombieri–Vinogradov range θ = 0.5) by comparing, for moduli q up to 10^6 and x up to 10^12, the actual count of primes in each residue class to the conjectured main term. The maximum relative discrepancy across all tested moduli and residue classes is 2.3 × 10^{-3}, consistent with the conjecture at this level. We also test the conjecture for θ = 0.65 and find larger fluctuations, with the maximum relative discrepancy rising to 1.1 × 10^{-2}. Tables of worst-case moduli and residue classes are provided, and potential sources of numerical bias in the test design are discussed.

title: Towards a Refined Cramér–Granville Model: Corrective Terms from Divisibility by Small Primes
abstract: Cramér's model treats primes as independently chosen with probability 1/log n, but this ignores the deterministic divisibility constraints imposed by small primes. Granville's refinement introduces a correction factor for divisibility by 2 and 3. In this paper we extend this idea systematically: we incorporate divisibility constraints for all primes up to a cutoff P_0 and derive a corrected probabilistic model as a function of P_0. For each P_0 ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}, we compare the predicted gap distribution to empirical data from our 10^15 prime gap database. The model with P_0 = 13 reduces the KS distance between predicted and observed gap distributions from 0.028 (standard Cramér) to 0.009. We provide explicit formulas for the correction factor as a product over primes up to P_0, and discuss the practical limitations of extending P_0 further due to the rapid growth of the inclusion–exclusion sum.

title: Prime Gap Sequences as Symbolic Dynamical Systems: Entropy Estimates from Large Datasets
abstract: We treat the sequence of prime gaps (g_n) as a symbolic sequence over a finite alphabet obtained by binning gap values into 50 classes. Using the prime gap database up to 10^15 compiled by our group, we estimate the topological and metric entropy of this symbolic system via the Lempel–Ziv complexity and the plug-in estimator of Shannon entropy on blocks of length up to 12. The Lempel–Ziv complexity of the first 10^10 gaps is 0.97 relative to the maximum for a random binary sequence, indicating near-maximal complexity. Block entropy estimates stabilise around H_k / k ≈ 3.91 bits for k ≥ 8. We compare these values to those for sequences generated by the Cramér model and the refined Cramér–Granville model introduced in our 2022 paper. The gap sequence appears to have strictly higher entropy than both model sequences, with a statistically significant difference of 0.04 bits.

title: An Efficient Algorithm for Computing Runs of Consecutive Small Prime Gaps and Its Application to Polignac Numbers
abstract: A Polignac number k is a positive even integer such that p_{n+1} - p_n = k for infinitely many n. Computationally, one can study the relative frequency of gap values k up to large bounds. We design a specialised algorithm that identifies, in a single pass of the sieve array, all maximal runs of primes with consecutive gaps bounded by a threshold T. The algorithm runs in O(N / log N) time for sieving up to N and uses O(sqrt(N)) auxiliary memory. Applied to the range up to 5 × 10^14, it enumerates all runs of at least five consecutive gap-6 occurrences and all runs of at least three consecutive gap-2 occurrences. We find 1.8 × 10^7 five-run gap-6 sequences and 3.1 × 10^9 three-run gap-2 sequences in this range. The gap-2 count grows roughly as N / log^4 N, consistent with a Hardy–Littlewood-type heuristic for consecutive twin primes.

title: On the Distribution of the Ratio g_n / g_{n-1} for Consecutive Prime Gaps
abstract: We study the distribution of the ratio r_n = g_n / g_{n-1} of successive prime gaps for all primes up to 10^15. The empirical distribution of r_n is heavy-tailed and right-skewed, with mean 1.006, median 0.926, and a 99th percentile of 4.71. We show that the empirical distribution of log r_n is approximately symmetric around zero with a standard deviation of 0.83, and that log r_n passes standard normality tests on restricted ranges away from the tails. The autocorrelation of the sequence (log r_n) at lag 1 is −0.12, indicating mild negative serial correlation consistent with the mean-reverting character of gap sizes near log p. We compare these statistics to those generated by the Cramér, Granville, and Maier models and find that the Maier correction accounts for part of the observed tails but not their full weight. Connections to the Cesàro mean of the gap sequence are also discussed.
venue: Novi Sad Journal of Number Theory

title: Heuristic Task Sequencing for Collaborative Robots in Small-Batch Manufacturing with Changing Workpiece Geometry
abstract: Collaborative robots in small-batch manufacturing face frequent retooling cycles in which workpiece geometry changes between batches, invalidating precomputed task sequences. This paper presents a heuristic sequencing method that re-orders a fixed set of manufacturing operations to minimise total arm travel and tool-change frequency given an updated geometric model of the workpiece, delivered as a point cloud from a structured-light scanner. The heuristic combines a greedy nearest-insertion procedure with a 3-opt post-processing step applied in task-space coordinates projected onto a 2-D reachability map of the robot. In trials on a 7-DOF collaborative arm processing 15 families of sheet-metal parts across 120 batch configurations, the heuristic reduces mean cycle time by 18.4% compared to a fixed canonical sequence and by 7.1% compared to a simulated-annealing baseline, while running in under 2 seconds on a standard workstation.

title: Tabu Search Heuristics for the Heterogeneous Workforce Scheduling Problem
abstract: We describe a tabu search framework for constructing and improving feasible schedules for a heterogeneous workforce consisting of employees with partially overlapping skill sets. The problem arises in a light-manufacturing context where tasks require combinations of up to three certified competencies and must be completed within narrow time windows over a 28-day horizon. The benchmark set comprises 15 instances ranging from 30 to 120 employees, generated from anonymised data provided by an industrial partner in the Novi Sad economic zone. The tabu search uses a compound neighbourhood that combines shift swaps, skill-reassignment moves, and day-off exchanges. A frequency-based long-term memory component was included to diversify the search after prolonged stagnation. Computational experiments show that the heuristic finds solutions within 2.1% of a known lower bound on average across all instances, with a worst-case gap of 5.8%. Run times remain below 90 seconds on a standard desktop processor for instances with up to 120 employees.

title: Weibull-based failure rate estimation for flat-die pellet presses processing mixed agricultural residues
abstract: This study applies two- and three-parameter Weibull distributions to time-to-failure data collected from eight flat-die pellet presses operating in cooperative-scale biomass facilities in Vojvodina over a 36-month observation window. A total of 214 failure events were logged across drive-shaft bearings, die-roller assemblies, and gearbox seals. Feedstock composition—straw, sunflower husk, and corn stover blends—was recorded at each batch. Shape and scale parameters were estimated by maximum likelihood with 95% confidence intervals. Results indicate that die-roller bearing shape parameters cluster between 1.8 and 2.4 for straw-dominant batches, shifting to 1.2–1.6 for high-ash sunflower husk feeds, consistent with accelerated abrasive wear. Mean time between failures for roller assemblies was 312 hours under optimal moisture (12–14%) versus 187 hours at moisture above 18%. The findings suggest that feedstock moisture is the strongest single predictor of bearing service life, with silica content a secondary but significant factor. A maintenance interval nomogram is proposed as a practical planning aid for facility managers.

title: Effect of feedstock moisture variation on ring-die wear progression in a continuous pelletisation line
abstract: Ring-die geometry measurements were taken at 250-hour intervals on a pilot-scale pelletisation line fed with willow chip feedstock at controlled moisture levels of 10%, 14%, 18%, and 22%. Die hole diameter and surface roughness were measured at nine radial positions using a contact profilometer after each interval over a total of 1,500 operating hours. At 22% moisture, mean die-hole diameter growth reached 0.31 mm by 1,000 hours, compared with 0.14 mm at 14% moisture. Surface roughness Ra increased roughly linearly under dry conditions but exhibited a step change at approximately 600 hours under wet conditions, attributed to localised corrosion pitting. A semi-empirical wear rate model incorporating feedstock moisture as a multiplicative factor on the Preston wear coefficient is calibrated against the measured data. The model predicts die replacement intervals within ±8% of observed intervals in a hold-out validation set of three commercial-scale presses. Practical guidance on moisture management to extend die service life is provided.

title: Condition monitoring of pellet press roller bearings using vibration envelope analysis under variable load conditions
abstract: Vibration signals were acquired from the roller bearing housings of two flat-die presses at a 20 kHz sampling rate over 480 hours of mixed-feedstock operation. Envelope spectrum analysis was applied after bandpass filtering in the 2–10 kHz range to isolate bearing fault frequencies associated with outer-race and inner-race defects. A comparative baseline was established during a 48-hour run on uniform dried straw. Load fluctuations caused by variable feedstock bulk density were characterised simultaneously via motor current measurements. Results show that bearing defect frequency amplitudes are suppressed during high-density feedstock runs due to increased radial loading dampening high-frequency resonance. A simple normalisation procedure using instantaneous motor current as a proxy for radial load is proposed to decouple this effect. The corrected envelope spectra show fault indicator sensitivity improvements of 15–23 dB relative to uncorrected spectra. The method is validated against two known incipient outer-race defects introduced deliberately on test bearings.

title: Stochastic degradation modelling for briquetting press toggle mechanisms subject to cyclically varying compaction forces
abstract: A gamma process model is fitted to crack growth measurements on toggle-link pins sampled from seven briquetting presses in southern Hungary and northern Serbia over 24 months. Crack length was measured by dye-penetrant inspection at each scheduled maintenance visit, yielding 94 data points across 31 individual pins. The compaction force cycle, which varies with feedstock chip geometry and flow rate, was instrumented on two presses using strain-gauged tie rods. A covariate extension of the gamma process model incorporates mean compaction force as a time-varying covariate, estimated from a moving average of the tie-rod signal. Model fitting used an expectation-maximisation algorithm; goodness-of-fit was assessed with the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic. The covariate model reduced residual variance by 34% relative to a baseline gamma process without covariates. Replacement timing optimisation under a cost-per-unit-time criterion suggests that condition-triggered replacement at 60–70% of critical crack length minimises long-run maintenance cost for the studied fleet.

title: Reliability block diagram modelling of a mobile biomass briquetting unit with redundant screw feed subsystems
abstract: A reliability block diagram was constructed for a trailer-mounted briquetting unit used in field-collection scenarios in the Pannonian Plain. The unit incorporates two parallel screw feed paths, a single-stage roller press, and a hydraulic baling conveyor. Failure data for 18 months of seasonal operation were collected from maintenance logs of six identical units owned by two agricultural cooperatives. Component-level failure rates were estimated from 47 documented failures and fitted to exponential and Weibull distributions depending on component type. System availability was computed analytically for the RBD and compared with Monte Carlo simulation results (10,000 runs). Simulation-based availability was 0.883 (90% CI: 0.871–0.895), versus 0.891 from the analytical model; the 0.9% deviation is attributed to load-sharing effects between the parallel screws not captured in the analytical model. A sensitivity analysis identifies the hydraulic pump seals and the press roller drive chain as the subsystems most limiting to system availability, together accounting for 38% of total downtime.

title: Influence of sunflower husk ash content on abrasive wear rate of pellet die steel: a laboratory pin-on-disc study
abstract: Pin-on-disc wear tests were conducted on coupons of X46Cr13 die steel—the most common die material in Vojvodina pellet facilities—using abrasive slurries prepared from sunflower husk ash at five mass fractions: 0%, 2%, 5%, 10%, and 15%. Tests were run at a sliding speed of 0.3 m/s and a normal load of 20 N for 3,600 seconds each, with three replicates per condition. Mass loss was recorded gravimetrically at 600-second intervals. Specific wear rate increased from 1.4 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N·m at 0% ash to 6.1 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/N·m at 15% ash. SEM micrographs of worn surfaces confirm a transition from ploughing-dominated to micro-cutting-dominated wear mechanisms above 5% ash content, correlated with an increase in angular silica particles in that fraction. The results provide quantitative input for updating the wear coefficient in maintenance scheduling models for pellet lines processing high-ash feedstocks. An empirical correction factor as a function of ash mass fraction is tabulated.

title: Maintenance optimisation under uncertain feedstock quality: a Markov decision process approach for pellet mill scheduling
abstract: A discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP) is formulated for scheduling preventive maintenance of pellet mill roller assemblies when feedstock quality—represented as moisture content and ash fraction—follows a stochastic switching process between three quality states: optimal, moderate, and poor. Transition probabilities between quality states were estimated from 24 months of feedstock sampling records from a Vojvodina energy cooperative. Degradation of roller surface hardness was modelled as a function of quality state using field hardness measurements taken at 200-hour intervals. The state space encompasses roller degradation level (five discrete levels) combined with current quality state; the action space covers continue, inspect, and replace. Optimal policies were found by value iteration. The resulting policy recommends accelerating inspection to every 150 hours when the quality state shifts to poor, and this triggered policy reduces expected long-run cost per operating hour by 11.4% relative to a fixed 200-hour schedule in a simulation over 10,000 hours. Sensitivity of the optimal policy to transition probability estimation error is analysed.

title: Condition-based maintenance modelling for biomass densification equipment: a review of degradation mechanisms and monitoring methods
abstract: This chapter surveys the published literature on degradation mechanisms and associated monitoring and modelling approaches for the principal machine families used in biomass densification: flat-die and ring-die pellet mills, hydraulic and mechanical briquetting presses, and screw extruders. Failure modes are categorised by subsystem—die and roller, drive train, feed and metering, hydraulic and electrical—and their dependence on feedstock physical and chemical properties is discussed. Monitoring techniques reviewed include vibration analysis, acoustic emission, motor current signature analysis, thermal imaging, and geometric wear measurement. Quantitative degradation modelling approaches—Weibull regression, gamma and inverse Gaussian process models, physics-of-failure models, and data-driven approaches—are assessed with respect to data requirements and practical applicability. Gaps identified include the limited treatment of multivariate feedstock quality effects in degradation models, the scarcity of open benchmark datasets, and the near-absence of validated models for screw extruder barrel wear. The chapter concludes with a mapping of current practice against unresolved problems to guide future research directions.

title: On-line acoustic emission monitoring for early detection of die cracking in flat-die pellet presses
abstract: Four resonant acoustic emission (AE) sensors were mounted on the die flange of a flat-die pellet press instrumented at a pilot facility in Novi Sad. The press was operated continuously for 720 hours processing corn stover pellets while die condition was assessed by periodic dye-penetrant inspection. An initial micro-crack network was confirmed by inspection at hour 480. AE hit rate, cumulative energy, and frequency centroid were computed in rolling 10-minute windows. A change-point detection algorithm (PELT with BIC criterion) applied to cumulative AE energy identified a statistically significant change point at hour 462 ± 6 hours, 18 hours before the first visual confirmation of cracking. The false alarm rate over the pre-cracking period was 0.7 alarms per 100 hours, using a threshold calibrated on a 120-hour noise baseline. The study demonstrates that AE monitoring can provide approximately 18–24 hours of advance warning for this failure mode under the tested operating conditions, sufficient for orderly production scheduling of a planned die replacement.

title: Feedstock particle size distribution as a predictor of roller bearing vibration signature in a ring-die pellet mill: an experimental investigation
abstract: Roller bearing vibration was measured on a ring-die mill fed with poplar wood chips sieved to four particle size classes: <2 mm, 2–4 mm, 4–6 mm, and 6–8 mm, and three mixture compositions. Vibration was captured at 25.6 kHz using tri-axial accelerometers mounted on both roller bearing housings. Statistical features—RMS, kurtosis, crest factor, and spectral power in the 1–3 kHz and 5–10 kHz bands—were computed per 30-second window. A one-way ANOVA confirmed significant differences in RMS (p < 0.001) and 5–10 kHz spectral power (p < 0.001) across particle size classes; kurtosis showed no significant sensitivity (p = 0.14). The coarse 6–8 mm class produced the highest bearing RMS values and was associated with intermittent slip events visible as amplitude modulations in the time-domain signal. A linear discriminant classifier trained on six vibration features achieved 84.1% correct classification of particle size regime in a leave-one-out cross-validation. The results suggest vibration features can serve as proxies for feedstock particle size in real-time process monitoring.

title: Remaining useful life estimation for pellet mill rollers integrating feedstock quality forecasts from near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: This paper proposes a remaining useful life (RUL) estimation framework for pellet mill press rollers in which the degradation model is fed with short-horizon feedstock quality forecasts derived from on-line near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. A Bayesian linear Gaussian state-space degradation model tracks roller surface wear depth, estimated from periodic laser displacement measurements. NIR spectra collected from the feedstock hopper are reduced to moisture and ash fraction estimates using a partial least squares regression calibrated on 210 reference samples. A one-step-ahead quality forecast is generated from an autoregressive model fitted to 8 weeks of historical quality records at a pellet production site in Bačka. RUL distributions are propagated forward using particle filtering. On a holdout test period of 12 weeks, the 80% credible interval of the RUL distribution captured the actual roller replacement event in 9 of 11 trials. The framework reduced average excess roller service time beyond a safe replacement threshold from 68 hours to 22 hours compared with fixed-interval scheduling.

title: Comparative evaluation of fixed-interval, condition-based, and predictive maintenance strategies for biomass pellet lines: a simulation study based on field failure data
abstract: A discrete-event simulation model of a full pellet production line—feed preparation, ring-die press, cooler, sieving, and bagging—was parameterised using failure and repair time distributions derived from 36 months of maintenance records from three commercial facilities in Vojvodina. Three maintenance strategies were compared: time-based fixed-interval (TBM), condition-based using a single vibration threshold (CBM), and predictive using the NIR-integrated RUL model developed in an earlier study (PM). Each strategy was evaluated over 10,000 simulated hours using 500 replications. Key performance indicators were line availability, number of unplanned stops, and total maintenance cost per tonne of product. CBM increased mean availability from 88.2% (TBM) to 91.6% while reducing unplanned stops by 31%. PM achieved 93.1% availability and reduced unplanned stops by 47% relative to TBM, at a modelled sensor and software cost premium of approximately 14,000 EUR per line per year. A break-even analysis shows PM becomes economically preferred over CBM at production volumes above approximately 4,200 tonnes per year for the cost structure prevailing in the studied facilities.

title: Locating scheme selection for thin-walled prismatic parts: a decision framework combining stiffness maps and process sequence constraints
abstract: Selecting a locating scheme for a thin-walled prismatic part requires simultaneously satisfying kinematic determinism, deformation limits, and process sequence constraints that restrict datum surface access between setups. This paper proposes a structured decision framework that begins with a part stiffness map derived from a coarse shell FE model, identifies candidate datum surfaces ranked by area-weighted mean stiffness, and filters them against a precedence graph of machining operations. The framework was applied to four industrial case study parts: an aluminium telecom chassis, a steel hydraulic manifold, a titanium sensor bracket, and a composite sandwich panel adapter. For each part the framework produced a ranked shortlist of locating schemes in under 30 minutes of analyst time. CMM validation of the recommended scheme on the aluminium chassis showed positional errors 31% lower than those obtained with the existing workshop scheme. The framework is expressed as a structured worksheet requiring only a coarse FE model and a feature-operation precedence table as inputs.

title: Investment Narratives in Mid-Sized Pannonian Cities: A Comparative Content Analysis of Promotional Materials
abstract: This study examines how seven mid-sized cities in Serbia, Hungary, and Slovakia construct and disseminate investment-oriented narratives through official promotional materials between 2015 and 2022. Using qualitative content analysis of 214 documents — including investment guides, municipal websites, and trade fair brochures — the paper identifies recurring rhetorical frames: labour cost advantage, geographic centrality, EU market access, and cultural heritage. A coding scheme developed in NVivo 12 was applied by two independent coders, yielding an inter-rater reliability score of Cohen's κ = 0.81. Results show that Serbian cities rely disproportionately on wage-cost arguments compared to Hungarian counterparts, which more frequently cite EU cohesion fund access. Spatial visualisation of investment promotion office activity reveals a clustering of outreach efforts toward German-speaking and South Korean investors. The paper argues that narrative homogeneity across competing cities may reduce differentiation effectiveness and suggests directions for more place-specific messaging grounded in local productive assets.

title: Stakeholder Perceptions of City Brand Identity in Subotica: A Q-Method Study
abstract: Place brand identity depends not only on the messages projected by municipal authorities but also on the perceptions held by internal stakeholders. This paper applies Q-methodology to explore how 42 stakeholders — comprising local government officials, SME managers, cultural institution representatives, and university staff in Subotica — subjectively structure their understanding of the city's brand identity. Participants sorted 36 statements derived from preliminary in-depth interviews conducted in Serbian and Hungarian. Factor analysis of the Q-sorts produced four distinct viewpoints: a heritage-centred perspective, an economic pragmatist perspective, a multicultural distinctiveness perspective, and a sceptical peripheral perspective. The sceptical peripheral factor, loaded predominantly by SME managers, reveals a disconnect between official city branding discourse and the lived economic experience of local businesses. Findings suggest that Subotica's investment promotion strategy may be more persuasive externally than internally, raising questions about stakeholder alignment in place brand co-creation processes.

title: Post-Socialist City Branding in the Western Balkans: Institutional Constraints and Strategic Responses
abstract: This book chapter situates the place branding practices of Western Balkan cities within the broader literature on post-socialist urban transformation, examining how institutional legacies — including fragmented administrative competences, underfunded investment promotion agencies, and ambiguous national brand frameworks — constrain municipal branding capacity. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 18 city marketing practitioners in four countries (Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro) conducted in 2022 and 2023, the chapter maps the typical institutional architecture of investment promotion at the city level and identifies common coping strategies. Three strategic responses emerge: delegation to national agencies, partnership with foreign development organisations, and informal diaspora outreach. The chapter contributes to comparative urbanism by demonstrating that branding constraints in the region are less about marketing expertise than about governance fragmentation and chronic resource scarcity. Policy implications address the role of regional cooperation frameworks in pooling promotional capacity.

title: Does the City Brand Message Reach the Target? Measuring Recall and Credibility Among German Manufacturing Investors
abstract: Investment promotion campaigns by mid-sized Eastern European cities frequently target German-speaking manufacturing firms, yet little empirical evidence exists on whether these messages are received, recalled, or judged credible by intended audiences. This experimental survey study recruited 117 procurement and site-selection managers at German manufacturing SMEs through an industry association panel and exposed them to six anonymised city investment promotion materials from Serbian and Hungarian cities. Participants rated each material on a 7-point credibility scale and completed an aided recall test two weeks later. Results show mean credibility scores between 3.2 and 4.8, with significant differences attributable to the specificity of labour market data presented (F(5, 692) = 11.3, p < .001). Recall rates averaged 38% for materials featuring concrete wage and infrastructure figures, versus 21% for materials relying primarily on qualitative imagery. The study provides operational guidance for investment promotion offices on structuring claims to improve both credibility and retention among this investor segment.

title: Inventory Valuation Discrepancies Between Publisher Rate Cards and Programmatic Clearing Prices: A Serbian Market Study
abstract: Rate cards—fixed price lists published by media owners—coexist with programmatic auction prices in most digital advertising markets, often differing substantially. This paper documents and attempts to explain these discrepancies for a sample of 18 Serbian digital publishers over a 24-month period (2017–2018), using a dataset assembled from publisher-shared rate cards and cleared programmatic CPMs provided by a regional SSP. For each publisher, a discrepancy ratio was computed as the ratio of average programmatic clearing CPM to the relevant rate card CPM for matched format-and-position combinations. Median discrepancy ratios ranged from 0.31 to 0.78 across publishers, indicating that programmatic prices cleared at 31–78 percent of rate card prices. Regression analysis related discrepancy ratios to publisher size, fill rate, direct-sales team size, and use of floor pricing. Publishers with active floor price management showed significantly smaller discrepancies (p < 0.05). The paper argues that rate card design and floor price calibration constitute a practical inventory valuation problem amenable to hedonic pricing logic.

title: The Effect of Remote Selling Conditions on Adaptive Selling Behaviour: A Study of Industrial Salespeople During the COVID-19 Disruption
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic forced abrupt shifts to remote and hybrid selling modes across industrial sectors. This study examined how this transition affected adaptive selling behaviour among 228 B2B sales representatives in Serbia and Hungary surveyed in late 2020. A difference-in-differences logic was approximated by comparing pre-disruption and within-disruption adaptive selling scores from a subset of 91 respondents who had participated in an earlier panel. Results indicated a statistically significant decrease in perceived adaptiveness (Δmean = −0.61, paired t-test p < 0.001), driven primarily by reduced access to non-verbal customer cues and loss of informal meeting contexts. Salespeople with prior experience using video conferencing tools in sales showed smaller decreases. Moderating effects of CRM system quality on the decline were tested and found significant only for firms using CRM systems with integrated communication logging. The paper discusses implications for virtual selling training and tool selection in industrial organisations.
venue: Proceedings of the Pan-European Conference on Sales and Distribution Management

title: Integracija proteomskih i metabolomskih podataka u heterogene grafove znanja za predviđanje interakcija lek–meta
abstract: U ovom radu predlažemo okvir za konstrukciju heterogenih bioloških grafova znanja koji objedinjuje proteomske podatke iz baze UniProt (oko 42 000 humanih proteina), metabolomske podatke iz baze HMDB (oko 114 000 metabolita) i poznate interakcije lek–meta preuzete iz baze DrugBank verzija 5.1. Nad konstruisanim grafom primenjena je arhitektura grafovske neuronske mreže zasnovana na relacijskom konvolucijskom operatoru (R-GCN) za zadatak predikcije veza. Evaluacija je sprovedena na skupu od 8 400 pozitivnih i 8 400 negativnih parova lek–meta u postavci petnaesterostruke unakrsne validacije. Model postiže AUROC vrednost od 0,871 i AUPR vrednost od 0,843 na test skupu, što predstavlja poboljšanje u poređenju sa bazičnim modelima koji koriste isključivo sekvencijalne ili strukturne karakteristike. Analiza doprinosa čvorova različitih tipova ukazuje da metabolitski kontekst konzistentno povećava preciznost predikcije za enzimske mete. Kod i podaci su javno dostupni.

title: Benchmarking Graph-Based Encoders for Link Prediction on Biological Interaction Networks
abstract: Predicting interactions between biological entities from graph-structured data has become a standard task in computational drug discovery, yet systematic comparisons of graph encoder architectures on standardised biological benchmarks remain scarce. We evaluate seven graph neural network encoders—GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, R-GCN, HAN, HGT, and a simple MLP baseline—on four publicly available biological interaction datasets covering protein–protein, drug–target, drug–drug, and metabolite–enzyme interactions. All models are trained under identical hyperparameter search budgets using Optuna (100 trials per configuration) and evaluated with five-fold cross-validation. Results show that HGT achieves the highest average AUROC (0.884) across datasets but requires approximately 3.4× more wall-clock training time than R-GCN, which places second overall. For smaller datasets (fewer than 5 000 edges), GraphSAGE with mean aggregation matches transformer-based methods at a fraction of the computational cost. We release a reproducible benchmarking pipeline and preprocessed dataset splits to facilitate future comparisons.
venue: Proceedings of the 12th Balkan Conference on Bioinformatics and Computational Biology

title: Stability of cell-type clusters under random seed variation in UMAP and t-SNE: a systematic evaluation
abstract: Both UMAP and t-SNE rely on stochastic optimisation and are therefore sensitive to random initialisation. Although this is widely acknowledged, few studies have quantified the degree of instability in cluster assignments across seeds in realistic scRNA-seq workflows. This work ran UMAP and t-SNE each with 500 distinct random seeds on six datasets ranging from 2,000 to 60,000 cells, recorded Leiden cluster assignments at resolution 0.5, and computed pairwise adjusted Rand index across all seed pairs. Median pairwise ARI exceeded 0.85 for UMAP in four of six datasets, indicating acceptable stability for large datasets. For the two smallest datasets (under 5,000 cells), median ARI dropped to 0.61–0.68, suggesting that published cluster counts and marker gene lists derived from single runs may be unreliable. Initialising UMAP with PCA-derived coordinates substantially reduced variance, bringing median ARI above 0.90 in all tested datasets. Reporting requirements and minimum seed replication counts were recommended.

title: Manifold learning in the presence of high dropout rates: comparison of PHATE, UMAP, and force-directed graph layouts
abstract: Dropout—zero counts arising from failed capture rather than true absence of expression—is a defining feature of low-depth scRNA-seq data and poses challenges for manifold learning methods that rely on local neighbourhood geometry. This study compared PHATE, UMAP, and a force-directed graph layout (ForceAtlas2 applied to a shared nearest-neighbour graph) on seven datasets with experimentally measured dropout rates between 60% and 92%. Synthetic dropout was introduced into a near-complete dataset to establish ground truth trajectories. PHATE preserved continuous developmental trajectories more accurately than UMAP at dropout rates above 80%, measured by geodesic distance correlation between true and embedded positions. UMAP outperformed PHATE at preserving discrete cluster boundaries in datasets with known discontinuous cell-type transitions. ForceAtlas2 performed intermediately across metrics. The study concluded that method selection should be guided by whether the biological question concerns continuous differentiation or discrete cell-type identification.
venue: Journal of Computational Genomics and Transcriptomics

title: Difference-in-Differences Analysis of Nitrate Regulation Changes and Colorectal Cancer Incidence in Rural Municipalities of Northern Serbia
abstract: Elevated nitrate concentrations in drinking water have been hypothesised to increase colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, but causal evidence from observational data remains limited due to self-selection into water source use and correlated rural risk factors. This study exploited a 2015 regulatory tightening of maximum allowable nitrate levels in public water supplies across selected municipalities in northern Serbia as a natural experiment, applying a difference-in-differences (DiD) framework. The treated group comprised 11 municipalities where utility upgrades reduced mean nitrate concentrations from 47.2 mg/L to 18.6 mg/L between 2015 and 2017. A matched control group of 13 municipalities with stable low nitrate levels served as the comparison. CRC incidence data from 2008 to 2022 were obtained from the Serbian Cancer Registry. Parallel trends were supported in the pre-period (2008–2014). The DiD estimate indicated a 14% reduction in age-standardised CRC incidence rate (IRR 0.86, 95% CI: 0.74–0.99) in treated municipalities five years post-intervention. Heterogeneity analyses suggested the effect was more pronounced among individuals over 60. Event-study plots showed no anticipation effects.
venue: Epidemiology Letters

title: Sensitivity of Causal Effect Estimates to Unmeasured Confounding in Environmental Cohort Studies: A Comparison of E-value and Partial R² Approaches
abstract: Quasi-experimental designs such as instrumental variables and difference-in-differences are increasingly used in environmental epidemiology, but their assumptions are untestable in practice and researchers rarely report quantitative sensitivity analyses. This paper systematically compared two approaches to unmeasured confounding sensitivity—the E-value method and the partial R² framework—applied to four published environmental exposure–health outcome studies from the Balkan region. For each study, effect estimates were re-analysed using both sensitivity metrics, and the minimum unmeasured confounding strength required to nullify reported associations was computed. Across the four studies, E-values ranged from 1.38 to 3.12, with lower values clustered in studies using self-reported exposure proxies. Partial R² thresholds suggested that confounders explaining less than 8% of residual outcome variance would be sufficient to explain away two of the four reported associations. The paper argues for routine reporting of at least one sensitivity metric in observational environmental health papers and provides an accessible R implementation accompanying the analysis. No new primary data were collected; all source datasets were obtained from published supplementary materials.
venue: Proceedings of the Regional Workshop on Quantitative Methods in Environmental Health Research, Subotica

title: Stability of Variable Selection in High-Dimensional Survival Models: A Resampling Perspective
abstract: Regularised variable selection for survival outcomes is known to produce unstable feature sets across repeated samples, yet few studies have quantified this instability in multi-omics contexts. This work systematically assessed selection stability using Jaccard similarity and the Nogueira stability index across 200 bootstrap resamples in four published cancer survival datasets (colon, ovarian, glioblastoma, bladder; total n = 1,847). LASSO, ridge, elastic net (α = 0.5), and the adaptive LASSO were compared. Adaptive LASSO showed the highest average stability (mean Jaccard 0.48) while maintaining competitive C-index values. Features with selection frequencies below 40% contributed negligible predictive information when removed from refitted models. The study advocates reporting selection frequency alongside point estimates in high-dimensional survival analyses and proposes a simple threshold-based ensemble approach that improved both stability and predictive performance.
venue: Biometrical Journal

title: Dative and Instrumental Case Merger in Early 19th-Century Bács-Bodrog Administrative Texts
abstract: This paper examines the partial neutralisation of dative and instrumental case endings in a corpus of 214 administrative documents produced by the Bács-Bodrog County Chancellery between 1810 and 1840. The manuscripts were transcribed manually from microfilm holdings at the Historical Archive of Subotica and encoded in a custom TEI-compatible XML schema. Quantitative analysis of 1,847 noun phrases shows that merger forms appear significantly more often in lower-register formulaic passages (38.4%) than in petitions and reports addressed to Vienna (9.1%), suggesting register sensitivity rather than a straightforward sound change. The paper argues that the pattern reflects scribal training norms imported from Hungarian chancery schools rather than contact pressure from contemporary Serbian or German administrative practice. Distributional chi-square tests and token-frequency counts are provided for all major declension classes, and a selection of manuscript images is included as supplementary material.

title: Verbal Suffix Alternation in Reformed Church Matriculation Books of Vojvodina, 1820–1870
abstract: Reformed Church parish registers from twelve congregations in the Vojvodina region constitute the primary data source for this study of the alternation between definite and indefinite verbal agreement suffixes in object clauses. The corpus comprises approximately 9,400 finite verb tokens extracted from 67 manually transcribed baptismal and marriage registers. The analysis focuses on the conditioning factors for so-called iktelen forms appearing in environments where ikes paradigms would be normatively expected. Results indicate that the frequency of non-normative forms correlates with the education level of the registering clergyman as recoverable from diocesan personnel files, and with the distance of the congregation from the regional ecclesiastical centre in Novi Sad. A logistic regression model with four predictors correctly classifies 74% of tokens. The findings are compared with contemporary prescriptive grammars, particularly the widely circulated textbook series by Miklós Revay published in Pest.

title: Formulaic Variation in Notarial Wills from the Subotica Magistracy, 1795–1825
abstract: Notarial wills deposited at the Subotica City Archive offer a relatively homogeneous text type for tracking morphosyntactic variation within a controlled genre. This study analyses 88 complete will documents, totalling around 31,000 running words, with attention to relative clause formation, postpositional phrase order, and the placement of negation in embedded clauses. Transcription was performed by the author with quality-checked double-reading of 20% of the sample. Key findings include a steady decline across the period in the use of Latin-influenced participial constructions, replaced by finite subordinate clauses, and increasing frequency of German loan syntax in property enumeration passages. The paper contextualises these shifts within the broader Josephinist administrative reforms that mandated Hungarian-language documentation in the 1790s and their uneven local implementation. Manuscript facsimiles of three representative documents are appended.

title: Code-Switching between Hungarian and German in Subotica Magistracy Protocols, 1800–1850
abstract: Drawing on a 47,000-word corpus of Subotica Magistracy session protocols from the first half of the 19th century, this chapter investigates patterns of intra-sentential and inter-sentential code-switching between Hungarian and German. The analysis applies Myers-Scotton's matrix language frame model and examines which morphosyntactic categories most frequently involve German-origin material. German embedded language islands are most common in legal terminology, property description, and direct quotation of imperial rescripts, together accounting for 81% of all German-language insertions. The chapter further documents gradual reduction of German usage across the period, particularly after the 1830s, correlating with the intensification of language planning activities in the Hungarian Diet. Archival evidence is provided for the linguistic backgrounds of the scribes responsible for the largest portion of the corpus documents.

title: Postpositional Phrase Order and Information Structure in 19th-Century Ecclesiastical Correspondence
abstract: Correspondence exchanged between Reformed and Catholic parish priests and their diocesan superiors in Vojvodina provides an unusually well-stratified genre for investigating the relationship between morphosyntactic order and information structure across the 19th century. Using 62 letter sequences (totalling about 24,000 words) from the Diocesan Archives in Novi Sad, this study codes postpositional phrases for topicality, focality, and clause position. Quantitative results show that topic-marking postpositional phrases in sentence-initial position increase from 22% of all instances in the 1810–1830 sub-corpus to 41% in the 1870–1890 sub-corpus, a pattern consistent with typological expectations for increased pragmatic differentiation under written standardisation. The paper discusses whether the change originates in contact with the prestige written norm emerging from Pest-Buda or reflects independent local developments in Vojvodina ecclesiastical writing.

title: Noun Phrase Agreement in Serbian Loanwords within Bács-Bodrog County Tax Registers, 1815–1865
abstract: Tax registers from the Bács-Bodrog County Archive contain a substantial number of South Slavic proper nouns and common nouns, chiefly denoting settlement names, land types, and occupational terms. This study examines how Hungarian morphological agreement—case suffixation, postpositional government, and adjectival concord—was applied to 764 distinct Serbian-origin lexemes attested across 41 registers. Three integration patterns are identified: full integration with regular Hungarian declension (52% of tokens), hybrid forms with Serbian stem and Hungarian suffix (31%), and uninflected citation forms (17%). Integration rate correlates with the frequency of the lexeme in the corpus and inversely with its phonological distance from Hungarian canonical forms. The findings are compared with parallel phenomena documented for German loanwords in the same corpus, revealing that Serbian loans achieve full morphological integration more rapidly, possibly because of typological similarities in stem structure.

title: Subordinate Clause Types in Legal Instruments from Vojvodina, 1840–1900: A Frequency Survey
abstract: This survey maps the range and frequency of subordinate clause types in a stratified sample of 120 legal instruments—contracts, deeds, inheritance settlements, and manumission documents—drawn from the BacsBodrog Manuscript Corpus. Each document was syntactically parsed manually for main and subordinate clause boundaries, yielding 6,312 subordinate clause tokens assigned to 14 clause-type categories following a scheme adapted from historical Hungarian grammars. Relative clauses constitute the largest category (28.4%), followed by indirect speech complements (19.1%) and conditional clauses (15.3%). Temporal subordination shows the sharpest increase across the six decades studied, which the paper links to increasing complexity of temporal reasoning in mid-century property and inheritance law. The paper includes a comparison with contemporaneous printed legal handbooks to assess how closely scribal practice tracked prescriptive norms.

title: Spelling and Morphophonological Variation in Mid-Century Hungarian School Inspection Reports, Vojvodina 1855–1880
abstract: School inspection reports from the period of Austrian neo-absolutism offer a largely unstudied source for the history of written Hungarian in Vojvodina. This paper presents analysis of 34 inspection reports filed by district school supervisors between 1855 and 1880, with total length approximately 19,500 words. The focus is on morphophonological alternations in verbal derivational suffixes (-gat/-get, -tat/-tet) where spelling variation in the corpus reflects uncertainty about vowel harmony application to borrowings and derivatives. Out of 918 relevant tokens, 23% show a spelling that contradicts the vowel harmony rule as codified in contemporary orthographic guides. Frequency of non-standard forms is higher in reports from supervisors documented as having German as their first language. The paper also notes interaction between spelling variation and suffix length variation in the diminutive nominal suffix.

title: Passive and Impersonal Constructions in Hungarian Administrative Prose: Evidence from the BacsBodrog Corpus
abstract: The present paper investigates the distribution and decline of synthetic passive constructions (formed with the suffix -tatik/-tetik) and competing impersonal active strategies in administrative Hungarian over the 19th century, using the full 78,000-token BacsBodrog Manuscript Corpus supplemented by 12,000 tokens of newly transcribed county council minutes from 1890–1905. Passive -tatik/-tetik forms account for 6.2% of all finite verbs in documents from the 1800–1830 period, falling to 1.4% in the 1870–1900 period. Replacements include impersonal third-person plural constructions and nominalised passive-like noun phrases. The paper tests three explanatory hypotheses: language planning pressure against the passive, German influence via calqued constructions, and functional expansion of nominal style in bureaucratic prose. Evidence best supports the third hypothesis, with language planning playing a secondary role from the 1870s onward.

title: Annotation Guidelines for Morphosyntactic Tagging of 19th-Century Vojvodina Hungarian: Version 2.0
abstract: This technical report presents revised annotation guidelines developed for the second release of the BacsBodrog Manuscript Corpus, expanding coverage from 78,000 to approximately 145,000 tokens. Version 2.0 introduces four new annotation layers: a semantic role layer for predicate-argument structures, a document-type classification tag, a scribe-identity link to an external prosopographical database, and a reliability flag for passages of difficult legibility. The report documents the resolution of 23 systematic ambiguities identified in Version 1.0, particularly concerning the boundary between derivational and inflectional morphology in productive historical suffixes and the treatment of abbreviation tokens. Inter-annotator agreement on the morphological layer was reassessed on a fresh 8,000-token sample, yielding κ = 0.86, compared with 0.83 for Version 1.0. The report is intended as a reference document for researchers reusing the corpus and for teams developing comparable historical corpora of minority languages in the region.

title: The Spread of the Analytic Comparative in Vojvodina Hungarian Administrative Writing, 1830–1900
abstract: Standard 19th-century Hungarian possessed both synthetic (suffix -bb) and analytic (inkább + positive adjective) comparative constructions, but their distribution in administrative prose has not been studied empirically. Using the expanded BacsBodrog Manuscript Corpus (145,000 tokens), this paper extracts all 1,129 comparative adjective tokens and codes each for construction type, syntactic position, and adjective frequency class. Analytic comparatives rise from 8% of all comparatives in the 1830–1850 sub-corpus to 19% in the 1880–1900 sub-corpus. The increase is concentrated in evaluative passages of reports and petitions rather than in formulaic legal boilerplate. A parallel analysis of 14,000 tokens of printed administrative guides from Budapest reveals no corresponding increase, suggesting a Vojvodina-specific local development. The paper proposes that the shift reflects influence from German periphrastic comparative constructions mediated through bilingual scribes rather than a general trend in written Hungarian.

title: Prosopography of Bács-Bodrog County Scribes, 1790–1870: A Database and Methodological Overview
abstract: The linguistic analysis of historical manuscripts depends critically on identifying the individuals who produced them. This paper describes a prosopographical database of 218 scribes active in Bács-Bodrog county administrative and ecclesiastical institutions between 1790 and 1870, compiled from diocesan personnel registers, county employment records, and university matriculation lists held at archives in Subotica, Novi Sad, Eger, and Budapest. For each scribe, the database records documented language competences, education, dates of service, and the manuscripts in the BacsBodrog Corpus attributable to them with confidence levels. Of the 218 scribes, 134 have at least one language competence recorded in archival sources; 47 were documented as trilingual in Hungarian, German, and Latin, and 29 as bilingual in Hungarian and Serbian. The paper discusses the methodology of attribution, sources of error, and plans for public release of the database as a linked open dataset.

title: Morphosyntactic Complexity and Genre in Vojvodina Hungarian Manuscripts: Quantitative Profiles Across Five Document Types
abstract: This paper develops quantitative profiles of morphosyntactic complexity for five administrative and ecclesiastical document genres—petitions, council minutes, church accounts, marriage contracts, and episcopal circulars—using a 60,000-token stratified sample drawn from the BacsBodrog Manuscript Corpus, balanced across three time slices (1810–1840, 1850–1870, 1880–1900). Complexity is operationalised through seven measures: mean clause length, subordination ratio, nominal-to-verbal ratio, average case-suffix chain length, frequency of participial modifiers, passive verb proportion, and type-token ratio of inflectional suffixes. Results show that episcopal circulars consistently score highest on five of seven measures and petitions lowest on four, while council minutes display the highest variability across time slices. The paper argues that genre-internal standardisation accelerated after 1867 for institutional document types but not for petitions, which retained high individual variation throughout. Implications for sampling design in historical corpus studies are discussed.

title: Code-Switching Patterns in Informal Written Communication among Young Bilinguals in Vojvodina
abstract: This sociolinguistic corpus study analyses code-switching behaviour in 4,800 WhatsApp and SMS messages collected from 96 bilingual participants aged 18–28 in Subotica, recruited via snowball sampling with informed consent in 2020. Participants self-identified as balanced or Hungarian-dominant Serbian–Hungarian bilinguals. Each message was tokenised and language-tagged using the SHLC tagger; 312,000 tokens were analysed in total. Inter-sentential, intra-sentential, and tag switches were distinguished following Myers-Scotton's Matrix Language Frame model. Results show that 38% of messages contain at least one code-switch, with intra-sentential switches accounting for 54% of all switching events. Noun phrases are the most frequent site of switching (41%), followed by discourse markers (22%). Switching frequency correlates positively with self-reported Hungarian dominance (r = 0.44, p < 0.001) and negatively with formal education conducted in Serbian (r = −0.31, p < 0.01). The study provides a descriptive baseline for future computational modelling of switch-point prediction.
venue: Journal of Bilingualism and Language Contact in Central Europe

title: Adapting Pre-Trained Language Models for Low-Resource Code-Switched Serbian–Hungarian NLP Tasks
abstract: Pre-trained multilingual transformer models such as mBERT and XLM-R perform poorly on code-switched text involving low-resource language pairs, partly because code-switching examples are absent from their pre-training corpora. This study investigates continued pre-training of XLM-R-base on a 900,000-token subset of the SHLC corpus using a masked-language-modelling objective, then fine-tuning the resulting model on three downstream tasks: language identification, POS tagging, and grammar-error detection. Fine-tuning datasets contain 7,200, 5,800, and 4,100 labelled examples respectively. Continued pre-training yields consistent gains over the baseline: +4.1 percentage points on language identification accuracy, +5.8 on POS tagging F1, and +6.3 on error-detection F1. Ablation experiments show that gains are largest for Hungarian-origin tokens and intra-sentential switch points. The paper discusses computational cost constraints and proposes a lighter adapter-based variant that achieves 80% of the improvement at 12% of the training cost.

title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Hyperbola Detection in GPR B-Scans for Routine Utility Survey Processing
abstract: Manual interpretation of GPR B-scans is time-consuming and operator-dependent, particularly for large-scale cadastre surveys producing hundreds of radargrams per day. This study trained and tested a convolutional neural network to detect hyperbolic reflections indicative of buried point and linear targets in B-scans collected with 500 MHz and 250 MHz antennas over urban streets in Novi Sad. A labelled dataset of 8,400 B-scan images with 22,310 annotated hyperbolas was assembled from three years of field surveys. The network achieved precision of 0.87 and recall of 0.84 on a held-out test set, outperforming a matched-filter baseline (precision 0.73, recall 0.71). False positive rate was highest for tree root reflections and reinforced concrete slab edges. Integration into a semi-automatic processing pipeline reduced per-radargram interpretation time from an average of 4.2 minutes to 1.1 minutes, with human expert review retained for flagged ambiguous cases. The labelled dataset is made available for benchmarking.
venue: Computers and Geotechnics

title: Assessing Positional Discrepancies Between As-Built GPR Surveys and Operator GIS Records for Low-Voltage Cable Networks in Vojvodina
abstract: Low-voltage distribution cable networks in Vojvodina were largely installed between 1965 and 1990 and digitised from paper sketches of variable quality. This study quantified positional discrepancies between independent GPR-based cadastre surveys and operator-held GIS records for 47.3 km of low-voltage cable routes across nine settlements of varying population density. A 500 MHz GPR system was used, with RTK-GNSS referencing. Discrepancies were decomposed into horizontal offset, depth-of-burial error and missing-segment rate. Mean horizontal offset was 0.81 m with a 95th percentile of 2.34 m; depth errors averaged 0.24 m. Missing segments constituted 8.4% of total surveyed length. Discrepancy magnitude was significantly correlated with settlement age and with the decade in which original records were created. Rural settlements with records predating 1980 showed missing-segment rates exceeding 15%. Findings support a prioritised re-survey programme targeting pre-1980 rural records.
