title: Razvoj instrumenta za dijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u organima lokalne samouprave
abstract: U radu je prikazana procedura razvoja i pilot-testiranja upitničkog instrumenta za procenu zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u organima lokalne samouprave. Instrument se oslanja na petostepeni model zrelosti izveden iz Crawfordovog CMM-I okvira, prilagođenog za postsocijalistički administrativni kontekst. Upitnik sadrži 54 stavke raspoređene u šest dimenzija: strategija znanja, kultura, procesi, tehnologija, merenje i liderstvo. Pilot-testiranje je sprovedeno u deset opština u Srbiji i Severnoj Makedoniji (N = 187 ispitanika). Konfirmatornom faktorskom analizom (CFA) potvrđena je šestofaktorska struktura (CFI = 0,94; RMSEA = 0,061). Cronbachov alfa koeficijent po dimenzijama kretao se od 0,71 do 0,86. Rad sadrži preporuke za dalju primenu instrumenta u regionalnim komparativnim studijama.

title: Organizacione prepreke uvođenja sistema upravljanja znanjem u javnim preduzećima: studija slučaja u energetskom sektoru Srbije
abstract: Rad analizira organizacione prepreke s kojima se suočavaju javna preduzeća u energetskom sektoru pri pokušaju uvođenja formalnih sistema upravljanja znanjem. Studija slučaja sprovedena je u tri javna preduzeća (ukupno 2.100 zaposlenih) primenom kombinovane metodologije: analiza internih dokumenata, posmatranje sa učešćem tokom tri meseca i 22 dubinska intervjua sa menadžerima i stručnjacima. Identifikovano je pet kategorija prepreka: otpor menadžmenta srednje linije, nejasna vlasnička struktura znanja, nedostatak podsticajnih mehanizama, fragmentisani IT sistemi i diskontinuitet strateškog liderstva. Utvrđeno je da prepreke nije moguće razumeti izolovano od specifičnog institucionalnog nasleđa, pre svega od hijerarhijske kulture i kratkih mandata rukovodilaca. Predložen je okvir za prioritizaciju intervencija koji uzima u obzir i resursna ograničenja karakteristična za javna preduzeća u tranziciji.

title: Integrating Knowledge Audit Methods into Public Sector Strategic Planning: Lessons from Two Vojvodina Pilot Projects
abstract: This chapter describes the design and outcomes of two pilot knowledge audits carried out in Vojvodina public institutions in 2016 and 2017 as part of a capacity-building initiative. The first pilot was conducted in a regional development agency (58 employees) and the second in a district administrative office (31 employees). Each audit combined a structured inventory of documented knowledge assets, network analysis of internal expertise flows, and individual competence mapping through a standardised card-sorting exercise. The chapter reports how findings were fed into each institution's three-year strategic plan and identifies the conditions under which audit results were actually used: senior management engagement, a dedicated knowledge coordinator role, and visible quick wins in the first six months. Conditions absent in one of the two pilots are linked to partial non-adoption of recommendations, illustrating the gap between diagnostic capacity and implementation readiness in under-resourced public bodies.

title: Merenje uticaja programa obuke na transfer znanja u opštinskim upravama: pre-post studija
abstract: Rad ispituje u kojoj meri strukturirani programi obuke dovode do merljivog transfera znanja u svakodnevnu praksu opštinskih službenika. Istraživanjem je obuhvaćeno 214 učesnika obuke u jedanaest opština u Srbiji tokom 2018. i 2019. godine. Primenom Kirkpatrickijevog četvorostepenog modela evaluacije, podaci su prikupljani na četiri tačke merenja: neposredno pre, neposredno posle, tri i šest meseci nakon završetka obuke. Instrumenti su uključivali standardizovane testove znanja, procenu nadređenih i analizu administrativnih ishoda (broj procesiranih predmeta, broj grešaka, vreme obrade). Rezultati pokazuju statistički značajan porast u znanju neposredno posle obuke (d = 0,74), ali znatan pad transfera na nivou prakse u šestomesečnom praćenju: samo 31% učesnika primenjivalo je stečene veštine. Kao ključni moderatori identifikovani su podrška neposrednog rukovodioca i prilike za primenu na radnom mestu.

title: Do E-Government Investments Translate into Knowledge Management Capability? Evidence from Serbian Municipalities 2015–2020
abstract: E-government projects are often justified partly on the grounds that digitisation of records and processes will improve organisational knowledge management. This paper tests that claim empirically using panel data from 120 Serbian municipalities over a five-year period. E-government investment levels were drawn from Ministry of Finance budget execution reports; knowledge management capability was operationalised using the six-dimension maturity instrument assessed at the beginning and end of the observation window (N = 720 matched responses from 1,440 municipal civil servants). Fixed-effects regression models show that investment in e-government is positively associated with improvements in the technology and process dimensions of knowledge management maturity (β = 0.28 and 0.21 respectively, both p < 0.01), but shows no significant association with the culture, strategy, or leadership dimensions. The paper argues that technology investment is a necessary but not sufficient condition for organisational knowledge capability, and that current e-government programmes in Serbia are not accompanied by the complementary organisational interventions needed for broader maturity gains.

title: Toward a Revised Maturity Framework for Knowledge Management in Post-Socialist Public Institutions: Theoretical Grounding and Empirical Refinement
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical foundations and empirical refinement of a revised five-level knowledge management maturity framework specifically designed for public institutions in post-socialist contexts. The revision draws on three sources: a critical review of existing frameworks (n = 31); expert consultation with 18 practitioners and academics from Serbia, Slovenia, Hungary, and Romania conducted via Delphi rounds; and item-level analysis of data from 490 respondents across four countries collected between 2019 and 2022. The framework retains six dimensions but reorganises subordinate indicators to reflect characteristics documented in post-socialist institutions: high procedural formalisation coexisting with low strategic coherence; strong interpersonal knowledge networks alongside weak documentation cultures; and recurrent disruption of learning cycles by leadership turnover. Confirmatory factor analysis and multi-group invariance testing across the four national samples support the revised factor structure (CFI = 0.96, RMSEA = 0.054). Implications for benchmarking and capacity-building programmes are discussed.

title: Knowledge Management Maturity and Organisational Resilience During Administrative Disruption: Evidence from Serbian Local Governments During 2020–2021
abstract: This paper examines whether pre-existing knowledge management maturity moderated the organisational resilience of Serbian local governments during the administrative disruptions of 2020–2021, a period combining public health crisis responses with a cycle of local elections. Resilience was operationalised as the ability to maintain service continuity, measured through administrative output indicators drawn from municipal reporting obligations. Knowledge management maturity scores from a 2019 baseline survey (N = 310 civil servants, 38 municipalities) were matched to 2020 and 2021 service output data. Multilevel regression models indicate that municipalities scoring in the top quartile on the leadership and culture dimensions of the maturity instrument maintained statistically higher service output continuity than those in the bottom quartile (difference = 14 percentage points, p < 0.05), controlling for municipality size, budget, and region. The effect was not significant for the technology dimension. Results suggest that relational and cultural aspects of knowledge infrastructure have practical consequences for public service robustness.

title: Multi-Criteria Decision-Making in Agri-food Supply Chains: Methods, Applications, and Open Problems
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods in agri-food supply chain management, with a focus on supplier selection, logistics partner evaluation, and procurement strategy formulation. The review covers studies published between 2005 and 2018 and categorises them by method family—deterministic, fuzzy, grey, stochastic, and hybrid—and by agri-food sector—cereals, dairy, meat, fruit and vegetables, and processed foods. A structured comparison table is provided for 43 reviewed studies, identifying the criteria sets used, the number of alternatives considered, and the data collection approach. The chapter identifies three recurring gaps: the underrepresentation of dynamic decision environments, the limited use of real procurement records as opposed to hypothetical expert judgements, and the near-total absence of post-hoc validation against actual supplier choices. Directions for future research are outlined, including the integration of demand forecast uncertainty and the use of simulation to stress-test supplier rankings.

title: Porting FreeRTOS to a Dual-Core ARM Cortex-M3 Microcontroller: Scheduler Modifications and Interrupt Latency Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the steps required to adapt the FreeRTOS kernel to a dual-core ARM Cortex-M3 device in which both cores share a single system-tick timer. The authors identify three regions of the scheduler that assume a single hart and propose locking primitives based on hardware spin-locks available on the target silicon. Interrupt latency was measured using a GPIO toggle method with a 100 MHz logic analyser over 50 000 task-switch events. On the unmodified single-core port, context-switch overhead averaged 1.84 µs; the adapted dual-core version achieved 2.11 µs per core with a worst-case jitter of 340 ns. Stack usage increased by 128 bytes per task due to the additional lock state. The paper also documents a linker-script modification needed to place critical scheduler data in tightly coupled memory. Ported code and measurement scripts are released under a BSD licence.

title: Configuring GCC Cross-Compilation Toolchains for Bare-Metal RISC-V Targets: A Systematic Comparison of Newlib and musl-libc Runtime Behaviour
abstract: Cross-compiling for bare-metal RISC-V requires explicit decisions about the C runtime library, the memory model, and the ISA extension subset passed to the compiler. This study systematically compares GCC 10.3 toolchains built with Newlib 4.1 and musl-libc 1.2.2 targeting the RV32IMC and RV64GC profiles. Twelve representative workloads were compiled under both configurations and executed on two evaluation boards: a custom RV32 FPGA softcore running at 50 MHz and a commercial RV64 SoC at 1 GHz. Code-size differences reached 18 % in favour of Newlib on the 32-bit target due to less aggressive printf formatting support in the default musl build. Dynamic memory allocation latency varied by up to 35 % depending on the heap implementation selected. The paper provides a decision flowchart and a set of CMake toolchain files to reduce configuration effort for new projects.

title: Deterministic Task Scheduling on ARM Cortex-A9 Under Simultaneous Hardware Interrupts: A Timing Analysis Study
abstract: Hard real-time workloads on application-class processors face interference from cache refills, branch mispredictions, and out-of-order execution that make worst-case execution time (WCET) estimation difficult. This paper examines a set of industrial-style control tasks running on a dual Cortex-A9 platform under a modified version of the Zephyr RTOS with the SMP scheduler disabled on one core. Tasks were instrumented with hardware performance counters; measurements were collected over 72 hours of continuous operation. The experiment shows that L2 cache evictions caused by interrupt service routines account for 61 % of WCET variance. A cache colouring scheme borrowed from the real-time hypervisor literature was adapted and applied, reducing that variance by 47 %. The paper reports scheduling overhead, memory footprint changes, and the effort in source lines of code required to integrate the colouring patches into the Zephyr tree.

title: A Practical Guide to RTOS Porting for Resource-Constrained Microcontrollers
abstract: This book chapter surveys the practical steps involved in porting a preemptive RTOS to a microcontroller that lacks an official vendor port. It covers four phases: processor-architecture assessment, context-switch implementation, timer and interrupt abstraction, and validation through a suite of conformance tests. The chapter uses three worked examples—an 8-bit AVR derivative, an ARM Cortex-M0+, and a RISC-V RV32E core—to illustrate tradeoffs. Special attention is given to toolchain constraints: some cores require assembly stubs that differ between GCC and LLVM/Clang, and the chapter documents these differences in annotated listings. A checklist of 24 porting tasks and a template port directory structure are provided as appendices. The chapter is aimed at practising engineers with C programming experience who are not necessarily familiar with operating system internals.

title: Memory Protection Unit Configuration for Safety-Relevant Firmware on ARM Cortex-M4: Fault Injection Experiments
abstract: Memory Protection Units (MPUs) on Cortex-M4 devices provide region-based access control without a full MMU, making them attractive for IEC 61508-style safety partitioning. This paper presents a methodology for deriving MPU region configurations from linker map files automatically and then validates the configurations through systematic fault injection. Faults were injected by corrupting stack and heap pointers of 14 representative tasks via a JTAG debug probe, and the firmware response was recorded. A correctly configured MPU triggered a MemManage fault within one processor cycle in all 1 400 injection trials; a control build with MPU disabled allowed stack corruption to propagate silently in 38 % of cases. The paper quantifies the code-size and execution-time overhead of the MPU driver (3.2 KB flash, 0.6 µs per region reconfiguration) and discusses limitations when tasks share read-only data.

title: Toolchain Reproducibility in Embedded Firmware Builds: An Analysis of GCC Version Drift Effects on Binary Size and Timing
abstract: Embedded firmware projects that evolve over years often accumulate silent changes caused by upgrading the GCC toolchain between releases. This study quantifies those effects by rebuilding 11 open-source RTOS-based firmware projects with GCC versions 8.5, 9.4, 10.3, 11.3, and 12.2, all targeting ARM Cortex-M targets with identical compiler flags. Binary size varied by up to 9.4 % across versions for the same source, driven primarily by changes in the inliner heuristics and loop-optimisation passes. Interrupt latency changed by up to 220 ns between consecutive GCC versions on one project due to altered instruction scheduling. The paper introduces a regression-testing harness that runs on a low-cost evaluation board and checks binary size, stack usage, and five timing metrics automatically as part of a CI pipeline. Configuration files for GitHub Actions and a Jenkins-compatible variant are provided.

title: Static Stack Depth Analysis for Multi-Tasking Firmware Using LLVM IR: Accuracy and Scalability on Cortex-M and RISC-V Targets
abstract: Stack overflows in embedded firmware are a common source of field failures yet are difficult to detect before deployment. This paper evaluates a static analysis approach that operates on LLVM intermediate representation to compute worst-case stack depth for each RTOS task, accounting for function-call graphs, interrupt nesting, and compiler-inserted code such as stack canaries. The analysis was applied to eight firmware projects ranging from 8 000 to 120 000 lines of C. On projects where dynamic measurements were also available, the static estimates exceeded the measured peaks by 4–19 %, a conservative overestimate. On two projects the static tool identified tasks whose stack size had been set below the computed bound, matching known crash reports in the projects' issue trackers. Runtime overhead of the analysis tool itself is reported, and limitations relating to indirect function calls and inline assembly are discussed.

title: Characterising RTOS Scheduler Overhead on Heterogeneous Multi-Core SoCs with Mixed Privilege Levels
abstract: Modern industrial SoCs increasingly combine application-class cores running a general-purpose OS with real-time cores running an RTOS, communicating through shared memory. This preprint characterises scheduler overhead on three such platforms: a dual Cortex-A55 plus Cortex-M33 device, a quad Cortex-A53 plus dual Cortex-R5 device, and a RISC-V cluster plus Cortex-M4 device. For each platform, the RTOS running on the real-time core was Zephyr 3.5; the application core ran Linux 6.1. Inter-processor communication latency was measured using shared-memory ring buffers with hardware timestamps. Median IPC latency ranged from 4.1 µs to 22.7 µs across platforms; the largest contributor in all cases was cache coherency management rather than scheduler decisions. A parameterised model with four platform variables is fitted to the data and validated on a fourth platform not used during model development.

title: Semi-Supervised Autoencoder Architecture for Anomaly Scoring in High-Frequency Game Telemetry
abstract: Reconstruction-error autoencoders have been applied to anomaly detection in images and network traffic, but their application to variable-length behavioural telemetry streams in games raises specific challenges including irregular sampling rates and session length variance. This study trains a shallow denoising autoencoder on 2.1 million unlabelled sessions and fine-tunes the encoder representation using a small labelled set of 6,400 sessions (12% confirmed anomalous). The architecture uses a bottleneck of dimension 32 with dropout regularisation. Sessions are encoded as fixed-length vectors via sliding-window aggregation with a 30-second window and 50% overlap before being passed to the autoencoder. Reconstruction error is used as an anomaly score, thresholded via a precision–recall analysis on the labelled validation set. The semi-supervised variant outperforms the fully unsupervised baseline by 9 percentage points in area under the precision–recall curve (0.87 vs. 0.78). The paper details the preprocessing pipeline and discusses the sensitivity of the approach to window size.

title: Synthetic-to-real transfer for pose estimation using style-consistent data augmentation
abstract: Annotating large datasets for pose estimation in specialised environments is expensive. We explore whether synthetic training data generated in a game engine and subject to style transfer can substitute for real annotation. A corpus of 120,000 synthetic frames was rendered with varied backgrounds, lighting rigs, and body textures, then passed through a style-transfer network conditioned on a small set of 300 unlabelled real images from the target domain. A ResNet-based pose estimator trained on style-transferred data alone achieved PCK@0.2 of 0.71 on a held-out real test set, compared with 0.79 for a fully supervised baseline using 5,000 real annotated frames. When 500 real annotated frames were added alongside the synthetic data, the gap closed to 0.76 versus 0.79. Sensitivity to the quality and diversity of the 300 unlabelled condition images is characterised empirically.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Automated Optical Inspection of SMT Solder Joints: A Comparative Study of Shallow and Deep Architectures
abstract: Five CNN architectures ranging from three to sixteen convolutional layers were trained and evaluated on a dataset of 28,400 labelled top-view AOI images of 0402 and 0603 passive components, spanning four defect categories: bridging, insufficient solder, tombstoning, and acceptable. Architectures were trained from random initialisation on 80% of the data and tested on a held-out 20% set collected from a separate production shift to introduce mild distribution shift. The deepest tested architecture (16 layers) did not outperform a seven-layer network on this dataset, with both achieving approximately 94.1% overall accuracy. The seven-layer model required 2.1× less training time. Confusion analysis showed that bridging and insufficient-solder categories were most frequently interchanged, motivating future work on domain adaptation. All models were implemented in Theano and experiments were conducted on a single NVIDIA GPU workstation. Training durations ranged from 2.4 h to 11.7 h.

title: Incremental Re-Execution Policies for Stale Cells in Jupyter Notebooks
abstract: When a user modifies a cell in a Jupyter notebook, downstream cells that depend on its output become stale but are not automatically re-executed by default. Re-executing the entire notebook is expensive for long-running computations. We formalise the cell-dependency graph using a combination of name-based dataflow analysis and time-stamp tracking, then define three re-execution policies—minimal, conservative, and speculative—and analyse their completeness and cost properties. The minimal policy re-executes only cells whose inputs transitively depend on a changed cell; the conservative policy additionally re-executes cells with uncertain dependencies arising from dynamic attribute access; the speculative policy pre-fetches results for likely next edits. We implemented the policies as a JupyterLab extension and measured re-execution time on 30 long-running notebooks drawn from climate-modelling and genomics repositories. The minimal policy reduced re-execution time by 62 % on average over full re-run, with zero missed updates in 97 % of test scenarios. The conservative policy eliminated missed updates at a cost of 11 % extra cells executed compared to minimal.

title: Effect of pH and soluble-solids content on high-methoxyl pectin gel strength in model strawberry preserve systems
abstract: High-methoxyl (HM) pectin gelation requires sufficient sugar concentration and acidic pH to suppress electrostatic repulsion and promote hydrophobic associations along the polymer backbone. This study systematically varied soluble-solids content (55–75 °Brix) and pH (2.8–3.6) in a model strawberry preserve using a 5×4 full factorial design with three replicates per combination. Storage modulus G′, loss tangent tan δ, and texture profile analysis hardness were measured 24 h after hot-fill at 85 °C. G′ ranged from 48 Pa at 55 °Brix/pH 3.6 to 1 240 Pa at 68 °Brix/pH 3.0, with pH exerting a stronger marginal effect than soluble-solids content above 65 °Brix. Loss tangent remained below 0.18 across all combinations that achieved stable network formation, indicating predominantly elastic behaviour. A response-surface model (R² = 0.93) was fitted to predict G′ as a function of both variables. Results confirm that the conventional 67–68 °Brix target can be relaxed to approximately 62 °Brix without meaningful network softening if pH is held at 3.0–3.1, supporting reformulation toward lower caloric density.

title: Water activity and microbiological shelf-life prediction in reduced-sugar apricot jam: influence of sucrose–sorbitol blends
abstract: Reducing sucrose in fruit preserves lowers water activity (aw) less efficiently per unit mass than in standard formulations, raising concerns about microbial stability. This work examined apricot jam formulations at 45, 52, and 58 °Brix in which sucrose was partially replaced with sorbitol at 10%, 20%, and 30% mass-fraction substitution levels. Water activity was measured using a dew-point hygrometer at 25 °C; mould growth challenge tests were performed with Aspergillus niger and Penicillium expansum over 120 days at 20 °C and 25 °C. At 52 °Brix with 20% sorbitol substitution, aw was 0.892 ± 0.003, compared with 0.880 ± 0.002 for a standard 65 °Brix sucrose-only control. Mould-free shelf-life at 25 °C fell from >120 days to 74 ± 6 days at that formulation without added hurdles. Adding 0.05% potassium sorbate restored mould-free shelf-life to >120 days. Predictive modelling using a modified Fermi equation described aw–shelf-life relationships with acceptable residuals (RMSE = 4.1 days), providing a practical tool for reformulation decisions at the factory level.

title: Thermal gelation behaviour of low-methoxyl amidated pectin in the presence of calcium chloride and isomaltulose
abstract: Low-methoxyl amidated (LMA) pectin forms calcium-mediated junction zones whose mechanical properties differ substantially from HM-pectin networks, making LMA systems attractive for reduced-sugar applications where aw constraints are relaxed. This study characterised the gelation kinetics of a commercial LMA pectin (degree of esterification 28%, degree of amidation 22%) at 0.6–1.2% w/w in the presence of CaCl₂ (5–20 mM) and isomaltulose (20–50% w/w) as the primary bulking agent. Oscillatory temperature sweeps from 90 °C to 20 °C at 1 °C/min and 1 Hz were performed, with the gel point defined as the crossover of G′ and G″. Gel point temperature increased from 41 °C to 63 °C as CaCl₂ rose from 5 to 20 mM. Isomaltulose concentration above 40% w/w raised G′ at 20 °C by 35–48% relative to isomaltulose-free controls at identical CaCl₂ levels, attributed to co-solute dehydration effects on pectin chain hydration. DSC thermograms showed a broad exotherm between 55 and 30 °C consistent with gradual network assembly. The findings indicate that CaCl₂ and isomaltulose can be used in combination to achieve target gel firmness at soluble-solids contents as low as 40 °Brix.

title: Textural and sensory properties of reduced-Brix raspberry preserve: comparing xylitol, erythritol, and inulin as partial sucrose replacers
abstract: This study compared three alternative bulking agents—xylitol, erythritol, and short-chain inulin (average DP 8)—as 30% molar-equivalent sucrose substitutes in a raspberry preserve formulated to 52 °Brix with HM pectin (0.5% w/w). Texture profile analysis (hardness, cohesiveness, springiness, gumminess), colorimetry (CIE L*a*b*), and a 9-point hedonic consumer test with 84 untrained panellists were conducted at day 1 and day 30 of storage at 20 °C. Erythritol-substituted preserves showed the highest hardness (TPA hardness 1.84 N vs. 1.52 N for sucrose control) but the lowest springiness, attributed to erythritol's tendency to co-crystallise on storage; visible grittiness was noted by 31% of panellists at day 30. Xylitol formulations most closely matched the control in all textural parameters and received the highest hedonic scores for overall acceptability (7.1 ± 0.9 vs. 7.3 ± 0.8 for control, p = 0.34). Inulin increased apparent viscosity during processing but resulted in softer, more spreadable gels. Water activity was lowest in the erythritol treatment (0.877) and highest in the inulin treatment (0.901). Results support xylitol as the most viable drop-in partial replacer for HM-pectin raspberry preserve at 52 °Brix.

title: Dielectric relaxation spectroscopy as a supplementary probe of pectin network formation in reduced-sugar fruit systems
abstract: Dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (DRS) measures the orientational mobility of water dipoles, which is modified as free water is immobilised within a polysaccharide gel network. This methodological paper reports DRS measurements at 200 MHz–20 GHz on HM-pectin gels (0.4–0.8% w/w) at 60, 65, and 70 °Brix over a temperature range of 20–80 °C, with simultaneous oscillatory rheometry as a reference. A decrease in the real permittivity ε′ at 2.45 GHz was observed to correlate linearly (r = 0.88) with increasing G′ across the soluble-solids range studied, suggesting that ε′ could serve as an in-line network-formation indicator. The α-relaxation frequency of water shifted from approximately 18.6 GHz in the sol state to 16.2 GHz in the fully formed gel at 65 °Brix, consistent with increased rotational hindrance. The method is non-destructive and does not require sample extraction, making it potentially applicable to in-line monitoring of jam production lines via waveguide probes. Limitations include temperature sensitivity of the dielectric baseline and the need for calibration at each pectin and sugar concentration.

title: Combined effect of degree of esterification and calcium concentration on the creep-recovery behaviour of mixed HM/LM-pectin gels
abstract: Industrial fruit preserve production increasingly uses blends of high-methoxyl (HM) and low-methoxyl (LM) pectins to extend the soluble-solids range over which stable gels form. This study examined binary HM/LM blends at HM:LM ratios of 100:0, 75:25, 50:50, 25:75, and 0:100 at total pectin concentration 0.6% w/w, soluble-solids content 58 °Brix, pH 3.2, and CaCl₂ concentrations of 0, 5, and 10 mM, using a Burgers four-element viscoelastic model fitted to creep-recovery curves (stress 10 Pa, 120 s creep, 180 s recovery). The instantaneous elastic compliance J₀ was lowest (most elastic) for the 50:50 blend at 5 mM CaCl₂ (J₀ = 2.1 × 10⁻³ Pa⁻¹), while pure HM at zero calcium showed the highest J₀ (8.7 × 10⁻³ Pa⁻¹). Recovery ratio after 180 s ranged from 48% (pure LM, 10 mM CaCl₂) to 81% (50:50, 5 mM). The retarded compliance component suggested that 50:50 blends with moderate calcium produce a tighter, more recoverable network than either pure pectin type alone. These findings have direct implications for formulating spreadable preserves with a short, non-syneretic texture at below-standard soluble-solids levels.

title: Pectin gelation systems for reduced-sugar fruit products: formulation principles and quality implications
abstract: This book chapter reviews the physical chemistry of pectin network formation as it applies to reduced-sugar (below 60 °Brix) fruit preserves, with emphasis on practical formulation decisions. The chapter covers (i) the structural basis of HM- and LM-pectin junction zones and how degree of esterification, amidation, and molecular weight distribution affect gel mechanics; (ii) the role of co-solutes including sucrose, glucose syrup, polyols, and soluble fibres in modulating chain hydration and junction-zone stability; (iii) the consequences of reduced soluble-solids content for water activity, syneresis, and shelf-life; and (iv) how pH and buffering capacity interact with pectin type to determine setting temperature and final gel texture. Case studies drawn from strawberry, apricot, and plum preserve systems illustrate trade-offs between textural acceptability and microbiological safety margins. The chapter is intended for food technologists and researchers working on reformulation of traditional preserve products toward lower caloric and sugar content without sacrificing the sensory characteristics associated with conventional recipes.

title: Influence of slow-release acidulants on setting behaviour and final texture of HM-pectin strawberry preserve at 58 °Brix
abstract: In conventional HM-pectin jam manufacture, pH drop during cooking can be uneven, leading to premature setting or insufficient network development. Slow-release acidulants—encapsulated citric acid, glucono-delta-lactone (GDL), and fumaric acid—were evaluated as replacements for free citric acid in a 58 °Brix strawberry preserve using HM pectin (degree of esterification 68%, 0.55% w/w). Setting time (defined as G′ = 500 Pa on cooling from 85 °C at 2 °C/min), final G′ at 20 °C, syneresis after 7 days at 20 °C, and pH trajectory during cooking were measured. GDL at 0.35% w/w gave the most reproducible setting behaviour (coefficient of variation for setting temperature: 3.8% across five batches vs. 9.2% for free citric acid), with final G′ of 1 105 ± 78 Pa and syneresis of 1.9 ± 0.4 mL per 100 g, lower than the citric acid control (3.7 ± 0.6 mL per 100 g). Encapsulated citric acid improved batch consistency but with a cost premium. Fumaric acid produced acceptable gels but left a perceptible residual bitterness noted by 44% of sensory panellists. GDL is recommended as a technically straightforward acidulant for reduced-Brix HM-pectin preserves when reproducibility and syneresis control are priorities.

title: Moisture sorption isotherms of reduced-Brix apricot and plum preserves: effect of pectin type and sucrose replacer on monolayer water content and hysteresis
abstract: Moisture sorption isotherms characterise the relationship between equilibrium water content and relative humidity, providing fundamental data for shelf-life and packaging design. This study determined adsorption and desorption isotherms at 25 °C for eight apricot and plum preserve formulations covering two Brix levels (50 and 58 °Brix), two pectin types (HM DE 65% and LM amidated DE 30%), and two sucrose-replacer conditions (no replacement; 25% replacement with maltitol). Static gravimetric method using saturated salt solutions (aw range 0.11–0.97) was employed with triplicate samples equilibrated for 21 days. The GAB model fitted adsorption data with RMSE ≤ 0.008 g/g across all eight formulations. Monolayer water content (W₀) ranged from 0.042 to 0.071 g/g dry solids and was consistently higher in LM-pectin formulations than HM-pectin formulations at the same Brix, consistent with LM pectin's greater number of free carboxyl groups available for hydration. Hysteresis loop width (defined as the difference in equilibrium moisture content at aw = 0.70) was widest in the maltitol-substituted, 50 °Brix, LM-pectin formulation (0.031 g/g), indicating the greatest structural irreversibility upon drying. These sorption characteristics should be considered when selecting packaging barrier requirements and storage temperature for reduced-sugar preserves.

title: Modelling multi-stage starch liquefaction–saccharification in a continuous plug-flow reactor configuration using a substrate depletion model
abstract: A mathematical model based on substrate depletion kinetics was developed and experimentally validated for a simulated continuous two-stage process comprising jet-cooking, alpha-amylase liquefaction in a plug-flow tubular reactor (residence time 30–120 min), and glucoamylase saccharification in a continuous stirred-tank reactor operating at steady state. Corn starch at 33% dry matter was used throughout. Liquefaction DE was varied between 8 and 16 by adjusting enzyme dose and residence time, and the effect on subsequent saccharification efficiency was evaluated over 24–72 hours. The model incorporated temperature-dependent enzyme inactivation terms calibrated from separate isothermal decay experiments. Predicted DE profiles deviated from measured values by less than 2 DE units across all conditions tested. Sensitivity analysis identified liquefaction DE and glucoamylase dose as the two parameters with the greatest influence on final glucose purity. The validated model can serve as a basis for digital twin development for continuous glucose syrup plants.

title: Effect of sorghum flour substitution (10–40%) on acrylamide formation and antioxidant capacity in corn extrudates
abstract: Corn extrudates with partial substitution of corn grit by white sorghum flour at 10, 20 and 40 g/100 g were produced at 160 and 180 °C on a pilot twin-screw extruder. Sorghum flour was characterised for free amino acids (RP-HPLC), reducing sugars (HPLC-RI) and phenolic content (Folin–Ciocalteu). Acrylamide in extrudates was quantified by LC-MS/MS. At 180 °C, the 40% sorghum substitution level reduced acrylamide by 22% compared to the 100% corn control, attributed to the lower asparagine content of sorghum. Simultaneously, total phenolic content increased with sorghum substitution and contributed to DPPH antioxidant capacity values 31% higher than the control at the same barrel temperature. Melanoidin fluorescence was not significantly elevated in sorghum-containing samples, suggesting the additional antioxidant capacity stems primarily from phenolic compounds rather than from new melanoidin formation. Physical properties (hardness, expansion, water absorption index) remained within commercially acceptable ranges up to 20% substitution.

title: Prebiotic index and short-chain fatty acid profiles of fermented arabinoxylan from teff bran: comparison of two in vitro batch fermentation protocols
abstract: Arabinoxylan (AX) isolated from teff bran (A/X = 1.74, MW = 168 kDa) was used as substrate in two in vitro batch fermentation systems: a pH-stat model maintained at pH 6.7 and a closed-batch model without pH control. Fermentation was conducted at 37°C for 24 h using inocula from three healthy volunteers with no antibiotic use in the preceding three months. SCFA were quantified by GC-FID and microbial community changes were assessed by qPCR for Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii. The prebiotic index (PI) calculated from SCFA ratios was 0.38 in the pH-stat model and 0.29 in the uncontrolled model. Bifidobacterium 16S copy numbers increased 2.8-fold over 24 h in the pH-stat model but only 1.6-fold in the uncontrolled model. F. prausnitzii increased significantly in both protocols. Total gas production at 24 h was 38.2 mL per 200 mg substrate. Results underline the sensitivity of prebiotic end-point measurements to fermentation protocol, a factor with practical implications for comparisons across laboratories.

title: Effect of hydrostatic pressure (200–600 MPa) on gelatinisation onset temperature and enthalpy of potato starch suspensions
abstract: Potato starch suspensions at 20% w/w were subjected to hydrostatic pressures of 200, 400 and 600 MPa at 20 °C for holding times of 5, 15 and 30 min. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed a progressive reduction of the gelatinisation onset temperature from 63.4 °C in untreated samples to 47.1 °C at 600 MPa / 30 min. Gelatinisation enthalpy decreased from 14.8 to 6.2 J/g over the same range. Wide-angle X-ray diffraction showed a transition from the native B-type crystalline pattern toward an amorphous profile beyond 400 MPa, with residual crystallinity dropping from 38% to 11%. Scanning electron microscopy indicated granule swelling and surface erosion at 600 MPa but no complete disruption at 200 MPa. The study establishes pressure–time–temperature combinations sufficient to induce partial versus complete gelatinisation, providing a basis for process design in pressure-assisted convenience food manufacture.

title: Cold-chain temperature abuse and its effects on resistant starch and sensory quality in HPP potato dumplings
abstract: Refrigerated potato dumplings processed at 450 MPa were exposed to controlled temperature abuse scenarios mimicking distribution chain deviations: stable 4 °C (control), single excursion to 12 °C for 4 h, repeated daily excursions to 8 °C, and sustained storage at 8 °C, all over a 21-day shelf life. Resistant starch, total starch, firmness, and microbial load were monitored at days 0, 7, 14 and 21. RS content at day 21 was highest under stable 4 °C storage (13.8 g/100 g dry weight) and lowest under sustained 8 °C (10.4 g/100 g), owing to accelerated amorphous reorganisation at higher temperatures reducing crystalline RS. Firmness followed the opposite trend, increasing most at stable 4 °C. Microbial counts remained within EU food safety limits across all scenarios at day 21. The results quantify the nutritional and textural penalties of realistic cold-chain deviations.

title: Influence of GNSS Observation Session Length on Datum Transformation Parameter Reliability in Low-Order Control Networks
abstract: Short-session GNSS observations are frequently used in cadastral densification campaigns where long static sessions are economically impractical. This paper investigates how session lengths of 20 min, 45 min, 1 h, 2 h, and 4 h affect the reliability of subsequently estimated datum transformation parameters. Fourteen points in the Srem district were repeatedly observed under each session-length scenario over six days in autumn 2014, using two Topcon HiPer V receivers on fixed monuments. Baseline solutions were computed with GNSS Solutions software and compared against reference coordinates derived from 24-hour sessions tied to three EUREF sites. Transformation parameters estimated from 45-minute sessions showed parameter standard deviations roughly 2.4 times larger than those from 4-hour sessions. The 2-hour threshold appeared sufficient to keep the translation parameter uncertainty below 1 cm. Practical guidelines for minimum session length in flat terrain densification are proposed.

title: Modelling Systematic Distortions in the Serbian Cadastral Coordinate System Using Thin-Plate Spline Interpolation
abstract: Systematic spatial distortions in the Serbian cadastral coordinate system accumulated over decades of analogue mapping and piecemeal digitisation. This study quantifies and models these distortions by comparing the cadastral coordinates of 312 boundary marks in four municipalities in the Bačka region against independently determined GNSS coordinates in ETRS89. Discrepancy vectors at check points reach magnitudes of up to 0.43 m and display spatial autocorrelation with ranges between 3 km and 11 km as characterised by variogram analysis. A thin-plate spline correction surface was fitted to the discrepancy field and validated by cross-validation on a 20 % holdout subset, yielding a mean absolute error of 4.7 cm. The paper discusses the feasibility of converting this surface into a NTv2-compatible grid for use in GIS and cadastral software. Implications for boundary dispute resolution and parcel area recomputation are addressed.

title: Evaluation of CORS-Based RTK Positioning for Datum Realisation in Urban Cadastral Surveys
abstract: Continuously operating reference station networks are increasingly used to replace conventional static GNSS campaigns in cadastral work. This paper evaluates how RTK positioning derived from the Serbian CORS network AGROS realises the national datum compared with post-processed static baselines at 54 test points across Novi Sad city territory. Three independent RTK fixes per point were collected on different days using a Leica GS18 rover. Horizontal discrepancies between RTK-derived and static-reference coordinates had a mean of 1.8 cm and a 95th-percentile value of 4.2 cm. Height component discrepancies were systematically larger in the old town area, attributable to multipath from dense building stock. The paper concludes that AGROS-RTK meets the accuracy requirements of the Serbian Regulation on Geodetic Works for cadastral surveys of class 3 and below, but marginal compliance in urban canyons warrants caution.

title: Datum Transformation Accuracy in Cross-Border Spatial Planning: A Case Study Along the Serbia–Hungary Administrative Boundary
abstract: Cross-border infrastructure projects and spatial plans require consistent coordinate reference frames on both sides of national boundaries. This paper examines the transformation accuracy achievable when combining Serbian D96/TM and Hungarian EOV coordinates in a unified ETRS89 framework along a 120 km segment of the Danube border. Forty common control points were surveyed by two teams using identical Leica GS18 equipment and a common processing strategy in Bernese 5.2 tied to five shared EUREF sites. Residual discrepancies after separate national-to-ETRS89 transformations reached 9–14 cm at points located in the bend of the Danube where both national networks show accumulated adjustment distortions. A localised correction procedure based on the Affine interpolation of residuals at the 40 control points reduced maximum discrepancies to 3.2 cm. The workflow is described in sufficient detail for replication in other Interreg planning contexts.

title: Residual Distortion Analysis After National Datum Modernisation: Vojvodina as a Test Area
abstract: Serbia completed a phased renewal of its national geodetic datum between 2005 and 2015. Despite this effort, residual distortions inherited from the former Gauss–Krüger coordinate system and from inconsistencies in the analogue cadastral archive remain detectable. This study analyses the spatial distribution of such residuals across Vojvodina using 489 benchmark coordinates from both the new D96 adjustment and historical D48 records, cross-checked against GNSS-derived positions. Semivariogram fitting reveals two dominant distortion scales: a regional trend with a range of approximately 40 km accounting for 58 % of total distortion variance, and a local component with a range near 4 km. The regional component correlates with administrative boundaries of former cadastral municipalities, suggesting that piecemeal digitisation of municipal cadastral plans introduced block-wise offsets. Kriging interpolation of the local component is shown to reduce RMS residuals from 12.3 cm to 4.1 cm in a cross-validation experiment.

title: Practical Guide to Datum Transformation in Serbian Cadastral and Engineering Geodesy
abstract: This book chapter provides a practitioner-oriented treatment of coordinate reference system conversion within the Serbian legal and technical framework. It covers the hierarchy of national reference frames from the Bessel ellipsoid–based systems through D48 and D96/TM to GNSS-compatible realisations, explains the legal status of each system under current Regulation on Geodetic Works, and describes step-by-step transformation workflows supported by worked numerical examples. Sections address the choice between rigid seven-parameter models, polynomial fitting and grid interpolation depending on accuracy requirements and geographic extent. A dedicated subsection treats datum issues specific to underground utility cadastre, where legacy coordinate records from multiple municipal sources must be harmonised. The chapter is aimed at licensed geodetic engineers, municipal GIS administrators and surveyors preparing for professional certification examinations.

title: Comparison of Grid-Based and Polynomial Datum Transformation Models for Cadastral Applications in Flat Agricultural Terrain
abstract: Vojvodina's predominantly flat agricultural landscape offers a relatively uniform environment in which to benchmark transformation models that differ in complexity. This paper compares four approaches—seven-parameter Helmert, second-degree polynomial, bilinear interpolation grid and thin-plate spline grid—at 215 points distributed across a 6 400 km² study area in southern Bačka. All reference coordinates were derived from 2-hour static GNSS sessions processed in Bernese 5.2. Each model was estimated on a 75 % training subset and validated on the remaining 25 %. The thin-plate spline grid produced the lowest cross-validation RMS of 2.3 cm horizontally, compared with 3.1 cm for bilinear interpolation and 9.4 cm for the seven-parameter model. However, the polynomial model showed more stable extrapolation behaviour at the study area boundary. Computation time and data requirements for each approach are tabulated to assist practitioners in making pragmatic choices.

title: Time-Dependent Coordinate Changes at GNSS Benchmarks in Vojvodina Caused by Subsidence and Their Effect on Datum Parameter Estimates
abstract: Land subsidence in the Vojvodina lowland, driven by groundwater extraction and sediment compaction, causes measurable vertical and horizontal coordinate drift at geodetic benchmarks. This study analyses time series from 14 GNSS monuments occupied in annual 48-hour campaigns between 2015 and 2023, supplemented by InSAR displacement maps derived from Sentinel-1 ascending and descending tracks for 2017–2023. Vertical velocities at the monitored sites range from −1.1 to −4.7 mm/yr. When datum transformation parameters are estimated from a network that contains subsiding points with epoch-inconsistent coordinates, the Z-translation parameter absorbs a systematic bias of approximately 0.8 mm per year of epoch mismatch. A correction procedure using velocity-field interpolation from InSAR to adjust benchmark coordinates to a common epoch is proposed and tested, reducing the Z-translation bias by 87 %. Implications for re-estimation of the national transformation grid are discussed.

title: Towards a NTv2 Distortion Grid for Vojvodina: Estimation Strategy, Data Requirements and Expected Accuracy
abstract: A NTv2-format datum shift grid for Vojvodina would allow GIS and cadastral software to apply spatially variable corrections automatically when converting between D96/TM and ETRS89. This preprint outlines an estimation strategy based on combining three data sources: 489 previously published benchmark comparisons, 312 cadastral boundary mark comparisons from earlier municipal studies, and a new set of 104 kinematic GNSS traverses carried out in 2024 using a vehicle-mounted Leica GS18 receiver logging at 1 Hz. The combined dataset is processed by iteratively reweighted least-squares fitting to a regular 2.5-arcminute grid. Predicted internal accuracy for the resulting grid is assessed by block cross-validation, yielding an estimated mean absolute error of 3.6 cm. The paper identifies data-sparse zones in the eastern Banat where additional control is needed before a final grid can be released for official use.

title: Characterisation of fly ash from the Kolubara thermal power basin as a precursor for alkali activation
abstract: Fly ash samples collected from two electrostatic precipitator fields of a coal-fired power station in the Pannonian lowland were characterised for use as alkali-activation precursors. Chemical composition was determined by X-ray fluorescence, mineralogy by XRD, and particle size distribution by laser diffraction. The sum of SiO2, Al2O3 and Fe2O3 exceeded 78 wt% in all samples, classifying them as Class F ash per ASTM C618. Reactive glass content estimated by selective dissolution ranged from 41 to 56 wt%. Pastes activated with 8 M NaOH developed compressive strengths between 18 and 34 MPa after 28 days of curing at 60 °C. Samples from the second precipitator field showed consistently higher strength, correlating with finer particle size (d50 = 14 µm versus 22 µm) and higher glass fraction. The results establish baseline material variability relevant to subsequent mix design studies using this regionally available precursor.

title: Thermal analysis and PXRD characterisation of carbamazepine–nicotinamide co-crystals prepared by three mechanochemical routes
abstract: Carbamazepine–nicotinamide (1:1) co-crystals were prepared by neat grinding, liquid-assisted grinding (LAG) with three solvents, and twin-screw extrusion, and the products were compared by PXRD, DSC, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Neat grinding at ambient temperature yielded a mixture containing approximately 30% residual Form III carbamazepine after 60 minutes, whereas LAG with ethanol and water produced phase-pure co-crystal within 20 minutes based on Rietveld refinement of PXRD patterns (Rwp < 4.2%). Twin-screw extrusion at 70 °C and 100 rpm gave phase-pure product with a mean crystallite size of 112 nm estimated by the Scherrer equation, substantially smaller than LAG product (340 nm). DSC showed a single melting endotherm at 158 °C for the co-crystal versus 174 °C for Form III carbamazepine. Intrinsic dissolution rate measured in phosphate buffer pH 6.8 was 1.4-fold higher for the co-crystal than for Form III. The work provides a quantitative comparison of three scalable preparation routes relevant to pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Solid-state screening of ibuprofen co-formers selected by hydrogen-bond propensity calculations
abstract: Fourteen co-former candidates for ibuprofen were ranked using hydrogen-bond propensity (HBP) scores calculated from a Cambridge Structural Database subset of 1 200 entries containing carboxylic acid donors. The six highest-scoring candidates—nicotinamide, isonicotinamide, caffeine, l-proline, saccharin, and urea—were subjected to solution crystallisation, LAG, and spray-drying. PXRD, DSC, and solution-state ¹H NMR (DMSO-d₆) were used to confirm co-crystal formation. Three new co-crystalline phases were obtained: ibuprofen–isonicotinamide (2:1), ibuprofen–saccharin (1:1), and ibuprofen–l-proline (1:1). The ibuprofen–isonicotinamide co-crystal showed a 2.1-fold increase in intrinsic dissolution rate in pH 7.4 phosphate buffer and a powder flowability improvement (Carr index decreased from 28 to 19) relative to racemic ibuprofen. The HBP ranking correctly predicted three of four successful outcomes, supporting its utility as a pre-screening filter to reduce experimental effort. The ibuprofen–urea and ibuprofen–caffeine combinations gave only physical mixtures under all conditions tested.

title: Variable-temperature PXRD study of a solvate–anhydrate transformation in a fluoroquinolone antibiotic
abstract: A monohydrate and a dimethylformamide (DMF) solvate of a fluoroquinolone compound (coded FQ-7, a developmental compound) were characterised by variable-temperature PXRD in the range 25–200 °C at 2 °C min⁻¹ using a Cu Kα source equipped with an Anton Paar TTK 450 chamber. The monohydrate lost water over 60–90 °C yielding an anhydrous Form A (confirmed by TGA mass loss of 5.4 wt%, theoretical 5.6 wt%), while the DMF solvate desolvated at 130–150 °C yielding anhydrous Form B. Form A and Form B show distinct PXRD patterns and do not interconvert below 180 °C. Form A dissolved 1.8× faster than Form B in 0.1 M HCl at 37 °C in a rotating disc experiment. Dynamic vapour sorption (DVS) showed that Form A re-hydrates reversibly above 55% relative humidity, while Form B does not sorb water below 80% RH. These results have implications for storage condition specification and manufacturing decisions for FQ-7.

title: Quantification of amorphous content in milled cefuroxime axetil by chemometric analysis of PXRD patterns
abstract: Ball milling of cefuroxime axetil (CA) at 400 rpm in a planetary mill introduced amorphous content that was quantified using two approaches: (i) a calibration curve based on physical mixtures of crystalline and spray-dried amorphous CA, and (ii) partial least squares (PLS) regression on the full 5–40° 2θ PXRD pattern. The PLS model, trained on 24 mixtures at 0–100% amorphous fraction (five replicates each), gave an RMSECV of 1.8% and RMSEP of 2.3% on an independent test set of 15 samples. The calibration curve method gave RMSEP of 4.1% under the same conditions. After 30 minutes of milling, amorphous content reached a plateau of approximately 42% ± 3%, as confirmed by independent DSC (measured by enthalpy of crystallisation on heating). Dissolution testing in pH 6.8 buffer at 37 °C showed that partially amorphous CA lots (≥ 35% amorphous) dissolved 1.6× faster than crystalline CA, but also showed greater variability across three production batches. The PLS-PXRD method is proposed as an in-line quantification tool.

title: Raman mapping of spatial co-former distribution in spray-dried co-crystal intermediates as a function of drying inlet temperature
abstract: Spray drying is increasingly considered for continuous manufacturing of pharmaceutical co-crystals, yet the effect of inlet temperature on intra-particle co-former distribution remains poorly understood. Naproxen–picolinamide co-crystal solutions in ethanol (5 wt% total solids, 1:1 molar ratio) were spray-dried at four inlet temperatures (80, 110, 140, and 170 °C) with a fixed outlet temperature range of 58–65 °C. Particles collected on filters were embedded in epoxy resin, sectioned to approximately 1 μm thickness, and mapped by confocal Raman microscopy (256 × 256 pixels, step 0.5 μm). At 80 °C, 94% of map pixels showed co-crystal phase; at 170 °C, this dropped to 71%, with naproxen-rich segregated domains appearing at the particle surface. PXRD quantification confirmed partial amorphisation (up to 18%) at 170 °C. Residual ethanol content measured by headspace GC decreased monotonically from 0.43 wt% at 80 °C to below the ICH Q3C limit at 140 °C. The findings indicate that an inlet temperature of 110–130 °C provides acceptable phase purity and solvent removal simultaneously.

title: Solid-state characterisation of a ternary co-crystal: indomethacin, saccharin, and l-tartaric acid
abstract: Ternary pharmaceutical co-crystals remain rare and their preparation is empirically guided. An indomethacin–saccharin–l-tartaric acid (1:1:1) ternary phase was obtained by LAG with acetonitrile and confirmed by PXRD (new diffraction peaks at 6.2°, 11.8°, and 17.4° 2θ not present in any binary sub-system), DSC (single eutectic-like endotherm at 148 °C), TGA, and solid-state ¹³C CP-MAS NMR collected at a national facility. Raman mapping of tablet cross-sections confirmed homogeneous co-crystal distribution. The ternary co-crystal dissolved 2.3× faster than crystalline γ-indomethacin in pH 6.8 phosphate buffer (USP Apparatus II, 37 °C, 75 rpm, n = 6), compared with 1.9× for the binary indomethacin–saccharin co-crystal prepared and tested under identical conditions. Physical stability testing at 40 °C / 75% RH for 12 weeks showed no detectable phase change by PXRD. The work demonstrates that controlled introduction of a third co-former can measurably improve dissolution performance beyond the binary co-crystal.

title: Crystal engineering of aceclofenac co-crystals for improved aqueous solubility: systematic co-former selection and scale-up by twin-screw extrusion
abstract: Aceclofenac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with low aqueous solubility (0.011 mg mL⁻¹ at 25 °C). Twenty-two co-formers listed on the GRAS list were screened by LAG; five yielded new crystalline phases by PXRD. The three most stable candidates—nicotinamide, caffeine, and theophylline—were selected for full characterisation. DSC, TGA, PXRD, and Raman mapping confirmed co-crystal identity and purity. Aqueous solubility measured by the miniaturised shake-flask method (n = 3) increased to 0.034, 0.029, and 0.021 mg mL⁻¹ respectively for the three co-crystals. All three were prepared at 50 g scale by twin-screw extrusion (temperature 65 °C, screw speed 80 rpm, feed ratio adjusted to 1:1 molar), yielding phase-pure product as confirmed by PXRD with Rwp < 5.0%. Flowability (Hausner ratio) improved from 1.41 for pure aceclofenac to 1.22, 1.18, and 1.25 for the three co-crystals. A 24-month open-dish stability study at 25 °C / 60% RH showed no polymorphic conversion for nicotinamide and caffeine co-crystals; the theophylline co-crystal showed partial conversion to theophylline monohydrate after 6 months.

title: Crystal engineering approaches to active pharmaceutical ingredients: from polymorph screening to co-crystal scale-up
abstract: This book chapter provides a methodological overview of solid-state screening workflows for active pharmaceutical ingredients, intended for graduate students and early-career researchers entering the field. The chapter covers the logical sequence from initial polymorph screening through co-former selection, crystallisation method optimisation, and scale-up considerations. Specific sections address PXRD data collection and interpretation, DSC experimental design (mass, scan rate, atmosphere), Raman mapping data acquisition parameters and chemometric processing, and the use of crystallographic databases in co-former selection. Case studies drawn from the authors' own laboratory data on ibuprofen, carbamazepine, and aceclofenac co-crystals are used throughout. Quantitative benchmarks are provided for typical experimental outcomes: for example, the success rate of LAG screening from a random 20-member co-former set is reported from several published studies as 15–30%. The chapter concludes with a discussion of regulatory expectations for co-crystal characterisation, referencing the EMA reflection paper and FDA guidance.

title: Fast-dissolving co-crystal pellets of piroxicam–malonic acid prepared by hot-melt extrusion: effect of polymer matrix on phase purity and in vitro release
abstract: Piroxicam–malonic acid co-crystal (PMC, 1:1) was incorporated into pellets by hot-melt extrusion (HME) using three hydrophilic polymers: polyvinyl caprolactam–polyvinyl acetate–polyethylene glycol graft copolymer (Soluplus equivalent), hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMCAS-MF grade), and polyvinylpyrrolidone–vinyl acetate 64 (PVP-VA64) at 20 wt% drug loading. Extrusion was carried out at 100–130 °C depending on polymer; torque and melt temperature were logged for all runs. Post-extrusion PXRD analysis showed that the PVP-VA64 matrix caused complete co-crystal-to-amorphous conversion, while HPMCAS-MF and Soluplus matrices retained 88% and 79% crystalline co-crystal, respectively (Rietveld quantification). Raman mapping of pellet cross-sections (64 × 64 pixels, step 3 μm) confirmed the co-crystal distribution correlated with PXRD results. In vitro dissolution in FaSSIF-V2 at pH 6.5 showed that all three pellet formulations exceeded the intrinsic dissolution rate of crystalline piroxicam by at least 2.1×, with the HPMCAS-MF pellets showing the most sustained supersaturation profile over 240 minutes. Six-month stability testing at 25 °C / 60% RH showed no further amorphisation in HPMCAS-MF pellets.

title: Distribution of dissolved iron species in the Tisa River tributaries of Vojvodina during seasonal low-flow periods
abstract: Iron speciation was investigated in twelve surface water sampling points along three tributaries of the Tisa River in northern Serbia during summer and early autumn low-flow conditions over two consecutive years. Total dissolved iron, Fe(II), and Fe(III) concentrations were determined by ferrozine spectrophotometry combined with 0.45 µm membrane filtration. Fe(II) fractions ranged from 18 to 64 % of total dissolved iron depending on sampling site and season, with the highest Fe(II) proportions observed in hyporheic exchange zones downstream of drainage channels. Dissolved oxygen, pH (6.8–8.1), and temperature (14–24 °C) were recorded in situ. A positive correlation between Fe(II)/Fe(total) ratio and turbidity was noted at two sites, indicating particle-associated reductive dissolution. The dataset provides a seasonal baseline for redox-driven iron cycling in lowland river systems receiving agricultural drainage. Implications for drinking water treatment intakes drawing from these tributaries are discussed.

title: Redox speciation of iron in constructed wetland outflows treating acid mine drainage
abstract: Iron speciation was characterised at the inflow, mid-zone, and outflow of two pilot-scale constructed wetlands built to treat low-pH drainage (pH 3.2–4.5) from an abandoned pyrite extraction site in eastern Serbia. Total Fe, Fe(II), and Fe(III) were determined at 48-hour intervals over six weeks by ferrozine photometry and ICP-OES. Fe(II) at the inflow averaged 48 mg/L and decreased to 3.1 mg/L at the outflow, while pH rose to 6.1–6.8 through bacterial sulfate reduction and alkalinity generation. Fe(III) accumulated transiently as schwertmannite-type precipitates in the mid-zone as confirmed by XRD analysis. Fe removal efficiency averaged 93.5 % across the six-week period but dropped to 81 % during a cold spell (air temperature below −3 °C) in week four, coinciding with reduced microbial activity. The dataset supports mechanistic modelling of coupled iron oxidation–precipitation–reduction in passive treatment systems.

title: A Rule-Based Architecture for Automating Payroll Tax Calculations in Serbian Labour Law Context
abstract: This paper presents a rule-based architecture designed to automate payroll tax and contribution calculations in compliance with Serbian labour legislation as it stood in 2009. The system encodes legal provisions as declarative production rules within a forward-chaining inference engine, separating legal logic from application code. A prototype was implemented using an open-source rule engine and integrated with a simplified HR database holding records for 240 employees across three simulated enterprises. Evaluation measured execution time, rule conflict frequency, and maintenance effort when legislation changed. Results showed that 91% of tested payroll scenarios were computed correctly on first pass, and rule update time following a statutory change was reduced by an estimated 60% compared to a hardcoded procedural baseline. Limitations include the manual encoding of rules and the absence of automated legal-text parsing. The work establishes a baseline architecture later extended in subsequent studies.

title: Comparative Analysis of BPMN 2.0 Modelling Tools for HR Workflow Design in Mid-Sized Enterprises
abstract: The study systematically compares five BPMN 2.0-compliant modelling tools—three open-source and two commercial—against a set of 18 criteria relevant to HR workflow design in mid-sized enterprises. Criteria span notation coverage, simulation capability, code generation support, learning curve, and integration interfaces. Evaluation was conducted by a panel of 12 practitioners and four academic researchers through structured task performance and questionnaire. Tasks included modelling an employee onboarding process, a leave-request approval chain, and a disciplinary procedure. Quantitative scoring showed that no single tool scored above 70% across all criteria; open-source tools performed competitively on notation coverage but lagged on simulation depth. The paper provides a selection matrix that practitioners can adapt by weighting criteria according to organisational priorities. Findings informed the tool choices adopted in subsequent research projects at the authors' institutions.

title: Integrating Decision Table Management into an Open-Source ERP Payroll Module
abstract: This paper describes the integration of a decision table management subsystem into an open-source ERP platform's payroll module. Decision tables were chosen over imperative code to represent tax brackets, contribution rates, and benefit eligibility conditions, which change with annual budget laws. The integration involved developing an API layer between the ERP's payroll engine and a standalone decision table interpreter, along with a browser-based editor for non-programmer HR staff. A pilot deployment covered a public-sector organisation with 510 employees. Over a 14-month observation period, the subsystem processed 17 monthly payroll runs with zero critical errors attributable to rule misconfiguration. Table update time following statutory changes averaged 3.2 hours, compared to an estimated 18 hours for equivalent code changes in the baseline system. The paper discusses versioning challenges and the need for rollback mechanisms when tables are updated mid-period.

title: Process Mining as a Diagnostic Tool for HR Workflow Bottlenecks: A Case Study in a Serbian Manufacturing Company
abstract: Process mining techniques were applied to event logs extracted from the HR information system of a Serbian manufacturing company employing approximately 800 workers. Logs covered 26 months of recruitment, onboarding, performance review, and termination processes. The Alpha++ algorithm was used for process discovery, and conformance checking was performed against manually modelled reference BPMN diagrams. Key findings included a consistent bottleneck at the line-manager approval step in recruitment, with a median delay of 11 working days against a target of 3, and a deviation rate of 34% in onboarding task ordering. Root causes were traced to ambiguous role assignments in the workflow system configuration rather than staffing shortages. Recommendations were translated into concrete workflow reconfiguration steps. The study illustrates the diagnostic value of process mining even with incomplete and noisy event logs typical of legacy HR systems.

title: Data Quality Issues in HR Information Systems: A Survey of Fifty Serbian Enterprises
abstract: A structured survey of 50 Serbian enterprises—spanning manufacturing, retail, public administration, and services—examined the prevalence and type of data quality issues in their HR information systems. Respondents were HR managers and IT administrators. Issues were classified across six dimensions: completeness, consistency, timeliness, accuracy, uniqueness, and validity. Completeness problems were the most frequently reported (72% of respondents), followed by consistency issues arising from manual duplicate entry (58%). Smaller enterprises reported proportionally higher rates of timeliness failures. The survey instrument was validated through a pilot with eight enterprises before full distribution. Findings were cross-tabulated by sector, enterprise size, and system age. Results indicate that most quality problems originate at data entry rather than in system logic, suggesting that workflow enforcement and validation rules at input points are a more cost-effective intervention than downstream data cleansing.

title: Workflow Engine Performance Under Variable Load: Benchmarking Three Open-Source Platforms for Payroll Batch Processing
abstract: Three open-source workflow engines were benchmarked for their suitability in payroll batch processing scenarios characterised by high transaction volume and strict completion deadlines. Test scenarios were constructed to simulate monthly payroll runs for organisations of 500, 2,000, and 10,000 employees, with varying proportions of exception cases requiring multi-step approval sub-processes. Metrics collected included throughput (cases per minute), mean case execution time, memory consumption, and failure rate under simulated node failure. Tests were run on a standardised virtual machine configuration. The fastest engine achieved 1,840 cases per minute for the 2,000-employee scenario with no exception cases, but degraded nonlinearly as exception proportion rose above 15%. Memory consumption differed by a factor of 2.7 between the most and least efficient engines at peak load. Practical guidance is offered for organisations selecting engines for payroll use cases with tight overnight batch windows.

title: Modelling Remote Work Policy Compliance as a Workflow Constraint Satisfaction Problem
abstract: The rapid shift to remote and hybrid work in 2020 exposed gaps in HR information systems' ability to track and enforce compliance with organisational remote work policies—particularly around working-hours recording, equipment allocation, and data handling obligations. This paper frames remote work policy compliance as a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) and maps policy clauses from 12 organisations onto CSP variables and constraints. A lightweight constraint solver is integrated into a workflow engine prototype to check compliance at each work-item transition. The approach was tested against a synthetic event log of 3,200 remote work transactions generated from the 12 policy documents. Constraint violations were detected with 94% recall; 11% of detected violations were false positives arising from underspecified policy language. The paper proposes a policy authoring template designed to reduce ambiguity and improve machine-processable representation of remote work rules.

title: Automated Generation of HR Process Documentation from BPMN Models Using Template-Driven Transformation
abstract: Organisations are required by audit and certification standards to maintain up-to-date written documentation of their HR processes. In practice, documentation lags behind process changes because it is maintained separately from executable BPMN models. This paper presents a template-driven transformation pipeline that generates structured HR process documentation directly from annotated BPMN 2.0 models. The pipeline uses XSLT-based transformation with documentation templates conforming to the ISO 9001-aligned quality management format common in Serbian certified enterprises. A prototype was tested with 14 BPMN models from three organisations, producing draft documentation that was reviewed by HR managers for completeness, accuracy, and readability using a structured rubric. Completeness scores averaged 88%, with gaps concentrated in exception-handling paths that were under-annotated in source models. The study also reports on the effort required to annotate models sufficiently for useful output generation.

title: Evaluating the Portability of Payroll Rule Sets Across ERP Platforms Using an Intermediate Representation
abstract: Organisations that migrate between ERP platforms face significant effort in re-implementing payroll rule logic because rule representations are proprietary and mutually incompatible. This paper proposes an intermediate XML-based representation for payroll rules—covering tax brackets, contribution formulas, and benefit conditions—that can be exported from one platform and imported to another via platform-specific adapters. Adapters were implemented for two open-source ERP platforms and one in-house legacy system. The intermediate representation was evaluated by migrating rule sets for five scenarios drawn from current Serbian payroll regulations. Semantic fidelity was measured by comparing payroll calculation outputs before and after migration across 1,200 synthetic employee records. Output agreement reached 99.1%; discrepancies arose in edge cases involving fractional-period employment and split tax responsibilities. The paper discusses the limits of rule portability when platform semantics differ in how they handle rounding and temporal validity.

title: Applying Large Language Models to Initial Triage of Employee Grievance Workflow Inputs: A Controlled Experiment
abstract: Employee grievance management workflows typically begin with a human triage step that classifies incoming complaints by type and assigns them to the appropriate handling unit. This paper reports a controlled experiment in which a locally deployed large language model (LLM) was used to perform this initial classification step on a dataset of 640 anonymised grievance submissions drawn from two organisations, covering a three-year period. Submissions were in Serbian; the LLM was a multilingual instruction-tuned model run on institutional hardware without external API calls. Human triage decisions served as ground truth. The LLM achieved 81% top-1 accuracy and 94% top-3 accuracy across eight grievance categories. Performance dropped to 71% on submissions containing domain-specific legal terminology. The paper does not advocate replacing human triage but evaluates the feasibility of LLM-assisted pre-classification to reduce repetitive clerical work. Ethical considerations around employee data privacy are discussed in detail.

title: Versioned Rule Stores for Retroactive Payroll Recalculation: Design Patterns and an Implementation Assessment
abstract: Retroactive payroll recalculation—required when legislative changes are enacted with backdated effect—presents a persistent challenge for rule-based payroll engines, as historical recalculations must use the rules valid at the original calculation date rather than current rules. This paper identifies five design patterns for versioned rule stores that address this requirement and evaluates them against four criteria: correctness of retroactive output, storage overhead, query complexity, and ease of rule authoring. The patterns range from full rule-set snapshots per period to delta-encoded change logs with replay. Each pattern is implemented as a proof-of-concept extension to an open-source workflow engine and tested against four retroactivity scenarios derived from real Serbian legislative changes enacted between 2019 and 2024. No single pattern dominates across all criteria; the paper provides a decision guide based on organisational characteristics such as payroll volume, frequency of retroactive events, and IT staffing capacity.

title: Interleaved BCH Schemes for Burst Correction in SLC Flash: Depth Selection and Overhead Trade-offs
abstract: Interleaving BCH codewords is a standard technique for converting random-error codes into burst-error correctors. This chapter surveys the theoretical relationship between interleaving depth d, BCH block length n, and the maximum correctable burst length b = d·t, where t is the BCH error-correction capability. We then apply the framework specifically to single-level cell flash pages of 512 bytes and 2 KB, deriving Pareto-optimal (d, t) pairs that minimise ECC overhead subject to a latency constraint modelled as a queuing delay proportional to d·n. For the 2 KB page case, a depth-4 BCH(2047,1979) configuration achieves burst correction up to 28 bits with 3.2% redundancy and mean decoding latency under 1.1 μs at a 100 MHz clock estimate. The chapter also discusses the interaction between interleaved BCH and low-density parity-check outer codes used in enterprise-grade flash.

title: Hepatocellular toxicity of combined St. John's wort and valerian root extracts in a primary rat hepatocyte model
abstract: St. John's wort (Hypericum perforatum) and valerian root (Valeriana officinalis) are frequently co-administered in Balkan folk medicine for anxiety and sleep disorders. This study examined the hepatotoxic potential of their combined standardized hydroalcoholic extracts using isolated rat hepatocytes (Sprague-Dawley, n=48). Cells were exposed to concentrations corresponding to two- and four-fold the common folk-medicine dose equivalent for 24 and 48 hours. Cell viability was assessed by MTT assay, lactate dehydrogenase leakage, and trypan blue exclusion. The combination showed a statistically significant reduction in cell viability at the four-fold dose equivalent at 48 hours (viability 54.3 ± 6.1% versus 89.2 ± 4.4% in controls, p<0.01), while single-extract exposures produced no significant toxicity at equivalent concentrations. Alanine aminotransferase leakage increased 3.2-fold in combination-treated cells. CYP3A4 activity, measured by testosterone 6β-hydroxylation, was induced 2.8-fold. The findings suggest synergistic hepatotoxicity mediated partly through CYP3A4 induction and subsequent reactive metabolite accumulation.

title: Survey of herbal supplement use among rural populations in Vojvodina: patterns of combination use and reported adverse effects
abstract: A cross-sectional survey was conducted in six rural municipalities of Vojvodina province to characterize patterns of herbal supplement use among adults aged 18–75. A structured questionnaire was administered to 614 participants recruited through primary healthcare centres between October 2010 and March 2011. Approximately 61% of respondents reported current or recent use of at least one herbal supplement; of these, 48% used two or more preparations simultaneously. The most frequently combined preparations were St. John's wort with valerian (22%), yarrow with dandelion root (18%), and milk thistle with artichoke extract (14%). Self-reported gastrointestinal complaints were the most common adverse effects (19% of combination users). Only 12% of herbal users had disclosed use to their physician. The data highlight substantial rates of concurrent herbal supplement use in the region and an important communication gap with formal healthcare providers, with implications for monitoring herb-induced liver injury in outpatient settings.
