title: Mitochondrial membrane potential changes in HepG2 cells treated with yarrow and greater celandine co-extracts
abstract: Yarrow (Achillea millefolium) and greater celandine (Chelidonium majus) are used concurrently in parts of Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina for gastrointestinal complaints. Greater celandine alkaloids, particularly chelidonine and sanguinarine, have established hepatotoxic potential, but their interaction with yarrow constituents at the mitochondrial level is not well characterized. HepG2 cells were treated with ethanolic co-extracts at concentrations of 25, 50, and 100 µg/ml total dry extract for 6, 24, and 48 hours. Mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) was measured by JC-1 fluorescence assay using flow cytometry. At 100 µg/ml and 48 hours, ΔΨm declined by 67% relative to vehicle control (p<0.001). Caspase-3/7 activation, measured by luminescent substrate assay, was 4.1-fold above control under the same conditions. ATP content fell by 58%. Single-extract exposures at equivalent concentrations reduced ΔΨm by 18–24%. The results indicate that yarrow constituents potentiate celandine-driven mitochondrial dysfunction, consistent with an intrinsic apoptotic pathway.

title: Induction of CYP1A2 and CYP2C9 isoforms by black cohosh and elderberry combination preparations in human liver microsomes
abstract: Black cohosh (Actaea racemosa) and elderberry (Sambucus nigra) preparations are frequently combined in Balkan traditional medicine for menopausal symptoms and respiratory infections. This study evaluated their effects on cytochrome P450 activity using pooled human liver microsome assays. CYP1A2 activity was assessed by phenacetin O-deethylation and CYP2C9 by diclofenac 4′-hydroxylation, each by LC-MS/MS. Microsomal incubations with the combination at concentrations corresponding to typical daily folk-medicine doses showed a 3.6-fold induction of CYP1A2 activity and a 2.1-fold induction of CYP2C9 activity relative to solvent control. Neither extract alone achieved statistically significant induction at equivalent concentrations. Molecular docking analysis with the pregnane X receptor binding site suggested that triterpene glycosides from black cohosh act synergistically with flavonoids from elderberry to enhance receptor activation. The clinical relevance is discussed in terms of potential interactions with narrow-therapeutic-index drugs metabolized by these isoforms.

title: Reactive oxygen species generation and glutathione depletion in rat liver slices exposed to dandelion root and artichoke leaf extracts
abstract: Dandelion root (Taraxacum officinale) and artichoke leaf (Cynara scolymus) extracts are widely used together in Balkan folk medicine as choleretics and hepatoprotectives, yet systematic toxicological assessment of the combination is limited. Precision-cut liver slices (PCLS) from male Wistar rats were prepared and exposed to individual and combined hydroethanolic extracts at concentrations from 0.1 to 1.0 mg/ml dry extract equivalent for 4 and 8 hours. Intracellular ROS was measured by DCFH-DA fluorescence, and total glutathione by Ellman's reagent. At 1.0 mg/ml combined extract for 8 hours, ROS generation increased 2.9-fold and total glutathione fell to 38% of control values (p<0.001). Individual extracts at equivalent concentrations produced modest and non-significant changes. Histological examination of PCLS by H&E staining revealed cytoplasmic vacuolation in the combination group not observed with single extracts. The paradox of hepatoprotective-labelled supplements causing oxidative stress in an ex vivo model is discussed with reference to dose equivalence and extract standardisation.

title: Herb-induced liver injury attributed to combination use of St. John's wort, milk thistle and licorice root: a case series from a hepatology outpatient clinic in Novi Sad
abstract: We report a retrospective case series of eight patients (five women, three men; mean age 44.6 years) referred to a hepatology outpatient clinic in Novi Sad between 2014 and 2017 with clinically significant liver enzyme elevations following self-medication with a combination of St. John's wort, milk thistle and licorice root preparations. Causality was assessed using the updated RUCAM scale. Five cases scored as probable (RUCAM 6–8) and three as possible (RUCAM 4–5). The clinical pattern was hepatocellular in six patients and mixed in two. Peak alanine aminotransferase ranged from 3.2 to 11.4 times the upper limit of normal. All patients recovered within 4–12 weeks after discontinuation of supplements. Biopsy was performed in two cases and showed centrilobular hepatocyte necrosis with mild inflammatory infiltrate. No viral, autoimmune, or metabolic liver disease aetiology was identified. The case series underscores the relevance of detailed herbal supplement history in clinical hepatology and documents a combination pattern consistent with prior in vitro findings.

title: Modulation of NF-κB signalling pathway by wormwood and gentian root co-treatment in LPS-stimulated primary Kupffer cells
abstract: Wormwood (Artemisia absinthium) and gentian root (Gentiana lutea) are frequently combined in traditional Balkan digestive bitters. Whether their combination affects hepatic inflammatory signalling beyond known gastrointestinal effects has not been investigated. Primary Kupffer cells isolated from Sprague-Dawley rats were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (1 µg/ml) and concurrently treated with standardised wormwood and gentian hydroethanolic extracts, individually and in combination, at 10, 50, and 200 µg/ml for 6 hours. NF-κB activation was assessed by nuclear p65 translocation (immunofluorescence) and a luciferase reporter system. TNF-α and IL-6 concentrations in conditioned medium were measured by ELISA. At 200 µg/ml combination, nuclear p65 signal increased 2.4-fold relative to LPS alone (p<0.01), and TNF-α production rose to 1840 ± 210 pg/ml versus 1120 ± 180 pg/ml in LPS-only control. Gentian alone showed a modest pro-inflammatory effect; wormwood alone had no significant effect. The data suggest that gentian-wormwood combinations may amplify LPS-driven hepatic inflammation at high doses, warranting caution in patients with underlying liver disease.

title: Herbal supplement hepatotoxicity in the context of Balkan folk medicine: mechanistic insights and clinical considerations
abstract: This book chapter reviews the evidence for hepatotoxicity associated with herbal supplement combinations traditionally used in the Balkan region, synthesising data from in vitro, ex vivo, and clinical case sources published between 2000 and 2019. The chapter addresses (1) the epidemiology of herbal supplement co-use in South-East Europe, (2) key cytochrome P450-mediated mechanisms of herb-herb pharmacokinetic interactions, (3) mitochondrial and oxidative stress pathways implicated in synergistic hepatocellular injury, (4) the strengths and limitations of available causality assessment tools for herb-induced liver injury in clinical settings, and (5) gaps in regulatory oversight of herbal products in Serbia and neighbouring countries. Particular attention is given to combinations involving St. John's wort, greater celandine, licorice root, and preparations containing pyrrolizidine alkaloid-containing species occasionally harvested in the Vojvodina region. Recommendations for clinicians, regulatory bodies, and future research are provided.

title: LC-MS/MS metabolite profiling of reactive intermediates formed during co-incubation of pyrrolizidine alkaloid-containing borage extract with CYP3A4-inducing herbal co-preparations in human liver microsomes
abstract: Borage (Borago officinalis) seeds and aerial parts are known sources of pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs), primarily intermedine and lycopsamine, and borage oil is consumed in Vojvodina both as a food supplement and a folk remedy. Co-administration with St. John's wort, a recognised CYP3A4 inducer, may increase the formation of toxic PA pyrrolic metabolites. Human liver microsomes (HLM) were pre-incubated with St. John's wort extract equivalent to a daily folk-medicine dose for 24 hours, then co-incubated with borage extract in an NADPH-fortified system. Pyrrolic metabolites dehydrointermesine and dehydrolycopsamine were quantified by LC-MS/MS (lower limit of quantification 0.5 ng/ml). Co-incubation with SJW-pre-treated HLM produced a 4.7-fold increase in total pyrrolic metabolite formation compared to untreated HLM (p<0.001). Glutathione trapping confirmed the electrophilic nature of the intermediates. A kinetic analysis (Km, Vmax) was performed for intermedine N-oxidation under both conditions. The findings support the hypothesis that CYP3A4-inducing herbs significantly amplify PA-derived reactive intermediate formation.

title: Transcriptomic response of HepaRG cells to combined exposure to milk thistle and turmeric extracts: a pathway-level analysis
abstract: Milk thistle (Silybum marianum) and turmeric (Curcuma longa) are among the most widely purchased hepatoprotective supplements in Serbia, and their combined use is common. Although individually they are considered hepatoprotective, high-dose combination effects on gene expression have not been characterised at the transcriptomic level. Differentiated HepaRG cells were treated with combined standardised extracts at doses corresponding to one-fold, three-fold, and six-fold the labelled daily dose equivalent for 24 hours. RNA sequencing (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, 150 bp paired-end, n=4 per group) was performed. Differential gene expression analysis identified 312 significantly upregulated and 187 downregulated transcripts at the six-fold dose (adjusted p<0.05, |log2FC|>1). Pathway enrichment analysis implicated unfolded protein response, ER stress signalling, and bile acid transport disruption as the predominant affected pathways. ABCB11 (BSEP) expression decreased 3.2-fold, consistent with potential cholestatic risk. No significant changes were observed at the one-fold dose. The data suggest dose-dependent ER and bile transport stress as the principal mechanisms at supratherapeutic combined doses.

title: Development and validation of an LC-MS/MS method for simultaneous quantification of twelve hepatotoxic herbal markers in human serum: application to exposed volunteers
abstract: Quantification of herbal supplement-derived compounds in human biological fluids is a prerequisite for pharmacokinetic studies and clinical monitoring. We developed and validated an LC-MS/MS method (Agilent 1290 Infinity II / 6470 triple quadrupole) for simultaneous determination of twelve analytes including hypericin, hyperforin, chelidonine, sanguinarine, intermedine, lycopsamine, glycyrrhizin, glabridin, cynaropicrin, artabsin, silymarin complex (silibinin A/B), and curcumin in human serum. Protein precipitation with acetonitrile followed by Ostro Pass-Through cleanup was used. Linearity was established over 0.1–500 ng/ml for all analytes. Intra- and inter-day precision (CV) was <10% and accuracy within ±12% at all quality control levels. Matrix effects were acceptable (<15%) after isotope-labelled internal standard correction. The method was applied to serum samples from twelve healthy volunteers who self-administered a three-herb combination for 14 days. Detectable levels of all target analytes were confirmed, with glycyrrhizin showing the highest serum concentrations (mean 38.4 ng/ml on day 14).

title: Gut microbiome modulation of hepatotoxic outcomes in rats chronically co-exposed to wormwood and calamus root extracts
abstract: Wormwood (Artemisia absinthium) and calamus root (Acorus calamus) are combined in traditional Balkan remedies for digestive and neurological complaints. Calamus contains β-asarone, a known genotoxic compound, but the role of the gut microbiome in modulating hepatic β-asarone exposure following co-administration with wormwood has not been examined. Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n=36) were divided into four groups and orally gavaged with individual and combined extracts, or vehicle, for 28 days. Serum liver enzyme profiles, hepatic histopathology, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of caecal contents were performed. The combination group showed a 2.3-fold elevation in serum ALT and histopathological evidence of periportal inflammation not seen in either single-extract group. Beta-diversity analysis (weighted UniFrac) demonstrated significant compositional divergence in the combination group (PERMANOVA p=0.008). Relative abundance of Bifidobacterium spp. decreased by 61% in the combination group. Targeted LC-MS/MS analysis confirmed elevated serum β-asarone in the combination group (mean 18.6 ± 3.2 ng/ml versus 9.1 ± 2.0 ng/ml in the single-extract group, p<0.01). The data implicate microbiome-mediated alterations in gut permeability and β-asarone bioavailability as contributing factors.

title: Dopamine D2 receptor binding and downstream cAMP signalling in striatal tissue of rats chronically exposed to low-dose organophosphate mixtures
abstract: Changes in dopamine receptor expression may represent an adaptive or pathological response to pesticide-induced dopamine depletion. Male Wistar rats (n = 8 per group) received a three-compound mixture—chlorpyrifos (1 mg/kg), dimethoate (0.5 mg/kg), and malathion (2 mg/kg)—by daily gavage for 35 days. These doses were individually chosen to cause less than 15% AChE inhibition. Striatal D2 receptor density was determined by radioligand binding assay using ³H-raclopride; cAMP accumulation following quinpirole stimulation was measured by ELISA. D2 receptor binding sites were upregulated by 23% in treated rats (p = 0.008), consistent with compensatory supersensitivity. Quinpirole-stimulated adenylyl cyclase inhibition was augmented in treated tissue (−42% cAMP vs. −27% in controls, p = 0.02). Total striatal dopamine was reduced by 21% (p = 0.01). These receptor-level changes at doses that individually appear safe reinforce concern about mixture effects and suggest that D2 receptor upregulation could be used as a sensitive intermediate endpoint in regulatory pesticide testing.

title: Validation of an HPLC-MS/MS method for simultaneous quantification of tacrolimus and cyclosporine in whole blood using a minimal sample volume
abstract: Accurate measurement of immunosuppressant concentrations in whole blood is essential for therapeutic drug monitoring in transplant patients. Existing methods often require sample volumes of 200–500 µL, which can be limiting in paediatric or critically ill patients. This study describes the development and full validation of an HPLC-MS/MS method enabling simultaneous quantification of tacrolimus and cyclosporine from 50 µL of whole blood. Protein precipitation with acetonitrile was used for sample preparation. The method was validated according to EMA bioanalytical guidelines for selectivity, linearity, precision, accuracy, matrix effects, and stability. Linearity was confirmed over 1–60 ng/mL for tacrolimus and 25–2500 ng/mL for cyclosporine. Within-run and between-run precision did not exceed 7.3% CV for either analyte. Recovery exceeded 85% for both compounds. The method was successfully applied to 124 clinical samples from the transplant unit, showing good agreement with the routine immunoassay results (Bland–Altman limits of agreement within ±12%).

title: Everolimus therapeutic drug monitoring in renal transplant recipients converted from tacrolimus: a 12-month prospective follow-up
abstract: Conversion from tacrolimus to everolimus is performed in some renal transplant recipients to reduce calcineurin inhibitor-related nephrotoxicity, but everolimus pharmacokinetics are also affected by CYP3A-related variability. This prospective study followed 44 renal transplant recipients who underwent tacrolimus-to-everolimus conversion at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina due to tacrolimus nephrotoxicity or malignancy. Everolimus trough concentrations were measured at months 1, 3, 6, and 12 post-conversion by HPLC-MS/MS. Target C0 range was 3–8 ng/mL. Time to stable therapeutic range was shorter in CYP3A5 non-expressers (median 6 weeks versus 11 weeks, p=0.02). At 12 months, 61% of patients maintained trough levels within target range. Proteinuria increased by a median of 0.4 g/day over follow-up. Serum creatinine remained stable in 75% of patients. Dyslipidaemia requiring statin initiation was observed in 18 patients (41%). CYP3A5 genotype predicted time to stable range but not long-term adherence to target.

title: Synergistic interactions between synthetic peptide derivative KCKP-05 and colistin against biofilm-embedded Acinetobacter baumannii
abstract: The study evaluated the combined antibiofilm efficacy of peptide derivative KCKP-05 and colistin against A. baumannii using a chequerboard microdilution assay and a static biofilm model on polystyrene surfaces. Twelve XDR clinical isolates characterised in earlier work were included. Fractional inhibitory concentration indices (FICI) were calculated for planktonic cells; FICI values ≤0.5 were observed in 10 of 12 isolates, indicating synergy. For biofilm eradication, two-dimensional MBEC chequerboard experiments showed that combining KCKP-05 at 0.25× its MBIC with colistin at 0.5× its MBEC resulted in a ≥ 3-log10 reduction in viable cell counts in 8 of 12 isolates compared to either agent alone. Time-kill kinetic experiments at those combination concentrations demonstrated complete bactericidal action within 6 hours in two representative isolates. Electron microscopy revealed disruption of both the outer membrane and exopolysaccharide matrix at the combination concentrations. No antagonism was detected in any isolate. These results support the rationale for testing KCKP-05 as an adjunct to colistin-based regimens for device-associated A. baumannii infections.

title: Effect of Bran Particle Size Distribution on NIR Spectral Response and Protein Prediction Accuracy in Whole-Wheat Samples
abstract: Particle size heterogeneity in whole-wheat flour introduces baseline shifts and scatter artefacts in NIR diffuse reflectance spectra, complicating protein prediction. This study examined how sieving whole-wheat samples to four particle size fractions (below 125 µm, 125–250 µm, 250–500 µm, and above 500 µm) affected spectral characteristics and PLS model performance. Twenty-eight whole-wheat batches from two Serbian varieties were fractionated and reassembled at controlled proportions to generate 112 sub-samples. Protein contents ranged from 9.1 to 16.4 g per 100 g. Models trained on unsieved material showed increased RMSECV when tested on samples dominated by coarser fractions, with prediction errors rising from 0.35 to 0.71 g per 100 g. Including a particle size descriptor as an ancillary variable in an augmented PLS model reduced prediction error on the coarse fraction to 0.42 g per 100 g. Results suggest that representative sampling and grinding standardisation are prerequisites for robust NIR protein models in wholegrain products.

title: Chemometric Discrimination of Protein Fractions in Binary Wheat–Soy Flour Blends Using NIR Spectroscopy
abstract: Blending wheat flour with soy flour modifies the gluten-to-globulin protein ratio, affecting both nutritional and functional properties. This study investigated whether NIR spectra, combined with PLS2 regression, could simultaneously quantify gluten-derived and globulin-derived protein fractions in wheat–soy binary blends without prior physical separation. Forty-five laboratory blends were prepared by varying soy flour content from 5% to 40% by mass. Total protein, wet gluten and water-soluble protein were determined by reference methods. PLS2 models with four latent variables returned RMSECV values of 0.44 g per 100 g for gluten protein and 0.29 g per 100 g for globulin protein when second-derivative spectra were used. Orthogonal signal correction as a preprocessing step marginally improved globulin prediction. The ability to estimate fraction composition without sequential extraction is discussed in the context of rapid quality control at blend preparation stages in food manufacturing.

title: Calibration Transfer of NIR Protein Models Between Two Benchtop Instruments Using Direct Standardisation and Piecewise Direct Standardisation
abstract: Spectral differences between instruments of the same nominal model from different production lots complicate the deployment of a master calibration on a secondary instrument. A calibration model for total protein in wheat–rye blend samples, originally developed on a first-generation instrument at the University of Novi Sad, was transferred to a second instrument at the University of Osijek using a set of 12 standardisation samples. Direct standardisation and piecewise direct standardisation were compared using a transfer set that included samples spanning the full protein range of 9.5–16.8 g per 100 g. Without transfer correction, the secondary instrument yielded a mean bias of 1.2 g per 100 g and RMSEP of 1.4 g per 100 g. Piecewise direct standardisation with a segment width of 20 nm reduced bias to 0.08 g per 100 g and RMSEP to 0.38 g per 100 g, achieving performance close to the master model. Selection of informative standardisation samples by Kennard–Stone sampling is described.

title: Robust PLS Models for Whey Protein Quantification in Liquid Dairy Matrices Under Temperature Variation
abstract: Temperature affects water absorption bands in NIR spectra and introduces systematic prediction errors for protein in liquid dairy samples measured at varying temperatures between 15 °C and 40 °C. Ninety liquid whey samples, prepared at three nominal protein concentrations (1.5, 3.0 and 5.0 g per 100 mL) by reconstitution of dried whey fractions, were measured at five controlled temperatures. Calibration models were built incorporating temperature as an explicit regression variable and compared to models without this variable and to models built only at 20 °C. Inclusion of temperature as an extra predictor reduced RMSECV for whey protein prediction from 0.27 to 0.11 g per 100 mL across the full temperature range. Spectral regions most affected by temperature were identified around 1440 nm and 1920 nm, confirming water combination band interference. The approach is applicable to inline NIR measurements in dairy processing lines where temperature is not tightly controlled.

title: Spectral Preprocessing Comparison for NIR Protein Prediction in Three-Component Legume Flour Blends
abstract: Ternary blends of wheat, chickpea and lentil flours present a compositionally varied matrix with overlapping protein absorption bands from gluten, legumin and vicilin fractions. This study evaluated 18 combinations of spectral preprocessing steps applied to NIR spectra of 96 ternary blends prepared according to a simplex-centroid design spanning blend proportions from 10% to 80% for each component. Reference total protein was determined by the Dumas combustion method. Preprocessing methods evaluated included raw spectra, first and second Savitzky–Golay derivatives, standard normal variate, multiplicative scatter correction, extended multiplicative scatter correction and their combinations. Model performance was assessed by leave-one-out cross-validation and an external set of 24 blends. The combination of extended multiplicative scatter correction followed by first derivative yielded the lowest RMSECV of 0.26 g per 100 g with five latent variables. The study provides a practical framework for preprocessing selection in multi-ingredient flour systems relevant to pulse-enriched product development.

title: Updating PLS Protein Models for NIR Spectroscopy When Blend Composition Shifts: A Comparison of Model Extension, Local Models and Slope-Bias Correction
abstract: Industrial flour blending operations frequently change the proportions and origin of raw materials, rendering existing calibration models less accurate without retraining. Three model-updating strategies were compared on a dataset of 180 wheat–corn starch blend samples divided into a base set (0–20% corn starch) and an extended set (0–45% corn starch). The strategies tested were: augmenting the calibration set with representative new samples and retraining, fitting a local PLS model on the near neighbourhood of each unknown sample, and applying slope-bias correction using ten update samples. For a shift from below 20% to above 30% corn starch content, slope-bias correction reduced prediction bias from 0.91 g per 100 g to 0.19 g per 100 g using only ten additional reference measurements, whereas local modelling achieved an RMSEP of 0.23 g per 100 g with no retraining. Full model retraining with 30 additional samples gave the lowest RMSEP of 0.18 g per 100 g. Practical recommendations for a staged updating workflow under production constraints are provided.

title: Interval PLS Variable Selection for Estimating Gliadin and Glutenin Contents Separately in Wheat Flour by NIR Spectroscopy
abstract: Gliadin and glutenin sub-fractions differ in their effects on dough rheology and are of individual interest in wheat quality assessment. Separate PLS calibration models for gliadin and glutenin were developed using interval PLS variable selection applied to NIR spectra of 78 wheat flour samples for which reference gliadin and glutenin contents were determined by size-exclusion HPLC. Seven spectral intervals of 40 nm width were selected for gliadin prediction, concentrated between 2050 and 2300 nm, and five intervals were selected for glutenin prediction, overlapping substantially with the amide II and III regions. Cross-validated models returned RMSECV of 0.38 g per 100 g for gliadin (RPD 3.4) and 0.41 g per 100 g for glutenin (RPD 3.1). Prediction accuracy was lower than for total protein but sufficient for screening-level classification into quality grades. The study highlights the spectral information limits imposed by the chemical similarity of the two fractions.

title: Assessment of Domain Shift in NIR Protein Calibrations Transferred Across Harvest Years Using a Small Annual Update Set
abstract: Calibration models for protein in wheat flour tend to lose accuracy across harvest years because of systematic differences in variety composition, growth conditions and moisture history of grain. This study followed the predictive performance of a master PLS protein model over three consecutive harvest years (2021, 2022 and 2023) using a fixed set of 155 flour samples from the 2020 harvest as calibration and fresh sets of 40–55 samples per year as independent test sets. Without any update, RMSEP increased from 0.29 g per 100 g in 2021 to 0.58 g per 100 g in 2023. Annual slope-bias corrections based on 8 selected update samples brought RMSEP back to below 0.35 g per 100 g in all years. The optimal size of the annual update set was investigated by random subsampling, showing diminishing returns above 6 samples. Recommendations are given for a low-cost annual recalibration workflow compatible with laboratory routine.

title: Meisenheimer complex formation and decomposition in the reaction of secondary amines with 4,6-dichloro-5-nitropyrimidine in DMSO–water
abstract: 4,6-Dichloro-5-nitropyrimidine reacts with morpholine and N-methylbenzylamine in DMSO–water (80:20 v/v) with accumulation of a distinct Meisenheimer σ-complex observable at 510 nm by stopped-flow UV/Vis spectrophotometry. Rate constants for complex formation (k1) and decomposition (k−1 and k2) were resolved by global fitting of multiwavelength absorbance–time traces using singular-value decomposition. At 25 °C, k1 = 620 ± 14 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ and k2 = 28 ± 1 s⁻¹ for morpholine, while N-methylbenzylamine gave k1 = 84 ± 3 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ and k2 = 9 ± 0.4 s⁻¹. The ratio k−1/k2 suggests that expulsion of chloride is partly rate-limiting for the bulkier amine. Temperature dependence studies (15–40 °C) yielded activation parameters consistent with a polar transition state for the addition step. Regioselectivity of the initial substitution, established by 1H NMR on isolated products, is exclusively at C-4.

title: Calorimetric and Potentiometric Determination of Thermodynamic Parameters for Nd(III)–DTPA Complexation
abstract: The complexation of Nd³⁺ with DTPA was studied by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and potentiometry in 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaClO4 at 25 °C. A Thermometric 2277 TAM microcalorimeter and a Metrohm potentiometric system were operated in parallel on identically prepared solutions. The ITC-derived enthalpy ΔH° = −24.7 ± 0.4 kJ mol⁻¹ and potentiometry-derived log β = 21.36 ± 0.04 were used to calculate ΔG° = −121.9 kJ mol⁻¹ and TΔS° = +97.2 kJ mol⁻¹ at 298 K, confirming a strongly entropy-dominated stabilisation. The titration calorimetry data were analysed with a 1:1 binding model using the SEDPHAT software package. Speciation diagrams constructed from the potentiometric constants show that the [NdDTPA]²⁻ species is dominant above pH 3.5. Discrepancies with earlier values in the literature are attributed to differences in activity-coefficient corrections.

title: Profiling Fragment Shader Bottlenecks on ARM Mali-400 Using Hardware Performance Counters
abstract: This paper describes a systematic methodology for identifying fragment shader bottlenecks on the ARM Mali-400 GPU using the hardware performance counter interface exposed through the vendor driver. We instrumented twelve synthetic benchmarks and four real game scenes to measure texture bandwidth, arithmetic instruction throughput, and early-Z rejection rates under varying shader complexity. Counter readings were cross-validated against frame-capture traces obtained with a custom OpenGL ES 2.0 interception layer. Results show that texture fetch stalls account for 61–74 % of total fragment processing time in three of the four game scenes, while arithmetic pressure is the dominant factor only in the remaining scene containing heavy procedural effects. The paper concludes with a priority ranking of optimisation targets derived from the counter data, and discusses the portability of the methodology to other tile-based architectures with similar counter granularity.

title: Reducing Overdraw in 2D Game Rendering on Tile-Based Mobile GPUs
abstract: Overdraw — the repeated shading of the same screen pixel — is a well-known performance cost in 2D sprite-based games, but its interaction with tile-based rasterisation has received limited attention. We analyse the overdraw patterns of five representative 2D game scenes rendered on an Imagination PowerVR SGX540 device, using a tile-occupancy model derived from the hardware documentation and confirmed by benchmark measurements. We then propose a static sprite-sorting pass that reorders draw calls by depth-estimate to maximise early-Z rejection within each tile, without requiring per-pixel depth testing. Across the five scenes, the sorting pass reduces shaded fragment counts by 28–43 % compared to painter's-order submission. The additional CPU cost of the sorting pass is below 0.4 ms per frame on a 1 GHz ARM Cortex-A8 for scene complexity up to 512 active sprites, making the technique practical for mobile game engines.

title: A Depth Prepass Strategy for Deferred Lighting on PowerVR Series 5XT
abstract: Deferred lighting pipelines accumulate per-pixel geometry and material data into a G-buffer before executing light accumulation, which on traditional IMR GPUs is straightforward but on tile-based architectures risks forcing tile-store operations that negate bandwidth savings. We investigate whether a depth-only prepass changes this trade-off on the PowerVR Series 5XT. Using the vendor's frame analyser tool and manual instrumentation with EGL timing extensions, we compare four rendering configurations — forward, deferred with full G-buffer flush, deferred with on-chip G-buffer, and depth prepass plus deferred — across scenes with 8, 16, and 32 dynamic lights. The depth prepass plus deferred configuration reduces tile-store bandwidth by approximately 35 % relative to a naive deferred implementation when the G-buffer fits within on-chip memory, and reduces total frame time by 18 % on average. We characterise the G-buffer size threshold above which this advantage disappears.

title: Bandwidth Cost Models for Tile-Based Deferred Rendering: A Survey and Unified Framework
abstract: Tile-based deferred rendering (TBDR) implementations differ across GPU vendors in on-chip memory size, tile dimensions, and render-pass semantics, making it difficult to reason about bandwidth costs in a vendor-agnostic way. This book chapter surveys TBDR bandwidth cost models from eight prior publications spanning 2009–2015 and proposes a unified parameterised framework that expresses tile-store and tile-load costs as functions of G-buffer layout, tile occupancy, and early-Z rejection probability. The framework is validated against measurements on three hardware platforms: a Mali-T628, a PowerVR GX6250, and an Adreno 430. We show that the unified model predicts tile-store costs within ±9 % across platforms and identifies G-buffer component packing as the single parameter with the greatest leverage on total bandwidth. The chapter is intended as a reference for engineers designing rendering pipelines for resource-constrained devices.

title: On-Chip G-Buffer Packing for Tile-Based Deferred Rendering on ARM Mali-G72
abstract: The introduction of Vulkan subpasses and explicit render-pass semantics allows applications to express G-buffer operations as on-chip memory transactions on Mali Bifrost-class hardware, potentially eliminating main-memory round-trips entirely. We evaluate four G-buffer packing configurations — ranging from 96 bits to 192 bits per pixel — for a physically-based rendering pipeline running on a Mali-G72 MP12. Using Vulkan performance queries and vendor-specific GPU counter extensions, we measure tile-store elimination rates and overall memory bandwidth for each configuration in a scene with 41 distinct material instances. The 128-bit configuration that stores albedo, packed normals, and a combined roughness–metalness–AO channel achieves full on-chip retention across all tiles at 1080p, reducing DRAM writes by 2.1 GB/s compared to the 192-bit layout while producing a maximum per-pixel colour difference of 0.003 in linear light relative to reference renders.

title: Measuring the Real Cost of Render-Pass Splits in Vulkan on Tile-Based Mobile GPUs
abstract: Vulkan exposes explicit render-pass objects and subpass dependencies, giving applications the ability to prevent tile flushes between render passes. In practice, third-party middleware and engine abstraction layers frequently split render passes in ways that force unnecessary tile flushes. This paper quantifies the cost of such splits on three commercially available TBDR devices using a controlled testbed in which render-pass splits are introduced programmatically at known boundaries. We measure tile-store bandwidth, frame time, and power draw using a combination of Vulkan timing queries, system-level power monitors, and vendor GPU counter APIs. Splitting a single render pass into two incurs a median frame-time increase of 1.9 ms and a power increase of 210 mW at 1080p with a 32-light deferred scene. We provide a decision procedure for engine developers to identify which splits are costly and which are benign based on G-buffer residency analysis.

title: Complexity-Adaptive Shadows for Real-Time Rendering on Mali Valhall-Class Hardware
abstract: Shadow rendering via shadow maps imposes a substantial per-light depth-pass cost that scales poorly on mobile hardware where vertex throughput is limited. We propose a complexity-adaptive scheme that selects among four shadow map resolutions and two filter kernel widths per light per frame based on a runtime cost estimate derived from visible light-volume coverage and current GPU utilisation counters sampled via the Mali performance counter interface. The scheme is implemented in OpenGL ES 3.2 with compute shader support and evaluated in a scene containing six shadow-casting lights on a Mali-G710 device. Compared to a fixed 1024×1024 shadow map with a 3×3 PCF kernel, the adaptive scheme reduces per-frame shadow-pass GPU time by 31 % on average over a 90-second gameplay sequence, with a shadow quality degradation below the just-noticeable-difference threshold in 94 % of evaluated frames according to a structured observer study with 18 participants.

title: Static Analysis of GLSL Shaders for Automatic Complexity Tier Assignment
abstract: Manually authoring multiple shader complexity tiers for LOD-based rendering pipelines is labour-intensive and error-prone. We describe a static analysis tool, implemented as a GLSL source-to-source pass, that parses fragment shader ASTs, estimates instruction count and texture operation count per tile per output variable, and assigns the shader to one of three complexity tiers based on configurable thresholds. The tool was applied to a corpus of 214 fragment shaders collected from three open-source mobile game projects. Tier assignments agreed with those produced by an experienced graphics engineer in 87 % of cases; disagreements clustered around shaders using dynamic branching that the static estimator conservatively over-counts. We discuss the integration of the tool into a CMake-based build pipeline and evaluate the end-to-end runtime performance improvement when the assigned tier information drives a draw-call-time shader-selection system on Mali-G57 hardware.

title: Subpass Merging in Vulkan: Conditions and Limits for On-Chip Retention on Adreno 7xx
abstract: Qualcomm's Adreno 7xx series introduced architectural changes to its tile-based renderer that affect which subpass merging configurations can retain intermediate attachments fully on-chip. The vendor documentation is incomplete on boundary conditions, and application developers frequently rely on trial-and-error. We reverse-engineer the retention conditions through a systematic sequence of 480 micro-benchmarks covering attachment format, dimension, sample count, and resolve operation combinations. Bandwidth is measured using Vulkan timestamp queries and the Snapdragon Profiler counter export API. We produce a decision table describing which configurations achieve full on-chip retention and validate it against 12 production-representative render graphs taken from game engine source code. The table correctly predicts on-chip retention in 97 % of cases. We also identify four configuration patterns that cause unexpected tile spills not predicted by public documentation, and propose workarounds for two of them.

title: Power-Aware Render-Pass Scheduling for Sustained Performance Under Thermal Throttling on Mobile Devices
abstract: Mobile devices operating under sustained GPU load reach thermal limits within minutes, triggering frequency scaling that reduces throughput by 30–60 %. Render-pass scheduling strategies that reduce peak power can defer throttling onset. We model the power draw of each render-pass type in a deferred rendering pipeline — depth prepass, G-buffer fill, lighting accumulation, post-process — using hardware counters and external current measurement at 1 kHz via a USB power monitor. Based on the model, we implement a scheduler that interleaves high-power and low-power passes to smooth instantaneous power draw without increasing total frame time by more than 2 ms. Tests on a Mali-G615 device running a 10-minute continuous workload show that the scheduler delays throttling onset by a median of 83 seconds and improves sustained frame-rate stability (σ of frame time) by 41 % compared to unmanaged submission order.

title: Tile-Bin Occupancy Estimation for Early Render-Pass Cost Prediction on TBDR Architectures
abstract: Predicting the per-tile shading cost of a render pass before submission requires an occupancy estimate — how many primitives overlap each tile — without executing the draw calls. We develop a software rasteriser running on ARM NEON SIMD that computes tile-bin occupancy from vertex buffer data and a bounding-box approximation in under 1.2 ms for scenes with up to 4096 primitives on a Cortex-A78 core. The estimate is used to pre-classify tiles into low, medium, and high occupancy bins, which in turn guides variable-rate shading rate selection in Vulkan on Mali-G715 hardware. In a set of 20 benchmark scenes, the predictor achieves a mean absolute occupancy error of 8.3 % relative to post-execution tile-occupancy counters. Variable-rate shading driven by the predictor reduces fragment shading time by 19 % compared to uniform-rate shading with a peak visual quality loss below 0.8 % SSIM.

title: Replication Strategies for Fault-Tolerant Stream Joins in Geo-Distributed Deployments
abstract: Maintaining join correctness across geographically distributed nodes introduces trade-offs between state replication overhead and recovery time after node failure. We formalised three replication strategies—full state mirroring, checkpoint-based recovery, and lineage logging—within a unified cost model that incorporates network round-trip time, state size, and failure rate estimates. The model was validated using a prototype deployed across three virtual data-centre regions with simulated wide-area network latencies of 20 ms, 60 ms, and 130 ms. State sizes ranged from 50 MB to 4 GB per operator, representing light to heavy join workloads. Under failure rates below 0.5 per hour, checkpoint-based recovery minimised total overhead by 22% relative to full mirroring. At higher failure rates, lineage logging reduced mean recovery time by 44% but imposed a consistent 9% throughput penalty. The cost model correctly predicted the crossover point in 87% of tested configurations.

title: Runtime Assertion Monitoring for CAN-Based Embedded Systems Using Low-Overhead Instrumentation
abstract: Runtime verification of distributed embedded systems must contend with strict memory and timing budgets. We describe a monitoring approach that compiles CAN-CL contracts into observer tasks co-located on existing ECU spare capacity, inserting checks at message reception and prior to message transmission. The observer code is generated automatically from contract annotations and requires no changes to application logic. On a target hardware platform (32-bit microcontroller at 80 MHz, 256 KB flash), monitoring a 9-message contract set adds at most 3.1% CPU overhead and 11 KB of code. Experiments on a hardware-in-the-loop rig injected 120 fault scenarios representing timing drift, signal corruption and missing messages; the monitors detected 108 of these within one CAN frame period of occurrence. False positive rate across 48 hours of fault-free operation was zero.

title: Asynchronous distributed Kalman filtering for multi-robot teams with heterogeneous sensing and update rates
abstract: Standard Kalman consensus filters assume synchronous communication, which is difficult to guarantee on real hardware where sensors operate at different rates and wireless channels introduce variable latency. This paper reformulates the distributed information filter to handle asynchronous measurement arrivals using a receive-buffer approach in which each robot processes its own measurements as they arrive and incorporates neighbour information whenever a consensus message is received. The filter is tested on a team consisting of two ground robots (encoder odometry at 50 Hz, UWB at 10 Hz) and one UAV (IMU at 200 Hz, barometer at 25 Hz, UWB at 10 Hz). Over 30 minutes of continuous operation the approach maintained a mean 3D localisation error of 0.24 m with no filter divergence events, while the synchronous baseline diverged in 4 out of 15 trial runs when simulated packet delays exceeded 120 ms. Timestamp jitter tolerance up to 80 ms is characterised.

title: A Longitudinal Study of Student Wallet Adoption for Verifiable Academic Credentials: Two Years After Pilot Deployment
abstract: We report a two-year follow-up to a verifiable credential wallet pilot conducted at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, originally launched in September 2023 with 610 enrolled students. Longitudinal surveys at 6, 12, and 24 months measured active wallet usage, credential sharing frequency, and reasons for non-use. Active usage (at least one credential share in the preceding 90 days) fell from 61% at 6 months to 44% at 24 months, primarily due to students graduating or losing motivation after initial curiosity. Among continuing users, the most frequent use case was sharing enrollment certificates to landlords (38% of shares) rather than the anticipated employer verification scenario. Students who had used the wallet for a cross-border Erasmus+ application reported the highest satisfaction. Identified barriers to sustained adoption include credential wallet app fragmentation, lack of institutional mandates, and limited employer readiness.

title: Carrier cooling rates in CdSe/ZnS core–shell nanocrystals probed by sub-picosecond transient absorption
abstract: We measured carrier cooling dynamics in colloidal CdSe/ZnS core–shell nanocrystals with core diameters of 3.2, 4.5, and 6.1 nm using transient absorption spectroscopy with a temporal resolution of 120 fs. Pump fluences were varied from 0.5 to 8 μJ cm⁻² at 400 nm excitation. Bleach recovery at the first exciton transition was monitored over a 0–200 ps window. Biexponential fits yielded fast components of 0.8–1.4 ps attributed to intraband cooling and slower components of 20–60 ps attributed to surface-trap-mediated relaxation. Larger cores showed systematically slower cooling consistent with a phonon-bottleneck contribution. Comparison with ensemble photoluminescence lifetimes confirmed that cooling and radiative recombination are decoupled on this timescale. These results establish baseline dynamics useful for subsequent studies of perovskite systems where similar hot-carrier phenomena have been reported.

title: Temperature dependence of exciton dephasing in ZnO thin films from 10 K to 300 K
abstract: Degenerate four-wave mixing experiments were performed on ZnO thin films deposited by pulsed laser deposition on sapphire substrates, covering the temperature range 10–300 K. The free-exciton dephasing time T₂ was extracted from the photon-echo decay and ranged from 310 fs at 10 K to 42 fs at room temperature. The temperature dependence was modelled by contributions from acoustic-phonon scattering (dominant below 80 K) and LO-phonon scattering (dominant above 150 K), yielding coupling constants of γac = 14 μeV K⁻¹ and γLO = 18 meV. Inhomogeneous broadening, inferred from the ratio of echo to free-induction-decay signals, accounted for 38% of the total linewidth at 10 K and decreased at elevated temperatures. The results are consistent with earlier studies on bulk ZnO but show increased homogeneous broadening attributable to surface and grain-boundary scattering in the 120-nm-thick film geometry.

title: Sub-nanosecond photoluminescence decay in solution-processed MAPbI₃ films: effect of precursor stoichiometry
abstract: Time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) decays were recorded for methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI₃) thin films prepared from one-step spin-coating with Pb:MA ratios of 0.9, 1.0, 1.05, and 1.15. Streak-camera detection with 15 ps resolution was used under 470 nm pulsed excitation at a fluence of 1 nJ cm⁻². Decay curves were fitted with a triexponential model. The dominant component had a lifetime of 30–80 ns depending on stoichiometry; two faster components with lifetimes of 2–5 ns and 0.3–0.8 ns were attributed to surface and grain-boundary trapping, respectively. Pb-rich conditions (ratio 1.05) produced the longest average lifetime (62 ns) and the lowest trap density as estimated by the Shockley–Read–Hall rate equation. X-ray diffraction confirmed phase purity across all samples. These findings indicate that modest Pb excess suppresses shallow trap formation under these processing conditions.

title: Hot-carrier lifetime extension in formamidinium lead bromide perovskite films at elevated carrier densities
abstract: We used two-colour pump–probe spectroscopy with 150 fs pulses to track hot-carrier distributions in FAPbBr₃ thin films over 0–500 ps. Carrier temperatures were extracted from the high-energy tail of the ground-state bleach feature at 530 nm as a function of pump fluence (10¹⁶–10¹⁸ cm⁻³ injected carrier density). At densities above 3 × 10¹⁷ cm⁻³ the effective carrier temperature remained above 600 K for more than 200 ps, a factor of four longer than at low fluences. This retardation is consistent with a hot-phonon bottleneck mechanism, supported by a reduction in LO-phonon decay rates inferred from a Fröhlich coupling analysis. Grain size, measured by atomic force microscopy, ranged from 200 to 800 nm and showed only weak correlation with hot-carrier lifetime, suggesting that the bulk phonon dynamics dominate. The results have implications for hot-carrier solar cell architectures operating under concentrated illumination.

title: Trap passivation in MAPbI₃ by phenethylammonium iodide surface treatment monitored via transient absorption
abstract: Surface passivation of MAPbI₃ films with phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI) was quantified using sub-picosecond transient absorption. Films with PEAI concentrations of 0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0 mg mL⁻¹ in isopropanol were spin-coated as a secondary layer. The amplitude of the fast (<1 ns) trap-filling component in the bleach recovery at 760 nm decreased by 74% for 1.0 mg mL⁻¹ PEAI compared with the unpassivated reference. Effective trap densities derived from the Auger–Mott model dropped from 1.8 × 10¹⁶ to 4.5 × 10¹⁵ cm⁻³. At concentrations above 2 mg mL⁻¹ a secondary phase was detected by XRD and recombination lifetimes shortened again. Steady-state photoluminescence quantum yield rose from 12% to 41% at optimal passivation. The correlation between spectroscopic trap density and PLQY provides a rapid non-contact screen for surface treatment optimisation.

title: Carrier recombination channels in mixed-halide FAPb(I₁₋ₓBrₓ)₃ films across the full composition range
abstract: A systematic transient absorption and TRPL study of FAPb(I₁₋ₓBrₓ)₃ films was performed for x = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0. Films were deposited by a two-step sequential conversion method. Carrier lifetimes, bimolecular recombination constants (k₂), and Auger constants (k₃) were extracted from fluence-dependent TRPL using a rate-equation model. k₂ increased monotonically from 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁰ cm³ s⁻¹ for pure I to 6.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ cm³ s⁻¹ for pure Br, consistent with the increase in oscillator strength. At intermediate compositions (x = 0.4–0.6) a fast non-radiative channel with an additional lifetime of 1.2–1.8 ns appeared and was correlated with halide segregation observed under prolonged illumination. Reversibility tests showed partial recovery of lifetimes in the dark within 12 hours. Phase segregation rates showed Arrhenius behaviour with an activation energy of 0.31 eV.

title: Influence of humidity-controlled annealing on carrier dynamics in CsFAMA triple-cation perovskite
abstract: CsFAMA triple-cation perovskite films (Cs₀.₀₅(FA₀.₈₃MA₀.₁₇)₀.₉₅Pb(I₀.₈₃Br₀.₁₇)₃) were annealed under controlled relative humidity (RH) of 0%, 10%, 20%, 35%, and 50% at 100 °C for 60 min. Transient absorption at 800 nm excitation/760 nm probe was used to measure ground-state bleach recovery from 0.5 ps to 5 ns. Films annealed at 20% RH showed the slowest bleach recovery, with average carrier lifetime τ_avg = 91 ns compared with 44 ns for dry-annealed films. SEM cross-sections indicated larger average grain size (480 nm vs. 280 nm) under 20% RH, supporting a grain-boundary passivation mechanism. At 50% RH a hydrated secondary phase was detected by XRD and carrier lifetimes degraded sharply. The optimal humidity window of 15–25% RH was robust across three different spin-coating setups, suggesting practical transferability.

title: Pump-fluence dependence of bleach saturation in MAPbI₃: artifact identification in transient absorption measurements
abstract: We report a systematic study of pump-fluence artefacts in transient absorption measurements of MAPbI₃ thin films that can lead to overestimation of carrier lifetimes and misidentification of Auger recombination thresholds. Fluences from 0.05 to 50 μJ cm⁻² were tested at 400 nm pump wavelength. Above 5 μJ cm⁻² the ground-state bleach at 760 nm showed saturation of ΔT/T beyond −30%, causing apparent lifetime elongation of up to 40% relative to low-fluence values. We identify two contributing factors: spectral broadening of the bleach at high carrier densities and laser-induced heating of the perovskite lattice (estimated ΔT < 8 K per pulse under our repetition conditions). Corrective procedures, including Beer–Lambert normalization and fluence extrapolation, are described. Applying these corrections to published literature data suggests that some reported hot-carrier lifetimes above 500 ps may require re-evaluation. Recommendations for measurement standards are proposed.

title: Carrier diffusion lengths in FA-rich perovskite films measured by one-dimensional transient grating spectroscopy
abstract: A transient grating (TG) technique was implemented to measure ambipolar carrier diffusion lengths in FA₀.₉₂MA₀.₀₈PbI₂.₉₂Br₀.₀₈ thin films without requiring a device architecture. Two 515 nm pump beams were crossed at angles producing fringe spacings Λ of 4, 7, 11, and 18 μm. The decay of the diffraction signal from a 800 nm probe as a function of grating spacing yielded a diffusion coefficient D = 0.18 cm² s⁻¹ at room temperature. Combined with TRPL lifetimes of 75 ns, an ambipolar diffusion length of 3.7 μm was calculated, consistent with independent time-of-flight data from a collaborating group. Measurements at 250, 280, and 310 K showed an Arrhenius-like decrease in D with decreasing temperature (activation energy 110 meV), attributed to polaron formation. The TG setup enables diffusion measurements on films not yet integrated into devices.

title: Spectral hole burning dynamics in Ruddlesden–Popper layered perovskites with n = 1 to 4
abstract: Spectral hole-burning experiments were performed on butylammonium lead iodide Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) perovskites with layer numbers n = 1, 2, 3, and 4, prepared by spin-coating from DMF/DMSO solutions. Narrow-band pump pulses (15 nm bandwidth, 400–490 nm) burned spectral holes that were probed by a white-light continuum. Hole widths at zero pump–probe delay were 22–36 meV across compositions, with broader holes observed for larger n. Hole filling times were 0.3 ps (n = 1) to 1.8 ps (n = 4), reflecting faster intraband scattering as the quantum-well structure approaches bulk. Carrier funnelling from low-n to high-n domains, expected in mixed-n films, was directly visualised as a rise in the n = 4 bleach feature delayed by 2–6 ps after excitation of the n = 1 exciton. The rate-limiting step for funnelling was modelled as Förster-type energy transfer with donor–acceptor overlap integral determined from steady-state spectra.

title: Effect of cesium content on non-radiative recombination in wide-bandgap perovskites for tandem applications
abstract: Wide-bandgap (Eg ≈ 1.75–1.82 eV) CsₓFA₁₋ₓPbI₁.₈Br₁.₂ films with x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, and 0.30 were characterised by transient absorption and absolute PLQY measurements to identify the Cs content that minimises non-radiative recombination losses. The non-radiative recombination rate knr was calculated from PLQY and TRPL according to knr = (1 − PLQY)/τ_avg. A minimum in knr of 3.1 × 10⁵ s⁻¹ was found at x = 0.15, corresponding to PLQY = 62% and τ_avg = 200 ns under 1-sun-equivalent continuous excitation. Transient absorption amplitudes at 2 ps correlated linearly with knr across the composition series, validating the short-time TA amplitude as a rapid predictor of non-radiative losses. Angle-resolved XRD confirmed that x = 0.15 also minimised microstrain, suggesting that lattice distortion contributes to trap formation in this system.

title: Time-resolved photoluminescence mapping of spatial inhomogeneity in perovskite films on 1 cm² areas
abstract: A scanning TRPL microscopy setup was constructed and used to map carrier lifetime spatial distributions across 1 cm² MAPbI₃ and CsFAMA films at 25 × 25 μm² pixel resolution (1600 pixels total). Lifetime maps were acquired under 470 nm pulsed excitation at 1 nJ cm⁻² per pulse. Coefficient-of-variation of τ_avg across the map was 18% for MAPbI₃ and 9% for CsFAMA, consistent with the better morphological uniformity of the triple-cation composition. Regions with lifetimes below 30% of the median clustered near film edges and were correlated with increased surface roughness (>15 nm rms). A gradient in lifetime from film centre to edge was found in all samples spin-coated at 3000 rpm but not in films processed at 4000 rpm with an anti-solvent drip. The spatial mapping approach provides quantitative input for device-level current-matching simulations.

title: Parametric Tauc–Lorentz dispersion model applied to spectroscopic ellipsometry data for amorphous carbon nitride
abstract: A Tauc–Lorentz (TL) oscillator model was used to describe the spectral dependence of the complex dielectric function ε(E) of a-CNx films over the photon energy range 1.2–5.0 eV. Films were deposited by reactive DC magnetron sputtering at five nitrogen concentrations (0, 5, 10, 20, 30 at.% N as determined by XPS). Ellipsometric spectra were recorded at 65° and 70° angle of incidence using a rotating-analyser instrument with a wavelength range of 250–900 nm. A two-layer optical model (surface roughness layer plus bulk film on Si) was fitted by Levenberg–Marquardt regression. The Tauc optical gap E_g extracted from the TL fit increased from 0.35 eV for pure amorphous carbon to 1.62 eV at 30 at.% N. The amplitude parameter A and broadening C of the TL oscillator varied monotonically with nitrogen content. Mean square error values for all fits were below 2.1, confirming model adequacy. The parametrised optical constants are made available as supplementary data.

title: Rotational Barriers in N-Acylhydrazones: Variable-Temperature ¹H NMR and Line-Shape Analysis
abstract: Restricted rotation around the C(O)–N bond in a series of twelve N-acylhydrazone derivatives was studied by variable-temperature ¹H NMR spectroscopy in DMSO-d₆ between 253 K and 373 K. Coalescence temperatures and line-shape fitting yielded free energies of activation ΔG‡ ranging from 68 to 89 kJ mol⁻¹, correlated with the electron-donating or electron-withdrawing character of para-substituents on the aryl ring (Hammett ρ = −1.3). Exchange of E and Z rotamers was confirmed by 2D EXSY experiments at 280 K. DFT calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) level reproduced measured barriers within ±4 kJ mol⁻¹. Population ratios of the two rotamers at 298 K span 60:40 to 96:4 depending on substitution pattern. The results establish a quantitative substituent–barrier relationship useful for predicting solution behaviour of this compound class.

title: E/Z Isomerism of Salicylaldehyde-Derived Hydrazones: NMR Assignment and Crystal Structures
abstract: Six hydrazone ligands derived from salicylaldehyde and substituted benzoylhydrazines were synthesised and characterised by ¹H, ¹³C, and ¹⁵N NMR spectroscopy in CDCl₃ and DMSO-d₆, as well as by X-ray crystallography. In the solid state all compounds adopt the E configuration with an intramolecular O–H···N hydrogen bond (O···N 2.61–2.68 Å). In DMSO-d₆ solution, E/Z ratios between 70:30 and 88:12 were measured by integration of resolved imine proton signals at 298 K. Assignment of configuration was made unambiguously using ¹H–¹⁵N HMBC correlations and comparison with DFT-predicted chemical shifts at the M06-2X/6-311+G(d,p) level. ¹⁵N chemical shifts of the imine nitrogen differ by approximately 20 ppm between the two isomers, providing a reliable diagnostic criterion for analogous series.

title: Solvent Dependence of Tautomeric Equilibria in Pyridine-2-carbaldehyde Hydrazones
abstract: The keto–enol and amino–imino tautomeric equilibria of seven pyridine-2-carbaldehyde hydrazones were examined in six solvents (CDCl₃, acetone-d₆, DMSO-d₆, methanol-d₄, acetonitrile-d₃, D₂O) by ¹H and ¹³C NMR at 298 K. Tautomeric populations were estimated from ¹³C shift differences between the C=O and C–OH carbons, calibrated against reference compounds of known tautomeric composition. In CDCl₃ the amino tautomer predominates (>90%) for all seven compounds, whereas in D₂O the imino tautomer fraction reaches up to 42% for electron-deficient derivatives. Linear regression against Kamlet–Taft solvent parameters shows that the π* polarity/polarisability scale accounts for 78% of variance in tautomeric ratio. DFT solvation energies computed with the SMD continuum model replicate the trend qualitatively.

title: Conformational Analysis of Thiosemicarbazone Schiff Bases by DFT and QTAIM: Intramolecular Hydrogen Bond Topology
abstract: Potential energy surfaces for internal rotation about the C=N–N–C(S) dihedral angle were computed for eleven thiosemicarbazone Schiff bases at the B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p) and M06-2X/6-311+G(d,p) levels in vacuo and in implicit DMSO. QTAIM analysis identified bond critical points characterising intramolecular N–H···N, N–H···S, and C–H···O interactions; the N–H···N bond path is present in the global minimum of nine out of eleven compounds, with electron density at the critical point ρ(r) between 0.023 and 0.031 a.u. Computed conformer populations were compared with integrals of rotamer-specific signals in variable-temperature ¹H NMR spectra (270–370 K, DMSO-d₆), yielding mean absolute deviation of 6% across the series. The relationship between the strength of the intramolecular hydrogen bond and the degree of conformational locking is discussed quantitatively.

title: Hydrazone Ligands as Extractants for Pb(II) and Cd(II) from Aqueous Model Solutions
abstract: Five hydrazone Schiff bases were evaluated for liquid–liquid extraction of Pb(II) and Cd(II) from buffered aqueous solutions (pH 3–8) into dichloromethane at ligand concentrations of 1–10 mM. Extraction efficiency was determined by atomic absorption spectroscopy on the aqueous phase after equilibration. The most effective ligand, bearing a pyridyl nitrogen and a terminal thioamide group, achieved 94% extraction of Pb(II) at pH 5.5 and 0.1 mM metal concentration, with a distribution ratio D = 16.3. Competitive extraction in the presence of equimolar Ca(II) and Mg(II) showed selectivity factors >30 for Pb over the alkaline earth ions. The speciation of extracted metal complexes was inferred from slope analysis (log D vs. log [L] gradients of 1.9–2.1), suggesting bis-ligand complex formation. NMR confirmation of the extracted species is included.

title: Substituent Effects on the E/Z Ratio of Aroylhydrazones in Aprotic Solvents: A Systematic ¹H NMR and DFT Study of 30 Derivatives
abstract: Thirty aroylhydrazone derivatives with systematically varied para-substituents on both the acyl aryl ring (σ_p from −0.83 to +0.78) and the imine aryl ring (σ_p from −0.66 to +0.66) were prepared and characterised in CDCl₃, acetone-d₆, and DMSO-d₆ at 298 K. E/Z ratios measured by ¹H NMR integration ranged from 98:2 to 52:48. Dual Hammett analysis with ρ_acyl = +0.41 (±0.05) and ρ_imine = −0.28 (±0.04) accounted for 91% of variance (R² = 0.91). DFT relative energies at the ωB97X-D/6-311+G(d,p) level in SMD-DMSO correlate with experimental ΔG values with a root-mean-square deviation of 1.2 kJ mol⁻¹. The study provides a predictive linear free-energy model for E/Z composition in this compound class, enabling rational design of predominantly E- or Z-configured hydrazone ligands.

title: DFT Benchmarking for Conformational Energies of Medium-Sized Hydrazone Schiff Bases: Selection of Functional and Basis Set
abstract: Relative energies of 48 conformer pairs of hydrazone Schiff bases were computed with 14 density functionals (GGA, hybrid, range-separated, and double-hybrid) paired with four basis sets (6-31G(d), 6-311+G(d,p), def2-TZVP, cc-pVTZ), and compared with DLPNO-CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ reference energies. Dispersion corrections (D3BJ) improved mean absolute deviations by 1.5–3.2 kJ mol⁻¹ for all hybrid functionals. The best performance was achieved by ωB97X-D/def2-TZVP (MAD = 0.8 kJ mol⁻¹, max error 2.1 kJ mol⁻¹) and B2-PLYP-D3/def2-TZVP (MAD = 0.6 kJ mol⁻¹). B3LYP/6-31G(d), widely used in earlier literature on this compound class, showed MAD = 3.4 kJ mol⁻¹ and systematic underestimation of conformer energy differences exceeding 2 kJ mol⁻¹ in 21 of 48 cases. Recommendations for practical computational workflows are provided with attention to computational cost.

title: Hydrazone Schiff Bases as Potential Ligands for Selective Complexation of Cu(II) over Zn(II) and Ni(II): Thermodynamic and Structural Study
abstract: Potentiometric titrations (298 K, I = 0.1 M KNO₃) were performed for twelve hydrazone ligands with Cu(II), Zn(II), and Ni(II), covering pH 2–11. Stepwise stability constants (log K_ML) for Cu(II) ranged from 9.8 to 13.2, exceeding those for Zn(II) by 1.8–4.1 log units and those for Ni(II) by 2.3–5.0 log units in the same series, consistent with the Irving–Williams order. The selectivity gap widened with increasing size of the intramolecular chelate ring from five to six members. ESI-MS confirmed 1:1 and 1:2 (M:L) stoichiometries in solution at pH 6 and 9 respectively. EPR spectra of Cu(II) complexes in frozen DMSO/water glass (77 K) showed axially symmetric signals with g‖ = 2.26–2.30 and A‖ = 165–178 × 10⁻⁴ cm⁻¹, confirming a CuN₂O₂ or CuN₂OS coordination environment.

title: Conformational Analysis of Fluorinated Hydrazone Schiff Bases: Effect of ortho-F Substitution on E/Z Ratio and Chelation Geometry
abstract: Introduction of fluorine at the ortho position of the imine aryl ring in a series of nine salicylaldehyde hydrazones produced systematic changes in E/Z equilibrium and in the geometry of the intramolecular O–H···N=C hydrogen bond. ¹H NMR in DMSO-d₆ at 298 K showed that ortho-F substitution increased the E isomer fraction from an average of 78% to 91% compared with unsubstituted analogues, attributed to a steric and electrostatic destabilisation of the Z rotamer. ¹⁹F NMR chemical shifts and ¹H–¹⁹F coupling constants provided additional conformational constraints, validated by DFT conformer geometries at ωB97X-D/def2-TZVP. Quantum theory of atoms in molecules analysis of the intramolecular hydrogen bond showed ρ(r) = 0.041–0.048 a.u. for the E conformer in the fluorinated series, compared with 0.035–0.042 a.u. for the unsubstituted series, indicating slight strengthening of the hydrogen bond on fluorination.

title: Hydrazone Schiff Base Ligands for Selective Sensing of Cu(II) in Water: Colorimetric Response and Solution Speciation
abstract: Three water-soluble hydrazone ligands incorporating sulphonate or quaternary ammonium groups were synthesised and evaluated as colorimetric probes for Cu(II) in buffered aqueous solution at pH 7.4. Addition of Cu(II) produced a bathochromic shift of 68–85 nm in the π→π* absorption band, with molar absorptivity changes Δε = 1.2–2.8 × 10⁴ L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹ at the detection wavelength. Limits of detection were 0.8–2.1 μM. Selectivity experiments with 12 competing metal ions at tenfold excess showed interference only from Fe(III) at micromolar concentrations. Job's method and UV titrations confirmed 1:1 Cu:L stoichiometry at pH 7.4. NMR speciation studies in D₂O at pD 7.4 confirmed the presence of a single complex species under analytical conditions. The ligands were tested in tap water spiked with 5 μM Cu(II), achieving recovery of 96–102%.

title: Low-Temperature ¹³C and ¹⁵N NMR of Hydrazone Tautomers: Quantitative Populations at 200 K in Glassy DMSO-d₆
abstract: Tautomeric equilibria in five pyridyl hydrazones were frozen out below 220 K in DMSO-d₆, allowing direct observation of individual tautomers by ¹³C and ¹⁵N NMR at 400 MHz. At 200 K, signals of the amino (NH–N=CH) and imino (N=N–CH=) tautomers are resolved by 4–9 ppm in ¹³C and 18–26 ppm in ¹⁵N. Integration of ¹³C signals after inverse-gated decoupling gave tautomeric ratios of 88:12 to 62:38 (amino:imino), varying with substituent electron demand. Van't Hoff analysis of ratios measured between 200 and 280 K yielded ΔH° = −3.4 to −8.9 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS° = −4 to +6 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ for the amino-to-imino equilibrium. These experimental thermodynamic parameters are compared with DFT-predicted free energy differences in SMD-DMSO, showing systematic overestimation of the imino tautomer stability by approximately 3 kJ mol⁻¹ at B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p).

title: Nickel(II) and Palladium(II) Complexes of Conformationally Locked Hydrazone Ligands: Solid-State and Solution Comparison
abstract: Eight hydrazone ligands designed to favour the E,s-trans conformation through an intramolecular five-membered hydrogen-bonded ring were complexed with NiCl₂ and PdCl₂ in ethanol. X-ray structures of six complexes confirmed square-planar geometry; Ni–N distances are 1.84–1.89 Å and Pd–N 1.99–2.05 Å. The solid-state conformation of the free ligands (E,s-trans) is retained upon coordination, as verified by comparison of bond lengths and angles with DFT-optimised structures at B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVP. In DMSO-d₆ solution, ¹H NMR of the Pd complexes shows broadened signals at 298 K that sharpen below 260 K, attributed to slow exchange between two coordination isomers. Variable-temperature spectra yield ΔG‡ = 72 ± 3 kJ mol⁻¹ for the isomerisation process. The Ni complexes show no such dynamics, consistent with the higher ligand-field stabilisation energy for Ni(II) in a square-planar environment.

title: Seasonal and varietal variation in carotenoid-derived aroma volatiles in Capsicum annuum grown under controlled field conditions in Vojvodina
abstract: Four Capsicum annuum varieties (two sweet, one mildly pungent, one hot) were grown in a single Vojvodina field location over two consecutive seasons (2014–2015). Fruit pericarp at five ripeness stages was analysed for carotenoid-derived volatiles (β-ionone, 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one, geranylacetone, pseudoionone) by HS-SPME-GC-MS. β-Ionone concentrations ranged from 1.4 to 12.8 µg/kg fresh weight across all samples. Season had a significant main effect on geranylacetone content (p < 0.01), with the drier 2015 season yielding higher concentrations. Varietal differences were most pronounced for β-ionone and pseudoionone. The data provide agronomic context for interpreting variability in flavour precursors before industrial processing.

title: Flavour chemistry of thermally processed Capsicum products: a review of compound classes, formation pathways, and analytical approaches
abstract: This chapter reviews the chemistry underlying flavour formation and off-flavour development in roasted, dried, and fermented Capsicum annuum products. Three main compound classes are discussed: (1) carotenoid oxidative cleavage products responsible for floral and fruity notes; (2) Maillard reaction-derived pyrazines, furans, and carbonyl compounds arising from thermal treatment of reducing sugars and free amino acids; and (3) polyphenol oxidation products associated with bitterness and astringency. Analytical methodology is surveyed, covering SPME-GC-MS, HPLC-DAD, HPLC-MS/MS, GC-olfactometry, and AEDA. The interaction between lipid oxidation and Maillard pathways is discussed with reference to pepper-specific substrate composition. Gaps in the literature concerning fermented Capsicum products and low-temperature processing are identified. The chapter is intended as a reference for food scientists working on quality control in the pepper processing industry.

title: Comparative kinetics of fluoride, chloride, and nitro displacement in 2,4-dinitrohalo- and 2,4-dinitroarenes: leaving-group ability revisited
abstract: The SNAr reactions of 2,4-difluoronitrobenzene, 2,4-dichloronitrobenzene, 2,4-dibromonitrobenzene, and 1-methoxy-2,4-dinitrobenzene with morpholine in aqueous acetonitrile (30% H2O, v/v) at 25 °C were compared under rigorously controlled conditions. Stopped-flow second-order rate constants were 740, 18, 6.2, and 0.08 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ for F, Cl, Br, and OMe leaving groups respectively. The leaving-group ability order F ≫ Cl > Br ≫ OMe is the reverse of that in aliphatic SN2 and is rationalised here using a thermodynamic cycle that accounts for C–X bond strength, electron-pair acceptance in the Meisenheimer complex, and partial negative charge on the leaving group in the transition state estimated from DFT Natural Bond Orbital charges (B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)). Activation parameters for each substrate are reported and compared with predictions from Marcus rate theory using DFT-computed reaction energies. The DFT calculations were performed by collaborators at the University of Tübingen.

title: Fluorescence spectroscopic characterisation of tryptophan and tyrosine environments in pumpkin seed 2S albumin
abstract: Intrinsic fluorescence spectroscopy was used to probe the microenvironmental changes around aromatic residues in the 2S albumin fraction isolated from pumpkin (Cucurbita pepo) seeds. Emission spectra were recorded at excitation wavelengths of 280 nm and 295 nm to resolve contributions from tyrosine and tryptophan residues, respectively. At neutral pH and 25 °C, the peak emission wavelength was 338 nm, suggesting partial burial of tryptophan in a moderately hydrophobic environment. Thermal scans from 20 to 95 °C at a heating rate of 1 °C/min revealed a cooperative red shift to 353 nm with a midpoint near 74 °C, consistent with exposure of the chromophore to solvent upon unfolding. Acrylamide quenching experiments confirmed reduced solvent accessibility of tryptophan in the native state (Ksv = 3.1 M⁻¹) compared to the thermally unfolded form (Ksv = 8.7 M⁻¹). The data indicate a two-state-like unfolding behaviour and provide baseline parameters for aggregation propensity studies.

title: Effect of Methyl Substitution on the Stability of Gd(III) Complexes with EDTA Derivatives: A Potentiometric Study
abstract: Four N-methyl derivatives of EDTA—NMe-EDTA, N,N'-diMe-EDTA, N,N,N'-triMe-EDTA, and N,N,N',N'-tetraMe-EDTA—were synthesised and their Gd³⁺ complexes characterised by potentiometric titration in 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaClO4 at 25 °C. Protonation constants of the free ligands and stability constants of the 1:1 Gd complexes were determined using the program HYPERQUAD2008; fits had σ < 0.003 in all cases. Log β for [GdEDTA]⁻ (17.35 ± 0.03) decreased to 14.82 ± 0.04 for the tetramethyl derivative. The progressive destabilisation, averaging −0.63 log units per methyl group, is attributed to steric constraints on N-coordination and a reduction in the number of effective donor atoms available for chelation. The pattern mirrors observations in Cu(II) and Zn(II) systems but is quantitatively more pronounced for Gd(III) due to its larger ionic radius and preference for higher coordination numbers.

title: Refusal Strategies in Serbian Learners of English: A Discourse Completion Task Study
abstract: This study investigates how Serbian-speaking university students in Novi Sad perform refusals in English compared with native English speakers. Sixty participants completed a written discourse completion task comprising twelve scenarios varying in social distance and power asymmetry. Responses were coded using a modified version of the Beebe, Takahashi, and Uliss-Weltz taxonomy. Results show that Serbian learners favour direct refusal formulas significantly more often than the British English baseline group (38% vs. 17%), and that mitigation devices such as preparators and reasons appear with lower frequency in higher-power scenarios. Transfer from L1 politeness norms is proposed as the primary explanatory factor. The findings carry implications for EFL curriculum design at Serbian universities, particularly regarding the explicit teaching of pragmatic mitigation.

title: Compliment Responses Among Hungarian–Serbian Bilingual Speakers of English: Evidence from Vojvodina
abstract: This paper examines compliment response behaviour in English produced by Hungarian–Serbian bilingual university students in Vojvodina, comparing them with monolingual Serbian-English learners and a British English reference group. Data consist of 144 recorded role-play interactions elicited in controlled lab sessions. Responses were classified into acceptance, deflection, and rejection sequences, with subcategories following Pomerantz's framework. Bilingual participants showed a statistically significant tendency toward deflection strategies (52%) compared with monolingual Serbian learners (39%), a pattern partially attributed to Hungarian politeness norms emphasising modesty. Token agreement followed by a topic shift was the most frequent deflection subtype across both learner groups. The study contributes to the growing body of research on how multiple L1 backgrounds shape L2 pragmatic choices, and raises questions about pedagogical treatment of compliment behaviour in regional EFL classrooms.

title: Teaching Pragmatics Explicitly: An Intervention Study in Serbian Secondary Schools
abstract: A quasi-experimental design was used to assess whether eight hours of explicit pragmatics instruction could reduce pragmatic failure rates in English-language classrooms in three secondary schools in Novi Sad. The treatment group (n = 67) received lessons targeting request and apology speech acts using authentic video stimuli and metalinguistic discussion, while the control group (n = 64) followed the standard curriculum. Pre- and post-tests employed role-play recordings scored for pragmatic appropriateness by trained raters. The treatment group showed a significant improvement in apology elaboration and request mitigation between test points (d = 0.62), while the control group showed no significant change. Gains were partially retained at an eight-week delayed post-test. The study supports the teachability of pragmatic competence and argues for explicit awareness-raising activities at secondary level.

title: Apology Strategies in a Multilingual Contact Zone: English as a Lingua Franca in Vojvodina Business Settings
abstract: This paper investigates English apology behaviour in professional interactions among Vojvodina employees who use English as a lingua franca. Twenty-four semi-structured role-play interviews were audio-recorded with participants from Serbian, Hungarian, and Slovak language backgrounds employed at five mid-sized companies in the Novi Sad area. Apologies were segmented and coded for strategy type, intensity markers, and sequential position. Across all groups, the most common apology formula was an explicit IFID followed by an explanation, but intensity upgraders appeared significantly more often in Serbian-background speakers than in Hungarian-background speakers. Pragmatic failure incidents were most frequent at conversation-closing sequences. The results suggest that lingua franca contexts in multilingual regions generate systematic, ethnolinguistically patterned variation rather than convergent ELF norms as proposed in some ELF literature.
