title: Face-Threatening Acts and Power in Serbian University Discourse: An L2 English Perspective
abstract: Drawing on Brown and Levinson's politeness framework, this chapter examines how Serbian university students navigate face-threatening acts when speaking English in hierarchically structured academic interactions. Data consist of 37 audio-recorded supervision meetings between students and tutors at the Faculty of Philosophy, collected over two academic years with full participant consent. Acts were tagged for face threat type, speaker role, and redressive action employed. Analysis reveals a pronounced asymmetry: students performing high-imposition acts in English employed on-record strategies with bald politeness mitigation at a higher rate than comparable data from British university corpora, suggesting that Serbian academic norms of directness persist in L2 performance. Power asymmetry was a stronger predictor of strategy selection than social distance, contrary to predictions from cross-cultural studies conducted outside the South Slavic area.

title: Cross-Cultural Pragmatic Failure in English-Mediated Job Interviews: Serbian Applicants and Austrian Interviewers
abstract: This paper reports a study of cross-cultural pragmatic failure in simulated job interviews conducted in English between Serbian university graduates (n = 30) and Austrian human resources professionals (n = 10) who served as interviewers. Interviews were video-recorded and transcribed; both parties completed post-interview questionnaires rating communication smoothness and candidate competence. Discourse analysis identified 218 instances of perceived interactional trouble, of which 41% were associated with candidate self-promotion acts: Serbian applicants consistently produced shorter, less elaborated self-presentation turns than interviewers expected. Interviewers rated candidates lower on communication competence than on technical knowledge, indicating that pragmatic failure had a measurable effect on professional evaluation. The paper argues for targeted preparation for Serbian graduates seeking employment in Central European multilingual workplaces.

title: Annotating Pragmatic Failure in a Learner Corpus: Scheme Development and Reliability Testing
abstract: This methodological paper describes the development and reliability assessment of a pragmatic failure annotation scheme designed for use with the Vojvodina English Learner Corpus (VELC), a 280,000-word collection of spoken and written L2 English produced by university students in Novi Sad between 2012 and 2017. The annotation scheme covers six failure categories: sociopragmatic failure, pragmalinguistic failure, register mismatch, formulaic underuse, implicature breakdown, and sequential disruption. Fourteen trained annotators applied the scheme to a 40,000-word subcorpus in two phases. Inter-annotator agreement was measured using Fleiss' κ, reaching 0.74 overall, with the lowest agreement for implicature breakdown (κ = 0.61). The paper discusses refinements made after phase one and provides annotation guidelines as a supplementary resource. The scheme is proposed as a tool for other researchers working with South Slavic learner corpora.

title: Politeness Norms in Technical English Communication: A Study of Engineering Students from Vojvodina
abstract: This paper examines politeness norms in written English technical communication produced by final-year engineering students (n = 112) at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. Participants wrote three task-based texts: a complaint letter to a supplier, a collaborative project update email, and a report section delivering negative results. Texts were analysed for positive and negative politeness strategies, use of hedging language, and explicit acknowledgement of the reader's face needs. Engineering students produced significantly fewer hedging devices in the negative-results report (mean = 1.8 per 100 words) compared with a reference corpus of published engineering research articles (mean = 4.3 per 100 words). Students with higher general English proficiency did not systematically produce more pragmatically appropriate texts, indicating that pragmatic competence and linguistic proficiency are partially dissociated skills in this domain.

title: Perception of Impoliteness in L2 English by Native Serbian Speakers: A Rating Scale Study
abstract: This study investigates whether Serbian speakers identify the same utterances as impolite when encountered in English as when encountered in Serbian translations of those utterances. One hundred and eight participants rated 48 constructed dialogue excerpts in both languages using a seven-point impoliteness scale; a two-week washout period separated the two rating sessions. Mixed-effects modelling showed that participants rated English-language versions as significantly less impolite than their Serbian equivalents (β = −0.41, p < .001), particularly for bald-on-record directives and sarcastic comments. The effect was moderated by participants' length of formal English instruction: those with more than ten years of instruction showed a smaller cross-language difference. Findings suggest that metalinguistic awareness of L2 pragmatic norms does not fully compensate for affect-loaded L1 perceptual defaults.

title: Pragmatic Competence Profiles Across Three Generations of Vojvodina Hungarians Speaking English
abstract: This intergenerational study compares pragmatic competence in English among three cohorts of Vojvodina Hungarians: grandparents (born 1945–1960, n = 24), parents (born 1970–1985, n = 26), and young adults (born 1998–2005, n = 28). A combination of discourse completion tasks, multiple-choice pragmatics tests, and short role-play recordings was used. Young adults scored highest on pragmatic appropriateness across all task types (mean composite score 71/100 vs. 48/100 for grandparents), reflecting greater cumulative English exposure through schooling, digital media, and travel. However, specific speech acts, notably condolences and formal protests, showed persistent low scores across all generations, suggesting that certain pragmatic domains are resistant to informal acquisition. The study is the first to take a lifespan perspective on EFL pragmatics in the Vojvodina Hungarian community.

title: Request Softening in AI-Mediated Communication: Do Vojvodina Students Adjust Politeness When Writing to Chatbots in English?
abstract: This exploratory study examines whether Vojvodina university students (n = 89) modulate request politeness strategies when addressing an English-language chatbot interface compared with addressing a human interlocutor in the same task. Participants completed matched sets of information-seeking requests directed at either a labelled chatbot or a labelled human respondent in a controlled online environment. Texts were coded for presence of greetings, please particles, modal hedges, and closing courtesies. Participants used significantly fewer politeness markers when addressing the chatbot condition across all four categories (e.g., modal hedge rate: 1.1 vs. 2.7 per request). Individual variation was high, with a minority (19%) showing no reduction. Age and self-reported frequency of chatbot use were not significant predictors. Results are discussed in relation to pragmatic awareness, human-computer interaction norms, and implications for workplace communication training involving AI tools.

title: Discourse Markers and Turn-Taking in English-Medium Instruction Lectures: A Vojvodina University Case
abstract: This paper reports findings from an observational study of twelve English-medium instruction (EMI) lectures delivered at the University of Novi Sad during the 2024–2025 academic year, covering disciplines including law, economics, and biology. Lectures were audio-recorded, transcribed, and coded for discourse markers signalling topic shifts, floor-holding, and student turn-yielding. Lecturers used an average of 4.2 discourse markers per minute, a rate comparable to EMI data from Slovak and Croatian universities in the literature, but student-initiated turn-taking was markedly lower (0.9 student turns per 10-minute segment) than in Western European EMI corpora. Post-lecture questionnaires indicated that students reported uncertainty about when turn-taking was pragmatically permissible in an English-language academic context. The paper argues that EMI policies at Serbian universities need to incorporate explicit guidance on interactive pragmatic norms for both lecturers and students.

title: Discourse of Stagnation: How Prolonged Candidate Status Is Narrated in Novi Sad English-Language Student Journalism
abstract: This paper investigates how student journalists at the University of Novi Sad construct EU accession in an English-language university publication over a five-year period (2017–2022). A corpus of 210 student-produced articles was analysed using keyword analysis in Sketch Engine and qualitative CDA. Student texts depart notably from professional press conventions: the journey metaphor is almost absent, replaced by stasis metaphors ('stuck', 'standstill', 'waiting room') at significantly higher rates than in professional corpora compiled for comparison. Evaluative language shows higher proportions of negative Judgement directed at both domestic politicians and EU officials. The paper contextualises these findings in relation to broader youth attitude surveys and argues that student journalism constitutes a distinct discursive space in which scepticism toward EU enlargement is more openly expressed than in professionally edited outlets.

title: Influence of bovine serum albumin and casein blocking on non-specific binding in nitrocellulose-based lateral-flow strips for ochratoxin A detection
abstract: Non-specific protein adsorption on nitrocellulose membranes is a primary source of false-positive signals in lateral-flow immunoassays. This study compared four blocking strategies—bovine serum albumin (BSA) at 0.5% and 2%, casein at 1%, and polyvinyl alcohol at 0.2%—applied to Whatman CN140 membranes functionalised with anti-ochratoxin A polyclonal antibodies. Blocking efficiency was quantified by measuring residual protein by micro-BCA assay and by recording background reflectance in a portable strip reader. Strips blocked with 1% casein showed the lowest background reflectance (4.1 ± 0.3 arbitrary units) and the highest signal-to-noise ratio at 2 µg/L ochratoxin A in buffer. Sensitivity was reduced by approximately 30% when the same strips were challenged with raw maize extract, attributable to phenolic compounds identified by HPLC. Pre-treating extracts with activated charcoal at 0.1 g/mL partially restored sensitivity. These findings provide a systematic basis for selecting blocking conditions that balance non-specific adsorption suppression with tolerance to complex grain matrices.

title: Effect of conjugate pad material and gold nanoparticle size on signal intensity in competitive lateral-flow immunoassays for deoxynivalenol
abstract: Conjugate pad selection and gold nanoparticle (AuNP) diameter are rarely studied together in lateral-flow immunoassay optimisation. This work evaluated three pad materials (glass fibre, polyester, and rayon) and three AuNP diameters (20, 40, and 60 nm) conjugated with anti-deoxynivalenol (DON) monoclonal antibody clone DON-7 in a competitive format targeting DON in wheat flour extracts. Reflectance at the test line was measured with a desktop strip analyser. The 40 nm AuNPs on glass fibre pads produced the lowest IC50 value (18 µg/L DON in buffer), with a detection limit of 4.3 µg/L. The 60 nm particles showed higher background signals and irregular flow on rayon pads. In spiked wheat flour extract (50% methanol/water extraction), the IC50 shifted to 29 µg/L, a 1.6-fold matrix-induced suppression. Pre-dilution of the extract twofold with PBS reduced suppression to 1.2-fold with acceptable sensitivity. Optimised strips were stable at 37°C for six weeks in sealed pouches.

title: Comparative performance of enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and lateral-flow immunochromatography for aflatoxin B1 screening in sunflower meal: interlaboratory evaluation
abstract: An interlaboratory exercise involving four laboratories in Serbia and Romania compared the performance of a microplate ELISA kit and an in-house lateral-flow strip for aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) in sunflower meal. Each laboratory analysed a set of 24 blind samples at AFB1 concentrations of 0, 2, 5, 10, and 20 µg/kg prepared by spiking certified blank material. The ELISA showed within-laboratory repeatability (CVr) of 7–14% and between-laboratory reproducibility (CVR) of 18–23%. The lateral-flow strip, read visually, achieved 94% correct classification at the 5 µg/kg threshold but produced three false negatives at 2 µg/kg. A portable reflectance reader improved false-negative rate to zero at 5 µg/kg across all sites. Matrix-matched calibration reduced bias in ELISA from −22% to −8%. Results support the use of lateral-flow strips as screening tools at EU regulatory thresholds when combined with quantitative readers, while confirming that sunflower meal lipids require a defatting step prior to extraction.

title: Matrix interference mitigation in urine-based lateral-flow immunoassays for cortisol: effect of sample dilution, pH adjustment, and competitive binding inhibitors
abstract: Urine presents substantial matrix challenges for immunochromatographic cortisol assays owing to variability in creatinine, pH (4.5–8.5 across donors), and co-eluting steroid metabolites. This study systematically examined three mitigation strategies applied to a competitive lateral-flow assay using an anti-cortisol monoclonal antibody (clone COR-3). Tenfold dilution with phosphate buffer (pH 7.2) reduced average cortisol cross-reactivity from corticosterone from 14% to 6% while shifting the assay detection limit from 1.8 to 18 nmol/L. pH normalisation to 7.0 ± 0.2 without dilution reduced false-positive rate from 11% to 3% in 120 clinical urine samples. Addition of 50 mM lithium chloride as a chaotropic agent did not significantly improve specificity. An optimised protocol combining fivefold dilution with pH adjustment achieved a bias of less than 10% versus LC-MS/MS reference values across the physiological range. The strip showed acceptable performance (sensitivity 92%, specificity 88%) against cortisol concentrations relevant to screening for adrenal dysfunction.

title: Quantitative lateral-flow immunoassay for fumonisin B1 in maize silage: optimisation of antibody loading density and hapten–protein conjugate molar ratio
abstract: Quantitative performance of competitive lateral-flow strips for fumonisin B1 (FB1) in maize silage is frequently limited by poorly controlled antibody loading density at the test line and variable hapten–protein conjugate ratios at the control line. Antibody (clone FUM-6) was dispensed at six concentrations (0.5–3.0 mg/mL) onto CN95 nitrocellulose membrane using a non-contact dispensing robot, and three hapten–ovalbumin molar ratios (5:1, 10:1, and 20:1) were evaluated. Signal response curves were fitted to a four-parameter logistic model. The 1.5 mg/mL antibody loading with a 10:1 hapten–ovalbumin ratio produced the widest dynamic range (0.5–80 µg/kg FB1) and the lowest coefficient of variation at IC50 (6.2%). Strips were evaluated on 46 naturally contaminated silage samples; results correlated with HPLC-FLD reference values (r = 0.96, slope = 0.98). The study demonstrates that antibody loading density rather than hapten conjugate ratio is the dominant factor governing strip sensitivity in this system.

title: Immunoassay development for feed analysis: principles, matrix challenges, and regulatory context in Southeast Europe
abstract: This book chapter reviews the theoretical and practical aspects of immunoassay development specifically for animal feed matrices, with an emphasis on conditions and regulatory requirements applicable to Serbia and neighbouring countries. Topics covered include selection of hapten design strategies for small-molecule mycotoxins, comparison of polyclonal and monoclonal antibody sources, validation parameters required under Serbian Regulation on Methods for Official Feed Control, and published performance data for lateral-flow and ELISA formats applied to cereals, oilseed meals, and mixed feeds. A section on matrix effect quantification reviews recovery experiments, matrix-matched calibration, and QuEChERS-based clean-up as applied to immunochromatographic formats. Practical guidance is given on establishing in-house reference material for laboratories without access to certified standards. The chapter concludes with a discussion of harmonisation challenges between domestic legislation and EU Regulation 2002/32/EC on undesirable substances in feed.

title: Effect of lipopolysaccharide co-extraction on anti-endotoxin antibody binding in lateral-flow immunoassays for bacterial contamination screening of poultry processing water
abstract: Lateral-flow strips designed to detect lipopolysaccharide (LPS) as a bacterial contamination marker in poultry processing water encounter interference from co-extracted humic substances and residual detergents. This study characterised LPS binding to anti-LPS IgG (clone LPS-9) by surface plasmon resonance and found that sodium dodecyl sulphate at 0.01% reduced ka by 40% without affecting kd, while fulvic acid at 5 mg/L inhibited both constants comparably. Strips were tested with 88 water samples from three poultry processing facilities; LPS concentrations ranged from below the detection limit to 240 EU/mL by the reference limulus amebocyte lysate (LAL) assay. At a cut-off of 10 EU/mL, the lateral-flow strip showed sensitivity of 87% and specificity of 91% before water sample pre-treatment. A solid-phase extraction step using C18 cartridges raised sensitivity to 95%. These results indicate that organic co-extractants rather than inorganic ions are the primary source of false negatives in this application.

title: Optimising regeneration conditions for surface plasmon resonance kinetic measurements of low-affinity mycotoxin–antibody interactions
abstract: Low-affinity interactions (KD > 100 nM) between small-molecule mycotoxin haptens and antibodies present specific challenges for surface plasmon resonance (SPR) measurements: incomplete regeneration leads to progressive ligand inactivation while harsh regeneration damages the chip surface. This study screened 12 regeneration solutions across four antibody–hapten systems relevant to mycotoxin immunoassay development (anti-AFB1, anti-DON, anti-ZEN, and anti-T2 toxin antibody–ovalbumin conjugates immobilised on CM5 chips). Conditions evaluated included glycine-HCl (pH 1.5–2.5), NaOH (1–10 mM), guanidine-HCl (1–4 M), and HCl/ethylene glycol mixtures. For the anti-DON system, 10 mM NaOH for 30 s provided >95% regeneration with less than 5% signal loss per cycle over 200 cycles. For anti-AFB1, 4 M guanidine-HCl was required, with 12% cumulative signal loss over 200 cycles. A flow rate of 30 µL/min during regeneration reduced carryover compared to 5 µL/min for all systems. Recommended regeneration protocols for each antibody class are tabulated with reproducibility data.

title: Signal drift and humidity-dependent performance variation in lateral-flow immunoassay strips stored under field conditions: a six-month study
abstract: Field deployment of lateral-flow immunoassay strips in agricultural environments involves temperature fluctuations and variable humidity, yet stability studies in regulatory submissions typically use controlled accelerated ageing at fixed conditions. This study monitored performance of anti-AFB1 lateral-flow strips (n = 720 strips across six lots) stored in sealed foil pouches at three field sites in Vojvodina across a full growing season (April–September). Relative humidity at storage sites ranged from 38 to 87%. Strips were retrieved monthly and tested with a five-point calibration set. IC50 values increased progressively from 2.8 to 5.1 µg/kg AFB1 over six months at the highest-humidity site (site 3, mean RH 74%), while strips at the lowest-humidity site (site 1, mean RH 44%) remained within 15% of baseline IC50 throughout. Visual inspection of used strips showed membrane yellowing correlated with humidity-associated signal drift (r = 0.83). A silica gel desiccant doubled in quantity per pouch stabilised IC50 drift to within 18% across all sites. These data support revising field-stability testing protocols to include humidity as a controlled variable.

title: Triacylglycerol Fingerprinting of Cold-Pressed Hemp Seed Oil as a Tool for Adulteration Detection
abstract: Hemp seed oil (Cannabis sativa L.) is susceptible to adulteration with cheaper refined sunflower or soybean oil due to its market price. Forty-seven commercial samples and twelve laboratory-prepared binary mixtures were analysed by reversed-phase HPLC-MS/MS in MRM mode targeting fourteen characteristic triacylglycerol species. A principal component analysis of the resulting fingerprints separated pure hemp seed oil from all binary mixtures containing ≥10% adulterant with 100% correct classification. A partial least-squares regression model for quantification of sunflower oil admixture achieved RMSECV of 3.2% and RMSEP of 4.1% on an independent validation set. The method requires no saponification or derivatisation and run time per sample is 22 minutes. Three of the commercial samples were classified as potentially adulterated based on the model output. The approach is proposed as a complementary tool to fatty acid profiling for quality assurance laboratories.

title: Kinetic model for co-fermentation of glucose and xylose by an engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain: parameter identifiability and confidence intervals
abstract: Lignocellulosic bioethanol production requires efficient co-fermentation of hexose and pentose sugars, but standard Monod kinetics do not adequately capture the competitive inhibition between glucose and xylose transport in engineered strains. A structured kinetic model incorporating competitive substrate inhibition terms, a variable maintenance coefficient, and product inhibition by ethanol above 60 g/L was developed and fitted to batch fermentation data from an engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain carrying xylose isomerase and xylulokinase overexpression constructs. Twelve batch experiments at glucose:xylose ratios of 2:1, 1:1, and 1:2 (w/w) with total sugar concentrations of 80 and 120 g/L were conducted. Profile likelihood analysis was used to assess parameter identifiability, revealing that three of eleven parameters were practically non-identifiable from batch data alone and required additional fed-batch experiments for unique estimation. Final model fits achieved R² > 0.95 for biomass, ethanol, and both sugar profiles. The identifiability analysis workflow is presented as a transferable procedure for similar fermentation modelling studies.

title: Microbial phytase from Aspergillus ficuum: characterisation of a commercial preparation and its performance in sourdough fermentation of rye flour
abstract: A commercial Aspergillus ficuum phytase preparation (Phytazyme CF, activity 5000 U/g as declared) was characterised for pH optimum, temperature stability, and kinetic parameters before application in rye sourdough. The enzyme showed maximum activity at pH 4.5 and 50 °C, with Km of 0.41 mM toward sodium phytate. Activity was retained above 80% after 2 hours at 45 °C but dropped to 34% after heating to 70 °C. In rye sourdough fermentation at 30 °C and pH 4.2, supplementation at 100 U/g flour reduced phytic acid from 8.7 to 1.4 mg/g after 16 hours, compared with 3.9 mg/g in an unsupplemented control. Caco-2 cell ferritin formation assay indicated a 2.4-fold increase in iron uptake efficiency for phytase-supplemented sourdough. No significant effect on loaf volume or crumb structure was detected by image analysis.

title: Influence of baking temperature profile on 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline concentration in the crust of white wheat bread
abstract: Five baking temperature profiles (constant 180 °C, constant 220 °C, and three stepped programmes with different pre-bake and final-bake stages) were applied to standardised white wheat bread loaves at pilot scale. Crust samples were separated by scraping within 5 min of baking and extracted by solvent-assisted flavour evaporation (SAFE). 2-Acetyl-1-pyrroline (2-AP) was quantified by GC–MS/MS using ²H₃-labelled internal standard; concentration ranged from 14 to 67 µg kg⁻¹ crust across profiles. A stepped profile with initial 180 °C for 10 min followed by 230 °C for 18 min produced the highest 2-AP at 67 µg kg⁻¹. Total pyrazine concentration correlated positively with final crust temperature (r = 0.91), but 2-AP showed a non-linear response with a maximum between 210–225 °C. Crumb volatile content was below quantification limits for 2-AP in all profiles. Results are relevant to industrial baking parameter optimisation for aroma quality.

title: Part-of-Speech Tagging of Serbian Internet Forum Text: Challenges from Phonological Respelling
abstract: This paper examines the degradation of a standard Serbian part-of-speech tagger when applied to forum discussion data collected from a domestic automotive enthusiast community. A corpus of approximately 42,000 tokens was manually annotated using the MULTEXT-East tagset adapted for Serbian. Analysis showed that phonological respelling conventions—such as omission of diacritics, phonetic elongation, and loanword integration without morphological adaptation—caused tagger error rates to rise from 4.2% on newspaper text to 19.7% on the forum corpus. The paper describes a post-processing layer that applies rule-based normalization to the most frequent respelling patterns before tagging. After applying this layer to the 300 most frequent non-standard forms, the error rate dropped to 11.4%. The study concludes that a dedicated normalization module is more effective than retraining the base tagger on a small informal corpus, given the annotation cost involved. Frequency profiles of error-inducing token classes are provided as supplementary material.

title: A Lexicon of Informal Serbian Morphological Variants for NLP Applications
abstract: The paper presents the construction and evaluation of a manually curated lexicon mapping 8,740 informal orthographic variants of Serbian word forms to their standard dictionary entries, along with their morpho-syntactic tags. Source material was drawn from three online registers: sports commentary forums, food review portals, and classified advertisement listings. Variants were identified by comparing tokenised text against a pre-existing standard Serbian morphological dictionary and manually reviewing unmatched tokens. Each entry records the variant form, the canonical lemma, the tag, the source register, and a confidence score based on annotator agreement. An inter-annotator agreement of κ = 0.81 was achieved across two annotators for lemma assignment. The lexicon was released under a CC-BY licence and integrated as an optional module into the Serbian TreeTagger pipeline. Lookup precision on a held-out test set of 1,200 tokens reached 91.3%. The resource is intended to support downstream tasks such as sentiment analysis and named-entity recognition on informal Serbian text.

title: Dependency Parsing of Short Telegraphic Sentences in Serbian Classified Advertisements
abstract: Classified advertisement text in Serbian frequently omits function words, drops subjects, and uses non-standard punctuation, making dependency parsing with models trained on newspaper treebanks unreliable. This study collected 5,600 advertisement sentences from a domestic generalist listing platform across six product categories and parsed them using three publicly available dependency parsers trained on the Serbian UD treebank. Labelled attachment score (LAS) on the advertisement sentences averaged 61.4% across the three parsers, compared to 82.1% on a newspaper held-out set. The paper then reports on the manual annotation of 1,200 advertisement sentences as a supplementary treebank extension, with inter-annotator UAS of 0.87. Fine-tuning one parser on a 900/300 train-test split of these sentences raised LAS to 74.2%. Error analysis identified nominal predicate constructions and asyndetic listing as the primary sources of residual error. The annotated sentences are deposited with the CLARIN-SR repository.

title: Semantic Role Labelling in Serbian Warranty Claim Texts: A Corpus Study
abstract: This paper investigates the distribution of semantic roles in a corpus of 3,200 warranty claim descriptions submitted via an online form by customers of a domestic household appliance retailer. The texts are short (median 34 tokens), domain-restricted, and exhibit a characteristic predicate structure centred on malfunction verbs. A frame-semantic annotation scheme derived from FrameNet was applied, with 14 frames covering 88% of predicate occurrences in the corpus. Two annotators achieved κ = 0.79 on frame assignment. The annotated corpus was used to train a CRF-based semantic role labeller, which reached an F1 of 0.74 on a 20% held-out test set. The study identifies three recurring argument structures—DEVICE_MALFUNCTION, TEMPORAL_ONSET, and SYMPTOM_DESCRIPTION—that together account for 61% of all clause types. The paper argues that shallow semantic annotation is sufficient for downstream fault routing and priority scoring tasks in customer service contexts, and discusses annotation guidelines developed during the project.

title: Character-Level Models for Morphological Analysis of Dialectally Influenced Serbian Social Media Text
abstract: Serbian social media posts frequently incorporate lexical and phonological features associated with regional dialects, particularly Šumadija-Vojvodina and Zeta-South Serbian varieties, alongside standard Ekavian and Ijekavian forms. This study evaluates three character-level architectures—a character n-gram logistic regression baseline, a bidirectional LSTM, and a transformer trained from scratch on a 40 MB informal Serbian corpus—on a morphological analysis task over a manually annotated dataset of 6,800 tokens sampled from Twitter and Instagram. The transformer model achieved the highest lemmatisation accuracy at 89.1% and tag accuracy at 86.3%, outperforming the BiLSTM by 2.9 and 3.4 percentage points respectively. Performance gaps were largest for verb forms showing Ijekavian-Ekavian alternation and for clitic variants. The paper includes an ablation study showing that subword tokenisation tuned to Serbian morpheme boundaries improves accuracy by 1.7 points on the verb subset. Training data and evaluation scripts are made publicly available.

title: Annotation Consistency and Label Stability in Informal Serbian Corpora: A Study Across Four Annotation Rounds
abstract: Repeated annotation of the same informal Serbian corpus segments by different annotators over a four-year period provides an opportunity to measure how guidelines, annotator training, and tagset revisions affect label consistency. This paper reports on four annotation rounds applied to a fixed 2,400-token sample drawn from forum and review text, each round involving a different pair of annotators using an evolving version of the morpho-syntactic guidelines. Pairwise Cohen's κ ranged from 0.71 in round one to 0.86 in round four, with the largest gains in tagging of particles and discourse markers. Across rounds, 14.3% of tokens received different majority tags, with verb aspect marking and reflexive pronoun classification as the most variable categories. The paper proposes a calibration protocol for informal corpus annotation projects and provides a freely downloadable inter-annotator disagreement log for the 2,400-token sample. Findings are relevant for teams building training data for Serbian NLP systems.

title: Morpho-Syntactic Profiling of Serbian Technical Support Chat Logs
abstract: Technical support conversations conducted via text chat present a dense mixture of standard Serbian, informal register, and domain jargon. This study analyses a corpus of 9,200 anonymised chat exchanges between agents and customers of a domestic internet service provider, totalling approximately 310,000 tokens. Morpho-syntactic profiles were constructed by running a normalisation-augmented tagger pipeline on the corpus and computing per-speaker type-token ratios, lemma entropy, and syntactic complexity proxies based on dependency arc lengths. Customer messages show significantly higher lexical entropy (mean 4.31 bits) compared to agent messages (3.19 bits), while agent messages exhibit longer average dependency arcs (3.8 vs. 2.6 tokens), reflecting formulaic syntax. The paper then trains a binary message-type classifier achieving F1 of 0.96, and a five-way intent classifier (complaint, inquiry, confirmation, instruction, escalation request) reaching macro-F1 of 0.81. Error cases are traced to morpho-syntactic ambiguity in elliptical customer turns. Implications for automatic ticket routing are discussed.

title: Cross-Domain Transfer of Serbian Morpho-Syntactic Taggers: Automotive, Medical, and Legal Short Text
abstract: This paper systematically tests how well a tagger trained on one informal domain transfers to two other informal domains in Serbian, using three corpora of roughly equal size (circa 15,000 tokens each): automotive forum posts, anonymised patient complaint summaries, and excerpts from online legal advice forums. All three corpora were annotated in-house using the MULTEXT-East 6.0 Serbian tagset. Cross-domain experiments show that the automotive-to-legal transfer retains 91.2% of in-domain F1, while automotive-to-medical drops to 81.7%, mainly due to Latinate medical terminology and nominal compound constructions absent from automotive text. A simple domain adaptation step using 500 in-domain labelled sentences recovers 5.1 F1 points in the medical condition. The paper presents confusion matrices for the six morpho-syntactic categories most affected by domain shift and provides practical guidance on minimum in-domain annotation effort as a function of target domain vocabulary overlap. All three corpora are deposited with CLARIN-SR.

title: Lexical Borrowing Patterns and Morphological Integration of English Loanwords in Serbian Tech-Sector Short Messages
abstract: This study examines how English loanwords are morphologically integrated in Serbian short messages produced by employees and customers in the information technology sector. A corpus of 7,800 messages was collected from two sources: internal project management tool threads from three IT companies operating in Novi Sad (shared under a data agreement with pseudonymisation) and publicly available technology product review pages. From this corpus, 2,140 loanword tokens were identified and classified according to their degree of morphological integration: unadapted citation forms, partially adapted forms retaining English plural marking, and fully integrated forms inflected according to Serbian nominal or verbal morphology. Results show that 38% of loanword tokens appear in unadapted form, 29% in partial adaptation, and 33% fully integrated. Integration rate correlates significantly with word frequency (Spearman r = 0.62) and with the part of speech, with verbs showing higher integration than nouns. Findings are discussed in relation to contact linguistics and as practical guidance for building normalization rules for Serbian tech-domain NLP pipelines.

title: Stance and Engagement in Serbian Economics Research Articles: A Corpus-Based Study
abstract: Drawing on a corpus of 75 Serbian-language economics research articles published in nationally ranked journals between 2008 and 2015, this study investigates stance and engagement features as defined within an interpersonal metadiscourse framework. The analysis quantifies the frequency and distribution of attitude markers, hedges, boosters, self-mentions, and reader-address forms, and examines their syntactic and pragmatic contexts. Economics articles in the corpus show comparatively high booster density (mean 8.9 per 1,000 words) relative to the author's earlier findings for natural-science and humanities texts, a result interpreted in relation to the persuasive demands of policy-relevant scholarship. Self-mention is present in 68 per cent of articles, predominantly in methods and conclusions sections. The paper contributes to the growing body of corpus evidence on academic discourse in smaller European languages and discusses implications for English-medium publication by Serbian economists.

title: Transmission Chains and Textual Divergence in the Serbian Hagiographic Corpus of the Late Fourteenth Century
abstract: This book chapter contributes to a collected volume on Balkan medieval textual transmission. It reconstructs partial transmission chains for four closely related vitae circulating in Serbian monastic scriptoria between approximately 1370 and 1430, using a combination of stemmatic analysis and orthographic profiling. The chapter identifies a previously overlooked intermediary manuscript tradition linking the Morava valley scriptoria to Athonite copying centres, evidenced by a cluster of shared orthographic deviations affecting 23 lexical items across all four texts. Particular attention is given to the role of deliberate editorial emendation versus mechanical copying error in producing observed textual divergences. The analysis makes use of a purpose-built collation database holding diplomatic transcriptions of 11 manuscript witnesses. The chapter argues for a more cautious use of single shared errors as indicators of direct copying relationships in this corpus, given the evidence for parallel consultation of common source texts by multiple independent scribes.

title: A Weighted Scoring Model for Technology Readiness Assessment in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs: Pilot Application
abstract: This paper presents a weighted scoring model designed to quantify technology readiness levels (TRLs) in small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises participating in a regional innovation support scheme in Vojvodina. The model aggregates 14 indicators across four dimensions—technical maturity, manufacturing scalability, supply-chain integration, and regulatory compliance—using analytic hierarchy process (AHP) weights derived from expert elicitation with 22 industry and academic panellists. The instrument was piloted on a sample of 31 SME project applications submitted to a provincial innovation call in 2011. Scoring outcomes correlated strongly (Spearman ρ = 0.74) with post-project assessor ratings collected two years after project completion, suggesting predictive validity. The paper discusses calibration limitations arising from sector heterogeneity within the sample and proposes a stratified scoring variant for food-processing and metal-fabrication subsectors separately. A sensitivity analysis shows that weighting the manufacturing-scalability dimension above 0.35 significantly shifts ranking outcomes for early-stage projects.

title: Stage-Gate Portfolio Selection in Publicly Funded R&D: A Review of European Practice from 2000 to 2012
abstract: This review systematically examines stage-gate portfolio selection procedures applied across 18 publicly funded manufacturing R&D programmes in seven European countries between 2000 and 2012. Sources include programme documentation, published evaluations, and 14 structured interviews with programme managers conducted by correspondence. The analysis maps gate criteria, scoring rubrics, and decision authority arrangements used at pre-selection, full-application, and mid-term review gates. Findings show that technology readiness criteria appear explicitly in only 9 of the 18 programmes, despite broad policy rhetoric around TRL frameworks. Among programmes that use TRL criteria, definitions are inconsistent: four apply NASA-derived scales, three use European Commission adaptations, and two employ proprietary variants. The review identifies a pattern in which gate criteria proliferate over successive programme cycles without evidence-based pruning, leading to scoring instrument complexity that reviewers report as unmanageable. The paper proposes a minimum-criterion principle for gate design and tabulates a reference set of 28 criteria observed across programmes.

title: Consistency of TRL Self-Assessment by Project Teams: Evidence from a Serbian National Innovation Call
abstract: Self-reported TRL scores submitted by project teams in a 2013 Serbian national innovation call are compared with independent expert assessments of the same 67 proposals to measure inter-rater agreement and systematic bias. Cohen's kappa across all nine TRL levels was 0.38, indicating fair agreement; collapsing the scale into three bands (TRL 1–3, 4–6, 7–9) raised kappa to 0.61. Teams systematically over-reported readiness: mean self-assessed TRL was 4.9 versus expert mean of 4.1, a difference significant at p < 0.01. Over-reporting was more pronounced in proposals from teams with no prior funded project experience (n = 29, difference = 1.2 levels) than in teams with prior experience (n = 38, difference = 0.6 levels). A logistic regression model identifies three proposal-text features—use of quantified performance targets, attachment of prototype photographs, and citation of standards compliance testing—as significant negative predictors of over-reporting. Practical implications for call design include mandatory evidence-attachment requirements and calibration training for both applicants and reviewers.

title: Multi-Criteria Portfolio Optimisation for R&D Grant Allocation: A Linear Programming Approach Applied to a Vojvodina Manufacturing Programme
abstract: This paper applies a multi-criteria linear programming model to the problem of selecting a portfolio of R&D projects from 89 applications submitted to a 2015 Vojvodina provincial manufacturing innovation call with a total budget of approximately 4.2 million EUR. Criteria include expected TRL advancement, employment effect, sectoral strategic alignment, environmental impact, and absorption probability. Weights were assigned by a programme management committee using a structured workshop process documented here. The optimised portfolio, constrained to 22 projects and three subsidy-rate tiers, achieves a 14 % higher aggregate expected TRL advancement score than the historically funded portfolio selected by expert panel alone, while staying within budget and satisfying minimum-sector-representation constraints. Sensitivity analysis on weight perturbations of ±20 % shows that 17 of the 22 selected projects are robust across all tested weight combinations. The model is implemented in Python with a documented repository and was used in an advisory capacity alongside the expert panel for the subsequent 2017 call.

title: Gate Reviewer Calibration in R&D Programme Evaluation: A Field Experiment
abstract: Inconsistency among reviewers at selection gates is a known but under-studied problem in publicly funded R&D programmes. This paper reports a field experiment conducted during the 2019 application cycle of a Serbian national manufacturing innovation call, in which 24 reviewers assessed a set of 12 anchor proposals whose TRL and quality scores had been pre-determined by a consensus panel. Reviewers were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: no calibration, a 90-minute calibration workshop using worked examples, and the calibration workshop plus a structured scoring rubric. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) for TRL scores were 0.41, 0.63, and 0.78 in the three conditions respectively. Score variance on anchor proposals was reduced by 38 % in the full-treatment condition relative to control. Effects were larger for proposals at TRL 4–6 than at TRL 1–3 or TRL 7–9, suggesting that mid-range readiness levels are hardest to assess consistently without calibration support. The study provides empirical grounds for mandatory reviewer training in future programme calls.

title: TRL-Based Reporting Requirements in Horizon 2020 Manufacturing Grants: A Document Analysis
abstract: This paper analyses TRL reporting practices across 94 Horizon 2020 projects classified under the LEIT-NMBP (nanotechnologies, advanced materials, biotechnology, and advanced manufacturing and processing) theme, drawing on publicly available grant agreements, periodic reports, and final reports accessed through the European Commission's project repository. The analysis codes TRL reporting frequency, granularity, and consistency across project lifecycle documents. In 61 of 94 projects, TRL values in the final report differed from grant agreement targets by at least one level; in 23 cases, the reported TRL exceeded the contracted target without explanatory narrative. Only 38 projects provided quantitative evidence artefacts (test data, certification documents, or prototype assessments) to substantiate reported TRL values. The paper maps reporting quality against project size, consortium size, and coordinator country and finds that smaller consortia and projects coordinated by SMEs show lower reporting consistency. Implications for the design of TRL reporting templates in Horizon Europe successor programmes are discussed.

title: A Decision Support Tool for Stage-Gate Portfolio Management in Regional Manufacturing Innovation Programmes: Design and Validation
abstract: This paper describes the design, implementation, and validation of a decision support tool (DST) for stage-gate portfolio management in regional manufacturing innovation programmes, developed in collaboration with a Vojvodina provincial funding body. The DST integrates a TRL-MRL assessment module, a multi-criteria scoring engine, a budget-constrained portfolio optimisation module, and a reviewer calibration dashboard. It was validated through a retrospective simulation using data from three completed programme cycles (2015, 2017, 2019), totalling 237 project assessments. The simulated portfolio outcomes under DST-guided selection showed a 17 % improvement in aggregate post-project TRL attainment and an 11 % reduction in inter-reviewer score variance compared with historical panel outcomes. User acceptance testing with nine programme officers produced a system usability scale score of 71.4, classified as acceptable. The paper discusses design trade-offs between model transparency and scoring complexity, and describes the iterative simplification process that reduced the original instrument from 31 to 18 criteria across three design cycles.

title: Sector-Specific TRL Scales for Agri-Food Manufacturing: Derivation and Preliminary Testing
abstract: Standard nine-level TRL scales were derived from aerospace and defence contexts and require adaptation for agri-food manufacturing, where regulatory validation, food-safety certification, and seasonal production constraints create maturity milestones not captured by generic descriptors. This paper reports the derivation of a sector-specific TRL scale for agri-food manufacturing through a three-round Delphi study involving 34 experts (food technologists, manufacturing engineers, and R&D funding officers) from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. The resulting scale preserves the nine-level structure but redefines level descriptors at TRL 4, 5, and 6 to incorporate pilot-scale food-safety testing, regulatory submission, and industrial hygiene compliance. Preliminary testing on 19 agri-food R&D projects assessed under both the generic and sector-specific scales shows that the sector-specific scale redistributes 37 % of projects to lower levels, primarily at TRL 5 and 6, suggesting that generic scales systematically over-rate maturity in this sector. The scale is proposed as a candidate instrument for use in Serbia's forthcoming agri-food innovation programme.

title: Cyclic shift schedule generation under Serbian Labour Law: a constraint programming approach
abstract: Serbian Labour Law imposes mandatory rest periods, weekly hour caps, and restrictions on consecutive night shifts that complicate the direct application of standard scheduling models. This paper formulates the problem as a constraint satisfaction programme and implements it in ILOG CP Optimizer. Test instances were constructed from anonymised rosters of three food-processing plants in Vojvodina, each employing between 120 and 340 workers across three production lines. Feasibility was achieved for all 27 benchmark instances within 300 seconds of CPU time. The resulting schedules reduced average overtime hours by 14 percent compared to manually designed rosters used by the same plants. The paper also identifies four constraint classes whose interaction most severely limits the feasible region, providing guidance for practitioners who negotiate collective agreements with trade unions. Sensitivity of schedule cost to the length of the planning horizon is discussed for horizons of 4, 8, and 13 weeks.

title: Mean-field variational inference for hidden Markov models with Dirichlet priors
abstract: Hidden Markov models with Dirichlet-distributed transition priors are widely used for sequential data but exact posterior inference is intractable for large state spaces. This paper develops a mean-field variational Bayes algorithm in which the variational distribution over transition matrices, emission parameters, and hidden states is updated in closed form using coordinate ascent. The algorithm is evaluated on three synthetic datasets with state spaces of size 8, 16, and 32, and on a real electromyographic signal corpus comprising 47 subjects and roughly 120,000 time steps per recording. Convergence diagnostics show that the evidence lower bound stabilises within 40–80 iterations for all tested configurations. Posterior estimates of the number of active states recover ground truth within ±1 state in 91% of synthetic trials. Runtime scales approximately linearly with sequence length, outperforming a collapsed Gibbs sampler by a factor of 6–12 on sequences longer than 50,000 steps. The method is compared against expectation propagation on the same data, with variational inference performing comparably in accuracy while requiring 3× less computation per iteration.

title: Expectation propagation for Gaussian mixture models: convergence properties and failure modes
abstract: Expectation propagation (EP) is an approximate inference scheme that iteratively matches moments of cavity distributions, but its convergence behaviour on multimodal posteriors is poorly understood. This paper provides a systematic empirical study of EP applied to Gaussian mixture models with 2 to 20 components, varying the degree of component overlap, dimensionality from 2 to 50, and the number of observations from 200 to 20,000. Convergence is assessed using fixed-point residuals and compared against the known analytic marginals for a set of low-dimensional test cases. Results show that EP fails to converge in approximately 34% of trials when component separation falls below 1.5 standard deviations in Euclidean distance. A damping scheme with step sizes chosen by line search reduces the failure rate to 11% at the cost of a 2.4× increase in iterations. The paper also characterises conditions under which EP and mean-field variational Bayes agree to within 2% in marginal variance estimates. All experiments are conducted on synthetic data with controlled ground truth.

title: Structured variational inference for Ising models on sparse graphs
abstract: The Ising model is a canonical pairwise Markov random field whose partition function is #P-hard to compute exactly. This work investigates structured mean-field and structured variational approximations that exploit the sparsity of the factor graph. Sparse graphs with average degree between 3 and 8 are generated using the Erdős–Rényi and Barabási–Albert procedures, with graph sizes ranging from 100 to 10,000 nodes. The structured mean-field factorisation respects clusters identified by a greedy graph decomposition, yielding cluster-level updates solved exactly using belief propagation within each cluster. Approximation quality is measured by KL divergence to the exact posterior obtained by brute force for graphs up to 22 nodes. For larger graphs, samples from parallel tempering serve as the reference. Structured factorisation reduces the KL divergence by 38–61% relative to naive mean-field across the tested graph families. Computational cost grows quadratically in cluster size but remains tractable for clusters up to 12 nodes.

title: Stochastic variational inference with control variates for large-scale topic models
abstract: Stochastic variational inference (SVI) replaces full data gradients of the evidence lower bound with noisy mini-batch estimates, enabling inference on corpora too large for batch updates. Variance in the gradient estimator is a principal obstacle to fast convergence. This paper evaluates three families of control variates — baseline subtraction, Rao–Blackwellisation, and leave-one-out estimators — within SVI for latent Dirichlet allocation with 50 to 400 topics. Experiments use a corpus of 1.2 million news articles totalling 480 million tokens. Mini-batches of size 128, 512, and 2048 are compared. Control variates reduce gradient variance by one to two orders of magnitude depending on mini-batch size, translating into 1.8–3.1× faster convergence in terms of wall-clock time to reach a target held-out perplexity. The leave-one-out estimator performs best for small mini-batches, while Rao–Blackwellisation is more effective at larger batch sizes. The method is also tested on a Serbian-language web corpus of 280,000 documents.

title: Amortised variational inference using recognition networks: a comparison of encoder architectures
abstract: Amortised variational inference replaces per-datapoint optimisation of variational parameters with a learned recognition network that maps observations to approximate posterior parameters. This study benchmarks five encoder architectures — multilayer perceptrons with 1–4 hidden layers, convolutional networks, residual networks, attention-based encoders, and bidirectional LSTMs — within a variational autoencoder framework. Experiments are conducted on image data (28×28 binary MNIST, 64×64 grayscale face images from a custom dataset of 38,000 samples) and on multivariate time series (a collection of 22,000 industrial vibration records sampled at 1 kHz). Metrics include evidence lower bound, reconstruction fidelity measured by mean squared error and structural similarity index, and posterior calibration assessed by coverage of 95% credible intervals on held-out data. Residual encoders achieve the highest ELBO on image data, while bidirectional LSTMs dominate on time-series inputs. Deeper encoders improve reconstruction but degrade posterior calibration in 6 of 10 settings tested.

title: Variational inference methods for Bayesian neural networks: an empirical survey
abstract: Bayesian neural networks quantify predictive uncertainty by placing priors over weights and performing approximate posterior inference. This chapter surveys variational inference methods applied to neural networks, covering mean-field Gaussian approximations, matrix-variate Gaussian priors, and implicit variational families. The treatment is deliberately empirical: each method is evaluated on four regression benchmarks (Boston housing, Concrete, Energy, and Kin8nm), two classification datasets (MNIST and a proprietary industrial fault dataset with 14 classes and 65,000 samples), and one out-of-distribution detection task. Results are reported for network sizes ranging from 1 hidden layer with 50 units to 5 layers with 512 units. The chapter provides worked derivations of the ELBO for each approximation family and discusses the computational overhead relative to maximum a posteriori estimation. Local reparameterisation tricks reduce mini-batch gradient variance by 1.5–4× depending on layer width. The chapter concludes with a discussion of pathologies including posterior collapse and weight symmetry.

title: Planar normalising flows for posterior approximation in hierarchical Bayesian models
abstract: Normalising flows construct flexible approximate posterior distributions by composing simple invertible transformations. Planar flows add a rank-one perturbation to the identity map at each layer, preserving tractable Jacobian determinants. This paper investigates planar flows as variational families for hierarchical Bayesian models with up to four levels of latent variables, including Bayesian linear mixed-effects models and nested Gaussian process models. Experiments use simulated data for which exact marginal likelihoods are available via numerical integration and three real ecological datasets with between 300 and 12,000 observations. Flow depth is varied from 4 to 32 layers. A 16-layer planar flow reduces the KL gap relative to the true posterior by 47–68% compared to a mean-field Gaussian baseline across all tested models. The improvement is most pronounced in the presence of posterior correlations induced by group-level random effects. Runtime overhead of the flow relative to mean-field inference scales linearly in flow depth and is less than 2× for all configurations tested.

title: Coupling-layer normalising flows for Bayesian inference in large Gaussian graphical models
abstract: Gaussian graphical models encode conditional independence through zero entries in the precision matrix, but posterior inference over the precision matrix in high dimensions is computationally demanding. This paper proposes using coupling-layer normalising flows — specifically RealNVP-style affine coupling blocks — as the variational family for the precision matrix posterior in graphs with up to 500 nodes. The flow is parameterised to respect the positive-definiteness constraint via a Cholesky decomposition of the flow output. Training minimises the evidence lower bound using the reparameterisation gradient. Experiments are performed on synthetic graphs with known sparsity patterns (Erdős–Rényi, scale-free, and block-diagonal) and on a gene co-expression dataset comprising 412 nodes and 280 samples. Graph structure recovery is measured by precision, recall, and F1 score on edges. The flow-based approximation recovers the true edge set with F1 scores 0.12–0.19 higher than a Laplace approximation baseline and 0.07–0.14 higher than a mean-field Gaussian baseline on the synthetic benchmarks.

title: Approximate inference for Bayesian change-point models using stochastic variational Bayes
abstract: Change-point models detect structural breaks in time series and are used in industrial monitoring, econometrics, and environmental sensing. Exact Bayesian inference in these models requires summing over an exponential number of segmentations. This paper derives a stochastic variational Bayes algorithm for a class of Bayesian change-point models with Gaussian segment likelihoods and geometric prior on segment duration. The variational distribution factorises over segment assignments and segment parameters. Gradients of the ELBO are estimated using mini-batches of time windows rather than full sequences, enabling application to streams. The algorithm is evaluated on three univariate synthetic series of length 50,000 with known change-point locations and on a multivariate industrial vibration dataset from a manufacturing process with 18 sensors and 14 months of 10 Hz recordings, totalling approximately 36 million samples. Detection latency and false-alarm rate are compared against an offline MCMC reference. The variational algorithm achieves mean detection latency of 4.3 samples versus 3.1 for MCMC, with false-alarm rate within 0.8 percentage points.

title: Scalable posterior inference for dynamic Bayesian networks using autoregressive normalising flows
abstract: Dynamic Bayesian networks (DBNs) model temporal dependencies among variables and are used in fault diagnosis, process monitoring, and biomedical applications. Exact inference in DBNs is exponential in the number of parents per node. This paper adapts autoregressive normalising flows — specifically masked autoregressive flows (MAF) — as variational families for the joint posterior over DBN parameters and hidden states in networks with up to 80 nodes and 5 time lags. The ELBO is optimised using Adam with a cosine learning-rate schedule. Experiments compare the flow-based approximation against a mean-field baseline and a sequential Monte Carlo reference on four synthetic networks and one real-world dataset: a 45-variable process monitoring dataset from a Serbian chemical production facility, spanning 6 months at 1-minute resolution. Structure learning accuracy is reported using structural Hamming distance. MAF-based inference reduces structural Hamming distance by 22% relative to mean-field and is within 8% of the SMC reference while being 15× faster.

title: Posterior predictive checks for normalising flow variational approximations
abstract: Posterior predictive checks (PPCs) assess model fit by comparing observed data statistics to the distribution of statistics simulated from the posterior predictive. When the posterior is approximated by a normalising flow, the approximation error introduces a bias in PPC p-values that has not been systematically studied. This paper characterises this bias for five normalising flow families — planar, radial, RealNVP, MAF, and neural spline flows — applied to eight statistical models drawn from the Stan model library, including regression, mixture, and hierarchical models. Bias in p-values is measured against reference p-values from Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with 20,000 samples. Results show that neural spline flows reduce PPC p-value bias to below 0.03 in absolute terms for six of eight models, while planar and radial flows produce biases exceeding 0.10 in models with strong posterior correlations. The paper also proposes a simple bootstrap correction that reduces residual bias by 40–70% at negligible computational cost.
venue: Bayesian Analysis

title: Failure Rate Data Sources for Automotive FMEA: A Comparative Study of MIL-HDBK-217F, IEC TR 62380, and SN 29500
abstract: Quantitative FMEA requires reliable component failure rate data, yet the three most commonly cited handbooks—MIL-HDBK-217F, IEC TR 62380, and SN 29500—frequently yield divergent estimates for the same component under identical operating conditions. This study applies all three sources to a common set of 47 automotive electronic components drawn from a representative powertrain ECU bill of materials and compares predicted failure rates, failure mode distributions, and the resulting safe failure fraction values. Across the component set, failure rates differ by up to a factor of 8.3 between the most and least conservative source. The impact on SFF and, consequently, on achievable ASIL classification is quantified: switching from SN 29500 to MIL-HDBK-217F for passive components shifts the system-level SFF by 4.1 percentage points in the examined design. Recommendations are provided for source selection in ISO 26262-compliant projects, with preference criteria tied to component category and operating environment.

title: Encoding Motion Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Industrial Robot Programs
abstract: Motion primitives are low-level, parameterised movement segments such as linear approach, arc weld, or joint-space transit. This study describes a library of 22 such primitives, each specified by a typed parameter schema, precondition predicates, and postcondition predicates expressed in a first-order logic subset. The library was constructed by analysing 130 robot programs from three automotive subassembly lines provided by a regional manufacturing partner. Primitive reuse was measured by counting the number of programs that could be fully reconstructed by composition of library entries without modification. Coverage reached 91 percent of programs after the library stabilised at iteration four of an incremental extraction process. Execution traces on a UR5e cobot confirmed that synthesised programs match manually written reference programs in cycle time within 2.1 percent on average across eight test tasks. The paper also reports on a small user study with five engineers who used the library to program two new tasks each, completing them on average 28 percent faster than with the standard teach-pendant method.

title: Coordinated VNF Placement and Traffic Engineering in Hierarchical SD-WAN Controllers
abstract: Hierarchical SD-WAN controller architectures separate global traffic engineering from local VNF placement, creating misalignment between the two optimisation layers. This paper proposes a coordination protocol, called placement-aware TE (PATE), in which the local controller exposes VNF resource shadows to the global controller and receives soft traffic-engineering hints in return. The protocol is specified formally and implemented inside a two-tier ONOS-based controller hierarchy. Experiments on a 60-node emulated topology with 12 active service function chains show that PATE reduces mean chain end-to-end latency by 19% and resource fragmentation by 24% compared to uncoordinated operation, at the cost of 6% higher inter-controller message volume. The paper analyses convergence time under burst traffic and discusses failure scenarios where PATE degrades gracefully to independent operation. Implementation artefacts are available on a public repository.

title: A Benchmark Corpus of Cross-Platform Desktop Applications for GUI Testing Research
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of GUI testing tools is hindered by the lack of shared, versioned application corpora with documented ground-truth state models. This paper presents DesktopBench-40, a curated collection of 40 open-source desktop applications available for Windows and Linux, spanning document editors, media players, archive managers, and configuration utilities. Each application entry includes three successive release versions, a manually verified FSM ground-truth, a set of known regression faults seeded across releases, and accessibility metadata extracted according to EN 301 549. The corpus is distributed with a reproducible build system and a lightweight test harness. Baseline measurements using four publicly available GUI exploration tools are reported, covering state discovery rate, fault detection rate, and runtime. DesktopBench-40 is intended to serve as a common evaluation platform for researchers working on model inference, test generation, and accessibility auditing for desktop software.

title: Extraction of Cauer Thermal Network Parameters for High-Power IGBT Modules Using Thermal Transient Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a measurement-based procedure for extracting Foster-to-Cauer converted thermal network parameters for 1200 V / 300 A IGBT half-bridge modules intended for traction applications. Thermal transient responses were recorded using a TERANOVA T450 thermal analyser over a junction-to-case temperature range of 25 °C to 150 °C. The measured Zth(j-c) curves were fitted to a four-stage Cauer RC ladder using a least-squares optimisation routine implemented in MATLAB. Parameters were extracted for three module samples from the same production batch, and batch-to-batch parameter spread was quantified. Maximum deviation in steady-state thermal resistance among samples was 4.1 %. The resulting Cauer models were validated against independent step-power experiments and showed root-mean-square errors below 0.9 K. The work provides a reproducible characterisation workflow applicable to module qualification procedures in railway rolling-stock development.

title: Influence of Duty-Cycle Asymmetry on Junction-Temperature Swing in Three-Phase Traction Inverters
abstract: Asymmetric motor loading during acceleration and braking phases produces unequal duty cycles across the six switch positions of a traction inverter, resulting in non-uniform junction-temperature swings among IGBT chips. This study quantifies those differences using an electrothermal simulation framework coupling a SPICE-based inverter model with Cauer thermal networks parameterised from measurements on 650 A / 1700 V modules. A representative urban rail acceleration profile with twelve start-stop cycles per hour was used as the input load pattern. Simulations show that the inner switch pair experiences ΔTj values up to 22 K higher than the outer pairs under full motor torque. Sensitivity analysis was performed by varying carrier frequency from 2 kHz to 4 kHz and DC-link voltage from 750 V to 1500 V. The results suggest that adaptive carrier-frequency reduction during peak loading can reduce worst-case ΔTj by approximately 14 % without significant harmonic penalty.

title: Power-Cycling Lifetime Estimation for IGBT Modules Using a Modified Coffin–Manson Model Calibrated Against Accelerated Test Data
abstract: Lifetime prediction models for IGBT solder-layer fatigue typically rely on Coffin–Manson or Norris–Landzberg equations calibrated from accelerated power-cycling tests. This paper reports accelerated cycling tests conducted on twelve 600 A / 1200 V half-bridge modules using controlled I²t pulses producing ΔTj values between 40 K and 100 K with mean junction temperatures Tjm of 80 °C and 100 °C. Failure was defined as a 20 % increase in Vce(sat) or thermal resistance. Cycle counts to failure ranged from 9 200 at ΔTj = 100 K to over 480 000 at ΔTj = 40 K. The Coffin–Manson exponent was determined to be 5.8, somewhat higher than values reported in older literature for similar module structures. An Arrhenius correction for mean temperature was included. The calibrated model was applied to a representative suburban rail duty cycle, predicting a B10 lifetime of approximately 11.4 years under that profile.

title: Bond Wire Lift-Off Detection in IGBT Modules by On-State Voltage Monitoring Under Controlled Gate Drive Conditions
abstract: Bond wire lift-off is among the primary wearout mechanisms in wire-bonded IGBT modules and manifests as a gradual rise in collector-emitter on-state voltage Vce(sat). This paper investigates the sensitivity of Vce(sat) monitoring as a condition indicator using twelve modules subjected to accelerated power cycling from ΔTj = 60 K. Vce(sat) was sampled at a fixed gate-source voltage and current of 15 V and 100 A respectively, using a purpose-built measurement circuit with sub-millivolt resolution. Results show a statistically consistent Vce(sat) increase of 8–12 mV per 10 % bond wire cross-section loss, estimated by post-mortem decapsulation and optical inspection. Temperature-induced Vce(sat) drift was compensated using a second-order polynomial correction derived from characterisation at multiple temperatures. The proposed threshold criterion of +40 mV relative to initial value provides advance warning approximately 7 % of remaining lifetime before catastrophic failure under the tested conditions.

title: Thermal Modelling of Multi-Chip IGBT Modules Including Lateral Heat Spreading in the Copper Baseplate
abstract: Standard one-dimensional thermal network models neglect lateral heat conduction within the copper baseplate, which can become significant when multiple dies operate simultaneously at different power levels. This work develops a two-dimensional finite-difference thermal model for a six-chip 1200 V / 450 A IGBT module and compares predictions against infrared thermography measurements taken under asymmetric loading. The module was mounted on a water-cooled cold plate maintained at 40 °C. Die-level surface temperatures measured by IR camera at 30 Hz frame rate were used as ground truth. The 2D model reduced peak die temperature prediction error from 8.3 K (1D model) to 2.1 K. Parameter sensitivity showed that baseplate thermal conductivity variation of ±10 % produced die temperature changes up to 3.8 K under full-load asymmetric conditions. The model is implemented as a compact descriptor suitable for real-time embedding in inverter control hardware.

title: Effect of Solder Layer Voiding on Thermal Resistance and Lifetime of IGBT Power Modules: A Combined X-Ray and Power-Cycling Study
abstract: Voiding in the die-attach solder layer increases thermal resistance and accelerates fatigue crack propagation, but the quantitative relationship between void fraction, thermal resistance increase, and cycling lifetime has not been thoroughly established for modern Sn-Ag-Cu solders. This study characterised eighteen 600 A / 1200 V IGBT modules by X-ray computed tomography before power-cycling tests, measuring void fractions ranging from 1.8 % to 17.4 % of die-attach area. Steady-state thermal resistance Rth(j-c) correlated with void fraction with a Pearson coefficient of 0.81. Power cycling at ΔTj = 70 K showed that modules with void fractions above 10 % reached the 20 % Rth increase failure criterion in 62 % fewer cycles than those below 5 %. Post-cycling CT scans revealed preferential crack initiation at void boundaries. The data support an empirical correction factor applied to the baseline Coffin–Manson model to account for initial voiding state.

title: Real-Time Junction Temperature Estimation for Traction IGBT Modules Using a Reduced-Order Thermal Observer
abstract: Direct junction temperature measurement is impractical in operating inverters; observer-based estimation from accessible signals offers a practical alternative. This paper presents a reduced-order Luenberger-type thermal observer implemented on a field-programmable gate array running at 10 kHz, estimating junction temperature from measured collector current and DC-link voltage. The observer state matrix is derived from a three-stage Cauer thermal model of the module. Observer gain was designed to achieve a settling time below 5 ms for step power changes. Validation was performed on a 110 kW laboratory inverter driving an induction motor through an urban acceleration profile; estimated junction temperature was compared against reference values obtained from a calibrated temperature-sensitive electrical parameter measurement. Root-mean-square estimation error was 1.7 K over a 40-minute test sequence with peak ΔTj of approximately 55 K. The implementation requires 2 100 logic elements on the target FPGA device.

title: Thermal Modelling of IGBT Power Modules in Railway Applications
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of thermal modelling approaches for IGBT power modules deployed in railway traction inverters, covering one-dimensional RC network models, compact multi-port thermal models, and the boundary conditions appropriate for vehicle-mounted cooling systems. The chapter discusses how load profile characteristics specific to urban, suburban, and mainline rail services translate into distinct thermal cycling regimes and how these regimes affect solder-layer and bond-wire lifetime. Parameter extraction from thermal transient measurements is described step by step, and worked numerical examples using a 1200 V / 600 A half-bridge module are included. Interactions between thermal model fidelity and lifetime prediction accuracy are analysed quantitatively. The chapter is aimed at practising engineers in railway rolling-stock development who need to select or validate thermal models without access to specialised simulation tools.

title: Influence of Coolant Temperature Variation on IGBT Junction Temperature and Predicted Lifetime in a Locomotive Traction Inverter
abstract: Coolant inlet temperature to the inverter heatsink varies substantially along a locomotive's route as a function of ambient temperature and auxiliary load. Standard lifetime calculations assume a fixed coolant temperature, introducing uncertainty in predicted cycle counts. This study integrates a measured coolant temperature profile from a 175 km freight rail route, recorded over 30 representative operating days in different seasons, into an electrothermal simulation of a 3 MW locomotive inverter. Coolant temperature ranged from 18 °C to 71 °C over the dataset. Results show that ΔTj is relatively insensitive to coolant temperature changes during motoring, where device self-heating dominates, but Tjm shifts considerably, influencing the Arrhenius lifetime term. Accounting for seasonal coolant variation reduced predicted B10 lifetime by 9 % compared to the fixed-temperature baseline. A simplified correction lookup table is derived for use in inverter design without full electrothermal simulation.

title: Condition Monitoring of Traction IGBT Modules Using Periodic Off-State Gate Charge Measurement
abstract: Mechanical stress from repeated thermal cycling causes delamination at the chip-substrate interface, which modifies the parasitic capacitances of the device and alters the gate charge characteristic. This paper investigates gate charge Qg as a non-invasive degradation indicator. Gate charge was measured periodically at controlled conditions (VGE sweep from −15 V to +15 V, VCE = 600 V) on 24 modules undergoing power cycling at ΔTj = 65 K and ΔTj = 85 K. Statistical process control charts were applied to the plateau region of the gate charge curve. Modules cycled at ΔTj = 85 K showed a detectable 3.2 % increase in Qg plateau length at approximately 65 % of their median lifetime, providing an early warning margin. No significant Qg change was observed for ΔTj = 65 K until within 5 % of end-of-life. The method requires only standard gate driver circuitry with modest measurement additions.

title: Comparative Assessment of Sn-Ag-Cu and Sintered Silver Die-Attach Materials for Power-Cycling Reliability in Traction IGBT Modules
abstract: Sintered silver die-attach has been proposed as a replacement for conventional SAC solder in high-reliability power modules, offering higher thermal conductivity and melting point. This work compares the power-cycling behaviour of identically packaged 1200 V / 200 A IGBT dies assembled with SAC305 solder and sintered Ag paste, using a force-pressure sintering process at 25 MPa. Both assembly types were subjected to power cycling at ΔTj = 60 K and ΔTj = 80 K. Cross-sections at defined cycle milestones were examined by scanning electron microscopy to track crack growth. Sintered Ag assemblies showed no measurable crack initiation at ΔTj = 60 K after 350 000 cycles, compared with the SAC305 samples reaching the 20 % Rth failure criterion at a median of 198 000 cycles under the same conditions. At ΔTj = 80 K, sintered Ag median lifetime was 2.4 times longer than SAC305. Initial thermal resistance was 6 % lower for sintered Ag assemblies.
