title: Modelling conducted emissions from LED drivers: comparison of behavioural and circuit-level approaches
abstract: Two modelling strategies for predicting conducted emissions from LED retrofit lamp drivers are compared: a behavioural model based on measured Thevenin equivalent source impedance and voltage, and a circuit-level model derived from the reverse-engineered schematic of three driver types with rated power of 7 W, 12 W and 18 W. Both models are embedded in a low-voltage network simulation and evaluated against LISN measurements over 150 kHz to 30 MHz. The behavioural approach reproduces measured emission profiles with an average RMS error of 3.1 dB but requires individual characterisation of each unit. The circuit-level model achieves 4.7 dB average error without unit-specific measurement but is sensitive to uncertainty in parasitic component values. A hybrid procedure combining measured impedance data with a simplified circuit skeleton reduces average error to 2.6 dB. The study covers 15 driver samples from four unnamed market sources. Implications for aggregated emission prediction when large numbers of LED luminaires are installed on a single feeder are discussed, with a Monte Carlo analysis of 50 to 500 simultaneous loads.

title: Photovoltaic system modelling under non-uniform irradiance: methods, applications, and open challenges
abstract: This book chapter surveys modelling frameworks for photovoltaic systems operating under non-uniform irradiance, covering cell-level, module-level, and string-level representations. The chapter opens with a discussion of the physical origins of irradiance non-uniformity—moving cloud shadows, architectural shading, soiling gradients, and inter-row shading in ground-mounted arrays—and explains why uniform-irradiance assumptions embedded in standard design tools underestimate mismatch losses. It then categorises modelling approaches from analytical diode-equation methods to look-up-table and neural-network surrogates, comparing their accuracy and computational cost. A section on bypass diode behaviour describes the multi-peak power–voltage characteristic and its dependence on bypass diode threshold voltage. The chapter closes with a discussion of open challenges: validation under transient cloud shadow events, integration of high-resolution numerical weather prediction data, and the lack of standardised partial-shading test protocols. It is intended for engineers designing MPPT algorithms and for researchers entering the field.

title: Calorimetric power-loss measurement bench for hard-switched converters up to 1 MHz: design and uncertainty analysis
abstract: Electrical power-loss integration at high switching frequencies suffers from bandwidth and time-alignment errors that can exceed 15 % at 500 kHz. This paper describes a differential calorimetric bench designed to measure total converter losses from 0.5 W to 50 W with an uncertainty of ±0.4 % at a 95 % confidence level. The bench uses two matched aluminium enclosures, Peltier coolers for temperature stabilisation, and PT100 sensors with 0.1 °C resolution. Thermal time constant of the measurement cell is 480 s, and the minimum resolvable loss change is 0.15 W. Cross-validation against a precision resistor reference load showed systematic offset below 0.2 %. The bench was applied to a 400 V / 48 V, 300 W, 650 kHz LLC converter using GaN HEMTs, yielding total losses of 4.3 W ± 0.02 W. Detailed uncertainty budgets for each error source are tabulated and a Python post-processing script is provided as supplementary material.

title: Degradation-Aware Sizing of Hybrid Energy Storage for Agricultural Pumping Stations
abstract: Agricultural irrigation pumping stations in flat terrain exhibit highly repetitive duty cycles characterised by frequent motor starts and stops, creating peak currents that accelerate battery ageing. This work incorporates a semi-empirical capacity-fade model calibrated on LiFePO4 cells cycled under controlled conditions in the authors' laboratory into an optimal sizing routine for a supercapacitor–battery hybrid. The ageing model accounts for both calendar ageing and cycle ageing as functions of C-rate, depth of discharge, and temperature, with parameters identified from 180-day accelerated ageing tests at 35 °C and 45 °C. Field load measurements from two pumping stations in the Vojvodina plain over one irrigation season provided the mission profile. Including degradation in the objective function shifts the optimal supercapacitor-to-battery energy ratio from 1:28 to 1:19 compared with a cost-only optimisation, and projected battery service life increases from 4.1 to 6.3 years. The economic break-even analysis indicates a payback period of 2.8 years at 2022 component prices.

title: Identifying Stack Buffer Overflows in MIPS Router Firmware Through Bounded Symbolic Execution
abstract: This paper addresses automated detection of stack buffer overflows in MIPS-based router firmware images obtained without access to source code. We lift binary code to an intermediate representation using a custom lifter built on top of the Valgrind VEX framework and apply bounded symbolic execution with a path depth limit of 400 basic blocks. Concolic inputs are seeded from reconstructed network packet headers. We evaluated the approach on a corpus of 38 firmware images from four consumer router product families, totalling approximately 12 million binary instructions after unpacking. The analysis identified 23 previously unreported overflow sites, of which 14 were confirmed exploitable by manual review. Path explosion was mitigated using loop summarisation and a context-sensitive function merging strategy. False positive rate on a set of known-safe library functions was 6.2 percent. Runtime per image averaged 4.1 hours on a 16-core workstation. The results suggest that bounded symbolic execution is viable for lightweight triage of router firmware without vendor cooperation.

title: Taint Propagation Across Shared Memory Regions in Multi-Process Embedded Firmware
abstract: Many network-attached embedded devices implement their control logic as a collection of cooperating processes that share data through POSIX shared memory or memory-mapped files. Standard dynamic taint analysis tools designed for single-process targets lose taint when data crosses process boundaries, producing high false negative rates. We extended the DECAF dynamic binary instrumentation framework to track taint through shared memory regions, anonymous pipes, and Unix domain sockets simultaneously. The modified framework was validated on three synthetic multi-process test cases with ground-truth taint flows, achieving 97 percent recall and 91 percent precision. We then applied the tool to six firmware images from industrial serial-to-Ethernet gateways, finding five cross-process injection vectors that single-process analysis missed entirely. The overhead of cross-process taint bookkeeping added approximately 34 percent to analysis wall-clock time compared to baseline DECAF. Instrumentation is implemented as a loadable plugin and does not require recompilation of the target firmware.

title: Firmware Re-Hosting Without Hardware: Accuracy and Limitations of Full-System QEMU Emulation for Taint Analysis of ARM Cortex-A Devices
abstract: Re-hosting firmware in software emulation is a prerequisite for applying dynamic analysis tools to devices for which physical hardware is scarce or inaccessible. We conducted a systematic study of QEMU full-system emulation accuracy for 29 ARM Cortex-A firmware images spanning five device categories: home routers, IP cameras, NAS units, VoIP adapters, and industrial Modbus gateways. For each image we compared behaviour during emulation against identical inputs on physical hardware across three metrics: network response correctness, filesystem state after operation, and taint flow completeness as measured by a reference taint analysis. Emulation was fully accurate for 17 images, partially accurate for 9, and failed to boot for 3. Peripheral emulation gaps were the dominant source of divergence, accounting for 74 percent of observed differences. We propose a lightweight peripheral stub library, PeriphStub, which resolves the most common MMIO read timeouts using heuristic default responses, improving full-boot success to 24 of 29 images. The results provide concrete guidance on when re-hosting is sufficient for security analysis purposes.

title: Automated Discovery of Command-Injection Vulnerabilities in Web Interfaces of Embedded Devices Using Combined Symbolic and Concolic Execution
abstract: Embedded devices frequently expose administrative web interfaces whose CGI scripts pass user-supplied strings directly to shell commands. We describe a pipeline that automatically identifies such command-injection sinks. The pipeline unpacks a firmware squashfs image, identifies CGI binaries, lifts them to LLVM IR using McSema, and then applies a concolic executor seeded with HTTP request templates derived from static analysis of the web server configuration files. Taint labels are assigned to HTTP parameters at the point of recv or read system calls, and a sink oracle flags any tainted argument reaching execve, system, or popen. Evaluated on 51 firmware images from consumer and small-business routers, the pipeline found 31 exploitable command-injection paths across 18 devices. Eight of these were in CGI scripts that prior static analysis alone had classified as safe. The entire pipeline runs without analyst interaction and produces a ranked report with concrete HTTP proof-of-concept payloads. Average analysis time per device was 2.8 hours.

title: Binary Analysis Methods for Embedded System Security: A Survey of Techniques Applied to Network-Attached Devices
abstract: This chapter surveys static and dynamic binary analysis techniques as applied specifically to firmware of network-attached embedded devices, a class of targets that differs from conventional desktop software in architecture diversity, operating system variation, hardware dependency, and the absence of debug symbols. We organise the survey around four analysis primitives: disassembly and control-flow recovery, symbolic and concolic execution, dynamic taint tracking, and fuzzing. For each primitive we describe the core mechanism, list representative tools, and summarise results from published evaluations on real firmware corpora. We give particular attention to practical obstacles—path explosion, peripheral emulation gaps, multi-architecture support, and filesystem unpacking—and catalogue workarounds reported in the literature. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems including partial firmware images, encrypted storage partitions, and the challenge of ground-truth evaluation. Intended for graduate students and practitioners entering the field, the chapter cites 84 primary sources published between 2008 and 2022.

title: Evaluating Constraint Solver Backends for Symbolic Execution of ARM Thumb-2 Firmware: Speed, Completeness, and Path Coverage
abstract: The choice of SMT solver backend has a substantial effect on the throughput of symbolic execution for binary targets, yet comparative studies specific to embedded firmware are scarce. We implemented a harness that feeds identical symbolic execution workloads, derived from ten ARM Thumb-2 firmware images of industrial sensors, to four SMT solver backends: Z3, Bitwuzla, CVC5, and Yices2. Metrics collected were queries per second, unsatisfiable-core generation time, path coverage at fixed 30-minute timeout, and rate of spurious unsatisfiable results on manually verified satisfiable path conditions. Bitwuzla achieved the highest queries-per-second rate (mean 1 840 q/s versus 1 210 q/s for Z3) and the highest path coverage on six of ten images. CVC5 produced fewer spurious unsatisfiable results (0.8 percent versus 2.1 percent for Bitwuzla). We provide a recommendation matrix mapping firmware characteristics to preferred solver. All benchmark scripts and firmware images redacted of proprietary content are released under an open licence.

title: A Taint-Guided Fuzzer for Discovering Memory Corruption in UPnP Service Handlers of Embedded Devices
abstract: UPnP service handlers in embedded devices parse complex XML-encoded SOAP messages and are historically prone to memory corruption. We present TaintFuzz, a grey-box fuzzer that uses dynamic taint analysis to identify which bytes of a UPnP SOAP request influence memory allocation sizes and buffer copy lengths inside the service handler binary. Taint-labelled byte offsets are fed back to the mutation engine as high-priority mutation targets, focusing energy on inputs that reach dangerous data-flow paths. TaintFuzz was compared against AFL++, Boofuzz, and a random baseline on 12 UPnP-enabled firmware images running under QEMU. TaintFuzz achieved a mean unique crash rate 2.3 times higher than AFL++ and 4.7 times higher than Boofuzz within a four-hour campaign per target. Seventeen previously unreported memory corruption bugs were found across eight firmware images; six were assessed as reachable from the local network without authentication. Proof-of-concept payloads were shared with affected vendors under a 90-day disclosure policy.

title: Recovering Structured Network Protocol Grammars from Firmware Binaries to Improve Fuzz Seed Generation
abstract: Effective fuzzing of network-facing firmware requires structured seeds that exercise deep parsing logic. We describe ProtoRec, a static analysis tool that operates on stripped ARM and MIPS binaries and recovers a partial grammar of the expected network protocol by tracing data-dependent branches from the recv system call. ProtoRec uses symbolic backward slicing to identify comparisons against constants and length fields, assembles them into a context-free grammar fragment, and serialises the result as a Peach Pit–compatible specification file. We evaluated ProtoRec on 15 firmware images implementing proprietary binary protocols used in industrial automation equipment. Recovered grammars covered a mean of 68 percent of the message fields identified by a human analyst spending eight hours per protocol. Seeds generated from recovered grammars increased AFL++ branch coverage by a mean of 31 percent and crash discovery rate by 2.1 times compared to seeds generated by Peach with generic TCP templates. ProtoRec runs in under 20 minutes per binary on a standard workstation.

title: Longitudinal Study of Patch Propagation Latency for Memory Safety Vulnerabilities in Consumer Router Firmware, 2018–2024
abstract: We investigated how quickly memory safety vulnerabilities that originate in third-party open-source components—primarily uclibc, busybox, and OpenSSL—appear in and are subsequently patched in consumer router firmware distributed across the European market. Starting from 61 CVEs published between January 2018 and December 2023 and affecting these three libraries, we downloaded all available firmware update archives for 22 router product lines sold under seven brand names, obtaining 847 firmware images spanning six years. For each CVE we determined the first image version to include the vulnerable code and the first to include the fix, computing patch latency as the difference. Median latency from CVE publication to a patched firmware release was 214 days; the 90th percentile exceeded 540 days. Six CVEs remained unpatched in at least one actively sold product as of December 2024. Brand-level regression showed a statistically significant correlation between firmware update frequency and patch latency (Spearman ρ = –0.71). These findings have direct implications for the firmware analysis community regarding the realistic window of exposure for discovered vulnerabilities.

title: Meta-Learning Initialisation for Absence Forecasting Across Organisations with Heterogeneous HR Systems
abstract: Organisations deploying absence forecasting models from scratch face a cold-start problem: insufficient local data to train reliable models. This paper investigates whether a MAML-style meta-learning initialisation, trained on data from 12 source organisations, can provide an improved starting point for fine-tuning on a new target organisation with limited data. The meta-training set covers 47,000 employee-years across manufacturing, logistics, and public administration sectors. The target evaluation uses leave-one-organisation-out cross-validation across six held-out organisations, with fine-tuning budgets of 30, 60, and 120 labelled employee-year observations. At a budget of 60 observations, meta-initialised models achieve mean AUC of 0.72 compared with 0.65 for random initialisation and 0.68 for initialisation from a single best-matching source organisation. Performance gains are largest when the target organisation's workforce composition differs substantially from the training distribution. Sensitivity to meta-learning hyperparameters is assessed over a grid of 48 configurations.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Judgment Outcomes: A Feasibility Study on Serbian Case Law
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems combine a retrieval component with a generative model and have been applied to question answering in several legal jurisdictions, but their use for outcome prediction on small corpora remains unexplored. This preprint describes a feasibility study in which a dense retrieval index is built from 1,840 Serbian civil court decisions and used to condition a fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence model on retrieved precedents at inference time. Three retrieval configurations—BM25, dense passage retrieval with a multilingual encoder, and a hybrid combination—are compared on a 200-instance test set. The hybrid configuration achieves the highest accuracy (0.71) and macro F1 (0.63), compared to 0.65 and 0.57 for the no-retrieval baseline. Analysis of retrieved documents shows that recency and jurisdictional tier of retrieved cases are positively associated with prediction correctness. The study flags limitations arising from incomplete metadata and inconsistent anonymisation in the source corpus.

title: Predicting 30-Day Hospital Readmission from Structured EHR Data Using Gradient-Boosted Trees
abstract: This study evaluates gradient-boosted tree classifiers for predicting 30-day all-cause hospital readmission using structured electronic health record data from a single tertiary hospital in Vojvodina covering 14,820 adult admissions between 2010 and 2012. Features included 47 clinical and demographic variables extracted from discharge summaries, laboratory results, and coded diagnoses. Models were trained with five-fold cross-validation; the final XGBoost model achieved an AUROC of 0.71 and a precision-recall AUC of 0.43 on a held-out test set. Feature importance analysis identified serum creatinine, number of prior admissions within 12 months, and primary diagnosis category as the strongest predictors. Missing value imputation strategy was compared across mean substitution, multivariate imputation by chained equations, and median carry-forward; MICE yielded a measurable improvement in AUROC (+0.03). The paper discusses limitations arising from single-site data and class imbalance (readmission rate 11.4 %) and outlines requirements for a future multi-site replication.

title: Partitioning Strategies for Distributed Logistic Regression Without Sharing Patient Records
abstract: We examine three data partitioning strategies — horizontal, vertical, and hybrid — for training logistic regression classifiers across two geographically separated hospital sites without transferring raw patient records. Using a synthetic dataset generated to match distributional properties of cardiovascular risk records from two collaborating institutions in Serbia and Croatia (combined N = 9,340), we implement a gradient-sharing protocol over an encrypted channel and compare convergence behaviour with centralised training as a reference. Horizontal partitioning converges to within 0.8 % of the centralised AUROC after 14 communication rounds; vertical partitioning requires an entity alignment step that adds latency but enables use of complementary feature sets. We identify conditions under which gradient inversion attacks are feasible in the vertical setting and propose a simple clipping threshold that substantially reduces reconstruction fidelity without degrading model accuracy by more than 1.2 %. The work is positioned as a feasibility study motivating subsequent use of formal differential privacy guarantees.

title: Differential Privacy Budgets in Federated Training of Sepsis Early-Warning Models: An Empirical Study
abstract: Federated learning with differential privacy (DP-FL) offers a mechanism to train clinical models across hospitals while providing formal privacy guarantees, but the privacy-utility trade-off is poorly characterised for high-stakes clinical tasks. This paper presents experiments on a sepsis early-warning task using time-series vital-sign and laboratory data from four simulated federated nodes, each containing between 1,800 and 4,200 patient stays from publicly available critical-care databases adapted to a federated split. We train a logistic regression and a shallow LSTM model under Gaussian noise mechanisms with ε ∈ {1, 2, 5, 10, ∞} and δ = 10⁻⁵, tracking AUROC, sensitivity at 90 % specificity, and Brier score across 50 communication rounds. Results show that for the LSTM, moving from ε = ∞ to ε = 5 costs 3.1 AUROC points; tightening to ε = 1 costs a further 6.8 points. Logistic regression degrades more gracefully under noise. We also analyse the effect of client heterogeneity (non-IID label distributions) on convergence, finding that heterogeneity amplifies the utility cost of tight privacy budgets. Recommendations for budget allocation in real hospital settings are provided.

title: Secure Aggregation Overhead in Cross-Silo Federated Learning: A Network-Level Benchmark
abstract: Secure aggregation protocols are a standard component of privacy-preserving federated learning, but their communication and computation overhead relative to plain gradient averaging is rarely quantified in realistic healthcare network conditions. We benchmarked three secure aggregation schemes — Bonawitz et al.'s masking protocol, TurboAggregate, and a lightweight secret-sharing variant — across a testbed of six emulated hospital nodes connected over links with bandwidth profiles sampled from hospital WAN measurements in Serbia and Romania. Experiments used a convolutional neural network for ECG arrhythmia classification trained over 100 rounds. Wall-clock time per round ranged from 1.4× to 4.7× that of plain FedAvg depending on the scheme and network condition. The lightweight secret-sharing variant achieved the best trade-off between overhead and resilience to up to two dropped clients per round. We provide an open configuration of the testbed for reproducibility.

title: Federated Learning for Chronic Kidney Disease Progression Prediction Across Three Balkan Hospital Networks
abstract: We report a pilot federated learning study for predicting chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression from stage 3 to stage 4/5 over a 24-month horizon, conducted across three hospital sites in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Data from 6,102 patients with documented CKD stage 3 at baseline were partitioned horizontally. A federated random forest implemented via gradient-boosted stump aggregation was compared against local models trained at each site and a pooled centralised baseline (computed post-hoc using anonymised data sharing approved for research purposes). The federated model achieved an AUROC of 0.76, compared with 0.78 for the centralised baseline and a mean of 0.70 across local models. Site-specific performance varied; the smallest site (n = 892) benefited most from federation, gaining 0.09 AUROC over its local model. eGFR slope over six months, proteinuria level, and haemoglobin were the most consistently selected features. Ethics approvals and data governance procedures are documented in full.

title: Client Selection Strategies in Heterogeneous Federated Learning for Clinical Tabular Data
abstract: In cross-silo federated learning, the choice of which clients participate in each communication round affects both convergence speed and the fairness of the resulting model across subpopulations. We study five client selection strategies — random, round-robin, loss-based, gradient diversity, and a bandwidth-aware variant — in the context of tabular clinical data with substantial inter-site heterogeneity in feature distributions and label prevalence. Experiments are conducted on four synthetic federated datasets generated from statistical models fitted to de-identified data from hospital information systems in Serbia and Hungary, with 5 to 12 simulated clients per dataset. Evaluation metrics include convergence rounds to within 1 % of FedAvg ceiling performance, variance of per-client AUROC in the final model, and communication cost. Gradient-diversity-based selection achieves the best balance between convergence speed and per-client fairness but at a 22 % higher communication cost than random selection. Round-robin performed surprisingly well as a zero-overhead baseline. Findings are expected to inform protocol design for the PRIVAMED project.

title: Auditing Membership Inference Risk in Differentially Private Federated Clinical Models
abstract: Differential privacy provides a mathematical bound on the worst-case privacy loss of a trained model, but empirical membership inference attack (MIA) success rates are a complementary practical measure of risk. We conduct a systematic audit of MIA risk on federated models trained with DP-SGD across a range of privacy budgets (ε from 0.5 to 50) using four clinical classification tasks: 30-day mortality, diabetes onset, atrial fibrillation detection from ECG features, and CKD progression. For each task, we train attacker models using the likelihood-ratio threshold attack and a shadow-model attack. We find that ε ≤ 5 reliably reduces MIA advantage to below 3 % above random guessing on all four tasks, while ε > 20 yields MIA advantages of 8–15 % on the two tasks with the most imbalanced class distributions. We also measure the effect of record repetition across local epochs on MIA vulnerability, confirming that fewer local epochs reduce risk independently of the global ε. A practical decision framework for setting ε in hospital deployment contexts is proposed.

title: Федерисано учење у сценарију вертикалног партиционисања медицинских података: студија случаја на интеграцији лабораторијских и радиолошких записа

Задатак је бинарна класификација — предикција развоја дијабетеса типа 2 у наредних 36 месеци. Протокол се ослања на PSI (Private Set Intersection) за усклађивање идентитета без откривања листа пацијената, а затим на сплит архитектуру неуронске мреже са шифрованим преносом прекидних активација. Федерисани вертикални модел постиже AUROC 0,79 у поређењу с 0,72 и 0,68 за локалне моделе установа А и Б. Анализирана је осетљивост поступка PSI на различите нивое преклапања (30–80 %) и утицај шума додатог активацијама на тачност. Резултати потврђују практичну примену вертикалне федерације у болничком окружењу без заједничке IT инфраструктуре.

title: Personalised Federated Learning for Patient Subgroup Adaptation in Stroke Outcome Prediction
abstract: Standard federated averaging produces a single global model that may underperform for subpopulations concentrated at individual sites. We investigate three personalisation strategies — fine-tuning on local data post-federation, mixture-of-experts weighting by site, and MAML-based meta-learning — for a stroke functional outcome prediction task (modified Rankin Scale ≤ 2 at 90 days) across six simulated sites derived from an openly available stroke registry, split to create realistic demographic heterogeneity. The global FedAvg model achieves AUROC 0.73; site-level fine-tuning raises the average to 0.76 but increases variance across sites. The MAML approach achieves 0.75 with lower inter-site variance (standard deviation 0.031 vs. 0.048 for fine-tuning). We also test whether personalisation affects calibration (measured by Expected Calibration Error), finding that fine-tuning degrades calibration at the two smallest sites. Results suggest that personalisation strategy selection should consider site size and calibration requirements alongside discrimination.
venue: Journal of Computational Medicine and Health Informatics

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Training with Sparse Gradient Compression Under Differential Privacy Constraints
abstract: Reducing communication volume in federated learning is important for hospital networks with limited or metered WAN bandwidth, but standard gradient sparsification techniques interact with differential privacy noise addition in non-obvious ways. This paper analyses the combined effect of top-k sparsification (k ∈ {1 %, 5 %, 20 %} of gradient coordinates) and Gaussian DP noise on convergence and final model quality for two clinical prediction tasks: ICU length-of-stay regression and cardiac readmission classification, each federated across eight simulated clients. We find that applying noise before sparsification consistently outperforms the reverse order in terms of AUROC at equivalent ε. At k = 5 % combined with ε = 5, communication volume is reduced by 89 % relative to full-gradient FedAvg while incurring only a 2.4-point AUROC penalty compared to full-gradient DP-FL at the same ε. We also characterise the interaction with client heterogeneity, showing that high heterogeneity amplifies the quality loss from aggressive sparsification more than it amplifies the loss from privacy noise. Implementation is provided in a publicly available repository.
venue: Transactions on Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning

title: Benchmarking tabular deep learning against gradient boosting for agronomic event prediction on small heterogeneous sensor datasets
abstract: Tabular deep learning architectures such as TabNet and FT-Transformer have been proposed as alternatives to gradient boosting on structured data. This paper evaluates both families on six agronomic event prediction tasks drawn from BioSense Institute sensor archives, covering frost occurrence, soil moisture regime classification, phenological stage identification, drought stress onset, mildew infection level, and irrigation demand. Dataset sizes range from 890 to 4 200 labelled instances with 12 to 61 input features derived from environmental sensor records. Gradient boosting (XGBoost and LightGBM) outperformed TabNet and FT-Transformer on four of six tasks by statistically significant margins according to paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests at α = 0.05. The two tasks where deep models matched gradient boosting involved the largest datasets and highest feature counts. Training time for gradient boosting was two to three orders of magnitude shorter. The paper concludes that, for the dataset scales typical in single-network agronomic sensor deployments, gradient boosting remains the preferred default and tabular deep learning does not yet justify the additional computational cost and tuning effort.

title: Threshold-free fault prognosis for tractor transmission systems using Gaussian process regression on sensor residuals
abstract: Predictive fault identification in tractor transmissions is approached by fitting Gaussian process regression (GPR) models to multi-channel sensor residuals derived from a physics-informed nominal model. The residuals—differences between observed and model-predicted values for oil temperature, pressure differential, and shift actuator current—are modelled jointly as a GP with a Matérn 5/2 kernel. An increase in posterior predictive variance is used as a threshold-free fault indicator. Data span three years of operation for a fleet of 12 tractors from a large estate farm in the Bačka region, totalling approximately 18,000 engine hours. GPR-based prognosis issued warnings an average of 31 hours before transmission failures requiring workshop intervention, versus 8 hours for a fixed-threshold detector on the same residuals. Calibration of the nominal model required 400 hours of fault-free baseline data per tractor model variant. The paper discusses scalability limitations when fleet size grows, and proposes a hierarchical pooling strategy to share baseline information across similar tractor models.

title: A benchmark of open-source Bayesian network learning tools for transcriptomic datasets with fewer than 50 samples
abstract: A large number of open-source packages implement Bayesian network structure learning, yet systematic benchmarks on biological transcriptomic data in the low-sample regime are rare. We evaluated eight packages—spanning R and Python ecosystems—on 90 real RNA-seq datasets collected from plant stress experiments available in public repositories, filtered to those with 15–48 samples. Packages were assessed on runtime, reproducibility of results across operating systems, flexibility of prior specification, and accuracy measured by SHD against gold-standard subnetworks. Bnlearn (R) and pgmpy (Python) offered the broadest algorithmic coverage; bnlearn recovered edges with the highest F1 (0.41 mean across datasets) while pgmpy was 2.3× faster on datasets exceeding 200 variables. Three packages produced non-reproducible results due to undocumented random seeds. We provide a reproducible benchmarking harness and a decision guide aimed at plant biologists with limited computational experience.

title: Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial models for multi-site microbiome surveys: pooling strength across Vojvodina agricultural districts
abstract: Multi-site microbiome surveys are common in regional agricultural monitoring but sites often differ in sample size and environmental heterogeneity, leading to unstable site-level estimates. We developed a Bayesian hierarchical extension of the Dirichlet-multinomial model in which site-level concentration parameters are drawn from a common hyperprior, enabling partial pooling across six districts of Vojvodina surveyed between 2018 and 2021 (total n = 312 samples, 19 sites). The model was implemented in Stan and fitted via NUTS sampling. Posterior predictive checks confirmed adequate fit at both the site and district levels. Partial pooling reduced the mean width of 95% credible intervals for phylum-level relative abundances by 28% compared to independent site models, with the largest gains for sites with fewer than 12 samples. District-level estimates identified consistent Acidobacteria enrichment in the northern sandy soils relative to southern chernozem sites (posterior probability of difference > 0.97). Code and anonymised data are archived on the Zenodo platform.
venue: Annals of Applied Microbial Statistics

title: Codling moth flight dynamics in apple orchards of northern Serbia
abstract: This study investigated the seasonal flight dynamics of codling moth (Cydia pomonella L.) across twelve commercial apple orchards distributed throughout the Vojvodina and Šumadija regions of northern Serbia over three consecutive growing seasons (2019–2021). Delta-type pheromone traps baited with a synthetic (E,E)-8,10-dodecadienol lure were deployed at weekly intervals and moth captures were recorded from early April through late September. Flight activity consistently followed a bimodal pattern, with a primary peak occurring in the second half of May and a secondary peak in late July, closely correlated with accumulated degree-days above a 10 °C base temperature. Inter-site variability in peak timing reached up to eleven days, attributable to differences in elevation, tree canopy density, and local microclimate. Generalised linear mixed models revealed that cumulative precipitation during the preceding week significantly suppressed trap catches, while mean daily maximum temperature above 28 °C showed a modest positive association. The findings provide empirically grounded parameters for regional degree-day models and underline the necessity of site-specific calibration for any operational pest warning service serving northern Serbian apple producers.

title: Counting moths in pheromone trap photos: agreement between experts and a neural network
abstract: Accurate counting of captured insects in pheromone trap images is an essential step in automated pest monitoring pipelines, yet the reliability of neural network predictions relative to trained expert assessors has rarely been quantified in operational conditions. In this study, 1,840 photographs of sticky-liner trap bottoms containing codling moth (Cydia pomonella) specimens were collected from twenty orchard sites across Vojvodina during 2022 and 2023. Three independent entomology experts each performed manual counts on all images; their mean score served as the reference standard. A convolutional neural network based on a fine-tuned ResNet-50 backbone was trained on 1,200 images and evaluated on a held-out set of 640 images. Agreement between expert pairs yielded intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) between 0.91 and 0.94. The network achieved an ICC of 0.89 against the expert mean, a mean absolute error of 1.4 moths per image, and showed no systematic bias across the density range of 0–47 specimens. Counting speed was approximately 340 images per hour compared to roughly 55 for a human annotator. These results indicate that neural network-based counting reaches near-expert accuracy while substantially reducing labour costs, supporting its integration into real-time pheromone trap monitoring systems.
venue: Plant Protection Science

title: Forecasting spraying windows from trap counts and degree-days
abstract: Accurate determination of optimal spray timing is central to effective integrated pest management for codling moth. This paper presents a decision-support framework that combines pheromone trap catch data with degree-day accumulation to forecast egg-hatch windows and recommend narrow, targeted spray intervals for apple orchards in northern Serbia. Using three seasons of field data (2017–2019) from eight orchard sites, we calibrated a nonlinear degree-day model with a lower developmental threshold of 10 °C and an upper threshold of 31 °C. Trap catch threshold algorithms were benchmarked against the degree-day forecasts; combined use of both signals reduced false-positive spray recommendations by 34 % compared to trap-count thresholds alone. Spray window predictions were validated against larval infestation assessments at fruit harvest, demonstrating a mean reduction in fruit damage from 8.1 % to 2.3 % when growers adhered to model-recommended timing. The framework is designed for straightforward adoption by agricultural advisory services and is compatible with low-cost, IoT-enabled trap data loggers. Presented outcomes informed the design of the ORCHARD-IPM regional warning service launched in 2019.

title: Spatial clustering of codling moth hotspots in Vojvodina orchards using geostatistical trap-network data
abstract: Understanding the spatial heterogeneity of codling moth (Cydia pomonella) pressure is essential for site-specific management decisions in large orchard landscapes. This study applied geostatistical methods, including variogram modelling and ordinary kriging, to pheromone trap catch data collected from 47 georeferenced traps distributed across the Vojvodina plain during 2020 and 2021. Semivariogram analysis revealed spatial autocorrelation at ranges between 1.8 and 3.4 km, suggesting that infestation hotspots are meaningfully clustered at the farm-cluster scale. Interpolated risk maps consistently identified three persistent high-pressure zones associated with fragmented orchard edges adjacent to abandoned plantations. Cluster-based spray recommendations derived from the kriged surfaces reduced total insecticide applications by 19 % compared to a blanket-treatment strategy, while maintaining fruit damage below the 2 % commercial threshold. The methodology is directly applicable to regional advisory services and can be updated in near-real time as seasonal trap data accumulate. Results advocate for coordinated monitoring networks that extend beyond individual farm boundaries.

title: Effect of pheromone lure age on codling moth trap efficacy across a full growing season
abstract: Pheromone lure longevity directly affects the reliability of trap-based monitoring programmes for codling moth (Cydia pomonella). Although manufacturers typically recommend lure replacement at four- to six-week intervals, empirical data on emission decay under field conditions in continental climates are limited. This factorial field experiment, conducted across six apple orchards in northern Serbia over two seasons, compared weekly trap catches obtained with fresh lures against lures aged 2, 4, 6, and 8 weeks in situ. Mean catch rates declined by 22 % at 4 weeks, 51 % at 6 weeks, and 78 % at 8 weeks relative to freshly replaced controls, with the steepest attrition occurring during July when ambient temperatures exceeded 30 °C for extended periods. A correction-factor regression model was developed to adjust aged-lure counts to fresh-lure equivalents, substantially improving consistency of phenological indices calculated from sequential trap records. Findings recommend a maximum four-week replacement interval under Vojvodina summer conditions and provide quantitative correction factors applicable to historical monitoring datasets that used variable replacement schedules.

title: IoT-enabled automated pheromone trap stations: field validation in a multi-orchard network
abstract: Manual inspection of pheromone traps is labour-intensive and introduces temporal gaps that can delay pest management decisions. This paper describes the field validation of a low-cost IoT-enabled automated trap station prototype, termed TrapNode-1, developed in collaboration with an electronics engineering group at the University of Novi Sad. Each station integrates a Raspberry Pi-based camera module, a LoRaWAN communication unit, and a solar power supply to deliver daily trap images to a cloud processing pipeline. Over the 2022 growing season, eighteen TrapNode-1 units were deployed across four commercial apple farms in Vojvodina alongside paired manual traps. Automated moth counts derived from an on-server convolutional neural network showed a mean absolute error of 1.7 moths per image relative to manual counts. Data upload reliability reached 96.3 % across the season, with most outages attributable to transient cellular coverage gaps. Station cost per unit was approximately 140 EUR in components. The study demonstrates that near-daily catch data from automated stations substantially refine degree-day model inputs, advancing spray-timing recommendations by one to two days compared to weekly manual readings, with direct implications for insecticide use reduction.

title: Monitoring the apple clearwing moth alongside codling moth in integrated pheromone trap programmes
abstract: Apple clearwing moth (Synanthedon myopaeformis Borkhausen) has emerged as a secondary but economically significant pest in Serbian apple production, yet it is rarely incorporated into existing pheromone monitoring protocols designed primarily for codling moth. This study assessed whether dual-lure trap configurations could simultaneously deliver reliable phenological data for both species without significant interference effects. Over two seasons across ten commercial orchards in Vojvodina and the Fruška Gora foothill zone, single-species lure traps were compared with dual-lure delta traps and dual-lure funnel traps in a randomised block design. Dual-lure funnel traps successfully captured both species at densities statistically indistinguishable from species-specific controls, whereas dual-lure delta traps showed a 17 % suppression of clearwing catches. A combined monitoring calendar integrating both species' degree-day thresholds is proposed, enabling growers to manage two damaging species within a single trap-inspection routine and reducing total monitoring infrastructure costs by approximately 30 %.

title: Deep learning architectures for multi-species insect classification in sticky-trap images: a comparative evaluation
abstract: Pheromone and yellow sticky traps capture not only target pest species but also a range of non-target insects, creating classification challenges for automated counting systems. This study benchmarked five deep learning architectures—VGG-16, ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B3, MobileNetV3, and a custom lightweight convolutional network—against a manually annotated dataset of 3,200 sticky-trap images collected from apple and pear orchards in northern Serbia. Images contained twelve insect morphospecies, with codling moth constituting 38 % of all specimens. EfficientNet-B3 achieved the highest overall top-1 accuracy of 91.4 % and the best F1-score of 0.89 for codling moth specifically. The custom lightweight network, designed for edge deployment on TrapNode-class hardware, reached 86.1 % accuracy while requiring only 4.2 MB of model storage and 210 ms inference time per image on a Raspberry Pi 4B. Data augmentation strategies, including synthetic background substitution and artificial occlusion, improved minority-class recall by up to 14 percentage points. Results provide practical guidance for selecting classification backends in automated field monitoring devices and publicly release the annotated image dataset for community benchmarking.

title: Integrated pest management adoption barriers among apple growers in Vojvodina: a survey-based analysis
abstract: Despite the well-documented efficacy of integrated pest management (IPM) strategies, adoption rates among commercial apple producers in Vojvodina remain uneven. This paper reports findings from a structured questionnaire survey administered to 214 apple-growing households across five districts of the autonomous province during 2021. Responses were analysed using logistic regression to identify socio-economic, informational, and infrastructural predictors of IPM adoption. Farms larger than 5 ha were 3.2 times more likely to use pheromone-trap monitoring than smaller holdings. Access to an agricultural extension advisor at least once per season increased the probability of degree-day-based spray timing by 2.7 times. Conversely, limited smartphone or internet access was the single strongest barrier to uptake of digital pest warning services, cited by 41 % of non-adopters. Growers who participated in producer cooperatives showed significantly higher IPM compliance scores. Findings directly informed the outreach and communication strategy of the ORCHARD-IPM warning service and highlight the need for offline-accessible advisory tools targeted at smaller and more isolated orchardists.

title: Pheromone trap monitoring and integrated management of orchard pests in the Western Balkans
abstract: This chapter synthesises two decades of research and extension experience with pheromone-trap-based monitoring programmes for key lepidopteran pests of pome and stone fruit orchards across the Western Balkan region, with emphasis on Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. It covers the biology and seasonal phenology of codling moth (Cydia pomonella), Oriental fruit moth (Grapholita molesta), and plum fruit moth (Grapholita funebrana), and reviews the calibration status of degree-day models for each species under Balkan continental climatic conditions. The chapter evaluates the transition from calendar-based to phenology-driven spray programmes, presenting case studies demonstrating reductions of 25–40 % in total insecticide applications without significant loss of pest suppression efficacy. Methodological standards for trap deployment, lure management, and count recording are harmonised across national practices to support cross-border data sharing. An outlook section discusses the integration of automated image-based trap stations and machine learning tools into national pest advisory systems, identifying key technical and policy prerequisites for regional-scale digital IPM infrastructure.

title: Distancing from the past self: Recall accuracy and evaluative bias in students facing academic failure feedback
abstract: When people receive negative feedback about their current competence, they sometimes cope by retrospectively lowering their evaluations of their past self, a process referred to as past-self derogation. This study tested whether such derogation is accompanied by measurable distortion in episodic recall. Sixty-two undergraduate students at the University of Novi Sad were randomly assigned to receive either failure or neutral feedback on a bogus cognitive test. They then completed a cued-recall task using autobiographical cues drawn from a structured diary they had kept for three weeks prior to the session. Recall intrusion rates, valence ratings, and response latencies were recorded. Participants in the failure condition rated their recalled past-self episodes as significantly more negative than their original diary entries had indicated (mean shift Δ = −0.43 on a 7-point scale, p < .01), whereas recall accuracy for factual content did not differ between conditions. Response latencies for positive past-self cues were longer in the failure group, suggesting suppression-like retrieval interference. The pattern was moderated by trait self-esteem: participants with higher baseline self-esteem showed larger derogation effects, consistent with a motivated self-protection account rather than a global mood-congruent recall explanation.

title: Narrative coherence and self-serving revision in weekly diary entries: A three-month longitudinal study
abstract: Diary methods offer a naturalistic window into how people reconstruct personal history over time. This study followed 47 first-year university students over twelve weeks, collecting structured weekly diary entries that included both factual records of events and self-evaluative ratings. At weeks four, eight, and twelve, participants were asked to re-read and rate a randomly selected subset of their earlier entries. Discrepancies between original and retrospective ratings were coded as consistent, self-enhancing, or self-diminishing revisions. Results showed that self-enhancing revisions outnumbered self-diminishing ones at all three time points (overall ratio 2.1:1), and the proportion of self-enhancing revisions increased across the twelve weeks, suggesting cumulative motivated reconstruction rather than random noise. Narrative coherence scores, derived from content analysis of the diary texts, were positively correlated with the frequency of self-enhancing revisions (r = .38, p < .01), indicating that individuals who construct more coherent autobiographical narratives are also more likely to revise their past in a self-favourable direction. No significant sex differences were found. Implications for diary-based assessment instruments used in clinical and occupational contexts are discussed.

title: Temporal distance manipulation and the clarity of past-self images: An experimental replication and extension
abstract: A widely cited finding in temporal self-appraisal research holds that increasing psychological distance from a remembered past self makes that self feel less connected to the present, thereby allowing more extreme evaluative revision. This preregistered study attempted a direct replication of that finding and extended it by including a measure of autobiographical reasoning style. Ninety-one participants at the University of Novi Sad and the University of Banja Luka were assigned to short (one-month), medium (one-year), or long (five-year) temporal distance conditions using standardised imagery instructions. They then rated a series of past-self vignettes on competence and warmth dimensions and completed a brief autobiographical reasoning questionnaire distinguishing assimilative from accommodative strategies. Replication of the core distance–derogation effect was partial: the long-distance condition produced reliably lower competence ratings for past-self vignettes compared to the short-distance condition (d = 0.41), but warmth ratings were unaffected by distance. Accommodative reasoners showed smaller distance effects than assimilative reasoners, suggesting that the tendency to integrate past experiences into a changed self-narrative buffers motivated derogation. Sample size limitations are noted and power calculations for a follow-up study are provided.

title: Self-concept threat and prospective memory for self-relevant events: Preliminary findings from a student sample
abstract: Research on autobiographical memory has mostly examined retrospective processes, but self-concept threat may also influence prospective memory — the ability to remember to perform intended actions linked to self-relevant goals. This conference paper reports preliminary data from 38 participants who completed a self-concept threat induction followed by a virtual-day prospective memory task in which some target events were self-relevant (e.g., sending a message about a personal achievement) and others were neutral. Participants under threat showed a 19-percentage-point drop in prospective memory accuracy for self-relevant targets compared to a control group, while accuracy for neutral targets did not differ between groups. Affect ratings collected after the task suggest that the effect is not fully explained by general negative affect, pointing to a more selective interference with self-relevant prospective intentions. The paradigm and preliminary effect sizes are reported as groundwork for a larger dissertation study.

title: Cognitive ergonomics of older adults
abstract: This book chapter reviews empirical research on the cognitive demands that digital interfaces impose on adults in late adulthood, drawing on the broader literature on working memory decline, processing speed reduction, and inhibitory deficits associated with normal aging. The chapter covers task analysis approaches adapted for older populations, measurement instruments used in laboratory and field evaluation, and common design principles derived from this evidence base including target sizing, contrast requirements, feedback latency, and error recovery. A section addresses the heterogeneity of the older adult population with respect to digital experience and sensorimotor ability. Methodological limitations in the existing literature, including small samples and laboratory artificiality, are discussed along with recommendations for evaluation practice in applied settings such as healthcare and public administration.

title: Perceived identity threat and outgroup attitudes among ethnic Hungarians in Vojvodina: A survey study
abstract: This study examined the relationship between perceived threats to ethnic Hungarian identity and negative attitudes toward Serbs in Vojvodina, drawing on identity threat theory and integrated threat theory. A community sample of 312 ethnic Hungarian adults was recruited in three municipalities (Subotica, Zrenjanin, Senta) through stratified random sampling. Participants completed validated scales measuring symbolic threat, realistic threat, intergroup anxiety, and attitude items adapted for the local context. Structural equation modelling showed that symbolic threat was the strongest predictor of prejudiced attitudes (β = 0.41, p < .001), while realistic threat operated partly through intergroup anxiety. Prior positive contact with Serbs moderated both threat pathways. The findings suggest that identity concerns specific to minority status are separable from general resource-based competition and have distinct implications for intervention design in multiethnic communities.

title: CYP3A5 genotype and tacrolimus dose requirements in the first three months after renal transplantation: a single-centre observational study
abstract: Tacrolimus exhibits wide inter-individual pharmacokinetic variability, partly attributed to CYP3A5 genetic polymorphisms. This prospective observational study enrolled 87 adult de novo renal transplant recipients at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2013 and 2015. Patients were genotyped for CYP3A5*1 and CYP3A5*3 alleles using real-time PCR. Whole-blood tacrolimus trough concentrations were measured at weeks 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12 post-transplant by HPLC-MS/MS. CYP3A5 expressers (n=19) required a mean dose 1.8-fold higher than non-expressers to achieve target trough levels of 8–12 ng/mL. Time to first therapeutic trough concentration was significantly longer in expressers (median 14 days versus 7 days, p=0.003). Acute rejection episodes within the first three months did not differ significantly between genotype groups (10.5% versus 8.8%, p=0.81). These findings support prospective genotyping as a practical tool for initial tacrolimus dose selection in this population.

title: Tacrolimus intra-patient variability as a predictor of graft function decline at 24 months in CYP3A5 non-expressers
abstract: High intra-patient variability (IPV) of tacrolimus trough concentrations has been associated with worse graft outcomes independently of average exposure. This retrospective cohort study examined 112 CYP3A5*3/*3 homozygous renal transplant recipients followed for 24 months at two centres in Vojvodina. IPV was calculated as the coefficient of variation (CV%) of trough concentrations measured monthly during months 3–12 post-transplant. Patients were stratified into low IPV (<25%) and high IPV (≥25%) groups. The primary endpoint was a decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of more than 20% from the month-3 baseline. High IPV was observed in 38 patients (33.9%) and was independently associated with eGFR decline at 24 months in multivariable logistic regression (OR 3.1, 95% CI 1.4–6.9, p=0.005) after adjustment for donor age, cold ischaemia time, and baseline eGFR. These data suggest that monitoring IPV alongside trough levels provides additional prognostic information even in genetically homogeneous patients.

title: Combined CYP3A4*22 and CYP3A5*3 genotyping improves prediction of tacrolimus dose-adjusted exposure in a cohort of 96 kidney transplant recipients
abstract: CYP3A4*22 is a low-frequency variant associated with reduced CYP3A4 activity that may further modulate tacrolimus pharmacokinetics in patients already carrying CYP3A5*3. This cross-sectional study genotyped 96 stable kidney transplant recipients at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina for both CYP3A4*22 and CYP3A5*3 alleles. Tacrolimus dose-adjusted C0 (C0/D) was computed from trough concentrations and daily doses recorded over three consecutive monthly visits. Patients carrying both CYP3A4*22 and CYP3A5*3 homozygously (n=11) had a mean C0/D of 248 (ng/mL)/(mg/kg/day), significantly higher than CYP3A5*3 homozygotes without CYP3A4*22 (mean 181, p=0.019) and double-wild-type patients (mean 102, p<0.001). Adding CYP3A4*22 to a regression model including CYP3A5 genotype increased adjusted R² from 0.31 to 0.44. These findings suggest that routine inclusion of CYP3A4*22 genotyping could modestly but meaningfully improve pre-transplant dose predictions.

title: Urinary kidney injury molecule-1 as an early marker of tacrolimus nephrotoxicity stratified by CYP3A5 genotype
abstract: Tacrolimus nephrotoxicity is a leading cause of late allograft loss but lacks sensitive early biomarkers measurable in routine monitoring. This study investigated urinary kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) as an early marker in 78 renal transplant recipients stratified by CYP3A5 genotype. Spot urine samples were collected at months 3, 6, and 12 post-transplant and KIM-1 was quantified by ELISA, normalised to urinary creatinine. Tacrolimus nephrotoxicity was defined by protocol biopsy criteria at 12 months. KIM-1/creatinine was elevated at 6 months in patients subsequently diagnosed with nephrotoxicity (median 1.84 versus 0.63 ng/mg, p<0.001). In CYP3A5 non-expressers, the area under the ROC curve for KIM-1 at 6 months predicting nephrotoxicity at 12 months was 0.78 (95% CI 0.65–0.91). No predictive value was found in expressers (AUC 0.54). Findings suggest KIM-1 monitoring may be particularly informative in CYP3A5 non-expressers who are at higher absolute tacrolimus exposure for a given dose.

title: Population pharmacokinetic modelling of tacrolimus in adult renal transplant recipients: influence of CYP3A5 genotype, haematocrit, and time post-transplant
abstract: Population pharmacokinetic (popPK) modelling allows estimation of individual tacrolimus exposure from sparse sampling designs, which is practical in outpatient transplant follow-up. This study developed a popPK model using NONMEM 7.5 with data from 134 renal transplant recipients (1,847 trough observations over 18 months). A one-compartment model with first-order absorption and elimination fitted the data adequately. CYP3A5 genotype was confirmed as a statistically significant covariate on apparent clearance (CL/F), with expressers showing 64% higher CL/F than non-expressers (p<0.001). Haematocrit was a significant covariate on volume of distribution (p=0.004). Time post-transplant influenced CL/F in a time-varying fashion, declining by approximately 18% between month 1 and month 6. Internal validation by visual predictive check and normalised prediction distribution errors supported acceptable model performance. The model may serve as the basis for Bayesian dose adjustment tools adaptable for clinical use in the region.

title: Pharmacogenomic testing in transplantation: current practice and barriers to implementation in transplant centres across the Western Balkans
abstract: Despite published guidelines recommending CYP3A5 genotype-guided tacrolimus dosing, uptake in clinical practice remains inconsistent. This cross-sectional survey study contacted 23 transplant centres across six Western Balkan countries between March and September 2024. A structured 42-item questionnaire assessed current TDM practices, availability of pharmacogenomic testing, perceived barriers, and willingness to adopt pre-transplant genotyping. Responses were received from 18 centres (78% response rate). Routine CYP3A5 genotyping before transplantation was performed by only 4 centres (22%). The most frequently cited barriers were cost (83%), lack of clear reimbursement pathways (72%), absence of local validation data (61%), and limited awareness among transplant surgeons (50%). Centres with on-site molecular diagnostics capability were more likely to perform genotyping (OR 8.4, 95% CI 1.7–41.5). The survey highlights substantial gaps between published pharmacogenomic recommendations and actual clinical adoption and identifies targets for capacity-building efforts.

title: Tacrolimus whole-blood protein binding and free-fraction estimation in renal transplant recipients with hypoalbuminaemia: a pilot study
abstract: Standard tacrolimus TDM relies on whole-blood trough concentrations, which predominantly reflect erythrocyte-bound drug. In patients with hypoalbuminaemia, redistribution of the unbound plasma fraction may alter the relationship between whole-blood concentration and pharmacological effect. This pilot study measured whole-blood tacrolimus, plasma tacrolimus, and plasma unbound tacrolimus by equilibrium dialysis followed by HPLC-MS/MS in 28 renal transplant recipients, of whom 12 had serum albumin below 30 g/L at the time of sampling. In hypoalbuminaemic patients, whole-blood C0 underestimated unbound plasma exposure relative to normoalbuminaemic patients (ratio of free plasma to whole-blood concentration 0.0047 versus 0.0031, p=0.03). CYP3A5 non-expressers showed numerically higher free-fraction values but the interaction with albumin status was not statistically significant in this small sample. These preliminary data suggest that hypoalbuminaemia may be a clinically relevant source of TDM inaccuracy and warrant investigation in a larger cohort.

title: Intra-individual variability in oral verapamil bioavailability across repeated dosing occasions in patients with type 2 diabetes and autonomic neuropathy
abstract: High intra-individual pharmacokinetic variability is a practical concern for drugs with a narrow therapeutic index. Verapamil, a CYP3A4 and P-gp substrate with first-pass metabolism sensitive to intestinal transit time, was chosen to quantify this variability in a population with fluctuating autonomic neuropathy severity. Fourteen type 2 diabetic patients with confirmed cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy received verapamil 80 mg immediate-release on four separate occasions 4 weeks apart under identical standardised conditions. Full pharmacokinetic profiles were obtained on each occasion. Within-subject coefficient of variation (CVw) for Cmax was 41% and for AUC0–12 h was 33%, compared with literature reference values of approximately 20–24% in healthy subjects. Gastric emptying t½ measured on each occasion (13C-breath test) accounted for 27% of the observed CVw in Cmax by mixed-effects modelling. Autonomic function scores (COMPASS-31 questionnaire) showed week-to-week variation that correlated moderately with gastric emptying changes (r = 0.39). The data argue for caution when interpreting single-occasion pharmacokinetic assessments in this population and for considering gastric motility as a covariate in trial design.

title: Sex differences in self-reported adverse effects of thiazide diuretics in hypertensive patients over 65: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: Thiazide diuretics are first-line agents for hypertension in the elderly, yet sex-stratified adverse effect data remain sparse in this age group. We conducted a cross-sectional study enrolling 312 outpatients (age ≥65) attending hypertension clinics in Vojvodina between 2009 and 2010. Patients completed a structured symptom questionnaire covering 18 predefined adverse effects; physicians recorded concurrent medications and comorbidities. Women accounted for 58% of participants. Adverse effect rates per 100 patient-months were significantly higher in women for hyponatraemia-related symptoms (RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.31–2.58) and muscle cramps (RR 1.67, 95% CI 1.14–2.45). Men reported erectile dysfunction in 14% of cases on hydrochlorothiazide, an outcome absent from female records by definition but factored into composite scoring adjustments. Logistic regression controlling for age, creatinine clearance and number of co-administered drugs confirmed sex as an independent predictor of electrolyte-related adverse events. These findings support the need for sex-specific monitoring protocols in geriatric antihypertensive practice.

title: Neuroinflammatory markers in the substantia nigra of rats chronically exposed to low-dose cypermethrin: microglial activation and cytokine profiling
abstract: Pyrethroid insecticides have recently attracted attention as possible triggers of microglial activation in the midbrain, potentially contributing to progressive dopaminergic cell loss. Male Wistar rats received cypermethrin at 2 mg/kg/day orally for 42 days; controls received vehicle (n = 10 per group). At sacrifice, substantia nigra sections were processed for Iba-1 immunostaining (microglial morphology) and CD68 expression (phagocytic activation). Nigral tissue cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-10) were quantified by multiplex ELISA. Iba-1-positive cell density was 37% higher in treated animals; CD68-positive cells were 2.4-fold more abundant, indicating a shift toward activated phenotype. TNF-α and IL-1β concentrations were elevated 2.1- and 1.8-fold respectively (both p < 0.01), while IL-10 was unchanged. Tyrosine hydroxylase-positive cell number was modestly but significantly reduced (−9%, p = 0.04). Correlational analysis showed that CD68 density predicted residual TH cell count (β = −0.58, p = 0.008). These findings suggest that microglial neuroinflammation may be an intermediate step between pyrethroid exposure and incipient dopaminergic cell loss.

title: Dropout Intentions Among Under-14 Football Players in Serbian Academies: A Cross-Sectional Survey
abstract: This study examined dropout intentions among 312 male players aged 12–14 years registered with first- and second-division football academies in Serbia. A structured questionnaire assessed motivational climate, perceived coaching support, training load satisfaction, and dropout intention. Hierarchical logistic regression indicated that ego-oriented motivational climate (OR = 2.41, p < .01) and perceived parental pressure (OR = 1.87, p < .05) were the strongest predictors of dropout intention, after controlling for age, playing time, and club tier. Mastery climate and coach–athlete relationship quality were negatively associated with dropout intention. Findings suggest that structural and relational factors within academies carry greater predictive weight than individual motivation alone. Implications for coach education in transitional sport systems are discussed.

title: Longitudinal Tracking of Physical Fitness in Youth Female Handball Players During a Three-Year Academy Programme
abstract: Thirty-two female handball players (entry age 12.3 ± 0.7 years) were tracked across three consecutive seasons in a regional academy in Vojvodina. Annual assessments included the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1, countermovement jump, 20-m sprint, and reactive agility. Mixed-effects models revealed significant season-by-playing-time interaction effects for aerobic capacity (F = 4.63, p = .01) and reactive agility (F = 3.81, p = .03), but not for maximal sprint speed. Players who reported training in a second sport during the off-season showed 8–12% higher increments in aerobic capacity by year three compared with single-sport specialists. Dropout occurred in nine players (28%) over the period; dropouts showed systematically lower coach-rated enjoyment scores at baseline, suggesting that affective indicators may serve as early monitoring markers alongside physical metrics.

title: Coaching Competencies and Athlete-Centred Practices in Post-Transitional Sport Systems: A Comparative Review
abstract: This book chapter reviews empirical literature published between 2000 and 2017 on coaching competencies and athlete-centred approaches in countries that underwent socio-political transition after 1989, with particular attention to sport systems in Serbia, Croatia, Slovakia, and Romania. Evidence is organised around three themes: formal coach education structures, informal knowledge transmission, and the persistence of command-style coaching in youth settings. The chapter argues that transition-era reductions in public sport funding created a coaching workforce gap that was partially filled by former elite athletes without formal pedagogical preparation, a pattern documented across all four countries. Athlete-centred practice adoption is slower in team sports than in individual disciplines, and slower in rural than in urban clubs. The chapter proposes a competency audit framework adapted to resource-constrained environments.

title: Training Volume and Injury Incidence in Under-16 Football: A One-Season Prospective Study in Vojvodina Regional Leagues
abstract: Eighty-three male footballers (mean age 15.4 ± 0.6 years) from six clubs in the Vojvodina regional league were monitored across a 34-week competitive season. Weekly training volume was recorded by coaches, and players reported acute injuries via weekly SMS-based questionnaires. Injury incidence was 4.7 injuries per 1000 training hours and 7.2 per 1000 match hours. Players with cumulative weekly training loads exceeding 420 minutes had significantly higher injury rates than those below 300 minutes (RR = 1.94, 95% CI [1.14, 3.30]). Early-specialised players (defined as single-sport since age ≤10) showed a 22% higher injury rate than late-entry players, independent of weekly volume. Overuse injuries accounted for 38% of all cases. The data support revised training-load guidelines for regional-level academies where medical monitoring is limited.

title: Perceived Organisational Support in Youth Sport Clubs and Its Relationship to Athlete Retention: A Multi-Club Study
abstract: Perceived organisational support (POS) was assessed in 415 youth athletes (aged 13–18) across 19 clubs in Serbia using an adapted version of the Survey of Perceived Organisational Support. POS was measured at the start of the competitive season, and retention was tracked over 12 months. Multilevel logistic regression, accounting for athlete nesting within clubs, showed that a one-unit increase in POS score was associated with a 17% reduction in dropout odds (OR = 0.83, p < .001). POS effects were stronger for athletes from lower socioeconomic backgrounds (interaction term p = .02). Club-level variance explained 23% of dropout, indicating that organisational factors operate beyond individual characteristics. The findings suggest that low-cost structural interventions—such as regular club communication, transparent selection criteria, and mentoring schemes—may be effective retention levers.

title: Gender Differences in Dropout Rates and Reasons Across Three Youth Team Sports in Serbia: A Five-Year Registry Analysis
abstract: Using registration records from the Serbian Football Federation, Basketball Federation, and Handball Federation for the period 2015–2020, dropout rates were calculated for 14,820 athletes (58% male, 42% female) aged 10–18. Female dropout rates were 11–18 percentage points higher than male rates in all three sports at each age bracket. Discrete-time survival analysis showed that the hazard of dropout peaked at ages 13–14 for females and 15–16 for males across sports. Multinomial logistic regression on a sub-sample surveyed at dropout (n = 624) indicated that females more frequently cited lack of visible pathways to senior competition, inadequate facility provision, and coach disinterest as reasons, while males more frequently cited competitive deselection. The study highlights systematic structural inequities rather than purely motivational explanations for gendered dropout patterns.

title: Perceived Competence and Enjoyment Trajectories in Early-Specialised vs. Multi-Sport Youth Athletes: A Two-Year Panel Study
abstract: A two-wave panel design tracked 196 youth athletes (aged 11–14 at wave 1; 49% female) from handball and football clubs in the Novi Sad metropolitan area. At each wave, participants completed the Perceived Competence Scale and Sport Enjoyment subscale of the Physical Activity and Leisure Motivation Scale. At baseline, early-specialised athletes showed higher perceived competence than multi-sport peers (d = 0.34), but this advantage diminished by wave 2 (d = 0.11, ns). Enjoyment scores declined significantly only in early-specialised athletes over the two years (Δ = −4.2 points on a 100-point scale, t = 3.21, p = .002), whereas multi-sport athletes showed no significant change. Moderation analysis indicated that the enjoyment decline was steeper in clubs with higher competitive-orientation climates. Results support developmental models that discourage single-sport commitment before age 13.

title: Athlete Development Environment Perceptions Among Elite Youth Handball Players in Serbia: Psychometric Evaluation of an Adapted Questionnaire
abstract: The Athlete Development Environment Questionnaire (ADEQ) was translated, culturally adapted, and evaluated for use with Serbian youth handball players. A sample of 341 athletes (aged 14–19, 47% female) from nine clubs completed the adapted instrument. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the original five-factor structure (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.057) after the removal of two items with poor cross-cultural fit. Internal consistency was acceptable across subscales (Cronbach's α = 0.71–0.87). Measurement invariance across sex was confirmed at the scalar level. Criterion validity was assessed against a single-item overall satisfaction measure (r = 0.51) and against dropout intention (r = −0.44). The adapted questionnaire is made available for use by clubs and researchers in Serbian-speaking contexts. Normative data stratified by sex and club tier are provided.

title: Effect of hook grip versus closed grip on wrist and finger extensor EMG during the clean deadlift
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) of the flexor digitorum superficialis, extensor digitorum communis, and flexor carpi radialis was compared between hook grip and conventional closed grip conditions during the clean deadlift in sixteen trained lifters (mean 1RM clean deadlift 142 ± 18 kg). A within-subject crossover design was used with lifts at 70% and 85% of 1RM. Delsys Trigno wireless sensors were placed according to SENIAM recommendations; signals were normalised to maximal voluntary contraction. Flexor digitorum superficialis activation was significantly lower under hook grip at both intensities (by 14–19%, p < 0.01), while extensor digitorum communis showed no significant difference. Thumb interphalangeal joint loading was estimated from a simplified mechanical model and averaged 47 ± 12 N under hook grip at 85% 1RM. Findings suggest that hook grip reduces extrinsic finger flexor demand but introduces localised thumb loading.

title: Kvalitet života pacijenata sa sistemskim lupusom u Vojvodini: preliminarni podaci
abstract: Cilj ove pilot studije bio je da proceni zdravstveni kvalitet života (HRQoL) kod pacijenata sa sistemskim eritematoznim lupusom (SLE) u Vojvodini primenom upitnika SF-36. U studiju je uključeno 48 pacijenata (42 žene, 6 muškaraca, prosečna starost 36,4 ± 11,2 godine) koji su bili praćeni u Klinici za reumatologiju Kliničkog centra Vojvodine u periodu od januara do juna 2013. godine. Podaci o aktivnosti bolesti prikupljeni su korišćenjem SLEDAI-2K indeksa. Rezultati su pokazali značajno snižene skorove na domenima fizičkog funkcionisanja (srednja vrednost 48,3 ± 18,6) i vitalnosti (42,1 ± 16,9) u poređenju sa srpskom opštom populacijom. Korelacija između SLEDAI-2K i fizičke komponente SF-36 bila je umerena (r = −0,44, p < 0,01), dok mentalna komponenta nije pokazala statistički značajnu vezu s aktivnošću bolesti. Studija ukazuje na potrebu za rutinskim merenjem HRQoL u kliničkoj praksi kod obolelih od SLE.

title: Depressive symptoms in female patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: prevalence and association with disease activity
abstract: Depression is frequently reported in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) but is often underdiagnosed in clinical settings. This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of depressive symptoms using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) in a cohort of 112 female SLE patients attending a tertiary rheumatology outpatient clinic in Novi Sad, Serbia, between 2015 and 2016. Disease activity was scored with SLEDAI-2K and organ damage with the SLICC/ACR Damage Index. Clinically significant depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥ 10) were found in 38.4% of participants. Multivariable logistic regression identified higher damage index scores (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.32–3.57), pain intensity (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.14–3.13) and unemployment (OR 2.44, 95% CI 1.21–4.93) as independent predictors of depression, whereas current SLEDAI-2K score was not a significant predictor after adjustment. These findings suggest that accumulated organ damage rather than acute disease activity drives psychological morbidity in this population, with implications for multidisciplinary care.
