title: Psihološki distres i strategije prevladavanja kod pacijenata sa sistemskim lupusom: kvalitativna studija
abstract: Ova kvalitativna studija istraživala je subjektivno iskustvo psihološkog distresa i strategija prevladavanja kod pacijenata sa SLE u Srbiji. Sprovedeni su polustrukturisani intervjui sa 22 pacijenta (19 žena, 3 muškarca) u periodu od oktobra do decembra 2017. godine. Intervjui su transkribovani i analizirani tematskom analizom prema Braun i Klarku. Identifikovane su četiri glavne teme: neizvesnost dijagnostičkog puta, gubitak uloga i identiteta, oslanjanje na neformalne socijalne mreže i ambivalentnost prema medicinskom sistemu. Pacijenti su navodili da prosečno čekaju 3,4 godine do postavljanja dijagnoze, što je opisivano kao posebno opterećujuće. Religijska prevladavanja bila su prominentna, naročito kod starijih ispitanika. Nalazi naglašavaju važnost uvođenja psihosocijalnih intervencija adaptiranih kulturnom kontekstu jugoistočne Evrope i ukazuju na nedovoljnu dostupnost psihoterapijske podrške u okviru reumatološke zdravstvene zaštite.

title: Validation of the Serbian-language version of the LupusQoL questionnaire
abstract: The LupusQoL is a disease-specific health-related quality of life instrument developed for use in SLE. This study reports the translation and psychometric validation of the Serbian-language version of LupusQoL. Forward–backward translation was performed according to established guidelines. The questionnaire was administered to 95 SLE patients (mean age 39.2 ± 12.7 years, 89 women) attending the rheumatology clinic in Novi Sad. Internal consistency was excellent for six of eight domains (Cronbach's α ranging from 0.81 to 0.93), with slightly lower values for the 'burden to others' domain (α = 0.74). Test–retest reliability over a two-week interval (n = 42) yielded intraclass correlation coefficients between 0.79 and 0.91. Convergent validity was supported by moderate-to-strong correlations with corresponding SF-36 domains (r = 0.51–0.77). Known-groups validity demonstrated lower scores in patients with SLEDAI-2K ≥ 6 compared to those with inactive disease (p < 0.01 for five domains). The Serbian LupusQoL is a reliable and valid instrument suitable for clinical research.

title: Fatigue u sistemskom lupusu eritematozusu: prevalencija i korelati u uzorku iz Zapadnog Balkana
abstract: Umor (fatigue) predstavlja jedan od najčešćih i najonesposobljavajućih simptoma SLE, ali ostaje nedovoljno istražen u regionu Zapadnog Balkana. U ovoj studiji preseka primenjen je Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) na uzorku od 134 pacijenta s potvrđenom dijagnozom SLE iz tri centra — Novog Sada, Beograda i Sarajeva — u periodu 2020–2021. godine. Klinički značajan umor (FSS ≥ 4) prijavilo je 67,2% ispitanika. Multivarijantna regresiona analiza identifikovala je anksioznost (GAD-7 skor, β = 0,31, p < 0,001), poremećaj spavanja (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index > 5, OR 3,12) i broj bolnih zglobova (β = 0,22, p < 0,01) kao nezavisne prediktore umora, dok aktivnost bolesti i hematološki parametri nisu bili statistički značajni prediktori. Rezultati sugerišu da intervencije usmerene na psihološke faktore i higijenu spavanja mogu biti efikasnije u redukciji umora nego isključivo farmakološka kontrola aktivnosti bolesti.

title: Health-related quality of life in systemic lupus erythematosus across the Western Balkans: a multicentre cross-sectional comparison with rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Few studies have directly compared health-related quality of life (HRQoL) between patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and those with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in Southeastern Europe. This multicentre study recruited 161 SLE patients and 158 RA patients from centres in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia between 2021 and 2022. HRQoL was measured with LupusQoL (SLE group) and RAQoL (RA group); SF-36 was administered to both groups to enable cross-condition comparison. SLE patients scored significantly lower on the SF-36 mental health component (mean 43.1 ± 14.3) compared to RA patients (mean 48.7 ± 13.1, p = 0.003), whereas physical component scores did not differ significantly (p = 0.21). Social functioning and emotional role limitations were the SF-36 domains with the greatest deficits in SLE. Younger age at diagnosis, female sex and unemployment were independently associated with worse mental HRQoL in SLE. These results highlight a distinct psychological morbidity profile in SLE relative to RA in this region.

title: Longitudinal changes in anxiety and depression among SLE patients during a two-year follow-up: results from the NovSLE registry
abstract: Longitudinal data on the trajectory of psychiatric comorbidities in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) remain scarce, particularly from Central and Eastern Europe. We analysed data from 87 SLE patients enrolled in the NovSLE registry at the University Clinical Centre of Vojvodina who completed PHQ-9 and GAD-7 assessments at baseline, 12 months and 24 months between 2021 and 2024. Linear mixed-effects models were used to estimate change over time, adjusting for disease activity, corticosteroid dose and sociodemographic variables. Mean PHQ-9 scores decreased modestly from 8.4 (±5.1) at baseline to 7.1 (±4.8) at 24 months (β = −0.64 per year, p = 0.03). GAD-7 scores showed no significant change (p = 0.18). Subgroup analysis revealed that patients who initiated hydroxychloroquine during the follow-up period showed greater reductions in both PHQ-9 (β = −1.82, p = 0.01) and GAD-7 (β = −1.34, p = 0.04) compared to those with no change in therapy. Findings support prospective psychiatric monitoring as a standard component of SLE management.

title: Socioekonomski determinanti psihološkog opterećenja kod pacijenata sa SLE u Srbiji: analiza podataka nacionalnog registra
abstract: Socioekonomski faktori imaju dokazanu ulogu u ishodima hroničnih bolesti, ali njihov doprinos psihološkom opterećenju kod SLE pacijenata u tranzicionim društvima ostaje nedovoljno dokumentovan. U ovoj studiji analizirani su podaci 203 pacijenta sa SLE iz srpskog nacionalnog reumatološkog registra za period 2019–2023. Psihološko opterećenje mereno je kompozitnim skorom koji integriše PHQ-9, GAD-7 i dimenziju emocionalnog zdravlja iz LupusQoL. Višestruka linearna regresija pokazala je da nezaposlenost (β = 0,29, p < 0,001), nivo obrazovanja niži od srednje škole (β = 0,18, p = 0,008) i ruralna sredina stanovanja (β = 0,14, p = 0,031) nezavisno doprinose višem psihološkom opterećenju, čak i nakon kontrole aktivnosti bolesti i oštećenja organa. Finansijsko opterećenje uzrokovano troškovima lečenja koreliralo je s psihološkim ishodom (r = 0,38, p < 0,001). Nalazi naglašavaju potrebu za sistemskom integracijom socijalne podrške u zbrinjavanju pacijenata s autoimunim bolestima.

title: Population decline in small Vojvodina settlements, 1991–2011: patterns and differentials
abstract: This study examined demographic trends in 199 settlements with fewer than 500 inhabitants in Vojvodina using data from the 1991, 2002, and 2011 Serbian national censuses. Age structure indices, natural population change rates, and net migration balances were calculated for each settlement. Results showed that 74 percent of the sampled settlements recorded continuous population decline across all three inter-census periods, with the steepest losses concentrated in the Banat subregion. The share of residents aged 65 and above exceeded 30 percent in 41 settlements by 2011, compared with 18 percent in 1991. Multivariate regression identified distance from a district centre, absence of a primary school, and reliance on livestock farming as significant predictors of accelerated decline. The paper concludes that demographic momentum in these communities is sufficiently negative that recovery without targeted in-migration policy is unlikely within a 20-year horizon.

title: Agricultural land use change in depopulated Vojvodina villages: a GIS analysis of cadastral and CORINE data, 2000–2012
abstract: The study combined Serbian cadastral records with CORINE Land Cover data for the years 2000, 2006, and 2012 to track transitions in land use across 48 villages that had lost more than 15 percent of their population between 1991 and 2011. Using change-detection matrices in ArcGIS, the analysis quantified shifts from arable land to fallow, grassland, and scrub. Across the study villages, approximately 8,400 hectares—representing 11.3 percent of total agricultural area—transitioned away from active cultivation over the 12-year period. Fallow expansion was highest in villages with fewer than 150 remaining residents. Spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.61) indicated strong clustering of abandonment in the north-eastern Banat zone. The findings challenge the prevailing assumption that large-scale farm consolidation after 2000 fully compensated for smallholder withdrawal from production.

title: Reasons for leaving and intentions to return: a household survey of former residents of declining Bačka villages
abstract: Structured face-to-face interviews were conducted with 312 individuals who had emigrated from 22 villages in Bačka to Novi Sad or Subotica between 2000 and 2015. The questionnaire covered stated reasons for migration, housing and land tenure status in the origin village, contact frequency with remaining residents, and stated probability of return. Employment-related motives dominated (67 percent of respondents), followed by educational access (48 percent) and dissatisfaction with rural services (31 percent); responses were not mutually exclusive. Only 9 percent stated a high probability of permanent return, though 38 percent indicated interest in seasonal or part-time presence if suitable income opportunities existed. Logistic regression showed that retaining agricultural land ownership significantly increased the odds of expressed return intention (OR = 2.4, 95% CI 1.6–3.6). The study highlights a potential but unrealised counter-urbanisation pool dependent largely on economic rather than amenity factors.

title: Post-socialist agrarian restructuring and smallholder exit in Serbia: a comparative village case study
abstract: Three Vojvodina villages—selected to represent high, medium, and low rates of land abandonment—were studied through mixed methods between 2014 and 2016. In each village, all households with agricultural holdings were enumerated using municipal tax records; 84 of 197 eligible households agreed to extended interviews covering farm size, labour inputs, subsidy uptake, and succession plans. The comparison revealed that villages with high abandonment rates had significantly lower rates of subsidy application (12 percent vs. 41 percent in low-abandonment villages), and that the median age of the primary farm operator was 71 years. Lease markets were nearly absent in high-abandonment villages despite formal land availability, pointing to transaction-cost and information barriers rather than purely demographic constraints. The chapter situates these findings within the broader literature on post-socialist agrarian dualism in Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Drone-assisted mapping of abandoned parcels in a peripheral Banat municipality
abstract: This methodological paper reports on a pilot workflow for identifying and classifying abandoned agricultural parcels using a DJI Phantom 4 Pro drone and supervised image classification. The study area was the municipality of Novi Bečej, covering approximately 6,200 hectares of agricultural land, flown in three campaigns during the 2018 growing season. Orthomosaic images at 8 cm ground resolution were classified into active arable, fallow, unkempt orchard, and non-agricultural categories using a random forest classifier trained on 430 ground-truth points. Overall classification accuracy was 88.2 percent (kappa = 0.84). The mapped fallow fraction (14.7 percent) was substantially higher than the figure derived from cadastral records (6.1 percent), suggesting that administrative data systematically undercount abandonment. The paper discusses the operational cost and logistical constraints of scaling the approach across the full Banat region.

title: Elderly residents as land custodians in shrinking Vojvodina villages: tenure behaviour and landscape outcomes
abstract: Drawing on 186 in-depth interviews conducted in 2018 across nine villages where residents aged 60 and above constituted more than half the population, this study examined how elderly households managed inherited and self-acquired agricultural land. Four tenure strategies were identified: continued self-cultivation (22 percent), informal lease to neighbours or relatives (38 percent), formal lease to corporate farms (19 percent), and effective abandonment with nominal ownership retention (21 percent). Informal arrangements predominated in villages further from road infrastructure and with weaker local land markets. Landscape-consequence mapping using Google Earth time series showed that parcels held under abandonment strategy had a 78 percent probability of transitioning to scrub vegetation within five years. The study argues that elderly tenure behaviour is an under-examined driver of the patchwork abandonment pattern visible across Vojvodina's peripheral landscapes.

title: Comparing depopulation trajectories across the Hungarian–Serbian border zone using harmonised census data
abstract: The Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia programme area contains a demographically fragile zone on both sides of the border where population loss has accelerated since the early 1990s. This paper harmonised settlement-level census data from Hungary (1990, 2001, 2011) and Serbia (1991, 2002, 2011) for 386 settlements within 30 km of the border, adjusting for differing administrative boundaries using dasymetric interpolation. Results showed broadly parallel decline trajectories but with Serbian settlements exhibiting steeper loss rates (mean –28 percent vs. –19 percent over 20 years). Cross-border differences in retirement income security, healthcare access, and land restitution outcomes were identified as institutional factors moderating local depopulation speeds. The paper proposes a joint monitoring framework using shared geodata infrastructure as a basis for coordinated rural development programming.

title: Village service closure sequences and their relationship to population loss: evidence from 127 Vojvodina settlements, 1990–2020
abstract: Using municipal administrative records supplemented by newspaper archives, this study reconstructed the closure dates of six key local services—primary school, postal outlet, general practitioner, pharmacy, retail food shop, and Orthodox or Catholic church congregation—across 127 Vojvodina settlements over the period 1990–2020. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis revealed that primary school closure was the most predictive event for subsequent accelerated depopulation, with settlements losing their school showing a hazard ratio of 2.7 for exceeding a 30 percent population loss threshold within the following decade compared with those retaining a school. Service closures tended to cluster within three-year windows, suggesting threshold dynamics rather than gradual linear deterioration. The analysis draws on a newly compiled dataset that is made available as a supplementary file and may serve as a baseline for monitoring rural service accessibility in the province.

title: Seasonal and temporary uses of abandoned rural properties: a typology from Srem
abstract: Rather than treating abandonment as a binary end-state, this paper investigates partial and intermittent uses of nominally abandoned residential and agricultural properties in 14 villages in the Srem subregion of Vojvodina. Data were collected through repeat visits (spring and autumn 2021 and 2022), property-owner interviews (n = 94), and cadastral cross-referencing. Five use types were identified: uninhabited but maintained family heritage property, seasonal vegetable garden maintained by urban relatives, informal grazing by neighbouring livestock keepers, hunter or angler seasonal lodging, and fully derelict with no use. Seasonal vegetable gardening was most common (39 percent of sampled properties) and showed a measurable landscape-maintenance function, keeping vegetation cover controlled on approximately 340 surveyed parcels. The typology suggests that simple vacancy statistics misrepresent the functional complexity of the shrinkage process.

title: The 2022 Serbian census in Vojvodina's smallest settlements: preliminary observations on continued demographic erosion
abstract: This short communication analyses preliminary results from the 2022 Serbian national census for the 234 Vojvodina settlements with fewer than 300 inhabitants, comparing figures with the 2011 census. Aggregate population in these settlements fell by 31.4 percent over the decade, a steeper rate than in the 2001–2011 period (22.8 percent). Seventeen settlements recorded zero or only one or two residents, compared with nine in 2011. The median age in the cohort rose from 58 to 67 years. The note cautions against over-interpreting preliminary figures pending full age-disaggregated data release, but argues that the broad direction is unambiguous and warrants immediate revision of provincial spatial planning assumptions that were based on more optimistic demographic projections. A follow-up full analysis is in preparation pending release of complete microdata.

title: Can agri-tourism slow depopulation? Household-level evidence from three Vojvodina villages with active rural tourism programmes
abstract: Three villages in Vojvodina that had established registered rural tourism operations by 2015 were selected as cases for evaluating whether tourism income affected household migration intentions and land management decisions. Between 2022 and 2024, the research team conducted 138 household interviews covering income sources, agricultural activity levels, and five-year migration intentions, plus a comparative cohort of 102 households in three matched non-tourism villages. Households with any tourism income were significantly less likely to express emigration intentions (OR = 0.38, 95% CI 0.22–0.66) and more likely to maintain or expand agricultural activity. However, tourism income was highly concentrated: the top 20 percent of tourism-active households accounted for 71 percent of total tourism revenue in their villages. The paper concludes that agri-tourism has a real but spatially and socially uneven stabilising effect, and that its potential as a generic depopulation remedy is limited without complementary infrastructure investment.

title: Mapping abandonment risk in Vojvodina: a predictive spatial model combining demographic, economic and land-quality indicators
abstract: This preprint presents a spatial risk model for agricultural land abandonment across all 460 Vojvodina settlements, combining 14 predictor variables drawn from the 2022 census, the 2023 Farm Structure Survey, cadastral parcel-size indices, soil quality class data, and road-network accessibility metrics. A gradient boosting classifier trained on a labelled dataset of 1,240 parcels observed via drone and satellite time series between 2015 and 2024 achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.87 on a held-out test set. Variable importance analysis ranked elderly operator share (>65 years), mean parcel size below 0.5 hectares, and distance to the nearest asphalt road as the three strongest predictors. The resulting abandonment-risk raster at 100 m resolution is provided as an open dataset. The model is intended as a planning tool for the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture and can be updated as new census and remote-sensing data become available.

title: Cross-border cycling route development in the Hungary–Serbia borderland: stakeholder perceptions and institutional obstacles
abstract: This paper reports on qualitative research conducted within the Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia programme area, focusing on the processes by which cross-border cycling routes are planned, approved, and maintained. Between 2021 and 2022, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 32 stakeholders including municipal planners, regional tourism organisations, national park administrators, and NGO representatives on both sides of the border. Interview transcripts were coded thematically using NVivo. Recurring themes included asymmetric funding cycles between the two countries, unclear maintenance responsibilities for transboundary route segments, and divergent signage standards that confuse long-distance cyclists. Positive outcomes associated with informal professional networks and bilateral municipal partnerships were also documented. The paper contributes to the literature on cross-border governance in post-enlargement EU borderlands and offers a set of procedural recommendations for future route development projects in the region.

title: Oxygen permeability of biaxially oriented polypropylene films: effect of draw ratio and crystalline lamellar thickness
abstract: Biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films prepared at draw ratios of 5×5 to 9×9 were characterised for oxygen transmission rate (OTR) using a coulometric sensor method at 23 °C and 0 % relative humidity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering confirmed an increase in crystallinity from 42 % to 61 % with rising draw ratio. OTR values decreased from 1840 to 890 cm³/(m²·day·bar) over the same range. DSC measurements showed that lamellar thickness, as estimated by the Thomson–Gibbs equation, increased from 8.2 to 14.7 nm. A linear correlation was established between the reciprocal of lamellar thickness and OTR, consistent with a tortuous-path diffusion model. FTIR-ATR band ratios at 998/973 cm⁻¹ were used as an independent crystallinity index and agreed within 4 % with WAXS results. The findings provide quantitative guidance for process optimisation of BOPP films where oxygen barrier is the primary constraint.

title: Water vapour transmission through polyethylene/tie-layer/polyamide-6 coextruded films: influence of tie-layer thickness
abstract: Three-layer cast films comprising linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE), maleic-anhydride-grafted polyethylene as a tie layer, and polyamide-6 (PA6) as a barrier layer were produced by blown coextrusion. Total film thickness was held constant at 80 µm while the tie-layer fraction was varied from 5 % to 25 % of total thickness. Water vapour transmission rate (WVTR) was measured at 38 °C and 90 % RH. An increase in tie-layer fraction from 5 % to 25 % raised WVTR from 4.1 to 7.8 g/(m²·day). FTIR mapping in cross-section confirmed tie-layer uniformity and the absence of delamination. Peel adhesion tests recorded values between 3.2 and 5.8 N/15 mm depending on tie-layer content. The results demonstrate that the tie layer, while necessary for adhesion, acts as a permeability penalty that must be balanced against structural integrity requirements in food packaging design.

title: Temperature dependence of oxygen permeability in LLDPE films: activation energy and free-volume analysis
abstract: Oxygen transmission rate was measured on commercial and laboratory-cast LLDPE films of three densities (0.918, 0.924, 0.932 g/cm³) across a temperature range of 5 °C to 50 °C. Arrhenius plots were constructed from OTR data collected at seven temperature points; activation energies for permeation ranged from 28.4 to 41.7 kJ/mol and increased with film density, in line with reduced chain mobility at higher crystallinity. Positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy (PALS) performed in collaboration with a partner institution provided free-volume hole radius estimates of 0.26–0.31 nm at 23 °C. A positive correlation (R² = 0.91) between hole radius and permeability coefficient was observed. Pre-exponential diffusivity factors derived from the Arrhenius fits correlated with crystallinity index from DSC. These data are intended as reference parameters for shelf-life modelling of chilled food products stored at variable temperatures.

title: Barrier performance of metallised polypropylene films as a function of optical density and post-metallisation ageing
abstract: Commercially metallised cast polypropylene (CPP) films with aluminium optical densities ranging from 2.1 to 3.6 were characterised for OTR and WVTR immediately after production and after 90-day ambient storage. At optical density 3.6, OTR was 4 cm³/(m²·day·bar) and WVTR was 0.18 g/(m²·day) immediately after metallisation. After 90 days these rose by 18 % and 24 % respectively. SEM cross-sections and atomic force microscopy revealed microcrack formation in the aluminium layer, with crack density correlating with ageing-induced OTR increase (R² = 0.87). Corona pre-treatment level (measured by contact angle) did not significantly affect initial barrier but reduced the rate of crack formation during ageing by approximately 30 %. The study provides quantitative ageing coefficients applicable to worst-case shelf-life calculations for hermetically sealed snack products.

title: Barrier properties of oriented polyethylene terephthalate/polyolefin laminates: delamination as a barrier failure mechanism
abstract: Biaxially oriented PET films laminated to LLDPE with solvent-based adhesive were stressed by repeated flexing (0, 100, 500, and 1000 flex cycles, Gelbo Flex tester) and characterised for OTR and peel strength. After 1000 flex cycles OTR increased from 8 to 67 cm³/(m²·day·bar) while peel force fell from 2.4 to 0.6 N/15 mm. Optical microscopy of laminates cross-sectioned after flexing showed progressive adhesive fracture at the PET–adhesive interface rather than within bulk layers. Energy-dispersive X-ray analysis confirmed adhesive residue remained on the LLDPE side post-delamination. A fracture energy model was applied to estimate critical debond propagation stress, yielding values of 180–240 J/m² consistent with literature for epoxy-bonded film laminates. The contribution of adhesive bond integrity to overall oxygen barrier is quantified and compared with contributions from individual plies.

title: Effect of processing temperature on crystalline morphology and gas barrier of high-density polyethylene blown films
abstract: High-density polyethylene (HDPE, MFI 0.9 g/10 min, density 0.961 g/cm³) was blown into films at die temperatures of 170, 190, 210 and 230 °C with blow-up ratios of 2.0 and 3.0. OTR and WVTR were measured at standard conditions; DSC, WAXS and polarised optical microscopy were applied to characterise crystalline morphology. At 170 °C die temperature and BUR 3.0 the lowest OTR of 310 cm³/(m²·day·bar) was obtained, corresponding to peak crystallinity of 71 %. Increasing die temperature to 230 °C raised OTR to 480 cm³/(m²·day·bar) at the same BUR, attributed to reduced nucleation density and larger spherulite size (mean diameter 9.4 µm vs. 4.1 µm at 170 °C). Shrinkage data at 80 °C showed a trade-off: films with the best barrier had 12 % higher transverse shrinkage. Findings are relevant to dairy and industrial liner applications where stiffness and barrier must be jointly optimised.

title: Passive layer-by-layer assembly of polyelectrolyte coatings on polyolefin films for oxygen barrier enhancement
abstract: Alternating layers of poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDADMAC) and poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) (PSS) were deposited on corona-treated LLDPE substrates via dip-coating at pH 4.0 and ionic strength 0.1 M NaCl. Films with 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 bilayers were produced and OTR measured at 23 °C and 50 % RH. OTR decreased from 1720 cm³/(m²·day·bar) for uncoated LLDPE to 210 cm³/(m²·day·bar) at 20 bilayers; total coating thickness was 380 nm by profilometry. Adhesion of the coating was assessed by tape-peel and cross-cut tests; failure occurred at the coating–substrate interface for samples with fewer than 8 bilayers, suggesting inadequate corona treatment recovery. Humid ageing at 85 % RH for 14 days caused an OTR increase of 35 % at 20 bilayers. The coating approach is positioned as an EVOH-free route to moderate oxygen barrier on flexible polyolefin substrates.

title: Permeability of ethylene–methyl acrylate copolymer films to a six-gas mixture: oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, argon, ethylene and water vapour
abstract: Ethylene–methyl acrylate copolymer (EMA, 18 % acrylate content) films of 50, 100 and 150 µm thickness were characterised for permeability to six gases individually using certified reference gas mixtures. Measurements covered 5–40 °C. Permeability coefficients at 23 °C ranged from 1.8 × 10⁻¹³ cm³·cm/(cm²·s·Pa) for N₂ to 9.4 × 10⁻¹² cm³·cm/(cm²·s·Pa) for water vapour. Ideal selectivity α(CO₂/O₂) was 4.1 at 23 °C and rose to 5.3 at 5 °C, indicating temperature as a practical tuning parameter for modified-atmosphere applications. Diffusivity and solubility coefficients were separated by a time-lag method; solubility dominated differences between gases in this amorphous-rich copolymer. Thickness had no measurable effect on permeability coefficient, confirming film homogeneity. The dataset is intended as a reference for EMA-based packaging design in fresh-produce and cut-flower applications requiring controlled atmosphere.

title: Characterisation of amorphous polyethylene terephthalate as a barrier component in mono-material polyolefin packaging: a feasibility study
abstract: Amorphous PET (APET) plies of 10, 20 and 30 µm were coextruded with LLDPE in five-layer configurations (LLDPE/tie/APET/tie/LLDPE) to explore whether a non-stretched PET layer can fulfil moderate barrier requirements without requiring separate recycling streams. OTR at 23 °C for the 30 µm APET configuration was 42 cm³/(m²·day·bar), against 1740 cm³/(m²·day·bar) for the LLDPE control. DSC of the PET layer in the coextrudate confirmed the absence of crystallisation during extrusion. Recycling compatibility was assessed by melt-mixing coextrudate strips with HDPE and PE recyclate at 5 % and 10 % PET contamination; OTR of remoulded plaques was not meaningfully different from the PE control, and visual transparency was adequate. Mechanical tests on coextruded films showed elongation at break above 350 % in all configurations. The study is framed as preliminary data for a broader mono-material high-barrier packaging development programme.

title: Pinhole density and oxygen transmission rate in thin polyolefin coextruded films: a statistical correlation across production batches
abstract: A dataset of 214 production batches of three-layer LLDPE/mLLDPE/LLDPE cast films (40–80 µm) collected over 18 months from an industrial film producer was analysed to establish a statistical relationship between pinhole density (measured by electrical discharge imaging) and OTR. Pinhole density ranged from 0 to 8 pinholes/m² and OTR ranged from 1600 to 3100 cm³/(m²·day·bar). A linear regression model explained 61 % of OTR variance (R² = 0.61) using pinhole density as the sole predictor; inclusion of film thickness, extrusion speed and melt temperature raised R² to 0.79. Films with zero pinholes showed an OTR range of 1580–1980 cm³/(m²·day·bar), confirming that pinhole-free conditions alone do not guarantee low OTR. These findings are communicated to the production partner as a quality-control decision tool. The methodology is generic and applicable to other thin film geometries.

title: Silica nanoplatelet aspect ratio as a determinant of oxygen barrier in polyethylene nanocomposite films
abstract: Synthetic hectorite and two aspect-ratio variants of synthetic fluoromica (mean platelet diameter 200 nm and 800 nm) were melt-compounded into LLDPE at loadings of 1, 3 and 5 wt% using a twin-screw extruder. Films were cast at 150 µm. TEM confirmed platelet exfoliation at 1 wt% and partial aggregation at 5 wt% for both fillers. OTR at 23 °C and 0 % RH was reduced from 1700 cm³/(m²·day·bar) in neat LLDPE to 840 cm³/(m²·day·bar) at 3 wt% 800 nm fluoromica. The Nielsen tortuosity model predicted OTR reductions of 32–48 % across conditions; experimentally achieved reductions were 18–51 %, with best agreement at intermediate loadings where exfoliation was most complete. Tensile modulus increased from 210 to 340 MPa at 5 wt% loading while elongation at break fell from 610 % to 290 %. The results quantify the aspect-ratio advantage but highlight a dispersion challenge at loadings above 3 wt%.

title: Water vapour permeability of cyclic olefin copolymer/polyolefin blend films across a humidity gradient: temperature sensitivity and dew-point effects
abstract: Films of cyclic olefin copolymer (COC, Tg 78 °C) blended with LLDPE at COC mass fractions of 0, 10, 20 and 30 % were prepared by blown film extrusion at 220 °C. WVTR was measured at 23 °C and 38 °C with humidity gradients of 0–50 %, 0–75 % and 0–90 % RH on the downstream face. At 30 % COC and 38 °C, WVTR was 1.1 g/(m²·day) against 4.4 g/(m²·day) for neat LLDPE under 0–90 % gradient, corresponding to a 75 % reduction. DSC showed no co-crystallisation, and SEM of cryo-fracture surfaces revealed COC-rich domains of 0.8–2.4 µm acting as dispersed impermeable inclusions. Activation energy for water vapour permeation increased from 22 kJ/mol in LLDPE to 31 kJ/mol at 30 % COC. Films were free-standing and optically clear up to 20 % COC. The humidity-gradient sensitivity of WVTR reduction is discussed in the context of flexible pharmaceutical blister packaging.

title: Comparative assessment of EIS and harmonic analysis for corrosion rate determination on carbon steel in saline soil electrolytes
abstract: This conference contribution presents a comparison of three electrochemical methods—linear polarisation resistance, EIS with equivalent circuit fitting, and second-harmonic nonlinear analysis—for determining corrosion rates of carbon steel in three saline soil electrolytes (0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 mol/L NaCl). Experiments were conducted on cylindrical electrodes embedded in compacted soil specimens to approach realistic geometry. EIS-derived Rp values agreed with LPR values within ±12% at all concentrations. Second-harmonic analysis provided Tafel slope estimates without requiring large-amplitude perturbation, yielding βa and βc values within 8 mV/decade of those from full Tafel extrapolation. Gravimetric confirmation after 30-day burial showed that EIS-based estimates were closer to the true mass-loss corrosion rate (mean relative error 9%) than LPR-based estimates (mean relative error 18%). The study supports EIS as a preferred in situ measurement approach for buried electrode applications.

title: Influence of grammage and recycled-fibre content on the moisture-barrier efficiency of extrusion-coated board
abstract: Six paperboard grades ranging from 200 to 400 g/m² and recycled fibre contents between 0 % and 100 % were extrusion-coated with LDPE at nominal add-on weights of 15 and 25 g/m². WVTR, Cobb60 water absorption, and cross-sectional void area (evaluated from polished cross-section SEM images at 500× magnification) were measured before and after coating. Statistical analysis by multiple linear regression identified recycled-fibre content as the strongest predictor of post-coating WVTR (standardised coefficient β = 0.61), followed by substrate grammage (β = −0.34) and LDPE add-on weight (β = −0.44). Substrates with ≥60 % recycled content exhibited surface pore areas up to 4.1 % (cross-section), causing pin-hole formation in the LDPE film at 15 g/m² add-on. Increasing add-on to 25 g/m² reduced WVTR to levels comparable to virgin-fibre boards but introduced a 40 % cost premium. A decision matrix linking substrate quality, add-on weight, and required WVTR threshold is provided.

title: Molecular weight distribution broadening in polypropylene recyclate blends: effect of virgin material addition ratios
abstract: Post-industrial polypropylene recyclate (five prior processing cycles) was blended with virgin iPP at ratios of 100:0, 75:25, 50:50 and 25:75 (recyclate:virgin by weight) and compounded on a co-rotating twin-screw extruder. GPC analysis showed that adding 25 wt % virgin PP narrowed the dispersity index Đ from 5.8 (pure recyclate) to 4.6, and 50 wt % addition brought it to 3.9, approaching the virgin value of 3.3. Izod impact strength scaled nearly linearly with virgin content, recovering from 18 kJ/m² (pure recyclate) to 34 kJ/m² (50:50 blend) and 42 kJ/m² (25:75 blend). Heat deflection temperature was largely insensitive to blend ratio, remaining between 91 °C and 94 °C. The results quantify the performance recovery achievable at different levels of virgin polymer dilution, providing guidance for down-cycling decisions.

title: Grain refinement with Al–5Ti–1B master alloy and its effect on SDAS and macrosegregation in DC-cast AA6082 billets
abstract: The influence of Al–5Ti–1B grain refiner additions (0, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 kg/tonne) on grain size, secondary dendrite arm spacing, and radial macrosegregation was quantified in 178 mm diameter AA6082 billets cast at 70 mm/min. Grain size was measured by polarised-light microscopy after Barker anodising; mean grain diameter decreased from 1840 µm in the unrefined billet to 290 µm at 2.0 kg/tonne addition. SDAS was reduced by 18% at the centreline and 11% at the mid-radius at the highest refiner addition. Radial magnesium segregation index (ratio of centreline to edge concentration) decreased from 1.09 to 1.04 with increasing refiner content, suggesting that equiaxed grain structure suppresses interdendritic flow channels. Manganese and chromium radial distributions showed no statistically significant response to grain refinement within the scatter of the measurements.

title: Three-dimensional simulation of thermosolutal convection and macrosegregation in a 250 mm DC-cast billet: effect of casting tilt on solute symmetry
abstract: A three-dimensional finite-volume model was applied to simulate DC casting of a 250 mm diameter AA7050 billet at a 2° axial tilt relative to vertical, motivated by a practical scenario of minor misalignment in industrial practice. The governing equations included momentum (Darcy-penalised Navier–Stokes), energy, and solute transport for Zn and Cu as the primary segregating elements. The mesh comprised 1.2 million hexahedral cells; steady-state was approached after 400 s simulated time on a 48-core cluster requiring approximately 31 hours wall-clock time. Tilt introduced a measurable asymmetry in the Zn distribution: the high side of the billet showed a centreline Zn concentration 0.23 wt% above the low side. Predicted radial macrosegregation profiles on the vertical plane of symmetry agreed with XRF measurements from a plant trial billet to within 0.3 wt% Zn across the radius.

title: Probabilistic fatigue life assessment of single-lap bolted joints under combined axial and shear loading using Monte Carlo simulation
abstract: This paper presents a probabilistic framework for estimating the fatigue life of single-lap bolted joints fabricated from 7075-T6 aluminium alloy, a common aerospace structural material. The joint geometry and loading conditions were parameterised to reflect realistic scatter in bolt preload (coefficient of variation 8%), hole clearance (±0.02 mm tolerance band), and applied load amplitude (coefficient of variation 12%). A total of 50 000 Monte Carlo realisations were conducted using a two-stage damage model that separates crack initiation at the bolt hole edge from propagation to a critical crack length of 2.5 mm. The stress state at the critical cross-section was computed using a validated finite element model in Abaqus 2021, with surrogate response surfaces constructed via polynomial chaos expansion to reduce computational cost. Results show that the coefficient of variation in predicted fatigue life reaches 34% under combined loading, compared with 21% under pure axial loading, highlighting the strong influence of shear-induced fretting on scatter. The predicted median life of 1.2 × 10^5 cycles at a reference load of 18 kN agreed with experimental data from 24 coupon tests within ±15%. Sensitivity analysis identified bolt preload as the dominant uncertainty contributor, accounting for approximately 47% of total output variance.

title: Effect of hole-diameter tolerance on failure probability of riveted lap joints: a parametric importance-sampling study
abstract: Hole-diameter tolerance is a key manufacturing parameter in riveted aerospace joints because it governs rivet fill, residual stress distribution after installation, and the onset of fretting at faying surfaces. This study quantifies its influence on the probability of fatigue failure using importance sampling centred on the design point identified by first-order reliability method (FORM). Three aluminium alloy sheet thicknesses (1.0, 1.6, and 2.0 mm, 2024-T3) and two rivet materials (monel and aluminium-alloy rivets) were considered in a full factorial arrangement, yielding 18 joint configurations. For each configuration, 5 000 importance-sampling realisations were drawn, requiring roughly one-tenth the computational effort of equivalent crude Monte Carlo runs at the same coefficient of variation of the failure probability estimate. Hole-diameter tolerance was modelled as a truncated normal distribution with standard deviation 0.015 mm. Results indicate that a one-standard-deviation increase in hole diameter scatter raises the probability of fatigue failure by a factor of 2.1 to 3.4 depending on sheet thickness, with thinner sheets showing greater sensitivity. Residual stress fields measured by X-ray diffraction on ten additional specimens corroborated the finite element predictions to within 9%. The findings suggest tighter tolerance specifications (IT6 rather than IT7) are warranted for joints exposed to cyclic loads exceeding 60% of the static shear allowable.

title: Reliability-based optimisation of bolt pattern geometry in multi-bolt flanged connections under bending and torsion
abstract: Flanged connections with multiple bolts appear widely in rotating machinery, pressure vessels, and aircraft structural frames, yet their optimisation under combined bending and torsion loading remains largely deterministic in current design standards. This paper formulates a reliability-based design optimisation (RBDO) problem in which bolt pitch circle diameter, number of bolts, and bolt nominal diameter are treated as design variables, while material yield strength, surface roughness, and applied moment amplitudes are modelled as random variables with distributions derived from a literature survey of 31 published datasets. The failure criterion combines bolt fatigue (using a modified Goodman diagram calibrated to ISO 898-1 grade 10.9) and flange yielding at the root fillet. The RBDO problem was solved using a sequential approximate optimisation loop coupling an inner FORM reliability analysis with a genetic algorithm for the outer optimisation. Three target reliability indices (β = 3.0, 3.5, 4.0) were explored. At β = 3.5, the optimised configuration reduced total bolt mass by 11% relative to a deterministic design sized to a safety factor of 2.5, while satisfying the probabilistic constraint. Validation against 16 experimental fatigue tests on scaled flanges showed that the predicted failure probability fell within the 90% confidence interval of the empirical estimate in 14 of 16 cases.
venue: Journal of Reliability Engineering and Machine Design

title: Comparative evaluation of circular and rectangular primary coil geometries for inductive power transfer in industrial floor-mounted charging stations
abstract: This paper compares circular and rectangular primary coil configurations for inductive power transfer (IPT) pads intended for stationary charging of automated guided vehicles (AGVs). A series of flat planar coils with outer dimensions ranging from 250 mm to 450 mm were wound from Litz wire and characterised using a programmable impedance analyser over 85–400 kHz. Finite-element simulations in FEMM 4.2 were cross-validated against measurements. At a nominal air gap of 15 mm, the rectangular coil achieved a coupling coefficient of 0.31 compared to 0.27 for the circular variant of equal conductor length, while the rectangular geometry exhibited 8% lower flux leakage outside the pad footprint. Transfer efficiency at 1 kW output reached 91.4% for the rectangular pad versus 89.6% for the circular one. Thermal images recorded after 30-minute continuous operation showed maximum winding temperatures of 54 °C and 61 °C respectively. The results suggest that rectangular coils are preferable when the AGV docking tolerance is constrained to ±10 mm laterally.

title: Impedance-based foreign-object detection in inductive charging pads: sensitivity to metallic contaminants of varying mass and position
abstract: Foreign metallic objects placed on or near an IPT pad can cause localised heating and represent a safety hazard in industrial environments. This paper investigates the use of reflected impedance changes as a low-cost detection mechanism, without dedicated additional sensor coils. A 300 W laboratory charging pad operating at 200 kHz was loaded with steel, aluminium, and copper coupons of masses 1–50 g placed at 16 positions across the pad surface. The transmitter-side input impedance was logged via a microcontroller-based monitoring circuit sampling at 10 kHz. Results show that the imaginary part of the input impedance shifts by at least 0.4 Ω for steel objects above 3 g at any pad position, while aluminium and copper require masses above 8 g for reliable detection at the pad periphery. A threshold-based detection algorithm achieved 94% sensitivity and 98% specificity across 512 controlled trials. False triggers caused by an AGV wheel rolling within 50 mm of the pad perimeter were below 2%. The approach requires no additional hardware beyond the existing resonant inverter measurement interface.

title: Resonant frequency drift in IPT pads under industrial floor temperature cycles: measurement and compensation strategy
abstract: Inductive charging pads installed in factory floors are exposed to temperature swings caused by forklift traffic, HVAC cycles, and production heat. This study quantifies how thermal cycling affects the resonant frequency of series-series compensated IPT pads and proposes a digital compensation scheme. Five identical 400 mm × 400 mm primary pads were subjected to temperature profiles from 10 °C to 65 °C in a climate chamber while resonant frequency and coupling coefficient were logged continuously. Resonant frequency shifted by up to 3.1 kHz across the tested range, predominantly due to capacitor dielectric coefficient variation. An FPGA-based phase-lock control loop was implemented on a Xilinx Spartan-6 development board to track the resonant frequency and adjust the inverter switching frequency accordingly. With compensation active, power delivery remained within ±1.8% of the 500 W setpoint across the full temperature range, compared with ±12.4% deviation in open-loop operation. Pad coupling coefficient was less sensitive to temperature, varying by only 1.3% over the same range.

title: Multi-coil primary pad topology for position-tolerant inductive charging of AGVs with ±30 mm docking uncertainty
abstract: Practical AGV docking systems exhibit positional uncertainty that degrades coupling and transfer efficiency in single-coil IPT pads. This work examines a segmented primary pad composed of four overlapping 200 mm × 200 mm sub-coils energised selectively based on secondary coil position estimated from reflected impedance signatures. Position estimation was performed using a lookup table trained on 144 measured impedance vectors distributed on a 12 × 12 grid with 10 mm spacing. The correct sub-coil combination was selected within 80 ms using a microcontroller running the lookup-table algorithm. At ±30 mm lateral offset, the four-coil topology maintained coupling coefficient above 0.25, compared with a single-coil baseline that dropped to 0.16 at the same offset. End-to-end efficiency at 800 W was 88.3% across the ±30 mm docking envelope versus 79.1% for the single-coil design. Hardware cost increase was estimated at 34% relative to the single-coil baseline, which is discussed in context of fleet operational savings.

title: Eddy-current loss modelling in aluminium AGV chassis plates placed over inductive charging pads
abstract: Aluminium structural plates forming the underside of AGV chassis are typically located 8–20 mm above floor-level IPT primary pads and can be significant sources of eddy-current losses. This study uses a three-dimensional finite-element model in COMSOL Multiphysics to quantify eddy-current power dissipation in flat aluminium plates of thicknesses 3, 6, and 10 mm as a function of operating frequency (85–300 kHz) and air gap. Simulated losses were validated against calorimetric measurements on three plates mounted over a laboratory pad. At 200 kHz and a 12 mm gap, a 6 mm plate dissipated 18.4 W from 500 W transferred, representing a 3.7% additional efficiency penalty. Increasing frequency to 300 kHz raised plate losses to 41.7 W under the same conditions. An empirical power-law fit relating dissipation to frequency and plate thickness is provided for use in system-level efficiency budgets. The results inform material selection guidelines recommending plate thicknesses below 4 mm when operating above 150 kHz.

title: Inductive power transfer for automated guided vehicles: system design considerations and standardisation landscape
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of IPT system design for AGV applications, covering coil topology selection, compensation network design, power electronics, foreign-object detection, and electromagnetic compatibility requirements. The chapter reviews the current state of IEC and ISO standardisation activities relevant to industrial IPT and identifies gaps between existing standard drafts and the operational requirements encountered in real logistics deployments. Design trade-offs are illustrated using data from a 1 kW prototype operated on a 40-metre test track at an academic laboratory. Particular attention is given to the interaction between charging pad placement density and fleet mission cycle optimisation. The chapter also discusses safety interlocking strategies for environments where human workers share floor space with AGVs. It is aimed at practicing engineers and graduate students entering the field and includes annotated references to primary literature published between 2005 and 2021.
venue: Handbook of Wireless Power Systems for Industrial Robotics (Springer, edited volume)

title: Simultaneous wireless power transfer and data communication over a shared inductive link for AGV status telemetry
abstract: Industrial AGVs require continuous status telemetry during charging intervals. This paper investigates frequency-division multiplexing of a 200 kHz power carrier and an 800 kHz data sub-carrier over a single inductive link using a shared pad structure. A custom analogue front end with a bandpass filter centred at 800 kHz was designed to extract the data signal at the secondary side without measurable interference with the power transfer stage. Data throughput of 38.4 kbit/s was achieved at a bit-error rate below 10⁻⁵ across the ±30 mm docking uncertainty envelope characterised in prior work. Power transfer efficiency was reduced by 0.9 percentage points relative to power-only operation at 800 W. Experiments were performed with a commercial 32-bit ARM microcontroller implementing a lightweight UART-over-inductive protocol. The approach eliminates the need for a separate near-field communication antenna on the pad assembly, reducing pad height by approximately 8 mm.

title: Machine-learning-assisted foreign-object classification in inductive charging pads using time-frequency features of primary-side current waveforms
abstract: This paper extends impedance-based foreign-object detection by applying short-time Fourier transform (STFT) features extracted from the primary-side current waveform as inputs to a random forest classifier. A dataset of 3 840 labelled events was collected using a 500 W laboratory pad loaded with 14 distinct object types including steel bolts, aluminium foil sheets, copper wire bundles, and wet cardboard, each placed at 20 pad positions. STFT windows of 2 ms duration at 10 MHz sampling yielded 48-dimensional feature vectors. A five-fold cross-validated random forest with 200 trees achieved 97.4% overall classification accuracy and distinguished metallic from non-metallic objects with 99.1% accuracy. Inference time on an ARM Cortex-M7 microcontroller was 11 ms per window, compatible with a 50 ms system response budget. False-positive rate in the presence of a correctly docked AGV was 0.4%. The dataset and feature extraction code are deposited in a public repository at the University of Novi Sad data portal.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Instrumentation and Measurement

title: Geometric parameter sensitivity analysis for DD and DDQ coil pads in 1–3 kW AGV inductive charging applications
abstract: Double-D (DD) and double-D quadrature (DDQ) coil topologies have been proposed for improved lateral tolerance and polarisation flexibility in IPT pads. This study performs a systematic sensitivity analysis of eight geometric parameters—wire pitch, outer pad dimension, D-coil overlap ratio, ferrite coverage area, and others—for both topologies at output powers of 1, 2, and 3 kW and operating frequencies of 85 and 150 kHz. A design-of-experiments approach using a Plackett-Burman screening matrix with 48 simulation runs per topology identified the three most influential parameters for coupling coefficient and efficiency: outer pad dimension, ferrite coverage ratio, and D-coil overlap. Surrogate response-surface models were fitted and used to locate Pareto-optimal designs balancing efficiency, pad weight, and manufacturing cost. The DDQ topology achieved coupling coefficients 12–18% higher than DD at ±25 mm lateral offset but required 31% more ferrite material by mass. Validated against twelve physical prototypes, the surrogate model predicted coupling coefficient within ±4%.

title: Fleet-level charging schedule optimisation for AGV systems with fixed inductive pad infrastructure: a mixed-integer linear programming approach
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of scheduling inductive charging events for a fleet of AGVs sharing a fixed set of floor-mounted IPT pads in a warehouse environment. A mixed-integer linear programme (MILP) is formulated that minimises total fleet idle time while satisfying mission deadlines, battery state-of-charge constraints, and single-occupancy constraints on each charging pad. Instance data were derived from a simulated 12-AGV, 8-pad warehouse layout with 480 mission tasks over an 8-hour shift, generated using a stochastic mission model calibrated to logged data from an academic test facility. The MILP was solved using the open-source HiGHS solver; instances with up to 12 AGVs and 8 pads solved to within 2% optimality gap in under 90 seconds on standard desktop hardware. A rolling-horizon implementation with a 15-minute planning window was tested in real-time simulation and maintained fleet utilisation above 83% compared with 71% for a first-come-first-served baseline. Sensitivity to pad charging power (500 W vs. 1 kW) is discussed.
venue: Robotics and Autonomous Systems

title: Thermal management of high-power density inductive charging pads embedded in industrial floor surfaces: a combined CFD and experimental study
abstract: As AGV fleet charging demands push pad power levels toward 3–5 kW, thermal management of floor-embedded IPT pads becomes a practical constraint. This preprint reports on a computational fluid dynamics model of heat dissipation from a 3 kW pad recessed 20 mm below a polyurethane-coated concrete floor, with natural convection to the underfloor cavity. The CFD model was developed in OpenFOAM and validated against thermocouple measurements at 12 locations on a laboratory-floor mock-up under continuous 3 kW operation over 90 minutes. Steady-state ferrite surface temperature reached 81 °C, 6 °C above the 75 °C design limit, indicating that passive cooling is insufficient at this power level without design modifications. Three mitigation strategies were evaluated: increasing the underfloor cavity height from 30 to 80 mm reduced peak temperature to 68 °C; adding a 2 mm aluminium thermal spreader reduced it to 72 °C; and reducing the duty cycle to 80% reduced it to 67 °C. The model is made available as a parameterised OpenFOAM case file.

title: Open-Source Real-Time Target Benchmarking for Automotive HIL: A Five-Year Longitudinal Study
abstract: This paper presents a longitudinal comparison of open-source real-time platforms evaluated in the authors' laboratory between 2019 and 2024, updating earlier single-point benchmarks with data from newer hardware generations and kernel versions. Platforms assessed include x86 mini-ITX systems, Raspberry Pi 3 and 4, Beaglebone AI-64, and Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC. For each platform, worst-case and mean task latency, model execution capacity (maximum state count at 1 ms step), CAN frame throughput, and approximate acquisition cost are tabulated. The dataset covers 14 440 individual measurement sessions totalling over 12 000 bench-hours. Results show that the Zynq UltraScale+ with a Xenomai partition achieves the best latency-to-cost ratio for step sizes at or above 0.5 ms, while x86 platforms retain an advantage for large model complexity. The paper identifies kernel version transitions and hardware errata that caused discontinuities in the latency data and documents the workarounds applied. All raw data and measurement scripts are provided in a public repository.
venue: Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems

title: Effect of conveyor vibration on sub-pixel barcode localisation accuracy: a frequency-domain analysis
abstract: Conveyor frames in food and pharmaceutical factories transmit vibration from motors and rollers to the belt surface, producing micro-displacements during image exposure that degrade barcode decode rates even when gross motion blur is controlled by strobe lighting. This study uses a laser vibrometer to characterise the dominant vibration frequencies (18–140 Hz) at six points on a standard roller conveyor under three load conditions. High-speed video at 2 000 fps was used to measure actual belt displacement amplitude during strobe flashes of 50, 100 and 200 µs duration. A simulation framework then predicts the resulting barcode element-width measurement error as a function of element width, exposure duration and vibration amplitude. Empirical decode-rate measurements across 7 200 trials confirmed the simulation predictions with a mean absolute error of 1.4 percentage points. The analysis provides a method for selecting strobe duration given a site vibration measurement, without requiring trial-and-error camera installation.

title: Butyrate supplementation increases colonic 5-HT content in conventionally raised Wistar rats fed a low-fibre diet
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids, particularly butyrate, have been proposed to stimulate enterochromaffin (EC) cell secretion, but quantitative data in dietary-restriction models remained sparse. We fed adult male Wistar rats (n=24) either a standard chow or a low-fibre diet for six weeks, with or without sodium butyrate supplementation in drinking water (100 mM). Colonic mucosal 5-HT was measured by HPLC-ECD and EC cell density by chromogranin A immunohistochemistry. Butyrate supplementation restored colonic 5-HT content to chow-fed levels (mean difference 38 ng/mg protein, 95% CI 22–54, p<0.001) and increased EC cell density by 21% in low-fibre animals. Faecal butyrate concentrations confirmed treatment compliance. Hippocampal 5-HT was unaffected at this supplementation duration, suggesting the central signal requires a longer exposure window. These findings support a direct trophic role of luminal butyrate on EC cell physiology under conditions of reduced fermentable substrate.

title: 16S rRNA profiling of caecal microbiota in germ-free versus conventionalised mice receiving propionate infusions
abstract: To isolate the contribution of propionate from the broader SCFA mixture, we colonised germ-free C57BL/6 mice (n=16) with a defined four-species consortium (Lactobacillus murinus, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, Ruminococcus gnavus, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii analogue) and performed intra-caecal propionate infusions (10 µmol/day) for 14 days. Caecal microbiota composition was characterised by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (V3–V4 region, Illumina MiSeq). Propionate infusion did not alter community diversity (Shannon index, p=0.41) but significantly upregulated mucosal Tph1 mRNA expression (2.3-fold, p=0.008) and increased portal vein 5-HT concentration from 12±3 to 27±5 nM. These data indicate that propionate acts through an epithelial rather than microbiota-compositional mechanism. Spearman correlation between caecal propionate and portal 5-HT was rs=0.74 (p<0.001).

title: Fibre-type differences in SCFA profiles and mucosal serotonin: a comparison of inulin, pectin, and resistant starch in rats
abstract: Three fermentable fibres were compared for their capacity to shift faecal SCFA profiles and downstream mucosal 5-HT in Sprague–Dawley rats (n=48, eight per fibre per sex). Animals received 5% (w/w) inulin, pectin, or resistant starch (Hi-Maize type analogue) for eight weeks. Faecal SCFAs were quantified by GC-FID. Inulin elevated butyrate most markedly (3.2-fold vs. control), pectin preferentially raised propionate (2.6-fold), and resistant starch produced the most balanced SCFA increment. Colonic mucosal 5-HT correlated positively with both butyrate (r=0.61) and propionate (r=0.54) but not acetate. Jejunal and ileal 5-HT were unaffected. Sex did not modify the SCFA–5-HT relationship. Results suggest that the butyrate/propionate ratio, not total SCFA load, predicts EC cell responsiveness.

title: Vagotomy attenuates the peripheral-to-central serotonin signal driven by colonic butyrate in rats
abstract: Whether gut-derived serotonin reaches the brain via the vagus nerve or systemic circulation remains debated. We performed subdiaphragmatic vagotomy or sham surgery in male Wistar rats (n=30) and then administered sodium butyrate by intra-colonic infusion for three weeks. Brain-region 5-HT was measured in prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and brainstem raphe by HPLC-ECD. In intact animals, butyrate raised hippocampal 5-HT by 18% and raphe 5-HT by 24% compared to saline controls. Vagotomy abolished these increments without altering colonic or portal 5-HT, confirming that the vagal pathway is necessary for the central effect. Prefrontal cortex 5-HT was not significantly affected in either surgical group. Tph2 mRNA in the raphe was upregulated 1.7-fold in intact-butyrate animals and was normalised by vagotomy, suggesting a transcriptional component to the relay.

title: Acetate does not replicate the EC-cell stimulatory effect of butyrate and propionate in an ex vivo colonic strip preparation
abstract: Using an ex vivo colonic mucosal strip preparation from Sprague–Dawley rats, we tested whether the three principal SCFAs—acetate, propionate, and butyrate—differ in their capacity to stimulate serotonin release from EC cells. Strips were perfused luminally with individual SCFAs at physiological concentrations (acetate 60 mM, propionate 10 mM, butyrate 5 mM) or vehicle for 60 minutes. Serotonin released into the serosal compartment was quantified by ELISA at 15-minute intervals. Butyrate and propionate each produced a sustained increase in serotonin release (peak 3.4-fold and 2.8-fold above baseline, respectively). Acetate produced no significant effect at equimolar or supra-physiological concentrations (up to 120 mM). Free fatty acid receptor 2 (FFAR2) and FFAR3 mRNA were detected in EC-enriched fractions; receptor antagonism with small-molecule blockers attenuated the propionate but not the butyrate response, suggesting distinct receptor pathways.

title: Tryptophan availability limits the butyrate-driven increase in colonic serotonin synthesis: isotope tracing in rats
abstract: EC cells synthesise serotonin from dietary tryptophan via tryptophan hydroxylase 1 (Tph1). We tested whether tryptophan availability caps the stimulatory effect of butyrate on colonic 5-HT. Rats (n=40) were randomised to four groups: standard diet ± sodium butyrate; tryptophan-restricted diet (0.05% Trp w/w) ± sodium butyrate. Isotopically labelled [U-¹³C₁₁]-tryptophan was administered by gavage and ¹³C-5-HT was tracked in caecal mucosa and portal blood by LC-HRMS. Tryptophan restriction reduced labelled 5-HT accumulation by 67% in standard-diet animals and by 74% in butyrate-treated animals, with no difference between restriction groups (p=0.32). Tph1 mRNA was equivalently upregulated by butyrate in both dietary backgrounds. These findings indicate that butyrate acts primarily at the transcriptional level of Tph1 but that substrate availability represents a distinct and non-redundant rate-limiting step.

title: Short-chain fatty acids and serotonin in the gut–brain axis: mechanisms and dietary determinants
abstract: This chapter reviews the evidence linking colonic SCFA production to serotonin signalling along the gut–brain axis, with emphasis on mechanistic pathways operating at the EC cell, the enteric nervous system, and central serotonergic nuclei. We discuss the role of free fatty acid receptors FFAR2 and FFAR3 in transducing luminal SCFA signals, the transcriptional regulation of Tph1 by histone deacetylase inhibition, tryptophan availability as a substrate constraint, and vagal versus humoral pathways to the brain. Dietary factors—fibre type and quantity, protein intake, and antibiotic exposure—are evaluated as modifiers of the SCFA–5-HT relationship. Clinical correlates in irritable bowel syndrome and mood disorders are discussed where supported by controlled data. Gaps in current knowledge, including the direction of causality in human studies and the species-specificity of receptor pharmacology, are identified.

title: Microbiota transplantation from high-butyrate donors raises hippocampal serotonin in recipient germ-free mice
abstract: We tested whether a microbiota characterised by high butyrate production is sufficient to transfer an elevated central-serotonin phenotype. Faecal microbiota from rats on a long-term inulin diet (high caecal butyrate donors) or standard chow (controls) were transplanted into germ-free C57BL/6 mice (n=20 per group). At four weeks post-colonisation, recipient microbiota composition was confirmed by 16S rRNA sequencing, and faecal butyrate was 2.9-fold higher in the inulin-microbiota group (p<0.001). Hippocampal 5-HT was 22% higher in inulin-microbiota recipients (p=0.009). Serum 5-HT was elevated 31% (p=0.003), and vagal c-Fos immunoreactivity in the nucleus tractus solitarius was increased, consistent with greater afferent traffic. Anxiety-like behaviour on the open-field test was not significantly different between groups, suggesting that the serotonergic shift at this magnitude did not produce a detectable behavioural phenotype.
venue: Neurogastroenterology and Gut Biology

title: Associations between habitual dietary fibre intake, faecal butyrate, and depressive symptom scores in a community sample: findings from the Vojvodina Cohort Study
abstract: The Vojvodina Cohort Study enrolled 621 adults (mean age 44±11 years, 56% female) from urban and rural Vojvodina municipalities. Habitual diet was assessed by a validated 168-item food frequency questionnaire. Faecal butyrate was quantified by GC-FID, and depressive symptoms were scored using the Serbian-validated PHQ-9. In multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI, physical activity, and income, each 10 µmol/g increment in faecal butyrate was associated with a −0.41-point PHQ-9 score (95% CI −0.72 to −0.10, p=0.009). Total dietary fibre intake was also inversely associated with PHQ-9 (β=−0.18 per 5 g/day, p=0.023). Plasma 5-HT was measured in a sub-sample (n=214) and partially mediated the butyrate–PHQ-9 association (mediation proportion 27%, bootstrap CI 8–49%). These observational data are consistent with a butyrate–serotonin–mood pathway but cannot establish causality.

title: Histone H3 acetylation at the Tph1 promoter as a mechanism for butyrate-dependent transcriptional activation in BON-1 cells
abstract: Butyrate is a well-characterised HDAC inhibitor, but whether this activity underpins its Tph1-stimulatory effect in EC-like cells has not been directly tested. We used the human EC-like BON-1 cell line treated with sodium butyrate (0.5–5 mM, 24–72 h). Chromatin immunoprecipitation with anti-H3K9ac antibody followed by qPCR showed a concentration-dependent increase in H3K9 acetylation at the proximal Tph1 promoter (peak 4.1-fold at 2 mM butyrate). This correlated with Tph1 mRNA upregulation (r=0.89, p<0.001) and increased intracellular 5-HTP and 5-HT content. The HDAC inhibitor vorinostat replicated the effect at equimolar concentrations, while a synthetic butyrate analogue lacking HDAC-inhibitory activity did not increase H3K9ac or Tph1 mRNA. These data support a chromatin-based mechanism as the primary route through which butyrate activates serotonin biosynthesis in EC-like cells.

title: Oral butyrate supplementation in adults with low-grade depression and low dietary fibre intake: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial
abstract: Forty-two adults with PHQ-9 scores of 5–14 and self-reported fibre intake below 15 g/day were randomised to sodium butyrate capsules (4 g/day) or microcrystalline cellulose placebo for 12 weeks. Co-primary outcomes were change in PHQ-9 score and plasma 5-HT concentration. Faecal butyrate, Tph1-expressing EC cell density (rectal biopsies), and gut microbiota composition were secondary outcomes. Plasma 5-HT increased by 19 ng/mL in the butyrate group vs. 3 ng/mL in placebo (difference 16 ng/mL, 95% CI 5–27, p=0.006). PHQ-9 scores declined by 2.8 points in the butyrate group vs. 1.3 in placebo (p=0.09), a trend that did not reach significance in this underpowered pilot. EC cell density was higher in the butyrate arm (p=0.03). No serious adverse events were recorded. A larger confirmatory trial is warranted.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing of rat colonic epithelium resolves heterogeneity in Tph1 expression within the enterochromaffin cell population
abstract: EC cells are operationally treated as a single population, but their transcriptional heterogeneity has not been characterised at single-cell resolution in the rat colon. We performed droplet-based scRNA-seq (10x Genomics platform) on 14,200 colonic epithelial cells isolated from proximal and distal rat colon under standard and butyrate-supplemented conditions. Unsupervised clustering resolved six epithelial subtypes including two EC subclusters distinguished by high and low Tph1 expression. The high-Tph1 subcluster was enriched for FFAR3 and HDAC2 transcripts and expanded 1.8-fold under butyrate supplementation. Trajectory analysis suggested the low-Tph1 subcluster as a transitional state. Ligand–receptor interaction analysis identified ENS-derived GDNF signalling as a candidate regulator of EC maturation. These data provide a transcriptional foundation for mechanistic dissection of EC heterogeneity and may explain variability in SCFA responsiveness across intestinal regions.

title: Concurrent antibiotic treatment eliminates the serotonergic response to dietary butyrate in mice: a causal test using controlled microbiota depletion
abstract: To confirm that the butyrate–serotonin link requires an intact gut microbiota rather than direct SCFA action, we treated C57BL/6 mice with a non-absorbable antibiotic cocktail (vancomycin, neomycin, metronidazole) for two weeks to achieve near-complete caecal microbiota depletion, confirmed by 16S rRNA sequencing (>99% reduction in total reads). Depleted and intact mice then received intra-caecal sodium butyrate or saline for two weeks. In intact mice, butyrate raised colonic 5-HT by 31% and portal 5-HT by 26%. In antibiotic-depleted animals, the same butyrate dose produced no significant change in either compartment, nor in hippocampal 5-HT. Tph1 mRNA response was similarly abolished. Re-colonisation with a minimal four-species consortium restored partial Tph1 responsiveness (1.5-fold vs. 2.4-fold in fully intact mice). These results indicate that live microbiota co-factors beyond butyrate itself are required for full EC cell activation.

title: Hypothalamic NPY mRNA expression is elevated in male Wistar rats after eight weeks on a high-fat diet independent of circulating leptin levels
abstract: We examined neuropeptide Y (NPY) gene expression in the arcuate nucleus of male Wistar rats maintained on a 45% kcal fat diet for eight weeks. Twelve animals per group were compared with chow-fed controls. Body weight, adiposity index, fasting insulin, leptin, and hypothalamic NPY mRNA (measured by quantitative RT-PCR) were assessed. High-fat-fed animals gained 38 ± 4 g more than controls and showed a 2.3-fold elevation in arcuate NPY mRNA despite plasma leptin concentrations that were 4.1-fold higher than controls (p < 0.001 for both). Insulin sensitivity, assessed by HOMA-IR, was significantly reduced. These findings indicate that hypothalamic NPY upregulation in early diet-induced obesity is dissociated from leptin signalling, consistent with a state of central leptin resistance. The data suggest that orexigenic drive persists even when peripheral satiety signals are elevated, contributing to positive energy balance.

title: Circulating microRNA-126 and microRNA-21 as candidate biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction severity in type 2 diabetes: a pilot cross-sectional analysis
abstract: MicroRNAs regulate endothelial gene expression and are detectable in plasma as stable extracellular species. In this pilot study, plasma miR-126-3p and miR-21-5p were quantified by RT-qPCR (normalised to cel-miR-39 spike-in) in 30 T2DM patients classified by FMD tertile (low: FMD < 4%; intermediate: 4–6%; high: > 6%) and 15 healthy controls. miR-126-3p was progressively lower across FMD tertiles (controls: 1.00 ± 0.12; high FMD: 0.74 ± 0.18; intermediate: 0.51 ± 0.15; low: 0.33 ± 0.11 relative units; p < 0.001 for trend). miR-21-5p showed the opposite pattern, increasing with worsening FMD (p < 0.01 for trend). Spearman correlation between miR-126-3p and FMD was r = 0.71 (p < 0.001). Receiver-operating characteristic analysis for discrimination of low-FMD tertile yielded AUC 0.83 for miR-126-3p alone. Although limited by sample size, these preliminary data suggest that circulating miR-126-3p may serve as a quantitative molecular correlate of endothelial vasodilatory capacity in T2DM, warranting validation in larger cohorts.

title: Fibre-type plasticity and muscle ultrasound: can B-mode echo intensity serve as a non-invasive proxy for histochemical fibre-type distribution in elderly sedentary men?
abstract: Muscle biopsy is the reference method for fibre-type assessment but is invasive. This study evaluated whether vastus lateralis echo intensity (EI) measured by B-mode ultrasound could predict type I fibre proportion determined histochemically in the same participants. Forty-one sedentary men aged 64–76 years underwent ultrasound imaging and needle biopsy on the same day. EI was corrected for subcutaneous fat thickness. Pearson correlation between corrected EI and type I fibre proportion was −0.38 (p = 0.014), indicating that higher EI—reflecting greater intramuscular fat and connective tissue—is associated with a lower proportion of oxidative fibres. However, 95% prediction intervals for individual biopsy-based values from ultrasound were wide (±18 percentage points), precluding clinical substitution. Ultrasound EI may serve as a population-level screening tool but cannot replace biopsy for individual fibre-type characterisation in research contexts.

title: Removal of Methylene Blue from Aqueous Solution Using Raw Sunflower Seed Husks: Equilibrium and Kinetic Study
abstract: Sunflower seed husks, an abundant agricultural by-product in Vojvodina, were evaluated as a biosorbent for methylene blue (MB) removal from synthetic wastewater. Batch experiments were performed at pH 3–10, biosorbent doses of 0.5–4 g/L, initial MB concentrations of 10–200 mg/L, and temperatures of 15, 25, and 35 °C. Maximum adsorption capacity determined from the Langmuir isotherm reached 48.3 mg/g at 25 °C and pH 7. Pseudo-second-order kinetics described the uptake accurately (R² > 0.99). FTIR spectra recorded before and after sorption indicated involvement of hydroxyl, carboxyl, and amine-like surface groups in dye binding. Thermodynamic parameters (ΔG°, ΔH°, ΔS°) suggested a spontaneous, endothermic process. The material was tested for two regeneration cycles using 0.1 M HCl, retaining approximately 82% of initial capacity. Results indicate that untreated sunflower husks can be a practical low-cost sorbent alternative for textile effluent polishing steps.

title: Effect of Alkali Pre-treatment on the Sorption Performance of Corn Cob Powder for Crystal Violet Uptake
abstract: Corn cob powder was subjected to NaOH pre-treatment at concentrations of 0.5, 1, and 2 M to increase surface hydroxyl density and porosity prior to use as a biosorbent for crystal violet (CV) removal. BET surface area increased from 4.1 m²/g (raw) to 18.7 m²/g (2 M NaOH-treated). FTIR analysis confirmed partial removal of lignin and an increase in accessible cellulose hydroxyl groups. Langmuir maximum capacities rose from 55.2 mg/g (raw) to 112.6 mg/g (2 M-treated) at pH 8 and 25 °C. Freundlich and Sips models were also fitted; the Sips model yielded the best statistical agreement across the full concentration range (10–500 mg/L). Intraparticle diffusion analysis suggested both film diffusion and pore diffusion as rate-controlling steps. Pre-treatment with 1 M NaOH was identified as the most cost-effective condition, balancing performance gain against reagent consumption. Column breakthrough experiments at 5 mL/min confirmed scalability of the result.

title: Biosorption of Safranin O onto Wheat Straw: Surface Characterisation by XPS and Modelling with Three-Parameter Isotherms
abstract: Wheat straw was characterised by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and FTIR before and after sorption of safranin O (SO), a cationic azo-phenazine dye used in textile printing. XPS C 1s and O 1s spectra revealed an increase in C–O and C=O contributions at the surface after SO loading, consistent with electrostatic interaction between protonated dye molecules and carboxylate/hydroxyl groups. Sorption isotherms were fitted to Langmuir, Freundlich, Redlich–Peterson, and Toth models using non-linear regression minimising the sum of squared errors. The Toth model gave the lowest SSE (0.12) and best described heterogeneous surface behaviour. Maximum Langmuir capacity was 79.1 mg/g at pH 6 and 20 °C. Ionic strength tests (0–0.1 M NaCl) showed a moderate capacity decrease of 18% at 0.1 M, indicating that electrostatic attraction is the dominant but not exclusive binding mechanism. The study provides quantitative surface-level evidence for binding mechanisms rarely reported for straw-type sorbents.
