title: Competitive Sorption of Methylene Blue and Malachite Green on Alkali-Modified Soybean Hulls
abstract: Binary-component sorption of methylene blue (MB) and malachite green (MG) onto NaOH-modified soybean hull powder was studied to replicate conditions closer to real mixed textile effluents. Single-component Langmuir capacities were 94.7 mg/g (MB) and 87.3 mg/g (MG) at pH 7 and 25 °C. In binary systems at equimolar initial concentrations (50–400 mg/L each), extended Langmuir and non-modified competitive Langmuir models underestimated the mutual inhibition, while the modified extended Langmuir model incorporating interaction coefficients provided reasonable fits (R² = 0.96–0.98). At high total dye concentrations (>300 mg/L), MG adsorption was suppressed more strongly than MB adsorption, attributed to the larger molecular size of MG reducing access to finer pores. FTIR spectra of the binary-loaded sorbent were deconvoluted and compared with single-component spectra to identify overlapping binding sites. The results suggest that soybean hulls can manage mixed dye streams but that capacity estimates from single-component data overestimate performance by 15–30%.

title: Thomas and Yoon–Nelson Column Modelling for Continuous Removal of Basic Blue 41 by Sunflower Head Biochar
abstract: Sunflower head residues were pyrolysed at 400 °C and 600 °C under nitrogen atmosphere to produce biochars for use in fixed-bed column experiments targeting Basic Blue 41, a reactive cationic dye common in Serbian textile industry effluents. BET surface areas of the 400 °C and 600 °C biochars were 126 and 342 m²/g, respectively. Column experiments were run at three flow rates (2, 5, and 10 mL/min) and two bed heights (5 and 10 cm) with a 50 mg/L inlet concentration. Breakthrough curves were fitted to Thomas and Yoon–Nelson models; both provided good agreement with experimental data (R² > 0.97). Maximum column sorption capacities were 68.4 and 91.2 mg/g for 400 °C and 600 °C biochars, respectively. Five adsorption–desorption cycles using 0.05 M HNO₃ showed capacity retention of 74% for the 600 °C biochar. Pyrolysis temperature was identified as the dominant factor controlling both surface area and column performance.

title: Influence of Humic Acid and Calcium Ions on Methylene Blue Biosorption by Corn Stover: Implications for Real Wastewater Treatment
abstract: Laboratory biosorption studies commonly use ultrapure water matrices, potentially overestimating performance under real conditions. This study examined the effect of humic acid (HA, 0–20 mg/L) and calcium ions (Ca²⁺, 0–5 mM) on methylene blue (MB) uptake by NaOH-activated corn stover. At 10 mg/L HA, MB sorption capacity decreased by 22%, attributed to competitive occupation of cationic binding sites by HA-associated metal complexes and partial pore blockage confirmed by BET analysis. Calcium ions at 2 mM increased MB removal by 8%, likely through bridging effects between carboxylate groups and the dye. Combined HA and Ca²⁺ conditions showed partially compensatory effects. Experiments were also carried out using centrifuged effluent from a fictional textile facility spiked with known MB concentrations; removal efficiency dropped from 94% (ultrapure) to 81% (real matrix). Findings demonstrate that matrix effects must be incorporated into biosorbent performance assessments before scale-up decisions are made.

title: Comparative FTIR and XPS Analysis of Functional Groups Responsible for Cationic Dye Binding on Six Agricultural By-products
abstract: A systematic comparison of six lignocellulosic by-products — sunflower husks, corn cob, wheat straw, soybean hulls, hemp shive, and tobacco stem — was performed to establish structure–activity relationships for cationic dye biosorption. All materials were characterised by FTIR (ATR mode, 400–4000 cm⁻¹) and XPS (C 1s, O 1s, N 1s regions) before and after saturation with methylene blue. Carboxylate (–COO⁻) surface density, estimated by XPS peak deconvolution, correlated positively with Langmuir maximum capacity across all materials (Pearson r = 0.91). Hydroxyl group contribution showed a weaker but still significant correlation (r = 0.74). Hemp shive displayed the highest carboxylate density (0.34 mmol/g by potentiometric titration) and the highest capacity (118.4 mg/g). Tobacco stem, with the lowest surface oxygen content by XPS, showed the lowest capacity (31.6 mg/g). The dataset provides a predictive framework allowing preliminary ranking of untested biomass materials based on XPS O 1s composition alone.

title: Pelletisation of Hemp Shive Biosorbent for Packed-Bed Applications: Mechanical Stability, Hydraulic Performance, and Dye Removal Efficiency
abstract: Powdered hemp shive biosorbent, identified in earlier work as a high-capacity material, was pelletised using carboxymethyl cellulose as a binder (5 and 10 wt%) and evaluated for column applications. Pellets of 3 and 5 mm diameter were tested for mechanical crush strength, water stability over 72 h, and methylene blue removal in fixed-bed columns (bed height 15 cm, flow rates 3–12 mL/min, inlet concentration 100 mg/L). The 5 mm pellets with 10 wt% binder showed adequate crush strength (>4.2 N) and maintained structural integrity over 72 h. Pressure drop across the bed was 30–65% lower compared to equivalent packed powder beds. Thomas model fits gave column capacities of 85–101 mg/g, representing a 15–20% reduction relative to unpelletised material, attributed to restricted intraparticle diffusion within pellets. Scanning electron microscopy of pellet cross-sections confirmed partial pore occlusion by the binder at 10 wt%. An optimised binder content of 7 wt% is proposed for future scale-up studies.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Langmuir Isotherm Parameters for Cationic Dye Biosorption: A Dataset-Driven Approach
abstract: A dataset of 310 biosorption experiments from published and in-house studies was assembled, covering 14 cationic dyes, 11 lignocellulosic by-products, and pH values of 4–10. Input features included dye molecular weight, charge, log P, biosorbent carboxylate density (mmol/g), BET surface area (m²/g), pH, and temperature. Random forest (RF) and gradient boosting (GB) regression models were trained to predict Langmuir q_max and K_L parameters using 5-fold cross-validation. GB outperformed RF for q_max prediction (RMSE 8.4 vs. 12.1 mg/g) while both models performed similarly for K_L (RMSE ~0.006 L/mg). Feature importance analysis confirmed carboxylate density and pH as the two dominant predictors of q_max, consistent with mechanistic understanding. The model was validated against 22 independent experiments not used in training, achieving a mean absolute percentage error of 14.2% for q_max. The trained model and dataset are made available as supplementary material to support rapid pre-screening of candidate biosorbents.

title: Continuous Flow Biosorption of Safranin O and Basic Red 46 in a Two-Stage Fixed-Bed System Using Hemp Shive Pellets
abstract: A two-stage fixed-bed configuration was designed and tested for continuous treatment of synthetic textile wastewater containing safranin O (SO) and Basic Red 46 (BR46) at inlet concentrations of 80 and 60 mg/L, respectively. Hemp shive pellets (7 wt% CMC binder, 5 mm diameter) were packed into two serially connected glass columns (15 cm bed height each). Flow rates of 5 and 8 mL/min were tested over 72-hour runs. Effluent was monitored by UV-Vis spectrophotometry at 520 and 498 nm for SO and BR46, respectively. The two-stage setup extended time to 10% breakthrough by 2.7-fold (5 mL/min) compared to a single-stage column of equal total volume, confirming better utilisation of sorption capacity. BDST (bed depth service time) model parameters were determined for both stages and both dyes. After exhaustion, regeneration with 0.1 M citric acid restored 88% of capacity for SO and 79% for BR46 over three cycles. Effluent quality met the Serbian national limit for colour discharge in 94% of the operational period tested.

title: Characterisation of ajvar off-flavour: identification of key odorants by GC-olfactometry and aroma extract dilution analysis
abstract: Ajvar, a roasted Capsicum annuum-based condiment widely consumed in the western Balkans, frequently develops off-flavours during storage. GC-olfactometry combined with aroma extract dilution analysis (AEDA) was used to identify the most potent odorants in commercial ajvar samples collected from Serbian producers. Fifteen samples were evaluated by a seven-member trained panel. Compounds with the highest flavour dilution (FD) factors included 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline (FD 512), (E)-2-decenal (FD 256), and guaiacol (FD 256). A paint-like off-note attributed to 1-octen-3-one was detected in four samples showing elevated lipid oxidation indices. The study maps the odorant landscape of both fresh and oxidatively degraded ajvar, providing targets for future quality control work.

title: Enantioselective esterification of (R,S)-ibuprofen with n-propanol catalysed by Burkholderia cepacia lipase on celite in isooctane
abstract: The resolution of racemic ibuprofen was investigated using Burkholderia cepacia lipase physically adsorbed onto Celite 545. Reactions were performed in isooctane at substrate concentrations between 25 and 200 mM, alcohol:acid molar ratios of 1:1 to 5:1, and temperatures of 30–50 °C. Enantiomeric excess of the (S)-ester product (ee_p) reached 94.2% at 40 °C with a 2:1 propanol:ibuprofen ratio and 0.1 g enzyme preparation per mmol substrate. The E value was calculated as 38 ± 3 across three replicate experiments. Conversion was limited to 42% to preserve high ee_p. A substrate inhibition model fitted the kinetic data better than Michaelis–Menten kinetics, with inhibition constant K_i of 98 mM. The work provides practical parameters for a preparative-scale resolution protocol applicable to production of the active pharmaceutical ingredient.

title: Effect of descriptor scaling and normalisation choices on QSAR model stability for antifungal azoles
abstract: Preprocessing decisions—mean centring, autoscaling, range scaling, and Pareto scaling—are rarely reported in detail yet can alter descriptor rankings and model coefficients substantially. This study evaluated four scaling strategies on a fixed dataset of 65 azole antifungals using MLR, PLS, and RF, with all other settings held constant. Autoscaling produced the most stable PLS models across 50 random train–test splits (variance in Q²ext = 0.0041), while range scaling led to the highest instability in MLR (variance = 0.019) due to sensitivity to descriptor outliers. RF was largely insensitive to scaling method (maximum variance in R²ext = 0.0018), consistent with its tree-based structure. For MLR and PLS, autoscaling is recommended as the default; range scaling is inadvisable when descriptors contain structural outliers. These findings have practical implications for QSAR reproducibility and should be reported alongside model statistics in publications.

title: Variogram Analysis of Cone Penetration Resistance in Alluvial Deposits of the Tisa Floodplain
abstract: The paper presents a systematic variogram analysis of cone tip resistance (qc) measured at 14 CPT locations across a 3.2 km² test area in the Tisa floodplain near Senta. Experimental directional variograms were computed for three depth intervals (0–5 m, 5–10 m, 10–18 m) to characterise horizontal and vertical spatial continuity separately. Exponential and spherical variogram models were fitted and their parameters compared across intervals. Results indicate that horizontal ranges decrease with depth, from approximately 480 m in the uppermost interval to 210 m at depth, reflecting increased lateral heterogeneity in deeper Pleistocene layers. Nugget-to-sill ratios remain below 0.15 in all cases, suggesting dominant structured variability. The fitted models provide a basis for ordinary kriging interpolation of qc fields subsequently used in settlement estimation for a planned road embankment. The study demonstrates that even with sparse sampling, statistically stable variogram models can be obtained when vertical stationarity is enforced within defined depth windows.

title: Ordinary Kriging versus Inverse Distance Weighting for Undrained Shear Strength Mapping: A Case Study from the Danube Terrace near Novi Sad
abstract: Undrained shear strength (cu) values derived from 22 field vane shear tests and 6 boreholes with laboratory UU triaxial data were used to compare ordinary kriging (OK) and inverse distance weighting (IDW) at p = 2 and p = 3 for spatial interpolation across a 1.8 km² terrace segment. Leave-one-out cross-validation was applied to quantify prediction errors. Mean absolute error for OK was 4.1 kPa compared to 6.8 kPa for IDW (p = 2) and 7.4 kPa for IDW (p = 3). OK also produced narrower prediction intervals in areas of dense sampling while correctly widening uncertainty in data-sparse zones. The kriging variance maps revealed three zones of high uncertainty coinciding with areas where borehole spacing exceeded 180 m. Recommendations are given for minimum sampling density needed to keep relative kriging standard deviation below 20% of the mean cu estimate in comparable alluvial settings. Results support replacing IDW with OK as the default interpolation method in routine geotechnical site investigations of similar scale.

title: Probabilistic Delineation of Soft Clay Lenses in a Multi-Layer Alluvial Profile Using Sequential Gaussian Simulation
abstract: Soft clay lenses embedded within silty sand sequences pose a significant risk for differential settlement and slope instability. This study applies sequential Gaussian simulation (SGS) to reconstruct the three-dimensional distribution of normalised cone resistance Qt from 19 CPT soundings at a highway construction site in southern Bačka. One hundred equiprobable realisations were generated using a spherical variogram model with horizontal range 320 m and vertical range 1.8 m. The frequency of Qt values below a threshold of 1.2—indicative of soft clay—was computed voxel-by-voxel to produce a probability-of-occurrence map for soft clay at each 0.5 m depth slice. Results show that a coherent soft clay body with greater than 60% probability of occurrence extends over approximately 0.4 ha at depths of 6.5–8.0 m, a feature not apparent from deterministic interpolation. The probabilistic maps were used to revise pile length recommendations, increasing average pile depth from 11 m to 13.5 m over the identified zone. The workflow is implemented in Python using the open-source GeostatsPy library and is fully reproducible.

title: Influence of Borehole Spacing on Kriging Uncertainty in Alluvial Soil Profiles: A Simulation-Based Study
abstract: A systematic investigation of how borehole spacing affects kriging prediction uncertainty was conducted using synthetic alluvial profiles generated via unconditional SGS with known variogram parameters calibrated to the Bačka Plain. Virtual sampling grids with spacings from 25 m to 400 m were applied to each synthetic field, and ordinary kriging was performed at each spacing to reconstruct the reference field. Average kriging standard deviation and fraction of the reference field lying outside 90% prediction intervals were computed as functions of spacing for three soil parameters: compression index Cc, friction angle φ', and oedometric modulus Es. For Cc, acceptable uncertainty levels (kriging CV < 25%) required spacing below 150 m for shallow layers and below 80 m for deeper, more heterogeneous layers. The results are presented as design charts directly usable by practitioners to plan site investigation campaigns. A simplified equation relating required borehole spacing to target uncertainty and variogram range is proposed and validated against three published datasets from Serbia and Hungary.

title: Geostatistical Methods in Geotechnical Site Investigation
abstract: This book chapter provides a practical introduction to geostatistical interpolation techniques applicable to geotechnical site characterisation, written for practitioners and graduate students with a background in soil mechanics but limited exposure to spatial statistics. Topics covered include experimental variogram computation, variogram model fitting, ordinary and simple kriging, indicator kriging for soil type classification, and stochastic simulation methods. Each method is illustrated with worked examples drawn from CPT and borehole datasets collected in the Pannonian Basin region. Particular attention is paid to common pitfalls: non-stationarity arising from depth trends, anisotropy caused by depositional layering, and the consequences of over-smoothing in kriging maps. The chapter also discusses how kriging variance can be propagated into geotechnical calculations such as bearing capacity and settlement estimates under uncertainty. Software options including GSLIB, SGeMS, and Python-based tools are briefly reviewed. The chapter forms part of a regional textbook on advanced geotechnical investigation methods.

title: Indicator Kriging for Soil Classification from CPT Data along the Danube–Tisa–Danube Canal Corridor
abstract: Soil type classification along a 12 km stretch of the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal embankment was performed using indicator kriging (IK) applied to CPT-derived soil behaviour type indices (Ic) from 31 soundings. Six soil classes were defined following Robertson's SBTn scheme, and indicator transforms were constructed for each class. Experimental indicator variograms were computed per class and fitted with nested spherical models. IK provided class-probability maps at 0.25 m vertical resolution and 20 m horizontal resolution. Post-processing by maximum-probability assignment yielded a most-likely soil type cross-section, while the probability fields quantified classification uncertainty. Comparison with lithological logs from 8 boreholes showed 82% agreement at borehole locations for the dominant classes (silty sand and sandy silt). Misclassification occurred primarily at thin clay interbeds less than 0.4 m thick, below the effective vertical resolution of the kriging grid. The IK outputs were used directly as input to a one-dimensional consolidation model for embankment settlement prediction.

title: Bayesian Updating of Prior Variogram Parameters Using CPT Data: Application to a Flood Protection Levee in Northern Serbia
abstract: Prior information about soil variability structures in the Pannonian Basin is available from published studies but may not be directly transferable to a specific site. This study applies a Bayesian framework to update prior distributions on variogram range and sill parameters as CPT soundings are progressively added during a phased investigation of a 4.2 km levee reach near Kanjiža. Prior distributions were derived from a database of 38 variogram models from comparable alluvial sites in Serbia and Hungary. Likelihood functions were constructed from cross-validation residuals at each investigation phase (8, 14, 22, and 29 CPT locations). Posterior mean horizontal range estimates converged from 380 m (prior) to 245 m after 22 soundings, with a 90% credible interval of 190–310 m. The updated variogram parameters reduced kriging variance by 31% on average compared to using the prior. The framework provides a practical tool for adaptive site investigation: quantifying how much uncertainty reduction is achieved by each additional sounding and informing decisions about when sampling is sufficient. Results are relevant to levee safety assessment under probabilistic failure criteria.

title: Combining CPT and Seismic Refraction Data for Constrained Geostatistical Modelling of a Shallow Aquifer–Aquitard System
abstract: CPT soundings provide high vertical resolution but limited horizontal coverage, whereas seismic refraction surveys yield continuous lateral profiles at lower vertical resolution. This paper presents a co-kriging approach that integrates 24 CPT-derived layer boundary depths with seismic refraction first-arrival velocity data acquired along four 300 m profiles at a groundwater monitoring site in the Subotica Sand area. A linear coregionalisation model was fitted to the cross-variogram between CPT-derived aquitard top depth and seismic interval velocity in the overlying saturated sand layer. Co-kriging reduced the average estimation standard deviation of aquitard top depth by 22% relative to ordinary kriging using CPT data alone. The resulting depth-to-aquitard surface showed a previously unmapped depression of approximately 1.5 m at the centre of the study area, consistent with a paleochannel inferred from aerial photograph interpretation. The co-kriged model was used as a geometric input to a MODFLOW groundwater flow model, and sensitivity analyses confirmed that the depression materially affected simulated hydraulic head distributions. The study argues for routine integration of shallow geophysics in geostatistical site modelling when CPT coverage is sparse.

title: A Benchmark Comparison of Machine Learning Interpolation and Ordinary Kriging for CPT-Derived Soil Properties in the Bačka Plain
abstract: Random forest regression, gradient boosting, and ordinary kriging were benchmarked for spatial prediction of friction ratio Rf and sleeve friction fs from a CPT dataset of 47 soundings in the Bačka Plain alluvial region. Each method was evaluated using 10-fold spatial cross-validation with folds defined by spatial block partitioning to avoid proximity bias. Kriging achieved the lowest root mean square error for Rf (0.31%) compared to random forest (0.38%) and gradient boosting (0.36%). For fs, performance differences were smaller and not statistically significant at the 95% level. Machine learning methods showed a tendency to underpredict extreme values in data-sparse zones, a consequence of regression toward the mean. Kriging prediction intervals were well-calibrated, with empirical coverage of 91% for nominal 90% intervals, whereas prediction intervals from gradient boosting required conformal post-processing to achieve comparable calibration. The paper concludes that ordinary kriging remains competitive for continuous soil property interpolation from CPT data in geologically simple alluvial settings, though machine learning may offer advantages when auxiliary environmental covariates are incorporated. Reproducible Python code and the full dataset are provided as supplementary material.

title: Geotechnical characterisation of deep peat deposits for infrastructure planning in northern Vojvodina
abstract: A systematic geotechnical investigation of deep peat deposits (thickness 2.5 to 11.8 m) in the northern Vojvodina region was undertaken as input for regional infrastructure planning. Thirty-two boreholes with continuous sampling were drilled at fourteen sites. Physical properties, Atterberg limits, grain size distribution, organic content, and basic compressibility parameters were determined for 124 specimens. Peat was classified according to the von Post scale as H3–H7 at most sites. Undrained shear strength measured by field vane tests ranged from 9 to 31 kPa and correlated strongly with bulk density (R² = 0.74). Depth profiles showed that in most locations the peat layer is underlain by soft organic clay before transition to medium stiff clay, requiring two-layer consolidation modelling. The data were compiled into a GIS database accessible to regional planning authorities and are intended to serve as a reference for future infrastructure projects.

title: Impedance Response of LiFePO4 Cells as a Function of State of Charge at Ambient Temperature
abstract: This paper presents a systematic measurement campaign on commercially available 26650-format LiFePO4 cells, recording electrochemical impedance spectra at eleven discrete states of charge between 10% and 100% SoC. Spectra were acquired over a frequency range of 10 mHz to 100 kHz using a Zahner IM6 analyser. A second-order Randles-type equivalent circuit was fitted to each spectrum using a complex nonlinear least-squares algorithm. The fitted parameters—ohmic resistance R0, charge-transfer resistance Rct, and constant-phase element coefficients—exhibit a monotonic and reproducible dependence on SoC above 30%, whereas the flat open-circuit voltage plateau of LiFePO4 frustrates conventional voltage-based estimation in that region. Results show that Rct varies by approximately 18% across the 30–80% SoC window, suggesting that impedance features may substitute for voltage as a state indicator within this chemically challenging plateau. Measurement uncertainty was quantified through repeated trials on five cells from the same production batch.

title: Separation of Ohmic and Charge-Transfer Contributions to Ageing in Cylindrical NMC Cells Using Partial-Discharge EIS
abstract: The study investigates how ohmic resistance and charge-transfer resistance evolve separately over calendar and cycle ageing in 18650-format NMC cells without recourse to full charge–discharge cycling. Cells were aged under three temperature regimes (25°C, 35°C, 45°C) and impedance was measured every two weeks at three fixed SoC setpoints (20%, 50%, 80%). Over 52 weeks, ohmic resistance increased by 6–11% depending on temperature while charge-transfer resistance grew by 23–41%, confirming that the latter is the dominant ageing indicator in early to mid-life. A linear regression model trained on impedance features at 50% SoC predicted remaining capacity with a mean absolute error of 1.3% relative to reference full-cycle capacity checks performed monthly. The protocol avoids full cycling, reducing the diagnostic overhead to under 15 minutes per cell.

title: Equivalent Circuit Parameter Extraction for Lithium-Ion Cells: Sensitivity of Fitting Algorithms to Frequency Range Selection
abstract: Equivalent circuit models (ECMs) for lithium-ion cells are routinely fitted to impedance spectra, yet the choice of frequency range can substantially alter the extracted parameters. This study compares four fitting approaches—complex nonlinear least squares, genetic algorithm optimisation, particle swarm optimisation, and a gradient-free Nelder–Mead simplex method—applied to spectra truncated at upper cut-offs of 1 kHz, 10 kHz, and 100 kHz and lower cut-offs of 1 Hz, 100 mHz, and 10 mHz. Tests were performed on sets of twenty NCA 18650 cells at two SoC levels. Results indicate that below 100 mHz, diffusion-related Warburg elements become significant and their omission from simplified ECMs inflates Rct estimates by up to 14%. The gradient-based CNLS method converges fastest but is most sensitive to initial parameter guesses, while particle swarm yields more robust fits at the cost of computation time roughly six times longer.

title: Temperature Compensation in EIS-Based State-of-Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Cells
abstract: Impedance parameters of lithium-ion cells are strongly temperature-dependent, complicating state-of-health (SoH) estimation in real-world environments where cell temperature is not controlled. This paper quantifies the temperature sensitivity of six ECM parameters extracted from EIS measurements on 26650 LFP cells at temperatures spanning −5°C to 45°C and proposes a compensation scheme based on an Arrhenius-type correction applied to Rct and on a first-order polynomial correction applied to R0. With compensation applied, a SoH model trained at 25°C retains a mean absolute error below 2.1% when deployed at temperatures from 5°C to 40°C on an independent validation set of twelve cells. Without compensation, errors exceed 8% at temperature deviations of ±15°C. The compensation coefficients are identified from a single three-temperature calibration sweep lasting approximately 90 minutes per cell.

title: On-Board EIS Excitation Using Existing Power Converter Ripple: Feasibility Study for Electric Bicycle Battery Packs
abstract: This work examines whether the current ripple naturally produced by a DC-DC converter in an electric bicycle drivetrain can be used as the excitation signal for in-situ electrochemical impedance measurements, removing the need for a dedicated impedance analyser. A 250 W front-wheel hub-motor bicycle was instrumented with voltage and current transducers at the battery terminals. Ripple spectra at converter switching harmonics between 1 kHz and 20 kHz were extracted via FFT, and the corresponding impedance values were compared against reference spectra obtained with a laboratory analyser at the same SoC and temperature. Agreement within 4% was achieved for the real part of impedance at frequencies above 2 kHz, covering the ohmic resistance region. Below 500 Hz, insufficient ripple energy limited accuracy. The results suggest that high-frequency impedance features, sufficient for detecting severe capacity fade, are accessible without hardware additions.

title: Impedance Spectroscopy Methods for Battery State Estimation
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of EIS measurement techniques applied to lithium-ion batteries, intended for practising engineers entering the field. It covers cell-level measurement setups, common equivalent circuit topologies from the simple Randles circuit to extended models incorporating finite-length diffusion, and the practical steps of fitting, validation, and uncertainty estimation. A section on partial-SoC measurement protocols addresses workflows suitable for field diagnostics, where full cycling is impractical. Representative data from NMC, LFP, and NCA chemistries are included to illustrate how model parameters differ across chemistries at comparable SoH. The chapter also discusses sources of artefact—cable inductance, contact resistance, temperature gradients—and describes mitigation measures used in laboratory and field settings. Worked numerical examples are provided for each fitting procedure.

title: Comparison of Single-Frequency and Multi-Frequency Impedance Features for State-of-Health Prediction Across Three NMC Cell Formats
abstract: The paper tests whether a single strategically chosen impedance measurement frequency can provide SoH estimates comparable in accuracy to full multi-frequency spectra, using three NMC cell formats: 18650, 21700, and prismatic pouch. A dataset of 108 cells aged to between 75% and 100% of initial capacity was assembled, with full EIS spectra recorded at 50% SoC. Feature importance analysis identified 1 kHz real impedance and 316 Hz imaginary impedance as the most predictive individual frequencies. A single-frequency model using only the 1 kHz real part achieved mean absolute error of 1.8% SoH across all three formats, compared to 1.2% for a ten-feature model using the full spectrum from 10 Hz to 10 kHz. The tradeoff suggests that single-frequency measurement, executable in under one second, is adequate for applications tolerating roughly 2% estimation error.

title: Ageing Diagnosis of Second-Life Lithium-Ion Cells Sourced from Retired E-Scooter Packs Using Partial-SoC EIS
abstract: Second-life applications of lithium-ion cells require rapid, reliable capacity assessment of cells with unknown usage histories. This study applies an EIS-based diagnostic protocol at three fixed SoC setpoints (20%, 50%, 80%) to 64 NMC cells recovered from retired shared e-scooter battery packs of varying operational age. Reference capacities were determined by a single full discharge. Impedance features extracted at 50% SoC, specifically R0 and Rct from a second-order ECM fit, explained 84% of variance in remaining capacity via multiple linear regression. A Gaussian process regression model trained on the same features reduced mean absolute error from 3.1% (linear model) to 2.2%. Cells below 78% of rated capacity were correctly flagged with 91% sensitivity and 88% specificity using a two-threshold decision rule. Total diagnostic time per cell was under 20 minutes, making the protocol compatible with high-throughput refurbishment workflows.

title: Sensitivity of EIS-Based SoH Models to Cell-to-Cell Manufacturing Spread in Large Lithium-Ion Battery Lots
abstract: Models that estimate state of health from impedance features are typically trained and validated on small cell samples, raising questions about their robustness when applied to large production lots with inherent manufacturing variability. This study characterises cell-to-cell spread in EIS parameters for a lot of 200 nominally identical 21700 NMC cells at beginning of life, quantifying coefficient of variation in R0 (3.1%), Rct (7.8%), and three further ECM parameters. A SoH estimation model trained on a random 60-cell subset was evaluated on the remaining 140 cells aged to varying depths. Cells in the upper quartile of initial Rct spread showed systematic SoH underestimation of approximately 2.4 percentage points when a single common model was applied. A simple per-cell normalisation step using a beginning-of-life reference measurement reduced this bias to below 0.8 percentage points without requiring retraining.

title: Near-Ground Path Loss Measurements at 433 MHz over Flat Agricultural Terrain in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper reports an empirical path loss study conducted over flat, open farmland in the Vojvodina plain at 433 MHz, a frequency band used by early low-power sensor networks. Measurements were taken with transmitter and receiver antenna heights between 0.5 m and 2.0 m, at separation distances ranging from 50 m to 2500 m. A total of 18 measurement runs were performed across three seasonal vegetation states: bare soil, low-crop, and full-canopy maize. Received signal strength was logged at 1 m intervals using a calibrated dipole reference antenna mounted on a wheeled cart. The data show that the two-ray ground-reflection model underestimates path loss beyond 800 m by 4–9 dB depending on soil moisture, and that canopy height adds a consistent excess loss of 2.1 dB per metre of effective crop height. A corrected empirical model with three seasonal coefficients is proposed and validated against a held-out test dataset from a separate farm site. The model achieves a root-mean-square error of 4.3 dB over all vegetation states.

title: Return voltage measurements on power transformers with mixed insulation: oil-impregnated kraft paper and aramid pressboard
abstract: Several transformer manufacturers have introduced aramid-fibre-based pressboard (aramid pressboard) as a partial replacement for kraft pressboard in high-temperature winding constructions. This creates insulation systems with two distinct dielectric components whose polarisation time constants differ substantially. Return voltage measurements were performed on laboratory models containing combinations of kraft pressboard and aramid pressboard in series, with oil-gap fractions of 10 %, 20 %, and 30 %. Measurements used a constant charge voltage of 1000 V with charge times ranging from 10 s to 10 000 s. The resulting return voltage spectra showed two overlapping peaks whose separation and relative amplitudes varied with the material ratio and moisture level of each component. A two-component generalised exponential model was fitted to 48 measured spectra. The fitted time constants for each component agreed with those measured on single-material specimens within 8 %. The study provides guidance on interpreting RVM data from transformers containing mixed insulation, where single-peak models may yield misleading central time constants.

title: Adaptive Spectral Subtraction for Wearable Microphone Arrays in Ambulatory Conditions
abstract: Wearable microphone arrays in ambulatory settings face severe non-stationary noise from clothing friction, movement artefacts, and environmental sources. This study evaluates a two-microphone adaptive spectral subtraction scheme implemented on a 16-bit fixed-point DSP running at 12 MHz. Thirty-two hour-long recordings were collected from eight healthy volunteers performing standardised daily activities—walking, stair climbing, and sitting—in a university corridor environment with measured background noise levels between 52 and 74 dB SPL. The proposed algorithm estimates a noise reference from the secondary microphone using a recursive minimum statistics tracker with a 0.4-second time constant, then subtracts a weighted spectral estimate from the primary channel. Compared with single-channel spectral subtraction, the two-channel approach reduced the signal-to-noise ratio estimation error by 3.1 dB on average across all activity conditions. Musical noise artefacts, measured by spectral flatness, were reduced by 18% relative to the single-channel baseline. Computational cost was 67% of available processor cycles at the target sampling rate of 16 kHz, leaving margin for a subsequent classifier stage. The work identifies specific failure modes at transition boundaries between activity types and proposes a heuristic activity-gating trigger to mitigate them.

title: Energy-Based Acoustic Event Detection on Cortex-M3 Microcontrollers for Ambient Monitoring
abstract: Ambient acoustic monitoring in residential settings for elderly care requires event detectors that can run continuously on coin-cell batteries. This paper describes an energy-based segmentation scheme paired with a short-time Fourier transform feature extractor implemented on a Cortex-M3 microcontroller clocked at 8 MHz. The target events are door closing, glass breaking, and a distress-call vocalisation. A dataset of 1,240 labelled clips was collected in three furnished rooms with varying reverberation times (RT60 between 0.18 s and 0.51 s). The detector uses a two-threshold hysteresis comparator operating on a 20 ms frame energy estimate, consuming an average of 1.4 mA in active mode and dropping to 0.08 mA during silence periods. On the collected dataset, the system achieved an F1 score of 0.83 for door closing, 0.79 for glass breaking, and 0.71 for distress vocalisation under background television noise. Total battery life in a simulated 24-hour deployment was estimated at 11 days with a 650 mAh cell. The paper discusses the trade-off between sensitivity threshold and false-alarm rate in detail, providing receiver operating characteristic curves for each event class.

title: Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients versus Gammatone Filter Bank Features for Cough Detection Under Cafeteria Noise
abstract: Cough is a clinically relevant acoustic event whose automatic detection is confounded by the high and variable background noise typical of public spaces. This paper compares MFCC (13 coefficients, 25 ms frames, 10 ms hop) with a 32-channel gammatone filter bank representation for cough detection using a support vector machine classifier with radial basis function kernel. Evaluation was performed on a 6-hour dataset recorded from 24 participants (12 with chronic respiratory conditions, 12 healthy controls) in a university cafeteria where ambient noise was measured at 61–78 dB SPL. Ground truth annotations were provided by two clinicians who reached agreement on 94% of events. The gammatone representation yielded a sensitivity of 0.86 and specificity of 0.91 on a held-out test set, compared with 0.81 and 0.88 for MFCCs. Adding first- and second-order delta features improved both representations by 2–4 percentage points. Computational profiling showed that gammatone extraction required 2.3 times more multiply-accumulate operations per frame than MFCC on a fixed-point target processor, an important consideration for embedded deployment. The paper recommends MFCC with delta features as the practical choice when processor headroom below 40% is required.

title: Real-Time Wheeze Detection on a Low-Power ARM Processor Using a Hidden Markov Model
abstract: Wheeze detection from tracheal sounds recorded with a contact microphone is examined using a discrete-state hidden Markov model (HMM) implemented in C on an ARM Cortex-M4 processor operating at 16 MHz. Tracheal recordings from 41 patients with obstructive lung disease and 20 healthy controls were collected during spirometry-guided breathing manoeuvres at the Institute of Pulmonology in Novi Sad. Each 30-second recording was segmented into inspiration and expiration phases using a hand-labelled reference; wheezes were identified by a pulmonologist. The HMM used eight states and was trained on 70% of recordings using the Baum–Welch algorithm offline; the decoder ran in real time. Features consisted of 10 LPC coefficients computed over 20 ms frames. On the test set, the system achieved sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.85, and an average detection latency of 62 ms. Current consumption in continuous operation was 1.9 mA at 3.3 V, giving an estimated runtime of eight hours on a 600 mAh lithium polymer cell. The study discusses misclassification caused by swallowing artefacts and proposes a simple artefact rejection rule based on energy spike duration.

title: A Benchmark Dataset of Indoor Acoustic Events for Evaluating Low-Power Classifiers in Assisted-Living Scenarios
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of acoustic event classifiers for assisted-living applications is hampered by the scarcity of publicly documented datasets recorded under realistic domestic conditions. This paper describes the construction and annotation of the NovSAL dataset, comprising 4,800 labelled clips across 12 event classes (including kettle boiling, telephone ringing, smoke alarm, and human fall impact) recorded in three instrumented apartments in Novi Sad over six weeks. Each apartment was occupied by a volunteer resident and contained realistic background sources. Recordings were made at 44.1 kHz, 24-bit, with calibrated omnidirectional microphones; they were subsequently downsampled to 16 kHz for classifier evaluation. Six baseline classifiers—energy threshold, Gaussian mixture model, random forest, k-nearest neighbour, support vector machine, and a two-layer perceptron—are evaluated with stratified 5-fold cross-validation. The random forest achieves the highest macro-average F1 of 0.80, while the energy threshold baseline reaches only 0.51. Inter-annotator agreement across three annotators was 0.87 Fleiss's kappa. The dataset, annotation protocol, and feature extraction code are released under a CC BY 4.0 licence.

title: Compressed Sensing Reconstruction for Sparse Acoustic Feature Vectors on Resource-Constrained Nodes
abstract: Transmitting raw audio from a wireless sensor node to a base station for event classification is energetically prohibitive for battery-powered devices. This paper investigates whether compressed sensing can reduce the communication payload while preserving sufficient information for a support vector machine classifier. Log-mel filter bank vectors (40 channels, 25 ms frames) from the NovSAL dataset are treated as the sparse signal; measurement matrices of sizes 10×40, 15×40, and 20×40 are tested. Reconstruction uses the LASSO algorithm on a host processor; the compressed measurements are transmitted over IEEE 802.15.4 radio. At a compression ratio of 2.7 (15 measurements), reconstruction error (normalised MSE) was 0.034, and classifier F1 on the 12 NovSAL classes dropped by only 0.03 points relative to the uncompressed baseline, while radio energy per classification was reduced by 41%. At ratio 4.0 the F1 drop grew to 0.09, making it impractical. The paper provides a theoretical bound on the number of measurements required as a function of feature sparsity and validates it empirically on four event subsets. The approach is implemented and timed on a Cortex-M0+ node to confirm that measurement projection is affordable at 4 kHz equivalent frame rate.

title: Acoustic Event Detection in Noisy Embedded Systems
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of the signal processing pipeline for acoustic event detection when the target platform is a microcontroller or low-power DSP. Topics covered include noise estimation in non-stationary environments (minimum statistics, MMSE-based estimators), feature extraction at fixed-point arithmetic precision, classifier selection criteria under memory and latency constraints, and quantisation-aware training for small neural networks. Each stage is illustrated with worked examples drawn from the authors' own experimental work on domestic event detection and wearable respiratory monitoring. The chapter discusses failure modes specific to embedded deployments—clock jitter, interrupt latency, and analogue front-end noise—and their measurable impact on detection performance. A practical guide to profiling energy consumption at each pipeline stage is included, with data from three representative microcontroller families. The intended audience is graduate students and practitioners entering the field of embedded health monitoring.

title: Evaluating Quantisation Schemes for Convolutional Neural Network Acoustic Classifiers on ARM Cortex-M7
abstract: Deploying convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for acoustic event classification on microcontrollers requires aggressive model compression. This paper systematically evaluates four quantisation schemes—float32, float16, int8 post-training, and int8 quantisation-aware training (QAT)—for a three-layer 1-D CNN applied to the NovSAL 12-class dataset. The target processor is an ARM Cortex-M7 running at 216 MHz with 512 KB SRAM and 1 MB flash. Model size ranged from 280 KB (float32) to 71 KB (int8 QAT). Inference time per 25 ms frame was 4.1 ms for float32 and 1.8 ms for int8 QAT, leaving sufficient headroom for audio capture and feature extraction at 16 kHz. Macro-average F1 was 0.87 for float32 and 0.85 for int8 QAT, a statistically non-significant drop (paired permutation test, p=0.11). Float16 showed unexpected numerical instability in two event classes attributed to narrow dynamic range in the second-layer activations. Energy measurements taken with a bench power analyser showed a 34% reduction in per-inference energy for int8 QAT versus float32. The paper recommends int8 QAT as the default for this class of target hardware.

title: Battery-Free Acoustic Event Detector Powered by Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting
abstract: Maintenance of coin-cell batteries in distributed ambient monitoring nodes is a significant practical barrier. This paper presents a battery-free acoustic event detector node that harvests energy from mechanical vibrations using a 30×15 mm bimorph piezoelectric element attached to a ventilation duct. A custom power management circuit stores harvested charge in a 1 mF supercapacitor and releases it to a Cortex-M0+ processor only when the terminal voltage exceeds 2.8 V. The processor wakes, captures 500 ms of audio, extracts MFCC features, classifies the event using a pre-loaded decision tree, and transmits a one-byte label over a 433 MHz radio before returning to deep sleep. Available harvested power in the target installation was measured at 18–42 µW depending on duct airflow. The system achieved 97% duty availability during operating hours (07:00–20:00) and correctly classified four event classes (occupancy sound, mechanical fault click, door slam, silence) with macro-F1 of 0.79 in a two-week building trial. The paper provides a detailed energy budget and discusses the effect of supercapacitor self-discharge on detection latency.

title: Combining On-Device and Edge Processing for Wearable Respiratory Monitoring: Latency and Power Trade-offs
abstract: Hybrid architectures that perform lightweight event detection on a wearable node and offload complex classification to a nearby edge server offer a middle path between full on-device and fully cloud-based approaches. This paper characterises the trade-off space using a wearable respiratory monitor (Cortex-M4, BLE 5.0) communicating with a Raspberry Pi 4 edge server. The on-device first stage uses a fixed-threshold energy detector on the 100–2500 Hz band to gate audio upload, transmitting only when breath-sound activity is detected. Three second-stage classifiers—linear discriminant analysis, random forest, and a four-layer MLP—run on the edge server and classify wheeze, stridor, and normal breath sounds. In a 24-hour simulated home deployment with 18 participants, gating reduced BLE transmission time by 73%, extending wearable battery life from 9 h to 31 h. End-to-end 95th-percentile latency was 210 ms for all second-stage classifiers. Macro-F1 on a held-out night-time subset was 0.84 for the MLP, with the largest error between wheeze and normal in high-ambient-noise conditions (bedroom fan noise above 45 dB SPL). The paper presents a latency breakdown by pipeline stage and a power consumption model.

title: Noise-Robust Feature Extraction Using Perceptually Weighted Spectral Entropy for Embedded Health Monitoring
abstract: Standard spectral features degrade rapidly when the ambient noise floor rises above 60 dB SPL, a condition common in clinical waiting rooms, home kitchens, and outdoor settings. This paper introduces a perceptually weighted spectral entropy (PWSE) feature computed from a Bark-scale filter bank with MMSE gain function pre-processing, designed to remain stable across noise levels from 40 to 80 dB SPL. The PWSE computation requires 14% fewer multiply-accumulate operations per frame than a comparable MFCC pipeline on a Cortex-M33, confirmed by cycle-accurate simulation. Evaluation was performed on three tasks drawn from published datasets: cough versus non-cough (2,200 clips), wheeze versus normal breath (3,100 clips), and fall impact versus domestic transient (1,800 clips). PWSE achieved or exceeded MFCC F1 at all tested noise levels; the gap was largest at 75 dB SPL, where PWSE outperformed MFCC by 0.07 F1 points on the cough task and 0.09 on wheeze. The paper provides open-source fixed-point C implementation benchmarked on three microcontroller families.

title: Apnoea Episode Detection from Tracheal Contact Microphone Signals on a Sub-mW Wearable Node
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea affects a large fraction of the adult population but remains substantially undiagnosed partly because laboratory polysomnography is resource-intensive. This paper describes a wearable tracheal contact microphone node targeting apnoea episode detection during unsupervised home sleep. The hardware is built around an ultra-low-power DSP co-processor consuming 0.42 mW during active detection, paired with a rechargeable 100 mAh cell sufficient for nine nights of continuous operation. The detection algorithm uses a 1-second frame energy ratio between the 150–600 Hz respiratory band and the 600–2000 Hz noise estimation band, with a context window of seven frames to identify absence-of-breath episodes longer than 10 seconds. Validation was performed against overnight polysomnography records from 29 participants (14 with confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA, 15 healthy sleepers) at the Sleep Disorders Unit, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. The algorithm detected apnoea episodes with sensitivity 0.84 and specificity 0.88 per 30-second epoch. Hypopnoeas were not targeted. False positives concentrated in the body-position-change transitions; a 3-axis accelerometer signal used as a gating veto reduced false positives by 31%. The paper provides a full energy budget and compares detection latency against a reference pulse-oximetry system.

title: Federated Domain Adaptation for Brain Lesion Segmentation Without Sharing Patient Data
abstract: Cross-institutional segmentation of white-matter lesions in FLAIR MRI is hampered by scanner heterogeneity and privacy constraints that prevent centralising data. We implemented a federated learning framework in which five sites each train a local U-Net on their own FLAIR data and exchange only model gradients, with domain adaptation achieved by aligning intermediate feature distributions through a site-adversarial head attached to the bottleneck layer. The five sites contributed between 63 and 141 annotated volumes each, acquired on scanners ranging from 1.5 T to 3 T with three different manufacturers. Federated training with domain adversarial alignment reduced mean surface distance error by 22% relative to training at each site independently and by 11% relative to federated training without alignment. Performance was within 4% of a centralised upper bound. The framework was tested under 200 ms simulated network latency with no convergence failure across 300 communication rounds.

title: Comparison of R-peak detection algorithms under motion artifact conditions in wrist-worn PPG
abstract: Wrist photoplethysmography (PPG) is widely used for heart rate estimation, but motion artifacts substantially degrade beat detection accuracy during physical activity. This study benchmarked six peak detection algorithms—including adaptive thresholding, matched filtering, and two deep-learning-based approaches—on a dataset of 22 participants who cycled on a stationary ergometer at 50, 100, and 150 W for four minutes each, with synchronous finger-clip PPG and single-lead ECG as references. Algorithms were evaluated by mean absolute error of inter-beat interval and by F1 score of individual beat detection. The matched-filter approach achieved MAE of 18.3 ms and F1 of 0.91 at 100 W, the best overall, while deep-learning methods underperformed on the small dataset. The findings emphasise that algorithm choice should depend on expected activity intensity and available computational resources.

title: Separating microvascular and macrovascular contributions to the NIRS signal during rhythmic handgrip exercise using a venous occlusion approach
abstract: Near-infrared spectroscopy signals in exercising muscle contain contributions from capillaries, venules, and arterioles whose relative volumes change with exercise intensity. We applied intermittent venous occlusion cuff inflation (50 mmHg, 10 s on, 30 s off) during a rhythmic handgrip protocol at 30% and 60% MVC in 14 volunteers to isolate the venous compartment contribution. The venous occlusion slope of OHb increase during occlusion intervals provided an estimate of muscle oxygen consumption (mVO₂). At 30% MVC, estimated mVO₂ was 0.11 ± 0.02 mL O₂ min⁻¹ 100 g⁻¹ and at 60% MVC it was 0.21 ± 0.04 mL O₂ min⁻¹ 100 g⁻¹. Comparison with simultaneous Doppler ultrasound blood flow measurements in the radial artery showed correlation r = 0.81 between optical and ultrasound-derived oxygen extraction estimates. The arterial portion was isolated by superimposing brief 20 s arterial occlusions and examining the desaturation kinetics. Results suggest that at moderate intensities approximately 55% of the signal variance originates from venous compartment dynamics.

title: Diffuse optical spectroscopy characterisation of the haemodynamic response to blood flow restriction training in the biceps brachii
abstract: Blood flow restriction (BFR) training combines low-load resistance exercise with partial arterial occlusion to induce metabolic stress comparable to high-load training. We monitored the biceps brachii using FD-NIRS in 24 participants performing three sets of dumbbell curls at 30% 1-RM with and without a pneumatic cuff inflated to 60% limb occlusion pressure. Absolute µa and µs′ were converted to OHb, DHb, and total haemoglobin (tHb) at 10 Hz. During BFR sets, end-set DHb peaked at 52 ± 11 µM versus 28 ± 9 µM in the control condition (p < 0.001), and tHb was elevated by 18% at set completion, consistent with venous trapping. Between-set StO₂ recovery was 47% slower under BFR (recovery half-time 62 ± 14 s vs. 33 ± 8 s). Lean arm cross-sectional area measured by ultrasound moderated the StO₂ response (β = −0.41, p = 0.03). These data characterise the optical oxygenation signature of BFR and provide reference values for future interventions.

title: Pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic modelling of gentamicin in neonates with hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy and varying degrees of renal maturation
abstract: Neonates with hypoxic–ischaemic encephalopathy undergoing therapeutic hypothermia present a pharmacokinetic challenge for aminoglycoside dosing because both renal maturation and hypothermia affect drug clearance. We developed a population PK–PD model for gentamicin using 218 serum concentrations from 53 term and near-term neonates treated at the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of the Institute for Child and Youth Healthcare of Vojvodina. A one-compartment model was fitted with postmenstrual age and serum creatinine as covariates on clearance, and body weight as a covariate on volume. Hypothermia (33–34 °C core temperature) was associated with a 22% reduction in clearance compared with normothermia (90% CI: 11–33%). PD target attainment for Cmax/MIC ≥ 10 at standard 5 mg/kg dosing was only 54% in cooled neonates, improving to 71% with an adjusted 6.5 mg/kg dose. Therapeutic drug monitoring with Bayesian feedback from the first dose is recommended to avoid both under-exposure and nephrotoxicity.

title: Estimating individual AUC from two timed samples during vancomycin therapy: performance of limited sampling strategies across renal function categories
abstract: Full pharmacokinetic profiles for vancomycin AUC estimation are impractical in routine hospital care. Limited sampling strategies (LSS) using one or two timed concentrations with regression equations or Bayesian estimation offer a workable alternative, but their performance across different levels of renal function has not been rigorously assessed in a regional clinical population. We collected full eight-point concentration–time profiles from 41 adult patients across four eGFR categories (≥60, 30–59, 15–29, <15 mL/min/1.73 m²) at steady state. Trapezoidal AUC24 from full profiles served as the reference. Seven published two-point LSS were evaluated by MPE and RMSE, and a locally derived regression equation was developed. Bayesian estimation using a locally calibrated prior outperformed all regression-based LSS in patients with eGFR below 30, achieving RMSE of 21.6 mg·h/L compared with 38–62 mg·h/L for regression methods. For patients with near-normal renal function, the simplest published regression performed comparably to Bayesian methods. Results inform practical TDM protocols stratified by renal function.

title: Forced Heirship in Socialist Yugoslavia: Legislative Origins and Doctrinal Foundations
abstract: This article traces the legislative history of compulsory share provisions in Yugoslav succession law from the enactment of the 1955 Law on Inheritance through the constitutional reforms of the 1970s. Drawing on parliamentary records, published commentaries, and doctrinal writings of the period, the study identifies three distinct rationales that shaped the Yugoslav forced heirship model: socialist redistribution ideology, protection of surviving dependants, and continuity with pre-war civil law traditions inherited from the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. The article maps how each rationale was weighted differently across the six republics and argues that the resulting normative compromise—generous reserved portions combined with broad testamentary discretion over the freely disposable share—was inherently unstable and became a source of litigation after 1990. The analysis provides a baseline for subsequent comparative work on post-1990 reforms in successor states. Sources include the Official Gazette of the SFRY for the period 1945–1990 and selected first-instance court decisions published in regional law reviews.

title: The Serbian Law on Inheritance of 1995: A Reform Interrupted
abstract: Serbia's 1995 Law on Inheritance was enacted during a period of acute political and economic instability, and this article examines how that context limited the scope of reform. Using a combination of legislative history analysis and structured comparison with the contemporaneous Hungarian and Croatian inheritance statutes, the study shows that Serbian lawmakers retained the socialist-era reserved portion of one-half for close relatives with only minor adjustments to the class of protected heirs. The article reconstructs the parliamentary debate through stenographic records and identifies three failed amendment proposals that would have introduced greater testamentary freedom. It further documents how notarial practitioners in Vojvodina adapted contract-based instruments—particularly the contract on lifetime maintenance—to achieve outcomes that strict testamentary rules did not permit. Forty-three published notarial decisions from the period 1996–2008 are coded and analysed. The article concludes that the 1995 law represents a missed opportunity for deeper liberalisation and sets out criteria for evaluating any future reform.

title: Testamentary Freedom and Its Limits: A Comparative Survey of Seven Post-Socialist Central European Jurisdictions
abstract: This book chapter presents a structured comparative analysis of testamentary freedom rules in Bulgaria, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Serbia, and Slovenia as of 2012. For each jurisdiction the chapter identifies: the size of the freely disposable share, the categories of heirs entitled to a forced portion, the legal consequences of violation, and mechanisms available to reduce or waive the forced share by agreement. Data were collected from primary legislation, constitutional court decisions, and academic commentaries in the respective national languages. The chapter finds that the seven countries cluster into two broad groups: those that retained large compulsory shares broadly comparable to the socialist baseline (Bulgaria, Serbia) and those that reduced or restructured forced heirship to emphasise claims-based rather than automatic share entitlement (Czech Republic, Hungary post-2013 draft). The chapter also notes a common trend across all jurisdictions toward expanded recognition of freedom of testation for childless testators. The analysis is intended as a reference tool for law reform commissions and comparative law scholars.

title: Disinheritance Clauses in Serbian Wills: An Empirical Study of Notarial Records 2000–2015
abstract: Serbian law permits testators to exclude compulsory heirs from the estate only on grounds expressly listed in the Civil Code, including serious criminal offences against the testator and deliberate failure to provide support. This article reports findings from a systematic review of 318 notarised wills deposited with four notary offices in Novi Sad and Subotica between 2000 and 2015 in which a disinheritance clause was present. The study codes each clause according to the stated ground, the kinship category of the disinherited heir, the estimated estate size, and whether the clause was subsequently challenged in contentious proceedings. Key findings: 71 per cent of disinheritance clauses cited lack of contact rather than a legally recognised ground, rendering them formally invalid; only 23 per cent of challenged clauses were ultimately upheld by first-instance courts; clauses targeting children were challenged at twice the rate of those targeting siblings. The article argues that the narrow statutory grounds for disinheritance are out of step with contemporary family structures and recommends a reform that introduces a general estrangement ground, as has been adopted in Austria and the Czech Republic after 2015.

title: The Austrian Succession Law Reform of 2015: Lessons for South-Eastern European Jurisdictions
abstract: Austria's Erbrechts-Änderungsgesetz 2015 introduced the most substantial revision of Austrian succession law since 1811, including a reduced and claims-based forced share, an estrangement ground for disinheritance, and new rules on gifts made during the testator's lifetime. This article examines the reform in detail and evaluates its potential as a model for South-Eastern European countries that retain the older forced heirship structure. The analysis proceeds in three stages: a doctrinal exposition of the Austrian changes; a structured comparison with Serbian, Croatian, and Slovenian rules; and an assessment of the socio-economic preconditions—especially pension system coverage and elderly care arrangements—that condition the feasibility of reducing forced shares. The article draws on Austrian parliamentary materials, the official explanatory memorandum, and published commentary by Viennese notarial practitioners. The conclusion is that a claims-based model is technically compatible with Serbian private law doctrine but would require simultaneous reform of elder care legislation to avoid adverse welfare effects for elderly parents.

title: Pact on Future Succession in Serbian Private Law: Prohibition, Circumvention, and Reform Prospects
abstract: Serbian law, following the socialist civil law tradition, prohibits contracts concerning a living person's future estate. This prohibition, enshrined in Article 102 of the 1995 Law on Inheritance, is subject to only one narrow exception: the contract on lifetime maintenance. This article maps the scope of the prohibition through an analysis of 87 published Supreme Court of Cassation and appellate court decisions issued between 1996 and 2020. It documents recurring patterns of circumvention through sale-of-future-claim agreements, gift instruments with reversion clauses, and mixed-type contracts. The article then examines the progressive relaxation of the prohibition in German, Austrian, and Czech law and assesses whether a limited admission of succession pacts—covering only spousal agreements and family business transfers—would be compatible with the Serbian constitutional framework and with EU succession regulation No. 650/2012. A draft statutory provision is proposed and its implications for forced heirship protection are assessed. The study relies on doctrinal analysis and comparative legal method; no primary empirical data were collected.

title: Cross-Border Succession in the Western Balkans: Jurisdictional Conflicts and the Reach of EU Regulation 650/2012
abstract: EU Succession Regulation 650/2012 applies to the estates of EU citizens dying after August 2015 but does not bind non-member states. For decedents with assets in both EU member states and Western Balkan non-member states (Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia), the regulation creates asymmetric conflict-of-law outcomes. This conference paper analyses three categories of recurring conflict: (i) characterisation disputes over whether a deceased's habitual residence was in an EU state or in Serbia; (ii) forced heirship renvoi problems when the applicable law points to Serbian law but the estate includes immovable property in Hungary or Croatia; and (iii) recognition of European Certificates of Succession in Serbian administrative proceedings. The paper draws on 14 interview transcripts with notaries practising in Subotica, Sombor, and Kikinda—border areas with a high incidence of cross-border estates—supplemented by documentary analysis. The paper recommends that Serbia conclude bilateral succession treaties with Hungary and Croatia as an interim measure pending potential EU accession.

title: Testamentary Capacity and Cognitive Decline: Medical Evidence in Serbian Inheritance Litigation
abstract: Challenges to testamentary capacity on grounds of dementia or other cognitive impairment have become more frequent in Serbian courts as the population ages. This article examines 102 first-instance judgments from Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin basic courts issued between 2010 and 2021 in which testamentary capacity was contested. Using content analysis, the study maps what categories of medical evidence were presented, how courts weighted psychiatric expert reports against earlier notarial assessments of capacity, and what the outcome distribution was across different dementia diagnoses. Findings show that psychiatric expert testimony was determinative in 68 per cent of cases; courts relied exclusively on the notarial record in only 9 per cent. Will invalidation rates were substantially higher (58 per cent) for holographic wills than for notarial wills (22 per cent). The article evaluates these patterns against comparative standards applied in Austrian and German courts and proposes procedural guidelines for Serbian notaries examining elderly testators.

title: Family Business Succession in Serbia: Gaps in Private Law and Practical Workarounds
abstract: Succession to small and medium-sized family businesses in Serbia is poorly served by the existing inheritance and company law framework. This article identifies four structural gaps: the prohibition on succession pacts, the absence of business continuation agreements, the mandatory equal division among forced heirs, and the lack of estate administration procedures suited to ongoing business assets. The analysis draws on 27 semi-structured interviews with business owners, notaries, and lawyers in Vojvodina conducted between 2019 and 2021, combined with a review of legislative materials and comparative examples from Slovenia (2019 Companies Act amendments) and Hungary (2013 Civil Code provisions on business succession). The interview data reveal that practitioners routinely combine lifetime gift contracts, company share restructuring, and loan agreements to simulate the economic outcome of prohibited succession pacts. The article evaluates these workarounds against the forced heirship rules and argues that reform of both succession law and company law is needed simultaneously. A legislative agenda is outlined, with reference to the EU Commission's 2006 Recommendation on business transfers.

title: The Reserved Share as a Percentage: Comparing Quantum Rules Across Twelve European Jurisdictions
abstract: This article compiles and compares the quantitative dimension of forced heirship across twelve European jurisdictions: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, and Slovenia. For each country the article records the current statutory fraction of the estate reserved for each category of heir, the treatment of inter vivos gifts in the calculation base, and the procedural mechanism through which a shortfall is remedied (automatic reduction, personal claim, or action for supplement). Data were drawn from current legislation, official legal databases, and published academic commentaries, all verified as of January 2024. The article constructs a comparative index of restrictiveness that ranks the twelve systems and finds that Serbia and Romania rank as the most restrictive, while Germany and the Czech Republic rank as least restrictive among the sampled group. The index controls for differences in gift claw-back rules and debtor-protection exemptions. The article does not advocate a particular reform direction but provides a reference tool intended to be used in policy discussions.

title: Succession Law Reform and the Serbian Civil Code Project: An Assessment of the 2023 Draft Provisions
abstract: The Serbian Ministry of Justice's ongoing Civil Code drafting project published succession law provisions in a consultative draft in late 2022. This article provides a systematic assessment of those provisions against the background of the existing 1995 Law on Inheritance, the comparative literature, and the results of empirical research conducted by the author over the preceding decade. The draft introduces three significant changes: a reduction of the reserved share for descendants from one-half to one-third of the intestate share; a new estrangement ground for disinheritance; and a limited recognition of succession pacts between spouses for the matrimonial home. The article evaluates each change for internal consistency, alignment with EU succession regulation requirements, and adequacy of transitional provisions. It identifies six ambiguities in the draft text that are likely to generate litigation and proposes specific textual corrections. The analysis is based on the published draft, the explanatory memorandum, and comparative material from Austria, Croatia, and the Czech Republic.

title: Digital Assets in Post-Socialist Succession Law: Conceptual Problems and Preliminary Observations
abstract: The inheritance of digital assets—cryptocurrency holdings, online business accounts, subscription services, and social media profiles—raises questions that post-socialist civil codes were not designed to answer. This preprint surveys the existing legal framework in Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary and identifies three structural difficulties: the characterisation of digital assets as property within civil law categories, the evidentiary challenge of locating and accessing assets whose existence may be unknown to heirs, and the interaction between platform terms of service and forced heirship rules where the platform operates under a foreign governing law. The paper draws on published court decisions from Germany and the United States, guidance documents from notarial associations in Austria and France, and 12 interviews with IT lawyers and notaries in Novi Sad and Zagreb conducted in 2024–2025. The paper is framed as a problem survey rather than a conclusions article; it is intended to inform an ongoing legislative working group convened by the Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad. Comments are invited before final submission.

title: Autonomous Systems in Construction Contracts: Risk Allocation and Supervision Duties
abstract: Automated construction management systems increasingly control scheduling, procurement, and quality monitoring on large infrastructure projects in Serbia. This article examines how the standard FIDIC contract forms and Serbian construction law allocate risk when these systems produce erroneous outputs leading to cost overruns or defects. The analysis covers three anonymised construction disputes from the period 2018–2022 involving infrastructure projects on the Corridor 10 and Corridor 11 road networks. Using a doctrinal method supplemented by structured interviews with five construction law practitioners, the article maps the duty of supervision under Serbian construction regulations against the outputs of automated project management tools. It finds that existing contractual risk matrices do not adequately address situations where no human reviewer checked an automated recommendation before it was acted upon, and proposes model contractual language for future procurements.

title: The EU AI Act and Serbian Contract Law: Liability Consequences of High-Risk AI System Classification
abstract: The EU AI Act (2024) introduces a risk-based classification of AI systems and imposes conformity obligations on providers and deployers, with high-risk systems facing the most stringent requirements. This article examines how the obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems under the AI Act interact with contractual liability toward affected natural persons under Serbian law in the context of Serbian EU accession negotiations. The author analyses the supply chain of obligations from AI provider to deployer to end user, and identifies three contract law problems: (i) how deployer conformity obligations translate into implied contractual terms; (ii) whether non-conformity constitutes a breach giving rise to damages claims by contractual partners; and (iii) how limitation clauses in provider–deployer agreements will be assessed for validity. The article uses a hypothetical case study involving an HR screening platform deployed by a Serbian employer and traces liability pathways for a rejected job applicant.

title: Co-Ownership of Common Parts in Multi-Unit Buildings: A Comparative Analysis of Serbian and Croatian Legislation
abstract: This article examines the statutory frameworks governing co-ownership of common parts in multi-unit residential buildings in Serbia and Croatia, focusing on the period following the adoption of Serbia's Law on Housing and Building Maintenance (2016) and Croatia's Ownership and Other Real Rights Act. The study employs doctrinal legal analysis and comparative methodology, drawing on primary legislative texts, commentary literature, and selected case law from both jurisdictions. Eighteen cases from Serbian municipal courts and twelve from Croatian county courts were reviewed to identify patterns in judicial interpretation of proportional share calculations and maintenance cost allocation. Results indicate significant divergence in how the two systems define the boundaries of exclusive versus common ownership, particularly regarding load-bearing structures, roof surfaces, and basement utility rooms. The article argues that the Serbian framework's reliance on building area ratios creates practical difficulties when buildings contain mixed residential and commercial units, and it proposes clarifying amendments modelled partly on the Croatian approach.

title: A Constraint-Based Framework for Schema Correspondence Discovery in Relational Databases
abstract: Schema matching between relational databases often relies on name similarity and structural heuristics, which perform poorly when attribute names are abbreviated or domain-specific. This paper introduces a framework that encodes integrity constraints—primary keys, foreign keys, check constraints, and functional dependencies—as logical predicates and uses constraint propagation to narrow the space of candidate correspondences. The approach was evaluated on 14 pairs of real administrative database schemas from three Serbian municipal registries, comprising between 40 and 210 attributes per schema. Precision of the top-ranked matches reached 0.81 on average, compared with 0.67 for a name-similarity baseline and 0.72 for a combined linguistic-structural baseline. The framework operates without a predefined domain ontology, making it applicable in settings where such resources are absent. Runtime scales roughly linearly with the number of constraints and remains under 90 seconds for all tested schema pairs on commodity hardware.

title: Benchmark Construction for Tabular Schema Matching: Methodology and a Regional Administrative Dataset
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of schema matching systems requires benchmark datasets that reflect realistic heterogeneity. Existing benchmarks predominantly cover English-language corporate or biomedical schemas; comparable resources for South-East European administrative data are lacking. This paper describes a methodology for constructing matching benchmarks from publicly available municipal and cadastral databases, covering attribute renaming, type coercion, vertical partitioning, and denormalisation as transformation types. A benchmark comprising 22 schema pairs derived from Serbian and Croatian administrative sources was assembled and manually annotated by three independent experts, with inter-annotator agreement measured using Fleiss's kappa (κ = 0.79). The benchmark is released under an open licence alongside tooling for generating transformation variants. Baseline results for five publicly available matchers are reported, revealing that all systems degrade substantially under vertical partitioning transformations, with F1 scores dropping by 18–34 percentage points relative to the renaming-only condition.
