title: Ontology Alignment as a Mediator for Cross-Source Record Linkage in Healthcare Data
abstract: Record linkage across healthcare datasets is hampered by inconsistent coding of clinical concepts alongside the usual name and date variation in patient identifiers. This paper presents a pipeline that first aligns source-specific informal terminologies to a shared biomedical ontology using a weighted combination of lexical and structural similarity, then uses the aligned concept mappings as typed blocking keys for subsequent probabilistic record linkage. The method was tested on two synthetic patient registries generated from a de-identified regional dataset of 120,000 records, with controlled introduction of errors at rates matching those observed in practice. Recall at a false-match rate of 1% reached 0.91 with ontology-guided blocking, versus 0.83 with standard phonetic blocking. The alignment step required manual validation of 7% of proposed correspondences, substantially lower than the 23% required by direct linkage without ontological mediation. The pipeline is implemented as modular Python components.

title: Declarative Data Quality Rules for Tabular Integration Pipelines: Specification and Automated Checking
abstract: Data quality problems in integration pipelines are often detected late, after erroneous records have propagated through multiple transformation steps. This paper proposes a declarative language for expressing data quality rules over tabular sources, covering completeness, domain conformance, referential consistency, and cross-column dependency constraints. Rules are compiled into SQL CHECK expressions and evaluated incrementally as new data batches arrive. The specification language was designed to be accessible to domain analysts without programming expertise, using a controlled natural language surface syntax. A user study with 12 participants from two Serbian public institutions showed that analysts with no SQL background could write correct rules for 78% of test scenarios after a two-hour training session. Automated checking was integrated into a lightweight ETL framework and evaluated on five operational data feeds from a regional land registry, detecting between 3% and 11% of records as quality-violating across the feeds.

title: Probabilistic Record Linkage Under Attribute Uncertainty: A Fellegi–Sunter Extension with Soft Evidence
abstract: The classical Fellegi–Sunter model assigns binary agreement weights to attribute comparisons, which is inadequate when attribute values are themselves uncertain—for instance, when OCR-transcribed documents carry confidence scores. This paper extends the model by replacing binary comparison outcomes with soft evidence distributions derived from OCR confidence, date parsing ambiguity, and address geocoding uncertainty. The extended model is estimated using the EM algorithm, with the soft-evidence likelihoods entering the expectation step as weighted fractional counts. Experiments were conducted on a historical population register from Vojvodina comprising approximately 85,000 transcribed entries with associated OCR confidence metadata. Compared with the standard binary Fellegi–Sunter baseline, the soft-evidence extension improved F1 by 4.2 percentage points at the operating threshold selected to minimise clerical review burden. The improvement was largest for records with moderate OCR confidence (0.6–0.8), where binary discretisation loses the most information.

title: Integrating Open Government Datasets via Lightweight Domain Ontologies: A Case Study in Urban Mobility
abstract: Open government data portals publish datasets in varied formats and with inconsistent vocabularies, limiting automated integration. This paper reports a case study in which seven open datasets related to urban mobility in the City of Novi Sad—covering public transport stops, road incidents, parking zones, and pedestrian counts—were integrated using a lightweight OWL ontology constructed semi-automatically from dataset metadata. Schema-to-ontology mappings were derived using an existing matcher extended with gazetteer-based geographic concept recognition. The integrated knowledge graph contained approximately 340,000 triples and was used to answer ten competency questions defined with municipal analysts. Four of the ten questions required multi-dataset joins that would have been impossible without mediation through the ontology. Mapping accuracy was 0.88 precision and 0.83 recall; remaining errors were concentrated in temporal attribute representations, where date format heterogeneity was particularly pronounced.

title: Entity Resolution in Multilingual Tabular Data: Handling Serbian Cyrillic–Latin Transcription and Diacritic Variation
abstract: Entity resolution in South-East European administrative data must contend with script duality (Cyrillic and Latin representations of Serbian), inconsistent diacritic usage, and transliteration variation that standard phonetic encoders do not handle. This paper presents a preprocessing and comparison layer specifically designed for Serbian-language tabular records, incorporating a rule-based Cyrillic–Latin normaliser, a diacritic-robust string distance metric derived from Jaro–Winkler, and a learned classifier that combines normalised string features with administrative code agreement. The system was evaluated on a manually labelled dataset of 9,400 record pairs drawn from two voter registration extracts with known linkage status. F-measure reached 0.94, compared with 0.87 for a Latin-only Jaro–Winkler baseline and 0.89 for an existing generic multilingual matcher. Error analysis shows that remaining false negatives are concentrated in records where both name and address were independently transcribed with errors.

title: Schema Matching for Tabular Data Exports from ERP Systems: Patterns and Failure Modes
abstract: Enterprise resource planning systems produce tabular exports whose schema structure is shaped by vendor conventions rather than domain semantics, creating systematic difficulties for automatic schema matching. This paper analyses 41 schema pairs from ERP export files provided by eight companies in the manufacturing and logistics sectors in the Vojvodina region. A taxonomy of 12 recurring schema patterns is introduced, covering code-column concatenation, multi-valued delimited cells, silent null conventions, and vendor-specific date epoch offsets. For each pattern, the failure rate of three representative matchers (a linguistic matcher, a structural matcher, and a machine learning matcher trained on public benchmarks) is reported. Linguistic matchers fail most severely on code-column patterns (precision drop of 0.31), while structural matchers are most affected by multi-valued cells. The analysis informs a set of pre-matching normalisation rules whose application raises average matcher precision by 0.12 across all three systems.

title: Incremental Ontology-Driven Integration of Streaming Agricultural Sensor Data
abstract: Precision agriculture deployments generate continuous streams from heterogeneous sensors—soil moisture probes, weather stations, and drone-mounted multispectral cameras—each with its own data model and update frequency. This paper describes an incremental integration architecture in which a shared agricultural ontology mediates between streaming sources, and schema-to-ontology mappings are maintained and revised as sensor firmware updates alter field names or units. The architecture uses a sliding-window change detector to identify structural drift in incoming streams and triggers targeted re-matching only for affected schema fragments. Evaluated on 18 months of operational data from a pilot precision agriculture installation covering 420 hectares in the Bačka region, the system processed an average of 2.1 million attribute values per day with a mapping latency under 400 milliseconds. Structural drift events occurred 14 times during the evaluation period; automated re-matching resolved 11 without human intervention.
venue: Computers and Electronics in Agriculture

title: Data Quality Profiling of Integrated Supply Chain Datasets: A Constraint Discovery Approach
abstract: Integrated supply chain datasets assembled from supplier, warehouse, and logistics systems accumulate quality problems that are difficult to characterise without domain-specific rule sets. This paper proposes an approach that mines approximate functional dependencies and inclusion dependencies from integrated tabular data and uses these as automatically discovered quality constraints for ongoing profiling. Discovered constraints are ranked by coverage and interestingness scores and presented to domain stewards for validation; accepted constraints are then applied to incoming data batches as quality monitors. The method was applied to a dataset of 1.4 million order and shipment records from a composite supply chain dataset assembled from four source systems in the food processing sector in Vojvodina. Automated mining proposed 218 candidate constraints; domain stewards validated 134, of which 41 were found to be violated in the current integrated dataset, flagging approximately 6.3% of records as requiring review. Runtime for the full mining pass was under three hours on a single server.

title: Measured transient voltages on DC cabling of a grid-connected PV system during nearby lightning events
abstract: Transient overvoltages induced by indirect lightning strikes were recorded over an 18-month period on the DC bus of a 30 kWp rooftop photovoltaic installation in Novi Sad. A custom data acquisition system sampled at 10 MS/s and captured 47 events associated with verified lightning location system data from the regional meteorological network. Peak voltages on the DC positive-to-earth path ranged from 180 V to 1 420 V, with rise times between 0.8 µs and 6.2 µs. The amplitude distribution was correlated with strike distance (0.3–4.5 km), return-stroke peak current, and loop area of the DC wiring. Statistical analysis showed a lognormal fit for amplitude at a given distance with a geometric standard deviation of 1.8. The results provide an empirical basis for selecting SPD voltage protection levels for systems in the Pannonian region, where flat terrain and isolated tall structures produce above-average indirect-strike exposure. The dataset has been made publicly available.

title: Simulation model for surge propagation along PV string wiring using PSCAD/EMTDC
abstract: A lumped-parameter transmission line model for a single PV string of 12 series-connected modules was developed and validated in PSCAD/EMTDC. Module capacitances to frame (measured at 28–62 nF per module depending on irradiance and temperature) and DC cable series impedances were extracted from laboratory measurements and incorporated into the model. Simulated transient waveforms at the inverter DC input terminals were compared against field recordings from 23 captured events; the model reproduced peak voltage within ±15% and front time within ±0.6 µs for 19 of the 23 events. The remaining four discrepancies were attributed to soil resistivity variation. Sensitivity analysis identified cable loop inductance and module frame capacitance as the dominant parameters governing peak voltage at the inverter. The validated model was used to evaluate the effect of cable routing geometry on induced surge amplitude, showing reductions of up to 38% when DC positive and negative conductors are routed in close proximity.

title: Influence of earthing system configuration on common-mode and differential-mode surges in ungrounded PV arrays
abstract: The partitioning of surge energy between common-mode and differential-mode paths in IT-earthed and TT-earthed photovoltaic arrays was investigated through laboratory impulse testing and circuit simulation. Three earthing configurations were tested on a scaled 6-string laboratory mock-up: floating DC with TT AC side, floating DC with TN-S AC side, and array frame connected to AC earth. Impulse generators producing 8/20 µs and 1.2/50 µs waveforms at peak currents from 1 kA to 10 kA were applied at representative injection points. Common-mode voltage ratios at the inverter input varied from 0.31 to 0.87 depending on configuration and injection point. The TT AC side with floating DC showed the highest differential-mode stress on the inverter input, reaching 2.1 kV at 5 kA injection. Practical guidelines are derived for earthing bond placement to reduce differential-mode stress below the 1.5 kV withstand level typical of transformer-less string inverters.

title: Coordination of type 2 and type 3 SPDs in the DC sub-array junction box of a medium-scale PV plant
abstract: A coordination study was conducted for the surge protective devices installed in the combiner boxes of a 480 kWp ground-mounted PV plant located in Vojvodina. The plant uses 16 combiner boxes, each aggregating eight strings. Type 2 varistor-based SPDs are installed in each combiner box, and type 3 devices are fitted at each inverter DC input. The coordination criterion requires that the energy absorbed by the type 3 device does not exceed 40% of its rated single-pulse energy. Coordination was checked by injecting combination waves (1.2/50 µs voltage, 8/20 µs current) at the combiner box SPD, measuring the residual wave at the inverter terminals. Tests on 12 representative combinations of cable length (8–35 m) and SPD voltage protection levels showed that standard combinations with 1 kV protection level at type 2 and 700 V at type 3 failed coordination criteria when cable length fell below 12 m. A minimum separation inductance of 18 µH, achievable by routing cable in a loop, restored coordination in all tested cases.

title: Parametric study of lightning protection zone boundaries for roof-mounted PV installations on industrial buildings
abstract: The rolling-sphere method and the protective-angle method were applied to determine lightning protection zone boundaries for PV arrays mounted at various tilt angles (10°, 20°, 30°) and setback distances on flat and sloped industrial roofs. Sixty roof geometries were evaluated for three lightning protection levels (I, II, III) corresponding to rolling-sphere radii of 20 m, 30 m, and 45 m. Results show that modules at 30° tilt with zero setback on a flat roof cannot be placed within LPZ 0B under LPL II conditions without supplementary air termination, regardless of array position. A chart-based design aid was produced mapping permissible array positions as a function of building height (5–20 m), tilt angle, and required LPL. The study also evaluated the feasibility of using PV mounting frames as natural air terminations and identified minimum conductivity and cross-section requirements for aluminium extrusion profiles commonly used in utility-scale racking systems.

title: Degradation of metal-oxide varistors under repetitive surge stress representative of indirect lightning exposure
abstract: Forty-eight zinc-oxide varistor discs rated 275 V rms, 6 kA (8/20 µs), were subjected to repetitive impulse stress to quantify degradation under conditions representative of indirect lightning exposure. Three stress protocols were used: 100 pulses at 1 kA, 50 pulses at 3 kA, and 20 pulses at 6 kA (all 8/20 µs). Varistor clamping voltage, leakage current at 0.9 times rated dc voltage, and thermal dissipation factor were measured before and after each protocol. Clamping voltage increased by 4–11% after 100 pulses at 1 kA and by 18–27% after 20 pulses at 6 kA. Leakage current increased by one order of magnitude in eight of sixteen specimens stressed at 6 kA, indicating incipient failure. Scanning electron microscopy of cross-sections revealed grain boundary degradation concentrated in a cylindrical core region. The results suggest that standard SPD replacement intervals based solely on visual inspection or power-frequency leakage tests are insufficient for sites with high indirect-lightning flash density above 2 flashes km⁻² yr⁻¹.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery

title: Soil resistivity seasonal variation and its effect on the earthing resistance of ground-mounted PV plants in the Vojvodina plain
abstract: Soil resistivity at six sites in the Vojvodina region was measured monthly over two years using the Wenner four-electrode method at electrode spacings of 1, 2, 5, and 10 m. Resistivity varied between 18 Ω·m and 142 Ω·m depending on season and depth, with the highest values recorded in dry summer months (July–August) at shallow depths. The measured resistivity profiles were used as input to FEM-based earthing simulations to compute expected earth electrode resistance for horizontal ring electrodes and driven rod arrays sized according to IEC 62305-3. Calculated earthing resistances varied by a factor of 2.1 to 3.6 between winter and summer for the same electrode geometry. The study recommends that earthing system design for PV plants in the Pannonian lowlands use summer worst-case resistivity values, and provides a correction factor table for the six representative soil types identified. Field verification against actual resistance measurements at one 120 kWp plant confirmed the FEM results within 8%.

title: Surge immunity testing of string inverters under combined AC and DC impulse injection
abstract: Current standards for surge immunity testing of PV inverters apply impulses separately to the AC and DC ports. This study evaluates whether simultaneous injection on both ports produces stresses exceeding those from sequential single-port injection, using four commercially available string inverters rated 3–10 kW. Combined injection was performed by synchronising two impulse generators to deliver 8/20 µs pulses at the DC input and AC output terminals within a 2 µs window, at peak currents of 1 kA and 3 kA on each port. Internal voltage stress at the DC-link capacitor was measured using a differential high-voltage probe and compared against single-port injection results. Combined injection increased peak DC-link voltage by 15–41% relative to the higher of the two single-port cases, depending on inverter topology. Two of the four inverters exhibited protection circuit activation under combined 3 kA injection that was not triggered by 3 kA single-port injection. The findings indicate that current test standards may underestimate the inverter stress occurring in real installations during nearby indirect lightning.

title: A review of conducted surge protection requirements for low-voltage PV installations: comparison of IEC 61643-32, IEC 62305, and national grid codes in Southeast Europe
abstract: This book chapter reviews the surge protection requirements applicable to low-voltage photovoltaic systems in Serbia, Romania, Hungary, and North Macedonia, comparing provisions of IEC 61643-32:2017 (SPD selection and application at PV power systems), IEC 62305 (lightning protection), and the national grid connection codes of the four countries as in force in 2024. Differences are identified in three areas: the method for determining the required impulse current class of DC-side SPDs, the treatment of floating versus grounded DC systems, and the earthing resistance thresholds triggering mandatory installation of additional earth electrodes. The chapter includes a worked example for a 100 kWp ground-mounted plant at a site with a flash density of 1.8 km⁻² yr⁻¹, showing that the four national frameworks produce SPD selection outcomes ranging from type 1 to type 2 for the same installation. Tables cross-referencing standard clauses to practical design decisions are provided for practising engineers.
venue: Handbook of Lightning and Surge Protection for Renewable Energy Systems, Springer

title: Radiated Emission Sensitivity to PCB Stack-Up Parameters in Eight-Layer High-Speed Digital Designs
abstract: The influence of dielectric thickness, copper weight, and layer ordering on radiated emissions from a standardised eight-layer stack-up is evaluated using a parametric FDTD study. A benchmark circuit, consisting of a 500 MHz single-ended clock distribution tree with three fanout nodes, was instantiated on 24 stack-up variants spanning dielectric thicknesses from 0.1 mm to 0.3 mm and copper weights of 0.5 oz and 1 oz. Each variant was simulated to obtain the radiated electric field at 3 m. Stack-ups with the signal layers closest to ground reference planes showed the lowest far-field peak, with a maximum suppression of 8.9 dB relative to the worst-performing arrangement. Dielectric thickness had a stronger influence than copper weight; halving the spacing between a signal layer and its reference plane reduced emissions by an average of 5.2 dB at the fifth harmonic. Simulation time per variant averaged 4.2 hours on a 16-core workstation. The results confirm that stack-up selection is an effective early-stage emission control tool that costs nothing in component budget.

title: Measurement-Based Sparsity Analysis of VHF/UHF Spectrum Occupancy in a Mid-Sized Urban Environment
abstract: Reliable compressed sensing reconstruction in cognitive radio depends on accurate prior knowledge of spectrum sparsity. This work reports a 14-day passive measurement campaign conducted in Novi Sad using a calibrated wideband receiver covering 80–860 MHz at a resolution bandwidth of 100 kHz. Occupancy was defined by an energy detection threshold set 6 dB above the measured noise floor. Across the observation window, mean occupancy was 11.3%, with pronounced temporal clustering around broadcast television slots and GSM uplink intervals. Frequency-domain sparsity followed a Zipf-like distribution with exponent 0.81. Diurnal occupancy variance exceeded 40% in the FM radio sub-band but was below 8% for digital television multiplexes. The data set provides empirical support for sparse prior assumptions used in sub-Nyquist sensing architectures and is made available in anonymised form as a supplementary dataset. Practical implications for measurement matrix design are discussed.

title: Equilibrium adsorption of caffeine and ibuprofen onto commercially available granular activated carbon from synthetic aqueous solutions
abstract: Batch adsorption experiments were conducted to establish equilibrium isotherms for caffeine and ibuprofen on a commercial granular activated carbon (GAC-800) at pH 6.5 and 25 °C. Langmuir, Freundlich, and Sips models were fitted to equilibrium data collected over an initial concentration range of 0.5–50 mg/L. The Langmuir maximum adsorption capacities were 48.3 mg/g for ibuprofen and 31.7 mg/g for caffeine. Thermodynamic parameters calculated from experiments at 15, 25, and 35 °C indicated exothermic, spontaneous adsorption for both compounds, with standard enthalpy changes of −22.4 kJ/mol and −18.1 kJ/mol respectively. Scanning electron microscopy and nitrogen adsorption confirmed a BET surface area of 912 m²/g and a predominantly mesoporous structure for GAC-800. The Sips model gave the best statistical fit (R² > 0.998) for both adsorbates, suggesting heterogeneous surface energetics play a role at intermediate concentrations. Results provide baseline parameters for subsequent column design studies.

title: Breakthrough behaviour of ibuprofen in fixed-bed columns packed with amine-functionalised granular activated carbon
abstract: Fixed-bed column experiments were performed to study the dynamic removal of ibuprofen from synthetic process condensate (initial concentration 2 mg/L, pH 6.0) using amine-functionalised GAC prepared by treatment with 25% aqueous ethylenediamine. Column dimensions were 2.5 cm internal diameter, with bed heights of 10, 15, and 20 cm and volumetric flow rates of 5, 10, and 15 mL/min. Breakthrough times ranged from 48 min at 15 mL/min and 10 cm bed to 380 min at 5 mL/min and 20 cm bed. The Thomas model and the Bohart–Adams model were fitted to all eighteen breakthrough curves; both described the data adequately (RMSE < 0.04), with Thomas rate constants (k_Th) between 0.0021 and 0.0078 L/mg·min decreasing with increasing flow rate. Maximum bed adsorption capacity estimated from Thomas fitting was 31.4–34.9 mg/g, consistent with batch equilibrium data. The amine modification improved capacity by approximately 28% compared to untreated GAC under identical column conditions, attributed to hydrogen bonding with the carbonyl group of ibuprofen.

title: Comparative performance of clinoptilolite and synthetic Na-Y zeolite for removal of benzotriazole from condensate streams
abstract: Benzotriazole, a corrosion inhibitor widely detected in industrial process condensates, was studied as an adsorbate on natural clinoptilolite (sourced from a deposit near Vranje, Serbia) and synthetic Na-Y zeolite. Batch equilibrium experiments at initial concentrations of 1–100 mg/L and pH 7 showed that Na-Y zeolite achieved a Langmuir maximum capacity of 22.6 mg/g compared with 8.9 mg/g for clinoptilolite, attributed to the larger internal surface area (580 vs. 32 m²/g). Fixed-bed columns were operated with a 5 mg/L inlet concentration at a superficial velocity of 1.4 m/h. Breakthrough at 5% of inlet occurred after 210 min for Na-Y and 75 min for clinoptilolite under identical bed depths of 12 cm. ANOVA-based error analysis confirmed that the Bohart–Adams model fitted the Na-Y column data better than the Thomas model for the lower concentration front, while both models performed equivalently for clinoptilolite. Cost considerations favour clinoptilolite for lower-stringency applications.

title: Regeneration cycles and capacity loss of HNO₃-oxidised activated carbon columns loaded with pharmaceutical micropollutants
abstract: The regenerability of HNO₃-oxidised GAC after adsorption of a three-component pharmaceutical mixture (ibuprofen, diclofenac, carbamazepine; each at 2 mg/L) was evaluated over five adsorption–desorption cycles in a fixed-bed setup. Thermal regeneration at 200 °C under nitrogen flow and solvent washing with 0.1 M NaOH were tested as desorption methods. Thermal regeneration restored 91–95% of initial capacity in cycles 1–3, but dropped to 82% by cycle 5, attributed to irreversible blocking of micropores as confirmed by post-cycle BET analysis showing a surface area decrease from 847 to 731 m²/g. NaOH washing recovered 85–88% across all five cycles with negligible surface area change, but produced a concentrated alkaline effluent requiring further treatment. Thomas model parameters refitted after each cycle showed a progressive decrease in the rate constant k_Th for carbamazepine (from 0.0034 to 0.0019 L/mg·min), indicating slower kinetics on the aged surface. Results suggest NaOH washing is preferable where minimising capacity loss outweighs effluent management costs.

title: Adsorption of 1H-benzotriazole and tolyltriazole mixtures on granular activated carbon: competitive equilibrium and binary fixed-bed dynamics
abstract: Competitive adsorption of 1H-benzotriazole (BT) and tolyltriazole (TT), two corrosion inhibitors frequently co-occurring in cooling water condensates, was studied in binary batch and fixed-bed systems using GAC-800. Single-solute Langmuir parameters obtained previously were used to predict binary equilibrium via the extended Langmuir and the ideal adsorbed solution theory (IAST); IAST predictions agreed with measured binary data within 12% relative error across all tested concentration ratios (BT:TT from 1:4 to 4:1). Fixed-bed column experiments with equimolar inlet concentrations (3 mg/L each) at a flow rate of 8 mL/min and bed height of 15 cm showed a characteristic rollover effect: the earlier-saturating component TT was partially displaced by BT, producing an effluent concentration transiently exceeding the inlet. Thomas model fitting to each individual component breakthrough underestimated the rollover peak by 18–23%, confirming that single-solute models are inadequate for binary systems. An empirical correction factor derived from IAST parameters reduced this discrepancy to below 7%.

title: Scale-up considerations for fixed-bed adsorption columns treating pharmaceutical-containing condensate: from laboratory to pilot scale
abstract: This book chapter reviews the application of the Thomas and Bohart–Adams models for scaling fixed-bed adsorption columns from laboratory (2.5 cm diameter, 5–20 cm bed depth) to pilot scale (10 cm diameter, 50–100 cm bed depth) for the removal of pharmaceutical micropollutants from industrial condensates. Dimensional analysis shows that maintaining the same superficial velocity and bed contact time (EBCT) is necessary but insufficient if the ratio of axial dispersion coefficient to convective flux changes significantly with scale. Experimental data from a pharmaceutical condensate treatment pilot operated over six months at a food processing facility in Vojvodina are used to illustrate how model parameters obtained at laboratory scale overestimated breakthrough time by 15–30% at pilot scale when axial dispersion was not accounted for. A correction procedure based on the Peclet number dependency of the Bohart–Adams rate constant is proposed, validated against pilot-scale data for ibuprofen and metformin (initial concentrations 1.8 and 3.5 mg/L respectively). Practical guidance on adsorbent pre-conditioning and flow distribution is included.

title: Zinc chloride-activated biochar from sunflower husk as a low-cost adsorbent for metformin removal from process condensate: equilibrium, kinetics, and column modelling
abstract: Biochar was produced from sunflower husk (a byproduct of edible oil production in Vojvodina) by chemical activation with ZnCl₂ at 600 °C under nitrogen. The resulting material (SH-ZnBC) had a BET surface area of 1,120 m²/g and a total pore volume of 0.63 cm³/g, predominantly microporous. Equilibrium adsorption of metformin at pH 7 followed the Sips model with a maximum capacity of 71.4 mg/g, substantially higher than commercial GAC-800 (34.2 mg/g) tested under identical conditions. Pseudo-second-order kinetics provided a good description of batch uptake with k₂ = 0.0019 g/mg·min. Fixed-bed columns (15 cm bed, 10 mL/min flow, 5 mg/L inlet) gave a breakthrough time of 290 min for SH-ZnBC versus 148 min for GAC-800. Thomas model fitting yielded k_Th = 0.0052 L/mg·min and a bed adsorption capacity of 58.8 mg/g for SH-ZnBC. Zinc leaching into effluent was below 0.03 mg/L throughout all experiments, within Serbian regulatory limits. The material shows promise as a regionally sourced, low-cost adsorbent.

title: Steady-state mass-balance model of a two-stage softening circuit for industrial boiler feed water
abstract: A lumped-parameter steady-state model was formulated for a two-stage lime–soda softening circuit supplying boiler feed water at a medium-sized food-processing plant in Vojvodina. The model comprises algebraic mass and charge balances for each precipitation reactor, a clarifier with empirical overflow-rate correlation, and two ion-exchange polishing columns. Equilibrium constants for calcium carbonate and magnesium hydroxide precipitation were taken from published thermodynamic databases and adjusted to local water composition measured over 18 months (n = 214 samples). Model predictions for hardness, alkalinity, and suspended solids at the circuit outlet agreed with plant measurements to within 7% for hardness and 12% for alkalinity under steady operating loads. Sensitivity analysis identified the clarifier sludge recycle ratio as the parameter with the largest influence on effluent hardness, accounting for 38% of total output variance. The model was implemented in MATLAB and is intended as a rapid-sizing tool for feasibility assessments of similar circuits.

title: Ozonation of reactive azo dye effluents: decolourisation rates, by-product identification and biodegradability enhancement
abstract: Bench-scale ozonation (applied ozone dose 10–80 mg/L, contact time 5–30 min) was studied on effluents containing three azo reactive dyes at 200 mg/L each. Decolourisation followed first-order kinetics with rate constants of 0.12–0.31 min⁻¹ at pH 9, approximately 2.4-fold higher than at pH 6, consistent with hydroxyl radical dominance under alkaline conditions. BOD₅/COD ratios increased from 0.08 in raw effluent to 0.38 after 20 mg/L ozone application, indicating a transition to biodegradable intermediates. LC-MS analysis identified six aromatic sulphonated by-products, with naphthalene sulphonic acid and phthalic acid among the most abundant. At the highest ozone dose tested, total aromatic content declined by 91% but TOC only by 34%, confirming partial mineralisation. The biodegradability improvement at moderate ozone doses is sufficient to support subsequent biological treatment, reducing ozone consumption and operating costs.
venue: Ozone: Science and Engineering Applications

title: Isobaric Vapour–Liquid Equilibria of the Ethanol–Water–Ethylene Glycol System at 101.3 kPa: Experiment and UNIFAC Correlation
abstract: Isobaric VLE data for the ternary system ethanol + water + ethylene glycol were measured using a modified Othmer still at 101.3 kPa over the full composition range. Forty-seven equilibrium points were collected and checked for thermodynamic consistency using the Wisniak L/W method; all passed at the 95% confidence level. Activity coefficients were correlated with the original UNIFAC model and with a modified UNIFAC version retaining Lyngby temperature-dependent interaction parameters. The modified version reduced the mean absolute deviation in vapour-phase mole fraction of ethanol from 0.0142 to 0.0081 and improved prediction of the azeotropic point location by approximately 3 K. The results confirm ethylene glycol as a suitable entrainer for breaking the ethanol–water azeotrope under atmospheric pressure and provide a validated parameter set for process simulation of the extractive distillation column. Experimental data are tabulated in full for use in design calculations.

title: Processing–property maps for extruded thermoplastic starch–sunflower protein films
abstract: A central composite design was used to map the effect of barrel temperature (120–160 °C), screw speed (80–200 rpm), and sunflower protein concentrate content (0–25 wt%) on the mechanical and barrier properties of blown films produced from the extruded blends via a subsequent film blowing step. Seventeen experimental runs yielded response surfaces for tensile strength, elongation at break, Young's modulus, water vapour transmission rate (WVTR), and oxygen transmission rate (OTR). Tensile strength ranged from 7.2 to 16.8 MPa across the design space; OTR varied from 180 to 620 cm³·m⁻²·day⁻¹·bar⁻¹. Optimal conditions identified by desirability function (maximum strength and minimum OTR) were 148 °C, 145 rpm, and 18 wt% protein. At the optimum, predicted and experimental values agreed within 6%. Specific mechanical energy was modelled as a secondary response and found to increase linearly with screw speed but to show a quadratic relationship with protein content, with a minimum near 12 wt% attributed to lubrication effects of denatured protein at low concentration.

title: Absolute quantification of oxyhaemoglobin and deoxyhaemoglobin concentrations in calf muscle using a two-distance continuous-wave near-infrared system
abstract: Continuous-wave near-infrared spectroscopy (CW-NIRS) can track relative changes in tissue chromophores but is limited in absolute quantification without assumptions about the differential path-length factor (DPF). This study applied a modified Beer–Lambert model with experimentally determined DPFs at 760 nm and 850 nm on 22 healthy adult volunteers to estimate absolute oxyhaemoglobin (OHb) and deoxyhaemoglobin (DHb) concentrations in the medial gastrocnemius muscle at rest. Resting OHb was 62 ± 9 µM and DHb was 28 ± 5 µM, yielding a mean tissue oxygen saturation (StO₂) of 68.7 ± 4.1%, consistent with venous blood sampling performed simultaneously. Source–detector separations of 25 mm and 35 mm were used to estimate the reduced scattering coefficient (µs′ ≈ 6.2 cm⁻¹ at 800 nm). The two-distance approach reduced cross-talk between absorption and scattering compared with single-distance measurements. Bland–Altman analysis showed a mean bias of −1.3 µM for StO₂ relative to venous co-oximetry. The instrument design and calibration procedure are described in sufficient detail to permit replication in clinical research settings.
venue: Journal of Biomedical Optics Research

title: Construction and characterisation of liquid optical phantoms for mimicking skeletal muscle scattering spectra between 650 and 900 nm
abstract: Reliable instrument calibration and inter-site comparisons in diffuse optical spectroscopy depend on well-characterised reference phantoms. We prepared 24 liquid phantoms using Intralipid-20% as scatterer and varying concentrations of India ink as absorber, targeting µs′ values of 5, 7, 10, and 13 cm⁻¹ and µa values of 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 cm⁻¹ at 800 nm. Full spectral characterisation from 650 to 900 nm was performed using an integrating sphere spectrophotometer. Mie-theory fits to the measured scattering spectra yielded scattering power exponents between 0.58 and 0.72, bracketing literature values for human skeletal muscle. Temperature stability over 6 hours at 22 °C was within 2% for µa and 1.5% for µs′. A recipe table with component masses, volumes, and expected optical properties is provided to facilitate replication. The phantoms were subsequently used to validate three commercial CW-NIRS devices and our in-house FD-NIRS instrument, revealing inter-device StO₂ discrepancies of up to 9 percentage points under identical conditions, highlighting the need for standardised phantom-based cross-calibration.

title: Adipose tissue thickness correction in near-infrared spectroscopy of thigh muscle: a comparison of skinfold, ultrasound, and MRI reference methods
abstract: Subcutaneous adipose tissue (AT) is a confounding layer in muscle NIRS measurements because it has lower scattering and different chromophore composition than muscle. Adipose tissue thickness (ATT) measured by skinfold calliper, B-mode ultrasound, and MRI was compared in 40 participants with ATT ranging from 3 to 22 mm over the vastus lateralis. MRI provided the reference standard. Skinfold measurements overestimated ATT by a mean of 3.1 mm (r² = 0.79 vs. MRI), while ultrasound showed a mean bias of 0.6 mm (r² = 0.96 vs. MRI). An ATT-stratified regression correction applied to CW-NIRS resting StO₂ measurements reduced the coefficient of variation from 11.2% to 5.8% across participants. Participants with ATT > 12 mm showed uncorrected StO₂ values 6.4 percentage points lower than those with ATT < 6 mm despite similar venous StO₂ at rest, confirming the magnitude of the bias. Ultrasound is recommended as the practical AT correction tool in field settings.

title: Multi-channel continuous-wave NIRS mapping of spatial heterogeneity in gastrocnemius oxygenation during calf-raise exercise
abstract: Skeletal muscle is metabolically heterogeneous and single-point NIRS measurements may not represent whole-muscle oxygenation. We built an 8-channel CW-NIRS array covering approximately 60 cm² over the medial and lateral gastrocnemius and characterised spatial heterogeneity in OHb, DHb, and StO₂ responses during a calf-raise protocol (60 raises/min, 10 min) in 20 healthy adults. Coefficient of variation of peak DHb response across channels was 18.3 ± 5.7%, with medial channels showing 14% greater peak DHb than lateral channels (p = 0.002). Principal component analysis of the 8-channel time series revealed that the first component explained 71% of the variance at rest but fell to 54% during exercise, indicating increased spatial divergence during muscle activation. Intra-subject spatial patterns were reproducible across two sessions (r = 0.84). These findings suggest that multi-channel recordings reduce the sampling bias inherent in single-optode designs and may improve sensitivity in intervention studies.

title: Oxygen kinetics at exercise onset in the vastus lateralis: characterising the phase II time constant using FD-NIRS
abstract: The kinetics of muscle oxygen consumption at exercise onset reflect mitochondrial activation and cardiovascular oxygen delivery dynamics. We used our FD-NIRS instrument to measure µa kinetics in the vastus lateralis during transitions from rest to 40% and 70% MVC during isometric knee extension in 18 volunteers. A mono-exponential model was fitted to DHb dynamics after a cardiodynamic correction window of 15 s. The phase II time constant (τ) for DHb at 40% MVC was 18.4 ± 3.2 s and at 70% MVC was 13.1 ± 2.8 s (p < 0.001). FD-NIRS-derived τ values correlated with pulmonary VO₂ kinetics measured simultaneously by breath-by-breath gas analysis (r = 0.76). The use of FD-NIRS eliminated the ambiguity in absolute chromophore estimation present in CW-based kinetics analyses. Signal-to-noise characterisation showed that phase II could be resolved in single-transition trials without ensemble averaging when DHb amplitude exceeded 8 µM.

title: Test–retest reliability of frequency-domain NIRS absolute optical properties in resting skeletal muscle across four European laboratories
abstract: Inter-laboratory reproducibility of absolute optical property measurements is a key prerequisite for multicentre clinical trials using FD-NIRS. Four laboratories in Novi Sad (Serbia), Innsbruck (Austria), Poznań (Poland), and Zagreb (Croatia) each measured the same cohort of 12 travelling volunteers on the vastus lateralis using their own FD-NIRS instruments within a 4-week window. Mean µa at 690 nm ranged from 0.061 to 0.069 cm⁻¹ across sites, and µs′ ranged from 5.8 to 7.1 cm⁻¹. Intraclass correlation coefficients across sites were 0.88 for µa and 0.79 for µs′ at 690 nm, and 0.91 and 0.83 respectively at 830 nm. Systematic offsets were partially explained by differences in source–detector geometry and fibre numerical aperture. A harmonisation protocol using shared solid phantoms reduced inter-site µa variability by 42%. These results indicate that FD-NIRS measurements are sufficiently reproducible for multicentre studies when phantom-based harmonisation is applied.

title: Comparing spatially resolved and broadband diffuse reflectance approaches for muscle optical property recovery: a simulation and experimental study
abstract: Spatially resolved reflectance (SRS) and broadband diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (BDRS) each offer practical advantages for portable muscle monitoring, but their µa and µs′ accuracy under realistic adipose-layer thicknesses has not been directly compared. Monte Carlo simulations using a two-layer slab model (adipose 3–15 mm; muscle semi-infinite) were run for source–detector distances from 15 to 40 mm at wavelengths 650–900 nm. SRS recovered µs′ with < 8% error for ATT < 8 mm but showed up to 22% error at ATT = 15 mm. BDRS with a 30–40 mm fixed separation recovered µa with < 6% error across the full ATT range when a two-layer inversion was applied. Experimental validation on five-layer tissue-simulating phantoms confirmed the simulation findings. Both methods showed equivalent StO₂ accuracy (±4 percentage points) for ATT < 6 mm, suggesting SRS is adequate for lean participants while BDRS with multi-layer inversion is preferable in obese populations or for absolute quantification.

title: Muscle oxygenation profiles during a six-minute walk test in patients with peripheral artery disease: a pilot observational study
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) limits oxygen delivery to leg muscles during walking, but the haemodynamic signature as measured by NIRS during the standardised six-minute walk test (6MWT) has not been well characterised in a Balkan patient cohort. Twelve patients with ankle-brachial index 0.51–0.79 and ten age-matched healthy controls underwent a 6MWT with FD-NIRS monitoring the gastrocnemius. PAD patients walked 312 ± 58 m versus 478 ± 44 m in controls. Peak DHb in PAD was 44 ± 12 µM versus 28 ± 8 µM in controls (p < 0.001), and StO₂ reached a nadir of 42 ± 9% during the 4th and 5th minutes versus 61 ± 7% in controls. Post-walk StO₂ recovery half-time was 78 ± 21 s in PAD versus 24 ± 7 s in controls. Nadir StO₂ correlated with ABI (r = 0.68) and with self-reported claudication onset distance (r = 0.61). The FD-NIRS 6MWT profile may provide a more sensitive marker of functional impairment than walk distance alone.

title: Wearable continuous-wave NIRS module for field-based muscle oxygenation monitoring: design, bench characterisation, and preliminary ambulatory data
abstract: Laboratory FD-NIRS instruments are not portable enough for field sports or unsupervised rehabilitation monitoring. We designed a wearable CW-NIRS module (78 g, 52 × 42 × 18 mm, two wavelengths 760 and 850 nm, two source–detector distances 25 and 35 mm) with on-board Bluetooth Low Energy data transmission at 50 Hz. Bench characterisation against solid phantoms showed StO₂ accuracy of ±5 percentage points versus integrating-sphere reference across µa 0.05–0.20 cm⁻¹. Motion artefact during walking at 5 km/h was assessed using a simultaneous accelerometer signal; median artefact-free data yield was 91% after wavelet-based filtering. In a preliminary study, six cyclists wore the module over the vastus lateralis during a 45-min outdoor ride. Mean ride StO₂ was 64 ± 7% with transient desaturation events reaching 48% during climbs. Module skin temperature remained below 37.2 °C throughout all recordings. Power consumption permitted 9-hour continuous operation from a 280 mAh battery.

title: Haemodynamic response asymmetry in the quadriceps during bilateral leg press in healthy adults and athletes: evidence from simultaneous bilateral FD-NIRS
abstract: Bilateral limb asymmetry is relevant in sport performance and injury prevention, but most NIRS studies monitor only the dominant limb. We simultaneously monitored both vastus lateralis muscles using two synchronised FD-NIRS instruments during a bilateral leg press protocol at 50% and 80% 1-RM in 30 participants (15 recreational athletes and 15 competitive cyclists). An asymmetry index (AI) was computed as |dominant − non-dominant| / 0.5 × (dominant + non-dominant) × 100%. Mean AI for peak DHb was 12.3 ± 7.4% in recreational participants and 6.1 ± 3.9% in cyclists (p = 0.002), suggesting trained limbs are more metabolically symmetrical. AI exceeded 15% in 8 of the 15 recreational participants at 80% 1-RM. Dominant-limb dominance in StO₂ nadir was not statistically significant. Strength asymmetry measured by force plate correlated moderately with DHb AI (r = 0.53). These bilateral optical oxygenation profiles provide a physiological complement to force-based asymmetry metrics.

title: Hyperelastic characterisation of residual-limb soft tissue using confined compression tests
abstract: Accurate material parameters for biological soft tissue are a prerequisite for meaningful finite-element socket simulations. This study subjected cylindrical biopsy-sized phantom specimens and ex-vivo porcine tissue samples to confined uniaxial compression at strain rates of 0.01, 0.1 and 1.0 s⁻¹ using a 5 kN load cell. A two-parameter Mooney–Rivlin model and a five-parameter Yeoh model were fitted to the resulting stress–strain curves via nonlinear least squares. The Yeoh model achieved a mean residual of 3.2% versus 7.8% for Mooney–Rivlin across 24 specimens. Rate dependence was pronounced above 0.5 s⁻¹, suggesting that quasi-static assumptions are acceptable for static socket loading scenarios but not for dynamic gait. Fitted parameters are tabulated for direct import into commercial FEA pre-processors and serve as a validated input dataset for subsequent patient-specific socket analyses.

title: Sensitivity of socket interface pressure to mesh density and element type in residual-limb FEA
abstract: Finite-element meshes of anatomical structures derived from medical images vary widely in density and element topology across published studies, making inter-study comparison unreliable. This paper evaluated four mesh configurations—coarse tetrahedral (CT4), fine tetrahedral (CT10), coarse hexahedral (CH8) and fine hexahedral (CH20)—applied to an identical residual-limb geometry under a standardised 600 N axial load. Peak contact pressure predictions differed by up to 38% between CT4 and CH20. The CH20 mesh converged at approximately 120 000 elements, with further refinement changing peak pressure by less than 1.5%. Computation time scaled nearly cubically with element count. Practical guidelines are proposed: a minimum of 40 000 second-order tetrahedral elements for clinically acceptable accuracy within a 15-minute solve time on a standard workstation. The findings provide a reproducibility framework for groups entering socket FEA research.

title: Effect of biphasic electrical stimulation frequency on spontaneous calcium transient amplitude in cultured ventricular cardiomyocytes
abstract: Neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes cultured on fibronectin-coated coverslips were exposed to biphasic square-wave electrical stimulation at frequencies of 0.5, 1, 2, and 3 Hz for 72 hours using carbon-rod electrodes at a field strength of 5 V/cm. Calcium transients were recorded using the fluorescent indicator Fluo-4 AM (5 μM) on an epifluorescence microscope equipped with a high-speed CMOS camera. Peak ΔF/F₀ increased from 1.3 ± 0.2 at 0.5 Hz to 2.1 ± 0.3 at 1 Hz and declined to 1.6 ± 0.2 at 3 Hz. Time-to-peak and decay tau were both shortened progressively with increasing frequency. Cells stimulated at 1 Hz showed the most consistent transient morphology across the culture well and the lowest coefficient of variation in inter-transient interval (CV = 0.08). These findings suggest an optimal pacing window near physiological resting heart rates for maximising calcium handling maturity during short-term in-vitro conditioning of neonatal ventricular myocytes.

title: Coagulation of simulated reactive dye bath effluent using aluminium sulphate: effect of pH, coagulant dose and dye structure
abstract: Coagulation-flocculation experiments were performed on synthetic effluents containing three structurally distinct reactive dyes (monochlorotriazine, vinyl sulphone, and bifunctional) at concentrations of 50–500 mg/L using aluminium sulphate as the primary coagulant. Jar-test trials at pH 5–10 and coagulant doses of 50–600 mg/L revealed that optimal removal of all three dyes occurred near pH 6.5–7.0. Colour removal exceeded 92% for the monochlorotriazine dye at an alum dose of 300 mg/L, but only 74% for the bifunctional dye under the same conditions, indicating that dye charge density and molecular weight significantly influence coagulation efficiency. Residual COD ranged from 180 to 340 mg/L after treatment, confirming that coagulation alone is insufficient for discharge compliance. Sludge volumes and specific resistance to filtration were characterised for each dye system. Results provide a structured basis for selecting coagulant conditions prior to downstream oxidative polishing.

title: Influence of anionic surfactant presence on coagulation of C.I. Reactive Red 198 in synthetic textile rinse water
abstract: Industrial textile rinse waters typically contain both residual reactive dye and anionic surfactants from washing auxiliaries. This study examined how sodium lauryl ether sulphate (SLES) at concentrations of 20–200 mg/L affects coagulation of C.I. Reactive Red 198 at 100 mg/L using ferric chloride. Zeta potential measurements demonstrated that SLES progressively stabilised dye-coagulant flocs at surfactant concentrations above 80 mg/L, reducing colour removal from 88% to 54%. Adding a cationic polyelectrolyte (polyDADMAC, 2–8 mg/L) as a coagulant aid partially restored performance, achieving 79% colour removal even at 200 mg/L SLES. Turbidity of treated effluent remained below 5 NTU across all conditions with polyelectrolyte addition. TOC reduction was modest (35–42%), indicating that dissolved organic load from surfactant fragments persists. Implications for sequential treatment design in dyeing facilities are discussed.

title: Fenton oxidation as a polishing step after coagulation-flocculation of reactive dye effluents: mineralisation kinetics and toxicity reduction
abstract: A two-stage treatment sequence was evaluated on real textile effluent collected from a knitting facility in Vojvodina: coagulation-flocculation with FeCl₃ (400 mg/L, pH 7.0) followed by Fenton oxidation (H₂O₂ 200–1000 mg/L, Fe²⁺ 10–80 mg/L, pH 3.0). After coagulation, COD was reduced from an initial 1840 mg/L to 760 mg/L and colour by 85%. Subsequent Fenton treatment at H₂O₂/Fe²⁺ molar ratio of 15 achieved further COD removal to 210 mg/L and near-complete decolourisation (>99%). Pseudo-first-order rate constants for COD decay ranged from 0.018 to 0.047 min⁻¹ depending on H₂O₂ dose. Acute toxicity to Daphnia magna (EC₅₀) improved from 3.2% v/v in raw effluent to >80% v/v after combined treatment. The combined process reduced sludge mass by 28% compared with coagulation alone at equivalent COD targets, an economically relevant outcome for small dyeing operations.

title: Activated sludge adaptation to pre-ozonated reactive dye wastewater: respirometry, biomass morphology and colour residuals
abstract: An acclimation study was conducted over 90 days using a lab-scale sequencing batch reactor (SBR, 4 L working volume) fed with pre-ozonated reactive dye effluent as a fraction (10–40% v/v) of synthetic municipal wastewater. Respirometric measurements showed that oxygen uptake rate stabilised within 21 days at 10% dye effluent fraction and within 42 days at 40%. Specific COD removal efficiency reached 87–91% under steady-state conditions at all fractions tested. Residual colour after biological treatment was 15–62 Pt-Co units depending on dye type, meeting Serbian discharge thresholds for three of four dyes studied. MLSS concentrations were maintained at 2.8–3.5 g/L throughout. Filamentous organism abundance, assessed by microscopy, remained low (score ≤ 1 on the 0–5 scale), suggesting no major settleability issues. The results confirm that moderate ozone pre-treatment enables stable aerobic biodegradation without dedicated biomass augmentation.

title: Techno-economic comparison of coagulation–ozonation–SBR and coagulation–Fenton–SBR sequences for treatment of knitting mill effluent
abstract: A comparative assessment was carried out for two treatment trains applied to 50 m³/day of real knitting mill effluent (COD 1600–2200 mg/L, colour 800–1500 Pt-Co, surfactant 40–90 mg/L): Train A used coagulation followed by ozonation (20 mg O₃/L) and aerobic SBR; Train B replaced ozonation with Fenton oxidation (H₂O₂ 300 mg/L, Fe²⁺ 25 mg/L). Both trains achieved final effluent quality within Serbian Class II discharge limits. Capital cost estimates based on vendor quotations placed Train A at approximately 1.15× the cost of Train B due to ozone generator investment. However, operating costs for Train A were 18% lower over a 10-year horizon, primarily because reagent costs for Fenton were higher than electricity for ozone generation at this scale. Sludge production in Train B was 2.1-fold higher than in Train A, creating additional disposal costs. Sensitivity analysis showed the crossover point at electricity prices above 0.18 €/kWh, relevant for current Serbian tariffs.

title: Removal of nonionic surfactants from textile effluents by coagulation with polyaluminium chloride: effect of ethoxylation degree
abstract: Four commercially available nonionic alcohol ethoxylate surfactants (AE) with ethoxylation degrees of 5, 9, 14, and 20 ethylene oxide units were studied at 100 mg/L in coagulation experiments with polyaluminium chloride (PACl, 50–500 mg/L, pH 5–9). Removal efficiency declined monotonically with increasing ethoxylation degree: AE-5 showed 81% TOC removal at 300 mg/L PACl, while AE-20 yielded only 31% under identical conditions. Surface tension measurements confirmed that higher-ethoxylation surfactants formed more stable colloidal dispersions that resisted charge neutralisation. Addition of 10 mg/L chitosan as a bio-based coagulant aid improved AE-20 removal to 58% without increasing sludge volume. Acute toxicity to Aliivibrio fischeri (luminescence inhibition, 15 min) was reduced by 60–75% across all surfactant types after combined PACl-chitosan treatment. The findings suggest that surfactant composition, not only total concentration, should inform coagulant selection in textile plant design.

title: UV/H₂O₂ treatment of pre-coagulated reactive dye effluent: quantum yield estimation and effect on downstream biological treatment
abstract: UV/H₂O₂ was evaluated as an alternative to ozonation for polishing pre-coagulated reactive dye effluent. Experiments used a 15 W low-pressure mercury lamp (λ = 254 nm, fluence rate 1.8 mW/cm²) with H₂O₂ doses of 50–400 mg/L and exposure times of 5–60 min. Apparent quantum yields for decolourisation of C.I. Reactive Blue 19 and C.I. Reactive Yellow 145 were 0.0041 and 0.0029 mol/Einstein, respectively. At a H₂O₂ dose of 200 mg/L and 30 min exposure, COD was reduced by 41% and BOD₅/COD increased from 0.11 to 0.45. Residual H₂O₂ at the end of UV treatment was quenched with sodium sulphite before SBR feeding to avoid inhibition; without quenching, SBR performance declined noticeably within five days. Electrical energy per order (EEO) for colour removal was 0.38 kWh/m³/order, lower than values reported for comparable ozone systems in the literature. Results support UV/H₂O₂ as a cost-competitive option for facilities with existing UV disinfection infrastructure.

title: Combined electrocoagulation and biological treatment of mixed reactive dye and surfactant effluent: pilot-scale results
abstract: A pilot unit (200 L/day) combining electrocoagulation (EC) with aluminium electrodes (current density 10–40 mA/cm², electrolysis time 10–30 min) and a moving bed biofilm reactor (MBBR, 120 L, HRT 18 h) was operated for 45 days on effluent from a textile finishing plant in Vojvodina. The effluent contained reactive dyes (80–240 mg/L), anionic and nonionic surfactants (combined 50–120 mg/L) and COD of 900–1600 mg/L. Electrocoagulation at 20 mA/cm² and 20 min achieved 89% colour removal and 62% COD reduction with specific energy consumption of 1.8 kWh/kg COD removed. The MBBR reduced remaining COD to below 120 mg/L on 38 of 45 operating days; exceedances corresponded to days with dye concentration spikes above 200 mg/L. MBBR biofilm carrier coverage reached 85% by day 21. Total treatment cost was estimated at 1.4 €/m³, competitive with chemical coagulation-Fenton sequences reported for similar effluent characteristics. The pilot data form the basis for a planned full-scale feasibility study.

title: Fouling mechanisms during ultrafiltration of corn steep liquor: a combined blocking model and rheological analysis
abstract: Corn steep liquor (CSL), a by-product of wet-milling, was subjected to ultrafiltration with 10 and 30 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at TMP values of 0.5–3.0 bar to characterise fouling mechanisms. Hermia's blocking models (complete, intermediate, standard blocking and cake filtration) were fitted to flux–time data. Cake filtration was the dominant mechanism at protein concentrations above 15 g/L and TMP above 1.5 bar, while intermediate blocking prevailed at lower concentrations. Dynamic viscosity of the feed ranged from 3.2 to 18.7 mPa·s depending on solids content, and cake compressibility index was determined to be 0.61, indicating a moderately compressible deposit. Backwash at 0.5 bar for 30 s every 15 min restored 70–85% of initial flux. The study provides design parameters for ultrafiltration as a clarification step in CSL-based fermentation medium preparation.

title: Reconciliation of measured flow and concentration data in water treatment plant networks using weighted least-squares adjustment
abstract: Measured flow rates and pollutant concentrations in operating water treatment plants contain random errors that violate mass-balance closure when checked against network equations. Data reconciliation by weighted least-squares (WLS) adjustment forces closure while distributing corrections proportionally to measurement uncertainties. This study applies WLS reconciliation to data from a 15,000 m³/day surface-water treatment plant in Serbia, using 10-minute averages of 31 flow meters and 14 in-line conductivity and turbidity sensors over a 45-day observation period. Measurement uncertainty estimates were derived from manufacturer specifications and short-term repeat measurements. Reconciled data reduced apparent mass-balance residuals by 82% on average. Gross-error detection using the global chi-squared test identified three sensors with systematic biases exceeding 12%, which were subsequently recalibrated. The reconciled dataset was then used to re-parameterise clarifier and filter submodels, improving their predictive accuracy relative to the models previously calibrated on raw data.

title: Uticaj veličine čestica biljnog materijala na prinos i sastav etarskog ulja lavande (Lavandula angustifolia Mill.) pri hidrodestilaciji
abstract: U radu je ispitivan uticaj granulacije sušenog cveta lavande na prinos i hemijski sastav etarskog ulja dobijenog hidrodestilacijom u laboratorijskom Clevenger-ovom aparatu zapremine 2 L. Primenjen je plan potpunog faktorijalnog eksperimenta sa tri nivoa veličine čestica (0,5–1 mm, 1–2 mm, 2–4 mm) i tri vremena destilacije (60, 90, 120 min). Prinos etarskog ulja određen je gravimetrijski, a hemijski sastav analiziran GC-MS metodom. Rezultati pokazuju da sitnije čestice (0,5–1 mm) daju statistički značajno veći prinos (do 1,84% v/m) u odnosu na krupniju frakciju (1,19% v/m pri istom vremenu destilacije). Udio linalola kao dominantne komponente kreće se između 28,4 i 35,7% u zavisnosti od granulacije, pri čemu finija mlevenje povećava udeo oksidacionih degradacionih produkata pri dužem vremenu destilacije. Zaključeno je da je optimalan kompromis između prinosa i kvaliteta ulja postignut pri veličini čestica 1–2 mm i vremenu destilacije od 90 minuta.

title: Reactive blending of pea protein isolate and corn starch in a twin-screw extruder: structural and mechanical outcomes
abstract: Pea protein isolate (PPI) was melt-blended with corn starch at protein contents of 10, 20, and 30 wt% in a co-rotating twin-screw extruder at barrel temperatures of 120–150 °C and screw speeds of 100–200 rpm. Cross-linking between starch hydroxyl groups and protein amino acid residues was promoted by adding 0.5 wt% citric acid as a reactive compatibiliser. FTIR spectra showed a new absorption band at 1 735 cm⁻¹ consistent with ester bond formation, whose intensity increased with citric acid concentration. Tensile strength of compression-moulded films increased from 8.4 MPa (neat TPS) to 14.7 MPa at 20 wt% PPI, while elongation at break decreased from 96 to 31%. Scanning electron microscopy of fracture surfaces revealed reduced phase domain size at 20 wt% PPI when citric acid was present. Water vapour transmission rate decreased by 29% relative to unfilled TPS at the same formulation, measured at 38 °C and 90% RH. Results suggest that moderate protein content with reactive compatibilisation improves stiffness and barrier properties without excessive embrittlement.

title: Frequency-domain characterisation of apple cortex tissue using a four-electrode impedance cell: Cole model fitting over 1 Hz–1 MHz
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectra were acquired from apple (Malus domestica cv. Idared) cortex plugs using a symmetric four-electrode cell over the frequency range 1 Hz to 1 MHz. A total of 180 specimens were harvested at three ripeness stages and conditioned at 4 °C and 20 °C. The Cole single-dispersion model was fitted to each spectrum via a trust-region nonlinear least-squares algorithm implemented in MATLAB. Fitted parameters R0, R∞, characteristic frequency fc, and the dispersion exponent α were compared across ripeness and temperature groups. Mean R0 decreased by 31 % between early and late ripeness at 20 °C, while α showed no statistically significant dependence on temperature (p = 0.18, ANOVA). Cole model residuals remained below 2.1 % RMS across the full band. The results indicate that R0 and R∞ are more reliable ripeness indicators than α or fc for this cultivar. The electrode geometry and measurement protocol are described in sufficient detail to permit replication with equivalent instrumentation.

title: Sensitivity of common equivalent-circuit topologies to electrode polarisation artefacts in plant tissue impedance measurements
abstract: Electrode polarisation (EP) arises at electrolyte–electrode interfaces and distorts low-frequency impedance data, complicating parameter extraction for biological tissue. This study compared five equivalent-circuit topologies—Cole, double-Cole, R-RC, R-RC-CPE, and a modified Randles cell—with respect to their susceptibility to EP in measurements on stem segments of maize (Zea mays) and sunflower (Helianthus annuus). Impedance was recorded between 10 mHz and 100 kHz using stainless-steel pin electrodes at three inter-electrode spacings (5, 10, and 20 mm). EP contributions were estimated by a subtraction method using blank agar phantoms matched to the tissue ionic conductivity. The double-Cole model produced the lowest residuals (mean 1.4 % RMS) and the most stable intracellular resistance estimates across spacings. Single-Cole fits were acceptable above 100 Hz but underestimated extracellular resistance by up to 18 % when EP was not corrected. Practical guidance on frequency-range selection and pre-measurement phantom calibration is provided.

title: Inversion of broadband EIS data for soil moisture estimation: comparison of gradient-based and differential evolution optimisers
abstract: Soil moisture content (SMC) estimation via EIS requires robust inversion of multi-parameter equivalent-circuit models. This paper compares three optimisation strategies—Levenberg–Marquardt (LM), L-BFGS-B, and differential evolution (DE)—applied to a modified Bruggeman effective-medium model with four free parameters. Synthetic datasets with additive white Gaussian noise (SNR 20–40 dB) and experimental datasets from sandy loam and clay loam soils at SMC values 5–40 % (v/v) were used. DE converged to the global minimum in 97.3 % of synthetic trials versus 84.6 % for LM, and showed less sensitivity to initial parameter guesses. On experimental data, DE-inverted extracellular resistivity correlated with gravimetric SMC with R² = 0.94 for sandy loam and 0.89 for clay loam. Computation time per spectrum was under 0.4 s for all methods on standard desktop hardware. The study concludes that DE is preferable for field deployment scenarios where initial parameter estimates are unreliable.

title: Equivalent-circuit modelling of impedance spectra collected from ex-vivo porcine liver under progressive dehydration
abstract: Porcine liver specimens were subjected to controlled dehydration in a climate chamber (25 °C, 10 % relative humidity) and impedance spectra recorded at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 hours of desiccation. Each measurement used a planar four-electrode configuration with gold-coated titanium electrodes. The frequency sweep covered 10 Hz to 5 MHz using a Solartron 1260A impedance analyser with a 1294A dielectric interface. Three candidate equivalent circuits—double-Cole, Fricke-Morse, and a distributed RC ladder (10 sections)—were fitted. The distributed ladder model produced consistently lower Akaike information criterion scores across all time points, suggesting that the spatial heterogeneity of dehydrating tissue warrants distributed rather than lumped representations. The extracellular resistance extracted by all three models increased monotonically with desiccation time, rising by a factor of 3.1 ± 0.4 over 12 hours, while intracellular resistance showed a non-monotonic profile attributed to progressive membrane disruption after 6 hours.

title: Effect of freeze–thaw cycles on the EIS signature of carrot root tissue: a parameter extraction study
abstract: Freeze–thaw (FT) cycles alter cell membrane integrity in plant tissue and are reflected in characteristic shifts in impedance spectra. Carrot (Daucus carota) root discs were subjected to 0, 1, 2, 4, and 8 FT cycles (−18 °C / 4 °C, 24 h each phase) and measured with a two-electrode impedance cell at 100 Hz to 1 MHz. The Cole model was fitted using a bounded interior-point solver. The parameter α decreased systematically from 0.71 ± 0.03 (intact) to 0.54 ± 0.04 (8 cycles), consistent with increased heterogeneity due to membrane rupture. The ratio R0/R∞ was a sensitive indicator of FT damage, increasing by 62 % after a single cycle. Scanning electron microscopy images of cross-sections confirmed progressive disruption of the parenchyma cell walls. The dataset (n = 240 spectra) and fitting scripts are publicly archived. This work provides a reference dataset for benchmarking impedance-based fresh-produce quality sensors.

title: Regularised total least squares for EIS equivalent-circuit parameter extraction in the presence of correlated input–output noise
abstract: Standard nonlinear least-squares fitting of EIS equivalent-circuit models assumes that noise affects only the measured impedance and not the excitation frequency axis. In practice, phase jitter and harmonic distortion introduce correlated errors in both axes. This paper applies regularised total least squares (RTLS) to the Cole model fitting problem and benchmarks it against ordinary NLS using 500 Monte Carlo trials over synthetic datasets with varying SNR (15–45 dB) and correlated noise levels (0–5 % in the frequency axis). RTLS reduced bias in the characteristic frequency fc by 34 % at SNR = 20 dB and showed negligible overhead at SNR > 35 dB. Experimental validation used impedance data from agar gels with known conductivity (0.1–1.0 S/m) and confirmed the simulation findings. An open-source Python implementation of the RTLS Cole fitter is provided. The method is applicable to any EIS measurement system where signal generator phase noise is non-negligible.

title: Impedance-based detection of fungal colonisation in wheat grain: a feasibility study using interdigitated microelectrode arrays
abstract: Fungal contamination of cereal grain alters tissue impedance through hyphal infiltration of the starchy endosperm and enzymatic degradation of cell walls. This feasibility study investigated whether EIS measured on single wheat grains via custom interdigitated microelectrode arrays (IMEA, 50 µm finger width, 50 µm gap) could distinguish healthy grains from those inoculated with Fusarium graminearum at three contamination levels. Spectra were collected between 1 kHz and 10 MHz after 48 h, 96 h, and 144 h of inoculation at 25 °C and 90 % relative humidity. A two-dispersion Cole model was fitted and the extracted parameters used as features for linear discriminant analysis. Classification accuracy reached 87.4 % at 144 h but fell to 61.2 % at 48 h, suggesting that EIS detection requires a minimum colonisation density. Impedance maps across the electrode array showed spatial heterogeneity consistent with localised hyphal growth. The IMEA geometry and fabrication protocol are described.

title: Sensitivity analysis of distributed transmission-line models for impedance spectra of hydrated porous ceramic matrices as tissue phantoms
abstract: Porous ceramics are used as tissue-mimicking phantoms in EIS calibration because their pore geometry can be characterised independently by mercury intrusion porosimetry. This study evaluates how well distributed transmission-line (TL) models recover known pore-network parameters from impedance spectra of three commercial alumina ceramics with mean pore diameters of 0.2, 1.0, and 5.0 µm, saturated with KCl solutions of three conductivities (0.1, 0.5, 1.0 S/m). Twelve spectra per condition were acquired between 100 mHz and 10 MHz. First- and second-order TL models (6 and 11 free parameters, respectively) were fitted by a combination of genetic algorithm pre-conditioning and gradient descent refinement. The second-order model recovered porosity within 4.2 % of gravimetrically determined values. Tortuosity estimates were less accurate (mean error 11 %) and correlated with measurement frequency range. The results quantify the minimum frequency bandwidth required for reliable inversion of TL models as a function of pore size.

title: Uncertainty quantification in Cole model inversion via Markov chain Monte Carlo: practical guidelines for EIS practitioners
abstract: Nonlinear least-squares fitting of Cole equivalent-circuit models provides point estimates of parameters but no direct uncertainty measure. This paper applies Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling—specifically the affine-invariant ensemble sampler implemented in the emcee library—to the Cole model and demonstrates its use on three classes of biological tissue EIS data: plant cortex, ex-vivo muscle, and hydrogel phantoms. Flat priors were used for all parameters; likelihood functions accounted for frequency-dependent noise estimated from replicate measurements. Posterior distributions revealed strong correlations between R0 and α in low-SNR regimes (<25 dB), which NLS fits obscured. For the hydrogel phantom dataset (n = 60 spectra), 95 % credible intervals for R0 were approximately 2× wider than NLS-derived confidence intervals, indicating that NLS underestimates parameter uncertainty at low SNR. A concise workflow and Python code for applying MCMC to arbitrary equivalent-circuit topologies are provided in a supplementary repository.

title: Interpolating missing sensor readings in sparse cold-chain networks using Gaussian process regression with logistics event covariates
abstract: Sensor nodes in refrigerated transport networks occasionally fail to transmit due to radio shadowing, node faults, or gateway downtime, leaving gaps in temperature records that complicate regulatory compliance documentation. This paper evaluates Gaussian process (GP) regression for imputing missing readings in a network of 8–16 nodes per vehicle, using observed node readings plus logistics event covariates (door state, vehicle speed, set-point, elapsed journey time) as model inputs. The method was validated on artificially masked segments of 18 months of field data from 32 vehicles. For gaps of up to 20 minutes, GP interpolation achieved a root mean square error of 0.31 °C compared to 0.74 °C for linear interpolation. For gaps of 20–60 minutes, RMSE was 0.58 °C versus 1.41 °C. The model's uncertainty estimates are shown to be well-calibrated, supporting their use in automated compliance flags that distinguish confirmed excursions from uncertain imputed periods.

title: Humidity-decoupled VOC sensing with bilayer SnO₂/Al₂O₃ structures: response to benzene at 0.3 ppm
abstract: A bilayer architecture consisting of a porous Al₂O₃ moisture barrier deposited on a SnO₂ sensing layer was investigated as a strategy to reduce humidity cross-sensitivity in sub-ppm benzene detection. Al₂O₃ layers of 10–80 nm were deposited by atomic layer deposition on pre-characterised SnO₂ films. Water vapour transmission rates through the Al₂O₃ were measured independently using a quartz crystal microbalance. Benzene response (0.1–1 ppm) was characterised at 20%, 50%, and 80% RH at 375 °C operating temperature. The 30 nm Al₂O₃ overcoat reduced RH-induced resistance variation from 38% to under 9% while retaining a benzene response factor of 3.1 at 0.3 ppm. Recovery time increased modestly from 55 to 82 s with the overcoat. Temperature-programmed desorption indicated that benzene desorption kinetics were not significantly modified by the Al₂O₃, suggesting the barrier acts primarily as a moisture diffusion limiter rather than a surface modifier. Benzene was chosen as a representative non-polar aromatic representative of indoor air quality concern.

title: Contact Angle Measurements as a Predictor of Inkjet Ink Spreading on Corona-Treated Polypropylene Films
abstract: This study examined the relationship between water contact angle and inkjet ink spreading behaviour on biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films subjected to varying corona discharge treatments. Five corona energy levels (0, 20, 30, 40, and 50 W·min/m²) were applied to BOPP substrates, and static contact angles were measured using distilled water, diiodomethane, and formamide to calculate surface free energy by the Owens–Wendt method. Four commercially available water-based pigment inkjet inks were deposited using a laboratory test printer, and dot gain, ink spread diameter, and feathering index were measured via optical microscopy. Surface free energy increased from 29 mN/m for untreated film to 48 mN/m at 40 W·min/m², with diminishing returns at higher energies. Dot gain correlated linearly with surface free energy up to 44 mN/m (R² = 0.91), beyond which excessive ink spreading degraded edge sharpness. Optimal printability was achieved at 38–42 mN/m. The results suggest that contact angle alone is insufficient for predicting ink behaviour; the polar component of surface energy is a more reliable indicator for water-based systems.

title: Effect of Atmospheric Plasma Pre-Treatment on Adhesion of UV-Curable Inkjet Inks to Low-Density Polyethylene Films
abstract: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) flexible films present persistent adhesion challenges for UV-curable inkjet inks owing to their low surface free energy (approximately 31 mN/m). This work compared atmospheric plasma treatment at three power levels (200, 350, and 500 W) and two exposure times (1 and 3 seconds) against conventional corona discharge as pre-treatment methods. Adhesion was evaluated by cross-cut tape test (ISO 2409) and by T-peel testing immediately after printing and after 7-day and 28-day ageing at ambient conditions. UV-curable inks based on acrylate chemistry were used. Plasma at 350 W / 3 s achieved cross-cut adhesion class GT0 immediately after treatment, but adhesion degraded to GT2 after 28 days for two of three ink formulations tested. Corona-treated samples showed faster hydrophobic recovery, reaching GT3 within 14 days. XPS analysis of treated surfaces confirmed that plasma generates a higher concentration of carbonyl and hydroxyl groups than corona at equivalent treatment times. No single treatment provided durable adhesion without an additional primer layer, a finding with direct implications for label and flexible packaging converters.
