title: Ink Migration Through Metallised Polyolefin Films: Comparing UV-Curable and Water-Based Inkjet Systems Under Simulated Retort Conditions
abstract: Migration of photoinitiators and colorants from printed packaging into food simulants is a regulatory concern under EU Regulation 10/2011. This study quantified migration from UV-curable and water-based inkjet inks printed on metallised oriented polypropylene (met-OPP) and metallised LDPE films. Samples were immersed in three food simulants (10% ethanol, 3% acetic acid, and vegetable oil simulant Tenax) at 40 °C for 10 days to represent long-term ambient storage, and in 10% ethanol at 70 °C for 2 hours to simulate retort conditions. Migration was quantified by HPLC-MS for four photoinitiators (ITX, benzophenone, 2-EHA, and BAPO) and by UV-Vis spectrophotometry for pigment colorants. Under retort conditions, ITX migrated at 18.2 µg/dm² from UV-curable inks on LDPE, exceeding the specific migration limit of 0.05 mg/kg when recalculated for a standard food package. Water-based systems showed negligible photoinitiator migration but detectable colorant migration in acetic acid simulant. Metallisation reduced but did not eliminate migration for small-molecule species. The data indicate that UV-curable inkjet inks as currently formulated are not compliant for direct food-contact flexible packaging under retort conditions.
venue: Packaging Technology and Science

title: Printhead Compatibility and Jetting Stability of Water-Based Inks on Modified Polypropylene: A Waveform Optimisation Study
abstract: Achieving stable drop formation is as important as substrate surface energy when inkjet printing on polyolefin films. This paper investigates the interaction between ink rheological properties and piezoelectric printhead drive waveform parameters for three water-based inkjet inks (viscosities 8–14 mPa·s at 25 °C, surface tensions 28–35 mN/m) on flame-treated isotactic polypropylene sheets. A drop-watching camera system was used to record droplet formation at 15 waveform configurations varying rise time (2–6 µs), dwell time (4–10 µs), and voltage amplitude (18–30 V). Stable jetting was defined as satellite-free formation over 500 consecutive drops. Optimal waveforms were identified for each ink and correlated with the Ohnesorge number. Flame treatment raised surface free energy to 42 mN/m with no measurable change in substrate planarity. Ink spreading and 60° gloss values were recorded on treated and untreated substrates. The study found that waveform optimisation specific to each ink–substrate combination reduced satellite frequency by 73% compared to the manufacturer default settings, and improved 60° gloss by an average of 8 GU on treated substrates.

title: Quantification of Photoinitiator Residues in UV-LED Cured Inkjet Coatings on Polyethylene Substrates by Attenuated Total Reflectance FTIR
abstract: UV-LED curing at 385 and 405 nm is increasingly used to replace medium-pressure mercury lamps in inkjet printing lines. This study assessed the degree of cure and residual photoinitiator content in UV-LED cured acrylate inkjet coatings deposited on LDPE and HDPE substrates at three lamp doses (100, 200, and 400 mJ/cm²). ATR-FTIR was used to track consumption of acrylate C=C double bonds (peak at 810 cm⁻¹) relative to a stable carbonyl reference peak. Degree of cure (DC) values ranged from 61% at 100 mJ/cm² to 88% at 400 mJ/cm² for LDPE. Residual ITX and benzophenone concentrations were estimated by extraction in acetonitrile followed by HPLC-UV quantification. At 400 mJ/cm², residual ITX was 680 µg/g of dry ink film, well above the 0.05 mg/kg migration limit when worst-case contact assumptions are applied. HDPE showed 4–6% higher DC values than LDPE at equivalent doses, attributed to lower surface roughness reducing light scattering. These findings support the conclusion that lamp dose must be considered a critical process parameter in food-packaging printing qualification procedures.

title: Silicone-Based Release Liners as Low-Energy Reference Substrates for Standardised Inkjet Printability Testing: Limitations and Alternatives
abstract: Standardised evaluation of inkjet printability on low-surface-energy substrates requires well-characterised reference materials. This paper critically examines silicone-coated paper and film release liners as candidate reference substrates. Surface free energy was measured by the Owens–Wendt and Wu harmonic mean methods on twelve commercial release liner products from five European suppliers. Values ranged from 19.4 to 24.7 mN/m, with substantial lot-to-lot variability (CV up to 11%) that undermines their use as standards. As an alternative, fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) films were evaluated: surface free energy was 17.8 ± 0.4 mN/m across three batches, offering better reproducibility. Inkjet printability metrics (dot diameter, circularity, ink absorption rate) were measured for six water-based and four UV-curable inks on both substrate types. FEP substrates produced more reproducible results (lower CV for dot diameter: 3.2% vs. 8.9% on release liners) and are recommended as a reference material in round-robin interlaboratory studies. The paper also discusses cost and availability constraints for adoption in industrial quality control settings.

title: Influence of Ink Layer Thickness on Specific Migration of Benzophenone from Water-Based Inkjet Prints on Polypropylene Food Packaging
abstract: Benzophenone (BP) occurs as a contaminant in water-based inks from recycled paperboard and as an intentionally added sensitiser in some formulations. This study measured specific migration of BP from water-based inkjet prints on oriented polypropylene (OPP) into food simulants as a function of deposited ink layer thickness (3, 6, 9, and 12 µm, verified by confocal profilometry). A monolayer migration model (Piringer model, SML = 0.04 mg/kg) and empirical migration data from immersion experiments at 23 °C and 40 °C in 10% ethanol were compared. Printed ink mass per unit area was determined gravimetrically. Migration increased non-linearly with ink layer thickness; at 12 µm and 40 °C, measured migration was 0.031 mg/kg, approaching the SML. The Piringer model overestimated migration by a factor of 1.6 at thin layers and 1.1 at thick layers, suggesting it remains conservative for OPP but should be validated per ink–substrate combination. Storage time (0, 7, 30 days) had a smaller effect than temperature on cumulative migration in all tested scenarios.

title: Water-Based Inkjet Printing on Recycled Polyethylene Film: Adhesion Performance and Migration Behaviour After Mechanical Flexing
abstract: Post-consumer recycled polyethylene (rPE) films are entering flexible packaging lines, but their printability characteristics differ from virgin PE due to contamination, variable surface topography, and inconsistent additive content from recycling batches. This study evaluated inkjet adhesion and ink migration behaviour on five rPE films (30–70% recycled content) sourced from two European converters, before and after 1000 flexing cycles using a Gelbo flex tester. Surface free energy was 27–33 mN/m for rPE vs. 30–31 mN/m for virgin LDPE reference; all substrates were corona-treated to 40 mN/m prior to printing. Cross-cut adhesion (ISO 2409) remained GT0 for all samples immediately after printing but degraded to GT1–GT3 after flexing, with higher recycled content correlating with poorer post-flex adhesion (r = 0.81). Migration of four trace organic compounds (identified by GC-MS as plasticiser residues from the recycling stream) increased after flexing, reaching up to 8.4 µg/dm² for diisobutyl phthalate in 10% ethanol simulant. These results indicate that mechanical deformation during packaging use is a relevant but under-studied factor in migration safety assessment for printed rPE.

title: Legibility of Mandatory Text on Small-Surface Product Labels: An Eye-Tracking Study
abstract: EU sector-specific regulations impose mandatory text elements on labels for products with limited available surface area, including cosmetics, medical devices, and small electrical appliances. This study examined how layout decisions—typeface choice, leading, character spacing, contrast ratio, and column width—affected reading accuracy and time-to-find for mandatory fields on labels with a printable area of 10–30 cm². Thirty participants completed a structured search task while eye movements were recorded with a remote eye tracker at 250 Hz. Stimuli were 24 label variants printed on a calibrated digital press and presented in physical form. Fixation count per target field correlated most strongly with contrast ratio (r = −0.61) and typeface x-height (r = −0.54). Sans-serif typefaces with an x-height above 1.4 mm and a contrast ratio above 4.5:1 consistently reduced time-to-find by 18–31% relative to the least legible variants. The findings are discussed in relation to current minimum requirements under CE marking guidelines.

title: Predicting fusing process windows for textured specialty substrates using machine learning regression on laboratory measurement data
abstract: A dataset of 540 fusing trials across 18 uncoated and textured specialty paper substrates, six temperature levels, and five pressure levels was compiled from laboratory measurements accumulated over four years. Response variables included peel adhesion force, 60° gloss, gloss uniformity coefficient of variation, and optical density. Four regression algorithms—ridge regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and a shallow feedforward neural network—were trained on 80% of the dataset (stratified by substrate) and evaluated on the remaining 20%. Substrate features included Ra, Rz, Rsk, Bendtsen roughness, basis weight, equilibrium moisture content, and caliper. Gradient boosting achieved the lowest mean absolute error for adhesion force prediction (0.18 N/cm) and gloss prediction (1.1 GU at 60°). Feature importance analysis consistently ranked Rsk and Bendtsen roughness as the two most predictive substrate descriptors. The trained models were used to define feasible fusing windows (regions where adhesion exceeds 0.8 N/cm and gloss CV is below 15%) for each substrate, reducing the number of physical trials needed for process qualification.

title: Structural colour in printed packaging: mechanisms, substrate interactions, and achievable gamut
abstract: This book chapter surveys the physical mechanisms—thin-film interference, photonic crystal arrays, and surface diffraction—by which structural colour is generated in printed packaging contexts, contrasting them with conventional dye-based colour reproduction. The interaction between microstructured colour elements and common packaging substrates (coated paperboard, BOPP, metallised polyester) is discussed in terms of base reflectance, surface roughness tolerance, and register constraints. Achievable colour gamut is quantified using measurements from 14 commercially produced structural-colour samples; the mean gamut area in CIELAB at L* = 50 is 3.8 times larger than sRGB but confined to high-chroma regions with limited dark colours. Authentication use cases—both overt rainbow-shift devices and covert machine-readable layers—are described with attention to the conflict between aesthetic and forensic requirements in label design. Practical fabrication cost benchmarks for small, medium, and large print runs are included.

title: Task partitioning in a two-class ground robot fleet for simultaneous weeding and irrigation in maize rows
abstract: Coordinating robots with different actuator capabilities in a shared field environment requires task allocation strategies that respect both spatial constraints and resource limits. This paper presents a decentralised partitioning scheme in which weeding robots and micro-irrigation robots negotiate row assignments through local broadcast messages without querying a central scheduler. The protocol was implemented in ROS2 and tested on a fleet of four wheeled platforms—two equipped with rotary hoe tools and two carrying drip-irrigation modules—across a 0.4 ha maize test plot at the BioSense Institute experimental farm near Novi Sad. Over twelve field trials conducted in June and July 2023, the protocol achieved 91% row coverage within a fixed two-hour operational window, compared with 74% under a static pre-assignment baseline. Inter-robot collisions were eliminated through a distance-vector avoidance layer integrated directly into the negotiation messages. Average battery consumption per robot decreased by 8% relative to the baseline, attributed to reduced redundant travel. Limitations include sensitivity to GPS dropout, which occurred in three trials and required manual restart. The results suggest that lightweight message-based negotiation is sufficient for small heterogeneous fleets operating in structured row-crop environments.

title: Evaluating stigmergy-based path planning for ground robots under variable soil resistance in vineyard corridors
abstract: Stigmergy—indirect coordination through environmental traces—has been studied extensively for aerial swarms but receives less attention for slow-moving ground robots where soil conditions directly affect traction and energy use. This study adapted a digital pheromone model, implemented as a decaying grid overlaid on a pre-loaded field map, to guide a fleet of three tracked robots through vineyard inter-row corridors of varying soil moisture content. Soil resistance was measured continuously via motor current draw and fed back to update pheromone decay rates, discouraging subsequent robots from following high-resistance paths until conditions changed. Experiments were run at an experimental vineyard in Sremski Karlovci across 18 passes in autumn 2023. Robots using the adaptive pheromone model completed corridor traversal with 12% lower average current draw than robots using a fixed decay rate and 19% lower than robots following identical fixed routes. The model added approximately 4 ms per planning cycle on the onboard Raspberry Pi 4 compute unit, which was within the acceptable latency budget. The paper discusses failure modes when two robots simultaneously updated the same grid cell and proposes a simple token-based write lock as a remedy.

title: A lightweight communication stack for heterogeneous agricultural robot fleets operating under intermittent LoRa connectivity
abstract: Many field deployments of ground robot fleets rely on WiFi or cellular links that are unreliable at distances beyond 150 m in crop canopies. This preprint describes a communication stack built on LoRa radio modules that supports the coordination messages required by swarm task-allocation algorithms while respecting LoRa's duty-cycle constraints (1% on the 868 MHz band in Serbia). The stack uses a prioritised message queue that distinguishes collision-avoidance alerts, task-state updates, and telemetry, transmitting only the highest-priority pending message in each transmission slot. A discrete-event simulation with five virtual robots and message inter-arrival statistics drawn from earlier field trials showed that collision-alert delivery probability remained above 98% even when the channel was saturated with telemetry traffic. A small hardware prototype consisting of two AgriBot-3 platforms and one base-station node was used to validate round-trip latency measurements: median 210 ms, 99th percentile 780 ms. The stack is released as an open-source ROS2 package. Known limitations include no support for multi-hop routing and reduced throughput when more than six robots share one channel.

title: Subsurface Stress Distribution in Case-Hardened Involute Gear Flanks Under Hertzian Contact: Influence of Hardness Gradient Depth
abstract: This study examines how the depth of the hardened case layer affects the principal subsurface stress distribution in involute spur gears under quasi-static Hertzian loading. Six batches of 20MnCr5 gear specimens were gas-carburised to case depths ranging from 0.4 mm to 1.2 mm in 0.16 mm increments, then ground to Ra 0.35 µm. Finite element models incorporating experimentally measured hardness-to-yield-strength conversions were used to resolve orthogonal shear stress maxima at depths between 0.15 and 0.85 mm below the contact ellipse. Results show that a case depth of 0.8 mm minimises the ratio of peak orthogonal shear stress to local yield strength, reducing it by 18% compared to the 0.4 mm case. Residual stress profiles measured by X-ray diffraction were incorporated as initial conditions. The work provides a quantitative basis for specifying minimum effective case depth in gears intended for high-contact-stress applications above 1500 MPa.

title: Early-Stage Micropitting Detection on Ground Gear Flanks Using Surface Topography Parameters
abstract: Micropitting in ground gears is often detected only after visible damage has accumulated. This paper evaluates the suitability of several ISO 25178 areal surface texture parameters—Sq, Ssk, Sku, and Sal—as early indicators of micropitting onset. Back-to-back gear tests were conducted at a constant 900 N·m input torque and 1500 rpm for intervals of 10, 25, 50, and 100 hours using a mineral gear oil of ISO VG 220 viscosity grade. Flank topography was measured with a contact profilometer at each interval across nine sampling locations per tooth. Ssk shifted from −0.12 to −0.61 between 10 and 50 hours, while Sku rose from 3.1 to 4.8, both preceding visible micropitting confirmed by scanning electron microscopy at 100 hours. Sal decreased monotonically, indicating progressive loss of directional anisotropy. The correlation between Ssk and pit density reached r = 0.91. These results suggest that Ssk and Sal together provide a reliable two-parameter indicator for incipient micropitting without requiring gear disassembly.

title: Effect of Reversing-Torque Cycles on Bending and Contact Fatigue Life of Carburised Spur Gears
abstract: Gear drives in crane hoists and reversing mill drives experience torque reversals that create symmetrical bending stress cycles at the tooth root and modify the lubrication regime at the flank. This experimental study compares fatigue outcomes under unidirectional and fully reversing torque loading at equal peak values of 750 and 1050 N·m. Specimens were 18CrNiMo7-6 carburised spur gears (module 4, 24 teeth) run at 1200 rpm until failure or 5×10^7 cycles. Under reversing torque at 1050 N·m, the gear flank micropitting area increased by a factor of 2.3 relative to unidirectional loading, while tooth-root crack initiation life decreased by 31%. The study attributes the micropitting increase to periodic lubricant film disruption caused by instantaneous speed reversal through zero and discusses implications for flank load capacity calculations following ISO 6336 annexes.

title: Thermal EHL Film Thickness Calculation for Rough Gear Flanks: Comparison of Coupled and Decoupled Reynolds–Energy Approaches
abstract: Thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication (TEHL) models for gear contacts differ in how strongly the Reynolds equation and the energy equation are coupled during iteration. This paper compares three numerical strategies—fully coupled, semi-coupled, and decoupled—applied to spur gear flank conditions at slide-to-roll ratios between 0.05 and 0.35. Gear geometry corresponds to a module-3 pair with a 20° pressure angle and a centre distance of 91.5 mm. Film thickness calculations were validated against optical interferometry measurements on a twin-disc apparatus at matching entrainment velocities from 0.8 to 6.2 m/s. The fully coupled solver predicted central film thicknesses within 7% of measured values across the range, while the decoupled approach deviated by up to 22% at high slide-to-roll ratios. Viscosity-pressure coefficients were determined separately using a high-pressure viscometer at temperatures of 40 °C, 60 °C, and 90 °C. The work provides practical guidance on model selection relative to computational cost for gear EHL analysis.

title: Variable-Amplitude Load Spectra and Their Influence on Micropitting Accumulation in Helical Gears
abstract: Most gear fatigue data are generated at constant load, yet field gearboxes experience highly irregular load histories. This paper reports back-to-back helical gear tests run under three load spectra derived from measured industrial duty cycles: a steep-gradient spectrum (Weibull shape k = 1.1), a flat-gradient spectrum (k = 3.4), and a constant amplitude baseline. All spectra shared the same nominal equivalent torque of 840 N·m calculated by the ISO 6336-6 cumulative damage method. Micropitting area fraction was assessed by optical microscopy after 2×10^7 revolutions. The steep-gradient spectrum produced 40% less total micropitted area than the constant amplitude case despite equal equivalent loading, suggesting that the sequencing of low–high cycles allows partial EHL film recovery. Crack depth measurements by interrupted sectioning confirmed that pit depth did not increase proportionally with area fraction. The results challenge direct equivalence assumptions embedded in current load spectrum conversion methods.

title: Influence of Gear Oil Additive Package on Micropitting Load Capacity: FZG Micropitting Test Results for Four Commercial Formulations
abstract: Additive chemistry strongly affects micropitting performance, yet gear standards provide limited guidance on oil selection beyond viscosity grade. Four commercially formulated industrial gear oils—an EP sulphur-phosphorus oil, a polyalphaolefin synthetic, a polyglycol, and a mineral oil without active EP additives—were tested using the FZG micropitting test procedure (FVA 54/7) on standard FZG type C gears. Tests were run at load stages 5, 7, and 9, corresponding to maximum Hertz pressures of approximately 1306, 1466, and 1611 MPa respectively. The polyglycol formulation showed no measurable micropitting at load stage 9, while the EP sulphur-phosphorus oil produced 12% micropitted area at the same load stage. The mineral oil baseline failed at load stage 7 with 28% afflicted area. Traction coefficient measurements on a mini-traction machine correlated inversely with micropitting severity (r = −0.87), supporting a frictional heating mechanism for film disruption. Recommendations for oil selection criteria are discussed.

title: Residual Stress Relaxation in Case-Hardened Gear Flanks During Cyclic Contact Loading
abstract: Compressive residual stresses introduced by carburising and shot peening are known to retard fatigue crack initiation at gear flanks, but their stability under cyclic Hertzian loading has received less attention than root bending effects. This study tracks near-surface residual stress profiles by X-ray diffraction at four depths (10, 50, 100, and 200 µm) before testing and after 10^5, 10^6, and 5×10^6 load cycles at a maximum Hertz pressure of 1550 MPa. Specimens were 20MnCr5 gears, carburised and then shot-peened with S110 cast steel shot at an Almen intensity of 0.20 mmA. Initial surface compressive stresses of −680 MPa relaxed to −390 MPa after 10^5 cycles, with further relaxation to −310 MPa by 5×10^6 cycles. Relaxation rate followed a logarithmic law, and an empirical coefficient was fitted for use in fatigue life modelling. The implications for shot-peening specification in reversing-torque applications are discussed.

title: Experimental Assessment of Micropitting Failure Modes in Gears Under Combined Speed and Torque Transients
abstract: Wind turbine and industrial drive gears experience simultaneous transients in both rotational speed and transmitted torque. Controlled back-to-back tests were conducted imposing sinusoidal torque modulation (±30% of mean torque at 0.5 Hz) superimposed on step speed changes between 600 and 1800 rpm on module-5 helical gears. Three mean torque levels—600, 900, and 1200 N·m—were investigated. Combined transients accelerated micropitting initiation by 22–45% relative to constant-speed, variable-torque tests at the same equivalent torque. Damage was concentrated in the dedendum region and showed a characteristic striped morphology aligned with the sliding direction, distinct from the more diffuse pitting observed in steady-state tests. EHL film thickness calculations performed at instantaneous operating conditions suggest that speed transients reduce the minimum film thickness by up to 38% during deceleration ramps. These findings are relevant for gearbox rating in variable-speed drive applications.

title: Gear Flank Contact Fatigue Under Reversing Torque: A Chapter on Load Capacity Assessment Methods
abstract: This book chapter reviews load capacity assessment methods for gear flank contact fatigue with specific emphasis on reversing torque loading, which is inadequately covered by mainstream standards. The chapter begins with the physics of torque reversal—lubricant film collapse during zero-speed crossing, altered residual stress state from symmetric bending, and changed asperity contact statistics. It then surveys ISO 6336, AGMA 2101, and FVA research methods, identifying gaps in their treatment of non-unidirectional loading. A working procedure for applying a reversing-torque correction factor to the allowable contact stress is proposed, drawing on experimental data from back-to-back tests published between 2010 and 2021. Practical calculation examples for a crane hoist gearbox and a cold-rolling mill drive illustrate the procedure. Limitations and open research questions—particularly regarding additive-film behaviour under oscillatory sliding—are discussed in the final section.
venue: Advances in Gear Technology: Design, Materials and Tribology (edited volume, Springer)

title: Influence of Superfinishing on EHL Film Formation and Micropitting Resistance of Case-Hardened Gears
abstract: Superfinishing reduces flank roughness from a typical ground Ra of 0.35–0.50 µm to below 0.08 µm, improving the specific film thickness ratio λ substantially. This study quantifies the benefit under variable-amplitude loading with a Weibull shape factor k = 2.1 approximating a medium-duty industrial drive cycle. Module-4 carburised 20MnCr5 spur gears in ground and superfinished condition were tested at three load levels (700, 950, and 1150 N·m peak torque) for 3×10^7 cycles each. Superfinished gears showed zero measurable micropitting at 700 and 950 N·m, compared with 4% and 17% flank area affected for ground gears. At 1150 N·m, superfinished gears accumulated 3% micropitted area, a factor of 5.8 reduction. EHL film thickness predictions incorporating the measured topography confirm that the improvement cannot be fully explained by λ ratio alone; friction coefficient reduction (measured on a twin-disc, −22%) appears to contribute independently to the improvement.

title: Numerical Modelling of Mixed-Lubrication Contacts in Gear Flanks with Measured Rough Surfaces: Validation Against Twin-Disc Experiments
abstract: Mixed lubrication models that couple a full-system EHL solution with deterministic asperity contact are computationally expensive; simplifications are needed for practical gear analysis. This paper presents a semi-deterministic mixed-lubrication model applied to gear flank conditions using actual measured surface topography from ground gears (Sq = 0.41 µm) as input. The model solves the Reynolds equation on a deformed, roughness-modified gap with asperity contact contributions calculated from a Persson contact mechanics approach. Predicted contact pressure distributions, asperity contact area fractions, and traction coefficients are compared against twin-disc measurements at nine combinations of entrainment velocity (0.5–3.5 m/s) and slide-to-roll ratio (0.05–0.25). The mean deviation in traction coefficient is 8.3%, and asperity contact area fraction predictions agree within 12% of fluorescence-based measurements. Computation time per operating point is 4–11 minutes on a standard workstation, suggesting feasibility for load spectrum fatigue calculations.

title: Moisture ingress risk mapping for outdoor electromechanical enclosures across climatic regions of the Western Balkans
abstract: Meteorological data from 41 weather stations across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia were used to compute three moisture-ingress risk indicators: annual condensation-degree-days, maximum sustained diurnal temperature amplitude, and annual precipitation contact hours estimated from enclosure orientation geometry. A risk score was defined by weighting these indicators using coefficients derived from a previous regression model. Spatial maps were produced at 10 km × 10 km resolution using ordinary kriging interpolation. The Pannonian lowland region, including Vojvodina, was classified as moderate risk, while mountain basins in the Dinaric area showed high risk due to frequent temperature inversions producing prolonged condensation conditions. For each risk zone, minimum gasket specifications in terms of compression-set limit and diffusivity threshold are proposed. The dataset and scoring tool are made available as a freely downloadable spreadsheet to support enclosure procurement decisions by practitioners.

title: Embodied Carbon Trade-Offs in Modular versus Integral Product Architectures: A Case Study on Power Tool Platforms
abstract: Product architecture decisions made at concept stage can determine whether downstream repair and remanufacture are economically and technically feasible. This paper quantifies embodied carbon trade-offs between modular and integral architectures for a family of corded angle grinders using a hybrid LCA approach that combines process data with economic input-output data for upstream material production. Three architecture variants were parameterised: fully integral, partially modular (motor and gear subassemblies separable), and fully modular (all major subassemblies independently replaceable). End-of-life scenarios were defined in terms of replacement rates and subassembly substitution ratios drawn from repair workshop records at two Serbian service centres. Fully modular architecture reduced cumulative embodied carbon by 19–27% over a 15-year service horizon compared with integral designs, but only when spare part availability was maintained above a 70% fill-rate threshold. The cost of achieving this threshold is estimated and discussed relative to current producer incentive structures.

title: Flood Frequency Analysis Under Non-Stationarity: Evidence from Annual Maximum Discharge Series on Pannonian Tributaries
abstract: Long discharge records from nine gauging stations on lowland tributaries of the Danube and Sava in the Pannonian sector of Serbia and Croatia were analysed for trends and change points in annual maximum series covering 50 to 80 years. The Mann-Kendall test detected statistically significant upward trends at four stations and a step change around 1970 at two stations, likely associated with upstream land-use conversion. Generalised extreme value (GEV) distributions were fitted under both stationary and time-covariate frameworks using maximum likelihood estimation. Return-level estimates for the 100-year flood differed by up to 22% between the two approaches at stations with pronounced trends. The paper discusses implications for design flood standards adopted in Serbian hydraulic engineering practice and recommends periodic re-estimation of return levels at 10-year intervals for infrastructure located in the floodplain.

title: Coupling a Lumped Rainfall-Runoff Model with a 2-D Hydraulic Solver for Operational Flash Flood Warning on the Moravica Catchment
abstract: A semi-distributed HBV-type rainfall-runoff model was coupled sequentially with a TELEMAC-2D hydraulic model to simulate inundation on the lower Moravica River, a fast-responding tributary in central Serbia with a catchment area of 2 850 km². The hydrological component was calibrated on 15 flood events between 1991 and 2010, achieving Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency values between 0.71 and 0.88. The coupled system was tested on the May 2014 event, which produced a peak discharge of approximately 430 m³/s at the Ivanjica gauge. Predicted peak water levels at three downstream cross-sections agreed with post-event marks within 0.25 m. Computational time for a 72-hour simulation on 8 CPU cores was approximately 40 minutes, consistent with operational forecasting requirements. Bottlenecks in the coupling interface, particularly the routing of lateral inflows from ungauged sub-catchments, are discussed together with practical recommendations for implementation in a regional warning system.

title: Quantifying Uncertainty in 100-Year Flood Inundation Maps Using a Monte Carlo Framework with Latin Hypercube Sampling
abstract: Uncertainty in flood inundation maps originates from multiple sources: the design flood hydrograph, terrain data quality, roughness parameters, and numerical discretisation. A Monte Carlo framework using Latin hypercube sampling was developed and applied to a 35 km floodplain reach of the Begej Canal in Vojvodina. Five hundred realisations were executed in TELEMAC-2D, sampling jointly from probability distributions assigned to peak discharge, Manning n for six land-cover classes, and LiDAR vertical error. The 5th–95th percentile band of predicted inundation extent spanned between 8% and 31% of the median inundated area depending on location, with the widest uncertainty near the distal floodplain boundary. Contribution of individual sources to total variance was assessed by Sobol indices; peak discharge dominated at 62%, followed by riparian roughness at 24%. The resulting probabilistic inundation maps are compared with the deterministic map currently used in official flood risk management plans for Vojvodina.

title: Assimilation of Sentinel-1 SAR Flood Extent Observations into a 2-D Hydraulic Model Using an Ensemble Kalman Filter
abstract: Satellite synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery from the Sentinel-1A/B constellation provides near-real-time flood extent maps at 10–20 m spatial resolution and 6-day revisit intervals under all weather conditions. This study investigated whether assimilating SAR-derived wet/dry masks into a running TELEMAC-2D simulation via an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) could reduce water-level prediction errors during an ongoing flood event. The test case was the March 2018 inundation of the right bank floodplain of the Danube between Novi Sad and Stari Banovci. An ensemble of 50 model runs was generated by perturbing initial conditions and roughness fields. Assimilation of three SAR scenes acquired over 12 days reduced RMSE of water levels at two interior monitoring points from 0.31 m to 0.14 m compared with the open-loop run. The method increased computational cost by a factor of approximately 55 relative to a single deterministic run, and strategies for reducing this burden in an operational context are discussed.

title: Terrain Preprocessing Strategies for LiDAR-Derived Digital Elevation Models Used in Lowland Floodplain Hydraulic Modelling
abstract: Digital elevation models derived from airborne LiDAR surveys contain systematic and random errors that propagate into hydraulic model predictions. This book chapter reviews terrain preprocessing strategies relevant to lowland floodplain applications where elevation differences controlling flow connectivity are often less than one metre. Topics covered include ground-return filtering in dense riparian vegetation, interpolation methods for removing artefacts under bridge decks and culverts, channel-burning procedures and their sensitivity to the assigned channel depth, and gridding resolution trade-offs for finite-volume mesh generation. Case studies draw on LiDAR datasets acquired over floodplains of the Sava, Tisa, and Tamiš rivers in Serbia, with vertical RMSE values between 0.06 m and 0.19 m across different land-cover types. Practical guidelines are provided for defining preprocessing workflows appropriate to survey density, vegetation cover, and available auxiliary bathymetric data, with the aim of reducing the manual intervention currently required in standard GIS software packages.

title: Comparison of Structured and Unstructured Mesh Approaches for Simulating Overbank Flow in a Braided Reach of the Tisa River
abstract: Braided and anastomosing channel planforms present challenges for 2-D hydraulic models because flow partitioning among channels depends sensitively on mesh alignment and resolution. This study compared structured rectilinear (HEC-RAS 2D) and unstructured triangular (TELEMAC-2D) mesh simulations of a 22 km braided reach of the Tisa between Kanjiža and Novi Kneževac for the 1999 and 2006 overbank events. Both models were calibrated using the same roughness values and DEM, differing only in spatial discretisation. Inundation extent predictions agreed within 6% at peak stage, but velocity magnitude distributions differed by up to 0.6 m/s in bifurcating channels, with TELEMAC-2D capturing secondary channels more accurately against ADCP transects. Computational times per simulation hour were 2.1 minutes for HEC-RAS 2D on a 25 m structured grid and 3.7 minutes for TELEMAC-2D on an equivalent unstructured mesh using the same hardware. Neither solver consistently outperformed the other on all metrics; the structured approach offered faster setup while the unstructured approach better resolved channel geometry.

title: Estimating Return Periods of Compound Pluvial–Fluvial Flooding in Urban Areas Adjacent to Lowland Riverbanks
abstract: Compound flooding, where high river stages coincide with intense local rainfall, can produce inundation depths substantially greater than either driver acting alone. This study developed a bivariate frequency analysis of daily discharge and areal rainfall for a 780 km² peri-urban catchment draining into the Danube near Novi Sad, using 48 years of concurrent records. Dependence between the two variables was modelled with a Clayton copula, selected through AIC comparison with four alternative families. Joint return periods for discharge–rainfall combinations exceeding empirically defined flood thresholds were estimated and mapped onto a TELEMAC-2D model domain encompassing both the riverine floodplain and urban stormwater drainage network. For the 100-year joint return period, compound inundation area exceeded single-driver estimates by 34% and mean inundation depth by 0.27 m. The analysis informs a revised zoning proposal currently under review by the City of Novi Sad urban planning office.

title: Impact of Levee Setback Scenarios on Flood Wave Attenuation Along the Middle Tisa: A 2-D Modelling Study
abstract: River channelisation and historical levee construction along the Tisa have reduced floodplain storage, increasing peak discharges downstream. This study used a calibrated TELEMAC-2D model of a 95 km middle Tisa reach to evaluate four levee setback scenarios in which embankments were relocated 200, 500, 1000, and 2000 m from the current bankline. The baseline model was validated for the 2006 and 2010 flood events; water-level RMSE was 0.22 m across nine gauging stations. In the 2000 m setback scenario, peak discharge at the downstream boundary was reduced by 8.4% and peak water level by 0.31 m relative to baseline, at the cost of permanently inundating approximately 4 200 ha of agricultural land. Trade-offs between flood attenuation benefit, agricultural land loss, and ecological restoration potential are quantified and discussed with reference to the EU Floods Directive targets applicable to the Hungary–Serbia cross-border reach.

title: A Benchmark Dataset of ADCP Discharge and Water-Level Measurements for Hydraulic Model Validation on the Vojvodina Canal Network
abstract: Reliable validation data are a limiting factor for hydraulic model development in artificially managed canal systems. This paper presents a curated dataset of 214 ADCP discharge measurements and concurrent water-level records collected between 2015 and 2022 at 18 cross-sections on the Danube–Tisa–Danube and Begej canals in Vojvodina. Measurement uncertainty was quantified following the ISO 748 moving-boat procedure, yielding expanded uncertainties between 2.1% and 6.8% of measured discharge. The dataset spans a discharge range from 0.4 to 185 m³/s and includes three high-flow events during which backwater interactions between intersecting canals were documented. Metadata follow the FAIR data principles and include GPS positions, cross-section geometry, instrument configuration, and quality-control flags. The dataset has been deposited in an institutional repository and is described here to facilitate its use for calibration and validation of 2-D hydraulic models in canal-dominated lowland settings.

title: Probabilistic Flood Hazard Maps Under Climate Projections for the Sava Lowlands: Combining Regional Climate Model Ensembles with a 2-D Hydraulic Solver
abstract: Flood frequency analysis for infrastructure design conventionally relies on historical discharge records, which may not represent future hydroclimatic conditions. This study propagated an ensemble of 18 EURO-CORDEX regional climate model runs at 0.11° resolution through a calibrated HBV hydrological model and a TELEMAC-2D hydraulic model to derive probabilistic flood hazard maps for a 120 km reach of the lower Sava for the 2071–2100 period under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5. The ensemble spread in projected 100-year flood peak was ±41% around the ensemble median under RCP 8.5, substantially larger than the sampling uncertainty derived from the historical record alone. Inundation extent under the 90th-percentile RCP 8.5 projection exceeded the present-day 100-year inundation area by 18%. The analysis highlights that climate model uncertainty dominates total uncertainty for long planning horizons and should be reflected in updated flood risk zoning ordinances in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Gravel augmentation as a countermeasure to bed incision downstream of dams: review of European case studies and design principles
abstract: This book chapter synthesises experience from fourteen gravel augmentation programmes carried out in regulated rivers across Germany, Austria, France, Switzerland, and the former Yugoslav states between 1990 and 2015. Each programme is characterised by dam height, tailwater length, pre-intervention incision depth, augmentation volume per kilometre, grain-size specification, and monitored bed-level response duration. Augmented volumes ranged from 1,500 to 48,000 m³/year. Programmes targeting grain-size distributions matching the pre-regulation subarmour showed the most durable morphological response. Section 4 discusses criteria for injection site selection, including proximity to the competent-transport threshold and reach-scale sediment deficit. Design equations relating augmentation volume to required bypass fraction are derived from the synthesised data. Monitoring intervals of 6 months or less are identified as essential during the first three years post-injection. The chapter concludes with a decision framework applicable to dam operators in the Pannonian Basin region.

title: Sensitivity of precast concrete LCA results to background database choice: ecoinvent, EF-compliant datasets and a locally adapted Serbian dataset
abstract: Life-cycle assessment results for construction products are sensitive to the background database used, yet most Serbian studies rely on unmodified European or global databases. This paper systematically compares three background datasets – ecoinvent 3.9, the European Commission Environmental Footprint (EF 3.1) dataset, and a locally adapted Serbian dataset compiled from national energy statistics, cement plant emission reports, and aggregates industry data – applied to five representative precast concrete product types. For GWP (climate change, fossil), the Serbian-adapted dataset yields values 9–17% higher than ecoinvent 3.9 for products with a high cement content, primarily due to higher clinker-to-cement ratios in Serbian cement production (average 84% vs. 76% in the European average). For acidification and particulate matter formation, the locally adapted dataset shows differences of up to 31% from ecoinvent values. The paper makes the compiled Serbian background inventory dataset publicly available and recommends its use as a default in future Serbian EPD programmes.

title: Estimation of blood–brain barrier transfer constant Ktrans in patients with leukoaraiosis using a two-compartment DCE-MRI model
abstract: Leukoaraiosis, visible as confluent white matter hyperintensities on FLAIR imaging, is associated with impaired blood–brain barrier (BBB) integrity. This study applied a two-compartment Tofts pharmacokinetic model to DCE-MRI data acquired at 1.5T in 38 patients with moderate-to-severe leukoaraiosis (Fazekas grade 2–3) and 20 age-matched healthy controls. Dynamic series were acquired over 8 minutes following a 0.1 mmol/kg gadoterate meglumine bolus at a temporal resolution of 6 seconds. Mean Ktrans in normal-appearing white matter was 0.0031 ± 0.0009 min⁻¹ in patients compared with 0.0018 ± 0.0006 min⁻¹ in controls (p < 0.001). Within hyperintense lesion tissue, Ktrans rose to 0.0062 ± 0.0014 min⁻¹. Ve values did not differ significantly between groups. These findings support the hypothesis that subtle BBB leakage precedes macroscopic lesion formation and suggest that DCE-MRI Ktrans mapping may serve as a quantitative surrogate marker for early microvascular damage in leukoaraiosis.

title: Reproducibility of DCE-MRI perfusion parameters in the white matter: a test–retest study at 1.5T
abstract: Reliable quantitative DCE-MRI requires acceptable measurement reproducibility before clinical translation. Sixteen healthy adult volunteers (mean age 44 years) underwent two identical DCE-MRI sessions separated by 7 ± 2 days on the same 1.5T scanner. Ktrans, ve, and vp were extracted using the extended Tofts model with an individually measured arterial input function from the internal carotid artery. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) for Ktrans in frontal and parietal normal-appearing white matter were 0.81 and 0.78 respectively. Coefficient of variation across sessions was 14.2% for Ktrans and 9.7% for ve. Scanner-related thermal noise and inconsistent arterial input function sampling were identified as the main sources of variability. Correction for flip-angle inhomogeneity using a separately acquired B1 map reduced Ktrans variability by approximately 18%. These results establish a baseline for longitudinal study design and power calculations for future patient cohorts.

title: Cerebral perfusion mapping with pulsed arterial spin labelling in lacunar stroke: comparison with DSC-MRI
abstract: Diffusion-weighted imaging localises acute lacunar infarcts, but perfusion changes in surrounding tissue remain incompletely characterised. This prospective study enrolled 29 patients within 72 hours of a first-ever symptomatic lacunar infarct confirmed on DWI and 24 healthy controls. Pulsed ASL (PASL, QUIPSS II, post-labelling delay 1800 ms) and dynamic susceptibility contrast MRI (DSC-MRI) were acquired on the same 1.5T session. Cerebral blood flow (CBF) maps derived from PASL showed a perilesional hypoperfusion zone extending 4–8 mm beyond the DWI lesion boundary, with mean CBF reduced by 22% relative to the contralateral hemisphere. DSC-MRI Tmax prolongation corresponded spatially to PASL hypoperfusion in 21 of 29 cases. PASL overestimated absolute CBF by a mean of 11 ml/100g/min relative to DSC reference values. Bland–Altman analysis demonstrated acceptable agreement in relative perfusion asymmetry. These data support PASL as a contrast-free alternative in patients with renal impairment.

title: Pharmacokinetic model selection for DCE-MRI in cerebral small vessel disease: Tofts, extended Tofts, and Patlak compared
abstract: The choice of pharmacokinetic model affects the magnitude and interpretation of DCE-MRI parameters in tissues with low permeability such as white matter. Using data from 44 CSVD patients and 20 controls acquired on a 3T scanner, we fitted three models—standard Tofts, extended Tofts (ETM), and Patlak—to DCE time-series in normal-appearing white matter (NAWM) and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) regions. Model fit quality was assessed by Akaike information criterion (AIC) and by residual analysis. In NAWM, the Patlak model yielded the lowest mean AIC (−312 ± 41) and produced the most stable Ktrans estimates across noise realisations in a bootstrap analysis (CV 12%). ETM frequently failed to converge in NAWM due to negligible plasma volume fraction. In WMH tissue, both ETM and Patlak performed comparably. We recommend the Patlak model as the default for low-permeability white matter applications and provide reference Ktrans values stratified by Fazekas grade.
venue: Quantitative Neuroimaging Bulletin

title: DCE-MRI and cognitive decline in elderly patients with white matter hyperintensities: a two-year longitudinal study
abstract: Whether BBB permeability predicts cognitive trajectory in patients with white matter hyperintensities (WMH) remains uncertain. Sixty-two patients aged 60–80 years with Fazekas grade 1–3 WMH underwent baseline DCE-MRI at 3T and annual neuropsychological assessment over 24 months using the MoCA, Trail Making Test, and verbal fluency. Baseline Ktrans in NAWM predicted two-year MoCA decline independently of WMH volume and cardiovascular risk factors (β = −0.34, 95% CI −0.54 to −0.14, p = 0.002). Patients in the highest Ktrans tertile lost a mean 2.8 MoCA points versus 0.9 points in the lowest tertile. WMH volume growth over 24 months correlated with baseline Ktrans (r = 0.48, p < 0.001). These longitudinal data support Ktrans as an early predictor of cognitive and structural progression in CSVD, independent of lesion burden at baseline.
venue: Cerebrovascular Disease and Cognition

title: Automated segmentation of white matter hyperintensities for DCE-MRI region-of-interest placement: validation against manual delineation
abstract: Accurate region-of-interest (ROI) placement on white matter hyperintensities is labour-intensive and subject to observer variability in DCE-MRI studies of CSVD. We developed a semi-automated pipeline combining FLAIR-based WMH segmentation using a threshold-and-morphology approach with affine registration to the DCE-MRI native space. Validation was performed on 30 datasets with manual delineations by two experienced radiologists. Dice similarity coefficients between automated and manual ROIs were 0.81 ± 0.07 (reader 1) and 0.79 ± 0.08 (reader 2). Inter-reader Dice for manual segmentation was 0.82 ± 0.06. Ktrans values derived from automated ROIs agreed with manual ROIs to within 7% in paired comparisons (Bland–Altman limits of agreement −0.0008 to +0.0009 min⁻¹). Processing time per dataset was reduced from approximately 35 minutes to under 4 minutes. The pipeline is implemented in Python and has been made available to collaborating sites under an institutional data-sharing agreement.

title: Blood–brain barrier permeability in hypertensive versus normotensive cerebral small vessel disease: a matched-cohort DCE-MRI study
abstract: Hypertension is the dominant vascular risk factor for CSVD, yet its specific contribution to BBB disruption relative to other CSVD aetiologies is not well established. This matched-cohort study compared Ktrans and ve in 27 hypertensive CSVD patients (mean systolic BP 158 mmHg, treated) with 27 normotensive CSVD patients matched for age, sex, and total WMH volume. DCE-MRI was acquired at 3T using the Patlak model as established in prior work. Hypertensive patients showed 34% higher mean Ktrans in NAWM (0.0051 vs 0.0038 min⁻¹, p = 0.003) and a trend toward larger periventricular WMH volume (p = 0.06). Within WMH tissue, Ktrans did not differ significantly between groups. Antihypertensive medication class (ACE inhibitor versus calcium channel blocker) was not associated with Ktrans differences in this sample. Findings suggest hypertension amplifies NAWM permeability beyond what is attributable to lesion burden alone.

title: Perivascular space burden and DCE-MRI permeability: converging markers of glymphatic and barrier dysfunction in CSVD
abstract: Enlarged perivascular spaces (EPVS) are an emerging MRI marker of impaired interstitial fluid clearance and potential glymphatic dysfunction. We investigated the relationship between EPVS burden and DCE-MRI Ktrans in 52 patients with CSVD and 20 controls. EPVS were rated semi-quantitatively in basal ganglia and centrum semiovale on 3T T2-weighted images using the STRIVE-2 scale (0–4). Ktrans was measured in NAWM and in tissue immediately surrounding manually identified perivascular spaces. Higher basal ganglia EPVS score was independently associated with greater NAWM Ktrans after adjustment for age and WMH volume (β = 0.28, p = 0.018). Perivascular tissue Ktrans was 18% higher than matched NAWM Ktrans within the same hemisphere. No significant association was found for centrum semiovale EPVS. These results are consistent with a localised increase in transcapillary water exchange adjacent to enlarged spaces in the basal ganglia, though causality cannot be established from cross-sectional data.

title: DCE-MRI pharmacokinetic modelling in neurological disease: methodological principles and clinical applications
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured account of DCE-MRI pharmacokinetic analysis as applied to the brain, intended for radiologists and neurologists with limited quantitative imaging background. The Patlak and Tofts model families are described with emphasis on the assumptions relevant to the low-permeability cerebral environment. Sections cover acquisition protocol design, arterial input function measurement and its sources of error, fitting algorithms, and common pitfalls in parameter interpretation. Clinical application sections address CSVD, brain tumour grading, and radiation necrosis. Parameter reference ranges from published cohort studies are tabulated by disease category and field strength. A dedicated section discusses current barriers to multicentre harmonisation, including scanner-dependent T1 mapping protocols and contrast agent variability. The chapter concludes with a practical checklist for study design and a discussion of open-source software tools available for pharmacokinetic analysis.

title: Predicting one-year white matter lesion progression from baseline DCE-MRI in CSVD: a machine learning approach
abstract: Lesion growth in CSVD is heterogeneous and difficult to predict from baseline structural MRI alone. We trained a gradient-boosted tree classifier to predict radiologically significant WMH volume increase (≥30% at 12 months) using 23 features derived from baseline DCE-MRI (Ktrans, ve in NAWM and WMH tissue, periventricular versus deep WMH Ktrans asymmetry), conventional MRI morphometry, and clinical variables in 81 CSVD patients. Fivefold cross-validated AUC was 0.74 (95% CI 0.63–0.84). The three highest-importance features were NAWM Ktrans, periventricular WMH volume, and age. Logistic regression using only NAWM Ktrans achieved an AUC of 0.68. Adding DCE-MRI features to a clinical-plus-morphometry baseline model improved AUC from 0.63 to 0.74. Calibration curves showed modest overconfidence at high predicted probabilities. External validation in an independent cohort is planned. Code and anonymised feature tables are deposited in a public repository.
venue: NeuroInformatics and Imaging

title: Temporal signal-to-noise ratio requirements for reliable Ktrans estimation in white matter: simulations and empirical validation
abstract: Ktrans estimation in white matter by DCE-MRI is challenging because signal enhancement is near the noise floor. Monte Carlo simulations were conducted to determine the minimum tSNR required for Patlak model Ktrans estimates to fall within 20% of the true value across a physiologically plausible Ktrans range of 0.001–0.010 min⁻¹. Simulations indicated that tSNR ≥ 80 is necessary for Ktrans values below 0.003 min⁻¹, whereas tSNR ≥ 40 suffices for Ktrans above 0.005 min⁻¹. Empirical validation used spoiled gradient echo acquisitions on a 3T scanner with varying flip angles (8°, 12°, 18°) in 15 healthy volunteers and 10 CSVD patients. At flip angle 12°, mean tSNR in white matter was 94 ± 11, satisfying simulation-derived thresholds for all Ktrans ranges encountered clinically. Flip angle 8° reduced tSNR to 71 ± 9 and introduced a 26% positive bias in low-Ktrans regions. These results provide concrete protocol guidance for future DCE-MRI studies of white matter.

title: Diffusion-weighted MRI apparent diffusion coefficients in grading hepatic fibrosis: a comparison with histopathological Ishak scores
abstract: This retrospective study examined whether apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values derived from diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) at 1.5 T could differentiate fibrosis grades F0–F4 according to the Ishak histological scale in 74 adult patients with chronic hepatitis C. All patients underwent liver biopsy within four weeks of MRI examination. ADC maps were generated using b-values of 0, 400, and 800 s/mm². Mean ADC values decreased monotonically with increasing fibrosis grade, from 1.61 × 10⁻³ mm²/s at F0 to 1.09 × 10⁻³ mm²/s at F4. ROC analysis showed AUC of 0.81 for distinguishing significant fibrosis (F2 or above) from early-stage disease. Inter-observer agreement between two radiologists was substantial (κ = 0.74). The study concludes that DWI-derived ADC provides useful staging information but cannot fully replace biopsy at intermediate fibrosis grades where ADC distributions overlap considerably.

title: Inter-scanner variability of radiomics features in liver MRI: implications for multicentre fibrosis staging studies
abstract: Radiomics features computed from MRI are known to depend on scanner vendor, acquisition protocol, and reconstruction parameters. This phantom and patient study quantified inter-scanner variability for 91 features extracted from T2-weighted liver MRI acquired on three 1.5 T scanners from two vendors at two clinical sites in Serbia and one in Croatia. A structured fat-gel phantom was scanned under standardised and non-standardised protocols. In patients (n = 54), features were extracted from the same liver regions after deformable registration. Of 91 features, only 34 were classified as robust (ICC > 0.75) across all scanners under standardised protocols; this dropped to 19 under non-standardised protocols. Intensity normalisation using a z-score approach improved robustness for 12 additional features. Results quantify the subset of features suitable for multicentre studies without harmonisation of raw scanner output, and provide a short-list of stable features for future fibrosis staging model development.

title: Comparison of three liver segmentation approaches for texture-based fibrosis staging on T1-weighted MRI
abstract: The reproducibility of texture-based fibrosis staging depends heavily on how the liver parenchyma region of interest is defined. This study compared three segmentation approaches—manual delineation by an experienced radiologist, semi-automatic threshold-based segmentation, and a deep learning U-Net segmentation trained on 200 annotated volumes—with respect to their impact on 42 radiomics features and downstream staging accuracy in 88 patients with biopsy-confirmed fibrosis. Dice similarity coefficients relative to manual segmentation were 0.83 for threshold-based and 0.94 for U-Net methods. Feature stability (ICC > 0.75) was achieved for 31 features using manual, 27 using threshold-based, and 38 features using U-Net segmentation. Staging AUC for advanced fibrosis (F3–F4) was 0.86 with U-Net, 0.82 with manual, and 0.79 with threshold-based segmentation. The results indicate that segmentation method affects both feature stability and diagnostic performance, and that automated deep learning segmentation improves overall pipeline consistency.

title: Dose audit of paediatric chest CT across three Serbian tertiary hospitals: protocol variability and radiation risk estimates
abstract: We conducted a retrospective dose audit of 614 paediatric chest CT examinations performed between 2016 and 2020 at three tertiary hospitals in Serbia (Novi Sad, Belgrade, Niš). Patient age, weight, CTDIvol, dose–length product (DLP), and reconstruction parameters were extracted from DICOM headers. Effective doses were estimated using PCXMC 2.0 with age-specific phantoms. Median CTDIvol across institutions ranged from 1.8 to 5.3 mGy for the 5–10 year age group, a nearly threefold variation. Only one centre had a written paediatric-specific CT protocol. Estimated effective doses for the 1–5 year group exceeded published European diagnostic reference levels in 34% of examinations. Iterative reconstruction was used in 58% of scans but without standardised blending level documentation. The findings highlight the need for national paediatric CT dose reference levels and structured protocol harmonisation across Serbian radiology departments.

title: Elastography chapter: thyroid and parathyroid glands
abstract: This book chapter reviews the technical principles of strain and shear-wave elastography, summarises clinical evidence for thyroid nodule characterisation accumulated between 2008 and 2022, and provides practical guidance for protocol standardisation. Sections cover equipment requirements, patient positioning, reference region selection for strain ratio, sources of measurement error, integration with EU-TIRADS, and reporting recommendations. A dedicated section addresses challenging scenarios: nodules adjacent to calcified structures, substernal goitres, and co-existing diffuse thyroid disease. Parathyroid applications are briefly surveyed, including limited data on elastographic differentiation of adenomas from lymph nodes. The chapter also discusses ongoing methodological debates regarding the superiority of quantitative SWE over qualitative strain scoring and the lack of universally agreed malignancy thresholds across equipment manufacturers. Intended for practising radiologists and radiology trainees, the chapter includes an illustrated case series of ten annotated clinical examples.

title: Characterisation of a screen-printed piezoresistive array for robotic fingertip applications
abstract: This paper describes the fabrication and static characterisation of a 4×4 piezoresistive taxel array produced by screen-printing carbon-black-loaded silicone ink onto a flexible polyimide substrate. Each taxel measures 4 mm × 4 mm with a 1 mm gap, giving a 64 mm² active area per finger segment. Resistance-force curves were acquired using a calibrated load cell over the range 0–10 N at 0.1 N steps. Sensitivity was found to average 0.18 kΩ/N across the array, with a taxel-to-taxel coefficient of variation of 12 %. Hysteresis measured at 1 Hz triangular loading reached 8 % of full-scale output. Crosstalk between adjacent taxels was below 4 % when single-taxel loads were applied. A simple row-column scanning circuit with transimpedance amplifiers was implemented on a four-layer PCB, sampling the full array at 200 Hz. The paper discusses how the ink curing temperature and squeegee pressure affect sensitivity uniformity, and proposes a per-taxel offset calibration procedure that reduces the coefficient of variation to 5 %.

title: Effect of substrate compliance on spatial resolution in flexible tactile sensor arrays
abstract: Spatial resolution in flexible tactile arrays is degraded when lateral load spreading within the substrate causes a single point contact to activate multiple taxels. This study quantifies that effect for three substrate materials — 0.5 mm silicone shore-A 30, 1 mm silicone shore-A 50, and 0.5 mm polyurethane foam — each laminated onto an identical 8×8 piezoresistive array with 3 mm taxel pitch. A micro-positioning stage applied 2 N point loads at 1 mm intervals across a 30 mm scan line, and the resulting activation profiles were fitted with a Gaussian to extract the effective spatial resolution. The soft silicone showed a half-power width of 6.1 mm, the harder silicone 4.4 mm, and the polyurethane 3.2 mm. Finite-element simulations of substrate deformation with a Neo-Hookean material model reproduced experimental results with less than 9 % error. Results suggest that for applications requiring sub-taxel contact localisation, a thin stiff overlay combined with post-processing deconvolution is preferable to maximising compliance.

title: A low-noise analogue front-end for high-density piezoresistive tactile arrays operating at sampling rates above 500 Hz
abstract: High-density tactile arrays used in dexterous manipulation require analogue front-ends that combine low input-referred noise, fast settling after multiplexer switching, and minimal power dissipation on the fingertip. This paper presents a front-end architecture built around a 32-channel analogue switch, a transimpedance amplifier stage with programmable feedback resistance (10 kΩ–1 MΩ), and a 16-bit successive-approximation ADC. The design targets a 16×16 taxel array sampled at 500 Hz per taxel. Noise analysis and measurements show an input-referred voltage noise of 42 nV/√Hz at 100 Hz and a total harmonic distortion below −68 dB at full scale. Switch-charge injection was reduced to below 1 LSB by careful bootstrapping. The entire front-end consumes 85 mW from a 3.3 V supply. Experiments with a resistive load network emulating a full 256-taxel array confirm that the architecture meets both noise and throughput targets, and a crosstalk model based on parasitic capacitance is validated against measurements at frequencies up to 1 kHz.

title: Contact-force distribution reconstruction using regularised least squares on a compliant tactile array
abstract: Recovering the full continuous contact-force distribution from a sparse taxel array is an ill-posed inverse problem, particularly when the substrate compliance couples neighbouring taxels. This paper formulates the reconstruction as a regularised least-squares problem in which the forward model relates a discretised pressure field to observed taxel resistances via a compliance-dependent coupling matrix identified through indentation experiments. Tikhonov regularisation with an L2 spatial smoothness constraint is applied; the regularisation parameter is selected by generalised cross-validation over a held-out calibration set. Experiments used a 12×12 array mounted on a 2 mm shore-A 40 silicone pad pressed by 3D-printed indenters of three shapes. The reconstructed pressure maps achieved a root-mean-square error of 1.8 kPa against reference profiles computed from indenter geometry and applied load. Reconstruction ran on a Cortex-M7 microcontroller at 120 Hz. The paper also discusses how errors in the coupling matrix affect reconstruction quality and proposes a sequential update scheme to track slow drift in sensor properties.

title: Thermal drift compensation in piezoresistive tactile arrays used in industrial assembly cells
abstract: Industrial environments impose temperature fluctuations of 10–25 °C over a working shift, causing substantial zero-drift in piezoresistive sensors based on carbon-black composites. This paper characterises the thermal drift behaviour of two commercial conductive silicone sheets and one in-house screen-printed ink over 0–50 °C using a climate chamber and a dead-weight load frame. Drift in the unloaded resistance reached 18 % of full scale for the worst-case material over a 20 °C step. A compensation scheme is proposed in which one sacrificial reference taxel per 4×4 zone is kept unloaded; its resistance is used to estimate local temperature and subtract drift from its neighbours. The scheme was tested on a 12×12 array mounted on a gripper installed in a small-parts assembly station that cycles between room temperature and a heated fixture at 45 °C. After compensation, the residual zero-drift was below 1.2 % of full scale across all tested temperature profiles. The computation adds less than 0.5 ms per frame at 200 Hz.

title: Estimating internal stress distribution in grasped soft objects from surface tactile measurements: a model-based approach
abstract: When a robotic gripper squeezes a soft object, the internal stress field determines whether the object will be damaged. Surface tactile measurements provide boundary conditions from which the internal field can be estimated if a material model is available. This paper presents a workflow in which a Neo-Hookean finite-element model of the grasped object is updated online by matching its predicted surface traction to the measured tactile pressure map via an extended Kalman filter that adjusts the shear modulus G and a shape-distortion parameter. Internal von Mises stress maps are then computed from the updated model at each timestep. The approach was evaluated on four gel phantoms with known material properties (G = 2–18 kPa) and five fruit specimens. For gel phantoms the estimated G agreed with reference rheometry values within 11 %. For fruit, predicted regions of stress concentration correlated spatially with post-grasp bruise patterns assessed by image segmentation, correctly identifying the highest-stress region in 7 of 8 trials. Computation runs at 30 Hz on a desktop GPU.

title: A multi-modal fingertip sensor combining tactile pressure and proximity for pre-contact and in-contact manipulation phases
abstract: Seamless transition between pre-contact approach and in-contact manipulation is hampered when the sensor modality changes between phases. This paper describes a fingertip module that integrates a 10×10 piezoresistive tactile array with four time-of-flight proximity cells spaced at 45° around the fingertip perimeter, sharing a single I²C bus and a common signal-conditioning board. The proximity cells detect objects within 5–80 mm with 0.3 mm resolution at 100 Hz; they are used to orient the fingertip and pre-position the fingers before contact. Upon contact, the tactile array takes over for force distribution measurement. A finite-state machine running on an STM32H7 microcontroller manages the handover. Grasping trials on 20 objects of varying geometry and compliance showed that fingertip orientation errors before contact were reduced from a mean of 11.4° (tactile-only baseline) to 2.8° when proximity feedback was used, leading to a 34 % reduction in required grip-force correction after first contact.

title: Data-driven contact-force estimation from tactile images using a lightweight convolutional architecture trained on synthetic data
abstract: Collecting large labelled datasets from physical tactile sensors is expensive. This paper investigates whether a convolutional neural network trained predominantly on synthetic tactile images — generated by a finite-element contact simulator calibrated on 800 real indentation samples — can estimate three-axis contact force (Fx, Fy, Fz) and contact area from 16×16 tactile frames without manual labelling at scale. The synthetic training set comprised 50 000 frames covering indenter shapes, orientations, and loading histories not present in the real calibration set. The network uses five convolutional layers and two fully connected layers (total 148 000 parameters) to enable deployment on a microcontroller with 512 kB SRAM. On a held-out real test set of 3 200 frames the model achieved mean absolute errors of 0.21 N (Fz), 0.09 N (Fx, Fy), and 4.7 mm² (contact area). A domain-randomisation study identifies surface friction coefficient and substrate thickness as the parameters most critical to sim-to-real transfer.
venue: Robotics and Autonomous Systems

title: Benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol for contact-force distribution estimation on soft robotic grippers
abstract: Progress in tactile sensing is hampered by the absence of shared benchmarks that allow direct comparison of sensor designs and estimation algorithms. This paper defines a benchmark consisting of 14 standardised indentation scenarios — covering point contacts, distributed loads, sliding events, and multi-finger squeeze of deformable cylinders — along with a repeatable measurement protocol using a 6-axis force-torque reference sensor and a motorised stage. A dataset collected on three different fingertip designs (one piezoresistive array, one capacitive array from a collaborating group, and one optical waveguide sensor) is made publicly available. Evaluation metrics include spatial RMSE of pressure maps, force magnitude and direction errors, contact-area Intersection over Union, and latency. Baseline results show that piezoresistive arrays achieve the lowest force-magnitude RMSE (0.18 N) but the highest spatial RMSE (2.3 kPa) compared with the optical sensor. The protocol and scoring scripts are released under an open licence.

title: Benchmarking Prognosis Models for Industrial Pump Bearings on a Common Multi-Site Dataset: Methodology and Preliminary Results
abstract: Comparisons of remaining useful life prognosis methods in the literature are often confounded by differences in experimental setup, health index definition, and evaluation metrics. This preprint describes a benchmarking protocol and a preliminary dataset collected from 31 pump bearing run-to-failure experiments across three industrial sites, standardising data format, health index construction, train/test split rules, and evaluation metrics (MAPE, scoring function, and coverage of 90% prediction intervals). Seven prognosis approaches were evaluated: Wiener-process model, particle filter with empirical degradation model, LSTM network, temporal convolutional network, Gaussian process regression, random survival forest, and a simple exponential smoothing baseline. No single method dominated across all sites and failure modes. The Gaussian process regression and random survival forest models showed the most consistent performance, while LSTM achieved the lowest MAPE on two of three sites but the widest prediction intervals. The dataset and evaluation code are provided as supplementary material.

title: Generating ISO 26262 test cases from Simulink models
abstract: This paper presents a systematic methodology for automatically generating ISO 26262-compliant test cases directly from Simulink models used in automotive software development. The approach leverages model-based design artifacts to extract safety requirements and derive corresponding test objectives at the software unit and integration levels, ensuring traceability from the Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) decomposition down to executable test scripts. A custom toolchain was developed to parse Simulink block diagrams, identify safety-relevant signal paths, and produce structured test case descriptions compatible with both MIL and SIL environments. The proposed method was validated on two industrial case studies involving an electronic stability control module and a battery management system. Results demonstrate a significant reduction in manual test case authoring effort—approximately 47%—while maintaining full compliance with ISO 26262 Part 6 requirements. The paper also discusses integration with existing CI/CD pipelines and addresses scalability challenges for large subsystem models. The findings suggest that model-driven test generation can substantially improve both the efficiency and auditability of the software verification process in safety-critical automotive projects.

title: A low-cost hardware-in-the-loop bench for body control modules
abstract: This paper describes the design, implementation, and validation of a low-cost hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) bench specifically targeting body control module (BCM) testing in automotive embedded systems. Conventional HIL platforms from major vendors impose significant cost barriers for small and medium enterprises as well as academic laboratories; the proposed bench achieves comparable functional coverage using commercial off-the-shelf single-board computers, open-source real-time operating system components, and a custom signal conditioning board developed in-house. The architecture supports CAN and LIN bus simulation, load simulation for actuators such as window motors and door locks, and fault injection at the electrical interface level. A set of standardized test sequences covering ISO 26262 hardware–software integration testing requirements was executed on a production BCM unit, and the results were compared against reference outputs from a commercial HIL system. Timing accuracy and signal fidelity measurements confirm that the bench meets the requirements for functional regression testing and early fault detection. The total bill of materials remains below 800 EUR, making it accessible for university laboratories and startup companies. The paper concludes with a discussion of current limitations and planned extensions toward AUTOSAR-aware test orchestration.

title: AUTOSAR Classic to Adaptive migration patterns for high-performance automotive controllers
abstract: The transition from AUTOSAR Classic Platform to AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform introduces significant architectural and toolchain challenges for automotive software teams. This paper systematically identifies and categorizes migration patterns applicable when porting existing Classic-based software components to the Adaptive Platform, focusing on service-oriented communication, POSIX-based execution environments, and updated memory protection models. A pattern catalog of fourteen recurring migration scenarios is presented, each accompanied by a rationale, structural transformation rules, and guidance on maintaining ISO 26262 compliance throughout the migration process. The patterns were derived from a combination of industrial case studies performed in collaboration with an automotive supplier in Novi Sad and from analysis of publicly available AUTOSAR specification documents. A prototype migration support tool implementing seven of the identified patterns was developed and evaluated on a real-time sensor fusion component. Evaluation metrics include migration effort in person-hours, residual defect density, and ASIL integrity preservation. The results indicate that structured pattern application reduces unplanned rework by approximately 38% compared to ad-hoc migration approaches. The paper concludes with an outlook on toolchain integration and standardization opportunities for the identified pattern catalog.
