title: Fault injection strategies for ASIL-D software components under AUTOSAR
abstract: Fault injection is a cornerstone technique for verifying the robustness of safety-critical embedded software, yet its systematic application within AUTOSAR-structured software stacks remains underexplored. This paper proposes a structured fault injection framework targeting ASIL-D software components deployed on AUTOSAR Classic-compliant electronic control units. The framework defines three injection layers—source code mutation, binary instrumentation, and hardware-level signal perturbation—and maps each layer to specific ISO 26262 Part 6 verification objectives. A classification of relevant fault models is introduced, covering stuck-at faults in inter-runnable variable communication, timing violations in OS task scheduling, and corrupted PDU data on CAN bus interfaces. The framework was implemented as a set of Eclipse-based plugins integrated with an existing MBT workflow and validated on an adaptive cruise control software component. Coverage metrics based on fault detection rate and diagnostic coverage are reported, demonstrating that the combined three-layer approach achieves a diagnostic coverage of 94.6% for the tested component. The paper also discusses the overhead introduced by instrumentation and proposes lightweight profiling strategies to minimize impact on real-time behavior. Recommendations for integrating the framework into continuous integration pipelines for automotive projects are provided.

title: Model-based coverage criteria for safety-critical automotive software: a comparative study
abstract: Coverage criteria are essential for assessing the thoroughness of testing activities mandated by ISO 26262 for automotive software. While several coverage metrics exist—ranging from statement and branch coverage to modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC)—their applicability and effectiveness within model-based development environments such as Simulink and TargetLink have not been comprehensively compared. This paper presents a controlled comparative study of six structural coverage criteria applied to model-based automotive software components across three ASIL levels (B, C, and D). Test suites generated using each criterion are evaluated with respect to fault detection effectiveness, test suite size, generation time, and alignment with ISO 26262 recommendations. The study uses a set of twelve Simulink subsystem models sourced from an industrial partner representing powertrain and chassis control domains. Results reveal that MC/DC consistently yields the highest fault detection rates for ASIL-C and ASIL-D components but incurs a test suite size penalty of up to 3.1× compared to branch coverage. A decision framework is proposed to guide engineers in selecting coverage criteria based on ASIL level, model complexity, and available testing budget. The paper also identifies gaps in current tool support for automated coverage measurement in model-based environments.

title: Real-time OS scheduling analysis for AUTOSAR multi-core ECUs under safety constraints
abstract: The adoption of multi-core processors in automotive electronic control units introduces complex scheduling challenges that directly affect functional safety compliance under ISO 26262. This paper analyzes real-time operating system scheduling strategies for AUTOSAR Classic multi-core configurations, focusing on task partitioning, inter-core communication latency, and deadline guarantee mechanisms. A formal timing analysis model based on response-time analysis is extended to account for AUTOSAR-specific constraints such as inter-runnable variable synchronization, OS counter resolution, and memory protection unit boundaries. The model is applied to three representative multi-core ECU configurations: a dual-core powertrain controller, a quad-core advanced driver assistance system module, and a dual-core body domain controller. Scheduling feasibility under worst-case execution time scenarios is evaluated, and the impact of different partitioning strategies on overall system latency is quantified. Additionally, the paper examines how ASIL decomposition across cores influences scheduling freedom and discusses trade-offs between safety isolation and computational efficiency. Experimental validation was performed on a development board equipped with a TriCore-class processor running an AUTOSAR-compliant RTOS. The results provide actionable guidance for engineers performing timing analysis during AUTOSAR-based ECU software integration.

title: Systematic safety analysis integration in AUTOSAR software development workflows
abstract: Safety analysis activities such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) are required by ISO 26262 but are often performed in isolation from the software development workflow, leading to inconsistencies and rework. This paper proposes a methodology for tightly integrating FMEA and FTA into AUTOSAR-based software development using a model-driven engineering approach. The methodology defines bidirectional traceability links between AUTOSAR software component models, safety analysis artifacts, and ISO 26262 work products, enabling automated consistency checks and impact analysis when software architecture changes occur. A prototype implementation using Eclipse Modeling Framework and a custom AUTOSAR metamodel extension is described and evaluated through an industrial case study involving an electronic power steering controller developed at an automotive supplier in Novi Sad. Quantitative evaluation shows that the integrated approach reduces safety analysis update effort by 31% following architecture changes and decreases the number of traceability gaps found during safety audits by 62%. Qualitative feedback from engineers involved in the case study highlights improved awareness of safety implications during routine software design decisions. The paper discusses open research challenges including scalability to full vehicle-level safety cases and integration with systems engineering tools such as SysML.

title: Embedded software testing for over-the-air update mechanisms in connected vehicles
abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) software update mechanisms are becoming standard features in modern connected vehicles, yet their interaction with safety-critical embedded software components raises unresolved testing and functional safety challenges. This paper investigates testing strategies for OTA update managers implemented within AUTOSAR Adaptive environments, with a focus on verifying that update procedures preserve ASIL integrity and do not introduce unsafe states during or after software installation. A risk-based test strategy is developed, identifying eleven critical test scenarios derived from ISO 26262 Part 6 and UNECE WP.29 cybersecurity regulation requirements. The paper describes a hardware-in-the-loop test environment extended with an OTA simulation backend to execute these scenarios under realistic network conditions including partial download failures, power interruptions during flashing, and rollback operations. The proposed test suite was applied to an OTA update manager prototype running on an Adaptive AUTOSAR stack, revealing three previously undiscovered fault handling deficiencies. Metrics including update success rate, recovery time, and post-update ASIL integrity indicators are reported and analyzed. The paper concludes with recommendations for standardizing OTA testing requirements within future revisions of automotive functional safety standards and proposes extensions to the existing HIL bench infrastructure described in prior work.

title: Automotive embedded software quality metrics: an industrial survey and taxonomy
abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of ISO 26262 in the automotive industry, there is no consensus on which software quality metrics best predict functional safety outcomes for embedded automotive software. This paper presents findings from a structured industrial survey involving 43 software engineers and safety managers from twelve automotive suppliers and OEM development centers across Central and Eastern Europe, supplemented by a systematic literature review covering 2010–2022. Participants were asked to rank the relevance, ease of collection, and predictive validity of 28 candidate quality metrics spanning code complexity, test coverage, defect density, static analysis violation rates, and AUTOSAR architecture compliance indicators. Survey results are synthesized into a taxonomy of automotive embedded software quality metrics organized along three dimensions: development phase applicability, ASIL sensitivity, and toolchain availability. The taxonomy reveals that metrics directly tied to AUTOSAR architectural constraints—such as inter-runnable variable coupling and software component interface complexity—are considered highly relevant by practitioners but lack standardized measurement tool support. The paper also reports correlation data between selected metrics and field defect rates obtained from three participating companies. Implications for process improvement, tool vendors, and future ISO 26262 revisions are discussed. The taxonomy is made available as a supplementary artifact to support replication and extension studies.

title: Removal of zinc and nickel from synthetic electroplating rinsewater by electrocoagulation with iron electrodes
abstract: Electrocoagulation (EC) was applied to treat synthetic rinsewater containing 50–200 mg/L Zn(II) and 30–150 mg/L Ni(II) using mild-steel iron electrodes in a monopolar batch reactor. Operating variables included current density (5–30 mA/cm²), electrolysis time (10–60 min), initial pH (4–9), and NaCl concentration (0.5–3 g/L). Removal efficiencies exceeding 98% for Zn and 95% for Ni were achieved at a current density of 20 mA/cm², pH 7, and 40 min electrolysis time. Specific energy consumption at optimal conditions was 1.8 kWh/m³. Electrode dissolution followed Faraday's law within ±6%. The resulting sludge was characterised by XRD and SEM-EDX, revealing amorphous iron hydroxide phases co-precipitating with metal hydroxides. The study provides baseline data for scaling the process toward SME applications where batch treatment cycles of 1–2 m³ per shift are typical.

title: Electrooxidation of free cyanide in alkaline rinsewater using dimensionally stable anode (DSA) cells
abstract: The destruction of free cyanide (CN⁻) in alkaline electroplating rinsewater (pH 10–12, CN⁻ 50–500 mg/L) was investigated using dimensionally stable anodes (Ti/RuO₂-IrO₂) in a flow-through reactor. Experiments examined the effects of current density (20–100 mA/cm²), flow rate (0.5–3 L/min), and initial cyanide concentration on removal efficiency and by-product distribution. At 60 mA/cm² and a hydraulic retention time of 12 min, CN⁻ was reduced from 200 mg/L to below 0.1 mg/L, meeting Serbian discharge limits. Cyanate (CNO⁻) formed as an intermediate, peaking at approximately 8 min and subsequently declining. Chlorine-mediated oxidation was identified as the dominant pathway when Cl⁻ exceeded 1 g/L. Total organic carbon measurements confirmed mineralisation rather than simple conversion to CNO⁻. Energy demand was 4.3 kWh per gram CN⁻ destroyed at optimal conditions.

title: Response surface optimisation of electrocoagulation parameters for simultaneous removal of Cu(II) and CN⁻ from mixed electroplating effluent
abstract: Mixed copper–cyanide effluents arising from copper cyanide plating baths present a dual treatment challenge because copper–cyanide complexes resist simple precipitation. A central composite design (CCD) with five factors—current density, pH, reaction time, NaCl concentration, and inter-electrode gap—was applied to a 2-litre batch EC reactor fitted with iron electrodes. Response surface methodology (RSM) identified optimal conditions at 22 mA/cm², pH 9.5, 45 min, 1.5 g/L NaCl, and 10 mm gap, yielding 99.4% Cu and 91.7% CN⁻ removal. The quadratic model showed good fit (R² = 0.964). Residual cyanide in the treated effluent was predominantly in the form of iron–cyanide complexes, suggesting that a polishing electrooxidation step would be required to meet discharge standards. The study demonstrates RSM as an efficient tool for multi-parameter EC optimisation in SME contexts.

title: Characterisation and leaching behaviour of electrocoagulation sludge from chromium-bearing electroplating rinsewater
abstract: Sludge generated during electrocoagulation treatment of Cr(VI)-containing rinsewater (80–250 mg/L) with iron electrodes was collected, dried, and characterised by XRD, FTIR, TGA, and scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray analysis. The dried sludge contained 12–18% Cr by mass, predominantly as Cr(III) hydroxide co-precipitated within an amorphous Fe(OH)₃ matrix. Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) tests at pH 4.9 and 2.88 showed Cr leaching below 5 mg/L, the Serbian hazardous-waste threshold, under most conditions, though sludge produced at pH below 5.5 during EC failed the test. Thermal treatment at 600 °C reduced TCLP leachate Cr to below 0.3 mg/L. These data inform SME operators on sludge disposal classification and handling requirements under national waste regulations. Sludge volume index data are provided as a function of initial Cr concentration.

title: Pilot-scale continuous-flow electrocoagulation for nickel removal from rinsewaters of a job-shop plating operation
abstract: A 50-litre per hour continuous-flow EC pilot unit was installed at a small job-shop electroplating facility in the Novi Sad industrial zone under a monitoring agreement. The unit used aluminium electrodes in a bipolar configuration. Influent Ni(II) varied from 18 to 210 mg/L across a 90-day operating period, reflecting batch-to-batch process variability typical of job-shop operations. Automatic pH adjustment to 7.5 and a current density set point of 15 mA/cm² maintained effluent Ni below 0.5 mg/L on 97% of sampling days. Electrode passivation was observed after 30 days of continuous operation and was mitigated by periodic polarity reversal. Energy consumption averaged 2.1 kWh/m³. Sludge production was 0.8 kg dry mass per m³ treated. The study documents operational parameters and failure modes relevant to SME-scale implementation.

title: Combined electrocoagulation–electrooxidation treatment of complex cyanide in spent copper–zinc plating bath dilutions
abstract: Complex cyanides (tetracyanozincate and copper–cyanide complexes) in diluted spent bath solutions (CN_total 100–800 mg/L) were treated in a two-stage reactor: an EC stage with iron electrodes followed by an electrooxidation (EO) stage with boron-doped diamond (BDD) anodes. In the EC stage, copper was reduced to below 0.3 mg/L and free cyanide to below 5 mg/L, but complex cyanide persisted. The subsequent BDD–EO stage at 40 mA/cm² and 20 min reduced total cyanide to below 0.2 mg/L and total Zn to below 0.5 mg/L. TOC decreased by 88% overall. The combined process consumed 6.7 kWh/m³. Cost modelling suggested that electricity represents 62% of the total variable operating cost for a 10 m³/day SME system. The two-stage approach is compared against single-stage alkaline chlorination as the current regulatory default.

title: Electrochemical treatment of heavy metals in industrial wastewater: fundamentals and SME-oriented applications
abstract: This chapter reviews the electrochemical mechanisms underpinning electrocoagulation and electrooxidation for the removal of Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, and Pb from industrial wastewaters, with emphasis on reactor design considerations applicable to small-to-medium enterprises. Electrode materials, cell configurations (monopolar vs. bipolar, batch vs. continuous), and the influence of key water quality parameters—conductivity, pH, competing anions, and organic complexing agents—are discussed in relation to treatment performance and operating economics. A section on sludge management addresses classification under EU and Serbian regulatory frameworks. Case examples drawn from electroplating, metal finishing, and printed circuit board manufacturing are included. The chapter is intended as a technical reference for environmental engineers and SME managers, and does not present original experimental data.

title: Effect of chloride and sulphate background electrolytes on electrooxidation efficiency for cyanide destruction at BDD anodes
abstract: The influence of background anion composition on cyanide electrooxidation at boron-doped diamond (BDD) anodes was systematically examined. Synthetic solutions containing 200 mg/L CN⁻ were prepared with Cl⁻/SO₄²⁻ molar ratios ranging from 0.1 to 10 at total ionic strengths of 20 and 50 mM. At Cl⁻/SO₄²⁻ > 1, the active chlorine pathway dominated, reducing treatment time by up to 45% compared to sulphate-only systems, but generating chlorate as a secondary by-product at concentrations up to 12 mg/L. At Cl⁻/SO₄²⁻ < 0.5, hydroxyl radical-mediated oxidation prevailed with no detectable chlorate but slower kinetics. A practical operating window of Cl⁻/SO₄²⁻ 0.5–2 is proposed to balance kinetics with by-product formation. The findings are relevant to electroplating facilities where bath chemistry determines the Cl⁻/SO₄²⁻ ratio of rinsewaters without additional electrolyte dosing.

title: Energy benchmarking of electrocoagulation systems for Zn, Ni, and Cr removal at Serbian electroplating SMEs: field survey and modelling
abstract: On-site measurements were conducted at seven electroplating SMEs in Vojvodina that had installed or were trialling EC units of varying design. Data collected over six months included influent and effluent metal concentrations, electrical energy meters, electrode mass loss records, and treated volume logs. Specific energy consumption ranged from 0.9 to 6.4 kWh/m³ across sites, with the widest variation attributable to incorrect pH management and oversizing. A simple empirical model based on current density and initial metal load predicted site-level energy use within ±20% for Zn and Ni systems but showed larger errors for Cr(VI) systems, likely due to variable organic complexing agent loads. Recommendations for reducing energy use at underperforming sites are presented. The dataset represents the first published field benchmark for EC at electroplating SMEs in Serbia.

title: Modelling of Cr(VI) electroreduction kinetics in iron-anode electrocoagulation systems using mechanistic and data-driven approaches
abstract: Chromium(VI) reduction kinetics during iron-anode EC were modelled using two approaches: a mechanistic model coupling Faradaic Fe²⁺ generation with Cr(VI) reduction stoichiometry, and a feed-forward artificial neural network (ANN) trained on 180 experimental runs. The mechanistic model fitted well at pH 5–7 (RMSE 2.1 mg/L Cr(VI)) but diverged at pH above 8, where Cr(VI)–Fe(II) reaction rates are suppressed. The ANN (three-layer, 12 hidden neurons) achieved RMSE of 1.3 mg/L across the full pH range. Sensitivity analysis of the ANN confirmed current density and pH as the two most influential variables, consistent with the mechanistic model. Both approaches were validated against an independent dataset from a continuous-flow pilot reactor. The study suggests that a hybrid mechanistic–ANN model could guide real-time control of EC reactors in SME settings.

title: Compact modular EC–EO reactor design for mobile rinsewater treatment at electroplating SMEs: laboratory prototype evaluation
abstract: A compact modular reactor combining an EC stage (iron bipolar electrodes, 8 L working volume) and an EO stage (BDD anodes, 5 L working volume) was designed, fabricated, and evaluated at laboratory scale. The design targets mobile deployment, allowing a single trailer-mounted unit to serve multiple SMEs on a scheduled rotation. Performance was assessed for three representative rinsewater compositions: Zn–CN, Ni–SO₄, and Cr(VI)–SO₄. All three streams were treated to below Serbian Regulation 67/2023 discharge limits in a single pass at throughputs of 20–40 L/h. Footprint is 1.8 × 0.6 × 1.2 m. Automated PLC-based control with pH and conductivity feedback reduced operator intervention to start-up and sludge removal. Projected capital cost for a full-scale 200 L/h unit is estimated at 28 000 EUR based on component quotations. Remaining challenges include automated sludge dewatering integration.

title: Recovery of copper from electrocoagulation sludge of copper–cyanide plating rinsewater by selective leaching
abstract: Sludge produced during EC treatment of copper–cyanide plating rinsewater (Cu 80–300 mg/L, CN⁻ 50–200 mg/L) was subjected to selective acid and ammoniacal leaching to evaluate copper recovery potential. Sulphuric acid leaching (0.5 M H₂SO₄, 60 min, 50 °C) dissolved 93% of Cu from dried sludge while co-dissolving 41% of Fe, necessitating a solvent extraction step with LIX 84-I for Cu/Fe separation. Ammoniacal leaching (3 M NH₃/NH₄⁺, pH 10, 60 min) recovered 87% of Cu with Fe co-dissolution below 2%, but required ammonia stripping from the spent leachate. Electrodeposition from the purified ammoniacal leachate at 200 A/m² yielded copper cathode of 99.1% purity. The recovered copper mass from 1 m³ of treated rinsewater averaged 0.18 kg. Results indicate a potential secondary-resource value that could partially offset EC operating costs.

title: Life cycle assessment of electrocoagulation versus chemical precipitation for nickel removal from electroplating rinsewater at the SME scale
abstract: A gate-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) was performed comparing electrocoagulation with lime-based chemical precipitation for Ni removal from electroplating rinsewater at a modelled 5 m³/day SME facility. Functional unit was 1 m³ of influent treated to Serbian discharge limit of 1 mg/L Ni. Inventory data for the EC scenario were drawn from the Vojvodina field survey published in 2021; chemical precipitation data were collected from three SMEs using this approach. EC showed lower global warming potential (1.8 vs. 3.2 kg CO₂-eq/m³) primarily because of avoided lime production and reduced sludge mass. However, EC had higher freshwater ecotoxicity impact due to electrode manufacturing. Sludge disposal contributed 35–48% of total impact in both scenarios. Uncertainty analysis using Monte Carlo simulation (1000 iterations) showed statistically significant differences in four of eight impact categories. The study supports EC as the preferable option under current Serbian energy and material prices.

title: Regulatory Compliance Audit Methodology for Environmental Aspects in Polymer Film Manufacturing: Application to a Serbian Production Site
abstract: Environmental compliance auditing in manufacturing requires a structured mapping of applicable legal obligations to measurable site conditions. This paper describes a step-by-step audit methodology developed and applied at a bi-axially oriented polypropylene film plant in Serbia with an annual output of approximately 18,000 tonnes. The methodology identifies legal requirements at four tiers: EU directives transposed into Serbian law, national environmental statutes, autonomous provincial regulations of Vojvodina, and facility-specific permit conditions. For each tier, measurable compliance indicators were defined and linked to monitoring data collected over a two-year period. The audit identified twelve non-conformances, of which four were classified as significant: two concerning VOC emissions from solvent-based coating units, one concerning stormwater runoff monitoring frequency, and one concerning hazardous waste labelling. Corrective action plans with target timescales were developed for each finding. The methodology is presented as a replicable framework applicable to other polymer processing sectors.

title: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing with Slip and Guess Parameters on Secondary-School Mathematics Data
abstract: This paper revisits the classic Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) model and investigates the effect of per-skill versus per-student estimation of slip and guess parameters on a dataset of 4,200 secondary-school students interacting with a mathematics practice platform over one academic year. The dataset comprised approximately 380,000 response records covering 47 distinct knowledge components. We fitted BKT models using expectation-maximisation and compared predictive accuracy under three parameterisation strategies. Per-skill parameterisation yielded an AUC of 0.71, while a mixed per-student model reached 0.74 on held-out data. We also analysed the correlation between estimated knowledge gain rates and teacher-assigned end-of-term grades, finding a Pearson r of 0.61. The study confirms known limitations of BKT regarding temporal spacing of practice sessions and suggests that richer contextual features are needed to improve short-term prediction. The results serve as a reproducible baseline for subsequent deep-learning knowledge tracing experiments conducted by the authors.

title: Comparing Deep Knowledge Tracing Architectures on a Regional Language-Learning Corpus
abstract: Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) models based on recurrent neural networks have shown strong performance on English-language datasets, but their applicability to smaller, less standardised corpora remains underexplored. We assembled a corpus from a Serbian-language online learning platform covering vocabulary and grammar exercises for adult learners (n=1,850 users, 210,000 interaction records, 63 skills). We trained and evaluated standard LSTM-based DKT, a bidirectional variant, and a memory-augmented network (DKVMN) under five-fold cross-validation. DKVMN achieved the best AUC of 0.782 compared to 0.761 for standard DKT and 0.769 for the bidirectional model. We find that sequence length and the proportion of cold-start users substantially affect model ranking. Hyperparameter sensitivity is documented in detail, and all code and anonymised data splits are released under an open licence. The paper discusses practical implications for deploying knowledge tracing in low-resource educational settings.

title: A Collaborative Filtering Baseline Suite for Learning Resource Recommendation in Higher Education
abstract: Recommendation of learning materials in higher education is often benchmarked against general-purpose collaborative filtering methods without careful attention to temporal leakage or cold-start conditions. This book chapter presents a reproducible baseline suite comprising user-based CF, item-based CF, matrix factorisation (SVD and NMF), and a popularity baseline, evaluated on interaction logs from a university learning management system (6,400 students, 14 courses, approximately 95,000 resource access events recorded over two academic years). Evaluation follows a strict time-based split to prevent future information leaking into training. Results show that NMF with 40 latent factors achieves NDCG@10 of 0.231, outperforming user-based CF (0.198) and item-based CF (0.204). We discuss the importance of distinguishing between mandatory and optional resource access in constructing implicit feedback signals, and provide practical guidance for researchers who wish to use LMS logs as a benchmark source. All preprocessing scripts are made available.

title: Incorporating Forgetting Curves into Transformer-Based Knowledge Tracing
abstract: Standard attention-based knowledge tracing models treat all past interactions as equally retrievable, which contradicts well-established memory consolidation findings. We propose a forgetting-aware self-attention mechanism that weights historical interactions according to an exponential decay function parameterised per knowledge component. The model is evaluated on three public benchmark datasets (ASSISTments 2009, Junyi Academy, and EdNet-KT1) as well as a proprietary corpus from a regional STEM tutoring platform (2,300 students, 48 skills). On ASSISTments 2009, the forgetting-aware model achieves AUC 0.821 versus 0.808 for a vanilla transformer baseline trained under identical conditions. On the regional STEM corpus, the improvement is smaller (0.793 vs. 0.787), likely due to the shorter average session gaps. Ablation experiments isolate the contribution of the decay function from other architectural choices. We also report calibration error (ECE) alongside AUC, arguing that well-calibrated confidence estimates are important for downstream mastery gating decisions in tutoring systems.

title: Offline Policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning-Based Learning Path Recommenders
abstract: Learning path recommendation is framed naturally as a sequential decision problem, yet online reinforcement learning evaluation in educational settings raises ethical and logistical concerns. This paper examines three offline policy evaluation (OPE) methods—inverse propensity scoring (IPS), doubly robust estimation, and fitted Q-evaluation—applied to a logged dataset from a mathematics adaptive learning platform (8,100 learners, 92,000 sessions). The logging policy was a rule-based system used in production. We estimate the value of two candidate RL policies: a Q-network trained on the same logs and a policy derived from a knowledge-tracing reward signal. Doubly robust estimation yields the narrowest confidence intervals and most stable rankings across bootstrap samples. The paper provides a practical guide for applying OPE in educational contexts, including discussion of distributional shift issues that arise when learner populations change across academic years. Limitations regarding unmeasured confounders are discussed explicitly.

title: Reward Shaping Strategies for Reinforcement Learning Tutors Targeting Long-Term Retention
abstract: Reinforcement learning tutors optimised for immediate correctness can implicitly encourage cramming behaviour, sacrificing long-term retention. We study four reward shaping strategies—immediate correctness, delayed post-test score, spaced-repetition bonus, and a composite reward—within a simulated student environment calibrated from real interaction logs. The simulator models forgetting using a two-parameter retention function estimated from data collected across three months of use of a vocabulary tutoring application (1,200 adult learners). Policies trained with the composite reward achieve 12.4% higher simulated retention at a 14-day lag compared to policies trained on immediate correctness alone, without requiring more practice items. We conduct sensitivity analyses on simulator parameters to assess how much the conclusions depend on the accuracy of the retention model. The paper also contributes a publicly released simulation framework written in Python that other researchers can extend with alternative student models.

title: Combining Knowledge Tracing and Collaborative Filtering for Cold-Start Exercise Recommendation
abstract: New exercises added to an adaptive platform lack interaction history, creating a cold-start problem for collaborative filtering-based recommenders. We address this by using a knowledge tracing model to generate pseudo-interaction vectors for new exercises based on their tagged knowledge components, then incorporating these vectors into a matrix factorisation pipeline. Experiments are conducted on a dataset from a regional online STEM preparation service (4,700 registered students, 310 exercises, of which 80 were designated cold-start items). The hybrid approach achieves Hit Rate@5 of 0.44 on cold-start exercises versus 0.29 for content-based filtering and 0.21 for random recommendation. On warm exercises, performance is comparable to standard NMF. We also report results segmented by student proficiency level, showing that low-proficiency students benefit most from the hybrid approach. Sensitivity to the quality of knowledge component tagging is examined through a manual tag-corruption experiment.

title: Evaluating Fairness Metrics in Knowledge Tracing Models Across Demographic Groups
abstract: Knowledge tracing models are increasingly used to trigger pedagogical interventions, yet their differential accuracy across demographic groups has received limited systematic attention. Using a dataset from a national mathematics competition preparation platform (11,200 students with self-reported gender and regional school category), we evaluate five knowledge tracing models—BKT, DKT, DKVMN, SAKT, and AKT—on per-group AUC, calibration error, and false mastery rate. We find that all five models show higher false mastery rates for students from rural school categories (up to 6.1 percentage points above the overall mean), with the gap being smallest for AKT. Gender differences in AUC are modest (under 1.5 percentage points) but calibration differences are more pronounced. We discuss potential sources of these disparities including uneven data density and systematic differences in item exposure. The paper proposes a reporting checklist for fairness-aware evaluation of knowledge tracing systems.

title: Towards Real-Time Adaptive Hint Delivery Using Multi-Armed Bandits in a Web-Based Tutoring Environment
abstract: Hints in tutoring systems are often delivered based on fixed rules or teacher intuition rather than empirical optimisation. We frame hint timing and type selection as a contextual multi-armed bandit problem and deploy a LinUCB agent within a web-based mathematics tutoring environment used by secondary-school students. A four-week in-classroom experiment involved 340 students from five schools in Vojvodina, randomised at the class level to bandit, fixed-schedule hint, and no-hint conditions. The bandit condition yielded a statistically significant improvement in post-test scores over the fixed-schedule condition (Cohen's d = 0.31, p = 0.018) and over no-hint (d = 0.47, p < 0.001). Engagement metrics (session length, voluntary return rate) also favoured the bandit condition. We describe the deployment architecture, discuss teacher acceptance challenges encountered during the study, and identify confounds arising from class-level randomisation.

title: Benchmarking Recurrent and Attention-Based Architectures for Short Industrial Time-Series Under Data Scarcity
abstract: Recurrent neural networks and transformer-based models have demonstrated strong performance on long, richly labelled time series, but their behaviour on short sequences with fewer than 200 training examples is less well characterised. This benchmark study evaluates LSTM, GRU, temporal convolutional networks, and a lightweight transformer variant across eight industrial classification tasks with training set sizes ranging from 45 to 190 labelled sequences. Each architecture is trained with five random seeds, and performance is reported as mean and standard deviation of macro-F1. The temporal convolutional network shows the most stable performance (standard deviation across seeds consistently below 2.1 F1 points) and achieves the highest average macro-F1 of 0.71 at training sizes below 100. Transformer models exhibit high variance at small sizes (standard deviation up to 6.8 F1 points) but improve rapidly as training data increase beyond 150 examples. Practical guidance on architecture selection as a function of dataset size is summarised in a decision table.

title: Factor structure of a newly constructed verbal reasoning battery in a Serbian undergraduate sample
abstract: This study examined the internal structure of the Verbal Reasoning Battery for Selection (VRBS), a 60-item instrument developed for use in personnel selection in Serbian-speaking contexts. A sample of 412 undergraduate students from three universities in Vojvodina completed the battery under controlled conditions. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) with oblimin rotation and parallel analysis indicated a two-factor solution distinguishing vocabulary-based items from inferential reasoning items, together accounting for 41% of common variance. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) on a hold-out subsample (n = 198) yielded acceptable fit (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.057). Internal consistency estimates (Cronbach's α) were 0.81 and 0.78 for the two subscales. Item difficulty indices ranged from 0.31 to 0.72, indicating moderate spread appropriate for selection contexts. The findings support a two-dimensional interpretation of verbal reasoning in this population and provide a basis for subsequent criterion validity studies with the VRBS.

title: Criterion-related validity of a general cognitive ability composite in predicting supervisory ratings in manufacturing
abstract: The study investigated the predictive validity of a composite general cognitive ability (GCA) score, derived from the VRBS and a numerical reasoning subtest, against supervisory performance ratings collected six months after hiring in three manufacturing plants in Vojvodina. The sample comprised 186 newly hired production workers (mean age 28.4, SD = 5.1; 61% male). Supervisory ratings on a five-dimension behavioural anchored scale served as the criterion. Corrected for range restriction and criterion unreliability, the GCA composite showed a validity coefficient of r = 0.34 (95% CI: 0.21–0.46) against an overall performance composite. Incremental validity of a conscientiousness scale over GCA was modest (ΔR² = 0.04, p = 0.09). The results are broadly consistent with meta-analytic estimates from Western European samples, suggesting reasonable transportability of the instruments to Serbian industrial contexts. Implications for local test norming are discussed.

title: Differential item functioning by gender in a numerical reasoning test used for bank teller selection
abstract: This study applied the Mantel–Haenszel procedure and logistic regression DIF detection to examine gender-related differential item functioning in a 40-item numerical reasoning test used operationally by a regional bank to screen applicants for teller positions. The analytic sample included 534 candidates (308 women, 226 men) who sat the test over two consecutive recruitment cycles. Eleven items were flagged for DIF at the Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold; of these, seven showed uniform DIF favouring male test-takers, four showed uniform DIF favouring female test-takers, and none showed non-uniform DIF. Effect sizes (ETS Δ) indicated that two items exceeded the C-category threshold, warranting removal or revision. After purification and removal of the two high-DIF items, the gender gap in total scores was reduced by approximately 0.12 standard deviations. Practical recommendations for periodic DIF monitoring in operational selection testing are offered.

title: Adapting the Hexagonal Personality Inventory for occupational use in Serbia: translation, pilot testing, and preliminary structural validity
abstract: The paper describes the Serbian adaptation of the Hexagonal Personality Inventory (HPI-S), a 180-item instrument covering six broad personality dimensions relevant to work behaviour. Following a committee translation–back-translation procedure with a bilingual panel of five psychologists, cognitive interviews were conducted with 24 working adults to assess item comprehensibility. A pilot sample of 310 employed adults from service and industrial sectors completed the inventory alongside the Eysenck Personality Questionnaire Revised (EPQ-R) as a convergent marker. CFA of the six-factor structure showed marginal fit in the full pilot sample (CFI = 0.88, RMSEA = 0.063), prompting revision of 18 items showing high residual correlations or low factor loadings (< 0.30). Convergent correlations with EPQ-R Extraversion and Neuroticism scales were in the expected direction (r = 0.61 and –0.54, respectively). The revised 162-item version is recommended for further large-scale validation before operational deployment.

title: IRT-based item analysis of a situational judgment test for customer service roles
abstract: Situational judgment tests (SJTs) are increasingly used in selection but rarely subjected to item response theory (IRT) analysis. This study applied a two-parameter logistic (2PL) model to responses from 621 candidates who completed a 32-scenario SJT developed for customer service roles in a telecommunications company. Item fit was evaluated using S-X² statistics; 28 of 32 items showed acceptable fit. Discrimination parameters (a) ranged from 0.52 to 1.89 (M = 1.21), and difficulty parameters (b) ranged from –1.43 to 1.67, indicating reasonable coverage of the latent trait continuum. Items with low discrimination (a < 0.70) were identified as candidates for revision. Test information peaked at θ = –0.4, suggesting the test discriminates best among candidates slightly below average on the measured construct. The study also compared IRT-based and CTT-based item selection procedures, finding modest but consistent advantages for IRT-selected item sets in terms of information across the score range.

title: Incremental validity of a work sample test over cognitive ability and personality in predicting performance among IT technicians
abstract: This study examined whether a structured work sample test (WST) assessing hardware troubleshooting and network configuration tasks provided incremental criterion-related validity beyond a GCA composite and the Conscientiousness scale of the HPI-S in predicting six-month job performance ratings for IT support technicians. Participants were 143 IT technicians hired across eight technology companies in Novi Sad and Belgrade. Job performance was assessed using structured supervisor ratings on a seven-point scale covering technical accuracy, problem resolution speed, and client communication. In hierarchical regression, GCA explained 18% of performance variance; adding Conscientiousness raised R² to 0.23 (ΔR² = 0.05, p = 0.021); the WST score added a further ΔR² = 0.09 (p = 0.003), yielding a total R² of 0.32. The work sample's incremental contribution was consistent across male and female subgroups. These results support the practical utility of including work sample components in selection processes for technical roles despite the higher development cost.

title: Uniform and non-uniform DIF by educational level in a verbal analogies test used for managerial selection
abstract: The study investigated differential item functioning related to educational level (secondary vs. tertiary education) in a 36-item verbal analogies test deployed in managerial candidate screening. The sample comprised 718 candidates from 14 organisations across Serbia who sat the test as part of routine selection procedures between 2018 and 2021. DIF was examined using logistic regression allowing detection of both uniform and non-uniform DIF, with ability matching via the purified total score. At α = 0.01, nine items showed statistically significant DIF; five were uniform and four non-uniform. Effect sizes (pseudo-R² Δ > 0.035) indicated practical significance for three uniform and two non-uniform items. Items with large non-uniform DIF typically involved analogical relations drawn from academic domains, suggesting content-based explanations rather than measurement artefacts. After removing the five largest-effect items and re-estimating the scale, the educational-group mean difference decreased from 0.68 to 0.51 standard deviations. Implications for content blueprinting in test revision are discussed.

title: Construct validity of a brief dark triad measure in Serbian job applicant versus non-applicant samples
abstract: Dark triad traits—narcissism, Machiavellianism, and psychopathy—have attracted interest in personnel psychology, yet most validation evidence derives from student samples in Western European countries. This study examined the factor structure and construct validity of the Serbian adaptation of the Short Dark Triad Scale (SDT-SR, 27 items) in two samples: 298 job applicants undergoing formal selection for supervisory positions and 244 non-applicant adults recruited via workplace contacts. CFA supported a three-factor correlated model in both samples (CFI ≥ 0.91, RMSEA ≤ 0.068). Multi-group tests confirmed metric but not full scalar invariance, with three Machiavellianism items showing elevated intercepts in the applicant sample, consistent with socially desirable responding under evaluation conditions. Correlations with HPI-S Agreeableness and Conscientiousness were in the expected negative direction (–0.41 to –0.52) in the non-applicant group and were attenuated in the applicant group. The findings underscore the importance of context-specific validation for dark triad instruments used operationally.
venue: European Journal of Psychological Assessment

title: Cross-national measurement equivalence of a cognitive ability battery across Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia
abstract: This study assessed whether a three-subtest cognitive ability battery—verbal reasoning, numerical reasoning, and abstract reasoning—showed measurement equivalence across Serbian (n = 512), Croatian (n = 438), and Slovenian (n = 391) employed adult samples. Participants were recruited through partnering companies in each country as part of a regional validation project. Multi-group CFA with Mplus tested configural, metric, scalar, and strict invariance models. Configural and metric invariance held across all three countries. Scalar invariance was partially supported: four items (two verbal, two abstract) showed country-specific intercept deviations. After freeing these intercepts, partial scalar invariance was achieved (ΔCFI = –0.007). Latent mean comparisons using the partial scalar model indicated no significant between-country differences in verbal or numerical reasoning but a small Slovenian advantage on abstract reasoning (d = 0.19 vs. Serbian baseline). The results support cautious cross-national comparison of cognitive ability scores in multinational selection processes within the region.

title: Automated item generation for numerical reasoning tests: evaluating psychometric properties of algorithmically produced items
abstract: Automated item generation (AIG) offers a scalable approach to constructing large item pools for high-volume selection programmes. This preprint reports psychometric properties of 120 numerical reasoning items generated from six cognitive models using a rule-based AIG system developed collaboratively with a commercial test vendor. Items were field-tested in an online proctored environment with 890 candidates applying for administrative roles across three organisations in Serbia and one in North Macedonia. 2PL IRT calibration indicated that AIG-produced items had slightly lower mean discrimination (a = 0.98) compared to a matched set of expert-written items calibrated in an earlier study (a = 1.18), though the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.07). Item difficulty distributions were similar between AIG and expert-written sets. DIF analyses by gender found no items exceeding B-category thresholds. The findings suggest AIG can produce serviceable numerical reasoning items for selection use, though discrimination quality merits attention during item model specification.

title: Extending the standard knowledge-tracing model with slip and guess priors estimated from population response distributions
abstract: The standard Bayesian knowledge-tracing (BKT) model assumes fixed, hand-tuned slip and guess parameters, which often leads to local optima and poor generalisation across learner populations. This paper proposes a population-informed BKT variant in which slip and guess priors are estimated from aggregate response distributions of a held-out calibration cohort before individual-level EM updating. The approach was tested on interaction logs from a secondary-school algebra tutoring system used by 2,104 students over one academic year, comprising 1.3 million item-response events. Compared to standard BKT, the population-prior model reduced mean absolute error in next-item predictions by 11.4 % and improved AUC from 0.71 to 0.76. Cross-validation over five disjoint school cohorts confirmed stability. The paper also provides identifiability conditions under which the prior-informed model is distinguishable from the standard formulation.

title: Cynicism Toward Academic Work: Construct Definition and Initial Item Pool Development
abstract: Academic cynicism—defined here as a detached or dismissive orientation toward study tasks and institutional requirements—has received limited psychometric attention compared with exhaustion. This paper reports two sequential studies aimed at operationalising the construct. Study 1 involved 18 semi-structured interviews with undergraduate students identified via purposive sampling as academically disengaged, from which 74 candidate item statements were extracted through thematic analysis. Study 2 refined the pool to 28 items via expert review (n = 6 psychologists) and cognitive interviewing with 12 students. A preliminary dimensionality check with 188 participants suggested a two-component structure distinguishing task-level from institutional-level cynicism. Test–retest reliability over four weeks was r = .71 for the full 28-item version. The paper argues that cynicism should be treated as a separable dimension in burnout batteries rather than collapsed with disengagement or alienation measures.

title: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of adult attachment measures: Methodological lessons from South Slavic populations
abstract: This book chapter synthesises methodological decisions and lessons accumulated over a decade of adapting adult attachment self-report and interview measures for Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian populations. Topics covered include translation and back-translation procedures, sample selection biases inherent to university-based convenience samples, the distinction between linguistic and conceptual equivalence in attachment terminology, and the implications of partial scalar invariance for cross-national latent mean comparisons. Special attention is given to the under-studied question of whether Western attachment constructs transfer meaningfully to cultural contexts characterised by higher multigenerational co-residence and stronger normative expectations of family loyalty. The chapter argues that researchers in the region should routinely report measurement invariance tests and refrain from directly comparing raw scores across national samples without establishing equivalence. A practical checklist for researchers adapting attachment instruments in South Slavic contexts is appended.

title: Time-Delay Embedding Dimension and Its Effect on Persistent Homology of Experimental Time Series
abstract: Takens' embedding theorem guarantees topological conjugacy for sufficiently large embedding dimension m and delay τ, but the choice of m and τ in practice affects the topology of the reconstructed attractor. We study this sensitivity using persistence diagrams computed on point clouds reconstructed from four benchmark experimental datasets: a Duffing oscillator driven at 8 Hz, a Rössler circuit recording at 10 kHz, and two publicly archived electroencephalographic segments. For each dataset, m ranges from 2 to 10 and τ is set by the first minimum of the average mutual information. We track β₀, β₁, and β₂ as functions of m and measure pairwise Bottleneck distances between diagrams at successive embedding dimensions. Stabilisation of β₁ occurs consistently at m = 4 or m = 5 for the oscillator datasets, while the EEG data show no clear plateau, suggesting higher intrinsic dimension. The results quantify, for each dataset, the embedding dimension above which topological descriptors are reliable, offering a practical convergence criterion complementary to false-nearest-neighbour analysis.

title: Topological Signatures of Period-Doubling Cascades in One-Dimensional Maps
abstract: We examine the logistic map and the cubic map over their respective period-doubling routes to chaos, constructing at each parameter value a point cloud by iterating the map for 50 000 steps after a transient of 5 000. Sublevel-set filtrations on the empirical density function, estimated by a kernel method with bandwidth selected by cross-validation, are used to track zero-dimensional persistence. The birth and death times of zero-dimensional features encode period-doubling events: each period-doubling step introduces a new pair of prominent off-diagonal points whose persistence grows logarithmically with the number of doublings. A simple threshold rule on the maximum persistence value correctly identifies the onset of chaos for 38 of 40 test parameters drawn from a held-out grid. The total computation for the full parameter grid (1 200 values) takes 43 minutes on a four-core workstation. We propose a normalised persistence entropy as a single-valued chaos indicator and compare it against the Lyapunov exponent; correlation is 0.97 in the chaotic regime.

title: Stability of Persistence Diagrams Under Stochastic Perturbations of Vector Fields
abstract: The stability theorem for persistence diagrams guarantees Bottleneck distance bounds under perturbations of filter functions, but explicit bounds for stochastic perturbations of the underlying vector field have not been worked out in the literature. We add Gaussian white noise of amplitude σ_n ∈ {0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05} to the right-hand sides of six autonomous three-dimensional flows (Lorenz, Rössler, Chen, Lu, Halvorsen, and a newly constructed polynomial system) and compute the mean Bottleneck distance between noisy and clean persistence diagrams as a function of σ_n and integration time T. For T = 200 time units and σ_n ≤ 0.01, mean Bottleneck distance in dimension one is below 0.08 for all systems tested. A regression model with terms σ_n, T, and the maximal Lyapunov exponent explains 89% of variance in Bottleneck distance across 1 440 experiments. The results provide practical noise-tolerance guidelines for users of persistence-based attractor analysis.

title: Computational Topology Methods for Detecting Regime Changes in Fluid Convection Data
abstract: Rayleigh–Bénard convection exhibits qualitatively distinct flow regimes as the Rayleigh number Ra increases. We apply persistent homology to velocity field snapshots from a two-dimensional spectral-element simulation run at eleven Ra values between 10⁵ and 10⁸. At each Ra, 200 snapshots separated by one convective turnover time are converted to point clouds by subsampling the vorticity field on a regular grid of spacing 0.02 in non-dimensional units, yielding clouds of approximately 2 500 points. Persistence diagrams in dimensions 0–2 are computed with a Čech filtration approximated by alpha complexes. The transition from steady rolls to time-periodic flow near Ra ≈ 5×10⁶ is reflected in a discontinuous jump in median β₁ persistence from 0.11 to 0.34. Clustering the 2 200 diagrams by k-medoids with the Wasserstein W₁ metric recovers the eleven Ra classes with 93% accuracy using only the topological summary, without any physical domain knowledge. This chapter also reviews related work on topology-based flow classification from the past decade.

title: Mapper Graphs and Persistent Homology: A Combined Framework for Attractor Skeleton Extraction
abstract: The Mapper algorithm produces a graph-based summary of high-dimensional point clouds, while persistent homology captures multi-scale topological features. We propose a two-stage pipeline: Mapper is first applied to reduce point cloud dimensionality and expose the coarse shape of the attractor, and persistence diagrams are then computed on the Mapper-induced simplicial complex rather than on the raw cloud. Applied to point clouds of size 20 000 from the Lorenz-96 model at dimension N = 8 and forcing F ranging from 4 to 12, the pipeline reduces filtration computation time by a factor of 6.3 compared to computing Rips filtrations on the full cloud, with a mean Bottleneck distance of 0.07 relative to full-cloud diagrams. The skeleton graphs extracted by Mapper reveal a qualitative change from a single connected component to a multi-lobed structure as F increases past 8, consistent with known dynamical transitions. We provide an open-source Python implementation requiring only NumPy and SciPy dependencies.

title: Persistent Homology of Poincaré Sections for Periodically Forced Nonlinear Oscillators
abstract: Poincaré sections reduce continuous-time dynamics to discrete maps, and the topology of section point clouds can reveal bifurcation structure efficiently. We compute persistence diagrams on Poincaré sections of the forced van der Pol and Duffing oscillators at 625 forcing-amplitude and frequency pairs each, using 3 000 intersection points per parameter pair after transient removal. In the Duffing system, the appearance of a persistent β₁ generator with lifetime above 0.2 (in normalised attractor units) coincides with the onset of chaotic behaviour as detected by a positive maximal Lyapunov exponent in 97.4% of tested parameter pairs. For the van der Pol oscillator, the number of zero-dimensional generators at threshold ε = 0.1 tracks the period of the limit cycle exactly for periods up to 8 across all tested parameters. We also quantify the computational advantage of using sections versus full trajectories: mean filtration time drops by 71% while classification accuracy is maintained.

title: Wasserstein Gradient Flows on Spaces of Persistence Diagrams with Applications to Attractor Tracking
abstract: We formulate a gradient flow on the space of persistence diagrams equipped with the Wasserstein W₂ metric and study its convergence properties when the underlying dynamical system drifts slowly in parameter space. The theoretical framework treats the diagram at time t as a probability measure on the extended plane and derives a continuity equation for its evolution. For a slowly varying Rössler system with ω increasing linearly from 0.90 to 1.05 over a non-dimensional time of 500, numerical integration of the gradient flow predicts persistence diagrams with mean W₂ error of 0.031 relative to diagrams computed directly from simulation data at each intermediate parameter value. The framework is compared with naive linear interpolation of diagrams, which yields mean error 0.074. Existence and uniqueness of solutions to the continuity equation are established under a Lipschitz condition on the parameter-to-diagram map. This work provides a theoretical foundation for online topological tracking of slowly changing attractors.

title: Persistent Homology Barcodes for Gear-Fault Detection in Rotating Machinery Vibration Signals
abstract: We investigate whether persistent homology barcodes extracted from vibration time series can detect incipient gear faults in rotating machinery without requiring labelled training data from the specific machine type. Accelerometer signals are recorded at 25.6 kHz from a test rig with five gear configurations: healthy, and four artificial fault severities (notch depths 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm). Signals are segmented into windows of 4 096 samples. For each window, a three-dimensional attractor is reconstructed by time-delay embedding, and Vietoris–Rips barcodes in dimensions 0 and 1 are computed. The total persistence in dimension one increases monotonically with fault severity (Spearman ρ = 0.94, p < 0.001 across 840 windows). A threshold on total β₁ persistence distinguishes healthy from all faulty conditions with 88.3% accuracy in a leave-one-severity-out evaluation. The method requires no labelled examples from the target machine and is compared against short-time Fourier features and empirical mode decomposition, which achieve 91.2% and 86.7% respectively but require problem-specific tuning.

title: Zigzag Persistent Homology for Tracking Topological Changes Along Bifurcation Paths
abstract: Standard persistent homology is defined for a single filtration, making it difficult to compare topology across disconnected parameter slices. Zigzag persistence allows inclusions in both directions and is therefore suited to tracking topological features along one-dimensional paths through parameter space where the filtration changes non-monotonically. We apply zigzag persistence to a family of three-dimensional vector fields parametrised by a single scalar λ ∈ [0, 1], with point clouds of 3 000 points sampled at 50 evenly spaced λ values. The zigzag module in dimension one reveals the creation and destruction of topological loops with a resolution of Δλ = 0.02, capturing a Hopf bifurcation at λ ≈ 0.34 and a torus-birth event at λ ≈ 0.71. We compare the computational cost of the zigzag approach (mean 28 seconds for the full path on a single core) against pairwise diagram comparisons (mean 340 seconds for the same resolution). A detailed description of the implementation using a boundary-matrix reduction adapted for zigzag sequences is included.

title: Topological Data Analysis of Power-System Frequency Oscillations: A Case Study on Synthetic Grid Data
abstract: Low-frequency oscillations in power systems arise from interactions between synchronous generators and can threaten grid stability. We apply topological data analysis to synthetic time series of rotor-angle and bus-voltage measurements generated by a 14-bus test network simulated in a custom Python solver over 60-second windows sampled at 100 Hz, covering 96 distinct loading scenarios. Time-delay attractor reconstruction is performed on the angular frequency deviation signal, and Vietoris–Rips filtrations yield persistence diagrams in dimensions 0 and 1. The maximum β₁ persistence value exceeds 0.25 in 100% of scenarios with inter-area oscillation modes having damping ratios below 3%, while staying below 0.10 in 87% of well-damped scenarios. A receiver-operating-characteristic analysis gives area under the curve of 0.93 for this single topological feature. The study explores whether persistence-based indicators could serve as early-warning signals for oscillatory instability, as a complement to modal analysis methods, and discusses the practical requirements for real-time implementation.

title: Sheaf-Theoretic Persistence and Its Relation to Classical Persistent Homology for Attractor Data
abstract: Sheaf-theoretic persistence generalises classical persistence by assigning data structures to open sets of a topological space and tracking their consistency under restriction maps. We investigate whether the additional expressiveness of sheaf persistence translates into practical gains for attractor characterisation tasks. Three attractor families are studied: the Lorenz system at five parameter values, the Rössler system at four, and a nine-dimensional Lorenz-96 system. Cellular sheaves are constructed from the Mapper skeleton of each point cloud, with stalks given by local PCA components in ℝ³. Sheaf Laplacian spectra are compared against classical Betti numbers and persistence diagrams as features for a 13-class classification task. Random forest classifiers achieve 89.1% accuracy using sheaf-Laplacian features versus 85.4% using classical Betti curves, both computed from point clouds of 8 000 points. Computational overhead is a factor of 2.8 relative to classical persistence. We identify specific attractor geometries—thin toroidal structures and multi-scroll shapes—where sheaf methods provide the clearest advantage.

title: Error analysis for a finite element approximation of the periodic cell problem in linear elasticity
abstract: The accuracy of homogenisation computations depends critically on how well the unit-cell problem is solved numerically. We provide a systematic error analysis for standard conforming P1 and P2 finite element approximations of the linear elastic cell problem on a square unit cell with piecewise constant coefficients that are discontinuous across a curved interface. Two families of meshes are considered: body-fitted meshes that resolve the interface and Cartesian meshes that cut across it. For body-fitted P2 elements the H¹ error in the cell solution is O(h²), and the resulting error in the homogenised tensor entries is O(h⁴) due to the quadratic dependence of the effective tensor on the cell solution. For cut Cartesian meshes the H¹ error deteriorates to O(h^(1/2)) unless an interface correction is applied. We implement and test an extended finite element correction and recover near-optimal O(h²) convergence in the effective tensor. Results are verified on 5 interface geometries with exact solutions constructed by the method of manufactured solutions.

title: Viskoelastično ponašanje gusto punjenih suspenzija silika sfera pri malim amplitudama oscilatornog smicaja
abstract: Ispitivano je linearno viskoelastično ponašanje suspenzija monodisperznih silika čestica (prečnik 320 nm) u glicerol-vodenim rastvorima pri zapreminskim udelima čestica od 0,45 do 0,62. Oscilatorni reometrijski testovi izvedeni su u frekventnom opsegu 0,01–100 rad/s pri konstantnoj amplitudi deformacije od 0,5 %, čime je obezbeđen linearni odgovor. Utvrđeno je da se prelaz iz tečnog u staklasto ponašanje javlja pri zapreminskom udelu oko 0,58 za ispitivanu veličinu čestica. Modul skladištenja G' i modul gubitka G'' pokazuju karakteristično ukrštanje na frekventnoj skali koja opada sa porastom zapreminskog udela. Temperatura i jonska jačina rastvarača sistematski su varirane kako bi se razdvojili doprinos hidrodinamičkih i koloidnih interakcija. Rezultati su upoređeni sa teorijskim predviđanjima modifikovane mode-coupling teorije i ukazuju na konzistentnost sa predviđenim eksponentima relaksacije pri niskim frekvencijama.

title: Urinary hippuric acid and methylhippuric acid as biological indicators of combined toluene–xylene exposure in offset printers
abstract: End-of-shift urine samples were collected from 55 offset printing workers and 22 unexposed administrative controls in three printing facilities in Novi Sad. Hippuric acid and o-, m-, and p-methylhippuric acid concentrations were determined by HPLC-UV. Geometric mean hippuric acid excretion in exposed workers was 1.42 g/g creatinine compared with 0.31 g/g creatinine in controls. A significant positive correlation was found between personal toluene air concentration and urinary hippuric acid (Spearman r = 0.73, p < 0.001). At simultaneous xylene co-exposure, hippuric acid excretion was systematically higher than predicted from toluene air concentrations alone, suggesting competitive metabolic interaction at the CYP2E1 pathway. This finding supports the need for mixture-specific biological exposure indices rather than single-compound reference values. The study provides quantitative data to inform revision of national biological monitoring guidance for the printing sector.

title: Dermal absorption of 2-butanone oxime from single-component polyurethane coatings: an in vitro permeation study
abstract: 2-Butanone oxime (MEKO) is a skinning inhibitor widely used in alkyd and polyurethane coatings and has been classified as a probable human carcinogen. Dermal permeation of MEKO from a commercial single-component polyurethane coating formulation was measured using Franz diffusion cells with excised human abdominal skin (n = 6 donors). Receptor fluid was collected at 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 24 hours and analysed by GC-FID. Steady-state flux was reached at approximately 8 hours, with a mean permeability coefficient (Kp) of 1.7 × 10⁻³ cm/h. Estimated daily dermal uptake under realistic occupational application scenarios (hand and forearm exposure, 4 h contact) ranged from 12 to 28 µg/cm² per application event. These values indicate that dermal absorption can contribute a substantial fraction of total internal dose alongside inhalation, underscoring the need to include the dermal route in exposure assessment for MEKO in coating workers.

title: Development of a near-field/far-field model for solvent vapour distribution in a mechanically ventilated spray-painting cabin
abstract: A two-zone near-field/far-field mass-balance model was parameterised and validated for a full-scale automotive spray-painting cabin (volume 42 m³, nominal ventilation rate 18 air changes per hour) using tracer gas experiments with isopropanol. Tracer concentration was measured at 16 fixed points using photoionisation detectors logging at 10-second intervals during simulated spray cycles. The model reproduced measured near-field concentrations within ±20% in 78% of measurement intervals and within ±35% in 95% of intervals. Sensitivity analysis identified spray duration and near-field volume as the dominant model parameters. The validated model was then used to estimate 8-hour time-weighted-average exposures under three work-organisation scenarios varying spray duration and rest-break placement. Results suggest that redistributing spray activity to shorter, more frequent cycles with enforced breaks can reduce TWA inhalation exposure by up to 34% without changes to ventilation infrastructure.

title: Physiologically based toxicokinetic model for toluene–ethylbenzene–xylene mixture in humans: inter-individual variability and sensitivity analysis
abstract: A physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK) model for simultaneous exposure to toluene, ethylbenzene, and the three xylene isomers was constructed in MATLAB/Simulink. The model included lung, liver, richly perfused tissue, poorly perfused tissue, and fat compartments, with competitive CYP2E1 inhibition described by a Michaelis–Menten framework using literature kinetic constants. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) was used to propagate uncertainty in body weight, cardiac output, tissue volumes, and CYP2E1 Km and Vmax values drawn from population distributions. The coefficient of variation for predicted peak venous blood concentration across the population ranged from 38% (toluene) to 57% (p-xylene) under a standard 8-hour inhalation exposure scenario. Sensitivity analysis identified CYP2E1 Vmax and alveolar ventilation rate as the parameters accounting for more than 60% of variance in all model outputs. The model was calibrated against an independent published dataset of blood and urinary biomarker concentrations from 28 printing workers and achieved acceptable agreement (root mean squared prediction error < 20% for all analytes).

title: Skin wipe sampling for organic solvent residues on hands of automotive refinishing workers: sampling efficiency and field application
abstract: A skin wipe sampling protocol for ten organic solvents (acetone, isopropanol, n-butanol, ethyl acetate, n-butyl acetate, toluene, xylene isomers, styrene) was evaluated using a silicone membrane surrogate skin model. Ghost wipe and polyurethane foam wipe materials were compared at three concentration levels. Ghost wipes showed significantly higher recovery for hydrophilic solvents (mean 87% vs. 61%), while differences were smaller for hydrophobic solvents. The validated ghost wipe protocol was applied to 44 workers in six automotive refinishing workshops. Median contamination on dominant hand palms was highest for isopropanol (14.2 µg/cm²) and n-butanol (9.6 µg/cm²). Using the validated Kp values from a companion in vitro study, estimated dermal dose contributions reached up to 18% of inhalation dose for isopropanol and up to 11% for n-butanol under real workplace conditions. The protocol is proposed as a practical tool for combined route exposure assessments.

title: Estimated aggregate (inhalation plus dermal) internal dose of ethyl acetate in flexographic printers and its implications for risk characterisation
abstract: Ethyl acetate is among the most widely used solvents in flexographic printing yet risk characterisation typically considers only the inhalation route. This study combined simultaneous personal air sampling and skin wipe sampling on 29 flexographic printing workers over five consecutive work shifts. Inhalation dose was estimated from measured TWA concentrations and literature respiratory parameters. Dermal uptake was estimated by multiplying hand-surface contamination by a literature-derived skin permeability coefficient for ethyl acetate (Kp = 0.22 × 10⁻³ cm/h) and estimated contact duration. Aggregate daily internal dose estimated from the combined routes was on average 14% higher than from inhalation alone, with the dermal contribution reaching up to 29% in workers with the highest hand contamination. A deterministic risk quotient calculated against a health-based occupational exposure limit was below unity for all workers when using only inhalation data; inclusion of the dermal contribution moved two workers above the threshold. The findings support systematic inclusion of dermal sampling in routine exposure monitoring programmes for this sector.

title: Long-term trends in occupational VOC exposure in the Serbian printing industry: a comparison of measurements from 2005 to 2019
abstract: Three cross-sectional measurement campaigns conducted in 2005, 2012, and 2019 in a stratified sample of 28 printing facilities in Vojvodina were analysed to assess temporal trends in worker exposure to ten VOCs. All campaigns used identical personal sampling and TD-GC-MS analysis protocols. Geometric mean concentrations of toluene fell from 89 mg/m³ in 2005 to 34 mg/m³ in 2019, a decline of 62%. Similar reductions were observed for xylene isomers and ethylbenzene. By contrast, geometric mean concentrations of isopropanol and acetone increased over the same period, consistent with a shift from aromatic-solvent-based inks to alcohol-based formulations. Despite these substitutions, the proportion of workers with combined VOC exposure exceeding 80% of the occupational exposure limit sum (ΣVOC/OEL) remained at approximately 18–22% across all three campaigns. The data suggest that solvent substitution has reduced hazard but not necessarily risk at the level of individual workers in smaller facilities.

title: Incorporation of dermal uptake into a PBTK model for isopropanol: model structure, parameterisation, and validation in coating workers
abstract: An existing PBTK model for isopropanol inhalation was extended to include a dermal exposure compartment. The dermal submodel consists of a stratum corneum layer described by a lag-time equation and a viable epidermis compartment transferring solvent into the systemic circulation. Permeability parameters were derived from published in vitro data and adjusted using Bayesian parameter estimation against blood acetone data from an in-chamber human volunteer study (8 subjects, ethics approved). The extended model was then validated against an independent dataset of end-of-shift blood isopropanol and acetone concentrations from 19 automotive coating workers for whom simultaneous inhalation and dermal exposure measurements were available. The dermal-inclusive model showed 23% lower residuals compared with the inhalation-only model. Scenario analysis indicated that workers performing manual wipe-cleaning tasks could receive up to 40% of their total absorbed dose via the dermal route, a finding with direct implications for biological monitoring interpretation.

title: Occupational exposure to UV-curable ink photoinitiators in digital flatbed printing: air and skin measurements
abstract: UV-curable inks contain photoinitiators such as benzophenone, 1-hydroxycyclohexyl phenyl ketone (HCPK), and 2-methyl-1-[4-(methylthio)phenyl]-2-morpholino-propan-1-one (MMMP) that may volatilise or form aerosols during printing and UV-lamp curing. Stationary and personal air samples were collected in five digital flatbed printing facilities using XAD-2 sorbent, extracted with acetonitrile, and analysed by HPLC-DAD. Benzophenone was detected in all facilities at concentrations of 0.04–1.2 mg/m³. HCPK and MMMP were detected at lower concentrations (< 0.3 mg/m³) in two facilities. Skin wipe samples from forearms and neck of press operators showed benzophenone at median 3.4 µg/cm². Estimated inhalation and dermal exposures were compared with available occupational health guidance values; no guidance value was exceeded, but data gaps for MMMP are highlighted. This study provides baseline exposure data for an emerging exposure category not covered by existing sector-specific monitoring programmes.

title: Comparison of deterministic and probabilistic approaches to occupational risk assessment for VOC mixtures: a case study in a wood-furniture coating workshop
abstract: Risk assessment for multi-compound occupational exposures is typically conducted deterministically using the hazard index approach, which sums ratios of individual compound concentrations to their occupational exposure limits. This paper compares the deterministic approach with a probabilistic Monte Carlo approach for a six-compound VOC mixture (n-butyl acetate, ethylbenzene, p-xylene, m-xylene, o-xylene, and n-butanol) measured in a wood-furniture coating workshop over 40 shifts. The deterministic hazard index, calculated from 90th-percentile concentrations, was 1.28, indicating marginal exceedance. The probabilistic approach, using fitted lognormal distributions for each compound and a Gaussian copula to represent inter-compound correlation (Spearman ρ ranging from 0.41 to 0.79), yielded a 90th-percentile hazard index of 1.11 with a 95th percentile of 1.43. The deterministic estimate fell at approximately the 88th percentile of the probabilistic distribution, confirming conservative but broadly comparable behaviour. The implications of correlation structure for risk management decisions are discussed, and a practical workflow for small-to-medium enterprises is proposed.

title: Inhalation and dermal exposure to 1-methoxy-2-propanol and its acetate in waterborne coating applications: field measurements and PBTK-based dose reconstruction
abstract: 1-Methoxy-2-propanol (1M2P) and 1-methoxy-2-propyl acetate (1M2PA) are glycol ether solvents increasingly used in waterborne industrial coatings as substitutes for aromatic hydrocarbons. Personal inhalation exposure and hand-skin contamination were measured concurrently across 22 shifts in a metal-parts coating facility in Novi Sad. Geometric mean inhalation exposure was 43 mg/m³ for 1M2P and 18 mg/m³ for 1M2PA. Hand contamination median was 8.1 µg/cm² and 3.4 µg/cm² respectively. An existing single-compound PBTK model for 1M2P was adapted to include 1M2PA hydrolysis as an input pathway; model predictions were compared with end-of-shift urinary propylene glycol monomethyl ether concentrations measured in 22 workers. Inclusion of the dermal route improved model–biomonitoring agreement (mean absolute error reduced from 31% to 17%). The study demonstrates the practical utility of PBTK-based dose reconstruction for quantifying combined exposure routes with waterborne solvent systems.
