title: Worker exposure variability and determinants in solvent-based wood staining: an application of mixed-effects modelling to repeated personal measurements
abstract: Understanding the sources of exposure variability is essential for designing effective monitoring strategies. This study used a mixed-effects model to decompose inhalation exposure variability for five solvents (white spirit aliphatic fraction, d-limonene, isobutanol, n-butanol, and 2-butoxyethanol) in a wood-staining workshop employing 18 workers measured on three occasions each. Variance components analysis showed that between-worker variance accounted for 42–61% of total log-scale variance depending on compound, day-to-day within-worker variability accounted for 28–38%, and residual within-day variability for 10–18%. Determinants investigated included workstation type, task duration, product used, and local exhaust ventilation status. Use of local exhaust ventilation was associated with a 48% reduction in geometric mean concentration for d-limonene (95% CI: 29–62%) but had a weaker and non-significant effect on white spirit aliphatics. Minimum adequate monitoring strategies derived from the variance estimates are compared with current Serbian and European monitoring guidance.

title: Coupling a RANS thermal model with the physiological strain index: a case study in a glass-melting plant
abstract: The physiological strain index (PSI) combines core body temperature and heart rate into a 0–10 scale and has been validated in field studies of heat-exposed workers. This paper describes a coupling procedure in which the PSI is computed spatially by post-processing RANS CFD output fields—air temperature, mean radiant temperature, air velocity—together with the task-specific metabolic rate and measured clothing insulation value. The procedure was applied to a flat-glass melting plant with a production rate of 400 tonnes per day. Furnace crown temperatures reached 1 550 °C and ambient air at machine-room floor level averaged 36 °C during summer. PSI maps were generated for three representative workstations and compared with PSI values derived from 8-hour field monitoring of core temperature (ingestible telemetry capsule) and heart rate in 11 workers. Spatial PSI predictions agreed with measured end-of-shift PSI within ±0.7 units for 9 of 11 workers. The approach identifies spatially localised strain hotspots that point-measurement campaigns may miss, and can guide targeted ventilation modifications without requiring full physiological monitoring campaigns.

title: Equivalent Circuit Parameter Identification for Electric Double-Layer Capacitors Using Pulse Discharge Tests
abstract: This paper presents a procedure for extracting the parameters of a three-branch equivalent circuit model for electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs) from controlled pulse discharge experiments. A 100 F EDLC cell was cycled at five different current rates between 5 A and 50 A, and terminal voltage transients were recorded at 10 kHz. A nonlinear least-squares fitting routine was applied to identify the series resistance, two RC branch time constants, and the voltage-dependent capacitance coefficient. The identified model was validated against an independent set of charge–discharge cycles not used during fitting, yielding a root-mean-square voltage error below 18 mV across all tested rates. The sensitivity of model accuracy to sampling frequency and current pulse duration was analysed systematically. Results indicate that the three-branch model adequately captures redistribution dynamics up to 200 s and that the series resistance exhibits a temperature dependence of approximately 0.6 mΩ/°C in the 10–40 °C range. The identified parameters are used as inputs to a power-split controller described in subsequent work.

title: Rule-Based Power-Split Strategy for a Supercapacitor–Lead-Acid Battery Hybrid in a Stand-Alone PV System
abstract: A rule-based energy management strategy is developed and experimentally evaluated for a hybrid storage unit comprising a 6 F supercapacitor module and a 100 Ah lead-acid battery bank connected to a 2 kWp photovoltaic array feeding a resistive–inductive load. The strategy allocates high-frequency load transients to the supercapacitor and low-frequency demand to the battery using a first-order low-pass filter with a tunable cut-off frequency. Four cut-off frequencies (0.01 Hz, 0.05 Hz, 0.1 Hz, and 0.5 Hz) were tested over a 14-day outdoor measurement campaign in summer conditions in Vojvodina. Battery current RMS values were reduced by 31–58% relative to a battery-only reference, and battery charge throughput per day decreased by 22% at the 0.05 Hz setting. The supercapacitor state of charge remained within a 20–80% window for over 94% of operating time. Energy efficiency of the combined system was 91.3%, compared with 88.6% for the reference.

title: Model Predictive Control for Power Splitting in a Supercapacitor–LiFePO4 Hybrid: Formulation and Laboratory Validation
abstract: A finite-horizon model predictive control (MPC) formulation is presented for the power management of a hybrid energy storage system consisting of a 600 F supercapacitor bank and a 40 Ah LiFePO4 battery pack connected through separate bidirectional DC–DC converters to a 48 V bus. The MPC minimises a cost function penalising battery current rate of change and deviation of supercapacitor state of charge from a reference trajectory, subject to converter current limits and storage voltage bounds, over a 30-second prediction horizon with a 1-second control step. Load profiles were generated by a programmable electronic load following measured industrial compressor duty cycles. Over 120 test cycles, peak battery current was reduced by 41% and RMS battery current by 27% compared with a low-pass filter baseline, at a computational overhead of 3.2 ms per control step on an embedded ARM Cortex-M7 processor. The sensitivity of performance to prediction horizon length and weighting matrix choice is discussed.

title: Supercapacitor–Battery Hybrid Energy Storage Systems for Off-Grid Applications
abstract: This book chapter surveys design considerations for supercapacitor–battery hybrid energy storage in off-grid contexts, covering component selection, converter topologies, control architectures, and sizing procedures. The chapter is organised around three representative application classes: remote telecommunications, agricultural machinery, and small island microgrids. For each class, the key load characteristics, reliability requirements, and dominant cost drivers are described. The chapter compares passive, semi-active, and fully active hybrid topologies in terms of component utilisation and efficiency, citing representative experimental results from the literature. A worked numerical example illustrates the sizing of a fully active hybrid for a 5 kW off-grid cabin load using the degradation-aware procedure described in earlier work by the authors. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current limitations in component standardisation and recommends areas where further experimental data are needed.

title: State-of-Charge Balancing in a Parallel Supercapacitor–Battery Configuration Without Dedicated Sensors
abstract: Passive parallel connection of supercapacitors and batteries simplifies converter count but creates uncontrolled current sharing that depends on instantaneous impedance differences. This paper analyses the transient sharing dynamics using an analytical model and proposes an observer-based scheme that estimates individual state of charge from terminal voltage and total bus current without current sensors on each branch. The observer uses an extended Kalman filter with the three-branch EDLC model and a Thevenin battery model, both parameterised at laboratory. Tests on a 200 F, 20 Ah passive parallel bench with injected load steps up to 60 A show that the observer tracks individual SOC with errors below 3.2% for the supercapacitor and 2.8% for the battery over a 2-hour mixed-profile test. A protection algorithm uses the estimated SOC values to activate a relay that limits deep battery discharge, reducing low-SOC excursions by 78% compared with an unprotected passive connection.

title: Frequency-Domain Analysis of Load Buffering Effectiveness in Supercapacitor–Battery Hybrids for Variable-Speed Compressor Drives
abstract: Variable-speed compressor drives present a load spectrum with energy concentrated at the fundamental switching frequency of the drive (typically 20–100 Hz mechanical cycles) and at lower frequencies corresponding to pressure regulation dynamics. This paper quantifies the load buffering effectiveness of a supercapacitor–battery hybrid using power spectral density analysis of battery current before and after hybrid insertion under different control bandwidths. A 3 kW compressor drive was operated under pressure-cycling conditions reproducing a refrigeration duty cycle on a test bench. Spectral analysis of battery current showed that a 600 F supercapacitor bank inserted with a cut-off frequency of 0.2 Hz reduces battery current spectral power in the 0.2–5 Hz band by 14 dB and in the 5–50 Hz band by more than 22 dB. The relationship between cut-off frequency and harmonic distortion factor of battery current is characterised, and a design guideline for selecting the cut-off frequency as a function of dominant load cycle frequency is derived.

title: Adaptive Low-Pass Filter Cut-Off Tuning for Hybrid Energy Storage Under Non-Stationary Load Statistics
abstract: Load profiles in off-grid systems often exhibit non-stationarity: the statistical properties change with season, occupancy, or production schedule. A fixed cut-off frequency in a low-pass filter power-split strategy may then be either too conservative or too aggressive at different times. This paper proposes an online adaptation scheme that estimates the dominant load cycle frequency from a 5-minute sliding window of load power data using a recursive autoregressive model of order 4, and adjusts the filter cut-off frequency every 5 minutes to maintain a target battery current harmonic distortion factor below a user-defined threshold. The scheme is tested in simulation using 12 months of 1-second load data recorded at a remote off-grid workshop in central Serbia. Compared with the best fixed cut-off frequency, the adaptive scheme reduces battery Ah throughput by 11.3% annually while maintaining identical loss-of-load performance. Computational requirements are compatible with a low-cost 32-bit microcontroller.

title: Second-Life Lithium-Ion Cells in Supercapacitor–Battery Hybrids: Capacity and Impedance Screening Protocol and Control Implications
abstract: Repurposing retired electric vehicle battery cells for stationary storage reduces costs but introduces cell-to-cell variability in capacity and internal resistance that affects hybrid sizing and control. This paper presents a screening protocol based on a 1C discharge capacity test and a 1 kHz AC impedance measurement to sort second-life 18650-format NMC cells into quality tiers. Sixty cells from three retired EV battery packs of the same chemistry but different provenance were characterised. Capacity spread within the full set was 1.1–2.0 Ah (nominal 2.1 Ah), and DC internal resistance ranged from 62 to 218 mΩ. Tier assignment criteria are derived from a sensitivity analysis showing how cell resistance variance affects battery current sharing in a parallel module. The paper then examines how the MPC power-split controller described in earlier work must be retuned when second-life cells are used: the penalty on battery current rate-of-change must increase by roughly 35% for the highest-resistance tier to achieve equivalent ageing protection.

title: Co-Sizing of Supercapacitor Bank and Diesel Generator Rated Power for Remote Off-Grid Sites Using Stochastic Dynamic Programming
abstract: Off-grid sites that cannot eliminate diesel generation entirely can still reduce fuel consumption and generator wear by combining a supercapacitor bank with a downsized generator. This preprint formulates co-sizing of the supercapacitor capacity and the generator rated power as a stochastic dynamic programming problem where the state is a pair (battery SOC, supercapacitor SOC) and the uncertainty is the renewable generation forecast error. A Markov chain model of forecast error is fitted to one year of measured solar irradiance and short-term forecast pairs for a location in Vojvodina. The resulting optimisation over a discretised state space of 80×40 nodes converges in under 4 minutes on a standard workstation. Compared with a rule-of-thumb design, the optimal co-sizing reduces annual fuel consumption by 19% and diesel start count by 44% for a representative 10 kW site, while holding loss-of-load probability below 0.1%. A parametric study shows that generator cost per kVA has a stronger influence on the optimal supercapacitor size than supercapacitor cost per farad.

title: Adaptive Spreading Factor Selection Using RSSI History and a Lightweight Decision Tree for Battery-Constrained LoRa Nodes
abstract: The standard ADR algorithm in LoRaWAN relies on the network server receiving at least 20 consecutive uplinks before adjusting the spreading factor, which is impractical for sensors transmitting infrequently. This paper describes an on-device decision tree trained on RSSI history from a 45-node deployment in Novi Sad collected over six months. The tree uses five features: last RSSI, RSSI variance over the last four frames, time of day, estimated battery voltage, and current SF. It was trained offline and compressed to a 2 kB lookup table deployable on Cortex-M0 class microcontrollers. In a six-week field evaluation, the algorithm reduced mean airtime per node by 23% compared with static SF10 and by 11% compared with standard ADR, while maintaining a packet delivery ratio above 96%. Mean current consumption per node decreased from 4.1 mA to 3.2 mA averaged over the evaluation period.

title: Switching loss reduction in a 400 V GaN DC–DC converter through synchronised adaptive gate drive voltage control
abstract: This paper describes a gate-driver circuit that adjusts the turn-on gate drive voltage Vgs_on between +4 V and +6 V in synchronisation with the measured load current to reduce total switching losses at partial load. At light load (20 % of rated), reducing Vgs_on from +6 V to +4.5 V decreased Eon by 1.1 µJ per event while maintaining dv/dt within acceptable EMI limits. A 100 MHz microcontroller implementing a proportional-integral current-to-voltage mapping updated Vgs_on every 10 switching cycles. The control circuit added 8 mW of quiescent overhead. In a 400 V / 48 V, 600 W, 300 kHz hard-switched full-bridge converter, total measured losses over a 10–100 % load sweep were reduced by 2.1 W on average compared to fixed +6 V drive, improving partial-load efficiency by up to 0.4 percentage points. Stability of the control loop under input voltage transients is analysed and experimentally verified.

title: Digital Pre-Distortion for RF Power Amplifiers: Architectures, Models and Practical Constraints
abstract: This chapter surveys the principal approaches to digital pre-distortion for broadband power amplifiers in modern wireless base stations. It covers memoryless polynomial correction, memory polynomial and generalised memory polynomial methods, Volterra series truncations, and machine-learning-based approaches that have appeared since 2015. For each class of model, the trade-off between coefficient count, extraction data volume, numerical conditioning, and achievable ACPR improvement is discussed. Practical implementation topics covered include observation receiver design, IQ imbalance and DC offset compensation, delay alignment, and coefficient update scheduling in time-division and frequency-division duplex systems. A unified notation is used throughout to allow direct comparison between model families. Numerical examples are drawn from published measurements on GaN and LDMOS devices in the 700 MHz–6 GHz range. The chapter concludes with a discussion of challenges introduced by carrier aggregation and 5G NR waveforms, including crest-factor reduction interaction with DPD.

title: Bilateral grip force asymmetry in recreational weightlifters: a cross-sectional descriptive study
abstract: This study examined the prevalence and magnitude of bilateral grip force asymmetry in 38 recreational Olympic-style weightlifters (27 men, 11 women; mean training age 2.4 ± 1.1 years) using a calibrated hydraulic dynamometer. Participants performed three maximal isometric grip trials per hand with 60-second rest intervals. An asymmetry index was calculated as the absolute percentage difference between dominant and non-dominant limb peak forces. Mean asymmetry was 9.3 ± 4.7%, with 42% of participants exceeding the 10% threshold commonly cited in rehabilitation literature. No significant correlation was found between training age and asymmetry magnitude (r = −0.12, p = 0.47). Women showed slightly higher mean asymmetry (11.1%) compared to men (8.7%), though the difference was not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Results suggest that bilateral grip force asymmetry is common in early-stage weightlifters and may warrant monitoring during technical skill development. Data were collected at the Faculty of Sport and Physical Education Biomechanics Laboratory.

title: Ground reaction force profiles during the first pull phase of the snatch in national-level competitors
abstract: Force platform data were collected from 14 national-level male weightlifters (body mass 77.4 ± 9.8 kg, competitive experience 5.1 ± 2.3 years) performing the snatch at 80%, 90%, and 100% of their one-repetition maximum. Two Kistler 9260AA3 force platforms were used synchronously at 1000 Hz to capture vertical and anterior–posterior ground reaction forces during the first pull. Peak vertical force during the first pull ranged from 1.84 to 2.31 times body weight and increased significantly with load (p < 0.001, η² = 0.61). Anterior–posterior impulse asymmetry between left and right platforms averaged 7.1 ± 3.4% at 100% 1RM, indicating consistent lateral loading bias at maximal effort. These lateral differences were correlated with self-reported dominant hand (r = 0.54, p = 0.04). Findings point to load-dependent intensification of lateral force bias that may relate to grip and upper-limb mechanics.

title: Upper-limb segment power contributions during the snatch pull: a multi-segment inverse dynamics approach
abstract: A multi-segment rigid-body model comprising the hand, forearm, upper arm, and shoulder girdle was applied to quantify segmental power contributions during the snatch pull in twelve competitive male weightlifters. Kinematic data from a Qualisys system (200 Hz) were combined with force platform measurements (1000 Hz) and processed using standard inverse dynamics. Elbow and wrist joint net powers were computed as the product of net joint moment and angular velocity. Results showed that the wrist joint contributed a mean peak power of 312 ± 89 W during the second pull, representing 18% of total upper-limb net power. Shoulder joint peak power (1,247 ± 204 W) dominated the upper-limb chain. Athletes with greater grip asymmetry index (>10%) showed larger wrist power asymmetry (r = 0.67, p = 0.018). The data support the hypothesis that grip asymmetry propagates through the kinetic chain and manifests as asymmetric wrist and elbow mechanics.

title: Inter-limb kinetic asymmetry during the jerk recovery phase: a conference report
abstract: This conference paper reports preliminary findings from ongoing research on ground reaction force asymmetry during the jerk recovery (catch) phase of the clean-and-jerk. Eight male lifters performed five maximal-effort clean-and-jerks on dual force platforms. Vertical ground reaction force was measured at the moment of foot contact after the split jerk. Peak vertical force asymmetry between front and rear foot averaged 23.4 ± 8.1% of total vertical force, with the front foot bearing the greater share in all but one participant. The rear foot showed higher rate of force development (RFD) in 87.5% of trials, possibly reflecting a compensatory braking strategy. A moderate negative correlation between split depth and asymmetry index (r = −0.48) suggests that deeper split positions are associated with more symmetric force distribution. Data collection is ongoing and full results will be submitted for journal review.

title: Sensitivity of wrist joint moment estimates to hand segment inertial parameter assumptions in weightlifting models
abstract: Monte Carlo simulations (n = 10,000 per condition) were used to quantify how uncertainty in hand segment inertial parameters propagates to wrist net joint moment estimates within a seven-segment upper-limb model applied to the snatch pull. Segment mass was varied ±15% and centre of mass position ±10% relative to reference values drawn from three published anthropometric data sets. Mean wrist peak moment across the simulated distributions differed by up to 22.4 N·m (approximately 18% of mean empirical peak moment) depending on the reference data set chosen. Sensitivity was highest during the second pull, when angular acceleration of the hand segment was greatest. Elbow and shoulder moments were substantially less sensitive, differing by less than 4% across data sets. Results suggest that conclusions about wrist-level mechanics in weightlifting studies should be interpreted cautiously until sport-specific hand segment data are available.

title: Grip strength symmetrisation training over eight weeks and its effects on barbell path deviation in junior weightlifters
abstract: A randomised controlled trial assigned 22 junior male weightlifters (age 17.4 ± 1.1 years) to either a grip symmetrisation group (GSG, n = 11) or a control group (CG, n = 11) for eight weeks. GSG participants completed supplementary unilateral grip and forearm exercises targeting the non-dominant limb three times per week. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included bilateral grip dynamometry, barbell trajectory capture (Qualisys, 200 Hz), and the asymmetry index for wrist joint power derived from inverse dynamics. GSG showed a significant reduction in grip asymmetry index (from 11.4 ± 3.2% to 6.8 ± 2.7%, p = 0.003) and a significant reduction in mediolateral barbell deviation during the snatch pull (from 3.1 ± 0.9 cm to 2.1 ± 0.7 cm, p = 0.011). CG showed no significant changes. Effect sizes (Cohen's d) for the grip asymmetry reduction were large (d = 1.48). Results provide preliminary evidence that targeted grip symmetrisation training reduces kinematic asymmetry in junior lifters.

title: Wrist kinematics during the catch phase of the snatch: flexion–extension and radioulnar deviation across load intensities
abstract: Wrist joint kinematics were examined in ten competitive male weightlifters performing snatch lifts at 70%, 80%, and 90% of 1RM using a Qualisys motion capture system with dedicated wrist marker clusters. Flexion–extension and radioulnar deviation were computed through a joint coordinate system approach. Peak wrist extension at catch ranged from 62° to 81° across participants and did not differ significantly across load intensities (F(2,18) = 1.74, p = 0.20). However, peak radioulnar deviation at catch increased significantly with load (p = 0.002, η² = 0.44), reaching 14.3 ± 4.1° ulnar deviation at 90% 1RM compared to 9.7 ± 3.2° at 70% 1RM. Dominant-hand wrist showed marginally greater ulnar deviation than non-dominant hand (2.3° on average, p = 0.041). Load-dependent increases in ulnar deviation may have implications for wrist injury risk and warrant prospective investigation.

title: Instrumented barbell collar for real-time lateral force differential measurement: design, calibration, and field validation
abstract: This paper describes the design and validation of an instrumented barbell collar prototype intended to estimate lateral force differential between the left and right hands during weightlifting training. Four miniaturised strain gauge bridges were embedded within a machined aluminium collar body to sense axial and transverse forces transmitted by the knurled barbell shaft. The device communicates wirelessly at 200 Hz via a Bluetooth Low Energy module to a custom receiver application. Calibration was performed against a reference load cell across forces of 0–600 N in five orientations. Mean calibration error was 2.1% of applied load. Field validation against force platform-derived lateral asymmetry indices in nine trained lifters showed a Pearson correlation of r = 0.83 (p < 0.001) and a mean absolute error of 4.3 N. The prototype provides a portable, low-cost alternative to laboratory force platforms for monitoring lateral loading asymmetry in training environments.

title: Sex differences in sweat rate and sodium loss during a 60 km trail race: a matched-sample analysis
abstract: Research on sex-based differences in thermoregulatory responses during ultra-endurance running remains limited, particularly under field conditions. This study matched 14 female and 14 male recreational ultra-trail runners by running pace and body surface area and measured whole-body sweat rate and sweat sodium loss during a 60 km Fruška Gora race in similar environmental conditions to earlier studies (28–30 °C, relative humidity 70–74%). Female runners demonstrated a significantly lower absolute sweat rate (0.84 ± 0.19 L·h⁻¹) compared to males (1.15 ± 0.24 L·h⁻¹; p < 0.01), but when expressed relative to body surface area, the difference was attenuated and non-significant (p = 0.12). Mean sweat [Na⁺] did not differ significantly between sexes (46 ± 15 vs 50 ± 17 mmol·L⁻¹; p = 0.43). Total sodium loss was lower in females owing primarily to the lower absolute sweat volume. These findings suggest that sex-specific hydration guidelines should account for absolute sweat volumes rather than assuming different sodium replacement needs per unit sweat.

title: Point mutations at Pro197 and Trp574 in the ALS gene of imazethapyr-resistant Amaranthus retroflexus biotypes from Serbia
abstract: ALS gene fragments spanning the conserved domains A and B were amplified by PCR and sequenced from 47 A. retroflexus individuals collected from eight field populations with elevated GR50 values for imazethapyr. Sequencing revealed two amino acid substitutions: Pro197Thr in 31 individuals and Trp574Leu in 9 individuals. Three individuals carried both substitutions. Six individuals showed no detectable target-site mutation despite confirmed resistance at the whole-plant level, suggesting that additional mechanisms may operate in those plants. Susceptible reference plants carried only wild-type codons at both positions. Allele frequencies at position 197 were highest in populations from the Bačka region, consistent with intensive sunflower cultivation and repeated ALS inhibitor use. The data provide the first direct molecular evidence of ALS target-site mutations in Serbian A. retroflexus and set the context for parallel investigation of non-target-site mechanisms.

title: Metabolic detoxification as a component of imazethapyr resistance in mutation-negative Amaranthus retroflexus plants: cytochrome P450 inhibitor studies
abstract: Six A. retroflexus individuals without target-site ALS mutations but with resistance factors above 12 were subjected to in vivo inhibition of cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs) using piperonyl butoxide (PBO) applied 1 h before imazethapyr treatment. Co-application of PBO at 4 g a.i. L−1 reduced the GR50 for imazethapyr by 6.8- to 14.2-fold compared with imazethapyr alone, restoring near-susceptible responses in five of the six plants. Malathion co-treatment had a smaller but significant effect, indicating a possible contribution from glutathione S-transferase activity. Radiolabelled 14C-imazethapyr metabolism studies in leaf disc assays showed faster conversion to polar metabolites in resistant plants relative to susceptible controls at 24 h after treatment (47 ± 6% versus 11 ± 3% radioactivity in the polar fraction). These results confirm functional CYP-mediated metabolism as a genuine non-target-site resistance mechanism in Serbian A. retroflexus.

title: Herbicide resistance in Vojvodina weeds: a survey of Amaranthus and Chenopodium biotypes from 2014 to 2016
abstract: A systematic field survey was conducted across 64 arable fields in the Bačka and Banat subregions of Vojvodina to assess the prevalence of herbicide resistance in the two most common broadleaf weeds, Amaranthus retroflexus and Chenopodium album. Seed families collected from individual maternal plants were evaluated in standard greenhouse bioassays against ALS inhibitors (imazethapyr, foramsulfuron), triazines (atrazine), and PPO inhibitors (lactofen). Among 64 A. retroflexus populations, 39% showed confirmed resistance to at least one ALS inhibitor and 12% showed triazine resistance. C. album populations showed lower overall resistance frequencies: 18% to ALS inhibitors and 29% to atrazines. Co-occurrence of ALS and triazine resistance within the same population was observed in 7% of A. retroflexus populations. The survey provides an updated regional resistance map and identifies fields where herbicide programme rotation is most urgently needed, and forms the empirical basis for mechanistic follow-up studies.

title: PsbA gene mutations conferring triazine resistance in Chenopodium album from maize fields of Vojvodina
abstract: Forty-two C. album plants sampled from maize fields with a history of atrazine use were tested for triazine resistance by measuring chlorophyll fluorescence inhibition (Fv/Fm) after atrazine treatment and confirmed using whole-plant bioassays. The psbA gene encoding the D1 protein of photosystem II was amplified and sequenced. A Ser264Gly substitution was found in 28 of 42 plants, all of which displayed reduced susceptibility in fluorescence assays (I50 > 8.5 µM versus 0.3 µM in susceptible controls). The mutation was maternally inherited, as confirmed by crossing experiments with susceptible males. In plants without the mutation but with elevated I50 values, no evidence of altered pigment composition or altered chloroplast ultrastructure was detected by transmission electron microscopy, and their resistance origin remains unclear. The Ser264Gly substitution is thus the principal triazine resistance mechanism in this C. album sample, consistent with findings from other European countries.

title: Constitutive overexpression of CYP81A-type genes in metabolically resistant Amaranthus retroflexus: transcript abundance and correlation with resistance level
abstract: RNA was extracted from leaf tissue of 18 A. retroflexus plants spanning a range of resistance factors (1.4–18.6) to imazethapyr, with and without confirmed ALS target-site mutations. Quantitative RT-PCR was performed using primers designed for CYP81A-type cytochrome P450 sequences identified by BLAST alignment against publicly available Amaranthus transcriptome assemblies. Normalisation was carried out against three reference genes (EF-1α, GAPDH, UBQ10) using the geometric mean method. Plants with resistance factors above 8 and no target-site mutation showed 4.8- to 11.3-fold higher CYP81A-like transcript levels compared with the susceptible reference, while plants with target-site mutations showed only 1.0- to 2.1-fold differences. A Spearman correlation of 0.71 (p < 0.001) was found between CYP81A-like transcript abundance and resistance factor across mutation-negative plants. These data support constitutive upregulation of CYP81A-type genes as a primary driver of metabolic resistance in this weed.

title: Cross-resistance profiles in PPO inhibitor-treated Amaranthus retroflexus from soybean fields: whole-plant and enzymatic evidence
abstract: Populations of A. retroflexus from soybean fields where lactofen had been applied continuously for at least four seasons were assessed for resistance to PPO inhibitors. Whole-plant bioassays were run with lactofen, fomesafen, and acifluorfen at seven rates per compound. Eight of 16 populations displayed resistance factors above 5 for lactofen. Cross-resistance within the PPO inhibitor class was variable: all lactofen-resistant populations also showed resistance to fomesafen (RF 3.1–9.4), while only four showed elevated tolerance to acifluorfen (RF 2.0–4.1). PPO enzyme activity was extracted from etiolated seedling shoots and measured by spectrophotometric protoporphyrin IX accumulation assay. Km values for the PPO substrate did not differ significantly between resistant and susceptible populations. In contrast, Vmax ratios suggested higher total PPO activity in resistant plants, potentially through target enzyme amplification rather than altered substrate affinity. Sequencing of the PPX2L gene is ongoing.

title: Stacked resistance mechanisms in a multiple-resistant Amaranthus retroflexus biotype: ALS mutation, CYP-mediated metabolism, and reduced leaf uptake
abstract: A single A. retroflexus biotype collected from a long-term sunflower monoculture in Bačka Palanka, showing resistance to both imazethapyr and tribenuron-methyl with resistance factors exceeding 50, was characterised in detail to disentangle the contribution of three putative resistance mechanisms. Sequencing confirmed a Trp574Leu ALS mutation in all 20 plants analysed. PBO co-treatment reduced the GR50 for imazethapyr by a further 6.3-fold beyond the effect of the target-site mutation alone, indicating an additive metabolic component. Foliar uptake and translocation were quantified using 14C-imazethapyr applied to intact leaves enclosed in treatment chambers: resistant plants absorbed 31 ± 5% of applied radioactivity at 48 h versus 54 ± 7% in the susceptible reference, pointing to a reduced uptake component. Cuticle composition analysis by GC-MS showed a higher proportion of long-chain alkanes in resistant plants. Taken together, three mechanisms—target-site mutation, CYP metabolism, and reduced foliar uptake—accumulate in this biotype, with each contributing measurably to the overall resistance phenotype.

title: Herbicide resistance diagnostics for Vojvodina arable weed management: a practical guide for extension services
abstract: This book chapter reviews and synthesises the methods used for routine herbicide resistance diagnostics applicable under the resource constraints typical of extension laboratory settings in Serbia and comparable countries. Covered methods include the petri-dish seedling test, whole-plant dose–response bioassay, chlorophyll fluorescence inhibition screening, ALS enzyme extraction and activity assay, and rapid PCR-based detection of the most prevalent target-site mutations (Pro197, Trp574 in ALS; Ser264 in psbA). For each method, practical guidance is given on sample sizes, adequate controls, and decision thresholds for designating a population as resistant. Case examples from Vojvodina field surveys between 2014 and 2022 are used to illustrate interpretation of ambiguous results and the importance of confirming putative resistance with at least two independent lines of evidence. The chapter is intended for use by certified crop advisors and plant protection inspectors rather than specialist research laboratories, and deliberately avoids techniques requiring radioisotope licensing.

title: Glutathione S-transferase activity profiles across susceptible and resistant Chenopodium album populations under sub-lethal tribenuron-methyl exposure
abstract: Ten C. album populations with varying resistance factors to tribenuron-methyl (RF 1.1–22.4) were used to profile glutathione S-transferase (GST) activity in response to sub-lethal herbicide exposure. Total soluble protein was extracted from shoot tissue at 0, 6, 24, and 72 h after treatment at one-tenth of the field rate. GST activity towards 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) was measured spectrophotometrically. Populations with RF > 10 consistently showed higher constitutive GST activity (1.8- to 3.4-fold over susceptible controls at 0 h) and a more pronounced induction response at 24 h. Populations with confirmed psbA Ser264Gly mutations but susceptible to ALS inhibitors showed constitutive GST activity indistinguishable from the fully susceptible reference, indicating that elevated GST is not a generic stress response to the psbA mutation but is linked to ALS inhibitor tolerance. Native PAGE zymograms revealed additional faint GST isoform bands in the high-resistance populations. Protein identification of these bands by LC-MS/MS is under way.

title: Soil compaction modifies root crown angle in maize but not in sunflower: a two-year field experiment on Chernozem
abstract: Soil compaction is widespread in Vojvodina due to repeated heavy machinery use on fine-textured Chernozem soils. We investigated whether experimentally imposed compaction (target bulk density 1.55 g cm⁻³ vs. 1.30 g cm⁻³ in control plots) altered root crown architecture traits in four maize hybrids and four sunflower inbred-line test-crosses over two growing seasons (2019–2020). Compaction was created by repeated passes of a loaded tractor before planting; soil penetration resistance was verified with a cone penetrometer at 10 cm intervals. Root crowns were excavated by shovelomics at V8 (maize) and R1 (sunflower). In maize, compaction significantly increased mean nodal root angle by 4.8° (P < 0.001) and reduced lateral root density by 19%; effects were consistent across all four hybrids. In sunflower, no significant effect of compaction on any measured trait was observed. Compaction reduced maize grain yield by 14% on average. The divergent response suggests that the tap-rooted architecture of sunflower provides greater mechanical tolerance to high bulk density compared to the fibrous-rooted maize crown.

title: Variogram analysis of topsoil electrical conductivity measured by EM38 in a salt-affected field in northern Vojvodina
abstract: Apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) measured with an EM38 electromagnetic induction sensor was used to characterise spatial variability of topsoil salinity in a 45-hectare salt-affected field near Bačko Gradište, Serbia. A total of 312 georeferenced ECa readings collected along transects at 10-metre intervals were analysed by fitting spherical, exponential, and Gaussian theoretical variogram models. The spherical model provided the best fit (nugget-to-sill ratio 0.18), indicating strong spatial structure with a range of approximately 87 metres. Cross-validation with leave-one-out ordinary kriging yielded a root mean squared error of 1.4 mS/m and a mean error close to zero. Interpolated ECa maps were compared with 42 soil core measurements of electrical conductivity of the saturation extract (ECe). The Pearson correlation between predicted ECa and measured ECe was 0.81, confirming the utility of EM38 data as a surrogate for direct salinity measurements in this landscape. Results suggest that a transect spacing of 15 metres would be sufficient for capturing the dominant spatial patterns without significant loss of mapping accuracy.
venue: Journal of Applied Soil Research

title: Isolation frequency and species diversity of Pythium spp. from carrot fields in Vojvodina: a two-season survey
abstract: Damping-off and root dieback of processing carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) have intensified in Vojvodina since the wet spring of 2021, yet species-level attribution of causal agents remains incomplete for the region. Soil and root samples were collected from 38 commercial carrot fields across six municipalities during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons. Isolation on selective PARP medium yielded 214 oomycete cultures, of which 178 were assigned to Pythium using ITS and cox2 sequencing. Six species were identified: P. ultimum var. ultimum (44 %), P. irregulare (21 %), P. sylvaticum (14 %), P. dissotocum (9 %), P. aphanidermatum (7 %), and P. helicoides (5 %). Pathogenicity was confirmed for all species by seedling inoculation assays at 15 °C and 25 °C under controlled conditions. P. ultimum var. ultimum dominated in fields with heavier soils and later planting dates, while P. aphanidermatum was associated with lighter soils and July sowing. The survey provides a baseline species inventory and preliminary habitat associations needed for subsequent population-genetic work across the Pannonian Plain.
venue: Acta Phytopathologica et Entomologica Pannonica

title: Hardness of Approximate Shortest Vector Problems in q-ary Lattices: A Reduction Framework
abstract: This paper revisits the hardness of the approximate shortest vector problem (SVP) in the specific class of q-ary lattices that arise naturally in cryptographic constructions. We formalize a reduction framework that maps instances of approximate SVP with gap factor γ to decision-LWE instances with explicitly computed noise parameters. The reduction is tight in the sense that the error rate grows only polynomially in the lattice dimension n for n up to 1024. We implement the framework in SageMath and run experiments on randomly generated q-ary lattices with q ≈ 2^13, measuring reduction success probabilities over 10,000 trial instances at dimensions 256, 512, and 1024. Results confirm that the reduction overhead is within a factor of 2.3 of the theoretical bound across all tested dimensions. We also identify a class of structured q-ary lattices where the reduction fails for γ < 1.8 sqrt(n), providing a concrete bound below which existing reductions break down. The findings are relevant to parameter selection in NTRU-style schemes.

title: Parameter Selection for Ring-LWE-Based Key Exchange: A Systematic Study
abstract: We carry out a systematic study of parameter choices for ring-LWE-based key exchange protocols, focusing on the trade-off between security level and ciphertext size. For polynomial rings Z_q[x]/(x^n+1) with n ∈ {256, 512, 1024} and moduli q ranging from 2^11 to 2^14, we evaluate the concrete security against known lattice attacks including BKZ-2.0, primal and dual distinguishing attacks, and hybrid meet-in-the-middle variants. Security estimates are computed using both the BKZ simulator and the lattice estimator library, yielding bit-security estimates that differ by up to 18 bits depending on the tool. We identify parameter sets achieving 128-bit post-quantum security with ciphertext overhead below 900 bytes. A reference implementation in C achieves encapsulation latency of 34 µs on an Intel Core i7-8700 at 3.2 GHz, with decapsulation at 41 µs. The paper provides parameter recommendation tables for practitioners.

title: On the Equivalence of Search and Decision Variants of Module-LWE
abstract: The Learning With Errors problem over module lattices (Module-LWE, or MLWE) generalizes both plain LWE and ring-LWE. While search-to-decision reductions are well established for standard LWE, the module setting introduces subtleties arising from the choice of rank k and the underlying number field. This work presents a self-contained proof that search-MLWE reduces to decision-MLWE for ranks k ≥ 2 over cyclotomic rings of conductor 2^m, under standard algebraic assumptions. The reduction is constructive and yields an explicit algorithm with running time polynomial in n, k, and log q. We also show that for rank k = 1 the reduction requires an additional algebraic condition on the error distribution that does not hold for all Gaussian parameters, clarifying a gap in prior literature. We verify the algebraic claims computationally in PARI/GP for m ∈ {8, 9, 10, 11}. The result strengthens the theoretical basis of the Kyber/ML-KEM family of schemes.

title: Timing Side-Channel Vulnerabilities in Lattice-Based Decapsulation: A Case Study on Polynomial Multiplication
abstract: We investigate timing side-channel leakage arising in the decapsulation procedure of lattice-based key encapsulation mechanisms, focusing on the polynomial multiplication step implemented via the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT). Using a cache-timing attack model on a shared-memory system, we demonstrate that branch-free NTT implementations can still leak information through operand-dependent memory access patterns during coefficient reduction modulo q. We instrument five publicly available reference implementations in C and measure execution times across 10^6 decapsulation operations at a ring dimension of n = 512 and modulus q = 3329, finding timing variance of up to 14 ns correlated with the Hamming weight of secret key coefficients. We propose two countermeasures: a fully constant-time coefficient reduction routine and an operand-blinding technique, and evaluate their overhead at 6% and 11% respectively. The work applies directly to software deployed on resource-constrained IoT devices.

title: Lattice-Based Cryptography in Practice: Design Principles and Implementation Pitfalls
abstract: This book chapter surveys the landscape of lattice-based cryptographic primitives from the perspective of practical deployment. We cover the mathematical foundations—SVP, CVP, LWE, NTRU, and their module variants—and describe how theoretical hardness results translate (or fail to translate) into implementation security guarantees. Special attention is given to three categories of implementation pitfall: incorrect error sampling that reduces effective entropy, improper handling of decapsulation failure probability leading to information leakage, and misuse of deterministic randomness in encapsulation. Each pitfall is illustrated with a concrete example drawn from published implementations. The chapter concludes with a checklist of 14 implementation requirements derived from observed errors in the literature, intended as a practical reference for software engineers integrating post-quantum primitives. The material is suitable for graduate students and practitioners without prior background in lattice mathematics.

title: Failure Probability Bounds for NTRU-Based Key Encapsulation Under Non-Uniform Error Distributions
abstract: NTRU-based key encapsulation schemes specify error polynomials drawn from distributions with small coefficients. In practice, hardware random number generators may produce distributions that deviate measurably from the target. This paper derives closed-form upper bounds on the decapsulation failure probability when the error distribution is a perturbation of the nominal distribution by a total-variation distance δ. We show that for standard NTRU parameters at n = 677 and q = 2048, a perturbation of δ = 2^{-20} inflates the failure probability by a factor of at most 3.2, while for δ = 2^{-14} the inflation factor reaches 47. The analysis uses moment-generating function techniques for bounded discrete distributions. We validate the bounds by Monte Carlo simulation over 5 × 10^7 key pairs generated with synthetically perturbed distributions. The results provide concrete guidance for hardware entropy source quality requirements in NTRU deployments.

title: Sieving Algorithms on Module Lattices: Complexity and Practical Limits at Dimension 400–600
abstract: Lattice sieving algorithms have become the dominant approach for solving SVP in high dimensions, but their practical behaviour on module lattices—relevant for post-quantum cryptography—is less well characterised than on random lattices. This paper reports a systematic computational study of three sieving algorithms (GaussSieve, BGJ1, and a multi-level bucket sieve) applied to module lattices of rank k ∈ {2, 4} at total lattice dimensions between 400 and 600. Experiments are run on a 32-core cluster using a distributed implementation in C++. We record wall-clock time, memory consumption, and the number of vectors found shorter than the Gaussian heuristic bound. At dimension 512, the module structure reduces sieving time by 23% compared to unstructured lattices of the same dimension, a non-trivial gap that affects concrete security estimates. We provide updated security estimate tables for ML-KEM parameter sets based on our empirical timings.

title: Algebraic Structure Exploitation in Quantum Lattice Attacks: Limits of the Hidden Subgroup Approach
abstract: A recurring question in post-quantum cryptography is whether quantum algorithms can exploit the ring or module structure of lattice problems to achieve superpolynomial speedup over classical sieving. This paper examines the applicability of the hidden subgroup problem (HSP) framework to ring-SIS and ring-LWE, formalising the conditions under which the algebraic structure of the cyclotomic ring Z[x]/(Φ_m(x)) could be cast as an HSP instance over a non-abelian group. We show that while a group-theoretic embedding exists for m = 2^k with k ≤ 5, the resulting HSP is over a group whose quantum Fourier transform has no known efficient implementation. The negative result implies that standard HSP-based quantum algorithms do not yield a superpolynomial advantage for ring-LWE at currently deployed parameter sizes. The argument is formalized using representation theory of dihedral groups and validated computationally for m ∈ {16, 32, 64}.

title: Compressed Public Keys in Module-NTRU: Balancing Size and Failure Rate
abstract: Module-NTRU schemes allow public keys to be compressed by rounding polynomial coefficients, reducing transmission overhead at the cost of a higher decapsulation failure probability. This paper gives a rigorous analysis of the trade-off for rank-k module-NTRU over Z_q[x]/(x^n + 1) at the specific parameter set n = 256, k = 4, q = 4096 targeted at 128-bit post-quantum security. We derive an explicit formula for failure probability as a function of the rounding step Δ and show that Δ = 4 yields a public key size reduction of 22% while inflating the failure probability from 2^{-138} to 2^{-97}, which remains acceptable for most applications. We implement the compressed scheme in constant-time C and benchmark it on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller, achieving encapsulation in 1.14 ms and decapsulation in 1.37 ms at 168 MHz clock speed. The implementation is made publicly available.

title: Tighter Noise Flooding Bounds for Lattice-Based Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Knowledge
abstract: Lattice-based zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge for linear relations modulo q frequently rely on noise flooding to achieve statistical zero-knowledge: the prover adds a fresh Gaussian noise vector large enough to mask the witness. Existing analyses require the flooding noise standard deviation to be at least 2^{40} times the witness norm, leading to large proof sizes. We present a refined analysis using the Rényi divergence instead of statistical distance to bound the distinguishing advantage, reducing the required flooding factor to 2^{22} for security parameter λ = 128. The reduction in flooding factor translates to a 42% decrease in proof size for a representative linear-relation statement over Z_q^n with n = 512. We construct an explicit proof system, implement it in SageMath, and provide proof-size and verification-time benchmarks. The proof system is compatible with the commitment schemes used in current post-quantum signature proposals.

title: Security Degradation in Hybrid Classical–Lattice KEM Combiners: An Analysis of XOR-Then-Hash Approaches
abstract: Hybrid KEM combiners are increasingly used in TLS 1.3 and other protocols to hedge against failures of either the classical (ECDH) or post-quantum component. A common construction takes the form K = H(K_1 || K_2 || ct_1 || ct_2), where H is a hash function. This paper analyses the security degradation incurred when the classical component is broken by an adversary with quantum access, focusing on XOR-then-hash combiners of the form K = H(K_1 XOR K_2). We show that if K_1 is a uniformly random string (indistinguishable-CCA assumption on the classical KEM) but K_2 leaks b bits of information due to a partial break of the PQ-KEM, then the combined key retains min(256 - b, λ_PQ) bits of security, where λ_PQ is the standalone security of the PQ-KEM. The proof uses hybrid arguments and the random oracle model. We evaluate the result numerically for ML-KEM-768 combined with X25519 across several partial break scenarios, providing a concrete security budget table.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Queue Management in Edge-Cloud Continuum Deployments
abstract: Edge nodes in a continuum deployment have limited queuing capacity and must decide whether to process requests locally or offload them to a central cloud tier. This paper formulates the per-edge offloading decision as a Markov decision process solved approximately by a tabular Q-learning agent. The state is a discretised pair of local queue length and observed round-trip latency to the cloud. Reward is the negative of per-request sojourn time. The agent is trained in a simulated environment parameterised from latency and arrival-rate measurements at two edge nodes of a pilot deployment at the NTP Novi Sad testbed during a three-week collection period. After convergence (approximately 800,000 simulated steps), the learned policy reduces mean sojourn time by 14 percent and 99th-percentile sojourn time by 23 percent compared to a static threshold offloading rule. Robustness to distributional shift is tested by applying the policy under a workload with 30 percent higher arrival rate; degradation is modest, with mean sojourn time increasing by 9 percent over the trained-condition optimum.

title: Topological analysis of pore networks in ceramic materials from micro-CT imaging
abstract: We analyse three-dimensional pore networks of five types of porous ceramic samples, each imaged by micro-CT at 1.8 μm voxel resolution, yielding binary volumes of approximately 500³ voxels. Skeletonisation produces point clouds of up to 180 000 points. We compute Čech complex persistent homology up to dimension 3 using a GPU-accelerated boundary matrix reduction implementation. H_0 features characterise connectivity of the pore space; H_1 and H_2 features correspond to tunnels and enclosed voids respectively. Samples with high sintering temperature exhibit fewer and larger H_1 generators, consistent with pore coarsening. We regress total porosity (range 12–38%) and pore-size distribution parameters from persistence diagram features using random forests, achieving R² = 0.91 on a held-out test set of 18 samples. The approach provides a parameter-free topological signature that complements mercury intrusion porosimetry. This is the first study applying persistent homology to sinter-controlled alumina ceramics.

title: Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Under Local Differential Privacy Constraints
abstract: Federated learning systems face two simultaneous threats: privacy leakage toward the aggregator and Byzantine clients that submit corrupted model updates. We study whether standard Byzantine-robust aggregation rules—coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, and Krum—remain effective when client updates are additionally perturbed for local differential privacy. We show analytically that the coordinate-wise median rule retains its Byzantine tolerance when the fraction of malicious clients is below 1/4, provided the LDP noise scale is below a threshold that we characterise in terms of model dimension and ε. Above this threshold, Byzantine clients can craft updates that are indistinguishable from honest noisy updates, defeating the robust rule. We verify these claims in a simulation with a 32-dimensional linear model, 100 clients, and up to 20 Byzantine clients using a sign-flip attack. Practical guidelines for choosing ε in adversarial deployments are provided.

title: Between Compliance and Conviction: How Primary School Teachers in Vojvodina Describe Compulsory Use of an Electronic Register System
abstract: The introduction of an electronic class register across public primary schools in Serbia's Vojvodina province in 2012 provided a natural context for examining teacher responses to top-down technology mandates. This study presents findings from semi-structured interviews with 24 primary school teachers conducted six months after mandatory rollout. Participants were recruited from eight schools in Novi Sad, Sombor, and Subotica, stratified by years of service and subject area. Interview transcripts were analysed using thematic analysis following the framework described by Braun and Clarke. Three dominant response patterns emerged: pragmatic compliance, identity-protective resistance, and reluctant integration. Teachers with more than fifteen years of service were overrepresented in the resistance pattern, while younger teachers more often reported pragmatic compliance. Findings suggest that the speed of mandate implementation, rather than the tool itself, is the primary source of identity disruption. Implications for policy rollout timelines and school-level mediation roles are discussed.

title: Identity Salience and Platform Anxiety: A Survey Study of Serbian Primary Teachers Using a Mandated Learning Management System
abstract: This paper reports on a cross-sectional survey investigating the relationship between professional identity salience and technology-related anxiety in Serbian primary school teachers following the institutional rollout of a commercially licensed learning management system called EduPortal-SR. A validated Serbian-language instrument combining the Professional Identity Scale for Teachers (adapted) and the Computer Anxiety Rating Scale was administered to 312 teachers across 31 primary schools in four municipalities in southern Vojvodina. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a three-factor solution for the identity measure. Multiple regression showed that identity salience significantly predicted technology anxiety scores after controlling for age, gender, and prior digital experience (β = 0.31, p < 0.001). Teachers who strongly identified with a non-digital pedagogical tradition showed the highest anxiety scores. The study adds quantitative support to qualitative findings from the same period and suggests that identity-focused professional development interventions may reduce implementation friction more effectively than skills-only training.

title: Narrative Disruption in Teaching Biographies: A Longitudinal Interview Study on Compulsory Digital Tool Adoption
abstract: Using a narrative inquiry approach, this study followed fourteen primary school teachers in Sombor and surrounding municipalities over a three-year period (2014–2017) as they integrated two consecutively mandated digital tools: an electronic grade-book and an online homework submission platform. Annual interviews were conducted with each participant, yielding 42 transcripts totalling approximately 180,000 words. Narrative analysis focused on shifts in how teachers described their 'good teaching' schema across interview waves. Eleven of the fourteen participants showed measurable disruption in their teaching biography narratives by year two, characterised by increased use of conditional and evaluative language when describing classroom practice. Six participants reconstructed a stable professional narrative by year three, typically by repositioning digital tools as administrative rather than pedagogical objects. The findings illuminate a coping mechanism not previously described in the technology acceptance literature and have direct implications for longitudinal support structures in schools.

title: When the Tool Becomes the Task: Teacher Perceptions of Pedagogical Displacement in Digitally Mandated Classrooms
abstract: This book chapter reviews empirical research published between 2008 and 2018 on teacher perceptions of role displacement arising from institutionally mandated digital tools. Drawing on 47 studies from Europe, Australia, and North America, the review identifies a recurring pattern termed 'tool primacy inversion', in which teachers report that managing the platform becomes more cognitively central than managing learning. The chapter synthesises findings thematically and proposes a three-stage displacement model: initial friction, compensatory adaptation, and either restoration or chronic displacement. Particular attention is paid to research from post-socialist education systems, where institutional trust dynamics differ from Western European contexts. The chapter also examines methodological gaps, noting that most studies rely on self-report data collected within twelve months of tool introduction and that longitudinal designs remain rare. Recommendations for research design and for school leadership practice conclude the chapter.

title: Pandemic Acceleration as a Natural Experiment: Primary Teacher Identity Strain Before and After Emergency Remote Teaching Mandates in Serbia
abstract: The abrupt shift to remote instruction in March 2020 created an unplanned quasi-experimental context for studying teacher identity strain under extreme mandate speed. This mixed-methods study combined DISTRA-T scale administration (n = 389) with 30 follow-up interviews drawn from respondents at high and low strain score extremes. Scale data were collected at three time points: pre-pandemic baseline (January 2020, n = 201 retrospective recall), four months post-mandate (July 2020), and fourteen months post-mandate (May 2021). Mean DISTRA-T scores increased significantly at T2 (d = 0.58) and partially recovered by T3 but remained above baseline. Interview analysis revealed that teachers who received peer-led, school-based support showed substantially faster narrative recovery than those who attended only centrally organised webinars. The study contributes to debates on the appropriate pace and support structure for digital transitions and demonstrates the practical utility of the DISTRA-T instrument at scale.

title: School Leadership Practices and Their Moderating Effect on Teacher Identity Strain During Mandated Platform Adoption: Evidence from 18 Primary Schools
abstract: This study examined whether and how school principal behaviours moderate the relationship between mandated digital tool adoption and teacher professional identity strain as measured by the DISTRA-T scale. Data were collected from 18 primary schools in Vojvodina selected to vary on school size and settlement type (urban, suburban, rural). A total of 276 teachers completed the DISTRA-T at two time points (before and six months after adoption of a new regional digital reporting platform), and 18 principals were interviewed about their support strategies. Multilevel modelling revealed significant between-school variance in identity strain trajectories (ICC = 0.19). Principal behaviours coded as 'meaning-making communication' and 'structured peer pairing' were associated with lower strain growth, while purely technical training provision showed no significant moderating effect. The findings suggest that principal training programmes should incorporate identity-sensitive communication strategies alongside technical upskilling.

title: Does Identity-Sensitive Onboarding Reduce Platform Abandonment? A Randomised Pilot in Six Primary Schools
abstract: This preprint reports the design and preliminary outcomes of a randomised pilot study testing an identity-sensitive onboarding protocol against standard technical training for teachers adopting a new school administration platform in six primary schools in the Sombor district. Schools were randomised at the unit level (three per condition). The identity-sensitive protocol included reflective journalling, structured peer observation, and facilitated discussion of how the new tool related to each teacher's expressed pedagogical values; total intervention time was 9 hours across three sessions. Platform usage logs were extracted at four and twelve weeks post-adoption. At twelve weeks, abandonment rates (defined as fewer than two logins per week) were 11% in the intervention condition versus 31% in the control condition. DISTRA-T scores were lower in the intervention group at both follow-up points. The study is small and the results should be interpreted with caution; a full trial is in preparation.

title: Adapting formative quiz feedback for learners with attention difficulties: format, immediacy, and length
abstract: Students with attention-related learning differences often disengage from formative feedback when it is presented in lengthy prose form after a delay. This study compared three feedback formats—extended prose, bulleted key-point summaries, and audio-recorded summaries—delivered either immediately or 24 hours after quiz completion, in a 3 × 2 factorial design with 96 upper-secondary students with documented attention difficulties. Immediate bulleted feedback produced the highest revision accuracy on a follow-up task (M = 71.4 %, SD = 9.2), outperforming delayed prose feedback by 18.6 percentage points. Audio summaries showed intermediate effects and were rated highest for perceived usefulness in a post-study questionnaire. Format and immediacy interacted significantly (F(2,90) = 6.14, p = .003). The results support the UDL guideline on providing options for self-regulation and suggest practical trade-offs for learning management system designers configuring automated feedback pipelines.

title: Perceptions of UDL-based digital adaptations among parents of children with dyslexia: a qualitative study from Serbia and Romania
abstract: Parents play a central role in supporting children with dyslexia when accessible digital materials are sent home for independent practice, yet their perceptions of UDL-based adaptations have received little research attention in the Western Balkans and Romania. This study conducted semi-structured interviews with 28 parents (17 from Serbia, 11 from Romania) whose children attended inclusive primary schools and used UDL-adapted digital materials as part of a pilot programme. Thematic analysis identified four main themes: (1) perceived reduction in child frustration during homework, (2) uncertainty about whether adaptations would disadvantage children in standardised testing contexts, (3) practical barriers related to device availability and internet stability at home, and (4) a desire for brief parent-facing guides accompanying adapted materials. Cross-national comparison revealed stronger scepticism among Romanian parents regarding accommodation validity, linked to differences in national assessment policy. Findings highlight the need to involve parents in co-designing accessible homework ecosystems alongside children and teachers.

title: Anxiety as a Moderator of Game-Based Mathematics Outcomes in Late Childhood: An Experimental Study
abstract: Mathematics anxiety has been identified as a factor that may suppress or amplify learning effects in game-based instruction. This experiment assigned 104 students in grades four and five to a competitive hybrid math game or a collaborative hybrid math game, crossing game type with a continuous measure of mathematics anxiety collected at baseline using the Child Mathematics Anxiety Questionnaire adapted for Serbian. Arithmetic post-test scores, timed fact recall, and self-reported task enjoyment were collected after five weeks of twice-weekly sessions. Regression models showed a significant interaction between anxiety level and game type on arithmetic post-test scores (β = −0.31, p = 0.02): highly anxious students performed better in the collaborative than in the competitive game, while low-anxiety students performed comparably across conditions. Enjoyment ratings mirrored this pattern. Findings suggest that competitive game formats should be used cautiously with anxious learners and that collaborative structures may offer a more robust default for heterogeneous classrooms.

title: Four-year longitudinal outcomes of asynchronous video instruction on metacognitive regulation: completing the cohort study
abstract: This paper reports the third and fourth measurement waves of the cohort study begun in 2016, now covering 98 of the original 143 participants over four years. Mixed-effects models with time-varying covariates (employment status, device access, course load) were used to estimate individual growth trajectories on all three SMRS sub-scales. By wave four, the structured-video group showed sustained advantages on monitoring (d = 0.47) and evaluation (d = 0.38) relative to the text-based comparison group, while the planning gap remained non-significant. Rural participants who persisted showed trajectories statistically indistinguishable from urban participants, suggesting that differential attrition rather than context per se explains earlier rural–urban gaps. The paper also reports qualitative data from exit interviews with 22 completers, identifying perceived instructor presence in video as a key mechanism underlying the monitoring advantage. Limitations relating to the non-randomised design are discussed at length.

title: Does prompt modality matter? Comparing text, audio, and talking-head prompts embedded in instructional video
abstract: An experiment was conducted with 91 adult learners randomly assigned to three conditions varying the modality of reflective prompts embedded in a six-module asynchronous video course: on-screen text prompts, audio-only prompts delivered by a voice-over, and talking-head prompts delivered by the instructor on-camera. Outcome measures were SMRS monitoring sub-scale scores, written reflection word count, and a domain knowledge posttest administered at weeks three and six. Mixed ANOVA revealed no significant main effect of prompt modality on SMRS scores (F(2, 88) = 1.84, p = .164) or knowledge posttest scores. The talking-head condition produced significantly longer written reflections (M = 187 words) compared to text (M = 134 words) and audio (M = 141 words) conditions (p = .03). A moderation analysis found that learners with lower baseline SMRS scores benefited more from talking-head prompts. Production cost and technical constraints for rural delivery are discussed as practical considerations alongside the effect-size findings.

title: Parental Digital Literacy and Co-Use During E-Learning Homework: Cross-Sectional Evidence from Three Serbian Cities
abstract: This cross-sectional survey examined links between parental digital literacy and the frequency and quality of co-use during children's e-learning homework sessions. Data were collected from 402 parents of children aged 8–12 in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin using an adapted version of the Digital Literacy Assessment Framework alongside a purpose-built co-use frequency measure. Parental digital literacy scores were positively correlated with co-use frequency (r = 0.41, p < 0.001) and with a composite measure of homework-session quality derived from child ratings. The relationship held after controlling for household income and number of children. Path analysis suggested that literacy influenced co-use quality both directly and indirectly through parental self-efficacy regarding digital tools. Practical implications for in-school digital literacy training programmes targeting parents are discussed.

title: Teacher Communication About Digital Homework and Its Effect on Parental Mediation Intensity
abstract: This experimental study assigned 26 primary school classes (n = 487 children) to one of three conditions varying in how teachers communicated digital homework expectations to parents: minimal instruction, structured guidance with suggested co-use activities, and structured guidance plus weekly brief feedback messages. Parental mediation was measured after eight weeks using the adapted mediation scale and platform log data. Classes in the structured guidance plus feedback condition showed significantly higher rates of active mediation (43% of parents classified as high active mediators) compared to minimal instruction (22%, χ² = 11.4, p = 0.003). Children's task completion rates followed the same pattern. Effect sizes were moderate (Cohen's d = 0.48). The study supports the view that teachers can meaningfully shift parental mediation behaviour through communication design, without requiring additional digital training for parents.

title: Pencil-and-paper versus brief computerised cognitive screening in workers with chronic solvent exposure: a cross-sectional pilot comparison
abstract: Organic solvents such as toluene and xylene are known to affect central nervous system function following prolonged occupational exposure, yet no consensus exists on which screening format is most sensitive in workplace settings. This cross-sectional pilot study recruited 58 male workers from two paint-manufacturing facilities in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin, all with documented exposure histories of at least five years, alongside 45 age- and education-matched controls from administrative staff. Participants completed the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Trail Making Test parts A and B, and a locally adapted 15-minute computerised battery assessing processing speed, sustained attention, and working memory. Blood and urine samples confirmed solvent metabolite levels. Workers showed statistically significant lower scores on Trail Making Test B (mean difference 18.3 s, p = 0.003) and computerised reaction time tasks (mean difference 42 ms, p = 0.011) relative to controls. MoCA total scores did not differentiate groups at standard cut-offs. Inter-rater reliability for the paper tests was high (ICC = 0.91). Results suggest that timed computerised subtests may capture attentional deficits that global screening scores miss, warranting further longitudinal follow-up.

title: Blood lead and cadmium concentrations and working memory performance in smelter workers: a 12-month follow-up
abstract: Heavy metal exposure in non-ferrous smelting is associated with neurotoxic effects, yet longitudinal data from workers in the Western Balkans remain sparse. This study followed 34 male smelter workers at a zinc-processing plant in southern Vojvodina over 12 months, measuring blood lead and urinary cadmium at baseline, six months, and 12 months alongside three neuropsychological outcomes: digit span forward and backward, the Corsi Block-Tapping Task, and a computerised n-back task (1-back and 2-back). Mean blood lead at baseline was 28.4 µg/dL (SD 9.1), well above the current NIOSH reference level. Mixed-effects linear regression showed that each 10 µg/dL increase in blood lead was associated with a 0.41-point reduction in digit span backward (95% CI −0.72 to −0.10, p = 0.011) over time, after adjusting for age, education, and alcohol use. Cadmium levels were low and not significantly associated with any outcome. The computerised 2-back task showed the steepest decline trajectory, suggesting it may be more responsive to lead-related working memory impairment than traditional span tasks. Sample size limits generalisation; a larger multisite study is planned.

title: Depressive symptomatology in workers with occupational neurotoxicant exposure: mediating role of sleep disturbance
abstract: Neuropsychiatric sequelae of chronic neurotoxicant exposure extend beyond cognitive performance to affective and vegetative symptoms. This cross-sectional questionnaire study included 112 workers with documented exposure to either organic solvents or heavy metals recruited through occupational health clinics in three Vojvodinian municipalities, plus 78 unexposed controls. Participants completed the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the Perceived Stress Scale. Structural equation modelling tested whether sleep disturbance mediated the relationship between self-reported cumulative exposure index and PHQ-9 score. Workers with high cumulative exposure had PHQ-9 scores averaging 3.2 points higher than controls (p < 0.001). PSQI global score partially mediated this relationship (indirect effect = 1.1, bootstrapped 95% CI 0.4–1.9), accounting for approximately 34% of the total effect. Perceived stress did not significantly mediate the association after adjusting for sleep. Findings suggest that sleep quality screening should be incorporated into routine neuropsychiatric monitoring in exposed worker populations. Limitations include reliance on self-report exposure indices and absence of biological exposure measurements in this sub-study.

title: Slow oscillation–spindle coupling in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: relationship to overnight memory consolidation
abstract: Slow oscillation–spindle coupling during NREM sleep is considered a mechanism of hippocampus-dependent memory consolidation. We tested whether this coupling is disrupted in drug-resistant focal epilepsy and whether disruption predicts declarative memory performance. Forty-two patients and 35 controls underwent overnight polysomnography with simultaneous 64-channel EEG. Spindle events were detected automatically and phase-locked to slow oscillations (<1 Hz). Coupling strength was quantified as modulation index. Patients showed reduced modulation index compared with controls (0.038 vs 0.061, p<0.001), with the largest reductions ipsilateral to the seizure onset zone. Coupling reduction was associated with worse next-morning performance on a word-pair recall task (r=0.47, p=0.002) even after controlling for seizure frequency and medication load. IED density during N2 was negatively associated with modulation index (r=−0.39, p=0.011). These findings link electrophysiological sleep disruption to a measurable functional consequence and suggest that improving coupling could be a treatment target.

title: Small Enterprise ERP Adoption in the Western Balkans: An Extended TAM Analysis
abstract: This study examines factors driving enterprise resource planning adoption among small firms in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia using an extended Technology Acceptance Model. Survey data were collected from 214 owner-managers between 2009 and 2010. The model incorporates perceived usefulness, ease of use, top management support, IT infrastructure quality, and vendor trust. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied to test eight hypotheses. Results indicate that vendor trust and top management support are the strongest predictors of adoption intention, together explaining 41% of variance. Perceived ease of use had a significant indirect effect mediated through perceived usefulness. The study provides early empirical evidence from post-transition small business contexts where institutional and market environments differ substantially from those in Western Europe. Practical implications concern vendor strategy and government ICT support programmes.

title: Internet Banking Adoption Among Retirees in Serbia: A Preliminary Survey
abstract: This paper presents findings from a cross-sectional survey conducted in 2012 with 187 retired individuals in the Vojvodina region of Serbia. The study employed an abbreviated TAM questionnaire supplemented by items on computer anxiety and social influence drawn from the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). Exploratory factor analysis confirmed a four-factor structure. Regression analysis showed that computer anxiety and lack of perceived security were the dominant barriers to internet banking adoption, while social influence from adult children positively predicted intention to use. Age within the retirement cohort (60–69 versus 70+) moderated the effect of ease of use. The findings establish baseline data for a longitudinal follow-up and highlight the heterogeneity of the older adult segment in digital financial services research.
