title: Trust Formation in Online Payment Systems: Evidence from Post-Transitional Economies in Central and Eastern Europe
abstract: Drawing on data from four countries — Serbia, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia — this study examines how institutional trust, prior banking experience, and perceived security jointly determine trust in online payment systems. An online survey administered in 2014 gathered responses from 641 adults aged 18–75. Multi-group confirmatory factor analysis established measurement invariance across country subsamples. Structural path estimates show that perceived security is the strongest antecedent of online payment trust in all four countries, but the effect of institutional trust is significantly larger in Serbia and Romania than in Slovakia and Slovenia, consistent with differences in the maturity of consumer protection regulation. Age moderates the security–trust link, with older adults showing steeper sensitivity to security cues. The study contributes a cross-national comparative baseline for fintech expansion strategies.

title: Longitudinal Measurement of Mobile Payment Intention Among Adults Over 60: A Two-Wave Panel Study in Serbia
abstract: This paper reports results from the first two waves of a panel study tracking mobile payment adoption intentions among Serbian adults aged 60 and older. Wave 1 was collected in 2015 (N = 312) and Wave 2 in 2017 (N = 271 retained respondents). The extended TAM framework includes effort expectancy, hedonic motivation, habit, and facilitating conditions adapted from UTAUT2. Cross-lagged structural models show that habit formed between waves is the single largest predictor of Wave 2 intention, surpassing effort expectancy. Facilitating conditions — operationalised as smartphone ownership, data plan availability, and proximity to bank branches — have a significant direct effect in Wave 1 that attenuates by Wave 2, suggesting early adoption gatekeeping. Attrition analysis confirms that non-retainees were older, less educated, and had lower Wave 1 intention scores, indicating a potential optimistic bias in Wave 2 estimates.

title: Financial Literacy as a Moderator of TAM Relationships in Digital Payment Adoption: A Multi-Group Analysis
abstract: This chapter reviews and synthesises evidence on how financial literacy moderates technology acceptance relationships in the context of retail digital payments, with particular attention to older adults in transition economies. The review covers 34 empirical studies published between 2008 and 2018 sourced from three databases. A meta-analytic structural path comparison is conducted for the perceived usefulness–intention link across low and high financial literacy groups, drawing on primary data from a 2017 Serbian survey (N = 486) as an illustrative case. Results consistently show that the usefulness–intention path is stronger for financially literate individuals, while ease of use matters more for those with low financial literacy. The chapter discusses implications for financial education policy and bank product communication strategies in Southeastern Europe.

title: Three-Wave Panel Evidence on the Role of Social Influence in Mobile Payment Adoption by Older Adults
abstract: This paper reports the third wave of the longitudinal panel begun in 2015, adding 2020 data (N = 244 completing all three waves). Between waves, the COVID-19 pandemic led to reported increases in contactless and mobile payment use across all age groups. Autoregressive cross-lagged models show that social influence — primarily from adult children and peers — grew markedly stronger as a predictor of adoption between Wave 2 (2017) and Wave 3 (2020) for respondents aged 70 and above, possibly reflecting pandemic-driven household technology transmission. Habit remained the dominant predictor for the 60–69 cohort. A latent growth curve model estimates average annual growth in mobile payment frequency of 1.1 transactions per month across the full panel. Mortality and health-related attrition over the five-year span is documented and discussed as a limitation affecting internal validity.

title: Comparing TAM-Based Adoption Models Across Digital Payment Channels: ATM, Internet Banking, and Mobile Apps in Serbia
abstract: This study uses a within-person design to compare technology acceptance across three digital payment channels simultaneously. A sample of 502 Serbian adults aged 40–75 completed channel-specific TAM questionnaires for ATM use, internet banking, and mobile banking apps in a 2021 cross-sectional survey. Latent mean comparison via multiple-group confirmatory factor analysis indicates that perceived usefulness scores are highest for ATMs and lowest for mobile apps, while ease of use scores show the opposite pattern for respondents under 55. A MIMIC model tests whether sociodemographic variables differentially suppress adoption across channels. Education and prior digital device experience are the strongest sociodemographic predictors for mobile apps, accounting for 19% of variance in adoption intention. The results suggest that channel-specific communication strategies are warranted rather than uniform digital banking campaigns.
venue: Proceedings of the 14th Conference on Information Systems and Technologies in Business (ISTB 2022), Novi Sad

title: Facilitating Conditions and Older Adults' Digital Payment Use: Evidence from Rural and Urban Vojvodina
abstract: Access to digital infrastructure is unevenly distributed across urban and rural Vojvodina, creating heterogeneous adoption environments for older adults. This study combines household survey data (N = 618, collected 2022) with municipality-level broadband penetration and bank branch density data from public registers. Multi-level modelling with respondents nested within municipalities shows that municipality-level broadband penetration significantly predicts mobile payment use frequency over and above individual-level TAM constructs (ICC = 0.11). The gap between rural and urban monthly mobile payment transactions narrows after controlling for smartphone ownership and perceived usefulness, suggesting that infrastructure and device access account for a substantial share of the rural-urban divide. Policy simulations indicate that raising rural broadband penetration to the Vojvodina average would close roughly 38% of the transaction frequency gap for the 65+ cohort.
venue: Journal of Regional Digital Economy and Society

title: Does Pension Payment Digitalisation Change Spending Behaviour? A Quasi-Experimental Study in Serbia
abstract: In 2019, the Serbian Pension and Disability Insurance Fund extended mandatory electronic pension disbursement to previously exempt rural post-office recipients. This policy change is used as a quasi-experiment to assess whether forced digital payment onboarding alters discretionary spending patterns and subjective financial wellbeing among retirees. Administrative disbursement records were linked to anonymised transaction data from a partner savings bank for 1,104 newly onboarded pensioners in two affected regions. A synthetic control group of 1,098 long-standing electronic recipients was constructed using propensity score matching. Difference-in-differences estimates over 18 post-treatment months show a modest but significant increase in non-cash retail spending (+7.4%) and a decrease in cash withdrawal frequency (-1.9 withdrawals per month). Subjective financial control, measured via a short embedded survey at 12 months, did not differ significantly between groups.
venue: Journal of Applied Behavioural Finance

title: Wearable Payment Adoption Intentions Among Adults Aged 55–75: An Exploratory Survey in Four CEE Countries
abstract: Wearable payment devices — smartwatches and NFC-enabled wristbands — represent a payment channel with very low penetration among older adults in Central and Eastern Europe. This exploratory cross-sectional survey collected data from 820 adults aged 55–75 in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia in late 2023. An extended TAM model incorporating perceived enjoyment, body image concerns, health data privacy worry, and social observability was estimated via PLS-SEM. Perceived enjoyment and social observability had significant positive effects on adoption intention across all four subsamples, while health data privacy worry was a significant negative predictor in Serbia and Romania only. Across countries, under 12% of respondents indicated high adoption intention, with the lowest share in rural subsamples. The paper treats the findings as exploratory and calls for replication with larger probability samples.
venue: Digital Finance and Emerging Payment Technologies

title: Four-Wave Longitudinal Study of Digital Payment Adoption Among Older Adults in Serbia: Cohort Attrition, Habit Consolidation, and Technology Generation Effects
abstract: This paper consolidates ten years of panel data (2015–2025, four waves) tracking mobile and contactless payment adoption among Serbian adults aged 60 and over (Wave 1 N = 312; Wave 4 N = 189). Latent class growth analysis identifies three adoption trajectories: early adopters (18% of Wave 1 sample) who plateau by Wave 2; gradual adopters (34%) who continue increasing use through Wave 3; and persistent non-adopters (48%) with near-zero trajectory throughout. Cox proportional hazard models on time-to-first mobile payment transaction show that smartphone ownership at Wave 1 halves the median time to adoption. Cohort replacement between Wave 3 and Wave 4 brings a detectable shift, as the newly aged-in cohort (born 1955–1960) enters with substantially higher smartphone and internet banking familiarity than those who entered in 2015. The paper discusses methodological lessons for longitudinal studies with older adult panels in low- and middle-income European countries.
venue: Journal of Digital Finance and Payments

title: Wavelet-Based Lossy Compression of Accelerometer Data for Rotating Machinery Monitoring
abstract: This paper evaluates the use of discrete wavelet transform (DWT) decomposition for compressing vibration signals acquired from a bearing test rig spinning at 1500–3000 RPM. Accelerometer data were sampled at 25.6 kHz using a 16-bit ADC and stored as 10-second frames. Five wavelet families (Daubechies 4, 8, Symlet 5, Coiflet 2, and biorthogonal 3.5) were compared at compression ratios between 8:1 and 64:1. Reconstruction fidelity was assessed by signal-to-noise ratio and by the ability to recover characteristic defect frequencies in the 2–8 kHz band. Daubechies 8 with hard thresholding at the fourth decomposition level achieved a 32:1 ratio with an average SNR loss below 1.4 dB and preserved bearing outer-race defect signatures in 94% of test frames. The study provides a baseline reference for embedded compression pipelines and identifies the threshold selection step as the main sensitivity point for downstream fault detection accuracy.
venue: Journal of Measurement and Instrumentation Engineering

title: Comparison of Fixed-Rate and Demand-Driven Sampling Strategies for High-Speed Vibration Acquisition on ARM Cortex-M4
abstract: Continuous acquisition of vibration data at 51.2 kHz on a Cortex-M4 microcontroller (STM32F407) saturates the DMA bus and leaves insufficient cycles for any in-situ processing. This work quantifies the trade-off between sampling rate, buffer management overhead, and available compute by profiling three strategies: fixed-rate DMA, triggered burst acquisition using an external comparator threshold, and a software-paced polling loop. Experiments used a belt-drive test bench with two imbalance levels and two misalignment conditions. Triggered burst acquisition reduced average data volume by 41% compared to fixed-rate while retaining all transient impact events with a false-negative rate below 3%. Profiling showed a 28% reduction in CPU cycles consumed per second. The paper provides concrete cycle-count and memory-footprint figures that are directly applicable to STM32-family deployments and discusses how the choice of strategy affects downstream FFT and envelope analysis routines.

title: Compressive Sensing Reconstruction of Vibration Spectra Using Bernoulli Measurement Matrices on a Low-Power Microcontroller
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) offers a route to reducing the raw data volume before transmission by exploiting sparsity in the frequency domain. This paper applies CS to vibration signals from a spindle motor running at 900–2700 RPM, using Bernoulli random measurement matrices generated on-chip with a hardware RNG on an STM32L476 (ultra-low-power line). Measurement vectors of length 128, 256, and 512 were tested against original frames of 2048 samples. Reconstruction used basis pursuit denoising solved offline; for embedded use, a greedy OMP variant was also evaluated. At a compression ratio of 8:1 and 256-sample measurements, reconstruction error remained below 4.2% RMS for signals with up to 12 significant spectral components. Power consumption during the measurement phase dropped by 62% relative to full-rate sampling. Limitations of on-chip RNG quality for matrix generation are discussed, and a lookup-table workaround is proposed for deterministic deployment.
venue: Signal Processing: Embedded and Real-Time Systems

title: On-Device Fault Classification for Rolling Element Bearings Using a Pruned Decision Tree Fitted to FFT Feature Vectors
abstract: This work targets a scenario where a wireless sensor node must classify bearing condition locally and transmit only a one-byte label rather than raw waveforms. Vibration data from a dedicated four-bearing test rig were recorded under healthy, inner-race defect, outer-race defect, and rolling-element defect conditions at three load levels. Feature extraction used 18 spectral amplitude ratios computed from 1024-point FFT frames. A CART decision tree was trained on 7200 frames (80/20 split) and pruned to a maximum depth of six nodes to fit within 2 kB of flash. Accuracy on the hold-out set was 91.3% overall; the inner-race defect class showed the lowest recall at 87.6%, attributed to load-dependent frequency smearing. Inference time on an STM32F103 at 72 MHz was 0.34 ms per frame. The paper also reports the sensitivity of classification accuracy to FFT window length and overlap ratio.
venue: Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Electrical, Electronic and Computing Engineering (IcETRAN)

title: Adaptive Frame Length Selection for Vibration Signals Based on Spectral Stationarity Estimation on a RISC-V Microcontroller
abstract: Fixed-length framing of vibration data wastes compute when the signal is stationary and may split transient events across frame boundaries. This paper presents a lightweight stationarity detector based on the Kullback–Leibler divergence between consecutive short-time spectral estimates, implemented entirely in integer arithmetic on a GD32VF103 RISC-V microcontroller running at 108 MHz. When divergence exceeds an empirically set threshold (calibrated per machine type in a 15-minute setup phase), the frame boundary is moved forward by one quarter-frame. Tests on a compressor drive-end dataset with injected gear-tooth crack events showed a 17% increase in the fraction of events fully contained within a single frame relative to fixed 256-sample framing, with a 6% increase in total processing time. Memory overhead is 420 bytes of RAM for the two spectral buffers. The detector adds no latency to the main acquisition path because it operates on a dedicated hardware timer interrupt.

title: A Structured Pruning Workflow for MobileNet-Style Architectures Targeting Sub-100 kB Flash Budgets in Industrial Sensor Nodes
abstract: Depthwise-separable convolution architectures such as MobileNet-V1 have been adapted for audio and vibration tasks, but published variants still exceed the flash and RAM available on mid-range microcontrollers. This book chapter describes a reproducible structured pruning workflow: (1) train a baseline model on a four-class vibration dataset (healthy, unbalance, misalignment, looseness) using a standard 70/15/15 split; (2) apply iterative channel pruning guided by the L1 norm of batch-normalisation scale factors; (3) fine-tune for 20 epochs after each pruning round. Starting from a 1.2 MB baseline, six pruning rounds reached a 94 kB model with an accuracy drop from 94.1% to 91.8% on the held-out set. The chapter provides a PyTorch reference implementation and discusses the portability of the resulting model to STM32CubeAI and TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, noting differences in operator support and latency.

title: Over-the-Air Model Update Protocol for Embedded Fault Detectors on BLE-Equipped Sensor Nodes
abstract: An edge inference node must occasionally be updated when the machine it monitors undergoes maintenance or retooling, yet full firmware flashing over BLE is impractical for large models. This paper describes and evaluates a delta-update protocol that transfers only the changed weight chunks of a quantised int8 model stored in external SPI flash. The protocol uses a 32-bit CRC per 512-byte block for integrity checking and falls back to full transfer on more than 40% block mismatch. Experiments transferred 12 model versions—differing by 5–35% of weights—to an nRF52840-based node over a 2 Mbit/s BLE connection in a factory-floor-noise environment (2.4 GHz interference from three co-located Wi-Fi networks). Mean transfer time for incremental updates was 8.3 seconds versus 41 seconds for full transfer. Inference accuracy after each update matched the reference PC evaluation to within 0.1%, confirming correct SPI flash write and read back.
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Embedded and Ubiquitous Computing (EUC-2023)

title: Benchmarking Integer-Only Inference Engines for 1-D Vibration CNNs on Four Microcontroller Families
abstract: Several open-source and vendor-supplied inference engines now claim to run int8 neural networks on Cortex-M and RISC-V targets, but published benchmarks rarely use identical models and datasets, making direct comparison difficult. This paper defines a fixed benchmark suite: two model sizes (small: 48 kB flash; medium: 92 kB flash), one standard four-class vibration dataset (25.6 kHz, 1024-sample input), and five microcontroller families (STM32H7, STM32F4, GD32VF1, ESP32-S3, RP2040). Inference engines evaluated are TFLite Micro, CMSIS-NN, uTensor, and a vendor SIMD library from one of the MCU suppliers. Results show that CMSIS-NN on STM32H7 at 480 MHz achieves the lowest per-frame latency (2.8 ms for the medium model), while RP2040 with TFLite Micro shows the highest variance (6.1 ± 1.9 ms) due to flash cache misses. The paper releases all benchmark scripts and model files under an open licence.

title: Automated shading loss estimation for urban rooftop PV planning using LiDAR-derived shadow maps and string simulation
abstract: Urban rooftop PV planning requires accurate shading loss estimates that account for neighbouring buildings, chimneys, and roof superstructures. This preprint describes a workflow that takes an airborne LiDAR point cloud of an urban block as input, derives hourly shadow maps at 0.2 m resolution using vector-based sun position calculation, and feeds per-panel irradiance estimates into a string-level simulator to produce annual energy yield and mismatch loss maps. The workflow was validated on fourteen rooftops in central Novi Sad for which post-installation monitoring data were available. Predicted annual energy yield matched measured values with a mean bias of −2.1% and root-mean-square error of 4.7%. Mismatch losses estimated by the tool ranged from 1.9% to 19.4% depending on roof complexity and string configuration. The preprint includes the simulation code and LiDAR preprocessing scripts as supplementary material to facilitate replication by other groups working on urban energy modelling.

title: Readability and comprehension outcomes when font spacing is adjusted for primary-school readers with dyslexia: a controlled classroom study
abstract: This study examined whether increasing inter-letter and inter-word spacing in digital reading materials improves comprehension scores for third- and fourth-grade students identified with dyslexia. Forty-two students from four primary schools in the Vojvodina region participated in a within-subject crossover design across six weeks. Each student read eight passages in standard formatting and eight in adjusted spacing (inter-letter +35 %, inter-word +20 %) matched for Flesch–Kincaid grade level. Comprehension was measured with researcher-developed cloze tasks administered immediately after each passage. Mean comprehension scores improved by 11.4 percentage points under the adjusted condition (t(41) = 3.87, p < .001, d = 0.60). Reading rate did not differ significantly between conditions. Teacher ratings of student engagement, collected via structured observation protocols, showed a modest positive shift under adjusted formatting. The findings support the inclusion of spacing customisation options in digital reading platforms used in inclusive Serbian primary classrooms and align with UDL guideline 1.1 on offering options for perception.

title: Teacher preparation for UDL implementation: a survey of pre-service educators in four Vojvodina faculties
abstract: Universal design for learning remains underrepresented in pre-service teacher curricula in Serbia despite its adoption in European inclusion policy frameworks. This cross-sectional survey recruited 318 final-year pre-service teachers from four faculties in the Vojvodina region (Sombor, Subotica, Zrenjanin, and Novi Sad). Participants completed a 42-item instrument measuring UDL knowledge, attitudes toward inclusive digital pedagogy, and self-efficacy for adapting digital materials. Mean UDL knowledge scores were low (M = 38.4 %, SD = 12.1), with no significant difference across institutions. Attitude scores were more positive but correlated weakly with knowledge (r = 0.31). Regression analysis indicated that prior contact with students with learning differences during practicum was the strongest predictor of both knowledge and self-efficacy. The paper recommends structured UDL modules in initial teacher education and suggests a minimum 12-hour practicum component focused on accessible material design.

title: Eye-tracking patterns of students with and without reading difficulties during interaction with annotated digital texts
abstract: Annotations embedded in digital texts—such as glossary pop-ups, pronunciation guides, and margin summaries—are widely recommended as UDL representation supports, but empirical data on how students with reading difficulties actually allocate visual attention to them are limited. This study used a Tobii TX300 eye-tracker to record fixation patterns of 22 students with identified reading difficulties and 22 matched controls (ages 12–14) as they read three annotated digital passages. Students with reading difficulties showed significantly more fixations on glossary pop-ups (mean 6.2 vs 2.8 per passage, p = .003) but shorter total dwell time per word in the main body text, suggesting a compensatory navigation strategy. Gaze replay analysis identified a subgroup of six students with reading difficulties who rarely accessed annotations despite lower comprehension scores, raising questions about annotation discoverability. Findings inform annotation placement and signalling conventions in accessible e-reading environments.

title: Inclusive authoring: a practical guide to designing accessible digital learning materials under UDL principles
abstract: This book chapter provides practitioners and instructional designers with a structured workflow for creating accessible digital learning materials grounded in UDL. It covers needs analysis for heterogeneous learner groups, tools for checking colour contrast and semantic markup, strategies for alternative text authoring, and procedures for piloting materials with students who have specific learning differences before finalisation. The chapter draws on practical experience from workshops delivered to over 140 teachers across primary and secondary schools in Serbia and Croatia between 2014 and 2018, summarising recurring design errors and the revisions that addressed them. It concludes with a self-evaluation checklist aligned with both the UDL guidelines (version 2.2) and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1) AA standard, offered as a practical quality-assurance tool for institutional e-learning teams.

title: Colour contrast and background complexity in digital worksheets: effects on reading speed for students with visual processing difficulties
abstract: Poorly chosen colour combinations and busy background patterns are common in digitised worksheets circulated in Serbian primary schools, yet their effect on students with visual processing difficulties has not been studied locally. This study recruited 36 students (ages 9–11) with identified visual processing difficulties and 36 age-matched peers. Participants read 16 short passages presented in a 4 × 2 design crossing contrast ratio (WCAG AA compliant vs non-compliant) and background complexity (plain vs textured). Reading speed was measured in words per minute; comprehension was assessed with four forced-choice questions per passage. For students with visual processing difficulties, WCAG AA-compliant contrast combined with plain backgrounds produced a mean reading speed 23 % higher than the non-compliant textured condition (p < .001). The control group showed smaller but statistically significant differences in the same direction. The study provides empirical grounding for existing accessibility guidelines in a population that is underrepresented in the evidence base.

title: A framework for rapid UDL auditing of existing LMS course structures in higher education
abstract: Learning management systems accumulate course materials over years without systematic accessibility review. This paper proposes a five-phase rapid auditing framework—inventory, automated check, manual check, learner-feedback probe, and remediation prioritisation—applicable within a single semester by a small institutional team. The framework was piloted at two Serbian universities, covering 47 active courses across four faculties. Automated checks using an open-source accessibility linter detected issues in 89 % of courses; manual checks revealed an additional 34 % of courses with problems invisible to automated tools, primarily in PDF attachments and embedded video without captions. Learner-feedback probes (n = 203 students) corroborated technical findings and added perceived barriers not captured by checklist approaches. The paper reports estimated remediation time per course type and discusses how remediation effort can be distributed between instructors and central e-learning support units without requiring large resource commitments.

title: Automated readability adjustment of instructional texts: comparing three algorithms against teacher-expert benchmarks
abstract: Automated text simplification tools are increasingly offered within e-learning platforms as a means of scaling UDL-consistent representation options. This study evaluated three publicly available readability-adjustment algorithms—two rule-based and one based on statistical language modelling—against a benchmark set of 60 instructional paragraphs that had been manually simplified by eight experienced special-education teachers. Texts covered science and social studies content for grades 4–6. Algorithm output was rated by five independent expert raters on vocabulary appropriateness, retention of meaning, and grammatical acceptability, each on a 1–5 scale. The statistical model outperformed both rule-based tools on vocabulary appropriateness (M = 3.81 vs 2.94 and 3.02, F(2,177) = 18.6, p < .001) but scored lower than teacher benchmarks on meaning retention (M = 3.62 vs 4.41). All automated outputs showed grammatical issues specific to Serbian morphology. Findings caution against unsupervised deployment of automated simplification and recommend human editorial review as a minimum quality gate.

title: Designing accessible video lectures: caption accuracy, speaker notes, and dual-coding effects for students with auditory processing difficulties
abstract: Video lectures have become a primary instructional format in higher education, yet their accessibility for students with auditory processing difficulties depends on caption quality and the availability of supplementary text. This study recruited 44 undergraduate students with documented auditory processing difficulties and 44 without, at two Serbian universities. Participants viewed six 8-minute video lectures presented in three conditions: no captions, auto-generated captions (mean word error rate 14.3 %), and manually corrected captions paired with downloadable speaker notes. A post-viewing retention test and a transfer application task measured learning outcomes. For students with auditory processing difficulties, the corrected-captions-plus-notes condition produced retention scores 21.7 percentage points higher than the no-caption condition (p < .001) and 9.4 points higher than auto-captions alone (p = .014). The no-caption vs auto-caption difference was not significant for this group. Control-group differences between conditions were smaller and only the corrected-plus-notes vs no-caption comparison reached significance. The study quantifies the cost of caption errors and supports the case for institutional captioning quality standards.

title: Student self-monitoring tools in UDL-aligned digital environments: a mixed-methods study across three schools
abstract: Self-monitoring is a key element of the UDL engagement principle, yet digital tools supporting it are rarely evaluated with students who have specific learning differences in South-Eastern European contexts. This mixed-methods study followed 87 primary students (grades 6–8) across three inclusive schools in Vojvodina over one academic year. Students used a purpose-built self-monitoring module embedded in the school's existing LMS: they set weekly reading goals, logged completion, and received graphic progress displays. Quantitative analysis of log data showed that students with specific learning differences used the tool less frequently than peers (mean 2.1 vs 3.6 check-ins per week, p = .002) but showed a steeper improvement in goal-attainment rates over the year (interaction F(3,249) = 5.22, p = .002). Focus groups with 24 students identified low initial self-efficacy and interface complexity as barriers. Teachers reported that the tool improved their ability to identify students needing additional support early in a unit. Revised interface recommendations are derived from student and teacher feedback.
venue: Journal of Learning Analytics

title: Cross-disciplinary teacher collaboration in UDL material adaptation: lessons from a two-year professional development programme in Vojvodina schools
abstract: Sustainable implementation of UDL in schools depends on cross-disciplinary teacher collaboration, yet most professional development programmes focus on individual skill acquisition. This paper reports a process evaluation of a two-year professional development programme delivered across nine primary and secondary schools in Vojvodina (2023–2025), in which 74 teachers from different subject areas worked in mixed-discipline teams to adapt digital materials for students with specific learning differences. The programme comprised four full-day workshops, monthly peer-review sessions, and individual coaching. Pre/post questionnaires measuring UDL knowledge, collaborative self-efficacy, and adaptation self-efficacy were administered at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Significant improvements were observed on all three scales at 24 months (d = 0.71, 0.58, 0.84 respectively). Qualitative coding of workshop artefacts and field notes identified sustained cross-disciplinary collaboration as the mechanism most frequently credited by teachers for improvements in material quality. Barriers included timetable constraints and inconsistent school leadership support.

title: Short-Term Retention of Multiplication Facts After Game-Based vs. Drill-Based Practice: A Randomised Controlled Trial
abstract: This randomised controlled trial compared retention of multiplication facts at one week and four weeks after learning in 96 fourth-grade students assigned to either a competitive card game condition or a self-paced digital drill condition. Both conditions received six 20-minute sessions over two weeks. Immediate post-test scores did not differ significantly between conditions (p = 0.41). At one-week follow-up, the game condition retained significantly more facts (mean difference = 4.2 correct items, 95% CI [1.1, 7.3], d = 0.53). At four-week follow-up the advantage was smaller and only marginally significant (d = 0.31, p = 0.08). Analysis of individual student logs showed that students in the game condition who experienced close-scoring competitive rounds had higher four-week retention than those in unbalanced games, suggesting that competitive balance may be an active ingredient. Parental reports of home practice did not differ between conditions and were treated as a covariate.

title: Developing and piloting a screencast quality rubric for use in Serbian vocational curriculum review
abstract: This paper describes the development, expert validation, and pilot application of a screencast quality rubric (SQR-Voc) designed for curriculum reviewers in Serbian secondary vocational education. Item generation was informed by multimodal discourse analysis literature and the multimodal learning framework, and an initial pool of 48 items was reduced to 22 through two rounds of expert panel review involving 11 educational technologists and vocational curriculum specialists from Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary. The rubric covers five domains: audio quality and narration clarity, visual layout and spatial organisation, caption use and text density, segmentation and pacing, and intermodal coherence. Pilot application to a sample of 80 screencasts drawn from four vocational subject areas yielded inter-rater reliability of κ = 0.76 overall. The rubric is released under a Creative Commons licence and instructions for its use in school quality assurance processes are provided.

title: Effect of hydropriming duration on germination rate and radicle uniformity in pepper seeds at 15 °C
abstract: Pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) seeds of two commercial cultivars were subjected to hydropriming for 12, 24, 36, and 48 hours at 20 °C before drying back to original moisture content. Germination tests were conducted at 15 °C and 25 °C on moistened filter paper in programmable incubation chambers. Mean germination time, germination uniformity index, and final germination percentage were recorded over 14 days. At 15 °C, 24-hour hydropriming reduced mean germination time by 2.1 days compared with unprimed controls and improved the uniformity index by 38% in the more cold-sensitive cultivar. At 25 °C differences were smaller and not statistically significant at the 5% level. Radicle length at 96 hours after sowing was 22% greater in primed seeds at the sub-optimal temperature. Seedling dry weight at 14 days was not significantly affected. The results confirm that hydropriming of moderate duration provides a practical low-cost intervention for early-season pepper production in temperate continental conditions without requiring specialised chemical inputs.

title: Osmotic potential levels of polyethylene glycol 6000 solutions and their influence on tomato seed priming efficiency at chilling temperatures
abstract: Tomato seeds (Solanum lycopersicum L., cv. Novosadski jabučar) were osmoprimed in polyethylene glycol 6000 solutions adjusted to −0.8, −1.0, −1.2, and −1.5 MPa for 48 hours at 15 °C. After priming, seeds were rinsed, surface-dried, and stored at 10 °C for 7 days before germination testing. Germination was evaluated at 10 °C and 15 °C. Electrical conductivity of seed leachate was measured as an indicator of membrane integrity. Priming at −1.0 MPa gave the highest germination percentage at 10 °C (74% versus 41% in controls) and the lowest leachate conductivity, suggesting improved membrane integrity. Lower osmotic potentials reduced final germination, possibly owing to excessive imbibition stress. A quadratic response surface model fitted to germination percentage and mean germination time data explained 81% of observed variance. The study provides quantitative guidance for selecting PEG concentration in commercial tomato seed priming protocols intended for cold-season greenhouse transplant production.
venue: Seed Science and Agronomy

title: Solid matrix priming of carrot seeds with vermiculite: moisture content ratios and germination outcomes
abstract: Carrot (Daucus carota L.) is notoriously slow and erratic in germination, particularly below 12 °C. This study examined solid matrix priming using three grades of horticultural vermiculite as the carrier matrix, testing seed-to-matrix-to-water mass ratios of 1:1:0.8, 1:1.5:1.0, and 1:2:1.2. Priming was conducted at 15 °C for 5, 7, and 9 days. Seeds were removed by sieving, surface-dried, and tested for germination at 8 °C and 15 °C. At 8 °C, the 1:1.5:1.0 ratio with 7-day priming produced the highest germination synchrony, reducing the time spread between first and last emergence by 4.8 days relative to untreated seeds. The finest vermiculite grade produced marginally better water distribution based on seed moisture content measurements. Scanning electron microscopy of seed surfaces indicated no physical damage from the priming procedure. The paper provides specific protocols for small-scale on-farm application of solid matrix priming for carrot intended for early spring direct sowing.

title: Comparison of osmopriming agents — potassium nitrate, potassium phosphate and polyethylene glycol — for onion seed germination uniformity under fluctuating temperature regimes
abstract: Three osmopriming solutions — 3% KNO₃ (approximately −0.75 MPa), KH₂PO₄/K₂HPO₄ buffer at −0.9 MPa, and PEG 6000 at −1.0 MPa — were compared for their effect on onion (Allium cepa L.) seed germination under a fluctuating temperature regime of 8/20 °C (16/8 h dark/light) simulating early spring field conditions in Vojvodina. Germination percentage, mean germination time, and coefficient of variation of germination time were measured. Additionally, seedling fresh and dry weight at 14 days post-sowing were recorded. KNO₃ priming gave the highest final germination percentage (88%) and lowest coefficient of variation (14%) at fluctuating temperatures, while PEG produced the shortest mean germination time. None of the priming treatments improved performance significantly over controls at the constant 20 °C regime. Ion leakage tests indicated that KH₂PO₄/K₂HPO₄ buffer maintained membrane integrity comparably to PEG. The study recommends KNO₃ as a practical priming agent for low-infrastructure production settings given its low cost and ease of preparation.

title: Seed ageing after priming: storage conditions and the durability of osmopriming benefits in lettuce
abstract: A practical limitation of osmoprimed seeds is the reduction in longevity during storage. Lettuce seeds (Lactuca sativa L., two cultivars) were osmoprimed with PEG 8000 at −1.2 MPa for 36 hours at 20 °C, then dried back over silica gel to approximately 6% moisture content. Seeds were stored at 5 °C/25% RH, 15 °C/40% RH, and 25 °C/55% RH for 0, 30, 60, and 120 days. After each storage interval, germination was tested at 8 °C and 20 °C. Germination percentage and vigour index were recorded. At 5 °C/25% RH, primed seeds retained 90% of their germination advantage at 8 °C after 60 days of storage, declining to 68% of the advantage at 120 days. At 25 °C/55% RH, the advantage was effectively lost within 30 days. Accelerated ageing tests after storage confirmed that low-temperature dry storage is critical for maintaining priming benefits. The findings have direct implications for the timing of priming relative to sowing in commercial lettuce production.

title: Hydropriming and osmopriming of sweet corn seeds: effects on field emergence under cool early-season conditions in Vojvodina
abstract: Sweet corn (Zea mays L. saccharata) is sensitive to soil temperatures below 10 °C at sowing. A two-year field trial (2019–2020) at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station evaluated hydropriming (24 h imbibition) and osmopriming with 3% KNO₃ (48 h at 18 °C) on field emergence percentage and emergence synchrony in early April sowings when mean soil temperature at 5 cm depth was 8.4–10.2 °C. Both priming treatments increased emergence percentage by 12–18 percentage points relative to controls across both years and cultivar types (supersweet sh2 and sugary su). Hydropriming advanced mean emergence date by 2.3 days on average; KNO₃ priming by 3.1 days. Plant height at the V3 stage was 11% greater in KNO₃-primed plots. Ear yield at final harvest showed no significant difference between primed and control plots, suggesting that the primary benefit of priming under cool conditions is improved stand establishment rather than yield gain per se. A cost–benefit analysis included for typical Vojvodina farm scale is presented.

title: Germination of primed cucumber seeds under waterlogging-combined low temperature stress: a controlled environment study
abstract: Early cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) production in unheated tunnels in Vojvodina can expose seedlings to simultaneous low temperature and transient waterlogging after irrigation or rainfall. This study tested whether osmopriming with PEG 6000 (−1.0 MPa, 36 h, 20 °C) provides tolerance to a combined stress of 12 °C and 48-hour waterlogging applied immediately after sowing. Germination percentage, radicle emergence time, and electrolyte leakage were measured at intervals over 10 days. Non-stressed primed seeds germinated at 88% versus 79% for controls; under combined stress, primed seeds reached 61% versus 38% for controls. Electrolyte leakage at 48 h was 23% lower in primed seeds under combined stress, indicating better membrane stabilisation. Image analysis of radicle curvature showed no significant geotropism disturbance from short-term waterlogging in primed seeds. The results suggest that PEG osmopriming provides measurable but partial protection against combined low-temperature and waterlogging stress in cucumber, warranting further investigation into the membrane lipid composition changes associated with priming.

title: Solid matrix priming with biochar-amended vermiculite for leek seed germination at sub-optimal temperatures: preliminary findings
abstract: Leek (Allium ampeloprasum var. porrum) seed germination at temperatures below 10 °C is slow and uneven, posing challenges for early outdoor transplant production. This preprint reports preliminary experiments testing solid matrix priming using vermiculite amended with 5%, 10%, and 20% (w/w) wood-derived biochar (particle size < 0.5 mm) as the carrier. The hypothesis was that biochar amendment would alter water retention characteristics and potentially moderate the priming microenvironment through its documented cation exchange and surface adsorption properties. Priming was conducted at 10 °C for 6 days at a seed:matrix:water ratio of 1:2:1.3. Germination was tested at 8 °C and 12 °C. At 8 °C, 10% biochar amendment produced a 9 percentage point increase in germination over plain vermiculite priming and a 29 percentage point increase over unprimed controls. Water retention measurements confirmed that biochar addition raised the matrix water potential at field capacity by approximately 0.04 MPa. Results are preliminary, based on a single cultivar and one seed lot, and replication across seasons is ongoing.

title: Drone-acquired canopy reflectance indices as in-season proxies for crop nitrogen status in winter wheat: calibration against soil mineral nitrogen and yield data
abstract: In-season adjustment of nitrogen top-dressing could reduce surplus application if reliable crop-N status proxies are available at field scale. This study evaluated five vegetation indices (NDVI, NDRE, GNDVI, CIre, and MCARI2) derived from drone-mounted five-band multispectral imagery at four growth stages (GS25, GS30, GS37, GS49 on the Zadoks scale) across eight fields (total 620 ha) in northern Vojvodina over two seasons. Indices were calibrated against destructive plant tissue N content (n = 240 sample points), soil mineral N at 0–60 cm, and end-of-season yield. CIre at GS37 explained 61% of variance in tissue N and 54% of yield variance across both seasons. A two-step prescription algorithm was derived: management zones from baseline ECa maps are used at pre-sowing, and CIre at GS37 triggers in-season adjustments bounded by ±30 kg N ha⁻¹ relative to the zone prescription. Field validation in year three reduced average N application by 14% without yield penalty.

title: Prescription algorithm transferability across farm holdings: evaluating the effect of soil-type mismatch on nitrogen use efficiency
abstract: Prescription algorithms developed on one farm are frequently applied, without recalibration, to neighbouring holdings with different soil properties. This study quantified the error introduced by such transfers using data from 22 farm holdings in Vojvodina. For each holding, a locally calibrated yield response function was treated as ground truth; the prescription error was then computed when applying functions calibrated on each of the other 21 holdings. Transfer error in prescribed N rate correlated strongly with ECa dissimilarity (Pearson r = 0.71) and less so with geographic distance (r = 0.38). Holdings sharing similar ECa ranges (within 15 mS m⁻¹) could exchange algorithms with mean prescription error below 12 kg N ha⁻¹. A simple pre-screening tool based on ECa summary statistics is proposed to identify candidate donor–recipient pairs. The findings have direct practical implications for advisory services managing large and heterogeneous farm portfolios.

title: Whole-genome SNP data indicate recent range expansion of Pythium irregulare across the central Pannonian Plain
abstract: Pythium irregulare causes significant losses in sunflower and processing tomato nurseries across central Europe, but whether local populations in the Pannonian Plain represent long-established lineages or recent introductions remains unclear. We generated whole-genome sequencing data (Illumina short-read, ~30× coverage) for 62 P. irregulare isolates sampled from Hungary, Serbia, and Romania between 2021 and 2024. After variant calling and filtering, 41,337 high-quality biallelic SNPs were retained. TreeMix and ADMIXTURE analyses indicate that Serbian isolates form a subset of Hungarian genetic diversity, consistent with northward-to-southward colonisation within the last few decades. Nucleotide diversity was lower in Serbian (π = 0.0031) than in Hungarian populations (π = 0.0049). A signature of recent demographic expansion was detected by Tajima's D in the Serbian sample (D = −1.42). Runs-of-homozygosity analysis identified two putative selective sweeps overlapping loci with predicted roles in sporangium development. These results are consistent with a range expansion model driven by intensification of irrigated vegetable production and suggest that diversity in the source population should be monitored to anticipate adaptation.

title: Cytological characterisation of pollen tube growth in the style of Capsicum annuum following cross-pollination between divergent genetic backgrounds
abstract: Incompatibility reactions in interspecific and wide-cross pepper breeding can slow or arrest pollen tube growth before fertilisation occurs. This study examined pollen tube behaviour in the styles of twelve Capsicum annuum genotypes following self-pollination and cross-pollination with two C. chinense accessions. Styles were harvested 6, 12, 24, and 48 h after pollination, softened in NaOH, stained with decolorised aniline blue, and examined by fluorescence microscopy. Self-pollinations showed unobstructed tube growth reaching the ovary within 24 h in all genotypes. In seven of twelve genotypes, cross-pollinations with C. chinense produced callose plugs arresting tubes at the mid-style by 24 h; the remaining five allowed tube progression to the ovary by 48 h. Seed set per fruit ranged from 0.8 to 68.2 in the wide crosses, correlating with tube-passage rate. These results identify five C. annuum genotypes as suitable bridge parents for introgression of C. chinense traits.

title: Comparison of hand-emasculation methods and their effect on seed yield in greenhouse-produced tomato F1 hybrids
abstract: Three emasculation methods — forceps removal at balloon stage, vibration-assisted style extraction, and thermotherapy (43 °C, 2 h pre-anthesis) — were compared for their effect on stigma integrity, subsequent pollen adherence, and seed yield in two indeterminate tomato F1 hybrid combinations produced under greenhouse conditions over one season. Stigma damage, assessed microscopically, was lowest after thermotherapy (4.2% damaged) compared with forceps (18.7%) and vibration extraction (11.3%). Pollen adherence on intact stigmas, measured by counting pollen grains under a stereo microscope, was equivalent across methods. Seed number per fruit was highest in the thermotherapy treatment (142 ± 18 seeds) relative to forceps (108 ± 22) and vibration (127 ± 16). Thermotherapy required additional equipment investment but reduced labour time per flower by approximately 35%. The method's applicability under large-scale production conditions is discussed.

title: Baseline spirometric values in a healthy adult population of Vojvodina: a cross-sectional reference study
abstract: Reference equations for spirometric indices are typically derived from Western European or North American cohorts and may not accurately represent populations in Central and South-Eastern Europe. This study recruited 812 healthy non-smoking adults (18–75 years, 423 women) from primary care centres in the Vojvodina region of Serbia, applying American Thoracic Society and European Respiratory Society exclusion criteria. Forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), and their ratio were measured using a Jaeger SensorMedics device. Age- and height-stratified reference equations were derived using ordinary least-squares regression with lambda-mu-sigma normalisation. Compared with the European Community for Steel and Coal equations, our male equations yielded FEV1 predicted values 4.2% lower on average, while female values differed by less than 1.5%. Body mass index was a significant independent predictor in both sexes. These locally derived equations reduce misclassification of obstruction and restriction in regional clinical and occupational settings.

title: Occupational dust exposure and accelerated FEV1 decline in grain elevator workers: a five-year prospective cohort
abstract: Chronic inhalation of organic dust in agricultural settings is associated with accelerated spirometric decline, but longitudinal data from South-Eastern Europe remain scarce. We followed 194 male grain elevator workers and 118 unexposed controls from the Bačka region over five annual spirometric assessments. Linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts and slopes for age were fitted to FEV1 trajectories, adjusting for height, BMI, smoking history, and atopy. Exposed workers showed a mean annual FEV1 decline of 48.3 mL/year (95% CI: 42.1–54.5) compared with 29.7 mL/year (95% CI: 25.0–34.4) in controls. Effect modification by atopic status was statistically significant; atopic workers displayed the steepest trajectories. Dust concentration, measured by personal sampling, explained 18% of the variance in slope estimates. These findings support the adoption of periodic spirometric surveillance in grain-handling occupational settings as a practical risk management tool.

title: Penalised spline modelling of height-for-age effects on spirometric reference values in Serbian school-age children
abstract: Paediatric spirometric reference values in the Western Balkans are underrepresented in international databases. We enrolled 1,043 children aged 7–17 years from twelve primary schools in Novi Sad and Subotica in a single cross-sectional session. Spirometry was performed according to ATS/ERS acceptability criteria on a Schiller SP-260 device. Penalised regression splines were used to model non-linear height and age effects on FVC, FEV1, and peak expiratory flow separately for boys and girls, avoiding arbitrary knot placement. Sex differences in FVC trajectories emerged at mean height 142 cm and were sustained throughout adolescence. Comparison with the Global Lung Initiative (GLI-2012) equations showed that GLI systematically underpredicted FVC by 3.1% (SD 4.8%) in girls aged 11–14. The derived look-up tables and R code are provided as supplementary materials for use in paediatric pulmonology clinics across the region.

title: Incorporating body composition indices into spirometric reference equation derivation: fat-free mass versus BMI as a covariate
abstract: Standard spirometric reference equations use height and age as primary anthropometric predictors, with BMI as an optional covariate. This study examined whether fat-free mass (FFM), estimated from bioelectrical impedance analysis, provides better model fit than BMI in a cross-sectional sample of 534 adults (259 women) aged 20–65 years recruited at a tertiary medical centre in Novi Sad. Separate linear regression models were compared using AIC, BIC, and leave-one-out cross-validation error. FFM significantly improved prediction of FVC (ΔAIC = −14.3) but not FEV1/FVC ratio in men. In women, FFM and BMI performed comparably. Residual analysis indicated that BMI-based models systematically over-predicted FVC in obese men (BMI > 32). These results suggest that body composition measurements, where available, should be incorporated into occupational spirometry surveillance programmes to reduce bias in impairment classification.

title: Bayesian mixed-effects framework for detecting individual-level spirometric decline beyond population trajectories
abstract: Population reference equations define normative thresholds but cannot, on their own, flag individuals whose personal decline exceeds their expected trajectory. We present a Bayesian hierarchical model that estimates individual-specific FEV1 trajectories using prior distributions informed by regional reference data derived from our earlier studies, updating estimates as serial measurements accumulate. The model was applied to a retrospective dataset of 311 workers from a ceramics manufacturing plant with at least four annual spirometric assessments. The posterior probability that annual decline exceeded 40 mL/year—a clinically meaningful threshold—was computed for each worker at each time point. Simulations showed that the approach detects accelerated decline on average 1.8 years earlier than a fixed lower-limit-of-normal criterion applied cross-sectionally. Stan and R code implementing the model are provided. This framework is intended for integration into occupational health surveillance software where repeated measurements are routinely collected.

title: Ethnic and geographic variation in spirometric norms across the Danube macroregion: a pooled multi-centre analysis
abstract: Whether spirometric reference values should be adjusted for ethnicity within heterogeneous South-Eastern European populations remains debated. We pooled cross-sectional data from eight research groups in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia, comprising 4,211 healthy non-smoking adults. A harmonised spirometry protocol and common quality-control script were applied retrospectively to all datasets. Mixed-effects regression with study site as a random effect was used to estimate fixed effects of sex, age, standing height, and self-reported ethnicity (Serbian, Hungarian, Romanian, Croatian, Roma). After adjusting for anthropometrics, statistically significant ethnic differences in FVC were found for Roma participants (−5.1%, 95% CI: −7.3 to −2.9%), consistent with a well-documented pattern in other European studies. No significant differences were found among the other four groups. A common set of equations applicable across the majority Slavic and Hungarian populations of the region is derived and validated internally.

title: Decline trajectories after SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia: six-month serial spirometry in a cohort of hospitalised adults from Vojvodina
abstract: Post-acute respiratory sequelae of COVID-19 include diffuse parenchymal changes that may persist for months, but the trajectory of recovery in Central European populations is poorly characterised. We followed 187 adults hospitalised for moderate-to-severe COVID-19 pneumonia at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina with spirometry at hospital discharge and at 6, 12, and 24 weeks. Linear mixed-effects models estimated group-average and individual FVC and DLCO trajectories, stratified by disease severity grade. At discharge, mean FVC % predicted was 72.4% (SD 11.2%); by week 24 it reached 88.6% (SD 9.4%). Recovery was significantly slower in patients aged over 55 and in those with pre-existing obesity. DLCO remained below the lower limit of normal in 31% of patients at 24 weeks regardless of age group. The time-course data and model code are deposited in an open repository to facilitate meta-analysis.

title: Automatic quality grading of spirometric manoeuvres using gradient-boosted classifiers trained on a regionally collected dataset
abstract: Manual quality grading of spirometric manoeuvres is time-consuming and subject to inter-rater variability, creating bottlenecks in large surveillance programmes. We assembled a labelled dataset of 9,847 individual spirometric manoeuvre files collected across three occupational health studies in Vojvodina, each graded by two experienced physiologists according to ATS/ERS 2019 criteria. Gradient-boosted classifiers (XGBoost) were trained on extracted waveform features including back-extrapolated volume, time-to-peak flow, and expiratory plateau metrics. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1 score of 0.87 for acceptable versus unacceptable classification and 0.79 for the full A–F grading scale. Misclassification was most common at the B/C boundary. A calibrated probability output allows downstream users to set their own acceptance thresholds. The trained model and feature extraction pipeline are released as an open-source Python package. This approach is intended to assist, not replace, technician review in high-throughput settings.

title: Stratified reference centiles for forced oscillometry technique outcomes in adults: a comparison with spirometric classification
abstract: Forced oscillometry technique (FOT) measures respiratory system impedance and is sensitive to peripheral airway dysfunction not captured by spirometry. Reference data for FOT in South-Eastern European adults are absent from published literature. We measured respiratory resistance at 5 Hz (R5) and 20 Hz (R20) and reactance at 5 Hz (X5) using an Resmon Pro device in 388 healthy non-smoking adults stratified by sex, age decade, and height tertile. Quantile regression was used to derive 5th, 50th, and 95th centiles for each outcome. R5−R20, a surrogate of frequency dependence of resistance, was significantly higher in women and in shorter stature groups. Agreement between FOT-based and spirometric classification of airflow obstruction was moderate (Cohen's κ = 0.54), with FOT identifying 22 participants as obstructed despite normal FEV1/FVC. These centiles provide a starting point for FOT integration into occupational surveillance protocols in the region.

title: Acute hyperglycaemia impairs endothelium-dependent vasodilation in healthy young adults: a controlled oral glucose challenge study
abstract: Twenty-two healthy non-diabetic volunteers (mean age 24.6 years, BMI 22.8 kg/m²) underwent a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). FMD of the brachial artery was measured at baseline, 60 minutes, and 120 minutes post-glucose ingestion. Blood glucose, insulin, and plasma NOx were measured at the same time points. A control session with water ingestion was performed on a separate day in randomised crossover order. Peak glucose at 60 minutes averaged 8.1 ± 1.2 mmol/L. FMD fell from 8.6 ± 1.4% at baseline to 5.9 ± 1.3% at 60 minutes (p < 0.001) and partially recovered to 7.1 ± 1.4% at 120 minutes. Plasma NOx decreased in parallel (from 30.4 ± 5.2 to 21.8 ± 4.6 µmol/L at 60 minutes; p < 0.001). No significant FMD changes occurred in the water control session. The magnitude of FMD reduction correlated with peak glucose excursion (r = −0.61; p < 0.01), indicating that acute glycaemic spikes transiently suppress endothelial NO production even in metabolically healthy individuals.

title: Thermoregulation precision in European pond turtles along a Danube floodplain gradient: field body temperatures and operative model comparisons
abstract: We measured cloacal body temperatures of 47 adult Emys orbicularis at four sites spanning a 120 km section of the Danube floodplain in Vojvodina during two active seasons (2008–2009). Hollow copper models were deployed at basking and aquatic microsites to estimate operative environmental temperatures (Te). Thermoregulation accuracy (db) was calculated as the mean deviation of field body temperature from a preferred range of 28–33 °C determined in a laboratory thermal gradient. Mean db across all sites was 2.1 °C, indicating moderately precise thermoregulation. Turtles at sites bordered by maize monocultures showed higher db values (3.4 °C) than turtles at sites with dense riparian vegetation (1.4 °C), suggesting that structural simplification of the landscape reduces access to suitable basking sites. Thermal quality of the habitat (de) correlated positively with the proportion of open-water edge retaining emergent macrophytes (r = 0.71, p < 0.01). These results point to riparian vegetation management as a tractable lever for supporting thermoregulatory opportunities in agricultural drainage networks.

title: Microhabitat selection and daily activity patterns of Lacerta agilis and Podarcis muralis in fragmented field-margin habitats of the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Lacerta agilis and Podarcis muralis were surveyed at 12 field-margin strips of varying width (1–8 m) and substrate composition in Srem district, Serbia, during spring and summer 2010. We recorded activity state, perch height, substrate type, and shaded fraction every 30 minutes from 07:00 to 19:00 on 48 observation days. Both species preferred south-facing stone rubble edges, but P. muralis shifted to vertical concrete surfaces at midday when air temperatures exceeded 30 °C, whereas L. agilis retreated to grass tussocks. Activity window duration for L. agilis was 6.2 ± 0.8 h compared with 8.1 ± 0.6 h for P. muralis on the same days. Occupied strips were significantly wider than random strips (mean 4.3 m vs. 2.1 m, Mann–Whitney U, p < 0.001). The results suggest that field-margin width and structural heterogeneity are stronger predictors of lizard presence than landscape connectivity at the 500 m scale assessed here.

title: Body condition, blood glucose and hepatic lipid reserves in Emys orbicularis emerging from hibernation: effects of winter water temperature
abstract: We sampled 62 pond turtles (32 females, 30 males) at two overwintering sites in Vojvodina in late March 2012 and 2013, immediately after emergence. One site had naturally buffered winter water temperatures (mean 4.2 °C) and the other experienced intermittent freezing events (mean 2.1 °C) due to shallow depth and agricultural drainage modifications. Body condition index (BCI) was lower at the colder site in both years (2012: −0.18 vs. 0.04; 2013: −0.22 vs. 0.01; p < 0.01 both years). Hepatic lipid content, quantified by Soxhlet extraction from biopsy samples, was 23% lower at the cold site. Fasting blood glucose did not differ significantly between sites but correlated positively with BCI (r = 0.54, p < 0.001). Female BCI predicted first nesting date (r = −0.62, p < 0.01), indicating reproductive carry-over effects of winter thermal regime. Habitat modifications that reduce winter water depth may therefore reduce reproductive output the following season.

title: Nest-site selection and incubation thermal profiles of Emys orbicularis in agricultural landscapes: temperature loggers in 83 natural nests
abstract: We located 83 active nests of European pond turtles in Vojvodina between 2012 and 2015 using radio-tagged females and systematic transect searches. Ibutton DS1921G loggers were placed at egg depth (4–9 cm) in 61 nests that survived to completion. Mean incubation temperature ranged from 23.8 to 31.4 °C across nests; 14 nests (23%) experienced at least one day below 20 °C, and 7 nests (11%) exceeded 35 °C for more than 48 consecutive hours. Hatching success was 68% overall, dropping to 41% in nests exceeding 35 °C threshold. Females preferentially selected south-facing disturbed-soil banks over flat crop fields (χ² = 38.4, df = 3, p < 0.001), and nest survival was lower in tilled fields than in road embankments or vineyard terraces (OR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.18–0.54). Inter-annual variation in spring rainfall explained 44% of variance in mean nest temperature through soil moisture effects. These data provide a baseline for projecting hatching success under regional climate scenarios.

title: Reptiles of Vojvodina lowlands: a field guide to identification, ecology and distribution
abstract: This book chapter covers the 11 reptile species confirmed as breeding in the Vojvodina Province, Serbia, within a multi-author regional herpetofauna volume. For each species we provide an updated distribution map derived from 4,200 georeferenced records compiled between 2005 and 2015, a description of diagnostic characters, habitat associations, and phenological windows based on temperature-degree-day thresholds calibrated from field data. Three species—Emys orbicularis, Lacerta agilis, and Coronella austriaca—are flagged as declining in intensively farmed areas based on occupancy modelling across 110 atlas grid squares. The chapter includes protocols for non-invasive population monitoring adapted to Pannonian agricultural landscapes and discusses legal protection frameworks under Serbian and EU regulations.

title: Thermal performance curves of sprint speed in three Lacerta agilis populations along a latitudinal gradient in Serbia and Hungary
abstract: Sprint speed was measured on a 1 m racetrack at eight controlled temperatures (10, 15, 20, 25, 28, 32, 35, 38 °C) for 90 adult L. agilis from three populations: Fruška Gora foothills (Serbia, 45.1° N), Bačka plain (Serbia, 45.8° N), and Somogy County (Hungary, 46.6° N). Thermal performance curves were fitted using the asymmetric beta function. Critical thermal maximum (CTmax) did not differ significantly among populations (36.8–37.3 °C), but optimal temperature for sprint speed (Topt) was 1.6 °C lower in the northernmost population (28.2 °C vs. 29.8 °C in Fruška Gora). Acclimation to 35 °C for 14 days raised Topt by 0.9 °C on average but did not close the population gap. The performance breadth (B80) was broadest in the plains population, suggesting greater thermal generalism in open agricultural habitats. These data imply limited capacity for acclimation to buffer projected warming of 1.5–2.0 °C in this region.

title: Hours lost to thermoregulatory restriction under climate warming: a mechanistic forecast for Lacerta agilis in Vojvodina
abstract: We used a biophysical model combining Fry's operative temperature framework with 30-year regional climate projections (RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5) to estimate the fraction of daylight hours during which L. agilis body temperatures would exceed the voluntary thermal maximum (VTmax = 37.5 °C) and thus require shade retreat. Operative temperature time series were reconstructed from hollow copper models deployed at 18 sites in 2016–2018 and from downscaled CORDEX-EUR-44 climate data. Under RCP 4.5, mean annual restricted hours increase from a current 1.8 h day⁻¹ to 3.1 h day⁻¹ by 2060; under RCP 8.5 the increase reaches 5.4 h day⁻¹. Losses are most severe in July and August in open ploughed-field habitats, where shade availability is below 12%. Habitat strips with shrub cover >30% reduce projected restriction by 38% relative to open margins. The model identifies mid-summer shade provision as the most tractable management intervention for preserving lizard activity time.

title: Population genetic structure of Emys orbicularis in Vojvodina drainage canals inferred from microsatellite markers
abstract: We genotyped 148 Emys orbicularis individuals from nine canal-connected wetland patches across the Vojvodina canal network using 12 microsatellite loci. Allelic richness averaged 5.2 per locus. Global FST among subpopulations was 0.14 (95% CI: 0.09–0.20), indicating moderate genetic differentiation consistent with limited dispersal across agricultural matrices. STRUCTURE analyses at K = 3 suggested three genetic clusters corresponding broadly to the Tisa corridor, the Danube-Begej confluence area, and central Bačka canals. Pairwise FST values were positively correlated with road density between patch pairs (Mantel r = 0.48, p = 0.002) but not with straight-line distance alone (r = 0.19, p = 0.12), implying roads as barriers rather than distance per se. Effective population sizes estimated by linkage disequilibrium ranged from 18 to 74 adults. Results support prioritising road-crossing structures and buffer-strip connectivity between Tisa and Danube drainage networks for genetic rescue.

title: Incubation temperature sex-ratio response in Emys orbicularis: revisiting pivotal temperature across three Pannonian populations
abstract: We performed constant-temperature incubation experiments at 25, 27, 29, 30, 31, and 33 °C using eggs from three Vojvodina populations sampled in 2018 and 2019 (total 312 eggs from 41 clutches). Hatchling sex was determined by gonadal histology. Pivotal temperature (Tpiv) was 29.4 °C (95% CI: 28.9–29.9 °C) pooled across populations, consistent with earlier European estimates, but population-level Tpiv estimates differed by up to 0.9 °C. Transitional range of temperatures (TRT) spanned 2.3 °C on average. Fertilisation rate was 82% and hatching success peaked at 30 °C (74%) and declined sharply above 32 °C (38%). Applying current and RCP 8.5 nest temperature distributions to the reaction norm predicts a shift from the current 54% female hatchlings to 71% by mid-century at the Bačka plain site, potentially skewing adult sex ratios within 20–30 years given the long juvenile period of this species.

title: Metabolic rate and water loss of Podarcis muralis under acute temperature ramp: comparison of urban heat island and rural populations near Novi Sad
abstract: We measured standard metabolic rate (SMR) by flow-through respirometry and cutaneous water loss by gravimetry in 44 adult P. muralis from two urban sites (city centre fortification walls, mean summer Tair 28.3 °C) and two rural agricultural margins (mean 25.7 °C) around Novi Sad. Animals were tested at 20, 25, 30, and 35 °C following three-day acclimation at the respective test temperature. Urban lizards had 12% higher SMR at 30 °C than rural conspecifics (0.71 vs. 0.63 mL CO₂ h⁻¹ g⁻¹, p = 0.03) and 17% lower mass-specific water loss rate at 35 °C. Body size did not differ significantly between groups. The pattern is consistent with metabolic upregulation and reduced epidermal permeability as responses to chronic heat exposure in urban populations, though we cannot exclude selective immigration. Urban populations may serve as a functional analogue for future thermal conditions in currently rural habitats.

title: Monitoring Emys orbicularis in lowland agricultural canal systems: a drone-assisted mark–recapture pilot study
abstract: We tested whether drone-based thermal infrared imaging could reliably detect basking Emys orbicularis and supplement traditional boat-based visual encounter surveys in three canal sections in Vojvodina (combined 18.6 km) during spring 2024. A DJI Mavic 3T drone was flown at 30 m altitude along each canal between 08:00 and 11:00 on six survey days. Video was reviewed by two independent observers; detection objects were cross-checked with simultaneous boat counts on the same sections. Drone surveys detected 78% of individuals confirmed by boat surveys and recorded an additional 14% of individuals invisible from the water surface due to bankside vegetation. Observer agreement was high (Cohen's κ = 0.83). Mark–recapture population estimates from PIT-tagged animals (n = 39 tagged individuals) were similar between methods (drone: N̂ = 84 ± 11; boat: N̂ = 79 ± 9). Flight time and personnel costs per surveyed kilometre were 40% lower for drone surveys. Drone-assisted monitoring appears feasible for long-canal sections where boat access is restricted.

title: Repeatability of preferred body temperature and voluntary thermal maximum in Lacerta agilis: implications for individual-level vulnerability assessment
abstract: Thermal preference (Tpref) and voluntary thermal maximum (VTmax) were measured twice, 21 days apart, in 56 adult L. agilis from a single Fruška Gora foothill population in May–June 2025. Tpref was assessed in a 1.8 m shuttle-box gradient; VTmax was determined as the temperature at which righting response was lost during a 1 °C min⁻¹ ramp. Repeatability (R) of Tpref was 0.61 (95% CI: 0.44–0.75, p < 0.001) and of VTmax was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.60–0.85, p < 0.001), indicating substantial among-individual consistency. Body mass and SVL explained less than 8% of variation in either trait. The coefficient of variation of VTmax within individuals (mean 0.9%) was far lower than among individuals (mean 3.4%), confirming that single-measurement population means underestimate among-individual variance for vulnerability assessments. We argue that individual-based thermal data are needed for meaningful prediction of population-level extinction risk under climate scenarios, and we provide a protocol for efficient single-session dual measurement.

title: Interaction between UV-A and blue light in CRY1-mediated stomatal opening in Arabidopsis thaliana
abstract: Stomatal opening is driven primarily by blue light through phototropins and, to a lesser extent, cryptochromes, but the role of co-incident UV-A radiation in modulating CRY1 activity at the guard cell level has received limited attention. We used epidermal peel assays on wild-type Col-0, cry1, phot1phot2 double, and CRY1-overexpression lines under 450 nm blue light (50 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) with and without supplementary 365 nm UV-A (0, 2, and 8 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹). Aperture widths were measured microscopically from 60 stomata per treatment per line. UV-A at 8 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ increased aperture width by 12% in Col-0 but by 31% in the CRY1-overexpressor, suggesting that CRY1 amplifies UV-A sensitivity in guard cells. The phot1phot2 background eliminated the additive UV-A response, indicating phototropin dependence. Hydrogen peroxide levels, measured by DAB staining, did not differ significantly across UV-A treatments, arguing against a reactive oxygen species mechanism.

title: Intraspecific variation in ailanthone content across Ailanthus altissima populations from three Pannonian river systems
abstract: Ailanthone content was measured in root bark samples from 18 Ailanthus altissima populations established along the Danube, Tisa, and Drava rivers in Serbia and Croatia. Fifteen individuals per population were sampled at the end of the growing season. Ailanthone was quantified by HPLC-MS/MS against an external standard. Mean ailanthone concentration ranged from 0.44 to 1.87 mg g⁻¹ DW across populations, with significant among-population differences (one-way ANOVA, F₁₇,₂₅₂ = 14.3, p < 0.001). Populations from the Drava corridor showed the highest mean concentrations and lowest within-population variance. No significant correlation was detected between ailanthone content and stand density, soil pH, or soil organic matter. Genetic differentiation assessed by eight microsatellite markers was low (FST = 0.06), suggesting that chemical variation is not primarily explained by population genetic structure and may reflect phenotypic plasticity or local microenvironmental factors.

title: Effect of experimental drought on cellulolytic and ligninolytic enzyme activities in oak forest floor litter
abstract: Rainfall exclusion shelters were installed in four 4 × 4 m plots in an oak-hornbeam stand on Fruška Gora to impose a 40% reduction in throughfall over two growing seasons (2003–2004). Four control plots received ambient precipitation. Litter samples were collected every six weeks and assayed for cellulase (CMCase), xylanase, laccase, and Mn-peroxidase activities. Under drought treatment, cumulative mass loss after 18 months was 29% lower than in control plots (41% versus 58%). CMCase activity in drought plots declined by a mean of 47% relative to controls, while laccase activity showed a smaller reduction of 28%. Ergosterol concentrations in drought litter were on average 38% lower than in controls throughout the study. Multiple regression indicated that litter moisture content alone explained 62% of the variance in CMCase activity across all plots and sampling dates. Results suggest that cellulolytic activity is more sensitive to moisture limitation than ligninolytic activity, with potential implications for carbon accumulation in forest soils under projected drier summers in continental Europe.

title: Seasonal variation in baseline antioxidant enzyme activities in Gammarus fossarum from unpolluted streams in the Fruška Gora region
abstract: Establishing seasonal baseline values for antioxidant enzyme activities in reference organisms is a prerequisite for meaningful biomarker studies. This study measured SOD, CAT, glutathione peroxidase (GPx), and glutathione S-transferase (GST) activities in Gammarus fossarum collected monthly over 14 months from three unpolluted headwater streams in Fruška Gora National Park. Metal concentrations in stream water were consistently below detection thresholds for copper, cadmium, and lead throughout the sampling period. SOD and CAT activities showed significant seasonal variation (ANOVA, p < 0.001), peaking in February–March and reaching minima in July–August, likely linked to temperature-driven metabolic changes. GPx and GST activities were less variable seasonally. No significant differences were detected among the three sites for any enzyme. The dataset provides reference ranges for each enzyme and season that can be applied in field ecotoxicology studies using G. fossarum as a sentinel species in the Pannonian region.
