title: Endophytic fungi isolated from Festuca rupicola in the Deliblato Sands: a preliminary culture-based survey
abstract: This study presents the first systematic isolation of endophytic fungi from leaf sheaths and culms of Festuca rupicola collected at five sites across the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve, Serbia. Surface-sterilised tissue segments were plated on potato dextrose agar and malt extract agar; 214 fungal isolates were recovered from 180 plant fragments over two growing seasons (2009–2010). Morphological identification, supplemented by ITS rDNA sequencing for ambiguous taxa, resolved 31 morphospecies spanning 19 genera. Alternaria, Phoma, and Epicoccum dominated the assemblage, collectively accounting for 58% of isolates. Colonisation frequency varied significantly between leaf sheaths (74%) and culms (41%). Shannon diversity index values ranged from 1.8 to 2.6 across sites. No Neotyphodium-type systemic endophytes were detected. The data establish a baseline for future community-level and metabolite-focused investigations in this habitat.

title: Comparison of endophyte communities in three co-occurring Stipa species from the Fruška Gora foothills
abstract: Endophytic fungal assemblages were compared across three Stipa species (S. capillata, S. tirsa, and S. pennata) growing in sympatry at two grassland remnants on the southern slopes of Fruška Gora, Serbia. Leaf tissue from 30 individual plants per species was processed using a standardised surface sterilisation protocol, yielding 547 isolates across 44 morphospecies. ITS and partial LSU sequencing confirmed identifications. Community composition differed significantly among host species (PERMANOVA, p = 0.003), while geographic location had a smaller but detectable effect (p = 0.04). Cladosporium and Fusarium were shared dominants across all three hosts, whereas several Periconia and Nigrospora taxa showed apparent host-associated patterns. Indicator species analysis identified five taxa as statistically associated with a single host. These results suggest partial host specificity operating within the same microhabitat, warranting further molecular and experimental work.

title: Secondary metabolite screening of Alternaria isolates recovered from Pannonian steppe grasses: antimicrobial and phytotoxic activity
abstract: Forty-three Alternaria isolates obtained from five grass species across the Pannonian steppe region were grown in liquid culture (potato dextrose broth, 14 days, 22 °C). Ethyl acetate extracts of culture filtrates were tested for antimicrobial activity against four bacterial strains (Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633, Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923, Escherichia coli ATCC 25922, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC 27853) using agar disc diffusion, and for phytotoxicity in a radish seedling bioassay. Fourteen isolates (33%) inhibited at least one bacterial target; inhibition zones ranged from 7 to 19 mm. Phytotoxic activity was detected in 22 isolates (51%), reducing root elongation by 18–67% relative to solvent controls. HPLC-DAD profiling identified tentative alternariol and tenuazonic acid peaks in eight and twelve isolates respectively, based on UV spectra and retention time comparison with authentic standards. Metabolite profiles did not correlate clearly with host grass species origin.

title: Illumina-based profiling of endophytic fungal communities in Bothriochloa ischaemum along a land-use gradient in Vojvodina
abstract: Bothriochloa ischaemum (yellow bluestem) is an invasive grass spreading into degraded steppe fragments in Vojvodina, and its endophyte community has not previously been characterised using high-throughput methods. Root and leaf tissue from 45 plants was sampled across three land-use categories (intact steppe, moderately disturbed margins, and roadsides). After DNA extraction and ITS2 amplification, 150-bp paired-end sequencing on an Illumina MiSeq platform yielded 1.24 million quality-filtered reads assigned to 387 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs). OTU richness was highest in intact steppe (mean 89 OTUs per sample) and lowest at roadsides (mean 54 OTUs). Glomeromycota dominated root tissue in steppe sites, while Dothideomycetes were proportionally more abundant in disturbed settings. The presence of B. ischaemum was not associated with a distinct or impoverished endophyte guild relative to co-occurring native grasses sampled in parallel, though several Fusarium ASVs were enriched in the invasive host.

title: Endophytic Epicoccum nigrum strains from Pannonian grasses: variability in polyketide metabolite profiles assessed by HPLC-MS
abstract: Epicoccum nigrum is among the most frequently recovered endophytes from Pannonian steppe grasses, yet intraspecific chemical variability among strains from this habitat is poorly documented. Nineteen E. nigrum isolates, verified by combined ITS–β-tubulin phylogeny, were cultivated in three liquid media (PDB, Czapek-Dox, and rice-water medium) for 21 days at 24 °C. Extracts were profiled by reverse-phase HPLC coupled to a quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer. Epicorazine A and B, flavipin, and several uncharacterised m/z ions were detected. Medium composition significantly influenced the number of detected features (ANOVA, p < 0.001); rice-water medium yielded the highest chemical diversity. Flavipin was produced by all 19 strains regardless of medium, while epicorazine production was restricted to seven strains and showed no clear correlation with geographic origin or host species. Molecular networking (GNPS) clustered 68% of MS2 spectra into eight metabolite families, four of which contained features unmatched in current databases.

title: Diversity of dark septate endophytes in roots of Festuca valesiaca and Poa angustifolia in steppe habitats of northern Serbia
abstract: Dark septate endophytes (DSE) were isolated from surface-sterilised roots of Festuca valesiaca and Poa angustifolia at eight steppe localities across northern Serbia, sampled in May and September 2019. Microscopy of cleared root segments showed mean DSE colonisation of 43% (F. valesiaca) and 38% (P. angustifolia) with no significant seasonal difference. Eighty-one isolates were obtained and assigned to 12 species via multi-locus (ITS, RPB2) sequencing; Phialocephala fortinii s.l. and Cadophora finlandica were most frequent. A germination bioassay using surface-sterilised seeds of F. valesiaca inoculated with four representative DSE strains under phosphorus-limited conditions showed modest but statistically significant root dry mass increases (9–21%) in three inoculation treatments relative to uninoculated controls. The fourth strain had no detectable effect. Results indicate that DSE in this system are functionally heterogeneous and not uniformly mutualistic.

title: Grass endophytes of the Pannonian steppe: a review of diversity studies and research gaps
abstract: This book chapter synthesises published and grey literature on fungal endophytes associated with grasses of the Pannonian biogeographical region, covering work from the late 1990s to 2022. The review covers both culture-based and metabarcoding studies, discusses methodological inconsistencies that complicate cross-study comparisons, and evaluates the evidence for host specificity, habitat effects, and seasonal dynamics. A particular focus is placed on the near-complete absence of functional studies linking endophyte community composition to host plant performance under the drought and grazing pressures typical of this habitat. The chapter also identifies major taxonomic gaps: the Chaetothyriales and early-diverging fungal lineages remain poorly characterised in Pannonian grasses. Recommendations are made for standardised sampling protocols and for extending molecular work to include non-ITS markers. The text is aimed at graduate students and researchers entering the field.

title: Temporal turnover of leaf endophyte communities in Chrysopogon gryllus across a single growing season: a monthly sampling study
abstract: Monthly sampling of Chrysopogon gryllus leaf tissue at a single grassland site near Titel, Serbia, from April to October 2022 (seven time points, n = 15 plants per time point) was used to track within-season turnover of endophyte communities using ITS2 amplicon sequencing. A total of 512 ASVs were detected across 105 samples. Community dissimilarity (Bray–Curtis) increased progressively from spring to mid-summer, peaked in July, then partially reversed in autumn. ASV richness was lowest in April (mean 31 per sample) and highest in June–July (mean 67–71 per sample). Taxon-specific temporal patterns were diverse: Cladosporium ASVs were persistent throughout the season, while several Pleosporales taxa showed pronounced midsummer peaks coinciding with low soil moisture periods inferred from meteorological records. Shared ASVs between April and October samples accounted for only 22% of the total pool, indicating substantial compositional replacement over a single growing season.

title: Antifungal activity of crude extracts from Pannonian grass endophytes against Fusarium graminearum: a screening of 120 isolates
abstract: One hundred and twenty endophytic fungal isolates recovered from Pannonian steppe grasses were screened for antifungal activity against Fusarium graminearum PH-1, an economically significant cereal pathogen. Ethyl acetate extracts of 21-day PDB cultures were tested using a microplate broth microdilution assay at four concentrations (500, 250, 125, and 62.5 µg/mL). Eighteen isolates (15%) caused ≥50% growth inhibition at 250 µg/mL. The most active group comprised five Trichoderma-affiliated isolates and three unidentified Hypocreales. Two isolates showed MIC values of 125 µg/mL. Active fractions from the two most potent isolates were subjected to HPLC-MS dereplication; preliminary results indicated the presence of gliotoxin-related masses in one and a series of unknown peptaibols in the other. Follow-up purification work is ongoing. No correlation was found between geographic origin or host species and antifungal activity.

title: Biofilm formation potential of isolates recovered from cooling tower basin water in the Novi Sad industrial zone
abstract: Sixty-three bacterial isolates were recovered from cooling tower basin water at four industrial facilities in the Novi Sad area during summer operation. Isolates were identified by partial 16S rRNA gene sequencing and screened for biofilm formation on polystyrene microplates using crystal violet staining. Forty-one percent of isolates were classified as moderate or strong biofilm formers. Pseudomonas and Aeromonas genera contained the highest proportion of strong biofilm-forming strains. Temperature-dependent biofilm assays at 25, 37, and 42 °C showed that several Pseudomonas strains increased biofilm mass by more than 2.5-fold at 42 °C relative to 25 °C, a finding relevant to warm operational conditions. Antibiotic susceptibility testing revealed that 67 % of strong biofilm formers were resistant to at least two antibiotics tested, though the study did not examine resistance genes. Results provide a culture-based reference dataset for cooling water biofilm risk assessments in the region.

title: Plant extract fractions as non-biocidal biofilm inhibitors: activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 on stainless steel coupons
abstract: Crude and fractionated extracts from six plant species collected in Fruška Gora National Park were screened for the ability to reduce Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 biofilm formation on stainless steel AISI 316L coupons under flow conditions simulating industrial water circuits. Biofilm mass was quantified by protein assay after sonication and by confocal laser scanning microscopy with SYTO 9/propidium iodide staining. Minimum inhibitory concentrations were determined to exclude direct bactericidal effects; only concentrations below MIC were used in biofilm assays. Three fractions — two phenolic-enriched and one terpenoid-enriched — reduced attached biomass by 48–72 % relative to solvent controls without detectable effects on planktonic growth rates. Quorum sensing inhibition was investigated using a violacein reporter assay; two active fractions reduced violacein production by more than 55 %, suggesting interference with N-acyl homoserine lactone signalling as a likely mechanism. No cytotoxic effects were detected in a 3T3 cell line assay at the concentrations tested.

title: Morphometric discrimination of sibling species in the Pterostichus complex using landmark-based geometric morphometrics
abstract: Four morphologically similar Pterostichus species collected from 12 localities across the Carpathian Basin were analysed using landmark-based geometric morphometrics applied to dorsal habitus images. Twenty-two landmarks were placed on pronotal and elytral outlines of 320 specimens. Principal component analysis of Procrustes-aligned coordinates separated three of the four species with less than 4% misclassification in cross-validated linear discriminant analysis, while the fourth species showed considerable overlap attributable to clinal variation. Centroid size differed significantly among species (ANOVA, p < 0.001), correlating negatively with elevation of the collection locality. The study demonstrates that geometric morphometrics can resolve taxonomic ambiguity where classical key characters are insufficient, provided specimen imaging meets defined resolution standards of at least 1,200 dpi. A protocol for standardised macro-photography of pinned beetles is proposed.

title: Freshwater macroinvertebrate population genetics in the Pannonian Basin: current knowledge and research gaps
abstract: This chapter reviews published phylogeographic and population genetic data for freshwater macroinvertebrates in the Pannonian Basin from 2000 to 2016. We synthesise findings across 12 taxonomic groups including stoneflies, mayflies, caddisflies, amphipods, and chironomids, identifying patterns of concordance and discordance in inferred recolonisation routes. Major themes include the underutilisation of nuclear markers, poor taxonomic resolution within certain genera, and an almost complete absence of seascape-style multispecies analyses. The chapter also evaluates methodological biases introduced by differential sampling effort across the region: Serbian and Ukrainian sections of the basin are substantially undersampled relative to Hungarian and Austrian sections. We outline a set of research priorities, including coordinated multi-species sampling campaigns and integration of geometric morphometrics with genetic data.

title: Gene expression responses to artificially shaded conditions in Potamogeton perfoliatus: acclimation versus stress signatures
abstract: Shade cloths providing 25%, 50%, and 75% light reduction relative to ambient were deployed over mesocosm tanks containing Potamogeton perfoliatus for five weeks in summer 2018. Transcriptomic analysis via Illumina RNA-seq (n = 3 replicates, ~40 million 150 bp paired-end reads per sample) was complemented by chlorophyll fluorescence and biomass measurements. At 50% light reduction, 1,204 genes were differentially expressed compared with full light, with upregulation of ELIP (early light-inducible proteins) and downregulation of starch synthesis genes. At 75% reduction, a further 2,109 genes were altered; stress-responsive genes including those encoding reactive oxygen species scavenging enzymes were strongly induced. Biomass decreased significantly only at 75% shading. Comparison with field transcriptomes from turbid lake sites showed partial overlap, but field plants exhibited additional upregulation of pathogen-response genes absent in physically shaded mesocosm plants, suggesting that eutrophication stress involves factors beyond light attenuation alone.

title: Chloride and ammonium as leachate tracers in an unconfined gravel aquifer beneath a closed municipal landfill in northern Serbia
abstract: A closed landfill in northern Vojvodina was monitored over a 30-month period using a network of 18 piezometers installed along three transects perpendicular to the predominant groundwater flow direction. Groundwater samples were collected quarterly and analysed for chloride, ammonium, COD, and electrical conductivity. Chloride concentrations in the proximal monitoring wells reached 1 840 mg/L in the wet season, declining to background levels (< 12 mg/L) at 210 m downgradient. Ammonium showed a more retarded plume, consistent with sorption to aquifer sediments characterised by a measured Kd of 0.31 L/kg. A calibrated MT3DMS transport model reproduced observed concentration profiles with a normalised root-mean-square error of 8.4 % for chloride and 14.1 % for ammonium. The study confirms that conservative tracer monitoring alone underestimates reactive species travel distances and recommends dual-tracer campaigns for compliance monitoring at comparable sites.

title: Passive interceptor drain sizing for leachate containment in shallow alluvial aquifers: a design chart approach
abstract: Passive interceptor drains placed perpendicular to groundwater flow are a cost-effective alternative to pump-and-treat systems at small municipal landfills where leachate concentrations are moderate. This paper develops dimensionless design charts for drain spacing, penetration depth, and gravel-pack hydraulic conductivity ratio, derived from 1 200 steady-state FEFLOW simulations spanning a range of aquifer thickness (4–18 m), regional gradient (0.001–0.015), and leachate source flux. Chart validation was performed against three field installations in Vojvodina, where measured drain capture efficiencies ranged from 84 to 97 %, compared with chart predictions of 88–99 %. Sensitivity analysis identified regional gradient and drain penetration ratio as the dominant controls on capture efficiency, together explaining 74 % of output variance. The charts are presented as a practical decision-support tool for environmental engineers without access to numerical modelling software.

title: Seasonal fluctuation of the water table and its effect on leachate mounding beneath an active transfer station in Novi Sad
abstract: Transfer stations present an often-overlooked source of diffuse leachate infiltration in urban hydrogeological settings. This study monitored water table levels at 15-minute intervals over 24 months using pressure transducers installed in six piezometers around a municipal transfer station in Novi Sad. Water table depths ranged from 0.4 m (spring snowmelt) to 3.1 m below ground (late summer), modulating the unsaturated travel time for leachate from the station floor by a factor of approximately 7. A variably saturated flow model (HYDRUS-2D) was calibrated to soil moisture profiles measured with TDR probes. Simulated annual leachate loads reaching the water table were 3.2–11.8 m³ per metre of station length depending on season. Results indicate that containment designs based solely on mean annual conditions may underestimate peak infiltration by up to 40 % in this climatic setting.

title: Geochemical attenuation of heavy metals in the leachate-affected zone of a Vojvodina sanitary landfill
abstract: Sorption, precipitation, and cation exchange control the mobility of heavy metals released from municipal solid waste leachate. Sediment cores collected from beneath the Tisa Valley landfill at depths of 1–12 m were analysed for Pb, Cd, Zn, and Ni content alongside sequential extraction to distinguish geochemical fractions. Total metal enrichment declined sharply below 4 m, with Zn showing the greatest attenuation factor (AF = 28) and Cd the least (AF = 6). Batch sorption experiments yielded Freundlich Kf values of 12.4, 3.1, 8.7, and 5.5 mg^(1−1/n) kg⁻¹ L^(1/n) for Zn, Cd, Pb, and Ni respectively. These parameters were incorporated into a reactive transport module in MT3DMS and increased predicted containment distances by 35–60 % relative to conservative assumptions. The findings support the practice of reporting geochemical attenuation factors as part of site-specific risk assessments for Serbian landfill permit applications.

title: Evaluation of permeable reactive barrier materials for ammonium removal from landfill leachate in column experiments
abstract: Permeable reactive barriers (PRBs) using natural zeolite (clinoptilolite) represent an inexpensive passive remediation option for ammonium-laden leachate plumes in alluvial aquifers. Column experiments were conducted at 20 °C using landfill leachate from two Vojvodina sites (NH₄⁺ influent concentrations 480 and 1 120 mg/L) passed through 0.6 m zeolite columns at pore velocities of 0.5, 2, and 5 m/day. Breakthrough curves were fitted using the advection-dispersion equation with a linear retardation factor ranging from 14 to 31 depending on influent concentration and velocity. Regeneration experiments with 1 M NaCl solution recovered 91–96 % of sorbed ammonium within six pore volumes. A reactive transport model calibrated on column data predicted that a 1.2 m-thick field-scale PRB would maintain effluent NH₄⁺ below 10 mg/L for approximately 4.5 years before regeneration is required under median leachate flux conditions. Cost comparison with constructed wetland treatment is included.
venue: Journal of Subsurface Remediation Research

title: Three-dimensional transport modelling of a leachate plume at a decommissioned industrial landfill using time-domain electromagnetic survey data for aquifer characterisation
abstract: A three-dimensional contaminant transport model was constructed for a decommissioned industrial landfill in the Srem sub-region, where legacy chlorinated solvents and inorganic leachate co-occur in a heterogeneous alluvial sequence. Aquifer geometry was derived from 22 km of time-domain electromagnetic (TDEM) profiles, supplemented by lithological logs from 14 boreholes, enabling interpolation of six hydrostratigraphic units without the cost of a dense drilling programme. MODFLOW-NWT with MT3DMS was used to simulate steady-state flow and transient transport over a 25-year period. Calibrated dispersivities (αL = 3.8 m, αT = 0.4 m) and retardation factors for tetrachloroethylene (PCE, R = 2.3) and trichloroethylene (TCE, R = 1.9) were obtained by pilot-point inversion against 34 monitoring well observations. Simulated plume extents matched observed 10 µg/L isoline positions within 18 m on average. The study demonstrates the feasibility of TDEM-assisted model setup for brownfield risk assessments in data-sparse environments.
venue: Applied Hydrogeology and Contaminant Transport

title: Dissolved organic carbon as a co-transport vector for trace organic contaminants in landfill leachate plumes: batch and column evidence from alluvial sediments
abstract: Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) present in landfill leachate can enhance the apparent mobility of hydrophobic trace organic compounds through colloidal facilitated transport. This laboratory study examined the effect of DOC concentrations representative of fresh leachate (380 mg/L) and aged leachate (85 mg/L) on the transport of four pharmaceutical compounds (carbamazepine, ibuprofen, diclofenac, sulfamethoxazole) through alluvial sand columns (L = 0.9 m, v = 1 m/day). Breakthrough curves showed that carbamazepine retardation decreased from R = 3.4 to R = 1.8 when DOC was increased from 85 to 380 mg/L, while ibuprofen retardation decreased from R = 2.1 to R = 1.1. Diclofenac and sulfamethoxazole were less affected (ΔR < 0.3). A two-site DOC-facilitated transport model reproduced breakthrough data with mean absolute errors below 5 %. Results suggest that risk assessments at landfills receiving mixed municipal and pharmaceutical waste should account for DOC-mediated mobility enhancement.
venue: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology

title: Mapping leachate vulnerability of alluvial aquifers in the Vojvodina region using a modified DRASTIC index calibrated against field conductivity surveys
abstract: Regional vulnerability mapping of shallow alluvial aquifers to leachate contamination supports strategic siting of waste facilities and remediation prioritisation. This study modified the standard DRASTIC index to include a waste-facility proximity factor and calibrated index weights against electrical conductivity anomalies measured in 312 monitoring wells across 22 000 km² of the Vojvodina alluvial plain. GIS layers for depth to water, recharge, aquifer media, soil texture, topography, vadose zone media, and hydraulic conductivity were compiled from existing borehole databases, soil maps, and published hydrogeological reports. Stepwise multiple regression against field-measured contamination indicators yielded revised DRASTIC weights that improved the area under the ROC curve from 0.61 (standard DRASTIC) to 0.79. High-vulnerability zones aligned well with known leachate-impacted sites and with areas of thin unsaturated zone and coarse vadose sediments. The resulting map is proposed as a planning tool for the Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning and Environmental Protection.
venue: Environmental Earth Sciences and Regional Planning

title: Coupling unsaturated and saturated zone models for leachate infiltration prediction beneath waste transfer stations: sensitivity to liner defect size and antecedent soil moisture
abstract: Liner integrity at waste transfer stations is rarely monitored with the rigour applied to regulated landfill cells, creating uncertainty in leachate infiltration estimates. This study used a coupled HYDRUS-1D/MODFLOW model to simulate leachate infiltration through partially defective compacted clay liners (defect diameters 5–200 mm, equivalent liner hydraulic conductivity 10⁻⁹ to 10⁻⁷ m/s) for three antecedent soil moisture scenarios (field capacity, wilting point, and median observed). Simulations covered a 10-year operational horizon using measured daily leachate generation data from a transfer station in the Srem district. Results showed that a 50 mm circular defect increased cumulative groundwater loading by 340 % relative to an intact liner under wet antecedent conditions, but by only 62 % under dry antecedent conditions. Sensitivity analysis ranked defect hydraulic conductivity, antecedent moisture, and leachate head as the three most influential parameters. Practical liner inspection intervals are suggested based on simulated exceedance probabilities for a 1 mg/L chloride threshold at the water table.
venue: Journal of Hazardous Materials – Subsurface and Groundwater

title: Occupational Exposure to Thermal Degradation Products During Purging Operations in Injection Moulding: A Measurement Campaign
abstract: During material changeovers in injection moulding, purging of residual polymer from the barrel generates thermal degradation products including formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, acrolein, and particulate matter. This study reports personal and area air monitoring results from purging operations at four injection moulding facilities in Serbia, covering polystyrene, ABS, and polyamide 6 materials. Sampling was conducted using NIOSH-validated methods over forty-eight production shifts. Formaldehyde concentrations during ABS purging reached 0.24 mg/m³ as a shift average, exceeding the Serbian occupational exposure limit of 0.12 mg/m³ in two of twelve measured events. Acrolein peaks during PS purging reached 0.09 mg/m³. PM2.5 concentrations at the machine operator position ranged from 18 to 74 µg/m³ depending on ventilation conditions. The study identifies ventilation adequacy, purging temperature settings, and purge compound selection as primary determinants of worker exposure. Practical control measures are recommended, including local exhaust ventilation specifications and revised standard operating procedures.
venue: Annals of Occupational and Industrial Hygiene

title: Scheduling Uncertainty in Last-Mile Distribution: A Stochastic Programming Model
abstract: Last-mile delivery schedules are disrupted by uncertain customer availability windows. This paper formulates a two-stage stochastic program in which first-stage decisions fix route assignments and second-stage decisions adjust delivery sequences after demand realisation. Scenarios are generated via Monte Carlo sampling from a dataset of 6,800 recorded delivery attempts in an urban area in northern Serbia, annotated with time-of-day, day-of-week, and building-type features. The sample average approximation method is used to solve the stochastic program, with sample sizes ranging from 50 to 500 scenarios. Computational experiments show that a 200-scenario approximation yields solutions within 2.1% of the estimated true optimum on average. The expected cost of the stochastic solution is 9.7% lower than that of the deterministic mean-value solution. Sensitivity of this gap to demand variability is characterised through a structured set of variance perturbation experiments.
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Operational Research in the Western Balkans (ISOROWB)

title: Integer Programming Formulations for Multi-Commodity Flow with Consolidation on Fixed Transport Graphs
abstract: Multi-commodity flow problems on fixed transport graphs require simultaneous routing and consolidation decisions when shipment sizes are heterogeneous. This paper systematically compares four integer programming formulations—arc-flow, path-flow, cut-set, and clique-based—on a test bed of 80 instances derived from a stylised representation of the Danube inland waterway network. Instances range from 15 to 80 commodities and 20 to 55 arcs. LP relaxation quality, branch-and-bound tree size, and CPU time are reported for each formulation using Gurobi 9.1 on a 16-core server. The path-flow formulation with a column generation pricing subproblem achieves the best performance, solving 76 of 80 instances to optimality within one hour. The paper also derives valid inequalities based on arc capacity covers and shows that adding them reduces the average LP gap from 8.4% to 3.1%.
venue: Central European Journal of Operations Research

title: Robust Timetabling for Bus Rapid Transit Under Stochastic Travel Times
abstract: Bus rapid transit systems operating on fixed-corridor networks face persistent schedule deviations caused by stochastic dwell and travel times. This chapter reviews deterministic timetabling models and then develops a robust counterpart formulation in which travel time uncertainty is captured by an interval uncertainty set calibrated from GPS traces collected over 18 months on the Novi Sad BRT pilot corridor. The robust model minimises worst-case passenger waiting time subject to headway bounds and driver duty constraints. A Benders decomposition scheme separates timetabling and driver assignment decisions. On a test network of 12 lines and 94 stops, the robust timetable increases average on-time performance from 71% to 84% relative to the deterministic baseline, at a 6.2% increase in total operating cost. Practical implementation considerations including rolling horizon re-optimisation are discussed.

title: A Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Consolidation Point Selection in Intermodal Freight Networks
abstract: Consolidation point selection determines which nodes in an intermodal freight network serve as transshipment hubs. This paper models the problem as a p-hub median problem on a directed graph and analyses structural properties of optimal hub sets using polyhedral combinatorics. A preprocessing procedure based on dominance relations among candidate nodes reduces the graph by an average of 31% across 60 synthetic instances generated from topological parameters calibrated to the Pannonian Plain logistics zone. The reduced graph is passed to a branch-and-cut solver. The paper establishes conditions under which the LP relaxation of the standard linearised formulation is tight, and identifies a class of facet-defining inequalities based on arc-disjoint path covers. Empirical results confirm that these inequalities reduce the branch-and-cut tree size by 44% on average compared to the base formulation.

title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Stochastic Load Consolidation via Distributionally Robust Optimisation
abstract: Stochastic load consolidation models require demand distribution assumptions that are often poorly supported by limited historical data. This paper formulates a distributionally robust consolidation scheduling problem in which the ambiguity set is a Wasserstein ball centred on the empirical distribution of shipment volumes. Finite-sample guarantees are derived showing that the out-of-sample constraint satisfaction probability exceeds 1 − δ when the Wasserstein radius is set according to an explicit formula depending on sample size n and confidence parameter δ. The reformulation as a tractable second-order cone program is derived for the case of polyhedral transport costs. Numerical experiments on instances with n ranging from 30 to 500 historical observations show that the distributionally robust solution achieves lower empirical violation rates than sample average approximation at the cost of a 5–18% increase in expected objective value, with the gap shrinking as n grows.
venue: Mathematical Programming Computation

title: Warm-Starting Integer Programming Solvers for Online Rescheduling in Fixed-Route Freight Networks
abstract: In online freight rescheduling, a sequence of disruptions—vehicle breakdowns, demand cancellations, road closures—requires repeated re-optimisation of a load consolidation schedule. Re-solving from scratch at each event is computationally expensive. This paper investigates warm-starting strategies that initialise the branch-and-bound tree using the basis and incumbent from the previous solve. Three strategies are compared: full basis transfer, partial basis filtering based on changed constraint activity, and incumbent injection without basis transfer. Experiments are conducted on a rolling-horizon simulation of a fixed-route network with 28 nodes over 500 simulated operating days, with disruptions modelled as a Poisson process with rate calibrated to operator incident logs. Full basis transfer reduces average re-solve time by 37% and partial filtering by 52% relative to cold starts, while incumbent injection alone yields only 11% improvement. Solution quality is statistically indistinguishable across strategies.

title: Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom
abstract: Sistemi za pretragu u realnom vremenu nad tokovima vesti zahtevaju inkrementalno ažuriranje indeksa s niskim kašnjenjem. Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja. Ovaj rad opisuje arhitekturu sistema koji obrađuje do 1 200 novinskih članaka u minuti, sa prosečnim kašnjenjem indeksiranja od 340 ms na jednom serverskom čvoru s 16 jezgara. Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije. Evaluacija preciznosti pretrage sprovedena je na simuliranom toku od 2,1 miliona članaka prikupljenih tokom 30 dana. Sistem je prilagodljiv i može se horizontalno skalirati dodavanjem čvorova za normalizaciju nezavisno od čvorova za indeksiranje.

title: Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval
abstract: Pretrained multilingual transformer models encode text at the subword level and might be expected to handle script variation implicitly, since their vocabularies cover both Serbian scripts. This paper measures to what extent this expectation holds in practice. We fine-tuned three publicly available multilingual models of different sizes on SrMIR-1, the mixed-script Serbian retrieval benchmark, and compared their nDCG@10 scores against a script-normalizing BM25 baseline and a hybrid model. Without fine-tuning, the multilingual models rank below the BM25 baseline on mixed-script queries. After fine-tuning on 12 000 query–passage pairs, the best model reaches nDCG@10 of 0.601, above the hybrid BM25 baseline of 0.587. However, for queries and documents that mix scripts within a single sentence, fine-tuned models underperform by up to 9 percentage points relative to their performance on single-script inputs, indicating that subword tokenization does not fully resolve the alignment problem. We release the fine-tuning splits and evaluation scripts.

title: A Benchmark Suite for Model Checkers Applied to Industrial-Scale Concurrent C Code
abstract: Evaluating model checkers in a reproducible way requires benchmarks that reflect the scale and structure of real industrial code rather than toy examples. We present VeriBench-C, a suite of 40 verification tasks derived from open-licensed industrial C codebases in the domains of automotive firmware, PLC controllers, and network protocol stacks. Each task is accompanied by a formal property in LTL and a ground-truth verdict established by at least two independent tools. We run five model checkers — SPIN 6.5, CBMC 5.12, CPAchecker 2.2, Seahorn, and ESBMC — on the full suite and report verification time, memory consumption, and verdict accuracy. SPIN solves 28 of 40 tasks within a 4 GB / 3600 s budget; CBMC solves 35 but produces two incorrect verdicts. We analyse the sources of divergence and provide all models, property files, and analysis scripts in a public repository. The suite is intended as a living resource for future comparisons.
venue: Journal of Automated Reasoning and Formal Methods (JARFM)

title: Uticaj izbora instrukcija u LLVM bekend fazi na potrošnju energije RISC-V mikrokontrolera
abstract: Rad istražuje vezu između strategija izbora instrukcija u LLVM bekend fazi kompajlera i izmerene potrošnje energije na mikrokontroleru GD32VF103. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na skupu od 24 sintetička i 6 realnih ugradbenih programa preuzetih iz skupa testova BEEBS. Potrošnja energije merena je eksternim strujnim šantom i osciloskopom u tački napajanja jezgra, s vremenskom rezolucijom od 10 µs. Rezultati pokazuju da alternativni obrasci pokrivanja stabla instrukcija, koji generišu do 8% više mašinskih instrukcija, u 14 od 30 testovanih programa ipak troše manje energije — u proseku 6,3% — zbog povoljnijeg rasporeda pristupa registrima i smanjenja hazarda u cevovodu. Rad predlaže modifikovani troškovni model za TableGen definicije koji uzima u obzir statičku procenu energetskog troška svake instrukcije, dobijenu merenjem na referentnoj ploči. Rezultati ukazuju da standardni model minimizacije broja instrukcija nije uvek adekvatan kriterijum za energetski efikasan kod.

title: Register Allocation Strategies and Their Effect on Dynamic Energy in RISC-V Bare-Metal Applications
abstract: This paper evaluates four register allocation algorithms available in LLVM — greedy, basic, fast, and a prototype graph-colouring variant — with respect to dynamic energy consumption on a 32-bit RISC-V core running at 8 MHz without an operating system. A corpus of 18 bare-metal benchmarks drawn from control-loop and signal-processing domains was compiled at optimisation level O2, with only the register allocator varied. Energy was logged via a dedicated current-sensing board providing per-cycle granularity. The greedy allocator reduced spill-store frequency by 22% compared to fast allocation across the benchmark set, yielding a mean energy saving of 4.1% and a worst-case saving of 11.4% on a matrix convolution kernel. However, greedy allocation increased compile time by a factor of 3.8. The paper discusses under which conditions the compile-time overhead is acceptable in a typical firmware development workflow and proposes a heuristic for selecting the allocator based on function call-graph depth and loop nesting level. Results are reproducible using the openly published build scripts and board schematics.

title: Analiza petlji u SSA formi za smanjenje energetski skupih memorijskih pristupa na RISC-V platformama
abstract: Statička analiza petlji u okviru kompajlerske IR u SSA (Static Single Assignment) formi koristi se za identifikaciju varijabli čiji životni vek prelazi granice bloka i koje uzrokuju ponavljane pristupe memoriji. U ovom radu predložen je prolaz za LLVM koji detektuje ovakve varijable u unutrašnjim petljama i vrši njihovo agresivno podizanje (loop-invariant code motion) uz istovremenu proveru dostupnosti registara. Evaluacija je izvedena na 32 funkcije iz open-source firmware-a za senzorske čvorove (temperatura, vlažnost, protokol I2C). Na GD32VF103 ploči zabeleženo je smanjenje prosečne potrošnje po ciklusu izvršavanja petlje od 3,8%, a maksimalno smanjenje od 9,1% kod petlji s više od 4 nivoa ugneždavanja. Predloženi prolaz ima zanemariv uticaj na veličinu koda (povećanje od 0,3% u proseku) i ne menja semantiku programa, što je verifikovano diferencijalnim testiranjem na skupu ulaza. Implementacija je dostupna kao open-source zakrpa za LLVM 14.

title: Comparing GCC and LLVM Code Generation for Energy Efficiency on RV32IMC Targets
abstract: A systematic comparison of GCC 12 and LLVM/Clang 15 code generation pipelines was conducted for the RV32IMC instruction set subset, focusing on energy consumption rather than execution time or code size. Forty-seven open-source embedded applications spanning cryptographic primitives, sensor fusion, and motor control were compiled with both toolchains at O2 and Os optimisation levels. Energy was measured over ten repeated runs per benchmark using a shunt resistor and a 16-bit ADC logging at 100 kHz. LLVM-generated binaries consumed less energy in 29 of 47 cases at O2 (mean difference 2.9%), while GCC produced lower energy binaries in 13 cases, with 5 statistically tied. At Os, the gap narrowed to 1.1% in favour of LLVM. Qualitative disassembly analysis identifies peephole differences in multiply-accumulate sequences and branch prediction hints as primary contributors. The dataset and measurement infrastructure are published to support reproducibility.

title: Pregled tehnika optimizacije međureprezentacije kompajlera za ugradbene procesore s ograničenim resursima
abstract: Poglavlje daje sistematičan pregled tehnika optimizacije kompajlerske IR — uključujući vrednosno numerisanje, eliminaciju zajedničkih podizraza, peephole optimizacije i prolaze za smanjenje snage (strength reduction) — s naglaskom na primenu u kontekstu mikrokontrolera s ograničenom memorijom i baterijski napajanih IoT uređaja. Posebna pažnja posvećena je razlikama između optimizacija koje smanjuju broj instrukcija i onih koje eksplicitno ciljaju smanjenje energije, pri čemu ove dve grupe nisu uvek u korelaciji. Analizirani su LLVM i GCC kao dominantne open-source platforme, uz osvrt na akademske kompajlerske infrastrukture poput MLIR-a. Poglavlje uključuje i kratak prikaz metoda za merenje potrošnje energije na nivou firmware-a, relevantnih za validaciju optimizacionih prolaza. Namenjeno je istraživačima koji tek ulaze u ovu oblast, kao i inženjerima koji žele da razumeju kompajlerske mehanizme iza alata koje koriste u svakodnevnoj razvojnoj praksi.

title: Energy-Aware Inlining Decisions in LLVM for RISC-V Firmware
abstract: Function inlining is known to reduce call overhead but can increase instruction cache pressure and register spilling, with energy effects that are difficult to predict statically. This study introduces a modified inlining cost model for LLVM that incorporates an energy term derived from offline profiling of instruction-class energy costs on a specific RISC-V core family. The model is parameterised by three core-specific constants measurable in under two hours on any target board. Evaluation on 22 firmware images for industrial sensor applications showed that the energy-aware model reduced total execution energy by 5.7% on average compared to the default LLVM inlining heuristic, with no benchmark showing an energy regression exceeding 1.2%. Code size increased by 3.1% on average. The constants for GD32VF103 and ESP32-C3 are provided in a supplementary table, enabling practitioners to apply the model without re-profiling. The LLVM pass is released under Apache 2.0 at an openly accessible repository.

title: Uticaj MLIR prolaza za smanjenje redundantnih operacija na potrošnju RISC-V čipova u senzorskim mrežama
abstract: MLIR (Multi-Level Intermediate Representation) omogućava definisanje i primenu optimizacionih prolaza na više nivoa apstrakcije, što otvara mogućnosti koje su u klasičnim jednonivojskim IR-ovima teže ostvarive. Ovaj rad opisuje implementaciju prolaza na Affine nivou MLIR-a koji eliminiše redundantne operacije sabiranje-oduzimanje u adresnim izrazima unutar gusto pakovanih petlji tipičnih za obradu senzorskih podataka. Prolaz je integrisan u tok kompajliranja koji za ciljnu arhitekturu koristi RISC-V bekend putem LLVM. Testiranje je sprovedeno na skupu od 15 programa za bežične senzorske čvorove (merenje temperature, pritiska i ubrzanja) kompajliranih za SiFive FE310 jezgro. Izmerena ušteda energije iznosi 2,1–7,4% u zavisnosti od programa, s prosekom od 4,3%. Posebno je analiziran uticaj na veličinu koda i vreme kompajliranja, od kojih je svako povećano za manje od 2%. Rad diskutuje ograničenja pristupa u slučajevima s nepravilnim pristupom memoriji.

title: Static Energy Estimation for RISC-V Binaries Using Instruction-Level Power Models: Accuracy and Limits
abstract: Static estimation of energy consumption from compiled binaries, without requiring hardware execution, would significantly accelerate the compiler optimisation feedback loop. This paper evaluates the accuracy of instruction-level power models (ILPMs) for RISC-V RV32IMC when applied to binaries produced by LLVM 16 at O2. Four published ILPMs from the literature, originally derived for ARM Cortex-M and ported by the authors to RV32IMC using characterisation measurements on GD32VF103, were compared against ground-truth dynamic measurements on 30 benchmark programs. Mean absolute percentage error ranged from 8.3% to 21.7% across models, with control-flow-heavy programs showing the largest discrepancies due to branch misprediction effects not captured by static models. A corrected model incorporating a pipeline stall penalty term reduced the best-case error to 6.1%. The paper concludes with a discussion of scenarios where static estimation is and is not reliable enough to guide automated compiler pass selection.

title: Automating Compiler Pass Ordering for Energy Reduction on RISC-V Using Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The order in which optimisation passes are applied within a compiler pipeline affects the final energy consumption of the generated binary in ways that are difficult to predict analytically. This preprint describes an offline reinforcement learning approach — specifically, a fitted Q-iteration agent trained on a corpus of 480 firmware compilation episodes — for selecting pass orderings in LLVM targeting RISC-V RV32IMC. The state representation encodes IR-level statistics computed after each pass application, and the reward signal is the fractional reduction in measured dynamic energy relative to the O2 default ordering. On a held-out test set of 60 programs, the learned policy reduced energy by 8.2% on average compared to the O2 ordering, and by 3.1% compared to the Os ordering, with a worst-case overhead of 0.4%. Training required approximately 14 hours on a workstation with 16 CPU cores and no GPU. The work is preliminary; the authors intend to submit an extended version with additional ablation studies.

title: Verification of a Wireless Sensor Network MAC Protocol Using Timed Automata: Timing Anomalies and Their Sources
abstract: Time-division multiple access protocols for wireless sensor networks impose strict timing requirements on frame transmission, acknowledgment windows, and sleep–wake cycles. This study models the MAC layer of a custom TDMA protocol implemented on CC2650 sensor nodes using a network of timed automata in UPPAAL. The model includes four node types and a base station, totaling 11 automata components with 23 clock variables. Verification targets three properties: collision freedom, bounded end-to-end latency (≤ 120 ms for a six-hop topology), and guaranteed duty-cycle bounds. Model checking reveals two previously unknown timing anomalies: a race condition between the acknowledgment timer and the slot-guard interval, and a scenario where clock drift accumulation across six hops causes a latency violation with probability estimated at 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ per hour under the assumed drift model. Corrections to the protocol specification are proposed and re-verified. The paper discusses the gap between the idealized timed automata model and the physical layer behavior.

title: A Data-Flow Framework for Detecting Array Bound Violations in ANSI C Programs
abstract: This paper presents a data-flow analysis framework designed to detect potential array bound violations in programs written in ANSI C. The approach constructs an interprocedural control-flow graph and propagates symbolic range information for array index expressions using a variant of the interval abstract domain. Widening and narrowing operators are applied to ensure termination over loops with up to five levels of nesting. The framework was evaluated on a benchmark of 34 publicly available C utility programs totalling approximately 180,000 lines of code. The analysis flagged 217 candidate violations, of which manual inspection confirmed 149 as genuine bugs or latent errors; the false-positive rate was approximately 31%. Comparison with a standard lint-based checker on the same corpus showed a 40% improvement in true-positive rate at comparable runtime cost. The paper also discusses limitations of the interval domain in capturing relational constraints between loop indices and array dimensions, motivating future extensions using the octagon domain.

title: Pointer Aliasing in the Presence of Heap Allocation: A Conservative Abstract Interpretation Approach
abstract: Precise alias information is essential for any analysis that must reason about memory safety in C. This paper addresses the problem of alias analysis when heap-allocated objects are involved, proposing a flow-sensitive, context-insensitive abstract interpretation scheme that represents heap cells by allocation-site abstraction. The approach tracks must-alias and may-alias sets through a monotone framework on the program's control-flow graph. The implementation, built on top of an internal intermediate representation derived from GCC 2.95, was tested on eight medium-sized open-source C programs ranging from 5,000 to 60,000 lines of code. Precision was evaluated by counting the fraction of pointer dereferences that could be resolved to a single abstract object; the analysis resolved 63% of dereferences with no aliasing ambiguity. The paper characterises the main sources of imprecision as function pointer calls and multi-level pointer arithmetic, and discusses conservative over-approximation strategies that preserve soundness in both cases.

title: Towards Automatic Identification of Use-After-Free Patterns Using Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Use-after-free errors constitute a persistent and exploitable class of memory vulnerability in C programs. This paper proposes an analysis that tracks the deallocation state of heap-allocated memory regions throughout program execution paths. Each pointer variable is associated with an abstract state drawn from the lattice {live, freed, unknown}, and transfer functions are defined for malloc, free, realloc, and their common wrapper variants. The implementation was integrated into an LLVM-based pass operating at the level of LLVM IR. Experiments were conducted on 22 programs from the NIST SARD vulnerability database and on six real-world CVE-correlated programs in which use-after-free bugs had been publicly documented. The analysis detected 19 of 24 known use-after-free instances across these programs. The five missed cases all involved use-after-free through function pointers stored in structs, a pattern identified as requiring context-sensitive interprocedural treatment to resolve adequately.

title: Widening Strategies for Numerical Abstract Domains Applied to Security Analysis
abstract: The convergence speed and precision of abstract interpretation analyses depend critically on the choice of widening operator. This paper conducts a comparative study of six widening strategies applied to numerical abstract domains—specifically the interval and octagon domains—in the context of analysing security-relevant properties of C programs. The strategies compared include standard threshold widening with fixed sets of constants, widening with syntactically extracted loop bounds, delayed widening up to a given iteration count, and a simple heuristic that selects threshold values from program constants appearing in conditional guards. Experiments were run on a corpus of 15 C programs selected from embedded automotive control software released under open licence. Metrics collected include number of loop iterations to convergence, percentage of definitely-safe array accesses, and number of spurious alarms. The results show that syntactic bound extraction reduces false alarms by 18–27% relative to standard threshold widening, with a runtime overhead below 12% on all tested programs.

title: Static Analysis of Format String Vulnerabilities in C: A Structural Pattern Approach
abstract: Format string vulnerabilities arise when user-controlled data is passed directly as the format argument to functions such as printf or sprintf without an explicit format specifier. Although well understood, such errors continue to appear in production C code. This paper describes a lightweight static analysis that combines control-flow-graph traversal with taint tracking to identify paths along which externally sourced string data reaches a format function argument without sanitisation. The analysis operates at the source level using a custom parser and does not require full compilation. It was evaluated on 41 C projects from a Debian GNU/Linux package archive snapshot, totalling approximately 1.4 million lines of code. The tool reported 93 candidate vulnerabilities; 71 were confirmed as genuine after manual review, giving a false-positive rate of 24%. Eleven of the confirmed cases corresponded to CVE entries not yet patched in the Debian version under analysis.

title: Memory Safety Analysis for Embedded C Code Using Resource-Constrained Abstract Domains
abstract: Applying full abstract interpretation to embedded C code poses practical difficulties: embedded targets often use non-standard memory models, fixed-size stack frames, and compiler extensions not captured by standard front-ends. This paper adapts a previously developed abstract interpretation framework to handle three common embedded toolchain extensions—segment-based memory addressing on 16-bit architectures, compiler-specific __far pointer qualifiers, and inline assembly blocks that modify memory. The adapted analysis is evaluated on driver-level C code from two industrial microcontroller families. The evaluation set contains 38 code modules with a combined size of approximately 95,000 lines. Across these modules, the analysis identifies 34 potential out-of-bounds accesses and 12 potential null-pointer dereferences that were not caught by the target compiler's own diagnostic pass. All findings were cross-validated by the firmware team of the industrial partner, confirming 29 out-of-bounds and 9 null-pointer cases as genuine.

title: Compositional Analysis of Memory Safety Across Module Boundaries in Large C Projects
abstract: Large C projects are commonly analysed either whole-program, which is expensive, or file-by-file, which loses cross-module information. This paper presents a compositional approach in which each compilation unit is summarised as a set of precondition–effect pairs over memory regions, and summaries are composed at link time to reconstruct interprocedural safety guarantees. The summary representation uses a restricted fragment of separation logic that allows efficient computation of composition. The approach was implemented as a set of LLVM passes and evaluated on four large open-source projects: two database engines, one network daemon, and one compression library, totalling approximately 600,000 lines. Total analysis time was under 40 minutes per project on a standard desktop workstation, compared to several hours for a full whole-program analysis. Summary composition missed four of 31 known bugs in these projects, all due to indirect calls whose targets were unresolvable statically.

title: Practical Lessons from Twenty Years of Static Memory Safety Analysis in Academia and Industry
abstract: This chapter reflects on practical experience with deploying static memory safety analysis tools in academic research and small industrial settings over a twenty-year period. The discussion is organised around recurring difficulties: the gap between the clean models used in analysis and the actual behaviour of compilers and linkers, the management of false positives in analyst workflows, and the challenge of maintaining analysis tools as C language extensions and compiler versions change. Concrete observations are drawn from seven distinct tool-building efforts carried out between 1995 and 2015 at the University of Novi Sad and at collaborating institutions. The chapter argues that the single largest source of analysis abandonment in practice is not technical but organisational: teams rarely allocate time to triage tool output systematically. It concludes with a set of tool-design heuristics intended to reduce triaging burden without compromising soundness.

title: Combining Interval and Congruence Domains for Detecting Integer-Overflow-Induced Memory Errors in C
abstract: Integer overflows in size and index computations are a frequent indirect cause of memory safety violations in C: an overflowed value may cause an allocation to be too small, or may serve as an out-of-range array index. This paper proposes a reduced product construction combining the interval domain and the congruence domain to track both magnitude bounds and residue constraints on integer-valued expressions simultaneously. The combined domain is more precise than either component on expressions of the form n * k + c, which appear frequently in stride calculations for multi-dimensional arrays. The analysis is implemented as an LLVM pass and evaluated on a set of 17 cryptographic library modules where integer-size arithmetic is pervasive. The combined domain eliminated 34% of false alarms that arose when using the interval domain alone on these modules, while increasing per-module analysis time by an average of 22%.

title: Admissibility of Electronically Signed Contracts in Serbian Civil Proceedings: A Pre-eIDAS Baseline
abstract: This paper examines the treatment of electronically signed contractual instruments in Serbian civil courts in the period 2006–2012, prior to the adoption of the eIDAS Regulation and its indirect influence on Serbian domestic law. Drawing on 47 published first-instance and appellate decisions retrieved from the Official Gazette database and the Paragraf Lex repository, the study codes judicial reasoning into three categories: outright rejection, conditional admission contingent on expert testimony, and full admission under the Electronic Signature Act of 2004. Results show that approximately 61 percent of contested electronic documents required supporting expert opinion before courts would assign them probative value, and that no uniform standard existed for assessing certificate authority reliability. The paper argues that the absence of a hierarchical trust framework, later provided at EU level by eIDAS, produced significant legal uncertainty for commercial parties. Findings were benchmarked against contemporaneous Croatian and Hungarian case law to situate Serbian practice within a regional context.

title: The eIDAS Regulation and Trust Service Provider Supervision: Divergence in National Supervisory Body Mandates across Five EU Member States
abstract: The eIDAS Regulation (EU No 910/2014) requires each member state to designate a supervisory body for trust service providers, but leaves organisational details to national discretion. This comparative study analyses the supervisory frameworks established in Germany, Austria, Hungary, Croatia, and Slovenia through a structured review of transposing legislation, secondary regulations, and published supervisory reports covering 2016–2019. The study identifies three structural models: telecommunication regulator–anchored supervision (Germany, Austria), dedicated digital infrastructure agencies (Slovenia), and ministries exercising residual competence (Croatia, Hungary). Audit frequency, sanction repertoires, and incident-reporting obligations differ substantially across models, creating asymmetric compliance burdens for trust service providers operating cross-border. The paper maps these divergences against eIDAS articles 17–19 and evaluates whether supervisory fragmentation undermines the mutual recognition objective. Qualitative coding of 112 supervisory guidelines and circulars was performed using NVivo 12. The findings have direct implications for Serbian candidates seeking EU interoperability.

title: Qualified Electronic Timestamps as Evidence in Commercial Arbitration: A Review of ICC and Regional Arbitral Practice
abstract: Qualified electronic timestamps issued under eIDAS article 42 carry a presumption that the indicated time is accurate and that the timestamped data have not been altered since that time. This paper investigates whether commercial arbitral tribunals operating under ICC rules and under the rules of regional arbitral institutions in Austria, Croatia, and Serbia actually apply this presumption in practice, or whether they treat qualified timestamps as merely one form of digital evidence subject to general evidentiary discretion. Analysis is based on a review of 31 arbitral awards issued between 2016 and 2021 that were accessible through institutional archives or published in legal periodicals, supplemented by structured interviews with nine arbitrators. The study finds that arbitral panels in the surveyed proceedings rarely invoked article 42 explicitly, and that the statutory presumption was effectively displaced by ad hoc expert assessment in more than two-thirds of cases. The paper proposes procedural guidance for parties seeking to rely on qualified timestamps, including pre-hearing stipulation practice modelled on English arbitral procedure.

title: Electronic Record Admissibility in Croatian Courts after eIDAS: An Empirical Assessment, 2016–2020
abstract: Croatia transposed eIDAS requirements through amendments to its Electronic Signature Act in 2017. This study presents the first systematic empirical assessment of how Croatian commercial and civil courts have handled electronic records since that transposition. A dataset of 89 published court decisions from the Zagreb Commercial Court, the High Commercial Court, and four municipal courts was assembled through the Croatian judiciary's public portal and manually coded for: type of electronic record presented, citation of eIDAS or domestic transposition provisions, outcomes of admissibility challenges, and recourse to expert witnesses. Findings indicate that qualified electronic signatures were admitted without expert opinion in 78 percent of cases once counsel explicitly invoked the statutory presumption, whereas advanced but non-qualified signatures still prompted expert referral in 54 percent of contested instances. Courts displayed considerable inconsistency in distinguishing between eIDAS signature levels. The paper draws methodological lessons for assembling comparable datasets in other Western Balkan jurisdictions, where court decisions are less systematically published.

title: Timestamp Granularity and Legal Sufficiency: Technical Standards and Their Legal Interpretation in German and Austrian Administrative Proceedings
abstract: Qualified electronic timestamps under eIDAS must be issued by a qualified trust service provider and must bind date and time to data using an advanced electronic signature or seal. However, eIDAS does not specify timestamp granularity (i.e., precision to the second, millisecond, etc.), leaving this to ETSI EN 319 421. This paper examines whether German and Austrian administrative courts and authorities have engaged with timestamp granularity as a legal question, and how ETSI technical standards have been incorporated into legal reasoning. The analysis covers 24 administrative appeal decisions in Germany (Verwaltungsgericht level) and 11 decisions by the Austrian Federal Administrative Court between 2018 and 2023, supplemented by guidance documents from BSI (Germany) and RTR-GmbH (Austria). The study finds that granularity has been raised as a challenge in procurement and land registry contexts, and that neither jurisdiction has developed consistent doctrine. The paper argues for explicit legislative reference to the relevant ETSI standard to resolve ambiguity and reduce litigation risk.
venue: Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Digital Law and Technology (CEDIT 2023), Bratislava

title: eIDAS 2.0 and the European Digital Identity Wallet: Implications for Commercial Contract Formation under Serbian Law
abstract: The revised eIDAS framework (Regulation EU 2024/1183, commonly called eIDAS 2.0) introduces the European Digital Identity Wallet and extends the scope of qualified electronic attestations of attributes. This paper analyses the implications of these changes for commercial contract formation rules in Serbian law, which remains outside the EU but is subject to gradual approximation obligations. The analysis proceeds in three steps: first, it describes the new wallet architecture and attribute attestation scheme drawing on the recitals and articles of Regulation 2024/1183; second, it maps these against the Serbian Law on Obligations and the Law on Electronic Document (2017); and third, it identifies five specific provisions in Serbian law that would require amendment to allow wallet-based identity assertions to produce equivalent legal effects in cross-border transactions involving Serbian parties. The paper also considers the practical situation of Serbian companies contracting with EU-based counterparts pending full approximation, proposing contractual drafting strategies to manage the resulting legal gap.

title: Evidentiary Weight of Long-Term Validation Formats (PAdES-LTV, XAdES-LTA) in Western Balkan Court Practice
abstract: Long-term validation formats for electronic signatures and seals, standardised in ETSI EN 319 132 and EN 319 122, embed timestamp tokens and revocation data to allow verification of signature validity after the original certificate has expired. This preprint reports preliminary findings from an ongoing study of how courts in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia handle these formats in evidentiary proceedings. Data collection involved requesting records from commercial court archives under freedom-of-information legislation and reviewing 38 usable decisions issued between 2019 and 2025. A striking finding is that in 29 of 38 decisions the long-term validation layer was entirely ignored, with courts treating the document as a simple electronic record. In six cases courts incorrectly concluded the signature was invalid because the certificate had expired, unaware that the LTV structure preserved validity. The paper outlines a training proposal for commercial judges and discusses whether explicit legislative reference to ETSI standards would reduce such errors. Full dataset and coding guide will be deposited in the University of Novi Sad institutional repository upon final publication.

title: Efikasnost B+-stabla nasuprot LSM-stablu u okruženjima s intenzivnim čitanjem: empirijska analiza
abstract: Rad poredi performanse B+-stabla i LSM-stabla (Log-Structured Merge-tree) u scenarijima u kojima dominiraju operacije čitanja, što je tipično za sisteme za proveru statusa sertifikata. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na skupu podataka od 50 miliona sintetički generisanih X.509 sertifikata raspoređenih na klasteru od osam čvorova. Merene su latencija tačkastih upita, propusnost pri 10.000 zahteva u sekundi i zauzeće memorije tokom šestočasovnih opterećenja. Rezultati pokazuju da B+-stablo ostvaruje za 18% nižu medijanu latencije pri čistim radnim opterećenjima čitanja, dok LSM-stablo pokazuje prednost u scenarijima s mešovitim operacijama čitanja i pisanja u omeru 70:30. Rad identifikuje prag od oko 40% pisanja kao tačku u kojoj LSM-stablo postaje povoljniji izbor za datu klasu aplikacija.

title: Consistent Hashing with Bounded Load for Certificate Revocation List Distribution
abstract: Certificate revocation list (CRL) distribution in large-scale PKI deployments creates uneven load across serving nodes when naive hashing schemes are used. This paper applies a bounded-load variant of consistent hashing to a simulated CRL distribution network of 32 nodes serving up to 80,000 requests per second. We define a load imbalance coefficient and show that the bounded scheme keeps it below 1.12 across all tested configurations, compared with values up to 2.4 under standard consistent hashing. The evaluation uses trace data from a regional government PKI deployment anonymised for research purposes, comprising approximately 12 million certificate entries. We also characterise the overhead introduced by the bounding mechanism, which amounts to an average of 3.1 additional hash lookups per request. The approach is shown to be practical within the constraints of commodity hardware.

title: Particionisanje podataka o statusu sertifikata u Apache Cassandra klasterima: strategije i kompromisi
abstract: Ovaj rad istražuje tri strategije particionisanja podataka o statusu sertifikata u Apache Cassandra klasteru: particionisanje po serijskom broju, po vremenskom periodu isteka i po izdavačkom autoritetu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na klasteru od 12 čvorova sa skupovima podataka veličine između 5 i 200 miliona zapisa. Strategija particionisanja po serijskom broju pokazala je najravnomerniju distribuciju podataka, ali najlošije karakteristike lokalnosti upita pri pretrazi po izdavačkom autoritetu. Particionisanje po isteku pogoduje scenarijima masovnog brisanja isteklih zapisa i smanjuje amplifikaciju pisanja za 22%. Rad pruža preporuke za odabir strategije na osnovu profila opterećenja i nudi analitički model za procenu veličine particije pri različitim stopama rasta sertifikata.

title: Reducing OCSP Responder Latency Through Probabilistic Caching with Staleness Bounds
abstract: Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responders in high-traffic deployments frequently become bottlenecks due to repeated identical queries. This paper proposes a probabilistic caching layer that serves cached responses while providing a configurable staleness bound expressed in seconds. The cache uses a counting Bloom filter to track query frequency and promotes entries to a fixed-size LRU tier above a frequency threshold. We evaluate the design against a synthetic query workload modelled on TLS handshake patterns, reaching peak loads of 45,000 queries per second. The cache achieves an 87% hit rate at a staleness bound of 30 seconds, reducing mean responder latency from 14.2 ms to 2.1 ms. We formally characterise the probability that a served response misrepresents true certificate status, showing it remains below 10^-5 at the tested revocation rates. The implementation is available as an open-source Java library.

title: Distributed OCSP Responder Architecture for National-Scale PKI: A Case Study in Deployment Design
abstract: This book chapter describes the architectural considerations involved in designing a distributed OCSP responder system intended to serve a national-scale PKI with an estimated 8 million active certificates and peak query rates of 120,000 requests per second. The chapter covers the selection of a sharding strategy based on issuer DN hash, the placement of read replicas across three geographic regions, and the consistency model chosen — eventual consistency with a maximum staleness window of 60 seconds. Failure modes analysed include responder node loss, network partition between regions, and upstream CA unavailability. The chapter also discusses monitoring instrumentation using time-series metrics at one-second resolution and describes an alerting policy calibrated to detect latency regressions within 90 seconds. The described architecture was developed as a reference design during a joint research engagement and has not been deployed in production.

title: Merenje uticaja veličine Bloom filtera na stopu lažno pozitivnih odgovora u OCSP keš slojevima
abstract: Bloom filteri se često koriste u OCSP keš slojevima za brzo odbacivanje upita za sertifikate koji sigurno nisu u kešu, ali veza između dimenzionisanja filtera i operativnih performansi nije detaljno dokumentovana u kontekstu OCSP sistema. Ovaj rad sistematski meri stopu lažno pozitivnih odgovora za Bloom filtere veličina od 1 do 64 bita po elementu, pri populacijama od 100.000 do 10 miliona zapisa o statusu sertifikata. Eksperimenti potvrđuju teorijsku krivu lažno pozitivnih odgovora u okviru 2% pri svim testiranim veličinama i pokazuju da 8 bita po elementu pruža prihvatljiv kompromis između memorijskog zauzeća i stope lažno pozitivnih od ispod 2,2% pri 10 miliona elemenata. Rad opisuje i merenu cenu osvežavanja filtera pri inkrementalnim ažuriranjima statusa i predlaže prag za planiranje potpune rekonstrukcije filtera.

title: Benchmarking Query Latency in Multi-Region Certificate Status Databases Under Simulated WAN Conditions
abstract: Cross-region replication of certificate status data introduces variable latency that is difficult to characterise from first principles alone. This paper presents a controlled benchmark of four distributed database systems — Apache Cassandra, CockroachDB, YugabyteDB, and a custom single-purpose store — under simulated wide-area network conditions with round-trip delays between 20 ms and 120 ms and packet loss rates of 0%, 0.1%, and 0.5%. The workload consists exclusively of OCSP-style point lookups and bounded-range scans over serial number ranges. We report 50th, 95th, and 99th percentile latencies at throughputs of 5,000, 20,000, and 60,000 queries per second per region. CockroachDB shows the most stable p99 latency under packet loss, while the custom store achieves the lowest p50 at 60,000 QPS under zero-loss conditions. Results include confidence intervals derived from ten independent runs per configuration. All benchmark scripts and dataset generation code are published under an open licence.
venue: Proceedings of the European Workshop on Databases and Security Systems (EWDSS)

title: Adaptivno particionisanje vremenskih serija u bazama podataka za revokaciju sertifikata sa promenljivim stopama izdavanja
abstract: Sistemi za revokaciju sertifikata u savremenim mrežama suočavaju se s visokim i neravnomernim stopama izdavanja koje otežavaju statičke strategije particionisanja. Ovaj rad predlaže shemu adaptivnog particionisanja zasnovanog na praćenju gustine zapisa po vremenskom prozoru i automatskom deljenju particija kada gustina premaši konfigurabilni prag. Implementacija je realizovana kao proširenje iznad Apache Cassandre i evaluirana je na sintetičkim skupovima podataka koji modeluju rast od 1.000 do 50.000 novih sertifikata na dan tokom perioda od godinu dana. Mereni su vreme upita, balans particija i troškovi reparticionisanja. Adaptivna shema smanjuje maksimalno odstupanje veličine particija sa 340% na 28% u poređenju sa statičkim mesečnim particionisanjem, uz prosečni troškak reparticionisanja od 1,4 sekunde po operaciji deljenja na testnom klasteru. Rad takođe analizira ponašanje sheme pri naglim skokovima broja vydatih sertifikata.

title: Comparative evaluation of temporal feature sets for frost event detection using surface microclimate loggers
abstract: Frost events cause substantial yield losses in early-season vegetable cultivation across the Pannonian plain. This study compared six families of time-series features — including autocorrelation coefficients, entropy measures, wavelet sub-band energies, slope statistics, rolling quantiles, and tsfresh-style catch22 descriptors — extracted from 15-minute air and soil temperature records collected at 23 stations over four growing seasons (2009–2012). Binary classifiers (logistic regression, k-nearest neighbours, random forest, and support vector machine with RBF kernel) were trained and evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The dataset contained 1 847 station-days, of which 214 were labelled frost days, creating notable class imbalance. SMOTE oversampling was applied before each training fold. The random forest trained on wavelet plus slope features achieved the highest F1 score of 0.81 on the held-out test set, compared to 0.63 for logistic regression on raw temperature statistics. Feature importance analysis identified minimum overnight temperature slope and 4-hour wavelet detail energy as the two most discriminative descriptors. Results suggest that simple distributional statistics underperform relative to dynamical features for frost detection at short time horizons.
venue: Journal of Agricultural Informatics and Remote Sensing

title: Soil moisture regime classification for irrigated maize using hidden Markov models fitted to capacitance sensor sequences
abstract: Accurate classification of soil moisture regimes supports irrigation scheduling in large-scale maize production. Hidden Markov models (HMMs) with Gaussian emission distributions were fitted to hourly capacitance sensor readings from 18 instrumented maize fields in Vojvodina across the 2010 and 2011 seasons. Fields were manually labelled into three moisture regimes — deficit, adequate, and excess — by agronomists using gravimetric reference samples taken at weekly intervals. A three-state left-right HMM topology was compared against a fully connected topology; the fully connected model achieved mean classification accuracy of 78.4 % against the expert labels. A baseline majority-class classifier scored 51.2 %. The study also examined the effect of sensor depth (10, 30, and 60 cm) on classification performance; the 30 cm depth provided the best balance between surface noise and root-zone relevance. HMM log-likelihood trajectories were used to detect regime transitions, with a mean detection lag of 2.7 hours relative to expert annotations. The approach requires no manual threshold setting and adapts across soil texture classes represented in the dataset.
