title: Handling sensor dropout in agricultural time-series archives: a structured comparison of imputation strategies
abstract: Long-term environmental sensor archives frequently contain gaps caused by power outages, transmission errors, and hardware failures. This study benchmarked seven imputation strategies on a 6-year hourly temperature and relative-humidity archive from 27 Vojvodina stations: last-observation carry-forward, linear interpolation, seasonal decomposition with LOESS residual filling, k-nearest-neighbour spatial borrowing, matrix factorisation, a regression tree trained on auxiliary weather model output, and a recurrent neural network (LSTM). Gaps were simulated by masking known complete records at three gap lengths: 1 hour, 6 hours, and 24 hours. Performance was measured by RMSE and mean absolute error against the held-out true values, averaged across 500 independent random masking trials. LSTM achieved the lowest RMSE for 24-hour gaps (0.41 °C) but required substantially more computation than spatial k-NN (RMSE 0.58 °C). For 1-hour gaps, linear interpolation was within 0.05 °C RMSE of the best method. The study provides practical guidance on method selection given gap length and available computational budget, and is accompanied by a Python package deposited on the institutional repository.

title: Feature stability across growing seasons for machine-learning models in precision agriculture: a replication study
abstract: Machine-learning models for agronomic prediction are typically evaluated on held-out data from the same or adjacent seasons as the training set. This study examined whether feature importances and classification boundaries remain stable when models are applied to data collected two to five seasons after training. Five previously published random forest and gradient boosting models addressing frost, drought stress, phenological stage, irrigation regime, and pest pressure were retrained on data from 2010–2013 and prospectively applied to 2014–2018 records from the same sensor networks. Shapley value profiles were computed annually for each model. Rank correlation between feature importance in the training period and each subsequent season was calculated; median Spearman ρ across models was 0.74 in year one post-training, declining to 0.51 by year five. Classification accuracy declined by a mean of 6.3 percentage points per season for models that did not undergo any retraining. Annual partial retraining on 10 % new labelled data recovered most of the performance loss. The study argues for embedding retraining schedules into operational deployment pipelines rather than treating trained models as static artefacts.

title: Drought stress onset prediction in sunflower from multi-depth soil moisture and canopy temperature: an ensemble regression study
abstract: Early prediction of drought stress onset in sunflower allows irrigation to be applied before yield-limiting physiological damage occurs. This study combined multi-depth capacitance soil moisture readings (10, 30, 60, and 90 cm) with infrared canopy temperature measured by stationary radiometers at 14 instrumented plots in Vojvodina across three growing seasons (2016–2018). The target variable was time-to-stress onset in days, defined as the first day leaf water potential fell below −0.8 MPa as measured weekly by pressure chamber. Features were extracted over a rolling 5-day window: mean, variance, linear trend, and cross-depth Pearson correlation coefficients of soil moisture, plus the canopy-minus-air temperature differential. Five regression algorithms were evaluated — ridge regression, random forest, gradient boosting, k-NN regression, and a Gaussian process regressor — via 5-fold cross-validation. Gradient boosting achieved the lowest mean absolute error of 1.3 days against measured stress onset. Cross-depth soil moisture correlation emerged as the most informative feature class according to permutation importance. The model was deployed experimentally on two commercial farms in the 2019 season and issued stress warnings between one and two days before observed wilting symptoms in 11 of 14 monitored plots.

title: Time-series classification of hyperspectral reflectance trajectories for early detection of powdery mildew in winter wheat
abstract: Powdery mildew caused by Blumeria graminis reduces winter wheat yields by 5–15 % in epidemic years in Vojvodina. Hyperspectral reflectance time series were collected at weekly intervals from 32 field plots across the 2017 and 2018 growing seasons using a ground-mounted spectroradiometer covering 400–2 500 nm at 1 nm resolution. Disease severity ratings were assigned by plant pathologists on the same weekly schedule. After dimensionality reduction by principal component analysis retaining 95 % of spectral variance, temporal features including derivatives of PC scores, area under the reflectance curve in the red-edge region, and dynamic time warping distances to a healthy reference trajectory were computed. A multiclass SVM with radial basis function kernel was trained to distinguish healthy, mildly infected (1–10 % leaf area affected), and severely infected (> 10 %) canopy states. Leave-one-season-out accuracy was 74 %, compared to 58 % for a single-date spectral classifier. The temporal derivative of the red-edge PC score provided the largest gain in F1 relative to the static baseline. The method detected onset of mild infection on average 8 days before visual symptoms were rated as actionable by field agronomists.

title: Sensor fusion from heterogeneous archive types for crop water stress index estimation: aligning satellite revisit cycles with ground sensor intervals
abstract: Satellite-derived thermal infrared data and ground-based microclimate sensor records operate on incompatible temporal grids: satellite revisit cycles of 5–16 days versus hourly ground observations. This study developed a temporal alignment and fusion pipeline for estimating the crop water stress index (CWSI) across a 3 000-hectare maize-growing area in southern Vojvodina using Sentinel-3 land surface temperature composites and a network of 19 ground stations recording air temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed at hourly resolution. Gaussian process regression with a time-warping kernel was used to interpolate ground measurements to satellite overpass times. CWSI estimates from fused data were compared against reference values computed from eddy covariance flux tower measurements at two locations. Fusion-derived CWSI tracked the flux-tower reference with Pearson r = 0.83 and RMSE of 0.07 index units across the 2019 and 2020 seasons, compared to r = 0.61 when satellite data alone was used. The pipeline processes a new satellite scene in under four minutes on standard workstation hardware. Code is available under a permissive open licence.

title: Conformal prediction intervals for agronomic event classifiers: coverage guarantees on temporally autocorrelated sensor data
abstract: Standard conformal prediction methods assume exchangeability of calibration and test samples, an assumption violated by temporally autocorrelated environmental sensor data. This paper adapts split conformal prediction to produce marginal and conditional coverage guarantees for agronomic event classifiers trained on sequential sensor records. The adaptation uses a block-hold-out calibration scheme that respects the autocorrelation structure of daily and weekly sensor cycles. Four classifiers — random forest, XGBoost, ridge logistic regression, and a 1-D convolutional neural network — were wrapped with the adapted conformal layer and evaluated on phenological stage and frost event datasets from BioSense Institute archives. Empirical coverage of 90 % prediction sets was 89.1 % to 90.8 % across classifiers and datasets, compared to 84.3 % to 87.9 % under naive exchangeable conformal calibration. Prediction set sizes were larger in periods of high sensor noise and smaller in meteorologically stable periods, which corresponds to intuitive uncertainty behaviour. The method requires no modification of the underlying classifier and adds negligible inference-time overhead.

title: Multi-site transfer learning for phenological event detection when labelled target-domain data are scarce
abstract: Obtaining labelled phenological observations at new sensor network sites is costly and time-consuming, creating a barrier to deploying trained prediction models in new regions. This study evaluated four transfer learning strategies — direct transfer, feature normalisation followed by direct transfer, fine-tuning on small labelled target sets, and domain-adversarial training — for phenological stage classifiers moving from a Vojvodina source network of 31 stations to three target networks located in Hungary (12 stations), Romania (8 stations), and Slovenia (6 stations). Transfer was tested at labelled-target-data budgets of 0, 10, 30, and 100 instances. At zero labelled target data, fine-tuning was not applicable; domain-adversarial transfer yielded macro-F1 of 0.61 on the Hungarian target compared to 0.70 for a fully supervised in-domain model. At 30 labelled instances, fine-tuning matched in-domain performance for the Hungarian and Romanian targets. The Slovenian target remained consistently harder to transfer to due to greater climatic divergence. Results suggest that investing effort in collecting 20–40 labelled instances in a new deployment region is more cost-effective than pursuing zero-shot domain adaptation for this application.
venue: Proceedings of the AgriML Symposium, Prague 2025

title: Temporal Alignment of Multi-Site Electronic Health Record Data: Challenges and a Case Study from Three Vojvodina Hospitals
abstract: When aggregating EHR data from multiple hospitals for longitudinal analysis, differences in timestamping conventions, fiscal-year resets, and local workflow patterns produce artefactual temporal patterns that can bias any time-sensitive model. This case study documents alignment problems encountered while merging discharge records from three Vojvodina hospitals (combined n = 22 600 admissions, 2010–2016) and describes rule-based and statistical correction procedures for eight identified artefact classes. A particularly common issue was duplicate admissions split across calendar-year system resets, affecting 3.1 % of records. Corrective procedures raised within-hospital event sequence consistency scores from a median of 0.81 to 0.96, measured by a proposed rank-correlation-based consistency index. The chapter situates these problems in the broader EHR data quality literature and offers a reproducible data-quality reporting template adaptable to similar regional settings.

title: Integrating satellite-derived soil moisture indices as external drift variables in microbiome kriging models
abstract: Soil moisture is a primary driver of microbial community structure, yet it is seldom measured exhaustively at field scale. Satellite remote sensing offers spatially dense moisture proxies that could serve as external drift variables in kriging. We evaluated this idea using a dataset of 64 soil samples from an organic wheat farm near Sremska Mitrovica. Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter and a derived surface soil moisture index were extracted for each sampling date and location. Universal kriging with SAR-derived moisture as drift variable was compared to ordinary kriging for predicting Shannon diversity and three indicator taxa. The external drift reduced RMSE for Shannon diversity from 0.31 to 0.22 nats and improved spatial maps visually by resolving a low-diversity patch aligned with a slight topographic depression. Variogram parameters estimated with and without the drift variable differed substantially, highlighting the importance of removing large-scale trends before estimating spatial dependence. Practical constraints related to temporal mismatch between SAR acquisition and soil sampling are discussed.

title: A Unified Regularised Framework for Absolute Risk Estimation Under Competing Risks in Clinical Genomics Pipelines
abstract: Absolute risk—the probability that a specific event occurs by a given time in the presence of competing hazards—is more directly actionable for clinical decision-making than relative hazard ratios, yet few software tools integrate penalised estimation with reliable absolute risk calibration. This paper describes a coherent framework combining subdistribution hazard modelling (elastic net Fine–Gray), baseline cumulative incidence estimation via smoothing splines, and isotonic regression post-calibration. Performance was evaluated on three cancer datasets: hepatocellular carcinoma (n = 287), chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (n = 331), and endometrial cancer (n = 214), all with competing causes of death. The framework consistently produced better-calibrated absolute risk predictions than the standard cause-specific hazard approach (mean calibration slope 0.96 vs. 0.81 across datasets). An R package, survAbsRisk, is described and illustrated, providing a reproducible pipeline from raw feature matrix to patient-level risk curves.

title: Wavelet energy features extracted from acoustic emission signals as indicators of flank wear in end milling of AISI H13 steel
abstract: This study examines the relationship between discrete wavelet transform energy features and flank wear progression during end milling of AISI H13 tool steel (52 HRC) at cutting speeds between 80 and 140 m/min. AE signals were acquired at 2 MHz sampling rate using a KISTLER 8152B sensor mounted on the spindle housing. Signals were decomposed to level 8 using the Daubechies-4 mother wavelet, and energy ratios in frequency bands 100–300 kHz were computed for each pass. Tool wear was measured offline with a Mitutoyo toolmaker's microscope at 20-pass intervals. Correlation analysis over 14 tool runs (each run producing approximately 120 measurement points) showed that the D5 sub-band energy ratio tracked flank wear with a Pearson coefficient of 0.91. A linear regression model built on three wavelet features achieved a mean absolute error of 18 µm across a wear range of 0 to 340 µm. Results indicate that high-frequency AE sub-bands are more sensitive to the abrasive wear mechanism dominant in hardened steel machining than to built-up edge formation.

title: Integration of AE and cutting force signals for improved tool wear estimation: a sensor fusion approach
abstract: Tool wear estimation based on a single sensor type is prone to false triggers caused by workpiece material inhomogeneity or chatter. This paper investigates whether fusing acoustic emission RMS with the resultant cutting force improves wear estimation accuracy in face milling of hardened AISI H11 (54 HRC). A Kistler 9257B dynamometer was mounted beneath the workpiece fixture while a wideband AE sensor was attached to the spindle housing. Data were collected over 22 tool runs. Individual models (ridge regression on AE features alone, and on force alone) were compared with two fusion strategies: feature-level concatenation and decision-level averaging. Feature-level fusion reduced mean absolute wear error from 26 µm (AE only) and 31 µm (force only) to 17 µm, using a random forest regressor with 100 trees. The improvement was statistically significant at p < 0.01 across cross-validation folds. The paper also reports the computational cost of each strategy, relevant for real-time deployment on an industrial PC.

title: Rule-based adaptive feed-rate controller driven by real-time AE wear estimates: design and shop-floor validation
abstract: This paper describes the design, implementation, and validation of a feed-rate adaptation system for CNC milling that uses real-time acoustic emission-based wear estimates to prevent tool breakage and maintain surface quality within specified limits. The controller runs on a Beckhoff CX5140 industrial PC connected to the CNC via an OPC-UA link and adjusts the programmed feed rate within a ±30% window based on five discrete wear-state thresholds. Validation was performed over 60 consecutive tool lives in production-representative milling of AISI H13 (52 HRC) at a partner workshop. Compared with a fixed-parameter baseline, adaptive control extended tool life by a mean of 23% (95% CI: 18–28%) while keeping surface roughness Ra below 0.8 µm in 94% of passes. Cycle time increased by an average of 8% due to conservative feed reductions near wear thresholds. The paper discusses threshold tuning procedure and the latency budget imposed by the OPC-UA communication layer (measured mean round-trip: 4.2 ms).

title: Empirical mode decomposition of acoustic emission for detecting the onset of catastrophic tool failure in hard milling
abstract: Catastrophic tool failure (CTF) in milling of hardened steels typically occurs with little warning and causes surface damage that is costly to recover. This study applies empirical mode decomposition (EMD) to AE signals to extract intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) that change character shortly before CTF events. Experiments were run on AISI D2 steel (60 HRC) under aggressive cutting conditions (vc = 160 m/min, fz = 0.08 mm/tooth, ap = 0.5 mm) until tool breakage. Twenty-seven separate tool runs produced CTF events at various stages of wear, providing 27 labelled pre-failure sequences. The energy ratio of IMF-3 to total signal energy showed a statistically significant rise (mean +34%, σ = 9%) in the 15 passes preceding failure, whereas IMF-1 energy remained flat. A simple threshold rule on IMF-3 energy detected impending CTF with 89% sensitivity and 83% specificity on a held-out set of eight runs. EMD required 6.2 ms per 50 ms analysis window on a Core i5 processor, meeting the 10 ms latency budget.

title: Influence of workpiece hardness variability on AE-based wear model transferability across AISI H13 batches
abstract: Wear estimation models trained on one workpiece batch often degrade when applied to another batch of nominally identical material due to hardness scatter within tolerance bands. This paper quantifies the effect by measuring hardness (Rockwell HRC) at 30 points across five AISI H13 billets certified at 52 ± 2 HRC. Hardness ranged from 50.1 to 54.3 HRC across billets and showed within-billet standard deviations up to 0.8 HRC. AE-based ridge regression wear models trained on data from one billet were tested on the remaining four; mean absolute error increased by 14–31% relative to within-billet cross-validation. Including a two-point hardness correction coefficient at the start of each billet reduced the cross-billet MAE increase to 6–11%. The paper provides a practical recalibration procedure requiring only two short test cuts and proposes hardness range and within-batch variance as reporting requirements for machining datasets published for model benchmarking.

title: Long short-term memory networks for wear state tracking using AE time-series in CNC milling: training data requirements
abstract: Recurrent neural networks can in principle model the cumulative nature of tool wear better than snapshot-based regression, but their data hunger is a practical obstacle in industrial settings. This paper investigates the minimum number of labelled tool runs needed to train an LSTM network that tracks wear state continuously from acoustic emission RMS time series during milling of AISI H13 (52 HRC). Networks with one and two LSTM layers (64 and 128 units) were trained on datasets of 5, 10, 20, 40, and 80 complete tool runs. Below 20 runs, both architectures showed high variance across five random seeds; at 40 runs the two-layer network reached a mean absolute wear error of 22 µm, comparable to the random forest baseline (21 µm). Beyond 40 runs, additional data yielded diminishing returns. The paper also evaluates transfer learning from a public turning dataset, which reduced the threshold to approximately 25 runs. Inference time for one 50 ms window was 1.1 ms on the target embedded controller.

title: Open AE-wear dataset for CNC hard milling: description, collection protocol, and baseline benchmarks
abstract: Reproducible research in tool condition monitoring is hindered by a lack of publicly available datasets collected under well-documented conditions. This paper describes the release of an open dataset comprising AE signals, cutting force measurements, spindle vibration records, and offline tool wear measurements from 96 complete tool runs during slot and face milling of AISI H13 (52 HRC) on a Haas VF-2 machining centre. Each run includes approximately 200 wear measurement points at 5-pass intervals, yielding over 19 000 labelled samples. The collection protocol, sensor specifications, calibration records, and machining parameters are fully documented. Baseline results are reported for five regression methods: linear regression (MAE 38 µm), random forest (21 µm), gradient boosted trees (19 µm), a two-layer LSTM (22 µm), and a one-dimensional CNN (20 µm), all evaluated under 5-fold cross-validation at the run level. The dataset is hosted on a Zenodo repository under a CC-BY 4.0 licence.

title: Quantifying the energy cost of adaptive feed-rate control strategies in hard milling: a machine-level measurement study
abstract: Energy consumption in CNC machining is affected by feed-rate variations introduced by adaptive controllers, but this side effect is rarely measured directly at the machine level. This paper reports spindle and axis drive energy measurements taken via a Janitza UMG 604 power analyser during 48 milling trials on AISI H13 at three fixed feed rates and three adaptive control profiles. Total electrical energy per workpiece ranged from 1.84 to 2.37 kWh depending on strategy. The conservative adaptive profile (feed reduced early and steeply) consumed 9% more energy per part than the fixed baseline while extending tool life by 19%. The aggressive adaptive profile consumed 4% more energy and extended tool life by 11%. A simple energy-per-tool-life index is proposed and calculated for each strategy. The data suggest that the energy penalty of adaptive control is modest compared with the material cost savings from longer tool life, but should be included in full cost analyses.

title: AE-based detection of coating delamination in TiAlN-coated end mills during early-phase milling of hardened steel
abstract: TiAlN coatings on cemented carbide end mills delaminate progressively under thermal and mechanical cycling, but conventional wear metrics such as flank wear VB do not capture the onset of delamination well. This paper investigates whether AE frequency-domain features can distinguish intact, partially delaminated, and fully delaminated tool states during milling of AISI H13 (52 HRC). Tool state was verified after each run by scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. Power spectral density estimates in the 250–400 kHz band showed a statistically significant shift (mean +2.1 dB, p = 0.003, n = 31 runs) when partial delamination was present, compared with intact coatings. A three-class linear discriminant classifier trained on four spectral features achieved 82% overall accuracy on a 12-run test set. The paper proposes that spectral AE monitoring be used as a complementary check alongside VB measurement in coating performance evaluation studies.

title: Frequency-selective AE filtering for suppression of coolant-flow noise in real-time tool wear monitoring
abstract: High-pressure coolant delivery generates broadband acoustic noise that overlaps the frequency ranges used for tool wear estimation, degrading model accuracy when switching between dry and wet cutting conditions. This paper characterises the power spectral profile of coolant noise at three supply pressures (20, 40, 70 bar) using a calibrated AE sensor in the absence of cutting, then designs a set of finite impulse response band-stop filters targeting the identified noise bands. The filtered features are evaluated in a wear estimation experiment on AISI H13 (52 HRC) under all three coolant pressures across 30 tool runs. Without filtering, random forest MAE rose from 21 µm (dry baseline) to 38 µm at 70 bar coolant pressure. With the proposed filters applied, MAE at 70 bar was reduced to 25 µm, a 34% improvement. Filter design parameters and a Python implementation are provided in supplementary material. The study is relevant to shops that use the same monitoring system across multiple machining conditions.

title: Hyperspectral Imaging in Industrial Waste Sorting: Sensor Technologies, Processing Chains, and Open Challenges
abstract: This book chapter surveys the state of hyperspectral near-infrared sensing as applied to solid waste sorting, covering sensor architectures (pushbroom, snapshot, acousto-optic), illumination strategies, and computational pipelines from raw datacube to actuation signal. The chapter discusses calibration protocols, spectral library management, and the impact of particle geometry, surface gloss, and moisture on identification accuracy. Processing approaches reviewed include classical chemometric methods, support vector machines, and early convolutional architectures. Deployment constraints specific to industrial sorting — throughput requirements, dust and vibration, low-latency control interfaces — are analysed alongside reported field performance figures from 14 published studies. The chapter concludes with a structured discussion of open problems: black polymer identification, multi-layer laminate discrimination, and real-time adaptation to feed composition drift. Written for an audience of automation engineers and environmental technologists, it bridges laboratory research and industrial practice.

title: Transmissibility characterisation of commercial wire-rope isolators under combined static preload and lateral excitation
abstract: Wire-rope isolators are widely used for passive vibration isolation, but their published stiffness values are typically derived from purely axial loading conditions. This experimental study examines how simultaneous static vertical preload and horizontal dynamic excitation alter the transmissibility of three commercial wire-rope isolator types with wire diameters of 4 mm, 6 mm, and 8 mm. Specimens were tested on a custom-built single-axis shaker table using swept-sine excitation from 2 Hz to 200 Hz at three preload levels corresponding to 25 %, 50 %, and 75 % of rated capacity. Transmissibility curves were computed from accelerometer pairs above and below each isolator. Resonance frequencies shifted between 8 Hz and 23 Hz depending on preload, and insertion loss at 50 Hz ranged from 14 dB to 27 dB. A Voigt model was fitted to each configuration; fitted damping ratios varied from 0.06 to 0.19. The data indicate that isolator selection based solely on axial stiffness catalogues can result in under-isolation by up to 9 dB in lateral directions relevant to optical alignment stability.

title: Dominance rank and its relationship to feeding duration in group-housed Simmental bulls
abstract: Thirty-two growing Simmental bulls were allocated to four pens of eight animals each and observed over a 70-day finishing period. Dominance hierarchies were established using the David's score method applied to recorded agonistic interactions during the first two weeks. Individual feeding durations were measured using RFID-tagged ear tags at six electronic feed bins per pen. Subordinate animals (ranks 6–8) spent on average 18% less time at the feeder than dominant animals (ranks 1–3), and this difference was statistically significant (p < 0.01). Average daily gain for the lowest-ranking third of animals was 12% lower than for the highest-ranking third (1.09 vs. 1.24 kg/day). A moderate positive correlation (r = 0.54) was found between dominance rank and cumulative feed intake. Results suggest that pen composition and access to feeders disproportionately constrain subordinate individuals, with measurable consequences for production performance.

title: Effect of linear feeder length per animal on agonistic behaviour and growth in finishing beef bulls
abstract: An experiment was conducted at the University of Novi Sad experimental cattle unit using 64 Charolais × Simmental crossbred bulls divided into eight pens. Four pens were equipped with 60 cm of linear feeder space per animal and four with 90 cm per animal, all other conditions being equal. Behaviour was recorded by continuous video during three 5-day observation windows at the start, middle, and end of a 90-day trial. Pens with 60 cm feeder space showed 34% more displacements per hour at the feeder than pens with 90 cm (p < 0.001). Feed consumption uniformity, expressed as the coefficient of variation of individual intakes within pens, was higher in restricted-space pens (CV = 22%) compared with ample-space pens (CV = 14%). Average daily gain was 1.18 kg in restricted pens versus 1.31 kg in ample pens. Body-weight variation within pens widened over time more in restricted-space conditions.

title: Social hierarchy stability over consecutive feeding periods in indoor-housed beef bulls
abstract: This study examined how stable dominance hierarchies remain across three consecutive 30-day periods in pens of beef bulls under standard indoor management. Forty-eight Hereford bulls were housed in six pens of eight animals; agonistic interactions were recorded by scan sampling at 5-minute intervals over three 48-hour observation sessions per period. Landau's linearity index was calculated per pen and per period. Hierarchies were highly linear (h′ > 0.75) in all pens and remained consistent across periods, with a mean rank-order correlation between consecutive periods of rs = 0.88. Weight gain showed no significant change across periods, indicating that once a stable hierarchy is formed, its impact on growth is relatively constant rather than cumulative. Minor rank reversals occurred predominantly in the middle-rank animals and were not associated with changes in body weight. These findings have implications for interpreting results from short observation windows in applied studies.

title: Pen shape and spatial arrangement of feeding areas: consequences for movement patterns and feeding access in bulls
abstract: Two pen geometries — elongated rectangular (3:1 length-to-width ratio) and square — were compared in a crossover study using 40 Simmental bulls. Feeding troughs were placed along one short wall in the rectangular pens and along one full wall in the square pens, resulting in identical feeder length per animal. Animal positions were recorded via ceiling-mounted video cameras and digitised using semi-automated tracking software. Bulls in rectangular pens travelled on average 23% greater daily distances within the pen (p < 0.05) and showed higher rates of feeder approach per hour. Despite similar total feeder access time, feeding events were more fragmented in rectangular pens (mean bout duration 4.1 min) than in square pens (5.6 min). Dominant animals in rectangular pens controlled a proportionally larger feeder segment. No significant difference in average daily gain was detected over the 60-day trial, though a trend toward lower gain variance was observed in square pens.

title: Body weight at regrouping as a predictor of rank acquisition and subsequent feeding behaviour in growing beef bulls
abstract: Animals are routinely regrouped in commercial beef production, yet the determinants of post-regrouping rank are not well characterised. Eighty Simmental bulls were weighed individually and then formed into ten new groups of eight, each group spanning a body-weight range of approximately 30 kg. Agonistic interactions were recorded continuously for the first seven days after regrouping and ranks were determined by the priority-of-access method at a single-space feeder. Body weight at regrouping was the strongest single predictor of final rank (r = −0.71; heavier animals ranked higher). In pens where the body-weight range was narrowest (< 20 kg), hierarchies took longer to stabilise and rank reversals were more frequent. Bulls that fell in rank relative to their pre-regrouping position showed reduced feeding time (−16%) and reduced average daily gain over 30 days post-regrouping compared with bulls that rose in rank. These results argue for weight-graded grouping strategies at regrouping.

title: Feed bunk management in practice: a survey of beef bull fattening units in Vojvodina
abstract: A questionnaire-based survey combined with on-farm observations was conducted at 34 beef fattening operations in Vojvodina housing a total of 6,200 bulls. Data were collected on pen dimensions, stocking density, feeder type, feeder length per animal, feeding frequency, and management practices relating to group composition. Feeder space per animal ranged from 32 to 95 cm across farms, with a median of 58 cm, falling below widely cited recommendations of 75–80 cm. Farms using ad libitum silage-based systems tended to provide less feeder space and reported higher observed displacement rates. Pen size ranged from 4 to 26 animals per group. Farmers with smaller groups (≤ 8) reported fewer injuries and lower within-pen variation in slaughter weight. Only 11 of 34 farms recorded individual weights at intervals shorter than 60 days, limiting producers' ability to detect growth suppression in subordinate animals. The survey data provide a baseline for extension and improvement recommendations.

title: Partition walls inside pens: effects on sub-group formation and feeding behaviour of bulls at high stocking densities
abstract: At commercial stocking densities (above 10 animals per pen), social complexity increases and feeding competition may intensify. This experiment tested whether installing a single central partition wall dividing a pen of 16 bulls into two visually connected but physically separated sub-areas of 8 changed feeding behaviour and growth. Sixteen pens of 16 bulls were assigned to partitioned or non-partitioned treatment. Animals in partitioned pens showed significantly lower rates of active displacement at the feeder (2.3 vs. 3.8 per animal per hour; p < 0.01) and spent more total time feeding per day (198 vs. 172 min; p < 0.05). Coefficient of variation in average daily gain within pens was reduced from 18% to 12% with partitioning. No significant difference in mean daily gain was found, but the reduction in within-pen variation suggests that partitions primarily benefit lower-ranking individuals. Installation cost was estimated at approximately 12 EUR per animal place, which is recoverable given reduced performance variability.

title: Behavioural indicators of chronic subordination stress in finishing beef bulls and their correlation with cortisol and growth parameters
abstract: Chronic social subordination is hypothesised to suppress growth through neuroendocrine pathways, but evidence in finishing bulls remains limited. Thirty-two Simmental bulls were ranked by dominance score after two weeks of cohabitation and assigned to low-rank (positions 6–8 in groups of 8) or high-rank (positions 1–3) categories. Blood samples for cortisol analysis were collected via jugular venepuncture on days 30, 60, and 90 of a 90-day finishing period. Low-rank bulls showed elevated mean serum cortisol (28.4 vs. 19.6 nmol/L; p < 0.01), higher lying bout fragmentation (more frequent but shorter bouts), and reduced daily gain (1.07 vs. 1.29 kg/day). A path analysis model indicated that approximately 40% of the growth difference between rank categories was mediated by cortisol-related pathways, with the remainder attributable directly to reduced feed intake. Pen modifications that alleviate competition may therefore act through both behavioural and physiological routes.

title: Camera-based activity monitoring versus direct observation for quantifying feeding competition in beef bull pens: a method comparison
abstract: As automated video analysis becomes more accessible, it is important to establish how closely it agrees with trained human observers for quantifying feeding competition. In four pens of 8 Simmental bulls, agonistic interactions at the feeder were scored simultaneously by continuous focal sampling (two trained observers) and by a commercial activity-monitoring camera system with built-in motion-event detection during three 48-hour sessions. Agreement between methods was assessed by intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland–Altman analysis. The camera system detected 91% of displacements identified by observers but overclassified 14% of non-agonistic pen entries as displacement events, yielding a slight positive bias of 1.9 events per pen per hour. Rank orders derived from the two methods correlated strongly (rs = 0.92). The camera system underperformed at low light levels and in the hour after morning feeding when animal density at the feeder was highest. Results suggest camera-based systems are adequate for group-level metrics but require calibration before use in individual-rank studies.

title: Life-cycle inventory of heatset web-offset printing: a gate-to-grave approach for a commercial newspaper insert
abstract: This study established a life-cycle inventory (LCI) for a heatset web-offset job producing 50,000 copies of a 16-page newspaper insert on 52 g/m² LWC paper. Data were collected directly from a printing house in Novi Sad over three production runs. Inventory boundaries extended from ink and substrate delivery to post-consumer waste collection. Energy consumption per functional unit (1,000 printed sheets A3) was measured at 4.7 kWh, with isopropyl alcohol (IPA) dampening solution contributing 18% of total volatile organic compound emissions. Ink coverage averaged 34% across all four CMYK stations. The global warming potential (GWP) was calculated at 2.3 kg CO₂-eq per functional unit using the CML 2002 methodology in SimaPro 8. Paper production dominated the impact profile at 61% of GWP, followed by energy supply at 22%. The results indicate that substrate choice represents the highest leverage point for environmental improvement in short-run newspaper supplement production.

title: Comparison of mineral-oil and vegetable-oil based offset inks across three environmental impact categories
abstract: Mineral-oil and linseed-oil based offset inks were compared using an attributional LCA framework, evaluating three impact categories: GWP100, photochemical ozone creation potential (POCP), and freshwater eutrophication potential. Ink samples from two European suppliers were characterised for their pigment loading, oil fraction composition, and photoinitiator content. Production data for each ink type were sourced from published ecoinvent 3.4 datasets supplemented by supplier environmental product declarations. A common functional unit of 1 kg of ink deposited on coated paper at standard coverage was applied. Vegetable-oil based inks showed a 29% reduction in GWP100 relative to mineral-oil inks but a 14% increase in freshwater eutrophication due to agricultural upstream processes. POCP results were broadly comparable. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that the agricultural cultivation stage accounts for most of the uncertainty in the vegetable-oil scenario. The findings support selective substitution of mineral-oil inks where GWP reduction is prioritised, while flagging eutrophication trade-offs that are frequently overlooked in marketing claims.

title: Screen printing with UV-curable inks on PET and polypropylene: an LCA sensitivity study on curing energy and film recyclability
abstract: UV-curable screen printing inks applied to two flexible substrates—PET film (125 µm) and biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP, 40 µm)—were assessed using the ReCiPe Midpoint (H) method in OpenLCA 1.9. The functional unit was 1 m² of printed film at full-tone coverage. UV lamp energy consumption during curing was measured on a flatbed screen press at 0.11 kWh/m² for PET and 0.09 kWh/m² for BOPP. Four end-of-life scenarios were modelled: landfill, mechanical recycling, energy recovery, and solvent delamination prior to recycling. Across all impact categories examined (GWP, terrestrial acidification, human toxicity), the delamination-before-recycling scenario reduced total impact by 17–31% compared to landfill for PET, but produced higher human toxicity scores due to solvent use. BOPP responded more favourably to energy recovery owing to its high calorific value. The study provides quantitative data to support end-of-life labelling decisions for screen-printed flexible packaging.

title: Environmental profile of fountain solution systems in sheetfed offset: IPA-free alternatives evaluated by LCA
abstract: Isopropyl alcohol (IPA) in offset dampening systems is a well-documented source of VOC emissions, yet IPA-free alternatives introduce different chemical burdens. This study compared three fountain solution formulations—standard IPA (10% v/v), IPA-free with propylene glycol substitute, and fully deionised water system—under controlled press conditions on a Heidelberg SM74 using coated art paper. Process chemistry consumption was tracked over 20,000-sheet production runs for each formulation. LCA was performed using CML-IA baseline v3.05 in SimaPro 9.1. The IPA-free glycol system reduced POCP by 44% relative to standard IPA but increased freshwater ecotoxicity by 11% due to glycol manufacturing. The deionised water system offered the lowest environmental impact across seven of nine categories examined but required additional conductivity-management additives not always quantified in supplier declarations. Missing primary data for additive production represented the most significant inventory gap and is flagged as a research priority.

title: Carbon footprint benchmarking of four commercial print products: business cards, folding cartons, posters, and catalogues
abstract: A comparative carbon footprint study was conducted for four print product categories commonly produced in Serbian commercial printing houses. Data were gathered from five printing companies in Vojvodina through structured interviews and metered energy records over a 12-month period, covering substrate procurement, prepress, presswork, finishing, and outbound logistics. Functional units were defined per 1,000 finished pieces for each product type. GWP100 values (kg CO₂-eq per functional unit) were: business cards 1.2, A3 posters 3.8, folding cartons (cereal box format) 14.6, and 48-page catalogues 31.4. In all cases, paper and board accounted for 52–67% of the carbon footprint, with electricity consumption second at 12–21%. Logistics contributed less than 5% in all scenarios. The data set provides a regionally specific baseline for Serbian printing SMEs seeking to report or reduce their Scope 3 emissions and may inform sector-level environmental benchmarking exercises.

title: Recyclability of paper substrates printed with water-based flexographic inks: deinkability tests and LCA integration
abstract: Recycled fibre yield and ink removal efficiency were measured for three coated paper grades printed with water-based flexographic inks of varying pigment concentrations (5%, 10%, 15% by weight). Deinkability tests followed INGEDE Method 11 at the Paper and Board Testing Laboratory, Faculty of Forestry, University of Belgrade. Effective residual ink area (ERIA) ranged from 0.8% to 4.3% depending on pigment loading and surface coating chemistry. These empirical recyclability data were then integrated into an LCA model to adjust the recycled content credit in the end-of-life module, using the 50/50 cut-off approach. Adjusting the recyclability penalty for high-pigment substrates increased the GWP100 of the 15% pigment scenario by 8% compared to the default ecoinvent end-of-life assumption. The paper highlights that generic database end-of-life assumptions for printed paper may systematically underestimate environmental impacts when high-pigment or UV-varnished substrates are involved, and recommends printability-linked deinkability factors in future LCA databases.

title: Hotspot analysis in label printing: comparing pressure-sensitive labels produced by offset, flexography and digital toner processes
abstract: Pressure-sensitive labels for food packaging were assessed using a consequential LCA approach for three production processes: sheetfed offset, narrow-web UV flexography, and dry electrophotographic digital printing. The functional unit was 10,000 labels (format 60×40 mm) on 80 g/m² semi-gloss face stock with silicone-coated release liner. Primary data were collected from two label converters in Serbia and one in Romania. Release liner end-of-life received particular attention because silicone-treated paper is excluded from standard paper recycling streams in all three countries studied. Across all impact categories, the release liner's landfill disposal contributed 18–24% of total GWP, regardless of printing process. Offset showed the highest per-label ink waste in makeready (37 g per job start), while digital toner printing had the highest energy intensity per label at low run lengths (below 3,000 labels). Flexography occupied an intermediate position. A break-even run length crossover was identified at approximately 6,200 labels for the GWP comparison of flexography and digital.

title: Washing agents in offset press cleaning cycles: toxicity and climate trade-offs assessed by LCA
abstract: Press blanket and roller washing agents are consumed in significant quantities in sheetfed offset production but are rarely included in published LCAs of print products. This study quantified washing agent consumption across a full production week on two presses (4-colour and 5-colour plus coating) at a commercial printing house, recording volume per wash cycle, number of cycles per job, and substrate type. Three washing agent types were tested: petroleum-distillate based, fatty-acid methyl ester (FAME) based, and aqueous emulsion. LCA was performed using the EF 3.0 method. The petroleum-distillate agent had the highest GWP (1.8 kg CO₂-eq/litre used) but the lowest aquatic toxicity score. The FAME-based agent showed a 31% lower GWP but elevated eutrophication and land-use scores. The aqueous emulsion agent had the best toxicity profile but required heated water, shifting the impact burden to energy supply. A decision matrix weighting scheme is proposed to support printing house sustainability managers in agent selection.

title: Environmental implications of replacing solvent-based with water-based screen-printing inks in textile decoration: a midpoint LCA
abstract: The textile screen-printing sector in Serbia relies predominantly on plastisol and solvent-based inks, both associated with significant VOC emissions and persistence in aquatic environments. This study compared a conventional plastisol system with a water-based acrylic alternative across 10 midpoint impact categories using the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) method. The functional unit was 100 printed T-shirts (single-colour design, 20×20 cm, 180 g/m² cotton). Ink consumption, cure energy (conveyor oven at 160°C), and wastewater generation were measured in a textile print shop in Novi Sad over 15 production runs. Water-based inks reduced human toxicity (cancer) by 58% and POCP by 47% relative to plastisol. However, wastewater treatment for water-based systems generated a measurable eutrophication contribution absent in the plastisol scenario. Energy for curing was comparable between systems (0.08 vs. 0.09 kWh per shirt). The results provide quantitative grounding for environmental claims used by textile printers seeking eco-label certification.

title: Life-cycle assessment of printed electronics: conductive silver ink on PET substrate versus conventional copper-clad PCB for a simple RFID antenna
abstract: Gravure-printed silver nanoparticle ink on 125 µm PET was compared to a conventional etched copper-clad FR4 laminate for a single-turn RFID antenna operating at 13.56 MHz. The study was motivated by growing interest in printed electronics as a lower-impact manufacturing route. The functional unit was 10,000 antenna units with equivalent electrical performance verified by impedance measurement. LCA was performed using the EF 3.0 method; silver nanoparticle production data were taken from published peer-reviewed inventory studies, supplemented with sintering energy measured on a laboratory conveyor oven. Silver nanoink production dominated the impact profile of the printed alternative, contributing 74% of GWP and over 90% of mineral resource use. The copper-clad FR4 scenario had higher acidification and human toxicity scores associated with copper smelting. At current silver nanoink film weights (approximately 3.2 g/m²), the printed electronics route does not offer a systematic GWP advantage, though it eliminates the etching chemicals entirely. Reducing silver loading and exploring copper nanoink alternatives are identified as priority levers.

title: Scope and system boundary decisions in LCA studies of printed products: a structured review of 64 published studies (2005–2024)
abstract: Methodological inconsistencies across published LCA studies of printed products make cross-study comparison difficult and limit the usefulness of findings for industry decision-making. This paper reviewed 64 peer-reviewed LCA studies of printed products published between 2005 and 2024, coding each for system boundary definition, functional unit specification, impact assessment method, data source type, and whether post-consumer waste was included. Findings show that 41% of studies excluded the post-consumer phase entirely, and 28% used only secondary data for all inventory modules. Only 17% of studies reported uncertainty analysis. Impact assessment methods varied across 11 distinct approaches, with CML and ReCiPe most common. The review proposes a minimum reporting checklist adapted specifically for graphic reproduction LCA studies, covering 12 items considered essential for reproducibility and comparability. The checklist was validated against five recent studies in the corpus, identifying gaps in each. The paper is intended as a methodological reference for researchers and a procurement guide for printing companies commissioning third-party LCA studies.

title: Evaluation of chromatic adaptation transforms for soft-proofing applications across LCD and wide-gamut display technologies
abstract: Soft-proofing relies on chromatic adaptation transforms (CATs) to simulate press output on calibrated displays, yet the choice of CAT is rarely reported in production workflows. This study evaluated five widely used CATs — Bradford, CAT02, von Kries, Sharp, and CMCCAT2000 — within a soft-proofing pipeline connecting an offset press characterised to ISO 12647-2 with three display technologies: a standard sRGB LCD, a wide-gamut LED-backlit display, and an IPS panel with hardware LUT. Evaluation was performed using 180 colour patches spanning the CIELAB gamut boundary and 12 representative photographic and flat-colour test images. Observer assessments from 24 trained evaluators were collected using a paired comparison methodology. CAT02 and Bradford yielded the lowest mean ΔE2000 errors (1.8 and 2.1 respectively) and the highest observer preference scores. The wide-gamut display showed the largest sensitivity to CAT selection, with differences reaching ΔE2000 3.7 between best and worst transform. Practical recommendations are given for workflow standardisation in pressroom environments.

title: Age-Related Changes in Upper Body Measurements of Women Aged 50–75 and Their Implications for Blouse Pattern Construction
abstract: Changes in body shape accompanying ageing are well documented medically but rarely translated into apparel engineering literature in operational terms. This cross-sectional study compared 24 upper body measurements between three age cohorts of Serbian women: 50–59 (n=95), 60–67 (n=81), and 68–75 (n=64). Measurements were taken manually following ISO 8559-1 by trained technicians. Relative to the youngest cohort, the oldest group showed a mean increase of 3.1 cm in back width, 1.8 cm in nape-to-waist length, and 2.2 cm reduction in shoulder length, alongside a 4.7° increase in mean shoulder slope. These changes were not recoverable by simple grade-up from a standard size 46 block. A modified block for each cohort was constructed in Optitex and validated by virtual fitting on scanned avatars of four representative participants per cohort. Fitters' evaluations confirmed improved back-neck and shoulder region fit for the cohort-specific blocks.

title: Matrix metalloproteinase-8 in gingival crevicular fluid as an indicator of attachment loss: comparison between smokers and non-smokers
abstract: Matrix metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) is a collagenase released predominantly by neutrophils and is implicated in periodontal connective tissue breakdown. This study quantified MMP-8 in gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) collected by the paper-strip method from 88 adult patients stratified by smoking status (44 smokers, 44 non-smokers), all diagnosed with generalised chronic periodontitis. MMP-8 concentration was measured by ELISA. GCF MMP-8 was significantly higher in smokers (mean 18.4 ng/mL) than in non-smokers (mean 11.2 ng/mL, p = 0.003). Clinical attachment loss correlated more strongly with MMP-8 in non-smokers (r = 0.68) than in smokers (r = 0.44), suggesting that smoking partially uncouples the enzymatic response from tissue destruction. Receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.79 for MMP-8 as a predictor of sites with attachment loss ≥ 3 mm. Results indicate that smoking modifies the GCF MMP-8 response and should be accounted for in biomarker-based diagnostic models.

title: Salivary 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine as a marker of oxidative DNA damage in periodontitis patients with controlled and uncontrolled type 2 diabetes
abstract: Oxidative stress is elevated in both periodontitis and type 2 diabetes, yet the interaction between glycaemic control and salivary oxidative DNA damage markers has not been well characterised. This case-control study recruited 120 participants divided into four groups: periodontitis with controlled T2DM (HbA1c < 7 %, n = 30), periodontitis with uncontrolled T2DM (HbA1c ≥ 7 %, n = 30), periodontitis without diabetes (n = 30), and healthy controls (n = 30). Unstimulated saliva was analysed for 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) by competitive ELISA. Salivary 8-OHdG was highest in the uncontrolled T2DM with periodontitis group (mean 4.8 ng/mL) and lowest in healthy controls (0.9 ng/mL). Two-way ANOVA demonstrated significant main effects of both diabetes status (p < 0.001) and glycaemic control (p = 0.004) on 8-OHdG levels. 8-OHdG correlated moderately with probing depth (r = 0.53) and HbA1c (r = 0.49). These data suggest that salivary 8-OHdG reflects a combined oxidative burden and may be relevant for monitoring dual-diagnosis patients.

title: Multiplex salivary cytokine profiling in type 2 diabetes patients with varying periodontal severity
abstract: This study applied Luminex-based multiplex immunoassay to measure a panel of 12 cytokines — including IL-1β, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-17A, IL-18, TNF-α, IFN-γ, MCP-1, RANTES, and VEGF — in unstimulated saliva from 95 patients with type 2 diabetes categorised by periodontal severity (none, mild, moderate, severe) according to the 2017 AAP/EFP classification. Principal component analysis of cytokine profiles separated the severe periodontitis subgroup from the rest with reasonable accuracy (cross-validated misclassification rate 19 %). IL-1β, IL-8, and IL-17A showed the strongest association with increasing periodontal severity in stepwise ordinal regression (odds ratios 2.1–3.4 per quartile increase). IL-10 did not differ significantly across groups. Intra-group variability was substantial, partly attributable to differences in insulin regimen and disease duration. The multiplex approach identified cytokine clusters that single-analyte methods would miss and warrants further validation in prospective cohorts.

title: Changes in salivary MMP-8 and TIMP-1 six months after non-surgical periodontal therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes
abstract: Non-surgical periodontal therapy (NSPT) reduces local inflammation, but the extent to which salivary biomarkers normalise after treatment in diabetic patients is unclear. Forty-eight patients with type 2 diabetes and moderate-to-severe periodontitis underwent full-mouth scaling and root planing. Unstimulated saliva was collected before treatment and at six months post-treatment. MMP-8 and its tissue inhibitor TIMP-1 were measured by ELISA; the MMP-8/TIMP-1 molar ratio was calculated as an index of net enzymatic activity. At six months, mean MMP-8 decreased from 16.9 to 9.4 ng/mL (p < 0.001) and TIMP-1 increased from 83 to 107 ng/mL (p = 0.002), resulting in a significant reduction of the MMP-8/TIMP-1 ratio. Patients with HbA1c < 7 % showed greater biomarker normalisation than those with HbA1c ≥ 7 % (p = 0.03 for between-group difference in ratio change). Clinical outcomes (probing depth reduction, attachment gain) were comparable between groups. Salivary MMP-8/TIMP-1 ratio may serve as a biochemical endpoint for therapeutic monitoring in this population.

title: Association between salivary lactoferrin concentration and subgingival microbiome composition in periodontitis patients with and without type 2 diabetes: a pilot study
abstract: Lactoferrin, an iron-binding glycoprotein with antimicrobial properties, is secreted by neutrophils into saliva and GCF during infection. This pilot study investigated whether salivary lactoferrin concentration correlates with subgingival microbiome composition in 36 participants (18 with T2DM and periodontitis, 18 with periodontitis only). Salivary lactoferrin was quantified by ELISA. Subgingival plaque samples were subjected to 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3-V4 region) on an Illumina MiSeq platform. Lactoferrin was significantly higher in the T2DM group (median 7.2 µg/mL versus 4.1 µg/mL, p = 0.01). Spearman correlations between lactoferrin and the relative abundance of six periodontal pathogens (including Porphyromonas gingivalis and Tannerella forsythia) were weak to moderate (ρ 0.29–0.51). Alpha diversity was lower in the T2DM group (Shannon index p = 0.04). Given the small sample, these associations are preliminary and a larger study with longitudinal sampling is planned.

title: Salivary biomarkers as predictors of one-year tooth loss in patients with type 2 diabetes and periodontitis: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Identifying patients at highest risk of tooth loss is a clinical priority in diabetic periodontitis management. This prospective cohort study enrolled 110 patients with confirmed type 2 diabetes and generalised stage III or IV periodontitis and followed them for 12 months after standardised non-surgical treatment. Baseline unstimulated saliva was analysed for IL-1β, MMP-8, TIMP-1, 8-OHdG, and adiponectin by ELISA and Luminex. Tooth loss was recorded at 6 and 12 months. Twenty-three patients (20.9 %) lost at least one tooth during follow-up. In multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, smoking, HbA1c at enrolment, and baseline tooth mobility, elevated baseline MMP-8 (HR 1.08 per ng/mL, 95 % CI 1.02–1.14) and low adiponectin (HR 0.74 per µg/mL, 95 % CI 0.59–0.93) were independently associated with tooth loss. A combined biomarker score incorporating MMP-8 and adiponectin showed a C-statistic of 0.74. These findings support further investigation of salivary biomarker panels for risk stratification in this population.

title: Merenje nivoa zvučne snage aksijalnih ventilatora sušara pšenice primenom metode slobodnog polja prema EN ISO 3744
abstract: U radu je prikazana procedura merenja nivoa zvučne snage tri tipa aksijalnih ventilatora koji se koriste u komornim sušarama pšenice kapaciteta 20–50 t/h. Merenja su obavljena na otvorenom poligonu u uslovima koji zadovoljavaju kriterijum K2A < 2 dB prema standardu EN ISO 3744. Za svaki tip ventilatora definisana je hipotaktna površ merenja sa 10 mikrofona. Izmereni nivoi zvučne snage kretali su se u opsegu od 98,4 do 104,7 dB(A) pri nominalnom broju obrtaja. Utvrđeno je da dominantne komponente spektra leže u opsezima 250–1000 Hz, što je u skladu s teorijskim predviđanjima za aerodynamički šum lopatica. Poređenjem rezultata s deklarisanim vrednostima proizvođača uočena su odstupanja do 3,1 dB(A), što upućuje na neophodnost nezavisnih verifikacionih merenja pri nabavci opreme.

title: Uticaj geometrije ulaznog difuzora na emisiju buke centrifugalnih ventilatora u sušarama kukuruza
abstract: Ispitivanje je obuhvatilo pet konfiguracija ulaznog difuzora centrifugalnog ventilatora nominalne snage 37 kW koji se ugrađuje u tunelske sušare kukuruza. Merenja su realizovana u polubeszvučnoj komori Tehničkog fakulteta 'Mihajlo Pupin' u Zrenjaninu, pri protocima vazduha od 2,5, 3,0 i 3,5 m³/s. Promena ugla konusa difuzora od 15° na 30° dovela je do smanjenja ukupnog nivoa buke za 2,8 dB(A) pri maksimalnom protoku. Frekvencijska analiza pokazala je da se redukcija pretežno odnosi na opseg 500–2000 Hz. Geometrija s paralelnim ulaznim kanalom bez difuzora generisala je najizraženije tonalne komponente na frekvenciji prolaska lopatica. Rezultati potvrđuju da optimizacija ulazne geometrije predstavlja ekonomičnu meru smanjenja emisije buke bez intervencije na pogonskom sklopu.

title: Projektovanje i ispitivanje parcijalne akustične ograde za ventilatorski agregat kanalske sušare
abstract: Rad opisuje projektovanje i laboratorijsko ispitivanje parcijalne akustične ograde od sendvič panela (mineralna vuna 50 mm između čeličnih limova debljine 1,2 mm) namenjene ventilatorskim agregatima kanalskih sušara snage 18,5–30 kW. Ograda je projektovana kao trostranski štit s otvorenim bočnim stranama radi nesmetanog pristupa za servisiranje. Umetanje gubitak (IL) mereno je prema EN ISO 11546-2 pri pet radnih tačaka ventilatora. Srednja vrednost IL iznosila je 9,4 dB(A) pri nominalnom opterećenju, s maksimumom od 12,1 dB(A) u opsegu 500–1000 Hz. Termička analiza potvrdila je da temperatura surface panela ne prelazi 42 °C pri kontinuiranom radu, čime su ispunjeni uslovi za trajnu primenu. Masa ograde iznosi 34 kg, što je prihvatljivo za retromontažu na postojeće instalacije.

title: Vibro-acoustic characterisation of drive-belt transmission in stationary drying fan units using acceleration and sound intensity measurements
abstract: Belt-driven fan assemblies are common in older grain drying installations across the Pannonian Basin, yet their vibro-acoustic contribution is rarely separated from overall machine noise in field studies. This paper reports simultaneous triaxial acceleration measurements on the motor and fan bearing housings and sound intensity scanning of the belt guard enclosure for four units with V-belt and flat-belt configurations. Measurement uncertainty was assessed following GUM guidelines. Structural resonances of the belt guard at 420 Hz and 840 Hz amplified radiated sound pressure by up to 6 dB relative to a damped reference guard. Correlation analysis between r.m.s. acceleration at the motor bearing and A-weighted sound power level yielded Pearson r = 0.87 across 18 operating points, suggesting acceleration monitoring as a proxy for rapid noise screening. Adding a constrained-layer damping treatment (1.5 mm viscoelastic adhesive sheet) to the original guard reduced the 420 Hz resonance peak by 4.3 dB.

title: Prediction of A-weighted sound power levels for axial drying fans using dimensional analysis and empirical regression on a dataset of 27 units
abstract: Selecting grain drying equipment based on acoustic performance is hampered by the lack of standardised prediction tools accessible to farm engineers. This study assembled noise emission data from 27 axial fan units installed at grain handling facilities in Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary, all measured under ISO 3744 conditions. Using dimensional analysis, a set of five non-dimensional groups was derived incorporating fan diameter, rotational speed, static pressure rise, and motor rated power. Multiple linear regression on log-transformed variables yielded a model explaining 91% of variance in LWA with a standard error of 1.6 dB(A) on the validation subset (n = 7). The model was compared against two published empirical formulae from the German agricultural machinery noise database; the present model performed comparably within its intended operating range (D = 0.45–1.1 m, n = 480–1450 rpm). A look-up table formatted for practical use by procurement personnel is appended.

title: Uticaj starenja mineralno-vunenog apsorpcionog sloja na gubitak umetanja akustičnih ploča u agroindustrijskim uslovima
abstract: Akustične obloge od mineralne vune izložene su u sušarama žitarica povišenoj vlažnosti, prašini i cikličnom zagrevanju, što može degradirati njihove apsorpcionc osobine. U ovom radu uzorci mineralne vune gustine 60 i 100 kg/m³ sa zaštitnim polipropilenskim flisom ubrzano su stare metodom kombinovanog klimatskog ciklusa (80 ciklusa vlaženje/sušenje, temperatura 20–65 °C) kojim se simulira petogodišnja eksploatacija. Merenje koeficijenta apsorpcije zvuka obavljeno je u impedansnoj cevi prema ISO 10534-2. Gubitak umetanja kompletnih sendvič panela meren je po EN ISO 11546-2. Uzorci gustine 100 kg/m³ pokazali su statistički neznačajan pad IL od 0,4 dB(A) nakon ubrzanog starenja, dok su uzorci 60 kg/m³ pokazali pad od 1,9 dB(A) usled kompakcije vlakana. Preporučuje se primena materijala veće gustine za instalacije s godišnjim radom dužim od 1200 sati.

title: Low-cost frequency-selective acoustic treatment for reducing tonal fan noise in grain drying facilities
abstract: Tonal components at blade pass frequency (BPF) and its harmonics dominate the noise spectrum of many axial and centrifugal fans in grain drying applications, yet broadband treatments are often over-specified and unnecessarily costly for these installations. This paper evaluates a frequency-selective approach combining a quarter-wave resonator array tuned to BPF (typically 200–450 Hz for common fan types) with a thin porous facing layer. Prototypes were fabricated using mild steel tubes and tested in a reverberation room according to EN ISO 354. Absorption coefficients exceeding 0.80 were measured in a ±15% band around the target frequency. Installation trials at two commercial drying stations in Vojvodina demonstrated reductions of 7.2 and 8.9 dB in the BPF octave band, with overall A-weighted sound pressure level reductions of 4.1 and 5.3 dB(A) at the operator position. Materials cost per unit treated surface was approximately 60% lower than an equivalent mineral-wool solution.

title: Effect of variable-frequency drive control on noise emission of centrifugal fans in modular grain drying towers
abstract: Variable-frequency drives (VFDs) are increasingly retrofitted to centrifugal fans in modular grain drying towers as an energy-saving measure, but their acoustic side-effects are not well documented. This study measured LWA and one-third-octave spectra at 12 operating frequencies (25–50 Hz, step 2.5 Hz) for two fan models installed in a commercial 80 t/h drying tower in Bačka. At reduced speeds (30–35 Hz), overall LWA decreased by 8–11 dB(A) relative to full-speed operation, consistent with fan noise scaling laws. However, at 37.5 Hz a tonal component at 1250 Hz appeared, attributable to VFD switching frequency interaction with structural modes of the fan casing, increasing the one-third-octave band level by 9 dB relative to the broadband baseline. A passive notch filter on the VFD output and additional damping of the casing eliminated this artefact. Results suggest that acoustic screening should be part of VFD commissioning procedures.

title: Comparative acoustic performance of three enclosure panel types for retrofitting noise control on legacy grain drying fan installations in Vojvodina
abstract: A significant share of grain drying infrastructure in Vojvodina predates current occupational noise standards and cannot be replaced in the short term. This paper compares three enclosure panel types—(A) single-leaf steel sheet with mineral wool lining, (B) double-leaf steel with air gap and fibre glass, and (C) recycled rubber composite—applied as full-coverage removable enclosures on fans at three sites. Enclosures were installed and removed by two workers in under 30 minutes at each site. Insertion loss was measured in situ per EN ISO 11546-2. Type B achieved the highest mean IL of 14.2 dB(A), followed by A at 11.8 dB(A) and C at 9.1 dB(A). Life-cycle cost analysis over a 10-year horizon showed Type A to be the most cost-effective when accounting for material, installation, and maintenance costs. Type C, despite lowest acoustic performance, showed the best resistance to moisture and mechanical damage during 18 months of field observation.

title: Mapping occupational noise exposure across a large grain cooperative: integrating fixed monitoring and personal dosimetry with spatial interpolation
abstract: Grain cooperatives operating multiple drying lines simultaneously present complex noise environments that point measurements alone cannot adequately characterise. At a cooperative in Srem with four parallel drying lines and a total installed fan power of 480 kW, 44 fixed-point SPL measurements and personal dosimetry on 19 workers across all job roles were combined with 2D Kriging interpolation to produce a facility-wide noise map. LEX,8h exceeded 85 dB(A) for 11 of 19 workers; the highest recorded value was 93.2 dB(A) for a grain intake operator working adjacent to two running fan units. Kriging maps revealed that noise hotspots extended 8–12 m beyond the fan room walls into adjacent working areas not previously identified as requiring hearing protection. Uncertainty of interpolated values was below 2.5 dB(A) for 90% of the covered area. The methodology is transferable to other multi-source agricultural processing facilities.

title: Influence of moisture content on wheat grain flow behaviour in a threshing drum: experimental and DEM study
abstract: Grain moisture content at harvest ranges widely (13–22% w.b.) and affects mechanical properties such as stiffness, surface friction, and viscoelastic damping, all of which influence DEM contact parameters. This study measured bulk angle of repose, surface friction, and coefficient of restitution for wheat grain conditioned to five moisture levels (13, 15, 17, 19, and 21% w.b.) and fitted moisture-dependent contact parameter correlations. These correlations were incorporated into an EDEM 2021 model of a small-scale threshing drum (cylinder diameter 400 mm, 50 mm concave clearance) fed at 2 kg/s. At 21% w.b., the rolling friction coefficient increased from 0.04 to 0.09 and static friction from 0.38 to 0.51. Simulated grain residence time in the drum increased by 28% from 13% to 21% moisture, and specific energy consumption rose by 34%. Experimental validation using a load-cell-instrumented small-scale drum showed agreement within 11% for torque across all moisture levels. The results indicate that constant-parameter DEM models calibrated at a single moisture content may substantially mispredict performance under wet-harvest conditions.

title: Calibration protocol for variable-rate spreaders: three seasons of field data and controller responsiveness evaluation
abstract: Variable-rate (VR) granular applicators require field-specific calibration linking controller output to actual application rate. We tested two hydraulic-drive and three electric-drive spreaders across fifty-four field plots (4 ha each) in the Pannonian Plain over three growing seasons (2017–2019). Calibration runs used both static (plot collection) and dynamic (real-time weight sensors) methods. Controller step increments (0–100%) were evaluated at five nominal rates (100, 150, 200, 250, 300 kg/ha). System lag (delay between command and application change) varied from 0.8 to 3.2 seconds depending on metering mechanism. Linearity of response differed significantly: hydraulic spreaders showed ±8% deviation; electric systems ±5%. Seasonal variation due to granule moisture content was quantified using calibration curves fitted every two weeks. A simplified three-point calibration method (0, 50, 100%) achieved ±12% prediction accuracy for rates within the tested range. Field validation on winter wheat and maize confirmed that proper calibration reduced application variability (coefficient of variation) by 40–55% compared to manufacturer defaults. We recommend site-specific calibration before each campaign.

title: Hydraulic implications of partial root-zone drying irrigation scheduling for drip lateral design in sloped vineyards
abstract: Partial root-zone drying (PRD) alternates irrigation between opposite sides of vine rows on a cycle of 10–14 days, which effectively halves the number of active laterals at any one time and doubles the flow demand on the active side. This study examined how PRD scheduling modifies hydraulic conditions in laterals originally designed for conventional full-root-zone irrigation. Simulations were run for 16 lateral configurations representing combinations of two slope gradients (8%, 16%), two lengths (80 m, 120 m), and two pipe diameters (16 mm, 20 mm). Under PRD, inlet velocities increased by 85–97% and head losses per 100 m increased by 3.2–5.7 m, pushing several configurations below the minimum design EU of 85%. For the 120 m, 16 mm, 16% slope configuration, EU dropped from 89% under conventional irrigation to 71% under PRD. The analysis indicates that laterals need to be upsized by one diameter class or shortened by 25–35% when PRD scheduling is adopted in sloped vineyards.

title: Estimating sedimentation basin performance under variable influent suspended-solids loading using a one-dimensional flux model
abstract: Sedimentation basins in water treatment plants frequently receive influent with time-varying suspended-solids concentrations that deviate significantly from design assumptions. This study applies a one-dimensional solids-flux model to three rectangular basins at a municipal surface-water treatment plant in northern Serbia, using continuous turbidity data logged at 15-minute intervals over 12 months. The flux model was parameterised by batch settling tests conducted on raw-water samples collected in each season (48 tests total), yielding Vesilind settling velocity constants that differed by up to 40% between summer and winter. Dynamic simulations reproduced measured effluent turbidity trends with a root-mean-square error below 2.4 NTU across all basins. An operational chart was derived relating influent concentration and flow rate to safe operating zones, which plant operators adopted as a scheduling aid. The approach requires only standard turbidity instrumentation and can be retro-fitted to existing control systems without hardware modifications.

title: Dynamic modelling of a spiral-wound reverse-osmosis unit for brackish groundwater desalination: parameter estimation and scenario analysis
abstract: A dynamic model of a three-stage spiral-wound reverse-osmosis (RO) train for brackish groundwater desalination was developed and calibrated against pilot-plant data collected over six months of continuous operation in the Banat region of Serbia. The model couples the solution-diffusion membrane transport equations with axial concentration-polarisation corrections and includes a hydraulic submodel for inter-stage pressure drop. Eighteen membrane transport parameters were estimated by minimising the weighted sum of squared residuals between simulated and measured permeate flux, conductivity, and pressure at each stage outlet. The calibrated model reproduced step-change responses in feed pressure and feed conductivity within 5% and 8% error respectively across 42 test scenarios. Scenario analysis explored the effect of feed temperature variation between 8 °C and 24 °C on specific energy consumption and permeate quality, finding a 0.18 kWh/m³ increase per 5 °C temperature drop. The model was coded in Aspen Custom Modeler for integration into plant-wide flowsheet simulations.

title: Compact water reuse circuits in the food industry: a framework for steady-state optimisation of make-up and blowdown streams
abstract: Many food-industry plants operate water circuits that recycle rinse and cooling water, yet sizing of make-up and blowdown streams is often done empirically rather than by systematic mass-balance methods. This chapter reviews the formulation of steady-state network mass-balance problems for compact reuse circuits, covering source–sink matrix representations, concentration constraints on regulated contaminants, and single-objective linear programming for minimum freshwater intake. Three worked examples drawn from dairy, sugar, and beverage production sectors are presented, with contaminant data taken from published surveys supplemented by measurements at regional plants. The chapter discusses software implementation in GAMS and compares results obtained by linear programming with heuristic shortcut methods in common industrial use. Typical freshwater savings identified by the optimisation approach ranged from 12% to 31% relative to current plant practice, depending on circuit complexity and the tightness of concentration constraints.

title: Influence of backwash frequency on effluent quality and energy use in rapid sand filtration: simulation and experimental validation
abstract: Rapid sand filters are widely used as a polishing step in surface-water treatment, yet the scheduling of backwash cycles is typically based on fixed time intervals rather than model-based decisions. This study presents a one-dimensional dynamic model of a pilot-scale rapid sand filter (0.2 m² cross-section, 0.8 m bed depth) that tracks suspended-solids accumulation, head-loss development, and breakthrough as functions of filtration velocity, influent turbidity, and backwash timing. The model was validated against 90 filtration runs performed at the Faculty of Technology pilot facility over two years, covering influent turbidities between 2 NTU and 18 NTU and filtration velocities of 5–12 m/h. Simulations showed that extending backwash intervals by 30% under low-turbidity conditions reduced total backwash water volume by 19% with a less than 4% increase in mean effluent turbidity. An energy accounting submodel indicated that 73% of filter-section electricity consumption was attributable to backwash pumping.
