title: Ion-exchange column cycling in nitrate removal: a column model coupled with a plant-scale mass-balance and regenerant recovery circuit
abstract: Nitrate contamination of drinking-water sources is a persistent problem in agricultural regions of Vojvodina. This paper presents a coupled modelling approach in which a pore-diffusion ion-exchange column model (calibrated against 24 breakthrough curves measured in the laboratory with locally collected groundwater) is linked to a plant-level mass-balance model that tracks chloride, sulphate, and nitrate concentrations through exhaustion, rinse, and regeneration phases of a multi-column system. Regenerant brine reuse was assessed through a cyclic steady-state algorithm that iterates column and plant-level models until cycle-to-cycle variation in regenerant composition falls below a tolerance of 0.1 meq/L. Results showed that two-stage countercurrent brine recovery could reduce fresh salt consumption by 34% and wastewater discharge by 28% compared with single-pass regeneration. The model was used to screen five column configurations differing in bed depth and resin type without additional experimental runs.

title: Simulation-based assessment of cooling tower blowdown reuse in a compact industrial water circuit: effects on scaling and corrosion indices
abstract: Cooling tower blowdown is a significant source of wastewater in process industries, and its reuse in other plant circuits requires careful assessment of scaling and corrosion risks. A steady-state simulation model was developed for the integrated water circuit of a small chemical manufacturing facility in Novi Sad, including the cooling tower make-up, blowdown, and a softener–RO treatment train proposed for blowdown polishing. The model tracks calcium, magnesium, silica, chloride, and alkalinity through all circuit streams and computes Langelier Saturation Index and Ryznar Stability Index for each recycle point. Sixteen blending scenarios were evaluated, varying blowdown treatment fraction from 0% to 100% in 10-percentage-point increments. Results showed that treating 60% of blowdown through the softener–RO train and recycling it as make-up maintained both scaling and corrosion indices within acceptable bounds while cutting freshwater intake by 22% and wastewater discharge by 31%. Silica accumulation was identified as the binding constraint above 70% recycle fraction.

title: A modular dynamic simulator for multi-unit water treatment trains: architecture, unit library, and illustrative case study
abstract: This conference paper describes the architecture of a modular dynamic simulation environment, called WaterSim-NS, developed at the University of Novi Sad for assembling multi-unit water treatment trains from a library of pre-coded unit-operation modules. The unit library currently contains 11 modules: raw-water storage, coagulation–flocculation reactor, rectangular sedimentation basin, rapid sand filter, activated carbon adsorber, ion-exchange column, nanofiltration membrane, reverse-osmosis membrane, pH adjustment tank, storage equalisation tank, and a generic mixing junction. Each module exposes a standardised interface of inlet/outlet flow vectors and parameter structures, enabling automated mass-balance connectivity checking. The simulator is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink. A case study assembles a seven-unit train treating surface water to drinking-water standards and demonstrates simulation of a 6-hour diurnal flow variation cycle. Simulation run time for a 24-hour horizon at 1-minute resolution was 38 seconds on standard desktop hardware.

title: Multi-objective optimisation of a zero-liquid-discharge circuit for a small electroplating facility: trade-offs between freshwater use, energy, and evaporator capacity
abstract: Zero-liquid-discharge (ZLD) systems for electroplating rinsewaters involve interconnected ion-exchange, reverse-osmosis, and evaporation stages whose sizing presents competing objectives. This paper formulates a multi-objective nonlinear programme for a ZLD circuit at a small electroplating shop in Serbia, minimising simultaneously freshwater consumption, total electrical energy, and installed evaporator heat-exchange area. The Pareto frontier was generated using the ε-constraint method with 120 constraint combinations, solved with sequential quadratic programming in MATLAB. Input data — rinsewater flow rates, nickel and chromate concentrations — were measured over four weeks at the facility. The Pareto analysis showed that reducing freshwater consumption from 8.5 to 4.2 m³/day required a 67% increase in evaporator area, while the marginal energy penalty per cubic metre of water saved rose steeply below 5 m³/day freshwater intake. A preferred solution was selected using the TOPSIS method weighting the three objectives equally, resulting in 5.1 m³/day freshwater, 38 kWh/day energy, and 12 m² evaporator area.

title: Benchmarking dynamic simulation tools for industrial water circuit modelling: a comparison of Aspen Plus Dynamics, MATLAB/Simulink, and gPROMS on three test cases
abstract: Practitioners choosing a simulation platform for industrial water circuit modelling face limited comparative guidance in the literature. This preprint reports a structured benchmarking exercise in which three test cases — a two-stage RO train responding to feed salinity steps, a sedimentation–filtration sequence under diurnal flow variation, and a cyclic ion-exchange system — were implemented independently in Aspen Plus Dynamics, MATLAB/Simulink (using the WaterSim-NS unit library), and gPROMS ProcessBuilder. Each platform was evaluated on five criteria: model development time, solver robustness for stiff systems, run time, ease of parameter estimation integration, and accessibility for non-specialist users. Results showed that gPROMS achieved the shortest run times (factor of 2.3 faster than MATLAB for the cyclic ion-exchange case) but required the longest model development time. MATLAB/Simulink scored highest on parameter estimation integration due to direct coupling with the Optimization Toolbox. Aspen Plus Dynamics performed best on accessibility owing to its graphical flowsheeting interface. Quantitative comparison tables and model files are provided as supplementary material.

title: Effect of diatomite particle size distribution on filtration resistance in crude vegetable oil clarification
abstract: Three commercial diatomite grades with median particle diameters of 12, 22, and 41 µm were evaluated as filter aids for clarifying crude rapeseed oil containing 0.4–1.2 % w/w wax-phospholipid sediment. Dead-end constant-pressure filtration experiments were conducted at 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4 MPa using a 47-mm disc filter. The coarsest grade reduced final specific cake resistance by 58 % compared with the finest grade at equivalent dosage (1.5 % w/w). Blending 70 % coarse with 30 % fine grade achieved a permeability intermediate between the two pure grades while maintaining turbidity below 5 NTU in the filtrate. Scanning electron microscopy of cross-sectioned cakes confirmed that the mixed grades produced a more open pore network. A modified Kozeny–Carman model incorporating bimodal pore size was fitted to the data. The findings support a blending strategy that reduces diatomite consumption by approximately 20 % without exceeding target pressure drop.

title: Melt Flow and Crystallisation Behaviour of Metallocene Linear Low-Density Polyethylene Grades Used in Blown-Film Extrusion
abstract: Three commercial metallocene linear low-density polyethylene (mLLDPE) grades with melt flow indices between 1.0 and 3.5 g/10 min were characterised by oscillatory shear rheometry over the frequency range 0.01–100 rad/s at 160, 180 and 200 °C. Storage and loss moduli, complex viscosity, and crossover frequencies were determined to establish structure–property relationships. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed crystallisation onset temperatures spanning 108–116 °C and crystallinity fractions of 31–38 %. Time–temperature superposition was applied successfully to all three grades, yielding master curves consistent with narrow molecular-weight distribution typical of single-site catalysis. The results were correlated with blown-film bubble stability observations from a pilot-scale 45 mm extruder. Grade C, with the highest zero-shear viscosity (18 200 Pa·s at 180 °C), gave the most stable bubble but required a melt temperature 12 °C higher than the others to maintain acceptable die pressure. The data establish a baseline for blend design aimed at seal-layer applications.

title: Phytochrome photoequilibrium thresholds governing hypocotyl elongation in Arabidopsis thaliana under narrowband red and far-red LED treatments
abstract: Hypocotyl length in Arabidopsis thaliana is commonly used as a proxy for shade-avoidance intensity, yet the quantitative relationship between phytochrome photoequilibrium (PPE) and elongation rate has not been systematically mapped across a continuous PPE range under monochromatic LED sources. We grew Col-0 seedlings for five days under 14 combinations of 660 nm and 730 nm LEDs, achieving PPE values from 0.31 to 0.87, at a constant photon fluence rate of 50 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Hypocotyl lengths were measured with ImageJ on scanned seedling images (n = 30 per treatment). A sigmoidal dose–response model explained 91% of variance, with an inflection point at PPE = 0.54. Elongation saturated below PPE = 0.38 and was fully suppressed above PPE = 0.78. Transcript levels of HFR1 and PIL1, quantified by qRT-PCR, tracked elongation responses closely. These thresholds provide a practical design parameter for specifying red-to-far-red ratios in plant growth installations.

title: A dynamic mathematical model of phytochrome A and phytochrome B activation kinetics under fluctuating light quality
abstract: Phytochrome A (phyA) and phytochrome B (phyB) differ fundamentally in their dark reversion rates and light-lability, causing divergent activation trajectories under fluctuating spectra typical of greenhouse supplemental lighting. We constructed a system of ordinary differential equations describing Pr–Pfr interconversion, nuclear import, and proteolytic degradation for both photoreceptors, parameterised using published spectroscopic constants and in-house qRT-PCR data for downstream marker genes (HY5, COP1, PIF4). The model was fitted to time-course data from Arabidopsis seedlings exposed to sinusoidally modulated red/far-red ratios cycling with periods of 15, 30, and 60 minutes. Root mean square error between predicted and observed PIF4 transcript fold-change was below 0.18 across all treatments. Sensitivity analysis identified phyA dark reversion rate as the parameter with greatest influence on short-period responses. The model is made available as a Matlab Simulink file in supplementary materials.

title: Shade-avoidance morphology in lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.) cultivars exposed to red-to-far-red ratios representative of dense canopy conditions
abstract: Commercial lettuce production in vertical farms relies on LED systems that rarely consider far-red content, yet even small proportions of far-red radiation can trigger shade-avoidance elongation and reduce marketable yield. We exposed four lettuce cultivars (Batavia, Butterhead, Lollo Rosso, Romaine) to three red-to-far-red ratios (1.0, 2.5, and 5.0) at constant photosynthetically active radiation of 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for 21 days in a controlled growth cabinet. We measured petiole length, leaf area, fresh weight, dry weight, and chlorophyll content. Shade-avoidance responses were strongest in Lollo Rosso, which showed a 34% increase in petiole length at R:FR = 1.0 compared with R:FR = 5.0. Butterhead was least responsive (+9%). Dry weight declined significantly only at R:FR = 1.0 in Batavia and Lollo Rosso. Results suggest cultivar selection can partly compensate for suboptimal spectral conditions in cost-constrained installations.

title: Spectral effects of multi-channel LED arrays on hypocotyl photomorphogenesis: comparison of stepwise and continuous spectral tuning protocols
abstract: Multi-channel LED luminaires allow arbitrary spectral power distributions to be generated, but experimental protocols typically apply discrete treatment steps rather than continuous gradients. We compared the two approaches for mapping hypocotyl elongation response surfaces in Arabidopsis Col-0 across a two-dimensional space of red-to-far-red ratio (0.3–10) and blue fraction (5–30% of total PAR). Stepwise protocols used 20 discrete combinations; continuous tuning traversed the same space along 8 paths using ramp signals. Both protocols agreed within 5% for interpolated hypocotyl lengths, but the continuous protocol reduced plant numbers needed by 40% for equivalent spatial resolution. Response surfaces showed a saddle region around R:FR = 2, blue = 15%, where hypocotyl length was relatively insensitive to both variables. Practical guidance for designing screening experiments with limited plant material is discussed.

title: Photomorphogenetic responses of basil (Ocimum basilicum L.) under variable blue-to-red LED ratios: growth, essential oil content, and phenolic profiles
abstract: Sweet basil is increasingly produced under artificial lighting, but spectral optimisation for simultaneous biomass and secondary metabolite production remains underexplored. We grew basil (cv. Genovese) for 28 days under five blue-to-red ratios (B:R = 0.05, 0.15, 0.30, 0.50, 0.75, blue peak 450 nm, red peak 660 nm) at 180 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ PAR. Shoot fresh weight, dry weight, leaf area, essential oil yield by hydrodistillation, linalool and eugenol fractions by GC-MS, and total polyphenol content by Folin–Ciocalteu assay were measured. Maximum fresh weight (38.4 g plant⁻¹) was recorded at B:R = 0.15. Essential oil yield peaked at B:R = 0.30 (1.8% of dry weight). Linalool proportion declined from 62% at B:R = 0.05 to 44% at B:R = 0.75. Polyphenol content increased monotonically with blue fraction. The results indicate that simultaneous optimisation of biomass and oil quality requires a compromise B:R around 0.20–0.30.

title: Quantitative photomorphogenesis modelling as a tool for light recipe optimisation in plant factories
abstract: This chapter surveys mechanistic and empirical modelling approaches that link spectral irradiance parameters to plant developmental outputs in closed plant factory environments. The first section reviews Pfr/Ptotal formalisms and their extension to multi-photoreceptor systems including cryptochromes and phototropins. The second section describes how ODE-based signalling network models can be coupled with growth sub-models to predict elongation, leaf expansion, and pigment accumulation as functions of spectrum, photoperiod, and developmental stage. The third section presents a case study using a simplified two-photoreceptor model calibrated to tomato seedling data, demonstrating that 80% of observed phenotypic variance across 12 light treatments can be captured with 14 free parameters estimated by nonlinear least squares. The final section discusses practical barriers to deploying such models in commercial settings and proposes a tiered modelling framework that scales from rapid empirical recipes to full mechanistic simulation depending on available data.

title: Far-red pre-treatment accelerates de-etiolation kinetics and modulates COP1 abundance in white-light-grown Arabidopsis seedlings
abstract: The interaction between end-of-day far-red treatment and subsequent white-light exposure during de-etiolation is poorly characterised in terms of COP1 protein dynamics. We applied a 10-minute far-red pulse (730 nm, 15 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) immediately before transferring 4-day-old dark-grown Arabidopsis Col-0 seedlings to white fluorescent light and tracked cotyledon opening angle, hypocotyl elongation rate, and COP1 protein abundance by western blot at 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, and 24 hours. Far-red pre-treatment accelerated cotyledon opening by approximately 1.8 hours relative to control and was associated with a 30% lower COP1 band intensity at the 2-hour time point. Hypocotyl elongation ceased 2.3 hours earlier in pre-treated seedlings. A phyA null mutant abolished the pre-treatment effect, confirming phyA as the primary mediator. These results are consistent with a model in which far-red-driven phyA nuclear accumulation pre-primes COP1 degradation before white-light exposure.

title: Canopy-level red-to-far-red ratio dynamics in tomato rows under supplemental LED interlighting: measured profiles and predicted photomorphogenic effects
abstract: Interlighting LEDs placed between tomato rows alter the spectral environment experienced by leaves at different canopy positions, yet systematic in-canopy spectroradiometric surveys combined with photomorphogenesis predictions are scarce. We installed calibrated spectroradiometers at five canopy heights in a glasshouse trial in Sombor using a commercial interlighting system (660 nm dominant spectrum) and recorded red-to-far-red ratio, blue fraction, and PAR continuously over 14 days. R:FR ranged from 1.1 at the canopy base to 4.3 near the LED fixtures. We applied our previously published phytochrome photoequilibrium model to predict phyB Pfr/Ptotal at each position and correlated predictions with internode length measurements from the same plant positions (Pearson r = −0.81, p < 0.001). Variance unexplained by phyB Pfr/Ptotal alone was partly accounted for by leaf temperature (partial r² = 0.09). The dataset is archived at the Open Research Data Repository of Serbia.

title: Phytotoxic potential of aqueous root extracts from Fallopia japonica on germination and early growth of Poa pratensis and Festuca rubra
abstract: Root extracts of Fallopia japonica were prepared at four concentrations (5, 10, 25, and 50 mg dry weight mL⁻¹) and applied to seeds of Poa pratensis and Festuca rubra in standardised bioassay conditions at 22 °C under 12/12 h photoperiod. Germination rate, radicle length, and fresh biomass were recorded after seven days. At 25 mg mL⁻¹, germination of P. pratensis was reduced by 41% and radicle elongation by 67% relative to distilled-water controls. F. rubra showed comparable sensitivity. HPLC-DAD analysis identified resveratrol, emodin, and three hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives as dominant components, with emodin concentration correlating positively with inhibitory effect (r = 0.84, p < 0.01). Results indicate that F. japonica root material releases biologically active compounds under aqueous extraction conditions relevant to soil pore-water chemistry in riparian sediments. Dose–response curves suggest that field-realistic concentrations in dense stands may suppress native grass recruitment.

title: Karyotype analysis of three diploid Centaurea endemics from the central Balkans
abstract: Chromosome number, karyotype morphology, and relative genome size were determined for three Centaurea species endemic to the central Balkan peninsula: C. radovanovicii, C. sumadijensis, and C. pelisterensis. All three species were confirmed as diploid (2n = 2x = 18). Karyotypes were constructed from root-tip mitotic squashes stained with DAPI. Mean genome sizes, estimated by flow cytometry using Solanum lycopersicum as an internal standard, ranged from 3.14 to 4.02 pg/2C. Asymmetry indices (TF%, A1, A2) indicated a moderate degree of karyotype asymmetry in all three taxa, with C. pelisterensis showing the highest asymmetry (A2 = 0.47). Fluorescence banding with CMA3 and DAPI revealed consistent patterns of GC-rich pericentromeric and interstitial bands in C. radovanovicii, differing from the other two taxa. The data are discussed in the context of karyotype evolution within the Balkan Centaurea complex.

title: Metabarcoding of soil nematode communities using 18S rRNA amplicon sequencing: performance comparison with morphological identification in Vojvodina agricultural soils
abstract: Environmental DNA metabarcoding using the SSU rRNA V1–V2 region was applied to 30 soil samples from three contrasting agricultural management types in Vojvodina. Morphological identification was performed in parallel on the same samples. Metabarcoding detected 54 nematode genera compared with 41 by morphology. Agreement at genus level was 78% for the 10 most abundant genera. Several rare genera detected by morphology were absent from metabarcoding results due to primer bias, while metabarcoding revealed three additional genera not recorded morphologically, likely due to cryptic species or damaged specimens. Nematode community indices calculated from metabarcoding data correlated strongly with morphology-derived values for MI (r = 0.91) and EI (r = 0.85). Bioinformatics pipeline settings, particularly OTU clustering threshold (97% vs. 99%), influenced genus-level assignments substantially. Practical guidance for integrating both approaches in routine monitoring is provided. Raw sequences are deposited in a public repository.

title: Population-level variation in male song pulse rate within Chorthippus parallelus across a latitudinal gradient from Serbia to Slovakia
abstract: Male stridulatory pulse rate in Chorthippus parallelus is temperature-dependent, but population-intrinsic variation also exists. We recorded songs from 267 males at 18 localities spanning a 620 km latitudinal gradient and measured pulse rate at a standardised body temperature of 25°C maintained in a temperature-controlled chamber. Mixed-effects models controlling for body size showed a significant positive correlation between latitude and pulse rate (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Common-garden rearing of eggs from four population pairs confirmed that the latitudinal pulse rate differences persist in laboratory-reared adults (F3,148 = 9.3, p < 0.001), indicating a heritable component. Playback trials using synthesised songs at northern and southern pulse rates showed that females from southern populations discriminated more strongly against northern-rate songs than vice versa. The asymmetry in female preference suggests directional evolution in perceptual tuning that partially parallels the signal shift.

title: Rule-Based Difficulty Scaling in a DOS-Era Serbian Grammar Tutor: Design Rationale and Classroom Observations
abstract: This paper documents the architecture and early classroom deployment of a text-based grammar tutoring program written in Turbo Pascal for secondary school students learning standard Serbian morphology. Difficulty was controlled by a hand-coded decision tree that branched on the student's last three response outcomes, advancing or retreating through a fixed exercise hierarchy of 14 levels. Forty-two students at two gymnasiums in Zrenjanin used the system for one semester in 1994–1995. Accuracy on post-tests measuring nominal case agreement improved by 18 percentage points relative to a control group using printed workbooks, though the between-group difference was not statistically significant given the sample size. Detailed interaction logs captured per-exercise latency and error type. The paper discusses design trade-offs between pedagogical sequencing and the memory constraints of the target hardware, and identifies three recurring error patterns not anticipated in the original content taxonomy. The work establishes a baseline interaction dataset that was reused in two subsequent studies.

title: Comparing Linear and Branching Exercise Sequences in a Web-Based English Vocabulary Platform for Engineering Students
abstract: A controlled experiment compared two sequencing strategies for English technical vocabulary acquisition among first-year engineering students at the Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin'. One group (n=61) worked through a fixed linear sequence of 200 vocabulary items grouped by domain; a second group (n=58) used a branching system that routed students to remedial clusters when error rates on a category exceeded 30 percent within a session. Both groups completed eight weeks of voluntary platform use during the 1999–2000 academic year. The branching group showed higher retention on a delayed four-week post-test (mean score 71.4 vs. 63.8 out of 100, t-test p=0.04) and completed more optional review exercises. Dropout from voluntary sessions was similar in both groups. Platform interaction logs totaling approximately 24,000 exercise events were used to reconstruct session paths. The paper argues that even simple conditional routing offers measurable retention benefits without requiring probabilistic student modeling, and suggests criteria for choosing branching threshold values in resource-constrained development contexts.

title: Point Economies and Learner Motivation in a Pilot Serbian-as-a-Second-Language Module for Hungarian-Speaking Students
abstract: This study examined how a simple point-and-level reward structure affected voluntary usage of a web-based Serbian language module among Hungarian-speaking students at secondary schools near Subotica. The module covered basic conversational Serbian across six thematic units. In a six-week trial, 83 students were randomly assigned to a version with visible point counters, level badges, and a class leaderboard, or to an identical version with all reward displays hidden. Session logs showed that the reward-visible group initiated 2.3 times more voluntary review sessions per student per week. However, performance on graded written assessments did not differ significantly between groups (mean scores 64.1 vs. 62.7 out of 100). Qualitative interviews with 24 participants suggested that students valued the sense of progress more than competitive standing, and several found the leaderboard demotivating when they fell behind peers. The paper discusses the mismatch between engagement metrics and learning outcomes, and recommends separating progress indicators from competitive displays in minority-language learning contexts.

title: An Item Response Theory Approach to Adaptive Exercise Selection in a Grammar Drill Platform
abstract: This paper reports the integration of a one-parameter logistic IRT model into an online grammar drill platform to drive real-time exercise selection. Item difficulty parameters were estimated offline from a corpus of 18,400 completed exercises collected from 312 students over two academic years. At runtime, the platform selected the next exercise whose estimated difficulty was closest to the current ability estimate for each student, updating the estimate after each response using a maximum likelihood step. A prospective study with 94 students in introductory university Serbian courses compared the adaptive version against a version using random selection within difficulty bands. Over ten weeks, the adaptive group required 17 percent fewer exercises to reach an 80 percent accuracy criterion on a standardised grammar test. The paper provides a detailed account of item bank construction, calibration procedures, and the practical constraints of running IRT estimation on server hardware available in 2005. Limitations include item exposure imbalance and the absence of guessing-parameter estimation.

title: Designing Feedback Timing in Computer-Based Language Exercises: Immediate, Delayed, and Summary Conditions
abstract: Feedback timing is a persistent variable in drill-and-practice research, yet most deployed platforms default to immediate error correction without empirical justification. This experiment assigned 174 first-year students across three faculties in Novi Sad to one of three feedback conditions in an online English reading comprehension module: immediate sentence-level feedback after each answer, delayed feedback at the end of each ten-item block, or summary feedback at the end of the session only. Students completed eight sessions over four weeks. Comprehension scores on matched transfer texts were highest in the delayed condition (mean 72.1 out of 100) compared to immediate (67.4) and summary (65.8), with a significant main effect (F(2,171)=4.83, p=0.009). Time-on-task was shortest in the immediate condition. Think-aloud data from a sub-sample of 18 students indicated that immediate feedback disrupted inference-building for longer texts. The paper recommends configurable feedback windows rather than fixed platform defaults, and provides a decision rubric based on exercise type and target skill.

title: Learner-Facing Difficulty Labels and Their Effect on Task Persistence in an Online Language Platform
abstract: Most adaptive systems adjust difficulty silently, without informing the learner of the system's current assessment of their level. This study investigated whether displaying explicit difficulty labels ('beginner', 'intermediate', 'advanced') on exercise cards affected persistence and performance among adult learners using a free online Croatian-language module. A between-subjects design with 220 registered users compared labeled and unlabeled interface versions over a self-paced four-week period. Users in the labeled condition completed on average 34 more exercises per person (p=0.03) and were less likely to abandon a session mid-exercise (abandonment rate 9.1% vs. 14.6%). Performance differences on a post-use proficiency task were not significant. Open-ended survey responses suggested that the labels helped users set expectations and reduced frustration when an exercise proved harder than anticipated. The paper discusses implications for transparent learner modeling and cautions that label granularity matters: a five-point scale piloted in a smaller sample produced higher anxiety than the three-point scale reported here.

title: A Comparative Review of Difficulty Adaptation Algorithms in Open-Source Language Learning Platforms, 2005–2012
abstract: This book chapter surveys the adaptation mechanisms present in seven open-source or publicly documented language learning platforms released between 2005 and 2012. For each platform, the authors describe the student model used (if any), the exercise selection or sequencing algorithm, the granularity of the difficulty dimension, and the evidence base cited in the platform documentation. Platforms examined include systems built on Moodle plugins, standalone Java applications, and two early browser-based environments. The analysis finds that five of the seven systems relied on threshold rules rather than probabilistic models, that only two systems updated difficulty estimates within a session rather than only between sessions, and that none provided a documented calibration procedure for item difficulty values. The chapter identifies four recurring design gaps: absence of item exposure controls, conflation of speed and accuracy into a single performance signal, lack of support for multi-skill learning objectives, and missing fallback behaviour when the item bank is exhausted at a given difficulty tier. Each gap is illustrated with interaction log excerpts from published studies.

title: Badge Design Parameters and Their Differential Effects on Low- and High-Performing Learners in a Grammar Tutoring System
abstract: Badge-based reward systems are widely adopted in educational software, but empirical guidance on design parameters such as badge frequency, visual salience, and social visibility remains sparse. This study systematically varied three badge design parameters in a within-subjects factorial experiment using a Latin square design with 96 university students using an online German grammar tutor over six weeks. Dependent variables included voluntary session count, exercise completion rate, and grammar post-test scores. Main effects were found for badge frequency (F(2,93)=6.12, p=0.003) and social visibility (F(1,94)=4.47, p=0.037) on session count, but not on post-test scores. Stratified analysis showed that low-performing students (bottom quartile on pre-test) responded more positively to frequent, low-threshold badges, while high-performing students showed slight negative effects of high-frequency badges on engagement. Visual salience had no significant main effect. The paper provides concrete parameter recommendations for practitioners and discusses floor and ceiling effects in badge-based motivation designs.

title: Longitudinal Decay of Gamification Effects in a University Language Learning Platform: A Four-Year Follow-Up
abstract: Much gamification research measures effects over weeks rather than semesters. This paper reports a four-year observational follow-up of a cohort of 211 students who were initially exposed to a gamified English for Academic Purposes platform during the 2010–2011 academic year. Annual voluntary usage logs were collected for each subsequent year, supplemented by annual 12-item motivation surveys. Median voluntary session counts declined from 14.3 in year one to 3.1 in year four, with the steepest drop between years one and two. Students who had scored in the upper half on initial engagement measures retained above-median usage longer, but the effect attenuated by year three. Survey data indicated that novelty was cited as the primary initial motivator by 68 percent of respondents, and only 21 percent reported the reward mechanics as a continued reason for use in year three or four. The paper argues that gamification in formal educational platforms functions as an onboarding mechanism rather than a sustained engagement driver, and recommends phased reward designs that evolve with learner familiarity.

title: Revisiting Adaptive Difficulty in Language Apps: What Has Changed Since 2010 and What Has Not
abstract: This co-authored position paper, written with colleagues active in current research, revisits the state of adaptive difficulty in mobile and web language learning applications a decade after an earlier survey. The paper examines ten widely used application categories documented in the research literature between 2017 and 2024, assessing changes in the underlying adaptation mechanisms against the baseline gaps identified in a 2013 review. Key findings are that probabilistic student modeling has become more common, driven largely by the availability of machine learning libraries, but that item calibration practices remain poorly documented in most systems. Social comparison features have proliferated, often without evidence-based design rationale. The paper identifies new concerns absent from earlier work, including the use of streaks as a retention mechanism and the privacy implications of granular learner data collection by commercial platform operators. Recommendations are oriented toward platform evaluators and procurement decision-makers in educational institutions rather than platform developers.

title: Undrained cyclic shear strength of low-plasticity silts from the Danube floodplain near Novi Sad
abstract: Undrained cyclic triaxial tests were performed on 24 undisturbed specimens of low-plasticity silt (PI 6–12 %) recovered by fixed-piston sampling from depths of 3–9 m at three sites along the right bank of the Danube near Novi Sad. Specimens were isotropically consolidated to effective stresses of 50, 100 and 150 kPa before application of sinusoidal cyclic deviator stress at 1 Hz. Cyclic stress ratios (CSR) between 0.10 and 0.30 were applied. Failure was defined at 5 % double-amplitude axial strain or excess pore pressure ratio ru = 1.0, whichever occurred first. Results show that silt specimens reached ru = 0.90–1.0 within 10–30 cycles at CSR ≥ 0.20, while specimens with PI > 10 % required 40–80 cycles at the same CSR. A cyclic resistance ratio (CRR) for 15 cycles was established at 0.155 ± 0.012, lower than values commonly reported for Holocene alluvial sands. The findings indicate that fine-grained Danube floodplain deposits should not be excluded from liquefaction screening based solely on grain size criteria.

title: Effect of consolidation stress ratio on pore pressure generation in cyclic triaxial tests on Pannonian silts
abstract: The influence of the initial consolidation stress ratio K0 on excess pore pressure generation was investigated using cyclic triaxial tests on reconstituted specimens of Pannonian silt obtained from the Sava River valley near Sremska Mitrovica. Three K0 values (0.50, 0.65, 0.80) were applied prior to undrained cyclic loading at CSR = 0.15, 0.20 and 0.25. A total of 72 tests were conducted. Excess pore pressure ratio ru was recorded at each loading cycle. Results show that specimens consolidated under K0 = 0.50 reached ru = 0.9 approximately 35 % faster than isotropically consolidated specimens at the same CSR. An empirical pore pressure generation model calibrated to the Pannonian silt data set is proposed, with three fitted parameters determined by nonlinear least squares regression. The model reproduces measured ru–cycle curves with a root mean square error below 0.04 across all stress ratios tested.

title: Comparison of cyclic simple shear and cyclic triaxial responses for low-plasticity silty clays
abstract: A side-by-side laboratory comparison of cyclic simple shear (CSS) and cyclic triaxial (CTX) test results was carried out on silty clay specimens (CL classification, PI 14–18 %) from the Tisa River floodplain near Senta, northern Vojvodina. Undisturbed specimens were obtained by Shelby tube sampling from depths of 4–8 m. In CTX tests, the CSR was corrected to equivalent simple shear CSR using the standard correction factor Cr = 0.65. Twelve pairs of CSS and CTX tests were performed at matched effective confining stresses of 100 kPa. CSS specimens exhibited 15–25 % lower cyclic resistance at 15 cycles compared to CTX specimens after correction, consistent with published findings for sandy soils. Shear strain accumulation patterns differed: CSS tests showed progressive ratcheting behaviour whereas CTX tests showed more symmetric strain accumulation. Both devices recorded similar final pore pressure states. The data support using a device-specific correction factor of 0.72 for this deposit.

title: Seismic microzonation input parameters from in-situ and laboratory testing: a case study at a bridge site over the Danube
abstract: Laboratory cyclic triaxial data were integrated with cone penetration test (CPT) and seismic CPT profiles to derive site-specific dynamic soil parameters for a bridge crossing in the Vojvodina lowland. CPT soundings at six locations revealed alternating layers of fine sand, silt and soft clay to depths of 20 m. Shear wave velocities measured by seismic CPT ranged from 120 to 210 m/s in the upper 10 m. Cyclic triaxial tests on undisturbed silt specimens confirmed CRR15 values between 0.13 and 0.18. Liquefaction triggering analysis following the Robertson and Wride (1998) CPT-based procedure was applied and results compared with laboratory CRR values. Agreement was within 12 % for silt layers and 18 % for transitional silt–clay layers. The study highlights the importance of laboratory verification when CPT-based screening is applied to fine-grained Holocene deposits rather than clean sands.

title: Cyclic softening of medium-plasticity clays under earthquake-equivalent loading histories
abstract: Six earthquake acceleration records from the Balkans region (Mw 5.2–6.4) were used to derive irregular loading sequences applied in displacement-controlled cyclic triaxial tests on medium-plasticity clay specimens (PI 22–31 %) from the Fruška Gora piedmont zone. Specimens were consolidated to in-situ effective stresses and tested under irregular loading using a servo-hydraulic actuator. Equivalent number of uniform cycles was calculated using the Seed et al. fatigue approach at τ/τmax = 0.65. Stiffness degradation index δ, defined as the ratio of secant shear modulus at cycle N to initial modulus, dropped to 0.45–0.62 after equivalent 15 cycles. Peak excess pore pressure ratios reached 0.55–0.75; full liquefaction did not occur in any specimen. Post-cyclic undrained shear strength ranged from 62 to 78 % of the monotonic value. Results provide quantitative evidence for cyclic softening of these clays in the absence of liquefaction, relevant to slope stability assessment on Fruška Gora foothill slopes.

title: Influence of sample disturbance on cyclic triaxial test results for Holocene floodplain silts
abstract: The effect of sampling method on cyclic triaxial test outcomes was evaluated by comparing results from three sampling techniques: Shelby thin-wall tube, fixed-piston sampler and block sampling from test pits. Twenty-seven specimens per technique were prepared from a single Holocene silt deposit near Bačka Palanka. Physical properties (void ratio, degree of saturation, Atterberg limits) were measured before each test. Skempton B-values exceeded 0.96 for all specimens. CRR15 values from block specimens averaged 0.178, from fixed-piston specimens 0.162, and from Shelby tube specimens 0.141. The 21 % reduction in CRR between block and Shelby tube samples is attributed to partial loss of fabric and minor densification during tube insertion. Corrections for sample disturbance following the Lunne et al. (1997) quality rating are evaluated and partially vindicated. The study recommends fixed-piston sampling as the minimum acceptable quality for cyclic testing of Vojvodina silts.

title: Dynamic soil properties of Vojvodina alluvial deposits: a regional database
abstract: This book chapter synthesises cyclic triaxial and resonant column test data collected over a decade from 14 sites across Vojvodina Province, covering deposits of the Danube, Tisa, Sava and Begej floodplains. The database contains 312 cyclic triaxial tests and 84 resonant column tests on silt and low-to-medium-plasticity clay specimens. For each site, median shear modulus reduction (G/Gmax) and damping ratio curves are reported as functions of cyclic shear strain amplitude. Regional mean G/Gmax curves for silt and clay are compared with published reference curves for similar deposits in the Po Valley and Hungarian lowlands. Vojvodina silts show slightly lower normalised shear moduli at strains above 0.1 % than Po Valley silts, tentatively attributed to differences in depositional history and organic content. The chapter also provides a summary table of CRR15 values and index properties intended for use in regional probabilistic seismic hazard assessments.

title: Plasticity index as a screening criterion for liquefaction susceptibility of fine-grained soils: evaluation against Vojvodina field evidence
abstract: Plasticity index (PI) thresholds proposed in various national and international standards (EC8, NCEER, JRA) for excluding fine-grained soils from liquefaction assessment were evaluated against an empirical database of 47 sites in Vojvodina where cyclic failure or ground deformation was documented or excluded following historical earthquakes. A logistic regression model was fitted to the binary response variable (failure / no failure) using PI, liquid limit and fines content as predictors. PI alone correctly classified 79 % of sites; adding liquid limit improved classification to 84 %. The EC8 criterion (PI > 15 % as non-liquefiable) was non-conservative at 6 out of 47 sites, all with PI between 10 and 15 %. The study recommends a lower threshold of PI = 12 % for Vojvodina conditions and proposes a probabilistic liquefaction screening chart combining PI and liquid limit.

title: Cyclic resistance of undisturbed versus reconstituted fine-grained specimens: implications for sample preparation in seismic design
abstract: Forty pairs of undisturbed and reconstituted specimens from four Vojvodina sites spanning silt, silty clay and lean clay were tested in cyclic triaxial apparatus under matched consolidation stresses. Reconstituted specimens were prepared by slurry consolidation to the same void ratio and water content as undisturbed specimens. CRR15 values for undisturbed specimens exceeded those of reconstituted specimens by 12–34 %; the largest difference occurred for lean clay (CL) and the smallest for low-plasticity silt (ML). The difference correlated (R² = 0.71) with the sensitivity St measured by fall-cone tests on companion specimens. Scanning electron microscope images of fractured surfaces confirmed that undisturbed specimens retain a preferred particle orientation and aggregated fabric absent in reconstituted material. The findings caution against using reconstituted specimens for final design CRR values, even when void ratios are carefully matched.

title: Liquefaction susceptibility mapping of the Novi Sad urban area using a combined CPT and laboratory approach
abstract: A liquefaction susceptibility map for the Novi Sad metropolitan area was produced by combining a GIS-compiled database of 214 CPT soundings with targeted cyclic triaxial laboratory testing at 18 representative sites. CPT-based liquefaction triggering was assessed using the Robertson (2009) Ic-based procedure for a design earthquake of Mw 6.0 and peak ground acceleration 0.10 g, consistent with the Serbian seismic hazard map. Laboratory CRR15 values were used to calibrate and locally adjust the CPT-based Kc correction factor for fine-grained Holocene deposits. Five susceptibility classes were defined: negligible, low, moderate, high and very high. Approximately 22 % of the urban area was mapped as moderate-to-high susceptibility, primarily in the floodplain zones north of the Danube embankment. The map is intended to support urban planning decisions and site-specific investigation requirements under the provisions of Eurocode 8 Part 5.

title: Post-cyclic consolidation and settlement of low-plasticity silt after partial liquefaction
abstract: Nine undisturbed silt specimens from the Bačka lowland were subjected to cyclic triaxial loading to controlled excess pore pressure ratios (ru = 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0), after which drainage was permitted and post-cyclic consolidation strains were measured for 24 hours under the original effective stress. Post-cyclic volumetric strains ranged from 0.4 % at ru = 0.4 to 2.1 % at ru = 1.0. A linear relationship between post-cyclic volumetric strain and peak ru was observed (R² = 0.88). Post-cyclic coefficient of consolidation cv was 25–40 % lower than the pre-cyclic value, attributed to disruption of the inter-particle fabric during cyclic loading. Using these data in a one-dimensional settlement calculation for a representative two-metre-thick liquefiable silt layer under a 2 kPa surface load, estimated ground settlement ranged from 18 to 42 mm depending on the applied CSR. The results provide input parameters for post-earthquake settlement assessments in Vojvodina lowland areas.

title: Rate effects in undrained cyclic triaxial tests on saturated silts: frequency from 0.01 Hz to 2 Hz
abstract: The influence of loading frequency on undrained cyclic triaxial behaviour was investigated for saturated Holocene silt specimens (LL 28–34 %, PI 7–11 %) from the Sava floodplain. Tests were performed at four frequencies: 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 2 Hz, at CSR = 0.18 and 0.22 under isotropic consolidation to 100 kPa. At 2 Hz, excess pore pressure generation was 10–15 % slower than at 0.1 Hz at the same cycle count. Number of cycles to ru = 0.9 increased from a median of 14 at 0.01 Hz to 22 at 2 Hz at CSR = 0.18, a difference of 57 %. Shear modulus at small cyclic strains was frequency-insensitive below 0.1 Hz but increased by approximately 8 % at 2 Hz. The results suggest that laboratory tests at the standard frequency of 1 Hz slightly overestimate cyclic resistance relative to the low-frequency components of long-period earthquake motions, warranting a minor conservative correction of approximately 5 % in CRR for design.

title: Creep behaviour of fibrous peat from the Sava floodplain under sustained vertical stress
abstract: Laboratory creep tests were conducted on eleven undisturbed peat specimens from the Sava floodplain near Sremska Mitrovica using a modified oedometer apparatus allowing continuous displacement recording over periods of 30 days per stress increment. Organic content ranged from 55 to 82 percent. The secondary compression index Cα was determined for stress levels from 20 to 160 kPa and found to increase with applied stress up to about 80 kPa before stabilising at mean values of 0.058 ± 0.011. The ratio Cα/Cc remained approximately constant at 0.056, consistent with the isotache framework. A comparison between Singh–Mitchell and Bjerrum creep models showed that the Singh–Mitchell model reproduced measured displacement–log time curves more accurately for strains below 15 percent. The study provides reference parameters for design of road embankments on similar floodplain deposits in the region.

title: Numerical modelling of staged embankment construction on creeping peat using an isotache model
abstract: Two-dimensional plane-strain finite element analyses were carried out in PLAXIS 2D to simulate staged construction of a 4.5 m high flood protection embankment on a peat layer of variable thickness (3.1 to 8.4 m) at a site in the Tisa River valley. The Soft Soil Creep model was calibrated against laboratory CRS and creep oedometer data from 24 specimens. Construction was divided into three loading stages separated by waiting periods of 45 days each. Computed settlements at 36 months after final construction stage differed from observed values by less than 8 percent at three instrumented cross-sections. Computed horizontal displacements matched inclinometer readings to within 15 mm. Sensitivity analyses showed that the intrinsic creep parameter μ* had the greatest influence on long-term settlement predictions, more so than the permeability anisotropy ratio kh/kv. The model was used to evaluate the effect of delaying the final stage by an additional 90 days, which reduced post-construction creep settlement by approximately 22 percent.

title: Rowe cell permeability measurements on organic clays at different consolidation stress levels
abstract: Hydraulic conductivity of four organic clay specimens was measured in a Rowe cell consolidation apparatus at six successive stress levels between 20 and 320 kPa, allowing simultaneous determination of compressibility and permeability parameters. Specimens had initial void ratios ranging from 2.1 to 4.8. Vertical hydraulic conductivity kv decreased by two orders of magnitude over the applied stress range, from 1.8 × 10⁻⁹ m/s to 2.4 × 10⁻¹¹ m/s. The permeability change index Ck ranged from 0.72 to 1.04, closely matching the initial void ratio of specimens. Horizontal conductivity kh was 1.2 to 3.4 times kv at low stresses and converged toward isotropy at high stresses. The Ck values were incorporated into PLAXIS analyses as a stress-dependent permeability function, which improved agreement between modelled and measured dissipation curves. The results confirm that ignoring permeability reduction in consolidation analyses leads to underestimation of construction-period excess pore pressures.

title: Primena Cox-ovog modela proporcionalnih hazarda na predikciju odliva klijenata u B2B softverskim pretplatama: studija slučaja na tržištu jugoistočne Evrope
abstract: Rad istražuje primenu Cox-ovog modela proporcionalnih hazarda za identifikaciju predikatora odliva (churn) u segmentu malih i srednjih preduzeća koja koriste pretplatne softverske usluge. Skup podataka obuhvata 1.847 aktivnih i 612 ugašenih ugovora prikupljenih od tri SaaS provajdera sa sedištem u Srbiji i Severnoj Makedoniji, u periodu od 36 meseci. Kao kovariante korišćene su: dužina trajanja pretplate, frekvencija prijava na sistem, broj prijavljenih tehničkih tiketa, vrednost ugovora i tip industrije klijenta. Rezultati pokazuju da frekvencija korišćenja sistema i broj eskaliranih tiketa imaju statistički značajan efekat na hazard (p < 0,01), dok vrednost ugovora sama po sebi nije pouzdan prediktor. Konkordancijski indeks modela iznosi 0,74. Rad doprinosi razumevanju specifičnosti B2B tržišta u tranzicionim ekonomijama gde je dostupnost longitudinalnih podataka ograničena.

title: Temporal Patterns in Customer Lifetime Value Decay Among Mid-Market B2B Software Subscribers: A Parametric Survival Approach
abstract: This study models the rate at which contracted customer lifetime value (CLV) erodes over the duration of a subscription in mid-market B2B software accounts. Using a dataset of 3,214 annual subscription contracts drawn from two anonymised enterprise resource planning vendors operating in Central and Eastern Europe, we fit Weibull, log-logistic, and generalised gamma accelerated failure time models to time-to-significant-downsell events, defined as a revenue reduction of 20% or more at renewal. The Weibull model with shape parameter 1.43 provides the best fit by AIC. Key predictors of accelerated CLV decay include a high ratio of support interactions to active users (HR = 1.31, 95% CI: 1.18–1.46) and contract vintage exceeding 24 months without an upsell event (HR = 1.19). Controlling for firm size and sector, companies in professional services show lower decay hazard relative to manufacturing. The findings suggest that CLV decay is not uniform and that usage intensity metrics available within the first six months of a contract carry strong prognostic value for long-term revenue trajectories.

title: Identifikacija ranih indikatora odliva u pretplatnim B2B uslugama korišćenjem recurrent event survival modela
abstract: Rad se bavi problemom ponavljajućih događaja downgrade-a pretplate pre konačnog raskida ugovora, koji klasični single-event modeli ne uspevaju adekvatno da obuhvate. Korišćenjem AG (Andersen–Gill) modela na uzorku od 980 ugovornih odnosa praćenih tokom 48 meseci, analiziran je vremenski sled parcijalnih smanjenja vrednosti pretplate kao prediktor konačnog odliva. Podaci su obezbeđeni kroz anonimizovanu saradnju s jednim regionalnim provajderom poslovnog softvera. Rezultati ukazuju da prisustvo bar dva downgrade događaja u prvih 18 meseci udvostruičava verovatnoću raskida ugovora u narednom kvartalu. Rad takođe ispituje vremensku zavisnost kovarijanti, posebno promene u broju licenci i administrativnih kontakata, kao signal organizacionih promena kod klijenta. Ograničenje studije leži u oslonjenosti na podatke jednog provajdera, što može umanjiti eksternu validnost nalaza.

title: Incorporating Session-Level Behavioural Signals into a Content-Based Recommender for a Sparse Transactional Log
abstract: This paper proposes a recommendation architecture that augments a content-based item similarity model with short-session behavioural signals derived from point-of-sale sequences. The hypothesis is that items co-purchased within the same basket, even without long-term user history, carry exploitable proximity information. Data come from two small clothing retailers operating in Serbia, collectively yielding 9,200 baskets over 18 months, with a median basket size of three items. Item content features include garment category, fabric type, and price range. A weighted combination of cosine attribute similarity and within-session co-occurrence frequency is used to score candidate recommendations. Grid search over the weighting parameter identifies an optimal blend of 0.6 content to 0.4 session co-occurrence, yielding a precision at three of 0.38 against a pure content baseline of 0.29. The study highlights that even minimal session data meaningfully stabilises recommendation quality when transaction histories per user are fewer than five.

title: Semantic Heterogeneity in Serbian Public Procurement Notices: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: This study examines the degree of semantic heterogeneity present in machine-readable procurement notices published on the Serbian Public Procurement Portal between 2008 and 2011. A corpus of 18 340 notices was parsed and their textual fields tokenised and lemmatised using a custom Serbian-language NLP pipeline. Cluster analysis identified 214 terminological clusters with overlapping intended meanings but inconsistent labelling, particularly in works and services categories. The paper quantifies homonymy and synonymy rates per procurement category and correlates heterogeneity scores with contracting authority type (ministry, local government, public enterprise). Local government notices exhibit the highest heterogeneity index (0.71 on a 0–1 scale) compared to ministries (0.44). Findings provide an empirical baseline for ontology normalisation efforts and suggest that mandatory use of a reference vocabulary would reduce ambiguity in approximately 62 % of problematic notice fields.

title: PAH profiles in surface soils along a traffic-intensity gradient in Novi Sad: source diagnostics using isomer ratios and principal component analysis
abstract: Surface soil samples (0–5 cm, n = 48) were collected along four transects crossing Novi Sad's urban core, suburban zone, and peri-urban fringe, stratified by road traffic intensity. Sixteen EPA-priority PAHs were extracted by Soxhlet extraction with dichloromethane and quantified by GC-MS with deuterated internal standards. Total PAH concentrations ranged from 340 µg/kg dry weight in peri-urban parks to 4,870 µg/kg near a major arterial road junction. Diagnostic ratios (fluoranthene/pyrene, indeno[1,2,3-cd]pyrene/benzo[ghi]perylene, anthracene/anthracene+phenanthrene) consistently indicated mixed pyrogenic sources dominated by vehicular emissions and asphalt-related inputs, with a subordinate coal-combustion signal in the city centre. Principal component analysis resolved three source factors explaining 78% of total variance. Benzo[a]pyrene toxic equivalency factors were applied to estimate incremental lifetime cancer risk, which exceeded the 1×10⁻⁶ threshold at six sampling points in the core commercial district. Results suggest that road traffic is the predominant contemporary PAH source and that spatial heterogeneity is primarily driven by traffic load rather than land-use category.

title: Vertical PAH distribution in urban soil cores as a proxy for combustion history: a case study from a mid-sized Pannonian city
abstract: Three undisturbed soil cores (depth 0–60 cm, sectioned at 5 cm intervals) were retrieved from a city park in Novi Sad that has remained unexcavated since at least the 1950s. Each section was dated by ¹³⁷Cs and ²¹⁰Pb activity measurements carried out at a partner laboratory, allowing PAH concentration profiles to be anchored to approximate deposition decades. Total PAH concentrations peaked in sections corresponding to the 1975–1990 interval (up to 3,200 µg/kg), coinciding with maximum coal and heavy fuel oil use for district heating as documented in municipal energy records. A marked decline in higher-molecular-weight PAHs (4–6 rings) in post-2000 sections reflects the regional transition to natural gas. Weathering corrections were applied using the fluoranthene/benzo[k]fluoranthene ratio as a relatively degradation-resistant index, reducing apparent concentration scatter between replicate cores by 22%. The corrected profiles show statistically significant agreement (Spearman ρ = 0.84, p < 0.01) between PAH flux and independently reconstructed local emission inventories. The study demonstrates that park soils with minimal disturbance can serve as usable archives of urban combustion history even in the absence of continuous emission monitoring records.

title: Comparison of PAH source fingerprints in street dust and adjacent topsoil in three Serbian cities of different industrial character
abstract: Paired street dust and topsoil (0–2 cm) samples were collected from Novi Sad, Zrenjanin, and Pančevo during a single summer campaign (n = 90 paired sets). The three cities differ markedly in dominant industrial activity: Novi Sad is primarily a commercial and administrative centre, Zrenjanin has a significant food-processing and light-industry profile, and Pančevo hosts a petrochemical complex. PAHs were quantified by GC-MS; positive matrix factorisation (PMF) with five factors was applied to the pooled dataset. Street dust consistently showed higher total PAH concentrations than co-located topsoil (median ratio 2.3), attributable to direct atmospheric deposition and resuspension dynamics. In Pančevo, the petroleum-refining source factor contributed 41% of total PAH mass compared with less than 9% in the other two cities. Benzo[a]pyrene equivalents in Pančevo street dust (median 1,140 µg BaP-eq/kg) exceeded Serbian regulatory guidance values at 67% of sampling points. The study provides baseline fingerprint data that can support future regulatory monitoring programmes and illustrates that PMF applied across cities with contrasting sources improves factor resolution relative to single-city analyses.

title: Temperature dependence of hydrogen sulphide generation kinetics in sulphonate resin biofilms over a 5–35 °C range
abstract: Temperature is rarely considered explicitly in risk assessments for biogenic H2S in water-softening units, despite significant seasonal variation in distributed water temperatures. Colonised resin columns were equilibrated to five target temperatures (5, 12, 20, 28 and 35 °C) and H2S generation rates were measured under identical hydraulic and chemical conditions. An Arrhenius fit to the data yielded an activation energy of 62 kJ mol⁻¹ (R² = 0.96), corresponding to a Q10 of approximately 2.8. At 5 °C, H2S generation was only 8% of the rate observed at 28 °C. Below 8 °C, SRB activity was not detectable within 48 h stagnation periods. The data suggest that cold-water systems in northern Serbian municipalities face negligible H2S risk during winter months but that the risk becomes appreciable in summer, particularly in basement-located units where temperatures may reach 30 °C.

title: Alkaline saponification under reduced water activity: implications for anhydrous soap noodle carbonation
abstract: Soap noodles with moisture contents of 2, 5, 10, and 15 wt% and 1.2 wt% excess NaOH were stored in sealed containers at 35 °C with CO2 headspace maintained at 0.04 kPa for 60 days. CO2 consumption was tracked by pressure transducer at 1 h intervals. Carbonation rate dropped by two orders of magnitude between 15 and 2 wt% moisture, following a power law with exponent 2.3 relative to water activity. At 2 wt% moisture no significant carbonation was detected within 60 days. XRD of samples from the 5 and 10 wt% moisture series showed amorphous sodium carbonate as the primary product rather than crystalline calcite, because calcium ion availability was limited. SEM showed no discrete precipitate crystals at 5 wt% moisture; instead a thin conformal coating on fatty acid salt lamellae was identified by EDS. The results indicate that moisture control during extrusion and packaging is the most effective lever for preventing carbonate formation in noodle-to-bar manufacturing.

title: Harmonic Distortion Signatures for Open-Circuit Switch Fault Detection in Three-Phase Voltage Source Inverters
abstract: This paper investigates the use of current harmonic distortion patterns as diagnostic indicators for open-circuit switch faults in three-phase voltage source inverters operating under grid-connected conditions. Experiments were conducted on a 5 kVA laboratory prototype with six independently controllable IGBT switches. Faults were introduced sequentially in each switch position, and the resulting harmonic spectra of the output current were recorded using a 16-bit data acquisition system at a sampling rate of 50 kHz. A feature set based on the magnitudes of the 5th, 7th, 11th, and 13th harmonic components, as well as their phase relationships, was extracted for each fault scenario. A k-nearest-neighbour classifier trained on 120 fault instances achieved a classification accuracy of 94.1% across six fault locations, outperforming a threshold-based reference method by 11.3 percentage points. The influence of load variation and DC-link voltage fluctuation on classification robustness was also examined, showing that moderate load changes of up to 30% did not significantly degrade performance.

title: Short-Time Fourier Transform Applied to Gate Driver Voltage Monitoring for IGBT Health Assessment
abstract: Gate driver voltage waveforms contain subtle timing and shape deviations that correlate with IGBT aging and thermal stress accumulation. This study evaluates the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) as a non-intrusive tool for extracting degradation indicators from gate-emitter voltage signals in a single-phase grid-tied inverter. A controlled accelerated aging procedure was applied to eight IGBT modules over 400 thermal cycles ranging from 25 °C to 125 °C, simulating approximately three years of field operation. STFT spectrograms were computed with a 256-sample Hann window and 75% overlap. Two features—the centroid frequency shift and the energy concentration in the 200–500 kHz band—showed monotonic trends with cycle count, achieving a Pearson correlation of 0.88 and 0.91, respectively, across the eight samples. The results suggest that real-time STFT analysis of gate signals, implementable on a low-cost FPGA, could serve as a practical early-warning mechanism without requiring additional current sensors.

title: Modbus RTU Integration for Distributed Fault Logging in Photovoltaic Inverter Arrays
abstract: This paper describes the design and testing of a Modbus RTU-based data collection architecture for fault event logging across arrays of photovoltaic string inverters. Six commercial single-phase inverters rated at 3.6 kW each were networked over a 485-ohm RS-485 bus with a polling interval of 500 ms. A master controller based on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller stored timestamped fault codes, DC-link voltage, and AC output current RMS values in a circular buffer on a microSD card. Field tests at a 22 kWp rooftop installation near Novi Sad over a six-month period recorded 143 fault events, of which 78% were traceable to grid voltage disturbances and 14% to partial shading conditions. Communication latency remained below 12 ms for up to 12 slave devices. The architecture required no modification to inverter firmware, relying solely on read-only register access through the standard Modbus function code 0x03.

title: IEC 61850 GOOSE Messaging for Real-Time Fault Notification in Grid-Tied Converter Substations
abstract: The IEC 61850 standard's Generic Object-Oriented Substation Event (GOOSE) mechanism provides low-latency peer-to-peer communication suited to protection and monitoring applications. This paper examines the feasibility of using GOOSE messages to propagate converter fault notifications between an inverter controller, a feeder protection relay, and a substation automation gateway in a test setup representative of a small industrial photovoltaic substation. A hardware testbed was assembled using two industrial Ethernet switches, an embedded Linux platform running an open-source IEC 61850 stack, and a commercial protection relay. GOOSE transmission times for fault notifications were measured at 2.1 ms on average over 500 triggered events, with a 99th percentile of 3.8 ms, satisfying the Class P2 requirement. The paper also discusses the configuration of Logical Nodes LLN0, GGIO, and MMXU within the substation configuration language and reports on interoperability tests with two different relay vendors' equipment. Limitations related to cybersecurity and VLAN configuration are discussed.

title: Condition Monitoring Techniques for Power Electronic Converters: A Survey of Signal-Based Methods
abstract: This book chapter reviews signal-based condition monitoring methods for power electronic converters published between 2005 and 2019, with emphasis on approaches that do not require additional sensors beyond those already present in standard converter control loops. The chapter is structured around three component classes: switching devices (IGBTs and MOSFETs), DC-link capacitors, and magnetic components. For each class, the available signal sources (gate voltage, DC-link voltage ripple, output current, heat-sink temperature) are described alongside the processing methods—Fourier analysis, wavelet transforms, principal component analysis, and machine learning classifiers—most commonly applied to them. Practical constraints including computational load, memory requirements, and real-time implementation on microcontrollers and FPGAs are discussed quantitatively where data are available from the reviewed literature. The chapter identifies open challenges including the scarcity of publicly available aging datasets and the difficulty of validating laboratory results under field operating conditions. A comparison table summarising 47 reviewed studies by component, signal source, method, and reported detection accuracy is included.

title: Embedded Implementation of On-Line ESR Estimation for DC-Link Capacitors Using Recursive Least Squares
abstract: Equivalent series resistance (ESR) estimation provides a reliable proxy for electrolytic capacitor health in converter DC-link stages. This paper presents a recursive least squares (RLS) algorithm for on-line ESR estimation implemented on a 32-bit microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M7, 216 MHz) operating within the control loop of a 7.5 kVA three-phase inverter. The estimation model relates the measured DC-link current ripple and voltage ripple through a first-order discrete-time model updated at each 100 µs control cycle. With a forgetting factor of 0.98, the algorithm converged to within 5% of the true ESR within 200 ms from start-up in bench tests across capacitors with ESR values ranging from 8 mΩ to 180 mΩ. CPU load added by the RLS routine was 4.2% of the available compute budget, leaving sufficient headroom for standard field-oriented control tasks. The algorithm was validated against off-line impedance analyser measurements on twelve capacitor samples at three states of degradation. Estimation error remained below 8% in all tested conditions.

title: False Alarm Rate Reduction in Current-Based IGBT Fault Detection Through Adaptive Threshold Calibration
abstract: Current-based fault detection algorithms for IGBT open-circuit failures are prone to false alarms under transient load conditions, grid voltage dips, and start-up sequences, limiting their practical deployment. This paper proposes an adaptive threshold calibration scheme in which alarm thresholds for normalised current residuals are updated every 50 fundamental cycles using a sliding-window estimate of residual variance. The scheme was evaluated on a 15 kVA three-phase inverter test rig subjected to 240 fault-free test scenarios encompassing grid voltage dips of 10–40%, step load changes of 25–100% rated power, and motor start-up events, as well as 80 genuine open-circuit fault scenarios. Compared to a fixed-threshold baseline, the adaptive scheme reduced false alarms from 31 to 4 over the fault-free set while maintaining 100% fault detection across all 80 genuine fault events. Worst-case detection delay was 1.8 fundamental cycles. The calibration algorithm adds negligible computational overhead and is compatible with existing DSP-based control platforms.

title: Edge Computing Platform for Aggregating Condition Monitoring Data from Multiple Grid-Connected Converters via IEC 61850 MMS
abstract: As the number of distributed grid-connected converters in industrial and prosumer installations grows, centralised condition monitoring architectures face scalability and latency constraints. This paper presents an edge computing platform that collects condition monitoring data—ESR estimates, thermal resistance trends, and fault event logs—from up to 16 converter nodes over an IEC 61850 Manufacturing Message Specification (MMS) connection and performs local aggregation, anomaly flagging, and compressed data forwarding to a cloud historian. The platform runs on an embedded quad-core ARM processor under a real-time Linux kernel and handles polling periods of 1 s per node without packet loss at 100 Mbps Ethernet. Data compression using a piecewise linear approximation with a maximum error bound of 0.5% reduced storage requirements by 73% relative to raw logging. A 14-day continuous test on a 110 kW photovoltaic installation involving seven string inverters confirmed stable operation and successfully triggered two early-warning alerts for capacitor ESR drift confirmed by subsequent off-line measurement.

title: Electromagnetic interference characterisation of a 1 MHz GaN-based DC–DC converter: conducted and radiated emissions
abstract: A 400 V / 48 V, 500 W DC–DC converter using 650 V GaN HEMTs and switching at 1 MHz is characterised for conducted and radiated electromagnetic emissions per CISPR 32 Class B limits. Conducted emissions were measured using a line-impedance stabilisation network in the 150 kHz–30 MHz band. Differential-mode and common-mode noise contributions were separated using a current probe and a 180° hybrid coupler. Radiated emissions were measured in a semi-anechoic chamber in the 30 MHz–1 GHz band. Without input filtering, differential-mode conducted noise at 1 MHz exceeded the Class B quasi-peak limit by 18 dBµV. A two-stage LC input filter reduced differential-mode noise by 24 dB and common-mode noise by 19 dB, achieving compliance with 4 dB margin. Parasitic capacitance of the heat-sink was identified as the dominant common-mode noise path and a Y-capacitor between heat-sink and DC bus reduced common-mode noise by a further 7 dB. Correlation between near-field scan results and far-field measurements is discussed.

title: Geometry-Based Stochastic Channel Model for V2X Links at T-Intersections Calibrated from Measurements in Novi Sad
abstract: A geometry-based stochastic channel model (GBSM) for vehicle-to-everything links at T-intersections is presented and calibrated against a dedicated measurement dataset collected at five T-intersection sites in Novi Sad. The model extends the standard two-ring scatterer approach by introducing a third semi-elliptical cluster aligned with the lateral road arm, which accounts for the late-arriving reflections from buildings at the corner positions characteristic of dense European urban blocks. Cluster parameters—mean delay, angular spread, and Rician K-factor—are extracted via expectation-maximisation clustering applied to delay-Doppler resolved multipath components obtained through ESPRIT-based super-resolution processing of 1 200 sounding sequences per intersection. The calibrated model reproduces measured power delay profile shapes with a normalised RMSE of 0.18 and matches empirical small-scale fading amplitude distributions with Kolmogorov-Smirnov p-values above 0.05 in 91 % of cases. The model is intended for system-level simulation of C-V2X and ITS-G5 safety applications where intersection channel accuracy is critical.

title: Peroxide Formation Kinetics in Cold-Pressed Pumpkin Seed Oil at Elevated Storage Temperatures
abstract: This study examined the rate of hydroperoxide accumulation in cold-pressed Cucurbita pepo seed oil stored at 25, 40, and 60 °C over 90 days in amber glass under air. Peroxide value (PV) was measured every ten days by iodometric titration (ISO 3960). A pseudo-first-order kinetic model was fitted to PV–time data at each temperature. Rate constants increased from 0.018 meq O₂/(kg·day) at 25 °C to 0.091 meq O₂/(kg·day) at 60 °C. Activation energy calculated from the Arrhenius plot was 48.3 kJ/mol, consistent with autoxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acids rather than photosensitised oxidation. Fatty acid composition determined by GC-FID confirmed high linoleic acid content (57.4%), correlating with the relatively low activation energy. The study provides a predictive shelf-life tool applicable to production-scale storage and shows that temperature control below 20 °C roughly doubles induction period length compared with ambient storage.

title: Comparison of DPPH and ABTS Assays for Quantifying Radical-Scavenging Capacity of Phenolic Extracts from Cold-Pressed Grape Seed Oil
abstract: Cold-pressed grape seed oil from three Serbian Vitis vinifera varieties (Prokupac, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Chardonnay) was extracted and its phenolic fraction isolated by solid-phase extraction on C18 cartridges. Radical-scavenging capacity was quantified by both DPPH (515 nm) and ABTS (734 nm) decolorisation assays under identical concentration ranges (0.05–2.0 mg GAE/mL). Results showed significant assay-dependent differences: ABTS IC₅₀ values were consistently 15–30% lower than DPPH IC₅₀ values for the same extract, suggesting that ABTS detects a broader spectrum of hydrophilic phenolics present in these oils. Total phenolic content ranged from 22.1 to 48.7 mg GAE/100 g oil, with Prokupac variety yielding the highest value. Spearman correlation between total phenolics and ABTS IC₅₀ was rs = −0.87 (p < 0.01). The study recommends reporting both assay results concurrently and cautions against using only DPPH as a sole antioxidant capacity indicator for grape seed oil phenolics.

title: Effect of Natural Tocopherol Mixtures on Secondary Oxidation Product Formation in Refined Sunflower Oil
abstract: Secondary oxidation products in refined sunflower oil supplemented with three concentrations (100, 300, and 500 ppm) of a natural mixed-tocopherol concentrate (predominantly γ- and δ-tocopherol, sourced from soy deodoriser distillate) were monitored over 12 weeks at 40 °C. P-anisidine value (p-AV) and TBARS (expressed as malondialdehyde equivalents, MDA-eq) were determined weekly alongside PV to compute totox values. At 100 ppm addition, totox value at week 8 was 27.4 versus 52.1 in the unsupplemented control. At 500 ppm, a slight pro-oxidant effect was detected after week 10, with MDA-eq rising to 1.8 μmol/g versus 1.6 μmol/g in the 300 ppm treatment, supporting the known concentration-dependent antioxidant/pro-oxidant duality of tocopherols in bulk oils. HPLC-FLD confirmed that γ-tocopherol was depleted faster than δ-tocopherol across all concentrations. Results indicate that 300 ppm mixed tocopherol addition is the practical optimum for refined sunflower oil stabilisation under the tested conditions.

title: Lipid Oxidation in Cold-Pressed Hemp Seed Oil: Influence of Oxygen Headspace and Light Exposure During Bottling
abstract: Hemp seed oil (Cannabis sativa L.) is rich in α-linolenic acid (ALA, approximately 18% by GC-FID) and consequently sensitive to autoxidation. This work investigated the combined effect of two headspace atmospheres (air vs. nitrogen flush) and two light conditions (dark vs. diffuse daylight) on PV, p-AV, and chlorophyll content (spectrophotometric) over 60 days of storage in 250 mL amber PET bottles at 20 °C. A 2×2 factorial ANOVA was applied (n = 4 per cell). Nitrogen flushing significantly reduced PV at day 30 (3.2 vs. 9.7 meq O₂/kg, p < 0.001) and suppressed chlorophyll-mediated photosensitised oxidation under daylight conditions. Interaction between light and headspace atmosphere was statistically significant (p = 0.03), indicating that light accelerates oxidation most strongly when oxygen is available. The paper proposes practical filling-line specifications for small-scale cold-press operations, including a maximum residual oxygen threshold of 2% in the headspace.
