title: Rancimat Induction Period as a Predictor of Real-Time Shelf Life for Cold-Pressed Flaxseed Oil: Correlation and Limitations
abstract: The Rancimat accelerated oxidative stability test (ISO 6886) was applied to cold-pressed flaxseed oil at 80, 100, and 120 °C with an airflow of 10 L/h. Induction periods (IP) at these temperatures were 0.8, 2.1, and 5.4 h respectively. Parallel real-time storage experiments at 5, 15, and 25 °C were carried out for up to 180 days, and actual sensory rancidity onset was determined by a trained panel (n = 8). Arrhenius extrapolation from Rancimat data overestimated practical shelf life by a factor of 1.6–2.3, likely because the mechanism shifts from radical-chain autoxidation at storage temperatures to thermally accelerated hydroperoxide decomposition at Rancimat temperatures. The study presents a correction factor derived from the ratio of actual to predicted shelf life and discusses its applicability range. It concludes that Rancimat is useful for relative comparisons but should not be used as the sole basis for labelling shelf-life claims on ALA-rich oils without real-time verification.

title: Antioxidant Capacity and Phenolic Profile of Cold-Pressed Black Cumin Oil from Domestically Cultivated Nigella sativa
abstract: Black cumin (Nigella sativa L.) seed oil cold-pressed from seed lots grown at three locations in Vojvodina province was characterised for its phenolic composition by HPLC-DAD (thymoquinone, carvacrol, thymol) and total phenolics by Folin–Ciocalteu, then assessed for radical-scavenging capacity (DPPH and FRAP). Thymoquinone was the dominant phenolic at 2.1–3.8 mg/g oil depending on location. DPPH IC₅₀ ranged from 0.41 to 0.68 mg/mL (Trolox equivalent). Oxidative stability measured by Rancimat at 100 °C ranged from 3.1 to 4.9 h, which is markedly higher than for flaxseed oil tested under identical conditions, attributed to lower PUFA content (41% linoleic, 0.3% ALA) and higher thymoquinone levels. Significant location effects were detected for all phenolic markers (one-way ANOVA, p < 0.05), indicating agro-climatic influence on accumulation of bioactive constituents. The data support the potential of Vojvodina-grown black cumin as a source of naturally stabilised edible oil.

title: Lipid Oxidation Markers and Tocopherol Retention in Cold-Pressed Oils After Filtration with Activated Bleaching Earth
abstract: Cold-pressed oils (sunflower, rapeseed, and pumpkin) were treated with activated bleaching earth (ABE) at 1, 2, and 4% (w/w) at 60 °C for 30 min under nitrogen to assess the effect of a minimal refining step on oxidation markers and fat-soluble antioxidants. PV, p-AV, and TBARS were measured before and after ABE treatment; tocopherols were quantified by HPLC-FLD. ABE treatment at 2% reduced initial PV by 38–55% across oil types, confirming its known adsorption of polar hydroperoxides, but simultaneously caused a 12–29% loss of total tocopherols, with α-tocopherol being more susceptible than γ and δ homologues. TBARS did not decrease proportionally, suggesting that secondary aldehydes are retained in the oil phase under the tested conditions. Colour measurements (CIELab) confirmed chlorophyll removal efficiency above 90% at 2% ABE in rapeseed oil. The paper discusses trade-offs relevant to operators of small cold-press facilities seeking modest quality improvement without full refining.

title: Rosemary Extract and Ascorbyl Palmitate Combinations for Oxidative Stabilisation of Cold-Pressed Walnut Oil: A Response Surface Study
abstract: Walnut (Juglans regia) oil is especially prone to oxidation because of its high ALA and linoleic acid content (combined PUFA > 75%). This study applied a central composite design to optimise the combined addition of rosemary extract (RE, 0–600 ppm carnosic acid basis) and ascorbyl palmitate (AP, 0–400 ppm) as antioxidant stabilisers. Responses were PV and p-AV at day 45 of storage at 40 °C. The response surface showed a saddle-point region indicating synergistic interaction between RE and AP: combined addition of 350 ppm RE and 150 ppm AP yielded PV = 4.8 meq O₂/kg and totox = 9.1, superior to either additive alone at its optimum single concentration. Exceeding 500 ppm RE without AP increased p-AV, possibly due to carnosic acid degradation products. Optimal combination maintained sensory acceptance above threshold for 90 days under the stated conditions. All additive combinations tested comply with EU Regulation 1333/2008 maximum limits.

title: Lipid Oxidation Stability of Cold-Pressed Seed Oils: Overview of Analytical Markers and Their Interrelationships
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic review of the primary and secondary oxidation markers routinely used for quality assessment of cold-pressed seed oils, including PV, conjugated diene and triene values, p-anisidine value, TBARS, hexanal by static headspace GC, and the derived totox value. The chapter discusses the chemical basis of each measurement, its detection range, and known interferences or limitations specific to cold-pressed (unrefined) matrices that contain residual phospholipids, pigments, and water. Case studies drawn from the authors' laboratory data illustrate discrepancies that arise when a single marker is used in isolation: for example, high PV with low p-AV in freshly pressed oil versus low PV with elevated p-AV in oil approaching the end of its oxidative induction period. A decision framework is presented for selecting the minimum marker set appropriate to the production and storage context. The chapter is intended for analytical chemists and small-scale cold-press operators rather than specialists in mechanistic oxidation chemistry.

title: Malondialdehyde Determination in Cold-Pressed Oils by HPLC-UV After Derivatisation with Thiobarbituric Acid: Comparison with the Classical Spectrophotometric TBARS Procedure
abstract: The thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) assay is widely used for secondary oxidation assessment, but the classical spectrophotometric version suffers from pigment interference in coloured cold-pressed oils such as pumpkin and rapeseed. This study evaluated an HPLC-UV method after TBA derivatisation for quantification of the MDA–TBA adduct at 532 nm against the standard spectrophotometric procedure in a set of 42 cold-pressed oil samples covering eight species. HPLC-UV gave MDA values of 0.11–1.84 μmol/g, while spectrophotometric TBARS overestimated MDA by 22–68% in deeply coloured samples (r = 0.71, p < 0.001 for correlation, but with proportional bias confirmed by Bland–Altman analysis). Matrix-spiked recovery experiments showed HPLC-UV recovery of 94–103% versus 81–121% for spectrophotometric TBARS. The HPLC method showed better reproducibility (RSD < 5% intra-day) and is recommended as the reference procedure for coloured cold-pressed oils, particularly pumpkin seed oil with its characteristic carotenoid and chlorophyll load.

title: Oxidative Stability of Cold-Pressed Camelina Oil Enriched with Plant-Based Polyphenol Concentrates Under Accelerated Storage Conditions
abstract: Camelina (Camelina sativa) oil was enriched with three polyphenol concentrates — grape pomace extract (GPE), rosemary extract (RE), and buckwheat hull extract (BHE) — each at 200 ppm and in a ternary mixture at 67 ppm each. Samples were stored at 60 °C for 15 days in open beakers (Schaal oven test). PV, p-AV, TBARS, and remaining radical-scavenging capacity (DPPH) were measured every three days. All individual extracts extended induction period compared with the control, with RE performing best (IP 9.1 days vs. 5.2 days for control). The ternary mixture showed an additive rather than synergistic effect (IP 8.8 days), suggesting no antagonism between the three plant extracts under the tested conditions. Camelina oil's high ALA (36.5% by GC-FID) was confirmed as the main driver of rapid oxidation in the control. The study was conducted as preliminary work in support of a funded project on plant-derived antioxidants for edible oil stabilisation.

title: Fatty Acid Composition and Primary Oxidation Markers in Cold-Pressed Oils from Seven Underutilised Seed Species Cultivated in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Seven seed species with potential for cold-pressing in the Vojvodina region — sea buckthorn, milk thistle, chia, camelina, black cumin, hemp, and evening primrose — were cold-pressed under standardised conditions (hydraulic press, 20 °C, no heat pre-treatment). GC-FID fatty acid profiles, PV by iodometric titration, conjugated diene value (CDV, UV 232 nm), and Rancimat IP at 100 °C were determined immediately after pressing (day 0) and at day 14 under ambient storage. ALA-rich species (chia 62.1%, camelina 36.5%, evening primrose 0.1% but high γ-linolenic acid 9.8%) showed fastest primary oxidation onset. Milk thistle oil had the lowest day-0 PV (1.1 meq O₂/kg) and highest Rancimat IP (12.4 h), attributable to high oleic acid (25%) and substantial silymarin content. The paper presents a comparative dataset intended to support regional diversification of cold-press production beyond the dominant sunflower and pumpkin oil sector.

title: Kinetics of Tocopherol Depletion and Hydroperoxide Accumulation in Binary Mixtures of Sunflower and Linseed Oil During Isothermal Storage
abstract: Binary blends of refined high-oleic sunflower oil and cold-pressed linseed oil were prepared at five mass ratios (100:0, 75:25, 50:50, 25:75, 0:100) and stored at 40 °C in sealed amber glass for 120 days. PV, α-, γ-, and δ-tocopherol (HPLC-FLD), and conjugated diene values were tracked fortnightly. A pseudo-first-order depletion model was fitted independently to each tocopherol homologue. α-Tocopherol depletion rate constant in the 50:50 blend (0.024 day⁻¹) was higher than the weighted average of pure-component rate constants (0.018 day⁻¹), indicating a cross-mixture acceleration effect attributed to radical transfer from linseed-derived peroxyl radicals to the sunflower-oil matrix. PV accumulation was superadditive in the 25:75 blend above day 60. The work provides parameters for a simple predictive mixing model useful to blenders seeking to set shelf-life labels for custom seed oil blends.

title: Effect of Short-Term Elevated Temperature During Hydraulic Pressing on Oxidation Marker Levels and Radical-Scavenging Capacity of Pumpkin Seed Oil
abstract: Temperature control during hydraulic cold-pressing is difficult in practice, and press barrel temperatures can transiently reach 50–65 °C. This study simulated three temperature scenarios (controlled 25 °C, transient 45 °C for 10 min, and transient 65 °C for 10 min) during pressing of identically conditioned Styrian pumpkin (Cucurbita pepo var. styriaca) seeds. Day-0 PV, p-AV, TBARS, FRAP, and DPPH were measured across n = 5 replicate pressings per scenario. The 65 °C transient significantly elevated p-AV (6.9 vs. 2.4 in the controlled pressing, p < 0.001) without a corresponding PV increase, indicating that secondary oxidation was already initiated during the thermal event. FRAP and DPPH antioxidant capacity decreased by 18 and 22% respectively in the 65 °C treatment, consistent with partial thermal degradation of tocopherols and carotenoids. Results provide quantitative support for industry guidance recommending barrel cooling during pressing of high-PUFA pumpkin seed varieties.

title: Lubrication in Mechanical Power Transmission: Gear Oils and Rolling-Element Bearings
abstract: This book chapter provides a treatment of lubrication science as applied to enclosed gear drives and rolling-element bearings in mechanical power transmission systems. The chapter covers the fundamentals of elastohydrodynamic and boundary lubrication regimes, Stribeck curve interpretation, and the role of base-stock chemistry (mineral, PAO, ester, and PAG) in determining film-forming capacity. Additive chemistry is discussed with emphasis on antiwear, extreme-pressure, and antioxidant systems. Lubricant selection criteria for industrial worm, helical, and bevel gear drives are presented alongside service life assessment methods including PDSC and RBOT. The chapter includes three worked examples applying the Hamrock–Dowson film-thickness equation to realistic gear geometry and operating conditions. Failure modes including micropitting, scuffing, and deposit formation are illustrated with optical micrographs and profilometry data from laboratory gear tests. The chapter is designed for final-year undergraduate and postgraduate students in chemical and mechanical engineering.

title: Hansen sphere radius as a predictor of membrane swelling in solvent-based polymer processing
abstract: Solvent-induced membrane swelling is a recurring problem in solvent-based polymer processing and membrane fabrication, yet solvent selection for these steps is rarely approached through quantitative solubility models. This chapter reviews the use of HSP Ra values as predictors of equilibrium swelling ratios for five commodity polymer membranes—polyethylene, polyvinylidene fluoride, polysulfone, cellulose acetate, and polyamide-6—in a set of 30 solvents spanning wide ranges of dispersion, polarity, and hydrogen-bonding components. Literature swelling data were compiled and correlated with Ra; Spearman rank correlation coefficients ranged from 0.71 to 0.89 across polymer types. Practical guidance is provided for selecting low-swelling solvents for washing and conditioning steps without sacrificing transport property targets. The chapter also discusses limitations of the spherical HSP model for strongly hydrogen-bonded systems and recommends supplementary use of Kamlet–Taft parameters in those cases.

title: Kinetika formiranja biofilma sojeva Pseudomonas fluorescens izolovanih iz rashladnih komora pogona za preradu mesa u Vojvodini
abstract: Ispitano je petnaest sojeva Pseudomonas fluorescens izolovanih s površina opreme i zidnih obloga rashladnih komora u pet pogona za preradu mesa na teritoriji Vojvodine. Biofilm je kvantifikovan kristal-violet esejem na polistirenskim mikrotitar pločama pri temperaturama 4 °C, 10 °C i 22 °C u vremenskim intervalima od 6, 12, 24, 48 i 72 sata. Sve izolate moguće je svrstati u tri fenotipska klaster na osnovu OD595 vrednosti na 48 h: slabi (OD < 0,3), umereni (0,3–0,8) i jaki producenti biofilma (OD > 0,8). Šest sojeva pokazalo je značajno pojačanu produkciju biofilma pri 4 °C u odnosu na 22 °C (p < 0,05), što ukazuje na psihrotrofnu adaptaciju mehanizama adherencije. Rezultati ukazuju da standardni temperaturni režimi hlađenja ne inhibiraju formiranje biofilma kod svih izolata, što ima praktičan značaj za higijenu u prehrambenoj industriji.
venue: Prehrambena industrija – Acta Periodica Technologica

title: Molecular detection of N-acyl homoserine lactone synthase genes in Pseudomonas isolates from refrigerated meat-processing facilities
abstract: Quorum sensing (QS) in Pseudomonas species is primarily mediated by N-acyl homoserine lactone (AHL) signals encoded by LuxI-family synthase genes. We screened 28 Pseudomonas isolates from cold-chain meat-processing environments in northern Serbia for the presence of the pcoI and hdtS AHL synthase gene homologues by PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing. Twenty-one isolates (75%) carried at least one synthase gene variant, with pcoI detected in 17 isolates and hdtS in 9, including 5 carrying both. Phylogenetic analysis of partial synthase sequences grouped isolates into two clades corresponding broadly to P. fluorescens and P. putida species clusters. AHL production was confirmed by thin-layer chromatography biosensor assay using Chromobacterium violaceum CV026 as reporter. Positive correlations were found between AHL production intensity and both biofilm biomass (r = 0.68, p < 0.001) and protease secretion (r = 0.59, p < 0.01), supporting the hypothesis that QS coordinates spoilage-related virulence traits in these environmental strains.

title: Inhibition of quorum sensing and biofilm formation in Pseudomonas fluorescens by plant-derived phenolic extracts
abstract: Ethanolic extracts of grape pomace, rosehip, and common thyme were prepared and their total phenolic content determined by Folin–Ciocalteu assay (range 18.4–74.6 mg GAE/g dry extract). Sub-inhibitory concentrations (0.25–2 mg/mL) of each extract were tested against five strong-biofilm-producing P. fluorescens strains isolated from a meat-processing cold chain. Biofilm biomass was assessed by crystal violet assay; AHL-mediated QS activity was measured by violacein inhibition in C. violaceum CV026. Thyme extract at 1 mg/mL reduced biofilm formation by 61–78% across all strains without significant reduction in planktonic growth (< 8% decrease in OD600). Grape pomace extract reduced violacein production by 54% at 2 mg/mL, indicating QS interference independent of bacteriostatic effects. Rosmarinic acid, identified as a major component by HPLC-DAD, showed dose-dependent QS inhibition with IC50 values of 0.31–0.48 mg/mL. Results suggest that phenolic fractions from agro-industrial by-products could be applied as surface treatment additives in food processing facilities.

title: Uticaj materijala površina u kontaktu s hranom na adherenciju i razvoj biofilma odabranih Pseudomonas sojeva
abstract: Adhezija bakterija i razvoj biofilma na površinama zavisi kako od karakteristika soja tako i od fizičko-hemijskih svojstava podloge. U ovom radu ispitana je sposobnost četiri soja P. fluorescens i dva soja P. putida da formiraju biofilm na kuponima od nerđajućeg čelika AISI 304, polipropilena i hlorisanog PVC-a pri 10 °C tokom 48 h. Kvantifikacija biofilma izvršena je resazurin esejem za procenu metaboličke aktivnosti i kristal-violet esejem za ukupnu biomasu. Na nerđajućem čeliku sa prosečnom hrapavošću Ra = 0,42 µm formiran je statistički značajno veći biofilm u poređenju s polipropilenom (Ra = 0,18 µm) za četiri od šest sojeva (p < 0,05). Konfokalna laserska skenirajuća mikroskopija potvrdila je razvoj trodimenzionalnih biofilmskih struktura debljine do 38 µm na čeliku nakon 48 h. Rezultati imaju direktan značaj za izbor materijala pri projektovanju opreme u rashladnim pogonima.

title: Transcriptomic response of a cold-adapted Pseudomonas fluorescens meat isolate to sub-inhibitory concentrations of chlorine-based sanitizers
abstract: Chlorine-based sanitizers are widely used in meat-processing facilities, yet repeated sub-inhibitory exposures may alter gene expression in sessile bacterial populations. We exposed biofilm-forming P. fluorescens strain NS-14, isolated from a slaughterhouse drain in Novi Sad, to 20 mg/L and 50 mg/L free chlorine for 15 min and characterized transcriptional changes by RNA-seq 30 min post-treatment. At 20 mg/L, 142 genes were differentially expressed (|log2FC| > 1.5, FDR < 0.05), including upregulation of catalase-encoding katA (log2FC = 3.1), the alginate biosynthesis gene algD (log2FC = 2.4), and the efflux pump component mexB (log2FC = 2.2). At 50 mg/L, 309 genes showed differential expression, with strong induction of oxidative stress response genes and suppression of flagellar assembly genes. These results indicate that sub-lethal chlorine stress promotes biofilm-protective and efflux-mediated responses, and that standard sanitizer concentrations applied in brief contact-time regimens may be insufficient to suppress adaptive transcriptional programs in established biofilms.

title: Kombinovano dejstvo hlapivih jedinjenja eteričnog ulja origana i nisina na biofilm Pseudomonas fluorescens na nerđajućem čeliku
abstract: Ispitana je sposobnost isparljivih komponenti eteričnog ulja origana (EUO), pre svega karvakrola i timola, da u kombinaciji s nisinskim preparatom inhibiraju biofilm P. fluorescens soja NS-07 na kuponu od nerđajućeg čelika AISI 316 pri 10 °C. Eksponirana površina tretirana je parama EUO (150–600 µL/L) i/ili nisinskim rastvorom (250–1000 IU/mL) u trajanju od 60 min. Sinergistički efekat kombinovane primene potvrđen je metodom frakcionih inhibitornih koncentracija (ΣFIC = 0,42 za kombinaciju 300 µL/L EUO + 500 IU/mL nisina). Broj vijabilnih ćelija u biofilmu smanjen je za 3,4 log CFU/cm² u poređenju s netretiranom kontrolom. Skeniranjem elektronskim mikroskopom uočeno je razaranje ekstracelularnog matriksa i gubitak integriteta ćelijskih membrana. Rezultati pružaju osnovu za razvoj kombinovanih protokola sanitacije u rashladnim pogonima koji bi smanjili upotrebu hemijskih dezinficijensa.

title: Quantitative modelling of Pseudomonas fluorescens biofilm development on stainless steel under simulated cold-chain temperature fluctuations
abstract: Temperature fluctuations during cold-chain transport and storage create dynamic growth environments for spoilage microorganisms. We developed a modified Gompertz-based kinetic model to describe biofilm accumulation by P. fluorescens strain NS-14 on AISI 316 stainless steel coupons subjected to programmed temperature cycles (4 °C / 10 °C alternating every 8 h) over 72 h, compared to constant 4 °C and 10 °C controls. Biofilm biomass was measured at 12 h intervals by both crystal violet (OD595) and viable plate count (CFU/cm²). The model achieved good fit for all three conditions (R² ≥ 0.96, RMSE ≤ 0.04 OD units). Maximum specific biofilm formation rate (µmax,BF) was 21% higher under temperature-cycling conditions (0.043 h⁻¹) than at constant 4 °C (0.036 h⁻¹), indicating that fluctuations accelerate surface colonisation. Lag phase for biofilm initiation was reduced by approximately 3.5 h under cycling versus constant 4 °C. The model parameters are suitable for integration into predictive microbiology software platforms used in HACCP plan development.

title: Detection and quantification of quorum sensing signal molecules in meat processing plant drainage water by LC-MS/MS
abstract: Drainage water from meat-processing facilities constitutes a concentrated reservoir of microbial metabolites including AHL quorum sensing molecules. We collected 36 drainage water samples from six processing lines across three plants in Vojvodina over a 12-month period. AHL compounds were extracted by ethyl acetate partition, concentrated by solid-phase extraction, and quantified by LC-MS/MS using stable isotope-labelled internal standards. Eight distinct AHL species were detected, with C6-HSL and 3-oxo-C8-HSL most prevalent (mean concentrations 4.7 nM and 2.1 nM, respectively). Seasonal variation was statistically significant for three AHL species, with higher concentrations in summer months (June–August). Total AHL load correlated positively with total viable count (r = 0.72, p < 0.001) and Pseudomonas-selective count (r = 0.65, p < 0.001). These findings demonstrate that drainage water monitoring could serve as a rapid, non-destructive indicator of QS-active biofilm burden within processing environments.

title: Quorum quenching lactonase expression in Bacillus licheniformis as a biocontrol strategy against Pseudomonas biofilm in simulated meat-contact conditions
abstract: Enzymatic quorum quenching (QQ) via AHL lactonases offers a resistance-resilient strategy for biofilm control. We cloned and heterologously expressed the aiiA lactonase gene from a Bacillus licheniformis soil isolate in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) and characterised the purified enzyme kinetically. The enzyme displayed broad substrate specificity against C6- to C12-HSL substrates, with Km values ranging from 0.18 to 0.41 mM and kcat values from 12.3 to 31.7 s⁻¹. When immobilised on chitosan-coated stainless steel coupons at 5 U/cm², the enzyme preparation reduced AHL-mediated QS activity by 83% (CV026 reporter assay) and suppressed P. fluorescens NS-14 biofilm formation by 71% after 48 h at 10 °C, compared to uncoated controls. Enzyme activity was retained at 78% after five wash–rewet cycles, supporting feasibility for surface coating applications. Cytotoxicity testing on two food-contact regulatory cell lines showed no adverse effects at the tested enzyme concentrations.

title: Dielectric spectroscopy for online biomass estimation in high-cell-density yeast fermentations: applicability limits and correction strategies
abstract: Dielectric spectroscopy based on the β-relaxation of viable cell membranes is a well-established approach for online biomass estimation, but its accuracy degrades at cell densities above approximately 40 g dry cell weight (DCW)/L due to cell–cell interactions affecting the permittivity signal. This study characterised measurement accuracy of a commercial multi-frequency dielectric probe across biomass concentrations of 5 to 85 g DCW/L in fed-batch Saccharomyces cerevisiae cultures. At densities above 50 g DCW/L, permittivity-based estimates deviated from gravimetrically determined DCW by up to 32%. Two correction strategies were evaluated: a polynomial correction curve fitted to calibration data, and a Kalman filter combining dielectric and off-gas CO₂ measurements. The Kalman filter reduced estimation error to below 9% across the full concentration range tested. Applicability in high-gravity fermentations for bioethanol production is discussed, along with practical guidelines for probe placement and cleaning-in-place compatibility.
venue: Measurement Science in Fermentation and Bioprocessing

title: Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software
abstract: This paper defines a catalogue of 18 mutation operators tailored to finite state machine (FSM) specifications commonly used in embedded control firmware. Operators cover state deletion, transition guard modification, action substitution, and reset-condition negation. An experiment was conducted on four open-source microcontroller firmware projects totalling approximately 14,000 lines of C code. Mutants were seeded automatically using a custom Python tool, and an existing hand-written test suite was used as the baseline oracle. Mutation scores ranged from 41% to 67% across the four subjects, revealing systematic gaps in transition coverage. The paper reports the proportion of equivalent mutants identified through static analysis (approximately 12% of all seeded mutants) and discusses the effort required for manual equivalence classification. The results motivate the need for specification-driven test generation rather than ad hoc test suite growth.

title: Deriving Test Suites from UML Statecharts: A Comparison of Three Path-Selection Strategies
abstract: Model-based test generation from UML statecharts can follow different path-selection criteria, each yielding test suites of different size and fault-detection capability. This study compares all-transitions, all-transition-pairs, and boundary-interior path selection applied to a set of seven industrial-scale statechart models provided by a regional automotive supplier. Models ranged from 12 to 89 states and 18 to 204 transitions. Test cases were generated automatically and executed against seeded mutation faults. All-transition-pairs coverage detected 14% more mutants on average compared with all-transitions, while increasing test suite size by a factor of 3.1. Boundary-interior selection offered a middle ground but showed inconsistent results across subjects. Execution times on target hardware were measured to assess whether suite sizes remain feasible under real-time constraints. The paper recommends a hybrid strategy that applies all-transition-pairs only to safety-critical subsystems and all-transitions elsewhere.

title: Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes
abstract: Regression testing of embedded firmware is expensive because full test suite execution on hardware targets can take hours. This paper presents a lightweight change-impact analysis technique that identifies which tests in an existing suite are affected by a given firmware patch without requiring full re-execution. The method instruments the firmware binary at basic-block granularity to record coverage during an initial full run, then uses static call-graph differencing to predict which blocks are reachable from changed functions. On a dataset of 120 patches drawn from the version history of three open-source firmware projects, the technique retained on average 31% of the original test suite while missing 2.1% of fault-detecting tests. False negative rates are characterised per patch type. The implementation is released as a set of scripts wrapping GCC and a custom binary instrumentation tool. Practical integration into a continuous integration pipeline is described.
venue: Journal of Embedded Computing and Control

title: Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation
abstract: Interrupt-driven firmware presents challenges for model-based testing because interleaving of interrupt service routines (ISRs) with the main execution thread produces combinatorial state spaces. This paper proposes a contract language, IFContract, that allows engineers to annotate ISR entry and exit conditions, shared-variable invariants, and timing constraints using a syntax embedded in C comments. A parser translates annotations into an extended FSM representation. Test cases covering pairwise ISR–main-thread interactions are generated from this model. The approach was evaluated on firmware for a battery management unit implemented on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The generated suite comprised 147 test cases and detected all 38 manually seeded interface faults. Compared with a randomly generated suite of the same size, the model-based suite found 23% more faults. Annotation effort was measured at 2.3 lines of contract per 10 lines of ISR code on average.

title: Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems
abstract: This book chapter surveys the state of practice in model-based testing (MBT) as applied to embedded and cyber-physical systems. It covers modelling notations including UML statecharts, extended finite automata, and timed automata, and maps them to corresponding test generation algorithms. Coverage criteria are categorised into structural, fault-based, and requirements-based families. A discussion of toolchain integration addresses challenges specific to embedded targets: cross-compilation, hardware-in-the-loop execution, and limited observability. Two worked examples illustrate applying MBT to an automotive body control module and an industrial motor controller. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems including scalability to large state spaces, handling of real-time constraints, and the lack of standardised interfaces between modelling and test execution tools.

title: Measuring the Cost of Test Suite Maintenance Over Multiple Firmware Releases
abstract: Automated test suites generated from formal models must be updated as firmware specifications evolve, yet the maintenance cost of model-based suites is rarely quantified empirically. This study tracks five firmware products through 8 to 14 release cycles, recording the time engineers spent updating model specifications, regenerating test cases, and resolving obsolete test oracles. On average, model update effort represented 18% of total release testing effort, compared with 27% for manually maintained suites managing the same products in a parallel control group. The study also records the number of regression faults detected per release and finds that model-based suites detected faults 1.4 releases earlier on average. Threats to validity related to the single-organisation setting and self-reported effort data are discussed. The dataset, anonymised, is made available for further analysis.

title: Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic
abstract: Specifying correct output behaviour for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) firmware tests is labour intensive because engineers must manually define acceptable signal ranges and timing windows for each scenario. This paper investigates the use of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) formulas as automatically checkable test oracles in HIL test environments. STL formulas are mined from a set of passing execution traces using a template-guided parameter synthesis procedure. The synthesised formulas are then used as oracles for new test runs. The approach was evaluated on a DC motor control firmware and a temperature regulation firmware, each executed on physical target hardware. Oracle construction time dropped from a median of 47 minutes per scenario (manual) to under 4 minutes (automated). False positive and false negative rates of synthesised oracles were 3.1% and 1.8% respectively across 310 test scenarios. Limitations related to non-deterministic hardware timing are discussed.

title: Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm
abstract: Adopting formal specification practices in industry requires integrating review steps into existing development workflows without excessive overhead. This paper reports a two-year action research study conducted with a Serbian firm that develops programmable logic controllers. The study introduced a lightweight formalism based on communicating extended finite automata (CEFA) for specifying firmware modules, along with a peer-review checklist and a set of automated consistency checks. Defect data were collected for 34 firmware modules developed before and after adoption. Post-adoption modules showed a 29% reduction in defects found during system integration testing. Developer survey data indicate that engineers found the notation acceptable after a two-day training course. Barriers including tool fragmentation and version control of model artefacts are documented. The paper provides a replication package containing the checklist, consistency check scripts, and anonymised defect logs.

title: SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models
abstract: Most mutation testing tools operate at the source code level, but for model-based testing workflows it is useful to seed faults into the formal model rather than the implementation. SpecMutate is a framework that applies 23 mutation operators directly to extended finite automata (EFA) models serialised in an XML interchange format. Operators include guard weakening, output-action swapping, state-merge, and variable initialisation faults. The framework integrates with an open-source model-based test generator and reports the model mutation score alongside the implementation mutation score. An experiment on six firmware EFA models with a combined 312 states found that model mutation scores and code mutation scores diverged significantly for three of the subjects, indicating that the model had lower fidelity than assumed. Runtime for model mutation analysis was under two minutes per model on a standard workstation, making it suitable for pre-commit checks.

title: Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data
abstract: Test prioritisation orders a regression suite so that fault-detecting tests execute earlier, reducing feedback latency. This paper proposes a history-based prioritisation strategy that weights tests by the fault-localisation entropy of the code regions they cover across previous test campaigns. Coverage and fault data from nine firmware projects with histories spanning 12 to 31 releases were used to train and evaluate the strategy. The proposed approach achieved an average percentage of faults detected (APFD) of 0.78, compared with 0.61 for random ordering and 0.71 for a coverage-based baseline. Computational overhead of computing prioritisation order was below 90 seconds for all subjects. The paper also analyses how quickly the historical model degrades after a major refactoring event and proposes a simple reset heuristic triggered by structural change thresholds.

title: Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios
abstract: Model-based test generation is constrained by the completeness of the formal model: scenarios not captured in the specification are not tested. This preprint explores a workflow where an LLM is prompted with natural-language firmware documentation and existing EFA models to suggest additional test scenarios that may correspond to specification gaps. Suggested scenarios are reviewed by engineers and, if accepted, formalised as model extensions. The approach was piloted on three firmware modules from an industrial PLC project. Engineers accepted 41% of LLM suggestions after review; of those, 17 were formalised and added to the model. Subsequent mutation analysis showed an increase in model mutation score of 6.3 percentage points on average. The paper does not claim that LLM suggestions are reliable in general but characterises conditions under which they are useful as a complement to structured specification review.

title: Automated Generation of Compatibility Test Cases from Android Permission Change Logs
abstract: Android's permission model underwent significant restructuring between API levels 22 and 23 with the introduction of runtime permissions, causing widespread behavioural incompatibilities in deployed applications. This paper presents PermGen, a tool that parses Android SDK change logs and permission usage declarations in application manifests to automatically generate JUnit-based test cases targeting permission-related execution paths. The tool was evaluated on 45 applications from the Google Play Store's productivity category, generating on average 17.3 test cases per application. Execution of generated suites on a physical device pool covering API levels 21 through 27 revealed 83 previously undocumented permission-handling defects across 31 applications. Compared to manually authored test suites covering the same permission scenarios, PermGen achieved 78% of the fault detection rate at 12% of the authoring effort, measured in developer-hours. Limitations regarding obfuscated code and dynamically requested permissions are discussed.

title: Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data
abstract: Small wind turbines installed on agricultural and industrial premises in Serbia are often maintained reactively due to the absence of dedicated condition monitoring. This paper fits gradient-boosted survival models—specifically, a discrete-time hazard model and a random survival forest—to a combined dataset of SCADA telemetry and tower-mounted accelerometer readings from 17 turbines over five years. Predictors include nacelle vibration root-mean-square in three frequency bands, rotor speed deviation, and nacelle temperature differential. The discrete-time hazard model achieved a concordance index of 0.73 on a held-out cohort, outperforming a Cox baseline at 0.65. Predicted 30-day failure probability was used to generate ranked maintenance schedules, which were evaluated in a retrospective simulation against actual maintenance logs, showing an estimated 22 % reduction in unscheduled downtime hours.

title: Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration
abstract: Full regeneration of PLC source code from a configuration model is straightforward but can be impractical in projects where manually authored customisation sections exist alongside generated code. This paper presents an incremental generation strategy that identifies which model elements have changed between two configuration revisions and regenerates only the affected Structured Text compilation units, preserving protected regions in unaffected units. Change detection is implemented as a model differencing step operating on XMI serialisations of feature model configurations, producing a delta structure that drives selective Xtend template invocation. The strategy was evaluated on a synthetic benchmark of 50 configuration pairs derived from a packaging-machine product line model with 41 features. Regeneration time was reduced by a mean of 74% compared to full regeneration, with no instances of incorrect code produced across 1,200 generated file revisions as verified by a regression test suite. The paper formalises the notion of generation dependency to characterise when incremental regeneration is sound.

title: Measuring Coupling in Polyglot Repositories: A Metric Suite Based on Cross-Language Dependency Edges
abstract: Standard coupling metrics such as afferent/efferent coupling and instability were designed for single-language object-oriented systems. In polyglot repositories, cross-language calls—for example, from Python orchestration scripts into compiled C extensions, or from JVM-hosted Kotlin into native libraries via JNI—create dependency edges that existing metrics ignore. We define an extended metric suite that accounts for cross-language edge weight, directionality, and language-pair asymmetry. We computed the suite on 23 open-source polyglot repositories and validated its discriminative power against manually assigned architectural quality ratings provided by eight independent evaluators. Cross-language instability correlated more strongly with subjectively rated architectural fragility (Spearman ρ = 0.71) than standard within-language instability alone (ρ = 0.48). We provide a reference implementation for the metric suite as a command-line tool.

title: Superoxide dismutase and catalase activities in the gills of Unio pictorum exposed to cadmium-contaminated sediment from the Tisa River
abstract: Freshwater mussels Unio pictorum were collected from two sites along the Tisa River: a reference site with background cadmium concentrations below 0.5 mg/kg dry sediment weight, and an impacted site where concentrations reached 4.2 mg/kg. Gill tissue was dissected and homogenised for spectrophotometric measurement of superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) activities, alongside tissue cadmium quantification by flame atomic absorption spectrometry. Mean tissue cadmium in mussels from the impacted site was 18.3 ± 2.1 µg/g dry weight, compared to 1.4 ± 0.4 µg/g at the reference site. SOD activity was elevated by 67% and CAT activity by 43% at the impacted site. Significant positive correlations were found between tissue cadmium concentration and both enzyme activities (r = 0.81 and r = 0.74, respectively; p < 0.01). Results indicate that antioxidant enzyme upregulation in U. pictorum gill tissue can serve as a sensitive early-warning biomarker for sediment cadmium contamination in lowland rivers.

title: Lipid peroxidation and glutathione status in the caddisfly larvae Hydropsyche pellucidula along a copper gradient in the Moravica River
abstract: Caddisfly larvae (Hydropsyche pellucidula) were sampled from five stations along the Moravica River spanning a gradient of copper contamination (dissolved copper 3–62 µg/L) associated with legacy mining drainage. Whole-body homogenates were used to measure malondialdehyde (MDA) as an index of lipid peroxidation via the thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) assay, as well as total glutathione (GSH) and oxidised glutathione (GSSG) by enzymatic recycling. MDA concentrations increased approximately fourfold between the least and most contaminated stations, while the GSH/GSSG ratio fell from 18.2 ± 1.4 to 5.6 ± 0.9. Glutathione reductase activity showed a modest but statistically significant increase at intermediate copper levels (p = 0.03) but was not elevated at the highest concentrations, suggesting enzymatic capacity was overwhelmed. These findings illustrate a shift from compensatory antioxidant response to oxidative damage under sustained high copper exposure, with implications for using H. pellucidula as a bioindicator species in metal-impacted streams.

title: Histopathological changes and oxidative stress markers in common barbel (Barbus barbus) from the Sava River near industrial discharge points
abstract: Liver and gill tissues were sampled from common barbel (Barbus barbus) captured at three locations on the Sava River: two near identified industrial discharge points and one upstream reference location. Sediment samples at the two impacted sites contained lead concentrations of 87 and 134 mg/kg dry weight, and zinc concentrations of 320 and 480 mg/kg, both well above background levels. Histopathological analysis of liver sections revealed increased vacuolisation, hydropic degeneration, and focal necrosis at impacted sites. CAT and SOD activities in liver homogenates were significantly elevated at both impacted sites (p < 0.05). Protein carbonyl content, a marker of oxidative protein damage, was 2.3-fold higher at the most contaminated site compared to reference fish. Correlation analysis indicated that liver lead concentration was the strongest predictor of protein carbonyl levels (r = 0.78). The combination of histopathology and biochemical endpoints provided a more complete picture of sublethal toxicity than either approach alone.

title: Metal fractionation in Danube River sediments and its relationship to antioxidant responses in the zebra mussel Dreissena polymorpha
abstract: Sequential extraction was used to fractionate copper, cadmium, lead, and nickel into exchangeable, carbonate-bound, Fe–Mn oxide-bound, organic matter-bound, and residual fractions in sediment cores from six Danube sites between Apatin and Bečej. The exchangeable and carbonate-bound fractions, considered most bioavailable, varied considerably among sites and with sediment depth. Dreissena polymorpha was collected from the same sites and soft tissues were analysed for metal accumulation and antioxidant enzyme activities. Tissue copper concentrations ranged from 4.1 to 31.7 µg/g dry weight and correlated most strongly with the sum of exchangeable and carbonate-bound copper fractions in surface sediment (r = 0.89, p < 0.01). SOD and GPx activities in digestive gland tissue tracked tissue copper levels rather than total sediment copper, underscoring the importance of bioavailable fractions for interpreting biological responses. These results support the use of fractionation-corrected exposure metrics in sediment quality assessments.

title: Antioxidant enzyme responses in Chironomus riparius larvae after short-term laboratory exposure to lead-spiked sediment: dose–response relationships and recovery
abstract: Chironomus riparius fourth-instar larvae were exposed for 96 hours to control sediment and four lead-spiked concentrations (50, 150, 400, and 800 mg/kg dry weight) in a standardised laboratory assay. After the exposure period, half of the animals from each treatment were transferred to clean sediment for a 48-hour recovery period. Whole-body SOD, CAT, and GST activities were measured at both time points. Dose-dependent increases in all three enzymes were observed at exposure concentrations of 150 mg/kg and above. At 800 mg/kg, SOD activity was 3.1-fold above control, CAT 2.4-fold, and GST 1.9-fold. Following transfer to clean sediment, SOD and CAT activities returned to near-control levels within 48 hours at all but the highest dose, whereas GST recovery was incomplete at 400 mg/kg. Survival was unaffected across all treatments. The recovery data suggest that SOD and CAT in C. riparius are highly responsive but reversible biomarkers suitable for monitoring episodic contamination events.

title: Multi-biomarker index for assessing sediment quality in tributaries of the Tisa River in Vojvodina
abstract: This study applied an integrated biomarker response (IBR) index to data from three species—Gammarus fossarum, Dreissena polymorpha, and Chironomus sp.—sampled simultaneously at nine sites across five Tisa tributaries in Vojvodina during spring and autumn of 2021. Measured endpoints included SOD, CAT, GPx, and GST activities, MDA concentration, and metallothionein content. Sediment metal concentrations (Cu, Cd, Pb, Ni, Zn) and physicochemical parameters were recorded at each site. IBR scores ranged from 1.3 at the least impacted site to 8.7 at the most contaminated site, which had sediment cadmium concentrations exceeding 6 mg/kg. IBR values were significantly correlated with a chemical contamination index based on sediment metal loads (r = 0.84, p < 0.001). Metallothionein induction showed the tightest relationship with cadmium among all individual endpoints. The multi-species IBR approach reduced uncertainty compared to single-species assessments and is proposed for inclusion in routine monitoring programmes for rivers in the Pannonian Plain.

title: Oxidative stress and immune-related gene expression in the digestive gland of Unio crassus under combined cadmium and temperature stress
abstract: Global warming is predicted to amplify the toxic effects of metals on freshwater organisms. Unio crassus individuals were acclimated for two weeks at 18 °C or 26 °C before exposure to 5 µg/L dissolved cadmium for seven days. Digestive gland tissue was sampled for antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, GPx), lipid peroxidation (TBARS), and mRNA expression of five genes: sod1, cat, gpx1, hsp70, and nf-κb, quantified by RT-qPCR. At 26 °C and cadmium exposure combined, TBARS levels were 2.8-fold higher than in cadmium-exposed mussels at 18 °C, and sod1 and gpx1 transcripts were elevated to a greater degree than the corresponding enzyme activities suggested, indicating post-transcriptional regulation. Expression of nf-κb was significantly induced only in the combined stress treatment (p < 0.01), pointing to inflammation pathway involvement. The results indicate that temperature elevation substantially worsens cadmium-induced oxidative damage in U. crassus, with consequences for risk assessment under climate change scenarios.

title: Interannual consistency of isotopic niches in autumnal Blackcap (Sylvia atricapilla) at a Danube corridor stopover: a six-year dataset
abstract: We examined whether the isotopic niche of a migratory passerine population at a single stopover site remains consistent across years with different phenological conditions. Using blood δ13C and δ15N from Blackcap captured at a standardised mist-netting station on the Danube floodplain near Novi Sad over six consecutive autumns (2016–2021; total n = 547), we calculated annual Bayesian standard ellipse areas (SIBER) and tested for year-to-year differences using posterior comparison. SEAc values ranged from 2.14‰² to 3.07‰² and did not differ significantly between years (all pairwise posterior probabilities of difference < 0.10). Mean annual δ13C ranged from −23.0‰ to −22.3‰ and mean δ15N from 8.1‰ to 8.9‰. Isotopic overlap between consecutive years exceeded 65% in all pairwise comparisons. Results suggest that isotopic niche structure at this site reflects stable habitat features rather than interannual climatic variability, supporting its use as a long-term monitoring reference.

title: Integrating morphological and transcriptomic data to classify eutrophication stress response phenotypes in Ceratophyllum demersum: a multivariate approach
abstract: We combined 14 morphological variables (including shoot elongation, internode length, lateral branching density, and leaf dimensions) with normalised expression values of 112 a priori selected stress-marker genes from RNA-seq data for Ceratophyllum demersum sampled across 22 sites in Vojvodina lakes. Principal component analysis of morphological data and sparse partial least squares discriminant analysis on gene expression data were performed independently, then integrated via DIABLO (Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker discovery using Latent cOmponents). Three reproducible phenotypic clusters emerged: an unstressed phenotype (sites with TP < 80 µg L⁻¹), an acclimation phenotype (TP 80–300 µg L⁻¹), and a stress phenotype (TP > 300 µg L⁻¹). The acclimation phenotype was characterised by upregulation of LHCII genes and increased shoot elongation, while the stress phenotype showed LHCII downregulation and upregulation of protease and ubiquitin pathway transcripts. Cross-validated classification accuracy was 87%. This framework may be applicable for rapid bioassessment of lake trophic status using macrophyte multi-level indicators.

title: A Two-Level Additive Schwarz Preconditioner for Linear Elasticity on Shared-Memory Architectures
abstract: This paper presents a two-level additive Schwarz preconditioner tailored for the linear elasticity equations discretised with trilinear hexahedral finite elements. The coarse space is constructed using energy-minimising basis functions that capture near-kernel rigid-body modes, which are critical for nearly incompressible materials. Implementation targets shared-memory multicore platforms using OpenMP thread parallelism. The preconditioner is tested on three benchmark meshes ranging from 200 000 to 4.2 million degrees of freedom, representing a steel beam under point loading, a hollow cylinder under internal pressure, and a simplified femur geometry. Convergence is measured in terms of iteration counts and wall-clock time against a standard one-level restricted additive Schwarz baseline. For the largest problem, the two-level variant reduces conjugate gradient iterations from 312 to 47 and achieves a speedup factor of 4.6 on a 16-core workstation. Parallel efficiency drops from 94% to 81% when moving from 8 to 16 threads due to memory bandwidth saturation on the coarse problem. The implementation is released as an extension to the faculty's in-house FEM library.

title: Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints for the Stokes Equations on Unstructured Tetrahedral Grids
abstract: This work applies the Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) method to the stabilised P1–P1 finite element discretisation of the Stokes equations on unstructured tetrahedral meshes. The BDDC coarse problem incorporates both velocity and pressure constraints at subdomain corners and edges, addressing the saddle-point structure that complicates standard BDDC formulations. Scalability experiments are performed using MPI on up to 256 processes on the PARADOX-IV cluster at the Institute of Physics Belgrade. Three test cases are used: lid-driven cavity flow at Re=400, flow around a cylinder in a channel, and internal flow through a simplified valve geometry with 8.7 million total degrees of freedom. The condition number of the preconditioned operator is bounded independently of the number of subdomains in all tested configurations. Iteration counts stay below 55 for all cases. Strong and weak scaling results are reported; parallel efficiency at 256 processes reaches 78% for the valve geometry. An analysis of the coarse-problem cost identifies it as the primary bottleneck above 128 processes.

title: GPU-Accelerated Assembly of Finite Element Matrices for Nonlinear Elasticity
abstract: Finite element matrix assembly is typically memory-bound and difficult to parallelise efficiently on GPUs due to race conditions when threads write to shared global entries. This paper describes a GPU-resident assembly strategy based on graph colouring of mesh elements, where elements in each colour share no common degrees of freedom and can be assembled concurrently without atomic operations. The approach is implemented in CUDA for a compressible Neo-Hookean material model with trilinear hexahedral elements. Benchmarks are carried out on three NVIDIA GPU models available at the Faculty of Sciences GPU cluster, with mesh sizes between 500 000 and 12 million elements. Compared to a single-threaded CPU baseline, the GPU assembly achieves speedups of 18× to 31× depending on mesh regularity and GPU memory capacity. A hybrid scheme combining GPU assembly with CPU-based iterative solving via PETSc is also described, demonstrating that assembly time is no longer the bottleneck for problems below 6 million elements when a K40-class card is used. Code is made available on the faculty repository.

title: Parallel Finite Element Simulation of Soft Tissue Deformation for Surgical Training Applications
abstract: Soft tissue simulation for surgical training requires update rates of at least 30 Hz to maintain haptic realism, while retaining sufficient mechanical fidelity. This chapter reviews the computational requirements for real-time finite element simulation of viscoelastic soft tissue and surveys domain decomposition approaches that have been proposed to meet them. A practical pipeline is described combining a corotational linear elasticity formulation to handle large displacements cheaply, a one-level FETI-DP solver for distributed time stepping, and an asynchronous GPU-based rendering thread. The pipeline is evaluated on a liver mesh of 180 000 elements and a kidney mesh of 97 000 elements, both segmented from publicly available CT data. Achieved simulation rates are 42 Hz and 68 Hz respectively on a four-node workstation cluster with one GPU per node. The chapter discusses accuracy trade-offs introduced by the corotational approximation and by using a fixed coarse mesh for the solver's coarse problem across multiple deformation states.

title: Mixed-Precision Iterative Refinement for Sparse Linear Systems Arising in Finite Element Analysis
abstract: Modern GPU hardware supports half-, single-, and double-precision floating-point operations, with half-precision throughput often four times that of double. This paper investigates a three-level iterative refinement strategy in which the initial approximate solution is computed in half precision, the residual is evaluated in single precision, and correction solves use a double-precision FGMRES accelerated by an incomplete LU preconditioner. The approach is applied to linear systems from static structural finite element analysis of a bridge girder and a gear assembly, with system sizes from 80 000 to 1.1 million unknowns. Convergence to a double-precision residual norm below 10⁻¹⁰ is achieved within at most four refinement steps for all tested problems. Wall-clock time is reduced by 38% to 52% compared to pure double-precision FGMRES with the same preconditioner. Rounding error analysis following standard backward stability bounds is provided. Failure cases associated with highly ill-conditioned subsystems near geometric singularities are identified and a local precision upgrade heuristic is proposed.

title: Load-Adaptive Subdomain Partitioning for Heterogeneous CPU–GPU Clusters in Time-Dependent FEM Computations
abstract: In heterogeneous clusters where nodes differ in GPU generation or CPU core count, static load-balanced partitioning of finite element domains leads to idle time on faster nodes. This paper proposes a dynamic repartitioning scheme where subdomain sizes are adjusted between time steps based on measured solve times, using a weighted version of the recursive bisection algorithm with weights updated from runtime profiling. The scheme is implemented within a FETI-type framework and tested on three heterogeneous configurations combining nodes with NVIDIA K40, P100, and V100 GPUs alongside CPU-only nodes. Test problems include a transient heat equation on a 3D geological model with 22 million degrees of freedom and a transient linear elasticity problem over 120 time steps. The adaptive partitioner reduces total wall-clock time by 19% to 34% compared to static partitioning based on theoretical peak performance estimates. Repartitioning overhead per time step averages 3.1% of solve time.

title: A Comparison of Coarse Space Constructions for Two-Level BDDC Applied to Parameterised Elasticity Problems
abstract: When material or geometric parameters vary across a family of related finite element problems—such as occurs in design optimisation or uncertainty quantification loops—the optimal coarse space for a BDDC preconditioner may change between solves. This paper compares four coarse space constructions (classical vertex-based, edge-average based, spectral BDDC with threshold selection, and a fixed offline-constructed space computed from a reference parameter set) on a batch of 500 linear elasticity problems with Young's moduli sampled from a log-normal distribution over a two-material domain. Condition number bounds, iteration counts, and total solve times are recorded. The spectral coarse space maintains iteration counts below 60 across all samples but incurs a construction overhead that is only amortised after solving approximately 15 systems. The fixed offline space performs comparably for moderate parameter variation but degrades for samples more than two standard deviations from the reference. Recommendations for practical use in optimisation loops are given.

title: Towards Real-Time Flood Inundation Simulation Using Domain-Decomposed Shallow Water Equations on GPU Clusters
abstract: Operational flood forecasting requires solving the two-dimensional shallow water equations over large irregular domains in under-real-time conditions. This paper describes a finite volume discretisation on unstructured triangular grids, combined with a domain decomposition strategy in which each GPU handles one subdomain and inter-subdomain fluxes are communicated via MPI between time steps. An explicit Runge–Kutta time integration scheme with local time stepping is used to avoid global CFL constraint bottlenecks in regions with small cells near embankments. The method is validated against two benchmark cases: a dam-break problem with an analytical solution and a historical flood event on the Tisa River in 2006, using a 1 km² mesh of 180 000 cells. Simulation of 24 hours of flood evolution is completed in 7.3 minutes on four GPU nodes, compared to 3.1 hours on a 48-core CPU cluster. Sensitivity of inundation extent predictions to Manning roughness coefficient uncertainty is also explored using 40 ensemble runs.

title: Batched Low-Rank Updates for Domain Decomposition Preconditioners in Repeated Assembly–Solve Cycles
abstract: In manufacturing simulation workflows, the geometry and material distribution of a component remain fixed while boundary conditions or load cases change across dozens of solves. Each change in loading alters the global stiffness matrix only locally—near applied forces and contacts—making a full preconditioner rebuild wasteful. This paper proposes a batched low-rank update strategy for BDDC and one-level additive Schwarz preconditioners, where only the affected subdomain factors are refactored and the coarse problem is updated via a bordered system solve. The update cost is proportional to the number of altered subdomains rather than total problem size. Tests on a stamping-die simulation with 2.3 million degrees of freedom and 80 load cases show that the update strategy reduces total preconditioner build time by 61% while increasing solve-phase iteration counts by no more than 8% compared to fresh builds. An error indicator based on the local residual is proposed to trigger full rebuilds when updates accumulate.

title: Communication-Avoiding One-Sided FETI-DP for Latency-Sensitive Simulation on Multi-GPU Workstations
abstract: Multi-GPU workstations with NVLink interconnects present a qualitatively different communication profile from MPI-based clusters: data transfers between GPUs are fast but the latency of CPU-mediated synchronisation points can dominate for small subdomain problems. This preprint proposes a one-sided FETI-DP variant in which all inter-subdomain communication is handled through direct GPU memory access using CUDA-aware MPI and persistent requests, eliminating CPU involvement from the inner solver loop. A communication-avoiding Krylov method (CA-GMRES with s=4) is used to further reduce synchronisation points. The method is evaluated on a four-GPU workstation (NVIDIA A100 GPUs connected via NVLink) solving transient structural dynamics problems with time step sizes chosen to require between 20 and 80 FETI-DP iterations per step. For problems with 4 to 8 subdomains per GPU, wall-clock time per time step is reduced by 27% to 41% compared to standard FETI-DP with blocking MPI. Detailed communication trace analysis is included.

title: Cross-Lingual Transfer for Mood Classification in Streaming Audio Metadata: Balkan Language Varieties
abstract: Mood classification of audio content is commercially valuable for playlist curation but manually labelled data in minority languages remain scarce. We study zero-shot and few-shot cross-lingual transfer from English and German mood-labelled datasets to Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, and Macedonian audio metadata. Source datasets contain 22 000 and 14 000 labelled examples respectively. Experiments use a multilingual transformer fine-tuned on source languages and evaluated on 1 500 labelled examples per target language. Zero-shot transfer yields macro F1 of 0.55–0.61 across target languages, while five-shot prompted adaptation raises this to 0.66–0.71. We additionally probe the extent to which orthographic differences between Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts affect transfer, finding only marginal impact after transliteration. Results indicate that cross-lingual transfer is a practical path toward mood classifiers for these languages without requiring large annotated corpora.

title: On the Minimal Consistent DFA Problem and Its Approximability
abstract: The problem of finding a smallest deterministic finite automaton consistent with a given set of positive and negative strings is NP-hard. This paper revisits the approximability of Minimum Consistent DFA (MCDFA) under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions. We tighten a known inapproximability lower bound, showing that MCDFA cannot be approximated within a factor of n^(1/3 − ε) in polynomial time unless P = NP, where n is the total length of the input sample. The proof uses a reduction from graph colouring adapted to the automaton setting. We also describe a branch-and-bound exact solver that outperforms previous implementations on instances with up to 18 states, verified against a corpus of 3,400 randomly generated instances. Practical implications for grammatical inference pipelines that rely on minimality as a regulariser are discussed.

title: In-situ characterisation of brick masonry mechanical properties in pre-1945 residential buildings in northern Serbia
abstract: This study reports flat-jack and minor destructive testing results collected from 34 pre-1945 brick masonry residential buildings in Subotica, Sombor, and Kikinda. Single and double flat-jack tests were performed at 68 measurement points to determine compressive stress states and elastic moduli; diagonal compression tests were conducted on extracted panel specimens to obtain shear strength parameters. Mean compressive strength of the brick units was 8.4 MPa (CoV 0.31), and mortar compressive strength averaged 1.7 MPa. Elastic moduli derived from flat-jack data ranged from 1,100 to 3,800 MPa. The results are compared with values prescribed in Serbian and Eurocode 6 standards, revealing that code default values overestimate stiffness by approximately 25% for lime-mortar joints. A database of 204 individual test records is made available as supplementary material, intended to support regional fragility model calibration.

title: A rapid visual screening form adapted for the unreinforced masonry building stock of the Vojvodina region
abstract: Rapid visual screening (RVS) methods developed for Mediterranean or North American contexts do not adequately capture the specific typological and seismological characteristics of the Vojvodina flatland region. This paper presents a modified RVS form derived from the FEMA 154 framework but recalibrated using local building inventory data from three municipalities. Scoring modifiers are introduced for shallow foundation soils typical of alluvial plains, single-wythe cavity wall construction, and original lime-mortar bed joints. The form was tested by six trained evaluators on 220 buildings in Subotica; inter-rater reliability measured by Cohen's kappa reached 0.74. Comparison with detailed analytical vulnerability indices computed for a 40-building subset shows the RVS correctly identifies high-vulnerability structures with 82% precision and 78% recall. The form is designed to be completed in under 12 minutes per building without interior access.

title: Nonlinear static analysis of unreinforced brick masonry walls under combined gravity and lateral loading: sensitivity to material parameter uncertainty
abstract: Pushover analyses of single-storey unreinforced brick masonry wall assemblies were performed in a commercial finite-element environment using a smeared-crack constitutive model. A Monte Carlo sampling scheme with 500 realisations was applied to propagate uncertainty in five input parameters: compressive strength, tensile strength, shear bond strength, elastic modulus, and fracture energy. Geometry and boundary conditions were based on a prototype wall configuration extracted from the Vojvodina survey database. Results show that peak lateral resistance is most sensitive to shear bond strength (Sobol index 0.41) and least sensitive to fracture energy (0.04). The coefficient of variation of peak resistance was 0.19, and of ultimate displacement capacity 0.28. Implications for fragility function dispersion parameters are discussed, and recommendations are made for the minimum number of material tests needed to constrain dispersion below 0.20.

title: Seismic fragility functions for low-rise unreinforced masonry buildings in the Pannonian Basin derived from observed damage data
abstract: Empirical fragility functions were derived for three URM building classes (pre-1919 solid brick, 1919–1945 solid brick, post-1945 mixed masonry) using post-earthquake damage survey records from four moderate-intensity earthquake events in Hungary and Serbia between 1956 and 2013. Damage observations totalled 1,847 building entries coded to the EMS-98 scale. Intensity measure was peak ground acceleration estimated from recorded or simulated ground motion fields. Lognormal fragility parameters were estimated by maximum likelihood for five damage states. Median PGA for complete damage (DS4) ranges from 0.18 g for the oldest class to 0.27 g for post-1945 construction. Epistemic uncertainty bounds are reported alongside aleatory dispersion values (β between 0.52 and 0.71). The functions are compared with Hazus and Risk-UE curves and show systematically lower medians, attributed to construction practice differences and soil amplification in the Pannonian Basin.

title: Masonry building typology and seismic vulnerability: a chapter on Central European flatland urban stock
abstract: This book chapter synthesises typological classification schemes for urban unreinforced masonry buildings in Central European flatland cities, with emphasis on the Vojvodina and Great Hungarian Plain regions. It describes constructional periods, dominant wall systems, floor typologies, and foundation practice from pre-Ottoman through socialist-era construction. The chapter reviews available mechanical property datasets from regional literature and presents a harmonised typology matrix with 12 building classes aligned to the European Taxonomy for Seismic Vulnerability. Vulnerability index ranges are assigned to each class based on a combination of analytical and empirical evidence reviewed from 23 regional studies. The chapter closes with a discussion of data gaps and recommendations for coordinated survey campaigns across national borders, noting that administrative fragmentation has hindered the development of cross-border exposure models.

title: Ground motion record selection for nonlinear time-history analysis of low-rise masonry structures in low-to-moderate seismicity zones
abstract: Nonlinear time-history analyses of URM structures in low-to-moderate seismicity environments require ground motion records that are scarce in regional databases. This study evaluates three record selection strategies—conditional mean spectrum (CMS) matching, uniform hazard spectrum scaling, and stochastic simulation using regional source parameters—applied to a reference site in Subotica (rock reference PGA hazard 0.07 g at 475-year return period). Fourteen synthetic and 22 recorded ground motion sets were compiled and used as input for incremental dynamic analyses of a two-storey URM index building. Drift capacity exceedance probabilities at the 475-year hazard level differed by up to 31% across selection methods. CMS-matched recorded sets produced the lowest dispersion (σ_ln 0.38). Recommendations are given for minimum suite size (at least 11 records) and for handling near-zero-crossing ground motions from shallow crustal sources characteristic of the Pannonian region.

title: Structural performance of load-bearing masonry walls after simulated freeze–thaw cycling: implications for seismic capacity in continental climates
abstract: Forty-eight full-scale brick masonry wall specimens with two mortar types (hydraulic lime and Portland-lime blend) were subjected to 0, 25, 50, and 75 freeze–thaw cycles following EN 12371 procedures, then tested under combined axial and shear loading. Diagonal tensile strength decreased by 18% after 50 cycles and 34% after 75 cycles for lime mortar specimens; Portland-lime specimens showed 9% and 21% reductions respectively. Elastic modulus degradation was more pronounced, reaching 41% after 75 cycles for lime mortar. Cyclic shear envelope curves were recorded and used to update constitutive model parameters. Fragility shift calculations indicate that buildings with frost-damaged mortar joints may reach a one-damage-state shift in median PGA capacity, which is relevant for municipalities in the northern Vojvodina plain where freeze–thaw cycles exceed 40 annually. Maintenance and repointing implications for seismic risk management are outlined.

title: Cross-border seismic exposure model for the Hungary–Serbia border region: combining cadastral data with remote-sensing building footprints
abstract: A georeferenced exposure model covering approximately 94,000 residential buildings in the Hungary–Serbia border zone was assembled by combining national cadastral records, OpenStreetMap footprints, and Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery. Building age and height were estimated using a supervised random-forest classifier trained on 1,200 field-surveyed reference buildings; overall accuracy was 79% for construction period assignment. Masonry typology shares derived from field surveys in Subotica and Szeged were assigned spatially using a dasymetric mapping approach. The resulting model was coupled with a probabilistic seismic hazard model (50-year exceedance curves at 475- and 2475-year return periods) to compute municipality-level expected annual losses. Results indicate that pre-1919 URM stock concentrated in historical city centres dominates risk despite representing only 14% of the total building count. The model data are formatted for compatibility with the ESRI-based risk workflow.

title: Bayesian updating of masonry fragility functions using post-inspection data from a municipality-scale screening campaign
abstract: A Bayesian framework is presented for updating lognormal fragility function parameters using data gathered during a rapid post-earthquake inspection campaign. The methodology is demonstrated using 312 building inspection records collected after a magnitude 4.6 event near Senta in 2021, combining prior distributions derived from the 2018 regional empirical fragility study with likelihood functions formed from EMS-98 damage assignments. Posterior median PGA values shifted by between −6% and +14% relative to priors depending on building class, with the largest updates for the post-1945 class due to the large number of inspected specimens. Posterior dispersion was reduced by 0.07–0.12 in logarithmic units. The workflow is implemented as a scripted pipeline in the R statistical environment and is described sufficiently to allow replication. Sensitivity of posterior estimates to the choice of ground motion field interpolation method is assessed through a cross-validation exercise.

title: Automated detection of wall crack patterns in masonry buildings using convolutional neural networks applied to smartphone photographs
abstract: A convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained to detect and classify crack patterns in external brick masonry walls from photographs taken with standard smartphones under variable lighting and angle conditions. Training data consisted of 8,400 annotated images collected during field campaigns in Subotica, Sombor, and Pécs over three years; four crack classes were defined following EMS-98 damage grade descriptors. The best-performing architecture (a modified ResNet-50 with transfer learning from ImageNet weights) achieved 83% macro-averaged F1 on a held-out test set of 960 images. A lightweight deployment version was packaged as an Android application for field use on low-specification devices. Integration into the adapted RVS workflow from the 2015 study is described, and preliminary results from a pilot deployment involving 18 volunteer assessors on 95 buildings are reported. Limitations regarding shadow artefacts and painted surfaces are discussed.

title: Influence of irregular plan geometry on seismic vulnerability indices of single-storey farm buildings in the Vojvodina agricultural landscape
abstract: Single-storey unreinforced masonry farm outbuildings in rural Vojvodina frequently exhibit L-shaped, T-shaped, or elongated rectangular plan geometries resulting from incremental construction over decades. This study evaluates whether standard vulnerability index methods, calibrated on regular residential blocks, adequately capture the increased torsional demand in irregular layouts. Forty-three buildings of documented plan geometry were modelled using equivalent frame methods; six regularity metrics were computed and correlated with displacement capacity reduction factors. Buildings with eccentricity ratios exceeding 0.25 showed ultimate drift capacities 22–35% lower than regular counterparts of identical wall density. A correction factor table is proposed for application within the vulnerability index method. Field data from 211 rural buildings in three municipalities support the statistical basis of the correction. The findings have direct relevance for rural seismic risk assessments and post-earthquake recovery planning in agricultural regions.

title: Towards a seismic risk dashboard for local authorities: pilot implementation in two Vojvodina municipalities
abstract: This preprint describes the architecture and preliminary outputs of a web-based seismic risk dashboard designed for use by municipal civil protection offices. The system integrates the cross-border exposure model, Bayesian-updated fragility functions, and a probabilistic seismic hazard module into a GIS-backed interface accessible without specialist software. For each of the two pilot municipalities (Kanjiža and Bačka Topola), the dashboard displays building-level vulnerability scores, municipality-aggregate loss exceedance curves, and scenario shake-maps for a set of predefined earthquake scenarios. Response time for scenario computation is under 40 seconds on a standard virtual server instance. User testing with eight municipal staff members identified usability issues primarily around legend interpretation and export formats. Known limitations of the underlying data, particularly sparse instrumental recordings for calibrating the hazard model, are documented openly. Full release is anticipated following revision based on user feedback.
