title: Semi-Rigid Behaviour of Dowel-Type Connections in Glulam Portal Frames: Influence on Second-Order Effects
abstract: The doctoral work underlying this study examined how joint semi-rigidity affects second-order sway in single-storey glulam portal frames. A parametric finite element model was assembled in which each connection was represented by a non-linear rotational spring calibrated from experimental moment–rotation data obtained on 48 beam-column specimens. Frame spans of 12, 18, and 24 m with rafter slopes of 3° and 6° were analysed under characteristic wind and snow loads from EN 1991. Ignoring joint flexibility underestimated horizontal apex displacement by up to 28 % and overestimated critical load multiplier by 19 % relative to the semi-rigid model. A simplified correction factor, expressed in terms of the ratio of connection stiffness to member stiffness, is proposed for direct use in design practice without full second-order analysis.

title: Benchmark Dataset and Acceptance Criteria for Eurocode 5 Connection Stiffness Formulae: A Multi-Laboratory Round Robin
abstract: Eurocode 5 provides slip-modulus expressions for several connector types that are widely used in structural analysis software but rarely validated across independent laboratories. This paper reports a coordinated round-robin exercise conducted at five university testing facilities in Serbia, Slovenia, Croatia, and Austria, using identical specimen batches cut from a single GL24h glulam batch and a single three-layer CLT batch. Dowel, bolt, nail, and STS connections were each tested by all five laboratories following a common protocol. Coefficients of variation in slip modulus across laboratories ranged from 6.2 % (dowel) to 18.4 % (STS), indicating substantial inter-laboratory variability for screw-type connections. Code predictions fell within the 25th–75th percentile band for dowels and bolts but underestimated STS stiffness by a median of 17 %. Proposed tolerance limits and minimum specimen counts for future standardisation of connection stiffness testing are derived from the data.

title: Rate-Distortion Analysis of Scalable Video Coding for Wireless Multicast Channels
abstract: This paper examines the trade-offs between spatial scalability layers and channel error rates in H.264/SVC streams delivered over simulated wireless multicast links. Using a custom OPNET-based simulation framework, we modelled three packet-loss distributions corresponding to indoor 802.11g environments and measured peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) across eight standard test sequences encoded at four quality levels. Results show that two-layer SVC configurations provide a 1.8 dB average PSNR improvement over single-layer streams at loss rates above 4 % without increasing average throughput demand. The layered approach also reduces rebuffering events by approximately 22 % in simulated mobile receiver scenarios. A closed-form rate-distortion bound is derived for the two-layer case and validated against empirical measurements. The model predicts observed PSNR within 0.4 dB on average, confirming its practical utility for network planner dimensioning exercises.

title: Buffer-Based Adaptive Streaming with Segment Size Heterogeneity: A Comparative Study
abstract: Adaptive bitrate (ABR) streaming clients typically assume uniform segment durations, yet content-aware encoders increasingly produce variable-length segments. This study quantifies the impact of segment duration heterogeneity on three open-source ABR algorithms—a rate-based controller, a buffer-based controller, and a combined hybrid—using traces collected from a campus LTE network over 14 days. Segment durations in the test library ranged from 1.8 s to 6.2 s. Buffer occupancy models were re-derived for non-uniform segments and integrated into each algorithm. Experiments over 1 200 simulated sessions show that the hybrid controller degrades least (mean rebuffering ratio increases by 0.3 percentage points) when segment duration variance is high, while the pure rate-based controller suffers a 1.1 percentage point increase. Bitrate switch frequency rises by up to 40 % for all controllers under high variance, reducing perceptual smoothness scores in a 24-participant subjective test.

title: Subjective Quality Assessment Methodology for Compressed Video on Small Mobile Screens
abstract: Standard video quality assessment methodologies defined by ITU-R BT.500 were designed for large-display environments and do not directly translate to smartphones with screens smaller than 6 inches. This paper describes an adapted single-stimulus methodology applied to 30 source sequences encoded at six H.264 bitrates between 150 kbps and 4 Mbps and presented on three device models with different display resolutions. A panel of 48 non-expert observers rated each clip on a 5-point absolute category rating scale in a controlled lighting environment. Statistical analysis reveals that mean opinion score differences between device classes are significant at the 5 % level only for bitrates below 600 kbps, suggesting that display resolution influences perceived quality mainly in bandwidth-constrained regimes. A linear mapping from full-reference SSIM to predicted mean opinion score is fitted per device class, with R² values between 0.87 and 0.93.

title: Projection Format Selection for 360-Degree Video Encoding: Bandwidth and Distortion Trade-offs
abstract: Omnidirectional video can be projected onto a 2D plane using equirectangular projection (ERP), cubemap projection (CMP), or equi-angular cubemap (EAC) before conventional video encoding. This paper provides a systematic comparison of these three formats across five 8K 360-degree source sequences encoded with HEVC at bitrates from 8 Mbps to 80 Mbps. Weighted spherical PSNR (WS-PSNR) and spherical SSIM (S-SSIM) are used as distortion metrics. CMP and EAC both outperform ERP by 0.5–1.2 dB WS-PSNR at equivalent bitrates for head-frontal viewport windows, but ERP retains an advantage of 0.3 dB in peripheral regions. Encoding complexity, measured in CPU-seconds per encoded frame on a reference platform, is 11 % higher for EAC than ERP. The findings inform a simple heuristic for format selection based on content motion statistics and target viewport distribution.

title: Tile-Based HEVC Encoding for Viewport-Adaptive 360-Degree Streaming
abstract: Tile-based HEVC encoding partitions an omnidirectional video frame into independently decodable spatial regions, enabling a client to request only tiles within the predicted viewport at high bitrate while fetching peripheral tiles at lower bitrate. We describe an encoder configuration that partitions 4K ERP frames into a 6×4 tile grid and evaluate it against monolithic encoding across twelve content sequences. A greedy viewport-area selection algorithm allocates a higher-bitrate tile set covering a 100° × 90° head-movement prediction window. In network simulations with throughput traces from a 4G field trial, the tile-based scheme reduces average segment payload by 34 % while maintaining mean viewport WS-PSNR within 0.8 dB of a full-frame high-bitrate reference. Tile boundary artefacts account for a 0.4 dB penalty observable with full-reference metrics but rated insignificant in a 32-participant subjective experiment.

title: Head Motion Prediction for 360-Degree Video Streaming Using Recurrent Neural Networks
abstract: Accurate head motion prediction is a prerequisite for viewport-adaptive streaming systems that must pre-fetch tiles before the user moves. This paper trains and evaluates three LSTM architectures on a dataset of 1 440 head-tracking sessions collected from 40 participants watching twelve 360-degree videos on a commercial head-mounted display. Prediction horizons of 250 ms, 500 ms, and 1 000 ms are evaluated. At 500 ms horizon, the best LSTM variant achieves a mean angular prediction error of 4.8° compared with 7.2° for a linear extrapolation baseline. The model with 128 hidden units and a 15-frame input window provides the best accuracy-to-complexity ratio, requiring 0.9 ms inference time on an embedded ARM processor at 2.0 GHz. A viewport coverage analysis shows that the predicted viewport window covers the actual user viewport in 93.2 % of frames when a 10° safety margin is applied.

title: Quality of Experience Modelling for Omnidirectional Video: Influence of Bitrate Switching and Viewport Mismatch
abstract: This paper develops an integrated QoE model for 360-degree video streaming that jointly accounts for three impairment dimensions: average encoded quality, mid-session bitrate switches, and viewport mismatch events caused by prediction errors. A subjective experiment recruited 52 observers who watched 180 video sessions on an HTC Cosmo HMD across a designed factorial experiment combining three quality levels, two switch frequencies, and three mismatch magnitudes. A random-effects regression model fit to the resulting mean opinion scores yields a QoE score function with R² = 0.91. Viewport mismatch events lasting longer than 300 ms carry a penalty coefficient four times larger than a quality-level reduction of one tier. The model is expressed in closed form and can be evaluated in fewer than 1 ms, making it suitable for real-time ABR decision algorithms. Validation on an independent dataset of 18 participants yields a root-mean-square prediction error of 0.31 MOS points.

title: Adaptive Streaming of 360-Degree Video over LTE-A with Handover-Aware Bitrate Selection
abstract: Mobile users streaming omnidirectional video over LTE-Advanced experience throughput drops during handover events that last 50–300 ms but may force multiple bitrate downgrades under aggressive ABR policies. We instrument a commercial LTE-A modem to expose handover prediction signals to a modified DASH.js client and design a handover-aware bitrate selection algorithm that proactively reduces segment bitrate one segment before a predicted handover and recovers over the subsequent two segments. Evaluation uses 7 200 handover events recorded from three mobile routes in Novi Sad with base-station density of approximately 0.8 cells/km². The algorithm reduces handover-induced rebuffering by 61 % relative to a buffer-based baseline while keeping average bitrate within 4 % of the baseline. QoE model scores, using the model described in our 2020 paper, improve by 0.27 points on average.

title: Survey of Adaptive Bitrate Algorithms for 360-Degree Video: From Heuristic to Learning-Based Approaches
abstract: This survey reviews approximately 60 published ABR algorithms proposed specifically for omnidirectional video streaming between 2016 and 2022. Algorithms are classified into four families: buffer-based heuristics, model predictive control approaches, reinforcement learning methods, and hybrid schemes that combine learned viewport prediction with classical rate control. For each family the review discusses design assumptions, computational requirements, and reported QoE gains. A unified evaluation framework is described in which algorithm descriptions are mapped onto five common axes: prediction horizon, tile granularity, network model type, QoE target metric, and deployment complexity. The survey identifies three open problems: the lack of standardised public head-tracking datasets for fair comparison, the absence of energy consumption metrics in most evaluations, and the limited treatment of multi-user shared-link scenarios. A table of 38 datasets used in surveyed papers is included.

title: Network-Aware Encoding Parameter Selection for Live 360-Degree Streaming Using Feedback from 5G NR Radio Measurements
abstract: Live 360-degree streaming with sub-second latency imposes tight constraints on encoder configuration because encoding delay and bitrate must be determined before network conditions fully evolve. This paper describes a system that ingests 5G NR layer-1 channel quality indicator (CQI) reports from a gNB and uses them to set HEVC encoder quantisation parameters and tile bitrate allocations 300 ms ahead of segment transmission. A Kalman-filter-based CQI predictor feeds a model predictive controller that adjusts QP per tile column to match predicted available throughput. Experiments on a private 5G NR testbed at 3.5 GHz with two indoor users show that the system reduces encoder throughput overruns by 78 % relative to a reactive scheme and cuts mean startup delay from 1.9 s to 0.7 s. Viewport quality in the high-priority tile region degrades by less than 0.6 dB WS-PSNR compared with an unconstrained offline encode.

title: Energy Consumption of ABR Streaming Clients on Android Devices Under Viewport-Adaptive 360-Degree Workloads
abstract: Viewport-adaptive 360-degree streaming requires continuous head-tracking, tile selection logic, multi-track decoding, and spherical rendering, all of which affect device energy consumption beyond what standard video streaming imposes. We instrument five mid-range Android smartphones with external power meters and measure per-component energy under six streaming configurations varying tile grid density (3×2, 4×3, 6×4), rendering resolution (2K, 4K), and prediction model complexity (linear, 64-unit LSTM, 128-unit LSTM). Tile grid density has the dominant effect: moving from 3×2 to 6×4 increases total session energy by 18–27 % depending on device, driven mainly by decoder and network interface costs. The 128-unit LSTM predictor adds only 2 % energy overhead versus linear extrapolation while reducing angular prediction error by 2.1°. A Pareto frontier analysis identifies three configurations that balance energy use and QoE model score for different battery-life targets.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Joint Viewport Prediction and Bitrate Adaptation in Multi-User 360-Degree Streaming Scenarios
abstract: In shared wireless cells, a single user's aggressive bitrate selection degrades QoE for other users. This paper formulates the joint viewport prediction and bitrate adaptation problem for multiple co-located 360-degree streaming clients as a multi-agent reinforcement learning task, where each agent observes its own buffer state and viewport history and a shared channel occupancy signal. Agents are trained with proximal policy optimisation on a trace-driven simulator built from 5G NR throughput logs collected in a suburban environment over six weeks. A cooperative reward structure penalises agents that monopolise channel capacity. After 200 000 training episodes, the trained policy increases mean per-user QoE score by 0.19 points compared with independent single-agent baselines in two-user scenarios and by 0.31 points in four-user scenarios, at the cost of 7 % lower peak single-user bitrate. Ablation experiments confirm that the shared channel occupancy signal accounts for two-thirds of the multi-user gain.

title: Low-Latency 360-Degree Video Streaming over Wi-Fi 6E: Measurement Study and Latency Decomposition
abstract: Wi-Fi 6E opens the 6 GHz band and introduces features—multi-link operation, target wake time scheduling, and 320 MHz channels—that reduce airtime contention and queuing delay. This paper presents a measurement study of live 360-degree streaming latency over a single Wi-Fi 6E access point serving one to eight concurrent HMD clients in an open-plan office. End-to-end latency is decomposed into encoder, packetisation, wireless transmission, decoder, and render pipeline components using hardware timestamps at each stage. At one client, median end-to-end latency is 68 ms; at eight clients it rises to 142 ms. The dominant latency contributor shifts from encoder buffering (single user) to wireless queuing (eight users) as load increases. A lightweight scheduling policy based on per-client buffer state reduces eight-client median latency to 109 ms without measurable throughput loss. The paper provides per-component latency distributions as open data to support future protocol design.

title: Container-Aware Attack Surface Enumeration in Kubernetes Deployments
abstract: Kubernetes-based deployments introduce attack surface components—pod-to-pod network policies, service mesh configurations, and shared kernel namespaces—that conventional host-centric scanning pipelines do not model. This paper extends an existing agent-based reconnaissance framework with three Kubernetes-aware modules: a policy extractor that reads NetworkPolicy and Ingress resources via the API server, a container-image vulnerability mapper that correlates image SBOMs with NVD records, and an inter-pod reachability analyser that annotates the attack graph with lateral-movement edges. The extended framework was evaluated on six synthetic Kubernetes clusters ranging from 20 to 180 pods. Compared to a host-centric baseline, the extended approach discovered 37% more reachability edges and mapped 51% more unique vulnerabilities. Runtime overhead of the additional modules was under 8 seconds per cluster for the largest evaluated configuration.

Eksperiment koristi tri različito anotatovane verzije istog korpusa od 3.600 dokumenata: prvu anotiranu od strane pravnih eksperata (visoka konzistentnost, kapa = 0,82), drugu od strane studenata prava (srednja konzistentnost, kapa = 0,67) i treću od strane opštih korisnika putem platforme sličnoj crowdsourcing modelu (niska konzistentnost, kapa = 0,54). Na svakoj verziji trenirani su logistička regresija, Random Forest i BERT-baziran model. Rezultati pokazuju da razlika u F1 meri između ekspertske i crowdsourced anotacije iznosi između 3,1 i 7,8 procentnih poena, zavisno od modela i pravne kategorije. BERT model pokazuje veću robustnost na bučne oznake od klasičnih modela. Diskutovane su implikacije za praktičnu organizaciju anotacionih projekata u pravnom domenu.

title: Topic Model Diagnostics for Newsroom Monitoring: A Pilot Deployment at a Regional Serbian Media Outlet
abstract: This preprint documents a pilot study carried out in collaboration with a regional Serbian online news outlet (anonymised) in which an HDP-based topic monitoring pipeline was deployed over a six-month period from July to December 2023. The pipeline ingests roughly 200 articles per day, updates the topic model incrementally using a mini-batch Gibbs sampler, and exposes topic trend summaries and anomaly alerts through a lightweight web dashboard built with a Python framework. Twenty-three editorial staff members used the dashboard; structured interviews and a standardised usability questionnaire (SUS score: 74.1 ± 8.3) were administered at the end of the pilot. The main reported benefits were rapid identification of emerging local topics and easier cross-desk story coordination. Primary friction points included confusing topic label wording and slow initial loading. The paper describes the system architecture, operational statistics, and lessons for researchers deploying topic models in resource-constrained media organisations.

title: Probabilistic Change Propagation Models for Reducing Unnecessary Recompilation
abstract: Conservative incremental build systems recompile any artifact that transitively depends on a changed input, even when the change is likely semantically irrelevant (e.g., a comment edit or a reformatting commit). We train a logistic regression model on historical build logs from two organisations to estimate the probability that a given file change causes an observable output change in each downstream artifact. The model uses 14 features derived from the dependency graph topology, change size, file type, and historical change frequency. On a held-out test period spanning six months of commits, the model correctly identified as unnecessary 38% of recompilation tasks that a conservative policy would have scheduled, with a false-negative rate of 1.7% (i.e., missed necessary recompilations). We discuss the safety implications and propose a two-tier build policy that uses the model output as a scheduling hint rather than a hard decision.

title: Avoiding the news or avoiding the noise? Motivations for news disengagement among university students in Serbia
abstract: This study examines the motivations behind news avoidance among Serbian university students aged 18–26. Drawing on a mixed-methods design, the research combined an online survey (n=412) administered at four Serbian universities with 24 semi-structured interviews. Participants were asked about their daily media routines, emotional reactions to news content, and trust in specific news sources. Results indicate that avoidance is most commonly driven by emotional fatigue and perceived irrelevance rather than deliberate political disengagement. Social media emerged as both a gateway and a barrier: 61% of respondents reported encountering news incidentally via Instagram or TikTok, yet 44% said they actively muted or unfollowed news-related accounts in the previous month. Qualitative data suggest that news avoidance is often situational and cyclical rather than a stable disposition. The findings are discussed in relation to post-communist media trust deficits and implications for public service broadcasting outreach.

title: Platform switching and news habits: A longitudinal diary study among young adults in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper reports findings from a two-week media diary study conducted with 87 young adults (aged 19–29) recruited from Novi Sad and surrounding municipalities in Vojvodina. Participants submitted daily structured logs recording each news encounter across television, print, online news portals, and social media platforms. The study tracked how consumption patterns shifted across the fortnight in response to a regional political event that occurred during the data-collection period. Results show that the event temporarily reversed avoidance behaviours for 38% of participants, but that this reversal was largely confined to social media platforms rather than traditional news outlets. Long-form article engagement remained low throughout. The diary method allowed granular tracking of platform-switching behaviour not captured in standard survey instruments. Findings contribute to debates about incidental news exposure as a substitute for intentional news-seeking in low-trust media environments.

title: News avoidance in four post-communist contexts: Comparing Serbia, Poland, Czech Republic, and Hungary
abstract: This comparative study investigates the prevalence and character of news avoidance across four Central and Eastern European countries with distinct post-communist media trajectories. Using harmonised online surveys administered in Serbia (n=503), Poland (n=518), Czech Republic (n=496), and Hungary (n=511), the research targeted respondents aged 18–35. The questionnaire drew on adapted items from the Reuters Institute Digital News Report, supplemented with country-specific items addressing institutional trust and press freedom perceptions. Avoidance rates varied markedly: 34% of Serbian respondents classified themselves as active avoiders compared with 21% in the Czech Republic. Regression models identified distrust in political ownership of media and low perceived news utility as the strongest cross-national predictors of avoidance. The paper argues that media system legacies shape avoidance not only through structural conditions but through culturally embedded expectations of news as government communication.

title: When algorithms decide: Young news avoiders' awareness of algorithmic curation on social media
abstract: This qualitative study explores how young news avoiders in Serbia conceptualise and respond to algorithmic curation on social media platforms. Twenty-eight in-depth interviews were conducted with participants aged 20–30 who had previously identified themselves as news avoiders in a screening survey. Interview questions probed understanding of how content appears in feeds, experiences of unexpected news exposure, and strategies for controlling news visibility. Findings reveal that most participants hold only a vague understanding of algorithmic filtering, referring to it in folk terms such as 'what the app thinks I like'. Despite limited technical awareness, many had developed practical avoidance strategies—unfollowing, blocking keywords, using secondary accounts—that effectively reduce news encounter. The paper discusses implications for media literacy education and the design of civic information tools aimed at re-engaging avoiders through platform-native formats rather than traditional news presentation conventions.

title: Short-form video and hard news: Do TikTok news clips reduce avoidance among young Serbian adults?
abstract: This experimental study tested whether exposure to short-form video news content on a TikTok-style interface reduces subsequent news avoidance intentions compared with exposure to equivalent text-based news articles. A between-subjects online experiment was conducted with 243 participants recruited from three universities in Serbia (mean age 22.4 years). Participants were randomly assigned to view five news items in one of three formats: text article, vertical video with captions, or vertical video without captions. Post-exposure measures included avoidance intention, perceived effort, emotional arousal, and subjective comprehension. Vertical video with captions produced significantly lower avoidance intention scores than text (p < .01), with effect sizes in the small-to-medium range (d = 0.41). Emotional arousal partially mediated the effect. Comprehension did not differ significantly across conditions. Results suggest that format rather than topic selection may be a more tractable lever for reducing avoidance, though long-term retention effects remain untested.

title: Measuring news avoidance: A methodological review of survey instruments used in European audience research, 2010–2022
abstract: This article reviews survey instruments used to measure news avoidance in European audience research published between 2010 and 2022. Forty-one studies were identified through systematic database searches; their measurement approaches were coded for dimensionality, item wording, reference period, and platform specificity. The review finds substantial heterogeneity: 27 studies used single-item measures, 11 used multi-item scales with varying factor structures, and only 3 employed platform-disaggregated measures that distinguished avoidance across television, print, and digital channels. Cronbach's alpha values where reported ranged from 0.61 to 0.89, reflecting inconsistent construct operationalisation. The paper proposes a minimal harmonised item set suitable for cross-national replication studies and discusses the particular challenges of adapting instruments for Central and Eastern European contexts where the meaning of 'news' and trusted source categories differ from Western European norms. Practical guidance for researchers planning comparative work is provided.

title: Генерацијске разлике у избегавању вести: Поређење миленијалаца и генерације Z у Србији [Generational differences in news avoidance: Comparing Millennials and Generation Z in Serbia]
abstract: This study compares news avoidance patterns between Millennials (born 1982–1996) and Generation Z (born 1997–2010) in Serbia, using an online survey administered in 2015 with a quota sample of 620 respondents balanced by generation, gender, and region. The analysis focuses on differences in platform use, avoidance frequency, and stated reasons for avoidance. Generation Z respondents reported higher avoidance rates on television (72% rarely or never watched television news) but lower avoidance on social platforms, confirming a platform-specific rather than generalised avoidance pattern. Millennials showed higher avoidance of online news portals and greater engagement with aggregators. Qualitative follow-up focus groups (n=3 groups, 6–8 participants each) elaborated on perceived irrelevance of news content as the dominant motivation for both cohorts, though Millennials more frequently cited work-related information overload. Findings are discussed in relation to the Serbian media landscape of the mid-2010s.

title: News avoidance, political knowledge gaps, and democratic participation in a low-trust media environment: Evidence from Serbia
abstract: This paper examines the downstream consequences of habitual news avoidance for political knowledge and civic participation, using data from a two-wave panel survey conducted in Serbia in 2022–2023 (n=389 at Wave 2). Participants completed measures of news consumption frequency disaggregated by platform, a 12-item factual political knowledge quiz, and self-reported participation in four civic activities (voting, signing petitions, attending public meetings, engaging in online political discussion). Cross-lagged panel models show that avoidance at Wave 1 significantly predicted lower political knowledge at Wave 2 (β = −0.19, p < .001), and that this knowledge deficit partially mediated reduced participation in offline civic activities. Online political discussion was not significantly predicted by avoidance, suggesting compensatory information-seeking via non-news social media. The paper contributes to debates about whether news avoidance poses a systemic risk to democratic functioning or whether alternative information pathways can compensate in high-avoidance populations.

title: Between distrust and disinterest: News avoidance narratives among young adults in the Western Balkans
abstract: This preprint reports preliminary findings from narrative interviews conducted in 2025 with 45 young adults aged 18–32 across five Western Balkan countries (Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, and Albania). Participants were asked to narrate their relationship with news from adolescence to the present, allowing the research team to identify turning points and sustained patterns in avoidance behaviour. Thematic analysis identified three dominant narrative types: the 'burned once' narrative, in which a single perceived instance of media manipulation produced lasting distrust; the 'it doesn't affect me' narrative, centring on perceived distance between news content and lived experience; and the 'I already know' narrative, in which participants relied on peer social networks for news. Cross-country comparison suggests the 'burned once' narrative is more prevalent in contexts with recent experience of media censorship, while the 'I already know' narrative is more common in urban, higher-education samples. Full dataset analysis is ongoing.

title: Panel Design for Audience Research in Small Language Communities: Methodological Reflections from a Serbian Study
abstract: This methodological article reports on the design and first-wave execution of a longitudinal audience panel for Serbian-language media consumers. The panel recruited 1,104 respondents in 2011 using stratified random sampling from the city of Novi Sad and two smaller towns in Vojvodina, with quotas for gender, age bracket, municipality, and education level. The article discusses the specific challenges of panel maintenance in a small language community, including attrition risks, response fatigue, and the thin market for professional market-research infrastructure. First-wave descriptive statistics on media diet, trust in public versus commercial broadcasters, and digital news engagement are presented as a baseline for future waves. Retention incentive structures are evaluated, and a predictive model of dropout propensity using logistic regression (AUC = 0.71) is proposed. The panel dataset is described as openly accessible to researchers affiliated with the University of Novi Sad.

title: Remote Work and Editorial Coordination in Serbian Television During the COVID-19 Restrictions of 2020
abstract: This article examines how editorial coordination practices at Serbian commercial and public television broadcasters were adapted during the period of strict movement restrictions in spring 2020. Based on 33 interviews conducted by video call with editorial staff at 11 broadcasters between May and July 2020, supplemented by analysis of scheduling data and publicly available broadcast archives, the study documents shifts in story selection, source access, and internal communication. Interviewees at commercial stations reported a marked increase in reliance on institutional press releases and official briefings as primary sources, with field reporting dropping from an average of 7.4 to 2.1 reporter packages per bulletin at the three stations where longitudinal data were available. Public broadcaster staff reported better-resourced remote working arrangements but noted comparable reductions in source diversity. The article discusses implications for understanding how external crises interact with pre-existing labour conditions to shape journalistic output.

title: Memory Work and Platform Vernaculars: Serbian Music Video Nostalgia on YouTube Comment Sections
abstract: This study shifts analytical focus from music video texts to their reception, examining how audiences perform collective memory work in the YouTube comment sections beneath a selection of Serbian pop and folk music videos from the 1990s and early 2000s. A dataset of 14,320 comments was collected across 22 videos re-uploaded between 2018 and 2022, using the YouTube Data API v3. Thematic coding identified five recurrent memory practices: temporal anchoring ('this was playing when…'), generational address, expressions of loss tied to political rupture, comparative nostalgia contrasting the Yugoslav past with the present, and ironic distancing. Quantitative analysis shows that comments referencing Yugoslavia directly constitute 18.3% of the corpus and cluster heavily around videos from the transitional 1991–1996 period. The study also documents how platform affordances, particularly the chronological threading of comments, shape the temporality of nostalgic expression. Implications for the study of digital memory practices in post-conflict societies are discussed.

title: Mapping Pornography Regulation Research in Europe: A Systematic Review, 1995–2020
abstract: This systematic review maps published academic research on pornography regulation in European contexts over a 25-year period. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors searched seven databases and identified 183 peer-reviewed articles, book chapters, and doctoral theses meeting inclusion criteria. Items were coded for theoretical framework, method, geographic focus, and policy orientation. Quantitative analysis reveals that 61 percent of items focused on UK, Germany, or Sweden, with post-socialist European countries severely underrepresented at 7 percent of the total. Qualitative coding identifies four dominant research paradigms: feminist political economy, public health, legal positivism, and digital rights liberalism. The review documents limited dialogue between paradigms and a near-absence of empirical research on enforcement outcomes. The authors identify post-socialist regulatory contexts, platform-level governance, and intersections with algorithmic content moderation as underexplored areas warranting further research investment.

title: Minority press in transition: the Hungarian-language weeklies of Bačka in the first decade of Yugoslav rule, 1919–1929
abstract: This article examines six Hungarian-language weeklies published in the Bačka sub-region during the first decade of Yugoslav administration, drawing on holdings preserved at the Petőfi Literary Museum in Budapest and the City Library in Subotica. A comparative content analysis of 480 sampled issues addresses three themes: the negotiation of cultural identity under the new state, coverage of agrarian reform as experienced by Hungarian smallholders, and the management of advertising revenue in a shrinking readership environment. Findings show that the papers maintained a consistent editorial strategy of cultural continuity while largely avoiding direct political confrontation with Yugoslav authorities. Advertising content suggests a stable if contracting commercial base dominated by local merchants and craftsmen. The article contributes to scholarship on minority media survival strategies in post-1918 Central Europe and offers Vojvodina as a case study for comparison with Slovak and Romanian minority press situations.

title: Optical constants of reactively sputtered a-CNx films derived from single-wavelength ellipsometry: a baseline study
abstract: Amorphous carbon nitride films were deposited on silicon substrates by reactive DC magnetron sputtering at nitrogen partial pressures ranging from 0.05 to 0.4 Pa, with total argon–nitrogen pressures held at 0.6 Pa and a target power of 150 W. Film thickness (50–350 nm) and optical constants at 632.8 nm were extracted using a single-wavelength null ellipsometer assuming a uniform isotropic layer model. The refractive index n decreased from 2.31 to 1.84 as nitrogen partial pressure increased, while the extinction coefficient k fell from 0.41 to 0.12 over the same range. Thickness values were independently verified by profilometry, showing agreement within 4%. XRD confirmed amorphous structure for all deposition conditions. The data establish a consistent baseline for subsequent spectroscopic measurements and demonstrate that nitrogen incorporation systematically reduces the optical absorptance of the films. Deposition rate and film density inferred from optical data are reported as a function of sputtering conditions.

title: Effect of substrate temperature on the Raman-active bonding configurations of a-CNx films grown by magnetron sputtering
abstract: Amorphous carbon nitride films were deposited at substrate temperatures of 25, 150, 300, and 450 °C using a reactive RF magnetron sputtering system. Micro-Raman spectra excited at 514 nm were acquired and deconvolved into D and G bands using a four-Gaussian fitting procedure. As substrate temperature increased, the G-band position shifted from 1538 to 1567 cm⁻¹ and the integrated intensity ratio I(D)/I(G) rose from 0.71 to 1.14, indicating progressive graphitisation of the carbon network. XPS C 1s spectra showed a decreasing fraction of C–N and C≡N bonds above 300 °C. Spectroscopic ellipsometry measured at three angles (60°, 65°, 70°) revealed a correlated increase in the imaginary part of the dielectric function ε₂ at photon energies below 3 eV, consistent with increased π-state density. The results establish a clear correlation between sp² cluster growth and optical absorptance as a function of substrate temperature.

title: Anisotropic optical response of magnetron-sputtered a-CNx films on obliquely oriented substrates
abstract: Thin carbon nitride films deposited at substrate tilt angles of 0°, 20°, and 40° relative to the sputtering flux direction were examined for optical anisotropy using Mueller matrix spectroscopic ellipsometry. Measurements were performed at three azimuthal orientations (0°, 45°, 90°) and two angles of incidence (65°, 70°). The off-diagonal Mueller matrix elements m₁₃ and m₃₁ were non-zero for tilt angles above 20°, indicating in-plane uniaxial anisotropy. A biaxial dielectric model was fitted to the data, yielding a birefringence Δn = n_e − n_o of up to 0.09 at 2 eV photon energy for the 40° tilt case. Cross-sectional TEM imaging confirmed an oblique columnar microstructure consistent with the optical anisotropy. Deposition rate anisotropy was identified as the primary microstructural driver. The study provides guidance for applications requiring controlled optical anisotropy in carbon-based coatings.

title: Ageing effects on the optical constants of a-CNx films exposed to ambient conditions
abstract: Amorphous carbon nitride films stored under ambient laboratory conditions (22 ± 2 °C, 45–55% relative humidity) were re-examined by spectroscopic ellipsometry after intervals of 1, 3, 6, and 12 months following deposition. Films with nitrogen content of 0, 10, and 25 at.% (XPS-determined at deposition) were studied. The refractive index at 2 eV showed statistically significant drift only for the 25 at.% N series, decreasing by 0.03 ± 0.01 over 12 months. Contact angle measurements indicated a gradual increase in surface hydrophilicity for nitrogen-rich films, consistent with slow oxidation of surface C–N bonds confirmed by O 1s XPS after 12 months. The optical gap E_g, extracted from TL fits, increased by up to 0.08 eV for nitrogen-rich films over the same period. The study suggests that films with low to moderate nitrogen content are stable enough for long-term optical applications without encapsulation.

title: Spectroscopic ellipsometry as a non-destructive thickness monitor for multilayer a-CNx/SiNx antireflection stacks
abstract: Three-layer antireflection stacks consisting of alternating a-CNx and silicon nitride (SiNx) films were deposited by sequential reactive magnetron sputtering. Layer thicknesses were designed to minimise reflectance near 550 nm for silicon solar cell applications. Spectroscopic ellipsometry at 65° and 70° was used as the primary thickness characterisation tool, with a global regression strategy applied sequentially layer by layer after each deposition step. Measured thickness values agreed with target values within ±2 nm for layers between 30 and 120 nm. Reflectance spectra calculated from ellipsometry-derived optical constants matched direct spectrophotometer measurements to within 0.5% absolute reflectance over 400–1000 nm. XRR confirmed the density and interface roughness assumed in the optical model. The study demonstrates that spectroscopic ellipsometry, combined with a sequential fitting protocol, is adequate for process control of multilayer carbon-based antireflection coatings without additional cross-sectional TEM verification.

title: Ellipsometric characterisation of a-CNx films on flexible polymer substrates: correction for substrate compliance
abstract: Amorphous carbon nitride films 50–200 nm thick were deposited on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) foils and characterised by spectroscopic ellipsometry. PET substrates introduce optical complexity due to birefringence, surface roughness (Ra ≈ 3 nm), and thickness non-uniformity. A correction procedure was developed in which the PET substrate Mueller matrix was measured independently and incorporated into the optical model as a fixed backplane. Systematic errors in refractive index arising from substrate birefringence reached up to Δn = 0.05 when using a standard isotropic substrate model; the correction reduced this to below 0.01. Film optical constants extracted on PET agreed within 2% with values measured on reference Si substrates for identically sputtered films. The approach is relevant to roll-to-roll coating processes where silicon reference substrates are impractical. Mechanical flexibility did not alter optical constants at tensile strains below 1%.

title: Optical bandgap engineering in a-CNx films through co-sputtering with boron targets
abstract: Amorphous carbon boron nitride (a-CBxNy) films were prepared by simultaneously sputtering a graphite target and a boron target in an Ar/N₂ atmosphere. Boron content was varied from 0 to 18 at.% by adjusting the relative power of the boron target between 0 and 80 W while holding total pressure at 0.5 Pa. Spectroscopic ellipsometry over 250–1700 nm was fitted with a combined Tauc–Lorentz plus Drude model. The optical gap increased from 1.58 eV (B-free) to 2.34 eV at 18 at.% B, while the refractive index at 2 eV decreased from 2.01 to 1.73. XPS and FTIR confirmed the incorporation of B–N and B–C bonds. Hardness measured by nanoindentation increased from 14 to 22 GPa with boron addition, with no corresponding degradation of optical transparency. The dataset provides a map of achievable optical and mechanical properties as a function of boron content.

title: Spectroscopic ellipsometry in the mid-infrared: extending the optical constant dataset for a-CNx films to 25 µm
abstract: Spectroscopic ellipsometry measurements of a-CNx films were extended into the mid-infrared range (400–4000 cm⁻¹, corresponding to 2.5–25 µm) using a Fourier-transform infrared ellipsometer. Films 200–800 nm thick deposited on double-side polished silicon were investigated. A multi-oscillator model combining five Lorentz oscillators was fitted to match ellipsometric angles Ψ and Δ across the full infrared spectral range. Strong absorption features at 1580, 2190, and 3380 cm⁻¹ were assigned to C=N stretching, C≡N stretching, and N–H stretching modes, respectively, by comparison with FTIR transmission spectra. The imaginary part of the refractive index showed a maximum k of 0.31 at the C=N absorption peak. Combining the mid-IR data with visible-range data allowed a Kramers–Kronig-consistent optical model spanning 0.05–5 eV to be constructed. The full dataset is provided as supplementary material for use in optical simulation tools.

title: Machine-learning-assisted inversion of spectroscopic ellipsometry data for a-CNx films: accuracy and generalisability
abstract: A feedforward neural network was trained on a library of 48 000 synthetic ellipsometric spectra generated from randomised Tauc–Lorentz parameter sets for a-CNx films on Si, covering thickness from 20 to 500 nm and optical gap from 0.3 to 2.5 eV. The network was trained using 80% of the library and validated on the remaining 20%. Mean absolute errors on the test set were 2.1 nm for thickness and 0.03 for n at 2 eV. The trained network was then applied to 35 experimental spectra measured on films with independently known thicknesses (profilometry). Agreement was within 4 nm for films thicker than 50 nm. Generalisation to a different sputtering system at a partner laboratory degraded accuracy by a factor of approximately 1.8 but remained within practical limits after fine-tuning on 10 experimental spectra from the new system. The study examines the practical conditions under which neural network inversion can supplement or replace conventional regression for routine optical characterisation.

title: Prirodna radioaktivnost građevinskih materijala na teritoriji Vojvodine: cigla, malter i beton
abstract: Ispitana je prirodna radioaktivnost 28 vrsta građevinskih materijala (cigle pune i šuplje, malteri na bazi krečnjaka i cementa, kao i različiti betoni) koji se koriste u stambenoj gradnji na teritoriji Vojvodine. Aktivnosti Ra-226 kretale su se od 18 do 74 Bq/kg, Th-232 od 14 do 61 Bq/kg, a K-40 od 130 do 720 Bq/kg. Indeks radioaktivnosti I izračunat prema evropskoj metodologiji (Direktiva 2013/59/Euratom) bio je ispod granične vrednosti 1,0 za sve uzorke. Najniže vrednosti indeksa zabeležene su kod betonskih blokova od rečnog šljunka (I = 0,28), a najviše kod cigle sa primesama fosfogipsa (I = 0,87). Rezultati su prodiskutovani u kontekstu doprinosa unutrašnjoj dozi izloženosti za tipične stambene objekte u ravničarskom delu Srbije.

title: Hydraulic gradients and exchange fluxes at a bank filtration site on the Middle Danube near Novi Sad
abstract: Bank filtration (BF) sites along the Middle Danube supply roughly 40 % of the drinking water used by Novi Sad municipality. This study characterised hydraulic gradients and vertical exchange fluxes at an operational BF site over a 24-month period using a network of 18 multi-level piezometers installed at three transects perpendicular to the riverbank. Stage and groundwater-head data collected at 15-minute intervals were combined with streambed vertical hydraulic conductivity estimates obtained from falling-head slug tests. Seepage fluxes ranged from 0.3 to 2.1 m/d depending on river stage and antecedent soil moisture. Riverbank clogging was quantified by comparing hydraulic conductivity measured in November 2008 and June 2009, revealing a 35 % reduction in the upper 0.5 m of the streambed during the low-flow period attributed to fine sediment deposition. Results provide a calibration dataset for subsequent numerical modelling and highlight the sensitivity of BF efficiency to seasonal stage fluctuations.

title: Estimating groundwater recharge in the Bačka loess plateau under maize-dominated land use using chloride mass balance and water-table fluctuation methods
abstract: Two independent methods were applied to estimate annual groundwater recharge in a 420 km² agricultural catchment in the Bačka region of Vojvodina, where continuous maize cultivation covers approximately 68 % of the surface area. The chloride mass balance (CMB) method used monthly precipitation and unsaturated-zone pore water samples collected from 12 sites over two hydrological years (2009–2011). The water-table fluctuation (WTF) method relied on 23 existing monitoring wells of the Provincial Hydrogeological Network. CMB estimates ranged from 18 to 54 mm/yr, with a mean of 31 mm/yr. WTF-derived values were systematically 15–25 % higher, a discrepancy attributed to lateral inflow from irrigation canals. Specific yield was estimated at 0.12 ± 0.03 using laboratory permeameter tests on 48 core samples. Recharge was strongly correlated with autumn precipitation totals (r² = 0.71) and inversely correlated with summer evapotranspiration computed by the Penman–Monteith equation.

title: Numerical simulation of bank filtrate travel times in a heterogeneous gravel-sand aquifer using MODFLOW-2005 with the MT3DMS transport package
abstract: A steady-state and transient groundwater flow model was constructed for a 3.2 km reach of the Tisa River near Titel, Vojvodina, to simulate bank filtrate travel times under varying pumping and river-stage conditions. Aquifer stratigraphy was characterised using 34 borehole logs and 6 electrical resistivity tomography profiles, identifying three distinct hydrofacies with hydraulic conductivities of 1.2 × 10⁻³, 4.7 × 10⁻⁴, and 8.1 × 10⁻⁵ m/s. The model was calibrated against 14 months of observed heads (RMSE = 0.18 m) and validated against a river-stage recession event. MT3DMS particle tracking indicated median travel times of 18–42 days at the production well field, consistent with environmental tracer data (δ¹⁸O, tritium) collected from six monitoring wells. Sensitivity analysis showed travel time to be most sensitive to hydraulic conductivity in the high-permeability facies and to the abstraction rate at the well field.

title: Impact of forest-to-cropland conversion on shallow groundwater recharge in the Fruška Gora piedmont zone
abstract: Land-use change from mixed deciduous forest to arable land in the Fruška Gora piedmont affects unsaturated-zone water balance and ultimately recharge to shallow quaternary aquifers. Paired catchment monitoring was established at two 1.2–1.8 km² subcatchments with contrasting land cover. Soil moisture was logged continuously at three depths (0.3, 0.6, 1.0 m) using capacitance probes; actual evapotranspiration was estimated from eddy covariance measurements over the 2015–2018 period. Annual recharge under cropland was 78 ± 12 mm compared with 41 ± 9 mm under forest, reflecting lower interception and root-zone uptake. However, the elevated recharge under cropland was associated with increased nitrate concentrations in shallow wells (mean 38 mg/L NO₃⁻ versus 7 mg/L), indicating a water quality trade-off. A simple transfer function model reproducing the observed recharge dynamics is presented for use in scenario analyses.
venue: Acta Agriculturae et Environmentalis

title: Hyporheic exchange in a channelised lowland river: field measurements and 2D hydrodynamic modelling along the Begej Canal, Vojvodina
abstract: Channelisation of natural rivers in Vojvodina has dramatically altered the hyporheic exchange capacity of riparian systems. This study quantified hyporheic exchange fluxes in a 4.8 km reach of the Begej Canal using vertical streambed temperature profiles measured at 12 locations with high-resolution thermistors deployed over three seasons. One-dimensional heat-transport inversion using the VFLUX toolbox yielded vertical flux estimates ranging from −0.8 to +1.4 cm/d, indicating alternating gaining and losing conditions linked to canal operating schedule. A 2D hydrodynamic model of the reach (MIKE 21 FM) was used to derive spatially distributed bed shear stress, which correlated positively with upwelling flux (r = 0.62). Streambed grain size was characterised at each measurement point using sieve analysis. Results suggest that current canal management practice suppresses hyporheic exchange by maintaining artificially uniform stage, with implications for self-purification capacity and ecological status under the Water Framework Directive.
venue: River Research and Environmental Engineering

title: Groundwater–surface water interaction in alluvial aquifers of the Pannonian Plain: a synthesis
abstract: This book chapter synthesises knowledge on groundwater–surface water (GW–SW) interactions specific to the Pannonian Plain, a large intramontane sedimentary basin with characteristic flat topography, thick Quaternary sediments, and dense agricultural land use. The chapter covers the geological and hydrogeological framework of Pannonian alluvial aquifers, reviews methods applicable in data-sparse lowland settings (slug tests, streambed temperature profiling, environmental tracers, water balance approaches), and discusses how irrigation, drainage, and river regulation have modified natural exchange fluxes over the past century. Case studies from Vojvodina (Serbia), the Tisza Plain (Hungary), and the Sava corridor (Croatia) are presented to illustrate common patterns and regional differences. Particular attention is given to the implications of altered GW–SW exchange for drinking water supply via bank filtration and for wetland and riparian habitat maintenance. The chapter concludes with a discussion of monitoring gaps and priorities for regional research cooperation.

title: Responses of a shallow phreatic aquifer to irrigation canal recharge: evidence from a dense piezometer network in the DTD canal system, Vojvodina
abstract: The Danube–Tisa–Danube (DTD) hydro-engineering system, one of the largest canal networks in Southeast Europe, acts as both a drainage and irrigation infrastructure across Vojvodina. This study tracked aquifer responses to canal recharge events at 31 piezometers installed along a 12 km transect perpendicular to the main DTD canal near Bečej during the 2018 and 2019 irrigation seasons. Water-table hydrographs were decomposed to separate canal-recharge signals from precipitation-driven responses using a cross-correlation approach. Canal recharge elevated groundwater levels by up to 0.9 m within 200 m of the canal within 48–72 hours of gate opening, with the response attenuating to below detection threshold at 1.4 km. Leakage coefficients averaged 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ m/s across the lined and unlined canal sections, with unlined sections showing 2.7-fold higher leakage. Implications for waterlogging risk and soil salinity management in adjacent agricultural fields are discussed.

title: Seasonal variability of bank filtrate quality at a municipal well field on the Danube: two years of high-frequency monitoring
abstract: Water quality at a well field supplying approximately 85,000 residents along the Middle Danube was monitored at biweekly intervals from January 2019 to December 2020. Samples were collected from 8 production wells and 4 riverbank monitoring points and analysed for turbidity, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), UV absorbance at 254 nm, temperature, specific conductance, and a suite of microbiological parameters. DOC concentrations in bank filtrate were 40–70 % lower than in river water, with attenuation efficiency declining during high-flow events when travel times fell below 12 days as inferred from temperature cross-correlation. Turbidity spikes in the river were entirely removed in all monitoring wells. Thermophilic bacteria counts in production wells increased measurably in late summer, correlating with river water temperature exceeding 24 °C. Results are discussed in the context of climate-driven increases in river temperature and implications for treatment requirements at the water works.

title: Projected changes in groundwater recharge across Vojvodina under CMIP6 climate scenarios using a coupled soil–water balance model
abstract: Future groundwater recharge in the Vojvodina plain was assessed for the 2041–2060 and 2071–2090 periods using a daily soil water balance model driven by statistically downscaled outputs from five CMIP6 general circulation models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. The model was calibrated and validated against observed water-table hydrographs at 17 monitoring stations operated by the Provincial Hydrogeological Network over 1990–2020. Baseline mean annual recharge across the study domain was estimated at 43 mm/yr (range 22–68 mm/yr) depending on soil texture and land use. Under SSP5-8.5, ensemble-median recharge declined by 28 % (range −12 to −41 %) by 2071–2090, driven primarily by increased summer potential evapotranspiration. Uncertainty in recharge projections was dominated by inter-model spread in summer precipitation rather than by the choice of soil hydraulic parameterisation. Spatial patterns show the most pronounced reductions in the sandy Deliblato area and in the Bačka loess plateau.

title: Using environmental tracers (δ¹⁸O, δ²H, ³H) to delineate recharge zones and groundwater age in the Titel loess plateau aquifer
abstract: The Titel loess plateau, a distinctive geomorphological unit at the confluence of the Danube and Tisa rivers, hosts a multilayer aquifer system used for local water supply. Stable water isotopes (δ¹⁸O, δ²H) and tritium were measured in 41 groundwater samples collected from wells spanning depths of 8–95 m in 2022. Isotopic compositions of shallow groundwater (δ¹⁸O: −9.2 to −8.4 ‰) were depleted relative to local meteoric water, suggesting a component of recharge from cold-season precipitation. Tritium activities ranged from <0.5 to 4.8 TU; wells with activities below detection limit were considered pre-bomb (pre-1952) water and constitute approximately 30 % of sampled sites. A two-component mixing model was applied to quantify the proportion of modern versus pre-modern water at each well. Results have direct implications for the vulnerability of the deeper aquifer to land-surface contamination and for sustainable abstraction planning.

title: Clogging dynamics at bank filtration intake structures: column experiments with Danube riverbed sediment
abstract: Biological and physical clogging reduces the hydraulic efficiency of bank filtration systems over time. Laboratory column experiments were conducted using intact sediment cores (n = 12, length 0.4 m, diameter 0.1 m) extracted from the Danube riverbed at an operational BF site to evaluate clogging development under controlled conditions. Columns were fed with Danube surface water at flow rates mimicking natural seepage (0.5–2.0 m/d). Hydraulic conductivity was measured every 48 hours for 60 days using constant-head permeameter tests. Total suspended solids, turbidity, and total cell counts were monitored in influent and effluent. Hydraulic conductivity declined by 55–82 % over the experiment duration, with steeper declines at higher flow rates. Microscopic examination and phospholipid fatty acid analysis indicated that biofilm growth contributed 40–60 % of total clogging in low-TSS treatments, while physical filtration of fine particles dominated at high-TSS influent. Protocols for maintenance backwashing intervals are proposed.

title: Aquifer thermal energy storage feasibility in alluvial sediments of the Pannonian Basin: site assessment and groundwater flow implications
abstract: Growing interest in shallow geothermal energy use in Vojvodina raises questions about the suitability of alluvial aquifers for aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) and about potential thermal plume interference with bank filtration operations. This study assessed a potential ATES site in a suburban area of Novi Sad using existing borehole data, pumping test results, and ambient groundwater temperature profiles. Groundwater flow velocity was estimated at 0.5–1.4 m/d from tracer tests, which is relatively high for ATES and implies rapid plume advection. Numerical simulations with FEFLOW coupled with a heat transport module projected thermal plume extents of 80–130 m after five years of cyclic operation at a 250 kW system. A minimum setback distance of 300 m from active BF production wells is recommended based on sensitivity analysis across a range of hydraulic conductivity values. Regulatory and monitoring framework requirements are outlined.
venue: Geothermal Energy and Groundwater

title: Suspended sediment rating curves and their seasonal variability at three gauging stations on the Bega River
abstract: Suspended sediment concentration was measured biweekly over three hydrological years (2011–2013) at Zrenjanin, Srpski Itebej, and Žitište gauging stations on the Bega canalised reach. Depth-integrated isokinetic sampling was combined with turbidity probe deployment to produce continuous surrogate records. Rating curve exponents derived from ordinary least squares regression ranged from 1.41 to 1.89 across stations, with systematic seasonal hysteresis: clockwise loops predominated in spring snowmelt events while counterclockwise patterns were observed during summer convective floods. Annual suspended load estimates at Zrenjanin averaged 24 300 tonnes per year, approximately 35 percent lower than values reported for the same station in the 1970s. The reduction is attributed to a combination of reduced discharge variability following channel deepening and increased riparian vegetation cover in the headwater zone. Uncertainty propagation analysis suggests 90th-percentile load errors of ±18 percent at the best-instrumented station.

title: Bank erosion rates and controlling factors at 12 sites on unregulated meander bends of the Zlatica stream, Banat
abstract: Repeated RTK-GPS surveys of eroding outer banks were conducted quarterly over 24 months (2023–2025) at 12 meander bends on the Zlatica stream in eastern Banat. Bank retreat distances varied from 0.08 to 1.6 m per year, with the highest rates associated with bends where toe scour exposed fine-sand layers overlain by silt–clay composites prone to cantilever failure. Bulk density, Atterberg limits, and undrained shear strength were measured for 58 bank samples stratified by lithological unit. Logistic regression identified three significant predictors of retreat rate exceeding 0.5 m per year: low plasticity index, bank height above 2.2 m, and curvature radius-to-width ratio below 3.5. Riparian tree root reinforcement was quantified at six sites using the perpendicular root density method, and root-reinforced banks exhibited retreat rates 40–55 percent lower than comparable non-vegetated banks. Results are intended to support prioritisation of bank protection works within the provincial drainage maintenance programme.
venue: Geomorphological Processes and Landforms in European Lowlands

title: Seasonal variation in nutrient load from subsurface tile drains under conventional cereal production in the southern Pannonian Plain
abstract: Tile drain outflow chemistry was monitored over two complete hydrological years (2013–2015) at four 5–12 ha cereal production fields in Bačka and Banat districts. Automatic samplers and continuous flow sensors recorded drainage volumes and captured time-proportional samples during all significant drainage events. Nitrate-N export ranged from 12 to 47 kg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ across sites, with peak concentrations of 28–41 mg NO₃-N L⁻¹ occurring in late autumn and early spring following fertiliser application events. Dissolved reactive phosphorus export was lower (0.08–0.31 kg P ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹) but showed strong event-driven pulses coinciding with heavy rainfall on recently fertilised soils. Inter-site variability was explained in part by soil texture and drain depth. The dataset provides empirical loading estimates for sizing constructed wetland treatment systems at farm scale in the region, where such field-specific data had previously been scarce.

title: Institutional Disintegration and Recomposition of Irrigation Cooperatives in Vojvodina, 1989–1995
abstract: This paper examines the structural breakdown of socialist irrigation collectives in the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia following the political transitions of 1989–1991, and the early attempts at recomposing water management authority under nascent water-user associations (WUAs). Drawing on archival records from twelve canal districts and semi-structured interviews with forty-three former cooperative officials and successor association managers conducted in 1995–1996, the study documents the redistribution of infrastructure responsibilities, fee collection failures, and the rapid decline of canal maintenance. Ostrom's institutional design principles are applied as an evaluative framework. Findings indicate that only three of the twelve studied districts achieved minimally functional self-governance within the first five post-transition years, largely due to retained social networks from the previous cooperative era. The paper concludes that informal trust capital from the socialist period was a stronger predictor of early WUA viability than formal legal provisions introduced after 1992.

title: Water-Allocation Equity Among Smallholders and Agro-Industrial Estates in the DTD Canal Network: A Gini-Based Assessment
abstract: The DTD (Danube–Tisa–Danube) hydro-engineering system in Vojvodina serves a heterogeneous landscape of subsistence smallholders and large agro-industrial estates. This study develops a field-applicable water-allocation equity index adapted from the Gini coefficient, using volumetric delivery records from four lateral canal branches over the irrigation seasons of 1998 and 1999, supplemented by on-site interviews with 61 water users stratified by farm size. Results show a Gini coefficient for water delivery ranging from 0.38 to 0.52 across branches, indicating moderate to high inequality, systematically favoring farms above 50 ha. Multivariate regression identifies proximity to pumping stations, membership in formal WUA committees, and historical cadastral classification as the three strongest predictors of favorable allocation outcomes. The study provides a replicable measurement protocol for monitoring equity obligations embedded in Serbian water law, and recommends revising fee structures to reduce infrastructure-proximity advantages.

title: Visual Differential Assertions for Cross-Platform GUI Regression Detection
abstract: Screenshot-based regression detection is common in web testing but has received less attention for native desktop applications, where rendering differences across operating systems complicate pixel-level comparison. This paper proposes a visual assertion framework that decomposes screenshots into widget-level regions using a trained convolutional classifier, then applies per-region perceptual hashing rather than direct pixel comparison. The classifier was trained on 12,000 annotated widget screenshots from DesktopBench-40 and achieved 91.4% widget-boundary precision on a held-out test set. The framework was evaluated on 22 application pairs (Windows vs. Linux builds of the same release) and detected 94 genuine rendering regressions while producing 11 false positives, compared to 38 false positives from a baseline pixel-diff tool at matched sensitivity. Runtime overhead per test run averaged 3.1 seconds. The approach tolerates font-rendering and anti-aliasing differences that are cosmetically acceptable but flags layout shifts and color-scheme deviations reliably.

title: Automated Accessibility Compliance Checking for Desktop Applications: Mapping EN 301 549 Requirements to Testable Assertions
abstract: EN 301 549 mandates accessibility requirements for ICT products procured by European public bodies, yet automated verification tooling for desktop software lags far behind the web domain. This paper presents an analysis of 112 EN 301 549 criteria applicable to desktop applications, classifying each as fully automatable, partially automatable, or requiring human judgment. For the 43 criteria classified as fully automatable, the paper defines a corresponding set of programmatic assertions expressed against the Microsoft UI Automation and AT-SPI2 accessibility trees. A prototype checker implementing these assertions was applied to 15 applications from DesktopBench-40. On average, 31 of the 43 assertions could be evaluated per application (depending on which widget types were present), and violations were found in all 15 applications, ranging from 4 to 29 distinct issues per product. The paper discusses common violation patterns, including missing name properties on icon-only buttons and incorrect focus-order sequences.

title: Combining Model Inference and Visual Assertions in a Unified Desktop Test Generation Pipeline
abstract: This chapter surveys the integration of state-machine inference with screenshot-based visual assertions as a unified pipeline for regression test generation targeting cross-platform desktop applications. The chapter covers four stages: automated model extraction via event exploration, abstraction of inferred models to reduce test-suite size, test-case instantiation with embedded visual checkpoints, and oracle evaluation using the visual differential assertion framework. Practical considerations including handling of non-deterministic transitions, OS-specific widget rendering, and test maintenance under version churn are discussed. A worked example using a file-manager application across three successive releases on Windows 10 and Ubuntu 20.04 illustrates the pipeline end-to-end. The chapter also reviews relevant tools, pointing to open research questions around scalability to applications with large widget hierarchies and the handling of animated or data-driven UI states.

title: Screen-Reader Compatibility Testing of Desktop Applications Using Scripted AT-SPI2 Interaction Traces
abstract: Screen-reader users interact with desktop applications through accessibility APIs rather than direct graphical input, but most automated test suites exercise only the graphical pathway. This paper introduces a testing approach that replays synthetic AT-SPI2 interaction traces—sequences of keyboard events and accessibility-tree queries—against running application instances, comparing the resulting spoken output (captured via a headless speech-synthesis engine) to a reference transcript. Traces were constructed for 12 task scenarios covering common operations such as file opening, form completion, and menu navigation. The method was applied to eight desktop applications on Linux, identifying 17 screen-reader regressions across two successive releases that standard GUI regression tests missed entirely. Inter-release trace stability was measured: 71% of traces required no modification between minor releases, while major feature additions necessitated partial trace repair. The paper reports average trace construction time of 45 minutes per task scenario.

title: Measuring the Stability of Inferred GUI Models Across Application Releases: A Longitudinal Study
abstract: Automated GUI models inferred from one application release may degrade in quality as the application evolves, undermining the value of model-based test suites. This study tracks FSM model quality across 24 consecutive releases of five long-lived open-source desktop applications over periods ranging from 18 to 36 months. Model stability metrics—state retention, transition retention, and new-state discovery rate—are computed at each release boundary. Results show that median state retention across minor releases is 87%, dropping to 61% at major releases. Transition retention follows a similar pattern at 84% and 55% respectively. Applications that adopted a component-based architecture showed 12 percentage points higher stability than monolithic codebases at major boundaries. The data suggest that incremental re-inference at each release, combined with a differential model-merging step, is more cost-effective than full re-inference for minor releases. Practical guidance for scheduling re-inference in CI pipelines is provided.

title: Widget Recognition in High-DPI and Mixed-Scaling Environments Using Lightweight Convolutional Models
abstract: Visual GUI testing tools that rely on widget recognition face increasing difficulty as applications are deployed across displays with varying DPI settings and OS-level scaling factors. This paper studies the degradation of a widget classifier trained on standard-DPI screenshots when evaluated on images captured at 150%, 175%, and 200% scaling, finding accuracy drops of up to 19 percentage points on minority widget classes such as sliders and spin boxes. Three mitigation strategies are evaluated: training-time augmentation with synthetic scaling, test-time multi-scale aggregation, and a lightweight EfficientNet-B0 model fine-tuned on a 3,200-image high-DPI dataset collected specifically for this work. The fine-tuned model recovers accuracy to within 3 percentage points of the baseline at all tested scaling factors while adding only 14 ms inference overhead per screenshot on a mid-range GPU. The high-DPI dataset is released alongside the paper.

title: An Empirical Comparison of Accessibility-Tree and Visual Methods for Detecting Focus-Order Violations in Desktop GUIs
abstract: Keyboard focus-order violations—where the tab sequence does not follow a logical reading order—are among the most frequently reported accessibility defects in desktop applications, yet detection methods vary widely. This paper compares three approaches: static analysis of the accessibility-tree focus-chain, dynamic replay of tab-key sequences with focus logging, and a visual heuristic that infers expected order from widget bounding-box geometry. The evaluation uses a set of 28 applications containing 94 manually verified focus-order violations sourced from public accessibility audit reports. The dynamic replay method achieved the highest precision (89%) and recall (82%), while the visual geometric heuristic performed comparably on single-window forms (precision 85%, recall 79%) but degraded substantially on applications with multi-pane layouts. Combining dynamic replay with geometric cross-validation raised recall to 91% with a modest precision cost. The paper provides a detailed error analysis and discusses conditions under which each method is preferable.

title: Towards Automated WCAG 2.2 Compliance Reporting for Electron and Qt Desktop Applications
abstract: Desktop applications built with Electron and Qt occupy an ambiguous position in accessibility standards: they are not web pages yet some WCAG 2.2 success criteria have plausible analogues in their rendering and input models. This preprint presents a mapping study and a prototype tool, DesktopAudit, that applies 29 mapped WCAG 2.2 criteria to Electron apps via Chromium DevTools Protocol and to Qt apps via the Qt Accessibility Bridge. The tool was tested on 10 Electron and 8 Qt applications, generating compliance reports in a format aligned with the Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) template. On Electron targets, 26 of 29 criteria were evaluable; on Qt targets, 21 were evaluable. Preliminary results indicate that Electron apps violate colour-contrast and focus-visible criteria most frequently, while Qt apps show higher rates of missing accessible-name violations. The mapping methodology and tool configuration are documented to support replication.

title: Geofence-Aware Replanning for Multi-UAV Swarms Using Distributed Constraint Optimisation
abstract: This paper addresses in-flight replanning when a geofence boundary is updated dynamically—as occurs when temporary restricted areas are activated by air traffic control. Each UAV agent maintains a local constraint optimisation problem (DCOP) representing its remaining coverage assignments; boundary updates are broadcast as hard constraint changes, and agents apply asynchronous backtracking with forward checking to revise their plans without centralised coordination. The approach is tested in a ROS/Gazebo simulation environment with 3 and 5 UAV configurations over a 4 km² area subject to up to three mid-mission geofence changes. Average replanning latency is 2.1 seconds for 3 UAVs and 4.8 seconds for 5 UAVs. Coverage completeness remains above 96% in all scenarios, with a mean increase in total flight distance of 8.7% relative to missions without boundary changes. The paper also includes a brief hardware demonstration using two indoor quadrotors.
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Autonomous Robotic Systems and Competitions

title: ISO 26262 Part 5 Compliance Checklist for ASIL-D Power Management ICs: A Case Analysis
abstract: Power management integrated circuits in ASIL-D electronic control units carry stringent diagnostic requirements that are often difficult to satisfy with commercially available off-the-shelf components. This paper presents a systematic compliance checklist derived from ISO 26262-5:2011 hardware design requirements and applies it to four representative automotive-grade power management IC families. The checklist covers 38 hardware safety requirements, including voltage monitoring, current limiting, thermal shutdown, and communication interface integrity. For each IC family, gaps between datasheet-documented diagnostics and standard requirements are identified and mitigation strategies are proposed, ranging from external voltage supervisor additions to software-based periodic checks. The analysis finds that two of the four devices cannot achieve ASIL-D classification without external safety mechanisms contributing at least DC = 90 % for the voltage monitoring function. The paper provides a reusable checklist template formatted for use within a standard FMEA worksheet.

title: Skill-Based Robot Programming: Methods, Representations, and Deployment Tools
abstract: This book chapter surveys the state of skill-based approaches to robot programming, covering three main representation styles: procedural skill trees, ontology-based capability models, and learning-from-demonstration encodings. For each style the chapter reviews published implementations, discusses deployment tool support, and compares the programmer effort required for initial authoring versus reuse. A structured comparison table covers 31 selected systems published between 2005 and 2021. The chapter then describes in detail the authors' own ontology-driven tool chain, walking through the workflow from skill library construction to executable program generation for a KUKA KRC4 controller. Two worked examples illustrate the workflow: a palletising task and a camera-guided bin-picking task. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open challenges including handling of run-time exceptions, scalability of the ontology to large libraries, and integration with digital twin environments. It is intended as a reference for graduate students and practicing engineers entering the field.
