title: A Retiming-Aware Operator Binding Algorithm for HLS with Heterogeneous DSP Blocks
abstract: Modern FPGA families include DSP blocks with configurable pre-adder and post-accumulator pipelines that can absorb retiming registers, reducing the LUT cost of retimed datapaths. Existing HLS tools treat DSP blocks as fixed-latency operators and do not exploit this flexibility during binding. This paper presents a binding algorithm that models DSP pre-adder and accumulator optionality, integrates retiming feasibility checks derived from the bound schedule, and selects binding assignments that maximise internal DSP pipeline use. The algorithm is implemented as a post-synthesis pass processing netlists exported from Vitis HLS 2024.1 in Verilog form. Evaluated on twelve arithmetic-heavy signal processing kernels targeting a Versal AI Core VC1902, the pass reduces registered LUT count by 9–22% with no change in clock period. Compile-time overhead is under 8 seconds per kernel.

title: Greenhouse Gas Emission Factors for Heavy-Duty Road Freight in Serbia: A Bottom-Up Estimation Using Fleet Survey Data
abstract: This study derived vehicle-specific CO2, CH4, and N2O emission factors for the Serbian heavy-duty road freight fleet using a bottom-up methodology. Data were collected through a structured survey of 214 transport operators covering fuel consumption logs, vehicle age distribution, and annual mileage. Emission factors were calculated per tonne-kilometre following the GHG Protocol Scope 1 guidelines. Results indicated a fleet-average CO2 factor of 112 g CO2e/tkm, approximately 18% higher than the EU-28 average reported by Eurostat for the same reference year, largely attributed to the older average vehicle age (13.4 years) in the Serbian fleet. Sensitivity analysis showed that vehicle load factor had the strongest influence on final emission intensity. The derived factors were compared against IPCC Tier 2 defaults and the COPERT IV model outputs, revealing systematic underestimation by the default values for this regional context. The dataset is intended to support LCA practitioners and national greenhouse gas inventory compilers working with Serbian transport data.

title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of Pallet Distribution Networks: Rail vs. Road in the Western Balkans
abstract: A comparative cradle-to-gate LCA was carried out for two pallet distribution scenarios covering a 450 km corridor in the Western Balkans region: a road-only scenario using Euro III trucks and a combined rail–road scenario using standard freight wagons for the trunk leg. The functional unit was defined as the delivery of one standard EUR-pallet over the full corridor distance. Primary energy demand, global warming potential (GWP100), and acidification potential were assessed using the CML 2002 impact assessment method implemented in SimaPro 7.3. GWP100 for the rail–road scenario was 3.1 kg CO2e per pallet compared with 5.8 kg CO2e for the road-only scenario, a reduction of 47%. Acidification potential, however, was only marginally lower for rail due to the regional electricity grid mix dominated by lignite-fired generation. Results highlight the importance of using region-specific electricity emission factors rather than European averages when assessing rail freight in the Balkans.

title: Accounting for Refrigeration Energy in Cold Chain Logistics: A Carbon Footprint Case Study for a Dairy Distributor in Vojvodina
abstract: Cold chain transport introduces auxiliary fuel or electricity consumption from refrigeration units that is often omitted in standard freight carbon footprint calculations. This paper presents a carbon footprint study for a regional dairy product distributor operating across Vojvodina, combining Scope 1 emissions from traction fuel and refrigeration diesel with Scope 3 upstream emissions from fuel extraction and refining. Data were collected over a full calendar year from on-board telematics and fuel purchase records covering 28 refrigerated vans. The refrigeration unit was found to account for 19.3% of total tailpipe CO2e emissions on average, rising to 31% during summer months. The carbon intensity of delivered product reached 0.31 kg CO2e per kg of dairy product. Scenario modelling showed that replacing auxiliary diesel refrigeration with electric standby units powered from the national grid would reduce total carbon intensity by 11%, contingent on grid mix assumptions. The study was conducted following the GHG Protocol Product Standard and ISO 14044.

title: Sensitivity of Freight LCA Results to Background Database Choice: A Benchmarking Exercise Using Ecoinvent and ELCD
abstract: Life cycle assessment of transport activities requires background inventory data for fuels, vehicles, and infrastructure. This study systematically compared results obtained using two widely used background databases — ecoinvent 3.1 and the European Life Cycle Database (ELCD) — for seven freight transport scenarios spanning road, rail, and inland waterway modes. For each scenario, GWP100, cumulative energy demand, and particulate matter formation potential were calculated in openLCA. Differences in GWP100 attributable to database choice ranged from 4% to 22% depending on transport mode and distance, with the largest discrepancy observed for diesel production chains. Inland waterway transport showed the highest sensitivity because barge fuel supply chains are represented with different system boundaries in the two databases. The paper provides a quantified decision framework to help practitioners select background databases consistently and understand the uncertainty introduced by this choice. Recommendations are made for freight LCA studies in the Central and Eastern European context where local supply chain data are scarce.

title: Life Cycle Assessment of Urban Last-Mile Delivery: Diesel Van, Electric Van, and Cargo Bicycle Compared for a Mid-Sized Serbian City
abstract: Three last-mile delivery configurations were compared using LCA for a parcel delivery service operating in a mid-sized Serbian city with approximately 280,000 inhabitants. The configurations studied were: Euro V diesel vans, battery electric vans charged from the Serbian national grid, and electrically assisted cargo bicycles serving a consolidated micro-depot. The functional unit was defined as delivery of 100 parcels within the city boundary in a single working day. Inventory data were gathered from operator records and supplemented with vehicle manufacturer datasheets. Using ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H), the electric van scenario showed a 29% reduction in climate change impact relative to the diesel baseline, while the cargo bicycle scenario achieved a 68% reduction. However, the electric van scenario showed higher freshwater ecotoxicity due to battery manufacturing. Human health impacts from particulate matter were substantially lower for both electric options. The study demonstrates that grid carbon intensity strongly moderates the climate benefit of electric vehicles in Serbia's current energy context.

title: Carbon Footprint of Inland Waterway Freight on the Danube Corridor: Scope 1 and Scope 3 Contributions
abstract: Inland waterway transport on the Danube is often cited as a low-emission alternative to road freight, but comprehensive GHG accounting covering both direct and upstream emissions is rarely performed for actual operating vessels. This study presents GHG Protocol-compliant Scope 1 and Scope 3 carbon footprint calculations for four push-barge convoys operating regularly between Novi Sad and the Port of Constanța. Fuel consumption data were obtained from vessel logbooks over two complete navigation seasons. The average Scope 1 emission intensity was 17.4 g CO2e/tkm, and Scope 3 upstream fuel emissions added a further 3.1 g CO2e/tkm. Cargo utilisation rates, which averaged 72% of rated capacity, had the single largest influence on emission intensity. A partial comparison with equivalent road transport showed a 4.2-fold higher emission intensity per tkm for road, though this ratio narrows when low-capacity barge runs are considered. The study also identifies gaps in internationally available emission factor datasets for Danube push-barge propulsion engines.

title: Incorporating Infrastructure Life Cycle Burdens into Road Freight Carbon Footprint Accounting: Magnitude and Practical Implications
abstract: Standard corporate carbon footprint frameworks such as the GHG Protocol typically exclude infrastructure construction and maintenance emissions. This paper quantifies the magnitude of road infrastructure life cycle burdens — covering pavement construction, maintenance, and end-of-life — allocated to freight vehicles using a physical allocation approach based on equivalent single axle loads. LCA inventory data for Serbian national roads were compiled from public procurement records and supplemented with literature data for material production. Allocated infrastructure GWP100 for a fully laden 40-tonne articulated truck was found to be 2.1 g CO2e/tkm, representing approximately 1.9% of total traction-related emissions. While this share is small for standard hauls, it becomes more significant for construction logistics where roads carry repeated overloaded vehicles. The paper discusses whether and when practitioners should include infrastructure burdens and proposes a tiered inclusion criterion based on vehicle type and road segment usage intensity.

title: GHG Accounting for Agricultural Supply Chains in Vojvodina: A Case Study from Sunflower Seed to Refined Oil
abstract: This paper applies GHG Protocol value chain accounting to a sunflower oil supply chain in Vojvodina, tracing emissions from field cultivation through oil extraction to outbound distribution. Logistics activities — including in-field harvesting machinery, short-haul truck transport from farms to crushing mill, and long-haul delivery of refined oil — contributed 12% of the total supply chain GWP100, with the crushing mill's energy consumption accounting for a further 34%. Transport emission factors derived from regional fleet data collected in earlier work by the authors were used in preference to default database values. A hotspot analysis identified fertiliser production as the dominant contributor at 41% of total GWP100. The study was conducted under ISO 14044 and the GHG Protocol Product Standard, and an uncertainty analysis using Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 runs) showed that the 95th percentile of total supply chain GWP100 was 31% above the mean, driven primarily by variability in fertiliser application rates. The findings are intended to guide emission reduction prioritisation for agri-food companies in the region.

title: Scope 3 Category 4 Emissions in Manufacturing SMEs: A Methodology Assessment and Application to Three Case Companies in Serbia
abstract: Scope 3 Category 4 (upstream transportation and distribution) is frequently reported as material by manufacturing companies yet remains poorly quantified in small and medium-sized enterprises due to limited data access. This paper evaluates three calculation methods — spend-based, distance-based, and fuel-based — as specified in the GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, applying each to empirical data from three Serbian manufacturing SMEs with annual revenues between €4M and €18M. Results showed that the spend-based method systematically underestimated emissions by 23–41% compared with the fuel-based method, which was taken as the reference. The paper identifies the primary data requirements for the fuel-based method and assesses the practical feasibility of data collection in SME contexts. A simplified data collection template developed during the project is described and its application illustrated. The paper concludes with a recommended default method selection framework for practitioners working with Serbian and regional Balkan SMEs where carrier cooperation on data sharing is limited.

title: Life Cycle Assessment of Wooden Pallet versus Plastic Pallet in a Fast-Moving Consumer Goods Supply Chain: A Cradle-to-Grave Study
abstract: Pallets are an ubiquitous yet rarely assessed packaging element in supply chain LCA. This cradle-to-grave study compared a standard EUR wooden pallet and a high-density polyethylene (HDPE) plastic pallet over a declared lifespan of 10 and 25 trips respectively, for a fast-moving consumer goods distributor operating in Serbia and Hungary. Seven impact categories from ReCiPe 2016 were assessed, with GWP100 as the primary indicator. The wooden pallet showed a GWP100 of 3.4 kg CO2e per functional trip versus 2.1 kg CO2e for the plastic pallet when full lifespans were realised. However, sensitivity analysis on realised trip numbers showed that if wooden pallet service life drops below 7 trips due to damage — a common outcome in the observed supply chain — the wooden pallet becomes less favourable on climate impact. End-of-life assumptions, particularly landfill versus incineration with energy recovery for HDPE, strongly influenced fossil resource depletion results. The study was carried out in openLCA 1.10 using the ecoinvent 3.7 database.

title: Carbon Footprint Verification Readiness of Serbian Logistics Companies: Survey Results and Gap Analysis
abstract: As the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and corporate sustainability reporting requirements extend their reach, logistics companies in candidate countries such as Serbia face growing pressure to provide verified carbon footprint data to customers. This paper reports results from a structured questionnaire survey of 87 logistics and freight forwarding companies registered in Serbia, assessing their current GHG data collection practices, familiarity with GHG Protocol and ISO 14064, use of telematics systems, and perceived barriers to third-party verification. Only 14% of respondents reported systematic fuel-based emission tracking, and fewer than 5% had undergone any form of external GHG assurance. Barriers most frequently cited were lack of internal expertise, cost of verification, and absence of customer demand. The paper cross-tabulates findings by company size, fleet type, and international versus domestic operation scope. A readiness maturity model with four levels is proposed to help companies and support organisations prioritise capacity-building efforts. Policy implications for the Serbian Ministry of Environmental Protection and industry associations are discussed.

title: Dynamic LCA for Logistics Decarbonisation Pathways in a Regional Distribution Network: Modelling Grid Decarbonisation Effects to 2035
abstract: Static LCA results for electric freight vehicles in carbon-intensive grids may misrepresent long-term climate performance if the electricity mix evolves substantially over the vehicle lifetime. This paper applies a dynamic LCA approach to a regional distribution network in Serbia, modelling three grid decarbonisation trajectories to 2035 based on published national energy strategy scenarios. Five fleet electrification pathways — ranging from business-as-usual diesel to full electric fleet replacement by 2030 — are evaluated for GWP100 calculated with time-differentiated characterisation factors following Levasseur et al. 2010. Under the medium decarbonisation scenario, full fleet electrification completed by 2030 yields a cumulative 2025–2035 GHG reduction of 38% relative to the diesel baseline; under the low decarbonisation scenario this falls to 17%. The paper demonstrates that the timing of vehicle replacement and grid cleaning have comparable influence on cumulative climate impact, and argues that fleet operators should align vehicle procurement schedules with grid improvement milestones. Limitations related to battery production temporal allocation are discussed.

title: Estimating Fugitive Refrigerant Emissions from Transport Refrigeration Units in the Serbian Cold Chain: A GHG Protocol Scope 1 Methodology
abstract: Hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) refrigerant leakage from transport refrigeration units (TRUs) represents a Scope 1 GHG emission source with high global warming potential that is systematically underreported in corporate inventories. This paper develops a practical estimation methodology for TRU refrigerant emissions applicable to Serbian cold chain operators, drawing on GHG Protocol Tier 2 simplified mass-balance and sales-data methods. Data were collected from five refrigerated transport companies covering 312 TRU units over three years, including refrigerant purchase invoices and service records. Annual leakage rates averaged 22% of TRU charge mass, consistent with rates reported in Western European studies but higher than values assumed in Serbian national inventory submissions. When valued at GWP100 of the dominant refrigerant (R-404A: 3,922 CO2e), refrigerant losses contributed between 8% and 15% of total fleet GHG footprint. The paper provides simplified calculation worksheets and discusses implications for mandatory emissions reporting under forthcoming Serbian environmental legislation.

title: LCA Data Quality Assessment for Freight Transport Studies in Emerging Economies: A Structured Review and Scoring Framework
abstract: Data quality in LCA is a well-established concern, but existing data quality assessment frameworks were largely developed in the context of Western European inventory datasets. This paper examines whether widely used data quality indicators — including temporal, geographical, technological, and completeness dimensions — adequately capture the specific data quality challenges encountered in freight transport LCA studies conducted in emerging and transition economies. A structured review of 43 freight transport LCA studies published between 2010 and 2024 from countries outside the EU-15 was conducted, and each study was scored using three established frameworks: the ecoinvent data quality system, the pedigree matrix from Weidema and Wesnæs, and the ISO 14044 data quality requirements. Results show that geographical representativeness is the most frequently deficient dimension, with 68% of studies relying on emission factors from regions with significantly different fleet compositions. A revised scoring framework with additional sub-criteria specific to transport in data-scarce contexts is proposed and illustrated with examples from the authors' own prior studies in Serbia and the Western Balkans.

title: Computational Optimisation of Exhaust Plenum Design for Bucket-Elevator Heads in Grain Handling Terminals
abstract: Bucket elevators are persistent dust sources in grain terminals because grain is accelerated and released at the elevator head, generating turbulence that defeats simple enclosures. This study used a parametric CFD approach in ANSYS Fluent to evaluate 27 plenum configurations varying in depth (120–360 mm), inlet slot width (40–120 mm), and slot position (top, mid, and bottom of the head enclosure). A discrete-phase model tracked particles of 10, 50, and 200 µm aerodynamic diameter at an elevator throughput representative of a 200 t/h terminal. The objective function was the ratio of captured particle mass to total released mass at a fixed exhaust volume flow of 0.35 m³/s. The best-performing configuration — mid-height slot, 240 mm depth — captured 89 % of the 50 µm fraction compared with 61 % for a baseline shallow enclosure. The penalty in required static pressure was 18 Pa. Designs are presented as dimensionless charts suitable for direct use by ventilation engineers without requiring site-specific CFD runs.

title: Scope 3 Category 11 for Electricity Distribution: Adapting a Consumer-Goods Framework to Network Infrastructure
abstract: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Category 11 (use of sold products) was designed primarily for consumer goods and does not map directly onto electricity distribution, where the 'product' is energy conveyance rather than a physical artefact. This paper examines how distribution network operators should interpret Category 11 and proposes a calculation framework treating downstream resistive losses — energy consumed by the network itself during delivery — as the relevant product-use emission. Using data from three Serbian distribution areas for 2019–2021, annual Category 11 emissions are estimated at between 28 400 and 34 700 t CO2e depending on loss rate and the emission factor methodology applied. The paper discusses boundary overlaps with Scope 2 of downstream consumers and with upstream generators' Scope 3 Category 11, and recommends explicit disclosure of double-counting risks. A worked numerical example is provided for a hypothetical 100 000-customer urban distribution zone.

title: Uncertainty Propagation in Cradle-to-Gate LCA of Mineral Wool Insulation: A Monte Carlo Approach
abstract: Mineral wool insulation boards are frequently assessed in building energy LCA studies, but the uncertainty of the underlying cradle-to-gate inventory data is rarely quantified. This study applied Monte Carlo simulation (n = 10,000 runs) in SimaPro 9.1 to propagate uncertainty through the LCA of stone wool board produced at a factory in Hungary, representing a product type also manufactured in northern Serbia. Input distributions for key parameters—basalt extraction energy, binder resin mass fraction, curing oven temperature, and transport distances—were estimated from factory records and expert elicitation. The resulting 95% confidence interval for GWP100 was 1.08–1.54 kg CO2-eq per kg product, with a median of 1.29 kg CO2-eq/kg. The binder resin production module contributed most to variance (38%), followed by melting furnace energy (29%). Results demonstrate that point-estimate EPDs for mineral wool may understate or overstate GWP by up to 19% relative to the median, with implications for comparative building assessments. Recommendations are given for minimum data quality requirements in future EPD programmes.

title: Life-Cycle Assessment in the Construction Sector: Methods, Data Sources, and Regulatory Context in Southeast Europe
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of LCA methodology as applied to construction products in Southeast Europe, with emphasis on the regulatory and normative framework relevant to practitioners in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Romania. The chapter covers the EN 15804 and ISO 14044 requirements, the role of programme operators and independent verifiers in EPD schemes, and the challenges of applying European background datasets—principally ecoinvent and the European Life Cycle Database—in regional industrial contexts. A section on life-cycle inventory modelling addresses primary data collection protocols for energy-intensive manufacturing processes including cement clinker production, ceramic tile firing, and flat glass melting. Case studies drawn from the authors' own work illustrate cradle-to-gate boundary definition decisions and allocation procedures for multi-output production systems. The chapter concludes with a discussion of the anticipated changes under the EU Construction Products Regulation revision and their implications for manufacturers in non-EU countries seeking to export to the single market.

title: Two-scale convergence for a class of periodic elastic laminates with soft inclusions
abstract: This paper applies the method of two-scale convergence to a family of linearly elastic composite media composed of a stiff matrix periodically punctuated by soft ellipsoidal inclusions. The period parameter ε is taken in the range 10⁻² to 10⁻⁴ relative to the macroscopic domain size. Cell problems are derived rigorously from the variational formulation, and closed-form bounds on the effective elasticity tensor are obtained for aspect ratios between 0.1 and 1.0. Numerical experiments using a finite element discretisation of the unit cell on meshes of up to 120 000 tetrahedral elements confirm that the homogenised solution reproduces the energy of the original problem to within 1.2% for ε ≤ 5 × 10⁻³. The corrector term is estimated in the H¹ norm and shown to decay as O(ε^(1/2)) in agreement with the theoretical prediction. The results provide a rigorous justification for existing engineering approximations used for glass-fibre reinforced polymers with periodic lay-up patterns.

title: Effective thermal conductivity of three-dimensional periodic fibre-reinforced composites: an asymptotic approach
abstract: We study the effective thermal conductivity of a three-dimensional composite consisting of cylindrical fibres with conductivity ratio κ_f/κ_m ranging from 5 to 500, arranged in a square periodic array. Using formal asymptotic expansion in the small parameter ε, we derive the leading-order homogenised equation and the first-order corrector. The unit-cell boundary value problem is solved numerically by a finite difference scheme on a 200×200×200 Cartesian grid. Computed effective conductivities are compared with 47 published experimental datasets for carbon-fibre epoxy systems; the mean relative error is 3.7%. We also examine the influence of fibre cross-sectional shape, comparing circular, square, and hexagonal cross-sections at volume fractions between 0.10 and 0.65. The asymptotic method consistently outperforms the Maxwell–Garnett estimate at volume fractions above 0.40, where inclusion interaction effects become significant. Limitations at near-percolation volume fractions are discussed.

title: Homogenisation of a thermoelastic periodic medium: coupling effects in the unit-cell problem
abstract: This work addresses the homogenisation of a thermoelastic composite in which thermal and mechanical fields are fully coupled through the standard linear thermoelastic constitutive relations. The periodic cell contains two isotropic phases whose Lamé parameters differ by a factor of up to 20 and whose thermal expansion coefficients differ by up to a factor of 6, values representative of metal-ceramic systems. The two-scale asymptotic expansion yields a macroscopic coupled system and two sets of cell problems: one mechanical and one thermal-mechanical. A key observation is that the effective thermal stress tensor cannot, in general, be obtained independently of the elastic cell problem. Numerical solutions to the cell problems are computed using a mixed finite element formulation in two space dimensions for 12 microgeometries. We quantify the error introduced by decoupling the cell problems, finding it to reach 8–14% in the effective thermal stress coefficient for high contrast ratios. Implications for engineering modelling of bimetallic strips and thermal barrier coatings are noted.

title: Corrector results for a degenerate diffusion problem in a perforated domain with Robin boundary conditions
abstract: We consider a diffusion equation with a degenerate diffusion coefficient posed in a perforated domain Ω_ε, where the holes are periodically distributed and the boundary of each hole carries a Robin condition with coefficient β(ε) scaling as ε. The degenerate case corresponds to a diffusion coefficient that vanishes on the boundary of the solid phase. Using the unfolding operator framework, we derive the homogenised equation and establish corrector results in the L² norm without the customary smoothness assumptions on the data. The main technical contribution is a compactness argument valid when the diffusion coefficient belongs only to L^p for p > 2. Error estimates of order O(ε^(1/2)) are proved rigorously and verified numerically on a sequence of meshes with ε = 0.1, 0.05, 0.025, 0.0125. The problem is motivated by models of contaminant transport in porous geological media with reactive surfaces, and the results extend earlier work that required Lipschitz diffusion coefficients.

title: Effective medium approximations for quasi-periodic composites: a numerical comparison
abstract: Classical homogenisation theory relies on strict periodicity of the microstructure. This paper investigates how well standard effective medium approximations perform when the microstructure is only quasi-periodic, generated by a cut-and-project construction from a five-fold symmetric lattice in two dimensions. We compare four approximation strategies—Voigt, Reuss, Hashin–Shtrikman bounds, and the classical periodic homogenisation solution—against direct numerical simulations on domains containing up to 1 400 inclusions. Elastic moduli are evaluated as a function of inclusion volume fraction (0.05 to 0.55) and stiffness contrast (2 to 100). The Hashin–Shtrikman bounds remain valid throughout the tested range. The periodic homogenised value overestimates the effective Young modulus by up to 11% at volume fraction 0.45 and contrast 50, indicating that aperiodic fluctuations in local arrangement are non-negligible at moderate contrasts. We propose a simple correction factor depending on the pair-correlation function of the inclusion centres.

title: Homogenisation-based bounds for the dynamic effective mass density of a phononic periodic composite
abstract: Dynamic homogenisation at low frequencies is applied to a two-phase periodic composite consisting of heavy cylindrical inclusions embedded in a light elastic matrix, a configuration used in laboratory-scale phononic structures. We derive frequency-dependent effective mass density and effective stiffness using the time-harmonic two-scale expansion, retaining terms up to order ε². The resulting effective medium supports negative effective mass density in a frequency band of width approximately 0.08 times the first Bragg frequency for inclusion-to-matrix density ratios between 5 and 15. This band width is computed for 6 inclusion radii (r/a = 0.2 to 0.45) and compared with direct Bloch-wave dispersion curves obtained by finite element analysis of the periodic cell; agreement is within 4% for frequencies below 0.6 times the Bragg frequency. The analysis confirms that the homogenised description loses accuracy near band-gap edges, where higher-order terms are needed.

title: On the Composition of ε-Differentially Private Mechanisms over Sequential Queries
abstract: Composition theorems for differential privacy establish how privacy guarantees degrade when multiple mechanisms are applied in sequence to the same dataset. We revisit the standard sequential composition theorem and derive refined bounds under the assumption that queries are drawn from a restricted query class with bounded overlap in their sensitivity sets. Using a measure-theoretic framing, we prove that for k queries drawn uniformly from such a class, the composed privacy loss grows as O(k^{0.7}) rather than O(k) in expectation. Experiments on a synthetic tabular dataset with 200,000 rows and 14 numeric attributes confirm that the tighter bound allows an additional 2–4 queries per privacy budget unit without measurable increase in empirical disclosure risk under membership inference attack. We also provide a counterexample showing the bound fails for adversarially ordered query sequences.

title: Geometric Mechanism for Integer-Valued Queries Under Local Differential Privacy
abstract: The Geometric mechanism is a discrete analogue of the Laplace mechanism suited to integer-valued query outputs. We extend its analysis to the local differential privacy setting, where each data holder randomises their own record before transmission. We characterise the optimal noise parameter as a function of the privacy budget ε and the integer domain width, and derive expressions for the mean squared error of frequency estimates reconstructed at the aggregator. We compare the Geometric mechanism against the Randomised Response and the Unary Encoding mechanisms on three benchmarks: a synthetic income histogram with 50 bins, a mobility dataset with 30 location categories, and a health survey with 12 ordinal responses. The Geometric mechanism achieves lower mean squared error than the alternatives at ε values below 1.5 across all three benchmarks, with reductions of 9–23% depending on domain size.

title: Differentially Private Histogram Estimation for Skewed Distributions
abstract: Standard differentially private histogram mechanisms allocate noise uniformly across all bins regardless of bin occupancy, which is inefficient when the underlying distribution is heavily skewed. We propose a two-stage approach in which a small portion of the privacy budget is spent identifying high-occupancy bins via a private threshold test, and the remaining budget is reallocated to those bins with reduced noise. The approach is analysed under both ε-DP and (ε, δ)-DP. We prove that for Zipfian-distributed data with parameter α > 1.5, the proposed scheme reduces total squared error by a factor of roughly (1 − 1/α) compared to uniform allocation. Experiments using a synthetic word-count corpus of 10 million tokens and a real-shaped e-commerce order distribution (anonymised to 100,000 records) confirm the theoretical prediction within 5% relative error. The method is applicable to any ordinal or categorical attribute with a known or estimable skew parameter.

title: Privacy-Preserving Logistic Regression via Objective Perturbation: A Comparative Study
abstract: Objective perturbation adds calibrated noise directly to the loss function before optimisation, offering an alternative to output perturbation for differentially private empirical risk minimisation. We conduct a systematic comparison of objective perturbation against output perturbation and gradient perturbation for logistic regression classifiers under ε values ranging from 0.1 to 5.0. The study uses four binary classification datasets with between 3,000 and 120,000 samples and 8 to 64 features, all synthetically generated to mirror publicly described demographic and credit-scoring distributions. We measure classification accuracy, calibration error, and empirical privacy leakage under a shadow-model attack. Objective perturbation achieves the best accuracy-privacy tradeoff at moderate ε (1.0–2.0) in three of four datasets, but is consistently outperformed by gradient perturbation at very low ε (below 0.5). We provide practical recommendations for choosing the perturbation strategy based on dataset size and desired ε.

title: Federated Mean Estimation with Heterogeneous Client Data Under Local Differential Privacy
abstract: We study the problem of estimating a population mean from horizontally distributed data when each client applies a local differential privacy mechanism before communicating with a central server. We model heterogeneity through a mixture of Gaussian client distributions with varying means and variances, and analyse the bias and variance of the federated estimator as a function of the number of clients n, their local sample sizes m_i, and the privacy parameter ε. We show that the mean squared error of the federated estimator scales as O(1/(nε²)) under standard conditions, matching a lower bound we derive for this setting. Simulations with n ∈ {50, 200, 1000} clients and m_i drawn from a Pareto distribution confirm the scaling, and we observe that variance heterogeneity increases estimation error by up to 31% at n = 50. The paper provides sample size guidelines for practitioners deploying federated analytics pipelines.

title: Rényi Differential Privacy and Its Application to Adaptive Query Release
abstract: Rényi differential privacy (RDP) provides tighter composition bounds than standard (ε, δ)-DP by tracking privacy loss through the Rényi divergence at a chosen order α. We survey the RDP framework with unified proofs and extend two existing results: we show that the Gaussian mechanism satisfies RDP of order α with parameter αΔ²/(2σ²) for sensitivity Δ and noise scale σ, and we prove a subsampled RDP bound for Poisson subsampling that improves on prior work by a constant factor at orders α > 4. We then design an adaptive query release system that selects α dynamically to minimise total noise while respecting a global privacy budget. On a synthetic longitudinal dataset with 80,000 individuals and 24 time steps, the adaptive system serves on average 17% more queries per budget unit than a fixed-α baseline. A worked example in a healthcare analytics scenario is included.

title: Differential Privacy in Federated Learning: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Open Problems
abstract: This book chapter surveys the integration of differential privacy mechanisms into federated learning systems, covering the spectrum from centralised DP-SGD to fully decentralised local DP protocols. We organise the literature around three axes: the trust model (honest-but-curious vs. malicious aggregator), the communication topology (star, ring, and arbitrary graphs), and the privacy accounting method (moments accountant, RDP, and zero-concentrated DP). For each combination we summarise known convergence rates, communication costs, and empirical utility benchmarks drawn from published studies. We identify six open problems, including the lack of tight lower bounds for heterogeneous federated estimation and the absence of practical Byzantine-robust local DP protocols. The chapter is intended as a reference for researchers entering the field and includes a taxonomy table and a consolidated bibliography of 94 works.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Estimation via Quantisation and Local Differential Privacy
abstract: In bandwidth-constrained federated settings, clients must compress their updates before transmission. We study the joint effect of stochastic quantisation and local differential privacy noise on the accuracy of a federated mean estimator. We model each client as applying a k-level uniform quantiser followed by a Laplace or Gaussian noise injection, and derive the combined distortion as a function of k, ε, and the update magnitude. We show that there exists an optimal quantisation level k*(ε) that minimises total mean squared error for a given bandwidth budget, and provide a closed-form approximation for k* that is accurate within 8% across all tested configurations. Simulations using a federated linear regression task with 500 clients, each holding between 20 and 200 samples, show that the optimised scheme achieves equivalent accuracy to an unquantised baseline while reducing communication volume by 63% at ε = 1.0.

title: Privatised Sufficient Statistics for Exponential Family Models in Federated Inference
abstract: Exponential family distributions are parameterised by sufficient statistics, which makes them natural targets for differentially private federated inference: perturbing sufficient statistics preserves model structure while limiting disclosure. We formalise this approach for Gaussian, Poisson, and Bernoulli models, deriving the minimum noise required to achieve (ε, δ)-DP for each model's sufficient statistic given a dataset of n records. We then study the posterior contraction rate of a Bayesian estimator that operates on privatised sufficient statistics and show that the posterior contracts at rate n^{-1/2} ε^{-1} for Gaussian models, matching a minimax lower bound. Experiments on a synthetic longitudinal healthcare dataset with 15,000 patients across five federated sites demonstrate that the privatised sufficient statistic approach yields narrower credible intervals than a gradient-based DP-SGD baseline at equal privacy cost. An R implementation is provided as supplementary material.

title: Auditing Differential Privacy Guarantees in Deployed Federated Systems: A Black-Box Approach
abstract: Differential privacy proofs establish theoretical guarantees, but deployed implementations may violate these guarantees through numerical errors, incorrect clipping, or library bugs. We describe a black-box auditing procedure that estimates the empirical ε of a federated learning system by constructing worst-case adjacent datasets and measuring the likelihood ratio of observed outputs. The procedure requires only query access to the system's aggregator endpoint and uses a sequential hypothesis test to control false-positive and false-negative audit error rates at specified levels. We apply the auditor to three open-source federated learning frameworks configured with advertised ε values of 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0. In one framework, the auditor detects an empirical ε of 3.4 at the advertised setting of 2.0, tracing the discrepancy to an incorrect per-sample gradient clipping implementation. Runtime for a single audit at the 0.05 significance level is approximately 4 hours on a 16-core server.

title: Adaptive Privacy Budget Allocation Across Rounds in Federated Learning
abstract: In multi-round federated learning with a fixed total privacy budget, the allocation of per-round budget affects both final model utility and convergence speed. Static equal allocation is the default, but it ignores that early rounds benefit more from accurate gradient estimates when the model is far from convergence. We formulate budget allocation as a constrained optimisation problem and derive an adaptive schedule that allocates larger per-round ε to early rounds and smaller ε to later rounds, following a decreasing geometric sequence. We prove that this schedule achieves the same asymptotic convergence rate as equal allocation while reducing excess risk by a factor proportional to the geometric ratio. Experiments on a federated regression task with 200 clients and T ∈ {20, 50, 100} rounds show that the adaptive schedule reduces mean squared prediction error by 7–14% relative to equal allocation at equal total budget. The result is robust across three data heterogeneity levels.

title: Tight Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Distribution Testing
abstract: Distribution testing asks whether an unknown distribution P equals a known reference distribution Q, or is far from it in total variation distance. We study the sample complexity of this task under ε-differential privacy and derive lower bounds using a fingerprinting lemma adapted from the mean estimation setting. For distributions supported on d elements, we show that any ε-DP tester requires at least Ω(d^{1/2}/ε + d^{2/3}) samples to distinguish P = Q from total variation distance at least 0.1, improving the previously best known lower bound by a d^{1/6}/ε factor in the privacy-dominated regime. The proof constructs a family of hard instances using a combinatorial design with d/2 elements of equal probability mass. We also show the lower bound is matched up to logarithmic factors by an existing mechanism, closing the gap for ε ≥ 1. A preprint extends these results to the local DP model.

title: Hybridising Simulated Annealing with Constraint Propagation for Healthcare Rostering
abstract: We describe a hybrid method that interleaves simulated annealing moves with forward-checking constraint propagation for a healthcare rostering problem involving 180 nurses distributed across six wards of a regional hospital in northern Serbia. The propagation step prunes infeasible assignments after each move, allowing the annealing component to operate over a reduced feasible neighbourhood without explicit constraint checking in the objective function. The cooling schedule uses a geometric decay with reheat phases triggered when the acceptance rate drops below 2 percent. On a set of 30 real-world monthly rostering instances, the hybrid finds solutions with an average weighted penalty 18 percent lower than standalone simulated annealing and 9 percent lower than a CP solver with a 30-minute limit. Solution times average 47 seconds. Robustness to changes in ward staffing levels is evaluated through perturbation experiments.

title: Developing a Resilience Index for Small Manufacturing Firms: Preliminary Evidence from Vojvodina
abstract: This paper reports the construction and initial validation of a composite resilience index (CRI) designed for small manufacturing enterprises in the Vojvodina region of Serbia. Drawing on a pilot survey of 47 firms employing between 10 and 49 workers, the study identifies five latent dimensions—absorptive capacity, adaptive capacity, resource redundancy, managerial awareness, and inter-firm connectivity—and constructs a weighted index using principal component analysis in SPSS 26. Cronbach's alpha values ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 across dimensions. Preliminary results indicate that resource redundancy and managerial awareness account for the largest share of variance in self-reported recovery speed following supply disruptions. The paper acknowledges the small sample size and the cross-sectional design as limitations, and proposes a longitudinal follow-up with a minimum of 150 firms. The index provides a practical diagnostic tool applicable by regional development agencies and chamber-of-commerce practitioners without specialist statistical expertise.

title: Supply Chain Disruption Exposure and Recovery Patterns Among Metal-Processing SMEs in the Western Balkans: A Cross-Country Survey
abstract: This study examines how small and medium-sized metal-processing manufacturers in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia experienced and recovered from supply chain disruptions during 2020–2022, a period that included pandemic-related shocks and raw-material price volatility. A standardised questionnaire was administered to 214 firms across the three countries, stratified by firm size and subindustry. Logistic regression models identify the factors associated with recovery within six months: diversified supplier base (OR = 2.31, p < 0.01), existence of a written contingency plan (OR = 1.87, p < 0.05), and access to short-term credit lines (OR = 1.64, p < 0.05). Country-level differences were modest once firm size was controlled. The results point to the practical value of even informal contingency planning in contexts where formal enterprise risk management frameworks are rare. Limitations include self-reported disruption data and variation in questionnaire administration procedures across countries.

title: Toward a Sector-Specific Resilience Scorecard for Food and Beverage Manufacturers in Serbia: Instrument Design and Factorial Validation
abstract: Generic organizational resilience instruments do not fully capture sector-specific vulnerabilities such as perishable inventory, seasonal demand swings, and tight regulatory requirements in food and beverage manufacturing. This study reports the design and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) of a 28-item resilience scorecard tailored to this sector. Items were generated through a three-round Delphi process involving 14 industry experts and validated on survey data from 121 Serbian food and beverage SMEs. CFA in SmartPLS 4 confirmed a four-factor structure (adaptive procurement, regulatory compliance capacity, workforce flexibility, and demand-sensing) with composite reliability values above 0.80 and average variance extracted above 0.50 for all constructs. Discriminant validity was confirmed using the heterotrait-monotrait ratio. The resulting instrument is presented as a practical scorecard suitable for self-administration by company management, with scoring guidelines provided in an appendix.

title: Measuring Idle and Active Energy Consumption in a Small-Series Metal Fabrication Cell
abstract: This study presents a methodology for separating idle-state from active-state electricity consumption in a four-machine sheet-metal fabrication cell at a job-shop in Vojvodina. Three-phase power analysers were installed on each machine for a continuous eight-week monitoring campaign. Idle energy was found to account for 31–47 % of total machine consumption depending on shift patterns. The paper introduces a simple idle-fraction index and demonstrates its calculation from standard power-logger CSV exports without additional instrumentation. Measurement uncertainty is discussed in detail, and the authors show that a sampling rate of 1 Hz is sufficient to capture the dominant consumption events for the machine classes examined. The results suggest that staggered start-up scheduling could reduce standby losses by approximately 18 % at the studied facility. The methodology is intended to be replicable by practitioners with commercially available metering equipment costing under EUR 2 000 per measurement point.

title: Energy Value-Stream Mapping: A Step-by-Step Procedure Adapted for Small and Medium Enterprises
abstract: Value-stream mapping (VSM) has been used extensively for material and information flow analysis; its extension to energy flows has been proposed in the literature but practical guidance for SMEs remains sparse. This paper describes a structured eight-step procedure for constructing an energy VSM in a discrete manufacturing environment with fewer than 50 production workers. The procedure covers meter placement, data normalisation per unit of production, icon conventions, and the identification of energy kaizen bursts. It was validated at two SMEs in the Novi Sad area, one producing agricultural equipment components and one producing aluminium window frames. At the first site, the mapping exercise identified a hydraulic press as responsible for 38 % of total process energy while contributing only 12 % of value-adding time. Cycle times, machine power demands, and shift schedules were recorded manually and cross-checked against utility invoices. A template spreadsheet accompanies the paper. Limitations regarding measurement granularity and the treatment of compressed air are discussed.

title: Load Profile Characteristics of MIG/MAG Welding Stations Under Production Conditions
abstract: The electrical load profile of MIG/MAG welding power sources differs substantially from those of machine tools because arc-on time is typically a small fraction of total station time and the power demand fluctuates on a sub-second scale. This paper reports measurements collected at five welding stations in a structural steel workshop over a four-week period. Current and voltage were sampled at 10 kHz using a purpose-built data acquisition board; one-minute averages were retained for trend analysis. Arc-on fraction ranged from 0.12 to 0.41 across stations. Standby consumption at the inverter power sources was 45–80 W, while peak welding power reached 6.2 kW. A piecewise linear model of the station load profile is proposed with three states: off, standby, and welding. The model is parameterised from routine production data and validated against sub-metered energy readings with a mean absolute percentage error of 4.3 %. The paper also discusses power quality aspects, including current harmonic distortion during arc ignition.
venue: Welding Technology Review – European Edition

title: Comparison of Three Data-Collection Strategies for Per-Process Energy Monitoring in Machining
abstract: Per-process energy monitoring can be implemented via direct metering at the machine, via disaggregation from a subpanel meter, or via hybrid approaches combining measurements with process simulation. This paper compares these three strategies applied to a turning and milling cell comprising six CNC machines. Direct metering was taken as the reference. Subpanel disaggregation was carried out using a non-negative matrix factorisation algorithm applied to 1-second active power data from a single three-phase meter. The hybrid approach used a specific energy consumption model calibrated on 30 test cuts. Direct metering achieved a mean error of 1.8 % relative to submetered ground truth. Disaggregation produced errors of 9–24 % per machine, performing better on machines with distinctive load signatures. The hybrid model reached 6.1 % mean error under stable conditions but degraded when tool wear was not updated. Cost and installation complexity are compared, and a decision tree for strategy selection is provided.
venue: International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Systems

title: Energy Mapping of a Manual Arc Welding Repair Shop: From Data Collection to Improvement Measures
abstract: Manual metal arc (MMA) welding repair operations are energy-intensive and irregularly scheduled, making systematic energy analysis difficult. This paper presents a case study of an MMA repair shop with 14 welding bays at a heavy machinery maintenance facility in Serbia. An energy VSM was constructed using clamp-meter measurements taken at each bay during representative repair jobs over three weeks. Total electrical energy per kilogram of deposited weld metal was used as the primary performance indicator, yielding values of 9.4–17.1 kWh/kg depending on electrode type and operator technique. The energy VSM revealed that pre-heating ovens contributed 22 % of process energy yet were idle for over 60 % of shift time. Two improvement scenarios are evaluated: oven scheduling based on the repair queue and replacement of ageing transformer rectifiers with modern inverter units. The scenarios are estimated to reduce total facility welding energy by 14 % and 21 % respectively, based on manufacturer data and measured load profiles.
venue: Thermal Science and Engineering Applications

title: Integrating Energy Consumption Data into Production Scheduling: A Mixed-Integer Formulation for a Welding Workshop
abstract: Production scheduling in discrete job shops typically optimises makespan or tardiness without considering electricity costs. This paper proposes a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that incorporates time-of-use electricity tariffs and machine-level load profiles into job sequencing for a welding workshop with eight stations. Load profiles for each station were derived from four weeks of sub-metering data. The model minimises a weighted combination of total energy cost and makespan across a rolling 24-hour planning horizon. Computational experiments on 40 instances generated from real shop floor data show that energy-aware scheduling reduced electricity cost by 8–15 % relative to earliest-due-date dispatching, with a makespan increase of less than 4 % in 35 of 40 instances. The MILP was solved in CPLEX 20.1; instances with up to 30 jobs and 8 machines solved to within 2 % optimality gap in under 90 seconds. The paper discusses how load profile uncertainty propagates into cost estimates.
venue: European Journal of Industrial Engineering and Operations

title: Benchmarking Specific Energy Consumption Across Robotic MIG Welding Cells in the Automotive Supply Chain
abstract: Robotic MIG welding cells in automotive component manufacturing show substantial variation in specific energy consumption (SEC) even when welding similar joint geometries. This paper reports a benchmarking exercise covering nine robotic welding cells at four automotive Tier-2 suppliers in Serbia and Hungary. SEC was defined as kWh per linear metre of weld and per kilogram of part mass; both metrics are discussed. Data were collected over one production month per site using permanently installed submeters. SEC ranged from 0.18 to 0.54 kWh/m across cells. Robot motion between weld sequences, torch service routines, and pallet transfer times accounted for 28–51 % of total cell energy. A regression analysis identifies wire feed speed and inter-pass dwell time as the two variables most strongly correlated with SEC. Practical guidelines for cell programming aimed at reducing dwell-related consumption are formulated and an estimated 11 % reduction in SEC is projected for two of the participating cells.

title: Energy Value-Stream Mapping with Dynamic Demand Overlays: Method Development and a Fabrication Case Study
abstract: Standard energy VSM represents energy as a static attribute of each process step. This paper proposes an extension in which time-varying demand curves — measured load profiles aggregated by shift interval — are overlaid on the value-stream map using a colour-coded intensity scale. The extension allows planners to identify coincident peak demand events across multiple processes, which static VSM cannot capture. The method was developed collaboratively with practitioners at a structural steel fabrication company and applied to a value stream comprising plasma cutting, press-braking, MIG welding, and painting. Monitored over six weeks, the value stream exhibited a coincident peak of 112 kW during the first 30 minutes of the morning shift, driven by simultaneous warm-up cycles at three processes. Redistributing warm-up schedules reduced peak demand by 23 kW, with a projected annual saving of EUR 3 200 at prevailing demand-charge tariffs. A set of seven VSM icon extensions is proposed and a mapping procedure compatible with standard VSM software templates is described.
venue: Journal of Cleaner Production Technologies

title: Towards an Energy Digital Twin for a Welding Cell: Data Requirements, Architecture, and Preliminary Validation
abstract: A digital twin (DT) of a manufacturing cell that accurately reflects energy consumption must integrate process parameters, machine states, and utility measurements at appropriate fidelity. This preprint describes the architecture of an energy-focused DT developed for a two-robot MIG welding cell. The DT combines a physics-informed arc energy model, a thermal model of the power source, and a data-driven state machine calibrated on six months of sub-metered production data. Inputs are welding procedure parameters extracted from the robot controller log; outputs are predicted active power, reactive power, and cumulative energy per job. Preliminary validation on 45 production jobs shows a mean absolute percentage error of 5.8 % for cumulative job energy and 12.4 % for instantaneous power peaks. Key open questions regarding synchronisation latency and model drift over tool life are identified. The work is part of an ongoing project; a fully validated version is intended for journal submission in 2026.

title: Pricing under learning: updating demand elasticity estimates as orders accumulate in a make-to-order shop
abstract: Demand elasticity in custom manufacturing is not stationary: it shifts with market conditions, competitor capacity, and material price fluctuations. This paper proposes a Bayesian updating scheme in which the firm maintains a posterior distribution over its price elasticity parameter and updates it with each observed order (accepted or rejected). A Thompson-sampling pricing rule selects prices that balance revenue exploitation with information acquisition. Simulation experiments over a 52-week horizon show that the Bayesian learning policy converges to within 2% of the true optimal revenue after approximately 120 orders, compared with 350 orders required by a frequentist rolling-window estimator. The rate of convergence depends strongly on the prior variance assigned to elasticity; the paper provides practical guidance for prior elicitation based on survey or historical quote data. An extension to non-stationary elasticity using exponential forgetting is also evaluated.

title: Forty years of maize yield records at Rimski Šančevi: separating crop sequence effects from nitrogen input trends using linear mixed models
abstract: Long-term maize yield data spanning 1979–2018 from a continuous rotation trial at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station were subjected to variance decomposition using linear mixed-effects models. Three rotation treatments — continuous maize, maize–wheat two-year, and maize–wheat–sunflower three-year — were compared against annual nitrogen input records and 39-year climate reanalysis data from the E-OBS gridded dataset. Nitrogen application rates increased markedly between 1990 and 2005 before stabilising, creating a trend confounded with putative rotation benefits. After partitioning nitrogen input as a fixed covariate and treating year as a random slope, the three-year rotation showed a stable yield advantage of 0.41 t/ha over continuous maize, robust across all decadal subsets. Climate terms explained 18% of interannual variance, primarily driven by July mean maximum temperature and April precipitation totals. Soil organic carbon measured at five-year intervals co-varied significantly with rotation diversity, suggesting a partial mediation pathway. The results indicate that naive before–after comparisons substantially overestimate rotation benefits in periods of rising inputs.
venue: Journal of Agronomy and Crop Research

title: Wheat yield response to preceding crop in Vojvodina: a 25-year panel analysis
abstract: Wheat yields recorded annually from 1993 to 2017 across four rotation experiment blocks at Rimski Šančevi were analysed as an unbalanced panel dataset. Preceding crops included sunflower, sugar beet, maize, and wheat itself. Fixed-effects panel regression controlled for block-specific soil heterogeneity and annual growing-degree-day sums derived from daily station measurements. Sugar beet and sunflower predecessors yielded a consistent wheat advantage of 0.31 and 0.24 t/ha respectively relative to monoculture wheat, after removing a positive time trend attributable to improved variety succession. The interaction between predecessor type and spring precipitation in the 30-day window before heading was statistically significant, with the sunflower–wheat advantage narrowing in dry springs. Soil nitrate measurements at sowing correlated with predecessor identity (r = 0.61), and inclusion of sowing-date nitrate as a covariate reduced the predecessor main effect by approximately 30%, implicating residual nitrogen as a dominant mechanism. Variety-change intervals were reconstructed from station records and included as a binary covariate.

title: Disentangling climate warming from management intensification in a 30-year sunflower rotation trial
abstract: Mean growing-season temperature at Rimski Šančevi increased by 0.38 °C per decade between 1986 and 2015, coinciding with shifts in fungicide application frequency and hybrid replacement cycles. This study used structural equation modelling to apportion sunflower yield variance across four causal pathways: rotation position, thermal accumulation, fungicide input, and hybrid improvement. Data comprised 360 plot-year observations from three rotation sequences. A path coefficient of 0.29 was estimated for rotation position (sunflower grown after wheat vs. after maize), stable after conditioning on hybrid introduction year. The direct effect of growing-season mean temperature was negative (−0.18 standardised units), partially offset by increased radiation use efficiency in warmer years. Fungicide input frequency explained 12% of yield variance independently. The decomposition reveals that approximately one-quarter of the apparent trend improvement in sunflower yields over the period can be attributed to rotation management rather than technology or climate, a share that would be invisible in aggregated regional statistics.

title: Do decade-scale soil organic carbon trends track rotation diversity? Evidence from four experimental series
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) was measured at 0–30 cm depth at five-year intervals from 1982 to 2017 across four long-term rotation series at Rimski Šančevi. Rotations ranged from monoculture maize to five-species sequences including legumes. A multivariate analysis of covariance treated clay content, initial SOC, and cumulative organic manure additions as covariates. Rotation diversity, expressed as the Shannon evenness index of crop species per rotation, showed a positive partial regression coefficient on SOC change rate (β = 0.034 kg C m⁻² per unit evenness per decade, p < 0.01). Legume presence in the rotation added an independent positive term. Cumulative manure additions dominated SOC dynamics in the highest-input treatments, partially masking rotation effects. After removing manure-amended plots, the rotation diversity effect strengthened. These results are consistent with rhizodeposition-mediated carbon inputs as a mechanism but the dataset lacks root biomass measurements sufficient to confirm this. Implications for carbon credit calculations based on rotation records are discussed.
venue: Soil and Tillage Research

title: Yield stability metrics in multi-year rotation datasets: a comparison of Eberhart–Russell regression, coefficient of variation, and Huehn's rank statistics
abstract: Yield stability analyses are commonly applied to variety trials but are less often used to characterise rotation-position effects over time. This methodological study applies three stability metrics — Eberhart–Russell regression coefficients, coefficient of variation across years, and Huehn's non-parametric rank statistics — to a 28-year maize and wheat yield dataset from Rimski Šančevi. Four rotation treatments served as 'genotype-analogue' groupings across 28 environments (years). The three methods agreed on ranking rotation treatments by mean yield but diverged in stability classification: Eberhart–Russell identified the three-year maize–wheat–sunflower rotation as above-average in both yield and stability, while Huehn's statistics ranked two-year rotations as more stable due to fewer extreme low-yield years. The coefficient of variation inflated instability estimates for higher-yielding treatments. The choice of stability metric materially affects recommendations about rotation adoption under variable climate conditions. Practitioners are advised to report at least two complementary metrics.
venue: Acta Agriculturae Pannonica

title: Historical nitrogen input reconstruction for long-term experimental sites in northern Serbia using fertiliser delivery records and crop removal estimates
abstract: Accurate historical nitrogen input series are a prerequisite for confounder control in long-term rotation experiments, yet pre-1990 records for sites in the former Yugoslavia are often incomplete or stored in paper archives. This study reconstructs annual nitrogen balances for four experimental series at Rimski Šančevi from 1970 to 2005 by combining digitised fertiliser delivery records, provincial agricultural statistics, and nitrogen removal calculations based on harvested yields and standard grain nitrogen concentrations. Gaps of one to three years were imputed using a locally weighted regression on surrounding years and provincial purchase statistics. Reconstructed inputs showed a pronounced peak in 1985–1988 followed by a sharp decline during the economic disruptions of the 1990s, then partial recovery post-2001. The reconstructed series were validated against a subset of plot-level farm books held in the station archive. The resulting dataset has been deposited in the institutional repository and is used as a covariate in ongoing rotation effect analyses. Imputation uncertainty is propagated into subsequent regression analyses using 500 bootstrap replicates.

title: Segmented regression detection of structural breaks in a 45-year maize yield series: rotation versus non-rotation explanations
abstract: Structural break detection in long agronomic time series is valuable for identifying the timing and magnitude of management or climate regime shifts. Maize yield data (1971–2015) from continuous maize and three-year rotation plots at Rimski Šančevi were analysed using the Bai–Perron multiple structural break test implemented in R. Three breaks were identified in the continuous maize series (1979, 1993, 2003) and two in the rotation series (1993, 2003). The 1993 break coincided with a documented reduction in mineral fertiliser application and was present in both series with similar magnitude (−0.52 and −0.49 t/ha respectively), suggesting a shared input-driven rather than rotation-specific explanation. The 2003 break corresponded to the extreme European drought and heat wave year, with a larger yield depression in continuous maize (−1.1 t/ha) than in the rotation treatment (−0.7 t/ha), consistent with a buffering effect of rotation diversity under stress. The 1979 break in continuous maize only coincided with a pathogen outbreak recorded in station field diaries.

title: Sugar beet position effects in a long-term rotation: yield and quality trends 1985–2019 at two sites in Vojvodina
abstract: Sugar beet was grown in its first, second, and third year after a cereal in replicated plots at Rimski Šančevi and at a second experimental station near Sombor from 1985 to 2019. Root yield and sugar content were recorded annually; soil pH, sodium, and boron were measured every five years. A two-site mixed model with site as a random effect confirmed that first-year beet outyielded third-year beet by 4.8 t/ha on average. Sugar content showed a weaker rotation response, declining only 0.3 percentage points by third-year position. The yield gap between positions widened after 2005, coinciding with the mandatory reduction in soil fumigant use and a corresponding increase in free-living nematode counts documented through separate soil sampling. Site differences were modest relative to position effects. Climate terms including winter soil temperature and April rainfall contributed significantly to interannual variance but did not interact with rotation position. The data suggest that nematode pressure amplification partly accounts for apparent rotation-position effects in beet.

title: Long-term rotation experiments in south-east Europe: a structured inventory of active and discontinued series
abstract: Long-term field experiments (LTEs) are irreplaceable infrastructures for crop science, yet many series established during the socialist period in south-east Europe were discontinued after 1990 or exist only in grey literature. This chapter presents a structured inventory of 31 rotation LTEs in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, Croatia, and Bulgaria, compiled through direct contact with experimental stations and a review of domestic journal archives. For each series, we recorded start year, crop sequence treatments, input level documentation quality, soil characterisation frequency, data availability, and current operational status. Of 31 series identified, 18 remain active; 7 were discontinued between 1991 and 2002 due to funding loss; 6 were discontinued with partial data rescue completed. The chapter discusses metadata standards needed for cross-site synthesis and identifies three sites with multi-decade datasets suitable for climate–rotation interaction modelling at the regional scale. A common data template developed within the inventory project is appended.

title: Weed flora shifts over 35 years in rotation and monoculture plots: are changes driven by rotation diversity or herbicide regime?
abstract: Weed species composition was assessed by quadrat counts in 1985, 1995, 2005, and 2018 across maize monoculture, two-year, and three-year rotation plots at Rimski Šančevi, yielding 192 plot-census combinations. Herbicide application records were available for the full period. Redundancy analysis of species-abundance matrices showed that herbicide active-substance diversity explained 34% of floristic variance, while rotation sequence explained an additional 19% after conditioning on herbicides. Rotation plots showed higher weed species richness in all census years, but the gap narrowed from 3.2 species/m² in 1985 to 1.4 in 2018, tracking a period of increasing herbicide complexity. Two problematic annual species — Amaranthus retroflexus and Sorghum halepense — increased substantially in monoculture from 2005 onwards; rotation plots showed the same directional trend but with a 12-year lag. The findings caution against attributing weed shifts entirely to rotation management without controlling for concurrent herbicide regime changes.

title: Comparing parametric and machine-learning yield trend decomposition on a 30-year rotation dataset: what do the models agree on?
abstract: This conference paper reports a preliminary comparison of three modelling approaches applied to the same 30-year maize yield series from Rimski Šančevi: ordinary least squares with polynomial time trend, linear mixed-effects model with crossed random effects for plot and year, and a gradient-boosted tree ensemble. All three approaches received identical predictor sets: rotation treatment code, annual growing-degree days, April–June precipitation total, mineral nitrogen applied, and a variety-generation indicator variable. The OLS and mixed-effects models agreed on the sign and approximate magnitude of the rotation main effect (0.38–0.44 t/ha for the three-year rotation relative to monoculture). The gradient-boosted model yielded a higher estimate (0.61 t/ha) with a wide bootstrap interval. Feature importance rankings from the tree model broadly matched parametric coefficients for climate and input variables. The paper concludes that the rotation effect estimate is robust to modelling choice when parametric models are used, but that tree-based approaches require careful regularisation to avoid capturing plot-level idiosyncrasies as rotation signals.

title: Soybean as a rotation entry in Vojvodina: yield, nodulation efficiency, and residual nitrogen effects over 22 years
abstract: Soybean was introduced into a previously cereal-dominated rotation experiment in 1999. Plot-level data through 2020 allow analysis of (i) soybean yield trends in its first, second, and third year of inclusion; (ii) nodulation efficiency assessed by acetylene reduction assay at R2 stage in eight selected years; and (iii) residual mineral nitrogen measured in autumn after soybean harvest across all 22 years. Soybean yield was stable across years after accounting for variety succession, showing no significant trend, unlike concurrent wheat and maize series which exhibited positive trends. Nodulation efficiency declined in four of the five drought years identified in the dataset, with a threshold summer water deficit of approximately 120 mm triggering a statistically significant reduction. Residual autumn nitrate after soybean averaged 38 kg N/ha, compared with 17 kg/ha after maize, and the difference remained consistent across decades and nitrogen input levels. Subsequent wheat yield benefited significantly from soybean predecessors, with the benefit attributable primarily to the residual nitrogen pathway rather than disease suppression based on partial correlation analysis.

title: Weed seedbank composition under conventional and reduced tillage in sunflower on Chernozem soils of Vojvodina
abstract: Seedbank samples were collected at two depths (0–10 cm and 10–30 cm) in spring 2008 and 2009 from six paired fields managed under conventional mouldboard ploughing or reduced tillage for at least five consecutive years. Twelve dominant weed species were identified through forced germination on moist filter paper at controlled temperature. Reduced tillage plots showed a 34% higher total seedbank density in the surface layer (mean 4 820 viable seeds m⁻²) compared with ploughed plots (3 590 seeds m⁻²), driven mainly by Ambrosia artemisiifolia and Chenopodium album. In deeper layers, the ploughed treatment retained significantly higher densities of large-seeded species. Redundancy analysis linked seedbank composition to prior herbicide programme and preceding crop identity. Results suggest that switching to reduced tillage without adjusting weed management increases near-surface seedbank pressure within three seasons.

title: Timing of nitrogen mineralisation from cover crop residues and its synchrony with maize nitrogen demand in Vojvodina
abstract: This study combined a field incubation approach with the nitrogen uptake curve of maize to assess synchrony between nitrogen supply from cover crop residues and crop demand. Hairy vetch monocultures and 50:50 hairy vetch/winter rye mixtures were incorporated in three termination windows: late March, mid-April and early May, over 2013–2016. Net mineralised nitrogen was estimated from KCl-extractable mineral nitrogen in polyethylene-covered microplots. A synchrony index (SI) was calculated as the ratio of cumulative mineral nitrogen available during the grand growth period (V6–VT) to maize total seasonal uptake requirement (180 kg N ha⁻¹). SI was highest for the mid-April hairy vetch termination (SI = 0.58) and lowest for late March winter rye mixture (SI = 0.19). Late termination of high-legume mixtures most closely matched the maize uptake curve but increased the risk of delayed sowing. A decision tool for selecting termination date based on accumulated degree-days is presented.

title: Quantifying the microclimate penalty of narrow-strip intercropping for organic pepper production: a multi-site assessment across Vojvodina
abstract: Four certified organic farms across Vojvodina were instrumented with identical sensor networks (quantum sensors, thermocouple psychrometers, leaf wetness plates) during the 2024 growing season. Pepper–onion strip intercrops of 0.6 m and 1.2 m strips were compared with sole-crop pepper at each site. Data from 112 sensor-days were pooled and analysed with a mixed model accounting for site as a random effect. Narrow 0.6 m strips increased cumulative leaf wetness duration by a mean of 31 % and Botrytis cinerea incidence by 16 percentage points relative to sole-crop controls, while 1.2 m strips showed no significant increase in either variable. The microclimate penalty was strongest at the farm with the densest surrounding hedgerow structure, suggesting that wind environment interacts with strip geometry. Farmers reported yield advantages from the 1.2 m design consistent with weed suppression without a disease penalty, supporting adoption under organic management constraints.

title: Timing Analysis of ISO 11783 Message Scheduling on Low-Cost ARM Cortex-M3 Microcontrollers
abstract: This paper examines the timing behaviour of the ISO 11783 transport protocol (TP) and working-set maintenance messages when implemented on an ARM Cortex-M3 microcontroller running at 72 MHz with a bare-metal scheduler. Measurements were conducted using a custom CAN bus test bench consisting of three ECU nodes and a CANalyzer logging unit. Worst-case response times for address-claim procedures, process-data objects, and ETP multi-packet frames were recorded over 10 000 bus cycles under simulated load from a virtual terminal and a task controller. Results show that address-claim collisions increase worst-case latency by up to 38% compared to uncontested scenarios, and that standard FreeRTOS priority assignment does not meet all timing constraints under simultaneous TP and ETP traffic. A revised priority mapping scheme is proposed and validated experimentally, reducing deadline misses from 4.1% to 0.3% in the test configuration.

title: Comparative Evaluation of ISOBUS Conformance Test Suites for Aftermarket Task Controllers
abstract: ISO 11783 conformance testing is carried out by accredited laboratories using proprietary test suites, but aftermarket ECU developers frequently rely on open-source or self-developed tools whose coverage is incomplete. This paper documents a structured comparison of three freely available ISOBUS test frameworks against the official AEF conformance test specification version 3.2, focusing on the task controller (TC-BAS, TC-SC, TC-GEO) server functionality. Each framework was applied to the same firmware image running on a prototype TC ECU, and discrepancies in test outcomes were logged across 247 individual test cases. The open-source tools missed 31 to 59 failure conditions identified by the reference suite, primarily in section 9 multi-section control and DDOP version negotiation. The analysis highlights specific gaps and proposes a supplementary test script library written in Python and distributed under an MIT licence that closes 24 of the identified gaps.
