title: Gateway Architectures for Mixed ISO 11783 and SAE J1939 Networks in Multi-Implement Tractor Configurations
abstract: Modern tractors often expose both an ISOBUS (ISO 11783) connector and a diagnostic SAE J1939 backbone, and integrating implements that assume one standard with a tractor that exposes only the other is a recurring problem for fleet operators. This dissertation chapter surveys five gateway topologies — transparent bridge, selective filtering, protocol translation, store-and-forward, and hybrid — and evaluates them against criteria of latency, bus load, configurability, and failure isolation. Experimental data were collected using a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test bench comprising a dSPACE MicroAutoBox (fictional equivalent: TechSim RapidECU) and three CAN channels. Results indicate that selective-filtering gateways provide the best latency profile (median 1.4 ms end-to-end) but require per-installation configuration, whereas store-and-forward designs tolerate baud-rate mismatches at the cost of a 6–12 ms additional delay. A decision matrix is offered to guide implementation choices based on application requirements.

title: Object Dictionary Management Across Multiple CANopen Device Profiles in Distributed Seeding Machines
abstract: Pneumatic seed drills for row crops increasingly carry sensors and actuators from multiple vendors, each conforming to different CANopen device profiles (DS406 encoders, DS408 drives, DS401 I/O). Managing the resulting heterogeneous object dictionary landscape on a central master node is a non-trivial firmware engineering problem. This paper presents a dynamic object dictionary framework implemented on an STM32H7 master node that loads device-specific sub-dictionaries at run-time from CRC-verified flash partitions. The framework was validated on a 24-row seed drill with 72 CANopen nodes operating at 1 Mbit/s over a 6-metre cable harness. SDO access times remained below 3 ms for 98.7% of read operations across 48 hours of bench testing. The paper also reports on node guarding and heartbeat event timing under conditions where three or more nodes are simultaneously reinitialised, which is common during headland turns.

title: Latency Profiling of ISOBUS Virtual Terminal Sessions over Extended CAN Harnesses Using Differential Probing
abstract: ISOBUS virtual terminal (VT) responsiveness degrades measurably on long cable runs typical in articulated combine harvesters and road-train configurations. This paper reports a systematic profiling study in which a VT client ECU communicating with a server was tested over harness lengths from 1 m to 40 m at 250 kbit/s, with termination resistance varied between 100 Ω and 130 Ω. Differential voltage probing at seven bus positions provided eye-diagram data alongside software-layer timing logs captured with microsecond resolution. Softkey and numeric-input response latencies increased by 18–34 ms on the 40 m harness compared to 1 m baselines, primarily attributable to ACK-bit timing margin erosion causing retransmissions. Improvements achieved by replacing standard 0.35 mm² twisted pair with 0.5 mm² screened cable and repositioning terminators to within 2 m of end nodes are quantified. The study provides guidance for harness design in large-format machinery.

title: A Lightweight ISOBUS Task Controller Client Stack for Microcontrollers with 64 kB Flash
abstract: Most open-source ISOBUS TC client implementations target MCUs with at least 256 kB of flash, which excludes a large class of low-cost sensor ECUs used on small farm implements in developing or budget-constrained markets. This paper describes the design and verification of a TC-BAS client stack written in C99 that compiles to 47.2 kB on a Cortex-M0+ target at -Os optimisation, leaving adequate space for application code. Design decisions including static DDOP allocation, integer-only arithmetic for device-descriptor encoding, and a two-state process-data pump are detailed. The stack was integrated into a prototype section-control module for a 6 m boom sprayer and tested against four commercial task controllers using the AEF plugfest procedure. Interoperability was confirmed with all four controllers for TC-BAS functionality; two edge cases in setpoint handling were identified and resolved during testing. Code is available on a public repository.

title: Evaluation of FD-CAN for High-Speed Sensor Aggregation in ISOBUS-Connected Implements
abstract: CAN FD (flexible data rate) has been standardised but is not yet part of ISO 11783, leaving implement designers who require high sensor data throughput with an interoperability gap. This paper evaluates a hybrid architecture in which an implement-internal FD-CAN backbone at 2 Mbit/s data phase aggregates data from 18 soil-sensing nodes, while a translation ECU presents the aggregated values to the ISOBUS backbone at 250 kbit/s in standard-frame format. The translation ECU uses a Renesas RH850-based prototype board. Round-trip delay from sensor sampling to task-controller reception was measured at 4.7 ms median and 11.2 ms at the 99th percentile under full network load. Bus utilisation on the ISOBUS segment remained below 38% even during simultaneous VT and TC sessions. Limitations due to DDOP element count restrictions in TC-BAS profiles when representing 18 sensors are discussed.

title: Interoperability Testing Methodology for ISOBUS AUX-N Function Assignments Across Implement Generations
abstract: The ISOBUS Auxiliary Control (AUX-N) service allows operators to assign joystick or button inputs from one ECU to functions on another. In mixed fleets combining implements manufactured over a decade-long span, AUX-N assignment tables stored in VT memory frequently produce mismatches after ECU replacement or firmware updates. This paper presents a structured testing methodology for AUX-N interoperability using a scripted test harness that replays 320 assignment sequences across four VT server implementations and six auxiliary-input-unit firmware versions. The study found that 41% of tested pairings produced at least one incorrect preferred-assignment restore after a power cycle, and that the root cause in most cases was differing interpretations of the AUX-N object UID persistence rules in the standard. Recommended firmware practices for UID management are described and an errata proposal for ISO 11783-6 is outlined.

title: FPGA-Based Analog Front-End Emulation for Knock Sensor Signal Generation in Engine HiL Testing
abstract: Knock sensors produce broadband vibration signals in the 5–15 kHz range that engine ECUs process through bandpass filters and envelope detectors to identify combustion knock events. Emulating these signals accurately on a HiL bench requires waveform generation with sufficient bandwidth and amplitude resolution. This work presents an FPGA-based waveform generator implemented on an Artix-7 device that produces synthetic knock and non-knock signals based on parameterised cylinder pressure traces from a four-cylinder naturally aspirated engine model. The generator uses a 16-bit DAC at 250 kS/s per channel and a lookup-table synthesis approach with four independently configurable channels. Signal quality was assessed by comparing spectra from the emulated output against recordings taken from a motored engine on a dynamometer test bench. Spectral flatness error within the 5–15 kHz band was below 1.8 dB. An ECU under test correctly classified knock events in 97.3% of 600 injected test cases. The paper details the fixed-point filter coefficients, DAC interface timing, and calibration procedure.

title: Floor vibration survey in a manufacturing hall: spectral content and dominant excitation sources at sub-100 Hz
abstract: Precision optical instruments installed on industrial floors are sensitive to vibration at frequencies from roughly 1 Hz to 100 Hz. This paper reports a systematic measurement campaign conducted in an automotive component assembly hall in Novi Sad over four working days. Triaxial MEMS accelerometers were deployed at 24 grid points; simultaneous records were collected during normal production, reduced production, and shutdown periods. Power spectral densities were estimated using Welch's method with 50 % overlapping Hann windows and 8192-point FFTs. Dominant peaks at 12.5 Hz and 47 Hz were traced to a conveyor drive unit and a hydraulic press, respectively. RMS acceleration levels during full production reached 18 mg vertically and 9 mg horizontally at measurement points within 6 m of the conveyor. Coherence analysis showed that press-induced excitation propagated coherently up to 22 m from the source. The spatial attenuation data and spectral maps produced here are intended to support isolation platform sizing in subsequent work.

title: Gelatin methacrylate hydrogels with tunable stiffness as substrates for neonatal rat cardiomyocyte culture
abstract: This study characterised a series of gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) hydrogels with compressive moduli ranging from 3 kPa to 22 kPa, prepared by varying monomer concentration (5–15 wt%) and UV exposure time (20–120 s). Neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes were seeded at 1.5 × 10⁵ cells/cm² and maintained for 14 days. Cell viability exceeded 85% across all formulations at day 7 assessed by live/dead fluorescence. Spontaneous beating frequency was highest on 8–12 kPa substrates (62 ± 7 beats/min), while cells on 3 kPa gels showed irregular contractile activity and poor sarcomere alignment. Immunofluorescence for α-actinin revealed sarcomere spacing of 1.82 ± 0.09 μm on optimal substrates, comparable to values reported for isolated adult cardiomyocytes. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed uniform pore architecture between 30 and 80 μm in diameter depending on crosslinking conditions. The results indicate that substrate stiffness in the physiological myocardial range significantly influences early contractile phenotype and sarcomere organisation in cultured cardiomyocytes.

title: Incorporation of reduced graphene oxide flakes into gelatin hydrogels to improve electrical conductivity and cardiomyocyte coupling
abstract: Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) flakes at loadings of 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 mg/mL were blended into 10 wt% GelMA solutions prior to photocrosslinking. Bulk electrical conductivity measured by four-point probe rose from 0.004 S/m (plain GelMA) to 0.031 S/m at 1.0 mg/mL rGO. Tensile modulus increased proportionally from 9.2 to 14.6 kPa. Neonatal rat cardiomyocytes seeded on 0.5 mg/mL rGO-GelMA composites showed synchronised beating across culture areas of 4 mm² within 48 hours, compared with asynchronous activity on plain GelMA. Cx43 gap junction immunostaining area per cell was 38% greater on rGO composites relative to plain GelMA controls. Cytotoxicity assessed by caspase-3 activation showed no significant elevation at 0.5 mg/mL. The 0.5 mg/mL formulation was identified as providing an acceptable balance between electrical performance, mechanical stiffness, and cytocompatibility for use in stimulation-based maturation protocols.

title: Comparative assessment of three hydrogel backbone chemistries for long-term cardiomyocyte viability under continuous electrical stimulation
abstract: Gelatin methacrylate, hyaluronic acid methacrylate (HAMA), and polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogels were each prepared at a compressive modulus of approximately 10 kPa. hiPSC-CMs were embedded at 2 × 10⁶ cells/mL and stimulated continuously at 1 Hz for up to 28 days. Live/dead quantification at days 7, 14, 21, and 28 showed viability above 80% only in GelMA and HAMA constructs; PEGDA constructs dropped to 61% viable by day 21. Metabolic activity by alamarBlue assay showed a plateau in PEGDA from day 14 onwards, while GelMA and HAMA constructs maintained linear increases. Contractile force measurements using a custom cantilever array recorded peak twitch forces of 0.48 ± 0.09 μN (GelMA), 0.39 ± 0.07 μN (HAMA), and 0.18 ± 0.05 μN (PEGDA) at day 28. GelMA was identified as the preferred backbone for long-term stimulation studies due to its integrin-binding RGD motifs supporting sustained cell–matrix interaction.

title: A desktop-fabricated carbon electrode array for applying uniform electric fields across multi-well cardiomyocyte cultures
abstract: A stimulation chamber accommodating standard 24-well plates was constructed from laser-cut acrylic frames holding paired carbon-rod electrodes in each well at a fixed separation of 10 mm. Field uniformity across the well floor was characterised by finite-element simulation and validated by potential mapping with a microelectrode array, showing less than 8% spatial variation in field magnitude at 5 V/cm. The device was driven by a custom pulse generator outputting biphasic square pulses adjustable from 0.1 to 5 Hz with pulse widths from 1 to 10 ms. Total materials cost per unit was approximately 140 EUR. Comparison of cardiomyocyte calcium transient amplitudes in wells at four positions within the plate showed no statistically significant difference (one-way ANOVA, F = 1.24, p = 0.31), confirming plate-to-plate and position-to-position reproducibility. The design files and firmware were deposited in an open repository to support replication at other laboratories.

title: Maturation state of hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes modulates their sensitivity to isoproterenol: a calcium imaging study
abstract: hiPSC-CMs were cultured on rGO-GelMA substrates and subjected to either a standard 7-day electrical stimulation protocol (1 Hz) or left unstimulated. On day 14, both groups were exposed to isoproterenol at concentrations from 1 nM to 10 μM. Calcium transients were recorded with Fluo-4 AM at each concentration step. Stimulated, more mature cells showed a positive chronotropic response with an EC50 of 18 ± 4 nM and a maximum beat-rate increase of 42%, closely matching values reported for adult atrial tissue. Unstimulated, less mature cells had an EC50 of 130 ± 22 nM and a smaller maximum response of 27%. Hill coefficients were 1.1 and 0.8, respectively. These data indicate that maturation state substantially shifts β-adrenergic pharmacology in hiPSC-CM cultures and that stimulated substrates are better suited to drug-response studies than standard unstimulated controls.

title: Ramp-up versus constant-frequency electrical stimulation for accelerated cardiomyocyte maturation: a controlled comparison
abstract: Two electrical stimulation regimens were applied to hiPSC-CMs embedded in 10 wt% rGO-GelMA (0.5 mg/mL rGO) over 14 days. In the ramp-up protocol, frequency increased from 0.5 Hz on day 1 to 2 Hz by day 7 and was held at 2 Hz through day 14. In the constant protocol, 1 Hz was maintained throughout. Fourteen maturation markers were assessed including sarcomere length, MYH7/MYH6 transcript ratio by RT-qPCR, calcium transient rise and decay kinetics, peak twitch force, and SERCA2a and RyR2 protein levels by western blot. The ramp-up group showed significantly higher MYH7/MYH6 ratio (4.1 vs. 2.7), longer sarcomere length (1.94 vs. 1.86 μm), and faster calcium transient decay (tau 180 vs. 230 ms) compared with the constant group. Peak twitch forces were 0.61 ± 0.11 μN versus 0.44 ± 0.09 μN. No difference was observed in cell viability. The ramp-up protocol was adopted as the group's standard conditioning regimen for subsequent studies.

title: Integration of collagen type I microfibers into GelMA hydrogels to mimic endomysial architecture and its effects on cardiomyocyte contractile function
abstract: Aligned collagen type I microfibers were electrospun onto a temporary PVA sacrificial layer and transferred into 10 wt% GelMA precursor solution before photocrosslinking, yielding composite hydrogels with fibers oriented within ±15° of a principal axis. Fiber diameters averaged 1.2 ± 0.3 μm. Composite gel stiffness along the fiber axis measured 13.1 kPa versus 9.8 kPa in the transverse direction, providing mild mechanical anisotropy. hiPSC-CMs seeded on composite gels aligned preferentially along fiber direction with an orientation index of 0.78 ± 0.04. After 14-day ramp-up electrical stimulation, contractile force measured with the cantilever array averaged 0.74 ± 0.13 μN in the fiber-aligned direction, 54% greater than in plain rGO-GelMA constructs. Passive tension at 10% stretch was 0.22 ± 0.04 μN. Histology showed cell elongation and nuclear aspect ratios of 3.4 ± 0.5, approaching values seen in adult tissue sections.

title: Calcium transient heterogeneity as a metric of maturation homogeneity in hiPSC-CM monolayers: image analysis methodology
abstract: A custom image analysis pipeline written in Python was developed to quantify spatial heterogeneity of calcium transient parameters across hiPSC-CM cultures imaged with Fluo-4 AM. The pipeline segmented individual cells from time-lapse fluorescence stacks, extracted per-cell ΔF/F₀, time-to-peak, and decay tau, and computed their coefficients of variation as a maturation homogeneity score. Validation was performed on 48 culture wells from three independent experiments with known stimulation histories. Coefficient of variation in decay tau correlated with MYH7/MYH6 ratio across wells (Pearson r = −0.74, p < 0.001), indicating that more mature cultures also displayed more uniform calcium handling. Analysis time per well was reduced from approximately 4 hours using manual methods to 8 minutes. The pipeline was made available under an open-source licence. Inter-operator reproducibility for segmentation was assessed by intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC = 0.91) across three operators.

title: Dose-dependent effects of doxorubicin on contractile force and calcium transient kinetics in electrically matured hiPSC-CM constructs
abstract: Electrically conditioned hiPSC-CM constructs in rGO-GelMA scaffolds were exposed to doxorubicin at 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, and 5.0 μM for 48 hours. Contractile force was measured by cantilever deflection and calcium transients by Fluo-4 AM imaging at baseline and at 6, 24, and 48 hours post-treatment. At 1.0 μM, twitch force declined to 51 ± 9% of baseline by 48 hours. Calcium transient amplitude decreased proportionally, while decay tau lengthened from 182 ± 18 ms to 271 ± 24 ms at 1.0 μM. Cell viability by SYTOX Green showed 72% survival at 1.0 μM and 38% at 5.0 μM. IC50 for force loss was estimated at 0.85 μM. Recovery experiments with a 48-hour washout at 0.5 μM showed partial force recovery to 78% of baseline by 24 hours post-washout. The assay distinguished doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity from baseline variability with a Z-factor of 0.62, indicating suitability for screening applications.

title: Benchmarking contractile force measurement approaches for thin hydrogel cardiac constructs: cantilever arrays, traction force microscopy, and optical fibre sensors
abstract: Three contractile force measurement methods were applied to identical hiPSC-CM constructs embedded in 10 wt% GelMA at 10 kPa, stimulated under the group's standard ramp-up protocol for 14 days. Cantilever deflection, traction force microscopy (TFM) with embedded 1 μm fluorescent beads, and a custom optical fibre Bragg grating (FBG) sensor were each used to record active twitch forces from ten independently prepared constructs per method. Mean twitch force values were 0.68 ± 0.12 μN (cantilever), 0.61 ± 0.15 μN (TFM), and 0.70 ± 0.11 μN (FBG), with no statistically significant difference between methods (one-way ANOVA, p = 0.18). Measurement bandwidth was highest for FBG (2 kHz), enabling resolution of individual contraction phases. TFM provided spatially resolved force maps but required 40 minutes of post-processing per construct. The cantilever method offered the best trade-off between throughput and precision for routine screening applications in the group's workflow.

title: Optical emission spectroscopy of N2–H2 glow discharges at pressures between 2 and 8 mbar: identification of active species and gas temperature estimates
abstract: A DC glow discharge in N2–H2 mixtures (25–75 vol% H2) was characterised by optical emission spectroscopy (OES) over a pressure range of 2–8 mbar and a current density range of 0.5–3.0 mA cm−2. Rotational temperatures were derived from the second positive system of N2 (C³Πu→B³Πg) and the first negative system of N2+ using a Boltzmann plot method applied to 12 rotational lines. At 4 mbar and 1.5 mA cm−2 the rotational temperature was found to be 620 ± 30 K, rising to 810 ± 40 K at 8 mbar. NH emission intensity at 336 nm increased linearly with hydrogen fraction up to 50 vol% H2 and then saturated. Atomic nitrogen line intensities at 746 and 821 nm tracked discharge current closely but were weakly dependent on pressure in the studied range. The data provide a baseline for correlating discharge chemistry with nitriding layer growth rates measured simultaneously by in situ quartz crystal microbalance on AISI H13 coupons placed at the cathode surface.

title: Effect of cathodic current density on the compound layer structure of plasma-nitrided AISI D2 tool steel
abstract: AISI D2 cold-work tool steel specimens were plasma-nitrided in a 75% N2 / 25% H2 atmosphere at 520 °C for 4 h while systematically varying cathodic current density from 0.8 to 4.0 mA cm−2. Cross-sectional X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (SEM/EDX) were used to characterise the compound layer and diffusion zone. At current densities below 1.5 mA cm−2 the compound layer was exclusively γ'-Fe4N; above 2.5 mA cm−2 a mixed γ'/ε phase was observed. Compound layer thickness increased from 2.1 μm at 0.8 mA cm−2 to 6.8 μm at 4.0 mA cm−2. The diffusion zone depth, measured by microhardness profiling in 10 μm steps, was relatively insensitive to current density and ranged from 145 to 165 μm. Vickers surface hardness increased from 850 HV0.1 for the lowest current to 1020 HV0.1 for the highest, correlated with the growing ε-phase fraction. The results indicate that current density is a more decisive parameter for phase composition than treatment duration under these conditions.

title: Langmuir probe measurements in a planar cathodic glow discharge at elevated pressure: comparison with OES-derived electron densities
abstract: Electron density and electron temperature in a DC glow discharge sustained between parallel-plate electrodes (inter-electrode gap 30 mm) were measured with a cylindrical Langmuir probe (tungsten, 0.2 mm diameter, 5 mm length) at pressures of 3–7 mbar in pure nitrogen. Orbital-motion-limited (OML) theory was applied to current–voltage sweeps acquired at 500 Hz to suppress cathode-fall perturbations. Electron densities were in the range 1.5–4.8 × 10¹⁵ m−3 and electron temperatures 1.8–2.6 eV over the studied conditions. The same discharge was characterised simultaneously by OES using the ratio of N2 (C→B, 0-0 band) to N2+ (B→X, 0-0 band) intensities as a proxy for Te. Agreement between probe- and OES-derived electron temperatures was within 15%, while the absolute electron densities differed by up to a factor of two, attributed to probe contamination by nitrogen adsorption and probe-current-induced discharge perturbation. A correction procedure based on periodic probe cleaning cycles is proposed and validated.

title: Plasma nitriding of AISI H11 hot-work tool steel: influence of treatment temperature on wear and fatigue resistance
abstract: AISI H11 hot-work die steel was plasma-nitrided at temperatures of 480, 520, and 560 °C for 6 h in a 70% N2 / 30% H2 mixture at 4 mbar. Wear resistance was evaluated by pin-on-disc testing against an Al2O3 ball (5 N load, 0.1 m s−1, 1000 m sliding distance) and fatigue resistance by rotating-bending tests on un-notched specimens at 800 MPa stress amplitude. The compound layer was removed by grinding prior to fatigue testing to isolate the diffusion zone contribution. Nitriding at 520 °C produced the best wear performance, with a specific wear rate of 1.2 × 10−6 mm3 N−1 m−1 compared with 4.8 × 10−6 mm3 N−1 m−1 for the untreated reference. Fatigue life improved by a factor of 2.1 at 520 °C relative to the reference, whereas the 560 °C sample showed only a 1.4-fold improvement due to surface roughening and partial compound layer spallation observed in SEM. Residual stress profiles measured by sin²ψ X-ray diffraction confirmed compressive stress maxima of −320 MPa at 520 °C.

title: Mass spectrometric sampling of a N2–H2 glow discharge through the cathode fall: ion composition as a function of gas mixture and pressure
abstract: A differentially pumped quadrupole mass spectrometer was coupled to a DC glow-discharge reactor through a 50 μm orifice drilled in the nitriding cathode. Ion energy-resolved mass spectra were acquired for N2–H2 mixtures containing 10–90 vol% H2 at pressures of 2, 4, and 6 mbar and a fixed current density of 1.5 mA cm−2. The dominant positive ion at all conditions was N2+ (m/z 28), constituting 55–70% of total ion current, followed by N+ (m/z 14) and NH4+ (m/z 18) whose relative abundances grew with increasing H2 fraction. At 50 vol% H2 the NH4+/N2+ ratio was 0.18 at 2 mbar and 0.31 at 6 mbar, indicating three-body recombination pathways become significant at higher pressures. N2H+ (m/z 29) appeared as a minor species, accounting for 2–5% of total ion current independent of hydrogen fraction. The ion energy distributions were narrow (FWHM ≈ 1.5 eV) for all identified species. These ion flux data are correlated with nitrogen uptake rates measured by weighing steel coupons treated under identical conditions.

title: Active screen plasma nitriding of PM tool steel Vanadis 10: layer uniformity and microstructural characterisation
abstract: A laboratory active screen plasma nitriding (ASPN) reactor was built and used to treat powder-metallurgy cold-work tool steel Vanadis 10 specimens. The active screen was a cylindrical cage of AISI 304 stainless steel mesh powered at 600 V DC; specimens rested on a floating potential table inside the cage. Treatments were performed at 510 °C for durations of 2, 4, and 8 h in 75% N2 / 25% H2 at 4 mbar. Compared with direct DC plasma nitriding under identical thermal conditions, ASPN produced more uniform compound layer thickness (standard deviation across specimen surface ≤ 0.4 μm vs. 1.8 μm for DC) and no hollow-cathode arcing on sharp edges and holes. XRD showed predominantly γ'-Fe4N for all durations; ε-phase fraction stayed below 8 vol% even at 8 h. Hardness profiles indicated a case depth of approximately 200 μm after 8 h. The temperature uniformity inside the screen cage was ±8 °C, measured by four type-K thermocouples.

title: Plasma nitriding parameter optimisation for AISI M2 high-speed steel using a response surface methodology
abstract: A Box-Behnken design with three factors — temperature (480–540 °C), pressure (3–7 mbar), and H2 fraction (20–60 vol%) — was applied to plasma nitriding of AISI M2 high-speed steel with treatment duration fixed at 5 h. Seventeen experimental runs were conducted in a randomised order. Response variables were surface hardness (HV0.05), compound layer thickness, and diffusion zone depth. Second-order polynomial models were fitted to each response with adjusted R² values of 0.94, 0.91, and 0.88, respectively. The interaction between temperature and hydrogen fraction was statistically significant (p < 0.01) for both surface hardness and compound layer thickness. Optimal conditions for maximum surface hardness (1210 HV0.05) with a compound layer below 3 μm were identified at 515 °C, 4.5 mbar, and 45 vol% H2. Analysis of the fitted surfaces reveals that temperature is the dominant factor, accounting for 61% of the explained variance in hardness. The optimised parameters were validated in three confirmation experiments with results within 4% of predicted values.

title: Absolute nitrogen atom densities in a DC N2–H2 glow discharge by two-photon absorption laser-induced fluorescence: comparison with actinometry
abstract: Absolute ground-state nitrogen atom densities were measured in a DC glow discharge in a 60% N2 / 40% H2 mixture at 4 mbar using two-photon absorption laser-induced fluorescence (TALIF) calibrated against xenon as a reference gas. Measurements were performed at five axial positions between the cathode sheath edge and the plasma bulk at current densities of 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 mA cm−2. Absolute N atom densities in the bulk plasma ranged from 3.2 × 10¹⁹ m−3 at 1.0 mA cm−2 to 7.8 × 10¹⁹ m−3 at 2.0 mA cm−2, with a pronounced density minimum approximately 5 mm from the cathode sheath edge consistent with dissociative recombination at the sheath boundary. Actinometry using trace argon (1 vol%) overestimated N atom density by 35–50% compared with TALIF, a discrepancy attributed to non-proportionality between Ar and N excitation rate coefficients at low electron temperatures in this pressure range. The TALIF data were used to calculate N-atom surface fluxes at the nitriding cathode, yielding values of 1.1–2.6 × 10²¹ m−2 s−1.

title: Cross-border radon potential mapping in the Pannonian Basin: harmonisation of measurement protocols between Serbia, Hungary and Romania
abstract: Consistent radon potential mapping across national borders in the Pannonian Basin has been hampered by differences in measurement protocols, detector calibration and reporting conventions. This paper describes a harmonisation exercise conducted under a trilateral research agreement involving three national institutions. Fifty-four co-located measurement sites were equipped with both the Serbian standard passive CR-39 system and the soil-gas syringe-plus-electret ion chamber system used in Hungary, as well as the Romanian ionisation chamber approach. Measurements were made simultaneously over a 90-day period at each site. Inter-method agreement was within ±15 % for 80 % of sites; systematic offsets were identified for the electret system in high-clay soils and corrected via a site-specific calibration factor. The paper presents a recommended common protocol for future cross-border surveys, a conversion table between the three national reporting units and a preliminary merged radon potential map for the study region covering approximately 18 000 km². The merged dataset reduces the number of interpolation artefacts at borders by 60 % compared to nationally-produced maps.

title: Мезбауерова спектроскопија и рендгенска дифракција лесних узорака из профила Стари Сланкамен: поређење са Тителском лесном зараван
abstract: У раду су упоређени резултати Мезбауерове спектроскопије и рендгенске прашкасте дифракције за узорке лесно-палеоземљишне секвенце из профила Стари Сланкамен (Срем) и профила на Тителској лесној заравни (Бачка). Анализирано је укупно 48 узорака, при чему су трансмисиони Мезбауерови спектри снимљени на собној температури и на 77 K. Однос гетит/хематит у палеоземљишним хоризонтима је на профилу Стари Сланкамен у просеку за 18% нижи него на Тителском профилу за исте изотопске етапе, што може указивати на локалне разлике у дренажним условима или различиту прашкасту провенијенцу. Рендгенска анализа показује да садржај кварца и плагиокласа варира у оквиру ± 3% између два профила, те се разлике у Gt/Hm вероватно не могу приписати провенијенци. Резултати указују да су локалне геоморфолошке разлике значајан извор варијабилности при регионалним палеоклиматским корелацијама заснованим на Fe-оксидним прокси параметрима.

title: Lab-on-chip platforms for biological sample processing: microfluidic principles and device construction
abstract: This chapter provides a didactic account of the physical principles underlying continuous-flow and digital microfluidic lab-on-chip platforms, with emphasis on droplet-based approaches. Coverage includes the fluid mechanics of droplet generation at T-junction, co-flow, and flow-focusing geometries; scaling of viscous, capillary, and inertial forces at the micron scale; fabrication of PDMS, glass, and PCB substrates; and electrowetting-on-dielectric actuation principles. Practical considerations in device testing, surface treatment, and electrode design are discussed with reference to published experimental data from the authors' laboratory. The chapter concludes with a comparative assessment of platform suitability for nucleic acid amplification, immunoassay, and cell encapsulation applications, drawing on literature up to 2014. Intended for graduate students and researchers entering the microfluidics field without a dedicated engineering background.

title: Heat dissipation and irreversibility in driven granular gases: a simulation study
abstract: We report event-driven molecular dynamics simulations of a two-dimensional granular gas of 2000 inelastic hard disks in a rectangular cell with vibrating walls. The coefficient of restitution is varied from 0.6 to 0.99 in steps of 0.01. We compute the spatial distribution of dissipated power and compare it with kinetic-theory predictions based on the homogeneous cooling state. Clusters form spontaneously for restitution coefficients below 0.85, and the dissipation field becomes strongly inhomogeneous, deviating from the homogeneous prediction by up to 60% in local density. The entropy production density, estimated via the Kullback–Leibler divergence between time-forward and time-reversed trajectory ensembles, is shown to localise at cluster boundaries. Cluster merger events produce transient spikes in global entropy production roughly three times the steady-state value. These findings suggest that standard mean-field kinetic theory substantially underestimates irreversibility in the clustering regime and motivate spatially resolved corrections.

title: Comparing Fidelity of Local Surrogate Explanations Across Ensemble Classifiers on Tabular Credit Data
abstract: Local surrogate models such as LIME approximate the behaviour of a black-box classifier in the neighbourhood of a single prediction. This paper examines how faithfully LIME surrogates represent random forests, gradient-boosted trees, and bagged decision trees when applied to a tabular credit-scoring dataset of 42,000 anonymised loan applications from a regional bank. Fidelity is measured as the mean squared error between surrogate predictions and original model predictions across 5,000 randomly sampled neighbourhoods. Results show that fidelity deteriorates substantially for gradient-boosted models with shallow trees (mean MSE 0.09) compared with random forests (0.04), and that the choice of neighbourhood kernel width is the single largest source of variance. The paper proposes a cross-validated kernel width selection procedure that reduces mean MSE by 31% without modifying the underlying classifier. Experiments are repeated on two publicly available UCI datasets to assess generalisability.

title: Auditing a Public Sector Candidate Screening Tool for Disparate Impact Across Protected Groups
abstract: Automated resume screening tools are increasingly used in public sector hiring in Central and Eastern Europe. This paper describes an audit of a commercially deployed screening system used by two Serbian municipal institutions, conducted using a shadow-testing protocol in which synthetic candidate profiles were submitted to the system in a controlled manner. Protected attributes covered include gender, age group, and settlement type (urban/rural). Disparate impact is measured using the four-fifths rule and a logistic regression parity gap analysis. The audit finds that candidates listed as residing in rural areas receive rejection recommendations at a rate 1.7 times higher than urban-equivalent profiles with identical qualifications. Gender-based disparities are smaller but statistically significant for technical roles. The paper discusses audit methodology limitations, including the inability to inspect internal model weights, and proposes a public disclosure checklist for procuring authorities. No proprietary data are published; only aggregate statistics are reported.

title: A Benchmark of Post-Hoc Explanation Methods for Neural Networks on Structured Healthcare Data
abstract: The paper systematically benchmarks six post-hoc explanation methods — LIME, SHAP (TreeSHAP and KernelSHAP), integrated gradients, LOCO, and permutation importance — applied to three feed-forward neural networks predicting 30-day hospital readmission from structured electronic health record data. The dataset comprises 18,400 adult inpatient episodes from a regional hospital, with 47 numeric and categorical features. Evaluation criteria include fidelity to the original model, runtime, and agreement between methods (measured by pairwise rank correlation of feature attributions). KernelSHAP and integrated gradients show the highest fidelity (R² > 0.91) but differ substantially in attribution agreement (ρ = 0.61 on average), suggesting that method choice materially affects which features appear important. Runtime for KernelSHAP scales quadratically with background dataset size, making it impractical above 500 background samples on the available hardware. Practical recommendations for clinical informatics teams are provided.

title: Intersectional Bias in Automated Decision Systems: Measurement Challenges and a Decomposition Approach
abstract: Most fairness metrics assess bias with respect to one protected attribute at a time, but real-world discrimination often operates across intersecting characteristics. This paper proposes a decomposition framework that partitions a classifier's total parity gap into single-attribute components and pairwise interaction terms using an ANOVA-style analysis. The framework is applied to a synthetic population generator calibrated against Serbian Labour Force Survey statistics, producing 100,000 hypothetical job applicant profiles. Three classifiers trained on the synthetic data — logistic regression, a gradient-boosted tree, and a neural network — are audited. Interaction terms account for 18–27% of total demographic parity gap depending on the model, with the gender × age interaction consistently the largest. The paper provides an open-source R package implementing the decomposition and discusses the statistical power required to detect interaction effects reliably in datasets of realistic size.

title: Explainability Methods for Time-Series Classification: Adapting SHAP to Temporal Feature Structures
abstract: SHAP values are well understood for tabular data, but their application to time-series classification raises questions about how to define meaningful coalitions of temporal features. This paper examines three strategies for grouping time steps into coalitions — contiguous windows, wavelet-band grouping, and learned segment boundaries — and compares their effect on explanation quality when applied to a univariate industrial sensor dataset (vibration readings from a compressor, 8,400 samples, 120 time steps each) used to classify fault types. A convolutional neural network trained on this data achieves 91.4% classification accuracy. Explanation quality is assessed via a deletion metric: progressively masking features identified as important and measuring accuracy drop. Window-based grouping with an adaptive overlap procedure produces the steepest accuracy-deletion curve, suggesting higher explanation relevance. Computational cost remains manageable; full SHAP estimation takes under 4 minutes per batch on a mid-range GPU.

title: Explainable AI in Regulated Industries: A Practitioner's Guide to Selecting Post-Hoc Methods
abstract: This book chapter surveys the landscape of post-hoc explainability methods from the perspective of practitioners working under regulatory constraints, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation and forthcoming AI Act provisions. The chapter organises methods along two axes: the level of explanation (local versus global) and the type of model assumption (model-agnostic versus model-specific). For each category, the chapter discusses what the method can and cannot guarantee about faithfulness to the underlying model, what documentation artefacts can be derived from it, and what computational resources are typically required. Case studies drawn from credit risk, insurance underwriting, and automated triage are used to illustrate trade-offs. The chapter concludes with a decision flowchart intended to help compliance teams select a suitable explanation approach given their model class, data type, and regulatory reporting requirements. No new empirical results are presented.

title: Evaluating Consistency of SHAP Explanations Across Model Retraining Cycles in Production Systems
abstract: Machine learning models deployed in production are periodically retrained on new data. Each retraining cycle may produce a model with similar predictive performance but different internal structure, potentially yielding different SHAP explanations for the same input. This paper quantifies explanation drift — the change in SHAP value vectors for a fixed set of 1,000 held-out test instances across 12 monthly retraining cycles — for a gradient-boosted tree model used in a fictional financial services context. Explanation drift is measured as the cosine distance between SHAP vectors before and after retraining and as rank-order correlation of feature attributions. Over 12 cycles, mean cosine distance accumulates to 0.18, and the top-three feature set changes for 31% of instances. The paper proposes a monitoring statistic based on median cosine distance that can trigger a fairness and explainability re-audit when it exceeds a threshold calibrated on a held-out validation window.

title: Fairness Auditing of a Municipal Social Benefit Allocation Algorithm: Methodology and Findings
abstract: This paper reports an external fairness audit of an automated scoring system used by a mid-sized Serbian municipality to prioritise applicants for a means-tested housing assistance programme. The audit was conducted under a data access agreement and covered 6,800 applications submitted over three years. The system's scoring formula is partially transparent; audit access included the scoring code but not training data. Demographic data were obtained by linking application records with census microdata using approximate matching. Four fairness criteria are evaluated: demographic parity, equalised odds, calibration, and individual fairness via a similarity metric defined over observable financial features. The system satisfies demographic parity at the aggregate level but exhibits an equalised odds gap of 0.11 between applicants of Roma and non-Roma ethnicity, driven largely by differential error rates in the income imputation sub-module. Remediation options including re-calibrating the imputation model and adding an ethnicity-blind income proxy are discussed with their legal and operational implications.

title: Comparing Global Surrogate Model Complexity and Accuracy Trade-offs for Regulatory Reporting
abstract: Global surrogate models fit a simple interpretable model (typically a shallow decision tree or linear model) to the input-output behaviour of a complex black box. Regulatory frameworks increasingly require that institutions provide comprehensible model documentation, making surrogate depth and fidelity a practical engineering choice. This paper systematically varies surrogate tree depth from 2 to 12 and measures fidelity (R² and area under the ROC curve relative to the black-box labels) and comprehensibility (number of leaves, depth, and a human-rated clarity score from a panel of 20 domain experts) across five datasets. A Pareto frontier analysis identifies depth-4 and depth-5 trees as consistently near-optimal across both dimensions. The paper further tests whether fidelity improvements from increasing depth beyond 6 are statistically significant using a permutation test, finding that they rarely are for datasets under 50,000 instances. Recommendations for regulatory documentation templates are included.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for SHAP Values: A Bootstrap Confidence Interval Framework
abstract: SHAP values are typically reported as point estimates, but any estimate derived from a finite sample carries uncertainty that is rarely communicated to end users or auditors. This paper develops a bootstrap-based confidence interval framework for KernelSHAP and TreeSHAP, estimating interval width as a function of background dataset size, model complexity, and input point location in feature space. Experiments on four tabular datasets (ranging from 3,000 to 120,000 instances) show that 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for individual feature attributions are wide enough to include zero for the second and third ranked features in 44% of cases with background sets of 100 samples, dropping to 18% with 1,000 samples. The paper provides guidelines for minimum background set size under different desired interval widths and discusses implications for audit reports that rely on single-run SHAP estimates. An accompanying Python library implements the interval estimation.
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research

title: Embedded Wavelet Lifting for ECG Compression on Wearable Cortex-M0 Nodes
abstract: Electrocardiogram data transmitted from chest-patch wearables place a disproportionate load on BLE bandwidth. We ported a fixed-point integer lifting-scheme wavelet transform (5/3 Le Gall filter) to an ARM Cortex-M0 running at 48 MHz and paired it with a simple threshold quantiser and arithmetic coder. The implementation stores all intermediate coefficients in 12 kB of SRAM, fitting within the budget of low-cost microcontrollers. Compression was evaluated on 30-minute, two-lead recordings from 18 subjects sampled at 500 Hz. The scheme achieved a mean compression ratio of 9.4:1 at a percent root-mean-square difference (PRD) of 2.7%, which is within the clinically acceptable range for rhythm monitoring. QRS peak locations in reconstructed signals deviated by a mean of 1.2 ms from reference annotations. Runtime was 1.8 ms per 500-sample frame, leaving the processor idle for 64% of each sampling period. Power consumption during active compression was 3.1 mW.

title: Modelovanje sorpcionih izotermi međuvlažnih konditorskih sistema na bazi suve šljive primenom GAB modela
abstract: U radu su određene sorpcione izoterme za tri komercijalna konditorska proizvoda na bazi suve šljive sa različitim sadržajem dodanog šećera (15, 25 i 35 % m/m) pri temperaturama od 15, 25 i 35 °C i rasponu aktivnosti vode 0,11–0,90, korišćenjem statičke metode zasićenih rastvora soli. Na eksperimentalne podatke primenjen je GAB model, čiji su parametri (Cm, C i K) određeni nelinearnom regresionom analizom. Vrednost Cm kretala se od 6,8 do 9,3 g/100 g suve materije i opadala je s povećanjem temperature, dok je parametar C pokazao suprotan trend. Utvrđeno je da povećanje udela šećera statistički značajno snižava ravnotežni sadržaj vlage pri aktivnostima vode ispod 0,60. Model je validovan na nezavisnom skupu podataka sa relativnom greškom manjom od 4 %. Rezultati ukazuju da GAB model adekvatno opisuje sorpciono ponašanje ovih sistema i mogu poslužiti kao osnova za projektovanje uslova pakovanja i skladištenja.

title: Glass transition temperatures of dried apricot and quince products as influenced by water content and sugar composition
abstract: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to determine glass transition temperatures (Tg) for dried apricot and quince-paste products containing 10–35 % (w/w) total soluble solids, at moisture contents ranging from 8 to 22 g/100 g dry basis. Tg decreased from 42.3 °C to −18.7 °C for apricot and from 38.1 °C to −22.4 °C for quince as moisture content increased, consistent with plasticization by water. The Gordon–Taylor equation fitted the data well (R² > 0.97), yielding k-values of 4.8 and 5.2 for apricot and quince, respectively. Fructose-dominant sugar profiles were associated with lower Tg values compared to glucose-dominant samples at equivalent moisture content, suggesting a compositional effect on structural relaxation. Practical implications for minimum safe storage temperatures and packaging specifications are discussed. A safety margin of at least 10 °C above ambient temperature was recommended to maintain glassy-state stability during summer storage in the Western Balkans region.

title: Uticaj cikličnih promena relativne vlažnosti na teksturna svojstva i aktivnost vode sušenih bresaka tokom skladištenja
abstract: Sušene breskve (aw 0,52–0,56) izložene su cikličnim promenama relativne vlažnosti (55 % RH–75 % RH–55 % RH) u klimatizovanim komorama na 25 °C tokom 12 nedelja. Aktivnost vode merena je instrumentom sa kapacitivnim senzorom (Rotronic HC2-AW) na svake dve nedelje, a tekstura instrumentalnom analizom na teksturometru (test kompresije, 75 % deformacije). Nakon dva ciklusa (8 nedelja) zabeležen je porast aw za 0,06 jedinica i smanjenje čvrstoće tkiva za 23 % u poređenju sa kontrolnim uzorcima čuvanim pri stalnoj relativnoj vlažnosti od 55 % RH. Povratna desorpcija nije bila potpuna, što ukazuje na histerezis od 0,03–0,04 aw jedinice. Mikrostrukturne promene potvrđene su skenirajućom elektronskom mikroskopijom (SEM). Rezultati ukazuju da se u uslovima sezonskih fluktuacija relativne vlažnosti karakterističnih za region Vojvodine mogu očekivati značajne promene senzornih i fizičkih svojstava proizvoda koji nisu zaštićeni parnom barijerom.

title: Water activity and glass transition interplay in sugar-based confectionery gels: effect of polyol humectants
abstract: The combined influence of glycerol, sorbitol and propylene glycol (0–12 % w/w) on water activity and glass transition temperature was investigated in pectin-based confectionery gels with total soluble solids content of 65–72 °Brix. Water activity was measured by chilled-mirror dewpoint (Aqualab 4TE) and glass transition by DSC (heating rate 5 °C/min, second heating scan). All three humectants reduced aw at equivalent concentrations, with glycerol showing the greatest effect (Δaw = −0.07 per 4 % addition). Glass transition temperatures dropped markedly with humectant addition, reaching −35 °C at 12 % glycerol compared to −19 °C in the humectant-free reference. Moisture sorption isotherms showed that humectant-containing gels absorbed less water at elevated relative humidity (75 and 85 % RH), indicating improved moisture barrier properties. A predictive model combining aw and Tg as dual stability criteria is proposed and validated against independent samples, achieving prediction errors below 6 % for shelf-life end-point estimation at 20 and 30 °C.

title: Određivanje kritične aktivnosti vode za kristalizaciju u modelnim sistemima konditorskog punjenja na bazi invertnog šećera
abstract: Kristalizacija je jedan od glavnih uzroka kvarenja konditorskih punjenja na bazi invertnog šećera pri neodgovarajućim uslovima skladištenja. U ovom radu identifikovana je kritična aktivnost vode za nukleaciju i rast kristala saharoze i fruktoze u modelnim sistemima sa 60, 65 i 70 % ukupnih rastvorenih materija. Uzorci su izloženi uslovima aw 0,55–0,85 pri 20 i 30 °C tokom osam nedelja. Pojava kristalizacije praćena je diferencijalnom skenirajućom kalorimetrijom, merenjima entalpije topljenja i vizuelnom kontrolom pod polarizacionim mikroskopom. Kritična aw za saharozu iznosila je 0,72 pri 20 °C i 0,68 pri 30 °C za sistem sa 65 % suve materije, dok je za fruktozu iznosila 0,78 odnosno 0,74. Porastom temperature kritična aw se smanjivala za sve sisteme, što ukazuje na termičku labilizaciju amorfo-kristalnog ravnoteže. Predložen je dijagram stabilnosti koji može biti primenjen pri formulisanju recepata i definisanju uslova pakovnja.

title: Primena dinamičke sorpcije para (DVS) u karakterizaciji higroskopnosti sušenog groždja i suvih smokava
abstract: Higroskopnost sušenog groždja (sultanina) i suvih smokava ispitana je metodom dinamičke sorpcije para pri 20 i 35 °C u opsegu 0–90 % RH, korišćenjem instrumenta DVS Advantage (SMS, London). Analiziran je uticaj stepena sušenja (aw 0,45, 0,55 i 0,65), kao i tretmana površine (uljani premaz u poređenju s netretiranim uzorcima). Sultaninice su pokazale brže uravnoteženje i veće ukupno primanje vlage (do 42,3 g/100 g suve materije pri 90 % RH) u poređenju sa smokvama (31,7 g/100 g), što se pripisuje višem udelu fruktoze. Uljani premaz smanjio je brzinu primanja vlage za 35 % u prvoj fazi sorpcije ali nije promenio ravnotežni kapacitet. Histerezisna petlja bila je šira kod uzoraka sa nižom početnom aw, sugerirajući veće strukturno preuređenje pri rehidrataciji. Kinetički parametri sorpcije prilagođeni su Fickinom modelu difuzije sa efektivnim koeficijentima difuzivnosti u opsegu 1,2–4,8 × 10⁻¹⁰ m²/s.

title: Predicting shelf-life endpoints of intermediate-moisture plum confections using a combined water activity–glass transition stability map
abstract: A stability map integrating water activity (aw) and glass transition temperature (Tg) was constructed for three traditional Serbian plum confection formulations (šljivovača, šljivin pekmez-bonbon and sugar-coated dried plum) with varying sucrose-to-glucose-syrup ratios. Products were stored at 20 and 30 °C under cyclic RH conditions (50–70 % RH, 2-week cycles) for up to 24 weeks. Aw was monitored weekly; Tg was measured by DSC at weeks 0, 8, 16 and 24. Shelf-life endpoints were defined as the first week at which aw exceeded 0.70 or Tg dropped below ambient temperature. Products at ambient temperature fell below the glassy state threshold after 10–14 weeks at 30 °C and 70 % RH, while those at 20 °C remained stable for the full 24-week trial. The stability map correctly predicted endpoint week within ±1 week for 11 of 12 product-condition combinations. The map is presented as a practical tool for small and medium food producers in the region who lack access to extensive shelf-life testing facilities.

title: Uticaj fluktuacija relativne vlažnosti tokom transporta na fizičkohemijsku stabilnost voćnih grickalica na bazi jabuke i dunje
abstract: Voćne grickalice na bazi jabuke i dunje (aw 0,50–0,58) praćene su tokom simuliranog transporta koji uključuje tri klimatske zone (hladna/suva skladišna zona na 15 °C/40 % RH, topla/vlažna zona na 28 °C/75 % RH i zona klimatizovanog kamiona na 20 °C/55 % RH). Svaka tranzicija trajala je 48 sati, a ukupna trajanje simulacije iznosila je 18 dana. Mereni su: aktivnost vode (kapacitivni senzor), boja (kolorimetrija, CIE L*a*b*), čvrstoća (instrumentalna teksturalna analiza) i stepen kristalizacije (DSC). Aktivnost vode oscilirala je u opsegu 0,11 aw jedinica između zona, a konačna aw bila je za 0,04 viša od polazne vrednosti. Čvrstoća se smanjila za 18 % kod uzoraka od jabuke i 12 % kod uzoraka od dunje. Promene boje (ΔE > 3) zabeležene su samo kod uzoraka jabuke izloženih vlažnoj zoni dulje od 48 sati. DSC analizom nije utvrđena rekristalizacija u nijednom uzorku, što ukazuje da temperatura u svim zonama nije premašila Tg + 10 °C.

title: Water plasticisation of amorphous lactose–fructose blends relevant to fruit-dairy confectionery coatings
abstract: Binary amorphous mixtures of lactose and fructose (molar ratios 1:1, 2:1 and 1:2) were prepared by freeze-drying and characterised by DSC and dynamic vapour sorption at 20 and 30 °C. The Gordon–Taylor model was extended to three-component systems by incorporating water as a third plasticiser, with k-parameters fitted separately for each binary pair. Tg decreased from 78 °C (dry 1:1 blend) to −26 °C at 15 g/100 g moisture content. Water uptake at 75 % RH was highest for fructose-rich blends (29.4 g/100 g) and lowest for the 2:1 lactose-rich blend (22.1 g/100 g). A critical moisture content below which the glassy state was maintained at 25 °C was identified as 8.3 g/100 g for the 1:1 blend. These results are directly applicable to formulation of fruit-dairy coated wafer and biscuit products, for which the coating layer is the primary site of moisture-induced quality loss. Predictive accuracy of the extended Gordon–Taylor model was within 3 °C across all compositions and moisture levels tested.

title: Kinetika strukturnih promena u sušenim šljivama na temperaturi staklo–guma prelaza: praćenje DMA i DSC metodama
abstract: Sušene šljive sorte Čačanska rodna (aw 0,54 ± 0,01) podvrgnute su izotermnoj inkubaciji na temperaturama od 20, 25, 30 i 35 °C radi praćenja kinetike strukturnih relaksacija u blizini temperature staklo–guma prelaza metodama dinamičko-mehaničke analize (DMA, frekvencija 1 Hz) i diferencijalne skanerske kalorimetrije. Tg određena DSC metodom iznosila je 27,4 ± 1,2 °C za dati sadržaj vlage. DMA merenja pokazala su postepen pad modula skladištenja (E') od 1,8 × 10⁶ Pa na 20 °C do 4,2 × 10⁴ Pa na 35 °C. Kinetika relaksacije opisana je Williams–Landel–Ferry (WLF) modelom sa konstantama C₁ = 14,2 i C₂ = 51,8 K. Aktivaciona energija strukturnih promena iznosila je 98,4 kJ/mol. Rezultati potvrđuju da su šljive u gumastom stanju na temperaturama iznad 28 °C pri datom sadržaju vlage, što se poklapa s uslovima letnjeg skladištenja u Vojvodini i predstavlja kritičan faktor za dizajn ambalažnih rešenja.

title: Comparative moisture buffering capacity of natural and modified atmosphere packaging for intermediate-moisture dried berry products
abstract: Dried cranberry and blueberry products (aw 0.53–0.57, moisture content 16–18 g/100 g) were packed in four packaging systems: (1) oriented polypropylene (OPP), (2) OPP with silica gel sachet, (3) modified atmosphere (MAP, 70 % N₂/30 % CO₂) in metallised film, and (4) MAP with silica gel sachet. Packs were stored at 20 °C under programmed RH cycling (50–75 % RH, 4-week cycle) for 32 weeks. Headspace RH, product aw, and sorption isotherm parameters were tracked at 8-week intervals using chilled-mirror dewpoint and DVS. Silica gel sachet packages maintained aw within 0.03 units of initial values for 24 weeks; MAP without desiccant showed aw drift comparable to OPP after 16 weeks (Δaw +0.06). The combination of MAP and silica gel was the only system maintaining aw below 0.60 throughout the 32-week trial. Glass transition temperatures remained above ambient temperature only in the combined MAP–silica gel system, suggesting this is the minimum packaging specification for maintaining glassy-state stability during long-distance distribution of premium dried berry products.

title: Particle Formation of Lycopene-Enriched Extracts by Supercritical Antisolvent Precipitation
abstract: Lycopene-enriched tomato extract obtained by supercritical CO₂ extraction was subjected to supercritical antisolvent (SAS) precipitation using dichloromethane as the liquid solvent and CO₂ as the antisolvent at pressures of 100–200 bar and temperatures of 35–55 °C. Particle size, morphology, and crystallinity were characterised by laser diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and powder X-ray diffraction. At 150 bar and 40 °C, mean particle diameter was 2.1 ± 0.4 µm with a narrow size distribution (span 0.9). Lycopene content in particles was 47 mg/g dry weight, and all-trans isomer content was maintained above 89% as confirmed by HPLC. Encapsulation efficiency was 76%. Dissolution rate tests in simulated intestinal fluid showed a 2.3-fold increase in bioaccessibility compared with unprocessed extract. The SAS conditions were reproducible across five consecutive runs with less than 5% variability in particle size.

title: A Comparison of Linearisation Strategies for the DC Optimal Power Flow Problem on Radial Distribution Networks
abstract: This paper examines three linearisation approaches for the DC optimal power flow (OPF) problem applied to radial distribution networks with 33 to 118 buses. The approaches considered are the standard B-theta formulation, a piecewise-linear loss approximation, and a current-injection reformulation. Test cases are drawn from publicly available IEEE benchmark systems as well as a synthetic 87-bus network derived from a regional Serbian distribution operator's anonymised data. Computational experiments are carried out using CPLEX 12.6 on a single-core workstation. For the 33-bus case, all three methods produce solutions within 0.4% of the nonlinear AC benchmark; for the 118-bus case, the piecewise-linear loss approximation reduces the optimality gap to 1.1% compared with 2.8% for the B-theta method. Solution times remain below 0.9 seconds in all linearised cases. The results suggest that loss approximation quality, not computational cost, is the binding constraint when selecting a linearisation strategy at this network scale.

title: Warm-Start Strategies for Interior-Point Solvers in Repeated Optimal Power Flow: A Case Study on Intraday Rescheduling
abstract: In intraday electricity market operations, the optimal power flow problem must be solved repeatedly over a rolling horizon with small changes in load and generation forecasts between successive instances. Cold-starting an interior-point solver for each instance wastes computation that could be avoided by exploiting the solution to the previous instance. This paper evaluates four warm-start strategies—direct primal initialisation, primal-dual initialisation, perturbation-based central path restoration, and an SOCP-derived starting point—on a sequence of 96 OPF instances representing a 24-hour day with 15-minute resolution on a 57-bus test network. Metrics are iteration count, time to feasibility, and total CPU time. Primal-dual initialisation reduces mean iteration count by 38% relative to cold start; the SOCP-derived strategy achieves the best total CPU time, a 51% reduction. The gains diminish when forecast changes between consecutive instances exceed 12% of peak load.

title: Branch-and-Bound with SOCP Bounds for Unit Commitment in Small Island Systems
abstract: Unit commitment in isolated island power systems involves small numbers of generating units but tight operational constraints arising from lack of interconnection and high renewable penetration. This paper formulates the problem as a mixed-integer second-order cone program and implements a customised branch-and-bound algorithm in which node relaxations are solved as SOCP subproblems. Branching is guided by a pseudo-cost rule calibrated on a set of 200 training instances. The algorithm is benchmarked against a standard MIP formulation solved with a commercial solver (Gurobi 9.1) on 15 test instances representing a 12-unit, 24-hour horizon with 30% wind penetration. The proposed method closes the root-node gap from 4.7% to 1.9% through SOCP tightening alone and finds a feasible integer solution on average 2.3 times faster than the baseline. Memory overhead remains moderate at below 400 MB for the largest instances tested.

title: Sensitivity of SOCP Relaxation Quality to Network Parameter Uncertainty in Low-Voltage Distribution Grids
abstract: Parameters of low-voltage distribution cables—resistance, reactance, and rated capacity—are often known only approximately in practice, particularly for older infrastructure. This study quantifies how uncertainty in these parameters affects the tightness of the SOCP relaxation of the branch flow OPF model. A Monte Carlo experiment is run over 5,000 parameter perturbation samples for each of three 52-bus low-voltage test feeders. Resistance uncertainty of ±15% increases the mean relaxation gap from 0.08% to 0.31%; reactance uncertainty of the same magnitude has a smaller effect, raising the gap to 0.19%. Correlation between resistance and reactance errors, as occurs when cable cross-section is misrecorded, amplifies the gap further to 0.47%. The results motivate tighter data-collection standards and suggest that a robust SOCP formulation with ellipsoidal parameter uncertainty sets may be worth developing for grids with poor asset records.
venue: Proceedings of the 12th Symposium on Mathematical Optimisation in Engineering, Novi Sad

title: Real-Time Feasibility Recovery for AC Optimal Power Flow Solutions Obtained from SOCP Relaxations
abstract: When the SOCP relaxation of the AC OPF is not exact, the relaxed solution is infeasible for the original nonlinear problem. Recovering a nearby feasible AC solution quickly is essential for real-time dispatch applications. This preprint proposes and compares three recovery procedures: (1) a single Newton–Raphson power flow solve with SOCP outputs as initialisation, (2) a penalty-based nonlinear programming step using IPOPT warm-started from the SOCP point, and (3) a projection onto the AC feasible set via successive linear approximations. On a test suite of 80 instances derived from 14-, 57-, and 118-bus networks with varying load levels and renewable injection profiles, the IPOPT warm-start procedure achieves feasibility recovery in under 0.4 seconds on average and produces solutions within 0.9% of the AC OPF optimum in 77 of 80 cases. The successive linear projection method is faster (0.11 seconds) but fails to recover feasibility in 9 cases with high renewable variability.
venue: arXiv preprint, arXiv:2603.14872

title: Rigorous Enclosures for Linear ODE Systems with Uncertain Coefficients via Müller's Theorem
abstract: Linear ODE systems whose coefficient matrices are only known to lie within an interval matrix arise naturally in circuit simulation, structural dynamics, and control. This paper applies Müller's monotonicity theorem to derive analytic bounds on the solution set and compares these bounds with those produced by direct interval Taylor integration. For coefficient matrices with interval radius up to 5% of the spectral norm, Müller bounds are tighter than Taylor-model enclosures by a median factor of 2.3 across 18 test cases drawn from circuit simulation netlists. For larger uncertainties the comparison reverses. A hybrid algorithm that selects the tighter enclosure automatically is implemented and tested. The paper also provides a formal characterisation of the subclass of interval matrices for which Müller bounds are guaranteed to be non-explosive over unbounded time intervals.

title: Passive Inference of Regular Tree Languages from XML Document Corpora
abstract: Finite tree automata generalise string automata to tree-structured inputs. This paper extends the RPNI state-merging strategy to infer regular tree automata from corpora of XML documents treated as ordered labelled trees. We evaluate the approach on three real-world XML corpora: a collection of 9,400 bibliographic records, a set of 4,200 configuration files, and a corpus of 7,800 scientific article metadata documents. Ground-truth schemas expressed as Document Type Definitions (DTDs) are used as reference models. The inferred tree automata correctly accepted 96–99% of held-out valid documents and rejected 88–93% of artificially corrupted counterexamples across the three corpora. Merging order heuristics modelled on EDSM are shown to reduce the size of the inferred automaton by 15–30% compared to canonical RPNI ordering. Running times remain below two minutes on a commodity workstation for all corpora tested.

title: Spatial copula modelling of extreme precipitation fields over the Carpathian–Pannonian region using max-stable processes
abstract: Spatial risk assessment of extreme precipitation requires models that capture both the marginal behaviour at individual sites and the spatial dependence structure across the region. Max-stable processes provide a coherent framework for this task. Daily precipitation records from 62 stations in Hungary, Romania, Croatia and Serbia for the period 1971–2015 were obtained from national meteorological services. Marginal generalised extreme value parameters were estimated at each station, and three max-stable models — Smith, Schlather and Brown–Resnick — were fitted by pairwise composite likelihood. The Brown–Resnick model with an empirically estimated variogram was selected by the composite likelihood information criterion. Extremal coefficients between station pairs indicate that stations separated by more than 180 km are effectively independent for annual maximum daily precipitation. Areal reduction factors derived from the fitted model differ by up to 25 percent from those currently used in regional design guidelines.

title: Kinetics of Mn(II) Oxidation by Dissolved Oxygen on Naturally Formed MnOx Filter Coatings
abstract: The oxidative removal of dissolved manganese in granular filter beds depends critically on the catalytic activity of MnOx coatings that accumulate on filter grains during operation. This study quantified the surface-catalysed oxidation rate of Mn(II) in a bench-scale quartz-sand column operated at pH 7.2–8.0, dissolved oxygen 3–9 mg/L, and inlet Mn(II) concentrations of 0.2–2.5 mg/L. Rate data were fitted to a Langmuir–Hinshelwood model, yielding an apparent surface rate constant of 4.1 × 10⁻³ L·m⁻²·min⁻¹ at pH 7.5 and 20 °C. Activation energy was estimated at 38 kJ/mol from experiments at 10, 20 and 30 °C. Coating characterisation by XRD and BET showed birnessite-type MnO₂ with specific surface area increasing from 12 to 74 m²/g over 180 days of filter ripening. Effluent Mn concentrations fell below 0.05 mg/L after 45 days of continuous operation. The results support a two-step autocatalytic mechanism and provide parameters suitable for reactor design models.

title: Effect of pH and Carbonate Alkalinity on Iron(II) Oxidation Rates in Aerated Groundwater
abstract: Iron removal from groundwater by aeration and filtration is well established, yet the inhibitory role of carbonate species on Fe(II) oxidation kinetics remains incompletely characterised under conditions typical of the Vojvodina aquifer system. Batch oxidation experiments were conducted at pH 6.5–8.5, total alkalinity 1–8 meq/L, temperature 15 °C, and initial Fe(II) concentrations of 0.5–8 mg/L. Dissolved oxygen was maintained at saturation throughout. Second-order rate constants decreased from 8.2 × 10¹³ to 1.4 × 10¹³ L·mol⁻¹·min⁻¹ as alkalinity increased from 1 to 8 meq/L at pH 7.5, consistent with competitive complexation of Fe(II) by carbonate ligands reducing the reactive hydroxo-Fe(II) fraction. A modified rate law incorporating a carbonate inhibition term reproduced 91% of variance across all conditions. Practical implications for cascade aeration design serving high-alkalinity Vojvodina wells are discussed.

title: Column Breakthrough Behaviour of Arsenic(V) in Iron-Oxide-Coated Sand Beds: Influence of Competing Anions
abstract: Iron-oxide-coated sand (IOCS) prepared by co-precipitation on quartz grains was tested for As(V) removal in fixed-bed columns at superficial velocities of 5–15 m/h and bed depths of 30–90 cm. Feed water contained 50–200 µg/L As(V) with variable concentrations of phosphate (0–2 mg/L) and silicate (0–20 mg/L) as competing anions. Thomas and Bohart–Adams models were fitted to breakthrough curves; Thomas rate constants ranged from 2.1 to 6.8 × 10⁻⁴ mL·µg⁻¹·min⁻¹ depending on flow rate and competitor loading. Phosphate at 1 mg/L reduced bed capacity by 38%, while silicate at 10 mg/L caused a 19% reduction. SEM-EDX confirmed As surface loading up to 1.8 mg/g on exhausted media. Results indicate that IOCS columns are feasible for rural groundwater treatment in Serbia but require pre-dephosphatisation when P exceeds 0.5 mg/L.
venue: Desalination and Water Treatment Research

title: Comparative Performance of Quartz Sand, Anthracite, and Pyrolusite Filter Media for Simultaneous Fe and Mn Removal
abstract: A pilot study compared three single-medium and two dual-medium filter configurations for removing Fe(II) (3–6 mg/L) and Mn(II) (0.5–1.2 mg/L) from a municipal well in Sremska Mitrovica over a 12-month operational period. Pyrolusite-based media achieved Mn effluent concentrations below 0.02 mg/L from the first week of operation, bypassing the ripening period required by quartz sand. Dual-medium quartz–anthracite beds showed superior turbidity removal but lagged in Mn oxidation for 60–80 days. Head loss development was 30–45% lower for anthracite-containing beds. Backwash frequency and water consumption were monitored; pyrolusite required 20% more frequent backwashing due to higher bed expansion resistance. A cost-per-cubic-metre analysis over the monitoring period favoured quartz–pyrolusite dual media for Fe/Mn combined removal when source Mn exceeded 0.8 mg/L.

title: Catalytic Decomposition of Hydrogen Peroxide on MnO₂ Pellets: Surface Deactivation Under High-Flux Conditions
abstract: MnO₂ pellets synthesised by thermal decomposition of MnCO₃ were tested as catalysts for H₂O₂ decomposition in a tubular reactor at H₂O₂ feed concentrations of 50–500 mg/L, flow rates yielding residence times of 30–300 s, and temperatures of 20–40 °C. Initial first-order rate constants ranged from 0.8 to 3.4 min⁻¹. Under sustained operation above 200 mg/L H₂O₂, surface activity declined by 60% over 72 hours, attributed to oxidative dissolution of Mn(III/IV) surface sites and re-precipitation as amorphous MnO(OH). XPS spectra before and after deactivation showed a shift in the Mn 2p₃/₂ binding energy from 642.1 to 641.5 eV consistent with partial reduction. Activity was partially restored by alkaline washing followed by re-oxidation in KMnO₄ solution. The findings are relevant to advanced oxidation pre-treatment steps coupled with aeration–filtration trains for heavy-metal groundwater remediation.

title: Modelling Dissolved Oxygen Profiles in Cascade Aerators for Groundwater Pre-Treatment: Field Validation at Three Sites in Vojvodina
abstract: A one-dimensional plug-flow mass-transfer model for dissolved oxygen (DO) re-aeration in multi-step cascade aerators was calibrated and validated against field measurements at three groundwater treatment stations in Vojvodina. Model inputs included weir geometry, step height (0.15–0.35 m), number of steps (4–8), and inlet DO (0.1–1.8 mg/L). The overall volumetric mass-transfer coefficient KLa ranged from 0.12 to 0.41 min⁻¹ across sites; a correlation with hydraulic loading rate (r² = 0.87) was derived. Outlet DO predictions deviated from measured values by less than 8% at all three sites across twelve sampling campaigns. The calibrated model was used to evaluate retrofitting options for an ageing four-step cascade needing to achieve DO > 7 mg/L for downstream biological Mn oxidation. Sensitivity analysis identified step height and flow per unit weir width as the dominant design variables.

title: Nickel and Cobalt Removal from Dilute Aqueous Streams by Oxidative Precipitation at Controlled pH: Batch and Semi-Continuous Studies
abstract: The removal of Ni(II) and Co(II) at concentrations typical of contaminated groundwater near laterite processing sites (0.1–5 mg/L each) was investigated by oxidative precipitation using KMnO₄ as oxidant at pH 7–10. In batch experiments, Ni removal exceeded 95% only above pH 9.0 regardless of oxidant dose, while Co removal reached 97% at pH 8.5 with a 2:1 molar ratio of KMnO₄ to Co. In a semi-continuous stirred tank with continuous feed and periodic sludge withdrawal, steady-state effluent concentrations of 0.03 mg/L Ni and 0.01 mg/L Co were achieved at pH 9.2 and 30-minute hydraulic retention time. Sludge characterisation by ICP-OES and TEM confirmed mixed Mn–Ni and Mn–Co oxide precipitates with mean particle sizes of 80–120 nm. The influence of Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ hardness on precipitation efficiency was minor below 400 mg/L CaCO₃ equivalent.

title: In Situ Formation of MnOx Catalysts on Zeolite Clinoptilolite Carriers for Mn(II) Oxidation in Packed-Bed Filters
abstract: Clinoptilolite from the Igroš deposit (Serbia) was evaluated as a carrier for in situ MnOx catalyst formation by sequential treatment with KMnO₄ and reduction cycling. BET surface area increased from 18 to 52 m²/g after three coating cycles; Mn loading reached 4.2% w/w as determined by acid digestion and ICP-OES. Packed columns (diameter 5 cm, bed depth 40 cm) were operated at pH 7.0–8.5 and inlet Mn(II) of 1.0 mg/L. Steady-state effluent Mn fell below 0.02 mg/L within 10 days, compared to 45 days for quartz sand controls. The catalytic first-order rate constant on coated clinoptilolite was 0.078 min⁻¹, approximately 3.4 times higher than on coated quartz under identical conditions. Mechanical abrasion tests showed acceptable grain attrition below 2% mass loss after 50 backwash cycles. The material is available locally and represents a lower-cost alternative to pyrolusite import.
venue: Applied Mineral Engineering and Water Treatment

title: Biologically Mediated Manganese Oxidation in Trickling Filter Media: Microbial Community Shifts Under Varying Hydraulic Loading
abstract: Biological Mn(II) oxidation was studied in a laboratory trickling filter packed with polyethylene biofilm carriers, operated at hydraulic loading rates of 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 m³·m⁻²·h⁻¹ with inlet Mn(II) of 0.8 mg/L at pH 7.2. 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (Illumina MiSeq) revealed a community dominated by Pseudomonas-like and Hyphomicrobium-like genera, whose combined relative abundance correlated inversely with hydraulic loading (r = −0.91). At 0.5 m³·m⁻²·h⁻¹, effluent Mn averaged 0.03 mg/L; at 2.0 m³·m⁻²·h⁻¹, it rose to 0.28 mg/L. Abiotic controls with sterilised media produced effluent Mn of 0.55–0.62 mg/L across loading rates, confirming biological contribution of 40–60% to total removal. Biomass-specific Mn oxidation rates ranged from 0.9 to 2.4 mg Mn·g VSS⁻¹·h⁻¹. The results suggest that biological and chemical pathways can be distinguished operationally using temperature and pH manipulation.

title: Pore-Scale Modelling of Reactive Transport in MnOx-Coated Filter Beds Using a Lattice-Boltzmann Approach
abstract: A two-dimensional lattice-Boltzmann model was implemented to simulate reactive transport of Mn(II) in idealized packed-bed filter geometries representing circular and angular grain assemblies at porosities of 0.35–0.45. Surface reaction was represented as a first-order boundary condition with rate constants derived from earlier experimental work. Simulated effluent concentration profiles agreed with column data within 12% root-mean-square deviation across five grain packing configurations. Local Mn(II) concentration gradients near grain surfaces reached up to 18 times the bulk concentration, indicating external mass-transfer limitation at superficial velocities above 8 m/h. The Thiele modulus was below 0.3 for grain diameters under 0.6 mm, confirming surface-reaction-limited behaviour for standard filter sands. Model outputs were used to generate dimensionless design charts relating bed depth, contact time, and target effluent Mn for operational practice.

title: Trace Barium and Strontium Removal from Drinking Water by Oxidative Softening and Filtration: Bench-Scale Assessment
abstract: Elevated barium (100–300 µg/L) and strontium (3–8 mg/L) concentrations occur in certain deep Vojvodina aquifers. Conventional lime softening and oxidative filtration were tested sequentially at bench scale to evaluate combined removal efficiency. Lime addition to pH 10.5 reduced Ba to 40–60 µg/L and Sr to 0.8–1.5 mg/L through co-precipitation with CaCO₃ and Mg(OH)₂. Subsequent MnOx-catalysed oxidation with O₂ at pH 8.0 did not further reduce Ba or Sr, confirming that oxidative filtration is ineffective for these alkaline earth metals in the absence of a redox transition. Addition of Na₂CO₃ post-softening to achieve residual alkalinity of 0.5 meq/L drove Ba to below 10 µg/L. XRD of sludge confirmed BaCO₃ (witherite) and SrCO₃ (strontianite) as minor phases co-precipitated within the CaCO₃ matrix. Sludge dewatering behaviour and disposal constraints are discussed.
venue: Water Quality and Drinking Water Research
