title: Long-Term Stability of MnOx Filter Coatings Under Intermittent Operation: A 24-Month Column Study
abstract: Filter ripening studies typically run under continuous operation, but many rural waterworks in Serbia operate intermittently, shutting down for 8–16 hours per day. A 24-month column experiment investigated how daily interruptions to flow affect the catalytic activity, physical integrity and metal retention capacity of MnOx coatings on quartz sand. Three operational schedules (continuous, 8 h off per day, 16 h off per day) were run in parallel. After 24 months, BET surface area of coatings was 71, 64, and 49 m²/g respectively, and Langmuir–Hinshelwood rate constants were 4.0, 3.6, and 2.5 × 10⁻³ L·m⁻²·min⁻¹. Mn retained within the bed increased under intermittent schedules due to partial desiccation and structural densification, raising head loss by 18% in the 16-h-off column. Coating XRD patterns shifted toward more crystalline MnO₂ phases under longer rest periods, which partly explains reduced surface area. Recommendations for minimum flushing duration before return-to-service are provided.

title: A Nagel–Schreckenberg variant with variable deceleration probabilities for single-lane arterial roads
abstract: The classical Nagel–Schreckenberg cellular automaton assigns a fixed randomisation probability to all vehicles, which tends to overestimate queue dissolution times on arterial roads with intermediate traffic densities. This paper proposes a modified rule set in which the deceleration probability is conditioned on the local density within a three-cell neighbourhood, yielding a piecewise stochastic update. Calibration was performed against 45-minute loop-detector records collected on three arterial segments in Novi Sad during morning peak hours. The modified model reduced the root-mean-square error in space-mean speed by 18% compared to the standard NS model and reproduced the empirical scatter in occupancy–flow diagrams more faithfully. Sensitivity analysis showed that the neighbourhood radius parameter had the largest influence on queue length estimates. The approach remains computationally lightweight, requiring less than 0.4 seconds of CPU time per simulated minute on a standard desktop machine, making it suitable for real-time advisory applications.

title: Saturation flow rate estimation at isolated signalised intersections using video-extracted headway distributions
abstract: Saturation flow rate is a fundamental parameter in signal timing design, yet field measurement procedures vary widely across national guidelines and introduce systematic biases. This study describes a semi-automated procedure for extracting discharge headways from overhead video recordings at four signalised intersections in Novi Sad. Frame-by-frame vehicle detection was implemented using background subtraction followed by contour tracking, with manual correction of misdetections. A total of 3,840 discharge headways were collected across 22 signal cycles. Observed headway distributions were fitted with log-normal and inverse-Gaussian models; the inverse-Gaussian provided the better fit in all four sites (p < 0.01, Kolmogorov–Smirnov test). Resulting saturation flow estimates ranged from 1,710 to 1,885 passenger car equivalents per hour per lane, lying within the range reported for comparable central European cities. The dataset and extraction scripts are made available as supplementary material.

title: Incorporating driver reaction time variability into a stochastic car-following framework for stop-and-go conditions
abstract: Most deterministic car-following models treat reaction time as a fixed parameter, whereas empirical studies report considerable inter- and intra-driver variability. This paper embeds reaction time as a Gamma-distributed random variable within a modified Gipps model and evaluates the consequences for queue formation and dissipation at a signalised intersection approach. Simulations were run for 1,000 independent replicates per scenario across three demand levels (600, 900, and 1,100 vehicles per hour). Stochastic reaction time increased the 95th-percentile queue length by 9–14% relative to the deterministic baseline and shifted the onset of overflow queuing to lower arrival rates. Rear-end conflict surrogates (time-to-collision below 1.5 s) increased by 22% at the highest demand level. The model was validated against trajectory data extracted from drone video at one intersection approach in Novi Sad. Parameter identifiability was assessed through a Morris screening experiment covering six model parameters.

title: Comparing cellular automaton and car-following approaches for the reproduction of empirical flow–density relations on urban networks
abstract: Cellular automaton and car-following models differ in their spatial discretisation and update rules, leading to different macroscopic flow–density relations even when calibrated to the same dataset. This book chapter reviews both model families and applies representative examples—a two-lane Nagel–Schreckenberg extension and the Intelligent Driver Model—to a small grid network in central Novi Sad comprising seven intersections. Both models were calibrated against 24-hour automatic traffic count data from five counting stations. The chapter presents side-by-side fundamental diagrams, network-level travel time estimates, and computational cost comparisons. The CA model underestimated travel times by 7% at peak hour while the IDM variant overestimated by 4%, suggesting complementary calibration biases. Practical guidance is offered for practitioners selecting a modelling approach based on network size, data availability, and the dominant traffic regime of interest.

title: Effect of adaptive signal control on queue length variability under stochastic arrival patterns: a cellular automaton simulation study
abstract: Adaptive signal control systems adjust green durations in response to real-time detector data, but their benefit relative to fixed-time plans depends on the degree of arrival randomness. This study uses a two-dimensional cellular automaton on a four-leg signalised intersection to compare a Webster-based fixed-time plan against a simple max-pressure adaptive scheme across Poisson and over-dispersed (negative binomial) arrival processes. Simulations were conducted for 500 independent runs of 60 simulated minutes each, at five demand levels spanning 0.6 to 1.05 volume-to-capacity ratio. The adaptive scheme reduced mean queue length by 11–19% under Poisson arrivals but by only 4–8% under over-dispersed arrivals at v/c above 0.9, suggesting that the benefit of adaptation diminishes when arrival clustering is high. Standard deviation of queue length was reduced more consistently across scenarios. Results are discussed in relation to detector placement and the polling interval of the control algorithm.

title: Microscopic modelling of mixed human–automated vehicle platoons at signalised intersections: departure headway and capacity implications
abstract: The introduction of automated vehicles into urban signalised intersections alters departure headway distributions because AVs can react to signal phase changes with shorter and less variable response times than human drivers. This paper defines three AV behaviour classes—conservative, standard, and cooperative—within a stochastic car-following framework and simulates departure processes for mixed platoons at penetration rates ranging from 0% to 100% AV in steps of 10%. Simulation runs were conducted at a calibrated single-approach model representing a high-flow intersection in Novi Sad. At 50% AV penetration, capacity increased by 8–12% depending on AV class and platoon composition; at 100% penetration the cooperative class yielded a 23% increase. However, stochastic placement of AVs within the queue produced high variance in estimated capacity at intermediate penetration rates, with coefficients of variation of 0.09–0.14. The analysis highlights that performance gains are sensitive to the assumed AV headway distribution and the degree of vehicle-to-infrastructure communication.

title: Drone-based trajectory extraction for calibrating microscopic traffic models: methodology and accuracy assessment
abstract: Drone-based video collection provides continuous trajectory data over a wider area than fixed cameras, but positional accuracy depends on camera altitude, frame rate, lens distortion correction, and geo-referencing method. This paper describes a workflow for extracting vehicle trajectories from footage recorded at 25 fps at altitudes of 40–60 m over two intersections in Novi Sad using a commercially available quadcopter. Lane-level positional accuracy was assessed by placing 24 ground control points with survey-grade GNSS equipment, yielding a mean planimetric error of 0.18 m at 50 m altitude. Extracted speed profiles were compared against independent radar gun measurements at the stop line; mean absolute error was 1.4 km/h. The paper also reports minimum detectable headway (0.6 s at the tested frame rate) and discusses the sensitivity of calibrated car-following parameters to trajectory noise via a synthetic experiment with known ground truth.

title: Influence of connected vehicle market penetration on spillback frequency in an urban grid: a cellular automaton study
abstract: Connected vehicles can broadcast their speed and position to downstream intersection controllers, potentially enabling pre-emptive signal adjustments that reduce queue spillback. This paper embeds a simplified vehicle-to-infrastructure communication layer into a two-dimensional cellular automaton representing a 3×3 urban grid, parametrised on the street network geometry of central Novi Sad. Connected vehicle penetration rates of 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100% were tested against a baseline without communication. A spillback event was defined as a queue extending beyond the upstream intersection stop line. At 25% penetration, spillback frequency decreased by 17% during peak-hour demand compared to baseline; at 50% the reduction reached 31%. Benefits were non-linear and saturated above 70% penetration under the tested communication latency of 0.3 s. Network-level mean delay decreased by up to 14% at 50% penetration, but individual intersection performance varied considerably depending on grid position.

title: Sensitivity of intersection delay estimates to car-following model parameter uncertainty under mixed human–AV traffic
abstract: Calibrated microscopic models are routinely used to estimate intersection delay for planning purposes, yet parameter uncertainty is rarely propagated through to performance indicators. This study applies a variance-based global sensitivity analysis (Sobol indices) to a stochastic car-following model of a signalised intersection approach, focusing on the transition scenario of 40% AV penetration. Eleven model parameters were varied within empirically plausible ranges derived from published trajectory datasets. Simulations comprised 4,096 parameter combinations using a quasi-random Saltelli sequence, each repeated 50 times to separate parameter uncertainty from stochastic noise. Human driver desired headway and AV minimum gap accounted jointly for 58% of the variance in mean delay, while reaction time variability contributed 14%. The AV aggressiveness parameter interacted significantly with signal offset, highlighting that delay estimates under mixed traffic are sensitive to assumptions that are difficult to validate without dedicated field data. The analysis suggests priority data collection targets for future calibration studies.

title: Stochastic green-wave coordination for mixed human–AV traffic on an urban arterial: simulation-based evaluation
abstract: Green-wave signal coordination is conventionally designed for a homogeneous stream of human-driven vehicles travelling at a target speed. The presence of AVs, which may travel at different target speeds and with tighter headways, alters the conditions under which a coordinated band accommodates the majority of through vehicles. This paper formulates green-wave optimisation as a stochastic program that accounts for the headway distribution of mixed platoons and solves it using a simulated annealing procedure. The approach is tested on a seven-intersection arterial model calibrated to conditions on a major boulevard in Novi Sad, using demand data from 2023 turning-movement counts. At 30% AV penetration, the stochastic programme increased through-band efficiency by 9 percentage points relative to a deterministic plan designed for the same arterial. Fuel consumption estimates derived from second-by-second speed profiles indicated a 6% reduction for the AV subfleet and a 2% reduction for human drivers under the stochastic plan.

title: Estimating Arterial Travel Times from Sparse Probe Vehicle Data Using Kalman Smoothing
abstract: Probe vehicles equipped with low-cost GPS loggers provide spatially distributed but temporally sparse observations of arterial travel times. This study develops a Kalman smoother framework that fuses probe observations with historical travel-time distributions derived from two years of loop detector records on four arterial corridors in Novi Sad. The state vector encodes segment travel time and its first temporal derivative. Measurement noise covariance is estimated per segment from the empirical variance of detector-derived travel times. Evaluated on held-out probe traces, the smoother achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 8.3 % compared with 13.7 % for a baseline nearest-probe interpolation. Performance degrades to 11.1 % during weekend evenings when detector coverage is sparse, motivating a hybrid fallback strategy. The paper provides a practical discussion of the tuning procedure for process noise in the absence of ground-truth vehicle counts.

title: A Middleware Architecture for Aggregating Heterogeneous Vehicle Telematics Feeds in Multimodal Urban Corridors
abstract: Urban multimodal corridors generate concurrent telematics streams from buses, trams, taxis, and freight vehicles, each using different communication protocols and update cadences. This paper describes a middleware prototype, implemented in Python and Apache Kafka, that normalises these streams into a unified positional event model with mandatory uncertainty fields. The prototype is deployed in a testbed environment connected to live feeds from two transit operators and a taxi dispatch company in Novi Sad, processing an average of 4,200 events per minute during peak hours. Latency from raw message arrival to normalised output is below 220 milliseconds at the 95th percentile under sustained peak load on commodity server hardware. The paper reports four failure scenarios observed during a six-month pilot and documents the recovery procedures implemented. Source code is published under an open licence.

title: Formalising EU Drivers' Hours Rules as a Constraint Satisfaction Problem
abstract: Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 defines a set of interlocking time constraints governing driving periods, breaks, and rest intervals for professional drivers. This paper presents a formal representation of those rules as a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP), using finite-domain variable assignment to encode driving and rest states over a rolling two-week window. The model was implemented in SWI-Prolog and validated against 112 manually annotated driver activity logs collected from a Serbian long-distance carrier. The system correctly identified the compliance status of 108 of the 112 logs, with four cases involving ambiguous multi-manning situations that required manual resolution. The paper discusses the structural complexity introduced by derogations and discusses how partial observability of cross-border rest periods complicates automated reasoning. The approach is compared to a rule-tree baseline, showing a reduction in false-positive violation flags from 14.3% to 3.6%. The work provides a formal basis for subsequent automated auditing tools.

title: Equity Implications of a Proposed Bus Network Restructuring in Novi Sad: A Before–After Isochrone Analysis
abstract: In 2016 the City of Novi Sad prepared a draft bus network restructuring plan that would consolidate 22 lines into 18 higher-frequency routes. This paper evaluates the accessibility equity implications of that plan by comparing 30-minute isochrones from every residential building polygon before and after the proposed change. Routing was performed in OpenTripPlanner using peak-hour (07:30–09:00) departure windows with 60-second resolution. A Gini coefficient of transit accessibility was computed for both scenarios, disaggregated by income quintile estimated from 2011 census housing quality indicators. The restructuring would improve median accessibility by 8.4% but increase the Gini coefficient from 0.31 to 0.34, disproportionately disadvantaging low-income tracts in the northern industrial periphery. The paper recommends three targeted line modifications to reduce this equity gap without increasing operating costs by more than 4%.

title: Latent Class Segmentation of Freight Shippers on the Danube Corridor: Identifying Preference Heterogeneity
abstract: Aggregate mode choice models often mask systematic differences in shipper preferences that are not captured by observed firm characteristics alone. This study applies latent class analysis to a dataset of 189 completed discrete choice experiments collected from Serbian and Hungarian shippers operating bulk, liquid bulk, and containerised freight on the Danube corridor. A three-class solution was selected based on BIC and interpretability criteria. Class one, representing approximately 38 percent of the sample, exhibited strong price sensitivity and near-zero valuation of transit time reduction, consistent with firms shipping homogeneous bulk commodities under relaxed delivery schedules. Class two (34 percent) showed high reliability valuation and moderate time sensitivity, corresponding to shippers of semi-finished manufactured goods. Class three (28 percent) placed the highest weight on transit time, consistent with time-sensitive cargo. Firm size and commodity type were the strongest membership predictors. The three-class structure outperformed a two-class model on both statistical and behavioural grounds.

title: Bedload transport rates in the regulated reach of the Drava River under variable discharge: field measurements and formula comparison
abstract: This paper presents bedload transport measurements collected at three cross-sections in a 14 km regulated reach of the Drava River during ten discharge events ranging from 180 to 640 m³/s. Helley-Smith sampler data were compared against estimates from five widely used transport formulae (Meyer-Peter & Müller, Wilcock-Crowe, Parker, van Rijn, and Recking). Median grain size D50 ranged from 22 to 38 mm across the reach. Results showed that the Wilcock-Crowe approach reproduced measured flux within a factor of 1.8 for the majority of events, while Meyer-Peter & Müller systematically overpredicted by up to 3.2 times under low-mobility conditions. Grain-size fractional analysis revealed selective entrainment of the 16–32 mm fraction during rising limb stages. The data set comprises 210 individual trap samples and is made publicly available. The findings support the use of surface-based mixture formulae for regulated gravel-bed rivers with armoured beds.

title: One-dimensional sediment continuity modelling of long-term bed degradation in the channelised Tisa River
abstract: A calibrated one-dimensional sediment transport model was applied to a 62 km regulated reach of the Tisa River between Kanjiža and Titel to reproduce observed bed level changes documented by cross-section surveys conducted between 1960 and 2010. The model used an advection-diffusion sediment continuity equation coupled with the Engelund-Hansen transport formula adjusted for gravel-sand mixtures. Boundary conditions included daily discharge records from three gauging stations and annual gravel supply estimates derived from historic dredging records. Simulated cumulative bed lowering at the downstream end reached 1.05 m over the 50-year period, against a surveyed value of 0.93 m. Sensitivity analysis identified sediment supply from the Hungarian reach as the dominant control on degradation rate, with a 20% reduction in upstream supply translating to an additional 0.18 m of lowering at Titel. The model was used to test two gravel nourishment scenarios showing partial recovery of bed levels.

title: Effect of hydropower peaking frequency on diel bedload flux variability in the Drina tailwater
abstract: Continuous bedload transport was inferred from high-frequency (10-minute interval) acoustic bed-level sensors deployed over 28 days in the tailwater reach 4.5 km downstream of the Bajina Bašta hydropower dam on the Drina River. Three operational periods were identified: minimum-flow base operation (Q ≈ 70 m³/s), single-peak daily operation (peak Q ≈ 310 m³/s), and double-peak operation (morning and evening peaks, Q ≈ 290 m³/s). Bedload activity, estimated via bed-level variance, was 4.7 times higher during single-peak days than during base-flow days, and 6.1 times higher during double-peak days. The lag between flow peak and peak sediment flux at the sensor cross-section averaged 42 minutes. Suspended fine gravel mobilised during each peak event had not fully redeposited before the onset of the second daily peak, resulting in net downstream export. Results are relevant for scheduling hydropower dispatch to limit geomorphic disturbance.

title: Two-dimensional morphodynamic simulation of a gravel bar in a meander bend: sensitivity to bedload formula choice
abstract: A two-dimensional depth-averaged morphodynamic model was applied to a well-documented gravel bar in a single-thread meander of the Bosut River, using field bathymetry from drone-based photogrammetry and ground-penetrating radar. The model was run with four bedload transport formulae (Meyer-Peter & Müller 1948 modified, Wilcock-Crowe 2003, Recking 2013, and Parker 1990 surface-based) over a 14-day hydrograph representing a spring flood event with peak discharge of 87 m³/s. Predicted bar head erosion volumes ranged from 1,240 m³ to 3,810 m³ depending on formula choice, a threefold spread. The Recking formula produced the best agreement with repeat survey volumes (surveyed: 2,050 m³). Secondary flow correction using the Engelund (1974) spiral flow model reduced bar-apex deposition errors by 18%. The study highlights that formula selection is the largest source of morphodynamic uncertainty for low-submergence gravel bars at moderate flood stages.

title: Grain-size response of a gravel-bed riverbed to a controlled gravel injection: 18-month monitoring on the Tara River
abstract: Following a pilot gravel injection of 4,200 m³ into the Tara River 2.1 km downstream of the Štrbački Buk reference section, bed surface grain-size distributions were monitored at six transects over 18 months using Wolman pebble counts and automated digital grain-sizing from oblique photographs. Injection grain-size was matched to the D50 of the subsurface layer (28 mm) with a slightly elevated D84 (61 mm) to increase initial stability. At month 6, median surface D50 at the injection site had increased from 19 mm (pre-injection armour D50) to 34 mm, indicating new armour formation over injected material. By month 18, the downstream-most monitoring transect (1.8 km from injection) showed a D50 increase from 17 mm to 24 mm, indicating measurable sediment wave propagation. Annual flood events with peak Q ≈ 520 m³/s drove the majority of displacement. Bedload trap measurements confirmed increased fractional transport in the 22–45 mm window during the first post-injection flood.

title: Calibrating a two-dimensional bedload transport model using drone-derived DEMs of difference: application to the Studenica River
abstract: Repeat drone photogrammetry surveys at three-week intervals over a 900 m study reach of the Studenica River produced digital elevation models with a vertical precision of ±0.04 m, enabling DEMs of difference (DoDs) that resolve volumetric change at approximately 0.1 m horizontal resolution. The DoDs were used as the calibration target for a two-dimensional Shallow Water Equations model with an active-layer sediment transport module, implementing the Wilcock-Crowe formula. Model parameters adjusted during calibration included bed roughness (Manning n), active layer thickness, and porosity. The final calibrated model reproduced 78% of the spatial pattern of erosion and deposition cells in the DoDs when evaluated using a fuzzy-logic spatial agreement index. Calibrated Manning n values ranged from 0.032 to 0.047 s/m^(1/3) across lithological units. The approach reduces reliance on bedload trap data, which is expensive to collect continuously.

title: Numerical simulation of bedload response to regulated discharge ramping rates on a Drina tailwater reach
abstract: Hydropower operators on the Drina River commonly employ discharge ramp rates of 30–80 m³/s per hour during daily peaking operations. This study applied a calibrated one-dimensional unsteady-flow sediment transport model to assess the morphological sensitivity of a 9 km tailwater reach to ramp rates ranging from 15 to 120 m³/s per hour, with all other operational parameters held constant. Simulations used 10-year daily flow sequences derived from operational records. At 120 m³/s per hour, annual net bedload output from the reach was 1.9 times higher than at 15 m³/s per hour, and bed lowering at the downstream end reached 0.31 m over the 10-year simulation versus 0.12 m. Peak shear stress events exceeding the D84 threshold occurred 38 days per year at the highest ramp rate, compared with 11 days at the lowest. The results provide quantitative input to minimum ramping rate criteria currently under development for Serbian hydropower licensing.

title: Estimating annual sediment budgets in ungauged gravel-bed tributaries of the Danube using regime morphology and LiDAR
abstract: Annual bedload budgets were estimated for eight ungauged gravel-bed tributaries entering the Serbian Danube reach between Bezdan and Novi Sad, where direct measurement is logistically constrained. The method combined (i) airborne LiDAR-derived channel geometry acquired in 2018 and 2021 with (ii) regional hydraulic geometry relationships calibrated on four gauged tributaries in the same physiographic region, and (iii) the Recking supply-limited bedload transport model driven by regionalised flood frequency curves. Estimated annual bedload contributions to the Danube from the eight tributaries ranged from 2,400 to 41,000 t/year, with the Karaš River contributing the largest share at 39%. Budget closure was tested against reach-averaged net deposition volumes in the Danube channel estimated from the LiDAR DEM difference, with agreement within 28%. Uncertainties were dominated by LiDAR point density in vegetated channel margins and the assumed proportion of bedload versus suspended bed-material load.

title: Morphodynamic modelling of gravel augmentation scenarios in the Drava River: effect of injection volume and grain-size on downstream sediment flux
abstract: A two-dimensional morphodynamic model was applied to a 28 km reach of the Drava River downstream of the Dubrava dam to compare three gravel augmentation scenarios: (A) annual injection of 15,000 m³ matching subsurface D50, (B) annual injection of 30,000 m³ matching subsurface D50, and (C) annual injection of 15,000 m³ with coarser grain-size (D50 = 1.5× subsurface). Scenarios were run over 20-year synthetic discharge series derived from stochastic modelling of the regulated flow regime. Scenario B produced the greatest reduction in net bed lowering (0.41 m over 20 years, against 0.73 m in the no-augmentation reference), while Scenario C showed an unintended increase in bedform height that locally reduced conveyance capacity by 6%. Scenario A achieved a balance between morphological improvement and manageable operational cost. Sediment injection timing relative to the annual flood peak significantly affected the distance of gravel wave propagation, with pre-flood injection increasing transport distance by 35% on average.

title: Short-term bedload flux measurement using painted tracer particles and structure-from-motion photogrammetry in a shallow gravel-bed river
abstract: A combined methodology using painted tracer particles and structure-from-motion (SfM) photogrammetry was tested during five controlled release events (peak Q = 25–110 m³/s) in the Moravica River near Ivanjica. A total of 840 painted clasts spanning five size fractions (8–128 mm) were seeded at two cross-sections. Post-event recovery surveys used a combination of manual search and overhead SfM photography processed at 2 cm/pixel resolution. Recovery rates ranged from 61 to 79% across events. Virtual velocity of tracers increased with grain size up to 45 mm and then declined, consistent with hiding effects. Short-term bedload flux was estimated by combining virtual velocity with sediment storage change from repeat SfM DEMs and compared against Helley-Smith trap measurements made simultaneously; agreement was within 22% for four of the five events. The methodology is judged suitable for reaches inaccessible to wading-based trap deployment.

title: Transferability of bedload transport model parameters between gauged and ungauged reaches: testing with leave-one-out cross-validation on Dinaric rivers
abstract: Parameter transferability is a persistent challenge when applying calibrated bedload transport models to ungauged river reaches. This study assembled a database of calibrated bedload model parameters from 19 gauged gravel-bed reaches in the Dinaric river system (Tara, Lim, Piva, Neretva, Zeta, and their tributaries), each calibrated independently against measured bedload flux data collected between 2009 and 2022. Leave-one-out cross-validation was applied: for each reach, the model was parameterised using regional regression equations derived from the remaining 18 reaches and then evaluated against withheld measurements. The Wilcock-Crowe formula with D50 and D84 of the surface layer as predictors produced median prediction errors of 0.52 log-units, comparable to typical within-reach calibration uncertainty. Including reach slope and width-to-depth ratio as additional predictors reduced median errors to 0.38 log-units. The database and regression equations are provided as supplementary material to support operational sediment modelling in the Western Balkans.

title: Influence of bed surface heterogeneity on spatially distributed bedload predictions in a braided gravel-bed reach: a preprint
abstract: Braided gravel-bed reaches pose particular challenges for spatially distributed bedload modelling because grain-size heterogeneity between braid channels, bars, and bar margins varies at scales of metres to tens of metres. This study used 3 cm/pixel hyperspectral imagery from an unmanned aerial vehicle to derive spatially continuous grain-size maps (D16, D50, D84) over a 1.4 km braided reach of the Pek River, using a convolutional neural network trained on 312 field-sampled patches. The grain-size maps were ingested into a two-dimensional morphodynamic model and compared against a baseline scenario using a single spatially uniform grain-size value. During a simulated moderate flood (Q = 145 m³/s, recurrence interval approximately 5 years), the spatially distributed grain-size model predicted 31% higher total bedload output and substantially different spatial patterns of bar head erosion, driven by locally finer material in inter-braid channels. The distributed approach also captured observed lateral bar migration more accurately than the uniform approach based on post-flood survey comparison.

title: Influence of Floor Diaphragm Stiffness on the Seismic Response of Multi-Storey Unreinforced Masonry Buildings
abstract: The effect of floor diaphragm in-plane stiffness on the lateral load distribution and failure mechanism of multi-storey unreinforced masonry buildings is examined through a parametric numerical study. Three diaphragm configurations representing timber, concrete-timber composite, and reinforced concrete slabs were modelled within a three-storey building archetype typical of Novi Sad's interwar housing stock. For each configuration, 50 nonlinear dynamic analyses were performed in OpenSees using ground motion records scaled to three intensity levels compatible with the regional hazard. Flexible timber diaphragms consistently produced asymmetric damage patterns and reduced the effective lateral resistance by 22–35% compared with rigid reinforced concrete diaphragms. The findings suggest that fragility models that assume rigid diaphragm behaviour may underestimate damage probabilities for the dominant building type in the study region. Recommendations are made for adjusting fragility curve parameters as a function of diaphragm class.

title: Vowel space compression in heritage Serbian speakers resident in English-speaking countries: a preliminary acoustic analysis
abstract: This study examines whether long-term exposure to English leads to measurable compression of the vowel space in heritage speakers of Serbian. Twenty-two adults who had emigrated from Serbia before age twelve and had been resident in the United Kingdom or Australia for a minimum of ten years were recruited via community organisations and recorded reading a standardised Serbian wordlist and a spontaneous speech task. Formant frequencies F1 and F2 were extracted for the five Serbian monophthongs using Praat and compared against a control group of twenty monolingually raised Serbian adults residing in Novi Sad. Results show statistically significant F1 lowering and F2 centralisation for the front vowels /e/ and /i/ in heritage speakers, consistent with patterns of attrition reported for other Slavic heritage languages. The back vowel /u/ showed only marginal centralisation. Degree of compression correlated positively with self-reported English dominance but not with age of emigration alone. The findings suggest that vowel attrition in Serbian is gradient rather than categorical.

title: Perception of Serbian place of articulation contrasts by English-dominant heritage speakers
abstract: Serbian distinguishes dental from alveolar fricatives and affricates at a phonological level, a contrast that English does not maintain in the same way. This study investigates whether heritage Serbian speakers who have become dominant in English retain perceptual sensitivity to these contrasts. Thirty heritage speakers (mean residence in English-speaking contexts: 14 years) and twenty-five homeland Serbian controls completed an AXB discrimination task using minimal pair stimuli synthesised and recorded by a professional phonetician. Signal-detection theory measures (d-prime) were computed for each listener. Heritage speakers showed significantly lower d-prime scores for the dental–alveolar affricate contrast than controls, while the fricative contrast remained largely intact. The pattern did not replicate the results seen in phonological production studies, pointing to a dissociation between perceptual and productive attrition. Individual differences in formal Serbian literacy correlated with better discrimination performance in the heritage group.

title: Prosodic attrition in diasporic Serbian: pitch accent realisation among heritage speakers in Vienna
abstract: Serbian has a lexical pitch-accent system that distinguishes words by tone (rising vs. falling) and quantity. This system is typologically unusual in Europe and is often reported as vulnerable to attrition. The present study recruited twenty-eight Serbian heritage speakers based in Vienna who had emigrated between ages four and fifteen and had been resident in Austria for between eight and twenty-two years. Participants were recorded producing minimal pairs contrasting the four Serbian accent types in a carrier sentence frame. Fundamental frequency contours were extracted and compared with data from thirty homeland speakers. Heritage speakers showed categorical neutralisation of the short rising vs. short falling distinction in over sixty percent of tokens; long accent distinctions were better preserved. The degree of neutralisation increased with self-rated English dominance and decreased with frequency of Serbian use at home. These results are discussed in relation to typological markedness and processing load accounts of attrition.

title: Final obstruent devoicing in heritage Serbian: production and perception in English-dominant bilinguals
abstract: Serbian, like other South Slavic languages, applies word-final obstruent devoicing obligatorily. English does not impose this constraint categorically, and voiced-voiceless contrasts in word-final position are phonemically active. This paper asks whether English dominance leads heritage Serbian speakers to weaken or lose the devoicing process. Thirty-three heritage speakers from the United Kingdom and Canada and thirty homeland controls produced one hundred and twenty target words in a reading task. Voice onset time and closure voicing measurements were made in Praat. Sixty-two percent of heritage speakers showed at least some word-final partial voicing in ostensibly devoiced obstruents, compared with three percent of homeland speakers. A follow-up perceptual experiment with the same participants suggested that partially voiced tokens were not categorically perceived as violations by heritage speakers, while homeland speakers rated them as noticeably foreign-accented. Results are consistent with phonological transfer rather than simple phonetic drift.

title: Sociolinguistic predictors of phonological attrition in Serbian emigrants: a regression study across three diaspora communities
abstract: Most acoustic studies of L1 phonological attrition focus on one community at a time, making cross-community generalisation difficult. This study assembled data from sixty-eight Serbian heritage speakers across three cities—London, Toronto, and Melbourne—recruited through Serbian cultural associations. Participants completed a sociolinguistic questionnaire measuring frequency of Serbian use, network density with other Serbian speakers, formal instruction in Serbian, affective attachment to Serbian identity, and self-rated dominance in English. A battery of acoustic tasks probed vowel space area, final obstruent devoicing, and pitch accent integrity. Multiple linear regression identified self-rated English dominance and Serbian network density as the strongest independent predictors of aggregate attrition score, while age of emigration contributed only marginally when the other variables were controlled. Formal Serbian instruction was a significant protective factor. The results have implications for community language planning in diaspora contexts.

title: Heritage language phonology and identity negotiation: qualitative evidence from Serbian speakers in Germany
abstract: Quantitative acoustic studies of attrition rarely explore how speakers themselves understand changes in their L1 phonology. This chapter draws on thirty hours of recorded sociolinguistic interviews with twenty heritage Serbian speakers living in Hamburg and Frankfurt. Speakers were aged between twenty-five and fifty-five and had emigrated between ages two and eighteen. Thematic analysis of interview transcripts identified three recurring orientations: speakers who associated phonological divergence from homeland norms with social advancement in Germany; speakers who experienced it as involuntary loss and expressed shame; and speakers who actively used modified Serbian phonology as a marker of a hyphenated identity. These stances were not consistently predicted by degree of acoustic attrition as measured in the same sessions, suggesting that phonological identity and phonological production are partly decoupled. The chapter also documents metalinguistic commentary on specific sounds, particularly the pitch accent system and the palatal consonants.

title: Coronal affricate production in Serbian heritage children in English-medium schooling: longitudinal data over two academic years
abstract: Most attrition research focuses on adult speakers; much less is known about phonological development in children who enter English-medium schooling with Serbian as their home language. This study followed twenty-one children aged five to seven in primary schools in Coventry and Nottingham over two academic years, recording them at the start and end of each year producing Serbian affricates /tʃ/, /dʒ/, /ts/, and the palatal pair /tɕ/, /dʑ/ in word-initial and medial positions. Spectral centre of gravity and duration measures were analysed. By the end of the second year, seventeen of the twenty-one children showed reduced spectral differentiation between the dental and palatal affricates. Mergers were significantly more frequent in word-medial than word-initial position. Children who received supplementary Serbian literacy instruction at a weekend school maintained significantly better contrast between the two affricate series. The study underscores the rapid pace of phonological change in early English-medium immersion.

title: Attrition or simplification? Cluster reduction in heritage Serbian across speech styles
abstract: Serbian permits complex consonant clusters that are typologically marked and have been hypothesised to be erosion-prone under attrition. This study investigated word-initial and word-final cluster reduction in forty heritage Serbian speakers in English-dominant contexts (United States and United Kingdom) compared with twenty-five homeland controls. Three speech styles were elicited: formal reading, sentence repetition, and informal narrative. Cluster reduction rates were coded from spectrograms and waveforms. Heritage speakers showed higher reduction rates than controls across all styles, but the difference was most pronounced in informal narrative, where heritage speakers produced target-like clusters only fifty-three percent of the time versus ninety-one percent for homeland speakers. The gap narrowed considerably in formal reading, suggesting style-shifting ability is preserved. The findings complicate a strict attrition framing, since the patterns partly mirror rapid speech phenomena observable even in homeland speakers, and raise questions about what counts as the attrition baseline.

title: Rhotics in transition: /r/ realisation in English-dominant heritage Serbian speakers
abstract: The Serbian trill /r/ has no close equivalent in English, and even the syllabic /r̩/ is unattested in English phonology. This makes the Serbian rhotic a plausible target for attrition. The present study analysed the production of /r/ in word-initial, intervocalic, and syllabic positions in thirty-eight heritage speakers from four countries (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia) and thirty homeland controls. Acoustic measures included trill cycle count, duration, and degree of periodicity. Heritage speakers produced fewer trill cycles on average (mean 1.4 vs. 2.8 for controls), and twenty-two percent of heritage tokens were realisations with a single brief tap or an approximant. Syllabic /r̩/ showed the most variability, with nine speakers producing vowel-like segments without any lingual trill gesture. These substitutions were most frequent in the oldest emigrants who had spent the longest time in English-dominant environments. The rhotic thus appears to be one of the more vulnerable segments in heritage Serbian phonological inventories.

title: A spoken corpus of heritage Serbian in English-dominant diaspora communities: design, collection, and annotation protocols
abstract: Systematic corpus resources for heritage Serbian are lacking, hindering reproducibility and cross-study comparison. This paper describes the design and first release of the Heritage Serbian Spoken Corpus (HSSC), which currently holds recordings from seventy-four speakers across six English-dominant host countries. Speakers completed a standard protocol including a reading passage, minimal pair production list, picture description task, and semi-structured interview. Audio was recorded at 44.1 kHz and force-aligned using an adapted Serbian acoustic model trained on the homeland Serbian broadcast corpus. The paper details the recruitment and ethical approval procedures, the annotation scheme covering orthographic transcription, broad phonetic transcription, and speaker metadata, and known limitations including sampling bias toward educated emigrants. Preliminary corpus statistics on segment durations and attrition proxies are reported. The corpus files will be made available via the repository of the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Morphological tagging of Serbian technical texts: a rule-based finite-state approach
abstract: This paper describes the construction and evaluation of a finite-state morphological tagger for Serbian, applied specifically to technical documentation in the automotive and machinery sectors. The tagger was built using the Stuttgart Finite State Transducer toolkit and a hand-crafted lexicon of approximately 48,000 lemmas with full inflectional paradigms. A test corpus of 310,000 tokens drawn from maintenance manuals and technical standards was annotated semi-automatically and then used for evaluation. The tagger achieved a lemmatization accuracy of 94.3% and a part-of-speech tagging accuracy of 91.7% on held-out data. Error analysis showed that the main source of mistakes was nominal compounds borrowed from German and not yet registered in the lexicon. The paper discusses strategies for extending the lexicon incrementally using a back-off mechanism based on suffix-stripping heuristics. Results are compared against a statistical baseline trained on a general-language corpus, which underperformed on domain-specific tokens by 6.4 percentage points.

title: Serbian–German bilingual lexical database for the engineering domain: design principles and coverage
abstract: The paper reports on the design and initial population of a Serbian–German bilingual lexical database targeted at engineering terminology. The resource encodes 12,400 term pairs extracted semi-automatically from a 4.2-million-token parallel corpus of EU-translated technical standards and verified by two domain-expert translators. Each entry stores a canonical lemma, inflectional class, syntactic valency frame, domain label, and up to three usage examples drawn from the source corpus. The database schema follows an extended version of the TermBase eXchange format to ensure interoperability with existing translation memory systems. Coverage was assessed against a reference terminology list compiled by the Serbian Standards Institute, yielding recall of 71% for core engineering concepts. The paper also discusses the treatment of multi-word terms, which account for 38% of all entries, and the specific difficulties posed by prefixal verb derivation in Serbian when mapping to German particle-verb equivalents.

title: Inflectional paradigm clustering in Serbian: implications for lexicon compression
abstract: Serbian nominal and verbal inflection presents a large number of partially overlapping paradigm classes, whose exact count and internal structure affect the size of any morphological lexicon. This study applies agglomerative hierarchical clustering to the paradigm tables of 8,700 lemmas from the Serbian Reference Lexicon project to identify natural groupings that minimize storage redundancy. Using normalized edit distance between paradigm vectors as the similarity measure, the analysis converges on 42 nominal and 27 verbal macro-classes, compared to the 104 micro-classes traditionally assumed in descriptive grammars. Compression experiments show that adopting macro-classes reduces the lexicon file size by 34% with a loss in tagging precision of less than 0.8 percentage points on a 200,000-token evaluation corpus. The paper argues that this trade-off is acceptable for resource-constrained deployment scenarios such as mobile translation assistants and lightweight corpus search tools.

title: Cross-lingual query expansion for Serbian–German document retrieval using morphology-aware translation lexicons
abstract: Cross-lingual information retrieval between Serbian and German is complicated by the mismatch between Serbian's fusional morphology and German's compounding strategies. This paper presents a retrieval framework in which user queries formulated in Serbian are expanded using a morphology-aware translation lexicon before being matched against an indexed German document collection. The lexicon was derived from the bilingual database described in earlier work and extended with 3,800 compound decompositions on the German side. Experiments were conducted on a collection of 22,000 technical patent abstracts with 120 manually constructed query-relevance judgement pairs. Mean Average Precision improved from 0.41 for a baseline bag-of-words approach to 0.58 when using the expanded lexicon with morphological normalization on both sides. The largest gains were observed for queries containing deverbal nouns, which are frequent in technical language and morphologically opaque to naive stemming. Error analysis identified 14% of failures as due to false friends between the two languages.

title: Loanword integration in Serbian technical registers: a corpus-based morphophonological study
abstract: Technical registers in Serbian have absorbed large numbers of loanwords from German, English, and Latin over the past century. This corpus-based study examines the morphophonological adaptation of 1,240 technical loanwords extracted from a 38-million-token corpus of Serbian professional writing spanning 1950–2010. Each token was annotated for source language, phonological adaptation strategy (substitution, deletion, epenthesis), and inflectional class assignment. Quantitative analysis shows that 67% of German-origin loanwords are assigned to the masculine a-declension, while English-origin items show greater variability. Temporal trends reveal increasing phonological retention of source-language consonant clusters after 1990, correlating with greater direct exposure to English-language technical literature. The findings have implications for lexicon design: inflectional class assignment for new technical borrowings cannot be predicted purely from phonological form and requires a probabilistic model with language-of-origin as a feature.

title: Towards a SerbianWordNet: linking synsets to inflectional paradigms
abstract: This book chapter describes the methodology and current state of SerbianWordNet, a lexical semantic network developed at the University of Novi Sad following the EuroWordNet model. The chapter focuses specifically on the problem of linking Princeton WordNet synsets to Serbian lemmas while preserving full morphological information. At the time of writing, the resource contained 32,000 synsets mapped from English, of which 21,400 had been manually verified by lexicographers. Each synset member is associated with an inflectional class identifier from the Serbian Reference Lexicon, enabling downstream applications to generate correctly inflected forms. The chapter discusses inter-annotator agreement on synset membership (Kappa 0.74) and describes a semi-automatic procedure for extending coverage by exploiting translational equivalents found in the Serbian–German bilingual database. Three application case studies are presented: a morphologically aware lexical simplification tool, a terminology extraction pipeline, and a query reformulation module for a Serbian patent search engine.

title: Annotating semantic roles in a Serbian–German parallel corpus of legal texts
abstract: Semantic role labeling in morphologically rich languages requires annotation schemes that can accommodate the greater word-order freedom that morphological case marking permits. This paper presents a semantic role annotation study conducted on a 280,000-token Serbian–German parallel corpus of EU legal texts. Annotation followed a PropBank-style scheme extended with five additional roles for beneficiary, causal, and concessive relations that occur frequently in legal prose. Inter-annotator agreement reached a Kappa of 0.69 for core roles and 0.54 for adjunct roles on a double-annotated subset of 40,000 tokens. The parallel structure of the corpus allowed contrastive analysis of how oblique arguments in Serbian, marked by morphological case, map to German prepositional phrases with varying degrees of ambiguity. Results suggest that automatic role labeling for Serbian can benefit from projection of labels from the German side using word alignment, increasing F1 from 0.61 to 0.68 in preliminary experiments.

title: Evaluation of open-source morphological analyzers on Vojvodina regional administrative texts
abstract: Administrative and official texts produced by institutions in Vojvodina are characterized by frequent multilingual insertions from Hungarian and German, archaic Serbian inflectional forms, and specialized terminological layers absent from general-language training data. This paper benchmarks four freely available Serbian morphological analyzers—two rule-based and two based on conditional random fields—against a hand-annotated corpus of 95,000 tokens of Vojvodina administrative language collected from municipal websites and official gazettes between 2010 and 2016. Lemmatization accuracy ranges from 79.1% to 88.4% across systems; POS accuracy ranges from 82.3% to 90.1%. All systems degrade significantly on tokens containing Hungarian proper nouns used as base forms for Serbian derivative suffixation. The paper proposes a lightweight post-processing layer using a small hybrid lexicon of 2,100 regional-specific forms, which raises the best system's lemmatization accuracy to 92.6%.

title: Bilingual term extraction from comparable corpora: Serbian and German annual reports in the financial sector
abstract: This study presents a method for extracting bilingual financial terminology from comparable—rather than parallel—corpora. The source corpus consists of 180 Serbian and 210 German annual reports from banking and insurance companies published between 2012 and 2018, totaling approximately 9.4 million tokens across both languages. Candidate terms were first extracted monolingually using a C-value measure combined with morphological normalization; 6,700 Serbian and 7,200 German candidates were retained. Bilingual alignment relied on a combination of cross-lingual word embeddings trained on a small seed lexicon of 1,800 verified financial term pairs and a cognate-detection component handling Internationalismen shared by both languages. Precision at rank 10 reached 0.72 for the embedding-based method, compared to 0.59 for a translation-dictionary baseline. Manual post-editing by two professional financial translators produced a verified bilingual glossary of 4,100 entries, which has been deposited in the departmental lexical resource archive.

title: Constructing a morphosyntactic lexicon for Serbian sign-language finger-spelled loanwords: a feasibility study
abstract: Finger-spelled words in Serbian Sign Language frequently originate as borrowings from written Serbian, and their morphosyntactic behavior differs from both their source forms and from native sign constructions. This feasibility study investigates whether existing Serbian morphological lexicons can be adapted to handle the restricted inflectional behavior of finger-spelled forms. Data were collected through structured elicitation sessions with twelve deaf informants from Novi Sad and Belgrade, producing a corpus of 4,400 finger-spelled tokens covering 310 distinct base forms. Analysis shows that finger-spelled nouns behave like Serbian masculine a-declension nouns in 82% of contexts regardless of their source paradigm class, suggesting a default assignment rule. A small proof-of-concept lexicon module of 310 entries was integrated into the existing Serbian Reference Lexicon infrastructure and evaluated in a retrieval task, where it improved recall for documents mentioning finger-spelled technical terms by 11 percentage points.

title: Low-resource neural lemmatization for Serbian: comparing data augmentation strategies using inflectional paradigm tables
abstract: Neural sequence-to-sequence lemmatizers trained on small annotated corpora suffer from sparse coverage of infrequent inflected forms. This paper compares five data augmentation strategies for Serbian, all of which exploit the paradigm tables stored in the Serbian Reference Lexicon. Strategies range from simple oversampling of low-frequency paradigm cells to generating synthetic training sentences by substituting lemma slots in dependency-parsed gold sentences. Experiments use a base training set of 90,000 tokens from the SETimes corpus and evaluate on a held-out 18,000-token slice. A transformer-based lemmatizer trained on the base data achieves an accuracy of 91.3%; augmenting with paradigm-table oversampling raises this to 93.8%; the best-performing strategy—slot-substituted synthetic sentences combined with paradigm oversampling—reaches 95.1%. The gap relative to a fully supervised model trained on 500,000 tokens is 1.9 percentage points. Results suggest that morphological lexicons remain a cost-effective resource for low-resource lemmatization even in the neural era.

title: Cross-lingual passage retrieval for Serbian–Hungarian bilingual administrative portals: a case study from Vojvodina
abstract: Vojvodina's bilingual administrative portals publish documents in both Serbian and Hungarian, creating a practical need for cross-lingual search that allows users querying in one language to retrieve relevant passages in the other. This paper describes a retrieval system built for a corpus of 640,000 documents totaling 310 million tokens collected from eleven municipal portal archives between 2015 and 2021. The retrieval backbone uses BM25 with morphological normalization on both language sides; cross-lingual query translation relies on a bilingual lexicon of 28,000 administrative term pairs assembled from earlier terminology projects and extended with a cognate list. A dense retrieval component based on multilingual sentence embeddings fine-tuned on 12,000 manually aligned passage pairs was integrated as a re-ranking layer. On 200 test queries, NDCG@10 improved from 0.49 (BM25 baseline) to 0.63 (hybrid system). The paper discusses user acceptance issues and ongoing cooperation with the Provincial Secretariat for Administration.

title: Multilingual named entity alignment across Serbian, German, and Hungarian in a shared industrial corpus: annotation scheme and baseline results
abstract: Named entities—company names, product identifiers, standards codes, and role designations—constitute a structurally important layer in industrial documents and present particular challenges when texts circulate across Serbian, German, and Hungarian. This paper proposes an annotation scheme for multilingual named entity alignment that accounts for the grammatical integration of foreign entity names into Serbian morphology (case suffixation, possessive clitic attachment) and the compounding behavior of entity names in German. The scheme was applied to a 520,000-token corpus of industrial tender documents and procurement records contributed by three manufacturing companies from the NTP Novi Sad ecosystem. Fourteen annotator sessions produced a triple-annotated gold standard of 42,000 tokens with Cohen's Kappa of 0.81 for entity span detection and 0.74 for cross-lingual alignment links. A CRF-based baseline system trained on 80% of the data achieved F1 of 0.77 for Serbian and 0.71 for Hungarian entity spans; cross-lingual link precision was 0.66.

title: Diachronic stability of Serbian inflectional paradigms in specialized registers, 1960–2020: evidence from a 200-million-token corpus
abstract: Descriptive grammars of Serbian were largely codified in the mid-twentieth century, but the inflectional behavior of nouns in specialized professional registers has not been systematically tracked across time. This study uses a 200-million-token diachronic corpus spanning 1960–2020, drawn from digitized issues of twelve Serbian trade and professional journals, to track frequency distributions across competing inflectional variants for 380 lexemes that exhibit paradigm instability in contemporary usage. Mixed-effects logistic regression models, with decade, register, and domain as fixed effects, show statistically significant drift toward the -a genitive singular for masculine inanimate nouns in technical registers (OR 1.34 per decade, p < 0.001), consistent with analogical leveling toward the most productive paradigm. These findings have practical implications for the design of morphological analyzers: models trained on pre-2000 data systematically underperform on post-2010 technical text due to unmodeled paradigm drift.

title: Polysemy Patterns in Serbian Newspaper Vocabulary: A Frequency-Based Pilot Study
abstract: This study examines polysemy distribution in a 2.4-million-token corpus of Serbian daily newspaper articles drawn from three national dailies published between 2006 and 2010. Using frequency ranking and concordance analysis in SketchEngine, the author identifies 318 high-frequency lemmas exhibiting at least three distinguishable senses in context. Sense boundaries were established through manual annotation following adapted WordNet criteria. Results indicate that approximately 34% of polysemous nouns in political reporting acquire secondary evaluative senses not attested in standard lexicographic sources. The paper argues that journalistic register drives systematic sense extension in a relatively short time window and proposes a preliminary taxonomy of extension types. Findings are compared with analogous observations in Croatian and Polish newspaper corpora from published literature. The study serves as a baseline for subsequent automated approaches to Serbian lexical sense disambiguation.

title: Šokački i bunjevački govori u Bačkoj: dijalektološka monografija
abstract: Monografija predstavlja sintezu desetogodišnjih terenskih istraživanja šokačkih i bunjevačkih govora na području Bačke. Opisuje se fonetski i fonološki sistem oba vernakula, s poglavljima posvećenim vokalizmu, konsonantizmu, prozodijskom sistemu i morfonološkim alternacijama. Poseban deo bavi se leksičkim elementima mađarskog porekla i njihovom fonetskom adaptacijom. Monografija sadrži i gelingvistički prilog — 14 karata distribucije odabranih dijalekatskih obeležja — kao i transkripcioni rečnik termina koji nije uvršten u standardnu IPA notaciju. Korpus na kome se zasniva obuhvata 212 govornika iz 27 naselja, snimljenih u periodu od 2008. do 2017. godine. Monografija je namenjena dijalektolozima, sociolingvistima i istraživačima jezičke politike zainteresovanim za situaciju romaniziranih slovenskih manjinskih govora u kontaktu s finougarskim jezicima.

title: Prefixed Verbs in Learner Serbian: A Corpus-Based Account of Prefix Selection Errors at B1–B2
abstract: Using the NoSLeCS learner corpus, this study analyses prefix selection errors in written texts produced by B1 and B2 learners of Serbian. A total of 3,218 prefixed verb tokens were identified in texts from 284 learners; 427 (13.3%) were manually coded as erroneous, subdivided into wrong-prefix, missing-prefix, and superfluous-prefix categories. Wrong-prefix errors were most frequent (58% of errors), and a large proportion involved substitution of a directional or spatial prefix for an aspectual one in telic contexts. Error rate per prefix type ranged from 3% for u- to 29% for po- in certain aspectual functions. Learners whose L1 was a Slavic language (Polish, Czech, Slovak, n = 44) showed significantly lower overall prefix error rates than non-Slavic L1 learners, but showed a distinct pattern of near-misses with cognate prefixes that carry subtly different meanings in their L1.

title: Rule-Based Feature Recognition for Turned Parts: A Taxonomy of Machinable Features and Implementation in a Prototype CAPP Module
abstract: This paper presents a rule-based approach to identifying machinable features on rotational workpieces from boundary representation CAD models. A taxonomy of 24 feature classes—including external cylinders, grooves, tapers, threaded surfaces, and undercuts—was developed through analysis of 180 part drawings collected from three contract machining shops in Vojvodina. Recognition rules were encoded in a Prolog-based inference engine interfaced with a mid-range CAD system via a neutral STEP AP214 exchange format. The prototype was tested on a validation set of 60 parts not used during rule development. Feature recognition accuracy reached 91.3% for external features and 84.7% for internal bore features, with misclassifications concentrated at compound groove–thread transitions. Processing time per part averaged 4.2 seconds on standard workstation hardware. The paper discusses the sensitivity of rule thresholds to geometric tolerancing data embedded in the STEP file and identifies tolerance propagation as a primary source of recognition errors. Limitations and a planned extension to prismatic part families are outlined.

title: Mapping CAPP Process Plan Outputs to PDM Bill-of-Process Structures: A Pilot Study in an SME Context
abstract: Computer-aided process planning systems in small and medium-sized enterprises frequently operate in isolation from product data management platforms, requiring manual re-entry of operation sequences, tool lists, and setup data. This study investigates a semi-automated mapping procedure that translates structured CAPP output—encoded as XML operation sheets—into the bill-of-process schema of a commercially available PDM system deployed at a Serbian automotive component supplier. The mapping was implemented as a middleware script and tested on 45 manufacturing orders covering turned and milled steel components. Data completeness after automated transfer reached 87% without manual correction, compared with an estimated baseline completeness of 61% under the previous manual workflow. Remaining gaps were attributed to non-standard fixture identifiers and the absence of cutting-condition data in legacy process plans. Interviews with process engineers at the partner company indicated a perceived reduction in re-entry time of approximately 40 minutes per order. The paper discusses schema alignment challenges and proposes a minimal common data dictionary for CAPP–PDM interoperability in SME settings.

title: Feature-Recognition Challenges for Prismatic Parts with Intersecting Pockets: A Comparative Assessment of Hint-Based and Graph-Based Approaches
abstract: Recognising machinable features in prismatic workpieces with intersecting pockets and slots presents persistent difficulties for automated CAPP because standard convex-decomposition methods produce ambiguous or redundant feature sets. This paper compares two established approaches—hint-based recognition and attributed adjacency graph (AAG) decomposition—on a controlled test set of 72 prismatic part models containing between one and five pocket intersections per part. Models were generated parametrically using a commercial CAD kernel to ensure controlled variation in intersection topology. Hint-based recognition correctly identified the intended manufacturing feature in 78% of cases, while the AAG approach reached 83%, with both methods degrading significantly (to 61% and 69%, respectively) when three or more pockets intersected a common face. Computational cost of the AAG approach was on average 3.1 times higher. The paper quantifies error types by intersection class and discusses implications for algorithm selection in CAPP systems targeting small-batch prismatic part families typical of tooling and fixture manufacture.

title: Kinetika enzimske sinteze etil-butanoata katalizovane imobilisanom lipazom iz Candida rugosa u heksanskom sistemu
abstract: U radu je ispitana kinetika sinteze etil-butanoata reakcijom između butanske kiseline i etanola u bezvodnom heksanskom sistemu uz korišćenje komercijalne lipaze iz Candida rugosa imobilisane na silikagel nosač. Eksperimenti su izvođeni na temperaturama od 30 do 55 °C, pri molskom odnosu supstrata 1:1 do 1:5 i koncentraciji enzima od 5 do 30 g/L. Dobijeni podaci opisani su ping-pong Bi-Bi mehanizmom sa inhibicijom etanolom. Parametri kinetičkog modela određeni su nelinearnom regresijom: maksimalna brzina reakcije iznosila je 2,4 mmol/(g·min) na 45 °C, a konstanta inhibicije etanolom Ki = 0,18 mol/L. Reakciona ravnoteža dostigla je prinos od 87% posle 6 sati pri optimalnim uslovima. Rezultati ukazuju da se inhibicija alkoholom može ublažiti postepenim doziranjem etanola, što je potvrđeno u fed-batch eksperimentu pri kome je prinos porastao na 93%. Model je validiran na nezavisnom skupu podataka sa relativnom greškom ispod 5%.

title: Effect of water activity on lipase-catalysed isoamyl acetate synthesis in solvent-free media
abstract: Isoamyl acetate, a banana-note aroma compound, was synthesised from isoamyl alcohol and acetic acid using Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase immobilised on a macroporous acrylic resin. Reactions were carried out in solvent-free conditions at water activities (aw) ranging from 0.03 to 0.45, controlled with saturated salt solutions in closed vessels. Maximum initial reaction rate of 3.1 µmol/(mg protein·min) was observed at aw = 0.11; rates declined sharply above aw = 0.25 due to hydrolytic back-reaction. Equilibrium ester yields varied from 32% at aw = 0.45 to 91% at aw = 0.07. Water produced during esterification was continuously removed by molecular sieves (3 Å), extending the aw range of efficient synthesis. The immobilised preparation retained 78% of initial activity after ten consecutive batch cycles. Kinetic data were fitted to a modified Michaelis–Menten model incorporating aw-dependent inhibition, yielding Ki,w = 0.19. These findings provide practical guidelines for reactor design without added organic solvent.

title: Poređenje homogene kisele i enzimske katalize pri sintezi propil-propanoata u kotlastom reaktoru
abstract: Rad sistematski poredi kinetičke karakteristike sinteze propil-propanoata posredstvom sumporne kiseline (1–5 mas.%) i imobilisane lipaze Candida antarctica B pri istim temperaturama (50–80 °C za kiselu, 30–55 °C za enzimsku katalizu) i molskim odnosima propanolne kiseline i propanola od 1:1 do 1:4. Kiselo-katalizovana reakcija opisana je kinetičkim modelom drugog reda sa aktivacionom energijom Ea = 62,4 kJ/mol. Enzimski sistem pokazao je nižu aktivacionu energiju (38,1 kJ/mol) i manji prinos hemijskih nečistoća u sirovom produktu. Međutim, kiselo-katalizovana sinteza dostigla je 90% ravnotežnog prinosa za 45 minuta pri 70 °C, dok je enzimski sistem zahtevao 180 minuta pri 45 °C za isti prinos. Troškovna analiza pokazuje da je kisela kataliza povoljnija za jednokratne serije velikog obima, dok je enzimska kataliza konkurentnija kada se enzim recikluje više od sedam ciklusa. Rezultati su od direktnog značaja za izbor procesa pri industrijskoj produkciji aroma.

title: Downstream separation of isoamyl acetate from reaction mixtures using vacuum distillation: mass balance and energy assessment
abstract: Isoamyl acetate produced by enzymatic esterification in a solvent-free system was purified by two-stage vacuum distillation. Feed streams with ester content between 55 and 90 mol% were processed at pressures of 20–80 mbar over a column with eight theoretical plates. Material balance experiments showed recovery of 97.4% isoamyl acetate with final purity above 99.5 GC area% at an operating pressure of 40 mbar and reflux ratio of 3. Energy consumption measured via calorimetry amounted to 3.2 MJ per kilogram of purified ester. Residual acid and alcohol were recovered for recycle, reducing raw material waste by 88% compared to a single-pass process. Process simulation using steady-state models agreed with experimental data within 4% on all major streams. Economic estimates suggest that the combined enzymatic synthesis and vacuum distillation step achieves a product cost of approximately 18 EUR/kg at 10 kg/day throughput, competitive with solvent-extraction-based purification routes.

title: Primena odzivne površine za optimizaciju enzimske sinteze butil-acetata na imobilisanoj lipazi iz Rhizomucor miehei
abstract: Metodom odzivne površine (RSM) sa centralnim kompozitnim dizajnom (CCD) optimizovani su uslovi sinteze butil-acetata posredstvom lipaze iz Rhizomucor miehei imobilisane na jonski izmenjivač. Nezavisne promenljive bile su temperatura (30–60 °C), molski odnos supstrata (1:1 do 1:5, sirćetna kiselina:1-butanol), sadržaj vode (0–5%, v/v) i masa enzima (2–20 g/L). Odzivna površina opisana je polinomom drugog reda sa koeficijentom determinacije R² = 0,964. Optimalni uslovi dobijeni numeričkom optimizacijom: 48 °C, molski odnos 1:3, 1% vode i 12 g/L enzima, dali su prinos butil-acetata od 94,7 ± 1,2% posle 4 sata. Validacioni eksperiment potvrdio je predviđanje modela sa greškom od 1,9%. Analiza uticaja faktora pokazala je da je molski odnos supstrata bio najznačajniji faktor (p < 0,001), a sadržaj vode najmanje značajan (p = 0,08) u ispitivanom opsegu.

title: Thermodynamic analysis of short-chain ester synthesis equilibria: Gibbs energy and activity coefficient estimation
abstract: Equilibrium constants and thermodynamic state functions were determined for the esterification of acetic, propionic, and butyric acids with ethanol and isoamyl alcohol at temperatures between 30 and 70 °C. Reactions were conducted in sealed glass ampoules to true equilibrium, verified by bidirectional approach. Activity coefficients in the liquid phase were estimated with the NRTL model, with binary parameters fitted to VLE data collected from the literature and supplemented by five new isothermal measurements. Standard Gibbs energies of reaction ranged from −1.2 to −3.8 kJ/mol across the six ester systems, confirming mild thermodynamic favourability. Enthalpy changes (ΔH°) were small and negative (−4 to −9 kJ/mol), indicating exothermic reactions with weak temperature dependence on equilibrium conversion. These results were incorporated into a reactor design tool that predicts maximum achievable yield as a function of temperature, feed ratio, and water removal efficiency. The tool is validated against published and original batch data with mean absolute deviation below 3 percentage points.

title: Sinteza etil-acetata kiselo katalizovanom esterifikacijom u reaktoru s membranom za odvođenje vode: uticaj tipa membrane i transmembranskog pritiska
abstract: Ispitan je uticaj tipa hidrofilne zeolitne membrane (NaA i LTA) i transmembranskog pritiska (0,5–3,0 bar) na prinos etil-acetata u kontinualnom reaktoru sa in-situ uklanjanjem vode. Membranski reaktor, zapremine 500 mL, rada je pod kontrolisanim uslovima pri temperaturi 60 °C sa sumpornom kiselinom kao katalizatorom (2 mas.%). Propusnost vode kroz NaA membranu iznosila je 0,42 kg/(m²·h·bar) pri selektivnosti voda/etil-acetat > 850. Prinos etil-acetata u membranskom reaktoru dostigao je 98,3% pri protoku supstrata od 120 mL/h, za razliku od 68,5% u konvencionalnom kotlastom reaktoru na ravnoteži. Stabilan rad membrane potvrđen je tokom 72 časa bez merljive degradacije selektivnosti. Ekonomska analiza ukazuje na 22% smanjenje specifičnih energetskih troškova u poređenju sa konvencionalnom destilacionom separacijom pri istoj propusnosti.

title: Deactivation kinetics of Candida antarctica B lipase under operational conditions relevant to flavour ester production
abstract: Long-term deactivation of Novozym 435 was studied under conditions representative of industrial flavour ester synthesis: temperatures 40–70 °C, water activities 0.05–0.40, and substrates including acetic, butyric, and hexanoic acids with ethanol or isoamyl alcohol. Residual activity was assayed at regular intervals using a standard p-nitrophenyl palmitate hydrolysis assay. At 50 °C and aw = 0.11 the operational half-life was 520 h; increasing aw to 0.30 reduced it to 190 h. Acid substrates caused concentration-dependent inactivation interpretable as competitive inhibition of the deactivation step. A two-state irreversible deactivation model with aw- and temperature-dependent rate constants described all data with R² > 0.95. The model was used to predict when enzyme replacement becomes economically justified, yielding break-even points at 8–14 batch cycles depending on substrate and operating temperature. Practical guidelines for maximising enzyme utilisation in fed-batch and continuous modes are presented.

title: Reactive distillation for ethyl propanoate synthesis: column design, steady-state multiplicity, and experimental validation
abstract: A reactive distillation column (RDC) for acid-catalysed synthesis of ethyl propanoate was designed, simulated, and tested at pilot scale (column diameter 50 mm, 12 reactive stages, Amberlyst-15 catalyst packing, 200 g per stage). Steady-state simulations using a non-equilibrium stage model predicted the existence of three steady states at certain feed compositions; experimental operation confirmed bistable behaviour with switching hysteresis between high-conversion (ethyl propanoate 97.2 mol%) and low-conversion (34.8 mol%) states depending on reboiler duty trajectory. Total acid conversion under stable high-conversion operation was 99.1% at a feed flow rate of 0.8 L/h (equimolar propionic acid and ethanol). Catalyst mechanical stability was assessed by sieve analysis before and after 200 h operation, showing less than 3% fines generation. Column energy demand was 2.7 kW per kg/h of ester produced, approximately 15% lower than a conventional reactor-separator sequence modelled under the same throughput.

title: Poređenje imobilizacionih nosača za lipazu Thermomyces lanuginosus pri sintezi izoamil-acetata: aktivnost, stabilnost i ponovna upotreba
abstract: Lipaza Thermomyces lanuginosus (TLL) imobilisana je na četiri nosača: silikagel, makroporozni akrilatni polimer, magnetne Fe₃O₄-SiO₂ čestice i hitozan kuglice. Imobilizovani preparati upoređeni su prema specifičnoj aktivnosti (mereno hidrolizom trioleinata), prinosu imobilizacije (62–95%), kinetičkim parametrima za sintezu izoamil-acetata u bezvodnom sistemu i operativnoj stabilnosti tokom deset šaržnih ciklusa. Magnetni nosač pokazao je najvišu specifičnu aktivnost (47 U/g nosača) i zadržao 81% aktivnosti posle deset ciklusa zahvaljujući lakom magnetnom odvajanju bez mehaničkog oštećenja enzima. Akrilatni polimer ostvario je 71% zadržane aktivnosti, ali uz najlakšu primenu u pakovanim slojevima. Hitozan kuglice pokazale su najnižu prividnu aktivnost (28 U/g) zbog difuzionih ograničenja. Procena troškova imobilizacije po kilogramu proizvedenog estara favorizuje magnetni nosač za šaržni proces i akrilatni polimer za kontinualni proces u pakovanom sloju.
