title: Solubility and partition behaviour of C2–C6 carboxylic acids and their corresponding ethyl esters in aqueous two-phase systems relevant to aroma recovery
abstract: Partition coefficients (P) of acetic, propionic, butyric, pentanoic, and hexanoic acids and their ethyl esters between water and five organic solvents (ethyl acetate, n-hexane, di-isopropyl ether, 2-methyltetrahydrofuran, and ethanol-modified supercritical CO₂ extract) were measured at 25 °C and atmospheric pressure. P values for esters ranged from 8.4 (ethyl acetate) to 136 (ethyl hexanoate) in the hexane–water system, while free acids partitioned predominantly into the aqueous phase (P < 0.6 for all except hexanoic acid, P = 4.1). Temperature dependence (15–40 °C) showed a 12–22% decrease in P per 10 °C rise for esters in hexane. A group-contribution model (modified UNIFAC-Dortmund) reproduced experimental P values with mean absolute relative deviation of 8.3%. Results are used to design a liquid–liquid extraction stage downstream of a continuous enzymatic reactor, targeting ester recovery above 95% in a single-stage extractor at solvent-to-feed ratios of 0.3–0.7.

title: Microreactor screening of acid catalysts for propyl butyrate synthesis: Brønsted acid resins versus zeolites
abstract: A glass microreactor system (channel volume 1.2 mL) was used to rapidly screen six solid acid catalysts—three sulfonated polystyrene-divinylbenzene resins (Amberlyst-15, Amberlyst-35, Lewatit K2629) and three zeolites (H-ZSM-5 Si/Al 25, H-Beta Si/Al 12.5, H-Y Si/Al 5)—for propyl butyrate synthesis from butyric acid and 1-propanol. At equimolar feed, 60 °C, and 10 min residence time, Amberlyst-35 delivered the highest initial activity (TOF = 0.51 mmol acid converted per meq H⁺ per min), while H-Beta gave 0.34 mmol/meq·min. Deactivation in the microreactor over 120 min was negligible for resins but reached 18% for H-Y zeolite, attributed to pore blockage by water clusters confirmed by post-run N₂ physisorption (BET surface area reduction 210 to 163 m²/g). Activation energies determined from Arrhenius plots (30–70 °C) were 58.3 kJ/mol for Amberlyst-35 and 71.4 kJ/mol for H-Beta. Scale-up to a 150 mL packed-bed unit with Amberlyst-35 reproduced microreactor selectivity within 4%, demonstrating reliable scale translation.

title: Integrated enzymatic reactor and membrane pervaporation unit for continuous butyl acetate production: pilot-scale performance over 500 hours
abstract: A pilot-scale integrated system combining a 2-litre stirred-tank enzymatic reactor (Candida antarctica B lipase on acrylic resin) with a PDMS pervaporation membrane module (effective area 0.18 m²) was operated continuously for 512 hours to produce butyl acetate from acetic acid and 1-butanol. The pervaporation module removed water produced during reaction, maintaining aw below 0.12 in the reactor and driving equilibrium conversion above 95 mol% compared to 72 mol% without water removal. Average ester production rate was 14.3 g/h at 45 °C; enzyme activity declined by 9% over the entire run. Membrane permeance for water averaged 0.61 kg/(m²·h·kPa) and remained stable throughout. Product stream from reactor overflow (ester content 88–92 mol%) was processed by a single-stage flash at 60 mbar, yielding final butyl acetate purity of 99.1 GC area%. Total specific energy consumption for synthesis and separation combined was 4.1 MJ/kg product. These results demonstrate sustained integrated operation at pre-industrial scale and provide data for techno-economic assessment.

title: Viscosity–Pressure–Temperature Correlations for Polyalkylene Glycol Gear Oils: Evaluation of Equation-of-State Models Against Experimental Data
abstract: Accurate viscosity–pressure–temperature (VPT) relationships are required for EHD film-thickness predictions in enclosed gears. This study measured dynamic viscosities of three polyalkylene glycol (PAG) fluids (MW 1 000, 2 000, and 4 000 g·mol⁻¹) at pressures from 0.1 to 800 MPa and temperatures from 20 to 120 °C using a falling-cylinder high-pressure viscometer. Experimental viscosities were fitted to three VPT models: Barus, Roelands, and Doolittle free-volume. The Doolittle model provided the best overall fit, with a mean absolute percentage error below 3.8% across the full pressure–temperature range, while the Barus model overestimated viscosity by up to 62% at pressures above 400 MPa. Pressure–viscosity coefficients at 40 °C ranged from 9.1 to 11.4 GPa⁻¹, substantially lower than PAO equivalents, consistent with the known poor EHD film-forming tendency of PAG oils at low speeds. An empirical correction factor relating PAG molecular weight to the Roelands pressure–viscosity exponent is proposed for engineering use.

title: Speciation of zinc and copper in pore water extracts of twelve Vojvodina calcareous soils: measured concentrations versus model predictions
abstract: Bioavailability models for micronutrients in calcareous soils require validation against real pore water data. Pore-water extracts from twelve Vojvodina calcareous soil profiles (pH 7.6–8.4, CaCO₃ 8–34%) were obtained by 1:2 (w/v) centrifuge extraction. Total dissolved Zn and Cu, and dissolved organic acid concentrations (citrate, malate, oxalate, succinate by ion-chromatography), were measured. Speciation was modelled in MINEQL+ 4.6 using stability constants from the group's own experimental database and the NIST database. Predicted free Zn²⁺ activity matched measured DPASV-labile Zn within a factor of 1.8 for 9 of 12 soils. Discrepancies in the remaining three soils, which had the highest dissolved organic carbon (>12 mg L⁻¹), suggest that uncharacterised humic ligands contribute significantly. Free Cu²⁺ predictions were less reliable (factor 3–6), consistent with Cu's stronger affinity for humic matter. Results define the applicability window of low-molecular-weight organic acid–based speciation models.

title: Bayesian Change-Point Detection in Non-Stationary Industrial Time Series
abstract: This paper addresses the identification of abrupt structural changes in time series generated by industrial sensors operating at sampling rates between 10 Hz and 100 Hz. A Bayesian online algorithm based on a product-partition model is adapted to handle autocorrelated noise and missing observations, which are common in factory-floor deployments. The method was evaluated on 14 months of vibration data from three manufacturing sites in central Serbia, comprising approximately 2.1 billion data points. Posterior inference was carried out using a Rao–Blackwellised particle filter, with run-time profiling showing the algorithm processes a 100 Hz stream in under 8 milliseconds per sample on standard server hardware. Against a ground-truth log of 47 documented equipment incidents, the approach achieved a detection rate of 91.5% with a median latency of 1.3 seconds. A comparison with CUSUM and PELT baselines shows consistent improvement in false-positive rate at fixed recall. Model hyperparameters were set via empirical Bayes using an initial 30-day warm-up period.

title: Feature Extraction Benchmarks for Multivariate Sensor Streams in Predictive Maintenance
abstract: A systematic comparison of 22 feature extraction approaches is presented for multivariate time-series data from rotating machinery. Feature families evaluated include statistical moments, entropy-based descriptors, wavelet sub-band energies, and autoregressive coefficients, each extracted over sliding windows of 0.5 s, 1 s, and 5 s. Experiments used publicly available bearing datasets supplemented by proprietary vibration logs from a Serbian automotive components supplier, totalling roughly 650 hours of continuous recording across six sensor channels. Features were fed into random forest and gradient-boosted classifiers. Wavelet sub-band energy features consistently ranked highest by mutual information with failure labels, and combining them with sample entropy yielded the best downstream F1 score of 0.88 on held-out data. Computational cost per feature family is reported in CPU-seconds, providing guidance for real-time deployment choices. The paper also proposes a simple dimensionality reduction step that retains 95% of predictive power while cutting feature dimensionality by a factor of four.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Models for Failure Rate Heterogeneity Across Machine Populations
abstract: Industrial fleets of nominally identical machines exhibit substantial heterogeneity in failure rates even after controlling for operating conditions. This paper develops a hierarchical Bayesian Poisson–Gamma model for failure counts observed over irregular inspection intervals, allowing partial pooling of information across 312 compressor units monitored over three years at a natural gas distribution company. A Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler (No-U-Turn) was used for posterior estimation; convergence was verified via Gelman–Rubin diagnostics on 4 independent chains. Unit-level posterior failure rate estimates had a coefficient of variation of 0.34, confirming meaningful heterogeneity. Predictive posterior distributions for time to next failure were used to rank units by expected residual life, and a field trial showed that prioritising the bottom 20% of units by posterior mean life reduced unplanned outages by 31% compared to the previous calendar-based schedule. The sensitivity of results to prior hyperparameter choice is discussed, and a weakly informative default prior is recommended.

title: Extreme-Value Modelling of Pressure Spike Amplitudes in Water Distribution Networks
abstract: Transient pressure spikes in water distribution networks can cause pipe fatigue and burst failures. This study fits generalised extreme-value (GEV) distributions to block maxima of pressure readings collected at 4 Hz from 28 monitoring nodes across the Novi Sad municipal network over 26 months. Block sizes of one week and one month are compared; likelihood ratio tests favour weekly blocks for this dataset. Maximum likelihood estimates indicate heavy-tailed behaviour (shape parameter ξ̂ ranging from 0.11 to 0.29 across nodes) that is inconsistent with Gaussian or exponential tail assumptions used in standard hydraulic standards. Return-level estimates at 10-year and 50-year periods are reported with 95% profile-likelihood confidence intervals. A spatial analysis using a max-stable process model reveals a correlation range of approximately 2.1 km, meaning that simultaneous extreme events at nodes within this distance must be treated as dependent. The results inform updated inspection intervals recommended to the municipal utility.

title: Individualised Actuarial Pricing Using Telematics Features: A Credibility Theory Perspective
abstract: Usage-based insurance pricing has shifted from simple mileage adjustments to models that incorporate behavioural features extracted from vehicle telematics. This paper re-examines the problem through the lens of Bühlmann–Straub credibility theory, showing that classic credibility estimators can be embedded in a Bayesian linear model with conjugate normal–inverse-gamma priors. Trip-level feature vectors (hard-braking rate, speed percentiles, time-of-day distribution, cornering events) were derived from 1 Hz GPS and accelerometer streams of 4,200 policyholders over 12 months, yielding approximately 18 million trip records. The credibility-weighted premium estimator reduced the mean squared prediction error of claim costs by 14.2% relative to a market-segment flat rate and by 6.8% relative to a generalised linear model with the same features but no credibility adjustment. The paper discusses regulatory constraints on feature selection under Serbian and EU insurance law and outlines a procedure for updating the model quarterly as new data arrive.

title: Online Variational Inference for Streaming Sensor Anomaly Detection
abstract: Batch Bayesian inference is impractical when sensor streams arrive continuously and model parameters must be updated in near real time. This paper investigates stochastic variational inference (SVI) as an online alternative, using a Gaussian mixture likelihood with a Dirichlet process prior to model the multimodal distribution of normal operating states. The algorithm processes mini-batches of 500 observations drawn from four temperature and humidity sensors on a cold-chain logistics platform, with one parameter update per second. On a 90-day evaluation dataset with 63 labelled anomaly episodes (ranging from 4 minutes to 11 hours), the SVI approach reached an area under the ROC curve of 0.93, compared to 0.89 for a static trained model retrained nightly. Memory footprint was 12 MB for the variational parameters, making the method deployable on edge devices with modest RAM. Drift in the variational posterior over time is characterised and a forgetting factor mechanism is proposed to prevent stale components from dominating.

title: Risk Scoring for Agricultural IoT Networks Under Sparse and Irregular Sampling
abstract: Soil moisture, leaf wetness, and microclimate sensors deployed across vineyards in Fruška Gora are sampled irregularly owing to energy-harvesting constraints, yielding gaps that can span several days. This paper adapts a Gaussian process regression framework to reconstruct latent continuous processes from irregular observations and derives a composite risk score for fungal disease onset. The GP kernel is chosen by leave-one-vineyard-out cross-validation among Matérn 3/2, squared-exponential, and rational-quadratic families; Matérn 3/2 was selected in 11 of 14 vineyard sites. Risk score thresholds calibrated to achieve 85% sensitivity for disease onset predicted spray interventions 2.1 days earlier on average than the standard phenological calendar used by local agronomists, over three growing seasons across 14 sites. A cost-benefit analysis using spray cost and expected yield loss figures from local agricultural records shows a mean saving of approximately 310 EUR per hectare per season under the model-guided schedule.

title: Probabilistic Load Forecasting for Small Industrial Consumers Using Meter Data and Bayesian Quantile Regression
abstract: Short-term electricity load forecasting for small and medium industrial consumers is more difficult than for large sites owing to high variability relative to mean demand. This study uses 15-minute smart meter readings from 87 SME customers of a regional distribution company in Vojvodina, covering 28 months. A Bayesian quantile regression model is fitted for each customer, with temperature, hour-of-day, day-of-week, and a 5-lag autoregressive component as covariates. Posterior predictive intervals at the 10th, 50th, and 90th quantiles are evaluated using the pinball loss and empirical coverage. Compared to a pooled point-forecast baseline, the per-customer Bayesian model reduces pinball loss by a median of 18% and achieves nominal coverage within 2 percentage points for 81 of 87 customers. The paper discusses practical aspects of deploying the model in a metering data management system, including re-estimation frequency and handling of customers with fewer than six months of history.

title: A Survey of Bayesian Methods for IoT-Driven Actuarial Modelling
abstract: This survey reviews 15 years of literature at the intersection of Bayesian statistics, IoT sensor data, and actuarial modelling, covering approximately 140 papers published between 2009 and 2024. The scope includes telematics-based motor insurance, sensor-monitored property insurance, maintenance-linked warranty pricing, and health wearable applications. The review is organised around four modelling tasks: hazard rate estimation, claims severity modelling, experience rating, and catastrophe risk quantification. For each task, the survey describes the predominant likelihood structures, prior specification strategies, and computational approaches. Key findings include a shift from conjugate analytical solutions to variational and sequential Monte Carlo methods after 2018, driven by data volume growth, and a persistent gap between academic model complexity and insurer implementation capacity. The paper identifies open problems in non-stationarity handling, regulatory interpretability requirements, and cross-domain transfer of fitted models as priorities for future research.

title: Sequential Bayesian Updating of Remaining Useful Life Distributions Under Concept Drift
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) models for rotating equipment are typically trained once and then applied statically, but operating conditions and load profiles drift over months or years, causing predictive accuracy to degrade. This preprint proposes a sequential Bayesian updating scheme in which the posterior over RUL model parameters is revised each time a failure or censoring event is recorded, using an importance-weighted likelihood that down-weights observations older than a tunable half-life τ. The method is evaluated on three datasets: a benchmark turbofan engine simulation, a set of 41 conveyor belt drives monitored over 31 months, and compressor units from a previous study by the same group. Choosing τ by cross-validation over a held-out cohort reduced mean absolute RUL error by 22% compared to the static model and by 9% compared to periodic full re-fitting on a 90-day rolling window. Computational overhead relative to a static model is approximately 3% per update cycle.

title: Grammar Inference from Domain Equations to Bootstrap Symbolic Regression Constraints
abstract: When domain equations are partially known, the information they contain can be used to infer a context-free grammar that guides symbolic regression toward physically meaningful solutions. This work proposes a two-stage pipeline: first, a small set of validated domain equations is used to extract production rules via a rule-mining procedure based on frequent subtree enumeration; second, the resulting grammar seeds the hypothesis space for grammar-guided genetic programming. The approach is evaluated on problems from process engineering and soil mechanics, where partial knowledge of governing equations exists. On six benchmark problems with 150–600 data points, the bootstrapped grammar recovers correct functional forms in 83% of runs compared with 51% for uninformed grammar-guided GP and 44% for standard GP. A sensitivity analysis shows performance degrades gracefully when the seed equations contain up to 30% incorrect terms, making the method robust to imperfect domain knowledge.

title: Psychological contract formation among newly hired IT professionals in Serbia: a longitudinal survey
abstract: This study traced the development of psychological contracts during the first 18 months of employment among 134 software developers hired by ten Serbian IT companies between 2009 and 2011. Using a three-wave panel design with questionnaires administered at months 3, 9, and 18, the study measured employees' relational and transactional contract beliefs alongside supervisor trust and job embeddedness. Latent growth curve analysis in LISREL showed that relational beliefs grew significantly faster when direct supervisors provided consistent feedback (β = 0.41, p < 0.01), while transactional beliefs remained relatively stable across the observation window. Breach perceptions at month 9 predicted a 22 percentage-point increase in turnover intention by month 18, controlling for salary level. The paper argues that early managerial communication patterns set the baseline for later contract content, and recommends structured onboarding conversations as a low-cost retention measure for Serbian software firms facing acute skill shortages.

title: Affective commitment under resource scarcity: evidence from non-profit knowledge organisations in Hungary and Serbia
abstract: Drawing on a cross-national sample of 211 professionals employed in non-profit research and cultural organisations in Hungary (n = 112) and Serbia (n = 99), this article investigates how perceived resource adequacy moderates the relationship between psychological contract fulfilment and affective commitment. Data were collected via structured online questionnaires in 2012. Multigroup structural equation modelling in AMOS revealed that the positive path from contract fulfilment to affective commitment was significantly weaker when employees reported below-average resource availability (Δχ² = 6.84, p < 0.05). The moderation effect was stronger in the Serbian subsample, consistent with the institutional context of constrained public funding. These findings suggest that organisational commitment programmes cannot be substituted for adequate physical and informational resources, even when relational contract beliefs are intact. Practical implications for public-sector HR in transitional economies are discussed.

title: Breach salience and exit behaviour: a vignette experiment with IT project managers
abstract: This paper reports a scenario-based vignette experiment conducted with 88 active IT project managers recruited through a professional network in Serbia and Croatia. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four vignette conditions varying the type of breach (relational vs. transactional) and the perceived intentionality of the organisation (deliberate vs. circumstantial). Multinomial logistic regression showed that deliberate relational breaches produced the highest proportion of exit responses (61%), whereas circumstantial transactional breaches yielded the lowest (17%). Intention to remain was significantly higher when the breach was attributed to external economic pressure rather than management decision (OR = 2.31, 95% CI [1.42, 3.76]). The study contributes experimental evidence to a literature dominated by cross-sectional surveys and highlights attribution as a key moderator that practitioners can address through transparent communication during periods of organisational change.

title: Psychological contract breach and knowledge-sharing behaviour: mediating role of trust in the team
abstract: This study tested a mediated model in which trust in the immediate team mediates the relationship between psychological contract breach and employees' willingness to share tacit knowledge, using survey data from 267 knowledge workers in 18 companies based in the Science Technology Parks of Novi Sad and Belgrade, collected in 2017. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped confidence intervals (5,000 iterations) confirmed full mediation: breach was negatively associated with team trust (β = −0.38, p < 0.001), and team trust was positively associated with knowledge sharing (β = 0.44, p < 0.001); the direct path from breach to knowledge sharing became non-significant when the mediator was included. The result held across both parks and across four industry sectors. The study suggests that retention of tacit knowledge within firms depends more on maintaining trust climates than on preventing breach per se, and recommends team-level trust audits as a diagnostic tool.

title: Psychological contracts in cross-border remote teams: evidence from Hungarian–Serbian software partnerships
abstract: Remote collaboration between Hungarian and Serbian developers, facilitated by proximity and bilingualism, has grown substantially since 2015. This study surveyed 158 employees working in seven such cross-border partnerships in 2018, comparing psychological contract content, breach perceptions, and affective commitment between the two national groups. Independent samples t-tests and multigroup confirmatory factor analysis indicated that Serbian employees reported significantly higher relational contract expectations (M = 4.12 vs. 3.74 on a five-point scale, t(156) = 3.21, p < 0.01) and more frequent breach perceptions regarding career development promises. Hungarian respondents reported higher scores on transactional items related to pay transparency. Affective commitment was lower in both groups when communication norms across the border were perceived as inconsistent. The paper provides HR recommendations for companies operating in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region and underscores the importance of explicit expectation-setting in multilingual virtual environments.

title: Organisational justice perceptions as antecedents of breach: a longitudinal replication in Serbian manufacturing and ICT sectors
abstract: This article replicates and extends a two-wave longitudinal study (N = 302; T1 2018, T2 2019) examining whether procedural and distributive justice perceptions at T1 predict psychological contract breach at T2, separately in manufacturing (n = 151) and ICT (n = 151) workers in Serbia. Cross-lagged panel models estimated in R (lavaan package) showed that procedural justice at T1 was a significant negative predictor of breach at T2 in both sectors (manufacturing: β = −0.29, p < 0.001; ICT: β = −0.35, p < 0.001), while distributive justice predicted breach only in the manufacturing sample. These sector differences suggest that ICT workers may evaluate fairness more through process than outcome, consistent with their emphasis on professional autonomy. The replication design and publicly archived dataset address concerns about single-source bias that affect much of the breach literature.

title: Turnover intention among knowledge workers during organisational restructuring: the buffer role of affective commitment
abstract: Using data collected from 214 employees of three mid-sized technology firms in Vojvodina undergoing restructuring between January and June 2020, this paper tests whether affective commitment buffers the positive effect of perceived psychological contract breach on turnover intention. Hierarchical multiple regression and simple slope analysis indicated that the breach–turnover path was significant at low (b = 0.52, p < 0.001) and moderate (b = 0.31, p < 0.01) but not at high levels of affective commitment (b = 0.09, p = 0.38), supporting a buffering interaction. The pattern was consistent across three occupational groups (software developers, data analysts, technical writers). These results have practical relevance for Vojvodina-based firms that rely on restructuring as a cost-control strategy while simultaneously attempting to retain scarce technical talent, and support investment in commitment-building practices before, rather than after, restructuring announcements.

title: Psychological contract breach in hybrid work arrangements: a cross-sectional survey of knowledge workers in the Western Balkans
abstract: Hybrid work became widespread in the Western Balkans following 2020, creating new conditions for psychological contract breach. This cross-sectional study surveyed 389 knowledge workers across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia in late 2021, measuring breach perceptions on Morrison and Robinson's scale, affective commitment (Allen and Meyer), and three dimensions of hybrid work quality: schedule flexibility, digital tool adequacy, and informal contact access. SEM in SmartPLS 4 showed that inadequate digital tools (β = 0.33) and loss of informal contact (β = 0.27) were the strongest predictors of breach, while schedule flexibility was unrelated. Breach in turn predicted lower affective commitment (β = −0.41) and higher turnover intention (β = 0.38). Sector moderation tests indicated that effects were stronger in flat, project-based firms than in hierarchical organisations, reinforcing the argument that flat structures amplify contract vulnerability during work-arrangement transitions.
venue: Balkan Journal of Management and Business Research

title: Manager replacement as a breach trigger: a diary study of affective responses over four weeks
abstract: Manager replacement is a common but understudied form of organisational change that may trigger psychological contract breach through loss of relationship-specific promises. This diary study recruited 61 knowledge workers from eight companies in Novi Sad who were experiencing a direct manager replacement, collecting daily entries on breach cognitions, affect, and work engagement over 20 working days in 2022. Multilevel modelling (HLM, person-centred) showed that breach cognitions spiked significantly during the first five days after replacement (d = 0.67 relative to pre-change baseline), then gradually declined but did not return to baseline by day 20. Negative affect fully mediated the within-person relationship between daily breach and next-day work engagement (indirect effect = −0.18, 95% CI [−0.28, −0.08]). Employees with higher pre-change affective commitment showed faster recovery trajectories, supporting the protective function of prior commitment investment.

title: Perceived overqualification, contract breach, and staying despite discontent: a moderated mediation model
abstract: Overqualification is prevalent among knowledge workers in Serbia, where the supply of graduates exceeds absorption by the labour market. This study tested a moderated mediation model in which psychological contract breach mediates the positive effect of perceived overqualification on turnover intention, and affective commitment moderates the mediated path. A sample of 244 knowledge workers from the Novi Sad region completed an online survey in 2023. PLS-SEM results confirmed the mediated path (indirect effect = 0.21, 95% CI [0.11, 0.31]) and the moderating role of affective commitment: at high commitment, the indirect effect shrank to 0.09 (95% CI [0.01, 0.19]), while at low commitment it reached 0.34 (95% CI [0.21, 0.48]). These results highlight that overqualified employees who are emotionally attached to the organisation are less likely to translate breach into exit intent, suggesting that commitment cultivation is especially valuable for firms employing workers in roles below their qualification level.

title: Sustainability Reporting Practices of Agri-food SMEs in Serbia: A Content Analysis
abstract: This paper examines the voluntary sustainability reporting behaviour of 63 small and medium-sized agri-food enterprises in Serbia, using content analysis of corporate documents, websites, and publicly available supplier declarations collected in 2016. Reporting is coded across six dimensions: environmental performance indicators, labour conditions, food safety, traceability, community impact, and governance structures. The median firm reports on fewer than two dimensions, and the reporting that does exist is predominantly qualitative and unverified. Cross-tabulation with firm characteristics reveals that export orientation and the presence of a foreign equity partner are the only attributes consistently associated with broader reporting scope. The paper contrasts these findings with GRI-aligned practices documented in Western European agri-food firms and discusses the institutional conditions—weak civil society demand, limited investor pressure, and thin regulatory enforcement—that sustain reporting minimalism in the Serbian context.

title: Handling Irregular Observation Intervals in Hospital Discharge Records: A Simulation Study
abstract: Longitudinal clinical records frequently contain measurements collected at irregular and patient-specific time points, complicating downstream analysis. This simulation study systematically evaluated six imputation strategies—last-observation-carried-forward, linear interpolation, cubic spline, multivariate imputation by chained equations (MICE), k-nearest neighbours, and a Gaussian process model—on synthetic discharge datasets constructed to mirror the missingness patterns of a 4 200-patient internal medicine cohort from a Serbian tertiary hospital. Performance was assessed via root mean squared error and downstream classification accuracy on a 30-day readmission label. Gaussian process imputation achieved the lowest RMSE across all missingness rates tested (10 %–60 %), while MICE performed comparably at rates below 30 % and required substantially less computation time. Last-observation-carried-forward degraded classification AUC by up to 0.09 at 60 % missingness. The study provides practical guidance for selecting imputation methods under realistic hospital data conditions and offers a reproducible benchmark codebase released under an open licence.

title: A Probabilistic Framework for Imputing Missing Laboratory Values in Longitudinal EHR Cohorts
abstract: Laboratory test results in electronic health records exhibit structured patterns of missingness driven by clinical decisions rather than random processes. This paper presents a probabilistic graphical model that explicitly represents the missing-at-random versus missing-not-at-random distinction for twelve common blood panel measurements observed in a 6 800-patient longitudinal cohort spanning three years. The model uses a mixture of Dirichlet process priors to capture patient subgroups with distinct measurement trajectories and employs variational inference for scalable posterior approximation. Compared to MICE and mean imputation baselines, the proposed model reduced absolute error in held-out complete-case experiments by 14 % for creatinine and 11 % for haemoglobin. Downstream 90-day readmission prediction using logistic regression reached AUC 0.74, a gain of 0.04 over MICE-imputed inputs. Runtime on a 16-core workstation was under three hours for the full cohort. Code is available on an institutional repository.

title: Ontology-Driven Normalisation of Diagnosis Codes Using SNOMED CT for Cross-Border EHR Interoperability
abstract: Clinical diagnosis codes recorded in hospital information systems across the Western Balkans span at least three competing terminologies: ICD-10, MKB-10 (the Serbian adaptation), and legacy institutional code lists. This work describes a semi-automated pipeline that maps all three to SNOMED CT concept identifiers using a combination of lexical matching, edit-distance scoring, and a support vector classifier trained on 3 200 manually labelled code pairs. The pipeline was evaluated on a bilingual Serbian–Croatian test set of 1 800 codes; precision was 0.88 and recall 0.84 at the exact SNOMED concept level, rising to 0.94 precision when evaluated at the ancestor level two hops up the hierarchy. An iterative active-learning loop reduced the manual annotation burden by approximately 40 % relative to random sampling. The resulting mappings support construction of a harmonised 12 000-patient retrospective cohort spanning institutions in two countries.

title: Readmission Risk Within 30 Days of Discharge: Feature Selection and Model Comparison on a Serbian Internal Medicine Cohort
abstract: Predicting hospital readmission from structured EHR data is well studied in North American and Western European contexts but rarely validated on Balkan hospital populations. This retrospective cohort study used discharge records of 9 100 adult patients from a single tertiary centre over five years. After harmonising diagnosis codes and imputing seven laboratory and vital-sign features, logistic regression, random forest, and gradient boosted trees were trained and evaluated in a time-split validation design. Gradient boosted trees achieved the best AUC of 0.77 (95 % CI 0.74–0.80). The most informative features were number of prior admissions in twelve months, serum sodium at discharge, and Charlson Comorbidity Index score. Calibration curves showed that all tree-based models required isotonic regression recalibration to be clinically usable. The study provides an open benchmark dataset and baseline code to facilitate comparisons from other regional groups.

title: Effect of Ontology Granularity on Downstream Readmission Model Performance: An Ablation Study
abstract: When diagnosis codes are mapped to a hierarchical ontology such as SNOMED CT, the researcher must decide at which level of the hierarchy to encode diagnoses as model features. This ablation study varied the ancestor level—from the original leaf concept to four levels up—for the 50 most frequent diagnostic categories in a 10 200-patient cohort and measured the effect on a gradient boosted readmission classifier. AUC degraded monotonically from 0.76 at the leaf level to 0.69 at four levels up, but Brier score improved slightly at two levels up, suggesting a variance–bias trade-off. Rare diagnoses (appearing in fewer than 50 patients) benefited from one-level aggregation, improving their individual precision–recall AUC by an average of 0.08. The results provide actionable guidance for ontology feature engineering in clinical prediction tasks where code sparsity is a concern.

title: Federated Imputation for Multi-Hospital EHR Cohorts Without Centralising Patient Data
abstract: Privacy regulations and data governance barriers frequently prevent centralisation of EHR data from multiple hospitals, yet pooled datasets are needed for robust model training. This paper adapts the FedAvg federated learning protocol to the MICE imputation algorithm and evaluates it across three simulated hospital nodes derived by stratified partitioning of a 14 000-patient cohort. Federated MICE achieved imputation RMSE within 4 % of centralised MICE after twelve communication rounds while exposing only summary statistics between nodes. Differential privacy noise at ε = 2 increased RMSE by a further 7 % but remained within clinically acceptable bounds for downstream readmission prediction (AUC drop of 0.02). Communication overhead was measured at 340 MB per round for the parameter vectors used. The protocol is described in sufficient detail for replication and extension to additional imputation methods.

title: Benchmarking ICD-to-SNOMED Mapping Tools on a Serbian Language Clinical Corpus
abstract: Most ICD-to-SNOMED mapping tools are developed and evaluated on English-language clinical documentation. This benchmark study tested five publicly available mapping tools—including two rule-based systems and three neural embedding approaches—against a manually annotated set of 2 600 ICD-10 codes drawn from Serbian hospital discharge summaries that include free-text diagnostic qualifiers. Annotations were produced by two independent clinical coders with adjudication of disagreements. The best-performing tool, a bilingual sentence-transformer fine-tuned on Croatian and Serbian clinical notes, achieved exact-match accuracy of 0.79 and SNOMED ancestor-match accuracy of 0.91. Rule-based tools lagged by 10–14 percentage points. Inter-annotator agreement was κ = 0.83. The study makes the benchmark annotation set available under a data-sharing agreement and recommends minimum reporting standards for future mapping evaluations on low-resource clinical languages.

title: Survival Analysis of Repeated Readmissions Using Joint Models of Longitudinal Biomarkers and Time-to-Event Outcomes
abstract: Thirty-day readmission as a single binary outcome discards information about repeated hospitalisation patterns. This study applied a joint model combining a linear mixed-effects submodel for four longitudinal biomarkers (creatinine, haemoglobin, C-reactive protein, and albumin) with a recurrent-events survival submodel for readmission episodes in a 5 400-patient cardiology cohort followed for up to four years. The joint model outperformed a Cox model using last-observed biomarker values, reducing Brier score from 0.19 to 0.15 at twelve-month follow-up. Creatinine trajectory slope was the strongest predictor (hazard ratio per unit increase in monthly slope: 1.38, 95 % CI 1.22–1.56). Model fitting used an expectation–maximisation algorithm implemented in R and required approximately 90 minutes per model on a standard workstation. Clinical interpretation and calibration diagnostics are discussed in detail.

title: A Reusable Python Toolkit for ICD Code Normalisation and Ontology-Aware Feature Extraction from EHR Data
abstract: Clinical researchers frequently reimplement the same preprocessing steps—code normalisation, ontology traversal, feature matrix construction—with varying correctness and without shared test suites. This software paper describes EHRonto, a Python package that provides a validated pipeline from raw ICD-9/ICD-10/MKB-10 code lists to SNOMED CT–annotated feature matrices ready for machine learning. The package wraps SNOMED CT release files under a licence-compliant access layer, implements the mapping SVM from earlier published work, and includes MICE and Gaussian process imputation backends. Unit tests cover 1 200 code mapping cases. Performance benchmarks show that processing a 10 000-patient cohort takes under eight minutes on a four-core laptop. The package is documented with worked examples on two anonymised synthetic cohorts that mimic Serbian hospital data distributions. Version 1.0 is archived on Zenodo with a DOI.

title: Prospective Validation of an EHR-Based Readmission Risk Score in Two Serbian Hospitals: Eighteen-Month Follow-Up
abstract: Retrospective development of readmission prediction models is common but prospective validation in the originating healthcare system is rare. This report describes an eighteen-month prospective validation of a gradient boosted readmission score developed on historical data at two Serbian hospitals not used in model development (combined n = 6 800 index admissions). The score was integrated into the hospital information system as a read-only alert and evaluated against observed 30-day readmission outcomes. In intention-to-screen analysis, AUC was 0.73 (95 % CI 0.70–0.76), consistent with the retrospective estimate of 0.75. Net reclassification improvement over the existing clinical judgement practice was 0.11. Drift in feature distributions was monitored monthly; a creatinine calibration shift at month nine was detected and corrected by recalibrating the output layer. The study establishes a monitoring and recalibration protocol applicable to similar deployments.

title: Integration of multi-omics layers in Bayesian network inference: a case study in soybean salt tolerance
abstract: Combining transcriptomic and proteomic measurements can, in principle, improve the accuracy of inferred gene regulatory networks by providing complementary information about regulatory state. We investigated whether joint modelling of RNA-seq and label-free quantitative proteomics data improves Bayesian network structure recovery in salt-stressed soybean, using a dataset of 20 paired samples. Three integration strategies were compared: early integration (concatenated feature matrices), late integration (separately learned networks merged by edge-weight thresholding), and a structured joint BGe scoring approach adapted for heterogeneous measurement types. The joint BGe approach yielded the highest F1 against the reference network (0.49 versus 0.41 and 0.38 for early and late integration, respectively), but required careful normalisation of cross-modality covariance terms. We detail the normalisation pipeline, identify failure modes when proteomics coverage is below 40% of transcriptomic gene set, and propose a practical quality filter for deciding when multi-omics integration is likely to help.

title: Thermal boundary resistance at GaN/AlN interfaces grown by molecular beam epitaxy
abstract: We report measurements of thermal boundary resistance (TBR) at GaN/AlN interfaces prepared by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on silicon substrates. Time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) was used to extract TBR values across a temperature range of 80–400 K. Samples with three different buffer layer thicknesses (50 nm, 150 nm, and 300 nm) were compared. TBR values at room temperature ranged from 1.8 × 10⁻⁸ to 3.4 × 10⁻⁸ m² K W⁻¹, increasing systematically with interface roughness as characterised by X-ray reflectometry. Atomistic Green's function calculations were performed to separate the contributions of elastic and inelastic phonon scattering channels. The elastic channel accounts for roughly 60% of the total conductance at 300 K. The results suggest that interface roughness is a more decisive factor than mismatch in phonon density of states for this material combination, with implications for thermal management in high-electron-mobility transistor structures.

title: Phonon mean free path distributions in InGaAs/InAlAs superlattices from first-principles scattering rates
abstract: We combine density functional perturbation theory calculations of phonon–phonon scattering rates with an iterative solution of the phonon Boltzmann transport equation to predict mean free path (MFP) distributions in InGaAs/InAlAs superlattices relevant for terahertz device applications. Superlattice periods ranging from 4 nm to 20 nm were considered. Calculated room-temperature cross-plane thermal conductivities lie between 1.9 and 5.6 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, in good agreement with experimental values obtained by the differential 3ω method on samples grown at the University of Ljubljana. The MFP distributions show that phonons with free paths shorter than 10 nm carry over 70% of the heat flux in the shortest-period structures, confirming a transition from particle-like to diffusive-coherent transport. Interface mass mixing, modelled as a Gaussian compositional profile, reduces cross-plane conductivity by up to 22% relative to the ideal interface case. These findings provide guidance for tuning thermal isolation in heterostructure lasers.

title: Merenje toplotnog otpora granica faza u Si/Ge nanomultisloju metodom impulsne lasерske kalorimetrije
abstract: Primenjena je metoda impulsne laserske kalorimetrije sa vremenskom rezolucijom od 50 ps za direktno merenje toplotnog otpora granica faza u Si/Ge nanomultislojevima. Ispitano je pet serija uzoraka sa periodom supermreže između 3 i 25 nm, deponovanih metodom magnetronskog raspršivanja na Institutu za fiziku u Beogradu. Izmereni TBR pri 300 K iznosi od 0,9 × 10⁻⁹ do 2,1 × 10⁻⁹ m² K W⁻¹ po granici, uz izrazitu zavisnost od perioda supermreže. Phonon mismatch model (AMM) i difuzni mismatch model (DMM) su sistemastki upoređeni s eksperimentalnim podacima: DMM precenjuje TBR za oko 35% u svim ispitanim uzorcima. Korigovani DMM koji uključuje inelastično rasejanje bolje opisuje rezultate pri niskim temperaturama (ispod 200 K). Dobijeni podaci su korisni za projektovanje termoelektričnih naprava zasnovanih na Si/Ge heterostrukturama.

title: Acoustic phonon transmission across abrupt and graded AlGaN/GaN interfaces: a non-equilibrium Green's function study
abstract: We apply the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism to calculate frequency-resolved phonon transmission coefficients across abrupt and compositionally graded AlGaN/GaN interfaces. Graded interlayers with widths of 1, 2, and 5 nm were modelled using a virtual crystal approximation for interatomic force constants extracted from density functional theory. Transmission spectra reveal a pronounced dip near 5 THz for the abrupt interface, attributed to the mismatch in acoustic phonon dispersion. Grading over 5 nm partially fills this dip, increasing the integrated transmission by 14% at 300 K compared to the abrupt case. Temperature-dependent interface conductance from 100 to 500 K was computed and compared against our own TDTR measurements, showing agreement within 12%. The study identifies the 1–3 THz spectral window as dominant for heat transfer across this interface, underscoring the importance of low-frequency phonon engineering in GaN-based power devices.

title: Upoređivanje Ramanovske i 3ω metode za karakterizaciju toplotne provodnosti tankih filmova na izolatorskim podlogama
abstract: Sistematski smo uporedili dve standardne metode za merenje toplotne provodnosti tankih filmova – Ramanovu termometriju u stacionarnom režimu i 3ω metodu – primenjene na iste uzorke oksid-poluprovodničkih struktura (HfO₂/Si i Al₂O₃/Si) debljine od 30 do 200 nm. Kod HfO₂ uzoraka pri sobnoj temperaturi razlike između metoda iznose do 18%, dok su kod Al₂O₃ razlike ispod 7%. Detaljnom analizom toplotnih otpora kontakta i optičkih apsorpcionih koeficijenata identifikovane su sistemske greške svojstvene svakoj metodi. Pokazano je da 3ω metoda daje konzistentnije rezultate ispod 100 nm debljine filma zbog manje osetljivosti na toplotni otpor film–supstrat, dok Ramanova metoda ima prednost kod optički transparentnih supstrata. Preporučene su smernice za odabir metode u zavisnosti od debljine filma i optičkih karakteristika sistema.

title: Thermal conductivity reduction in GaN films by controlled nitrogen vacancy introduction
abstract: Nitrogen vacancies were introduced into MOCVD-grown GaN films via low-energy ion implantation at doses between 5 × 10¹¹ and 5 × 10¹³ cm⁻². Raman thermometry and the 3ω method were used in parallel to measure in-plane and cross-plane thermal conductivities before and after implantation and after subsequent annealing at 900 °C. At the highest implantation dose, cross-plane conductivity dropped from 178 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ to 43 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. Partial recovery to 94 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ was observed after annealing, consistent with vacancy clustering into larger defect complexes as observed by positron annihilation spectroscopy performed at the Slovak University of Technology. A modified Klemens model including point-defect and cluster scattering terms reproduces the experimental conductivity values within 8% across all doses and temperatures from 100 to 400 K. The results demonstrate a route to engineering phonon scattering in GaN without altering electrical doping profiles.

title: Transport fonona u β-Ga₂O₃/4H-SiC heterostrukturama: merenje i modelovanje
abstract: Ispitivali smo transport toplote u heterostrukturama β-Ga₂O₃/4H-SiC, koje su od interesa za primenu u visokonaponskim prekidačkim elementima. Uzorci su pripremljeni pulsnom laserskom depozicijom u saradnji s partnerskim laboratorijem u Krakovu, s debljinom Ga₂O₃ sloja između 80 nm i 600 nm. Merenja TDTR pri temperaturama od 100 do 450 K pokazala su TBR na granici Ga₂O₃/SiC od 5,3 × 10⁻⁸ m² K W⁻¹ pri 300 K, što je znatno veće od vrednosti za slične nitridne sisteme. NEGF simulacijama identifikovana je velika razlika u gustini fonona pri 7–10 THz kao primarni uzrok visokog TBR. Modelovanjem je predloženo uvođenje međusloja AlGaO debljine 3–5 nm koji bi postepeno prebacivao fonoske spektre i smanjio TBR za procenjenih 30%. Dobijeni rezultati direktno su primenjivi na termodinamičko projektovanje β-Ga₂O₃ tranzistorskih struktura.

title: Size-dependent cross-plane thermal conductivity of AlN films measured by frequency-domain thermoreflectance
abstract: We use frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR) to measure the cross-plane thermal conductivity of sputter-deposited AlN films with thicknesses from 20 nm to 1 µm on silicon and sapphire substrates. Measurements cover the temperature range 150–400 K. Conductivity increases from 11 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 20 nm to 218 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1 µm at 300 K, following a trend well captured by the phonon size-effect model. The frequency-domain approach allows simultaneous extraction of film conductivity and film–substrate TBR from a single experiment. TBR on sapphire substrates (3.1 × 10⁻⁸ m² K W⁻¹) is about 40% lower than on silicon (5.2 × 10⁻⁸ m² K W⁻¹), consistent with better acoustic impedance matching. The FDTR data were validated against 3ω measurements at five selected thicknesses, with agreement better than 6%. Results support the use of AlN as an intermediate thermal spreading layer in III-N device stacks.

title: Phonon transport across two-dimensional material interlayers at III-N interfaces
abstract: We investigate how single- and bilayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) interlayers modify phonon transport across GaN/AlN interfaces. Interlayers were transferred onto MBE-grown GaN surfaces using a polymer-free dry transfer process in collaboration with the Centre for 2D Materials at the University of Vienna. TDTR measurements show that a single hBN layer increases TBR by 1.1 × 10⁻⁸ m² K W⁻¹ relative to the bare interface, while a bilayer increases it by 1.8 × 10⁻⁸ m² K W⁻¹ at 300 K. Contrary to expectations based solely on added thermal resistance, atomistic simulations using the LAMMPS package with Tersoff potentials indicate that the hBN layer redistributes the spectral phonon flux, suppressing contributions from the 8–12 THz range by up to 45%. The practical implication is that hBN interlayers should be avoided in thermally critical paths of GaN-on-AlN transistor stacks despite their beneficial role as chemical barriers.

title: Empirijski model za brzu procenu termičkog otpora granica faza u III-N heterostrukturama zasnovan na akustičkim parametrima materijala
abstract: Predlažemo empirijski model koji koristi samo tabelarno dostupne akustičke parametre – Debyejevu temperaturu, gustinu i transversalnu brzinu zvuka – za procenu termičkog otpora granica faza u binarnim i ternarnim III-azotidnim sistemima, bez potrebe za ab initio računanjem ili vremenski zahtevnim eksperimentima. Model je kalibrovan na skupu od 47 merenih TBR vrednosti iz literature i sopstvenih merenja za sisteme GaN/AlN, AlN/SiC, InGaN/GaN i GaN/Si, obuhvatajući temperaturni opseg 100–500 K. Srednja apsolutna relativna greška na skupu za validaciju iznosi 16,4%. Poređenjem s DMM i AMM modelima pokazano je da predloženi model daje bolje rezultate za sisteme s jakim fonoskim neusklađenostima, uz drastično smanjenje računarskog vremena. Model je implementiran kao slobodno dostupna Python biblioteka i namenjen je inženjerima koji projektuju toplotni menadžment III-N naprava.

title: Fluctuation theorems in active particle baths: breakdown of the Crooks relation
abstract: We investigate whether the Crooks fluctuation theorem holds for a passive tracer immersed in a bath of active self-propelled particles. The active bath is modelled as a collection of active Ornstein–Uhlenbeck particles (AOUPs) with persistence times ranging from 0.01 s to 10 s. The tracer is subjected to switching harmonic potentials between two stiffness values, and work distributions are recorded over 10⁶ switching cycles in simulation. For short persistence times the Crooks relation is satisfied within statistical error. As the persistence time exceeds the tracer relaxation time, systematic deviations appear: the log-ratio of forward and reverse work distributions is no longer linear in work, and the effective temperature inferred from the intercept differs from the solvent temperature by up to a factor of 2.4. We propose a modified detailed balance relation involving an effective free-energy functional that accounts for non-Markovian bath correlations, and validate it numerically. The work has implications for interpreting single-molecule pulling experiments in active biological environments.

title: Building a Telephone Speech Corpus for Serbian: Collection Protocol and Baseline Recognition Results
abstract: This paper describes the design and collection of TelSrp-100, a corpus of 103 hours of Serbian speech recorded over public switched telephone network and VoIP channels, spanning 412 speakers from four dialect regions of Serbia. Audio was downsampled to 8 kHz and passed through a narrowband codec simulation pipeline before annotation. Transcription was performed by trained annotators following guidelines adapted from existing South Slavic corpus projects. A hybrid HMM–DNN acoustic model was trained in Kaldi using 39-dimensional MFCC features with cepstral mean and variance normalisation. The baseline system achieved a word error rate (WER) of 24.3% on a held-out test set of 8.2 hours. Analysis of errors by channel type showed that VoIP segments introduced 18% more substitution errors than PSTN segments, attributed to packet-loss artefacts. The corpus and baseline recipe are made available under a Creative Commons licence through the CLARIN.SI infrastructure. The work establishes a reproducible benchmark for future Serbian telephone ASR research.

title: Noise Adaptation Strategies for Serbian Telephone ASR Using Convolutional Front-End Augmentation
abstract: This study examines the effect of three front-end augmentation strategies on the word error rate of a Serbian telephone speech recogniser when the channel introduces additive background noise, codec distortion, and linear convolutional reverberation. The baseline system is a time-delay neural network (TDNN) acoustic model trained on TelSrp-100. The three conditions evaluated are: (1) multi-condition training using simulated noise from the MUSAN noise set mixed at SNR levels between 0 and 20 dB, (2) SpecAugment applied during training, and (3) a learnable convolutional front-end replacing the fixed filterbank. All models are evaluated on 120 held-out recordings collected in three real call-centre environments in Vojvodina. Multi-condition training gave the largest absolute WER reduction of 4.1 percentage points compared to the clean-trained baseline. Combining multi-condition training with SpecAugment yielded an additional 1.3 percentage-point reduction. The learnable front-end offered marginal gains of 0.7 percentage points but increased training time by approximately 35%. Results suggest that data augmentation at the feature level remains more practical than architectural changes for low-resource conditions where the training set is under 200 hours.

title: Transfer Learning from Multilingual Wav2Vec 2.0 for Low-Resource Serbian Telephone ASR
abstract: Pre-trained self-supervised speech representations have shown strong results for low-resource languages, but their behaviour on narrowband telephone audio is not well characterised. This paper evaluates fine-tuning of a multilingual Wav2Vec 2.0 model (trained on 128 languages, excluding Serbian) on two Serbian telephone speech datasets: TelSrp-100 and a newly collected 22-hour set of customer-service calls, TelSrp-CS22. Fine-tuning was performed with connectionist temporal classification (CTC) loss using ESPnet2. Experiments examined the effect of fine-tuning data volume, ranging from 5 to 103 hours, and the effect of resampling the 16 kHz model inputs to simulate 8 kHz telephone bandwidth. With 103 hours of fine-tuning data and bandwidth-matched resampling, the model reached a WER of 16.7% on the TelSrp-100 test set, compared to 24.3% for the MFCC-TDNN baseline. With only 22 hours the model achieved 21.4% WER, suggesting useful transfer even with limited in-domain data. Error analysis found that digits and proper nouns remain the primary source of errors, accounting for 31% of substitutions.

title: Cardinal temperatures for germination and emergence in winter wheat cultivars grown in the Vojvodina region
abstract: Germination and emergence rates of seven winter wheat cultivars registered in Serbia were measured at nine constant temperatures ranging from 2 °C to 32 °C in controlled-environment chambers. A beta function was fitted to rate-temperature data to estimate base, optimum, and ceiling temperatures for each cultivar and developmental stage. Base temperatures for germination ranged from 1.8 °C to 3.1 °C, while ceiling temperatures varied between 29.4 °C and 33.7 °C. Emergence in soil showed a narrower thermal range than germination on filter paper, attributed to soil thermal buffering. Cultivars with lower base temperatures accumulated fewer degree-days to 50 % emergence under simulated early-autumn sowing conditions. The estimated cardinal temperatures were compared with values reported for Western European cultivars and showed systematically lower optima, consistent with the adaptation of local genotypes to continental autumn conditions. Results are directly applicable to parameterising the germination sub-module of process-based crop models.

title: Comparison of three thermal-time scales for predicting anthesis date in winter wheat across seven sowing dates
abstract: Predicting anthesis date in winter wheat is sensitive to the choice of thermal accumulation method. This study compared simple degree-days with a fixed base of 0 °C, degree-days with a cultivar-specific base temperature, and an asymmetric beta function accumulation for seven sowing dates ranging from mid-October to late November over three growing seasons (2011–2014) at an experimental station near Novi Sad. The dataset comprised 168 field observations across three cultivars. Root mean squared error of anthesis prediction was 5.2 days for the fixed-base method, 3.8 days for the cultivar-specific base, and 2.9 days for the beta function approach. The improvement from calibrated cardinal temperatures was largest for early sowings that exposed plants to extended cold periods. Vernalisation completeness, estimated from accumulated chilling units, explained residual variance not captured by any thermal accumulation method alone. Recommendations are given for selecting the appropriate time scale depending on data availability.

title: Photoperiod sensitivity coefficients for heading in winter wheat: estimation from field trials in Serbia and Hungary
abstract: Photoperiod sensitivity is a key parameter governing time to heading in winter wheat and is often poorly defined for locally bred cultivars. Using a dataset of heading dates from replicated field trials conducted at four sites in Serbia and two in Hungary between 2009 and 2015, photoperiod sensitivity coefficients were estimated for eleven cultivars by fitting a linear-plateau response to day-length at the time of double-ridge formation. Critical photoperiod ranged from 13.1 h to 14.7 h across cultivars, and sensitivity coefficients (additional thermal time required per hour of photoperiod below critical) ranged from 18 to 54 °Cd h⁻¹. Hungarian cultivars showed, on average, higher sensitivity than Serbian ones, consistent with their origin at slightly higher latitudes. A cross-validation leaving one site out confirmed that coefficients estimated at three or more site-years were stable enough for prediction at an independent location, with mean absolute error remaining below 4 days.

title: Thermal time requirements for developmental stages of FAO 300–500 maize hybrids in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Accurate thermal time requirements for successive developmental stages of maize are needed to schedule irrigation and predict grain-fill duration. This study characterised degree-day accumulation from emergence to ten defined Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt und CHemische Industrie (BBCH) stages for eight commercial maize hybrids of FAO maturity groups 300, 400, and 500, grown at two locations in Vojvodina over four seasons (2015–2018). Base temperature was fixed at 8 °C following published literature; upper threshold was set at 34 °C. Thermal time from emergence to silking ranged from 680 °Cd for the earliest hybrid to 870 °Cd for the latest. The fraction of total thermal time allocated to grain fill was more stable (0.40–0.44) than earlier studies suggested, regardless of FAO group. Year-to-year variability in accumulated degree-days to silking was less than 6 % at both locations, confirming thermal time as a reliable predictor of this stage. Grain moisture at physiological maturity was negatively correlated with post-silking thermal time accumulation rate.

title: Sensitivity of a simple wheat phenology model to errors in daily minimum and maximum temperature inputs
abstract: Phenology models driven by daily temperature records are subject to error propagation from the meteorological input layer. Using a validated degree-day model for winter wheat calibrated for four Vojvodina cultivars, systematic and random errors were introduced into daily minimum and maximum temperature series from three weather stations to quantify their effect on predicted anthesis and maturity dates. Systematic positive biases of 1 °C and 2 °C advanced predicted anthesis by 2.8 and 5.6 days on average, while random errors with standard deviations up to 2 °C caused shifts of less than 1 day because errors cancelled over the accumulation period. Errors in minimum temperature had roughly twice the impact on prediction of vernalisation completion compared with equal errors in maximum temperature. The study identifies the early-spring warming period (March–April) as the phase during which temperature measurement errors most strongly affect model output, suggesting that quality control of meteorological data should prioritise this window.

title: Estimating vernalisation requirements of winter wheat cultivars using controlled-environment experiments and field back-calculation
abstract: Vernalisation requirement is a poorly constrained parameter for many Central and Eastern European winter wheat cultivars. Controlled-environment experiments subjected five cultivars to vernalisation treatments of 0, 14, 28, 42, and 56 days at 4 °C before transferring plants to long-day growth conditions. Time to double ridge was recorded and used to estimate the minimum and saturation vernalisation requirements using a piecewise linear model. Saturation vernalisation ranged from 35 to 52 days, consistent with a facultative-to-winter habit classification. Results were compared with back-calculated vernalisation requirements derived from six years of field phenology records using a published chilling model. Agreement between laboratory and field estimates was within 5 days for four of five cultivars. The outlier cultivar showed anomalously early heading in warm winters, interpreted as incomplete vernalisation combined with strong photoperiod compensation. The parameterised values are provided in a table formatted for direct import into the DSSAT CERES-Wheat model.

title: Inter-annual variability in maize silking date at three Vojvodina locations 1991–2020: trends and the role of temperature change
abstract: Phenological records for maize silking maintained at three experimental stations in Vojvodina over thirty years (1991–2020) were analysed for temporal trends and their relationship to observed temperature change. Mean silking date advanced by 3.2 days per decade across all three stations and all tested FAO maturity groups, with the strongest trend at the southernmost station. Accumulated growing degree-days (base 8 °C, ceiling 34 °C) to silking showed no significant trend, while calendar date of silking advanced in parallel with the trend in spring-summer warming, confirming that earlier silking is thermally driven rather than a management artefact. Years with April–May mean temperature above the 75th percentile saw silking 7–9 days earlier than in cool years. The consistency of thermal time accumulation across decades supports the stability of the degree-day approach for long-term scheduling in the region, though it also implies that total heat stress exposure after silking may be increasing.

title: Cross-site transferability of winter wheat phenology model parameters within the Pannonian Basin
abstract: Phenology model parameters calibrated at one location may not predict correctly at distant sites due to differences in soil thermal regime, microclimate, and cultivar availability. Parameters for a three-phase thermal-photoperiod model were calibrated using data from six sites in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania for three widely grown winter wheat cultivars. A leave-one-site-out cross-validation was applied to test transferability. When parameters were calibrated at sites within 150 km of the target site, root mean squared error for anthesis was 3.1 days; when the nearest calibration site was more than 300 km away, RMSE increased to 5.7 days. The main source of transferred-parameter error was misrepresentation of the vernalisation environment rather than thermal time accumulation per se. Grouping calibration sites by winter severity class (using mean January temperature) reduced cross-site RMSE to 3.8 days even at distances above 300 km. Practical guidelines for regional model deployment are proposed.

title: Variable-rate fungicide scheduling in winter wheat using spatially explicit canopy wetness and disease risk indices
abstract: Timing and spatial targeting of fungicide applications in winter wheat are typically uniform across fields, despite documented within-field variation in canopy microclimate and disease pressure. This study coupled a spatially distributed canopy wetness model, driven by interpolated field-level air temperature and relative humidity from a temporary 12-node sensor network, with a published Septoria tritici blotch (STB) infection risk index across four fields (total 510 ha) in two growing seasons. Management zones were defined by combining baseline ECa-derived soil texture classes with crop canopy architecture estimated from early-season drone NDVI. Application decisions were made at zone level rather than field level. Compared with standard timing based on growth stage alone, the zone-based schedule reduced total fungicide active substance use by 16% over two seasons while maintaining grain yield and marketable quality. The sensor network deployment protocol is described in detail to enable replication.

title: Three-component cover crop mixtures and their effect on earthworm abundance and species composition in a maize–soybean–sunflower rotation
abstract: Earthworm abundance and species composition were assessed in plots with three-component cover crop mixtures (hairy vetch, winter rye, phacelia at equal proportions; and hairy vetch, oat, oilseed radish at equal proportions) and bare fallow over three years in a maize–soybean–sunflower rotation on Vojvodina chernozem. Earthworms were hand-sorted from three 25 × 25 × 30 cm soil blocks per plot in April and October. The hairy vetch/oat/radish mixture increased earthworm abundance by 31% over bare fallow (mean 78 versus 60 individuals m⁻²). Lumbricus terrestris made up 44% of individuals under cover crop treatments but only 28% under bare fallow. Earthworm abundance was positively correlated with soil organic carbon inputs estimated from cover crop biomass (r = 0.63). Results demonstrate that cover crop mixture choice influences soil macrofauna communities beyond effects attributable to tillage alone.

title: Inhibitory control in three-year-olds: comparing a structured toy-sorting task with the standard Day–Night paradigm
abstract: This study compared performance on a researcher-developed toy-sorting task with the widely used Day–Night paradigm in a sample of 87 children aged 36–42 months recruited from four preschool facilities in Novi Sad. The toy-sorting task required children to switch sorting rules mid-session under naturalistic play conditions. Both tasks were administered in counterbalanced order across two sessions separated by one week. Concurrent validity was examined using Pearson and Spearman correlations. The toy-sorting task showed moderate convergent validity with Day–Night scores (r = .54, p < .001), and its variance was better predicted by age in months. Test–retest reliability for the toy-sorting measure was adequate (r = .62) compared with Day–Night (r = .58). Findings suggest that behavioural observation tasks can capture inhibitory control with comparable psychometric properties to standardised paradigms while being more easily embedded in routine preschool activities. Implications for assessment in non-laboratory settings are discussed.

title: Age-related change in working memory updating between 48 and 72 months: a longitudinal observational study
abstract: Working memory updating was tracked in 61 children across four measurement points between ages 48 and 72 months using a researcher-developed object-substitution task administered during free play. At each session, children were asked to track changes in the location and identity of hidden objects under varying interference conditions. Raw scores and growth curve parameters were estimated using multilevel modelling. Results indicated a steep linear increase in updating capacity between 48 and 60 months, followed by a decelerating but still positive slope toward 72 months. Individual differences at 48 months predicted approximately 18% of variance in updating scores at 72 months after controlling for vocabulary and parental education. Sex differences were non-significant at all time points. The longitudinal design allowed separation of within-person change from between-person variation, addressing a limitation common in cross-sectional studies of this age range.

title: Cognitive flexibility measured through a rule-switching puppet game: factor structure and age norms for children aged 4 to 6
abstract: A puppet-based rule-switching game designed to elicit cognitive flexibility in a naturalistic context was standardised in a cross-sectional sample of 214 children aged 48–72 months from preschools in Vojvodina. The game involved sorting picture cards according to rules announced by a puppet character that changed rules every six trials. Confirmatory factor analysis tested whether the task loaded on a single flexibility factor versus a bifactor model including a general inhibition component. Results favoured the bifactor solution (CFI = .96, RMSEA = .047). Age-based norms expressed as T-scores are reported by 6-month bands. Socioeconomic status as indexed by parental occupation and education accounted for 11% of score variance. The task showed acceptable internal consistency (ω = .71) and inter-rater reliability for coding response accuracy (κ = .88). Normative tables and scoring guidelines are provided as supplementary materials for use by practitioners.

title: Relations among the three core executive function components in 5-year-olds: a latent variable analysis
abstract: Unity and diversity among inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, and working memory updating were examined in a sample of 142 five-year-olds using six behavioural tasks. Three tasks were standard laboratory measures and three were observationally derived tasks developed in the authors' laboratory. A correlated-factors confirmatory factor model fit the data better than either a single-factor or orthogonal solution (CFI = .94, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .051). Inter-factor correlations ranged from .41 to .63, consistent with the unity-and-diversity framework described in adult literature. The observational and laboratory tasks loaded comparably on their respective factors, supporting the validity of observational measurement. Language ability showed specific association with the updating factor (β = .29) but not with inhibition or flexibility factors after controlling for age and general cognitive ability. Findings are discussed in terms of measurement breadth in early assessment batteries.

title: Do observational EF tasks predict kindergarten academic readiness above laboratory measures? A six-month follow-up
abstract: This study tested whether ecologically valid observational executive function tasks provided incremental prediction of academic readiness over standard laboratory tasks in a follow-up design. A sample of 98 children (mean age at baseline 66 months) completed three laboratory EF tasks and three observational EF tasks in the final kindergarten semester. Six months later, teachers rated children's early literacy and numeracy readiness and behavioural regulation using structured scales. Hierarchical regression analyses indicated that observational tasks accounted for an additional 9% of variance in teacher-rated numeracy readiness (ΔR² = .09, p = .003) and 7% in behavioural regulation (ΔR² = .07, p = .011) after entering laboratory task scores in the first step. Literacy prediction was not significantly improved. Results suggest that observational measures capture context-relevant aspects of self-regulation that complement laboratory assessments for school-readiness purposes.

title: Parenting stress and children's inhibitory control at age 4: cross-lagged associations in a two-wave community sample
abstract: Bidirectional associations between maternal parenting stress and children's inhibitory control were examined across two waves in 134 mother–child dyads from Vojvodina. Parenting stress was assessed at child age 36 and 48 months using a Serbian adaptation of the Parenting Stress Index short form. Inhibitory control was measured at the same time points with three observational tasks embedded in a standardised play session. A cross-lagged panel model showed that parenting stress at 36 months predicted lower inhibitory control at 48 months (β = −.22, p = .009) after controlling for initial child ability and maternal education. The reverse path, from child inhibitory control to subsequent parenting stress, was non-significant (β = −.09, p = .21). The effect remained after including child temperament ratings as a covariate. Results point to a directional influence from the parenting context to children's self-regulatory development rather than a purely child-driven effect.

title: Assessing executive function in Roma preschool children: task adaptation and preliminary data from a community sample in southern Serbia
abstract: Standard executive function tasks rely on verbal instructions, pictorial conventions, and test-taking familiarity that may disadvantage children from minority cultural contexts. This paper reports the adaptation and preliminary validation of three observational EF tasks for use with Roma preschool children from settlements in southern Serbia. Task stimuli were revised following structured interviews with community mediators and two rounds of cognitive pretesting with 24 children. Adapted and original task versions were then administered to 41 Roma and 43 non-Roma children aged 54–66 months matched on age, sex, and preschool attendance. On adapted tasks, the performance gap between groups narrowed substantially for inhibitory control (Cohen's d reduced from 0.81 to 0.44) and working memory (d reduced from 0.74 to 0.39). Flexibility scores remained more disparate. The paper discusses practical and ethical considerations in adapting assessments for underrepresented groups in the Serbian early childhood context.

title: Measurement invariance of observational executive function tasks across age groups from 36 to 84 months
abstract: Three observational EF tasks developed by the Novi Sad group were administered to 328 children distributed across five 12-month age bands from 36 to 84 months to test measurement invariance across the preschool period. Multigroup confirmatory factor models were estimated for configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Results indicated configural and metric invariance across all age bands but only partial scalar invariance: two item intercepts showed significant non-invariance at the youngest band (36–48 months). Practical implications of partial invariance are quantified using latent mean difference estimates with and without constraining non-invariant intercepts. The pattern suggests that the tasks measure the same constructs across the preschool period but that direct score comparisons at the youngest ages should be interpreted cautiously. Suggestions for item revision to achieve full scalar invariance are discussed, along with considerations for longitudinal tracking studies that span a wide age range.
