title: EF trajectories from age 3 to 6 in children with and without language delay: results from a prospective cohort study
abstract: Executive function development was compared between children with identified expressive language delay (ELD) and typically developing peers across four annual measurement points from age 36 to 72 months in a cohort of 189 children (63 with ELD, 126 controls) followed through the Vojvodina Early Development Study. Three core EF components were each assessed with two observational tasks per wave. Multilevel growth curve models indicated that children with ELD showed lower initial levels of working memory and inhibitory control but similar rates of growth compared with controls, resulting in a persistent gap without convergence. Cognitive flexibility trajectories did not differ significantly between groups at any time point. Language comprehension at age 36 months was a stronger predictor of initial EF level than expressive vocabulary. Findings support partial independence of EF from expressive language ability and have implications for early intervention prioritisation.

title: Hand grip strength as a predictor of touchscreen task performance in adults over 60: a correlational study
abstract: Sensorimotor research in HCI has tended to focus on tremor and reaction time, while grip strength—a widely used clinical marker of overall physical decline—has received less attention in usability contexts. This study measured hand grip strength using a Jamar hydraulic dynamometer in 74 adults aged 60–81 alongside a battery of standardised touchscreen tasks covering tapping, swipe gestures, pinch-to-zoom, and text entry. Grip strength ranged from 8 to 31 kg in the sample. Correlation analysis revealed moderate negative associations between grip strength and task completion time for swipe gestures (r = −0.39, p < 0.001) and pinch-to-zoom (r = −0.42, p < 0.001), but a weaker association for single-target tapping (r = −0.22, p = 0.06). Hierarchical regression controlling for age, cognitive screening scores (MoCA), and digital experience showed that grip strength explained an additional 7 % of variance in swipe task time. These findings suggest that grip strength assessment could provide useful supplementary information in pre-deployment usability screening for health and assistive applications targeting older populations.

title: Cognitive accessibility in public health campaigns: a framework for Serbian health communicators
abstract: This book chapter presents a practical framework for assessing and improving the cognitive accessibility of materials produced by public health bodies in Serbia. The framework integrates three evaluation layers: linguistic complexity (using the SRI readability index), visual information load (assessed via expert panel rating), and audience mental model alignment (assessed via brief structured interviews with target readers). Each layer is operationalised with a five-point scale, and cutoff scores corresponding to different literacy strata of the Serbian adult population are provided based on data from the 2014 European Health Literacy Survey Serbia subsample (n = 412). Two case studies are presented: a national tuberculosis awareness poster and a paediatric vaccination leaflet, both of which underwent full framework evaluation and revision. The chapter is intended as a practical resource for health communication officers working in public health institutes and hospitals without access to specialist academic expertise.

title: Autonomy-supportive versus controlling language in motivational texts for increasing walking behaviour: a two-week diary study
abstract: Grounded in self-determination theory, this experiment examined whether daily motivational text messages framed with autonomy-supportive language (emphasising choice and personal relevance) differed from controlling language (emphasising obligation and external expectations) in promoting daily step counts and intrinsic motivation for walking. Eighty-four sedentary adults from Novi Sad were randomised to one of three conditions: autonomy-supportive SMS, controlling SMS, or no-message control. Step counts were logged via a wrist-worn accelerometer over 14 days. Participants receiving autonomy-supportive messages accumulated on average 1,240 more steps per day than the control group (95% CI: 490–1,990) and reported higher autonomous motivation on a post-study questionnaire. The controlling message group did not differ significantly from the control. Autonomous motivation at day 7 partially mediated the effect on day-14 step counts (indirect effect β = 0.18, bootstrapped CI: 0.06–0.33). Findings support applying autonomy-supportive communication principles when designing brief mobile health nudges.

title: Grief after war-related loss: Bereavement experiences among elderly survivors in Bosnia-Herzegovina twenty years on
abstract: Twenty years after the 1992–1995 war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, this study examined grief in 24 older adults (aged 63–81) who had lost a spouse or child to wartime violence. Conducted in Sarajevo and Tuzla in collaboration with a local non-governmental organisation, the research used narrative biographical interviews of 90–120 minutes. Thematic analysis identified persistent features of traumatic grief that did not follow normative recovery timelines reported in Western European literature, including cyclical re-experiencing triggered by political commemorations and ongoing impunity for wartime violence. Many participants described grief as inseparable from unresolved questions of truth and justice, complicating conventional diagnostic framing. Findings suggest that political context should be treated as a structural determinant of grief chronicity rather than an individual moderating variable.

title: Greek Liturgical Loanwords in the Vita of a Serbian Holy Monk: A Lexical Survey
abstract: The paper presents a lexical survey of Middle Greek loanwords embedded in a fifteenth-century Serbian Church Slavonic vita of a monastic saint preserved in two manuscript copies held at the Hilandar Research Library digital collection. Working from diplomatic transcriptions of both copies, 312 lexemes of demonstrable Greek origin were identified and classified according to semantic domain (liturgical action, monastic hierarchy, sacred objects, temporal markers), phonological adaptation pattern, and morphological integration into the Church Slavonic nominal and verbal systems. The survey draws on the Lexicon of Medieval Serbian Language (Rečnik crkvenoslovenskog jezika) for comparison and supplements it with unpublished glosses from marginalia in both manuscripts. Results show that approximately 68% of Greek-origin terms are restricted to one of the two manuscript copies, pointing to divergent editorial strategies in transmission rather than simple copying. The study also notes eight previously unrecorded lexical calques not listed in existing reference dictionaries, proposed here for inclusion in ongoing lexicographic revision.

title: Identifying Scribal Hands in the Resava Corpus: A Statistical Approach to Letter-Form Distribution
abstract: Scribal hand identification in Resava-tradition manuscripts has relied largely on qualitative paleographic judgment. This paper tests whether quantitative letter-form analysis can provide reproducible, examiner-independent attribution. Forty-three digitised folios from six manuscripts conventionally assigned to the Resava orthographic school (late fourteenth to mid-fifteenth century) were processed using a semi-automated contour-extraction procedure applied to high-resolution scans, measuring seventeen morphological parameters per character type for five high-frequency letters. A hierarchical cluster analysis of the resulting 3,612-instance dataset produced groupings consistent with traditional attributions in four of the six manuscripts and suggested revised attributions in two cases, including a colophon-identified codex previously considered homogeneous. The method is presented not as a replacement for expert paleographic evaluation but as an auxiliary screening tool for large-scale corpus work. All parameter data and clustering scripts are deposited in an open repository maintained by the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.

title: Orthographic Markers as Indicators of Scribal Training: Evidence from Colophon-Dated Serbian Church Slavonic Manuscripts
abstract: This study uses a set of 18 Serbian Church Slavonic manuscripts bearing reliable colophon dates between 1380 and 1480 to evaluate six candidate orthographic features previously proposed in the literature as school-specific markers. The features examined are: yat reflex spelling, jer handling in weak position, ligature usage frequency, nasal vowel retention, Greek-origin titlo placement, and word-division practice. Each feature was coded across all dateable manuscript pages (totalling 2,140 folios) and subjected to logistic regression modelling to assess predictive strength for Resava-versus-Raška school assignment. Four features showed statistically significant discriminatory power (p < 0.05), while two — nasal vowel retention and titlo placement — proved inconsistent across the dated sample and are argued to reflect individual scribal preference rather than school training. The study provides a ranked feature list intended as a practical decision aid for manuscript attribution work and comments on the limitations of the method when applied to undated or partially legible material.

title: Greek Ecclesiastical Terminology for Monastic Rank in Serbian Vitae: Phonological Adaptation Across Two Centuries
abstract: The paper traces the phonological adaptation of twelve Greek terms designating monastic ranks (e.g. equivalents of hieromonachos, protosyngkellos, megaloskhemos) as they appear in Serbian hagiographic vitae spanning the thirteenth through fifteenth centuries. Drawing on a corpus of 34 texts, the study documents how the phonological shape of each term shifts across the period, distinguishing between adaptation patterns attributable to oral transmission, those traceable to the influence of contemporaneous Byzantine Greek pronunciation, and those produced by analogical pressure from the native Church Slavonic morphological system. Quantitative coding of 684 individual attestations shows that adaptation trajectories differ significantly between terms with high liturgical frequency and those occurring only in narrative contexts, suggesting that high-frequency liturgical vocabulary was subject to conservative orthographic stabilisation in scribal practice while lower-frequency terms continued to vary. The paper proposes a differentiated model of lexical integration that supplements the single-pathway accounts found in earlier Church Slavonic lexicology.

title: A Digitisation and Annotation Protocol for Serbian Church Slavonic Hagiographic Manuscripts: Lessons from a Pilot Corpus of Twelve Codices
abstract: This paper reports on the design and testing of a digitisation and XML-based annotation protocol developed for Serbian Church Slavonic hagiographic manuscripts as part of a pilot project conducted between 2021 and 2023. Twelve codices from four holding institutions in Serbia were digitised using standardised lighting conditions and a resolution of 600 dpi; 1,340 folios were then transcribed diplomatically and encoded in a TEI P5-compatible schema extended to accommodate features specific to medieval South Slavic manuscripts, including marginal glosses, scribal corrections, catchword positions, and rubrication. The paper discusses decisions made during schema design, particularly regarding the representation of ambiguous letterforms and the handling of damaged or illegible passages, and evaluates inter-annotator agreement scores (Cohen's kappa ranging from 0.71 to 0.89 across feature types) obtained in a consistency trial involving three annotators. The protocol documentation and a sample of 120 annotated folios are released under an open licence to facilitate comparable work on related corpora.

title: Marginal Glosses as Evidence of Reader Competence in Serbian Church Slavonic Vitae: A Survey of Lexical Commentary in Fifteen Manuscripts
abstract: Marginal glosses in Serbian Church Slavonic manuscripts have received comparatively little systematic attention as sources of evidence for the linguistic competence of medieval readers and the circulation of liturgical knowledge. This paper surveys all identifiable lexical glosses — defined as interlinear or marginal explanations of single words or short phrases — in fifteen hagiographic manuscripts dating from the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, drawn from collections in Serbia, Montenegro, and North Macedonia. A total of 418 glosses were catalogued, of which 61% gloss Greek-origin terms with Serbian vernacular or simpler Church Slavonic equivalents, 24% provide synonyms within Church Slavonic, and 15% are content annotations without strict lexical function. Analysis of the gloss hands against the main text hands in each codex suggests that glossing was predominantly a post-copying activity carried out by different readers, though in three manuscripts gloss hands are consistent with the main scribal hand. The paper argues that the distribution of glossed Greek vocabulary reflects changing levels of active Greek literacy among Serbian monastic readers across the period.

title: Dialect Colouring in Serbian Rural Prose Dialogue, 1900–1935: Lexical and Morphophonological Markers
abstract: Writers of rural-themed Serbian prose in the early twentieth century commonly introduced dialect features into character dialogue as a marker of authenticity and local colour. This paper systematically documents which morphophonological and lexical features appear in dialogue in 65 rural-set short stories published between 1900 and 1935, comparing them against attestations in the available historical dialectological literature for the relevant regions. Features coded include reflex of Old Slavic yat, loss of infinitive ending -ti, pronoun form variation, and region-specific vocabulary items. The study finds that authors selectively reproduced three to five salient dialect features per text while avoiding rarer or typographically awkward ones. Comparison across three regional settings (Šumadija, Vojvodina, and Stara Raška) shows that Vojvodina-set texts display the lowest rate of morphophonological dialect marking, likely reflecting the more standardised editorial environment of the Novi Sad press.

title: Terenski protokol za dokumentaciju ugroženih vojvođanskih vernakula: iskustvo iz Bačke
abstract: Rad opisuje metodologiju terenskog rada primenjenu u okviru višegodišnjeg dokumentacionog projekta šokačkih i bunjevačkih govora u Bačkoj. Razrađen je protokol koji uključuje sociolingvistički upitnik, slobodni narativni intervju i niz fonetski kontrolisanih čitalačkih zadataka. Posebna pažnja posvećena je etičkim aspektima rada s manjinskim zajednicama i postupku dobijanja informisane saglasnosti. Opisuje se tehničko rešenje za terensko snimanje: korišćenje kondenzatorskih mikrofona u kombinaciji sa prenosivim snimačima visokog dinamičkog opsega. Prikazuju se izazovi pristupa govornicima najtanarijeg starosnog sloja (75+) i problemi transkripcionog kodiranja specifičnih fonetskih obeležja koja nisu pokrivena standardnim IPA simbolima. Na osnovu dosadašnjeg iskustva predložen je skup preporuka za buduće terenske kampanje u sličnim kontaktnim sredinama.

title: Flux decline during cross-flow ultrafiltration of whey protein concentrate: effect of pH and ionic strength on cake layer resistance
abstract: Flux decline was examined during dead-end and cross-flow ultrafiltration of whey protein concentrate (WPC-35) using 10 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at pH values of 4.6, 6.0, and 7.0 and NaCl concentrations of 0, 50, and 150 mM. Flux was measured at transmembrane pressures of 1–4 bar at 25 °C. The cake filtration and intermediate blocking models were fitted to experimental flux–volume data. At pH 4.6 (near the isoelectric point of β-lactoglobulin), specific cake resistance increased by a factor of 3.2 compared with pH 7.0, attributed to denser packing of aggregated protein particles. Ionic strength of 150 mM reduced electrostatic repulsion and increased resistance by 40% relative to salt-free conditions. Scanning electron microscopy of the membrane surface confirmed a compact, heterogeneous deposit at low pH. The results provide quantitative input for process design when handling acid whey fractions.

title: Characterisation of protein deposit layers on polyethersulphone membranes by atomic force microscopy and confocal laser scanning microscopy
abstract: Protein deposit layers formed during ultrafiltration of bovine serum albumin (BSA) and β-lactoglobulin solutions were characterised by atomic force microscopy (AFM) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). Membranes with nominal molecular weight cut-offs of 10, 30, and 50 kDa were fouled at constant transmembrane pressures of 1.5 and 3.0 bar. AFM height images revealed root-mean-square roughness values of 38–112 nm for fouled surfaces compared with 6–14 nm for clean membranes. CLSM cross-sections using fluorescently labelled BSA showed deposit thicknesses of 2–8 µm depending on operating pressure and protein concentration. Adhesion force measurements by AFM colloidal probe technique indicated protein–membrane adhesion forces of 1.2–4.7 nN, with the 10 kDa membrane showing the highest adhesion. These data support mechanistic fouling models that distinguish surface coverage from pore blockage.

title: Comparison of sodium hydroxide and alkaline hypochlorite cleaning protocols for ultrafiltration membranes fouled with dairy process streams
abstract: Three laboratory-scale cleaning protocols were evaluated for polyethersulphone and ceramic ultrafiltration membranes fouled with skim milk and cottage cheese whey streams. Protocol A used 0.5% NaOH at 50 °C for 30 min; Protocol B used 200 ppm NaOCl followed by 0.5% NaOH at 40 °C; Protocol C used 0.3% NaOH with 0.1% sodium dodecyl sulphate at 45 °C. Hydraulic cleaning efficiency was assessed by pure water flux recovery (PWFR) and irreversible fouling resistance. Protocol B achieved the highest PWFR of 97.4% for polyethersulphone membranes but reduced membrane lifetime by approximately 18% after 30 cleaning cycles, as indicated by contact angle measurements and SEM analysis. Protocol C preserved membrane integrity better and achieved PWFR of 93.1%. Ceramic membranes showed consistently higher PWFR across all protocols (>98%). The results inform CIP cycle design for dairy ultrafiltration plant operations.

title: Transmembrane pressure control strategies for minimising irreversible fouling in continuous whey protein ultrafiltration
abstract: A pilot-scale cross-flow ultrafiltration system (10 m² polyethersulphone, 10 kDa) was used to investigate three transmembrane pressure (TMP) control strategies during continuous concentration of sweet whey protein from an initial 0.9% total protein to a target 4.5% total protein. Strategy 1 maintained constant TMP at 2.5 bar; Strategy 2 applied a stepwise TMP ramp from 1.0 to 3.5 bar over 120 min; Strategy 3 implemented feedback TMP reduction triggered when the flux decline rate exceeded 5% per 10 min. After 8-hour runs, irreversible fouling resistance was 31% lower under Strategy 3 compared with Strategy 1, and total volumetric throughput was equivalent within 4%. Protein transmission at the permeate side was maintained below 2% in all runs. Energy consumption per kilogram of processed protein was reduced by 12% under Strategy 3. The findings support closed-loop TMP management as a practical approach to extending membrane service intervals.

title: Enzymatic pre-treatment with protease to reduce membrane fouling during ultrafiltration of fermentation broths
abstract: Pre-treatment of a model fermentation broth (Bacillus subtilis cultivation medium containing 12 g/L total protein) with a commercial serine protease (Alcalase 2.4L, 0.05–0.5% v/v, 40–55 °C, pH 7.5–8.5) was evaluated as a fouling mitigation strategy prior to 30 kDa polyethersulphone ultrafiltration. Hydrolysis degree was measured by the OPA method and ranged from 8 to 24%. At a hydrolysis degree of 16%, the limiting flux increased by 38% compared with untreated broth, and the total fouling resistance measured at 2 bar TMP was reduced by 47%. Permeate protein content increased proportionally with hydrolysis degree, which presents a trade-off for downstream product recovery. Circular dichroism confirmed partial loss of secondary structure in treated fractions. The study demonstrates that controlled proteolytic pre-treatment can serve as a feasible upstream option for bioreactor clarification steps.
venue: Biochemical Engineering and Bioprocess Journal

title: Temperature dependence of resistance-in-series parameters during ultrafiltration of milk protein concentrate
abstract: The resistance-in-series model was applied to cross-flow ultrafiltration of milk protein concentrate (MPC-80) at temperatures of 10, 20, 30, and 40 °C using a 50 kDa regenerated cellulose membrane. Intrinsic membrane resistance, reversible fouling resistance, and irreversible fouling resistance were quantified after 2-hour filtration runs at 2 bar TMP and a feed velocity of 0.5 m/s. Membrane resistance was temperature-independent at 1.8 × 10¹² m⁻¹, consistent with viscosity correction. Reversible fouling resistance decreased from 6.1 × 10¹² m⁻¹ at 10 °C to 2.7 × 10¹² m⁻¹ at 40 °C, attributed to reduced protein–protein interactions at higher temperature. However, irreversible fouling resistance increased above 35 °C, likely due to thermal denaturation and irreversible protein adsorption. An optimal operating temperature window of 25–32 °C was identified that balances low viscosity with acceptable irreversible fouling. These findings are relevant to CIP scheduling and inter-run flux restoration.

title: Effect of membrane surface modification with polyethylene glycol grafting on fouling propensity during β-lactoglobulin ultrafiltration
abstract: Polyethersulphone membranes (10 kDa) were surface-modified by UV-initiated grafting of polyethylene glycol methacrylate (PEGMA) at monomer concentrations of 1, 3, and 5 wt% in aqueous solution. Grafting density was characterised by ATR-FTIR, XPS, and water contact angle measurement. Contact angle decreased from 68° for unmodified membranes to 34° for the 5 wt% PEGMA membrane, confirming increased hydrophilicity. Fouling experiments with β-lactoglobulin (2 g/L, pH 6.8, 50 mM phosphate buffer) at 2 bar TMP showed that total fouling resistance was reduced by 56% for the 5 wt% grafted membrane relative to the control. Pure water flux after a standard NaOH cleaning step was 99.1% recovered for the modified membrane versus 88.4% for the unmodified control. Protein transmission was not significantly affected by grafting at the concentrations tested. Long-term stability of the graft layer over 20 fouling–cleaning cycles was confirmed by reproducible contact angle values.

title: Ultrafiltration membranes in bioprocess clarification: fouling, cleaning and lifetime considerations
abstract: This chapter reviews the use of polymeric ultrafiltration membranes in the clarification and concentration of protein-rich bioprocess streams, with emphasis on the mechanisms governing flux decline, strategies for fouling prevention, and approaches for determining cleaning protocol effectiveness. Topics covered include: the role of protein conformation and aggregation state in foulant deposit formation; the resistance-in-series framework as a diagnostic and modelling tool; alkaline and oxidative CIP chemistries and their impact on membrane material integrity over extended operational lifetimes; and criteria for membrane replacement decisions based on irreversible fouling resistance accumulation. The chapter draws on experimental data from dairy whey, fermentation broth, and plant protein extract filtration studies conducted over the past decade. Practical guidance is provided for selecting membrane materials, operating conditions, and CIP schedules in industrial bioprocess clarification applications.

title: Fouling behaviour of pea protein isolate during ultrafiltration: comparison with whey protein at equivalent protein content
abstract: The fouling behaviour of pea protein isolate (PPI) solutions at 1, 3, and 6 g/L total protein was compared with that of whey protein isolate (WPI) at equivalent concentrations during ultrafiltration through 10 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at 2 bar TMP and 25 °C. PPI solutions exhibited 2.1-fold higher initial fouling rates than WPI at 6 g/L, attributed to the larger hydrodynamic diameter (122 nm vs. 18 nm, by dynamic light scattering) and broader size distribution of PPI aggregates. The cake compressibility index for PPI was 0.71 versus 0.54 for WPI. Alkaline CIP with 0.5% NaOH at 50 °C restored flux to 91% of initial for PPI-fouled membranes compared with 97% for WPI-fouled membranes, indicating a greater proportion of irreversibly adsorbed pea protein. Circular dichroism and intrinsic fluorescence confirmed that PPI contained higher levels of denatured globulin fractions contributing to irreversible adsorption. The study informs process design for plant-based protein ingredient manufacturing.

title: Inline turbidity and UV absorbance as real-time fouling indicators during ultrafiltration of fermentation harvest streams
abstract: Inline turbidity (860 nm) and UV absorbance (280 nm) sensors were installed upstream and downstream of a 30 kDa polyethersulphone ultrafiltration module operated during concentration of a model Escherichia coli cell lysate stream at pilot scale (2 m² membrane area). Sensor signals were correlated with offline measurements of total fouling resistance, cake layer dry mass, and irreversible fouling resistance across 24 filtration runs. Permeate-side UV absorbance showed a Pearson correlation of r = 0.91 with irreversible fouling resistance, enabling online prediction of cleaning requirement. A threshold permeate UV absorbance value of 0.08 AU was identified, above which irreversible resistance exceeded 2 × 10¹² m⁻¹ and CIP was necessary. Feed-side turbidity alone was a poor predictor of fouling severity (r = 0.46). The proposed inline monitoring approach allows data-driven CIP scheduling and reduces unnecessary cleaning interventions by an estimated 30% based on historical run data.

title: Impact of diafiltration buffer composition on fouling accumulation and product yield during ultrafiltration of antibody fragment fermentation permeate
abstract: Diafiltration of an antibody fragment (Fab) containing fermentation permeate (initial Fab concentration 0.8 g/L, host cell protein 2.3 g/L) was performed using 30 kDa polyethersulphone membranes with five buffer compositions varying in pH (6.0–8.0), ionic strength (50–250 mM NaCl), and the presence of 0.01% polysorbate 20. Total fouling resistance after 10 diavolumes was lowest at pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, with polysorbate 20 (3.8 × 10¹² m⁻¹), compared with highest resistance at pH 6.0, 50 mM NaCl, without polysorbate (9.4 × 10¹² m⁻¹). Fab yield in the retentate was 88–94% across all conditions. Host cell protein clearance improved significantly at higher ionic strength, reaching 72% reduction after 8 diavolumes at 250 mM NaCl. Polysorbate 20 addition reduced surface adsorption losses without measurable impact on membrane permeability after cleaning. The results identify practical buffer formulation criteria for Fab concentration steps in downstream processing.

title: Quantifying the contribution of protein–calcium complexes to irreversible membrane fouling in casein whey ultrafiltration
abstract: The role of calcium–protein interactions in irreversible fouling was investigated during ultrafiltration of model casein whey streams at calcium concentrations of 0, 1, 2, and 4 mM (as CaCl₂) at pH 6.2 and 7.0 using 10 kDa polyethersulphone membranes. Complexation of calcium with β-casein fragments and soluble caseins was monitored by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) of permeate fractions. Irreversible fouling resistance increased linearly with calcium concentration at pH 6.2, reaching 5.9 × 10¹² m⁻¹ at 4 mM Ca²⁺, versus a near-independent response at pH 7.0 (2.1–2.6 × 10¹² m⁻¹). A 0.2% citric acid pre-rinse prior to NaOH CIP improved irreversible resistance removal by 34% under high-calcium conditions. ICP-OES profiling of the cleaned membrane surface confirmed calcium persistence after alkaline-only cleaning. The findings support inclusion of an acidic chelating rinse step in CIP protocols for casein whey processing lines.

title: Effect of atomisation pressure on particle size distribution and reconstitution behaviour of encapsulated ascorbic acid by spray drying
abstract: Ascorbic acid solutions (20 % w/w) were spray-dried with maltodextrin DE 10–12 as wall material at wall-to-core ratios of 3:1, 4:1 and 5:1. Atomisation air pressure was varied between 1.5 and 3.5 bar in a two-fluid nozzle system. Outlet particle size (d50) ranged from 18 to 47 µm and was well described by a power-law correlation with atomisation pressure (R² = 0.93). Encapsulation efficiency, assessed by extracting surface versus total ascorbic acid, improved from 71 to 89 % as wall-to-core ratio increased. Reconstitution time in 50 mL of water at 25 °C was measured by turbidimetry and showed a 22 % reduction at higher atomisation pressure due to more porous particle structures revealed by SEM. Retention of ascorbic acid after 8 weeks at 38 °C and 75 % RH was above 85 % at the highest wall-to-core ratio tested.

title: Spatial variability of near-surface air temperature across a heterogeneous maize field in Vojvodina: a summer campaign
abstract: Near-surface air temperature was logged at 24 stations deployed across a 40-hectare maize field near Sremska Mitrovica during June–August 2012. Station spacing ranged from 80 to 320 m, with sensors mounted at 1.5 m above the canopy. Ordinary kriging and regression kriging against terrain-derived covariates were compared for spatial interpolation at 20-m resolution. Regression kriging reduced root-mean-square error from 0.61 °C to 0.38 °C relative to leave-one-out cross-validation. The largest temperature contrasts—up to 2.1 °C within a single afternoon—were associated with differences in soil moisture rather than topographic position, which is subdued in the flat Pannonian terrain. The study established a baseline dataset for subsequent downscaling experiments and identified soil moisture heterogeneity as the primary driver of within-field thermal variability in this region.

title: Bias correction of ERA5 near-surface temperature over flat agricultural terrain in the Pannonian Basin
abstract: ERA5 reanalysis hourly 2 m temperature fields were evaluated against a network of 31 meteorological stations distributed across northern Serbia and southern Hungary for the period 2010–2016. Mean absolute error for daily maximum temperature reached 1.8 °C during summer and 1.3 °C during winter before correction. Three bias-correction methods were tested: quantile mapping, empirical quantile mapping with seasonally stratified transfer functions, and a simple linear scaling approach. Empirical quantile mapping reduced mean absolute error to below 0.7 °C across all seasons. Performance was notably better at stations surrounded by irrigated fields compared to dryland sites, suggesting that local evapotranspiration feedbacks not captured in the reanalysis contribute a systematic cold bias. The corrected ERA5 product was then used as a background field for sensor-based downscaling experiments.

title: Estimating field-scale frost occurrence probability using a sparse thermistor network and logistic regression
abstract: Frost events pose significant risk to early-season vegetable crops in Vojvodina. This study developed a logistic regression model to estimate the probability of frost occurrence at unobserved field locations using minimum temperature readings from eight low-cost thermistor nodes, synoptic forecast output, and static spatial covariates including distance to water bodies and land cover class. A dataset of 312 nights from three growing seasons (2014–2016) was used for model fitting, with 78 additional nights from 2017 reserved for validation. The model achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.91 on the validation set. False-negative rate for actual frost nights was 6 %, which the authors consider acceptable for advisory purposes. Deployment cost per field using the proposed sensor configuration was estimated at under 400 EUR, making the approach accessible to medium-sized farms.

title: Statistical downscaling of synoptic temperature observations to 50-metre resolution using topographic and land surface indices
abstract: This paper presents the core methodological work from the author's doctoral research. Daily maximum and minimum temperature observations from 18 synoptic stations were downscaled to 50-metre grid cells over a 3 600 km² domain in Vojvodina using a regression tree ensemble trained on seven topographic and land surface covariates derived from a 10-metre DEM and MODIS land surface temperature composites. The ensemble comprised 200 bagged regression trees. Independent evaluation against 42 station years of withheld automatic weather station data showed a mean absolute error of 0.52 °C for daily maximum and 0.68 °C for daily minimum temperature. The larger error for minima reflects the more complex boundary layer processes governing nocturnal cooling. Seasonal stratification of the model improved winter minimum temperature estimates by 0.14 °C. The resulting daily temperature grids for 2010–2018 are archived and available on request.

title: Calibration drift in low-cost capacitive humidity sensors deployed outdoors: a 14-month field assessment
abstract: Low-cost capacitive humidity sensors are widely used in agricultural wireless sensor networks, but long-term field performance is poorly characterised. Sixty sensors of three commercial types were deployed at outdoor stations in Vojvodina from March 2020 to April 2021 and compared monthly against a calibrated chilled-mirror reference hygrometer. All three sensor types exhibited upward drift in relative humidity readings, averaging between 2.1 % RH and 5.8 % RH over 14 months depending on type. Drift rate accelerated after rainfall events exceeding 20 mm per day. A piecewise linear drift model fitted to monthly calibration points reduced residual error to below 1.5 % RH across all sensor types. The study recommends a maximum 90-day recalibration interval for unhoused capacitive sensors in continental climates with significant summer convective precipitation.

title: Combining low-cost IoT sensor networks and NWP model output for real-time heat stress index mapping in agricultural landscapes
abstract: Heat stress indices such as the temperature-humidity index are relevant for both livestock welfare and crop management. This study describes a data fusion system that ingests 10-minute observations from 34 IoT sensor nodes distributed across a 120 km² agricultural area in southern Vojvodina and combines them with hourly output from the ALADIN numerical weather prediction model operated by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. A weighted Bayesian updating scheme merges the NWP background field with sensor observations, accounting for sensor location quality flags and estimated representativeness errors. The fused temperature-humidity index fields were produced at 100-metre resolution. Comparison with independent reference stations during a nine-day heat wave in July 2022 showed that the fused product reduced spatial root-mean-square error by 31 % relative to the NWP field alone. Latency from measurement to map delivery averaged 4.2 minutes.

title: Microclimate sensor data fusion for site-specific irrigation scheduling: methods, data requirements, and operational constraints
abstract: Precision irrigation scheduling benefits from spatially detailed estimates of evapotranspiration and thermal stress, yet few operational systems integrate distributed sensor observations with weather model output in a coherent way. This book chapter reviews data fusion approaches applicable to field-scale agrometeorological applications, with emphasis on methods suitable for sparse sensor networks of 5–50 nodes. Kalman filter variants, optimal interpolation, and machine learning blending approaches are discussed in terms of computational requirements, sensitivity to sensor calibration errors, and data latency. Case studies drawn from deployments in Serbia and Hungary illustrate achievable accuracy and practical failure modes. The chapter also addresses data management obligations under precision agriculture contracts and discusses the mismatch between the spatial resolution of standard weather products and the resolution demanded by variable-rate irrigation systems.

title: Uncertainty quantification in field-scale minimum temperature forecasts derived from ensemble NWP and sparse sensor networks
abstract: Minimum temperature forecasts at field scale carry uncertainties arising from NWP model spread, representativeness errors in sensor observations, and interpolation artefacts. This preprint presents a framework that propagates all three uncertainty sources through a statistical downscaling chain to produce calibrated probability distributions of minimum temperature at 100-metre resolution for a 48-hour forecast horizon. The framework was evaluated over two growing seasons (2024–2025) using a 22-member NWP ensemble from the ECMWF open-data stream and 28 sensor nodes in Vojvodina. Coverage probability for the 80 % prediction interval was 0.77, indicating slight over-confidence attributed to spatial correlation in NWP errors. Sensitivity analysis showed that adding as few as four strategically placed sensors reduced the width of the 80 % interval by 18 % compared to the NWP-only baseline.

title: A Comparison of Map-Matching Algorithms for Low-Frequency GPS Traces in Urban Road Networks
abstract: Low-frequency GPS logging (one fix per 30–60 seconds) is common in commercial fleet telematics yet introduces significant positional ambiguity on dense urban grids. This paper evaluates four map-matching algorithms—Viterbi hidden Markov model, incremental shortest-path, fuzzy inference, and a baseline nearest-edge method—on a ground-truth dataset of 412 manually annotated bus trips collected in Novi Sad over three months in 2010. Matching accuracy is measured as the fraction of correctly assigned road segments. The Viterbi HMM achieves 91.4 % segment accuracy at 30-second intervals, outperforming the nearest-edge baseline by 14.2 percentage points. Runtime scales linearly with trip length for all tested methods. The paper also reports sensitivity to GPS horizontal dilution of precision values above 4.0, which reduces HMM accuracy by up to 6 percentage points and suggests a pre-filtering step. Code and dataset are made available for replication.

title: Schema Alignment Strategies for CAN-Bus and OBD-II Telematics Streams in Mixed Commercial Fleets
abstract: Commercial vehicle fleets increasingly combine older vehicles reporting proprietary CAN-bus frames with newer units transmitting standardised OBD-II PID data over cellular networks. Integrating these two streams without a shared schema produces duplicated or missing signal coverage for variables such as engine load, instantaneous fuel consumption, and wheel speed. This paper defines a two-layer alignment architecture: a syntactic translation layer that normalises byte encoding and unit conventions, and a semantic reconciliation layer that resolves overlapping variable definitions using an ontology derived from SAE J1939 and ISO 15765-4. The architecture is evaluated on a dataset from a Serbian logistics operator covering 38 vehicles and 14 months of operation. After alignment, cross-stream correlation of fuel consumption estimates improves from r = 0.61 to r = 0.94, and data completeness rises from 73 % to 96 %. Failure modes related to firmware versioning are discussed.

title: Interoperability of Telematics Data Formats in Road Transport: A Review of Standards and Gap Analysis
abstract: This book chapter surveys the landscape of telematics data interchange standards relevant to road freight and passenger transport as of 2016, covering DATEX II, SIRI, FCD formats from the TPEG family, and proprietary vendor schemas from five major European fleet management platforms. For each standard the chapter documents supported data types, update frequency assumptions, geographic scope, and licence conditions. A gap analysis identifies three recurring incompatibilities: inconsistent timestamp granularity across systems, absence of uncertainty quantification in position fixes, and conflicting definitions of trip boundaries in multi-stop operations. The chapter concludes with a compatibility matrix indicating which standard pairs can be bridged with deterministic transformations versus those requiring heuristic matching. The material is aimed at transport authorities and fleet operators planning data integration projects and does not assume deep technical background.

title: Real-Time ETA Estimation for Urban Bus Services Using a Gradient Boosting Model Trained on Historical GPS Trajectories
abstract: Accurate real-time arrival prediction for urban buses requires accounting for dwell time variability, signal timing, and traffic congestion simultaneously. This paper trains a gradient boosting model on 18 months of archived GPS fixes and schedule data from the Novi Sad public transport operator, covering 11 bus lines and approximately 2.4 million individual trip segments. Features include time of day, day of week, stop sequence position, distance to next stop, number of preceding stops in current trip, running headway deviation, and a rolling average of the past three segment travel times. The model achieves a mean absolute error of 42 seconds for predictions with a horizon of up to three stops, compared with 71 seconds for the schedule-based baseline and 58 seconds for a linear regression. Feature importance analysis shows that running headway deviation and recent travel time history account for 61 % of model gain. Deployment considerations related to data latency are discussed.

title: Uncertainty Propagation in ETA Estimates Derived from Multi-Source Telematics Data
abstract: ETA predictions that combine GPS probe data, loop detector readings, and schedule information inherit uncertainties from each source, but operational systems rarely quantify or communicate these uncertainties to end users. This paper develops a Monte Carlo propagation framework in which each input source is characterised by an empirically fitted error distribution: Gaussian for loop detector occupancy, truncated Laplace for GPS position error, and empirical bootstrap for schedule adherence. Propagated prediction intervals are calibrated against 90 days of ground-truth arrival records from three bus lines and two suburban train routes in the Vojvodina region. Coverage of nominal 80 % prediction intervals is 76.3 %, indicating mild overconfidence. Recalibration using isotonic regression raises coverage to 79.1 %. The framework adds approximately 18 ms per prediction on a standard workstation, which is acceptable for real-time use. Implications for passenger information displays are discussed.

title: Benchmarking Trajectory Segmentation Methods for Detecting Stop Events in Fleet GPS Data
abstract: Accurate automated detection of stop events—periods when a vehicle is stationary at a customer location, depot, or traffic signal—is a prerequisite for reliable trip chaining and dwell-time modelling in logistics applications. This paper benchmarks six segmentation methods against a manually labelled reference dataset of 1,180 trips from a regional courier operator, covering approximately 28,000 km of driving over four weeks. Methods include speed threshold, speed-and-duration threshold, density-based spatial clustering, change-point detection, and two hybrid variants. Evaluation metrics are precision, recall, and mean positional error of stop onset and offset times. The density-based method achieves the best F1 score of 0.91 but requires careful bandwidth selection; the speed-and-duration threshold method reaches F1 = 0.87 with no hyperparameter tuning and is recommended as a baseline. The paper characterises failure cases associated with urban congestion, which degrades all methods by up to 9 percentage points in F1.

title: Federated Data Exchange for Regional Freight Telematics: A Pilot Between Serbian and Romanian Operators
abstract: Cross-border freight operations in Southeast Europe involve multiple national telematics platforms that do not share a common interface standard, forcing operators to manage parallel systems and creating gaps in journey visibility at border crossings. This paper reports on a pilot federated exchange architecture developed under a bilateral research agreement, connecting telematics back-ends of two Serbian and two Romanian freight operators without requiring centralised data storage. The architecture uses a REST-based gateway with OAuth 2.0 authentication and a shared positional event schema negotiated among the four operators. During a three-month pilot covering 214 cross-border journeys, end-to-end position update latency across the federation averaged 1.4 seconds, and schema compliance reached 98.3 % of transmitted messages. Governance challenges—particularly around liability for data quality and divergent national regulations on driver data—are documented as lessons learned for future regional deployments.

title: Evaluating Transformer-Based Sequence Models for Short-Horizon ETA Prediction in Urban Bus Networks
abstract: Recurrent and attention-based sequence models have shown promise for time-series prediction tasks, but their performance relative to gradient boosting on operational bus ETA problems has not been systematically evaluated with matched feature sets and training data. This paper compares a vanilla Transformer encoder, a temporal convolutional network, an LSTM, and gradient boosting on the same dataset of 26 months of GPS and schedule data from Novi Sad city buses. Prediction horizons of one, three, and five stops are tested. At three stops the Transformer achieves a mean absolute error of 38.1 seconds versus 40.7 seconds for gradient boosting and 53.2 seconds for LSTM, a difference that is statistically significant at α = 0.01. However, the Transformer requires approximately 40 times more compute at inference time on CPU hardware, which is relevant for deployment on embedded roadside units. Recommendations for practitioners are provided based on the compute–accuracy trade-off analysis.
venue: European Journal of Transport Modelling and Simulation

title: Integrating Cellular Network Positioning Data with GPS Fixes for Continuous Vehicle Tracking in Tunnels and Parking Structures
abstract: GPS signals are unreliable inside tunnels and multi-level parking structures, creating gaps in continuous vehicle trajectory records that are problematic for applications such as tolling, fleet tracking, and ETA estimation. This paper investigates the use of LTE cell-ID positioning, which remains available in many such environments, as a gap-filling mechanism. A fusion algorithm combines GPS fixes with cell-ID observations weighted by an empirically derived accuracy model built from 3,800 km of ground-truth driving in the Vojvodina and Šumadija regions. Position error during GPS-unavailable segments falls from an interpolation baseline of 87 metres median error to 34 metres median error using the fused approach. The paper also characterises the accuracy degradation as a function of cell tower density and reports that rural areas with fewer than 0.8 towers per km² see limited benefit from the fusion. Dataset and accuracy model parameters are provided in supplementary material.
venue: Journal of Location-Based Services

title: Comparing Replanning Triggers in Dynamic VRP: Time-Based, Event-Based, and Hybrid Policies
abstract: Rolling-horizon frameworks typically replan at fixed time intervals, but event-triggered and hybrid policies have been proposed as alternatives. This paper presents a systematic comparison of three replanning trigger policies—fixed-interval, threshold-triggered (replanning when unserved request count exceeds a set value), and a hybrid combining both conditions—across 216 problem instances generated from real demand data in two Serbian cities. The hybrid policy reduces total route cost by 5.7 % relative to fixed-interval replanning with no increase in computation time, primarily by avoiding unnecessary replanning during low-activity periods and responding faster to demand surges. Threshold calibration is shown to be network-dependent: the optimal threshold in the denser city network is 40 % lower than in the sparser one. The paper provides a calibration procedure based on historical demand statistics.

title: Sensitivity of LWR-Based Corridor Models to Fundamental Diagram Shape: A Comparative Study on the E75 Corridor
abstract: Macroscopic corridor models derived from the Lighthill–Whitham–Richards kinematic wave theory require a specified fundamental diagram; however, the sensitivity of model outputs to the choice of diagram shape is rarely quantified in practice. This study implements four single-regime fundamental diagrams—Greenshields, Greenberg, Underwood, and Northwestern—within a discretised LWR solver and applies each to a 42 km stretch of the E75 corridor between Novi Sad and Subotica. Calibration relied on hourly loop detector volumes from eight counting stations for the years 1997–1998. Validation used independently collected travel times from a probe vehicle run on 34 days. The Underwood model produced the lowest mean absolute error in predicted travel time (2.4 minutes against a mean observed travel time of 31.8 minutes), while the Greenshields model consistently overestimated congestion propagation speed by 18–22%. The paper concludes that model choice has a material effect on queue spillback prediction and recommends the Underwood diagram as a default for free-flow-dominated rural corridors in the study region.

title: Electrodermal activity as an indicator of mental workload in simulated urban driving
abstract: This study investigated the sensitivity of electrodermal activity (EDA) to varying levels of cognitive demand during a simulated urban driving task. Twenty-two participants completed three driving scenarios of increasing complexity—residential street, signalised arterial, and high-density commercial zone—while EDA was recorded continuously at 256 Hz using a wrist-worn sensor. Skin conductance level (SCL) and the number of non-specific skin conductance responses were extracted per two-minute epoch. A repeated-measures ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of scenario complexity on SCL (F(2,42) = 14.3, p < 0.001), with SCL increasing by approximately 0.6 µS between the residential and commercial conditions. Phasic EDA burst frequency was moderately correlated with subjective NASA-TLX scores (r = 0.54). The results support EDA as a feasible, non-intrusive proxy measure of workload in short-duration driving tasks, though individual variability was substantial. Implications for real-vehicle deployment are discussed.

title: Gaze fixation patterns and lane-keeping deviation during hands-free phone conversation: a simulator study
abstract: Driver distraction from hands-free telephone use remains a contested issue in road safety research. This experiment used a fixed-base driving simulator with a 180-degree field of view to compare gaze behaviour and lateral vehicle control of 30 drivers under baseline (no secondary task) and hands-free conversation conditions. A remote eye-tracker sampled gaze at 60 Hz; lane position deviation and standard deviation of lateral position (SDLP) were computed from simulator logs at 10 Hz. During phone conversation, mean SDLP increased by 18% (p = 0.008) and the proportion of time drivers fixated on the forward roadway dropped from 78% to 64%. Fixation duration per glance increased by approximately 40 ms. Conversation content difficulty was manipulated using a spatial reasoning task versus a personal narrative; the spatial task produced larger SDLP increases. The findings indicate that cognitive load from verbal interaction, beyond manual distraction, impairs lane control measurably.

title: A multimodal approach to driver workload classification using heart rate variability and pupil diameter
abstract: Accurate, real-time estimation of driver cognitive workload requires signals that can be acquired unobtrusively in a moving vehicle. This paper reports a classification study in which 34 participants drove an instrumented vehicle on a 28 km mixed urban–rural route while performing auditory n-back tasks (0-back, 1-back, 2-back) presented via earpiece. Interbeat interval time series from a chest-worn ECG monitor and pupil diameter from a camera-based eye tracker served as features. Time-domain HRV metrics (RMSSD, pNN50) and mean pupil dilation relative to baseline were computed over 60-second windows. A linear discriminant analysis classifier achieved 71.4% accuracy in distinguishing three workload levels using combined features, compared to 58.2% with HRV alone. Pupil diameter contributed most to distinguishing the 0-back from 2-back conditions. Practical constraints on in-vehicle deployment of remote eye trackers under varying illumination are discussed.

title: Speed adaptation and headway maintenance among older drivers on interurban roads: an instrumented vehicle study
abstract: Older drivers are disproportionately represented in certain crash types associated with reduced hazard perception and slower information processing. This study examined speed choice and time headway in 42 drivers aged 65–78 and 42 younger controls (25–40) on a 55 km instrumented vehicle route covering two-lane rural, dual carriageway, and motorway sections. Vehicle speed, time headway, and lateral position were logged at 10 Hz via CAN bus. Older drivers maintained significantly shorter mean time headways on dual carriageways (2.1 s vs. 2.7 s, p < 0.01) despite lower mean speeds. Speed variance was higher in the older group on curved rural sections. Hierarchical regression indicated that self-reported driving confidence and miles driven per week were significant predictors of headway in the older group (adjusted R² = 0.39). The results suggest that older drivers may be more susceptible to workload-induced headway compression than speed reduction.

title: Characterising cognitive load during roundabout negotiation using OBD-II and wearable ECG data
abstract: Roundabouts reduce conflict points relative to signalised intersections but require continuous gap acceptance decisions that impose transient cognitive load. This field study recruited 29 licensed drivers who completed repeated passes through five single-lane roundabouts in Novi Sad under naturalistic conditions. Vehicle kinematics were captured via OBD-II at 5 Hz, and ECG was recorded at 500 Hz using a textile chest strap. Workload-related episodes were identified by HRV suppression (RMSSD < 20 ms) coinciding with deceleration events. Compared to straight mid-block segments, RMSSD dropped by a mean of 8.3 ms in the five seconds preceding roundabout entry. Heavier traffic volumes at peak hour amplified both the RMSSD decrease and braking intensity. Drivers with fewer than five years of experience showed a 40% longer HRV recovery period post-negotiation. The study demonstrates that OBD-II combined with wearable ECG is a low-cost alternative to full instrumented vehicle setups for targeted road geometry studies.

title: Naturalistic driving data collection methodology: lessons from a six-month study in Vojvodina
abstract: Large-scale naturalistic driving studies (NDS) generate rich behavioural data but require careful protocol design to control for habituation, data quality, and participant attrition. This chapter describes the methodological framework developed for a six-month NDS conducted with 61 volunteer drivers in Vojvodina province, Serbia. The instrumented platform logged forward video at 30 fps, GPS at 1 Hz, and four-axis accelerometry at 100 Hz. Recruitment, informed consent, and data anonymisation procedures are detailed. Attrition reached 18% by month four, primarily among participants over 60. Data completeness averaged 94.2% of expected trip records. Event detection algorithms for hard braking (longitudinal deceleration > 0.4 g) and sharp cornering were validated against manually coded video. The chapter identifies data synchronisation, storage costs, and regulatory compliance under Serbian personal data protection law as primary operational challenges, and recommends minimum viable instrumentation sets for research groups with limited budgets.

title: Effect of in-vehicle navigation instruction timing on glance behaviour and lateral control at motorway exits
abstract: Navigation systems that issue route guidance too early or too late relative to manoeuvre points can create transient workload spikes. This experiment tested three instruction timing conditions (800 m, 400 m, and 200 m advance distance) at motorway exit ramps in a fixed-base simulator. Forty participants, stratified by age (25–40, 41–60) and familiarity with the route, completed 12 exit events each. Glance frequency toward the instrument cluster display and mean gaze deviation from the road ahead were measured with a head-mounted tracker. SDLP in the 15 seconds before exit was lowest at 400 m instruction timing across both age groups. The 200 m condition produced the highest proportion of last-moment lane changes and the greatest SDLP increase. Older drivers showed larger gaze deviations regardless of timing condition. The 400 m timing recommendation aligns with existing EU human machine interface guidelines, providing experimental support for Serbian national adoption.

title: Workload-induced braking response time changes detected from naturalistic trip data in mixed urban–rural contexts
abstract: Braking response time (BRT) is a safety-critical parameter affected by driver cognitive state. This analysis used naturalistic trip data from 61 drivers collected over six months in Vojvodina to extract 1,847 hard-braking events meeting a threshold of 0.35 g deceleration onset. A proxy for prior workload was constructed from road geometry complexity (curve density per kilometre) and traffic density estimated from GPS stop-and-go patterns. Linear mixed-effects models with driver as a random effect showed that high-geometry-complexity segments preceded braking events with 53 ms longer estimated BRT compared to straight low-density segments (p < 0.001). Younger drivers (< 35 years) showed smaller workload-associated BRT increases (31 ms) than middle-aged drivers (50–65 years, 74 ms). Mileage accumulated in the preceding 90 minutes was independently associated with BRT elongation, suggesting a fatigue interaction. The methodology demonstrates that proxy workload variables derived from passive GPS and accelerometry can reveal population-level behavioural trends.

title: Comparing self-reported and physiologically derived workload measures across driver age groups: a field experiment
abstract: Discrepancies between subjective workload ratings and physiological indicators complicate the design of driver assistance systems tuned to actual cognitive state. This field experiment drove 45 participants (three age groups: 20–35, 36–55, 56–72) through a standardised 34 km route with defined segments of varying complexity. After each segment drivers completed the Subjective Workload Assessment Technique (SWAT), and mean HRV (SDNN), EDA mean level, and heart rate were recorded continuously. Pearson correlations between SWAT scores and physiological indices were moderate in the youngest group (r = 0.49–0.61) and consistently lower in the oldest group (r = 0.21–0.38), particularly for EDA. Age-group differences in the magnitude of physiological response per unit of subjective workload change were statistically significant. The findings suggest that physiological sensing systems calibrated on young-adult data may underestimate workload in older drivers, with direct implications for adaptive driver monitoring systems.

title: Suitability of consumer-grade smartwatch photoplethysmography for HRV-based workload monitoring in drivers
abstract: Research-grade ECG monitors are impractical for large-scale naturalistic driving studies. This paper evaluates whether a consumer smartwatch (optical PPG sensor) can provide HRV metrics of sufficient accuracy for driver workload estimation. Forty-one participants wore both a research ECG chest strap and a smartwatch during a 45-minute instrumented vehicle drive. Interbeat interval series from both devices were compared using Bland–Altman analysis; mean bias for RMSSD was −3.1 ms and limits of agreement were ±12.4 ms. Classification accuracy for high vs. low workload epochs using smartwatch HRV matched ECG-derived classification within 4.2 percentage points (67.9% vs. 72.1%). Agreement degraded at speeds above 90 km/h, plausibly due to motion artefact. PPG data quality dropped below acceptable thresholds in 11% of epochs, concentrated in periods of heavy braking. The results suggest that smartwatch PPG is adequate for group-level workload trend analysis but unreliable for individual real-time monitoring.

title: Lane change decision timing under workload: evidence from an instrumented vehicle study on the Novi Sad ring road
abstract: Lane change manoeuvres require visual scanning, gap estimation, and steering execution, tasks whose coordination may degrade under cognitive load. This study used an instrumented vehicle to record 28 regular commuters over four weeks of daily driving on a 12 km stretch of the Novi Sad ring road. Lane changes were detected automatically from lane departure warning system signals validated against forward video annotation. Cognitive workload was estimated from a composite score of EDA mean level and HRV RMSSD sampled in the 30 seconds before each lane change event. High-workload lane changes were characterised by shorter pre-change turn-signal activation intervals (mean 2.1 s vs. 3.4 s), higher lateral jerk, and less time-to-collision margin with the following vehicle. Drivers with higher trait anxiety, measured by the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory at recruitment, showed the largest timing reductions under workload. Implications for lane change assist system activation thresholds are discussed.

title: Pilot assessment of eye-blink rate and PERCLOS as passive workload indicators during urban commuting: preliminary data from Novi Sad
abstract: PERCLOS (percentage of eyelid closure) and blink rate are candidate passive indicators for drowsiness and cognitive overload that can be extracted from in-cabin cameras already present in newer production vehicles. This preprint reports preliminary data from an ongoing study in which 19 commuters drove their habitual morning and evening routes in Novi Sad (mean duration 22 minutes) while a cabin-facing camera recorded eye behaviour at 60 fps. OpenFace 3.0 was used to extract action unit AU45 (blink) and eyelid aperture time series. Morning drives showed lower PERCLOS values and higher blink rates compared to evening drives, consistent with fatigue accumulation. Segments with objectively higher traffic density correlated weakly with blink rate suppression (r = −0.31), suggesting active engagement. Data collection is ongoing; a full-sample analysis with physiological co-registration is planned for late 2026. Preliminary results are shared to invite methodological feedback ahead of journal submission.

title: Seasonal Decomposition of Facebook Page Engagement: A Weekly-Cycle Perspective
abstract: This study examines weekly cyclical patterns in engagement metrics—likes, comments, and shares—across 42 public Facebook pages operated by Serbian retail brands between January and December 2012. Classical multiplicative decomposition and X-11 filtering were applied to daily time series for each page. Results confirmed a consistent seven-day periodicity in all three engagement indicators, with Sunday and Monday showing statistically significant troughs relative to midweek peaks. The magnitude of the weekly cycle varied substantially across content categories: promotional posts exhibited sharper weekend drops than editorial or community-focused posts. A regression model including day-of-week dummies and post-type indicators explained 61% of variance in daily like counts. Findings suggest that retail page administrators systematically misalign posting schedules with observed audience activity windows, particularly for promotional content. The paper provides a straightforward diagnostic framework that brand managers can apply to their own page-level data without requiring advanced statistical tools.

title: Clustering Twitter Audiences by Intraday Activity Signatures
abstract: Twitter users exhibit distinct intraday rhythms of activity that are rarely exploited in content targeting. This paper applies k-means and hierarchical agglomerative clustering to 24-bin hourly activity histograms derived from 18,400 follower accounts of ten mid-sized news portals in the Western Balkans, collected over a 90-day window in 2013. Five robust audience clusters emerged: early-morning commuters, midday browsers, late-afternoon professionals, evening consumers, and irregular night users. Cluster membership was stable across the observation window (adjusted Rand index 0.74 on 30-day subsets). Multinomial logistic regression linked cluster membership to self-reported location, device type inferred from the API, and account age. The five-cluster solution replicated in a held-out sample of three additional portals. These activity signatures are proposed as scheduling anchors that allow portal editors to target content delivery to dominant audience clusters rather than posting at uniform hourly intervals.

title: ARIMA-Based Forecasting of Instagram Follower Growth for Small and Medium Enterprises
abstract: Reliable short-term forecasts of follower counts help SME managers allocate community-management resources. This paper fits univariate ARIMA models to weekly follower-count series for 67 Serbian SMEs across six industry sectors, covering 104 weeks ending in mid-2015. Model identification followed the Box-Jenkins procedure; automatic order selection via AICc was benchmarked against manual identification. For 51 of 67 series, ARIMA(1,1,1) or ARIMA(0,1,1) specifications produced the lowest out-of-sample RMSE over a 12-week forecast horizon. Sector-level differences were modest, though hospitality accounts showed higher residual variance attributed to event-driven spikes. Comparison with naïve random-walk and exponential-smoothing benchmarks confirmed statistically significant accuracy gains (Diebold-Mariano test, p < 0.05) for 38 series. The study also demonstrates that spike-filtering through Hampel identifier prior to model fitting reduces RMSE by an average of 9% across the sample. Practical guidance for SME practitioners is provided in an accessible appendix.

title: Engagement Rate Decay After Post Publication: A Hazard-Function Analysis
abstract: Once a social-media post is published, engagement accumulates rapidly and then decays. Quantifying this decay is useful for scheduling follow-up content and for comparing platform-level virality. This paper models the time-to-last-engagement distribution for 9,200 posts published on Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter by 30 organisations in Serbia and Croatia during 2015–2016. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and parametric Weibull hazard models were estimated for each platform. Median engagement half-life was 3.1 hours on Twitter, 11.4 hours on Facebook, and 18.7 hours on Instagram. The Weibull shape parameter indicated monotone decreasing hazard on all platforms, with the steepest decay on Twitter. Content type (video, image, link, text) significantly moderated decay rate; video posts showed 34% longer half-lives on Facebook relative to image posts. Results are used to derive platform-specific scheduling windows within which republication or boosting generates the largest incremental reach.

title: Detecting Structural Breaks in Brand Engagement Time Series: Evidence from Crisis Events
abstract: Corporate crises frequently cause sudden, lasting shifts in social-media engagement. This paper applies Bai-Perron multiple structural-break tests to daily engagement time series for 15 Serbian companies that experienced a publicly documented crisis event between 2014 and 2017. Series span 24 months per company. Structural breaks were detected in 13 of 15 series within a seven-day window around the crisis onset date. Post-break engagement levels were on average 22% lower than pre-break levels, and the autoregressive structure of the series changed for eight companies—indicating altered audience response dynamics, not merely a level shift. GARCH(1,1) models estimated on pre- and post-break sub-series showed increased conditional variance in the post-break period for nine companies. The paper discusses implications for crisis communication timing and for baseline recalibration when constructing engagement benchmarks after a reputational event.

title: Time-Series Segmentation of Content Calendars: A Dynamic Time Warping Approach
abstract: Content calendars for social-media channels often follow implicit rhythms that reflect editorial practice rather than audience demand. This paper uses dynamic time warping (DTW) distance and DTW-barycenter averaging to cluster the weekly posting-frequency series of 120 media and brand accounts across four platforms over 52 weeks in 2017. Clustering produced four interpretable calendar archetypes: burst-and-pause, steady-cadence, weekend-heavy, and reactive. Accounts following the steady-cadence archetype showed median engagement-per-post values 18% higher than the burst-and-pause group, controlling for follower count and content type via a fixed-effects panel regression. The reactive archetype, characterised by spikes triggered by external news events, showed the highest variance in engagement outcomes. DTW-based clustering is compared with Euclidean-distance clustering; DTW produced more homogeneous clusters (lower within-cluster sum of squares by 27%). The method is demonstrated as a diagnostic tool for content strategy audits.

title: Audience Behaviour Segmentation Using Recurrent Neural Networks on Longitudinal Engagement Logs
abstract: Long short-term memory (LSTM) networks can capture audience behaviour patterns that fixed-window statistical models miss. This paper trains LSTM-based sequence encoders on 18 months of per-user engagement logs (reactions, comments, shares, view durations) from a regional streaming and content platform with 340,000 registered users in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Encoded representations were fed into a k-means layer to derive behavioural segments. Six stable segments emerged from a sweep of k from 3 to 10, evaluated by silhouette score and external validation against self-reported survey preferences collected from 2,100 users. The LSTM-derived segments outperformed segments produced by aggregated frequency-recency-monetary (FRM) features on prediction of next-week content consumption category (macro-F1: 0.61 vs 0.48). Segment profiles—labelled binge viewers, topical dippers, passive scrollers, commenter-contributors, share-motivated readers, and lapsed returnees—are described and their implications for personalised push-notification scheduling are discussed.

title: Multivariate Granger Causality Among Engagement Signals Across Linked Social-Media Accounts
abstract: Organisations maintaining accounts on multiple platforms often observe correlated engagement movements, but the directional structure of those correlations is seldom examined. This paper applies pairwise and multivariate Granger causality tests to daily engagement series (reach, reactions, click-throughs) for 28 organisations maintaining simultaneous presence on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube over 156 weeks (2018–2020). Vector autoregression (VAR) models with lag order selected by AIC were estimated for each organisation. Granger causality ran predominantly from YouTube view counts to Facebook reactions (significant for 19 of 28 organisations at the 5% level), while LinkedIn engagement was largely Granger-independent of other platforms. Impulse-response functions show that a one-standard-deviation shock to YouTube views generates a detectable, positive response in Facebook reactions within two days for organisations in media and education sectors, but not for retail. These findings suggest platform sequencing strategies for cross-channel content amplification.
venue: International Journal of Digital Communication and Media Management

title: Predicting Optimal Posting Windows Using Gradient Boosting on Historical Engagement Features
abstract: Predicting the best time to post requires combining temporal features, content attributes, and platform-level contextual signals. This paper builds gradient boosting (XGBoost) models to predict whether a given one-hour posting window will fall in the top quartile of engagement-rate outcomes, using a dataset of 210,000 posts from 95 brand and media accounts in the Western Balkans region, spanning 2019–2021. Features include hour-of-day, day-of-week, lag-one and lag-seven engagement values, post type, account size bin, and a rolling 28-day audience activity index derived from follower interactions. The model achieves an AUC of 0.79 on a held-out test set, compared to 0.63 for a logistic regression baseline. SHAP decomposition identifies hour-of-day and the rolling activity index as the dominant contributors. A simulated A/B scheduling experiment on 12 accounts over eight weeks shows a 14% average increase in median engagement rate when posts are timed using model predictions versus the accounts' historical default schedules.

title: Content Scheduling Optimisation Under Algorithmic Feed Constraints: A Simulation Study
abstract: Platform feed algorithms throttle organic reach in ways that interact with posting time and frequency. This paper builds a discrete-event simulation of a feed-ranking process calibrated to publicly documented parameters of a major social platform's ranking model, and uses it to evaluate 48 scheduling policies across a grid of posting frequencies (1–5 per day) and inter-post intervals (2–12 hours). Simulated reach and engagement outcomes are generated for 1,000 virtual follower agents whose activity follows empirically fitted lognormal intraday distributions derived from a real-follower panel dataset (n = 4,200 users, 12 weeks). Policies with moderate frequency (2–3 posts per day) and asymmetric timing—skewed toward identified activity peaks—consistently outperform uniform-interval policies by 8–21% in simulated reach. Diminishing returns to frequency become sharply negative above four posts per day under low-overlap scheduling. The simulation framework is made available as a configurable Python tool.

title: Temporal Attention Mechanisms for Engagement Forecasting in Sparse Data Regimes
abstract: Small organisations with limited posting histories present a sparse-data challenge for engagement forecasting models trained on large accounts. This paper investigates whether transformer-style temporal self-attention models—pre-trained on a large multi-account corpus and then fine-tuned—outperform account-specific ARIMA and gradient boosting models for accounts with fewer than 52 weeks of history. Experiments use a corpus of 1,840 brand accounts (800,000 posts, 2020–2023) covering Serbia, Croatia, Hungary, and Romania. Pre-trained temporal attention models fine-tuned on as few as 12 weeks of account-specific data match the RMSE of fully fitted ARIMA models at 40 weeks of history on average, and outperform them below 20 weeks. Performance gains are largest for accounts in volatile engagement regimes (high kurtosis in raw series). The paper also documents failure cases where pre-training corpus mismatch—different platform or language—degrades fine-tuned model accuracy relative to simple baselines.

title: Benchmarking Engagement Metrics Across Platforms: Comparability, Definitions, and Measurement Artefacts
abstract: Cross-platform engagement comparisons are routinely made in industry reports but rarely scrutinised for definitional consistency. This paper documents the operational definitions of nine engagement metrics (reach, impressions, reactions, comments, shares, saves, click-throughs, video views, and story exits) as specified in the developer documentation of four major platforms during 2022–2024, identifying 23 definitional divergences that affect cross-platform aggregation. Using data from 55 accounts tracked simultaneously across platforms, the paper quantifies the magnitude of artefactual differences attributable purely to definition divergence: reach figures for the same underlying content differ by up to 38% depending on which platform's counting convention is applied. A harmonisation protocol is proposed and tested, reducing cross-platform variance attributable to measurement artefacts by approximately 60%. The paper is intended as a reference for researchers designing multi-platform studies and for practitioners constructing unified analytics dashboards.

title: A meta-learning framework for few-shot financial time-series forecasting: design and initial evaluation
abstract: This paper presents the design and preliminary evaluation of a Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) framework adapted to financial time-series forecasting tasks where each target series contains very few observations. The meta-training set is constructed from 1,200 synthetic series generated by a parameterised data-generating process calibrated to observed statistical properties of e-commerce revenue data, supplemented by 140 real series from anonymised partner datasets. The meta-learner is a two-layer LSTM initialised via MAML; inner-loop adaptation uses between 5 and 15 gradient steps on 8 to 16 support examples. Evaluated on 60 held-out real series with horizons of 1 to 4 weeks, the meta-learned initialisation reduces RMSE by an average of 17 percent relative to random initialisation and by 9 percent relative to pre-training on the full synthetic corpus without MAML. The paper discusses limitations related to the synthetic data generation assumptions and the sensitivity of results to the inner learning rate.
