title: Applying AHP to Municipal Budget Allocation: A Case Study of Three Vojvodina Municipalities
abstract: This paper presents an application of the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to assist local government decision-makers in allocating capital budgets across competing infrastructure projects in three municipalities in the Vojvodina region of Serbia. A hierarchical criteria structure was developed through semi-structured interviews with 18 municipal officials, yielding four main criteria—economic impact, social benefit, environmental sustainability, and implementation feasibility—and 14 sub-criteria. Data on 27 candidate projects were collected from municipal planning documents for the fiscal years 2010–2012. Pairwise comparisons were gathered from a panel of five experts and aggregated using the geometric mean method. Consistency ratios remained below 0.08 across all comparison matrices. Results showed that economic impact criteria carried the highest aggregate weight (0.38), while environmental sustainability was systematically underweighted relative to stated policy priorities. The paper discusses structural biases in expert judgment within public administration contexts and proposes a procedure for consistency-guided revision of pairwise matrices during stakeholder workshops.

title: Coupling Agent-Based Market Models with Satellite-Derived Crop Yield Estimates: A Feasibility Study
abstract: Exogenous supply shocks driven by weather and crop failure are a primary source of price volatility in regional commodity markets, yet most agent-based microstructure models treat supply as either fixed or drawn from stylised stochastic processes. This paper explores the feasibility of coupling an agent-based grain market model with Sentinel-2 derived NDVI-based crop yield estimates for the Vojvodina region, covering the 2018–2022 growing seasons. Yield estimates are produced at municipality resolution (45 spatial units) and aggregated to produce a seasonal supply signal fed into the simulation's supply schedule. In three out of four years tested, coupling the satellite-derived signal reduces the root mean squared error of simulated end-of-season price levels relative to observed prices by 14–22 percent compared with the climatological baseline. The main limitation is a six-week lag in NDVI-based yield confidence, which limits operational usefulness. The study is intended as a feasibility assessment rather than a production system and identifies three data processing bottlenecks requiring further engineering work.

title: Reusing the Core Criterion and Evidence Vocabulary in Western Balkan ESPD Implementations
abstract: The European Single Procurement Document (ESPD) relies on the Core Criterion and Evidence Vocabulary (CCCEV) to express exclusion grounds and selection criteria as machine-readable structured data. This paper examines whether CCCEV can be reused in Western Balkan ESPD implementations where the underlying legal criteria differ from EU directives. The analysis focuses on Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. A comparison of CCCEV criterion types against national exclusion ground lists reveals that 68 % of Serbian grounds can be expressed using existing CCCEV patterns without modification. For the remaining 32 %, new criterion subclasses are specified. A prototype ESPD form generator was built using Apache Jena and tested with procurement officers from three Serbian ministries; usability evaluation with 18 participants produced a mean System Usability Scale score of 72.4, classed as acceptable. The paper concludes with recommendations for a regional CCCEV extension registry.

title: Succession Events and AIS Continuity Risk in Serbian Family Manufacturing Enterprises
abstract: Ownership succession in family businesses frequently disrupts established accounting information workflows, yet this transition risk has received little attention in the AIS literature. This study investigates how succession events—defined as a transfer of majority ownership or managerial authority between family generations—affect AIS continuity and the quality of accounting outputs in the post-succession period. A mixed-methods design combined a retrospective survey of 62 firms that completed succession between 2010 and 2021 with four in-depth case studies. Survey data were analyzed using logistic regression to predict post-succession AIS disruption, defined as a drop of at least one standard deviation in the firm's PIQ score within 24 months of succession. Successor age below 35, absence of a documented system handover protocol, and single-vendor dependency were significant predictors of disruption. Case studies illuminated informal knowledge transfer practices that mitigate formal documentation gaps. The paper proposes a four-phase AIS continuity checklist for succession planning.

title: Starch–PLA blends with improved water vapour barrier
abstract: Blending starch with polylactic acid (PLA) is a well-established strategy for reducing the cost and carbon footprint of bio-based packaging, yet achieving adequate water vapour barrier performance remains a persistent challenge. This study investigates the effect of starch content, plasticiser type, and processing conditions on the water vapour transmission rate (WVTR) of starch–PLA blend films prepared by melt extrusion. Glycerol and sorbitol were evaluated as plasticisers at concentrations ranging from 10 to 30 wt%. Morphological characterisation via scanning electron microscopy revealed that finer starch particle dispersion, achieved through twin-screw extrusion at optimised screw speed, correlated with significantly reduced WVTR values. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed partial compatibilisation between the two phases when a maleic anhydride compatibiliser was employed. Mechanical tensile testing demonstrated that elongation at break improved with increasing starch content while Young's modulus remained within commercially relevant ranges. Films incorporating 20 wt% starch and sorbitol as plasticiser exhibited the most favourable balance of barrier and mechanical properties. These findings support the feasibility of starch–PLA blends as practical replacements for conventional petroleum-based flexible packaging films, provided that processing parameters are carefully controlled.

title: Antimicrobial edible coatings from plant extracts for fresh-cut fruit
abstract: Fresh-cut fruits are highly susceptible to microbial spoilage and oxidative browning, shortening their commercial shelf life considerably. This work examines the formulation and performance of edible coatings based on plant extracts—specifically rosemary, thyme, and grape seed—incorporated into a hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) matrix for application on fresh-cut apple and melon slices. Minimum inhibitory concentration assays confirmed antimicrobial efficacy against Listeria innocua and Escherichia coli surrogate strains commonly associated with fresh produce spoilage. Coated fruit samples stored at 4 °C for twelve days showed significantly lower total viable counts and reduced browning index compared to uncoated controls, as assessed by colorimetric analysis. Texture profile analysis indicated that coating application preserved firmness more effectively than untreated samples across the storage period. Sensory evaluation panels rated the coated fruits as acceptable in terms of flavour and appearance. The results demonstrate that plant-extract-enriched edible coatings represent a promising, clean-label strategy for extending the shelf life of minimally processed fruit without compromising consumer acceptability.

title: Home compostability of bio-based films under Serbian conditions
abstract: Reliable home composting data collected under locally relevant climatic and soil conditions are essential for validating the compostability claims of bio-based packaging films. This conference paper presents the results of a twelve-month field study in which five commercially relevant bio-based films—including PLA, thermoplastic starch (TPS), PLA/starch blends, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), and a cellulose-based material—were buried in domestic compost heaps at ten residential sites across the Vojvodina region of Serbia. Mass loss, tensile strength retention, and visual disintegration were monitored at two-month intervals. Results showed that TPS and cellulose-based films disintegrated substantially within four months, while PLA films retained significant structural integrity beyond six months under the measured temperature ranges of 28–42 °C. Blend films showed intermediate behaviour. Seasonal temperature fluctuations were identified as the dominant factor governing degradation rate, with slower progress observed during winter months. These findings highlight the need for regionally specific composting standards and suggest that single-material TPS or cellulose films are better suited for home-compostable claims in Serbian climatic conditions than PLA-dominant formulations.

title: Effect of nanoclay incorporation on the oxygen barrier properties of PLA films for food packaging
abstract: Improving the oxygen barrier of polylactic acid (PLA) films is critical to broadening their applicability in food packaging, particularly for oxygen-sensitive products. This study examines the incorporation of organically modified montmorillonite nanoclay at loadings of 1, 3, and 5 wt% into PLA matrices via melt compounding. X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy confirmed an intercalated–exfoliated nanoclay morphology at 3 wt% loading, corresponding to the lowest oxygen transmission rate measured—a reduction of 47% compared to neat PLA. Dynamic mechanical analysis showed an increase in storage modulus with nanoclay addition, while differential scanning calorimetry revealed a slight increase in crystallinity attributed to nanoclay nucleation effects. Thermogravimetric analysis confirmed that thermal stability improved marginally at 3 wt% loading. Transparency, assessed by UV-Vis spectrophotometry, decreased modestly but remained within acceptable limits for retail packaging applications. Migration testing according to EU food contact material regulations showed no detectable nanoclay migration into fatty food simulants. These results establish organically modified montmorillonite as an effective additive for enhancing PLA oxygen barrier without compromising the material's biodegradable nature.

title: Plasticisation strategies for thermoplastic starch: a comparative study of polyols and citrate esters
abstract: Thermoplastic starch (TPS) is one of the most abundant and low-cost biopolymers available for packaging applications, but its inherent brittleness and sensitivity to humidity restrict practical deployment. This study systematically compares six plasticisers—glycerol, sorbitol, xylitol, triethyl citrate, tributyl citrate, and acetyl triethyl citrate—at concentrations of 20 and 30 wt% in corn starch films processed by compression moulding. Tensile properties, elongation at break, moisture uptake, and glass transition temperature were determined as primary performance indicators. Citrate ester plasticisers produced films with lower moisture sensitivity and higher elongation at break compared to polyol-plasticised counterparts, while glycerol-plasticised films demonstrated superior processability at the extrusion stage. X-ray diffraction confirmed a reduction in starch crystallinity across all plasticiser systems, with the greatest amorphisation observed for tributyl citrate. Long-term stability under 75% relative humidity showed that citrate-plasticised films maintained mechanical integrity for significantly longer periods. The findings provide a practical selection guide for formulators developing TPS-based compostable packaging films, highlighting citrate esters as particularly promising plasticisers for humid storage environments.

title: Chitosan-based edible coatings enriched with lavender essential oil: application on strawberries
abstract: Strawberries are among the most perishable of commercially cultivated fruits, with post-harvest losses attributed primarily to fungal spoilage and mechanical damage during transport. This study investigates edible coatings formulated from medium-molecular-weight chitosan (1.5% w/v) enriched with lavender essential oil at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5% v/v for application on fresh strawberries. In vitro antifungal assays against Botrytis cinerea demonstrated dose-dependent inhibition, with complete mycelial growth inhibition at 1.5% oil concentration. Coated strawberries stored at 4 °C for fourteen days exhibited significantly lower weight loss, higher firmness values, and reduced decay incidence compared to uncoated controls. Total phenolic content and antioxidant capacity were better preserved in coated fruit, suggesting a protective effect against oxidative deterioration. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed uniform coating coverage without cracking. Sensory panels found no significant difference in taste or aroma acceptability between coated and uncoated samples at the 1.0% oil concentration. The study supports chitosan–lavender oil coatings as an effective, food-safe strategy for extending strawberry shelf life with minimal sensory impact.

title: Life cycle assessment of starch-PLA composite packaging versus conventional polyethylene pouches
abstract: The environmental credentials of bio-based packaging materials are frequently claimed but rarely substantiated through rigorous comparative life cycle assessment (LCA). This study presents a cradle-to-grave LCA comparing starch–PLA composite pouches (30/70 wt% blend) against conventional low-density polyethylene (LDPE) pouches of equivalent functional unit—specifically, packaging sufficient to contain one kilogram of dry food product. Inventory data were collected from the authors' pilot-scale extrusion facility and supplemented with Ecoinvent 3.8 background datasets adapted to the Serbian energy mix. Results showed that starch–PLA pouches offered a 38% reduction in global warming potential and a 52% reduction in fossil resource depletion compared to LDPE pouches. However, land use and eutrophication potential were higher for the bio-based option, driven primarily by starch feedstock agriculture. End-of-life scenarios were modelled for industrial composting, home composting, and landfill disposal. Industrial composting yielded the most favourable overall environmental profile. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that the regional electricity mix significantly influenced the comparative advantage of the bio-based option. These findings provide a nuanced environmental basis for decision-making by packaging manufacturers and retailers considering a transition to bio-based materials.

title: Barrier and mechanical properties of PLA films modified with beeswax and carnauba wax coatings
abstract: Wax-based coatings have a long history in food preservation and represent a natural, food-safe route to improving the moisture barrier of biopolymer films. This study evaluates the application of beeswax and carnauba wax coatings, applied at thicknesses of 5, 10, and 15 µm, onto PLA base films by a laboratory-scale gravure coating process. Water vapour transmission rate, oxygen transmission rate, and water contact angle were measured as primary barrier indicators. Both wax types significantly reduced WVTR, with carnauba wax coatings at 15 µm achieving a 63% reduction relative to uncoated PLA. Surface energy analysis confirmed the hydrophobic character introduced by wax layers. Adhesion between wax and PLA substrate was assessed by peel testing; surface corona treatment of PLA prior to coating improved adhesion strength by over 40%. Mechanical testing revealed that wax-coated films retained adequate tensile strength and elongation for practical handling. Compostability under industrial conditions was not adversely affected by the wax coating at the tested thicknesses, as confirmed by disintegration testing according to EN 13432. The results position wax-modified PLA films as a commercially viable option for moisture-sensitive dry food packaging.

title: Incorporation of rosemary extract into starch-based films: antioxidant activity and film properties
abstract: Active packaging incorporating natural antioxidants offers a strategy for reducing oxidative deterioration in packaged food without the use of synthetic additives. This study investigates the preparation and characterisation of starch-based films containing rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis) extract at concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0 wt% relative to starch dry mass. Films were prepared by solvent casting using glycerol as plasticiser. DPPH and ABTS radical scavenging assays confirmed a concentration-dependent increase in antioxidant activity, with the 3.0 wt% film retaining 78% DPPH scavenging capacity. FTIR analysis indicated physical interactions between polyphenolic extract components and starch hydroxyl groups. Mechanical testing showed a modest decrease in elongation at break with increasing extract content, attributed to cross-linking effects, while tensile strength was not significantly affected. Colour measurements indicated a progressive yellowing with increasing extract concentration, remaining within acceptable limits for opaque packaging applications. Water vapour permeability was slightly reduced in extract-containing films. Migration testing into 95% ethanol food simulant confirmed that polyphenol release was sustained over 72 hours, suggesting potential controlled-release active packaging behaviour. These findings support the use of rosemary extract as a multifunctional active ingredient in starch-based biodegradable films.

title: Compostable multilayer structures combining PLA and thermoplastic starch: processing and performance
abstract: Monolayer bio-based films rarely satisfy the combined mechanical and barrier requirements of real food packaging applications, motivating interest in compostable multilayer structures. This study reports the development and characterisation of three-layer coextruded films consisting of PLA outer layers and a thermoplastic starch (TPS) core layer, with overall thicknesses of 80–120 µm. A maleic anhydride-grafted PLA compatibiliser was applied at the PLA/TPS interface to improve interlayer adhesion. Peel strength testing confirmed that compatibiliser inclusion increased adhesion energy by 55% compared to uncompatibilised reference structures. Oxygen and water vapour barrier properties of the multilayer films were found to be intermediate between those of neat PLA and neat TPS monolayers, with the PLA outer layers providing the dominant barrier contribution. Compostability under industrial conditions (EN 13432) was verified through disintegration and ecotoxicity testing; all formulations passed within the 12-week test period. Mechanical properties including puncture resistance and dart drop impact were superior to either monolayer alone. The study demonstrates a viable route to compostable multilayer packaging with commercially relevant performance, opening a path toward replacing conventional co-extruded polyolefin structures in dry and semi-dry food applications.

title: Benchmarking bio-based packaging regulations: implications for Serbian manufacturers
abstract: The regulatory landscape governing bio-based and compostable packaging is evolving rapidly across the European Union and candidate states, creating both opportunities and compliance challenges for manufacturers in countries seeking EU accession. This book chapter reviews the current state of EU regulations relevant to bio-based packaging—including the Single-Use Plastics Directive, the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation revision, and EN 13432 compostability certification—and analyses their practical implications for packaging manufacturers operating in Serbia. The chapter draws on case studies from three anonymised Serbian food companies that have begun transitioning to certified compostable packaging, documenting the technical and economic barriers encountered. Key issues identified include the limited availability of industrial composting infrastructure in Serbia, the absence of a national eco-label for compostable packaging, and the cost premium associated with EN 13432 certification for small and medium-sized enterprises. The chapter proposes a roadmap for Serbian regulatory alignment, recommending phased adoption of EU compostability standards, investment in municipal organic waste infrastructure, and the establishment of a national centre of excellence for bio-based materials testing. The analysis is intended to inform both policy makers and industry stakeholders in Serbia and comparable EU candidate economies.

title: Oxidative stress indices in the rat midbrain following repeated low-dose dimethoate administration
abstract: Dimethoate is a systemic organophosphate commonly used on fruit crops in Vojvodina. This study examined oxidative stress responses in rat midbrain tissue after 21 days of oral dimethoate at 0.5 mg/kg/day (approximately one-tenth of the established NOAEL). Thirty-two male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomised to four groups: vehicle, 0.5 mg/kg, 1.5 mg/kg, and a positive-control group receiving paraquat 5 mg/kg. Tissue superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, glutathione peroxidase activities, and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were determined spectrophotometrically. At 1.5 mg/kg, SOD activity declined by 27% and MDA increased by 41% relative to vehicle (both p < 0.05). The 0.5 mg/kg group showed a non-significant trend toward elevated MDA. Dopamine concentrations in the same tissue showed a moderate inverse correlation with MDA (r = −0.52, p = 0.02). These data support the hypothesis that lipid peroxidation in the midbrain contributes to dopamine depletion at doses that do not cause overt cholinergic symptoms.
venue: Acta Toxicologica et Pharmacologica Centralis

title: Cypermethrin-induced deficits in open-field and rotarod performance in rats: dose-response and time-course analysis
abstract: Type II pyrethroids such as cypermethrin are extensively used substitutes for organophosphates in Serbian cereal and vegetable cultivation, but their behavioural neurotoxicity at low repeated doses is not well characterised. Forty male Wistar rats received cypermethrin (0.5, 2, or 8 mg/kg/day p.o.) or corn-oil vehicle for 14, 28, or 42 days in a 3×3 plus control factorial design (n = 8 per cell). Open-field locomotion, thigmotaxis, and rotarod latency were recorded at each time point. At 8 mg/kg, rotarod latency decreased significantly at day 28 and 42 (p < 0.01); locomotor distance in open field was reduced at all time points. At 2 mg/kg, only rotarod performance showed a borderline significant decline at day 42. Striatal dopamine and serotonin measured at sacrifice by HPLC-ECD were reduced at 8 mg/kg (DA: −29%, 5-HT: −18%, both p < 0.05) but unaltered at lower doses. The 0.5 mg/kg group displayed no significant differences from vehicle at any endpoint, suggesting a threshold-like behaviour for the behavioural and neurochemical effects of cypermethrin under these conditions.

title: Comparative neurotoxicity of three organophosphate insecticides used in Vojvodina: chlorpyrifos, dimethoate, and malathion
abstract: Vojvodina's agricultural landscape features simultaneous seasonal use of multiple organophosphate insecticides, raising questions about which compounds pose the greatest risk to the dopaminergic system at realistic exposure levels. This comparative study administered chlorpyrifos, dimethoate, or malathion at 2 mg/kg/day orally for 28 days to separate groups of male Wistar rats (n = 10 per group) alongside a vehicle control. All three compounds inhibited erythrocyte AChE to a similar extent (~15–22%). Striatal dopamine depletion was most pronounced with chlorpyrifos (−38%), intermediate with dimethoate (−22%), and absent with malathion. Nigral tyrosine hydroxylase-positive cell counts were reduced only in the chlorpyrifos group (−11%, p = 0.04). Mitochondrial complex I activity in striatal synaptosomes, measured by NADH oxidation rate, was significantly lower in chlorpyrifos and dimethoate groups. These results indicate that beyond AChE inhibition, the degree of mitochondrial complex I impairment may be a key determinant of dopamine-specific toxicity among structurally similar organophosphates.

title: Effects of combined chronic exposure to chlorpyrifos and the fungicide tebuconazole on dopaminergic and cholinergic markers in the rat striatum
abstract: Farmers in Vojvodina regularly apply insecticides and fungicides together during the same growing season, yet nearly all rodent toxicity studies examine compounds individually. This study investigated joint exposure to chlorpyrifos (1 mg/kg/day) and tebuconazole (5 mg/kg/day), alone and in combination, for 35 days in male Wistar rats (n = 8 per group). Endpoints included striatal dopamine (HPLC-ECD), AChE activity, muscarinic receptor density (³H-QNB binding in striatal membranes), and a rotarod task. Chlorpyrifos alone reduced striatal DA by 26% and AChE by 18%. Tebuconazole alone had no significant effect on any neurochemical endpoint. The combination group showed DA reduction of 41%—significantly greater than either compound alone (p = 0.03, one-way ANOVA post-hoc Tukey)—and a 31% upregulation of muscarinic receptor density, suggesting compensatory cholinergic plasticity. Rotarod performance in the combination group was impaired relative to both single-exposure groups. These data indicate additive-to-synergistic dopaminergic toxicity when two agrochemicals commonly co-applied in this region are combined at individually subclinical doses.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction as an upstream event in pesticide-induced dopaminergic toxicity: evidence from a chronic low-dose rotenone–chlorpyrifos co-exposure model
abstract: Both rotenone and chlorpyrifos inhibit mitochondrial complex I and have been independently associated with Parkinson's disease risk in epidemiological studies. To examine whether co-administration at doses individually insufficient to impair dopamine produces additive mitochondrial pathology, male Wistar rats received rotenone (0.5 mg/kg/day, s.c.) plus chlorpyrifos (1 mg/kg/day, p.o.) for 28 days, with each compound administered alone as separate positive controls and a vehicle group (n = 10 per group). Striatal ATP content, complex I activity, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in isolated synaptosomes, and dopamine quantification by HPLC-ECD were the primary endpoints. Both compounds alone produced marginal effects on ATP and ROS at the chosen doses. The combination caused a 44% reduction in complex I activity (p < 0.001), a 52% increase in ROS, and a 38% drop in striatal dopamine compared with vehicle. Mitochondrial swelling assessed by transmission electron microscopy confirmed structural damage in the combination group only. The findings strengthen the case that mitochondrial complex I is a convergent target amplifying dopaminergic damage when mechanistically related environmental toxicants co-occur.

title: Pesticide neurotoxicology and Parkinson's disease risk: mechanisms and epidemiological context
abstract: This book chapter reviews the mechanistic evidence linking chronic low-level pesticide exposure to nigrostriatal dopaminergic dysfunction in the context of Parkinson's disease aetiology. Coverage includes organophosphates, type I and II pyrethroids, paraquat, and triazole fungicides. For each class, the chapter summarises rodent model data on dopamine depletion, mitochondrial impairment, neuroinflammation, and alpha-synuclein aggregation, cross-referencing where available with human occupational cohort data from Southern and Central Europe. A section addresses the special challenge of mixture toxicity, noting that agricultural workers are typically exposed to several compounds simultaneously, while almost all mechanistic studies use single compounds. Methodological considerations for translating rodent findings to human risk assessment are discussed, including allometric scaling of doses and the limited availability of validated biomarkers for subclinical dopaminergic injury in living subjects. The chapter is intended as a reference for pharmacologists, occupational physicians, and toxicologists working at the interface of environmental exposure and neurodegeneration.

title: Sex differences in striatal dopamine depletion after chronic chlorpyrifos exposure in Wistar rats
abstract: Most rodent neurotoxicology studies use only male animals, leaving uncertainty about whether findings apply equally to female subjects. This study directly compared male and female Wistar rats (n = 12 per sex per group) receiving chlorpyrifos at 2 mg/kg/day for 28 days or vehicle. Endpoints were striatal dopamine and metabolite concentrations (HPLC-ECD), plasma oestradiol and testosterone, erythrocyte AChE, and open-field locomotion. Male rats showed a 33% reduction in striatal DA (p < 0.001). In females, DA was reduced by only 14% and did not reach significance (p = 0.09). AChE inhibition was comparable between sexes (~20%). Plasma oestradiol levels correlated positively with residual striatal DA across individuals (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Ovariectomised females showed DA reductions similar to males, while oestradiol repletion in ovariectomised animals restored partial protection. These data suggest that endogenous oestrogens modulate vulnerability to pesticide-induced dopaminergic toxicity, with implications for the interpretation of male-only data and for sex-stratified occupational risk assessment.

title: Urinary 3,5,6-trichloro-2-pyridinol as a biomarker of chlorpyrifos exposure in agricultural workers in Vojvodina and its association with self-reported neurological symptoms
abstract: Translating rodent toxicology findings to occupationally exposed human populations requires validated biomonitoring. This cross-sectional study enrolled 87 male agricultural workers from Vojvodina counties with documented chlorpyrifos use and 44 matched controls without occupational pesticide exposure. Urinary 3,5,6-trichloro-2-pyridinol (TCPy) was measured by HPLC-MS/MS as the primary chlorpyrifos metabolite. Participants also completed the validated Neurotoxicology Symptom Checklist (NSC-21) covering tremor, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and memory complaints. Median urinary TCPy was 4.8 μg/g creatinine in workers versus 0.6 μg/g in controls (p < 0.001). Workers in the highest TCPy tertile reported significantly more NSC-21 symptoms than the lowest tertile (median score 8 vs. 4, p = 0.003). After adjustment for age, smoking, and alcohol use, TCPy tertile remained independently associated with symptom burden (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.3–6.4 for high vs. low tertile). The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and objective neurological examination data were not collected, limiting interpretation. Prospective follow-up of this cohort is planned.

title: Prefrontal cortex dopaminergic and glutamatergic changes after long-term subclinical pyrethroid exposure: an exploratory study
abstract: Research on pesticide-induced dopaminergic neurotoxicity has focused almost exclusively on the nigrostriatal pathway; far less is known about effects in the prefrontal cortex (PFC), which also depends on dopaminergic tone for executive and working memory functions. This exploratory study exposed male Wistar rats to permethrin (3 mg/kg/day, p.o., 56 days) or vehicle (n = 10 per group). PFC was dissected for HPLC-ECD quantification of dopamine and glutamate, ³H-SCH23390 binding (D1 receptor density), and Western blot for glutamate transporter GLT-1. PFC dopamine was reduced by 19% (p = 0.03); D1 receptor density was increased by 17% (p = 0.04). Glutamate concentration was elevated by 28% (p = 0.01) and GLT-1 expression was reduced by 31% (p = 0.007). Rats showed impaired performance on an attentional set-shifting task (increased errors to criterion, p = 0.02). These preliminary findings suggest that chronic pyrethroid exposure may perturb PFC dopamine–glutamate crosstalk in a manner relevant to cognitive function, warranting further mechanistic investigation.

title: Polypharmacy burden and adverse drug reaction incidence in geriatric hypertensive patients: a pharmacovigilance registry study from Serbia
abstract: Pharmacovigilance data from Serbia have rarely been analysed specifically for elderly hypertensive patients on multiple agents. We extracted all spontaneous reports submitted to the Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia between 2007 and 2013 that involved at least two antihypertensive drug classes in patients aged ≥65. After deduplication and expert triage, 1,087 valid reports were analysed. The median number of reported drugs per case was 5 (IQR 4–7). The most frequently implicated drug classes were beta-blockers (28%), calcium channel blockers (24%), and ACE inhibitors (21%). The five most common adverse reactions were dizziness, hypotension, cough, ankle oedema, and bradycardia. Female patients constituted 62% of reports and had a disproportionality score (reporting odds ratio) significantly elevated for symptomatic hypotension compared with male patients (ROR 2.11, 95% CI 1.63–2.73). Underreporting and the voluntary nature of the reporting system are acknowledged limitations. Results indicate a reporting signal that warrants formal pharmacoepidemiological follow-up.

title: Transcriptomic response of Acinetobacter baumannii ATCC 19606 to sub-inhibitory concentrations of peptide derivative KCKP-05
abstract: RNA sequencing was used to characterise transcriptome-wide changes in A. baumannii ATCC 19606 following 4-hour exposure to KCKP-05 at 0.25× MIC (4 μg/mL). Three biological replicates per condition were processed with a standard ribosomal RNA depletion protocol, followed by paired-end 150 bp sequencing on a next-generation sequencing platform. Differential expression analysis (DESeq2, adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC| ≥ 1.5) identified 312 significantly altered genes. Downregulated genes included bfmS and bfmR (two-component regulatory system governing biofilm), pgaABCD operon genes responsible for poly-β-1,6-GlcNAc synthesis, and csuA/B pilus assembly genes. Upregulated genes were enriched in oxidative stress response categories (katE, sodB) and membrane repair functions. Gene ontology enrichment and pathway mapping suggested that KCKP-05 primarily disrupts biofilm initiation signals rather than causing broad membrane toxicity at sub-inhibitory doses. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for the preferential antibiofilm activity observed at concentrations below the MIC.

title: Process windows that reduce porosity in SLM-printed 316L steel
abstract: This study investigates the definition and characterization of process windows that minimize porosity in 316L stainless steel components fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM). A systematic design-of-experiments approach was employed, varying laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, and layer thickness across a broad parameter space. Relative density measurements were performed using Archimedes' method and validated through cross-sectional metallographic analysis and X-ray micro-computed tomography. The results identify distinct porosity regimes—lack-of-fusion, keyhole, and balling—and establish the boundary conditions separating them. A combined energy-density metric, refined with separate scanning strategy considerations, is proposed as a practical tool for practitioners to select parameters that consistently achieve relative densities above 99.5%. Statistical regression models derived from the experimental data are presented, enabling prediction of porosity levels for untested parameter combinations. The findings were validated on an independent parameter set, demonstrating strong predictive capability. This work provides a transferable methodology applicable to other austenitic steels processed by powder-bed fusion and highlights the importance of coupled parameter optimization rather than single-variable tuning for achieving high-integrity SLM components.

title: Topology optimization with self-supporting constraints
abstract: This paper presents a topology optimization framework that incorporates self-supporting geometric constraints, enabling the direct manufacture of optimized components via selective laser melting without the need for additional support structures. Traditional topology optimization methods generate geometries that frequently include overhanging features below a critical angle, necessitating supports that increase material consumption, post-processing effort, and surface roughness. The proposed method integrates a continuous overhang constraint formulated in the density field, penalizing the formation of unsupported material during the optimization iteration. The constraint is implemented within a SIMP-based (Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization) optimization algorithm and applied to benchmark mechanical loading cases. Comparative studies show that self-supporting designs achieve structural performance within 8–15% of unconstrained optima while completely eliminating critical overhangs. The computational overhead introduced by the constraint evaluation is analyzed and shown to be acceptable for practical part sizes. Experimental validation is carried out by printing selected optimized geometries in Ti-6Al-4V and assessing support-free printability. The framework demonstrates a viable path toward fully automated, support-free design-to-manufacture workflows in metal additive manufacturing.

title: Effect of scanning strategy on microstructure and mechanical anisotropy in SLM-produced AlSi10Mg parts
abstract: Selective laser melting of AlSi10Mg aluminum alloy is gaining traction for lightweight structural applications, yet the influence of scanning strategy on resulting microstructure and mechanical anisotropy remains incompletely understood. This study systematically evaluates four scanning strategies—unidirectional, bidirectional, island, and rotating stripe—applied to identical part geometries under otherwise fixed process parameters. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and optical microscopy are used to characterize grain morphology, texture, and melt pool geometry. Tensile specimens extracted in three orientations are tested to quantify anisotropy in ultimate tensile strength, yield strength, and elongation at break. Results demonstrate that the rotating stripe strategy produces the most isotropic mechanical response and the finest average grain size, attributed to more uniform thermal gradient distribution. Island scanning yields the highest porosity among the tested strategies under the selected parameters. A correlation between melt pool aspect ratio and degree of columnar grain growth is established. These findings provide actionable guidance for selecting scanning strategies in applications where directional mechanical performance must be controlled, and form the basis for a process-structure-property linkage model applicable to powder-bed fusion of aluminum alloys.

title: Gradient lattice infill generation for metal additive manufacturing using topology-driven density maps
abstract: This work presents a computational methodology for generating functionally graded lattice infill structures for metal additive manufacturing components, driven by stress-based density maps derived from topology optimization. Rather than applying uniform lattice patterns, the proposed approach maps local von Mises stress distributions onto a library of strut-based unit cells—including body-centered cubic, face-centered cubic, and octet-truss variants—scaling cell size and strut diameter continuously according to normalized stress intensity. The resulting gradient lattice geometries are evaluated for printability in selective laser melting by analyzing strut inclination angles and minimum feature sizes relative to machine capabilities. Finite element simulations of the gradient lattice components are compared against both solid and uniform lattice counterparts, showing up to 34% mass reduction while maintaining structural compliance within a 5% margin. Physical specimens in 316L stainless steel are produced and subjected to compressive and three-point bending tests, confirming the simulation predictions with deviations below 7%. The methodology is implemented as a parametric design pipeline compatible with standard CAD and slicing software environments, making it accessible for industrial application. This contribution bridges topology optimization and lattice design in a unified workflow targeting the metal additive manufacturing context.

title: Thermal residual stress prediction in SLM components using layer-by-layer finite element simulation
abstract: Residual stresses arising from the rapid thermal cycles inherent to selective laser melting significantly affect dimensional accuracy, fatigue life, and susceptibility to cracking in as-built metal components. This paper develops a layer-by-layer finite element thermal-mechanical simulation framework capable of predicting residual stress distributions in SLM-fabricated parts without requiring per-scan resolution, thereby achieving a practical balance between accuracy and computational cost. The model employs an equivalent heat source calibrated against melt pool geometry measurements and incorporates temperature-dependent material properties for 316L stainless steel. A thermo-elasto-plastic constitutive model accounts for phase transformation effects. Simulation predictions of residual stress magnitudes and distributions are validated against neutron diffraction measurements performed on benchmark geometries. The framework is then applied to investigate the influence of substrate preheating temperatures ranging from 20°C to 300°C on residual stress reduction. Results show that preheating at 200°C reduces peak tensile residual stresses by approximately 40%, with diminishing returns at higher temperatures. The model is further used to evaluate the effect of part orientation and scanning strategy rotation angle. This work provides a validated numerical tool for guiding process planning decisions aimed at minimizing distortion and residual stress in SLM production.

title: Support structure optimization for overhanging features in metal powder-bed fusion: a review and comparative assessment
abstract: Support structures are indispensable in metal powder-bed fusion processes yet represent a significant source of material waste, build time, and post-processing effort. This book chapter provides a comprehensive review of support structure optimization strategies developed over the past decade, encompassing geometric design, topology-based approaches, and machine learning-assisted generation methods. The review is organized around three primary objectives: minimizing support volume, ensuring thermal management and part anchoring during the build, and facilitating clean removal without surface damage. Particular attention is given to lattice and fractal support architectures, breakaway interface designs, and integrated topology optimization frameworks that produce self-supporting geometries. Comparative assessment criteria are defined across printability, mechanical adequacy, removability, and computational cost. The chapter also identifies open research challenges, including the lack of standardized benchmarks for support performance evaluation and the limited integration of residual stress considerations into support optimization workflows. Case studies in stainless steel and titanium alloys are used throughout to illustrate the comparative performance of selected methods. The chapter concludes with a roadmap for future development, highlighting the potential of combined build-orientation and support co-optimization strategies to substantially reduce support dependency in industrial metal additive manufacturing practice.

title: Pore morphology classification in SLM-printed metals using convolutional neural networks applied to micro-CT images
abstract: Accurate classification of pore morphology in selectively laser melted components is critical for diagnosing process defects and guiding parameter correction. This study presents a deep learning pipeline based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) image stacks to automatically classify pores into keyhole, lack-of-fusion, and gas pore categories. A labeled dataset of 4,200 individual pore instances was constructed from 316L stainless steel specimens manufactured under deliberately varied process parameters to induce each defect type. Three-dimensional pore features including sphericity, elongation ratio, nearest-neighbor distance, and orientation relative to build direction were extracted and used as auxiliary inputs alongside raw image patches in a hybrid CNN-feature fusion architecture. The model achieves a classification accuracy of 94.3% on a held-out test set, outperforming prior morphology threshold-based classifiers by a margin of 11%. Grad-CAM visualization confirms that the network focuses on physically meaningful geometric features. The pipeline is integrated into a semi-automated quality assessment workflow that produces per-specimen defect maps linked to local process parameter deviations. This tool enables rapid, objective defect characterization that can inform closed-loop process control strategies in industrial SLM environments, reducing reliance on manual metallographic inspection.

title: Multi-objective topology optimization balancing stiffness, thermal conductivity, and printability for SLM components
abstract: Engineering components produced by selective laser melting increasingly serve multi-physical functions, requiring simultaneous optimization of structural stiffness and thermal performance. This paper formulates and solves a multi-objective topology optimization problem targeting concurrent maximization of structural stiffness and effective thermal conductivity while enforcing a self-supporting printability constraint. The problem is cast as a weighted-sum Pareto optimization within a density-based SIMP framework extended with anisotropic thermal conductivity interpolation. The printability constraint is implemented as a cumulative overhang measure that penalizes designs containing angles below 45° relative to the build platform. A sensitivity filtering scheme adapted for multi-physics problems prevents checkerboard instabilities. Pareto fronts are computed for a range of weighting coefficients and analyzed to identify compromise designs. Selected Pareto-optimal geometries are fabricated in 316L stainless steel and evaluated through mechanical testing and thermographic imaging under controlled heat flux boundary conditions. Experimental results confirm that the multi-objective optimization framework produces physically valid designs that satisfy both performance objectives with deviations of less than 10% from predicted values. The framework is demonstrated on a heat exchanger bracket application, showing meaningful improvements over single-objective benchmarks. This contribution addresses a growing need for integrated design tools in multi-functional metal additive manufacturing.

title: Benchmarking powder flowability and layer uniformity for stainless steel powders used in selective laser melting
abstract: Powder quality is a fundamental determinant of part integrity in selective laser melting, yet standardized characterization protocols for correlating powder properties to as-built density and surface quality remain underdeveloped for industrial practice. This study benchmarks five commercially sourced 316L stainless steel powder batches using a comprehensive suite of flowability and morphology metrics: Hall flow rate, Carr index, Hausner ratio, angle of repose, laser diffraction particle size distribution, and scanning electron microscopy morphology assessment. Powder spreading experiments on a laboratory-scale recoating testbench quantify layer density uniformity and the formation of streaking defects as a function of powder characteristics. Correlation analysis reveals that powder batches with a D50 in the range of 28–35 μm and sphericity above 0.92 consistently produce the most uniform deposited layers. SLM build experiments using identical process parameters across all batches demonstrate that layer uniformity metrics derived from the recoating testbench predict as-built relative density with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.89. Recycled powder behavior after up to five reuse cycles is also assessed, showing measurable degradation in flowability and a 0.3% average reduction in relative density by the fifth cycle. The study provides practical threshold values for incoming powder quality control applicable to production environments.

title: Material Flow Analysis in a Thermoplastic Extrusion Plant: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region
abstract: This study applies material flow analysis (MFA) to a medium-sized thermoplastic extrusion facility in Vojvodina, Serbia, processing approximately 4,200 tonnes of polyethylene and polypropylene annually. System boundaries were drawn from raw pellet delivery to finished pipe dispatch. Mass balances were compiled for twelve input and output streams, including resin, pigment masterbatch, process cooling water, and solid scrap. Field measurements over six months revealed that 6.3% of input polymer leaves the process as off-specification product or trim waste, while cooling water circuits contributed to 18% of total site water consumption. A Sankey diagram representation was constructed and cross-checked against utility invoices. Discrepancies between metered and calculated values were below 5% for energy carriers and below 9% for water streams. Results were used to identify three priority areas for environmental improvement: lubricant oil management, die-cleaning solvent recovery, and edge-trim recycling. The methodology is presented in a format compatible with ISO 14001 planning requirements.

title: Characterization of Aqueous Effluents from PVC Compounding Operations: Physicochemical and Regulatory Parameters
abstract: PVC compounding generates process effluents that carry residual plasticizers, thermal stabilizers, and suspended polymer fines. This paper reports the physicochemical characterization of wastewater collected at three compounding lines in two Serbian facilities over a twelve-month campaign. Samples were analysed for pH, COD, BOD5, total suspended solids, total dissolved solids, phthalate esters (DEHP, DINP), organotin stabilizer residues, and heavy metal content (Pb, Cd, Sn). DEHP concentrations ranged from 0.8 to 14.2 µg/L depending on production grade; organotin compounds were detected in cooling-water blowdown at 3–27 µg/L as Sn. COD values in direct process effluents reached 680 mg/L. Measured parameters were compared against Serbian national emission limit values and EU Industrial Emissions Directive thresholds. Eight out of thirty-six sampling events produced at least one exceedance, mostly for COD and DEHP. Recommendations for point-source control and pre-treatment options are discussed.

title: Implementing ISO 14001 in Small and Medium Polymer Processors: Barriers and Practical Approaches
abstract: This paper examines the adoption of ISO 14001 environmental management systems in fourteen small and medium-sized polymer processing enterprises (injection moulding, blow moulding, and film extrusion) in Serbia and northern Croatia. Data were collected through structured interviews with environmental coordinators and quality managers, supplemented by document review of existing environmental programmes, energy bills, and waste disposal records. The main barriers identified were insufficient internal expertise (reported by 71% of respondents), high perceived documentation burden (64%), and unclear regulatory requirements at the municipal level (57%). Enterprises that had completed certification reported a median reduction of 11% in energy intensity per tonne of product in the first two years post-certification, attributable primarily to compressed-air system improvements and cooling-water recirculation upgrades. A simplified gap-analysis checklist aligned with ISO 14001:2015 clause structure is proposed, field-tested in four enterprises. The tool reduces initial assessment time by approximately 30% compared to a full consultant-led audit.

title: Life-Cycle Inventory Dataset for Polypropylene Injection Moulding in Southeast European Manufacturing Conditions
abstract: Existing commercial LCA databases contain life-cycle inventory (LCI) data predominantly derived from Western European manufacturing conditions, which may introduce systematic errors when applied to assessments in Southeast Europe. This study constructs a foreground LCI dataset for polypropylene injection moulding based on primary data collected from five facilities in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Hungary. Data collection covered electricity consumption (average 2.31 kWh/kg product), natural gas for mould heating, cooling water makeup, hydraulic oil losses, mould-release agent, and solid waste streams. Electricity grid mixes specific to each country were applied. The resulting dataset covers seventeen elementary flow categories and is formatted for compatibility with ecoinvent 3.x conventions. Unit process outputs per functional unit (one kilogram of moulded PP part) are reported with uncertainty ranges estimated via pedigree matrix. The dataset is compared against the ecoinvent 'injection moulding' proxy, revealing a 14–22% underestimation of GWP when the proxy is applied to Serbian grid conditions.

title: Comparative Eco-Profile of Recycled and Virgin Granulate in Pipe Extrusion: An LCA Perspective
abstract: Post-consumer and post-industrial recycled polymer granulate is increasingly used in non-pressure pipe extrusion as a partial substitute for virgin resin. This study presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of pipe production using three material compositions: 100% virgin HDPE, a 30% recycled/70% virgin blend, and a 50% recycled/50% virgin blend. Primary LCI data were collected at a pipe extrusion plant in Serbia; recycled granulate supply chain data were sourced from two regional collection and reprocessing facilities in Serbia and Romania. Impact categories assessed include global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, water depletion, and urban land occupation. Results show that substituting 30% virgin HDPE with post-industrial recyclate reduces GWP by 19% per linear metre of DN110 pipe, while the 50% blend achieves a 31% reduction. Energy demand reductions are partially offset by higher scrap rates and increased sorting energy at the recycler. Sensitivity analysis was performed on transport distance assumptions and electricity grid mix.

title: Integration of Environmental Aspect Register with EMAS Reporting in a Polymer Recycling Facility
abstract: This paper describes the construction and integration of a structured environmental aspect register at a polymer mechanical recycling facility in Vojvodina that sought EMAS registration. The facility processes mixed post-consumer polyolefin waste at approximately 6,500 tonnes per year through sorting, granulation, and compounding lines. The aspect register was built following ISO 14001:2015 clause 6.1.2, covering thirty-one identified aspects across four process areas. Significance criteria applied were regulatory sensitivity, frequency of occurrence, severity of potential impact, and stakeholder concern. Eight aspects were rated significant, including cooling water discharge, granulator dust emissions, solvent use in quality testing, and noise from outdoor shredding. The environmental performance indicators (EPIs) derived from the register were mapped to EMAS Annex IV core indicators. Baseline performance data for three consecutive years (2017–2019) are reported. The paper discusses practical difficulties encountered in quantifying diffuse dust emissions and in aligning aspect significance rankings with operator safety risk assessments.

title: Effluent Treatment Options for Cooling Tower Blowdown in Polymer Processing: Technical and Cost Comparison
abstract: Cooling tower blowdown in polymer processing facilities contains biocides, corrosion inhibitors, and scale-control agents that complicate discharge to municipal sewer systems. This paper evaluates four treatment configurations for blowdown streams at two facilities in Serbia: direct discharge with pH correction only, coagulation–flocculation followed by sand filtration, electrocoagulation, and membrane filtration (ultrafiltration + reverse osmosis). Assessment criteria were removal efficiency for key parameters (COD, conductivity, total hardness, biocide residues), capital and operating cost per cubic metre treated, and sludge generation. Electrocoagulation achieved 87% COD removal and 94% biocide removal at a treatment cost of approximately 1.8 EUR/m³, compared with 3.4 EUR/m³ for the membrane option, which produced superior effluent quality but generated a concentrated reject stream requiring separate management. A decision matrix weighted for regulatory compliance probability, operating complexity, and total cost is presented to guide facility selection of appropriate treatment technology.

title: Carbon Footprint Scope 3 Estimation for a Serbian Plastics Converter: Data Quality Challenges and Methodological Choices
abstract: Scope 3 greenhouse gas accounting is increasingly expected of manufacturing companies seeking environmental certification or responding to supply chain due diligence requirements. This paper documents a Scope 3 inventory developed for a Serbian plastics converter producing packaging components, with annual turnover of approximately 12 million EUR. Following GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain Standard categories, the study covers upstream raw material extraction and transport, waste disposal, employee commuting, and downstream transport to customers. Primary data were available for seven of fifteen relevant categories; spend-based and average-data methods were applied for the remainder. Total Scope 3 emissions were estimated at 8,240 tCO2e per year, with upstream polymer production accounting for 74% of that total. The paper identifies five categories where data quality is insufficient for confident reporting and proposes a prioritised data collection roadmap. Sensitivity of total Scope 3 to polymer granulate emission factor choice is demonstrated through a ±15% scenario analysis.

title: Mapping Environmental Legal Obligations for Polymer Processors Under the Updated Serbian Environmental Protection Act: A Practitioner's Analysis
abstract: Serbia amended its core Environmental Protection Act and associated by-laws in 2021–2022 in the process of aligning national legislation with the EU acquis. This paper analyses the implications of these changes for polymer processing facilities subject to integrated environmental permits (operators above threshold emission values) and those covered only by the simplified permit regime. Key changes examined include revised best available technique (BAT) applicability criteria for the plastics sector, updated emission limit values for volatile organic compounds, new requirements for soil and groundwater monitoring at industrial sites, and expanded environmental liability provisions. The analysis is based on review of primary legal texts, comparison with the corresponding EU Industrial Emissions Directive articles, and structured interviews with twelve compliance officers at Serbian polymer processing companies. The paper identifies seven compliance gaps that are commonly observed in current facility permit conditions and are likely to trigger corrective requirements during the next permit review cycle.

title: Dynamic LCI Modelling for Polymer Processing Facilities: Accounting for Production Rate Variability and Seasonal Grid Mix
abstract: Standard life-cycle inventory modelling assumes static production conditions, but polymer processing facilities operate at variable production rates and are supplied by electricity grids whose carbon intensity changes seasonally and hour-by-hour. This preprint presents a dynamic LCI framework in which production rate data (sampled at fifteen-minute intervals from SCADA logs at a cast film extrusion facility over twelve months) are combined with hourly marginal electricity emission factors derived from the Serbian transmission operator's dispatch data. Results show that the GWP of one kilogram of produced film varies by a factor of 1.7 between high-output summer shifts and low-output winter weekend periods, driven primarily by electricity carbon intensity variability. A simplified annual average LCI underestimates peak-period GWP by up to 34%. The framework is implemented in a Python workflow interfacing with SimaPro via CSV import, and the code is deposited in a public repository. Implications for EPD verification and environmental benchmarking programmes are discussed.

title: Full QMRA framework for household use of shallow alluvial well water in a Vojvodina village: from source to tap
abstract: A complete quantitative microbial risk assessment was assembled for Cryptosporidium and Campylobacter in the village of Mokrin, where approximately 340 households rely on privately-owned shallow wells. The framework integrated hazard identification, concentration data from 36 monthly samples per well (12 wells monitored), dose–response models, and exposure estimates based on a household consumption survey (n = 187 households). A stochastic Monte Carlo simulation (100 000 iterations) was run in a custom R script. Median annual infection risk from Cryptosporidium was 1.8 × 10⁻³ per person-year (95th percentile: 6.4 × 10⁻³), exceeding the WHO guideline by more than one order of magnitude. Campylobacter risks were lower but still above guideline values at the 75th percentile. Sensitivity analysis identified oocyst/cell concentration at the wellhead and ingestion volume as the dominant variance contributors. Practical risk reduction options, including simple chlorination and well lining, were modelled and compared.

title: A four-wire-rope passive isolation platform for a machine-vision camera on a milling machine table: design, analysis and bench test
abstract: Machine-vision cameras co-located with CNC milling machines must tolerate spindle-frequency vibrations that can blur images and introduce measurement errors. This paper describes the mechanical design and experimental validation of a compact passive isolation platform sized to carry a 3.2 kg area-scan camera. The platform uses four identical 6 mm wire-rope isolators arranged symmetrically at the corners of an aluminium base plate. A lumped-parameter model with six degrees of freedom was assembled and its natural frequencies predicted analytically; the lowest mode was placed at 11 Hz to provide at least 20 dB isolation above 35 Hz. The assembled platform was tested on a laboratory shaker with representative spindle harmonics at 25 Hz, 50 Hz, and 75 Hz. Measured isolation ratios were 18 dB, 24 dB, and 31 dB at these frequencies, agreeing with model predictions to within 2 dB. Image blur was quantified using a resolution target: MTF50 improved from 38 lp/mm on the bare machine table to 61 lp/mm on the isolated platform under 50 Hz excitation at 12 mg input amplitude.

title: Effect of elastomeric pad material selection on low-frequency isolation performance for interferometric displacement sensors
abstract: Interferometric displacement sensors used in dimensional metrology require isolation from floor vibration below 20 Hz, a frequency range where most commercial elastomeric mounts provide little attenuation. This study compares four elastomeric pad materials—natural rubber, neoprene, silicone foam, and polyurethane—as under-platform isolators for a commercial Michelson interferometer weighing 5.1 kg. Static stiffness was measured via dead-weight loading; dynamic stiffness and loss factor were obtained by base-excitation tests from 1 Hz to 50 Hz. Natural rubber provided the lowest natural frequency at 6.8 Hz but the smallest loss factor of 0.04 at resonance, resulting in a transmissibility peak of 28 dB. Polyurethane achieved a loss factor of 0.18 with a natural frequency of 9.4 Hz, producing a peak of only 15 dB and better attenuation above 20 Hz than all other candidates. Fringe-count error rate during vibration events was used as an application-level metric; polyurethane reduced error events by 63 % compared to the unmodified setup. Material aging effects over eight weeks were also monitored; silicone foam stiffened by 11 % while others changed by less than 4 %.

title: Towards standardised micro-vibration acceptance criteria for optical inspection stations in Serbian manufacturing: a measurement-based proposal
abstract: There are no regionally adopted vibration acceptance criteria specific to optical inspection stations installed in Serbian manufacturing facilities. This preprint proposes a draft criterion derived from 14 measurement campaigns at seven plants covering automotive, food processing, and electronics assembly sectors. Vibration environments were characterised as one-third-octave RMS acceleration spectra from 1 Hz to 250 Hz. Instrument sensitivity data from five commercial optical systems—two laser trackers, two structured-light scanners, and one coordinate-measuring interferometer—were collated from their technical manuals and used to define maximum allowable input spectra. A proposed acceptance curve is given at two tiers: a tighter Tier A for sub-micrometre measurement tasks and a relaxed Tier B for dimensional tolerances above 10 µm. Comparison with the VC-A through VC-E curves used in semiconductor facilities shows that Tier A corresponds approximately to VC-B conditions, which are achievable by passive isolation in most surveyed environments. The intention is to submit this proposal to the relevant Serbian standardisation body after community review.

title: Uticaj raspodele opterećenja od teških vozila na kumulativno zamorno oštećenje zavarenih rebrastih veza čeličnih mostova
abstract: U radu je analiziran uticaj statističke raspodele opterećenja osovina teških vozila na kumulativno zamorno oštećenje zavarenih rebrastih veza čeličnih mostova. Korišćeni su podaci sa WIM stanice na auto-putu E-75 u Srbiji, prikupljeni tokom 18 meseci, sa ukupno 1,24 miliona registrovanih prolaza vozila. Raspodela opterećenja modelovana je trokomponentnom mešovitom normalnom raspodelom. Primenom Majner-Palmgrenove teorije kumulativnog oštećenja i modifikovanog Goodmanovog dijagrama izračunato je ekvivalentno naponsko kolebanje za četiri karakteristična detalja zavarenih veza klase FAT 71 i FAT 90 prema EN 1993-1-9. Rezultati pokazuju da je korišćenje uniformnog modela opterećenja, propisanog Evrokodom, konzervativno za 18–34% u poređenju sa stvarnom raspodelom, zavisno od klase detalja i raspona mosta. Predložen je korekcioni faktor za lokalne uslove saobraćajnog toka.

title: Calibration of Paris–Erdogan crack growth parameters for structural steel S355 weld toes under variable amplitude loading
abstract: This study reports fatigue crack growth tests on S355 structural steel specimens with simulated weld toe geometry under variable amplitude loading sequences derived from measured traffic data. Forty-eight compact tension specimens were prepared according to ASTM E647, with weld toe notches machined to reproduce the typical geometry found in longitudinal rib-to-deck connections. Load sequences were generated from a filtered WIM dataset representing mixed highway traffic. Crack lengths were tracked using the direct current potential drop method at intervals of approximately 0.1 mm. The Paris–Erdogan constants C and m were determined as 3.21 × 10⁻¹³ and 3.07 respectively in SI units, with a coefficient of variation of 8.4% for C across the specimen population. Comparison with constant amplitude results showed a 12% reduction in effective crack growth rate under variable amplitude loading, attributed to crack closure effects. The calibrated parameters are directly applicable to fracture mechanics-based remaining life calculations for Serbian highway bridge stock.

title: Integration of structural health monitoring data and fracture mechanics models for real-time fatigue damage tracking in steel bridges
abstract: A framework is described for updating fracture mechanics-based fatigue damage estimates in real time as strain monitoring data accumulate on an instrumented steel plate girder bridge on a Serbian provincial road. The bridge carries a span of 44 m and was instrumented with 16 foil strain gauges and a WIM pad embedded in the approach slab. Strain histories sampled at 200 Hz were processed with a rainflow-counting algorithm to produce daily stress-range spectra at four critical weld details. These spectra fed a Bayesian updating scheme in which the Paris law parameter C was treated as a lognormally distributed random variable with prior calibrated from the laboratory data described in an earlier publication. After 14 months of monitoring the posterior coefficient of variation of C decreased from 0.41 to 0.19, demonstrating effective learning. Predicted crack initiation times for the most loaded detail shifted from a median of 9.2 years under the prior to 12.4 years under the posterior, a change attributed to lower measured stress ranges than assumed in the design-phase analysis.

title: Sensitivity of fatigue life estimates for welded bridge connections to WIM measurement uncertainty and traffic extrapolation assumptions
abstract: WIM-based fatigue assessments inevitably involve two sources of uncertainty: sensor calibration errors affecting the measured load spectrum and statistical assumptions used to extrapolate short records to the design life. This paper quantifies the sensitivity of fatigue life estimates to both sources for a representative set of welded steel bridge connections. WIM calibration uncertainty was characterised from repeated static weighing trials at a test site, yielding a relative standard deviation of 4.3% for gross vehicle weight. Extrapolation uncertainty was assessed by comparing damage estimates from subsampled records of 3, 6, 12 and 24 months drawn from a 36-month baseline dataset. For FAT 71 and FAT 90 details on a 50 m span bridge, the 90th-percentile error in damage ratio due to calibration error alone was below 9%, while extrapolation from a 3-month record introduced errors up to 31%. Minimum monitoring duration recommendations are derived as a function of heavy vehicle flow rate and acceptable error tolerance.

title: Procena zamornog veka starih nitovanih čeličnih mostova prevedenih na teži drumski saobraćaj: slučaj mosta u Sremu
abstract: Rad se bavi procenom zamornog veka nitovanih čeličnih nosača na mostu izgrađenom 1927. godine, koji je 2019. nakon rekonstrukcije lokalne saobraćajne mreže preusmeren na drumski saobraćaj sa povećanim udelom teških vozila. Geometrija popречnog preseka i stanje nita dokumentovani su kombinovanjem arhivskih nacrta i terestričkog laserskog skeniranja. Kontaktni pritisak u nitovanim vezama modelovan je MKE analizom uz pretpostavku delimično popuštenih nita utvrđenu ultrazvučnom kontrolom. WIM merenja obavljena su tokom 90 dana na prilazniku mosta. Primenom modifikovane Miners Rule uz efektivni stepen uzdužnog smicanja u nitovanim vezama dobijeno je da je preostali zamornni vek nosača između 12 i 19 godina za mereni saobraćajni tok, a svega 5–8 godina pri pretpostavljenom rastu saobraćaja od 3% godišnje. Preporučen je program instrumentacije za praćenje stanja.

title: Detecting inconsistencies in multi-epoch cadastral boundary datasets using persistent homology
abstract: Cadastral parcel databases accumulated over long periods often contain geometric inconsistencies arising from boundary updates that were not propagated to all dependent layers. This paper investigates the use of persistent homology, specifically Vietoris-Rips filtration on point clouds derived from parcel corner coordinates, to identify topological anomalies indicative of incomplete updates. A dataset of 9 400 parcels in a suburban fringe zone of Novi Sad spanning four cadastral update epochs (1987, 1999, 2008, 2019) was used. Persistent H0 and H1 features were computed and compared across epochs; anomalous persistence intervals flagged 312 boundary segments requiring manual inspection, of which 278 (89%) were confirmed as genuine inconsistencies by a cadastral surveyor. Computation was performed using the Gudhi library in Python. The method requires no prior knowledge of intended parcel topology and is applicable to legacy datasets lacking structured change history. Runtime on the test dataset was under four minutes on a standard workstation.

title: Development of an environmental product declaration for precast prestressed hollow-core slabs manufactured in the Western Balkans
abstract: The paper describes the process of preparing a Type III Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) for prestressed hollow-core slabs (HC-265 and HC-320 profiles) produced at a precast plant in the Western Balkans region. The EPD was developed in accordance with ISO 14025 and the construction product standard EN 15804+A1. Primary data covering one full calendar year of production (approximately 38 000 m² of slab area) were verified by an independent third-party body. The declared unit is 1 m² of hollow-core slab installed in its intended application. The GWP result for modules A1–A3 is 43.8 kg CO₂-eq./m² for HC-265 and 52.1 kg CO₂-eq./m² for HC-320. Background data were drawn from ecoinvent 3.8. The paper also discusses obstacles specific to Balkan precast manufacturers in meeting EPD programme operator requirements, including data collection practices and verification costs, and proposes a simplified industry-level data collection protocol.

title: Acoustic Emission Detection of Partial Discharges in Oil-Filled Model Transformers Using PVDF Sensors
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and PZT piezoelectric sensors for detecting partial discharge (PD) events in a laboratory-scale oil-filled transformer model. A needle-to-sphere electrode arrangement was used to generate controlled PD activity at three voltage levels (25, 40, and 55 kV rms). Six PVDF sensors and four PZT sensors were mounted on the tank surface. Acoustic signals were recorded at a sampling rate of 5 MHz and compared against simultaneous IEC 60270 electrical PD measurements. PVDF sensors exhibited a flatter frequency response between 50 and 300 kHz, while PZT sensors showed higher sensitivity in the 100–250 kHz band. Localisation errors using time-difference-of-arrival on the PVDF array averaged 18 mm, compared with 31 mm for the PZT array under the same conditions. Signal attenuation through transformer oil was characterised as a function of temperature between 20 and 80 °C. Results suggest that PVDF arrays offer a practical advantage for wideband acquisition in compact tank geometries.

title: Influence of Oil Temperature on Acoustic Propagation Velocity and Partial Discharge Localisation Accuracy in Power Transformers
abstract: Accurate source localisation of partial discharges via acoustic emission methods depends on a reliable estimate of sound propagation velocity in transformer oil, which varies with temperature and oil ageing. This study measured acoustic propagation velocity in new and thermally aged mineral insulating oil samples at temperatures ranging from 15 to 85 °C using a pulse-echo technique at 150 kHz. Velocity decreased from 1430 m/s at 15 °C to 1280 m/s at 85 °C in new oil, with aged samples showing velocities approximately 2–4% lower across the same range. A correction algorithm was derived from polynomial regression on the measured data and integrated into a four-sensor time-difference-of-arrival localisation routine. Experimental validation in a 100 kVA model transformer showed that applying the temperature correction reduced mean localisation error from 27 mm to 11 mm when oil temperature shifted from 20 to 70 °C during a measurement session. The correction coefficients are provided in tabulated form for direct implementation.

title: Wavelet Packet Decomposition of Acoustic Partial Discharge Signals for Discharge-Type Discrimination in Transformer Insulation
abstract: Three representative partial discharge source types relevant to power transformer insulation — surface discharge along pressboard barriers, internal void discharge in oil-impregnated paper, and corona from a metallic protrusion — were produced in a controlled test cell and characterised using a six-element piezoelectric sensor array. Acoustic emission signals were processed with a wavelet packet decomposition scheme using a Daubechies-8 mother wavelet at five decomposition levels. Energy distribution across the resulting 32 sub-bands was used as a feature vector for each discharge type. A k-nearest-neighbour classifier trained on 480 labelled waveforms achieved 91.4% classification accuracy on a 120-sample test set, outperforming a threshold-based frequency centroid method that reached 74.2% under the same conditions. Misclassifications occurred primarily between surface and internal void sources when signal-to-noise ratio fell below 12 dB. The paper also examines the effect of sensor coupling agent (silicone grease versus epoxy) on sub-band energy reproducibility across repeated mounting cycles.

title: Frequency-Selective Impedance Measurement as an Indirect Indicator of Partial Discharge Onset Voltage in Oil-Paper Insulation
abstract: This study investigates whether changes in the complex impedance spectrum of oil-paper insulation at frequencies between 1 Hz and 1 MHz can serve as a precursor to partial discharge inception, measured by conventional IEC 60270 methods. Flat test cells consisting of three layers of thermally aged kraft paper impregnated with mineral oil were subjected to a step-ramp voltage protocol while simultaneous impedance spectra were recorded with a four-terminal impedance analyser at 50 V signal amplitude. For cells aged at 110 °C for periods of 0, 250, 500, and 1000 hours, the partial discharge inception voltage decreased from 12.1 kV to 7.4 kV while the loss tangent at 1 kHz increased from 0.0031 to 0.019. A peak in the derivative of the imaginary impedance component with respect to voltage, observable at frequencies above 10 kHz, consistently preceded electrical PD inception by 3–8% of the inception voltage in all 27 tested specimens. The method is proposed as a non-disruptive complement to acoustic PD monitoring during field transformer inspections.
