title: Combined Acoustic–Electrical Partial Discharge Measurement System for On-Site Power Transformer Diagnostics: Design and Field Evaluation
abstract: A portable measurement system combining an eight-channel piezoelectric acoustic emission array with a synchronised electrical partial discharge acquisition channel compliant with IEC 60270 was designed and evaluated at three 110/35 kV transformers in substations in Vojvodina. The system uses a compact field-programmable gate array data acquisition unit with 10 MHz sampling on each acoustic channel and 30 MHz on the electrical channel, synchronised via GPS pulse-per-second signal to permit time correlation of acoustic and electrical events. On-site measurements at each transformer spanned six hours under normal service voltage. At one unit, consistent acoustic events were detected correlating with electrical PD charges of 180–420 pC, and the three-dimensional source position was estimated at 340 mm from the HV lead-out bushing, which aligned with findings from subsequent internal inspection. The paper describes the hardware architecture, shielding approach for the electrical channel in the substation electromagnetic environment, and the semi-automatic event correlation procedure used in data post-processing.

title: Short-Time Fractional Fourier Transform Applied to Partial Discharge Acoustic Emission Signals in Power Transformers
abstract: Standard time-frequency representations such as the short-time Fourier transform and continuous wavelet transform have known limitations when applied to dispersive acoustic signals recorded on transformer tank walls, where multiple propagation modes arrive at different times with different frequency contents. This paper examines the short-time fractional Fourier transform (STFrFT) as an alternative representation, evaluating its ability to concentrate energy for chirp-like acoustic PD signals generated by needle-plate discharges in a 630 kVA transformer model. The optimal rotation angle in the fractional Fourier domain was estimated from the chirp rate extracted from Wigner–Ville distributions of reference signals, yielding rotation angles between 0.81π and 0.94π for the discharge configurations tested. STFrFT representations improved energy concentration by 23–38% compared with the standard STFT as measured by the Rényi entropy criterion, and the improved localisation of impulse energy in the joint domain reduced the uncertainty in time-of-arrival estimation by approximately 1.2 µs on average. Computation time on a standard workstation was 340 ms per waveform at 5 MHz sampling, which is discussed in the context of practical implementation.

title: Effect of Mechanical Clamping Pressure on Piezoelectric Sensor Sensitivity and Repeatability in Acoustic Partial Discharge Measurements
abstract: Attachment consistency of piezoelectric sensors to transformer tank walls is rarely controlled in practice and may contribute substantially to inter-measurement variability in acoustic PD diagnostics. This paper reports a systematic study in which six PZT-5A disc sensors were attached to a 100 mm thick steel plate using a spring-loaded clamping fixture allowing controlled normal forces between 5 and 80 N, with and without silicone coupling gel. Frequency response functions were measured by pencil-lead break excitation at a fixed point, with 30 repeated attachment–detachment cycles at each force level. Sensitivity at 150 kHz varied by up to 8.4 dB across the 5–80 N range, with a plateau of stable response above 35 N. Cycle-to-cycle reproducibility, expressed as standard deviation of the peak sensitivity, was 0.9 dB above 35 N and 2.6 dB below 20 N. A minimum clamping force of 40 N with coupling gel is recommended for field measurements where quantitative comparison between sessions is required. These findings are directly relevant to the design of permanent or semi-permanent sensor fixtures for continuous monitoring systems.

title: Impedance-Acoustic Joint Feature Extraction for Ageing-Condition Classification of 110 kV Power Transformers: A Data Collection Study
abstract: This preprint describes a field data collection campaign carried out at 18 power transformers of the same series (110/10 kV, 40 MVA) operated by a regional distribution company in Vojvodina, spanning installation dates from 1987 to 2009. For each unit, the following data were collected during planned outages: broadband impedance spectra (1 Hz–1 MHz, four-terminal), dissolved gas analysis results, degree of polymerisation from oil furfural content, and a one-hour acoustic PD survey under induced voltage at 1.05 pu. A feature vector of 38 parameters extracted from impedance spectra and acoustic PD pulse descriptors was computed for each transformer. Hierarchical clustering on the feature matrix suggested three groups broadly corresponding to low, moderate, and high insulation degradation as judged by the furfural-based DP estimates. Within-group variance was dominated by acoustic features in the 100–200 kHz band and by the imaginary impedance slope between 10 and 100 kHz. The dataset (anonymised) is made available as a supplement to encourage independent analysis. A follow-up study with a larger sample is planned.

title: Diversity Combining Schemes for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Metallic Farm Environments
abstract: This work evaluates three receive-diversity combining strategies—selection combining, equal-gain combining, and maximal-ratio combining—for wireless sensor nodes operating at 868 MHz in the vicinity of metallic agricultural structures. A testbed consisting of four sensor nodes equipped with dual-dipole antenna pairs at orthogonal polarisations was deployed around a steel machinery shed (40 m × 20 m footprint) on a cooperative farm near Srbobran. Over 72 hours of continuous link-quality logging were collected, yielding approximately 260 000 received signal strength indicator samples per node pair. Selection combining provided a median diversity gain of 5.2 dB relative to a single-antenna reference, while maximal-ratio combining reached 7.8 dB. The gain was most pronounced within the shed's specular reflection zone, where single-antenna packet error rates exceeded 18 % without diversity. Practical implications for sensor node PCB layout and antenna separation constraints are discussed.

title: Channel Sounding Measurements for LoRaWAN at 868 MHz in a Mixed Crop-and-Infrastructure Farm Environment
abstract: A wideband channel-sounding campaign was conducted on a 320-hectare farm in Srem featuring sunflower and soybean fields, a central machinery courtyard with metal implements, a cluster of grain silos, and a 600 m greenhouse complex with aluminium framing. The sounding system transmitted a chirp spread-spectrum signal with 500 kHz bandwidth, enabling delay-spread characterisation alongside path loss. At 142 receiver positions, the RMS delay spread ranged from 18 ns in open-field locations to 210 ns near the silo cluster. A distance-dependent path loss exponent of 2.8 was found for open subfields and 3.6 in the machinery courtyard. Coherence bandwidth estimates at 90 % correlation threshold fell below 800 kHz in 22 % of courtyard positions, implying frequency-selective fading relevant to LoRaWAN subband planning. The measured dataset is made available as a public repository hosted at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

title: Influence of PCB Laminate Dielectric Loss on Eye Diagram Closure at 25 Gbit/s: A Comparative Simulation and Measurement Study
abstract: As serial link speeds increase toward 25 Gbit/s and beyond, dielectric loss in standard FR4 laminates becomes the dominant degradation mechanism. This paper compares four laminate materials—standard FR4 (Df 0.022 at 1 GHz), a mid-loss halogen-free variant (Df 0.015), a low-loss material (Df 0.008), and an ultra-low-loss ceramic-filled PTFE composite (Df 0.003)—using both electromagnetic simulation and physical test boards. Insertion loss was measured from 1 to 25 GHz over 300 mm stripline traces using a vector network analyser with 1.85 mm connectors. Eye diagrams at 25 Gbit/s were generated by convolving the measured insertion loss with a PRBS31 pattern using a time-domain link model. FR4 produced fully closed eyes at trace lengths above 180 mm; the PTFE composite maintained open eyes to 260 mm. Eye height degradation as a function of loss tangent follows a near-linear relationship in the simulated data, allowing interpolation for materials not tested. Cost and processability implications of laminate selection are discussed for designers working within standard volume PCB fabrication constraints.

title: Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations
abstract: IEC 62443 defines security levels and component requirements for industrial automation and control systems but provides limited normative guidance on firmware update mechanisms. This paper analyses firmware update security requirements implied by IEC 62443-3-3 and IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Levels 1 through 3, identifying 23 specific requirements that a compliant OTA firmware update subsystem must satisfy. For each requirement, the paper maps existing technical mechanisms — from HMAC-based integrity checking to certificate-based authentication and monotonic rollback counters — and identifies three areas where current practice does not clearly satisfy the standard's intent: cryptographic agility, update transaction atomicity across power loss events, and audit logging on Class 1 devices. A reference architecture for a compliant firmware update service is outlined, and the paper estimates implementation effort in person-months for each architectural component at three device capability tiers. The analysis is illustrated using data from two anonymised industrial deployments reviewed during the study.

title: Indirect Learning Architecture for Digital Pre-Distortion of Multi-Carrier PA Signals
abstract: This work implements and evaluates an indirect learning architecture (ILA) for digital pre-distortion (DPD) of a Doherty power amplifier driven by four aggregated LTE carriers totalling 80 MHz bandwidth at 3.5 GHz. The pre-distorter is based on a GMP model with cross-term envelopes; coefficients are updated iteratively over 20 adaptation cycles using a recursive least-squares algorithm with forgetting factor 0.998. Measured results show that DPD reduces the ACPR from −32.4 dBc to −51.8 dBc at 1 dB compression, and the error vector magnitude (EVM) of the innermost carrier improves from 5.1% to 1.6%. The effect of IQ imbalance in the observation receiver on coefficient convergence is studied; a compensation pre-processing step reduces residual distortion by a further 1.4 dB. Experiments were repeated over a 40°C temperature range to assess thermal drift, showing less than 0.8 dB ACPR degradation without re-adaptation over a 30-minute period.

title: Chopper Stabilisation Impact on Noise Figure and Bandwidth in a 0.85 V Instrumentation Amplifier for ECG
abstract: Chopper stabilisation effectively up-converts flicker noise to the chopping frequency, but at sub-1 V supply the switching overhead and charge injection introduce artefacts that are less benign than at higher voltages. This paper analyses and quantifies these effects for a chopper-stabilised instrumentation amplifier built around a 0.85 V PMOS-input OTA in a 180 nm CMOS process. Chopping frequencies between 4 kHz and 32 kHz are evaluated. At 8 kHz chopping, the input-referred noise at 1 Hz is reduced from 210 nV/√Hz to 18 nV/√Hz, while the effective noise bandwidth narrows by approximately 22% due to the low-pass filter required to attenuate chopping ripple. Charge injection measured from transient simulations is 3.1 fC per switching event, giving a differential offset of 340 µV at 8 kHz that is not fully cancelled by the auto-zeroing auxiliary path. A modified switch bootstrapping scheme reduces this residual offset to 41 µV without requiring a supply above 0.9 V. Total harmonic distortion at 1 mV input and 100 Hz remains below 0.08%. The amplifier achieves a noise efficiency factor of 3.4, benchmarked against eight published chopper amplifiers.

title: Adsorption of cellulase components onto wheat straw cellulose: equilibrium and kinetic parameters
abstract: The adsorption behaviour of a commercial cellulase mixture (Trichoderma reesei origin) onto microcrystalline cellulose and milled wheat straw was studied at pH 4.8 and temperatures of 25, 35, and 45 °C. Langmuir and Freundlich isotherms were fitted to equilibrium data collected over a concentration range of 0.1–5.0 mg protein mL⁻¹. Maximum adsorption capacities of 28–42 mg protein g⁻¹ substrate were obtained depending on substrate crystallinity index, determined by X-ray diffraction. Kinetic adsorption experiments showed rapid initial uptake (>60% within 10 min) followed by slower redistribution over 60 min. A simple two-step kinetic model reproduced the data with R² > 0.97. The work demonstrates that substrate crystallinity is a stronger predictor of adsorption capacity than total surface area under the tested conditions, with implications for dosing strategies in industrial saccharification processes.

title: Effect of glucose and cellobiose accumulation on the rate of enzymatic hydrolysis of dilute-acid pre-treated corn stover
abstract: End-product inhibition by glucose and cellobiose is a recognised bottleneck in enzymatic saccharification. This study quantified inhibition constants for a Trichoderma-derived cellulase preparation acting on dilute-acid pre-treated corn stover at 50 °C and pH 4.8. Batch hydrolysis experiments were conducted at enzyme loadings of 10, 20, and 30 FPU g⁻¹ substrate and initial substrate concentrations of 2–10% (w/v). Glucose was added exogenously at 0–40 g L⁻¹ to decouple inhibition from the conversion effect. A competitive inhibition model for the endo- and exocellulase activities was parameterised; Ki,glucose and Ki,cellobiose were estimated as 6.2 and 1.1 g L⁻¹, respectively. Cellobiose was confirmed as the dominant inhibitor at typical hydrolysate compositions. The model showed acceptable predictive accuracy (mean absolute error < 8%) for independent validation runs at 8% solids loading.

title: Mild ethanol-based organosolv pre-treatment of sunflower stalks: effect of temperature and ethanol concentration on lignin removal and cellulose accessibility
abstract: Sunflower stalks, an abundant agricultural residue in Vojvodina, were subjected to organosolv pre-treatment using aqueous ethanol (40–70% v/v) at 140–180 °C for 60 min in a pressure vessel. Lignin removal efficiency ranged from 28% to 74% across conditions, assessed gravimetrically and by Klason lignin analysis. Cellulose accessibility was characterised by the Simons' staining technique using direct orange and direct blue dyes. The accessible surface area correlated strongly (r² = 0.91) with subsequent 72 h enzymatic digestibility at 15 FPU g⁻¹ loading. Pre-treatment at 160 °C and 60% ethanol gave the best balance between delignification (61%) and cellulose preservation (96% retention). Scanning electron microscopy images confirmed fibre delamination under optimised conditions. Hemicellulose recovery in the liquid fraction was 65–78%, indicating potential for co-valorisation of xylose-rich streams.

title: Comparison of empirical and mechanistic models for the enzymatic hydrolysis of organosolv-pre-treated lignocellulosic substrates
abstract: Four kinetic model classes — empirical power-law, Langmuir-type, modified Michaelis–Menten with inactivation, and a surface-based mechanistic model — were evaluated for their ability to describe the enzymatic hydrolysis of organosolv-pre-treated wheat straw and sunflower stalks. Hydrolysis experiments were performed in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks at 50 °C, pH 4.8, over 96 h, with enzyme loadings of 5–30 FPU g⁻¹. All models were fitted by nonlinear least squares; parameter identifiability was assessed by profile likelihood. The mechanistic surface-based model provided the best predictive performance (RMSE 1.8 g L⁻¹) but required the largest parameter set (eight parameters) and showed identifiability issues for three parameters at low enzyme loadings. The modified Michaelis–Menten model with thermal inactivation offered the best compromise between accuracy (RMSE 2.6 g L⁻¹) and parsimony. Recommendations for model selection depending on available experimental data are discussed.

title: Fed-batch feeding of pre-treated wheat straw to a stirred-tank reactor: effect of feeding interval on mixing and final glucose titre
abstract: High solids content in enzymatic hydrolysis reactors is desirable to achieve industrially relevant glucose concentrations but creates significant mixing challenges. This study investigated fed-batch addition of organosolv-pre-treated wheat straw to a 5 L jacketed stirred-tank reactor equipped with a helical ribbon impeller. Initial solids loading was set at 5% (w/v), with subsequent additions of 5% every 6, 12, or 24 h to reach a target of 20% total solids. Torque, dissolved oxygen, and rheological data were collected throughout. Adding substrate every 12 h produced the highest final glucose concentration (87 g L⁻¹ after 72 h), with acceptable power consumption (mean 42 W m⁻³). The 6 h interval led to incomplete liquefaction and elevated torque spikes, while the 24 h interval underutilised enzyme capacity in the initial phase. The helical ribbon impeller maintained near-homogeneous mixing at apparent viscosities up to 4.5 Pa·s.

title: Thermal inactivation of cellulase during prolonged hydrolysis: model-based estimation of effective enzyme half-life
abstract: Cellulase preparations lose activity during extended hydrolysis runs due to thermal denaturation and irreversible adsorption to lignin. This work estimated the effective half-life of a commercial Trichoderma cellulase mixture under batch hydrolysis conditions (50 °C, pH 4.8, 96 h) using pre-treated wheat straw with varying residual lignin content (8–25%). Activity was measured by the filter paper assay at regular intervals on aliquots withdrawn and centrifuged to separate free enzyme. A first-order inactivation term was incorporated into the existing modified Michaelis–Menten model. Estimated half-lives ranged from 38 h (25% lignin substrate) to 67 h (8% lignin substrate), confirming that residual lignin accelerates inactivation beyond thermal denaturation alone. The lignin-dependent inactivation rate constant showed a linear relationship with acid-insoluble lignin content (R² = 0.94). The extended model improved prediction of glucose production beyond 48 h compared to a model without inactivation.

title: Enzymatic hydrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass: reactor engineering considerations
abstract: This book chapter reviews the engineering aspects of enzymatic saccharification at the reactor scale, covering mass transfer limitations, rheology of high-solids slurries, reactor configurations (stirred tank, horizontal drum, and oscillatory flow reactors), and strategies for fed-batch substrate addition. The chapter discusses how slurry rheology evolves from a shear-thinning paste to a less viscous suspension as hydrolysis proceeds, and how this transition affects mixing power requirements. Comparisons of reactor productivity at pilot scale (50–500 L) drawn from the published literature are tabulated. The chapter also covers enzyme recycling options — ultrafiltration membrane recycle and magnetic particle immobilisation — and their techno-economic implications. The target audience is graduate students and engineers entering biomass processing, and the chapter includes worked design examples for sizing a continuous hydrolysis reactor for a 10 tonne day⁻¹ biomass input.

title: Characterisation of cellulose accessibility in mild organosolv pre-treated poplar wood by nitrogen BET, Simons' staining, and Congo red adsorption
abstract: Three methods for characterising cellulose accessibility — nitrogen BET surface area, Simons' staining with direct dyes, and Congo red adsorption — were compared on a set of poplar wood samples subjected to ethanol organosolv pre-treatment at 150 °C with varying residence times (30, 60, 90, 120 min). BET surface area ranged from 1.2 to 4.8 m² g⁻¹ across pre-treatment conditions and correlated poorly (r² = 0.61) with 72 h enzymatic digestibility. Simons' staining accessible surface values (4–22 mg dye g⁻¹ substrate) and Congo red adsorption capacity (0.9–6.1 mg g⁻¹) both correlated more strongly with digestibility (r² = 0.88 and 0.84, respectively). Correlation of accessibility metrics with lignin content and cellulose crystallinity index was also assessed. The results indicate that Simons' staining remains the most informative rapid screening tool for pre-treatment efficacy among the three methods tested.

title: Optimisation of enzyme loading and feeding profile in fed-batch saccharification of organosolv-pre-treated sunflower stalks using response surface methodology
abstract: A response surface methodology (RSM) approach based on a central composite design was applied to optimise three variables in fed-batch enzymatic hydrolysis of organosolv-pre-treated sunflower stalks: initial enzyme loading (5–25 FPU g⁻¹ substrate), supplementation enzyme loading at 24 h (0–10 FPU g⁻¹), and total solids content (10–25% w/v). The response variables were glucose concentration at 72 h and hydrolysis efficiency. The quadratic model explained 94% of variance for glucose concentration and 91% for efficiency. The optimum conditions predicted by the model (initial loading 18 FPU g⁻¹, supplementation 6 FPU g⁻¹, solids 18% w/v) were experimentally verified in triplicate 5 L reactor runs, yielding 76 ± 3 g L⁻¹ glucose at 71% theoretical maximum. Enzyme cost per gram of glucose was estimated as a secondary metric, highlighting that enzyme supplementation beyond 6 FPU g⁻¹ at 24 h gave diminishing returns.

title: Lignin redistribution and cellulose structure changes during mild organosolv pre-treatment of wheat straw monitored by ATR-FTIR and XRD
abstract: The structural evolution of wheat straw during organosolv pre-treatment (60% ethanol, 140–180 °C, 30–90 min) was monitored by attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Crystallinity index calculated by the Segal method increased from 41% (untreated) to 58% (180 °C, 90 min), indicating preferential removal of amorphous cellulose fractions and lignin redistribution rather than structural disruption at milder conditions. ATR-FTIR band ratios associated with syringyl and guaiacyl lignin units indicated a selective extraction of syringyl-rich lignin at lower temperatures. Cellulose lattice parameters were largely unaffected, suggesting the pre-treatment does not significantly alter crystallite dimensions. These structural observations were linked to enzymatic digestibility data from parallel hydrolysis experiments, supporting the interpretation that delignification rather than cellulose disruption is the dominant mechanism improving accessibility under mild organosolv conditions.

title: Mechanistic modelling of fed-batch enzymatic hydrolysis incorporating substrate accessibility loss and enzyme redistribution
abstract: A mechanistic model for fed-batch enzymatic hydrolysis was developed by extending a substrate-accessibility-based kinetic framework to account for: (i) batch-wise addition of pre-treated biomass substrate; (ii) redistribution of free enzyme to freshly added substrate; and (iii) progressive loss of accessible substrate surface area with conversion. Model equations were solved numerically in MATLAB. Parameters were estimated from 96 h batch hydrolysis experiments on organosolv-pre-treated wheat straw at 50 °C and pH 4.8, with enzyme loadings of 10–25 FPU g⁻¹. The model was validated against four independent fed-batch reactor runs (5 L stirred tank, 15–20% total solids, three addition events). Predicted glucose profiles agreed with measured profiles within ±9% relative error over the full 96 h horizon. Sensitivity analysis identified accessible surface area at zero conversion and the enzyme redistribution rate constant as the most influential parameters, guiding future experimental efforts.

title: Feasibility of continuous enzymatic saccharification in a membrane bioreactor with ultrafiltration enzyme recycle for pre-treated wheat straw
abstract: A laboratory-scale membrane bioreactor (MBR) consisting of a 2 L stirred reactor coupled to a 10 kDa cutoff hollow-fibre ultrafiltration module was evaluated for continuous enzymatic saccharification with enzyme recycle. Pre-treated wheat straw (organosolv, 60% EtOH, 160 °C) was fed as a 10% (w/v) suspension. The permeate glucose concentration was monitored continuously by an in-line refractometer. Enzyme retention was 87–92% across 14 days of continuous operation based on protein mass balance. Steady-state glucose concentrations of 42–48 g L⁻¹ were achieved at hydraulic residence times of 18–24 h. Membrane fouling was characterised by trans-membrane pressure increase; a daily 15 min backwash protocol maintained acceptable flux over the operating period. The enzyme productivity (g glucose per mg enzyme per day) was 2.3-fold higher in the MBR than in an equivalent batch process, primarily due to enzyme reuse rather than improved intrinsic kinetics.

title: A Group Contribution Approach for Estimating σ-Profiles of Oligomeric Plasticisers for COSMO-RS Activity Coefficient Prediction
abstract: COSMO-RS requires a quantum-chemically derived sigma (σ) profile for each molecule, which is computationally prohibitive for oligomeric or polymeric species. This work develops an additive group-contribution scheme for σ-profile construction applied to phthalate and adipate plasticisers with molecular weights from 278 to 530 g/mol. σ-Profiles for 18 plasticiser molecules were computed at the BP/TZVP level and decomposed into contributions from 12 structural groups by least-squares regression. The assembled σ-profiles were used in COSMO-RS to predict activity coefficients of 24 small solvent molecules (alcohols, esters, ketones) in each plasticiser matrix; mean absolute relative deviation against available experimental data was 17.4%, compared to 13.1% when using fully computed σ-profiles. The method reduces DFT computation time by 95% for new oligomers and is implemented as a Python script released with the paper. Applications include solvent selection for plasticiser removal in solvent-based polymer recycling.

title: Resolvability in 2-designs derived from affine planes of small order
abstract: This paper examines the resolvability properties of 2-(v,k,λ) designs constructed from affine planes of orders 3 through 7. A systematic enumeration approach, implemented in GAP, was used to classify all non-isomorphic resolutions of each design up to automorphism group action. For affine planes of order 5, 214 distinct resolutions were identified, extending earlier tables that had been incomplete. The relationship between the automorphism group of the base plane and the number of admissible resolutions is made explicit through a series of orbit-counting arguments. Several infinite families of resolvable designs are identified whose parallel class structures satisfy a regularity condition that proves useful for subsequent applications in scheduling and code construction. The paper also provides a corrected count for the order-4 case, where a previously published table contained a duplication error affecting 11 entries. All classification data are made available as supplementary files.

title: Bounds on the minimum distance of codes constructed from symmetric designs
abstract: The paper investigates binary linear codes obtained as row spaces of incidence matrices of symmetric 2-(v,k,λ) designs, with particular attention to how the parameters v, k, and λ determine the minimum distance. Using a combination of shadow bounds and the linear programming bound adapted to this family, tight bounds on the minimum distance are derived for all symmetric designs with v ≤ 80. A new lower bound is established that improves on the previously known bound by at least 2 in 34 of the 91 parameter triples examined. Several extremal cases are identified where the code achieves the derived bound with equality; these correspond to designs admitting large automorphism groups. The constructions rely on known symmetric designs from the literature together with three previously unreported designs with parameters 2-(56,11,2) whose existence is confirmed computationally. Comparisons with the Griesmer bound and the Plotkin bound are tabulated.

title: A construction of locally repairable codes from combinatorial designs with disjoint repair groups
abstract: Locally repairable codes (LRCs) allow recovery of a single erased symbol by contacting at most r other symbols, where r is the locality parameter. This paper presents a direct construction of LRCs from resolvable 2-designs in which the parallel classes serve as disjoint repair groups. Codes with locality r = 4 and r = 5 are constructed from resolvable designs on 20, 40, and 45 points, yielding parameters [n, k, d] that meet the Singleton-like bound for LRCs with equality in several cases. The encoding and repair procedures are described explicitly, and the decoding complexity per repair operation is shown to be O(r^2) field operations over GF(q) for q ≥ 5. A comparison with known optimal LRC families from algebraic geometry codes shows that the new codes achieve the same parameters for short lengths n ≤ 50 while admitting simpler combinatorial descriptions. Implementations were tested in Magma.

title: Codes with multiple disjoint repair sets from transversal designs
abstract: A code has availability t if every symbol has at least t mutually disjoint repair sets each of size at most r. Such codes are relevant in distributed storage when multiple simultaneous reads must be served in parallel. This paper uses transversal designs TD(k, n) to construct linear codes over GF(q) achieving availability t = 2 and t = 3 for a range of length and dimension parameters. The key observation is that the groups of a transversal design naturally define the repair sets, and the code parameters are computed directly from the design parameters k and n. For transversal designs derived from mutually orthogonal Latin squares of orders 5, 7, 8, and 9, families of codes are obtained with rates between 1/3 and 1/2 and minimum distances meeting a new availability-aware Singleton bound derived here. The paper also provides a necessary condition on n for the existence of a TD-based code with availability 3 and locality 4.

title: Cyclic constructions of optimal LRCs meeting the distance bound for small field sizes
abstract: Most known constructions of optimal locally repairable codes require large field sizes growing with the code length. This paper considers cyclic codes over small fields GF(q) with q ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5} and identifies generator polynomials whose zero sets yield codes with locality r ∈ {2, 3, 4} achieving the LRC Singleton bound d = n − k − ⌈k/r⌉ + 2. A computational search over all cyclic codes of lengths n ≤ 63 over these fields was performed, identifying 47 parameter triples for which the bound is achieved and which had not been previously reported. For r = 2 over GF(4), a complete characterisation of achieving codes is given in terms of their factored generator polynomials. The paper also shows that for binary codes with r = 2 and k ≤ 10, the bound cannot be achieved for n > 2k − 1, confirming a conjecture stated in earlier work by other authors. All generator polynomials and code parameters are tabulated.

title: Repair bandwidth and storage overhead trade-offs in LRCs with hierarchical locality
abstract: Hierarchical locally repairable codes introduce two levels of locality: a local level with small repair groups for frequent single-node failures and a global level for multiple simultaneous failures. This paper analyses the bandwidth consumed during repair at both levels and derives a trade-off curve between storage overhead and repair bandwidth for codes constructed from nested block designs. A family of nested designs NB(v, k1, k2, λ1, λ2) is defined, and conditions on the parameters under which they yield valid hierarchical LRCs are established. For designs derived from the points and lines of AG(2, q) with secondary structure from a parallel class partition, explicit codes are constructed for q = 4, 5, 7 with two-level localities (r1, r2) = (3, 6) and (4, 8). The bandwidth required for local repair is shown to be exactly r1 symbols, matching the information-theoretic lower bound. Storage overheads range from 1.50 to 1.75 across the constructed examples, with all parameters verified by direct computation.

title: Constructions of LRCs with availability from partial Steiner systems and their application to rack-aware storage
abstract: Rack-aware distributed storage requires that repair of a failed node avoids cross-rack traffic when possible, placing additional structural constraints on the code's repair sets. This paper models rack-aware repair using partial Steiner systems pS(2, k, v) in which blocks correspond to repair groups confined to individual racks. Necessary and sufficient conditions on the partial Steiner system parameters for the resulting code to have availability t ≥ 2 are derived. Constructions based on resolutions of packing designs P(2, 5, v) for v ∈ {25, 30, 35} are given, producing codes over GF(5) with parameters [25, 10, 9], [30, 12, 10], and [35, 14, 11] with availability 2 and locality 4. A simulation study using a rack model with 5 nodes per rack and 5 racks compares repair traffic against standard LRCs without rack awareness; the proposed codes reduce cross-rack repair traffic by 38–45% under a Poisson failure model with rate λ = 0.01 per node per day.

title: Enumerating optimal LRCs of length at most 30 over small fields: tables and asymptotic observations
abstract: This paper presents a systematic enumeration of all optimal locally repairable codes with parameters n ≤ 30, k ≤ 15, and r ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5} over GF(q) for q ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8}. Optimality is measured against the LRC Singleton bound. A total of 1,842 distinct parameter triples were tested; for 613 of these, at least one achieving code was found, and for 291 triples the non-existence of an achieving code is proved by exhaustive search or analytic argument. The enumeration reveals that the density of optimal triples decreases roughly as r^{-0.7} for fixed n and k as r grows. For r = 2, a complete existence characterisation is proposed and verified for all tested parameters. The tables extend and partially correct two earlier compilations from the literature. All data, together with generator matrices for representative optimal codes, are provided as an open dataset at a public repository.

title: Capillary surfaces on non-smooth substrates: existence via relaxation in the space of functions of bounded variation
abstract: Classical results on capillary surfaces assume at least Lipschitz regularity of the solid substrate. We consider the case in which the substrate is only a rectifiable set of finite two-dimensional Hausdorff measure, which arises in applications to rough or patterned surfaces. We reformulate the total energy functional — combining surface tension, gravitational energy, and wetting energy along the substrate — as a lower-semicontinuous functional on BV(Ω). Applying a relaxation procedure in the sense of Buttazzo and Dal Maso, we identify the relaxed functional and show that it admits minimizers. The relaxed wetting energy is expressed as an integral of a density depending on the approximate normal to the drop's boundary and the local normal to the substrate. We compute this density explicitly for two periodic substrate geometries (sawtooth profile and sinusoidal profile with amplitude-to-wavelength ratios 0.1, 0.3, 0.5) and compare the resulting apparent contact angles with those predicted by the classical Wenzel and Cassie–Baxter formulas.

title: Scalability Analysis of Evolutionary NAS under Strict Latency Budgets on Heterogeneous Embedded Targets
abstract: This paper studies how the difficulty of multi-objective NAS scales with the number of objectives and the strictness of latency constraints when targeting a heterogeneous set of three embedded platforms: an ARM Cortex-M4, a RISC-V MCU, and a low-power DSP. Latency is treated as a separate objective for each target, yielding a five-objective problem when combined with accuracy and model size. Experiments compare NSGA-III and a reference evolutionary strategy across search spaces of increasing depth (4, 8, and 12 cells). Hypervolume scales sub-linearly with the number of cells but degrades faster under tight latency budgets. An analysis of Pareto front collapse—where the feasible set shrinks to near-zero under the tightest constraints—is presented with practical implications for search space design. Results suggest that decoupling the latency constraints into soft penalties rather than hard objectives preserves Pareto front diversity without significant accuracy loss.

title: Bivariate tail dependence in simultaneous flood peaks on tributaries of the Danube in the Vojvodina region
abstract: Simultaneous high-discharge events on adjacent tributaries of the Danube present a compound flood risk that univariate frequency analysis cannot capture. Daily mean discharge records from six gauging stations in Vojvodina for the period 1961–2005 were assembled from the Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. Pairwise tail dependence coefficients were estimated using the non-parametric rank-based estimator of Coles, Heffernan and Tawn, and three Archimedean copula families — Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard and Frank — were fitted by maximum likelihood. The Gumbel–Hougaard copula consistently gave the best fit according to the Cramér–von Mises goodness-of-fit statistic for the upper tail. Estimated upper tail dependence coefficients ranged from 0.18 to 0.47 depending on the station pair, indicating moderate but non-negligible co-occurrence risk. Joint exceedance probabilities for the 100-year marginal quantile were computed and compared with those implied by the independence assumption; the independence assumption underestimated joint exceedance probability by up to 31 percent. Implications for levee design standards under simultaneous loading are discussed.

title: Influence of DC-Link Capacitor Equivalent Series Inductance on High-Frequency Conducted Emissions in AC Motor Drives
abstract: The equivalent series inductance (ESL) of the DC-link capacitor bank in a pulse-width-modulated inverter drive is often overlooked in EMC pre-compliance analysis yet contributes measurably to conducted emissions above 5 MHz. This study quantifies the effect by replacing a standard electrolytic capacitor bank (ESL ≈ 45 nH) with a film capacitor arrangement (ESL ≈ 8 nH) in a 4 kW test drive and recording the full conducted emission spectrum from 150 kHz to 30 MHz under identical load conditions. Peak differential-mode emissions between 10 MHz and 30 MHz were reduced by 6–11 dB with the lower-ESL bank. Impedance spectroscopy measurements confirmed the resonance shift from 9.2 MHz to above 30 MHz. A circuit-level simulation model incorporating measured parasitic parameters reproduced the spectral features within ±2 dB. The findings are directly applicable to PCB layout guidelines for compact drive modules targeting IEC 61800-3 Category C2 limits.

title: A Lumped-Parameter EMI Source Model for Three-Phase PWM Drives: Parameter Extraction and Frequency-Range Validation
abstract: Accurate EMI source models are needed to reduce reliance on full-system measurements during filter development. This work describes a parameter extraction procedure for a lumped CM and DM source model of a three-phase 7.5 kW drive. Impedance parameters were extracted from open- and short-circuit measurements at the drive AC terminals using a vector network analyser across 100 kHz–30 MHz. The resulting model comprises eight passive elements representing the inverter module, gate-drive supply, motor cable, and chassis coupling capacitances. Model predictions of conducted emission spectra were compared against LISN measurements at three load points (25%, 50%, and 100% rated torque), yielding a root-mean-square spectral error of 2.1 dB for CM and 2.8 dB for DM components. The extraction procedure is repeatable and requires less than two hours of bench time, making it practical for production-variant characterisation in industrial settings.

title: Passive EMC Filter Sizing for IEC 61800-3 Category C2 Compliance: A Design Procedure Based on Attenuation Margin Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a structured procedure for dimensioning passive EMC input filters for variable-speed drives to meet IEC 61800-3 Category C2 quasi-peak limits. The procedure uses measured CM and DM source impedances and a target attenuation profile derived from the gap between unfiltered emission spectra and the regulatory limit line, with a 6 dB safety margin applied throughout. Filter topologies (LC, LCL, and CL stages) are compared for a 15 kW test drive, and component values are selected to avoid resonances within the 150 kHz–2 MHz band that could cause limit exceedances at intermediate frequencies. Prototype filters were wound on nanocrystalline toroidal cores and verified by insertion-loss measurement per IEC 60939-3 before integration. Final compliance measurements confirmed that all quasi-peak and average readings were at least 5 dB below the Category C2 limit across the full 150 kHz–30 MHz range. Total filter volume was 0.38 litres and mass 0.61 kg for the 15 kW case.

title: Effect of Motor Cable Length on Common-Mode Conducted Emissions in Variable-Speed Drive Systems
abstract: Long motor cables are common in industrial installations and amplify common-mode conducted disturbances by adding distributed capacitance to ground. This experimental study quantifies the effect for shielded and unshielded cables of lengths 5 m, 20 m, and 50 m connected to a 5.5 kW drive. CM conducted emission levels at the drive input were measured for each combination. Unshielded 50 m cables increased broadband CM noise by 10–14 dB relative to the 5 m reference below 1 MHz, primarily due to cable-to-ground capacitance estimated at 3.4 nF for the 50 m case. Shield grounding at both ends reduced CM emissions by 5–9 dB across 150 kHz–5 MHz for the 20 m cable. A transmission-line model incorporating per-unit-length parameters measured by time-domain reflectometry reproduced the resonant structure of the emission spectrum within ±3 dB. Practical wiring recommendations derived from the data are summarised for installation engineers.

title: Thermal Derating of EMC Filter Components Under Continuous Duty in Enclosed Drive Cabinets
abstract: EMC input filters for variable-speed drives are frequently mounted inside closed industrial cabinets where ambient temperatures can reach 55–65 °C, yet most component datasheets specify capacitance and ESR at 25 °C. This study characterises the thermal behaviour of X2 and Y2 film capacitors and nanocrystalline common-mode chokes under continuous 100% rated current at cabinet temperatures up to 70 °C. Capacitance drift in Y2 components reached −12% at 65 °C, shifting insertion-loss notch frequencies by 4–7% and potentially reducing CM attenuation by up to 4 dB near design-critical frequencies. Core loss in nanocrystalline chokes increased surface temperature by 18 K above ambient at rated current, consistent with manufacturer core-loss curves. Updated derating guidelines are proposed that increase capacitor values by 15% and choke inductance by 10% relative to room-temperature designs to maintain compliant insertion loss across the operating temperature range.

title: EMC Filter Design for SiC MOSFET-Based Motor Drives: Comparison with IGBT Baseline at 150 kHz–30 MHz
abstract: Silicon carbide MOSFET inverters switch at voltages and currents with rise times below 50 ns, generating significantly higher high-frequency conducted emissions than conventional IGBT-based drives of equivalent power rating. This work compares the conducted emission spectra of a 7.5 kW SiC MOSFET drive (switching at 50 kHz) and an IGBT baseline (switching at 8 kHz) under the same load, and documents the additional filter attenuation required to achieve IEC 61800-3 Category C2 compliance for the SiC case. The SiC drive exceeded the Category C2 quasi-peak limit by up to 22 dB in the 5–30 MHz band compared to 9 dB for the IGBT. An optimised four-stage LC filter reduced the worst-case exceedance to within the 6 dB safety margin, at the cost of a 40% increase in filter volume relative to the IGBT design. Measured and simulated spectra agree within ±3 dB across the full range.

title: EMC Considerations for Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Automation
abstract: This book chapter provides a self-contained treatment of EMC requirements and mitigation strategies for variable-speed drive systems in industrial automation contexts. It covers the regulatory framework (IEC 61800-3, IEC 61000-6-2, and IEC 61000-6-4), the physical origins of conducted and radiated disturbances in PWM inverter drives, and practical filter and shielding design methods. Worked examples are based on measurement data from 2.2 kW to 55 kW drive systems. The chapter addresses installation variables including motor cable routing, grounding topology, and proximity to sensitive signal cables, with quantitative guidance on separation distances and screen termination. A section on SiC-based drives discusses how faster switching transitions alter both emission profiles and filter requirements relative to IGBT designs. The chapter is intended for practising engineers and postgraduate students with a background in power electronics.

title: Frequency-Domain Characterisation of Ground Impedance Effects on Common-Mode Filter Performance in Drive Systems
abstract: The attenuation provided by Y-capacitors in common-mode EMC filters depends on the impedance of the protective earth (PE) connection, which varies substantially between industrial installations. This paper characterises PE impedance at 47 industrial sites across northern Serbia using a vector network analyser, finding that impedance magnitude at 1 MHz ranges from 0.4 Ω to 18 Ω and exhibits significant inductive character above 500 kHz. The measured impedance profiles are used as input to a circuit simulation of a 15 kW drive with a three-stage CM filter, evaluating worst-case degradation in CM insertion loss. CM attenuation at 1 MHz degraded by up to 9 dB between the best and worst PE cases, rendering a filter that passed IEC 61800-3 Category C2 under laboratory conditions non-compliant in 14% of simulated field conditions. A modified filter topology using a split CM choke with partial differential-mode rejection reduces this variability to within ±2 dB.

title: Active Common-Mode Voltage Reduction in SiC Inverter Drives Using Predictive PWM with Reduced Switching Vectors
abstract: Common-mode voltage (CMV) generated by three-phase two-level inverters reaches peak values of Vdc/2 per switching event and is the primary driver of CM conducted emissions and bearing current damage in motor drives. This preprint evaluates a PWM strategy that restricts the active switching vector set to eliminate zero vectors, thereby reducing the peak CMV from Vdc/2 to Vdc/6 with no additional hardware. Implemented on a 7.5 kW SiC inverter drive, the strategy reduced CM conducted emission peaks in the 150–500 kHz band by 8–14 dB compared to standard space-vector PWM at equal fundamental output quality. Total harmonic distortion of the output phase voltage increased from 2.1% to 3.8%, remaining within acceptable limits. CM choke size in a co-designed filter was reduced by 35% for equivalent IEC 61800-3 Category C2 compliance. Thermal measurements confirm no significant change in switch loss distribution.

title: Comparison of Deterministic and Empirical Propagation Models for Gateway Coverage Estimation in a European City Centre
abstract: Gateway placement in LoRaWAN deployments is commonly guided by empirical models calibrated for generic urban environments, yet their accuracy in dense historic city centres with irregular street patterns is poorly documented. This paper compares predictions from the Okumura–Hata, COST 231 Walfisch–Ikegami, and a 3-D ray-tracing tool (implemented in-house) against 6 200 measurement points collected in the old town area of Pécs, Hungary. Building geometry was derived from a municipal GIS dataset at 1:500 scale. The ray-tracing model achieved a mean absolute error of 3.1 dB, compared with 6.4 dB and 8.9 dB for the two empirical models. Computational time for ray tracing was approximately 40 minutes per gateway location on a standard workstation; a reduced-order version using only two-bounce reflections reduced this to 9 minutes with a 0.8 dB increase in error. Practical implications for rapid deployment planning are discussed.

title: Separation of Overlapping Tonal Components in Gearbox Noise Using Frequency-Domain ICA
abstract: This paper examines independent component analysis (ICA) applied in the frequency domain to separate tonal noise components emitted by a two-stage helical gearbox operating at variable load. Acoustic signals were recorded with a six-microphone planar array at a sampling rate of 51.2 kHz in a semi-anechoic test cell. The mixing matrix was estimated separately within 16 Hz sub-bands, and phase ambiguity across bands was resolved using a cross-band consistency constraint. Separation quality was assessed using the signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) and a gear-mesh harmonic isolation index. At nominal load, SDR improved by 8.4 dB over single-channel cepstral filtering. At partial load, where spectral overlap was more pronounced, the gain reduced to 5.1 dB. The method was compared against FastICA and JADE on the same dataset; the proposed approach outperformed both when source stationarity assumptions were relaxed. Results suggest that frequency-domain ICA with band-wise phase correction is practical for routine gearbox noise audits without requiring encoder feedback.

title: Zooplankton assemblages of sodic shallow lakes in Vojvodina: a first regional survey
abstract: We conducted a baseline survey of zooplankton communities across 24 sodic shallow lakes in Vojvodina (northern Serbia) during spring and summer 2009. Lakes were sampled with 55 µm mesh tow nets and water chemistry was characterised by 14 physicochemical variables including conductivity, pH, and major ion concentrations. A total of 87 zooplankton taxa were identified, dominated by Cladocera (41 taxa) and Copepoda (29 taxa). Cluster analysis resolved four community types broadly associated with conductivity gradients. High-conductivity lakes (>5 mS cm⁻¹) were characterised by halotolerant cladocerans such as Moina brachiata and Arctodiaptomus spinosus, while lower-conductivity sites supported more typical freshwater assemblages. Species richness per lake ranged from 7 to 31 taxa. The data provide a reference baseline for ongoing metacommunity and biogeographic studies of this threatened wetland type.

title: Sezonska varijabilnost zajednica veslonožaca (Copepoda) u plitkim slatinskim jezerima Vojvodine
abstract: Analizirane su sezonske promene u strukturi zajednica veslonožaca u šest plitkih slatinskih jezera na teritoriji Vojvodine u toku 2011. i 2012. godine. Uzorkovanje je obavljano mesečno mrežom za zooplankton (55 µm) i cilindričnim uzorkivačem zapremine 10 L. Zabeleženo je ukupno 22 vrste veslonožaca. Abundanca kalanoidnih kopepoda pokazala je statistički značajnu pozitivnu korelaciju sa koncentracijom rastvoredog kiseonika (r = 0,61, p < 0,001) i negativnu korelaciju sa temperaturom vode u letnjim mesecima. Ciklopoidni veslonošci dominirali su kasno leti i u jesen. Analiza glavnih komponenti pokazala je da fizičko-hemijski parametri objašnjavaju 54% varijabilnosti u sastavu zajednica, dok je sezonski efekat odgovarao za dodatnih 18%. Rezultati ukazuju na izrazitu sezonsku dinamiku koja može maskirati prostorni metacomunity signal ukoliko se ne kontroliše pri analizi.

title: Patch connectivity and passive dispersal of Cladocera propagules in a fragmented sodic wetland landscape
abstract: We examined how landscape connectivity among 27 sodic wetland patches in the Vojvodina lowlands influences the passive dispersal of cladoceran resting eggs (ephippia). Connectivity was modelled as effective distance accounting for land cover resistance (arable land, road infrastructure, grassland corridors) using circuit-theory analysis in Circuitscape. Sediment cores (0–2 cm) from each wetland were subjected to egg-bank extraction; hatching experiments identified 34 Cladocera taxa. We tested whether effective connectivity predicted compositional similarity (Sørensen dissimilarity) between egg banks, controlling for environmental distance. Partial Mantel tests revealed a significant negative relationship between connectivity and egg-bank dissimilarity (r = −0.31, p = 0.002), independent of environmental dissimilarity. Wetlands connected by semi-natural grassland corridors showed 22% lower dissimilarity than equivalent pairs separated by arable land. These findings indicate that landscape permeability matters for zooplankton propagule exchange even in taxa considered highly mobile.

title: DNA metabarcoding reveals cryptic zooplankton diversity in Pannonian sodic lakes previously undetected by morphological identification
abstract: We applied DNA metabarcoding (18S rRNA V9 region) to zooplankton communities from 15 sodic lakes in Vojvodina and compared taxonomic richness to parallel morphological identification by light microscopy. DNA was extracted from size-fractionated (55–200 µm and >200 µm) ethanol-preserved net samples from summer 2021. Illumina MiSeq sequencing yielded a mean of 48,600 quality-filtered reads per sample. Metabarcoding detected a mean of 47 operational taxonomic units (OTUs) per lake compared to 23 morphological taxa; overlap between methods was 61% at genus level. Seven putative cryptic Cladocera lineages were identified that matched no described species in regional reference libraries. Morphological identification systematically underestimated rotifer diversity. Correspondence between community dissimilarity matrices from the two methods was moderate (Procrustes r = 0.63, p < 0.001), suggesting that metacommunity inferences may differ depending on the identification approach used. A regional reference barcode library is in preparation.

title: Stochastic and deterministic assembly processes along a salinity gradient in Pannonian wetlands: insights from null-model analysis
abstract: We applied null-model approaches to disentangle stochastic (neutral) and deterministic (niche-based) assembly processes in zooplankton communities across a salinity gradient (0.3–18.2 mS cm⁻¹) encompassing 33 Pannonian sodic wetlands sampled in 2022. Standardised effect sizes (SES) of beta-NTI and RC-Bray were calculated from 999 randomisations of the species-by-site matrix. At low to intermediate salinity (0.3–5 mS cm⁻¹), variable selection accounted for 38% of community turnover, while stochastic dispersal accounted for 29%. At high salinity (>10 mS cm⁻¹), homogeneous selection dominated (52%), indicating strong environmental filtering by ionic stress. Heterogeneous dispersal was negligible (<8%) across all salinity classes. A piecewise structural equation model confirmed that salinity mediated the shift from stochastic to deterministic assembly. Results clarify the conditions under which connectivity restoration can be expected to enhance beta diversity in this wetland type.

abstract: Ispitivane su promene u sastavu zajednica Cladocera kroz vreme rekonstrukcijom paleolimnoloških zapisa iz sedimentnih jezgara uzetih u pet slatinskih jezera u Vojvodini. title: Heterotrophic plate count versus flow cytometry for monitoring microbial regrowth in treated water: a comparative field study
abstract: Heterotrophic plate count (HPC) on R2A agar and flow cytometry with SYBR Green I staining were applied in parallel to water samples from three waterworks in the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal catchment area over six months. Flow cytometric total cell counts were consistently 10–100-fold higher than HPC values, with the greatest divergence observed after secondary chlorination steps. Intact cell counts correlated positively with dissolved organic carbon levels (Spearman ρ = 0.63) but showed weaker correlation with turbidity. HPC proved insensitive to uncultivable fractions that comprised, on average, 92 % of the cytometrically enumerated population. Regression analysis indicated that neither method alone predicted downstream biofilm accumulation indices adequately; a combined index incorporating both measures performed better (R² = 0.71). Findings support incorporating flow cytometry into routine monitoring alongside HPC for a more complete picture of regrowth potential.

title: Short-term heart rate variability indices in medical students during a sustained academic examination period: a repeated-measures observational study
abstract: Chronic academic stress is associated with measurable shifts in autonomic tone, yet within-individual trajectories across an extended examination period remain poorly characterised. Forty-one first-year medical students at the University of Novi Sad were monitored at four time points across a six-week examination session and one recovery week. Five-minute resting ECG recordings were obtained under standardised conditions each morning. Time-domain indices (SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50) and frequency-domain indices (LF power, HF power, LF/HF ratio) were derived using a Biopac MP160 system and analysed with custom MATLAB scripts. Perceived stress was quantified using the Serbian adaptation of the Cohen Perceived Stress Scale. RMSSD fell by a mean of 11.2 ms between baseline and peak examination week (p = 0.003), while LF/HF ratio rose by 0.38 units (p = 0.007), indicating a shift toward sympathetic dominance. Salivary cortisol collected at two time points correlated negatively with RMSSD (r = −0.44, p = 0.004). Recovery-week values returned toward baseline but did not fully normalise within seven days. The findings support using short HRV recordings as a practical, low-burden biomarker of accumulated academic stress in student populations.

title: Comparison of fast Fourier transform and continuous wavelet transform for LF/HF ratio estimation in non-stationary heart rate variability recordings
abstract: Standard power spectral analysis of heart rate variability assumes signal stationarity, an assumption frequently violated in real recordings obtained under psychological stress. This methodological study compared fast Fourier transform (FFT) applied to five-minute epochs against a Morlet-based continuous wavelet transform (CWT) applied to the same recordings, using data from 28 healthy adult volunteers who underwent a Stroop colour-word interference task of ten minutes duration followed by a ten-minute recovery phase. ECG was recorded at 1000 Hz; R-R interval series were extracted by automated detection with manual correction. LF power (0.04–0.15 Hz) and HF power (0.15–0.40 Hz) were computed using both methods across three consecutive sub-epochs. Agreement between FFT and CWT estimates was assessed with Bland-Altman plots and intraclass correlation. ICC values were high during rest (0.91) but substantially lower during active stress (0.67), with FFT systematically underestimating transient LF bursts captured by CWT. The results indicate that CWT provides more temporally resolved spectral estimates during periods of rapid autonomic fluctuation and should be preferred when recordings cannot be restricted to steady-state conditions.

title: Autonomic modulation during a simulated occupational stress protocol in administrative workers: HRV and blood pressure variability analysis
abstract: Occupational stress in sedentary administrative roles is a recognised cardiovascular risk factor, but controlled laboratory models capturing its autonomic signature are scarce in regional populations. Thirty-two administrative employees (17 women, 15 men; mean age 34.6 ± 7.1 years) from two public institutions in Novi Sad underwent a 25-minute protocol combining time-pressured cognitive tasks and simulated supervisory criticism. Continuous beat-to-beat blood pressure was recorded with a Finapres NOVA device alongside ECG; baroreflex sensitivity was estimated by the sequence method. HRV spectral analysis used a Morlet CWT applied to five-minute segments. During the stress phase, LF/HF rose from 1.8 ± 0.6 to 3.1 ± 0.9 (p < 0.001), mean arterial pressure increased by 9.4 mmHg, and baroreflex sensitivity decreased from 14.2 to 9.7 ms/mmHg (p = 0.002). Women showed a smaller LF/HF increase than men (interaction p = 0.04), consistent with reported sex differences in sympathovagal reactivity. Trait anxiety scores obtained by the Serbian STAI-X2 were independently associated with larger LF/HF responses (β = 0.31, p = 0.03). The protocol appears reproducible and suitable for future field-validation studies.

title: Resting vagal tone as a moderator of cortisol reactivity to acute psychosocial stress: a pilot study in young adults
abstract: Vagally mediated heart rate variability (vmHRV) has been proposed as an index of self-regulatory capacity, yet its relationship with hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis reactivity in response to acute psychosocial stress is inconsistently reported. This pilot study recruited 24 healthy university students (12 men, 12 women; age 22–27 years) who underwent the Trier Social Stress Test adapted for a laboratory setting. Resting vmHRV was characterised by RMSSD and HF power derived from a five-minute baseline ECG recorded the morning before testing. Salivary cortisol was collected at baseline, immediately post-stress, and at 15- and 30-minute recovery time points. Participants in the high vmHRV tertile showed a peak cortisol response 28% lower than the low vmHRV tertile (p = 0.04) and faster return to baseline by the 30-minute sample. Linear regression controlling for sex and body mass index retained vmHRV as a significant negative predictor of cortisol area under the curve (β = −0.38, p = 0.03). The sample size limits generalisation, and replication in a larger cohort with ambulatory cortisol measurement is warranted.
venue: Journal of Psychophysiological Research

title: Heart rate variability monitoring in shift workers: a six-month longitudinal study of autonomic adaptation and subjective well-being
abstract: Rotating shift work disrupts circadian rhythms and is associated with impaired cardiovascular autonomic regulation, but longitudinal within-subject data extending beyond twelve weeks are limited. Twenty-six nurses from a general hospital in Novi Sad participated in a six-month observational study. HRV was recorded on four scheduled occasions aligned with morning, afternoon, and night shift cycles using a validated wrist-worn ECG sensor (mean recording duration 20 minutes per session). Time-domain, frequency-domain, and non-linear indices (SD1, SD2, sample entropy) were computed. Mixed-effects models indicated that SDNN declined progressively over the first three months during night-shift weeks (mean reduction 14.7 ms, p = 0.001) with partial stabilisation thereafter, suggesting incomplete adaptation. Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores worsened in parallel and were associated with lower RMSSD (r = 0.39, p = 0.005). Daytime HRV recordings on rest days partially recovered but remained below baseline in 17 of 26 participants at month six. These findings suggest cumulative rather than transient autonomic strain in rotating shift nurses and point to specific time windows where targeted interventions may be most effective.

title: A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments
abstract: This paper describes the design and evaluation of an authenticated bootloader protocol intended for 8-bit microcontroller-based sensor nodes communicating over IEEE 802.15.4 radio links in industrial SCADA deployments. The protocol uses HMAC-SHA256 for image authentication and a two-phase commit scheme to prevent partial writes during interrupted transmissions. Experimental evaluation was conducted on a testbed of 24 nodes deployed across a simulated substation environment, with artificial packet-loss rates ranging from 5% to 40%. Mean firmware delivery time for a 64 KB image increased from 38 seconds under ideal conditions to 147 seconds at 40% packet loss, while no corrupted images were accepted across 2 400 delivery trials. Code size overhead on the target MCU was 3.2 KB of flash. The paper also discusses replay-attack resistance and the limitations of symmetric key management at scale, proposing a zone-based key hierarchy as a practical mitigation for deployments with up to 500 nodes.

title: Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links
abstract: Firmware images for constrained devices rarely change more than a few percent between successive releases, yet most over-the-air update mechanisms transmit full images. This paper evaluates three binary delta algorithms — bsdiff, VCDIFF, and a purpose-built block-aligned differencer — applied to firmware images from four representative industrial sensor product lines. Patch sizes across 38 consecutive release pairs averaged 11.4% of full image size for bsdiff and 14.7% for the block-aligned approach, with the latter requiring 40% less RAM during reconstruction. Transmission time over a simulated 1.2 kbit/s channel, representative of 868 MHz narrowband industrial radio, was reduced from an average of 4.1 minutes to 28 seconds. Reconstruction failure rates under 10% artificial bit-error conditions were below 0.3% for all schemes when combined with a 16-bit CRC per block. The paper includes a complexity analysis and discusses applicability to devices with less than 8 KB of available RAM.

title: Формална верификација протокола за испоруку фирмвера методом провере модела
abstract: У овом раду примењен је алат за проверу модела SPIN на протокол за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера у бежичним телеметријским мрежама. Протокол је моделован у Прометеловом језику, а верификација је обухватила 14 безбедносних и животних особина формулисаних у линеарној темпоралној логици. Пронађена су три услова у којима поновна репродукција старе поруке може да доведе до инсталације претходне верзије фирмвера ако је монотони бројач секвенце нулиран након ресетовања уређаја. Предложено је проширење протокола са тrajnim бројачем у заштићеном нелетљивом меморијском простору. Исправљени протокол је верификован без кршења постављених особина у простору стања са до 2,1 × 10⁸ стања. Рад такође дискутује ограничења апстракције криптографских примитива у SPIN моделу и предлаже методологију за раздвојено моделовање протоколне логике и криптографских претпоставки.

title: Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study
abstract: Managing cryptographic keys across hundreds of constrained field devices is a practical bottleneck in industrial wireless deployments. This paper systematically compares five key distribution schemes — pre-shared master key, pairwise key pre-distribution, a Blom matrix scheme, a hierarchical certificate authority approach adapted for 6LoWPAN, and an elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman bootstrapping protocol — across three criteria: memory footprint on a Cortex-M0 class device, time to complete key establishment after node power-on, and resilience to node capture. Measurements were taken on a physical testbed of 60 nodes. The Blom scheme achieved the best balance for networks under 200 nodes, requiring 1.8 KB RAM and completing key establishment in under 400 ms. The ECC bootstrapping protocol was the only scheme providing forward secrecy but demanded 14 KB RAM and 2.3 seconds for key exchange, making it unsuitable for the lowest-tier devices. Practical recommendations are derived for three deployment tiers based on device capability.
venue: International Journal of Industrial Communication and Control Systems

title: Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site
abstract: LoRa physical layer spreading factors SF7 through SF12 offer data rates from roughly 250 bit/s to 5.5 kbit/s at the expense of airtime, a constraint with direct implications for over-the-air firmware update feasibility. This paper reports on measurements conducted at a chemical plant in Novi Sad over six weeks using a network of 18 end-devices at distances between 80 m and 1.4 km from a single gateway. Packet delivery ratio at SF12 averaged 91.3% under normal plant operation but dropped to 73.8% during periods of heavy crane and conveyor activity. A store-and-forward segmentation protocol with per-segment HMAC authentication was deployed, and mean time to complete a 32 KB firmware update was measured at 22 minutes at SF12. The paper proposes an adaptive spreading-factor selection policy that reduced average update time to 9.4 minutes while maintaining delivery success above 97% across all trials.

title: Replay Attack Taxonomy and Countermeasure Classification for Over-the-Air Firmware Update Protocols
abstract: Replay attacks against firmware update protocols can result in downgrade to vulnerable firmware versions, denial of service, or unnecessary device reboots in safety-critical industrial settings. This book chapter surveys replay attack vectors specific to constrained wireless devices, classifying them along four axes: attacker capability (passive monitor, active injector, insider), network topology (star, mesh, multi-hop), device state (idle, update-in-progress, post-install reboot), and available countermeasure class (nonce-based, timestamp-based, monotonic counter, challenge–response). For each combination, the chapter provides an analysis of effectiveness and implementation cost in terms of RAM, non-volatile write cycles, and required time synchronization infrastructure. Fourteen representative firmware update protocols from research literature and three from open-source embedded projects are mapped onto the taxonomy. The chapter concludes with a decision framework that assists protocol designers in selecting countermeasure combinations appropriate to their threat model and device constraints.

title: Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers
abstract: Applying binary patches to firmware in the field requires verification mechanisms that can detect partial or corrupted patch delivery without storing the complete expected image. This paper proposes a Merkle hash tree construction adapted for delta patches, where leaf nodes correspond to fixed-size patch chunks and the root hash is authenticated by an ECDSA signature over NIST P-256. The scheme was implemented on an STM32L4 series microcontroller with 64 KB RAM. Hash tree construction over a 16 KB patch (32 leaves) required 210 ms and consumed a peak of 4.1 KB stack space. Verification of a partial delivery — detecting one corrupted chunk among 32 — required fewer than 50 ms. The paper compares this approach against full-image HMAC and rolling-hash alternatives in terms of detection granularity, storage requirements, and recovery strategy. A discussion of the tradeoffs in choosing tree depth is included, with measurements at depths 3, 4, and 5.

title: Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model
abstract: Regulatory duty-cycle limits in the European 868 MHz ISM band constrain transmission time to 1% in sub-band 1, directly affecting over-the-air firmware update completion times for LPWAN devices. This paper develops a queuing-theory-based analytical model for firmware delivery latency under duty-cycle constraints, accounting for segmentation overhead, retransmission probability, and concurrent traffic from non-update messages. The model is parameterised using empirical measurements from a 30-node LoRaWAN testbed. Analytical predictions of mean delivery time matched measurements within 8% across all tested configurations. The model predicts that for a 64 KB image at SF10, mean delivery time under 1% duty cycle is 4.7 hours in a lightly loaded network and rises to over 18 hours under moderate concurrent telemetry load. A scheduling strategy that prioritises update segments during predicted low-traffic windows is described and shown analytically to reduce mean delivery time by 31%.

title: Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee
abstract: When many co-located devices require the same firmware update simultaneously, unicast delivery multiplies airtime linearly with node count. This paper describes a secure multicast delivery scheme for Zigbee-based industrial sensor clusters, using AES-128 CCM* group encryption with individual per-device session key wrapping to prevent one node from decrypting another's update confirmation. The protocol was implemented on CC2530-based nodes and evaluated in a testbed of 8 and 16 node clusters. For a 48 KB image, multicast delivery to a 16-node cluster completed in 6.8 minutes versus 41.3 minutes for sequential unicast, a factor of 6.1 improvement. Delivery success rate was 98.7% at 16 nodes under representative packet loss of 8%. The paper analyses the key management overhead introduced by per-device key wrapping and discusses the session key refresh interval as a function of assumed node compromise rate.

title: Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity
abstract: Public-key certificate validation normally depends on online revocation checking, which is infeasible for industrial field devices that communicate only intermittently. This paper proposes an offline certificate validation scheme for firmware authentication in which short-lived leaf certificates, valid for a configurable window of 24–168 hours, are bundled with the firmware image and verified against a pre-installed intermediate CA certificate stored in device ROM. Certificate revocation is handled by expiry rather than CRL or OCSP. The scheme uses X.509 profiles trimmed to fit within 512 bytes using a custom DER subset. Implementation and evaluation were performed on an ARM Cortex-M3 device with 32 KB RAM; certificate parsing and verification completed in 310 ms using a software ECC library. The paper analyses the security implications of the short-lived certificate approach under various attacker models, including the case where the attacker can delay delivery to extend a certificate's apparent validity.

title: Протокол за верификацију ланца испоруке фирмвера у вишестепеним телеметријским мрежама
abstract: У вишестепеним индустријским мрежама фирмвер може проћи кроз неколико посредничких чворова — концентратора и гетвеја — пре него што стигне до крајњег уређаја. Свaki посреднички чвор представља потенцијалну тачку манипулације. Овај рад предлаже протокол за верификацију ланца испоруке у коме сваки посреднички чвор потписује потврду о пријему и прослеђивању фирмверског сегмента, формирајући верификабилни низ потврда. Коначни уређај верификује цео ланац пре инсталације. Протокол је анализиран у моделу са до четири посреднička нивоа. Поред безбедносне анализе, рад мери додатно кашњење које уносе операције потписивања на различитим класама чворова: 28 ms по потпису на концентратору са Cortex-M4 процесором наспрам 190 ms на Cortex-M0+ чвору. Предложена је хибридна шема у којој само концентраtори потписују ланац, а крajnji уређаји верификују само коренски потпис произвођача, чиме се кашњење своди на прихватљив ниво.

title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices
abstract: Anticipated deployment lifetimes of industrial sensor nodes of 10–20 years motivate evaluation of post-quantum signature algorithms for firmware authentication on severely constrained hardware. This paper benchmarks four NIST post-quantum signature candidates — CRYSTALS-Dilithium2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and a lattice-based scheme submitted to the ongoing standardisation process — on two representative Class 1 IoT platforms: an ARM Cortex-M0+ at 48 MHz with 32 KB RAM and a Cortex-M4 at 120 MHz with 256 KB RAM. Metrics collected include signature verification time, public key and signature sizes, and peak RAM consumption. On the Cortex-M0+ platform, Falcon-512 verification completed in 480 ms consuming 28 KB RAM peak, which exceeds available memory, while SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s verified in 1 140 ms with 6.2 KB peak RAM, making it the only scheme feasible on the lower-end device. Dilithium2 was feasible on the Cortex-M4 at 94 ms. The paper discusses the practical tradeoffs for protocol designers choosing between these schemes given device capability distribution in a deployment.

title: Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments
abstract: NB-IoT deployment in basement-level and shielded industrial environments produces highly variable signal conditions, with RSRP measurements in one monitored processing facility ranging from −85 dBm to −138 dBm across 22 fixed sensor positions. This paper describes an adaptive firmware delivery protocol that adjusts segment size and retransmission window based on real-time channel quality indicator reports available in the NB-IoT stack. Segment sizes were varied between 64 and 512 bytes; the adaptive scheme selected optimal sizes per device per update session. In a 22-device testbed deployment over four months, the adaptive protocol reduced total update time by 38% compared to a fixed 128-byte segment baseline and reduced the number of incomplete update sessions from 11.4% to 2.1%. Energy consumption per completed update was also measured on battery-powered nodes, with the adaptive scheme consuming 12% less energy due to fewer retransmissions. A lightweight predictor using a 5-point CQI moving average was sufficient to achieve near-optimal segment sizing.
