title: Scheduling Strategies for Minimising Latency in FPGA-Based FIR Filter Datapaths
abstract: This paper examines four list-scheduling heuristics—ASAP, ALAP, force-directed, and a proposed priority-function variant—applied to finite impulse response filter datapaths targeting a mid-range Virtex-4 device. Benchmarks consist of eight filter specifications ranging from 16 to 128 taps with coefficient word-lengths between 12 and 20 bits. The proposed priority function combines slack and operator mobility to defer binding decisions until resource pressure peaks are identified. Across all benchmarks, the heuristic achieves average latency reductions of 11.3% over ALAP and 6.8% over force-directed scheduling, while keeping DSP48 utilisation within 5% of the ALAP baseline. Register usage increases modestly, by 8% on average. Synthesis and place-and-route results are obtained with Xilinx ISE 10.1. The study concludes that scheduling order significantly affects registered pipeline depth even when the nominal clock cycle count is equal, and recommends latency measurement after routing rather than after synthesis.

title: Fixed-Point Wordlength Optimisation for IIR Filters Implemented on Xilinx FPGAs
abstract: Infinite impulse response filters are sensitive to coefficient quantisation, and selecting wordlengths that respect a signal-to-noise ratio constraint while minimising LUT and DSP slice consumption is a non-trivial combinatorial problem. This work applies a branch-and-bound search over the space of per-coefficient wordlengths for second-order section cascades with up to six sections. The objective function is a weighted sum of estimated LUT cost and DSP48E slice count derived from Xilinx XST synthesis reports. Fourteen filter designs from audio and control applications with SNR requirements between 55 dB and 90 dB serve as benchmarks. The branch-and-bound procedure finds solutions that reduce total slice count by 17–34% compared with uniform wordlength assignment at the maximum required precision, with runtime under 40 seconds for all tested cases on a standard workstation. Overflow protection via saturation arithmetic is included in the cost model.

title: A Comparison of Commercial and Open-Source High-Level Synthesis Flows for Small DSP Kernels
abstract: This comparative study evaluates three high-level synthesis tools—two commercial (AutoPilot-derived and a proprietary academic spin-off) and one open-source (LegUp 3.0)—against manually written VHDL for a set of six DSP kernels: a 32-tap FIR filter, a radix-2 FFT butterfly, a biquad filter, a CIC decimator, a moving-average block, and a simple correlator. Each kernel is described in ANSI C with pragmas as required by each tool. Quality metrics include clock frequency achieved on a Cyclone IV device, logic element count, DSP block consumption, and lines of constraint needed. Commercial tools match or exceed hand-coded frequency on four of six kernels; LegUp trails by 12–28% on frequency but produces substantially fewer lines of RTL. The biquad and CIC cases reveal sensitivity to loop trip-count annotation. The paper provides concrete guidance on pragma usage and discusses where manual RTL remains preferable.

title: Resource Sharing Constraints in HLS for Multi-Rate Signal Processing Chains
abstract: Multi-rate signal processing chains contain blocks operating at different sample rates, which creates asymmetric operator utilisation across pipeline stages and makes naive resource sharing ineffective or harmful. This paper formulates resource sharing as an integer linear program in which operators are grouped by compatible sample rates and binding feasibility constraints are derived from a combined control-data flow graph. The ILP is solved with GLPK for chains of up to twelve blocks at four distinct rates. Results on a Kintex-7 XC7K160T show reductions in DSP48E2 count of 19–31% over Vivado HLS with default settings, at the cost of a 7 ns increase in initiation interval for the fastest chains. The method is implemented as a post-processing pass on the HLS-generated schedule and does not require modifications to the HLS front-end. Experimental chains include a software-defined radio receive path and a sonar preprocessing chain.

title: Loop Flattening and Unrolling Trade-offs in HLS-Generated FFT Pipelines on UltraScale Devices
abstract: Vivado HLS and its successor Vitis HLS expose loop unrolling, flattening, and pipelining pragmas whose interactions are not always predictable from documentation alone. This paper presents a systematic design-space exploration for radix-2 and radix-4 FFT pipelines with transform sizes from 64 to 4096 points. For each combination of transform size and radix, a two-level loop in Vivado HLS 2017.4 is compiled under 18 pragma configurations. The exploration metric is a product of initiation interval, DSP48E2 count, and BRAM utilisation normalised to the device's XC7VX485T capacity. Results identify that partial unrolling factors that are not powers of two systematically cause HLS to insert unnecessary FIFOs, inflating BRAM by up to 40%. Fully flattened loops with a pipeline pragma at the inner level provide the best metric in 14 of 18 configurations. A lookup table of recommended pragma combinations is provided.

title: An AXI4-Stream Interface Generator for HLS-Synthesised Signal Processing IP Cores
abstract: Integrating HLS-generated IP cores into SoC designs requires correct AXI4-Stream handshake behaviour that commercial tools sometimes implement inconsistently, particularly regarding TLAST assertion and backpressure handling. This work describes a Python-based generator that takes a JSON description of data width, throughput, and latency and emits a thin VHDL wrapper enforcing strict AXI4-Stream protocol compliance verified against the ARM AMBA specification. The generator was tested with 11 signal processing IP cores synthesised with Vitis HLS 2020.1 and integrated on a Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC. Co-simulation using ModelSim confirms zero protocol violations across all cores. End-to-end throughput measurements on a ZCU102 board show that wrapper overhead does not reduce maximum throughput below 95% of the bare HLS core rate in any case. The generator is released under BSD-2 licence and is available from the laboratory repository.

title: FPGA Acceleration of Adaptive Beamforming for a Small Ultrasonic Sensor Array
abstract: Delay-and-sum and minimum variance distortionless response beamforming for a 16-element ultrasonic sensor array are implemented on a Xilinx Kintex UltraScale KCU105 board. Sample rate is 2 MSPS per channel with 14-bit ADC output. The MVDR beamformer requires a matrix inversion step; this is realised via a pipelined QR decomposition based on CORDIC rotations. Both beamformers are described in HLS C++ and synthesised with Vitis HLS 2021.1. The MVDR design achieves an update rate of 48,000 steering vectors per second at a 200 MHz clock, consuming 312 DSP58E2 slices and 1.1 Mb of BRAM. A fixed-point CORDIC unit accurate to 16 bits is characterised in isolation. Measured null depth in an anechoic chamber confirms that the fixed-point MVDR implementation degrades null depth by no more than 2.1 dB relative to a floating-point software reference. Power consumption is measured at 4.3 W.

title: Partial Reconfiguration of Signal Processing Pipelines Under Real-Time Constraints on Zynq-7000
abstract: Partial reconfiguration allows sections of an FPGA fabric to be reprogrammed while the remainder continues operating. This paper quantifies the latency and data integrity cost of partial reconfiguration when switching between three signal processing kernels—an FIR decimator, a DFT-based spectrometer, and a matched filter—on a Zynq-7000 XC7Z045. Reconfiguration bitstreams of 1.2–2.8 Mb are loaded via the ICAP port driven by the ARM Cortex-A9 processor running bare-metal code. Measured reconfiguration times range from 8.4 ms to 19.1 ms. A double-buffering scheme using BRAM for incoming sample storage ensures zero sample loss during reconfiguration when the input sample rate is at or below 1.5 MSPS. The paper characterises the pblock size and placement constraints needed to keep static routing clean, and reports one failure mode caused by partial bitstream misalignment in Vivado 2019.2 with a proposed workaround.

title: Automated Precision Analysis for HLS-Based Radar Signal Processing with Interval Arithmetic
abstract: Selecting fixed-point formats in HLS designs typically relies on simulation-based statistical analysis, which can miss worst-case inputs. This paper uses interval arithmetic to propagate wordlength bounds through a pulse-compression radar processing chain described as a directed graph of arithmetic operations. The chain includes range FFT, Doppler FFT, CFAR detection, and a moving-target indicator filter. For each arithmetic node, interval width is mapped to a minimum wordlength that bounds the absolute truncation error below a user-specified threshold. The method is implemented as a Python tool that reads Vitis HLS 2022.1 intermediate representation and outputs #pragma HLS interface bitwidth directives. Applied to three radar waveform configurations (pulse width 1–10 µs, bandwidth 5–80 MHz), the tool reduces total bit-width by 14.7% on average compared with double-precision floating-point emulation-derived formats, while the CFAR false alarm rate remains within 0.3% of the floating-point reference.

title: Benchmarking Vitis HLS 2023.1 Against OpenCL-Based HLS for FPGA-Accelerated Signal Processing on Alveo Cards
abstract: AMD Alveo U250 and U55C data-centre cards support both Vitis HLS and Vitis OpenCL kernel flows. This paper benchmarks both flows on eight signal processing kernels including a polyphase channeliser, a recursive least-squares adaptive filter, and a short-time Fourier transform block. Compilation time, kernel clock frequency, DDR4 bandwidth utilisation, and host-to-device transfer overhead are measured for each kernel under both flows. The OpenCL flow achieves slightly higher frequencies (mean +4.2%) on memory-bandwidth-bound kernels owing to better automatic burst inference, while the HLS C++ flow requires fewer lines of host code and shows shorter incremental compile times. Kernel latency measured end-to-end from the host differs by less than 3% for five of eight kernels. Practical recommendations for choosing between the flows based on kernel type and iteration cycle are drawn.

title: Label noise in wrist-worn activity datasets: sources, prevalence, and impact on CNN training
abstract: Activity recognition datasets collected in free-living conditions frequently contain noisy labels arising from annotation latency, ambiguous transitions, and participant non-compliance. This chapter reviews the literature on label noise in inertial-sensor datasets and presents an empirical analysis on a corpus of 40 hours of wrist IMU recordings from 60 subjects annotated via diary and button-press protocols. Three synthetic noise injection schemes (symmetric, asymmetric class-pair, and transition-boundary noise) are applied at rates from 5% to 30%, and their effect on a depthwise-separable CNN is measured. Transition-boundary noise at 20% degrades macro-F1 by 7.3 points while symmetric noise at the same rate degrades it by only 3.1 points, indicating that model performance is more sensitive to noise concentrated near activity boundaries. Loss-correction and sample-reweighting approaches are evaluated as practical remedies.

title: Composing Information-Flow Policies from Multiple Tenants in a Shared Microservice Platform
abstract: When a shared platform operator hosts workloads from multiple independent tenants, information-flow policies defined by different tenants may conflict or compose unsoundly. This paper studies the problem of policy composition in that setting. A composition algebra is defined over a lattice-indexed policy language; the algebra specifies meet and join operators for combining policies at shared service boundaries. An automated checker, implemented in approximately 3,000 lines of OCaml, verifies that a composed policy satisfies joint non-interference for all tenant pairs. The checker is evaluated on 30 synthetic multi-tenant scenarios ranging from 5 to 120 services and 2 to 8 tenants. Verification completes in under 4 seconds for all scenarios with up to 6 tenants and under 40 seconds for 8-tenant scenarios with 80 services. The paper also identifies three classes of policy conflict that arise frequently in practice and proposes canonical resolution strategies.

title: Structured Priors for Multilingual Joint Topic Modelling Across Serbian and Romanian Web Corpora
abstract: Joint topic models trained on parallel or comparable multilingual corpora can share statistical strength across languages, but require a principled way to couple language-specific Dirichlet processes. This paper proposes a cross-lingual HDP that uses bilingual word embeddings to construct an informative prior linking Serbian and Romanian vocabulary items whose embeddings are within a fixed cosine-distance threshold. The model is estimated via a blocked Gibbs sampler on a comparable corpus of 320,000 news documents (160,000 per language) spanning 2010–2017, drawn from fifteen Serbian and twelve Romanian online outlets. Cross-lingual topic alignment is measured using a translation-based coherence score; the proposed model improves alignment by 18 % over a baseline that treats the two languages independently. A qualitative analysis of three recovered topic clusters—regional politics, agriculture, and flooding events—illustrates how shared topics capture genuinely comparable discourse across the two languages.

title: A lemmatizer for Serbian that handles both scripts
abstract: This paper presents a rule-based and machine-learning hybrid lemmatizer designed specifically for Serbian, a morphologically rich language written in two scripts — Cyrillic and Latin. A major challenge in Serbian natural language processing is that the same lexeme may appear in either script within a single corpus, leading to fragmented frequency counts and unreliable concordances. The proposed system handles both scripts transparently by applying a unified internal representation before lemmatization, then restoring the original script in the output. The lemmatizer was trained on data drawn from the KORPUS-NS reference corpus and evaluated against a manually annotated gold standard of 120,000 tokens. Results show a lemmatization accuracy of 94.7% across both scripts, outperforming existing monoscript baselines by 6.2 percentage points. The paper discusses error analysis, focusing on ambiguous noun–adjective forms and irregular verbal paradigms, and outlines future integration with part-of-speech tagging pipelines. All models and evaluation datasets are released under an open licence.

title: Inflection and search: why Serbian queries miss relevant documents
abstract: Users of Serbian-language search engines and document retrieval systems frequently fail to retrieve relevant documents because queries and indexed texts contain different inflected forms of the same lexeme. This paper investigates the scope of this problem through a systematic corpus study using data from the KORPUS-NS project, quantifying the proportion of query–document mismatches attributable to inflectional variation. Serbian nouns, adjectives and verbs exhibit up to seventeen distinct surface forms per lexeme, and the study demonstrates that naive string matching misses between 31% and 58% of relevant documents depending on the domain. The paper evaluates three mitigation strategies — stemming, full lemmatization, and paradigm-based query expansion — comparing their precision and recall on a purpose-built retrieval test collection of 4,800 queries. Full lemmatization combined with paradigm-aware indexing yields the highest F1 score. The authors argue that language-aware indexing should be considered a standard requirement for Serbian-language information retrieval systems and provide open-source reference implementations of the tested approaches.

title: Designing KORPUS-NS: corpus architecture and annotation scheme for contemporary Serbian
abstract: This paper describes the design decisions underlying KORPUS-NS, a 500-million-token reference corpus of contemporary Serbian covering written and transcribed spoken language from 2000 to the present. We discuss the selection of text domains — journalism, fiction, academic prose, legal documents, social media and broadcast transcripts — and justify the proportional representation of each. The annotation scheme covers tokenisation, sentence segmentation, lemmatisation, part-of-speech tagging and morphosyntactic description using a tagset derived from the MULTEXT-East standard and extended to capture Serbian-specific categories such as verbal aspect and clitic position. Special attention is given to the treatment of orthographic variants, including the coexistence of Cyrillic and Latin scripts, Ekavian and Ijekavian dialect norms, and borrowing-related spelling inconsistencies. The paper also details the metadata schema used to encode source, domain, date and register for each document. A preliminary version of the corpus containing 120 million tokens is available through a web concordancer for academic users.

title: Spelling variants in Serbian corpora: typology, frequency and normalization strategies
abstract: Serbian written language exhibits a wide range of spelling variants arising from script duality, competing orthographic norms, dialect influence and unconstrained digital writing practices. This paper presents the first large-scale typological study of spelling variation in Serbian, drawing on a 200-million-token sample from the KORPUS-NS corpus. We identify six major variant classes: script-switching (ćao/chao), norm-competing variants (vjerovatno/verovatno), foreign-word adaptation variants (menadžer/manager), phonetic spelling (dođi/dodji), cliticisation variants and typographic variants. Frequency analysis reveals that script-switching and norm-competing variants account for over 70% of all variant pairs and that their distribution differs markedly across domains, with social media showing the highest variant density. We evaluate three normalization strategies — lookup-table replacement, phonological rule application and neural sequence-to-sequence mapping — on a held-out test set of 15,000 variant instances. The lookup-table approach achieves the highest precision while the neural model generalises better to unseen foreign borrowings. Practical implications for corpus building, lexicography and search are discussed.

title: A morphological lexicon for Serbian derived from corpus evidence
abstract: Morphological lexicons are foundational resources for natural language processing of inflectionally complex languages. Existing Serbian lexicons were largely constructed by hand and cover limited vocabulary, particularly in the domains of new borrowings and internet slang. This paper describes a semi-automatic method for building a broad-coverage morphological lexicon from the KORPUS-NS corpus using paradigm induction: candidate lemmas are identified through lemmatisation, and their full inflectional paradigms are hypothesised by a rule engine and then validated against corpus evidence. The resulting lexicon contains 187,000 lemmas with full or partial paradigm coverage across nouns, adjectives, verbs, numerals and pronouns. We evaluate quality through human expert judgement on a stratified sample of 2,000 entries, finding 91.3% paradigm correctness for common vocabulary and 78.6% for borrowings. The lexicon is integrated into the KORPUS-NS toolchain and released under a Creative Commons licence. We discuss how corpus-driven derivation captures productive neologisms that manual lexicography consistently misses.

title: Morphological complexity and readability in Serbian administrative texts: a corpus study
abstract: Administrative language is frequently criticised for being inaccessible to general readers, but quantitative evidence for Serbian is scarce. This paper uses a 12-million-token subcorpus of administrative texts from KORPUS-NS to examine the relationship between morphological complexity and readability. We operationalise morphological complexity through three measures: mean paradigm depth (the average number of inflectional categories per word form), type-to-token ratio computed at lemma level, and the proportion of analytically ambiguous forms — word forms that are compatible with more than one morphosyntactic reading. Readability is approximated using human judgement scores collected from 200 participants with varying educational backgrounds. Regression analysis shows that paradigm depth is the strongest predictor of perceived difficulty, explaining 34% of variance, while lexical TTR adds a further 12%. Comparison with journalistic and literary subcorpora reveals that administrative texts have significantly higher ambiguity ratios. The paper proposes a morphology-sensitive readability index for Serbian and discusses applications in plain-language reform and automated text simplification.

title: Cross-script tokenisation challenges in Serbian social media corpora
abstract: Collecting and processing Serbian social media text presents tokenisation challenges that do not arise in standard corpus work: users freely mix Cyrillic and Latin scripts within a single sentence, use non-standard punctuation, employ emoji as discourse markers, and produce unconventional compounds through agglutinative typing conventions absent from the standard language. This paper reports on the construction of a 10-million-token Serbian social media subcorpus incorporated into KORPUS-NS and the tokenisation pipeline developed to handle it. We introduce a cross-script tokeniser that identifies script boundaries within tokens and normalises them before downstream processing, a hashtag and mention segmenter, and a rule set for emoji handling. Intrinsic evaluation on a manually tokenised gold standard of 50,000 tokens shows a token boundary F1 of 98.1%, compared to 91.4% for an off-the-shelf tokeniser not adapted for social media. Extrinsic evaluation through part-of-speech tagging accuracy shows a 3.8-point improvement when the social media tokeniser is used upstream. The tools are released openly.

title: Inflectional paradigms of Serbian verbs: gaps, defectiveness and corpus evidence
abstract: Serbian verbal morphology is characterised by a complex interaction of conjugation class, aspect, transitivity and reflexivity that generates paradigms of up to forty distinct synthetic forms per lemma. Theoretical grammars acknowledge paradigm gaps — cells in the paradigm that lack an attested form — but systematic empirical data on their distribution is lacking. This paper uses corpus evidence from KORPUS-NS to map gap distributions across 8,200 verbal lemmas, distinguishing absolute gaps (no attestation in 500 million tokens) from near-gaps (fewer than five attestations). We find that first and second person forms of weather verbs and cognition verbs show the highest gap rates, consistent with semantic defectiveness, while motion verbs and communication verbs exhibit near-complete paradigms. The paper also examines inter-speaker variation in defective paradigms, using regional subcorpus splits to test whether gaps are uniform across dialect regions. Findings have implications for the completeness requirements of morphological lexicons and for training data coverage in NLP applications.

title: Using KORPUS-NS for automated spelling error detection in educational contexts
abstract: Automated spelling feedback tools for Serbian are hindered by the language's morphological richness: a correctly inflected form that is unusual in frequency may be flagged as an error, while a plausible but morphologically impossible form may pass undetected. This paper proposes a corpus-informed spelling checker that combines a statistical language model trained on KORPUS-NS with the morphological lexicon derived from the same corpus, enabling the system to distinguish unlikely-but-correct forms from genuinely erroneous ones. We evaluate the system on a corpus of 4,500 student essays from secondary schools in Vojvodina, annotated by trained linguists for spelling errors. The proposed system achieves a precision of 88.4% and recall of 83.7% on real-word errors, substantially outperforming both a commercial Serbian spell-checker and a frequency-only baseline. Error analysis highlights persistent difficulties with homograph resolution and Ekavian–Ijekavian alternations. The paper discusses deployment considerations for integration into learning management systems used at Serbian secondary schools.

title: Uticaj brzine acidifikacije na reološka svojstva jogurt gelova dobijenih primenom različitih starter kultura
abstract: U radu je ispitivan uticaj brzine acidifikacije na formiranje gelova u jogurtu primenom četiri komercijalne starter kulture različitih tehnoloških karakteristika. Acidifikacija je praćena kontinualnim merenjem pH u intervalu od 15 minuta tokom 8 sati inkubacije na 43 °C. Reološka svojstva gelova određivana su oscilatornom reologijom pri malim amplitudama deformacije; mereni su moduli G' i G'' kao i tačka geliranja. Rezultati pokazuju da kulture sa sporijim tempom acidifikacije (ΔpH/h < 0,18) obrazuju gelove veće vrednosti G' (do 285 Pa na pH 4,6) u poređenju sa brzorastućim kulturama (G' < 160 Pa). Teksturnom profilnom analizom utvrđena je pozitivna korelacija između modula elastičnosti i kohezivnosti gela (r = 0,81). Elektronska mikroskopija pokazala je gušću, finiju mrežu proteina kod sporijih kultura. Rezultati ukazuju da je brzina zakiseljavanja ključna procesna varijabla za postizanje željene teksture jogurta.

title: Kombinovana primena EPS-produkujućih sojeva Streptococcus thermophilus i Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus u proizvodnji jogurta smanjenog sadržaja mlečne masti
abstract: Cilj rada bio je ispitati mogućnost supstitucije mlečne masti teksturnim dejstvom egzopolisaharida u jogurtu sa 0,5% m.m. Korišćene su tri kombinacije starter kultura: (K1) komercijalna kultura bez EPS produkcije, (K2) EPS-produkujući Streptococcus thermophilus ST-12 + Lactobacillus bulgaricus LB-07, i (K3) kombinacija ST-12 + LB-07 sa dodatnim sojem Lactobacillus acidophilus LA-5. Jogurtovi su fermentisani na 42 °C do pH 4,6, a zatim čuvani 21 dan na 4 °C. Praćeni su: pH, titraciona kiselost, sinereза (% izdvojene surutke), teksturna profilna analiza i senzorska ocena. Kombinacija K2 pokazala je najmanji stepen sinereze (8,3 ± 0,4%) u poređenju sa K1 (17,1 ± 0,9%) i K3 (11,2 ± 0,6%) na kraju perioda čuvanja. Čvrstoća gela K2 jogurta bila je uporediva sa punomasnim uzorkom referentne kulture. Senzorska analiza sa panelom od 12 ocenjivača pokazala je statistički značajno bolju ocenu konzistencije za K2 grupu (p < 0,05). Rezultati potvrđuju da odabrana kombinacija starter kultura može kompenzovati teksturni deficit niskomasnih mlečnih gelova.

title: Mapping the gel network microstructure of fermented milk gels by confocal laser scanning microscopy: effect of inoculation temperature on casein strand thickness
abstract: Fermented skim milk gels were prepared at three inoculation temperatures (38, 42, and 45 °C) using a single EPS-negative starter culture to isolate the effect of temperature on network architecture independent of EPS contributions. Samples were stained with Fast Green FCF for protein and Nile Blue for residual fat and imaged by confocal laser scanning microscopy at 63× magnification. Image analysis was performed with ImageJ; casein strand thickness and pore size distribution were quantified by skeletonisation and Euclidean distance mapping on at least 25 fields per treatment. Gels formed at 38 °C showed thicker strands (mean 1.84 ± 0.21 µm) and larger pores (mean equivalent diameter 4.1 ± 0.6 µm) compared to 45 °C gels (strand thickness 1.12 ± 0.14 µm; pore diameter 2.3 ± 0.3 µm). Oscillatory rheology measurements showed an inverse relationship between pore size and storage modulus G' (R² = 0.91). These structural differences are consistent with the greater degree of whey protein denaturation at higher temperatures accelerating network formation before extensive strand rearrangement can occur.

title: Rheological fingerprinting of set-type yoghurts during cold storage: distinguishing contributions of EPS and protein network stiffening
abstract: The rheological evolution of set-type yoghurt gels during 28 days of cold storage at 4 °C was characterised for five formulations differing in EPS production capacity of their starter cultures (confirmed by EPS yield measurements ranging from 0 to 162 mg/L). Frequency sweeps (0.1–10 Hz) and strain sweeps (0.01–100%) were performed on days 1, 7, 14, and 28. Linear viscoelastic region (LVR) limits, the loss tangent tan δ, and the crossover frequency were used as comparative metrics. In EPS-producing formulations, tan δ remained below 0.18 throughout storage, indicating predominantly elastic behaviour, while the non-EPS control showed tan δ rising from 0.22 to 0.31 by day 28, indicative of progressive structural weakening. Storage modulus G' increased by 12–34% across all samples from day 1 to 28, attributed to ongoing casein rearrangement. Principal component analysis of the full frequency-sweep dataset separated samples by EPS status on PC1 (48.3% variance) and by storage time on PC2 (27.1% variance). The approach provides a reproducible protocol for distinguishing EPS-mediated texture stabilisation from age-related protein stiffening.

title: Effect of partial substitution of bovine milk with oat drink on acidification kinetics, EPS incorporation, and gel texture in stirred fermented products
abstract: Plant-based milk alternatives are increasingly blended with bovine milk to reduce animal-sourced content while retaining fermented-product functionality. This study examined binary blends of pasteurised bovine milk and commercially available oat drink (0, 20, 40, and 60% oat v/v) fermented with an EPS-producing Streptococcus thermophilus strain (EPS yield in bovine milk: 134 mg/L). Acidification curves were recorded at 42 °C; gel properties were assessed after stirring and cooling to 10 °C. Time to reach pH 4.6 increased from 285 min at 0% oat to 418 min at 60% oat, attributed to buffering by oat β-glucan. Apparent viscosity at 50 s⁻¹ decreased from 420 mPa·s (0% oat) to 118 mPa·s (60% oat), partially mitigated by EPS; a non-EPS control at 60% oat reached only 61 mPa·s. Water-holding capacity dropped from 84% to 63% across the blend range. Confocal images showed increasingly discontinuous protein matrices at oat fractions above 40%. The 20% oat blend retained texture parameters within ±15% of the all-bovine reference, suggesting a technically feasible substitution level for this starter culture.

title: Modelovanje kinetike acidifikacije u fermentisanim mlečnim gelovima modifikovanim dodatkom inulina primenom Logističkog i Gompertz modela
abstract: Inulin kao prebiotička komponenta menja puferski kapacitet mlečne smeše i potencijalno utiče na dinamiku rasta starter kultura. U ovom radu ispitivane su smeše obranog mleka sa 0, 1, 2 i 4% (m/v) inulina kratkih lanaca (Orafti® GR analog) fermentisane dvema starter kulturama različitih EPS karakteristika. Krive acidifikacije fitovane su Logističkim i Gompertz modelima; poređeni su parametri: maksimalna brzina acidifikacije (Vmax), vreme do tačke infleksije (ti) i asimptotski pH. Gompertz model pokazao je bolje prilaganje podacima (srednja apsolutna greška 0,021 pH jedinice prema 0,034 za logistički model). Dodavanje 4% inulina povećalo je ti za 19–26% u zavisnosti od kulture. Reološka merenja na kraju fermentacije pokazala su smanjenje G' za 31% pri 4% inulina uz EPS-negativnu kulturu, ali svega 11% uz EPS-produkujuću kulturu, što ukazuje na kompenzatorno dejstvo EPS-a. Predloženi modelski parametri mogu se koristiti za predviđanje trajanja procesa pri formulacionim promenama.

title: Benchmarking Raster Image Processors Under Variable Colour Space Transformations: A Comparative Study
abstract: This study evaluates the rendering performance and colour fidelity of four commercially available raster image processors (RIPs) when processing PDF jobs containing embedded source profiles that differ from the output intent. A structured test suite of 240 pages with mixed RGB, CMYK, and LAB colour spaces was prepared and sent through each RIP under identical hardware conditions. Spectrophotometric measurements using a hand-held spectrodensitometer were taken on 1,200 colour patches per output run. Delta-E2000 deviations were recorded and compared against ISO 12647-2 tolerances. Results showed that two of the four RIPs produced systematic hue errors exceeding 3.0 ΔE2000 in saturated red regions when source and destination profiles were both embedded but conflicting. A correction procedure based on pre-processing source profile normalisation reduced the mean error to below 1.4 ΔE2000 across all test targets. The findings suggest that pre-flight profile conflict detection should be mandatory in high-volume digital print workflows before RIP submission.

title: Pre-flight Rule Sets for Variable-Data PDF/VT Jobs: Design and Validation
abstract: Variable-data printing jobs encoded in PDF/VT introduce structural complexity that conventional pre-flight tools developed for static PDF are not equipped to handle reliably. This paper describes the design of an extended pre-flight rule set targeting PDF/VT-specific constructs, including DPart metadata hierarchies, reusable content streams, and record-boundary font embedding. A rule set of 34 individual checks was implemented as a plug-in for an open-source pre-flight engine and tested against a corpus of 510 variable-data job files sourced from three commercial print service providers in Serbia and Hungary. The validation campaign measured false-positive rates, missed-error rates, and processing time per file. The implemented rule set achieved a missed-error rate of 2.1% and a false-positive rate of 4.7%, compared with 18.3% and 9.2% respectively for the baseline generic PDF/X checks applied to the same corpus. Processing overhead relative to standard pre-flight was 38% on average. The rule set and test corpus are made available for independent replication.

title: Spectral Characterisation of Electrophotographic Toner Sets on Coated and Uncoated Substrates
abstract: The spectral behaviour of four electrophotographic toner sets from different manufacturers was measured on six substrate types ranging from 90 g/m² uncoated woodfree to 170 g/m² silk-coated paper. Measurements were performed with a 45/0 geometry spectrophotometer at 10 nm intervals across the 380–730 nm range. A total of 3,840 spectral curves were collected and used to build substrate-conditional ICC output profiles using a matrix-based and a lookup-table-based modelling approach. Profile accuracy was assessed using 928-patch IT8.7/4 targets. The LUT-based profiles outperformed the matrix approach for all toner-substrate combinations, with mean ΔE2000 values of 1.02 versus 2.34. Fluorescent whitening agent interference was measurable on three of the six substrates and caused systematic errors below 400 nm that propagated into skin tone and neutral grey reproduction. A practical workflow recommendation for FWA compensation in profile construction is provided.

title: Automated Job Ticket Validation in a JDF-Based Print Management Environment
abstract: Job Definition Format (JDF) tickets are the standard mechanism for communicating job parameters between management information systems and production devices in digital printing. Errors in JDF tickets—such as inconsistent media definitions, out-of-range ink coverage limits, or missing finishing specifications—cause costly production interruptions. This chapter reviews validation strategies for JDF tickets in heterogeneous print environments, covering schema validation, semantic consistency checks, and device-capability matching. A decision-tree model for automated ticket correction is presented based on a study of 2,100 production jobs at two mid-sized print service providers. The model achieved autonomous correction of 61% of detected ticket errors without operator intervention, reducing job-start failures by 44% over a four-month observation period. The chapter also discusses integration architectures linking MIS ticket generation modules with RIP front-ends through a mediation layer.

title: Influence of PDF Transparency Flattening Strategies on Colour Accuracy in Composite CMYK Output
abstract: Transparency flattening is required when PDF jobs containing live transparency are sent to PostScript-based output pipelines or older RIP versions that do not natively process PDF 1.4 and later transparency models. Different flattening algorithms produce visually and colorimetrically distinct results, particularly in regions where transparent objects overlap process colour elements. This study compares five flattening presets available in a widely used page layout application, measuring output on two electrophotographic devices. Measurements of 480 composite test regions showed that aggressive rasterisation flattening introduced ΔE2000 differences of up to 6.1 relative to native transparency rendering on a reference RIP, concentrated in overprint-simulation areas. A moderate vector-preserving preset reduced the maximum difference to 2.4 ΔE2000 with no statistically significant increase in RIP processing time. Practical guidance is provided for selecting flattening parameters based on job content type and target device capability.

title: Automated Detection of Image Resolution Violations in High-Volume Variable-Data Jobs
abstract: Variable-data print jobs may contain tens of thousands of individually placed images whose effective resolution depends on placement scale and output DPI. Manual inspection is infeasible at production volumes. This paper presents an automated resolution-checking module that traverses PDF/VT DPart structures, extracts all image XObjects including those embedded in reusable content streams, computes effective output resolution considering transformation matrices and target device DPI, and flags images below a configurable threshold. The module was implemented in Python using a PDF parsing library and evaluated on 180 production-scale PDF/VT files containing between 500 and 28,000 records each. Processing time scaled at approximately 0.4 seconds per thousand records on a mid-range workstation. The module correctly flagged 99.3% of known low-resolution images and produced no false positives on a 50-file clean validation set. Integration into a pre-flight pipeline reduced human inspection time by an estimated 94% for the tested job types.

title: Statistical Process Control Applied to Digital Press Colour Output: Control Chart Selection and Sampling Strategies
abstract: Statistical process control methods developed for offset and flexographic printing have been transposed to digital press monitoring with varying success. This paper examines the applicability of Shewhart X-bar, CUSUM, and EWMA control charts to ΔE2000 data collected from a cut-sheet toner press operating in a commercial environment over 22 production weeks. Reference measurements were taken from a control strip printed at the start and end of each job, yielding 3,410 data points per colour channel. Chart sensitivity, false alarm rate, and time-to-detection for gradual tone drift were compared across chart types. EWMA charts with a smoothing constant of 0.2 detected the onset of a gradual cyan drift 4.3 hours earlier than Shewhart charts, with an equal false alarm rate of 2.1%. Sampling frequency requirements for early drift detection without excessive media waste are quantified and tabulated as a function of job length and drift rate.

title: Impact of Variable Font Subsetting Strategies on PDF File Size and RIP Processing Time in Large-Scale Personalised Document Production
abstract: Personalised document production may require embedding font subsets that vary record-by-record when character sets differ across recipients, increasing PDF/VT file sizes and RIP load. This paper systematically compares four font subsetting strategies—full font embedding, per-file global subsetting, per-DPart-node subsetting, and character-sharing across nodes—in terms of file size, RIP processing time, and text rendering fidelity. Test jobs of 5,000 and 25,000 personalised records were generated using a variable-data composition system with a corpus of Serbian and Latin-extended characters. Full embedding increased file size by a factor of 3.1 over per-node subsetting for the mixed-character-set corpus. Character-sharing across DPart nodes reduced RIP time by 19% relative to per-node subsetting at the 25,000-record scale, with no observed text rendering errors on two of three tested RIP platforms. Edge-case rendering failures on the third platform are documented and attributed to a font cache indexing defect.

title: Colour Gamut Mapping Strategies for Reproducing Memory Colours in Personalised Photo Print Products
abstract: Personalised photo print products—calendars, photo books, and greeting cards produced via variable-data workflows—are particularly sensitive to memory colour reproduction because customers compare output directly against familiar objects. This study evaluates five gamut mapping algorithms for reproducing skin tones, sky blue, and foliage green on three inkjet photo printers with different gamut volumes. Each algorithm was assessed using a psychophysical paired-comparison experiment with 42 participants recruited from the university community, alongside instrumental ΔE2000 measurements. Participants' preference rankings diverged significantly from ΔE2000 rankings for sky blue reproduction, where a chroma-preserving mapping was preferred despite a higher ΔE2000 score. For skin tones, lightness-preserving compression was preferred and correlated well with ΔE2000. The results are used to recommend algorithm selection per memory colour category for photo product workflows and to critique the adequacy of ΔE2000 as a sole quality metric.

title: Integration of Inline Spectrophotometric Sensors in a Digital Press Fleet: Data Synchronisation and Closed-Loop Control Architecture
abstract: Inline spectrophotometric sensors fitted to digital presses generate dense colorimetric data streams during production runs, but integrating measurements from sensors of different makes and firmware versions across a printer fleet into a unified quality management system is non-trivial. This paper documents the integration of inline sensors from two hardware suppliers installed on four devices into a common data collection middleware. Synchronisation issues arising from differing measurement trigger modes, spectral sampling intervals, and proprietary data formats are described along with the resolution strategies applied. A closed-loop tone correction algorithm driven by the unified data stream was implemented and tested over 14 production weeks. The algorithm reduced the proportion of sheets with neutral ΔE2000 exceeding 2.0 from 8.4% to 2.9% across all four devices. Latency between sensor measurement and correction application averaged 340 ms, which was sufficient for sheet-by-sheet correction at the tested press speeds.

title: Structured Audit Methodology for Variable-Data Workflow Compliance with PDF/VT-3 and ISO 16612-2
abstract: ISO 16612-2 and the associated PDF/VT-3 specification impose requirements on job structure, metadata, colour management, and font handling that are only partially covered by existing conformance checkers. This paper proposes a structured audit methodology comprising a four-layer compliance check: file-level syntax and schema validation, DPart metadata consistency verification, colorimetric conformance of embedded profiles against the declared output intent, and output fidelity sampling via test rendering. The methodology was applied to 94 variable-data jobs submitted to a print service provider over a three-month period. Of these, 61% contained at least one non-conformance. The most frequent issues were missing output intent objects (34% of jobs), DPart node metadata gaps (28%), and embedded profiles inconsistent with declared printing conditions (19%). A triage priority scheme is recommended based on the impact of each non-conformance class on output quality and downstream archiving.

title: Crease-stiffness prediction for recycled cartonboard across a humidity range using near-infrared spectroscopy of incoming reels
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectra were collected from reel samples of recycled grey cartonboard at the rewinder station of a carton-converting plant before conditioning. A partial least squares (PLS) regression model was trained using 210 reel samples with crease stiffness at 50 % and 75 % RH as response variables. Spectral pretreatment used standard normal variate correction and first-derivative transformation. The PLS model for crease stiffness at 75 % RH achieved a cross-validated RMSECV of 0.31 mN·m and an R² of 0.86 on a hold-out test set of 52 samples, enabling prediction before converting. Feature wavelengths identified as most informative (around 1450 and 1940 nm) correspond to OH-stretch overtones associated with fibre bonding and moisture accessibility. The approach was tested in a simulated inline scenario with a 2-second scan time, achieving prediction accuracy within ±7 % for 88 % of samples. The study offers a practical path to real-time sorting of incoming reels by their humidity-conditioned crease behaviour without destructive testing.

title: Contact angle hysteresis on corona-treated polyethylene terephthalate films: effect of storage time and humidity
abstract: The ageing of corona-treated polyethylene terephthalate (PET) films was studied by tracking static contact angle, advancing and receding contact angles, and resulting hysteresis over a 21-day storage period at three relative humidity levels (30 %, 55 % and 75 % RH). Sessile-drop measurements were performed with water, diiodomethane and formamide using an optical goniometer with automatic image analysis. Total surface free energy was decomposed into dispersive and polar components using the OWRK model. At 55 % RH, the polar component decreased from 11.4 mN/m immediately after treatment to 6.8 mN/m after 7 days, stabilising near 5.9 mN/m by day 14. Higher humidity delayed but did not prevent surface reorientation. XPS spectra confirmed a reduction in oxygen-containing functional groups concurrent with the contact angle recovery. The findings are directly relevant to scheduling corona treatment in roll-to-roll flexographic printing lines where treated film is stored before printing.

title: Portable spectroscopic reader for field verification of diffractive security labels: hardware design and classification algorithm
abstract: This paper describes the hardware design and classification algorithm of a portable fibre-optic spectroscopic reader intended for field verification of diffractive security labels. The reader uses a 5 mW 532 nm laser, two fibre-coupled spectrometers accepting light at 0° and 22.5° from specular, and a Bluetooth link to a smartphone application. Calibration uses a NIST-traceable barium sulphate tile. A support-vector-machine classifier was trained on spectral signatures from 480 genuine labels across eight product categories and 120 replicated fakes; 10-fold cross-validation yielded sensitivity 97.3 % and specificity 98.1 %. Field trials at three logistics checkpoints over 60 days processed 2 140 labels; the device flagged 14 suspected fakes, of which 11 were confirmed by laboratory analysis and 3 were false positives caused by label surface soiling. Reader weight is 210 g and battery life 6 hours continuous. Hardware schematics and the classifier training dataset are released under an open licence.

title: Living without the other: A phenomenological study of spousal bereavement in Serbian women aged 65 and above
abstract: This study examined subjective experiences of widowhood among 18 Serbian women aged 65–84, recruited through community health centres in Novi Sad and Sombor. Semi-structured interviews lasting 60–90 minutes were conducted at two time points, six months apart. Interpretative phenomenological analysis revealed four superordinate themes: disruption of daily temporal structure, renegotiation of social identity, somatic expressions of grief, and selective remembrance as a coping mechanism. Participants who reported stronger ties to Orthodox religious practice described bereavement rituals as providing temporal anchoring, whereas those with weaker religious affiliation reported more prolonged disorientation. Findings highlight the need to integrate cultural and religious context when interpreting grief symptom severity in this population. Implications for adaptation of grief screening instruments to Serbian older adult samples are discussed.

title: Screening for prolonged grief disorder in primary care settings in Vojvodina: Psychometric evaluation of a Serbian adaptation of the Grief Severity Inventory
abstract: The study adapted and validated a 20-item self-report instrument for prolonged grief disorder screening in a Serbian-speaking older adult population. A convenience sample of 312 participants aged 60–89 (mean age 71.4, SD 6.8) who had experienced a close bereavement within the preceding two years was recruited from 11 general practice surgeries across Vojvodina. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a two-factor structure comprising yearning and functional impairment. Internal consistency was adequate (α = 0.83 for total scale). Convergent validity was established against an established depression measure (r = 0.54) and a measure of social support (r = −0.41). A cut-off score of 32 yielded sensitivity of 0.79 and specificity of 0.74 against a structured clinical interview as criterion standard. Normative data are provided by age group, sex, and type of loss.

title: Gender differences in grief expression and help-seeking following spousal loss in urban and rural Serbian samples
abstract: This mixed-methods study compared grief expression and help-seeking behaviour in 204 bereaved individuals (112 women, 92 men) aged 60–80 from urban Novi Sad and rural municipalities of Bačka Topola and Bečej. Quantitative data were collected using validated measures of grief severity, emotional expressivity, and attitudes toward professional help-seeking. Fifteen purposively selected participants also took part in individual interviews. Men in rural settings reported significantly lower emotional expressivity scores (M = 2.1, SD = 0.6) compared with urban men (M = 2.8, SD = 0.7) and both female groups (rural M = 3.4, SD = 0.8; urban M = 3.5, SD = 0.9). Qualitative data elaborated how norms of masculine stoicism intersected with rural isolation to deter help-seeking. Grief severity did not differ significantly by gender after controlling for social support, suggesting that observed expressivity differences do not reflect lower suffering.

title: Posttraumatic growth and grief coexistence in bereaved older adults: A mixed-methods longitudinal investigation
abstract: This study investigated whether posttraumatic growth and prolonged grief symptomatology can coexist over time in a sample of 88 bereaved older adults (aged 62–79, mean age 69.3) followed at six, twelve, and twenty-four months post-loss. Quantitative trajectories were modelled using latent class growth analysis, identifying three trajectory classes: resilient-low grief (37%), moderate-declining grief (45%), and high-persistent grief (18%). Posttraumatic growth scores increased over time in the resilient and moderate groups but remained flat in the high-persistent group. Semi-structured interviews with 20 participants nested within the study clarified that personal meaning reconstruction and continued bond maintenance were perceived as complementary rather than contradictory processes. These findings challenge models that position growth and grief as mutually exclusive outcomes and support a dual-process interpretation.

title: Bereavement support provision in Serbian social care homes: A survey of staff knowledge, attitudes, and practices
abstract: Staff working in residential care homes are frequently the primary witnesses to resident bereavement, yet their preparedness varies widely. This study surveyed 187 care staff across 14 state-registered social care homes in Serbia using a structured questionnaire assessing knowledge of grief processes, attitudes toward open discussion of death, and current support practices. Fewer than 30% of respondents had received any formal training in grief support; 62% reported feeling insufficiently equipped to respond to residents showing signs of prolonged grief. Ordinal logistic regression identified professional role, years of experience, and access to supervision as significant predictors of higher practice quality scores. Qualitative focus groups with 28 staff members across four homes identified institutional time pressure and absence of protocols as primary barriers to practice improvement. Findings were used to inform a brief workforce training outline.

title: Continued bonds with the deceased among Serbian Orthodox older adults: A qualitative study of rituals, objects, and inner dialogue
abstract: Drawing on continued-bonds theory, this study examined how 21 older Serbian adults (aged 67–83) who identified as Serbian Orthodox Christians maintained relationships with deceased spouses in the months and years following bereavement. Data were generated through two rounds of in-depth interviews and a supplementary photograph-elicitation task in which participants brought objects representing their relationship with the deceased. Analysis identified three modes of continued bonding: ritualistic maintenance through church-prescribed memorial practices (parastosi), object-mediated presence through everyday household items, and internalized dialogue experienced during solitary moments. Participants generally perceived these bonds as adaptive and consistent with Orthodox theological understandings of the soul. Grief counsellors working in this cultural context are encouraged to assess continued-bond practices before attempting to reframe them as pathological.

title: Cross-national comparison of prolonged grief prevalence in community-dwelling older adults in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia
abstract: This collaborative cross-national study estimated the prevalence of probable prolonged grief disorder in community-dwelling older adults in three post-Yugoslav successor states. Stratified random samples were drawn from 2021 national population registers or municipal records in Novi Sad (Serbia, n = 341), Zagreb (Croatia, n = 328), and Ljubljana (Slovenia, n = 296). Participants were aged 65 and above and had experienced bereavement within the preceding three years. Using ICD-11 diagnostic criteria operationalised through the Grief Severity Inventory, probable prolonged grief was found in 12.1% of the Serbian sample, 9.4% of the Croatian sample, and 8.7% of the Slovenian sample, with differences between Serbia and Slovenia reaching statistical significance after adjusting for age, sex, and years since loss. Social isolation and absence of ongoing family contact emerged as the strongest cross-national predictors. Methodological challenges of cross-national comparability are discussed.

title: Grief narratives and temporal disorientation: A phenomenological analysis of time experience in prolonged grief disorder
abstract: This study explored how individuals meeting criteria for prolonged grief disorder subjectively experience time in comparison with bereaved individuals who do not meet those criteria. Seventeen participants with probable prolonged grief disorder and 15 bereaved controls, all aged between 60 and 78, took part in single in-depth phenomenological interviews guided by a temporality-focused interview protocol adapted from existential psychology. Phenomenological reduction and thematic analysis identified a pronounced sense of temporal arrest in the prolonged grief group, characterised by the felt impossibility of imagining a meaningful future and a compulsive reliving of the period immediately before and after the death. Control participants described a gradual reintegration of past and future into an ongoing present. The findings are interpreted through a Husserlian framework of inner time-consciousness, with implications for psychological support approaches targeting temporal reorientation.

title: Caregiver grief among adult children providing informal care to a dying parent: Anticipatory and post-death grief in Serbian families
abstract: This mixed-methods study examined anticipatory and post-death grief in 62 adult children (aged 40–65) who had provided informal home care to a parent who died of a chronic illness in the previous 12 months. Quantitative data collected at three months post-death assessed grief severity, caregiver burden retrospectively recalled, and family communication quality. Qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with 18 participants elaborated subjective experiences of the caregiver role, meanings attached to the dying process, and perceived quality of the death. Higher retrospective burden scores were significantly associated with elevated post-death grief severity (β = 0.39, p < 0.01). Participants whose parent had a prolonged period of cognitive decline reported a form of anticipatory mourning that sometimes, but not invariably, attenuated post-death grief intensity. Findings have relevance for palliative care planning and family bereavement support in Serbian healthcare settings.

title: Between memory and obligation: Qualitative investigation of grief and intergenerational transmission of loss in post-Yugoslav families
abstract: This qualitative study examined how unresolved parental grief following significant losses in the 1990s conflicts and post-war period was perceived and experienced by adult children in fifteen Serbian families. Dyadic interviews were conducted with one bereaved older parent (aged 65–80) and one adult child (aged 35–50) in each family, with data analysed using constructivist grounded theory. Emerging theory centred on a process termed obligated witnessing, in which adult children felt a duty to absorb and carry parental grief narratives despite the psychological costs of doing so. Patterns of communication varied from explicit and detailed narrative sharing to silent transmission through behavioural and emotional cues. Findings contribute to literature on secondary traumatisation and intergenerational transmission of grief and have implications for family-level bereavement support interventions.

title: Loneliness as a mediator between bereavement and prolonged grief disorder in adults over 70: Findings from a two-wave panel study in Vojvodina
abstract: This study tested a mediation model in which loneliness at six months post-loss mediates the association between bereavement severity at baseline and prolonged grief disorder probability at eighteen months, using data from a two-wave panel study of 219 bereaved adults aged 70 and above residing in Vojvodina. Baseline data were collected in 2023 and follow-up in 2024. Bereavement severity was rated using a structured clinical interview; loneliness was assessed with an established three-item scale; prolonged grief was operationalised against ICD-11 criteria using the clinician-administered PGIOA. Path analysis supported a partial mediation model: the indirect effect of bereavement severity through loneliness accounted for 38% of the total effect on prolonged grief probability. Social isolation at six months emerged as a stronger predictor than either pre-loss social network size or physical health status. Implications for early identification and intervention are discussed.

title: Sensitivity of deep-knowledge-tracing variants to hyperparameter choices: a systematic benchmarking on three open educational datasets
abstract: Deep knowledge tracing (DKT) and two extensions—DKT+ with forgetting regularisation and DKVMN with memory-augmented networks—were systematically benchmarked across three publicly released educational interaction datasets representing algebra tutoring (N ≈ 300,000 events), geometry tutoring (N ≈ 70,000 events), and a reading skills platform (N ≈ 45,000 events). A grid search over 216 hyperparameter combinations per model variant examined hidden-unit counts (32–256), dropout rates (0–0.5), learning-rate schedules, and sequence-length truncation thresholds. AUC for next-item prediction ranged from 0.71 to 0.79 across conditions; variance attributable to hyperparameter choice exceeded variance attributable to model variant for two of three datasets. A comparison with a well-tuned four-state hidden Markov baseline showed that HMM matched DKT AUC within 0.02 on the reading dataset while requiring 40-fold less computation. Recommendations for reproducible DKT evaluation are provided.

title: Morphological Disambiguation in Serbian: A Maximum Entropy Approach on a Balanced News Corpus
abstract: This paper describes the construction and annotation of a 200,000-token Serbian newspaper corpus and the training of a maximum entropy morphological disambiguator on it. Serbian presents particular challenges for disambiguation due to its free word order, extensive inflectional paradigms, and syncretism across several case forms. The corpus was sampled from three regional dailies covering the period 2005–2009 and annotated manually by two linguists following an adapted MULTEXT-East tagset. Inter-annotator agreement reached κ = 0.87 on the full tagset. The maximum entropy model trained on 80% of the data achieved a per-token accuracy of 91.3% on the held-out test set, outperforming a rule-based baseline by 4.1 percentage points. Error analysis showed that the remaining errors cluster heavily around nominal case syncretism in neuter nouns and verbal aspect ambiguity. The annotated corpus and tagger are made available under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Annotation Consistency in Dependency Treebanks: A Case Study on Serbian and Croatian Parallel Texts
abstract: Consistent syntactic annotation across closely related language varieties is essential for cross-lingual experiments, yet disagreements between annotation teams are common even when shared guidelines are nominally in use. This study examines annotation consistency in a 50,000-token parallel Serbian–Croatian dependency treebank constructed as part of a bilateral research effort. Five annotators from two institutions independently labelled a common 5,000-token subset, and discrepancies were systematically catalogued and attributed to guideline ambiguity, language-variety differences, or genuine annotator uncertainty. We propose a set of revision criteria for eleven frequently disputed dependency relation categories and demonstrate that applying them retrospectively raises the macro-averaged labelled attachment score (LAS) agreement from 76.4% to 83.1% across the full annotator set. The revised guidelines and the reconciled treebank subset are released alongside the paper. Findings are relevant to any team maintaining parallel treebanks for closely related South Slavic varieties.

title: Transferring POS Taggers Across the Slavic–Finno-Ugric Boundary: Experiments with Serbian and Hungarian
abstract: This paper investigates how much morphological tagging accuracy can be retained when a tagger trained on Serbian is transferred—without any target-language labelled data—to Hungarian, and vice versa. Despite the typological distance between a South Slavic language and a Finno-Ugric agglutinative language, both exhibit rich morphology, which motivates the comparison. We map the MULTEXT-East tagsets of the two languages onto a reduced shared feature schema covering part of speech, number, and case, then apply three transfer strategies: direct model transfer, feature projection via word alignments, and self-training with a small unlabelled Hungarian/Serbian target corpus. Using Serbian SETimes-derived text and a Hungarian news corpus of comparable size (circa 180,000 tokens each), we find that self-training with 20,000 unlabelled target tokens recovers roughly 60% of the performance gap relative to a fully supervised target-language model. Results suggest shared morphological feature spaces are an effective bridge even across unrelated families.

title: A Spoken Serbian Corpus for Sociolinguistic and Computational Research: Design, Recording, and Transcription Protocol
abstract: This book chapter describes the methodology behind the Spoken Serbian Resource Corpus (SpoSReC), a 120-hour collection of semi-spontaneous speech recorded across four dialect regions of Serbia and Vojvodina between 2013 and 2016. The chapter covers microphone selection, recording environment norms, speaker recruitment targeting balanced age, gender, and education profiles, and the transcription annotation scheme adapted from CHAT with additional tiers for dialect-specific phonological features. Transcription was performed by twelve trained student annotators following two rounds of calibration; a 5% re-annotation sample showed token-level accuracy above 94%. The chapter discusses particular challenges around code-switching with Hungarian in the Vojvodina sub-corpus, which accounts for roughly 18% of recorded hours. Intended uses include sociolinguistic analysis of dialect contact, acoustic modelling, and as a complement to written corpora in multilingual NLP pipelines. The corpus is deposited at the CLARIN.SI repository.

title: Zero-Shot Dependency Parsing of Bosnian Using a Serbian Transition-Based Parser
abstract: Bosnian and Serbian share the majority of their grammar and lexicon, yet separate standardisation efforts mean that available NLP models almost never target Bosnian explicitly. This paper evaluates whether a transition-based dependency parser trained exclusively on a 90,000-token Serbian treebank can parse Bosnian texts without any adaptation. We test on a newly constructed 8,000-token Bosnian web-text gold standard annotated in Universal Dependencies (UD) format. Unlabelled attachment score (UAS) reaches 81.7% and LAS 74.2%, which we compare against two multilingual baselines (mBERT fine-tuned on Serbian UD data, and a delexicalised cross-lingual parser). We also report results for a shallow domain-adaptation step that replaces Bosnian-specific orthographic conventions and select lexical items, which raises LAS by 2.4 points. The work argues for treating Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian as a resource-sharing cluster within UD rather than as fully independent treebank targets.

title: Evaluating Multilingual BERT Representations for Serbian Morphosyntactic Tagging Across Domains
abstract: Contextualised word representations from multilingual pretrained transformers have shown strong performance on many NLP tasks, but their behaviour on morphologically complex languages with limited training data in the pretraining corpus is not well understood. We fine-tune multilingual BERT (mBERT) and XLM-RoBERTa on Serbian morphosyntactic tagging across four domains: news, parliamentary proceedings, social media, and legal text, using gold-standard data sets totalling approximately 130,000 tokens. Results show that mBERT fine-tuned on news data drops from 94.1% accuracy on in-domain test data to 87.6% on social media text, with the largest error categories being unknown tokenisation units and non-standard inflected forms. XLM-RoBERTa is more robust across domains, with a 3.2-point smaller drop on social media. We also test both models on a 15,000-token Pannonian Rusyn test set as an extreme low-resource condition and observe that XLM-RoBERTa achieves 71.3% even without any Rusyn fine-tuning data, apparently through transfer from Serbian and Ukrainian subword overlap.

title: Annotation of Aspect and Actionality in Serbian Verbal Predicates: Guidelines and a Pilot Corpus
abstract: Grammatical aspect in Serbian interacts with lexical actionality (Aktionsart) in ways that create persistent disagreements among annotators and inconsistencies across existing resources. This paper presents a detailed annotation scheme for aspect-actionality combinations in Serbian verbal predicates, developed iteratively over eighteen months through repeated annotation cycles on a pilot corpus of 25,000 tokens drawn from fiction and journalistic prose. The scheme distinguishes five aspectual classes and four primary actionality types, with explicit rules for handling borderline prefixation patterns that shift a verb from imperfective to perfective without clear lexical change. Inter-annotator agreement after guideline stabilisation reached κ = 0.81 for aspect and κ = 0.74 for actionality. We report a frequency distribution of the resulting cross-classifications and show that approximately 12% of verb tokens in our pilot corpus are genuinely ambiguous under context, requiring discourse-level cues for resolution. The annotated pilot corpus and guidelines are released publicly.

title: Cross-Lingual Propagation of Named Entity Annotations from Serbian to Macedonian via Bilingual Lexicons
abstract: Named entity recognition (NER) for Macedonian is severely constrained by the lack of annotated training data. This paper investigates whether named entity labels from a 95,000-token Serbian NER corpus can be projected onto a parallel Macedonian corpus through automatic word alignment combined with bilingual lexicon filtering, producing usable silver-standard training data. We compare three projection strategies and train a BiLSTM-CRF model on the resulting Macedonian silver data, evaluating on a 3,000-token manually annotated Macedonian gold test set. The best projection strategy yields an F1 of 68.4% for the three-class scheme (PER, ORG, LOC), compared to 51.3% for a naive direct-transfer baseline. We further show that adding 2,000 manually corrected tokens to the silver training set pushes F1 to 76.1%, pointing to a cost-effective data-creation strategy. Macedonian gold test data are released through the CLARIN infrastructure.

title: A Morphological Lexicon for Pannonian Rusyn: Construction, Coverage, and Integration into an NLP Pipeline
abstract: Pannonian Rusyn is a regional language spoken by approximately 15,000 people in Vojvodina, Serbia, and parts of Croatia. It has received almost no computational treatment despite holding official minority language status in Serbia. This paper describes the construction of a morphological lexicon for Pannonian Rusyn containing 28,400 lemmas with full inflection tables generated by a hand-crafted finite-state transducer. Lexicon coverage was evaluated against a 40,000-token web-crawled corpus: the lexicon covers 84.6% of tokens and 61.3% of types, with the largest coverage gap in recent borrowings from Serbian and English. We integrate the lexicon into a simple morphological analysis pipeline and report tagging accuracy of 78.9% on a 2,500-token gold standard. Challenges specific to the language include dialectal spelling variation across the Bačka and Srem sub-varieties and the absence of a stable computational orthography standard. The lexicon is deposited at CLARIN ERIC and licensed under CC BY 4.0.

title: Sentence Boundary Detection in Historical Serbian Church-Slavonic Texts: Rule-Based and Statistical Approaches Compared
abstract: Historical digitisation projects increasingly produce raw OCR output from Serbian Church-Slavonic manuscripts, but standard sentence segmentation tools trained on modern text fail on these materials due to inconsistent punctuation, abbreviation conventions, and interlinear glosses. This paper evaluates three segmentation strategies on a 60,000-character corpus of digitised 18th-century ecclesiastical texts: a rule-based approach built on paleographic knowledge, a CRF model trained on 8,000 manually segmented characters, and a fine-tuned multilingual sentence segmenter. The CRF model achieves the best balance of precision (91.2%) and recall (88.7%), while the rule-based system has higher precision (94.1%) but lower recall (81.3%). We also quantify the downstream effect of segmentation errors on a subsequent keyword-in-context (KWIC) retrieval task, finding that even a 5% boundary error rate reduces KWIC precision by roughly 9 percentage points. The annotated subset and CRF model are shared via the project repository.
venue: Digital Humanities and Historical Linguistics Quarterly, Vol. 6, No. 3

title: Benchmarking Low-Resource Multilingual Transformers on Four Vojvodina Minority Languages
abstract: Vojvodina hosts several small language communities—Hungarian, Slovak, Rusyn, and Romanian—each with official status but minimal NLP resources. This paper constructs a unified benchmark covering three tasks (morphosyntactic tagging, named entity recognition, and sentence-level sentiment classification) for all four languages, using data sets of 10,000–18,000 tokens per language assembled from local newspaper archives and social media under appropriate licences. We evaluate five multilingual transformer models (mBERT, XLM-R base, XLM-R large, a Slavic-focused model, and a model pre-trained on Hungarian) under three data regimes: zero-shot, 500-example few-shot, and full fine-tuning. Results confirm that language family proximity to high-resource languages in the pre-training data is a stronger predictor of zero-shot performance than script similarity. Hungarian achieves the highest zero-shot scores benefiting from the Hungarian-focused model; Rusyn consistently scores lowest across all models and tasks. The benchmark data, evaluation scripts, and all fine-tuned model checkpoints are released publicly.

title: Towards a Unified Annotation Scheme for Information Structure in Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian Treebanks
abstract: Information structure—the encoding of topic, focus, and contrast in discourse—is systematically marked in South Slavic languages through word order variation, prosodic prominence, and particle placement, yet no shared annotation scheme currently covers Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian simultaneously. This paper proposes such a scheme, derived from a comparative analysis of 120 ambiguous sentences drawn from parallel news texts in all three varieties. The scheme distinguishes topic span, narrow focus, broad focus, and contrastive topic using a two-tier annotation model compatible with the Universal Dependencies extended relation framework. We report pilot annotation statistics on a 6,000-token shared sample involving annotators from three institutions and discuss the main sources of disagreement, particularly around verum focus and the annotation of cleft-like constructions. A revised annotation manual and the pilot sample are submitted to the UD repository as a discussion document for community feedback.

title: Interjections in Serbian Prose Dialogue 1890–1940: Form, Function, and Editorial Normalisation
abstract: Interjections in Serbian dialogue of the early twentieth century form a heterogeneous class that has received little systematic corpus attention. This paper identifies and classifies 2,340 interjection tokens from the dialogue-annotated SerbProsRef corpus, grouping them into expressive, responsive, and discourse-structuring subtypes. Formal analysis documents considerable orthographic and morphological variation across publishers, with some interjections appearing in up to seven spelling variants across the corpus. Diachronic frequency analysis shows that expressive interjections decline after 1920 relative to corpus size while responsive interjections (confirmations, rejections, hesitations) remain stable, suggesting that later dialogue writing reduced overt emotional signalling in favour of conversational exchange patterns. A comparison of interjection density across genres (popular serial fiction vs. literary short fiction) confirms that popular serial fiction maintains approximately 1.8 times the interjection rate of its literary counterpart throughout the period.

title: Comparative evaluation of planar-target calibration methods for industrial area-scan cameras under varying illumination
abstract: This paper compares four planar-target calibration procedures—checkerboard, circular dot grid, ArUco marker board, and a custom asymmetric ring pattern—applied to three commercially available area-scan cameras with resolutions of 1.3, 5, and 12 megapixels. Calibration datasets were collected under four controlled illumination levels (200, 500, 1000, and 2000 lux) using a motorised goniometric stage to ensure repeatable target poses. Reprojection errors, lens distortion coefficient stability, and principal-point repeatability were measured across 30 independent calibration trials per condition per method. Results show that the asymmetric ring pattern achieves the lowest mean reprojection error (0.18 px at 1000 lux for the 5 MP camera) and the most stable radial distortion coefficients across illumination changes, while checkerboard performance degraded noticeably below 300 lux. The circular dot grid exhibited consistent principal-point drift between trials at all resolutions. Recommendations are provided for target selection based on sensor resolution and working illumination range.

title: Radial distortion correction for wide-angle lenses in robotic bin-picking applications
abstract: Wide-angle lenses mounted on robot-arm end-effectors introduce significant radial and tangential distortion that degrades the accuracy of pose estimation for bin-picking tasks. This study evaluates three distortion correction models—the Brown–Conrady polynomial model with two, four, and six coefficients, and a division model—across two wide-angle lenses with nominal fields of view of 90° and 120°. Calibration was performed using a multi-plane target fixture in 48 distinct poses. Grasp-pose estimation accuracy was subsequently measured on a set of 200 metallic prismatic parts placed randomly in a bin, using a Garbuz RV-6 six-axis robot. With the four-coefficient Brown–Conrady model, mean position error dropped from 3.1 mm (uncorrected) to 0.6 mm for the 90° lens, and from 6.8 mm to 1.2 mm for the 120° lens. The division model offered comparable accuracy with fewer parameters and faster fitting, making it preferable for embedded processing.
