title: Hand-eye calibration accuracy as a function of robot joint noise and calibration pose distribution
abstract: Hand-eye calibration, which determines the rigid transform between a camera mounted on a robot flange and the robot tool-centre point, is sensitive to both the geometric distribution of calibration poses and the repeatability of the robot arm. This paper reports a controlled study using a Serbot MR-5 industrial robot with nominal position repeatability of ±0.03 mm. Calibration was performed using 10, 20, 40, and 80 poses drawn from three sampling strategies: random, uniform spherical, and an optimised D-optimal design. Artificial joint noise at levels of 0.01°, 0.05°, and 0.1° per axis was injected in simulation to augment the physical measurements. Four algebraic and iterative solvers were compared. Results show that the D-optimal pose set reduces rotational calibration error by 31–44% relative to random sampling for the same number of poses, and that the iterative dual-quaternion solver is more robust to joint noise than the linear formulation. Practical guidelines for pose selection in confined workspaces are provided.

title: A self-calibration procedure for line-scan cameras integrated in a conveyor inspection system
abstract: Line-scan cameras are widely used for web and conveyor inspection but require precise knowledge of mounting geometry and lens parameters to enable quantitative measurement. Standard calibration with a planar target is inconvenient when the camera is fixed above a moving belt. This work presents a self-calibration procedure that exploits the motion of a flat, randomly textured belt carrying known-dimension reference tiles. The algorithm estimates focal length, principal-point offset, and two radial distortion coefficients jointly with the belt velocity and camera tilt angle, using a non-linear least-squares formulation initialised by a closed-form estimate. Experiments on a prototype inspection cell running at belt speeds of 0.2–1.5 m/s show that the procedure converges in under 80 iterations and recovers focal length with an error below 0.4% and radial distortion coefficients within 3% of the ground-truth values obtained from a static multi-pose calibration. Width measurements of tile edges achieved a mean absolute error of 0.11 mm over a 400 mm field of view.

title: Structured light system calibration using a single reference plane and a translation stage
abstract: Structured light scanners require accurate knowledge of the projector–camera geometric relationship to recover three-dimensional surface coordinates. This paper proposes a calibration approach that uses a single planar reference surface stepped through eight translation stage positions, eliminating the need to print or manufacture multiple calibration planes. A phase-shifting fringe projection system with four-step phase shifting was used. The homography-based method estimates projector intrinsic and extrinsic parameters together with camera parameters in a joint bundle adjustment. Calibration was validated by measuring ten gauge blocks with nominal thicknesses between 2 and 50 mm. Mean absolute thickness error was 18 µm, and the 95th percentile error was 34 µm over 200 measurements. Comparison with a commercial calibration package showed equivalent accuracy, while the proposed procedure reduced setup time from approximately 45 minutes to 12 minutes in a production-floor trial.

title: Camera calibration for reconfigurable robot cells: managing parameter drift between cell reconfigurations
abstract: In reconfigurable manufacturing cells, cameras are repositioned every time the cell layout changes, requiring a fresh extrinsic calibration. This chapter reviews strategies for managing intrinsic and extrinsic camera parameters across multiple cell configurations. Topics covered include pre-calibrated camera modules with fixed intrinsics, rapid extrinsic re-estimation from three or more known cell features, and the use of permanent embedded reference markers on cell frames. A case study in an automotive component cell at a Vojvodina-based supplier is described, in which three area-scan cameras were reconfigured seven times over a six-month production period. Using a permanent-marker extrinsic update protocol, the mean time to restore operational vision accuracy dropped from 38 minutes to under 7 minutes per camera per reconfiguration. Parameter drift of intrinsic coefficients between configurations was found to be negligible (< 0.2% change in focal length) when cameras were temperature-stabilised before use.

title: Simultaneous estimation of camera pose and lens distortion from planar homographies: a direct algebraic method
abstract: Existing closed-form calibration solvers typically decouple intrinsic estimation from pose recovery, which introduces bias when distortion is large. This paper presents a direct algebraic method that jointly estimates the camera pose and two radial distortion coefficients from a single homography computed from a planar calibration target. The method reformulates the distortion-aware homography constraints as a polynomial eigenvalue problem solved by linearisation, with a subsequent Gauss–Newton refinement step. Synthetic experiments with distortion coefficients spanning −0.3 to +0.1 and target poses from 10° to 60° off-normal show that the direct method reduces mean rotational error by 18% and translational error by 22% compared with decoupled approaches, at the cost of approximately 1.4× longer computation time per pose. Real-data experiments on 120 target images from four camera models confirm the synthetic findings. The method is suited to single-shot calibration scenarios where only one target view is available.

title: Evaluation of thermal effects on industrial camera calibration parameters over an eight-hour production shift
abstract: Temperature variation in production environments is a known but rarely quantified source of drift in camera calibration parameters. This study monitored ambient temperature and camera body temperature at five-minute intervals over eight-hour production shifts on 15 days at a sheet-metal pressing facility. Three camera types—a cooled scientific CCD model, an uncooled CMOS area-scan model, and a GigE line-scan model—were permanently mounted and calibrated at the start of each shift. Calibration was repeated at the end of the shift and at three intermediate intervals. Focal length variation correlated significantly with camera body temperature (Pearson r = 0.81, p < 0.001), with a mean gradient of 0.012 px/°C for the uncooled CMOS model. Principal-point drift was smaller but detectable above 8°C body temperature rise. Recommendations for warm-up protocols and temperature-compensated recalibration triggers are provided, including a simple linear compensation model that reduced end-of-shift reprojection error by 41%.

title: Automated geometric self-calibration of a multi-camera array using scene-point correspondences without a physical target
abstract: Target-free self-calibration of multi-camera arrays avoids the practical difficulties of placing calibration objects in dense robot workcells. This paper describes a pipeline in which a four-camera array observing a static but texturally rich workspace is self-calibrated using feature correspondences extracted by a learned keypoint detector. Fundamental matrix estimation with RANSAC, followed by a factorisation-based structure-from-motion step, produces an initial projective reconstruction that is upgraded to metric using the modulus constraint. A final bundle adjustment refines all intrinsic and extrinsic parameters simultaneously. On a synthetic benchmark with known ground truth, mean angular error in camera orientation was 0.08° and mean baseline error was 0.31 mm over arrays of 4–8 cameras. In a physical four-camera cell, the self-calibrated system achieved a 3-D point reconstruction error of 0.48 mm RMS compared with a laser tracker reference, versus 0.41 mm for a conventional target-based calibration, at roughly comparable setup effort once the scene is sufficiently textured.

title: Marker-embedded cell frames for sub-minute extrinsic re-calibration in reconfigurable assembly cells
abstract: This paper presents the design and validation of a passive marker system embedded permanently into structural aluminium cell frames, intended to support rapid extrinsic camera re-calibration after cell reconfigurations. Fourteen AprilTag-derived fiducial markers with a 50 mm body size are laser-engraved onto frame cross-members at positions determined by an offline optimisation that maximises geometric diversity from any camera viewpoint within the cell volume. Given a camera with known intrinsics, a single image capture is sufficient to recover the extrinsic pose with a mean positional error of 1.3 mm and mean rotational error of 0.21° across 96 tested camera positions in a 2 × 2 × 1.2 m cell. The system was tested in a reconfigurable welding cell operating over 14 reconfiguration episodes; mean recalibration time per camera was 4.2 minutes including software processing, versus 34 minutes for a full target-based procedure.

title: Fisheye camera calibration for overhead workspace monitoring: a comparison of three projection models
abstract: Fisheye cameras mounted overhead can monitor an entire robot workcell from a single viewpoint, but their strong projection nonlinearity requires careful model selection. This paper compares the equidistant, equisolid-angle, and stereographic projection models, each augmented with a residual polynomial correction term, for calibrating two commercial fisheye lenses (183° and 195° field of view) fitted to 5 MP sensors. Calibration data consist of 60 images of a large 800 × 600 mm dot-grid board captured at varied heights and rotations. Model fitting accuracy, reprojection error, and the ability to unproject image points to 3-D rays were assessed. The equisolid-angle model with a four-term residual polynomial achieved the lowest reprojection error (0.23 px mean) across both lenses and transferred best to an independent validation set. An overhead monitoring application demonstrated 3-D worker-hand position estimation with a mean error of 8.6 mm in the horizontal plane at 1.8 m camera height.

title: Calibration uncertainty propagation from camera parameters to robot grasp-pose estimates in a pick-and-place cell
abstract: Manufacturing vision systems are typically validated by reprojection error, but this metric does not directly reflect the downstream impact on robot task accuracy. This paper derives an analytical uncertainty propagation model that maps covariances of camera intrinsic and extrinsic parameters to positional and orientational uncertainty of robot grasp poses estimated from 2-D image measurements. The model is based on first-order error propagation through the full perspective projection chain and the robot inverse kinematics. Numerical experiments show that for a typical 5 MP camera at 800 mm working distance, a 0.5 px standard deviation in principal-point uncertainty contributes approximately 0.4 mm to grasp-position uncertainty, whereas focal-length uncertainty at the same level contributes only 0.08 mm. Physical validation using 300 grasp trials on a Serbot MR-5 robot agreed with model predictions to within 12%. The model is used to derive calibration accuracy targets as a function of required grasp tolerance.

title: Online intrinsic parameter monitoring for vision systems on vibrating machine tools
abstract: Cameras mounted on or near CNC machine tools experience continuous vibration that can mechanically shift lens elements and alter intrinsic parameters between maintenance cycles. This paper proposes an online monitoring scheme in which a small embedded reference pattern, fixed in the camera's field of view on the machine enclosure wall, is imaged once per machining cycle to track focal length and principal-point position without interrupting production. A Kalman filter processes the streaming estimates to separate genuine parameter drift from measurement noise. Tests on a three-axis vertical machining centre running at spindle speeds of 1000–8000 rpm over 30 production days showed that principal-point shifts of more than 1.5 px occurred on four occasions, each correlated with spindle impacts during tool changes. The system triggered recalibration alerts on all four occasions and produced no false positives. Continuous monitoring reduced accumulated measurement error by 63% compared with a fixed weekly recalibration schedule.

title: A dataset and benchmark for evaluating self-calibration algorithms in reconfigurable robot workcells
abstract: Progress in target-free self-calibration is difficult to benchmark because no shared dataset with ground-truth camera parameters exists for the reconfigurable-cell setting. This paper introduces RCBench-1, a dataset comprising 14 workcell configurations, each with 4–6 cameras, totalling 8 400 images with ground-truth intrinsic and extrinsic parameters measured by a laser tracker and a reference calibration procedure. Dataset scenes include a sparse-object configuration, a dense-parts-bin configuration, and a configuration with partial occlusions from safety fencing. Four published self-calibration algorithms are evaluated: a structure-from-motion baseline, a homography-pooling method, a deep feature matching variant, and the authors' own bundle-adjustment-based approach from 2020. Metrics reported are rotation error, translation error, reprojection error, and convergence rate. The dataset is made publicly available under a Creative Commons licence. Results reveal that all tested methods degrade substantially in the partial-occlusion configuration, suggesting this as a priority for future work.

title: Sliding mode observer-based sensorless force estimation for hydraulic injection moulding machines
abstract: Force sensors in injection moulding clamping units are subject to fatigue failure and chemical contamination from mould release agents, motivating sensorless force estimation. This paper implements a super-twisting sliding mode observer that estimates clamping force from hydraulic pressure measurements alone, accounting for seal friction, oil compressibility, and hose compliance as modelled disturbances. A grey-box model of the clamping unit is identified from 2,200 injection cycles across six mould cavity geometries. Observer gains are scheduled with injection phase (fill, pack, hold) to maintain estimation accuracy across a 10:1 variation in pressure rate of change. Estimation error over a 48-hour production run is below 2.1 kN RMS against a reference strain-gauge load cell, meeting the ±3 kN accuracy requirement stated by the machine manufacturer. The approach eliminates the need for external force sensors in three out of four measurement points on a standard 550-tonne machine.

title: Estimating Belt Wear State from Motor Current Signatures to Schedule ILC Filter Updates
abstract: Belt wear in synchronous-drive gantries gradually reduces tooth mesh stiffness and increases backlash, causing slow drift in the system's frequency response. This paper explores whether belt wear state can be estimated from motor phase current signatures collected during normal ILC operation, without additional sensors. Current power spectra from 40 wear-state stages were recorded on a test bench where belt wear was induced by running the drive continuously at rated speed while applying lateral misalignment. A support vector regression model trained on 28 stages and tested on the remaining 12 predicted a wear index (correlated to belt mass loss) with a mean absolute error of 4.1% of the full wear range. The estimated wear index is used to trigger re-identification of the ILC learning filter when the predicted stiffness change exceeds a threshold of 8%. In a 500-trial endurance test, this adaptive scheme maintained RMS position error below 0.035 mm compared to a fixed-filter baseline that drifted to 0.11 mm by trial 400.

title: Sensitivity of torsional dynamics simulations to damping model choice in early-pitting planetary gearbox scenarios
abstract: The choice of damping model in multi-body torsional simulations of planetary gearboxes is examined for its effect on predicted vibration signatures when small pitting defects are present. Four damping models are compared: constant viscous mesh damping, load-dependent viscous damping, Rayleigh proportional damping, and a hysteretic damping formulation. Simulations are performed for a 3-planet gearbox at carrier speeds of 200, 400, and 800 rpm with sun gear pitting areas of 1, 3, 6, and 10 mm². The pitting severity index and its standard deviation over 50 simulated revolutions are used as comparison metrics. Hysteretic damping produces PSI values closest to experimental measurements from the department test rig, with a mean absolute error of 7.3% versus 14–22% for the other models. The sensitivity is most pronounced at low carrier speeds and small pit areas, where the difference between damping models in the PSI can reach 31%. Practical guidance for model selection based on available damping characterisation data is provided.

title: Extracting and Pre-processing Event Logs from a University Student Services ERP: A Case Study at a Serbian Faculty
abstract: Event log extraction from enterprise resource planning systems used in academic administration is rarely straightforward because these systems were not designed with process mining in mind. This paper reports on a systematic procedure for transforming raw database audit records from the student services module of a Serbian faculty into XES-compliant event logs suitable for process mining. The source data covered 14,847 student applications processed over three academic years (2018–2021). The procedure addresses four recurring data quality issues: missing case identifiers, overlapping timestamps caused by batch processing, inconsistent activity labels across module versions, and incomplete traces resulting from legacy migration. After cleaning, 91.3% of traces were retained as complete. A comparative evaluation using three filtering strategies—frequency-based, time-based, and hybrid—shows that the hybrid approach preserves the highest proportion of structurally meaningful traces while reducing noise. The resulting log and transformation scripts are described in sufficient detail to allow replication in comparable institutional settings. Lessons learned point to the need for standardised logging conventions in academic ERP procurement specifications.

abstract: Administrative workflows surrounding thesis submission and defence at Serbian faculties involve multiple offices, approval chains, and externally imposed deadlines, making them prone to queuing delays that affect graduation timelines. This paper applies performance spectrum analysis and dotted-chart visualisation to event logs covering 1,118 master's thesis defence cases from three academic years at one faculty. Waiting time distributions are computed per activity transition, and a Kaplan–Meier survival analysis is used to characterise time-to-completion across student cohorts stratified by study programme and submission month. Results identify two persistent bottlenecks: the commission nomination step, which accounts for a median wait of 11 working days, and the library archiving step following defence, which delays the formal completion record by a median of 6 days. Seasonal effects are pronounced, with June and September submissions showing 40% longer overall cycle times than other months. Simulation experiments using a simplified CPN model suggest that redistributing nomination authority to department coordinators could reduce median total duration by approximately 18%. The findings are presented to administrative staff at the host institution and reactions are discussed.

title: A Comparative Review of Recommendation Approaches for Sparse Purchase Histories in Small Retail
abstract: This paper surveys techniques applied to recommendation tasks where transaction logs contain fewer than twenty interactions per user on average, a condition common in independent and small-chain retail settings. The review covers memory-based collaborative filtering, content-based methods using product attribute vectors, and several hybrid architectures published between 2005 and 2013. Evaluation metrics across surveyed studies are standardised to precision at five and normalised discounted cumulative gain to allow comparison. The analysis identifies consistent shortcomings in purely collaborative approaches when item catalogues exceed a few hundred products but user bases remain small. Content-based methods show more stable baseline performance under these conditions but tend to over-specialise recommendations. The paper concludes by outlining criteria for selecting hybrid strategies depending on catalogue density, session length, and the availability of product metadata, offering a structured decision guide intended for practitioners in the regional retail sector.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Semi-Automated Population of Procurement Ontologies from Unstructured Tender Documents
abstract: A substantial proportion of procurement information in Western Balkan portals is embedded in free-text PDF attachments—technical specifications, terms of reference, evaluation criteria—rather than structured fields. This paper evaluates four large language models (two multilingual, two Serbian-language fine-tuned) for extracting ontology-conformant instances from 240 unstructured tender documents spanning four sectors: road construction, medical supplies, IT services, and school catering. Extraction performance is measured against a gold standard annotation produced by two domain experts. F1 scores across all entity types range from 0.53 to 0.79 depending on model and sector. Performance is highest for numeric quantity extraction (F1 0.82) and lowest for procedure type classification (F1 0.51). Post-processing with SHACL constraint validation catches a further 18 % of entity errors not penalised by F1. The paper discusses implications for ontology population workflows in low-resource Slavic language settings.

title: Reproducibility of manual CVP waveform component measurement in mechanically ventilated patients: an inter-rater study
abstract: Accurate identification of the a, c, and v components of the central venous pressure waveform is a prerequisite for any morphological analysis, yet reproducibility data in ventilated patients are scarce. We recruited 38 adult patients from a mixed medical ICU who were mechanically ventilated for at least 24 hours and had a functioning central venous catheter with continuous pressure monitoring. Five physicians independently measured peak a-wave amplitude, x-descent nadir, v-wave amplitude, and y-descent slope from the same ten-second strip for each patient. Intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.81 for a-wave amplitude, 0.74 for v-wave amplitude, and 0.68 for y-descent slope. Disagreement was greatest in patients with atrial fibrillation, where the a-wave was absent or poorly defined in 61% of strips. We conclude that manual waveform component identification is reasonably reproducible for amplitude measures but less so for slope parameters, and that rhythm status should be recorded as a covariate in any morphological study. Standardised training reduced inter-rater variance by approximately 22% when repeated after a structured calibration session.

title: Changes in the v-wave to a-wave amplitude ratio during volume loading in stable cardiac surgery patients
abstract: The ratio of v-wave to a-wave amplitude in the central venous pressure trace has been proposed as an indirect index of right atrial compliance, but its behaviour during acute preload augmentation has not been characterised in a surgical population. We prospectively enrolled 52 patients scheduled for elective coronary artery bypass grafting and recorded continuous CVP waveforms before and after a passive leg raise followed by a 250 mL crystalloid bolus. The v/a ratio increased significantly after volume loading (median 0.94 to 1.18, p < 0.001), while absolute a-wave amplitude remained stable. Responders, defined as those showing a ≥ 10% rise in stroke volume by transoesophageal Doppler, had a greater change in v/a ratio than non-responders (0.29 vs. 0.09, p = 0.003). These findings suggest that the v/a ratio may carry information about right heart filling dynamics that complements standard CVP interpretation. The practical implication is limited by individual variation in cardiac rhythm and respiratory cycle artefacts, which excluded 11 patients from final analysis.

title: CVP waveform morphology in early versus late septic shock: a descriptive cross-sectional analysis
abstract: We sought to describe differences in CVP waveform morphology between patients in early (< 6 hours) and late (24–72 hours) septic shock to generate hypotheses for subsequent studies. Forty-four consecutive adults admitted to a medical ICU with a confirmed diagnosis of septic shock were categorised by time from shock onset. Waveforms were digitised at 500 Hz and semi-automatically segmented into component phases. Patients in late shock had a significantly steeper y-descent slope (mean 8.3 vs. 5.1 mmHg/s, p = 0.007) and a higher v-wave amplitude (mean 11.4 vs. 7.8 mmHg, p = 0.012) compared with early-shock patients. The c-wave was identifiable in only 40% of tracings overall. SOFA scores correlated modestly with y-descent steepness (r = 0.44). The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the use of different catheter insertion sites across patients. These morphological shifts are consistent with progressive right ventricular diastolic impairment but causality cannot be inferred from this data.

title: Agreement between echocardiographic and CVP-derived estimates of right atrial pressure in septic patients
abstract: Right atrial pressure estimated from inferior vena cava collapsibility index (RAP-IVC) was compared with directly measured mean CVP and with a CVP waveform-derived composite index in 61 adult septic patients. The composite waveform index was calculated as a weighted sum of mean CVP, v-wave amplitude, and y-descent slope, fitted to an empirical formula developed from a training cohort. Bland–Altman analysis of RAP-IVC versus mean CVP showed a bias of −1.4 mmHg with limits of agreement of −8.2 to 5.4 mmHg. The composite waveform index produced narrower limits (−5.1 to 4.0 mmHg) with a smaller bias of −0.6 mmHg. Patients on positive pressure ventilation showed the greatest discordance for the IVC method. Echocardiographic windows were technically inadequate in 18% of patients, underscoring the practical value of continuous waveform monitoring. These data suggest the waveform composite may marginally outperform the IVC method in this population but validation in a separate cohort is required before clinical adoption.

title: Automated detection of c-wave absence in CVP traces as a surrogate marker of AV conduction delay
abstract: The c-wave in the CVP trace reflects tricuspid valve closure and is known to disappear or merge with the a-wave in the presence of prolonged PR intervals or conduction block. We implemented a threshold-crossing algorithm applied to a moving second-derivative filter on digitised CVP signals from 80 ICU patients with concurrent 12-lead ECGs. C-wave presence was detected automatically in 48 patients and absent or undetectable in 32. Automatic detection agreed with cardiologist visual interpretation in 88% of cases (κ = 0.75). Among patients with confirmed first-degree AV block (PR > 200 ms), c-wave absence was found in 78%. Specificity for PR prolongation was 0.71 and sensitivity 0.78. A secondary analysis showed that false c-wave detection occurred preferentially when respiratory oscillation amplitude exceeded 3 mmHg. The algorithm runs in near-real-time on standard bedside monitoring hardware and requires no additional sensors. This work lays groundwork for incorporating conduction status into continuous waveform-based haemodynamic indices.

title: Right ventricular longitudinal strain and CVP y-descent slope in septic shock: a prospective observational cohort
abstract: We hypothesised that the y-descent slope of the CVP waveform reflects early right ventricular diastolic dysfunction in septic shock and therefore correlates with echocardiographic right ventricular longitudinal strain (RVLS). Seventy-three adult patients with septic shock requiring vasopressors were enrolled within six hours of ICU admission. CVP waveforms were recorded continuously via a femoral or subclavian catheter; RVLS was measured by speckle-tracking echocardiography at 0, 12, and 24 hours. A steeper y-descent at 12 hours was associated with worse (more positive) RVLS at 24 hours (Pearson r = 0.51, p < 0.001). For every increase of 1 mmHg/s in y-descent steepness, RVLS worsened by 0.41 percentage points in adjusted linear regression. Among patients who developed overt right ventricular failure within 48 hours, y-descent steepening preceded the echocardiographic finding by a median of 7.2 hours. The area under the ROC curve for y-descent slope predicting right ventricular failure was 0.74 (95% CI 0.61–0.87). These findings support the y-descent slope as an early and non-invasive-equipment-free haemodynamic marker warranting prospective validation.

title: Haemodynamic monitoring in the ICU: from pressure numbers to waveform interpretation
abstract: This chapter reviews the physiological basis and clinical application of invasive haemodynamic monitoring in critically ill patients, with a focus on interpreting continuous pressure waveforms beyond mean values. Sections cover arterial line waveform interpretation, pulmonary artery catheter tracings, and central venous pressure morphology in detail. The CVP section describes the anatomical and electromechanical determinants of each waveform component, reviews literature on pathological waveform changes in right heart failure, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, and sepsis, and discusses practical pitfalls in catheter positioning and transducer zeroing. A clinical decision framework for integrating waveform findings with point-of-care echocardiography and clinical signs is presented. The chapter is directed at specialist trainees in internal medicine, anaesthesia, and emergency medicine and draws on both published evidence and the authors' institutional protocols.

title: Variability of CVP waveform morphology across catheter insertion sites in ICU patients: a matched comparison
abstract: Central venous catheters placed in different anatomical sites may introduce signal distortion that affects waveform morphology independently of true haemodynamic changes. We compared simultaneously recorded waveforms from internal jugular (IJ) and femoral central venous catheters in 34 ICU patients who required dual-site access for clinical reasons. Paired waveforms were recorded over ten minutes and segmented. V-wave amplitudes were on average 1.9 mmHg higher from femoral lines than from IJ lines (p = 0.004), while a-wave amplitudes did not differ significantly. Y-descent slopes were steeper in femoral recordings by a mean of 1.1 mmHg/s (p = 0.01). Time delay between matching waveform features was 0 ms in 62% of pairs, and ≤ 20 ms in all others, confirming synchrony. The morphological differences likely reflect compliance and inertance characteristics of the catheter-tubing-transducer system rather than true physiological gradients. These findings imply that waveform thresholds derived from one insertion site should not be directly applied to another without correction.

title: Albuminuria versus tubular proteinuria as predictors of eGFR decline over three years in hypertensive patients
abstract: This prospective cohort study followed 168 hypertensive patients with baseline eGFR between 45 and 90 mL/min/1.73 m² for 36 months. Albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, UACR) and tubular proteinuria markers (urinary retinol-binding protein, RBP, and urinary alpha-1-microglobulin, A1M) were quantified at baseline, 12, and 36 months. The primary outcome was a decline in eGFR of ≥5 mL/min/1.73 m² from baseline. In Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, diabetes and blood pressure control, elevated baseline urinary A1M (>12 mg/g creatinine) was associated with a hazard ratio of 2.4 (95% CI 1.4–4.1) for the primary outcome, compared to 1.9 (95% CI 1.1–3.3) for albuminuria. A combination of elevated UACR and A1M identified a subgroup with the steepest eGFR trajectory (mean annual decline −3.8 mL/min/1.73 m²). These data suggest that tubular proteinuria markers add prognostic information beyond albuminuria alone.

title: Long-term gut microbiome trajectories twelve months after Helicobacter pylori eradication: preliminary findings from an ongoing longitudinal study
abstract: Most studies assessing gut microbiome recovery after H. pylori eradication therapy use follow-up periods of six to eight weeks, leaving long-term compositional trajectories poorly characterized. This preprint presents preliminary data from an ongoing longitudinal study tracking 29 patients who completed successful clarithromycin-based triple therapy, with fecal sample collection at baseline and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post-treatment. 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data processed with QIIME2 showed that, while alpha diversity measures approached baseline by month three in the majority of participants, beta diversity analysis using Bray–Curtis dissimilarity indicated that community composition at twelve months remained distinguishable from pre-treatment baseline in 55% of subjects. Persistent depletion of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a butyrate-producing taxon, was noted at twelve months in 41% of participants. No clinical symptoms attributable to persistent dysbiosis were systematically recorded in this subset, though a structured symptom questionnaire has been introduced prospectively. Full dataset collection is expected to conclude in late 2026.

title: Medication discrepancies at hospital discharge in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes and hypertension: a prospective observational study
abstract: Medication reconciliation failures at the point of hospital discharge represent a well-documented source of adverse drug events, yet data from Central and Eastern Europe remain sparse. This prospective observational study enrolled 178 patients aged 65 or older with coexisting type 2 diabetes and hypertension discharged from internal medicine wards in Novi Sad between January and June 2015. Discharge prescriptions were compared with pre-admission medication lists and in-hospital treatment records. At least one unintended medication discrepancy was found in 58.4% of patients; omissions (42.7%) were more common than additions or dose changes. The highest discrepancy rates involved antihypertensives (particularly ACE inhibitors), oral hypoglycaemics, and statins. Patients with five or more comorbidities were significantly more likely to experience multiple discrepancies. The results support the introduction of structured pharmacist-led reconciliation at discharge for high-risk elderly patients.

title: Physician knowledge and attitudes towards deprescribing in elderly multimorbid patients: a survey of internists and general practitioners in Serbia
abstract: Despite growing evidence for the benefits of deprescribing in elderly patients, implementation in clinical practice remains limited. This cross-sectional survey was distributed to 214 internists and general practitioners across three healthcare regions of Serbia (Novi Sad, Belgrade, Niš) in 2018. The instrument comprised 32 items covering knowledge of polypharmacy risks, confidence in initiating deprescribing, and perceived barriers. Response rate was 74.3%. Only 31% of respondents reported routinely reviewing all medications at each patient encounter. The main perceived barriers were time constraints (cited by 68%), fear of adverse withdrawal effects (54%), and uncertainty about patient adherence post-discharge (49%). Internists showed significantly higher knowledge scores than general practitioners (mean 21.4 vs. 16.9 out of 32, p=0.003). Targeted educational interventions for general practitioners and standardised deprescribing guidelines adapted to the Serbian healthcare context are recommended.

title: Dose reduction feasibility in paediatric chest CT using adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction: a phantom study
abstract: Standard filtered back-projection (FBP) in paediatric chest CT produces unacceptable noise levels when tube current is lowered to safe paediatric ranges. This study evaluated an adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR) approach on a thorax-equivalent phantom across five simulated patient size classes (5–15 years). Scans were acquired at 80, 100, and 120 kVp with tube–current–time products ranging from 10 to 80 mAs. Noise power spectra, contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and modulation transfer function (MTF) were measured. ASIR at 60% blending achieved a 41–53% reduction in volume CT dose index (CTDIvol) relative to FBP-matched CNR targets across all size classes. Spatial resolution loss at 50% MTF was below 8% at equivalent CNR. The results provide a quantitative basis for protocol optimisation across paediatric age groups without subjective observer studies, establishing dose–noise curves that can guide prospective clinical protocol adjustment.

title: Observer study of image quality in low-dose paediatric lung CT reconstructed with model-based iterative reconstruction
abstract: Model-based iterative reconstruction (MBIR) incorporates a physical forward model of the CT acquisition process, potentially enabling deeper dose reductions than statistical methods. We recruited 12 paediatric patients (age 4–14 years, mean 8.3 years) referred for suspected pulmonary infection. Each examination was performed at clinical dose (CTDIvol 2.1–4.7 mGy) and a 50%-reduced protocol in the same session using a split-dose approach. Images were reconstructed with FBP and MBIR and rated by four radiologists using a five-point scale for noise, sharpness, and diagnostic confidence regarding lung parenchyma and airways. MBIR at 50% dose achieved scores statistically non-inferior to FBP at full dose for all three criteria (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p > 0.05). Effective dose estimates calculated with Monte Carlo-derived conversion coefficients showed a mean reduction of 48%. Inter-rater agreement was moderate to good (κ = 0.54–0.71). The study supports prospective implementation of reduced-dose MBIR protocols.

title: Characterisation of noise texture in iteratively reconstructed paediatric chest CT using local noise power spectrum analysis
abstract: Iterative reconstruction methods alter the spatial frequency content of image noise relative to FBP, producing a blotchy or waxy appearance that may impair low-contrast lesion detection even when global noise magnitude is reduced. We measured local noise power spectra (NPS) from uniform liver and lung phantom regions in scans acquired with FBP, ASIR-V at 40% and 80% blending, and MBIR across a 10–100 mAs range at 100 kVp. NPS peaks shifted from approximately 0.25 mm⁻¹ (FBP) to 0.15 mm⁻¹ (MBIR at 100 mAs), indicating texture coarsening. Frequency-weighted noise figures were computed and plotted against CTDIvol. ASIR-V 40% offered the most favourable compromise between noise magnitude and texture preservation. These measurements provide vendor-independent metrics for comparing reconstruction algorithms and can be used to design task-specific image quality targets for paediatric protocols.

title: Transfer learning for denoising of paediatric chest CT using a convolutional neural network trained on adult thoracic data
abstract: Deep learning denoising networks require large training datasets that are scarce in paediatric radiology due to ethical constraints on data acquisition. We investigated whether a residual convolutional neural network (ResNet-based, 17 layers) trained on 4 200 adult thoracic CT slices at matched dose levels could be adapted to paediatric images through fine-tuning on a small paediatric dataset of 310 slices (11 patients, ages 3–14 years). Training used paired full-dose and simulated quarter-dose images. After fine-tuning with 200 paediatric slices, SSIM improved from 0.879 to 0.923 on a 101-slice paediatric test set compared with direct application of the adult-trained network. FBP at quarter-dose had SSIM 0.841. Visual inspection by two radiologists confirmed improved airway wall delineation. The results indicate that transfer learning with modest paediatric fine-tuning data substantially bridges the domain gap, reducing the barrier to clinical deployment of deep learning denoisers.

title: Unrolled iterative network for low-dose paediatric chest CT reconstruction: architecture design and evaluation on clinical phantom data
abstract: Algorithm unrolling converts a fixed-iteration optimisation procedure into a trainable neural network by replacing hand-crafted regularisation proxies with learned components at each unrolled step. We designed a 10-stage unrolled network based on the ADMM algorithm, replacing the denoising proximal step with a small U-Net (3 scales, 32 base channels). The network was trained on 6 000 paired full-dose and quarter-dose chest phantom projections reconstructed with FBP, with ground truth taken from full-dose FBP. On a held-out clinical paediatric dataset (18 patients, ages 2–15 years), the unrolled network outperformed both a standard U-Net post-processing baseline and MBIR in SSIM (0.947 vs 0.921 vs 0.908) and mean radial artefact index around rib edges. Inference time per slice was 38 ms on a single NVIDIA GPU. The modular ADMM structure allows straightforward integration of physical noise models derived from scanner calibration data.

title: Perceptual image quality metrics for evaluating deep learning CT reconstruction in paediatric lung imaging
abstract: Standard pixel-wise metrics such as SSIM and PSNR do not reliably predict radiologist preference in CT reconstruction evaluation. We compared seven perceptual and task-based metrics—including visual information fidelity (VIF), learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS), and channelised Hotelling observer (CHO) for a low-contrast lung nodule detection task—against a radiologist ranking of images reconstructed by FBP, MBIR, a residual U-Net, and our previously published unrolled network, applied to 22 paediatric chest cases. Spearman rank correlation between CHO detectability index and radiologist preference ranking was 0.83, the highest among all tested metrics. SSIM correlated poorly (ρ = 0.41). LPIPS showed intermediate correlation (ρ = 0.67). The findings suggest CHO is a more reliable surrogate for diagnostic quality in paediatric chest CT and support its adoption as a primary evaluation metric in reconstruction algorithm development for this population.

title: Federated learning for low-dose CT denoising across multi-site paediatric data without raw image sharing
abstract: Centralising paediatric CT data from multiple hospitals for neural network training is often legally and ethically impractical. We implemented a federated learning (FL) framework in which three hospital sites (Novi Sad, Ljubljana, Pécs) each trained a local residual denoising network on their own paediatric chest CT data and exchanged only model weight updates. The global model was aggregated using FedAvg over 50 communication rounds. Local datasets comprised 320, 280, and 195 patient cases respectively. The federated global model achieved mean SSIM 0.938 on a pooled external test set of 47 cases, compared with 0.924 for the best single-site locally trained model and 0.944 for a centrally trained model. No patient data left institutional boundaries. Communication overhead was 1.2 GB total across all rounds. The framework demonstrates that competitive denoising performance is achievable under data-sharing constraints typical of European healthcare regulations.

title: Automated tube current modulation adjustment using body composition estimates from low-dose scout images in paediatric chest CT
abstract: Standard automated tube current modulation (ATCM) algorithms calibrate on scout radiograph attenuation, which correlates imperfectly with cross-sectional anatomy in paediatric patients due to body composition variability. We trained a lightweight convolutional regression network to predict per-slice optimal mAs from lateral and anteroposterior scout images, using a dataset of 540 paediatric chest CT examinations as ground truth (optimal mAs defined as the minimum yielding CHO detectability index d′ ≥ 2.5 for a 5 mm simulated nodule). On a prospective cohort of 31 patients (ages 3–13 years), the network-guided mAs prescription reduced mean CTDIvol by 17% relative to the manufacturer ATCM setting while maintaining d′ above threshold in 94% of slices. Overcurrent slices decreased from 23% to 9%. The approach requires no modification to scanner hardware and runs on the radiographer workstation prior to scanning.

title: Prospective validation of a combined EU-TIRADS and shear-wave elastography protocol for deferring biopsy in intermediate-risk thyroid nodules
abstract: Following a previously published retrospective proposal, this prospective study formally tested the combined EU-TIRADS plus SWE protocol in a single-centre cohort of 196 patients with 214 nodules classified as EU-TIRADS 3 or 4. The deferral rule (SWE mean < 28 kPa → observation with 12-month repeat ultrasound) was applied by radiologists blinded to clinical outcome. Sixty-eight nodules (31.8%) were assigned to the observation arm. At 24-month follow-up, two nodules in the observation arm showed size progression and were biopsied; both proved benign on cytology. No malignancy was detected in the deferred group. In the biopsy arm, 12 malignancies were confirmed among 146 nodules. Protocol sensitivity for clinically relevant malignancy was 100% (95% CI 73.5–100%) and FNAB reduction was 31.8%. The results support the safety of the combined protocol as an adjunct to standard TIRADS triage in selected intermediate-risk nodules.

title: Fixation duration and saccade amplitude as indicators of workload during initial procedural learning in a simulated assembly task
abstract: This study examined whether basic oculomotor parameters could differentiate workload levels across three phases of procedural learning in a laboratory assembly task. Forty-two undergraduate participants learned a 12-step assembly sequence over four sessions. Remote eye-tracking data were recorded at 300 Hz. Fixation duration increased significantly from early to mid-acquisition (mean increase 87 ms, p < .01) and then decreased at a late stage, consistent with a schema-consolidation account. Saccade amplitude followed the inverse pattern, being shortest during the mid-acquisition phase when error rates were highest (mean 3.1°). Subjective NASA-TLX ratings correlated moderately with fixation duration (r = .48) but not with saccade amplitude. The results support the use of fixation-based metrics as a continuous, unobtrusive workload index in procedural training contexts, complementing but not replacing self-report measures. Implications for adaptive training system design are discussed.

title: Pupil dilation as a real-time index of mental effort during sequential decision-making in trained versus untrained operators
abstract: Pupil dilation is sensitive to changes in mental effort, but its utility in distinguishing trained from untrained operators on the same task has received limited systematic attention. Thirty-two participants were split into a trained group (20 sessions on a fault-diagnosis simulator) and an untrained control group. Pupillometric data were recorded under controlled luminance conditions. The trained group showed a 14% smaller peak pupil dilation during the critical decision phase compared with controls (p < .001), alongside lower error rates (7% vs. 31%). Task-evoked pupillary responses correlated negatively with session number (r = −.62) across training, suggesting that pupil dilation tracks the progressive automatisation of decision steps. Baseline pupil diameter did not differ between groups, ruling out tonic arousal as a confound. These findings have practical implications for the objective monitoring of operator readiness in industrial settings.

title: Scanpath similarity across learning trials predicts retention of procedural sequences one week later
abstract: Scanpath analysis provides a spatial and temporal description of gaze behaviour, but its predictive value for long-term procedural retention is not well established. In this study, 56 participants practised a software-based data-entry procedure across five training sessions. Scanpath similarity scores (computed using the ScanMatch algorithm) between consecutive trials were calculated for each participant. Participants whose scanpaths converged (similarity index above the median) during sessions 3–5 recalled the procedure with significantly fewer step-order errors at a one-week retention test (M = 1.4 errors vs. M = 4.1 errors, p < .001, d = 1.21). Multiple regression showed that scanpath convergence explained 29% of variance in retention scores, above and beyond self-reported confidence and total practice time. The findings suggest that gaze-pattern stabilisation is a measurable behavioural signature of robust procedural encoding.

title: Measuring workload during laparoscopic skill training: a comparison of oculomotor, cardiovascular, and subjective indices
abstract: The study compared four workload indices during three stages of laparoscopic box-trainer practice in 24 surgical residents: pupil dilation, fixation rate, heart rate variability (SDNN), and the NASA-TLX. All four indices changed significantly from novice to intermediate to proficient performance levels (all p < .05), but divergence in sensitivity was evident. Fixation rate showed the greatest effect size across the novice–intermediate transition (η² = .41), while pupil dilation was most sensitive at the intermediate–proficient transition (η² = .35). Heart rate variability had lower discriminant validity between stages. Correlation among indices was modest (r range .21–.44), confirming that they tap partially independent aspects of workload. The multi-modal measurement approach is recommended for training assessment in surgical education, particularly where unobtrusive monitoring is required.

title: Attentional tunnelling in novice air traffic control trainees: evidence from fixation dispersion analysis
abstract: Attentional tunnelling—the narrowing of attentional focus to a subset of relevant stimuli—is a known risk factor in safety-critical work, yet its emergence during initial training has been studied with limited objective methods. We examined fixation dispersion in 18 air traffic control trainees during a radar simulation task at three time points (weeks 1, 4, and 8 of training). Fixation dispersion (standard deviation of fixation coordinates) decreased from week 1 to week 4 and then partially recovered at week 8. The decrease at week 4 corresponded to a period of highest task complexity in the curriculum and was accompanied by elevated mean fixation duration (+112 ms relative to week 1). Trainees who showed the most pronounced tunnelling at week 4 committed more coordination errors at week 8. The results have direct implications for curriculum pacing and for the use of dispersion metrics as early warning signals in training evaluation.

title: Workload and attention in procedural skill learning: a review of oculomotor methods
abstract: This book chapter reviews the empirical literature on oculomotor measurement of cognitive workload and attentional allocation specifically within procedural skill learning paradigms. The review covers fixation-based measures (duration, rate, dispersion, area of interest dwell time), pupillometry, and scanpath comparison methods, evaluating their psychometric properties, sensitivity at different skill levels, and practical constraints for deployment in applied settings. The chapter discusses conceptual distinctions between workload and attention, arguing that these constructs map onto dissociable oculomotor signatures. Methodological issues including luminance control, equipment choice, and data-loss management are addressed in a dedicated section. The review identifies gaps in research on transfer of gaze-based findings across task domains and recommends standardised reporting practices for future studies.

title: Cognitive load during CNC machine operation training: an eye-tracking study with experienced and inexperienced operators
abstract: This study investigated how cognitive load, measured through fixation count, mean fixation duration, and pupil dilation, varies between experienced CNC machine operators (M = 6.4 years experience) and trainees (no prior experience) during a standardised tool-change procedure. Twenty operators and twenty trainees were recruited from technical vocational schools and a manufacturing firm in Vojvodina. Trainees showed 62% more fixations per trial and 31% longer mean fixation durations than experienced operators. Task-evoked pupil dilation was 0.41 mm larger in trainees on average. Fixation count correlated significantly with error rate in trainees (r = .56, p < .01) but not in operators (r = .09). Qualitative analysis of gaze sequences revealed that trainees frequently revisited the instruction display, accounting for 18% of total fixation time vs. 4% in experienced operators. Results are discussed in relation to cognitive load theory and the design of in-machine guidance systems.

title: Gaze-based workload monitoring during robotic-assisted surgery training: a feasibility study with a head-mounted eye-tracker
abstract: Remote eye-trackers are impractical in sterile surgical settings; head-mounted devices may offer a viable alternative, but their performance in this context is understudied. This feasibility study tested a head-mounted Pupil Core eye-tracker on 12 surgical residents performing tasks on a robotic surgery simulator across six sessions. Calibration stability was assessed before and after each session; post-session calibration error was below 1.2° in 91% of recordings. Mean fixation duration decreased from 342 ms (session 1) to 218 ms (session 6), consistent with automatisation. Pupil dilation showed a statistically significant session effect (F(5, 55) = 8.3, p < .001). Data-loss rate due to head movement averaged 9.4%. The study demonstrates that head-mounted pupillometry is feasible in a surgical training context, though a protocol for recalibration between simulator runs is recommended.

title: Does dual-task interference reveal hidden workload in expert operators? An eye-tracking and secondary-task study
abstract: Expert operators often appear to have spare cognitive capacity, but secondary-task methods have produced inconsistent results. This study combined oculomotor measurement with a secondary auditory reaction-time task to probe residual workload in 25 expert switchboard operators and 25 novices. During a primary fault-identification task, experts showed shorter mean fixation durations (196 ms vs. 289 ms) and faster secondary-task reaction times (M = 348 ms vs. 441 ms) than novices, confirming lower primary-task load. However, when task difficulty was increased by adding ambiguous fault signals, expert fixation durations increased by 48 ms and secondary-task RT degraded by 71 ms, indicating that residual capacity was not unlimited. Pupil dilation tracked both manipulations linearly. The combined approach proved more sensitive to graded difficulty changes than either method alone, with effect sizes for the combined index (d = 1.42) exceeding those of oculomotor-only (d = 0.98) or RT-only (d = 0.87) measures.

title: Workload trajectory modelling across a six-month apprenticeship: longitudinal eye-tracking evidence from metalworking trainees
abstract: Longitudinal studies of skill acquisition using objective physiological measures are scarce because of the practical burden of repeated data collection in real work settings. We conducted eight eye-tracking sessions over six months with 21 metalworking apprentices in a vocational training centre, measuring fixation rate, dwell time on control panels, and pupil dilation during a standardised lathe-operation task. Mixed-effects growth-curve models indicated a non-linear workload trajectory: rapid decrease in fixation rate during months 1–2 (slope = −0.8 fixations/min per week), plateau during months 3–4, and a further decrease during months 5–6 coinciding with introduction of advanced operations. Individual differences in learning rate, estimated from the growth-curve models, correlated with end-of-apprenticeship practical examination scores (r = .61, p < .001). The study provides longitudinal validation for oculomotor workload indices in authentic vocational settings and identifies modelling approaches suitable for tracking individual learning trajectories.

title: Sensitivity of entropy-based gaze metrics to attentional strategy changes during instrument panel monitoring
abstract: Transition entropy and stationary gaze entropy are two metrics derived from fixation transition matrices that quantify the regularity or predictability of gaze behaviour. This study evaluated their sensitivity compared with conventional fixation duration and count measures during a simulated instrument panel monitoring task manipulated for display density (3, 6, or 9 instruments) and event rate (low, medium, high). Sixty participants completed a 2 × 3 factorial design. Both entropy measures increased significantly with display density and event rate, and showed interaction effects absent in conventional metrics. Transition entropy discriminated between medium and high event rates with greater power (η² = .29) than mean fixation duration (η² = .14). The entropy metrics were also less correlated with each other than with conventional measures, suggesting they capture partially distinct gaze properties. Practical guidance for selecting among these indices for workload monitoring applications is provided.

title: Eye-tracking-based workload assessment in warehouse picking tasks: effects of augmented reality guidance on fixation behaviour
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) picking guidance systems are increasingly deployed in logistics, but their effects on operator cognitive workload as measured by eye-tracking have not been well characterised. In a simulated warehouse environment, 34 participants performed order-picking under three conditions: paper list, handheld scanner, and AR head-up display guidance. Remote eye-tracking was used to measure fixation duration, fixation count, and saccadic peak velocity. AR guidance reduced fixation count relative to paper list (M = 12.4 vs. 17.1 fixations per pick, p < .001) and scanner (M = 14.6, p < .05) conditions, suggesting reduced visual search. However, fixation duration on non-guidance areas (shelving labels, floor) was longer under AR, indicating partial attentional distraction from the overlay. Pupil dilation did not differ between scanner and AR conditions. The findings suggest that AR guidance reduces visual search load while introducing mild attentional competition from the overlay itself.

title: Pupillometric and fixation indices of cognitive load during adaptive e-learning: a preregistered study
abstract: Adaptive e-learning platforms adjust content difficulty in real time, but most adaptation algorithms rely on performance accuracy alone and discard moment-to-moment workload information. This preregistered study examined whether pupillometry and fixation metrics collected during adaptive online instruction could provide additional predictive signal for learning outcomes. Seventy-one participants learned a statistics module over two 90-minute sessions. Pupil dilation and fixation duration were recorded using a remote eye-tracker integrated with the learning platform. Both pupil dilation amplitude (β = .22, p = .03) and mean fixation duration (β = .19, p = .04) at the end of session 1 predicted session 2 performance scores, after controlling for session 1 accuracy and prior statistics knowledge. A combined index (z-scored mean of both measures) showed the highest incremental validity (ΔR² = .07, p = .01). Results support the feasibility of using passive oculomotor data streams to augment adaptation logic in e-learning systems.

title: Eye-tracking patterns during reading of numerical and pictographic risk formats in pharmaceutical package inserts
abstract: Pharmaceutical package inserts routinely present adverse-event frequencies using natural frequencies, percentages, and the EU pictogram system. This study used eye-tracking to compare visual attention patterns during reading of three risk formats in a within-subjects design with 54 healthy adults. Participants read eight matched inserts (two per format, with one hybrid format), and fixation count, total dwell time, and first-pass regression rate were recorded using a Tobii TX300 system. Pictograms attracted significantly more first-pass fixations than numerical formats (F(2,106) = 18.7, p < .001, η² = .26), but comprehension accuracy—assessed by a post-reading forced-choice task—was highest for natural frequency text. Hybrid formats (frequency text accompanied by a simple icon array) produced both high attention and high comprehension scores. Subjective difficulty ratings were lowest for pictograms yet comprehension was lowest for stand-alone pictograms, indicating a fluency illusion. Recommendations for insert redesign are proposed.

title: The role of implementation intentions in moderating the intention–behaviour gap for fruit and vegetable consumption
abstract: Despite generally positive attitudes, adults in Serbia consume fruit and vegetables below recommended levels. This study tested whether prompting formation of implementation intentions (specifying when, where, and how to act) could reduce the gap between stated intentions and actual dietary behaviour over a four-week period. A sample of 203 adults was randomly allocated to an implementation intention condition or a motivational information-only control. Dietary behaviour was assessed via a validated 24-hour food recall administered at baseline and weeks 2 and 4. The implementation intention group showed a significantly higher proportion meeting the five-portion guideline at week 4 (38% vs. 22%, χ²(1) = 7.81, p = .005). Effect size was moderate (φ = 0.20). Participants high in action self-efficacy at baseline benefited most from the implementation intention prompt. Results replicate and extend prior European studies to a post-socialist dietary context where structural barriers to healthy eating are distinct.

title: Comparative Assessment of Lead-Acid and Lithium-Ion Battery Technologies for Off-Grid Residential Applications in the Western Balkans
abstract: This study evaluates the techno-economic suitability of valve-regulated lead-acid and lithium iron phosphate batteries for off-grid residential systems in rural settlements across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. Thirty-two representative households were instrumented over 12 months to obtain measured load profiles with 15-minute resolution. A deterministic sizing procedure based on peak shaving requirements and autonomy targets of 24–72 hours was applied. Capital cost data were collected from five regional distributors. Results show that lithium iron phosphate systems achieve a levelised cost of storage 18–24% lower than lead-acid equivalents over a 10-year horizon when cycle counts exceed 800 per year. Lead-acid retains a cost advantage only at very low utilisation rates below 200 cycles per year. The study provides tabulated sizing guidelines for system integrators and notes significant sensitivity to assumed electricity tariff structures prevailing in the region.

title: A Rainflow-Counting Degradation Model for Lithium-Ion Cells Calibrated Against Accelerated Ageing Data
abstract: Accurate prediction of capacity fade in lithium-ion cells under irregular residential duty cycles requires degradation models that can handle variable depth-of-discharge and state-of-charge ranges. This paper presents a rainflow-counting framework calibrated against capacity measurements from 28 NMC pouch cells cycled under 14 distinct protocols covering depths-of-discharge from 10% to 90% and temperatures from 15 °C to 40 °C. A weighted Ah-throughput damage accumulation function with two exponential terms is fitted to the data using nonlinear least squares; the root mean square error on held-out test cells is 1.4% of nominal capacity at end of test. The model is formulated as a computationally tractable auxiliary constraint for inclusion in dispatch optimisation problems. Comparison with a simpler equivalent full-cycle model shows that rainflow counting reduces overestimation of remaining cycle life by up to 31% for highly irregular profiles.

title: Optimal Sizing of Grid-Connected Residential Photovoltaic–Battery Systems Incorporating Electrochemical Ageing Constraints
abstract: This paper formulates a mixed-integer linear programming model for the joint optimisation of photovoltaic panel capacity and battery storage capacity for grid-connected single-family houses. The ageing model derived from accelerated cycling experiments is linearised and embedded as a constraint limiting cumulative cycle damage over the planning horizon of 15 years. Stochastic load and irradiance inputs are represented by 50 scenarios generated via Latin hypercube sampling from empirical distributions. The model is applied to three house archetypes in the Vojvodina region using measured irradiance data from a rooftop station at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Optimal photovoltaic capacity ranges from 3.2 to 5.8 kWp and optimal battery capacity from 4.1 to 9.3 kWh depending on archetype and tariff structure. Including the ageing constraint increases optimal battery capacity by 12–19% compared with a degradation-free formulation, reflecting the need to reduce per-cycle stress.

title: Stochastic Dispatch Strategies for Residential Battery Storage Under Time-of-Use Tariffs: A Monte Carlo Approach
abstract: Time-of-use electricity tariffs create an incentive for residential battery storage to perform price arbitrage, but the profitability depends heavily on the realised load profile, which varies significantly from day to day. This study applies Monte Carlo simulation with 10 000 annual scenarios, drawn from the clustered load profile library developed in earlier work, to assess the distribution of annual savings achievable by three dispatch heuristics: greedy peak shaving, price-threshold arbitrage, and a model predictive control policy with a 24-hour look-ahead. A degradation penalty derived from the rainflow counting model is incorporated into the economic accounting. Results show that the model predictive control policy achieves median annual savings of 187 EUR per household at a battery size of 7 kWh but has a 90th-percentile loss of 43 EUR in adverse load years. The greedy heuristic is more robust but yields savings 22% lower on average. Sensitivity to forecast horizon length and tariff spread is quantified.

title: Battery Sizing and Ageing Modelling for Residential Storage: Methods, Data Requirements, and Practical Limitations
abstract: This book chapter reviews the state of practice in optimal sizing and dispatch modelling for residential battery energy storage with an emphasis on electrochemical ageing. The chapter covers three families of ageing models—equivalent full-cycle counting, rainflow-based damage accumulation, and physics-based single-particle models—and assesses their tractability when embedded in optimisation frameworks. Data requirements for each approach are discussed, including the number of laboratory cycling tests needed to achieve calibration uncertainty below 5% capacity fade error. Practical limitations arising from the mismatch between laboratory cell data and module-level behaviour in field installations are addressed, with reference to reported case studies from Germany, Italy, and Serbia. The chapter concludes with a structured comparison table mapping model complexity to computational cost and recommends research priorities for the integration of temperature effects and calendar ageing into sizing workflows.

title: Effect of Temperature Variation on Optimal Dispatch Policy for Residential Lithium-Ion Storage in Continental Climate Zones
abstract: Most residential battery dispatch models assume isothermal operation, which is not representative of systems installed in unheated utility rooms in continental climates where ambient temperature ranges from −5 °C in winter to 35 °C in summer. This study augments an existing dispatch model with a lumped thermal model of a 10 kWh lithium-ion module and a temperature-dependent degradation rate derived from Arrhenius fitting to calendar ageing data at five temperatures. A year-long simulation using measured ambient temperatures from ten sites in Vojvodina and a 24-hour model predictive control policy is performed. Results indicate that ignoring temperature effects underestimates annual capacity fade by 8–14% at sites with prolonged summer periods and overestimates it by 4–7% at cooler upland sites. An adjusted dispatch policy that limits C-rate at high temperatures reduces total annual degradation by 6% at a cost of 3% reduction in annual arbitrage savings.

title: Economic Feasibility of Second-Life Lithium-Ion Batteries in Residential Storage Under Serbian Regulatory Conditions
abstract: Repurposed electric vehicle battery modules offer a lower upfront cost than new cells but arrive with heterogeneous state of health, typically in the range 70–82% of original capacity based on data from three domestic automotive service centres. This paper develops a sizing and dispatch model that explicitly accounts for initial state-of-health uncertainty using a two-stage stochastic programme. In the first stage, battery capacity procurement is decided under uncertainty; in the second stage, dispatch is optimised for each state-of-health scenario. A set of 30 representative scenarios is generated by fitting a beta distribution to measured state-of-health data from 47 retired modules. Under current Serbian net-metering regulations and a 30% cost discount relative to new cells, second-life systems reach breakeven in 9–11 years for high-utilisation households. Breakeven extends beyond 15 years for low-consumption households, making second-life storage financially marginal in that segment without additional policy support.

title: Benchmarking Stochastic Optimisation Formulations for Residential Battery Sizing: Scenario Trees Versus Chance Constraints
abstract: Stochastic programmes for battery sizing can be formulated either by explicit enumeration of load and generation scenarios or by imposing chance constraints that bound the probability of constraint violation. This paper provides a systematic comparison of both approaches applied to a standardised residential sizing problem with a 15-year planning horizon, five house types, and three Serbian climate zones. Scenario tree formulations with 20, 50, and 200 scenarios are tested alongside chance-constrained formulations at reliability levels of 90%, 95%, and 99%. Computational times, optimal battery capacities, and out-of-sample economic performance are evaluated across 1 000 test scenarios. The scenario tree approach with 50 scenarios achieves near-identical out-of-sample performance to the 200-scenario version while reducing solution time by a factor of 3.8. Chance constraints at 95% reliability yield solutions with 7–11% larger battery capacities than corresponding scenario formulations and exhibit higher variance in out-of-sample cost.

title: Integrated Cycle-Ageing and Dispatch Co-optimisation for Residential Battery Storage with Rooftop Photovoltaics: A Receding-Horizon Framework
abstract: Previous work has typically treated battery ageing either as an offline constraint in the sizing phase or as a penalty term in heuristic dispatch rules. This paper presents a receding-horizon optimisation framework in which a linearised cycle-ageing submodel is included as a dynamic constraint within a 48-hour dispatch problem solved every 24 hours. The framework is implemented in Python using an open-source MILP solver and tested on a hardware-in-the-loop platform connected to a 7.2 kWh lithium iron phosphate module and a 4.8 kWp PV emulator. Experiments spanning 90 simulated operating days show that the co-optimised policy extends projected end-of-life by 1.3 years relative to a price-threshold dispatch policy while sacrificing less than 4% of annual electricity bill savings. Computational time per optimisation step averages 11 seconds on a standard desktop processor, which is compatible with embedded controller deployment.

title: Effect of inverter clipping on annual energy yield and demand-peak offset for oversized PV systems at Serbian industrial sites
abstract: Inverter clipping—the curtailment of PV output when DC generation exceeds AC inverter rating—is examined for DC-to-AC ratios between 1.0 and 1.6 at five industrial sites in Serbia with measured irradiation and load data spanning 2021–2024. Annual clipping losses ranged from 0.9% to 6.8% of DC yield depending on ratio and site orientation. However, clipping predominantly occurs at solar noon, outside the late-afternoon demand-peak window defined by the local industrial TOU tariff. As a result, increasing the DC-to-AC ratio from 1.0 to 1.4 improved the fraction of tariff-relevant peaks offset by PV from 41% to 53% on average across sites, while clipping losses remained below 3%. A simple analytical correction factor is derived to adjust standard annual yield estimates for clipped oversized systems without detailed simulation, valid for the continental climate zone of northern Serbia.

title: Density and porosity evolution in laser-sintered PA12 parts as a function of energy density input
abstract: This study examined the relationship between volumetric energy density and porosity in polyamide 12 specimens produced by selective laser sintering. Forty-eight specimen sets were fabricated by varying laser power (10–20 W), scan speed (1000–2500 mm/s), and layer thickness (0.10–0.15 mm) in a 4×3×2 factorial arrangement. Archimedes displacement measurements and X-ray micro-computed tomography (voxel size 8 µm) were combined to quantify total void fraction and pore morphology. Results showed that volumetric energy density alone was insufficient to predict porosity; scan speed exerted a disproportionate influence, with specimens sintered above 2000 mm/s displaying interconnected pore networks accounting for up to 6.8 % of cross-sectional area. Pore aspect ratios measured from reconstructed CT data ranged from 1.1 to 4.3, indicating partial coalescence at intermediate energy inputs. A response-surface model relating energy density and scan speed to void fraction achieved an R² of 0.91. The findings suggest that scan-speed control deserves independent attention in process qualification protocols beyond composite energy-density metrics.

title: Build orientation effects on tensile and flexural properties of SLS-processed polyamide 12
abstract: Rectangular tensile bars and flexural beams were fabricated in five build orientations (0°, 22.5°, 45°, 67.5°, and 90° relative to the build platform) using a commercial SLS system with fixed process parameters. Tensile testing (ISO 527-2) on twenty specimens per orientation revealed that ultimate tensile strength varied from 43.1 MPa (0°) to 36.4 MPa (90°), a reduction of 15.5 %, while elongation at break dropped from 18.3 % to 9.7 %. Three-point bending tests showed a parallel trend, with flexural modulus declining by 11 % between the most and least favourable orientations. Scanning electron microscopy of fracture surfaces identified inter-layer delamination as the dominant failure mode at high inclination angles. A linear regression model using orientation angle as predictor accounted for 84 % of the variance in strength but only 61 % of the variance in modulus, indicating that stiffness is less sensitive to orientation than strength. Practical build-orientation guidelines for structural SLS components are discussed.

title: Fatigue life characterisation of selective laser sintered PA12: S–N curves and failure mode analysis
abstract: Fully reversed axial fatigue tests (R = −1) were conducted on dog-bone specimens of selective laser sintered PA12 fabricated in three orientations (0°, 45°, 90°) to determine S–N relationships and identify failure mechanisms under cyclic loading. Stress amplitudes ranged from 12 to 32 MPa; run-out was defined at 5 × 10⁶ cycles. A total of 126 specimens were tested at 10 Hz in ambient laboratory conditions (23 °C, 50 % RH). Runout-adjusted Basquin parameters were derived: fatigue strength coefficient σ′f ranged from 78 to 91 MPa and fatigue ductility exponent b from −0.082 to −0.097 across orientations. Fractographic examination using scanning electron microscopy showed crack initiation predominantly at inter-layer boundaries and large pores (diameter > 80 µm). The 45° specimens exhibited the shortest average fatigue life at intermediate stress amplitudes, attributed to the oblique alignment of inter-layer planes relative to the loading axis. Correlation between void fraction measured by micro-CT and fatigue life followed a power-law trend (R² = 0.79).

title: Thermal history and its influence on crystallinity and mechanical performance in SLS polyamide parts
abstract: Differential scanning calorimetry and wide-angle X-ray diffraction were used to quantify the degree of crystallinity in PA12 specimens extracted from different positions within an SLS build chamber (top, middle, bottom layers; near-wall and centre positions). Build position influenced crystallinity significantly: centre specimens showed 28–31 % crystallinity while near-wall specimens reached 36–40 %, consistent with longer exposure to elevated ambient temperature in the powder bed. Hardness (Shore D) followed crystallinity trends, with near-wall parts averaging 74 HD versus 69 HD at centre positions. Quasi-static tensile tests confirmed that higher crystallinity correlated with increased stiffness (+9 % Young's modulus) but reduced ductility (−22 % elongation at break). A one-dimensional thermal model calibrated to thermocouple data captured the observed crystallinity gradient with a mean absolute error of 1.8 percentage points. The results indicate that chamber position should be treated as an independent variable in process characterisation studies.
