title: Quantitative void fraction analysis in SLS polyamide using laboratory micro-CT: methodology and uncertainty assessment
abstract: This methodological paper addresses the reproducibility and uncertainty of void-fraction measurement in SLS polymer specimens by X-ray micro-computed tomography. Four scanning protocols differing in tube voltage (50–90 kV), voxel size (5–20 µm), and reconstruction algorithm (filtered back-projection vs. iterative) were applied to twenty nominally identical PA12 bars. Threshold selection (global Otsu, local adaptive, and manual) was compared using phantom specimens with known void fractions (0.5–8.0 %) fabricated by controlled gas injection. The global Otsu threshold overestimated void fraction by 0.8–1.4 percentage points relative to the phantom reference, while the adaptive threshold reduced bias to below 0.3 percentage points. Voxel size had a stronger effect on pore-size distribution accuracy than threshold choice; pores smaller than three voxels were systematically undersized regardless of threshold. A step-by-step measurement protocol and uncertainty budget are proposed to enable inter-laboratory comparison of SLS porosity data. The protocol was validated on specimens shared with two partner laboratories in Novi Sad and Brno.

title: Influence of powder refresh ratio on surface roughness and subsurface porosity in reused PA12 powder for SLS
abstract: Selective laser sintering relies on partial reuse of unsintered powder, yet the effect of refresh ratio on part quality is incompletely characterised. This study tested PA12 powder at five refresh ratios (100 % virgin to 20 % virgin / 80 % recycled) across three production runs. Gel-permeation chromatography showed progressive increase in weight-average molecular weight from 62 to 81 kg/mol after three cycles at 20 % virgin ratio, indicating thermal-oxidative chain extension. Confocal profilometry of part surfaces showed Ra increasing from 11.3 µm (100 % virgin) to 19.7 µm (20 % virgin) after three cycles. Subsurface porosity measured by micro-CT rose from 1.9 % to 4.8 % over the same range. Quasi-static tensile strength declined by 14 %, while fatigue life at 22 MPa stress amplitude was reduced by approximately one order of magnitude in the most degraded powder. A minimum refresh ratio of 40 % is recommended to maintain mechanical properties within 10 % of virgin-powder benchmarks.

title: Fatigue crack propagation in SLS PA12 monitored by in-situ digital image correlation
abstract: Compact tension specimens of SLS PA12 fabricated in 0° and 90° build orientations were tested under cyclic loading (R = 0.1, 5 Hz) while surface strain fields were simultaneously recorded by digital image correlation at 2 Hz. Crack-tip plastic zone size was estimated from the DIC-measured strain fields and compared with predictions from linear elastic fracture mechanics. At equivalent stress intensity factor ranges (ΔK = 0.6–1.2 MPa·m^0.5), the plastic zone in 90° specimens was 1.6 times larger than in 0° specimens, consistent with the lower yield stress of the weaker orientation. Crack growth rates followed Paris law with exponents of 3.8 (0°) and 5.1 (90°), indicating stronger sensitivity to ΔK in the transverse orientation. Crack deflection events at inter-layer boundaries were recorded in 17 of 24 transverse specimens, causing local reductions in crack growth rate of up to 35 %. DIC proved effective for tracking these deflections without specimen interruption.

title: Glass-bead reinforced PA12 for SLS: microstructure, filler distribution, and cyclic mechanical response
abstract: Glass beads (20 µm median diameter) were blended into PA12 SLS powder at 0, 10, 20, and 30 wt% and sintered under identical conditions. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray mapping confirmed homogeneous bead dispersion at 10 and 20 wt% loadings, while 30 wt% exhibited localised clustering and increased inter-particle voids. Tensile modulus increased from 1.65 GPa (unfilled) to 2.41 GPa (20 wt%), but elongation at break fell from 17.1 % to 6.4 %. Fatigue tests at R = 0.1 and 22 MPa stress amplitude showed that the 10 wt% composite had a median fatigue life 2.3 times longer than unfilled PA12, attributed to crack-deflection and energy absorption at the bead–matrix interface. Above 20 wt% loading, bead clustering introduced stress-concentrating defects that reversed the fatigue benefit; the 30 wt% specimens failed at fewer cycles than unfilled material. Dynamic mechanical analysis indicated that glass beads raised the storage modulus across the −20 to +60 °C range without shifting the glass transition temperature significantly.

title: Statistical process monitoring for SLS using in-situ layer imaging and post-build CT: a paired dataset approach
abstract: This study presents a paired dataset of 312 SLS builds in which each layer was photographed during fabrication using a fixed overhead camera and each finished part was subsequently scanned by micro-CT. Image processing of layer photographs extracted sintering boundary regularity, melt-pool width, and local contrast features for each layer. Regression and random-forest models were trained to predict post-build void fraction from in-situ layer features. The best-performing model (random forest, 150 trees) predicted void fraction with a mean absolute error of 0.41 percentage points on a held-out test set, compared with a baseline MAE of 1.12 percentage points for a model using process parameters alone. Feature importance analysis identified melt-pool width variability as the strongest predictor, followed by layer contrast entropy. The dataset and trained model weights are published openly. Practical integration of the in-situ camera output into a statistical process control chart is demonstrated for a production scenario with a reject threshold set at 3 % void fraction.

title: High-cycle fatigue behaviour of SLS PA12 under variable-amplitude loading: sequence effects and damage accumulation
abstract: Variable-amplitude fatigue tests were performed on SLS PA12 specimens (0° build orientation) using a standardised block-loading sequence derived from a lightweight structural component duty cycle. Three block sequences—low–high, high–low, and randomised—were applied at peak stress amplitudes of 18 and 26 MPa, cycling at 10 Hz to failure or run-out at 10⁷ cycles. Miner's rule predictions overestimated fatigue life by a factor of 1.4–2.1 depending on sequence order, consistent with mean-stress-dependent damage accumulation in polymers. High–low sequences produced shorter lives than predicted, while low–high sequences produced longer lives, attributed to cyclic hardening effects observed in dynamic mechanical analysis after partial loading. Stiffness degradation curves derived from cycle-by-cycle displacement records correlated with residual life: a 4 % stiffness reduction corresponded to 70–80 % of total fatigue life consumed across all sequences tested. A modified damage summation rule incorporating sequence weighting is proposed and validated against the experimental dataset.

title: A diode-based single-cell model for PV modules under non-uniform irradiance: parameter extraction and validation
abstract: This paper describes a single-diode equivalent circuit model for photovoltaic cells adapted for scenarios in which irradiance across a module is spatially non-uniform. Model parameters—saturation current, series resistance, shunt resistance, and ideality factor—were extracted from manufacturer datasheets for three commercially available 250 Wp polycrystalline modules using a least-squares fitting procedure applied to measured I-V curves at five irradiance levels between 200 and 1000 W/m². The extracted parameters were validated against indoor flasher measurements performed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences test facility. Mean absolute error in predicted short-circuit current was below 1.4% across all tested modules. The model was subsequently used to construct a bypass-diode-aware string model capable of reproducing the multiple local maxima that appear under partial shading. Simulated power–voltage curves for a six-module string with one module shaded to 40% irradiance showed three distinct local maxima, consistent with experimental hardware measurements. The approach provides a reproducible baseline for further MPPT algorithm studies.

title: Comparison of hill-climbing and incremental conductance MPPT methods for partially shaded residential PV arrays
abstract: Hill-climbing and incremental conductance are the two most widely deployed maximum power point tracking algorithms in residential inverter firmware, yet their comparative performance under partial shading—where the power–voltage characteristic exhibits multiple local maxima—is rarely quantified under identical, reproducible conditions. This study used a programmable four-channel solar array simulator to impose twelve predefined shading patterns on a simulated 8-panel string with bypass diodes. Each pattern was held steady for 60 seconds while both algorithms were run independently on a dSPACE rapid-prototyping controller. Hill-climbing converged to a local maximum in 7 of 12 patterns, losing between 6% and 23% of available power. Incremental conductance performed similarly in 5 of those cases. Tracking efficiency, defined as the ratio of extracted energy to theoretical maximum over the test window, averaged 81.3% for hill-climbing and 79.7% for incremental conductance under the shaded patterns, confirming that neither algorithm is reliable when multiple power peaks are present. The results motivate the adoption of global search strategies for rooftop arrays on complex geometries.

title: String-level I-V curve reconstruction for arbitrarily shaded roof sections using irradiance interpolation from sparse sensor networks
abstract: Monitoring partial shading on large rooftop PV installations typically requires more irradiance sensors than are economically justifiable. This paper proposes a method for reconstructing full string I-V curves using irradiance values interpolated from a sparse network of pyranometers, with interpolation performed by ordinary kriging on a two-dimensional roof plane. The method was tested on a 24-panel, four-string installation on an industrial building in Zrenjanin monitored from April to September 2017. The roof carried eight sensors; simulated reconstructions used subsets of two, four, and six sensors. With six sensors, mean relative error in predicted string maximum power was 3.1% over 4,800 ten-minute intervals. Reducing to two sensors raised error to 9.4%, which was judged insufficient for diagnostic purposes. The kriging approach outperformed inverse-distance weighting interpolation by an average of 1.8 percentage points across all sensor-count scenarios. The paper also reports that east-facing roof sections exhibited a distinct afternoon mismatch signature that was recoverable from the six-sensor configuration but not from two sensors.

title: Particle swarm optimisation as a global MPPT algorithm for multi-string PV systems: implementation on a low-cost microcontroller
abstract: Global maximum power point tracking algorithms based on population-based search avoid the local-maximum trapping that affects gradient methods, but their computational requirements have historically limited deployment on embedded hardware. This paper presents an implementation of particle swarm optimisation (PSO) adapted for real-time MPPT on a 120 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller with 256 kB RAM. The swarm size was reduced to six particles without significant accuracy loss by analysing the expected number of local maxima as a function of string length and bypass diode configuration. Tracking experiments using a solar array simulator confirmed global maximum capture in 43 of 45 shading scenarios; the two failures occurred under patterns producing nearly equal-height adjacent peaks separated by less than 2 V. Average tracking time to steady state was 1.8 seconds, and steady-state oscillation was limited to ±0.4 W on a 1 kW simulated string. Power consumption of the microcontroller circuit was 340 mW, acceptable for the intended residential inverter application. The firmware is described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Effect of roof pitch and azimuth distribution on annual mismatch losses in residential PV installations in Vojvodina
abstract: Residential rooftops in Vojvodina commonly present multiple surfaces with different pitches and azimuths, forcing installers to split panels across orientations or accept significant mismatch penalties. This study quantified annual mismatch losses for 72 geometrically distinct roof configurations using one year of measured hourly global horizontal and diffuse irradiance data from Novi Sad, combined with the transposition model of Perez et al. applied at a 10-minute resolution. For each configuration, string layouts were evaluated with and without module-level power electronics. Results show that single-string wiring across two roof faces with a 90° azimuth difference produces median annual mismatch losses of 8.3% relative to optimally configured installations. Adding module-level DC optimisers reduced this figure to 1.9%. Configurations with three or more roof orientations saw median losses exceeding 14% without optimisers. The paper provides tabulated loss estimates for the 12 most common roof geometries in the region, intended as a reference for local installers and energy auditors.

title: Transient I-V curve tracing under moving cloud shadows: measurement methodology and simulation accuracy assessment
abstract: Most I-V curve simulation studies assume steady-state irradiance conditions, but moving cloud shadow fronts produce transient irradiance gradients that alter string behaviour on timescales of one to ten seconds. This paper describes a synchronised measurement setup combining a 12-bit I-V curve tracer with a 10 Hz sampling pyranometer array mounted at module corners, deployed on a 6-module string at the Faculty of Technical Sciences rooftop station during summer 2022. Forty-seven shadow transit events were captured. During transients, instantaneous string power deviated from the steady-state model prediction by up to 17%, with the largest deviations occurring when the shadow front bisected a single module. A dynamic string model incorporating capacitive effects of the module laminate reduced the mean deviation from 9.1% to 3.6% across all events. The paper discusses the practical implication that MPPT benchmarking performed exclusively with static shading patterns may overestimate real-world tracking efficiency by several percentage points.

title: Benchmarking six global MPPT algorithms on a hardware-in-the-loop platform with real-sky irradiance sequences
abstract: A persistent difficulty in comparing global MPPT algorithms is the inconsistency of test conditions across publications—different hardware platforms, shading patterns, and performance metrics make results incomparable. This paper introduces a hardware-in-the-loop benchmarking platform in which a programmable solar array simulator replays 48-hour irradiance sequences recorded from the Faculty rooftop station, ensuring identical input conditions for all algorithms under test. Six algorithms were evaluated: particle swarm optimisation, grey wolf optimiser, firefly algorithm, a divide-and-conquer sweep, variable-step hill-climbing, and a look-up-table method pre-trained on historical shading data. Metrics reported include tracking efficiency, convergence time, steady-state ripple, and energy lost during re-tracking after cloud events. The look-up-table method achieved the highest average tracking efficiency (96.8%) but performed poorly on shading patterns absent from its training set, dropping to 88.1%. PSO and grey wolf optimiser achieved 95.2% and 94.7% respectively with more consistent behaviour across all sequences. Ripple and convergence results are reported in full for all six algorithms.

title: Finite-Element-Calibrated Torque-Sharing Functions for an 8/6 Switched Reluctance Motor: Design, Implementation and Bench Validation
abstract: Torque-sharing functions (TSFs) distribute the instantaneous torque demand among the phases of a switched reluctance motor as a function of rotor position. Classical sinusoidal and cubic TSFs ignore the nonlinear and position-dependent torque-current relationship of real machines, leading to current references that are difficult to track and that increase copper losses. This paper derives TSFs directly from the nonlinear static torque surface of an 8/6 SRM rated at 7.5 kW, obtained by FE simulation calibrated with locked-rotor torque measurements at 24 operating points. Optimal overlap angles between incoming and outgoing phase contributions are determined by minimising a cost function combining torque-ripple coefficient and RMS phase current. The resulting TSFs were implemented as two-dimensional look-up tables on a dSPACE MicroLabBox and tested at shaft loads from 10 Nm to 55 Nm and speeds from 300 rpm to 1800 rpm. Torque-ripple coefficient dropped from a baseline of 74% under simple single-pulse operation to below 18% across the central operating region, with copper losses increasing by at most 9% relative to the single-pulse baseline at matched mean torque.
venue: IET Electric Power Applications

title: A Lumped-Parameter Digital Twin Architecture for Continuous Dielectric Ageing State Estimation in Buried 110 kV Cable Circuits
abstract: This paper proposes a digital twin structure for a 110 kV underground cable circuit composed of modular lumped-parameter elements representing discrete cable sections, joints, and terminations. Each element maintains a state vector encompassing conductor temperature, insulation loss factor, estimated void volume fraction, and a cumulative ageing index derived from an Arrhenius-based thermal ageing model. The twin is updated at 15-minute intervals using SCADA-sourced load current and soil temperature sensor readings from five measurement points distributed over a 4.2 km cable route in northern Serbia. Over a 14-month monitoring period, the predicted cumulative ageing index showed a mean absolute error of 4.1% against offline tan-delta measurements taken at four scheduled outages. Computational runtime per update cycle averaged 0.8 seconds on a standard workstation, making the approach suitable for real-time deployment. The paper also describes the data pipeline, sensor calibration procedure, and a rule-based alarm threshold scheme derived from IEC 60840 service guidelines.

title: Convolutional Neural Network Classification of Phase-Resolved Partial Discharge Patterns in XLPE Cable Joints Under Variable Humidity
abstract: Phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) patterns were collected from 15 artificially defective XLPE cable joint specimens maintained in a climate chamber at relative humidity levels of 30%, 60%, and 90% during 50 Hz AC voltage application at 1.2U0. Four defect types were introduced: metallic protrusion on the conductor screen, air void in the insulation bulk, delamination at the inner screen interface, and moisture contamination at the joint body. A total of 4 800 PRPD maps of resolution 360 × 128 pixels were assembled and split 70/15/15 for training, validation, and test sets. A convolutional neural network with five convolutional layers and batch normalisation was trained for 80 epochs with early stopping. Overall test accuracy reached 93.2%. Confusion analysis revealed that moisture contamination patterns were most frequently misclassified as delamination defects at 90% relative humidity, with a confusion rate of 11%. The humidity effect on discharge inception voltage was quantified separately, showing a 6–9% reduction at 90% RH compared with 30% RH across all defect types.

title: Polyploid series in Campanula secundiflora agg. (Campanulaceae) in the Dinaric Alps: chromosome counts and genome size variation
abstract: The Campanula secundiflora aggregate comprises morphologically cryptic taxa distributed across the Dinaric limestone karst. We sampled 42 populations from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and northwestern Serbia and combined standard chromosome counts with flow cytometric genome size estimation to resolve ploidy levels. We identified diploid (2n = 34), tetraploid (2n = 68), and hexaploid (2n = 102) cytotypes, with tetraploids being the most widespread. Genome size per monoploid unit (Cx value) showed significant variation between ploidy levels: 1.81 pg in diploids, 1.76 pg in tetraploids, and 1.68 pg in hexaploids, suggesting genome downsizing with increasing ploidy. Mixed-ploidy populations were found at two contact zones. The results support the hypothesis of independent autopolyploidisation events across the range, with possible allopolyploid origin in the hexaploid cytotype.

title: Characterisation of a centromeric satellite DNA family in Seseli pallasii (Apiaceae)
abstract: A tandemly repeated satellite DNA family, designated SpaeSat1, was isolated and characterised from Seseli pallasii, a steppe endemic of the Pannonian–Pontic region. Genomic library screening and restriction digestion revealed a monomer unit of 171 bp with an AT content of 63.2%. Southern blotting showed that SpaeSat1 constitutes approximately 4.8% of the haploid genome. Fluorescence in situ hybridisation on mitotic chromosomes localised SpaeSat1 signals to centromeric regions of all nine chromosome pairs. Sequence analysis of 38 cloned monomers indicated homogenisation consistent with concerted evolution, with intermonomer similarity averaging 94.7%. Comparison with published satellite sequences from related Apiaceae genera revealed no significant homology, suggesting SpaeSat1 is lineage-specific. The repeat is proposed as a cytogenetic marker for the genus. This is the first satellite DNA characterised in the genus Seseli.

title: Ribosomal DNA loci dynamics in polyploid Allium species of the Balkan-Anatolian distribution range
abstract: The number and chromosomal position of 35S and 5S rDNA loci were mapped by two-colour FISH in eleven Allium species with Balkan and Anatolian distributions, representing diploid, tetraploid, and hexaploid taxa. Species-specific numbers of 35S rDNA loci ranged from two to twelve per diploid complement, while 5S loci ranged from two to eight. In polyploids, the total locus number was generally subadditive compared to expectations from diploid progenitors, indicating locus elimination after polyploidisation. Physical mapping showed that 35S and 5S loci were consistently non-syntenic in all examined taxa. In Allium rhodopense (hexaploid), only four 35S loci were detected against an expected minimum of six, with signals of unequal intensity suggesting partial locus silencing. The data contribute to understanding rDNA evolution following polyploidisation in a cytogenetically diverse genus.

title: Genome size diversity in the genus Dianthus across the western Balkans: a flow cytometric survey
abstract: Flow cytometric genome size data are reported for 28 Dianthus taxa occurring in the western Balkans, including 19 endemic or sub-endemic species for which no prior estimates existed. Leaf tissue was analysed using propidium iodide staining with Raphanus sativus as the primary standard. 2C values ranged from 1.53 pg in D. dalmaticus to 4.38 pg in D. viscidus (tetraploid). Within diploid taxa (2n = 30), 2C values spanned a 1.7-fold range (1.53–2.61 pg), a relatively wide span indicating substantial genome size diversification at the diploid level. Polyploidy was confirmed or detected for seven taxa, including new tetraploid records for two morphologically defined species. Genome size showed no significant phylogeographic structure when mapped onto a published ITS phylogeny, suggesting multiple independent expansions and contractions. The survey provides a reference dataset for future molecular and ecological studies.

title: Physical mapping of transposable element families in the Balkan endemic Pančićia serbica (Asteraceae)
abstract: Pančićia serbica is a monotypic Balkan endemic confined to serpentine outcrops in southwestern Serbia and northern Kosovo. We characterised two families of Ty3/gypsy retrotransposons, designated PsGypsy1 and PsGypsy2, from an Illumina-sequenced genome survey library (20× coverage, paired-end 150 bp reads). Sequence clustering with RepeatExplorer identified PsGypsy1 as constituting 9.4% and PsGypsy2 as 3.1% of the genome. FISH mapping with probes derived from the reverse transcriptase domain of each family produced distinct pericentromeric signals on most of the 18 chromosome pairs for PsGypsy1, and scattered interstitial signals for PsGypsy2. Phylogenetic analysis of reverse transcriptase sequences placed both families within different lineages of the Athila superfamily. This is the first genomic characterisation of repetitive elements in this genus, and the results provide insights into repeat landscape evolution in a species with a highly restricted distribution.

title: Cytogenetic differentiation between autopolyploid and allopolyploid cytotypes in Knautia drymeia s.l. (Caprifoliaceae)
abstract: Knautia drymeia sensu lato encompasses diploid and polyploid populations across the Balkans and Carpathians. We applied genomic in situ hybridisation (GISH) and multicolour FISH with 35S and 5S rDNA probes to determine the hybrid or autoploid origin of tetraploid populations sampled from 18 sites in Serbia, Romania, and Hungary. In populations from the Fruška Gora and southern Carpathians, GISH using labelled genomic DNA of K. albanica as probe produced signals on approximately half the chromosomes, indicating allopolyploid contribution. In contrast, populations from the Vojvodina foothills showed uniform GISH signal distribution consistent with autopolyploidy. The number of 35S rDNA loci differed between the two polyploid types: four loci in putative autopolyploids versus six in allopolyploids. These findings suggest that morphologically similar tetraploid plants in K. drymeia s.l. have at least two independent cytogenetic origins within the study area.

title: Chromosome morphology and fluorescent banding in selected serpentine endemics of southeastern Serbia
abstract: Serpentine soils in southeastern Serbia harbour several narrowly endemic plant species whose cytogenetic data are largely unknown. We present karyotype analyses, CMA3/DAPI fluorescent banding, and genome size estimates for six species: Cerastium perplexum, Minuartia baldaccii subsp. doerfleri, Alyssum smolikanum, Viola eximia, Potentilla haynaldiana, and Linum elegans. Chromosome numbers confirmed previously published counts for three species and provided new records for the remaining three, including first counts for V. eximia (2n = 20) and L. elegans (2n = 18). CMA3-positive bands were detected at secondary constrictions in all species and additionally at subtelomeric positions in Alyssum smolikanum. Genome sizes ranged from 0.94 pg (2C) in M. baldaccii subsp. doerfleri to 4.18 pg in P. haynaldiana. The data collectively suggest that chromosome numbers and karyotype organisation are relatively conserved within these phylogenetically diverse serpentine specialists.

title: Repetitive DNA landscape of the Balkan endemic Ramonda serbica (Gesneriaceae) inferred from low-coverage genome sequencing
abstract: Ramonda serbica is one of only three European desiccation-tolerant angiosperms and a recognised Balkan relict endemic. We characterised its repetitive DNA complement using graph-based clustering of Illumina reads (25× coverage) with the RepeatExplorer2 pipeline. Repetitive elements accounted for approximately 47.3% of the estimated genome (2C = 3.65 pg). The most abundant repeat class was Ty3/gypsy retrotransposons (22.1% of reads), followed by Ty1/copia elements (11.4%) and tandem repeats (8.8%). The dominant satellite DNA family, RsSat1 (monomer 178 bp, AT content 58.3%), was localised by FISH to pericentromeric regions of five of the twelve chromosome pairs. Comparison with the related and co-occurring R. nathaliae revealed generally similar proportions of major repeat categories but diverged satellite DNA sequences, suggesting lineage-specific satellite turnover after speciation. This dataset constitutes the most comprehensive genomic repeat characterisation available for either Ramonda species.

title: Ploidy variation and morphological differentiation in the Sesleria caerulea complex along an altitudinal gradient in the Prokletije Mountains
abstract: The Sesleria caerulea species complex (Poaceae) in the Prokletije Mountains spans an altitudinal range from 900 m to 2,430 m a.s.l. and shows considerable morphological variability. We sampled 31 populations across this gradient, measured 14 morphological traits, and estimated ploidy by flow cytometry. Three ploidy levels were detected: diploid (2n = 2x = 26, six populations), tetraploid (2n = 4x = 52, twenty-one populations), and hexaploid (2n = 6x = 78, four populations). Diploids were restricted to low-altitude calcareous grasslands, whereas hexaploids occurred exclusively above 2,100 m. Tetraploids showed the broadest ecological and morphological amplitude. Morphological differentiation between ploidy levels was statistically significant for ligule length, culm width, and spikelet density, but extensive morphological overlap renders ploidy identification by morphology unreliable. Contact zones between diploids and tetraploids were identified at two localities; no mixed-ploidy individuals were detected by flow cytometry.

title: Heterochromatin composition and karyotype asymmetry in tetraploid Onosma species (Boraginaceae) from the Balkan hotspot
abstract: Onosma (Boraginaceae) is one of the most species-rich genera in the Balkans, yet cytogenetic data remain sparse. We present karyotypes, CMA3/DAPI banding, and FISH with 35S and 5S rDNA probes for seven tetraploid Onosma species from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria (2n = 4x = 40 throughout). CMA3-positive bands occurred in a consistent pericentromeric pattern in O. visianii and O. pseudoarenaria, while O. javorkae showed additional bright subtelomeric CMA3 signals at two chromosome pairs. FISH revealed two 35S rDNA loci in four species and four loci in three species; 5S rDNA loci numbered two in all taxa. Karyotype asymmetry measured by the MCA index ranged from 0.38 (O. stellulata) to 0.61 (O. thracica), with asymmetry positively correlated with genome size (Spearman ρ = 0.74, p = 0.048). The results support the utility of fluorescent banding and rDNA FISH in discriminating morphologically similar species within this taxonomically difficult genus.

title: Утицај поплавног режима на концентрацију алелохемикала у ризосфери Fallopia japonica у рипаријалним стаништима Тисе
abstract: На три локалитета дуж Тисе (Кањижа, Бечеј, Titel) праћене су концентрације ресвератрола, емодина и феруличне киселине у ризосфери Fallopia japonica у периодима поплаве, оседања воде и суше током 2019–2020. године. Узорковање земљишне воде обављено је лизиметарским цевима на дубини 20 и 40 cm. HPLC-DAD анализа показала је да су концентрације свих три алелохемикала биле значајно ниже за време поплаве него у периоду суше (p < 0,01 за сва три једињења и оба нивоа дубине). Феруличка киселина на 20 cm дубине у периоду суше достигла је 0,34 µg mL⁻¹, насупрот 0,06 µg mL⁻¹ током поплаве. Резултати указују да хидролошки режим у значајној мери модулира биорасположивост алелохемикала у рипаријалним стаништима, са импликацијама за тумачење поплавима условљеног прекида инвазивне супресије домаће вегетације.

title: Two-Year Airborne Pollen Record from a Burkard Trap Station in Central Novi Sad: Taxon Composition and Seasonal Trends
abstract: Continuous volumetric sampling of airborne pollen was conducted at a rooftop Burkard 7-day spore trap station positioned at 12 m height in central Novi Sad from January 2022 through December 2023. Weekly tape sections were prepared by standard glycerine-jelly mounting and counts performed along two longitudinal traverses per day-section at 400× magnification. Over the two-year period, 48 pollen types were identified. Poaceae contributed 31% of total annual pollen load in both years, followed by Corylus (14%), Betula-type (11%), and Artemisia (9%). The main pollen season for grasses began on average on 5 May and lasted 68 days. Correlation with meteorological data from a co-located weather station showed that daily maximum temperature and wind speed from the southwest explained 58% of daily Poaceae pollen variance (multiple regression, R² = 0.58, p < 0.001). Inter-annual differences in Betula-type pollen peak were 12 days, consistent with the warm spring of 2023.

title: English commercial terms in Serbian merchant ledgers from Sremski Karlovci, 1740–1780
abstract: This study examines a corpus of 47 merchant ledgers held at the Archive of Vojvodina, dating from 1740 to 1780, in search of lexical items with traceable English commercial origins. Using manual transcription and comparative dictionary analysis against Johnson's Dictionary and the Oxford English Dictionary historical entries, the paper identifies 38 candidate loanwords in domains of textile trade, weights and measures, and maritime insurance. Phonological adaptation patterns are analysed systematically: most items entered Serbian via German or Latin intermediary forms, showing characteristic vowel shifts and consonant cluster simplifications. The paper argues that direct English-to-Serbian transfer was negligible before 1780 and that Dutch served as an equally important conduit for mercantile vocabulary in the Danube trading zone. Frequency tables and attestation dates are provided for all 38 items.

title: Latin as intermediary: the route of English legal vocabulary into 18th-century Serbian administrative texts
abstract: Drawing on a digitised corpus of 112 administrative documents from the Patriarchate of Karlovci (1700–1760), this paper traces how English legal terms such as variants of 'testament', 'covenant', and 'petition' entered Serbian ecclesiastical administration through Latin scholarly and chancery writing rather than through direct contact. The methodology combines etymological tracing with collocation analysis performed using a custom concordance tool developed at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad. Nineteen lexical entries are reconstructed from their probable English or Anglo-Latin origin through documented Latin intermediary forms to their attested Serbian orthographic variants. The paper contributes a preliminary lemma list of 19 items with full attestation histories, suitable for inclusion in a future historical dictionary of Serbian administrative vocabulary. Implications for periodisation of Serbian lexical modernisation are discussed.

title: Orthographic variation in borrowed administrative terms in Serbian documents of the Vojvodina region, 1720–1790
abstract: This paper presents a quantitative analysis of orthographic variation affecting 54 loanwords of Western European origin in a corpus of 230 Serbian administrative texts spanning 1720 to 1790, sourced from five archival collections in Vojvodina. For each item, all attested spellings are catalogued and variation indices are calculated. The analysis distinguishes between scribe-induced variation, regional convention, and temporal drift toward standardisation. Items of probable English or Dutch commercial origin show higher variation indices than Latin administrative terms, suggesting weaker normative pressure on non-Latin borrowings at this period. The paper also tests whether scribal training background, inferred from paleographic evidence, correlates with lower variation scores; a modest positive correlation (r = 0.41) is found for scribes trained in Viennese institutions. Data tables covering all 54 items are included as an appendix.

title: Textile trade vocabulary of English origin in Serbian guild records of the 18th century
abstract: Guild records from tailors', drapers', and wool merchants' associations in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zemun for the period 1730–1800 are examined for vocabulary items denoting cloth types, measurements, and trading practices. A corpus of 89 guild documents was transcribed and annotated for part of speech and semantic domain. Twenty-two terms with probable English or Anglo-Dutch textile trade origins were identified, including adapted forms corresponding to broadcloth, serge, and yard. For each term, the paper provides the earliest Serbian attestation date, the likely source language and intermediary, the semantic range in context, and modern Serbian descendants or cognates where traceable. The study also notes eleven terms that resist confident attribution and flags them for future archival investigation. The findings support a model of diffuse, multi-channel borrowing rather than a single traceable trade contact.

title: Towards a historical dictionary of Western European loanwords in Serbian administrative language, 1700–1800: scope, methodology, and sample entries
abstract: This chapter outlines the conceptual and methodological framework for a projected historical dictionary covering Western European loanwords—primarily of English, Dutch, French, and Italian origin—attested in Serbian administrative and commercial writing during the eighteenth century. The chapter defines the target corpus (estimated at over 400 documents held across six archives in Serbia and Austria), the editorial conventions for lemmatisation, the classification scheme for source languages and intermediaries, and the structure of dictionary entries, which include attestation timeline, morphological variants, semantic glosses in Serbian and English, and cross-references. Fifteen sample entries illustrating different borrowing scenarios are presented in full. The chapter concludes by discussing analogous historical dictionary projects in Hungarian and Croatian lexicography, drawing methodological comparisons and identifying practical lessons for the Serbian case.
venue: Historical Lexicography of the Danube Region: Methods and Case Studies, edited volume, University of Pécs Press

title: Habsburg administrative formulas and their English-origin lexical components in Serbian land registry documents
abstract: Land registry documents (urbarial records and cadastral surveys) issued by Habsburg authorities in Vojvodina between 1760 and 1790 are examined for fixed administrative formulas that contain lexical items of demonstrable or probable English origin. A set of 67 documents from the State Archive of Novi Sad was transcribed and parsed into formulaic units. Eight recurring formulas were identified that incorporate adapted English commercial or legal terms, most frequently in contexts of property valuation, surveying measures, and title transfer. The paper argues that these formulas were borrowed as entire units from German-language model documents that themselves drew on Dutch and English mercantile legal conventions. The analysis provides a counterpoint to word-by-word borrowing models and highlights the role of documentary genre transfer in shaping administrative vocabulary.

title: Digitising the Vojvodina chancery corpus: practical decisions in OCR correction and TEI annotation for historical Serbian texts
abstract: This paper reports on the digitisation workflow developed for a corpus of 185 eighteenth-century Serbian chancery documents as part of preparatory work for a planned historical dictionary. The documents, written in a mixed Cyrillic-Latin script with frequent abbreviations and interlinear glosses, posed specific challenges for optical character recognition. The paper describes the two-pass manual correction protocol adopted, the inter-annotator agreement scores achieved (overall kappa 0.83), and the TEI XML tagset selected to encode lemma forms, language-of-origin tags, and scribal hands. Issues of encoding policy for uncertain attributions and for words straddling two language systems are discussed in detail. The paper also presents basic corpus statistics: 185 documents, approximately 94,000 tokens, 1,240 unique lemmas flagged as probable loanwords. The corpus is being prepared for restricted-access deposit with the CLARIN.SI repository.

title: English nautical vocabulary in inland Serbian administrative texts: attestations and their commercial context
abstract: Despite Serbia's landlocked geography, several nautical terms of English or Dutch-English origin appear in Serbian administrative texts dealing with Danube river trade from the 1750s onward. This paper examines 14 such terms attested in a corpus of 43 river trade contracts and customs declarations held at the Archive of Vojvodina. For each term, the paper reconstructs the probable borrowing chain, citing parallel attestations in German, Hungarian, and Romanian administrative texts of the same period. The semantic narrowing or broadening that occurred during adaptation is documented: several terms shifted from sea-going to river-going contexts, and two items were repurposed entirely for land transport. The paper argues that the Danube served not merely as a trade route but as a lexical corridor, channelling maritime vocabulary from North Sea commercial centres into Central European administrative writing.

title: Comparative borrowing paths: English loanwords in 18th-century Serbian versus Croatian administrative registers
abstract: This comparative study aligns evidence from Serbian and Croatian administrative corpora to assess whether English and Dutch commercial vocabulary followed the same borrowing routes and adaptation patterns in both languages during the eighteenth century. The Serbian dataset comprises 94,000 tokens from the Vojvodina chancery corpus; the Croatian dataset of approximately 78,000 tokens was provided by a collaborating team at the University of Zagreb. Automated lemma alignment was performed using an adapted Levenshtein-distance script, followed by manual verification. Of 58 candidate loanwords examined, 31 appear in both corpora with cognate forms, 14 appear only in Serbian, and 13 only in Croatian. Divergences in phonological adaptation are tabulated and explained by reference to differing German and Latin intermediary traditions in the two administrative cultures. The results suggest that Habsburg administrative unity produced lexical convergence in legal domains but not in commercial ones.

title: Scribal networks and vocabulary diffusion: evidence from colophons in Serbian administrative manuscripts, 1750–1800
abstract: Colophons in Serbian administrative manuscripts sometimes identify the scribe, his training location, and his institutional affiliation, providing rare individual-level data for the study of vocabulary diffusion. This paper catalogues 61 colophons from the Vojvodina chancery corpus and cross-references the named scribes with records in the Archive of the Serbian Orthodox Church to reconstruct partial career trajectories for 19 individuals. Vocabulary profiles derived from each scribe's documents are compared to assess whether scribes trained in Vienna or Bratislava used higher proportions of Western European loanwords than those trained locally. A chi-square test on loanword-to-total-lemma ratios across the two training groups yields a statistically significant difference (p = 0.03). The paper discusses the implications for understanding how individual mobility transmitted lexical innovation in pre-standardisation Serbian.

title: Annotated glossary of English-origin administrative terms in Serbian texts, 1700–1800: first instalment (A–K)
abstract: This preprint releases the first instalment of an annotated historical glossary covering loanwords of English or Anglo-Dutch origin attested in Serbian administrative writing between 1700 and 1800. The instalment covers lemmas beginning with A through K, comprising 94 entries. Each entry provides: the headword in standardised modern Serbian orthography; all attested historical spellings with source document references; proposed etymon with intermediary language chain; earliest and latest attestation dates; semantic definition in Serbian and English; and notes on subsequent lexical history. Entries are drawn from the Vojvodina chancery corpus and supplemented by material from the Archive of the Serbian Orthodox Church in Sremski Karlovci. The glossary is intended as a working document and will be revised in response to community feedback before print publication. A companion dataset in TSV format is appended.

title: Measuring semantic drift in administrative loanwords: a diachronic collocational study of Serbian chancery texts, 1700–1800
abstract: This paper applies diachronic collocational analysis to 27 Western European loanwords in the Vojvodina chancery corpus, dividing the century into four 25-year periods and computing pointwise mutual information scores for the top ten collocates of each item per period. The aim is to detect semantic drift—changes in the range and character of collocates that indicate shifts in conceptual domain or register. Results show that 11 of the 27 terms exhibit measurable collocational change across periods, with six showing broadening and five showing narrowing. Three terms show abrupt collocational restructuring concentrated in the 1760s, coinciding with Josephine administrative reforms. The methodology, adapted from computational historical semantics, is applied here to a small specialised corpus (94,000 tokens), and the paper reflects on the statistical limitations of such an approach and the interpretive adjustments required.

title: Epistemic Modal Verbs in Serbian Researchers' English Abstracts: A Corpus Study
abstract: This study examines the frequency and distribution of epistemic modal verbs in a 120,000-word corpus of English-language abstracts written by Serbian researchers across four disciplines: linguistics, chemistry, civil engineering, and economics. Abstracts were retrieved from journals indexed in Scopus between 2000 and 2009. Frequency counts and concordance analysis were performed using AntConc 3.2. Results show that 'may' and 'could' account for 61% of all epistemic modal occurrences, with marked disciplinary asymmetry: linguistics abstracts favour 'might' at more than twice the rate found in engineering abstracts. Compared to a reference corpus of abstracts by British academics drawn from the same journals, Serbian authors use epistemic modals at a significantly lower overall rate (4.2 per thousand words vs. 6.8), suggesting a preference for more assertive propositional framing. The paper discusses pedagogical implications for academic writing instruction in EFL university contexts.

title: Stance Adverbials in Serbian Academic English: Frequency and Placement Patterns
abstract: This corpus study investigates stance adverbials—items such as 'clearly', 'apparently', 'presumably', and 'arguably'—in a 400,000-word corpus of research articles written in English by Serbian academics published between 2005 and 2011. The corpus spans six disciplines. Frequency, syntactic position (sentence-initial, mid-clause, sentence-final), and co-occurrence with hedging devices were coded manually for a stratified 80,000-word subcorpus and automatically for the remainder using a Python-based tagger. Serbian academics use stance adverbials at roughly 70% of the rate observed in a matched native-speaker reference corpus, and sentence-initial placement is proportionally over-represented. Boosting adverbials ('clearly', 'obviously') outnumber epistemic ones across all disciplines, contrasting with patterns documented for British academic English. The findings have direct relevance to EAP curriculum design.

title: Cross-disciplinary Variation in Epistemic Stance: Linguistics vs. Electrical Engineering Research Articles by Serbian Authors
abstract: Comparing epistemic stance marking across disciplines with markedly different epistemological traditions, this study analyses 100 research articles (50 from linguistics, 50 from electrical engineering) authored by Serbian academics and published in English between 2008 and 2013. Combined corpus size is approximately 520,000 words. Stance markers were identified using a semi-automated procedure combining keyword lists with manual post-editing. Linguistics articles contain 2.3 times more hedges per thousand words than electrical engineering articles. However, electrical engineering texts show a higher ratio of boosters to hedges (0.68 vs. 0.31 in linguistics), suggesting that certainty framing is more normative in that discipline even among Serbian authors. The paper situates these findings within broader debates about the universality versus discipline-specificity of epistemic norms in academic writing.

title: Mapping Material Flow Complexity in Job-Shop Environments: A Modified VSM Approach
abstract: Standard value stream mapping was developed primarily for repetitive, single-product flows and loses precision when applied to job-shop settings where routing variability is high. This paper proposes a modified VSM procedure that segments product families by process similarity using production flow analysis, then constructs separate current-state maps for each cluster. The method was applied in a metalworking company with 47 active part numbers routed across 12 work centres. Mapping was conducted over four weeks using direct observation and ERP time-stamp extraction. Results identified seven distinct waste categories; the dominant waste was excessive work-in-process inventory accumulating before two bottleneck machining centres, accounting for 68% of total lead time. A future-state map with consolidated scheduling points reduced simulated lead time by 34%. The paper discusses practical constraints in maintaining multiple stream maps simultaneously and proposes a simplified visual management board adapted for the job-shop context.

title: SMED Implementation in a Low-Volume Stamping Cell: Quantitative Assessment of Internal-to-External Conversion
abstract: This study documents a structured SMED application in a stamping cell producing 31 different sheet-metal components for the agricultural equipment sector. Baseline changeover times were recorded via video analysis across 22 observed setups, yielding an average of 94 minutes with a standard deviation of 18 minutes. Activities were classified as internal or external using a time-coded observation sheet; 41% of recorded internal time was found convertible to external activities with no capital investment. A further 17% reduction was achieved by standardising tool-holding fixtures for the five highest-frequency part transitions. After a three-month implementation period, average changeover time fell to 52 minutes, a 45% reduction. Statistical process control charts confirmed the reduction was sustained over the subsequent six-month monitoring period. The paper discusses operator training time requirements, which averaged 6.5 hours per person, and resistance patterns observed during the transition phase.

title: Kanban Loop Sizing Under High Demand Variability: A Simulation Study for Multi-Product Job Shops
abstract: Determining appropriate kanban loop sizes in environments with highly variable demand is complicated by the interaction between replenishment cycle time, demand coefficient of variation, and the number of distinct part numbers sharing a work centre. This paper develops a discrete-event simulation model of a two-stage job-shop cell producing 18 part types with monthly demand coefficients of variation ranging from 0.28 to 1.14. Five kanban sizing formulas from the literature were tested against a simulated twelve-month demand trace derived from historical order data. Service level and average inventory were recorded for each formula across 30 simulation replications. The formula incorporating demand variance and machine utilisation as dual inputs achieved the best balance, maintaining a 96.4% service level at an average WIP inventory 22% lower than the next best alternative. Results suggest that single-parameter formulas commonly found in textbooks are inadequate for environments with product-mix coefficients of variation above 0.7.

title: Lean Transformation Readiness in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs: A Survey-Based Assessment
abstract: This paper presents findings from a structured survey of 64 manufacturing small and medium enterprises in the Vojvodina region, conducted to assess their current state of lean practice adoption, barriers to implementation, and organisational readiness factors. The questionnaire covered 38 items grouped into five categories: management commitment, workforce competence, process documentation quality, measurement systems, and supplier integration. Responses were collected in 2018 from production managers and quality managers. Cluster analysis identified three distinct readiness profiles. Firms in the lowest-readiness cluster, representing 41% of the sample, lacked standardised work documentation and had no formal loss-measurement systems. The highest-readiness cluster (17% of firms) had implemented 5S and some form of visual management but had not yet moved to pull-based scheduling. The paper maps observed barriers to specific intervention types and proposes a staged lean adoption roadmap calibrated to SME resource constraints.

title: Integrating SMED and Value Stream Mapping: A Combined Framework for Changeover-Driven Lead Time Reduction
abstract: Changeover time and batch-size policy interact strongly in job-shop environments: reducing changeover enables smaller batches, which in turn alters queue dynamics and lead times. This paper proposes a combined analysis framework in which VSM current-state data on batch sizes and queue lengths is used to prioritise which changeover operations to target with SMED, and SMED outcome estimates are fed back into future-state VSM projections. The framework was applied in a plastics processing facility with 23 injection moulding machines and 58 active mould tools. Starting from a baseline average lead time of 11.4 days, the analysis identified four mould families where combined changeover and batch-size intervention would yield the greatest lead-time reduction. After implementation, average lead time fell to 7.1 days over a six-month period. Batch sizes for the targeted families decreased by an average of 38% without increasing machine utilisation beyond 87%.

title: Doctoral Research Perspectives on Lean in High-Mix Manufacturing: A Structured Literature Review 2010–2020
abstract: This chapter reviews 112 peer-reviewed publications and 14 doctoral dissertations addressing lean manufacturing in high-mix, low-volume and job-shop contexts published between 2010 and 2020. The review is structured around four themes: value stream mapping adaptations, pull-system design under variability, changeover reduction methods, and performance measurement. Content analysis was performed using a coding scheme with 22 categories. Findings indicate that VSM adaptations account for 31% of the reviewed works, but fewer than half of these validate their proposed modifications with empirical data from production environments. Pull-system design papers increasingly rely on simulation rather than analytical models, reflecting the difficulty of closed-form solutions under variable routing. The chapter identifies three underexplored areas: multi-site lean coordination in SME networks, integration with ERP scheduling, and longitudinal studies tracking lean sustainability beyond 24 months. A research agenda is proposed for each gap.

title: Operator Time Allocation During Changeover: A Workload Balancing Model for Multi-Machine SMED Programmes
abstract: When SMED is applied across several machines in the same cell, operator availability during setup becomes a shared constraint that standard SMED analysis ignores. This paper formulates a workload balancing model that, given a set of partially overlapping changeover activity sequences and a fixed operator team size, determines which external activities can be parallelised and how operators should be assigned to minimise total changeover duration. The model is formulated as a mixed-integer programme and solved for instances with up to 8 machines and 4 operators using a commercial solver within acceptable time limits. The model was validated against observed data from a machining cell with 6 CNC turning centres. Compared with the current operator assignment practice, the optimised schedule reduced average multi-machine changeover duration from 78 to 59 minutes. Sensitivity analysis shows that adding a third operator yields diminishing returns when machine count exceeds five.

title: Pull System Design for a Mixed-Model Assembly Line with Sequence-Dependent Changeovers
abstract: This paper examines pull-system design in a mixed-model assembly line where the time required to transition between consecutive model variants depends on the specific pair being sequenced. Sequence-dependent setup times break the standard kanban replenishment logic, since production cycle times vary with the production sequence and are not fixed a priori. A two-phase design procedure is proposed: first, a sequencing heuristic minimises expected total setup time for a given demand mix; second, kanban quantities are computed using a modified formula that incorporates the sequence-adjusted average cycle time. The procedure was applied to a small-appliance assembly line with 14 model variants and setup times ranging from 4 to 31 minutes. Over a 90-day pilot, average WIP inventory decreased by 29% and the proportion of tardy orders fell from 14% to 6% compared with the prior push-scheduling baseline.

title: Sustained Lean Performance in Job Shops: A Longitudinal Case Study Over 36 Months
abstract: Sustained improvement after lean implementation is less studied than the implementation phase itself. This paper reports a 36-month longitudinal case study of a precision parts manufacturer that completed a lean transformation programme in early 2021. Performance indicators including lead time, on-time delivery, WIP inventory value, and changeover frequency were tracked monthly. After an initial improvement phase lasting approximately eight months, lead time and WIP stabilised at values 31% and 27% below the pre-transformation baseline respectively. However, on-time delivery performance declined modestly between months 18 and 26, coinciding with a 35% increase in active part numbers following a new customer contract. Interviews with production staff and supervisors identified three mechanisms contributing to partial backsliding: dilution of lean knowledge following staff turnover, incomplete updating of kanban parameters after product-mix changes, and reduced management attention after the initial programme closed. Corrective interventions applied in month 27 restored performance within four months.
venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Operations Management

title: Takt Time Calculation Under Intermittent Demand: Implications for Pull-System Pacemaker Placement in Job Shops
abstract: Takt time is a foundational parameter in lean system design, but its standard formulation assumes stable, continuous demand. In job shops with intermittent customer orders and irregular demand patterns, naive takt-time calculations lead to either over-production or chronic capacity shortfalls at the pacemaker. This paper analyses historical order data from three job-shop companies over 24-month periods, characterising demand interarrival distributions by part family. Using these empirical distributions, a demand-smoothing procedure based on rolling horizon aggregation is proposed to compute a robust effective takt time for pacemaker scheduling. Simulation experiments show that the proposed procedure reduces pacemaker queue overflow events by between 41% and 57% compared with standard takt-time calculation across the three companies. The paper also discusses the trade-off between smoothing window length and responsiveness to genuine demand trend shifts.

title: Criteria for Judicial Assessment of Non-Pecuniary Damages in Serbian Case Law: An Empirical Overview
abstract: This article examines how Serbian courts apply the criteria set out in Article 200 of the Law of Obligations when assessing non-pecuniary damages for personality rights violations. The study is based on a systematic review of 214 first-instance and appellate court decisions issued between 2015 and 2022, retrieved from the Official Gazette jurisprudence database and the Supreme Court of Cassation portal. Cases were coded according to the type of personality right infringed, the category of harm claimed, the awarded sum, and the reasoning provided by the court. Results indicate significant inter-court variability in awarded amounts for comparable injury types, with awards for impaired reputation ranging from approximately 50,000 to 400,000 Serbian dinars in factually similar cases. The analysis finds that courts rarely articulate explicit weighting of individual statutory criteria, and that references to comparative awards from other decisions are inconsistent. The article argues that greater transparency in judicial reasoning would improve predictability and serve the compensatory function of damages more effectively.

title: Compensation for Violation of the Right to Privacy in the Digital Environment: Serbian Law in Comparative Perspective
abstract: The article considers how Serbian tort law addresses non-pecuniary harm resulting from online privacy violations, particularly the unauthorised disclosure of personal data and the non-consensual publication of images. It proceeds in three parts. The first part outlines the relevant provisions of the Law of Obligations and the Personal Data Protection Act of 2018, identifying points of potential overlap and divergence between tort and data protection remedies. The second part presents a comparative analysis of Croatian and Austrian approaches to damages for privacy breaches in digital contexts, drawing on legislative texts and selected case law. The third part evaluates ten Serbian appellate decisions from 2019 to 2023 involving online privacy claims, focusing on the courts' treatment of causation and quantum. The study finds that Serbian courts have largely applied traditional tort categories without adapting their reasoning to the specific characteristics of digital harm, resulting in undercompensation in several identifiable case types. Adjustments to judicial methodology, rather than legislative reform, are proposed as the more immediate remedy.

title: Defamation and Damage Awards in Serbia: Between Tort Law and Media Legislation
abstract: This conference paper addresses the relationship between civil liability for defamation under general tort law and the specific damage provisions of the Serbian Public Information and Media Act. The paper focuses on cases in which plaintiffs have pursued parallel or alternative claims under both regimes, examining five published court decisions from 2017 to 2022. It considers whether the statutory caps and presumptions introduced by the Media Act effectively displace or merely supplement the general tort framework, and whether courts have articulated a consistent position on this question. The paper also briefly compares the Serbian situation with the approach taken in Montenegrin media legislation, where the interaction between the two regimes has been addressed more explicitly in statute. The central finding is that Serbian courts have treated the two regimes as largely independent, occasionally producing outcomes that appear inconsistent across similar cases. The paper was presented at the Regional Conference on Media Law and Civil Liability held in Novi Sad in 2023.

title: Combining Bagging and Cost-Sensitive Weighting for Imbalanced Binary Classification on Network Intrusion Data
abstract: This paper addresses binary classification in a network intrusion dataset containing approximately 490 000 connection records with a positive-class rate of 0.8%. Three ensemble strategies—standard bagging, balanced bagging with undersampling, and cost-sensitive bagging with an asymmetric misclassification penalty—are evaluated using a stratified 10-fold cross-validation protocol. Classifiers are decision trees with Gini splitting and maximum depth of ten. Performance is measured with the area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC), geometric mean (G-mean), and F1 score. Cost-sensitive bagging achieves AUPRC of 0.81 and G-mean of 0.79, outperforming standard bagging (0.61 and 0.67) and balanced bagging (0.74 and 0.75). Feature importance rankings are stable across folds, with packet-rate and inter-arrival-time features consistently ranked highest. The study confirms that cost-sensitive weighting is more effective than random undersampling alone for this density regime.

title: Threshold Selection Strategies for Anomaly Scorers: An Empirical Study on Six Industrial Sensor Datasets
abstract: Anomaly detectors trained on imbalanced tabular data typically produce continuous scores that require a decision threshold to yield binary predictions. This study systematically compares seven threshold selection strategies—fixed percentile, maximum F1, maximum G-mean, precision–recall breakeven, expected cost minimisation at three cost ratios, and Youden's J—across six industrial sensor datasets ranging from 12 to 89 features and imbalance ratios from 1:30 to 1:420. The base scorer in all experiments is an isolation forest with 200 trees. Threshold selection is performed on a held-out calibration set representing 15% of available labelled data. Results show that expected cost minimisation with an asymmetric penalty of 10:1 yields the best F1 on five of six datasets, whereas Youden's J performs poorly at extreme imbalance. Cross-dataset variance is high, motivating dataset-specific calibration rather than universal rules.
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (ICSI)

title: SMOTE Placement Relative to Feature Scaling in Ensemble Pipelines: Order Effects on Precision–Recall Performance
abstract: Preprocessing pipelines for imbalanced tabular data often apply SMOTE oversampling and z-score standardisation without clear guidance on their relative order. This paper presents a controlled experiment on eight UCI-style tabular datasets with imbalance ratios between 1:15 and 1:200. Four pipeline orderings are compared: no SMOTE, SMOTE before scaling, scaling before SMOTE, and SMOTE on already-encoded but unscaled data, each fed into a random forest of 500 trees with out-of-bag estimation. Results, evaluated by AUPRC and macro-averaged F1, show that applying standardisation before SMOTE consistently reduces intra-class variance of synthetic samples and improves AUPRC by 2–7 percentage points compared with the reverse order for datasets with high-variance continuous features. The effect is negligible for purely ordinal or binary feature spaces. Recommendations for pipeline construction are provided with supporting statistical tests using Wilcoxon signed-rank at α=0.05.
venue: Acta Polytechnica Hungarica

title: Gradient Boosted Trees with Asymmetric Loss for Fraud Detection in Retail Banking Transactions
abstract: Retail banking transaction records collected over 18 months from an anonymised Serbian bank contain 2.3 million entries, of which 0.11% are labelled fraudulent. A gradient boosted tree classifier using a custom asymmetric log-loss function, parameterised by a false-negative penalty weight ranging from 5 to 50, is compared against a standard cross-entropy gradient boosting baseline and a class-weight-adjusted logistic regression. Model performance is measured on a temporally separated test set of 230 000 transactions using AUPRC, recall at 5% false positive rate, and calibration error (ECE). The asymmetric loss model with penalty weight 20 achieves recall of 0.74 at 5% FPR versus 0.59 for the standard gradient boosting baseline. Feature engineering includes velocity features, merchant-category deviation scores, and day-of-week interaction terms. Calibration deteriorates at higher penalty weights, and isotonic regression post-hoc calibration partially restores reliability curves.

title: Detecting Anomalous User Behaviour in Enterprise Software Logs Using Random Forests with Class-Weighted Leaf Distributions
abstract: Enterprise application logs from a manufacturing ERP system contain timestamped action sequences for 1 240 users over 12 months. After aggregating per-user daily activity into 47 behavioural features—including action-type entropy, session duration statistics, and off-hours access frequency—labelled anomalies constitute 1.3% of user-day records. A random forest classifier with class-weighted leaf probability distributions is compared against one-class SVM and isolation forest in a leave-one-week-out evaluation. The random forest achieves AUPRC of 0.68 compared with 0.44 for isolation forest and 0.39 for one-class SVM, confirming the advantage of partial supervision when even a small number of positive labels is available. Feature importance analysis identifies off-hours access frequency and action-type entropy as the two strongest predictors. Temporal drift in feature distributions is documented across quarters and addressed with a sliding recalibration window of 30 days.

title: Evaluation Protocol Choices and Their Effect on Reported Performance in Imbalanced Classification Studies
abstract: A meta-analysis of 84 published papers on imbalanced classification identifies six protocol dimensions—train/test split strategy, metric selection, threshold choice, comparison baselines, statistical testing, and oversampling leakage—and records whether each paper follows recommended practice for each dimension. Only 11 of 84 papers correctly prevent SMOTE from being applied before cross-validation splitting, resulting in optimistically biased AUPRC estimates of 3 to 14 percentage points on average. Papers using G-mean as their sole metric are over-represented in the literature relative to those using AUPRC, and fewer than 30% apply any significance test. Concrete recommendations for reproducible evaluation are presented, accompanied by a checklist and a Python reference implementation applied to three datasets. The study does not introduce a new classifier but focuses entirely on evaluation methodology.
venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research and Practice

title: Borderline-SMOTE Variants Under Extreme Imbalance: Behaviour in the 1:500 to 1:5000 Regime
abstract: Standard SMOTE and its borderline variants are rarely evaluated at imbalance ratios beyond 1:100, yet many operational datasets—credit card fraud, rare disease onset, critical infrastructure events—fall in the 1:500 to 1:5000 range. This study generates synthetic experiments at controlled imbalance ratios using five base datasets, reducing the minority class by subsampling to reach target ratios. Borderline-SMOTE-1, Borderline-SMOTE-2, SVM-SMOTE, and ADASYN are applied and fed into a random forest with 300 trees. At ratios beyond 1:1000, all SMOTE variants produce minority-region interpolations that increasingly fall in ambiguous border zones, and AUPRC drops by 15–40% compared with performance at 1:100. Density-based neighbourhood size k=3 consistently outperforms k=5 at the most extreme ratios. Results motivate caution when extrapolating published results from moderate imbalance to the extreme regime.
venue: Pattern Recognition and Machine Intelligence Letters

title: Feature Selection Stability Under Class Imbalance: An Analysis of Filter, Wrapper and Embedded Methods
abstract: High-dimensional behavioural datasets with hundreds of engineered features are common in anomaly detection pipelines, yet feature selection for such data under class imbalance has received limited systematic study. This paper evaluates eight feature selection methods—mutual information, chi-squared, ReliefF, mRMR, Lasso-L1, random forest importance, recursive feature elimination with gradient boosting, and Boruta—on twelve tabular datasets spanning 40 to 380 features and imbalance ratios from 1:20 to 1:300. Stability is measured using the Kuncheva stability index over ten bootstrap subsamples. Boruta and random forest importance show the highest stability (mean index > 0.72), while chi-squared and mutual information are the least stable at high imbalance (mean index < 0.45). Subset size of 20–30 features achieves predictive performance within 2% AUPRC of using all features on nine of twelve datasets.

title: XGBoost Hyperparameter Sensitivity Under Class Imbalance: A Large-Scale Grid Search on Industrial Tabular Benchmarks
abstract: Gradient boosting frameworks such as XGBoost expose numerous hyperparameters whose interactions under class imbalance are poorly understood. This paper performs a structured grid search over seven hyperparameters—learning rate, maximum depth, number of estimators, subsample rate, column subsample rate, minimum child weight, and scale_pos_weight—using a full factorial design at three levels on nine industrial tabular benchmarks with imbalance ratios between 1:25 and 1:450. Over 13 000 model configurations are evaluated. The scale_pos_weight parameter has the largest main effect on AUPRC (mean rank correlation 0.61), followed by minimum child weight (0.43) and maximum depth (0.38). Learning rate and subsample rate show strong interaction effects. A lookup heuristic for initial scale_pos_weight based on imbalance ratio is derived from regression trees fitted to the results, reducing median hyperparameter tuning cost by approximately 35% compared with uniform grid search.

title: Detecting Concept Drift in Imbalanced Behavioural Streams: A Comparison of Window-Based and Statistical Drift Detectors
abstract: Operational anomaly detection systems face distribution shift over time as both normal and anomalous behaviour patterns evolve. This paper evaluates eight drift detection methods—ADWIN, Page-Hinkley, DDM, EDDM, STEPD, HDDM-A, HDDM-W, and a windowed Kolmogorov–Smirnov test applied to feature marginals—in the context of imbalanced data streams with minority class rates between 0.5% and 3%. Synthetic streams are constructed from three real tabular datasets by injecting controlled gradual and abrupt drifts at known positions. Drift detectors are combined with a random forest base model retrained on detection. ADWIN achieves the best trade-off between true-detection rate (0.82) and false-alarm rate (0.09) for gradual drift, while HDDM-W performs best for abrupt drift (detection rate 0.91). All methods show degraded performance when minority class density changes independently of the majority class, a scenario that standard drift benchmarks do not cover.

title: Conformal Prediction Sets for Anomaly Detection Under Class Imbalance: Coverage Guarantees and Practical Efficiency
abstract: Conformal prediction provides distribution-free coverage guarantees for classification but has rarely been studied in the imbalanced class setting where the minority class is sparsely represented in calibration sets. This paper applies split conformal prediction and mondrian conformal prediction to four ensemble anomaly detectors—random forest, gradient boosting, stacking, and EasyEnsemble—on eleven benchmark datasets with imbalance ratios from 1:30 to 1:800. Marginal coverage is verified empirically at target levels 0.9 and 0.95; class-conditional coverage for the minority class fails to reach target levels with split conformal prediction when fewer than 50 minority-class calibration samples are available, and mondrian conformal prediction reduces this gap at the cost of larger prediction sets. Prediction set efficiency (mean set size) is reported alongside coverage, and a practical guideline for minimum calibration set size as a function of imbalance ratio is derived.
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning and Data Analysis

title: Domain-Specific Language for Configuring AUTOSAR Communication Matrices
abstract: Communication matrix configuration in AUTOSAR involves mapping signals to PDUs, defining timing parameters, and assigning network identifiers, all expressed in verbose ARXML. This paper presents ComMatDSL, a textual domain-specific language designed to express communication matrix configurations concisely. The language was defined using Xtext and includes a type system aligned with AUTOSAR data types. A model-to-ARXML generator was implemented using Xtend. The language was evaluated with five engineers from a regional embedded-software consultancy, each of whom configured three bus networks of increasing complexity. Compared to direct ARXML editing, ComMatDSL configurations were on average 76% shorter in character count and contained 58% fewer syntactic errors in the first-draft stage. A round-trip test on 22 reference matrices confirmed semantic equivalence of the generated ARXML with manually authored originals. The DSL is available as an Eclipse feature and targets AUTOSAR 4.2.

title: Ontology-Driven Normalisation of Heterogeneous Vulnerability Feed Data
abstract: Vulnerability intelligence is distributed across NVD, vendor advisories, and commercial feeds whose data models differ in severity scoring, affected-product representation, and remediation guidance. This paper describes an OWL 2 ontology designed to normalise records from five distinct vulnerability data sources into a unified schema suitable for automated ingestion by attack-graph construction pipelines. The ontology contains 84 classes and 47 object properties; a mapping layer implemented in SPARQL handles source-specific identifier schemes. Evaluation on 6,400 vulnerability records shows that the normalisation procedure resolves 93.1% of duplicate entries that span two or more sources and reduces manual curation effort by an estimated 68% in a controlled analyst-time study involving four participants. The ontology and mapping scripts are released under an open licence. Integration with the incremental attack-graph tool described in earlier work is demonstrated on a 300-node test network.

title: Verifikacija binarnih sabirača realizovanih u VHDL-u primenom SAT/SMT rešavača
abstract: Rad se bavi primenom SAT i SMT rešavača za automatsku verifikaciju binarnih sabirača opisanih u VHDL-u, sa fokusom na kolo tipa carry-lookahead za 16-bitne i 32-bitne operande. Prikazan je tok verifikacije koji počinje od RTL opisa, prolazi kroz konverziju u Bit-Vector SMT logiku i završava se proverom ekvivalentnosti u odnosu na referentni model. Testiranje je izvršeno nad deset varijanti sabirača preuzetih iz industrijskog IP repozitorijuma. Rezultati pokazuju da SMT pristup sa rešavačem Z3 pronalazi greške unutar 4,2 sekunde prosečno za 32-bitna kola, dok formalno dokazivanje ispravnosti za isti skup traje ispod 18 sekundi. Poređenje je učinjeno i sa BDD-baziranim pristupima: SMT metoda pokazuje bolje skaliranje za reči dužine iznad 24 bita. Rad doprinosi standardizaciji verifikacionog toka za akademske i manje industrijske projekte koji koriste open-source alate.
venue: Journal of Microelectronics and Electronic Components
