title: Fixed-Point Multiplier Synthesis for FIR Filter Cores: A Comparison of VHDL Templates on Spartan-6 and Cyclone IV
abstract: This paper evaluates six VHDL multiplier templates — including shift-and-add, Booth-encoded, and DSP-block-mapped variants — targeting two mid-range FPGA families: Xilinx Spartan-6 and Intel Cyclone IV. The study focuses on 12-bit by 16-bit fixed-point operands typical of FIR filter coefficient paths in audio DSP cores. Each template was synthesized with vendor tools at a target frequency of 100 MHz, and post-place-and-route resource utilization, timing slack, and power estimates were recorded. The Booth-encoded template mapped onto Cyclone IV DSP blocks achieved the lowest LUT count (38 LUTs) and met timing with 1.7 ns slack, while the shift-and-add variant on Spartan-6 consumed 94 LUTs but allowed finer pipeline control. Formal equivalence checking between templates was performed using SymbiYosys. Recommendations are given for choosing template style based on device availability, pipeline depth requirements, and available DSP block count.

title: Primena SystemVerilog Assertions u verifikaciji pipeline množača za DSP procesore
abstract: Ovaj rad istražuje upotrebu SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) za verifikaciju pipeline množača s fiksnim zapisom u kontekstu DSP procesora namenjenih telekomunikacionim primenama. Razmatrana su kola sa dubinom pipeline-a od 2 do 5 stepeni za 16-bitne množioce. Definisano je 47 assertion iskaza koji pokrivaju uslove prekoračenja, tačnost zaokruživanja (round-half-up i round-to-zero), te validnost handshake signala između pipeline stepena. Verifikacija je sprovedena u kombinovanom okruženju: SystemVerilog + UVM testbench uz ModelSim simulaciju i formalna provera u Cadence JasperGold okruženju akademske licence. Postignuto je 94% pokrivenost grana u simulacionom modu, dok je formalni alat potvrdio ispravnost svih definisanih svojstava za operande do 16 bita. Rad identifikuje klasu greški koja se konzistentno izmakne simulaciji ali bude detektovana formalnom proverom, posebno u slučajevima graničnih vrednosti argumenata.

title: Formal Verification of MAC Units for Fixed-Point DSP Cores Using Bounded Model Checking
abstract: Multiply-accumulate (MAC) units are central to virtually all DSP workloads, yet their formal verification at the RTL level remains non-trivial due to accumulator overflow and rounding mode interactions. This work applies bounded model checking (BMC) with bit-vector arithmetic to MAC units described in VHDL, targeting a 24-bit fixed-point core intended for software-defined radio signal chains. The BMC depth was set to 256 clock cycles, covering typical FIR convolution lengths. Three accumulator overflow strategies — saturation, wrap-around, and exception flag — were each modelled and verified against a golden C reference using a cross-language property binding methodology. Counterexamples were generated for eight known bug seeds injected into the RTL; BMC found all eight within a maximum of 2 minutes per property on a standard workstation. The verified core was subsequently deployed on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA and achieved 210 MHz post-route timing at 1.0 V core voltage.

title: HDL sinteza aritmetičkih kola za obradu govora sa minimalnom potrošnjom na Zynq platformi
abstract: Rad prikazuje projektovanje aritmetičkih kola za obradu govora (filterska banka sa 16 kanala i IFFT blok) na Xilinx Zynq-7020 platformi, uz minimizaciju dinamičke potrošnje energije. Korišćena je fiksna aritmetika Q1.15 formata. Prikazana su tri pristupa smanjenju potrošnje: clock gating na nivou podmodula, operand isolation za neaktivne grane pipeline-a i resinteza s niskom pragom napona (0,9 V). Merenja su sprovedena u laboratoriji korišćenjem Xilinx Power Advantage alata i eksternog preciznog ampermetra. Dinamička potrošnja smanjena je za 31% u odnosu na osnovno rešenje bez modifikacija, uz zanemarijivo povećanje kašnjenja od 0,4 ns. Rad takođe sadrži detaljan opis toka sinteze od VHDL opisa do bitstre datoteke, koji može poslužiti kao metodološka osnova za slične projekte u oblasti prenosnih uređaja za obradu govora.

title: Equivalence Checking Between VHDL and HLS-Generated Verilog for a Cordic-Based Angle Computation Unit
abstract: High-level synthesis (HLS) tools promise shorter design cycles but their RTL output must be verified against manually written reference HDL. This paper presents an equivalence checking flow for a CORDIC-based angle computation unit: one implementation written in VHDL by hand and one generated by Vivado HLS from a C++ specification, both targeting 18-bit fixed-point precision. The flow uses sequential equivalence checking (SEC) performed by an academic tool built on top of ABC, augmented with manual pipeline alignment scripts to reconcile different II (initiation interval) choices made by HLS. Out of 120 sampled input angle vectors uniformly distributed in [−π, π], the HLS version produced results deviating by more than 1 ULP in 3 cases attributable to a pipelining-induced accumulation of rounding error. The deviation was corrected by a guard-bit annotation in the HLS source. Post-correction, formal equivalence was confirmed for all tested input classes. The paper discusses the practical limitations of SEC when pipeline depths differ between the two implementations.

title: Automatsko generisanje SMT-LIB modela iz VHDL opisa: alat i studija slučaja na 32-bitnom deljenom kolu
abstract: Formalna verifikacija HDL opisa zahteva prevođenje RTL koda u formalni model. Ovaj rad opisuje prototipski alat koji automatski generiše SMT-LIB 2.6 modele iz podskupa VHDL-a relevantnog za kombinaciona i jednocikelna sekvencijalna kola. Alat je implementiran u Pythonu i testiran na 32-bitnom kolu za celobrojno deljenje (SRT algoritam, radiks 2). Iz 412 linija VHDL koda generisan je SMT-LIB model od 1.840 iskaza koji je prosleđen rešavaču CVC5. Provera ispravnosti ostatka i količnika trajala je prosečno 34 sekunde po ulaznoj kombinaciji za granične vrednosti (maksimalni i minimalni operandi, deljenje nulom). Alat detektuje 6 od 7 ubačenih grešaka. Preostala greška zahteva dublje razmatranje opsega promenljivih i planirana je kao pravac budućeg rada. Izvorni kod alata je javno dostupan na institucionskom repozitorijumu.

title: Formalna specifikacija i verifikacija zaokruživanja u IEEE 754-kompatibilnim konvertorima između fiksnog i pokretnog zareza na FPGA
abstract: Konverzija između fiksnog i pokretnog zareza u softverski-definisanim radio platformama mora garantovati korektnost zaokruživanja radi sprečavanja akumulacije greške u dugačkim lancima obrade. Rad formalizuje pet IEEE 754 načina zaokruživanja (round-to-nearest-even, round-toward-zero, round-up, round-down, round-away-from-zero) kao SMT-LIB svojstva i primenjuje ih na VHDL konvertor projektovan za Xilinx UltraScale+ familiju. Konvertor prihvata 32-bitni Q16.16 ulaz i generiše IEEE 754 single-precision izlaz u tri pipeline stepena. Za svaki način zaokruživanja formalno je dokazana ispravnost za sve 2^32 ulazne vrednosti primenom bit-vektor aritmetike i simboličke enumeracije. Ukupno vreme verifikacije na 16-jezgarnom serveru iznosilo je 9 sati i 12 minuta. Detektovana je i ispravljena jedna greška u round-toward-zero putanji koja je nastala zbog netačne maske za detekciju nultog ostatka.
venue: Automatika – Journal of Control, Measurement, Electronics, Computing and Communications

title: Systematic RTL Bug Seeding for Evaluating HDL Formal Verification Toolchains: A Benchmark Suite
abstract: Assessing the effectiveness of formal HDL verification tools requires repeatable, categorised bug sets. This paper presents a benchmark suite of 84 seeded bugs across 12 arithmetic RTL modules — adders, multipliers, dividers, and MAC units — all described in synthesisable VHDL and targeting fixed-point DSP use cases. Bugs are classified into seven categories: bit-width truncation, off-by-one in control logic, incorrect saturation boundary, missing pipeline flush, wrong rounding constant, carry chain break, and sign-extension error. The suite was used to evaluate four open-source and two commercial formal verification toolchains. Detection rates ranged from 61% (a lightweight open-source SAT-based tool) to 97% (a commercial model checker with automatic abstraction). Category-level analysis reveals that sign-extension errors are consistently missed by three of the six tools. The benchmark is released under CC-BY 4.0 and hosted on the faculty GitLab instance to allow third-party toolchain evaluation.

title: Verified VHDL Library of Fixed-Point Elementary Functions for Zynq UltraScale+ DSP Cores
abstract: Elementary mathematical functions — reciprocal, square root, sine, cosine, and base-2 logarithm — are frequently needed in DSP signal chains and are often implemented via piecewise-polynomial or table-lookup methods in fixed-point hardware. This paper describes a verified open VHDL library providing all five functions in Q2.30 and Q4.28 formats, targeting Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ DSP slices. Each function module is accompanied by a machine-checked correctness proof in the SMT-LIB format, establishing worst-case absolute error bounds relative to the IEEE 754 double-precision reference. Error bounds achieved are: reciprocal 2.1 × 10⁻⁸, square root 1.4 × 10⁻⁸, sine/cosine 3.0 × 10⁻⁸, log₂ 4.7 × 10⁻⁸. Resource utilisation ranges from 2 DSP slices (reciprocal) to 11 DSP slices (log₂) at a clock frequency of 250 MHz. Comparative benchmarking against Xilinx CORDIC IP and a commercial fixed-point math library shows comparable accuracy at 15–30% lower LUT cost. The library is distributed under the LGPL-2.1 licence.

title: Congestion-Responsive Bitrate Ladder Design for MPEG-DASH Over Satellite Backhaul Links
abstract: Satellite backhaul introduces high and variable propagation delay—typically 550–620 ms round-trip for geostationary links—which undermines the responsiveness of standard MPEG-DASH ABR controllers. This paper proposes a congestion-responsive bitrate ladder design that accounts for the large bandwidth-delay product of satellite paths. The ladder's representation set is derived from a capacity model that incorporates measured rain-fade attenuation statistics from a Ka-band link at a rural site in southern Serbia, monitored over 18 months. Segments are sized at 4 s to reduce switching overhead, and a predictive pre-fetching buffer of 40 s is combined with a delay-tolerant feedback controller parameterised for the high-BDP environment. In playback trials over 200 simulated sessions, mean stall rate was 0.8% compared to 4.1% for an unmodified DASH reference player, while average quality level was maintained within 1 representation step of the channel capacity 91% of the time.

title: Coil Design for Wireless Power Transfer in Electric Vehicles
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of coil design principles for electric vehicle wireless power transfer, covering the progression from single-layer circular pads to multi-layer DDQ geometries. The chapter begins with analytical expressions for self-inductance and mutual inductance of common coil shapes and discusses their accuracy limits as operating frequency increases toward 85 kHz and beyond. Subsequent sections address the practical effects of Litz wire strand count and bundle diameter on AC resistance at operating frequency. Ferrite shielding layout strategies are reviewed with reference to IEC and SAE flux density emission limits. A section on misalignment tolerance formalises the concept of coupling-coefficient sensitivity maps, illustrating how these can guide the selection between circular, DD, and DDQ topologies at the system definition stage. Worked design examples use parameters representative of light urban electric vehicles with ground clearances of 100–180 mm.

title: Effect of measurement window length on Pst estimation accuracy for rapidly varying flicker sources
abstract: The IEC 61000-4-15 standard mandates a 10-minute observation window for computing Pst. For arc furnace loads that cycle through melting phases shorter than 10 minutes, this window length can mix stationary segments of different statistical character, potentially biasing the index. This paper investigates the sensitivity of Pst estimates to observation window lengths ranging from 2 to 10 minutes using both synthetic signals with known statistical properties and field recordings from a 30 MVA steelmaking arc furnace. Synthetic tests employ the IEC flickermeter reference model implemented in MATLAB. Field data cover 480 complete melting cycles logged at 10 kHz sampling rate. Results show that reducing the window to 4 minutes decreases estimation bias in rapid-cycle furnace operation by 18% at the cost of a 31% increase in estimator variance. A weighted sliding-window estimator is proposed and evaluated, achieving a balanced trade-off between bias and variance for cycles shorter than 6 minutes.

title: Ownership Concentration and Dividend Payout in Serbian Family Firms: Evidence from Listed and Unlisted Companies
abstract: This study examines whether ownership concentration affects dividend payout decisions in Serbian family-controlled firms, using a hand-collected dataset of 214 firms drawn from Business Registers Agency filings for the period 2017–2021. The sample includes both Belgrade Stock Exchange-listed companies and a matched set of unlisted firms with comparable size and sector profiles. A Tobit regression is applied to account for the censored nature of dividend data, with ownership concentration measured as the Herfindahl–Hirschman index of shareholding. Results indicate that firms in which a single family shareholder holds more than 50 percent of equity distribute significantly lower dividends than firms with more dispersed ownership, consistent with minority expropriation concerns. The effect is stronger in unlisted firms, where external monitoring is limited. Firm size, profitability, and leverage are included as controls. The findings align with principal–principal agency theory and suggest that statutory dividend protections under Serbian company law have limited practical effect for minority shareholders in closely held family enterprises.

title: Independent Directors on Family Firm Boards in the Western Balkans: Appointment Patterns and Actual Independence
abstract: Independent directors are widely prescribed in corporate governance codes across the Western Balkans, yet their practical independence in family-controlled firms remains uncertain. This paper analyses board composition data from 318 firms in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, drawn from annual reports and court registry filings for 2019 and 2020. Independence is assessed both formally, using national regulatory criteria, and substantively, by tracing personal and business ties between directors and controlling families through LinkedIn profiles, media sources, and registry cross-references. Logistic regression results show that firms with a family blockholder exceeding 60 percent ownership are approximately 2.4 times less likely to have at least one substantively independent director compared with firms below that threshold, even when formal compliance is achieved. Firm age, sector, and whether the firm has external bank debt are included as controls. The paper argues that disclosure requirements without enforcement mechanisms produce cosmetic rather than functional board independence in the region's family-firm-dominated corporate landscape.

title: Minority Shareholder Remedies in Serbian Company Law: A Gap Between Statute and Practice
abstract: Serbian company law provides minority shareholders with several formal remedies including the right to request extraordinary general meetings, oppression claims, and appraisal rights in squeeze-out transactions. This chapter reviews how these instruments function in practice by combining a doctrinal analysis of the Law on Companies (2011, as amended) with a case review of 47 commercial court decisions from the period 2015–2022 involving minority shareholder disputes. The analysis finds that oppression-based claims succeed in fewer than one in five cases brought to first-instance courts, with courts frequently deferring to majority decisions absent clear evidence of fraud. Appraisal rights in squeeze-outs are exercised rarely, partly because valuation disputes are costly and slow. The chapter situates these findings within comparative literature on investor protection in post-Yugoslav transition economies and argues that procedural barriers, rather than substantive law gaps, are the principal constraint on effective minority protection in Serbia. Recommendations focus on procedural simplification and specialist commercial adjudication.

title: Digitisation of Supplier Compliance Documentation in South-East European Agri-food Chains: Current State and Obstacles
abstract: Cloud-based supplier portals and digital traceability platforms are increasingly common among large retailers in Western Europe, but their penetration into supplier bases in South-East Europe remains uneven. This paper maps the current state of digital compliance documentation across 78 agri-food suppliers located in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina that supply to at least one retailer using a digital supplier portal. Data were collected via an online survey in 2022 supplemented by 14 telephone interviews. Only 31 percent of surveyed firms actively upload documents to buyer portals rather than submitting paper copies converted to scans. Key obstacles cited are unstable internet connectivity at farm or processing locations, the cost of internal IT administration, and contractual ambiguity about which party bears the integration cost. The paper provides a descriptive taxonomy of digitisation levels and identifies firm characteristics associated with each level, offering practical guidance for buyers seeking to raise portal adoption rates among their regional suppliers.

title: Analytical Springback Prediction for Air Bending of Mild Steel Sheets Under Plane-Strain Conditions
abstract: This paper presents a closed-form model for springback angle in air bending of mild steel sheets, derived from beam-bending theory with a bilinear elastoplastic material description. Experiments were conducted on a hydraulic press-brake using DC04 mild steel strips of 1.0 mm and 1.5 mm thickness, at punch radii between 2 mm and 8 mm and bending angles from 30° to 150°. The model accounts for neutral-axis shift as a function of punch radius-to-thickness ratio. Predicted springback angles were compared with 120 measured specimens; the mean absolute error was 0.41° across all configurations. A sensitivity study showed that uncertainty in yield stress (±5%) contributed more to prediction error than uncertainty in sheet thickness (±0.05 mm). The model is computationally inexpensive and was implemented in a spreadsheet tool used in the undergraduate laboratory course. Results confirm that the bilinear description is adequate for mild steel but becomes less accurate for bending angles above 130°, where a power-law hardening correction is recommended.

title: Influence of Bauschinger Effect on Springback in Repeated-Bending Operations: An Experimental Study
abstract: Repeated bending-straightening cycles are common in coil-fed press-brake lines and introduce the Bauschinger effect, which reduces the apparent yield stress on load reversal and modifies springback behaviour. This study characterises the Bauschinger effect in three structural steels—S235, S355, and DP600—using cyclic tension-compression tests on flat specimens machined to avoid buckling. The isotropic-kinematic hardening parameters of the Chaboche model were fitted to the cyclic test data. Air-bending experiments with pre-deformed blanks (one to three prior reverse-bending cycles) were then performed on a 40-tonne CNC press-brake. FEM simulations in ABAQUS using the fitted Chaboche parameters reduced springback prediction error from 2.1° (isotropic hardening only) to 0.6° (mixed hardening) for DP600 at a 90° target angle. Practical implications for setting backstop offsets in multi-step bending sequences are discussed. The dataset of 216 cyclic test curves and 144 bending experiments is included as supplementary material.

title: FEM-Based Process Window for Springback-Controlled Bending of DP780 Advanced High-Strength Steel
abstract: Advanced high-strength steels (AHSS) of the dual-phase family are increasingly used in automotive structural parts, but their high yield-to-tensile ratio makes springback prediction and compensation challenging. This paper maps a process window for air bending of DP780 sheets (1.2 mm and 1.5 mm gauges) by running a full-factorial FEM study in PAM-STAMP covering five punch radii (2–10 mm), seven target bending angles (60°–150°), and three friction coefficients (0.05–0.15). In total, 210 simulations were evaluated. Springback angle ranged from 2.3° to 14.8° across the studied parameter space. A response-surface model (second-order polynomial) was fitted to the simulation results with an adjusted R² of 0.971 and validated against 48 physical press-brake experiments, yielding a mean absolute error of 0.72°. The fitted response surface was encoded as a look-up correction table suitable for integration into CNC press-brake controllers. Limits of the approach when material batch variability exceeds ±3% in yield stress are quantified.

title: Thickness Strain Distribution in V-Die Bending: Comparison of Hill'48 and Barlat'89 Yield Criteria in FEM Simulations
abstract: Accurate thickness strain prediction matters for subsequent forming operations and for springback calculation in multi-step sequences. This study compares the Hill'48 and Barlat'89 anisotropic yield criteria in FEM models of V-die bending for three aluminium alloys (AA5754-O, AA6016-T4, AA7075-T6) at 1.0 mm thickness. Lankford r-values and yield loci were determined from uniaxial and biaxial tensile tests. ABAQUS simulations using each yield criterion were run for 45°, 90°, and 135° bending angles at two die widths. Through-thickness strain profiles were extracted and compared with measurements from cross-sectioned and etched specimens using optical microscopy. For AA5754-O, both criteria performed similarly (error < 4%). For AA7075-T6, Barlat'89 reduced maximum thickness-strain error from 9.2% to 3.8% relative to Hill'48. The paper quantifies when the added complexity of Barlat'89 calibration is justified. Springback angle predictions showed smaller sensitivity to criterion choice (< 0.5° difference), consistent with findings from other groups.

title: Real-Time Springback Compensation on a CNC Press-Brake Using In-Process Angle Measurement
abstract: This paper describes a closed-loop control scheme implemented on a retrofitted 63-tonne CNC hydraulic press-brake to achieve target bending angles despite springback variability. An optical angle sensor mounted in the die measures the instantaneous bend angle during the downstroke. A proportional-integral controller adjusts the punch penetration depth on the basis of the difference between the measured release angle and the target angle, iterating within a single stroke using incremental re-strikes. The control algorithm was tested on S355 (1.5 mm and 2.0 mm), DP600 (1.2 mm), and AA6016-T4 (1.5 mm) over 500 bending cycles per material grade. Angle accuracy after the closed-loop correction was ±0.3° (2σ) for all materials, compared with ±2.1° (2σ) without compensation. Cycle time increased by an average of 1.8 seconds per part due to re-strike iterations. The system requires no prior knowledge of material properties beyond a first-bend calibration stroke, making it practical for mixed-batch production. Failure modes related to sensor contamination and asymmetric die wear are discussed.

title: Springback in Sheet-Metal Forming: Physical Mechanisms, Prediction Methods, and Industrial Compensation Strategies
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured review of springback in sheet-metal forming operations with emphasis on press-brake bending. The chapter is organised into four sections. The first covers elastic recovery mechanics and the role of material hardening models. The second surveys analytical prediction methods from simple beam theory to multi-layer models. The third covers FEM-based approaches, discussing mesh sensitivity, element type selection, and the choice of constitutive model. The fourth section reviews industrial compensation strategies: overbending, die geometry correction, bottoming, and adaptive CNC control. Approximately 90 references spanning 1980 to 2017 are cited, with emphasis on works validated against physical experiments. The chapter is written for practising engineers and advanced students and includes worked numerical examples for a 90° air-bending case in DP600. Tables compare the accuracy and computational cost of representative prediction methods.

title: Effect of Residual Stress from Laser Cutting on Springback in Subsequent Air Bending of S355 Blanks
abstract: Laser-cut blanks carry edge residual stresses that can alter springback behaviour relative to blanks produced by guillotine shearing. This study quantifies the effect by measuring residual stress distributions in S355 steel strips (2.0 mm, 3.0 mm thick) cut by fibre laser at three power/feed combinations using X-ray diffraction at multiple distances from the cut edge (0.1 mm to 10 mm). The stressed strips were subsequently bent at 45°, 90°, and 135° on a V-die press-brake, and springback angles were compared with those of shear-cut reference strips. Springback differences up to 0.9° were observed at 90° for the highest-energy laser setting and 2.0 mm thickness. FEM models incorporating the measured residual stress as an initial condition reproduced the observed differences within 0.25°. The practical conclusion is that, for part tolerances tighter than ±1°, the cutting method and laser parameters should be included in press-brake setup procedures.

title: Reduced-Order FEM Surrogate for Springback Prediction in CNC Press-Brake Bending Using Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
abstract: Full FEM simulations of bending operations are too slow for real-time use inside CNC controllers. This paper constructs a surrogate model using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) applied to a training set of 360 ABAQUS shell-element simulations of air bending across a five-dimensional parameter space: yield stress (200–700 MPa), hardening exponent (0.05–0.30), sheet thickness (0.8–3.0 mm), punch radius (2–12 mm), and target angle (45°–135°). The POD basis retains 99.5% of variance with eight modes. A radial-basis-function interpolant maps parameter vectors to POD coefficients. Springback angle predictions from the surrogate have a mean absolute error of 0.38° against a 60-simulation test set not used in training and execute in under 2 ms on standard industrial PC hardware. The surrogate was embedded in the press-brake controller developed in earlier work and tested with mixed batches of S235, S355, and DP600, maintaining ±0.4° accuracy. Limitations related to extrapolation outside the training domain are characterised.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in FEM-Based Springback Prediction: Effect of Material Property Scatter in DP600 and DP780 Coils
abstract: Material properties of advanced high-strength steel coils vary between and within production batches, introducing uncertainty into deterministic springback predictions. This paper applies a Monte Carlo approach to quantify how yield stress, ultimate tensile strength, and normal anisotropy coefficient r—each described by measured statistical distributions drawn from 24 coils of DP600 and 18 coils of DP780 supplied by two European steel producers—propagate to uncertainty in predicted springback angle. Input distributions were characterised from 720 tensile tests. For each steel and three bending configurations (90°, t = 1.2 mm; 90°, t = 1.5 mm; 120°, t = 1.5 mm), 1000 ABAQUS simulations were run using Latin-hypercube-sampled property sets. The 95th-percentile spread in springback angle was 2.4° for DP600 and 3.7° for DP780, with yield stress contributing approximately 65% of the variance in both grades. Results are used to define tolerance bands for adaptive CNC controller targets, replacing single-point predictions with stochastic bounds.

title: Characterisation of the Young's Modulus Degradation in Dual-Phase Steels and Its Influence on Springback
abstract: The apparent elastic modulus of dual-phase steels decreases with accumulated plastic strain, a phenomenon sometimes called chord-modulus degradation or elastic modulus reduction. This degradation directly affects springback through the elastic-recovery term. The present work measures chord modulus as a function of pre-strain for DP600 and DP800 using loading-unloading tensile tests at seven pre-strain levels from 0% to 16%, with three specimens per level. Modulus values dropped from approximately 205 GPa at zero pre-strain to 178 GPa and 171 GPa at 16% for DP600 and DP800 respectively. A modified exponential degradation law is fitted and incorporated into both an analytical springback model and an ABAQUS user material subroutine. FEM predictions of springback at 90° air bending improved from a mean error of 1.8° with constant modulus to 0.6° with degraded modulus for DP800. The user subroutine is made available via the departmental repository.

title: Press-Brake Bending of Aluminium-Lithium Alloy AA2198-T8 for Aerospace Structural Brackets: Springback and Cracking Limits
abstract: Aluminium-lithium alloys offer attractive stiffness-to-weight ratios for aerospace brackets but are prone to cracking at small bend radii and exhibit larger springback than conventional aluminium alloys. This study investigates air bending of AA2198-T8 sheet (1.6 mm) on a CNC press-brake, mapping the boundary between acceptable bends and edge cracking as a function of punch radius (2–8 mm) and bending direction relative to rolling direction (0°, 45°, 90°). Forming limit curves and anisotropy coefficients were measured; the minimum safe punch-radius-to-thickness ratio was found to be 2.8 for bends parallel to the rolling direction and 3.5 for transverse bends. Springback angles ranged from 5.2° to 11.4° across the studied parameter space, substantially higher than for AA6016-T4. ABAQUS FEM simulations using a Barlat'89 yield surface and damage indicator reproduced the cracking boundary within one punch-radius increment. Recommended CNC overbend angles for the safe process window are tabulated.

title: Digital Twin Framework for an Instrumented Press-Brake: Synchronising FEM State Estimates with Live Sensor Data
abstract: This paper describes a prototype digital twin architecture for a CNC hydraulic press-brake in which a continuously updated FEM state estimate runs in parallel with the physical machine. The physical press-brake is instrumented with four load cells in the bed, a laser angle sensor, two linear encoders on the ram, and a thermocouple array for hydraulic-fluid temperature. Sensor readings at 100 Hz are streamed to a workstation running a reduced-order FEM model (constructed via POD as in prior work) whose material parameters are updated by an unscented Kalman filter using the punch force–displacement curve as the primary observable. The filter converges to within ±2% of tensile-test yield stress values after the first production stroke for S235, S355, and DP600. Springback angle predictions using the filter-updated model achieved 0.31° mean absolute error over a 200-part production run with intentionally mixed material batches. The architecture is described in sufficient detail for replication, and the filter code is released under an open licence.

title: A Weighted TOPSIS Approach for Supplier Selection in the Automotive Tier-2 Supply Chain: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region
abstract: This paper applies a weighted Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) model to evaluate and rank a set of 14 candidate suppliers for a Vojvodina-based automotive component manufacturer. Seven criteria were defined through structured interviews with procurement managers, covering price, delivery reliability, quality rejection rate, financial stability, geographic proximity, environmental certification, and responsiveness. Criteria weights were elicited using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with input from five domain experts. The consistency ratio for all pairwise comparison matrices remained below 0.08. Sensitivity analysis was performed by varying the weight of the top two criteria by ±20%. Results show that the final supplier ranking is stable under moderate weight perturbations, with the top three suppliers retaining their positions across all tested scenarios. The paper discusses practical limitations of the model, including the difficulty of obtaining reliable financial data from smaller regional suppliers, and suggests a periodic re-evaluation protocol aligned with annual procurement cycles.

title: A constraint-based fixture layout optimisation algorithm using sequential quadratic programming
abstract: This paper describes a constraint-based optimisation algorithm for determining locator and clamp positions that minimise workpiece deformation under prescribed cutting-force profiles. The objective function is the Euclidean norm of the nodal displacement vector at machined surfaces, evaluated from a reduced-order finite-element model of the workpiece. Geometric constraints enforce minimum spacing between fixture elements and clearance from part features. Sequential quadratic programming is used as the solver, initialised from a 3-2-1 reference layout. The algorithm was implemented in MATLAB and tested on two benchmark workpieces: a thin-walled titanium bracket (Ti-6Al-4V, 5 mm wall) and a steel housing with multiple pockets. For the titanium bracket, the algorithm reduced peak deformation from 38 μm to 19 μm in 47 iterations. Convergence was sensitive to the initial locator spacing when the primary datum surface area was less than 60% of the part footprint. Computational time on a standard desktop was under four minutes per case.

title: Quantitative XRD phase analysis of PVD coating cross-sections after high-temperature oxidation and machining exposure
abstract: TiAlN, CrAlN and TiSiN coatings were subjected to two degradation routes: isothermal furnace oxidation (700 °C, 2 h in air) and actual turning exposure (AISI 4140, 45 HRC, 200 m/min, until VB = 0.3 mm). XRD patterns collected from coating cross-sections prepared by FIB milling were refined by the Rietveld method. After furnace oxidation, TiAlN showed 18 vol% rutile TiO₂ and 9 vol% α-Al₂O₃; CrAlN showed 6 vol% Cr₂O₃ and no alumina phase; TiSiN showed 3 vol% TiO₂. After machining exposure, oxide fractions were systematically lower for all coatings, suggesting that mechanical wear removes oxidised surface layers faster than they form. The retained face-centred cubic phase fraction correlated positively with residual hardness measured by nanoindentation (R² = 0.84). Results provide a quantitative basis for linking XRD phase changes to tribological performance degradation in used cutting inserts.

title: Register Stratification in Serbian Serialised Fiction, 1900–1920: A Corpus-Based Overview
abstract: The study examines register variation across 47 serialised prose texts published in three Belgrade and Novi Sad periodicals between 1900 and 1920. A corpus of 310,000 tokens was compiled from digitised issues and annotated for part-of-speech, clause type, and discourse marker presence. Frequency profiles of subordinating conjunctions, nominal phrases, and reported-speech frames were compared across narrator text and character dialogue using log-likelihood significance tests. Results show that dialogue in this period consistently employs shorter clause chains, a higher proportion of particle-initial utterances, and more frequent use of the Serbian aorist than contemporary narrator prose. The findings are discussed in relation to the hypothesis that serialised popular fiction preserved older spoken features longer than prestige literary forms. The annotated corpus is made available through the repository of the Faculty of Philosophy, Novi Sad.

title: Lexical Borrowings from German in Serbian Newspaper Dialogue Representations, 1895–1915
abstract: Drawing on a 180,000-token subcorpus of feuilletons and satirical columns from four Vojvodina newspapers, this paper traces the density and distribution of German-origin lexical items in represented speech. Items were identified through comparison with a historical dictionary of Serbian-German contact vocabulary compiled for the project and cross-checked against existing etymological resources. Results indicate that German borrowings appear at nearly three times the rate in dialogue representations of urban male characters compared with rural or female characters, suggesting that editors and writers used borrowings as a sociolinguistic marker of class and urbanity rather than as transparent reflections of actual speech. A secondary finding concerns the stability of particular borrowings across the two decades: roughly 40 percent of attested items disappear from the corpus after 1908, correlating with Serbian language-purification movements of that period.

title: Towards a Reference Corpus of Serbian Prose Registers 1890–1945: Design, Sampling, and Annotation Principles
abstract: This paper describes the design decisions behind the SerbProsRef corpus, a stratified reference collection of Serbian prose texts from 1890 to 1945. The corpus targets 2.5 million tokens drawn from five text categories: literary short fiction, serialised popular fiction, newspaper feuilletons, private letters published in literary almanacs, and official correspondence excerpts. Sampling followed decade-by-decade quotas with genre balance enforced within each stratum. Digitisation relied on manually corrected OCR output from scans held at the Matica srpska library in Novi Sad and the National Library of Serbia. Annotation layers include orthographic normalisation, lemmatisation, morphosyntactic tags following an adapted version of the MULTEXT-East tagset, and a dialogue-span layer marking direct, indirect, and free indirect speech. Inter-annotator agreement on the dialogue-span layer reached 0.83 kappa across three annotators. The paper discusses recurring ambiguities in pre-standardisation orthography that complicate automatic processing.

title: The Aorist in Serbian Narrative Dialogue, 1890–1940: Frequency, Function, and Decline
abstract: The Serbian aorist tense is widely described as having retreated from spoken registers during the twentieth century, but corpus evidence for the timing and pattern of this retreat in written dialogue is scarce. This paper uses the SerbProsRef corpus to track aorist frequency per 10,000 tokens of dialogue text across five-year intervals from 1890 to 1940. Results confirm a decline from 48 instances per 10,000 tokens in the 1890–1905 window to 19 in the 1930–1940 window, but the decline is non-linear: a temporary stabilisation occurs in the 1915–1925 window across authors associated with the Serbian literary revival movement. Qualitative analysis of 200 randomly sampled aorist tokens in dialogue reveals that the tense retained its evidential-narrative function in first-person dramatic utterances longer than in third-person reported speech. The study also compares decline rates across regional origin of authors, finding faster decline in texts by authors documented as Belgraders.

title: Address Forms and Social Distance in Serbian Epistolary Fiction, 1900–1930
abstract: Using a 95,000-token subcorpus of epistolary novels and letter-embedded short fiction published between 1900 and 1930, this study maps the distribution of second-person address forms—ti, Vi, and the archaic plural vi—across relationships characterised by kinship, professional hierarchy, gender difference, and social class. Each letter excerpt was coded for relationship type, author gender, and publication decade. Logistic regression modelling shows that gender of the addressee is the strongest predictor of the formal Vi in non-hierarchical dyads, with male addressees receiving formal address at 2.3 times the rate of female addressees in cross-gender correspondence. The archaic plural vi declines sharply after 1910 in texts associated with urban settings but persists in rural-set fiction through the 1920s. The findings contribute to ongoing debates about the codification of Serbian politeness norms in the early standardisation period.

title: Collocational Stability and Change in Serbian Dialogue Verbs of Speaking, 1890–1945
abstract: This paper investigates the collocational behaviour of the 30 most frequent verbs of speaking in dialogue-framing clauses (e.g. reče, odgovori, upita, viknu) across the full SerbProsRef corpus. Using a log-dice association measure, the study identifies stable collocates shared across all five decades and collocates that are decade-specific. Stable collocates are predominantly manner adverbs and subject-denoting nominals, while decade-specific collocates cluster around culturally variable content words. A secondary analysis focuses on the gradual displacement of reče by odgovori as the most frequent dialogue verb in literary short fiction after 1920, tracking the shift through mutual information scores and dispersion measures. The paper argues that the displacement reflects an increasing preference for dialogue frames that encode interactional structure rather than narrative report, consistent with a broader stylistic shift toward scene-based narrative composition.

title: Punctuation Conventions in Transcribed Dialogue and Their Implications for Automatic Dialogue Detection in Serbian Historical Texts
abstract: Automatic detection of dialogue spans in historical Serbian prose is complicated by the variety of punctuation conventions used across publishers, decades, and typesetters. This paper analyses punctuation practices in 120 texts drawn from 12 publishers active between 1895 and 1940, cataloguing six distinct systems for marking direct speech (em-dash opening, guillemets, quotation marks, indentation-only, and hybrid combinations). Across 4,200 manually verified dialogue openings and closings, automatic rule-based detection achieves precision between 0.71 and 0.94 and recall between 0.68 and 0.91 depending on publisher convention. A publisher-specific lookup table developed during the study raises overall F1 from 0.74 to 0.88 on a held-out test set of 30 texts. The paper provides the lookup table and rule specifications as supplementary materials, and discusses implications for corpus pipelines that must handle heterogeneous historical sources without prior normalisation.

title: Temporal Reference in Serbian Dialogue of the Interwar Period: A Tense and Aspect Study
abstract: This paper examines how tense and aspect interact in dialogue to construct temporal meaning in Serbian prose fiction of the 1920s and 1930s. The data consist of 8,200 finite verb tokens extracted from dialogue spans in the interwar subcorpus of SerbProsRef. Each token was coded for tense category, aspect, and clause position (main vs. subordinate). Conditional distributions show that present-tense forms account for 44 percent of dialogue tokens but only 18 percent of narrator-text tokens in the same subcorpus. Within dialogue, the imperfective present strongly correlates with background-setting functions, while perfective present forms cluster in narrative-climax contexts. The paper also documents a statistically significant increase in the proportion of perfect-tense tokens across the interwar decades, which it links to the increasing influence of spoken Belgrade vernacular on literary dialogue norms. Findings are compared with parallel observations in Croatian prose corpora from the same period.

title: Preparing Period-Accurate Dialogue Data: A Methodological Guide for Corpus Linguists and Content Developers
abstract: This book chapter addresses the practical problem of creating linguistically authentic dialogue for historical fiction and related content authoring, drawing on a decade of corpus construction and analysis work on early twentieth-century Serbian prose. The chapter outlines a four-stage workflow: (1) identification and stratified sampling of source texts for a target period; (2) automatic and manual extraction of dialogue spans; (3) compilation of period-specific lexical, morphosyntactic, and pragmatic feature inventories from the extracted data; and (4) validation of drafted dialogue against corpus frequency norms. Concrete examples are drawn from the SerbProsRef corpus, with feature inventories given for three contrasting social registers: educated urban male speech, rural female speech, and bureaucratic-official speech. The chapter also discusses the tension between full historical accuracy and readability, noting that corpus frequencies should function as constraints and tendencies rather than prescriptive rules. Intended audiences include both researchers setting up similar corpus workflows and practitioners in cultural heritage, publishing, and interactive media.

title: A Frequency Dictionary of Dialogue Vocabulary in Serbian Prose, 1890–1945: Compilation, Validation, and Selected Observations
abstract: This paper reports on the compilation and validation of a frequency dictionary of 18,400 lemmas drawn exclusively from dialogue spans in the SerbProsRef corpus. The dictionary covers the full 1890–1945 range and is subdivided into five chronological bands of roughly eleven years each. Lemmatisation of historical spelling variants was performed using a combination of a rule-based normaliser and manual correction of the 2,000 most frequent types. Validation consisted of comparison against three existing historical Serbian dictionaries and assessment of coverage on a held-out set of 50,000 tokens of dialogue from texts outside the corpus. Coverage on the held-out set reaches 94.1 percent at the lemma level. Selected observations concern: (a) the stable core of approximately 800 lemmas present in all five chronological bands; (b) the 120 lemmas that appear exclusively in the pre-1914 band, mostly archaic or Turkish-origin items; and (c) collocational differences between near-synonymous pairs in dialogue contexts. The dictionary will be made available as a searchable online resource.

title: A Treebank Extension for Spoken Serbian: Annotation Scheme and Parsing Experiments
abstract: Existing dependency treebanks for Serbian cover almost exclusively written, edited text. This paper extends the Serbian Dependency Treebank with 9,400 sentences of transcribed spoken language from sociolinguistic interviews, telephone conversations, and classroom interactions. The annotation follows the Universal Dependencies scheme with six additional relation types introduced to handle disfluencies, fragmentary utterances, and topic-drop constructions frequent in spoken Serbian. Inter-annotator agreement measured on a 400-sentence sample reaches LAS of 0.87 and UAS of 0.91. A BiLSTM-based dependency parser trained on the combined written and spoken data achieves LAS 78.3% on the spoken test set, compared with 65.1% when trained on written data only. The paper also includes a frequency analysis of constructions that differ markedly between the spoken and written registers.

title: Metadiscourse Across Generations: Comparing Serbian Research Articles from the 1990s and the 2010s in Three Disciplines
abstract: This chapter contributes to an edited volume on European academic writing traditions by reporting a generational comparison of metadiscourse use in Serbian journal articles. Two cohorts of articles—90 texts from 1992–1997 and 90 texts from 2011–2016—were sampled from sociology, materials science, and pharmacology periodicals. Metadiscourse features were coded using a unified taxonomy to permit direct comparison. Results show statistically significant increases in self-mention and engagement markers across all three disciplines over the twenty-year interval, while hedging density remained relatively stable. Frame markers increased most sharply in materials science. The authors discuss whether the observed shifts reflect genuine rhetorical change, the influence of international peer review norms, or the growing proportion of Serbian researchers with publication experience in English-medium venues. Methodological limitations and directions for further research are addressed.

title: Sensitivity of Winkler Spring Coefficients to Subgrade Modulus Uncertainty in Shallow-Founded RC Frames
abstract: The study examines how uncertainty in the subgrade reaction modulus propagates into the computed dynamic stiffness of strip footings supporting three-storey reinforced concrete frames. A parametric Monte Carlo scheme with 1 200 realisations was applied to a plane-frame model implemented in OpenSees, varying the subgrade modulus over a range representative of medium-dense sand profiles in the Pannonian Basin. Impedance functions were computed at frequencies from 0.5 to 10 Hz using a frequency-domain sub-structuring approach. Results show that a ±30 % variation in the subgrade modulus produces up to 18 % scatter in the fundamental period and up to 24 % scatter in peak base shear under a suite of 20 recorded ground motions scaled to 0.1 g PGA. The sensitivity is strongest for frame aspect ratios between 3 and 5. The paper concludes that simplified fixed-base analyses underestimate period elongation by a median factor of 1.14 for the profile class considered.

title: A Simplified Frequency-Dependent Impedance Model for Strip Footings on Stratified Deposits
abstract: Existing simplified impedance models for strip footings generally assume homogeneous half-space conditions, which rarely match field conditions in alluvial plains. This paper proposes a two-layer frequency-dependent impedance model derived from cone models, calibrated against 3-D finite-element results for layer thickness ratios H/B between 1 and 6 and stiffness contrasts between 2 and 8. The calibration dataset consists of 216 parametric finite-element runs. The proposed expressions reproduce vertical and rocking impedance components with errors below 8 % across the calibration domain and below 13 % in a held-out validation set of 48 cases. An application to a four-storey RC frame building in Sremska Mitrovica shows that accounting for the two-layer profile shifts the fundamental frequency by 0.31 Hz compared with a homogeneous half-space assumption.

title: Calibration of Soil–Structure Interaction Parameters from Ambient Vibration Measurements on Existing RC Buildings in Novi Sad
abstract: Ambient vibration testing was carried out on seven existing three-to-five-storey reinforced concrete frame buildings in Novi Sad, built between 1970 and 1990 on medium-dense sandy gravel. Operational modal analysis using the stochastic subspace identification method identified fundamental frequencies between 1.8 and 3.4 Hz. Fixed-base finite-element models overestimated the measured fundamental frequencies by 6 to 19 %, depending on the building. A direct soil–structure interaction identification procedure was used to back-calculate effective subgrade stiffness values. The calibrated values cluster around 35–55 MN/m² for the subgrade modulus, which is consistent with CPT-derived estimates from nearby boreholes. The calibrated models then reproduce measured frequencies within 3 % and damping ratios within 0.5 percentage points for all seven buildings, providing a validated basis for future predictive modelling.

title: Influence of Foundation Embedment Depth on Period Lengthening of RC Frame Buildings on Sandy Gravel
abstract: Foundation embedment modifies both the static stiffness and the radiation damping of shallow footings, yet its effect on period elongation in low-to-moderate seismic regions is rarely quantified separately. This paper uses a parametric study of 108 OpenSees models representing two-to-six-storey RC frames with strip footings embedded between 0.5 and 2.0 m in a dense sandy gravel profile (shear wave velocity 280–350 m/s). The impedance functions are computed following the approach of Apsel and Luco, adapted for the embedding range. Period elongation due to soil–structure interaction decreases monotonically with embedment depth, from a median ratio of 1.18 at 0.5 m embedment to 1.07 at 2.0 m. The reduction in interaction-induced base shear amplification with increasing embedment is between 5 and 11 percentage points across the frame heights studied.

title: Soil–Structure Interaction in Seismic Assessment: A Review of Simplified Methods Applicable to Low-to-Moderate Seismicity Regions
abstract: This book chapter reviews the development and current state of simplified soil–structure interaction methods intended for design practice in regions where peak ground acceleration rarely exceeds 0.20 g. The treatment covers Winkler-type subgrade models, cone models, and the equivalent-linear sub-structuring approach, tracing each from its theoretical basis to its implementation in regional design codes, including Eurocode 8 and the Serbian seismic design standard. The chapter discusses the conditions under which each method is appropriate, the data required for practical application, and known limitations such as the neglect of kinematic interaction in shallow foundations. Case studies from Serbian and Hungarian design practice are included to illustrate parameter selection. The chapter concludes with a discussion of unresolved issues, including the treatment of soil nonlinearity at small strain amplitudes and the choice of input ground motion for SSI analysis.

title: Rocking Response of Isolated Footings under Moderate Seismic Excitation: Experimental and Numerical Investigation
abstract: Small-scale shaking table tests were performed on isolated square footing specimens (1:10 scale) resting on compacted silty sand (relative density 55 and 75 %) and subjected to 18 recorded ground motion sequences with PGA between 0.08 and 0.22 g. Footing rocking was measured by a pair of inductive displacement transducers. Residual rotations after the strongest inputs reached 0.9 mrad and 0.4 mrad for the lower and higher density specimens, respectively. Numerical simulations using a macro-element model with an associated flow rule reproduced measured peak rotations within 15 % and residual rotations within 25 % for 14 of the 18 records. The two poorest predictions coincided with near-fault pulse-type records, suggesting that the macro-element overestimates recentring for impulsive loading. The study provides a small but locally relevant dataset for validating soil–foundation macro-elements under Pannonian Basin ground motion characteristics.
venue: Earthquake Engineering and Structural Dynamics

title: Period Lengthening Ratios for RC Frame Buildings in the Pannonian Basin: A Dataset from Ambient Vibration Surveys and Analytical Models
abstract: This paper reports fundamental period estimates obtained from operational modal analysis of 23 reinforced concrete frame buildings in northern Serbia and southern Hungary, complemented by analytical fixed-base period estimates using the Eurocode 8 expression and eigenvalue analysis of detailed finite-element models. Measured-to-code period ratios range from 1.08 to 1.41 with a median of 1.22. Ratios increase with building height and with softer soil conditions as characterised by MASW-derived shear wave velocity profiles. Fixed-base finite-element models consistently underestimate measured periods, with a mean error of 14 % compared with 22 % for the Eurocode 8 expression. A simple linear regression model using building height and average shear wave velocity to 10 m depth predicts measured periods with a root-mean-square error of 0.11 s for the dataset, offering a practical correction tool for use in regional seismic hazard assessments.

title: Assessment of Eurocode 8 Soil–Structure Interaction Provisions against Nonlinear Time-History Analyses for Shallow-Founded Frames
abstract: Eurocode 8 Annex D provides optional provisions for accounting for soil–structure interaction in building design, but their accuracy relative to detailed nonlinear analysis has not been systematically evaluated for the low-to-moderate seismicity context of central Europe. This paper compares the Eurocode 8 simplified SSI procedure with results from fully coupled nonlinear time-history analyses in OpenSees for a set of 36 RC frame building configurations (two to eight storeys, three soil classes, two footing sizes). The comparison is made in terms of period elongation ratio, effective damping increase, and peak inter-storey drift. The Eurocode 8 procedure predicts period elongation within 10 % of the time-history results for 28 of 36 configurations but systematically overestimates effective damping by a median of 1.8 percentage points. Overestimation of damping leads to unconservative base shear reductions of up to 9 % in softer soil classes.

title: Footing-Soil Interface Modelling Options in OpenSees for SSI Analyses of RC Frames: A Practical Comparison
abstract: Several contact and interface element formulations are available in OpenSees for modelling the soil–footing boundary, but guidance on their relative merits under seismic loading is sparse. This preprint compares four approaches: a node-to-node zero-length element with p-y springs, a beam-on-nonlinear-Winkler-foundation model, a thin-layer interface element, and a penalty-based contact formulation. All four are applied to the same benchmark four-storey RC frame subject to five ground motion records at 0.10 and 0.15 g PGA. Differences in peak inter-storey drift predictions among the four formulations reach 17 % in the worst case and are below 8 % in the best case. Computational cost differs by a factor of up to 6 between the least and most expensive formulations. Practical recommendations are made for engineering office use, favouring the beam-on-nonlinear-Winkler formulation for most practical cases below 0.20 g.

title: Creep Behaviour of Glulam Beams with Semi-Rigid Connections Under Long-Term Service Loads
abstract: Eight full-scale glulam beams (GL24h, 120 × 360 mm cross-section, 6 m span) fitted with bolted end connections of varying initial stiffness were subjected to sustained mid-span loads of 40 % and 65 % of mean short-term capacity over 18 months in a climate-controlled indoor environment (service class 1). Deflections were recorded weekly by digital displacement loggers. Final deflection at 18 months exceeded Eurocode 5 kdef-based predictions by 12–23 % in beams with more flexible connections, while stiffer connections showed better agreement (within 8 %). The contribution of connection creep to total mid-span deflection was 18–31 % depending on configuration—substantially more than typically assumed. An additive creep model for the combined beam–connection system is proposed, with separate creep coefficients for the timber member and the connection rotational stiffness.

title: Influence of recycled aggregate replacement ratio on the compressive strength development of concrete mixes intended for precast production
abstract: Six concrete mix designs with recycled coarse aggregate replacement ratios of 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% by mass were prepared and cured under controlled conditions replicating a precast plant environment at 20 °C and 65% relative humidity. Compressive strength was measured at 3, 7, 14, 28, and 90 days on 150 mm cube specimens, with 12 replicates per age and mix. Results showed that 28-day compressive strength decreased by approximately 5% at 20% replacement and by 22% at 100% replacement relative to the reference mix. Early strength development up to 7 days was more sensitive to replacement ratio than later-age strength. Water-to-cement ratios were adjusted to achieve equivalent workability across mixes, which partially offset strength reductions. Scatter in compressive strength, quantified by standard deviation, increased monotonically with replacement ratio, reaching 4.8 MPa at full replacement compared with 2.1 MPa for the reference mix. Implications for characteristic strength determination under EN 206 are discussed.
venue: Journal of Concrete Technology and Structural Applications

title: Quantifying mould growth risk at thermal bridges in prefabricated wall panels using long-term humidity monitoring and the WUFI Bio model
abstract: Surface relative humidity was monitored at 24 internal wall corners in six prefabricated apartment buildings in Novi Sad over a period of 18 months using combined temperature–humidity loggers at 15-minute intervals. Corner geometries corresponded to the three most common IMS panel junction types. The WUFI Bio mould growth model was then applied to the measured surface climate datasets to calculate the Biohygrothermal Index (BHI). BHI exceeded the growth threshold at 17 of the 24 monitored corners, with the most critical locations concentrated at northeast-facing external corners on unretrofitted facades. Mean indoor relative humidity in affected apartments was 58%, consistent with overcrowded occupancy in undersized units. The paper discusses the correlation between corner geometry, panel joint conductance, occupancy density, and mould risk, and proposes a triage matrix that housing companies can use to prioritise remedial works without full thermographic surveys.

title: Droplet Size Distribution and Evaporation Rate Comparison Across Three Atomiser Types in a Pilot-Scale Spray Dryer
abstract: This study compared the performance of a rotary atomiser, a two-fluid pressure nozzle, and an ultrasonic nozzle installed in a 5 kg/h pilot-scale spray dryer processing a maltodextrin–water feed solution at 20% solids content. Droplet size distributions were measured by laser diffraction at the dryer inlet, yielding volume-weighted median diameters of 48 µm, 31 µm, and 22 µm for the rotary, two-fluid, and ultrasonic configurations, respectively. A one-dimensional evaporation model based on the D² law was fitted to thermocouple and humidity sensor data collected at three axial positions inside the drying chamber. The fitted evaporation constants differed by up to 34% across atomiser types when inlet air temperature was held constant at 160 °C. Outlet powder moisture content ranged from 3.1% to 4.8% across configurations under otherwise identical conditions. The results indicate that the ultrasonic nozzle achieved the lowest residual moisture but required 18% more specific energy input per kilogram of dried product compared with the two-fluid nozzle, a trade-off relevant for energy-sensitive production environments.

title: Predicting Shell Thickness and Hollow Particle Formation During Spray Drying of Whey Protein Isolate Using a Crust Formation Model
abstract: Spray drying of whey protein isolate (WPI) frequently produces hollow or partially collapsed particles, which affects bulk density and reconstitution behaviour. This work applied a crust formation model coupling internal diffusion of protein solutes with surface tension-driven shell solidification to predict the critical solidification time as a function of initial droplet diameter, inlet air temperature, and feed concentration. Feed solutions at 15%, 20%, and 25% WPI were spray dried at inlet temperatures of 140 °C, 160 °C, and 180 °C using a two-fluid nozzle. Particle cross-sections prepared by cryogenic milling and examined by scanning electron microscopy showed shell thickness values between 1.8 µm and 6.4 µm. Model predictions agreed with measured shell thickness within ±15% across 22 of 27 experimental conditions. Buckling index calculations indicated that hollow particle formation was promoted at inlet temperatures above 160 °C combined with feed concentrations below 20%, consistent with experimental yields of collapsed morphologies. The validated model provides a basis for selecting operating conditions that favour dense, spherical particles for pharmaceutical powder applications.

title: Energy Benchmarking of Spray Drying Operations for Probiotic Encapsulation: Specific Evaporation Cost as a Function of Inlet–Outlet Temperature Differential
abstract: Spray drying is the dominant industrial method for producing probiotic powders, yet energy consumption data reported across published studies are rarely comparable because of inconsistent system boundaries and differing feed compositions. This conference paper presents a structured benchmarking framework applied to a laboratory-scale spray dryer (1.5 kg/h evaporative capacity) processing Lactobacillus rhamnosus suspended in skim milk carrier at three solids concentrations (10%, 15%, 20%) and four inlet–outlet temperature differentials (ΔT = 90, 100, 110, 120 °C). Specific evaporation cost, defined as megajoules per kilogram of water evaporated, was calculated from logged electrical power, inlet air flow rate, and outlet humidity measurements. Values ranged from 4.1 MJ/kg at ΔT = 120 °C and 20% solids to 7.8 MJ/kg at ΔT = 90 °C and 10% solids. Probiotic viability, measured by plate count after drying, showed no statistically significant difference across ΔT conditions when outlet temperature was kept below 80 °C. The framework and dataset are provided as a supplementary spreadsheet to facilitate comparison with industrial-scale installations.
venue: Proceedings of the 9th Central European Symposium on Food and Bioprocess Engineering

title: Statistical downscaling of satellite-derived solar irradiance products for sub-regional yield assessment in Vojvodina
abstract: Satellite-derived solar irradiance products provide spatial coverage essential for regional planning but typically carry spatial resolutions of 3–10 km and may exhibit systematic biases relative to ground measurements. This paper applies a statistical downscaling and bias-correction scheme to two commercial and one open-access satellite products over the Vojvodina administrative region, using a network of eleven pyranometer stations operated by the authors and collaborating institutes between 2014 and 2019. Correction is performed separately for clear-sky and overcast conditions using quantile mapping on monthly sub-samples. After correction, the mean absolute error in annual GHI is reduced from 42–68 kWh/m² to 14–21 kWh/m² across the validation stations. The corrected gridded product is then used to produce a 5 km resolution annual irradiation map for Vojvodina and to estimate the inter-site variability of expected PV energy yield, which reaches ±4.2% at the 90th percentile range across the region.

title: Egzergijska analiza postrojenja za sušenje u prehrambenoj industriji: studija slučaja mlekare u Vojvodini
abstract: U radu je primenjena egzergijska analiza na industrijsko postrojenje za sušenje raspršivanjem u mlekari kapaciteta 8 t/h praškastog mleka. Identifikovani su glavni tokovi egzergijskog razaranja kroz sve komponente sistema: komoru za sušenje, rekuperator toplote dimnih gasova i kondenzator. Ukupno razaranje egzergije iznosi 4,2 MW, od čega 61% otpada na komoru za sušenje. Egzergijska efikasnost postrojenja određena je na 34,7%, što je znatno niže od referentnih vrednosti za slična postrojenja u EU. Predložene su dve mogućnosti unapređenja zasnovane na povećanju stepena predhrevanja ulaznog vazduha. Analizom osetljivosti utvrđeno je da povećanje temperature predhrevanja za 20 °C smanjuje ukupno egzergijsko razaranje za oko 9%. Rezultati ukazuju na konkretne prioritete za rekonstrukciju postrojenja uz minimalna kapitalna ulaganja.

title: Characterising API-Level Incompatibilities in Open-Source Android Applications: An Empirical Survey
abstract: This study examines the prevalence and distribution of API-level incompatibilities across 320 open-source Android applications drawn from a curated repository of F-Droid projects. Applications were analysed using a combination of static bytecode inspection and dynamic instrumentation across eight Android API levels ranging from level 16 to level 28. Incompatibilities were classified into four categories: deprecated API usage, removed method invocations, permission model changes, and layout inflation failures. Results show that 61% of surveyed applications contain at least one deprecated API call, and 18% exhibit runtime crashes attributable to removed or renamed methods when executed on API levels two or more versions above the target declared in the manifest. The study further correlates repository commit frequency with incompatibility density, finding that applications updated more than twice per year exhibit 34% fewer critical incompatibilities. The classification taxonomy and annotated dataset are released publicly to support further research.
venue: Journal of Software Engineering Practice

title: A Regression Testing Strategy for Android Applications Targeting Multiple API Levels Simultaneously
abstract: Maintaining regression test suites that remain valid across a wide span of Android API levels is a practical challenge for small development teams. This paper proposes a layered test architecture in which test cases are tagged with applicability metadata specifying minimum and maximum API levels, deprecation-aware skip conditions, and device-class constraints such as screen density and form factor. The architecture was implemented as an extension to the Espresso UI testing framework and evaluated through a longitudinal case study with three mobile application projects maintained by student teams over two academic semesters. The extended framework reduced the number of false-positive test failures caused by platform differences by 47% compared to unmodified Espresso suites run across the same device pool. The approach added an average overhead of 9% to test execution time. Interviewed developers reported reduced confusion when interpreting test results on mixed-API-level device farms.

title: Static Detection of Deprecated API Usage Chains in Android Codebases Using Interprocedural Call Graph Analysis
abstract: Deprecated API calls in Android applications are often not isolated but form chains in which a deprecated method invokes other deprecated or soon-to-be-removed methods across multiple classes and libraries. This paper describes a static analysis approach that constructs interprocedural call graphs from compiled APK files using a modified version of the Soot analysis framework and identifies deprecation chains of length two or more. The technique was applied to 150 applications sampled from five categories on the Google Play Store, each analysed against the API level corresponding to its targetSdkVersion. Deprecation chains were found in 43% of applications, with an average chain length of 2.7 nodes. Chains involving third-party library code accounted for 61% of detected instances, highlighting the role of library update lag in fragmentation risk. A prioritisation score based on chain length and method removal probability is proposed to guide developer remediation efforts.

title: Fragmentation Impact on Mobile Application Energy Consumption Across Android Versions
abstract: Platform fragmentation affects not only functional correctness but also non-functional characteristics of Android applications. This study investigates whether energy consumption profiles of Android applications differ systematically across API levels due to changes in system services, scheduling, and I/O subsystems. Twelve applications from diverse categories were instrumented using Monsoon power monitors and executed on eight physical devices running Android 7.1 through 12.0 under controlled workloads. Statistically significant differences in energy consumption between API levels were found for nine of twelve applications, with median differences ranging from 4% to 31% across tested scenarios. Multimedia and background-sync-heavy applications showed the largest variance. The paper presents a lightweight test harness that automates power measurement across a device pool and produces cross-version energy comparison reports, and discusses the implications for battery-sensitive deployment decisions.

title: Continuous Integration Pipelines for Multi-Version Android Testing: Configuration Patterns and Failure Analysis
abstract: Continuous integration (CI) adoption in Android projects frequently stalls because configuring emulator matrices across multiple API levels is error-prone and time-consuming. This chapter reviews common CI configuration patterns observed in 200 public GitHub repositories hosting Android projects, focusing on how developers specify emulator targets, handle flaky tests attributable to version-specific emulator behaviour, and manage CI execution time budgets. Five recurrent anti-patterns are identified, including hard-coded API level values in CI scripts and the absence of conditional test skipping for deprecated paths. For each anti-pattern, a recommended configuration pattern with concrete YAML examples is provided. Flaky test rates attributable to emulator instability are estimated at 8–14% across the studied repositories, with higher rates on API levels below 24. The chapter closes with a decision guide for teams selecting between physical device clouds and local emulator matrices.

title: DroidDelta: A Differential Testing Framework for Identifying Behavioural Changes Between Consecutive Android Releases
abstract: Each Android release modifies system behaviour in ways not always reflected in API changelogs, creating latent compatibility defects. DroidDelta is a differential testing framework that automatically executes identical Espresso test scripts on two Android versions side-by-side, captures UI state snapshots at each interaction step, and uses a pixel-cluster comparison algorithm to identify rendering divergences alongside logcat-based behavioural divergence detection. The tool was evaluated comparing Android 12 versus 13 and Android 13 versus 14 release pairs across 30 applications. DroidDelta detected 124 rendering divergences and 41 behavioural divergences not reported in the official release notes. Manual inspection confirmed 87% of rendering divergences as genuine compatibility concerns and 78% of behavioural divergences as developer-relevant. Average per-application analysis time was 22 minutes on a mid-range workstation paired with two physical devices. The framework is designed to integrate as a CI stage triggered by SDK update events.

title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Lint-Based Fragmentation Warnings in Reducing Compatibility Defect Density
abstract: Android Lint includes a set of checks for fragmentation-related issues, but their effectiveness in practice has not been systematically evaluated. This study compares compatibility defect densities in 80 Android application projects before and after developers were asked to address all Lint fragmentation warnings in a controlled setting. Projects were drawn from an industry partner pool and ranged from 5,000 to 120,000 lines of Kotlin and Java code. Defects were measured by executing a standardised test suite across API levels 26 through 34 before and after warning remediation. Addressing Lint warnings reduced API-level-attributable defect density by 29% on average, with the largest reductions in projects with higher initial warning counts. However, 54% of defects detected by the test suite had no corresponding Lint warning, indicating substantial gaps in Lint's fragmentation coverage. A supplementary checklist of 18 fragmentation risk patterns not covered by Lint is provided.

title: Predicting Compatibility Risk of Android Library Updates Using Dependency Graph Metrics
abstract: When Android applications update a third-party library, the new library version may introduce or resolve platform compatibility issues in ways that are difficult to anticipate. This paper presents a predictive model for compatibility risk that uses dependency graph metrics—including fan-in, fan-out, version distance, and deprecation ratio of exported symbols—computed from library release artefacts available on Maven Central. A dataset of 1,140 library update events across 95 applications was constructed retrospectively by replaying version histories and running DroidDelta-based compatibility checks. A gradient-boosted classifier trained on dependency graph metrics achieved an AUC of 0.81 in predicting whether a library update would introduce a new compatibility defect. The model performs best for multimedia and networking libraries and worst for UI component libraries. Integration of the predictor as a pre-merge CI check is described, along with a discussion of threshold selection for different risk tolerances.
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology

title: Estimation of Flory–Huggins interaction parameters for poorly soluble drugs in hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate using melting point depression
abstract: Flory–Huggins interaction parameters (χ) were determined for three BCS Class II drugs—fenofibrate, indomethacin, and carbamazepine—dispersed in hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMC-AS) grades MF, MG, and HF. Melting point depression experiments were performed by modulated DSC over a polymer volume fraction range of 0.1–0.9. χ values ranged from −0.42 to +0.31 depending on drug and polymer grade, indicating that miscibility is grade-specific and not predictable from gross polymer chemistry alone. Calculated spinodal and binodal boundaries showed that fenofibrate–HPMC-AS MF mixtures were miscible across the full composition range at 25 °C, while carbamazepine–HPMC-AS HF showed a miscibility window limited to polymer-rich compositions above 70 wt% polymer. The results were validated against 24-month ambient-storage XRPD data, and the predicted miscibility limits correctly identified the compositions that remained X-ray amorphous. The approach provides a practical screening tool for selecting polymer grade before spray-drying trials.

title: Effect of feed concentration and inlet temperature on residual moisture and amorphous content of spray-dried indomethacin–PVP VA64 dispersions
abstract: A two-factor central composite design was used to examine the combined influence of feed solution concentration (5–20% w/v) and inlet air temperature (100–160 °C) on the properties of spray-dried indomethacin–polyvinylpyrrolidone vinyl acetate 64 (PVP VA64) dispersions prepared from ethanol:water 9:1 v/v. Responses included residual solvent content (Karl Fischer titration), particle yield, bulk density, amorphous fraction (quantitative XRPD), and glass transition temperature (DSC). Residual moisture varied from 0.4% to 2.1% w/w across the design space and was the most influential predictor of glass transition temperature depression, which followed the Gordon–Taylor equation with a k parameter of 0.22. At feed concentrations above 15% w/v, partial crystallisation was detected in the collected powder regardless of inlet temperature. The study defines an operating window—feed concentration below 12% w/v, inlet temperature 130–150 °C—that consistently yields fully amorphous product with Tg above 60 °C.
