title: Recrystallisation kinetics of spray-dried itraconazole–HPMC dispersions at 40 °C / 75% RH: a time-resolved XRPD study
abstract: Spray-dried dispersions of itraconazole in hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC E5 and E15) at drug loadings of 20, 30, and 40 wt% were stored at 40 °C and 75% relative humidity and characterised by X-ray powder diffraction at 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, and 24 weeks. Crystalline itraconazole Form I was the sole polymorph detected upon recrystallisation. At 20 wt% drug loading, neither HPMC grade showed detectable crystallinity after 24 weeks. At 40 wt% drug loading, Form I crystallinity reached 18% in HPMC E5 dispersions and 11% in HPMC E15 dispersions after 12 weeks, with no further increase at 24 weeks, suggesting a plateau governed by residual amorphous drug fraction. The Avrami exponent n derived from isothermal crystallisation data was 1.1–1.4, consistent with surface-initiated one-dimensional growth. Water activity measurements using DVS indicated that moisture uptake occurred predominantly in the HPMC phase and that the drug-rich domains remained effectively plasticiser-depleted below 60% RH, explaining the loading-dependent stability threshold.

title: Plasticisation of HPMC-AS by water: quantification via modulated DSC and implications for spray-dried dispersion design
abstract: The Tg–water activity relationship for HPMC-AS grades MF, MG, and HF was mapped by exposing polymer films to thirteen relative humidity levels (11–97% RH) and measuring Tg by modulated DSC. The Gordon–Taylor k values for water plasticisation were 7.1, 6.8, and 5.3 for MF, MG, and HF grades respectively, indicating that the more hydrophilic MF and MG grades depress Tg more steeply with absorbed moisture. At 75% RH and 40 °C the Tg of HPMC-AS MF fell to 42 °C, only 2 °C above the storage temperature. Dynamic vapour sorption isotherms fit a Park model and showed sigmoidal moisture uptake. For spray-dried dispersions containing 25 wt% felodipine in HPMC-AS MF, 18-month XRPD monitoring showed onset crystallisation at 75% RH but not at 60% RH, directly correlating with the temperature margin to Tg. The data support a minimum Tg–T margin of at least 20 °C at the intended storage humidity as a conservative formulation criterion.

title: Prediction of long-term physical stability of amorphous solid dispersions using accelerated isothermal crystallisation data and the Arrhenius equation
abstract: A predictive framework was developed to estimate room-temperature crystallisation half-lives of spray-dried amorphous dispersions from accelerated isothermal DSC crystallisation experiments conducted at three temperatures above Tg (Tg + 10, Tg + 20, Tg + 30 °C). Five systems were studied: fenofibrate–PVP VA64, carbamazepine–HPMC-AS MF, griseofulvin–Soluplus, piroxicam–PVP K30, and nifedipine–HPMC E15, all at 30 wt% drug loading. Activation energies for crystallisation ranged from 96 to 218 kJ mol−1. Extrapolated half-lives at 25 °C and 40% RH agreed with observed 30-month stability outcomes to within a factor of 1.8 for four of five systems; the griseofulvin–Soluplus system was underestimated by a factor of 3.2, possibly due to antiplasticisation effects not captured by the Arrhenius model. The method requires approximately 48 hours of DSC measurement per system and offers a practical early-stage stability screen.

title: Influence of spray-drying process parameters on particle morphology and surface energy of amorphous dispersions: a cohesion–adhesion analysis
abstract: Surface energies (dispersive and polar components) of spray-dried dispersions of celecoxib in HPMC-AS MF were measured by IGC-ID (inverse gas chromatography at infinite dilution) for powders prepared at five inlet temperatures (90–150 °C) and three atomisation air flow rates (357, 473, and 601 L h−1). Scanning electron microscopy showed a transition from buckled, raisin-like particles to hollow spheres as atomisation flow rate increased, with a corresponding increase in dispersive surface energy from 34.2 to 41.8 mJ m−2. Higher dispersive surface energy correlated with faster moisture uptake during DVS analysis (r = 0.88), suggesting that process-induced surface heterogeneity affects storage behaviour independently of bulk composition. The polar component of surface energy was insensitive to process parameters, remaining within 5.1–6.4 mJ m−2 across all conditions. Results indicate that atomisation flow rate is an important but often overlooked process variable for dispersion physical stability.

title: Co-amorphous systems as an alternative to polymer-based dispersions: miscibility and stability of naproxen–indomethacin binary amorphous mixtures
abstract: Binary amorphous mixtures of naproxen and indomethacin were prepared by spray drying from ethanol at six molar ratios (1:5, 1:3, 1:1, 3:1, 5:1, and neat amorphous components) and characterised by DSC, XRPD, and solid-state NMR. A single composition-dependent Tg was observed for all mixtures, consistent with complete miscibility, and fitted well (R² = 0.994) to the Gordon–Taylor equation with k = 1.18. Solid-state 13C NMR showed changes in the carbonyl chemical shift of indomethacin relative to the neat amorphous form, suggesting hydrogen-bond formation with the carboxylic acid group of naproxen. At 40 °C/75% RH, equimolar mixtures remained fully amorphous for 12 months, compared with 4 months for neat amorphous indomethacin and 8 months for neat amorphous naproxen. The enhanced stability is attributed to a combination of Tg elevation (equimolar Tg = 57 °C vs. 42 °C and 51 °C for neat components) and intermolecular hydrogen bonding that reduces molecular mobility. The co-amorphous approach is presented as a polymer-free route for BCS Class II drug combinations.

title: Mechanistic modelling of water sorption in spray-dried HPMC–drug dispersions using a two-domain Fickian diffusion model
abstract: A two-domain diffusion model was developed to describe water transport in spray-dried dispersions of ibuprofen in HPMC E15, distinguishing diffusion within the HPMC matrix from diffusion in drug-rich domains. Gravimetric sorption data were collected by DVS at 25 °C from 0 to 90% RH in 10% RH steps, with 240-minute equilibration periods. The model was fitted to the kinetic sorption traces at each humidity step using a nonlinear least-squares algorithm, yielding domain-specific diffusion coefficients and partition coefficients. Diffusivity in HPMC-rich domains was approximately 40-fold higher than in drug-rich domains at 60% RH, increasing to 90-fold at 80% RH. The model correctly reproduced hysteresis observed on desorption and predicted the humidity threshold above which drug-domain saturation occurs, which was independently confirmed by Raman mapping. The approach reduces reliance on empirical sorption isotherms and provides physically interpretable parameters for formulation optimisation.

title: Screening of excipient combinations for spray-dried dispersions of a heat-sensitive API: the role of outlet temperature control and antiplasticiser addition
abstract: A heat-sensitive model compound (designated API-7, a BCS Class II lactam derivative with degradation onset at 118 °C) was spray-dried with five polymer carriers—PVP VA64, HPMC-AS MF, Soluplus, Eudragit L100-55, and a 1:1 blend of PVP VA64 and Eudragit L100-55—at outlet temperatures kept below 65 °C by adjusting feed flow rate and atomisation gas flow. Excipient function was extended by adding silica (Aerosil 200, 2% w/w) as antiplasticiser. Formulations were characterised for chemical purity (HPLC), amorphous content, Tg, and moisture uptake. The 1:1 PVP VA64–Eudragit L100-55 blend with silica yielded the highest Tg (84 °C) and the lowest moisture uptake at 75% RH (4.1% w/w), while maintaining API purity above 99.5% and full amorphicity. Silica addition raised Tg by 6–11 °C across all polymer systems, consistent with antiplasticisation, and reduced moisture uptake by 15–28% relative to silica-free controls. Chemical stability under stressed conditions (40 °C/75% RH, 3 months) was acceptable only for the two systems containing Eudragit L100-55.

title: Integrating design space construction with MSPC dashboards for day-to-day operation of a pan coating line: practical framework and pilot implementation
abstract: This paper describes a practical framework for integrating quality-by-design design space information with real-time MSPC monitoring in a pan coating operation at pilot scale. The design space for aqueous ethylcellulose sustained-release coating of 500 mg metformin hydrochloride tablets was established using a Definitive Screening Design (12 runs) exploring five process parameters, yielding a Bayesian design space with 95% probability of meeting dissolution specifications at 2 h and 8 h. MPCA monitoring models built from 17 reference batches within the design space were deployed alongside the design space boundary in a unified dashboard for the pan coating operator. A six-month pilot implementation period covered 41 production batches. The dashboard correctly flagged all four batches that subsequently failed dissolution testing, while generating two false alarms. Integration of design space contour overlays with MPCA scores provided operators with directional guidance for corrective action that pure MSPC charts do not supply. Operator feedback collected via structured interviews is reported.

title: Continuous enzymatic phospholipid synthesis in a packed-bed reactor: residence time distribution and productivity analysis
abstract: A continuous packed-bed reactor (PBR) packed with Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase immobilised on acrylic beads (20 g, bed volume 45 mL) was evaluated for phosphatidylcholine synthesis as an alternative to batch operation. Substrate feed (lysophosphatidylcholine and oleic acid, 1:3 molar ratio in tert-amyl alcohol/water 96:4 v/v) was delivered at flow rates of 0.2–1.5 mL/min. Residence time distribution was characterised by tracer experiments with acetone, yielding a Bodenstein number of 28, indicating near-plug-flow behaviour. At 0.5 mL/min, PC yield was 65.8 ± 2.3% at steady state, with a volumetric productivity of 4.1 g PC/L·h, approximately 2.4-fold higher than comparable batch experiments. Enzyme half-life in continuous mode was 22 days compared with 14 days in batch mode. The PBR approach reduces downstream processing volume and improves throughput, making it attractive for scale-up to pilot level.

title: Formation of N-nitroso-triacetyl-glucosamine as an unexpected nitrosamine in excipient–API interactions: identification and structural characterisation
abstract: During forced degradation studies of a film-coated tablet formulation containing an amino-functionalised API and partially deacetylated chitosan excipient, an unknown peak was detected by LC-HRMS at m/z 349.1247 [M+H]⁺. Exact mass and MS² fragmentation data were consistent with N-nitroso-triacetyl-glucosamine (NTAG), a previously unreported nitrosamine formed by nitrosation of the free amine on a deacetylated chitosan monomer unit. The compound was synthesised independently for confirmation and quantified by isotope dilution LC-MS/MS; concentrations reached 0.21 ppm in tablets stored at 40 °C/75% relative humidity for six months. In-silico genotoxicity predictions (two independently applied QSAR tools) gave a positive alert for structural alerts class 12 (α,β-unsaturated carbonyl adjacent to nitroso group), indicating a genotoxic concern under ICH M7 category 2. The paper discusses the need to include polysaccharide-based excipients in nitrosamine risk assessments for amino-API formulations.

title: Prevalence of CHIP-associated somatic variants in a cross-sectional cohort of adults with premature carotid atherosclerosis in Vojvodina
abstract: Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been linked to excess cardiovascular risk beyond conventional lipid-based models, but population-level data from Central and Eastern Europe remain sparse. We enrolled 214 adults aged 40–65 years attending the lipid clinic of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina who had carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) ≥ 0.9 mm confirmed by standardised B-mode ultrasound. Targeted sequencing of a 36-gene haematopoietic panel was performed on peripheral blood DNA using an Illumina MiSeq platform with a variant allele fraction (VAF) cut-off of 2%. CHIP was detected in 38 participants (17.8%). The most frequently mutated genes were DNMT3A (42% of CHIP carriers) and TET2 (34%). CHIP carriers had significantly higher high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (median 3.1 vs 1.6 mg/L, p = 0.003) and higher cIMT (0.98 vs 0.91 mm, p = 0.018) compared with non-carriers after adjustment for age, sex, smoking status, and LDL cholesterol. These findings suggest that CHIP contributes to a pro-inflammatory vascular milieu in this regional population and support the case for larger prospective studies.

title: Detection thresholds and false-positive rates in low-depth targeted sequencing for CHIP screening: a comparison of three bioinformatics pipelines
abstract: Reliable CHIP detection in clinical research depends heavily on the bioinformatics pipeline used to call low-frequency somatic variants, yet direct pipeline comparisons in real-world haematological samples are uncommon. We extracted DNA from peripheral blood mononuclear cells of 40 donors (20 previously confirmed CHIP carriers, 20 healthy controls) and processed all samples through a standardised 36-gene panel at mean depths of 500×, 1000×, and 2000×. Variant calls were processed in parallel using three pipelines: VarScan2, Mutect2, and a custom ensemble approach combining both callers with a majority-vote filter. Sensitivity and specificity were calculated against orthogonal droplet digital PCR validation. At 500× depth and a 2% VAF threshold, Mutect2 achieved sensitivity of 88% with a false-positive rate of 6%, while VarScan2 reached 81% sensitivity and 11% false positives. The ensemble approach improved sensitivity to 91% with a false-positive rate of 4% at 1000×. These results inform sequencing depth and pipeline choices for ongoing CHIP research in resource-limited clinical laboratory settings.

title: Diastolic dysfunction assessed by tissue Doppler imaging in postmenopausal women with subclinical hypothyroidism
abstract: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD) may represent an early cardiac consequence of subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH), but data in postmenopausal women are limited. We prospectively enrolled 92 postmenopausal women (≥12 months amenorrhoea); 44 had SCH (TSH 4.5–9.8 mIU/L) and 48 were age-matched euthyroid controls. Standard transthoracic echocardiography with tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) was performed. The E/e' ratio, a surrogate for left ventricular filling pressure, was significantly higher in the SCH group (9.6 ± 1.8 vs. 8.1 ± 1.5, p = 0.002). The proportion meeting criteria for grade I diastolic dysfunction was 52% in SCH versus 27% in controls (p = 0.01). TSH correlated positively with E/e' (r = 0.38, p < 0.001) independently of age and metabolic variables. These results indicate that the myocardium is a clinically relevant target of mild thyroid hormone insufficiency in this population.

title: Lyapunov time estimates for orbits in the outer asteroid belt using the MEGNO indicator
abstract: We apply the Mean Exponential Growth factor of Nearby Orbits (MEGNO) to a sample of 1 240 test particles distributed across the 3:1 and 5:2 mean-motion resonances with Jupiter, integrating each trajectory for 10 Myr using a fourth-order symplectic leapfrog scheme with a time step of 0.01 yr. For strongly chaotic orbits the MEGNO value converges to 2 within roughly 0.5 Myr, while weakly chaotic orbits require integration times exceeding 5 Myr before the indicator stabilises. We find a bimodal distribution of Lyapunov times centred near 0.18 Myr and 1.4 Myr, with the shorter peak dominated by orbits in the 3:1 gap. Comparison with the classical maximum Lyapunov exponent computed over the same interval shows that MEGNO reaches reliable estimates roughly four times faster in CPU time. The results confirm a sharp boundary in eccentricity near e = 0.15 below which regular orbits persist for the full integration window, consistent with analytical KAM estimates reported in earlier literature.

title: Frequency map analysis of the Sun–Jupiter–Saturn–Uranus four-body problem over 500 Myr
abstract: We perform frequency map analysis (FMA) on the reduced Sun–Jupiter–Saturn–Uranus system, treating Uranus as a test planet with initial conditions drawn from a 60 × 60 grid in semi-major axis and eccentricity space centred on its nominal orbit. Each trajectory is integrated for 500 Myr using the SABA4 symplectic integrator. Fundamental frequencies are extracted from windowed fast Fourier transforms applied to complex orbital elements, following the method of Laskar. The resulting frequency map reveals four distinct chaotic web branches associated with secular resonances between Jupiter and Saturn precession frequencies. Orbits within these branches show frequency drift rates of order 10^{-4} per Myr. About 6.3 % of sampled initial conditions are classified as chaotic by a frequency diffusion index exceeding 0.01. We also construct a stability map colour-coded by the diffusion index, which shows a layered structure consistent with the expected topology of Arnold resonance zones in a three-degree-of-freedom system.

title: Arnold diffusion rates in a 2.5-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian model: dependence on perturbation amplitude
abstract: We study numerically the rate of Arnold diffusion in a model Hamiltonian consisting of two coupled nonlinear pendula perturbed by a weak periodic forcing, forming a 2.5-degree-of-freedom system. The perturbation amplitude ε is varied over the range 10^{-4} to 5 × 10^{-2} in steps of half an order of magnitude. For each value of ε we track 500 orbits initialised on a single resonance web branch and measure the mean squared action displacement as a function of time over 10^8 periods. In the volume-preserving regime (ε < 10^{-3}) diffusion is consistent with a power-law D ∝ ε^{2.8 ± 0.2}, in reasonable agreement with theoretical predictions from Nekhoroshev theory. Above ε ≈ 5 × 10^{-3} the diffusion coefficient saturates and the scaling breaks down, indicative of overlap between neighbouring resonance channels. We also compare diffusion coefficients obtained from the fast Lyapunov indicator (FLI) contour maps with direct action-space measurements and find good qualitative agreement, though the FLI maps overestimate the boundary of the diffusion zone by roughly 12 %.

title: Chaos indicators in Trojans of Saturn: a comparative study of MEGNO, FLI and the Smaller Alignment Index
abstract: We apply three widely used chaos indicators—MEGNO, the fast Lyapunov indicator (FLI), and the Smaller Alignment Index (SALI)—to a uniform grid of 2 500 test Trojans of Saturn in the planar elliptic restricted three-body problem, spanning libration amplitude from 1° to 75° and eccentricity from 0 to 0.12. Each orbit is integrated for 20 Myr. The three indicators classify 78 %, 81 %, and 74 % of orbits consistently as regular or chaotic; disagreements cluster near the boundary of the chaotic sea and in thin resonance chains. Computation times per orbit scale as 1:1.3:0.7 for MEGNO:FLI:SALI. SALI is fastest but gives false-regular assignments for 4.2 % of borderline orbits that FLI correctly identifies as chaotic. A combined decision rule requiring agreement of at least two indicators reduces misclassification to under 1 % at a cost of roughly 1.15× the single-indicator run time. The stability map derived from the combined rule shows a triangular stable core extending to libration amplitudes of 45° for e < 0.04.

title: Symplectic correctors for high-order leapfrog integrators applied to planetary N-body systems
abstract: We investigate the application of symplectic corrector maps to the SABA family of integrators for Hamiltonian systems of the form H = T(p) + εV(q). Four corrector levels (0th through 3rd order) are implemented and tested on the Sun–Jupiter–Saturn system over integration spans of 1 Gyr. Energy error is monitored through the relative change in the Jacobi constant. At ε = 10^{-3} a 3rd-order corrector reduces the RMS energy error by a factor of 28 compared with the uncorrected SABA4 integrator at equal step size. We carry out a step-size convergence study at six step sizes from 0.005 yr to 0.5 yr, showing that the corrected scheme maintains near-machine-precision energy conservation up to step sizes of 0.05 yr, roughly four times larger than those required by the uncorrected integrator for the same error tolerance. The correctors are implemented in an open Fortran 90 module and benchmarked on a 16-core shared-memory cluster; a 1 Gyr integration of a 5-planet system requires approximately 11 hours with the corrected SABA4 scheme at step 0.04 yr.

title: Long-term orbital evolution of hypothetical Earth-mass planets in the habitable zone of binary star systems
abstract: We examine the dynamical stability of Earth-mass test planets in the habitable zones of 12 fictitious S-type binary systems with mass ratios μ ranging from 0.1 to 0.5 and binary eccentricities e_b from 0 to 0.6. For each system a 40 × 20 grid in test-planet semi-major axis and eccentricity is integrated for 100 Myr using a Bulirsch–Stoer adaptive integrator. Stability is assessed via the MEGNO indicator and by direct monitoring of orbit crossing. Stable zones shrink monotonically with increasing binary eccentricity, losing approximately 15 % of their radial extent per 0.1 increase in e_b. For μ = 0.3 and e_b = 0.4 no stable orbit survives beyond 0.78 times the critical semi-major axis predicted by Holman and Wiegert's empirical formula, suggesting that the formula overestimates stability boundaries for intermediate mass ratios. We also track the secular evolution of inclination for 60 selected stable orbits and find libration amplitudes below 4° over the full integration, confirming planar stability.

title: Resonance overlap and the onset of global chaos in a simplified asteroid belt model
abstract: Using a planar elliptic restricted three-body model with Jupiter on a fixed orbit at e_J = 0.048, we construct a Chirikov resonance overlap criterion for the asteroid belt region between 2.1 and 3.3 au. Overlap widths for 34 mean-motion resonances up to order 5 are estimated analytically from the pendulum approximation and compared with numerically determined widths from surface-of-section maps for 12 selected resonances. Analytic estimates agree with numerical widths to within 18 % for low-order resonances but deviate by up to 40 % for fifth-order resonances. We then seed a 200 × 50 grid in (a, e) with test particles and integrate for 5 Myr, identifying the chaotic fraction in each 0.01-au strip. Strips where the analytic overlap criterion is satisfied show a chaotic fraction of 83 %, versus 21 % in non-overlapping strips. The transition region, where the criterion is marginally satisfied, yields intermediate chaotic fractions of 45–60 %, consistent with partial overlap of resonance wings.

title: Phase-space structure of the 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Jupiter from a high-resolution FLI map
abstract: We compute a 1 200 × 1 200 pixel fast Lyapunov indicator (FLI) map of the 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Jupiter in the (a, e) plane, covering semi-major axes from 3.20 to 3.30 au and eccentricities from 0 to 0.35. Each pixel represents a single orbit integrated for 2 Myr under the planar elliptic restricted three-body approximation with Jupiter's current orbital elements. The map reveals three distinct regular islands embedded in the chaotic sea at eccentricities of 0.04, 0.13, and 0.22, which we identify as bifurcations of the family of symmetric periodic orbits. The innermost island shrinks by approximately 70 % when Jupiter's eccentricity is increased from the nominal value to 0.06 in a parameter sensitivity test. We compare the FLI map with an independent SALI map computed on a coarser 400 × 400 grid and find structural agreement at scales above 0.001 au, with the FLI map resolving thin chaotic layers approximately 0.0003 au wide that are missed by SALI at the coarser resolution.

title: Diffusion along thin resonance channels in a 3-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian: a numerical study with implications for Kuiper Belt dynamics
abstract: We examine diffusion along the resonance web of a 3-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian composed of three coupled quartic oscillators with a weak inter-mode coupling ε ranging from 10^{-5} to 10^{-2}. For ε = 10^{-4}, Arnold diffusion along thin resonance channels is detectable only after integration times exceeding 10^9 unperturbed periods, with mean-squared action displacement growing as t^{0.7 ± 0.05}, suggesting anomalous sub-diffusion. At ε = 10^{-3} the exponent rises to 0.93, approaching normal diffusion. We then transfer these results qualitatively to a Kuiper Belt context by mapping the model parameters to the Neptune 3:2 resonance geometry and estimating diffusion lifetimes for Plutino-like orbits. Estimated diffusion timescales across the resonance separatrix range from 2 to 20 Gyr depending on initial eccentricity, consistent with the observed population surviving over the age of the solar system. The study also benchmarks three parallelisation strategies on the university cluster, finding that orbit-level MPI parallelism gives 94 % efficiency on 32 cores.

title: Analytical and numerical bounds on the stability lifetime of near-Earth asteroid families under the Yarkovsky effect
abstract: We combine Nekhoroshev stability estimates with a simplified Yarkovsky drift model to bound the orbital lifetimes of test bodies in three fictitious near-Earth asteroid families, designated here as NF-1, NF-2, and NF-3. Each family is modelled as a cloud of 300 particles in the initial osculating element space around a parent body, with Yarkovsky semi-major axis drift rates drawn from a uniform distribution between 3 × 10^{-5} and 2 × 10^{-4} au/Myr based on typical thermal parameters for S-type bodies. Particles are integrated for 50 Myr using a Bulirsch–Stoer integrator including all eight planets. The Nekhoroshev confinement time is estimated analytically for each initial condition and compared with the numerically observed first escape time from a 0.05-au neighbourhood of the nominal orbit. Analytical bounds underestimate median escape times by a factor of 1.6 for NF-1 and 2.3 for NF-3, with the discrepancy growing for families closer to secular resonance. Results suggest that the Yarkovsky drift, rather than intrinsic chaos, dominates escape for bodies smaller than roughly 1 km diameter.

title: On the reliability of chaos indicators for detecting slow diffusion near invariant tori
abstract: We test six chaos indicators—MEGNO, FLI, SALI, the Relative Lyapunov Indicator (RLI), the Orthogonal Fast Lyapunov Indicator (OFLI), and the Deviation Vector Method (DVM)—on a family of orbits chosen to lie within 10^{-3} of invariant KAM tori in the standard map extended to three dimensions. For each indicator we record the time T_{detect} at which the indicator first correctly identifies the orbit as chaotic versus quasi-periodic, defined against a ground truth established by a 10^9-step benchmark integration. MEGNO achieves the lowest median T_{detect} of 6 × 10^5 map iterations for weakly chaotic orbits, while DVM and OFLI require roughly 2.5 times longer. All indicators fail to classify 3–9 % of orbits within the tested integration window when chaos is extremely weak (maximum Lyapunov exponent below 10^{-6} per iteration). We discuss practical implications for large-scale stability surveys where CPU time per orbit is limited, and propose a two-stage screening protocol: a short MEGNO run to flag candidates followed by a longer SALI run to confirm borderline cases. This protocol reduces total CPU cost by 38 % relative to a single long SALI survey.

title: Transition to global chaos in a perturbed Kepler potential: a surface-of-section study
abstract: We examine the transition from regular to chaotic motion in a two-dimensional Kepler potential perturbed by a quadrupole term of strength q, applicable to motion around oblate bodies such as rapidly rotating asteroids. Surfaces of section are computed for 18 values of q between 0 and 0.08 at five energy levels corresponding to orbits with semi-major axes of 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 body radii. At each energy level we track the area of the last surviving KAM torus as a function of q, finding a power-law decrease with exponent approximately −1.4 for the innermost orbits. At q ≈ 0.05 global chaos occupies more than 80 % of the accessible phase-space volume at the 1.5-radius level. Periodic orbit families are continued numerically via a Newton correction scheme; three previously unreported bifurcations are identified at q values of 0.021, 0.037, and 0.059. The results are discussed in the context of particle dynamics around elongated small solar system bodies.

title: PALS-based surveillance monitoring protocol for irradiated specimens from a decommissioned VVER-440 unit: methodology and results
abstract: A practical measurement protocol was developed and applied to archive surveillance specimens retrieved from a decommissioned VVER-440 reactor pressure vessel at a site in Central Europe. Forty-seven specimens spanning five irradiation capsules (fluences 5×10^17 to 4×10^19 n/cm², irradiation temperatures 268–278 °C) were characterised by PALS. Measurement reproducibility over a six-month campaign was validated with repeated measurements on three reference specimens; standard deviation in mean positron lifetime was less than 1.2 ps across all sessions. The derived mean positron lifetime increased monotonically from 115 ps at the lowest fluence to 162 ps at the highest, plateauing above 2×10^19 n/cm². Specimen-to-specimen scatter at fixed fluence was ±4 ps and correlated weakly with Charpy transition temperature shifts archived in the original surveillance records (Pearson r = 0.61). The study demonstrates that PALS can serve as a non-destructive complement to mechanical surveillance testing and proposes a simplified two-parameter characterisation index for archival use.

title: Entropy production rate in overdamped colloidal systems driven by time-periodic potentials
abstract: We examine entropy production in a single Brownian particle confined in a one-dimensional harmonic potential that oscillates at frequencies between 0.01 Hz and 10 Hz. Using the Sekimoto path-integral formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the mean entropy production rate as a function of driving frequency and temperature. Numerical integration of the Fokker–Planck equation is used to validate the analytical results across a parameter grid of 144 configurations. Entropy production exhibits a maximum near the relaxation frequency of the trap and decays as a power law at higher frequencies with an exponent of approximately 1.8. The ratio of irreversible to reversible heat fluxes is measured experimentally using video microscopy of 1 µm silica beads in an optical tweezer setup, confirming the predicted scaling over one decade in frequency. Discrepancies at low driving amplitudes are attributed to detection noise in particle tracking. These results establish a clean experimental benchmark for stochastic thermodynamics tests in simple single-particle systems.

title: Televised Yearning: Nostalgic Visual Codes in Serbian Pop Music Videos, 1991–2001
abstract: This article examines a corpus of 87 Serbian pop and folk-pop music videos broadcast on state and commercial television between 1991 and 2001, focusing on the recurring visual grammar through which nostalgia is encoded and transmitted. Using multimodal discourse analysis following Kress and van Leeuwen's framework, the study identifies four dominant nostalgic registers: the rural idyll, the socialist-era domestic interior, the pre-war urban streetscape, and the family tableau. Quantitative content coding of the corpus was performed by two independent coders (inter-rater agreement κ = 0.81), followed by close reading of 14 selected videos. Results indicate that nostalgia in this period is predominantly oriented toward a pre-war, often pre-1990 imaginary, and that it functions less as a direct political statement than as an affective stabilisation strategy during social upheaval. The article also notes significant gender asymmetry in how nostalgic figures are deployed, with female performers more frequently positioned as embodiments of a lost past rather than as subjects of memory.

title: Singing the Ruins: Yugoslav Socialist Heritage in Post-2000 Serbian Turbo-Folk Aesthetics
abstract: This conference paper investigates the selective appropriation of Yugoslav socialist visual heritage in Serbian turbo-folk music videos produced between 2003 and 2018. Drawing on a sample of 41 videos collected from three major commercial music portals, the study applies Svetlana Boym's distinction between restorative and reflective nostalgia as an analytical lens. Semiotic analysis reveals that the majority of videos (29 of 41) employ industrial or brutalist architectural backdrops associated with the socialist period, yet strip these of explicit political meaning, recoding them instead as markers of authenticity, masculinity, or working-class belonging. The paper argues that this selective heritage use constitutes a form of 'aesthetic amnesia', in which the material culture of socialism is retained while its ideological content is deliberately obscured. Six in-depth interviews with video directors were conducted to triangulate the visual analysis. The paper was presented at the annual conference of the Central European Media and Communication Studies Association.

title: Between Ostalgie and Tranzicija: Comparative Frameworks for Post-Socialist Nostalgia in Popular Music Video
abstract: This book chapter contributes to an edited volume on post-socialist popular cultures in Central and Eastern Europe, positioning the Serbian case within broader comparative frameworks. The chapter reviews the scholarly literature on Ostalgie in the former East Germany and Yugonostalgia in the successor states of the former Yugoslavia, identifying points of convergence and divergence. It then offers a close analysis of three Serbian music videos from 2015 to 2022 that explicitly cite Yugoslav-era televisual conventions—particularly the aesthetic vocabulary of the JRT (Yugoslav Radio-Television) musical programme Jugoton Hitparada—to argue that Serbian popular music video nostalgia is distinct in its entanglement with nationalist political discourse in a way that East German Ostalgie generally is not. The chapter draws on production context research including archival materials held at the Radio Television of Vojvodina documentation centre, and situates findings within debates about memory, transitional identity, and cultural resilience.

title: Sonic Landscapes of Loss: Music, Landscape Imagery, and Regional Identity in Vojvodina-Based Music Videos, 2010–2024
abstract: This preprint presents preliminary findings from an ongoing study examining how landscape imagery in music videos produced by artists based in Vojvodina encodes regional, rather than national, forms of identity and memory. A sample of 53 videos was assembled through purposive selection from streaming platforms and the archives of two Novi Sad-based production houses. Multimodal analysis focuses on the interplay between lyrical content, landscape shots (plains, rivers, agricultural land), and musical genre conventions spanning folk, pop-folk, and indie-folk. Preliminary results suggest that flat Pannonian landscape imagery functions as a place-based memory trigger distinct from the mountain and rural iconography dominant in Serbian national popular culture broadly, and that this regional visual vocabulary is deployed with greater frequency by artists who explicitly identify as Vojvodinian rather than simply Serbian. The preprint invites feedback prior to journal submission.

title: Serialised fiction in provincial newspapers: reading habits and popular literature in interwar Vojvodina
abstract: Between 1920 and 1940, feuilleton fiction serialised in Vojvodina provincial papers constituted one of the most consistent and widely consumed forms of popular reading outside urban centres. This study analyses 143 serialised prose works published in eight newspapers, coding each for genre, author provenance, translation status, and publication length. The corpus was assembled from original newspaper runs in four repositories and supplemented with contemporary bibliographic periodicals. Results indicate that 61% of serialised fiction was translated, predominantly from French and German, with detective and adventure genres accounting for 47% of all fiction columns. Author identification, conducted through comparison with national bibliographic databases in Serbia and Croatia, succeeded for 89 of 143 works. The article discusses what the selection of titles reveals about editors' assumptions regarding reader taste and the logistical constraints of serialised newspaper fiction in a resource-limited provincial context.

title: Sports pages and civic identity: football, gymnastics societies, and their press representation in Vojvodina, 1921–1939
abstract: This study examines sports coverage in five Vojvodina newspapers between 1921 and 1939, focusing specifically on football match reports and coverage of Sokol and other gymnastic societies. A dataset of 2,341 sports articles was assembled from digitised and microfilm runs and coded for event type, club affiliation, national/ethnic descriptor use, and tone. Results show that football coverage expanded sharply after 1928, coming to occupy 34% of sports column space by 1935, while gymnastic society events, heavily promoted by state ideological apparatus, maintained consistent coverage throughout the period. Ethnic descriptors were applied inconsistently, more frequently when reporting on multi-ethnic competition than in intra-community events. Close reading of match reports and club announcements tracks the emergence of local civic pride discourse attached to football clubs as quasi-representative institutions of the provincial town. The study builds on recent historiography of sport and nationalism in interwar Yugoslavia.

title: Women's pages and gendered consumption: domestic life columns in Vojvodina newspapers, 1920–1940
abstract: Women's supplement pages and domestic life columns published across seven Vojvodina newspapers from 1920 to 1940 are examined as sites of normative construction of femininity, domesticity, and bourgeois household management. A content analysis of 1,870 column entries was conducted from microfilm and digitised sources, coding for thematic category, prescriptive tone, product reference, and reader address form. Dominant themes were household economy (29%), child-rearing (22%), and personal appearance (18%), with recipe content constituting a stable 15% of column space throughout the period. The analysis traces changes in the address of female readers: earlier columns typically addressed the rural housewife, while post-1930 columns increasingly presuppose an urban apartment-dwelling readership. Thirteen reader letters published in dialogue with domestic columns are analysed as evidence of audience engagement. The article situates these findings within debates on the modernisation of women's domestic roles in the interwar Yugoslav provincial press.

title: Benefit–risk structures in EMA assessment reports for approved TNF-α inhibitor biosimilars: a retrospective document analysis
abstract: This study examined publicly available European Public Assessment Reports (EPARs) for all TNF-α inhibitor biosimilar monoclonal antibodies approved through the EMA centralised procedure between 2013 and 2022. Thirty-one EPARs were retrieved and coded using a structured content analysis framework adapted from the Pharmacoepidemiological Research on Outcomes of Therapeutics (PROTECT) benefit–risk methodology. For each product, the study catalogued the number of pivotal studies cited, the clinical endpoints accepted as primary comparability evidence, and the explicit statements justifying extrapolation to non-studied indications. Of the 31 products, 27 relied on a single pivotal randomised equivalence trial for the primary benefit assessment. Immunogenicity data were presented inconsistently across dossiers: anti-drug antibody assay sensitivity thresholds were reported in only 14 cases. The analysis identified a systematic absence of quantified uncertainty around risk estimates for rare adverse events. Findings suggest that the current EPAR template does not mandate a standardised uncertainty communication format, which may complicate benefit–risk comparisons across products by regulators and prescribers.

title: Extrapolation of indications for biosimilar anti-IL-6 receptor antibodies: a benefit–risk re-analysis of available evidence
abstract: Extrapolation of clinical data from a studied indication to additional indications without direct clinical evidence remains one of the most debated aspects of biosimilar regulatory science. This study focused on anti-IL-6 receptor monoclonal antibody biosimilars, for which EPARs described extrapolation from rheumatoid arthritis trials to giant cell arteritis and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. A structured benefit–risk model was applied using the Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) framework recommended in the EMA reflection paper on benefit–risk assessment. For each extrapolated indication, the study scored the mechanistic plausibility of shared receptor pharmacology, the quality of the reference product's clinical data in that indication, and the post-marketing safety record. Scores were derived from three independent assessors and inter-rater reliability was calculated (Krippendorff's α = 0.71). Results indicated that mechanistic justification was consistently strong (mean score 4.1/5), whereas clinical data density for extrapolated indications scored substantially lower (mean 2.6/5). The paper proposes a minimum evidence threshold checklist for extrapolation decisions.

title: Regulatory pathways for biosimilar mAbs in the Western Balkans: mapping divergence from EMA requirements
abstract: Countries in the Western Balkans region that have not yet acceded to the European Union maintain national medicines regulatory frameworks that differ in important ways from the EMA centralised procedure. This paper mapped the current biosimilar mAb regulatory requirements in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro by reviewing national pharmaceutical legislation, guidance documents, and interviews with five regulatory staff members per country. Comparisons were made against the EMA biosimilar guideline package (2014 revision and subsequent updates). Major divergences included: absence of a mandatory extrapolation justification module in three of four countries, no requirement for a risk management plan in two countries, and permitted reliance on WHO prequalification in place of full comparability data in one country. The paper does not assess the adequacy of these approaches but describes them as a baseline for regional harmonisation initiatives, including those pursued under the Pharmaceutical Regulatory Harmonisation project of the Regional Cooperation Council.
venue: Southeastern European Pharmaceutical Law Review

title: Quantitative benefit–risk assessment using the SMAA-MCDA framework: a worked example with a biosimilar anti-VEGF antibody
abstract: Stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis (SMAA) combined with MCDA weighting was applied to a hypothetical regulatory scenario involving a biosimilar anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody for age-related macular degeneration and metastatic colorectal cancer. Input data were drawn entirely from publicly available sources: the originator's product information, published phase III trials, and literature estimates of adverse event rates. Four benefit criteria (visual acuity improvement, progression-free survival, response rate, and patient-reported outcomes) and four risk criteria (arterial thromboembolic events, hypertension, proteinuria, and infusion reactions) were scored and weighted by a panel of five pharmacists and two clinical pharmacologists. SMAA simulations (10,000 iterations) were run with uniform uncertainty distributions over criterion weights. The biosimilar scenario maintained a positive expected benefit–risk balance across 94% of weight combinations for the macular degeneration indication and 87% for colorectal cancer. The paper discusses how sensitivity of the SMAA output to immunogenicity uncertainty bands can be presented to decision makers.

title: Transition from originator to biosimilar monoclonal antibodies in Serbian hospitals: pharmacist perspectives on switching protocols
abstract: A cross-sectional survey was administered to 214 hospital pharmacists across 18 hospitals in the Republic of Serbia between March and June 2018. The questionnaire addressed awareness of EMA and national ALIMS guidance on non-medical switching, perceived barriers to implementing biosimilar switching protocols, and confidence in current labelling information for immunogenicity risk communication. Response rate was 71%. Key findings: 61% of respondents were unaware of any formally approved hospital-level switching protocol for biosimilar mAbs; 48% reported that physicians in their institutions routinely requested originator continuity without documented clinical justification; 34% felt that available patient information leaflets adequately explained the difference between originators and biosimilars. Logistic regression identified hospital size (>400 beds, OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.4–3.8) and prior pharmacist training in regulatory science (OR 3.1, 95% CI 1.8–5.2) as significant predictors of protocol existence. Recommendations for continuing professional development are provided.

title: Structural analysis of quality comparability data in EMA assessment reports for anti-CD20 biosimilars
abstract: EMA EPARs for all anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody biosimilars approved up to December 2020 were reviewed to characterise how physicochemical and functional comparability data are presented and evaluated. Eight products were eligible. For each, the study recorded: the number and type of analytical methods used in the quality module, whether higher-order structure data (circular dichroism, hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry) were reported, the number of batches tested, and the regulatory outcome of any quality-related deficiency letter. Across the eight products, a median of 14 analytical methods were reported (range 9–21). Higher-order structure data were reported in six products but described as confirmatory rather than pivotal in all cases. Deficiency letters citing quality comparability were issued for three products; in two cases the deficiency related to glycan profile variability. The analysis shows that the regulatory threshold for acceptable glycosylation variability is applied inconsistently, and that EPAR language does not always make the committee's reasoning transparent to external reviewers.

title: Teaching regulatory science in pharmacy curricula: experience from a graduate elective at the University of Novi Sad
abstract: This article describes the design, delivery, and evaluation of a one-semester elective course in European Medicines Regulation introduced at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad in 2017. The course was attended by 22 to 31 graduate pharmacy students per year over four cohorts (2017–2020). Core modules covered centralised and decentralised EMA procedures, benefit–risk assessment frameworks, pharmacovigilance legislation, and biosimilar regulatory pathways. Teaching methods combined lecture-based sessions, structured analysis of publicly available EPARs, and a group dossier simulation exercise. Pre- and post-course assessment of regulatory knowledge was measured using a validated 40-item multiple-choice instrument. Mean score improvement was 18.4 percentage points (95% CI 15.1–21.7). Student feedback rated the EPAR analysis component highest for perceived learning value. The paper discusses transferability of the course design to other regional pharmacy faculties where regulatory science is not part of the standard curriculum.

title: Risk management plans for biosimilar mAbs: a comparative review of EMA and FDA requirements and their implications for global development strategies
abstract: Risk management plans (RMPs) required by EMA and risk evaluation and mitigation strategies (REMS) required by FDA for biosimilar monoclonal antibodies differ in structure, mandatory content, and update frequency. This book chapter reviews the two frameworks side by side, drawing on 12 case studies—six EMA-approved and six FDA-approved biosimilar mAbs—to illustrate how the same underlying safety concern may be managed through different instruments. For instance, the same cardiovascular risk associated with biosimilar bevacizumab analogues was addressed through an EMA RMP additional pharmacovigilance activity (registry) and through a prescriber communication programme under the FDA pathway. The chapter examines how companies pursuing simultaneous EMA and FDA submissions reconcile divergent requirements in a single global development plan, and where alignment may be possible under the ongoing EMA–FDA bilateral cluster on biosimilar pharmacovigilance. Practical considerations for regulatory affairs teams at mid-sized biopharmaceutical companies are highlighted.

title: Application of Bayesian benefit–risk models to rare adverse events in biosimilar mAb post-authorisation studies
abstract: Phase III equivalence trials supporting biosimilar mAb authorisation are typically powered for efficacy comparability and are underpowered to detect differences in rare adverse events with incidences below 1%. This preprint explores whether Bayesian hierarchical models that borrow strength from originator post-marketing data can improve rare adverse event risk estimation for biosimilar products. Using simulated datasets parameterised from published infliximab and adalimumab safety registries (total N = approximately 28,000 patient-years), informative prior distributions were constructed for four rare adverse events: serious infections, demyelination, hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma, and lupus-like reactions. Posterior estimates were computed under three scenarios varying the assumed biosimilarity coefficient. Results show that even moderate prior information substantially reduces uncertainty around the biosimilar rare event rate when biosimilar-specific data are limited to 500 patient-years. The model structure and R code are shared as supplementary material. This work is under review at a peer-reviewed journal.
venue: PharmReg Preprints

title: Documentation requirements for biosimilar oncology mAbs under the EMA centralised procedure: a dossier checklist derived from CHMP assessment experience
abstract: Preparing a regulatory dossier for a biosimilar oncology monoclonal antibody requires integrating quality, non-clinical, and clinical comparability data within the Common Technical Document structure. This conference paper, presented at the Symposium on Pharmaceutical Regulatory Science in Central and Eastern Europe (Bratislava, 2015), reported a practical checklist derived from a structured review of CHMP questions and answers from ten oncology biosimilar dossiers submitted between 2010 and 2014. The checklist comprised 47 items across Module 3 (quality), Module 4 (non-clinical), and Module 5 (clinical), each flagged as mandatory, conditional, or best-practice. Items most frequently generating CHMP questions in the reviewed dossiers included reference product sourcing documentation (8 of 10 dossiers), the fingerprint-like analytical comparability study design (6 of 10), and the statistical analysis plan for the pivotal equivalence trial (9 of 10). The checklist was subsequently incorporated into a regulatory affairs training programme for pharmacy graduates at two Serbian universities.

title: Photodegradation Kinetics of Bisoprolol and Hydrochlorothiazide in Model Tablet Matrices: A Stress Testing Study
abstract: This study examined the photolytic stability of bisoprolol fumarate and hydrochlorothiazide, individually and in combination, within lactose-based and microcrystalline cellulose-based tablet matrices. Samples were exposed to fluorescent and xenon-arc light sources following ICH Q1B option 1 conditions. HPLC-DAD analysis was performed using a C8 column with isocratic elution (methanol : 10 mM phosphate buffer pH 3.0, 35:65 v/v). Hydrochlorothiazide underwent measurable photodegradation after 48 h of xenon exposure, with a primary degradation product identified at a retention time of 6.3 min accounting for approximately 1.4% of total peak area; bisoprolol remained stable under all tested photolytic conditions. The lactose-based excipient matrix did not significantly alter the degradation rate compared to the microcrystalline cellulose matrix (p > 0.05). First-order rate constants were determined for hydrochlorothiazide photo-degradation at 6.2 × 10⁻³ h⁻¹ under xenon illumination. The validated HPLC method showed adequate specificity with no co-elution of excipient-related peaks. Results provide a basis for recommending amber-glass secondary packaging for this combination product.

title: Pectin supplementation shifts Bacteroidetes-to-Firmicutes ratio and alters quercetin metabolite profiles in a static in vitro colon model
abstract: We examined the influence of three pectin types—high-methoxyl citrus pectin, low-methoxyl apple pectin, and amidated beet pectin—on microbial community composition and quercetin catabolism using a single-stage batch fermentation model inoculated with human faecal slurry (n = 6 donors). After 24-hour incubations at 37 °C under strict anaerobiosis, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing (V3–V4 region, Illumina MiSeq) revealed a consistent decrease in the Bacteroidetes-to-Firmicutes ratio for all three pectins compared with a glucose control. Quercetin (50 µM initial concentration) degradation was monitored by HPLC-DAD; the principal metabolites identified were 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetic acid and 3-hydroxyphenylacetic acid. High-methoxyl pectin produced the highest yield of 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetic acid (18.4 ± 2.1 µM), approximately 2.3-fold greater than the glucose control. Short-chain fatty acid production (acetate, propionate, butyrate) was quantified by GC-FID and correlated positively with metabolite yield. The findings indicate that pectin type influences both microbial ecology and the downstream biotransformation capacity for dietary flavonoids.
venue: Journal of Functional Food Research

title: Reachability-Based Deadlock Detection in Workflow Nets: A Structural Characterisation
abstract: This paper investigates structural conditions sufficient to guarantee deadlock freedom in workflow nets, a subclass of Petri nets widely used to model business processes. We derive a set of necessary and sufficient conditions based on trap and siphon analysis applied to a corpus of 47 industrial workflow schemas collected from a regional manufacturing consortium. The analysis is performed using a custom extension of the PIPE2 tool. We show that 38 of the 47 schemas contain at least one improper minimal siphon that can lead to deadlock under realistic resource contention. A repair procedure using place invariant augmentation is described and validated against the original schemas. The corrected nets are verified for soundness using the LoLA state-space explorer, with verification times remaining under 90 seconds for nets with up to 120 places and 95 transitions. The approach reduces manual inspection effort compared to exhaustive simulation by a factor of approximately 4.3 on the given benchmark.
venue: Journal of Applied Formal Methods

title: Comparing CTL and LTL for Liveness Verification in Coloured Petri Net Models of Web Service Orchestration
abstract: Web service orchestration engines implement complex concurrent control flows that are difficult to verify using testing alone. This paper compares the expressiveness and practical efficiency of CTL and LTL model checking when applied to Coloured Petri Net (CPN) models of two open-source BPEL engines. We translated execution semantics of both engines into CPN models with between 210 and 340 coloured places, and encoded seventeen liveness and safety properties in both temporal logics. Experiments were conducted using CPN Tools and the SPIN model checker after unfolding to ordinary nets. CTL verification with symbolic BDD-based representation proved two to five times faster than explicit-state LTL checking on fourteen of the seventeen properties. However, three fairness-related properties expressible in LTL had no natural CTL counterpart. Results suggest a hybrid property specification strategy for practical engine verification. All models and property files are made publicly available.

title: A Petri Net Semantics for a Fragment of the YAWL Workflow Language
abstract: The Yet Another Workflow Language (YAWL) provides constructs for OR-joins and multiple-instance tasks that lack a standard, unambiguous Petri net translation. This paper proposes a formal Petri net semantics for a well-defined fragment of YAWL covering sequence, AND-split/join, XOR-split/join, OR-split/join, and cancellation regions. The translation is defined compositionally and proven to preserve soundness: a YAWL net in the fragment is sound if and only if its translation is a sound workflow net. The proof relies on a bisimulation argument over the labelled transition systems of the two representations. We implement the translation as a Java plugin for the ProM framework and validate it on eighteen benchmark YAWL models from the public WF-net repository. Eleven of these models contain deliberate errors; all eleven are flagged correctly by reachability analysis on the translated nets.

title: State-Space Reduction Techniques for Verifying Large Free-Choice Nets
abstract: Free-choice Petri nets admit efficient polynomial-time algorithms for soundness checking, yet state-space-based verification is still used when richer behavioural properties must be confirmed. This paper surveys and benchmarks five state-space reduction techniques—partial-order reduction, symmetry reduction, slicing, abstract interpretation, and region-based lumping—when applied to free-choice workflow nets with between 50 and 600 places. We use a benchmark suite of 120 synthetically generated nets at six size tiers. The primary metric is the ratio of reduced to full state space, measured in number of reachable markings. Partial-order reduction achieves the best average reduction ratio of 94.7% at the 600-place tier, while symmetry reduction is most effective for nets with repetitive structure (up to 98.1% reduction). The chapter concludes with practical recommendations for choosing techniques based on net topology.

title: Detecting Resource Starvation in Token-Passing Protocols Using Reachability Graphs
abstract: Token-passing protocols underlie a broad class of mutual exclusion mechanisms in distributed systems. This paper uses reachability graph analysis to characterise and detect resource starvation, a liveness failure distinct from deadlock in which one process is indefinitely bypassed. We model eight classical and four industrial token-ring protocols as bounded Petri nets and compute their full reachability graphs using the LoLA tool. Starvation is encoded as the absence of a specific infinite firing sequence, which we reduce to a nested depth-first search for accepting cycles in a product automaton. All twelve protocols are verified within 40 minutes on a standard workstation with 16 GB RAM; four of the twelve industrial protocols exhibit starvation under specific initial markings that were not documented in the original specifications. The paper discusses how minimal marking changes eliminate these starvation traces.

title: Modular Verification of Hierarchical Workflow Nets Through Interface Refinement
abstract: Verifying large workflow nets monolithically becomes intractable as the number of reachable markings grows exponentially with net size. This paper presents a modular verification framework in which a hierarchical workflow net is decomposed into subnet modules connected through typed interface places. Each module is verified independently for soundness and interface compatibility; a composition theorem then guarantees global soundness without constructing the full state space. We define interface refinement as a partial order over interface type assignments and show that refinement preserves the soundness certificate. The approach is evaluated on three enterprise resource planning workflow models from the manufacturing sector, ranging from 85 to 340 top-level places after flattening. Modular verification reduces peak memory consumption by 61–78% compared to monolithic LoLA runs with identical property specifications.

title: Bounded Liveness Certificates for Timed Petri Nets in Real-Time Workflow Systems
abstract: Real-time workflow systems impose timing constraints on task execution that ordinary Petri nets cannot capture. This paper extends standard workflow net soundness to timed Petri nets by introducing bounded liveness certificates: proofs that every enabled transition fires within a bounded time interval under all schedulings consistent with the timing annotations. We define a certificate structure based on time-annotated invariants and implement a certificate checker using the UPPAAL model checker as a back-end. The approach is applied to a medical triage workflow obtained from a regional hospital in Vojvodina and described as a timed workflow net with 64 places and 51 transitions and 23 timing constraints. The certificate checker confirms bounded liveness for 21 of the 23 constraints; the two failures correspond to documented bottlenecks in the paper-based process that had not been formally quantified before.

title: Incremental Reachability Analysis After Small Net Modifications
abstract: When a workflow net undergoes a small structural change—addition or removal of at most k places or transitions—recomputing the full reachability graph from scratch is wasteful. This paper introduces an incremental reachability algorithm that identifies which portions of the existing reachability graph remain valid after a modification of size k ≤ 5. The algorithm partitions the old reachability graph into a stable region and an affected frontier using a backward reachability cone, then re-explores only the frontier. On a benchmark of 200 nets from the WF-net repository subjected to 1 000 random single-step modifications, the incremental algorithm visits on average 14.3% of the states visited by full recomputation. Correctness is established by a formal invariant that the stable region is identical in old and new reachability graphs. The implementation is released as an open-source extension to LoLA.

title: Verifying Absence of Deadlock in a BPMN-Based Order Fulfilment Engine: A Case Study
abstract: This paper reports a full industrial case study in which formal verification was applied to the order fulfilment workflow of a regional logistics company. The workflow was modelled in BPMN 2.0 and automatically translated to a sound workflow net using an extended version of the mapping described in prior literature. The resulting net contains 98 places, 87 transitions, and 14 resource places modelling shared transport assets. Deadlock freedom is verified using reachability analysis in LoLA and checked against nine operational scenarios derived from the company's incident log. Three of the nine scenarios expose a previously unknown deadlock caused by simultaneous booking conflicts on two shared vehicles. The paper documents the correction, the re-verification, and the deployment of the corrected specification. Verification turnaround time after model updates averaged 7.4 minutes, which the company's process team found acceptable for their change management cycle.

title: A Survey of Model Checking Tools for Concurrent Workflow Verification: Coverage, Scalability, and Usability
abstract: This survey systematically evaluates eleven model checking tools—LoLA, SPIN, UPPAAL, nuSMV, CPN Tools, Tapaal, Tina, INA, GreatSPN, PRISM, and Storm—with respect to their applicability to concurrent workflow verification. Each tool is assessed on five dimensions: supported net classes, property specification languages, scalability on nets with up to 500 places, quality of counterexample output, and integration with standard process modelling notations. Scalability is measured empirically on a shared benchmark of 60 nets. LoLA and SPIN offer the best scalability for plain reachability properties; PRISM and Storm dominate for probabilistic specifications; UPPAAL is preferred when timing constraints are present. Usability ratings are based on a structured questionnaire administered to 31 graduate students at three regional universities. The survey concludes with a decision tree guiding practitioners to the appropriate tool for a given verification task.

title: Formal Specification and Verification of a Microservice Orchestration Layer Using Labelled Petri Nets
abstract: Microservice architectures decompose applications into loosely coupled services whose interactions can produce emergent concurrency failures. This paper applies labelled Petri net modelling and reachability-based verification to the orchestration layer of a microservice platform developed by a software company based in Novi Sad. The orchestration logic—comprising 11 services, 34 REST endpoints, and an event bus—is modelled as a labelled net with 157 places and 143 transitions derived by semi-automated extraction from OpenAPI specifications. Deadlock freedom and a bounded response property (every service call completes within k=3 orchestration steps under nominal load) are verified. Deadlock freedom is confirmed for the nominal model; two bounded-response violations are found under a high-load scenario where the retry timeout is set below 200 ms. The fixes involve adding two inhibitor arcs, which are verified to restore both properties. The approach integrates into the company's CI pipeline with a mean verification time of 4.1 minutes per commit.

title: Coverability and Boundedness Checking for Inhibitor-Arc Petri Nets in Workflow Contexts
abstract: Inhibitor arcs extend the expressive power of Petri nets to Turing completeness but invalidate many classical decidability results, including boundedness. This paper examines which practically relevant subclasses of inhibitor-arc nets used in workflow modelling retain decidable coverability and boundedness. We identify a class we call k-inhibited workflow nets, where each inhibitor arc is guarded by a threshold k, and prove that coverability is decidable for this class via a reduction to the coverability problem for reset nets. Boundedness remains undecidable in general but is decidable for the subclass where every cycle through an inhibitor arc is structurally bounded. Algorithms for both problems are implemented and evaluated on 45 workflow models augmented with inhibitor arcs extracted from a healthcare process library. Coverability checking completes in under 3 minutes for all 45 models.

title: From BPMN Collaboration Diagrams to Communicating Workflow Nets: Formalisation and Deadlock Analysis
abstract: BPMN 2.0 collaboration diagrams describe multi-party processes exchanging messages across pool boundaries. This paper provides a formal translation from BPMN collaboration diagrams to pairs of communicating workflow nets connected via synchronous message places. The translation is defined for the full collaboration subset excluding event sub-processes, covering 22 of the 27 BPMN flow elements. Soundness of the joint model—meaning both participants terminate and no message is permanently pending—is encoded as a reachability property and verified using LoLA. We apply the translation to eight collaboration diagrams modelling inter-organisational supply chain processes from three Vojvodina manufacturing firms. Four diagrams contain unsound interactions; all four involve asymmetric message loops in exception-handling paths that had been designed informally. The paper proposes a catalogue of five correction patterns covering the observed failure modes.

title: Automated Generation of Petri Net Workflow Models from Event Log Data Using Structural Constraints
abstract: Process mining algorithms can discover workflow models from event logs, but the discovered models often violate structural properties required for formal verification, such as free-choice or well-nestedness. This paper presents a constrained discovery algorithm that incorporates structural workflow net constraints directly into the inductive miner framework, ensuring that every discovered net belongs to the free-choice subclass and therefore admits efficient soundness checking. The algorithm is evaluated on six publicly available event logs and four logs from manufacturing companies in the Novi Sad region, comprising between 3 400 and 112 000 traces. Compared to unconstrained inductive mining, constrained discovery produces nets with slightly lower fitness (average drop of 3.1 percentage points) but with 100% of nets immediately verifiable for deadlock freedom in under 90 seconds, versus 61% of unconstrained nets meeting the same criterion.

title: Batch Query Strategies Under Annotator Capacity Constraints
abstract: Most batch-mode active learning methods optimise for informativeness without accounting for the number of items a human annotator can reliably process in a single session. We model annotator capacity as a hard constraint and compare three batch construction strategies—greedy diversity, core-set selection, and a proposed ranked-truncation heuristic—under fixed batch sizes of 10, 25, and 50. Evaluation uses an image classification dataset of industrial surface defects (12,000 images, 6 classes) provided by a manufacturing partner under a non-disclosure agreement. ResNet-18 is used as the base model. Across five independent trials, core-set selection degrades gracefully as batch size grows but is computationally expensive; ranked truncation achieves comparable accuracy at one-tenth the selection time. At batch size 25, both outperform greedy diversity by 2.1 percentage points in mean accuracy at round 10. The results support a practical recommendation that batch size should not exceed 25 items per annotator session for fine-grained visual tasks.

title: Comparing SMOTE and ADASYN on Short Legal Texts with Fewer Than 500 Training Instances
abstract: Resampling techniques designed for tabular data are often applied to text feature vectors without assessing whether interpolation in high-dimensional TF-IDF space produces semantically coherent synthetic documents. This paper applies SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and ADASYN to a dataset of 487 Serbian misdemeanour rulings represented as 2,000-dimensional TF-IDF vectors, with minority classes containing as few as 31 samples. Classification performance is assessed using stratified five-fold cross-validation with SVM and gradient boosting classifiers. ADASYN yields the highest macro F1 improvement (from 0.34 to 0.51 for SVM), but manual inspection of 50 synthetic vectors shows that 38% contain feature combinations absent in any real document. The paper proposes a nearest-neighbour coherence filter that removes synthetic points deviating beyond two standard deviations from their class centroid, recovering coherence while retaining 81% of generated samples. This filtered variant outperforms unfiltered ADASYN on two of three evaluation metrics.

title: Practical Aspects of Deploying Wireless Sensor Networks for Thermal Comfort Monitoring in Occupied Office Buildings
abstract: Field identification of building thermal models requires reliable, low-latency sensor data under practical constraints of occupied buildings: network interference, occupant interaction, and power limitations. This paper reports lessons learned from deploying a mesh sensor network of 24 nodes across three open-plan offices at the Science and Technology Park area in Novi Sad over a six-month period. Each node measured operative temperature, relative humidity, CO₂ concentration, and plug load power draw at 1-minute resolution. Battery life, packet loss rates, and synchronisation drift were monitored continuously. Median packet loss was 2.8% per link; clock drift reached 4 seconds per day without software correction, introducing noticeable errors in correlation-based identification experiments. A lightweight time-synchronisation protocol reduced drift to under 0.3 seconds. The paper provides a checklist of calibration and network configuration steps that reduced temperature measurement uncertainty to ±0.15 °C across all nodes, and discusses how sensor placement relative to occupant workstations affects the usability of data for grey-box model estimation.

title: Gramatički vođeno genetsko programiranje za otkrivanje algebarskih zakona u fizičkim merenjima
abstract: U radu je predložen pristup simboličkoj regresiji zasnovan na bezkontekstnim gramatikama kojima se ograničava prostor pretrage kandidatskih izraza. Gramatika je definisana tako da garantuje dimenzionalnu konzistentnost generisanih formula u odnosu na ulazne fizičke veličine. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na 14 skupova podataka iz klasične mehanike i termodinamike, pri čemu su skupovi sadržavali između 80 i 400 mernih tačaka sa različitim nivoima šuma. Predložena metoda pronašla je tačnu analitičku formulu u 11 od 14 slučajeva, dok je standardno genetsko programiranje bez gramatičkih ograničenja postiglo tačnost na samo 7 skupova. Prosečna veličina finalnih izraza smanjena je za 34% u poređenju sa referentnim algoritmom. Rezultati pokazuju da eksplicitno kodiranje dimenzionalne analize u gramatiku značajno ubrzava konvergenciju i smanjuje prekomerno prilagođavanje na male skupove podataka.

title: Comparative Study of Tree Encoding Schemes for Symbolic Regression on Small Tabular Datasets
abstract: This paper systematically compares five tree encoding strategies used in genetic programming for symbolic regression tasks where training sets contain fewer than 200 samples. The encodings evaluated are standard prefix-tree, linear genome with decoding, push-based stack representation, graph-based DAG encoding, and a grammar-constrained derivation tree. Benchmarks consist of 22 datasets drawn from material science, hydrology, and agricultural yield prediction, standardised to remove dimensional differences. Evaluation metrics include median relative error on held-out test sets, average expression depth, and frequency of bloat-induced fitness stagnation. The DAG and grammar-constrained representations show substantially lower bloat rates (12% and 9% stagnation events respectively, versus 38% for prefix-tree). Predictive accuracy differences are modest but consistent in favour of grammar-constrained derivation trees across datasets with fewer than 100 samples, suggesting that restricting syntax is more helpful when training data are sparse. Runtime overhead of grammar enforcement averages 18% per generation.

title: Simbolička regresija sa kontrolom složenosti putem kažnjavanja Kolmogorov-Čaitinovom aproksimacijom dužine opisa
abstract: Prezentovana je metoda koja u funkciju dobrote simboličke regresije uvodi kazneni član zasnovan na aproksimativnoj Kolmogorov-Čaitinovoj složenosti kandidatskog izraza, procenjenoj kompresionim algoritmom primenjenim na serijalizovano sintaksičko stablo. Cilj je automatska ravnoteža između tačnosti prilagođavanja i parsimonioze modela bez ručnog podešavanja težinskog parametra. Metod je testiran na 30 sintetičkih skupova podataka generisanih iz poznatih jednačina iz literature, sa skupovima veličine 50 do 500 uzoraka i tri nivoa aditivnog Gausovog šuma (σ = 0.01, 0.05, 0.10). Na skupovima sa visokim šumom, predloženi pristup ostvaruje prosečnu grešku 12% manju od standardnog Pareto-frontovskog pristupa, uz prosečno kraće izraze za 2.3 čvora. Analiza osetljivosti pokazuje da kompresiona aproksimacija složenosti daje stabilnije rezultate od broja čvorova kao mere složenosti.

title: Otkrivanje empirijskih formula za prinos useva primenom simboličke regresije na agronomskim tabelarnim podacima
abstract: Istraživanje ispituje primenu simboličke regresije vođene gramatikom za pronalaženje analitičkih formula koje objašnjavaju varijacije prinosa kukuruza u Vojvodini u zavisnosti od agrotehničkih i meteoroloških faktora. Korišćeni skup podataka obuhvata 11 ulaznih promenljivih i 620 merenja prikupljenih tokom 18 vegetacionih sezona na eksperimentalnim parcelama Instituta za ratarstvo i povrtarstvo u Novom Sadu. Gramatikom su definisani algebarski operatori i elementarne funkcije; konačno rešenje testirano je na odvojenom skupu iz dve sezone koje nisu korišćene u treningu. Otkrivena formula sa četiri promenljive postiže R² = 0.81 na test skupu, što je uporedivo s rezultatima ansambla slučajnih šuma (R² = 0.84), ali uz znatno veću interpretabilnost. Formula identifikuje temperaturni deficit u fazi cvetanja i kumulativnu padavinu u junu kao dominantne prediktore, što je konzistentno sa agronomskim znanjem.

title: Parallel Island-Model Genetic Programming for Symbolic Regression on Multi-Core Architectures
abstract: Population-based symbolic regression methods are computationally expensive due to repeated fitness evaluation of large expression trees. This paper describes a parallel island-model implementation of grammar-guided genetic programming targeting shared-memory multicore systems with up to 32 cores and distributed GPU clusters. The island topology, migration interval, and migration rate are treated as tunable parameters and studied via a grid search across 108 configurations on six benchmark regression problems. Results show that a ring topology with migration every 15 generations and a 5% migration rate provides the best trade-off between exploration and convergence speed. On a 12-core workstation, wall-clock time per run decreases by a factor of 8.3 relative to the sequential baseline, with no statistically significant reduction in solution quality (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p > 0.05). GPU acceleration of fitness evaluation yields an additional 2.1× speedup on problems with more than 1000 data points.
