title: Upotreba simboličke regresije za rekonstrukciju diferencijalnih jednačina iz vremenskih serija
abstract: Predložena je metoda za otkrivanje oblika diferencijalnih jednačina koje opisuju dinamiku sistema isključivo iz merenih vremenskih serija, bez prethodnog poznavanja strukture modela. Numeričke derivacije potrebne za formiranje biblioteke kanditat-termova procenjene su regularizovanim diferencijalnim filtrom kako bi se smanjio uticaj šuma. Simbolička regresija zatim pretražuje prostor mogućih desnih strana obične diferencijalne jednačine prvog reda koristeći gramatiku ograničenu na polinome i trigonometrijske funkcije. Metoda je validirana na četiri sintetička primera: linearni oscilator, Van der Polov oscilator, Lotka-Volterra sistem i jedačina logističkog rasta. Korektna funkcionalna forma otkrivena je u svim slučajevima kada je odnos signal-šum bio iznad 20 dB. Ispod tog praga korektnost opada, a metoda otkriva aproksimativne forme koje zadržavaju kvalitativne dinamičke osobine originalnog sistema.

title: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression Algorithms on Tabular Scientific Datasets: A Reproducibility Study
abstract: Reproducibility problems in evolutionary computation benchmarks are well documented, yet symbolic regression comparisons frequently rely on heterogeneous evaluation protocols. This paper presents a controlled benchmarking study comparing eight symbolic regression methods, including three grammar-guided GP variants, two neural-network-based equation learners, a sparse regression baseline (LASSO on a fixed function library), and two commercial tools, across 40 tabular datasets collected from published scientific literature covering biology, chemistry, and geophysics. All methods are evaluated under identical train/test splits, computational budgets (10,000 fitness evaluations), and five random seeds. Results show that grammar-guided GP with a domain-informed grammar achieves the lowest median test error on 18 of 40 datasets, while neural-network approaches perform best on 12 datasets, predominantly those with more than 500 training points. Sparse regression dominates on 7 datasets where the true model lies within the pre-defined function library. Code and datasets are provided as a reproducible benchmark suite.

title: Primena simboličke regresije na modelovanje potrošnje energije u stambenim zgradama na osnovu podataka o merenjima
abstract: Rad istražuje mogućnost automatskog otkrivanja analitičkih modela za predikciju mesečne potrošnje toplotne energije stambenih zgrada primenom gramatički vođenog genetskog programiranja. Podaci su prikupljeni iz 47 stambenih zgrada u Novom Sadu i Subotici tokom perioda od tri godine, obuhvatajući merenja spoljašnje temperature, solarnog zračenja, zauzetosti i karakteristika omotača zgrade — ukupno 9 ulaznih promenljivih i 1692 mesečnih mernih tačaka. Gramatika je konstruisana tako da dozvoljava racionalne funkcije i eksponencijalne termine, ali isključuje implicitne rekurzije. Pronađena formula postiže RMSE od 4.7 kWh/m² na test skupu, što odgovara performansama regresionog ansambla, ali pruža eksplicitnu zavisnost od tri dominantna faktora: temperaturnog deficita, površine ostakljenja i koeficijenta transmisije. Rezultati su relevantni za projektovanje sistema za upravljanje energijom u zgradama.

title: Confidence Estimation for Symbolic Regression Solutions Using Ensemble Disagreement
abstract: Symbolic regression algorithms typically return a single best expression without any indication of prediction uncertainty. This work proposes a post-hoc uncertainty quantification method based on disagreement among the top-k expressions retained from the final generation of a grammar-guided GP run. For each test point, the prediction interval is estimated from the empirical distribution of outputs produced by the k = 20 retained expressions, weighted by their training fitness. The method is evaluated on 15 regression datasets by comparing estimated 90% prediction intervals against bootstrap-based reference intervals. Coverage probabilities average 87.3% across datasets, compared to a nominal 90%, representing a modest but acceptable underestimation. Interval width is on average 1.4 times larger than bootstrap intervals. The computational overhead relative to a standard single-run symbolic regression is negligible since no additional GP runs are required. The approach is applicable to any population-based symbolic regression method.

title: Multi-Objective Grammar-Guided Genetic Programming: Balancing Accuracy, Complexity, and Extrapolation Quality
abstract: Standard single-objective symbolic regression optimises predictive accuracy within the training domain and uses complexity as a secondary criterion. This paper formulates the problem as a three-objective optimisation task, adding an explicit extrapolation quality objective measured by evaluating candidate expressions on a held-out extrapolation set drawn from outside the training input range. A NSGA-III selection mechanism is adapted for grammar-guided genetic programming populations of size 500, run for 300 generations on 20 benchmark problems. The resulting Pareto fronts contain expressions that dominate single-objective solutions in both complexity and extrapolation accuracy on 14 of 20 problems. An analysis of selected Pareto-front members shows that expressions with lower extrapolation error tend to contain fewer non-monotone sub-expressions, suggesting that structural regularity correlates with extrapolation reliability. The method is demonstrated on a materials hardness prediction dataset with 210 training points and an extrapolation test set drawn from a different temperature range.

title: Symbolic Regression as an Audit Tool for Black-Box Regression Models in Industrial Quality Control
abstract: When a trained black-box model is deployed in a manufacturing quality control pipeline, operators often need a human-readable approximation of its behaviour to satisfy regulatory or safety requirements. This paper investigates the use of symbolic regression to distill a gradient-boosted tree model into a concise mathematical expression by treating the black-box model's predictions on a dense synthetic grid as training targets. Grammar-guided genetic programming is applied with a grammar tailored to the physical variables of an injection moulding process. The resulting symbolic approximations are evaluated on a held-out set of 1,200 real production measurements. Across five process variables, the distilled expressions achieve a median relative error of 3.1% with respect to the black-box model's predictions, and 4.8% with respect to actual quality measurements. The approach is tested in collaboration with a manufacturing partner and reduces the average operator interpretation time from 18 minutes (reading model documentation) to under 2 minutes (reading a four-term formula).

title: Modelling Non-Stationarity in Small-Business Revenue Streams: A Local Level Model with Regime-Switching Drift
abstract: Small-business revenue series frequently alternate between growth and contraction regimes driven by seasonal demand, credit conditions, and policy changes, making fixed-drift local level models inadequate. This paper introduces a hidden Markov switching extension of the standard local level DLM in which the drift term follows a two-state Markov chain with state-dependent Gaussian innovations. Parameters are estimated jointly using the EM algorithm combined with the forward–backward recursion. The model is fitted to monthly revenue records from 68 small retailers in Vojvodina spanning 2009–2014, obtained through an anonymised dataset provided by a regional chamber of commerce. Out-of-sample one-step-ahead log-scores improve by 0.31 nats relative to a fixed-drift local level model. The paper also investigates the identifiability of the switching parameters and provides conditions under which the EM solution is consistent under mild regularity assumptions.

title: Scheduling Inspection Drones in Industrial Facilities: A Variable Neighbourhood Search Approach
abstract: Autonomous drone inspection of industrial facilities requires scheduling flight routes subject to battery endurance, no-fly zones, mandatory inspection windows, and charging station availability. This paper models the problem as a variant of the vehicle routing problem with time windows (VRPTW) incorporating energy constraints and formulates it for a heterogeneous fleet of two drone types with differing payloads and endurance. A variable neighbourhood search (VNS) metaheuristic with five neighbourhood structures is applied. The shaking procedure uses random segment reversal and inter-route swaps. Tests are performed on instances derived from floor plans of three anonymised manufacturing facilities with 80 to 220 inspection points and fleets of 4 to 12 drones. VNS closes 78% of the gap between the greedy initialisation and the LP relaxation bound on average, compared to 61% for a simulated-annealing benchmark, and runs in under 60 seconds for all instances.

title: Automata-Theoretic Models in Formal Language Theory: A Pedagogical Survey
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured introduction to automata-theoretic foundations of formal language theory intended for graduate students in mathematics and computer science. Topics covered include the Myhill–Nerode theorem, minimisation of DFAs, the Pumping Lemma for regular languages, closure properties, and the relationship between regular expressions and finite automata. Each section includes worked examples and a set of exercises graded by difficulty. The chapter also gives a brief account of learning-theoretic aspects, specifically the Gold limit-identification result for the class of regular languages from positive examples alone, motivating the use of negative examples or active query mechanisms. The exposition is self-contained, assuming only undergraduate-level discrete mathematics. The chapter is part of a regional collaborative textbook project involving universities from Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia.

title: Least-Squares Channel Estimation for OFDM Systems over Frequency-Selective Fading Channels: A Pilot Density Study
abstract: This paper examines the trade-off between pilot density and mean squared error (MSE) in least-squares (LS) channel estimation for OFDM systems operating over frequency-selective Rayleigh fading channels. A pilot grid design methodology is proposed based on the maximum Doppler frequency and the channel coherence bandwidth, derived analytically from a standard exponential power delay profile. Using simulations over a bandwidth of 10 MHz with 512 subcarriers and vehicular channel models at carrier frequencies of 900 MHz and 2.1 GHz, the study evaluates MSE and bit-error-rate (BER) performance for QPSK and 16-QAM modulations. Results indicate that reducing pilot overhead by 30% relative to the Nyquist-rate criterion incurs less than 0.4 dB degradation in SNR at a BER of 10^{-3} for pedestrian scenarios but up to 1.8 dB at vehicular speeds above 60 km/h. The findings provide practical guidelines for pilot resource allocation in LTE-compatible systems.

title: Effect of Antenna Spacing on Spatial Correlation in Linear Arrays: Measurements at 2.6 GHz
abstract: Spatial correlation between antenna elements is a critical factor limiting the capacity gains predicted by multi-antenna theory. This work presents an empirical characterisation of the spatial correlation matrix for a uniform linear array (ULA) with eight elements measured at 2.6 GHz in an indoor office environment at the Faculty of Technical Sciences campus, Novi Sad. Measurements were taken at 47 distinct receiver positions covering both line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight conditions. The exponential and Kronecker correlation models were fitted to measured data and compared using a normalised Frobenius-norm error metric. Results show that the exponential model underestimates correlation at antenna spacings below 0.4 wavelengths by up to 18%, while the Kronecker model matches well in LOS conditions. The study also quantifies how increased spatial correlation reduces effective degrees of freedom, reducing mutual information by 2.1 bits/s/Hz at 10 dB SNR compared to the uncorrelated case for four active streams.
venue: Proceedings of the 20th International Conference on Telecommunications and Signal Processing (ICTSP)

title: MMSE Channel Estimation in Multi-Cell MIMO with Inter-Cell Interference: Analytical Bounds and Simulation
abstract: Pilot contamination arising from pilot sequence reuse across cells is a fundamental impairment in multi-cell MIMO uplink training. This paper derives a closed-form expression for the MMSE estimation error in a seven-cell hexagonal deployment where all cells share the same pilot set of length 10 symbols. The analysis assumes Rayleigh fading with full spatial correlation described by the one-ring scattering model. Closed-form lower bounds on the MSE are obtained as a function of the inter-cell interference-to-signal ratio, pilot length, and the number of base station antennas. Numerical evaluation for a system with 64 and 128 antennas at the base station shows that doubling antenna count reduces the contamination-induced MSE floor by 3.1 dB on average across the cell edge user positions considered. The derived bounds are tighter than Jensen-based approximations from prior literature in the moderate-to-high interference regime, differing by less than 0.2 dB at SNRs above 5 dB.

title: Pilot Decontamination via Subspace Projection in Massive MIMO Uplink
abstract: This paper proposes a subspace-based pilot decontamination scheme for the uplink of a massive MIMO system operating under spatially correlated Rayleigh fading. The approach exploits the low-rank structure of the spatial covariance matrices of desired and interfering users: when the signal subspaces of co-pilot users are sufficiently separated in the angle domain, an oblique projection onto the desired user's subspace suppresses contaminating pilots without requiring coordination between base stations. The rank of each covariance matrix is estimated from received pilot observations using a threshold on the eigenvalue profile. For a 100-antenna base station serving 10 users per cell in a three-cell layout with pilot reuse factor one, simulations show that the proposed method reduces normalised MSE by 6.4 dB relative to standard MMSE estimation and improves uplink achievable rate by 1.3 bits/s/Hz per user at 0 dB SNR. Performance degrades gracefully when covariance subspaces overlap by up to 15%.

title: Covariance Matrix Estimation for Massive MIMO Under Limited Pilot Budget
abstract: Accurate spatial covariance estimation is a prerequisite for subspace-based channel estimation methods in massive MIMO. This paper analyses the sample covariance matrix estimator under the constraint that the number of pilot observations per coherence interval is comparable to or smaller than the number of base station antennas. Using random matrix theory results for the spiked covariance model, analytical expressions are derived for the detection probability of each signal eigenvalue as a function of observation count, array size, and signal-to-noise ratio. A shrinkage estimator is then constructed that minimises the expected Frobenius-norm error between the estimated and true covariance matrix. For a 128-antenna array with 20 pilot symbols per coherence interval and 8 active users, the shrinkage estimator reduces covariance estimation MSE by 4.7 dB compared to the sample covariance matrix and by 1.9 dB compared to a diagonal-loading baseline. The improved covariance estimate is propagated through an MMSE channel estimator, yielding a 0.8 dB gain in channel estimation MSE.

title: Channel Estimation in Ricean Fading Massive MIMO: Impact of the K-Factor on MMSE Performance
abstract: Most massive MIMO analysis assumes Rayleigh fading, yet many deployment scenarios — rooftop-to-indoor, fixed wireless access, stadium coverage — exhibit a strong specular component characterised by a non-trivial Ricean K-factor. This paper extends the MMSE channel estimation framework to spatially correlated Ricean fading, deriving an exact expression for the achievable estimation MSE as a function of K, the number of antennas M, the pilot length τ, and the spatial covariance matrix. It is shown analytically that ignoring the line-of-sight component in the estimator design causes an MSE penalty that grows with K and saturates at approximately 10 log10(K+1) dB for large K. For K values between 3 and 10 dB, common in measured 3.5 GHz urban microcell channels, this penalty ranges from 1.9 to 4.1 dB with M = 64. A modified MMSE estimator that incorporates the known mean component is proposed and shown to recover the optimal MSE when the mean is estimated from long-term observations over 200 coherence intervals.

title: Pilot Contamination Mitigation in Correlated Ricean Massive MIMO via Statistical Beamforming
abstract: This paper addresses pilot contamination in multi-cell massive MIMO when both desired and interfering channels follow spatially correlated Ricean fading with distinct mean directions of arrival. A statistical precoding and combining scheme is derived that exploits both the covariance structure and the mean direction information to separate co-pilot users. The combining vector is designed by maximising the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio averaged over fast fading realisations, leading to a generalised eigenvector problem solved at the timescale of covariance updates. In a simulation study with three cells, 128 antennas per base station, and K-factors between 0 and 10 dB, the proposed scheme achieves pilot-contamination-free scaling behaviour: per-user spectral efficiency grows without bound as M increases when mean directions of interfering users are separated by more than 5 degrees. For a fixed M = 128 and a 10-degree separation, uplink sum-rate improves by 2.7 bits/s/Hz over standard MMSE combining.

title: Massive MIMO Channel Estimation: From Rayleigh to Ricean Fading
abstract: This book chapter provides a self-contained treatment of channel estimation theory for large-scale antenna systems, tracing the progression from independent Rayleigh fading through spatially correlated Rayleigh and finally to the spatially correlated Ricean model. The chapter covers the Bayesian MMSE estimator derivation, the role of the spatial covariance matrix and its acquisition, the structure of the pilot contamination interference term in each fading model, and the conditions under which contamination can be mitigated through statistical processing. It includes worked examples for a 64-antenna single-sector base station, illustrating how increasing the K-factor from 0 to 6 dB changes the optimal pilot allocation strategy. Connections to practical system design choices, including pilot reuse patterns and covariance feedback overhead, are discussed. The chapter also surveys selected results from measured channels at 3.5 GHz and 26 GHz to ground the theoretical development in empirical observations.

title: Uplink Spectral Efficiency Analysis of Massive MIMO with Imperfect CSI and Hardware Impairments
abstract: Practical massive MIMO deployments are affected not only by pilot contamination but also by hardware impairments such as phase noise, quantisation distortion, and nonlinear amplification. This paper provides a unified spectral efficiency analysis that accounts for both imperfect channel state information from MMSE estimation under correlated Ricean fading and additive hardware distortion modelled as a Gaussian random variable whose variance scales with signal power. Closed-form lower bounds on per-user uplink achievable rate are derived using the use-and-then-forget bounding technique. For a 200-antenna base station, 20 simultaneous users per cell, and a hardware distortion level of -30 dBc, the combined effect of imperfect CSI and hardware impairments reduces the sum spectral efficiency by 17% compared to the ideal case, with pilot contamination and hardware distortion contributing roughly equally at intermediate SNR. The analysis suggests that hardware quality requirements can be relaxed for arrays larger than 150 antennas at the cost of at most 10% rate loss.

title: Data-Aided Covariance Matrix Tracking for Slowly Time-Varying Massive MIMO Channels
abstract: Spatial covariance matrices in massive MIMO change on a timescale much longer than the fast fading but must still be updated periodically to maintain estimation quality. This paper proposes a data-aided covariance tracking algorithm that uses tentative data symbol decisions, made after initial detection with an outdated covariance estimate, to refine the covariance estimate within the same coherence block. The estimator is formulated as a rank-one update to the current estimate, weighted by the decision reliability metric derived from the posterior symbol probabilities. In a simulation campaign covering 500 coherence intervals with covariance variation modelling user movement at 3 km/h in a 3.5 GHz deployment, the proposed tracker reduces the covariance estimation normalised MSE by 2.3 dB compared to pilot-only estimation and maintains within 0.5 dB of a genie-aided benchmark that has access to true channel realisations. The algorithm adds less than 4% computational overhead relative to standard MMSE detection.

title: Angle-Domain Pilot Assignment for Pilot Contamination Reduction in Ricean Massive MIMO
abstract: Pilot assignment policies that account for the spatial structure of user channels can substantially reduce pilot contamination without requiring inter-cell coordination beyond a one-time information exchange. This paper formulates pilot assignment as a combinatorial optimisation problem where the objective is to minimise the sum of pairwise subspace overlaps — quantified by the squared Frobenius norm of the product of covariance matrices — across all pairs of users sharing the same pilot in adjacent cells. A greedy assignment algorithm is proposed and benchmarked against an exhaustive search for systems with up to 8 pilots and 3 cells. In a 128-antenna Ricean fading scenario with K-factors drawn from a uniform distribution on [2, 8] dB and angular spread of 10 degrees, the greedy scheme achieves within 5% of the optimal sum overlap and reduces pilot contamination MSE by 4.9 dB compared to random pilot assignment. The overhead for the inter-cell covariance exchange is estimated at less than 0.3% of channel coherence bandwidth.

title: Near-Field Channel Estimation for Extremely Large Aperture Arrays at Sub-6 GHz Frequencies
abstract: As antenna apertures grow beyond several metres, users within tens of metres of the array may reside in the near-field Fresnel region, invalidating planar wavefront assumptions used in standard channel models and estimators. This paper studies channel estimation for a 256-element uniform linear array at 3.7 GHz when one or more users are located between 5 m and 40 m from the array. A polar-domain channel representation using a discretised set of range-angle bins is adopted, and a compressed sensing estimator based on iterative reweighted least squares is used to recover sparse channel coefficients. Simulated channels based on a ray-tracing output for a factory-floor geometry are used for evaluation. At 10 dB SNR, the polar-domain estimator reduces MSE by 7.1 dB compared to an angular-domain estimator that neglects near-field curvature, and by 2.4 dB compared to a direct least-squares approach. The study highlights which array lengths and distances trigger a practically significant near-field estimation penalty.

title: Coordinated Reactive Power Dispatch in Low-Voltage Networks Using a Two-Stage Optimisation Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage optimisation framework for coordinating reactive power resources in low-voltage distribution networks, combining a day-ahead scheduling stage based on forecast generation and load profiles with a real-time correction stage executed at 15-minute intervals. Reactive power resources considered include smart photovoltaic inverters, a single on-load tap changer at the MV/LV transformer, and a switched capacitor bank at the feeder midpoint. The day-ahead stage minimises total reactive power losses subject to voltage band constraints using a linear programming relaxation of the power flow equations. The correction stage applies a rule-based droop adjustment using local voltage measurements only, requiring no communication infrastructure. The framework is tested on a 52-node low-voltage benchmark network and validated on a real feeder topology from Novi Sad obtained from the distribution system operator. Simulation over a 30-day period shows average voltage deviation reduction of 34 % and reactive energy import reduction of 41 % relative to a no-control baseline. Computational time for the day-ahead stage is under 8 seconds on standard hardware.

title: Thermal bridge effect at horizontal panel joints in IMS-type prefabricated residential buildings in Novi Sad
abstract: This paper investigates thermal bridging at horizontal concrete joints in large-panel IMS-type residential buildings constructed in Novi Sad between 1965 and 1985. Thermographic surveys were conducted on six building facades during the heating season, with outdoor temperatures between −5 °C and +2 °C and indoor temperatures held at 20 °C. Surface temperature measurements obtained from FLIR imagery were compared against two-dimensional finite-element heat-flow simulations performed in a custom script. The linear thermal transmittance (ψ-value) of the horizontal joint was found to range from 0.38 W/(m·K) to 0.61 W/(m·K), depending on the degree of joint deterioration and original design variant. These values exceed the limit prescribed by the 2012 Serbian Rulebook on Energy Efficiency in Buildings by factors of 2.5 to 4.1. The paper proposes a simplified correction factor for use in building energy certificates when detailed joint geometry is unavailable, calibrated against the surveyed dataset of 74 individual joint sections.

title: Interstitial condensation risk in original and retrofitted external wall panels of Serbian prefabricated housing stock
abstract: Glaser-method and transient hygrothermal simulations are applied to four wall assembly configurations representative of Serbian prefabricated housing built between 1960 and 1990: the unmodified sandwich panel with mineral wool core, two variants with externally applied expanded polystyrene (EPS) insulation of 8 cm and 12 cm thickness, and one variant with mineral wool external insulation. Boundary conditions were derived from ten-year hourly climate data from the Novi Sad meteorological station. Results show that the original unmodified panel exceeds the condensation-onset threshold during 63 nights per heating season on average, concentrated at the inner concrete leaf–mineral wool interface. Addition of 12 cm EPS reduces condensation episodes to fewer than four nights per season but shifts the dew-point plane outward, raising questions about vapour retarder placement. The paper tabulates monthly moisture accumulation for each configuration and compares compliance with requirements of the Serbian standard SRPS EN ISO 13788.

title: Field calibration of thermographic defect detection against destructive core sampling in post-war prefabricated panel facades
abstract: The accuracy of infrared thermography in identifying delaminated insulation, mortar-joint voids, and moisture infiltration in prefabricated concrete facade panels is assessed through a paired field study. Thirty-two panels on two residential towers in Subotica were first surveyed with a FLIR T640 camera under controlled steady-state temperature difference (ΔT ≥ 10 K). Suspected anomaly locations were then opened by destructive core sampling at 48 points, of which 31 had been flagged as defective by thermography. The false-positive rate was 19% and false-negative rate 11%. False positives were predominantly associated with steel reinforcement shadows rather than true insulation voids. A set of image-interpretation criteria is proposed that reduces the false-positive rate to 8% when applied retrospectively. The paper discusses practical constraints on ΔT requirements in the continental climate of northern Serbia and provides guidance on optimal survey timing relative to sunset.

title: Mapping the spatial distribution of thermal defects across large residential blocks using low-altitude thermographic surveys: a pilot study
abstract: A methodology for systematic thermographic mapping of multi-storey prefabricated residential blocks is described and tested on a 12-storey, 96-apartment building in Novi Sad. The building was surveyed from ground level using a tripod-mounted FLIR T840 camera with a 15° lens at five standoff distances between 8 m and 32 m. Image rectification and mosaicking were performed using photogrammetric control points measured by total station. The resulting composite thermal orthophoto at 4 cm/pixel resolution allows individual panel joints, window frame perimeters, and balcony slab penetrations to be distinguished and classified. Defect density was highest at floor-level horizontal joints on the north-west facade (3.1 anomalies per 10 m²) and lowest on the south-east facade (0.6 per 10 m²). The orthophoto workflow is described step by step and the metadata format proposed for integration with building energy audit databases maintained under Serbian regulations.

title: Sensitivity of calculated energy consumption to assumed ψ-values for panel joints in Serbian energy certificates
abstract: Serbian building energy certificates require declaration of thermal bridge linear transmittance values for each junction type. Because detailed joint geometry is rarely available for prefabricated buildings constructed before 1990, practitioners routinely apply default tabulated ψ-values from the national guideline. This paper quantifies the error introduced by that practice. A parametric study uses a representative five-storey, 20-apartment prefabricated block as a reference model and varies the panel-joint ψ-value over the range 0.2–0.8 W/(m·K), as bounded by the field measurements reported in prior work. Annual heating energy demand calculated by the monthly quasi-steady method of SRPS EN ISO 13790 changes by up to 24 kWh/(m²·year) across this range, sufficient to shift a building between energy class E and class G. The paper recommends a minimum thermographic survey protocol and a simplified two-dimensional simulation procedure that practitioners can complete within one working day per building.

title: Effect of EPS thickness and surface finish on hygrothermal performance of ETICS retrofits on large-panel facades in a continental climate
abstract: External thermal composite insulation systems (ETICS) with EPS thicknesses of 8, 10, 12, and 15 cm were applied to four identical staircase segments of a 1975-era prefabricated residential building in Sombor as part of a municipal renovation programme. Each segment was equipped with three embedded flat-plate heat flux sensors and four relative humidity/temperature probes at the insulation–concrete interface, logging at 10-minute intervals over two full heating seasons. Heat flux through the retrofitted sections was 38–52% lower than through the unretrofitted reference section. Interface relative humidity remained below 80% in all monitored configurations throughout both seasons. However, the 8 cm configuration showed moisture accumulation exceeding 0.1 kg/m² at the interface during the second January, attributed to wind-driven rain penetration at the base rail. The paper presents the complete sensor dataset and a calibrated hygrothermal model validated against it.

title: Air leakage at prefabricated panel joints and its contribution to measured heat loss: blower-door tests on two residential towers
abstract: Two residential towers of identical construction in Novi Sad, one unretrofitted and one with recently applied EPS ETICS, were subjected to blower-door pressurisation tests at 50 Pa and 100 Pa differential pressure following the procedure of SRPS EN ISO 9972. The unretrofitted tower achieved n₅₀ = 4.1 h⁻¹ and the retrofitted tower n₅₀ = 1.6 h⁻¹. Simultaneous smoke-pencil and thermographic imaging during pressurisation located 87% of air leakage in the unretrofitted tower at horizontal and vertical panel joints, with a secondary concentration at window frame perimeters (9%). In the retrofitted tower the base rail joint and penetrations through the EPS layer for utility brackets were the dominant leakage sites. Convective heat loss calculated from the infiltration rate accounted for 18% of total measured heat loss in the unretrofitted case and 7% in the retrofitted case, indicating that fabric retrofit alone substantially reduces infiltration.

title: Compliance assessment of prefabricated housing renovation projects with the 2020 revision of the Serbian Rulebook on Energy Efficiency
abstract: The 2020 revision of the Serbian Rulebook on Energy Efficiency in Buildings (Official Gazette 61/2011, 43/2020) introduced tightened U-value limits and mandatory thermal bridge documentation for residential renovations. This paper examines whether 14 completed renovation projects on prefabricated residential buildings in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina, undertaken between 2017 and 2022, would have satisfied the revised requirements had they been submitted under the new rules. Project energy audits, architectural drawings, and building permits were collected from four municipal archives. Eight of the 14 projects would not comply due to insufficient insulation thickness at balcony slab edges; three further projects lack adequate documentation of window frame perimeter bridging. The paper identifies the documentation gaps most commonly encountered in practice and proposes a checklist aligned with the revised Rulebook that could be incorporated into the municipal permit review process.

title: Thermal bridge catalogue for the five most common prefabricated panel systems built in Vojvodina 1960–1990: geometry, ψ-values, and retrofit recommendations
abstract: A systematic catalogue of two-dimensional thermal bridge calculations is presented for 38 junction configurations extracted from original design documentation of five prefabricated building systems used in Vojvodina: IMS, Jugomont, Trudbenik, LRPC-Novi Sad, and a locally adapted Camus variant. Junction types include horizontal and vertical panel joints, window sill, head and jamb junctions, balcony slab penetrations, and roof–wall connections. Geometry data were digitised from archival drawings held at the Urban Planning Institute of Vojvodina. ψ-values were calculated using two-dimensional finite-element heat flow simulation conforming to SRPS EN ISO 10211. The catalogue provides ψ-values for the as-built condition and for four retrofit scenarios (8, 12, and 15 cm EPS; 12 cm mineral wool). Values range from 0.02 W/(m·K) for internal vertical panel joints to 0.74 W/(m·K) for uninsulated balcony slab edges. The catalogue is formatted for direct entry into Serbian energy certification software.

title: Drone-assisted thermographic survey of a prefabricated residential neighbourhood: workflow, data quality, and comparison with ground-level surveys
abstract: A residential neighbourhood of 22 prefabricated buildings in Sombor was surveyed using a DJI Matrice 300 RTK drone equipped with a FLIR Zenmuse XT2 thermal camera during a calm, clear night with outdoor temperature −3 °C and indoor temperature 21 °C. Flight paths were planned to maintain a constant 15 m standoff distance from each facade. The resulting thermal orthomosaic covers 8 400 m² of facade area at 5 cm/pixel ground sampling distance. Defect detection rates were compared against a subset of 340 m² of facade previously surveyed from the ground under identical weather conditions. Agreement in defect location between methods was 84%; drone imagery missed narrow vertical joint anomalies narrower than 15 cm due to pixel resolution limits. Georeferenced defect shapefiles were exported and overlaid on the municipal GIS cadastre, enabling prioritisation of renovation investment across the neighbourhood. Radiometric calibration procedures and metadata standards are described in detail.

title: Predicted versus measured in-use energy consumption in prefabricated buildings after ETICS renovation: a gap analysis for 18 buildings in Vojvodina
abstract: Energy consumption predicted in renovation energy audits is compared with actual metered heat consumption recorded by district heating billing data for 18 prefabricated residential buildings in three municipalities in Vojvodina, all renovated with EPS ETICS between 2016 and 2021. Predicted post-renovation heating demand was on average 31% lower than metered consumption in the first full heating season after renovation, a gap consistent with the energy performance gap reported in the international literature for similar building types. Analysis of variance identifies occupancy-related internal gains and ventilation behaviour as the largest contributors to the discrepancy, together accounting for 58% of explained variance in the regression model. Thermal bridge treatment quality—assessed by post-renovation thermographic re-survey—explains a further 19%. Buildings where balcony slab edges were left uninsulated show a 12 kWh/(m²·year) higher metered demand than those where edge insulation was applied, a difference statistically significant at p < 0.01.

title: Scanning electron microscopy characterisation of the interfacial transition zone between recycled aggregate and cement paste: effect of pre-soaking treatment
abstract: The interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between recycled coarse aggregate and fresh cement paste was examined using scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy on polished cross-sections. Specimens were prepared with untreated dry aggregate, aggregate pre-soaked for 30 minutes, and aggregate pre-soaked for 24 hours to evaluate how aggregate moisture state affects ITZ microstructure. Backscattered electron images were acquired at magnifications of 500× to 5,000× across ten randomly selected aggregate–paste interfaces per specimen. Image analysis software was used to quantify portlandite crystal orientation, porosity gradient, and ITZ width, defined as the zone with measurable compositional deviation from bulk paste. Pre-soaked aggregate showed a 15–20% reduction in average ITZ thickness and a measurable decrease in oriented portlandite relative to dry aggregate. However, 24-hour pre-soaking produced localised water pockets at the interface, visible as irregular voids up to 85 µm wide. Results suggest that 30-minute pre-soaking offers a practical balance for precast production schedules.

title: Statistical variability of splitting tensile and flexural strength in recycled aggregate concrete: dataset from a multi-batch production study
abstract: Splitting tensile strength and flexural strength were measured across eight production batches of recycled aggregate concrete at 40% and 70% replacement levels, with each batch mixed on separate days using aggregates sourced from the same demolition stockpile. A total of 96 cylinder specimens (150 × 300 mm) and 96 prisms (150 × 150 × 600 mm) were tested. Within-batch and between-batch components of variance were separated using a nested ANOVA. Between-batch variance accounted for 38% of total tensile strength variance and 42% of flexural strength variance at 70% replacement, compared with 18% and 21% respectively at 40% replacement. These proportions are notably higher than values reported for natural aggregate concrete in comparable studies. Correlation between splitting tensile and compressive strength followed the EN 1992-1-1 relationship closely at 40% replacement but diverged at 70%, with measured tensile values approximately 11% lower than predicted. Results suggest that current code relationships require revision for high-replacement recycled aggregate mixes.

title: Latent class recovery of arithmetic skill states in primary-school learners: a simulation and empirical study
abstract: This study evaluated the accuracy of latent class analysis (LCA) for recovering discrete skill states in a sample of 412 third-grade pupils completing a computer-administered arithmetic battery. Three-, four-, and five-class solutions were compared using BIC, AIC, and entropy indices. Simulation conditions varied sample size (100–800), class separation (low, medium, high), and item discrimination. Results showed that four-class solutions with medium-to-high separation were recovered reliably at sample sizes above 250. Applied to the empirical data, a four-class model distinguished non-starters, counting-based solvers, partial-fact retrievers, and fluent retrievers, with class membership predicting end-of-year teacher grades (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Response latency added incremental classification accuracy beyond accuracy scores alone (ΔBIC = −38). Implications for adaptive routing in primary mathematics software are discussed.

title: Fit indices for polytomous Rasch models applied to reading comprehension items in Serbian secondary schools
abstract: Polytomous items from a standardised reading comprehension test administered to 1,847 ninth-grade pupils in Serbia were analysed under the partial credit model (PCM) and the generalised partial credit model (GPCM). Item fit was evaluated using infit and outfit mean-square statistics, Q3 residual correlations, and signed chi-square tests. Thirteen of 42 items showed misfit primarily attributable to non-ordered thresholds, a pattern linked to ambiguous intermediate response categories identified through expert review. Reordering category labels improved fit for eight of these items in a validation subsample (n = 623). Person-fit analysis identified approximately 4.2 % of respondents as aberrant responders, concentrated in lower-ability ranges. The study provides normative fit benchmarks for Serbian large-scale educational surveys and recommends threshold disorder checks as a routine step before IRT scaling.

title: Response time as a diagnostic signal in adaptive vocabulary tests: evidence from an IRT-based speed–accuracy model
abstract: This study applied a joint speed–accuracy IRT model—specifically a hierarchical version of the van der Linden (2007) framework—to data from an adaptive English vocabulary test taken by 934 university students in Serbia. The test consisted of 60 items drawn from a calibrated bank and was delivered via a browser-based platform that logged response times at millisecond resolution. Separate latent dimensions for ability and speed were estimated; the correlation between person speed and ability was −0.22, indicating that faster responders were not reliably more accurate. Item-level analyses showed that high-frequency vocabulary items elicited shorter and less variable response times, while low-frequency items produced bimodal response-time distributions consistent with dual-process retrieval. A subscore derived from response-time residuals predicted self-reported study habits independently of accuracy-based scores. Implications for adaptive test termination rules are discussed.

title: Hidden Markov models for tracking conceptual change in secondary-school physics: a comparison of transition structures
abstract: Conceptual change in Newtonian mechanics was modelled as a latent Markov process using interaction logs from a physics simulation environment used by 318 high-school students across eight weeks. Four hidden states—misconception-dominant, transitional, partial-correct, and expert—were hypothesised based on prior qualitative research. Three transition structures (unconstrained, left-to-right, and partially ordered) were compared by marginal likelihood. The partially ordered model, which permitted regression from partial-correct to transitional but not to misconception-dominant, provided the best fit (ΔBIC = 112 versus unconstrained). State residence times averaged 3.1 instructional sessions for the transitional state. Instructional scaffolding events logged by the system were associated with a 2.3-fold increase in forward transition probability. The study provides a template for embedding hidden Markov diagnostics in simulation-based science learning environments.

title: Psychometric modelling of cognitive skill acquisition in technology-enhanced learning environments
abstract: This book chapter surveys quantitative methods for diagnosing and tracking cognitive skill acquisition from digital trace data, with emphasis on item response theory, Bayesian knowledge tracing, and latent Markov models. The chapter begins with a unified notation covering item-level parameters, person parameters, and time-indexed state vectors. It then describes estimation strategies—maximum likelihood, EM, MCMC—and discusses practical sample-size requirements for each. A running example based on an arithmetic tutoring platform illustrates how each framework represents the same learner trajectory differently and what diagnostic inferences each affords. The chapter closes with a discussion of validity threats specific to trace-data measurement: log missingness, engagement artefacts, and confounding of ability with interface familiarity. A checklist for practitioners is provided as an appendix. The chapter is intended for researchers and developers working on educational technology platforms who need to select and implement appropriate psychometric frameworks.

title: Detecting disengaged response patterns in large-scale online assessments using mixture IRT with a non-effortful responder class
abstract: A mixture IRT model was developed to jointly estimate item parameters and classify respondents as effortful or non-effortful, using both accuracy and response-time features. The model was applied to data from a national diagnostic assessment of mathematics delivered online to 11,342 eighth-grade students in Serbia in 2018. The non-effortful class, characterised by near-chance accuracy and response times below 4 seconds, comprised 8.7 % of the sample. Excluding non-effortful respondents shifted item difficulty estimates by up to 0.42 logits for cognitively demanding items and narrowed ability-distribution standard deviation from 1.21 to 1.09. A sensitivity analysis using three alternative time thresholds confirmed stability of class membership above 82 % agreement. The study quantifies the impact of disengagement on population ability estimates and provides a mixture-model framework that can be integrated into operational assessment pipelines.

title: Clickstream feature engineering for early prediction of learning outcomes in a university-level statistics MOOC
abstract: Forty-seven clickstream features—covering session frequency, video replay rates, quiz attempt sequences, forum post counts, and time-of-day patterns—were extracted from the activity logs of 2,891 enrolees in a university-level introductory statistics MOOC run over 12 weeks. Feature importance was assessed via gradient-boosted trees and logistic regression; a parsimonious nine-feature model achieved AUC = 0.81 for dropout prediction at week four, compared to AUC = 0.68 for a baseline demographic model. Psychometric analysis using a two-parameter IRT model applied to weekly quiz items showed that estimated ability trajectories up to week three predicted final certificate attainment with r = 0.74. Combining ability trajectories with clickstream features in a stacked model improved AUC to 0.84. The study identifies a minimal feature set suitable for deployment in low-resource learning management systems.

title: Estimating knowledge-state transitions without ground-truth labels: an expectation-maximisation approach for unstructured course logs
abstract: Most knowledge-tracing studies rely on structured item banks with known correct answers; many real-world e-learning platforms produce unstructured logs where correctness labels are absent or unreliable. This paper develops an EM-based procedure that infers binary correctness proxies from response-time distributions, item co-occurrence patterns, and sequential consistency, without requiring manual item annotation. The procedure was validated on two datasets: a synthetic log generated from a known BKT model (parameter recovery RMSE ≤ 0.06) and an anonymised log of 7,200 learners using a corporate onboarding platform where ground-truth performance ratings were available for a 15 % subsample. On the subsample, inferred correctness correlated r = 0.68 with human ratings. Knowledge-state trajectories estimated from the inferred labels predicted six-month retention test scores (β = 0.41, p < 0.001) after controlling for time on platform. The procedure requires only event-timestamp and item-identifier fields.

title: Psychometric calibration of an eye-tracking-based reading fluency diagnostic for early primary grades
abstract: An eye-tracking-based reading fluency assessment was developed and calibrated for first- and second-grade children (N = 344, ages 6–8) using a Rasch model applied to fixation-derived accuracy scores and a log-normal response-time model for reading rate. Stimuli consisted of 36 short passages graded by lexical frequency and syntactic complexity. Item calibration indicated good fit (infit MNSQ range: 0.83–1.17) for 31 of 36 passages; five passages were revised after think-aloud protocols revealed ambiguous illustrations. Test information peaked at θ = −0.8, appropriate for the target population. A concurrent validity study against an established teacher-administered oral reading fluency probe yielded r = 0.73. Differential item functioning by gender was absent for 34 of 36 items. The diagnostic was subsequently embedded in a tablet-based assessment application deployed in 12 primary schools in Vojvodina.

title: Alignment between formative diagnostic inferences and summative grades: an IRT-based audit across six secondary-school subjects in Serbia
abstract: Data from six secondary-school subjects—mathematics, Serbian language, biology, history, physics, and English—were collected from a digital learning management platform used by 3,412 students in 22 schools across Serbia during one academic year. For each subject, a multidimensional IRT model was estimated from platform quiz responses, and inferred diagnostic ability scores were compared to end-of-year teacher grades using Pearson and Spearman correlations, classification accuracy matrices, and Bland–Altman agreement plots. Correlations ranged from 0.51 (history) to 0.74 (mathematics). Systematic grade inflation relative to diagnostic scores was found in 14 of 22 schools, with a mean offset of 0.4 grade points on a five-point scale. Schools with higher diagnostic–grade alignment also showed lower within-school grade variance. The findings suggest that diagnostic platform scores and teacher grades measure partially overlapping but non-redundant constructs.

title: Reliability of Psychodynamic Case Formulation Components in Routine Clinical Practice: A Naturalistic Study
abstract: Most reliability studies of psychodynamic case formulation are conducted under controlled research conditions that differ substantially from everyday clinical practice. This naturalistic study assessed inter-rater agreement for five formulation components—core conflictual relationship theme, dominant defence level, quality of object representations, ego strength, and developmental vulnerability index—in a routine outpatient psychiatry setting. Forty-six consecutive new referrals to a psychiatric outpatient unit were each independently formulated by two clinicians (drawn from a pool of eight) after a standard initial assessment interview. ICC values ranged from 0.48 (developmental vulnerability index) to 0.71 (dominant defence level). Components requiring inference about developmental history showed the lowest reliability. Regression analyses showed that rater dyad composition, not patient diagnosis, was the strongest predictor of agreement level. Implications for quality assurance in clinical training programmes are considered.

title: Nature connectedness as a predictor of restorative experience quality: evidence from a sample of urban and peri-urban residents in Vojvodina
abstract: Nature connectedness—the dispositional tendency to feel part of the natural world—has been proposed as a predictor of both frequency of nature contact and its psychological benefits, but most supporting evidence comes from Western European or North American samples. This study administered the Nature Relatedness Scale (NRS-6), the Connectedness to Nature Scale, and a custom restorative experience quality index to 312 adults (182 women, mean age 38.7, SD 13.1) recruited from Novi Sad and four smaller peri-urban settlements in Vojvodina. Hierarchical regression, controlling for green space access (self-reported and GIS-derived), age, gender, and education, showed that NRS-6 explained an additional 9% of variance in restorative experience quality (ΔR² = .09, F(1,304) = 31.4, p < .001). The Connectedness to Nature Scale added no incremental variance beyond NRS-6. Rural-versus-urban residence did not significantly moderate the nature connectedness–restoration relationship. Results replicate the importance of dispositional connectedness in a regional sample previously underrepresented in the literature.

title: Influence of Passenger Demand Fluctuation on Dwell Time Distribution at High-Frequency Urban Bus Stops
abstract: This paper examines how short-term fluctuations in passenger demand affect dwell time distributions at three high-frequency bus stops in Novi Sad. Field data were collected over eight weeks using manual counting supplemented by video recording, yielding 4,820 individual stop events. Dwell times were modelled using a log-normal distribution fitted separately for peak and off-peak periods. Results show that coefficient of variation for dwell time increases from 0.31 during off-peak to 0.54 during the morning peak, driven primarily by bunching of demand in narrow time windows. A regression model relating dwell time to boarding count, alighting count, and door configuration explains 67% of observed variance. The findings suggest that fixed-schedule BRT planning tools systematically underestimate stop delay by 18–25% when demand variability is ignored. Implications for buffer time allocation in BRT timetabling are discussed.

title: Stop Capacity Estimation for BRT Stations with Single and Dual Berths Under Mixed Traffic Entry
abstract: The paper presents a capacity estimation procedure for BRT stations where buses share approach lanes with general traffic before reaching dedicated stopping areas. Single-berth and dual-berth configurations at four stations on the proposed Novi Sad east–west BRT corridor are analysed using queuing theory adapted from HCM 6th edition methods. Entry traffic volumes ranged from 420 to 1,140 pcu/h, and bus frequencies from 6 to 20 buses per hour per direction. Simulation experiments in PTV Vissim were calibrated against 12 days of field observation. The analysis shows that mixed-entry conditions reduce effective stop capacity by 22–38% relative to fully separated BRT, depending on bus frequency and entry saturation degree. A look-up table framework is proposed for practitioners to quickly estimate capacity reduction factors without running full microsimulations. The method is validated against an independent dataset from a BRT corridor in Budapest.

title: Headway Irregularity Propagation Along a BRT Corridor: A Segment-Level Analysis
abstract: Using GNSS trajectory data from 14 buses operating on a 9.2 km BRT-like corridor in Novi Sad over a 30-day period, this study quantifies how headway deviations initiated at the first stop propagate downstream. A total of 3,106 one-way trips were analysed. Headway coefficient of variation increases monotonically from 0.18 at the first stop to 0.47 at the terminal, with the steepest growth occurring at two intermediate stops where mixed traffic intersections cause unpredictable approach delays. A first-order Markov model is fitted to headway sequences and achieves a mean absolute prediction error of 41 seconds at the corridor midpoint. The study identifies three stop locations where operational interventions—such as holding strategies or signal priority extensions—would yield the greatest reduction in end-to-end irregularity. Results are compared with published findings from BRT systems in Łódź and Brno.

title: Effect of Kneeling Bus Technology on Boarding Times for Passengers with Reduced Mobility at BRT Stops
abstract: A controlled field experiment was conducted at two BRT-standard stops in Novi Sad to measure the effect of automatic kneeling on boarding and alighting times for passengers with reduced mobility. Sixty-two volunteers participated across four sessions: 31 ambulant passengers with walking aids and 31 wheelchair users. Kneeling reduced mean boarding time for wheelchair users from 28.4 seconds to 19.1 seconds (a 33% reduction) and reduced mean boarding time for ambulant passengers with walking aids from 9.8 seconds to 7.2 seconds (26% reduction). Alighting times showed similar reductions. A Monte Carlo simulation incorporating these distributions into a peak-hour stop model shows that mandatory kneeling at all stops would increase mean dwell time by 2.1 seconds per stop cycle on average, because the time savings for mobility-impaired users are offset by the kneeling and rising cycle of the vehicle. The trade-off has direct implications for accessibility policy and BRT scheduling.

title: Sensitivity of BRT Level-of-Service Metrics to Stop Spacing Under Varying Mixed-Traffic Intensities
abstract: Stop spacing is a primary design variable in BRT planning, yet its interaction with mixed-traffic interference on level-of-service outcomes is poorly understood at the corridor scale. This study uses a PTV Vissim model of a 7.4 km hypothetical BRT corridor calibrated to conditions typical of mid-size Serbian cities, systematically varying stop spacing from 250 m to 700 m in 50 m increments and mixed-traffic volume from 300 to 900 pcu/h. Twelve performance indicators are computed for each combination, including average commercial speed, on-time performance, and passenger wait time. Results show that commercial speed is most sensitive to stop spacing at low traffic volumes (elasticity 0.61) but becomes relatively insensitive at high volumes (elasticity 0.22), where mixed-traffic delay dominates. On-time performance degrades non-linearly once mixed-traffic volume exceeds 600 pcu/h regardless of spacing. A response surface methodology is applied to summarise results in a form usable in early-stage corridor planning.

title: Estimating Residual Queue Lengths at BRT Stops Caused by Downstream Signal Cycles
abstract: When a downstream traffic signal turns red, buses queued at a BRT stop cannot depart, effectively extending dwell time beyond the passenger exchange period. This paper quantifies residual queue effects at four signalised intersections immediately downstream of BRT stops on two corridors in Novi Sad and Subotica. A residual queue model based on Webster's delay formula is adapted to account for bus length and reaction time. Field validation using time-stamped GNSS records from 1,840 trips shows that the model predicts departure delays within ±6 seconds for 81% of observations. Residual queue events account for 11–19% of total stop-level delay during peak hours. The paper discusses how signal offset adjustments of 8–14 seconds could eliminate residual queue delay at three of the four study sites without adverse effects on general traffic progression, based on TRANSYT-style optimisation runs.

title: Comparison of Dwell Time Prediction Models for BRT Stops: Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting
abstract: Three classes of dwell time prediction model—multivariate linear regression, random forest, and gradient boosting—are trained and tested on a dataset of 9,170 stop events collected from four BRT-like stops in Novi Sad between 2019 and 2022. Input features include boarding count, alighting count, passenger load ratio, time of day, day of week, weather category, and door opening duration. The gradient boosting model achieves the lowest root mean square error (8.2 seconds) compared to random forest (9.7 s) and linear regression (12.4 s) on a held-out test set of 1,834 events. Feature importance analysis consistently identifies boarding count and passenger load ratio as the two most influential predictors across all models. A partial dependence analysis reveals a non-linear increase in dwell time when load ratio exceeds 0.85, consistent with congestion at the door. The models are intended for integration into real-time dispatching support tools.

title: Field Measurement Protocol for BRT Stop Capacity Assessment in Mixed-Traffic Corridors: A Practitioner's Guide
abstract: This book chapter presents a standardised measurement protocol developed over several years of fieldwork on BRT corridors in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. The protocol covers equipment selection (video cameras, GNSS loggers, pneumatic axle counters), sampling duration requirements based on bus frequency and desired precision, data cleaning procedures for GNSS trajectory gaps, and conversion of raw observations into stop capacity estimates compatible with HCM 6th edition and the TCQSM 3rd edition frameworks. Minimum sample sizes are derived analytically for three levels of estimation precision (±5%, ±10%, ±20%) under typical BRT demand conditions. The chapter also addresses common sources of measurement error, including camera occlusion at multi-berth stops and GNSS multipath in narrow urban canyons. Worked examples from sites in Novi Sad and Timișoara are included. The protocol has been reviewed and adopted as a reference document by the Serbian Chamber of Engineers for public transport studies.

title: Seasonal variability of aerosol optical depth over the Vojvodina agricultural plain derived from MODIS Terra retrievals, 2003–2010
abstract: This study analysed eight years of MODIS Terra Collection 6 Dark Target and Deep Blue aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrievals at 550 nm over Vojvodina province, northern Serbia, a region dominated by intensive cereal and sunflower cultivation. Monthly composites were constructed from MOD04_L2 granules filtered by quality assurance flags 2 and 3, yielding approximately 1,100 cloud-free observations per year. A clear spring maximum in AOD (mean 0.28 ± 0.09) was attributed to wind-blown soil dust from tilled fields, confirmed by backward trajectory analysis using HYSPLIT with ERA-Interim meteorological fields. Summer AOD values were lower (mean 0.17 ± 0.06), coinciding with established crop canopy. Comparison with AERONET data from the Belgrade site showed a root-mean-square deviation of 0.06 AOD units, consistent with published Collection 6 validation results for continental Europe. The findings suggest that agricultural management calendars leave a detectable and reproducible seasonal imprint on the regional aerosol loading over flat terrain with minimal topographic complexity.

title: Comparison of MODIS Dark Target and Deep Blue AOD retrievals over heterogeneous agricultural land in the central Balkans
abstract: Dark Target (DT) and Deep Blue (DB) AOD retrievals from MODIS Aqua Collection 6 were evaluated over a 300 × 200 km domain covering Vojvodina and adjacent areas of Hungary and Croatia for the period 2007–2013. The two algorithms differ in their surface reflectance assumptions, and the agricultural mosaic of the study area—a mixture of bare soil, winter wheat, maize, and fallow—presented a challenging intermediate case. DT retrievals were excluded for approximately 30 % of granules due to bright-surface masking, whereas DB provided continuous coverage. Agreement between the two products was highest in summer (R² = 0.87, slope = 0.96) and weakest in March–April (R² = 0.71, slope = 1.15), when freshly tilled soils elevated surface reflectance. Validation against AERONET Subotica station data showed that DB had a lower mean bias (−0.03) compared with DT (+0.07) during the spring tillage window. Results indicate that DB should be preferred for air quality applications during the planting season over this landscape type.
venue: Remote Sensing of the Lower Atmosphere

title: Estimating near-surface PM10 concentrations from MODIS AOD using a mixed land-use regression model over the Pannonian lowland
abstract: The relationship between MODIS-derived AOD at 550 nm and measured PM10 mass concentrations from 14 monitoring stations across Vojvodina and the northern Balkans was examined for 2011–2016. A land-use regression model was constructed incorporating AOD, planetary boundary layer height from ERA5 reanalysis, surface wind speed, relative humidity, and fractional land cover variables within a 3 km radius of each station. The model was calibrated on 70 % of station-days (n = 8,420) and validated on the remaining 30 %. Cross-validated R² reached 0.61 and RMSE was 11.4 µg m⁻³ for daily PM10, improving on a simple AOD-to-PM10 linear regression (R² = 0.38). Spatial prediction maps showed elevated PM10 along major road corridors and near the Novi Sad urban fringe, as well as diffuse agricultural dust episodes in April and October. Uncertainty was highest at stations with complex industrial point-source influences, suggesting the model is more appropriate for rural and peri-urban applications in flat agricultural regions.

title: Radiative transfer modelling of aerosol direct effects on downwelling shortwave radiation during a dust episode over the Pannonian Plain, May 2012
abstract: A multi-day dust transport event in May 2012, originating from agricultural fields in northern Vojvodina during a prolonged dry and windy period, was analysed using the 6SV radiative transfer code. Aerosol input parameters—single scattering albedo (ω₀ = 0.89–0.93), asymmetry factor (g = 0.69–0.73), and size distribution—were derived from AERONET Belgrade Level 2.0 inversion products. AOD peaked at 0.71 on 14 May 2012. Modelled surface downwelling shortwave irradiance was compared with measurements from three pyranometer stations in Vojvodina, yielding mean absolute differences of 18–31 W m⁻². Aerosol direct radiative effect at the surface was estimated at −22 to −38 W m⁻², representing a 7–12 % reduction relative to the aerosol-free baseline. The study demonstrates that even moderate agricultural dust loadings cause non-negligible reductions in photosynthetically active radiation, with potential consequences for crop energy balance models used in regional yield forecasting.

title: Combining Sentinel-3 SLSTR fire radiative power with MODIS aerosol retrievals to characterise smoke plumes from agricultural burning in the Balkans
abstract: Post-harvest burning of wheat and maize stubble produces substantial aerosol emissions each summer and autumn across the Pannonian region. This study combined Sentinel-3A/B SLSTR active fire detections and fire radiative power (FRP) estimates with MODIS Aqua Dark Blue AOD at 550 nm to characterise smoke plume aerosol loading for the summers of 2018 and 2019. A total of 214 burning episodes affecting areas larger than 200 ha were identified in Vojvodina and adjacent Slavonia, Croatia. Using HYSPLIT forward trajectories, smoke-affected MODIS pixels were identified within 48 hours of detected fires. AOD in smoke-affected pixels averaged 0.41 compared with a background of 0.18 for the same period in the same region. Angström Exponent values (1.3–1.6) confirmed fine-mode dominance consistent with biomass burning aerosol. FRP correlated moderately with same-day AOD anomaly (R = 0.52), with scatter attributable to variations in combustion efficiency and meteorological dilution. The dataset and methodology are made available to support national air quality reporting under the EU Air Quality Directive framework.

title: Sensitivity of SBDART-simulated TOA reflectance to aerosol single scattering albedo over bright agricultural soils: implications for satellite AOD retrieval
abstract: Satellite AOD retrieval algorithms over bright surfaces require accurate knowledge of aerosol single scattering albedo (ω₀) to separate aerosol and surface contributions to top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance. This study used the SBDART radiative transfer code to conduct a sensitivity analysis over a synthetic bright agricultural soil surface (broadband albedo 0.18–0.27) typical of spring conditions in Vojvodina. Simulations were run at 550 nm for AOD values of 0.1–0.8, ω₀ values of 0.80–0.98, and solar zenith angles of 25°–65°. TOA reflectance sensitivity to a ω₀ perturbation of 0.05 was equivalent to an AOD error of 0.04–0.09, depending on geometry and surface brightness. Errors were largest at low solar elevation (SZA > 55°) and high surface albedo. The results suggest that using a fixed ω₀ value of 0.95 (the MODIS Deep Blue operational assumption for coarse continental dust) will underestimate AOD by 0.03–0.08 during events dominated by freshly disturbed soil with lower ω₀. Recommendations are made for region-specific ω₀ constraints in next-generation retrieval schemes targeting agricultural zones.

title: Multi-year PM2.5 estimation over northern Serbia using Sentinel-3 OLCI aerosol products and machine learning with ground-truth from low-cost sensor networks
abstract: This study developed a random forest regression model to estimate daily PM2.5 concentrations at 300 m spatial resolution over Vojvodina province for 2020–2024, combining Sentinel-3 OLCI-derived AOD, meteorological reanalysis variables from ERA5 (boundary layer height, wind speed, temperature, specific humidity), and land cover fractions from the Copernicus Global Land Service. Ground-truth PM2.5 data were obtained from a network of 22 calibrated low-cost sensors (Plantower PMS5003-based, laboratory-corrected against reference-grade beta-attenuation monitors) deployed by the provincial environmental authority. The model was trained on station-days from 2020–2022 (n = 14,310) and validated on 2023–2024 data (n = 5,870), achieving R² = 0.72, RMSE = 6.1 µg m⁻³, and mean absolute error of 4.4 µg m⁻³. Gradient partial dependence plots showed boundary layer height and AOD as the two most important predictors. Predicted annual mean PM2.5 exceeded the WHO 2021 guideline of 5 µg m⁻³ across 94 % of the study area. Spatial maps revealed concentration hotspots near industrial facilities and along main arterial roads, but also diffuse agricultural contributions during spring and autumn.

title: Evaluation of PERSIANN-CDR Satellite Precipitation Estimates Against Ground Observations Over the Middle Danube Basin, 2003–2013
abstract: Satellite-derived precipitation products are increasingly used in data-sparse regions, but their accuracy must be assessed against independent ground observations before application in agronomic or hydrological models. This study evaluated PERSIANN-CDR daily and monthly precipitation estimates over the Middle Danube Basin covering Serbia, northern Croatia, and southwestern Hungary, comparing them with records from 47 synoptic stations for the period 2003–2013. Statistical metrics including bias ratio, correlation coefficient, probability of detection, and false alarm ratio were computed at both temporal aggregations. At the monthly scale, PERSIANN-CDR showed a mean wet bias of 8.4% over the study area, with overestimation concentrated in the Fruška Gora foothill zone and underestimation over the flat Vojvodina plain. Daily performance was markedly lower, with a probability of detection of 0.61 and a false alarm ratio of 0.34 for events exceeding 10 mm. Systematic biases identified here were used as inputs for a multiplicative bias correction scheme applied in follow-up downscaling work.

title: Constructing a 25-Year Field-Scale Rainfall Archive for Vojvodina and Its Application to Historical Burn Analysis of Parametric Crop Insurance
abstract: Actuarially sound index insurance products require long historical records at the spatial resolution at which policies will be written. This paper describes the construction of a daily, 1 km resolution rainfall archive for Vojvodina spanning 1999–2023, produced by applying the KED downscaling framework to a blended ERA5–IMERG covariate and using all available station records (29–48 stations per year depending on network completeness). Archive consistency across the pre-IMERG era was maintained by substituting TMPA 3B42 for years before 2014 after demonstrating statistically equivalent covariate performance. A burn analysis was performed for three parametric products—sowing-period deficit, flowering-period excess, and grain-filling deficit—for maize and sunflower across 1,214 cadastral municipalities. Mean annual payout frequencies under tested trigger calibrations ranged from 14% to 27% depending on product and crop. The archive and analysis scripts are made publicly available. These outputs are intended to support insurers and reinsurers operating in the Pannonian agricultural zone in setting actuarially fair premiums.

title: Voxel resolution effects on canopy gap fraction and leaf area index retrieval from terrestrial LiDAR in a mixed oak–hornbeam stand
abstract: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) data were collected at nine plots within a mixed oak–hornbeam forest in the Fruška Gora mountain range, Serbia, using a Riegl VZ-400i scanner. Point clouds were voxelised at five resolutions ranging from 0.02 m to 0.20 m, and canopy gap fraction was estimated along 57 zenith angle classes per plot using a ray-tracing approach. Leaf area index (LAI) was derived via the Miller formula and compared against destructive litter-trap measurements at the same plots. Results showed that voxel edge lengths between 0.04 m and 0.08 m minimised commission errors from occlusion while retaining sufficient angular resolution, yielding LAI estimates within 9.3% of litter-trap values on average. Coarser resolutions (≥0.15 m) overestimated LAI by up to 31% due to artificial gap closure. These findings provide practical guidance for TLS-based LAI retrieval in structurally complex broadleaf canopies and inform optimal voxel size selection for subsequent biomass modelling workflows in temperate European forests.

title: Cluster-Based Size System for Serbian Adult Women: A Statistical Approach Using Multivariate Body Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a data-driven construction of a size system for adult women in Serbia, derived from a cross-sectional anthropometric survey of 1,247 participants aged 18–65 conducted in Vojvodina. Thirty-two primary and secondary body measurements were recorded using standard anthropometric instruments and a Vitus Smart XXL 3D body scanner. Principal component analysis reduced dimensionality to six composite shape descriptors, followed by k-means clustering to identify eight distinct size categories. Resulting size intervals were compared against the EN 13402 standard and the existing JUS F.G2.001 Yugoslav-era norm, revealing systematic underrepresentation of larger bust-to-hip ratios and shorter stature groups in the historical standard. The proposed system covers 91.4% of the sampled population within one half-size step for chest girth, compared to 76.8% coverage by the legacy standard. Grading increments were derived analytically and validated against a subset of 80 participants through prototype garment fitting trials. Implications for domestic apparel manufacturers are discussed.

title: Postural Variation and Its Effect on Pattern Construction: A Pilot Study Using 3D Scan Data
abstract: Conventional flat-pattern methods assume standardised posture archetypes that frequently diverge from measured body postures in real populations. This pilot study extracted posture parameters—spinal curvature index, shoulder slope angle, and forward neck tilt—from 3D scan data of 210 women aged 20–40 using landmark-based surface analysis in a custom Python pipeline. Five posture clusters were identified, and their deviation from the neutral posture assumption embedded in standard bodice blocks was quantified. For the most common non-neutral cluster (anterior pelvic tilt with increased lumbar lordosis, n=67), front waist length exceeded block values by a mean of 1.8 cm while back waist length was shorter by 1.4 cm. Pattern modifications addressing each cluster were proposed and visualised in CLO3D. Fit quality was assessed by three experienced technologists using a standardised 24-point evaluation protocol. The study highlights measurable consequences of ignoring postural diversity in mass-market pattern templates.

title: Ease Allowance Values for Close-Fitting Knitwear: Deriving Empirical Guidelines from Pressure Comfort Thresholds
abstract: Standard ease allowance tables for knitwear are largely inherited from woven-fabric practice with limited empirical grounding in fabric stretch behaviour or wearer comfort. This study combined pressure sensor measurements and subjective comfort ratings to establish ease allowance guidelines for close-fitting knitwear across six body circumference positions. Forty female participants (bust 80–104 cm) wore eight prototype garments manufactured from single jersey with three different stretch recovery characteristics. A TekScan FlexiForce array recorded interface pressure at bust, underbust, waist, upper hip, and thigh positions during static stance and five standardised motions. Subjective comfort was rated on a ten-point scale. Mixed-effects regression linked pressure values and self-reported comfort, yielding pressure threshold boundaries for each circumference position. Recommended negative ease ranges of 4–12% were derived and tabulated by fabric class. Results challenge the uniform 0 cm ease convention common in current industry specifications.

title: Grading Rules for Maternity Wear Derived from Longitudinal Anthropometric Measurements
abstract: The abdominal and breast volume changes during pregnancy are rapid and asymmetric compared with overall weight gain, yet commercial maternity garment grading typically applies isometric scaling borrowed from standard womenswear. This study followed 62 primiparous women across five measurement sessions (pre-pregnancy, 12, 20, 28, and 36 weeks gestation) recording 24 body measurements at each session. Regression models were fitted to describe the trajectory of key measurements as functions of gestational week and pre-pregnancy body type (classified by bust–waist–hip ratio). Abdominal depth showed the largest relative change, increasing by a mean of 14.4 cm between pre-pregnancy and 36 weeks. Derived trimester-differentiated grading increments were compared with those published by two major European maternity clothing brands obtained through reverse engineering of purchased garments. Significant differences were found at the abdomen, side seam length, and sleeve underarm curve. Proposed grading tables are provided as supplementary data.
