title: Automatic Landmarking of 3D Female Body Scans: Comparison of a Geometric Heuristic Method with Manual Expert Annotation
abstract: Reliable extraction of anthropometric landmarks from 3D body scans remains a bottleneck for large-scale measurement surveys. This paper evaluates a geometric heuristic landmarking algorithm implemented in Python against expert manual annotation on a dataset of 320 female scans obtained from a Vitus Smart XXL scanner. The algorithm locates 18 landmarks using surface curvature extrema and slice-based contour analysis. Agreement was assessed using Euclidean distance between algorithmically placed and manually placed landmark coordinates for each scan. Mean error across all 18 landmarks was 6.3 mm (SD 4.1 mm), with highest errors at the cervicale (12.1 mm) and lowest at the bustpoint (3.8 mm). Seven circumference measurements derived from algorithmic landmarks differed from manually derived values by less than 5 mm on average. Processing time per scan averaged 4.2 seconds compared to approximately 18 minutes for manual annotation. The algorithm performs adequately for population-level statistical analysis but requires refinement for individual fit applications.

title: Virtual Try-On Accuracy for Woven Trousers: Validating CLO3D Simulation Against Physical Fit Trials
abstract: Virtual fit simulation is increasingly used in product development to reduce physical sampling costs, but its accuracy for specific garment categories is unevenly documented. This study assessed the agreement between CLO3D simulated fit and physical fit trial outcomes for woven trousers across three size-shape combinations. Twelve test garments (four size variants × three fabric types) were physically fitted on eight female participants and assessed on 20 fit criteria by two garment technologists. The same garments and fabrics, with measured mechanical properties inputted, were simulated on matched digital avatars and evaluated on equivalent criteria. Criterion-level agreement was quantified using weighted kappa. Mean weighted kappa was 0.62, indicating moderate-to-substantial agreement. Agreement was highest for circumference-related criteria (κ = 0.74) and lowest for crotch seam placement (κ = 0.41). Fabric bending rigidity, inputted as KES-F measured values, was the most influential simulation parameter. Results suggest CLO3D can replace first physical samples for circumferential fit decisions but not for detailed seam positioning.

title: Body Shape Descriptors for Plus-Size Women: Defining Proportional Categories Beyond Girth Measurements
abstract: Standard sizing systems for plus-size apparel are typically constructed as linear extensions of straight-size systems, ignoring differences in the proportional distribution of body volume. This study analysed 3D scan data from 418 women with bust circumference above 100 cm, recruited from Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Fourteen shape indices combining girth measurements, body segment lengths, and volume-based descriptors were computed per participant. Hierarchical cluster analysis on the shape index matrix yielded five proportional body categories, labelled by the position of maximum body depth and the waist-to-hip ratio profile. The five categories differed significantly in abdomen protrusion index (F = 89.3, p < 0.001) and in the front-to-back length asymmetry ratio. Existing plus-size patterns from two regional manufacturers were overlaid on the category centroids in 3D, revealing systematic fit deficits at the abdomen and upper arm for three of the five categories. A block pattern modification strategy for each category is outlined.

title: Parametric Grading Model for Menswear Trousers Based on Regression Analysis of Hip-to-Waist Ratio Variability
abstract: Traditional grading for menswear trousers applies fixed increments across size steps that implicitly assume a constant hip-to-waist ratio. This study tests that assumption against an anthropometric dataset of 784 adult men aged 20–55 from northern Serbia. Waist and hip circumferences, crotch depth, inside leg length, and thigh circumference were regressed against pant size (defined by waist girth) using ordinary least squares and piecewise linear models. Hip-to-waist ratio decreased significantly across size steps in the 88–104 cm waist range (slope −0.008 per 2 cm step, p = 0.003) but stabilised above 104 cm. A parametric grading model in which hip increment is a function of size step rather than a fixed value was constructed. Comparison of patterns graded by the traditional and parametric methods across nine sizes showed divergence at the seat seam exceeding 1.5 cm by size 108, with the parametric method producing better alignment with measured seat circumferences. The model is implemented in a spreadsheet tool available as supplementary material.

title: Integrating Consumer Body Scan Data into a Make-to-Order Workflow: A Case Study with a Regional Sportswear Producer
abstract: This chapter describes the implementation of a scan-based made-to-measure workflow at a medium-sized sportswear producer in Vojvodina over a twelve-month pilot period. The company collected full-body scans of 143 customers using a mobile scanning cabin placed at two retail outlets. Scans were processed with an automated landmarking script, extracting 16 measurements per customer. A parametric pattern adjustment algorithm, developed in collaboration with the company's pattern room, mapped individual measurements to pattern modifications within tolerances agreed with the production team. Orders were fulfilled and returned for customer evaluation. Eighty-one percent of customers rated fit as better than their previous off-the-shelf purchase from the same brand. Main operational challenges included scan data privacy consent, scanner calibration drift between locations, and communication of size uncertainty to customers. Lessons learned and a proposed data flow diagram are presented for practitioners considering similar implementations.

title: Comparative Analysis of Three Size Labelling Systems for Women's Dresses Sold in the Western Balkans Market
abstract: Garment size labels in the Western Balkans retail market are applied inconsistently, mixing numeric systems inherited from Yugoslav standards, European alphabetic labels, and retailer-specific proprietary codes. This study purchased 96 women's dresses (size 38 or equivalent) from 12 retailers across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia and measured each garment at nine locations following EN 13402-4. Label-to-measurement correspondence was evaluated against each retailer's own size chart where available and against the EN 13402 reference intervals. Mean bust measurement across garments labelled size 38 ranged from 84.0 cm to 93.5 cm. Waist measurement variance was even larger. Only four of twelve retailers' labelling practices were internally consistent across garment styles. Consumer confusion implications are discussed, and a simplified cross-reference table aligning three common labelling conventions with EN 13402 intervals is proposed for use in retail settings.

title: Mesh-Based Avatar Personalisation from Sparse Measurement Input: Accuracy Limits for Fit Simulation Applications
abstract: Digital avatars for virtual fit simulation are typically generated from a predefined mesh model deformed to match user-provided measurements. This preprint evaluates the accuracy of three mesh deformation pipelines—linear blend skinning, radial basis function interpolation, and a learned statistical shape model—when personalised from six commonly collected measurements (height, bust, waist, hip, inside leg, shoulder width) and validated against full-body scans of 50 women not included in training data. Accuracy was measured as mean per-vertex surface distance between the deformed avatar and the actual scan. The statistical shape model achieved the lowest mean error (8.4 mm), followed by RBF interpolation (11.2 mm) and LBS (15.9 mm). Errors concentrated at the upper arm and neck regions across all methods. Implications for fit prediction reliability at specific garment zones are discussed. A supplementary dataset of measurement-scan pairs is made available for benchmarking.

title: Variability in spectrophotometric measurement of metallic ink patches: instrument geometry and angle dependence
abstract: Metallic inks printed by offset and screen processes exhibit strong goniochromatic behaviour that standard 45°/0° and integrating-sphere geometries cannot fully capture. This study measured a set of 36 metallic ink patches — gold, silver, and bronze formulations printed at three ink-film thicknesses on coated and uncoated board — using a 45°/0° spectrophotometer, an integrating-sphere instrument in both specular-included and specular-excluded modes, and a multi-angle spectrophotometer at 15°, 45°, and 110° illumination. Measurement repeatability within each instrument was assessed across 20 repeat measurements per patch; inter-instrument agreement was evaluated using mean ΔE2000. Standard 45°/0° readings showed the highest inter-patch discrimination for relative colour comparison but the lowest absolute agreement with multi-angle readings (mean ΔE2000 8.4). Integrating-sphere specular-included measurements yielded the best instrument-to-instrument repeatability (ΔE2000 0.6). Recommendations are given for selecting measurement geometry depending on whether the goal is process control or cross-site colour communication.
venue: Journal of Coatings and Surface Measurement

title: Braille Label Legibility After Repeated Thermal Cycling in Cold-Chain Pharmaceutical Logistics
abstract: Braille labels embossed onto 350 µm SBS cartonboard were subjected to 0, 10, 25, and 50 thermal cycles between −20 °C and +25 °C, simulating cold-chain distribution conditions for temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals. Dot height and base diameter were measured by profilometry after each cycle interval; 360 individual dots across four label types (two embossing depths, two board moisture contents) were tracked. Dot height loss after 50 cycles ranged from 6 % to 19 %; boards conditioned at 10 % moisture before embossing showed greater resilience than those conditioned at 6 %. None of the 50-cycle specimens fell below the EN ISO 17351 minimum height threshold. However, boards with shallower embossing depth (0.45 mm target) approached the threshold at 50 cycles, leaving a conformity margin of only 0.03 mm. Results suggest that cold-chain products should be embossed to a height at least 15 % above the standard minimum.

title: Discrete-Ordinates Modelling of Radiative Transfer in a Pilot-Scale Tunnel Kiln for Ceramic Tile Production
abstract: This study presents a three-dimensional computational model of radiative heat transfer inside a pilot-scale tunnel kiln used for ceramic tile firing. The discrete-ordinates method (DOM) with an S8 angular quadrature was implemented within an OpenFOAM framework, coupled to a steady-state energy equation solver. The kiln geometry was discretised into approximately 1.2 million hexahedral cells. Spectral gas absorption was handled using a weighted-sum-of-grey-gases (WSGG) model fitted to CO2–H2O mixtures at temperatures between 900 °C and 1250 °C. Validation was performed against thermocouple measurements taken at twelve axial positions along a 24-metre kiln operating at a production facility in Subotica. Simulated temperature profiles agreed with measurements to within 4.1% root-mean-square error across all monitored cross-sections. The results identify a recirculation-driven cold zone between 8 m and 11 m from the kiln entrance that correlates with documented underfiring defects. Recommendations for modified setting arrangements are discussed based on the computed heat flux distributions.

title: Effect of Burner Arrangement on Temperature Uniformity in a Roller-Hearth Glass Annealing Furnace: A Parametric CFD Study
abstract: Temperature uniformity across glass ribbon width is critical in roller-hearth annealing furnaces to prevent residual stress and optical distortion. This paper investigates five burner placement configurations in a 15-metre annealing furnace operating at a peak temperature of 620 °C using a coupled convection–radiation CFD model. Radiation was modelled with the discrete-ordinates method at S4 order, and combustion products were treated as grey participating media with spatially averaged absorption coefficients derived from HITRAN database entries for the operating temperature range. Simulations were run in steady state with inlet boundary conditions derived from manufacturer burner data sheets. A uniformity index based on the standard deviation of surface heat flux over the glass ribbon was used as the primary performance metric. The staggered offset configuration reduced the peak-to-mean heat flux deviation from 18.3% to 7.6% compared to the baseline symmetric arrangement. Pressure drop penalties across the configurations were within 3% of each other, indicating that the preferred layout carries no meaningful aerodynamic disadvantage.

title: Influence of Refractory Lining Emissivity on Firing Energy Consumption in Intermittent Ceramic Kilns
abstract: Refractory materials in ceramic kilns act as both thermal insulators and radiative surfaces, yet their spectral emissivity at elevated temperatures is rarely incorporated into furnace simulation studies. This work uses a DOM-based radiation model to quantify the sensitivity of energy consumption and product temperature history to refractory emissivity values ranging from 0.55 to 0.92, covering the range reported for commercially available high-alumina and mullite-based linings. An intermittent box kiln geometry of 2.4 m³ chamber volume, representative of small-batch sanitaryware production, was modelled. Firing cycles of 18 hours with a peak hold at 1220 °C were simulated. Results show that increasing refractory emissivity from 0.60 to 0.85 reduces the total thermal energy input by 6.8% while maintaining comparable product temperature uniformity, primarily due to enhanced radiative redistribution during the soaking phase. The sensitivity is more pronounced in the 900–1100 °C range where convective contributions are relatively smaller. These findings provide a quantitative basis for refractory material selection criteria beyond purely insulating performance.
venue: Thermal Science and Engineering Practice

title: Benchmarking S4, S6, and S8 Discrete-Ordinates Quadratures for Radiative Heat Transfer in Elongated Industrial Furnace Geometries
abstract: The discrete-ordinates method requires selection of an angular quadrature set, and the computational cost scales substantially with quadrature order. This study compares S4, S6, and S8 quadratures applied to three standardised elongated furnace geometries representing length-to-width ratios of 5:1, 10:1, and 20:1, with optically thin and optically thick participating media. Reference solutions were generated using a Monte Carlo method with 10⁷ photon bundles. Metrics include maximum local irradiation error, overall energy balance residual, and wall-clock time on a 16-core workstation. For the 10:1 geometry with a medium optical thickness of τ = 0.8, S6 achieved an irradiation error below 3.2% at 61% of the computational cost of S8. At τ = 0.2 (optically thin), S4 produced unacceptable ray-effect artefacts exceeding 12% local error in all geometries studied. Practical guidance for selecting quadrature order as a function of geometry aspect ratio and optical thickness is summarised in a decision chart intended for practitioners setting up industrial furnace simulations.
venue: Journal of Computational Heat Transfer

title: Projection-Based Reduced-Order Models for Euler–Bernoulli Beams Under Parametric Stiffness Variation
abstract: This paper investigates the construction of projection-based reduced-order models (ROMs) for slender beam structures whose cross-sectional stiffness varies as a continuous parameter. Starting from a full finite element discretisation with 1 200 degrees of freedom, a Petrov–Galerkin projection onto a 12-dimensional subspace is constructed using a greedy basis-enrichment strategy. The parameter space covers Young's modulus variations of ±30 % around a nominal steel value. Reduction errors measured by the H2 norm remain below 0.4 % across the sampled parameter range. Frequency response functions computed from the ROM and from the full model agree to within 1.2 % at the first five natural frequencies. The approach is tested on a simply supported laboratory beam instrumented with eight piezoelectric accelerometers and excited by a calibrated impulse hammer. Measured frequency response functions match ROM predictions with a relative error below 3.1 %, confirming that the subspace captures the dominant dynamics even under moderate boundary-condition uncertainty.

title: Optimal Sensor Placement for Modal Identification of a Pre-stressed Concrete Footbridge Using the Effective Independence Method
abstract: Effective placement of a limited number of accelerometers is critical for reliable operational modal analysis of civil structures. This study applies the Effective Independence (EfI) method, augmented with a kinetic energy constraint, to determine the placement of 12 sensors on a 47-metre pre-stressed concrete footbridge located in the Vojvodina region. The candidate set comprised 96 candidate nodal positions derived from a calibrated shell finite element model. Sensor configurations selected by EfI are compared against configurations produced by a genetic algorithm and a random baseline using the Fisher information matrix determinant as the performance criterion. The EfI configuration achieves a determinant 2.3 times larger than the random baseline and 8 % larger than the genetic algorithm result at equal computational cost. Ambient vibration data recorded over 48 hours are processed with stochastic subspace identification, yielding the first six mode shapes with a Modal Assurance Criterion cross-matrix diagonal above 0.98 for all six modes.

title: A Comparison of Krylov and POD Subspace Methods for Parametric Model Order Reduction in Structural Acoustics
abstract: Parametric model order reduction (pMOR) methods based on Krylov subspaces and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) are compared on a benchmark plate-cavity structural-acoustic problem. The full model has 8 400 structural and 3 100 acoustic degrees of freedom. The parameter of interest is the plate thickness, ranging from 3 mm to 8 mm in steps of 0.5 mm. Krylov-based reduction at a single expansion frequency preserves acoustic transfer functions to within 1.8 % across the 20–400 Hz band, but deteriorates above 600 Hz. POD bases constructed from 22 snapshot solutions at parameter samples achieve 0.9 % relative error across the full 20–800 Hz range with a basis of dimension 18. Computational speed-up relative to the full-order solve is 47× for POD and 31× for Krylov. Both methods are implemented in MATLAB and benchmarked on a shared server. Recommendations for selection between the two approaches based on available snapshots and frequency range requirements are given.

title: Finite Element Model Updating for an Aging Reinforced Concrete Bridge Using Measured Ambient Frequencies
abstract: This paper presents a model-updating procedure applied to a 62-year-old reinforced concrete arch bridge crossing the Danube tributary in northern Serbia. Ambient vibration measurements were collected with 16 MEMS accelerometers over three separate 24-hour campaigns conducted in summer and autumn to account for temperature-dependent stiffness variation. The finite element model contains 4 780 shell elements and parameterises material stiffness, bearing stiffness, and abutment boundary conditions through seven updating parameters. Bayesian model updating is performed using a Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler with 50 000 accepted samples. Posterior means of Young's modulus for the deck concrete are 11.2 % lower than design values, consistent with observed surface carbonation. Temperature sensitivity of the first natural frequency is estimated at −0.07 Hz per degree Celsius. Modal frequencies from the updated model match measured values within 1.5 % across the first four modes. The study provides quantified uncertainty bounds on the updated parameters.

title: Damage Localisation in Steel Frame Structures via Changes in Transmissibility Functions
abstract: Transmissibility functions, defined as the ratio of output responses at two sensor locations, carry information about the location and magnitude of structural changes independently of the unmeasured input. This study investigates their utility for damage localisation in a three-storey steel laboratory frame (mass per floor: 48 kg; storey height: 0.35 m) under broadband random excitation. Damage is simulated by removing bolted connections at 11 predefined joint locations. Transmissibility-based damage indices are constructed from changes in the imaginary part of the transmissibility matrix at 45 frequency lines between 10 and 200 Hz. A principal component analysis compression retains 95 % of variance in four components. A nearest-neighbour classifier trained on undamaged and five damage scenarios correctly localises damage in 87 % of 220 test cases. False-positive rates remain below 6 %. The method requires no finite element model and operates on data from six accelerometers mounted on the frame.

title: Real-Time Digital Twin Calibration of an Industrial Floor Slab Using Recursive Least Squares Parameter Estimation
abstract: This contribution describes the continuous calibration of a digital twin for a 2 400 m² post-tensioned industrial floor slab in a warehouse facility. The digital twin is a reduced-order shell model with 320 degrees of freedom obtained by component mode synthesis from the full 47 000-degree-of-freedom model. Seven parameters—post-tensioning force level, slab-to-wall bearing stiffness at four edges, and elastic modulus of the concrete—are updated online as new accelerometer data arrive. Recursive least squares with exponential forgetting (forgetting factor 0.997) is implemented on an embedded microcontroller connected via CAN bus to 14 wireless MEMS sensors. In a 30-day in-situ trial, the tracked elastic modulus decreased monotonically by 3.4 %, consistent with a measured increase in surface crack density. Update latency per 10-minute data window is 0.8 seconds on the embedded hardware. The paper quantifies tracking speed against batch Bayesian updating and discusses implementation constraints.

title: Interpolatory Methods for Constructing Parametric Reduced-Order Models on Riemannian Matrix Manifolds
abstract: When the parameter space of a structural system is multidimensional, reduced-order model bases computed at isolated parameter points cannot be directly interpolated in Euclidean space because they lie on the Grassmann manifold. This paper implements and compares three interpolation strategies—geodesic interpolation, tangent-space interpolation, and barycentric interpolation on the manifold—for parametric ROMs of a truss bridge model with four independent parameters: two material moduli, cross-section area ratio, and temperature. The full model has 6 200 degrees of freedom; each ROM basis has dimension 15. A grid of 81 training points and 25 test points is used. Geodesic interpolation reduces frequency prediction error at test points to 0.6 % compared with 2.1 % for direct Euclidean interpolation. Computational overhead of the manifold operations is negligible (below 2 ms per query on a standard workstation). The implementation is made available as a documented MATLAB toolbox with five worked examples.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Digital Twin Predictions for a Masonry Viaduct: Comparison of Monte Carlo and Polynomial Chaos Expansion
abstract: Masonry viaducts present significant material heterogeneity that translates into wide uncertainty bands in digital twin predictions. This paper quantifies prediction uncertainty for a 19th-century nine-arch masonry viaduct in the Fruška Gora corridor using two propagation methods: Monte Carlo sampling with 10 000 runs and a sparse polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) of total degree 4. Six uncertain parameters describe joint cohesion, friction angle, arch fill density, and pier elastic modulus. The full finite element model runs in approximately 4 minutes on 8 cores; the PCE surrogate is trained on 148 model evaluations and evaluates in microseconds. For the first natural frequency, Monte Carlo gives a 95 % credible interval of [1.81, 2.34] Hz; PCE yields [1.83, 2.31] Hz, agreeing closely. Total-order Sobol indices identify joint cohesion and arch fill density as the two dominant uncertainty contributors, each accounting for over 28 % of frequency variance. Results are validated against 72-hour ambient vibration measurements.

title: Embedded Physics-Informed Constraints in Neural-Network Surrogate Models for Structural Frequency Prediction
abstract: Fully data-driven neural network surrogates for structural frequency prediction can extrapolate poorly when training data are scarce. This paper embeds two physics-informed constraints—non-negative mass–stiffness eigenvalue inequality and monotone frequency ordering—as penalty terms in the loss function of a feedforward network trained to predict the first five natural frequencies of parameterised frame structures. The training set contains 600 finite element evaluations; a test set of 150 independent samples is used for evaluation. Without constraints, the network violates frequency ordering in 9.4 % of test cases and produces negative predicted frequency shifts in 3.1 %. With the proposed penalties (weight 0.1), ordering violations drop to 0.3 % and non-physical predictions disappear. Mean absolute prediction error for the fifth mode decreases from 1.8 % to 1.2 %. The approach is demonstrated on a parameterised portal frame with five geometric and material parameters. Sensitivity to penalty weight and training set size is reported.

title: A Survey of Logic-Based Methods in Scene Understanding: 2015–2022
abstract: This survey covers 134 papers published between 2015 and 2022 that combine formal logic with neural components for scene understanding tasks, including object detection, scene graph generation, visual question answering, and embodied navigation. Papers are classified along four axes: the logic formalism used (Datalog, ASP, Markov logic networks, probabilistic soft logic, neural theorem proving), the interface between neural and symbolic components (fact injection, differentiable unification, teacher-forcing), the evaluation domain (indoor, outdoor, synthetic, medical), and the degree of interpretability support. Key findings: ASP usage peaks around 2019 and declines relative to differentiable approaches; interpretability evaluation is reported in only 29% of papers; the majority of datasets used are English-language or culturally Western. The survey identifies three underexplored areas: cross-lingual scene graph alignment, compositional generalisation benchmarks for logic-augmented systems, and formal verification of neuro-symbolic pipelines. An annotated bibliography is provided as supplementary material.

title: Seasonal variation in allelopathic compound profiles of Fallopia × bohemica along the Danube floodplain in Vojvodina
abstract: Leaf litter, rhizome, and root samples of Fallopia × bohemica were collected monthly from six stands along a 140 km stretch of the Danube floodplain between April and October 2011. GC-MS and HPLC-DAD were used to quantify stilbenes, anthraquinones, and phenolic acids in each tissue type. Rhizome trans-resveratrol content peaked in October (mean 3.2 mg g⁻¹ DW), while root emodin was highest in July (2.8 mg g⁻¹ DW). Leaf litter showed lowest concentrations in spring but accumulated ferulic and p-coumaric acids by September (combined 1.9 mg g⁻¹ DW). Principal component analysis separated samples by both season and tissue type, explaining 74% of total variance. Correlations with soil moisture and temperature were significant for resveratrol (r = −0.71 with temperature, p < 0.001). These patterns suggest that allelopathic pressure on co-occurring native species may peak at specific phenological windows, with implications for riparian restoration timing.

title: Алелопатски утицај коренских ексудата Ailanthus altissima на клијање аутохтоних врста рода Quercus у контролисаним условима
abstract: У огледу изведеном у контролисаним лабораторијским условима испитиван је утицај синтетских коренских ексудата Ailanthus altissima на клијавост и рани пораст жира Quercus robur и Quercus petraea. Симулирани ексудати справљени су на основу хемијских профила добијених GC-MS анализом природних коренских ексудата са три локалитета у рипаријалним стаништима Фрушке горе. Препознате су три доминантне компоненте: ailanthone, ацетивинол и хлорогенска киселина. Тест-биомаса сеjaнаца мерена је након 14 дана. Ailanthone у концентрацији 50 µM инхибирао је клијање Q. robur за 58%, а Q. petraea за 49%. Ацетивинол је показао знатно слабији ефекат (инхибиција испод 15% при истој концентрацији). Резултати потврђују да ailanthone представља примарни алелохемикалац ове врсте у испитиваним стаништима и да постоји значајан потенцијал за угрожавање природне обнове храстових шума у оквиру заштићених подручја.

title: Root exudate collection methods compared: hydroponics versus in situ rhizosphere wash for Fallopia japonica under field conditions
abstract: Four collection protocols — trap solution, centrifugation of rhizosphere soil, in situ root washing, and hydroponic cultivation — were compared for their yield and compound integrity when applied to mature Fallopia japonica plants in a riparian stand on the Tisa River, Serbia. Each method was replicated across eight individual plants. Compound profiles were assessed by HPLC-DAD and quantified for resveratrol, emodin, catechin, and p-coumaric acid. Hydroponic cultivation yielded the highest resveratrol concentrations (mean 1.8 µg mL⁻¹) but altered emodin:resveratrol ratios relative to in situ methods. Rhizosphere centrifugation gave the best correspondence to field conditions for all four target compounds but showed high variability (CV > 35%). In situ root washing offered a practical field compromise with lower compound degradation compared to transport-delayed centrifugation. Recommendations are provided for standardising future comparative allelopathy studies in riparian settings.

title: Ailanthus altissima invasion alters soil microbial community structure in riparian oak woodland fragments along the Sava River
abstract: Paired soil samples (invaded vs. uninvaded plots, n = 24 each) were collected from riparian oak woodland fragments along a 60 km stretch of the Sava River in Serbia. Bacterial and fungal community composition was assessed by 16S rRNA and ITS2 amplicon sequencing (Illumina MiSeq). Alpha diversity (Shannon index) was significantly lower in invaded plots for bacteria (6.1 vs. 7.4, p = 0.003) but not for fungi. Beta-diversity analysis (Bray–Curtis, PERMANOVA) explained 18% of variance by invasion status. Ailanthone concentration in soil (measured by HPLC-MS) was negatively correlated with relative abundance of Nitrobacter (r = −0.61, p < 0.01). Functional prediction using PICRUSt2 indicated reduced nitrification potential in invaded soils. These results suggest that A. altissima alters nitrogen cycling in part via allelopathic suppression of nitrifying bacteria, which may feedback to reduce competitive ability of native oak regeneration.

title: Comparing allelopathic suppression of Fallopia japonica and Fallopia sachalinensis under simulated nutrient gradient conditions
abstract: F. japonica and F. sachalinensis were grown in sand culture at three nitrogen levels (2, 10, and 40 mg N L⁻¹) for 12 weeks. Root exudates were collected by rhizosphere wash at weeks 4, 8, and 12 and analysed by HPLC-DAD for resveratrol, emodin, catechin, and two unidentified compounds tentatively identified as hydroxystilbene derivatives. Bioassays with Lolium perenne as a target species were conducted using exudate concentrations normalised to root biomass. F. sachalinensis exudates showed 15–22% higher inhibition of L. perenne radicle growth across all treatments compared to F. japonica. High nitrogen supply reduced emodin production in F. japonica by 38% but had no significant effect in F. sachalinensis. Results indicate that the allelopathic potential of these two closely related invaders responds differently to soil nutrient enrichment, with implications for management in eutrophic riparian margins.
venue: Journal of Plant Interactions

title: Exudate-mediated interference between Ailanthus altissima and Fraxinus angustifolia seedlings: a split-root experiment
abstract: A split-root design was used to distinguish between direct chemical interference and resource competition in interactions between A. altissima and F. angustifolia seedlings. Fraxinus angustifolia seedlings were divided into two compartments: one root half shared soil with A. altissima root material (exudate-exposure treatment) and the other half with sterile sand (control). Twenty replicates per treatment were grown for 10 weeks in a climate chamber. Shoot height increment, root dry mass, leaf chlorophyll content (SPAD), and nitrogen uptake were measured. Exudate-exposed root halves showed 31% lower root dry mass and 19% lower SPAD values compared to the sterile-sand halves. Ailanthone was detected in exudate-exposed compartment soil at 0.22 µg g⁻¹ DW. Resource competition was excluded by equalising nutrient supply. These results provide mechanistic evidence that A. altissima can inhibit F. angustifolia seedlings through root-exuded ailanthone independently of above-ground competition.

title: Temporal dynamics of phenolic acid accumulation in riparian soils beneath monospecific Fallopia japonica stands during a three-year monitoring period
abstract: Soil phenolic acid concentrations were monitored quarterly for three years (2022–2024) at four Fallopia japonica monoculture stands on the Tisa floodplain, with paired reference plots in adjacent native Salix–Populus woodland. Twelve phenolic acids were quantified by HPLC-DAD from 0–5 cm and 5–20 cm soil layers. Ferulic, p-coumaric, and vanillic acids were consistently elevated under F. japonica (mean 2- to 4-fold higher than reference plots, p < 0.005 for all). Concentrations peaked in autumn, coinciding with litter fall and rhizome senescence. Three-year trends showed no significant increase in baseline concentrations, suggesting a dynamic equilibrium between input and microbial degradation. Microbial phenol-oxidase activity (measured by colorimetric assay) was positively correlated with total phenolic concentration (r = 0.62, p < 0.001), indicating partial buffering by soil biota. The data provide a multi-year baseline for assessing long-term phytochemical footprint of established F. japonica stands.

title: Combining acoustic and photographic monitoring to survey nocturnal ground-active arthropods in Pannonian forest edges
abstract: A multimodal monitoring approach was tested at six forest-edge transects in Fruška Gora over two seasons. Passive acoustic recorders logged stridulation from orthopteran species from dusk to dawn, while time-lapse macro-photography traps recorded arthropod activity at pitfall openings. Manual review of 42,600 image frames and 1,140 hours of audio yielded occurrence data for 38 Carabidae and 12 Orthoptera species. Automated frame-filtering using a random forest classifier trained on edge-detected foreground objects reduced manual review time by 73% while retaining 96% of true-positive arthropod frames. Acoustic detections added four Orthoptera species not captured in pitfall samples. Temporal activity curves derived from image sequences differed between forest interior and edge microsites, with carabid peak activity two hours later at interior sites. The combined protocol provides richer community data than either sensor alone at comparable field labour cost.

title: Soil nematode assemblages along an urban-to-agricultural gradient around the city of Novi Sad
abstract: An urban-to-agricultural gradient was delineated along four transects radiating from the Novi Sad city centre to surrounding agricultural land. Seventeen sites were sampled in spring and autumn of 2013. Nematode diversity measured by genus richness was lowest at heavily disturbed peri-urban sites (mean 9 genera) and highest at reference arable fields with low-input management (mean 22 genera). Omnivore and predator proportions decreased sharply within 3 km of the city centre, correlating with elevated concentrations of Cu (r = −0.71) and Pb (r = −0.65) in soil. Bacterivore opportunists (cp-1 and cp-2 colonisers) dominated inner-urban soils. Canonical correspondence analysis identified soil pH, heavy-metal content, and organic carbon as the strongest explanatory variables. Findings suggest that nematode community indices can serve as integrative tools for urban soil quality assessment alongside classical physicochemical measurements.

title: Nematode bioindicator indices as complements to microbial biomass measurements in long-term field trials: a case study from Bačka
abstract: Long-term field trials running since 1977 at an experimental station in southern Bačka provided a unique opportunity to compare nematode community indices with established soil health indicators. Soils from four treatment histories — unfertilised control, mineral NPK, farmyard manure, and combined mineral + manure — were sampled in 2016. Microbial biomass carbon, basal respiration, and nematode community parameters including MI, EI, CI, and SI were measured on the same samples. Structural Index and Maturity Index showed strong positive correlations with microbial biomass carbon (r = 0.82 and 0.76 respectively), while the Enrichment Index was inversely correlated with metabolic quotient (qCO₂), suggesting that microbial community efficiency and nematode enrichment status carry complementary information. PCA analysis confirmed that nematode and microbial indicators occupy different axes of variation, supporting their use as independent lines of evidence in soil quality assessment rather than redundant substitutes.

title: Three-dimensional contact stress distribution in a trans-tibial prosthetic socket during simulated heel-strike
abstract: A patient-specific finite-element model of a trans-tibial residual limb was constructed from MRI data of a single male volunteer (age 44, body mass 78 kg, amputation level 15 cm below the knee). Bone, muscle, adipose tissue and skin were segmented semi-automatically and assigned distinct linear-elastic or hyperelastic constitutive laws. A rigid polypropylene socket with total-surface-bearing geometry was modelled with a friction coefficient of 0.45. Vertical load of 650 N was applied to simulate heel-strike during level walking. Peak von Mises stress occurred at the fibular head (182 kPa) and the distal tibia (214 kPa). Computed contact pressure maps correlated with clinically recorded pressure-mat data with a Pearson r of 0.81. The model reproduced pressure hot-spots reported by the subject, supporting its use as a pre-fitting design tool.

title: Effect of liner material stiffness on peak interface pressure at bony prominences: a parametric FEA study
abstract: Silicone and polyurethane liners are routinely placed between the residual limb and prosthetic socket, yet quantitative guidance on liner stiffness selection for individual patients is limited. This parametric study varied the Shore A hardness of a homogeneous liner layer (25A, 35A, 45A, 55A) in a validated trans-tibial FEA model across three residual-limb geometries representing slender, medium and bulbous morphologies. A total of 48 simulations were executed under a standardised 700 N stance-phase load. Peak pressure at the fibular head decreased monotonically with decreasing hardness, from 198 kPa at 55A to 127 kPa at 25A for the slender geometry. However, shear stress at the distal stump increased by 22% as liner stiffness decreased from 45A to 25A. These opposing trends suggest that a 35A liner represents a practical compromise for most geometries, though bulbous limbs tolerate softer materials with less shear penalty.

title: Computational assessment of pressure ulcer risk at the ischial tuberosity under wheelchair seating orthoses
abstract: Pressure ulcers at the ischial tuberosity are a major complication for wheelchair users. This study developed a two-dimensional axisymmetric FEA model of buttock soft tissue under a contoured seating orthosis, calibrated against published indentation data from 12 seated subjects. Three orthosis geometries—flat, pre-contoured and custom-moulded—were compared under a 400 N seated load. Internal tissue stress at a depth of 20 mm from the skin surface, corresponding approximately to the tissue–bone interface, reached 48 kPa for the flat insert, 31 kPa for the pre-contoured insert, and 22 kPa for the custom-moulded geometry. Stresses exceeding a published damage threshold of 35 kPa occupied 4.1 cm² and 1.2 cm² of tissue cross-section for flat and pre-contoured inserts respectively, but zero for the custom geometry. Results provide quantitative motivation for custom-moulded seating prescription in high-risk patients.

title: Automated socket geometry generation from CT data using statistical shape modelling
abstract: Prosthetic socket fabrication typically requires iterative manual rectification by an experienced prosthetist. This paper describes an automated pipeline that fits a statistical shape model, built from CT scans of 63 residual limbs, to a new patient scan to produce an initial socket geometry without manual intervention. The shape model captured 92% of geometric variance in the first eight principal components. For a leave-one-out cross-validation over the 63 subjects, the mean surface deviation between the auto-generated socket and the clinician-approved socket was 1.8 mm (SD 0.6 mm). Subsequent FEA of auto-generated versus clinician-generated sockets on ten held-out cases showed peak pressure differences below 12% at all anatomical sites. The pipeline executes in under four minutes on standard hardware, making it compatible with a clinical workflow. Limitations include a relatively small training dataset and the exclusion of paediatric cases.

title: Validation of a wearable pressure-mapping insole array against FEA predictions for below-knee socket loading
abstract: Wearable thin-film pressure sensors offer a means to collect in-socket interface data during community ambulation, but their accuracy relative to FEA predictions has not been systematically examined. Seventeen ambulatory trans-tibial prosthesis users wore a custom 32-sensor array inside their existing sockets for a 10-minute overground walking trial. Simultaneously, subject-specific FEA models constructed from MRI data were driven with ground reaction forces measured on a portable force plate. Sensor-to-model agreement was assessed at 12 anatomically defined zones. Mean absolute error was 14.2 kPa (range 6–28 kPa), with the largest discrepancies at the fibular head and anterior distal tibia where tissue curvature was highest. Sensor drift over the trial period introduced a 3–6 kPa offset correctable by linear recalibration. The study establishes quantitative accuracy bounds for this class of sensor under clinical conditions.

title: Influence of residual-limb volume fluctuation on interface pressure: a longitudinal FEA study over a six-month period
abstract: Residual-limb volume is known to change postoperatively and in response to activity, hydration and body weight. This longitudinal study re-scanned seven trans-tibial amputees with MRI at baseline, three months and six months after prosthetic fitting. Subject-specific FEA models were rebuilt at each time point and interface pressures compared for a constant socket geometry. Limb volume decreased by a mean of 7.3% (range 2–14%) over six months. This reduction increased peak contact pressure at the fibular head from a mean 168 kPa at baseline to 221 kPa at six months, a 31.5% increase. Three subjects exceeded a clinically proposed discomfort threshold of 200 kPa by month three, consistent with their reported pain scores (r = 0.74, p < 0.05). Results quantify the mechanical consequences of limb shrinkage and provide numerical targets for socket refitting schedules.

title: Comparison of total-surface-bearing and patella-tendon-bearing socket designs using subject-specific FEA in ten trans-tibial amputees
abstract: The clinical choice between total-surface-bearing (TSB) and patella-tendon-bearing (PTB) socket designs is informed largely by clinical experience rather than biomechanical data at the individual level. This study built ten subject-specific FEA models from MRI scans of active unilateral trans-tibial amputees and simulated both socket types under identical gait-derived loading conditions. TSB designs reduced peak fibular-head pressure by a mean of 24% compared with PTB, while PTB designs reduced anterior-tibial-crest pressure by 18%. Stump geometry—specifically the ratio of tissue depth over the fibular head to total limb diameter—was the strongest predictor of which design produced lower peak pressure (Spearman ρ = 0.82). Subjects with tissue-depth ratios below 0.14 showed lower peak pressures with TSB in nine of ten cases. These findings support developing a simple morphological screening rule to guide socket design selection.

title: Finite-element optimisation of ankle-foot orthosis trim-line geometry for reduced tibial crest pressure
abstract: Ankle-foot orthoses (AFOs) are widely prescribed for drop foot and spastic paresis, yet trim-line geometry is typically determined by clinical convention rather than individualised pressure analysis. A parametric FEA study varied trim-line position at six anatomical zones (medial and lateral malleoli, tibial crest, proximal anterior, proximal posterior, heel cup) across a grid of 144 design combinations applied to a standardised lower-leg geometry. Loading replicated the stance phase of walking at 1.2 m/s derived from motion-capture data. Tibial-crest peak pressure ranged from 68 kPa to 189 kPa across configurations; the most influential design parameter was the anterior proximal trim-line position, which alone explained 41% of pressure variance. Three trim-line configurations consistently kept all anatomical site pressures below 120 kPa and are proposed as default starting geometries for clinical customisation.

title: Viscoelastic modelling of residual-limb soft tissue under cyclic prosthetic loading
abstract: Most socket FEA studies treat soft tissue as a purely elastic material, ignoring creep and stress relaxation that occur during sustained standing and repetitive gait. This study characterised residual-limb tissue viscoelastic behaviour in ten subjects using an indentation device applying sinusoidal loads at 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 Hz over the fibular head region. A generalised Maxwell model with two relaxation time constants (τ₁ = 0.8 s, τ₂ = 12.4 s, mean across subjects) fitted the resulting force–displacement data with normalised root-mean-square errors below 4.5%. Incorporating these parameters into FEA predicted a 19% reduction in peak contact pressure after 60 seconds of static standing compared with the elastic baseline. Cyclic loading at 1 Hz produced residual strain accumulation of 3.2% over 200 cycles. The findings suggest that elastic FEA over-predicts contact pressure during prolonged standing and under-predicts cumulative tissue deformation during walking.

title: Patient-specific socket optimisation using gradient-free geometry perturbation and FEA in a clinical pilot study
abstract: This paper reports a clinical pilot study in which iterative FEA-guided geometry perturbation was used to design prosthetic sockets for five new trans-tibial amputees before their first fitting. Starting from an automated shape-model socket, a Nelder–Mead simplex algorithm perturbed 18 independently adjustable surface regions to minimise a weighted sum of peak contact pressure and pressure non-uniformity over anatomically sensitive zones. Each optimisation required between 60 and 110 FEA evaluations and converged in under 90 minutes on a 16-core workstation. Prosthetists rated the initial fit of the optimised sockets as requiring fewer adjustments (mean 1.4 modifications at first fitting) compared with a matched historical control group (mean 3.8 modifications; p = 0.03, Mann–Whitney U). Interface pressure measured with the sensor array was reduced by 22% at the fibular head on average. The study is limited by small sample size and absence of randomisation.

title: Comparing 3D-printed and conventionally fabricated socket geometries: mechanical stiffness, dimensional accuracy and FEA-predicted interface pressure
abstract: Three-dimensional printing of prosthetic sockets has attracted interest as a means of lowering fabrication cost and integrating digital design workflows. This study compared ten paired sockets—one 3D-printed in a glass-fibre-reinforced nylon (PA12-GF) and one thermoformed polypropylene—fabricated to identical geometries from digitised residual-limb scans of five subjects. Dimensional accuracy, measured with structured-light scanning against the nominal CAD geometry, was 0.4 mm (RMS) for 3D-printed versus 0.7 mm for thermoformed sockets. Four-point bending stiffness of 3D-printed sockets was 12% lower than polypropylene equivalents at 23°C, decreasing a further 9% at 37°C (body temperature). FEA incorporating measured stiffness differences predicted a 7–11% increase in peak contact pressure for the more compliant 3D-printed material. All pressures remained within the range observed across conventionally fabricated sockets in the existing dataset, suggesting 3D-printed sockets are mechanically acceptable for everyday use if wall thickness is increased by approximately 15%.

title: Поређење методa екстракције обележја за класификацију интракортикалних јединица у условима нестационарног шума
abstract: У овом раду испитујемо утицај нестационарног позадинског шума на тачност класификације неуронских јединица из интракортикалних снимака. Коришћени су снимци са 64-канaлних сонди код три субјекта (пацов, хронична имплантација) у трајању од четири недеље. Упоређена су четири скупа обележја: таласни облик у временском домену, PCA коефицијенти, Haar вејвлет коефицијенти и обележја заснована на енергији. Класификација је извршена помоћу Support Vector Machine са RBF кернелом и Gaussian Mixture Model. Резултати показују да вејвлет обележја задржавају тачност изнад 84% чак и при порасту нивоа шума за 6 dB, за разлику од PCA чија тачност пада испод 71% у истим условима. Рад такође анализира осетљивост свaке методе на промену импедансе електроде, мерену на почетку и крају четворонедељног периода.

title: Legal Personality and Decision-Making Authority of Homeowners Associations in Serbian Law
abstract: The article investigates whether Serbian homeowners associations constitute legal persons in domestic private law and what practical consequences flow from the answer for their capacity to enter contracts, hold accounts, and initiate litigation. Drawing on the provisions of the Law on Housing and Building Maintenance and the Law on Obligatory Relations, the study analyses thirty-two court decisions issued between 2017 and 2022 in which the legal standing of homeowners associations was contested. The article also surveys analogous solutions in Slovenian, Austrian, and German law to identify interpretive benchmarks. Findings confirm that Serbian law grants associations a limited form of legal subjectivity but that courts apply this inconsistently, particularly in disputes over utility contracts and liability for common-area accidents. The article recommends a legislative clarification specifying the scope of capacity and liability allocation between the association and individual co-owners.

title: Utility Infrastructure in Residential Buildings: Ownership, Maintenance Duties, and Liability Allocation
abstract: This chapter examines the legal classification of utility networks—water supply pipes, electrical conduits, gas installations, and heating systems—that run through both private and common parts of multi-unit residential buildings. Using the doctrinal method alongside an analysis of fifty-one arbitration and court decisions from Serbian, Slovenian, and Bosnian-Herzegovinian jurisdictions issued between 2010 and 2016, the chapter maps how ownership boundaries are drawn at the point where individual apartment connections branch from the shared riser. Special attention is paid to cases involving pipe bursts and water damage, where liability allocation between the building co-owners' collective and the individual flat owner proved contentious. The chapter identifies three recurring interpretive approaches in the region and evaluates each against general principles of co-ownership liability. A practical typology of infrastructure components is proposed as a basis for drafting clearer condominium by-laws.

title: Renovation Decisions in Condominium Buildings: Voting Thresholds and Dissenting Owners
abstract: The article studies the legal rules governing collective decisions on renovation and capital repairs in Serbian condominium buildings, with focus on the voting majority requirements and the legal remedies available to dissenting co-owners. The research is based on analysis of the Law on Housing and Building Maintenance provisions on assembly quorum and majority, supplemented by a review of twenty-seven municipal court judgments from Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Niš decided between 2016 and 2021. The study also draws comparisons with Austrian and German condominium legislation, both of which underwent recent reform to facilitate renovation decisions related to energy efficiency. Findings show that the Serbian absolute majority rule for ordinary renovation decisions is frequently circumvented through procedural manipulation of meeting notices, and that the sole judicial remedy—annulment of the assembly decision—offers inadequate relief because renovation work is often already completed by the time judgment is rendered. The article proposes the introduction of a suspensory effect for timely-filed annulment claims in defined categories of cases.

title: Shared Façades and Energy Renovation: Property Law Barriers to Thermal Insulation of Apartment Buildings
abstract: This article investigates the property law obstacles that impede thermal insulation projects on residential apartment buildings in Serbia, with a focus on how co-ownership rules, the requirement for unanimous versus majority consent, and the legal status of façade surfaces interact with national energy efficiency programmes. The empirical basis consists of a survey conducted in 2020–2021 among 46 licensed building managers in Novi Sad and Subotica, supplemented by interviews with seven urban planning officials and analysis of 19 administrative decisions issued under the national Energy Efficiency Fund programme. Results show that disputes over façade colour, insulation thickness encroaching on public space, and the refusal of ground-floor commercial unit owners to co-finance roof insulation are the three most commonly reported legal bottlenecks. The article contextualises these findings within EU member state experiences, particularly the Czech Republic and Hungary, and proposes targeted amendments to the Law on Housing and Building Maintenance.

title: Property Rights in Underground Parking Structures Beneath Condominium Buildings: Serbian and Comparative Perspectives
abstract: This study addresses the property law status of underground parking garages constructed beneath multi-unit residential buildings in Serbia, examining whether parking spaces and access ramps constitute separate objects of property rights, parts of the common property, or elements of a sui generis parking condominium. The analysis proceeds through doctrinal examination of the Law on Fundamentals of Property Relations, the Law on Housing and Building Maintenance, and the Law on State Survey and Cadastre, focusing on cadastral registration practice. Data from the Republic Geodetic Authority covering 214 newly registered underground parking facilities in Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Novi Pazar (2015–2022) are used to map actual registration approaches. Comparative material from Slovenian, German, and French law is incorporated to identify functionally distinct regulatory models. The article concludes that Serbian law contains a latent regulatory gap regarding multi-storey underground parking and proposes a registration model based on a modified floor ownership analogy.

title: Digital Infrastructure in Residential Buildings: Ownership and Access Rights for Fibre-Optic Cabling Under Serbian Property Law
abstract: The paper examines the legal framework governing the installation and ownership of fibre-optic cabling and related active equipment inside multi-unit residential buildings in Serbia, with particular reference to the interaction between property law and the Electronic Communications Act. Using doctrinal analysis of primary sources and a review of 31 complaints filed with the Regulatory Agency for Electronic Communications and Postal Services between 2018 and 2023, the study identifies the main conflicts arising when competing telecommunications operators seek access to in-building wiring infrastructure. The paper discusses whether in-building cabling automatically becomes part of the building's common property upon installation, or whether it retains the character of movable property belonging to the operator. Three factual scenarios are constructed and tested against relevant property law rules on accession, superficies solo cedit, and co-owners' right to exclude. Comparative reference is made to EU Directive 2014/61/EU on reducing the cost of deploying high-speed electronic communications networks and its implementation in Austria and the Czech Republic.

title: Enforcing Maintenance Obligations Against Unresponsive Co-Owners: Procedural and Substantive Dimensions
abstract: This conference paper examines the legal mechanisms available under Serbian law for compelling individual co-owners who refuse to participate financially in the maintenance of shared building infrastructure. The study focuses on three enforcement pathways: civil litigation for the recovery of unpaid maintenance contributions, the administrative penalty regime under the Law on Housing and Building Maintenance, and the possibility of imposing statutory charges registered against the apartment title. Drawing on a dataset of 68 first-instance decisions from Serbian municipal courts issued between 2019 and 2024, the paper analyses success rates, duration, and enforceability of judgments in maintenance contribution disputes. Findings show that average proceedings last 14 months and that successful claimants face substantial difficulties in enforcement against owners with no attachable assets other than the apartment itself. The paper argues for a strengthened lien mechanism linked to the apartment's cadastral record, similar to instruments used in the Slovak Republic and Poland.

title: Vicarious Liability Doctrine and Artificial Intelligence Systems: A Serbian Private Law Analysis
abstract: Classical vicarious liability doctrines premise liability on a relationship of subordination between a principal and an agent capable of independent wrongdoing. This article asks whether those doctrines can be applied by analogy when the wrongdoer is an AI system. The analysis draws on Serbian doctrinal sources, the comparative commentary of Zweigert and Kötz as adapted for Southeast European systems, and a review of legal scholarly literature from Germany, France, and the United Kingdom published between 2015 and 2022. The article constructs three models: (i) the tool model, denying independent agency to AI; (ii) the auxiliary model, treating AI as a legal auxiliary of the operator; and (iii) the independent entity model, requiring new legislation. It subjects each model to a stress test using five hypothetical cases covering medical diagnosis, autonomous vehicle routing, and automated fraud detection, and concludes that the auxiliary model is best suited to Serbian positive law but requires doctrinal refinements articulated in detail.

title: Effect of stylus tip diameter on measurement uncertainty for internal bores in cast aluminium housings
abstract: Stylus tip diameter is a frequently overlooked source of systematic error in CMM measurement of internal cylindrical features. This study quantified the contribution of tip-diameter variation (1 mm, 2 mm, and 3 mm ruby spheres) to the combined measurement uncertainty of bore diameter and cylindricity error in a cast aluminium gearbox housing with nominal bore diameters ranging from 18 mm to 62 mm. Measurements were performed on a Zeiss Contura G2 under controlled temperature (20 ± 0.5 °C). A Monte Carlo simulation with 10 000 trials was used alongside the analytical GUM approach to compare uncertainty estimates. Results showed that for bores below 25 mm diameter, the 1 mm stylus introduced a systematic underestimation of cylindricity error by up to 3.1 µm compared to the 2 mm stylus, attributable to filter-band effects in Gaussian least-squares fitting. Expanded uncertainties (k = 2) for diameter ranged from 0.8 µm to 2.4 µm depending on stylus configuration and feature size. Recommendations for stylus selection criteria keyed to bore-diameter classes are provided.

title: Comparison of minimum-zone and least-squares fitting algorithms for flatness evaluation of ground steel surfaces on CMMs
abstract: Flatness error evaluation depends critically on the fitting algorithm applied to point-cloud data acquired by a CMM. This paper compares minimum-zone (Chebyshev) and least-squares (Gaussian) fitting for flatness assessment of ground carbon steel plates (300 mm × 200 mm, Ra 0.4–1.6 µm) across four sampling densities: 9, 25, 49, and 81 points in a uniform grid pattern. Measurements were repeated five times per configuration on a Wenzel LH 65 CMM. The minimum-zone algorithm consistently produced flatness values 8–22% lower than least-squares across all sampling densities; the discrepancy increased with sampling density and surface roughness. Statistical significance was confirmed using paired t-tests at α = 0.05. The influence of probe qualification uncertainty on the fitting outcome was also modelled analytically and found to contribute less than 0.15 µm to the total flatness uncertainty at 81-point density. Practical guidance for selecting fitting algorithms in conformance testing against ISO 12781 tolerances is discussed.

title: Measurement uncertainty budgeting for position tolerances of multi-hole patterns using virtual CMM simulation
abstract: Position tolerances on hole patterns in prismatic machined parts involve compound geometric relationships that complicate straightforward GUM-based uncertainty budgeting. This study applied virtual CMM simulation (VCMM) to a representative aluminium bracket with a 12-hole pattern, nominal hole diameter 8 mm, positional tolerance of 0.05 mm at maximum material condition. The VCMM model incorporated geometric errors of the Zeiss Contura G2 machine geometry, probe qualification uncertainty, thermal drift estimated from laboratory records, and workpiece fixturing repeatability. Simulation runs of 5 000 iterations yielded expanded uncertainties (k = 2) for true-position deviation between 1.8 µm and 4.3 µm per hole, depending on hole location relative to datum planes. A sensitivity analysis identified workpiece fixturing as the dominant contributor, accounting for 38–51% of variance. The study also assessed the adequacy of a simplified two-point probing strategy versus a six-point strategy for each hole; the six-point strategy reduced uncertainty by 18% on average. Results are structured as a worked example conforming to ISO/TS 15530-4.

title: Probe-path length minimisation for CMM inspection of stepped prismatic parts using a graph-based travelling salesman approach
abstract: Reducing probe travel time on CMMs without compromising measurement integrity is an operational priority in high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environments. This paper formulates the probe-path planning problem for stepped prismatic parts—featuring planar faces, bores, grooves, and external shoulders—as a weighted graph in which nodes represent individual measurement feature clusters and edge weights encode Euclidean probe-travel distance plus collision-clearance penalties. A nearest-neighbour heuristic and a 2-opt local search were implemented and compared against the factory default path generated by Calypso software on a test part containing 34 features. The optimised 2-opt path reduced total probe travel by 23.4% and inspection cycle time by 17.8% over the default. Measurement results for all 34 features agreed within 1.5 µm of the default-path results, confirming that path reordering did not introduce statistically significant thermal or dynamic artefacts at the measurement speeds used (5 mm/s scanning). The method is applicable without modification to Calypso-controlled Zeiss machines.

title: Influence of workpiece temperature non-uniformity on CMM measurement of angular features in steel prismatic components
abstract: ISO 1 specifies 20 °C as the reference temperature for dimensional measurement, but real workshop-transferred parts frequently exhibit internal temperature gradients due to prior machining heat. This study characterised the effect of temperature non-uniformity (gradients of 0.5–3.0 K measured by a 12-point thermocouple grid) on CMM measurement of angular features—chamfers, dovetail slots, and inclined surfaces—in a medium-carbon steel prismatic component (260 mm × 140 mm × 80 mm). Thermal expansion modelling used a finite-element thermal model validated against measured surface temperatures. For a 3 K gradient, angular errors of up to 12 arcseconds were observed on a 45° chamfer, compared to a reference measurement after 2-hour thermal soak. A simple correction procedure based on three-point surface temperature measurement and linear interpolation reduced residual angular error to below 2 arcseconds. The expanded uncertainty contribution from uncorrected thermal gradient at 1 K was estimated at 4 arcseconds (k = 2). Practical settling-time guidelines are proposed for steel parts of this size class.

title: Standardisation of CMM measurement strategies for families of hydraulic manifold blocks: a classification and coding approach
abstract: Hydraulic manifold blocks constitute a geometrically diverse but internally structured part family—rectangular aluminium or steel blocks with intersecting drilled passages, threaded ports, and precision-ground mounting faces. Developing individual CMM inspection plans for each variant is time-consuming and prone to inconsistency. This paper describes a classification and coding system (12-digit code) derived from variant geometry attributes that automatically assigns standardised measurement strategy templates to manifold block families. Templates encode feature sequence, probing point counts, stylus configurations, and datum establishment procedures consistent with ISO 10360 and ISO 15530 series. The system was validated against 48 existing manifold block designs from three industrial collaborators; 43 of the 48 were matched to existing templates without modification, reducing strategy preparation time from an average of 3.4 hours to 22 minutes per part variant. Residual measurement uncertainty across the template-assigned inspections was within 5% of custom-developed plans. A worked example for a seven-port aluminium manifold is provided in full.

title: Evaluation of CMM probing force effects on measurement of thin-walled aluminium prismatic parts
abstract: Thin-walled prismatic aluminium components used in aerospace subassemblies are susceptible to elastic deflection during CMM probing, introducing systematic errors that conventional uncertainty budgets based on ISO/TS 15530-3 do not capture explicitly. This study measured probing-induced deflection on a set of reference specimens (wall thickness 1.5 mm, 2.5 mm, and 4.0 mm; alloy EN AW-6082) using a capacitive displacement sensor mounted in-fixture alongside the CMM stylus. Deflections of 1.8–7.4 µm were recorded at standard trigger force (0.1 N) for the 1.5 mm wall, depending on probing direction relative to wall orientation. A finite-element model of the specimen-fixture system showed good agreement (mean deviation 0.6 µm). Reduced probing force (0.03 N) lowered deflection to 0.5–1.9 µm for the same wall thickness but increased the scatter of repeated measurements by 0.4 µm (1σ). A decision rule for selecting probing force based on wall thickness and required positional tolerance is proposed and illustrated with a case study.

title: Measurement uncertainty in perpendicularity assessment of precision-ground datum faces: a calibrated artefact study
abstract: Perpendicularity of datum faces is a foundational tolerance in the inspection of prismatic machine parts, yet the uncertainty associated with its CMM-based evaluation is often reported without adequate traceability to artefact calibration. This study used a calibrated granite square artefact (manufacturer-stated perpendicularity error: 0.3 µm over 150 mm) as a reference to audit CMM-based perpendicularity assessment procedures. Measurements were performed on a Wenzel LH 65 CMM at three probe approach angles and two sampling patterns (uniform grid and stratified random) across ten repeat sessions over 30 days. Combined measurement uncertainty for perpendicularity ranged from 0.9 µm to 2.1 µm (k = 2), primarily driven by CMM geometric error (34%), day-to-day thermal variation (28%), and sampling pattern (21%). Stratified random sampling outperformed uniform grid sampling by reducing uncertainty by 14% on average for the same number of points (25 per face). A correction table for CMM geometric error contribution as a function of measurement height is provided.

title: Review of substitute geometry element fitting methods and their uncertainty implications for CMM-based GD&T evaluation
abstract: Geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) evaluation on CMMs requires fitting mathematical substitute geometry elements—planes, cylinders, spheres, cones—to discrete point clouds. The choice of fitting method (least-squares, minimum-zone, maximum-inscribed, minimum-circumscribed) directly affects the numerical value of the evaluated tolerance and its associated uncertainty. This book chapter reviews the theoretical basis of the four principal fitting methods, their computational implementation in common CMM software packages (Calypso, PC-DMIS, Metrolog X4), and their uncertainty implications under ISO GPS standards (ISO 1101, ISO 14253 series). Particular attention is given to the behaviour of each method under point-cloud sparsity and systematic spatial bias introduced by structured sampling patterns. The chapter includes a structured comparison table across fourteen tolerance types, illustrating cases where the choice of fitting method changes the conformance decision at standard manufacturing tolerances. Case data drawn from measurements of seven industrial prismatic part types are used throughout. Intended as a reference chapter for practitioners setting up inspection routines.

title: Automated CMM inspection planning for prismatic parts from STEP AP242 models: feature recognition and probing point assignment
abstract: Automated generation of CMM inspection routines directly from CAD models reduces the manual effort in inspection planning and minimises transcription errors. This paper presents a rule-based system that parses STEP AP242 model files to extract geometric and tolerance annotations (GD&T callouts embedded as PMI), recognises prismatic feature types (planes, cylinders, slots, pockets, chamfers), and assigns probing point counts and distributions according to a lookup table derived from ISO 15530 recommendations and in-house uncertainty data. The system was implemented in Python 3.10 using the pythonOCC library for STEP parsing and tested on a library of 22 industrial prismatic parts with between 8 and 61 annotated features. Inspection routines were generated in Calypso-compatible XML format. For 19 of the 22 parts, generated routines required no manual correction before execution; the three remaining parts had non-standard groove geometries that fell outside the feature recognition scope. Measurement results from the automatically generated routines agreed with manually developed routines within 1.2 µm for 94% of evaluated features. Runtime for routine generation was under 40 seconds per part on standard desktop hardware.

title: Effect of stylus qualification interval on long-term CMM measurement uncertainty: a 14-month longitudinal study
abstract: CMM stylus qualification (re-qualification of the probe tip by measurement of a reference sphere) is performed at intervals ranging from every part cycle to once per shift, depending on operator practice and machine manuals. The uncertainty contribution of qualification interval has not been systematically characterised in long-term production conditions. This study monitored stylus qualification data and associated measurement results on a Zeiss Contura G2 operating in a temperature-controlled (20 ± 1 °C) production-support metrology room over 14 months, covering 3 840 qualification events and approximately 12 600 part measurements. Statistical process control charts were applied to effective tip-radius estimates derived from qualification measurements. Drift between successive qualifications exceeded 0.3 µm (1σ) in 7.4% of intervals when qualification was performed at intervals greater than 4 hours; for intervals under 1 hour, the exceedance rate was 1.1%. A qualification-interval recommendation model is derived as a function of ambient temperature stability, stylus reach length, and part tolerance class (IT5–IT9), expressed as a simple look-up table for operators. The model reduces unnecessary qualification overhead by an estimated 31% while maintaining measurement uncertainty within specified limits.

title: Joint optimisation of preventive maintenance intervals and spare-parts reorder points for a multi-component system using simulation
abstract: Maintenance scheduling and spare-parts stocking decisions are typically made by separate organisational functions, yet they are tightly coupled: a shorter maintenance interval increases parts demand frequency while reducing the variance of that demand. This paper formulates the joint problem for a system of five interacting components—representative of a compressor train—where component lifetimes follow independent two-parameter Weibull distributions fitted to 11 years of plant data. A discrete-event simulation model is built in an open-source Python environment and combined with a Nelder–Mead optimiser to minimise total expected cost per unit time, encompassing maintenance labour, spare-parts holding, emergency procurement, and production downtime. Results show that the jointly optimised solution reduces total cost by 9.3% relative to the sequentially optimised baseline. The cost reduction is driven mainly by a 22% reduction in emergency procurements. Sensitivity to parts lead time and holding-cost ratio is explored through a one-at-a-time analysis over 36 scenarios.

title: Rule compliance and free-riding in a Vojvodina irrigation cooperative: evidence from structured interviews
abstract: This study examines patterns of rule compliance and free-riding behaviour among members of a mid-sized irrigation cooperative in the Bačka region of Vojvodina, Serbia. Using structured interviews with 87 farm operators conducted during the 2010 irrigation season, the analysis tests whether farm size, membership duration, and perceived fairness of water allocation predict self-reported compliance with rotational delivery schedules. Ordinal logistic regression models show that perceived fairness is the strongest predictor of compliance (OR 3.4, p < 0.01), while farm size has a modest negative association. Membership duration is not statistically significant after controlling for farm type. Free-riding is reported by 31 percent of respondents, predominantly at the tail end of delivery channels. The findings suggest that enforcement mechanisms alone are insufficient; interventions should address distributional equity in water allocation to sustain cooperative norms.

title: Linking bonding and bridging social capital to maintenance cost-sharing in small-scale irrigation schemes
abstract: Maintenance of shared irrigation infrastructure depends on collective contributions that are difficult to sustain when social ties are weak or heterogeneous. This paper reports findings from a comparative survey of 14 small-scale irrigation schemes in northern Serbia, collecting data from 312 farm households on bonding and bridging social capital dimensions as operationalised by adapted versions of the Integrated Questionnaire for the Measurement of Social Capital. Multilevel logistic models reveal that bridging capital—measured by participation in mixed-crop producer associations—is more strongly associated with voluntary labour contributions to canal maintenance than bonding capital based on kinship ties. Schemes with higher bridging capital contributed on average 1.8 voluntary workdays per household per season compared with 0.9 in low-bridging schemes. The paper concludes that policies promoting cross-community producer networks may indirectly support irrigation infrastructure upkeep.

title: Gender differences in participation and voice within water-user associations: survey evidence from Serbia and Hungary
abstract: Women's participation in water governance bodies is constrained by formal and informal barriers even when gender-neutral membership rules apply. This paper presents findings from a cross-border survey administered to 198 members of water-user associations in southern Hungary and northern Serbia, comparing men's and women's self-reported attendance at meetings, holding of committee positions, and perceived influence over water delivery decisions. Logistic and OLS models show that women are 42 percent less likely to hold committee positions (p < 0.05) and report 0.6 standard deviations lower perceived influence scores. Land ownership held in their own name partially mediates the influence gap. Qualitative responses from 34 female respondents indicate that meeting times during peak agricultural hours deter participation. The paper recommends scheduling reforms and quota provisions for committee membership.
