title: Network density and sanction capacity in irrigation collectives: a social network analysis of seven Vojvodina associations
abstract: This study applies social network analysis to assess whether network density and centrality within water-user associations predict the associations' capacity to sanction rule violations. Ego-network surveys were conducted with all active members of seven associations in Vojvodina (total n = 241) during 2016. Density, betweenness centrality, and clustering coefficients were calculated for each association using standard graph metrics. Multilevel negative binomial regression reveals that associations in the upper density quartile recorded on average 2.3 times more formal sanctions per irrigation season than those in the lower quartile (IRR 2.31, 95% CI 1.44–3.71). Bridging ties to external institutions—water management agencies and agricultural advisory services—independently contribute to sanction capacity. Highly centralised networks show no sanction advantage over decentralised ones when density is controlled. Practical implications for association design are discussed.

title: Does EU agri-environment scheme participation affect collective water management behaviour? Preliminary findings from Vojvodina
abstract: This conference paper reports preliminary findings from a study examining whether participation in agri-environment schemes under the EU IPARD programme alters farmers' attitudes toward and participation in collective irrigation governance. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 44 farmers in two municipalities in Vojvodina; approximately half had participated in IPARD agri-environment measures since 2014. Thematic analysis of interview transcripts identifies four recurrent framings of collective water management among IPARD participants: stewardship obligation, contractual compliance, economic calculation, and indifference. Non-participants predominantly employ the economic calculation framing. The paper argues that programme participation generates some stewardship orientation but that this does not automatically translate into increased engagement with water-user associations. Further quantitative follow-up is indicated.

title: Collective action under climatic uncertainty: responses of water-user associations in the Pannonian Plain to increased drought frequency
abstract: Between 2011 and 2021, the Pannonian Plain experienced four severe drought years, placing unusual demand pressure on irrigation associations not designed for sustained high-frequency use. This paper analyses responses of 19 water-user associations across northern Serbia and southern Hungary, drawing on annual administrative records, manager interviews, and a member survey (n = 388) conducted in 2021. Associations with higher pre-drought social capital scores—measured in a 2017 baseline survey—were more likely to implement emergency water-sharing protocols (OR 4.1, p < 0.01) and less likely to experience member exit. Financial reserves and physical infrastructure quality also predict adaptive response but are less decisive than governance quality. The paper quantifies the buffering effect of social capital under stress and discusses implications for climate adaptation policy in the region.

title: Smallholder exit from irrigation associations: a discrete-time hazard model for Vojvodina, 2005–2020
abstract: Membership attrition from water-user associations undermines their financial viability and weakens collective governance. Using administrative membership records from 11 associations covering the period 2005–2020, this study constructs a panel dataset of 1,047 individual member spells and estimates discrete-time hazard models to identify predictors of voluntary exit. Key predictors include farm size (smaller farms exit faster; HR 1.8 per 10-hectare decrease), years of consecutive water fee arrears (HR 2.4 per additional year), and distance from delivery channel (HR 1.3 per kilometre). Associations that underwent formal rule revision after 2012 show significantly lower exit hazard among all member categories. Unobserved heterogeneity is accounted for using shared frailty terms at the association level. Policy simulations suggest that targeted fee relief for small farms could reduce overall exit rates by approximately 17 percent over a ten-year horizon.

title: Information asymmetry and monitoring costs in layered irrigation governance: evidence from three Danube basin countries
abstract: This book chapter examines how information asymmetry between state water agencies, water-user associations, and individual farm members generates monitoring costs that erode governance efficiency in irrigation systems across Serbia, Romania, and Bulgaria. Drawing on 68 interviews conducted between 2021 and 2023 with agency officials, association managers, and farmers, and supplemented by budget and audit data from 24 associations, the chapter maps principal-agent relationships at two governance layers. At the state–association layer, audit frequency and reporting mandates vary substantially across the three countries; associations facing lighter oversight show higher rates of undetected fee evasion. At the association–member layer, metered delivery reduces monitoring costs but metering adoption remains below 30 percent in all three country samples. The chapter argues for harmonised minimum monitoring standards across national systems sharing transboundary water infrastructure.

title: Digital water metering and collective governance: early evidence from a pilot in two Vojvodina irrigation associations
abstract: This preprint describes early findings from an ongoing study of digital ultrasonic water metering introduced in 2023 in two irrigation associations in Vojvodina under a pilot supported by the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture. Data collected over one irrigation season (April–September 2024) from metered delivery records and a follow-up survey of 134 members are used to assess whether real-time consumption visibility affects compliance with delivery schedules, inter-member conflict rates, and willingness to pay. Preliminary results indicate a 14 percent reduction in unauthorised after-hours withdrawals compared with the pre-pilot season and a modest increase in reported satisfaction with water distribution fairness. Member survey data show higher acceptance of metering among younger and larger-farm operators. Concerns about data privacy and distrust of remotely accessible records are expressed by 28 percent of respondents. Full results pending the 2025 season.

title: Federating water-user associations: governance outcomes of two merger experiments in northern Serbia
abstract: Consolidation of small water-user associations into federated structures is advocated in Serbian water policy as a means of achieving economies of scale in infrastructure maintenance and improving negotiating power with state water agencies. This paper analyses two merger processes completed between 2019 and 2023 in northern Vojvodina, drawing on pre- and post-merger administrative data, attendance and voting records from 48 association meetings, and interviews with 31 elected officials and members. One merger produced measurable gains in maintenance spending efficiency (cost per irrigated hectare fell by 19 percent over three years) and sustained membership levels, while the other experienced 23 percent net member exit within 18 months of consolidation. The difference is attributed primarily to procedural fairness during the merger negotiation phase and to whether pre-existing informal water-sharing agreements were explicitly incorporated into the new federation's bylaws.

title: Subsidy dependency and adaptive capacity: longitudinal evidence from cereal farms in northern Serbia
abstract: Using an unbalanced panel of 143 cereal farms in northern Serbia tracked over 2008–2014, this paper estimates the degree to which direct payment receipts crowd out private investment and reduce adaptive capacity at the farm level. A fixed-effects instrumental variable estimator is applied, using lagged payment rates as instruments for subsidy income. The results suggest a statistically significant negative relationship between subsidy intensity and the probability of undertaking machinery investment in a given year, with an estimated elasticity of −0.31. Farms with higher subsidy dependency also show lower rates of crop diversification and lower adoption of precision input management practices. The paper argues that payment design, specifically decoupled area-based payments with no conditionality on investment or management change, may unintentionally reduce rather than support long-run farm resilience in the region.

title: Short Food Supply Chains as a Rural Development Tool: A Comparative Review of Policy Frameworks in the Western Balkans
abstract: This paper reviews policy frameworks governing short food supply chains (SFSCs) in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and North Macedonia, drawing on legislative documents, rural development programme texts, and semi-structured interviews with 22 national-level policy officials conducted in 2012. The analysis identifies a common pattern of weak definitional clarity around SFSCs in national legislation and limited financial incentives compared with EU member states at the same period. Croatia, on the eve of EU accession, showed the most developed regulatory environment, while Serbia lagged in formal recognition of direct-sales categories. The paper argues that clearer legal definitions and dedicated funding lines within national agri-environment schemes would increase uptake by smallholders. Recommendations are grounded in observed gaps between stated rural development objectives and actual instrument design.

title: Digital Tools and Small Producers: Adoption of Online Direct Sales in Serbia During the COVID-19 Period
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted traditional market attendance in Serbia from March 2020, prompting some small producers to explore online and social-media-based direct sales. This paper presents results of a rapid telephone survey of 119 small-scale producers in Vojvodina and Šumadija conducted in May–June 2020, supplemented by analysis of 24 social media sales groups active during the same period. Results show that 27% of surveyed producers experimented with online direct sales during the lockdown period, with Facebook Marketplace and WhatsApp being the most commonly used platforms. Younger producers and those with prior farmers' market experience were significantly more likely to adopt online channels. Most adoptions were temporary: two-thirds of online sellers had returned exclusively to physical channels by autumn 2020. The paper discusses the conditions under which emergency-driven digital adoption could be consolidated into lasting livelihood diversification.

title: Transaction Cost Perceptions Among Small Producers Considering Entry into Community-Supported Agriculture Schemes in Vojvodina
abstract: Community-supported agriculture (CSA) schemes remain uncommon in Vojvodina despite recorded consumer interest. This preprint reports preliminary findings from a structured survey of 74 small-scale producers in Vojvodina conducted in early 2026 about their perceptions of transaction costs associated with potential CSA entry. Respondents assessed twelve cost categories on a five-point burden scale, covering subscriber management, logistics, payment handling, communication, and quality assurance. Logistics and subscriber communication were rated highest in perceived burden, while payment handling and quality documentation were rated lower than expected given regulatory complexity. Regression analysis suggests that producers with prior farmers' market experience perceive significantly lower transaction costs across all categories. The paper outlines implications for CSA facilitation services and identifies areas where collective or platform-based solutions might reduce perceived barriers to entry.

title: Succession Intentions Among Elderly Farmers in Depopulating Villages of the Fruška Gora Foothills
abstract: Farm succession is a central mechanism linking demographic aging to the future structure of agriculture. This paper reports findings from semi-structured interviews with 68 farm operators aged 60 and over in 14 settlements along the southern slopes of Fruška Gora, conducted in 2019. Thematic analysis identifies three dominant succession orientations: planned intra-family transfer (27 percent of respondents), intended market sale or lease upon retirement (38 percent), and de facto abandonment with no identified successor (35 percent). The abandonment-prone group is characterised by farms smaller than 2 hectares, operators without children residing within 50 kilometres, and households dependent on pension income for more than 60 percent of total income. Barriers to market transfer include low land prices, unclear cadastral records, and lack of information about lease instruments. The study concludes that targeted advisory services and simplified land transfer procedures could substantially increase the share of farms finding productive successors.

title: Price transmission asymmetry and consumer welfare losses in the Serbian pork market: a counterfactual simulation
abstract: Asymmetric price transmission implies that consumers pay more on average than they would under symmetric adjustment. This paper translates estimated asymmetry parameters from a threshold vector error correction model—calibrated on 2010–2021 monthly Serbian data—into consumer welfare measures using a partial equilibrium simulation framework. The counterfactual symmetric price scenario is constructed by replacing observed asymmetric adjustment coefficients with the average of upward and downward adjustment speeds. Estimated annual consumer welfare losses attributable to asymmetry in the pork market amount to approximately 1,340 million Serbian dinars (roughly 11.5 million euros at 2021 exchange rates), equivalent to about 0.4 percent of total annual household expenditure on pork. Sensitivity analysis over plausible ranges of demand elasticity (−0.4 to −0.8) confirms that welfare losses are positive and economically meaningful across all scenarios. The paper argues for mandatory reporting of retail-to-wholesale price margins under a revised agricultural market transparency regulation.

title: Combining MCDA and ecosystem service mapping to prioritise PES instrument rollout in the Pannonian lowland: a stepwise procedure
abstract: The spatial heterogeneity of ecosystem service provision and the diversity of available payment instruments make sequencing decisions for policy rollout analytically demanding. This paper proposes a five-step procedure combining ecosystem service mapping with multi-criteria decision analysis to identify which instrument type should be introduced first in which area. The procedure was applied to 17 planning units covering the Serbian portion of the Pannonian lowland. Ecosystem service supply was quantified for four services—pollination support, carbon storage in permanent grasslands, flood regulation, and farmland bird habitat—using publicly available land-cover datasets and field-calibrated supply coefficients. ELECTRE-III was used to rank five candidate instruments against criteria including ecological urgency, instrument-service fit, administrative feasibility, and cost per expected outcome unit. Results show that discriminatory-price auctions are most appropriate in the four planning units with the highest ecological urgency and moderate administrative capacity, while simpler result-based pilots are preferable in areas with weaker institutional infrastructure. A decision support table is provided for direct use by provincial planning authorities.

title: Mapping Common Procurement Vocabulary Codes to a Regional OWL Ontology: A Pilot Study
abstract: The Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code system used in EU public procurement is not directly adopted in Western Balkan national portals, creating alignment barriers for cross-border suppliers. This paper describes the construction of a regional OWL 2 ontology that maps CPV 2008 codes to the procurement classification schemes of Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. Using manual expert mapping supplemented by string-similarity heuristics, 4 812 CPV leaf classes were aligned to 3 290 regional counterparts, achieving a coverage ratio of 68.4 %. A prototype SPARQL endpoint was used to validate alignment consistency against 1 200 historical tender notices. Results show that direct equivalence mappings account for 51 % of aligned pairs, while skos:narrowMatch and skos:broadMatch account for 28 % and 21 % respectively. The paper discusses limitations arising from inconsistent national classification updates and proposes a lightweight governance model for maintaining the mapping over time.

title: Towards an Interoperability Reference Architecture for Western Balkan e-Procurement Portals
abstract: Interoperability between national e-procurement portals in the Western Balkans is constrained by divergent data models, legal frameworks, and technical standards. Drawing on the European Interoperability Framework (EIF) as a structural template, this chapter proposes a four-layer reference architecture covering legal, organisational, semantic, and technical dimensions specific to the region. The semantic layer centres on a shared core procurement ontology expressed in OWL 2 DL, with national extension modules accommodating jurisdiction-specific requirements. The organisational layer specifies a proposed regional coordination body and update procedures. The architecture is evaluated against three use cases: cross-border supplier registration, tender notice aggregation, and contract award transparency reporting. A gap analysis comparing the architecture against the then-current state of portals in Serbia, Montenegro, and Albania identifies 27 concrete technical barriers, of which 14 are classified as addressable through ontology alignment alone.

title: Alignment of the eProcurement Ontology with the Serbian Law on Public Procurement: A Formal Gap Analysis
abstract: The eProcurement Ontology (ePO) developed under the EU's ISA² programme formalises the concepts of the EU public procurement directives. Serbia's Law on Public Procurement, revised in 2012, shares many structural elements with EU directives but diverges in areas such as negotiated procedure thresholds, domestic preference provisions, and complaint handling. This paper conducts a systematic formal gap analysis by comparing ePO version 1.0 class and property definitions against the Serbian legal text, encoded as a structured glossary of 312 defined terms. Using a modular OWL extension pattern, 47 Serbia-specific classes and 19 properties are added to a national profile ontology, while 23 existing ePO classes require scope restriction through hasValue or allValuesFrom axioms. Reasoning experiments with HermiT 1.3 confirm that the extended ontology remains consistent and that the added axioms do not introduce unsatisfiable classes.

title: Using SPARQL Federation to Query Heterogeneous Procurement Linked Data Across Multiple Balkan Portals
abstract: When procurement data from multiple national portals is published as RDF linked data, federated SPARQL queries provide a mechanism for cross-border retrieval without requiring a centralised data warehouse. This paper reports on a controlled experiment in which RDF datasets derived from Serbian, Montenegrin, and Macedonian procurement portals—comprising 6 200, 2 100, and 3 800 notices respectively—were loaded into separate Virtuoso 7.1 instances. Eleven cross-portal query templates of varying complexity were executed using SPARQL 1.1 federation extensions. Query execution times ranged from 0.4 s for simple lookups to 187 s for multi-hop award-chain queries. Query rewriting strategies that push FILTER clauses closer to remote endpoints reduced average execution time by 34 %. The paper identifies cardinality estimation as the principal bottleneck and discusses practical trade-offs between federation and materialised integration for operational deployment.

title: Ontology-Based Validation Rules for Procurement Notice Quality Assurance in Transition Economies
abstract: Procurement notice data quality in transition economies is frequently undermined by incomplete fields, inconsistent classification, and erroneous date entries. This paper proposes a set of 58 SHACL constraint shapes derived from ePO and Serbian national profile axioms to validate procurement notices at point of submission. The constraint set was applied retrospectively to a random sample of 5 000 Serbian portal notices from 2013–2015. Validation identified at least one violation in 61 % of notices; the most frequent violations concern missing contracting authority NUTS codes (38 %), mismatched procedure type and estimated value (22 %), and absent award date in completed contracts (17 %). A subset of 12 constraints was implemented as a browser-based pre-submission checker and piloted with four contracting authorities during a three-month field trial. Pilot participants reduced validation failures by 74 % relative to a control group.

title: Controlled Vocabularies for Public Works Procurement in Serbia: Current State and Harmonisation Scenarios
abstract: Public works procurement in Serbia relies on a mixture of sector-specific classification schemes inherited from Yugoslav-era standards and informal thesauri maintained by individual contracting authorities. This paper surveys 11 distinct controlled vocabularies currently in use across central government, local government, and public enterprise procurers, covering approximately 9 400 distinct terms. Vocabulary characteristics—scope, granularity, maintenance body, machine-readability—are systematically compared. Three harmonisation scenarios are evaluated: (i) adoption of the EU CPV works subhierarchy without modification, (ii) a mapped national thesaurus preserving existing terms as preferred labels, and (iii) a federated polyhierarchy linking national and CPV terms through SKOS mappings. A survey of 34 procurement officers at the Serbian Public Procurement Office suggests scenario (ii) as the most practically acceptable, with 71 % of respondents indicating preference for familiar terminology.

title: Cross-Border eTendering Between Serbia and Hungary: Technical and Semantic Barriers
abstract: The Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia cross-border programme funds public infrastructure projects jointly managed by contracting authorities on both sides of the border. In practice, joint tendering is rare because of incompatible eTendering platforms and divergent semantic models. This paper documents the technical and semantic barriers through structured interviews with 12 contracting authorities and a comparative technical analysis of the Hungarian EKR and Serbian portal APIs. Semantic barriers include: incompatible bidder qualification ontologies, different XML schemas for technical specification attachments, and conflicting currency handling. A total of 31 barriers are catalogued. A semantic mediation layer based on RDF mappings and a shared SKOS qualification vocabulary is prototyped and demonstrated for the simplified procedure type applicable to joint infrastructure contracts. The prototype reduced manual re-keying of bidder data from an average of 4.2 h to 0.6 h per tender.

title: Ontology Modularisation Strategies for National Profile Extensions of the eProcurement Ontology
abstract: The eProcurement Ontology (ePO) is designed as a core ontology intended to be extended by national profiles. This paper evaluates three modularisation strategies—monolithic extension, module-per-jurisdiction, and aspect-oriented slicing—against criteria of reasoning scalability, maintainability, and alignment robustness. Experiments use synthetic datasets of 10 000, 50 000, and 200 000 procurement instances loaded into OWL 2 RL materialisation pipelines. Monolithic extension causes a 3.8× increase in reasoning time at 200 000 instances compared to module-per-jurisdiction. Aspect-oriented slicing reduces ontology load time by 61 % when only the qualification aspect is needed. A decision matrix for profile ontology architects is derived. The paper also reports on applying the module-per-jurisdiction strategy to produce a validated Serbian ePO national profile covering 89 % of the scope of the national procurement law.

title: Semantic Annotation of Procurement Contract Award Notices for Corruption Risk Detection: A Feasibility Study
abstract: Contract award notices contain structured signals that civil society organisations and oversight bodies use to assess corruption risk, but manual review is labour-intensive and inconsistent. This feasibility study explores whether semantic annotation of award notices with a purpose-built risk indicator ontology (PRIO) can support semi-automated risk scoring. PRIO defines 24 risk indicator classes derived from the academic literature and the OECD integrity framework. A sample of 3 600 Serbian award notices from 2017–2020 was annotated semi-automatically using a pipeline combining SHACL-derived feature extraction with a random forest classifier trained on 800 manually labelled notices. Precision and recall on a held-out test set of 400 notices were 0.78 and 0.71 respectively. The paper discusses ontological design choices that affect recall, particularly the granularity of single-bidder procedure classes, and proposes three ontology revisions to improve coverage.

title: Mapping eProcurement Ontology 3.1 to the OpenContracting Data Standard: A Bidirectional Alignment
abstract: The eProcurement Ontology (ePO) and the Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) both describe public procurement lifecycles but differ in their conceptual scope, granularity, and serialisation format. ePO is an OWL ontology targeting semantic reasoning; OCDS is a JSON Schema targeting publication and data exchange. This paper documents a bidirectional alignment between ePO 3.1 and OCDS 1.1.5. Alignment is expressed using a combination of SKOS mapping properties and SPARQL CONSTRUCT rules that generate OCDS-conformant JSON from ePO RDF instances. Coverage analysis shows that 83 % of OCDS fields can be populated from ePO triples without information loss, while 17 % require supplementary provenance or process fields absent from ePO. A reverse alignment from OCDS JSON to ePO RDF achieves 91 % property coverage. The alignment artefacts are tested on 420 Serbian and 310 Montenegrin procurement records.

title: A Linked Data Publication Framework for Western Balkan Public Procurement Registers: Design and Pilot Deployment
abstract: Western Balkan countries are under gradual pressure from EU accession conditionality to publish procurement data as open linked data. This paper describes the design and pilot deployment of a linked data publication framework, RegiLink, covering Serbia and Montenegro. The framework ingests data from national portals via REST APIs, applies RML mapping rules to convert portal records to ePO-conformant RDF, mints persistent URIs following a regional URI policy, and exposes the resulting datasets via a Virtuoso-based SPARQL endpoint and a Linked Data Fragments server. A pilot dataset covering 2022–2024 and containing 284 000 Serbian and 61 000 Montenegrin notices was published and validated. End-to-end latency from portal publication to triple store availability averages 4.1 hours. A user study with 11 data journalists and civil society analysts assessed the usability of the SPARQL interface and Linked Data Fragments client, finding the fragments interface preferable for exploratory querying by non-technical users.

title: Nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus among pig farm workers in Vojvodina: a cross-sectional study
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus among 148 pig farm workers on 22 farms in the South Bačka and Srem districts of Vojvodina between 2005 and 2006. Nasal swabs were cultured on selective media, and confirmed S. aureus isolates were screened for methicillin resistance by disk diffusion and mecA PCR. Carriage prevalence was 38.5% overall, with methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) detected in 6.1% of workers. Workers with more than five years of daily direct animal contact had a carriage rate 2.4 times higher than those with less than one year of exposure (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3–4.5). Spa typing identified spa type t011 as predominant, consistent with livestock-associated MRSA CC398 circulating in neighbouring countries. No community controls from non-farming households carried MRSA. The findings suggested that occupational exposure to pigs in this region constituted a meaningful acquisition risk well before systematic surveillance was in place.

title: Household transmission of livestock-associated MRSA from pig farmers to family members: a prospective cohort study in rural Vojvodina
abstract: A prospective cohort of 62 pig farm workers and 184 household contacts was followed over 12 months to measure within-household transmission of livestock-associated MRSA. Participants provided nasal and throat swabs at enrolment, three months, six months, and twelve months. Whole-household secondary attack rates were calculated using survival analysis with time-varying MRSA status of the index farmer as the exposure. At least one household contact acquired MRSA in 19 of 62 households (30.6%). Sharing a bedroom with the index farmer (adjusted hazard ratio 3.1, 95% CI 1.6–5.9) and the absence of handwashing facilities adjacent to the livestock area (adjusted hazard ratio 2.0, 95% CI 1.1–3.7) were independent predictors of transmission. Children under 12 cleared MRSA more rapidly than adults. Whole-genome sequencing on a subset of 38 household pairs confirmed near-identical isolates in 27 pairs (71%), providing molecular evidence of direct within-household spread.

title: Prevalence and molecular epidemiology of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae in cattle on smallholder farms in Serbia
abstract: Rectal swabs were collected from 412 cattle on 31 smallholder farms across three districts of Vojvodina in 2011. Samples were screened on CHROMagar ESBL and confirmed by double-disc synergy test; positive isolates were characterised by PCR for blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M gene families. ESBL-producing Escherichia coli was isolated from 18.4% of animals; blaCTX-M group 1 genes predominated (67% of ESBL producers). Multilocus sequence typing placed 38% of isolates into ST131 and ST10 complexes. Farms with documented use of third-generation cephalosporins in the preceding 12 months had a 2.8-fold higher prevalence of ESBL producers. The study provides the first systematic molecular characterisation of ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae from cattle in Vojvodina, offering a baseline for longitudinal surveillance. Results were shared with the Provincial Veterinary Directorate and informed subsequent monitoring protocols.

title: Risk factors for fecal carriage of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in adults living in livestock-farming households in rural Serbia
abstract: A case-control study enrolled 110 adults with fecal ESBL-producing E. coli and 220 matched controls from the same rural villages in 2013–2014. Cases and controls were drawn from a cross-sectional screening of 1,240 individuals across 410 farming households. Conditional logistic regression identified direct daily contact with cattle or poultry (adjusted OR 3.6, 95% CI 2.0–6.5), consumption of water from unprotected wells (adjusted OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.2–3.7), and recent antibiotic use by the participant (adjusted OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.5–5.5) as independent risk factors. Molecular typing showed that human and co-resident animal isolates on the same farm shared indistinguishable PFGE profiles in 23 of 61 pairs where both sources yielded an ESBL producer. The findings pointed to both direct zoonotic transfer and shared environmental reservoirs as contributors to human acquisition in this setting.

title: Antibiotic use practices among livestock farmers in Vojvodina: a qualitative study of knowledge, attitudes and practices
abstract: Fifteen in-depth interviews and four focus groups were conducted with cattle and pig farmers in four rural municipalities of Vojvodina in 2014 to explore knowledge, attitudes, and practices relating to antibiotic use in animals. Thematic analysis identified three dominant patterns: self-prescribed antibiotic use obtained without veterinary prescription, deliberate under-dosing to reduce costs, and widespread belief that antibiotic residues in meat posed no human health risk. Participants were largely unaware of concepts such as antimicrobial resistance or the possibility that resistant organisms could transfer to family members. Structural barriers included limited veterinary availability in remote areas and financial constraints. The study highlighted gaps in farmer education programmes and pointed to opportunities for behaviour change communication that frame antibiotic stewardship in terms of family health rather than abstract resistance risk. Findings informed the design of a subsequent mixed-methods surveillance study.

title: Genomic relatedness of MRSA isolates from pigs, farmers, and household contacts on 12 farms in Vojvodina: a One Health approach
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing was performed on 116 MRSA isolates collected simultaneously from pigs, farm workers, and their household members on 12 farms in 2015. Core genome MLST (cgMLST) using a scheme of 1,861 targets revealed that isolates from pigs and co-resident humans on the same farm were more closely related (median allelic distance 4, range 1–18) than isolates from different farms (median distance 142, range 47–381). All human and animal isolates belonged to CC398; spa types t011 and t034 each accounted for approximately 40% of the collection. Resistance gene profiling showed that tetracycline resistance genes (tetM, tetK) and the vga(A) gene conferring streptogramin resistance were carried on mobile genetic elements shared across pig and human isolates. The data provided direct genomic evidence for ongoing bidirectional transfer between the livestock and human niche in this setting.

title: Persistence of livestock-associated MRSA carriage in farm workers after temporary cessation of animal contact: a six-month observational study
abstract: Twenty-eight pig farm workers who temporarily ceased livestock contact for at least four weeks (due to illness, holiday, or farm closure) were followed with monthly nasal swabs for six months to track persistence of MRSA carriage. All workers had tested MRSA-positive during active farm work. After one month without animal contact, 64% remained MRSA-positive; by six months, 32% still carried MRSA. Workers with more than eight years of farming history had significantly longer persistence (log-rank p = 0.03). Spa typing confirmed the same spa type was maintained through follow-up in all persistent carriers, ruling out repeated community re-acquisition. The data suggest that in a proportion of long-term livestock workers, MRSA carriage may become semi-permanent and is not fully reversed by short-term cessation of exposure. This has implications for defining the decolonisation target population in intervention studies.

title: Transmission of colistin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae between poultry and farm workers in Serbia: a case series
abstract: Following the detection of the mcr-1 gene in poultry isolates during routine surveillance by the Provincial Veterinary Institute in 2017, a rapid investigation was undertaken on three broiler farms in the Bačka Palanka area. Cloacal swabs from 247 birds and fecal/rectal swabs from 19 farm workers and 41 household contacts were cultured and screened by mcr-1 PCR. mcr-1-positive Klebsiella pneumoniae was identified in birds on all three farms (farm-level prevalence 100%) and in four farm workers (21%) and two household contacts (4.9%). Plasmid replicon typing identified IncI2 plasmids in both animal and human isolates; Southern blot hybridisation confirmed that mcr-1 was carried on the same plasmid type across species. This is the first documented case series of putative human acquisition of mcr-1-positive K. pneumoniae from poultry in Serbia and underscores the public health significance of colistin use in broiler production.

title: Longitudinal dynamics of ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae in a cohort of swine farm workers and household members: two-year follow-up
abstract: A prospective cohort of 94 swine farm workers and 212 co-residing household members was followed with quarterly fecal sampling over 24 months (2018–2020). Incidence density of new ESBL-producing E. coli acquisition, clearance rates, and predictors of prolonged carriage were estimated using multi-state Markov models. Annual incidence of new acquisition in farm workers was 42.1 per 100 person-years, compared with 18.7 in household members and 9.2 in a non-farming village comparison group. Clearance from a positive state was faster in household members (mean duration 2.8 months) than in farm workers (mean 4.9 months). Antibiotic courses during follow-up were paradoxically associated with temporary clearance but also with subsequent acquisition of a different sequence type. Whole-genome sequencing on a subset confirmed that 61% of acquisitions in household members represented strains also detected in the co-resident farmer, while 39% appeared to derive from other household or environmental sources.

title: Environmental contamination of farm surfaces and drinking water with antimicrobial-resistant organisms on pig and poultry farms in Vojvodina
abstract: Environmental sampling was conducted on 18 pig and 14 poultry farms during summer and winter seasons in 2020. Swabs were taken from pen walls, feed troughs, manure handling areas, and doorknobs; water samples were collected from animal drinking lines and, on six farms, from adjacent wells used for household drinking water. ESBL-producing E. coli was recovered from 73% of farms, MRSA from 44%, and mcr-1-positive isolates from 22%. Adjacent household well water yielded ESBL-producing E. coli on 3 of 6 tested farms. Seasonal differences were modest for MRSA but significant for ESBL E. coli counts, which were higher in summer (geometric mean 2.3 × 10³ CFU per 100 mL well water vs. 4.1 × 10² in winter, p = 0.04). Comparison of environmental and human isolate genomes from four farms showed convergent resistance gene content, suggesting the farm environment constitutes a persistent reservoir linking animal and human carriage.

title: Antimicrobial resistance at the livestock–human interface in Central and Southeast Europe: a scoping review of study designs, pathogens, and findings 2010–2022
abstract: This scoping review systematically mapped evidence on AMR transmission between livestock, farm workers, and household contacts published from 2010 to 2022 for studies conducted in Austria, Croatia, Hungary, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, and Slovenia. Searches of PubMed, Embase, and regional databases retrieved 1,847 records; 74 studies met inclusion criteria after full-text review. Most studies were cross-sectional (58%), with only 14 prospective cohort studies identified across the entire region. MRSA CC398 and CTX-M-group-1-producing E. coli were the most frequently reported resistance phenotypes. Molecular evidence of direct livestock-to-human transmission was provided in 29 studies; evidence of household onward spread in only 11. Substantial heterogeneity in sampling frames, case definitions, and typing methods precluded quantitative pooling. The review identified the near-absence of longitudinal data from smallholder mixed-farming systems and intervention trials as critical gaps, and proposed a minimum reporting standard for future studies in the region.

title: Characterisation of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in environmental samples from two intensive livestock farms in Serbia
abstract: Between 2022 and 2023, environmental swabs from equipment surfaces, manure pits, and adjacent soil were collected on two large-scale intensive cattle farms in Vojvodina where carbapenem-resistant organisms had previously been detected during routine veterinary monitoring. Forty-seven Acinetobacter baumannii isolates were recovered; carbapenem resistance was confirmed in 29 (61.7%) by broth microdilution and EUCAST breakpoints. OXA-23 carbapenemase genes were detected in all resistant isolates by PCR; whole-genome sequencing of 20 representative isolates assigned them to international clone IC2 (ST2 under the Pasteur scheme). Biocide resistance genes (qacE, qacEdelta1) were co-located on the same chromosomal resistance islands in 16 isolates. While no human sampling was performed in this study, the detection of a globally disseminated healthcare-associated clone in an agricultural environment raises questions about reservoir ecology and spillover potential. The study was conducted as a preliminary investigation for a larger One Health surveillance project.

title: Transmission probability and dose-response modelling for livestock-associated MRSA exposure in farming households: a Bayesian approach
abstract: Using longitudinal household data collected over two years from 62 farming families in Vojvodina, a Bayesian hierarchical model was fitted to estimate within-household MRSA transmission probabilities conditional on index farmer carriage status, contact intensity, and household size. Posterior median daily transmission probability per susceptible household contact was 0.0041 (95% credible interval 0.0019–0.0087) given a MRSA-positive farmer with regular indoor contact. Sensitivity analyses incorporating MRSA load estimated from semi-quantitative culture yielded higher estimates for high-load carriers (posterior median 0.0078). The model was used to project expected secondary cases under two hypothetical interventions: daily farmer decolonisation attempts (projected reduction in household acquisitions 38%) and improved farm-to-house hygiene barriers (projected reduction 27%). This modelling framework, calibrated to local epidemiological parameters, offers a tool for ranking intervention options before costly field trials. Code and data are deposited in the Open Science Framework repository.

title: Protocol and baseline characteristics of the FARMLINK cohort: a prospective One Health study of antimicrobial resistance transmission on mixed livestock farms in Serbia
abstract: FARMLINK is a prospective observational cohort study recruiting 200 mixed livestock farming households across five districts of Vojvodina, with concurrent sampling of farmers, household contacts, farm animals (cattle, pigs, poultry), and environmental compartments (water, soil, surfaces) at six-monthly intervals over three years. This paper reports the study protocol and baseline characteristics of the first 148 enrolled households. At enrolment, ESBL-producing E. coli was detected in at least one household member in 61 (41.2%) of households, MRSA in 22 (14.9%), and at least one of these organisms in farm animals in 109 (73.6%) of households. Whole-genome sequencing is performed on all AMR isolates; metagenomics is applied to water and soil samples. The primary endpoints are incidence of new AMR acquisition in household members and genomic relatedness between human and animal isolates over time. FARMLINK is funded under the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia and is registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews.

title: Address completeness in the Vojvodina Cancer Registry, 2000–2007: patterns and predictors of missing geocoding information
abstract: Reliable spatial analysis of cancer incidence depends on accurate patient address data. This study quantified missing and partial address information in 14,203 colorectal and colon cancer records registered in the Vojvodina Cancer Registry between 2000 and 2007. Records were classified into three tiers: full street address (62.4%), municipality only (28.9%), and settlement only without street (8.7%). Logistic regression identified older age at diagnosis (OR 1.8 per decade, 95% CI 1.6–2.1), rural place of residence (OR 2.4, 95% CI 2.0–2.9), and diagnosis in hospitals outside Novi Sad (OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.5–2.0) as independent predictors of incomplete address. Temporal trends showed modest improvement in completeness over the study period, from 55% full-address in 2000 to 70% in 2007. The results establish the magnitude and structure of the missingness problem and inform the design of statistical approaches that can accommodate hierarchical, partially geocoded registry data.

title: A Bayesian Poisson model with spatially structured random effects for small-area colorectal cancer mapping under partial geocoding
abstract: When registry records carry only administrative-unit identifiers for a fraction of cases, naïve area-level rate estimation is biased. This paper presents a Bayesian hierarchical Poisson model that treats the stratum of incompletely geocoded cases as a latent allocation problem. Cases known only to municipality level are redistributed probabilistically to constituent census tracts using population-weighted priors informed by the geocoded fraction. Spatially structured random effects follow a conditional autoregressive (CAR) prior. The model was applied to 3,218 colorectal cancer cases from Vojvodina registered 2003–2008, of which 31% lacked tract-level addresses. Posterior median incidence rate ratios across 312 census tracts ranged from 0.62 to 1.89 relative to the regional mean. Compared to a complete-case analysis excluding partially geocoded records, the full model produced narrower credible intervals and smoothed out artefactual high-rate areas near large hospitals. Model fit was assessed by the deviance information criterion and posterior predictive checks.

title: Temporal trends in colorectal cancer incidence in Vojvodina municipalities, 2000–2014, estimated by a spatio-temporal Bayesian model
abstract: This study extended earlier cross-sectional small-area models to a spatio-temporal framework to estimate trends in colorectal cancer incidence across Vojvodina municipalities over a fifteen-year period. A total of 21,340 incident cases were obtained from the Vojvodina Cancer Registry for 2000–2014. A Bayesian hierarchical model with separable spatial and temporal random effects and a type IV interaction term was fitted in R-INLA. The proportion of records with incomplete geocoding averaged 27% over the period and was handled by the probabilistic reallocation approach developed in prior work. Male incidence increased at an average posterior rate of 1.4% per year (95% credible interval 0.9–1.8%), while female rates were stable. Three northern municipalities showed significantly increasing trends independent of age structure shifts. Results were robust to alternative prior specifications. The analysis demonstrates that spatio-temporal smoothing can recover meaningful trend signals even when registry completeness varies across both space and time.

title: Integrating opportunistic screening participation data into small-area colorectal cancer incidence models: a feasibility analysis
abstract: Serbia launched an organised national colorectal cancer screening programme in 2013, but participation rates vary markedly across municipalities and have been recorded at programme level since 2015. This preprint explores whether incorporating municipality-level faecal immunochemical test (FIT) participation rates as a time-varying covariate improves small-area CRC incidence estimates. Using Vojvodina Cancer Registry data for 2015–2023 and programme participation data supplied by the Institute of Public Health of Serbia, a spatio-temporal Bayesian model with and without the participation covariate was fitted for 45 municipalities. Inclusion of participation rates improved DIC by 8.4 points and shifted posterior incidence estimates upward in high-participation municipalities, consistent with detection of prevalent undiagnosed cases. The analysis is limited by municipality-level aggregation of participation data; finer-resolution linkage is not yet available. Results suggest that screening uptake data should be incorporated in future registry-based models as this information becomes available at smaller geographic scales.

title: Salivary Cortisol and Pre-Competition Anxiety in Adolescent Swimmers: A Field Study
abstract: This study examined the relationship between salivary cortisol levels and self-reported pre-competition anxiety in adolescent competitive swimmers aged 13–17 years (n = 38; 21 female, 17 male) during a regional championship in Novi Sad. Salivary samples were collected at three time points: the evening before competition, 30 minutes before the start, and 60 minutes after competition. Anxiety was assessed using the Sport Anxiety Scale-2 (SAS-2). Cortisol concentrations peaked at the 30-minute pre-competition measurement (mean 18.4 nmol/L, SD 5.2), representing a significant increase from baseline (p < 0.01). Somatic anxiety subscale scores correlated positively with cortisol peak values (r = 0.54, p < 0.001), while cognitive anxiety showed a weaker association (r = 0.31, p < 0.05). Female athletes showed consistently higher cortisol reactivity than male counterparts at both pre-competition time points. The findings support the use of salivary cortisol as a practical, non-invasive field measure of acute competitive stress in youth sport contexts and suggest that somatic anxiety components may be more closely tied to neuroendocrine stress activation than cognitive appraisal components in this age group.

title: Heart Rate Variability as an Indicator of Stress Load in Young Handball Players During a Tournament Week
abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) was monitored across a five-day youth handball tournament in 26 male adolescent players (mean age 15.3 ± 1.1 years) to assess autonomic nervous system responses to accumulated competitive and training stress. Resting HRV measurements (RMSSD, SDNN, LF/HF ratio) were recorded each morning using a portable short-term ECG protocol lasting five minutes. Perceived stress and recovery were tracked daily with the Short Recovery and Stress Scale (SRSS). RMSSD values declined significantly from day one (mean 62.4 ms) to day four (mean 47.1 ms; p < 0.001), reflecting progressive parasympathetic withdrawal. LF/HF ratio increased across the tournament, consistent with sympathetic dominance under accumulated load. Players reporting higher perceived competition stress on SRSS showed steeper RMSSD decreases than those reporting lower stress. These results indicate that daily HRV monitoring during tournament contexts can serve as a practical, low-burden method for tracking psychophysiological stress accumulation in adolescent team sport athletes and may assist coaching staff in scheduling recovery interventions.

title: Acute Cortisol and HRV Responses Before a Simulated Competition in Adolescent Track and Field Athletes: Influence of Trait Anxiety
abstract: The study investigated whether trait anxiety moderates acute psychophysiological stress responses in a controlled pre-competition simulation. Twenty-two adolescent track and field athletes (mean age 16.0 ± 1.3 years; 12 female, 10 male) completed the Sport Anxiety Scale-2 trait version four weeks before a simulated competition event held under standardised laboratory and outdoor conditions. On test day, salivary cortisol was sampled at rest, 30 minutes prior to the simulated start, and 45 minutes post-event. Resting HRV was recorded 30 minutes before the start. High trait anxiety athletes (n = 11, upper tertile) showed significantly greater cortisol increases from rest to pre-event (Δ mean 9.7 nmol/L vs. 4.3 nmol/L; p < 0.01) and lower pre-event RMSSD values (mean 41.2 ms vs. 58.6 ms; p < 0.05) compared to low trait anxiety athletes (n = 11, lower tertile). Trait anxiety was a significant predictor of cortisol reactivity magnitude (β = 0.48, p < 0.01) after controlling for event distance category. Results support trait anxiety as a meaningful predictor of physiological stress load in adolescent athletes and underscore the value of trait assessment in routine sport psychology screening.

title: Solid-state fermentation of wheat bran into a protein-rich ingredient
abstract: Wheat bran, a major by-product of the flour milling industry, is underutilised despite its considerable nutritional potential. This study investigated the application of solid-state fermentation (SSF) using selected fungal strains to enhance the protein content and digestibility of wheat bran. Fermentation was carried out using Aspergillus oryzae and Rhizopus oligosporus under optimised moisture, temperature, and inoculation conditions over a 72-hour period. The protein content of fermented bran increased by up to 38% compared with untreated bran, while in vitro protein digestibility improved significantly. Scanning electron microscopy revealed substantial structural changes in the bran matrix, consistent with cell wall degradation. Sodium dodecyl sulphate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis confirmed the generation of lower-molecular-weight protein fractions. Anti-nutritional factors, including phytic acid and tannins, were reduced following fermentation. The resulting ingredient demonstrated promising functional properties, including water-holding capacity and emulsification, making it suitable for incorporation into bakery and meat analogue formulations. These findings support SSF as a viable, low-cost route for converting milling waste into a commercially relevant protein-rich food ingredient.

title: Extracting ferulic acid from milling by-products
abstract: Ferulic acid is a hydroxycinnamic acid found predominantly in the arabinoxylan-bound fraction of cereal bran cell walls and is recognised for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. This study evaluated enzymatic and alkaline hydrolysis methods for liberating ferulic acid from wheat bran and other milling by-products, including rye and spelt bran. Xylanase and feruloyl esterase combinations were compared with sodium hydroxide treatment under varying concentrations and incubation times. Alkaline hydrolysis yielded the highest total ferulic acid content (2.8 mg g⁻¹ dry weight in wheat bran), while the enzymatic approach offered superior selectivity and reduced co-extraction of interfering phenolics. High-performance liquid chromatography with diode-array detection was used for quantification, and antioxidant activity was assessed by DPPH and ABTS assays. Spelt bran emerged as a particularly rich source, yielding 3.4 mg g⁻¹ under optimised alkaline conditions. The study also examined the stability of extracted ferulic acid under different storage conditions, confirming that refrigeration in amber glass vessels preserved over 90% of activity over 60 days. These findings provide a practical basis for designing extraction protocols adaptable to industrial milling facilities.

title: Arabinoxylan fractionation from wheat bran: impact of particle size reduction on yield and purity
abstract: Arabinoxylans (AX) constitute a major component of wheat bran dietary fibre and exhibit prebiotic and viscosity-enhancing properties relevant to functional food development. This study examined how ball milling and jet milling as pre-treatment methods influence the extractability and structural characteristics of AX from hard and soft wheat bran. Sequential aqueous and alkaline extractions were performed at laboratory scale, and AX fractions were characterised by their arabinose-to-xylose ratio, molecular weight distribution (gel permeation chromatography), and degree of feruloylation. Ball-milled bran produced AX fractions with higher purity (82% compared with 67% in unmilled controls) but lower average molecular weight, suggesting partial chain scission. Jet milling preserved molecular integrity while still improving yield by 24%. Infrared spectroscopy confirmed the preservation of the characteristic AX backbone in all extracted fractions. In vitro fermentation trials using human faecal inocula indicated that high-purity AX fractions selectively stimulated Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus populations. The findings highlight a trade-off between particle size reduction intensity and AX structural integrity that must be managed in process design for prebiotic ingredient manufacturing.

title: Submerged fermentation of wheat bran hydrolysates for the production of ferulic acid-enriched phenolic extracts
abstract: This work explored the use of submerged fermentation (SmF) as a complementary strategy to solid-state fermentation for valorising wheat bran hydrolysates rich in ferulic acid and other hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives. Enzymatic pre-treatment with a commercial xylanase–feruloyl esterase blend was used to generate a soluble hydrolysate, which was subsequently fermented using Lactobacillus plantarum and Bacillus subtilis strains selected for their phenolic acid-releasing capacity. Fermentation conditions (pH, temperature, agitation rate) were optimised using a Box–Behnken response surface design. SmF with L. plantarum increased free ferulic acid concentration by 2.1-fold relative to the unfermented hydrolysate control, while antioxidant capacity (FRAP assay) improved by 45%. Total phenolic content was measured by Folin–Ciocalteu reagent, and individual phenolic acids were identified and quantified by HPLC-MS. Safety profiling of the fermented extracts, including determination of biogenic amine content, confirmed suitability for food-grade applications. The process demonstrated good reproducibility at 10-litre bioreactor scale, supporting further techno-economic evaluation for industrial deployment within milling facilities.

title: Valorisation of cereal milling by-products: a systematic review of fermentation-based approaches
abstract: Cereal milling generates substantial quantities of bran and other by-products that are currently underutilised in food and feed applications. Fermentation represents a cost-effective and scalable bioprocess for upgrading these streams into value-added ingredients. This systematic review consolidates findings from peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2022, covering solid-state and submerged fermentation applied to wheat, rye, oat, and maize bran. A total of 112 studies were screened and 64 included after quality assessment. Key outcomes analysed include changes in dietary fibre composition, bioactive compound release, protein enrichment, reduction of anti-nutritional factors, and functional property improvement. The review identifies consistent trends: fungal SSF is most effective for protein enrichment and ferulic acid liberation; lactic acid bacterial SmF excels at producing bioavailable phenolic fractions; combined enzymatic and microbial strategies outperform single-step approaches. Critical process variables—moisture content, inoculum load, substrate particle size, and incubation time—are mapped against output quality metrics. Gaps in the literature, including the lack of life-cycle assessment data and limited pilot-scale studies, are highlighted, and priority research directions for industrial translation are proposed.

title: Optimisation of enzyme-assisted extraction of dietary fibre from wheat bran using response surface methodology
abstract: Dietary fibre derived from wheat bran has attracted growing interest as a functional ingredient due to its established health benefits, including modulation of glycaemic response and promotion of gut microbiota diversity. This study applied response surface methodology (RSM) with a central composite design to optimise the enzyme-assisted aqueous extraction of total dietary fibre (TDF) from wheat bran. Cellulase, xylanase, and protease dosages, reaction temperature, and incubation time were selected as independent variables, with TDF yield and β-glucan content as response variables. The optimal conditions identified were: xylanase 15 U g⁻¹, protease 8 U g⁻¹, 50 °C, and 90 minutes, yielding TDF at 41.3 g per 100 g dry bran. β-Glucan content reached 4.2 g per 100 g under these conditions. The extracted fibre exhibited high water-swelling capacity and bile acid-binding ability in vitro. Comparative analysis with alkali extraction confirmed that enzyme-assisted extraction produced fibre fractions with better solubility and lower colour impact, both desirable for food ingredient application. Scale-up trials at 5-litre reactor volume confirmed RSM predictions with less than 8% deviation, indicating robust process transferability.

title: Life cycle assessment of wheat bran valorization pathways: fermentation versus conventional processing
abstract: As the food industry faces increasing pressure to reduce environmental impact while maximising resource efficiency, life cycle assessment (LCA) has become a key tool for evaluating the sustainability of alternative processing routes. This study presents a cradle-to-gate LCA comparing three wheat bran valorization scenarios: (1) conventional animal feed use, (2) alkaline extraction of dietary fibre and phenolics, and (3) sequential solid-state fermentation followed by extraction. System boundaries included milling by-product generation, pre-treatment, bioprocessing, downstream separation, and drying. Functional unit was defined as 1 kg of ingredient solids with a minimum dietary fibre content of 30% (dry weight basis). Global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, water consumption, and land use were assessed using SimaPro software and Ecoinvent 3.8 background data. Fermentation-based valorization exhibited a 31% lower global warming potential compared with alkaline processing, primarily due to reduced chemical inputs. Energy demand was the main environmental hotspot in all scenarios, highlighting the importance of heat integration. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of results across varying electricity grid mixes, which is particularly relevant to Serbia's evolving energy profile. The study provides quantitative sustainability evidence to support decision-making by both industry and policy stakeholders.

title: Functional characterisation of fermented wheat bran as a bakery ingredient: texture, colour, and shelf-life effects
abstract: Incorporating fermented wheat bran into bread and other bakery products offers a dual benefit of nutritional enrichment and waste valorization, yet the technological implications for product quality remain insufficiently characterised. This study evaluated the effect of substituting 10, 20, and 30% of wheat flour with solid-state fermented bran (produced using Aspergillus oryzae) on bread loaf volume, crumb texture, colour, and sensory attributes. Fermented bran inclusion at 20% yielded loaves with specific volume comparable to the control (2.8 mL g⁻¹) and crumb hardness within acceptable consumer limits, outperforming unfermented bran at equivalent substitution levels. Crust and crumb colour were measured by CIE L*a*b* colorimetry; fermented bran produced a slightly darker crumb but improved Maillard reaction-associated colour, which was scored positively in sensory evaluation. Shelf-life assessment over 7 days demonstrated that bread containing fermented bran exhibited reduced staling rate, attributed to the water-binding properties of modified arabinoxylan fractions. Mould-free shelf life was extended by 1.5 days relative to unfermented bran controls. Consumer acceptability testing (n = 60) indicated a preference for 20% fermented bran bread over both the control and higher-substitution variants, particularly regarding flavour and texture.

title: Pilot-scale biorefinery design for integrated recovery of protein, dietary fibre, and ferulic acid from wheat bran
abstract: A biorefinery approach enabling simultaneous recovery of multiple high-value fractions from a single agri-food by-product stream offers significant economic and environmental advantages over single-product extraction strategies. This study presents the conceptual design and experimental validation of a three-stage pilot-scale process for wheat bran valorization, integrating enzymatic hydrolysis, solid-state fermentation, and sequential extraction to co-produce a protein-enriched ingredient, an arabinoxylan-rich dietary fibre fraction, and a ferulic acid extract. Process flow was established at 50 kg bran input per batch, and mass balances were constructed for each operational stage. Protein-enriched fermented bran achieved 42 g protein per 100 g dry matter; arabinoxylan fraction purity was 78%; and ferulic acid yield was 2.1 mg g⁻¹ original dry bran. Energy consumption was measured at each stage using inline metering, and water use was quantified to support resource efficiency calculations. A simplified techno-economic analysis indicated a break-even point at approximately 200 tonnes bran processed per year for a small milling enterprise. The integrated biorefinery model outperformed individual single-product processes in terms of total economic value recovered per tonne of bran, demonstrating its viability as a business model for milling companies in the Western Balkans region.

title: Digital twins for planning the energy retrofit of school buildings
abstract: This paper presents a digital twin framework developed specifically for planning energy retrofit interventions in school buildings. The approach integrates geometric and semantic data from BIM models with real-time sensor readings and historical energy consumption records, producing a continuously updated virtual replica of each facility. The framework was validated on three primary schools in the Vojvodina region, where energy audits had identified significant thermal deficiencies in the building envelope and HVAC systems. By coupling the digital twin with dynamic thermal simulation, the study evaluated a range of retrofit scenarios—including external wall insulation, window replacement, and mechanical ventilation with heat recovery—against cost-effectiveness and energy-saving targets. Results demonstrated that the digital twin approach reduced the time required for scenario evaluation by approximately 40% compared to conventional audit-based methods. The paper also discusses data governance challenges, interoperability standards, and the integration of occupancy behaviour models into the simulation pipeline. Findings highlight the potential for scaling such frameworks to regional building stock assessments and support evidence-based decision-making for public sector energy renovation programmes.

title: From BIM to energy simulation without manual remodelling
abstract: The conversion of a BIM model into an energy simulation-ready format typically requires substantial manual intervention, introducing errors and discouraging iterative design. This paper proposes a semi-automated workflow that extracts geometric, material, and spatial data directly from an IFC-compliant BIM model and maps it to the input schema of a widely used dynamic thermal simulation engine, eliminating the need for manual remodelling. The methodology employs a rule-based parser combined with a lookup table for construction assemblies and HVAC component libraries. The workflow was tested on four public buildings of varying age and complexity, comparing simulation results with monitored energy data. Discrepancies between automated and manually prepared models were below 8% in all cases, demonstrating acceptable accuracy for early-stage design and retrofit planning. The paper identifies the key data quality issues in typical BIM deliverables that hinder full automation and proposes modelling conventions that practitioners can adopt to improve downstream interoperability. The work contributes to reducing the technical barrier between architectural modelling and building performance analysis, supporting more frequent use of simulation in practice.

title: IFC-based semantic enrichment for automated thermal zone generation in energy models
abstract: Accurate thermal zoning is a prerequisite for reliable building energy simulation, yet the manual delineation of thermal zones from BIM geometry is laborious and subjective. This paper presents an algorithm that parses IFC files to infer thermal zone boundaries automatically, using space-boundary geometry, room adjacency graphs, and occupancy classification metadata. The algorithm assigns default thermal properties and internal load profiles based on building use type, drawing from a curated Serbian national building database. The method was applied to a set of eight mixed-use public buildings, and the resulting energy models were benchmarked against models prepared by experienced energy auditors. Annual energy demand predictions agreed within 6% for heating and 9% for cooling loads. A sensitivity analysis revealed that space-boundary completeness in the source IFC file was the dominant factor affecting accuracy. The paper discusses strategies for detecting and correcting incomplete space-boundary data before processing. The proposed tool is released as an open-source plugin compatible with major BIM authoring environments, lowering the threshold for small design offices to incorporate energy simulation into their standard practice.

title: Energy performance benchmarking of public kindergartens using BIM-derived simulation models
abstract: Kindergartens represent a distinct building typology with high internal gains from occupancy and stringent ventilation requirements, yet they remain under-represented in building energy benchmarking studies. This paper develops an energy performance benchmarking methodology for kindergarten buildings, using BIM-derived simulation models as the primary data source. Thirty-two kindergartens across the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina were modelled in BIM by trained surveyors following a standardised data collection protocol. Automated workflows converted each model into an energy simulation input, and annual simulations were run to produce energy use intensity indicators for heating, cooling, domestic hot water, and lighting. Cluster analysis identified three performance archetypes based on construction period and envelope configuration. The paper quantifies the energy saving potential achievable by bringing each archetype to current regulatory standards and calculates the associated CO₂ reduction. The benchmarking database is designed to be updatable as buildings undergo retrofit, enabling longitudinal tracking of the public building stock's energy trajectory. Results are intended to support municipal authorities in prioritising renovation investments and applying for European structural fund financing.

title: Coupling digital twins with occupant feedback for adaptive energy management in administrative buildings
abstract: Digital twins of buildings are typically driven by physics-based simulation and sensor data, but rarely incorporate structured occupant feedback as a dynamic input. This paper proposes a framework that integrates an occupant comfort survey module with a real-time digital twin of an administrative building, enabling the energy management system to adapt setpoint schedules based on aggregated thermal comfort votes. The digital twin was deployed in a government office building in Novi Sad, instrumented with indoor climate sensors and a web-based comfort survey accessible to occupants on mobile devices. A model predictive control algorithm adjusted HVAC operation to minimise energy consumption while satisfying comfort constraints derived from the live feedback stream. Over a six-month monitoring campaign spanning the heating season, the system achieved a 14% reduction in heating energy compared to the previous year's baseline under comparable outdoor conditions. The paper analyses the spatial distribution of comfort complaints and identifies envelope hotspots that were subsequently targeted for insulation improvement. The study demonstrates that occupant-in-the-loop digital twins can serve both operational optimisation and retrofit prioritisation objectives simultaneously.

title: Barriers to BIM adoption for energy retrofit in the Serbian public sector: a stakeholder survey
abstract: Despite the recognised potential of building information modelling to streamline energy retrofit planning, adoption in the Serbian public sector remains limited. This paper reports findings from a structured survey of 124 stakeholders including architects, civil engineers, energy auditors, and municipal procurement officers, targeting the barriers and enablers of BIM use in publicly funded renovation projects. Responses were analysed using descriptive statistics and factor analysis, revealing five principal barrier dimensions: lack of skilled personnel, absence of regulatory mandate, high software licensing costs, fragmented project delivery chains, and insufficient guidance from national energy agencies. The survey also captures perceived benefits, with energy performance prediction and clash detection cited most frequently. Comparative analysis with similar surveys from EU member states contextualises the Serbian situation within broader Central and Eastern European patterns. The paper proposes a roadmap for BIM mandating in public renovation procurement, aligned with the Serbian Energy Efficiency Law and forthcoming EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive revisions. Recommendations address training curricula, open-source toolchain development, and pilot project structures that could accelerate uptake.

title: Parametric BIM modelling for rapid generation of energy retrofit design alternatives
abstract: Energy retrofit design involves exploring a large space of possible interventions, each with different cost, energy and embodied carbon implications. This paper presents a parametric BIM modelling approach that allows designers to generate and evaluate hundreds of retrofit alternatives within a single model environment without reconstructing geometry. Parameters controlling insulation thickness, glazing type, window-to-wall ratio adjustments, shading device geometry, and HVAC system selection are exposed through a visual scripting interface, allowing non-programmer designers to configure design of experiments tables. Each parameter combination is automatically exported to a thermal simulation engine, and results are returned to the BIM environment as colour-mapped overlays on building components. The method was applied to a 1970s-era secondary school building requiring major renovation, generating 360 design variants. Pareto-optimal solutions on the cost versus energy saving frontier were identified and presented to the client as a shortlist for detailed design. The paper discusses computational performance, model management strategies for large variant sets, and how the workflow integrates with life-cycle cost analysis modules. The approach is shown to support earlier and more informed decision-making in the retrofit design process.

title: Thermal simulation accuracy of BIM-derived models: sensitivity to construction assembly data quality
abstract: The reliability of BIM-based energy simulation depends critically on the accuracy of construction assembly data embedded in the model. This paper conducts a systematic sensitivity analysis examining how errors and omissions in thermal conductivity, layer thickness, and air gap properties of wall, roof, and floor assemblies propagate into annual heating and cooling energy predictions. A reference BIM model of a typical Serbian public office building was perturbed using a Monte Carlo approach, sampling construction property values from distributions representing realistic data quality levels encountered in practice—ranging from design specification documents to on-site thermographic surveys. Over 5,000 simulation runs were executed using the automated IFC-to-simulation workflow developed in prior work by the authors. Results indicate that wall assembly thermal resistance is the dominant uncertainty driver for heating energy, accounting for 38% of output variance, while glazing solar heat gain coefficient dominates cooling uncertainty. The paper provides practical guidance on measurement prioritisation for energy auditors seeking to maximise simulation accuracy within limited survey budgets. A data quality scoring rubric for BIM models intended for energy analysis is proposed and illustrated with case study applications.

title: A review of digital twin platforms for the built environment: capabilities, interoperability and energy use cases
abstract: Digital twin technology has attracted substantial commercial and academic interest in the built environment sector, yet the landscape of available platforms remains fragmented and difficult to navigate for practitioners. This review systematically analyses twenty-three digital twin platforms documented in peer-reviewed literature and commercial product documentation, evaluating them against a capability framework comprising geometric fidelity, sensor data integration, simulation coupling, interoperability standards support, and energy-specific analytical functions. Platforms are categorised into three tiers: geometry-centric BIM viewers with IoT connectivity, simulation-integrated operational twins, and multi-physics predictive twins. The review identifies a clear gap between the first and third tiers, with few platforms offering mature, validated links between live sensor streams and calibrated dynamic thermal simulation. Energy use cases covered include fault detection and diagnostics, demand response, retrofit planning, and regulatory compliance monitoring. The paper highlights the importance of open standards—particularly IFC, CityGML, and BRICK schema—for ensuring long-term data portability and vendor independence. Recommendations are provided for public building owners and municipalities evaluating digital twin procurement, with specific attention to the Serbian and wider Western Balkans regulatory context.

title: Pollen Grain Dimensions and Aperture Variability in Five Poaceae Species Common to Novi Sad Urban Greenways
abstract: Precise morphometric characterisation of grass pollen is relevant for aerobiological source attribution and allergy diagnostics. This study measured 18 morphological parameters on acetolysed pollen grains of five Poaceae species—Poa pratensis, Festuca rubra, Lolium perenne, Dactylis glomerata, and Arrhenatherum elatius—collected from five urban greenway sites in Novi Sad during May–June 2022. At least 50 grains per species per site were measured under light microscopy at 400× magnification using calibrated image analysis software. Polar diameter, equatorial diameter, and annulus width showed the lowest intraspecific coefficient of variation (CV < 6%), whereas pore diameter exhibited higher variability (CV up to 14%). Principal component analysis separated all five species using only four variables. Dactylis glomerata showed statistically larger pore diameters than the remaining taxa (ANOVA, p < 0.01). Results suggest that a reduced four-variable protocol can reliably distinguish these co-occurring grass taxa and may streamline morphometric workflows in routine aerobiological analysis.
