title: Scanning Electron Microscopy Characterisation of Onopordum acanthium and Carduus acanthoides Pollen: Implications for Entomophilous versus Wind Dispersal in Disturbed Vojvodina Habitats
abstract: Onopordum acanthium and Carduus acanthoides are thistles increasingly colonising disturbed peri-urban and roadside habitats in Vojvodina, where their pollen occasionally appears in aerobiological samples at low concentrations. To evaluate whether morphological features are consistent with incidental anemophily, pollen grains from herbarium vouchers and fresh collections were processed by acetolysis and examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) at 2,000–10,000× magnification. Quantitative descriptors included polar and equatorial axis lengths, exine thickness, spine height and base width, and colpus length-to-polar-axis ratio. Onopordum acanthium exhibited mean spine heights of 8.3 ± 0.9 µm, significantly longer than those of Carduus acanthoides (5.1 ± 0.7 µm; t-test, p < 0.001). Exine sculpturing in both species retained the reticulate pattern expected of insect-pollinated Asteraceae, and mass-to-surface-area estimates suggest aerodynamic properties unfavourable for sustained wind transport. These data do not support classifying either species as a significant anemophilous contributor to urban aerobiological loads.

title: Artemisia pollen morphometrics across three Vojvodina populations: does habitat type affect grain size?
abstract: Artemisia is one of the principal late-summer allergenic pollen types in the Pannonian Basin, yet intrageneric morphometric variability within Vojvodina populations is poorly documented. Pollen from three Artemisia vulgaris populations—a dry loess slope near Fruška Gora, an irrigated agricultural margin near Zrenjanin, and an urban ruderal site in Novi Sad—was collected at peak anthesis in August 2024. Following acetolysis, 60 grains per population were measured for polar diameter, equatorial diameter, exine thickness, and colpus length. One-way ANOVA indicated that polar diameter differed significantly across populations (F₂,₁₇₇ = 9.3, p < 0.001), with the loess-slope population producing the smallest grains (mean 18.4 µm) compared to the urban ruderal population (mean 20.1 µm). Soil nitrogen content, measured at each site, was positively correlated with polar grain diameter (r = 0.61). Results suggest that grain size metrics from urban aerobiological stations may not be directly transferable to rural reference pollen libraries without site-specific calibration.

title: Effect of non-uniform bed material gradation on local scour at bridge piers: laboratory investigation
abstract: Local scour at bridge piers is commonly studied using uniform sediment, yet natural gravel-bed rivers exhibit broad grain-size distributions. This paper reports 36 flume runs using four graded sediment mixtures with geometric standard deviations σg between 1.4 and 3.1 and median diameters D50 of 8 mm and 15 mm. A single circular pier of diameter 0.05 m was placed in a 10 m flume and subjected to flows with depth-to-pier diameter ratios from 2 to 6. Maximum scour depths were measured with a digital point gauge and three-dimensional bed surveys were performed with a laser distance sensor on a motorised traverse. Results show that increasing sediment non-uniformity reduces equilibrium scour depth by up to 27% relative to uniform sediment of equivalent D50, attributed to selective entrainment forming a coarse armour layer at the scour hole rim. A correction factor as a function of σg is proposed for integration with existing scour prediction formulas. The factor is validated against eight independent literature datasets.

title: Debris accumulation at bridge piers during flood events: a review of field evidence and laboratory simulations
abstract: Woody debris transported by rivers during floods frequently accumulates against bridge piers, altering the effective width of the obstruction and intensifying local scour. This chapter reviews field documentation from 14 flood events on Central European rivers recorded between 1990 and 2010, drawing on inspection reports from road authorities in Hungary, Serbia, and Romania. It then summarises laboratory studies that simulated debris accumulation using scaled wooden analogues placed at single piers in flume environments. Findings indicate that a debris raft of width equal to two pier diameters and depth equal to the approach flow depth increases maximum scour depth by 35–70% compared to the clean-pier condition, depending on porosity and submergence of the raft. The chapter discusses limitations of current predictive models, which generally treat debris as a solid rectangular body, and outlines directions for more realistic representation of raft geometry and porosity. Practical implications for inspection and bridge design are noted.

title: Horseshoe vortex dynamics at a rectangular bridge pier: ADV measurements in a laboratory flume
abstract: The horseshoe vortex system at the base of a bridge pier is the primary mechanism driving local scour. This study presents detailed three-component velocity measurements acquired with a 16 MHz acoustic Doppler velocimeter (ADV) around a rectangular pier (0.06 m × 0.12 m) in a 12 m laboratory flume with a fixed smooth bed. Measurements were taken at 63 positions in the upstream symmetry plane and lateral cross-sections at approach flow depths of 0.18 m and 0.24 m and bulk velocities of 0.32–0.58 m/s. Turbulent kinetic energy maps reveal a concentrated region of elevated TKE immediately upstream of the pier base, with peak values approximately 12 times the background level. Vortex core positions were identified from time-averaged streamlines and exhibit periodic oscillation between single-vortex and multi-vortex states at Strouhal numbers consistent with previous studies. The rectangular pier produces a stronger and more stable horseshoe vortex than an equivalent-width circular pier at the same flow conditions, partly explaining higher observed scour rates for rectangular cross-sections.

title: Scour protection using riprap collars at bridge piers in gravel-bed streams: size criteria from flume tests
abstract: Riprap collars placed around bridge piers are among the most common scour countermeasures, yet sizing criteria derived from sand-bed research may not transfer directly to gravel-bed conditions. This paper reports 52 flume experiments in which circular piers of diameter 0.05 m were protected by circular riprap collars of varying outer diameter (2–5 pier diameters) and stone size (D50 of 14–32 mm) at approach flow velocities of 0.40–0.75 m/s in a gravel bed with D50 of 9 mm. Collar performance was assessed by the degree to which equilibrium scour depth was reduced relative to unprotected pier conditions. A collar outer diameter of three pier diameters with stone D50 approximately 3.5 times the bed material D50 eliminated measureable scour in 44 out of 52 runs. Partial failure occurred in eight runs characterised by high Froude number and thinner collars. A design envelope based on the Shields parameter and collar geometry ratio is proposed. Results agree well with an independent dataset from a Slovak laboratory.

title: Influence of skew angle on scour depth at single circular piers in gravel beds
abstract: Bridge piers are frequently skewed relative to the approach flow direction due to geometric constraints, yet most scour prediction formulas assume alignment. This experimental study examines pier skew angles of 0°, 10°, 20°, and 30° for a circular pier of diameter 0.05 m in a 12 m × 0.8 m flume with a gravel bed of D50 equal to 10 mm. Thirty-two runs were conducted across four approach flow depths and two bulk velocities. Maximum scour depth, measured with the laser bed profiler, increased by 12%, 24%, and 41% relative to the aligned case at 10°, 20°, and 30° skew respectively. High-speed camera recordings of dye injections at the pier base confirm that skew displaces the horseshoe vortex laterally and creates a secondary scour hole on the downstream flank at angles above 20°. The skew correction factor recommended in existing bridge design standards underestimates observed depth increases for angles above 15° in gravel-bed conditions.

title: Combined effect of debris accumulation and pier skew on local scour: flume observations
abstract: Most studies on debris accumulation at bridge piers assume flow aligned with the pier axis, yet skewed piers are common in practice. This paper presents 40 flume experiments combining debris raft analogues with pier skew angles of 0°, 15°, and 30° at a circular pier in a gravel bed. Debris rafts were constructed from groups of wooden cylinders yielding bulk porosities of 35% and 55%. At zero skew, a 35%-porosity raft of width equal to three pier diameters increased scour depth by 58% relative to the clean pier. When the same raft was applied at 30° skew, the scour depth increase reached 89%. Interaction between the asymmetric debris raft and the skew-displaced horseshoe vortex was identified as the cause of the amplification. Three-dimensional bed surveys show that the scour hole at combined skew and debris conditions extends further downstream compared to either factor acting alone. These findings suggest that current design practice, which often treats debris and skew effects multiplicatively, overestimates scour at low skew but underestimates it above 20°.

title: Temporal evolution of scour at a bridge pier under unsteady flow hydrographs in a gravel-bed flume
abstract: Bridge scour during floods is driven by unsteady flow, yet most design methods apply peak-flow assumptions that may produce conservative or non-conservative estimates depending on hydrograph shape. This study reports 24 flume experiments using idealised triangular and asymmetric hydrographs with peak discharges producing Froude numbers of 0.45–0.65 and total durations of 40–120 minutes at laboratory scale. A circular pier of diameter 0.05 m was placed in a gravel bed with D50 of 9 mm. Bed elevation at the deepest scour point was logged every 2 minutes using the automated laser profiler. For triangular hydrographs, the maximum scour depth reached 72–81% of the equivalent steady-flow equilibrium depth at the peak discharge. Asymmetric hydrographs with a slow recession produced scour depths 9–14% deeper than those with a fast recession at identical peaks, because sediment removed during rising limb is not redeposited under slow recession. A simple empirical adjustment factor based on hydrograph rise-to-total-duration ratio is fitted to the data.

title: Scale effects in physical modelling of bridge pier scour: assessment through Froude and densimetric Froude similarity
abstract: Physical hydraulic models of bridge pier scour are typically designed using Froude number similarity, but uncertainties arise from scale effects related to viscosity, sediment transport mode, and armour layer development. This paper analyses data from 18 published laboratory datasets and 12 new experiments conducted in two flume sizes (4 m and 12 m long) at geometric scales of 1:10 and 1:20 relative to a prototype gravel-bed pier. Both the conventional Froude approach and the densimetric Froude criterion, which accounts for sediment mobility, were evaluated against measured scour depths. Across the test conditions, densimetric Froude scaling reduced the average prediction error from 22% to 11% for scour depth and from 28% to 16% for scour hole volume. Scale effects were most pronounced at low approach flow depths in the 4 m flume, where sidewall effects contributed to flow non-uniformity. Recommendations for minimum flume width-to-pier diameter ratios and sediment scaling are derived. The findings support the use of densimetric Froude similarity as the primary scaling criterion for gravel-bed scour models.

title: Debris clogging at multiple-pier bridges: flume investigation of inter-pier spacing effects on scour
abstract: Real bridges often have two or more piers in close proximity, and debris accumulation spanning adjacent piers can substantially redirect flow and concentrate scour. This experimental study used a 12 m × 0.8 m flume with pairs of circular piers at centre-to-centre spacings of 3, 5, and 8 pier diameters in a gravel bed with D50 of 10 mm. Debris analogues of three width categories were placed to span either one or both piers. At 3-diameter spacing with a full-span debris raft of low porosity (30%), maximum scour depth at the downstream side of the rear pier reached 2.4 times the clean single-pier equilibrium depth. At 8-diameter spacing, the scour increase dropped to 1.6 times. Flow velocity distributions measured with ADV at six cross-sections show that inter-pier contraction accelerates flow in the gap by up to 37% above approach velocity when full-span debris is present. Scour hole planform maps reveal merging of individual holes into a continuous trench for spacings below 4 diameters under debris conditions.

title: Gravel-bed armouring below bridge piers: grain-size evolution during scour events measured by image analysis
abstract: Armour layer formation at the periphery of scour holes modifies sediment mobility and limits the final depth of bridge pier scour. This study used image analysis of high-resolution photographs taken at fixed positions during 20 flume runs to track surface grain-size distribution changes over time in a gravel-bed channel (D50 = 11 mm, σg = 2.2). A circular pier of 0.05 m diameter was subjected to flows with Froude numbers from 0.35 to 0.58. Photographs were acquired every 10 minutes and processed with a purpose-written image analysis routine that identifies individual grains using edge detection and fits ellipses to estimate b-axis diameter. Results show that surface D50 at the scour hole rim increases by a factor of 1.8–2.4 relative to the undisturbed bed by the time equilibrium scour depth is reached. A mobility index based on local near-bed velocity and armoured D50 collapses the temporal scour depth data from all 20 runs onto a single curve with a coefficient of determination of 0.91.

title: Vulnerability of road bridges to scour during extreme floods on Pannonian Plain tributaries: inspection data synthesis
abstract: This paper synthesises post-flood inspection records from 73 road bridges on gravel-bed tributaries of the Tisa and Danube rivers in Vojvodina and the Bačka region, collected after flood events between 2006 and 2021. Inspection reports were obtained from the Roads Directorate of Serbia and municipal engineering departments. For each bridge, pier geometry, foundation depth, observed scour category (none, moderate, severe), and peak discharge estimates were recorded. Logistic regression analysis identifies relative pier width, foundation embedment depth below the theoretical scour line, and presence of woody debris in post-flood photographs as significant predictors of scour severity classification. Bridges with foundation embedment below 2.0 m over the HEC-18 predicted scour depth had a 64% probability of receiving a severe classification at peak flows exceeding a 50-year return period. The paper highlights data gaps in existing inspection programmes and proposes a standardised recording protocol for future surveys.

title: Effect of artificial debris raft porosity on scour depth at a circular bridge pier: systematic variation of constituent element geometry
abstract: Previous laboratory studies of debris accumulation at bridge piers have used debris analogues of fixed geometry, making it difficult to isolate porosity as a variable. This paper presents 45 flume experiments in which debris rafts were assembled from cylindrical wooden dowels of diameter 5, 8, and 12 mm arranged in regular arrays to produce five target bulk porosities between 25% and 65%. Raft width was fixed at three pier diameters and submergence at 80% of approach flow depth. The pier diameter was 0.05 m and the bed material D50 was 9 mm. Scour depth decreased monotonically with increasing porosity: maximum scour depth at 25% porosity was 2.06 times the clean-pier value, falling to 1.31 times at 65% porosity. A non-linear regression model relating scour amplification factor to porosity and element diameter normalised by pier diameter fits the experimental data with a root mean square error of 0.08 pier diameters. The model is shown to reproduce results from three independent datasets within 15%.

title: Comparison of empirical scour depth formulas against a compiled European gravel-bed dataset
abstract: Numerous formulas exist for predicting local scour depth at bridge piers, but their performance on European gravel-bed streams has not been systematically assessed against a unified dataset. This study assembles 198 data points from 11 laboratory studies and 14 field observations carried out in the Pannonian, Alpine, and Dinaric regions, covering pier diameters from 0.05 m to 1.8 m and median bed material diameters from 5 mm to 45 mm. Eight commonly referenced formulas, including HEC-18, Melville–Coleman, and three European variants, are evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean square error, and a bias index. The HEC-18 formula overestimates field scour depths by a mean of 31% across the dataset but underestimates in 18% of cases where debris accumulation was documented. The Melville–Coleman formula performs best among the eight, with mean absolute error of 0.21 pier diameters on field data. Recommendations are made for formula selection depending on data availability and design objective.

title: Longitudinal dispersion of a passive tracer in a channel with patchy emergent vegetation: laboratory experiments and a simple predictive model
abstract: Tracer dispersion in vegetated channels governs pollutant transport and retention times in riparian and wetland systems. Dye injection experiments were carried out in a 12 m flume with two alternating bare and vegetated patches (each 1.5 m long), using a 0.01 % rhodamine WT solution and fluorescence sensors placed at 1 m intervals downstream. Solid volume fraction of the emergent cylinder arrays was 0.015 and 0.030. Breakthrough curves were fitted using a one-dimensional advection–dispersion model with a dead-zone storage term. Longitudinal dispersion coefficients ranged from 3.1 × 10⁻⁴ m²/s in the low-density configuration to 6.8 × 10⁻⁴ m²/s in the high-density configuration, approximately 2.4 times higher than in the bare channel at the same discharge. Storage zone exchange coefficients increased with density and with mean flow velocity. A dimensionless regression model based on solid volume fraction and bulk Reynolds number predicted dispersion coefficients within ±22 % across all 28 tested runs. The results suggest that even sparse patchy vegetation substantially increases tracer retention compared with uniform bare-channel conditions.

title: Sensitivity of detention basin design volume to the choice of stationary versus non-stationary intensity–duration–frequency curves: a case study from Subotica
abstract: This study compares detention basin design volumes obtained from classical stationary IDF curves with those derived under a non-stationary framework for a 4.7 km² urban catchment in Subotica. Hourly rainfall data from 1965 to 2022 were used to construct both stationary GEV-based IDF curves and time-covariate GAMLSS-based non-stationary IDF curves for return periods of 5, 10, 25, and 100 years. The urban drainage network was modelled in SWMM 5.1 using surveyed pipe dimensions and land-use data from the municipal GIS database. Design storm hydrographs were routed through the network to size a hypothetical online detention basin at the catchment outlet for a target 5% annual exceedance probability. The required storage volume under the non-stationary IDF curves at the 2022 time slice was 8–14% larger than under the stationary curves across the tested storm durations. Uncertainty bounds on the non-stationary estimates were wide, indicating that ensemble-based approaches are warranted before their direct adoption in design standards. The study discusses implications for the revision of the Serbian technical regulation on urban drainage.

title: A risk-based framework for evaluating retrofit options for existing urban stormwater retention ponds under projected rainfall intensification
abstract: Ageing urban retention ponds designed to pre-1990 standards may offer insufficient flood attenuation under projected increases in short-duration rainfall extremes. This paper presents a risk-based evaluation framework that combines non-stationary rainfall frequency analysis, continuous SWMM simulation, and expected annual damage estimation to rank four retrofit options for a retention pond serving a mixed-use catchment of 2.1 km² in northern Serbia. Options considered include: outlet structure modification, pond volume expansion by 20%, a supplementary upstream infiltration trench, and a green roof programme covering 15% of impervious area. Monte Carlo sampling of non-stationary GEV parameters—propagated from a 58-year record—was used to represent uncertainty in future design storms. Over a 30-year appraisal horizon, outlet modification and volume expansion reduced expected annual flood damage by 31% and 44% respectively, while the infiltration trench yielded a 19% reduction at lower cost. The green roof programme performed best on a cost-per-unit-risk-reduction basis under median projections but was highly sensitive to assumed maintenance effectiveness. The framework is structured to accommodate updated regional climate projections as they become available.

title: Scheduling a job shop of 3D printers with build-plate nesting
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of scheduling a job shop composed exclusively of fused-deposition-modelling 3D printers, where the classical job-shop makespan objective is compounded by the geometric build-plate nesting sub-problem. Each machine cycle can simultaneously process multiple parts provided their two-dimensional footprints fit within the printer's build plate, creating a bin-packing dependency that couples assignment and sequencing decisions. A mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation is presented that captures nesting feasibility through an area-relaxation surrogate and a set of no-overlap constraints derived from rectangular bounding boxes. Because exact solution becomes intractable for instances exceeding twelve jobs, a two-phase metaheuristic is proposed: an iterated greedy algorithm first generates job sequences, then a first-fit-decreasing heuristic packs each resulting batch. Computational experiments on a benchmark set of 120 instances show the hybrid approach achieves solutions within 4.2 % of the MILP optimum on small instances and reduces makespan by up to 23 % compared to a first-come-first-served baseline on large instances. A case study conducted at a prototyping facility in Vojvodina further validates practical applicability, demonstrating a 17 % throughput improvement after policy adoption.

title: OEE decomposition and root-cause mapping in a multi-stage automotive assembly job shop
abstract: Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) is widely adopted as a key performance indicator in lean manufacturing, yet its standard three-factor decomposition into availability, performance, and quality often masks the interdependencies between successive workstations in a job shop. This paper proposes an extended OEE framework that incorporates blocking and starving losses arising from buffer constraints between sequential operations. A directed-graph model of the production line is constructed from time-study data, and a simulation-based root-cause attribution algorithm assigns throughput losses to specific stations and shift patterns. The methodology is validated on a multi-stage automotive subassembly facility near Novi Sad comprising eleven workstations and three product families. Results demonstrate that conventional single-station OEE overestimates true system efficiency by an average of 8.6 percentage points and misattributes up to 34 % of availability losses to downstream rather than upstream causes. The proposed decomposition provides production managers with actionable targets, and a prioritized improvement roadmap generated by the framework led to a 12 % OEE gain over a six-month pilot period.

title: A discrete-event simulation framework for evaluating lean tool combinations in small-batch job shops
abstract: Lean manufacturing tools such as 5S, SMED, kanban, and visual management are frequently implemented in isolation, yet their interactions in small-batch job shop environments can be synergistic or antagonistic depending on product mix variability and routing flexibility. This paper presents a discrete-event simulation (DES) framework that systematically evaluates combinations of up to five lean interventions across a configurable job shop model parameterized by the number of machine centres, job routing complexity, and demand coefficient of variation. A full factorial design of experiments covering 64 lean-tool configurations is executed within the DES environment, with makespan, WIP inventory, and OEE as response variables. Analysis of variance reveals significant two-way interactions between SMED and kanban under high-mix conditions, and between 5S adherence scores and unplanned downtime rates. Guidelines for lean tool sequencing are derived and expressed as a decision tree that practitioners can apply based on easily observable shop-floor metrics. The framework is illustrated through application to a metal fabrication job shop producing customized HVAC components.

title: Minimizing total weighted tardiness in flexible job shops with sequence-dependent setup times: a hybrid genetic algorithm approach
abstract: The flexible job shop scheduling problem with sequence-dependent setup times (FJSP-SDST) is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem of high industrial relevance, particularly in make-to-order manufacturing where customer due-date adherence directly affects contractual penalties. This paper formulates the FJSP-SDST as a multi-objective problem targeting total weighted tardiness and machine utilization balance, and proposes a hybrid genetic algorithm (HGA) that integrates a greedy insertion heuristic for initialization, an adaptive crossover operator that preserves machine-assignment building blocks, and a local search phase based on critical-path shifting. The algorithm is benchmarked against published results on the Brandimarte and Hurink standard instances, achieving best-known solutions on 71 % of benchmark cases and improving 14 previously reported bounds. A sensitivity analysis on population size, crossover rate, and local search depth provides practical tuning guidance. Industrial validation is carried out on a woodworking job shop with nine machine centres and 47 recurring job types, where the HGA reduced average tardiness by 31 % compared to the existing dispatching rule-based scheduler.

title: Integrating value stream mapping and simulation for production planning improvement: a case study in the furniture industry
abstract: Value stream mapping (VSM) is a foundational lean tool for visualizing material and information flows, but its static nature limits its ability to quantify the dynamic effects of proposed improvements on production scheduling performance. This paper presents an integrated methodology in which a current-state VSM is translated into a parameterized discrete-event simulation model, enabling quantitative assessment of future-state scenarios before physical implementation. The translation procedure defines mapping rules for converting VSM symbols into simulation constructs including process blocks, inventory buffers, push and pull triggers, and operator resource pools. The methodology is applied to a medium-sized furniture manufacturer in the Vojvodina region that produces semi-customized upholstered items in a hybrid push-pull job shop. Four future-state scenarios combining supermarket pull, pitch increment adjustment, and load leveling (heijunka) are evaluated. Simulation results indicate that a combined supermarket-pull and heijunka scenario reduces average lead time by 38 % and WIP by 44 % while maintaining OEE above the baseline level. The integrated approach provides a structured decision-support tool for production planning managers considering lean transformation investments.
venue: International Journal of Lean and Industrial Engineering

title: Reactive rescheduling strategies for job shops under stochastic machine breakdowns: a rolling-horizon evaluation
abstract: Production schedules in real job shop environments are continuously disrupted by unplanned machine failures, and the choice of reactive rescheduling strategy profoundly affects both schedule stability and efficiency recovery speed. This paper evaluates four reactive strategies—right-shift, partial rescheduling, complete rescheduling, and a predictive-reactive hybrid—within a rolling-horizon simulation framework driven by empirical breakdown distributions collected from a plastics processing facility. Performance is assessed across three dimensions: makespan deviation from the proactive baseline, schedule nervousness measured by job sequence disruption index, and OEE of individual machine centres during recovery windows. Experimental results show that partial rescheduling with a stability weight of 0.4 achieves the best trade-off between efficiency and nervousness across all tested utilization levels. The predictive-reactive hybrid outperforms pure reactive strategies when mean time between failures exceeds 180 minutes but incurs higher computational overhead. A decision framework mapping machine criticality and MTBF ranges to recommended strategies is provided, offering practical guidance for production planners in discrete manufacturing environments.
venue: Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Intelligent Manufacturing and Automation

title: Production scheduling in Industry 4.0 environments: challenges, methods and research directions
abstract: The proliferation of cyber-physical systems, industrial IoT sensors, and digital twins in manufacturing has substantially altered the data landscape available to production schedulers, yet classical scheduling theory has only partially adapted to exploit these new capabilities. This book chapter provides a structured review of production scheduling research conducted in Industry 4.0 contexts, classifying contributions along three axes: the information richness exploited (real-time machine state, energy prices, supplier lead times), the algorithmic paradigm employed (exact methods, metaheuristics, machine learning, simulation-optimization), and the shop configuration addressed (flow shop, job shop, open shop, hybrid). Particular attention is given to dynamic and predictive-reactive scheduling approaches that leverage continuous sensor streams to update schedules in near-real time. The chapter identifies six open research challenges including data quality management, interpretability of learned scheduling policies, scalability of digital twin-based optimization, and human-scheduler interaction design. Recommendations for industrial implementation are structured around a maturity model that helps manufacturers assess their readiness to adopt advanced scheduling technologies aligned with lean and OEE improvement goals.
venue: Advances in Industrial Engineering and Smart Manufacturing, Springer

title: Benchmarking dispatching rules for multi-objective job shop scheduling under variable demand arrival rates
abstract: Dispatching rules remain the most widely deployed scheduling mechanism in industrial job shops due to their low computational overhead and ease of implementation, yet systematic benchmarking across multi-objective performance landscapes and realistic demand patterns is scarce. This paper conducts a large-scale computational study comparing twenty-two dispatching rules—including SPT, WSPT, EDD, CR, MOD, and six composite rules—across a factorial experiment spanning four job shop sizes, three machine utilization levels, four demand arrival distributions, and three objective weighting schemes covering makespan, mean flow time, and total weighted tardiness. Over 18 000 scheduling episodes are simulated using an event-driven simulator implemented in Python. Results reveal that no single rule dominates across all conditions; however, COVERT-based rules consistently perform within 6 % of the best rule across 84 % of tested scenarios. A classification tree model trained on shop-state features accurately predicts the best-performing rule with 79 % accuracy, forming the basis of a lightweight adaptive dispatching policy. Implications for production planning practice and directions for reinforcement-learning-based rule selection are discussed.
venue: European Journal of Industrial Engineering and Operations

title: A Metamodel for Compositional Enterprise Integration Patterns
abstract: Enterprise integration patterns (EIPs) are widely used as building blocks in message-oriented middleware, yet no formally grounded metamodel existed that captured their compositional semantics. This paper proposes a UML-profile-based metamodel covering 47 patterns drawn from canonical pattern catalogues, extended with OCL constraints that encode valid composition rules. The metamodel was validated against six open-source integration projects by manually mapping their routing logic to the proposed meta-level; conformance was measured at 89% of constructs successfully represented. A comparison with two earlier informal taxonomies shows that the proposed approach catches eight categories of composition error that the informal approaches do not distinguish. The work provides a foundation for automated tooling that checks integration model well-formedness before deployment.

title: Formal Verification of Message-Routing Compositions Using Alloy
abstract: Routing logic in enterprise integration systems can exhibit subtle deadlocks and message-loss faults that surface only under specific load conditions. This paper encodes a subset of EIP routing patterns—splitter, aggregator, content-based router, and filter—as Alloy signatures and predicates, allowing exhaustive bounded-scope analysis. Seventeen integration scenarios derived from production healthcare data-exchange systems were modelled; the Alloy Analyzer found counterexamples in four scenarios within scopes up to size 8, two of which were confirmed as real faults in the reference implementations. The encoding approach is described in sufficient detail to be reproducible, and the full Alloy models are provided as supplementary material. Execution times on a standard workstation ranged from 1.2 seconds to 47 minutes depending on scope and constraint density.

title: Survey of Model Transformation Approaches for Integration Architecture Migration
abstract: Legacy integration architectures are frequently migrated to service-oriented or event-driven platforms, yet the model transformation techniques employed are rarely compared systematically. This survey analyses 63 peer-reviewed papers published between 2003 and 2012 that describe transformation-based migration approaches. Papers are classified along five dimensions: source and target architectural style, transformation language used, degree of automation, evaluation method, and domain of application. ATL and QVT-Relations account for 54% of the surveyed approaches combined. Only 19 of the 63 papers report quantitative evaluation with more than one industrial case. The survey identifies gaps in traceability preservation and in handling of non-functional constraints during transformation, and proposes a research agenda for the subsequent five years. A replication package including the classification spreadsheet is available.
venue: ACM Computing Surveys in Software and Systems

title: Interface Contract Specification for Event-Driven Microservices Using a Formal Pattern Language
abstract: Microservice architectures that rely on asynchronous messaging lack a standardised means of expressing interface contracts that go beyond data schema. This paper introduces a formal pattern language, denoted IPL-EDA, in which each interface contract specifies permitted message sequences, routing obligations, and timing constraints using a combination of regular expressions over message types and linear temporal logic formulae. IPL-EDA contracts are expressed as annotations on a service's OpenAPI-style description and checked automatically using a prototype contract verifier. An evaluation against a synthetic benchmark of 120 service pairs and a real logistics platform with 14 services shows that the verifier detects 91% of injected contract violations with a false-positive rate of 3.2%. Annotation overhead averages 38 additional lines per service description.

title: Towards a Formal Semantics for the Saga Pattern in Distributed Transaction Management
abstract: The Saga pattern decomposes a distributed transaction into a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions, but existing descriptions in the literature are informal and implementation-dependent. This paper gives a formal operational semantics for Sagas using labelled transition systems, covering both choreography-based and orchestration-based variants. Fifteen Saga implementations taken from open-source repositories were encoded in the formal model; model checking with SPIN revealed two previously unreported scenarios in which compensating actions could be skipped under concurrent failure. The formalisation also clarifies the relationship between Sagas and the classical two-phase commit protocol, showing that two-phase commit is a degenerate Saga under additional locking assumptions. The paper is intended as groundwork for future tool support rather than an industrial deployment guide.

title: Model-Driven Configuration of API Gateways from Architectural Intent
abstract: API gateway products such as reverse proxies and service meshes require extensive low-level configuration that must remain consistent with a system's intended integration architecture. This paper proposes a two-layer approach: an architecture-level model expressed in a lightweight DSL captures routing intent, authentication boundaries, and rate-limiting policies; a set of ATL transformations then generates gateway-specific configuration files for two target platforms. An evaluation conducted on a medium-sized e-commerce platform with 31 services compared manually written configuration with generated configuration on seven quality criteria. Generated configuration had fewer inconsistencies (4 vs. 19) and reduced configuration size by 28% on average through deduplication of repeated policy blocks. Round-trip regeneration after architectural change took under 90 seconds for the largest tested model.

title: Consistency Checking Between Architectural Models and Runtime Integration Behaviour
abstract: Architectural drift—the divergence between a documented software architecture and the system as actually deployed—is a common maintenance problem. This paper addresses drift detection in integration-heavy systems by instrumenting message brokers to capture runtime message-flow graphs and comparing them against the architectural intent model using a graph-homomorphism-based matching algorithm. The approach was evaluated on two industrial systems: a logistics information platform and a public-sector document-exchange infrastructure. In the logistics system, 11 undocumented message paths and three deprecated routes still receiving traffic were detected automatically within a 72-hour observation window. Precision was 94% and recall 88% relative to manually verified ground truth. The paper also discusses how detected deviations can be fed back to update the architectural model semi-automatically.

title: Interface Adaptation Strategies for Heterogeneous IoT Device Integration: A Model-Driven Study
abstract: Industrial IoT deployments regularly combine devices that communicate over incompatible protocols—MQTT, CoAP, Modbus, and proprietary serial formats are common simultaneously. This paper applies the model-driven adapter generation framework developed in earlier work to IoT device integration, extending the original finite-state-machine interface model with data-type coercion rules and timing constraints specific to sensor data streams. Twelve device pairs from a smart-factory pilot in Vojvodina were used as test cases; nine generated adapters functioned correctly without modification, two required minor timing adjustments, and one could not be handled due to a stateful proprietary protocol. Adapter round-trip latency overhead was measured at 1.8 ms median on a Raspberry Pi 4, which was acceptable for all non-real-time use cases in the pilot.

title: Specification and Automated Verification of Choreography Contracts in Event-Driven Systems: Lessons from Three Industrial Cases
abstract: Choreography-level contracts define the observable interaction obligations of multiple participants in a distributed system without centralising control. This paper reports on the application of a contract specification language based on multiparty session types to three real industrial systems: a regional healthcare interoperability platform, a customs document exchange service, and a retail supply-chain event bus. For each system, existing informal specifications were re-expressed as session-typed choreographies and checked for well-formedness and progress guarantees. The process uncovered two liveness violations in the healthcare system and one safety violation in the customs system that had manifested as intermittent timeout errors in production. The paper discusses the practical friction involved in eliciting the information needed for formal specification from integration teams unfamiliar with formal methods, and proposes a lightweight elicitation protocol.

title: Occlusion-Aware LOD Transitions Without Popping Artefacts Using Temporal Blending in WebGPU
abstract: Abrupt LOD transitions produce visible popping artefacts that degrade user experience in 3D web applications, particularly during camera motion. This paper proposes a temporal blending strategy in which the outgoing and incoming LOD meshes are both rendered for a short overlap window and their contributions linearly interpolated using a per-pixel alpha accumulated in a history buffer. The approach is implemented entirely in WebGPU using a two-attachment render pass and a resolve compute pass. Five transition scenarios were tested: flyover, close approach, lateral pan, static scene with dynamic lighting, and object rotation. A 28-participant study comparing temporal blending with three alternative anti-popping methods (alpha testing, morphing via vertex attributes, dithered cross-fade) found that temporal blending received the highest fidelity ratings in three of five scenarios. Frame overhead of the resolve pass was 0.9 ms at 1920×1080 on a mid-range discrete GPU. Limitations under rapid camera motion and high polygon-count transitions are discussed.

title: Benchmarking Embedded Lossy Compressors for Structural Health Monitoring on a 32-Node Piezoelectric Sensor Array
abstract: Structural health monitoring of bridges and tunnels increasingly relies on dense piezoelectric sensor arrays generating sustained data rates of hundreds of kilobytes per second. This paper benchmarks seven embedded lossy compressors — including DPCM, adaptive PLA, Haar filterbank, spectral peak preservation, and three variants of learned vector quantisation — on a 32-node wireless array deployed on a pedestrian footbridge in Novi Sad over four weeks. Evaluation metrics include compression ratio, reconstruction SNR, preservation of guided-wave arrival time picks (used for damage localisation), and energy per sample. The learned vector quantiser with 256-centroid codebook trained offline on historical data achieved the best damage-localisation accuracy (mean error 4.8 cm at 8:1 compression) but required 24 kB of flash for the codebook. Adaptive PLA achieved competitive localisation accuracy (mean error 6.1 cm) with only 2.1 kB of code and data memory. Practical trade-off recommendations are given for deployment scenarios constrained by either memory or localisation precision requirements.

title: Latency-Bounded VNF Placement Under Fluctuating Traffic in Regional ISP Networks
abstract: Meeting end-to-end latency budgets for latency-sensitive VNF chains in regional ISP networks requires placement decisions that account for traffic variability. This paper proposes a two-stage stochastic programming model where the first stage determines VNF-to-server assignment and the second stage routes traffic across scenarios sampled from a 30-day flow-level measurement trace collected from a mid-sized Serbian ISP with 22 PoPs. Scenarios are reduced to 50 representative samples using k-medoids clustering on traffic matrices. The stochastic model is compared against a deterministic peak-load formulation and a reactive re-placement heuristic. The stochastic approach reduces constraint violations by 37% versus deterministic placement under median traffic conditions while using 12% fewer server resources. The paper characterises which VNF types (firewall, DPI, NAT) are most sensitive to traffic variability and recommends placement policies for each.

title: Detecting Implicit Dependencies Introduced by Code Generators in Polyglot Build Pipelines
abstract: Code generation steps—protocol buffer compilation, OpenAPI client generation, lexer/parser generation—introduce implicit dependencies that are absent from hand-written BUILD files. If these are not recorded, incremental build systems may silently produce stale artifacts. We present a dynamic tracing approach that intercepts file-system calls during a full build to discover implicit edges, then infers a static approximation using file naming conventions and generator invocation patterns. Applied to eleven repositories using at least two distinct code generators each, the tracing step uncovered a median of 47 undeclared edges per repository. We evaluated whether the static approximation, computed without tracing, could recover these edges, achieving an F1 score of 0.84 averaged across repositories. Cases where the static approach failed are categorised and used to motivate three proposed BUILD file annotations that would make implicit dependencies machine-readable.

title: Deflagration index determination for wood pellet dust using a 20-litre sphere: effect of moisture content and particle size distribution
abstract: Kst and Pmax values were measured for wood pellet dust samples obtained from three pellet production facilities in Vojvodina. Samples were sieved to five fractions between 63 µm and 500 µm and conditioned to moisture contents of 4%, 8%, and 12%. Tests followed the EN 14034 protocol using a 20-litre Siwek sphere with chemical ignitors of 2 kJ and 10 kJ. Results showed Kst ranging from 41 bar·m/s for the coarsest fraction at 12% moisture to 112 bar·m/s for the finest fraction at 4% moisture. Pmax varied between 6.8 and 8.3 bar. A regression model linking median particle diameter and moisture content to Kst was fitted with R² = 0.87. The data indicate that moisture reduction during summer storage significantly elevates explosion severity and that particle segregation in hoppers can produce locally hazardous fractions not represented by bulk sampling.

title: Minimum ignition energy of sunflower husk dust under variable humidity and turbulence conditions
abstract: Minimum ignition energy (MIE) was measured for sunflower husk dust using a Hartmann tube apparatus combined with a capacitive spark discharge system. Dust concentrations from 250 to 1500 g/m³ were tested at relative humidities of 30%, 50%, and 70%, and at two turbulence delay intervals of 60 ms and 120 ms. MIE ranged from 11 mJ at 30% RH to over 200 mJ at 70% RH for the optimal concentration of approximately 750 g/m³. The 60 ms delay produced consistently lower MIE values, confirming greater ignitability at higher suspension turbulence. Comparison with published data for wheat flour and maize starch shows sunflower husk dust to be less sensitive but still falls within the St 1 explosion class. The results have direct implications for grounding and bonding requirements at sunflower processing plants in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina.

title: Explosion vent sizing for silo bins handling torrefied wood pellets: comparison of EN 14491 and VDI 3673 approaches
abstract: Cylindrical steel silo bins with L/D ratios of 1.5, 3.0, and 5.0 were modelled for explosion vent sizing using two established methods: EN 14491:2012 and VDI 3673 Part 1 (2002 edition). Input explosion parameters for torrefied wood pellets were taken from experimental characterisation: Kst = 148 bar·m/s and Pmax = 8.9 bar, obtained with 10 kJ ignitors in a 20-litre sphere. Vent areas predicted by EN 14491 were 12 to 23% larger than those from VDI 3673 across the range of vessel volumes from 10 to 200 m³, with the divergence increasing at higher L/D ratios. The static activation pressure of the vent panel was varied between 0.1 and 0.5 bar to assess sensitivity. Required vent areas at 0.1 bar activation exceeded those at 0.5 bar by a factor of up to 1.8. Guidance is offered for selecting the more conservative method in facilities lacking suppression systems.

title: Hybrid mixture explosion behaviour of methane–wood dust combinations at sub-LEL methane concentrations
abstract: Experiments were conducted in a 20-litre sphere to quantify the change in explosion severity when wood pellet dust is suspended in atmospheres containing methane at 10%, 20%, 30%, and 50% of its lower explosive limit (LEL = 5 vol%). Wood dust concentrations ranged from 125 to 1000 g/m³. At 50% LEL methane, Kst increased by up to 38% compared to the dust-only baseline and Pmax increased by 0.6 bar on average. At 10% LEL methane, statistically significant increases in Kst were still observed at dust concentrations below 250 g/m³, a range where the dust alone would not sustain propagation. The findings confirm that sub-LEL methane cannot be disregarded in risk assessments for pellet facilities co-located with biogas infrastructure. A correction factor applicable to EN 14491 vent area calculations for such hybrid scenarios is proposed and validated against two additional datasets from the literature.

title: Explosion risk zoning in a biomass pellet warehouse: field measurements and ATEX area classification
abstract: A risk zoning survey was carried out in an operational pellet warehouse with a floor area of 4 200 m² and roof height of 12 m in the Srem district. Airborne dust concentrations were measured at 48 fixed points during loading, unloading, and idle periods using isokinetic sampling and gravimetric analysis. Peak concentrations of 320 g/m³ were recorded at the belt conveyor transfer points during unloading. Time-averaged concentrations at floor level remained below the minimum explosible concentration of 60 g/m³ during idle periods. ATEX Zone 20, 21, and 22 boundaries were delineated based on the measurement campaign and frequency analysis. Ignition source identification identified eleven categories of potential ignition in the facility, of which friction from belt misalignment and electrostatic discharge from the conveyor were rated highest. Recommendations for ATEX-compliant equipment selection and housekeeping procedures are included.

title: Effect of pellet fines content on explosion propagation velocity in a horizontal duct connected to a vented vessel
abstract: A steel duct of 0.2 m internal diameter and 6 m length was connected to a 1 m³ cylindrical vessel fitted with a rupture disc vent. Wood pellet dust with fines fractions (< 63 µm) of 5%, 15%, 30%, and 50% by mass was dispersed at 500 g/m³ using a compressed air injection system. Flame arrival times were recorded by seven ionisation probes along the duct. At 5% fines, flame did not propagate beyond 2 m from the vessel. At 50% fines, sustained propagation to the duct exit was observed in 7 of 10 trials, with a maximum mean flame velocity of 78 m/s at the 4 m probe. Overpressure in the connected duct reached 0.35 bar at 50% fines compared to 0.04 bar at 5% fines. The results indicate that fines content thresholds in quality standards for pellets have a direct bearing on secondary explosion risk in conveying systems.

title: Thermal stability and self-ignition temperature of agglomerated biomass dusts from pelletising operations
abstract: The Grewer oven method and BAM oven test were applied to characterise the thermal stability of dust layers and bulk deposits from four biomass feedstocks: wood, miscanthus, wheat straw, and sunflower husk. Layer ignition temperatures at 5 mm depth ranged from 218°C for miscanthus to 267°C for wheat straw. Bulk self-ignition temperatures for 1-litre samples ranged from 172°C to 204°C. Differential scanning calorimetry was used to identify exothermic onset temperatures, which correlated with the lignin and extractive content of each feedstock rather than with ash content. An empirical relationship between onset temperature and layer ignition temperature was found with R² = 0.91 across the four materials. The data suggest that hot surface ignition limits specified in ATEX equipment categories should account for deposit thickness in pellet storage, where layers up to 20 mm accumulate on structural surfaces over days of operation.

title: Comparative Kst characterisation of corn stover, miscanthus, and switchgrass dusts: influence of harvesting season and pre-treatment
abstract: Kst and Pmax values were determined for dusts derived from three energy grasses at two harvesting seasons (autumn and late winter) and two pre-treatment conditions (raw and steam-exploded). Tests followed EN 14034-1/2 in a 20-litre sphere with 10 kJ ignition energy. Kst values for raw autumn samples ranged from 58 bar·m/s (switchgrass) to 94 bar·m/s (corn stover). Steam explosion consistently raised Kst by 15 to 28%, attributed to increased fine fraction generation confirmed by laser diffraction sizing. Late winter harvesting produced slightly lower Kst in all three crops, possibly due to reduced sugar content after cold conditioning. The study provides explosion data for crops being evaluated for co-firing at Serbian and regional power utilities, where such characterisation data are currently absent from the literature.

title: Suppressed explosion pressure in hybrid wood dust–propane mixtures: effect of sodium bicarbonate suppression agent concentration
abstract: Suppressed explosion tests were carried out in a 20-litre sphere for wood pellet dust at 500 g/m³ combined with propane at 30% and 60% LEL. Sodium bicarbonate was injected at concentrations from 50 to 400 g/m³ using a secondary dispenser triggered 10 ms before the ignitor. Unsuppressed Pmax for the 60% LEL hybrid was 9.4 bar compared to 8.2 bar for dust alone. At 300 g/m³ sodium bicarbonate, suppressed pressure dropped to 4.1 bar for the 60% LEL hybrid and 3.3 bar for the dust-only case under identical dust loading. Higher propane content required proportionally more suppressant to achieve equivalent pressure reduction. A linear model relating suppressant concentration to residual pressure ratio was fitted separately for each propane level. The results can inform the specification of suppression system activation thresholds in facilities where propane is used for pellet drying.

title: Influence of turbulence intensity on Kst measurement in the 20-litre sphere: correction procedure for biomass dusts with high moisture affinity
abstract: Systematic over-estimation of Kst in the 20-litre sphere has been reported for hygroscopic dusts when ambient humidity during testing is not controlled. This study quantified the turbulence decay between dust injection and igniter activation for wood pellet dust, wheat straw dust, and miscanthus dust using high-speed particle image velocimetry adapted for the sphere geometry. Root-mean-square velocity at the sphere centre was 4.2 m/s at 60 ms and 2.1 m/s at 120 ms delay for the standard 2-bar injection pressure. Increasing injection pressure to 3 bar to overcome agglomeration in high-moisture wood pellet dust raised turbulence intensity by 31% at 60 ms, inflating Kst by an average of 18% relative to the 2-bar result. A correction factor based on measured turbulence intensity and initial pressure is proposed and validated against independent tests at a partner laboratory using a 1 m³ vessel.

title: Explosion hazard assessment of a pellet district heating plant: integration of consequence modelling and risk matrix
abstract: A quantitative explosion hazard assessment was performed for a district heating plant firing wood pellets with an annual throughput of 8 000 tonnes. The facility layout included a day-silo of 120 m³, two screw conveyors, a day-hopper of 3 m³, and two 600 kW boilers. Kst and Pmax data measured for the plant's own pellet supply were used as inputs. PHAST and in-house spreadsheet tools were used to estimate overpressure contours for credible explosion scenarios in the day-silo, with vent areas sized per EN 14491 for Pred = 0.2 bar. Consequence analysis showed that fragment throw from an unvented silo explosion would exceed 50 m with a peak overpressure of 0.3 bar at the property boundary. Risk matrix scoring placed the unvented scenario in the intolerable region. After venting design, the residual risk was reduced to the ALARP region. The integrated method is offered as a template for municipal energy planners commissioning similar facilities.

title: Explosibility screening of refuse-derived fuel pellets blended with biomass: Kst, Pmax, and MIE data for regulatory classification
abstract: Refuse-derived fuel (RDF) pellets blended with 20%, 40%, and 60% wood biomass by mass were characterised for explosion parameters to support permitting under Serbian national fire and explosion protection regulations. Samples were milled to a d50 of approximately 100 µm before testing. Kst for pure RDF dust was 31 bar·m/s, rising to 78 bar·m/s at 60% biomass blend; Pmax increased from 7.1 to 8.6 bar over the same range. MIE for pure RDF exceeded 1 000 mJ, falling to 68 mJ at 60% biomass. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated that the chlorinated plastic fraction in RDF suppressed flame propagation at low blend ratios, consistent with the low Kst measured. All blends with more than 30% biomass exhibited MIE values below 100 mJ, placing them in the electrostatically sensitive category under EN 13237. The data fill a gap relevant to co-processing RDF in biomass-certified heating facilities.

title: Vent duct flow resistance and its effect on reduced explosion pressure in a pellet bucket elevator: experimental and CFD study
abstract: Bucket elevators are among the most frequently involved equipment in grain and biomass facility explosions yet are often fitted with vent ducts that introduce significant flow resistance. Reduced explosion pressure Pred was measured in a 0.8 m³ laboratory elevator casing fitted with vent ducts of 0, 1, 2, and 4 m length at activation pressures of 0.1 and 0.2 bar. Wood pellet dust at 500 g/m³ was used throughout. Pred increased from 0.38 bar with no duct to 0.91 bar with a 4 m duct at 0.1 bar activation, a factor of 2.4. CFD simulations in OpenFOAM using a combustion model calibrated to the measured Kst reproduced the trend within 12% across all duct length cases. A correction to EN 14491 Appendix C duct resistance formulae is proposed that reduces mean error from 21% to 8% for the tested configuration. Results indicate that current code provisions underestimate Pred for duct lengths above 2 m in elevator-scale vessels.

title: Benchmarking Declared GWP Values in Serbian Construction Product EPDs Against European Programme Averages: 2015–2024
abstract: As the number of published Environmental Product Declarations for Serbian construction products has grown from fewer than ten in 2015 to approximately 60 by 2024, it has become possible to conduct a first benchmarking analysis of declared environmental performance against European programme averages. This preprint compiles and harmonises declared GWP100 values from 58 valid Serbian EPDs across seven product categories: cement, ready-mix concrete, fired clay brick, AAC block, ceramic floor tile, mineral wool, and expanded polystyrene. Harmonisation accounted for differences in functional unit, system boundary, and characterisation method. Serbian cement EPDs declared an average GWP of 847 kg CO2-eq per tonne of CEM I 42.5, 12% above the European EPD programme average, driven by higher clinker-to-cement ratios. Ceramic tile and EPS values were within 5% of European averages. The dataset is shared openly to support sector-level decarbonisation target setting and policy development by the Serbian Chamber of Construction Engineers. Peer review is ongoing.

title: Comparative Analysis of Passive and Active Power Factor Correction Methods for Low-Power LED Drivers
abstract: This paper presents a systematic comparison of passive valley-fill circuits and active boost-based power factor correction (PFC) stages for LED driver applications in the 10–40 W power range. Six prototype circuits were assembled and tested under resistive-equivalent LED load conditions using a programmable AC source set to 230 V / 50 Hz. Power factor, total harmonic distortion of input current (THDi), and efficiency were measured at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of rated load. Active PFC achieved power factors above 0.97 and THDi below 8% across the entire load range, while passive solutions peaked at 0.82 power factor with THDi reaching 32% at partial load. Thermal imaging confirmed that the active topology imposed an additional 3–4 °C junction temperature rise in the switching transistor relative to the passive counterpart at full load. The results provide a quantitative basis for selecting between topologies under IEC 61000-3-2 Class C constraints.

title: Design and Implementation of a Single-Stage Flyback Converter with Integrated PFC for 25 W LED Street Lighting
abstract: A single-stage flyback converter combining power factor correction and output regulation in a single magnetic structure is designed, built, and evaluated for a 25 W LED street-lighting module. The converter operates in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) at a fixed switching frequency of 65 kHz, which naturally shapes the input current waveform toward sinusoidal profile without a separate PFC pre-stage. The prototype was tested from 195 V to 265 V AC input, yielding a power factor between 0.93 and 0.96 and a THDi between 11% and 15% across the input voltage range. Output current ripple was maintained below 5% peak-to-peak under worst-case conditions. Efficiency at nominal input reached 87.3%. Startup inrush current was limited to 18 A by an NTC thermistor. Conducted electromagnetic interference was measured and found to comply with CISPR 15 Class B limits after a two-stage differential-mode filter was added. Component stress analysis and a loss breakdown are included.

title: Bridgeless Totem-Pole PFC Rectifier for High-Efficiency LED Driver Applications at 150 W
abstract: This paper describes the design, simulation, and experimental verification of a bridgeless totem-pole power factor correction rectifier intended for 150 W LED drivers used in indoor luminaires. The topology eliminates the full-bridge diode rectifier, reducing conduction losses by approximately 1.2 W at rated current. Two GaN enhancement-mode transistors replace the slow diodes in the return path, controlled by a digital signal processor executing a standard average-current-mode control loop at a 100 kHz switching frequency. Simulation in PSIM was followed by a hardware prototype built on a four-layer PCB with co-planar shielding to reduce common-mode noise. Measured efficiency at 230 V AC input and full load was 98.1%, with a power factor of 0.998 and a THDi of 4.3%. Thermal measurements at ambient temperature of 40 °C confirmed that both GaN devices remained below 85 °C junction temperature without a heatsink. Conducted EMI pre-compliance testing indicated that a single common-mode choke was sufficient to meet CISPR 32 Class B limits.

title: Interleaved Two-Phase Boost PFC Converter with Coupled Inductor for Ripple Current Cancellation
abstract: Interleaving two boost converter phases with a 180° phase shift reduces input and output current ripple in PFC applications, but the achievable ripple cancellation depends strongly on the degree of magnetic coupling between the two inductors. This work investigates the use of a single coupled-inductor structure wound on an EE-core in place of two discrete inductors in a 300 W PFC stage. A parametric study using finite-element magnetic simulation identified an optimal coupling coefficient of k = 0.52 that balances differential-mode ripple cancellation and differential-mode EMI filter size. The coupled inductor was wound and characterised, and a full prototype was assembled and tested at 230 V / 50 Hz input. At rated load, input current ripple amplitude was reduced by 63% compared to the non-coupled interleaved design, enabling a 30% reduction in the differential-mode filter capacitor. Efficiency across the 50–100% load range exceeded 97.8%. Inductor core temperature was measured by embedded thermocouples and remained below 70 °C at full load.

title: Active Harmonic Filter Sizing for a Distribution Panel Supplying a Mixed Load of LED Luminaires and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Mixed nonlinear loads combining LED luminaires and variable-speed motor drives produce harmonic spectra that interact in ways not predictable from individual load measurements alone. This paper presents a measurement campaign and filter sizing study conducted at a manufacturing facility with 140 LED panel luminaires (total 18 kW) and eleven variable-speed drives (total 55 kW). Current harmonics were recorded over 72 hours at the main low-voltage panel using a class-A power quality instrument. The 5th, 7th, and 11th harmonics from the drives partially cancelled the 3rd and 5th contributions from the LED loads, reducing aggregate THDi to 19.4% compared to a modelled worst-case of 27.1%. Based on the measured spectra, a 30 kVAr shunt active power filter was sized using an optimisation procedure that minimised total filter VA rating subject to IEC 61000-3-4 compliance. Post-installation measurements confirmed THDi reduction to 4.8% and a 1.1% improvement in overall system efficiency.

title: Uticaj nesimetrije napona napajanja na raspodelu zajedničkog napona u trofaznom invertoru s prostorno-vektorskom modulacijom
abstract: U radu se analizira kako nesimetričnost ulaznog napona napajanja (do 5% nebalansa amplitude) utiče na raspodelu zajedničkog napona (common-mode voltage, CMV) u dvostepenom trofaznom invertoru koji koristi prostorno-vektorsku pulsno-širinsku modulaciju (SV-PWM). Razvijen je analitički model koji uzima u obzir nesimetriju amplituda i faznih uglova napona napajanja i implementiran u simulacionom okruženju. Simulacije su sprovedene za frekvencije komutacije od 4 kHz, 8 kHz i 16 kHz, a rezultati su verifikovani merenjima na laboratorijskom postolju s asinhroni motorom snage 7,5 kW. Pokazano je da nebalans od 3% povećava vršnu vrednost CMV za 12–18% u odnosu na simetričan slučaj, zavisno od primenjene modulacione sekvence. Analiza je provedena za standardne sekvence 0127 i 0121. Rezultati ukazuju da izbor modulacione sekvence ima značajniji uticaj na CMV od samog stepena nebalansa napajanja pri umerenim nesimetrijama.

title: Analiza ležajnih struja asinhroning motora napajanih iz invertora pri radu sa delimično opterećenim fazama
abstract: Rad razmatra slučaj kada samo jedna ili dve faze trofaznog asinhronog motora nose struju različitu od nominalne usled kvara u mreži ili greške u zaštitnom prekidaču. Ovakvi uslovi rada, koji se u praksi javljaju pri kratkim asimetričnim poremećajima, uzrokuju pojačanu generaciju zajedničkog napona i posledično veće ležajne struje. Eksperimentalni postav uključuje motor snage 11 kW, trofazni invertor s podešavanjem SV-PWM parametara, programabilni izvor nesimetrije napajanja i merni lanac za merenje ležajnih struja direktno na osovini i oklopima ležaja. Merenja su sprovedena za sedam kombinacija amplitudnog nebalansa u opsegu 0–8%. Frekvencija i amplituda EDM impulsa su statistički obrađeni metodom parcijalnog pražnjenja. Utvrđeno je da su EDM struje najosetljiviji pokazatelj promena modulacionog obrasca pri nesimetriji i da se statistički značajna promena može detektovati već pri nebalansu od 2,5%. Rezultati su poređeni s numeričkom simulacijom razvijenom u sopstvenom kodu zasnovanom na Matlabovom Simulink okruženju.

title: Effect of dead-time compensation on common-mode voltage and bearing current spectrum in SV-PWM inverters under unbalanced conditions
abstract: Dead-time insertion in voltage-source inverters introduces low-order harmonic distortion and modifies the common-mode voltage spectrum. This paper examines how two standard dead-time compensation strategies — voltage-error feedforward and current-polarity-based correction — alter the common-mode voltage waveform and the associated bearing current spectrum when the motor is supplied under voltage imbalance. A 7.5 kW induction motor drive was tested at imbalance levels of 0%, 3%, and 5% with dead times of 2 µs and 4 µs. Fast Fourier analysis of shaft voltage signals revealed that feedforward compensation reduces the third harmonic component of CMV by up to 34% under balanced conditions but provides less benefit under 5% imbalance due to interaction between compensation error and the asymmetric switching pattern. Bearing current measurements confirmed that EDM pulse energy increases when dead-time compensation is absent, and this effect is amplified under imbalance. Practical guidelines for selecting compensation strategy under variable grid conditions are provided.

title: Comparative study of symmetric and asymmetric SV-PWM sequences for bearing current mitigation in drives with distorted supply
abstract: Several modified space-vector PWM sequences have been proposed in the literature to reduce common-mode voltage amplitude. This paper compares five such sequences — standard 0127, reduced CMV sequence RCMV-3, and three asymmetric variants — specifically under supply voltage distortion conditions representative of industrial grid environments in southeastern Europe, where harmonic distortion of 4–7% THD and imbalance of 2–5% are common. Tests were performed on a 15 kW induction motor drive at 6 kHz and 10 kHz switching frequencies. Bearing currents were measured using the wideband Rogowski method described in earlier authors' work, and the drive thermal performance was also monitored. The RCMV-3 sequence achieved the largest reduction in peak shaft voltage (−41% at balanced supply) but showed reduced effectiveness at 4% imbalance, dropping to −18%. An asymmetric sequence exploiting the imbalance phase angle demonstrated more robust CMV reduction of −28% across all tested imbalance levels. Total harmonic distortion of stator current increased modestly by 1.2–1.8 percentage points for the asymmetric sequences compared to standard 0127.

title: Zajednički napon i ležajne struje u asinhronim motorima pri harmonijskom izobličenju mreže — pregled metoda merenja i modelovanja
abstract: Ovaj pregledni rad sistematizuje metode merenja i modelovanja zajedničkog napona i ležajnih struja u invertorski napajenim asinhronim motorima s naglaskom na rad u uslovima harmonijskog izobličenja i nesimetrije napajanja. Obuhvaćena je literatura od 2000. do 2021. godine, s posebnim osvrtom na radove koji eksplicitno razmatraju neidealne uslove mreže. Klasifikovani su modeli visokofrekventnih strujnih puteva (modeli visokih frekvencija, ekvivalentna kola, FEM pristupi) i metode merenja (stezaljke struje visoke propusnosti, Rogowski namotaji, naponske sonde osovine). Identifikovane su tri grupe nekonzistentnosti u literaturi: razlike u definicijama nebalansa napona, razlike u pozicioniranju mernih sondi i razlike u frekvencijskom opsegu koji se smatra relevantnim. Predložena je jedinstvena terminologija i preporuke za postavljanje mernih tačaka u laboratorijskim uslovima. Pregledni rad je namenjen istraživačima koji planiraju eksperimentalna merenja u industrijskim uslovima sa nestabilnom mrežom.

title: Shaft voltage spectral fingerprinting as a diagnostic indicator of supply imbalance in operating induction motor drives
abstract: This paper investigates whether the spectral content of shaft voltage can reliably indicate the degree of supply voltage imbalance during normal drive operation, without access to the supply terminals. Shaft voltage signals were recorded at 50 MS/s sampling rate on a 15 kW four-pole induction motor operated at 50%, 75%, and 100% load under imbalance levels of 0% to 6% in 1% steps. Short-time Fourier analysis was applied to identify spectral sidebands around the switching frequency harmonics that correlate with imbalance. A linear discriminant classifier trained on six spectral features correctly identified imbalance above 2% with 91% accuracy in leave-one-out cross-validation across 126 test records. The diagnostic approach requires no additional hardware beyond a shaft voltage probe and standard data acquisition. Sensitivity decreases at low load (50%) due to increased noise floor from mechanical vibration coupling. Implications for condition monitoring of motors connected to weak grids are discussed.

title: Influence of DC-link capacitor aging on common-mode voltage ripple and bearing current in SV-PWM drives
abstract: Electrolytic DC-link capacitors degrade over their service lifetime, increasing equivalent series resistance and reducing capacitance. This paper examines how such aging affects the common-mode voltage ripple and, consequently, bearing current generation in a SV-PWM inverter-fed induction motor. Four capacitor banks at different stages of simulated aging (new, 30%, 60%, and 90% capacitance loss verified by impedance spectroscopy) were installed in a 7.5 kW drive system and tested under both balanced and 4% imbalanced supply. Common-mode voltage peak values increased by up to 9% and ripple frequency content shifted measurably at 60% capacitance loss. Bearing current EDM pulse energy rose by 14% between new and 90% degraded capacitor banks under imbalanced supply, compared to 6% under balanced conditions. These results suggest that drive aging and grid imbalance have a synergistic effect on bearing current severity, relevant for predictive maintenance scheduling in industrial environments.

title: Modifikovana SV-PWM sekvenca za istovremeno smanjenje zajedničkog napona i ležajnih struja pri nesimetričnom napajanju trofaznih pogona
abstract: U radu je predložena modifikovana SV-PWM sekvenca koja uzima u obzir trenutni vektorski položaj referentnog napona i izmereni stepen nesimetrije napajanja radi dinamičke adaptacije trajanja aktivnih vektora. Algoritam je implementiran na digitalnom signalnom procesoru tipa ControlCore DSP-F28 i testiran na pogonu s asinhronim motorom 11 kW. Ispitivanja su sprovedena za nebalans od 0%, 2%, 4% i 6% pri frekvencijama komutacije od 6 kHz i 10 kHz. Predložena sekvenca smanjila je vršnu vrednost zajedničkog napona za 22–31% u poređenju sa standardnom 0127 sekvencom pri svim ispitanim stepenima nebalansa. Merenje ležajnih struja pokazalo je smanjenje učestalosti EDM impulsa za 19% pri nebalansu od 4% i frekvenciji 6 kHz. Uvođenje adaptivne sekvence nije prouzrokovalo merljivo povećanje harmonijskog izobličenja izlaznog napona motora iznad standardnih granica prema IEC 61800-3. Predloženi postupak je pogodan za retrofitovanje postojećih inversorskih pogona sa dostupnim DSP resursom.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time EV Charging Control Under Stochastic Arrivals and Price Uncertainty
abstract: Model-based optimisation of EV charging requires accurate forecasts of vehicle arrivals and electricity prices that are often unavailable in real time. This paper applies a deep Q-network (DQN) agent to control the charging power of a 50-space public car park in Novi Sad in a simulated environment. The state space encodes queue state, current price, time of day, and remaining time windows; the action space discretises charger power into five levels between 0 and 22 kW. The reward function balances charging cost minimisation against a penalty for unmet energy demand at departure. The agent is trained over 10 000 simulated days using historical price data from a regional day-ahead market and arrival statistics derived from a six-month car park monitoring campaign. After training, the DQN policy reduces average cost per vehicle by 13.7% compared with greedy immediate-charge, and by 5.2% compared with a model predictive control baseline that uses perfect forecasts degraded with realistic noise. Robustness to sudden price spikes is demonstrated through stress testing.

title: Implementation of Model Predictive Control for Current Regulation in a Five-Level NPC-Based Medium-Voltage Drive
abstract: Finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) is evaluated as an alternative to conventional PI current regulators for a five-level neutral-point-clamped inverter connected to a 6 kV, 200 kW synchronous reluctance motor. The predictive model includes the motor electrical equations discretised at 50 µs sampling intervals and a capacitor voltage balance term weighted by a tunable factor λ. Two cost function formulations are compared: one penalising only current error and one additionally penalising switching frequency through a transition count term. Experimental validation was performed on a down-scaled 400 V, 7.5 kW laboratory drive using hardware-in-the-loop testing with a dSPACE DS1104 system. The switching-frequency-penalising formulation achieved a 22% reduction in average switching frequency compared to the basic formulation at equivalent current tracking error. Steady-state current THD measured at the motor terminals was 3.2% for the switching-penalised MPC versus 2.9% for PI with conventional space-vector PWM, a trade-off considered acceptable given the reduced thermal stress.

title: Validation of a Static Biomechanical Model for Lumbar Compression Force Estimation in Repetitive Lifting Tasks
abstract: This paper presents a validation study of a three-dimensional static biomechanical model against measured lumbar compression forces collected from 24 male participants performing standardised box-lifting tasks at three load levels (5, 10, and 15 kg). The model was implemented in MATLAB and relied on inverse statics with anthropometric scaling drawn from the ANSUR II dataset. Ground reaction forces were measured with a force plate, and surface EMG signals from six trunk muscle groups were used as a secondary validation criterion. Predicted L4–L5 compressive forces deviated from measured values by a mean absolute error of 8.3% across all conditions, which falls within the accepted tolerance reported in comparable literature. Shear force predictions showed slightly higher deviations (mean 11.7%) at the highest load level. The results confirm that the static model provides acceptable accuracy for occupational risk screening purposes under the conditions tested, and highlight the need for dynamic corrections when cycle times fall below four seconds.
