title: Comparison of RULA and OWAS Posture Assessment Tools in Automotive Sub-Assembly Operations: A Field Study
abstract: Observational ergonomic assessment tools differ in their sensitivity to specific body regions and task durations, yet direct field comparisons in identical production settings remain sparse. This study applied both RULA and OWAS simultaneously to 18 workstations at an automotive sub-assembly plant in Zrenjanin, Serbia, using video recordings at 25 fps with a minimum of 60 observation cycles per workstation. Inter-rater reliability was established between two trained assessors (Cohen's kappa 0.71 for RULA, 0.68 for OWAS). RULA classified 11 of 18 workstations as requiring immediate investigation, while OWAS flagged only 7 under equivalent risk categories. Discrepancies were most pronounced at stations involving sustained neck flexion beyond 20° combined with moderate arm elevation, a combination that OWAS encodes at lower resolution. Agreement between tools was strongest for whole-body awkward postures in material transfer tasks. The findings support using RULA as the primary screening instrument for upper-limb intensive tasks at this facility type.

title: ISO 11228-1 Compliance Mapping in a Digital Human Modelling Environment: Methodology and Case Study
abstract: Manual handling risk assessment in product design phases is complicated by the absence of physical prototypes. This paper describes a methodology that integrates ISO 11228-1 lifting and carrying limits directly into a digital human modelling (DHM) workflow implemented with Siemens Jack 8.2. The approach maps the standard's reference mass, coupling quality, and frequency correction factors onto DHM task simulation parameters, allowing compliance status to be evaluated at each simulated posture frame. A case study covering the assembly of an industrial pump housing (mass 18 kg) demonstrated that the method correctly identified three out of four non-compliant handling sequences detected by a subsequent physical trial with instrumented mannequins. False-positive rate was 12.5% across all evaluated frames. Computation time for a full assembly sequence of 47 steps averaged 34 minutes on standard engineering workstation hardware. Limitations related to DHM population variability and the omission of psychophysical factors are discussed, along with a proposed extension to ISO 11228-2 for push–pull tasks.

title: Predicting Cumulative Lumbar Load in Manual Packing Lines Using Inverse Dynamic Simulation Driven by Accelerometer Data
abstract: Wearable accelerometers offer a low-cost alternative to full optical motion capture for monitoring occupational movement, but their use in inverse dynamic models requires careful signal processing. This study presents a pipeline in which tri-axial accelerometer data from seven body segments, collected at 100 Hz from 10 workers on a food packing line, were processed through a Kalman filter and fed into a segment-based inverse dynamic model to estimate cumulative lumbar load over an 8-hour shift. Results were compared against reference estimates from simultaneous optical capture (Vicon, eight cameras) on a subsample of 90-minute recordings. Mean cumulative L4–L5 compression force estimated by the accelerometer-driven model differed from the optical reference by 6.9% across all participants. The accelerometer pipeline overestimated peak load by 14% during rapid trunk flexion events, identified as the primary source of systematic error. Daily cumulative lumbar load exceeded the NIOSH recommended action limit in seven of ten workers. The pipeline is presented as open-source code in MATLAB and is suitable for deployment in production environments without fixed infrastructure.

title: Incorporating Anthropometric Variability into Virtual Assembly Ergonomics Assessment: A Percentile Boundary Approach
abstract: Virtual ergonomics assessments in DHM software typically rely on a small number of boundary manikins, often the 5th and 95th percentile stature, and ignore the multivariate covariance structure of human anthropometry. This book chapter reviews the limitations of that approach and proposes a percentile boundary method based on principal component analysis of a combined European–Serbian anthropometric dataset (n = 4,240 adults). The first three principal components explained 68% of anthropometric variance. The chapter illustrates the method for a simulated overhead tightening task, showing that the standard two-manikin approach misclassified ergonomic risk for 22% of the modelled population when compared against a Monte Carlo simulation with 500 virtual workers drawn from the PCA-derived distribution. Practical guidance is provided on selecting a minimum set of five representative manikins that reduces misclassification to under 8% with acceptable added analysis time. The chapter also discusses how the method interfaces with ISO 11228-3 repetitive task assessment.

title: Biomechanical Assessment of Exoskeleton-Assisted Manual Handling: A Simulation-Based Study Using ISO 11228 Criteria
abstract: Passive back-support exoskeletons are increasingly deployed in industrial settings, but quantifying their effect on spinal load in the design phase—before physical prototypes exist—remains difficult. This study used a validated DHM model in Siemens Jack to simulate 12 manual material handling tasks with and without a passive lumbar exoskeleton, parameterised from published kinematic and force data for a commercially representative device class. ISO 11228-1 reference masses and NIOSH revised lifting equation outputs were computed for each condition. The exoskeleton reduced predicted peak L4–L5 compressive force by 17–28% depending on task geometry, with the largest reductions occurring in symmetric forward-bending lifts from floor level. However, for lateral-reach tasks the predicted compressive force reduction fell to 6%, and horizontal shear forces increased by up to 9% in three of twelve tasks. The results suggest that ISO 11228-1 compliance status improved for 8 of 12 tasks after simulated exoskeleton use, but three tasks shifted from compliant to non-compliant for shear, highlighting a limitation of current standards that focus on compression. Recommendations for updating simulation workflows to include shear criteria are provided.

title: Real-Time Ergonomic Risk Feedback in Assembly Training Using Depth-Camera Skeleton Tracking and REBA Scoring
abstract: This conference paper describes the design and preliminary evaluation of a real-time feedback system for ergonomics training in assembly tasks. A Microsoft Azure Kinect depth camera captures skeleton joint positions at 30 fps; joint angles are extracted and fed into a software implementation of the REBA scoring algorithm that updates every 500 ms and displays a colour-coded risk indicator on a monitor visible to the trainee. The system was tested with 22 engineering students performing a standardised assembly task on a adjustable workbench across two sessions separated by one week. The control group (n = 11) received standard written instructions only. The feedback group showed a 31% reduction in mean REBA score from session one to session two (from 7.4 to 5.1), compared with a 9% reduction in the control group (7.6 to 6.9). Tracking accuracy relative to the laboratory's Vicon system showed joint angle root-mean-square error of 4.2° for trunk flexion and 6.8° for wrist deviation, with the wrist error identified as the primary limitation. The system is described in sufficient detail for replication using open-source components.

title: Mapping Musculoskeletal Disorder Risk Factors Across Small and Medium Enterprises in Vojvodina: A Cross-Sectional Survey
abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) impose considerable costs on SMEs, yet systematic regional prevalence data are sparse in Serbia. This cross-sectional study surveyed 43 manufacturing SMEs in the Vojvodina region using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire and a structured workplace exposure checklist administered to 631 workers (58% male, mean age 38.4 years, SD 9.7). Twelve-month prevalence of low back symptoms was 52%, followed by neck (41%) and shoulder (37%). Logistic regression identified repetitive handling (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.7–3.4), awkward trunk posture more than two hours per shift (OR 3.1, 95% CI 2.1–4.5), and absence of job rotation (OR 1.9, 95% CI 1.3–2.7) as significant predictors of low back symptoms. Sector analysis showed food processing and woodworking sub-sectors had the highest WMSD prevalence. The paper provides baseline regional data and discusses barriers to ergonomics implementation specific to SME context in the Western Balkans, including limited access to occupational health expertise and low awareness of ISO 11228 requirements.

title: Sensitivity of ISO 11228-3 OCRA Index to Task Duration Estimation Errors in DHM-Based Pre-Production Assessments
abstract: The OCRA index, as specified in ISO 11228-3, requires accurate estimates of net task duration and recovery time to yield reliable risk classification. In pre-production DHM assessments, these values are derived from simulated cycle times that may deviate from actual production rates. This paper quantifies the sensitivity of OCRA index outputs to systematic and random errors in task duration estimation using a Monte Carlo approach applied to 15 representative upper-limb assembly tasks parameterised from DHM simulations in Siemens Jack. Task duration was perturbed by ±5%, ±15%, and ±25% of the nominal value, and OCRA index change and risk category shifts were recorded across 10,000 samples per perturbation level. Results show that a ±15% duration error leads to OCRA index changes of up to 0.8 units on average, causing risk category misclassification in 18% of tasks in the borderline green–yellow zone. Tasks with high technical action frequency (≥30 actions/min) were three times more sensitive to duration errors than low-frequency tasks. Practical thresholds for acceptable duration estimation uncertainty in pre-production ergonomics screening are derived from the results.

title: A Framework for Integrating Ergonomic Constraints into Early-Stage Collaborative Robot Workcell Layout Optimisation
abstract: Human–robot collaboration introduces ergonomic exposures that differ from fully manual assembly, particularly with respect to constrained working envelopes and externally paced task rhythms imposed by robot trajectory speed. This paper proposes a framework that encodes ergonomic constraints derived from ISO 11228 and RULA action limits as penalty terms in a multi-objective workcell layout optimisation model. The layout variables include workbench height, robot base position, and part-presentation angle. Ergonomic objectives are evaluated at each candidate layout using an automated DHM scoring routine scripted around Siemens Jack batch processing. The framework is demonstrated on a prototype collaborative assembly cell for small electromechanical sub-assemblies; three Pareto-efficient layouts are identified that reduce mean RULA score from 6.8 (initial layout) to between 3.9 and 4.6 without increasing cycle time beyond a 5% tolerance. The paper also reports a preliminary user trial with 8 technicians that confirmed the direction of ergonomic improvement, though sample size precludes statistical inference. Computational cost and integration steps for industrial use are discussed.

title: Estimating Age-Related Changes in Manual Handling Capacity for ISO 11228-1 Reference Population Assumptions: A Scoping Review
abstract: ISO 11228-1 reference mass limits are derived from population capacity data that do not explicitly account for workforce ageing, yet demographic projections in European manufacturing indicate that the proportion of workers aged 50 and above will increase substantially through 2035. This scoping review synthesised 38 studies published between 2000 and 2024 that reported age-stratified isometric or isokinetic strength data relevant to manual handling capacity, including grip, trunk extension, and knee extension torques. Studies were identified from four databases using a predefined search string and screened by two reviewers independently (kappa 0.77 at full-text stage). Pooled results indicate that trunk extension torque declines on average by 1.4% per year after age 45 in mixed-sex industrial samples, with women showing steeper relative decline than men from age 50 onward. The review finds that applying ISO 11228-1 reference masses uniformly to workers aged 55+ results in an estimated 18–23% underestimation of spinal compression force relative to measured capacity in that subgroup, based on the biomechanical modelling assumptions embedded in the standard. The review concludes with a set of research priorities for updating the anthropometric and physiological basis of ISO 11228-1.

title: Joint optimisation of line balancing and component supermarket sizing for a low-volume sterilisation device assembly line
abstract: Lean assembly systems operating under kanban-driven component replenishment must coordinate station workload assignments with the sizing of lineside supermarkets to avoid both stockouts and excessive floor space consumption. This paper formulates a bi-level optimisation model where the upper level solves the ALBP-2 for a 6-model sterilisation device line and the lower level determines supermarket capacities for 34 component types under stochastic daily demand. The upper-level problem is solved by a beam search heuristic; the lower level uses a newsvendor-type model with component-specific holding and stockout cost ratios. An iterative coupling scheme alternates between the two levels until the total cost improvement between iterations falls below 0.5%. Applied to a 9-month planning horizon calibrated with real demand data, the joint optimisation reduces total cost by 8.4% compared to sequential optimisation and by 21.7% compared to a current-practice rule-of-thumb supermarket sizing policy.

title: Developing a Modular Parametric Cost Model for Custom Industrial Conveyor Systems
abstract: Custom conveyor systems present a suitable application domain for modular parametric cost modelling because they combine a defined set of recurring subsystems with highly variable configuration. This paper describes the development of a modular parametric model covering five subsystem types: drive units, carrying frames, tensioning assemblies, transfer points, and electrical controls. Cost equations for each subsystem were derived from 77 historical orders provided by a conveyor manufacturer based in Vojvodina. Independent variables included conveyor length, belt width, carrying capacity, inclination angle, and drive power. The overall model predicts total manufactured cost with a mean absolute percentage error of 9.7% on a validation set of 14 orders. The modular structure allows the model to be updated subsystem by subsystem as cost data accumulate, without refitting the complete model. Integration with the company's ERP quotation module is described, and the practical workflow for quotation engineers is outlined.

title: Uticaj brzine postmerger integracije na kompetencijski profil inženjerskih timova: komparativna studija slučaja
abstract: Studija upoređuje dva slučaja integracije inženjerskih timova u prerađivačkim preduzećima u Srbiji: jedno preduzeće je sprovelo ubrzanu integraciju u trajanju od četiri meseca, a drugo faznu integraciju tokom 16 meseci. Podaci su prikupljeni kombinacijom strukturisanih intervjua (n=24) i analizom internih evidencija kompetencija na godišnjem nivou tokom tri godine post-merger perioda. Kompetencijski profili su kvantifikovani kroz kompozitni indeks koji obuhvata tehničke veštine, procesno znanje i timske kompetencije. Rezultati pokazuju da preduzeće sa ubrzanom integracijom beleži pad kompozitnog indeksa od 22% u prvoj godini, dok preduzeće sa faznom integracijom beleži pad od svega 9%. U drugoj i trećoj godini razlika se smanjuje, ali ostaje statistički značajna (p < 0,01). Rad diskutuje ograničenja studije slučaja i predlaže parametre za buduće simulacione modele.

title: Long-term planimetric changes of the Tisa River channel in Serbia inferred from nineteenth-century cadastral maps and recent aerial imagery
abstract: This study reconstructed the planimetric trajectory of a 280 km reach of the Tisa River in Serbia between 1884 and 2009 using digitised cadastral maps at 1:28 800 scale and orthorectified aerial photographs. Channel centrelines were extracted manually and compared using geographic information system overlay analysis. Results indicate a reduction in sinuosity from 1.87 to 1.43 over the study period, with total channel shortening of approximately 164 km attributable to systematic cutoff works carried out between 1855 and 1870. Post-regulation lateral migration rates, measured as mean annual bank displacement, averaged 0.8 m yr⁻¹ for bank-erosion-prone reaches and 0.3 m yr⁻¹ elsewhere. Active oxbow development was documented at four locations where remnant meander bends continued adjusting after severing. The findings highlight that the Tisa channel remains in a prolonged post-regulation adjustment phase more than 140 years after intervention.

title: Bank material composition and its influence on erosion rates along a channelised reach of the Tisa River
abstract: Bank erosion on lowland rivers is strongly conditioned by the stratigraphy and cohesive properties of bank materials. This paper presents results from sediment sampling at 42 cross-sections along a 90 km reach of the regulated Tisa River between Kanjiža and Novi Bečej, conducted in 2012–2013. Grain-size analysis, Atterberg limits, and organic content were determined for samples from three stratigraphic layers at each cross-section. Erosion pins installed at 18 sites recorded displacement over two hydrological years. Statistical correlation showed that reaches with sandy basal layers underlain by less than 0.5 m of cohesive overbank sediment exhibited mean erosion rates of 1.4 m yr⁻¹, compared with 0.4 m yr⁻¹ where cohesive overbank thickness exceeded 1.2 m. Flood duration above bankfull stage was the most significant hydrological predictor of annual erosion, explaining 61% of variance in a simple linear model. Results support a two-layer stratigraphy model for bank stability assessment on Pannonian lowland rivers.

title: Remote sensing classification of active and relict oxbow features along the middle Tisa floodplain using multitemporal Landsat imagery
abstract: Oxbow lakes and palaeochannels on the Tisa floodplain represent geomorphological and ecological archives of pre-regulation channel behaviour. This paper applies supervised classification to a 30-image Landsat 5 and 8 time series spanning 1988 to 2018 to map water-body extent, vegetation encroachment, and sediment infilling dynamics at 74 oxbow features within a 220 km floodplain corridor in Serbia and Hungary. A support vector machine classifier trained on field-verified polygons achieved an overall accuracy of 88.4% (kappa 0.84). Analysis shows that 31% of oxbow lakes lost more than half their open-water area over the 30-year period primarily through macrophyte expansion and sedimentation. Oxbows connected to the main channel during high-water events displayed significantly slower infilling rates than isolated features. The resulting geodatabase of oxbow morphodynamic states is offered as a baseline for wetland management planning.
venue: Central European Journal of Earth Observation and Remote Sensing

title: Nineteenth-century engineering surveys as a source for pre-regulation fluvial reconstruction: a methodological assessment using the Begej River
abstract: Engineering surveys produced during Austro-Hungarian river regulation projects between 1851 and 1880 constitute among the most geometrically precise historical channel records available for the Pannonian Plain, yet their systematic use in geomorphological research remains limited. This study evaluates the accuracy and spatial consistency of six original survey sheets for the Begej River canal corridor in Vojvodina by co-registering them with LIDAR-derived topography and comparing planimetric features against contemporaneous ground-truth points. Root-mean-square positional error across 84 check points averaged 18.3 m, acceptable for channel centreline extraction at 1:25 000 analytical scale. Reconstructed pre-regulation sinuosity of the natural Begej channel was 2.14, considerably higher than the current value of 1.08 following canalisation. The paper discusses scanning protocols, georeferencing workflows, and uncertainty propagation relevant to researchers working with similar archival sources across the region.

title: Sediment budget estimation for a short embanked reach of the Danube between Apatin and Bogojevo using repeated cross-section surveys
abstract: Accurate sediment budgets for regulated reaches of the middle Danube are required for maintenance planning of navigation channels and flood-protection embankments. This study presents a reach-scale sediment budget for a 38 km embanked Danube reach in northwestern Serbia based on 24 cross-section surveys conducted in 2016 and 2019 at approximately 1.6 km spacing, supplemented by suspended sediment sampling at upstream and downstream gauging stations. Net bed volume change was computed by integrating cross-sectional area differences over the survey interval. The reach exhibited a mean net incision of 0.12 m over three years, corresponding to a sediment deficit of approximately 0.48 × 10⁶ m³. Bedload transport estimated from the Einstein–Brown formula at mean annual discharge yielded values consistent within 20% of the morphological budget. The results suggest continued bed lowering attributable to upstream gravel extraction activities that ceased in 2007, with the deficit wave propagating downstream at roughly 3–5 km yr⁻¹.

title: Floodplain connectivity and overbank sedimentation rates on the lower Tisa reach in Serbia: evidence from OSL-dated flood deposits
abstract: Overbank sedimentation records preserve information about historical flood regimes and floodplain–channel connectivity that is difficult to obtain from instrumental data alone. This paper reports optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating and grain-size analysis of sediment cores extracted from eight floodplain sites along the lower Tisa reach between Titel and the Danube confluence. Core lengths ranged from 1.8 to 3.4 m. OSL ages constrained six sedimentation phases between approximately 1650 CE and 2005 CE. Mean vertical accretion rates during the pre-regulation period (before 1870) averaged 3.8 mm yr⁻¹, declining to 1.1 mm yr⁻¹ post-regulation as embankments restricted inundation frequency. Grain-size fining upward in all cores reflects reduced flood energy after embankment construction. Two sites proximal to remnant floodplain lakes showed persistent higher accretion (2.4 mm yr⁻¹) attributed to local connectivity through drainage structures. These data contribute to regional Holocene alluvial chronologies for the Pannonian Plain.

title: Channel geometry adjustments on the Sava River downstream of the Brčko gravel reach: a 40-year analysis using topographic maps and satellite imagery
abstract: The Sava River transitions from a gravel-bed reach upstream of Brčko to a sand-bed system over its lower 200 km course to the Danube confluence. This study examines width and centreline changes along the sand-bed reach using topographic maps from 1980–1982 and Google Earth and Sentinel-2 imagery from 2018–2020. Sixteen representative sub-reaches of 5–8 km length were delimited by channel pattern and bank composition. Mean bankfull width decreased from 312 m in 1980 to 287 m in 2019 across all sub-reaches, with the greatest narrowing (up to 22%) observed in areas where riparian vegetation colonised former mid-channel bars. Lateral migration was spatially variable; three sub-reaches showed lateral shift rates exceeding 3 m yr⁻¹ attributed to asymmetric revetment placement. Comparison with contemporaneous discharge records at Sremska Mitrovica station shows no significant trend in mean annual flow, suggesting that channel narrowing reflects vegetation dynamics rather than discharge reduction.

title: Mapping gravel bar dynamics on the Drava River using UAV photogrammetry and structure-from-motion: a pilot study at Batina reach
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry combined with structure-from-motion (SfM) processing offers sub-decimetre resolution topographic models of exposed gravel bars at low cost compared to conventional airborne survey. This paper presents results from four UAV surveys conducted in 2021–2022 at two gravel bar complexes on the Drava River near Batina, covering approximately 0.6 km² of exposed bar surface per survey. A DJI Mavic 3 platform with a 20 Mp sensor was flown at 80 m altitude; ground control was established using differential GNSS. SfM-derived digital elevation models (DEMs) were differenced between successive surveys to quantify volumetric change. Cumulative bar volume change over the survey period ranged from −840 to +1 120 m³ between individual bar units, reflecting highly dynamic conditions during the 2022 spring flood. The study documents the UAV-SfM workflow adapted for access-constrained international border river conditions and discusses licensing and safety constraints encountered during fieldwork.

title: Reconstruction of Vojvodina canal network planimetry from Habsburg military surveys, 1763–1787, and comparison with current drainage geometry
abstract: The Vojvodina lowland drainage canal network has been modified repeatedly since its initial construction under Habsburg administration in the eighteenth century, yet systematic comparison of early and current canal geometries across the region has not previously been undertaken. This study digitised canal alignments from 106 sheets of the First Military Survey of the Habsburg Empire (1763–1787) covering Vojvodina and compared them with the current hydrographic layer of the Water Directorate for Vojvodina at 1:10 000 scale. Total mapped canal length increased from approximately 1 850 km in the survey period to 18 600 km in the current network, reflecting multiple phases of agricultural drainage expansion. Original canal sinuosity averaged 1.31, substantially higher than the 1.06 mean for contemporary canals, indicating progressive geometric straightening. Positional accuracy of the First Military Survey sheets was assessed at ±60–110 m after affine registration, adequate for network topology but not for precise morphometric analysis. The dataset offers a historical baseline for long-term management assessments of the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal system.

title: Night-time outdoor thermal comfort in Novi Sad: measurements in three morphologically distinct neighbourhoods
abstract: Outdoor thermal comfort research has predominantly focused on daytime conditions; night-time measurements are rare in Serbian urban climatology. This study presents continuous night-time microclimate data (20:00–06:00 local time) collected at nine measurement points distributed across three Novi Sad neighbourhoods with contrasting morphologies: the compact historic core, a 1970s residential block area, and a low-rise detached housing zone on the urban periphery. Measurements were conducted on 20 summer nights in 2021 using fixed meteorological stations and roving globe thermometers. UTCI was calculated at hourly intervals. The compact core showed the highest nocturnal air temperatures (mean 27.3 °C at 22:00) and the slowest cooling rates, consistent with urban heat island retention. The block neighbourhood showed intermediate values, and the periphery cooled most rapidly. Despite these differences, UTCI fell below the 'no thermal stress' threshold of 9 °C at all sites well before dawn. Perceived thermal comfort scores collected from local residents correlated moderately with UTCI (r = 0.54).

title: Life cycle inventory for a mid-scale hotel in the Vojvodina plain: boundary definition and data quality challenges
abstract: This study presents a cradle-to-gate life cycle inventory (LCI) for a 64-room business hotel operating in the Vojvodina lowland region of Serbia. System boundaries were drawn to include energy consumption, water use, food procurement, laundry services, and guest transport to and from the facility. Primary activity data were collected through an 18-month metered monitoring campaign covering electricity, natural gas, and water flows. Ecoinvent 2.2 background datasets were adapted for the Serbian electricity grid mix using data from the national energy balance. The resulting inventory showed that energy use in heating and cooling accounted for 58% of the global warming potential (GWP), while food procurement contributed an additional 21%. Data quality was assessed using a pedigree matrix approach; geographic and temporal representativeness scored poorly for food supply chains, identifying this as the main uncertainty driver. The paper proposes a tiered data collection protocol suitable for small-to-medium hospitality operators lacking in-house environmental management systems. Functional unit was defined as one occupied guest-night.

title: Environmental impact assessment of a spa resort using LCA: water consumption as an overlooked hotspot
abstract: Spa and wellness resorts represent an energy- and water-intensive subset of the hospitality sector, yet most existing LCA studies focus on conventional hotels. This paper presents a full LCA of a geothermal spa resort in the Bačka region, Serbia, covering a one-year operational period. The functional unit was one visitor-day. Eight midpoint categories were assessed using the CML-IA baseline method: global warming, ozone depletion, photochemical oxidant formation, acidification, eutrophication, freshwater aquatic ecotoxicity, human toxicity, and water depletion. The analysis showed that water depletion ranked second after climate change in relative contribution, accounting for 19% of total normalised impact, due to the high-temperature geothermal drawdown rate of approximately 340 m³ per day. Chemical treatment of pool water contributed significantly to eutrophication and ecotoxicity endpoints. The study used a combination of metered primary data and ecoinvent 3.4 background processes adapted with Serbian electricity and water treatment datasets. Recommendations for hotspot reduction focus on heat recovery from geothermal discharge and circulation-loop redesign.

title: Carbon accounting in rural agritourism: methodological adaptation for smallholder-operated accommodation
abstract: Agritourism in the Fruška Gora and Bačka Topola sub-regions of Vojvodina involves hundreds of smallholder-operated guesthouses that lack the metering infrastructure assumed by standard carbon accounting frameworks. This paper develops a simplified carbon accounting tool calibrated against full-scope LCA results from six instrumented pilot farms. The tool uses three input parameters—annual guest-nights, heated floor area, and livestock unit equivalents—to estimate GHG emissions within ±18% of the LCA benchmark. Validation was performed against a holdout set of nine additional farms. The GWP estimates ranged from 12 to 47 kg CO₂-eq per guest-night across the sample, with wood combustion for space heating and enteric fermentation from on-site livestock as dominant contributors at 44% and 23% respectively. The paper also discusses how the simplified tool could be embedded in agritourism certification schemes administered by regional tourism clusters, reducing reporting burden while maintaining acceptable accuracy for portfolio-level carbon inventories.

title: Scope 3 emission factors for food and beverage supply in Serbian hotel restaurants: a procurement-linked dataset
abstract: Scope 3 Category 1 (purchased goods and services) is consistently the largest and least accurately quantified component of hotel carbon footprints in Southeast Europe, owing to the absence of regionally calibrated emission factors. This study develops a dataset of 48 emission factors for food and beverage commodities commonly procured by full-service hotel restaurants in Serbia, expressed in kg CO₂-eq per kilogram of purchased product. Data collection involved primary interviews with 11 catering suppliers and secondary LCA literature review. Where primary data were unavailable, ecoinvent 3.5 processes were adapted using local agricultural statistics. Factors for locally grown seasonal vegetables were 35–60% lower than the ecoinvent European averages, while imported out-of-season produce showed factors up to 2.4 times higher. The dataset is provided as a supplementary spreadsheet tool intended for use by hotel environmental managers and auditors. Uncertainty bounds at 95% confidence are reported for each factor using Gaussian error propagation.

title: Life cycle assessment of a scientific conference: comparing in-person, hybrid, and fully virtual formats
abstract: Academic conferences generate measurable GHG emissions primarily through delegate air travel, yet few empirical LCA studies cover the full event system boundary including venue energy, catering, printed materials, and digital infrastructure. This paper presents an attributional LCA of a 320-delegate engineering conference held in Novi Sad, comparing the actual in-person event against two counterfactual scenarios: a hybrid format (50% remote delegates) and a fully virtual format. The functional unit was defined as one successfully delivered scientific presentation session. Air and ground transport dominated in-person event GWP at 73%, equivalent to 42.6 tonnes CO₂-eq total. The hybrid scenario reduced total GWP by 38%, and the virtual scenario by 81%, though the virtual scenario increased electricity consumption for streaming infrastructure by a factor of 3.4. Catering contributed 14% of in-person GWP, with meat-based menus showing 2.1× higher impact than vegetarian alternatives. The study used a process-LCA approach with ecoinvent 3.6 and was conducted in OpenLCA 1.10. Results suggest that even partial remote participation yields substantial emissions reductions per unit of scientific output.

title: Environmental product declarations for tourism service bundles: feasibility and standardisation gaps
abstract: Environmental product declarations (EPDs) are well established for manufactured goods but have rarely been applied to service bundles such as packaged holidays. This book chapter examines the technical and institutional feasibility of extending the EPD framework (ISO 14025 and EN 15804) to tourism service systems. The analysis is structured around three hypothetical service bundles—a domestic river cruise, a city-break package, and a rural wellness retreat—drawn from operator interviews conducted in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia. For each bundle, a system boundary diagram and a list of required life cycle inventory modules are proposed. Key standardisation gaps identified include the treatment of shared infrastructure (transport networks, airports), allocation of accommodation impacts across multiple booking channels, and the absence of a tourism-specific product category rule (PCR). The chapter concludes that EPD issuance for tourism bundles is technically feasible but requires a dedicated PCR developed under International EPD System governance, and proposes a minimum data requirement set that operators could realistically compile within existing management reporting cycles.

title: Dynamic carbon accounting for seasonal tourism destinations: incorporating grid emission factor variability
abstract: Static carbon accounting methods apply a single annual average emission factor to grid electricity, which can underestimate or overestimate impacts for tourism destinations with strong seasonal demand patterns. This paper proposes a dynamic accounting approach that matches hourly electricity consumption profiles of four tourist accommodation facilities in Vojvodina with hourly marginal emission factors derived from Serbian transmission system operator dispatch data for 2019 and 2020. The facilities included a summer-season-only camp, a year-round spa hotel, a ski lodge, and a conference centre. Results showed that the dynamic approach yielded GWP estimates 8–23% higher than the static approach for summer-peak facilities, due to the higher dispatch share of lignite thermal plants during peak cooling periods. For the ski lodge, the dynamic estimate was 6% lower, reflecting higher renewable dispatch in winter months. The methodology is implemented in a Python script released under an open-source licence. Practical implications for operators purchasing renewable electricity certificates (RECs) in Serbia are discussed.

title: Benchmarking carbon intensities of hotel chains operating in the Danube macro-region: a multi-country dataset
abstract: Carbon intensity benchmarks (kg CO₂-eq per guest-night) are used by hotel chains for target-setting and by investors for ESG screening, yet comparable data for Central and Southeastern Europe remain sparse. This study compiles a dataset of carbon intensity estimates for 74 hotels across eight countries in the Danube macro-region, derived from audited environmental reports, voluntary disclosure databases, and direct operator surveys. Intensities ranged from 8.3 to 96.1 kg CO₂-eq per guest-night. The variation was explained primarily by hotel category (3–5 stars), heating fuel type, and climate zone. Multiple linear regression accounted for 61% of variance (R² = 0.61, n = 74). Hotels in Serbia had a mean intensity of 38.4 kg CO₂-eq, 22% above the regional median, attributable mainly to the high coal share in the national electricity grid. The paper discusses how benchmarking exercises interact with national energy policy trajectories and argues for the inclusion of projected grid decarbonisation pathways in forward-looking carbon intensity targets for the hospitality sector.

title: Carbon footprint attribution in platform-mediated short-term rentals: allocation challenges for shared apartment buildings
abstract: Short-term rental platforms have redistributed a significant share of tourist accommodation into residential buildings, creating unresolved methodological questions for carbon footprinting: how should the energy and maintenance impacts of a multi-apartment building be allocated between tourist-use nights and residential-use nights? This paper develops three allocation approaches—physical (floor area and occupancy hours), economic (rental income versus imputed residential rent), and system expansion—and applies them to metered data from 14 apartments in Novi Sad registered on a major short-term rental platform for at least 24 months. Results show that the physical allocation approach yields per-guest-night GWP estimates 31% lower than the economic approach, because tourist stays command higher nightly prices relative to occupied hours. System expansion produced results closest to a full-building LCA reference case. The paper discusses implications for municipal carbon accounting in cities where short-term rentals represent more than 5% of total accommodation capacity, and proposes a provisional ISO 14064-compatible allocation procedure for platform operators.

title: Kinetics of Strecker aldehyde formation from phenylalanine and glucose in a low-moisture wheat flour model at varying water activity
abstract: Strecker degradation of phenylalanine was studied in binary model mixtures with glucose at water activity values of 0.30, 0.45, and 0.60, heated at 140, 160, and 180 °C for up to 60 min. Phenylacetaldehyde was quantified by headspace SPME–GC–MS using a stable-isotope dilution assay with deuterated internal standard. First-order formation kinetics were confirmed at all conditions; the apparent rate constant at 160 °C and aw 0.45 was 0.018 min⁻¹. Increasing water activity from 0.30 to 0.60 reduced phenylacetaldehyde yield by 34% at 160 °C, attributed to hydrolytic side reactions competing for the α-dicarbonyl intermediate. A stoichiometric balance showed that approximately 22% of consumed phenylalanine was recovered as phenylacetaldehyde under optimum conditions. Parallel formation of benzaldehyde accounted for a further 4%. Results provide quantitative constraints useful for mechanistic modelling of Strecker pathways in low-moisture bakery doughs.

title: GC–MS profiling of headspace volatiles in wheat crust model systems: effect of reducing sugar type
abstract: The influence of reducing sugar identity (glucose, fructose, maltose, and lactose) on the volatile profile of wheat starch–gluten model crust sheets baked at 200 °C for 12 min was investigated by static headspace SPME–GC–MS. Forty-three volatile compounds were identified and semi-quantified relative to an ethyl undecanoate internal standard. Glucose and fructose systems generated significantly higher concentrations of 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline (2-AP) and methylbutanal compared with maltose and lactose systems, by factors of 2.8 and 1.9 respectively. Pyrazine distribution patterns clustered by sugar type in principal component analysis, with maltose systems showing elevated 2,5-dimethylpyrazine. Furanic compound formation did not differ significantly across sugars. The data support a sugar-specific modulation of Strecker and enolisation pathways rather than a general glycolytic route. A compound identity table with retention indices on DB-Wax and DB-5 columns is provided for all 43 compounds.

title: Stoichiometric mapping of lysine consumption and pyrazine production in a glucose–lysine model system under isothermal conditions
abstract: A molar balance approach was applied to the glucose–lysine binary system heated isothermally at 150 and 170 °C (aw 0.40, pH 6.5) to quantify the fraction of lysine directed toward pyrazine formation via Strecker pathways versus glycosylamine condensation. Lysine depletion was tracked by o-phthalaldehyde HPLC assay, while seven pyrazines were individually quantified by GC–MS/MS with stable-isotope standards. At 170 °C and 30 min reaction time, total molar pyrazine yield accounted for 6.3 ± 0.8% of initial lysine, with 2-methylpyrazine being the dominant species at 2.1%. Glycosylamine-derived coloured product formation (measured as absorbance at 420 nm) consumed a further 18% of lysine equivalents. A two-pathway kinetic model fitted the experimental data with R² > 0.97. The study provides stoichiometric parameters applicable to predictive flavour modelling in low-protein bakery formulations.

title: Precursor amino acid supplementation as a strategy to modulate Strecker aldehyde profiles in rye sourdough bread
abstract: Exogenous addition of methionine, leucine, and valine at concentrations of 0.1–0.5% (flour basis) to a standardised rye sourdough formulation was evaluated for its effect on the volatile aldehyde profile of the final baked crust. Methional, 2-methylpropanal, and 2-methylbutanal were quantified by SPME–GC–MS following dynamic headspace collection at 60 °C. Methionine supplementation at 0.3% increased methional concentration 4.2-fold relative to unsupplemented control (p < 0.01), with a near-linear dose–response up to 0.4%. Leucine addition raised 2-methylbutanal and 3-methylbutanal by 2.7-fold. Fermentation step contribution was separated from baking step contribution by sampling sourdough headspace prior to moulding; approximately 30% of total aldehyde yield originated during fermentation. Sensory triangle tests (n = 24 panellists) showed significant differentiation of methionine-supplemented loaves from control at the 0.3% level.

title: Effect of pH adjustment on the ratio of Strecker-to-caramelisation volatile markers in sucrose–asparagine model bakery gels
abstract: Model gels consisting of 10% sucrose, 0.5% asparagine, and 2% wheat starch were prepared at pH 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, and 8.0 using citrate–phosphate buffer and baked at 190 °C for 20 min. Headspace volatiles were collected by SPME and analysed by GC–MS. Strecker-derived acetaldehyde and 3-methylbutanal decreased by 41% and 29% respectively when pH was raised from 5.0 to 8.0, while furfural, a caramelisation marker, increased by 68% over the same range. Total alkylpyrazine concentration peaked at pH 7.0. Principal component analysis separated samples along PC1 (52% variance explained) primarily driven by the Strecker-to-furfural aldehyde ratio. These findings suggest that dough pH, commonly manipulated by acidulant type in industrial formulations, has measurable consequences on the balance between Strecker and caramelisation flavour pathways that are analytically distinguishable by GC–MS profiling.

title: Quantitative stoichiometric model for simultaneous prediction of Strecker aldehyde and alkylpyrazine yields from amino acid–dicarbonyl mixtures
abstract: A deterministic stoichiometric model was developed to predict molar yields of five Strecker aldehydes (acetaldehyde, methylpropanal, 2-methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal, phenylacetaldehyde) and six alkylpyrazines from mixtures of five amino acids (alanine, valine, leucine, isoleucine, phenylalanine) reacting with methylglyoxal at defined temperatures (140–180 °C) and water activities (0.30–0.55). Model parameters were estimated from 96 isothermal binary experiments; validation used 18 multicomponent mixture experiments not included in fitting. Predicted-versus-measured correlation yielded r² = 0.89 for Strecker aldehydes and r² = 0.84 for pyrazines. The model incorporates competitive Strecker reaction versus imine dimerisation pathways with experimentally fitted branching ratios. A sensitivity analysis identified the dicarbonyl-to-amino-acid molar ratio as the most influential parameter, accounting for 61% of output variance in aldehyde yield. The model is implemented in a freely distributed spreadsheet tool.

title: Maillard reaction volatiles in gluten-free bread matrices: comparison of rice flour, corn starch, and buckwheat flour base systems
abstract: Gluten-free bread analogues formulated with rice flour, corn starch, and buckwheat flour as single-base flours were baked under identical conditions (200 °C, 28 min) and analysed for crust volatile profiles by SPME–GC–MS. Fifty-one volatile compounds were identified, of which 19 were Maillard- and Strecker-derived. Buckwheat-based crusts showed the highest total pyrazine content (312 µg kg⁻¹ crust), attributed to the elevated free amino acid content of buckwheat (measured by HPLC at 2.8 mg g⁻¹ flour). Rice flour crusts had the lowest Strecker aldehyde yield, with 3-methylbutanal at only 24 µg kg⁻¹ versus 91 µg kg⁻¹ in the wheat control baked in parallel. Furanones were detected exclusively in corn starch and rice flour systems and attributed to higher available glucose. The data provide a matrix-specific volatile composition baseline relevant to gluten-free product development without requiring additional flavour supplementation.

title: Headspace volatile evolution during proofing and baking of wheat dough: time-resolved SPME–GC–MS sampling at 5-minute intervals
abstract: A time-resolved SPME sampling protocol was developed to monitor headspace volatile evolution throughout the bread-making process from end of mixing to 30 min post-bake, sampling at 5-minute intervals with an autosampler-coupled fibre housed in a Teflon cap inserted into the baking mould. Twenty-eight compounds were monitored in 14 sequential sampling points. Ethanol, acetaldehyde, and isoamyl alcohol dominated the proofing phase headspace (0–60 min). Pyrazine appearance was first detected at the 80-min point corresponding to crust surface temperature exceeding 135 °C. 2-AP concentration increased steeply between 90 and 105 min then plateaued. Strecker aldehydes (3-methylbutanal, phenylacetaldehyde) peaked at 100–105 min and declined slightly thereafter, consistent with evaporative loss from the open crust surface. The protocol yields a continuous record of volatile onset temperatures and times, providing data for process window definition in commercial baking control systems.

title: Isotope dilution GC–MS/MS method for simultaneous quantification of twelve Strecker aldehydes and five alkylpyrazines in baked cereal crusts
abstract: A multi-analyte stable-isotope dilution assay (SIDA) was developed and validated for the simultaneous quantification of twelve Strecker aldehydes and five alkylpyrazines in wheat, rye, and spelt bread crusts. Deuterium- and ¹³C-labelled internal standards were used for nine of the seventeen target analytes; unlabelled structural analogues served as surrogates for the remaining eight. Sample preparation combined SAFE distillation with solvent evaporation to 0.5 mL. Method validation covered linearity (r² > 0.995 for all analytes), limits of quantification (0.5–8 µg kg⁻¹ crust), intra-day repeatability (RSD 3–9%), and inter-day reproducibility (RSD 6–14%). Trueness was assessed by standard addition at three levels; recoveries ranged from 88 to 107%. The method was applied to 24 commercial bread samples from Serbian retail; concentration ranges for individual compounds and inter-matrix comparison statistics are reported. The validated method is suitable for regulatory and quality-monitoring applications.

title: Influence of reducing agent addition (L-cysteine, sodium metabisulfite) on Strecker aldehyde formation in cracker model sheets
abstract: L-Cysteine and sodium metabisulfite were added at 0, 50, 100, and 200 ppm (flour basis) to thin cracker model sheets (5 mm, 0% added fat, 38% initial moisture) baked at 210 °C. Headspace Strecker aldehydes were quantified by SPME–GC–MS/MS. L-Cysteine at 100 ppm reduced total Strecker aldehyde concentration by 58% relative to control, with the largest proportional reduction for 3-methylbutanal (−72%). Sodium metabisulfite at equivalent concentration reduced total Strecker aldehydes by 44%. Colour development (CIE L*a*b*) showed that L-cysteine at 100 ppm reduced browning (ΔE = 7.1 units relative to control) while metabisulfite had a smaller effect (ΔE = 3.3). A mechanistic rationale based on competitive trapping of α-dicarbonyl intermediates is discussed. The results quantify the trade-off between flavour suppression and colour reduction relevant to savoury cracker manufacturers seeking to standardise aroma intensity.

title: Comparative volatile profiling of heritage and modern wheat varieties in standardised model crust baking: an untargeted GC–MS approach
abstract: Twelve wheat varieties (six heritage: Emmer, Einkorn, Red Fife, Khorasan, Spelt, Rouge de Bordeaux; six modern registered varieties from the Vojvodina region) were evaluated for Maillard and Strecker volatile generation in a standardised model crust baking protocol at 200 °C for 15 min. Untargeted headspace SPME–GC–MS profiling identified 87 compounds; 61 were Maillard- or Strecker-related based on literature assignment. Heritage varieties showed significantly higher total alkylpyrazine content (mean 410 µg kg⁻¹) compared with modern varieties (mean 271 µg kg⁻¹, p = 0.008, Mann–Whitney U test). Free amino acid composition of flour, measured by HPLC-OPA derivatisation, explained 44% of variance in Strecker aldehyde concentration by partial least squares regression. Emmer produced the highest 2-AP concentration (89 µg kg⁻¹) of all twelve varieties. The dataset provides a volatile composition reference for heritage grain product development and labelling claims.

title: First-order degradation kinetics of β-carotene in sunflower oil-in-water emulsions during pasteurisation at 72 °C and 85 °C
abstract: β-Carotene retention in sunflower oil-in-water emulsions (2 % w/w oil, 1 % Tween 80) was monitored over 30 min heat treatment at 72 °C and 85 °C. Carotenoid concentration was quantified by HPLC-DAD at 450 nm after hexane extraction. Degradation followed pseudo-first-order kinetics at both temperatures, with rate constants of 0.0041 min⁻¹ at 72 °C and 0.0112 min⁻¹ at 85 °C, yielding an activation energy of 68.4 kJ mol⁻¹. Half-lives decreased from 169 min at 72 °C to 62 min at 85 °C. Droplet size (measured by dynamic light scattering) remained below 220 nm throughout heating and did not correlate significantly with carotenoid loss, indicating that thermal oxidation rather than coalescence drove degradation. These kinetic parameters provide practical baseline data for pasteurisation protocol design in carotenoid-enriched beverage formulation.

title: Predictive shelf-life modelling of carotenoid-fortified oil-in-water nanoemulsions under variable temperature–light profiles using accelerated degradation data
abstract: A kinetic shelf-life model for β-carotene and lycopene in lecithin-stabilised nanoemulsions was constructed by integrating isothermal degradation data (40 °C, 50 °C, 60 °C) and photodegradation data (0, 600, 1200 lux) through an extended Arrhenius–additive approach. A total of 216 data points collected over 10 weeks were used for model fitting; validation was performed at 35 °C/800 lux using independent formulations. Predicted β-carotene half-lives under simulated retail display conditions (20 °C, 800 lux, 8 h light per day) were 47 days (lecithin only) and 83 days (lecithin + 0.1 % ascorbyl palmitate). Model predictions fell within ±12 % of observed values across all validation conditions. Sensitivity analysis identified light intensity as the dominant variable controlling shelf life under retail conditions, exceeding the effect of temperature fluctuations typical of Serbian supermarket cold chains. Results are intended to assist functional food manufacturers in setting realistic use-by dates for carotenoid-enriched beverages.

title: Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija
abstract: U radu se opisuje metodologija izgradnje invertovanog indeksa koji istovremeno obrađuje ćirilična i latinična pojavljivanja srpskih reči bez prethodnog potpunog prevođenja u jedno pismo. Predloženi postupak uključuje korak normalizacije tokena kojim se za svaki token generiše kanonska forma zasnovana na fonemskoj reprezentaciji, a zatim se fonemski ključevi koriste kao primarni identifikatori u indeksu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na korpusu od 120 000 novinskih članaka preuzetih iz tri srpska dnevna lista u periodu 2000–2008. Mere preciznosti i odziva upoređene su s dva bazična sistema koji koriste isključivo ćirilični, odnosno isključivo latinični indeks. Predloženi sistem postiže F1 vrednost od 0,81 u zadatku ad-hoc pretrage, što je povećanje od 14 procentnih poena u odnosu na bolji od dva bazična sistema. Rad takođe razmatra pitanje memorijskog otiska hibridnog indeksa i predlaže strategiju kompresije rečnika.

title: Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification
abstract: Serbian is officially written in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts, and documents frequently contain tokens in both scripts within a single sentence or paragraph. This paper presents a token canonicalization procedure in which each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence using deterministic grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions, and the resulting phoneme string serves as the canonical form for retrieval purposes. We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions. The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline and from 11.7% to 2.4% compared with a Cyrillic-only baseline. Precision at rank 10 improved by 8 percentage points over both baselines. Edge cases involving foreign loanwords and proper nouns are discussed, and a set of override rules is proposed for the 230 most frequent exceptions identified in the corpus.

title: Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search
abstract: Users searching Serbian-language web content often type queries in one script while relevant documents are stored in the other. This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index. We constructed a test collection of 1 800 queries and 210 000 web pages crawled from .rs domains, with relevance judgments pooled from four assessors. Three expansion strategies were compared: (1) appending the full transliteration variant, (2) appending only tokens whose transliteration differs from the original by more than two characters, and (3) expanding only named entities detected by a rule-based tagger. Strategy 3 achieved the best mean average precision of 0.497, versus 0.431 for no expansion, while reducing index bloat to 6% over the baseline index size. We also report retrieval latency measurements on a commodity server, showing that the overhead introduced by expansion remains under 12 ms at the 95th percentile for queries up to eight tokens.

title: Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima
abstract: Digitalni arhivi srpskih novina i institucionalnih dokumenata često sadrže nedoslednosti gde je isti dokument delom u ćirilici, a delom u latinici, ponekad zbog grešaka pri skeniranju ili uredničkih intervencija. Ovaj rad predlaže metod automatske detekcije takvih nedoslednosti na nivou rečenice, korišćenjem klasifikatora koji kao atribute uzima raspodelu skriptnih blokova, učestalosti bigrama i morfosintaksičke signale. Klasifikator je treniran na 9 400 ručno označenih rečenica iz arhive jednog novosadskog lista i testiran na 2 100 rečenica iz arhive beogradskog lista. Postiže preciznost od 0,91 i odziv od 0,88 u klasi nedoslednih rečenica. Korak korekcije primenjuje fonemsku transliteraciju na detektovane nedosledne tokene. Eksperiment na donstremu (pretragom dokumenta) pokazuje da korigovana verzija arhive daje veću tačnost od nekorigovane za 7 procentnih poena u prosečnoj preciznosti.

title: A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of retrieval systems for Serbian requires a shared test collection that explicitly accounts for mixed-script documents. This paper describes the construction of SrMIR-1, a benchmark corpus comprising 95 000 documents from four genres — news, law, literature, and social media — with 600 topics and graded relevance judgments produced by 12 trained assessors following TREC-style pooling at depth 30. Approximately 41% of documents contain tokens in both scripts. Inter-assessor agreement, measured by Cohen's kappa, was 0.73 across all topics. The paper reports baseline results for five retrieval models: BM25, language modelling with Dirichlet smoothing, a transliteration-aware BM25 variant, a neural dense retrieval model fine-tuned on Serbian, and a hybrid sparse–dense model. The transliteration-aware BM25 variant achieves the highest nDCG@10 of 0.531 among sparse models, while the hybrid model reaches 0.587. The corpus is publicly available under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Indeksiranje pravnih dokumenata sa heterogenim pismom: studija slučaja sudske prakse u Srbiji
abstract: Sudske odluke u Srbiji nastajale su kroz nekoliko decenija u različitim pisarskim praksama i sistemima za obradu teksta, što je rezultovalo korpusom u kome se isti pravni termin pojavljuje u ćiriličnom i latiničnom obliku, ponekad unutar istog paragrafa. Ovaj rad opisuje sistem za pretragu koji je prilagođen ovoj karakteristici i koji se koristi u pilot projektu jednog regionalnog suda. Sistem koristi troslojan pristup: normalizaciju pisma, pravno-specifičnu listu sinonima i rangirač koji uvažava strukturu dokumenta (izreka, obrazloženje, dispozitiv). Evaluacija je sprovedena na 5 800 upita sudskog osoblja tokom tromesečnog pilot perioda. Sistem je postigao prosečnu preciznost od 0,74, uz korisničku ocenu zadovoljstva 4,1 od 5. Rad diskutuje tehničke i organizacione izazove uvođenja pretražnog sistema u pravnu praksu.

title: Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering
abstract: Open-domain question answering over Serbian-language document collections requires a passage retrieval component that is robust to the script in which both the question and the passage are written. This paper describes an adaptation of a BM25-based passage retrieval pipeline in which the tokenizer applies script normalization before indexing and at query time. We built an evaluation set of 340 factoid questions with 1 to 4 correct passages each, drawn from a mixed-script encyclopedia-style corpus of 180 000 passages. We compared four configurations: BM25 with no normalization, BM25 with script normalization, a dense bi-encoder model trained on Serbian data, and a hybrid of the latter two. The script-normalized BM25 retrieves at least one correct passage in the top 20 for 72% of questions, a gain of 17 percentage points over unnormalized BM25. The hybrid model reaches 81%. Failure analysis highlights questions containing transliterated foreign proper nouns as the main remaining challenge.

title: Normalizacija skripte u kontekstu pretraživača internih dokumenata za mala i srednja preduzeća: iskustva iz prakse
abstract: Mala i srednja preduzeća u Srbiji čuvaju interne dokumente — ugovore, zapisnike, izveštaje — u mešovitom pismu bez konzistentne politike. Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma razvijenim u okviru naše istraživačke grupe. Pilot kompanije imale su kolekcije između 8 000 i 45 000 dokumenata. Merili smo preciznost pretrage pre i posle uvođenja normalizacije, korisnički odaziv i troškove uvođenja. U svim slučajevima normalizacija je poboljšala preciznost za najmanje 11 procentnih poena. Administrativni troškovi uvođenja bili su niski jer je modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema. Rad identifikuje i ograničenja: module treba ažurirati kada kompanija uvede novu terminologiju u jednom pismu, jer inicijalni rečnik sinonima nije potpun.

title: SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers
abstract: SrMIR-1, released in 2017, covered news, law, literature, and general web content. Since then, social media posts and administrative e-government documents have become important retrieval targets, both exhibiting pronounced script mixing and informal orthography. This paper describes SrMIR-2, which adds two new document registers to the benchmark: 60 000 posts from a Serbian microblogging platform and 28 000 administrative forms and decisions from three municipal e-government portals. We created 280 new topics for these registers with relevance judgments from six trained assessors (kappa = 0.69). Baseline experiments show that script-normalizing BM25 outperforms unnormalized BM25 by a larger margin on social media (22 percentage points in nDCG@10) than on administrative documents (9 points), attributable to the higher rate of informal transliteration in social media. The benchmark is released with code for reproducible evaluation. We also report an ablation study isolating the contribution of named-entity handling in the normalization pipeline.

title: Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load
abstract: Deploying script-normalizing retrieval in production requires careful attention to latency, especially when normalization involves neural components. This paper presents a systematic study of trade-offs along the latency–accuracy spectrum for five pipeline configurations ranging from a purely deterministic rule-based normalizer to a full transformer-based normalizer, tested on a simulated production workload derived from query logs of a Serbian news aggregator with peak loads of 340 queries per second. We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes. The deterministic normalizer adds 3 ms median latency with MRR of 0.61. The transformer-based normalizer achieves MRR of 0.68 but adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile. A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms. Detailed profiling data and configuration files are provided.

title: A Corpus Study of Designer Intent Encoding in Commercial Game Level Data
abstract: Understanding how human designers encode intent in level geometry is necessary for building generators that align with design goals. We manually annotated 620 levels from six released commercial-style games distributed under open licenses, tagging 14 categories of spatial intent including chokepoint placement, reward pacing, and difficulty escalation. Inter-annotator agreement reached Cohen's κ = 0.71 across three annotators. Statistical analysis reveals that chokepoint density correlates negatively with level width-to-length ratio (Pearson r = −0.43, p < 0.001) and that reward pacing patterns cluster into four archetypes by k-means on pacing-curve descriptors. We use these findings to propose a vocabulary of 14 soft-constraint templates that can be embedded in a CSP-based generator. Preliminary generation tests using three templates show that 73% of generated levels are classified into the intended archetype by a trained SVM classifier.

title: Sampling Theorems on Homogeneous Trees via Spectral Theory of the Laplace Operator
abstract: Homogeneous trees of degree q+1 carry a natural group structure when q is a prime power, allowing the application of harmonic analysis on p-adic groups. This paper establishes a Whittaker–Shannon-type sampling theorem for band-limited functions on such trees, where band-limitation is defined via the spherical Fourier transform and the spectrum of the combinatorial Laplacian. We prove that the critical sampling density for exact reconstruction equals (q+1)/2q per vertex in the natural metric on the tree, and provide an explicit interpolation formula using spherical functions as kernels. Stability under perturbation of sample locations is quantified in terms of the tree's girth. Numerical experiments on trees with q = 2, 3, 5 show that the interpolation formula converges in at most 15 iterations of a conjugate-gradient scheme to relative errors below 10^{-8}.
venue: Proceedings of the Applied Harmonic Analysis Conference (AHAC 2021), online

title: A Comparison of Signature Truncation Depths for Short Financial Price Paths
abstract: The path signature of a continuous or piecewise-linear path provides a graded sequence of features whose informational content grows with truncation depth. In practice, choosing a truncation depth involves a trade-off between feature dimensionality and expressive power. We study this trade-off systematically on intraday foreign-exchange price paths of varying length, constructed from one-minute mid-price data over a 24-month window covering four currency pairs. For each path length (30, 60, 120, and 240 minutes) and truncation depth (2 through 6), we train a regularised logistic regression to predict direction of the subsequent 15-minute return, reporting area under the ROC curve across 500 walk-forward validation windows. Depth 4 consistently offers the best accuracy-to-dimensionality ratio across all path lengths tested, with depth 5 providing marginal gains at substantially higher cost when the number of channels exceeds 5. We further show that lead-lag transformation of the bivariate price-volume path before signature extraction improves AUC by an average of 0.023. These findings provide practical guidance for practitioners applying signature methods to financial tick data without access to large computational budgets.
venue: Journal of Applied Stochastic Methods and Financial Mathematics

title: Contact quality versus contact quantity: Differential effects on prejudice reduction in a mixed Serbian–Hungarian sample
abstract: Although frequency of intergroup contact is widely studied, its qualitative dimensions—self-disclosure, equal status, institutional support—may be more consequential. A cross-sectional survey (N = 528; 267 ethnic Serbs, 261 ethnic Hungarians) was conducted across four multiethnic municipalities in Vojvodina. Respondents reported contact frequency, contact quality sub-dimensions, and attitudes toward the outgroup on a 24-item scale. Hierarchical regression analyses controlling for sociodemographic variables showed that contact quality explained an additional 17% of variance in positive outgroup attitudes beyond frequency alone (ΔR² = .17, p < .001). Self-disclosure and perceived equal status were the strongest quality components. Effects were roughly symmetric across the two groups, though equal-status perceptions were rated lower on average by minority respondents. Results are discussed in relation to the conditions that make contact effective in post-conflict settings.

title: Does reminding people of their ethnic identity increase outgroup derogation? A laboratory experiment
abstract: Identity salience manipulations are commonly used to study intergroup bias, but evidence from small minority groups in post-Yugoslav contexts is sparse. In a between-subjects experiment (N = 144 ethnic Hungarian students at the University of Novi Sad), participants were randomly assigned to an ethnic identity prime, a superordinate (European) identity prime, or a control condition before completing an outgroup evaluation task. Mixed-design ANOVA showed that ethnic priming increased derogation of Serbs relative to the superordinate prime condition (F(2, 141) = 8.34, p < .001, η² = .11) but did not significantly differ from control. Superordinate priming reduced derogation below control levels. Mediator analysis indicated that identity threat perceptions partially mediated the priming effect. Limitations include reliance on a student sample and a single ethnic community.

title: Anxiety as a mediator between contact and attitudes in Serbian–Hungarian and Serbian–Roma dyads: A comparative analysis
abstract: Intergroup anxiety is theorised to mediate the effect of contact on prejudice, but it is unclear whether this pathway is equally strong across groups with different social standing. This study used data from two independent samples collected in Vojvodina: 487 ethnic Serbs reporting on contact with ethnic Hungarians, and 423 ethnic Serbs reporting on contact with Roma. Parallel mediation models with bootstrapped confidence intervals (5,000 iterations) confirmed that intergroup anxiety significantly mediated the contact–attitude link in both samples, but the indirect effect was substantially larger for the Serbian–Roma dyad (indirect effect = −0.29, 95% CI [−0.38, −0.21]) than for the Serbian–Hungarian dyad (indirect effect = −0.14, 95% CI [−0.20, −0.09]). Group status asymmetry and historical patterns of social exclusion are proposed as explanatory factors. Policy implications for municipal integration programmes are discussed.

title: Intergroup contact and its limits: Segregated schooling as a structural barrier in Vojvodina
abstract: This book chapter reviews evidence on how school-level segregation between Serbian and Hungarian-language streams in Vojvodina constrains opportunities for meaningful intergroup contact in adolescence. Drawing on two survey studies conducted with secondary school students (Study 1: N = 389, ages 14–18; Study 2: N = 412, ages 15–19) and on qualitative interviews with school administrators (N = 14) conducted between 2014 and 2017, the chapter argues that structural separation produces low contact frequency, high intergroup anxiety, and limited friendship formation across ethnic lines. Quantitative data show that students in segregated school environments reported significantly fewer cross-ethnic friendships (M = 0.8 vs. M = 3.2 in mixed-stream schools) and higher prejudice scores on standardised measures. The chapter situates these findings within broader debates about the conditions under which institutional support for contact is necessary for prejudice reduction.

title: Threat appraisal under demographic change: Longitudinal evidence from a Vojvodina border municipality
abstract: Demographic shifts—such as outmigration of one ethnic group—can alter the perceived group size and status of both majority and minority populations, with consequences for identity threat. A two-wave longitudinal panel study (T1: 2016, T2: 2019; N = 301 retained participants; initial N = 448) tracked symbolic and realistic threat perceptions, national identification, and outgroup attitudes among ethnic Serbs and ethnic Hungarians in a municipality where the Hungarian-speaking population declined by approximately 11% over the period. Growth-curve modelling showed that symbolic threat increased significantly among ethnic Hungarians over time (B = 0.22, SE = 0.07, p = .002), while realistic threat remained stable for both groups. Stronger national identification at T1 predicted greater increase in symbolic threat at T2 among minority participants. Results underscore the value of longitudinal designs for capturing threat dynamics that cross-sectional studies miss.

title: Cross-ethnic extended contact through social media: A field survey in Novi Sad
abstract: Extended contact—the knowledge that ingroup members have outgroup friends—has been studied mainly in face-to-face contexts. This survey (N = 624, age range 18–45, residents of Novi Sad) examined whether having cross-ethnic online connections (followed or connected with members of another ethnic group on social media platforms) predicted more positive outgroup attitudes, and whether this relationship was mediated by reduced intergroup anxiety and increased outgroup inclusion in the self. Path modelling showed that online extended contact predicted positive outgroup attitudes both directly (β = 0.18, p < .001) and indirectly via reduced anxiety (β = 0.09, 95% CI [0.04, 0.15]). Effect sizes were modest and smaller than for offline extended contact measured in the same survey. The study is limited by cross-sectional design and self-reported social media use. Implications for digital platforms as potential contact spaces in multiethnic urban settings are considered.

title: Experience-sampling of intergroup encounters: Daily contact, mood, and prejudice among Hungarian-speaking students in Vojvodina
abstract: Standard survey measures of contact are retrospective and may be biased by participants' current attitudes. This study used a smartphone-based experience-sampling design over 21 consecutive days to capture naturally occurring intergroup encounters and their immediate emotional and attitudinal sequelae. Forty-eight ethnic Hungarian undergraduate students completed short end-of-day questionnaires rating the quality of any contact with ethnic Serbs that day, their current mood, and momentary warmth toward Serbs. Multilevel modelling of 862 usable day-records showed that days with at least one positive contact event were associated with higher same-evening warmth ratings (B = 0.34, SE = 0.08, p < .001) and lower negative affect (B = −0.21, SE = 0.06, p < .001). Between-person variability in average contact quality was also a significant predictor of the pre–post change in stable attitude measures collected before and after the sampling period. The methodology is resource-intensive but provides ecological validity absent from laboratory designs.

title: Does outgroup contact buffer against the prejudice-increasing effects of identity threat? An experimental test
abstract: Identity threat is generally expected to increase outgroup derogation, but prior positive contact may attenuate this response. A two-stage laboratory experiment was conducted with 186 ethnic Serbian adults recruited from the general population in Novi Sad. In Stage 1, participants completed a baseline contact quality measure. In Stage 2, half were exposed to an identity threat induction (reading a text portraying Serbian culture as declining) and half to a neutral text. Dependent variables were implicit associations (Single Category IAT) and explicit attitude ratings toward Hungarians. Consistent with predictions, the threat manipulation increased explicit derogation in the low prior-contact group (d = 0.51) but not in the high prior-contact group (d = 0.09, n.s.). No significant moderation was found for implicit associations. Findings support the idea that positive contact provides a psychological buffer against identity-threat-driven prejudice escalation.

title: Measuring contact quality in multiethnic Balkans communities: Adaptation and validation of a short scale
abstract: Existing contact quality instruments were developed mostly in Western European or North American contexts and may not transfer directly to post-conflict multiethnic settings. This paper reports the adaptation and validation of a 12-item Contact Quality Scale (CQS-12) for use in Serbian, Hungarian, and Croatian language versions in the Western Balkans. Scale items covering equal status, cooperation, self-disclosure, and institutional support were translated using committee translation and back-translation procedures. Validation was conducted across four samples totalling 1,247 participants (Vojvodina, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia) using confirmatory factor analysis. A four-factor structure showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.056) and was largely invariant across ethnic groups and countries at the metric level. Predictive validity was supported by significant correlations with outgroup attitude measures in all samples. The scale and its instructions are made available as supplementary materials.

title: Threat, contact, and policy support: Predicting attitudes toward Hungarian-language education rights in Vojvodina
abstract: Support for minority-language education policies is a politically salient outcome in Vojvodina yet has received little empirical attention from social psychologists. A representative-quota sample of 601 ethnic Serbian adults was surveyed on symbolic threat perceptions, prior contact with Hungarians, national identification, and support for institutional Hungarian-language education. Multiple regression and moderated-mediation analysis showed that symbolic threat negatively predicted policy support (β = −0.33, p < .001), and that this effect was significantly attenuated among respondents reporting high-quality prior contact (interaction B = 0.19, p = .004). National identification moderated the threat–policy link only in the subsample with low prior contact. The pattern held after controlling for political orientation and education level. Results suggest that contact interventions targeting identity-relevant policy attitudes need to address symbolic threat specifically rather than contact quantity alone.
