title: Lateral Load Capacity of Brick Masonry Wall Panels with Varying Mortar Strength: An Experimental Study
abstract: This paper presents results from a series of diagonal compression and in-plane shear tests conducted on 24 full-scale unreinforced brick masonry wall panels assembled with three mortar classes commonly used in Vojvodina's pre-1980 housing stock. Panels measured 1.2 m × 1.2 m and were constructed using locally sourced solid-fired bricks with nominal dimensions 250 × 120 × 65 mm. Mortar joint thickness was kept at 12 mm. Failure modes, peak lateral resistance, and post-peak ductility were recorded. Results indicate that panels built with weaker lime-cement mortars (compressive strength below 2.5 MPa) exhibit up to 38% lower shear capacity and markedly more brittle behaviour compared to those with standard cement mortars. The data were subsequently used to calibrate material parameters for nonlinear macro-element models. Coefficient of variation for shear strength across nominally identical specimens ranged from 0.18 to 0.24, underlining the need for probabilistic treatment of masonry material properties in vulnerability assessments.

title: Typological Classification of Pre-1980 Unreinforced Masonry Residential Buildings in Novi Sad
abstract: A systematic field survey of 312 residential buildings in four central urban blocks of Novi Sad was conducted to develop a typological classification suited to seismic vulnerability studies. Buildings were documented according to construction period, number of storeys, plan geometry, floor diaphragm type, and wall material. Approximately 64% of the surveyed stock dates from the 1918–1970 interval and uses solid fired-brick walls with timber floor beams, a combination that strongly conditions seismic response. Six building typology classes were defined, each described by a set of structural parameters with associated probability distributions derived from the survey data. The classification scheme is compatible with the European Macroseismic Scale EMS-98 vulnerability classes while incorporating local construction details specific to the Pannonian building tradition. The resulting typology matrix is intended as a reusable input layer for urban-scale fragility and loss models.

title: Derivation of Analytical Fragility Curves for Single-Storey Unreinforced Masonry Buildings Using Nonlinear Static Procedures
abstract: Fragility curves expressed in terms of peak ground acceleration (PGA) and spectral displacement (Sd) are derived for single-storey unreinforced masonry buildings representative of rural Vojvodina. Pushover analyses were performed in TREMURI for an ensemble of 80 building models whose structural parameters were sampled by Latin Hypercube Sampling from distributions established through prior field work. Four damage states corresponding to EMS-98 grades D1–D4 were defined by inter-storey drift thresholds calibrated against the experimental database assembled in earlier work. Lognormal cumulative distribution functions were fitted to each damage state, yielding median PGA values of 0.06 g, 0.10 g, 0.18 g, and 0.31 g for D1 through D4 respectively, with dispersions (β) between 0.52 and 0.68. Sensitivity analysis identifies wall slenderness ratio and mortar cohesion as the parameters with the greatest influence on median fragility. The curves are compared against macroseismic fragility functions from the literature and show reasonable consistency.

title: Seismic Loss Estimation at the Urban Block Scale: A Case Study of Three Residential Blocks in Central Novi Sad
abstract: A fully probabilistic seismic loss estimation is carried out for three adjacent residential blocks in the historic centre of Novi Sad, comprising 87 buildings representing approximately 1,400 dwelling units. Building-specific fragility curves derived from nonlinear static analysis were combined with the probabilistic seismic hazard model for the Vojvodina region, expressed as hazard curves at seven spectral periods. Monte Carlo simulation was used to propagate uncertainty through the loss model, yielding expected annual loss (EAL) values in the range of 0.08–0.22% of replacement cost per building, depending on typology class. At the block level, mean economic loss conditional on the 475-year return period ground motion is estimated at approximately €4.2 million. Spatial correlation of ground shaking within the block is shown to increase the 90th-percentile block-level loss by 31% relative to the assumption of full independence. Results are presented as loss maps intended to support municipal risk management decisions.

title: Comparison of Capacity Spectrum and N2 Methods for Estimating Seismic Displacement Demand in Masonry Building Archetypes
abstract: The Capacity Spectrum Method (CSM) and the N2 method are compared for estimating maximum inelastic displacement demand in seven unreinforced masonry building archetypes derived from the Vojvodina building stock. For each archetype, pushover curves were computed in TREMURI and transformed into capacity spectra or ADRS format as required by each procedure. Demand was evaluated using uniform hazard spectra for return periods of 95, 475, and 975 years, constructed from the national seismic hazard model. The two methods yield displacement estimates that agree within 12% for the 475-year demand level but diverge by up to 29% at the 975-year level, particularly for squat, stiff buildings where the corner period of the demand spectrum falls close to the building period. The discrepancy originates in different handling of the short-period range degradation. Implications for selecting a performance-based assessment procedure in Serbian engineering practice are discussed in light of Eurocode 8 Part 3 requirements.

title: Effect of Vertical Irregularity on the Fragility of Brick Masonry Buildings: Evidence from Post-Earthquake Reconnaissance in the Western Balkans
abstract: Post-earthquake reconnaissance data from three moderate-magnitude events (Mw 5.1–5.5) that affected predominantly masonry towns in Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia between 2013 and 2019 were compiled into a database of 641 inspected buildings. For each building, a vertical irregularity index was defined based on differences in storey height, wall density, and opening ratio between consecutive storeys, and was computed from photographic and measured survey data. Statistical analysis shows that buildings classified as vertically irregular have a 1.8 to 2.4 times higher probability of reaching damage state D3 or above at equivalent PGA levels compared with regular buildings of the same typology class. Logistic regression models are fitted to quantify the relationship between irregularity index and conditional damage probability. These results are used to propose modification factors for fragility curves derived from regular archetype analyses, providing a correction applicable when building-specific geometric data are available from GIS or cadastral sources.

title: Towards a Building-Level Exposure Model for Vojvodina Using Cadastral Records and Street-Level Imagery
abstract: A semi-automated workflow for constructing a building-level exposure model for the Vojvodina region is described, combining data from the Serbian Real Estate Cadastre, municipal building permits, and approximately 180,000 street-level photographs collected by car-mounted camera in 2021. A convolutional neural network classifier was trained on 4,200 manually labelled building façade images to assign each building to one of the six typology classes defined in earlier work, achieving a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.74 on the held-out test set. The resulting exposure model covers 47,200 residential and mixed-use buildings across 12 municipalities. Attribute completeness and classification confidence are quantified at the cadastral unit level to support uncertainty-aware loss calculations. The model is evaluated by comparing predicted typology distributions against the ground-truth field survey data collected for Novi Sad's central blocks, showing a mean absolute deviation of 8.4 percentage points across typology classes.

title: Risk-Targeted Ground Motion Parameters for Masonry Building Design in Serbia: A Preliminary Assessment
abstract: This study examines whether the constant-hazard design spectra prescribed by the current Serbian seismic code result in consistent risk levels across regions with different seismic hazard characteristics, focusing specifically on unreinforced masonry construction. Risk-targeted ground motion values are computed for 22 urban centres in Serbia by convolving code-compatible fragility curves with probabilistic seismic hazard curves derived from the 2021 national hazard model. Results show that the implied annual probability of collapse for a code-conforming one-storey masonry building ranges from 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ to 6.7 × 10⁻⁵ across the analysed locations, a factor-of-five variation that indicates significant inconsistency in the risk implied by the current prescriptive approach. Risk-targeted spectral accelerations are computed following the ASCE 7 framework and are compared with current code values; adjustments of up to +0.07 g at the 0.2 s period are identified for several moderate-seismicity towns. The study is intended to provide input to an ongoing revision of the Serbian national annex to Eurocode 8.

title: Fragility Functions for Retrofitted Unreinforced Masonry Buildings: Reinforced Plaster and Horizontal Tie Beams
abstract: Fragility curves are derived for two common low-cost seismic retrofit interventions applied to unreinforced masonry buildings: reinforced cement-mortar plaster overlay and the introduction of horizontal reinforced concrete tie beams at floor level. An ensemble of 120 building models was generated for each of three configurations—unretrofitted, plaster-retrofitted, and tie-beam-retrofitted—and analysed using nonlinear static procedures in TREMURI. Material and geometric parameters were sampled from the same probabilistic distributions used in earlier unretrofitted studies to allow direct comparison. Median PGA capacities at damage state D3 increase by 28% for the plaster intervention and by 19% for the tie-beam intervention relative to the unretrofitted baseline. Dispersion values change only modestly, remaining in the range 0.55–0.71. The study also performs a cost-benefit calculation assuming a 50-year service life and the regional hazard, finding benefit-cost ratios of 1.6–2.3 for the plaster intervention in the typology classes with the highest baseline vulnerability. Limitations related to the simplified treatment of plaster bonding failure are discussed.

title: Subsidence Detection in the Subotica–Horgoš Area Using Repeated GNSS Campaigns and Levelling Cross-Checks
abstract: The area north of Subotica along the Serbia–Hungary border has experienced observable land subsidence attributed partly to groundwater withdrawal for irrigation. Four GNSS campaign surveys (2010, 2013, 2016, 2019) at 31 benchmarks were combined with two first-order levelling runs (2011 and 2018) to construct a consistent vertical motion field. GNSS campaign data were processed with PPP using 48-hour sessions and compared against the nearest continuous station. Vertical velocities from campaign GNSS ranged from −1.1 to −4.6 mm/yr; levelling differences over seven years were consistent within ±0.5 mm/yr at 27 of 31 benchmarks. Four benchmarks near irrigation pump stations showed accelerated subsidence exceeding 5 mm/yr. Time-domain correlation with groundwater level records from eight observation wells yielded Pearson coefficients between 0.62 and 0.81 for the most affected sites. The study establishes a monitoring framework that can be maintained with biennial GNSS campaigns.

title: One-dimensional consolidation behaviour of Vojvodina lacustrine clay: comparison of Terzaghi and isotache-based models
abstract: Lacustrine clay deposits in the Vojvodina lowland exhibit pronounced creep behaviour that is poorly captured by classical Terzaghi consolidation theory. This study presents results from a series of incremental load oedometer tests conducted on undisturbed samples taken from three borehole locations near Novi Sad, at depths between 3 m and 9 m. Vertical stress increments ranged from 25 kPa to 400 kPa. The modified creep index Cα/Cc ratios were found to fall consistently between 0.045 and 0.062, suggesting moderate to high secondary compression potential. A one-dimensional isotache model implemented in a finite-difference scheme was calibrated against the measured time–settlement curves for each stress increment. Predicted end-of-primary settlements matched measurements within 8% for five of six samples, while the Terzaghi model underestimated long-term settlement by 15–30% in the same dataset. The results indicate that isotache-based formulations should be preferred for design calculations involving embankment loads on this clay unit, and a preliminary set of regional parameters is proposed for use in preliminary assessments.
venue: Geotechnical Engineering Journal of the Balkans

title: Effect of sodium silicate modulus on setting time and early strength of fly ash–slag blended alkali-activated pastes
abstract: Binary pastes containing 70 wt% Class F fly ash and 30 wt% granulated blast furnace slag were activated with sodium silicate solutions of silica modulus Ms (SiO2/Na2O molar ratio) varying from 0.5 to 2.0 at a fixed Na2O dosage of 6 wt% relative to binder mass. Isothermal calorimetry at 23 °C revealed a two-stage heat release attributed separately to slag dissolution and secondary aluminosilicate polycondensation. Initial setting time measured by Vicat needle decreased from 95 to 18 minutes as Ms increased from 0.5 to 1.5, then rebounded slightly at Ms = 2.0. Compressive strength at 7 and 28 days peaked at Ms = 1.0, reaching 42 MPa at 28 days. SEM imaging showed a denser, more homogeneous gel at Ms = 1.0 compared with the cracked morphology observed at Ms = 2.0. The study recommends Ms = 1.0 as a practical optimum for the tested precursor blend under ambient curing.

title: CFD Assessment of Stack-Driven Cross-Ventilation Through Transom Windows in a Protected Early Twentieth-Century Classroom: Influence of Furniture Layout on Air Distribution
abstract: Natural ventilation retrofits in heritage classrooms are constrained by preservation rules that typically prohibit alterations to primary facades. Transom windows above existing door and window frames represent one permissible intervention point. This study uses steady-state Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes CFD modelling in OpenFOAM 8 to assess stack-driven cross-ventilation through transom openings in a representative 72 m² classroom with a 4.2 m ceiling height. Boundary conditions were derived from a typical spring shoulder-season scenario in Novi Sad (outdoor temperature 14 °C, indoor 22 °C). Four furniture arrangements were tested, varying desk orientation and grouping pattern. Simulated air-change rates ranged from 2.1 to 4.7 ACH depending on transom opening area (0.15–0.45 m² per facade) and furniture layout. Velocity magnitude at student breathing height (1.1 m seated) remained below the 0.2 m/s draught threshold in three of four layouts. The study identifies a diagonal desk arrangement as most compatible with both adequate ventilation and draught avoidance, providing practical guidance for school administrators and conservation architects.

title: Comparative LCA of cast-in-place and precast reinforced concrete frame systems for residential buildings in Serbia
abstract: This study presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of two reinforced concrete structural systems used in Serbian residential construction: a conventional cast-in-place frame and a precast frame assembled from factory-produced columns, beams and hollow-core slabs. The system boundary follows a cradle-to-practical-completion scope (modules A1–A5 of EN 15978). Primary production data were collected from two construction sites in Novi Sad and supplemented with SimaPro 9.1 calculations using the ecoinvent 3.7 background database adapted with Serbian electricity grid data from 2019. For a representative six-storey residential building of 2 400 m² gross floor area, the precast system showed a GWP of 278 kg CO₂-eq./m² compared with 305 kg CO₂-eq./m² for cast-in-place, representing an 8.9% reduction. The dominant contributor in both cases is cement production (56–61%). Results for cumulative energy demand and water depletion show smaller differences between systems. The paper discusses sensitivity to concrete strength class and transport distance from the precast plant.
venue: Journal of Building Engineering and Materials Science

title: Adapted CUSUM Charts for Short-Run PCB Assembly Processes with Frequent Product Changeovers
abstract: Standard CUSUM charts assume steady-state process behaviour over long production runs, an assumption rarely met in contract electronics manufacturing where batch sizes range from 20 to 200 boards. This paper derives standardised CUSUM statistics referenced to a nominal process mean estimated from first-article inspection data, allowing the chart to be restarted at each product changeover without retraining. The method was validated on solder paste deposition data collected over six months at a Vojvodina-based electronics subcontractor, covering 38 distinct PCB types and 4 140 measurement records. Average run-length simulations confirm that the adapted chart reaches ARL₀ ≈ 370 at the designed false-alarm rate while achieving ARL₁ ≈ 12 at a 1.5σ shift, comparable to a conventional CUSUM under ideal long-run conditions. The paper also provides practitioner guidelines for selecting the reference value k when historical data are limited to a single reference lot.

title: Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility Study for Automated Optical Inspection Systems in Mixed-Model SMT Lines
abstract: Automated optical inspection (AOI) systems are frequently treated as error-free reference instruments in production quality loops, yet their measurement variability can be substantial when component geometry or solder fillet colour varies across product families. This study applies an expanded gauge R&R protocol, based on the AIAG MSA manual but extended for attribute and continuous mixed outputs, to two AOI stations operating in a low-volume, high-mix SMT line. Fourteen operators simulating re-inspection decisions and 120 boards carrying 18 component types were used. The within-system repeatability component accounted for 31% of total observed variation, while the between-system reproducibility component accounted for 22%. Lighting calibration drift between morning and afternoon shifts was identified as the dominant assignable cause. Recommended recalibration intervals and reference master-board specifications are proposed based on the variance component estimates.

title: Image Segmentation Threshold Selection for Solder Joint Classification Under Variable PCB Surface Finish
abstract: Global thresholding in AOI solder-joint image analysis is sensitive to surface finish variation between HASL, ENIG, and OSP boards, leading to false-reject rates that increase by a factor of two to four when finish type changes mid-batch. This paper evaluates four local thresholding approaches—Otsu, Niblack, Sauvola, and a histogram-valley method—applied to 9 600 greyscale solder-joint images captured on a custom bench-top inspection rig. Ground truth was established by cross-section analysis of 480 selected joints. Sauvola's method achieved the best F₁ score of 0.91 across all three finish types, with a false-reject rate of 4.1% and a false-accept rate of 1.8%. Processing time per image averaged 38 ms on the test hardware. The paper discusses how threshold window size interacts with pad geometry and recommends a window-size selection rule based on minimum pad dimension.

title: Control Chart Pattern Recognition Using Multilayer Perceptrons: A Comparative Study with Run-Rule Methods
abstract: Recognising non-random patterns in Shewhart X-bar charts—trends, cycles, mixtures, and stratification—is typically handled by supplementary run rules codified in Western Electric and Nelson guidelines. This paper trains a multilayer perceptron on 12 000 synthetically generated chart sequences, each 25 points long, labelled with one of eight pattern classes including in-control. Network architecture and training hyperparameters were selected by five-fold cross-validation. The neural network achieved an overall classification accuracy of 93.7%, compared with 81.2% for the full Nelson rule set and 76.5% for the Western Electric rules on the same held-out test set. False-alarm rates for the in-control class were 3.1%, 8.4%, and 9.7% respectively. The paper also reports degradation in neural-network accuracy when autocorrelation is present in the simulated data, suggesting that pattern-recognition aids should be combined with autocorrelation diagnostics in electronics assembly contexts.

title: Short-Run Process Capability Assessment for BGA Component Placement Using Bootstrap Confidence Intervals
abstract: Process capability indices such as Cp and Cpk are asymptotically derived and their confidence intervals require large sample assumptions that are violated when lot sizes are below 50 units. This paper examines bootstrap-based confidence interval construction for placement offset capability of BGA components in a small-batch electronics manufacturing context. Data were collected from a six-axis pick-and-place machine over 14 months, comprising 62 short runs of between 10 and 45 boards each, yielding 3 410 individual X-Y offset measurements verified by post-placement AOI. Bias-corrected accelerated (BCa) bootstrap intervals at 95% confidence were compared with exact non-central t-distribution intervals and standard asymptotic intervals. BCa intervals showed 12 to 18% narrower width than asymptotic intervals for n < 25, with empirical coverage probability of 94.2% versus 89.7% for the asymptotic approach. Practical tables for minimum sample size are provided.

title: In-Line Defect Detection Latency and Its Effect on Yield Loss in Low-Volume PCB Assembly: A Simulation Study
abstract: Detection latency—the number of boards produced between the onset of a process fault and its detection by in-line inspection—directly determines the expected yield loss in a batch. This paper builds a discrete-event simulation model of a representative low-volume SMT line comprising printer, SPI, placement, reflow, and AOI stations, parameterised with fault arrival rates and detection probabilities derived from 18 months of production logs at two Novi Sad contract manufacturers. Monte Carlo experiments with 10 000 replications per scenario evaluated five inspection placement strategies, ranging from AOI-only after reflow to full in-line SPI plus mid-placement inspection. Adding in-line SPI reduced mean detection latency from 7.4 boards to 2.1 boards for print-related faults, while per-board rework cost decreased by 34% on average. The model is made available as a supplementary spreadsheet tool parameterisable by the user.

title: Statistical Methods for Small-Batch Electronics Manufacturing: A Practitioner's Handbook
abstract: This book chapter reviews the landscape of statistical tools applicable when production quantities per order range from 5 to 500 units, a regime common in defence, medical device, and industrial electronics subcontracting in Central and Eastern Europe. The chapter covers short-run control charting (Q charts, DNOM charts, standardised CUSUM), attribute data analysis with small denominators, process capability estimation under non-normality, and sampling plan selection when destructive testing is required. Each section includes worked examples drawn from PCB assembly scenarios. Emphasis is placed on the organisational conditions—data recording discipline, calibration infrastructure, operator training—that determine whether statistical methods produce actionable results rather than decorative charts. The chapter is part of a multi-author handbook on quality management in SME manufacturing, edited by researchers from the University of Novi Sad and the Slovak University of Technology.

title: Colour Space Selection and Feature Extraction for AOI Classification of Tombstoned 0201 Chip Resistors
abstract: Tombstoning of 0201 chip resistors is a reflow soldering defect with a low but non-zero occurrence rate that is difficult to classify reliably with AOI systems calibrated primarily on larger components. This study compares classification performance across five colour spaces (RGB, HSV, L*a*b*, YCbCr, greyscale) and three feature extraction strategies (histogram statistics, Haralick texture features, Hu moments) using a labelled dataset of 2 240 images, 340 of which contain tombstone defects, collected from production boards. A linear discriminant classifier and a support vector machine with RBF kernel were applied to each feature-colour combination. The L*a*b* space combined with Haralick features achieved the highest classification accuracy at 97.3% with a false-accept rate of 1.2%. Run-time per image was 54 ms, consistent with in-line deployment on a standard industrial PC. Recommendations for illumination geometry are included.

title: Measurement Invariance of AOI Pseudo-Attribute Scores Across Two Inspection Generations at the Same Assembly Site
abstract: When an AOI system is replaced with a newer generation at an existing assembly site, historical quality data collected on the old system may not be directly comparable to data from the new system, compromising trend analysis and SPC continuity. This paper applies a confirmatory factor analytic framework, adapted from psychometric measurement invariance testing, to sequences of pseudo-attribute scores produced by two successive AOI systems at the same Vojvodina contract manufacturer. Data comprised 8 820 board-level score vectors spanning a 24-month transition period. Configural, metric, and scalar invariance models were fitted and compared by RMSEA, CFI, and chi-square difference tests. Scalar invariance was rejected for three of seven inspection zones, indicating that raw scores in those zones are not on a comparable scale across generations. A post-hoc equating procedure is proposed and validated on holdout data.

title: Adaptive Sampling Intervals for In-Line SPI Based on Exponential Weighted Moving Average Residuals
abstract: Fixed-interval sampling in solder paste inspection wastes inspection capacity during stable periods and responds too slowly during fault transients. This paper proposes a variable sampling interval scheme in which the time to the next mandatory inspection measurement is a decreasing function of the current EWMA residual from a target paste volume. The scheme is derived under a cost model that weights missed detections against unnecessary inspection overhead, with cost parameters estimated from historical rework logs. Simulations using paste volume sequences from three production campaigns (totalling 41 000 individual deposit measurements) show that the variable-interval scheme reduces total inspection overhead by 28% compared with a fixed 100% in-line sampling strategy while maintaining an ARL₁ of 4.1 boards at a 20% volume shift, versus ARL₁ = 3.8 for fixed-interval 100% sampling. An Excel-based setup tool is provided for practitioners.

title: Transfer Learning for AOI Defect Classification in Low-Data PCB Assembly Environments
abstract: Deep learning classifiers for AOI typically require thousands of labelled defect images per class, a volume rarely available in low-volume, high-mix PCB assembly where individual product runs are short. This paper evaluates three transfer learning strategies—feature extraction, fine-tuning of the last two convolutional blocks, and progressive unfreezing—applied to a pre-trained compact convolutional backbone retrained on an in-house dataset of 1 870 labelled solder-joint images across seven defect classes. Experiments vary the number of labelled training images per class from 20 to 200. Fine-tuning with progressive unfreezing achieved a macro-averaged F₁ score of 0.884 at 100 images per class, compared with 0.731 for feature extraction only and 0.802 for standard fine-tuning. At 40 images per class, the gap widened to 0.179 in favour of progressive unfreezing. Data augmentation strategies specific to PCB imagery, including simulated lighting variation and pad-rotation augmentation, contributed an additional 3.2 percentage points.

title: Correlating In-Line SPI Metrics with Post-Reflow AOI Outcomes: A Multivariate Regression Analysis Across Eight PCB Families
abstract: Whether solder paste inspection data can reliably predict downstream reflow defects is a practically important question for deciding where to invest inspection resources. This paper builds multivariate regression models linking eight SPI metrics (volume, area, height, X offset, Y offset, shape index, peak height, smearing ratio) to four AOI defect categories (bridging, insufficient solder, tombstoning, open joint) using matched SPI–AOI records from 14 200 boards across eight distinct PCB assemblies produced over 20 months. Ridge regression was used to handle multicollinearity among SPI predictors. Paste volume and X/Y offset emerged as the strongest predictors for bridging (R² = 0.61) and open joint (R² = 0.57) categories respectively, while tombstoning showed weak linear predictability (R² = 0.19), suggesting dominant upstream component-tape factors. Component-family-specific threshold tables derived from the regression models are reported.

title: Effect of Wire Feed Speed and Arc Voltage on Spatter Generation in Short-Arc MIG Welding of 1.5 mm Mild-Steel Sheet
abstract: This study examines the combined influence of wire feed speed (3.5–7.0 m/min) and arc voltage (16–22 V) on spatter mass loss and bead geometry in short-arc MIG welding of 1.5 mm S235JR sheet. A 3² full-factorial design with three replicates was used, yielding 27 weld runs on 150 × 80 mm coupons in flat position. Spatter was collected on adhesive-coated collector plates and weighed on a 0.1 mg resolution balance. Bead cross-sections were metallographically prepared and measured for width, penetration depth, and reinforcement height. Results show that arc voltage has the dominant effect on spatter mass, accounting for 61 % of total variance in the ANOVA model, while wire feed speed primarily governs penetration. A voltage window of 17.5–18.5 V at 5.5 m/min feed rate reduced spatter by 38 % relative to the supplier-recommended default settings without compromising joint tensile strength, verified by cross-weld tensile tests at 415 ± 12 MPa.

title: Particle filter estimation of remaining useful life for carbide turning inserts under variable cutting conditions
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) estimation for turning inserts under variable cutting conditions requires a state-estimation framework that can handle nonlinear wear dynamics and changing inputs. This paper applies a sequential Monte Carlo (particle filter) approach in which the state variable is flank-wear land VB and the observation is a fused feature derived from cutting force ratio Fp/Fc and AE RMS. The wear evolution model follows a modified Paris-law form with feed rate and cutting speed as exogenous inputs; model parameters were identified from 40 reference trials. RUL was estimated online and compared against true remaining tool life measured post-hoc. At 50% of tool life consumed, the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of RUL prediction was 14.3% across 20 validation trials with varying speed–feed profiles. A baseline autoregressive model yielded MAPE of 31.7% on the same set. Computational cost was 38 ms per update step (500 particles) on a standard laptop, compatible with real-time operation at 1 Hz update rate.

title: Surface roughness prediction in CNC boring using process-parameter regression augmented with in-cycle vibration features
abstract: Dimensional and surface-finish compliance in bored bearing seats depends on both programmed cutting parameters and on dynamic events within the cut. This study constructs regression models for Ra and Rz in horizontal boring of nodular cast iron GJS-500-7, combining six process parameters (cutting speed, feed, depth, bore diameter, bar overhang ratio, insert nose radius) with four vibration-based features extracted from radial accelerometer signals. A dataset of 144 bores under a central-composite design was split 70/30 for training and testing. A gradient-boosting tree model (50 trees, maximum depth 4) achieved RMSE of 0.11 µm for Ra on the test set, versus 0.19 µm for a purely parametric multiple-regression baseline. Feature importance analysis showed that the vibration feature representing 3rd-harmonic amplitude at the boring-bar resonance frequency ranked second overall, behind feed rate. The practical implication is that damping the boring bar at its first bending mode can reduce surface roughness scatter by approximately 22% without changing programmed parameters.

title: Benchmark of density-based topology optimisation solvers for stiffness-constrained aerospace bracket geometries
abstract: This study compares three density-based topology optimisation implementations—two commercial finite-element packages and one open-source MATLAB routine—applied to a standardised aerospace-style bracket subject to three independent load cases. The test geometry was a 120 × 80 × 60 mm aluminium alloy design domain with a mass target of 40 % of the solid volume. Convergence behaviour, final compliance values, and grey-element fraction were recorded across 200 iterations for each solver. The commercial solvers reached comparable compliance minima within 5 % of each other, while the open-source routine produced 12 % higher grey-element fractions and required manual filtering. Penalisation exponents from 2 to 4 were tested; p = 3 gave the most manufacturable result across all three tools. The paper provides input files and mesh descriptions to support reproducibility. Results indicate that solver choice has a moderate but non-negligible influence on final geometry, and that post-processing thresholding strategy accounts for a larger share of geometric variation than the optimisation algorithm itself.

title: Effect of pH and dissolved oxygen on Fe(II) oxidation kinetics in synthetic groundwater matrices
abstract: Laboratory kinetic experiments were conducted to quantify the rate of Fe(II) oxidation to Fe(III) in synthetic groundwater over a pH range of 6.0–8.5 and dissolved oxygen concentrations of 1.0–8.5 mg/L. Initial Fe(II) concentrations of 0.5, 2.0, and 5.0 mg/L were tested in buffered solutions at 20 °C and ionic strength adjusted to 0.01 M with NaClO₄. Pseudo-first-order rate constants increased by approximately one order of magnitude per pH unit increase above pH 7, consistent with the empirical rate law reported in earlier literature. The half-life of Fe(II) at pH 6.5 and 2 mg/L dissolved oxygen was approximately 180 minutes, dropping to under 4 minutes at pH 8.0. Bicarbonate alkalinity at 250 mg/L as CaCO₃ accelerated the oxidation relative to phosphate-buffered controls, suggesting carbonate complex participation. Results are relevant to aeration–oxidation sequences in iron removal plants in Vojvodina where groundwater alkalinity is high.

title: Cr(VI) and Cr(III) speciation in electroplating effluents using differential pulse cathodic stripping voltammetry
abstract: A differential pulse cathodic stripping voltammetric (DPCSV) method was adapted for simultaneous determination of Cr(VI) and Cr(III) in effluents from three electroplating facilities in the Novi Sad industrial zone. Sample pre-treatment involved complexation with diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (DTPA) at controlled pH prior to adsorptive accumulation on a hanging mercury drop electrode. Calibration was linear between 0.5 and 120 µg/L for both species, with detection limits of 0.18 µg/L for Cr(VI) and 0.24 µg/L for Cr(III). Matrix interference from Fe(III) was suppressed by 1,10-phenanthroline masking. Analysis of twenty-three effluent samples showed Cr(VI) concentrations between 1.2 and 87 mg/L, substantially exceeding current Serbian discharge limits in eleven cases. Results were cross-validated against ICP-OES after speciation-preserving ion exchange separation. The method provides a practical analytical tool for routine industrial monitoring without requiring expensive instrumentation.

title: Coagulation of synthetic manganese-bearing water with aluminium sulfate: jar-test optimisation and floc characterisation
abstract: Jar-test experiments were performed on synthetic water containing 0.5–4.0 mg/L dissolved Mn(II) at pH values between 6.5 and 8.5 to optimise aluminium sulfate (alum) dosing for manganese removal. Pre-oxidation with KMnO₄ at stoichiometric doses converted Mn(II) to colloidal MnO₂ prior to coagulation. Optimal alum dose was 25 mg/L at pH 7.8, achieving residual total manganese below 0.05 mg/L and turbidity below 0.5 NTU after 20-minute sedimentation. Floc size distribution was measured by laser diffraction; mean volume-weighted diameter increased from 18 µm at sub-optimal doses to 112 µm at optimal conditions. Zeta potential shifted from −22 mV at under-dosing to near-zero at optimal conditions, consistent with charge neutralisation as the dominant destabilisation mechanism. Alum dose requirements increased linearly with initial Mn concentration. The results support design guidelines for small water treatment plants in communities relying on Mn-rich aquifer sources.

title: Influence of natural organic matter fractions on copper speciation in drinking water distribution systems
abstract: Copper speciation in water samples collected from fourteen points along a municipal distribution network in Vojvodina was examined as a function of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) fractions separated by size exclusion chromatography. Total copper, dissolved copper (<0.45 µm), and electrochemically labile copper were quantified by ICP-OES and anodic stripping voltammetry (ASV). DOC fractions ranged from 1.8 to 6.4 mg/L with hydrophilic acids constituting 55–70 % of total DOC. Labile Cu(II) correlated inversely with the high-molecular-mass humic fraction (r = −0.81), indicating preferential complexation by humic substances. At sites with longer hydraulic residence time, total copper increased by up to 0.12 mg/L relative to the treatment plant outlet, attributed to pipe corrosion under locally low pH conditions (6.9–7.1). The findings suggest that DOC management at source could reduce copper complexation capacity and hence corrosion-derived copper accumulation in distribution.

title: Optimisation of polyaluminium chloride dosing for removal of iron and turbidity from lowland river intakes
abstract: A systematic jar-test study examined polyaluminium chloride (PACl) as an alternative to conventional alum for treating Tisa River intake water during high-turbidity flood periods. Seven PACl basicity levels (Al₂O₃ content 9–18 %) and doses of 5–50 mg/L were tested against raw water turbidity of 30–280 NTU, total iron 0.8–5.6 mg/L, and temperature ranging from 5 to 22 °C. At 12 °C, PACl with 14 % Al₂O₃ at 20 mg/L reduced turbidity to below 1 NTU and total iron to below 0.1 mg/L with a shorter flocculation time (12 min) compared to alum (20 min). Response surface methodology (Box–Behnken design) was applied to model residual turbidity as a function of dose, basicity, and temperature; the fitted model had R² = 0.94. PACl performed better than alum at water temperatures below 10 °C. Sludge volume index was 20 % lower for PACl-generated flocs, reducing sludge handling costs. Practical implications for seasonal treatment strategy are outlined.

title: Chromium(VI) reduction kinetics by dissolved Fe(II) in the presence of phosphate and silicate ligands at circumneutral pH
abstract: Batch experiments quantified the rate of Cr(VI) reduction by Fe(II) under conditions relevant to subsurface remediation: pH 6.5–8.0, Fe(II) 0.1–5.0 mM, Cr(VI) 0.05–0.5 mM, and background electrolyte containing 0, 1, and 5 mM orthophosphate or orthosilicate. Second-order rate constants were derived from initial-rate data at 25 °C. Phosphate at 1 mM decreased the apparent rate constant by 35–48 % across all pH values tested, attributed to Fe(II)-phosphate complexation reducing the reactive free Fe²⁺ fraction. Silicate at equivalent concentration had negligible effect below pH 7.5 but caused a 22 % rate reduction at pH 8.0. The reduction product was characterised by XPS as a mixed Cr(III)/Fe(III) oxy-hydroxide with a Cr:Fe molar ratio of approximately 1:4. Ionic strength (0.01–0.1 M NaClO₄) had no significant effect. Results constrain the range of Fe(II) doses required for in situ Cr(VI) remediation in phosphate-rich alluvial aquifers.

title: Speciation and mobility of trace copper in sediment pore water from agricultural drainage channels: a sequential extraction study
abstract: Copper speciation and mobility were investigated in sediment and overlying pore water from six agricultural drainage channels in Vojvodina, areas receiving effluent from orchards treated with copper-based fungicides. Sequential extraction (Tessier scheme, five fractions) was applied to surface sediment (0–5 cm) and two deeper layers (5–10 and 10–20 cm) at each site. Total copper in surface sediments ranged from 42 to 318 mg/kg dry weight. The exchangeable plus carbonate-bound fraction accounted for 8–21 % of total copper in surface layers, indicating moderate potential mobility. Pore water Cu concentrations determined by DPASV ranged from 12 to 180 µg/L and correlated positively with the exchangeable fraction (r = 0.88). Organic-matter-bound fraction dominated (38–55 %) in the upper horizon. Seasonal redox fluctuations, inferred from dissolved Fe/Mn ratios in pore water, influenced the partitioning between reducible and residual fractions. The data support risk assessment under European Water Framework Directive criteria.

title: Electrocoagulation as a pretreatment for chromate-bearing industrial rinse water: effect of current density and electrolysis time
abstract: Electrocoagulation (EC) with iron sacrificial electrodes was evaluated for Cr(VI) removal from rinse water collected at a surface finishing plant in Novi Sad. Experiments were carried out in a batch EC reactor (2-litre working volume, two parallel Fe electrode pairs) at current densities of 5, 10, 20, and 40 mA/cm², electrolysis times of 5–60 minutes, and initial Cr(VI) concentrations of 5–50 mg/L. At 20 mA/cm² and 30 minutes, Cr(VI) removal exceeded 99 % for initial concentrations up to 20 mg/L at pH 7.0. Mechanism analysis using Fe:Cr molar ratios in the sludge confirmed simultaneous Cr(VI) reduction by electrogenerated Fe(II) and co-precipitation of Cr(III) with Fe(III) hydroxide. Energy consumption was 1.8 kWh/m³ at optimal conditions. Electrode passivation was observed above 40 mA/cm² after 20 minutes, reducing removal efficiency by up to 15 %. Scale-up implications and comparison with chemical reduction–precipitation are discussed.

title: Speciation of vanadium in petrochemical wastewater using solvent extraction coupled with ICP-OES
abstract: A sequential solvent extraction procedure was developed and validated for the determination of V(IV) (vanadyl) and V(V) (vanadate) in complex petrochemical process water with high sulfate and chloride backgrounds. V(V) was selectively extracted into 0.1 M Aliquat 336 in toluene at pH 2.0, while V(IV) was determined in the raffinate after oxidative back-extraction. Method validation was performed on certified reference material (synthetic multi-element water standard) and spiked petrochemical samples. Recovery ranged from 94 to 103 % for both species. The procedure was applied to effluent samples from a refinery in the Pannonian region collected across four seasons; V(V) ranged from 0.08 to 1.34 mg/L and V(IV) from 0.02 to 0.47 mg/L, with V(V) dominating in aerobic process streams and V(IV) in anaerobic equalization basins. Implications for catalytic vanadium recovery and discharge compliance are briefly discussed.

title: Coagulation–flocculation of nickel-bearing electroplating wastewater with ferric chloride: response surface optimisation and residual speciation
abstract: Response surface methodology (central composite design) was applied to optimise ferric chloride coagulation for nickel removal from synthetic and real electroplating rinse water. Factors studied were FeCl₃ dose (10–150 mg/L), pH (7.0–10.5), and rapid-mix intensity (G = 40–150 s⁻¹). Residual total Ni, dissolved Ni, and dissolved Fe in the clarified effluent were measured by ICP-OES. The empirical model for residual Ni showed R² = 0.96; optimal conditions were pH 9.8, FeCl₃ dose 80 mg/L, and G = 80 s⁻¹, yielding residual dissolved Ni below 0.1 mg/L from an initial concentration of 12 mg/L. At pH values above 10.2, Ni removal declined due to anionic nickelate complex formation. DPASV analysis of clarified water indicated that the residual Ni was predominantly in a labile free-ion or weakly complexed form, not adsorbed to colloidal Fe-hydroxide. Sludge Ni content averaged 3.8 % by mass under optimal conditions, relevant for recovery decisions.

title: Iron and manganese co-removal in a pilot-scale continuous-flow coagulation–sedimentation unit: interactions and treatment efficiency at varying Fe/Mn ratios
abstract: A pilot-scale continuous-flow unit (30 L/h) was operated over fourteen weeks to examine the simultaneous removal of iron and manganese from synthetic water at Fe/Mn mass ratios of 1:1, 5:1, and 20:1, representing conditions encountered at different groundwater sources in Vojvodina. Pre-oxidation with ozone (1.0 mg/L) was followed by coagulation with polyaluminium chloride at a fixed dose of 18 mg/L. Effluent total Fe and Mn were measured daily by ICP-OES; Mn speciation in the clarified effluent was assessed weekly by DPCSV. At Fe/Mn = 20:1, Mn removal was enhanced (96 %) compared to single-solute tests (88 %), consistent with autocatalytic Mn(II) oxidation on freshly formed Fe-hydroxide surface sites. At low Fe/Mn ratios (1:1), competition for coagulant capacity reduced Fe removal by 12 percentage points. Floc settling velocity data fitted a modified Stokes relation with a density correction term for mixed Fe/Mn oxide composition. These results inform simultaneous Fe and Mn removal strategies in rural water supply systems.

title: Effect of humectant type and concentration on water activity and microbial challenge performance in oil-in-water facial emulsions
abstract: Three humectants—glycerol, propylene glycol, and sorbitol—were evaluated at four concentrations (5, 10, 15, and 20% w/w) in a standardised oil-in-water facial emulsion containing 0.8% phenoxyethanol as the sole preservative. Water activity (aw) was measured using a capacitance-based dew-point meter at 25 °C. A modified challenge test following ISO 11930:2019 criteria was performed with Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Candida albicans, Aspergillus brasiliensis, and Escherichia coli inocula of approximately 106 CFU/g. Glycerol reduced aw from 0.992 to 0.961 at 20%, whereas sorbitol achieved 0.953 at the same level. Challenge test category A criteria were met only when aw ≤ 0.970 regardless of humectant type, suggesting that aw reduction rather than humectant identity is the controlling factor. Rheological measurements confirmed that sorbitol at 15% produced a yield stress of 8.4 Pa, which may independently limit microbial motility. The results allow formulation of adequate preservation with reduced preservative concentrations when humectant selection is guided by aw targets.

title: Low-molecular-weight organic acid concentrations in soil pore water of sunflower and maize rhizospheres in calcareous Chernozem: field measurements over a growing season
abstract: Input concentrations of organic acids for speciation models are often taken from pot experiments or single-time-point measurements, which may not reflect field variability. This study measured citrate, malate, oxalate, succinate and acetate by ion chromatography in pore-water centrifuge extracts from rhizosphere and bulk soil of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) and maize (Zea mays) grown on a calcareous Chernozem near Srbobran, Vojvodina. Samples were collected at five growth stages (V4, V8, flowering, grain fill, maturity) in 2018. Citrate ranged 0.8–18.4 µM (rhizosphere) and 0.3–3.1 µM (bulk); malate ranged 1.2–22.7 µM and 0.5–4.0 µM. Oxalate was consistently the most abundant acid (8–52 µM rhizosphere). Maize rhizosphere citrate concentrations at flowering were 2.3-fold higher than sunflower. These seasonal and crop-specific ranges define realistic boundary conditions for speciation model scenarios rather than single assumed values.

title: Genetic and phenotypic parameters for litter size at birth and weaning in a Mangalica × Landrace F1 population
abstract: Crossbreeding Mangalica sows with Landrace boars is a common practice among Vojvodina producers seeking to improve litter size while retaining carcass quality associated with the indigenous breed. This study estimated genetic and phenotypic parameters for TNB, NBA, number weaned (NW), and piglet weight at weaning (PWW) using records from 2,318 litters on seven commercial and semi-commercial farms collected over eight farrowing seasons (2009–2016). Bivariate animal models were fitted with ASReml 4.1. Heritabilities ranged from 0.06 for NW to 0.12 for PWW. Genetic correlations between TNB and NBA were high and positive (0.87 ± 0.09), while the genetic correlation between NBA and NW was moderate (0.41 ± 0.14). Permanent environmental effects of the sow accounted for 6–9% of phenotypic variance across traits. Results suggest that selection on NBA would produce modest correlated responses in NW under field conditions typical of Vojvodina smallholder farms.

title: Inbreeding trends and their association with litter size in the registered Vojvodina Mangalica population, 1995–2015
abstract: Using pedigree records from the Vojvodina Mangalica Breeders Association covering 4,786 animals born between 1995 and 2015, the effective population size and inbreeding coefficients were computed with the CFC software. Mean inbreeding increased from near zero in the mid-1990s to 3.8% by 2015, with an effective population size estimate of 42 animals based on the rate of inbreeding per generation. Regression of total number born on the individual inbreeding coefficient of the sow showed a statistically significant inbreeding depression of −0.18 piglets per 10% increase in F (P < 0.05). Litter size of inbred litters as a whole was not significantly affected when controlling for sow age and herd environment, indicating that dam performance dominates over direct litter inbreeding at current levels. These findings support the implementation of minimum-kinship mating schemes to slow the accumulation of inbreeding in this numerically small indigenous breed.

title: Comparison of single-trait and multi-trait animal models for estimating breeding values for litter size in Mangalica × Landrace crossbreeds
abstract: Breeding value estimation for litter size in pig populations with small datasets may be sensitive to the choice of model structure. This study compared estimated breeding values (EBVs) and their accuracies obtained from single-trait versus multi-trait animal models applied to records for TNB, NBA, and NW from 1,894 F1 Mangalica × Landrace sows on five farms over nine years. Variance components were estimated by REML and EBVs were computed using BLUP methodology in ASReml. Rank correlations between EBVs from the two model types exceeded 0.93 for TNB and NBA but dropped to 0.81 for NW, suggesting that the multi-trait model provides more stable ranking of sows for weaning performance. Mean EBV accuracy was slightly higher under the multi-trait model (0.41 vs. 0.37 for TNB), primarily because of the borrowing of information across correlated traits. Practical implications for small-scale selection programs in Vojvodina are discussed.

title: Fixed and random effects structure for litter size models in Vojvodina Mangalica crossbreeds: sensitivity analysis
abstract: The robustness of variance component estimates for total number born (TNB) and number born alive (NBA) to alternative specifications of fixed and random effects was examined using a dataset of 3,041 farrowing records from six farms spanning parities 1–7. Models tested differed in the inclusion of herd-year-season, year-season across herds, linear and quadratic parity regressions, and the presence or absence of a common litter environment effect. Restricted maximum likelihood was applied with a derivative-free algorithm. Heritability estimates for TNB ranged from 0.07 to 0.13 depending on model specification, with the largest inflation occurring when herd-year-season was omitted. Including a common litter random effect did not significantly improve model fit as assessed by log-likelihood ratio tests. Results indicate that proper accounting for contemporary group is more influential than litter environment specification in this crossbred population. Recommendations for routine genetic evaluation practice are provided.

title: Estimation of genetic trend for litter size in registered Vojvodina Mangalica herds under selection using national recording data
abstract: Using 22 years of official performance recording data (2000–2021) from the Vojvodina Mangalica Breeders Association, this study estimated annual genetic trends for TNB and NBA by regressing average annual EBVs on birth year. Records encompassed 6,114 litters from 1,823 sows across 18 registered herds. EBVs were derived from a repeatability model using ASReml. The estimated genetic trend was near zero for TNB (+0.004 piglets per year, P = 0.38) and marginally positive for NBA (+0.006 piglets per year, P = 0.09). Phenotypic trends over the same period were slightly larger, suggesting that management improvement contributed more to observed performance gains than selection. Heritability from the full dataset was 0.10 ± 0.02 for TNB. The absence of a meaningful positive genetic trend reflects the absence of a structured selection program and the priority given to conservation objectives over performance improvement in Mangalica breeding.

title: Genomic versus pedigree-based breeding value prediction for litter size in a small Mangalica × Landrace reference population
abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of genomic prediction for TNB and NBA in a limited-size reference population of 412 genotyped Mangalica × Landrace F1 sows phenotyped over five consecutive farrowing seasons. Animals were genotyped on the PorcineSNP60 array and quality-controlled markers numbered 43,218 after filtering for call rate and minor allele frequency. Genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs) were obtained with a single-step GBLUP (ssGBLUP) approach blending the genomic and pedigree-based relationship matrices. Predictive ability, assessed by five-fold cross-validation, was 0.24 for TNB and 0.21 for NBA, marginally exceeding pedigree BLUP accuracies of 0.19 and 0.18 respectively. The modest gain reflects the low heritability of the target traits and the small reference population size. A power analysis indicates that at least 1,200 phenotyped and genotyped sows would be needed to achieve a meaningful improvement in prediction accuracy under this population structure.

title: Dietary DDGS level influences rumen archaeal community structure and methanogen relative abundance in Holstein heifers
abstract: Methanogenic archaea in the rumen are the primary source of enteric methane, yet their response to bioethanol co-products in the diet of young dairy heifers is undercharacterised. Rumen contents from 30 Holstein heifers (5 per dietary group: 0, 10, 20, 30% corn DDGS) were collected at slaughter after 75 days on trial. DNA was extracted and the archaeal 16S rRNA gene (V4–V5 region) was sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform. Methanobrevibacter dominated all samples, accounting for 78–84% of archaeal reads. Its relative abundance declined with increasing DDGS inclusion, reaching its lowest value in the 30% group (78.1%, vs. 84.3% in control; P = 0.02). Methanosphaera abundance was inversely related to DDGS level. Total archaeal alpha diversity (Shannon index) increased slightly at 20% inclusion. Partial least squares regression linked lower archaeal abundance to higher propionate concentration in rumen fluid, consistent with competitive hydrogen utilisation. Findings support the hypothesis that DDGS-driven propionate shifts modestly suppress methanogenesis.

title: Residues of chlorpyrifos and cypermethrin in compound cattle feed from Vojvodina and their in vitro androgenic antagonism potential
abstract: Organophosphate and pyrethroid insecticides applied during cereal production can persist in finished feed. This study quantified chlorpyrifos and cypermethrin in 68 commercial compound cattle feed samples using QuEChERS extraction and GC-MS/MS. Chlorpyrifos was detected in 54% of samples (mean 0.018 mg/kg; max 0.081 mg/kg) and cypermethrin in 61% (mean 0.024 mg/kg; max 0.11 mg/kg). All values remained below the EU MRLs for animal feed. A reporter gene assay using an AR-CALUX cell line was performed on sample extracts at environmentally relevant concentrations. Extracts from 11 samples (16%) showed statistically significant androgen receptor antagonism at concentrations equivalent to 0.1 g feed/mL medium, with the effect attributable predominantly to cypermethrin based on fractionation. Estimated daily intakes were below threshold levels for systemic effects in adult cows; however, given accumulation potential in high-producing animals, continued surveillance is warranted. The study establishes a combined chemical-analytical and bioassay surveillance framework applicable to regional feed monitoring.

title: Seasonal dynamics of zearalenone and phytoestrogen co-exposure and their association with first-service conception rate in a commercial Holstein herd: a 3-year longitudinal analysis
abstract: Reproductive performance in dairy herds fluctuates seasonally and is influenced by numerous factors, including diet composition. This 3-year longitudinal study (2019–2022) followed a single commercial Holstein herd of 310 cows in southern Vojvodina, recording monthly ZEN concentrations in total mixed ration, estimated daily isoflavone intake, first-service conception rate (FSCR), and serum progesterone at day 7 post-insemination as a corpus luteum function proxy. Mixed-effects logistic regression showed that monthly TMR ZEN above 0.6 mg/kg DM was associated with a 14 percentage-point reduction in FSCR (OR 0.52; 95% CI 0.38–0.72), independently of parity, days in milk, and BCS. Isoflavone intake above 200 mg/cow/day further reduced the probability of conception (OR 0.71; 95% CI 0.53–0.96), and the two predictors showed a borderline interaction (p = 0.06). Autumn seasons, coinciding with peak silage ZEN, consistently showed the lowest FSCR (mean 32% vs. 44% in spring). The results support routine feed ZEN monitoring as a management tool to improve reproductive outcomes.
venue: Journal of Dairy Cattle Management and Science

title: Effect of extrusion temperature on starch gelatinisation and subsequent digestibility in carp diets
abstract: Extrusion barrel temperature was varied at four levels (110, 130, 150, and 170°C) during processing of a maize-soybean-based diet to examine the relationship between starch gelatinisation degree and apparent digestibility of dry matter, starch, and crude protein in common carp. Gelatinisation was quantified by differential scanning calorimetry. Diets were fed to carp averaging 85 g initial weight in indoor tanks over 42 days, with chromic oxide included as a marker. Starch gelatinisation increased from 48% at 110°C to 97% at 170°C. Starch ADC improved from 74.1% to 89.3% across the same range, while crude protein ADC showed a smaller but significant increase from 82.1% to 86.8%. Feed pellet water stability declined at higher temperatures. The 150°C treatment offered the best balance between nutrient digestibility and pellet integrity, with a specific growth rate of 1.43% body weight per day. Results suggest that extrusion temperature is a critical processing parameter for carp diets.

title: Chromium propionate and betaine co-supplementation under heat stress: effects on insulin sensitivity, dry matter intake, and milk fat desaturation indices in early-lactation cows
abstract: Forty early-lactation Holstein-Friesian cows (5–45 days in milk) were enrolled in a 2×2 factorial trial during a summer period with mean THI of 76.9. Treatments were chromium propionate (Cr, 10 mg/day), betaine (Bet, 100 g/day), both (Cr+Bet), or control. Blood glucose, insulin, and non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) concentrations were measured on days 0, 15, and 42. Milk fatty acid profiles were determined by GC-FID. The Cr+Bet group maintained significantly lower NEFA concentrations on day 15 compared to control (0.31 vs. 0.52 mmol/L, p < 0.01), suggesting improved negative energy balance management. Desaturation index (C18:1/C18:0) was highest in the Cr+Bet group, indicating maintained delta-9-desaturase activity under heat load. Dry matter intake was 0.8 kg/day higher in Cr+Bet than control. No differences in milk protein content were found. Results support a potential combined use of osmoregulatory and insulinogenic additives to preserve milk fat quality during thermally stressful periods.

title: Markov-Based Transition Systems for Adaptive Ambient Sound in Branching Narrative Games
abstract: This paper examines first- and second-order Markov chains as a mechanism for governing timbral and harmonic transitions in ambient soundscapes designed for video games with branching story structures. A prototype system was implemented in Max/MSP and tested within a purpose-built text-adventure game environment across two narrative trees containing 47 and 63 decision nodes respectively. Twenty-four participants completed both linear and non-linear playthroughs while self-reporting immersion and emotional coherence on validated post-session questionnaires. Results showed that second-order Markov models produced significantly fewer perceptually abrupt transitions compared to first-order models (p < 0.05), while maintaining an acceptable degree of sonic unpredictability rated positively by 79% of participants. The paper also discusses the computational overhead of the two approaches on standard consumer hardware and proposes a lightweight implementation strategy suitable for real-time deployment. Limitations include the small sample size and the use of a text-only game engine, which removes visual context as a confounding variable.

title: Procedural Audio for Emotional Valence Modulation: A Comparative Study of Rule-Based and Data-Driven Approaches
abstract: The paper compares two architectures for real-time procedural audio generation intended to modulate listener emotional valence: a rule-based system encoded with music-theoretic heuristics and a data-driven system trained on a corpus of 340 short electroacoustic pieces labelled by affect using a two-dimensional valence-arousal model. Both systems were implemented in SuperCollider and evaluated in a within-subjects experiment with 40 participants who navigated a custom 3D environment. Emotional state was measured every 90 seconds using the Self-Assessment Manikin scale and cross-validated with continuous galvanic skin response recordings. The rule-based system achieved more predictable valence trajectories (deviation from target: mean 0.31 on a 9-point scale), while the data-driven system produced ratings of greater naturalness and variety. The paper argues for hybrid architectures that delegate coarse emotional shaping to rule-based logic while using learned models for fine-grained timbral variation. Source code is provided as a supplementary appendix.

title: Granular Synthesis Parameters as Narrative Signifiers in Non-Linear Cinema
abstract: This chapter examines how granular synthesis parameters—grain density, grain duration, and pitch scatter—can function as consistent audio signifiers encoding narrative information in interactive film systems where traditional non-diegetic music is impractical. Drawing on semiotic frameworks from film sound theory, the author proposes a mapping schema in which three discrete narrative states (tension, resolution, ambiguity) correspond to measurable parameter ranges empirically derived from listener sorting tasks with 22 participants. Participants were presented with 90 granular audio fragments and asked to assign each to one of the three categories; inter-rater reliability reached Krippendorff's alpha of 0.71 for tension and 0.68 for resolution, with ambiguity proving less reliably categorised (0.44). The chapter concludes with a discussion of how such a schema can be embedded in branching video players without disrupting narrative continuity at decision points, and notes the difficulty of maintaining signifier stability across widely varying source material.

title: Spatialisation Strategies for Ambisonics-Based Procedural Soundscapes in Museum Contexts
abstract: This paper reports on the design and technical evaluation of a third-order ambisonics playback system installed in a permanent exhibition room at the Museum of Vojvodina, Novi Sad. Procedurally generated soundscapes representing three historical periods were decoded to a 16-speaker array using a custom Max/MSP decoder patch calibrated to the irregular room geometry. Room impulse responses were measured at 12 listener positions and used to adapt the decoding matrix. Localisation accuracy was assessed in a controlled perceptual test with 18 listeners using a head-pointing method; mean angular error was 8.3 degrees in the horizontal plane and 14.1 degrees in the vertical plane. Dynamic object spatialisation driven by exhibit proximity triggers was found to sustain visitor attention measurably longer (mean 4.2 minutes versus 2.7 minutes in a control condition with stereo playback). Practical constraints of museum installation—irregular ceilings, diffuse surfaces, and variable visitor density—are discussed in detail.

title: State-Machine Audio Engines: Architecture and Authoring Workflow for Small Independent Game Studios
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of a lightweight state-machine audio engine called Resonator, built on top of the FMOD Studio API, intended specifically for independent game studios with limited audio programming resources. The engine allows composers and sound designers to author procedural audio behaviours through a graphical node-based interface without writing engine-level code. A usability evaluation was conducted with six two-person teams from three independent studios in Novi Sad and Zagreb; teams were asked to reproduce a reference adaptive audio implementation from a published game and then extend it with a new mechanic. Task completion time dropped by approximately 38% compared to native FMOD scripting in a counterbalanced within-subjects design, and perceived workload measured by the NASA-TLX was significantly lower (p < 0.01). The paper includes architecture diagrams and a discussion of the trade-offs between authoring accessibility and runtime flexibility.

title: Perceptual Thresholds for Procedural Variation in Looping Game Audio
abstract: A persistent challenge in game audio is the audible repetition of looped sound assets, which can break immersion. This study empirically measures perceptual thresholds for detecting repetition in procedurally varied audio loops by systematically modulating five synthesis parameters—filter cutoff frequency, reverb pre-delay, tempo microvariation, stereo width, and grain density—across eight levels each. Sixty participants completed an ABX discrimination test for each parameter independently, and detection thresholds were estimated using a maximum-likelihood method. Results show that filter cutoff shifts below approximately 180 Hz in the low-mid band and tempo microvariation below 3 ms were reliably undetected, providing practical minimum variation budgets for designers aiming to create perceptually distinct loops within tight computational budgets. Interactions between parameters were explored in a secondary experiment with 30 participants, revealing that simultaneous modulation of three or more parameters at sub-threshold levels was detected significantly more often than single-parameter modulation at equivalent magnitude.

title: Designing Silence: The Structural Role of Deliberate Audio Absence in Interactive Narrative
abstract: While procedural audio research has focused largely on sound generation, this paper examines the design and perceptual function of deliberately engineered silences within procedural audio systems for interactive narrative. Drawing on 14 semi-structured interviews with professional game audio designers from studios in the former Yugoslav countries, the paper develops a taxonomy of five functional silence types: anticipatory, consequential, liminal, disorienting, and contemplative. Each type is characterised by its triggering condition, typical duration range, and the procedural audio state it interrupts or follows. The taxonomy was validated through a second round of interviews and a card-sorting exercise with eight additional designers. A short experimental game prototype implementing all five silence types was used to test whether players could correctly attribute intended emotional function to silence episodes; attribution accuracy ranged from 61% (disorienting) to 84% (anticipatory). The paper argues that silence deserves explicit representation in procedural audio authoring tools.

title: Generative Score Composition for a 90-Minute Interactive Documentary: Process and Evaluation
abstract: This paper describes the compositional process and post-release evaluation of the generative musical score created for the interactive documentary Reka, a 90-minute non-linear film about the Danube waterway released through an online platform in 2020. The score comprised 214 audio modules organised into a hierarchical state machine implemented in Max/MSP and compiled to a WebAudio API runtime. Module transitions were governed by viewer navigation events, time-of-day metadata, and cumulative viewing history. A content analysis of 3,400 anonymously logged viewer sessions tracked which narrative paths were taken and correlated path length with session abandonment. Sessions in which procedural score continuity was preserved across three or more editorial cuts had a 22% lower abandonment rate than sessions encountering a detectable musical discontinuity. Composer's log excerpts illustrate decisions about modular granularity and the management of harmonic ambiguity across unforeseeable viewing sequences.

title: Real-Time Timbral Morphing Between Environmental Sound Categories Using Spectral Interpolation
abstract: Environmental sound design in interactive media commonly requires smooth transitions between acoustically dissimilar sonic environments—for example, interior to exterior or urban to natural. This paper presents a spectral interpolation method for real-time timbral morphing between pairs of procedurally synthesised environmental sound textures. The method operates on time-varying spectral envelopes extracted at 512-band resolution and interpolates between source and target envelopes using a perceptually weighted distance metric derived from a listener study with 30 participants who rated the naturalness of 120 morphed transitions. Morphing paths with minimum perceptual distance produced naturalness ratings averaging 3.8 out of 5, compared with 2.4 for linear spectral interpolation. Processing load on a mid-range CPU was 4–7% for a stereo output at 48 kHz and 512-sample buffer, which is acceptable for real-time game deployment. A comparison with three established middleware morphing solutions is included.

title: Neural Audio Codec Artefacts and Their Perceptual Impact in Procedurally Generated Game Audio
abstract: Neural audio codecs have been adopted in some interactive media pipelines for their compression efficiency, but their characteristic artefacts under procedurally varied input have not been systematically studied. This paper evaluates four publicly available neural audio codec implementations—each decoded at bitrates between 3 and 12 kbps—against procedurally generated inputs spanning five audio categories: environmental noise, musical texture, impact sound, speech, and synthesised tone. Artefact severity was rated by 34 trained listeners using MUSHRA methodology. Results indicate that procedurally varied inputs with high intra-clip spectral variability, such as algorithmic noise textures, produce artefact scores 31–47% higher than static recordings processed through the same codecs at equivalent bitrates. A practical threshold analysis suggests that for game audio applications relying on procedural generation, bitrates below 6 kbps introduce artefacts detectable by a majority of trained listeners. The paper provides codec-specific recommendations for procedural audio pipeline design.

title: Authoring Procedural Audio for Accessibility: Supporting Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing Players in Non-Linear Game Narratives
abstract: This paper investigates how procedural audio systems can be designed with deaf and hard-of-hearing players in mind without removing the sonic layer from the game's narrative communication. Working with a group of 11 deaf and 9 hard-of-hearing participants over three co-design sessions, the study identifies which procedural audio events carry narrative-critical information in a test game containing 38 discrete audio-triggered narrative cues. Co-design outputs informed a set of design guidelines for redundant multimodal encoding—pairing each audio cue with a corresponding haptic, visual, or textual signal generated at runtime—while preserving the auditory experience for hearing players through a unified event system. A follow-up playtest with 24 participants (8 deaf, 8 hard-of-hearing, 8 hearing) using the revised prototype found that narrative comprehension scores were comparable across groups for 31 of the 38 cues. The remaining seven cues, all relying on spectral texture alone, are analysed as a design problem requiring further authoring tool support.

title: Compositional Control Vocabularies for Large Language Model-Assisted Procedural Audio Generation
abstract: Recent large language models have been applied to music and sound generation tasks, but their integration into game audio pipelines for procedural non-linear narrative presents specific challenges around runtime control and narrative coherence. This preprint reports on a prototype pipeline in which a fine-tuned text-to-audio model is queried at narrative branch points to generate short audio segments that are then stitched and cross-faded by a conventional procedural audio engine. A controlled vocabulary of 64 compositional directives—covering tempo range, timbral category, spatial density, and emotional target—was developed through iterative testing and used to constrain model outputs. Forty-eight audio segments generated via the pipeline were rated by 20 listeners on four dimensions: coherence with preceding audio, narrative appropriateness, audio quality, and perceived procedural origin. Ratings were compared with segments generated by a conventional Max/MSP procedural system and by a human composer under the same narrative briefs. The LLM-assisted pipeline scored between the procedural and human baselines on all dimensions except audio quality, where artefact rates were notably higher.

title: Long-Term Storage Outcomes for Digitised Yugoslav Film Materials: A Survey of Repository Infrastructure at Regional Archives
abstract: This paper reports findings from a survey of nine archival institutions in the former Yugoslav states concerning the storage infrastructure supporting digitised film materials produced through restoration projects between 2005 and 2020. Data were collected via structured questionnaire and follow-up telephone interviews with archive technical staff. Key indicators examined included storage medium type, redundancy architecture, checksum verification frequency, geographic distribution of copies, and format migration history. Findings indicate that only three of the nine institutions maintained geographically distributed copies with automated fixity checking; the remainder relied on locally stored LTO tape with manual verification intervals of six months or longer. Format migration practices were inconsistently documented. The paper does not advocate for a single technical standard but maps the gap between existing IASA and FIAF digital preservation guidelines and current regional practice, identifying resource constraints and institutional capacity as the primary limiting factors.

title: A PC-Based Real-Time Target for Engine Control Unit Testing Using RTAI-Linux and a Low-Cost DAQ Board
abstract: This paper describes the construction and validation of a low-cost hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) test bench built around a standard x86 PC running RTAI-Linux 3.8 and a commercially available 16-channel analog/digital acquisition board. The setup was used to emulate the sensor and actuator environment of a diesel engine management ECU supplied by a regional automotive Tier-1 supplier. A mean-value engine model with six state variables was implemented and executed at a fixed step size of 1 ms, achieving worst-case jitter below 35 µs across a 4-hour continuous run. CAN communication between the real-time host and the ECU was handled through a standard USB-to-CAN adapter operating at 500 kbit/s. Forty-two ECU software variants were tested against a library of 180 deterministic test cases covering cold-start, idle, and wide-open-throttle scenarios. The paper reports pass/fail statistics, timing overhead, and the cost breakdown of the bench, which totaled under 1 200 EUR in hardware. Limitations related to I/O bandwidth and USB latency are discussed and partly mitigated through interrupt coalescing.

title: Modelling and Real-Time Implementation of a Brushless DC Motor Drive for HiL Emulation of Electric Power Steering Loads
abstract: Electric power steering (EPS) systems place demanding requirements on HiL test benches because the steering column torque sensor and motor current feedback must be emulated at update rates below 500 µs. This work presents a BLDC motor model parameterised from bench measurements on a 48 V, 400 W motor taken from a mid-class passenger car. The model captures back-EMF harmonics up to the 7th order and includes a thermal sub-model with two lumped time constants. It was compiled to a Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA using a fixed-point arithmetic pipeline operating at 50 MHz, achieving a simulation step of 20 µs. Analog outputs were generated through on-board 16-bit DACs. A comparison between the FPGA model and a reference floating-point Simulink simulation showed RMS current errors below 1.2% over standard SAE J266 steering manoeuvres. The paper also quantifies resource utilisation: 31% of available LUTs and 18% of DSP48 blocks on the target device.
