title: Fault Injection Framework for Automotive Body Control Module Testing on an Open-Source HiL Platform
abstract: Body control modules (BCMs) must tolerate a range of electrical faults including open circuits, shorts to battery and shorts to ground on their I/O lines. Commercial HiL systems provide programmable fault relays, but their cost is prohibitive for small development teams. This paper presents a fault injection board designed around solid-state relay arrays and a microcontroller interface, integrated with a Beaglebone Black running a Xenomai real-time patch as the simulation host. The board supports 32 independent fault channels switchable within 2 ms. A BCM with 28 digital outputs and 14 analog inputs was tested under 96 fault combinations derived from ISO 26262 FMEA tables. The framework detected seven previously unreported software anomalies in the BCM firmware relating to debounce timer behaviour under simultaneous multi-line faults. Replication cost for the fault injection hardware was 340 EUR per board. The design files and driver code are released under a permissive open-source licence.

title: Latency Characterisation of Open-Source Real-Time Kernels for Automotive HIL Applications
abstract: Several open-source options exist for turning a general-purpose Linux system into a deterministic real-time platform: RTAI, Xenomai 3, and the PREEMPT_RT patch. This paper provides a systematic comparison of all three on two hardware platforms—a standard Intel Core i5 desktop and an ARM Cortex-A9 single-board computer—under automotive HiL workloads. Latency was measured using a hardware timer circuit with 100 ns resolution over 72-hour test windows while simultaneously running a 23-state vehicle dynamics model, a CAN stack, and a UDP telemetry stream. Xenomai 3 with the Cobalt core achieved the lowest worst-case latency on the x86 platform at 18 µs, while PREEMPT_RT showed marginally better throughput at the cost of 47 µs worst-case. On the ARM platform, Xenomai 3 and PREEMPT_RT performed comparably. The paper provides configuration recipes, kernel version numbers, and patch sets used, making the results reproducible. Recommendations are given for selecting a kernel flavour based on step-size and I/O bandwidth requirements.

title: Integration of a FlexRay Bus Interface into a Low-Cost FPGA-Based HiL Bench for Chassis Domain ECU Testing
abstract: FlexRay is used in safety-critical chassis domains such as active suspension and brake-by-wire. Integrating a FlexRay interface into a low-cost HiL platform is non-trivial because commercially licensed IP cores are expensive. This work documents the integration of an open FlexRay communication controller implemented in VHDL on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA with a Linux-based simulation host connected via PCIe. The controller supports static segment scheduling with a cycle time of 5 ms and up to 64 frame slots. Two ABS/ESC ECUs from a regional supplier were used as devices under test. The paper reports successful execution of 214 scheduled test sequences covering wheel speed sensor emulation, hydraulic pressure command injection, and inter-ECU synchronisation checks. Timing accuracy of the FlexRay frames was within ±250 ns of nominal, verified with a dedicated bus analyser. Integration effort and remaining limitations regarding the dynamic segment are also discussed.

title: A Semi-Automated Test Case Generation Method for ECU Validation Based on Boundary-Value Analysis of CAN Signal Databases
abstract: ECU test suites are typically assembled manually from specification documents, which is time-consuming and incomplete. This paper describes a tool that parses CANdb++ DBC files to extract signal definitions—including physical ranges, factors, offsets, and initial values—and automatically generates boundary-value and equivalence-partition test cases for each signal. The tool was applied to two DBC databases: one covering a powertrain domain (312 signals, 47 message IDs) and one covering a body domain (198 signals, 31 message IDs). Test case counts of 1 847 and 1 203 were produced respectively and executed on the low-cost HiL bench described in earlier work. Execution time per test case averaged 4.3 seconds on the powertrain database. Twelve defects were identified in the body domain ECU firmware that manual testing had not found, including three out-of-range handling errors and two incorrect default value responses. The paper discusses integration with a lightweight Python-based test management framework and export to an XML format compatible with standard reporting tools.

title: Power Consumption Profiling of Real-Time Simulation Targets Under Variable ECU Testing Workloads
abstract: HiL test benches in embedded development teams often run continuously for extended periods. Understanding their power draw is important for infrastructure planning and for estimating operational costs. This paper presents power measurements taken on four representative real-time targets—an x86 mini-ITX board, a Raspberry Pi 4, a Beaglebone AI, and a Xilinx Zynq-7020 SoC board—while running engine, transmission, and body domain simulation workloads at step sizes of 0.5, 1, and 2 ms. Power was logged at 1 Hz using a calibrated USB power meter and a bench power supply with current monitoring. The x86 platform consumed 38–54 W depending on workload, while the Zynq SoC consumed 4.1–6.8 W for equivalent model complexity. Thermal imaging was used to identify hot spots on each board. The paper also discusses the trade-off between determinism margin and power saving modes, noting that CPU frequency scaling degraded worst-case latency by up to 90 µs on the x86 platform when not properly managed.
venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Embedded Systems and Real-Time Computing (ESRC)

title: Containerised Deployment of Real-Time ECU Test Environments Using Docker and Xenomai on Embedded Linux Platforms
abstract: Reproducing a specific HiL software environment across multiple bench instances and over time is a persistent problem in automotive software development. This paper investigates whether Docker containers can be used to encapsulate the user-space components of a Xenomai 3 real-time application—model binaries, CAN stack configuration, test scripts—while the host kernel retains the Cobalt real-time core. Experiments were conducted on two identical Raspberry Pi 4 platforms running an identical Xenomai-patched kernel. Containerised and native deployments were compared for latency, throughput, and deployment time across three ECU test suites. Worst-case latency overhead introduced by the container runtime was 3 µs in all measured cases, considered acceptable for step sizes of 1 ms and above. Deployment time was reduced from approximately 45 minutes of manual setup to under 6 minutes. The paper also describes a versioning workflow using a private registry and discusses limitations when hardware access to GPIO and CAN interfaces is required inside the container.

title: Ethernet-Based Time-Sensitive Networking as a Backbone for Distributed Automotive HiL Benches: Feasibility Assessment
abstract: As automotive architectures shift toward Ethernet-based in-vehicle networks, HiL benches must emulate Ethernet traffic alongside classical fieldbuses. This preprint reports preliminary measurements on using IEEE 802.1AS time synchronisation and 802.1Qbv time-aware shaper on a three-node distributed HiL bench where each node hosts a partial vehicle subsystem model. Nodes are connected through a managed switch with TSN support. Clock synchronisation accuracy between nodes was measured at 120 ns RMS over a 48-hour window using a shared GPS-disciplined reference. Model state exchange over scheduled Ethernet frames at 1 ms intervals showed zero missed deadlines in a 24-hour test. The preprint describes the network configuration, measurement methodology, and a preliminary cost comparison against dedicated real-time Ethernet solutions. Limitations include the current absence of a fault simulation capability for the TSN link itself. Full journal submission is planned after completing automotive protocol conformance tests.

title: A method for simultaneous identification of geometric and thermal error parameters using a laser tracker and redundant joint sensors
abstract: Standard kinematic calibration and thermal error identification are usually performed as sequential, separate procedures, which introduces coupling errors when both geometric drift and thermal expansion are active simultaneously. This paper formulates a unified parameter identification problem that simultaneously estimates the 24 DH parameters and 12 thermal expansion coefficients from a single measurement campaign. A Gauss–Newton algorithm with regularisation was used to solve the combined 36-parameter system. The measurement campaign consisted of 480 TCP position measurements acquired with a FARO laser tracker at six thermal states ranging from cold start to full thermal equilibrium. Compared with sequential identification, the unified approach reduced the RMS TCP error on a 240-point validation set from 0.13 mm to 0.09 mm. Condition number analysis confirmed that geometric and thermal subspaces are distinguishable provided measurements are taken at a minimum of four distinct thermal states. The method is compatible with standard industrial laser tracker workflows without requiring specialised fixturing.

title: Adaptive Safety Distance Margins Under Varying Human Motion Speed: An Online Estimation Approach
abstract: Fixed safety distance margins in speed-and-separation monitoring are conservative because they are sized for the fastest plausible human motion. This paper investigates an online estimation scheme that continuously updates the human velocity upper bound used in the margin calculation based on a sliding window of measured velocities from the current work session. A robust estimator based on exponentially weighted order statistics is applied to 200 ms velocity windows, producing an updated margin every control cycle. The scheme was tested in a 90-minute laboratory experiment with 18 participants performing assembly tasks at self-selected pace. Compared to the ISO/TS 15066 worst-case fixed margin, the adaptive scheme reduced the mean protective distance by 13 cm without any margin underestimations relative to the participant's actual worst-case velocity in that session. Safety guarantees under the scheme are discussed with reference to the assumptions required for the estimator to remain conservative.

title: Rotational thromboelastometry-guided fibrinogen supplementation during elective colorectal resection: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Intraoperative hypofibrinogenaemia is a recognised contributor to perioperative blood loss during major colorectal surgery, yet systematic ROTEM-guided supplementation protocols remain inconsistently applied in Serbian tertiary centres. This retrospective cohort study analysed 84 adult patients who underwent elective open or laparoscopic colorectal resection at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between January 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into two groups: those managed with a ROTEM-guided fibrinogen concentrate protocol (n = 41) and those receiving standard empirical fresh-frozen plasma (n = 43). The primary outcome was total intraoperative allogeneic red blood cell transfusion volume. Secondary outcomes included postoperative drainage output at 24 hours and length of ICU stay. The ROTEM-guided group received significantly less packed red blood cell transfusion (median 1.0 vs 2.5 units, p = 0.03) and showed shorter median ICU stay (1.2 vs 2.1 days, p = 0.048). FIBTEM A10 values below 8 mm predicted the need for fibrinogen concentrate with a sensitivity of 76% and specificity of 81%. Retrospective design and single-centre data limit generalisability; a prospective validation is ongoing.

title: Adherence to restrictive transfusion thresholds in abdominal surgery: a survey of practice among general surgeons in Vojvodina
abstract: International guidelines recommend a restrictive transfusion strategy (haemoglobin trigger of 7–8 g/dL) for most surgical patients, but adoption in everyday practice varies considerably. This cross-sectional survey was distributed to 96 general surgeons working at public hospitals across Vojvodina province between October and December 2022; 73 completed responses were analysed (response rate 76%). Participants were asked about their routine transfusion triggers, familiarity with point-of-care coagulation testing, and barriers to protocol implementation. Only 38% reported consistently applying a haemoglobin threshold at or below 8 g/dL; 54% cited concern about haemodynamic instability as the main reason for earlier transfusion. Awareness of ROTEM was high (81%) but regular use was reported by only 22% of respondents, most of them employed at tertiary-level centres. Shortage of standardised institutional protocols was the most frequently identified systemic barrier (61%). The results suggest a gap between guideline awareness and clinical practice that warrants targeted educational and organisational intervention at the regional level.

title: Platelet function in the early postoperative period following major abdominal surgery: changes detected by whole-blood impedance aggregometry
abstract: Surgical trauma triggers a transient platelet activation response whose magnitude and duration in the context of abdominal surgery have not been systematically characterised using impedance aggregometry. This prospective study followed 38 patients undergoing elective open surgery for colorectal cancer at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Whole-blood impedance aggregometry (using an Aggrecorder 500 analyser, stimulated with ADP, TRAP-6, and collagen) was performed at four time points: the evening before surgery, two hours postoperatively, 24 hours postoperatively, and on postoperative day five. ADP-stimulated aggregation rose significantly from a preoperative median of 47 AU to 74 AU at 24 hours (p < 0.001), normalising by day five. TRAP-6-stimulated values followed a similar pattern. Patients who received intraoperative transfusion of more than two units of packed red blood cells showed attenuated aggregation responses at 24 hours compared with those transfused less or not at all (median 61 vs 78 AU, p = 0.04). These data provide a quantitative basis for timing decisions regarding postoperative antithrombotic prophylaxis restart and warrant confirmation in a larger multicentre cohort.

title: Intraoperative cholangiography during laparoscopic cholecystectomy: detection rate of unsuspected common bile duct stones in a single-centre series
abstract: This retrospective single-centre study examined the diagnostic yield of routine intraoperative cholangiography (IOC) during laparoscopic cholecystectomy over a five-year period (2008–2012) at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. A total of 487 consecutive patients undergoing elective or urgent laparoscopic cholecystectomy were included. IOC was technically successful in 461 cases (94.7%). Unsuspected common bile duct (CBD) stones were identified in 38 patients (8.2% of successful IOCs). Factors associated with positive IOC included elevated serum bilirubin, dilated CBD on preoperative ultrasound, and history of acute biliary pancreatitis. Patients with positive IOC proceeded to laparoscopic CBD exploration in 21 cases and to postoperative ERCP in 17. The conversion rate to open surgery was 3.1%. Operating time was significantly longer in the IOC-positive group (mean 97 vs. 68 minutes, p < 0.001). The study supports selective rather than routine IOC in centres where preoperative stratification protocols are in place.

title: Primary duct closure versus T-tube drainage after laparoscopic choledochotomy: a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
abstract: Controversy persists regarding optimal management of the common bile duct after transcholedochal exploration. This meta-analysis identified randomised controlled trials comparing primary duct closure (PDC) with T-tube drainage (TTD) following laparoscopic choledochotomy, searching MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library up to December 2020. Nine trials involving 714 patients were included. PDC was associated with significantly shorter operative time (mean difference −18.4 min, 95% CI −24.1 to −12.7), shorter hospital stay (mean difference −2.1 days, 95% CI −2.9 to −1.3), and lower total complication rate (RR 0.61, 95% CI 0.45–0.83). Retained stone rates and bile leak rates did not differ significantly between groups. Heterogeneity was moderate (I² = 42% for complications). Sensitivity analyses restricted to trials with low risk of bias confirmed the main findings. The data support PDC as the preferred closure method when the duct wall is of adequate quality and there is no distal obstruction.

title: PERCO-RCT: interim analysis at 50% enrolment—perfusion-guided vs. standard colorectal anastomosis in a five-centre Balkan and Central European trial
abstract: The PERCO-RCT randomised controlled trial is comparing perfusion-guided (ICG fluorescence angiography) and standard intraoperative decision-making in patients undergoing elective sigmoid or rectal resection with primary anastomosis at five centres in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. This pre-specified interim analysis was conducted when 340 of the planned 680 patients had been enrolled and had completed 30-day follow-up. In the perfusion-guided arm (n = 170), intraoperative anastomotic level revision occurred in 22 patients (12.9%) based on fluorescence findings. Grade B/C anastomotic leak occurred in 12 perfusion-guided patients (7.1%) and in 19 standard-arm patients (11.2%); the difference was not statistically significant at interim (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.28–1.30, p = 0.19). The independent data safety monitoring board reviewed the analysis and recommended continuation without modification. Secondary outcomes including proximal margin revision rate and 90-day Clavien–Dindo ≥3 complications showed no significant differences. Patient accrual is on schedule; final results are expected in 2026.

title: Tensile properties of polypropylene mesh after six months of intraperitoneal implantation in a rat model
abstract: Lightweight polypropylene mesh is widely used for incisional hernia repair, but its mechanical properties after biological integration are incompletely characterised. Twenty-four Wistar rats received 3 × 3 cm mesh implants intraperitoneally; animals were sacrificed at 4, 12, and 24 weeks. Explanted composite samples underwent uniaxial tensile testing at a crosshead speed of 10 mm/min. Ultimate tensile strength decreased by 18% at 24 weeks compared with unimplanted controls (p = 0.03), while elongation at break increased by 31%. Histological sections showed progressive fibrous encapsulation with collagen type I deposition predominant beyond 12 weeks. Mesh–tissue interface strength was highest at 12 weeks (mean 28.4 N ± 4.1) and plateaued thereafter. These data suggest that mechanical integration stabilises within three months but is accompanied by a measurable reduction in stiffness that may influence long-term hernia recurrence risk.

title: Second-harmonic generation imaging of collagen fibre orientation in fascial biopsies from hernia patients
abstract: Collagen fibre architecture in the linea alba may influence mechanical competence and hernia recurrence. We applied second-harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy to fascial biopsies obtained from 30 patients: 10 with no prior hernia, 10 with primary incisional hernia, and 10 with recurrent incisional hernia. Fibre orientation index (FOI) and mean fibre angle relative to the midline were quantified from SHG image stacks. FOI was significantly lower in recurrent hernia tissue (0.31 ± 0.06) than in primary hernia (0.47 ± 0.08) or control tissue (0.62 ± 0.09), indicating greater fibre disorganisation. Mean fibre angle deviated most from the transverse axis in recurrent cases (38° ± 11° versus 22° ± 8° in controls). These findings link structural disorganisation of fascial collagen to the recurrence phenotype and suggest SHG-derived FOI may serve as a tissue-quality marker in future studies.

title: Surgeon experience and RLN signal loss events: analysis of a prospective IONM registry
abstract: Using a prospectively maintained single-institution IONM registry covering 2010–2019, we analysed 624 thyroid and parathyroid procedures to determine the relationship between surgeon case volume and the rate of significant intraoperative signal loss events (SLE), defined as amplitude decrease exceeding 50% from baseline. Surgeons were categorised as low volume (<30 IONM cases), intermediate (30–100), and high volume (>100). SLE rates were 14.2%, 8.7%, and 5.3% respectively (p=0.003, chi-square trend). Multivariate logistic regression controlling for diagnosis, reoperative status, and tumour size confirmed high case volume as an independent protective factor (OR 0.38; 95% CI 0.17–0.83). Conversion of SLE to permanent palsy was 18% in low-volume and 8% in high-volume surgeons, though this subgroup comparison did not reach significance. The data support structured IONM credentialing programmes and minimum case volume thresholds.

title: Compliance with enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols and its association with SSI rates in elective colonic surgery: audit results from Vojvodina 2022–2025
abstract: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols are increasingly adopted in Serbian hospitals, but compliance monitoring is inconsistent and the relationship between compliance and SSI outcomes has not been quantified locally. This audit covered 481 elective colonic procedures across five Vojvodina hospitals from January 2022 to June 2025. ERAS compliance was assessed across 16 elements using prospective checklist data; overall compliance was 54% (range across hospitals: 38%–71%). SSI rates were 13.1% in the lowest compliance tertile (<45%) versus 6.2% in the highest tertile (>65%), a difference that persisted after case-mix adjustment (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.29–0.93). The elements with lowest compliance were preoperative carbohydrate loading (28%), avoidance of nasogastric tube (44%), and goal-directed fluid therapy (41%). The audit highlights institutional variation and supports targeted ERAS implementation support for lower-performing hospitals.

title: Daughters Left Out: Gender Disparities in Agricultural Land Inheritance in Three Bačka Villages
abstract: This study examines inheritance outcomes for daughters versus sons in 214 farm households across three villages in the Bačka subregion of Vojvodina, drawing on semi-structured interviews conducted between 2010 and 2011 and cross-referenced with municipal cadastral registers. The analysis finds that daughters received agricultural parcels in only 31 percent of cases where siblings of both sexes were present, compared with 87 percent for sons. Qualitative data reveal that parents and children alike frequently invoke the expectation that daughters will marry out and that farm continuity requires a male heir, even in households where daughters are the primary farm workers. The paper argues that formal legal equality in Serbian inheritance law does not translate into equal outcomes at the household level, owing to persistent informal norms reinforced through village social networks. Implications for rural development policy, particularly EU pre-accession agricultural support programmes targeting land consolidation, are discussed.

title: Cadastral Records as a Source for Gendered Land Tenure Research: Opportunities and Limitations in the Vojvodina Context
abstract: Land cadastres maintained by the Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia record ownership by name and parcel but provide no information on management rights, usage arrangements, or the processes by which ownership was acquired. This methodological paper evaluates the utility of cadastral data for studying gendered land tenure in Vojvodina, using a sample of 1,840 parcels from four municipalities drawn in 2012. The paper reports that women appear as sole owners on 18.4 percent of agricultural parcels and as co-owners on a further 12.1 percent, but that these figures mask significant variation between municipalities and between parcel categories. Cross-referencing with household survey data collected from 310 respondents shows that female cadastral ownership frequently coexists with de facto male management. The paper recommends supplementary data collection strategies, including spousal agreement mapping and use-right interviews, to complement cadastral sources in gender-sensitive land research.

title: Between Law and Custom: Inheritance Negotiations in Mixed-Ethnicity Villages of Northern Vojvodina
abstract: Northern Vojvodina contains villages where Serbian, Hungarian, and Rusyn households live in close proximity, each community carrying distinct customary inheritance norms alongside the shared legal framework of Serbian civil law. This paper reports findings from twenty-six in-depth household interviews conducted in two mixed-ethnicity villages in the Subotica district in 2014, focusing on how couples negotiate land succession across ethnic and sometimes cross-ethnic marriages. The analysis identifies three recurring negotiation scripts: silent male default, explicit sibling buy-out, and deferred joint ownership. The deferred joint ownership arrangement, most common among younger Hungarian-Serbian couples, keeps parcels formally undivided for a generation, creating practical barriers to land consolidation. The paper contributes to the comparative literature on customary versus statutory inheritance by showing that ethnic community membership shapes negotiation context even when all parties operate under the same formal law.

title: Who Signs the Lease? Women Landowners and Rental Market Participation in Vojvodina
abstract: Agricultural land rental markets have expanded substantially in Vojvodina since 2005 as smallholders lease parcels to larger operators. This paper asks whether female landowners participate in rental markets on equal terms with male landowners, using a survey of 389 landowners across six municipalities conducted in 2015. Logistic regression models show that female sole owners are 22 percentage points less likely to have an active lease contract than comparable male owners, controlling for parcel size, distance from settlement, and household composition. Qualitative follow-up interviews with 40 respondents suggest that women more often rely on informal oral arrangements, frequently with male relatives, rather than formal contracts, leaving them with less legal protection and lower effective rents. The paper discusses the role of agricultural service cooperatives in mediating or reinforcing these disparities.

title: Gendered Land Tenure in Post-Socialist Vojvodina: Continuity and Change Since 1989
abstract: This book chapter situates contemporary gender disparities in Vojvodina land tenure within a longer trajectory of socialist collectivisation, decollectivisation, and post-2000 agricultural restructuring. Drawing on historical records from the Provincial Archive of Vojvodina, municipal cadastral data spanning 1990 to 2016, and oral history interviews with twenty-two elderly respondents, the chapter traces how the abolition of the socially-owned sector returned land to household control in ways that often reinforced pre-socialist patrilineal customs rather than the gender-neutral ownership norms that socialist policy had formally promoted. The chapter argues that decollectivisation created a structural moment in which customary norms reasserted themselves because state capacity to enforce formal inheritance law at the village level was weak during the 1990s. The findings contribute to a broader comparative volume on post-socialist agrarian transformations across Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Village Women as De Facto Farm Managers: A Typology from Eastern Srem
abstract: Formal ownership statistics in Vojvodina undercount women's roles in agricultural decision-making because management and ownership are often legally and practically separated. This paper develops a typology of female farm management arrangements through analysis of household survey data collected from 178 farming households in Eastern Srem in 2018. Using a combination of activity diaries, decision-mapping questions, and cadastral ownership data, the study identifies four types: titular-only owners who cede all management; co-managing wives in formally male-headed households; de facto sole managers with no formal land rights; and formal owners who are also primary managers. The last type represents only 14 percent of women in the sample. The typology is cross-tabulated with household lifecycle stage, off-farm employment of spouses, and distance from urban centres, revealing that de facto management without ownership is most common in middle-aged households where husbands hold off-farm jobs.

title: Does Agricultural Extension Reach Female Landowners? Evidence from Vojvodina Advisory Service Records
abstract: Agricultural extension services are a primary channel through which land management advice and subsidy information reach farmers, yet their reach may differ by the gender of the registered landholder. This study analyses administrative records from the Vojvodina Agricultural Advisory and Expert Service covering 4,312 farm visits in 2019 and 2020, supplemented by a telephone survey of 200 registered landholders who did not receive visits. Female sole owners account for 17.6 percent of the land registry in the covered area but received only 9.3 percent of advisory visits. Survey data indicate that extension officers systematically contact the male household member when records show female ownership, reflecting assumptions about who makes farming decisions. The paper recommends gender disaggregation in extension service planning and proposes an audit protocol for monitoring reach by ownership type.
venue: Journal of Agricultural Extension and Education in Southeast Europe

title: Inheritance Expectations Among Young Adults in Rural Vojvodina: A Survey of University Agriculture Students
abstract: This conference paper reports preliminary findings from an online survey of 312 students enrolled in agriculture-related programmes at the University of Novi Sad in the 2022–2023 academic year, asking about their expectations regarding inheritance of parental agricultural land. The survey finds that 68 percent of male respondents expect to inherit the primary farm parcel, compared with 29 percent of female respondents, even though 71 percent of all respondents correctly identify that Serbian law provides equal inheritance rights regardless of sex. Students from villages of fewer than 1,000 inhabitants show larger gender gaps in expectation than those from larger settlements. Open-text responses frequently cite family harmony and the avoidance of sibling conflict as reasons for anticipated unequal division. The paper discusses implications for rural labour market projections and for gender-sensitive curricula in agricultural education.

title: Land Fragmentation and Gendered Ownership Patterns in Vojvodina: A Spatial Analysis at the Parcel Level
abstract: Vojvodina has one of the highest rates of agricultural land fragmentation in the Western Balkans, with average holdings consisting of multiple non-contiguous parcels. This paper asks whether female and male landowners differ in the spatial configuration of their holdings, using parcel-level cadastral data for three complete municipalities georeferenced against ownership records from 2022. Female sole owners hold on average 2.3 parcels compared with 3.8 for male sole owners and tend to own parcels closer to the settlement boundary, which typically carry lower commercial value. Spatial autocorrelation analysis shows that female-owned parcels cluster near former homestead plots, consistent with the hypothesis that women inherit residential-adjacent land while brothers receive more productive field parcels further from the village. The paper combines GIS mapping with logistic regression to model the determinants of parcel location by owner sex.

title: Farm-level responses to Green Deal-aligned conditionality: simulation evidence from a Vojvodina farm typology
abstract: This working paper simulates the farm-level income effects of introducing European Green Deal-aligned conditionality requirements—specifically crop rotation mandates and 10% non-productive area set-asides—on a typology of 14 representative farm types constructed from Vojvodina FADN-compatible data for the period 2019–2023. A linear programming model maximises gross margin subject to agronomic, labour, and land constraints under the baseline and two policy scenarios. Results indicate that large arable farms specialising in maize–wheat rotations face average gross margin reductions of 8–12% under the combined scenario, while mixed farms and those with established agri-environmental contracts show smaller losses of 3–5%. The simulation also identifies that access to advisory services is the most important moderating factor in minimising adjustment costs. The paper is intended to inform ongoing stakeholder consultations on Serbia's alignment with EU CAP Green Architecture requirements.

title: Spatial price integration between Serbian and German pork wholesale markets: a nonlinear VECM approach
abstract: This paper tests for spatial price integration between the Serbian wholesale pork market and the German wholesale pork market—the EU's benchmark—using weekly price data from 2009 to 2017. A nonlinear vector error correction model (VECM) with two regimes separated by a transaction cost band is estimated. Results indicate that the two markets share a long-run cointegrating relationship, but adjustment within the band is negligible. Above the upper threshold, Serbian prices adjust to close approximately 22 percent of the gap per week; German prices show no significant adjustment, consistent with Serbia being a price-taker relative to the EU reference market. The estimated transaction cost band of ±18 percent around parity reflects transport costs, sanitary certification fees, and exchange rate uncertainty. The finding has implications for Serbian producers' ability to benefit from export opportunities and for EU accession preparations in the livestock sector.

title: Did COVID-19 disruptions alter price transmission in the Serbian pork chain? A comparative pre- and post-shock analysis
abstract: Supply chain disruptions during the COVID-19 pandemic affected labor availability at Serbian slaughterhouses and altered retail demand patterns for different pork cuts. This paper compares pre-pandemic (January 2017–February 2020) and pandemic-period (March 2020–June 2021) price transmission dynamics using rolling-window cointegration tests and time-varying parameter error correction models estimated on weekly price data. The proportion of weeks in which cointegration between farm-gate and retail prices is confirmed fell from 87 percent in the pre-pandemic window to 64 percent in the pandemic window, suggesting a temporary breakdown in long-run market linkages. Asymmetry coefficients increased markedly for the fresh pork leg and shoulder cuts, while bacon and processed meat products showed more stable transmission. The episode provides a natural experiment illustrating how supply-side disruptions at the processing stage can decouple farm-retail price relationships even in the absence of changes in retail market structure.

title: Creep compliance of bisphenol-A epoxy resin at elevated temperatures: time–temperature superposition and Prony series fitting
abstract: This paper examines the time-dependent deformation behaviour of a commercial bisphenol-A epoxy system cured with an aromatic amine hardener. Creep compliance data were collected at seven temperatures between 30 °C and 110 °C using a three-point bending configuration on a dynamic mechanical analyser, with test durations of up to 3600 s per isotherm. Time–temperature superposition was applied and a master curve at a reference temperature of 25 °C was constructed, spanning approximately eight decades of reduced time. A 12-term Prony series was fitted to the master curve using a least-squares optimisation procedure; the mean relative error across all data points was below 2.1 %. The horizontal shift factors followed the Williams–Landel–Ferry equation with fitted constants C1 = 11.4 and C2 = 54.3 K. The results provide material input parameters for finite-element simulations of encapsulant stress relaxation during the cooling phase of electronic assemblies. The fitted Prony coefficients are reported in full to allow direct use in commercial FE codes.

title: Interfacial adhesion loss between underfill epoxy and FR-4 substrate after 500 thermal shock cycles: a fractographic study
abstract: Epoxy underfill specimens bonded to FR-4 glass-fibre substrates were subjected to repeated thermal shock between −40 °C and +125 °C in a two-zone chamber, with a transition time of 10 s. Sets of specimens were extracted at 100, 250, 350, and 500 cycles. Fracture surfaces were examined by scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. After 100 cycles, failure was predominantly cohesive within the epoxy, with river-mark patterns consistent with fast fracture. By cycle 350, the failure mode had shifted toward interfacial debonding at the epoxy–glass interface; EDX confirmed local silica enrichment on detached fragments, indicating adhesive failure at the coupling-agent layer. After 500 cycles, 61 % of the bond area exhibited interfacial failure, compared with 8 % in uncycled controls. Crack density at the epoxy–copper pad boundary increased by a factor of 3.2 between 100 and 500 cycles. The findings indicate that thermal shock accelerates interfacial degradation more rapidly than bulk cohesive damage, with implications for accelerated life test design.

title: Influence of anhydride hardener content on the glass transition temperature and fracture toughness of casting epoxy systems
abstract: Four epoxy formulations based on a diglycidyl ether of bisphenol-A resin were prepared with stoichiometric ratios of methylhexahydrophthalic anhydride hardener set at 80, 90, 100, and 110 % of the theoretical equivalent. Specimens were cast in steel moulds and cured at 80 °C for 2 h followed by a post-cure at 140 °C for 4 h. Glass transition temperatures were determined by DMA (storage modulus onset) and DSC (midpoint method), yielding values between 118 °C and 141 °C. Plane-strain fracture toughness KIc was measured on single-edge notched beam specimens according to ISO 13586; values ranged from 0.61 to 0.89 MPa·m^0.5, with the 90 % stoichiometry formulation giving the highest toughness. Flexural modulus and strength were also recorded. Cross-link density was estimated from rubbery-plateau modulus and correlated with both Tg and KIc, showing that the relationship is nonmonotonic: toughness peaks at intermediate cross-link density while Tg continues to rise.

title: A linear viscoelastic finite-element model for stress prediction in glob-top encapsulants on flexible substrates
abstract: A two-dimensional plane-stress finite-element model was developed in Abaqus to predict stress distributions in glob-top epoxy encapsulants applied to flexible polyimide substrates during thermal cycling between −55 °C and +85 °C. The epoxy was represented by a generalised Maxwell model using Prony series parameters derived from DMA measurements. Temperature-dependent elastic properties of the polyimide film were taken from supplier data sheets and verified by tensile testing at five temperatures. The model incorporated a cooling rate of 10 °C/min consistent with IEC 60068-2-14 test condition Na. Peak maximum principal stresses of 38.4 MPa were predicted at the encapsulant corners at the end of the cold dwell period, with stress relaxation reducing this value by approximately 23 % during a 15-minute dwell. Model predictions were compared against digital image correlation measurements on physical specimens; the mean deviation in surface strain was 7.3 %. Mesh sensitivity was assessed over three refinement levels. The work demonstrates that neglecting viscoelastic relaxation leads to a systematic overestimate of peak stress by roughly 18 %.

title: Moisture absorption kinetics in silicone-modified epoxy encapsulants and its effect on viscoelastic parameters
abstract: Silicone-toughened epoxy discs (30 mm diameter, 3 mm thick) containing 0, 5, 10, and 15 wt% polydimethylsiloxane modifier were immersed in deionised water at 40 °C and 85 °C. Mass uptake was monitored gravimetrically at 24-hour intervals for 90 days. Fickian diffusion coefficients were extracted; at 85 °C the coefficient for the unmodified epoxy was 3.1 × 10^−13 m²/s and decreased to 2.4 × 10^−13 m²/s at 15 wt% silicone content, consistent with the hydrophobic contribution of the modifier. After conditioning to saturation, DMA was performed to extract storage modulus and loss factor as a function of temperature. Moisture uptake depressed Tg by 11 °C in the unmodified system and by 7 °C at 15 wt% silicone. Loss factor peaks broadened with absorbed moisture, suggesting increased heterogeneity in segmental mobility. The Prony series representation of the wet material was compared with the dry-state baseline; relaxation times shortened by up to 35 % in the terminal region, which has direct implications for reliability models that assume constant viscoelastic parameters.
venue: Journal of Polymer Mechanics and Materials

title: Residual stress accumulation in multilayer encapsulant systems after repeated thermal shock: analytical model versus strain gauge measurements
abstract: An analytical beam-on-elastic-foundation model was developed to estimate residual stress build-up in a two-layer system comprising an epoxy primary encapsulant and a polyurethane conformal coat after N thermal shock cycles (−40 °C to +130 °C, 500 cycles total). The model incorporated cycle-to-cycle stress accumulation through a simple ratcheting rule calibrated against isothermal stress-relaxation tests. Strain gauges bonded to the surface of the polyurethane layer recorded curvature changes at intervals of 50 cycles. Measured curvature values after 500 cycles were 0.24 m^−1, against a model prediction of 0.21 m^−1, an underestimate of 12.5 %. The analytical model runs in under one second on standard hardware and is therefore useful for parametric sensitivity studies; a Monte Carlo analysis with ±10 % variation in layer thickness and modulus inputs yielded a coefficient of variation in predicted peak stress of 14 %. The paper also documents a systematic shift in the neutral axis position as layers soften differently at low temperature, which previous simplified models had neglected.

title: Effect of thermal shock rate on delamination onset in epoxy-encapsulated surface-mount components: experimental mapping and energy release rate estimates
abstract: Surface-mount resistor packages encapsulated with a standard novolac epoxy compound were subjected to thermal shock cycling at three ramp rates: 5, 15, and 30 °C/min, between −40 °C and +125 °C, for up to 1000 cycles. Delamination area at the die-attach interface was mapped after every 200 cycles using scanning acoustic microscopy. At the fastest ramp rate, measurable delamination appeared by cycle 200 in 60 % of specimens, compared with cycle 600 at the slowest rate. An energy release rate estimate at the delamination front was derived from the analytical model of the preceding study, using measured curvature data as input. Critical energy release rate values back-calculated at delamination onset ranged from 68 to 84 J/m², consistent with values reported in the literature for similar die-attach adhesives. A log-linear relationship between ramp rate and cycles-to-onset was established (R² = 0.94), providing an empirical acceleration factor for test design. The role of in-plane constraint from package geometry was examined qualitatively through comparison of two package footprint sizes.

title: Thermoset encapsulant materials in power electronics: failure mechanisms, characterisation methods, and modelling approaches
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured survey of failure mechanisms in thermoset encapsulant materials used in power electronic modules, with emphasis on phenomena driven by cyclic thermal loading. The text is organised around three scales: macroscopic (package-level delamination and warpage), mesoscopic (filler–matrix decohesion and microcrack networks), and molecular (chain scission, physical ageing, and Tg drift). Characterisation techniques are discussed in terms of practical application, covering DMA, thermomechanical analysis, scanning acoustic microscopy, SEM-EDX, and nanoindentation. Modelling approaches range from elastic laminates and viscoelastic Prony-series FE models to cohesive-zone treatments of interfacial crack growth. A comparative table of material parameters reported in the literature for twelve commercial encapsulant systems is included. The chapter concludes with a discussion of gaps between accelerated test conditions and field use, and identifies areas where material data are most often missing in published studies. The intended audience is engineers and researchers entering the field of encapsulant reliability.

title: Physical ageing effects on stress relaxation in anhydride-cured epoxy encapsulants aged at 80 °C for up to 5000 hours
abstract: Specimens of an anhydride-cured epoxy encapsulant representative of those used in automotive sensor packaging were isothermally aged at 80 °C in a forced-air oven for periods of 500, 1000, 2000, 3500, and 5000 hours. Stress relaxation tests in three-point bending were performed at 60 °C after each ageing interval, and the relaxation modulus at 100 s was used as a single-parameter descriptor. After 5000 h, the 100-second relaxation modulus had increased by 19 % relative to the as-cured state, and the relaxation rate (slope of the log–log relaxation curve) decreased from 0.078 to 0.051, indicating a progressive shift toward more elastic behaviour. DSC measurements confirmed a Tg increase of 8 °C over the ageing period, attributed to continued cross-linking. FTIR spectra showed a reduction in the epoxide absorption band at 915 cm^−1 and growth of the hydroxyl ether band, quantitatively consistent with the Tg change. The implications for long-term stress prediction models are discussed: using as-cured viscoelastic parameters leads to overestimation of stress relaxation and thus unconservative lifetime estimates.

title: Effect of accelerated hydrothermal ageing on the heat release characteristics of polyurethane-bonded aramid/viscose laminate assemblies
abstract: Aramid/viscose blend fabric bonded to an expanded polytetrafluoroethylene membrane via a polyurethane hot-melt adhesive was subjected to accelerated hydrothermal ageing cycles (48, 96 and 192 h at 60 °C, 90% RH) and subsequently characterised by cone calorimetry at 35 kW/m². TTI decreased from 31 s in unaged samples to 22 s after 192 h ageing. Peak heat release rate increased from 143 to 198 kW/m², and THR over 300 s rose by 17%. FTIR analysis of the adhesive layer after ageing showed progressive hydrolysis of urethane linkages, evidenced by reduction of the carbonyl band at 1710 cm⁻¹ and growth of free amine and hydroxyl absorption. Dynamic mechanical analysis confirmed a 31% reduction in storage modulus at 120 °C after 192 h, consistent with network degradation. The data indicate that service lifetimes based purely on mechanical criteria may underestimate concurrent deterioration of fire performance in humid environments.

title: Between the Farm and the Factory: Informal Work Strategies of Young Adults in Rural Vojvodina, 2003–2008
abstract: Drawing on 48 semi-structured interviews conducted in four municipalities in southern Vojvodina between 2008 and 2009, this study examines how young adults aged 18–30 navigated informal work arrangements during a period of rapid agricultural privatisation and industrial downsizing. Respondents described a layered coping economy in which undeclared agricultural day labour, cross-border petty trade with Hungary, and seasonal construction work were combined to approximate a living income. The analysis identifies three dominant trajectory types: persistent informality, transitional informality leading to formal employment within five years, and recursive informality marked by repeated entry and exit from declared work. Women were disproportionately represented in the recursive category, primarily due to care responsibilities and employer discrimination. The findings challenge policy assumptions that informal work is a temporary phase and suggest that structural factors, particularly the collapse of large agro-industrial combines, reproduce informality across generations.

title: Measuring Informal Employment Among Young People: Methodological Challenges in Household Survey Data from Serbia
abstract: Official labour force surveys systematically undercount informal employment, particularly among youth, because respondents underreport undeclared income-generating activities. This paper compares results from the Serbian Labour Force Survey (2005–2010) with a supplementary household questionnaire administered in Vojvodina to 612 households containing at least one member aged 15–29. The supplementary instrument used indirect questioning techniques and a broadened definition of work covering unpaid family labour, barter arrangements, and platform-mediated tasks. The gap between official and supplementary estimates reached 18.4 percentage points for the 20–24 age cohort, with the discrepancy most pronounced in peri-urban municipalities. The paper proposes a set of question revisions and sampling adjustments applicable to future waves of the national survey and reflects on ethical considerations when collecting sensitive income data in small communities.

title: Post-Socialist Precarity: A Conceptual Framework for Analysing Youth Labour in the Western Balkans
abstract: Precarity as an analytical category has been developed largely in Western European contexts where stable, Fordist employment was the historical baseline. This book chapter argues that applying the concept unreflexively to the Western Balkans obscures the specific genealogy of labour instability in post-socialist societies, where formal full employment was itself a state-administered fiction and informality was embedded in everyday economic practice well before 1989. The chapter develops a modified framework that distinguishes between inherited precarity, rooted in socialist-era second-economy practices, and induced precarity, produced by structural adjustment and labour market liberalisation after 2000. The framework is illustrated with case material from Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, drawing on secondary analysis of national youth surveys and existing ethnographic literature. The chapter closes with a set of analytical propositions for comparative research.

title: Registered and Real: Dual Employment Arrangements Among Young Workers in Novi Sad's Service Sector
abstract: A common form of semi-informality in Serbian urban labour markets involves a formal contract declaring a minimum statutory wage alongside an undeclared supplement paid in cash. This study investigates the prevalence, structure, and subjective experience of such dual arrangements among workers aged 18–35 in Novi Sad's retail, hospitality, and personal services sectors. Data were collected through a targeted questionnaire administered to 284 workers recruited via snowball sampling at six sites between 2013 and 2014, supplemented by 22 in-depth interviews. Results indicate that 61% of respondents in hospitality and 39% in retail reported receiving part of their remuneration off the books. Workers expressed ambivalence rather than clear opposition to these arrangements, citing the trade-off between immediate income and future pension entitlements. Employer leverage was maintained through short-term contracts and the threat of non-renewal.

title: Gendered Dimensions of Youth Precarity in Vojvodina: Evidence from a Panel Study, 2010–2015
abstract: This paper presents findings from a five-year panel study tracking 198 young adults (94 women, 104 men) first interviewed in 2010 in three Vojvodina localities. Attrition over the five waves was 22%, and the analysis uses multiple imputation to address non-random dropout. The study finds that women's labour market trajectories were significantly more volatile, with 58% experiencing at least two transitions between formal employment, informal employment, and inactivity over the observation period, compared with 37% of men. Care events, specifically the birth of a child or the onset of a parent's health problem, accounted for 44% of women's transitions out of formal employment. Men's transitions were more strongly associated with employer insolvency and seasonal demand. These asymmetric patterns persisted after controlling for education level, suggesting that structural and normative factors independent of human capital drive gendered precarity.

title: Platform Work as New Informality? Freelancing Platforms Among Young Graduates in Serbia
abstract: Online freelancing platforms such as those aggregating translation, design, data entry, and software tasks have attracted growing numbers of young graduates in Serbia since approximately 2014. This study examines whether platform work constitutes a structurally new labour form or a digitally mediated continuation of existing informality patterns. Using a web-based survey administered to 431 platform workers aged 22–35 recruited through social media and platform community groups, combined with 18 interviews, the study maps income levels, working hours, formal employment status, and self-reported reasons for platform participation. Median monthly earnings from platforms were €290, used primarily as supplementary rather than primary income. Only 14% of respondents declared platform income to the Tax Administration. The analysis draws on the inherited/induced precarity framework developed in earlier work to situate platform work within the longer history of informal earnings in post-socialist Serbia.

title: Informal Employment and Social Protection Gaps: Pension and Health Insurance Coverage Among Precarious Youth Workers in Serbia, 2008–2018
abstract: Ten years of administrative data from the Serbian Pension and Disability Insurance Fund (PIO Fund) and the National Health Insurance Fund, combined with a supplementary survey of 376 young adults, are used to quantify social protection gaps associated with informal and semi-informal employment. Over the observation decade, the average contributory years recorded for young adults between ages 20 and 30 fell from 5.2 to 3.9 years per decade of potential working life, indicating a widening gap. Health insurance coverage through personal contribution, as opposed to family dependency coverage, declined by 11 percentage points in the same age group. The paper estimates that current trajectories, if unchanged, will leave approximately 34% of today's 25-year-olds below minimum contributory thresholds for pension entitlement at statutory retirement age. Policy simulations modelling a simplified contribution scheme for informal workers suggest a partial but meaningful reduction in this share.

title: Youth Employment Policy in Serbia since 2000: A Documentary and Stakeholder Analysis
abstract: National and local employment policies targeting youth in Serbia have been reformulated at least six times since 2000, often in response to EU accession conditionality rather than domestic evidence. This study combines systematic documentary analysis of 41 policy texts, action plans, and evaluation reports with 27 interviews conducted in 2020–2021 with policymakers at national, provincial, and municipal levels, employment service officers, and youth NGO representatives. The analysis reveals a persistent gap between policy rhetoric emphasising activation and the structural conditions workers face, including an underfunded National Employment Service, short-duration active labour market programmes, and employer subsidy schemes that are frequently gamed through short-term hiring followed by dismissal. The paper identifies three recurrent policy cycles and argues that formal policy change has often served to legitimate inaction rather than alter labour market outcomes.

title: Coping Strategies Under Precarity: A Typology Based on Longitudinal Qualitative Data from Vojvodina, 2010–2022
abstract: This article returns to a subset of participants first interviewed in 2010 for a study of informal rural labour and recontacts 31 individuals who could be located and consented to further participation, conducting life-history interviews in 2021–2022. The twelve-year span allows examination of how coping strategies evolved as respondents moved through their twenties and thirties. The analysis develops an empirically grounded typology of five coping patterns: portfolio accumulation, anchored informality, strategic formality, welfare dependency, and emigration. The typology differs from earlier cross-sectional accounts by showing that individuals frequently move between types in response to household composition changes, macro-economic shocks, and shifts in local labour demand. The 2020 COVID-19 shock appears prominently as a forcing event that accelerated both the emigration and welfare dependency patterns. The article reflects methodologically on long-term qualitative re-contact studies in small communities.

title: Platform Work Regulation and Its Reception Among Young Serbian Freelancers: Evidence from a Follow-Up Survey, 2019–2024
abstract: Serbia introduced a simplified taxation scheme for online freelancers in 2020, representing the first formal policy attempt to bring platform-mediated income into the tax and contribution system. This paper reports findings from a follow-up survey of 218 individuals who also participated in a 2019 survey on platform work, supplemented by 24 interviews conducted in 2023–2024. Formal registration under the new scheme increased from 14% to 31% among the panel respondents, but qualitative data reveal that registration was largely motivated by pressure from international clients and payment processors rather than by normative acceptance of contribution obligations. Respondents' pension and health coverage improved only marginally, as many chose the lowest permissible declared income base. The paper also documents a shift in platform composition, with coding and IT tasks displacing translation and design tasks as the dominant category of work among this cohort.

title: Farmers' willingness to accept payments for grassland bird habitat maintenance in the Vojvodina plain: a contingent valuation study
abstract: This study estimated the minimum compensation required by grain farmers in the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia to voluntarily maintain field margins and grassland strips as habitat for declining farmland bird species. A contingent valuation survey was administered to 214 farm operators across three districts in 2012. Using a double-bounded dichotomous choice elicitation format, median willingness to accept (WTA) was estimated at 187 EUR per hectare per year for uncultivated margin maintenance of 3–5 metres. Multivariate regression revealed that farm size, off-farm income share, and prior participation in any agri-environment measure were significant predictors of WTA bids. Farmers with larger holdings and diversified income showed substantially lower per-hectare WTA values. The results suggest that a flat-rate payment scheme at the national level would be financially inefficient, and that spatially differentiated or auctioned contracts could reduce public expenditure by 20–30 percent while achieving similar habitat area targets. Policy implications for the design of forthcoming Serbian agri-environment regulations are discussed.

title: Additionality constraints in agri-environment contract design: evidence from experimental auctions in Hungary and Serbia
abstract: Payment schemes for ecosystem services risk purchasing conservation outcomes that would have occurred anyway under normal farming practice. This paper examines additionality in a comparative experimental auction conducted simultaneously in Bács-Kiskun County, Hungary, and South Bačka District, Serbia, in 2014. A total of 312 farm operators participated. Each auction round required bidders to specify both their payment demand and the baseline management they would apply without a contract. Regression discontinuity and matching methods were used to isolate genuine additionality. Results show that approximately 34 percent of accepted bids in a simulated flat-rate scheme would have delivered no additional conservation benefit, compared with only 11 percent under a discriminatory-price auction with an explicit additionality screen. The cross-border comparison reveals that higher baseline heterogeneity in Serbian farms produces larger efficiency gains from auctions than in the more homogenous Hungarian sample. The findings support including verifiable baseline declarations in contract terms for schemes targeting pollinators and ground-nesting birds.

title: Multi-criteria ranking of ecosystem service payment instruments for arable land: an AHP application in the Central Pannonian Basin
abstract: Five distinct payment instruments for farmland ecosystem services—flat-rate subsidies, discriminatory-price auctions, agglomeration bonuses, result-based payments, and conservation easements—were evaluated using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with two panels: 18 agricultural policy experts and 24 farm advisors from Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary. Criteria included cost-effectiveness, administrative burden, biodiversity outcome certainty, farmer acceptance, and monitoring feasibility. Each criterion was weighted through pairwise comparisons within the respective panel. Across both panels, result-based payments ranked highest on biodiversity outcome certainty but lowest on administrative tractability for the current Serbian institutional context. Discriminatory-price auctions scored best overall when cost-effectiveness and monitoring feasibility were weighted equally. Sensitivity analyses showed that the ranking of flat-rate subsidies was the most unstable, shifting position under moderate changes to the weighting of farmer acceptance. The study provides a structured basis for prioritising instrument adoption in the revision of Serbian rural development programming beyond 2020.

title: Spatial targeting of agri-environment payments using habitat suitability scores: a case study for the little bustard in Vojvodina
abstract: Flat-rate payment schemes commonly fail to direct conservation funds towards parcels where the ecological return per euro is highest. This paper integrates a maximum-entropy habitat suitability model for the little bustard (Tetrax tetrax) with farm-level WTA estimates from a 2015 postal survey of 189 crop farmers across Srem and South Bačka. Suitability scores were computed from 14 landscape and land-use variables at 100-metre resolution. A spatial targeting algorithm then ranked parcels by the ratio of predicted habitat gain to WTA, generating an efficiency frontier. Full spatial targeting would achieve the same predicted area of suitable habitat as an untargeted scheme at 41 percent lower cost, or alternatively increase habitat area by 58 percent at the same budget. Sensitivity tests using alternative suitability thresholds confirm the robustness of efficiency gains above the 0.4 suitability threshold. Practical constraints including parcel accessibility and farmer participation rates are discussed, with implications for the design of forthcoming Serbian biodiversity strategy instruments.

title: Institutional barriers to result-based agri-environment schemes in post-socialist farming systems: interviews from Serbia and Romania
abstract: Result-based payment schemes link farmer remuneration directly to measurable ecological outcomes rather than prescribed management actions. While evidence from Western Europe suggests they can improve farmer motivation and conservation effectiveness, their transferability to post-socialist farming systems is poorly understood. This paper presents findings from 46 semi-structured interviews conducted in 2019 with farmers, local agricultural advisors, and ministry officials in Vojvodina, Serbia, and Timiș County, Romania. Thematic analysis identified five recurring institutional barriers: absence of reliable ecological monitoring capacity at the parcel level, weak extension service networks, low farmer trust in public payment reliability, fragmented land tenure reducing scheme eligibility, and ambiguous contract enforcement mechanisms. Barriers were more pronounced in Serbia than in Romania, partly because Romanian accession to the EU introduced administrative routines familiar with agri-environment regulation. Proposed adaptations include tiered entry schemes, collective contracts for fragmented holdings, and phased monitoring requirements calibrated to available advisory resources.

title: Agglomeration bonuses for pollinator habitat: a framed field experiment with smallholders in northern Serbia
abstract: Agglomeration bonuses reward farmers who coordinate land management with neighbours to create spatially contiguous habitat patches. This mechanism addresses the coordination externality inherent in farmland biodiversity conservation but has rarely been tested outside Northern Europe. A framed field experiment was conducted with 96 smallholder farmers in six villages in Severnobanatski and Zapadno-bački districts during spring 2020. Participants played a repeated coordination game in which they allocated hypothetical land parcels to either production or pollinator-friendly management under three payment treatments: flat-rate, flat-rate with agglomeration bonus, and auction with agglomeration bonus. Contiguous habitat formation reached 28 percent of available parcels under flat-rate payments, 51 percent with agglomeration bonuses, and 63 percent in the auction-bonus treatment. Communication rounds increased coordination rates by a further 9–12 percentage points regardless of treatment. Bonus magnitude had a nonlinear effect: bonuses below 30 EUR per hectare produced negligible coordination gains, while bonuses above 80 EUR per hectare showed diminishing returns. Results support including agglomeration provisions in Serbian pollinator strategy action plans.

title: How do organic certification and agri-environment scheme participation interact? Evidence from a panel of Vojvodina farms 2010–2021
abstract: Organic certification and agri-environment scheme participation both aim to alter farm management towards more environmentally benign outcomes, yet their interaction is rarely studied in a longitudinal framework. Using an unbalanced panel of 341 farms in Vojvodina observed over the period 2010–2021, this paper applies a bivariate probit model with endogenous switching to estimate whether the two instruments are complements or substitutes at the farm level. Data were sourced from the Provincial Fund for Agricultural Development administrative records and supplemented by phone interviews in 2022. Results indicate that certified organic farms were 18 percentage points more likely to participate in agri-environment schemes than comparable conventional farms, even after controlling for farm size, type, and operator age. However, the marginal biodiversity-related management changes associated with scheme participation were smaller for organic farms, suggesting partial overlap in prescriptions. Financial stacking—drawing payments from both instruments simultaneously—was practiced by 12 percent of the sample and was associated with significantly higher shares of uncultivated habitat features on farms. Policy implications for double-funding rules in Serbian rural development programming are discussed.

title: Farmer preferences for biodiversity credit scheme design: a discrete choice experiment in the Central Balkans
abstract: Biodiversity credit markets are being discussed as a complement to public payment schemes, but farmer-side preferences for credit scheme attributes remain poorly documented in Southeast Europe. This paper reports a discrete choice experiment administered to 278 arable and mixed farmers across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia in 2024–2025. Attributes included credit price, contract duration, verification method, buyer type, and flexibility to exit. Conditional logit and mixed logit models were estimated. Willingness to accept estimates showed that farmers required on average 31 EUR per credit as a premium to accept remote-sensing-based verification over on-farm inspection, and a further 44 EUR per credit to accept contracts longer than five years. Heterogeneity analysis using latent class models identified three farmer segments: risk-averse smallholders with strong preferences for short contracts and familiar buyers, commercially oriented larger farms willing to accept remote monitoring, and a middle group with ambiguous preferences. The findings inform the architecture of voluntary biodiversity credit pilots currently under discussion by the regional environmental ministries.

title: Designing monitoring protocols for result-based agri-environment schemes: cost, accuracy and scalability trade-offs
abstract: Result-based payment schemes require reliable monitoring of ecological outcomes, yet monitoring costs can erode the cost-effectiveness advantages these schemes hold over prescription-based alternatives. This paper examines three monitoring protocols—on-farm botanical transects conducted by trained inspectors, farmer self-assessment validated by spot checks, and satellite-derived vegetation indices—applied to 60 experimental farm contracts established under a pilot scheme in Vojvodina in 2023. Protocols were evaluated on classification accuracy against a ground-truth dataset, per-contract cost, scalability to 500 and 5,000 contracts, and the incentive compatibility of each method for participating farmers. Botanical transects achieved the highest accuracy (F1 = 0.84) but cost 310 EUR per contract annually, making large-scale rollout financially prohibitive. Satellite indices were cheapest (22 EUR per contract) but accuracy fell to F1 = 0.61 for heterogeneous small parcels below 0.8 hectares. A hybrid protocol combining annual satellite screening with targeted on-farm audits for flagged contracts reduced average cost to 67 EUR while maintaining F1 = 0.79. Practical recommendations for integrating the hybrid protocol into Serbian agri-environment scheme administration are provided.

title: Callus induction and embryogenic competence in leaf explants of wild Balkan pear (Pyrus communis subsp. pyraster): effects of 2,4-D and BAP concentration
abstract: Somatic embryogenesis in Pyrus species is notoriously recalcitrant, and protocols established for cultivated pear often fail with wild subspecies. This study examined the effect of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D; 0.5–4.0 mg/L) combined with 6-benzylaminopurine (BAP; 0.1–1.0 mg/L) on callus induction frequency and embryogenic potential in leaf explants of three wild Balkan pear accessions collected from Fruška Gora National Park. Explants were cultured on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium with half-strength macronutrients. After eight weeks, callus induction ranged from 18% to 74% depending on accession and treatment. Embryogenic callus, identified by its compact, nodular appearance under stereomicroscopy, was most frequent at 2.0 mg/L 2,4-D with 0.5 mg/L BAP, reaching 41% in accession FG-07. Histological sections confirmed the presence of bipolar embryo-like structures with distinct protoderm. Accession FG-02 showed consistently low response across all treatments, suggesting genotype-dependent recalcitrance. These results provide a baseline protocol for further optimisation and serve as a starting point for long-term conservation efforts targeting this underrepresented subspecies.

title: Sucrose pre-treatment duration and osmoprotectant concentration influence regrowth after cryopreservation of Pyrus communis subsp. pyraster embryogenic callus by vitrification
abstract: Cryopreservation by vitrification requires careful osmotic pre-conditioning to limit ice crystal damage. This study tested the effect of sucrose pre-culture duration (one, two, or three days at 0.3 M sucrose) and plant vitrification solution 2 (PVS2) exposure time (20, 40, or 60 minutes at 0 °C) on post-thaw regrowth of embryogenic callus derived from Balkan pear accession FG-07. Cryopreserved samples were stored in liquid nitrogen for 30 days before rapid warming in a 40 °C water bath. Regrowth was assessed at four and eight weeks on callus maintenance medium. A two-day sucrose pre-culture combined with 40-minute PVS2 loading yielded the highest regrowth rate of 38.4 ± 4.2%. Longer PVS2 exposure (60 min) reduced regrowth to below 15%, likely due to toxicity effects. Histological examination of regrown tissue confirmed retention of embryogenic characteristics. The results suggest that PVS2 exposure window is a more critical determinant of viability than sucrose pre-treatment duration within the ranges tested, informing future protocol refinement for this material.

title: Encapsulation-dehydration as an alternative cryopreservation route for somatic embryos of wild Balkan pear: a comparison with droplet-vitrification
abstract: Two cryopreservation approaches, encapsulation-dehydration and droplet-vitrification, were compared for their effectiveness in preserving somatic embryos of Pyrus communis subsp. pyraster accession FG-07. For encapsulation-dehydration, embryos were encapsulated in 3% sodium alginate beads, sucrose-loaded stepwise to 0.75 M over 48 hours, desiccated in a laminar flow cabinet to approximately 20–25% moisture content, and plunged directly into liquid nitrogen. For droplet-vitrification, embryos were placed in 3 µL PVS3 droplets on aluminium foil strips before plunging. Post-thaw regrowth at four weeks reached 29.1 ± 5.6% for encapsulation-dehydration and 44.7 ± 6.1% for droplet-vitrification. Conversion of regrown embryos to plantlets on hormone-free MS medium was assessed at 12 weeks; droplet-vitrification-derived material showed a conversion rate of 22%, compared to 17% for encapsulation-dehydration. Both methods yielded morphologically normal plantlets with no obvious somaclonal variation detected by visual scoring. These findings support droplet-vitrification as the preferred method for this accession while confirming encapsulation-dehydration as a viable backup strategy for field-collected material.

title: Morphological and phenological characterisation of wild Balkan pear (Pyrus communis subsp. pyraster) populations on Fruška Gora and Vršačke Planine mountains
abstract: Prior to establishing in vitro conservation collections, accurate characterisation of source populations is necessary to capture representative genetic and phenotypic diversity. This study recorded 22 morphological descriptors following IPGRI/UPOV guidelines across 47 individual trees sampled from two mountain populations on Fruška Gora (n = 29) and Vršačke Planine (n = 18) during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons. Traits included leaf shape index, fruit weight, stone cell density assessed by hand sections, flowering date, and fruit ripening date. Significant variation was observed between and within populations for most quantitative traits. Fruit weight ranged from 4.3 g to 31.7 g across all individuals. Flowering date differed by up to 11 days between the earliest and latest individuals within the Fruška Gora population. Principal component analysis of the morphological data separated the two populations along a gradient primarily associated with fruit size and leaf dimensions, accounting for 58.3% of total variance in the first two components. These data were used to select 12 priority accessions for subsequent tissue culture and cryopreservation work, prioritising phenotypically divergent individuals.

title: Influence of antioxidant supplementation during pre-culture on browning reduction and embryogenic callus quality in Pyrus communis subsp. pyraster tissue cultures
abstract: Oxidative browning of explants and callus is a persistent problem in pear tissue culture, reducing viable material and compromising subsequent cryopreservation outcomes. This study evaluated the effect of adding polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP; 0.5 and 1.0 g/L), L-ascorbic acid (50 and 100 mg/L), and activated charcoal (1.0 g/L) individually and in selected combinations to MS establishment medium, using leaf explants from accessions FG-07 and FG-11. Browning index was scored visually on a 0–4 scale at weekly intervals for six weeks. Callus fresh weight and embryogenic potential were recorded at the end of the observation period. PVP at 1.0 g/L combined with 50 mg/L ascorbic acid reduced browning index by 1.8 units relative to the unsupplemented control in FG-07, while activated charcoal alone gave a 1.4-unit reduction but also suppressed callus growth by approximately 30%. Embryogenic callus frequency was highest in the PVP plus ascorbic acid treatment at 36% for FG-07. Accession FG-11 showed lower overall browning but also lower callus induction, independent of antioxidant treatment. These results indicate that a low-concentration PVP and ascorbic acid combination offers an effective and growth-compatible approach to browning management for this subspecies.

title: Effect of imposed soil water deficit on phenylpropanoid pathway gene expression and anthocyanin yield in Sambucus nigra
abstract: Twelve elderberry cuttings of a single Pannonian-origin accession were subjected to four levels of soil water potential (−0.03, −0.1, −0.3, and −0.8 MPa) in a controlled greenhouse experiment over 60 days. Leaf gas exchange, shoot elongation, and berry dry mass were monitored weekly. At harvest, total anthocyanin content in berries increased by 34% under the −0.3 MPa treatment relative to well-watered controls, while it declined sharply at −0.8 MPa, coinciding with a 62% reduction in berry fresh mass. Reverse transcription PCR targeting chalcone synthase and dihydroflavonol 4-reductase transcripts showed up-regulation at moderate stress and suppression at severe stress. The results indicate a threshold response, with moderate water deficit acting as a mild elicitor of polyphenol accumulation without substantially compromising yield. Implications for irrigation management in commercial elderberry cultivation are discussed.
