title: Rootstock effect on nitrogen use efficiency in high-density apple orchards under two fertilisation regimes
abstract: The study quantified nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) in 'Fuji Kiku-8' apple trees grafted on M.9 NAKB T337 and B.9 rootstocks under conventional and reduced-input nitrogen fertilisation at a commercial orchard in Sremski Karlovci over four seasons (2010–2013). Labelled ¹⁵N ammonium nitrate was applied in split doses in spring and post-harvest, and isotope enrichment was measured in leaves, current-year shoots, fruit, and fine roots by isotope ratio mass spectrometry in collaboration with a partner laboratory at the University of Belgrade. Trees on B.9 showed 18% higher whole-tree NUE under reduced input compared to M.9 T337, driven primarily by greater retention in fine root tissue. Canopy light interception data collected with ceptometers indicated no significant difference between rootstocks in light distribution. Yield efficiency (kg fruit per cm² trunk cross-sectional area) was 15% higher on M.9 T337 under both fertilisation treatments. Results are discussed in the context of reducing nitrate leaching risk in sandy loam soils of the Vojvodina plain.

title: Latency Characterisation of Publish-Subscribe Messaging in Constrained Sensor Networks
abstract: This paper reports measurements of end-to-end message latency in a publish-subscribe architecture deployed over a ZigBee mesh network of 24 sensor nodes. Using a custom traffic generator and a GPS-disciplined timestamp reference, we collected roughly 1.2 million message delivery records under five broker configurations varying queue depth and QoS levels. Median latency ranged from 38 ms at QoS 0 with shallow queues to 310 ms at QoS 2 with 512-message queues under sustained 80 Hz injection. We identify queue saturation as the dominant latency contributor beyond congestion effects. Statistical models fitted to the empirical distributions allow practitioners to dimension broker resources for given latency budgets. The results are directly applicable to time-sensitive industrial monitoring deployments where sensor data must reach display or control surfaces within bounded intervals.

title: A Broker Federation Model for Multi-Site Industrial Sensor Deployments
abstract: Large industrial sites often require sensor data to traverse organisational boundaries, yet existing MQTT broker configurations provide no standardised federation mechanism. This paper presents a hierarchical broker federation model in which site-level brokers forward filtered topic subtrees to a central aggregation broker using persistent bridge connections. We implemented the model on three open-source broker platforms and evaluated it on a synthetic topology of five sites, each emitting between 200 and 800 events per second across 60 topic paths. Message loss under normal operation stayed below 0.03 percent; recovery after a simulated WAN link outage restored full throughput within 4 seconds using the proposed reconnect-and-replay procedure. Configuration complexity is addressed through a declarative YAML descriptor that generates broker bridge definitions automatically. The approach was validated in a pilot deployment at a food-processing facility in Vojvodina operating 17 monitoring stations.

title: Context Inference from Ambient Sensor Streams for Dynamic Public Display Content Selection
abstract: Digital signage in public spaces typically cycles content on fixed schedules regardless of audience size, time of day, or environmental conditions. This work proposes a context inference layer sitting between raw sensor feeds—occupancy IR arrays, CO2 sensors, noise-level microphones, and BLE beacon receivers—and a display management system. A rule engine with 34 hand-authored production rules maps sensor state combinations to content-category weights; the display scheduler then selects playlist entries proportional to those weights. A four-week field trial in a university building corridor using a six-screen installation showed that context-driven scheduling increased measured dwell time in front of displays by 22 percent compared with the fixed-rotation baseline, evaluated through a separate overhead camera with OpenCV-based pedestrian counting. Energy draw of the inference layer on a Raspberry Pi 4 averaged 3.1 W under peak sensor load.
venue: Proceedings of the Balkan Symposium on Pervasive Computing and Smart Environments (BalkanPerComp)

title: Middleware Abstractions for IoT-Driven Display Control: A Comparative Survey
abstract: This book chapter surveys middleware approaches used to connect IoT sensor infrastructure to presentation and display control layers, covering publish-subscribe systems, event stream processors, and RESTful polling architectures. For each category, the chapter examines data model expressiveness, latency guarantees, scalability evidence from published benchmarks, and suitability for scenarios ranging from single-room smart environments to campus-wide digital signage networks. Seven open-source and four commercial middleware platforms are assessed against a common evaluation grid of 18 criteria. The chapter also reviews protocol bridging strategies needed when legacy BACnet or Modbus installations must feed modern MQTT or AMQP buses. A short case study drawn from the authors' own testbed illustrates how multiple middleware layers can be composed without introducing unacceptable end-to-end latency. The chapter is aimed at practitioners designing IoT-to-display pipelines and at researchers seeking gaps in the literature.

title: Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Occupancy Sensor Streams Using Lightweight Statistical Models on Edge Nodes
abstract: Building automation and smart signage systems depend on reliable occupancy estimates, yet raw IR array and PIR sensor streams contain frequent artefacts: sensor dropout, motion blur at entry zones, and heating-induced false positives. This paper implements three lightweight anomaly detectors—exponentially weighted moving average control charts, interquartile-range filters, and a small one-class support vector machine with RBF kernel—on Cortex-M4 class microcontrollers acting as edge nodes. Each detector was trained on two weeks of labelled data from a 12-sensor corridor installation and evaluated on a further four-week hold-out set. The EWMA chart achieved the best trade-off, reaching 91.4 percent recall on injected drop-out anomalies at 1.8 percent false positive rate while consuming under 6 KB of RAM. Detection latency stayed below 15 ms in all tested configurations, preserving the real-time behaviour required by downstream display control loops.

title: Evaluating WebSocket and Server-Sent Events as Transport Alternatives to MQTT for Low-Latency Signage Control
abstract: MQTT is the dominant choice for IoT-to-display pipelines, but browser-native transports such as WebSocket and Server-Sent Events are attractive when display clients run in standard web browsers without additional agent software. This paper presents a controlled benchmark comparing all three transports over a 100 Mbit/s LAN and a throttled 10 Mbit/s WAN emulation under message rates of 10, 100, and 500 messages per second, with payload sizes of 64 B, 512 B, and 4 KB. At 100 msg/s and 512 B payloads on the LAN, median latency was 2.1 ms for MQTT QoS 0, 3.4 ms for WebSocket with a lightweight broker relay, and 5.9 ms for SSE. Under WAN conditions, WebSocket with binary framing closed the gap substantially. CPU overhead on the broker-side relay process was measured at 4–12 percent depending on connection count (10–200 clients). The findings inform protocol selection guidelines for signage deployments where browser rendering is preferred.

title: Schema-on-Read vs. Schema-on-Write for Heterogeneous IoT Sensor Metadata in Signage Control Pipelines
abstract: Integrating sensors from multiple vendors into a unified signage control pipeline exposes a fundamental tension between enforcing a common message schema at ingestion time versus deferring schema interpretation to query time. This paper formalises both strategies as pipeline configurations and evaluates them against three criteria: integration effort when adding a new sensor type, query execution time over a six-month archive of 4.2 billion records stored in a columnar store, and the frequency of downstream rendering errors caused by unexpected field absence. Experiments used a dataset from a 40-device heterogeneous sensor installation combining weather stations, CO2 meters, and BLE scanners. Schema-on-write reduced rendering errors by a factor of 8 but required an average of 3.2 developer-hours per new sensor type for schema adaptation. Schema-on-read cut integration effort to under 40 minutes but increased query latency by 34 percent. A hybrid strategy with a thin normalisation shim is proposed and evaluated.

title: A Declarative Rule Language for Context-Triggered Display Scheduling in Smart Building Environments
abstract: Configuring context-aware digital signage currently requires programming expertise, limiting deployment to organisations with dedicated software staff. This paper presents DispRule, a declarative domain-specific language that allows facility managers to express content scheduling policies as condition-action rules referencing named sensor streams and content tags. The language compiler translates rules into a directed event-processing graph executed by a lightweight engine running on commodity x86 hardware. We describe the language grammar, the compilation pipeline, and a runtime with a worst-case rule evaluation cycle of 8 ms on an Intel NUC with 64 active rules and 30 concurrent sensor feeds. A usability evaluation with 14 non-programmer participants using a think-aloud protocol showed that participants could author correct three-condition rules within an average of 11 minutes after a 20-minute tutorial. Two deployment case studies—a hospital outpatient waiting area and a university canteen—illustrate practical rule sets.
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Context-Aware Computing and Adaptive Systems (ICCAS)

title: Backpressure Propagation in Chained MQTT Broker Topologies Under Burst Sensor Traffic
abstract: When sensor networks emit short traffic bursts—common during building entry rushes, alarm events, or scheduled batch reports—chained broker topologies can experience cascading queue growth that degrades end-to-end latency well beyond steady-state expectations. This paper models backpressure propagation analytically using a tandem M/D/1 queue approximation and validates predictions against measurements on a three-tier broker chain running Mosquitto 2.0. Burst scenarios were generated by replaying traces captured from a 55-sensor smart building installation over 30 days. The model predicted 90th-percentile latency spikes within 18 percent of measured values across all tested burst amplitudes (2×–10× baseline rate) and durations (0.5–8 s). Based on the analysis, we propose two broker-side mitigations—adaptive rate shaping at ingress brokers and selective topic prioritisation—and show through experiments that combining both reduces latency spike magnitude by 61 percent without message loss.

title: Energy-Proportional Scheduling of Display Panel Arrays Driven by Occupancy Prediction Models
abstract: Large digital signage installations in public buildings consume significant standby power when screens remain active in unoccupied spaces. This paper investigates whether short-horizon occupancy predictions derived from IoT sensor streams can be used to schedule panel sleep-wake cycles without degrading perceived content availability. Three prediction models are compared—a seasonal naive baseline, a gradient-boosted tree, and a compact LSTM—trained on four months of occupancy data from a 12-panel corridor installation. The LSTM achieved 87 percent accuracy on 5-minute ahead predictions using inputs from PIR sensors, door contact switches, and calendar data. A simulated annealing scheduler translated predictions into panel state plans, evaluated against a cost function balancing energy use and missed-audience penalties. In a six-week live deployment, the approach reduced panel active hours by 29 percent while keeping content visible to 96 percent of observed passersby, compared with a motion-triggered baseline retaining 98 percent coverage.

title: Test Flakiness in Machine Learning Pipelines: Characteristics and Preliminary Detection Heuristics
abstract: Machine learning (ML) training pipelines introduce sources of non-determinism—random weight initialisation, data shuffling, hardware-level floating-point variability—that make conventional flakiness detection approaches ill-suited. This paper characterises flakiness in 8 Python ML projects that use pytest for unit and integration testing, identifying 94 flaky tests through repeated reruns (each test executed 50 times per configuration) across three hardware environments. Findings show that 61 % of flakiness in this corpus is attributable to unseeded random operations and 22 % to floating-point tolerance mismatches in assertion statements. A set of lightweight static heuristics based on AST patterns—detecting torch.manual_seed absence, numpy.random calls, and hard-coded floating-point thresholds in assertions—detects 68 % of flaky tests at a false positive rate of 11 %. The paper positions ML pipeline flakiness as a distinct sub-problem requiring dedicated tooling, and outlines a research agenda.

title: Continual Learning for OCR Systems Deployed on Evolving Financial Form Templates
abstract: Financial authorities periodically revise standardised form templates, causing distribution shift that degrades deployed OCR systems. We study continual learning strategies for a CRNN-based financial OCR pipeline subjected to four sequential template revision events, using real data from Serbian fiscal years 2018–2024. Four strategies are evaluated: fine-tuning, elastic weight consolidation, experience replay with a 5% memory buffer, and a task-conditional adapter approach. Catastrophic forgetting is measured by character error rate on all previously seen template versions after each update. Experience replay provides the best retention (average CER increase of 0.9 points over the four events) while adapter-based methods provide the best accuracy on new templates (CER 2.3%) but at the cost of higher forgetting (3.8 points). We discuss deployment trade-offs and propose a mixed strategy triggered by statistical drift detection on incoming document batches.

title: Exploiting Temporal Correlation in Multi-Sensor Nodes: Joint Source Coding Without Inter-Sensor Communication
abstract: When multiple sensors share a single microcontroller, their streams are often temporally correlated, but joint source coding typically requires a coordination step. This paper proposes a correlation-exploiting compressor that operates independently on each stream yet achieves joint compression gains by using a shared codebook trained offline on historical multi-sensor data. The codebook is partitioned by predicted correlation class, selected at runtime via a three-feature lightweight classifier running in 80 bytes of RAM. We evaluate the scheme on a 6-sensor indoor air-quality dataset (PM2.5, CO2, VOC, temperature, humidity, pressure) collected over 12 weeks in three office buildings in Novi Sad, totalling 41 million samples. Compared to independently trained per-sensor codebooks, the shared-codebook scheme reduces average bit rate by 17% at equal distortion. Codebook size is 6.8 kB, fitting in the flash of a Cortex-M0+. The classifier overhead is 12 cycles per sample. The paper analyses sensitivity to training-deployment distributional shift across seasons.

title: Automating MISRA-C:2012 Violation Repair Using Syntax-Directed Rewriting
abstract: Achieving compliance with MISRA-C:2012 in a legacy codebase typically involves many hundreds of manual edits. This paper describes a tool, MisraFix, that uses Clang's LibTooling infrastructure to implement syntax-directed rewriting rules for 34 of the 143 MISRA-C:2012 rules classified as decidable and automatable by the authors. The tool is evaluated on a corpus of five embedded firmware codebases totalling 312 kB of C source. Before applying MisraFix, a commercial MISRA-C checker reported 2,847 violations across the five projects; after automated repair, 1,654 violations were resolved (58.1%). All repaired versions compile and pass their existing test suites without modification. The paper categorises the remaining violations by reason for non-automation: semantic ambiguity, required developer intent, or interaction with platform-specific extensions. Runtime of the tool ranges from 3 to 41 seconds per project. Source code and the rewriting rule descriptions are published under a permissive open-source licence.

title: Event-Based Visual Odometry Using a Continuous-Time Trajectory Representation
abstract: Discrete-time pose representations introduce integration errors when event data arrives at sub-millisecond intervals. We model the camera trajectory as a B-spline in SE(3) and formulate event-based visual odometry as a continuous-time estimation problem. Events are associated with map points through a predict-and-render loop: the spline is used to warp a stored gradient map to predicted event positions, and a photometric residual drives optimisation via Gauss–Newton iterations. On the publicly available ECD benchmark sequences, our method achieves mean translational RMSE of 12.3 cm on the boxes_6dof sequence and 8.7 cm on the poster_6dof sequence, comparing favourably against three state-of-the-art frame-based and event-based baselines. Computation requires 18 ms per 10,000-event batch on a mid-range desktop GPU, meeting real-time requirements for most robotic platforms.

title: Comparison of IDW and Ordinary Kriging for Monthly Rainfall Interpolation in the Vojvodina Lowlands Using a Sparse Station Network
abstract: Accurate spatial representations of monthly rainfall in flat agricultural regions are difficult to achieve when ground station density is low. This study compared inverse distance weighting (IDW) and ordinary kriging (OK) for interpolating monthly precipitation totals across Vojvodina using data from 24 meteorological stations maintained by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia for the period 2001–2010. Cross-validation was performed by withholding one station at a time; root mean square errors were 18.3 mm for IDW and 14.7 mm for OK at the monthly scale, with the largest discrepancies occurring during convective summer months. Semivariogram analysis revealed a mean range of approximately 62 km for summer months and 110 km for winter months, indicating substantial seasonal changes in spatial autocorrelation structure. The results suggest that ordinary kriging outperforms IDW in this region but that both methods underestimate peak rainfall cells associated with localised convective events. These findings informed subsequent work on integrating satellite data as auxiliary covariates.

title: Kriging with External Drift Using IMERG Precipitation as a Covariate for Sub-Monthly Rainfall Mapping at 1 km Resolution in Northern Serbia
abstract: This study applied kriging with external drift (KED) to downscale 10-day accumulated rainfall to a 1 km grid over northern Serbia, using GPM IMERG Late Run estimates as the external drift variable and data from 31 ground stations as primary observations. The analysis covered the 2014–2018 growing seasons (April–September). IMERG values were resampled from their native 0.1° resolution to 1 km using bilinear interpolation before entering the KED framework. Leave-one-out cross-validation showed that KED reduced RMSE by 21% relative to ordinary kriging and by 34% relative to IDW, averaged across the study period. Performance gains were most pronounced during spatially heterogeneous convective periods in June and July. The resulting 1 km grids captured within-field rainfall gradients of up to 15 mm per 10-day period across large agricultural parcels, which ordinary kriging had smoothed over. Maps produced in this study were subsequently used as candidate index layers for parametric crop insurance pilot design.

title: Design of a Rainfall Deficit Index for Maize Insurance in the Vojvodina Region: Sensitivity to Spatial Resolution of Input Precipitation Grids
abstract: Index insurance products that trigger payouts based on area-average rainfall can suffer from basis risk when the spatial resolution of the underlying precipitation data does not capture field-level variability. This study quantified how the choice of precipitation grid resolution (0.25°, 0.05°, and 1 km downscaled) affects the properties of a 30-day rainfall deficit index (RDI) designed for rainfed maize in Vojvodina. Historical RDI series were reconstructed for 1995–2018 using ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25°, CHIRPS at 0.05°, and a KED-downscaled product at 1 km. Basis risk was approximated by computing the correlation between field-scale simulated crop water deficits from a DSSAT maize model and each RDI series for 120 sample parcels. Pearson correlation with the 1 km RDI was 0.71, versus 0.58 for CHIRPS and 0.49 for ERA5. Trigger and exit thresholds calibrated on the 1 km product changed payout frequency by up to 18 percentage points compared with coarser inputs. The findings support the use of downscaled grids in parametric product design where field-level basis risk reduction is a priority.

title: Field-Level Validation of Downscaled Precipitation Grids Using Dense Micro-Station Networks in Two Vojvodina Municipalities
abstract: Validating precipitation downscaling products at the field level requires ground truth at sub-kilometre spacing, which standard meteorological networks cannot provide. This study deployed a temporary network of 18 tipping-bucket rain gauges at 300–600 m spacing across two municipalities in Vojvodina—Bačka Palanka and Zrenjanin—during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons, collecting data at 15-minute resolution. These measurements were withheld from the downscaling model and used exclusively for validation. The KED-downscaled product at 1 km showed mean absolute errors of 3.1 mm per 10-day period, compared with 5.8 mm for bilinearly resampled IMERG and 4.4 mm for CHIRPS. The micro-station data also revealed that within-field gradients exceeding 8 mm per 10-day period occurred in approximately 12% of observed convective events, confirming that field-level insurance products cannot rely on grid spacings coarser than 1–2 km in this region. Equipment deployment and data management protocols developed here are available as a supplementary technical guide.

title: Assessing sub-kilometre spatial coherence of convective rainfall using a dense disdrometer transect across the Fruška Gora ridge
abstract: A transect of 22 optical disdrometers spaced 800 m apart along a 17.5 km line perpendicular to the Fruška Gora mountain ridge was operated during May–September 2022 to characterise the spatial decorrelation of convective rainfall intensity at sub-kilometre scales. During 38 convective events, inter-instrument correlation coefficients for 5-minute intensities were computed as a function of separation distance and storm advection direction. The correlation length for 5-minute intensities exceeded 8 km for stratiform rainfall but dropped to 2.1 km for intense convective cells (R > 20 mm h⁻¹). An anisotropy ratio of 1.6 was identified between the ridge-parallel and ridge-perpendicular directions, attributable to orographic forcing of cell alignment. These results impose quantitative limits on the validity of spatial interpolation at spacings used by most national rain-gauge networks. Implications for the accuracy of kriging-merged products at sub-hourly time steps are discussed with reference to the error budgets reported in our earlier Pannonian Plain merging study.

title: Atmospheric correction of Landsat-5 TM imagery over lowland agricultural areas using MODIS-derived aerosol optical depth
abstract: Accurate atmospheric correction is a prerequisite for quantitative surface reflectance retrieval in flat, spectrally homogeneous landscapes. This study evaluates the MODTRAN-based Second Simulation of a Satellite Signal in the Solar Spectrum (6S) code applied to a 2008–2010 Landsat-5 TM archive covering the Vojvodina plain, using collocated AERONET and MODIS MOD04 aerosol optical depth (AOD) at 550 nm as input. Twenty-seven cloud-free scenes were processed. Substituting MODIS-derived AOD for the standard rural aerosol model reduced the root-mean-square error of surface reflectance in the red band from 0.031 to 0.018 when validated against 14 in-situ spectroradiometer measurements collected on concurrent ground-truth campaigns. Corrections were smallest in the blue band (residual RMSE 0.025) owing to remaining uncertainty in the fine-mode fraction. Results confirm that MODIS MOD04 provides a practical, spatially continuous AOD input suitable for retrospective archive processing in the region, avoiding the dependence on sparse sunphotometer networks.

title: Object-based classification of informal housing clusters in post-socialist peri-urban zones: a case study of Novi Sad
abstract: This study applied object-based image analysis (OBIA) to a 2009 QuickBird-2 mosaic (0.6 m pan-sharpened) covering 48 km² on the southern and eastern fringes of Novi Sad to delineate informal residential clusters. Segmentation was performed with a multiresolution algorithm at scale parameters 40–80. Seventeen spectral, textural and geometric features were derived per segment, and a random forest classifier trained on 620 manually labelled reference objects achieved an overall accuracy of 87.3 % (kappa 0.83). The method distinguished informal structures from formal low-density housing and agricultural storage buildings with a producer accuracy of 84 % and user accuracy of 89 % for the informal class. Results documented approximately 340 ha of informally constructed residential fabric predating the 2009 imagery, concentrating along the Danube floodplain margins and two main arterial corridors. The paper discusses the sensitivity of results to segmentation scale choice and the transferability of the feature set to adjacent municipalities.

title: Temporal comparison of peri-urban expansion in three Vojvodina towns using Ikonos and WorldView-1 imagery, 2003–2010
abstract: Change between 2003 Ikonos (4 m multispectral) and 2010 WorldView-1 (0.5 m panchromatic) imagery was assessed for peri-urban zones of Subotica, Zrenjanin and Sombor to quantify the rate and spatial pattern of new construction at urban fringes. Pre-processing included sensor-specific radiometric normalisation, histogram matching, and co-registration to sub-pixel accuracy (RMSE < 0.4 m). Binary change maps derived from post-classification comparison were validated against municipal building permit records and field survey points. Across the three towns, a combined 178 ha of new built-up area was detected, of which 41 % lacked corresponding building permit records, indicating informal construction activity. Growth was markedly asymmetric: southern peripheral zones showed the highest expansion rates, coinciding with proximity to road infrastructure and lower agricultural land values. Seasonal spectral variability between acquisition dates introduced a false-alarm rate of approximately 7 %, which was reduced to 3 % after applying a minimum mapping unit of 100 m².

title: Automated extraction of road network encroachment by informal construction from multi-temporal VHR imagery
abstract: Informal buildings constructed within legal road reserve setbacks reduce effective carriageway width and complicate future road improvement projects. A workflow was developed to detect such encroachments automatically by overlaying multi-temporal change maps (2012–2023, derived from Pléiades and WorldView-2) with cadastrally defined road reserve polygons for 85 km of peri-urban road network in four Vojvodina municipalities. Encroachment detection used a 3 m buffer inward from the road reserve boundary to account for co-registration uncertainty. Over the period, 138 discrete new structures were detected within road reserves, totalling 2,940 m² of footprint. The approach was validated against a municipal road authority field inventory conducted in 2022, achieving 83 % concordance at the segment level. Processing time for the 85 km network was approximately 4 hours on a single GPU workstation. The workflow is designed to run within Google Earth Engine with minor adaptation.
venue: Applied Geomatics

title: Seasonal variation in voxel-based canopy structure metrics derived from repeated UAV LiDAR acquisitions in a temperate mixed forest
abstract: The sensitivity of voxel-based structural metrics to seasonal leaf phenology was assessed through five repeated UAV LiDAR acquisitions conducted at three mixed broadleaf forest plots in northern Serbia between March and October 2024. Metrics examined included filled-voxel ratio, vertical plant area volume density profiles, and upper canopy rugosity index, computed at a 0.10 m voxel resolution. Leaf-off acquisitions in early spring showed filled-voxel ratios 41–58% lower than peak leaf-on values in July, with the largest relative changes observed in the understorey layer (below 8 m). Height percentile metrics (P70–P95) remained comparatively stable across seasons (coefficient of variation < 6%), suggesting utility as season-independent inputs for AGB models. Point cloud density varied from 95 to 220 points m⁻² across flights due to wind-induced platform instability. The study provides a seasonal calibration reference for researchers integrating multi-temporal LiDAR data into continuous forest monitoring workflows in continental European climates.
venue: Remote Sensing Letters

title: Effect of Post-Weld Heat Treatment on Residual Stress Distribution in T-Joint Welds of Low-Alloy Steel
abstract: Residual stresses in as-welded and post-weld heat-treated (PWHT) T-joint specimens of S460M low-alloy steel were measured by hole-drilling with strain-gauge rosettes and compared with sequentially coupled thermal–mechanical FE simulations. Six as-welded and six PWHT specimens (650 °C for 1 h, furnace-cooled) were examined. The FE model employed a double-ellipsoid heat source and temperature-dependent material data derived from dilatometry. Peak tensile residual stresses at the weld toe in the as-welded condition reached 312 MPa in the longitudinal direction and 187 MPa transversally. After PWHT, peak values fell to 74 MPa and 41 MPa, respectively. Agreement between hole-drilling measurements and simulation was within 15% at all measurement points. The study quantified how PWHT redistribution of residual stress affected predicted fatigue lives using a linear-elastic fracture-mechanics assessment: estimated endurance at the design stress range of 90 MPa increased from 1.2 × 10⁶ to 3.8 × 10⁶ cycles following PWHT.

title: Low-Cycle Fatigue Behaviour of Cruciform Welded Joints at −40 °C: An Experimental Study
abstract: The paper reports strain-controlled low-cycle fatigue (LCF) tests on cruciform fillet-welded joints machined from S355J2+N plate and tested at both room temperature (20 °C) and −40 °C. A total of 32 specimens were cycled at total strain amplitudes of 0.25%, 0.50%, 0.75%, and 1.00% using a servo-hydraulic machine equipped with a liquid-nitrogen climate chamber. Cyclic stress–strain curves, Coffin–Manson parameters, and fatigue ductility exponents were extracted from the hysteresis data. At −40 °C, the fatigue ductility coefficient εf′ decreased by 22% relative to room temperature, whereas the fatigue strength coefficient σf′ increased by 11%, resulting in a crossover in life predictions near 3 × 10³ reversals. Fractographic examination by SEM confirmed transgranular cleavage facets in low-temperature specimens at strain amplitudes above 0.75%, indicating a mixed ductile–brittle fracture mode not observed at room temperature. The Morrow mean-stress correction improved life predictions in the −40 °C dataset.

title: Interaction of Mechanical Cyclic Loading and Thermal Cycling on Fatigue Life of Butt-Welded Structural Steel Plates
abstract: This work examined whether superimposed thermal cycling (between −30 °C and +20 °C at 0.5 cycles per hour) during mechanical fatigue loading alters crack initiation and growth behaviour in butt-welded S275JR plates. Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF, with twelve specimens per programme. Crack initiation life, defined as a 5% stiffness drop, was shortest in the out-of-phase TMF condition, averaging 28% fewer cycles than the room-temperature baseline. Crack growth rates in both TMF programmes exceeded predictions based on simple superposition of mechanical and thermal stress intensities, suggesting a synergistic damage mechanism tentatively linked to accelerated oxidation at crack flanks during temperature excursions. FE simulations using temperature-dependent elastic–plastic material models reproduced the crack-tip opening displacement within 8% of experimental digital image correlation measurements. Design implications are discussed in the context of the IIW fatigue assessment recommendations.

title: Fracture Toughness of Heat-Affected Zone Microstructures in S690QL High-Strength Steel Welds at Sub-Zero Temperatures
abstract: Charpy impact and CTOD (crack-tip opening displacement) tests were performed on specimens extracted from the coarse-grained heat-affected zone (CGHAZ) of single-pass submerged-arc welds in 20 mm S690QL plate at temperatures of +20, 0, −20, −40, and −60 °C. The CGHAZ was reproduced by Gleeble thermal simulation at peak temperatures of 1350 °C and cooling times t8/5 of 8 s and 20 s to replicate low and high heat-input conditions. At −40 °C, mean CTOD values dropped from 0.18 mm (t8/5 = 8 s) to 0.07 mm (t8/5 = 20 s), confirming sensitivity of toughness to heat input. A Weibull statistical analysis of CTOD scatter, using the master-curve approach per EN ISO 27306, yielded reference temperatures T0 of −62 °C and −38 °C for the two thermal cycles. These values were incorporated into a fracture-mechanics fitness-for-service assessment of a hypothetical pressure vessel nozzle weld, defining the tolerable flaw size at operating temperature.

title: Finite-Element Estimation of Stress Intensity Factors for Surface Cracks at Weld Toes Under Combined Bending and Torsion
abstract: Semi-elliptical surface cracks at the toe of transverse attachment welds were modelled in Abaqus using the extended finite element method (XFEM) to compute stress intensity factors KI and KIII under proportional and non-proportional combinations of four-point bending and torsion. Weld-toe geometry was parameterised by toe radius ρ (0.5–2.5 mm) and flank angle θ (30°–60°), yielding a factorial design of 25 configurations. Stress intensity factors normalised as geometric correction functions F(a/c, a/t) were tabulated for aspect ratios a/c from 0.2 to 1.0 and relative depths a/t from 0.05 to 0.6. Under non-proportional loading (90° phase shift between bending and torsion), effective ΔKeq computed via the Richard criterion exceeded the proportional-loading values by up to 34% at shallow crack depths, highlighting the inadequacy of simple scalar superposition. The resulting correction-factor tables are formatted to be compatible with the BS 7910:2013 Level 2 assessment procedure.

title: Weld Residual Stress Relaxation Under Cyclic Loading: Measurements and Modelling for S355 Cruciform Joints
abstract: Residual stress relaxation in S355 cruciform fillet-welded joints was tracked over 10, 100, 1000, and 10 000 fatigue cycles at three nominal stress ranges (60, 120, and 180 MPa) using X-ray diffraction (XRD) on polished surfaces at the weld toe. Initial peak longitudinal residual stress averaged +287 MPa in the as-welded state. After 1000 cycles at 180 MPa, surface residual stresses had relaxed to +61 MPa, while deeper stresses (measured by sequential electropolishing to 1.2 mm depth) retained 40–60% of their initial values. A cyclic plasticity FE model employing a Chaboche kinematic hardening rule reproduced the surface relaxation trend within 12% across all conditions. A semi-empirical relaxation factor was derived and incorporated into a fatigue life calculation, reducing the unconservative error in life prediction from 42% to 11% compared with assuming fixed residual stresses. Practical guidance for applying the relaxation factor in design is summarised.

title: Fatigue Assessment of Welded Joints in Crane Runway Girders Subjected to Operational Temperature Variations: A Case Study
abstract: A fatigue assessment was performed for the welded runway girder of an outdoor overhead crane operating in a continental climate where ambient temperature ranges from −28 °C to +38 °C over a calendar year. Operational load spectra were recorded by a data logger over an eight-month measurement campaign using strain gauges at twelve positions on two girders at a metalworking plant in the Vojvodina region. Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment. Fatigue life estimates were computed following the IIW recommendations, both with and without temperature-dependent fracture-mechanics corrections derived from the authors' earlier low-temperature CTOD dataset. Ignoring temperature dependence overestimated fatigue life at the weld toe by factors of 1.3–1.7 depending on detail category. The study recommends that crane structures in cold continental climates should apply a temperature knock-down factor on the fatigue strength class.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Fatigue Life Prediction Models for Welded S355 and S460 Steels Under Multiaxial Proportional Loading at Low Temperatures
abstract: Five multiaxial fatigue models — Findley, Fatemi–Socie, Smith–Watson–Topper, Liu, and a critical-plane von Mises variant — were evaluated against an experimental dataset of 84 fatigue tests on tubular welded specimens of S355J2 and S460NL steels tested under combined axial–torsional proportional loading at 20 °C, 0 °C, −20 °C, and −40 °C. Specimens failed either at the weld toe or in the weld metal, and failure locations were identified post-fracture by SEM. All five models were calibrated using room-temperature fatigue data and then applied predictively at sub-zero temperatures. The Fatemi–Socie model, when modified to incorporate temperature-dependent shear modulus and yield strength, produced the lowest scatter band (factor of 2.1 on life) across the full temperature range. The Liu model was accurate at room temperature but increasingly non-conservative below −20 °C. A correction procedure for the low-temperature regime is proposed and validated against the experimental data.

title: Thermal Gradient-Induced Residual Stress in Welded Box Sections: A Parametric Finite-Element Study
abstract: Welded box-section columns fabricated from 10 mm S355 plate were analysed by sequentially coupled thermal–structural FE simulations in Abaqus to evaluate how diurnal and seasonal thermal gradients (ΔT = 20–60 K through the wall thickness) modify as-welded residual stress fields. The parametric study varied four weld sequences (one-sided, two-sided symmetric, and two asymmetric sequences) and three wall thicknesses (8, 12, and 16 mm). Thermal gradients were imposed as boundary conditions representing solar irradiation on one face of the section. Results showed that a steady 40 K gradient reduced peak tensile weld-toe residual stresses by 8–14% on the heated face while increasing compressive stresses on the opposite face by a comparable margin, with the effects being most pronounced in one-sided welding sequences. At 60 K, bending stresses induced by the gradient were of the same order as the fatigue-relevant residual stress range, justifying their inclusion in fitness-for-service assessments of outdoor structures. A simplified formula, calibrated against the FE results, is provided for quick engineering estimation.

title: Crack Closure and Effective Stress Intensity Under Superimposed Mechanical and Thermal Cycling: Measurements by Digital Image Correlation
abstract: Crack closure behaviour was quantified experimentally in centre-cracked tension specimens of butt-welded S355JR plate subjected to mechanical fatigue (R = 0.05, ΔP = 18 kN) combined with slow thermal cycling between −25 °C and +15 °C. Full-field displacement maps were acquired by two-camera stereo DIC at six points within each mechanical load cycle and at five points within each thermal half-cycle. The crack opening load Pop was identified as the load at which DIC-detected displacements became linear over a 2 mm gauge length straddling the crack tip. Pop was 12–19% higher in the thermal-cycling condition than in the isothermal baseline, and the effective stress ratio Reff was reduced accordingly. Plasticity-induced closure, measured as the reversed plastic zone size from DIC strain fields, was 0.18 mm at room temperature and increased to 0.27 mm at −20 °C, consistent with reduced crack-tip plasticity at lower temperature. Incorporating the measured Reff into a modified Paris-law prediction reduced the mean life-prediction error from −31% to −7%.

title: Adaptive Octree Subdivision for Dynamic Particle Systems Under Frame-Rate Constraints
abstract: Static octree depths impose either unnecessary memory costs or insufficient spatial resolution when particle distributions change rapidly. This work presents a per-frame adaptive subdivision scheme in which leaf nodes are split or merged based on occupancy thresholds measured during the previous simulation step. The algorithm runs entirely on GPU using CUDA dynamic parallelism, avoiding CPU round-trips. Experiments use three test scenarios: a fluid splash (up to 800 k particles, high locality), a smoke dispersion (600 k particles, diffuse), and a collision debris field (1.2 M particles, mixed). Subdivision decisions are propagated asynchronously alongside the integration kernel. The adaptive scheme maintains a target of 60 fps on an NVIDIA Maxwell GPU at 800 k particles, whereas a fixed-depth octree at equivalent resolution drops to 41 fps. Memory overhead is reduced by 34 % relative to a worst-case pre-allocated fixed tree. Limitations in highly turbulent distributions are discussed.

title: Level-of-Detail Particle Rendering on Tile-Based Deferred GPU Architectures
abstract: Tile-based deferred rendering (TBDR) architectures, used in mobile and embedded GPUs, exhibit different bottleneck profiles than immediate-mode desktop GPUs when rendering large particle counts with per-particle alpha blending. This paper adapts a screen-space LOD scheme, originally designed for desktop hardware, to TBDR constraints by reorganising draw calls to minimise tile-memory evictions and reduce overdraw in the fragment pipeline. The LOD scheme discretises particles into four distance bands and substitutes billboard geometry of decreasing vertex count and texture resolution at each band. Tests are conducted on a Mali-T880 development board and an Adreno 530-based platform using particle counts from 10 k to 300 k. The adapted scheme achieves a 2.1× frame-time reduction versus the unmodified pipeline at 200 k particles on the Mali target, with a perceived visual difference below the threshold used in a small (n=24) paired-comparison user study.

title: Hierarchical Simulation Methods for Real-Time GPU Particle Systems with Spatial Coherence Exploitation
abstract: Doctoral dissertation presenting a unified framework that combines adaptive octree structures, spatial-coherence-aware scheduling of CUDA thread blocks, and a four-level LOD rendering pipeline. The framework is evaluated on five application domains: fire, fluid surface foam, granular material settling, dust suspension, and crowd silhouette effects. Hardware targets include a desktop NVIDIA Pascal GPU and an embedded NVIDIA Tegra X1 platform. On the desktop target, the framework sustains 60 fps at 1.5 M particles for all five domains. On the Tegra X1, throughput reaches 60 fps at 180 k particles for low-variance distributions and 60 fps at 90 k particles for turbulent distributions. The dissertation contributes: a formal model of spatial coherence metrics used to drive adaptive scheduling; an analysis of false-sharing patterns in octree traversal on TBDR hardware; and a parametric LOD budget allocation method for scenes with multiple concurrent particle emitters.

title: Compute Shader Implementations of Parallel Prefix Scan for Particle Sort on OpenGL ES 3.1 Hardware
abstract: Sorting particles by depth prior to alpha-blended rendering requires an efficient parallel sort on hardware where CUDA is unavailable. This paper implements and compares four parallel prefix scan variants — Kogge-Stone, Brent-Kung, decoupled look-back, and a bank-conflict-free Hillis-Steele variant — using OpenGL ES 3.1 compute shaders, targeting the constraint that only 32 KB of shared memory per workgroup is available. A radix sort built on each scan variant is benchmarked sorting arrays of 64 k to 1 M 32-bit keys on three embedded GPU platforms. Decoupled look-back achieves the highest throughput (870 M keys/s at 1 M elements on the strongest target) but requires careful handling of incomplete wavefronts at array boundaries. Bank-conflict-free Hillis-Steele is the most portable across the three tested drivers. The paper reports driver-specific anomalies that affect barrier semantics, along with workarounds validated on each platform.

title: Particle System Optimisation Techniques for Real-Time Applications on Constrained Hardware
abstract: A survey and synthesis chapter covering the period 2008–2019, examining spatial acceleration structures (grids, k-d trees, octrees, bounding volume hierarchies), GPU scheduling strategies, LOD approaches, and memory layout choices specifically in the context of particle systems with fewer than 2 M particles on hardware without dedicated ray-tracing cores. The chapter evaluates 47 primary works against a unified benchmark taxonomy, identifying that LOD transition artefacts and dynamic subdivision overhead are the two most frequently underreported costs. It introduces a classification of hardware constraint regimes — memory-limited, bandwidth-limited, and compute-limited — and maps the surveyed techniques to each regime. The chapter is directed at practitioners working on game engines, embedded simulation tools, and scientific visualisation systems who must select from a range of established methods under known hardware budgets.

title: Frame-Budget-Aware LOD Switching for Multi-Emitter Particle Scenes on Mobile GPUs
abstract: Scenes with five or more concurrent particle emitters require per-emitter LOD budgets that sum to a global frame-time constraint. Prior work allocates LOD budgets statically or by simple distance ranking. This paper formulates the allocation problem as a knapsack variant where each LOD level of each emitter has a measured cost in GPU milliseconds and a perceptual weight derived from screen-space projected area and emitter opacity. A greedy heuristic and a short-horizon dynamic programming solver are evaluated; the greedy heuristic achieves within 4 % of the DP solution at one-tenth the CPU overhead. Evaluation uses a test harness with eight emitter configurations (3–12 emitters, 50 k–600 k total particles) on an Adreno 640 device. The frame-budget method reduces frame-time variance by 61 % compared to distance-only LOD at mixed-emitter scenes, keeping 97.3 % of frames within a 16.67 ms budget.

title: Profiling Memory Access Patterns in Hierarchical Particle Simulations on Unified Memory Architectures
abstract: Unified memory architectures, in which CPU and GPU share a physical memory pool, alter the cost model for hierarchical data structures compared to discrete GPU memory systems. This paper instruments an octree-based particle simulation using hardware performance counters on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin platform to measure page migration frequency, cache-line utilisation, and TLB miss rates during three simulation phases: tree build, neighbour search, and integration. At 500 k particles, neighbour search generates 2.3 M TLB misses per frame under a naive pointer-based octree layout; a linearised depth-first node layout reduces this to 410 k misses and improves neighbour search throughput by 38 %. The paper reports the measurement methodology in detail, discusses reproducibility across firmware versions, and provides a layout transformation utility. Results are also compared against discrete-memory results from a previous study to quantify the architecture effect.

title: Granularity Selection for GPU Thread Block Decomposition in Hierarchical Particle Neighbour Searches
abstract: Thread block granularity — the number of particles assigned per block — interacts non-trivially with octree node occupancy distributions, warp divergence, and shared-memory usage during neighbour search. This study conducts a systematic sweep over block sizes of 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512 threads on four GPU architectures (Volta, Turing, Ampere desktop; Ampere embedded) using five particle distributions generated by a stochastic emitter model with controllable clustering coefficient. For uniform distributions, 128 threads per block is consistently near-optimal on all tested architectures. For highly clustered distributions (clustering coefficient above 0.6), 64 threads reduces warp divergence enough to outperform 128 threads by up to 19 % on the Ampere desktop device. A simple compile-time heuristic based on the expected clustering coefficient is proposed and validated against the sweep results, achieving within 7 % of the optimal block size in 91 % of tested configurations.

title: Temporal Upsampling of Sparse Particle Updates for Power-Constrained Embedded Targets
abstract: Running a full particle simulation step every frame is infeasible on low-power embedded GPUs when particle counts exceed device-specific thresholds. This paper investigates temporal upsampling: running the full simulation step every k frames and interpolating or extrapolating particle positions in between. Linear interpolation, velocity-field-guided advection, and a lightweight learned residual corrector (a 3-layer MLP with 4 k parameters) are compared at k = 2 and k = 4. At k = 2, velocity-field-guided advection keeps per-particle position error below 1.1 % of mean inter-particle spacing for fluid-like distributions. At k = 4, the learned corrector reduces position error by 44 % relative to linear interpolation. Tests run on a Rockchip RK3588 target at 120 k particles. The paper also characterises the visual artefacts introduced at each k level using a small perceptual study (n=18) to establish acceptable k bounds for different emitter types.

title: Comparative evaluation of feature descriptors for outdoor point cloud classification: FPFH, SHOT, and learned local features
abstract: Classical handcrafted feature descriptors and early learned representations are compared on a benchmark comprising five outdoor scenes captured with a Velodyne HDL-64E mobile scanner in Novi Sad and Subotica. The dataset contains roughly 4.5 million labelled points across eight semantic classes including ground, building, vegetation, vehicle, and street furniture. Fast Point Feature Histograms (FPFH) and Signature of Histograms of Orientations (SHOT) are evaluated alongside a shallow PointNet-style encoder trained from scratch. Mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) scores are 51.4% for FPFH with a random forest classifier, 54.9% for SHOT, and 62.8% for the learned encoder, all using identical training and test splits. Error analysis reveals that the building class benefits most from learned features due to heterogeneous surface textures, whereas ground and vegetation classification is robust across all three approaches. The benchmark data and evaluation scripts are released publicly.

title: Semi-Supervised Topic Labelling Using Automatically Harvested Seed Terms from Wikidata
abstract: Automatically labelling latent topics with human-readable names remains largely a post-hoc manual step in most applied projects. This paper proposes a semi-supervised extension of HDP in which seed term sets harvested from Wikidata concept hierarchies are used as soft constraints during Gibbs sampling via a biased urn model. For a given candidate topic label in Wikidata, the ten most specific descendant terms are retrieved and assigned elevated sampling weights in the relevant Dirichlet parameters. The approach is evaluated on a Serbian health-discourse corpus (Facebook groups, 2019–2023, 860,000 posts) using two metrics: label accuracy judged by three domain experts and the fraction of topics for which a satisfactory label is found without manual intervention. With 120 seed concept sets loaded, 71 % of discovered topics receive an acceptable automatic label, compared to 38 % in a keyword-only baseline. Runtime overhead relative to standard HDP is less than 4 % on the tested hardware.

title: Continuity and Rupture in Early Adolescent Self-Narratives During School Transition
abstract: This study examined how 68 pupils aged 11–12 in three primary schools in Novi Sad constructed written self-narratives at four time points across the final primary-school semester and the first secondary-school semester. Participants completed structured diary prompts every three weeks. Narratives were coded for thematic continuity, temporal orientation, and evaluative stance using a scheme adapted from McAdams's narrative identity framework. Results showed that 54% of participants displayed a marked disruption in narrative continuity in the first two months after transition, characterised by increased use of present-tense self-description and reduced reference to past events. Girls showed higher rates of evaluative elaboration than boys at all time points. Cluster analysis identified three dominant narrative adjustment patterns. The findings suggest that narrative discontinuity at transition is normative but unevenly distributed across gender and prior academic achievement groupings.

title: Autobiographical Reasoning in Younger Adolescents: Coding Scheme Development and Reliability Testing
abstract: Autobiographical reasoning — the process by which individuals draw lessons or causal inferences from personal memories — has been studied mainly in adult samples. This methodological paper reports the development and reliability testing of a coding scheme adapted for use with 12–14-year-old Serbian-speaking participants. The scheme distinguishes four levels of autobiographical reasoning: descriptive, causal-personal, comparative, and integrative. Two independent coders applied the scheme to 120 narrative interview excerpts drawn from an archival sample collected in Vojvodina between 2009 and 2011. Inter-rater reliability reached Cohen's κ = 0.77 across all four levels after two rounds of calibration. Item-level analysis identified specific linguistic markers associated with each level. The resulting scheme and its Srpski-language cue glossary are available as supplementary materials. The paper also discusses adaptations required for younger participants relative to existing adult-focused instruments.

title: Self-Authorship as a Pedagogical Concept: Reviewing Its Use in European Educational Research
abstract: Kegan's theory of self-authorship has been applied across higher education contexts in North America but has seen uneven uptake in European educational research and almost none in Serbian-language scholarship at the secondary level. This review systematically examined 47 peer-reviewed articles published in European educational journals between 2000 and 2013 that invoked self-authorship as a theoretical or analytical construct. Articles were coded for age group, institutional level, methodological approach, and fidelity to the original theory. Findings reveal that 36 of the 47 studies concerned university students, leaving the 11–18 age range substantially underexamined. Methodological approaches were predominantly qualitative interview studies. The review proposes a modified framework applicable to secondary-school contexts and outlines three research gaps relevant to Central and South-East European educational settings, including attention to collectivist family structures and post-socialist schooling traditions.

title: Memory Specificity and Identity Coherence Among Adolescents Navigating Social Disruption
abstract: The study tested whether individual differences in autobiographical memory specificity predicted rated identity coherence in a sample of 94 adolescents (aged 13–15) attending secondary schools in Novi Sad. Memory specificity was measured using a Serbian adaptation of the Autobiographical Memory Test, in which participants generated memories in response to 18 cue words. Identity coherence was assessed through a structured narrative interview rated on a five-point coherence scale. Regression analysis, controlling for verbal fluency and academic performance, showed that memory specificity scores explained 14% of variance in identity coherence ratings (β = 0.38, p < .001). Adolescents classified as having experienced a significant family disruption (parental separation, relocation) in the preceding two years showed lower specificity scores on average. The discussion considers implications for school counsellors working with pupils after disruptive life events.

title: Telling the School Story: Narrative Constructions of Belonging in the First Year of Secondary School
abstract: Using semi-structured narrative interviews administered three times across the first academic year of secondary school, this study explored how 41 pupils aged 14–15 in two gymnasiums in the Vojvodina region described experiences of belonging and exclusion. Interviews were transcribed and subjected to holistic content analysis. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling to ensure variation in prior academic achievement and school type. Three master narratives emerged from the data: the 'competent survivor' narrative, the 'social outsider seeking entry' narrative, and the 'continuation' narrative in which secondary school was framed as unproblematically continuous with primary school experience. The study found that 'competent survivor' narratives were more common among pupils from lower socioeconomic backgrounds, while 'continuation' narratives appeared more frequently in narratives produced by pupils transitioning to schools attended by older siblings. Implications for guidance counsellors are discussed.

title: Narrative Identity Formation in Adolescence
abstract: This book chapter provides a synthetic account of theoretical frameworks and empirical findings on narrative identity formation during adolescence, written for an edited volume on developmental pedagogy in South-East Europe. The chapter traces the transition from early accounts rooted in Eriksonian identity theory to more recent narrative approaches associated with McAdams and Habermas. It then summarises methodological approaches used in the region, including interview-based, diary-based, and mixed methods designs. A section on implications for school pedagogy discusses how educators can create structured opportunities for narrative self-reflection without producing performative or coerced self-disclosure. The chapter draws on original data from two studies conducted in Serbian secondary schools to illustrate theoretical points. It is intended for postgraduate students and practising educators rather than specialist researchers.

title: How Adolescents Narrate Academic Failure: Self-Concept Threat and Repair in Written Accounts
abstract: This study investigated the narrative strategies used by adolescents to account for academic failure events — receiving a failing grade, being held back, or experiencing a significant drop in assessed performance — within school transition periods. Sixty-one students aged 13–16 from four secondary schools in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin wrote narrative accounts of a recent academic setback as part of a classroom-based protocol. Accounts were coded for four repair strategies: externalisation, reframing, minimisation, and acceptance-and-growth. Externalisation was the most frequently used strategy (present in 61% of accounts), while acceptance-and-growth was the least frequent (18%). Students who had experienced the failure event more than six months before writing showed higher rates of reframing compared to those writing within one month of the event. Gender and school type did not significantly differentiate strategy use. Implications for how teachers frame feedback on academic performance are considered.

title: Using Structured Diary Protocols in Classroom Settings: Practical and Ethical Considerations
abstract: Diary-based methods offer rich longitudinal data on identity development but present specific challenges when administered within school contexts, including issues of voluntary participation, confidentiality within institutions, and the boundary between research and pastoral intervention. This paper draws on experience from four studies conducted in Serbian secondary schools between 2012 and 2021, involving a total of 247 participants, to outline practical procedures and ethical decision points researchers and school-based practitioners encounter. Topics addressed include informed assent procedures for minors, protocols for handling disclosures of distress within diary entries, storage and anonymisation of handwritten materials, and managing participant attrition over multi-month protocols. The paper presents a decision-tree instrument for researchers and school counsellors planning diary-based data collection in educational settings. It is intended as a practical methodological resource rather than a primary empirical report.

title: Memory Integration and Identity Distress in Adolescents After Residential Relocation
abstract: Residential relocation in early adolescence disrupts the spatial and social contexts that anchor autobiographical memory, potentially creating difficulties in maintaining a coherent life narrative. This study compared 38 adolescents aged 12–15 who had relocated between municipalities within the past 18 months with a matched comparison group of 40 non-relocated peers. Both groups completed a narrative interview and the adolescent version of the Identity Distress Survey. Relocated participants scored significantly higher on identity distress (M = 24.3 vs. 19.7, t(76) = 3.21, p = .002) and produced narratives rated lower in overall coherence and higher in temporal disorientation. However, the relationship between relocation and distress was substantially moderated by narrative integration ability: relocated participants who demonstrated high autobiographical reasoning capacity showed identity distress scores comparable to non-relocated peers. School counselling implications are discussed, including suggestions for structured narrative exercises in the first months after enrolment.

title: Narrative Self-Concept Across the Transition Year: What Diary Data Add to Survey Measures
abstract: Surveys remain the dominant method for assessing self-concept in school-based research, but they capture only cross-sectional snapshots of a construct that unfolds over time. This study compared data from a standardised self-concept questionnaire (administered at three time points) with longitudinal diary data collected from the same 49 participants aged 11–13 over their transition year. Discrepancy analyses examined the degree to which diary-derived narrative self-descriptions aligned with, diverged from, or complicated survey profiles. In 31% of cases, diary data revealed identity themes not captured by any questionnaire subscale, particularly themes related to peer reputation and moral self-evaluation. Survey scores showed higher stability over time than narrative indicators, but narrative indicators were more sensitive to event-specific change. The paper argues for complementary use of both data types in school-transition research and discusses practical constraints on mixed-methods data collection in school settings.

title: Structuring Learning Objectives for Adult Technical Education: A Taxonomy-Based Approach in Serbian Vocational Programmes
abstract: This paper examines the applicability of a revised Bloom taxonomy framework to vocational training programmes in the metalworking and electrical installation sectors in Serbia. The study involved 14 accredited vocational training centres and a sample of 312 adult learners aged 22–51. Curriculum documents were coded against six cognitive levels, and trainer interviews (n=28) were conducted to evaluate alignment between stated objectives and actual instructional activities. Results showed that 61% of stated objectives clustered at the two lowest cognitive levels, with minimal representation of analysis or synthesis tasks. A restructured objective template was piloted in three centres over one semester, yielding statistically significant improvements in post-training competency scores (p<0.05) compared to control groups. The paper proposes a practical checklist for objective reformulation that can be integrated into existing accreditation workflows without additional administrative burden.

title: Polytechnic Education and the Worker-Citizen Ideal: Curriculum Documents from SR Serbia, 1958–1974
abstract: This study examines the construction of the polytechnic curriculum ideal in socialist Serbia through close reading of 47 official curriculum documents, party directives, and pedagogical journals held in the Archive of Vojvodina and the Archive of Serbia. The analysis identifies three successive interpretive frames—Marxist productivism, Yugoslav self-management theory, and pragmatic vocational adaptation—each of which reshaped the relationship between general schooling and productive labour. Particular attention is given to how pedagogical theorists at Belgrade and Novi Sad universities mediated Soviet Makarenko-influenced models against distinctly Yugoslav doctrinal demands following the Tito–Stalin split. The paper shows that the polytechnic ideal was never internally consistent but was held together by a procedural consensus among curriculum committees. A quantitative content analysis of recurrent normative terms across the document corpus tracks shifts in emphasis decade by decade. The findings complicate retrospective accounts that treat Yugoslav socialist education as a uniform ideological project.

title: Fairness Judgments in Three-Year-Olds During Free Play: A Preliminary Observational Study
abstract: This study examined spontaneous fairness-related utterances and actions in a sample of 24 children aged 36–42 months at two preschool institutions in Novi Sad. Over eight weeks, researchers conducted unstructured observations totaling approximately 96 hours of video-recorded free play, coding incidents involving object sharing, turn-taking disputes, and verbal appeals to fairness norms. A total of 312 codable incidents were identified. Results indicated that children at this age produced recognizable fairness-based objections in roughly 38% of observed disputes, most frequently in dyadic rather than group interactions. Appeals to adult authority accompanied only 21% of incidents, suggesting emerging peer-level norm enforcement. The findings support the view that rudimentary fairness reasoning appears before age four and is expressed primarily in the context of resource competition rather than harm. Limitations include the single-site nature of two of the observation classrooms and possible observer effects during the early recording sessions.

title: The Role of Emotional Vocabulary in Children's Justifications During Moral Dilemma Tasks
abstract: Forty-two children aged five to six completed a dilemma story battery and their verbal justifications were transcribed and coded both for moral reasoning level and for the presence of emotion-related words. Emotion vocabulary was also assessed independently using a standardised picture-labelling task administered separately. Children with higher emotion vocabulary scores produced justifications containing more emotional content (r = 0.48, p < .001) and scored higher on moral reasoning level (r = 0.39, p = .010). Regression analysis indicated that emotion vocabulary predicted reasoning level above and beyond age and verbal ability as measured by a receptive vocabulary task, accounting for an additional 8% of variance. Qualitative analysis of selected transcripts illustrates how children used emotional attribution to construct arguments about the protagonist's inner states and obligations. The findings suggest that emotion language development and moral reasoning development are closely intertwined in this age range, with implications for how dilemma tasks are scored.

title: Concurrent use of ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics in elderly women: frequency and clinical consequences of hyperkalaemia episodes
abstract: Combining ACE inhibitors with potassium-sparing diuretics elevates hyperkalaemia risk, but whether this risk differs by sex in older patients is underexplored. We performed a retrospective cohort study using pharmacy dispensing records and laboratory data from three primary care centres in Novi Sad covering 2008–2012. The cohort comprised 504 patients aged 65–85 (54% women) on stable dual therapy for at least six months. Hyperkalaemia episodes (serum K⁺ ≥5.5 mmol/L) were identified from routine biochemistry results. Incidence in women was 18.3 per 100 person-years compared with 11.7 in men (adjusted HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.11–2.16), after controlling for renal function, diabetes, and dietary assessment scores. Women also had longer mean time to potassium normalisation (9.4 vs 6.8 days). The disparity was most pronounced in the 75–85 age subgroup. Sex-based prescribing caution and more frequent laboratory monitoring appear warranted for this drug combination in older women.

title: Beta-blocker tolerability in elderly women with isolated systolic hypertension: comparison of metoprolol and bisoprolol in routine clinical practice
abstract: Isolated systolic hypertension is prevalent in older women yet tolerability data for specific beta-blockers in this subpopulation are limited. This observational study followed 228 female patients aged ≥70 diagnosed with isolated systolic hypertension attending two Novi Sad cardiology outpatient units between 2013 and 2015. Patients were divided into those initiated on metoprolol succinate (n=114) or bisoprolol (n=114) by their treating physician; allocation was not randomised. Primary endpoints were treatment discontinuation due to adverse effects and frequency of bradycardia, fatigue, and cold extremity complaints over 12 months. Discontinuation rates were 19.3% for metoprolol and 12.3% for bisoprolol (p=0.12). Fatigue was reported significantly more often in the metoprolol group at six months (34% vs 21%, p=0.03). Bradycardia incidence did not differ between groups. Regression analysis identified baseline heart rate and creatinine clearance as stronger predictors of tolerability than drug choice. The results do not support strong preference of one agent over the other on tolerability grounds alone.

title: Drug–drug interaction potential in antihypertensive polypharmacy regimens: sex-stratified assessment using an interaction severity scoring tool
abstract: We adapted a published drug–drug interaction severity scoring algorithm to retrospectively evaluate prescriptions from 680 hypertensive patients aged 65–89 attending primary care in South Bačka District during 2015–2016. Prescriptions were extracted from electronic medical records; each unique drug pair was scored for interaction potential using a locally validated four-tier severity scale (negligible, minor, moderate, severe). Women comprised 59% of the sample. The mean number of antihypertensive agents per patient was 2.8 (SD 0.9), with women prescribed slightly more agents on average (2.9 vs 2.7, p=0.04). Severe interaction pairs were identified in 8.4% of female prescriptions and 5.6% of male prescriptions (p=0.03). The most common severe pair was verapamil combined with a beta-blocker, appearing in 31 cases. Moderate interactions involving ACE inhibitor–NSAID combinations were more prevalent in women (14.2% vs 9.8%), possibly reflecting higher NSAID use for comorbid osteoarthritis. Prescriber awareness campaigns focused on sex-specific comorbidity patterns may reduce preventable interactions.

title: Differences in adverse reaction reporting between male and female elderly patients on triple antihypertensive therapy: findings from a prospective cohort
abstract: Triple antihypertensive therapy—typically combining an ACE inhibitor or ARB, a calcium channel blocker, and a thiazide diuretic—is increasingly common in resistant hypertension, yet sex-disaggregated prospective safety data from southeastern European populations are scarce. We recruited 189 patients (≥65 years) newly initiated on triple therapy at the Hypertension Outpatient Unit, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, between January 2016 and June 2018. Follow-up visits occurred at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Structured adverse event interviews and laboratory panels were conducted at each visit. Women (n=112) reported a higher total adverse event burden at every time point. At 12 months, the mean number of adverse events per patient was 3.1 in women versus 2.2 in men (p=0.007). Symptomatic hypotension, peripheral oedema, and dry cough were the most common events and each showed female preponderance. Blood pressure control at 12 months did not significantly differ by sex. Renal function deterioration occurred in seven patients, all women, though numbers were too small for statistical inference. Longer follow-up and larger samples are needed to quantify renal risk.

title: Influence of renal function decline on adverse drug reaction risk in elderly women receiving antihypertensive polypharmacy: a longitudinal analysis
abstract: Renal function declines with age and may amplify adverse drug reaction (ADR) risk in patients on multiple antihypertensives, but the interaction between sex and renal function in this context has not been systematically quantified. We analysed longitudinal laboratory and clinical data from 310 women aged 65–85 enrolled in a Vojvodina-based hypertension registry between 2017 and 2021. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was calculated at baseline and annually. Patients were categorised into stable renal function (eGFR decline <3 mL/min/1.73 m² per year) and progressive decline groups. ADRs were identified through structured physician interviews and laboratory flags. The progressive decline group (n=98) had a significantly higher ADR incidence rate (5.8 vs 3.3 events per 100 person-months, adjusted IRR 1.71, 95% CI 1.28–2.28). Hyperkalaemia, worsening oedema, and symptomatic hypotension dominated the excess events. Time-varying eGFR was a stronger predictor of ADR incidence than baseline eGFR alone. These data suggest that dynamic renal monitoring, rather than a single baseline assessment, should guide dosing decisions in older women on polypharmacy.

title: Sex-disaggregated spontaneous reporting data for antihypertensive drugs in Serbia: ten-year trends and signal detection
abstract: Spontaneous reporting systems generate valuable real-world drug safety signals, but data are rarely stratified by sex before publication. We obtained the full national dataset of antihypertensive-related adverse drug reaction reports submitted in Serbia between 2012 and 2022, comprising 3,214 records after quality filtering. Reports were coded using MedDRA preferred terms and grouped by drug class, patient sex, and age band. Female patients accounted for 66% of all reports and this proportion increased over the decade. Disproportionality analysis using the reporting odds ratio detected significant female-predominant signals for: dry cough with ACE inhibitors (ROR 2.44), angioedema with ACE inhibitors (ROR 1.88), peripheral oedema with calcium channel blockers (ROR 1.73), and bradycardia with beta-blockers (ROR 1.39). Male-predominant signals were limited to sexual dysfunction with beta-blockers and thiazide diuretics. Temporal trends showed increasing reporting completeness for sex and age data after 2017, coinciding with a national pharmacovigilance training programme. Signal stability across sub-periods was confirmed by resampling. Results provide a baseline for future sex-specific regulatory risk communications.

title: Patient-reported outcome measures in antihypertensive polypharmacy studies involving older adults: a methodological review and recommendations for sex-stratified analysis
abstract: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) are increasingly used in drug safety research, but their application in geriatric antihypertensive polypharmacy studies is methodologically inconsistent, and sex-stratified reporting remains infrequent. We searched five databases for studies published between 2000 and 2023 that used PROMs to capture adverse drug reactions or treatment tolerability in patients aged ≥65 receiving two or more antihypertensive agents. Forty-three studies met inclusion criteria. Only 18 (42%) reported results separately by sex, and of these, only 7 used sex as a pre-specified stratification variable rather than a post hoc subgroup. The most widely used instruments were the Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire for Medication and a modified Morisky Adherence Scale; neither has been validated specifically for elderly polypharmacy contexts. Sample sizes in stratified analyses were frequently underpowered. Based on these findings, we propose a minimum reporting standard for sex-stratified PROM data in this field, including guidance on sample size calculation and instrument selection. The recommendations are intended for use by clinical researchers and trial sponsors.
venue: Clinical Pharmacology Methods and Practice
