title: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling of empagliflozin absorption under conditions of delayed gastric emptying
abstract: Empagliflozin, an SGLT2 inhibitor, is rapidly absorbed from the upper small intestine. Delayed gastric emptying in patients with type 2 diabetes and gastroparesis may shift its absorption profile and affect the early renal glucose-lowering effect. A physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model was constructed in PK-Sim version 9 using published physicochemical parameters, human intestinal permeability data, and regional intestinal expression data for UGT1A3 and P-gp. Simulated gastric half-emptying times were varied from 45 min (normal) to 240 min (severe gastroparesis) in a virtual population of 500 type 2 diabetic patients. Under severe gastroparesis, predicted tmax shifted from 1.5 h to 4.1 h, Cmax fell by 38%, and AUC0–6 h decreased by 29% relative to normal motility, whereas AUC0–24 h was essentially unchanged (−4%). Sensitivity analysis identified gastric emptying rate and jejunal permeability as the two parameters contributing most to absorption variability. The model was qualified against three published clinical datasets; predicted Cmax fell within 1.25-fold of observed means in all three. These findings support the hypothesis that early post-prandial glucose control with empagliflozin may be attenuated in gastroparetic patients.

title: Job Demands, Personal Resources and Exhaustion Among Secondary School Teachers in Serbia: A Cross-Sectional Survey
abstract: Using the job demands–resources (JD-R) model as a theoretical framework, this cross-sectional study examined predictors of emotional exhaustion in a sample of 428 secondary school teachers across four Serbian cities. Participants completed measures of quantitative workload, role ambiguity, colleague support, self-efficacy, and the exhaustion subscale of the MBI-GS. Hierarchical multiple regression indicated that quantitative workload (β = 0.38, p < .001) and role ambiguity (β = 0.22, p < .001) were the strongest demand predictors of exhaustion, together explaining 31% of variance. Self-efficacy moderated the relationship between workload and exhaustion (ΔR² = 0.03, p = .018), such that the positive association was attenuated for teachers with higher self-efficacy scores. Colleague support showed a direct negative effect on exhaustion (β = −0.17, p = .004) but did not interact significantly with demands. Findings are discussed in relation to practical implications for school-level intervention design and teacher wellbeing policy in Serbia.

title: Construct Validity of the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale in Serbian Healthcare Workers
abstract: The Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-17 and UWES-9) was examined for structural validity and measurement invariance across gender in a sample of 516 healthcare workers employed at three general hospitals in Vojvodina. Competing factor structures (one-factor, three-factor, bifactor) were tested using confirmatory factor analysis in Mplus. The bifactor model with a general engagement factor and three specific factors (vigour, dedication, absorption) showed best fit (CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.057), though model-based reliability estimates indicated that the specific factors contributed limited unique variance beyond the general factor. Multigroup CFA supported configural and metric invariance by gender but partial scalar invariance, with two dedication items showing differential intercepts. Correlations with job satisfaction (r = 0.49) and organisational commitment (r = 0.41) supported convergent validity. Practical implications for the use of engagement subscale scores versus composite scores in Serbian healthcare settings are discussed.

title: Psychometric Properties of the Organisational Climate Measure (OCM) in Serbian Companies: A Multi-Sample Replication
abstract: This paper reports the Serbian adaptation of the Organisational Climate Measure (OCM) developed by Patterson and colleagues. Data were collected from employees in three sectors—manufacturing (n = 203), information technology (n = 187), and public administration (n = 224)—totalling 614 participants. Exploratory structural equation modelling was used to examine the factor structure, followed by confirmatory analysis in the replication samples. Results supported a reduced 14-factor solution after dropping items with high cross-loadings and low communalities (final pool = 56 items from the original 82). Internal consistencies for retained subscales ranged from α = 0.71 to 0.90. Cross-sector measurement invariance was largely supported at the metric level, though two subscales (formalisation, tradition) showed non-invariant loadings in the public administration sample. Normative data stratified by sector and company size are provided. The adapted OCM-SR is made freely available for non-commercial research.

title: Short Measures of Burnout for Organisational Surveys: Comparing the OLBI, MBI-GS Short Form and Single-Item Approaches
abstract: Organisations frequently request brief wellbeing screening tools that minimise respondent burden. This study compared the Oldenburg Burnout Inventory (OLBI), the six-item MBI-GS Short Form, and two single-item exhaustion indicators in a sample of 389 white-collar employees from companies in Novi Sad and Subotica. Criterion validity was evaluated against the full MBI-GS and the Shirom-Melamed Burnout Measure. Convergent correlations for the OLBI exhaustion subscale (r = 0.79) and MBI-GS Short Form exhaustion scale (r = 0.84) with the full MBI-GS exhaustion subscale were both high; single-item indicators showed acceptable convergent validity (r = 0.68–0.72) but missed a meaningful proportion of respondents classified as high risk by full scales. Disengagement (OLBI) and cynicism (MBI-GS Short Form) subscales correlated moderately (r = 0.61). Classification agreement tables and ROC analyses are reported. The OLBI is recommended for short surveys requiring both burnout dimensions; the MBI-GS Short Form suits contexts where continuity with MBI-GS norms is required.

title: Remote Work, Boundary Management and Psychological Detachment During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Longitudinal Study in Serbian Knowledge Workers
abstract: This three-wave longitudinal study (T1: April 2020, T2: October 2020, T3: April 2021) tracked 241 knowledge workers who transitioned to full-time remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia. Variables included work–home boundary management style, psychological detachment from work during off-time, exhaustion, and work engagement. Latent growth curve modelling revealed that exhaustion increased from T1 to T2 and partially recovered by T3, while engagement trajectories were flat on average but showed substantial individual variability. Boundary management style (preference for segmentation vs. integration) moderated exhaustion trajectories: integrators showed steeper initial increases in exhaustion (B = 0.29, p = .011) than segmenters. Psychological detachment declined across all three waves, particularly among employees with children under 12 at home. Cross-lagged paths from T1 boundary management to T2 exhaustion remained significant after controlling for T1 exhaustion. Results are discussed in relation to boundary theory and practical recommendations for remote work policy.

title: Factorial Invariance of Burnout Measures Across Occupational Groups: A Meta-Analytic Structural Equation Modelling Approach
abstract: Burnout research frequently aggregates findings across occupational groups, implicitly assuming that burnout scales function equivalently across contexts. This paper applies meta-analytic structural equation modelling (MASEM) to correlation matrices extracted from 48 published studies (total N = 24 317) reporting MBI or MBI-GS data across at least two distinct occupational groups. Pooled correlation matrices were compared using TSSEM in R. Results indicated that the three-factor structure replicated consistently across groups, but factor loadings for cynicism/depersonalisation items showed greater variability across non-human-services occupations. Strict factorial invariance was not supported in models comparing human-services workers with non-human-services workers, though metric invariance held. Latent mean comparisons uncorrected for partial non-invariance overestimated occupational group differences in cynicism by approximately 0.15 standard deviation units. Recommendations are offered for reporting practices in cross-occupational burnout research and for the interpretation of normative data.

title: Wellbeing Survey Design for Small and Medium Enterprises: Methodological Challenges and Practical Recommendations
abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) face specific constraints when implementing employee wellbeing surveys, including small sample sizes that limit psychometric analyses, concerns about employee anonymity, and limited internal HR research capacity. This chapter reviews methodological challenges in adapting validated occupational health instruments for SME contexts, drawing on the authors' experiences conducting surveys in 17 Serbian SMEs between 2017 and 2023 (total N = 1 124 employees). Topics covered include sample size planning for confirmatory factor analysis with fewer than 100 respondents, the use of short-form instruments, procedures for protecting anonymity in small teams, and communication of results to management without compromising individual confidentiality. A practical checklist is provided for researchers and HR professionals designing wellbeing monitoring systems in companies with 10–250 employees. Worked examples illustrate common pitfalls and their solutions using data from manufacturing and service-sector SMEs.

title: Psychometric Evaluation of the Job Crafting Scale in Serbian White-Collar Workers and Its Relationship with Engagement Trajectories
abstract: Job crafting—the proactive modification of task, relational, and cognitive boundaries of work—has attracted growing research attention, but validated Serbian instruments are lacking. This preprint reports the translation and confirmatory psychometric evaluation of Tims and colleagues' 21-item Job Crafting Scale in a sample of 344 white-collar employees in Vojvodina, recruited through LinkedIn and company HR contacts. The hypothesised four-factor structure (increasing structural resources, increasing social resources, increasing challenging demands, decreasing hindering demands) showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.91, RMSEA = 0.067) after the removal of three items with cross-loadings exceeding 0.35. Convergent validity was supported through correlations with proactive personality (r = 0.44) and work engagement (r = 0.38). A two-wave follow-up subsample (n = 118, 3-month interval) showed that increasing challenging demands at T1 predicted engagement growth (B = 0.19, p = .031), while decreasing hindering demands did not. Full data and analysis code are deposited in the Open Science Framework repository.

title: Designing behaviour change messages for older adults: font size, colour contrast and comprehension of cardiovascular risk information
abstract: Health information materials for older adults often fail to account for age-related perceptual and cognitive changes. This study assessed how systematic variation in font size (12 pt vs. 16 pt) and colour contrast ratio (4.5:1 vs. 7:1, per WCAG 2.1 AA and AAA standards) affected comprehension of a cardiovascular risk leaflet among adults aged 60–80 (N = 96, recruited from a Novi Sad community health centre). Comprehension was measured with a 10-item recall and inference test administered immediately after reading. Eye-tracking (Tobii TX300) recorded fixation duration and re-reading behaviour. Participants reading 16 pt text with 7:1 contrast achieved significantly higher comprehension scores (M = 7.8/10) than those reading 12 pt/4.5:1 text (M = 5.9/10; p < .001, d = 0.88). Re-reading rates were 34% lower in the high-legibility condition. These data provide a concrete evidence base for formatting standards in Serbian primary prevention materials targeting older adults.

title: Applying Fuzzy AHP to Supplier Evaluation in a Serbian Automotive Component Manufacturer: A Case Study
abstract: This paper presents the application of fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) to the supplier evaluation problem at a mid-sized automotive component manufacturer based in Vojvodina. Fourteen suppliers were assessed across seven criteria including delivery reliability, unit cost, quality rejection rate, and financial stability. Linguistic judgements from a panel of five purchasing managers were aggregated using triangular fuzzy numbers, and consistency was checked via the fuzzy consistency ratio. Results identified three suppliers rated significantly higher than the remaining eleven, with delivery reliability and quality rejection rate receiving the highest aggregate weights (0.28 and 0.24, respectively). Sensitivity analysis showed that the top-ranked supplier retained its position under all tested weight perturbations of ±20%. The study demonstrates that FAHP can be operationalised with limited data availability typical of Serbian SME manufacturers, and provides a structured template for purchasing decisions where verbal assessments dominate numerical records.

title: Comparative Analysis of TOPSIS and VIKOR under Fuzzy Environments for Supplier Ranking in Tier-2 Automotive Chains
abstract: The paper compares the outputs of fuzzy TOPSIS and fuzzy VIKOR when applied to the same supplier ranking problem in a tier-2 automotive supply chain operating across Hungary, Serbia, and Romania. A dataset of 22 suppliers and 9 evaluation criteria was constructed from procurement records and supplemented by expert elicitation. Both methods used trapezoidal fuzzy numbers to represent imprecise performance scores. The two methods agreed on the top two and bottom three suppliers but diverged substantially for middle-ranked alternatives. Spearman rank correlation between full TOPSIS and VIKOR orderings was 0.71. Sensitivity tests showed that VIKOR rankings were more sensitive to the weight assigned to the group utility parameter v. The paper recommends running both methods in parallel and treating divergent middle-rank cases as candidates for further due-diligence rather than automated exclusion. Practical guidance is offered for purchasing teams with limited quantitative modelling experience.

title: Scenario Construction for Supply Chain Disruption Risk in the Automotive Sector: A Delphi-Based Approach
abstract: This study uses a structured Delphi process to build a set of disruption scenarios applicable to Central and Eastern European automotive supply chains. Forty-one experts from procurement, logistics, and risk management at eleven companies participated across three Delphi rounds. The process produced nine distinct disruption scenarios covering geopolitical border restrictions, port congestion, single-source component shortages, currency volatility, and regulatory change. Each scenario is described by an estimated probability range and a severity index calibrated against historical disruption events from 2000 to 2011. The paper discusses the challenges of reaching consensus in heterogeneous expert panels and proposes a partial consensus criterion (agreement among at least 65% of respondents) to resolve persistent disagreements. The resulting scenario set is intended as a reusable input library for simulation-based supply chain resilience assessments in the region. A cross-validation exercise comparing expert probability estimates with actuarial data from a regional trade insurer found reasonable alignment for five of the nine scenarios.

title: Measuring Single-Source Dependency Risk in Automotive Supply Networks Using Network Centrality Metrics
abstract: The paper proposes a quantitative framework for identifying and measuring single-source dependency risk in multi-tier automotive supply networks. Using supply network maps reconstructed from bill-of-materials and procurement records of three Vojvodina-based Tier-1 suppliers, the study applies betweenness centrality, degree centrality, and an adapted supplier criticality index to a network of 148 nodes and 214 directed edges. Results show that 11 Tier-2 nodes accounted for more than 60% of aggregate betweenness centrality, with four nodes having no identified alternative source. Removing the single highest-centrality node from the simulated network increased average path length by 34% and disconnected 17 downstream nodes. The framework is implemented in Python using the NetworkX library and takes procurement data formatted as an adjacency list as input. The paper also discusses practical barriers to obtaining full network visibility in industrial settings, including data confidentiality and supplier reluctance to disclose their own supply base.

title: Integrating Geopolitical Risk Scores into Multi-Criteria Supplier Selection: A Weighted Fuzzy TOPSIS Model
abstract: This paper extends the standard fuzzy TOPSIS framework by incorporating geopolitical risk scores as an additional criterion in supplier selection. Geopolitical risk is operationalised using a composite index assembled from three publicly available country-risk databases, normalised to a 0–10 scale and fuzzified into triangular fuzzy numbers. The extended model is applied to a selection problem involving 18 potential suppliers for an electronic control unit subcomponent sourced across seven countries. Compared to a baseline fuzzy TOPSIS model without the geopolitical criterion, the ranking of the top-five suppliers changed substantially: two suppliers from high-risk jurisdictions dropped by four and six positions respectively. A weight sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the geopolitical criterion begins to dominate the overall ranking when its assigned weight exceeds 0.30, which the paper argues is unrealistically high for most procurement contexts. The paper proposes a calibration procedure to set the geopolitical weight based on the firm's strategic exposure and contractual hedging capacity.

title: Supply Chain Resilience Metrics: A Structured Review and Classification for Manufacturing Industries
abstract: This chapter reviews and classifies quantitative resilience metrics proposed in the supply chain literature between 2000 and 2016. Starting from a corpus of 214 papers identified through systematic database search, 47 papers were retained after full-text screening based on applicability to manufacturing supply chains and presence of empirical or simulation-based validation. Metrics are grouped into four categories: recovery speed indicators, network redundancy measures, adaptive capacity proxies, and financial impact indices. The chapter highlights that recovery speed indicators dominate the literature (23 of 47 papers), while adaptive capacity measures remain the least developed category with significant definitional inconsistency across studies. A mapping exercise shows partial overlap and occasional contradictions between metrics used in academic research and those reported by industry practitioners in procurement surveys. The chapter concludes with a proposed minimum reporting standard for empirical resilience studies and identifies three measurement gaps requiring further methodological attention.

title: Agent-Based Simulation of Disruption Propagation in a Tier-2 Automotive Supply Network under Border Closure Scenarios
abstract: The study uses agent-based simulation implemented in AnyLogic to model disruption propagation through a reconstructed Tier-2 automotive supply network following a hypothetical 14-day border closure between two Central European countries. The modelled network comprises 94 supplier agents and 6 assembler agents linked by 138 directed material flow edges. Each supplier agent is parameterised with empirical inventory holding data, lead times, and alternative sourcing probabilities derived from procurement records. Three closure scenarios are simulated: full closure, partial closure with 40% throughput restriction, and closure with emergency rerouting via a third-country corridor. Simulation runs (500 replications per scenario) show that full closure causes production stoppages at 4 of 6 assembler agents within 9 days; partial closure causes stoppages at 2 assemblers within 18 days; emergency rerouting delays stoppage onset by 11 days on average but increases logistics cost by 23%. The paper discusses the sensitivity of results to inventory parameter assumptions and the limitations of reconstructing network topology from incomplete procurement data.

title: Fuzzy TOPSIS with Interval-Valued Weights for Supplier Selection under Simultaneous Cost and Resilience Objectives
abstract: This paper addresses the supplier selection problem when decision-makers cannot agree on precise criteria weights, using interval-valued weight vectors within a fuzzy TOPSIS framework. The approach assigns each criterion a weight interval rather than a point value, derived from the range of expert opinions collected during two rounds of structured interviews with eight procurement managers at automotive companies in Serbia and Hungary. Seventeen candidate suppliers for a hydraulic sealing component are evaluated across eight criteria including unit price, lead time variability, financial health, geographic concentration risk, and quality certification level. The interval-weight model yields a set of non-dominated suppliers rather than a single ranked list, accommodating genuine disagreement about cost–resilience trade-offs. In the case study, the non-dominated set contains four suppliers, compared to a single top-ranked supplier produced by a standard point-weight fuzzy TOPSIS run. The paper argues that presenting procurement teams with a small non-dominated set is practically more honest than a precise ranking when weight uncertainty is substantial.

title: Assessing Supply Chain Exposure to Geopolitical Disruption: Evidence from Automotive Tier-2 Suppliers in the Western Balkans
abstract: Using a structured survey administered to 63 procurement and logistics managers at automotive Tier-2 suppliers operating in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, this paper quantifies the frequency, duration, and cost impact of supply disruptions attributable to geopolitical events between 2015 and 2021. Respondents reported 187 disruption episodes in total; 41% were attributed primarily to geopolitical factors including trade restrictions, customs delays linked to bilateral disputes, and sanctions-related payment complications. Median disruption duration was 8 days (IQR: 3–21 days), and median self-reported cost per episode was €14,000. Suppliers with a higher share of inputs sourced from a single country reported significantly longer disruption durations (Mann-Whitney U test, p = 0.008). The paper also finds that only 22% of respondents had a formal disruption response procedure. Results are used to calibrate a risk exposure index that can serve as an input to scenario-based supply chain simulations for the region.

title: A Combined Fuzzy TOPSIS and Monte Carlo Framework for Evaluating Dual-Sourcing Strategies in Automotive Tier-2 Networks
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage decision support framework that first ranks candidate second sources using fuzzy TOPSIS and then evaluates the financial and resilience impact of adopting the top-ranked alternatives through Monte Carlo simulation. The framework is applied to a case involving a Serbian Tier-1 automotive supplier dependent on a single source for five critical sub-components. Fuzzy TOPSIS ranking is performed over 31 candidate alternative suppliers using ten criteria; the three highest-ranked candidates per component are passed to the simulation stage. The Monte Carlo model (10,000 runs per configuration) estimates expected annual disruption cost, buffer inventory requirements, and service level under each dual-sourcing configuration. Results indicate that adopting dual sourcing for the two highest-criticality components reduces expected annual disruption cost by €87,000 while increasing procurement management cost by an estimated €12,000 per year. The paper provides a worked numerical example and discusses implementation prerequisites including minimum viable information requirements from suppliers.

title: Resilience-Cost Trade-offs in Supplier Portfolio Redesign: A Scenario-Optimisation Approach for Geopolitically Exposed Supply Chains
abstract: The paper formulates supplier portfolio redesign as a bi-objective optimisation problem balancing total procurement cost against a composite resilience score under a set of geopolitical disruption scenarios. The resilience score aggregates three sub-metrics: expected demand coverage in the worst-case scenario, geographic diversification index, and average lead-time buffer. A ε-constraint method is used to generate the Pareto frontier, and fuzzy TOPSIS is applied post-hoc to select a preferred solution given decision-maker preferences. The model is instantiated using data from a Vojvodina-based component manufacturer sourcing 12 categories of inputs from 47 potential suppliers across 9 countries. The Pareto frontier reveals that a 12% increase in procurement cost above the cost-minimising solution yields the largest resilience gain per euro spent, after which the resilience–cost curve flattens considerably. The paper also examines how the shape and position of the Pareto frontier shift under different geopolitical scenario weightings, showing that the frontier is relatively stable for moderate scenario weight changes but shifts significantly when high-severity low-probability scenarios are assigned weights above 0.40.

title: Integrating Political Instability Forecasts into Dynamic Supplier Requalification Processes: A Pilot Study
abstract: This study investigates whether incorporating quarterly political instability forecasts from a country-risk intelligence provider into a dynamic supplier requalification process changes requalification decisions relative to a static annual review. A pilot was conducted with one Tier-1 automotive supplier in Novi Sad over 18 months, monitoring 28 active suppliers across 11 countries. The dynamic model triggered requalification reviews 14 times during the pilot period; 9 reviews resulted in no change of decision, 3 resulted in accelerated qualification of an alternative source, and 2 resulted in strategic inventory increases. A post-hoc comparison with the company's standard annual review showed that 2 of the 3 accelerated qualifications involved suppliers who subsequently experienced confirmed disruptions, while the annual review would not have triggered early action in either case. The paper discusses the operational overhead of more frequent reviews, the cost of subscribing to political risk intelligence services, and the conditions under which the dynamic approach is likely to be cost-beneficial for SME suppliers.
venue: Journal of Supply Chain Analytics and Management

title: Predicting Final Cost Overrun in Fixed-Price Software Contracts: A Regression Analysis Using Early EVM Signals
abstract: Fixed-price contracts expose software vendors to cost overrun risk that is difficult to detect early. This study examines whether earned value signals measured at 20% and 35% of planned project duration are predictive of final cost overrun in fixed-price engagements. A dataset of 67 completed fixed-price projects from four Serbian software companies was assembled, with overrun defined as actual effort exceeding planned effort by more than 10%. Logistic regression and linear regression models were built using CPI, SPI, and the To-Complete Performance Index at the two measurement points as predictors. The logistic model achieved AUC = 0.79 on a stratified hold-out set for predicting the overrun/no-overrun binary outcome. The linear model explained 52% of variance in final overrun magnitude. CPI at 35% was the single strongest predictor in both models. Results suggest that early monitoring intervention triggered at CPI < 0.88 at the 20% milestone could prevent a substantial fraction of severe overruns.

title: Affine Arithmetic Relaxations for Bounding the Parameter Space in a Nonlinear Pharmacokinetic Compartment Model
abstract: Parameter identification in pharmacokinetic models is complicated by measurement noise and the nonlinear coupling between state variables. This paper applies affine arithmetic to construct tight outer enclosures of the feasible parameter set for a two-compartment model describing drug absorption and elimination. The approach replaces standard interval evaluation with affine forms that track linear correlations between quantities, reducing the wrapping effect that causes excessive overestimation in box-based methods. A branch-and-bound procedure is used to enumerate and discard infeasible parameter boxes against a synthetic measurement dataset of 40 time points corrupted by bounded noise of up to 5% relative error. Compared with a pure interval arithmetic implementation on the same problem, the affine arithmetic branch-and-bound required 38% fewer bisections to reduce the enclosure volume below a prescribed tolerance of 10^-4. The method is validated against Monte Carlo sampling with 10^5 particles, confirming that the verified enclosure contains all sample-based estimates. Computational experiments are conducted in MATLAB using a prototype implementation building on the INTLAB library.

title: Comparison of Interval Newton and Krawczyk Operators for Parameter Bounds in a Lorenz-Type System
abstract: The Lorenz-type ordinary differential equation system is widely used as a testbed for nonlinear parameter estimation because its sensitivity to initial conditions and parameter values makes classical gradient-based methods unreliable. This conference paper presents a systematic numerical comparison of the interval Newton operator and the Krawczyk operator for computing guaranteed enclosures of equilibrium-consistent parameter sets in a three-dimensional Lorenz-type system. Six parameter configurations are studied, covering both chaotic and non-chaotic regimes. Integration of the state equations is performed using a validated Runge–Kutta scheme with step-size control based on interval extensions. Results show that the Krawczyk operator converges to tighter boxes in four of the six cases but incurs a 22% higher per-iteration cost due to the matrix–vector product with the interval remainder term. Both operators are embedded within the same branch-and-bound framework, and wall-clock times for achieving a relative box diameter below 10^-3 are reported. The study finds no single operator that dominates across all tested regimes, motivating a hybrid switching strategy for future work.

title: Set-Membership Parameter Estimation for a DC Motor Model Using Interval Constraint Propagation
abstract: This paper investigates set-membership estimation of electrical and mechanical parameters—armature resistance, back-EMF constant, and rotor inertia—in a permanent-magnet DC motor model under bounded output noise. Interval constraint propagation is applied iteratively over a time series of 200 current and angular velocity measurements sampled at 1 kHz from a laboratory motor test rig. The propagation exploits the algebraic structure of the motor equations at each time step to tighten the parameter box without requiring full branch-and-bound enumeration. Four propagation orderings are tested; the ordering that processes torque balance before electrical dynamics yields the smallest final enclosure, with a volume roughly 3.1 times smaller than the initial box. The resulting parameter enclosures are cross-checked against least-squares point estimates obtained from the same dataset, and the verified intervals are found to contain the point estimates in all cases. The work is intended as a first step toward embedding such verified identification within a real-time fault detection scheme for electric drives.

title: Reducing Dependency Effect in Interval Evaluation of Polynomial ODE Right-Hand Sides via Horner Reformulation
abstract: Interval arithmetic evaluation of multivariate polynomials that appear on the right-hand sides of ordinary differential equations suffers from the dependency problem: repeated occurrences of the same variable inflate the width of the resulting interval. This short paper examines how Horner-scheme reformulation of the polynomial right-hand sides reduces this inflation for a class of biochemical reaction network models. Three reformulation strategies—standard Horner, factored Horner, and a greedy term-ordering heuristic—are compared on four benchmark reaction networks from the BioModels repository, with polynomial degrees ranging from two to five and between three and nine state variables. Interval widths after 50 integration steps are recorded for each strategy. The greedy heuristic achieves width reductions of between 12% and 41% relative to naive evaluation, depending on the network, with negligible preprocessing overhead. No single reformulation dominates all networks, and the paper provides a simple criterion based on variable occurrence counts to predict which strategy is likely to perform best for a given right-hand side.

title: Transfer learning from ImageNet to pavement distress classification: which layers to freeze?
abstract: Pre-trained ImageNet weights provide a useful initialisation for pavement distress classifiers, but the appropriate depth at which to stop fine-tuning the source model is not well understood in this application domain. This study systematically freezes all layers up to each of the five convolutional blocks of a standard VGG-16 architecture and records classification accuracy across seven pavement distress categories on a dataset of 11,400 images collected from urban roads in Novi Sad and Subotica. The smallest target-domain training subsets tested contain 200 images per class. A clear interaction between available labelled data and optimal freeze depth emerges: with fewer than 400 images per class, freezing the first three blocks outperforms full fine-tuning by 7.2 percentage points on average. The paper quantifies this relationship and proposes a simple selection heuristic depending on per-class sample count.

title: Automated Reconstruction of Road Topology from Mobile LiDAR Point Clouds Using Projected Intensity Images
abstract: Mobile laser scanning produces dense 3D point clouds from which road-surface markings can be extracted to infer lane boundaries and intersection layout. This paper presents a method that projects point-cloud intensity values onto a locally flat 2D image and applies a sequence of image-processing steps—contrast normalisation, morphological filtering, and skeletonisation—to extract lane marking polylines. The polylines are then assembled into a directed lane graph using a graph-matching heuristic that associates skeleton endpoints within a 0.35-metre proximity threshold. Experiments were conducted on three LiDAR datasets covering approximately 6.8 km of urban road in Novi Sad, collected with a Velodyne HDL-64E scanner mounted on a survey vehicle. Lane boundary detection recall was 0.88 and precision was 0.84. The reconstructed graphs were converted to OpenDRIVE format and loaded into a driving simulator; visual inspection by two domain experts identified no safety-critical topology errors. Processing time was 4.2 minutes per kilometre on a GPU-accelerated workstation.

title: Coordinating Distributed Scanning Agents Under Bandwidth Constraints
abstract: Port and service scanning in large networks is often limited by available bandwidth and the risk of disrupting production traffic. This paper studies the scheduling problem that arises when multiple scanning agents must collectively cover a target address space without exceeding per-link bandwidth thresholds. The problem is formulated as a bin-packing variant with time windows, and a greedy heuristic with backtracking is compared against an integer-programming baseline on instances of 50 to 500 agent-target pairs. The heuristic achieves solutions within 6% of optimal in under two seconds for 500-pair instances. A prototype was integrated into an open-source scanning framework and evaluated on a physical testbed of 80 hosts; no link exceeded 70% of its configured capacity cap during any scanning window. Scan completion times improved by 31% compared to uncoordinated parallel scanning with the same aggregate bandwidth limit.

title: Network partitioning strategies for scalable distributed MPC of large district heating systems
abstract: Centralised MPC for large district heating networks with hundreds of nodes becomes computationally intractable within practical control intervals. This paper investigates three graph-based partitioning strategies—spectral clustering, flow-betweenness decomposition, and community detection via modularity maximisation—for splitting a 94-node synthetic network into sub-problems solvable in parallel. Each partition is controlled by a local stochastic MPC agent; coupling constraints at partition boundaries are handled by a dual-decomposition coordination step. Convergence properties of the coordination algorithm are analysed as a function of partition count and coupling edge density. Simulations over 30 heating days show that a 6-partition configuration recovers 91% of centralised controller performance in terms of cost and constraint satisfaction while reducing per-iteration wall-clock time from 38 seconds to under 8 seconds on a six-core workstation. The paper also discusses failure isolation properties that arise as an operational benefit of the partitioned structure.

title: Formation of Contracts by Software Agents: Offer, Acceptance and the Problem of Intent
abstract: The article investigates whether a binding contract can be formed when both offer and acceptance are generated without contemporaneous human review, as occurs in algorithmic trading and automated procurement platforms. Drawing on Serbian contract law doctrine and the UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts, the author examines three requirements—offer, acceptance, and meeting of minds—and assesses how each is affected when a software agent acts on pre-programmed parameters. The article draws on a comparative survey of German, Austrian, and Dutch scholarly opinion and selected case law. It identifies two interpretive strategies: treating the software agent as a mere instrument of the principal's will, and treating automated execution as a new category of juridical act requiring sui generis rules. The article favours a modified instrument theory subject to an objective reasonableness test, and maps the practical consequences of this choice for dispute resolution under Serbian law.

title: Consumer Protection in Automated Online Contracting: Withdrawal Rights and the Digital Services Directive
abstract: This book chapter analyses the interaction between the EU Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU and automated online contracting platforms as observed in practice across five EU member states (Germany, France, the Netherlands, Romania, and Bulgaria) and two candidate states (Serbia and North Macedonia). The chapter focuses on the right of withdrawal when contract terms are generated or modified by algorithmic pricing engines without explicit consumer awareness. Using a structured comparative method and a dataset of 120 standard-form contracts collected from e-commerce platforms in 2013–2014, the chapter identifies four patterns of potential violation of the pre-contractual information duty. It concludes that the Directive's information requirements are poorly calibrated for algorithmic environments and recommends that the forthcoming Digital Services Directive incorporate explicit disclosure duties regarding automated personalisation of contract terms.

title: Liability Allocation in Algorithmic Credit Scoring: A Private Law Perspective
abstract: Credit scoring algorithms used by Serbian banks and non-bank lenders produce binary or ranked outputs that determine access to credit for individuals and small enterprises. This article examines who bears civil liability when an erroneous algorithmic score leads to financial harm: the software developer, the lender, or the data provider. The analysis applies classical Serbian private law categories—contractual liability, liability for acts of auxiliaries under Article 170 of the Law on Obligations, and product liability principles—to a constructed set of twelve hypothetical scenarios drawn from anonymised complaints filed with the National Bank of Serbia between 2014 and 2016. The article finds that contractual liability of the lender toward the borrower is the most tractable claim, but that evidentiary challenges around algorithmic opacity substantially reduce claimants' practical prospects. It proposes a rebuttable presumption of fault when a lender cannot produce an intelligible account of the scoring decision.

title: Contractual Clauses Excluding Liability for Algorithmic Errors: Validity under Serbian and EU Law
abstract: Standard-form contracts in digital platform markets frequently contain clauses that exclude or limit the service provider's liability for harm caused by algorithmic outputs such as recommendation errors, pricing anomalies, or misclassification decisions. This article assesses the validity of such clauses under the Serbian Law on Obligations, the Law on Consumer Protection, and the emerging EU Unfair Contract Terms framework as applied to B2C digital service agreements. Thirty-nine terms-of-service documents from platforms active in the Serbian market in 2016 were coded against a rubric of eight validity criteria. Results indicate that 61 per cent of the clauses examined would be unenforceable under at least one of the applicable Serbian law criteria, primarily the prohibition of clauses excluding liability for intentional acts or gross negligence. The article argues for a specific legislative provision addressing algorithmic liability exclusions.

title: The Duty to Explain Automated Decisions: Article 22 GDPR and Its Private Law Consequences in Serbia
abstract: Article 22 of the EU General Data Protection Regulation grants data subjects the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with significant effects and establishes a qualified right to explanation. This article examines how this provision, as transposed into Serbian law through the Law on Personal Data Protection 2018, interacts with civil liability doctrine. The author analyses whether a failure to explain an automated decision can ground a claim for non-material damage under Article 166 of the Law on Obligations and reviews the administrative enforcement practice of the Serbian Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection in 2019–2020. Eighteen supervisory decisions are examined. The article argues that the link between data protection violations and civil damages claims remains structurally weak in the current Serbian framework and that explicit provision for private enforcement is needed.

title: Platform Operator Liability for Algorithmic Content Curation: Mapping the Gap Between DSA and Serbian E-Commerce Law
abstract: The EU Digital Services Act (DSA, 2022) imposes specific obligations on platform operators regarding algorithmic recommendation systems, including transparency and auditability requirements. This article asks whether comparable duties exist under the Serbian Electronic Commerce Law and general contract law, using a side-by-side normative comparison and interviews with five legal officers at Serbian e-commerce companies conducted in 2021. The article identifies three categories of DSA obligation that have no functional equivalent in current Serbian law: systematic risk assessment for recommender systems, access for vetted researchers, and user-facing algorithmic transparency. It discusses the implications for Serbian companies operating in EU markets under the DSA's extraterritorial scope and for the ongoing process of Serbian EU accession. The author argues that proactive legislative alignment is preferable to reliance on general tort principles.

title: Compensation for Algorithmic Discrimination in Consumer Contracts: Serbian and European Approaches Compared
abstract: Algorithmic pricing and personalised offer systems can produce outcomes that, while not explicitly based on protected characteristics, systematically disadvantage particular demographic groups. This article examines the legal tools available to affected consumers under Serbian anti-discrimination law and the Law on Obligations, and compares them with the remedial frameworks available under the EU Equality Directives and the evolving jurisprudence of the Court of Justice of the European Union. The comparison covers six CJEU decisions from 2016 to 2024 involving automated or data-driven discrimination. The article finds that Serbian law contains a formal prohibition of indirect discrimination but lacks procedural mechanisms—in particular, disclosure orders and statistical evidence rules—that would make it effective against algorithmic discrimination. It recommends specific amendments to the Serbian Law on Prohibition of Discrimination and notes the impact of the forthcoming EU AI Liability Directive on the evidentiary landscape.

title: Contractual Transparency Obligations for Generative AI Services: Draft Framework for Serbian Law
abstract: Generative AI services deployed under contract raise transparency questions distinct from those addressed by earlier automated decision-making rules: outputs are probabilistic, often not reproducible, and their derivation from training data is largely opaque. This preprint proposes a framework of contractual transparency obligations tailored to Serbian private law for three categories of generative AI deployment: professional services contracts, consumer subscription agreements, and B2B software licences. The framework is developed through a method that combines doctrinal analysis of the Law on Obligations with a systematic reading of EU Commission guidance documents published between 2023 and 2025 and comparative review of draft model clauses proposed by legal scholars in France, the Netherlands, and Germany. The paper identifies six core transparency obligations and discusses how breach of each would be characterised and remedied under current Serbian contract law, with proposed statutory language for a future reform.

title: Parametric Study of Circular Flexure Hinges Under Combined Loading Conditions Using Finite Element Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a systematic parametric study of circular flexure hinges subjected to simultaneous bending, axial, and shear loading. A total of 216 hinge geometries were modelled in a commercial finite-element package, varying the notch radius from 0.5 mm to 3.0 mm, the minimum thickness from 0.2 mm to 0.8 mm, and the material between two aluminium alloys (Al 6061-T6 and Al 7075-T6). Compliance matrices were extracted for each case and compared against closed-form analytical expressions available in the literature. Deviations between FEA results and the analytical predictions reached up to 18% for the parasitic axial compliance at small radii-to-thickness ratios, indicating limitations of the standard beam-theory approximation in that regime. A corrective polynomial factor is proposed and fitted to the numerical dataset with a coefficient of determination R² = 0.987. The corrected expression reduces mean prediction error to below 3.5% across the parameter space studied. Results suggest that the correction is particularly relevant for hinges operating at radii-to-thickness ratios below 2.5. The study provides a practical reference for designers selecting hinge proportions for planar compliant stages.

title: Synthesis of a Four-Bar Compliant Linkage for Linear Micro-Displacement Using the Pseudo-Rigid-Body Method
abstract: A systematic synthesis procedure for a four-bar compliant linkage intended to produce near-linear output displacement over a stroke of 200 µm is described. The pseudo-rigid-body (PRB) model with torsional spring constants is used to replace each flexure hinge, reducing the synthesis problem to a rigid-body dimensional synthesis augmented by stiffness constraints. The procedure applies Freudenstein's equation to a discretised set of five precision positions, with spring stiffness introduced as an additional constraint equation. Two candidate geometries were fabricated from Al 7075-T6 by wire electrical discharge machining, and their quasi-static force–displacement responses were measured using a calibrated micro-force transducer. The measured stiffness values agreed with PRB predictions to within 6.1% and 8.4% for the two prototypes respectively. Parasitic lateral displacement at full stroke was below 1.8 µm in both cases, meeting the stated design target. The paper reports the full dimensional synthesis equations and provides a worked numerical example to facilitate reproduction.

title: Stress Concentration Factor Corrections for Elliptical Flexure Hinges Under Out-of-Plane Bending
abstract: Elliptical flexure hinges are frequently preferred over circular ones because of their lower stress concentrations in the primary bending plane, but their behaviour under out-of-plane bending is less well characterised. This paper derives stress concentration factors (SCFs) for elliptical notch profiles loaded in out-of-plane bending using a combination of photoelastic experiments and three-dimensional finite-element models. Polycarbonate specimens with ellipse semi-axis ratios of 1:1, 2:1, 3:1, and 4:1 and minimum thicknesses of 0.5 mm and 1.0 mm were tested. SCFs measured photoelastically ranged from 1.31 to 2.78 across the parameter space, and FEA predictions matched measurements within ±7%. A regression equation relating SCF to the axis ratio and the ratio of minimum thickness to hinge width is fitted and validated. The implications for fatigue life in mechanisms that experience parasitic out-of-plane loading are discussed, using S–N data for Al 6061-T6 from the literature to estimate life reduction relative to pure in-plane loading. Reductions of 25–60% in predicted fatigue life are indicated for the geometries with the highest SCFs.

title: Kinetostatic Analysis of a Compliant Pantograph Mechanism for Scaled Micro-Positioning
abstract: This paper presents a kinetostatic analysis of a planar compliant pantograph mechanism designed to scale input displacements by a ratio of 1:5 while maintaining output force within a specified corridor. The mechanism is constructed from a single monolithic Al 7075-T6 blank with eight circular flexure hinges. The PRB model is applied to derive the full stiffness matrix of the mechanism in matrix form, incorporating all six hinge spring constants. Equations of static equilibrium are solved symbolically in a computer algebra system and validated against FEA for 21 discrete input positions spanning a ±150 µm input stroke. Maximum discrepancy between PRB-predicted output force and FEA was 9.2 N at the extreme positions, corresponding to a relative error of 4.1%. Experimental measurement on a fabricated prototype using a piezoelectric actuator and a capacitive displacement sensor confirmed the simulated displacement ratio to within 1.3%. Sensitivity of the output displacement ratio to manufacturing tolerances of ±10 µm on hinge thickness was also assessed, showing a worst-case ratio variation of ±0.08.

title: Compliant Mechanisms for Precision Engineering: Synthesis, Analysis and Fabrication Considerations
abstract: This book chapter gives a self-contained treatment of compliant mechanism design aimed at practising engineers and advanced students. It covers the derivation and limitations of the pseudo-rigid-body model, closed-form compliance expressions for four standard hinge profiles (circular, elliptical, corner-filleted, and leaf-type), and a synthesis procedure based on dimensional synthesis of the equivalent rigid-body mechanism. A section on material selection discusses relevant fatigue, corrosion, and machinability criteria for aluminium alloys, spring steels, and titanium alloys at the millimetre scale. Fabrication aspects of wire EDM, conventional milling, and laser cutting are compared in terms of achievable minimum thickness, surface roughness, and residual stress, with data drawn from the published literature and from measurements in the authors' laboratory. Two worked design examples are included: a linear translation stage with 500 µm stroke and a rotary stage with ±5° angular range. The chapter concludes with a discussion of sources of modelling error, including the PRB assumption, geometric nonlinearity, and residual stress effects.

title: A Comparison of PRB Model Variants for Tapered Leaf-Flexure Hinges in the Large-Deflection Regime
abstract: Standard pseudo-rigid-body models assume small deflections and assign a single characteristic radius factor to represent the distributed compliance of a leaf-spring flexure. This paper compares four PRB model variants—the classical single-pivot model, the two-pivot model, the variable characteristic radius model, and a novel three-segment piecewise-linear approximation—against geometrically nonlinear FEA results for tapered leaf flexures with taper ratios between 1.0 and 2.5 and deflection angles up to 30°. A total of 108 load cases were evaluated. The two-pivot and variable characteristic radius models reduce tip position error relative to the classical single-pivot model by factors of 2.1 and 2.7 respectively at 30° deflection, while the three-segment approximation reduces error by a factor of 3.8 with only a modest increase in algebraic complexity. Input stiffness predictions show a similar trend, with the three-segment model yielding errors below 5.1% across all taper ratios and deflection angles studied. Practical guidance on selecting the appropriate model variant based on application accuracy requirements and acceptable computational overhead is provided.

title: Effect of packing pressure on crystallinity distribution and warpage in polyamide 6 injection mouldings
abstract: This study examines how packing pressure level affects the degree of crystallinity distribution and final part warpage in polyamide 6 (PA6) flat components (100 × 100 × 2 mm). Experiments were performed on a 60-tonne hydraulic injection moulding machine at packing pressures ranging from 40 to 100 MPa in steps of 20 MPa. Crystallinity was measured by DSC on specimens cut from five through-thickness positions. Warpage was quantified with a coordinate measuring machine at a 5 × 5 grid of points. Higher packing pressure increased average crystallinity from 28% to 36% but reduced warpage from 0.41 mm to 0.17 mm due to reduced volumetric shrinkage. A commercial process simulation code was used to model the crystallisation kinetics using an Avrami-type model with parameters fitted to the DSC data. Simulated crystallinity gradients matched measured gradients with a mean absolute error of 2.3 percentage points across all packing conditions.

title: Cross-Border Shopping and Petty Trade at the Horgoš–Röszke Crossing: Mobility Patterns and Local Economic Effects
abstract: Based on 340 intercept interviews conducted at the Horgoš–Röszke road border crossing in 2012, supplemented by customs declaration data obtained from the Serbian Customs Administration, this paper documents the volume, frequency, and commodity composition of cross-border shopping flows between Serbia and Hungary. Respondents made an average of 3.2 trips per month for shopping purposes, with automotive fuel, foodstuffs, and electronic goods representing the three most purchased categories on the Hungarian side, while Serbian visitors from Hungary predominantly purchased agricultural produce and tobacco products. Regression analysis shows that crossing frequency is positively associated with Hungarian-language competence and proximity to the border, and negatively associated with income level. The paper estimates annual household expenditure from the Serbian side at approximately €8.4 million and discusses implications for retail development policy in Subotica and Kanjiža municipalities.

title: Rethinking Territorial Cohesion in the Western Balkans: Lessons from the Serbia–EU Border Interface
abstract: This book chapter situates Serbia's pre-accession cross-border cooperation experience within broader debates on territorial cohesion as defined in EU Cohesion Policy documents from 2007 to 2013. Drawing on comparative analysis of Interreg IPA programme data for the Hungary–Serbia and Romania–Serbia cross-border programmes, the chapter identifies patterns of project concentration, sectoral prioritisation, and fund absorption across two programming periods. The analysis shows that approximately 68% of approved project value in both programmes clustered in municipalities within 30 km of the border, raising questions about the reach of territorial cohesion instruments into deeper hinterland areas. The chapter also reviews institutional learning effects on the Serbian side, noting improvements in project preparation capacity between the 2007–2013 and 2014–2020 programme cycles. Policy recommendations address multi-level governance gaps and the role of regional development agencies.

title: Border Landscape Perception Among Secondary School Students in Subotica, Zrenjanin, and Kikinda
abstract: This paper investigates how adolescents living in border municipalities of Vojvodina perceive the Serbia–Hungary and Serbia–Romania borders as landscape and social phenomena. A mixed-methods approach combined a Likert-scale questionnaire (n = 614, grades 10–12) with 18 focus group sessions conducted in 2015–2016. Quantitative findings indicate that students in Subotica, located closest to the EU border, rate cross-border interaction opportunities significantly higher than peers in Kikinda or Zrenjanin. Qualitative analysis of focus group transcripts using Atlas.ti identifies three dominant narrative frames: the border as economic opportunity, as cultural divide, and as bureaucratic obstacle. The study contributes to educational geography by linking place-based identity formation to proximity effects and family histories of cross-border mobility, and has implications for geography curriculum design in border regions.

title: Rural Depopulation and Cross-Border Labour Commuting in the Serbian–Romanian Border Zone: Evidence from the 2011 Census
abstract: This study combines 2011 census microdata from Serbia and Romania with a purpose-designed telephone survey of 285 households in eight rural municipalities along the Banat border strip to document interactions between depopulation dynamics and cross-border labour commuting. Net population loss in Serbian Banat border municipalities averaged 12.4% between 2002 and 2011, with the 20–35 age cohort showing the highest emigration rates. Survey data reveal that 34% of households with at least one working-age member reported cross-border employment in Romania, predominantly in agriculture and construction sectors in Timiș County. Spatial regression models show that commuting propensity increases with road infrastructure quality and decreases with distance to the nearest Romanian town. The paper discusses the extent to which cross-border commuting partially compensates for domestic rural out-migration rather than substituting for it.

title: Tourism Cooperation in the DKMT Euroregion: Audit of Joint Initiatives 2005–2018
abstract: Cross-border tourism is frequently cited as a development priority in Euroregion strategy documents, yet systematic evaluation of joint tourism initiatives remains scarce. This paper audits all tourism-related projects funded under the DKMT Euroregion framework and parallel Interreg IPA programmes between 2005 and 2018, identifying 41 completed projects with a combined budget of approximately €14.7 million. Content analysis of project reports and outcomes data reveals that 29 of the 41 projects delivered primarily physical infrastructure outputs—cycling trails, signage, visitor centres—while only 8 produced joint marketing materials or booking platforms, of which 5 were no longer operational at the time of audit in 2019. In-depth interviews with 11 project coordinators highlight sustainability gaps linked to maintenance funding and cross-border institutional continuity. The paper recommends a shift in programme logic from infrastructure investment toward destination management capacity building.

title: Governance Rescaling and the Vojvodina Autonomous Province: Implications for Cross-Border Cooperation Capacity
abstract: Debates about regionalisation in Serbia have periodically intensified around the constitutional status of Vojvodina, and this paper asks how shifts in Vojvodina's autonomous competences have affected its practical capacity to engage in cross-border cooperation programmes. Drawing on 32 semi-structured interviews with provincial and municipal officials conducted in 2020–2021 and a review of provincial budget documents from 2012 to 2021, the study traces the contraction of provincial co-financing powers following the 2009–2012 fiscal recentralisation. The analysis shows that the provincial secretariat's direct contribution to Interreg IPA co-financing declined by approximately 38% in real terms between 2012 and 2020. The paper discusses how this fiscal squeeze constrained municipal project preparation and counterpart funding availability, disproportionately affecting smaller border municipalities. Comparative reference is made to the Vojvodina–Baranya comparison with Hungarian sub-national arrangements.

title: Cycling Tourism Across the Serbia–Hungary Border: User Profiles and Infrastructure Gaps on the EuroVelo 6 Segment
abstract: The EuroVelo 6 long-distance cycling route crosses the Serbia–Hungary border near Bačko Novo Selo, yet this segment receives negligible attention in tourism statistics or planning documents. This paper presents results of a field survey of 276 cyclists intercepted at border crossing points and rest stops along the Serbian stretch of EV6 during the 2021 cycling season, supplemented by a systematic audit of 214 km of route infrastructure. The surveyed cyclists were predominantly from Germany, Austria, and the Netherlands, with a median trip length of 18 days and daily expenditure in Serbia averaging €34. Infrastructure audit findings document 47 separate gaps or hazards, including nine stretches lacking surfacing, four missing wayfinding signs at border approaches, and three rest stop facilities in disrepair. The paper estimates unrealised visitor expenditure at approximately €2.1 million per season due to documented deterrents and recommends priority investment segments.

title: Post-Pandemic Recovery of Cross-Border Day Tourism in the Vojvodina Border Zone: Evidence from Mobile Positioning Data
abstract: This paper uses aggregated mobile network positioning data licensed from a Serbian telecommunications operator for the period 2019–2024 to reconstruct cross-border day tourism volumes at the Serbia–Hungary and Serbia–Romania border crossings in Vojvodina before, during, and after the COVID-19 disruption. The dataset covers approximately 340 million anonymised device-day records. Results show that Serbian inbound day tourism from Hungary returned to 94% of 2019 levels by mid-2022, while inbound flows from Romania recovered more slowly, reaching 81% by the end of 2023. Departure-side data indicate that Serbian resident cross-border day trips to Hungary exceeded pre-pandemic levels by 17% in 2023, driven primarily by weekend leisure travel to Szeged and the southern Hungarian thermal bath circuit. The paper discusses methodological limitations of mobile data for tourism measurement and proposes a data-sharing framework for cross-border tourism monitoring.

title: Stable isotope records from two coeval stalagmites in Đavolja Varoš karst system: testing inter-stalagmite reproducibility over the last 12,000 years
abstract: Reproducibility of speleothem stable isotope records is a prerequisite for palaeoclimatic interpretation, yet few Balkan stalagmite studies have tested this explicitly. Two stalagmites (DV-1 and DV-2) from the same drip zone in the Đavolja Varoš karst system (southern Serbia) were dated by U-Th (14 ages combined) and analysed at 1 mm sampling resolution for δ¹⁸O and δ¹³C, yielding 740 and 680 data points respectively. Age models constructed using a Bayesian Monte Carlo approach place both records within the Holocene (11,800–220 cal a BP). Inter-stalagmite correlation of δ¹⁸O is strong (Pearson r = 0.76 on a common 100-year timescale), with systematic offsets of less than 0.4‰ attributable to kinetic fractionation differences between drip sites. A mid-Holocene δ¹⁸O minimum centred at 7,200–6,400 cal a BP is replicated in both records and interpreted as the regional Holocene Thermal Maximum. The results validate single-stalagmite interpretations from this region and provide a well-dated reference curve for cross-site comparisons.
venue: Journal of Cave and Karst Research

title: Control-Flow Coverage Criteria for Embedded C Programs: A Comparison of Branch, Decision, and MC/DC Coverage Under Resource Constraints
abstract: This paper examines three widely used structural coverage criteria—branch, decision, and modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC)—as applied to embedded C programs running on microcontrollers with limited RAM and flash memory. We implemented a static instrumentation framework on top of Frama-C and evaluated it against a suite of 14 open-source RTOS driver modules totalling approximately 18,000 lines of code. Measurements were collected on an STM32-based hardware testbed. Results show that MC/DC achieves a 12–18% higher fault-detection rate compared to branch coverage on arithmetic faults injected using mutation testing, at a code-size overhead of 9–23% depending on loop density. Decision coverage proved most cost-effective for memory-constrained targets below 32 kB flash. The paper also identifies a class of unreachable branches produced by compiler optimisations that inflate apparent coverage scores, and proposes a correction heuristic validated on two industrial driver code samples.

title: Bounded Model Checking of Timed Automata Models for Automotive Body-Control Modules
abstract: We present a bounded model checking workflow for detecting timing violations in timed automata specifications of automotive body-control module (BCM) software. The approach translates UPPAAL timed automata into SMT-LIB 2 formulas and applies the Z3 solver to search for counterexamples within a user-specified time bound. We validated the method on four BCM specifications derived from an open automotive benchmark suite, covering window-lift, central-locking, and wiper subsystems. The tool found three previously undocumented timing violations in two specifications, all confirmed by back-simulation in UPPAAL. Average verification time was 4.2 seconds per property on a standard desktop workstation. Compared to exhaustive UPPAAL exploration, the SMT-based approach reduced peak memory consumption by 34% on the largest model while retaining full counterexample traceability. A detailed discussion of false negatives introduced by the chosen bound is included.

title: Automated MISRA-C 2012 Violation Detection Using Abstract Interpretation: Scope, Precision, and False-Positive Rate
abstract: MISRA-C 2012 defines 143 rules for writing safe C code in safety-critical domains. Existing commercial checkers report high false-positive rates that burden code reviewers. This paper describes a rule-checking engine built on an abstract interpretation framework within Frama-C, targeting the 27 rules most commonly violated in embedded automotive and avionics code according to published defect datasets. We evaluated the engine on a corpus of 31 open-source embedded projects (total 94,000 lines of C). The engine achieved a false-positive rate of 8.3% and a false-negative rate of 4.1% on a manually annotated ground-truth subset of 1,200 injected violations. Runtime remained below 90 seconds for all projects. The paper discusses precision losses caused by pointer aliasing and provides a categorisation of 12 rule types where sound over-approximation is insufficient and bounded unrolling is required instead.

title: A Survey of Counterexample Generation Techniques in Software Model Checking
abstract: This chapter reviews counterexample generation methods used in software model checking tools from 2005 to 2017, covering CEGAR-based refinement, interpolant-based approaches, and SMT-guided path enumeration. The survey organises 62 primary studies along four dimensions: the underlying logic fragment used, the class of properties addressed, scalability with respect to program size, and quality of counterexample explanation for human reviewers. We identify a gap in the literature regarding counterexample minimisation for concurrent embedded programs: only 7 of the 62 studies address concurrency, and fewer than half provide mechanically reproducible experimental setups. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems, including the need for domain-specific explanation formats suited to control engineers who are not formal methods specialists, and the relationship between counterexample quality and debugging time in industrial settings.

title: Verifying Stack Boundedness in Interrupt-Driven Embedded Programs Using CBMC
abstract: Stack overflow is a leading cause of failure in interrupt-driven embedded software but is rarely addressed by standard model checkers because interrupt interleaving is difficult to model. This paper presents an analysis method that encodes interrupt preemption semantics into CBMC's C verification harness to check worst-case stack usage bounds statically. The encoding introduces a scheduler model with configurable priority levels and nondeteministic interrupt timing. We applied the method to eight firmware projects written for Cortex-M microcontrollers, ranging from 2,000 to 15,000 lines of C. CBMC found potential stack overflows in three projects; two were confirmed on hardware using JTAG stack monitoring. Analysis time ranged from 11 seconds to 8.4 minutes depending on interrupt nesting depth. We report on the trade-off between the precision of the interrupt model and solver performance, and discuss conditions under which the method produces safe over-approximations.

title: Model-Based Test Suite Generation from UML State Machines Using SMT-Guided Path Selection
abstract: We describe a test suite generation method for safety-critical software specified as UML state machines. The method translates state machines into transition systems and uses an SMT solver to select execution paths that satisfy user-specified coverage targets, including all-transitions, all-pairs, and a new metric we call fault-boundary coverage (FBC) designed to exercise guard conditions at their boundary values. Test cases are generated as concrete C test vectors using symbolic execution over the extracted paths. We evaluated the approach on a medical-device alarm management component (5 concurrent state machines, 78 transitions) and a railway interlocking subsystem specification (4 state machines, 112 transitions). FBC-guided selection achieved 100% mutation score on arithmetic guard faults with 23% fewer test cases than random path selection. The paper includes a formal definition of FBC and a proof that it subsumes branch coverage on guard conditions.

title: Precision of Pointer Analysis Algorithms in Frama-C for Small Embedded Programs: An Empirical Study
abstract: Pointer aliasing undermines the precision of dataflow-based static analyses in embedded C code. This paper empirically compares four pointer analysis configurations available in Frama-C—Eva's default value analysis, a field-sensitive extension, a context-sensitive variant, and a hybrid combining the latter two—on a benchmark of 20 embedded programs between 500 and 4,000 lines. We measure precision as the ratio of resolved pointer targets and report analysis time and memory use. The context-sensitive variant resolves 91% of pointer accesses compared to 74% for the default, but requires 3.4× more time. For programs below 1,500 lines, the hybrid configuration matches context-sensitive precision with only 1.6× overhead. We also identify 11 program patterns where all four configurations produce identical imprecision, attributable to non-local pointer escapes through function pointers, and suggest a lightweight pre-pass to mitigate three of them.

title: Integrating Formal Verification Artefacts into IEC 61508 Safety Cases: A Process Proposal and Case Study
abstract: IEC 61508 requires documented evidence of software correctness for Safety Integrity Levels 2–4 but does not specify how formal verification artefacts—property files, solver logs, coverage reports—should be structured as safety case arguments. This paper proposes a process for integrating CBMC verification runs and Frama-C analysis reports into Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) safety cases. We instantiated the process on a pressure-sensor firmware component developed by a Serbian automation equipment manufacturer under a research cooperation agreement, covering 14 safety requirements at SIL 2. The resulting safety case argument tree contains 47 nodes; 31 are supported directly by machine-generated artefacts. We report on practical difficulties encountered, including solver non-determinism affecting reproducibility of evidence and the challenge of explaining SMT solver outputs to functional-safety auditors. The process was reviewed by two independent safety assessors.

title: Incremental Verification of Patched Embedded Firmware Using Change-Impact Analysis and Reuse of SMT Proofs
abstract: When firmware is patched to fix a defect, re-running full formal verification from scratch is costly. This paper presents an incremental verification approach that (1) identifies which program paths are affected by a source-level patch using a lightweight static differencing tool, (2) reuses previously computed SMT unsatisfiability certificates for unaffected paths, and (3) runs bounded model checking only on affected paths and a configurable neighbourhood. We evaluated the approach on 24 patch pairs extracted from the commit history of three open-source embedded firmware projects. Incremental verification reduced total solver time by a median of 68% compared to full re-verification, with no loss in soundness on properties that remained within the original proof scope. We characterise six patch patterns for which certificate reuse is unsafe and must be suppressed, and provide a decision procedure for detecting these patterns in under 2 seconds.

title: Data-Flow Coverage Adequacy for Safety-Critical PLC Programs: Adapting Software Testing Criteria to IEC 61131-3 Structured Text
abstract: Programmable logic controller programs written in IEC 61131-3 Structured Text are used in process-control and building-automation systems but receive less formal analysis attention than C-based firmware. This paper adapts classical data-flow coverage criteria—all-defs, all-uses, and all-du-paths—to Structured Text by defining a control-flow graph construction for ST's iteration and selection constructs and handling its typed variable model. We implemented the analysis as a standalone tool and evaluated it on 17 ST programs from the OpenPLC benchmark, ranging from 80 to 640 lines. All-uses coverage detected 83% of seeded data-flow faults; all-du-paths detected 91% at the cost of a 2.3× increase in required test cases. The paper also identifies five ST language features—function-block instantiation, retain variables, edge-detection functions, task interleaving, and direct addressing—that require extensions to the standard du-pair definition, and proposes concrete extensions for each.

title: Ugrađeni ugljenik montažnih armirano-betonskih greda: inventar životnog ciklusa na primeru fabrike u Vojvodini
abstract: U radu je prikazana izrada inventara životnog ciklusa (LCI) za montažne armirano-betonske grede koje se proizvode u fabrici prefabrikovanih elemenata u Vojvodini. Prikupljeni su primarni podaci o potrošnji energije, cementa, čelika i vode za period 2018–2020. godine, koji pokrivaju ukupno 14 200 tona gotovih elemenata. Funkcionalna jedinica definisana je kao jedan metar kvadratni horizontalne nosivosti pri opterećenju od 5 kN/m². Rezultati pokazuju da faza proizvodnje betona doprinosi 68% ukupnog potencijala globalnog zagrevanja (GWP), koji iznosi 312 kg CO₂-ekv./m². Upoređenjem sa evropskim EPD bazama utvrđeno je da vrednost GWP premašuje medijanu sličnih sistema za oko 18%, što se pripisuje većem udelu portland cementnog klinkera u lokalnim mešavinama. Rad identifikuje supstituciju dela cementnog veziva zgurnim cementom CEM III kao najefikasniju meru smanjenja ugrađenog ugljenika.

title: Modeliranje scenarija kraja životnog veka montažnih armirano-betonskih hala u Srbiji: recikliranje, deponovanje i ponovljena upotreba
abstract: Rad analizira tri scenarija kraja životnog veka (EoL) za montažne armirano-betonske hale tipičnog industrijskog karaktera u Srbiji: (1) selektivnu demontažu i ponovnu upotrebu elemenata, (2) drobljenje i recikliranje betona kao sekundarnog agregata, i (3) mešano odlaganje na deponiju građevinskog otpada. Modelovanje je sprovedeno u OpenLCA 1.10 uz korišćenje srpskog inventara za transport i deponovanje. Za objekat gabarita 60 × 30 m i mase konstrukcije oko 850 tona, scenario selektivne demontaže donosi negativan GWP od –28 kg CO₂-ekv./toni zahvaljujući kreditima izbegnute proizvodnje, dok scenario deponovanja generiše dodatnih 14 kg CO₂-ekv./toni. Analiza osetljivosti pokazuje da je stopa razdvajanja armature najvažniji parametar: pad stope sa 90% na 60% smanjuje korist scenarija reciklaže za 35%. Rezultati su relevantni za buduće planove ponovne industrijalizacije vojvođanskog regiona gde postoji veliki broj zastarelih hala iz 1970-ih i 1980-ih.

title: Uticaj izbora metode alokacije na rezultate procene životnog ciklusa prefabrikovanih betonskih elemenata
abstract: Alokacija input-output tokova između ko-produkata u postrojenjima za prefabrikaciju betona značajno utiče na rezultate LCA studija, ali je retko transparentno dokumentovana u regionalnoj literaturi. U ovom radu poređene su tri metode alokacije – alokacija na osnovu mase, ekonomske vrednosti i fizičke uzročnosti – primenjene na studiju slučaja fabrike koja istovremeno proizvodi stubove, grede i ploče. Analiza je sprovedena u SimaPro 9.2 za 12 kategorija uticaja prema CML-IA karakterizacionom modelu. Rezultati pokazuju da razlike između metoda iznose do 24% za GWP i do 41% za potencijal acidifikacije. Alokacija na osnovu mase daje najkonzervativnije rezultate za produkte sa višim sadržajem armature. Zaključuje se da harmonizacija metoda alokacije mora biti prioritet za uspostavljanje pouzdanih nacionalnih EPD benčmarkova u Srbiji.
