title: Carbon benchmarking of precast concrete structural systems in Central and South-Eastern Europe: a dataset of 47 EPDs
abstract: Reliable carbon benchmarks for precast concrete structural products are scarce for Central and South-Eastern Europe. This paper compiles and harmonises a dataset of 47 Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) for precast columns, beams, slabs, and wall panels published between 2012 and 2021 by manufacturers in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, Croatia, Slovenia, and Austria. All EPDs were re-expressed in terms of GWP per kilogram of structural element to enable cross-product comparison. The dataset reveals a wide range of GWP intensities: from 0.086 to 0.198 kg CO₂-eq./kg across all product types, with the highest values concentrated in Serbian and Romanian manufacturers. The main explanatory variables identified through regression analysis are cement content (r² = 0.61), concrete strength class, and the share of recycled steel reinforcement. Benchmarks are proposed at three percentile levels (25th, 50th, 75th) for use in national building regulation and green procurement criteria. Data gaps and inconsistencies in declared system boundaries are discussed.

title: Primena metode Monte Karlo za analizu neizvesnosti u LCA prefabrikovanih nosača: slučaj srpskog elektroenergetskog miksa
abstract: Srpski elektroenergetski miks podložan je značajnim godišnjim varijacijama u udjelu termoelektrana na lignit, što unosi merljivu neizvesnost u LCA studije građevinskih proizvoda. U ovom radu izvršena je Monte Karlo simulacija sa 10 000 iteracija za LCA prefabrikovanog armirano-betonskog nosača raspona 18 m, koristeći trogodišnje podatke o mešavini goriva iz srpske elektroenergetske mreže (2018–2020). Analiza neizvesnosti sprovedena je u OpenLCA 1.11 sa pdfPredictive modulom. GWP za fazu A1–A3 kreće se u opsegu 215–289 kg CO₂-ekv./komadu na nivou poverenja od 95%, što predstavlja raspon od 26%. Zaključuje se da su LCA studije zasnovane na jednoj godini podataka o mreži nedovoljno reprezentativne za srpski kontekst i da bi srpski program za EPD trebalo da propisuje trogodišnji prosek podataka o mreži.

title: Life-cycle carbon assessment of a precast reinforced concrete school building: cradle-to-grave analysis including 50-year operational energy
abstract: This study presents a full cradle-to-grave LCA of a precast reinforced concrete school building (2 780 m² gross floor area) constructed in Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia in 2018. The assessment covers modules A1–C4 and module D (beyond system boundary) in line with EN 15978:2011, with a reference service life of 50 years. Primary embodied carbon data were derived from verified EPDs for the precast structural system; operational energy was modelled using EnergyPlus v9.4 and calibrated against 24 months of measured consumption data. Embodied carbon for the structural system (A1–A5) amounts to 168 kg CO₂-eq./m², while cumulative operational carbon over 50 years represents 1 940 kg CO₂-eq./m² under a static grid assumption and 1 220 kg CO₂-eq./m² under a decarbonisation trajectory scenario aligned with Serbia's National Energy and Climate Plan. End-of-life credits (module D) offset 6.8% of total life-cycle GWP. The results indicate that operational emissions dominate even under conservative assumptions, but that the relative importance of embodied carbon increases substantially under the decarbonisation scenario.

title: End-of-life treatment pathways for demolition concrete in Serbia: current practice, regulatory gaps and LCA implications
abstract: Serbia generates an estimated 4.2 million tonnes of construction and demolition waste annually, yet official statistics on concrete fraction recycling rates remain incomplete. This paper combines a field survey of 11 demolition contractors operating in Vojvodina and Belgrade with a regulatory review and LCA modelling of three waste treatment pathways: landfilling, crushing for unbound sub-base aggregate, and closed-loop recycling as recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) for structural use. Survey results indicate that landfilling still accounts for roughly 58% of demolition concrete by mass, primarily due to the absence of mandatory waste sorting requirements and the low gate fees at regional landfills. LCA results show that the RCA pathway reduces module C GWP contributions by up to 48 kg CO₂-eq./tonne compared with landfilling, provided that transport distances remain below 35 km. The paper identifies three specific gaps in Serbian waste regulations that prevent the circular economy pathway from becoming economically competitive.

title: Poređenje sistema dodele ekoloških bodova za prefabrikovane AB konstrukcije u nacionalnim zelenim standardima: analiza kriterijuma BREEAM, LEED i srpskog pravilnika o energetskoj efikasnosti
abstract: Zeleni standardi za zgrade – BREEAM International, LEED v4.1 i srpski Pravilnik o energetskoj efikasnosti zgrada (2023) – različito tretiraju ugrađeni ugljenik i EPD dokumentaciju prefabrikovanih nosećih konstrukcija. U ovom radu izvršena je uporedna analiza releventnih bodovnih kategorija primenom virtuelnog modela stambene zgrade u Novom Sadu sa prefabrikovanim AB skeletom. Analiza pokazuje da srpski pravilnik ne dodeljuje direktne bodove za EPD ni za benčmarking ugrađenog ugljenika, dok BREEAM Mat 01 i LEED MRc2 pružaju merljive podsticaje koji su dostigli prag bodova u 34 od 40 simuliranih scenarija. Razmatrana je mogućnost uvođenja nacionalnog sistema kreditiranja ugrađenog ugljenika zasnovanog na predloženim regionalnim benčmarkovima. Zaključci su upućeni Ministarstvu građevinarstva, saobraćaja i infrastrukture kao doprinos tekućoj reviziji pravilnika.

title: Antenna Phase-Centre Variation Corrections in Continuous GNSS Stations: Impact on Vertical Velocity Estimates at Mixed-Receiver Networks
abstract: Networks in which antenna and receiver models change over time are susceptible to apparent vertical offsets when phase-centre variation (PCV) corrections are applied inconsistently. Using a subset of 13 stations from the Serbian national CORS network with documented equipment changes between 2004 and 2019, this study systematically tested three PCV correction approaches: igs14.atx individual calibrations, type-mean calibrations, and robot-calibrated site-specific values obtained for five stations. Equipment change epochs were identified from log files and validated against discontinuity detection using the interquartile range method. Applying individual calibrations in place of type-mean values altered vertical velocities by −0.12 to +0.27 mm/yr depending on the antenna combination involved. Robot-calibrated corrections agreed with individual igs14.atx values at the 0.05 mm/yr level. Recommendations for network operators on maintaining consistent PCV correction chains through hardware upgrades are summarised.

title: Energy Consumption Mapping of a Multi-Stage Turning Process Chain: A Shop-Floor Measurement Approach
abstract: This study presents a structured methodology for mapping energy consumption across a three-stage CNC turning process chain producing automotive shaft components. Energy data were collected using clip-on power analysers at 1 Hz sampling rate over 40 production shifts at a mid-sized Serbian metalworking company. The process chain comprised roughing, semi-finishing, and finishing operations on a 42CrMo4 steel workpiece. Specific energy consumption values were determined for each stage, ranging from 1.8 kWh/kg for roughing to 4.3 kWh/kg for finishing. Material removal rate and spindle load were identified as the primary drivers of energy variation across stages. A simple regression model was fitted to predict stage-level energy demand from cutting parameters, achieving an R² of 0.84 on a hold-out validation set. Results indicate that rescheduling finishing operations to avoid partial-load spindle conditions could reduce chain-level energy use by approximately 12%. The paper contributes empirical shop-floor data to a literature that has relied largely on simulation or laboratory-scale experiments.

title: Life-Cycle Cost Assessment of Conventional versus Minimum Quantity Lubrication in Milling of Aluminium Alloy EN AW-6082
abstract: The paper compares the life-cycle costs (LCC) of flood cooling and minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) across a representative milling process chain for producing aerospace-grade aluminium bracket parts. Cost categories considered include cutting fluid procurement, waste disposal, tool wear, energy consumption, machine maintenance, and labour. Primary data were gathered from a contract manufacturer in Novi Sad over a six-month production period covering 1,200 machined parts. Auxiliary data on fluid toxicity and disposal were sourced from material safety data sheets and regional waste handler invoices. Under flood cooling, cumulative LCC per part amounted to 3.74 EUR, compared to 2.61 EUR under MQL, a reduction of 30.2%. Tool life under MQL was 18% shorter on average, partially offsetting savings on fluid costs. A sensitivity analysis showed that results are robust to ±20% variation in fluid disposal fees. Environmental impact was quantified using CML 2002 midpoint indicators; MQL reduced the global warming potential contribution of the lubrication sub-system by 44%. The study argues that LCC and environmental indicators should be assessed jointly rather than separately when selecting lubrication strategies.

title: Material Flow Analysis of a Small-Batch Sheet Metal Fabrication Chain and Its Implications for Scrap Rate Reduction
abstract: Small-batch sheet metal fabrication is characterised by high setup-to-production ratios and variable scrap generation, yet material flow data for such settings are scarce. This paper reports a material flow analysis (MFA) conducted at a subcontractor producing enclosure components from DC01 cold-rolled steel sheet. Data were collected over three months, tracking material inputs, intermediate waste streams, and finished-part outputs across laser cutting, bending, and spot-welding stages. Overall material utilisation efficiency was found to be 71.3%, with laser cutting accounting for 68% of total scrap by mass. Nesting optimisation using a commercially available CAM tool was tested retrospectively on the recorded cutting jobs; it would have raised material efficiency to an estimated 78.9% without any process modification. Energy-related CO2 emissions were allocated proportionally to material processed per stage, yielding an emission intensity of 2.1 kg CO2-eq per kilogram of finished part. The analysis provides a quantitative basis for prioritising improvement actions and demonstrates that MFA can be executed with production records alone, without additional sensing infrastructure.

title: Residual stress evolution in TiAlN-coated carbide inserts measured by synchrotron XRD before and after interrupted turning tests
abstract: Residual stress in TiAlN-coated WC-Co inserts was measured by synchrotron X-ray diffraction (beamline energy 87 keV) at three states: as-deposited, after turning of AISI 52100 steel (62 HRC) for 500 m at 150 m/min, and after 1000 m at the same conditions. Measurements were taken at 12 positions along the cutting edge at each state. As-deposited compressive stress in the TiAlN coating was −3.8 ± 0.2 GPa. After 500 m, stress relaxed to −2.1 ± 0.4 GPa in the contact zone and −3.5 ± 0.2 GPa outside it. At 1000 m, the contact zone showed near-zero stress in two inserts with visible delamination and −1.4 GPa in the three without. The WC substrate showed compressive stresses of −0.4 GPa as-deposited with no statistically significant change after 500 m. Stress relaxation in the contact zone correlated with higher flank wear rate (r = 0.81, n = 15). Synchrotron measurement allowed a 30 µm spatial resolution, providing spatially resolved data unavailable from laboratory XRD.

title: Nitrate content in leafy vegetables from market gardens in Vojvodina: a seasonal survey
abstract: We measured nitrate concentrations in spinach, lettuce, and Swiss chard sampled from 38 market gardens across 12 Vojvodina municipalities during spring and autumn of 2008. A total of 342 composite samples were analysed by ion chromatography at the Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad. Nitrate concentrations ranged from 820 mg/kg fresh weight in autumn lettuce to 4,310 mg/kg in spring spinach, with significant municipality-level variation (ANOVA, p < 0.001). Soil nitrogen content, obtained from the Provincial Institute of Agriculture, explained 41% of the variance in vegetable nitrate levels in a linear regression model. Autumn samples showed consistently lower concentrations than spring samples across all species, likely reflecting reduced fertiliser application and higher light exposure. These baseline data were compiled into a regional food composition supplement that has since been used in dietary exposure calculations for Vojvodina populations.

title: Estimated dietary nitrate intake in adult populations of Srem and Bačka subregions using 24-hour recall data
abstract: This cross-sectional study estimated daily dietary nitrate intake among 1,204 adults (ages 35–74) recruited from general practitioners' registers in Srem and Bačka subregions of Vojvodina. Dietary data were collected using three non-consecutive 24-hour recalls per participant. Nitrate values were assigned using a regionally calibrated food composition table constructed from our earlier survey data and supplementary European food composition databases. Mean estimated intake was 147 mg nitrate per day (95% CI: 138–156 mg/day) in Srem and 121 mg/day (95% CI: 114–128 mg/day) in Bačka. Vegetable sources accounted for 89% of total nitrate intake in both subregions, with spinach, lettuce, and beetroot as the dominant contributors. Men showed higher absolute intake than women, largely explained by greater total food consumption. The study provides the first subregion-specific nitrate intake estimates for Vojvodina and serves as an exposure baseline for subsequent ecologic analyses.

title: Gastric cancer incidence trends across Vojvodina municipalities, 1990–2010: a registry-based analysis
abstract: We analysed age-standardised gastric cancer incidence rates across 45 Vojvodina municipalities using data from the Cancer Registry of the Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, covering the period 1990–2010. A total of 8,743 incident cases were included after exclusion of cases with incomplete address records. Poisson regression with municipality as the unit of analysis revealed a mean annual percentage change of −1.8% (95% CI: −2.3% to −1.3%) in age-standardised incidence, consistent with declining trends observed across most of southeastern Europe. Municipality-level incidence varied three-fold, with higher rates concentrated in agricultural municipalities of southern Bačka and Banat. Urban municipalities showed significantly lower rates after adjustment for age structure (rate ratio 0.74, 95% CI: 0.61–0.90). These spatial and temporal patterns form the outcome framework for linking dietary nitrate exposure data in subsequent ecological studies. Data quality checks identified reporting gaps in three small municipalities before 1997, which were handled by multiple imputation.

title: Helicobacter pylori seroprevalence and its confounding role in nitrate–gastric cancer ecological studies in Vojvodina
abstract: Ecological analyses of dietary nitrate and gastric cancer must account for Helicobacter pylori infection, a primary causal risk factor. We used seroprevalence data from a 2009 cross-sectional study of 2,110 adults across 14 Vojvodina municipalities to construct municipality-level H. pylori prevalence estimates. Seroprevalence ranged from 47% to 71% across municipalities. In multivariable ecological models predicting gastric cancer incidence rates (2005–2012), inclusion of H. pylori seroprevalence substantially attenuated the crude nitrate–cancer association (ecological regression coefficient reduced by 38%). The H. pylori variable itself was the strongest single predictor (β = 0.61, p < 0.001). This finding underscores that ecological nitrate–cancer associations in this region are substantially confounded by infection prevalence and that infection data must be incorporated into any causal model. We describe a practical approach to partial ecological confounding adjustment applicable to similar studies in regions without individual-level data linkage.

title: Association between municipality-level dietary nitrate intake and gastric cancer incidence in Vojvodina: an ecological study
abstract: We conducted a cross-sectional ecological study using 42 Vojvodina municipalities as units of analysis to examine the association between estimated mean dietary nitrate intake and age-standardised gastric cancer incidence. Nitrate exposure estimates were constructed by combining municipality-level vegetable consumption data from a 2009 nutrition survey with nitrate concentration data from local produce markets. Gastric cancer incidence was taken from the 2004–2013 registry data. After adjustment for H. pylori seroprevalence, smoking prevalence (from the 2010 Vojvodina Health Survey), and per-capita income, dietary nitrate intake was not significantly associated with gastric cancer incidence (ecological regression coefficient 0.003, 95% CI: −0.002 to 0.008, p = 0.23). Municipalities in the highest nitrate intake quartile showed age-standardised incidence rates of 21.4 per 100,000 compared with 23.1 per 100,000 in the lowest quartile, a non-significant inverse pattern. These results do not support a strong positive ecological association under current dietary exposure levels in Vojvodina.

title: Dietary exposure to nitrate and nitrite among children aged 6–10 in rural Vojvodina: a repeated 24-hour recall study
abstract: Children represent a distinct population for nitrate exposure assessment given their smaller body mass and different food patterns. We recruited 384 children aged 6–10 from primary schools in four rural Vojvodina municipalities and collected three non-consecutive 24-hour dietary recalls per child across one school year. Nitrate and nitrite values were assigned using our regional food composition supplement. Mean daily nitrate intake was 68 mg (95% CI: 62–74 mg), equivalent to 2.4 mg/kg body weight, exceeding the EFSA acceptable daily intake of 3.7 mg/kg body weight in 8% of the sample. Spinach consumed as school-meal side dishes was the single largest contributor (29% of total nitrate). Nitrite intake from processed meats averaged 0.09 mg/kg body weight per day. Households using well water with nitrate levels above 50 mg/L showed higher total nitrate exposures in children, adding a non-dietary exposure pathway. Findings were communicated to participating municipalities and the Provincial Secretariat for Health.

title: Nitrate in drinking water from private wells and its contribution to total dietary nitrate exposure in Vojvodina agricultural zones
abstract: A substantial proportion of rural Vojvodina residents use private wells as their primary water source. We measured nitrate concentrations in 214 wells across 18 municipalities and cross-referenced well users identified in a 2015 household survey covering 3,240 adults. Well nitrate concentrations ranged from 4 mg/L to 198 mg/L (median 31 mg/L). Among well users, 22% consumed water exceeding the EU limit of 50 mg/L. For the subset of respondents with both dietary recall data and well water measurements, drinking water contributed a mean 19% (range 2%–64%) of total daily nitrate intake, increasing to 41% among high-concentration well users. Linear mixed models showed that agricultural land use within 500 m of a well (estimated via municipal cadastral data) was associated with higher well nitrate concentrations (β = 12.4 mg/L per 10% increase in surrounding arable land, p = 0.004). These results suggest that well water is a material nitrate exposure route that should not be omitted from epidemiological studies in the region.

title: Time trends in per-capita vegetable supply and implications for population nitrate exposure in Vojvodina, 1980–2015
abstract: Changes in agricultural production and consumer behaviour affect population-level dietary nitrate exposure over time. We reconstructed per-capita vegetable supply series for 12 vegetable categories in Vojvodina from 1980 to 2015 using Provincial Statistical Office data, complemented by household budget survey food acquisition data. Nitrate content values were assigned from our measured regional database and supplemented with published European data for years before 2008. Estimated population mean daily nitrate intake from vegetables declined from approximately 198 mg/day in 1985 to 133 mg/day in 2015, driven primarily by a 47% reduction in spinach consumption and a 28% reduction in beet consumption. Conversely, estimated nitrate from rocket salad and other imported leaves increased from negligible to approximately 11 mg/day. These supply-side trends parallel the observed decline in gastric cancer incidence, though causal attribution is confounded by simultaneous changes in H. pylori prevalence, refrigeration access, and salt intake. The reconstructed time series is provided as supplementary data.

title: Nitrate and nitrite intake and gastric cancer risk: a systematic review of ecological and cohort studies in Central and Eastern Europe
abstract: We systematically reviewed epidemiological studies published between 1990 and 2019 that examined associations between dietary nitrate or nitrite intake and gastric cancer incidence in Central and Eastern European populations. MEDLINE, EMBASE, and regional databases were searched, yielding 31 eligible studies: 18 ecological, 9 cohort, and 4 case-control. Meta-analysis of cohort and case-control studies produced a pooled relative risk of 1.09 (95% CI: 0.95–1.24) for the highest versus lowest nitrate intake category, with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 63%). Ecological studies showed inconsistent effect directions. Assessment of bias indicated that the majority of ecological studies did not adequately control for H. pylori prevalence, and only 7 of 31 studies used regionally calibrated food composition data. Publication year was inversely associated with reported effect size in meta-regression, suggesting earlier studies may have overestimated associations. We conclude that evidence from this region does not establish a clear dose-dependent positive association and highlight methodological gaps requiring attention.

title: Dietary patterns, nitrate intake, and gastric cancer risk in a Vojvodina case-control study: preliminary findings
abstract: We present preliminary findings from an ongoing hospital-based case-control study of gastric cancer in Vojvodina, with 214 incident cases recruited from the Oncology Institute of Vojvodina and 428 frequency-matched controls recruited from surgical wards of the same hospital between 2018 and 2021. Dietary exposure was assessed retrospectively using a validated food frequency questionnaire adapted to Vojvodina food culture, with nitrate values assigned from our regional food composition database. Conditional logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, H. pylori status, smoking, alcohol, and socioeconomic score yielded an odds ratio of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.67–1.23) per 50 mg/day increment in vegetable nitrate intake, indicating no significant association. A traditional Vojvodina dietary pattern characterised by high consumption of smoked meats, lard, and pickled vegetables was associated with elevated gastric cancer risk (OR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.44–3.18). Recruitment is ongoing with a target of 400 cases; final analysis is expected in 2025.

title: Validation of a nitrate-specific food frequency questionnaire against 24-hour urinary nitrate excretion in a Vojvodina adult sample
abstract: Accurate dietary nitrate assessment in epidemiological studies requires validated instruments. We validated a 68-item food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) developed for Vojvodina dietary patterns against 24-hour urinary nitrate excretion, a biomarker of total nitrate intake, in a convenience sample of 128 adult volunteers from Novi Sad and Zrenjanin. Participants completed the FFQ and provided two 24-hour urine collections within a four-week period. Spearman rank correlation between FFQ-estimated nitrate intake and mean urinary nitrate excretion was 0.54 (95% CI: 0.40–0.65). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean difference of 18 mg/day (FFQ higher than biomarker), with limits of agreement of −72 to 108 mg/day. Correlation was stronger in participants with higher vegetable variety (ρ = 0.63) than in those with monotonous diets (ρ = 0.44). The FFQ showed acceptable ranking ability for epidemiological use and is recommended for studies prioritising exposure ranking rather than absolute intake estimation.

title: Nitrate concentrations in conventionally and organically grown vegetables from certified farms in Vojvodina: a comparative survey, 2021–2022
abstract: Consumer interest in organic produce raises questions about whether organic farming reduces dietary nitrate exposure. We compared nitrate concentrations in five common vegetables (spinach, lettuce, carrot, kohlrabi, and beetroot) sampled from 9 certified organic farms and 15 conventional farms across Vojvodina during the 2021 and 2022 growing seasons. A total of 520 samples were analysed by ion chromatography. Mean nitrate concentrations were significantly lower in organically grown spinach (2,140 vs. 3,280 mg/kg, p < 0.001) and lettuce (1,560 vs. 2,310 mg/kg, p = 0.002), but did not differ significantly for carrots, kohlrabi, or beetroot. Mixed-effects models accounting for municipality and season confirmed farming system as a significant predictor for leafy species only. Given that leafy vegetables dominate population nitrate intake in Vojvodina, a shift toward organic leafy vegetable consumption could reduce estimated mean daily intake by approximately 15–20%, based on current consumption patterns.

title: Epidemiology of upper gastrointestinal cancers in Vojvodina
abstract: This book chapter reviews the descriptive and analytic epidemiology of gastric, oesophageal, and gastro-oesophageal junction cancers in Vojvodina, drawing on registry data from 1985 to 2020. Age-standardised gastric cancer incidence declined from 32.1 per 100,000 in 1985–1989 to 17.4 per 100,000 in 2016–2020, while oesophageal cancer rates remained relatively stable at 4–5 per 100,000 throughout the period. The chapter synthesises evidence on regional risk factors including H. pylori prevalence, dietary habits (salt, smoked meats, pickled vegetables, vegetable consumption), smoking, alcohol, and socioeconomic determinants. A section is devoted to the specific question of dietary nitrate and nitrite, summarising published ecologic and individual-level studies conducted in the region and their methodological limitations. The chapter is intended as a reference for clinicians, public health practitioners, and researchers initiating epidemiological work in the Vojvodina context, and includes an annotated bibliography of regional sources.

title: Final results of the Vojvodina case-control study of gastric cancer: dietary nitrate, nitrite, traditional dietary patterns, and H. pylori interaction
abstract: This paper reports the final analysis of a hospital-based case-control study conducted at the Oncology Institute of Vojvodina between 2018 and 2024, including 389 histologically confirmed gastric cancer cases and 778 frequency-matched hospital controls. Exposure was assessed by interviewer-administered food frequency questionnaire with regionally calibrated nitrate and nitrite values. Conditional logistic regression yielded an odds ratio of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.70–1.11) per 50 mg/day increment in vegetable nitrate intake after full adjustment, confirming no significant protective or harmful association. Processed-meat nitrite intake showed a borderline positive association (OR 1.19 per 10 mg/day, 95% CI: 0.99–1.42). A statistically significant multiplicative interaction was observed between H. pylori seropositivity and a traditional Vojvodina smoked-meat dietary pattern (OR for joint exposure 4.37, 95% CI: 2.81–6.80, versus neither). These findings suggest that population strategies targeting H. pylori eradication and smoked-meat reduction are more likely to reduce gastric cancer burden in Vojvodina than policies focused primarily on vegetable nitrate.

title: Seasonal timing of Ixodes ricinus questing activity in lowland riparian habitats of northern Serbia
abstract: Questing tick density was monitored at eight riparian sites along the Tisa and Begej rivers in Vojvodina from March to November 2012 using standardised drag-sampling on 100 m transects repeated bi-weekly. A total of 3,847 Ixodes ricinus individuals were collected across all life stages. Peak nymphal activity occurred in the second half of May, approximately two weeks earlier than recorded in montane habitats of Fruška Gora in concurrent studies. Adult activity showed a bimodal pattern with spring and autumn peaks. Generalised additive models related questing density to accumulated degree-days above 7°C and relative humidity, explaining 61% of deviance in nymphal counts. These phenological data provide empirical input for seasonal risk windows in TBE transmission models applicable to the flat agricultural landscape of the Pannonian basin.

title: Sex differences in the age-related decline of HDL cholesterol in a Vojvodinian multigenerational cohort
abstract: HDL cholesterol was measured at four time points over 16 years in 974 participants (51.3% women) from a post-industrial Vojvodinian community cohort. Linear mixed-effects models with age as a continuous predictor and interaction terms for biological sex were used to characterise the trajectory of HDL decline. Women showed a significantly slower mean annual rate of HDL decline than men across the full follow-up period (−0.021 vs. −0.041 mmol/L per year; p < 0.001). However, postmenopausal women (defined by self-report and age ≥ 52) experienced a sharper decline in the five years following menopause, narrowing the gap with men. Statin use, which was more prevalent in men by age 55, was associated with modest attenuation of HDL decline in both sexes. These findings highlight the importance of sex-stratified analysis when interpreting lipid trajectories in middle-aged and older adults.

title: Comparison of three commercial anti-HEV IgG ELISA kits for use in occupational seroprevalence surveys in low-to-middle endemic settings
abstract: Discordant seroprevalence estimates across European HEV studies are partly attributable to variability in ELISA performance. This study evaluated three widely used commercial anti-HEV IgG ELISA kits—designated Kit A, Kit B, and Kit C—against a panel of 192 sera from slaughterhouse workers with known exposure histories and 48 sera from confirmed acute HEV cases archived at the Institute for Public Health of Vojvodina. Sensitivity was 81.3%, 87.5%, and 93.8% respectively, and specificity was 97.9%, 94.8%, and 91.7%. Overall agreement between Kit A and Kit C was 84.4% (kappa 0.61). Discordant results were concentrated in the low-titre range (0.5–2.0 IU/mL). Avidity testing on a subset of 35 discordant samples showed that most Kit-A-negative, Kit-C-positive results had low avidity indices, suggesting early or waning antibody responses. Kit selection substantially affects seroprevalence estimates in occupational cohorts and should be standardised in multi-site studies.

title: Adsorption of CO on close-packed Pd(111) and Pd(100) surfaces: a comparative DFT study
abstract: The adsorption of carbon monoxide on two low-index palladium surfaces was investigated using spin-polarised density functional theory within the PBE generalised gradient approximation. Calculations were performed using the VASP code with PAW pseudopotentials and a plane-wave cutoff of 400 eV. A four-layer slab model with 15 Å of vacuum was used, with the two bottom layers fixed. Adsorption energies were evaluated at hollow, bridge, and top sites for both Pd(111) and Pd(100). On Pd(111) the bridge site was found to be preferred with an adsorption energy of −1.84 eV, consistent with calorimetric measurements from the literature, while on Pd(100) the hollow site was marginally more stable at −1.91 eV. Charge density difference maps and projected density of states showed stronger d–π* back-donation on Pd(100), correlating with the slightly elevated binding energy. The d-band centre positions, −1.73 eV for Pd(111) and −1.61 eV for Pd(100), support this trend. Dispersion corrections (DFT-D3) shifted adsorption energies by approximately 0.12 eV upward but did not change site preference. These results provide a well-converged reference set for subsequent bimetallic surface studies.

title: Oxygen dissociation barriers on Ru(0001): effect of surface coverage from first principles
abstract: Dissociative adsorption of molecular oxygen on Ru(0001) was studied using the climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) method within the DFT-PBE framework. Coverage effects were modelled by varying the supercell size from (2×2) to (4×4), corresponding to oxygen coverages of 0.25 to 0.0625 monolayers. The dissociation barrier at zero coverage was calculated to be 0.31 eV, rising to 0.67 eV at 0.25 ML coverage, indicating significant lateral repulsion between co-adsorbed oxygen atoms. Minimum energy paths were mapped with seven images per path and forces converged to below 0.03 eV/Å. Bader charge analysis showed that oxygen acquires approximately 0.9 electrons upon adsorption irrespective of coverage, while the Ru surface atoms directly beneath the adsorbate lose between 0.3 and 0.5 electrons depending on local geometry. Work function changes as a function of coverage were calculated and found to increase monotonically from 5.41 eV at clean Ru(0001) to 5.89 eV at 0.25 ML. These data are relevant for modelling Ru-based catalysts for ammonia synthesis and CO oxidation under oxygen-rich conditions.

title: Surface segregation in Pd–Cu alloys under adsorption conditions: an ab initio thermodynamics approach
abstract: The thermodynamic stability of Pd–Cu alloy surface compositions under reactive gas atmospheres was examined using ab initio thermodynamics combined with DFT-PBE total energy calculations. Six stoichiometries between pure Cu and pure Pd were studied on (111)-oriented four-layer slabs. Segregation free energies were computed as a function of CO and O chemical potentials, covering temperature ranges from 300 to 900 K and pressures from 10⁻¹⁰ to 10 bar. At low CO pressure and elevated temperature, Cu tends to segregate to the surface, lowering the surface energy by approximately 0.18 J/m². CO adsorption reverses this trend above a CO partial pressure of roughly 10⁻⁴ bar at 500 K, stabilising Pd-enriched surfaces. Adsorption energy maps across compositions showed a 0.4 eV spread in CO binding energy, bracketed by values on the two pure metals. The results suggest that the active surface composition of Pd–Cu catalysts under working conditions differs substantially from the bulk nominal composition and from composition measured ex situ.

title: First-principles study of N adsorption and diffusion on Fe(110) relevant to ammonia synthesis
abstract: Atomic nitrogen adsorption and surface diffusion on the Fe(110) surface were studied by DFT using the PBE functional and Grimme D3 dispersion corrections. Adsorption at long-bridge, short-bridge, and quasi-three-fold hollow sites was evaluated; the long-bridge site was found most stable with an adsorption energy of −5.29 eV, in good agreement with earlier experimental estimates. Diffusion pathways connecting neighbouring adsorption minima were mapped with CI-NEB: the minimum barrier for surface hopping was 0.72 eV, with a secondary path via the short-bridge site carrying a barrier of 0.91 eV. Subsurface penetration barriers were also computed; the barrier for N entering the first subsurface layer is 1.14 eV, consistent with the known resistance of Fe(110) to nitridation at moderate temperatures. A vibrational analysis using the finite displacement method yielded N–Fe stretch frequencies of 348 and 412 cm⁻¹ at the long-bridge site. These results refine the input parameters available for microkinetic modelling of ammonia synthesis on Fe-based catalysts.

title: Comparative adsorption energetics of formic acid decomposition intermediates on Pt, Pd and Ni (111) surfaces
abstract: The decomposition of formic acid (HCOOH) on three catalytically important (111) surfaces was studied using plane-wave DFT-PBE with van der Waals corrections. Intermediate species — HCOOH, HCOO*, COOH*, CO*, OH*, H* — were fully relaxed on each surface and adsorption energies as well as binding configurations were determined. On Pt(111) the HCOO* bidentate configuration was found to be the most stable intermediate with an adsorption energy of −2.67 eV, while on Ni(111) the same species bound more strongly at −3.11 eV, reflecting the higher d-band centre of Ni. Transition states between HCOO* decomposition to CO₂ + H* were located by CI-NEB; the corresponding barriers are 0.54, 0.61 and 0.46 eV on Pt, Pd, and Ni respectively. A microkinetic analysis using harmonic transition state theory at 400 K suggested that Ni exhibits the highest turnover frequency for CO₂ formation among the three metals but is also more susceptible to CO poisoning, as reflected in a CO adsorption energy of −1.97 eV compared to −1.63 eV on Pt.

title: DFT benchmarking of van der Waals functionals for small-molecule adsorption on transition-metal surfaces
abstract: A systematic comparison of twelve dispersion-corrected and non-local van der Waals density functionals was performed for the adsorption of CO, NO, CH₄, and C₂H₄ on Pt(111), Pd(111), Cu(111), and Ag(111). Reference adsorption energies were taken from a curated database of single-crystal calorimetry and thermal desorption measurements compiled from the literature. Mean absolute errors (MAE) relative to experiment were computed for each functional-surface-adsorbate combination. The optB86b-vdW functional yielded the lowest overall MAE of 0.11 eV across the test set, while PBE-D3(BJ) performed similarly at 0.13 eV. Standard PBE without dispersion showed an MAE of 0.21 eV, systematically underestimating binding on the coinage metals. For CH₄ on Ag(111) all tested functionals overestimated the adsorption energy by at least 0.06 eV, suggesting remaining deficiencies in describing physisorbed hydrocarbons. The benchmarking set and converged calculation parameters are made available as supplementary data to facilitate reproducibility. These results are intended as practical guidance for selecting functionals in computational heterogeneous catalysis studies.

title: Adsorption of sulfur-containing poisons on Ni(111) and its consequences for steam methane reforming activity: a first-principles study
abstract: Sulfur poisoning of nickel-based steam methane reforming catalysts was examined through DFT calculations of H₂S, SH*, and S* adsorption on Ni(111) and on Ni(111) surfaces pre-covered with 0.11, 0.25, and 0.44 ML of sulfur. H₂S adsorption at the top site is weak (−0.38 eV) and dissociation to SH* + H* is thermodynamically favoured by 0.82 eV. The subsequent SH* → S* + H* step has a reaction energy of −0.54 eV and a barrier of 0.28 eV. At 0.25 ML S coverage, CH₄ dissociation barriers — evaluated via CI-NEB — increase from 0.91 eV on clean Ni(111) to 1.38 eV, reflecting strong ensemble effects as well as electronic modification. Projected density of states showed a downshift of the Ni d-band centre by 0.19 eV at 0.25 ML S coverage. These findings are consistent with industrial observations of rapid activity loss at sulfur feed concentrations above a few ppm and provide atomistic parameters for kinetic models of catalyst deactivation.

title: Reaction pathway analysis for CO₂ hydrogenation to methanol on Cu/ZnO model surfaces using DFT and microkinetics
abstract: The CO₂ hydrogenation pathway to methanol was investigated on a Cu(111)/ZnO(0001) model system using DFT-PBE+D3 and microkinetic modelling. The interface between Cu and ZnO was constructed as a stepped Cu(211) slab partially decorated with Zn adatoms to mimic strong metal–support interaction conditions inferred from electron microscopy studies in the literature. Twenty-two elementary steps covering CO₂ adsorption, RWGS side reaction, formate and carboxyl pathways were considered. Transition states were located using CI-NEB with forces converged to 0.02 eV/Å. The formate pathway was found to be kinetically preferred, with the hydrogenation of HCOO* to H₂COO* being the rate-determining step carrying a barrier of 0.88 eV on the Zn-decorated surface versus 1.07 eV on clean Cu(211). Microkinetic simulations at 523 K and 50 bar yielded a methanol turnover frequency of 0.08 s⁻¹ per active site, within a factor of two of experimental rates reported for commercial catalysts. Sensitivity analysis identified the H₂COO* hydrogenation and CH₃O* dehydrogenation steps as having the highest degree of rate control.

title: Droplet-based extraction of heavy metal ions from water samples on a PDMS chip using tributyl phosphate as carrier
abstract: A PDMS flow-focusing device was adapted for liquid–liquid extraction of Cu²⁺ and Pb²⁺ ions from aqueous samples using a continuous organic phase of n-dodecane containing 5–15 vol% tributyl phosphate (TBP) as extractant. Aqueous feed concentrations ranged from 0.1 to 50 mg/L. Extraction efficiency, defined as the fraction of metal ions transferred to the organic droplet phase, reached 87 % for Cu²⁺ and 79 % for Pb²⁺ at 10 vol% TBP and a flow rate ratio of 10:1, with a residence time of approximately 4 s in a 4 cm serpentine channel. Comparison with batch extraction under the same concentration and TBP conditions showed equivalent efficiency at 30-fold lower sample volume (200 nL per droplet). Ion concentrations were quantified by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry on collected fractions. The device was tested on spiked tap water samples from the Novi Sad municipal network with satisfactory recovery.

title: Thermodynamic cost of sensing in active matter: information and dissipation at the single-particle level
abstract: Biological microswimmers such as bacteria perform chemotaxis by coupling their motility to chemical gradient sensing, a process that necessarily incurs a thermodynamic cost. We analyse this cost using a model in which a run-and-tumble particle modulates its tumbling rate based on a noisy estimate of a local attractant gradient. The sensing mechanism is described by a two-state receptor with methylation dynamics following the Berg–Purcell scheme. We derive exact expressions for the entropy production associated with the signalling network and the motility engine separately, and compute the total dissipation as a function of receptor gain and signal-to-noise ratio. At optimal receptor gain, the sensing subsystem contributes 20–35% of total dissipation for the parameter ranges examined. We find a trade-off: higher chemotactic drift velocity requires disproportionately higher dissipation, following a power law with exponent 1.6 ± 0.1 across three orders of magnitude in drift velocity. The results are compared with existing estimates for E. coli-like parameters and are broadly consistent.

title: Willingness to pay for locally produced food in Vojvodina
abstract: This study investigates consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) a premium for locally produced food products in the Vojvodina region of Serbia. Drawing on a combination of contingent valuation surveys and incentive-compatible choice experiments conducted with 412 adult respondents across Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin, the research identifies key sociodemographic and attitudinal drivers of WTP premiums. Results indicate that consumers are, on average, willing to pay 18–24 percent above standard retail prices for locally labelled fresh produce, with trust in local producers and perceived freshness emerging as the strongest predictors. Importantly, the study documents a substantial hypothetical bias, with stated WTP exceeding revealed WTP by approximately 30 percent, underscoring the need for calibration techniques in agricultural market research. The findings contribute to the broader behavioural economics literature on label effects and regional identity cues, and offer practical recommendations for local food producers, retailers, and regional development agencies seeking to strengthen short supply chains in the northern Serbian market.

title: Anchoring effects in online retail pricing: evidence from a controlled experiment
abstract: Anchoring is among the most robust and replicated phenomena in behavioural economics, yet its precise mechanisms in digital retail environments remain underexplored. This paper reports findings from a pre-registered online experiment with 538 participants recruited via a Serbian consumer panel, in which participants were exposed to varying anchor prices before evaluating a target product. Using a between-subjects design, we systematically varied anchor magnitude, anchor credibility, and the temporal gap between anchor exposure and price evaluation. Results confirm strong anchoring effects across all conditions, with high-credibility anchors producing significantly larger adjustments toward the anchor value. Crucially, time pressure attenuates adjustment away from implausible anchors, suggesting that cognitive load moderates the correction mechanism. The study extends dual-process models of price cognition and discusses implications for e-commerce platform design, dynamic pricing strategies, and consumer protection policy. Methodologically, the paper advocates for pre-registration and power analysis as standards for pricing experiments in consumer research.

title: Price fairness perceptions and purchase intentions in subscription-based services
abstract: Subscription pricing models have proliferated across digital and physical service markets, yet consumer perceptions of price fairness in these contexts have received limited empirical attention. This study integrates dual entitlement theory with prospect theory to develop and test a model of price fairness perception in subscription services. Survey data were collected from 601 Serbian consumers with active subscriptions in categories including streaming, software, and fitness services. Structural equation modelling reveals that perceived procedural fairness and price transparency are stronger determinants of continued subscription intention than the absolute price level itself. Loss aversion amplifies negative reactions to price increases, particularly among consumers who perceive the original price as a reference point rather than a market rate. The paper identifies meaningful differences across product categories and age cohorts. Findings offer actionable guidance for subscription-based businesses on how to communicate price changes in ways that minimise churn, and contribute theoretically to the literature on behavioural pricing and relational marketing.

title: Nudging healthy food choices in workplace canteens: a field experiment in Novi Sad
abstract: This paper presents results of a randomised field experiment testing the effectiveness of behavioural nudges in promoting healthier food choices in four workplace canteens in Novi Sad, Serbia. Building on choice architecture principles, we implemented three interventions—default healthy option placement, calorie salience labelling, and descriptive social norm messages—across a twelve-week study period involving approximately 1,100 employees. Sales data and brief intercept surveys were collected weekly. All three nudges significantly increased selection of nutritionally balanced meals relative to the control condition, with default placement producing the largest effect (23% increase in healthy meal uptake). Social norm messages were most effective among younger employees, while calorie labelling had greater impact among respondents with higher nutritional literacy. Interaction effects between nudge type and individual difference variables are modelled using multilevel regression. The findings contribute to applied behavioural economics in the Central and Eastern European context and carry direct implications for workplace wellness programmes and public health catering policy.

title: Measuring hypothetical bias in contingent valuation: a meta-analytic review
abstract: Hypothetical bias—the systematic overstatement of willingness to pay in stated preference surveys relative to actual payment—poses a fundamental validity threat to contingent valuation research. This paper presents a meta-analysis of 87 primary studies published between 2000 and 2022, covering diverse product categories including environmental goods, food products, and health services. Using random-effects modelling, we estimate an average hypothetical bias ratio of 2.6, with substantial heterogeneity explained by study design features such as payment vehicle, elicitation format, and the use of cheap-talk scripts. Pre-commitment mechanisms and certainty follow-up questions are found to be the most effective mitigation strategies, reducing bias by 38 and 29 percent respectively. The analysis also documents a publication bias toward larger bias estimates. Findings are synthesised into a practical decision framework for researchers designing willingness-to-pay studies, with particular attention to the needs of applied consumer research in emerging markets. The paper advances methodological rigour in behavioural economics survey methodology.

title: Loss aversion and promotional framing: how message valence shapes discount evaluation
abstract: Promotional messages are ubiquitous in consumer markets, yet the role of loss aversion in moderating responses to differently framed discounts is not fully understood. This paper investigates whether framing a price reduction as avoiding a loss ('you would pay X more without this offer') versus achieving a gain ('save X with this offer') produces differential evaluations of deal quality and purchase intentions. A series of three online experiments, conducted with Serbian adult consumers (total N = 892), manipulates framing, discount depth, and product involvement. Results consistently show a loss-frame advantage for purchase intentions when discount depth is moderate, but this advantage disappears for high-involvement products where deliberative processing overrides the affective loss aversion response. Mediation analysis indicates that perceived deal value mediates the framing–intention relationship, while need for cognition moderates it. The study contributes to the intersection of behavioural economics and promotional strategy, with implications for retail advertising and digital marketing copywriting.

title: Behavioural economics methods in marketing research: a practitioner's guide
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of behavioural economics methods as applied in marketing research contexts, targeting both academic researchers and practitioners who design market intelligence studies. The chapter covers the theoretical foundations of key concepts—bounded rationality, heuristics and biases, prospect theory, and choice architecture—before turning to a taxonomy of empirical methods including incentive-compatible experiments, conjoint analysis, eye-tracking protocols, and implicit association tests. Each method is evaluated for its suitability across research contexts such as new product pricing, brand perception, and promotional design. Special attention is given to the challenges of conducting behavioural research in Central and Eastern European market contexts, including sample recruitment, cultural moderators, and institutional review board requirements. The chapter concludes with a discussion of integrating behavioural insights into marketing decision-making processes within organisations, drawing on case examples developed from hypothetical company scenarios relevant to the regional innovation ecosystem.

title: Price sensitivity segmentation using latent class analysis: an application to organic cosmetics
abstract: Understanding heterogeneity in consumer price sensitivity is critical for effective market segmentation and targeted pricing strategy. This study applies latent class analysis to willingness-to-pay data collected through a contingent valuation survey among 523 consumers of organic cosmetic products in Serbia. Three distinct price sensitivity segments are identified: value seekers with low WTP and high elasticity, quality-conscious mainstream buyers with moderate WTP and strong label responsiveness, and premium adopters exhibiting inelastic demand driven by ethical and status motivations. Segment membership is predicted by age, income, environmental attitudes, and prior organic purchase experience. The paper demonstrates how latent class segmentation outperforms traditional a priori demographic segmentation in explaining WTP variance and in generating actionable pricing recommendations. Findings are directly applicable to small and medium-sized enterprises in the natural cosmetics sector seeking to optimise pricing tiers and communication strategies. The study contributes methodologically to the application of finite mixture models in consumer research.

title: Preparation and physicochemical characterisation of solid lipid nanoparticles loaded with ketoprofen for topical application
abstract: Solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) containing ketoprofen were prepared by hot high-pressure homogenisation using glyceryl monostearate as the lipid matrix and polysorbate 80 as the stabiliser. A three-factor, two-level full factorial design was applied to evaluate the influence of lipid concentration (5% and 10% w/w), surfactant concentration (1% and 2% w/w), and homogenisation cycles (3 and 5) on particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), and zeta potential. Particle sizes ranged from 168 to 312 nm, PDI values from 0.18 to 0.38, and zeta potential from −22 to −34 mV across all formulations. The optimised SLN formulation showed a mean diameter of 193 nm, PDI of 0.21, and zeta potential of −30 mV. Encapsulation efficiency was determined by ultrafiltration–centrifugation and reached 78.4 ± 3.1%. Differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray powder diffraction confirmed partial crystallinity of the lipid matrix, consistent with drug entrapment. Storage stability was assessed over 90 days at 4 °C and 25 °C; formulations stored at 4 °C showed no significant change in particle size, while those at 25 °C exhibited a 15% increase in mean diameter by day 60.

title: In vitro skin permeation of ibuprofen from SLN-based gels compared with a conventional emulsion gel
abstract: Franz diffusion cells with excised porcine ear skin were used to compare the permeation of ibuprofen from two SLN-based hydrogel formulations (carbopol 940 gel base, 0.5% w/w) with a commercially available ibuprofen emulsion gel (50 mg/g). SLN formulations were prepared by hot melt emulsification using beeswax and hydrogenated palm oil as the lipid phase. Ibuprofen concentrations in receptor fluid (phosphate buffer pH 7.4 with 30% polyethylene glycol 400) were quantified by reverse-phase HPLC at 221 nm over 24 hours. The cumulative amount of drug permeated per unit area at 24 h was 38.6 ± 4.2 µg/cm² for SLN gel 1, 51.3 ± 5.8 µg/cm² for SLN gel 2, and 67.4 ± 6.1 µg/cm² for the reference emulsion. Tape stripping experiments indicated that both SLN formulations deposited approximately 2.4-fold more ibuprofen within the stratum corneum compared with the emulsion gel, suggesting a depot effect. The results indicate that SLNs may favour local tissue retention over systemic permeation, which is desirable for anti-inflammatory dermal therapy.

title: Effect of lipid matrix composition on the polymorphic behaviour and drug release kinetics of diclofenac-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles
abstract: Diclofenac sodium was incorporated into SLNs prepared from binary lipid mixtures of glyceryl behenate and caprylocaproyl macrogolglycerides at ratios of 9:1, 7:3, and 5:5 (w/w). Nanoparticles were characterised by dynamic light scattering, DSC, and synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) performed at the ELETTRA facility in Trieste, Italy. SAXS data revealed that the 9:1 ratio retained a predominantly β-polymorph structure, while higher proportions of the liquid lipid fraction led to mixed β'/α phases. In vitro drug release was assessed in pH 5.5 acetate buffer containing 0.5% Tween 80 at 32 °C using the dialysis bag method. Release profiles fitted best to the Higuchi model for all formulations (r² = 0.94–0.98). The 7:3 binary mixture exhibited the slowest release rate (k = 4.8 µg·cm⁻²·h⁻⁰·⁵) alongside the highest encapsulation efficiency (84.2 ± 2.6%), likely due to the formation of an ordered yet imperfect crystal lattice accommodating the drug. These findings demonstrate that controlled adjustment of lipid polarity ratio is a practical approach to modulating drug release from SLNs.

title: Nanostructured lipid carriers versus solid lipid nanoparticles for dermal delivery of naproxen: stability and skin uptake comparison
abstract: Naproxen-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) and SLNs were prepared by hot high-pressure homogenisation and compared with respect to long-term physical stability and ex vivo skin uptake. NLCs were formulated with a 7:3 solid-to-liquid lipid ratio (cetyl palmitate:isopropyl myristate), while SLNs used pure cetyl palmitate as the matrix. Both systems were characterised monthly over six months stored at 25 °C/60% RH. SLNs showed a statistically significant increase in mean particle size from 210 to 278 nm (p < 0.05) and an increase in PDI from 0.22 to 0.41 over six months, whereas NLCs remained stable (198 ± 9 nm, PDI 0.24 ± 0.03). Ex vivo skin uptake using porcine ear skin demonstrated that NLCs delivered 1.9-fold more naproxen into the viable epidermis than SLNs after 12 h. Confocal laser scanning microscopy using a rhodamine B-labelled lipid tracer confirmed deeper penetration of NLC particles into skin appendages. Encapsulation efficiency of NLCs (88.7%) exceeded that of SLNs (74.3%), attributed to reduced drug expulsion during lipid recrystallisation in the disordered NLC matrix.

title: Influence of preparation technique and lipid type on mean particle size and zeta potential of piroxicam-loaded SLNs: a comparative study
abstract: Four preparation methods—hot high-pressure homogenisation (HHPH), cold high-pressure homogenisation (CHPH), solvent injection, and microemulsion dilution—were evaluated for producing piroxicam-loaded SLNs using three lipid matrices: glyceryl monostearate, compritol 888 ATO, and carnauba wax. A total of 12 formulation combinations were characterised by DLS, electrophoretic mobility measurement, and transmission electron microscopy. HHPH yielded the smallest particles across all lipid types (mean 154–221 nm), while microemulsion dilution produced the largest (298–415 nm). Compritol-based SLNs prepared by HHPH showed the lowest PDI (0.19 ± 0.03) and highest absolute zeta potential (−36.2 ± 2.1 mV). Encapsulation efficiency ranged from 55.2% (carnauba wax, solvent injection) to 82.7% (compritol, HHPH). TEM images confirmed spherical morphology for HHPH-prepared samples and irregular shapes for microemulsion-diluted samples. The data suggest that HHPH combined with compritol 888 ATO provides the most reproducible and stable SLN platform for hydrophobic anti-inflammatory drugs with log P values between 1.5 and 3.5.

title: Anti-inflammatory activity of celecoxib-loaded SLNs in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages
abstract: Celecoxib was encapsulated in compritol 888 ATO-based SLNs and evaluated for COX-2 inhibitory activity in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. SLNs had a mean diameter of 187 ± 11 nm, PDI of 0.23, zeta potential of −28.4 mV, and encapsulation efficiency of 86.3 ± 1.9%. Cytotoxicity was assessed by MTT assay at concentrations from 0.1 to 100 µM celecoxib equivalent; no significant reduction in cell viability was observed up to 50 µM for either free drug or SLN formulation. COX-2 protein expression was determined by Western blotting after 18 h LPS stimulation (1 µg/mL). Prostaglandin E₂ (PGE₂) levels in cell supernatants were measured by ELISA. SLN-encapsulated celecoxib reduced PGE₂ by 71.3 ± 4.8% at 10 µM compared with 58.9 ± 5.2% for free celecoxib at the same concentration, indicating moderately enhanced activity. The difference was statistically significant (p < 0.05) and is attributed to improved intracellular uptake of SLNs through endocytic pathways. Unloaded blank SLNs did not significantly alter PGE₂ levels relative to the LPS control.

title: Scaling from laboratory to pilot-scale production of SLNs: influence of homogenisation pressure and cycle number on particle characteristics
abstract: Laboratory-scale SLN batches (50 mL) loaded with flurbiprofen were prepared at three homogenisation pressures (500, 800, and 1000 bar) and two cycle numbers (3 and 6) using a microfluidiser. Scale-up to pilot scale (500 mL) was performed maintaining the same pressure–cycle combinations. At laboratory scale, increasing pressure from 500 to 1000 bar at 3 cycles reduced mean particle size from 295 to 171 nm; additional cycles provided marginal further size reduction. At pilot scale, equivalent pressures yielded sizes 12–18% larger than corresponding laboratory batches, with increased PDI (0.27–0.39 versus 0.19–0.28). Encapsulation efficiency was reproducible across scales (76–83%), suggesting that drug distribution within the lipid matrix was not significantly affected by volume. Thermal analysis showed no change in crystallisation enthalpy between scales. The results indicate that maintaining pressure is more critical than cycle number during scale-up, and that a 1000 bar / 6-cycle protocol yields the closest match between laboratory and pilot batches in terms of particle size distribution.

title: SLN-enriched hydrogels for dermal delivery of indomethacin: rheological characterisation and in vitro–ex vivo correlation
abstract: Indomethacin-loaded SLNs (mean diameter 204 nm, PDI 0.24, EE 80.1%) were incorporated at concentrations of 5%, 10%, and 15% (w/w) into carbopol 974P and hydroxyethylcellulose gel bases at two polymer concentrations each, yielding twelve gel formulations. Rheological characterisation using an oscillatory rheometer revealed viscoelastic gel behaviour in all formulations; incorporation of SLNs at 15% w/w reduced gel rigidity by approximately 20% compared with drug-free gels of the same polymer concentration. In vitro drug release through synthetic cellulose acetate membranes (12–14 kDa MWCO) was compared with ex vivo permeation through porcine ear skin. Carbopol-based gels with 10% SLNs provided the best correlation between in vitro release (Higuchi, r² = 0.97) and ex vivo permeation data (r² = 0.93, slope 0.81). Skin flux was 3.2 ± 0.4 µg·cm⁻²·h⁻¹ for the optimised carbopol formulation versus 1.8 ± 0.3 µg·cm⁻²·h⁻¹ for the HEC equivalent. Tape-strip analysis confirmed preferential indomethacin accumulation in the upper stratum corneum layers for both gel types.

title: Quality by design approach to optimising mefenamic acid SLN formulations using Box-Behnken design and desirability functions
abstract: A Quality by Design (QbD) framework was applied to develop mefenamic acid-loaded SLNs. Critical material attributes (lipid type: compritol vs. precirol; drug loading: 2%, 4%, 6% w/w) and critical process parameters (homogenisation pressure: 600–1000 bar; homogenisation temperature: 70, 80, 90 °C) were screened using Plackett-Burman design. Homogenisation pressure, temperature, and drug loading were identified as significant factors and included in a Box-Behnken design with particle size, PDI, and encapsulation efficiency as responses. Desirability function optimisation identified a formulation with compritol, 4% drug loading, 900 bar, and 80 °C as optimal (predicted: 178 nm, PDI 0.20, EE 85.5%; observed: 181 ± 8 nm, PDI 0.21 ± 0.02, EE 84.9 ± 1.7%). Accelerated stability testing (40 °C/75% RH, 3 months) demonstrated acceptable physical stability with size increase below 10% and PDI remaining below 0.30. The QbD model showed good predictive power (R² > 0.92 for all responses), supporting its use in guiding formulation development before full experimental campaigns.

title: Freeze-drying of SLNs loaded with ketoprofen: effect of cryoprotectant type and concentration on redispersibility and long-term storage stability
abstract: The feasibility of lyophilising ketoprofen-loaded SLNs was investigated using four cryoprotectants—trehalose, sucrose, mannitol, and polyvinylpyrrolidone K30—at concentrations of 5%, 10%, and 15% w/w. Pre-lyophilisation SLNs had a mean diameter of 196 nm, PDI 0.21, and zeta potential of −29 mV. After reconstitution in deionised water, formulations with 10% trehalose showed the best redispersibility, recovering 97.3% of original particle size and PDI values below 0.25. Mannitol at all concentrations produced agglomerates with mean diameters exceeding 800 nm after reconstitution. Residual moisture content of lyophilised cakes was determined by Karl Fischer titration and ranged from 0.8 to 2.4%; trehalose-containing formulations showed the lowest values (0.8–1.1%). Physical stability of lyophilised formulations stored at 25 °C in amber glass vials was assessed over 12 months; trehalose-protected SLNs showed no significant change in particle size or drug content. In vitro release profiles of reconstituted SLNs matched those of the original liquid dispersion within experimental error, confirming preservation of the nanoparticulate structure through the freeze-drying cycle.

title: Pharmacogenomics of antidepressants in the Serbian population: a review and clinical guidance framework
abstract: This book chapter synthesises approximately fifteen years of pharmacogenomic research on CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 conducted primarily in Vojvodina and Serbia. The review covers allele frequency data, phenotype prevalence, and clinical pharmacokinetic studies of the principal antidepressant substrates: tricyclic antidepressants (nortriptyline, amitriptyline), SSRIs (escitalopram, sertraline, fluoxetine), and the SNRI venlafaxine. For each drug–gene pair the available evidence is graded using a simplified adaptation of the Clinical Pharmacogenomics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) framework. The chapter proposes a practical clinical guidance table for prescribers working in Serbian psychiatric practice, indicating where pre-treatment genotyping is likely to affect dosing decisions. Limitations discussed include the persistent under-representation of ethnic minority populations resident in Vojvodina (Romani, Hungarian) in existing pharmacogenomic cohorts, and the absence of prospective randomised trials demonstrating that genotype-guided prescribing reduces adverse events in this population.

title: Effect of flux composition on the morphology of Fe–Zn layers formed during batch galvanizing of medium-silicon steel
abstract: Fluxing pre-treatment is a critical step in batch hot-dip galvanizing, and its chemistry directly influences zinc–iron reaction behaviour. This study compared four flux formulations based on zinc ammonium chloride (ZnCl2·xNH4Cl) with varying molar ratios (1:1 to 1:4) applied to a medium-silicon steel (Si = 0.15 wt.%) before immersion in a zinc bath at 450 °C. After galvanizing, cross-sections were examined by SEM-EDS to characterise intermetallic layer morphology and elemental distribution. Fluxes with higher NH4Cl content produced smoother zeta–delta transitions and reduced outburst formation associated with the reactive Sandelin regime. Total coating thickness ranged from 180 µm to 310 µm depending on flux composition. The results suggest that flux chemistry modulates the initial iron dissolution rate, indirectly controlling nucleation of the gamma and delta phases. Practical guidelines for flux bath maintenance in industrial batch plants are discussed.

title: CALPHAD-based assessment of the Fe–Zn–Si ternary system relevant to reactive galvanizing
abstract: The Fe–Zn–Si ternary phase diagram was assessed using the CALPHAD method with thermodynamic data from binary sub-systems taken from critically reviewed literature. Gibbs energy functions for the relevant intermetallic phases (gamma, delta, zeta) were re-optimised to reproduce experimental liquidus and solidus data and known phase boundaries. The assessed database was used to calculate isothermal sections at 440 °C, 450 °C, and 460 °C, covering the composition ranges encountered in industrial batch galvanizing baths. Calculated phase stabilities in the silicon-reactive range (0.05–0.12 wt.% Si in steel) show that silicon partitioning into the delta phase lowers its stability window, consistent with experimental observations of anomalous coating growth. Predicted phase fractions at selected compositions were compared to XRD quantitative analysis results from laboratory-galvanized specimens, showing agreement within 5–8 relative percent. The database is made available as a supplementary file for use in diffusion simulation software.

title: Sandelin silicon effect revisited: quantitative mapping of coating mass in the silicon range 0–0.35 wt.%
abstract: A systematic experimental study was conducted in which eighteen structural steel grades with silicon contents from 0.005 to 0.35 wt.% were batch-galvanized under identical conditions (450 °C bath, 5-minute immersion, standard ZnCl2·2NH4Cl flux). Coating mass was determined by gravimetry before and after acid stripping, and coating thickness was measured metallographically at ten locations per specimen. The characteristic Sandelin peak near 0.07 wt.% Si was reproducibly observed with a coating mass of 870 ± 40 g/m², approximately 3.5 times greater than coatings on near-zero silicon steel. A secondary Sebisty peak near 0.22 wt.% Si was also confirmed at 620 g/m². Microstructural analysis showed that the Sandelin regime is associated with complete consumption of the delta layer and an unusually thick, porous zeta layer. Statistical analysis indicates that even minor batch-to-batch variation in Si content near the Sandelin peak (±0.01 wt.%) produces 15–20% variation in coating mass.

title: Influence of bismuth and tin additions to the zinc bath on Fe–Zn reaction rate in batch galvanizing
abstract: The effect of small alloying additions to the zinc bath (0.05–0.15 wt.% Bi, 0.05–0.15 wt.% Sn) on Fe–Zn reaction kinetics was studied using a laboratory-scale galvanizing bath. Steels with three silicon levels (0.02, 0.08, and 0.20 wt.% Si) were galvanized at 450 °C for immersion times of 1–10 minutes. Coating thickness and layer sequence were characterised by SEM cross-sections. Bismuth additions up to 0.10 wt.% had no measurable effect on total coating thickness for low-silicon steel but reduced the peak coating thickness in the Sandelin regime by approximately 12% relative to a pure zinc bath. Tin additions at 0.10 wt.% showed a more pronounced suppressive effect on Sandelin-range growth, reducing the zeta layer fraction by 18%. Possible mechanisms related to tin adsorption at the delta–zeta interface are discussed in the context of available surface energy data.

title: Temperature dependence of flux bath aging and its effect on galvanizing quality
abstract: Flux baths in batch galvanizing plants gradually accumulate iron from steel surface dissolution, shifting the ZnCl2/NH4Cl molar ratio and reducing fluxing effectiveness. This study followed the chemical evolution of a laboratory flux bath (initial composition: 450 g/L ZnCl2·2NH4Cl) over 60 galvanizing cycles at 60 °C and 70 °C bath temperatures. Iron concentration in the flux was monitored by atomic absorption spectroscopy at regular intervals. At 70 °C, the iron content reached the critical 8 g/L threshold after 38 cycles versus 52 cycles at 60 °C. Specimens galvanized with aged flux showed a progressive increase in bare-spot defect frequency as measured by a standardised area-fraction method on cross-sections. Correlations between flux iron content, ZnCl2/NH4Cl ratio, and coating defect frequency are presented. A simple predictive model for flux bath service life based on the number of processed steel surface area units is proposed.

title: Diffusion modelling of the Fe–Zn intermetallic layer sequence using DICTRA software: comparison with experimental data for Si-bearing steels
abstract: Diffusion simulations of Fe–Zn intermetallic layer growth were performed using DICTRA software coupled with a re-assessed Fe–Zn–Si thermodynamic database. Simulations were run at 450 °C for immersion times from 30 seconds to 15 minutes for steel compositions with 0.01, 0.07, and 0.20 wt.% Si. Simulated layer thickness profiles for gamma, delta, and zeta phases were compared to metallographically measured values from laboratory-galvanized specimens. For low-silicon steel, agreement between simulation and experiment was within 10% for all phases. For 0.07 wt.% Si (Sandelin regime), the simulation underestimated total coating thickness by 35–45%, indicating that the purely diffusional model cannot capture the accelerated dissolution mechanism operating in this regime. Modifications to the model incorporating a silicon-dependent interface mobility parameter are proposed and their effect on simulation output is assessed. The work establishes limits of applicability of current CALPHAD-coupled diffusion models for reactive galvanizing.

title: Effect of steel surface roughness on intermetallic layer morphology and adhesion in batch hot-dip galvanizing
abstract: Surface preparation prior to galvanizing typically includes acid pickling, but residual surface roughness depends on the pickling parameters and original steel surface condition. This study used eleven steel panels with controlled average roughness values (Ra) from 0.4 µm to 8.2 µm, prepared by mechanical grinding and acid etching, and galvanized at 450 °C for 4 minutes. Total coating thickness, intermetallic layer sequence, and adhesion (measured by a standardised bend-and-peel test) were characterised. Ra values above 4 µm were associated with irregular gamma layer nucleation and localised zeta outgrowths, increasing coating thickness variance by a factor of 2.3. Adhesion scores (rated 1–5) did not differ significantly between smooth and moderately rough surfaces (Ra < 4 µm) but dropped sharply at Ra > 6 µm. The results have direct relevance to the selection of pickling conditions for heavily corroded structural steel.

title: Thermogravimetric study of zinc evaporation losses from batch galvanizing baths containing lead-free additive elements
abstract: The phase-out of lead as a bath additive in batch galvanizing has driven interest in alternative elements (Bi, Sn, Ni) to maintain bath fluidity and drainage. This study used thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) to measure evaporative zinc losses from molten zinc alloy samples containing 0.05–0.20 wt.% of each element at temperatures from 440 °C to 500 °C over 4-hour isothermal holds. Mass loss rates (mg/cm²·h) were calculated from continuous weight recordings. Bi-containing alloys showed zinc evaporation rates 6–9% higher than pure zinc at 460 °C, attributed to reduction in Zn surface activity by Bi surface segregation being less effective than Pb. Ni additions showed no statistically significant effect on evaporation rates within the studied range. The data provide practical input for assessing zinc consumption differences when switching from Pb-containing to lead-free bath formulations.

title: Fe–Zn reaction layer characterisation on recycled steel with elevated residual element content
abstract: Structural steel produced from electric arc furnace scrap often contains elevated levels of Cu, Ni, Cr, and Sn as residual elements. This study examined eight industrial steel heats with total residual element contents from 0.10 to 0.48 wt.% and silicon contents in the low range (0.02–0.06 wt.%). All heats were galvanized under identical conditions (450 °C, 3-minute immersion) and coating cross-sections were analysed by SEM-EDS and electron probe microanalysis (EPMA). Ni concentrations up to 0.04 wt.% were detected in the gamma phase by EPMA, while Cu and Sn were not measurably incorporated. Heats with Cu + Sn > 0.15 wt.% showed a 12–18% reduction in total coating thickness compared to low-residual reference steels, suggesting a mild inhibitory effect. No adverse effects on coating adhesion were observed by bend testing. The findings are relevant for galvanizers processing steel from diverse scrap sources.

title: Validation of a laboratory-scale galvanizing bath as a surrogate for industrial conditions: thermal profile, bath chemistry, and coating reproducibility
abstract: Laboratory-scale galvanizing setups are widely used in research but their representativeness of industrial conditions is rarely quantified. This paper presents a full validation study of the laboratory bath used at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad (capacity: 8 litres, resistive heating, Ar atmosphere). Thermal profiles during immersion of steel specimens (dimensions: 100 × 50 × 5 mm) were recorded with embedded K-type thermocouples. Temperature recovery after specimen immersion was complete within 35 ± 4 seconds for a 450 °C set point, comparable to published data for industrial baths with large thermal mass. Bath chemistry (Fe content, Al content) was monitored throughout 120 galvanizing cycles and remained within industrial tolerance limits with periodic dross removal. Coating thickness distributions from the laboratory bath were statistically compared to measurements from three Serbian galvanizing plants, showing no significant difference in mean values at the 95% confidence level but higher variance in the laboratory setting. Correction factors for immersion time are proposed.

title: Kinetics of iron dissolution into the zinc bath during the initial seconds of batch galvanizing: an interrupted immersion study
abstract: The earliest stages of Fe–Zn reaction determine the nucleation sequence of intermetallic phases and are poorly characterised because conventional specimen cross-sectioning is difficult at immersion times below 30 seconds. This study used an interrupted immersion technique with rapid withdrawal and water quench to produce specimens at 3, 6, 10, 20, 30, 60, 120, and 300 seconds at 450 °C. Ion dissolution rates were estimated from iron concentration increases in the zinc bath (measured by ICP-OES) and from gravimetric mass loss of the steel substrate. SEM-EBSD was used to identify phase crystallography in cross-sections of specimens galvanized for 3–20 seconds. The gamma phase was detected as the first identifiable layer at 6 seconds, followed by delta at 10 seconds and zeta at 20 seconds. A peak in iron dissolution rate was observed between 6 and 20 seconds, corresponding to the period before the continuous zeta layer forms a diffusion barrier. Implications for the onset of the Sandelin effect are discussed.
