title: Effect of pre-galvanizing annealing on intermetallic layer growth in structural steels with silicon content near the Sandelin peak
abstract: Steels with silicon in the range 0.06–0.09 wt.% are particularly problematic in batch galvanizing due to the Sandelin effect. This study examined whether a low-temperature pre-annealing treatment (200–400 °C for 1–4 hours in air) applied before galvanizing could modify the steel surface layer sufficiently to reduce reactive growth. Six steel grades with Si in the Sandelin range were treated under twelve annealing conditions and galvanized at 450 °C for 5 minutes. Coating thickness, morphology, and silicon distribution near the steel surface were measured. Pre-annealing at 350 °C for 2 hours reduced average coating thickness by 14–22% relative to untreated control specimens, with a corresponding decrease in zeta layer porosity. XPS depth profiles confirmed the formation of a thin amorphous silicon-rich oxide layer (2–5 nm) on the steel surface after annealing, which appears to moderate the initial iron dissolution rate. The treatment is assessed for practical feasibility in an industrial context.

title: Long-term corrosion performance of batch-galvanized coatings on Sandelin-range silicon steels in a chloride-containing atmosphere
abstract: The corrosion performance of unusually thick intermetallic-rich coatings produced on Sandelin-range silicon steels has not been studied as systematically as that of normal coatings. This study exposed galvanized specimens with four coating types (normal thickness ~80 µm, Sandelin-thick ~270 µm, Sebisty-range ~170 µm, and a reference hot-dip galvanized batch with zinc-rich top layer) to a prohesion cyclic salt spray test (ASTM G85 Annex A5) and a real outdoor exposure station in Novi Sad for 36 months. Zinc consumption rates were measured gravimetrically at 6-month intervals. Sandelin coatings, although thicker, showed 28% higher zinc consumption rates per unit surface than normal coatings, attributed to their higher porosity and the lower corrosion resistance of the Fe-rich zeta phase relative to pure zinc. Real outdoor exposures confirmed the accelerated rate, though absolute coating lifetimes remained long (>60 years estimated by linear extrapolation) for all types. Phase distribution in remaining coating cross-sections after 36 months was characterised by SEM-EDS.

title: Hardness distribution and tensile properties of friction stir welded AA6082-T6/AA5083-H111 butt joints at varying tool rotation speeds
abstract: Dissimilar butt joints between AA6082-T6 and AA5083-H111 plates (4 mm thickness) were produced by friction stir welding at tool rotation speeds of 600, 800, 1000, and 1200 rpm with a constant traverse speed of 100 mm/min. A threaded cylindrical pin tool with a shoulder diameter of 18 mm was used throughout. Vickers microhardness mapping on cross-sections revealed a pronounced softening zone in the heat-affected area on the AA6082 side at all conditions, with minimum hardness values dropping to 68–74 HV compared to 105 HV in the base material. Ultimate tensile strength ranged from 241 MPa at 600 rpm to 268 MPa at 1000 rpm, representing 78–87% joint efficiency relative to the weaker base alloy. Optical metallography showed consistent grain refinement in the nugget, with average grain sizes between 4.1 and 7.8 µm. Wormhole defects were observed at 600 rpm on the advancing side, confirmed by cross-sectional etching. Results indicate that 1000 rpm provides the best combination of defect-free microstructure and mechanical performance for this alloy combination under the tested conditions.

title: Language Attitudes Toward Romani Among Serbian Adolescents in Mixed-Ethnicity Schools in Novi Sad
abstract: This study examines the attitudes of 94 Serbian-dominant adolescents (aged 14–18) toward Romani as spoken in their schools and neighbourhoods in Novi Sad. Data were collected through a matched-guise experiment using audio recordings of eight speakers—four Serbian-dominant, four Romani-dominant—reading the same neutral text. Participants rated speakers on scales of solidarity, prestige, and competence. Results indicate a consistent prestige disadvantage for Romani-accented speech, with mean prestige scores approximately 1.4 points lower on a 7-point Likert scale than Serbian-accented equivalents. Solidarity ratings were more varied, with female participants assigning higher solidarity scores to Romani-accented speakers than male participants. Qualitative follow-up interviews with a subsample of 18 participants revealed recurring associations between Romani speech and spatial stigma tied to specific peripheral neighbourhoods. The paper contextualises findings within broader research on language stigmatisation in post-Yugoslav urban settings and discusses implications for inclusive language education.

title: Between Two Codes: Identity Positioning in the Narrative Accounts of Serbian–Romani Bilingual Youth
abstract: Drawing on narrative analysis of sociolinguistic interviews with 31 Serbian–Romani bilingual adolescents (aged 13–19) from two peri-urban settlements outside Novi Sad, this paper investigates how speakers position themselves relative to Serbian-dominant peers and older members of their Romani-speaking communities. Interviews averaged 45 minutes and were transcribed and coded using MAXQDA 22. Three recurring positioning strategies were identified: language concealment in school contexts, selective code-switching as an in-group solidarity marker among peers, and appeals to heritage language competence as a source of status within the family. Notably, 19 of 31 participants reported deliberately suppressing Romani in formal school settings, while 24 reported regular code-switching in peer interactions. The analysis draws on Davies and Harré's positioning theory and Woolard's concept of simultaneity to interpret these patterns. Findings suggest that institutional language norms exert a stronger homogenising pressure than peer-group practices in this population.

title: Schoolyard Repertoires: Peer-Group Language Practices Among Serbian–Romani Adolescents Across Three Urban Schools
abstract: This ethnographically informed study tracked peer-group language practices among 58 Serbian–Romani bilingual adolescents across three mixed-ethnicity primary schools in Novi Sad over a seven-month observation period. Observation notes, audio recordings of informal interaction (totalling approximately 34 hours), and short elicitation tasks were combined to document the distribution of Serbian, Romani, and mixed-code utterances across spatial settings within the school—classrooms, corridors, the canteen, and the schoolyard. Romani and mixed-code speech was almost entirely absent from classrooms (less than 3% of coded utterances) but constituted 41% of utterances in the schoolyard among participants who self-identified as Romani-dominant. Cluster analysis of speaker networks revealed that high-density peer clusters with more than 60% Romani-heritage membership showed significantly higher rates of in-group Romani use than looser, ethnically mixed clusters. The paper contributes to understanding how architectural and institutional spaces structure minority language use among young urban bilinguals.

title: Irony Detection in Serbian Sports Journalism: Annotation Scheme and Baseline Experiments
abstract: Irony represents a persistent source of misclassification in Serbian sentiment analysis systems. This paper introduces an annotation scheme for irony detection tailored to Serbian sports journalism and applies it to a 28,000-sentence corpus drawn from match reports and post-match commentary published between 2018 and 2022. Two annotators labelled sentences as ironic or non-ironic using a protocol with four irony subtypes: propositional, interpersonal, situational, and self-deprecatory. Cohen's kappa reached 0.72 overall and 0.58 on the interpersonal subtype, which was the most contested. Baseline classification experiments using a fine-tuned Serbian RoBERTa model achieve 68.1% F1 on ironic sentences and 91.4% on non-ironic sentences, confirming the class-imbalance difficulty (7.3% ironic). The paper publishes the annotation guidelines and 3,000 labelled sentences as an open resource and discusses which linguistic cues proved most reliable during annotation.

title: Mechanochemical synthesis of hydroxyapatite from calcium hydrogen phosphate and calcium carbonate: effect of milling time on phase composition
abstract: Hydroxyapatite (HA) powder was synthesised by dry mechanochemical milling of CaHPO4 and CaCO3 in a planetary ball mill at 300 rpm. Milling durations of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 hours were investigated. X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed complete conversion to HA after 8 hours, with residual CaO below 0.5 wt% at 16 hours as determined by Rietveld refinement. Crystallite size, estimated by the Scherrer equation, decreased from 48 nm at 1 hour to 22 nm at 16 hours. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) confirmed the presence of characteristic phosphate and hydroxyl bands. Scanning electron microscopy showed agglomerates of 1–3 µm formed from primary particles below 100 nm. The Ca/P molar ratio measured by ICP-OES was 1.67 ± 0.02 across all samples milled beyond 4 hours, consistent with stoichiometric HA. Milling beyond 16 hours introduced iron contamination from the steel vial exceeding 200 ppm, suggesting an upper time limit for this process configuration.

title: Influence of bioglass content on the sintering behaviour and phase stability of hydroxyapatite–bioglass composites
abstract: Composites of hydroxyapatite (HA) with 45S5-type bioglass (BG) at 0, 5, 10, 20, and 30 wt% BG were prepared by wet mixing of mechanochemically synthesised HA powder with melt-quenched BG powder, followed by uniaxial pressing and conventional sintering at 1000–1200 °C. XRD analysis after sintering at 1100 °C revealed partial decomposition of HA to tricalcium phosphate (TCP) in samples containing more than 10 wt% BG, attributed to reaction with SiO2. Relative densities ranged from 88% for pure HA to 95% for the 10 wt% BG composite. Compressive strength peaked at 112 MPa for the 10 wt% BG sample sintered at 1100 °C. Higher BG contents promoted secondary crystallisation of wollastonite, confirmed by XRD and FTIR. Results indicate that BG content must be kept below 15 wt% to preserve phase integrity under conventional sintering conditions above 1050 °C.

title: Spark plasma sintering of mechanochemically derived hydroxyapatite: densification kinetics and microstructure
abstract: Mechanochemically synthesised hydroxyapatite powder was densified by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at temperatures between 800 and 1050 °C, with a uniaxial pressure of 50 MPa and dwell times of 5, 10, and 15 minutes. Relative density reached 99.1% at 950 °C with a 10-minute dwell, compared with 93% achieved by conventional sintering under equivalent thermal conditions. XRD showed no detectable decomposition to TCP or CaO up to 1000 °C in SPS, in contrast to conventional sintering where TCP appeared above 1050 °C. Vickers hardness of 6.8 GPa was measured for the 950 °C / 10-minute sample. Grain size by EBSD was 0.4 ± 0.1 µm, substantially finer than conventionally sintered counterparts at 1.8 µm. Shrinkage rate curves obtained from SPS displacement data indicated two distinct densification events at approximately 700 °C and 880 °C, tentatively attributed to grain boundary diffusion and lattice diffusion respectively.

title: In-vitro dissolution of hydroxyapatite–bioglass composites in simulated body fluid: ion release and surface layer formation
abstract: Disk-shaped samples of HA and HA–10 wt% BG composites sintered by SPS at 950 °C were immersed in Kokubo simulated body fluid (SBF) at 37 °C for periods of 1, 3, 7, 14, and 28 days. Calcium and phosphate ion concentrations in solution were monitored by ICP-OES, and pH was measured daily. The HA–BG composite released 18% more Ca²⁺ at day 7 compared with pure HA disks of equivalent surface area. Silicon was detected in solution from BG-containing samples at a concentration of 2.1 mg/L at day 14, stabilising thereafter. SEM-EDS on specimen surfaces after 28 days showed formation of a carbonated apatite-like surface layer approximately 3 µm thick on the composite but less than 0.5 µm on pure HA. XRD of retrieved surfaces confirmed the layer was poorly crystalline. Mass loss of HA–BG composites over 28 days was 1.4 ± 0.2%, compared with 0.6 ± 0.1% for pure HA.

title: Compressive strength and porosity of SPS-densified HA–BG scaffolds as a function of sacrificial pore former content
abstract: Open porosity in spark plasma sintered HA–10 wt% BG compacts was introduced by adding 0, 10, 20, and 30 vol% PMMA microspheres (diameter 50–80 µm) before compaction. After SPS at 950 °C, PMMA was pyrolysed by a subsequent heat treatment at 500 °C for 2 hours in air. Mercury intrusion porosimetry showed that total open porosity increased from 1.2% (no pore former) to 28.6% (30 vol% PMMA). Pore diameters were predominantly in the range 40–90 µm, suitable for osteoconduction according to published criteria. Compressive strength fell from 102 MPa at 1.2% porosity to 24 MPa at 28.6% porosity, following a power-law relationship with an exponent of 2.1. The 20 vol% PMMA sample (22% porosity, 38 MPa) was identified as the composition offering the best compromise between mechanical integrity and interconnected pore volume for trabecular bone replacement.

title: Effect of strontium substitution on crystallographic parameters and dissolution rate of mechanochemically synthesised hydroxyapatite
abstract: Strontium-substituted hydroxyapatite powders with nominal compositions Ca10-xSrx(PO4)6(OH)2 for x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 were prepared by mechanochemical milling of CaHPO4, SrCO3, and CaCO3 for 12 hours at 350 rpm. Rietveld refinement of XRD patterns showed a linear increase in unit cell parameter a from 9.418 Å (x = 0) to 9.461 Å (x = 2.0), confirming Sr²⁺ incorporation into the Ca(I) and Ca(II) sites. Crystallite size remained in the range 18–25 nm across all compositions. In-vitro dissolution tests in acetate buffer (pH 5.0, 37 °C) over 24 hours showed that Ca²⁺ release increased by 34% for x = 2.0 relative to unsubstituted HA, while Sr²⁺ release reached 8.6 µmol/L at the same composition. FTIR confirmed no secondary phases. These results indicate that low-level Sr substitution may enhance resorption kinetics without compromising phase purity.

title: Thermal stability of 45S5-type bioglass powder synthesised by sol-gel and melt-quench routes: a comparative study
abstract: 45S5-type bioglass powders were produced by two routes: a conventional melt-quench method at 1350 °C and an acid-catalysed sol-gel method using tetraethyl orthosilicate, triethyl phosphate, calcium nitrate, and sodium nitrate. Both powders were characterised by XRD, FTIR, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and nitrogen adsorption (BET). Sol-gel-derived powder had a BET surface area of 148 m²/g versus 2.1 m²/g for the melt-quenched product. DSC revealed a glass transition at 544 °C and a primary crystallisation peak at 612 °C for the sol-gel glass, compared with 551 °C and 640 °C for melt-quenched glass. After heating to 700 °C, both samples crystallised predominantly to Na2CaSi2O6. The higher surface area and lower crystallisation onset temperature of sol-gel glass were found relevant when mixing with HA for composite preparation, as crystallisation can begin during SPS at temperatures above 600 °C.

title: Bioceramic composites for bone repair: processing routes, mechanical properties, and in-vitro performance
abstract: This chapter reviews the preparation of calcium phosphate–bioglass composite materials intended for bone substitute applications, with emphasis on powder synthesis, densification methods, and characterisation. The mechanochemical synthesis of hydroxyapatite is described in detail, covering reaction stoichiometry, milling parameters, and phase evolution. Sintering methods, including conventional pressureless sintering and spark plasma sintering, are compared with regard to densification efficiency, grain growth, and phase stability. Mechanical property data from the literature are tabulated, covering compressive strength (24–140 MPa), fracture toughness (0.8–2.1 MPa·m½), and Vickers hardness (4–8 GPa) as functions of composition and processing route. In-vitro testing protocols in simulated body fluid are discussed critically, noting the sensitivity of results to surface area, fluid volume, and refresh interval. Limitations of current composite systems, including brittleness and mismatch with cortical bone modulus, are identified as areas requiring further study. Approximately 180 references are cited.

title: Low-temperature spark plasma sintering of HA–bioglass composites: suppression of TCP formation and retained porosity
abstract: The formation of tricalcium phosphate during sintering of HA–bioglass composites was investigated as a function of SPS temperature (700–950 °C), BG content (5–20 wt%), and BG particle size (d50 of 2 µm and 8 µm). Rietveld refinement showed that TCP content exceeded 3 wt% in samples with 20 wt% fine BG sintered above 850 °C, whereas coarse BG at the same loading produced less than 1 wt% TCP under identical conditions. Reducing sintering temperature to 800 °C suppressed TCP formation in all compositions but lowered relative density to 91–94%. A compromise condition of 875 °C, 50 MPa, 8-minute dwell with 10 wt% coarse BG yielded 97.4% density, 0.8 wt% TCP, and compressive strength of 94 MPa, which was selected for further scaffold fabrication. Energy dispersive spectroscopy line scans confirmed local Si enrichment at HA grain boundaries in fine-BG samples, supporting the hypothesis that SiO2 activity drives the HA-to-TCP conversion.

title: Mechanical behaviour of HA–bioglass scaffolds under cyclic compressive loading: fatigue limit and failure mode characterisation
abstract: Cylindrical scaffold specimens (ø8 × 12 mm) of SPS-densified HA–10 wt% BG with 22% porosity were subjected to uniaxial cyclic compressive loading at stress ratios R = 0.1 and R = 0.3, with maximum stresses ranging from 30% to 80% of the monotonic compressive strength (38 MPa). Tests were conducted on a servo-hydraulic machine at 5 Hz in ambient air. Fatigue limit at 10⁶ cycles was approximately 40% of the monotonic strength (15 MPa), consistent with values reported for porous alumina. Failure occurred by crack initiation at macropore edges, propagating through strut junctions, as shown by post-fracture SEM. Digital image correlation during loading revealed localised strain concentrations around pores exceeding 2× the nominal applied strain. Weibull modulus estimated from monotonic strength data was 8.2, indicating moderate reliability. Immersion in SBF for 14 days before testing reduced the fatigue limit by approximately 12%, attributed to surface hydration lowering surface energy.

title: Freeze-casting of hydroxyapatite–bioglass slurries: pore orientation, strut morphology, and compressive anisotropy
abstract: Aqueous slurries containing 30 vol% solids (HA–10 wt% BG) were freeze-cast unidirectionally at controlled freezing front velocities of 5, 10, and 20 µm/s using a copper cold-finger apparatus. After sublimation drying and sintering at 1150 °C for 2 hours, samples were characterised by micro-CT, mercury intrusion porosimetry, and uniaxial compression parallel and perpendicular to the freezing direction. At 10 µm/s, micro-CT showed lamellar pore channels approximately 80 µm wide aligned within 8° of the freezing direction and a total porosity of 56%. Compressive strength parallel to pore channels was 8.4 MPa and perpendicular was 3.1 MPa, giving an anisotropy ratio of 2.7. Strut thickness was 35 ± 8 µm at 10 µm/s. XRD confirmed partial decomposition of HA to α-TCP at 1150 °C, amounting to 7 wt%. Comparison with SPS-densified porous scaffolds indicated that freeze-cast samples have lower strength but higher interconnected porosity, a trade-off relevant to vascularisation requirements.

title: Correlation between milling atmosphere and oxygen stoichiometry in mechanochemically synthesised hydroxyapatite: nitrogen versus air milling
abstract: Hydroxyapatite powders were synthesised by mechanochemical milling in two controlled atmospheres: air and high-purity nitrogen (99.998%). Milling was carried out at 300 rpm for 12 hours using zirconia vials and balls to eliminate metallic contamination. XRD and Rietveld refinement showed no measurable difference in lattice parameters or TCP content between the two atmospheres. However, FTIR detected a broader B-type carbonate substitution band at 1420 cm⁻¹ in air-milled samples, and thermogravimetric analysis revealed 0.9 wt% additional mass loss between 600 and 800 °C attributed to carbonate decomposition. ICP-OES confirmed a marginally lower Ca/P ratio of 1.64 in air-milled versus 1.67 in nitrogen-milled powder. After SPS at 950 °C, no significant difference in densification or compressive strength was found between the two sets of samples, suggesting that the level of carbonate incorporation achievable under air milling does not practically affect final mechanical properties at this sintering temperature.

title: Evaluating Two-Phase Locking Overhead in Multi-Node Relational Stores Under Skewed Access Patterns
abstract: Two-phase locking (2PL) remains a practical concurrency control mechanism in distributed relational databases, but its overhead under skewed key-access distributions is poorly characterised at scale. This paper presents a controlled benchmarking study using a four-node PostgreSQL-based cluster running TPC-C workloads modified to follow a Zipfian distribution with skew parameters ranging from 0.6 to 1.4. Lock contention rates, abort ratios, and mean transaction latencies were measured across 72-hour continuous runs. Results show that at skew parameter 1.2, abort ratios increase by a factor of 3.1 compared to uniform access, while median latency degrades by 58 ms per transaction hop. The paper further analyses how partition key selection interacts with skew to either amplify or partially absorb contention. A simple heuristic for adaptive partition key rotation is proposed and shown to reduce the 95th-percentile latency by approximately 22% under high-skew conditions without modifying the underlying locking protocol.

title: A Comparison of Consistency Guarantees Across Three Open-Source Distributed Key–Value Stores
abstract: Distributed key–value stores expose different consistency models—eventual, causal, and linearisable—but empirical comparisons under realistic mixed read/write workloads are scarce. This study benchmarks three open-source systems (anonymised as KVS-A, KVS-B, and KVS-C in accordance with project policy) on a five-node cluster using a workload generator producing 80% reads and 20% writes at throughput levels from 2 000 to 20 000 operations per second. Consistency anomalies were counted using a custom log-replay checker applied to 48-hour traces. At 10 000 ops/s, the eventually consistent store showed 0.4 anomalies per 10 000 operations, while the linearisable store showed zero but exhibited a median write latency 4.7× higher. Causal consistency offered an intermediate point with anomaly rates of 0.05 per 10 000 and a write latency penalty of 1.9× relative to eventual consistency. The paper discusses the practical implications for workload types common in inventory and session management applications.

title: Static vs. Adaptive Query Scheduling in Multi-Tenant OLTP Databases: A Trace-Driven Analysis
abstract: Multi-tenant OLTP databases face scheduling decisions that balance fairness across tenants with aggregate throughput goals. This paper uses six months of anonymised query traces from a regional ERP service provider to compare three scheduling policies: strict FIFO, weighted round-robin, and a feedback-driven adaptive scheduler that adjusts tenant weights every 500 ms based on queue depth. Trace analysis covers approximately 2.1 million distinct query events across 14 tenant accounts with highly heterogeneous arrival rates. The adaptive scheduler reduces 99th-percentile latency for the most resource-constrained tenant by 31% compared to weighted round-robin, at a cost of a 4% reduction in mean throughput for the heaviest tenant. The study identifies inter-arrival time variance as the dominant predictor of scheduling policy sensitivity and proposes a lightweight variance estimator that can be computed at negligible overhead. The findings suggest that tenant profiling updated on sub-second timescales is sufficient for most practical deployments.

title: Latency-Bounded Scheduling for Distributed Transactional Systems
abstract: This dissertation addresses the problem of enforcing per-transaction latency bounds in distributed database systems where node load fluctuates over time. The core contribution is a scheduling framework, LatSched, that decomposes each incoming transaction into a directed acyclic graph of sub-operations, assigns soft deadlines to each sub-operation based on the transaction's end-to-end latency budget, and dispatches sub-operations to nodes using a modified earliest-deadline-first policy augmented with a load-forecast component. The load forecaster uses a short-window exponential moving average over observed queue lengths, updated every 100 ms. Experiments on an eight-node cluster running a modified TPC-E benchmark at loads between 40% and 95% of theoretical capacity show that LatSched keeps 93% of transactions within their declared latency bounds at 80% load, compared to 74% for unmodified earliest-deadline-first. At 95% load the advantage narrows to 7 percentage points. The dissertation also analyses the scheduling overhead, which averages 0.8 ms per transaction.

title: Replication Lag Patterns in Synchronous and Semi-Synchronous PostgreSQL Streaming Replication Under Bursty Writes
abstract: Synchronous and semi-synchronous replication in PostgreSQL are often chosen for durability guarantees, but their behaviour under bursty write workloads is not well documented. This paper describes an experiment using a three-node streaming replication setup where synthetic write bursts of 5 000 to 50 000 rows per second are injected for durations of 5 to 60 seconds. Replication lag, standby CPU utilisation, and WAL receiver buffer occupancy are logged at one-second resolution over 200 burst events per configuration. Synchronous replication shows near-zero lag but causes a 19% increase in primary write latency during 50 000-row-per-second bursts. Semi-synchronous replication accumulates lags peaking at 8.4 seconds during the largest bursts but recovers within 12 seconds after burst cessation. A simple analytical model is fitted to the recovery curves and validated against held-out traces. The model is accurate to within 1.2 seconds for 90% of recovery events.

title: Cost-Model Calibration for Query Optimisers Under Variable Cluster Load: A Feedback Loop Approach
abstract: Query optimisers rely on cost models calibrated at installation time, but these models become inaccurate as cluster load changes throughout the day. This paper proposes a lightweight feedback mechanism that re-calibrates three cost-model parameters—sequential scan speed, random I/O speed, and CPU operator cost—every 60 seconds using runtime statistics from recently executed queries. The calibration runs as a background process with a CPU budget capped at 1.5% of a single core. Experiments on a four-node cluster replaying a 30-day production trace from a logistics operator show that re-calibrated plans are chosen over the static-model plans in 23% of query invocations, with those substitutions yielding a mean latency reduction of 18%. Overall workload 95th-percentile latency falls by 9% compared to the static baseline. The paper also reports two cases where recalibration increased latency, attributing them to cost-model oscillation during rapid load transitions, and proposes a damping heuristic to address this.

title: Estimating Transaction Abort Probability from Queue-Length Signals in Distributed Databases
abstract: Predicting which transactions are likely to abort before they complete allows a scheduler to defer or re-order them, reducing wasted work. This paper investigates whether queue-length signals observable at the coordinator node are sufficient to build a useful abort predictor. Using 90 days of operational logs from a distributed inventory system (11 nodes, roughly 4 million transactions per day), logistic regression and a small decision-tree ensemble are trained to predict abort within the next scheduling cycle using only queue-depth, arrival-rate estimate, and transaction type as features. On a held-out 30-day period the decision-tree model achieves an F1 score of 0.61 for abort prediction at a 200 ms horizon, compared to 0.54 for logistic regression and 0.47 for a naive rate-based baseline. The paper discusses the practical deployment constraints, noting that the model adds 0.3 ms overhead per scheduling cycle and requires no changes to the underlying database engine.

title: Prepoznavanje entiteta u srpskim sudskim odlukama: poređenje uslovnih slučajnih polja i transformerskih modela
abstract: Rad poređuje uslovne slučajne mreže (CRF) i dva transformerska modela (multilingualni BERT i srpski RoBERTa) na zadatku prepoznavanja imenskih entiteta u korpusu od 2.100 anonimizovanih prvostepenih presuda iz oblasti krivičnog prava. Definisano je osam tipova entiteta: lice, organizacija, lokacija, datum, sudska referenca, zakonska odredba, novčani iznos i kaznena mera. CRF model dostiže F1 od 0,78, multilingualni BERT 0,84, a srpski RoBERTa 0,87, mereno kao mikro prosek po svim tipovima. Najveće relativno poboljšanje transformerskih modela beleži se za tip 'zakonska odredba' (F1 raste sa 0,61 na 0,83). Rad opisuje posebne izazove u anonimizovanim tekstovima gde su lična imena zamenjena oznakama, što otežava razrešavanje koreferencije. Priložena je detaljna analiza grešaka po tipovima entiteta.

title: Prior Knowledge Heterogeneity and Learning Rate Differences Among New Factory Employees: A Longitudinal Field Study
abstract: This study examined how variability in prior domain knowledge affects the rate at which newly hired workers reach acceptable performance standards in a medium-sized manufacturing firm in Vojvodina. Forty-one employees hired over a six-month period completed a structured knowledge pre-assessment on their first day and were then tracked via weekly supervisor ratings and error-log records for sixteen weeks. Hierarchical linear modelling revealed that employees in the lowest quartile of prior knowledge took on average 9.3 weeks longer to reach the target performance threshold compared with the highest quartile, after controlling for educational attainment and job complexity. Notably, the relationship was non-linear: mid-range prior knowledge scores predicted steeper early learning curves than either extreme. Implications for adaptive onboarding sequencing are discussed, with reference to element interactivity as defined in cognitive load theory. The findings suggest that uniform onboarding programmes systematically under-serve both very experienced and very inexperienced new hires.

title: Intrinsic and Extraneous Load in Paper-Based Versus Digital Onboarding Manuals: An Experimental Comparison
abstract: Using a between-subjects design with 84 undergraduate volunteers acting as novice learners, this experiment compared cognitive load and immediate recall when training materials were presented in a conventional printed manual format versus a structured digital document with embedded hyperlinks and short video clips. Participants studied a realistic but fictional set of workplace procedures adapted from an administrative job description. Cognitive load was measured using a validated nine-item subjective rating scale administered immediately after the learning phase, and retention was assessed through a twenty-item cued-recall test thirty minutes later. The digital format produced significantly higher extraneous load ratings (M = 4.8 vs. 3.6 on a seven-point scale, p < .01) and marginally lower recall scores, an effect that was fully mediated by extraneous load. Split-attention effects in the digital condition, arising from simultaneous navigation demands, are proposed as the primary mechanism. Practical guidance for digital manual design is outlined.

title: Situated Learning in a Bank Branch: How Peripheral Participation Shapes Procedural Knowledge Acquisition
abstract: This qualitative and quantitative mixed-methods study tracked eight newly hired customer service representatives at a regional bank over their first twelve weeks of employment. Using a combination of structured observation, semi-structured interviews at weeks two, six, and twelve, and a procedural knowledge test, the study examined how informal participation in routine branch activities contributed to competency development beyond that attributable to formal training sessions. Thematic analysis of interview transcripts identified five recurring situated learning mechanisms: observation of senior colleagues, informal question-answer exchanges, error correction in real transactions, gradual task responsibility expansion, and narrative sharing of past client cases. Regression analysis showed that self-reported frequency of informal learning activities at week six predicted procedural knowledge test scores at week twelve (β = 0.41, p = .008), above and beyond formal training hours. Results are discussed in relation to Lave and Wenger's community-of-practice model and its applicability to structured corporate onboarding design.

title: Measuring Onboarding Programme Quality: Development and Initial Validation of the Structured Onboarding Assessment Inventory (SOAI)
abstract: This paper describes the construction and initial psychometric validation of the Structured Onboarding Assessment Inventory, a 32-item self-report instrument designed for use by HR practitioners and researchers to evaluate the quality of formal employee onboarding programmes across four dimensions: informational completeness, social integration support, role clarity facilitation, and workload pacing. Items were generated through a systematic review of existing onboarding literature and expert interviews with twelve HR managers from companies in Serbia and Croatia. An initial item pool of 61 items was administered to 267 employees from nine organisations who had been hired within the preceding six months. Exploratory factor analysis supported the four-factor structure, explaining 54% of total variance. Internal consistency was acceptable to good across subscales (Cronbach's α = .72–.84). Convergent validity was demonstrated through significant correlations with time-to-competency supervisor ratings. The instrument is made available in Serbian and English translations.

title: Worked Examples Versus Problem-Solving Practice in IT Helpdesk Training: A Randomised Field Experiment
abstract: Fifty-three newly hired IT helpdesk agents at a software services company in Novi Sad were randomly assigned to one of three training conditions during their second week of employment: (a) worked-example sequences for all twelve procedural modules, (b) problem-solving practice with minimal guidance, or (c) a faded worked-example schedule transitioning to independent problem-solving. Outcome measures were ticket resolution speed, first-contact resolution rate, and supervisor-rated quality at four and eight weeks post-training. At week four, the faded condition outperformed both alternatives on resolution speed (M = 7.1 min per ticket vs. 9.4 and 8.8) and supervisor quality ratings. By week eight, differences in resolution speed had attenuated, but first-contact resolution rate remained higher in the faded condition (74% vs. 61% and 65%). The results support the expertise reversal effect and suggest that static training designs which do not adapt to growing learner competence are suboptimal even over short time horizons.

title: Remote Onboarding During Organisational Disruption: Knowledge Gaps and Social Integration Deficits Compared with In-Person Cohorts
abstract: This retrospective comparative study examined outcomes for 112 employees onboarded entirely remotely during a period of organisational disruption against a matched group of 98 employees who had undergone standard in-person onboarding at the same set of six companies in Vojvodina and the Belgrade area in the preceding two years. Matching criteria included job family, seniority level, and educational background. Structured interviews at six months post-hire and archival records of supervisor performance ratings were used as outcome measures. Remote cohorts showed significantly lower scores on role clarity (d = 0.54) and social integration (d = 0.71) but comparable declarative knowledge test scores (d = 0.12, ns). Qualitative data indicated that remote new hires consistently reported difficulty identifying informal knowledge sources and experienced fewer spontaneous mentoring interactions. Practical recommendations for hybrid onboarding designs that preserve social and tacit knowledge transmission are presented.

title: Microlearning Bursts Versus Massed Training Sessions for Procedural Skill Retention: A Six-Month Follow-Up
abstract: This study compared two delivery formats for a standardised procedural training curriculum used in the logistics sector: a conventional massed format delivering four full training days in week one, and a microlearning format distributing the same content across twelve brief daily modules (15–25 minutes each) over three weeks, with two follow-up refresher modules at weeks six and twelve. Participants were 46 newly hired warehouse operations coordinators across two depots of the same logistics company in Serbia. Procedural skill was assessed using a standardised performance checklist at one month, three months, and six months post-training. At the six-month assessment, the microlearning group retained significantly more procedural steps correctly (M = 87% vs. 71%, t(44) = 3.21, p = .003) and committed fewer sequencing errors. Working memory load ratings during the training period, collected via daily brief surveys, were lower in the microlearning condition throughout. Results are interpreted in terms of spacing effects and germane load accumulation.

title: Mental models of hereditary disease risk among women referred for BRCA counselling in Serbia
abstract: The study investigated mental models that women hold about hereditary breast and ovarian cancer risk prior to genetic counselling sessions at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 45 women (mean age 39.4, SD = 8.1) who had been referred following a family history assessment. Interview transcripts were analysed using framework analysis. Five distinct mental model types emerged, ranging from fatalistic inheritance views ('if mother had it, I will have it') to probabilistic-quantitative models closer to clinical accuracy. Model type was associated with prior education level (χ² = 14.3, p = .006) but not with age or parity. Women holding fatalistic models reported significantly higher cancer worry (mean Penn State Worry Questionnaire score 48.2 vs. 39.6, p = .01) and expressed less willingness to consider risk-reducing surgery. Implications for counsellors' communication strategies are discussed, including the use of branching analogies to introduce probabilistic thinking.

title: Psychological reactance to mandatory vaccination messaging among parents of pre-school children in Serbia
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the antecedents and communication consequences of psychological reactance to pro-vaccination messages in a sample of 347 parents of children aged 0–6 attending paediatric check-ups in the South Bačka district. Reactance was measured using the Hong Psychological Reactance Scale and a message-specific reactance index developed for the study. Higher trait reactance predicted more negative attitudes toward childhood vaccination (β = −0.34) and lower vaccination compliance intentions (β = −0.27), independent of vaccine hesitancy and general health locus of control. Messages emphasising parental autonomy in decision-making reduced state reactance scores compared with authority-based messaging (Mdiff = 1.2, t(345) = 4.6, p < .001). The study also found that reactance was elevated among parents who had encountered vaccine misinformation online in the prior month. Findings have direct implications for how paediatric health authorities in Serbia should frame immunisation communication materials.

title: Extracting Structured Fields from PDF Engineering Reports Using Rule-Based Parsing: A Case Study in the Construction Sector
abstract: Engineering project reports produced by construction firms typically arrive as PDF documents with inconsistent layouts, mixing tabular cost summaries, free-text progress narratives, and embedded images of site sketches. This paper describes a rule-based extraction pipeline applied to a corpus of 340 quarterly reports collected from four Serbian construction companies over five years. The pipeline uses layout analysis via PDFMiner, followed by a set of 87 hand-crafted regular-expression rules targeting 14 field types including project milestone dates, cost variance figures, and contractor identifiers. Extracted data were loaded into a PostgreSQL staging area and validated against manually annotated ground-truth records for 60 documents. Field-level precision reached 0.84 and recall 0.79 across all field types, with milestone date fields performing best at 0.93 precision. The paper discusses failure cases arising from scanned documents with low OCR quality and proposes a preprocessing step using adaptive binarisation that recovers approximately 11 percentage points of recall on the degraded subset. Limitations of purely rule-based approaches when report templates change between reporting periods are acknowledged and directions for future hybrid approaches are outlined.

title: A Star-Schema Design for Integrating Heterogeneous Project KPIs Across an Infrastructure Portfolio
abstract: Portfolio managers in infrastructure organisations frequently need to compare performance indicators defined differently across individual projects. This paper proposes a dimensional model designed to accommodate KPI heterogeneity by introducing a flexible measure-metadata layer that records unit of measurement, aggregation rule, and data-source provenance for each metric. The schema was implemented in PostgreSQL and populated with data from 112 road infrastructure projects drawn from publicly available Serbian investment programme documentation spanning 2008 to 2013. The model supports 23 pre-defined KPI families covering cost performance index, schedule performance index, resource utilisation ratios, and environmental compliance scores. Query response times for typical portfolio-level OLAP queries were measured at under 1.2 seconds on a commodity server with no query caching. The paper compares the proposed design against three alternative schemas from the literature, evaluating storage overhead, query complexity, and flexibility to accommodate new KPI definitions without schema migration. Results indicate a 17 percent reduction in query lines for cross-project comparisons relative to the closest competing design.

title: Benchmarking ETL Tool Performance for Incremental Loading of Semi-Structured Report Data
abstract: Incremental loading strategies are critical when engineering report data arrive continuously and full reloads are impractical. This paper presents a benchmarking study comparing four ETL tools—Apache NiFi, Talend Open Studio, Pentaho Data Integration, and a custom Python-based pipeline—on three incremental loading scenarios: new document ingestion, field-level updates to existing records, and schema drift recovery. Test datasets consisted of synthetic engineering report batches ranging from 500 to 50,000 documents, generated to mimic realistic field distributions observed in an earlier extraction study. Metrics collected include throughput in documents per minute, memory consumption, error recovery time after deliberate record corruption, and ease of implementing change-data-capture logic assessed by two independent developers. Apache NiFi achieved the highest throughput at scale (4,200 documents per minute for the largest batch) but required the most configuration effort. The custom Python pipeline was fastest to configure and performed adequately up to 5,000 documents before memory use became prohibitive. Practical guidance is provided for organisations selecting an ETL tool based on report volume and in-house technical capacity.

title: Automated Classification of Progress Report Sections Using Shallow Machine Learning
abstract: Before structured fields can be extracted from engineering progress reports, it is useful to segment documents into functional sections such as financial summary, technical progress, risk log, and appendix. This paper investigates whether shallow machine learning classifiers can reliably perform this segmentation without deep syntactic analysis. A corpus of 620 reports from energy-sector projects was manually segmented into six section types by two annotators, achieving inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) of 0.81. Paragraph-level feature vectors were constructed from bag-of-words representations augmented with positional features (relative page position, proximity to page header) and simple formatting signals (presence of bold text, table borders). Five classifiers were evaluated: Naive Bayes, logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and k-nearest neighbours, using five-fold cross-validation. The SVM with a linear kernel achieved the best macro-averaged F1 of 0.87. Errors were concentrated at boundaries between consecutive sections of similar vocabulary, particularly between technical progress and risk sections. The classifier was integrated as a preprocessing module into the extraction pipeline described in earlier work, reducing manual intervention in document processing by an estimated 60 percent.

title: Design Principles for KPI Dashboards Serving Multi-Project Portfolio Reviews: Evidence from Four Organisations
abstract: This paper reports findings from an action research study conducted over eighteen months in four organisations managing engineering project portfolios: a regional utility company, a municipal infrastructure directorate, a mid-sized construction firm, and a technology park management body, all based in Vojvodina. Workshops with portfolio managers (n=19) and dashboard prototype iterations were used to elicit and refine dashboard requirements. Six design principles emerged from the iterative process: explicit KPI provenance labelling, drill-down paths aligned with organisational reporting hierarchy, separation of status and trend visualisations, colour conventions consistent with existing paper reports, configurable alert thresholds editable without IT involvement, and export formats compatible with standard office tools. Prototype dashboards were built in Metabase and evaluated through a structured usability test with 14 participants using a simplified System Usability Scale, yielding a mean score of 74.3 (SD 8.1), placing the designs in the 'good' category. The paper also documents three design choices that were initially assumed beneficial but were consistently rejected by participants, including animated transitions and real-time auto-refresh.

title: Handling Schema Drift in Long-Running Engineering Report Repositories
abstract: Engineering organisations revise their standard report templates periodically, introducing new mandatory fields, renaming existing ones, or changing value formats. When historical documents conforming to older templates coexist in a data warehouse with newer documents, query consistency degrades unless schema drift is explicitly managed. This paper categorises observed drift patterns across a repository of 1,840 reports spanning 11 template generations from a single infrastructure agency over 14 years. Four drift types are defined: field addition, field removal, field rename, and value-format change. A versioned metadata registry approach is proposed, in which each extracted field is linked to a template version identifier and a normalisation mapping table is maintained to reconcile equivalent fields across versions. The approach was implemented on top of an existing PostgreSQL warehouse and evaluated by rerunning a set of 38 benchmark portfolio queries, comparing result correctness against a manually reconciled gold standard. Query accuracy improved from 61 percent to 94 percent for queries spanning more than three template generations. Computational overhead of the registry lookup was negligible at under 3 milliseconds per query.

title: Integrating Textual Risk Entries from Engineering Reports into a Quantitative Risk KPI Framework
abstract: Risk sections of engineering progress reports contain free-text descriptions of identified risks alongside semi-structured severity and probability fields. This paper investigates a pipeline that extracts and normalises risk entries from 480 quarterly reports produced by energy infrastructure projects and feeds them into a quantitative KPI framework tracking portfolio-level risk exposure over time. A two-stage extraction approach is used: first, the section classifier from earlier work isolates risk sections; second, a combination of dependency parsing and heuristic slot-filling extracts risk description, category, severity score (ordinal 1–5), probability estimate, and mitigation action where stated. Of 3,214 identified risk entries, 78 percent could be mapped to one of nine pre-defined risk categories with confidence above 0.7. Extracted severity and probability values were used to populate a risk-adjusted schedule performance index computed monthly at portfolio level. Time-series visualisations of this index, presented to portfolio managers in a dashboard pilot, were rated as more actionable than the existing Excel-based risk logs in post-session interviews with eight participants.

title: A Data Warehouse Reference Architecture for Small and Medium Infrastructure Operators: Design, Implementation, and Evaluation
abstract: Small and medium-sized infrastructure operators in the Western Balkans frequently lack the in-house capacity to design and maintain business intelligence systems, yet they accumulate substantial volumes of project report data that remain analytically unexploited. This paper proposes a reference architecture tailored to this organisational context, comprising a document ingestion layer, a staging database, a core dimensional warehouse, and a dashboard layer, implemented entirely with open-source components (Apache NiFi, dbt, PostgreSQL, Metabase). The architecture was instantiated at three pilot organisations—a water utility, a road maintenance agency, and a municipal energy company—and evaluated over six months of operation. Quantitative evaluation covers data latency (median 4.2 hours from report submission to dashboard availability), data completeness (average 91 percent of expected field values populated), and user adoption (active dashboard sessions per week grew from 3 to 27 across the three sites). Qualitative feedback from 11 operational staff and 6 managers is summarised. The paper also documents recurring deployment difficulties including network policy restrictions blocking NiFi listeners and staff turnover affecting institutional knowledge of the pipeline configuration.

title: Conformal prediction intervals for meta-learned short-horizon forecasts: coverage and width under data scarcity
abstract: Quantifying uncertainty in few-shot forecasts is important for business decisions but underexplored in the meta-learning forecasting literature. This paper applies split conformal prediction to wrap uncertainty intervals around point forecasts produced by a MAML-initialised LSTM on short e-commerce revenue series. The calibration set consists of 30 held-out series per experimental condition; coverage and average interval width are reported for nominal levels of 80, 90, and 95 percent. At nominal 90 percent coverage, empirical coverage across 180 test series ranges from 87.2 to 91.8 percent, confirming approximate validity. However, interval width increases substantially when fewer than 10 adaptation examples are available, reaching up to 2.3 times the width observed with 20 examples. The paper evaluates three strategies for reducing width—shrinkage of the nonconformity score, auxiliary covariate inclusion, and calibration set pooling across related series—finding that pooling yields the most consistent width reduction without sacrificing coverage.

title: Estimating soil organic carbon from airborne VNIR-SWIR hyperspectral data over Vojvodina agricultural fields using partial least-squares regression
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of partial least-squares regression (PLSR) to predict topsoil organic carbon (SOC) content from airborne hyperspectral imagery acquired by a HySpex VNIR-1600 and SWIR-320m-e sensor pair over three agricultural test sites in Vojvodina during spring 2022. A total of 84 soil samples were collected at 0–20 cm depth and analysed for SOC using the Walkley–Black wet oxidation method in the laboratory. Reflectance spectra were measured for all samples using an ASD FieldSpec 4 spectroradiometer under controlled conditions before model calibration. PLSR models were calibrated on 60 samples and validated on the remaining 24. The best-performing model, using continuum-removed reflectance in the 400–2450 nm range, achieved a cross-validated R² of 0.74 and an RMSEP of 0.31% SOC on the independent validation set. Spatial maps of predicted SOC showed clear correspondence with known field management history. The study identifies spectral regions around 1730 nm, 2100 nm, and 2310 nm as the most influential wavelengths, consistent with organic matter absorption features reported in the literature. Challenges related to soil moisture variation and atmospheric correction residuals are discussed.

title: Comparison of spectral unmixing and regression approaches for sub-pixel soil organic carbon mapping in heterogeneous agricultural landscapes
abstract: Airborne hyperspectral pixels over cultivated fields frequently contain mixed spectral signals from bare soil, crop residue, and sparse vegetation. This paper compares linear spectral unmixing (LSU) with direct PLSR calibration for SOC estimation in 15 m spatial resolution imagery acquired over a mixed-land-use area near Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia. Endmembers for bare soil, dry vegetation, and green canopy were extracted using the N-FINDR algorithm and validated against field observations. SOC was predicted from the soil endmember abundance fraction weighted spectrum rather than from raw pixel reflectance. Accuracy assessment against 47 withheld soil samples showed that the unmixing-corrected PLSR model reduced RMSEP from 0.38% to 0.27% SOC compared with uncorrected pixel-level regression, with R² improving from 0.68 to 0.79. Benefits were most pronounced in fields with greater than 15% residue cover. The workflow is reproducible using open-source Python libraries and the full processing code is provided as a supplementary archive. Results suggest that even moderate residue contamination meaningfully biases SOC predictions if left unaddressed.

title: Transferability of a laboratory-calibrated PLSR model for soil organic carbon to airborne hyperspectral data: influence of preprocessing choices
abstract: Models calibrated on laboratory-measured soil spectra often perform poorly when applied directly to remotely sensed imagery because of differences in illumination geometry, atmospheric effects, and soil moisture state. This conference paper reports a controlled experiment examining how five preprocessing strategies—continuum removal, Savitzky–Golay smoothing, external parameter orthogonalisation (EPO), standard normal variate (SNV) transformation, and their combinations—affect the transferability of an ASD-calibrated PLSR model to HySpex airborne data acquired over test plots at the BioSense experimental farm in Čenej. Thirty-six soil samples with laboratory-measured SOC values ranging from 0.9% to 3.4% were used as ground truth. EPO combined with SNV produced the highest agreement between lab-model predictions and field predictions (r = 0.82, bias = −0.08% SOC), while uncorrected direct application yielded r = 0.51 and a positive bias of 0.29%. The results highlight preprocessing as a decisive step before any operational deployment of spectroscopic SOC models from airborne platforms.

title: Sentinel-2 Red-Edge Bands as Auxiliary Variables for Spatial Interpolation of Canopy Temperature: A Case Study in Sunflower Fields of Vojvodina
abstract: Thermal infrared sensors aboard Landsat-8 and Sentinel-3 provide land surface temperature at resolutions too coarse for field-scale crop stress assessment. This study tested whether Sentinel-2 red-edge and near-infrared reflectance bands, sampled in July–August 2017 during cloud-free overpasses over 4 200 ha of commercial sunflower in Vojvodina, could serve as auxiliary predictors in a kriging-with-external-drift model for canopy temperature. Canopy temperature was measured with 22 handheld infrared thermometers installed at 10-minute intervals across three farms. KED using a linear combination of the 705 nm and 740 nm Sentinel-2 bands reduced interpolation RMSE from 1.8 °C (OK) to 1.1 °C at 10 m resolution, a 39 % improvement. Spatial maps produced daily from the KED surface correlated with manually scouted water-stress incidence zones at r = 0.74. The method requires no additional satellite acquisitions beyond the freely available Sentinel-2 archive.

title: Performance of Orthogonal Matching Pursuit Under Structured Measurement Matrices for Wideband Spectrum Sensing
abstract: This paper investigates the recovery performance of Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) when the measurement matrix is derived from a partial random Fourier ensemble rather than a fully random Gaussian construction. Motivated by practical analog front-end constraints in wideband receivers, structured circulant matrices are evaluated against Gaussian i.i.d. matrices across sparsity levels ranging from 2 to 40 active sub-bands within a 200 MHz observation window. Experiments are conducted in simulation using synthetic multi-tone signals and replicated on a 30 MHz hardware capture from a USRP N210 testbed operating in the 400–600 MHz band. Results show that circulant matrices achieve recovery rates within 4 percentage points of Gaussian matrices at sparsity levels up to 18, while reducing matrix storage by a factor of eight. Reconstruction SNR degrades by less than 1.2 dB at the same compression ratio of 0.25. The findings suggest that structured matrices are viable for real-time compressed spectrum sensing without significant accuracy loss.

title: Sparsity Order Estimation for Blind Compressed Spectrum Recovery Without Prior Channel Knowledge
abstract: Reliable reconstruction in compressive sensing requires knowledge of the signal sparsity level, which is rarely available in opportunistic spectrum monitoring. This paper proposes an iterative sparsity order estimator based on the residual energy trajectory produced during CoSaMP iterations. The estimator is evaluated on synthetic sparse signals with sparsity levels between 5 and 50 over a 512-dimensional measurement space, and on 1000 independently drawn signal realizations per sparsity value. The proposed method correctly identifies sparsity order with probability above 0.91 for compression ratios of 0.3 or higher, compared to 0.74 for a cross-validation baseline. Importantly, the estimator adds fewer than 8% to total reconstruction time on a standard desktop CPU. The method is also tested on captured DVB-T and GSM signal mixtures, achieving 93% correct occupancy classification across 16 sub-bands. This approach enables fully blind compressive spectrum monitoring in environments where channel activity statistics are unknown.

title: Basis Pursuit Denoising with Adaptive Regularisation for Impulsive Noise Environments in Spectrum Monitoring
abstract: Standard ℓ1-minimisation via Basis Pursuit Denoising (BPDN) assumes Gaussian measurement noise, which is a poor model for spectrum monitoring environments affected by impulsive interference from industrial machinery or switching electronics. This work reformulates the BPDN objective by replacing the ℓ2 data fidelity term with a Huber loss function, whose threshold parameter is adapted per iteration using a robust scale estimator derived from the median absolute deviation of the current residual vector. The modified solver is implemented using ADMM and tested on 50,000 simulated compressed measurements with varying impulsive noise fractions (0–30%) at fixed compression ratio 0.35 and sparsity 12 out of 256. Recovery error (normalised ℓ2) is reduced by 38% relative to standard BPDN at 20% impulsive noise fraction. On live 2.4 GHz ISM-band captures, channel occupancy detection F1-score improves from 0.79 to 0.88. Convergence requires on average 14% more ADMM iterations than standard BPDN.

title: Compressed Sensing Techniques for Spectrum Monitoring: Reconstruction Algorithms and Practical Constraints
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured survey of compressed sensing reconstruction methods applicable to broadband spectrum monitoring, with emphasis on practical implementation constraints. It covers three algorithm families: greedy pursuit methods (OMP, CoSaMP, SP), convex relaxation solvers (BPDN, Dantzig selector), and Bayesian sparse recovery (BSBL, SBL). Each family is analysed in terms of reconstruction accuracy, computational complexity, sensitivity to measurement matrix structure, and behaviour under non-Gaussian noise. The chapter includes a side-by-side numerical comparison on a standardised benchmark consisting of 10,000 synthetic sparse signal instances at five compression ratios between 0.15 and 0.5. Hardware deployment considerations for FPGA and embedded DSP platforms are discussed, with reference to timing measurements obtained on a Xilinx Zynq-7020 prototype board. The chapter concludes with a discussion of remaining open problems, including time-varying sparsity and non-stationary spectral environments.

title: Block-Sparse Recovery for Multi-Band Signals Using a Modified Block-OMP with Automatic Block Boundary Detection
abstract: Licensed spectrum bands occupy contiguous frequency ranges, which induces block-sparse structure in the compressed measurements of multi-band signals. Exploiting this structure can improve recovery accuracy relative to algorithms that treat each spectral coefficient independently. This paper proposes a modified Block-OMP variant in which block boundaries are not assumed known in advance but are inferred from the support estimate during iterations using an agglomerative clustering step on the current residual spectrum. The algorithm is evaluated on signals occupying 2–8 occupied blocks of widths 1–6 MHz within a 200 MHz band, sampled at compression ratio 0.25. On 5,000 test realisations, proposed Block-OMP achieves 96.1% exact block support recovery at sparsity 6, versus 88.4% for standard OMP and 93.7% for fixed-boundary Block-OMP. Reconstruction SNR improves by 3.1 dB on average. Runtime overhead is 11% relative to standard OMP in MATLAB.

title: Temporal Correlation Exploitation in Sequential Compressive Spectrum Sensing via a Kalman-Guided Pursuit Algorithm
abstract: Broadband spectrum occupancy is not independently distributed across time: licensed services exhibit bursty on/off patterns with durations on the order of tens to hundreds of milliseconds. Standard compressive sensing algorithms ignore this temporal structure, processing each measurement frame independently. This paper proposes Kalman-Guided OMP (KG-OMP), which maintains a Kalman filter state for each spectral coefficient and uses the predicted support probability to bias atom selection during OMP iterations. The algorithm is evaluated on 200 MHz synthetic spectrum sequences generated from a two-state Markov chain occupancy model with mean on-durations of 5 to 200 frames, at compression ratio 0.25. KG-OMP achieves exact support recovery probability 0.93 at sparsity 15, compared to 0.81 for standard OMP and 0.87 for a dynamic compressive sensing baseline. False-alarm rate drops from 0.11 to 0.05. Computational overhead is 9% per frame relative to OMP due to Kalman prediction steps.

title: Benchmarking Sparse Recovery Solvers for Narrowband Interference Detection in 5G NR Guard Bands
abstract: 5G New Radio deployments in the 3.4–3.8 GHz band generate guard-band regions that are legally unoccupied but in practice subject to narrowband interference from adjacent legacy systems. Detecting such interference using full-Nyquist ADCs is costly; this paper evaluates whether sub-Nyquist compressive sensing at compression ratio 0.20–0.40 provides sufficient recovery accuracy for reliable interference flagging. Seven solvers are benchmarked: OMP, CoSaMP, SP, SOMP, BPDN, ADMM-Lasso, and SBL. Evaluation uses 80,000 synthetic frames and 4,000 captured frames from a 3.5 GHz USRP testbed. At compression ratio 0.30 and interference sparsity 5 out of 512, SBL achieves the highest F1-score of 0.96, followed by ADMM-Lasso at 0.94 and CoSaMP at 0.91. SBL runtime is 47× that of CoSaMP. A latency-versus-accuracy Pareto analysis identifies ADMM-Lasso as the preferred operating point for real-time deployment. Datasets and solver implementations are released as open-source.

title: Progressive growing GAN for high-resolution whole slide image patch synthesis in colorectal cancer subtyping
abstract: Progressive growing GAN (PGGAN) training is adapted for the synthesis of 512×512-pixel patches from colorectal whole slide images covering six tissue subtypes: tumour epithelium, simple stroma, immune cell conglomerates, debris, normal mucosa, and adipose tissue. The model was trained on 12,480 patches from 86 slides, with subtype frequencies ranging from 6% (immune conglomerates) to 28% (tumour epithelium). Progressive resolution scaling from 4×4 to 512×512 was used, with minibatch standard deviation and equilised learning rate regularisation. FID scores per subtype were computed against a held-out real patch set; the immune cell conglomerate class achieved the highest FID (52.1), reflecting its structural heterogeneity. Augmenting a DenseNet-121 classifier with synthetic patches for the three rarest classes improved macro F1 from 0.83 to 0.87. Runtime and memory profiling on NVIDIA A100 hardware are provided to guide practical deployment.

abstract: Istraživanje je sprovedeno tokom 2011. i 2012. godine na 14 lokaliteta u Vojvodini s ciljem utvrđivanja učestalosti kdr (L1014F) i super-kdr (M918T) mutacija u populacijama zelene breskvine vaši prikupljenim sa suncokreta. Ukupno je analizirano 387 jedinki metodom alel-specifičnog PCR-a. Učestalost kdr alela kretala se od 0,21 do 0,58, dok je super-kdr alel detektovan na svega četiri lokaliteta s učestalošću ispod 0,10. Bioesejima sa lambda-cihalotrinskom (25 mg a.s./l) potvrđena je smanjena osetljivost u populacijama s višim frekvencijama kdr alela (RR > 12 na tri lokaliteta). Korelacija između alel-frekventnosti i stepena rezistentnosti bila je statistički značajna (r = 0,74, p < 0,01). Dobijeni rezultati ukazuju na široku rasprostranjenost piretroidne rezistentnosti u vojvođanskim populacijama M. persicae i potrebu za rotacijom insekticida različitog mehanizma delovanja.

title: Seasonal abundance and natural enemy associations of Brevicoryne brassicae on winter oilseed rape in northern Serbia
abstract: Aphid counts and parasitoid emergence rates were recorded weekly at six field sites in Vojvodina from sowing to harvest of winter oilseed rape during 2012–2013. Peak infestations of Brevicoryne brassicae reached 184 ± 31 aphids per plant at the onset of flowering. Parasitism rates, assessed by mummy dissection, averaged 23% at peak aphid density and were dominated by Diaeretiella rapae (76% of all parasitoids reared). Predatory Coccinellidae and Syrphidae reduced aphid numbers by an estimated 38% in plots where insecticide applications were withheld. Population growth rates (r m) were significantly lower in unsprayed plots than in sprayed plots, suggesting compensatory suppression by natural enemies. A degree-day model calibrated to local temperature data predicted peak abundance within ±5 days for five of six sites. The data provide baseline information for optimising spray thresholds under current resistance management guidelines.

title: Metabolička rezistentnost na organofosfate posredovana esterazama u populacijama Myzus persicae iz useva uljane repice u Panonskoj niziji
abstract: Enzimskim metodama (spektrofotometrijskim testom sa α- i β-naftil acetatom) ispitana je aktivnost esteraza kod 512 jedinki M. persicae sakupljenih na 19 lokaliteta u Vojvodini, Slavoniji i južnoj Mađarskoj tokom 2014. i 2015. godine. Povišena aktivnost esteraza (E4 ili FE4 fenotip) utvrđena je kod 34,2% analiziranih jedinki. Genotipizacija PCR metodom potvrdila je amplifikaciju gena E4 kod 89% fenotipski pozitivnih jedinki. Bioesejima sa dimetoatom (LC50) utvrđen je faktor rezistentnosti od 8,4 do 31,7 u uzorcima s visokom esteraznom aktivnošću. Između lokaliteta nije utvrđena značajna geografska strukturiranost populacija (FST = 0,04), što ukazuje na visok protok gena. Dobijeni rezultati sugerišu da su esterazni mehanizmi rezistentnosti stabilni u panonskim populacijama bez obzira na razlike u primenjenim insekticidima na lokalnom nivou.

title: Comparative virulence of entomopathogenic fungi Beauveria bassiana and Metarhizium brunneum against insecticide-resistant and susceptible clones of Myzus persicae
abstract: Laboratory bioassays were conducted to determine whether resistance to pyrethroids or organophosphates in M. persicae influenced susceptibility to two commercial strains of entomopathogenic fungi. Eight clones — four kdr homozygous, two esterase-overproducing and two susceptible reference clones — were exposed to conidial suspensions of Beauveria bassiana (strain NsBb-7) and Metarhizium brunneum (strain NsMb-3) at 1×10⁶, 1×10⁷ and 1×10⁸ conidia ml⁻¹. Mortality was assessed at 48, 72 and 96 h. LT50 values did not differ significantly between resistant and susceptible clones for either fungal species at the highest concentration (p > 0.05), confirming the absence of cross-resistance. At 1×10⁷ conidia ml⁻¹, M. brunneum caused higher mortality (78 ± 5%) than B. bassiana (61 ± 6%) after 96 h. Results support the potential use of mycoinsecticides as rotational tools in resistance management programmes for aphids in oilseed crops.

title: Praćenje osetljivosti populacija Lipaphis erysimi na lambda-cihalotrin i imidakloprid u Vojvodini: petogodišnja studija
abstract: U periodu od 2014. do 2018. godine praćena je osetljivost repičine lisne vaši (Lipaphis erysimi Kaltenbach) na piretroid lambda-cihalotrin i neonikotinoid imidakloprid u 11 opština Vojvodine. Standardizovanim bioesejima (topikalna aplikacija i uranjanje lisnih diskova) obrađeno je ukupno 2 340 jedinki s 23 lokacije. Faktor rezistentnosti na lambda-cihalotrin povećao se sa 3,1 (2014) na 11,4 (2018) u uzorcima s najprimenjenijim piretroidima, dok je osetljivost na imidakloprid ostala u okviru divlje osetljivosti (RR < 3) tokom celog perioda. Alel-specifični PCR na kdr pozicijama L1014F i M918T potvrdio je prisustvo kdr alela u 27% analiziranih uzoraka 2018. godine. Rezultati ukazuju na sporu, ali uočljivu eroziju efikasnosti piretroida kod ove vrste u severnoj Srbiji, dok neonikotinoidi ostaju pouzdana alternativa.

title: Landscape heterogeneity and aphid resistance allele frequencies: does field isolation matter in Vojvodina cereal–oilseed rotations?
abstract: We tested whether the degree of landscape isolation — measured as the proportion of semi-natural habitat within a 1 km radius — was associated with kdr allele frequencies in M. persicae sampled from 30 oilseed rape fields across three Vojvodina districts in 2019. Allele frequencies were determined by TaqMan real-time PCR on 20 individuals per site. Landscape metrics were derived from CORINE land-cover data. A linear mixed model showed no significant effect of semi-natural habitat proportion on kdr frequency (β = −0.08, SE = 0.11, p = 0.47), whereas cumulative insecticide application intensity (number of applications over three previous seasons, derived from farm records) was a significant positive predictor (β = 0.19, SE = 0.06, p = 0.003). Fields in intensive continuous oilseed rape cultivation harboured the highest kdr frequencies (mean 0.61 ± 0.09). The results suggest that local selection pressure, rather than landscape structure, drives resistance allele dynamics at this spatial scale.

title: CYP6CY3 overexpression as a marker of neonicotinoid resistance in field populations of Myzus persicae from sunflower crops in Serbia and Romania
abstract: Cytochrome P450-mediated metabolic resistance to neonicotinoids in M. persicae has been linked to overexpression of CYP6CY3 in laboratory-selected lines, but field evidence from south-eastern Europe remains sparse. We collected 410 M. persicae from sunflower in 12 Serbian and 8 Romanian sites during 2020–2021 and quantified CYP6CY3 transcript levels by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR normalised to two reference genes. Overexpression (≥ 5-fold relative to a susceptible reference clone) was detected in 29% of Serbian and 18% of Romanian samples. Imidacloprid RR50 values correlated significantly with overexpression level (Spearman r s = 0.68, p < 0.001). RDNA microsatellite genotyping placed high-CYP6CY3 individuals across three genetic clusters, suggesting independent origins. Synergism assays with piperonyl butoxide reduced imidacloprid LC50 by 4.1–6.8-fold in overexpressing individuals, confirming a functional role for P450 enzymes. These data point to an emerging metabolic resistance trend in sunflower-colonising aphid populations.

title: Temporal changes in Aphis fabae complex abundance on sunflower border rows: influence of surrounding winter oilseed rape harvest
abstract: A two-year field experiment (2021–2022) at three sites in Srem tracked black bean aphid (Aphis fabae complex) densities on sunflower plants positioned at 0, 10, 30 and 60 m from the nearest oilseed rape field. Weekly counts were made from seedling emergence to heading. In both years, aphid densities in the 0 m rows peaked 9–12 days after adjacent oilseed rape harvest, reaching 340–490 aphids per plant tip, compared with 80–120 at the 60 m distance. Alate proportions at the 0 m border reached 68% at peak, confirming active migration. ANOVA showed a significant distance × harvest-timing interaction (F = 14.7, p < 0.001). No insecticide resistance screening was conducted on A. fabae in this study, but results have practical implications for buffer-zone management and for placement of resistance monitoring traps in future programmes.

title: Distribucija rezistentnih genotipova Myzus persicae duž toka reke Tise: implikacije za strategije upravljanja rezistencijom
abstract: Uzorkovanjem na 16 tačaka duž toka Tise od Horgoša do Titel tokom 2022. godine prikupljeno je 640 jedinki M. persicae sa suncokreta i uljane repice. Genotipizacijom real-time PCR metodom određene su frekventnosti kdr (L1014F), super-kdr (M918T) i MACE mutacije (A302S u acetilholinesterazi). kdr alel bio je prisutan na svim lokalitetima (raspon 0,18–0,72), dok je MACE mutacija detektovana na 6 od 16 lokacija, uvek s frekvencijom ispod 0,15. Super-kdr alel nije detektovan ni na jednom uzorku. Klaster analiza na osnovu genotipske frekvencije nije pokazala jasnu geografsku grupisanost, što ukazuje na visoku stopu genske razmene između populacija. Korelacija s podatkom o broju tretmana piretroidima na nivou katastarskih opština bila je statistički značajna jedino za kdr alel (r = 0,63, p = 0,009). Rezultati imaju direktan značaj za procenu rizika rezistentnosti na regionalnom nivou.

title: Whole-transcriptome profiling of insecticide-resistant and susceptible Myzus persicae clones under field-temperature fluctuations
abstract: RNA sequencing was performed on four M. persicae clones — two with confirmed kdr homozygosity and esterase overproduction, two susceptible — reared under a simulated Vojvodina spring temperature regime (12–24 °C diurnal cycle). Libraries were sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform (paired-end 150 bp; 28–34 million read pairs per sample). Differential expression analysis using DESeq2 identified 387 genes significantly upregulated in resistant clones (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1.5), with enrichment of cytochrome P450, carboxylesterase and ABC transporter gene families. At elevated temperatures (24 °C phase), resistant clones showed additional induction of heat-shock proteins (Hsp70, Hsp90) not observed in susceptible clones, suggesting a potential metabolic cost under thermal stress. Oxidative stress response genes were also upregulated in resistant clones regardless of temperature phase. The dataset has been deposited in a public repository and provides a reference for functional genomics studies of aphid resistance in continental European populations.

title: Field efficacy of spirotetramat and sulfoxaflor against pyrethroid-resistant Myzus persicae in winter oilseed rape: a multi-site trial across Vojvodina
abstract: A randomised complete block design experiment was conducted at eight sites in Vojvodina during the 2023–2024 growing season to evaluate spirotetramat (100 g a.i. ha⁻¹) and sulfoxaflor (48 g a.i. ha⁻¹) against pyrethroid-resistant M. persicae populations (confirmed kdr frequency 0.42–0.68 at all sites). Lambda-cyhalothrin (7.5 g a.i. ha⁻¹) and an untreated control were included as reference treatments. Aphid counts were made at 7, 14 and 21 days after application. Spirotetramat reduced aphid numbers by 84 ± 6% and 91 ± 4% at 14 and 21 days, respectively. Sulfoxaflor achieved 77 ± 8% and 88 ± 5% control. Lambda-cyhalothrin reached only 38 ± 11% control at 14 days across all sites. Yield differences between spirotetramat and sulfoxaflor treatments were not statistically significant (t-test, p = 0.31). Both alternatives are effective for rotation strategies where pyrethroid resistance is prevalent.
