title: Desetogodišnji trend frekventnosti alela rezistentnosti kod Myzus persicae u vojvođanskim usevima uljane repice i suncokreta (2014–2024): sinteza podataka
abstract: Analizom serije uzoraka prikupljanih godišnje od 2014. do 2024. godine na 12 fiksnih monitorinških lokacija u Vojvodini sprovedena je retrospektivna procena promene učestalosti kdr (L1014F), E4 esteraznog fenotipa i CYP6CY3 prekomerne ekspresije kod M. persicae. Ukupno je obrađeno 4 820 jedinki u standardizovanim laboratorijskim uslovima. Rezultati pokazuju porast kdr frekvencije sa prosečnih 0,28 (2014) na 0,54 (2024), s ubrzanjem trenda posle 2018. godine koje se poklapa s povećanom primenom piretroida kao zamene za zabranjene neonikotinoide na otvorenom. Učestalost E4 fenotipa ostala je relativno stabilna (26–33%), dok je CYP6CY3 prekomerna ekspresija porasla sa 7% (2018, kada je merenje uvrsteno u protokol) na 31% (2024). Modelovanjem logističke regresije utvrđeno je da je intenzitet primene insekticida na lokalnom nivou značajno bolji prediktor promene alel-frekvencije od klimatskih varijabli. Ova sinteza služi kao osnova za ažuriranje preporuka u integralnoj zaštiti bilja.

title: Oxidative stability of sunflower-oil-in-water emulsions stabilised by lecithin–Tween 80 blends at varying pH
abstract: The influence of pH on the oxidative stability of 20% sunflower-oil-in-water emulsions was investigated over a 90-day storage period at 40 °C. Emulsions were stabilised by mixed lecithin–Tween 80 systems at three HLB-matched ratios. Primary and secondary oxidation products were tracked using peroxide value and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) assays at 15-day intervals. Droplet size distributions were measured by dynamic light scattering and showed a bimodal shift only at pH 4.5 after day 45. At pH 6.0 and 7.4, the mean droplet diameter remained below 450 nm throughout the study. Peroxide values at pH 4.5 reached 18.3 meq O2/kg oil by day 90, roughly 2.4-fold higher than at pH 7.4. The zeta potential declined from −38 mV to −21 mV at acidic pH, correlating with increased flocculation. Results indicate that even modest pH shifts substantially accelerate lipid oxidation in lecithin-stabilised emulsions and that electrostatic repulsion is a stronger determinant of oxidative shelf life than previously assumed in this system.

title: Synergistic antioxidant activity of tocopherol and rosemary extract in anhydrous cream bases: a full-factorial screening
abstract: A 2³ full-factorial experimental design was applied to evaluate the individual and combined effects of α-tocopherol (0.05–0.5%), rosemary diterpene extract (0.1–0.3%), and temperature (25 vs. 40 °C) on the oxidative stability of a petrolatum–mineral oil anhydrous cream base. Stability was assessed over 12 weeks by measuring the induction period using Rancimat at 98 °C, TBARS concentration, and colour change (ΔE* via reflectance colorimetry). A statistically significant positive interaction between tocopherol and rosemary extract was detected (p < 0.01), with the combination of 0.2% tocopherol and 0.2% rosemary extract extending the Rancimat induction period by 3.1-fold relative to either antioxidant used alone at the same total concentration. Colour stability was similarly improved, with ΔE* values below 2.0 only in the synergistic combination at 40 °C. The data support a hydrogen-donation/chelation complementarity mechanism and provide practical guidance for selecting antioxidant concentrations in petrolatum-based formulations without water activity as a confounding variable.

title: Accelerated stability testing of W/O emulsions by centrifugal stress: correlation with 12-month real-time storage data
abstract: Water-in-oil emulsions (n = 14 prototype formulations) were subjected to centrifugal stress at 500, 1500, and 3000 rpm for 30 min as a rapid screening tool, and the resulting creaming index was compared to 12-month real-time stability data collected at 25 °C/60% relative humidity and 40 °C/75% relative humidity. Droplet size, turbidity, and visual phase separation were recorded monthly. Pearson correlation coefficients between the creaming index at 3000 rpm and 12-month visual separation scores were 0.81 for the 25 °C cohort and 0.76 for the 40 °C cohort. Formulations with creaming indices below 5% at 3000 rpm were stable in all real-time conditions. The method showed lower predictive power for formulations stabilised by polymeric emulsifiers than for those using small-molecule surfactants. A receiver-operating-characteristic analysis yielded an AUC of 0.88, supporting use of the centrifugal protocol as a binary pass/fail screen during early-stage development.

title: Rheological profiling of cosmetic emulsions under temperature cycling: a comparison of three thickener systems
abstract: Oscillatory and steady-shear rheological behaviour of oil-in-water emulsions thickened with carbomer 940, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), and a xanthan–locust bean gum blend was studied under repeated temperature cycling between 5 and 45 °C. Each cycle lasted 48 hours and 10 cycles were completed. Storage modulus (G′), loss modulus (G″), and flow consistency index were recorded before and after cycling. Carbomer-thickened emulsions showed the greatest G′ reduction (41% after 10 cycles) at pH 6.5, attributed to gradual ionic disruption of the carbomer network. HPMC-thickened emulsions exhibited thermal gelation artefacts above 60 °C during processing but remained structurally stable during cycling. The xanthan–locust bean gum blend maintained G′ within 12% of initial values across all cycles, performing best in terms of thixotropic recovery time (t½ = 18 s vs. 47 s for carbomer). Droplet size was unaffected by cycling in all systems. The study provides a practical basis for thickener selection in products likely to experience cold-chain transport or temperature fluctuations during retail storage.

title: Preservation efficacy of ethylhexylglycerin as a booster for low-concentration parabens in emulsified leave-on skin care products
abstract: Regulatory pressure to reduce paraben concentrations in leave-on cosmetics has prompted interest in boosting agents. This study evaluated ethylhexylglycerin (EHG) at 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5% as a booster for methylparaben at sub-regulatory concentrations (0.1, 0.2, and 0.3%) in an oil-in-water emulsion intended for twice-daily facial application. Challenge tests were conducted against a standard panel of five microorganisms at weeks 0 and 8 of shelf-life simulation. At 0.3% EHG combined with 0.2% methylparaben, ISO 11930:2019 category A criteria were met at both time points, whereas 0.2% methylparaben alone failed against Candida albicans at week 8. Water activity remained at 0.971 ± 0.002 across all formulations, ruling out aw as a confounding variable. Infrared spectroscopic analysis of the oil–water interface showed no evidence of EHG partitioning into the oil phase, suggesting that its boosting mechanism operates in the aqueous phase. The findings support a practical path for paraben reduction without switching to alternative preservatives with higher sensitisation profiles.

title: Interplay between emulsifier HLB, oil polarity, and antioxidant partitioning in W/O/W multiple emulsions stabilised by polyglycerol polyricinoleate
abstract: Encapsulation of a hydrophilic ascorbyl glucoside antioxidant in water-in-oil-in-water (W/O/W) multiple emulsions was studied across a matrix of five oils varying in polarity (dielectric constant range: 2.1–7.8) and three inner-to-outer water ratios (1:1, 1:2, 1:3 v/v). The primary emulsification used polyglycerol polyricinoleate (PGPR) at 2 and 4%. Antioxidant release into the outer water phase was quantified by UV-Vis spectrophotometry at 0, 7, 14, 28, and 56 days. Release rates correlated positively with oil polarity (r = 0.89), consistent with partitioning theory. At inner-to-outer water ratio 1:2 using medium-chain triglyceride oil (ε = 3.1), less than 18% of encapsulated antioxidant migrated to the outer phase over 56 days. Increasing PGPR from 2 to 4% reduced initial droplet median diameter from 9.8 μm to 4.3 μm but did not significantly affect long-term release rate. Osmotic balance between inner and outer phases, adjusted with NaCl, reduced osmotic migration artefacts by 60%. The data offer quantitative guidance for selecting oil phase and emulsifier loading to achieve controlled antioxidant delivery in complex emulsion architectures.
venue: Journal of Colloid and Formulation Science

title: Differential scanning calorimetry as a formulation screening tool: melting transitions of wax–lipid blends used in water-in-oil body creams
abstract: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to characterise nine binary wax–lipid blends commonly used as structuring agents in water-in-oil body creams. Blends were composed of carnauba wax, beeswax, or synthetic candelilla wax combined with either cetyl alcohol, stearyl alcohol, or glyceryl stearate at ratios of 1:1, 1:3, and 3:1 w/w. DSC thermograms were collected on heating and cooling at 5 °C/min between −20 and 100 °C. Melting onset temperatures, peak melting temperatures, and enthalpies of fusion were extracted and correlated with room-temperature hardness values measured by cone penetrometry. Eutectic interactions were identified in three of nine blends, notably the carnauba wax–cetyl alcohol 3:1 system (onset reduction of 8.4 °C vs. ideal mixing). These eutectic blends showed 22–34% lower hardness than predicted by additivity. DSC-derived enthalpy of fusion (r = 0.93) was a stronger predictor of cream hardness than melting onset alone. The study establishes a rapid pre-formulation screening workflow requiring less than 5 mg of sample per measurement, enabling rapid structure optimisation at an early development stage.
venue: Journal of Thermal Analysis and Calorimetric Methods in Materials Science

title: Stability of antioxidant-enriched sunscreen emulsions under UV stress: combined effect of iron-chelating agents and phenolic antioxidants
abstract: Sunscreen oil-in-water emulsions containing 7% ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate and 3% benzophenone-3 were enriched with combinations of EDTA disodium (0.05, 0.1%), citric acid (0.1, 0.3%), and quercetin (0.02, 0.05%) to assess combined antioxidant and chelating protection against UV-induced oxidative degradation. Emulsions were irradiated at 1.2 MJ/m² simulated solar radiation using a xenon arc lamp chamber over 72 hours. Conjugated diene content, DPPH radical scavenging capacity, and UV filter absorbance at 308 nm were measured at 0, 24, 48, and 72 hours. Quercetin at 0.05% combined with EDTA 0.1% preserved UV filter absorbance at 91% of initial after 72 hours, compared to 74% in the unprotected control. Citric acid alone provided negligible benefit at the concentrations studied. Emulsion droplet size increased from 210 to 480 nm in the control after 72 h irradiation, whereas the best-performing combination maintained it at 265 nm. The results indicate that UV-filter photostability can be substantially extended by coupling iron chelation with phenolic radical scavenging in the aqueous phase.

title: Reagent Stability Under Field Conditions: Degradation of Colorimetric Reagents for Iron, Phosphate, and Nitrite at 5–40 °C in High-Alkalinity Water
abstract: Colorimetric reagent kits intended for field deployment are typically characterised under laboratory conditions; their stability during extended field operations at variable temperatures is rarely reported. This study tracked the performance of prepared reagent solutions for iron (1,10-phenanthroline), phosphate (molybdate-ascorbic acid), and nitrite (Griess) over 30-day storage periods at 5, 20, and 40 °C in brown glass vials and low-density polyethylene (LDPE) bottles. Reagents were tested weekly against certified reference solutions and against two high-alkalinity groundwater matrices (400 and 600 mg/L alkalinity as CaCO3). The 1,10-phenanthroline reagent was the most stable, retaining >97% of initial sensitivity after 30 days at all temperatures in both vessel types. The ascorbic acid reducing agent for phosphate degraded significantly at 40 °C (sensitivity loss 22% in LDPE after 14 days). The Griess reagent showed accelerated degradation above 30 °C in high-alkalinity matrix, with sensitivity loss reaching 15% after 21 days. Recommendations on storage temperature, vessel choice, and preparation frequency are provided for each reagent.
venue: Journal of Field Analytical Chemistry and Environmental Monitoring

title: Lead and zinc distribution in soils and spontaneous plant cover at an abandoned battery recycling site in northern Serbia
abstract: Soils and above-ground plant biomass were sampled at 42 plots across a decommissioned battery recycling facility near Zrenjanin. Total Pb and Zn concentrations were determined by ICP-OES following aqua regia digestion. Soil Pb ranged from 340 to 14 200 mg kg⁻¹ and Zn from 210 to 3 800 mg kg⁻¹, both exceeding Serbian regulatory thresholds across more than 70% of plots. Eleven spontaneous herbaceous species were recorded; Calamagrostis epigejos and Tussilago farfara accumulated Pb above 800 mg kg⁻¹ dry weight in root tissues while maintaining low translocation factors (TF < 0.4), suggesting a phytostabilisation strategy. Bioconcentration factors (BCF) for Zn exceeded 1 in three grass species. Results indicate that the existing spontaneous cover provides partial immobilisation of Pb in surface horizons and could serve as a basis for assisted phytostabilisation.

title: Cadmium and nickel uptake by Agrostis capillaris on tailings deposits of the Fruška Gora foothill zone
abstract: A field study was conducted at two disused tailings piles derived from bauxite processing operations on the southern slopes of Fruška Gora. Surface soil samples (0–20 cm) and root, stem, and leaf tissues of Agrostis capillaris were collected at 28 paired plots during summer 2010 and spring 2011. ICP-OES analysis revealed mean soil Cd of 4.7 mg kg⁻¹ and Ni of 312 mg kg⁻¹. Cadmium BCF values in A. capillaris ranged from 0.8 to 2.3, while TF values consistently exceeded 1, classifying the species as a cadmium phytoextractor under these soil conditions. Nickel showed contrasting behaviour, with TF below 0.5 in all samples. Seasonal variation was significant for Cd root concentrations (ANOVA, p < 0.01) but not for Ni. These findings highlight the dual metal-response strategy of this common grass on heterogeneous post-industrial substrates.

title: Mapping heavy metal contamination gradients at post-industrial sites using portable XRF and vegetation indicators
abstract: Portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) was tested as a rapid soil screening tool across three post-industrial sites in Vojvodina, covering approximately 47 ha in total. At each site, pXRF readings were taken at 5-m grid intervals and calibrated against ICP-OES data from 96 soil samples. Correlation coefficients between pXRF and ICP-OES were 0.91 for Pb, 0.87 for Zn, and 0.76 for As. GIS-interpolated contamination maps were overlaid with vegetation composition data from 180 relevés. Cluster analysis identified three distinct plant communities associated with contamination severity classes. Elytrigia repens dominated moderately contaminated zones (Pb 200–1 000 mg kg⁻¹), while Dittrichia graveolens and Artemisia annua were strongly associated with highly contaminated soils. The combined pXRF–vegetation approach reduced assessment cost by an estimated 40% compared with full ICP-OES grid sampling.

title: Temporal dynamics of arsenic accumulation in Phragmites australis at a former chemical plant wetland margin
abstract: Phragmites australis was sampled monthly over two growing seasons (April–October 2013 and 2014) at a constructed wetland receiving drainage from a former agrochemical manufacturing site in southern Vojvodina. Arsenic concentrations were measured separately in roots, rhizomes, stems, and leaves. Root As concentrations peaked in June of both years, reaching mean values of 218 and 241 mg kg⁻¹ dry weight respectively, then declined through autumn. Rhizome As was notably stable across seasons (mean 45 ± 12 mg kg⁻¹). Leaf As never exceeded 18 mg kg⁻¹, yielding consistently low TF values (0.07–0.11). Sequential extraction of rhizosphere soil indicated that plant growth corresponded with a shift of As from exchangeable to residual fractions, consistent with rhizosphere-mediated stabilisation. Results suggest P. australis functions as an arsenic phytostabiliser rather than a phytoextractor at this site, with meaningful seasonal oscillation in root sequestration capacity.

title: Root morphology and metal exclusion mechanisms in three Fabaceae species colonising zinc-contaminated roadsides
abstract: Three leguminous species—Lotus corniculatus, Medicago lupulina, and Melilotus officinalis—were collected from road embankments adjacent to a zinc smelter in northern Serbia. Root cross-sections were examined by light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM–EDX) to localise Zn deposits. Zn tissue concentrations were measured by ICP-OES. All three species maintained shoot Zn below 100 mg kg⁻¹ despite root concentrations reaching 890 mg kg⁻¹ in M. lupulina. EDX mapping confirmed Zn accumulation at the endodermal cell wall, consistent with apoplastic immobilisation. Root anatomy of M. lupulina showed a notably thickened Casparian strip relative to reference plants from uncontaminated sites. Soil pH (mean 6.1) and organic matter content (2.8%) at the study site appeared to promote Zn adsorption and reduce bioavailable fractions as measured by DTPA extraction. Findings support the utility of native Fabaceae as component species in phytostabilisation seed mixes.

title: Phytostabilisation potential of spontaneous vegetation communities: a comparative assessment across six post-industrial sites in Serbia and Romania
abstract: Vegetation and soil data were compiled from six post-industrial sites spanning former lead–zinc mining, industrial landfill, and slag deposit contexts in the Pannonian–Carpathian transition zone. A total of 312 phytosociological relevés and 312 paired soil samples were analysed. Sites ranged in total contamination index from moderate to extreme based on combined Pb, Zn, Cd, and Ni loading. Mixed-effects models were used to partition variance in BCF and TF values among species identity, site type, and soil physicochemical variables. Soil pH explained 23% of variance in Zn BCF, and organic carbon content explained 18% of variance in Pb TF. Across all sites, 14 of 67 recorded species showed consistent phytostabiliser profiles (BCF > 1, TF < 1). Festuca rubra, Calamagrostis epigejos, and Silene vulgaris appeared in this category at four or more sites, representing regionally robust candidates for phytostabilisation programmes.

title: Soil organic matter amendments and their effect on cadmium mobility and Festuca rubra establishment on mining spoil
abstract: A pot experiment was conducted under greenhouse conditions over 16 weeks to test the effect of three organic matter amendments—composted municipal green waste, biochar derived from sunflower husks, and a mixture of the two—on cadmium mobility and the establishment of Festuca rubra on a mining spoil substrate collected from a tailings heap in the Fruška Gora region. DTPA-extractable Cd was reduced by 38% in the biochar treatment and 31% in the mixed treatment compared with unamended control. Plant biomass production was highest in the mixed treatment (mean shoot dry weight 4.8 g pot⁻¹ versus 1.9 g pot⁻¹ in control). Leaf Cd concentrations in amended treatments were 40–52% lower than in the control, while root Cd declined less markedly, suggesting continued rhizosphere immobilisation. Germination rate of F. rubra was not significantly affected by amendment type. Results indicate combined biochar–compost applications merit field-scale testing.

title: Spontaneous succession and metal accumulation kinetics on a decommissioned copper slag heap over a 30-year period
abstract: Archival vegetation records from 1989 and 1999 were combined with new field surveys conducted in 2018 to reconstruct succession trajectories on a copper slag heap in the Banat region. At each time point, matched plots were sampled for soil chemistry and plant tissue metal concentrations where archival biomass data permitted. Total soil Cu declined from 2 840 mg kg⁻¹ (1989) to 1 950 mg kg⁻¹ (2018) in upper horizons, attributed partly to leaching and partly to the accumulation of organic matter diluting the slag matrix. Plant species richness increased from 4 species in 1989 to 28 species in 2018. Cu BCF values declined with increasing successional age for all persistent species examined. Regression analysis showed that soil organic carbon was the strongest predictor of Cu immobilisation rate (R² = 0.61). Long-term succession appears to promote natural attenuation of plant-available Cu, but concentrations in dominant species (Epilobium angustifolium, Calamagrostis epigejos) remain above background levels.

title: Transfer factors and human exposure risk for Pb and Cd via incidental soil ingestion at contaminated urban–industrial margins in Novi Sad
abstract: Soil and vegetation samples were collected from 15 urban–industrial margin sites within and around Novi Sad, including former factory grounds and railway depot margins colonised by ruderal vegetation. Pb and Cd tissue concentrations in the five most abundant species at each site were combined with site-specific soil data to calculate bioaccessibility-adjusted transfer factors using the in vitro PBET extraction method. A simplified human exposure model was applied for the incidental ingestion pathway, assuming adult and child receptor scenarios. At seven sites, estimated child daily Pb intake via soil ingestion exceeded the provisional tolerable daily intake. Vegetation cover reduced dust resuspension and thus exposure, but several metal-accumulating species (notably Taraxacum officinale) contributed directly to the exposure pathway through potential incidental ingestion. The study highlights the need to consider spontaneous vegetation composition when conducting risk assessments at urban brownfields.

title: Phytostabilisation using native plant assemblages: design principles and an illustrated protocol for practitioners
abstract: This book chapter synthesises published evidence and the authors' field experience to provide a practical protocol for designing phytostabilisation interventions at central and eastern European post-industrial sites. It covers site characterisation procedures, plant species selection criteria based on BCF and TF thresholds, soil amendment options, and monitoring indicators for assessing stabilisation progress. The chapter gives worked examples from Vojvodina tailings and Romanian slag deposits, drawing on data from studies conducted between 2012 and 2020. Tables list regional native species with confirmed phytostabiliser profiles for Pb, Zn, Cd, Cu, and Ni. Common failure modes of phytostabilisation projects—including insufficient surface moisture retention, inappropriate species mixtures, and lack of aftercare—are discussed with reference to documented case studies. The chapter is aimed at environmental consultants, remediation engineers, and local authority land managers in post-socialist industrial regions.

title: Root exudate chemistry and rhizosphere pH modification in Silene vulgaris growing on Pb–Zn tailings: seasonal field measurements
abstract: Silene vulgaris was selected for detailed rhizosphere characterisation at a Pb–Zn tailing site in Vojvodina based on prior evidence of its consistent phytostabiliser profile. Rhizosphere soil and bulk soil were sampled separately at monthly intervals across two growing seasons using a modified rhizobox system installed in situ. Rhizosphere pH was on average 0.4 units lower than bulk soil pH across sampling dates. Low-molecular-weight organic acid concentrations (citric, malic, oxalic) were measured in rhizosphere leachates by ion chromatography and were significantly higher near roots in May and June than in August. Extractable Pb (DTPA) in rhizosphere soil was 17% higher than in bulk soil despite lower TF values in plant shoots, suggesting enhanced dissolution followed by root-surface immobilisation rather than phytoextraction. Iron plaque formation on fine roots was confirmed by SEM–EDX and appeared to co-localise with Pb deposits, implicating iron oxyhydroxide sorption as a stabilisation mechanism.

title: Microplastic co-contamination modifies cadmium uptake kinetics in Lolium perenne: a controlled mesocosm study
abstract: The interaction between microplastic particles (polyethylene, 100–500 µm) and cadmium in plant uptake was investigated in outdoor mesocosms using a factorial design with four Cd levels (0, 5, 10, 20 mg kg⁻¹ added as CdCl₂) and two microplastic concentrations (0 and 1% w/w). Lolium perenne was grown for 60 days and harvested for root and shoot tissue analysis. Microplastic addition at 1% significantly increased DTPA-extractable Cd in soil by 12–19% across Cd treatments, attributed to adsorption competition effects modifying Cd speciation. Shoot Cd concentrations were 8–22% higher in microplastic-amended pots at the two highest Cd levels (p < 0.05). Root biomass was reduced in combined treatments, potentially affecting total Cd immobilisation capacity. This study represents a first assessment of this interaction for a species with confirmed phytostabiliser characteristics under Pannonian soil conditions, and suggests that microplastic co-contamination may undermine phytostabilisation effectiveness at affected sites.

title: Changes in phytoseiid mite diversity across an agricultural intensification gradient in Fruška Gora foothill orchards
abstract: Orchard sites along Fruška Gora were classified into four intensification categories based on pesticide use records, ground cover management, and tree density obtained from farmer surveys. Phytoseiid mite communities were sampled on 100 leaves per orchard in early June and late August over two seasons from 22 orchards. Species richness declined significantly along the intensification gradient (Spearman ρ = −0.74, p < 0.001), from a mean of 9.2 species in extensive orchards to 2.1 species in high-intensity orchards. Functional diversity metrics, including Rao's quadratic entropy, paralleled species richness trends. Indicator Species Analysis identified Typhlodromus pyri and Euseius finlandicus as indicator species for moderate-intensity orchards, while Neoseiulus californicus was restricted to the most intensively managed sites. Environmental filtering by pesticide load explained 41% of community composition variation in a partial redundancy analysis, with orchard age and tree variety explaining an additional 18%. The findings have implications for landscape-level conservation planning under agri-environment schemes.

title: Silicon concentration in winter wheat tissues under varying soil pH and organic matter content in Vojvodina chernozem
abstract: This study examined how soil pH (5.8–7.6) and organic matter content (1.2–3.9 %) affected the concentration of plant-available monosilicic acid and its uptake into root, stem and leaf tissues of winter wheat (cv. Pobeda) grown on chernozem soils typical of the Vojvodina plain. Soil samples were collected from 12 experimental plots at the Rimski Šančevi research station across two growing seasons (2009–2010). Plant-available silicon was extracted with 0.5 M acetic acid and determined by molybdenum-blue colorimetry. Silicon concentration in straw at GS65 ranged from 1.8 to 4.6 mg Si g⁻¹ dry weight and was positively correlated with soil organic matter (r = 0.61, p < 0.01) but showed no significant relationship with pH in the tested range. Root silicon was consistently 30–40 % lower than leaf silicon regardless of treatment, suggesting preferential upward transport. The data provide baseline values for Vojvodina wheat production conditions and suggest that management of soil organic matter may passively support silicon availability without direct amendment.

title: Polarisation-entangled photon pair generation in type-II PPKTP waveguides at 810 nm
abstract: We report on the fabrication and characterisation of a periodically poled potassium titanyl phosphate (PPKTP) waveguide source designed for collinear type-II spontaneous parametric down-conversion at a pump wavelength of 405 nm. The waveguide was fabricated by proton exchange on a 2 cm flux-grown crystal. Entangled photon pairs at 810 nm were collected into single-mode fibres and directed to silicon single-photon avalanche diodes. Coincidence counting was performed with a time-to-digital converter at 81 ps timing resolution. We measured a pair generation rate of 1.4 × 10⁵ pairs per second per milliwatt of pump power, with a coincidence-to-accidental ratio of 420 at 1 mW. Bell state fidelity was determined to be 0.961 ± 0.008 using quantum state tomography on 16 projection settings. The CHSH parameter reached S = 2.74 ± 0.03, violating the classical bound by more than 24 standard deviations. Background fluorescence from the proton-exchange layer was identified as the primary source of fidelity reduction at pump powers above 3 mW.

title: Timing jitter characterisation of silicon and InGaAs single-photon avalanche diodes under pulsed illumination
abstract: Timing jitter is a key performance parameter for single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) used in quantum optics and time-of-flight applications. We systematically measured instrument response functions for four commercial silicon SPADs and two InGaAs/InP SPADs under pulsed laser illumination at 670 nm and 1310 nm respectively. A mode-locked fibre laser with 200 fs pulses and a calibrated optical attenuator were used to deliver mean photon numbers between 0.01 and 1.0 per pulse. Full-width at half-maximum jitter values ranged from 38 ps to 310 ps across devices. We examined the dependence of jitter on excess bias voltage and temperature, finding a 12 ps per degree reduction in FWHM for Si SPADs cooled from 25 °C to −20 °C. Secondary timing peaks attributed to after-pulsing were quantified using a dead-time sweep protocol. The results provide a practical basis for selecting detectors in coincidence-counting applications where the timing resolution directly limits the signal-to-noise of entanglement measurements.

title: Comparison of BB84 and E91 quantum key distribution implementations on a 400-metre free-space urban testbed
abstract: We describe the construction and operation of a 400-metre free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) link established between two buildings at the University of Novi Sad campus. The transmitter used a gain-switched diode laser attenuated to 0.12 mean photons per pulse at 780 nm for BB84, and a SPDC-based entangled photon source for an E91-protocol implementation. Both polarisation bases were encoded and analysed using liquid-crystal retarders and polarising beam splitters. The quantum bit error rate was monitored continuously over 48 hours under varying atmospheric turbulence conditions characterised by simultaneous scintillation measurements. BB84 yielded a mean QBER of 3.1 % with a sifted key rate of 14.2 kbit/s. E91 achieved a QBER of 4.8 % and 2.3 kbit/s after basis reconciliation. Pointing stability was maintained by active beam steering using a quadrant photodetector feedback loop. Privacy amplification was performed using a Toeplitz matrix construction. The testbed is now used as a demonstration and teaching platform.

title: Spectral brightness enhancement in bulk BBO downconversion by tight pump focusing and crystal temperature tuning
abstract: We investigated how pump beam waist and crystal temperature affect the spectral brightness of polarisation-entangled photon pairs produced in a 3 mm beta-barium borate (BBO) crystal in a crossed-crystal configuration at 532 nm pump. Pair brightness was measured as collected pairs per second per milliwatt per nanometre of bandwidth, using 3 nm interference filters centred at 1064 nm. Pump beam waist was varied from 80 µm to 400 µm using an adjustable telescope, and crystal temperature was controlled between 15 °C and 45 °C with a Peltier stage. A maximum spectral brightness of 830 pairs s⁻¹ mW⁻¹ nm⁻¹ was obtained at a 130 µm waist and 22 °C. Spatial mode quality, measured by beam propagation ratio M², was maintained below 1.12 across all settings. CHSH violation was confirmed at all brightness maxima. The results indicate that temperature fine-tuning can partially compensate for walk-off-induced degradation at tight focusing, reducing the need for longitudinal compensation crystals.
venue: Optics and Photonics Letters

title: Polarisation drift compensation in single-mode fibre channels for entanglement distribution
abstract: Thermal and mechanical perturbations cause slow polarisation drift in single-mode optical fibres, degrading the fidelity of entanglement distribution over fibre links. We characterised the drift rate on a 1.2 km spool of standard single-mode fibre at 810 nm over a 72-hour period, measuring the full Stokes vector with a motorised polarimeter at 1 Hz. Drift speeds reached 0.8 rad/hour under laboratory temperature fluctuations of ±1.5 °C. A closed-loop compensation scheme using three fibre-squeezer polarisation controllers driven by a gradient-descent algorithm was implemented. The system reduced residual polarisation mismatch to below 0.3° root mean square continuously. Entanglement fidelity, measured by Bell state projection, was maintained above 0.95 during 12-hour unattended operation. The control loop latency was 120 ms, sufficient for drift rates observed but insufficient for compensation of mechanical shocks. The approach is suitable for metropolitan-distance fibre QKD links without active cryogenic stabilisation.
venue: Journal of Optical Fibre Communication and Sensing

title: Dead-time and after-pulsing correction in coincidence measurements for entangled photon sources
abstract: Accurate characterisation of entangled photon sources requires correcting raw coincidence counts for detector dead-time and after-pulsing artefacts that bias estimates of pair generation rate and entanglement visibility. We derive analytical correction factors under Poissonian photon statistics and validate them experimentally using a PPKTP source with independently calibrated flux. Three silicon SPADs with dead times between 22 ns and 77 ns and after-pulsing probabilities between 0.4 % and 2.3 % per detected photon were tested at count rates from 10⁴ to 10⁶ counts per second. Uncorrected coincidence rates underestimated the true pair rate by up to 18 % at the highest flux. Corrected rates agreed with independently measured values to within 1.5 %. Applied to Bell inequality measurements, the corrections shifted the reconstructed CHSH S value by up to 0.07 at high pump power, a non-negligible effect for threshold violation experiments. A software tool implementing the corrections is made publicly available.

title: Entangled photon pair sources for quantum key distribution: a practical survey of source types and coupling geometries
abstract: This chapter reviews the main entangled photon pair source architectures relevant to practical quantum key distribution, covering bulk crystal sources in Sagnac and crossed-crystal geometries, periodically poled waveguide sources, and fibre-based sources. For each architecture the chapter discusses spectral brightness, polarisation fidelity, pump power requirements, and fibre-coupling efficiency based on published experimental results and the authors' own laboratory measurements. Coupling geometries are compared in terms of collection efficiency into single-mode fibre across the parameter space of crystal length and pump focussing. Common problems in practical implementations — including photoluminescence background, fibre dispersion at telecom wavelengths, and detector dark-count budget — are discussed with worked numerical examples. The chapter is aimed at researchers building or evaluating sources for metropolitan QKD testbeds rather than at fundamental entanglement experiments, and therefore emphasises stability and reproducibility over peak fidelity.

title: Heralded single-photon generation from a PPKTP source: heralding efficiency and g(2)(0) characterisation
abstract: We characterise heralded single-photon generation using a fibre-coupled PPKTP source pumped at 405 nm producing degenerate pairs at 810 nm. Detection of one photon of a pair heralds the presence of the conjugate photon in the signal channel. Heralding efficiency, defined as the probability of detecting a signal photon given a herald click, was measured as a function of coupling alignment and pump power over the range 0.1–3.0 mW. A maximum heralding efficiency of 61 % was achieved in the signal channel after optimising aspheric lens positions to within 5 µm. The second-order autocorrelation function g⁽²⁾(0) at zero pump power extrapolation was 0.008 ± 0.003, confirming strong single-photon character. Multi-pair contamination at 2 mW pump raised g⁽²⁾(0) to 0.038 ± 0.005. Spectral purity was estimated at 0.82 from Hong–Ou–Mandel interference visibility of 0.74 between independently prepared heralded photons. The source is used as an input for single-photon component testing in the group's QKD testbed.

title: Environmental noise impact on a campus free-space QKD link during winter and summer measurement campaigns
abstract: Seasonal and diurnal variations in atmospheric conditions affect the performance of free-space optical quantum key distribution links in continental climates. We operated our 400-metre campus free-space QKD testbed continuously during two two-week campaigns in January and July 2021 at 780 nm, recording sifted key rate, quantum bit error rate, and link attenuation every 30 seconds. Scintillation index ranged from 0.04 at night in winter to 0.31 on sunny summer afternoons, causing attenuation fluctuations of up to 9 dB. The sifted key rate dropped to zero during four fog events in January, each lasting between 20 minutes and 3.5 hours. Background solar radiation increased the QBER by an average of 0.9 percentage points on summer days relative to nights. We model the link budget under each condition using a log-normal turbulence model and compare predictions to measurements. The analysis identifies fog and direct solar background as the dominant operational constraints for urban free-space QKD in the region.
venue: Atmospheric and Optical Communications Research

title: Characterisation of a low-noise InGaAs SPAD module for 1310 nm quantum key distribution
abstract: We report detailed performance measurements of a thermoelectrically cooled InGaAs/InP single-photon avalanche diode module operated at 1310 nm in gated Geiger mode. Detection efficiency, dark count rate, after-pulsing probability, and timing jitter were measured as functions of excess bias voltage and gate repetition rate from 1 MHz to 100 MHz. At −40 °C and 10 % excess bias, detection efficiency was 18.4 %, dark count probability per gate was 3.1 × 10⁻⁵, and after-pulsing probability was 1.8 % for a 100 ns hold-off. Timing jitter FWHM was 210 ps at 1 MHz gate rate, increasing to 310 ps at 100 MHz due to incomplete recharge. We integrate the device into our QKD testbed at 1310 nm using a dispersion-shifted fibre spool of 5 km and measure a QBER of 3.8 % at a sifted key rate of 8.4 kbit/s. Comparison with Si SPAD performance at 810 nm under equivalent testbed conditions is provided.

title: Phase-encoded continuous-variable quantum key distribution: a feasibility assessment for short fibre links
abstract: Continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) protocols using coherent states and homodyne detection offer practical advantages over discrete-variable approaches at short distances due to the use of standard telecom components. We assess the feasibility of a Gaussian-modulated coherent-state CV-QKD implementation over a 5 km dispersion-shifted single-mode fibre link at 1550 nm. A home-built balanced homodyne detector with a common-mode rejection ratio of 52 dB and clearance of 14 dB above shot noise was constructed and characterised. Excess noise at the receiver was 0.018 shot-noise units under laboratory conditions and rose to 0.031 under electronic noise typical of the building environment. Secret key rate estimates using the asymptotic Gaussian security proof gave 42 kbit/s at 5 km. We identify the primary technical challenges as local oscillator intensity noise and phase locking stability rather than detector performance. The work is exploratory for the group, which maintains discrete-variable QKD as its primary research line.

title: Entanglement distribution over a 12 km deployed urban fibre segment with active polarisation control
abstract: We report entanglement distribution experiments over a 12 km segment of installed dark fibre in Novi Sad city, using a PPKTP-based entangled photon source at 810 nm located at the Faculty of Sciences and detection stations at two remote sites. The fibre loop was deployed through existing municipal conduits and experienced realistic urban vibration and thermal conditions. Active polarisation compensation using fibre squeezers reduced polarisation mode dispersion-induced fidelity loss from 0.08 to below 0.015 over a 10-hour period. At 810 nm, fibre attenuation on the deployed link was 4.1 dB, higher than the specified 3.2 dB due to connector aging. Coincidence counts were recorded over a 6-hour data run yielding a CHSH parameter of S = 2.61 ± 0.05 without background correction. A full link budget analysis is presented, and the bottleneck is identified as fibre-to-detector coupling loss at the remote stations rather than the source brightness. Lessons learned are discussed in the context of extending the link toward a three-node configuration.

title: Moisture-sorption isotherms of spray-dried whey permeate: fitting of GAB and BET models at three temperature levels
abstract: Whey permeate powder, a highly hygroscopic dairy by-product, was spray-dried under varying inlet air temperatures (150, 170 and 190 °C) and feed solid concentrations (20, 30 and 40 % w/w). Equilibrium moisture content was measured gravimetrically at 15, 25 and 35 °C over a water activity range of 0.11–0.85 using saturated salt solutions. The GAB and BET models were fitted by non-linear least squares; GAB consistently yielded lower residual sum of squares (mean RMSE 0.0041 g/g dry basis vs 0.0089 for BET). Monolayer moisture values from GAB ranged from 0.042 to 0.061 g/g d.b., decreasing with higher inlet temperature, consistent with partial lactose crystallisation confirmed by X-ray diffractometry. Critical water activity for caking onset was identified at approximately 0.45 at 25 °C. These results provide practical boundaries for packaging specification and storage conditions for whey permeate ingredients.

title: Rheological characterisation of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose binder solutions intended for fluidised-bed granulation
abstract: Aqueous solutions of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) grades E5, E15 and K100M were characterised rheologically at concentrations of 1–8 % w/w and temperatures of 20–60 °C using a rotational rheometer with cone-plate geometry. All solutions exhibited pseudoplastic behaviour well described by the power-law model; the flow behaviour index n ranged from 0.61 (K100M, 8 %) to 0.98 (E5, 1 %). Activation energy of viscous flow, determined from Arrhenius plots, decreased from 22.4 kJ/mol for K100M to 11.8 kJ/mol for E5. Surface tension measured by the Wilhelmy plate method fell between 46 and 54 mN/m across grades and concentrations. Droplet size produced by a two-fluid nozzle correlated inversely with binder viscosity (Pearson r = −0.87), providing a practical tool for atomisation parameter selection in granulation process design. Data are presented in tabular form suitable for direct use in population balance model parameterisation.

title: Granule growth kinetics in top-spray fluidised-bed processing of citric acid powder with starch binder
abstract: Top-spray fluidised-bed granulation of citric acid was carried out in a 5 kg batch unit at three air inlet temperatures (60, 70 and 80 °C), two spray rates (6 and 10 g/min) and two binder concentrations (5 and 10 % w/w maize starch). Granule size was monitored by withdrawing 5 g samples at 10-minute intervals and analysing by laser diffraction. Granule growth followed an exponential rate expression with a rate constant that increased with spray rate and decreased with inlet temperature. Final d50 ranged from 310 µm to 690 µm across conditions. Particle porosity, measured by mercury intrusion, fell from 38 to 19 % as granule size increased. Friability (Roche friabilator, 4 min, 25 rpm) correlated inversely with porosity (R² = 0.81). Moisture content of collected granules was below 2 % w/w in all successful runs, with one condition at 80 °C inlet air causing partial defluidisation attributed to excessive binder drying.

title: Comparison of spray drying and fluidised-bed coating for microencapsulation of lactic acid bacteria: survival and storage stability
abstract: Survival and storage stability of Lactobacillus helveticus ATCC 15009 were compared for two encapsulation methods: spray drying with whey protein isolate wall material and fluidised-bed coating with enteric-grade shellac applied in a Wurster insert. Inlet drying temperature, feed viscosity and coating thickness were systematically varied. Spray-dried capsules showed initial viability losses of 1.2–2.4 log CFU/g depending on inlet temperature (140–180 °C); Wurster-coated granules exhibited losses below 0.5 log CFU/g. After 12 weeks at 25 °C and 43 % RH, spray-dried preparations retained 6.1 log CFU/g on average versus 7.8 log CFU/g for coated granules. Differential scanning calorimetry of the wall materials indicated a 14 °C difference in glass transition temperature that partly explained the protective superiority of shellac coating. In simulated gastric fluid (pH 2.0, 2 h), coated granules released fewer than 1 % of viable cells, confirming adequate enteric protection.

title: Influence of bed temperature on moisture content profiles and agglomeration tendency during fluidised-bed drying of trehalose–glucose mixtures
abstract: Binary mixtures of trehalose and glucose (mass ratios 0:100, 25:75, 50:50, 75:25 and 100:0) were fluidised-bed dried from initial moisture contents of 15–18 % w/w at bed temperatures of 55, 65 and 75 °C. Moisture content was tracked by near-infrared spectroscopy at 2-minute intervals, calibrated against the Karl Fischer reference method (R² = 0.994). Time to reach the target endpoint of 2 % was shortest for pure trehalose (22 min at 75 °C) and longest for 75 % glucose (68 min at 55 °C). Agglomeration events, detected by pressure-drop monitoring, occurred in all mixtures with glucose fraction above 50 % at 75 °C, coinciding with glass transition temperatures below the bed temperature as measured by modulated DSC. Pycnometric particle density and bulk density were recorded after drying; Carr index increased from 14 % for pure trehalose to 31 % for the 75 % glucose mixture, indicating substantially reduced flowability.

title: Spray drying of elderberry extract with maltodextrin and gum arabic: powder characterisation and phenolic retention
abstract: Elderberry (Sambucus nigra) extract standardised to 3.2 % w/w total anthocyanins was spray-dried using maltodextrin DE 18 (MD), gum arabic (GA) and MD–GA blends (1:1 and 3:1 w/w) as carrier materials at a 1:4 core-to-wall ratio. Inlet temperature was 160 °C, outlet 75–82 °C. Total phenolic content (Folin–Ciocalteu), DPPH radical scavenging activity and anthocyanin concentration (pH differential method) were measured immediately after drying and after 90-day storage at 25 °C in sealed aluminium pouches. Anthocyanin retention after drying ranged from 74 % (MD alone) to 88 % (MD–GA 3:1). After 90-day storage, all powders showed further losses; MD–GA 3:1 retained 79 % of initial anthocyanins versus 58 % for MD alone. Scanning electron microscopy revealed smoother surface morphology for MD–GA 3:1 particles, attributed to reduced surface porosity. Hygroscopicity index (24 h at 75 % RH) was lowest for GA-containing samples.

title: Population balance modelling of particle size evolution in bottom-spray Wurster coating of microcrystalline cellulose beads
abstract: A one-dimensional population balance model (PBM) was developed and validated for Wurster fluidised-bed coating of microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) beads with aqueous ethylcellulose dispersion. The model incorporated a log-normal growth rate distribution and a binary breakage kernel calibrated from sieve analysis data collected at 15-minute intervals during 120-minute coating runs. Three spray rates (8, 12 and 16 g/min) and two partition gap heights (20 and 30 mm) were tested. The PBM predicted final d90 values within 8 % of measured values across all conditions. Coating uniformity was assessed by single-bead dissolution testing (UV spectrophotometry at 272 nm); relative standard deviation of dissolution lag times across 30 beads was 11–19 %, decreasing with lower spray rate. The validated model was used to construct an operating space diagram mapping spray rate and partition gap combinations that meet a target d90 of 550 ± 40 µm.

title: Characterisation of fat-coated sodium chloride granules produced by fluidised-bed coating: texture, dissolution and moisture barrier performance
abstract: Sodium chloride granules (d50 ≈ 420 µm) were coated with partially hydrogenated palm kernel fat in a top-spray fluidised-bed coater at four coating levels (5, 10, 15 and 20 % w/w) and two bed temperatures (30 and 40 °C). Coating level was verified gravimetrically and by chloride titration of dissolved samples. Texture profile analysis of compacted powder beds showed that hardness increased linearly with coating level (R² = 0.96). Dissolution rate in stirred water at 25 °C was characterised by a first-order rate constant that decreased by 78 % from uncoated to 20 % coated granules. Dynamic vapour sorption measurements at 25 °C demonstrated that 15 % coating reduced equilibrium moisture uptake at 0.75 aw from 2.8 to 0.9 % w/w. Cross-sectional SEM imaging confirmed continuous fat layers at 15 and 20 % coating levels, with occasional pinholes at 5 and 10 %. These granules are of interest as controlled-release salt ingredients in processed meat and bakery products.

title: Process parameter mapping for spray drying of inulin: impact on degree of polymerisation distribution and hygroscopicity
abstract: Inulin derived from chicory root (Chicorium intybus) at three molecular weight fractions (DP 10–12, DP 18–23 and mixed commercial grade) was spray-dried across a factorial design combining inlet temperatures (150, 170, 190 °C), feed concentrations (20, 30, 40 % w/w) and feed flow rates (5, 10 mL/min). Degree of polymerisation distribution before and after drying was determined by HPAEC-PAD. Thermal degradation to fructose and glucose monomers was detectable only at 190 °C, with monomer increase below 2 mol% in the worst case. Powder hygroscopicity (moisture gain at 0.75 aw, 25 °C, 24 h) increased markedly for DP 10–12 fractions (up to 14.3 % w/w) and was below 5 % for DP 18–23. Particle morphology ranged from wrinkled spheres at low feed concentration to smoother surfaces at 40 % w/w. A central composite design analysis identified feed concentration as the dominant factor controlling final bulk density (p < 0.001).

title: Scale-up considerations for fluidised-bed granulation of hygroscopic vitamin C premix: from 5 kg to 50 kg batch
abstract: Scale-up of fluidised-bed granulation from a 5 kg laboratory unit to a 50 kg pilot unit was investigated using a vitamin C premix (ascorbic acid co-crystallised with sodium ascorbate, 1:1 mol/mol) with PVP K30 binder at 5 % w/w. The Stokes deformation number and dimensionless spray flux were used as scale-up criteria. At matched dimensionless spray flux (Ψa = 0.012), final granule size d50 differed by less than 9 % between scales; at matched spray rate per unit bed area, differences reached 34 %. Granule friability was below 0.5 % at both scales when inlet air velocity was adjusted to maintain a bed expansion ratio of 1.4. Ascorbic acid content uniformity (RSD across 10 sampling points) was 1.8 % in the 50 kg batch versus 1.3 % in the 5 kg batch. Bed temperature transients during start-up were more pronounced at larger scale, requiring a 4-minute pre-conditioning period to avoid localised over-wetting.

title: Sorption isotherm modelling and shelf-life prediction for encapsulated iron sulphate produced by spray drying
abstract: Iron sulphate (FeSO4·7H2O) was encapsulated by spray drying with whey protein concentrate and modified starch at a 1:5 core-to-wall ratio to produce an iron fortification ingredient. Moisture sorption isotherms were determined at 20, 30 and 40 °C using a dynamic vapour sorption microbalance over 0 to 0.90 aw. Four models (GAB, Oswin, Peleg and Smith) were compared by Akaike Information Criterion; GAB provided the best fit with RMSE below 0.003 g/g d.b. across all temperatures. Colour change (ΔE in CIELAB) as a proxy for oxidative degradation was monitored at 0.53 aw over 16 weeks; an Arrhenius-based shelf-life model predicted 18 months at 20 °C before ΔE exceeded 3.0. Solubility of encapsulated iron in simulated intestinal fluid (pH 6.8) reached 91 % within 60 minutes, compared to 78 % for free FeSO4 granules, attributed to the dispersing effect of the protein matrix.

title: Binder distribution in fluidised-bed agglomerates studied by X-ray computed micro-tomography and image analysis
abstract: X-ray computed micro-tomography (µ-CT) at 2.5 µm voxel resolution was applied to characterise internal binder distribution in fluidised-bed agglomerates of lactose monohydrate produced with aqueous PVP K30 solutions (5 and 10 % w/w) at two spray rates (8 and 14 g/min). Reconstructed 3D images were segmented by threshold-based algorithms to identify solid lactose, binder bridges and pores. Binder bridge volume fraction was 3.1–8.7 % depending on condition and correlated with final agglomerate strength (tensile test on compressed beds, R² = 0.78). Pore size distributions derived from µ-CT showed a bimodal character: intra-primary-particle pores (mean diameter 12 µm) and inter-particle macropores (mean diameter 68 µm). Higher spray rate produced more heterogeneous binder distribution (spatial variance coefficient 0.38 vs 0.21 at lower spray rate). This work provides structural evidence linking process parameters to mechanical properties without destructive sample preparation.

title: Effect of inlet temperature and feed solid content on morphological descriptors of spray-dried pea protein isolate particles
abstract: Pea protein isolate (PPI, 85 % protein d.b.) was spray-dried at inlet temperatures of 150, 165 and 180 °C and feed solid contents of 10, 15 and 20 % w/w in a full 3×3 factorial design. Particle shape was characterised using automated image analysis on SEM micrographs, extracting circularity, aspect ratio and convexity for populations of 500–700 particles per condition. Circularity decreased from 0.91 to 0.76 as inlet temperature increased from 150 to 180 °C at 10 % feed solids, attributed to faster surface crust formation trapping internal vapour. Feed solid content had a dominant effect on d50 (range 18–64 µm, p < 0.001). Protein solubility index (PSI) measured after reconstitution in water at pH 7.0 ranged from 61 to 79 %, with the highest values at 150 °C inlet temperature. Bulk density increased from 280 to 430 kg/m³ with increasing feed solids content, relevant for packaging efficiency calculations.

title: Procesno inženjerstvo etarskih ulja: osnove i primenjena metodologija
abstract: Poglavlje prikazuje inženjerske osnove jediničnih operacija parne destilacije i hidrodestilacije primenjenih na biljne sirovine bogate etarskim uljima. Opisani su principi prenosa mase i toplote u biotičkim matricama, termodinamika ravnoteže para-tečnost za smeše isparljivih komponenti u prisustvu vode, kao i eksperimentalne metode za određivanje kinetičkih parametara ekstrakcije. Poseban odeljak posvećen je mernoj opremi i metodama uzorkovanja za pilot i industrijsku skalu. Razmatrani su i aspekti uštede energije: rekuperacija kondenzata, optimizacija trajanja destilacije i uticaj kvaliteta pare. Poglavlje uključuje studije slučaja za lavandu, nanu i kamilicu sa podacima iz originalnih istraživanja autora i saradnika. Namenjeno je studentima hemijskog inženjerstva i istraživačima koji ulaze u ovu oblast.
venue: Inženjerstvo prirodnih ekstrakata – monografija (ur. D. Savić, Tehnološki fakultet Novi Sad)

title: Shape grammar encoding of Austro-Hungarian block typologies in Pannonian lowland towns
abstract: Austro-Hungarian urban expansion in the late nineteenth century produced a recognisable set of block and parcel typologies across the Pannonian Plain. This paper develops a formal shape grammar that captures the generative rules governing courtyard block subdivision, facade rhythm, and cornice height relationships observed in cadastral survey records and historical photographs for five towns in Vojvodina. The grammar is implemented as a rule interpreter in a custom Python extension for the McNeel Rhinoceros environment. Validation is performed by generating synthetic block populations and comparing parcel area distributions, courtyard-to-footprint ratios, and facade setback statistics against a reference dataset of 1,240 parcels digitised from 1910–1920 cadastral sheets. Generated distributions match reference distributions with Kolmogorov–Smirnov test p-values above 0.12 for all four tested metrics. The work establishes a reusable grammar library for automated population of 3-D models of historical Vojvodina town centres and identifies four parcel sub-types not previously distinguished in the architectural history literature.

title: Extracting gable and hip roof planes from low-density airborne LiDAR over dense historical town centres
abstract: Low-density airborne LiDAR surveys (average 1.8 pts/m²) present challenges for roof plane segmentation over dense historical urban fabric where roofs are small, heavily articulated, and partially occluded by adjacent structures. This paper presents a segmentation pipeline combining RANSAC-based plane detection with a roof topology graph that enforces cadastral footprint constraints. The method is tested on a 42-hectare area of Sombor's protected historic core, containing 1,870 roof surfaces identified by manual reference annotation. Precision and recall for correct plane assignment reach 0.81 and 0.77 respectively, improving on a baseline normal-vector clustering approach by 11 and 14 percentage points. Error analysis shows the largest gains occur on L-shaped and T-shaped building footprints. Runtime on a standard workstation is under four minutes for the full test area. Reconstructed roof geometries are exported as CityGML LoD2 and validated against ground-truth photogrammetric models of 38 selected buildings.

title: Parametric reconstruction of mansard and broken-pitch roofs from cadastral footprint outlines alone
abstract: When airborne or satellite imagery is unavailable or of insufficient quality, 3-D city model generation must rely almost entirely on 2-D cadastral footprint geometry supplemented by local building regulations and typological priors. This paper addresses the specific case of mansard and broken-pitch roofs common in late nineteenth-century central European town houses. A probabilistic roof-type classifier is trained on 610 labelled footprints from four Vojvodina municipalities, using footprint shape indices, parcel area, street-front width, and inferred construction period as features. Classification accuracy on a held-out test set of 210 footprints is 74%. Roof geometry parameters are then sampled from type-conditional distributions fitted to measured survey data. The resulting models are compared visually and metrically against photogrammetric reference models; median roof ridge height error is 0.43 m. The approach is suitable for rapid LoD2 model generation where aerial coverage is absent and is intended as a fallback module within a broader reconstruction pipeline.

title: A comparative study of manual and semi-automated LoD2 city model production costs for medium-sized Serbian towns
abstract: 3-D city model production for municipalities with limited budgets requires realistic cost benchmarking to justify investment in semi-automated pipelines. This paper reports a controlled production experiment in which three medium-sized Serbian towns (Sombor, Zrenjanin, and Vršac) were modelled both manually by trained operators and through a semi-automated pipeline combining cadastral data, low-density LiDAR, and the rule-based roof reconstruction methods described in earlier work by the authors. Each approach was applied to 500-building subsets drawn from each town. Manual production required on average 4.7 operator-hours per 100 buildings at LoD2, while the semi-automated pipeline required 1.1 hours for operator oversight and correction. Geometric accuracy measured against field survey checkpoints was comparable (mean surface deviation under 0.6 m in both cases). The paper discusses error patterns specific to each town's historical building stock and recommends a hybrid workflow for projects with mixed data availability.

title: Urban morphology indices derived from procedurally generated 3-D city models: sensitivity to input data resolution
abstract: Urban morphology indices such as sky view factor, building volume density, and floor area ratio are increasingly computed from 3-D city models rather than from 2-D cadastral data alone. However, the sensitivity of these indices to the geometric accuracy of procedurally generated models has received limited systematic attention. This paper analyses a set of 18 morphology indices computed from four procedurally generated LoD2 city models of historic Novi Sad districts, each generated under five different input data resolution scenarios ranging from 0.5 pts/m² LiDAR with 1:500 cadastre to 8 pts/m² LiDAR with 1:1000 cadastre. Results show that volumetric indices are relatively insensitive to input resolution within the tested range, while indices depending on roof surface orientation—such as slope-weighted solar irradiation potential—vary by up to 23% across scenarios. Recommendations are given for minimum data requirements when specific index types are the intended output.

title: Encoding Ottoman-era building stock in the western Balkans for procedural 3-D reconstruction: a typological survey
abstract: Ottoman-era residential and commercial buildings surviving in western Balkan towns display distinct morphological features—including cumba projections, deep eaves, and irregular courtyard configurations—that are not well captured by typologies derived from central European urban models. This paper presents a field survey of 214 surviving structures across six towns in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia, measuring 31 geometric and compositional parameters per building. Cluster analysis identifies five building sub-types. For each sub-type, parametric models are constructed in Grasshopper, with parameter ranges calibrated to survey measurements. The paper discusses the difficulties of encoding irregular plan geometries and proposes a constraint relaxation strategy for footprints that deviate substantially from rectangular or L-shaped primitives. The resulting parametric models are intended as a contribution to a broader regional library of procedural building components for use in LoD2 and LoD3 city modelling projects.

title: Integrating oblique aerial photogrammetry with cadastral constraints for automated LoD3 façade reconstruction
abstract: Level-of-detail 3 (LoD3) city models require façade geometry and opening information that is difficult to derive automatically from nadir LiDAR or vertical aerial photography alone. This paper presents a workflow that combines dense point clouds from oblique aerial photogrammetry—acquired with a four-camera rig at 8 cm ground sampling distance—with cadastral footprint data and a rule-based window grammar to produce LoD3 models of a 14-block area of Subotica's Art Nouveau historic core. The photogrammetric pipeline is implemented in the Agisoft Metashape Python API, and façade segmentation uses a Random Forest classifier trained on 4,200 manually labelled façade patches. Window detection F1-score on the test façades is 0.79. The cadastral constraint step reduces footprint planimetric error by 0.18 m on average compared to unconstrained photogrammetric reconstruction. Final models are validated against 22 terrestrial laser scans of individual buildings.

title: Procedural generation of medieval street networks from sparse documentary evidence: a case study of Petrovaradin
abstract: The medieval morphological core of Petrovaradin survives only in fragmentary cadastral records, two partial vedute from the seventeenth century, and archaeological survey data collected during sewer construction in the 1990s. This paper develops a procedural reconstruction method that integrates these heterogeneous evidence sources within a probabilistic spatial model. A street network generator based on agent-based subdivision with historically informed parameter priors is calibrated against the surviving fragmentary data using approximate Bayesian computation. One hundred plausible network realisations are generated, and their statistical properties are compared with reference medieval street networks from contemporaneous Danubian towns. Results show that the surviving fragment constrains network connectivity statistics substantially but leaves local geometry distributions largely undetermined. The method is presented as a tool for heritage planning and interpretive visualisation rather than authoritative reconstruction, and all 100 realisations are made available as open data.

title: A labelled dataset of 4,800 roof segments from Serbian towns for training geometric reconstruction models
abstract: Supervised learning methods for 3-D roof reconstruction require labelled training data that reflects regional building stock characteristics. Publicly available benchmark datasets are dominated by western European and North American building types and are unsuitable for direct application to Serbian or broader Balkan urban areas without substantial distribution shift. This paper describes the construction and public release of a dataset of 4,800 manually labelled roof segments from eight Serbian towns, derived from 50 cm resolution aerial orthophotos and 2 pts/m² LiDAR surveys acquired between 2015 and 2021. Each segment is labelled with roof type (17 categories), material class (6 categories), approximate construction period, and a geometric quality flag. Inter-annotator agreement measured on a 500-segment double-annotated subset yields Cohen's kappa of 0.83 for roof type and 0.76 for material class. Dataset statistics, annotation guidelines, and baseline classification results using a standard convolutional network are reported. The dataset is released under a Creative Commons Attribution licence.

title: Roof geometry reconstruction as a service: a web API for municipality-scale LoD2 model generation
abstract: Generating LoD2 city models is technically demanding and lies outside the operational capacity of most Serbian municipalities. This paper describes the architecture and deployment of a web API that accepts cadastral footprint polygons and optional low-resolution LiDAR tiles as inputs and returns CityGML LoD2 geometries within minutes. The backend combines the roof type classifier and parametric geometry engine developed in the authors' prior work with a microservice architecture deployed on OpenStack virtual machines hosted at the University computing centre. A pilot deployment serving four municipalities in Vojvodina processed 18,400 buildings over a six-month trial period with a mean processing time of 1.3 seconds per building. Error rates measured against a 300-building validation subset drawn from each municipality are reported. The paper discusses data privacy considerations under Serbian spatial data legislation and documents the API specification to facilitate reuse by other regional research groups.

title: Detecting unauthorised rooftop additions using multi-temporal aerial orthophotos and parametric baseline models
abstract: Unauthorised construction on existing rooftops—additions of dormers, attic conversions, and terrace enclosures—is a persistent planning enforcement problem in Serbian cities. This paper presents a change detection method that compares parametric LoD2 roof models generated from cadastral data against multi-temporal aerial orthophotos acquired in 2017 and 2022 over a 9 km² area of central Novi Sad. Differences between the predicted roof appearance derived from the parametric model and observed radiometric and texture features in the 2022 orthophoto are used to flag candidate change locations. A Random Forest classifier operating on 22 image and geometry features achieves precision 0.72 and recall 0.68 on a labelled test set of 183 confirmed and 410 confirmed-negative cases. The paper discusses the method's limitations regarding small additions below 4 m² and proposes a field verification workflow for planning authorities. Results are shared with the City of Novi Sad Urban Planning Directorate.

title: Parametric roof modelling under incomplete cadastral data: handling merged parcels and split-building records in Serbian municipal registers
abstract: Serbian municipal cadastral registers contain a significant proportion of records that do not correspond one-to-one with physical buildings: parcels have been merged, subdivided, or carry building footprints that straddle parcel boundaries due to historical registration practices or incomplete updates following demolition and reconstruction. This paper analyses a sample of 6,200 building records from four municipalities and quantifies the prevalence of five problem record types. For each type, a resolution heuristic is developed and implemented as a pre-processing module for the authors' roof reconstruction pipeline. The heuristics rely on geometric consistency checks between footprint outline, parcel boundary, and a coarse orthophoto shadow mask. After pre-processing, the fraction of footprints that fail to produce geometrically valid LoD2 models drops from 18.4% to 6.1%. Residual failures are classified by cause to guide further development. The pre-processing module is released as open-source software.

title: Towards continuous LoD2 model maintenance using annually updated national aerial surveys: experience from Vojvodina 2019–2025
abstract: National mapping agencies in several European countries now conduct annual aerial surveys at resolutions sufficient to detect significant building changes. This paper reports on a six-year operational experiment exploiting the annual orthophoto and LiDAR campaigns of the Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia over Vojvodina province to maintain and incrementally update LoD2 city models for 11 municipalities. The update pipeline detects change candidates using the method reported in the authors' 2023 conference paper, then triggers targeted re-reconstruction for flagged buildings only, rather than reprocessing entire model areas. Over six annual cycles, the median number of buildings re-reconstructed per municipality per year is 340, representing approximately 2.8% of the total stock. Model currency as measured against field survey validation samples improves from 81% to 94% accurate-to-current over the six-year period. The paper discusses organisational arrangements with the municipalities and data licensing constraints encountered during the project.

title: The Spatial Structure of Noble Estate Complexes in Syrmia: Core, Service Yard, and Park Boundaries in Twelve Case Studies
abstract: Twelve manor estate complexes in the Syrmia region, dating from the late eighteenth to early twentieth century, were documented through measured drawing, archival plan retrieval, and photogrammetric recording of surviving structures. For each complex the relationships between the residential core, farm service yards, formal garden or park enclosure, and estate road network were mapped and described. The twelve cases were drawn from three ownership typologies: ecclesiastical estates, Habsburg military officer families, and Hungarian aristocratic landholdings. Comparative spatial diagrams highlight a recurrent tripartite organisation—formal approach axis, residential precinct, and productive rear yard—irrespective of ownership type or construction decade. Significant variation is found in the degree of axial symmetry and in the spatial integration of the icehouse, coach house, and granary. Two complexes retain original estate plans in Croatian and Serbian archives, which are reproduced and compared with current survey results, revealing post-1945 alterations in eight of the twelve cases.

title: The effect of tree species selection on summer thermal comfort along a pedestrian corridor: a simulation-based comparison
abstract: Urban tree planting is frequently cited as a heat mitigation measure, but the thermal benefits differ substantially among species depending on crown geometry, leaf area index (LAI), and albedo. This study compared four deciduous tree species — two large-crowned species (LAI ≈ 6.2 and 5.8) and two medium-crowned species (LAI ≈ 3.9 and 4.1) — planted in a 280-metre north–south pedestrian corridor in Novi Sad. Single-tree and avenue configurations were constructed in ENVI-met 4.4 using manufacturer-supplied morphological parameters verified against field measurements taken in Futog arboretum. Simulations were run for a reference summer design day (2 August 2021) under current climate data from the regional meteorological service. The large-crowned species reduced midday PET by 6.3–7.8 °C compared to a no-tree baseline, while medium-crowned species achieved reductions of 3.9–4.7 °C. Spacing between trees at 6 m vs 10 m intervals produced a further 1.2 °C PET difference. Wind speed reduction from avenue planting was limited to 8–12% at pedestrian level, suggesting radiation shading dominates the thermal effect in this corridor geometry.

title: Riverfront Brownfields as Habitat Stepping Stones: A Landscape Connectivity Analysis for the Vojvodina Danube Corridor
abstract: This paper applies graph-theoretic landscape connectivity analysis to assess whether the fragmented series of derelict and partially remediated riverfront brownfield sites along the Vojvodina Danube reach could function collectively as a habitat stepping-stone network for generalist wetland bird and amphibian species. Using habitat suitability models calibrated against breeding bird survey transect data (2011–2019) and amphibian population counts from 14 sites, the study calculates patch importance values (dPC index) for 38 brownfield parcels between Novi Sad and Bačka Palanka. Removing the five highest-ranked patches from the network would reduce overall connectivity by 43 percent for modelled bird species and 61 percent for amphibians. The results are used to argue that planning decisions about individual brownfield sites should reference network-level ecological value rather than site-level assessment alone. Integration of connectivity metrics into Vojvodina spatial planning documents is discussed, with reference to EU Biodiversity Strategy target frameworks.

title: Applying population surface modelling to monitor inter-censal demographic change in depopulating Vojvodinian municipalities
abstract: Census data in Serbia are collected decennially and published with a two- to three-year lag, creating significant uncertainty for planning purposes in rapidly depopulating areas. This paper tests the use of dasymetric population surface modelling, calibrated against the 2011 census and updated with annual municipal vital statistics and migration balance data, to generate inter-censal population estimates at the settlement level for 63 municipalities in Vojvodina for the years 2012–2021. Model estimates are validated against the preliminary results of the 2022 census. Mean absolute percentage error across settlements was 4.8%, rising to 9.2% in settlements below 2,000 inhabitants where administrative registration of migration is less reliable. The modelled surfaces show that eleven municipalities lost more than 15% of their 2011 population by 2021, with the highest losses concentrated in the north-eastern Banat area. Implications for updating local spatial plans on a sub-decennial basis are discussed.

title: Shrinkage indicators and spatial planning obligations in EU candidate countries: a comparative review of Serbia, North Macedonia, and Moldova
abstract: This preprint compares how three EU candidate or aspiring countries—Serbia, North Macedonia, and Moldova—have translated (or failed to translate) the EU Cohesion Policy objective of territorial cohesion into planning obligations addressing urban and rural shrinkage. The review covers national spatial planning legislation, regional development strategies, and any explicit shrinkage monitoring frameworks adopted between 2015 and 2025. Data were gathered through document analysis supplemented by 18 semi-structured interviews with national-level planners and ministry officials. Serbia is the furthest advanced in acknowledging shrinkage in regional planning documents but lacks binding municipal-level requirements. North Macedonia has produced demographic projections that acknowledge decline but these are not linked to land-use planning instruments. Moldova has the most severe depopulation rates among the three but the least developed planning response. The paper sketches a minimal harmonisation framework that EU accession negotiations could promote.

title: Lifecycle Carbon Assessment of a Prefabricated Timber-Frame Panel System Produced in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina
abstract: This paper presents a gate-to-grave lifecycle assessment of a prefabricated closed-panel timber-frame wall system manufactured by a small enterprise in the Srem district of Vojvodina. Primary production data were collected directly from the factory over a six-month monitoring period, covering electricity consumption, wood raw material volumes, waste board generation, and transport to construction sites. The functional unit is one square metre of installed exterior wall panel achieving a U-value of 0.22 W/m²K. Ecoinvent 3.6 datasets were used for background processes, with the Serbian electricity grid mix for 2019 applied from data published by the Energy Agency of the Republic of Serbia. The cradle-to-gate embodied carbon of the panel is 28.4 kg CO₂e/m². End-of-life scenarios tested include landfill, incineration with heat recovery, and mechanical recycling of the OSB facing; incineration with heat recovery produces the lowest net lifecycle carbon at 31.6 kg CO₂e/m² when displacement of natural gas heating is credited. Uncertainty analysis using Monte Carlo simulation (n = 10,000) yields a 90% confidence interval of ±4.8 kg CO₂e/m² for the cradle-to-gate figure.
