title: Acoustic correlator performance under varying pipe material and diameter conditions in municipal water mains
abstract: Acoustic leak detection by correlator relies on the propagation speed of leak noise along pipe walls, which differs substantially between ductile iron, PVC, and asbestos cement mains. This study reports controlled field experiments on 14 pipe segments of the Subotica municipal network, covering diameters from 80 mm to 400 mm, with artificially induced leaks at known positions. Correlation distances ranged from 40 m to 310 m. Signal propagation velocities were measured with calibrated hydrophones and compared against theoretical predictions based on pipe wall stiffness and fluid compressibility. Results showed that standard factory-default velocity values caused localisation errors exceeding 3 m in 60 percent of PVC trials. A correction procedure based on in-situ velocity calibration reduced median localisation error from 2.8 m to 0.7 m across all materials tested. Practical guidelines are proposed for field operators selecting propagation velocity settings prior to survey campaigns.

title: Pressure zone partitioning as a tool for reducing background leakage in a medium-sized Serbian town
abstract: Background leakage in water distribution systems is strongly pressure-dependent. This paper examines the restructuring of the distribution network of a town of approximately 85 000 inhabitants in northern Serbia into six district metered areas (DMAs). Hydraulic modelling was performed using steady-state and extended-period simulations calibrated against 18 months of SCADA flow and pressure data. Minimum night flow analysis was used to estimate real losses before and after DMA implementation. Pressure reducing valves were installed at five inlet points; setpoint optimisation was carried out to maintain service pressures above 2.5 bar at all demand nodes under peak-hour conditions. After restructuring, average system pressure dropped by 0.38 bar and estimated real losses decreased by 22 percent over a 12-month monitoring period. The paper discusses difficulties encountered in calibrating the model against a partially unmapped secondary network and proposes a field survey protocol for similar conditions.

title: Transient pressure wave analysis for leak detection: a comparison of time-domain and frequency-domain methods on laboratory pipe rigs
abstract: Transient-based leak detection exploits reflections of pressure waves generated by controlled valve operations. This study compares time-domain reflectometry and frequency-domain transfer matrix approaches on two experimental pipe rigs of 45 m and 120 m length with internal diameters of 50 mm and 100 mm, respectively. Leaks were simulated with calibrated orifices representing 0.05 to 0.5 percent of pipe cross-section. The frequency-domain method identified leak positions with a mean error of 1.2 m in the 45 m rig but degraded to 3.8 m mean error in the 120 m rig due to signal damping. Time-domain reflectometry performed more consistently across rig lengths when transient source rise times were below 20 ms. The influence of trapped air pockets on false-positive reflection signals is documented and quantified for four experimental configurations. Recommendations are given for instrumentation bandwidth and sampling frequency in practical surveys.

title: Minimum night flow decomposition for estimating customer night use and genuine leakage at DMA level
abstract: Separating genuine background leakage from legitimate night-time customer consumption is a persistent problem in minimum night flow (MNF) analysis. This paper presents a decomposition procedure applied to data from eight DMAs in two Serbian towns, using meter pulse logging at 15-minute intervals on 630 domestic meters over periods of 6 to 18 months. Customer night use was estimated from the logged data using a statistical mixture model fitted to demand patterns segmented by property type. Mean customer night use was found to be 1.7 litres per property per hour, with a 90th-percentile value of 4.1 litres per property per hour, somewhat higher than UK reference values commonly cited in the water loss literature. Applying local night use estimates reduced apparent per-connection leakage figures by 18 to 31 percent compared to using default values. Uncertainty bounds for the decomposition are derived and their sensitivity to meter coverage rate is analysed.

title: Pressure management in aged cast iron networks: balancing leakage reduction against burst risk
abstract: Lowering operating pressure to reduce leakage is sometimes argued to increase burst frequency in aged cast iron mains because residual soil and internal stresses become relatively larger. This study analyses burst records from a 340 km cast iron network in Vojvodina over a 15-year period, cross-referenced with historical pressure logs and pipe condition data from 1 240 inspected segments. A negative binomial regression model relates annual burst rate to mean operating pressure, pipe age, wall thickness category, and soil corrosivity index. The estimated pressure elasticity of burst frequency is −0.31 (95% CI: −0.52 to −0.09), indicating that modest pressure reductions do not increase burst risk in this network and may slightly reduce it. Threshold pressures below which burst rates begin to rise are identified for three age cohorts. Results challenge the assumption that pressure reduction is contraindicated in old cast iron systems without site-specific evidence.

title: Hydraulic simulation of pressure reducing valve setpoint optimisation under diurnal demand variation
abstract: Fixed-setpoint pressure reducing valves (PRVs) are sized for worst-case demand and consequently over-pressure the network during low-demand periods, sustaining unnecessary leakage. This paper evaluates time-modulated and flow-modulated PRV operation strategies using extended-period hydraulic simulations of a 1 200-node model of a northern Serbian distribution zone. Three control strategies are compared: fixed setpoint, time-of-day scheduling with four daily steps, and a flow-modulated setpoint derived from an empirically fitted downstream flow–pressure relationship. Modelled leakage is estimated using the FAVAD pressure–leakage relationship with exponents calibrated from field MNF data. Flow-modulated control reduced modelled annual leakage by a further 9 percent relative to fixed setpoint and 5 percent relative to time scheduling, with no service pressure violations recorded in 98 000 simulated demand scenarios drawn from demand uncertainty distributions. Practical implementation constraints related to SCADA latency and actuator reliability are discussed.

title: Water loss assessment in small rural distribution systems: applicability of IWA component analysis
abstract: The IWA water balance and component loss framework was designed primarily for urban distribution systems with reliable metering infrastructure. This paper tests its applicability in 12 rural supply zones in the Bačka region of Vojvodina, each serving between 800 and 6 000 connections with a mix of domestic meters of varying age and accuracy. Bulk meter data, customer billing records, and targeted MNF surveys were combined to construct annual water balances. Apparent losses attributable to meter under-registration were estimated by gravimetric bench testing of 240 removed meters stratified by age class; mean under-registration was 7.4 percent across meters older than 12 years. Real losses ranged from 31 to 58 percent of system input volume across the 12 zones. The paper identifies data gaps that limit the precision of component analysis in rural settings and proposes a simplified protocol adapted to available data quality.

title: Pipe network modelling for water utilities: from data collection to operational use
abstract: This book chapter provides a practical account of the full workflow for developing and maintaining hydraulic models of water distribution networks in small-to-medium utility contexts, drawing on two decades of project experience in Serbia and neighbouring countries. Topics covered include GIS data collection and quality checking, skeletonisation criteria for networks up to 2 500 km of main, calibration using fire-flow tests and continuous pressure monitoring, and the organisational steps needed to keep models current as the physical network changes. Particular attention is given to demand allocation methods when individual metering data are unavailable or incomplete, and to the transfer of models from consultants to in-house utility staff. Case examples from three Vojvodina utilities illustrate common calibration problems and their resolution. The chapter is aimed at practising engineers rather than researchers.

title: Evaluating correlator-based leak survey frequency and its effect on real loss levels in a medium-pressure distribution zone over an eight-year period
abstract: Leak detection survey intervals determine how long unreported bursts and seeping joint failures contribute to real losses before repair. This retrospective study analyses eight years of repair records, correlator survey logs, and quarterly MNF estimates for a defined 280 km distribution zone in northern Serbia. Survey intervals varied from 18 months to 4 years across sub-zones due to budget constraints, providing a quasi-natural experiment. For each sub-zone, real loss trajectories between successive surveys were reconstructed from MNF data, and the reduction achieved by each survey was estimated. The marginal benefit of shortening survey interval from 36 to 18 months was estimated at a 14 percent reduction in average annual real losses; further reduction to 12 months yielded an additional 7 percent. An economic optimisation framework is applied to identify cost-minimising survey frequencies under different repair cost and water value assumptions.

title: Pressure transient data as a secondary source for pipe condition assessment: a field study on a mixed-age network
abstract: Controlled transient tests generate pressure wave signals whose attenuation and dispersion carry information about pipe wall condition in addition to leak position. This paper reports a field study on 22 km of mixed-age ductile iron and steel mains in a Vojvodina distribution zone where independent condition data from external ultrasonic wall thickness measurements and excavation records were available for 38 pipe segments. Transient decay coefficients extracted from logged pressure traces were compared against wall thickness loss indices derived from the independent data. A moderate correlation (Pearson r = 0.61) was found between decay coefficient and wall loss index across the tested segments, with weaker correlation in segments with irregular tuberculation. The paper discusses the practical limitations of using transient data alone for condition assessment and identifies pipe configurations where the approach yields reliable supplementary information alongside conventional survey methods.

title: Brain tumour segmentation with limited annotations
abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain tumours in MRI scans is a critical step in clinical diagnosis and treatment planning, yet it remains challenging due to high variability in tumour appearance and the significant cost of obtaining expert annotations. This paper investigates semi-supervised and weakly supervised deep learning strategies for brain tumour segmentation when only a limited number of fully labelled training samples are available. We adapt a U-Net-based architecture augmented with consistency regularisation and pseudo-labelling to leverage a larger pool of unannotated MRI volumes. Experiments are conducted on a curated subset of publicly available multi-modal brain MRI data, including T1, T2, and FLAIR sequences. We evaluate the proposed approach against fully supervised baselines under annotation budgets ranging from 5% to 30% of the training set. Results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive Dice scores compared to fully supervised counterparts while requiring substantially fewer annotated cases. Qualitative analysis confirms that the model produces anatomically plausible segmentation boundaries even in low-data regimes. These findings suggest that semi-supervised U-Net variants offer a practical pathway toward deployable tumour segmentation in resource-constrained clinical environments.

title: Attention-gated U-Net for automated hippocampus segmentation in structural MRI
abstract: Hippocampus segmentation in structural MRI is a clinically relevant task for the assessment of neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease and temporal lobe epilepsy. Manual delineation by radiologists is time-consuming and subject to inter-rater variability, motivating the development of automated methods. In this work, we propose an attention-gated U-Net that incorporates soft attention mechanisms at skip connections to suppress irrelevant activations and focus feature learning on the small, irregularly shaped hippocampal region. The model is trained on T1-weighted MRI volumes and evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. We compare performance against a standard U-Net baseline and a V-Net variant, reporting Dice similarity coefficient, Hausdorff distance, and volumetric overlap error. Attention gating improves mean Dice by 2.3 percentage points over the standard U-Net while adding negligible computational overhead. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of attention modules at each decoder stage. Visual inspection shows sharper delineation of hippocampal boundaries, particularly near the subiculum. The results support the use of attention-gated architectures for small-structure segmentation tasks in neuroimaging pipelines.

title: Data augmentation strategies for improving MRI segmentation under domain shift
abstract: Deep learning models for MRI segmentation often suffer performance degradation when deployed on data acquired at different sites or with different scanner protocols, a phenomenon known as domain shift. Addressing this challenge without access to target-domain labels is essential for the clinical adoption of automated segmentation tools. This study systematically evaluates a suite of MRI-specific data augmentation strategies—including random bias field simulation, intensity histogram matching, and elastic deformations—as a low-cost approach to improve model robustness across domains. We train a U-Net backbone on single-site brain MRI data and assess generalisation on two held-out datasets acquired with distinct scanner vendors and field strengths. Augmentation strategies are evaluated individually and in combination, measuring Dice coefficient and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance on white matter lesion and ventricle segmentation tasks. Combined augmentation reduces the mean domain-shift performance gap by approximately 18% relative to a baseline trained without augmentation. Further analysis reveals that bias field simulation provides the largest individual contribution. These findings provide practical guidelines for practitioners seeking to enhance model generalisability without requiring additional labelled data from target domains.

title: Towards uncertainty-aware segmentation of white matter lesions in FLAIR MRI
abstract: White matter lesion segmentation in FLAIR MRI is complicated by the high variability in lesion size, shape, and spatial distribution, as well as by annotation ambiguity at lesion boundaries. Uncertainty estimation in deep learning segmentation models can provide clinicians with valuable information about prediction reliability, supporting safer integration into diagnostic workflows. This paper presents a Monte Carlo Dropout-based uncertainty estimation framework built on a U-Net architecture trained for white matter lesion segmentation. We generate voxel-level uncertainty maps by performing multiple stochastic forward passes at inference time and aggregating the resulting prediction distributions. We evaluate the correlation between predicted uncertainty and segmentation error, demonstrating that high-uncertainty voxels are strongly associated with incorrect predictions and ambiguous boundary regions. Experiments on a multi-site FLAIR MRI dataset show that uncertainty thresholding can flag unreliable predictions for human review, improving effective precision without sacrificing recall on high-confidence voxels. We further propose a simple active learning loop in which uncertain samples are prioritised for expert annotation, accelerating model improvement in low-resource settings. The proposed framework represents a step toward trustworthy, clinician-in-the-loop medical image segmentation systems.

title: Thermal denaturation of sunflower 2S albumin SFA-8: a differential scanning calorimetry study
abstract: The thermal stability of the major sunflower seed 2S albumin SFA-8 was investigated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) over a pH range of 4.0–9.0 and protein concentrations of 0.5–5.0 mg/mL. Calorimetric scans revealed a single endothermic transition with a denaturation temperature (Tm) of 83.4 °C at pH 7.0 and ionic strength 50 mM NaCl. Decreasing pH to 4.0 reduced Tm by approximately 6 °C and broadened the transition peak, indicating partial destabilisation of the tertiary structure. The calorimetric enthalpy (ΔHcal) ranged from 210 to 345 kJ/mol depending on conditions. Reversibility tests showed that approximately 40% of the transition was reversible at pH 7.0, dropping to below 15% at pH 4.0. These findings provide a quantitative thermodynamic framework for understanding sunflower protein behaviour under conditions relevant to oil seed processing and food ingredient manufacture.

title: Aggregation kinetics of sunflower seed albumins at mildly acidic pH: a combined light scattering and fluorescence approach
abstract: The aggregation behaviour of sunflower seed albumins at pH 5.0, close to the isoelectric point, was studied by dynamic light scattering (DLS) and thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence at temperatures between 60 and 80 °C. At 70 °C and pH 5.0, DLS revealed rapid formation of particles with hydrodynamic radii growing from approximately 5 nm to over 400 nm within 30 minutes. ThT binding assays indicated that early aggregates possessed modest amyloid-like cross-β character, with ThT fluorescence increasing three- to fourfold relative to baseline over 60 minutes. At pH 7.0, aggregation was substantially slower and produced smaller final particles (mean Rh ≈ 120 nm after 60 min). The presence of 150 mM NaCl accelerated aggregation at pH 5.0 but had negligible effect at pH 7.0. These results have practical implications for processing conditions in protein ingredient production from sunflower press cake.

title: Effect of ionic strength and divalent cations on the conformational stability of hemp seed 2S albumin
abstract: Hemp (Cannabis sativa) seed 2S albumin was isolated by ammonium sulfate precipitation followed by size-exclusion chromatography and its conformational stability examined by DSC and far-UV circular dichroism under varying ionic conditions. Addition of Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ (0–10 mM) produced concentration-dependent increases in Tm of up to 4.1 °C and 2.7 °C respectively, while monovalent Na⁺ at physiological concentration had no significant effect on Tm. Far-UV CD spectra at 25 °C showed a predominantly α-helical signature (minima at 208 and 222 nm) typical of 2S albumins, with helical content estimated at 42%. At elevated Ca²⁺ (5 mM), the melting enthalpy increased by approximately 18% relative to metal-free buffer, suggesting stabilisation of inter-helical contacts. These observations are consistent with a weak but specific divalent cation binding site and are relevant to formulation of hemp protein isolates for functional food applications.

title: Comparative thermodynamic profiles of 2S albumins from four oilseed species: rapeseed, sesame, sunflower and flaxseed
abstract: A systematic comparative analysis of the thermal stability of 2S albumins isolated from rapeseed (Brassica napus), sesame (Sesamum indicum), sunflower (Helianthus annuus) and flaxseed (Linum usitatissimum) was carried out by DSC at pH 7.0 and 4.5. Rapeseed albumin napin displayed the highest Tm (91.2 °C at pH 7.0), while flaxseed albumin showed the lowest (68.7 °C). Across all four species, reduction of pH from 7.0 to 4.5 lowered Tm by 4–9 °C and reduced ΔHcal by 10–25%. Comparison of ΔHcal/ΔHvH ratios suggested that all four albumins undergo predominantly two-state transitions, with napin showing the greatest cooperativity (ratio closest to 1.0). Sequence-based predictions of disulfide bond number correlated positively with Tm (r = 0.94), supporting the view that the conserved disulfide scaffold is the primary determinant of thermostability in this protein family. The study provides a reference dataset for food technologists selecting protein sources for heat-processed products.

title: Modulation of rapeseed napin unfolding by sucrose and trehalose: a DSC and fluorescence study with implications for spray-drying
abstract: The capacity of the disaccharides sucrose and trehalose to stabilise rapeseed napin against thermal denaturation and aggregation was investigated in the context of spray-drying applications. DSC experiments showed that both sugars increased Tm in a concentration-dependent manner: 300 mM sucrose raised Tm from 91.2 to 95.8 °C, while trehalose at the same concentration raised it to 97.1 °C. Preferential exclusion of both sugars from the protein surface was inferred from positive ΔTm/Δmolality slopes consistent with previously reported preferential hydration coefficients. Intrinsic fluorescence thermal scans confirmed a corresponding upward shift in the unfolding midpoint. DLS measurements of samples heated to 85 °C demonstrated that trehalose reduced the mean aggregate diameter from 310 nm to 74 nm relative to sugar-free controls. The aggregation suppression by trehalose was partly maintained even after reconstitution of spray-dried powders, suggesting practical utility for formulation of napin-enriched protein powders.

title: Sequential extraction and stability characterisation of albumin and globulin fractions from cold-pressed hemp seed cake
abstract: Hemp seed press cake, a by-product of cold-press oil extraction, was used as starting material for sequential protein extraction following Osborne fractionation adapted for small-scale laboratory processing. The albumin fraction (water-soluble) and globulin fraction (salt-soluble) were isolated, and their purity was confirmed by SDS-PAGE and size-exclusion HPLC. Yield was 8.3% and 21.4% of dry cake mass for albumin and globulin fractions respectively. DSC analysis of the albumin fraction showed a Tm of 71.3 °C at pH 7.0, with a ΔHcal of 189 kJ/mol. The globulin fraction exhibited two overlapping transitions at 78 °C and 87 °C, consistent with edestin subunit heterogeneity. Intrinsic fluorescence spectra suggested a more solvent-exposed tryptophan environment in the globulin fraction compared to albumin. Storage stability tests at 4 °C over 28 days showed albumin fractions retained over 85% of native secondary structure by CD, while globulin fractions aggregated partially under the same conditions.

title: Probing early aggregation intermediates of sesame 2S albumin by size-exclusion chromatography coupled with multi-angle light scattering
abstract: Early-stage aggregation intermediates of sesame 2S albumin were characterised by size-exclusion chromatography coupled online with multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS) and differential refractive index detection. Samples were heated at 65 °C for intervals of 2, 5, 10, 20, and 40 minutes at pH 5.5, conditions representing moderate thermal stress below the Tm. At 5 minutes, SEC-MALS resolved a dimer population with a molar mass of 31.4 kDa alongside the monomer peak (15.8 kDa). By 20 minutes, oligomeric species spanning 50–200 kDa comprised approximately 35% of total integrated elution area. The second virial coefficient A2, determined by static light scattering across protein concentrations of 0.2–2.5 mg/mL, shifted from positive at 25 °C to slightly negative at 65 °C, indicating a transition to net attractive intermolecular interactions at the stress temperature. Intrinsic fluorescence of isolated dimer fractions showed a 4 nm red shift relative to monomer, confirming partial structural rearrangement. These data define a pre-nucleation window potentially relevant to controlling texture formation in sesame-based food products.

title: Thermal and pH stability of 2S albumins as functional ingredients: an overview of biophysical approaches and industrial relevance
abstract: This chapter summarises biophysical methods used to characterise the conformational stability of 2S seed storage albumins from oilseed crops, with emphasis on DSC, intrinsic fluorescence spectroscopy, CD, and light scattering techniques. The discussion covers the thermodynamic parameters typically extracted from DSC experiments (Tm, ΔHcal, ΔHvH, and reversibility), the interpretation of fluorescence emission shifts and quenching data in terms of structural changes, and the added value of combining multiple methods for a more complete picture of the unfolding landscape. A section on pH effects relates pKa changes in ionisable side chains to destabilisation mechanisms at acidic and alkaline conditions. Case studies drawn from sunflower, rapeseed, and sesame albumins illustrate how these parameters map onto processing scenarios including pasteurisation, acid precipitation, and spray-drying. The chapter concludes by discussing how stability data can inform selection of oilseed proteins for incorporation into plant-based food products and nutraceutical formulations.

title: FISH-based localisation of ammonia-oxidising bacteria within drinking water pipe biofilms
abstract: Fluorescence in situ hybridisation (FISH) with probe Nso1225 targeting betaproteobacterial ammonia-oxidising bacteria (AOB) was combined with DAPI staining to examine the spatial distribution of AOB within intact biofilm sections recovered from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and ductile iron pipe coupons deployed for 90 days in a pilot-scale distribution loop operating at chloramine residuals between 1.0 and 2.5 mg/L as Cl₂. Confocal laser scanning microscopy revealed that AOB-positive cells were more abundant in the deeper, DAPI-dense microcolonies (mean depth 8–15 µm from the pipe surface) than in the biofilm–water interface layer, suggesting that the biofilm matrix attenuates chloramine penetration sufficiently to permit AOB survival. On iron coupons, corrosion tubercles harboured higher FISH signal intensities compared with PVC. Quantification of Nso1225-positive cells relative to DAPI yielded AOB fractions of 4.2 ± 1.1% (iron) and 1.9 ± 0.6% (PVC), with the difference being statistically significant (p = 0.018, Wilcoxon test).
venue: Biofilm Research and Environmental Applications

title: Fatigue Life Estimation of Involute Spur Gears Under Variable-Amplitude Tooth-Root Bending Using Rainflow Counting and Local Strain Approach
abstract: This study presents a fatigue life estimation procedure for involute spur gear pairs subjected to variable-amplitude bending loads at the tooth root. Stress histories were obtained from a combination of quasi-static finite-element analysis in MSC Nastran and measured torque spectra from a back-to-back gear test rig operating at 1450 rpm. Rainflow cycle counting was applied to recorded stress time series spanning 12 million cycles across three load levels. The local strain approach with the Morrow mean-stress correction was used to convert cycle counts into damage fractions. Predicted fatigue lives agreed with experimentally determined lives to within a factor of 1.8 across five gear pairs, which is within the typical scatter band for this material class (18CrNiMo7-6 case-hardened steel). Sensitivity analysis showed that the assumed surface finish correction factor contributed the largest uncertainty to the prediction, accounting for roughly 30% of the total variance in predicted life. The procedure was validated against two independent datasets from published literature.

title: Experimental Modal Analysis of a Centrifugal Pump Casing: Comparison of Impact Hammer and Stepped-Sine Excitation Methods
abstract: Modal parameters of a cast-iron centrifugal pump casing were identified using two experimental methods: roving impact hammer testing and stepped-sine forced excitation. Measurements were taken at 68 grid points using uni-axial accelerometers, and frequency response functions were computed in the range 20–2000 Hz. The PolyMAX estimator was applied to hammer test data, while the circle-fit method was used for stepped-sine results. Natural frequencies identified by the two methods agreed to within 1.2% for the first six elastic modes, but damping ratios showed greater discrepancy, differing by up to 18% for the third mode at 487 Hz, which exhibited close mode spacing. Mode shapes were compared using the modal assurance criterion; all MAC diagonal values exceeded 0.91. The study provides reference modal data that were subsequently used to validate a free-free finite-element model of the casing. Recommendations on accelerometer placement to avoid mass-loading effects on thin-walled sections are discussed.

title: Frequency-Domain Finite-Element Prediction of Vibration Fatigue Damage in a Welded Steel Frame Subjected to Random Base Excitation
abstract: A frequency-domain approach to vibration fatigue assessment was applied to a welded hollow-section steel frame used as a substructure in agricultural machinery. The power spectral density of the base acceleration input was measured on a working combine harvester at three locations over a 45-minute operating cycle and represented by a broadband PSD with dominant energy between 8 and 60 Hz. A linear finite-element model of the frame was built in ANSYS Mechanical and subjected to harmonic base excitation sweeps to obtain stress transfer functions at 14 weld toe locations identified by pre-service inspection as fatigue-critical. Damage was accumulated using the Dirlik probability density function for cycle amplitude estimation combined with an IIW class-71 S–N curve for fillet welds. Predicted damage indices ranged from 0.04 to 1.31 across the 14 locations, with one weld toe at the main longitudinal-to-cross-member junction exceeding unity. Physical crack initiation at that location after approximately 1200 operating hours confirmed the prediction. The mesh sensitivity around weld toes and the influence of residual stress assumptions are discussed.

title: Rotordynamic Analysis of a Two-Stage Helical Gearbox Including Bearing Flexibility and Gyroscopic Effects
abstract: A rotordynamic model of a two-stage helical gearbox was constructed using Timoshenko beam elements for the shafts, with bearing stiffness matrices derived from measured load-deflection curves of tapered roller bearings. Gyroscopic effects were included through the consistent mass matrix formulation. The model predicted critical speeds and unbalance response in the speed range 0–6000 rpm. Campbell diagram analysis revealed a resonance crossing near 3200 rpm where the second bending mode of the intermediate shaft coincided with the gear mesh frequency harmonic of the first stage (z₁ = 24 teeth). Experimental validation was performed using proximity probes at both bearing journals; measured shaft orbital amplitudes at run-up agreed with predictions within 15% at all test speeds. A parametric study examined the sensitivity of the first critical speed to bearing radial clearance, showing a shift of approximately 4.7% per 20 µm change in clearance. The model was used to guide shaft shoulder radius modifications that moved the resonance crossing above the operating range.

title: High-Cycle Fatigue Behaviour of Laser-Welded Thin-Walled Steel Tubes Under Combined Bending and Torsion
abstract: Thin-walled circular tubes of S355 structural steel, joined by circumferential laser welds, were tested under combined in-phase and out-of-phase bending–torsion loading at stress ratios of R = −1 and R = 0. A total of 72 specimens were tested to failure or run-out at 10⁷ cycles. The normal stress amplitude at the weld toe at 10⁷ cycles was 112 MPa for pure bending and 74 MPa for pure torsion. Under combined loading with a biaxiality ratio of λ = 0.5, the von Mises equivalent stress criterion over-predicted fatigue strength by 11% in-phase and under-predicted it by 8% out-of-phase, while the critical plane approach using the Findley criterion agreed with measured data to within ±6% across all load cases. Fracture surface examination by scanning electron microscopy confirmed fatigue crack initiation at weld root undercuts in 68% of specimens. Recommendations for weld quality class assignments under combined loading are proposed based on the experimental data.

title: Structural Health Monitoring of a Wind Turbine Tower Section Using Operational Modal Analysis Under Ambient Wind Loading
abstract: Operational modal analysis was applied to a 12-metre steel lattice tower section of a 750 kW wind turbine located in Vojvodina, Serbia, using only ambient wind excitation. Acceleration data were recorded over 30 ten-minute measurement blocks at eight tri-axial nodes during a one-week campaign covering wind speeds from 4 to 14 m/s. The stochastic subspace identification algorithm in the data-driven formulation identified five structural modes between 1.1 and 18.4 Hz consistently across all measurement blocks. Identified natural frequencies showed a repeatable variation of up to 2.3% with wind speed, attributed to aerodynamic stiffness contributions. A reference finite-element model was updated by minimising the frequency and MAC-based residuals, reducing the average frequency error from 6.1% to 1.4%. Changes in modal damping ratios between two inspection campaigns twelve months apart were within the estimation uncertainty, indicating no detectable structural change. The measurement protocol and SSI parameter selection guidelines derived from this study are applicable to similar lattice towers.

title: Comparative Assessment of S–N and Strain–Life Approaches for Fatigue Life Prediction of Notched Machine Components Under Spectrum Loading
abstract: Fatigue life predictions using two approaches—nominal stress S–N with Miner linear damage accumulation and strain–life with the Ramberg–Osgood cyclic stress–strain curve—were compared for a set of notched round bar specimens (Kt = 1.8, 2.5, 3.2) machined from 42CrMo4 quenched and tempered steel. Specimens were tested under four standardised variable-amplitude load sequences derived from automotive and agricultural machinery measurements with distinct irregularity factors (I = 0.62 and I = 0.34). At the two higher stress concentration factors, the strain–life method with Neuber plasticity correction produced life estimates within a scatter band of ±2.5 on life, while the nominal S–N approach yielded non-conservative estimates by a factor exceeding 4 at Kt = 3.2 under the irregular sequence (I = 0.34). Both methods converged for mild notches (Kt = 1.8). The study quantifies the boundary conditions under which each method is suitable and provides a decision matrix for practitioners selecting a fatigue assessment method for notched components at the design stage.

title: Fatigue Assessment of a Planetary Gearbox Ring Gear With Press-Fit Hub Interface Under Cyclic Torque Reversal
abstract: A fatigue assessment of the ring gear–hub press-fit interface of a planetary gearbox used in construction machinery was performed for operating torques cycling between +1850 N·m and −620 N·m at 0.5 Hz. The contact pressure distribution at the interference fit was computed with an axisymmetric finite-element model accounting for manufacturing tolerances (fit range H7/s6) and frictional contact (µ = 0.12). Cyclic fretting fatigue conditions were identified at the fit edge where the contact pressure dropped below a threshold of 18 MPa during the negative torque half-cycle, producing small relative microslip amplitudes of 3–7 µm. Fretting fatigue life was estimated using a critical plane criterion with an additional fretting damage factor calibrated from literature data on comparable interference-fit assemblies. Predicted crack initiation life of approximately 280 000 cycles agreed with a fleet inspection record showing ring gear replacements at 250 000–320 000 cycles. Geometry modifications reducing the peak hoop stress by 12% through an annular relief groove are proposed and evaluated.

title: Frequency-Domain Stress Analysis of a Reciprocating Compressor Frame Under Piston-Force Harmonics Using Component Mode Synthesis
abstract: A frequency-domain structural analysis of a two-cylinder reciprocating air compressor frame was performed to identify vibration-induced stress concentrations under the first eight harmonics of piston force (fundamental at 25 Hz, shaft speed 1500 rpm). The full-assembly finite-element model comprised approximately 1.2 million tetrahedral elements; component mode synthesis with 40 retained modes per substructure reduced the computational cost by a factor of 7.4 relative to direct harmonic analysis while preserving stress accuracy to within 3.5% at all monitored locations. Frequency response functions were computed from 10 to 400 Hz. Peak equivalent stress amplitudes of 87 MPa were found at the cylinder-to-frame fillet at the third harmonic (75 Hz) and 64 MPa at a main bearing housing rib at the fifth harmonic (125 Hz). Experimentally measured strain gauge signals at four frame locations confirmed predicted stress amplitudes to within 11%. The study also demonstrates that ignoring the sixth and seventh harmonics, common in simplified analyses, leads to underestimation of the maximum stress amplitude by 19%.

title: Updating a Finite-Element Model of an Agricultural Gearbox Housing Using Measured Frequency Response Functions and Bayesian Optimisation
abstract: A finite-element model of a cast-aluminium gearbox housing for a grain harvesting header was updated using measured frequency response functions from impact hammer tests at 54 degrees of freedom. Initial model errors arose from uncertain material damping, bolted joint stiffness, and wall thickness deviations due to casting. A Bayesian optimisation procedure with a Gaussian process surrogate model was employed to minimise a weighted residual combining natural frequency errors and MAC values for the first ten elastic modes. Starting from a mean frequency error of 8.4% and a minimum MAC diagonal of 0.71, the updated model achieved a mean frequency error of 1.9% and minimum MAC diagonal of 0.93 after 210 function evaluations. The updated model was then used to predict fatigue-critical stress concentrations under measured in-service vibration spectra. The computational framework, implemented in Python with an ANSYS APDL back-end, is described in sufficient detail to allow reproduction.

title: Thermomechanical Fatigue of Exhaust Manifold Brackets Under Combined Thermal Cycling and Engine-Induced Vibration
abstract: Cast stainless steel exhaust manifold brackets of a heavy-duty diesel engine were assessed for thermomechanical fatigue under a duty cycle combining thermal loading (85–620 °C, cycle duration 8 minutes) and engine-induced base vibration (broadband PSD, 20–500 Hz). A sequentially coupled thermal–structural finite-element analysis provided time-varying temperature distributions and mean stress fields; the vibration fatigue damage was superimposed in the frequency domain using the Dirlik–Tovo–Benasciutti formulation adapted for non-zero mean stress with the Smith–Watson–Topper parameter. Temperature-dependent material properties (Young's modulus, yield stress, fatigue coefficient) for the alloy 1.4837 were taken from standardised test data. Dominant fatigue damage accumulated during the thermal cool-down phase, when mean tensile stresses combined with high-frequency vibration amplitudes. The predicted location of crack initiation matched service-return brackets from a fleet of 34 vehicles. Sensitivity to the assumed heat transfer coefficient at the bracket–manifold interface is quantified.

title: Primary consolidation parameters of Vojvodina organic clays determined from incremental loading oedometer tests
abstract: Undisturbed samples of organic clay were collected at five locations across the Vojvodina lowland at depths ranging from 1.5 to 6.0 m. Incremental loading oedometer tests were performed on 88 specimens following ASTM D2435 procedures. Compression index Cc ranged from 0.41 to 1.23, and the coefficient of consolidation cv varied between 0.8 and 4.2 m²/year across the stress range 10–400 kPa. Organic content, determined by loss on ignition, ranged from 8 to 34 percent and showed a statistically significant positive correlation with Cc (R² = 0.71). The preconsolidation pressure estimated by the Casagrande method was compared with estimates from the strain energy method, showing systematic differences up to 18 percent. Results indicate that conventional correlations developed for Scandinavian clays underestimate Cc for Vojvodina deposits and that local regression equations are needed for reliable settlement forecasting in this region.

title: Comparison of constant rate of strain and incremental loading oedometer tests on peaty soils
abstract: Twelve pairs of specimens from three peat and organic clay sites in northern Serbia were tested in parallel using constant rate of strain (CRS) oedometer tests and conventional incremental loading (IL) oedometer tests. Strain rates of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 percent per hour were applied in CRS tests. Preconsolidation pressures from CRS tests were systematically 8 to 22 percent higher than IL estimates and increased with strain rate, consistent with viscoplastic soil behaviour. Compression curves from CRS tests at 0.5 percent per hour agreed most closely with IL results. Excess pore pressure ratios during CRS tests reached 0.15–0.28 depending on strain rate, remaining within ASTM-recommended limits only at the lowest rate. The study recommends CRS testing at rates not exceeding 0.8 percent per hour for organic soils in this region to ensure drainage conditions comparable to IL testing.

title: Effect of sample disturbance on compressibility parameters of low-plasticity organic clay
abstract: Tube sampling and block sampling were performed side by side at two sites in Vojvodina to assess the degree of disturbance imparted by thin-wall Shelby tubes relative to hand-cut block samples. Quality was assessed using the volumetric strain at in-situ effective stress method and the Lunne disturbance index. Compression index Cc from tube samples was on average 14 percent lower than from block samples, while the coefficient of consolidation cv was 23 percent higher for tube samples, suggesting partial destructuring of the fabric. The preconsolidation pressure was underestimated by 9 to 16 percent in tube samples. Scanning electron microscopy on selected specimens confirmed that tube sampling caused realignment of clay aggregates and partial collapse of macropores. The findings support the use of fixed-piston samplers or block sampling when obtaining parameters for settlement calculations at critical infrastructure sites in this region.

title: Long-term settlement of road embankments on organic soils in the Pannonian Basin: a database study
abstract: Settlement records from 23 road embankment cross-sections on organic clay and peat in Serbia, Hungary, and Croatia were compiled into a regional database. Monitoring periods ranged from 3 to 18 years. Post-construction creep settlements expressed as a fraction of primary settlement ranged from 0.12 to 0.61, with higher values associated with higher organic content and thicker organic layers. The ratio of secondary to primary compression was positively correlated with organic content (R² = 0.63) and weakly correlated with embankment height. Settlements were back-analysed using Asaoka's observational method to estimate ultimate primary settlement; residual creep settlements at the end of the monitoring period remained 15 to 40 percent of the estimated ultimate primary settlement. Regional average Cα values derived from back-analysis agreed within 12 percent with laboratory-determined values, validating the use of oedometer-based prediction methods for this geological context.

title: Evaluating vertical drain effectiveness in accelerating consolidation of Vojvodina organic clay: a case study
abstract: Prefabricated vertical drains (PVDs) were installed at a trial embankment site near Sombor to accelerate consolidation of a 9.3 m thick organic clay deposit. Two instrumented sections were compared: one with PVDs at 1.5 m triangular spacing and one without drains. Settlement and pore pressure data were collected for 30 months. The drain section reached 90 percent average degree of consolidation in 8 months compared to an estimated 47 months for the undrained section. Back-calculated horizontal coefficient of consolidation ch was 5.8 m²/year, approximately 6.1 times the laboratory-measured cv. The smear zone radius was estimated by Indraratna–Redana back-analysis as 3.2 times the equivalent drain radius, consistent with literature values for similar soils. Residual secondary compression at 30 months was 0.09 m in the drain section and 0.14 m in the undrained section, confirming that accelerated primary consolidation also reduces creep magnitude.

title: Creep of peat under cyclic embankment loading: laboratory simulation of seasonal water table fluctuation
abstract: Laboratory experiments were designed to simulate the influence of seasonal water table fluctuations on creep of peat specimens under embankment stress. Eight undisturbed peat specimens from the Tisa floodplain (organic content 61–78 percent) were consolidated to a vertical effective stress of 60 kPa in Rowe cells and then subjected to six cycles of drainage and re-wetting while maintaining constant total stress. Each drainage–wetting cycle lasted 30 days. Volumetric strain during drainage phases was 1.2 to 2.8 percent per cycle, while re-wetting caused partial recovery of 0.3 to 0.7 percent. Net creep strain accumulated over six cycles was 7.4 to 12.1 percent, substantially larger than creep under constant water table conditions (4.2 to 6.8 percent) for the same total time. The results indicate that seasonal water table fluctuations are an important but commonly neglected driver of long-term settlement in embankments overlying peat in lowland drainage basins.

title: Spatial variability of compressibility in a heterogeneous peat layer mapped by CPTU and oedometer data integration
abstract: A combined dataset of 41 CPTU soundings and 56 oedometer tests was used to map spatial variability of compression index Cc across a 1.2 km² peat deposit at a planned flood retention basin site in the Tisa catchment. CPTU net cone resistance qn and sleeve friction fs were used as predictors in regression models calibrated against oedometer-derived Cc values. Cross-validation showed that a two-predictor model (qn and fs) explained 68 percent of variance in Cc, compared to 52 percent using qn alone. Kriging interpolation was applied to residuals to produce continuous maps of Cc and its uncertainty. Settlement volume estimates for three alternative basin embankment configurations differed by up to 34 percent depending on whether spatial variability was accounted for or a single average Cc value was used. The study demonstrates the benefit of integrating in-situ and laboratory data for settlement estimation at sites with strongly heterogeneous organic deposits.

title: Consolidation and creep parameters for Pannonian lowland organic soils: a synthesis for geotechnical design practice
abstract: This book chapter synthesises consolidation and creep data collected from soft organic soils across the Pannonian lowland region, drawing on published literature and unpublished test databases from five laboratories in Serbia, Hungary, and Croatia. Compression index Cc, swelling index Cs, coefficient of consolidation cv, secondary compression index Cα, and creep rate parameter μ* are tabulated as functions of organic content, natural water content, and Atterberg limits for four soil categories: low-organic clay (LOI 5–15 percent), high-organic clay (LOI 15–35 percent), sedge peat (LOI 35–65 percent), and fibrous peat (LOI > 65 percent). Design charts are proposed for preliminary settlement estimation prior to laboratory testing. Limitations of the proposed correlations are discussed with reference to sample disturbance, testing protocol differences, and the restricted depth range of available data. The chapter is intended as a practical reference for geotechnical engineers working on infrastructure projects in lowland floodplain environments.

title: Loess slope stability along the Danube: a review of failure mechanisms and modelling approaches in the Pannonian region
abstract: This book chapter surveys research on loess slope failures along the Danube and its major tributaries published between 1980 and 2014, covering studies from Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Slovakia. The chapter classifies failure modes into five categories: shallow planar slides, deep rotational slides, retrogressive cracks, earthflows, and combined fluvial-erosion failures, and discusses the geomorphological and hydrological triggers associated with each. Modelling approaches reviewed include classical limit equilibrium methods, finite-element and finite-difference codes, and empirical statistical models. The chapter identifies the poor characterisation of unsaturated strength as the principal knowledge gap and recommends standardised borehole logging protocols for future site investigations. Regional compilations of published shear strength data are presented in tabular form, covering 312 test series from 28 studies, to serve as a reference for practitioners in the region.

title: Thermoeconomic evaluation of a district heating network supplied by industrial waste heat: a case study from a petrochemical complex
abstract: This paper presents a thermoeconomic analysis of a proposed district heating scheme supplied by low-grade waste heat (85–110 °C) recovered from cooling circuits at a mid-sized petrochemical facility. The analysis combines exergy costing based on the SPECO (Specific Exergy Costing) method with a simplified investment model for the pipeline network serving approximately 4,200 residential units. The levelised cost of heat was estimated at 28.4 €/MWh under base-case conditions, compared with 41.1 €/MWh for the reference natural-gas boiler scenario. Sensitivity analysis over discount rate (6–12%), supply temperature (80–105 °C) and pipeline length (2.5–7 km) shows that pipeline distance is the dominant cost driver, with each additional kilometre raising the levelised cost by approximately 3.1 €/MWh. The exergetic efficiency of the integrated system is 31.2%, with the greatest irreversibility occurring in the primary heat exchangers. The results provide a quantitative basis for feasibility decisions in similar post-industrial urban contexts.
venue: Journal of Thermal Engineering and Applied Energy

title: Primena pinch metodologije za rekonstrukciju mreže izmenjivača toplote u rafineriji biljnog ulja
abstract: Rad opisuje pinch analizu primenjenu na mrežu izmenjivača toplote u rafineriji biljnog ulja u Srbiji sa ukupnim toplotnim tokom od oko 12 MW. Definisane su kompozitne krive za 14 procesnih tokova pri minimalnoj razlici temperatura ΔTmin = 10 °C. Utvrđen je potencijal rekuperacije toplote od 1,84 MW, što odgovara smanjenju potrošnje pare od 18,3% u odnosu na tekuće stanje. Predložene su tri varijante rekonstrukcije koje se razlikuju po broju novih izmenjivača (2, 3 i 5) i odgovarajućim kapitalnim troškovima (od 185.000 do 420.000 evra). Varijantu sa dva nova izmenjivača karakteriše period povrata od 2,1 godinu pri ceni pare 22 €/t. Analizom mrežnih ograničenja i dostupnog prostora u pogonu utvrđeno je da je ova varijanta tehnički najizvodljivija za implementaciju bez zaustavljanja proizvodnje.

title: Multi-objective optimisation of heat exchanger network retrofit using a genetic algorithm with exergy and cost objectives
abstract: A bi-objective optimisation framework for the retrofit of industrial heat exchanger networks (HENs) is presented, combining second-law efficiency and total annualised cost as conflicting objectives. The algorithm uses a real-coded genetic algorithm (NSGA-II variant) with a penalty function for topology feasibility. The HEN superstructure is defined using the stage-wise representation with up to six stages and twelve process streams. Pareto-optimal solutions are obtained for a representative refinery pre-heat train benchmark (stream data from open literature, 10 hot and 8 cold streams). Results show that moving from the minimum-cost solution to the maximum second-law efficiency solution increases capital expenditure by 38% while improving overall exergetic efficiency from 54.1% to 67.8%. An intermediate solution on the knee of the Pareto curve, identified by the minimum distance method, achieves 63.4% exergetic efficiency at a 16% cost premium. The framework is implemented in MATLAB and validated against three published benchmark cases, with deviations below 2.1% in total annualised cost.

title: Exergoeconomic comparison of organic Rankine cycle configurations for low-temperature waste heat recovery in the food processing sector
abstract: Three organic Rankine cycle (ORC) configurations—simple, recuperated and two-stage—are evaluated for recovery of waste heat available at 95–130 °C from a corn-starch processing plant. Working fluids considered are R245fa, n-pentane and isobutane. Exergoeconomic analysis following the SPECO methodology is applied to each configuration at design-point conditions derived from plant measurements over a 30-day operational period. Net electrical output ranges from 210 kW (simple cycle, R245fa) to 388 kW (two-stage, n-pentane). The exergoeconomic factor for the evaporator ranges between 0.18 and 0.34, indicating that exergy destruction costs dominate over capital costs in all cases. Levelised cost of electricity for the recuperated cycle with n-pentane is estimated at 74 €/MWh at a 10-year plant life and 8% discount rate. Payback periods range from 4.2 to 7.8 years depending on the local electricity purchase price assumed (55–90 €/MWh). The two-stage configuration offers the lowest cost of electricity but has the longest payback period due to higher capital cost.

title: Uticaj raspodele minimalnih razlika temperatura na troškove rekuperacije toplote u hemijskim procesima: parametarska analiza
abstract: Rad istražuje kako izbor minimalnog temperaturnog pristupa ΔTmin utiče na ravnotežu između kapitalnih i operativnih troškova u mrežama izmenjivača toplote za četiri tipična hemijska procesa (destilacija etanola, sinteza amonijaka u malom obimu, prerada otpadnih voda i krekovanje na pari). Za svaki proces konstruisana je kriva ukupnih godišnjih troškova u funkciji ΔTmin u opsegu 5–25 °C primenom standardne pinch metodologije uz troškovne modele zasnovane na površini izmenjivača. Optimalne vrednosti ΔTmin variraju od 8 °C (sinteza amonijaka, visoke temperature) do 17 °C (prečišćavanje otpadnih voda, niske temperature), što ukazuje na zavisnost od temperaturnog nivoa procesa. Analiza je pokazala da korišćenje jedinstvene preporučene vrednosti ΔTmin = 10 °C može dovesti do precenjivanja troškova grejanja za do 23% ili kapitalnih troškova za do 31% u zavisnosti od procesa. Dat je i skup korekcionih faktora koji se mogu koristiti u preliminarnom projektovanju.

title: Retrofit of a ceramic tile production line: pinch analysis and heat exchanger network design for flue gas heat recovery
abstract: Industrial tunnel kilns used in ceramic tile production generate large volumes of flue gas at temperatures between 180 and 340 °C, which are currently vented without heat recovery at the studied facility in central Serbia. Pinch analysis was applied to the combined process and utility system, identifying a minimum hot utility target of 2.1 MW against a current consumption of 3.8 MW (44.7% reduction potential). Three retrofit designs were developed, varying in the number and arrangement of gas-to-air heat exchangers installed on the kiln exhaust duct. The preferred design, constrained by the available footprint and a maximum capital budget of 320,000 €, reduces hot utility consumption by 34.2% and achieves a simple payback of 1.8 years at current natural gas prices (0.048 €/kWh). Exergy analysis of the preferred design shows that 58% of the remaining exergy destruction occurs in the high-temperature kiln zone, suggesting future potential for combustion-air preheating beyond the current design scope.

title: Procena potencijala rekuperacije otpadne toplote u prerađivačkoj industriji AP Vojvodine: sektorska analiza
abstract: Studija sistematski procenjuje potencijal rekuperacije otpadne toplote u pet industrijskih sektora AP Vojvodine (prehrambena industrija, hemijska industrija, industrija građevinskog materijala, metalurgija i gumarska industrija) na osnovu energetskih audita 23 postrojenja prikupljenih u periodu 2018–2021. Svrstavanje otpadnih toplotnih tokova po temperaturnom nivou (ispod 100 °C, 100–200 °C, iznad 200 °C) pokazuje da 67% dostupne otpadne toplote pripada niskom temperaturnom nivou, što ograničava direktnu rekuperaciju. Ukupni procenjeni tehnički potencijal rekuperacije iznosi 38,4 MW termalne snage. Primenjena je standardizovana pinch analiza po sektoru radi poređenja specifičnih potencijala (MW po milion evra godišnjeg prihoda). Metalurška postrojenja imaju najveći specifični potencijal (0,84 MW/M€), dok prehrambena postrojenja pokazuju najkraće procenjene periode povrata (prosečno 2,4 godine). Rezultati se mogu koristiti kao osnova za regionalne programe energetske efikasnosti i industrijsku simbiozou.

title: Second-law analysis of a biomass combined heat and power plant with flue gas condensation: effect of moisture content and load variation
abstract: A biomass-fired combined heat and power plant of 4.8 MW thermal and 1.1 MW electrical output, operating on wood chips with moisture content between 30% and 55% (wet basis), is analysed using detailed exergy accounting across all major components: combustion chamber, steam generator, turbine, condenser, flue gas economiser and condensation unit. Data were collected during 120 hours of continuous operation across four load levels (50%, 70%, 85% and 100% of rated load). Total exergy destruction rate at full load is 5.63 MW, with the combustion chamber responsible for 49% of this figure. Flue gas condensation recovers 210–480 kW of additional heat depending on moisture content, but contributes less than 0.8% to overall plant exergetic efficiency due to the low temperature of condensate heat. The exergetic efficiency of the plant ranges from 22.1% (50% load, 55% moisture) to 31.4% (100% load, 30% moisture). Load-following operation causes disproportionate increases in combustion irreversibility at partial load, identified as the main target for operational improvement.

title: Heat integration across batch and continuous processes: a time-average model applied to a dairy production facility
abstract: Batch processes present particular challenges for heat integration because stream availability varies with time. This paper applies a time-average model extended with storage vessel sizing to a dairy facility operating three batch pasteurisation lines alongside two continuous cream separation circuits. Stream population comprises 9 continuous and 14 batch streams. The composite curve approach is adapted using time-slice decomposition with six 4-hour intervals per production day. Heat storage vessels of 8 m³ each are introduced to bridge temporal mismatches between batch heating and cooling demands. The resulting heat exchanger network design achieves a 29.3% reduction in hot utility (steam at 3 bar) compared with the existing network, and a 22.1% reduction in cooling water consumption. Capital cost of the proposed network including storage vessels is estimated at 195,000 €, with a projected simple payback of 3.1 years. The methodology is documented in sufficient detail to be reproducible for similar mixed batch–continuous food processing contexts.
venue: Journal of Food Process Engineering and Energy

title: Avoidable and unavoidable exergy destruction in industrial heat exchanger networks: a screening method for retrofit prioritisation
abstract: Advanced exergy analysis distinguishes between avoidable and unavoidable exergy destruction within components by comparing actual operation with an idealised theoretical limit and a best-practice reference case. This paper proposes a screening method that applies this decomposition at the network level, aggregating component-level results to produce a prioritised list of retrofit candidates for industrial heat exchanger networks. The method is demonstrated on two case studies: a solvent recovery system (6 streams, 4 existing exchangers) and a vegetable oil deodorisation unit (9 streams, 7 existing exchangers). In both cases, the screening correctly identifies the same top-priority exchangers flagged by full multi-objective optimisation, while requiring approximately 15% of the computational effort. Sensitivity of the prioritisation ranking to uncertainty in heat transfer coefficients (±20%) is assessed; ranking of the top three candidates is found to be robust in all tested scenarios. The method is intended as a practical tool for energy engineers conducting preliminary retrofit assessments without access to full optimisation software.

title: Time-of-use tariff impact on the operational cost of a combined compressed-air and chilled-water utility system: a linear programming approach
abstract: The paper formulates a linear programming model for the daily scheduling of a combined utility system that includes two fixed-speed air compressors (total 110 kW), one variable-speed chiller (75 kW), and buffer storage vessels for both compressed air and chilled water. The optimisation objective minimises daily electricity cost under a three-period time-of-use tariff structure representative of Serbian industrial tariff class VN-A. Load profiles for compressed air and cooling were derived from twelve-month sub-hourly measurements at a plastics manufacturing facility. Under the optimal schedule, daily electricity cost was reduced by 9.2% relative to uncontrolled baseline operation, and peak coincident demand was reduced by 18 kW. The model is solved to optimality in under four seconds on standard hardware, making real-time deployment feasible. Results are sensitive to buffer volume: doubling the air receiver from 2 000 to 4 000 litres improved savings by a further 3.1 percentage points.

title: Fouling resistance development in brazed plate heat exchangers handling hard groundwater: a six-month industrial monitoring study
abstract: Calcium carbonate scaling on BPHE surfaces in industrial water-heating applications increases thermal resistance and pressure drop over time, but long-term field data under real process conditions are scarce. This study presents fouling resistance measurements collected over 24 weeks at a food-processing facility in Vojvodina using two identically specified BPHEs: one operating continuously and one with weekly thermal shock cleaning cycles. Fouling resistance was calculated from overall heat transfer coefficient measurements recorded every four hours using calibrated flow meters and Pt100 temperature sensors. After 24 weeks, the continuously operated unit reached an asymptotic fouling resistance of 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ m²·K/W, while the cleaned unit stabilised at 6.4 × 10⁻⁵ m²·K/W. Scanning electron microscopy of extracted plates confirmed predominantly calcite crystalline deposits with median layer thickness of 38 µm on the hot side. The results support use of an asymptotic fouling model with time constants fitted to the measured data, and suggest that current TEMA-recommended fouling allowances overestimate resistance by a factor of 1.4–2.1 for this water chemistry.

title: Convergence Analysis of Iterative Hard Thresholding for Noisy Underdetermined MRI Systems
abstract: Iterative hard thresholding (IHT) is a computationally efficient approach to sparse signal recovery, but its convergence behaviour under measurement noise is incompletely characterised for the matrix structures that arise in Cartesian and radial MRI sampling. This paper provides a convergence rate bound for IHT applied to noisy underdetermined linear systems whose sensing matrices satisfy a restricted isometry property (RIP) with constant δ₂s < 0.4142. The analysis is carried out for fixed and adaptive step-size variants. Numerical experiments are performed on a synthetic phantom dataset and on 48 anonymised T1-weighted brain scans acquired at 1.5 T, with retrospective Cartesian undersampling at acceleration factors R ∈ {4, 6, 8}. At R = 6, the adaptive step-size IHT achieves a normalised mean squared error of 0.031 compared to 0.047 for the fixed step-size version. Runtime on a single GPU is reduced to under 0.9 s per slice at R = 6. The theoretical bounds are shown to be tight to within a factor of 1.8 on the experimental data.

title: Comparison of Greedy Pursuit Methods for Sparse Recovery Under Structured Random Projections
abstract: Greedy pursuit algorithms such as Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP), Subspace Pursuit (SP), and CoSaMP are widely used for sparse recovery but their relative performance depends strongly on the statistical structure of the measurement matrix. This study provides a systematic empirical comparison of these three methods under four structured random projection models relevant to medical imaging: Gaussian random matrices, partial Fourier matrices, random Bernoulli projections, and block-diagonal sensing matrices. Experiments are conducted on 1 200 synthetic sparse signals with sparsity levels s ranging from 5 to 40 in ambient dimension n = 256, and on 60 real MRI slices from a public cardiac dataset downsampled to simulate compressed acquisition. Recovery success rate, computation time, and l₂ reconstruction error are reported across all conditions. CoSaMP achieves the highest recovery rate (91.3 % at s = 20 for partial Fourier) but is 2.4 times slower than OMP on the same hardware. Block-diagonal matrices pose the greatest difficulty for all three methods. Results provide practical guidance for algorithm selection under hardware and latency constraints typical of clinical scanners.

title: Total Variation Regularisation with Adaptive Weighting for Undersampled Radial MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Total variation (TV) minimisation is a standard approach for recovering piecewise-smooth images from undersampled measurements, but uniform TV weighting does not account for spatially varying noise levels or object boundaries. This work proposes a spatially adaptive TV regularisation scheme in which the weighting map is estimated from a low-resolution pilot reconstruction obtained from the central 5 % of k-space lines. The resulting weighted l₁ minimisation problem is solved using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a warm-start strategy that reduces the iteration count by approximately 30 % compared to cold initialisation. The method is evaluated on 84 radial MRI acquisitions of knee joints acquired at 3 T with 20 %, 30 %, and 40 % of full k-space density. Structural similarity index (SSIM) improves by 0.06–0.09 over uniform TV at all undersampling levels. Cartilage boundary sharpness, measured by edge gradient magnitude, increases by 18 % on average. The computational overhead of the weighting estimation step is 0.12 s per volume on a standard workstation.

title: On the Null Space Property for Sparse Recovery from Partial Fourier Measurements with Random Phase Encoding
abstract: The null space property (NSP) provides a necessary and sufficient condition for exact sparse recovery via l₁ minimisation, yet explicit NSP constants are rarely computed for the partial Fourier matrices used in practice because of their deterministic row structure. This paper studies the NSP for partial Fourier matrices whose rows are selected according to a variable-density random sampling scheme with a polynomial decay profile, which is common in clinical MRI protocols. Using probabilistic arguments based on decoupling inequalities, we derive sufficient conditions on the number of measurements m required to guarantee the NSP of order s with high probability in ambient dimension n. For n = 512 and s = 30, the derived bound requires m ≥ 148 rows, which is within 12 % of the empirically observed phase transition threshold. Monte Carlo simulations over 10 000 matrix realisations confirm the sharpness of the bound. The result implies that variable-density sampling outperforms uniform random row selection by approximately 22 % in the number of measurements needed at fixed sparsity.

title: Sparse Recovery Guarantees for Block-Structured Sensing Matrices Arising in Parallel MRI
abstract: Parallel MRI acquires data simultaneously from multiple receiver coils, producing block-structured sensing matrices whose theoretical recovery guarantees differ substantially from those of single-coil compressed sensing. This preprint extends the concept of the block-RIP to non-square block partitions and derives recovery bounds for the block-OMP algorithm under this weaker condition. The analysis covers the case in which coil sensitivity maps are estimated with bounded error, contributing an additive perturbation term to the recovery guarantee that scales with the sensitivity estimation error. Experiments use an 8-coil synthetic parallel MRI setup with simulated sensitivity maps and retrospective undersampling of 90 brain MRI volumes at acceleration factors R ∈ {2, 4, 6}. At R = 4, block-OMP achieves a 94.1 % exact support recovery rate when sensitivity estimation error is below 5 %. The derived bounds are compared against standard per-coil l₁ minimisation, and conditions under which the block approach is theoretically superior are identified.

title: Domain-Specific Schema Grounding for Text-to-SQL in Retail Analytics
abstract: General text-to-SQL models are typically trained and evaluated on academic benchmarks whose schemas differ substantially from production business-intelligence databases, which feature denormalized tables, company-specific column naming conventions, and domain jargon. This paper examines the performance gap when applying a state-of-the-art seq2seq model to a retail analytics schema provided by a regional grocery chain, containing 31 tables and 284 columns. A schema grounding module is introduced that matches question tokens to column names using a combination of character-level edit distance, word embeddings trained on retail domain text, and manually authored synonym dictionaries. The grounding module is integrated into the decoder's attention mechanism and trained on 2,100 in-domain question–SQL pairs collected via an internal annotation effort. Fine-tuning with grounding increases execution accuracy from 51.2% to 73.6% on a held-out test split of 420 pairs, compared to a 58.9% accuracy achieved by fine-tuning without grounding. The synonym dictionary contributes 6.1 of the 22.4 percentage-point gain.

title: Transfer Learning from Sport Motion Capture to Clinical Gait: Domain Gap Analysis and Partial Fine-tuning Strategies
abstract: Sport motion-capture corpora are larger and more varied than clinical gait databases, making them attractive pre-training sources, yet the domain gap between athletic and pathological movement is substantial. This paper quantifies the domain gap between a 9,000-sequence sport corpus and a clinical gait dataset of 134 patients with three gait pathologies using maximum mean discrepancy and Fréchet skeletal distance metrics. Four partial fine-tuning strategies are compared: full fine-tuning, frozen encoder, progressive layer unfreezing, and adapter modules inserted at each transformer block of a spatial-temporal transformer pre-trained on the sport corpus. Adapter-based fine-tuning achieves 82.3% classification accuracy on gait pathology with 20 labelled samples per class, outperforming full fine-tuning by 6.1 points and frozen encoder by 13.4 points at that sample size. The paper discusses when sport pre-training helps and when it hurts, identifying rapid-acceleration sequences as the primary source of negative transfer.

title: A Constraint Programming Model for Cyclic Nurse Rostering with Skill Coverage Requirements
abstract: This paper presents a constraint programming (CP) model for cyclic nurse rostering in a hospital department with multiple ward units and four distinct skill grades. The scheduling horizon covers four weeks and involves 48 nurses assigned across day, evening, and night shifts. Hard constraints enforce minimum coverage per shift and per skill level, legal rest-period requirements of at least eleven consecutive hours, and a maximum of six consecutive working days. Soft constraints penalise deviations from individual nurse preferences and fairness in weekend assignments. The model was implemented in ECLiPSe and tested on data from two hospitals in the Vojvodina region. For the smaller instance, optimal solutions were obtained in under three minutes; for the larger 48-nurse instance, a branch-and-bound search with symmetry-breaking constraints reduced the search space by 34% compared to a baseline CP formulation. Solution quality was evaluated against a manual schedule prepared by a head nurse, showing a 21% reduction in soft constraint violations.
venue: Journal of Applied Operational Research

title: Encoding Strategies for Cell-Based Neural Architecture Search under Multiple Constraints
abstract: Cell-based neural architecture search constructs networks by stacking repeated cell templates, each defined by a directed acyclic graph of primitive operations. The choice of encoding—how a cell graph is represented as a genotype—strongly influences the effectiveness of evolutionary search. This chapter reviews and experimentally compares four encoding strategies: adjacency matrix, operation sequence, graph hash, and layer-wise factored encoding. Each is embedded within the same NSGA-II loop optimising accuracy, parameter count, and activation memory simultaneously on the NAS-Bench-201 proxy benchmark. The adjacency matrix encoding explores the Pareto front most uniformly, while the factored encoding converges faster but with lower diversity. The chapter also discusses how constraint tightness (memory budgets from 32 KB to 512 KB) interacts with encoding choice. Guidance is provided for practitioners selecting encodings for resource-constrained targets such as microcontrollers.
venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence Methods (edited volume, Springer regional series)

title: Одређивање триацилглицеролског састава хладно пресованог уља трпуца методом HPLC-ELSD
abstract: У раду је описана примена HPLC са детектором расејања светлости (ELSD) за квантификацију триацилглицерола у хладно пресованом уљу трпуца (Camelina sativa) произведеном у малим погонима у Бачкој. Идентификовано је шеснаест молекулских врста ТАГ употребом еквивалентних бројева угљеника (ECN), а потврда идентитета обавила се упоређивањем са стандардима и МС детекцијом на јонском хватачу. Доминантни триацилглицероли били су LnLnLn и LnLnL, одражавајући висок удео α-линоленске киселине (преко 35%). Метода је валидована са вредношћу RSD < 3,5% за свих шеснаест компонената. Упоређен је ТАГ профил три узорка различитих хладних пресовања и утврђена је добра репродуцибилност производног процеса. Резултати указују да HPLC-ELSD представља примењиву рутинску технику за контролу квалитета у малим уљарама.

title: Oxidative Stability and Minor Component Profiles of Selected Cold-Pressed Grape Seed and Rosehip Oils
abstract: Grape seed oil (Vitis vinifera, three Serbian winery by-product sources) and rosehip oil (Rosa canina, wild-harvested from Fruška Gora) were characterised with respect to fatty acid composition, tocopherols, total phenolics and oxidative stability. Linoleic acid accounted for 69–72% in grape seed oil and 44–48% in rosehip oil, with rosehip oil additionally containing 31–36% α-linolenic acid. Tocopherol analysis by HPLC-FLD showed α-tocopherol dominating rosehip oil (82 mg/100 g) while γ-tocopherol dominated grape seed oil (195–231 mg/100 g). Phenolic content by Folin–Ciocalteu ranged from 14 to 31 mg GAE/100 g. Rancimat induction periods were 2.4–3.8 h for rosehip oil and 4.1–5.9 h for grape seed oil at 110 °C. Correlations between tocopherol content and induction period were moderate (r = 0.61). Both oils are discussed as candidates for dermatological formulations on the basis of their fatty acid ratios and antioxidant profiles.

title: Prediction of Skin-Feel and Spreadability of Vegetable Oils Using Rheological and Tribological Parameters
abstract: Ten cold-pressed vegetable oils (hemp seed, black cumin, apricot kernel, walnut, milk thistle, marjoram seed, sea buckthorn pulp, evening primrose, camelina and pumpkin seed) were characterised by dynamic oscillatory rheology, small-amplitude oscillation and tribological sliding friction on a stainless-steel/PDMS contact pair. Viscosity at 25 °C ranged from 48 mPa·s (hemp seed) to 103 mPa·s (sea buckthorn pulp). Coefficient of friction at 10 mm/s varied from 0.041 to 0.089 across the set. Fatty acid unsaturation index correlated with viscosity (r = 0.71) but not with friction. Spreading coefficient, calculated from surface tension data measured by the pendant drop method, showed a stronger association with perceived spreadability in a small semi-trained panel (n = 8) than did viscosity alone. A linear regression model combining spreading coefficient and viscosity explained 74% of variance in panellist scores. The data form a reference framework for selecting oils in emollient formulation without relying solely on fatty acid composition.

title: Трансмасне киселине у комерцијалним хладно пресованим уљима са српског тржишта: ниво присуства и порекло
abstract: Анализирано је двадесет и два комерцијална хладно пресована уља купљена у малопродајним објектима у Новом Саду и Београду током 2018. и 2019. године. Садржај транс-масних киселина одређен је GC-FID методом на BPX-70 капиларној колони дужине 100 m. Укупан садржај ТФА кретао се у опсегу 0,04–0,38% укупних масних киселина, што је испод прага хидрогенизације. Геометријски изомери олеинске киселине (елаидинска) нису детектовани ни у једном узорку. У четири узорка уља ланеног семена регистровани су елевирани нивои trans-α-линоленске киселине (0,28–0,38%), приписани неповољним условима складиштења, а не технолошком поступку. Упоређивање резултата са декларисаним вредностима произвођача показало је одступање код два узорка за параметар пероксидног броја. Закључено је да српска тржишна хладно пресована уља у целини испуњавају европске регулаторне захтеве, уз препоруку строжијег надзора температуре складиштења.
