title: Emollient Performance of Apricot Kernel and Black Cumin Seed Oils in Simple Water-in-Oil Emulsions: Stability, Skin Hydration and Transepidermal Water Loss
abstract: Water-in-oil emulsions were prepared with 15% (w/w) cold-pressed apricot kernel oil (Prunus armeniaca) or black cumin seed oil (Nigella sativa) using a polyglycerol polyricinoleate emulsifier system. Emulsion stability was assessed by centrifugation, turbiscan backscattering and accelerated ageing at 40 °C over eight weeks. In a controlled in vivo study with eighteen healthy volunteers (Fitzpatrick skin types II–IV), a single forearm occlusion test measured skin hydration by corneometry and transepidermal water loss (TEWL) by tewameter at 0, 2 and 6 hours post-application. Apricot kernel oil emulsion produced a statistically significant reduction in TEWL at 2 h (–18%, p = 0.02) relative to the vehicle control, while black cumin emulsion did not reach significance (–9%, p = 0.14). Corneometry values increased significantly with both formulations at 2 h. No differences in physical stability were observed between the two systems across the eight-week period. Rheological profiles indicated both emulsions were viscoelastic solids with G' > G'' at 1 Hz.

title: Cold-Pressed Vegetable Oils as Functional Ingredients in Topical Formulations: Composition, Stability and Skin Interactions
abstract: This book chapter reviews the relationship between the molecular composition of cold-pressed vegetable oils and their behaviour when incorporated into topical emulsions and anhydrous preparations. The first section covers fatty acid and triacylglycerol diversity across commonly used oil crops, with data drawn from published literature and the authors' own GC-MS and HPLC-MS datasets. The second section addresses oxidative stability challenges in formulation, covering prooxidant–antioxidant balance and interaction with emulsifier systems. The third section examines in vitro and in vivo methods used to assess emollient performance, including occlusion, friction and penetration measurements. The chapter closes with a discussion of regulatory considerations under EU Regulation 1223/2009 as they apply to naturally derived oil ingredients. Throughout, specific numerical data from representative studies are cited to support practical formulation guidance rather than general recommendations.

title: Sterols and Wax Esters in Cold-Pressed Sea Buckthorn Pulp Oil: Quantification by GC-MS and Contribution to Emollient Function
abstract: Sea buckthorn pulp oil (Hippophae rhamnoides) contains an unusually high proportion of wax esters and phytosterols alongside its well-documented carotenoid and palmitoleic acid content. Six commercially sourced cold-pressed pulp oils were subjected to liquid–liquid fractionation to isolate the unsaponifiable fraction, which was then silylated and quantified by GC-MS using d6-cholesterol as internal standard. Total sterol content ranged from 910 to 1340 mg/kg, with β-sitosterol (44–52%) and campesterol (18–24%) predominating. Wax ester content, isolated by preparative thin-layer chromatography and quantified gravimetrically, ranged from 2.1 to 4.8% of total lipid. A comparison of oils with high versus low wax ester content in simple anhydrous sticks assessed spreading coefficient, coefficient of friction and water vapour transmission rate across a polysulfone membrane. Oils with higher wax ester content showed reduced coefficient of friction (0.042 vs. 0.071, p = 0.03) and lower membrane water vapour transmission rate (–22%). The contribution of wax esters to barrier function is discussed in the context of emollient formulation.

title: Influence of Seed Roasting on Triacylglycerol Molecular Species and Minor Lipid Components of Cold-Pressed Pumpkin Seed Oil
abstract: Seeds of Cucurbita pepo var. styriaca were subjected to light (120 °C, 15 min), medium (140 °C, 15 min) and heavy (160 °C, 15 min) roasting treatments before cold pressing. Unroasted seeds served as control. Triacylglycerol molecular species were profiled by HPLC-MS in positive ion mode using ammonium formate adducts. Eighteen species were identified; the dominant LLL and LLO species decreased by 4.1% and 3.7% relative, respectively, in heavy-roasted oil, with a corresponding increase in partially oxidised TAG species detected above the MRM threshold. Free fatty acid content increased from 0.18% (unroasted) to 0.49% (160 °C). Tocopherol and phytosterol contents were minimally affected up to 140 °C but showed statistically significant reductions at 160 °C (p < 0.05 for γ-tocopherol, p < 0.01 for δ-tocopherol). Maillard-derived alkylpyrazines, monitored as volatile markers by SPME-GC-MS, increased monotonically with roasting intensity. Results provide a basis for adjusting roasting conditions to balance sensory and lipid quality objectives.

title: Gelation behaviour of hemp protein isolate under varying ionic strength and pH: rheological and water-holding characterisation
abstract: Heat-induced gels of hemp protein isolate (HPI, 10–16% w/v) were prepared at pH values of 6.0, 7.0, and 8.0 in the presence of NaCl at 0, 50, 100, and 200 mM. Gelation was induced by heating at 90 °C for 30 minutes followed by cooling to 25 °C. Small-amplitude oscillatory rheology was used to record storage modulus (G′) as a function of temperature during the heating–cooling cycle. The highest G′ value of 1,840 Pa was obtained at pH 7.0 and 100 mM NaCl with 14% protein concentration, while gels formed at pH 6.0 with no added salt showed a G′ below 200 Pa. Water-holding capacity (WHC) ranged from 72% to 91% across conditions, with the highest WHC coinciding with the highest G′. Scanning electron microscopy of freeze-dried gels revealed a coarser network at elevated ionic strength, consistent with the screening of electrostatic repulsion facilitating hydrophobic aggregation. The relationship between gel firmness and WHC is described by a non-linear empirical model.

title: Ixodid tick infestation of roe deer (Capreolus capreolus) in the Fruška Gora region: species composition and seasonal dynamics
abstract: Roe deer were examined at three hunting grounds on the southern slopes of Fruška Gora between March 2010 and February 2011. Ticks were collected from 68 culled animals and identified morphologically to species level. A total of 1,247 ticks belonging to four species were recorded: Ixodes ricinus (74.3%), Dermacentor reticulatus (16.1%), Haemaphysalis punctata (6.2%), and Haemaphysalis concinna (3.4%). Infestation intensity peaked in April–May and again in October, corresponding to the bi-modal activity pattern of I. ricinus adults in this region. Mean tick burden per host was 18.3 (range 1–94). Adult ticks predominated on the head and neck region, while nymphs were distributed across the body. Seasonal variation in D. reticulatus abundance was marked, with the highest counts in late autumn. Results establish a baseline for tick community structure on roe deer in the lowland-to-hill transition zone of Vojvodina and provide foundational data for subsequent pathogen screening studies.

title: Tick infestation patterns on wild boar (Sus scrofa) in lowland hunting grounds of northern Vojvodina
abstract: Wild boar harvested during the 2012–2013 hunting season at five sites in Bačka and Banat were examined for tick infestation. Ticks were removed from 102 carcasses immediately after culling. Three species were identified: Dermacentor reticulatus (61.8%), Ixodes ricinus (34.5%), and Rhipicephalus sanguineus sensu lato (3.7%). Mean tick burden was lower than that reported for cervids in the same region (mean 9.7 ticks per host). Infestation was significantly higher in older age classes (p < 0.01, Kruskal–Wallis test). Predilection sites differed between tick species: D. reticulatus was predominantly found on the ventral abdomen and groin, while I. ricinus was concentrated around the ears and axillae. The study documents S. scrofa as a competent host for D. reticulatus under lowland conditions and highlights differences in tick community composition relative to sympatric cervids in the same landscape.

title: Anaplasma phagocytophilum in ticks collected from wild ungulates in Vojvodina: first molecular confirmation
abstract: This study reports the first confirmed molecular detection of Anaplasma phagocytophilum in ticks from wild ungulates in Vojvodina, Serbia. DNA was extracted from 204 I. ricinus adults collected from 41 roe deer and 28 wild boar during 2015. Real-time PCR targeting the msp2 gene was used for detection, with positive samples subsequently sequenced at the 16S rRNA locus. Overall prevalence was 8.3% (17/204); all positive ticks originated from roe deer. None of the ticks removed from wild boar tested positive. Sequences grouped with the ecotype I variant associated with ruminants and the granulocytic anaplasmosis cycle in Europe. Ct values ranged from 31.2 to 38.6, indicating low to moderate bacterial loads. Phylogenetic placement and host specificity data suggest that roe deer serve as amplifying hosts for the ruminant ecotype in this landscape, consistent with findings from Hungary and Romania.

title: A decade of tick surveillance in Vojvodina hunting grounds: trends in Dermacentor reticulatus range expansion
abstract: Dermacentor reticulatus has been expanding northward and westward across Central and Eastern Europe, but systematic longitudinal data from Serbia remain sparse. This study compiled tick collection records from 14 hunting grounds across Vojvodina between 2010 and 2020, totalling 4,318 ticks removed from roe deer, wild boar, and European hare (Lepus europaeus). D. reticulatus proportional abundance increased from 12.4% of all ticks collected in 2010–2012 to 27.1% in 2018–2020. The increase was most pronounced in Banat localities adjacent to the Romanian border. Generalised linear models identified mean October temperature and floodplain grassland area as significant positive predictors of D. reticulatus abundance. I. ricinus remained dominant overall but showed no significant directional trend. These data, combined with published records from Hungary and Romania, suggest ongoing range consolidation rather than a sudden invasion event, with implications for Babesia canis and Francisella tularensis risk in the region.

title: Molecular characterisation of Borrelia miyamotoi in Ixodes ricinus from wild ungulates in Serbia: a short communication
abstract: Borrelia miyamotoi, a relapsing-fever group spirochaete with documented human pathogenicity, has rarely been characterised in ticks from wildlife hosts in the Balkans. During routine screening of I. ricinus from roe deer in 2020, four ticks were found to carry a Borrelia sp. that did not conform to any B. burgdorferi sensu lato genospecies by 5S–23S spacer analysis. Subsequent PCR targeting the glycerophosphodiester phosphodiesterase (glpQ) gene confirmed B. miyamotoi in all four samples. Partial sequences of the flagellin gene showed 99.2% identity to European reference sequences deposited in GenBank. Prevalence in the screened sample (4/211, 1.9%) is consistent with figures reported from neighbouring countries. This communication represents the first documented detection of B. miyamotoi in ticks removed directly from wildlife hosts in Serbia, and its significance for clinical differential diagnosis of tick-borne febrile illness is briefly discussed.

title: Wild boar as hosts for Theileria and Babesia spp. in Vojvodina: PCR screening and phylogenetic analysis
abstract: Piroplasmid infections in wild boar have received less attention than bacterial tick-borne pathogens despite the potential for spill-over into domestic pigs and livestock. Blood samples were obtained from 63 wild boar at slaughter in the 2021–2022 season from five locations across Vojvodina. DNA was extracted using a commercial column-based kit and screened by PCR targeting the 18S rRNA gene, followed by sequencing of positive amplicons. Piroplasmid DNA was detected in 19.0% of animals (12/63). Sequence analysis identified Babesia microti-like sp. (6 samples), Theileria sp. OT3 (4 samples), and a sequence clustering with Theileria annae (2 samples). Mixed infections were not detected. No statistically significant association between piroplasmid status and body condition score was found (Mann–Whitney U, p = 0.41). Tick burden was higher in piroplasmid-positive animals (mean 14.2 vs. 8.6 ticks; p = 0.03). These findings extend the known host range of piroplasmids circulating in Vojvodina and raise questions about D. reticulatus as a potential vector for T. annae in this region.

title: Comparative morphometrics of Haemaphysalis punctata and Haemaphysalis concinna females from cervid hosts in the Western Balkans
abstract: Morphological separation of Haemaphysalis punctata and H. concinna females using standard dichotomous keys is unreliable in worn or partially engorged specimens. This study applied geometric morphometric analysis to scutal shape using landmark-based methods on 142 female ticks collected from roe deer across Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Procrustes ANOVA confirmed significant separation between species (p < 0.001), accounting for 68.4% of shape variance, while a cross-validated linear discriminant analysis achieved 91.5% correct classification. Allometric correction for engorgement level was necessary and improved classification accuracy by 7.3 percentage points. A supplementary PCR-RFLP assay targeting the ITS2 region provided molecular confirmation for a subset of 60 specimens and agreed with morphometric assignments in 95.0% of cases. Combined morphometric-molecular vouchers from each collection site were deposited in the University of Novi Sad reference tick collection. The protocol offers a practical tool for situations where molecular infrastructure is unavailable.

title: Molecular characterisation of Toxoplasma gondii isolates from seropositive sheep in Vojvodina using multilocus PCR-RFLP
abstract: Brain and heart tissue samples were obtained from 31 seropositive sheep at slaughter across farms in Vojvodina between 2014 and 2015. DNA extraction was performed using a commercial tissue kit, and genotyping employed a ten-locus PCR-RFLP scheme targeting SAG1, SAG2, SAG3, BTUB, GRA6, c22-8, c29-2, L358, PK1, and Apico markers. Viable isolates were bioassayed in mice prior to molecular analysis where tissue cyst burden permitted. Type II genotype accounted for 80.6% of successful typings, with two isolates showing an atypical profile at the L358 locus. The predominance of Type II mirrors findings from central and western Europe and supports the hypothesis of a shared T. gondii population structure in the continental livestock reservoir. Results provide the first multilocus genotyping dataset from sheep in Serbia and indicate limited local genotypic diversity in this host.

title: Detection of Toxoplasma gondii DNA in pork meat cuts from backyard-slaughtered pigs in Vojvodina: a market basket approach
abstract: Between November 2022 and February 2023, 148 pork meat samples representing diaphragm, tongue, masseter, and loin from 37 backyard-slaughtered pigs were collected immediately post-slaughter on farms across Vojvodina. DNA was extracted from 5 g homogenates and tested by real-time PCR targeting the REP-529 repeat element. Overall PCR positivity was 16.2% of individual samples and 35.1% of animals had at least one positive tissue. Diaphragm showed the highest positivity rate (20.9%), followed by masseter (18.2%). No significant difference in positivity was found between seropositive and seronegative animals at low MAT titres (1:25), though animals with titres ≥1:200 had markedly higher tissue PCR positivity (54.5%). These data indicate that conventional serology alone is insufficient to predict meat safety at the individual animal level and support the case for direct tissue testing protocols in any future regulatory framework for backyard slaughter.

title: Seroprevalencija parvovirusa svinja i PRRS virusa u farmskim zapatima u Vojvodini: rezultati pilot studije
abstract: Cilj ove studije bio je utvrđivanje seroprevalencije parvovirusa svinja (PPV) i virusa reproduktivnog i respiratornog sindroma svinja (PRRSV) u farmskim zapatima na teritoriji Vojvodine. Uzorkovano je 312 serumskih uzoraka sa 14 farmi u periodu od aprila do oktobra 2011. godine. Za detekciju PPV antitela primenjen je komercijalni ELISA test (blokiing format), dok je za PRRSV korišćen indirektni ELISA. Pozitivnost na PPV utvrđena je na 11 od 14 farmi (78,6%), sa prosečnom prevalencijom od 61,4% na nivou jedinke. PRRSV seropozitivnost registrovana je na 8 farmi (57,1%), sa prosečnom prevalencijom od 38,2%. Ko-infekcija oba patogena zabeležena je na 6 farmi. Rezultati ukazuju na visoku cirkulaciju oba virusa u ispitanom regionu i naglašavaju potrebu za redovnim serološkim nadzorom kao osnove za planiranje vakcinacionih programa.

title: Thermal resistance of Bacillus cereus spores in carrot purée: determination of D- and z-values at temperatures between 95 °C and 121 °C
abstract: Spores of three Bacillus cereus strains isolated from commercially produced vegetable purées were suspended in carrot purée adjusted to water activity 0.98 and subjected to isothermal heating in sealed capillary tubes at 95, 100, 105, 110, 115, and 121 °C. Survivor counts were obtained at six time intervals per temperature using a spiral-plater and tryptone soya agar with polymyxin B overlay. D-values ranged from 38.2 min at 95 °C to 0.41 min at 121 °C. The z-value calculated from the linear portion of the thermal death time curve was 9.4 °C (R² = 0.991). Log-linear first-order kinetics provided an adequate fit at temperatures above 105 °C, whereas a shoulder phase was observed at lower temperatures, consistent with heat activation of dormant spores. Results indicate that conventional retort conditions targeting a 6-log reduction require a minimum F₁₂₁ of 2.46 min for the tested strains in this matrix. Findings are relevant for process schedule validation of ambient-stable vegetable purées intended for infant nutrition.

title: Effect of pH and soluble solids content on heat resistance of Bacillus subtilis spores in tomato-based sauces
abstract: Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 spores were inoculated into four tomato sauce formulations differing in pH (3.8 and 4.4) and soluble solids content (8 and 14 °Brix) to assess the combined influence of these factors on thermal resistance at 90, 95, and 100 °C. Isothermal inactivation experiments were carried out using a temperature-controlled water bath and stainless-steel test tubes; samples were plated on nutrient agar after serial dilution. D-values at 95 °C ranged from 5.1 min in the low-pH, high-solids formulation to 14.7 min in the high-pH, low-solids formulation. A response surface model incorporating pH, Brix, and temperature explained 88.4% of the variance in log D. The interaction term between pH and solids content was statistically significant (p < 0.01), indicating a synergistic protective effect of lower acidity and higher dissolved sugar content. These data support the re-evaluation of pasteurisation schedules for artisanal tomato sauce products in the regional market.

title: Comparison of log-linear and Weibull models for describing inactivation of Clostridium sporogenes PA 3679 spores in pea soup under conventional heating
abstract: The suitability of the Weibull model versus first-order log-linear kinetics was evaluated for Clostridium sporogenes PA 3679 spores in a standardised pea soup matrix (pH 6.8, 8% dry matter) heated at 110, 115, 118, and 121 °C. Sealed glass ampules were used for isothermal experiments; duplicate series of five ampules were removed at successive time intervals and cooled in ice water before plating on reinforced clostridial medium incubated anaerobically at 37 °C for 48 h. The Weibull scale parameter β ranged from 0.71 to 0.94 across temperatures, indicating concave-downward survival curves at all four temperatures. The Weibull model consistently produced lower root mean square error values (mean RMSE 0.19 log CFU/g) compared with first-order kinetics (mean RMSE 0.41 log CFU/g). Activation energy estimated from the temperature dependence of Weibull scale parameters was 285 kJ/mol, comparable to published values for mesophilic Clostridium spores. The practical consequence for process design is a slightly more conservative F-value requirement when applying the Weibull framework.

title: Ohmic heating of spinach purée: temperature uniformity and inactivation of Bacillus licheniformis spores at equivalent F-values to conventional processing
abstract: A bench-scale ohmic heater (1.5 kW, stainless-steel electrodes, 50 Hz) was used to heat spinach purée inoculated with Bacillus licheniformis spores to target temperatures of 95, 100, and 105 °C. Temperature was monitored at five positions using calibrated thermocouples; electrical conductivity was measured in parallel. Inactivation was compared with conventionally heated samples processed to identical F-values calculated at a reference temperature of 100 °C (z = 9.8 °C). At F₁₀₀ = 3 min, ohmic heating produced a 4.1 ± 0.3 log reduction versus 3.9 ± 0.4 log under conventional heating; differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05, paired t-test, n = 6). Temperature gradients across the ohmic cell did not exceed 1.8 °C at steady state. Electrical conductivity of spinach purée increased from 0.42 S/m at 25 °C to 1.11 S/m at 100 °C, following a linear trend. Results indicate that inactivation efficacy of ohmic heating at equivalent F-values is comparable to conventional heating for this spore-former and matrix.

title: Sub-lethal heat stress and subsequent recovery of Bacillus cereus spores in lentil soup matrix: implications for chilled ready-meal safety
abstract: Spores of Bacillus cereus ATCC 14579 were exposed to sub-lethal temperatures (60, 70, and 80 °C for 5 min) in lentil soup (pH 6.5, 11% dry matter) and then stored at 4, 8, and 12 °C for 14 days to monitor outgrowth potential. At each storage interval, spore and vegetative cell counts were obtained by parallel plating with and without heat treatment (80 °C, 10 min). Sub-lethal heat treatment at 70 °C increased the fraction of heat-activated spores capable of germinating in nutrient broth by 2.3-fold relative to untreated controls. At 12 °C storage after 70 °C stress, vegetative cell counts exceeded 10³ CFU/g by day 10 in 4 of 6 replicate packages, while untreated controls remained below detection on day 14. No outgrowth was observed at 4 °C regardless of prior heat treatment. These findings highlight a safety concern for mildly pasteurised lentil soups distributed through cold chains with temperature abuse above 8 °C.

title: Inactivation kinetics of Bacillus cereus and Paenibacillus polymyxa spores in chickpea hummus under ohmic and water-bath heating: a side-by-side comparison
abstract: Hummus prepared from rehydrated chickpeas (pH 5.9, 28% dry matter, 8% fat) was inoculated with a binary spore suspension of Bacillus cereus ATCC 14579 and Paenibacillus polymyxa NCTC 10343. Ohmic heating was performed at field strengths of 20, 30, and 40 V/cm; conventional heating used a thermostatted water bath. Both regimes were run to three target temperatures (95, 100, 105 °C) at matching heating rates. Survival data were fitted using the Weibull model. For B. cereus at 100 °C, the Weibull scale parameter δ was 4.8 min (ohmic, 30 V/cm) versus 5.1 min (conventional), with overlapping 95% confidence intervals. For P. polymyxa, δ values were systematically lower under ohmic conditions at all temperatures tested, with statistically significant differences at 95 and 100 °C (p < 0.05). The fat content of the hummus matrix slightly reduced inactivation rates relative to fat-free buffer controls, an effect more pronounced in conventional heating. Electrical conductivity measurements confirmed uniform heat generation throughout the hummus mass under all tested field strengths.

title: Dynamic temperature profiles during ohmic heating of legume-based purées: modelling heat transfer and predicting spore inactivation using the GInaFiT tool
abstract: A mathematical model coupling Joule heating, convective heat transfer, and Weibull inactivation kinetics was developed and validated for three legume purées (lentil, green pea, white bean) in a static ohmic cell. Model inputs included measured electrical conductivity as a function of temperature, specific heat capacity, and kinetic parameters previously determined under isothermal conditions for Bacillus cereus spores. Dynamic heating experiments at ramp rates of 2, 5, and 10 °C/min were performed; temperature was recorded at three axial positions. The GInaFiT add-in for Microsoft Excel was used to estimate survival during non-isothermal heating using the differential form of the Weibull model. Predicted versus observed log reductions agreed within 0.3 log units for green pea and lentil purées across all ramp rates. Prediction error was higher for white bean purée (up to 0.6 log units), attributed to its higher starch content and associated changes in viscosity during heating. The model provides a basis for process optimisation without requiring exhaustive isothermal trials for every new formulation.

title: Thermal inactivation of Bacillus sporothermodurans spores in oat-based plant drinks: effect of calcium fortification on heat resistance
abstract: Bacillus sporothermodurans, recognised for its exceptional heat resistance, is an emerging challenge in plant-based drink production. Spores were produced in laboratory conditions and inoculated into plain oat drink and calcium-fortified oat drink (calcium carbonate added to 120 mg/100 ml) at pH 6.8. Isothermal inactivation was performed at 121, 125, 130, and 135 °C using sealed stainless-steel capsules submerged in a silicon oil bath. D-values for the fortified formulation were consistently 15–22% higher than those for the plain drink across all temperatures (e.g., D₁₂₅ = 3.8 min versus 3.1 min). X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed partial coating of spore surfaces with calcium carbonate micro-particles in the fortified samples, which may account for the observed protective effect. The z-value was 8.1 °C for plain oat drink and 7.6 °C for the fortified variant. These results suggest that routine UHT schedules validated for plain plant drinks may underestimate the inactivation time required for calcium-fortified equivalents.

title: Kinetics of ohmic inactivation of Clostridium pasteurianum spores in fruit-vegetable smoothies at 90–110 °C
abstract: Clostridium pasteurianum is a significant spoilage organism in acidified vegetable products. Spores were prepared from a strain isolated from a spoiled beetroot-apple smoothie and inoculated into three commercial smoothie bases (beetroot-apple, carrot-ginger, and red pepper-tomato) at natural pH values ranging from 4.1 to 4.6. Ohmic heating was applied at 25 V/cm and 50 Hz using a tubular flow cell with residence time control; conventional heating used a coiled tubular heat exchanger. Inactivation was modelled using the modified Gompertz equation to account for shoulder and tail phenomena observed in survivor curves. In the beetroot-apple matrix, Gompertz-derived Dref (100 °C) was 1.4 min under ohmic conditions versus 2.0 min conventionally. The shoulder duration decreased from approximately 0.8 min to 0.3 min under ohmic heating, suggesting earlier membrane disruption. Electrical field strength showed a statistically significant independent contribution to inactivation (p = 0.03) after controlling for temperature, consistent with an electroporation component at these field strengths and frequencies.

title: Variability in heat resistance among Bacillus cereus sensu lato strains isolated from plant-based ready meals in the Western Balkans
abstract: Twenty-three strains belonging to the Bacillus cereus group were isolated from recalled or suspect plant-based ready meals collected from food businesses in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia between 2019 and 2022. Strains were characterised by MALDI-TOF MS and panC group phylotyping. Isothermal inactivation assays were performed in a standardised pea soup matrix at 95 and 105 °C, with Weibull fitting applied to survivor data. D-values at 105 °C ranged from 0.6 min to 4.3 min, a more than sevenfold difference. Group II (Bacillus weihenstephanensis) strains clustered at the resistant end of the distribution, exhibiting D₁₀₅ values above 2.8 min in 80% of cases. Strains isolated from ambient-stable products were significantly more heat-resistant than those from chilled products (Mann-Whitney U, p < 0.01). The study identified two strains with exceptional resistance (D₁₀₅ > 4 min) suitable for use as challenge organisms in future process validation studies for the region.

title: Effect of exopolysaccharide matrix from co-cultivated lactic acid bacteria on the heat resistance of Bacillus cereus spores in fermented plant-based spreads
abstract: Plant-based spreads fermented with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Leuconostoc mesenteroides develop visible exopolysaccharide (EPS) layers during fermentation. This study investigated whether EPS produced by these organisms at concentrations typical of commercial ferments (0.5–2.1 g/kg product) modifies the heat resistance of co-inoculated Bacillus cereus spores. Spread samples with varying EPS concentrations were prepared by adjusting fermentation duration and substrate composition; EPS content was quantified by the phenol-sulphuric acid method after alcohol precipitation. Isothermal inactivation at 95 and 100 °C showed that D-values increased by up to 18% in spreads with the highest EPS content relative to EPS-depleted controls prepared by enzymatic hydrolysis with dextranase. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed spore entrapment within EPS fibres. At EPS concentrations below 0.8 g/kg, no significant protective effect was detected (ANOVA, p > 0.05). These findings have practical relevance for the thermal processing of minimally acidified fermented plant spreads and suggest that matrix characterisation should accompany process validation.

title: Population structure and competitive interactions among Pseudomonas fluorescens genotypes co-isolated from a single fresh-cut vegetable processing line
abstract: Processing lines for fresh-cut vegetables often harbour multiple co-existing Pseudomonas fluorescens genotypes, yet most laboratory studies use single strains. This work characterised eight genotypes co-isolated from a belt conveyor and two washing tanks in a Novi Sad facility using rep-PCR fingerprinting and whole-genome sequencing of three representative strains. Pairwise co-culture experiments in fresh-cut celery wash water at 6 °C tracked relative abundance by selective plating and strain-specific qPCR over five days. In five of the eight genotype pairs, one strain reached ≥ 80% numerical dominance by day 5. Dominant strains produced significantly more AHLs in co-culture than in monoculture (1.4–2.1-fold increase), suggesting competitive induction of QS signalling. Biofilm co-culture assays on stainless steel showed 20–45% greater total biomass than the sum of monoculture controls for three pairs, indicating synergistic biofilm enhancement. These results point to community-level dynamics as a factor shaping contamination risk that single-strain models do not capture.

title: Uncertainty analysis in carry-over factor estimation: comparing frequentist and Bayesian approaches using pig feeding trial data for doxycycline
abstract: Carry-over factors for doxycycline from medicated swine feed to muscle and kidney were estimated using two statistical frameworks. Experimental data came from a previously published feeding trial (n = 48 pigs, four dose groups, three sampling time points post-withdrawal). In the frequentist approach, carry-over factors were derived by ordinary least squares regression. In the Bayesian approach, a hierarchical model was fitted using Markov chain Monte Carlo (Stan, 4 chains, 4,000 iterations), with weakly informative priors on dose-response slope and intercept. The Bayesian model yielded posterior median carry-over factors of 0.0089 (muscle) and 0.031 (kidney), with 95% credible intervals 15–28% narrower than the corresponding 95% confidence intervals from the frequentist fit, owing to partial pooling across dose groups. When propagated into a dietary exposure model, the Bayesian-derived factor reduced the 95th percentile exposure estimate by 9%. The comparison illustrates that framework choice has practical consequences for regulatory margin-of-exposure calculations.

title: Texture gradient features for early crack detection in concrete bridge decks using support vector machines
abstract: Early-stage crack detection in reinforced concrete bridge decks relies on subtle texture discontinuities that are difficult to capture with simple intensity thresholding. This study proposes a texture gradient descriptor computed over multi-scale Gaussian filter responses and feeds the resulting feature vectors into a support vector machine classifier. A dataset of 2,840 greyscale images collected from five highway bridges in Vojvodina was used, with 70 % for training and 30 % for independent testing. The SVM kernel was selected by five-fold cross-validation over RBF and polynomial options. The proposed descriptor achieved 87.3 % accuracy on the held-out test set, outperforming a histogram-of-oriented-gradients baseline by 6.1 percentage points. The study also reports a confusion matrix analysis revealing that hairline cracks under 0.2 mm width remain the principal source of misclassification. These findings guided subsequent data collection campaigns by identifying the most informative camera standoff distances.

title: Comparative evaluation of pooling strategies in shallow convolutional architectures for spalling classification
abstract: Shallow convolutional networks trained from scratch were evaluated for the binary classification of concrete spalling in industrial facility images. Three pooling configurations—max pooling, average pooling, and a learnable weighted pooling layer—were compared across architectures with two to five convolutional stages. Experiments were conducted on a proprietary dataset of 6,200 labelled images captured in a precast concrete manufacturing plant in Novi Sad, with balanced class splits. Results show that average pooling in the penultimate feature map consistently produced the lowest validation loss across all depth configurations, reducing misclassification by 9 % relative to max pooling at five convolutional stages. The authors document training instability at depths beyond four layers with the available data volume and recommend regularisation schedules for practitioners working with similarly constrained industrial image collections.

title: Influence of image acquisition conditions on CNN-based corrosion detection performance
abstract: Corrosion detection models trained under controlled laboratory lighting frequently degrade when deployed on images collected under variable outdoor illumination. This paper systematically characterises the performance drop of a five-layer CNN classifier across twelve combinations of solar elevation angle, cloud cover category, and camera exposure compensation. A controlled outdoor testbed was constructed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences campus using steel plate specimens with six standardised corrosion grades according to ISO 8501-1. Results indicate that models trained exclusively on overcast images suffer a 14.8 percentage point accuracy drop when evaluated on direct-sunlight images with automatic exposure. Histogram equalisation applied as a preprocessing step reduces this gap to 5.3 percentage points. The paper provides a structured recommendation for data collection protocols aimed at minimising photometric domain shift.

title: Batch normalisation behaviour under small-batch fine-tuning for structural inspection networks
abstract: When fine-tuning convolutional networks on small domain-specific datasets, updating batch normalisation statistics from the source domain may harm or improve performance depending on dataset characteristics. This paper studies the effect of three batch normalisation update strategies—frozen source statistics, live re-estimation from small batches, and exponential moving average of mixed statistics—on networks fine-tuned for crack and delamination classification in railway tunnel linings. Experiments use a dataset of 3,600 images from three tunnels in Serbia and Croatia, with batch sizes ranging from 8 to 64. Frozen source-domain statistics coupled with per-channel affine rescaling delivered the most stable results, reducing variance across random seeds by a factor of 2.4 compared with live re-estimation. The paper includes an ablation identifying the interaction between batch size and update strategy.
venue: Pattern Recognition and Machine Intelligence

title: Adversarial domain adaptation for bridge railing damage detection across camera models
abstract: Domain shift caused by differences between camera sensor models is a practical obstacle in deploying visual inspection systems across heterogeneous inspection fleets. This paper applies a gradient-reversal adversarial domain adaptation framework to bridge railing damage detection, where source images were collected with a Canon industrial camera and target images with a Sony mirrorless device. The backbone is a ResNet-50 fine-tuned on 4,800 source images covering four damage classes; the target domain contains 320 unlabelled and 80 labelled images. Adversarial alignment of intermediate feature maps at the third residual block reduces target-domain classification error from 31.4 % to 18.7 % relative to standard fine-tuning without adaptation. Ablations isolate the contribution of the domain discriminator at different feature resolutions.

title: Data augmentation strategies for mitigating class imbalance in facade damage datasets
abstract: Building facade inspection datasets frequently exhibit severe class imbalance, with rare high-severity damage categories representing fewer than 3 % of all samples. This paper benchmarks nine augmentation pipelines—including geometric transforms, colour jitter, CutMix, and Mosaic—applied during fine-tuning of a MobileNetV2 backbone on a 7,200-image facade dataset assembled from pre- and post-flood inspections in Vojvodina. Macro-averaged F1 score is used as the primary metric to avoid bias toward the majority class. CutMix combined with mild colour jitter yields the highest macro-F1 of 0.74 compared with 0.61 for no augmentation, a gain attributable primarily to improved recall on the two rarest damage categories. The paper also reports that excessive geometric distortion hurts performance when structural orientation is a discriminative cue.

title: Layer-wise learning rate schedules for CNN fine-tuning on seismically damaged masonry images
abstract: After seismic events, rapid assessment of masonry damage depends on classifiers that must be re-trained quickly from limited post-event imagery. This paper investigates the use of layer-wise learning rate decay—assigning lower rates to early convolutional layers and higher rates to classification heads—during fine-tuning of an EfficientNet-B2 backbone. Experiments are conducted using source data from 12,000 images of undamaged and earthquake-damaged masonry buildings in Croatia collected after the 2020 Zagreb earthquake, and target data consisting of 540 images from a 2021 Vojvodina minor seismic event. A systematic grid over five decay ratios and three learning rate magnitudes is reported. The optimal layer-wise schedule reduces top-1 error on the target domain by 11.3 percentage points compared with a uniform learning rate baseline and converges 38 % faster.

title: Domain adaptation for drone-based road crack segmentation using pseudo-label refinement
abstract: Semantic segmentation of road cracks from drone imagery is challenged by altitude-dependent resolution and shadow patterns absent from ground-level training data. This paper presents a pseudo-label refinement loop in which a DeepLabV3+ network pre-trained on ground-level crack images generates initial pseudo-labels for unlabelled drone frames; a confidence filter retains only predictions exceeding a calibrated threshold, and the network is iteratively re-trained on accepted pseudo-labels. Experiments use 9,600 ground-level labelled images and 2,200 unlabelled drone images collected over 18 km of regional roads in Serbia. After three refinement iterations, mean intersection-over-union on a drone test split of 480 labelled images reaches 0.71, versus 0.52 for direct application of the source model without adaptation. The paper analyses threshold sensitivity and documents the per-iteration change in pseudo-label acceptance rate.

title: Contrastive pre-training on synthetic damage renders for improved target-domain fine-tuning
abstract: Collecting labelled real-world damage images is expensive, motivating the use of physically based renders as a pre-training source. This paper investigates whether contrastive self-supervised pre-training on a library of 28,000 synthetically rendered concrete crack and spalling images produced with a physically based renderer improves downstream supervised fine-tuning on real inspection photographs. A SimCLR framework is used for pre-training, followed by linear evaluation and full fine-tuning on three real datasets of sizes 200, 600, and 2,000 images. Contrastive pre-training on synthetic renders consistently outperforms ImageNet-supervised initialisation at 200 and 600 real samples, with gains of 5.8 and 3.2 percentage points respectively, but the advantage disappears at 2,000 samples. The paper discusses the role of render photorealism and augmentation policy alignment in determining this crossover point.

title: Low-rank adaptation of ResNet backbones for cross-dataset concrete damage classification
abstract: Low-rank matrix decomposition applied to weight updates during fine-tuning—an approach recently popularised in large language models—is adapted here to ResNet-50 backbones for concrete damage classification. The paper asks whether constraining weight updates to low-rank increments reduces overfitting on small target datasets while preserving source-domain representations. Four target datasets of sizes 180 to 1,400 labelled images are used, covering crack, delamination, efflorescence, and spalling categories sourced from different European inspection projects. At ranks 4 and 8, the low-rank approach reduces test error relative to standard full fine-tuning by 8.1 and 6.3 percentage points on the 180-image dataset, with negligible differences at 1,400 images. The parameter count during adaptation is reduced to 2.3 % of full fine-tuning. The paper provides an analysis of singular value spectra before and after adaptation.

title: Benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol for cross-climate damage recognition in central and southeastern Europe
abstract: The absence of a standardised benchmark impedes reproducible comparison of domain adaptation methods for visual damage assessment in climatic zones across central and southeastern Europe. This paper describes the construction and release of a benchmark dataset comprising 43,600 annotated images drawn from 22 inspection campaigns in seven countries, spanning continental, semi-arid, and humid subtropical microclimate zones. Damage categories include cracks, spalling, efflorescence, corrosion, and impact damage across reinforced concrete, masonry, and steel substrates. An evaluation protocol is defined specifying three experimental tracks: unsupervised, semi-supervised with ten labels per class, and fully supervised with 200 labels per class. Baseline results for eight published domain adaptation methods are reported on all three tracks. The dataset and evaluation scripts are made publicly available under a CC BY 4.0 licence. The paper also characterises distributional shift quantitatively using maximum mean discrepancy between all climate zone pairs.

title: Attention-gate selection for partial fine-tuning of vision transformers on structural damage imagery
abstract: Vision transformer architectures trained on large general-purpose corpora offer strong representations for downstream visual tasks, but their scale makes full fine-tuning impractical when target datasets contain fewer than 500 images. This paper studies selective fine-tuning guided by gradient-based attention gate scores, which rank transformer blocks by their sensitivity to target-domain inputs and update only the top-k ranked blocks. Experiments cover three structural damage datasets with 150 to 480 labelled target images, using a ViT-B/16 backbone. Updating the top-4 blocks identified by attention gate scoring achieves accuracy within 1.8 percentage points of full fine-tuning at one quarter of the trainable parameter count and reduces catastrophic forgetting on source-domain validation by 17 %. The paper compares this strategy against adapter modules and prompt tuning across all three datasets.

title: Partitioned Hash-Join Scheduling for Bursty Data Streams on Shared-Memory Clusters
abstract: This paper examines how hash-join scheduling strategies perform when input data streams exhibit bursty arrival patterns on shared-memory cluster nodes. We implemented four scheduling variants—static partition, work-stealing, demand-driven, and hybrid—on a six-node testbed running a custom stream processing prototype written in Java. Experiments used synthetically generated log streams with inter-arrival times drawn from a Pareto distribution, parameterised to model real-world sensor bursts. Throughput, join latency, and CPU utilisation were measured across four partition counts (8, 16, 32, 64). The work-stealing variant reduced tail latency at the 99th percentile by 31% compared with static partitioning under the highest burst intensity tested, at the cost of a 7% increase in average CPU utilisation. We provide an analytical model relating partition granularity to expected load imbalance and validate it against measured data. Results suggest that adaptive stealing thresholds calibrated to burst intensity outperform fixed-threshold policies across all tested partition counts.

title: Shear strength parameters of Pleistocene loess from the Fruška Gora foothills: laboratory determination and spatial variability
abstract: Accurate shear strength characterisation of loess deposits is a prerequisite for reliable slope stability calculations. This study reports results from 47 consolidated-drained triaxial tests and 32 direct shear tests performed on undisturbed samples collected from nine borehole profiles along a 14 km segment of the right Danube bank between Futog and Beočin. Cohesion values ranged from 8 to 27 kPa and internal friction angles from 22° to 31°, with pronounced vertical stratification linked to paleosol intercalations. Geostatistical analysis using ordinary kriging revealed spatial correlation lengths of approximately 120 m horizontally and 3 m vertically. The dataset was used to derive representative design parameter sets for subsequent limit equilibrium modelling. The results confirm that treating loess as homogeneous in stability calculations introduces factors of safety errors of up to 18 percent compared with layered representations. A publicly archived parameter database is provided for use in regional hazard assessments.

title: Rainfall-induced riverbank failures on the Tisa: a case study of the 2010 high-water event near Senta
abstract: The June 2010 flood on the Tisa River triggered a series of rotational and translational slope failures along a 6 km reach upstream of Senta, affecting approximately 2.4 ha of agricultural terraces and damaging one road embankment. This paper documents field mapping of 11 failure scarps, crack surveys, and inclinometer readings from two instrumented cross-sections installed immediately after the event. Pore pressure records showed a lag of 4 to 9 days between river stage peak and maximum positive pore pressure at 3 m depth. Limit equilibrium back-analyses using Bishop's simplified method and Spencer's method yielded mobilised friction angles of 19° to 23°, consistent with laboratory residual values. The study shows that rapid drawdown following the flood crest is the dominant destabilising mechanism, more critical than the saturated loading phase, and recommends staged drawdown rates not exceeding 0.3 m per day for bank management.

title: Finite-difference modelling of progressive failure in a stratified loess bluff: sensitivity to hydraulic conductivity contrasts
abstract: Progressive failure in loess bluffs is often controlled by thin, low-permeability paleosol layers that concentrate pore pressure build-up during infiltration events. This study uses FLAC 7.0 to model a 22 m high cross-section at the Čortanovci bluff, calibrated against a 2009 rotational failure whose geometry was reconstructed from aerial survey and auger records. A series of 36 parametric runs varied the ratio of loess-to-paleosol hydraulic conductivity between 5 and 500. Results show that failure initiation migrates from the toe to the mid-slope as the conductivity contrast exceeds approximately 50, and that time to critical state shortens by 40 percent when a second paleosol layer is present within 4 m of the first. Displacement vectors and plastic strain contours from FLAC are compared with field crack patterns, showing good spatial agreement. The findings suggest that standard single-layer models underestimate failure extent by 15 to 30 percent for bluffs with multiple paleosol intercalations.

title: Mapping landslide susceptibility on Danube loess bluffs using logistic regression and field-verified inventory data
abstract: A landslide inventory was compiled for a 42 km section of the right Danube bank between Sremski Karlovci and Slankamen using 1:5000 topographic maps, orthorectified aerial photographs from 2003 and 2013, and targeted field verification of 84 mapped polygons. Logistic regression was applied with nine conditioning factors: slope angle, curvature, lithological unit, distance to paleosol outcrop, proximity to drainage channels, land use, vegetation density index from Landsat 8, groundwater depth, and proximity to the river channel. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.82 on a 30 percent hold-out test set. High and very-high susceptibility classes cover 31 percent of the mapped bluff area and correspond closely with historically documented failures. The output raster at 10 m resolution is compared with a SLIDE-based deterministic safety factor map for selected cross-sections, and the two approaches show consistent spatial patterns with deviations below 12 percent in the classification of high-susceptibility cells.

title: Effect of vegetation root reinforcement on factor of safety in loess slopes: field measurements and incorporation into limit equilibrium models
abstract: Root reinforcement from riparian and agricultural vegetation is often neglected in slope stability assessments of loess bluffs despite evidence of its measurable contribution to apparent cohesion. This study presents results from 24 root pullout tests and 18 root tensile strength measurements conducted on three dominant species—black locust, willow, and corn stubble—at three sites on the Danube right bank. Additional root area ratio profiles were determined from 48 soil cores to 1.5 m depth. Apparent cohesion additions estimated using the Wu and Waldron model ranged from 1.2 to 6.8 kPa depending on species and rooting depth. These values were incorporated into SLIDE limit equilibrium models as depth-varying cohesion increments. For slopes of 30° to 45°, inclusion of root reinforcement increased factors of safety by 0.05 to 0.14 units, sufficient to shift marginally unstable configurations to stable for shallow failure surfaces. The results support retention of existing tree cover as a practical management measure for vulnerable bluff sections.

title: Monitoring seasonal pore pressure fluctuations in a Danube loess bluff using vibrating-wire piezometers: a three-year record
abstract: Pore water pressure is the primary variable controlling the factor of safety of saturated loess slopes, yet long-term field datasets from Serbian Danube bluffs remain scarce. This paper presents a three-year continuous record (2016–2019) from eight vibrating-wire piezometers installed at two depths (2.5 m and 5 m) across four cross-sections at the Stari Slankamen bluff. Seasonal pressure cycles showed amplitude of 18 to 42 kPa at shallow depth, correlating with cumulative rainfall above a threshold of 35 mm per 15-day period (R² = 0.71). River stage changes at a lag of 6 to 12 days explained a secondary pressure cycle of 5 to 14 kPa at the toe section. Limit equilibrium safety factors computed monthly from measured pore pressures ranged from 1.08 to 1.43, indicating that the slope approaches limit equilibrium conditions in late winter. Instrument installation details and data reduction procedures are documented to allow replication at comparable sites.

title: Coupling a 1D flood routing model with slope stability analysis to estimate failure probability during Tisa flood events
abstract: This study develops a coupled framework in which daily water levels generated by a 1D HEC-RAS model for a 180 km reach of the Tisa River are used as time-varying boundary conditions for pore pressure computation in a transient seepage FLAC model, which in turn feeds a Spencer limit equilibrium analysis at twelve representative cross-sections. The procedure is demonstrated for three historical flood events: 2000, 2006, and 2010. Probability of failure is estimated by Monte Carlo sampling of shear strength parameters over 500 realisations per event. Results show that failure probability at the most vulnerable cross-sections reached 0.22 to 0.31 during the 2010 event, compared with 0.08 to 0.14 during 2006, consistent with the observed higher failure incidence in 2010. Computation time per Monte Carlo set is approximately 4.5 hours on a 16-core workstation, making the approach feasible for operational early-warning applications if pre-computed response surfaces are used.

title: Influence of loess collapsibility on slope stability during first wetting: laboratory column tests and numerical reproduction
abstract: Loess is metastable under unsaturated conditions and undergoes significant volumetric collapse upon first wetting, which can reduce effective stress and trigger failure. This paper reports results from five large-scale column experiments (diameter 0.6 m, height 1.8 m) on intact loess samples from the Titel plateau, inundated at controlled rates of 0.5, 2, and 10 cm per hour. Measured settlement at the surface ranged from 14 to 38 mm and was accompanied by lateral pressure increases of 8 to 22 kPa recorded by embedded pressure cells. Collapse index values determined in oedometer tests on companion samples averaged 0.082, classifying the material as highly collapsible. A FLAC model incorporating a collapsible constitutive relationship calibrated to the column data was subsequently used to simulate wetting front advance in a 15 m slope at 38°. Computed factors of safety fell below 1.0 before the wetting front reached mid-slope depth for the two fastest inundation rates, suggesting that irrigation or rapid flood incursion poses higher risk than slow groundwater rise.

title: Retrospective analysis of a large retrogressive landslide at Titel bluff: geometry reconstruction and back-calculation of strength parameters
abstract: The Titel loess plateau represents the only significant loess bluff at the confluence of the Tisa and Danube rivers and has a well-documented history of retrogressive failures. This paper reconstructs the geometry of a major event that occurred in February 2007, using 1:1000 scale post-failure survey data, historical 1:5000 topographic maps from 1974 and 1998, and testimony from local residents. The failure involved a volume of approximately 85 000 m³ and displayed a stepped retrogressive pattern over 19 days. Back-calculation using Spencer's method with tension crack correction yielded residual friction angles of 16° to 19° and cohesion of 2 to 5 kPa for the basal surface, which coincides with a 0.3 m thick paleosol. A FLAC model reproduces the observed two-stage retrogression when residual parameters are applied to the basal zone and peak parameters elsewhere. Implications for the design of protective revetments at the bluff toe are discussed.

title: Measurement Invariance Testing in Cross-National Panel Surveys: A Comparison of Configural and Metric Models
abstract: Comparative longitudinal survey research relies on the assumption that questionnaire items measure the same underlying constructs across time points and national subgroups. This study evaluates measurement invariance using confirmatory factor analysis on three waves of a cross-national panel survey covering six Central and Eastern European countries, with a combined analytic sample of approximately 4,200 respondents per wave. Configural, metric, and scalar invariance models were estimated in Mplus using full-information maximum likelihood to handle item-level missing data. Results indicated metric invariance held across all six countries, but scalar invariance was violated for two items relating to institutional trust in three of the six countries, suggesting partial scalar invariance as a more defensible baseline for subsequent comparisons. Modification indices and expected parameter change statistics guided a stepwise model respecification procedure. The paper discusses the practical consequences of assuming full scalar invariance in regression and structural models when partial invariance is the true data-generating structure, and provides reproducible R code for replication.

title: Adjusting for Time-Varying Confounding in Longitudinal Mediation: An Application to Employment Status and Psychological Well-Being
abstract: Mediation analysis in longitudinal observational studies is complicated when the mediator and outcome share common time-varying causes. This paper illustrates the problem using four annual waves of a Serbian labour-force panel survey (n = 1,847 working-age adults) in which employment status is hypothesised to mediate the relationship between educational attainment and self-reported psychological well-being. A directed acyclic graph was constructed to identify confounders, including household income, health limitations, and regional unemployment rate, all measured at multiple time points. Three analytic approaches were compared: a conventional cross-lagged panel model, a structural equation model with time-varying covariate adjustment, and a marginal structural model with inverse probability weighting. Estimates of the indirect effect varied substantially across approaches—ranging from a standardised coefficient of 0.09 to 0.21—illustrating the sensitivity of mediation conclusions to confounding assumptions. Diagnostic plots for weight distributions and a simulation study under a known data-generating process are included to contextualise the empirical findings.

title: Handling Non-Ignorable Dropout in Longitudinal Social Surveys: A Comparison of Pattern-Mixture and Selection Models
abstract: Attrition in panel surveys is rarely missing completely at random, and analyses that ignore systematic dropout risk producing biased parameter estimates. This paper compares pattern-mixture models and selection models for handling non-ignorable dropout in a longitudinal study of civic participation among young adults in the Western Balkans, drawn from five annual waves with an initial sample of 2,310 participants and a final-wave retention rate of 61 percent. Both model families were implemented within a structural equation modelling framework in R using the lavaan and OpenMx packages. Sensitivity analyses used a range of plausible values for the association between dropout probability and the unobserved outcome to characterise how conclusions about the relationship between social trust and civic engagement change under departures from ignorability. Findings suggest that the substantive conclusion of a modest positive association is reasonably robust to the assumed dropout mechanism, though point estimates differ by up to 15 percent between the most and least conservative specifications. Practical guidance for applied researchers choosing between these approaches is provided.

title: Automatic Constraint Extraction from Employment Contracts Using Structured Text Parsing for Rostering Systems
abstract: A persistent bottleneck in deploying automated rostering systems is translating the natural-language clauses of collective employment agreements into formal scheduling constraints. This paper presents a rule-based structured text parsing pipeline that processes Serbian-language employment contract documents and produces a parameterised constraint specification compatible with a standard MILP rostering framework. The pipeline uses a domain-specific grammar with 140 production rules covering shift duration bounds, rest requirements, maximum consecutive working days, and overtime triggers. Evaluation on 22 employment contract documents from healthcare, retail, and manufacturing sectors shows that 87 percent of constraint clauses are correctly extracted and parameterised without manual intervention. Remaining errors involve conditional clauses with ambiguous scope. Integration with the CP-SAT solver via an intermediate constraint description language is described, and a small case study demonstrates end-to-end deployment for a 90-employee retail outlet.
venue: Expert Systems with Applications

title: Probabilistic Demand Forecasting for Slow-Moving Inventory Items
abstract: Slow-moving items—products sold fewer than five times per month—pose particular difficulties for demand forecasting because count distributions are highly zero-inflated and classical time-series methods assume continuous, approximately Gaussian series. This study compares zero-inflated Poisson regression, negative binomial regression, croston decomposition, and gradient-boosted quantile regression on a synthetic dataset of 4,200 SKUs across 24 months simulated to resemble a regional wholesale distributor. Calendar features, lagged demand counts, and aggregated purchasing event histories serve as predictors. Evaluation uses the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) and the pinball loss at the 80th and 95th quantiles, since inventory decisions depend on upper-tail accuracy. Zero-inflated negative binomial regression achieves the lowest mean CRPS (1.21 units) followed by gradient-boosted quantile regression (1.34). The paper discusses the practical implications for reorder-point calculation.

title: Capture Efficiency of Hood Geometries at Belt-Conveyor Transfer Points in a Wheat Flour Mill
abstract: Belt-conveyor transfer points are among the dominant dust-generating sources in wheat flour mills. This study evaluated three hood geometries — plain rectangular, flanged rectangular, and partial enclosure — installed at identical transfer points in a mid-sized mill in Vojvodina. Airflow velocities were mapped using a 16-point hot-wire anemometry grid, and respirable dust concentrations were measured at worker breathing zones with personal sampling pumps following EN 481 protocols. For a conveyor throughput of 12 t/h, the plain rectangular hood achieved a capture efficiency of 61 %, the flanged version 74 %, and the partial enclosure 91 %. Energy consumption was monitored over three-week periods for each configuration. The partial enclosure reduced fan power demand by 18 % compared with maintaining equivalent capture using the plain hood. Practical constraints on access for maintenance and belt inspection are discussed, and a simple selection chart relating throughput rate to minimum required face velocity is provided for practitioners.

title: CFD Simulation of Airflow Patterns Inside a Flat-Bottom Grain Silo During Filling Operations
abstract: During pneumatic filling of flat-bottom grain silos, the turbulent air displaced by incoming grain carries significant quantities of fine particulate matter. Predicting the movement of this displaced air is essential for positioning exhaust inlets effectively. A Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes model was constructed in OpenFOAM for a cylindrical steel silo 18 m in diameter and 22 m tall, using a realizable k–ε turbulence closure. Filling was simulated at two volumetric flow rates (0.4 m³/s and 0.8 m³/s) with grain represented as a rising porous medium. Results showed that without active exhaust, peak air velocities near the silo wall reached 1.7 m/s and particle-laden air reached the access hatch within 40 seconds at the higher fill rate. Three exhaust inlet configurations were tested virtually; a four-point symmetric arrangement near the roof reduced hatch escape velocities by 65 %. Model predictions were validated against pressure-tap measurements taken in a partner facility in Zrenjanin, with mean deviation of 8.4 %.

title: Measurement and Correction of Duct Leakage in Retrofitted Local Exhaust Systems in Flour-Milling Plants
abstract: Older flour mills in the Western Balkans frequently have exhaust ductwork installed incrementally over several decades, resulting in systems with uncharacterised leakage and unbalanced branch flows. This paper presents a diagnostic procedure applied to two mills in Novi Sad and one in Subotica, combining total flow measurement at the fan with branch-by-branch pitot-tube traverses and pressurisation tests adapted from HVAC practice. Leakage rates of 22–37 % of fan duty were detected. Leakage points were primarily at flanged joints sealed with degraded rubber gaskets. After resealing and replacing two undersized fan units, the mills achieved capture velocities at all designated hoods that met the ACGIH Industrial Ventilation Manual recommended values. The post-retrofit personal dust monitoring showed reductions in breathing-zone concentrations of 38–55 % across sampled tasks. A cost analysis showed payback periods between 14 and 22 months through energy savings alone, not accounting for reduced absenteeism.

title: Tracer-Gas Mapping of Air Age Distribution in a Large Wheat Flour Mill: Comparison with CFD Predictions
abstract: Air age, defined as the time elapsed since air entered the ventilated space, is a practical metric for identifying poorly ventilated zones where dust can accumulate to explosive concentrations. This paper describes tracer-gas experiments using sulfur hexafluoride injected at four representative locations in a six-storey wheat flour mill building (gross volume approximately 14 400 m³) in Novi Sad. Photoionisation detectors logged concentrations at 48 fixed points over 90-minute decay sequences. Local mean age of air ranged from 6 minutes near active exhaust hoods to 47 minutes in sub-floor cable runs. A steady-state CFD model of the building was constructed from as-built drawings; it reproduced measured age values within 15 % at 38 of 48 monitoring points. Six zones with mean age exceeding 35 minutes were identified and ranked for priority ventilation upgrades. The study provides one of the few published full-building air-age datasets for a multi-storey grain milling structure.

title: Effect of Seasonal Temperature Differentials on Thermal-Draft Interference with Local Exhaust Hood Performance in an Unheated Grain Storage Building
abstract: In unheated grain storage buildings in continental climates, winter temperature differences between indoor grain mass and ambient air generate buoyancy-driven airflows that can oppose or redirect designed exhaust streams. This field study monitored hood face velocities, ambient and indoor temperatures, and wind speed at an unheated flat-deck storage building in Sremska Mitrovica over a 12-month period at weekly intervals. When outdoor temperatures fell below −5 °C, measured face velocities at transfer-point hoods dropped by an average of 22 % relative to baseline values recorded in autumn, and in two instances fell below the minimum recommended capture velocity of 0.5 m/s. Regression analysis identified outdoor-to-indoor temperature differential as the strongest predictor of velocity deficit (R² = 0.71). Two mitigation strategies are evaluated: thermal vestibule construction at the building inlet and automatic fan-speed adjustment triggered by a temperature differential setpoint. The fan-speed approach is recommended on cost grounds for retrofit applications.

title: Benchmarking Serbian Occupational Exposure Limits for Grain Dust Against EU Member State Regulations: Implications for Engineering Control Targets
abstract: Occupational exposure limits (OELs) for grain dust vary considerably across European jurisdictions, and Serbian limits have not been systematically compared with current EU practice. This review and analysis examined OELs from 22 countries, drawing on national regulatory databases and the GESTIS international limit values database. The Serbian inhalable grain dust OEL of 10 mg/m³ is at the upper end of the European range; nine EU member states apply limits between 3 and 5 mg/m³ for mixed grain dust. The analysis considers the practical consequences for ventilation design target velocities: achieving 4 mg/m³ instead of 10 mg/m³ at a belt conveyor transfer point requires approximately 40–60 % higher exhaust volume flow, based on published dose–response datasets and dilution models. The paper argues that Serbian regulations are likely to be tightened under EU accession harmonisation obligations and recommends that newly designed ventilation systems in Serbia be sized to the 4 mg/m³ target to avoid premature plant modifications.

title: Second-order sliding mode control of an electrohydraulic load simulator under time-varying torque disturbances
abstract: Load simulators used in hardware-in-the-loop testing of vehicle steering systems must reproduce dynamic torque profiles while rejecting internal force feedback from the actuator under test. A super-twisting second-order sliding mode algorithm is implemented on a rotary vane electrohydraulic motor with a rated torque of 800 Nm. The sliding variable is defined on the torque tracking error and its integral. A disturbance observer based on the super-twisting structure independently estimates actuator reaction torques and feeds forward into the control signal. System identification experiments yield a bulk modulus of 1,450 MPa and a valve flow gain of 3.2 L/min/mA. With the proposed scheme, torque tracking RMS error is reduced to 4.1 Nm across 5–40 Hz bandwidth, compared to 18.7 Nm for a standard integral sliding mode controller. Finite-time convergence is verified analytically using a homogeneous Lyapunov function.

title: Parameter uncertainty bounds for electrohydraulic servo valves: identification and their effect on sliding mode controller design
abstract: Reliable sliding mode controller design requires explicit bounds on plant parameter uncertainty. This paper establishes such bounds for a proportional four-way servo valve by combining frequency-domain identification on 12 valve units sampled from production batches at two different manufacturing tolerances, and worst-case analysis using interval arithmetic. Identified parameters include null-shift current (range 0.8–2.3 mA), pressure gain (17.2–21.8 bar/mA), and threshold deadband (1.1–2.7 mA). A linear parameterisation of the actuator–valve system is then used to compute the minimum sliding mode gain that ensures reachability for all parameters in the identified polytope. Experimental validation on a 160 kN hydraulic press shows that the conservatively designed controller maintains sliding despite valve ageing, with chattering amplitude within 1.8% of full stroke. A comparison to a Gaussian-assumption design illustrates a 15% reduction in tracking error at the cost of 22% higher switching gain.

title: Nonlinear disturbance observer coupled with sliding mode control for a hydraulic excavator arm under varying payload
abstract: Hydraulic excavator arms experience payload variations up to 200% of rated load during digging cycles, causing significant position tracking degradation when conventional sliding mode controllers designed at nominal load are used. This paper couples a nonlinear disturbance observer with a standard first-order sliding mode controller, where the observer estimates the equivalent load torque at each joint based on cylinder pressure differentials and joint angle measurements from inertial sensors. Observer bandwidth is set at 25 Hz, approximately five times the joint bandwidth. Field experiments on a 12-tonne excavator prototype equipped with pressure transducers and angle encoders demonstrate that joint angle error during a repetitive trench digging cycle is reduced from a peak of 4.8° to 1.3°. Energy consumption per cycle is reduced by 8.3% due to reduced overcompensation of the switching term.

title: Sliding mode observers for state reconstruction in hydraulic servo drives: a comparative study
abstract: Three sliding mode observer topologies—first-order, super-twisting, and high-gain—are compared for state reconstruction in a hydraulic servo drive where only cylinder pressure and piston position are directly measured. The observers estimate piston velocity, load force, and effective bulk modulus as reconstructed states or equivalent disturbances. Each observer is synthesised for identical measurement noise characteristics (0.15% full-scale RMS on pressure, 0.02 mm RMS on position) derived from empirical sensor characterisation. Stability analysis uses separate Lyapunov candidates for each topology. Monte Carlo simulations with 500 randomised uncertainty realisations complement bench experiments. High-gain observers show fastest convergence (under 20 ms) but amplify noise by a factor of 3.4. Super-twisting observers achieve the best balance: convergence within 35 ms and noise amplification of 1.2. Practical implementation guidelines for dSPACE MicroLabBox are provided.

title: Adaptive sliding mode control with online bulk modulus estimation for electrohydraulic systems operating at variable temperature
abstract: Hydraulic fluid bulk modulus decreases by approximately 15–25% as fluid temperature rises from 20 °C to 80 °C, directly affecting actuator stiffness and closed-loop bandwidth. An adaptive sliding mode controller is designed where the bulk modulus is treated as a slowly time-varying parameter estimated by a gradient-descent adaptation law with a projection operator ensuring positivity. The adaptation gain is selected via Lyapunov-based stability analysis to decouple adaptation dynamics from tracking dynamics. Experiments on a 250-bar single-rod cylinder bench include a thermal cycling profile mimicking a typical 8-hour shift. Without adaptation, position tracking RMS error increases from 0.18 mm at startup to 0.71 mm at 80 °C. With adaptation, the error stays within 0.22 mm throughout the cycle. The estimated bulk modulus matches independent ultrasonic measurements within 4.7%.

title: Sliding mode-based impedance control for an electrohydraulic robot arm in contact with rigid and compliant environments
abstract: Impedance control is commonly implemented via torque feedback, but for electrohydraulic manipulators, accurate torque sensing is costly and prone to contamination. This study implements sliding mode impedance control using only cylinder pressure measurements as force surrogates. The desired impedance is specified as a mass–spring–damper model with selectable parameters. A sliding mode inner loop maintains the sliding surface on the impedance tracking error while an outer loop schedules impedance parameters based on detected contact stiffness estimated via recursive least squares. Experiments involve contact tasks on steel surfaces (stiffness 5×10⁶ N/m) and a rubber pad (stiffness 8×10³ N/m). Peak contact force overshoots are held below 12% of the target force across all tested conditions. A comparison with a linear impedance controller reveals improved robustness to valve deadband under light contact forces below 200 N.

title: Fault-tolerant sliding mode control for electrohydraulic servo drives with partial sensor failure
abstract: Industrial hydraulic servo drives rely on redundant sensing for safety-critical applications; however, single-sensor degradation is a common failure mode that standard controllers do not accommodate gracefully. This paper proposes a fault-tolerant control scheme combining a bank of three super-twisting observers, each operating from a different sensor subset (position only, pressure only, or velocity only), with a weighted voting logic for signal reconstruction. Fault isolation logic based on parity-space residuals selects the appropriate observer within 80 ms of fault onset. The scheme is validated on a 500 kN electrohydraulic bending press against four fault scenarios: sensor bias, gain drift, intermittent signal loss, and complete dropout. Position tracking error degrades by no more than 0.35 mm during transition to degraded mode, compared to 3.8 mm for a standard sliding mode controller without fault tolerance.

title: Lyapunov-based stability analysis of sliding mode observers for uncertain hydraulic actuator models: a structured singular value approach
abstract: Observer convergence proofs for hydraulic actuator models commonly assume exact knowledge of pressure-dependent bulk modulus, which is unavailable in practice. This paper formalises the stability analysis using structured singular values (μ-analysis) to certify convergence for observer gain matrices against parametric uncertainty polytopes derived from experimental data on six commercially available hydraulic oils. The analysis extends a classical quadratic Lyapunov function approach to include frequency-weighted uncertainty norms. Analytic bounds on convergence rate as a function of uncertainty magnitude are derived for the super-twisting and first-order sliding mode observer families. Numerical results confirm that super-twisting observers tolerate ±22% bulk modulus uncertainty while maintaining a guaranteed convergence rate of 18 rad/s, whereas first-order observers require 35% higher gain for equivalent robustness, increasing chattering energy by a factor of 2.1.
