title: Data-driven disturbance characterisation for sliding mode controller tuning in heavy forging presses
abstract: Tuning the switching gain in sliding mode controllers for heavy forging presses is typically done conservatively, leading to unnecessary energy dissipation and accelerated valve wear. This study proposes a data-driven approach in which disturbance signals are estimated from closed-loop operational data collected over 14 days of production at a steel forging facility, using a recursive extended Kalman filter operating in parallel with the existing controller. The estimated disturbance distribution is characterised by its 99th percentile value, which is used directly as the switching gain design criterion. Application to a 25 MN forging press shows a 19% reduction in switching gain compared to the prior conservative setting, with no degradation in position tracking accuracy (RMS error maintained at 0.23 mm). Valve duty cycle is reduced by an estimated 11%, with implications for maintenance interval extension.

title: Whole-body vibration exposure of tractor operators on unpaved field access roads in Vojvodina: baseline measurements
abstract: This study established baseline whole-body vibration (WBV) exposure data for tractor operators travelling on compacted-earth and gravel field access roads typical of the Vojvodina plain. Triaxial accelerations were recorded at the seat-operator interface on six tractors of 55–110 kW power class over a total of 48 measurement runs. Travel speed ranged from 8 to 22 km/h. Frequency-weighted root mean square accelerations in the vertical axis ranged from 0.42 to 1.18 m/s², with the dominant energy below 4 Hz. Daily vibration exposure A(8) exceeded the EU Machinery Directive action value of 0.5 m/s² in 71% of recorded shifts assuming a four-hour daily exposure. Road surface condition, measured by a profilometer, explained 63% of the variance in vertical WBV magnitude. Results provide a reference dataset for evaluating seat suspension performance and route planning interventions in flatland farming operations.

title: Effect of pneumatic tyre inflation pressure on seat-transmitted vibration during field road travel
abstract: Tyre inflation pressure is a low-cost adjustable parameter that may reduce WBV transmitted to tractor operators. This experiment tested four rear tyre inflation pressures (80, 120, 160, and 200 kPa) on a 75 kW two-wheel-drive tractor travelling at three speeds (10, 15, 20 km/h) on a standardised 400 m compacted-earth road segment. Frequency-weighted accelerations were measured simultaneously at the tyre–axle interface and at the seat surface using triaxial MEMS accelerometers. Reducing pressure from 200 to 80 kPa decreased vertical seat acceleration by a mean of 18% at 15 km/h but increased lateral acceleration by 9%. Seat effective amplitude transmissibility (SEAT) values ranged from 0.81 to 1.14 across conditions. The lowest SEAT value was associated with 80 kPa at 10 km/h. Interaction effects between speed and pressure were statistically significant (p < 0.05). Practical guidance for field operators is discussed in relation to tyre load ratings.

title: Comparative evaluation of passive and semi-active seat suspensions under measured field road excitation profiles
abstract: Seat suspension design is a primary engineering control for WBV. This study compared three commercial tractor seats—one passive coil-spring, one passive air-spring, and one semi-active magnetorheological (MR) fluid seat—using a laboratory hydraulic vibration simulator driven by road profiles recorded on Vojvodina field roads. Sixteen male volunteers participated in a randomised cross-over protocol. Frequency-weighted vertical accelerations at the seat surface were 0.71, 0.58, and 0.39 m/s² for the coil-spring, air-spring, and MR seats respectively under a representative 15-minute profile. The MR seat reduced vibration dose value by 34% relative to the coil-spring baseline. Subjective overall comfort ratings on a seven-point scale improved significantly with the MR seat (mean 5.1 vs. 3.2 for coil-spring). Cost and maintenance implications of each solution are discussed for adoption in Serbian agricultural enterprises.

title: Influence of field road surface texture parameters on whole-body vibration: a road profilometry approach
abstract: Quantitative road surface characterisation can inform route selection and maintenance priorities to reduce operator WBV exposure. Eighteen unpaved road segments of 200–500 m length in northern Serbia were characterised using a laser profilometer at 1 mm longitudinal resolution. International Roughness Index (IRI) and power spectral density slope were derived. Simultaneous WBV measurements were performed at 10 and 18 km/h travel speeds with a standardised 85 kW tractor. IRI ranged from 2.1 to 14.7 m/km across segments. Multiple linear regression with IRI, speed, and loaded/unloaded status explained 79% of variance in frequency-weighted vertical acceleration. A breakpoint in the IRI–acceleration relationship was identified near IRI = 7.5 m/km, above which vibration increased at a steeper rate. These findings support a threshold-based road maintenance protocol that prioritises the most deteriorated segments for grading.

title: A low-cost data acquisition system for long-term monitoring of tractor operator vibration exposure in small farming operations
abstract: Commercial WBV measurement systems cost 3,000–12,000 EUR and are inaccessible to small farming cooperatives. This paper describes the development and validation of a low-cost data acquisition system built around a calibrated triaxial MEMS accelerometer module, a single-board computer for on-board data storage, and open-source signal processing scripts implementing ISO 2631-1 weighting filters. The system was validated against a certified reference instrument in both laboratory (hydraulic shaker) and field conditions. Mean deviation in frequency-weighted acceleration across 24 paired runs was 3.8% (max 7.1%), within the ±10% acceptance criterion. Power consumption allowed 12-hour autonomous operation on a 5 Ah battery. Hardware component cost was approximately 180 EUR per unit. The system has been deployed on 11 tractors in three cooperatives in the Bačka region and has collected over 900 hours of operational data since deployment.

title: Whole-body vibration exposure during combined ploughing and transport cycles: time-weighted daily exposure estimation
abstract: Tractor operators rarely perform transport alone; their working day typically combines field tillage, headland turns, and road transport. This study characterised WBV exposure across the full working cycle of ploughing operations on flat Vojvodina fields, including intercycle transport on unpaved field roads. Thirty-two full-day measurement sessions were conducted on four-wheel-drive tractors (80–130 kW) with mounted ploughs. Time–activity logs were recorded in parallel with continuous triaxial seat acceleration measurements. Transport phases constituted 18–34% of total working time but contributed 31–52% of daily vibration dose owing to higher travel speeds on roads. Overall A(8) ranged from 0.48 to 0.89 m/s² across sessions. A simple time-weighted model using separately characterised exposure magnitudes for transport and tillage phases predicted measured A(8) with a mean absolute error of 0.06 m/s². The model is proposed as a practical tool for daily exposure assessment without continuous monitoring.

title: Discrete element modelling of grain flow in combine harvester threshing and cleaning units
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of DEM methodology as applied to the two principal grain-processing units of combine harvesters: the threshing unit and the cleaning unit. Covered topics include particle shape representation for wheat, barley, and maize; calibration protocols for contact and bonded-particle parameters; coupling of DEM with airflow solvers for the cleaning shoe; scaling strategies for industrial-scale simulation; and validation approaches using high-speed imaging and mass-balance measurements. Representative simulation results illustrate the sensitivity of threshing efficiency, grain damage, and cleaning loss to design variables including cylinder speed, concave geometry, sieve aperture size, and fan air velocity. Practical guidance on computational cost management for engineering design studies is provided, including particle scaling and periodic geometry approximations. The chapter draws on the author's group's work over a decade and is intended for graduate students and practicing engineers in agricultural machinery development.

title: Cephalometric Changes in Mouth-Breathing Children After Six Months of Rapid Maxillary Expansion: A Prospective Study
abstract: Rapid maxillary expansion (RME) is a common early intervention for children with transverse maxillary deficiency associated with habitual mouth breathing. This prospective study enrolled 38 children aged 7–10 years (21 boys, 17 girls) diagnosed with confirmed nasal obstruction and posterior crossbite. Lateral and posteroanterior cephalometric radiographs were obtained at baseline and at six-month follow-up. Measurements included ANB angle, mandibular plane angle, upper airway width at the nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal levels, and lower anterior face height. After six months of RME, statistically significant increases were observed in nasopharyngeal airway width (mean increase 2.1 mm, p < 0.01) and a reduction in mandibular plane angle steepening compared to an untreated control group of 20 children. ANB angle showed no significant change at this interval. Findings suggest that skeletal transverse correction may have measurable, if modest, effects on vertical craniofacial growth trajectory within the first six months, with longer follow-up required to assess stability.

title: Soft-Tissue Nasolabial Profile Changes Following Functional Appliance Therapy in Mouth-Breathing Children: A Pilot Cephalometric Assessment
abstract: Functional appliances used in early Class II correction are intended primarily to modify skeletal relationships, but their effect on soft-tissue profile in children with concurrent mouth-breathing habits is less documented. This pilot study included 22 children (aged 8–11 years) with Class II division 1 malocclusion and confirmed habitual mouth breathing, treated with a twin-block appliance over a 12-month period. Pre- and post-treatment lateral cephalograms were digitised and soft-tissue landmarks traced using standardised software. Measured parameters included nasolabial angle, soft-tissue convexity, upper lip length, and lip-to-E-plane distance. After 12 months, mean nasolabial angle increased by 4.3° (p = 0.03) and soft-tissue convexity decreased significantly (p = 0.04). Upper lip length showed a mean increase of 1.8 mm. No control group was included due to sample size limitations. Results are considered preliminary; a larger controlled trial is planned. The study provides baseline data for a subsequent adequately powered investigation.

title: Cone-Beam CT Assessment of Upper Airway Dimensions Before and After Adenotonsillectomy in Children Referred for Orthodontic Evaluation
abstract: Children referred for early orthodontic assessment frequently present with concurrent adenotonsillar hypertrophy contributing to mouth breathing and upper airway restriction. This retrospective study examined cone-beam CT (CBCT) datasets from 31 children (ages 6–12 years) who had CBCT scans taken both before adenotonsillectomy and approximately 9 months post-surgery as part of routine orthodontic follow-up at a dental clinic in Novi Sad. Three-dimensional airway segmentation was performed using dedicated volumetric software. Total nasopharyngeal airway volume increased by a mean of 34% (range 18–61%) post-surgery. Minimum axial cross-sectional area increased by a mean of 28 mm². Correlation analysis showed a moderate positive correlation between post-surgical airway volume increase and reduction in mandibular plane angle at the 9-month interval (r = 0.41, p = 0.02). This retrospective design limits causal inference, but findings are consistent with the hypothesis that airway patency restoration may partially redirect vertical craniofacial growth.

title: Parental Awareness of Mouth Breathing as a Risk Factor for Dental Development: Results from a Questionnaire Survey in Vojvodina
abstract: Early identification of mouth breathing in children depends substantially on parental recognition of the habit and its potential consequences. This study evaluated parental awareness and health-seeking behaviour regarding mouth breathing among 310 parents of children aged 4–8 years attending general dental practices in Vojvodina. A self-administered questionnaire covered recognition of mouth-breathing signs, beliefs about consequences, prior consultations sought, and information sources. Results showed that 58% of parents recognised mouth breathing as potentially harmful to dental development, while only 31% were aware of possible craniofacial effects. Parents with higher educational attainment scored significantly higher on the awareness index (p < 0.001). Only 19% of parents who reported observing habitual mouth breathing in their child had consulted a dentist specifically about the issue. Findings indicate a substantial gap between observed prevalence of the habit and appropriate dental or medical referral, with implications for public health messaging and dental practice education programmes.

title: Influence of pellicle formation time on CPP-ACP adsorption and subsequent mineral deposition: an atomic force microscopy study
abstract: The acquired enamel pellicle modulates ion and molecule access to the enamel surface, yet its effect on CPP-ACP adsorption is poorly characterised. Polished enamel discs were exposed to clarified whole saliva for 0, 30, 60, or 120 minutes to generate pellicles of increasing thickness (estimated 2–80 nm by ellipsometry), then treated with CPP-ACP suspension (2% w/v) for 5 minutes. Adsorption of CPP-ACP nanocomplexes was imaged by tapping-mode AFM before and after a subsequent demineralisation challenge. Disc surfaces were also analysed by XPS for calcium and phosphorus atomic percentages. Thicker pellicle reduced mean CPP-ACP nanocomplex surface density from 1 240/μm² (no pellicle) to 380/μm² (120-minute pellicle). Post-challenge XPS showed correspondingly lower residual calcium in the high-pellicle condition. These findings suggest that clinical application of CPP-ACP immediately after professional cleaning, before pellicle reformation, may maximise surface adsorption.

title: Narrative versus statistical evidence in public health messages about Type 2 diabetes prevention
abstract: A 3 × 2 between-subjects online experiment (N = 418, general adult population of Serbia) tested whether narrative evidence (a personal story from a diabetes patient) or statistical evidence (population-level risk figures) produced stronger intentions to reduce sugar intake and engage in regular exercise, and whether this interacted with participants' numeracy level. Narrative messages produced higher intention scores overall (η² = .04), but this advantage was fully confined to low-numeracy participants. High-numeracy participants showed comparable responses to both message types. Perceived similarity to the story protagonist moderated narrative effects: higher perceived similarity was associated with a 0.44-point increase on a 7-point intention scale (p < .001). Message credibility ratings did not differ between conditions. The findings suggest that segmenting audiences by numeracy and tailoring evidence type accordingly could improve population-level diabetes prevention communication without requiring substantially greater production costs.

title: Motivational interviewing training for community pharmacists: a pilot study of communication behaviour change
abstract: Community pharmacists are frequent points of contact with patients managing chronic conditions, yet their communication training rarely includes motivational interviewing (MI). This study evaluated a one-day MI workshop delivered to 28 pharmacists across five community pharmacies in Novi Sad. Communication behaviour was assessed using standardised simulated patient encounters recorded at baseline, one month post-training, and three months post-training, and coded with the Motivational Interviewing Treatment Integrity scale (MITI 4.2). Mean global spirit scores improved significantly from baseline (M = 2.3) to one month (M = 3.5, p < .001) but showed partial decay by three months (M = 3.1). Reflective listening ratios and MI-adherent utterance proportions followed similar trajectories. Pharmacists with higher baseline empathy scores (Interpersonal Reactivity Index) showed greater and more durable gains. Results support brief MI training as feasible in pharmacy settings while highlighting the need for booster sessions to sustain skill acquisition.

title: Effectiveness of brief autonomy-supportive counselling delivered via video call for increasing physical activity in adults with pre-hypertension: a pilot randomised trial
abstract: This pilot randomised controlled trial evaluated two sessions of autonomy-supportive counselling delivered by trained psychologists via video call, compared with written physical activity guidelines alone, in adults with pre-hypertension (systolic BP 120–139 mmHg, N = 60, aged 35–65). The primary outcome was accelerometer-measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) at 8 weeks. Secondary outcomes included autonomous motivation, self-efficacy, and systolic blood pressure. The counselling group accumulated 48 more minutes of MVPA per week at follow-up (95% CI: 18–78 min, p = .003) and showed higher autonomous motivation (d = 0.62). No significant group difference in blood pressure was observed, likely reflecting insufficient statistical power. Counsellors' MI-consistent behaviours, coded from session recordings, were positively associated with participant autonomous motivation at 4 weeks (r = .51). Results justify a fully powered trial and indicate that video-delivered autonomy-supportive counselling is acceptable in this population.

title: Message personalisation and perceived relevance in a workplace stress-reduction campaign: evidence from three Serbian companies
abstract: Workplace mental health campaigns often distribute uniform materials regardless of employee characteristics. This study tested whether personalising stress-reduction messages to employees' reported stress type (work overload, interpersonal conflict, or role ambiguity) increased perceived personal relevance and intention to use provided self-help resources. Employees at three medium-sized companies in Vojvodina (total N = 284) were randomly assigned to receive personalised or generic messaging via their internal e-mail system over three weeks. Perceived relevance was higher in the personalised condition (M = 5.1 vs. 4.3 on a 7-point scale, t(282) = 5.2, p < .001, d = 0.62). Clicks on self-help resource links were 2.3 times more frequent in the personalised group (rate ratio = 2.31, 95% CI: 1.54–3.46). No significant difference was found for self-reported stress levels at three weeks, suggesting that intention and engagement do not immediately translate to symptom reduction. These findings support personalisation as a cost-feasible enhancement to workplace health promotion.

title: Fear appeals in anti-sedentary behaviour campaigns: a meta-analysis of experimental studies published 2000–2022
abstract: Fear appeal interventions aimed at reducing prolonged sitting and sedentary behaviour have accumulated as a distinct literature separate from broader physical activity research. This meta-analysis aggregated 29 experimental and quasi-experimental studies (total N = 6,814) testing fear-based versus non-fear messages on sedentary behaviour outcomes. Random-effects models yielded a pooled effect size of d = 0.22 (95% CI: 0.13–0.31) in favour of fear appeals on behavioural outcomes; effects on intentions were somewhat larger (d = 0.31). Moderator analyses showed that studies including high-efficacy information alongside threat information produced significantly larger effects (Q = 9.4, p = .002), consistent with the Extended Parallel Process Model. Studies relying solely on self-reported sitting time as outcome showed inflated effect estimates relative to device-based measures. Publication bias was detected via Egger's test and trim-and-fill correction reduced the pooled estimate to d = 0.16. The review highlights the importance of pairing threat framing with actionable coping information in campaign design.

title: Designing chatbot-delivered behaviour change conversations for smoking cessation: user testing and interaction analysis
abstract: Conversational agents (chatbots) represent a scalable channel for delivering behaviour change support, but evidence on optimal conversational design remains limited. This preprint reports findings from a user-testing phase of a chatbot designed to deliver brief motivational enhancement for smoking cessation. Forty-two smokers (18–55 years) in Novi Sad interacted with a prototype chatbot across two sessions and completed measures of perceived autonomy support, conversational naturalness, and engagement. Think-aloud protocols were recorded during the first session and subjected to thematic analysis. Users responded positively to reflective listening utterances (coded from conversation logs) but found open-ended questioning excessive when not clearly linked to a visible conversational goal. Perceived autonomy support correlated with willingness to continue using the chatbot (r = .58, p < .001). Interaction log analysis identified six recurrent breakdown points where users disengaged or gave minimal responses. The findings are used to revise the chatbot script and interaction logic ahead of a planned randomised evaluation.

title: Reading speed and error patterns in older users navigating hierarchical menu structures on desktop computers
abstract: Menu navigation is among the most frequent tasks performed by older adults using administrative and healthcare software, yet menu depth and labelling conventions are rarely evaluated for this population. This study recruited 56 participants aged 60–78 with varying levels of prior computer experience, classified into three digital-literacy groups using the Česká–Šimková Digital Skills Scale adapted for Serbian. Participants completed 48 menu navigation tasks in a controlled environment using a prototype desktop application with three hierarchy depths (2, 3, and 4 levels) and two labelling schemes (functional versus categorical). Task completion time, error rate, and number of backtracking events were recorded. Three-level menus with functional labelling produced the lowest error rate (8.3 %) in low-literacy older users. Participants with four-level categorical menus showed backtracking in 41 % of trials. Reading speed measured during label scanning correlated moderately with task completion time (r = 0.48, p < 0.001). Recommendations for menu design in public-sector software are discussed.

title: Visual search efficiency on web pages differing in layout complexity: a comparison across age groups
abstract: Web pages encountered in everyday tasks such as online banking or governmental services vary substantially in visual complexity, but age differences in visual search on such pages are underexplored in ecologically valid conditions. This experiment used eye tracking (Tobii TX300, 300 Hz) to record fixation counts, first-fixation latency, and total dwell time while 34 participants aged 62–75 and 34 participants aged 20–30 searched for target items on 24 webpage screenshots classified into low, medium, and high visual complexity using the WCAG contrast and element-density criteria. Older adults exhibited 1.9 times more fixations per trial on high-complexity pages and their first-fixation latency on the target item was on average 2.3 seconds longer. A significant interaction between age and complexity emerged for dwell time (F(2,132) = 11.4, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.15). Scanpath tortuosity was substantially higher in older participants on all complexity levels, indicating less efficient search strategies. The data are discussed in relation to age-related decline in inhibitory control and visual crowding effects.

title: Usability of e-health appointment booking systems among rural older adults with low digital literacy
abstract: Primary care appointment booking has moved increasingly online in Serbia, yet usability evaluation of such systems for older rural users is sparse. This study recruited 61 adults aged 60–82 living in rural municipalities in Vojvodina, none of whom had formal computer training. Participants attempted to book a fictional medical appointment using a prototype modelled on a real regional health portal, with all personal data anonymised. Think-aloud protocols were recorded and analysed for error classification (slips, mistakes, and recovery failures). Overall task completion rate was 34 %. The most common failure points were password creation (58 % of participants abandoned at this step), CAPTCHA interaction (43 %), and date-picker widget use (61 % produced invalid inputs). Qualitative codes identified from think-aloud data included confusion about system status feedback, fear of making irreversible errors, and lack of familiarity with form field affordances. A revised low-fidelity prototype incorporating larger controls, plain-language labels, and an optional SMS-based confirmation pathway raised completion rates to 71 % in a second test session with 28 participants.

title: Scroll behaviour and content retention in older tablet users: an exploratory eye-tracking study
abstract: Scrolling is a fundamental but cognitively demanding interaction on tablet devices that requires continuous spatial updating. This exploratory study examined scrolling patterns and subsequent content recall in 39 adults aged 63–79 using a 10-inch Android tablet displaying two types of content: a news article (continuous text) and a product listing page (grid layout). Eye-tracking data (SMI RED250 mobile, 250 Hz) were combined with scroll-event logs and a free-recall test administered five minutes after each task. Participants made an average of 6.8 scroll gestures per task and re-scrolled to previously viewed content in 44 % of trials, suggesting difficulty maintaining a spatial model of page content. Recall scores for content appearing below the initial visible area were significantly lower than for above-the-fold content (t(38) = 4.12, p < 0.001, d = 0.66). Scroll velocity correlated negatively with recall (r = −0.41). The results suggest that long-scrolling page designs may be particularly disadvantageous for older tablet users and that pagination or section anchoring may improve content retention.

title: Comparing error rates on icon-only versus icon-plus-label navigation bars across age and digital experience levels
abstract: Mobile application navigation bars frequently use icons without text labels to save screen space, but the cognitive cost of this convention for older or inexperienced users is not well documented. This between-subjects experiment assigned 88 participants to one of two interface conditions (icon-only versus icon-plus-label) and crossed this with three age-by-experience groups: younger users (18–35), older experienced users (60+, regular smartphone users), and older inexperienced users (60+, fewer than 6 months smartphone use). Participants completed 30 navigation tasks per session in a prototype app covering five domains (calendar, messages, settings, search, home). Icon-only navigation produced error rates of 6.1 %, 12.4 %, and 31.7 % respectively across the three groups. The label condition reduced errors in older inexperienced users by approximately 18 percentage points. Subjective confidence ratings (7-point scale) were substantially lower in the icon-only condition for both older groups. Icon familiarity ratings collected post-task showed poor recognition of icons representing settings and account management in older inexperienced participants. Results support the mandatory inclusion of text labels in navigation interfaces targeting heterogeneous older adult audiences.

title: Momentary affect and physiological arousal during commutes through green and grey urban routes: an experience sampling study
abstract: Experience sampling methodology (ESM) was combined with continuous heart rate and electrodermal activity monitoring to track stress and affect during morning commutes in 63 employed adults (36 women, mean age 35.2, SD 8.7) living in Novi Sad. Over 10 working days, participants were randomly prompted four times per commute to report valence and arousal on single-item visual analogue scales via a smartphone app. GPS traces were coded for proportion of commute time spent along tree-lined streets or park paths versus fully built corridors using municipal spatial data. Multilevel models revealed that a 10% increase in the proportion of green-corridor commute time predicted a 0.16-point increase in same-moment valence ratings (95% CI: 0.07–0.25) and a −0.09 µS reduction in EDA (95% CI: −0.17 to −0.02), controlling for commute duration, mode, weather, and individual random intercepts. Effects were similar on Monday compared to other weekdays. The approach demonstrates the feasibility of naturalistic, longitudinal psychophysiological monitoring in commuting research.

title: Nominal Case Marking Errors in Hungarian as a Heritage Language Among Serbian-Dominant Bilingual Children
abstract: This study examined morphosyntactic errors in the written and oral production of Hungarian nominal case suffixes among 48 third- and fifth-grade students attending Hungarian-language primary schools in the Subotica region. Learners were classified as heritage speakers on the basis of a parental language-use questionnaire. Elicited imitation tasks and a sentence-completion test were administered over two consecutive school years. Error frequencies were coded by case type (accusative, dative, instrumental) and analysed using mixed-effects logistic regression. Results showed that accusative marking accuracy reached 72 % by grade three but dative suffix selection remained at 41 % by grade five. Serbian-dominant home environments predicted significantly lower accuracy on oblique cases (β = −0.43, p < .01). The findings suggest that existing curricula introduce oblique case paradigms too early relative to learners' developmental readiness, and that sequencing adjustments at grades two to four may reduce persistent errors.

title: Receptive Vocabulary Depth in Serbian-Hungarian Bilingual Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Survey
abstract: Receptive vocabulary breadth and depth were assessed in 134 students aged 12 to 17 enrolled in bilingual secondary programmes in Vojvodina. Three standardised measures were adapted and piloted in both languages: a yes/no recognition checklist, a word-associates test, and a graded definition task. Data were collected across four schools in Subotica and Senta. Mixed ANOVA indicated a significant language × grade interaction (F(3,260) = 8.74, p < .001), with Serbian vocabulary depth growing faster than Hungarian across all grade levels. Depth scores in Hungarian plateaued after grade 8 in students reporting low Hungarian use at home. Correlational analysis linked depth gains to the number of extended reading assignments in Hungarian, independent of total instruction hours. The study contributes evidence for prioritising extensive reading components in heritage-language curricula alongside conventional grammar instruction.

title: Contrastive Analysis of Verb Aspect in Hungarian and Serbian: Pedagogical Implications for Curriculum Design
abstract: Hungarian and Serbian encode aspect through fundamentally different morphological mechanisms. Serbian employs perfective-imperfective verb pairs as lexical units, while Hungarian uses prefixation productively. This contrastive study analysed textbook exercises and teacher-produced materials from 18 classrooms in three Vojvodina municipalities to document how aspect is currently taught to bilingual learners. A total of 1,240 exercise items were coded by linguistic target, task type, and grade level. Findings revealed that only 14 % of items explicitly addressed aspectual distinctions, and cross-linguistic comparison was virtually absent from all sampled materials. Interviews with 22 teachers confirmed awareness of learner confusion but uncertainty about instructional strategies. A sequenced contrastive module was proposed, with explicit metalinguistic explanation deferred to grade seven and practice activities introduced from grade four. The chapter argues that contrastive awareness benefits both minority-language and majority-language literacy development.

title: Parental Language Attitudes and Their Relation to Heritage Language Maintenance in Vojvodina Families
abstract: Language maintenance among minority communities depends partly on attitudes formed in the home. This survey study recruited 213 parents of Hungarian-heritage children enrolled in bilingual primary schools across northern Vojvodina. A validated 28-item Likert-scale questionnaire measured instrumental, integrative, and identity-related language attitudes separately for Hungarian and Serbian. Structural equation modelling tested whether parental attitude dimensions predicted reported home language use, which in turn predicted children's self-reported Hungarian proficiency. The model yielded acceptable fit (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.057). Identity-related attitudes toward Hungarian were the strongest predictor of home language use (standardised β = 0.51), while instrumental attitudes toward Serbian negatively predicted Hungarian home use (β = −0.28). The results suggest that teacher education programmes should include guidance on communicating the identity and cultural value of heritage language maintenance to parents, not only its academic utility.

title: Teacher Beliefs About Error Correction in Bilingual Heritage-Language Classrooms: An Interview Study
abstract: Corrective feedback practices in heritage-language classrooms differ from those in foreign-language settings because learners' emotional connection to the language and their family identity is implicated in error treatment. Twenty-seven Hungarian-language primary teachers in Vojvodina participated in semi-structured interviews of approximately 50 minutes each. Interview transcripts were subjected to thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's framework, with three independent coders reaching a Cohen's κ of 0.76. Five recurring belief clusters were identified: concerns about affective harm, uncertainty about which variety to model, preference for implicit recasts over explicit correction, attribution of errors to Serbian interference, and perceived insufficiency of pre-service training on corrective feedback. Teachers with more than ten years of experience reported marginally more systematic feedback routines. The findings have direct implications for revising teacher education curricula at the Faculty to include structured units on feedback in heritage contexts.

title: Oral Proficiency Development Across Two School Years: A Longitudinal Study of Heritage-Hungarian Speakers in Grade Five and Six
abstract: Oral proficiency in heritage Hungarian was tracked longitudinally in 61 students at four primary schools in Subotica and Kanjiža over 22 months. At four time points (September and May of each year), learners completed a 10-minute oral picture-narrative task. Transcripts were coded for mean length of utterance, lexical diversity (moving-average type-token ratio), morphological accuracy, and discourse connective use. Mixed-effects growth models showed statistically significant improvement in lexical diversity (t = 3.19, p < .01) and discourse connective use (t = 2.88, p < .01), while morphological accuracy gains were small and non-significant at the group level. Students whose teachers reported using structured narrative activities at least twice weekly showed steeper lexical diversity growth curves. The study provides baseline oral proficiency data for this learner population, which had not previously been examined longitudinally.

title: Designing a Diagnostic Assessment Battery for Bilingual Heritage-Hungarian Learners at School Entry
abstract: Reliable screening tools for Hungarian language development at school entry are needed to support differentiated instruction in Vojvodina bilingual schools. This study reports the development and initial validation of a 35-item diagnostic battery targeting phonological awareness, receptive morphosyntax, and vocabulary breadth in incoming first-graders. The battery was piloted with 89 children (mean age 6;4) at six schools across three municipalities. Item difficulty and discrimination indices were computed; 7 items were removed following Rasch analysis due to poor fit. Internal consistency of the revised 28-item battery was α = 0.81. Convergent validity was supported by moderate correlations with an established general language screener (r = 0.62, p < .001). Teacher-administered procedures were feasible within a single 25-minute session. The battery is intended for use by classroom teachers rather than specialist diagnosticians, and normative tables stratified by home language use are provided.

title: Classroom Code-Switching Patterns and Their Relation to Grammatical Accuracy in Heritage-Language Instruction
abstract: Code-switching between Hungarian and Serbian is common in Vojvodina bilingual classrooms, yet its relationship to learner accuracy outcomes remains underexamined. Sixteen classroom sessions taught by eight teachers at four primary schools were video-recorded and transcribed; 4,830 teacher utterances and 3,712 learner utterances were coded for language choice, discourse function, and interactional context. Learner grammatical accuracy on subsequent weekly written tasks was correlated with classroom code-switching patterns at the teacher level. Teachers who code-switched predominantly for procedural management (explaining tasks or behaviour) while keeping content explanation in Hungarian showed higher learner accuracy on morphological tasks (r = 0.61, p = .01). Teacher code-switching for content explanation was negatively associated with learner accuracy on subordinate clause production. Findings are discussed with respect to functional uses of code-switching and their incorporation into teacher education coursework.

title: Adapting the Common European Framework of Reference for Heritage-Language Learners: Challenges and a Provisional Rubric
abstract: The Common European Framework of Reference for Languages was designed primarily for foreign-language learners rather than heritage speakers, whose uneven proficiency profiles fit poorly into its unidimensional progression. This conceptual and empirical paper develops a provisional assessment rubric for heritage Hungarian adapted from CEFR descriptors. Expert teachers (n = 14) and applied linguists (n = 8) participated in two rounds of a Delphi procedure to evaluate and revise draft descriptor sets across listening, speaking, reading, and writing for the B1–B2 range most relevant to secondary heritage learners in Vojvodina. Inter-rater reliability for the final rubric was satisfactory (Fleiss κ = 0.69). The rubric was trialled with 33 grade-eight learners; score distributions showed less ceiling clustering than standard CEFR rubrics applied to the same learners. The paper calls for further empirical validation and proposes collaboration with provincial education authorities for piloting.

title: Pre-Service Teacher Preparation for Heritage-Language Instruction: A Programme Audit and Student Feedback Study
abstract: This study audited the teacher preparation curriculum at a faculty specialising in Hungarian minority education and collected feedback from current students and recent graduates on their readiness for heritage-language classroom contexts. Programme documents from 2015 to 2024 were analysed for coverage of second-language acquisition theory, bilingualism, and culturally responsive pedagogy. An online survey was administered to 68 current students and 41 graduates (graduated 2018–2023). Graduates rated their preparation for dealing with highly variable learner proficiency as the lowest-scoring domain (mean 2.3 on a 5-point scale), and reported that field placement hours were insufficient for developing corrective feedback routines. Current students identified a disconnect between theoretical coursework and observed classroom practice. Four programme modifications are proposed: a stand-alone heritage-linguistics module, extended supervised practicum in mixed-proficiency classrooms, peer observation protocols, and integration of diagnostic assessment tools into methods courses.

title: Transfer Errors in Hungarian L2 Serbian: A Corpus Study of Vojvodina Secondary School Writers
abstract: This study examines morphosyntactic transfer errors produced by Hungarian-speaking students learning Serbian as a second language in secondary schools across Vojvodina. A manually annotated corpus of 420 written compositions (approximately 84,000 tokens) was compiled from four schools in Subotica and Senta between 2009 and 2010. Errors were classified into eight categories following a modified version of the Contrastive Analysis Hypothesis framework, with case-suffix selection and verbal aspect marking accounting for 61% of all annotated instances. Inter-annotator agreement reached a Cohen's kappa of 0.74 across two trained annotators. Frequency distributions were compared against a reference corpus of L1 Serbian student writing. Results show that errors in case government are significantly more frequent than predicted by surface-level contrastive grammars, suggesting that lexical frequency effects modulate transfer. The findings are discussed in relation to existing typological accounts of the Finno-Ugric–Slavic contact zone.

title: Language Choice as Identity Statement: Code-Switching Episodes in Vojvodina Hungarian Young Adult Fiction
abstract: This study examines code-switching between Hungarian and Serbian in a corpus of 14 young adult novels and short story collections published in Vojvodina between 2010 and 2020. Using conversation analysis adapted for literary dialogue, the study identifies 312 discrete code-switching episodes and classifies them by function: social alignment, humour, emotional intensification, and identity boundary marking. Quantitative distribution shows that social alignment accounts for 41% of episodes, identity boundary marking for 26%, emotional intensification for 21%, and humour for 12%. Close reading of boundary-marking episodes reveals a pattern in which Serbian-language utterances are associated with institutional authority—schools, hospitals, government offices—while Hungarian is reserved for family intimacy and friendship. The study argues that authors use code-switching strategically to model a bilingual identity that is pragmatic rather than conflicted, offering adolescent readers a representational framework for everyday multilingual navigation in contemporary Vojvodina.

title: Active Learning of Network Protocol State Machines Using Membership and Equivalence Queries
abstract: Angluin's L* algorithm learns an unknown regular language by posing membership queries and equivalence queries to a teacher. We adapt this framework to learn state machines of application-layer network protocols, where a live server acts as the membership oracle and conformance testing acts as the approximate equivalence oracle. The approach is applied to four text-based protocols implemented by open-source servers. For each protocol, we measure the number of membership queries required until convergence, the size of the resulting hypothesis automaton, and the number of counterexamples returned during equivalence testing. Across all four protocols, learning converged within 2,100 to 14,700 membership queries and produced automata of 12 to 47 states. We discuss reset costs, timeouts, and non-determinism in server responses as practical obstacles and propose mitigations. The resulting models are validated against independently written RFC-compliant test suites.

title: Detecting Anomalous Protocol Behaviour Using Inferred Automaton Models
abstract: Once a finite automaton model of a protocol is inferred from normal traffic, it can serve as a baseline for anomaly detection: messages causing transitions absent from the model are flagged. We implement this principle and evaluate it on a dataset of 230,000 sessions from a SCADA communication protocol captured in a test environment, of which 4,800 sessions contain injected anomalies of five types (replay, truncation, out-of-order, field mutation, and session hijack simulation). The inferred DFA correctly flags anomalous sessions with a precision of 0.91 and a recall of 0.87 averaged across anomaly types. Replay and out-of-order anomalies are detected most reliably; field mutation is detected less well because it does not always alter the message-type sequence. We compare performance to a Hidden Markov Model baseline and a rule-based system, finding the automaton approach superior in precision at comparable recall levels.

title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Passive Learning of Regular Languages with One-Sided Error
abstract: We study the sample complexity of passive learning of regular languages in the PAC framework where learners are permitted only false-negative errors — that is, the hypothesis may reject strings in the target language but must not accept strings outside it. This one-sided error condition arises naturally in safety-critical protocol verification. We derive upper and lower bounds on the number of labelled examples sufficient and necessary for a consistent learner to achieve error at most ε with confidence at least 1 − δ. The upper bound, of order O(k² · n · log(1/δ) / ε), depends on k, the number of states of the minimal DFA, and n, the alphabet size. The lower bound construction uses a family of pairwise distinguishable automata to show that dependence on k is unavoidable. Connections to the VC dimension of DFA hypothesis classes are also established.

title: GInferLib: A Python Library for Grammatical Inference of Finite Automata
abstract: We present GInferLib, an open-source Python library providing implementations of seven grammatical inference algorithms for deterministic and nondeterministic finite automata, including RPNI, EDSM, L*, NL*, and three recent state-merging variants. The library offers a unified API for defining sample sets, running inference, inspecting intermediate hypothesis automata, and exporting results to standard formats including DOT, KISS, and a custom JSON schema. Benchmark results on 500 randomly generated regular languages show running times and accuracy figures consistent with published results in the original algorithm papers, validating the implementations. The library includes utilities for generating random DFAs, sampling strings, and computing standard metrics such as structural accuracy and Jaccard similarity between hypothesis and target. An interactive tutorial built with Jupyter notebooks is included in the repository. The library is intended primarily for researchers and graduate students.

title: Learning Automaton Models of IoT Device Behaviour from Encrypted Traffic Metadata
abstract: End-to-end encryption prevents direct inspection of protocol message content, but metadata features — packet sizes, inter-arrival times, and flow directions — remain observable. We investigate whether finite automaton models of IoT device communication behaviour can be inferred from such metadata alone. Twenty-two consumer IoT device types were placed in a controlled network testbed; traffic was captured over 72-hour periods under scripted usage scenarios. Message sequences were reconstructed from metadata clusters using a k-means procedure with k determined by a silhouette criterion. RPNI was applied to the resulting labelled sequences. The inferred automata reproduce 79–93% of transitions present in models derived from unencrypted reference captures of the same devices. Devices with highly regular behaviour (smart plugs, sensors) yielded better models than devices with irregular patterns (smart cameras during video streaming). The approach is evaluated on its suitability for network anomaly detection in encrypted environments.

title: Counterexample-Guided Refinement of Inferred Protocol Automata Using Fuzzing
abstract: An inferred automaton model of a protocol is only as good as the coverage of its training traces. We propose a refinement loop in which a fuzzer generates candidate inputs that drive the live protocol implementation into states not represented in the current hypothesis automaton, collecting new labelled counterexamples that are fed back to the inference algorithm. The process iterates until no new counterexamples are found within a time budget. Applied to four open-source implementations of a file-transfer protocol, the loop produces automata 23–41% larger than those obtained from passive inference alone, with a corresponding increase in structural accuracy of 8–17 percentage points when compared against a manually constructed ground-truth model. Total fuzzing budget across all experiments was 48 CPU-hours. We characterise which protocol features are most likely to be missed by passive inference and most reliably recovered by fuzzing.

title: Probably Approximately Correct Identification of Minimal DFAs Under Restricted Query Models
abstract: We examine a restricted active learning setting in which equivalence queries are replaced by statistical sampling: the learner draws random strings from a known distribution and observes their membership labels. This weakened query model is relevant when black-box testing of real systems cannot guarantee exact equivalence answers. We show that, for the class of languages accepted by DFAs of at most k states over an alphabet of size n, the number of samples required to achieve PAC identification with parameters (ε, δ) is Θ(k² log(k n / δ) / ε) under the uniform distribution over strings of bounded length. We also show that no consistent learner can do better than Ω(k log k / ε) samples in the worst case regardless of the string distribution. Experimental validation using GInferLib on synthetic targets confirms that empirical sample requirements track the theoretical bounds closely for k ≤ 25.

title: Preporučivanje podkast epizoda zasnovano na semantičkom ugrađivanju opisa: prototip i evaluacija sa korisnicima
abstract: Razvijen je prototip sistema za preporučivanje podkast epizoda koji koristi semantička ugrađivanja opisa epizoda za računanje srodnosti sadržaja. Sistem je implementiran nad korpusom od 14 200 epizoda na srpskom jeziku. Evaluacija je sprovedena sa 87 dobrovoljnih korisnika u kontrolisanom okruženju, pri čemu su korisnici ocenjivali relevantnost prvih pet preporuka na skali od 1 do 5. Prosečna ocena relevantnosti iznosila je 3,82, što je statistički značajno bolje od nasumičnog i popularnosnog osnivača (p < 0,01). Ispitana je i tzv. hladni start situacija — epizode bez dovoljno istorije slušanja — i pokazano je da semantički pristup zadržava prihvatljive performanse i u tom slučaju. Rad raspravlja o ograničenjima sistema vezanim za dijalektalne varijante i žargon.

title: Isolation and preliminary characterisation of exopolysaccharide-producing lactobacilli from Srem-region fresh cheese
abstract: Forty-eight lactic acid bacteria strains were isolated from artisanal fresh cheese produced in the Srem region of Vojvodina and screened for ropy colony morphology on modified MRS agar supplemented with sucrose. Twelve strains exhibited a mucoid phenotype. Crude exopolysaccharide (EPS) yields, determined gravimetrically after trichloroacetic acid precipitation, ranged from 38 to 214 mg/L in MRS broth at 30 °C over 24 h. The highest-producing strain, designated NS-FC-07, was identified as Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Monosaccharide composition analysed by GC-FID after acid hydrolysis and alditol acetate derivatisation showed a galactose-to-glucose ratio of approximately 2:1, consistent with a mixed hetero-EPS. Preliminary FTIR-ATR spectra confirmed polysaccharide-characteristic absorption bands at 1040–1080 cm⁻¹. These results provided a baseline for further structural and functional studies of dairy-origin EPS-producing lactobacilli in the region.

title: ¹H and ¹³C NMR structural analysis of the hetero-exopolysaccharide from Lactobacillus delbrueckii NS-FC-07
abstract: Purified exopolysaccharide from Lactobacillus delbrueckii NS-FC-07 was subjected to complete NMR structural analysis using 1D (¹H, ¹³C) and 2D (COSY, TOCSY, HSQC, HMBC) experiments recorded on a 400 MHz spectrometer at 70 °C in D₂O. Anomeric proton resonances at δ 4.52 and 4.91 ppm, combined with HMBC correlations, revealed a repeating unit composed of a β-D-galactopyranose-(1→3)-β-D-glucopyranose backbone with α-D-galactopyranose substituents at the C-6 of the glucose residue. The ratio of galactose to glucose was confirmed as 2:1, in agreement with methylation analysis performed by GC-MS. The structure closely resembles a type IIb EPS previously reported in thermophilic lactobacilli but differs in the proportion of branching. FTIR-ATR absorption at 891 cm⁻¹ confirmed the β-glycosidic linkage predominance. This constitutes the first full NMR structural report for an EPS from a Vojvodina dairy isolate.

title: Contribution of in situ EPS production to the rheological and textural properties of set-type yoghurt
abstract: Two yoghurt starter systems were compared in a controlled pilot-scale trial: a conventional non-ropy co-culture of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus, and the same co-culture supplemented with EPS-producing strain NS-FC-07. Fermentation was conducted at 42 °C to pH 4.60 in 200 mL polypropylene cups. Small-strain oscillatory rheometry (frequency sweeps 0.01–10 Hz) showed that storage modulus G′ at 1 Hz was 47% higher in the EPS-positive yoghurts (G′ = 312 Pa vs. 212 Pa). Texture profile analysis yielded a firmness increase of 38% and a springiness increase of 22%. Syneresis measured by centrifugation (500 × g, 10 min) was reduced from 18.2% to 11.6% (w/w whey expelled). No significant differences in titratable acidity or sensory scores were detected by a 12-member trained panel. Results demonstrate that in situ EPS production by NS-FC-07 meaningfully modifies gel network architecture without adversely affecting sensory acceptance.

title: FTIR-ATR spectroscopic differentiation of β-glucan and heteropolysaccharide EPS fractions from sourdough lactobacilli
abstract: A comparative FTIR-ATR spectroscopic study was conducted on purified EPS preparations from seven Lactobacillus strains isolated from rye and wheat sourdoughs. Spectra were recorded in the 4000–400 cm⁻¹ range at 4 cm⁻¹ resolution with 64 scans per sample using a diamond ATR crystal. Multivariate analysis (principal component analysis and hierarchical cluster analysis) of the fingerprint region (1200–800 cm⁻¹) resolved two main clusters corresponding to β-glucan-type and mixed hetero-EPS fractions. Key discriminant bands were identified at 1078 cm⁻¹ (C–O–C ring stretching), 1040 cm⁻¹ (C–O stretching) and 891 cm⁻¹ (anomeric β-configuration). The ratio of band intensities at 891 and 844 cm⁻¹ correlated with independently determined galactose-to-glucose ratios (R² = 0.88). This rapid FTIR-based approach allows classification of sourdough EPS types without prior acid hydrolysis, reducing analysis time from approximately 8 h to under 30 min.

title: In situ EPS formation and its influence on syneresis and water-holding capacity in stirred fermented milk with reduced fat content
abstract: Stirred fermented milk containing 1.5% fat was produced using a conventional starter and three experimental cultures differing in EPS-producing capacity (low: ~80 mg/L, medium: ~180 mg/L, high: ~310 mg/L in broth). Fermentation at 42 °C was terminated at pH 4.50, followed by cooling and gentle agitation. Water-holding capacity (WHC) was determined by centrifugation (3000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C) and expressed as a percentage of pellet weight. WHC increased monotonically with EPS level: 68.4%, 74.1%, and 81.3% for low, medium and high producers, respectively, compared to 63.2% for the control. Syneresis over 14 days at 4 °C was quantified gravimetrically; high-EPS samples showed 42% less whey separation than controls. Rheological flow curves fitted to the Herschel–Bulkley model indicated increasing consistency coefficient k from 1.8 to 4.3 Pa·sⁿ. Microstructural imaging by confocal laser scanning microscopy confirmed a denser, more continuous protein–EPS network in high-EPS samples.

title: Shelf-life extension of wheat-rye sourdough bread by EPS-producing Lactobacillus strains: crumb moisture, firmness and mould-free period
abstract: Wheat-rye (70:30) sourdough breads were prepared with and without EPS-producing Lactobacillus strains over a five-day accelerated storage trial at 22 °C and 65% relative humidity. Three EPS-producing strains (NS-SD-03, NS-SD-11, NS-SD-17) and a non-producing control culture were tested in a full factorial design with two baking replicates per treatment. Crumb moisture was measured by oven drying (105 °C, 4 h) at days 1, 3 and 5; EPS-containing breads retained 1.2–1.9 percentage points more moisture at day 5. TPA firmness at day 5 was 14–26% lower in EPS-producing variants. Mould-free period, assessed by visual inspection of vacuum-packaged samples stored at 25 °C, was extended by 3–4 days in EPS variants, attributable in part to lower water activity (aw 0.957 vs. 0.962) providing a marginal barrier to fungal growth. Sensory evaluation by a trained panel found no off-flavours attributable to increased fermentation activity.

title: Exopolysaccharide-enriched kefir: effect of EPS-producing adjunct strains on gel firmness, viscosity and post-acidification during refrigerated storage
abstract: Kefir was produced from pasteurised full-fat cow's milk using a traditional kefir grain culture supplemented with one of three EPS-producing adjunct lactobacilli strains (NS-FC-07, NS-FC-12, NS-FC-19) at inoculation levels of 10⁶ and 10⁷ CFU/mL. Fermentation proceeded at 20 °C for 24 h. Apparent viscosity (Brookfield, 60 rpm), firmness (penetrometry, 25 mm cylinder probe), pH and titratable acidity were monitored at days 1, 7, 14 and 21 of storage at 4 °C. NS-FC-07 at 10⁷ CFU/mL produced the greatest viscosity increase (+55% relative to control at day 1) and best maintained viscosity by day 21 (−12% vs. −31% in control). Post-acidification was slightly accelerated in EPS-positive kefirs (ΔpH = −0.18 vs. −0.12 over 21 days), which was considered acceptable within commercial specifications. EPS concentrations in the final product, quantified by anthrone assay, reached 142–198 mg/L across positive variants.

title: Optimisation of EPS yield from Levilactobacillus brevis NS-SD-11 in sourdough fermentation using response surface methodology
abstract: A central composite design (five levels of flour concentration: 10–30% w/w; inoculation rate: 10⁵–10⁸ CFU/g flour; fermentation time: 8–24 h; temperature: 25–37 °C) was applied to maximise EPS accumulation by Levilactobacillus brevis NS-SD-11 in a model wheat sourdough system. EPS was quantified by phenol–sulphuric acid assay after ethanol precipitation. The fitted quadratic model explained 91.3% of response variability (R² = 0.913, p < 0.001). Optimal conditions predicted by the model were: flour concentration 22% w/w, inoculation 10⁷ CFU/g flour, fermentation 18 h at 32 °C, yielding 0.74 g EPS per 100 g flour. Validation experiments gave 0.71 ± 0.04 g/100 g, confirming model adequacy. The primary significant factors were fermentation time and temperature (both p < 0.001), while inoculation level had a significant quadratic effect (p < 0.01). These optimised conditions were used as the baseline for subsequent bread-baking and rheological trials.

title: Biopolymer interactions between EPS and milk proteins in fermented dairy gels: a small-angle X-ray scattering and confocal microscopy study
abstract: Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) were used to examine the mesoscale network architecture of set-style fermented milk gels containing in situ produced EPS from NS-FC-07 at three concentration levels (0, 150 and 280 mg/kg estimated by anthrone assay). SAXS patterns collected at the ESRF BM29 beamline showed a systematic shift of the correlation peak from q* = 0.021 to 0.017 Å⁻¹ with increasing EPS level, indicating larger inter-aggregate distances of approximately 30 to 37 nm, consistent with EPS sterically repelling casein micelle clusters. CLSM images stained with rhodamine B (protein) and calcofluor white (polysaccharide) confirmed spatial co-distribution of EPS within the protein matrix without macro-phase separation. Fractal dimension, estimated from log-log plots of SAXS data in the Porod region (1.8 for control; 1.5 for high EPS), indicated a more open, less compact network, compatible with the observed improvements in water-holding capacity measured in parallel experiments.

title: Comparative characterisation of EPS from five Lactiplantibacillus plantarum strains isolated from spontaneously fermented Vojvodina sour turnip (mrsoljka)
abstract: Five Lactiplantibacillus plantarum strains isolated from spontaneously fermented sour turnip (mrsoljka) from three Vojvodina villages were characterised for EPS production in MRS broth at 30 °C and in a model brine system (1.5% NaCl, 2% sucrose, pH 5.5). EPS yields in broth ranged from 44 to 198 mg/L. All five EPS preparations contained glucose and galactose as dominant monomers, with one strain (NS-MT-04) producing an EPS rich in rhamnose (18 mol%). ¹H NMR spectra for all five EPS showed anomeric signals consistent with mixed α/β configurations. FTIR-ATR confirmed polysaccharide nature and revealed differences in carbonyl/ester band intensities (1730–1750 cm⁻¹) for NS-MT-04, suggesting partial acetylation. Emulsification activity, measured by the emulsification index E₂₄ assay using hexadecane, ranged from 31 to 58%. These strains represent previously undescribed EPS producers from Serbian fermented vegetable traditions and expand the regional strain collection.

title: Quantitative contribution of in situ EPS to crumb viscoelasticity in spelt sourdough bread assessed by dynamic mechanical analysis
abstract: Spelt sourdough breads were baked with and without EPS-producing Limosilactobacillus fermentum NS-SD-03 under identical processing conditions (dough yield 170, 18 h fermentation at 30 °C, final proofing 90 min at 37 °C, baking 220 °C, 30 min). Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) of crumb cylinders (25 mm × 10 mm) was performed in compression mode at frequencies of 0.1–10 Hz and temperatures of 5, 20 and 35 °C. At 20 °C and 1 Hz, storage modulus E′ of EPS-containing crumbs was 2.9 kPa vs. 4.1 kPa for control (p < 0.01), indicating a softer, less rigid crumb. The loss tangent tan δ was higher in EPS variants at all frequencies (0.28 vs. 0.21 at 1 Hz), indicating greater energy dissipation and a more viscoelastic character. EPS content in crumb, estimated after hot-water extraction and phenol–sulphuric acid assay, was 0.61 g per 100 g dry crumb. These data provide the first DMA-based quantitative assessment of EPS effects on spelt sourdough crumb mechanics.

title: Acrylamide mitigation in extruded snacks: a comparison of asparaginase treatment and calcium chloride addition
abstract: Two acrylamide-reducing strategies were evaluated in corn-wheat (60:40) extrudates: pre-treatment of the blend with fungal asparaginase (Aspergillus oryzae origin, 250 ASNU/g flour) for 30 min at 40 °C, and dry blending with CaCl₂ at 0.1 and 0.3 g/100 g. A co-rotating twin-screw extruder operated at 170 °C barrel temperature and 300 rpm was used throughout. Asparaginase treatment reduced asparagine content by 81% in raw flour and acrylamide in the final extrudate by 73%, from 480 µg/kg in the control to 130 µg/kg. CaCl₂ at 0.3 g/100 g reduced acrylamide by 34%, likely through pH modification. Combined treatment yielded a 79% reduction. Neither treatment significantly altered expansion ratio or breaking force. CIE L* values were slightly higher in asparaginase-treated samples, consistent with reduced melanoidin formation. Consumer panel evaluation (n = 42) found no significant difference in overall acceptability between the control and combined-treatment extrudates.

title: Dietary fibre enrichment of commercial gluten-free bread with pseudocereal bran fractions: consumer perception and sensory quality
abstract: Six prototype gluten-free bread formulations enriched with buckwheat, amaranth, or teff bran at 5 g and 10 g per 100 g flour were evaluated by a consumer panel of 87 participants recruited in Novi Sad, of whom 31 were self-reported gluten-intolerant. Evaluation included acceptability ratings for taste, colour, texture, and overall liking on a nine-point hedonic scale, and a check-all-that-apply (CATA) task with 24 descriptors. Bran addition at 10 g significantly reduced overall liking scores relative to the control (p < 0.01 for all three sources). At 5 g, teff bran was the least penalised, with no significant difference in overall liking from the control (p = 0.14). CATA analysis showed that 5 g teff bran bread was most frequently associated with 'earthy' and 'pleasant aftertaste', while amaranth bran at 10 g was associated with 'bitter' and 'dense crumb'. Gluten-intolerant consumers showed higher tolerance for the 10 g addition levels than non-intolerant consumers, suggesting differential acceptance thresholds. These findings offer practical guidance for commercially viable fibre enrichment levels.

title: Nucleation rate estimation in concentrated sucrose–trehalose binary systems by isothermal turbidity measurements
abstract: Binary solutions of sucrose and trehalose at total solute concentrations of 70 and 75 Brix with trehalose mole fractions of 0, 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 were held isothermally at temperatures between 20 and 35 °C in a purpose-built multi-well turbidity photometer monitoring 24 samples simultaneously at 850 nm. The method allowed determination of nucleation rate distributions from at least 60 replicates per condition. Nucleation rates decreased monotonically with increasing trehalose fraction, dropping by approximately one order of magnitude at xTre = 0.3 relative to pure sucrose at equivalent supersaturation and temperature. Activation energies derived from Arrhenius plots of nucleation rate were 88 ± 9 kJ mol⁻¹ for pure sucrose and 127 ± 12 kJ mol⁻¹ for the 0.3 mole fraction mixture. Viscosity measurements on the same solutions showed a 2.3-fold increase with trehalose substitution, and a diffusion-corrected nucleation model could account for roughly 60% of the observed rate reduction; the remainder is attributed to changes in solution structure. The study provides kinetic data relevant to sucrose-replacing formulations in confectionery.

title: Incidence and microbial aetiology of surgical site infections following elective colorectal resections at two tertiary hospitals in Vojvodina: a two-year prospective surveillance study
abstract: This prospective cohort study enrolled 418 patients undergoing elective colorectal resections at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina and the General Hospital Zrenjanin between January 2008 and December 2009. Wounds were classified according to the CDC NHSN definitions and followed for 30 days postoperatively. The overall SSI incidence was 14.6%, with superficial incisional infections accounting for 58% of cases. Escherichia coli and Enterococcus faecalis were the most frequently isolated pathogens, together representing 47% of positive cultures. Multivariate logistic regression identified diabetes mellitus (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3–4.4), ASA score ≥3 (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.2–3.7), and operative duration exceeding 180 minutes (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.0–3.2) as independent risk factors. Prophylactic antibiotic compliance was 71%, with deviation from protocol associated with a 1.9-fold increase in SSI risk. Findings provided a baseline for a subsequent regional surveillance programme.

title: Thirty-day postoperative SSI rates after elective open versus laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: This retrospective study compared 30-day SSI rates between open (n=284) and laparoscopic (n=631) elective cholecystectomy performed at three Vojvodina hospitals from 2009 to 2013. Routine postoperative follow-up records and readmission data were reviewed. The SSI rate was 6.7% for open procedures and 1.1% for laparoscopic procedures (p<0.001); after adjustment for age, BMI, ASA score, and surgeon experience, the odds ratio for SSI in the open group remained significant (OR 4.8, 95% CI 2.6–8.9). Organ-space infections accounted for two of the three most severe cases in the laparoscopic group, both related to bile duct injury. Median time to SSI diagnosis was 7 days (IQR 5–11). The study supports continued transition toward laparoscopic technique in eligible patients, while highlighting the distinct risk profile of organ-space infection even after minimally invasive surgery.

title: Seasonal variation in surgical site infection rates in gastrointestinal surgery: analysis of a regional surveillance database 2009–2015
abstract: Using data from a multi-hospital surveillance registry covering 3,842 elective gastrointestinal procedures performed between 2009 and 2015, this study examined whether SSI incidence exhibited statistically significant seasonal patterns. Monthly SSI rates were modelled using a negative binomial regression with calendar month, procedure category, and hospital type as covariates. A modest but statistically significant summer peak was identified (June–August adjusted IRR 1.28, 95% CI 1.09–1.51 compared to the December–February reference period). The effect was most pronounced for superficial incisional infections following large-bowel procedures. Ambient temperature and ward air-conditioning availability, assessed by a questionnaire survey, partially explained the seasonal pattern. No significant season–hospital type interaction was found. These findings are consistent with reports from comparable Central European climates and suggest that environmental temperature control may be a modifiable factor in SSI prevention.

title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus as a causative agent in postoperative wound infections at a tertiary surgical centre: five-year trend analysis
abstract: MRSA-attributed SSIs represent a disproportionately severe subset of postoperative wound infections. This study reviewed all culture-confirmed SSIs after elective gastrointestinal procedures at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina from 2012 to 2016 (n=187 SSI episodes from 2,614 procedures). MRSA was identified in 14 cases (7.5% of culture-confirmed SSIs), with an annual MRSA-SSI rate ranging from 0.3 to 0.7 per 100 procedures. Spa typing revealed two dominant clones, both consistent with hospital-acquired lineages. Patients with MRSA-attributed SSIs had significantly longer median hospital stays (22 vs. 11 days, p<0.001) and higher rates of secondary complications. A temporal decline in MRSA SSI proportion was observed following introduction of enhanced contact precautions in 2014. This trend analysis provides local reference data and supports ongoing investment in active MRSA surveillance.

title: Impact of preoperative nutritional screening on SSI outcomes in elective colorectal surgery: a prospective observational study
abstract: Malnutrition is an established risk factor for surgical complications, yet systematic nutritional screening before elective colorectal surgery is inconsistently applied in Serbian hospitals. This prospective study enrolled 203 patients at two hospitals in Vojvodina (2016–2018) and applied the Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS-2002) tool preoperatively. Patients scoring NRS ≥3 (38.4%) had a significantly higher 30-day SSI rate (22.1% vs. 10.4%, p=0.016) and longer median postoperative stay (14 vs. 9 days, p<0.001). After adjustment for age, procedure type, and ASA score, NRS ≥3 remained an independent predictor of SSI (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.1–4.7). Preoperative nutritional intervention was provided for only 29% of at-risk patients, indicating a gap between screening and action. The results support integrating a formal nutrition team referral pathway into preoperative colorectal surgical protocols.

title: Concordance between active inpatient and telephone-based 30-day postdischarge SSI surveillance in elective upper gastrointestinal surgery
abstract: Postdischarge surveillance is essential for capturing SSIs that manifest after early hospital discharge, but structured comparison of methods has rarely been undertaken in regional Balkan settings. Over 14 months in 2018–2019, 316 patients who underwent elective upper gastrointestinal procedures at two hospitals were monitored both by standardised daily wound assessment during admission and by structured telephone interview at day 21 and day 30 post-surgery. The inpatient method detected 24 SSIs (7.6%); telephone follow-up identified an additional 11 events (cumulative rate 11.1%). Sensitivity of inpatient-only surveillance relative to combined surveillance was 68.6%. Patient-reported outcomes via telephone agreed with subsequent clinical assessment in 89% of cases where reassessment was possible. Structured postdischarge telephone surveillance added minimal cost and substantially improved SSI detection, suggesting it is feasible for routine adoption in regional hospital settings.

title: Antibiotic-resistant Gram-negative pathogens in SSIs following elective colorectal surgery in Vojvodina: a multicentre cross-sectional microbiological analysis
abstract: Carbapenem-resistant and ESBL-producing Gram-negative organisms are an increasing concern in surgical wards across Southeast Europe. This cross-sectional microbiological study analysed all bacterial isolates from culture-confirmed SSIs following elective colorectal procedures at four Vojvodina hospitals between 2019 and 2022 (n=94 culture-confirmed SSI episodes). ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae were detected in 31.9% of Gram-negative isolates; carbapenem resistance was found in 4.3%. Klebsiella pneumoniae with ESBL phenotype was the dominant resistant organism (18 isolates). Resistance rates were higher at the two hospitals with a higher proportion of secondary-to-tertiary patient transfers. Whole-genome sequencing on a convenience subsample (n=22) revealed clonal spread of one K. pneumoniae sequence type. The findings underline the need for enhanced antimicrobial stewardship and cross-hospital infection control communication in elective surgical settings in the region.

title: Development and internal validation of a preoperative SSI risk score for elective gastrointestinal procedures in regional hospitals of Vojvodina
abstract: Existing generic SSI risk scores were developed on data from Western European or North American centres and may not translate well to regional Serbian hospital settings. This study used retrospective data on 2,108 elective gastrointestinal procedures from three Vojvodina hospitals (2015–2022) to develop a locally calibrated risk score. Candidate variables included in multivariate logistic regression were selected by clinical consensus and backward elimination. Six variables were retained in the final model: age >65, BMI >30, diabetes, ASA score ≥3, operative duration >150 minutes, and open surgical approach. The score showed good discrimination (c-statistic 0.73) and calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow p=0.41) in internal cross-validation. Score categories (low, moderate, high) corresponded to observed SSI rates of 3.1%, 9.8%, and 21.4% respectively. External validation in prospective data is planned as a next step.
venue: Surgical Infections

title: Fibroblast contractile activity in hernia scar explants measured by collagen gel contraction assay
abstract: Persistent myofibroblast activation in fascial scar tissue may impair mechanical remodelling and predispose to hernia recurrence. Fibroblasts were isolated from fascial biopsies of 18 patients: 6 controls (laparotomy closure with no hernia), 6 primary incisional hernia, and 6 recurrent incisional hernia. Cells were embedded in collagen gels at 2 × 10⁵ cells/mL and gel area was measured at 24, 48, and 72 hours. Mean gel contraction at 72 hours was 38% in controls, 52% in primary hernia, and 71% in recurrent hernia fibroblasts. Alpha-smooth muscle actin expression, quantified by western blot, correlated strongly with gel contraction rates (r = 0.84). TGF-β1 conditioned medium increased contraction in all groups; anti-TGF-β1 antibody partially reversed the effect in recurrent hernia cells. These results support myofibroblast hyperactivation as a feature of the recurrent hernia microenvironment.

title: Patient-reported outcomes at two years after open sublay repair: correlation with recurrence status and scar elasticity
abstract: Patient-centred evaluation of hernia repair outcomes is increasingly required alongside clinical endpoints. We prospectively enrolled 94 patients undergoing open sublay mesh repair and administered the Carolinas Comfort Scale and a pain numeric rating scale at 6, 12, and 24 months. Abdominal scar elasticity was measured at 12 months by cutaneous elastometry using a suction device. Recurrence occurred in 9 patients (9.6%) by 24 months. Recurrent patients reported significantly worse Carolinas Comfort Scale scores at 24 months (mean 22.4 ± 7.1 vs. 8.3 ± 5.2, p < 0.001). Scar elasticity was lower in recurrent cases at 12 months (mean 0.54 ± 0.09 vs. 0.71 ± 0.12, p = 0.002). A scar elasticity value below 0.60 at 12 months predicted subsequent recurrence with a sensitivity of 78% and specificity of 71%. These data suggest that cutaneous elastometry may provide an early functional signal of impending recurrence.

title: Central sensitisation inventory scores in patients with and without chronic pain after inguinal hernia repair: a case-control analysis
abstract: The Central Sensitisation Inventory (CSI) has been validated as a self-report measure of symptoms associated with central sensitisation syndromes. This case-control study compared CSI scores in 52 patients with confirmed chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP, defined as NRS ≥3 at six or more months post-surgery) and 52 age- and sex-matched controls who underwent the same procedure without persistent pain. CSI total score was significantly higher in the CPIP group (mean 38.4 ± 11.2 vs 21.7 ± 9.4, p < 0.001). Subscale analysis revealed that somatic complaints and headache-related items drove the group difference. Multivariable logistic regression identified CSI score (OR per 5-point increase: 1.67, 95% CI 1.28–2.18) and preoperative analgesic use (OR 3.14, 95% CI 1.22–8.07) as independent predictors of CPIP. The results support screening for central sensitisation features before elective hernia repair.
