title: Chronic post-surgical pain after inguinal hernia repair: pathophysiology and clinical assessment
abstract: Chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP) is one of the most studied examples of procedure-specific persistent pain and provides a useful model for understanding the transition from acute to chronic pain following soft-tissue and mesh-based surgery. This chapter reviews the anatomical basis of inguinal innervation, the operative factors that may injure or entrap the ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric, and genitofemoral nerves, and the evidence for inflammatory and neuropathic mechanisms underlying CPIP. Clinical assessment approaches are discussed, including validated questionnaires, QST protocols, and the role of diagnostic nerve blocks. The chapter evaluates current evidence on risk stratification and briefly addresses management options including targeted physiotherapy, pharmacotherapy, and surgical neurectomy. Intended for surgeons and anaesthesiologists managing patients in the perioperative and postoperative periods.

title: Core temperature responses during a simulated 50 km trail run in hot-humid laboratory conditions: a pilot study
abstract: This pilot study examined rectal temperature trajectories in twelve trained male recreational runners completing a simulated 50 km treadmill protocol under controlled hot-humid conditions (32 °C, 75% relative humidity). Rectal temperature was recorded every 10 minutes alongside heart rate and perceived exertion. Mean peak rectal temperature reached 38.9 ± 0.4 °C, with four participants briefly exceeding 39.5 °C during the final 10 km segment. No significant difference in peak temperature was observed between runners consuming ad libitum water versus a fixed 500 mL·h⁻¹ protocol. Pre-to-post body mass loss averaged 1.8 ± 0.6%. The results indicated that rectal temperature plateaued for most participants rather than rising continuously, suggesting effective though variable self-regulation. These preliminary findings informed subsequent field-based monitoring designs for multi-stage ultra events held in the region.

title: Sweat sodium concentration variability in recreational ultra-trail runners: field measurements on the Fruška Gora 60 km race
abstract: Sweat sodium concentration ([Na⁺]sw) is highly individual and its field measurement in ultra-endurance events remains methodologically challenging. This study recruited 34 recreational runners (27 male, 7 female) competing in a 60 km trail race on Fruška Gora during August, with ambient temperatures ranging from 24 to 31 °C and relative humidity between 62 and 78%. Absorbent Macroduct patches were applied to the forearm before the start, collected at the 30 km checkpoint, and analysed for sodium using ion chromatography. [Na⁺]sw ranged from 21 to 78 mmol·L⁻¹ (mean 48 ± 16 mmol·L⁻¹), with a coefficient of variation of 33% across participants. Runners in the highest sodium-loss quartile reported more frequent muscle cramping episodes. Whole-body sweat rate estimated from body mass change and fluid intake averaged 1.12 ± 0.31 L·h⁻¹. The wide interindividual variability observed supports the case for personalised hydration and sodium replacement strategies over generic race-day guidance.

title: Hydration status markers before and after a 100 km mountain ultra-marathon in Serbia: urine osmolality and plasma osmolality compared
abstract: Accurate pre-race hydration assessment is important for injury prevention in ultra-endurance events. This study compared urine osmolality (Uosm) and plasma osmolality (Posm) as hydration markers in 22 athletes (18 male, 4 female) the morning before and within 30 minutes after completion of a 100 km mountain ultra-marathon held in the Western Morava valley region. Mean pre-race Uosm was 712 ± 198 mOsm·kg⁻¹, with 9 of 22 runners classified as hypohydrated (Uosm > 700 mOsm·kg⁻¹). Post-race Posm averaged 294 ± 6 mOsm·kg⁻¹, representing a non-significant increase from pre-race values of 289 ± 5 mOsm·kg⁻¹. Two participants met biochemical criteria for exercise-associated hyponatraemia (serum [Na⁺] < 135 mmol·L⁻¹), both of whom had consumed hypotonic fluids at a rate exceeding estimated sweat losses. The correlation between Uosm and Posm was moderate (r = 0.54), reinforcing that single-void urine colour or osmolality alone is insufficient for pre-race hydration clearance.

title: Estimating whole-body sweat rate in multi-stage trail running: comparison of gravimetric and deuterium-dilution methods
abstract: Whole-body sweat rate estimation using the gravimetric method (body mass change corrected for fluid intake and urine output) is practical but subject to error from respiratory water loss and metabolic water production. This study compared gravimetric estimates to a deuterium-oxide dilution method for total body water change across a three-stage trail running event (total distance 120 km over three days) held in the Kopaonik region in late June. Seventeen male runners completed all stages and all sampling procedures. Mean sweat rate over Stage 1 (42 km, 28 °C mean) was 1.08 L·h⁻¹ by gravimetry versus 0.97 L·h⁻¹ by deuterium dilution, a difference of 10.2% (limits of agreement: −0.31 to +0.53 L·h⁻¹). Agreement was closer on Stage 3 when temperatures were lower (22 °C). The study concludes that gravimetric methods systematically overestimate sweat rate by 7–13% under warm continental summer conditions, an important correction factor for hydration prescription.

title: Skin temperature distribution in trail runners under continental humid conditions: an infrared thermography approach
abstract: Infrared thermography allows non-contact assessment of skin temperature distribution and may complement invasive core temperature measurement in field settings. This observational study applied thermographic imaging to 28 trail runners (24 male, 4 female) at the start, 25 km checkpoint, and finish of a 50 km race in Vojvodina during July (ambient temperature 33 °C, relative humidity 68%). Standardised anterior and posterior images were captured using a mid-range thermal camera with ±0.05 °C sensitivity. Mean forehead skin temperature increased from 33.4 ± 0.8 °C at the start to 36.1 ± 0.9 °C at the 25 km point, then declined to 35.3 ± 1.1 °C at the finish, likely reflecting adaptive vasomotor responses. Significant left-right asymmetry in calf skin temperature was found in 11 runners and was associated with self-reported unilateral lower-limb fatigue. Thermography proved feasible in outdoor race conditions but image acquisition required strict 5-minute rest standardisation to reduce artefacts from direct solar radiation.

title: Sodium supplementation during a 100 km ultra-trail race and its effect on serum sodium concentration and perceived cramp frequency
abstract: Exercise-associated muscle cramping and hyponatraemia are distinct but clinically relevant concerns in ultra-trail running. This randomised controlled trial assigned 36 runners (18 per group) completing a 100 km race in the Southern Banat region either to a structured sodium supplementation protocol (1000 mg Na⁺ per hour from 30 km onward) or a placebo control (identically packaged maltodextrin capsules). Serum sodium concentration measured at 50 km and post-race was the primary outcome. The supplementation group maintained serum [Na⁺] at 138 ± 3 mmol·L⁻¹ post-race compared to 136 ± 4 mmol·L⁻¹ in controls (p = 0.08); no clinical hyponatraemia cases occurred. Cramping episodes self-reported on a validated log were lower in the supplementation group (mean 1.4 vs 2.9 events; p = 0.03). Gastrointestinal comfort scores did not differ between groups. The sodium dose used appeared tolerable and was associated with reduced cramping frequency, though the mechanistic link between sodium status and cramping remains inconclusive.

title: Wearable biosensor accuracy for continuous sweat sodium estimation in trail running: a laboratory and field comparison
abstract: Consumer-grade wearable sweat sensors capable of continuous electrochemical sodium estimation have appeared in recent years but their accuracy under real exercise conditions has not been systematically tested in ultra-endurance contexts. This study evaluated one commercially available wrist-worn biosensor platform against Macroduct patch ion chromatography in 20 trained runners during a 3-hour treadmill run at 70% VO₂max under controlled conditions (30 °C, 65% RH) and subsequently during a 40 km field trail run. In laboratory conditions, mean absolute error of the biosensor for [Na⁺]sw was 9.2 mmol·L⁻¹ (range 1–22 mmol·L⁻¹), with larger errors at high sweat rates (> 1.2 L·h⁻¹). Field errors were higher (mean 13.7 mmol·L⁻¹), partly attributed to sensor displacement and sun exposure. Bland-Altman analysis revealed a proportional bias, with the sensor underestimating high sodium concentrations. The authors conclude that current consumer biosensor accuracy is insufficient for individual sodium replacement prescriptions without further calibration.

title: Heat acclimatisation protocols for amateur ultra-trail runners preparing for summer continental races: a review of evidence and practical considerations
abstract: Amateur ultra-trail runners competing in continental European summer conditions rarely follow structured heat acclimatisation protocols despite evidence of their thermoregulatory benefit. This review synthesises data from 24 controlled acclimatisation studies published between 2005 and 2025, with particular attention to protocols feasible for time-limited recreational athletes (5–10 days, 60–90 minutes daily). Passive heat exposure via repeated hot-water immersion and low-intensity exercise in heated environments both appear effective in increasing plasma volume by 4–8% and reducing resting core temperature by 0.2–0.4 °C. Evidence specific to humid continental climates, as opposed to dry heat, is limited: only 6 of 24 studies used relative humidity above 60%. The review identifies sweat rate increases of 8–18% as a consistent acclimatisation outcome, but sodium concentration in sweat decreases by a comparable proportion, meaning net sodium loss per bout remains roughly stable. Practical guidance is offered for coaches and athletes preparing for Fruška Gora-region summer races.

title: Relationship between passive drag index and inter-limb coordination in masters front crawl swimmers
abstract: This study examined whether passive drag force, normalised to body surface area (drag index), relates to the quality of inter-limb coordination in masters swimmers. Forty-one masters swimmers (38–71 years; 22 women, 19 men) completed both a passive tow test at 1.3 m/s and a 25-metre front crawl trial at race pace on the same day. Passive drag index ranged from 18.4 to 41.7 N/m². Index of Coordination was computed from underwater footage. Pearson correlation between drag index and IdC was −0.47 (p = 0.002), indicating that higher drag was associated with more pronounced catch-up coordination patterns. A moderation analysis showed that age strengthened this relationship (interaction term β = −0.31, p = 0.018). Swimmers with high drag indices also demonstrated shorter stroke length (r = −0.52, p < 0.001). The results suggest that hydrodynamic and coordinative inefficiencies co-occur and may share common underlying factors such as altered body position, reduced flexibility, or diminished proprioceptive feedback.

title: Post-anthesis nitrogen remobilisation from leaves and stalk internodes in two maize hybrids grown under contrasting nitrogen supply
abstract: Nitrogen remobilisation from vegetative organs to the grain was quantified in two commercial maize hybrids (ZP 434 and a local inbred-derived hybrid) grown under 60 and 180 kg N ha⁻¹ at the Rimski Šančevi field station over two growing seasons (2003–2004). Pulse-labelling with 15N-ammonium nitrate at anthesis allowed tracking of label redistribution at 14-day intervals until physiological maturity. Under low N, approximately 68% of final grain N originated from remobilised vegetative stores, compared with 44% under high N. Leaf nitrogen concentration declined more steeply in the low-N treatment from 35 days after anthesis onward. Stalk internode contributions were smaller in both treatments but more variable across genotypes. The study provides baseline quantitative data for dissecting genotypic variation in remobilisation capacity and highlights that source-organ identity shifts with nitrogen availability. Methods, raw label recovery values, and soil nitrogen measurements at three depths are reported in full.
venue: Journal of Cereal Science and Agronomy

title: Glutamine synthetase isoform activity in senescing maize leaves as a predictor of nitrogen remobilisation efficiency
abstract: Glutamine synthetase (GS) catalyses the primary assimilation of ammonium released during protein breakdown in senescing tissues. This study measured GS1 and GS2 isoform activities in blade tissue of the ear leaf and two leaves above the ear at 10-day intervals from anthesis to black-layer formation in six maize genotypes representing a range of stay-green phenotypes. Field trials were conducted at Rimski Šančevi in 2005 and 2006 under 120 kg N ha⁻¹. GS1 activity in the ear leaf at 20 days after anthesis explained 61% of genotypic variance in leaf-to-grain N remobilisation efficiency (r² = 0.61, P < 0.001). GS2 activity declined sharply after anthesis in all genotypes and showed no significant predictive relationship. Protein, chlorophyll, and free amino acid contents were measured in parallel. Results suggest that GS1 assay at a single early post-anthesis time point could serve as a biochemical selection criterion for improved nitrogen remobilisation.

title: Relationship between nitrogen uptake efficiency and remobilisation efficiency across a panel of Zea mays L. inbred lines
abstract: Nitrogen use efficiency can be decomposed into uptake efficiency (NUpE) and utilisation efficiency (NUtE), the latter further partitioned into remobilisation from vegetative organs (NRE) and post-anthesis uptake. A panel of 24 maize inbred lines from Central European breeding programmes was evaluated at two nitrogen levels (40 and 160 kg N ha⁻¹) at two locations in Vojvodina over 2007 and 2008. Above-ground biomass N at anthesis, at maturity, and in the grain was measured by Kjeldahl digestion. NUpE and NRE showed a negative correlation (r = −0.43, P < 0.05) across inbreds under low N, indicating that lines with high uptake capacity tended to rely less on remobilisation. No significant correlation was found under high N. Grain yield was more closely associated with NUpE than NRE in both environments. The data suggest that simultaneous improvement of both components may require explicit selection against the apparent compensatory relationship observed here.

title: Stay-green duration and its relationship with post-anthesis nitrogen remobilisation in maize under field conditions in Vojvodina
abstract: Functional stay-green—prolonged chlorophyll retention without corresponding photosynthetic activity—has been proposed as a phenotype that impairs nitrogen remobilisation to the grain. This study phenotyped 18 elite hybrids from Serbian and Hungarian breeding programmes for canopy greenness (SPAD readings), chlorophyll fluorescence (Fv/Fm), and leaf N concentration at weekly intervals from silking to black layer in field trials at two locations in 2009. Hybrids were classified as cosmetic, functional, or partial stay-green based on established criteria. Functional stay-green hybrids showed 12–18% lower grain N concentration compared with senescing types at equivalent yields, consistent with impaired protein catabolism. Cosmetic stay-green lines did not differ significantly from senescing lines in grain N. SPAD decline rate from 28 to 42 days after silking was the single greenness measure most tightly linked to grain N accumulation dynamics. Implications for hybrid selection under nitrogen-limited conditions are discussed.

title: Variation in proteolytic enzyme activity during leaf senescence and its contribution to nitrogen export in maize
abstract: Remobilisation of leaf nitrogen requires proteolysis of chloroplastic proteins, principally Rubisco. Cysteine protease, serine protease, and metalloprotease activities were assayed in ear-leaf extracts at five time points from anthesis to late senescence in 12 maize genotypes grown under 80 kg N ha⁻¹ at Rimski Šančevi in 2010. Total protease activity at 28 days after anthesis accounted for 54% of the genotypic variance in total leaf N export measured by 15N dilution. Cysteine proteases showed the strongest individual association (r² = 0.49). Activity of chloroplast-localised serine protease (Deg1-type) peaked earlier and was less variable across genotypes. Genotypes with high early cysteine protease induction also showed more rapid decline in Rubisco content. Correlations among enzyme activities and SPAD decline are reported for all genotype–time-point combinations. These data support targeting protease gene expression as a route to manipulate remobilisation capacity.

title: QTL mapping for nitrogen remobilisation efficiency in a maize RIL population under low and high nitrogen
abstract: A recombinant inbred line (RIL) population of 186 lines derived from a cross between a nitrogen-efficient inbred (L-47) and a nitrogen-responsive hybrid parent was genotyped with 312 SNP markers and phenotyped for nitrogen remobilisation efficiency (NRE), grain nitrogen concentration, and grain yield under 40 and 160 kg N ha⁻¹ at Rimski Šančevi across 2012 and 2013. Composite interval mapping identified six QTL for NRE under low N (explaining 38% of phenotypic variance collectively), three of which co-localised with QTL for leaf chlorophyll decline rate. Under high N, only two QTL were detected (combined R² = 14%). A QTL on chromosome 5 near the genomic region containing a characterised GS1 paralogue was significant in both environments. Marker–trait associations for yield, ear leaf N at anthesis, and stalk N at maturity are reported. The chromosome 5 region is proposed as a candidate interval for marker-assisted improvement of NRE.

title: Nitrogen fertilisation history affects the capacity for post-anthesis remobilisation in the subsequent crop generation: a three-year field experiment
abstract: Whether multi-year nitrogen management history alters intrinsic remobilisation capacity in maize was tested in a 2011–2014 field experiment at two sites. Continuous low N (40 kg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹) and continuous high N (160 kg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹) treatments were applied to plots planted with the same hybrid across all years. In year four, all plots received an intermediate rate (100 kg ha⁻¹) and were sampled for 15N-labelled N redistribution. No significant difference in NRE was detected between history treatments (mean NRE 61% vs. 63%, P = 0.31), indicating that the capacity is predominantly genetically fixed rather than conditioned by prior management. Soil organic nitrogen, microbial biomass N, and grain protein content were monitored across all years. The study addresses a practical question for farmers considering switching nitrogen management strategies mid-rotation.

title: Transcriptome profiling of ear leaf senescence in a high-NRE and low-NRE maize inbred pair
abstract: RNA-seq was used to compare gene expression in ear leaves of two near-isogenic lines differing at the chromosome 5 QTL region associated with nitrogen remobilisation efficiency, sampled at anthesis and at 14, 28, and 42 days post-anthesis under 60 kg N ha⁻¹. A total of 1,847 genes showed differential expression between lines at one or more time points (FDR < 0.05). Genes encoding SAG12-type cysteine proteases, GS1 paralogues, and several autophagy-related (ATG) genes were upregulated earlier in the high-NRE line. Downregulation of photosystem II subunit genes proceeded more slowly in the low-NRE line, consistent with a cosmetic stay-green signature. Gene ontology enrichment confirmed overrepresentation of protein catabolism and amino acid transport terms in the high-NRE contrast. Raw reads are deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive. Candidate gene targets for functional validation are identified.

title: Assessing the within-field spatial variability of maize nitrogen remobilisation efficiency using proximal canopy sensing
abstract: High-throughput phenotyping of nitrogen remobilisation in field conditions is constrained by the labour intensity of isotope tracing. This study evaluated whether proximal canopy reflectance indices could serve as indirect estimators of NRE in a 3-ha commercial field in Vojvodina seeded with a single hybrid. A hyperspectral camera mounted on a tractor boom collected canopy reflectance at 10-nm intervals (450–900 nm) at anthesis and at 21 and 42 days after anthesis across 312 sampling points. Destructive biomass and N samples were collected at 48 points at maturity. NDRE and the ratio of reflectance at 750 and 550 nm explained 47% and 51% of variance in leaf N export, respectively. A partial least squares regression model using the full spectral range improved prediction to R² = 0.68. The study demonstrates that within-field NRE variation is tractable with commercial hyperspectral platforms but prediction accuracy is insufficient for precision-management recommendations without further calibration.

title: GWAS of nitrogen remobilisation efficiency in a diverse maize association panel adapted to South-East European growing conditions
abstract: A genome-wide association study was conducted on 214 maize accessions representing elite, landrace, and exotic germplasm adapted to Balkan and Central European conditions. Accessions were grown under 40 and 140 kg N ha⁻¹ at three locations (Novi Sad, Osijek, and Szarvas) in 2019 and 2020. Nitrogen remobilisation efficiency was estimated from paired total above-ground N at anthesis and grain N at maturity measurements. GWAS identified 11 marker–trait associations at P < 1×10⁻⁶ after mixed-model correction for population structure. Three associations mapped within 50 kb of annotated GS1 or asparagine synthetase genes. A cluster of four associations on chromosome 8 co-located with a previously reported stay-green locus. Effect sizes were modest (1.8–4.3% of phenotypic variance per SNP). Combined SNP score explained 27% of genotypic variance in NRE under low N. Results are discussed in the context of the broader maize GWAS literature on senescence traits.

title: Carbon-to-nitrogen ratio dynamics in senescing maize leaves: consequences for remobilisation stoichiometry across nitrogen input levels
abstract: Leaf C:N ratio at the onset and during senescence constrains the quantity of nitrogen that can be mobilised per unit carbon respired. This study measured C and N content at weekly intervals in ear leaves of eight maize hybrids under 40, 90, and 160 kg N ha⁻¹ at Rimski Šančevi in 2021 and 2022. Initial leaf C:N at anthesis ranged from 9.2 to 15.4 across treatments and genotypes. Net N export per leaf dry weight loss was linearly related to initial leaf N concentration (r = 0.82, P < 0.001) and was independent of genotype when initial leaf N was included as a covariate. Under the lowest N rate, carbon remobilisation from leaves was also substantial (mean 18% of anthesis leaf C exported), complicating the interpretation of leaf N measurements alone as a proxy for senescence progress. The data challenge the common assumption that remobilisation efficiency is a fixed genotypic trait independent of leaf nitrogen status at anthesis.

title: Functional characterisation of ZmGS1-5, a maize glutamine synthetase paralogue expressed preferentially in senescing leaves under nitrogen limitation
abstract: The maize genome encodes five cytosolic GS1 paralogues with distinct expression domains. ZmGS1-5 was identified in earlier transcriptome work as upregulated in senescing ear leaves of high-NRE near-isogenic lines. CRISPR-Cas9 knockout lines in the B73 background were generated in collaboration with IPK Gatersleben and grown under 40 and 140 kg N ha⁻¹ at Rimski Šančevi in 2023. Knockout plants showed a 22% reduction in total leaf N export and a parallel accumulation of free ammonium in ear leaf tissue at 28 days after anthesis. Grain N concentration was reduced by 15% under low N but only 6% under high N in knockout lines compared with wild type. Complementation with the native promoter–ZmGS1-5 construct restored wild-type remobilisation. These results confirm a non-redundant role of ZmGS1-5 in senescence-associated nitrogen reassimilation and establish it as a specific functional determinant of NRE under nitrogen-limited conditions.

title: Multi-environment evaluation of nitrogen remobilisation efficiency as a target trait for improving nitrogen use efficiency in Vojvodina maize production
abstract: Nitrogen remobilisation efficiency was measured across 12 commercial maize hybrids currently marketed in Serbia at four nitrogen rates (0, 60, 120, 180 kg N ha⁻¹) and three locations in Vojvodina (Rimski Šančevi, Bačka Topola, Kikinda) over 2023 and 2024. Mixed-model analysis showed significant genotype × nitrogen rate × location interactions for NRE. Mean NRE across the trial set was 63% at 60 kg N ha⁻¹ and 46% at 180 kg N ha⁻¹. Genetic variance for NRE was 2.3-fold greater under low N than high N. Grain yield gains from improved NRE were estimated by simulation to reach 4–7% under 60 kg N ha⁻¹ scenarios assuming current genetic variance. Under high N, simulated gains were less than 2% and not economically meaningful given current fertiliser prices. Results support prioritising NRE as a selection criterion primarily for low-input production systems, which occupy roughly 30% of maize area in Vojvodina. Full dataset is deposited in the FAOSTAT-compatible Serbian Crop Phenotyping Repository.

title: Amaranthus tuberculatus occurrence and competitive dynamics in soybean: first systematic field assessment in Serbia
abstract: Amaranthus tuberculatus (waterhemp) was first recorded in Vojvodina in isolated patches in 2019. Systematic surveys across 34 soybean fields in 2023 and 2024 documented infestation frequency, density, and competitive impact. The weed was detected in 11 of 34 fields (32%), with densities up to 4.7 plants m⁻² in the heaviest-infested field. Competition experiments at three imposed densities (0.5, 2, and 5 plants m⁻²) were established in 2024; preliminary yield-loss data indicate i values of approximately 12% per plant m⁻², higher than previously recorded for Amaranthus retroflexus under local conditions. Post-emergence efficacy of four commonly registered herbicide active ingredients was tested in small plots; all treatments showed control efficacy below 70% at label rates for A. tuberculatus compared with 88–94% for A. retroflexus, suggesting early signs of reduced sensitivity. Continued monitoring and resistance screening are warranted.

title: Radiation interception and yield land equivalent ratio in a carrot–fennel strip intercrop across a north–south and east–west row orientation comparison
abstract: Row orientation (north–south versus east–west) was crossed with strip width (1.0 and 2.0 m) in a two-season experiment with carrot and fennel. PAR interception was measured with AccuPAR line ceptometers at solar noon and at two-hour intervals on clear days at 12, 35, 62, and 85 days after sowing. North–south orientation increased daily total intercepted PAR by the carrot component by 9 % relative to east–west orientation in the 1.0 m strip treatment, with no significant difference in the 2.0 m treatment. Land equivalent ratio calculated from marketable yield was 1.18 in north–south 1.0 m, 1.12 in east–west 1.0 m, 1.09 in north–south 2.0 m, and 1.06 in east–west 2.0 m arrangements. Orientation effects on foliar disease incidence were not significant, but humidity asymmetry across the canopy east–west cross-section was detectable in morning readings.

title: Advertising columns as social mirrors: consumer culture in Novi Sad daily newspapers, 1920–1930
abstract: This study examines 4,312 commercial advertisements published in three Novi Sad daily newspapers between 1920 and 1930, drawing on digitised holdings from the Matica srpska Library periodicals collection. Advertisements were coded across twelve product categories using a purpose-built scheme, and frequency distributions were compared decade-internally by year to detect shifts in consumer offer and visual presentation. Results show that food and household goods dominated advertising space throughout the period, accounting for 58% of all insertions, while pharmaceutical and cosmetic advertisements grew from 6% to 14% between 1924 and 1930. Changes in advertisement size and the gradual introduction of illustrated inserts are mapped against known circulation figures. The article argues that the advertising columns of regional dailies constitute an underused but systematically traceable index of middle-class purchasing behaviour in the interwar provincial city, complementing tax and census records.

title: Death notices and social stratification: a content-analytic reading of obituary pages in Vojvodina weeklies, 1919–1935
abstract: Obituary pages in four Vojvodina weekly newspapers are analysed as structured social texts that encode occupational identity, religious affiliation, and family network size. A corpus of 2,089 obituary notices was compiled from archival microfilm runs held at the Archives of Vojvodina in Novi Sad. Each notice was coded for occupational descriptor, number of mourners listed, presence of honorary titles, and religious formulae. Cluster analysis grouped notices into five socio-occupational profiles, revealing that merchant and artisan families published disproportionately elaborate notices relative to their share in census data, while agricultural households were systematically underrepresented. The study cross-references findings with civil registry data from three municipalities to test the representativeness of press coverage. The article concludes that obituary columns, though formulaic, preserve occupational and kinship information unavailable in standard demographic sources for this region and period.

title: Weather, harvest, and rural anxiety: agricultural reporting in the Bačka regional press between the wars
abstract: Agricultural reporting columns published in twelve issues per year across six Bačka regional newspapers from 1921 to 1938 were identified, transcribed, and subjected to thematic coding. The resulting dataset of 1,140 articles was analysed for the frequency and framing of weather events, harvest expectations, and market prices. Qualitative close reading of a random subsample of 200 articles examined the rhetorical construction of rural vulnerability and state agricultural policy. Quantitative results show that drought coverage peaked in 1924, 1928, and 1935, broadly consistent with meteorological records from the Hydrometeorological Institute archive. Framing analysis identifies a recurrent tension between optimistic official extension messaging and cautionary editorials. The study contributes to a broader project of using regional press as a distributed archive of agrarian experience across the new Yugoslav state.

title: Cataloguing the uncatalogued: a methodology for building a unified finding aid for Vojvodina periodicals, 1918–1941
abstract: This book chapter presents a practical methodology developed during the compilation of a regional union catalogue of interwar Vojvodina periodicals. The chapter describes the identification of 214 distinct periodical titles across eleven archival and library repositories in Serbia, Hungary, Austria, and Germany. It outlines the data collection protocol—including repository visits, photographic documentation, and collation with existing national bibliographies—and discusses challenges specific to incomplete runs, wartime destruction, and inconsistent title variants. A four-field minimum descriptive standard is proposed as compatible with existing national MARC records while accommodating gaps characteristic of provincial press holdings. The chapter also evaluates the utility of online access portals in Hungary and Austria for locating Serbian-language titles held outside Serbia. Practical recommendations are offered for future cross-border digitisation initiatives involving collections split between successor states.

title: Crime reportage and urban fear: the construction of public insecurity in Novi Sad press, 1925–1938
abstract: A corpus of 876 crime news items from two Novi Sad daily newspapers covering the period 1925–1938 was assembled from microfilm archives and coded for crime type, suspect descriptor, spatial reference, and narrative tone. The analysis traces the growth in column space devoted to street crime following the 1929 royal dictatorship proclamation and maps crime reports geographically against the city's quarter boundaries using historical cadastral maps. Results indicate a disproportionate association of crime with immigrant quarters and market spaces in newspaper accounts relative to police report frequencies found in the Historical Archive of the City of Novi Sad. Discourse analysis of 60 purposively selected reports examines how editorial choices produced a geography of fear that reinforced middle-class anxieties about urban disorder. The study connects press crime framing to broader scholarship on securitisation rhetoric in interwar Yugoslav public culture.

title: OCR-assisted corpus construction for early twentieth-century Serbian Cyrillic newsprint: accuracy assessment and correction workflows
abstract: This methodological paper reports on a project to digitise and machine-read 68,000 newspaper pages from Vojvodina periodicals printed in Serbian Cyrillic between 1919 and 1941. Two commercial and one open-source OCR engine were tested on a stratified sample of 500 pages representing five printing quality grades. Character error rates ranged from 4.2% to 18.7% across quality strata for the best-performing engine, with degraded wartime newsprint posing the greatest challenge. A semi-automated post-correction workflow using custom dictionary resources derived from period vocabulary reduced character error rates by an average of 6.1 percentage points. The paper documents the construction of a 12,000-entry domain-specific lexicon of interwar Serbian press vocabulary used in correction and describes the decision criteria for manual versus automated correction by page quality tier. Practical recommendations are offered for similar projects working with pre-1945 South Slavic Cyrillic newsprint in institutional settings with limited digitisation budgets.

title: Epidemic and epidemic rumour: health crisis reporting in Vojvodina newspapers during the interwar period
abstract: Drawing on a corpus of 634 health-related articles identified across ten Vojvodina newspapers between 1919 and 1941, this article analyses how the regional press reported on epidemic disease outbreaks and public health measures. Coverage is examined for three recurring episodes: the tail of the 1918–1919 influenza pandemic, a 1924 typhoid outbreak in Srem, and periodic cholera warnings in the 1930s. Coding categories included information source cited, prescription of individual versus institutional responses, and use of contagion metaphor. Results show that official health announcements were reproduced with minimal editorial addition in 71% of epidemic coverage, while anonymous community rumour appears as a framing device in 22% of articles. The article discusses the press as both information intermediary and anxiety amplifier in public health contexts, and draws connections to contemporary debates on health communication through historical media.

title: Annotation schema for historical newspaper corpora: lessons from a Vojvodina interwar press dataset
abstract: This conference paper presents the annotation schema developed for a 220,000-token annotated subcorpus drawn from digitised Vojvodina interwar newspapers. The schema addresses three layers of annotation: structural (article boundaries, headline, column type), thematic (topic classification across 34 categories), and sociolinguistic (register markers, dialect vocabulary, code-switching instances in multilingual papers). Inter-annotator agreement was measured across three trained annotators on a shared 10% subsample, yielding Krippendorff's alpha values of 0.81, 0.74, and 0.67 for the three layers respectively. Problem areas, particularly for thematic overlap between political and economic categories, are discussed. The schema and annotated subcorpus are described in terms of their compatibility with TEI P5 guidelines and their potential for reuse by researchers working on other regional historical newspaper collections in Southeast Europe. Data and schema documentation are deposited in an open repository.

title: Housing advertisements and the making of the urban rental market: evidence from Novi Sad daily press, 1922–1940
abstract: This article uses housing and rental advertisements published in two Novi Sad dailies between 1922 and 1940 as a quantitative source for reconstructing rental market conditions in a mid-sized provincial city. A dataset of 3,844 advertisements was assembled from digitised and microfilm sources and coded for dwelling type, number of rooms, listed amenities, neighbourhood descriptor, and price when stated. Price data, available for 1,612 advertisements, were converted to constant values using a regional wage index constructed from factory inspection reports in the Archives of Vojvodina. Results show a sustained rise in nominal rents from 1922 to 1931 followed by stagnation and nominal decline through 1937. Neighbourhood descriptors in advertisements are mapped against contemporary city plans to trace the spatial imagination of desirability. The study argues that housing advertisement series constitute a continuous and granular source for urban economic history in provincial centres where property transaction records are fragmentary.

title: Reader Trust in Print Versus Online News: A Survey of Novi Sad Adults in 2006
abstract: This cross-sectional survey investigated differences in perceived credibility between print and online versions of the same newspaper content among 612 adult residents of Novi Sad, stratified by age group (18–35, 36–55, 56+) and formal education level. Respondents were shown identical articles and asked to rate credibility on a seven-point Likert scale after being told the source medium. Results showed that respondents aged 56 and older rated print versions 1.4 points higher than online versions on average, while respondents aged 18–35 showed no statistically significant difference (p = 0.34). Education level moderated the effect: university-educated respondents in all age groups evaluated online content more favourably than did those with secondary education only. The study provides early evidence that medium-specific credibility perceptions are age-differentiated and that these differences may flatten as digital nativity spreads through the population.

title: Fitting Heavy-Tailed Severity Distributions to Internal Operational Loss Data: A Comparison of Lognormal, Pareto and Weibull Specifications
abstract: This paper evaluates three parametric families—lognormal, generalised Pareto, and Weibull—for modelling the severity of operational loss events recorded in the internal loss database of a mid-sized Central European bank over 2001–2008. The dataset comprises 1 147 loss observations across six Basel II event-type categories. Parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood and L-moments; goodness-of-fit is assessed via Anderson–Darling and Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics. For the external fraud and internal fraud categories, the generalised Pareto distribution with shape parameter estimated between 0.31 and 0.47 provides the best fit at the 5% significance level. For technology-related events, the lognormal remains competitive. The paper discusses implications for regulatory capital calculation under the Advanced Measurement Approach and recommends a mixed strategy in which the severity model is selected per business-line and event-type cell rather than applied uniformly. Sensitivity of Value-at-Risk at the 99.9% confidence level to distributional choice is shown to be substantial, with differences reaching 34% of the point estimate.

title: Poisson versus Negative Binomial Frequency Models for Operational Risk Event Counts: Evidence from a Serbian Banking Panel
abstract: Accurate frequency modelling is a prerequisite for credible operational Value-at-Risk estimation. This study tests whether the Poisson assumption for annual event counts is tenable using a balanced panel of eight Serbian commercial banks observed over 2005–2011, yielding 56 bank–year observations and 4 312 individual loss records obtained under a data-sharing agreement with the National Bank of Serbia. Likelihood-ratio tests and Vuong's statistic consistently reject equidispersion for five of the seven event-type categories examined, favouring the negative binomial specification. Estimated dispersion parameters range from 0.18 to 1.63 across categories. Monte Carlo experiments with 100 000 replications show that using Poisson instead of the negative binomial inflates the 99.9th-percentile aggregate loss estimate by 8–22% depending on severity tail weight. The paper recommends routine overdispersion testing as part of model validation procedures.

title: Threshold Selection for Extreme Value Modelling of IT Security Incident Costs in Financial Institutions
abstract: Applying extreme value theory to information security loss data requires a principled choice of threshold above which the generalised Pareto distribution is fitted. This paper compares four threshold selection methods—mean excess plot inspection, the Hill estimator stability plot, the automated metric of Danielsson and de Vries, and a minimum-distance criterion—using a synthetic dataset of 2 000 IT security incident costs constructed to resemble patterns reported in industry loss databases. The distribution of costs follows a mixture with a light-bodied bulk below USD 50 000 and a heavy tail above. Results show that automated methods select thresholds 15–30% higher than graphical inspection, leading to shape parameter estimates that differ by up to 0.12 and to 99th-percentile loss estimates differing by up to 28%. A bootstrap confidence interval procedure for the threshold-conditional GPD fit is proposed and illustrated. The findings have direct relevance for cyber risk capital allocation in small and medium financial institutions.

title: Operational Risk Capital Models Under Basel III: A Textbook Treatment with Worked Examples
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured exposition of the Loss Distribution Approach as implemented under Basel III requirements, written for graduate students in banking and finance. It begins with the actuarial foundations of compound distributions, proceeds through parameter estimation and Monte Carlo aggregation, and concludes with capital allocation across business lines using the Euler principle. Worked numerical examples use publicly available ORX consortium summary statistics. The chapter also covers the Standardised Measurement Approach introduced in the 2017 Basel Committee consultative document and discusses the tension between model complexity and supervisory comparability. An appendix provides annotated R code for a complete LDA workflow including fitting, simulation, and sensitivity analysis. The chapter is intended as course material for advanced risk management modules.

title: Estimating the Annual Frequency of Data Breach Events in European Financial Services: A Regression-Based Approach Using Publicly Reported Incidents
abstract: This study models the annual frequency of externally reported data breach events affecting European financial services firms over the period 2008–2015 using count regression applied to a hand-collected database of 341 publicly disclosed incidents drawn from regulatory notifications, press reports, and specialised security databases. Explanatory variables include firm size (log total assets), country-level cybersecurity maturity index scores, and year fixed effects. Negative binomial regression yields a significant positive elasticity of breach frequency with respect to firm size (coefficient 0.41, standard error 0.09) and a significant negative effect of cybersecurity maturity (coefficient −0.27, standard error 0.11). The model is validated on a holdout sample of 2016 events; predictive accuracy as measured by mean absolute percentage error is 19.3%. The results are used to construct a parametric frequency prior for Bayesian LDA models where internal event histories are sparse, which is typical for smaller institutions and emerging event categories such as ransomware.

title: A Scenario-Based Impact Estimation Framework for Ransomware Attacks on Small and Medium Enterprises
abstract: Small and medium enterprises have limited actuarial loss history to parameterise LDA models for ransomware risk. This paper proposes a structured scenario elicitation and quantification framework in which expert judgements are converted into truncated lognormal severity distributions using the SHELF protocol. Six scenario categories are defined—file encryption, operational downtime, recovery costs, reputational damage, regulatory fines, and third-party liability—and combined into a total impact distribution via Monte Carlo simulation with 500 000 trials. The framework is illustrated using data from 14 scenario workshops conducted with risk managers and IT security personnel at SMEs in the Vojvodina region, with total scenario coverage of 38 firms. The resulting aggregate loss distribution has a median of EUR 47 000 and a 95th percentile of EUR 310 000. Sensitivity analysis identifies operational downtime as the dominant contributor to tail risk, accounting for 58% of 99th-percentile loss variance. The framework is designed to be implementable without specialist software.

title: Bayesian Updating of Operational Loss Severity Parameters Using External Consortium Data
abstract: Institutions with short internal loss histories face the problem of sparse data in the tail, leading to high parameter uncertainty in fitted severity distributions. This paper develops a Bayesian framework that uses external consortium loss statistics as a prior and updates it with institution-specific internal data. The prior is elicited from ORX-style summary statistics (mean, standard deviation, and selected quantiles of annual aggregate loss by event category) using moment matching onto a lognormal hyperprior for the scale parameter. The posterior is approximated by Markov Chain Monte Carlo using a Metropolis–Hastings algorithm with 200 000 draws after a 50 000 draw burn-in. The framework is applied to a dataset from a Serbian savings bank with only 87 IT security loss observations over six years. Posterior predictive 99.9th-percentile estimates are compared to MLE-based estimates; the Bayesian approach reduces the coefficient of variation of the capital estimate from 0.61 to 0.29. The paper provides R code for all computations.

title: Measuring Cyber Resilience Loss in Critical Infrastructure: An Actuarial Perspective on Event Duration and Recovery Cost
abstract: Traditional operational risk models focus on direct financial loss and neglect recovery trajectory. This paper introduces an extended loss representation that appends to each event a recovery duration (days) and an associated daily cost, modelled jointly with the primary loss via a bivariate lognormal distribution. Parameters are estimated from 203 publicly documented cyber incidents affecting energy, transport, and financial infrastructure in Europe between 2012 and 2019, sourced from ENISA incident reports. The bivariate model is fitted by maximum likelihood; the correlation between log-severity and log-duration is estimated at 0.48 (standard error 0.07). A simulation study with 1 000 000 trials generates aggregate annual resilience-loss distributions for a stylised critical infrastructure operator. The 99th-percentile aggregate cost, integrating both direct and recovery components, exceeds the direct-only estimate by 37%. The paper concludes that ignoring recovery costs leads to systematic underestimation of the economic burden of cyber incidents.

title: Comparing the Standardised Measurement Approach and the Loss Distribution Approach for Cyber Risk Capital: A Simulation Study for Balkan Banking Sectors
abstract: The Basel Committee's 2017 decision to replace internal models with the Standardised Measurement Approach (SMA) for operational risk capital was contested by practitioners who argued it would disconnect capital from actual risk profiles. This paper uses a simulation study to compare SMA and LDA capital estimates for cyber risk specifically, using calibrated loss scenarios representative of banking sectors in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia. For each of 50 simulated bank profiles varying in size and cyber loss history, both methods are applied and results compared at the 99.9% confidence level. The SMA consistently overestimates capital for small banks (median ratio SMA/LDA = 1.43) and underestimates for large banks (median ratio = 0.86), consistent with its size-driven formula. The paper argues that a hybrid approach retaining internal frequency modelling within an SMA-compatible framework is feasible and quantifies the potential capital savings.

title: Frequency–Severity Decomposition of Phishing-Related Losses in Serbian Banks: A Zero-Inflated Compound Model
abstract: Many Serbian banks report zero phishing-related losses in a given quarter not because phishing attacks do not occur but because losses fall below internal reporting thresholds or are absorbed without formal recording. This paper addresses the resulting excess zeros in the frequency distribution by fitting a zero-inflated negative binomial model to quarterly event counts from 11 banks over 2015–2021 (308 bank–quarter observations). The probability of structural zero is modelled as a logistic function of the bank's cyber insurance indicator and its IT security expenditure per employee. The mixing probability is estimated at 0.34, meaning roughly one third of zero-count observations are structural. Severity is fitted with a lognormal distribution truncated below a EUR 1 000 reporting threshold; truncation correction raises the estimated mean severity by 18%. The paper is the first to apply zero-inflated frequency models specifically to phishing loss data from the Serbian banking sector.

title: Aggregate Loss Distribution Approximation Methods for Cyber Risk: Panjer Recursion, Fast Fourier Transform, and Monte Carlo Compared
abstract: Three numerical methods for computing aggregate loss distributions—Panjer recursion, Fast Fourier Transform inversion, and direct Monte Carlo simulation—are compared in terms of accuracy and computational cost for cyber risk applications characterised by heavy-tailed severities and overdispersed frequency distributions. The comparison is conducted on a standardised test battery of 24 frequency–severity combinations covering Poisson and negative binomial counts paired with lognormal, Pareto, and GPD severities, with tail parameters spanning from light to very heavy. Accuracy is measured relative to a high-precision reference obtained with 10 million Monte Carlo draws. FFT with discretisation step 100 EUR and grid size 2^20 achieves relative errors below 0.5% at the 99th percentile across all test cases in median CPU time of 0.8 seconds. Panjer recursion is accurate for Poisson–lognormal but fails to converge for heavy GPD tails. Monte Carlo with 100 000 draws achieves acceptable accuracy only above the 95th percentile. Practical guidance for practitioners choosing among methods is provided.

title: Operational Risk Disclosure and Cyber Incident Reporting Under the DORA Framework: Implications for Loss Data Quality in EU Banks
abstract: The EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) introduces mandatory ICT-related incident reporting for financial entities from January 2025. This paper analyses the expected impact of DORA reporting requirements on the quality and coverage of cyber loss datasets used to parameterise LDA models. Drawing on a survey of 31 risk and compliance officers at banks in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia conducted in late 2023, the paper documents current internal classification and reporting practices and identifies misalignments with DORA's taxonomy of significant cyber incidents. Simulation experiments show that under DORA-compliant reporting, the number of recordable cyber loss events per bank is expected to increase by a median factor of 2.7 relative to current Basel AMA/SMA thresholds, substantially reducing the excess-zero problem documented in earlier literature. The paper discusses transition challenges for non-EU countries with close financial links to the EU, including Serbia, and recommends adoption of compatible reporting standards by the National Bank of Serbia.

title: Tail Risk Estimation for Cloud Service Outage Losses: A Spliced Distribution Approach with Application to Serbian Fintech Firms
abstract: Cloud service outages generate bimodal loss profiles: a large mass of short, low-cost interruptions and a thin tail of prolonged outages with severe financial consequences. This paper fits spliced distributions combining a gamma body with a generalised Pareto tail to hourly downtime cost data collected from 19 fintech firms operating in Serbia between 2021 and 2024, yielding 2 641 outage episodes. The splice point is selected by minimising the integrated squared error between the empirical CDF and the fitted spliced distribution, resulting in an optimal threshold at the 87th empirical percentile. The GPD shape parameter governing the tail is estimated at 0.38 (95% CI: 0.21–0.55), confirming heavy-tail behaviour. Annual aggregate loss distributions are constructed via compound Poisson simulation. The 99th-percentile annual outage loss for a median-sized firm is estimated at EUR 180 000, with high sensitivity to the GPD shape parameter. Results inform cloud resilience investment decisions and business interruption insurance structuring for the fintech sector.

title: Seroprevalence of hepatitis E virus antibodies among swine slaughterhouse workers in Vojvodina: a cross-sectional study
abstract: This cross-sectional study estimated anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence among 214 full-time slaughterhouse workers at four pig-processing facilities in Vojvodina compared with 108 age- and sex-matched office-based controls. Blood samples were analysed using a commercial double-antigen sandwich ELISA. Overall seroprevalence was 28.5% among exposed workers versus 6.5% in controls (OR 5.6; 95% CI 2.8–11.2; p<0.001). Seroprevalence was highest among workers with more than ten years of occupational exposure (38.2%) and among those involved in evisceration tasks (34.7%). Multivariate logistic regression identified duration of employment, evisceration role, and absence of glove use as independent risk factors. No participant reported a prior clinical diagnosis of hepatitis E, suggesting predominantly subclinical infection. These findings support the designation of swine slaughterhouse workers in the region as a high-risk occupational group warranting targeted serological monitoring.

title: Longitudinal decline of anti-HEV IgG titres in previously seropositive slaughterhouse workers: a two-year follow-up cohort
abstract: Among 61 workers who tested anti-HEV IgG positive in the 2013 baseline study, 54 (88.5%) completed two annual follow-up blood draws in 2014 and 2015. Anti-HEV IgG was quantified using a WHO-standardised ELISA with results expressed in international units per millilitre. Median titre at baseline was 4.8 IU/mL (IQR 2.1–11.4). At year one, 33 participants (61.1%) showed titre reductions exceeding 50% from baseline; by year two, 14 participants (25.9%) had become seronegative using a cut-off of 0.5 IU/mL. A linear mixed-effects model estimated an average annual decline rate of 1.9 IU/mL (SE 0.3). Workers with baseline titres below 3 IU/mL were 4.1 times more likely to seroconvert to negative within two years. Continued occupational exposure did not prevent decline, suggesting that low-dose ongoing exposure is insufficient to boost immunity in most individuals.

title: Anti-HEV IgG avidity as a marker of infection recency in occupationally exposed workers: applicability and threshold validation
abstract: Avidity index measurement can distinguish recent from past HEV infection when IgM testing is negative or equivocal. A validation panel of 158 sera was assembled: 42 from acute HEV cases sampled within 12 weeks of symptom onset, 68 from slaughterhouse workers seropositive at baseline with known exposure timelines, and 48 from blood donors with no occupational risk. Avidity was determined by urea dissociation ELISA. ROC analysis identified an avidity index cut-off of 40% as optimal for discriminating recent infection (within 12 weeks) from past infection, yielding sensitivity 88.1% and specificity 91.2%. In the occupational cohort, 7 of 68 workers (10.3%) had avidity indices below 40% at baseline, indicating recent infection despite absence of symptoms. Repeated avidity testing at six-month intervals in 30 workers showed a mean avidity increase of 18 percentage points over 12 months. These data support routine avidity testing in occupational seroprevalence studies.

title: Occupational hepatitis E exposure in cattle slaughterhouses: is swine the only relevant reservoir in temperate Europe?
abstract: While swine are the established reservoir of HEV genotype 3 in Europe, evidence of HEV infection in cattle raises questions about whether cattle slaughterhouse workers face comparable exposure. This cross-sectional study enrolled 98 workers from two beef processing plants and 87 workers from pig processing plants in Vojvodina, comparing anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence, titre distributions, and avidity profiles. Seroprevalence was 12.2% in cattle workers versus 29.9% in pig workers (OR 0.33; 95% CI 0.16–0.68; p=0.002). Titre distributions did not differ significantly between the seropositive subgroups. Among five cattle-facility workers with low avidity index results, follow-up investigations traced exposure to co-housing areas where pigs were processed in an adjacent section of the same abattoir. No independent cattle-source transmission chain was confirmed. Findings suggest that cattle slaughter does not constitute an independent occupational HEV risk in this region.

title: Mathematical modelling of anti-HEV IgG waning in occupationally exposed adults: a Bayesian hierarchical approach
abstract: Quantitative prediction of seroreversion timing is needed to optimise surveillance intervals for occupationally exposed cohorts. Using longitudinal titre data from 54 slaughterhouse workers followed over two years (432 person-observations), a Bayesian hierarchical model was fitted to describe individual-level IgG waning trajectories. The model incorporated random effects for baseline titre, exposure intensity, and age. A two-phase exponential decay structure fitted the data substantially better than a single-phase model (WAIC difference 24.3). The fast-decay phase half-life was estimated at 98 days (95% credible interval 74–128), transitioning to a slow-decay phase half-life of 512 days (95% CrI 380–710). Workers in the lowest exposure-intensity tertile were predicted to reach seronegativity at a median of 2.8 years post-peak compared with 4.1 years for the highest tertile. The model provides a basis for risk-stratified re-testing schedules in occupational health programmes.

title: Seroprevalence of hepatitis E virus antibodies in a multi-country comparison of slaughterhouse workers from Serbia, Romania, and Hungary
abstract: Cross-national differences in HEV seroprevalence among occupationally exposed workers were examined in a coordinated cross-sectional survey conducted in 2020–2021 across eight abattoirs: three in Vojvodina (Serbia; n=186), three in Timiș County (Romania; n=172), and two in Bács-Kiskun County (Hungary; n=154). The same ELISA kit and standardised sampling protocol were used across all sites. Overall seroprevalence was 27.4% (Serbia), 21.5% (Romania), and 32.5% (Hungary). After adjustment for age, sex, employment duration, and task type in a pooled logistic regression, no statistically significant between-country difference remained (global p=0.19), suggesting that national variation is largely attributable to workforce composition. Genotype 3 was confirmed by PCR in a subset of 31 RNA-positive archived samples across all three countries. These results support the feasibility of harmonised occupational HEV surveillance protocols at the regional level.

title: Effect of personal protective equipment compliance on anti-HEV seroprevalence in pig slaughter workers: a structured observational study
abstract: Despite guidelines recommending gloves, eye protection, and aprons in abattoirs, compliance with personal protective equipment (PPE) is inconsistent. This study combined direct structured observation of 123 workers at three Vojvodina slaughterhouses—using a validated 26-item PPE compliance checklist administered over three shifts—with serological outcomes from the concurrent annual cohort blood draw. Workers were classified as high-compliance (≥80% adherence score; n=41), moderate-compliance (50–79%; n=51), or low-compliance (<50%; n=31). Anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence was 14.6%, 25.5%, and 45.2% across the three groups respectively. In multivariable analysis adjusting for task type and years of employment, moderate compliance (OR 2.0; 95% CI 0.8–5.0) and low compliance (OR 4.8; 95% CI 1.9–12.1) were each associated with higher odds of seropositivity compared with the high-compliance reference group. Observed compliance with glove use during evisceration was the single strongest determinant. Findings provide empirical support for targeted PPE training in occupational HEV prevention.

title: Temporal stability of anti-HEV IgG positivity over a decade in a cohort of occupationally exposed slaughterhouse workers: 10-year follow-up results
abstract: The 54 participants originally enrolled in the 2013 baseline serosurvey were re-contacted in 2023 for a ten-year follow-up blood draw; 38 agreed to participate (70.4%). Anti-HEV IgG, titre, and avidity were reassessed. Of the 16 participants who were seropositive at baseline, 9 remained seropositive at year 10 (56.3%), with a median titre of 1.8 IU/mL (IQR 0.9–3.4), substantially lower than the baseline median of 5.1 IU/mL. Among 22 participants who were seronegative at baseline, 5 (22.7%) were seropositive at year 10, indicating new acquisition during the decade. All five new seropositive participants had remained in active slaughterhouse employment throughout. Workers who had retired from slaughterhouse work (n=11) were more likely to be seronegative at year 10 than those still employed (OR 4.2; 95% CI 1.1–16.3). Results confirm that active occupational exposure sustains serological evidence of HEV exposure even as individual titres wane substantially over time.

title: Hepatitis E virus serology in immunocompromised patients employed in pig-related industries: a case series from Vojvodina tertiary hospitals
abstract: Chronic HEV infection can develop in immunocompromised individuals and is increasingly recognised as a clinical concern. This case series describes eight patients referred to the Infectious Disease Clinic and the Clinic for Gastroenterology and Hepatology of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2018 and 2024, all of whom had documented occupational pig or slaughterhouse exposure and were receiving immunosuppressive therapy for solid organ transplantation (n=5) or haematological malignancy (n=3). HEV RNA was detected in all eight patients by RT-PCR; six had HEV genotype 3 confirmed by sequencing. Liver enzyme elevations were moderate (median ALT 3.4× upper limit of normal). Two patients progressed to chronicity, defined by viraemia persisting beyond six months; both were on tacrolimus-based regimens. Ribavirin treatment was initiated in these two patients with virological response in one. The series highlights the importance of HEV testing in immunocompromised patients with occupational exposure histories and unexplained hepatitis.

title: Detection of spatiotemporal clusters of tick-borne encephalitis using SaTScan: Vojvodina 2005–2016
abstract: A retrospective space-time permutation scan statistic (SaTScan v9.4) was applied to 1,102 confirmed TBE cases reported in Vojvodina from 2005 to 2016 to identify statistically significant space-time clusters. Cases were aggregated by municipality of residence and month of symptom onset. Three primary clusters were identified: the most likely cluster centred on Sremska Mitrovica (RR = 4.7, p < 0.001, 2007–2009), a secondary cluster in the Bečej-Zrenjanin corridor (RR = 2.9, p = 0.003, 2013–2015), and a smaller late-period cluster near Sombor (RR = 3.2, p = 0.012, 2014–2016). The emergence of the Bečej-Zrenjanin cluster coincides with documented changes in drainage management and partial reforestation of canal embankments in that period. Results are visualised as risk-ratio maps overlaid on municipal boundaries and discussed in relation to concurrent land-management records from the Provincial Directorate for Water Management.

title: Using auxiliary covariates to improve small-area colorectal cancer estimates when registry geocoding is incomplete: a simulation study
abstract: When address geocoding is incomplete, auxiliary area-level covariates — such as population density, deprivation index, and distance to the nearest gastroenterology unit — can improve small-area estimates by informing both the spatial random effects and the missingness mechanism. This simulation study generated 1,000 synthetic cancer registry datasets mimicking the Vojvodina registry structure, with missingness fractions of 15%, 30%, and 45% and three missingness mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR). Five models were compared: a null CAR model, a CAR model with covariates, a model with covariate-informed imputation, a full-data oracle model, and a complete-case model. Incorporating covariates reduced root mean squared error of tract-level estimates by 12–18% under MAR and had negligible effect under MNAR. The deprivation index was the most informative single covariate. Results support routine inclusion of socioeconomic area-level covariates in registry-based small-area models.

title: Mapping seasonal inundation in the Obedska bara wetland complex using Envisat ASAR time series
abstract: Envisat ASAR Wide Swath data acquired between 2005 and 2010 were used to map seasonal flooding in the Obedska bara Ramsar site in the Sava floodplain, Serbia. A threshold-based change detection approach was applied to 47 multi-temporal VV-polarisation scenes calibrated to sigma-naught. Open water pixels were identified by a bimodal histogram separation technique, and inundated area was computed per acquisition date at 75 m spatial resolution. The resulting inundation time series revealed that peak flooding typically occurs in late March to early April, with median flooded area reaching approximately 4 200 ha. Inter-annual variability was high: the 2006 flood event inundated nearly 7 800 ha, roughly twice the long-term median. The study also compared radar-derived extents with contemporaneous Landsat ETM+ optical imagery, finding an overall agreement of 84 %. Discrepancies were concentrated in dense reed stands where SAR double-bounce returns caused systematic overestimation of water extent. Results provide a baseline inundation climatology useful for conservation management planning.

title: Evaluation of open-water detection algorithms for shallow floodplain lakes in the Middle Danube region
abstract: Four automated water detection algorithms were benchmarked against GPS-surveyed water boundaries across twelve oxbow lakes and shallow basins distributed along a 180 km reach of the middle Danube in Serbia and Croatia. Data consisted of 22 Sentinel-1A IW GRD scenes (VV and VH polarisations) acquired between June 2015 and November 2016. Algorithms tested included a fixed global threshold, an Otsu adaptive threshold, a hierarchical split-based approach, and a support vector machine classifier trained on 800 labelled samples. The SVM classifier achieved the highest median F1 score (0.91), while the Otsu method performed comparably (F1 0.88) with far lower computational cost. False detections increased substantially in wind-roughened lake surfaces under wind speeds above 4 m/s, reducing SVM F1 to 0.74 in those scenes. The paper recommends filtering acquisitions by wind speed metadata when building long hydroperiod records, and provides a lookup table of expected accuracy degradation as a function of wind speed and lake fetch.

title: Estimating above-ground herbaceous biomass in Pannonian wet meadows from Sentinel-1 backscatter using the water-cloud model
abstract: The water-cloud model (WCM) was parameterised and inverted to retrieve above-ground biomass in wet meadow parcels within the Vojvodina lowlands during the 2017 growing season. Field campaigns in April, June, and August collected destructive biomass samples at 48 plots across three landscape units, alongside measurements of canopy water content and height. Sentinel-1A ascending and descending VV backscatter time series at 20 m resolution were used as model inputs. WCM parameters were calibrated using a nonlinear least-squares routine; cross-validated biomass retrieval achieved RMSE of 43 g/m² against withheld field samples (relative RMSE 19 %). Sensitivity analysis indicated that VV backscatter in the 0–400 g/m² biomass range carries most discriminating information, but saturates beyond 600 g/m². The study also examined how soil moisture confounds retrieval and found that errors increased by 30–40 % when soil volumetric water content exceeded 0.35 m³/m³, motivating the need for simultaneous soil moisture constraints in future WCM inversions.

title: Hydroperiod maps for the Banat plain wetlands derived from a 2015–2020 Sentinel-1 archive
abstract: A six-year Sentinel-1A/B time series comprising 312 IW GRD scenes was processed to produce hydroperiod maps at 10 m resolution for the wetland complexes of the Banat plain in northern Serbia. Inundation was detected per scene using an adaptive local threshold applied within a 500 m moving window to account for spatial variation in radar response caused by soil type and land cover. Scenes with snow cover, flagged using auxiliary ERA5 temperature data, were excluded, leaving 287 usable acquisitions. Annual hydroperiod was expressed as the fraction of valid observations classified as flooded. The resulting maps distinguish permanently wet areas (hydroperiod > 0.9), seasonally flooded depressions (0.2–0.9), and rarely inundated land (< 0.2). Long-term mean hydroperiod correlates strongly (r = 0.83) with topographic wetness index derived from a 1 m LiDAR DEM. The 2019–2020 period shows markedly reduced flooding relative to the 2015–2018 mean, consistent with recorded precipitation deficits. Maps are archived as cloud-optimised GeoTIFF and made available through a public repository.

title: Separation of surface water and flooded vegetation in the Koviljsko-petrovaradinski rit wetland using dual-polarisation Sentinel-1
abstract: Distinguishing open water from water beneath emergent and flooded shrub vegetation is a persistent challenge in SAR-based wetland mapping. This study applied a dual-polarisation (VV, VH) classification scheme to 24 Sentinel-1 IW scenes acquired over the Koviljsko-petrovaradinski rit nature reserve on the Danube in Serbia between March and October 2020. A random forest classifier was trained on 1 200 manually labelled segments stratified by vegetation type: open water, reed (Phragmites australis), willow-poplar gallery forest, moist grassland, and dry land. The VH/VV ratio proved the most important feature for separating flooded woody vegetation (median ratio −2.1 dB) from open water (median −5.8 dB). Overall accuracy on a held-out test set reached 88.3 % (kappa 0.85). The classifier was then applied to the full seasonal stack to map the spatial extent and timing of the double-bounce zone associated with flooded forest, showing that this zone expands by a factor of 2.4 between low and peak flood stages. Results support habitat quality assessments under the Birds Directive.

title: Integrating Sentinel-1 backscatter and hydrological model outputs to improve inundation mapping in agriculturally drained lowlands
abstract: Standard SAR inundation classifiers often fail in flat, intensively drained agricultural plains where water depth is shallow and surface roughness from crops masks the open-water signal. This study coupled a calibrated HBV-Light hydrological model of three drainage basins in the Vojvodina lowlands with Sentinel-1 SAR observations to improve inundation mapping during 14 flood episodes between 2018 and 2023. Simulated soil saturation deficit was used as a prior to constrain per-scene SAR thresholds, reducing commission errors in dry agricultural fields by 22 % and improving recall of shallow inundation in subsurface-drained parcels by 17 % relative to a threshold-only baseline. Validation used field photographs and water-level records at 31 drainage canal gauges. The coupled approach better captures early-onset shallow flooding (< 5 cm depth) that optical sensors and standalone SAR methods miss. The framework is computationally lightweight and could be transferred to similar lowland systems in Hungary or Romania with modest recalibration effort.

title: Towards a pan-Pannonian wetland inundation database: harmonising national SAR processing chains across six countries
abstract: Wetland monitoring in the Pannonian Basin is fragmented across national institutions using heterogeneous processing workflows and inconsistent land-cover reference datasets. This paper reports on a harmonisation effort that compiled Sentinel-1-based inundation products from Serbia, Hungary, Croatia, Slovakia, Austria, and Romania covering the period 2017–2024. Processing chain parameters—including geometric correction grid spacing, speckle filter kernel size, and water detection threshold strategies—were documented and their effect on cross-border consistency quantified. At 32 test transects crossing international borders, discrepancies in mapped flooded area between adjacent national products ranged from 3 % to 28 %. A recommended minimum specification is proposed: 10 m pixel spacing, a refined Lee 5×5 speckle filter, and an adaptive local threshold with a 1 km window. Applying this specification retroactively to all six national archives reduced border discrepancies to below 8 % in 29 of 32 transects. The harmonised mosaic for 2022 is released as an open dataset and constitutes the largest consistent SAR-based wetland inundation archive for the region to date.

title: Moisture redistribution in flat-bottom steel silos during autumn storage of maize: a pilot-scale study
abstract: Moisture redistribution in bulk maize is a well-documented risk during the autumn cooling period, yet quantitative data from instrumented pilot silos under continental climatic conditions remain limited. This study tracked moisture content and temperature at 24 measurement points inside a 120-tonne flat-bottom steel silo over an 11-week period (September–November) at the FINS pilot facility in Novi Sad. Maize was loaded at a mean moisture content of 14.1 % (wet basis). Temperature cable readings were logged every two hours; grain samples were extracted weekly via sampling tubes at three heights and two radial positions. Results showed a maximum moisture gain of 1.8 percentage points in the upper peripheral zone by week six, coinciding with a 9 °C difference between the grain core and the silo wall. Dry matter loss estimated from CO₂ accumulation reached 0.11 % over the observation period. Intermittent natural aeration (six hours per night when outside air temperature was below 8 °C) reduced the peripheral moisture peak by approximately 0.5 percentage points compared with an unaerated reference section. The data provide a baseline for calibrating predictive moisture-migration models under Pannonian autumn conditions.

title: Effect of repeated freeze–thaw cycles on germination capacity and alpha-amylase activity in stored wheat
abstract: Continental storage sites in the northern Balkans and southern Pannonian Plain are occasionally exposed to sharp temperature reversals in late winter, raising concern about grain quality in partially emptied silos where insulation is reduced. This laboratory study simulated three magnitudes of freeze–thaw cycling (−5/+10 °C, −10/+10 °C, and −15/+10 °C) applied to wheat samples (cv. 'Zlatna njiva 3', moisture content 12.8 % w.b.) over four consecutive weekly cycles. Germination capacity, falling number, and alpha-amylase activity (measured by the Hagberg–Perten method) were determined after each cycle. Germination capacity declined significantly only in the −15/+10 °C treatment after the third cycle (from 97 % to 81 %). Falling number was not significantly affected at any temperature level across four cycles (p > 0.05). Alpha-amylase activity showed a small but consistent increase in the −15/+10 °C group (from 28 to 44 U/g), suggesting incipient stress sprouting is possible under severe conditions. Results indicate that standard aeration protocols maintaining grain temperature above −8 °C should be sufficient to protect milling quality under typical Vojvodina winter storage conditions.

title: Mixolab curve parameter prediction from near-infrared spectra of whole-meal wheat flour
abstract: A partial least squares (PLS) calibration was developed to predict eight Mixolab 2 parameters—dough development time, stability, weakening (C2), starch gelatinisation (C3), amylase activity (C3–C4 slope), retrogradation (C5), and two torque ratios—from near-infrared reflectance spectra (1100–2500 nm) of 112 whole-meal flour samples representing eleven Serbian wheat genotypes harvested across two seasons. Cross-validation yielded RMSECV values of 0.04–0.12 Nm for torque parameters and 0.6–1.1 min for time parameters. External validation on 28 independent samples confirmed acceptable predictive performance (RPD 2.1–3.4). Spectra from grain harvested under drought stress showed systematic deviations attributable to altered starch-lipid associations, necessitating separate sub-models. The calibration is intended as a rapid screening tool to guide mill blending decisions before full Mixolab runs, reducing reagent use and analysis time by an estimated 65 %.
