title: Iterative ICI Mitigation for Underwater Acoustic OFDM Using Basis Expansion Models
abstract: Doppler-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI) is a significant impairment in underwater acoustic OFDM systems. This work models the time-varying channel using a complex-exponential basis expansion model (CE-BEM) with five basis functions fitted to measured channel coefficients. An iterative receiver alternates between soft ICI cancellation using extrinsic information from a rate-1/2 convolutional decoder and CE-BEM coefficient re-estimation. Experiments were performed in a freshwater lake at 6 m depth, 200 m range, with a 128-subcarrier OFDM system at a centre frequency of 25 kHz, 5 kHz bandwidth, and a cyclic prefix of 8 ms. After three iterations, the receiver achieved a coded BER of 4 × 10^-4 at 16 dB SNR, compared with 2.1 × 10^-2 for a non-iterative equaliser at the same SNR. The CE-BEM order selection is discussed and a practical rule for shallow-water operation is proposed.

title: Turbo Equalization for OFDM in Shallow-Water Acoustic Channels: Convergence Behaviour Analysed via Extrinsic Information Transfer Charts
abstract: This paper examines the convergence of a turbo equaliser for underwater acoustic OFDM using extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) chart analysis. The equaliser consists of a soft MMSE frequency-domain equaliser exchanging log-likelihood ratios with a systematic convolutional code (rate 1/2, constraint length 7). The EXIT trajectories are computed both analytically, using a Gaussian approximation of the mutual information, and empirically from measured channels recorded at three shallow-water sites on the Danube river (depths 4–9 m, ranges 50–300 m). Measured trajectories match analytical predictions within 0.8 dB SNR across all sites. The tunnel width in the EXIT chart is shown to narrow considerably when the channel delay spread exceeds 40 ms, requiring a minimum of four iterations to avoid error floors. Practical design guidelines for subcarrier spacing selection based on EXIT chart geometry are presented, reducing the required number of turbo iterations from six to three while maintaining BER below 10^-4.

title: Block LDPC Codes for Shallow-Water Acoustic OFDM: Performance Under Measured Channel Conditions
abstract: Low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with belief-propagation decoding are evaluated as replacements for convolutional codes in a turbo-equalization framework for shallow-water acoustic OFDM. Three quasi-cyclic LDPC codes with rates 1/2, 2/3, and 3/4 and block lengths of 1944, 1296, and 648 bits (drawn from the IEEE 802.11n specification matrix set) are assessed using 47 channel realisations recorded in the Tikvara canal near Bačka Palanka at 18 kHz centre frequency. Belief propagation with 50 inner iterations is combined with soft MMSE equalisation iterated up to six times. The rate-1/2 code achieves a frame error rate below 1% at 15.5 dB SNR, outperforming an equivalent convolutional turbo code by 1.2 dB. However, the rate-3/4 code exhibits an error floor above 10^-2 FER under channels with delay spreads exceeding 30 ms, attributed to short cycles in the parity-check matrix interacting with residual ICI.

title: Sparse Channel Estimation via Compressed Sensing for Underwater Acoustic OFDM: Measurement-Based Validation
abstract: Underwater acoustic channels in shallow water often exhibit a sparse delay-power profile, with significant energy confined to a small number of paths. This work applies compressed sensing techniques—specifically the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) and the basis pursuit de-noising (BPDN) algorithms—to estimate these sparse channels from reduced pilot sets. Channel measurements were obtained in a 12 m deep section of the Danube river using a 256-subcarrier OFDM system at 20 kHz with an 8 kHz bandwidth and a 5 ms cyclic prefix. OMP with a pilot density of 12.5% achieved an NMSE of −18.3 dB, comparable to MMSE estimation using 25% pilots, a saving of half the pilot overhead. BPDN offered marginal additional gain (0.4 dB NMSE) at roughly 6× greater computational cost. Sensitivity to the sparsity order mismatch is analysed; errors below 20% in the assumed sparsity level incur less than 1 dB NMSE degradation.

title: Adaptive Receivers for Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: This book chapter reviews adaptive receiver algorithms applicable to underwater acoustic communication systems, with emphasis on shallow-water environments where multipath delay spread can extend beyond the OFDM symbol guard interval. The chapter covers linear and decision-feedback equaliser structures based on LMS, RLS, and Kalman filter adaptation, followed by frequency-domain soft equalisation for OFDM. Iterative (turbo) architectures combining equalisation and channel decoding are discussed in detail, including EXIT chart design tools. Performance data drawn from field measurements on inland waterways in the middle Danube basin are used throughout to ground the discussion. Practical considerations—pilot contamination, Doppler pre-compensation, receiver synchronisation—are addressed alongside algorithmic descriptions. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and engineers entering the field, and closes with a summary of open problems including real-time implementation constraints and deep-water applicability.

title: Variational Bayes Channel Tracking for Fast-Varying Underwater Acoustic OFDM Channels
abstract: This paper proposes a variational Bayes (VB) algorithm for online tracking of time-varying multipath channel coefficients within a single OFDM symbol duration. The channel is modelled as a first-order Gauss–Markov process per subcarrier, and the VB updates alternate between posterior approximations for the channel coefficients and for the noise variance, removing the need for explicit noise power estimation. The algorithm is initialised with an OMP-based sparse estimate from preamble pilots. In simulated channels matched to BELLHOP ray-trace predictions for the Begej canal (depth 3 m, range 150 m), VB tracking maintained an NMSE below −15 dB at SNR ≥ 12 dB through 32-symbol bursts, while a static MMSE equaliser degraded by 5 dB within 10 symbols. A computational complexity of O(N log N) per OFDM symbol is demonstrated, where N = 128 subcarriers, making real-time deployment feasible on a mid-range DSP platform.

title: Performance of Polar Codes with Successive-Cancellation List Decoding in Underwater Acoustic OFDM Systems
abstract: Polar codes with successive-cancellation list (SCL) decoding are evaluated for an underwater acoustic OFDM link operating at 22 kHz centre frequency in a shallow-water canal environment. Code rates of 1/3, 1/2, and 2/3 with block lengths of 512 and 1024 bits are considered. List sizes of L = 4 and L = 8 are tested together with a CRC-aided variant using a 16-bit CRC. Channel coefficients are emulated using a tapped-delay-line model fitted to 62 measured impulse responses from the Plovni kanal near Sombor. CRC-aided SCL decoding with L = 8 at rate 1/2 and block length 1024 achieves a frame error rate of 10^-3 at 13.8 dB SNR, representing a 1.8 dB gain over a rate-1/2 turbo code with comparable block length. Complexity comparison shows SCL decoding at L = 8 requires approximately 2.4× more operations per decoded bit than the turbo code at 6 iterations.
venue: Proceedings of the 30th International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)

title: Joint Doppler Compensation and Turbo Equalisation for High-Mobility Underwater Acoustic OFDM
abstract: Vessel-mounted receivers experience significant Doppler stretch and shift in shallow-water acoustic channels, complicating OFDM reception. This paper presents a receiver architecture that jointly estimates a bulk Doppler scale factor using maximum-likelihood search over a coarse grid followed by a Newton refinement step, then passes the resampled signal to a turbo equaliser based on soft MMSE frequency-domain processing coupled with a rate-1/2 LDPC decoder. The bulk Doppler estimation exploits a 64-sample Zadoff–Chu preamble. Testing was conducted using a boat moving at 1.2–3.5 m/s along the Danube near Novi Sad at a range of 300 m, water depth 7 m, carrier frequency 18 kHz, bandwidth 6 kHz, 128 subcarriers. At 3.5 m/s boat speed the uncorrected BER exceeded 0.4; after joint Doppler correction and four turbo iterations the coded BER fell below 8 × 10^-4 at SNR 17 dB. The Newton refinement reduced residual Doppler error by a factor of 6 compared with grid-only search.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Initialisation for Iterative Equalisation in Shallow-Water Acoustic OFDM
abstract: Warm-starting iterative equalisers with accurate initial channel estimates can reduce the number of turbo iterations required to convergence. This paper investigates replacing the standard pilot-interpolation initialisation step with a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a synthetic dataset of 50 000 channel realisations generated using a BELLHOP model parameterised to match measured profiles from three inland waterway sites. The CNN takes the received pilot sub-vectors as input and outputs an initial soft estimate of the channel frequency response. With CNN initialisation, the turbo equaliser with LDPC decoding reaches BER 10^-3 in two iterations at 15 dB SNR on unseen measured channels, whereas the standard interpolation initialiser requires four iterations for the same performance, reducing receiver latency by 47%. The CNN has 14 200 parameters and requires 0.31 ms per OFDM frame on a mid-range embedded GPU, assessed using a Jetson Nano development board.

title: Coded OFDM Link Budget Analysis for Shallow Inland Waterway Monitoring Networks
abstract: This preprint presents a link budget framework for planning multi-node underwater acoustic sensor networks on shallow inland waterways, targeting environmental and navigational monitoring applications. The framework integrates empirical propagation loss measurements collected at seven Danube and Sava cross-sections (depths 2–11 m, ranges 50–500 m) with a coded OFDM system model including turbo equalisation and rate-1/2 LDPC coding. Ambient noise spectra measured at each site are parameterised as a function of shipping traffic intensity, and a unified SNR–BER curve family is derived per site class. The analysis identifies a reliable coverage radius of 220 m in high-traffic conditions and 410 m under low-traffic conditions for a transmit power of 5 W at 20 kHz. Node placement guidelines for achieving 95% link availability are given for linear and mesh topologies. Comparison with a ray-tracing propagation model shows agreement within 2.5 dB across all measured sites.

title: FDTD Modelling of Differential Pair Routing Discontinuities on Multilayer PCBs at Frequencies up to 3 GHz
abstract: This paper presents a systematic finite-difference time-domain study of the electromagnetic radiation produced by differential signal pairs routed across layer transitions in a standard FR4 six-layer printed circuit board stack-up. Four transition geometries were modelled: uncapped via, back-drilled via, via with a single ground stitch, and via with a ground stitch array. Excitation was provided by a Gaussian pulse with a 3 GHz spectral ceiling. Radiated electric field at one metre was extracted using a near-to-far-field transformation. Results show that a single adjacent ground stitch reduces peak radiation by 6.1 dB relative to an uncapped via at 2.4 GHz, while a four-via stitch array achieves 11.3 dB suppression. The FDTD predictions were validated against near-field scan measurements taken on a dedicated test board using a semi-rigid loop probe on a motorised XY stage. Agreement within 2.1 dB was obtained across 18 measurement points in the frequency band of interest. The work provides quantitative guidance for stack-up design in boards carrying SerDes interfaces at data rates above 5 Gbit/s.

title: Open-Loop DPD Coefficient Initialisation Using Device Physics-Informed Regression for Rapid PA Swap-Out
abstract: In base station maintenance scenarios, replacing a faulty PA with a new unit currently requires full DPD re-training from live traffic, causing a period of elevated ACPR. This paper proposes an open-loop initialisation method in which device datasheet parameters — quiescent current, gate bias, and small-signal gain — are used as inputs to a regression model trained on a library of 47 characterised GaN devices spanning four manufacturers and three process nodes. The regression model predicts GMP model coefficients for the replacement device without requiring any over-the-air observation. Initial ACPR after open-loop DPD is −43.5 dBc on average across a leave-one-out cross-validation, compared to −28.3 dBc with no DPD and −50.1 dBc after full closed-loop adaptation. Fine-tuning from 500 observed samples brings the closed-loop result to within 0.7 dBc of the fully trained baseline. The approach reduces the number of adaptation samples needed by a factor of 18 compared to cold-start training, which is relevant for systems where observation bandwidth or processing time is limited during live operation.

title: Temperature Dependence of TDC Bin Width in 65 nm CMOS and Its Impact on PLL Phase Noise over the −40 °C to 125 °C Range
abstract: Time-to-digital converter bin width in deep-submicron CMOS processes varies with temperature primarily because gate propagation delay has a negative temperature coefficient above roughly 0.7 V supply. This paper characterises the bin-width temperature sensitivity of a 64-stage inverter-chain TDC fabricated in a 65 nm CMOS process across the −40 °C to 125 °C automotive temperature range. Mean bin width increases from 28 ps at −40 °C to 44 ps at 125 °C, a change of 57 %. Without compensation, the resulting variation in effective TDC gain shifts the PLL loop bandwidth by approximately the same fraction, moving the phase-noise optimum away from the design target. A first-order digital gain compensation table indexed by an on-chip temperature sensor reduces loop-bandwidth variation to under 4 % across the full range. Residual phase noise at 10 kHz offset changes by less than 1.2 dB after compensation, compared with 6.8 dB without it.

title: Compressive Delay-Doppler Channel Estimation for OFDM-Based V2X Systems Using Structured Sparsity
abstract: This paper proposes a compressive channel estimation scheme for OFDM V2X waveforms that exploits clustered sparsity in the delay-Doppler domain. Pilot subcarriers are designed according to a deterministic difference-set pattern that provides flat compressed sensing measurement matrices with low coherence. Reconstruction is performed via a block-sparse Bayesian learning (BSBL) algorithm adapted to the two-dimensional cluster structure expected in vehicular channels. Simulations are driven by channel parameters drawn from the measurement-validated stochastic model of Trifunović et al. (2014) and from a publicly available geometry-based model for urban intersections. With 25 % pilot overhead—half the standard ITS-G5 pilot density—the proposed method achieves mean squared error within 1.5 dB of the Cramér-Rao lower bound at SNR above 12 dB and supports vehicle speeds up to 130 km/h without performance floor. Hardware-in-the-loop validation is performed using a National Instruments software-defined radio platform at 5.9 GHz.

title: Shear-banding onset in concentrated hard-sphere-like suspensions under large-amplitude oscillatory shear
abstract: We report rheo-optical measurements of shear-band formation in suspensions of polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) spheres (diameter 430 nm) at volume fractions between 0.50 and 0.60. Large-amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) experiments were performed at strain amplitudes from 1 to 500 % and angular frequencies of 1 and 10 rad/s. Flow visualisation was achieved using a custom-built transparent Couette geometry mounted on a stress-controlled rheometer. Shear banding was identified above a critical strain amplitude that decreased monotonically from approximately 80 % at φ = 0.50 to 22 % at φ = 0.60. Time-resolved velocity profiles obtained by particle-image velocimetry revealed a low-viscosity band near the inner cylinder and a high-viscosity band occupying roughly 60 % of the gap at φ = 0.58. The band boundary oscillates at the applied frequency. Lissajous–Bowditch representations confirm the transition from weakly to strongly nonlinear response coincides with banding onset. These findings constrain existing constitutive models that predict a single yield surface.

title: Uticaj polidisperznosti čestica na reološki odgovor gustih kaolinski-vodenih suspenzija
abstract: Analiziran je uticaj distribucije veličina čestica na reološke karakteristike kaolinski-vodenih suspenzija pri zapreminskim udelima od 0,40 do 0,55. Korišćene su tri frakcije kaolina sa srednjim prečnikom čestica d50 = 1,2, 3,1 i 7,4 μm, kao i binarne i ternarne mešavine. Reometrijska merenja obuhvatala su amplitudne testove, frekventnu spektroskopiju i kontinualni tok. Utvrđeno je da binarne mešavine čija zapreminska frakcija krupnih čestica iznosi 0,7 pokazuju značajno niži viskozitet pri visokim brzinama smicanja u poređenju sa monodisperznim frakcijama ekvivalentnog zapreminskog udela. Vrednosti napona prinosa, određene Herschel–Bulkley fitovanjem, rastu sa povećanjem udela sitnih čestica pri konstantnom ukupnom zapreminskom udelu. Granulometrijska analiza laserskom difrakcijom i SEM snimci korišćeni su za karakterizaciju čestica pre i posle smicanja. Rezultati imaju direktnu primenu u optimizaciji reologije keramičkih past za ekstruziono procesovanje.

title: Reološka karakterizacija nanokompozinih suspenzija gline i polietilen glikola za primenu u bušotinskim fluidima
abstract: Ispitivane su suspenzije smektitnih glina (bentonit i laponit) modifikovanih polietilen glikolom (PEG, Mw = 4000 i 20000 g/mol) u cilju procene njihove primenjivosti kao komponenti bušotinskih fluida pri povišenim temperaturama. Merenja su vršena pri temperaturama od 25 do 80 °C na reometru sa kontrolisanom deformacijom. Amplitudni testovi pokazali su da je linearni viskoelastični region znatno sužen pri temperaturama iznad 60 °C kod uzoraka sa PEG 20000. Efektivni viskozitet pri brzini smicanja 100 s⁻¹ opada sa porastom temperature za oko 45 % u ispitivanom opsegu, dok napon prinosa raste za uzorke sa većim molekulskim masom PEG-a. Tixotropno ponašanje kvantifikovano je protokolom sa naglim promenom brzine smicanja, a dobijene vrednosti vremena oporavka kreću se između 80 i 340 s zavisno od formulacije. Rezultati sugerišu da je PEG 20000 efikasniji modifikator reologije u uslovima povišene temperature.

title: Rheo-SAXS characterisation of microstructural evolution in dense silica suspensions during LAOS
abstract: Simultaneous rheological and small-angle X-ray scattering (rheo-SAXS) measurements were performed on dense suspensions of silica spheres (d = 95 nm, φ = 0.50 and 0.56) subjected to large-amplitude oscillatory shear at the ESRF beamline ID02 in Grenoble. Strain amplitudes of 5, 50 and 200 % were applied at angular frequencies of 0.1, 1 and 10 rad/s. Two-dimensional SAXS patterns were collected at 10 frames per oscillation cycle. At γ₀ = 5 % the scattering patterns retained near-isotropic symmetry, consistent with weakly perturbed liquid-like order. At γ₀ = 200 % and ω = 1 rad/s, a pronounced two-lobed anisotropy developed along the flow direction in the first half-cycle and partially recovered during flow reversal. The degree of anisotropy correlated with the instantaneous strain rather than the instantaneous stress, suggesting affine microstructural deformation. The characteristic relaxation timescale extracted from the SAXS recovery curves agrees with the terminal relaxation time from bulk rheology to within 15 %. The data support a scenario in which cage distortion rather than cage break-up governs the nonlinear response at intermediate strain amplitudes.

title: Frequency-dependent viscosity scaling in binary mixtures of colloidal hard spheres
abstract: The dynamic viscosity of binary hard-sphere-like suspensions was measured as a function of frequency, total volume fraction, and mixing ratio using a stress-controlled rheometer with a double-gap geometry. Suspensions composed of PMMA spheres with diameter ratio 1:3.4 (small: d = 125 nm, large: d = 425 nm) were prepared at total volume fractions between 0.40 and 0.58 and large-particle mole fractions χ between 0 and 1. A scaling form η*(ω)/η∞ = f(ωτ(φ, χ)) was tested, where τ is an effective relaxation time. Collapse of the data onto a master curve was achieved for χ between 0.3 and 0.7 using a single φ-dependent τ, but failed for χ < 0.2 and χ > 0.8. The breakdown is attributed to size-asymmetry-induced structural heterogeneity, which was independently confirmed by confocal microscopy. The results indicate that simple effective-medium descriptions are insufficient for strongly asymmetric binary systems.

title: Nestabilnosti toka i formiranje traka u koloidnim gelovima pri smicanju male amplitude
abstract: Ispitivane su nestabilnosti toka u koloidnim gelovima formiranim od karboksimetil-celuloze (CMC) i laponita pri različitim koncentracijama polimera (0,2–1,0 wt%) i laponita (2,0–4,0 wt%). Oscilatorni testovi male amplitude izvedeni su u opsegu deformacija od 0,01 do 50 % pri fiksnoj frekvenciji od 1 Hz. Koristeći kombinaciju reometrije i vizualizacije fluorescentnim mikročesticama u ravni smicanja, detektovane su lokalne nehomogenosti toka već pri amplitudama deformacije iznad oko 3 %, što prethodi maksimumu napona smicanja u krivoj amplitudnog prolaska. Utvrđeno je da povećanje koncentracije CMC odlaže pojavu traka ka višim amplitudama, ali ne eliminiše nestabilnost. Merenja su ponovljena pri temperaturama od 20 do 50 °C; prag nestabilnosti raste za oko 40 % u tom temperaturnom opsegu. Dobijeni rezultati su relevantni za procesovanje prehrambenih i kozmetičkih formulacija na bazi polisaharida.

title: Wall slip quantification in oscillatory shear of concentrated starch suspensions using gap-dependent measurements
abstract: Wall slip was quantified in concentrated maize starch suspensions (40–55 wt%) during oscillatory shear by performing amplitude sweeps at five gap widths between 0.3 and 2.0 mm using a parallel-plate geometry with roughened and smooth surfaces. The apparent storage modulus at γ₀ = 0.1 % decreased by 38 % when the gap was reduced from 2.0 to 0.3 mm on smooth plates, while no gap dependence was observed on sandblasted plates with roughness Ra ≈ 12 μm, confirming that the gap effect is due to wall slip rather than sample heterogeneity. A slip velocity model based on a thin lubrication layer was fitted to the data; the slip layer thickness was estimated at 4–9 μm, increasing with starch concentration. Measurements at 25 and 50 °C showed that the slip contribution is more pronounced below the gelatinisation temperature. These findings have practical implications for the rheological characterisation of starch-based food systems and for the design of mixing equipment.

title: Thixotropic recovery dynamics in dense kaolin suspensions after cessation of large-amplitude oscillatory shear
abstract: The structural recovery of dense kaolin suspensions (φ = 0.42 and 0.50) was studied after pre-conditioning under large-amplitude oscillatory shear at three strain amplitudes (50, 150, 500 %) and two frequencies (0.5 and 5 rad/s). Recovery was monitored by time-resolved small-amplitude oscillatory measurements at γ₀ = 0.1 % for 3600 s following cessation of pre-shear. The storage modulus G' exhibited a two-stage recovery: a rapid initial increase within the first 60–120 s followed by a slower logarithmic growth. Both timescales increased with pre-shear amplitude and decreased with pre-shear frequency. At the highest pre-shear amplitude, recovery to 90 % of the quiescent G' value required between 900 and 2200 s depending on volume fraction. A stretched-exponential function with exponent β in the range 0.35–0.55 provided good fits to the slow-recovery stage. Measurements were repeated after three successive pre-shear–recovery cycles to assess reproducibility; the third cycle produced G' values within 5 % of the first, confirming reversible restructuring. The results are discussed in the context of aggregate break-up and reformation kinetics.

title: Uticaj geometrije elektroda na reološki odgovor elektroreoloških fluida baziranih na čestičnom zeolitu pri naizmeničnom polju
abstract: Ispitivan je elektroreološki (ER) efekat u suspenzijama zeolita tipa NaX (zapreminski udeo 20 %) u silikonskom ulju pri naizmeničnom električnom polju frekvencija 50–1000 Hz i intenziteta 0,5–3,0 kV/mm. Geometrija elektroda (paralelne ploče, cilindri i prstenaste elektrode) sistematski je variirana kako bi se procenio njen uticaj na efektivnu struju smicanja. Merenja su vršena pri amplitudama deformacije 0,5 i 5 % i frekvenciji smicanja 1 Hz. Dinamički prinos napona, definisan kao razlika G' u prisustvu i odsustvu polja, porastao je od 120 Pa pri 0,5 kV/mm do 1850 Pa pri 3,0 kV/mm za paralelne ploče. Prstenaste elektrode dale su za 18–24 % niže vrednosti dinamičkog prinosa pri istim uslovima, što se pripisuje rubnim efektima električnog polja. Rezultati su relevantni za projektovanje prigušivača sa ER fluidima koji rade pod oscilatorno promenljivim opterećenjem.

title: Electropolymerised poly(o-phenylenediamine) imprinted films on gold QCM electrodes for atrazine detection in river water
abstract: Molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) films were prepared by potentiostatic electropolymerisation of o-phenylenediamine in the presence of atrazine as template on gold quartz crystal microbalance electrodes. The influence of monomer-to-template molar ratio (2:1, 5:1, 10:1) on film thickness, measured by QCM-D and AFM, was investigated. Optimal conditions yielded films of 18–22 nm with a root-mean-square roughness below 1.2 nm. Template removal was monitored gravimetrically; approximately 87% removal was achieved after 45 min in acetic acid–methanol (1:9, v/v). Rebinding isotherms in phosphate-buffered saline showed a dissociation constant of 4.3 µM and maximum frequency shift of –42 Hz at saturation. In spiked Danube river water samples, the sensor responded linearly between 0.5 and 25 µM atrazine (R² = 0.994) with a limit of detection of 0.18 µM. Cross-reactivity tests with simazine, prometryn, and chlorpyrifos showed selectivity coefficients below 0.12 for each interferent, confirming adequate selectivity for field-relevant matrices.

title: Effect of self-assembled monolayer chemistry on adhesion and uniformity of spin-coated MIP films for QCM sensing
abstract: The adhesion and morphological uniformity of spin-coated acrylamide-based molecularly imprinted polymer films on quartz crystal microbalance gold surfaces were evaluated as a function of the underlying self-assembled monolayer (SAM) composition. Four SAM chemistries were compared: 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid (MUA), 11-mercapto-1-undecanol (MUO), cysteamine, and 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane (MPTMS, on silica reference substrates). Films were cast from prepolymerisation mixtures containing methacrylic acid as functional monomer and ethylene glycol dimethacrylate as crosslinker, with diclofenac as model template. AFM topographic maps showed that MUA-modified surfaces yielded the most uniform films (Ra = 0.9 ± 0.1 nm) compared to bare gold (Ra = 2.8 ± 0.4 nm). XPS confirmed successful SAM formation and covalent anchoring through ester bond formation. QCM-D dissipation data indicated that MUA-anchored films behaved more rigidly (ΔD/Δf ratio < 5 × 10⁻⁹ Hz⁻¹) than cysteamine-anchored equivalents. Imprinting factors calculated from rebinding experiments were 3.1 for MUA versus 1.8 for cysteamine, demonstrating the practical impact of SAM chemistry on sensing performance.

title: Optimisation of UV-initiated polymerisation conditions for ultrathin MIP coatings on AT-cut quartz resonators
abstract: A systematic study was conducted to identify UV exposure parameters that yield reproducible, ultrathin (<30 nm) molecularly imprinted polymer coatings directly on AT-cut 10 MHz quartz resonators without post-deposition mechanical polishing. Variables included UV intensity (5–20 mW cm⁻²), irradiation time (30–300 s), photoinitiator concentration (0.1–1.0 wt% Irgacure 651 analogue), and prepolymerisation mixture viscosity adjusted with propan-2-ol. Thickness was tracked by QCM baseline shift and cross-validated by ellipsometry on companion silicon wafer coupons. A response-surface design (Box–Behnken, 15 runs) identified 12 mW cm⁻², 90 s, and 0.5 wt% photoinitiator as optimal, yielding a mean dry film thickness of 21 ± 2 nm across eight resonators. Mass sensitivity coefficients were preserved within 2% of uncoated resonators, confirming that the rigid-film approximation remained valid. Atrazine was again used as model analyte; LOD in deionised water was 85 nM, a factor of two improvement over electropolymerised equivalents prepared in parallel, attributed to enhanced template accessibility in thinner films.

title: Antibody-free imprinted receptor layers for estrone detection in drinking water treatment plant effluents
abstract: This study describes the preparation and analytical characterisation of molecularly imprinted polymer receptor layers on 10 MHz QCM sensors for detection of estrone, an endocrine-disrupting steroid hormone, in water treatment plant effluents. Prepolymerisation complexes were characterised by ¹H NMR titration in DMSO-d₆; stoichiometry analysis indicated a 1:2 (estrone:methacrylic acid) complex with a binding constant of 310 M⁻¹. Films were deposited by spin-coating and UV polymerisation. Rebinding experiments in 10% methanol aqueous buffer yielded a linear dynamic range of 5–200 nM with LOD of 1.8 nM (based on three-sigma noise criterion). Endogenous matrix components (humic acid up to 20 mg L⁻¹, Cl⁻ up to 200 mg L⁻¹, Ca²⁺ up to 100 mg L⁻¹) caused frequency shifts below 2 Hz on non-imprinted control sensors and were considered negligible. Recovery experiments in spiked effluent samples (n = 9, three concentration levels) returned mean recoveries of 93–108% with RSDs of 4–11%. The sensor was stable for at least 21 days when stored dry at 4 °C.

title: Template molecule removal from thick MIP films: comparison of solvent washing, electrochemical overoxidation, and proteinase K digestion protocols
abstract: Efficient and reproducible template removal is a critical step in MIP sensor fabrication. This study compared three removal strategies applied to methacrylic acid–EGDMA films (approximately 50 nm dry thickness) imprinted with the herbicide mesotrione: (i) sequential solvent washing (acetic acid–methanol, 1:9, v/v), (ii) electrochemical overoxidation (cyclic voltammetry, 0 to +1.4 V, 10 cycles in 0.1 M H₂SO₄), and (iii) a protease-assisted method adapted from protein epitope imprinting, serving as a reference baseline for non-covalent template disruption. Template removal efficiency was quantified indirectly by frequency recovery (QCM) and directly by HPLC–UV analysis of washing fractions. Solvent washing removed 82 ± 4% of template; electrochemical overoxidation reached 91 ± 3% but altered surface oxidation state as confirmed by XPS C 1s spectra. Protease digestion was inapplicable to small-molecule templates but confirmed complete protein background removal. Extending solvent washing cycles from 3 to 9 improved removal to 90% without the oxidative side effects. Sensors prepared with 9-cycle washing showed imprinting factors of 3.4 ± 0.3 versus 2.7 ± 0.4 for 3-cycle washing, confirming the analytical relevance of thorough template removal.

title: Integration of a flow-through QCM cell with an upstream molecularly imprinted solid-phase extraction module for trace-level chlorpyrifos in irrigation canal water
abstract: A hyphenated system was constructed by coupling a molecularly imprinted polymer solid-phase extraction (MISPE) cartridge directly upstream of a flow-through QCM cell containing a surface-functionalised MIP sensor layer, both imprinted against chlorpyrifos. The MISPE step served as both a preconcentration and matrix cleanup stage, while the QCM provided quantification. Canal water samples collected along the Danube–Tisa–Danube hydrosystem in Vojvodina were processed at 2 mL min⁻¹. The MISPE cartridge (200 mg MIP sorbent) yielded enrichment factors of 85–120× depending on sample turbidity. The combined system produced a working range of 0.5–50 µg L⁻¹ and LOD of 0.18 µg L⁻¹, below the EU maximum residue level for surface water. Analysis of 24 authentic canal samples showed chlorpyrifos concentrations of 0.3–4.6 µg L⁻¹ in 10 of 24 samples. Results were confirmed by GC–MS/MS at an accredited laboratory; Bland–Altman analysis indicated a mean bias of –0.15 µg L⁻¹ and limits of agreement of ±0.9 µg L⁻¹, considered acceptable for field screening.

title: Receptor density and spatial distribution of MIP binding sites on QCM surfaces probed by colloidal gold labelling and SEM imaging
abstract: Understanding the spatial distribution of active binding sites on molecularly imprinted polymer QCM sensors has been limited by the absence of direct imaging methods. A colloidal gold labelling protocol was developed in which 5 nm AuNPs conjugated with the target analyte (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid, 2,4-D) were used as surrogate analyte probes to map binding site locations on MIP-coated QCM surfaces via scanning electron microscopy. Non-imprinted polymer (NIP) surfaces served as controls. On MIP surfaces, AuNP-analogue probe density averaged 340 ± 45 particles µm⁻² versus 38 ± 12 on NIP surfaces, giving an imprinting-attributed density ratio of 8.9. Probe density was spatially heterogeneous, with 2–5 µm domains of elevated binding site concentration correlating with AFM-measured topographic mounds linked to monomer pooling during spin-coating. Edge regions of the 5 mm active area showed 25% lower probe density than the centre. These findings support optimisation of spin-coating angular velocity and prepolymerisation mixture surface tension to improve binding site uniformity, which was demonstrated by reducing angular velocity from 3000 to 1800 rpm, increasing edge-to-centre homogeneity from 75% to 91%.

title: Dual-channel QCM array with molecularly imprinted and immunoaffinity reference channels for field-deployable detection of two sulfonamide antibiotics in groundwater
abstract: A two-channel quartz crystal microbalance array was constructed to allow simultaneous detection of sulfadiazine and sulfamethazine in groundwater with built-in referencing. Channel 1 carried an MIP layer selective for sulfadiazine; Channel 2 carried an MIP layer selective for sulfamethazine. Each channel was paired with an adjacent non-imprinted polymer reference to correct for non-specific matrix adsorption. Functionalisation used MAPTMS silane on SiO₂ QCM surfaces followed by spin-coated UV-polymerised MIP films. A portable readout unit with a Raspberry Pi-based frequency counter was assembled in-house. Field testing was carried out at four groundwater monitoring wells in the Vojvodina plain over three sampling campaigns (May, August, November 2023). Sulfadiazine was detected in two wells at 0.8–2.1 µg L⁻¹; sulfamethazine was below LOD (0.3 µg L⁻¹) at all sites. Cross-channel interference between the two sulfonamides was below 7% in binary mixture experiments up to 10 µg L⁻¹. On-site results agreed within 15% with laboratory LC–MS/MS reference values for 18 of 20 samples.

title: Thermal stability of methacrylic acid–EGDMA MIP films on gold and silicon dioxide QCM surfaces under temperature-cycling conditions relevant to on-site deployments
abstract: Sensor deployments in outdoor water monitoring applications expose QCM transducers to diurnal temperature cycles that may compromise MIP film integrity and baseline stability. This study subjected gold and SiO₂ QCM resonators coated with methacrylic acid–EGDMA MIP films (template: linuron herbicide) to repeated temperature cycles between 5 °C and 45 °C (ramp rate 1 °C min⁻¹, 30 cycles) in a humidity-controlled flow cell. Baseline frequency drift over 30 cycles was 18 ± 4 Hz for gold-substrate sensors and 9 ± 3 Hz for SiO₂-substrate sensors, attributed to differential thermal expansion coefficients of the gold layer amplifying film stress. XPS spectra before and after cycling showed no significant change in O/C ratio, confirming that oxidative degradation did not occur. AFM images revealed sub-nanometre crack formation in the thicker (>40 nm) films on gold after 30 cycles but not in films below 25 nm. Sensitivity to linuron after cycling was retained at 94 ± 5% of initial value for thin films. These results support using thinner films (<25 nm) and SiO₂ substrates for thermally stable outdoor deployments.

title: Molecularly imprinted QCM sensors for micropollutant detection in water: surface chemistry, transducer integration, and field application perspectives
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of the design principles and practical considerations for molecularly imprinted polymer layers on quartz crystal microbalance transducers intended for micropollutant detection in water matrices. The text covers the role of functional monomer selection in forming pre-polymerisation complexes with small-molecule targets, protocols for surface functionalisation of gold and SiO₂ transducer surfaces using thiol-based and silane-based chemistries, deposition methods and their effect on film morphology, and approaches to template removal and rebinding characterisation. A section addresses matrix effects in real water samples—ionic strength, natural organic matter, suspended solids—and mitigation strategies including MIP-SPE preconcentration and differential referencing. Data from peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025 are compiled to assess typical LOD ranges (0.05–5 µM for non-amplified sensors), imprinting factors (1.5–6), and sensor lifetimes (1–8 weeks). The chapter concludes with a discussion of unresolved challenges including long-term stability in saline matrices, miniaturisation toward array formats, and integration with autonomous data transmission for remote monitoring programmes.

title: Angle-resolved diffraction efficiency of embossed optical variable devices: measurement protocol and inter-laboratory comparison
abstract: Optical variable devices (OVDs) embossed on aluminium-metallised film exhibit substantial measurement variability across laboratories owing to differences in goniometric illumination geometry. This paper proposes a standardised angle-resolved measurement protocol and reports results from an inter-laboratory comparison involving five European institutions. Forty OVD specimens covering three grating periods (0.833, 0.714, and 0.556 µm) were distributed to participants. Coefficient of variation for first-order efficiency measurements decreased from 18.3 % under free-form measurement conditions to 4.7 % after adopting the proposed protocol, which fixes illumination at 45°, receiver aperture at 5°, and requires a calibrated reference grating traceable to a national metrology institute. Spectral bandwidth effects were modelled using rigorous coupled-wave analysis and shown to contribute up to 2.1 percentage points of systematic error when broadband sources replace monochromatic illumination. The protocol is compatible with the existing infrastructure of most printing-industry quality-control laboratories.

title: Counterfeit resistance mapping of retail product holograms available in the Serbian market
abstract: A sample of 230 holographic security labels collected from retail pharmaceutical, spirits, and electronics products sold in Serbian markets between 2013 and 2014 was analysed for micro-optical complexity, substrate bonding quality, and resistance to mechanical delamination. Labels were classified into four tiers based on grating spatial frequency, presence of a machine-readable covert feature, tamper-evidence design, and adhesive destruction behaviour. Only 34 % of sampled labels reached Tier 3 or Tier 4, indicating a machine-readable layer. Among pharmaceutical labels, 19 of 56 (34 %) showed grating profiles consistent with second-generation copies identified by an anomalous groove-depth-to-period ratio exceeding 0.55, a signature of contact-copy replication rather than optical recording. The study maps the practical security level of commercially deployed holograms and identifies the covert machine-readable layer as the single most effective discriminating feature against copying, informing procurement specifications for brand owners and regulatory agencies.

title: Fabrication of zero-order covert gratings below 300 nm period by two-photon laser direct writing and reactive ion etching in fused silica
abstract: Covert security gratings with periods below the visible diffraction limit (250 and 280 nm) were fabricated in fused silica substrates using two-photon direct laser writing followed by fluorine-based reactive ion etching. The resulting sub-wavelength surface relief structures produce no visible colour shift under white light but encode a strong polarisation-contrast signal detectable by a hand-held ellipsometric reader. Master quality was verified by cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy, confirming groove depths of 180 ± 8 nm and sidewall angles of 83 ± 2°. Nickel electroforming from the silica master yielded stamper tools with groove-depth standard deviation below 5 nm across a 50 mm × 50 mm active area. Embossed replicas on polycarbonate showed polarisation extinction ratios above 30 dB at 633 nm when read at normal incidence, sufficient for unambiguous binary decoding in a compact reader using a 5 mW diode laser and a crossed analyser pair. The process is transferable to roll-to-roll embossing at linear speeds above 20 m/min.

title: Adhesive-destruction tamper evidence in diffractive labels: peel force, delamination pattern, and re-adhesion detectability
abstract: Tamper-evident diffractive security labels rely on controlled adhesive or interface failure to produce a visible void pattern on removal. This study characterises the peel mechanics and re-adhesion detectability of five commercial label constructions using a motorised peel-test rig at 90° and 180° angles and peel rates of 50 and 300 mm/min. Constructions differed in metal layer splitting design (honeycomb, VOID text, and random-fracture patterns) and substrate thickness (12, 23, and 36 µm polyester). Peel force ranged from 0.8 to 4.1 N/25 mm; higher peel force correlated with larger intact-metal fragment area after removal (r = 0.87). Re-adhesion with a pressure roll was attempted on all removed labels; diffraction efficiency after re-adhesion was reduced by 31–67 % depending on construction, and AFM showed residual adhesive contamination of grating grooves at 0.2–1.8 µm depth. A simple optical detection criterion—reduction in first-order efficiency below 40 % of original—correctly identified 100 % of re-adhered specimens and generated no false positives on 60 intact controls.

title: Inkjet-printed alignment markers for registration of covert grating zones on pharmaceutical blister foil
abstract: Covert diffraction grating zones on pharmaceutical aluminium blister foil require precise in-register placement relative to printed product codes. This study evaluates inkjet-printed UV-fluorescent alignment markers as a low-cost registration aid during roll-to-roll hot embossing. Markers printed with a piezo-drop-on-demand head at 600 dpi on untreated aluminium foil achieved placement repeatability of ±18 µm (3σ) as read by a CCD camera at 10 m/min web speed. Camera-triggered embossing corrections reduced grating zone misregistration from a baseline of ±320 µm to ±35 µm across a 5 000 m production run of 80 µm aluminium foil. Marker ink compatibility with heat-seal lacquer overprint was confirmed by differential scanning calorimetry showing no shift in lacquer glass-transition temperature. The method requires no mechanical modifications to existing embossing equipment and adds estimated 0.003 EUR per unit in consumable cost.

title: Machine-learning-assisted spectral fingerprinting of embossed holographic labels for supply-chain track and trace
abstract: Each embossing cycle introduces deterministic micro-variations in grating groove depth arising from tool wear, temperature gradients, and web tension fluctuations. This study investigates whether these variations constitute a measurable spectral fingerprint sufficient for individual label identification within a production batch. Angle-resolved spectra (400–750 nm, 0.5 nm resolution) were acquired from 3 000 labels produced across three consecutive embossing runs. A convolutional neural network trained on 2 400 spectra correctly assigned held-out labels to their originating 100-label sub-batch with 91.4 % accuracy; a simpler random-forest baseline achieved 83.7 %. Fingerprint stability after 12 months of ambient storage showed a 3.2 % degradation in classification accuracy. The approach does not require any additional printing or marking; the hologram itself serves as the identifier. Integration with a serialised database and mobile reader is described conceptually, with estimated per-label enrolment cost of 0.008 EUR at 10 million labels per year.

title: Comparison of three nanoimprint resist formulations for high-spatial-frequency grating replication at 2400 lines/mm
abstract: Replicating gratings at 2400 lines/mm (period 417 nm) by nanoimprint lithography challenges resist flow into high-aspect-ratio grooves. Three resist formulations—a commercial thermoplastic, a UV-curable hybrid organosilicate, and a lab-synthesised thiol-ene system—were compared on groove fill ratio, pattern collapse rate, and mould release force using a silica master with groove depth 120 nm and sidewall angle 86°. The thiol-ene system achieved the highest fill ratio (96 %) and the lowest collapse rate (2 of 120 tested lines per field), attributed to its low polymerisation shrinkage (1.8 vol%). Release force was 0.41 N/cm², lower than the commercial thermoplastic (0.67 N/cm²). Diffraction efficiency of replicas at first order (532 nm, TE polarisation) was 29.1 %, 31.4 %, and 30.8 % for the three resists respectively, with no statistically significant difference (ANOVA, p = 0.41). The thiol-ene formulation is recommended for spatial frequencies above 2000 lines/mm where pattern collapse is the dominant failure mode.

title: Dual-layer overt/covert holographic patch for wine label authentication: design constraints and reader performance
abstract: A dual-layer holographic patch combining an overt rainbow-shift zone and a covert sub-wavelength grating zone was designed and characterised for application to wine bottle labels in the Serbian and regional premium wine market. The overt zone uses a 1200 lines/mm blazed grating producing a 25° colour sweep from 480 to 650 nm visible to the naked eye. The covert zone consists of a 270 nm period polarisation-grating array readable by the portable reader described in earlier work, producing a binary encoded producer identifier in a 4 × 4 grid. Manufacturing constraints arising from the simultaneous embossing of both zones on 23 µm metallised polyester are analysed: cross-zone groove crosstalk was measured at less than 4 nm depth by AFM when inter-zone gap exceeded 80 µm. Consumer acceptance trials with 94 participants showed 78 % correctly perceived the overt colour shift without instruction. Authentication accuracy with the portable reader was 98.8 % over 720 field scans at three wine fair locations.

title: Reflective colour gamut boundaries of thin-film structural colour filters on flexible polymer substrates
abstract: Structural colour filters based on Fabry–Pérot cavities deposited on flexible polyethylene terephthalate substrates are characterised with respect to achievable reflective colour gamut as a function of cavity material, spacer thickness tolerance, and substrate bending radius. Four cavity configurations—SiO₂/Al, TiO₂/Ag, ZnS/Al, and SiO₂/Ag—with spacer thicknesses from 60 to 380 nm in 20 nm steps were deposited by magnetron sputtering and measured with a spectrophotometer at D65/10°. The SiO₂/Ag configuration at 180 nm spacer produced the widest gamut, covering 61 % of the DCI-P3 area in CIExy. Bending to 10 mm radius caused a peak wavelength shift of 2–4 nm in SiO₂/Ag cavities and 6–9 nm in TiO₂/Ag, attributed to differential strain in the metal layer. Haze increased above 1.5 % only below 5 mm bending radius. The data provide a substrate-strain-aware design envelope for structural colour elements used in flexible brand protection packaging.

title: Automated step-and-repeat layout optimization for label printing with mixed-SKU jobs
abstract: Label converters increasingly run mixed-SKU jobs on a single web, placing multiple label designs in a step-and-repeat grid to minimize substrate waste and plate changes. This paper formulates the layout problem as a two-dimensional strip packing with orientation constraints and color-sequence dependencies. A simulated annealing metaheuristic was implemented and tested on 80 mixed-SKU job specifications drawn from a production log at a regional label converter. Run time on a standard desktop CPU averaged 8.4 seconds per job. Compared to operator-designed layouts, the automated approach reduced substrate waste by 11.2% and decreased the number of color-sequence violations from 14% to 1.3% of jobs. The system outputs an industry-standard CIP4/JDF layout file for direct import into the converter's workflow management system.

title: Merenje kontaktnog ugla na teksturiranim polimernim površinama: poređenje metoda sesile drop i OWRK sa Cassie–Baxter i Wenzel modelima
abstract: Rad analizira primenjivost standardnih modela kvašljivosti (Wenzel i Cassie–Baxter) na mikrostruktururisanim PP površinama dobijenim laserskim graviranjem sa dubinama teksture od 5 do 50 µm i rasporedom tačaka od 100 do 400 dpi. Kontaktni ugao meren je goniometrom na bazi snimanja kapi (metoda sesile drop) korišćenjem deset tečnosti sa poznatim površinskim naponima. Na hrapavijim površinama (Ra > 2,5 µm) izmereni statički kontaktni uglovi za vodu su bili veći od 130°, što ukazuje na prelaz u Cassie–Baxter režim. Poređenjem sa Wenzel modelom, utvrđeno je da on precenjuje kvašljivost za Ra > 1,5 µm. Praktična implikacija je da se kod laserski graviranog PP ambalaže korona doza mora povećati za oko 30 % u odnosu na ravnu foliju kako bi se dostigla ista adhezija boje.

title: Texture-Based Feature Extraction for Solder Paste Inspection Using Classical Machine Learning Classifiers
abstract: This paper investigates feature extraction strategies for classifying solder paste deposits on printed circuit boards prior to component placement. Four classical feature sets were compared—Haralick co-occurrence features, Local Binary Patterns, Gabor filter banks, and raw intensity histograms—across a dataset of 4,200 paste deposit images collected from a single SMT line operating at 40 cm/s belt speed. Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, and k-Nearest Neighbours were trained in a leave-one-board-out cross-validation scheme. Haralick features combined with an RBF-kernel SVM achieved the highest F1-score of 0.893 on the defect class, outperforming raw histogram features by 11.4 percentage points. Computational timing showed that all pipelines could process one inspection image in under 45 ms on a 2010-era dual-core workstation, satisfying inline inspection throughput requirements. The study establishes a baseline for subsequent deep-learning comparisons and identifies lighting inconsistency as the dominant source of misclassification.

title: Effect of Reflow Profile Variation on Through-Hole and SMT Joint Morphology: An Image-Based Statistical Study
abstract: Solder joint geometry changes measurably when reflow oven temperature profiles are varied within production-allowed tolerances. This study quantifies those geometric changes using 2D cross-sectional optical micrographs of 1,080 joints sampled across six reflow profiles spanning peak temperatures of 235°C to 252°C and soak durations of 60 s to 120 s. Eleven morphological descriptors—including fillet height, contact angle, void fraction estimated from thresholded cross-sections, and aspect ratio—were computed automatically using a custom segmentation pipeline. ANOVA tests showed that peak temperature accounted for 38% of fillet-height variance while soak duration had a statistically significant effect on void fraction (p < 0.01). The results are presented as a reference dataset for machine-learning researchers seeking ground-truth labels linked to controlled process parameters, and the dataset was deposited in a publicly accessible repository. No classification model is trained here; the contribution is purely descriptive and metrological.

title: Transfer Learning from ImageNet-Pretrained Networks for Low-Volume SMT Defect Datasets
abstract: In surface-mount technology inspection scenarios, labelled defect images are often scarce because certain defect types appear rarely in production. This paper examines whether features extracted from networks pretrained on a large general-purpose image corpus can be repurposed for solder joint classification when only 200–800 labelled domain images per class are available. Three pretrained backbone architectures were fine-tuned with varying proportions of frozen layers on a proprietary dataset of 5,600 images covering five defect classes. Fine-tuning only the final two convolutional blocks consistently produced higher validation F1 scores than full-network fine-tuning when fewer than 400 images per class were available, with improvements of 4.2 to 7.8 percentage points. The gain diminished and reversed beyond 600 samples per class. Experiments also reveal that batch normalisation statistics inherited from pretraining create a measurable calibration mismatch when applied to X-ray images, which differ texturally from optical images. Recommendations for practitioners are provided.
venue: International Journal of Computer-Aided Quality Engineering

title: Domain Shift in AOI Systems: Quantifying the Performance Degradation When Models Are Deployed Across Different PCB Assembly Lines
abstract: Automated optical inspection models trained on data from one SMT production line frequently underperform when deployed on a different line, even within the same factory, due to differences in camera optics, illumination geometry, and conveyor vibration. This study measures that degradation empirically using models trained on data from Line A and tested on Lines B and C, where all three lines produce nominally identical assemblies. Overall accuracy dropped from 94.3% (same-line evaluation) to 78.1% and 71.6% for the two target lines. Per-class analysis showed that class-conditional feature distributions shifted significantly for reflective component types (measured by maximum mean discrepancy). Four unsupervised domain adaptation strategies—instance reweighting, subspace alignment, correlation alignment, and adversarial feature alignment—were then applied without accessing target-domain labels. Adversarial alignment recovered 10.8 percentage points of the accuracy drop on Line C, while subspace alignment was most effective on Line B. The findings motivate a line-specific adaptation protocol.

title: Prototype Networks for One-Shot Solder Joint Classification Under Component Morphology Variation
abstract: Prototype-based meta-learning was applied to the problem of classifying solder joints for component package types that were absent during model training. A meta-training set was constructed from images of 23 component package types (SOT-23, QFN, TQFP, SOP, and others), and the model was evaluated in 5-way 1-shot and 5-way 5-shot episodes on four held-out package types not seen during meta-training. The prototypical network reached 71.4% accuracy in the 1-shot setting and 83.2% in the 5-shot setting, compared to 58.9% and 76.1% for a fine-tuned baseline requiring the same number of support samples. Ablation experiments indicate that the choice of distance metric (cosine vs. Euclidean) had a larger effect on performance than the embedding backbone depth, within the range tested. The study uses a dataset of 41,000 images collected from two production facilities and provides split specifications for reproducibility.

title: Batch Normalisation Adaptation Strategies for Cross-Domain CNN Deployment in Solder Inspection
abstract: Batch normalisation layers accumulate running statistics during training that are mismatched to target-domain data at inference time, contributing to accuracy degradation in cross-line and cross-factory deployments. This paper compares four lightweight adaptation strategies that adjust BN statistics using small unlabelled batches from the target domain: (1) full statistics reset using target data, (2) exponential moving average update with varying momentum, (3) per-layer selective reset guided by domain discrepancy scores, and (4) no adaptation baseline. Experiments were conducted across three source–target line pairs with domain gap sizes ranging from small to large, quantified by the A-distance proxy. Selective per-layer reset using a domain discrepancy threshold of 0.15 provided the best trade-off, recovering between 6.1 and 13.4 accuracy points with as few as 64 unlabelled target images. The method requires no retraining and adds negligible inference latency. Practical deployment guidelines are included.

title: Sim-to-Real Transfer for SMT Inspection: Evaluating Synthetic Training Data Generated from 3D Component Models
abstract: Acquiring large labelled datasets from real production lines is slow and expensive. This study evaluates whether synthetic AOI images rendered from parametric 3D models of SMT components and solder joints can supplement or replace real training data. A renderer was configured with randomised lighting direction, camera angle perturbations of ±5°, and procedurally varied solder fillet shapes parameterised by contact angle and height drawn from production measurement distributions. Three experimental conditions were compared: training on synthetic only, training on real only (10,000 images), and training on combined data. On a real-image test set, synthetic-only training yielded 67.3% accuracy, real-only yielded 91.8%, and combined training reached 93.6%, suggesting a complementary role for synthetic data when real data volume is limited. Per-defect analysis shows synthetic data helps most for tombstoning, where real defect examples are underrepresented. Renderer parameter sensitivity is analysed.

title: Few-Shot Learning for X-Ray Solder Joint Inspection: Benchmark and Baseline Results
abstract: X-ray imaging reveals internal voids, cold joints, and bridging defects invisible to optical AOI, but labelled X-ray datasets are even scarcer than optical ones due to equipment cost and radiation-safety constraints on continuous acquisition. This paper introduces a benchmark dataset of 9,800 2D X-ray images of BGAs and QFNs with per-joint labels verified by cross-sectional destructive analysis on a 5% sample. Six few-shot learning methods—prototypical networks, matching networks, MAML, relation networks, and two fine-tuning baselines—are evaluated in 5-way 1-shot, 5-shot, and 10-shot episodes. Across all episode configurations, MAML achieved the highest accuracy (up to 87.1% at 10-shot) but required 4.3× more meta-training computation than prototypical networks. The benchmark protocol, episode sampling code, and all baseline model weights are released under an open licence to facilitate comparisons.

title: Domain-Adaptive Feature Alignment with Class-Conditional Prototypes for Multi-Line SMT Inspection
abstract: This paper proposes a domain adaptation method that aligns feature distributions across multiple SMT production lines while preserving class-discriminative structure. The approach maintains a set of class-conditional prototype vectors updated online from labelled source data and unlabelled target batches. Alignment is enforced by minimising the Wasserstein distance between source and target prototype neighborhoods rather than aligning marginal distributions globally, which avoids collapsing class boundaries. Experiments span five source–target line pair combinations with varying degrees of domain gap. The method achieves mean accuracy of 91.2% across target lines compared to 88.7% for adversarial domain adaptation and 84.3% for no adaptation. The prototype update mechanism requires no additional labelled target samples. Computational overhead at inference is under 3 ms per image on the test GPU. An ablation study examines the sensitivity to prototype momentum and Wasserstein regularisation weight.

title: Few-Shot and Transfer Learning for Visual Inspection in Electronics Manufacturing
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of few-shot learning and transfer learning to automated visual inspection tasks in electronics manufacturing, with a focus on PCB assembly and SMT processes. The text is structured around three themes: (i) the taxonomy of data-scarcity scenarios that arise in production—new product introductions, rare defect classes, equipment changeovers—and how each maps to a different learning problem; (ii) a review of published methods categorised by inductive bias and data requirement; and (iii) practical implementation considerations including dataset construction, annotation strategies, and calibration of deployed models. Results from the authors' own production-environment studies are used as running examples throughout. The chapter concludes with an analysis of open problems, including the lack of standardised benchmarks, the treatment of class imbalance in meta-learning episodes, and the integration of inspection models into closed-loop process control systems.

title: Continual Learning Strategies for SMT Inspection Models Facing Gradual Component Portfolio Changes
abstract: SMT inspection systems must cope with gradual portfolio changes as product lines evolve: new component packages are introduced, old ones are retired, and existing defect distributions shift with supplier changes. This paper evaluates five continual learning strategies—elastic weight consolidation, progressive neural networks, replay buffers, learning-without-forgetting, and a fine-tuning lower bound—on a longitudinal dataset spanning 18 months of production from a single factory, covering 31 incremental data release events. Metrics include accuracy on the current task, backwards transfer (forgetting), and forward transfer to new classes. Replay-based methods controlled forgetting most effectively, keeping backwards transfer loss below 3.1% across all event sequences, but required a memory buffer storing 4.8% of historical images. EWC degraded on later tasks when the number of accumulated constraints grew large. The study provides a timeline-respecting evaluation protocol that avoids leaking future data into earlier training periods.

title: Identifying Undefined-Behaviour Patterns in NumPy Array Operations Through Symbolic Execution
abstract: Numerical Python code frequently triggers undefined or surprising behaviour when array shapes do not match, integer overflow occurs in index arithmetic, or broadcasting rules are applied unexpectedly. We developed a symbolic execution engine, called ArraySym, that tracks symbolic shape expressions and numerical ranges for NumPy arrays through sequences of operations. The engine encodes shape constraints as systems of linear integer arithmetic formulas and discharges them with the Z3 SMT solver. We applied ArraySym to 890 Python scripts extracted from course homework repositories at three South-East European universities, finding 312 shape-mismatch sites and 57 integer-overflow sites. Comparison against runtime execution revealed that 89 % of the flagged shape mismatches would have raised exceptions on at least one test input. The paper describes the constraint encoding for eleven NumPy operations, discusses scalability limitations for loops with symbolic iteration counts, and outlines a repair sketch generation procedure that corrects reshape calls automatically.

title: Continuous activity recognition under open-set conditions: rejecting unknown classes in wrist IMU streams
abstract: Most deployed activity recognition models operate under the closed-set assumption, meaning every inference window is assigned to one of the training classes. In practice, wrist-worn devices encounter movement patterns absent from training data. This paper evaluates four open-set rejection strategies—softmax thresholding, OpenMax, energy-based scoring, and a lightweight prototype-distance classifier—applied to a 1-D depthwise-separable CNN. The evaluation uses a dataset of ten known activities augmented with six unknown activity classes recorded from 20 additional subjects, totalling 31 hours. AUROC for distinguishing known from unknown windows ranges from 0.76 (softmax threshold) to 0.88 (energy-based scoring). Prototype-distance rejection achieves AUROC 0.86 with 4% lower known-class accuracy cost than energy scoring and adds only 6 KB of RAM overhead, making it suitable for Cortex-M deployment. Rejection thresholds calibrated at 5% false-rejection rate on a validation set are provided.

title: Interference Graph Colouring Under Heterogeneous Register-File Constraints for Sparse Tensor Cores
abstract: Tensor accelerators often expose multiple register files with different widths and access latencies, one set for dense accumulators and another for sparse index buffers. Classical graph-colouring register allocation assumes a uniform register file, and adapting it to heterogeneous files requires modifications to both the interference graph construction and the colouring heuristic. This paper presents a two-phase allocation algorithm: the first phase colours accumulator-class values using a Chaitin–Briggs-style approach on a subgraph restricted to accumulator registers; the second phase handles index-class values using a bipartite matching formulation. Tested on a cycle-accurate model of a custom tensor core with 48 accumulator registers and 64 index registers, the algorithm reduces register-file conflict stalls by 34% compared with a single-phase allocator that treats all registers uniformly. Compilation overhead is below 5% in all tested kernels.

title: Structured Authoring Frameworks for Multilingual Safety Data Sheets: A Comparative Study of DITA and DocBook Implementations
abstract: Safety data sheets (SDS) required under the EU REACH regulation must be produced in the official language of each target market, creating significant authoring and layout overhead for manufacturers. This study compared two XML-based structured authoring approaches—DITA 1.2 and DocBook 5.0—applied to a corpus of 48 SDS documents covering 12 chemical substance categories. Evaluation criteria included translation memory leverage rate, reuse of common content blocks, layout fidelity after automatic PDF rendering, and time-to-production per language variant. DITA achieved a mean content reuse rate of 61% across language variants, compared to 44% for DocBook, while DocBook produced more predictable page-break behaviour in multi-column layouts. Both frameworks required custom stylesheets to meet the minimum font-size and pictogram-size requirements set out in Annex II of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. The paper provides a decision matrix to guide medium-sized chemical manufacturers in selecting a framework based on translation volume and in-house IT capability.

title: Colour Accuracy of GHS Hazard Pictograms Reproduced Across Offset, Digital Electrophotographic, and Inkjet Print Processes
abstract: The Globally Harmonised System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS) prescribes specific visual requirements for hazard pictograms, including a red diamond border of defined minimum reflectance contrast. This study measured the colorimetric reproduction of all nine GHS pictograms printed by three process technologies—sheet-fed offset (four-colour), digital electrophotographic (toner-based), and wide-format inkjet—across five substrate types including uncoated label stock and polyethylene film. Measurements used a spectrophotometer under D50 illuminant and followed ISO 13655:2009 geometry. The red border ΔE00 deviation relative to the GHS reference value ranged from 1.8 (offset on coated stock) to 7.4 (inkjet on polyethylene film). Symbol legibility was assessed by five trained evaluators using a structured checklist. Results indicate that inkjet on non-absorptive substrates requires ICC profile adjustment and substrate priming to meet pictogram contrast requirements. Practical guidance for label printers is provided.

title: Automation of Variable-Data Label Composition for Food Products Under EU 1169/2011 Nutrition Labelling Rules
abstract: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers specifies minimum type sizes, mandatory field ordering, and legibility requirements that interact non-trivially with the variable nutritional data generated per product variant. This paper describes a rule-based composition engine developed to automate the layout of back-of-pack nutrition panels for a set of 320 product variants from three food categories (dairy, bakery, and meat products). The engine was implemented in Python 3.4 using a custom constraint solver that iteratively reduces font sizes and column widths while verifying compliance with the 1.2 mm x-height requirement. Out of 320 test labels, 94% were produced without manual intervention; the remaining 6% failed due to extreme values in the allergen field. Processing time averaged 0.8 seconds per label on commodity hardware. The paper discusses integration with ERP-sourced ingredient databases and the conditions under which fully automated compliance cannot be guaranteed.

title: Evaluation of PDF/X-4 and PDF/A-3 as Archival and Exchange Formats for Regulatory Label Artwork Files
abstract: Regulatory label artwork files must satisfy two partially conflicting requirements: reliable reproduction across print providers (exchange function) and long-term readability independent of proprietary software (archival function). This paper evaluates PDF/X-4 and PDF/A-3 against both requirements using a test set of 80 label artwork files collected from four label printing companies in Serbia and Hungary. Compliance was verified using three independent PDF validators; rendering fidelity was assessed by comparing rasterised outputs at 1200 dpi. PDF/X-4 passed exchange-function checks in 97.5% of files but failed archival requirements in 31% due to embedded proprietary ICC profiles and non-embedded fonts. PDF/A-3 satisfied archival requirements in 88.75% of files after conversion but introduced visible colour shifts in 14% of spot-colour elements. A hybrid workflow is proposed in which a PDF/X-4 master is accompanied by a PDF/A-3 derivative at sign-off, with an XML sidecar recording the colour conversion parameters applied.

title: Print Workflow Bottlenecks in Short-Run Compliance Label Production: A Process Mining Approach
abstract: Short-run label jobs for regulated products—typically 50–500 copies per variant—present different workflow challenges from high-volume label production. This paper applies process mining techniques to event log data extracted from the MIS systems of two label printing companies, covering 1,840 job tickets processed over 18 months. Process discovery using the Inductive Miner algorithm identified nine distinct workflow variants, of which three accounted for 78% of all jobs. Conformance checking against a normative reference model revealed that regulatory artwork approval steps were bypassed in 12.3% of jobs, typically under schedule pressure. Performance analysis showed that manual preflighting of customer-supplied artwork was the single largest contributor to lead-time variance (CV = 0.74), exceeding press make-ready time. The paper proposes a triage-based automated preflight rule set specifically tuned for compliance label files and estimates a 22% reduction in approval cycle time based on simulation.

title: Implementing the Unique Device Identifier (UDI) on Medical Device Labels: Layout Constraints and Data Carrier Selection
abstract: The EU Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745 requires that device labels carry a Unique Device Identifier encoded in a human-readable form and in at least one automatic identification and data capture (AIDC) carrier. This chapter reviews the layout constraints that UDI placement introduces on labels for three device categories—implantable devices, reusable surgical instruments, and in vitro diagnostic devices—and analyses the trade-offs between GS1 DataMatrix, PDF417, and QR Code as AIDC carriers with respect to printable area, substrate, and minimum module size requirements. A survey of 14 Serbian medical device manufacturers conducted in 2021 (n = 14 QA and regulatory affairs managers) found that 64% had not yet determined their AIDC carrier at the time of the survey, and 43% were unaware of the ISO/IEC 15415 print quality verification requirement. The chapter includes worked layout examples and a decision flowchart for carrier selection.

title: Consistency of Hazard and Precautionary Statement Translations on CLP Labels Sold in Serbian Retail: A Content Analysis
abstract: Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP) requires that hazard (H) and precautionary (P) statements appear on labels in the official language of the country of sale. Serbia, as a candidate country, has transposed CLP into national legislation, but enforcement capacity is limited. This study performed a content analysis of CLP labels on 210 consumer chemical products (cleaning agents, adhesives, paints) purchased from five retail chains in Novi Sad in 2022. Labels were photographed and the Serbian translations of H and P statements were compared against the official reference translations published by the Agency for Chemicals of the Republic of Serbia. Deviations were classified as: wrong statement number (3.4%), mistranslation affecting meaning (8.1%), truncation (11.9%), and font-size non-compliance (17.6%). Products imported from non-EU countries showed significantly higher error rates across all categories (χ² = 18.3, p < 0.001). The paper discusses implications for national market surveillance.

title: Automating Cross-Regulation Conflict Detection in Multi-Market Product Label Templates Using Rule-Based NLP
abstract: A product sold simultaneously in the EU, the UK, and Serbia may need to comply with three overlapping but non-identical labelling regimes. When a single label template is prepared for multi-market use, conflicts between regulatory requirements—such as differing mandatory statement orderings or incompatible minimum font-size thresholds—must be identified before artwork is finalised. This paper describes a rule-based natural language processing pipeline that ingests a label template marked up in an extended DITA schema and checks it against a structured database of 214 labelling rules drawn from CLP, UK CHIP 2015, EU 1169/2011, and Serbian transpositions. The rule database was built manually and validated against 30 reference label specimens. Applied to a test set of 55 multi-market template files, the pipeline detected 83% of manually identified conflicts (precision 0.79, recall 0.83) with a mean processing time of 4.2 seconds per template. False positives were most frequent in optional advisory statement fields. The paper discusses the limits of rule coverage for dynamically updated regulations.

title: Brachial artery flow-mediated dilation as an early marker of endothelial dysfunction in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetic patients
abstract: This cross-sectional study assessed flow-mediated dilation (FMD) of the brachial artery using high-resolution B-mode ultrasound in 58 patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and 54 age- and sex-matched normoglycaemic controls recruited from the Endocrinology Clinic of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. FMD was measured following a standard 5-minute forearm cuff occlusion protocol. Mean FMD in the T2DM group was 4.2 ± 1.3% compared with 7.8 ± 1.6% in controls (p < 0.001). Fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, and insulin resistance index (HOMA-IR) correlated inversely with FMD (r = −0.54, −0.61, and −0.48, respectively; all p < 0.01). Nitroglycerin-mediated dilation did not differ significantly between groups, suggesting endothelium-dependent rather than smooth muscle dysfunction as the predominant mechanism. These findings indicate that measurable impairment of endothelial vasodilatory capacity precedes overt macrovascular complications and is detectable at diagnosis, underscoring the potential clinical utility of FMD as a non-invasive screening index in early T2DM.

title: Plasma nitric oxide metabolites and superoxide dismutase activity in patients with metabolic syndrome: a comparative study
abstract: Forty-two subjects meeting the IDF criteria for metabolic syndrome (MetS) and 40 healthy volunteers were enrolled to compare circulating nitric oxide metabolite concentrations (nitrite/nitrate; NOx) and erythrocyte superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity. Plasma NOx was measured by the Griess colorimetric method after cadmium reduction. SOD activity was determined by an inhibition assay using xanthine oxidase as the superoxide-generating system. Subjects with MetS showed significantly lower plasma NOx (18.4 ± 4.7 µmol/L versus 31.2 ± 6.1 µmol/L; p < 0.001) and reduced SOD activity (12.1 ± 2.8 U/mg Hb versus 18.6 ± 3.4 U/mg Hb; p < 0.001) compared with controls. After adjusting for waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, and triglycerides in a multivariate regression, both NOx and SOD remained independent predictors of the MetS diagnosis. The results support a model in which oxidative quenching of nitric oxide contributes to reduced bioavailability independently of hyperglycaemia per se.

title: eNOS uncoupling and tetrahydrobiopterin depletion in the aortic endothelium of streptozotocin-treated rats: temporal profile over 12 weeks
abstract: The study tracked endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) coupling status and tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) levels in the thoracic aorta of male Wistar rats at 2, 4, 8, and 12 weeks after streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetes (55 mg/kg i.p.; n = 8 per time point) and in age-matched controls (n = 8 per time point). eNOS dimer-to-monomer ratio was assessed by low-temperature SDS-PAGE and western blot. BH4 was quantified by HPLC with fluorescence detection. Superoxide production was measured by lucigenin-enhanced chemiluminescence. The dimer-to-monomer ratio fell progressively from 4.1 ± 0.4 at baseline to 1.3 ± 0.3 at 12 weeks in diabetic animals (p < 0.001). BH4 content dropped by 68% at 12 weeks versus controls. Lucigenin signal in the aortic rings was 2.8-fold higher in the diabetic group at week 12. Supplementation with sepiapterin (a BH4 precursor) partially restored the dimer-to-monomer ratio at week 8, supporting the hypothesis that BH4 oxidation is a central driver of eNOS uncoupling in this model.
