title: Thermal boundary condition estimation from weld electrical signals: a Kalman filter approach
abstract: Knowledge of the effective thermal boundary condition at the workpiece—determined by fixture contact, clamping force, and underlying structure—is rarely available directly in production but strongly influences weld quality. This paper presents a Kalman filter-based observer that estimates an effective heat-transfer coefficient at the workpiece underside from arc voltage, current, and wire feed rate measurements recorded during welding, using a reduced-order thermal model as the process model. The observer was validated on 48 welds where ground-truth heat-transfer coefficients were set by controlled air-gap fixtures with known thermal resistance. Estimated coefficients fell within 12 % of ground truth in 40 of 48 cases. The observer converged within the first 80 mm of weld length. Integration with a travel-speed adaptive controller demonstrated a 31 % reduction in penetration variability compared to a controller operating without boundary condition estimates.

title: A lightweight digital-shadow architecture for small and medium-sized manufacturers: design principles and a reference implementation
abstract: Full digital-twin deployments require infrastructure investments that many small and medium-sized manufacturers cannot sustain. This paper proposes a lightweight digital-shadow architecture in which a discrete-event simulation model is updated periodically—rather than continuously—from data extracted via low-cost IoT sensors and an open-source data broker. The architecture targets a 72-hour planning horizon and uses a one-hour update cycle. A reference implementation was deployed at a 35-employee metal subcontractor producing custom hydraulic manifold assemblies. Sensors comprised eight cycle-count readers on existing pneumatic press buttons and two RFID readers at buffer entry and exit points, totalling hardware cost below €1 800. Over a 10-week trial, the shadow-based shift plan achieved 89% on-time delivery against a baseline of 74%. The paper discusses the trade-off between update frequency and model accuracy and provides a decision checklist for architecture configuration.

title: Cyclostationary Analysis of Bearing Fault Signatures Under Time-Varying Speed Conditions
abstract: Bearing faults in variable-speed drives produce cyclostationary vibration signatures whose characteristic frequencies shift with rotational speed, complicating conventional envelope analysis. This study applied the cyclic spectral coherence (CSC) and the cyclic modulation spectrum to vibration data collected from a 7.5 kW induction motor test rig instrumented with three piezoelectric accelerometers during run-up and coast-down sequences spanning 800 to 2800 rpm. Outer-race and inner-race defects were seeded on identical SKF-class bearings using electro-discharge machining to produce controlled spall areas of 3 mm² and 8 mm². The angle-time resampling was performed using a tacho pulse from an optical encoder at 3600 pulses per revolution. Cyclic spectral coherence maps identified outer-race faults at signal-to-noise ratios as low as −6 dB, whereas envelope spectrum analysis failed below 0 dB SNR. Detection probability exceeded 91% across all tested speeds for the 8 mm² defect. The paper provides a practical resampling workflow and discusses sensitivity to encoder jitter.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Time-Frequency Representations for Non-Stationary Vibro-Acoustic Signals
abstract: Selecting an appropriate time-frequency representation (TFR) for transient and non-stationary industrial vibro-acoustic signals remains largely empirical. This chapter reviews and compares five TFRs—short-time Fourier transform (STFT), Wigner–Ville distribution (WVD), smoothed pseudo-WVD, S-transform, and empirical mode decomposition-based Hilbert spectrum—applied to a common dataset of 240 labelled vibration records from a compressor station in the petrochemical sector. Records were labelled for four fault classes and one healthy class by domain engineers. Evaluation criteria include time-frequency resolution, cross-term suppression, computational cost, and classification accuracy when the TFR output fed a random forest classifier with fixed hyperparameters. The S-transform and smoothed pseudo-WVD achieved the best balance between resolution and cross-term suppression; however, the STFT remained competitive for classification (88.3% accuracy) at a fraction of the computational cost. The chapter concludes with practical selection guidelines indexed to fault class and available compute budget.

title: Blind Source Separation of Simultaneously Active Acoustic Emissions in a Multi-Machine Workshop Environment
abstract: Industrial workshops operate multiple machines concurrently, making it difficult to attribute acoustic emission (AE) events to specific sources for fault localisation. This paper presents a second-order blind identification (SOBI) approach applied to signals recorded by an eight-channel AE sensor array distributed across the floor of a metalworking workshop hosting three CNC milling centres and one hydraulic press. Measurements spanning four hours captured 1,142 AE bursts. SOBI was initialised with a spatial pre-whitening step derived from idle-state noise to improve conditioning of the covariance matrix. Source attribution was validated by deliberate sequential shutdown of each machine. Attribution accuracy reached 87% for the milling centres and 94% for the hydraulic press. Computational latency per 0.5 s analysis window was 23 ms on a standard workstation, suggesting near-real-time feasibility. The paper also reports on the sensitivity of SOBI to sensor placement geometry, quantified through a leave-one-sensor-out experiment.

title: Spectral Kurtosis Mapping for Early Detection of Cavitation in Centrifugal Pumps
abstract: Cavitation in centrifugal pumps generates broadband, impulsive pressure fluctuations that are masked by structural vibration and hydraulic noise at early onset. This study applied spectral kurtosis (SK) computed via the fast kurtogram to vibration signals from a 22 kW centrifugal pump tested at flow rates between 40% and 110% of best-efficiency-point (BEP). Cavitation was characterised visually through a transparent pump casing and quantified by the net positive suction head available (NPSHa). At 80% BEP, SK maps identified impulsive content in the 6–8 kHz band at NPSHa margins as large as 1.4 m above the critical cavitation threshold, while the broadband RMS level showed no significant change. The optimal demodulation band selected by the kurtogram was used to compute envelope spectra, which displayed sidebands at blade-pass frequency. Results from 60 independent runs were pooled to estimate detection probability and false alarm rate across the NPSHa range. Early detection was achieved with a probability of 0.84 at a false alarm rate below 0.07.

title: Performance of Sparse Recovery Algorithms for Underdetermined Blind Source Separation in Noisy Industrial Conditions
abstract: When fewer sensors than sources are available, the mixing system is underdetermined and standard ICA fails. This paper evaluates three sparse recovery strategies—basis pursuit denoising (BPDN), orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), and a morphological component analysis (MCA) variant—for separating vibro-acoustic signals from four rotating machines observed through two accelerometers mounted on a common gantry frame. Synthetic mixtures were constructed from independently recorded single-source signals with empirically measured mixing coefficients, enabling ground-truth comparison. Ambient noise was added at SNR levels of 0, 5, and 10 dB. At 10 dB SNR, MCA achieved a median SDR of 7.3 dB versus 5.8 dB for BPDN and 4.2 dB for OMP. Computational cost of MCA was approximately 12× higher than OMP per frame. The paper includes a sensitivity analysis showing that mixing matrix estimation errors above 8° degrade all three methods comparably. Practical recommendations are given for sensor placement to minimise mixing condition number.

title: Influence of Sensor Placement Geometry on Blind Separation Quality for Distributed Vibration Sources
abstract: Multi-channel vibration measurements for blind source separation are sensitive to the geometric arrangement of sensors relative to the source distribution, yet practical placement is often constrained by machine geometry. This study conducted a systematic experiment using a configurable aluminium test frame instrumented with up to twelve accelerometer positions in six predefined layouts. Four electrodynamic shakers served as controllable, independent vibration sources with bandlimited random excitation between 50 and 5000 Hz. FastICA and SOBI were applied to each layout for source separation, and separation quality was quantified by SDR and the inter-channel interference measure. Layouts with maximum angular spread between sensors consistently outperformed compact clusters by 3–6 dB in SDR. For SOBI, the benefit was maintained even at SNR of 0 dB, while FastICA showed degraded robustness. A simple placement quality index based on the condition number of the empirical mixing matrix is proposed, requiring only idle-state measurements. The index predicted poor-separation configurations with 89% accuracy across 144 tested layout-excitation combinations.

title: Tracking Spectral Changes in Compressor Discharge Noise During Thermal Transients Using Adaptive Short-Time Analysis
abstract: Reciprocating compressors exhibit systematic shifts in discharge valve noise spectra during thermal warm-up, which can mask or mimic incipient valve faults if a fixed analysis window is used. This paper proposes an adaptive STFT framework in which window length and overlap are updated at each frame using a local non-stationarity index derived from the instantaneous frequency variance of dominant tonal components. The approach was tested on 90-minute continuous recordings from a two-cylinder oil-free compressor during cold start from 5°C to steady-state operating temperature. Discharge valve click frequencies drifted by up to 340 Hz during warm-up. The adaptive method tracked this drift with a mean absolute frequency error of 18 Hz, compared to 87 Hz for a fixed 1024-point window at 51.2 kHz. False fault indications triggered by thermal drift were reduced from eleven to two over the recording set. The paper includes a lightweight real-time implementation running on an embedded ARM processor with 12 ms latency per frame.

title: Association between porcine parvovirus serostatus and reproductive outcomes in multiparous sows: a cross-sectional study on commercial farms in northern Serbia
abstract: This cross-sectional study investigated the association between porcine parvovirus (PPV) serostatus and reproductive performance indicators in multiparous sows on eight commercial farrow-to-finish farms in the Vojvodina region. A total of 228 sows were sampled at weaning, and reproductive records covering the previous three parities were extracted from farm management software. Seropositivity was determined by blocking ELISA with a cut-off S/P ratio of ≤0.4. PPV-seropositive sows had a significantly higher rate of mummified piglets per litter (mean 0.87 vs. 0.31; p < 0.01) and a lower total number of piglets born alive (10.2 vs. 11.1; p = 0.03) compared to seronegative animals. Logistic regression controlling for parity, farm, and season identified PPV seropositivity as an independent predictor of litter mummification (OR 2.84; 95% CI 1.61–5.03). These findings confirm a measurable reproductive penalty attributable to active PPV circulation even in partly vaccinated herds and support the case for systematic serological monitoring before breeding.

title: Procena titra neutrališućih antitela kod krmača vakcinisanih protiv parvovirusa svinja različitim komercijalnim vakcinama u uslovima terenske primene
abstract: Istraživanje je sprovedeno u cilju poređenja titra neutrališućih antitela (VN titar) kod krmača imunizovanih sa tri komercijalne inaktivisane PPV vakcine (označene kao V1, V2 i V3) u uslovima terenske primene na dve intenzivne farme u Srbiji. Ukupno 180 krmača podeljeno je u tri grupe od po 60 grla, vakcinisane po preporučenom protokolu proizvođača. Serum je uzorkovan pre vakcinacije, 28 dana nakon primarne vakcinacije i pred svako parenje. VN testovi rađeni su na ćelijskim kulturama SK-6. Sva tri preparata izazvala su signifikantan porast titra (p < 0,001), pri čemu je vakcina V2 postigla statistički viši geometrijski srednji titar 28. dana (GMT 1:1024) u poređenju sa V1 (GMT 1:512) i V3 (GMT 1:448). Razlika u titrovima između farmi bila je manja od razlike između vakcina, što ukazuje da je izbor preparata važniji faktor od uslova gajenja. Rezultati pružaju praktičnu osnovu za izbor vakcinalnog protokola.

title: Comparison of indirect ELISA and serum neutralisation for PRRSV-1 antibody detection in field serum samples from Serbian swine herds
abstract: Accurate serological detection of PRRS virus type 1 (PRRSV-1) is central to herd health monitoring in central and eastern Europe, yet the concordance of available assays has not been systematically evaluated in Serbian field conditions. We compared a commercially available indirect ELISA kit with an in-house serum neutralisation (SN) assay using a local PRRSV-1 isolate on 196 serum samples from 11 farms in Vojvodina. Overall agreement was 83.7% (kappa = 0.67; 95% CI 0.57–0.76), indicating substantial but imperfect concordance. Discordant results were concentrated in samples with low ELISA S/P ratios (0.4–0.6), where SN titres were predominantly below 1:8. The ELISA showed sensitivity of 91.2% and specificity of 78.4% relative to SN as reference. These data suggest that sole reliance on ELISA may overestimate true seroprevalence in low-exposure herds. A confirmatory SN step is advisable for borderline ELISA-positive samples when outbreak investigation or vaccine efficacy assessment is the objective.

title: Reproduktivni neuspeh krmača uzrokovan simultanom infekcijom PPV i PRRSV: patološki nalaz i serologiski profil zahvaćenih jata
abstract: Ko-infekcija parvovirusom svinja (PPV) i virusom reproduktivnog i respiratornog sindroma svinja (PRRSV) opisana je eksperimentalno, ali podaci iz terenskih uslova u Srbiji su retki. U ovoj studiji ispitali smo tri farme u Vojvodini kod kojih je 2019. godine registrovan naglo povećan broj mumificiranih i mrtvorođenih prasadi. Patohistološki pregled materijala iz pobačenih plodova i mrtvorođenih prasadi (n = 47 tkivnih uzoraka) dao je nalaze karakteristične za oba patogena: nekrotizujući miokarditis i hepatitis tipičan za PPV, kao i intersticijalna pneumonija i vaskulitis koji upućuju na PRRSV. Serologiški, sve tri farme imale su visoku seroprevalenciju PPV (>70%) i PRRSV (>55%) u trenutku uzorkovanja. Na jednoj farmi verifikovana je i pojava PRRS virusa genetski srodnog HP-PRRSV podtipu 1.3, što je doprinelo težini kliničke slike. Nalaz podvlači neophodnost kombinovane dijagnostike i prilagođenih vakcinacionih shema u slučajevima reproduktivnih poremećaja nepoznate etiologije.

title: Herd-level risk factors for PPV/PRRSV co-circulation on farrow-to-finish farms in the Pannonian Plain: a multivariable logistic regression analysis
abstract: We conducted a cross-sectional survey on 42 farrow-to-finish farms in the Hungarian–Serbian border region to identify herd-level management factors associated with simultaneous serological evidence of both porcine parvovirus (PPV) and PRRS virus type 1 (PRRSV-1). Farm managers completed a standardised questionnaire covering biosecurity measures, introduction practices, vaccination history, and facility characteristics. Blood samples were collected from 20 randomly selected sows per farm. Co-circulation (defined as ≥30% ELISA seroprevalence for both agents on the same farm) was detected on 19 of 42 farms (45.2%). In multivariable logistic regression, significant risk factors for co-circulation included: purchase of replacement gilts from multiple suppliers (OR 4.1; 95% CI 1.8–9.4), absence of an all-in/all-out system in the farrowing unit (OR 3.3; 95% CI 1.4–7.8), and herd size above 500 sows (OR 2.5; 95% CI 1.1–5.7). Consistent use of combined PPV/PRRS vaccination was associated with reduced odds (OR 0.38; 95% CI 0.16–0.89). Improving gilt sourcing and farrowing management appear to be the most actionable targets for reducing co-circulation risk.

title: Vakcinalni protokoli protiv PRRS-a na komercijalnim farmama u Srbiji: anketa o primeni i percepciji efikasnosti od strane veterinara
abstract: Uprkos dostupnosti nekoliko licenciranih PRRS vakcina u Srbiji, podaci o stvarnoj primenjenosti vakcinacionih protokola i percepciji njihove efikasnosti od strane terenske veterinarske prakse su oskudni. Sprovedena je anonimna anketa među 83 terenska veterinara koji rade sa svinjama u Srbiji i Republici Srpskoj. Anketa je sadržavala 28 pitanja o tipu korišćene vakcine (MLV ili inaktivisana), frekvenciji primene, načinu praćenja zaštite i subjektivnoj proceni uticaja vakcinacije na reproduktivne parametre. Rezultati su pokazali da 61% ispitanika koristi isključivo MLV vakcine, 22% kombinuje MLV i inaktivisane preparate, a 17% se oslanja na inaktivisane vakcine. Svega 34% veterinara redovno prati post-vakcinalne titare putem ELISA. Subjektivna efikasnost ocenjena je u proseku sa 3,4 od 5. Veterinari koji prate titare izveštavali su o statistički višem skorom efikasnosti (p = 0,04). Ovi podaci ukazuju na raskorak između preporučenih i primenjenih protokola i na potrebu za boljom edukacijom terenske prakse.

title: Serological dynamics following modified-live PRRS virus vaccination in gilts introduced into endemically infected herds: a longitudinal field study
abstract: Gilt acclimation to PRRS-endemic herds is a critical control point where serological monitoring can guide management decisions, yet longitudinal field data from the Balkan region are limited. We followed 96 gilts on three commercial sow farms in Serbia from arrival through first farrowing. Gilts were vaccinated with a European-lineage MLV PRRS vaccine at arrival and again 28 days later according to farm protocol. Serum was collected at arrival, 28, 56, and 112 days post-vaccination and at farrowing. ELISA S/P ratios, virus isolation attempts, and reproductive outcomes at first farrowing were recorded. Seroconversion was confirmed in 89/96 gilts (92.7%) by day 56. At farrowing, gilts with S/P ratios above 1.5 at day 112 had a significantly lower rate of stillborn piglets (3.2% vs. 6.7%; p = 0.02) compared to those with ratios below 1.0. Farm-level variation in antibody kinetics was substantial, suggesting differences in field virus exposure. These data support the use of day-112 ELISA S/P ratio as a practical on-farm marker for gilt readiness.

title: Point-of-care lateral flow assay for PPV antibody screening in sow herds: evaluation against ELISA and VN on 310 field samples
abstract: Rapid, on-farm serological screening for porcine parvovirus (PPV) would support timely herd management decisions, but published validation data for lateral flow assays (LFAs) in swine field conditions are sparse. We evaluated a prototype lateral flow immunoassay strip (developed by a regional diagnostic supplier) for PPV IgG detection against a validated blocking ELISA and serum virus neutralisation (VN) as reference standards, using 310 field serum samples from 16 Serbian and Hungarian farms. LFA results were read at 10 minutes by two independent observers blinded to ELISA and VN results. Against ELISA, the LFA showed sensitivity 87.3% (95% CI 81.2–91.9%) and specificity 91.6% (95% CI 85.4–95.7%), with moderate-to-good inter-observer agreement (kappa = 0.78). Against VN, sensitivity dropped to 82.1%. False-negative LFA results were associated with VN titres below 1:64. The assay performed acceptably as a herd-level screening tool when applied to pools of ≥5 samples, achieving sensitivity 95.1% and specificity 89.4% at that level. The LFA may be useful for rapid first-pass screening but should not replace quantitative serology for vaccine efficacy assessment.

title: Multivariate blood biomarker panel for early identification of transition cows at risk of multiple metabolic disorders
abstract: A panel of ten blood analytes—BHB, NEFA, glucose, insulin, AST, GLDH, total bilirubin, albumin, cholesterol, and haptoglobin—was measured in 192 Holstein cows at three days before and seven days after calving on five farms. Principal component analysis was followed by hierarchical cluster analysis to identify distinct metabolic phenotypes. Three clusters emerged: a 'low-risk' cluster (n = 97) characterised by stable glucose and low NEFA; a 'ketosis-prone' cluster (n = 61) with high BHB and NEFA postpartum; and a 'hepatic overload' cluster (n = 34) combining elevated AST, GLDH, and total bilirubin with low albumin and cholesterol. Animals in the hepatic overload cluster were 4.6 times more likely to be removed from the herd before 60 days in milk than the low-risk group (p < 0.001). The panel explained substantially more variance in adverse outcomes than any single biomarker alone, suggesting a multi-analyte approach is warranted in at-risk herds.

title: Molecular subtype classification of canine mammary carcinomas using ER, PR, HER2, and Ki-67: frequency and association with clinicopathological parameters
abstract: Adapting human breast cancer molecular subtype criteria, 102 canine mammary carcinomas were classified into luminal-A-like (ER+ and/or PR+, HER2−, Ki-67 < 22%), luminal-B-like (ER+ and/or PR+, HER2− or +, Ki-67 ≥ 22%), HER2-enriched-like (ER−/PR−, HER2+), and triple-negative-like (ER−/PR−, HER2−) subtypes. Frequencies were 31%, 18%, 14%, and 37% respectively. Triple-negative-like tumours were predominantly grade III (82%) and had the highest rate of lymph node metastasis (58%). Luminal-A-like carcinomas showed the most favourable two-year survival (median not reached). HER2-enriched-like and triple-negative-like subtypes had median overall survival of 11 and 9 months respectively. Age at diagnosis, reproductive history, and body condition score were not significantly associated with subtype distribution. These proportions and their prognostic implications correspond broadly to patterns in human breast oncology, reinforcing the value of the canine model for comparative research.

title: Pilot application of a portable saliva corticosterone reader for rapid on-line welfare monitoring at broiler slaughter lines
abstract: Real-time corticosterone measurement at abattoir intake could support welfare-based feedback to farms and transport contractors. This pilot study evaluated a portable lateral-flow reader (adapted for corticosterone quantification in avian saliva) against laboratory ELISA on 112 paired saliva samples collected from broilers at two abattoirs in Vojvodina. The reader yielded results within eight minutes of sample collection. Agreement between methods was assessed by Bland–Altman analysis; the mean bias was −1.3 ng/mL (limits of agreement −6.1 to 3.5 ng/mL). Classification concordance for a pre-defined threshold of 5 ng/mL was 79%. Reader performance was affected by ambient temperature above 30 °C, reducing concordance to 68% in summer conditions. The study identifies the need for temperature-compensated calibration curves and improved swab elution protocols before the device can be recommended for routine on-line use, but confirms the basic analytical feasibility of the approach.

title: Roughness thresholds in synthetic two-tone complexes: a listener study with musicians and non-musicians
abstract: This study measured roughness perception thresholds for pairs of sinusoidal tones whose frequency separation was varied systematically from 0 to 400 Hz around a 1 kHz centre frequency. Forty participants (20 trained musicians, 20 non-musicians) rated perceived roughness on a seven-point scale across 60 stimulus pairs presented over calibrated headphones. Results showed that musicians set their rough-to-smooth category boundary at a narrower frequency separation (mean 28.4 Hz) compared to non-musicians (mean 34.1 Hz), a difference significant at p < 0.01. The data replicated the classical Plomp–Levelt curve in its overall shape but revealed a systematic downward shift in threshold among musically trained listeners. Regression modelling confirmed that years of musical training accounted for approximately 19 % of threshold variance after controlling for age and hearing sensitivity. The findings suggest that long-term exposure to harmonic material sharpens sensitivity to spectral dissonance, with potential implications for mastering and mixing decisions in dense musical textures.

title: Spectral centroid drift and perceived brightness in additive synthesised organ timbres
abstract: Perceived brightness in musical tones is commonly associated with spectral centroid, yet the perceptual consequences of centroid drift over the duration of a sustained tone remain underexplored. This study constructed 48 additive synthesis patches modelled loosely on pipe organ stop spectra, each exhibiting one of four centroid trajectory types (stable, ascending, descending, or oscillating) over a 3-second duration. Thirty-two listeners rated brightness at onset, midpoint, and offset on a visual analogue scale. Analysis of variance indicated a significant main effect of trajectory type on brightness ratings at midpoint (F(3,124) = 18.7, p < 0.001), with oscillating centroid trajectories producing the highest variance in individual responses. A subsidiary test showed that onsets predicted overall brightness judgements more strongly (r = 0.71) than midpoints or offsets. The results support a perceptual primacy-of-attack model for brightness attribution and have practical relevance for designing synthetic timbres intended to evoke acoustic instrument character.

title: Fusion and segregation of concurrent synthesised streams: the role of onset asynchrony and spectral overlap
abstract: Auditory stream fusion—the perceptual binding of multiple simultaneous sound sources into a single object—was investigated using pairs of frequency-modulated tones with controlled degrees of spectral overlap (0 %, 25 %, 50 %, and 75 % of partials shared) and onset asynchronies (0, 20, 40, and 80 ms). Twenty-six participants performed a same–different judgement task and a subsequent fusion rating task. Logistic regression on fusion responses showed a strong interaction between spectral overlap and onset asynchrony: at 75 % spectral overlap, asynchronies beyond 40 ms reduced fusion probability from 0.83 to 0.47. The effect of onset asynchrony was more pronounced for overlapping spectra than for non-overlapping ones. These findings are discussed in relation to existing models of auditory scene analysis and their applicability to electroacoustic music contexts where composers deliberately blur source boundaries.

title: Perceived density and listener fatigue in multi-layer electroacoustic textures: an exploratory study
abstract: This paper reports an exploratory listening experiment in which participants were exposed to ten electroacoustic pieces selected from the IRCAM Solo Instruments catalogue (used under licence) and five purpose-built test compositions containing between 4 and 18 simultaneous synthesised layers. Participants completed a continuous density rating using a joystick controller and a retrospective fatigue questionnaire after each excerpt. Spectral analysis of the stimuli established layer count, spectral density (energy per critical band), and inter-layer roughness metrics as independent variables. Mixed-effects modelling revealed that inter-layer roughness was the strongest predictor of subjective density (β = 0.61, SE = 0.08) and listener fatigue ratings (β = 0.44, SE = 0.11), outperforming raw layer count and overall loudness. The study also identifies a non-linear relationship between roughness and fatigue, with a plateau emerging above a composite roughness index of approximately 2.8 arbitrary units. Implications for electroacoustic composition and sound-art installation design are discussed.

title: Binaural differences as a factor in spectral fusion: evidence from a lateralisation paradigm
abstract: When two tones with overlapping spectra are presented binaurally with interaural level differences, the resulting lateralisation cue can counteract spectral fusion and promote stream segregation. This study manipulated interaural level difference (0, 3, 6, and 9 dB) in spectrally overlapping tone pairs and measured their effect on fusion ratings from 30 listeners using a dummy-head binaural recording setup. Ratings were collected via a web-based listening interface, with stimuli delivered over individually fitted in-ear monitors. Analysis showed a monotonic decrease in fusion ratings as ILD increased (mean drop of 1.4 scale units per 3 dB step on a 10-point scale), an effect that was larger for pairs with higher spectral overlap. A secondary analysis of individual differences revealed that listeners who reported greater familiarity with spatial audio showed steeper ILD-by-fusion slopes. Results are interpreted within a common-fate framework and discussed in relation to spatial mixing practices.

title: Masking of low-amplitude partials in dense synthesised textures: thresholds as a function of layer count
abstract: This study quantified how increasing numbers of concurrent synthesised layers raise the masked threshold of a probe partial positioned at 880 Hz. Layer count was varied from 1 to 20 using spectrally randomised additive synthesis patches; the probe partial was embedded at signal-to-masker ratios from −20 to +10 dB in 2 dB steps. Thirty-five listeners performed a three-interval forced-choice detection task. Masked threshold increased approximately log-linearly with layer count up to 12 layers (slope ≈ 1.8 dB per doubling of layers) before levelling off. The levelling-off was attributed to energetic saturation near the probe frequency. A secondary condition tested probe partials at 2640 Hz and found a shallower slope (1.2 dB per doubling), suggesting frequency-region dependence of the masking growth. These data provide empirical constraints for psychoacoustic models used in electroacoustic production tools.

title: Roughness and perceived aggressiveness in electronic dance music mixdowns: a production-focused listening study
abstract: Producer and listener evaluations of 'aggressiveness' in electronic dance music have been linked informally to distortion and spectral density, yet controlled evidence remains sparse. This study recruited 18 professional mixing engineers and 22 non-professional listeners to rate perceived aggressiveness for 48 short EDM mixdown excerpts that varied systematically in composite roughness index (CRI), derived from the computational model described in Kiss & Kovačević (2018). Excerpts were drawn from three genre subsets: techno, drum and bass, and industrial. Linear mixed-effects modelling showed that CRI predicted aggressiveness ratings significantly (β = 0.58, p < 0.001), and that this effect was moderated by genre familiarity in non-professional listeners but not in engineers. Cluster analysis of engineer ratings revealed two subgroups with different roughness–aggressiveness mapping functions, suggesting that training shapes the perceptual weight given to spectral roughness in aesthetic evaluation. Practical guidelines for the use of roughness metrics in mastering workflows are outlined.

title: Spectral fusion in electroacoustic composition: techniques, perceptual correlates, and notation strategies
abstract: This book chapter surveys compositional strategies for spectral fusion in electroacoustic music from the early Cologne school to the present, situating them within a psychoacoustic framework drawn from stream analysis, roughness theory, and masking research. The chapter discusses how composers exploit onset synchrony, shared vibrato rates, and spectral complementarity to promote or disrupt perceived fusion between acoustic and electronic sources. A series of score excerpts and their spectral analyses are examined alongside listener data reinterpreted from three published studies, including roughness threshold measurements and stream segregation experiments. The chapter concludes with a set of notation proposals for specifying intended fusion states in mixed electroacoustic scores, arguing that conventional notation inadequately communicates intended perceptual outcomes to performers and sound engineers. The proposals are illustrated with three short original examples in which spectral targeting, layer allocation, and roughness indices are annotated alongside traditional notation.

title: Effect of room acoustics simulation on roughness perception in multi-layer audio: anechoic versus reverberant conditions
abstract: It is unknown to what extent simulated room acoustics modify perceptual roughness in dense multi-layer audio. This study presented identical 16-layer granular synthesis stimuli in three conditions: anechoic (direct signal only), simulated small room (RT60 ≈ 0.4 s), and simulated large hall (RT60 ≈ 1.8 s). Thirty listeners rated roughness on a continuous scale. Mixed-effects analysis revealed a significant reduction in roughness ratings from anechoic to large-hall conditions (mean decrease 1.1 scale units on a 0–10 scale, p < 0.001), with no significant difference between anechoic and small-room conditions. Acoustic analysis showed that reverberation increased inter-layer temporal overlap and reduced the amplitude modulation depth of individual partial pairs, the primary cue for roughness. A regression model incorporating amplitude modulation depth as a mediator accounted for 64 % of the variance in roughness ratings across conditions. The findings suggest that reverb settings in electroacoustic production workflows materially alter perceived roughness independently of spectral content.

title: Towards perceptually informed loudness normalisation for electroacoustic music: roughness as a complementary metric to LUFS
abstract: Current loudness normalisation standards for streaming platforms rely on integrated loudness units relative to full scale (LUFS), a measure that does not capture spectral roughness or timbral density. This preprint proposes a supplementary normalisation metric combining integrated LUFS with a time-averaged composite roughness index (CRI) derived from partial-pair analysis. The proposed dual-metric system was evaluated on a corpus of 200 electroacoustic works drawn from online distribution platforms, for which both LUFS and CRI were computed. Listening tests with 40 participants compared subjective loudness balance achieved by LUFS-only versus LUFS+CRI normalisation across pairs of excerpts differing in spectral character. The dual-metric normalisation was rated as better balanced in 61 % of trials (p < 0.001 by sign test). Limitations of the CRI computation in real-world multi-format audio are discussed, and a revised partial-tracking algorithm with improved performance on mp3-compressed sources is described. The preprint invites community feedback ahead of journal submission.

title: Perceptual thresholds for grain density variation in procedurally generated ambient sound
abstract: Granular synthesis systems for ambient soundscapes often update grain density continuously, but the perceptual salience of such changes has not been systematically quantified. This study measured just-noticeable differences (JNDs) for grain density in synthesised crowd and forest ambience using a three-interval forced-choice paradigm with 48 participants drawn from a music technology student population. Stimuli were generated with grain densities ranging from 10 to 200 grains per second. Results indicate a Weber fraction of approximately 0.18 for crowd textures and 0.22 for forest textures across the tested range, with notable differences at extremes below 20 and above 160 grains per second. These thresholds suggest that interactive systems can reduce update frequency substantially without perceptual artefact, offering a practical optimisation target for CPU-constrained real-time applications. Implications for game audio engine design are discussed, including recommended quantisation steps for density control parameters.

title: Adoption Barriers to Environmental Management Standards Among Small Agricultural Suppliers in Vojvodina
abstract: This study examines why small-scale vegetable and grain suppliers in the Vojvodina region of Serbia show low uptake of ISO 14001 and related environmental management standards. Drawing on 148 structured interviews conducted during 2010–2011 with farms supplying processors and retailers, the study applies binary logistic regression to identify factors associated with certification intent. Results indicate that farm size (measured in hectares and number of employees) and the proportion of revenue derived from a single buyer are the two strongest predictors of certification effort. Coercive pressure from lead firms is present but weak, partly because most dominant buyers at the time were domestic processors with limited export obligations. Normative channels, including agronomist advisory networks, exerted a modest but statistically significant positive influence. The paper argues that standard diffusion in this region is primarily buyer-demand-driven, and that public policy instruments would need to address the asymmetric cost burden on micro-farms to meaningfully increase uptake.

title: Mapping Vertical Governance Structures in the Serbian Sunflower Oil Supply Chain
abstract: Using value chain analysis and semi-structured interviews with 34 actors spanning seed producers, crushing mills, bulk traders, and retail buyers, this paper reconstructs the governance architecture of Serbia's sunflower oil supply chain as it stood in 2012. The analysis follows Gereffi's buyer-driven versus producer-driven typology and documents a transition from relational to captive governance as EU-oriented export volumes grew. Particular attention is given to contract clauses that implicitly or explicitly require tier-1 processors to monitor their own input suppliers for pesticide residue compliance and traceability documentation. The study finds that such clauses reached only 41 percent of surveyed tier-1 firms and were almost never transmitted formally to seed-producing farms. The paper identifies this gap as a structural vulnerability for export market access and proposes a typology of compliance transfer mechanisms ranging from audit pass-through to co-investment in supplier capacity.

title: Do GlobalAgriCode Certification Requirements Reach Tier-2 Suppliers? Evidence from Fruit Processors in South-East Europe
abstract: This paper investigates whether private sustainability standards applied at the processor level (tier 1) generate measurable compliance improvements at the farm level (tier 2) in fruit processing supply chains in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Romania. The fictional GlobalAgriCode scheme, closely modelled on comparable private voluntary standards, was used as a test case because it had achieved meaningful uptake among processors in all three countries by 2013. A three-wave panel survey covering 211 tier-2 farms over 2013–2015 tracked changes in pesticide record-keeping, water-use reporting, and worker safety documentation. Fixed-effects panel regression shows a statistically significant improvement in record-keeping compliance (β = 0.31, p < 0.01) among farms whose primary buyer had been certified for at least 18 months, but no significant effect on water or safety metrics. The findings suggest that governance diffusion is selective, concentrating on dimensions that buyers can verify cheaply during routine procurement interactions.

title: Network Position and Standard Adoption: A Social Network Analysis of Grain Traders in the Danube Region
abstract: This study applies social network analysis to a dataset of 87 grain trading firms operating across Serbia, Croatia, Hungary, and Romania, using data on inter-firm contracts and information-sharing ties collected through a 2015 mail survey. The objective is to test whether a firm's network centrality predicts its likelihood of holding a documented sustainability commitment (defined as membership in at least one recognised sustainability scheme or having a published supplier code of conduct). Betweenness centrality is the strongest predictor (OR = 2.14, 95% CI [1.47, 3.11]), suggesting that firms positioned as brokers between otherwise disconnected clusters are disproportionately exposed to heterogeneous institutional pressures and respond by formalising sustainability commitments. Degree centrality is significant but weaker. The paper uses UCINET for network computation and logistic regression for the outcome model. Results have implications for policy targeting: supporting connectivity among peripheral firms may be more efficient than working exclusively with large central actors.

title: Institutional Logics in Conflict: Organic Certification versus Retailer Codes of Conduct in Croatian and Serbian Vegetable Supply Chains
abstract: Organic certification schemes and retailer-imposed codes of conduct for fresh vegetable suppliers address overlapping sustainability concerns but embed different institutional logics: the former is state-sanctioned and process-oriented, the latter is market-driven and outcome-oriented. This paper reports on 27 in-depth interviews with vegetable suppliers in Croatia and Serbia who operate under both regimes simultaneously. Interview data are analysed using an inductive coding approach. Suppliers describe tensions between the documentation rhythms, inspection frequencies, and permissible input lists of the two schemes, and develop a range of coping strategies including parallel record-keeping systems, selective disclosure, and renegotiating delivery terms to avoid inspection overlaps. The paper draws on institutional logics theory to explain why the conflict is structural rather than incidental and argues that without deliberate harmonisation efforts at the policy level, dual compliance burdens are likely to discourage standard uptake among smaller farms.

title: Auditor Competence and Audit Depth in Agri-food Supply Chain Sustainability Assessments: Findings from a Certification Body Survey
abstract: Third-party auditing is central to private sustainability standards, yet audit quality varies substantially across certification bodies. This paper presents findings from a structured survey of 41 auditors employed by certification bodies operating in Serbia, Romania, and Bulgaria, conducted in 2019. Auditors were asked to describe their most recent agri-food sustainability audit in terms of site visit duration, document review depth, supplier interview practice, and follow-up verification procedures. Responses are benchmarked against the procedural requirements of four widely used schemes. The median audit lasted 3.8 hours on-site, well below the minimum stipulated by three of the four schemes assessed. Auditor background (agronomy vs. management training) does not significantly predict audit depth, but firm size of the certification body does: auditors at larger bodies report longer site visits and more systematic document triangulation. The paper discusses implications for the credibility of compliance signals transmitted up supply chains.

title: The Role of Farmers' Associations in Mediating Standard Diffusion to Smallholders: Evidence from the Serbian Raspberry Sector
abstract: Serbia's raspberry sector exports a large share of production to Western European processors and retail chains, creating a well-defined governance pressure from buyers. Yet the sector is characterised by very small farm units, averaging 0.4 hectares, for whom direct buyer relationships are rare. This study investigates whether and how farmers' associations serve as institutional intermediaries, translating buyer-driven standard requirements into guidance that smallholders can act upon. Using a mixed-methods design—a survey of 196 smallholders in the Arilje and Ivanjica regions combined with interviews with six association managers—the paper tests a mediation model in which association membership positively mediates the relationship between buyer pressure and farm-level compliance behaviour. The mediation coefficient is statistically significant (β = 0.19, bootstrapped CI [0.09, 0.31]). Qualitative findings reveal that associations primarily mediate through collective training sessions and group audit arrangements rather than through direct contract renegotiation.

title: Cross-Border Standard Harmonisation in the Hungary–Serbia Agri-food Corridor: Lessons from the Interreg AGRISUST Project
abstract: The Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia programme co-funded a three-year project aimed at aligning sustainability documentation requirements for agri-food suppliers operating across the two countries' shared border region. This paper reports an evaluation of that project's outcomes, drawing on project monitoring data, exit interviews with 22 participating firms, and a comparison of pre- and post-project audit pass rates. Pass rates for cross-border shipments improved by 18 percentage points among firms that completed the joint training and documentation harmonisation modules. Firms that participated only in training without updating their internal procedures showed no significant improvement. The paper uses process tracing to identify the causal mechanisms linking project activities to compliance outcomes and finds that the decisive mechanism was the adoption of a bilingual standardised declaration template, which reduced documentation errors rather than changing underlying farm practices. Lessons are discussed for the design of future cross-border standard harmonisation initiatives in the Western Balkans.

title: Governance Standard Stringency and Supplier Exit Risk: A Survival Analysis of Tier-2 Firms in Romanian and Serbian Dairy Chains
abstract: This paper examines whether heightened sustainability standard requirements increase the probability that tier-2 dairy suppliers exit the formal supply chain—either by ceasing operations, shifting to informal markets, or downgrading to buyers with lower requirements. Longitudinal data on 312 dairy farms in Romania and Serbia were assembled from official registry records, buyer compliance databases, and a retrospective survey, covering the period 2015–2023. A Cox proportional hazards model is estimated with standard stringency (measured as the number of verified compliance dimensions required by each farm's primary buyer) as the main covariate, controlling for herd size, farm age, region, and access to agri-environmental subsidies. The hazard ratio for stringency is 1.09 per additional compliance dimension (95% CI [1.03, 1.16]), indicating a modest but consistent association with exit risk. Subsidy access substantially moderates this relationship. The paper contributes to ongoing debates about whether private sustainability standards promote upgrading or exclusion of small producers.

title: Scope and Limits of Blockchain-Based Traceability in Vegetable Oil Supply Chains: An Assessment Framework for South-East European Conditions
abstract: Blockchain-based traceability systems are proposed with increasing frequency as a mechanism for verifying sustainability claims across agri-food supply chains. This preprint develops an assessment framework for evaluating the suitability of such systems under the infrastructure, regulatory, and organisational conditions typical of vegetable oil supply chains in South-East Europe. The framework draws on structured expert interviews with nine supply chain managers and five technology developers active in the region, conducted in 2025, as well as a review of 22 documented blockchain traceability deployments in comparable contexts worldwide. The assessment covers five dimensions: data entry integrity, consensus mechanism appropriateness, interoperability with existing ERP systems, cost per transaction at regional volumes, and regulatory recognition of on-chain records by national and EU food safety authorities. Preliminary findings suggest that permissioned blockchain architectures offer marginally better alignment with regional conditions than public ledgers, but that data entry integrity at the farm level remains the binding constraint regardless of ledger type.

title: Competency Profiling in the Serbian Automotive Supply Chain: A Study of Tier-2 and Tier-3 Suppliers
abstract: This article reports competency profiling data collected from 11 Tier-2 and Tier-3 automotive component suppliers located in Vojvodina. A mixed-methods design combined semi-structured interviews (n = 48 managers and team leaders), behavioural event interviews (n = 31 high-performing operators selected by management nomination), and a quantitative survey (n = 312 employees). Competency clusters derived from qualitative analysis were operationalised as rating scales and administered to a broader sample. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a six-cluster model: technical precision, equipment stewardship, procedural adherence, collaborative problem-solving, quality orientation, and adaptive response to production variability. Criterion-related validity was assessed against supervisor performance ratings; correlations ranged from r = 0.31 to r = 0.58 across clusters. The study also documents significant gaps between competencies demanded by Tier-1 customer audits and those currently cultivated in supplier training programmes. Findings informed a draft competency dictionary distributed to participating companies.

title: Digital Readiness Self-Assessment in Vojvodina SMEs: A Pilot Scale Development and Validation
abstract: Measuring an organisation's readiness for digital transformation is a prerequisite for targeting change management interventions effectively, yet validated instruments adapted to transition-economy SMEs are scarce. This paper reports the development and preliminary validation of a 22-item Digital Readiness Scale (DRS-22) tailored to the context of small and medium enterprises operating in lower-income EU candidate countries. Scale items were generated through a systematic review of existing readiness frameworks and two rounds of expert interviews with twelve managers from Serbian and Hungarian SMEs. A pilot sample of 87 employees and owners from Vojvodina-based firms completed the instrument, and exploratory factor analysis identified four stable dimensions: technological infrastructure, managerial commitment, employee digital competence, and process formalisation. Internal consistency was satisfactory across all subscales (Cronbach's α ranging from 0.71 to 0.84). Confirmatory analysis on a second hold-out subsample supported a four-factor structure with acceptable fit indices. The scale is intended as a free diagnostic tool for practitioners and as a baseline measure for longitudinal transformation studies. Limitations include the small pilot size and single-region sampling.

title: Firm Responses to Overlapping Regulatory Regimes: Evidence from the Serbian Pharmaceutical Wholesale Market, 2015–2022
abstract: Serbian pharmaceutical wholesalers operate under simultaneous oversight from the Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia, the Ministry of Health, the Competition Protection Commission, and, for firms seeking EU market access, European Medicines Agency guidelines. This paper examines how eight wholesale firms navigated these overlapping regimes over a seven-year period using a longitudinal case study design. Interview data (three rounds per firm) are combined with regulatory correspondence and annual compliance reports. Analysis reveals that firms developed differentiated stakeholder engagement teams assigned to specific regulatory arenas, a structural response the paper terms 'regulatory domain segmentation.' Firms that adopted segmentation earlier achieved shorter average approval timelines (mean 14.3 months vs. 22.7 months for non-adopters) and fewer compliance notices. The paper discusses the resource implications of segmentation for medium-sized firms and considers whether the strategy generalises to other industries with overlapping regulatory jurisdictions.

title: Stakeholder Salience and Corporate Sustainability Reporting in Regulated Central European Industries: A Configurational Analysis
abstract: This preprint investigates whether stakeholder salience profiles predict the scope and credibility of corporate sustainability reports in regulated industries. A configurational approach using fsQCA is applied to a dataset of 63 firms in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Slovakia that published sustainability or ESG reports between 2019 and 2024. Firm-level salience maps were reconstructed from manager surveys using the validated instrument published by Lukács et al. (2022). Outcome variable is report credibility, operationalised as a composite of third-party assurance, GRI compliance level, and analyst citation frequency. Three sufficient configurations for high credibility are identified, all requiring definitive-stakeholder pressure from at least one regulatory body combined with either external investor presence or civil-society salience above the 0.7 threshold. Configurations without any high-salience regulatory stakeholder do not produce high-credibility reports regardless of other conditions. The paper has been submitted for peer review; feedback is being incorporated.

title: Decomposition rates of winter cover crop residues in chernozem soil under continental climate conditions
abstract: A two-year field incubation experiment was conducted at Rimski Šančevi to quantify decomposition rates of five winter cover crop species—hairy vetch, winter rye, phacelia, oilseed radish and crimson clover—incorporated at vegetative peak biomass in late March. Mesh litterbags (2 mm pore size) containing 20 g air-dry residue were retrieved at 14-day intervals over 90 days. Mass loss followed a two-phase exponential decay model; hairy vetch reached 65% mass loss within 28 days while winter rye required 56 days to reach the same threshold. C:N ratio at incorporation explained 71% of variance in k-values (r² = 0.71, P < 0.001). Soil temperature was a stronger predictor of decomposition rate than soil moisture across the measurement period. Results indicate that termination timing relative to expected soil temperature accumulation determines whether mineralised nitrogen is available at maize sowing or is lost before crop uptake. Implications for scheduling termination in Vojvodina rotations are discussed.

title: Soil microbial biomass carbon and basal respiration following incorporation of legume and non-legume cover crop monocultures
abstract: Microbial biomass carbon (MBC) and basal soil respiration were measured in a replicated field experiment comparing incorporated monocultures of hairy vetch, white mustard, winter rye and bare fallow on a Vojvodina chernozem over two growing seasons (2006–2008). MBC was determined by chloroform fumigation-extraction at 7, 21, 42 and 84 days after incorporation. Hairy vetch incorporation increased MBC by 38% relative to bare fallow at day 21, declining to baseline by day 84. White mustard produced a pronounced but short-lived respiration peak (maximum metabolic quotient 4.2 µg CO₂-C mg⁻¹ MBC h⁻¹ at day 7) attributed to glucosinolate-derived compounds. Winter rye showed the slowest microbial response, consistent with its high C:N ratio (32:1). These dynamics suggest that microbial immobilisation of nitrogen following high-C cover crops may suppress early maize growth if termination-to-planting intervals are shorter than three weeks.

title: Nitrogen mineralisation from two-component cover crop mixtures with contrasting C:N ratios in a maize rotation
abstract: A controlled incubation study combined with a three-year field trial examined net nitrogen mineralisation from binary cover crop mixtures of hairy vetch with winter rye at seeding ratios of 75:25, 50:50 and 25:75 (by seed weight). Incubations at 15°C and 25°C using 250 g disturbed soil cores showed that the 75:25 mixture released 42 kg N ha⁻¹ equivalent within 21 days at 15°C, compared with 27 kg N ha⁻¹ equivalent for the 50:50 mixture and 11 kg N ha⁻¹ equivalent for the 25:75 mixture. In field trials, the 75:25 mixture supported maize seedling dry weight 18% higher than bare fallow at the V3 growth stage. Final grain yield differences were not statistically significant in two of three years, suggesting that early-season nitrogen is important but not the sole limiting factor. Aboveground biomass at termination ranged from 2.8 to 4.1 t dry matter ha⁻¹ depending on mixture ratio and year.

title: Effect of cover crop termination method on soil nitrate availability at soybean sowing
abstract: Three termination methods—mechanical rolling-crimping, herbicide desiccation (glyphosate 3 l ha⁻¹) and shallow incorporation (10 cm)—were compared across hairy vetch and hairy vetch/rye mixture cover crops in a soybean rotation on Vojvodina chernozem over 2010–2012. Soil mineral nitrogen (NO₃⁻-N + NH₄⁺-N) in the 0–30 cm layer was measured at termination and at soybean emergence. Shallow incorporation consistently produced the highest mineral-N concentrations at soybean emergence (mean 61 kg N ha⁻¹), compared with 44 kg N ha⁻¹ for herbicide desiccation and 39 kg N ha⁻¹ for rolling-crimping. However, rolling-crimped plots maintained higher soil moisture and lower penetration resistance (mean 1.8 MPa versus 2.4 MPa for incorporation), which improved soybean seedling emergence by 6 percentage points. No significant differences in final soybean grain yield were detected among termination methods in any year. Data suggest that termination choice involves trade-offs between nitrogen availability and seedbed physical conditions.

title: Cover crop diversity effects on weed suppression and cash crop establishment: results from a four-species mixture trial
abstract: A four-year field experiment tested the hypothesis that increasing cover crop species richness improves weed suppression and subsequent cash crop establishment. Treatments included monocultures of hairy vetch, winter rye, phacelia and oilseed radish, and a four-species mixture at equal seeding rate equivalents. Weed biomass at cash crop emergence was reduced by 54% under the four-species mixture compared with the mean of monocultures. The mixture also produced the most uniform residue distribution across the soil surface, assessed by digital image analysis of 0.25 m² quadrats. Maize plant population at V3 was 3.2% higher under the mixture than under bare fallow. Regression analysis indicated that residue cover percentage was a stronger predictor of weed biomass than total residue biomass (standardised β −0.61 versus −0.38). These results support designing cover crop mixtures for physical soil coverage alongside nitrogen management goals.

title: Cover crop mixture management in arable systems: a review of European evidence on nitrogen cycling and cash crop response
abstract: This chapter synthesises published research from 1995 to 2018 on the use of cover crop mixtures in European continental arable farming, with emphasis on nitrogen cycling and subsequent cash crop performance. The review covers 87 studies from 14 countries and organises findings around four themes: residue quality and decomposition, microbial community responses, nitrogen mineralisation timing and cash crop establishment outcomes. Meta-analysis of 34 experiments comparing binary legume/grass mixtures with legume monocultures showed that mixtures produced lower but more temporally extended nitrogen mineralisation, with a weighted mean difference of −8 kg N ha⁻¹ in the first 30 days but no significant difference by 60 days. Cash crop yield responses to cover crops were positive in 64% of included experiments, neutral in 28% and negative in 8%, with negative responses concentrated in dry springs. Gaps in knowledge regarding multi-species mixtures above three components and interactions with tillage intensity are identified.

title: Soil enzyme activities as indicators of biological activity following cover crop residue incorporation in a sunflower rotation
abstract: Urease, dehydrogenase and β-glucosidase activities were measured at six time points (0, 14, 28, 42, 63 and 90 days) after incorporation of hairy vetch, hairy vetch/winter rye (50:50) and winter rye cover crop residues in a sunflower rotation trial conducted in 2017–2019 at Rimski Šančevi. Urease activity peaked at 14 days post-incorporation for hairy vetch (62.4 µg NH₄⁺-N g⁻¹ soil h⁻¹), consistent with rapid protein mineralisation. Dehydrogenase activity showed a broader peak (days 14–42) for the mixture treatment. β-glucosidase activity was highest under winter rye residues at days 42–63, indicating continued carbohydrate decomposition. Principal component analysis grouped enzyme activity profiles clearly by residue C:N ratio, with sunflower plant counts positively correlated (r = 0.54, P = 0.02) with urease activity at day 14. Enzyme activity indices are proposed as practical diagnostic tools for assessing cover crop-induced biological activity in farm advisory contexts.

title: Winter cover crop performance under reduced autumn rainfall: observations from drought years 2019–2021 in Vojvodina
abstract: Three consecutive autumn seasons (2019, 2020, 2021) with below-average rainfall in Vojvodina (43%, 58% and 51% of the 30-year October–November mean, respectively) provided an opportunity to document cover crop establishment failure rates and biomass production under moisture stress. Seven cover crop species and two mixtures (hairy vetch/winter rye and phacelia/oilseed radish) were sown at standard commercial rates. Establishment failure (plant density below 30% of target) occurred in oilseed radish in all three years and in phacelia in 2019 and 2021. Hairy vetch/winter rye mixture showed the most consistent establishment across years (coefficient of variation in plant density = 14%). Aboveground dry matter at termination was 34–52% below the long-term trial mean in drought years. These data suggest that mixture design for drought resilience, prioritising species with lower germination soil water requirements, is necessary for reliable cover crop function in a changing regional climate.

title: Optimising the hairy vetch to winter rye seeding ratio for nitrogen mineralisation and sunflower yield stability across six site-years in northern Serbia
abstract: Six site-years of data from three field locations (Rimski Šančevi, Bačka Topola, Sremska Mitrovica) across 2020–2023 were used to evaluate five hairy vetch to winter rye seeding ratios (100:0, 75:25, 50:50, 25:75, 0:100) in terms of biomass production, nitrogen content at termination, mineralisation over 60 days (incubation subplots) and sunflower yield. A mixed model with site-year as a random effect identified the 75:25 ratio as optimal for total nitrogen mineralised by day 30 (mean 39 kg N ha⁻¹) and for sunflower yield stability (Finlay–Wilkinson stability coefficient b = 0.97). The 100:0 hairy vetch treatment mineralised more nitrogen in favourable years but was highly unstable (b = 1.38). The 25:75 rye-dominant treatment showed negative mineralisation (net immobilisation) in three of six site-years. Recommendations for farmers are expressed as a lookup table linking expected spring soil temperature to the advised seeding ratio.

title: Effects of multi-species cover crop mixtures on AMF colonisation of subsequent maize roots and early biomass accumulation
abstract: A pot and field dual experiment examined whether increasing cover crop species diversity (one, three and five species mixtures) altered arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal (AMF) colonisation of subsequent maize roots at V3 and V6 growth stages and maize shoot dry weight at V6. Pot trials used undisturbed soil cores (15 cm diameter, 20 cm depth) taken from plots after cover crop termination; field measurements used root washing and staining with trypan blue. AMF colonisation intensity at V3 was significantly higher in maize following the five-species mixture (mean 47% colonisation) than after bare fallow (mean 31%), with intermediate values for three-species (39%) and one-species (34%) treatments. Maize shoot dry weight at V6 correlated positively with AMF colonisation intensity (r = 0.58, P = 0.003). Soil phosphorus concentration did not differ significantly among treatments, suggesting that the AMF effect was not mediated through phosphorus alone. These results are preliminary and a full three-year field replication is ongoing.

title: Use of portable X-ray fluorescence spectrometry for estimating total potassium and calcium in saline soil profiles of the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) spectrometry was tested as a rapid, non-destructive method for estimating total potassium and calcium in soil profiles from six saline and saline-sodic sites across the Pannonian Plain in Serbia and Hungary. A total of 180 soil samples from depths of 0–100 cm were measured with a pXRF device and also analysed in the laboratory by acid digestion followed by ICP-OES. Linear regression models between pXRF and laboratory values achieved R² of 0.87 for potassium and 0.79 for calcium when field-moist samples were used. Predictive accuracy improved markedly (R² of 0.93 for K, 0.85 for Ca) after air-drying and sieving to 2 mm, suggesting that moisture content is a major source of error under field conditions. Depth-specific calibration equations were more accurate than a single pooled model, particularly below 40 cm where organic matter interference diminished. The findings support the use of pXRF as a screening tool for profile characterisation in salt-affected soil surveys where laboratory throughput is a limiting factor.

title: Bee visitation frequency and pollen deposition on stigmas of oilseed rape under contrasting landscape contexts in northern Serbia
abstract: Pollination effectiveness was quantified in oilseed rape at eight farms in northern Serbia differing in the proportion of semi-natural habitat (SNH) within a 1 km radius (range 2–22%). Focal-flower observations (total 480 h across four weeks of peak bloom in 2013) recorded visitor identity, visit duration, and contact with reproductive flower parts. Fluorescent dye powder was used as a pollen analogue to measure stigmatic deposition efficiency for the three most frequent wild bee taxa. Andrena and Halictus species showed pollen deposition rates 1.4–1.8 times higher per visit than honeybees. At farms with >10% SNH within 1 km, total wild bee visitation rates were 2.3-fold higher than at farms with <5% SNH. Seed set was positively correlated with wild bee visitation rate (r = 0.71, p < 0.01) but not with honeybee visitation rate alone. These results support a functional distinction between managed honeybee colonies and wild bee communities as pollination service providers in oilseed rape.

title: Skin conductance reactivity during a public-speaking stressor in undergraduate students with high versus low perfectionism concerns
abstract: This study examined electrodermal reactivity as a function of perfectionism concerns in a non-clinical student sample. Sixty-one undergraduates completed the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale and were exposed to a three-minute impromptu speech task in front of a two-person evaluative panel. Skin conductance level (SCL) and the number of non-specific skin conductance responses (NS-SCRs) were recorded continuously using a BIOPAC MP160 system with 8 mm Ag/AgCl electrodes placed on the index and middle fingers of the non-dominant hand. Participants scoring in the top tertile on Concern over Mistakes showed significantly higher mean SCL during anticipation (d = 0.61, p = .014) and recovery phases (d = 0.54, p = .031) compared to the low group, but groups did not differ reliably during the speech itself. NS-SCR frequency was elevated throughout the entire protocol in high-concern participants. Results suggest that heightened electrodermal arousal in perfectionistic individuals is most pronounced outside the peak stressor interval, pointing to prolonged anticipatory and perseverative processing rather than peak-moment hyperreactivity.

title: Resting vagally mediated heart rate variability as a predictor of cognitive reappraisal use in perfectionistic individuals
abstract: Vagally mediated heart rate variability (vmHRV), indexed by the root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), has been proposed as a physiological marker of self-regulatory capacity. This study tested whether resting RMSSD predicts habitual use of cognitive reappraisal in a sample of 88 psychology students selected to oversample high scores on the Hewitt–Flett Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale. A five-minute resting ECG was recorded in a supine position before participants completed the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire and a brief interview about recent academic performance appraisals. After controlling for trait anxiety and respiratory rate, resting RMSSD explained an additional 7.4% of variance in reappraisal frequency (β = 0.29, p = .008), but only among participants with self-oriented perfectionism scores above the sample median. Socially prescribed perfectionism did not moderate the association. Findings are consistent with the neurovisceral integration model and suggest that autonomic flexibility may buffer the tendency of self-oriented perfectionists to abandon adaptive reappraisal under self-evaluative pressure.

title: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia suppression under social evaluation: an exploratory comparison of adaptive and maladaptive perfectionism profiles
abstract: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) suppression from rest to a stressor is considered an index of vagal withdrawal supporting active coping. This exploratory study used latent profile analysis on Frost MPS subscale scores in a sample of 74 students to identify two perfectionism profiles: one characterised by high personal standards with low doubts and concerns (adaptive profile, n = 31) and one characterised by high doubts, concerns and parental criticism (maladaptive profile, n = 43). Participants completed a modified Trier Social Stress Test adapted for laboratory use, with concurrent respiration and ECG recording. RSA was estimated using the band-limited power method (0.12–0.40 Hz). Both groups showed RSA suppression during the stress task, but the maladaptive profile group showed significantly blunted suppression relative to baseline compared with the adaptive group (F(1, 71) = 5.18, p = .026, η²p = .068). Recovery RSA was also slower in the maladaptive group at the five-minute post-task interval. The findings replicate a pattern reported in emotion dysregulation research and extend it to a perfectionism-defined taxonomy.

title: Do perfectionistic cognitions mediate the link between trait perfectionism and autonomic stress reactivity? A pilot examination with concurrent EDA and ECG recording
abstract: Perfectionistic cognitions—intrusive thoughts about making mistakes—have been proposed as a proximal mechanism through which dispositional perfectionism translates into negative affect and physiological stress. This pilot study (N = 44) tested whether state perfectionistic cognitions, assessed immediately after a graded arithmetic task, mediated the association between trait Concern over Mistakes and two simultaneous physiological measures: mean skin conductance level (SCL) and RMSSD during the task. Electrodermal and cardiac data were co-registered on a BIOPAC MP160 platform. Bootstrapped mediation analysis (5,000 samples) indicated a significant indirect effect of Concern over Mistakes on RMSSD via perfectionistic cognitions (ab = −0.14, 95% CI [−0.27, −0.03]), but no reliable indirect effect on SCL. The differential pattern across the two autonomic channels suggests that perfectionistic cognitions may primarily suppress parasympathetic flexibility rather than amplify sympathetic activation. Sample size limits interpretation, and a pre-registered replication is underway.

title: Designing social media simulations for experimental bystander research: methodological considerations and a replication attempt
abstract: Laboratory research on online bystander behaviour depends heavily on the ecological validity of simulation environments. This methodological paper describes the design and iterative testing of a browser-based social media simulator developed at the University of Novi Sad that mimics common short-message platform features, including visible like counts, threaded replies, and follower indicators. Two pilot experiments (N = 64 and N = 89) were conducted to assess whether the simulator produced intervention rates consistent with published field-survey benchmarks. Intervention rates of 38% and 41% were observed respectively, compared with a meta-analytic estimate of approximately 35–45% from survey studies. Manipulation checks confirmed participants perceived the interactions as realistic. The paper discusses confounds introduced by artificial timers, researcher presence, and demand characteristics, and provides an open protocol and scenario scripts. Known limitations include the impossibility of genuine social consequences and the use of convenience student samples.

title: Bacteriological Profile of Puerperal Breast Abscess in a Tertiary Referral Centre: A Five-Year Retrospective Analysis
abstract: Puerperal breast abscess remains a significant cause of premature breastfeeding cessation. This retrospective study reviewed microbiological data from 148 women treated for lactational breast abscess at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2004 and 2009. Culture and sensitivity results were retrieved from institutional records. Staphylococcus aureus accounted for 74.3% of isolates, of which 18.2% were methicillin-resistant strains. Mixed flora was identified in 11.5% of cases. Abscess volume ranged from 3 to 87 mL (median 22 mL). Women with MRSA infection had significantly longer hospital stays (mean 8.4 vs. 4.1 days; p<0.001) and higher rates of surgical incision after failed needle aspiration. Empirical antibiotic therapy was appropriate in only 61% of cases based on final susceptibility data, suggesting a need to revise local treatment protocols. These findings provide a microbiological baseline for the region and support earlier targeted antibiotic prescribing.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Needle Aspiration versus Surgical Incision for Lactational Breast Abscess Smaller than 30 mL: A Prospective Comparative Study
abstract: This prospective study compared ultrasound-guided needle aspiration (UGNA) with surgical incision and drainage (SID) for lactational breast abscesses not exceeding 30 mL in volume. Between January 2008 and December 2011, 94 consecutive women presenting to the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina were enrolled. Fifty-one received UGNA with concomitant oral antibiotic therapy; 43 underwent SID. Primary outcomes were resolution rate, number of procedures required, duration of breastfeeding continuation, and wound healing time. Resolution was achieved in 78.4% of the UGNA group with a single aspiration; 14 women required a second procedure. In the SID group, resolution occurred in all cases after one procedure, but breastfeeding was discontinued in 65.1% versus 23.5% in the UGNA group (p<0.001). Wound healing time was significantly shorter after UGNA (mean 6.2 vs. 14.8 days). UGNA is effective for smaller abscesses and better supports continued lactation.

title: Pain Experience and Patient Satisfaction after Ultrasound-Guided Aspiration of Breast Abscess: Use of a Structured Visual Analogue Scale Protocol
abstract: Patient-reported outcomes are increasingly recognised as relevant endpoints in the management of breast abscess. This single-centre observational study assessed pain intensity and satisfaction in 67 lactating women undergoing ultrasound-guided needle aspiration at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina from 2011 to 2013. Pain was measured using a 100 mm visual analogue scale immediately after the procedure and at 24 hours and 72 hours. Satisfaction was recorded using a five-point Likert scale at the follow-up visit. Median procedural pain score was 38 mm (IQR 22–54). Pain decreased substantially by 72 hours to a median of 11 mm. Overall satisfaction was rated as good or very good by 82.1% of women. Anxiety about the procedure was identified as the strongest predictor of procedural pain (β=0.41; p=0.003). These data suggest that structured pre-procedural counselling could meaningfully reduce perceived pain and improve the clinical experience.

title: Non-Puerperal Breast Abscess: Clinical Features and Surgical Outcomes in 58 Cases
abstract: Non-puerperal breast abscess is less common than its lactational counterpart and carries a higher recurrence rate. This retrospective case series examined 58 women treated for non-puerperal breast abscess at two surgical centres in Vojvodina between 2008 and 2014. Cases were stratified by abscess location (central subareolar versus peripheral) and by smoking status. Central subareolar abscesses accounted for 67.2% of cases and were more frequently associated with periductal mastitis (74.4%). Recurrence occurred in 36.2% of all cases within twelve months; the recurrence rate was significantly higher in current smokers (53.6% vs. 21.4%; p=0.009) and in centrally located abscesses. Complete duct excision in centrally located cases reduced recurrence to 16.7%. Microbiological findings differed substantially from puerperal abscesses, with a higher prevalence of anaerobic organisms (27.6%). These findings argue for tailored surgical and antibiotic strategies in non-lactational presentations.

title: Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Lactational Mastitis in Primary Care in the Vojvodina Region: A Survey of General Practitioners
abstract: Lactational mastitis is commonly managed in primary care, yet prescribing practices vary widely. A structured questionnaire was distributed to 214 general practitioners working in primary health centres across Vojvodina in late 2015. The questionnaire addressed diagnostic criteria used, preferred antibiotics, duration of therapy, and advice given regarding breastfeeding continuation. The response rate was 71.5%. Flucloxacillin or cephalexin was the first-line choice in 48.4% of respondents; amoxicillin–clavulanate was preferred by 34.5%. Only 39% of respondents consistently advised continued breastfeeding or frequent milk expression during treatment. Treatment duration was seven days in 44.7% and ten or more days in 33.6% of cases. Fewer than one in five respondents had access to written local guidance. These results reveal substantial heterogeneity in practice and identify a need for region-specific clinical guidelines for lactational mastitis management in primary care settings.
