title: Intraoperative Frozen Section Analysis in Breast-Conserving Surgery for Early-Stage Invasive Carcinoma: Margin Assessment and Re-Excision Rates
abstract: Adequate surgical margins in breast-conserving surgery remain a source of intraoperative uncertainty. This study evaluated the performance of frozen section analysis (FSA) for intraoperative margin assessment in 112 consecutive women undergoing breast-conserving surgery for invasive carcinoma at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2013 and 2016. FSA sensitivity for positive margins was 81.3% and specificity 94.6% compared with definitive paraffin sections. The rate of intraoperative re-excision triggered by FSA was 17.9%; among these, final margins were clear in 90.0%. Overall re-operation rates (return to theatre) were 12.5% without FSA (historical control cohort, n=96) versus 6.3% with FSA (p=0.07). Tumour size, lobular histology, and proximity to the skin were independent predictors of positive margins on multivariate analysis. Processing time for FSA averaged 22 minutes. These data suggest FSA provides a clinically useful real-time margin assessment tool, although its incremental benefit requires evaluation in a larger randomised setting.

title: Breast Abscess Management in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Case Series from a Single Tertiary Centre
abstract: Breast abscess occurring during pregnancy is rare and poorly described in the literature. This paper presents a systematic review of published case reports and small series from 2000 to 2017 (17 publications identified; 49 total patients), combined with a retrospective case series of 11 pregnant women treated at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2007 and 2017. The review identified a predominance of Staphylococcus aureus aetiology (71.4%), with ultrasound-guided drainage used in 57.1% of published cases. In our series, nine women were managed with UGNA and two with SID; no adverse foetal outcomes were recorded. Gestational age at presentation ranged from 14 to 36 weeks. The main challenges identified were the safety of antibiotic choice in pregnancy, limited published guidance, and reluctance to perform repeated procedures near term. This combined analysis provides a practical reference for clinicians managing this uncommon condition.

title: Recurrence Predictors after Ultrasound-Guided Drainage of Lactational Breast Abscess: A Multivariate Analysis of 186 Women
abstract: Recurrence after apparently successful drainage of lactational breast abscess has been reported in 10–30% of cases. This prospective study enrolled 186 lactating women treated with ultrasound-guided needle aspiration at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2014 and 2018. Follow-up was conducted at one, four, and twelve weeks. Recurrence within twelve weeks occurred in 22.0% (n=41). Multivariate logistic regression identified initial abscess volume greater than 40 mL (OR 3.7; 95% CI 1.8–7.8), MRSA infection (OR 4.1; 95% CI 1.7–9.9), diabetes mellitus (OR 2.9; 95% CI 1.1–7.6), and a single aspiration without antibiotic therapy (OR 2.4; 95% CI 1.1–5.3) as independent predictors of recurrence. Breastfeeding cessation before drainage was associated with a trend toward higher recurrence but did not reach significance. A simple risk score derived from these predictors showed acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.73). These findings may help clinicians stratify patients for closer follow-up or earlier conversion to surgical drainage.

title: Impact of Delayed Presentation on Outcomes in Lactational Mastitis and Abscess: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Delay between symptom onset and first medical contact is considered a key determinant of outcomes in lactational mastitis and abscess, yet quantitative data from Southeast European settings are scarce. This retrospective cohort study included 224 women presenting to the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina with lactational mastitis (n=141) or abscess (n=83) between 2016 and 2020. Delay was defined as the interval between reported symptom onset and first medical consultation. Median delay was 4 days (IQR 2–7) in the mastitis group and 7 days (IQR 4–12) in the abscess group. Each additional day of delay was associated with a 19% increase in the odds of abscess formation (OR 1.19; 95% CI 1.09–1.30) and a 14% increase in the odds of requiring surgical rather than needle drainage (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.04–1.25). Women in rural municipalities showed significantly longer delays. Targeted public health messaging about early care-seeking may reduce disease severity and procedural burden.

title: Breastfeeding Support Practices of Maternity Ward Nurses and Their Association with Mastitis Incidence: A Cross-Sectional Study in Vojvodina Hospitals
abstract: Suboptimal breastfeeding technique is a modifiable risk factor for lactational mastitis. This cross-sectional study surveyed 178 maternity ward nurses working in eight hospitals across Vojvodina in 2021 using a validated knowledge and practice questionnaire, and linked aggregate nurse practice scores to institutional mastitis referral rates obtained from administrative databases. Nurses with higher scores on latch assessment and positioning guidance were employed in units with lower mastitis referral rates (Spearman ρ=−0.68; p=0.006). Forty-one percent of nurses reported they had not attended any breastfeeding-specific training in the preceding three years. Nurse-to-patient ratio and years of experience in maternity care were independently associated with practice score in multivariable linear regression. These findings suggest that structured continuing education for maternity nurses and improved staffing ratios may contribute to reducing mastitis incidence at the institutional level.

title: Outpatient versus Inpatient Management of Uncomplicated Lactational Breast Abscess: A Single-Centre Randomised Pilot Trial
abstract: Healthcare resource use in the management of lactational breast abscess can be reduced if outpatient protocols prove non-inferior to inpatient admission. This pilot randomised controlled trial allocated 64 women with abscesses between 10 and 50 mL to outpatient UGNA with oral antibiotics (n=32) or inpatient admission with UGNA and intravenous antibiotics for 48 hours followed by oral step-down (n=32). Primary outcomes were treatment failure at four weeks and breastfeeding continuation at eight weeks. Treatment failure occurred in 15.6% of the outpatient group versus 12.5% inpatient (risk difference 3.1%; 95% CI −14.2 to 20.4%). Breastfeeding continuation rates were comparable (59.4% vs. 56.3%). Mean inpatient stay was 3.2 days, with estimated bed-day cost saving of €210 per outpatient case. No serious adverse events occurred in either arm. The trial was not powered for definitive conclusions; a full multicentre trial with 220 participants per arm is warranted based on these estimates.

title: Tissue Biomarkers of Inflammation in Breast Abscess Capsule and Their Relationship to Recurrence: A Preliminary Histological and Immunohistochemical Analysis
abstract: The fibrous capsule surrounding a breast abscess may contain tissue changes that predispose to recurrence, yet its histological characterisation is rarely reported. In this preliminary study, capsule biopsy specimens were collected from 34 women undergoing surgical drainage of lactational (n=22) or non-lactational (n=12) breast abscess at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2022 and 2024. Haematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemical staining for CD68 (macrophages), CD3 (T-lymphocytes), and alpha-smooth muscle actin (myofibroblasts) were performed. Macrophage density was significantly higher in capsules from cases that subsequently recurred within six months (median 48 vs. 21 cells/HPF; p=0.01). Myofibroblast density was greater in non-lactational abscesses (p=0.03). No association was found between capsule thickness and recurrence. These preliminary data raise the question of whether capsule histology could serve as a tissue-based predictor of recurrence risk, pending validation in a larger prospective series.

title: Extracellular volume fraction by T1 mapping in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-sectional cardiac MRI study
abstract: Cardiac involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is frequently subclinical and underdiagnosed by conventional echocardiography. This cross-sectional study enrolled 48 consecutive SLE patients (mean age 38.4 ± 9.1 years, 87.5% female) fulfilling ACR/EULAR 2019 criteria and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. All participants underwent 1.5 T cardiac MRI using a Modified Look-Locker Inversion recovery (MOLLI) sequence for native and post-contrast T1 mapping, with extracellular volume fraction (ECV) calculated from haematocrit-corrected partition coefficients. Mean ECV was significantly elevated in SLE patients compared to controls (28.9 ± 3.4% vs. 25.1 ± 2.1%, p < 0.001). Late gadolinium enhancement was present in 10 of 48 patients (20.8%), predominantly in a non-ischaemic pattern. ECV correlated moderately with disease activity as measured by SLEDAI-2K scores (r = 0.41, p = 0.004). Left ventricular ejection fraction was preserved in all participants, underscoring the subclinical nature of observed changes. These findings suggest that diffuse interstitial fibrosis detectable by T1 mapping precedes overt functional impairment in SLE.

title: Late gadolinium enhancement patterns in systemic sclerosis: comparison of limited and diffuse cutaneous subtypes
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries one of the highest cardiovascular mortality rates among connective tissue diseases, yet cardiac MRI data from Southeast European cohorts remain scarce. This retrospective observational study reviewed cardiac MRI examinations performed between 2020 and 2023 in 35 SSc patients (22 limited cutaneous, 13 diffuse cutaneous) referred from the Rheumatology Ward of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was identified in 14 patients (40%), with the diffuse cutaneous subgroup showing a higher prevalence (7/13, 53.8%) compared to limited cutaneous patients (7/22, 31.8%), though the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.19), likely due to sample size limitations. LGE was most frequently located in the inferolateral and inferior segments in a patchy, mid-wall distribution consistent with replacement fibrosis. Right ventricular involvement, defined as RV free-wall LGE, was observed in 4 patients and was associated with elevated estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure on concurrent echocardiography. Findings indicate that cardiac MRI provides complementary information beyond echocardiography in SSc risk stratification.

title: Cardiac MRI in autoimmune rheumatic diseases: a practical review of acquisition protocols and clinical interpretation
abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging has become the reference standard for tissue characterisation of the myocardium, yet its application in autoimmune rheumatic diseases remains inconsistently implemented across clinical centres. This book chapter provides a structured overview of CMR acquisition protocols relevant to the rheumatological setting, covering cine imaging for functional assessment, T2-weighted sequences for oedema detection, T1 and T2 mapping for diffuse myocardial changes, and late gadolinium enhancement for focal fibrosis and necrosis. Practical guidance is offered on patient selection, contraindication screening for gadolinium-based contrast agents in the context of renal function, and reporting standards adapted from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance recommendations. Clinical interpretation sections are illustrated with representative cases from patients with SLE, SSc, and inflammatory myopathies. The chapter is aimed at rheumatology trainees and internal medicine residents beginning to incorporate CMR findings into multidisciplinary assessments.

title: Reproducibility of native T1 and ECV measurements at 1.5 T in a single-centre rheumatology cohort: intra- and inter-observer variability analysis
abstract: Quantitative cardiac MRI metrics such as native T1 relaxation times and extracellular volume fraction are increasingly used in research settings involving autoimmune diseases, but their reproducibility in routine clinical scanning environments has not been well characterised at regional centres. This methodological study assessed intra- and inter-observer variability of myocardial T1 and ECV measurements derived from MOLLI 5(3)3 sequences in 30 patients with systemic autoimmune diseases scanned on a 1.5 T Siemens Aera system at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Contour delineation was repeated by two independent observers and by the same observer at a two-week interval on standardised short-axis slices. Intraclass correlation coefficients exceeded 0.90 for both native T1 (ICC 0.93, 95% CI 0.87–0.96) and ECV (ICC 0.91, 95% CI 0.84–0.95). Coefficient of variation for native T1 was 2.7% intra-observer and 3.5% inter-observer. Results confirm adequate reproducibility for longitudinal monitoring applications in a non-dedicated cardiac MRI centre, provided standardised contouring guidelines are followed.

title: Subclinical myocardial involvement in early versus established rheumatoid arthritis assessed by cardiac MRI: preliminary findings from a prospective registry
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with excess cardiovascular mortality that is only partially explained by traditional risk factors. This preprint reports preliminary data from an ongoing prospective registry at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina enrolling RA patients stratified by disease duration: early RA (symptom onset < 12 months, n = 18) and established RA (disease duration > 5 years, n = 22). All participants underwent 1.5 T cardiac MRI including native T1 mapping, ECV quantification, and LGE imaging. Mean native T1 was higher in established compared to early RA patients (1006 ± 31 ms vs. 978 ± 28 ms, p = 0.008). LGE was detected in 4 patients with established RA (18.2%) and in none with early RA. Anti-CCP titre correlated positively with native T1 (r = 0.38, p = 0.02) across the full cohort. The registry is ongoing and powered for a final analysis at n = 80; current findings are considered hypothesis-generating. Full results are expected in 2026.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress markers in liver tissue from NASH patients: an immunohistochemical and gene expression study
abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress has been proposed as a mechanism linking lipid accumulation to hepatocyte injury in NASH, but tissue-level evidence in prospectively characterised human cohorts remains limited. We examined liver biopsies from 30 NASH patients (NAS ≥5) and 20 patients with simple steatosis (NAS ≤2) for protein expression of GRP78, CHOP, and phosphorylated eIF2α by immunohistochemistry, and quantified mRNA levels of ATF6, XBP1-spliced, and DDIT3 by real-time RT-PCR. GRP78 and CHOP protein expression were significantly higher in NASH versus steatosis (p<0.01 for both). XBP1-spliced mRNA was elevated 3.4-fold and DDIT3 4.1-fold in NASH tissue. GRP78 expression correlated with ballooning score (rs=0.58, p<0.001). These findings support a role for the unfolded protein response in hepatocyte ballooning and suggest that ER stress markers may help distinguish NASH from simple steatosis in tissue specimens when NAS scoring is borderline.

title: Shifts in fecal microbiota diversity during standard clarithromycin-based triple therapy for Helicobacter pylori: a prospective cohort study
abstract: This prospective cohort study examined gut microbiota changes in 48 adult patients receiving standard seven-day clarithromycin-based triple therapy (omeprazole, amoxicillin, clarithromycin) for confirmed Helicobacter pylori infection. Fecal samples were collected at baseline, on day seven of treatment, and at four and eight weeks post-treatment. Bacterial community profiles were generated using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing targeting the V3–V4 hypervariable region on an Illumina MiSeq platform. Alpha diversity, measured by Shannon index, decreased significantly from baseline (mean 3.41 ± 0.47) to end of treatment (mean 2.78 ± 0.52; p < 0.001). At four weeks post-treatment, partial recovery was observed, but Shannon index values remained significantly below baseline (mean 3.09 ± 0.49; p = 0.018). Bacteroidetes abundance declined by approximately 31% during treatment, while Proteobacteria showed a transient bloom. By week eight, microbiota composition had not fully returned to baseline in 62% of participants. These findings suggest that standard triple therapy produces measurable dysbiosis that persists beyond the conventional follow-up period in a substantial proportion of patients.

title: VDR polymorphisms as predictors of post-surgical relapse in Crohn's disease patients after ileocolic resection
abstract: Among 55 Crohn's disease patients who underwent ileocolic resection at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2012 and 2020, endoscopic recurrence at twelve months post-surgery (Rutgeerts score i2 or higher) was assessed in relation to preoperative VDR FokI and TaqI genotype, serum 25(OH)D, smoking status, and disease duration. Endoscopic recurrence occurred in 29 of 55 patients (52.7%). FokI FF genotype was present in 69% of those with recurrence versus 38% without (OR 3.62, 95% CI 1.28–10.23, p=0.015). Serum 25(OH)D below 25 nmol/L at the time of surgery was also independently associated with recurrence (OR 2.88, 95% CI 1.01–8.24). Neither smoking status nor disease duration reached significance in multivariate analysis. TaqI showed no significant association. These data suggest that VDR genotyping and perioperative vitamin D status measurement may help identify patients at elevated risk of post-surgical recurrence.

title: Range-only cooperative localisation for a pair of differential-drive robots using extended Kalman filtering
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of estimating the positions of two differential-drive robots that share only inter-robot distance measurements obtained from ultrasonic range sensors, with no access to fixed beacons or GPS. An extended Kalman filter is formulated in which the joint state vector concatenates the poses of both vehicles and range measurements enter as nonlinear observations. Wheel odometry provides the prediction step. Experiments were conducted on a 6 m × 4 m flat arena using two custom-built robots performing random waypoint trajectories. Over 20 runs of 5 minutes each, the proposed filter achieved a mean position error of 0.14 m compared with 0.41 m from dead reckoning alone. Observability conditions are analysed and it is shown that the system becomes unobservable when both robots move along parallel straight paths. The results confirm that even a single range link is sufficient for bounded error growth provided the robots maintain non-collinear motion.

title: Convergence analysis of a weighted average consensus protocol under intermittent communication links
abstract: Consensus-based distributed estimation relies on agents exchanging information over a network whose topology can change due to range limitations or packet loss. This paper analyses the convergence rate of a synchronous weighted average consensus protocol when the communication graph switches among a finite set of topologies according to a Markov chain. Using the joint spectral radius framework, sufficient conditions on the graph connectivity statistics are derived under which the protocol converges in mean square. Simulations with networks of 4, 8, and 16 nodes are used to validate the analytical bounds. For a packet loss probability of up to 0.3 on each link, the protocol converged in all tested configurations provided the expected graph remained connected. The study also quantifies the degradation in convergence speed as a function of link loss rate, offering practical guidance for setting communication duty cycles in battery-powered mobile robots.

title: Distributed Kalman consensus filter for localisation in a four-robot ground team
abstract: The Kalman consensus filter (KCF) extends the standard Kalman filter to a network of agents that each maintain a local state estimate and fuse information from neighbours via a consensus step. This paper presents an implementation of KCF for a team of four ground robots equipped with wheel encoders and a UWB ranging module per robot. Each robot runs a local filter using its own odometry and updates its estimate using range measurements to neighbours and a single consensus iteration per sampling period. The communication graph is fixed and fully connected. Indoor experiments in a 10 m × 8 m corridor environment show a mean absolute position error of 0.19 m averaged across all agents, compared to 0.52 m for independent dead reckoning. The number of consensus iterations needed for the filter to approximate the centralised Kalman solution is studied empirically, finding that two iterations suffice for the four-node graph tested.

title: Infrastructure-free relative pose estimation for heterogeneous ground–aerial robot pairs
abstract: Coordinating unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is complicated by their differing dynamics and the absence of a shared coordinate reference in GPS-denied environments. This paper proposes an approach in which a UGV and a quadrotor UAV each run local inertial–odometric filters and additionally exchange UWB range and Bluetooth received-signal-strength measurements. A cross-platform extended Kalman filter fuses these links to estimate the relative 3D pose between the two vehicles. The filter accounts for the height dimension explicitly, using barometric altitude from the UAV as a soft constraint. Datasets from 12 flight trials in a warehouse environment are used for evaluation, with a motion-capture system providing ground truth. The mean 3D position error between the two vehicles is 0.31 m at ranges up to 8 m. The paper also discusses failure modes when the UAV hovers directly above the UGV, which causes near-singular range geometry.

title: Effect of communication graph topology on localisation accuracy in distributed multi-robot Kalman filtering
abstract: In infrastructure-free multi-robot systems, the graph of inter-robot measurements directly shapes the information available to each local filter. This study systematically compares five graph topologies — path, ring, star, complete, and two random Erdős–Rényi graphs — for a team of six ground robots running a distributed information-form Kalman filter. Simulation experiments using a kinematic unicycle model and synthetic UWB noise (σ = 0.05 m) show that complete and star graphs yield similar final localisation error (0.12 m mean across agents), while path and ring graphs degrade to 0.28 m and 0.24 m respectively after 300 s. The relationship between algebraic connectivity of the graph and steady-state estimation covariance is examined and found to follow an approximately inverse-linear trend in the tested range. These results provide guidance on which inter-robot measurement links most improve collective localisation.

title: Distributed Kalman consensus filtering: algorithms and applications in multi-robot systems
abstract: This book chapter surveys the family of distributed Kalman consensus filters developed over the past decade and discusses their application to multi-robot localisation without fixed infrastructure. The chapter covers the derivation of the standard KCF, its information-form variant, and extensions that handle asynchronous communication and time-varying graphs. For each variant the conditions under which the distributed estimate converges to the centralised estimate are stated and the communication overhead is characterised. The second half of the chapter illustrates the algorithms on two case studies drawn from the authors' experimental work: a four-robot UWB-ranging system and a mixed ground–aerial team. Implementation notes address clock synchronisation, buffer management, and the handling of dropout events in ROS-based systems. The chapter concludes with a comparison table covering accuracy, bandwidth, and computational cost across the reviewed methods.

title: Tightly coupled IMU–UWB fusion for single-robot localisation as a building block for cooperative systems
abstract: Cooperative localisation algorithms typically assume that each robot has a reliable local motion model. This paper examines how tightly coupling an IMU with UWB two-way-ranging to a set of peer robots improves the single-agent state estimate that feeds into the cooperative filter. A multiplicative extended Kalman filter propagates IMU pre-integrated measurements and updates on UWB pseudo-ranges without first converting them to positions, avoiding linearisation errors introduced by range-to-position conversion. Tests on a single quadrotor in a 10 m × 6 m room show that the tightly coupled filter achieves 0.09 m RMSE in 3D position over 2-minute flights, versus 0.17 m for the loosely coupled baseline. When this improved local estimate is used as input to a two-UAV cooperative localisation trial, the cooperative estimate error drops by 22 % compared to using the loosely coupled input.

title: Characterising UWB ranging errors in industrial indoor environments for multi-robot localisation
abstract: UWB two-way ranging is a core measurement source for infrastructure-free cooperative localisation, but its error characteristics in cluttered industrial spaces are not well documented at the granularity needed for filter design. This paper presents a measurement campaign conducted in three indoor environments: an open sports hall, a workshop with metal shelving, and a partially obstructed warehouse aisle. A total of 48,000 range measurements were collected across robot-pair separations from 0.5 m to 15 m. The range error distribution is shown to be well approximated by a Gaussian with near-zero bias in line-of-sight conditions (σ = 0.04 m) but acquires a positive bias of up to 0.18 m and heavier tails in non-line-of-sight geometries. A simple geometric classifier using the received signal power and first-path amplitude identifies NLOS conditions with 83 % accuracy. Incorporating this classifier into the measurement noise model of a cooperative Kalman filter reduces the 95th-percentile position error by 31 % in the warehouse environment.

title: Latency and Throughput of ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in a Constrained TLS 1.3 Handshake Over LoRaWAN
abstract: LoRaWAN networks impose strict duty-cycle limits and maximum payload sizes (typically 51–242 bytes depending on spreading factor), making a standard TLS 1.3 handshake with post-quantum signatures highly problematic. We prototype a fragment-reassembly layer that segments ML-DSA-44 and SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s certificates and signature payloads across multiple LoRaWAN frames and measure end-to-end handshake completion time and energy on an STM32WL55 running at SF9 with BW125. ML-DSA-44 requires 38 uplink frames for a full handshake (certificate chain of one leaf and one intermediate), completing in 112 seconds under EU868 duty-cycle regulations; SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s requires 61 frames and 181 seconds. For comparison, a classical ECDSA P-256 handshake requires 9 frames and 26 seconds. We quantify the trade-off between quantum security and network overhead and propose a certificate compression scheme that reduces ML-DSA-44 frame count to 27 with no loss of security. Results are validated on a physical three-node LoRaWAN testbed using a Semtech SX1262 gateway.

title: Personalisation of wrist-based activity recognition models using federated fine-tuning on edge devices
abstract: Generic activity recognition models trained on population data perform unevenly across individuals due to differences in movement style, limb length, and device fit. This study examines federated fine-tuning as a means to personalise a shared 1-D CNN deployed on wrist-worn nodes without transferring raw sensor data to a central server. Twenty-two participants contributed 30 minutes each of labelled everyday activity data collected over one week at home. A federated learning protocol with five aggregation rounds and local fine-tuning on each device is compared against a static global model and a fully local model. Federated fine-tuning improves mean per-subject macro-F1 from 0.883 (global) to 0.911 while the fully local model achieves 0.918 but requires twice as much on-device labelled data per subject. Communication overhead and battery impact measured on a Nordic Semiconductor development kit are reported alongside accuracy results.

title: Carry-over of oxytetracycline from medicated broiler feed to muscle and liver tissue: a dose-response experiment under commercial feeding conditions
abstract: A controlled feeding trial was conducted with 240 Ross 308 broilers divided into four groups receiving oxytetracycline-supplemented feed at 200, 400, 600, and 800 mg/kg for seven days, followed by a five-day withdrawal period. Tissue samples (muscle, liver, kidney, skin-plus-fat) were collected at days 0, 1, 3, and 5 post-withdrawal and analysed by HPLC-MS/MS. Carry-over coefficients were calculated as the ratio of tissue residue concentration to mean daily feed intake-adjusted dose. At day 0 post-withdrawal, liver carry-over reached 0.042 at the highest dose level, exceeding the EU maximum residue limit of 600 µg/kg in all dosed groups. By day 5, muscle residues in the 200 mg/kg group fell below the 100 µg/kg MRL threshold. A linear relationship between dietary concentration and liver carry-over coefficient was observed (R² = 0.91). The data provide empirical basis for withdrawal period estimation models applicable under Serbian and EU regulatory frameworks.

title: Sulfonamide residues in eggs following administration of sulfadiazine in layer feed: kinetics and excretion patterns
abstract: Forty Lohmann Brown layers were fed sulfadiazine at 100 mg/kg feed for five consecutive days. Egg white and yolk samples were collected individually from each hen daily from day 1 of treatment through day 10 post-withdrawal. Sulfadiazine and its N4-acetyl metabolite were quantified by HPLC-MS/MS. Peak sulfadiazine concentrations in yolk reached 420 ± 38 µg/kg on day 3 of treatment, while egg white concentrations were consistently lower (mean 210 ± 29 µg/kg). Both compartments showed biphasic elimination; estimated half-lives were 1.9 days (egg white) and 3.2 days (yolk). Residues in yolk remained above the EU MRL of 100 µg/kg until day 7 post-withdrawal. Carry-over from feed to whole egg averaged 0.18% on a mass basis. Results indicate that current five-day withdrawal periods may be insufficient for yolk at this dosage, and regulatory guidance should account for compartment-specific kinetics.

title: A probabilistic dietary exposure model for sulfonamide residues in pork: integrating feed contamination variability and consumer intake distributions
abstract: A tiered probabilistic exposure assessment was developed for sulfonamide residues (sulfadiazine, sulfamethazine, sulfathiazole) in pork muscle, targeting the general adult population in Serbia. Residue concentration distributions were derived from 318 official monitoring samples collected by the Serbian Veterinary Directorate over 2012–2016. Consumer intake data were drawn from the national dietary survey conducted in 2013 (n = 1,847 adults). A Monte Carlo simulation with 100,000 iterations was implemented in R, sampling independently from residue and intake distributions. The 95th percentile estimated dietary exposure to total sulfonamides was 0.031 µg/kg body weight/day, well below the ADI of 0.1 µg/kg bw/day established by EMA. Sensitivity analysis showed that residue concentration variance contributed 73% of total output variance, underlining the importance of monitoring data quality. The model structure is adaptable to other drug–species combinations and can serve as a regulatory screening tool.

title: Residues of flubendazole in eggs and laying hen tissues after repeated oral administration via drinking water: a withdrawal period study
abstract: Flubendazole was administered to 60 commercial Hy-Line Brown layers via drinking water at a dose of 1 mg/kg body weight/day for five days. Birds were slaughtered in groups of 10 at 0, 2, 4, 7, 10, and 14 days post-treatment, and eggs were collected daily. Flubendazole and its hydrolysis metabolite (HFBZ) were quantified in yolk, albumen, muscle, liver, and kidney by validated HPLC-MS/MS (LOQ 1 µg/kg). Parent drug concentrations in liver peaked at 780 µg/kg on day 0 and declined to below the 400 µg/kg MRL by day 4. Yolk concentrations remained detectable until day 10 (mean 18 µg/kg), while albumen cleared by day 7. HFBZ constituted 30–45% of total hepatic residue marker fraction throughout the observation period. Observed kinetics were incorporated into a one-compartment depletion model to estimate a withdrawal period of 9 days for eggs with 95% statistical confidence at the 95th percentile of the flock.

title: Aggregate dietary exposure to tetracycline-class residues across poultry meat, eggs, and honey in Serbia: a deterministic and probabilistic comparison
abstract: An aggregate exposure assessment was performed for tetracycline residues (tetracycline, oxytetracycline, chlortetracycline, doxycycline) combining three food matrices: broiler muscle (n = 412 monitoring samples), table eggs (n = 187), and honey (n = 94), all from 2018–2022 national monitoring databases. A deterministic scenario used mean contamination and 97.5th percentile consumer intake; a probabilistic scenario ran 200,000 Monte Carlo iterations drawing from fitted log-normal residue distributions and empirical intake distributions from the 2019 Serbian national dietary survey. Aggregate tetracycline exposure at the 95th percentile was 0.048 µg/kg bw/day (probabilistic), compared with 0.071 µg/kg bw/day under the deterministic approach. Neither estimate exceeded the group ADI of 0.3 µg/kg bw/day. Honey contributed less than 4% of aggregate exposure despite higher mean residue concentrations, due to low consumption frequency. The study demonstrates that deterministic approaches may overestimate exposure by up to 48% compared with probabilistic methods for this compound group.

title: Effect of sulphur dioxide residues in grape pomace on the extractability and stability of anthocyanins
abstract: Winemaking pomace routinely contains residual SO₂ from oenological use, yet its effect on subsequent anthocyanin extraction is rarely quantified. This study used pomace batches from the same Merlot vintage with measured free SO₂ levels of 12, 45, and 89 mg kg⁻¹ fresh weight, obtained by varying SO₂ additions during winemaking at a cooperating facility. Extractions were performed under standardised UAE conditions (220 W, 28 min, 60% ethanol). TAC in extracts decreased from 7.4 to 5.1 mg CGE g⁻¹ dry weight as pomace SO₂ increased, likely due to anthocyanin–SO₂ adduct formation reducing free monomeric pigment. HPLC analysis confirmed a parallel reduction in detectable malvidin-3-glucoside peak area (−38% from low to high SO₂ batch). Colour intensity (A₅₂₀) was inversely correlated with pomace SO₂ (r = −0.94). After storing extracts at 20 °C for 14 days at pH 3.5, residual SO₂ in the extract did not confer a significant protective effect against colour loss, contrary to its known role in wine. These results suggest that low-SO₂ winemaking practices are preferable when pomace is destined for pigment recovery.

title: Cyclostationary Features for Modulation Classification of PSK and QAM Signals at Low SNR
abstract: This paper examines the use of second-order cyclostationary statistics for distinguishing between BPSK, QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM waveforms under additive white Gaussian noise conditions. Cyclic autocorrelation functions and spectral correlation density estimates were computed from captured baseband samples obtained with a USRP N210 platform. A total of 12,000 signal segments, each 4096 samples in length, were generated at SNR values ranging from −4 dB to 20 dB. Feature vectors of dimension 24 were constructed from cyclic frequency bins and fed into a multi-class support vector machine with an RBF kernel. Classification accuracy reached 91.3% at 0 dB SNR and 97.8% at 10 dB SNR across the five modulation classes. The effect of carrier frequency offset up to 500 Hz was also evaluated, showing a classification degradation of less than 3 percentage points. Results are compared against a likelihood-based classifier from the literature, with the SVM approach offering a factor of eight reduction in computational time per segment.

title: Influence of Multipath Fading on Cyclic Feature Extraction for Modulation Recognition
abstract: The paper investigates how multipath propagation distorts the cyclostationary properties of digitally modulated signals and the downstream effect on automatic modulation classification performance. Rayleigh and Rician fading channels with delay spreads of 0.5 µs and 2 µs were simulated for BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM, and MSK waveforms at symbol rates of 10 and 100 ksymbols/s. Cyclic autocorrelation estimates were computed using the time-smoothing method over observation windows of 8192 samples. A support vector machine trained on AWGN data was tested against faded signals without retraining to measure robustness. Average classification accuracy dropped from 94% under AWGN to 78% under Rayleigh fading at 6 dB SNR. A simple pre-equalisation step using a least-squares channel estimator partially recovered accuracy to 86%. The study quantifies the sensitivity of individual cyclic frequencies to channel dispersion, identifying the set of features that degrade least under realistic propagation. Practical implications for spectrum monitoring in urban radio environments are discussed.

title: Automatic Modulation Classification in Cognitive Radio Networks: A Feature-Based Approach Using Cyclostationary Analysis
abstract: Chapter examining modulation classification as an enabling technology for cognitive radio spectrum access. The chapter reviews cyclostationary feature extraction methods, contrasts them with likelihood-ratio and deep learning approaches, and argues for the continued relevance of SVM classifiers in resource-constrained cognitive radio terminals. A case study is presented in which a USRP-based secondary user node classifies incumbent transmissions across a 10 MHz band segment in real time. The experimental setup captures DVB-T, GSM, and LTE pilot bursts and extracts spectral correlation features at cycle frequencies corresponding to known symbol rates. Classification results are reported for each signal type, with overall accuracy of 88% under operational conditions. Computational profiling on an ARM Cortex-A9 processor shows that feature extraction accounts for 73% of total processing time, motivating selective cyclic frequency evaluation. The chapter concludes with a discussion of integration challenges in standards-compliant cognitive radio prototypes.

title: SNR Estimation as a Preprocessing Step in SVM-Based Modulation Classifiers
abstract: Accurate SNR estimation prior to classification can improve modulation recognition by allowing the classifier to operate on SNR-stratified feature spaces. This paper proposes a two-stage architecture in which a moment-based SNR estimator first partitions incoming signal segments into three SNR regimes — below 2 dB, 2–10 dB, and above 10 dB — and then routes them to one of three SVM classifiers trained specifically within that regime. The approach is validated on a dataset of 24,000 segments for eight modulation types generated at SNR values from −2 dB to 18 dB. The moment-based estimator achieved mean absolute estimation error of 1.2 dB across the tested range. The two-stage classifier improved overall accuracy by 4.1 percentage points compared to a single SVM trained across all SNR conditions, with the most significant gains observed for 64-QAM and 8-PSK below 6 dB. Computational overhead of the SNR estimation stage is 7% of total processing time. The architecture is implemented and tested on a GNU Radio flowgraph with a USRP B210 front end.

title: Comparison of Cyclostationary Feature Extraction and Convolutional Neural Networks for Modulation Classification Under Phase Noise
abstract: Phase noise introduced by oscillator imperfections degrades classification performance in both feature-based and deep learning approaches to automatic modulation recognition. This paper directly compares a cyclostationary-feature plus SVM pipeline against a convolutional neural network (CNN) applied to raw in-phase and quadrature samples, under phase noise conditions modelled by a Wiener process with variances of 10−4, 10−3, and 10−2 rad²/sample. Eight modulation classes were used: BPSK, QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM, AM, FM, and FSK. At low phase noise (10−4) and SNR above 8 dB, both methods achieved above 95% accuracy. At higher phase noise (10−3), the cyclostationary-SVM approach degraded by 6 percentage points less than the CNN on average, suggesting that cyclic features are more robust to oscillator drift. Below 0 dB SNR, the CNN outperformed the SVM by up to 5 percentage points for high-order QAM. The study also reports training and inference latency, showing that the SVM pipeline is 14 times faster at inference on a standard x86 CPU. Implications for hardware deployment in portable monitoring equipment are discussed.

title: Real-Time Modulation Classification on FPGA Using Reduced Cyclic Feature Sets
abstract: This paper addresses the implementation of a modulation classifier on an FPGA target with strict latency and power constraints, targeting applications in portable spectrum monitoring. A feature selection procedure based on mutual information ranking reduced a 24-dimensional cyclostationary feature vector to 8 dimensions while retaining 96% of the classification accuracy of the full feature set on a benchmark of seven modulation types. The selected feature set was implemented in fixed-point arithmetic on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA. The SVM decision function was pre-computed as a lookup table for the reduced input space. End-to-end latency from sample capture to classification output was 1.3 ms for a 4096-sample observation window at 2 Msamples/s, meeting the design target. Resource utilisation was 34% of available LUTs and 12% of DSP slices. Classification accuracy on hardware matched simulation results within 0.5 percentage points. Power consumption of the classification module measured 180 mW at operating frequency of 100 MHz. The design is compared with a CPU-based reference implementation and a previously published ASIC classifier from the literature.

title: Modulation Classification of Frequency-Hopping Signals Using Segment-Level Cyclostationary Analysis
abstract: Frequency-hopping spread spectrum signals present a particular challenge for automatic modulation classification because the dwell time per hop is short, limiting the number of samples available for feature estimation. This paper proposes a segment-level approach in which hop boundaries are first detected using an energy change-point algorithm, and cyclostationary features are then estimated independently for each dwell segment. A hop duration of 2 ms at symbol rates of 125 and 250 ksymbols/s was evaluated, yielding 250–500 symbols per segment. Experiments were conducted using over-the-air captures with two USRP X310 radios. Four modulation types — BPSK, QPSK, GFSK, and 16-QAM — were tested in an indoor office environment. Change-point detection achieved a hop boundary localisation error below 10 samples in 92% of cases at SNR above 4 dB. Per-hop classification accuracy was 87.4% on average. Aggregation of per-hop decisions using a majority vote over five consecutive hops increased accuracy to 93.6%. The method is compared against a short-time Fourier transform baseline that does not incorporate cyclostationary information.

title: Dataset and Benchmark for Automatic Modulation Classification Under Realistic Impairments: A Regional Radio Environment Survey
abstract: Publicly available modulation classification datasets are predominantly simulation-generated and do not reflect the impairments present in real regional radio environments. This paper describes the collection, annotation, and release of a captured signal dataset assembled from monitoring stations in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin over a six-month period in 2023–2024. Signals were recorded across the 70–900 MHz band using USRP B205mini units and calibrated omnidirectional antennas. A total of 38,400 labelled segments covering AM-DSB, AM-SSB, FM, GFSK, BPSK, QPSK, and 16-QAM were extracted through a semi-automated annotation pipeline verified by manual inspection. Each segment is accompanied by metadata including estimated SNR, centre frequency, bandwidth, and time of capture. Baseline classification results using three methods — cyclostationary-SVM, random forest, and a compact CNN — are reported. The cyclostationary-SVM achieved 85.2% accuracy on the full dataset; the CNN achieved 87.7%. The dataset is made available under a Creative Commons licence. Benchmark protocol and evaluation metrics are defined to facilitate future comparisons.

title: Gate driver propagation delay and its impact on dead-time setting in a 500 kHz GaN synchronous rectifier
abstract: Dead-time management in GaN synchronous rectifiers is constrained by propagation delay spread in the gate-driver path and by device turn-off speed. This paper characterises the propagation delay distribution of a commercial isolated gate driver IC over supply voltage (4.5–6 V), temperature (−20 to 150 °C), and input signal slew rate (1–50 V/ns). Mean propagation delay was 18.4 ns with a three-sigma spread of 5.1 ns. A statistical dead-time design methodology is derived, incorporating delay spread, device fall-time distribution, and converter-level shoot-through current risk. Experimental validation on a 48 V / 5 V, 300 W, 500 kHz synchronous buck converter showed that the statistically derived minimum dead time of 23 ns reduced body-diode conduction loss by 1.8 W compared to a conservative 50 ns dead time, improving full-load efficiency from 95.1 % to 95.9 %. An adaptive dead-time control loop based on drain-voltage zero-crossing detection is also evaluated.

title: Mössbauer characterisation of iron oxides in Pleistocene loess from the Titel plateau, Serbia
abstract: Loess-palaeosol sequences on the Titel plateau (Vojvodina, northern Serbia) were sampled at 5 cm resolution across three glacial–interglacial cycles. Transmission ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectra were recorded at 300 K and 77 K using a constant-acceleration spectrometer with a ⁵⁷Co/Rh source. Spectral fitting identified goethite, haematite, magnetite, ilmenite, and a ferrihydrite-like doublet in proportions that shift systematically between loess units and palaeosol horizons. The goethite-to-haematite area ratio (Gt/Hm) reached 3.1 ± 0.2 in the S1 palaeosol, compared with 0.8 ± 0.1 in the overlying L1 loess, consistent with wetter and warmer interglacial weathering. Magnetic hyperfine fields of haematite at 77 K ranged from 51.2 to 53.6 T across the sequence, suggesting variable Al-substitution. Results were correlated with independently obtained grain-size and carbonate records, confirming that Fe-oxide assemblages are a robust proxy for moisture availability on millennial timescales in the Pannonian Basin.

title: CEMS depth profiling of a modern Chernozem profile from Bačka: implications for iron redistribution under current land use
abstract: Conversion electron Mössbauer spectroscopy (CEMS) was applied to polished cross-sections of intact soil aggregates collected from a 150 cm deep Chernozem profile near Bečej, Vojvodina. Measurements at 300 K and 80 K resolved a surface-sensitive signal to depths of approximately 200 nm, allowing comparison of grain-surface iron speciation with bulk transmission spectra obtained from the same horizons. Fe²⁺ doublet contributions in the illite/smectite mixed-layer fraction increased from 8% at the surface to 19% at 90 cm depth, indicative of reducing microenvironments in the deeper Bk horizon. Magnetite octahedral-site occupancy estimated from low-temperature spectra was consistent with partial oxidation to maghemite in the upper 30 cm, plausibly linked to repeated tillage aeration. A companion X-ray diffraction dataset confirmed the clay mineralogy. The study demonstrates that CEMS is practical on intact soil aggregates and that a single Chernozem profile integrates both pedogenic and anthropogenic Fe-cycling signals separable by depth.

title: Effect of freeze–thaw cycling on iron oxide assemblages in loess: a laboratory simulation
abstract: Loess samples from the L2 unit of the Titel plateau were subjected to controlled freeze–thaw cycling in the laboratory: 0, 10, 50, and 100 cycles between −18 °C and +20 °C under two moisture conditions (field capacity and air-dry). After each treatment, samples were characterised by transmission Mössbauer spectroscopy at 300 K and 80 K, XRD, and magnetic susceptibility. After 100 cycles under moist conditions, the ferrihydrite doublet area fraction increased by 6 ± 1.5 percentage points relative to untreated controls, and the magnetite sextet showed a slight increase in vacancy concentration estimated from the B-site hyperfine field. Dry cycling produced no statistically significant change in Mössbauer parameters. Magnetic susceptibility increased by 12% after 100 moist cycles, consistent with a minor neoformation of fine-grained magnetite or maghemite. Results suggest that repeated periglacial freeze–thaw can partly overprint the primary pedogenic Fe-oxide signature in loess deposited at high latitudes or elevations, a factor to consider in palaeoclimate interpretations.

title: Mössbauer and thermogravimetric study of maghemite transformation during heating in palaeosol-derived samples
abstract: Samples from three S1 palaeosol horizons from sites in Vojvodina and one from Slavonia (Croatia) were heated stepwise from 25 °C to 700 °C in air in a tube furnace, with aliquots extracted at 100 °C intervals and analysed by transmission Mössbauer spectroscopy at 300 K and by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The sequential Mössbauer spectra tracked the conversion of maghemite (γ-Fe₂O₃) to haematite (α-Fe₂O₃), which was complete by 500 °C across all samples. The transformation onset temperature varied from 420 °C to 465 °C and correlated positively with initial Al content estimated from haematite hyperfine fields (r = 0.76). TGA mass loss curves between 200 and 400 °C were attributed to dehydroxylation of goethite; derived activation energies ranged from 88 to 103 kJ mol⁻¹. The dataset provides reference transformation temperatures useful for interpreting Mössbauer spectra of thermally affected archaeological and geological materials and contributes to understanding how maghemite abundance in palaeosols should be interpreted with respect to burning or volcanic heating events.

title: Low-temperature Mössbauer spectroscopy of iron-bearing minerals in aeolian dust collected over the southern Pannonian Plain: comparison with source loess
abstract: Aerosol filter samples and bulk dust collected at three monitoring stations in Vojvodina during nine Saharan dust episodes (2019–2022) were compared with loess and palaeosol reference samples from Titel using ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy at 300 K, 130 K, and 20 K. At 20 K, Saharan dust showed a broad haematite sextet with a mean hyperfine field of 52.8 ± 0.4 T and a goethite contribution constituting 31 ± 5% of total spectral area, whereas Vojvodina loess haematite fields peaked at 53.9 ± 0.3 T. The ferrihydrite-like doublet was proportionally larger (18 ± 4%) in Saharan dust than in local loess (4 ± 2%), consistent with transport of freshly weathered material. Isomer shift values for the Fe³⁺ doublet component differed by 0.04 mm s⁻¹ between the two sources, marginally but reproducibly. These fingerprinting parameters may assist in separating local and distal dust contributions when interpreting Fe-oxide records in Pannonian loess archives.

title: Mössbauer spectroscopy of iron phases in medieval kiln-fired ceramics from Sirmium: pedogenic versus pyrogenic iron signal
abstract: Twelve ceramic sherds from the late-Roman and early-medieval site of Sirmium (Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia) were analysed by ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy alongside six raw clay samples from geologically mapped sources within a 30 km radius. Spectra recorded at 300 K and 77 K were decomposed into contributions from haematite, ilmenite, a Fe²⁺ pyroxene-like doublet, and a paramagnetic Fe³⁺ doublet assigned to glass-phase iron. Firing temperature estimates based on the reduction of goethite and the appearance of pyroxene-like Fe²⁺ ranged from 750 °C to 1050 °C, consistent with archaeometric kiln-temperature estimates from associated slag. The Gt/Hm ratio was near zero in all fired sherds but ranged from 0.5 to 1.8 in raw clays, confirming thermal destruction of goethite above 400 °C. Source matching using Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ ratios and haematite hyperfine field values tentatively assigned eight sherds to a clay source south of the Sava River. This application demonstrates that Mössbauer spectroscopy developed for loess studies transfers with minor adaptation to archaeometry.

title: Stochastic energetics of run-and-tumble bacteria confined in microchannel geometries
abstract: This paper analyses the thermodynamic cost of run-and-tumble motility in bacterial populations confined to microchannels of widths between 5 µm and 100 µm. We model individual cells as point particles executing exponentially distributed run phases interspersed with instantaneous tumble reorientations, with experimentally motivated run speed of 20 µm s⁻¹ and tumbling rate of 1 s⁻¹. Entropy production is calculated along single trajectories using the Hatano–Sasa framework. Confinement reduces the effective diffusivity by up to 40% relative to bulk, while entropy production per unit time increases by 15–25% due to enhanced wall interactions. We demonstrate that the excess entropy production scales linearly with the inverse channel width for widths below 20 µm. The results are compared with simulations of 5000 independent trajectories and show good agreement. We discuss implications for energy consumption estimates in microfluidic devices used in biotechnology.

title: Uticaj koeficijenta prigušenja virtuelnog sinhronskog generatora na stabilnost frekvencije u islandovanim mikrogreжama
abstract: Rad analizira uticaj koeficijenta prigušenja D u modelu virtuelnog sinhronskog generatora (VSG) na dinamiku frekvencije u islandovanim mikrogreжama sa dominantnim udelom inverterskih izvora. Ispitivanje je sprovedeno na laboratorijskom postrojenju sastavljenom od dva trofazna naponska invertora snage 10 kVA svaki, povezana zajedničkim AC magistralom, sa otpornom i induktivnom opterećenjem promenljive veličine. Za svaki od sedam vrednosti koeficijenta D u opsegu 0,5–8,0, primenjena je skup-krok poremećaj opterećenjem od 30% nominalne snage, a registrovani su minimalna vrednost frekvencije (fmin), vreme oporavka i ustaljeno odstupanje. Rezultati pokazuju da povećanje D iznad vrednosti 4,0 smanjuje prenapon pri povratku frekvencije, ali produžava vreme oporavka za prosečno 18%. Identifikovana je zona optimalnih vrednosti D između 2,5 i 3,5 pri kojoj su istovremeno zadovoljeni kriterijumi minimalnog prepada i brzog oporavka. Analiza je potvrđena i HIL simulacijom na Typhoon HIL 604 platformi pri identičnim scenarijima poremećaja, uz slaganje rezultata unutar 4% u svim merenim veličinama.

title: Comparative Assessment of Droop and VSG Control for Frequency Regulation in a Photovoltaic-Battery Islanded Microgrid
abstract: This paper compares conventional droop control and virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control applied to a 20 kW islanded microgrid consisting of a photovoltaic array, a 48 V lithium-iron-phosphate battery bank, and a resistive–inductive load bank. Both controllers were implemented on a TMS320F28379D digital signal processor and tested under three load-step scenarios: 25%, 50%, and 75% of rated load applied within a 100 ms ramp. Frequency nadir, rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), and settling time were recorded for each scenario. VSG control reduced peak RoCoF by 34–41% compared to droop control across all tested scenarios, at the cost of a 12–17% longer settling time. Battery current stress, measured as the standard deviation of current over the transient window, was 22% lower under VSG control for the 75% step case. Harmonic distortion of the output voltage remained below 2.1% THD in all cases for both strategies. The results suggest that VSG control offers a meaningful improvement in frequency quality metrics relevant to sensitive loads, though the tuning of inertia constant H and damping coefficient D requires careful co-optimisation to avoid excessive transient duration.

title: Adaptivna emulacija inercije u mrežno-formirajućim invertorima primenom proporcionalnog skaliranja inercijske konstante u realnom vremenu
abstract: U ovom radu predložena je strategija adaptivne emulacije inercije za mrežno-formirajuće invertore u kojoj se vrednost virtuelne inercijske konstante H dinamički menja u zavisnosti od trenutne brzine promene frekvencije (RoCoF) i stanja napunjenosti (SoC) baterijskog sistema za skladištenje energije. Algoritam je implementiran na digitalnom signalnom procesoru i verifikovan na eksperimentalnoj platformi sa jednim invertorom snage 5 kVA i LFP baterijom kapaciteta 10 kWh. Konstanta H menja se linearno u opsegu 2–8 s u ovisnosti o izmerenom RoCoF i SoC, pri čemu je definisana zona zaštite kada SoC padne ispod 20%, u kojoj se H ograničava na vrednost 2 s radi zaštite baterije od prekomerne strujne naprezanja. U 45 testiranih scenarija poremećaja opterećenja, predložena adaptivna metoda smanjila je energiju prenesenu iz baterije za vreme frekventnog odziva za prosečno 16% u poređenju sa fiksnom vrednošću H = 5 s, uz istovremeno održavanje fmin iznad praga od 49,2 Hz u svim slučajevima. Rezultati HIL verifikacije potvrđuju konzistentnost sa laboratorijskim merenjima.

title: Small-Signal Stability Analysis of a Multi-Inverter Islanded Microgrid Under Mixed VSG and Droop Control
abstract: The paper presents a small-signal state-space model of a four-inverter islanded microgrid in which two units operate under VSG control and two under droop control, representing a realistic scenario of gradual converter replacement in an existing installation. The model captures the inner current and voltage control loops, the LC output filter dynamics, and the virtual inertia swing equation. Eigenvalue loci are computed for a range of load conditions (10–100% of rated 40 kW total capacity) and for VSG inertia constants H between 1 and 10 s. A critical oscillatory mode at approximately 8–12 Hz is identified whose damping ratio drops below 0.05 when H exceeds 7 s at light load, indicating a risk of sustained oscillation. Participation factor analysis shows that this mode is primarily associated with the VSG damping loops and the network inductance. The model predictions are validated against time-domain HIL simulations on a Typhoon HIL 604 platform, with eigenvalue estimates matching observed oscillation frequencies within 6% across all tested operating points. Practical tuning guidelines for the damping coefficient as a function of load fraction are derived from the analysis.

title: Gridless DOA Estimation via Atomic Norm Minimization for Small Arrays With Correlated Noise: A Comparative Study
abstract: Atomic norm minimization (ANM) provides a gridless alternative to subspace methods for DOA estimation, with theoretical recovery guarantees under certain conditions on source separation and snapshot count. This paper benchmarks ANM against MUSIC with covariance reconstruction on arrays of five and seven elements under spatially correlated noise, using between 20 and 500 snapshots. Three noise correlation levels (low: 0.2, moderate: 0.5, high: 0.75) are considered at SNRs of 0, 5, and 10 dB. ANM is solved using a standard semidefinite programming solver. For more than 100 snapshots and moderate SNR, ANM and reconstruction-based MUSIC show comparable RMSE. Below 50 snapshots, ANM is more stable but its computational cost is approximately 40 times higher on the tested hardware. The study identifies snapshot count and source separation as the main factors determining the crossover point, offering practical guidance for choosing between the two approaches in constrained systems.

title: Seminal root angle variability in winter wheat landraces grown on contrasting Chernozem soil moisture gradients
abstract: Seminal root angle (SRA) is a heritable trait that influences the spatial distribution of roots in the soil profile and may affect water uptake under terminal drought. We evaluated SRA in 48 winter wheat landraces from the ex situ collection of the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, across two growing seasons (2009–2010) at the Rimski Šančevi field station using a paper-based excavation and manual goniometry protocol. Soil volumetric water content was monitored at 20 cm intervals to 100 cm depth using a capacitance probe. SRA ranged from 28° to 67° across accessions. A mixed-model analysis of variance partitioned 61% of phenotypic variance to genotype and 18% to season, with a genotype-by-season interaction accounting for a further 11%. Five landraces from the Vojvodina region consistently displayed narrow angles below 35°, suggesting constitutive deep-rooting tendency. Correlation between SRA and grain yield under water-limited conditions was negative (r = −0.41, P < 0.01), supporting the hypothesis that steeper root growth is associated with better subsoil water capture in this environment. These results form the basis for targeted crossing programmes at the institute.

title: Comparison of shovelomics and soil core washing for estimating root crown architecture traits in field-grown maize
abstract: Shovelomics and soil core washing are the two most widely applied destructive field phenotyping methods for maize root crowns, yet systematic side-by-side comparisons under Pannonian field conditions are sparse. We assessed five root crown traits—nodal root number, first-whorl angle, lateral branching density, root diameter, and crown width—in 12 maize hybrids at two plant densities across two sites in 2012. At each site and density combination, 30 plants per hybrid were excavated by shovel and an adjacent 30 by 20 cm diameter soil core to 35 cm depth. Cores were washed on a 1 mm mesh and scanned with a flatbed scanner; shovel crowns were photographed with a calibrated overhead rig. Nodal root number showed strong agreement between methods (intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC = 0.91), while first-whorl angle deviated more substantially (ICC = 0.74), presumably because coring disrupts the natural root trajectory. Shovelomics throughput was 2.3-fold higher per person-hour. We recommend shovelomics for angle and count traits in large trials and core washing when fresh root mass and diameter distribution are required.

title: Root system architecture phenotyping of sunflower inbred lines at mid-season: protocol development and trait heritability
abstract: Sunflower root architecture has received substantially less phenotyping attention than that of maize or wheat, despite sunflower's importance in the Pannonian cropping system and its deep-rooting reputation. We developed a shovelomics-based field protocol adapted for sunflower's coarser, tap-rooted architecture and applied it to 24 inbred lines from the Novi Sad breeding programme at growth stage R2 in 2014 and 2015. Root crowns were excavated to 30 cm, placed on a scaled grid, and photographed. Seven traits were scored or measured: tap root diameter at 5 cm depth, number of primary lateral roots, lateral insertion angle (upper 10 cm), lateral root density (roots per 5 cm), presence of secondary branching, crown diameter, and lateral root length estimated by WinRHIZO on washed sub-samples. Broad-sense heritability ranged from 0.52 for lateral root density to 0.79 for tap root diameter. The protocol showed acceptable inter-rater repeatability (ICC > 0.80 for all traits). Results suggest that tap root diameter and primary lateral number are tractable targets for indirect selection in sunflower breeding.

title: Genotype-by-environment interaction for nodal root angle in maize across six Pannonian environments
abstract: Understanding the stability of root architecture traits across environments is essential before phenotypic selection can be incorporated into applied breeding. We evaluated nodal root angle (NRA) in 30 experimental maize hybrids across six environments (three sites × two years, 2014–2015) in northern Serbia, southern Hungary, and eastern Croatia. Sites differed in soil texture (sandy loam to clay loam) and available water capacity. Plants were excavated at V9 using shovelomics; NRA was measured on digital photographs in ImageJ. AMMI (Additive Main effects and Multiplicative Interaction) analysis explained 34% of total sum of squares by genotype, 28% by environment, and 22% by G×E. Biplot analysis identified four hybrids with above-average NRA stability across the moisture gradient. NRA was moderately correlated with grain yield across water-limited environments (r = 0.38) but not in high-rainfall environments (r = 0.06). Sandy-loam sites amplified G×E compared to clay-loam sites, likely reflecting differences in soil drying rate. The findings indicate that phenotyping across at least three contrasting soil textures is necessary for reliable G×E characterisation of root angle.

title: Image analysis pipelines for root crown phenotyping: a practical comparison of WinRHIZO, SmartRoot, and a custom thresholding script
abstract: Automated image analysis is the primary bottleneck in high-throughput root crown phenotyping pipelines. We compared three analysis approaches—WinRHIZO Pro 2016 (commercial), SmartRoot (ImageJ plugin, open-source), and a custom Python thresholding and skeletonisation script written in-house—applied to a set of 360 standardised flatbed scans of maize and wheat root crowns collected during the 2016 growing season. Reference measurements for total root length, mean diameter, and branching density were obtained by manual tracing in ImageJ on a 60-scan subset. WinRHIZO showed the highest agreement with manual reference for total root length (RMSE = 4.3 cm/cm, R² = 0.94) and mean diameter (RMSE = 0.08 mm, R² = 0.91). SmartRoot performed comparably for mean diameter but underestimated total length on crowns with overlapping roots (RMSE = 9.7 cm/cm). The custom script was fastest (mean processing time 4 s per image versus 38 s for WinRHIZO) but required manual correction for roughly 12% of images. We provide the Python script, threshold parameter recommendations, and a decision guide for laboratories choosing between these workflows.

title: Phenotypic plasticity of lateral root density in winter wheat under contrasting nitrogen supply in the field
abstract: Lateral root density (LRD) is considered a plastic trait responsive to localized nutrient availability, but most evidence comes from controlled environments. We tested whether LRD in winter wheat shows measurable phenotypic plasticity in field conditions across a range of nitrogen application rates. Four wheat varieties (two modern and two older) were grown at Rimski Šančevi in 2017–2018 under four nitrogen treatments (0, 40, 80, 120 kg N ha⁻¹) in a randomised complete block design with four replications. Root crowns were excavated at GS32 (stem elongation) and scored for LRD on washed sub-samples using WinRHIZO. LRD increased significantly from the 0 to 80 kg N ha⁻¹ treatment in all varieties (mean increase 31%), with no further significant increase at 120 kg N ha⁻¹. Plasticity index ranged from 0.22 to 0.41 across varieties; the two older varieties showed lower plasticity. Nitrogen treatment did not significantly alter nodal root number or crown root angle. These results suggest that LRD is a suitable indicator of root foraging response under field nitrogen gradients and could be incorporated into variety evaluation protocols.

title: Root architecture phenotyping in breeding programmes: constraints, opportunities, and decision points
abstract: This book chapter reviews the practical considerations for integrating root system architecture (RSA) phenotyping into applied cereal and oilseed breeding, drawing primarily on experience from Pannonian and Central European programmes. We discuss the trade-offs between throughput and precision at different selection stages, the choice of developmental stage for excavation, the minimum sample size required to achieve acceptable trait heritability estimates, and the organisational demands of field phenotyping campaigns. Particular attention is given to the translation gap between controlled-environment and field RSA phenotypes, and to cases where field measurements have contributed to variety advancement. We also address the integration of RSA traits with canopy-level remote sensing and soil electrical resistivity surveys. The chapter concludes with a framework for deciding which traits and methods are justified at early (F3–F4), intermediate (F5–F6), and advanced (pre-registration) selection stages, illustrated with worked examples from wheat and sunflower.

title: Assessing low-cost RGB imaging with consumer-grade cameras as a replacement for flatbed scanning in root crown phenotyping
abstract: Flatbed scanners are the standard tool for root image acquisition but are bulky, fragile in field conditions, and limited to roots that can be fully submerged or pressed flat. We tested whether photographs taken with a calibrated consumer-grade mirrorless camera (24 MP) on a portable lightbox could substitute for flatbed scans in estimating root length, mean diameter, and branching density in wheat root crowns. A total of 180 crowns were processed in parallel by both methods. A colour-correction card was placed in each photograph for post-processing normalisation. Trait estimates from camera images and flatbed scans were compared by Bland–Altman analysis and linear regression. For mean root diameter the bias was negligible (0.02 mm) and limits of agreement were narrow (±0.15 mm). For total root length the camera method underestimated by 8.4% on average, primarily for root diameters below 0.3 mm where depth-of-field limitations reduced detection. After applying a simple regression correction, the camera method recovered accuracy comparable to scanning. The portable setup weighed 2.1 kg versus 4.8 kg for the scanner and power supply, facilitating remote field use.

title: Stability of root crown traits across environments predicts neither yield stability nor yield level in maize under Pannonian production conditions
abstract: A common assumption in root phenotyping literature is that architecturally stable genotypes—those maintaining consistent root form across environments—will translate that stability into agronomic performance. We tested this assumption by correlating stability statistics for six root crown traits with yield stability (Finlay–Wilkinson regression slope and Eberhart–Russell deviation) in 22 experimental maize hybrids grown across eight environments in Serbia and Hungary between 2019 and 2022. Root traits were measured by shovelomics at V8–V9; yield was recorded at harvest. Spearman rank correlations between root trait stability indices and yield stability metrics ranged from −0.18 to 0.21 and none were significant after Bonferroni correction. Similarly, mean root trait values across environments showed weak and non-significant associations with mean yield across the same environments. The results suggest that, at least for the range of environments and genotypes sampled, root crown architecture at V8 is not a reliable proxy for agronomic performance stability in this region, and that its potential utility may be more context-specific than sometimes assumed.

title: Protocol for multi-site root crown phenotyping campaigns: scheduling, crew training, data management, and quality checks
abstract: Multi-site root phenotyping trials require standardised procedures across crews that may have different experience levels and operate under different logistical constraints. This methods paper describes the protocol developed and refined over three consecutive growing seasons (2021–2023) within the ROOTSPAN project, covering winter wheat, maize, and sunflower at eight locations across Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. The protocol encompasses: site preparation and excavation standardisation, a two-day crew training procedure with inter-rater reliability checkpoints, a chain-of-custody labelling and storage system for excavated crowns, image acquisition with the portable RGB lightbox setup described elsewhere, semi-automated quality control checks in Python that flag out-of-range values, and a structured metadata template compatible with MIAPPE (Minimum Information About a Plant Phenotyping Experiment). The paper reports inter-crew ICC values for key traits (0.76–0.93) and documents the reduction in missing or corrupted records from 8.1% in year one to 1.4% in year three. All protocol documents and quality-control scripts are available in an open repository.

title: Root crown architecture of winter wheat at stem elongation under variable spring temperature: a two-season field survey
abstract: Warming spring temperatures associated with recent climate variability alter the developmental trajectory of winter wheat and may affect root crown formation before stem elongation. We conducted a survey across 18 winter wheat varieties at two sites (Rimski Šančevi and Sombor) during the springs of 2024 and 2025, measuring air temperature accumulation (degree-days above 5 °C, from 1 January) at sampling and recording five root crown traits by shovelomics at GS30–32. Mean nodal root angle was negatively correlated with accumulated degree-days at sampling (r = −0.34, P = 0.03), suggesting that faster progression through early spring growth stages under warmer conditions was associated with shallower root growth at this phenological stage. Lateral root density showed no significant temperature relationship. Varieties differed significantly in mean angle (range 38°–57°) but variety-by-year interaction for angle was modest (ICC across years = 0.81), suggesting that the trait is reliable enough across seasons for comparative variety assessment. The Sombor site, with sandier soil, showed 6° steeper mean angles than Rimski Šančevi, consistent with known soil texture effects on root growth direction.

title: Delineation of within-field management zones using fuzzy k-means clustering of soil and topographic attributes
abstract: Management zone delineation groups within-field locations with similar production potential so that inputs can be tailored to each zone. This paper applied fuzzy k-means clustering to seven soil attributes (organic matter, pH, plant-available P and K, clay content, ECa at two depths) and three topographic indices derived from a 1 m LiDAR DTM across 18 fields (total 2 140 ha) in the Bačka region. The fuzziness performance index and modified partition entropy were used to determine the optimal number of zones (two to six). Three zones emerged as optimal for 14 of 18 fields. Subsequent soil sampling within delineated zones versus a regular grid showed that zone-based sampling captured 23% more variance in organic matter at 30% fewer samples. The approach is directly applicable to prescription generation within commercial advisory workflows.

title: A review of microclimate-mediated disease suppression in intercropped vegetable systems: mechanisms and quantitative evidence
abstract: This chapter synthesises published field studies from 1985 to 2013 that measured at least one microclimate variable alongside a disease outcome in intercropped or mulched vegetable systems. Sixty-two studies met inclusion criteria. Radiation reduction and canopy humidity elevation were the two most frequently documented modifications, reported in 71 % and 58 % of studies respectively. Disease suppression was observed in 39 of 62 cases; the remaining 23 reported neutral or disease-exacerbating outcomes. Fungal foliar pathogens accounted for 80 % of reported disease exacerbation, confirming the theoretical risk associated with increased canopy humidity in dense intercrops. The chapter discusses gaps in mechanistic understanding, particularly the scarcity of quantified leaf wetness data and the near-absence of studies linking canopy airflow reduction to spore dispersal dynamics. Management recommendations are synthesised from the most methodologically rigorous trials.

title: A Rule-Based System for Extracting Tabular Data from Scanned Laboratory Reports
abstract: This paper describes a deterministic pipeline for extracting numerical measurements from scanned paper laboratory reports produced by environmental testing labs in the Vojvodina region. The system applies binarisation followed by horizontal and vertical run-length projection to detect table boundaries, then uses a grammar of column-header keywords to assign semantic roles to extracted cells. A corpus of 1,240 single-page reports from three laboratories was annotated at the cell level, yielding 18,430 annotated cells. The rule-based extractor achieved a cell-level F1 score of 0.81 on held-out reports from the same labs and 0.63 on reports from a fourth, unseen lab, demonstrating the domain-transfer problem that motivated subsequent research. Processing time averaged 340 milliseconds per page on a 2009-era workstation. The paper also provides a taxonomy of layout variations observed in the corpus, distinguishing four broad structural classes that recur across regional labs.

title: Benchmark Dataset for Semi-Structured Industrial Form Recognition in the Western Balkans
abstract: We present FormBank-WB, a publicly released benchmark consisting of 4,870 scanned forms collected from manufacturing and environmental-testing companies in Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Forms span seven document classes, including quality-control checklists, calibration certificates, and chemical analysis reports. Each document is annotated with bounding boxes for text regions, tables, logos, and free-text zones, together with transcribed field values for 23 mandatory semantic slots defined in the annotation schema. Inter-annotator agreement, measured on a 500-document overlap subset, reached a Cohen's kappa of 0.87 for region type and 0.79 for semantic-slot assignment. The paper describes the collection protocol, anonymisation procedure, and annotation guidelines. Baseline results for three open-source OCR engines are reported: median character error rate ranged from 4.1 % for clean laser-printed pages to 19.3 % for faxed or photocopied originals. The dataset is hosted under a Creative Commons licence and is intended to support reproducible evaluation of form-understanding systems in regional languages and scripts.
