title: Influence of Scanning Resolution and Compression Artefacts on OCR Accuracy in Multi-Column Laboratory Forms
abstract: Laboratory forms often arrive as low-resolution JPEG images produced by office-class flatbed scanners or smartphone cameras. This study systematically measures how resolution, expressed in dots per inch, and JPEG compression quality interact to affect character recognition accuracy on a controlled corpus of 320 synthetic and 480 real laboratory forms. Documents were artificially degraded at seven resolution levels between 72 and 400 DPI and five compression quality factors. For each combination, three OCR engines were applied and character error rate was recorded. Results show that below 150 DPI, error rate increases non-linearly, with a particularly sharp inflection at 100 DPI where average CER rose from 7 % to 28 % across engines. JPEG quality below 60 introduced block artefacts that interacted destructively with resolution degradation. A simple pre-processing chain consisting of adaptive sharpening and JPEG artefact reduction recovered between 30 % and 45 % of the accuracy lost at 100 DPI / quality 50 settings. Practical recommendations for document capture workflows are derived.

title: Graph-Based Representation of Document Layout for Template-Independent Table Detection
abstract: This paper proposes representing a document page as an attributed relational graph in which nodes correspond to connected text components and edges encode spatial proximity relations. Table regions are then detected by finding dense subgraphs whose internal edge attributes satisfy constraints on vertical and horizontal alignment. The method requires no training data from the target document class and no prior template specification. Experiments were conducted on three corpora: FormBank-WB, the publicly available UNLV dataset, and a private collection of 780 pharmaceutical laboratory reports. On FormBank-WB, table-region detection reached an F1 of 0.86, compared with 0.83 for the best template-based baseline. On the pharmaceutical corpus, where templates were entirely unseen, the proposed method achieved F1 of 0.78 while the baseline fell to 0.51. Construction of the graph takes approximately 120 milliseconds per page for an average page containing 400 text components. The representation also supports detection of ruling lines, logos, and stamp regions as byproducts of the same graph analysis.

title: Combining CRF Sequence Labelling with Spatial Context Features for Field Extraction in Inspection Certificates
abstract: Inspection certificates issued by accredited testing laboratories follow loose conventions but no single fixed template. This work treats field extraction as a sequence labelling problem over sorted text tokens, augmented with spatial features derived from each token's bounding box and its nearest neighbours. A conditional random field model is trained on 1,100 annotated inspection certificates and evaluated on a held-out set of 275 certificates from laboratories not represented in training. The feature set includes token geometry, font-size estimates from bounding-box height, relative page position, left-margin alignment, and the label of the spatially closest token. Adding spatial context features raised per-field extraction accuracy from 72.3 % to 83.7 % compared with a purely sequential baseline. Error analysis identified measurement units as the most frequently mislabelled token class. The trained model is integrated into a prototype pipeline, and processing throughput of 8.4 certificates per second is reported on a standard 2014-era server.

title: Transfer Learning for Document Layout Segmentation Across Laboratory Report Domains
abstract: Deep convolutional networks trained for natural-image segmentation can be adapted for document layout segmentation with relatively small amounts of domain-specific labelled data. This paper fine-tunes a fully convolutional encoder–decoder architecture, originally trained on a large general document dataset, on 2,300 manually annotated laboratory report pages spanning four application domains: environmental, pharmaceutical, food safety, and metallurgical testing. Pixel-level mean intersection over union reached 0.84 on an in-domain test set and 0.76 on an out-of-domain set drawn from agricultural testing laboratories not included in fine-tuning. The study systematically varies the number of fine-tuning samples from 50 to 2,000 and reports the learning curve for each domain, showing that pharmaceutical and metallurgical documents, which have more regular layouts, saturate at around 400 samples, while environmental documents require at least 900. Qualitative error analysis highlights confusion between dense text blocks and small tables as the dominant failure mode.
venue: Journal of Imaging Science and Technology

title: End-to-End Parsing of Chromatography Analysis Reports Using Attention-Based Sequence Models
abstract: High-performance liquid chromatography reports produced by laboratory information management systems share broad structural conventions but vary in column ordering, unit notation, and the placement of quality-control metadata. This paper trains a transformer encoder over token sequences extracted by a commercial OCR engine to jointly detect, classify, and transcribe 31 semantic field types specific to chromatography reports. Training data consists of 3,400 annotated reports collected under a data-sharing agreement with four analytical chemistry laboratories. The model achieves a per-field exact-match rate of 88.6 % on a held-out set of 680 reports. Comparison with a CRF baseline trained on the same data shows an improvement of 9.1 percentage points. Attention visualisations are used to verify that the model relies on expected contextual cues such as column headers and unit tokens. The paper also discusses practical issues in handling multi-line cell values and merged header rows.
venue: ACM Transactions on Document Engineering

title: A Comparative Study of Open-Source and Commercial OCR Engines on Low-Quality Industrial Document Scans
abstract: This study evaluates five OCR engines—three open-source and two commercial—on a corpus of 1,080 low-quality scanned industrial documents including calibration certificates, material test reports, and delivery notes. Document quality was independently rated on a four-point scale by two annotators. Character error rate, word error rate, and a domain-specific field error rate were computed for each engine and each quality stratum. The best open-source engine achieved a median word error rate of 3.8 % on high-quality pages and 22.1 % on very-low-quality pages; the best commercial engine reached 2.1 % and 14.7 % respectively. Post-processing with a domain vocabulary reduced word error rate by 18–31 % across engines on low-quality pages. The study also measures throughput: the fastest open-source engine processes 4.2 pages per second on a four-core CPU, while the commercial engines operate as cloud services with round-trip latencies of 1.1 to 3.4 seconds per page. Results guide engine selection in deployment scenarios where document quality and throughput requirements vary.

title: Handling Multilingual Content in Serbian-Language Laboratory Reports: Script Detection and Mixed-Script OCR
abstract: Laboratory reports in Serbia frequently mix Serbian Cyrillic and Latin scripts, include measurement values with decimal separators that differ across regional conventions, and may contain excerpts in German or English for imported product references. This paper addresses the script-detection and mixed-script recognition problem in this specific context. A lightweight convolutional classifier is trained to assign each text-line image a script class: Cyrillic, Latin, or numeric/symbol. Classification accuracy on a 6,200-line test set reached 97.1 %. The classified lines are then routed to script-specific recognition models, which reduces overall character error rate from 11.4 % (single-script engine) to 6.8 %. The paper also analyses 540 reports to quantify the distribution of script-mixing patterns and finds that 63 % of multi-page reports contain at least one Latin-script word in an otherwise Cyrillic document, confirming the practical importance of the problem. An ablation study isolates the contribution of script routing versus language model adaptation.

title: Structured Information Extraction from Veterinary and Food Microbiological Reports: Dataset and Experiments
abstract: Veterinary and food microbiology laboratories produce reports that list detected micro-organisms, colony counts, and pass/fail judgements against regulatory limits. These documents combine free-text clinical observations with embedded tables and follow formats mandated by national accreditation bodies, creating a distinctive extraction challenge. This paper presents a 2,800-report annotated dataset covering 14 microbiology laboratories in Serbia and North Macedonia, together with extraction experiments using three methods: a rule-based baseline, a CRF model with layout features, and a fine-tuned document transformer. The document transformer achieves the best overall field-level F1 of 0.91, outperforming the CRF by 0.07. Performance drops to 0.82 on reports that include handwritten amendments, which constitute 12 % of the corpus. The paper discusses the regulatory context that determines required fields and provides an analysis of inter-laboratory format variation that may guide standardisation efforts.

title: Automatic Quality Assessment of OCR Output for Laboratory Document Pipelines Without Ground Truth
abstract: In production document processing pipelines, ground-truth transcriptions are unavailable for quality monitoring. This paper develops a reference-free OCR quality estimator trained to predict character error rate from features derived solely from the OCR output itself: character n-gram perplexity against a domain language model, proportion of out-of-vocabulary tokens, confidence score statistics reported by the OCR engine, and text-line geometry regularity. A gradient boosting regressor is trained on 9,400 page-level samples with known CER values from the FormBank-WB corpus and from chromatography reports. On a separate test set, the estimator predicts CER with a mean absolute error of 3.1 percentage points and Spearman correlation of 0.88 with true CER. The estimator is used to flag pages requiring manual review in a laboratory report processing workflow, reducing the manual review queue by 61 % compared with reviewing all pages while missing only 4.2 % of high-error pages.

title: Document Understanding for Regulatory Compliance: Mapping Extracted Laboratory Data to LIMS Schema Fields
abstract: Laboratory information management systems require incoming report data to be mapped to a defined schema before ingestion. When reports arrive as scanned PDFs from external laboratories, this mapping is currently performed manually. This paper describes and evaluates a two-stage approach: the first stage applies the group's template-agnostic extraction pipeline to produce a flat set of (field-name, value) pairs; the second stage uses a fine-tuned language model to align extracted field names to the target LIMS schema by semantic similarity. The method is evaluated on three LIMS schemata used by companies in the NTP Novi Sad technology park, covering 87, 112, and 143 target fields respectively. End-to-end correct field ingestion rates of 84 %, 81 %, and 78 % were achieved, compared with 91–93 % for manual entry, with average processing times of 1.8 seconds per report. Error categories are analysed and the paper identifies unit normalisation as the most frequent cause of incorrect ingestion.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Scanning Strategy Selection
abstract: Automated reconnaissance systems often rely on fixed scanning strategies that are suboptimal in environments where detection risk varies by subnet or time of day. This paper frames scanning strategy selection as a Markov decision process in which an agent observes partial information about target responsiveness and detection thresholds and selects among six predefined scan intensities. A Q-learning agent is trained in simulation using a parameterised network model and then evaluated on an emulated testbed of 120 hosts with an intrusion detection system configured to log and block excessive probe rates. The trained agent reduces IDS-triggered alerts by 58% compared to a fixed-intensity baseline while achieving 91% of the baseline's host-discovery coverage within the same time window. Ablation experiments confirm that the reward function weighting of coverage versus stealth has a strong effect on the coverage-alert trade-off.
venue: Journal of Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems in Security

title: Hidden Markov Models for Joint-Angle Time Series in Physical Therapy Exercise Classification
abstract: This paper presents a classification framework for physical therapy exercises using Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) applied to joint-angle time series extracted from a marker-based motion-capture system. Fourteen distinct rehabilitation exercises were recorded from 22 healthy participants performing each exercise ten times, yielding a dataset of 3,080 sequences. Joint angles at the hip, knee, shoulder, and elbow were computed and used as observation vectors after z-score normalisation. Left-right HMMs with between 4 and 10 states were trained per exercise class using Baum-Welch re-estimation. A held-out test set of five unseen participants showed a mean classification accuracy of 81.4%, with confusion concentrated between exercises sharing similar sagittal-plane kinematics. The paper includes an analysis of state-count sensitivity and proposes a simple cross-validation scheme for small clinical datasets. Results indicate that HMMs are competitive with DTW-based baselines while offering a generative probabilistic framework suitable for subsequent extensions toward online detection.

title: Temporal Segmentation of Continuous Skeletal Sequences Using Change-Point Detection
abstract: Continuous motion streams recorded during clinical assessments must be segmented into individual exercise repetitions before classification can proceed. This work evaluates three change-point detection algorithms—PELT, binary segmentation, and a sliding-window energy method—applied to 3D joint-position trajectories from 18 participants performing four upper-limb exercises. Sequences were captured at 30 Hz with a depth camera, and body joints were tracked using a commercial skeleton-estimation SDK. Ground-truth segment boundaries were labelled by a physiotherapist. PELT achieved the best F1 score of 0.87 for boundary localisation within a ±0.3 s tolerance, compared with 0.81 for binary segmentation and 0.76 for the sliding-window method. The paper analyses sensitivity to movement speed variability across participants and proposes a heuristic for penalty parameter selection based on mean sequence cadence. The resulting segmentation pipeline feeds directly into a downstream HMM classifier, improving end-to-end accuracy by 6.2 percentage points over unsegmented baseline experiments.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Skeleton Representations for Action Recognition: Absolute Coordinates, Relative Joints, and Bone Vectors
abstract: The choice of skeleton representation substantially affects classifier performance. This study benchmarks three representations—absolute 3D joint coordinates, pairwise relative joint displacements, and bone orientation vectors—on two publicly available motion-capture corpora: the CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database subset (15 action categories, 240 sequences) and an in-house clinical dataset (8 exercises, 176 sequences). For each representation, an SVM with an RBF kernel and a 1D convolutional network are trained and evaluated with five-fold cross-validation. Bone vectors consistently outperform absolute coordinates by 3–7% accuracy across both datasets and both classifiers. Relative joint displacements perform comparably to bone vectors on the clinical dataset but underperform on the larger public corpus, suggesting a dataset-size interaction. The paper discusses computational cost, sensitivity to sensor placement errors, and practical recommendations for choosing a representation when labelled data are scarce.

title: Pre-training Recurrent Networks on Heterogeneous Motion-Capture Corpora for Downstream Exercise Recognition
abstract: This paper investigates whether a long short-term memory (LSTM) network pre-trained on a large heterogeneous motion-capture corpus can improve classification of rehabilitation exercises when only small labelled sets are available for fine-tuning. Pre-training used 12,400 sequences from three public corpora spanning sport, dance, and daily-activity motions, unified by a shared 22-joint skeleton topology. Fine-tuning was performed on a clinical dataset of nine exercises with labelled sets ranging from 5 to 40 samples per class. Pre-trained models fine-tuned with 10 samples per class achieved mean accuracy of 74.3%, compared with 58.1% for models trained from scratch on the same data. Accuracy gains diminished as fine-tuning set size increased beyond 25 samples per class. The paper also reports layer-wise transfer analysis, showing that lower temporal encoding layers transfer more reliably than task-specific upper layers. This represents an early empirical study of cross-domain skeletal transfer learning in a rehabilitation context.

title: Data Augmentation for Skeletal Time Series via Controlled Spatial Jitter and Temporal Warping
abstract: Augmenting skeletal sequences can partially substitute for additional labelled data in low-resource settings. This study systematically examines three augmentation strategies applied to 3D joint trajectories: (i) Gaussian spatial jitter added independently to each joint at each frame, (ii) time-series warping using random piecewise-linear time maps, and (iii) a combined strategy. Experiments use a rehabilitation exercise dataset of nine exercise classes with between 8 and 25 labelled sequences per class. A baseline LSTM classifier is trained with and without augmentation at augmentation ratios of 2×, 4×, and 8×. The combined strategy at 4× augmentation improves mean F1 from 0.63 to 0.74. Spatial jitter alone provides larger gains for fast, ballistic movements, while temporal warping contributes more for slow, sustained exercises. The paper quantifies augmentation diversity through a pairwise sequence distance measure and identifies diminishing returns and distribution-shift artefacts at the 8× ratio.

title: Graph Convolutional Networks for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition: An Empirical Study with Small Training Sets
abstract: Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) that model the human skeleton as a spatial graph have become a dominant architecture for action recognition, but most published results assume thousands of labelled examples. This paper performs a controlled empirical study of three published GCN variants (a spectral formulation, a spatial-temporal formulation, and an adaptive adjacency formulation) under training set sizes from 5 to 200 samples per class. Experiments use the NTU RGB+D 60 cross-subject benchmark downsampled to simulate low-resource conditions, and an in-house rehabilitation corpus. At 10 samples per class, the adaptive adjacency model achieves 48.7% on NTU and 66.2% on the rehabilitation set; both numbers improve substantially with 50 samples. The paper characterises the sample-efficiency profile of each architecture and measures the effect of applying the augmentation pipeline from the authors' earlier work. Insights are provided for practitioners choosing architectures when clinical data collection is expensive.

title: Prototypical Networks for Few-Shot Rehabilitation Exercise Recognition from IMU-Derived Skeletons
abstract: This study adapts prototypical networks, originally proposed for image classification, to the few-shot recognition of rehabilitation exercises represented as skeleton sequences derived from inertial measurement units. Skeleton estimates are obtained by fusing signals from a 17-sensor IMU suit using a real-time inverse-kinematics solver. A sequence encoder based on a bidirectional LSTM produces fixed-length episode embeddings. In a 5-way 5-shot evaluation protocol over 11 exercise classes, the prototypical network achieves 79.1% accuracy, compared with 71.4% for a nearest-neighbour baseline using DTW distance and 68.9% for a fine-tuned LSTM. The paper analyses the effect of episode construction strategy on convergence and reports that sampling episodes from within-subject repetitions, rather than across subjects, degrades generalisation by approximately 8 percentage points. Sensitivity to IMU drift artefacts is examined through controlled noise injection experiments.
venue: Proceedings of the 18th International Conference on Wearable and Implantable Body Sensor Networks

title: Pose Interpolation and Mixup Strategies for Augmenting Skeleton Sequences in Low-Data Rehabilitation Tasks
abstract: Mixup augmentation, which linearly interpolates between pairs of training samples, has shown benefits for image and text classification. This paper adapts three interpolation-based augmentation approaches—frame-level Mixup, sequence-level spherical interpolation of quaternion joint orientations, and class-manifold interpolation using a variational autoencoder—to skeleton sequence classification under low-data conditions. Experiments use two rehabilitation datasets: an in-house IMU-based corpus of 12 exercises and a publicly released depth-camera dataset of 8 exercises. All three strategies are evaluated across training set sizes from 5 to 30 samples per class on top of both a prototypical network and a GCN classifier. Quaternion spherical interpolation achieves the most consistent improvements, increasing mean accuracy by 4.1 and 5.7 percentage points on the two datasets respectively at 10 samples per class. The variational autoencoder approach shows higher variance and underperforms at fewer than 15 samples, likely due to insufficient data for stable encoder training.
venue: Pattern Recognition and Computer Vision Letters

title: Benchmarking Few-Shot Skeletal Action Classifiers on a Unified Rehabilitation Exercise Corpus
abstract: Inconsistent dataset choices and evaluation protocols make it difficult to compare few-shot skeletal action classifiers reported in the literature. This paper introduces a unified rehabilitation exercise benchmark comprising 2,240 sequences from 56 participants across 16 exercise classes recorded with both a depth-camera and an IMU suit, with standardised train/validation/test splits and episode sampling procedures. Seven few-shot methods are re-implemented and evaluated: prototypical networks, matching networks, relation networks, MAML, a metric learning approach based on temporal attention, a GCN-based episodic classifier, and a contrastive pre-training baseline. Results under 5-way 1-shot and 5-way 5-shot protocols are reported with 95% confidence intervals over 2,000 test episodes. The contrastive pre-training baseline proves surprisingly competitive, reaching 76.4% under 5-way 5-shot despite its simplicity. The dataset and evaluation code are released publicly to encourage reproducible comparisons.
venue: Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Image Analysis

title: Self-Supervised Pre-training of Spatial-Temporal Transformers on Masked Skeleton Sequences
abstract: Masked autoencoding has improved representation learning in vision and language; this paper applies the paradigm to 3D skeleton sequences for use in downstream rehabilitation exercise recognition. A spatial-temporal transformer is pre-trained by randomly masking 40% of joint-frame tokens and reconstructing the missing values from context, using 18,000 unlabelled sequences drawn from three public motion-capture corpora. The pre-trained encoder is then fine-tuned on the rehabilitation benchmark introduced in the authors' preceding benchmarking study. At 5 labelled samples per class, masked pre-training improves 5-way accuracy from 68.1% (supervised baseline) to 81.7%. The paper ablates masking ratio, token granularity (per joint vs. per frame vs. per joint-frame), and reconstruction target (raw coordinates vs. normalised bone vectors). Bone vector reconstruction with per-joint-frame tokens and a 45% masking ratio gives the best downstream transfer. An analysis of learned attention maps shows that the model attends preferentially to joints near exercise-defining body segments.

title: Continual Few-Shot Adaptation of Skeleton Classifiers to New Exercise Classes Without Catastrophic Forgetting
abstract: Deployed rehabilitation systems must accommodate new exercise classes introduced by therapists over time without retraining from scratch or forgetting previously learned classes. This paper formulates a continual few-shot learning problem for skeleton-based exercise recognition and evaluates four strategies: experience replay with a small memory buffer, elastic weight consolidation, PackNet-style layer pruning and freezing, and prototype updating in a metric learning framework. Experiments use the unified rehabilitation benchmark extended with four additional held-out exercise classes introduced sequentially in batches of five labelled samples each. Prototype updating achieves the best balance: after three sequential task increments it retains 91.2% of original-task accuracy while reaching 73.8% on new tasks with five-shot support, outperforming elastic weight consolidation by 7.1 points on new tasks and replay by 4.3 points on original tasks. The paper identifies the prototype update learning rate as the most sensitive hyperparameter and provides a practical tuning procedure.

title: Temporal Aggregation Windows for Transactional Feature Construction: Sensitivity and Selection
abstract: Transactional datasets are commonly featurised by aggregating raw events within fixed lookback windows (e.g., sum of transactions in the last 7, 30, and 90 days). The number and boundaries of these windows are typically set heuristically. This paper investigates the sensitivity of classifier performance to window choice and proposes a data-driven selection procedure based on mutual information between windowed aggregates and the target label, combined with a forward-selection wrapper evaluated on a hold-out set. Experiments use synthetic datasets representing retail payment events (500,000 customers, 18 months of history, 3.2% positive rate). The automated window selection identifies a 14-day window as more informative than the conventional 30-day window for the specific generative process and reduces feature dimensionality by 38% without significant AUPRC loss (0.69 vs. 0.70 for full feature set). The procedure runs in under four minutes on standard workstation hardware for the given dataset size.

title: Effect of CaO/Al2O3 ratio in ladle slag on alumina inclusion modification in bearing-grade steel: an experimental and thermodynamic study
abstract: The composition of ladle slag strongly influences the type and morphology of non-metallic inclusions retained in the solidified steel. This study investigates the effect of systematically varying the CaO/Al2O3 mass ratio (0.8–1.8) in a CaO–Al2O3–SiO2–MgO slag system on the modification of alumina clusters to calcium aluminates in a 25 kg laboratory induction furnace. Steel samples were taken at 5-minute intervals during a 30-minute holding period at 1580 °C. Inclusions were characterised by automated SEM-EDS on polished cross-sections, with at least 300 inclusions analysed per sample. Thermodynamic equilibrium compositions were calculated using a FactSage 8.1 slag–metal module with the FToxid and FSstel databases. Results show that a CaO/Al2O3 ratio of 1.4 gives near-complete transformation of Al2O3 to CA2 and CA phases within 20 minutes, consistent with model predictions within ±4 mol%. At lower ratios, residual corundum-type inclusions persisted and were associated with higher measured oxygen activities (3.2–4.7 ppm dissolved oxygen). The findings provide quantitative targets for slag composition control in ladle furnace practice aimed at producing clean bearing steel.
venue: Journal of Metallurgical Process Engineering

title: Oxygen and sulphur activity in CaO–Al2O3–MgO–SiO2 slags equilibrated with liquid iron at 1600 °C
abstract: Reliable thermodynamic data for oxygen and sulphur partition between slag and liquid iron are essential for modelling ladle refining. This work reports measured equilibrium oxygen activities (electrochemical sensor) and sulphur partition coefficients (Ls) for a series of ten synthetic slags in the CaO–Al2O3–MgO–SiO2 system at 1600 °C in a resistance-heated vertical tube furnace under controlled Ar/CO/CO2 atmosphere. Slag basicity (B2 = CaO/SiO2) ranged from 3.5 to 7.0 and Al2O3 content from 20 to 35 wt%. Equilibration time was set to 60 minutes following prior kinetic tests confirming attainment of steady state within 45 minutes. Measured dissolved oxygen ranged from 1.8 to 9.4 ppm, and Ls from 180 to 640. Comparison with FactSage predictions using the modified quasichemical model showed systematic overprediction of Ls by 12–18% at high MgO contents (≥8 wt%), suggesting a need for database refinement in that compositional region. The dataset is intended to serve as validation input for process simulation tools used in secondary steelmaking.

title: Quantitative assessment of inclusion cleanliness in 52100-equivalent bearing steel produced by electric arc furnace route: a sampling and statistical methodology
abstract: Inclusion cleanliness assessment in bearing steel requires consistent sampling strategy and statistically sound analysis protocols. This paper proposes and evaluates a sampling scheme applied to industrially cast 100Cr6-equivalent billets obtained from a regional EAF–LF–VD–CC route. Four heats were examined; from each heat, six cross-sectional samples were taken at defined positions (surface, quarter-radius, centre) of the cast billet. Automated feature analysis by SEM-EDS (ASPEX PICA system) was applied to 15 mm² per sample, detecting inclusions down to 1 µm equivalent circle diameter. Inclusion populations were classified into oxides, sulphides, oxysulphides, and nitrides. The distribution of maximum inclusion size across sampling positions was analysed using extreme value statistics (Gumbel distribution). Results showed that centre-line samples consistently yielded the largest oxide inclusions (D90 = 12.4 µm) and highest areal density, while the proposed six-sample scheme reduced the 95% confidence interval on predicted maximum inclusion size by 34% compared to a two-sample reference scheme. Practical recommendations for in-plant quality control are discussed.
venue: Materials and Manufacturing Quality — An International Journal

title: Repeatability analysis of a pneumatic clamping jig for PCB sub-assembly under thermal cycling conditions
abstract: Pneumatic clamping jigs used in printed circuit board sub-assembly operations are subject to dimensional drift caused by thermal gradients introduced by reflow soldering cycles. This study characterises the positional repeatability of a four-point pneumatic jig over 500 thermal cycles spanning 25 °C to 260 °C. A coordinate measuring machine with a 1 µm resolution probe was used to track the displacement of four reference datums on aluminium and hardened-steel jig bodies. Results show that the aluminium variant accumulated a mean datum shift of 8.3 µm after 500 cycles, compared with 2.1 µm for the hardened-steel body. Cycle-to-cycle standard deviation remained below 1.4 µm for both materials. A finite element thermal model is validated against experimental data with a mean absolute error of 0.9 µm. The study recommends hardened-steel jig bodies for assemblies with positional tolerances tighter than 15 µm and proposes a simple compensation lookup table applicable to aluminium jigs in less demanding applications.

title: Calibration of a low-cost structured-light scanner for sub-millimetre dimensional verification of connector housings
abstract: Structured-light 3-D scanners offer high acquisition speed but require careful calibration to achieve sub-millimetre accuracy on small plastic connector housings with dimensions in the 5–30 mm range. This paper describes a calibration procedure based on a ceramic reference artefact carrying 24 spherical targets of known diameter (3.000 ± 0.002 mm). Calibration was performed at three working distances and five ambient illumination levels typical of production environments. After calibration, the scanner achieved a mean absolute surface error of 18 µm and a 95th-percentile error of 34 µm across 60 connector housing samples measured against CMM ground truth. The paper also evaluates the effect of surface finish: matte-black housings showed 22% lower error than glossy-white equivalents without anti-reflective spray. A practical calibration interval of 8 hours of continuous operation is recommended based on observed thermal drift of the projector unit.

title: Grip-force mapping for a two-finger parallel gripper handling flexible flat cables in confined assembly spaces
abstract: Flexible flat cables (FFCs) present particular handling challenges in automated assembly because excessive grip force causes permanent deformation while insufficient force results in slip. This study maps the minimum and maximum acceptable grip-force window for twelve FFC types differing in width (6–30 mm), thickness (0.1–0.3 mm), and pitch (0.5–1.0 mm) using a custom instrumented two-finger parallel gripper mounted on a six-axis robot. Force was measured at 1 kHz using strain-gauge transducers embedded in the gripper fingers. For the thinnest cables (0.1 mm, 0.5 mm pitch), the acceptable force window was 0.18–0.34 N; for the widest (30 mm, 1.0 mm pitch) it expanded to 1.2–4.7 N. Slip events were detected by a miniature optical encoder tracking cable displacement. A regression model predicting acceptable force bounds from cable geometry achieved R² = 0.91. The model was validated on three additional FFC types not used in training.

title: Statistical process control implementation for a six-station robotic assembly line producing miniature electromechanical relays
abstract: Miniature electromechanical relays contain components with tolerances as tight as ±10 µm, making process monitoring critical to sustaining yield. This paper reports the deployment of statistical process control on a six-station robotic assembly line at a relay manufacturer, covering armature gap measurement, spring preload verification, and contact resistance testing. Control charts were constructed from 18 weeks of production data totalling 142,000 relay units. Out-of-control signals were classified by cause using a Bayesian classifier trained on 340 labelled historical events; precision was 0.84 and recall 0.79 for the five fault categories. Implementing automatic line pause on Western Electric rule violations reduced the proportion of defective units escaping final test from 0.41% to 0.09%. The paper discusses practical obstacles encountered during deployment, including operator resistance to automated line stops and sensor drift in the armature gap station.

title: Design and evaluation of a modular tooling plate system for rapid changeover between small-form-factor assembly variants
abstract: Production lines assembling multiple variants of small electronic sub-assemblies require frequent changeover of workholding tooling. Manual changeover is a source of re-qualification time and positioning error. This paper presents a modular tooling plate system in which interchangeable fixture inserts locate on a common base plate via a kinematic coupling with measured repeatability of 1.8 µm over 200 exchange cycles. The base plate carries embedded proximity sensors confirming correct insert seating before the assembly cycle begins. Changeover time for a four-station cell was reduced from 34 minutes (manual pin-and-screw fixtures) to 7 minutes. First-article inspection after changeover showed all critical dimensions within tolerance in 97 of 100 trials, versus 81 of 100 with the previous system. Material and manufacturing cost of the insert set was estimated at 40% below an equivalent dedicated fixture set when amortised over 12 product variants.

title: Measurement uncertainty budget for in-line optical inspection of solder joint geometry on 0402 components
abstract: Automated optical inspection of solder joints on 0402 passive components (1.0 mm × 0.5 mm) involves multiple uncertainty sources that are rarely combined into a formal budget. This study derives a full GUM-compliant measurement uncertainty budget for a line-scan camera system operating at 5 µm pixel pitch, covering lens distortion, illumination non-uniformity, thresholding algorithm noise, and substrate thermal expansion during measurement. Uncertainty budgets were calculated for three measurands: fillet height, fillet width, and pad coverage ratio. The combined standard uncertainty for fillet height was 4.2 µm (coverage factor k = 2 giving 8.4 µm expanded uncertainty), which represents 28% of the minimum acceptable fillet height for the component type studied. Recommendations are provided for reducing the dominant uncertainty contributor — illumination non-uniformity at 38% of the combined variance — through structured LED ring design modifications.

title: Force-torque sensor integration for peg-in-hole insertion of press-fit connector pins with sub-50 µm clearances
abstract: Press-fit connector pins with diameters of 0.64 mm inserted into plated through-holes with 30–50 µm diametral clearance require precise alignment to avoid pin buckling. A six-axis force-torque sensor mounted at the robot wrist provides signals that can detect misalignment before buckling occurs. This paper presents an impedance-controlled insertion strategy that uses the measured force-torque vector to estimate lateral misalignment and issue corrective moves during the approach phase. Experiments on a test board with 96 pins per connector showed that the strategy reduced pin buckling rate from 3.1% (position-only control) to 0.2% (impedance control with correction). Insertion forces were monitored across 5,000 insertions; mean peak force was 18.3 N with standard deviation 1.1 N. The correction algorithm added a mean of 140 ms per insertion cycle. A cost-benefit calculation indicates break-even at approximately 9,000 connectors per year relative to a position-only cell.

title: Comparative evaluation of three 3-D measurement techniques for warpage quantification of populated PCBs after reflow
abstract: PCB warpage after reflow soldering affects the reliability of area-array packages and the dimensional reference provided to downstream assembly operations. This study compares structured-light scanning, fringe-projection profilometry, and tactile CMM scanning for measuring warpage of 120 mm × 80 mm double-sided populated boards at elevated temperature (25 °C, 50 °C, and 100 °C). A reference dataset was established by averaging five repeated CMM scans. Structured-light scanning showed mean absolute deviation from reference of 11 µm at 25 °C, degrading to 31 µm at 100 °C due to thermal emission interference. Fringe-projection profilometry performed best at 100 °C (14 µm mean deviation) owing to its narrowband illumination. Measurement throughput favoured both optical methods (under 40 seconds per board) over CMM (12 minutes). Recommendations for method selection based on temperature range, throughput requirements, and available budget are presented in a decision matrix.

title: Automated dimensional audit of injection-moulded connector bodies using a robot-mounted laser line scanner
abstract: Injection-moulded connector bodies for automotive electronics are produced in high volumes with tolerances of ±50 µm on critical features. Manual gauge-based inspection is slow and operator-dependent. This paper describes an automated inspection cell in which a laser line scanner is mounted on a six-axis robot that traces a pre-programmed path around each part held in a kinematic nest. Scan data are registered to a CAD nominal model using an iterative closest-point algorithm; feature deviations are extracted for 14 critical dimensions per part. Cycle time per part is 22 seconds. Gauge repeatability and reproducibility study across three robots and two scanner units showed combined GRR of 9.3% of tolerance, satisfying the automotive threshold of 10%. False-reject rate measured over 4,800 production parts was 0.6%; false-accept rate was below the detection limit of the validation study (< 0.02%).

title: Thermal compensation model for a robot-integrated CMM probe used in long-duration assembly-cell measurement cycles
abstract: When a touch-trigger probe is integrated into a robotic assembly cell and used over multi-hour measurement cycles, temperature gradients in the robot structure and the probe extension introduce systematic errors that exceed typical compensation built into standalone CMM systems. This study characterises the thermal error of a probe-on-robot configuration over 8-hour cycles with ambient temperature variation of ±3 °C. Errors were measured against a Zerodur reference artefact at 15-minute intervals. Without compensation, systematic Z-axis error accumulated to 28 µm and X-axis error to 14 µm by the end of an 8-hour cycle. A polynomial thermal compensation model using readings from five PT100 sensors on the robot links reduced these figures to 5 µm and 3 µm respectively. Model coefficients were stable across three recalibration intervals of 30 days. The approach requires no hardware modification beyond sensor attachment and is suitable for retrofit.

title: Fixturing strategy selection for heterogeneous small-form-factor sub-assembly batches: a decision-support framework
abstract: Contract electronics manufacturers frequently process heterogeneous batches of small sub-assemblies in the same cell, requiring a systematic approach to selecting fixturing strategy — dedicated, modular-insert, or reconfigurable — for each product family. This paper proposes a decision-support framework combining feature-based product classification with a cost model that accounts for fixture fabrication, changeover time, and first-article inspection overhead. The framework was applied retrospectively to 37 product families processed over two years at a partner manufacturer. Agreement between the framework recommendation and the expert-selected strategy used in production was 81%. In 11 disagreement cases, the framework recommendation was evaluated by manufacturing engineers and judged superior in 7. The paper identifies batch size below 200 units and feature count above 8 critical dimensions as the primary drivers of modular-insert fixture preference. A publicly available spreadsheet implementation of the cost model is described.

title: Simultaneous Estimation of Wind Velocity and Aerodynamic Coefficients for a Quadrotor Using an Unscented Kalman Filter
abstract: Accurate real-time knowledge of both wind velocity and vehicle aerodynamic coefficients is needed for high-performance disturbance compensation in UAV guidance. This paper presents an unscented Kalman filter (UKF) formulation that treats wind velocity components and four key drag coefficients as jointly estimated state variables alongside the vehicle's kinematic states. The filter uses IMU measurements, motor RPM feedback, and GPS velocity as observables, with no external wind sensor. Observability analysis shows that the drag coefficient states are locally observable when the vehicle performs attitude manoeuvres of amplitude ≥5°. Simulation experiments with Monte Carlo runs (n = 500) show that wind speed estimation error converges to below 0.5 m/s within 8 s from cold start, and drag coefficient estimates settle within 15% of true values within 20 s. Hardware experiments in an outdoor hover arena confirmed the simulation trends, with the filter performing adequately at wind speeds of 2–8 m/s. Divergence at wind speeds above 10 m/s is traced to model nonlinearity violations.
venue: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics

title: Transfer Learning from a Spectral CNN Trained on Synthetic Datacubes to Real Conveyor Data
abstract: Labelling large hyperspectral datasets for training convolutional classifiers is expensive. This paper explores whether a CNN trained entirely on physically simulated spectral datacubes — generated from measured pure-material spectra combined with a Monte Carlo optical mixing model — can be fine-tuned with a small number of real labels to achieve competitive accuracy on a six-class polymer sorting task. The simulated training set comprised 50 000 synthetic spectra per class; fine-tuning used 200 real labelled spectra per class collected on a laboratory conveyor. After fine-tuning, the model reached 95.2% accuracy on a 9 000-sample real test set, compared to 97.1% for a fully supervised baseline trained on 2 000 real labels per class and 78.4% for zero-shot transfer without fine-tuning. Model size was 1.2 M parameters. Inference ran at 3 200 spectra/s on a Jetson Xavier NX. The simulation pipeline and model architecture are made publicly available.

title: Thermal-Cycling-Induced Solder Joint Degradation and Its Effect on In-Circuit Test Yield in Surface-Mount Assemblies
abstract: Solder joint degradation under repeated thermal excursions alters joint resistance in ways that can shift in-circuit test measurements outside tolerance windows, producing false failures or masking real defects. This study subjected 120 FR-4 boards, each carrying 84 SOIC-16 and 48 QFN-32 packages, to 0–100 °C thermal cycling at 2 cycles per hour for 500, 1000, and 1500 cycles. Joint resistance was measured with a four-wire Kelvin technique after each milestone. In-circuit test pass rates were re-evaluated at each stage using a bed-of-nails fixture on a commercial ICT platform. Results show that mean joint resistance increased by 38 mΩ after 1500 cycles for QFN pads, causing a 6.1 % increase in false-open calls. A temperature-corrected threshold model is presented that reduces false calls to below 1 % across all cycle counts tested. The model parameters are extracted from a 15-minute characterisation run on a fresh board.

title: Iterative Learning Control for a Two-Dimensional Cartesian Gantry: Cross-Coupling and Decoupled Filter Design
abstract: In a two-axis belt-driven gantry, motion commands in the X direction generate small but measurable disturbances in the Y axis due to frame compliance and shared motor ground. This paper quantifies the cross-coupling experimentally for a 1.4 m × 0.9 m gantry and incorporates it into a multi-input multi-output NOILC formulation. The cross-coupling transfer function magnitude at typical trajectory frequencies (5–25 Hz) was between −28 dB and −18 dB relative to the direct channel, which is sufficient to cause positioning errors of 0.05–0.12 mm if ignored. Two ILC architectures are compared: a fully coupled 2×2 filter using the complete MIMO model, and a decoupled design that uses only the diagonal terms. The coupled filter achieves final RMS errors of 0.016 mm in X and 0.021 mm in Y after 60 trials. The decoupled filter converges to 0.019 mm and 0.038 mm, with the Y-axis penalty attributable directly to uncompensated cross-coupling. Computational cost of the coupled filter is 2.7 times that of the decoupled version but remains within real-time budget at 1 kHz.
venue: Journal of Mechatronics Engineering and Control

title: Design and SLS fabrication of a topology-optimised ankle-foot orthosis shell in PA12
abstract: An ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) shell was redesigned using topology optimisation to reduce material usage while preserving the structural stiffness required for a 90 kg user in level walking. Patient-specific geometry was derived from a structured-light scan; boundary conditions representing heel-strike and toe-off gait phases were applied based on published ground-reaction-force data. SIMP optimisation at 35 % volume fraction was followed by a graded lattice infill in low-stress regions identified post-optimisation. The resulting shell was manufactured in PA12 by SLS and compared with a conventional solid AFO shell of equal external geometry. Mass was reduced by 31 %, bending stiffness in the sagittal plane met the ISO 22523 category A stiffness requirement, and torsional compliance increased by 18 %, which is considered clinically acceptable. Three-point bend and torsion tests on five shells each confirmed the FEA predictions within 8 %. The workflow is documented in sufficient detail for replication with other SLS systems.

title: Uniaxial and Biaxial Characterisation of Silicone Elastomers for Pneumatic Bending Actuator Fabrication
abstract: Accurate finite element modelling of pneumatic soft actuators depends on reliable hyperelastic constitutive parameters derived from physical testing. This paper reports uniaxial and planar biaxial tensile tests performed on three commercially available platinum-cure silicone compounds at strain rates of 10, 50, and 200 mm/min, yielding stress–strain datasets used to fit Mooney–Rivlin, Neo-Hookean, and Yeoh material models. Specimens were cast in-house into dumbbell and cruciform geometries following ISO 37 and a custom biaxial protocol. Parameter fitting was carried out via nonlinear least squares minimisation. The Yeoh three-term model produced the lowest residual across all compounds and strain rates, with mean fit errors below 4.2%. FE models of a single-chamber bending actuator 80 mm in length were then constructed in a general-purpose implicit solver and validated against measured tip displacement at pressures from 0 to 80 kPa. Predicted tip angles agreed with optical measurements to within 6.1° root-mean-square across all three materials. The dataset and fitted parameters are provided as supplementary material to support reproducible actuator modelling in the region.

title: Torsional vibration decomposition in a two-stage helical gearbox using adaptive notch filtering
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive notch filtering approach for isolating torsional vibration components in a two-stage helical gearbox operating under steady-state conditions. Measurements were taken on a 7.5 kW test rig at shaft speeds ranging from 600 to 1800 rpm using piezoelectric accelerometers and a non-contact torque sensor. The adaptive notch filter was tuned iteratively to suppress the fundamental gear-mesh frequency and its first three harmonics, yielding residual signals used for fault feature extraction. Side-band energy ratios were computed from the residual spectra and compared against a healthy baseline. Results showed that even at an early fabricated wear stage, the side-band energy ratio increased by a factor of 2.3 relative to the healthy condition. The method was benchmarked against synchronous averaging and cepstrum pre-whitening on the same dataset. Computational cost and filter convergence time are discussed for potential real-time deployment on embedded hardware with limited processing resources.

title: Leaf water potential and osmotic adjustment in sunflower genotypes subjected to progressive soil drying at anthesis
abstract: Leaf water potential (Ψw) and osmotic potential (Ψs) were measured with a Scholander pressure chamber and a vapour-pressure osmometer, respectively, in eight sunflower genotypes during progressive soil drying imposed at anthesis under semi-controlled field conditions at Rimski Šančevi. Osmotic adjustment (OA) was calculated as the difference in Ψs between stressed and well-watered plants at equivalent relative water contents. Soil water content was monitored with TDR probes at three depths (0–30, 30–60, 60–90 cm). Genotypes ranged from 0.31 to 0.74 MPa in OA capacity, with the highest values recorded in two deep-rooted lines. Stomatal conductance measured with a portable porometer declined by 42–67 % across genotypes at a soil water potential of −0.6 MPa. A positive correlation (r = 0.71, p < 0.01) was found between OA and seed yield under stress, but not under well-watered conditions. Results indicate that OA contributes meaningfully to yield maintenance only when root depth allows access to subsoil moisture reserves.
venue: Journal of Field Crops and Stress Physiology

title: Root depth distribution and subsoil water extraction capacity in sunflower lines of contrasting drought tolerance under dryland conditions
abstract: Root architecture was characterised in twelve sunflower inbred lines and three hybrid checks grown in a dryland trial over two growing seasons (2022–2023) at Rimski Šančevi. Roots were sampled at 20 cm depth increments to 120 cm using a motorised corer, washed, and scanned with WinRHIZO Pro. Root length density (RLD), specific root length, and root diameter distribution were quantified. Lines varied substantially in RLD at 80–120 cm depth (range 0.12–0.89 cm cm⁻³), with three lines maintaining RLD above 0.60 cm cm⁻³ in the 100–120 cm layer. These deep-rooted lines extracted on average 18 mm more water from the 80–120 cm layer during the grain-filling period compared with shallow-rooted lines, as estimated from paired TDR measurements. Deeper rooting was associated with greater total dry matter accumulation (8–15 % higher) but not consistently with higher harvest index. Correlations between root traits and yield were stronger in the drier of the two seasons (r² = 0.61 vs 0.34).

title: Yield component partitioning under terminal drought in sunflower: head diameter, seed number and individual seed weight responses across eight genotypes
abstract: A pot experiment was conducted under controlled rainout-shelter conditions to isolate the effect of terminal drought (applied from R5 to physiological maturity) on yield component partitioning in eight sunflower genotypes. Drought was imposed by withholding irrigation when soil matric potential reached −0.35 MPa; control plants were maintained at −0.05 MPa. At harvest, head diameter, seeds per head, and individual seed weight (ISW) were recorded along with oil concentration determined by NMR. Terminal drought reduced seed number by 14–31 % and ISW by 8–22 %, depending on genotype. The relative contribution of seed number loss to total yield reduction exceeded that of ISW loss in six of eight genotypes. Oil concentration declined by 2.1–4.8 percentage points under stress. One genotype with above-average OA capacity (0.68 MPa) maintained ISW closest to the control, suggesting that osmotic adjustment partially protects seed-filling processes. These results are relevant for choosing selection criteria in breeding programmes targeting terminal drought environments in the Pannonian region.

title: Diurnal dynamics of leaf water potential in field-grown sunflower during a natural drought episode: genotype differences and their relation to canopy temperature
abstract: Leaf water potential was measured hourly from 06:00 to 20:00 across three days of an unirrigated period in July 2024 in a replicated field trial containing six sunflower hybrids at Rimski Šančevi. Predawn and midday Ψw were used to estimate the soil-to-leaf hydraulic conductance and the magnitude of daytime water deficit. Canopy temperature was measured simultaneously with a handheld infrared thermometer at 100 measurement points per plot. Midday Ψw ranged from −1.31 to −1.89 MPa across hybrids on the most water-limited day (soil Ψ ≈ −0.9 MPa at 30 cm). Canopy temperature depression relative to air temperature (CTD) was positively correlated with midday Ψw (r = 0.83) and negatively with stomatal conductance measured at 11:00. Two hybrids with deeper estimated root zones maintained less negative predawn Ψw on all three days, consistent with access to wetter subsoil layers. Diurnal courses differed substantially in the speed of afternoon Ψw recovery, a trait not yet routinely included in drought screening protocols.

title: Measurement uncertainty of Pst estimators under arc furnace operating conditions: a simulation-based assessment
abstract: The short-term flicker severity index Pst defined in IEC 61000-4-15 is subject to measurement uncertainty that depends on both the instrument implementation and the statistical properties of the input voltage signal. This paper quantifies measurement uncertainty for Pst values between 0.4 and 2.8 using a Monte Carlo simulation framework driven by synthetic arc furnace voltage waveforms. Arc furnace current models were calibrated against 72-hour field recordings at a 110/35 kV substation supplying an electric arc furnace of 80 MVA rated power in northern Serbia. Three commercial class-A flickermeters were compared against the IEC reference implementation. Results show that expanded uncertainty at 95% coverage probability reaches ±0.07 Pst units at Pst = 1.0 and grows non-linearly for Pst above 2.0. Differences among instrument implementations account for up to 40% of the total expanded uncertainty budget. The findings have direct implications for compliance assessments against grid code emission limits.

title: Statistical distributions of aggregated flicker indices in a 35 kV industrial feeder: a 12-month monitoring study
abstract: Long-term monitoring campaigns at medium-voltage busbars serving arc furnace installations rarely exceed a few weeks in published literature, leaving the tail behaviour of the Plt distribution poorly characterised. This paper reports a 12-month continuous power quality monitoring campaign at three 35 kV busbars in an industrial zone in the Vojvodina region, each supplying at least one electric arc furnace. Plt values were computed from IEC 61000-4-30 class-A instruments at ten-minute aggregation intervals, yielding approximately 52 000 valid Plt samples per site. The empirical distributions are fitted to log-normal, Weibull, and generalised extreme value models using maximum likelihood estimation. The log-normal model provides the best fit at all three sites (KS test, significance level 0.05). The 95th percentile of Plt at the most disturbed busbar was 1.74, exceeding the EN 50160 compatibility level of 1.0 in 8.3% of ten-minute intervals. Seasonal variation in arc furnace utilisation is identified as the dominant driver of distribution skewness.

title: Comparison of IEC and UIE flicker measurement methods applied to voltage recordings from an AC electric arc furnace
abstract: Two internationally recognised flicker measurement approaches—the IEC flickermeter defined in IEC 61000-4-15 and the UIE flickermeter described in UIE Publication 1992—differ in their detector stage weighting functions and in the statistical block used for Pst computation. Although both are in widespread use, systematic comparison studies using real arc furnace field data are sparse. This paper applies both methods to identical one-week voltage recordings captured at the 35 kV point of connection of a 60 MVA AC arc furnace in Serbia. The UIE method produced Pst values systematically 6–12% lower than the IEC method across the entire dataset, with the largest discrepancies occurring during the boring phase of the melt cycle when rapid current fluctuations dominate. The paper discusses the physiological weighting filter differences responsible for this divergence and their implications for grid code compliance assessment when different national standards reference different methods.

title: Voltage fluctuation propagation from 35 kV to 110 kV: attenuation factors observed during arc furnace operation
abstract: Flicker disturbances generated by arc furnace installations at medium voltage propagate upstream to the high-voltage transmission network, but the attenuation experienced during this propagation is seldom quantified from simultaneous measurements at both voltage levels. This paper presents synchronised measurements at the 35 kV and 110 kV busbars of two substations that supply arc furnace plants in northern Serbia, covering a combined monitoring period of 26 weeks. Simultaneous Pst and Plt indices were computed from class-A instruments with GPS time-synchronisation. The ratio Plt(110 kV)/Plt(35 kV) ranged from 0.31 to 0.68, with a median of 0.47. Attenuation was found to increase with short-circuit power at the 110 kV bus. A simple linear regression model predicts the 110 kV Plt from the 35 kV Plt and the short-circuit impedance ratio with an R² of 0.79. The model supports planning engineers in estimating upstream flicker impact without additional instrumentation.

title: Bootstrap confidence intervals for the 95th percentile of Plt in arc furnace installations
abstract: Grid codes and power quality standards typically specify compatibility levels in terms of high-order percentiles of power quality indices, yet the statistical uncertainty of those percentile estimates from finite monitoring campaigns is rarely reported by utilities or connection studies. This paper applies non-parametric bootstrap resampling to compute 95% confidence intervals for the 95th percentile of Plt distributions obtained from three industrial network monitoring campaigns of 4, 12, and 26 weeks duration. Using the 26-week campaign as a reference, the paper evaluates how the confidence interval width decreases as monitoring duration increases. A 4-week campaign yields confidence intervals of ±0.23 Plt units around the 95th percentile, while 12 weeks reduces this to ±0.11 units. The results suggest that current practice of using 4-week campaigns for connection studies may underestimate the risk of non-compliance at sites where arc furnace utilisation is seasonally variable. Practical guidance on minimum monitoring duration is proposed.

title: Power quality indices measurement methodology
abstract: This book chapter provides a comprehensive treatment of measurement methodology for power quality indices as standardised in IEC 61000-4-30, with particular attention to aggregation algorithms, flagging rules, and uncertainty sources. The chapter covers voltage characteristics (rms, dips, swells, interruptions, harmonics, flicker) and the instrumentation requirements for class-A, class-S, and class-B instruments. Special sections address the challenges specific to industrial network monitoring: high-frequency sampling demands, synchronisation across multiple measurement points, and the treatment of time-limited events such as arc furnace melt cycles within the standard aggregation framework. The chapter includes worked numerical examples using anonymised field data and discusses the reconciliation of IEC 61000-4-30 procedures with national grid code requirements in the Western Balkans and Central Europe. Aimed at practising engineers and graduate researchers, the text emphasises practical implementation rather than purely theoretical derivation.

title: Wavelet-based segmentation of arc furnace voltage signals for phase-resolved flicker analysis
abstract: Arc furnace melt cycles consist of several operationally distinct phases—bore-down, melting, refining, and tapping—each producing different voltage fluctuation characteristics. Standard ten-minute Pst computation cannot resolve this phase structure. This paper uses discrete wavelet packet decomposition (Daubechies-8 basis, six decomposition levels) to segment 240 complete melt cycle recordings from a 40 MVA arc furnace into operationally homogeneous segments. Segmentation is validated against furnace control system logs with a correct classification rate of 86%. Phase-resolved Pst values are subsequently computed over the identified segments. Bore-down phases produce median Pst of 2.41, significantly higher than the 1.12 observed during the refining phase. The segmentation approach also improves the fit of parametric flicker models calibrated to individual phases. The method requires no modification to the IEC flickermeter algorithm and can be implemented as a pre-processing layer on existing class-A instruments.

title: Influence of reactive power compensation on flicker indices at arc furnace busbars: field measurements before and after SVC installation
abstract: Static var compensators (SVCs) are widely deployed to reduce voltage fluctuations caused by arc furnace loads, yet published before-and-after field measurement studies are limited. This paper presents paired power quality monitoring data collected at the 35 kV connection busbar of a steelmaking plant in Serbia before and after commissioning of a ±60 Mvar SVC. The pre-SVC monitoring covered 8 weeks and the post-SVC monitoring covered 10 weeks, with both campaigns using the same class-A instrumentation installed at the same location. The 95th percentile of Pst fell from 2.31 to 0.87 after SVC commissioning, bringing the site into compliance with the applicable grid code limit of 1.0. Plt 95th percentile decreased from 1.96 to 0.74. The paper also documents a residual fast-flicker component at 8–12 Hz that the SVC did not suppress, attributed to the SVC's thyristor switching response time. The findings are relevant for SVC sizing studies at similar industrial sites.

title: Estimating flicker emission limits for multiple arc furnace installations sharing a common coupling point: an allocation methodology
abstract: When several arc furnace installations are connected to the same high-voltage busbar, grid codes require that a total emission level be allocated among them. IEC 61000-3-7 provides a general framework but leaves many implementation details to the discretion of the network operator. This paper develops a practical allocation methodology calibrated for the Serbian transmission network context, using simultaneous flicker measurements at nine coupling points over a six-month period to characterise the statistical correlation between simultaneous arc furnace operations. A key finding is that Pst values from different furnaces at the same busbar are weakly correlated (mean Pearson r = 0.18), allowing a near-quadratic summation rule to be applied with less than 5% overestimation error at the 95th percentile. The paper proposes an allocation procedure based on contracted apparent power and measured utilisation factor, and illustrates it with two worked case studies.

title: Characterisation of rapid voltage changes caused by arc furnace start-up events: frequency, magnitude and duration statistics
abstract: Rapid voltage changes (RVCs) produced during arc furnace start-up differ from steady-state voltage fluctuations and are governed by different IEC 61000-4-30 detection and characterisation rules. This paper analyses 14 months of continuous monitoring data at a 110/35/10 kV substation serving an integrated steelworks with two arc furnaces, identifying and characterising all RVC events meeting the IEC 61000-4-30 detection criteria. A total of 4 817 RVC events were detected, with median steady-state voltage change ΔUss of 1.8% and median duration of 340 ms. Extreme events (ΔUss > 5%) accounted for 3.1% of all events and were concentrated in the first 90 seconds after furnace energisation. The paper proposes empirical exceedance probability models for ΔUss and duration and discusses their use in connection assessment procedures. Results are compared against the EN 50160 indicative limit of ΔUss ≤ 3%.

title: Adequacy of EN 50160 flicker compatibility levels for high-utilisation arc furnace industrial parks: a data-driven review
abstract: EN 50160 sets a compatibility level of Plt ≤ 1.0 at medium-voltage public supply points, but industrial parks with dense arc furnace installation may structurally exceed this level during peak production periods. This paper assembles a database of 37 site-years of class-A power quality monitoring data from seven industrial medium-voltage networks in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, all characterised by arc furnace loads with utilisation factors above 0.6. The database is used to evaluate the exceedance frequency of the Plt = 1.0 limit under current operating conditions and to estimate how tightening or relaxing the limit would change the fraction of compliant sites. The analysis shows that 5 of 7 sites exceed Plt = 1.0 for more than 5% of weekly observation periods, making compliance formally unachievable without mitigation investment. The paper discusses the appropriateness of the single compatibility level for mixed public–industrial networks and proposes a differentiated limit framework analogous to the approach used in IEC 61000-3-7.

title: Wideband Propagation Measurements and Statistical Channel Model for Sub-GHz LPWAN in Vineyards with Wire-Trellis Support Structures
abstract: Vineyards present a propagation environment distinct from arable crops: the wire-trellis support system creates periodic metallic scattering structures with spacings of 2–3 m in the row direction and 1–1.5 m in the inter-row direction. This paper reports wideband channel sounding measurements at 433 MHz and 868 MHz in a 16-hectare vineyard in Fruška Gora foothills under three foliage states: dormant, flowering, and full-leaf. Delay spread statistics and path loss exponents are extracted per foliage state and per link orientation relative to the vine rows. A geometry-based stochastic channel model is parameterised for both frequencies; the model uses a dominant-cluster structure with two reflection clusters associated with the wire-trellis planes. Cross-row links show 3.1 dB lower path loss exponent than along-row links at both frequencies, attributed to waveguiding between trellis rows. The model parameters are provided in tabular form for use in simulation tools.

title: Heavy metal concentrations in Xanthoria parietina collected along a transect from an industrial zone in northern Serbia: baseline data and spatial patterns
abstract: Xanthoria parietina thalli were collected at 22 sites along a 40 km transect extending outward from a cement production facility in northern Vojvodina, Serbia. Samples were acid-digested and analysed by ICP-OES for Pb, Cd, Zn, Cu, Ni, and Cr. Mean Pb concentrations at sites within 2 km of the facility reached 48.3 µg g⁻¹ dry weight, compared to 6.1 µg g⁻¹ at background reference sites beyond 25 km. Cd showed the steepest distance-decay gradient, dropping from 2.9 to 0.3 µg g⁻¹ over the same range. Enrichment factors relative to local soil composition were calculated for all six elements, with Cd and Pb consistently exceeding factors of 10 in the near-source zone. Zn and Cu showed elevated but more spatially diffuse patterns. The results support the use of X. parietina as a reliable passive accumulator for near-source deposition studies and provide a reference dataset for future temporal comparisons in the region.

title: SEM-EDS characterisation of particulate matter trapped on lichen thallus surfaces near a petrochemical facility
abstract: The morphology and elemental composition of particles retained on thallus surfaces of Evernia prunastri and Flavoparmelia caperata were examined using scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) at five sites near a petrochemical processing facility in Vojvodina and two rural reference sites. Particle size distributions were determined from backscattered electron images of 200 fields per sample. Particles in the 1–10 µm range dominated at industrial sites, accounting for 63–78% of counted particles, while reference sites showed a broader distribution skewed toward coarser fractions. EDS mapping identified Fe-rich spherules consistent with combustion-derived particles at all industrial sites, alongside Ca–Al silicates and occasional Pb–Zn aggregates. Qualitative differences in particle loading density between the two lichen species were observed, with E. prunastri retaining approximately 1.4 times more particles per unit thallus area than F. caperata at comparable sites. Results are discussed in relation to thallus surface texture as a particle-trapping factor.

title: FokI and BsmI polymorphisms of the vitamin D receptor gene in Serbian patients with Crohn's disease: a case-control study
abstract: This case-control study examined the distribution of FokI (rs2228570) and BsmI (rs1544410) single-nucleotide polymorphisms of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) gene in 118 patients with Crohn's disease and 124 healthy controls recruited at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP. The FF genotype of FokI was significantly more frequent in patients than controls (OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.21–3.79, p=0.009), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed for BsmI genotype distribution. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels were lower in patients regardless of genotype. Logistic regression controlling for age, sex, and disease location confirmed independent association of the FokI FF genotype with disease presence. These findings suggest that the FokI polymorphism may contribute to Crohn's disease susceptibility in the Vojvodina population, warranting replication in larger regional cohorts.

title: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations at diagnosis predict one-year relapse in ulcerative colitis
abstract: A prospective cohort of 89 newly diagnosed ulcerative colitis patients was followed for twelve months to assess whether serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) concentration at diagnosis predicts clinical relapse, defined as a Mayo score increase of ≥3 with endoscopic confirmation. Serum 25(OH)D was measured by ELISA at diagnosis and at three-month intervals. At the end of follow-up, 41 patients (46%) had relapsed. Median 25(OH)D at diagnosis was significantly lower in relapsers (18.4 nmol/L) compared with non-relapsers (31.7 nmol/L, p<0.001). Cox proportional hazards modelling, adjusted for disease extent and baseline Mayo score, showed that each 10 nmol/L decrease in 25(OH)D was associated with a 1.38-fold increase in relapse hazard (HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.12–1.70). Seasonality of recruitment was accounted for in all analyses. These results support routine measurement of vitamin D status at IBD diagnosis.

title: TaqI and ApaI VDR variants and susceptibility to ulcerative colitis in a Vojvodina cohort
abstract: The TaqI (rs731236) and ApaI (rs7975232) polymorphisms of the VDR gene were genotyped in 102 ulcerative colitis patients and 108 healthy controls from the Vojvodina region using allelic discrimination real-time PCR on a CFX96 platform. Haplotype analysis was performed using the PHASE 2.1 algorithm. The tt genotype of TaqI was overrepresented among patients with extensive colitis compared with those with proctitis or left-sided disease (p=0.031). No significant main-effect association was found for ApaI alone, but the ApaI-A/TaqI-t haplotype was associated with disease susceptibility (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.10–3.24). C-reactive protein and faecal calprotectin at endoscopy did not differ significantly across genotype groups. These preliminary haplotype data indicate that combined analysis of VDR variants provides more informative risk stratification than single-locus testing in this population.

title: Interaction between VDR FokI genotype and vitamin D supplementation on relapse rate in Crohn's disease: a 24-month randomised pilot trial
abstract: Sixty patients with quiescent Crohn's disease in remission were randomised 1:1 to daily oral cholecalciferol 2000 IU or placebo for 24 months. The primary outcome was clinical relapse (Harvey–Bradshaw Index ≥5). VDR FokI genotype (FF, Ff, ff) was determined at baseline. Among patients carrying the FF genotype, supplemented participants had a significantly lower relapse rate at 24 months (20%) compared with placebo recipients (58%, log-rank p=0.028). In Ff and ff carriers, supplementation showed no significant effect on relapse. Adverse events were mild and equally distributed. Serum 25(OH)D rose to a mean of 68.3 nmol/L in the supplemented arm versus 21.7 nmol/L in placebo. Despite the small sample, the interaction term between FokI genotype and supplementation was statistically significant (p=0.041), suggesting genotype-guided vitamin D therapy may reduce relapse in a subset of patients.

title: Vitamin D receptor polymorphisms and response to biologic therapy in inflammatory bowel disease: a retrospective analysis
abstract: Medical records of 78 IBD patients (47 Crohn's disease, 31 ulcerative colitis) who received anti-TNF therapy (infliximab or adalimumab) for at least twelve months were reviewed retrospectively. Clinical response was defined as a drop of ≥70 points in CDAI or ≥3 points in total Mayo score sustained at week 52. VDR FokI, BsmI, TaqI, and ApaI genotypes were available from prior genotyping studies. Primary non-response rates were 38% in FF FokI carriers versus 17% in combined Ff+ff groups (p=0.048). Multivariate analysis adjusting for disease phenotype, prior immunomodulator use, and serum albumin retained FokI genotype as an independent predictor of primary non-response (OR 2.91, 95% CI 1.14–7.44). BsmI, TaqI, and ApaI showed no significant associations. These retrospective data motivate prospective evaluation of VDR genotyping before initiating biologic therapy.

title: Genetic susceptibility factors in inflammatory bowel disease: from association studies to clinical translation
abstract: This chapter reviews evidence from genome-wide association studies and candidate gene studies linking common genetic variants to IBD susceptibility and disease course, with emphasis on the VDR locus, NOD2, IL23R, and ATG16L1. The biological plausibility of each association is discussed in the context of innate immunity, autophagy, and epithelial barrier function. A section dedicated to the VDR locus critically evaluates published case-control and longitudinal data, including discrepancies attributable to population stratification and linkage disequilibrium differences between European subpopulations. The chapter also addresses practical barriers to clinical translation of pharmacogenomic findings in IBD, including lack of prospective validation, limited power in existing trials, and regulatory considerations. Directed at postgraduate students and clinician-scientists, the chapter provides a structured framework for evaluating genetic biomarkers in chronic inflammatory disease.
venue: Advances in Gastroenterology: A Postgraduate Textbook (University of Novi Sad Press)

title: Seasonal variation in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and disease activity in a longitudinal IBD outpatient cohort
abstract: One hundred and twelve IBD outpatients (64 Crohn's disease, 48 ulcerative colitis) were followed for two years with quarterly assessments of serum 25(OH)D, C-reactive protein, faecal calprotectin, and standardised disease activity indices. Mixed-effects linear regression was used to model within-patient seasonal variation. Mean 25(OH)D was lowest in February (19.2 nmol/L, SD 8.4) and highest in August (38.6 nmol/L, SD 11.1). Calprotectin levels were inversely correlated with concurrent 25(OH)D (β=−4.3 μg/g per 10 nmol/L, 95% CI −6.1 to −2.5, p<0.001) after adjustment for medication, age, and BMI. Relapse events were more frequent in winter quarters than summer quarters (34% vs 19%, χ²=7.8, p=0.005). FokI FF carriers showed larger seasonal amplitude in both 25(OH)D and calprotectin than other genotype groups. These findings suggest that monitoring and corrective supplementation should be intensified during autumn and winter in IBD patients, particularly FF carriers.
