title: Fecal microbiota composition in IBD patients stratified by VDR FokI genotype: a cross-sectional pilot study
abstract: Stool samples from 36 IBD patients in clinical remission were subjected to 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing (V3–V4 region) on an Illumina MiSeq platform to characterise gut microbiota composition across VDR FokI genotype groups (13 FF, 16 Ff, 7 ff). Alpha diversity did not differ significantly between groups. At the genus level, relative abundance of Faecalibacterium was lower in FF compared with ff carriers (mean 3.1% vs 8.6%, Wilcoxon p=0.037 after Benjamini–Hochberg correction). Bifidobacterium abundance showed a non-significant trend toward reduction in FF carriers. Serum 25(OH)D correlated positively with Faecalibacterium abundance across all patients (Spearman ρ=0.44, p=0.007). Given the small sample size, these associations are considered exploratory. The data are consistent with a model in which reduced VDR signalling in FF carriers contributes to diminished colonisation by butyrate-producing bacteria.

title: A multi-centre Balkan registry for VDR polymorphisms in inflammatory bowel disease: study protocol and baseline characteristics
abstract: This paper describes the design and baseline data of the BalkanVDR-IBD registry, a multi-centre observational study enrolling IBD patients from seven gastroenterology units in Serbia, Romania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Between January 2021 and December 2023, 487 patients (287 Crohn's disease, 200 ulcerative colitis) were enrolled. Standardised phenotyping followed the Montreal Classification. VDR genotyping covers FokI, BsmI, TaqI, and ApaI; serum 25(OH)D is measured annually. At baseline, mean age was 38.4 years (SD 13.1); 51.3% were female. The FF FokI genotype frequency was 29.4%, consistent with prior Balkan cohort estimates. Vitamin D insufficiency (25(OH)D <50 nmol/L) was present in 74% of the cohort at enrolment. Primary outcomes include annual relapse rate, need for biologic escalation, and hospitalisation. The registry will provide adequately powered analyses of genotype–outcome associations unavailable from any single-centre study in the region.

title: Preprint: Interaction of VDR FokI genotype with gut barrier integrity markers in IBD: serum zonulin and claudin-3 across genotype groups
abstract: We measured serum zonulin and claudin-3 as surrogate markers of intestinal barrier permeability in 68 IBD patients (40 active disease, 28 remission) and 30 controls, stratified by VDR FokI genotype. Zonulin was elevated in IBD patients relative to controls (mean 49.3 vs 28.1 ng/mL, p<0.001). Among IBD patients, FF carriers had higher zonulin than Ff+ff carriers in both active (66.2 vs 51.4 ng/mL, p=0.018) and remission states (38.9 vs 29.3 ng/mL, p=0.044). Claudin-3 showed a comparable pattern in active disease only. Linear regression adjusting for BMI, disease type, and medication showed that each unit increase in Harvey–Bradshaw Index and FF genotype independently predicted higher zonulin. These preliminary data, subject to peer review, suggest that the FokI FF genotype is associated with impaired barrier function beyond the effect of disease activity, and may contribute to the higher relapse susceptibility observed in this genotype group.

title: Ferritin, CRP, and procalcitonin as early markers of bacterial versus viral trigger in COPD exacerbations requiring hospitalisation
abstract: Identifying the infectious trigger of acute COPD exacerbations has practical implications for antibiotic stewardship. This prospective observational study enrolled 98 consecutive patients admitted to a secondary-level hospital in Novi Sad from March to November 2023. Sputum cultures, serology for common respiratory viruses, and serum ferritin, CRP, and procalcitonin were obtained within six hours of admission. A definite or probable bacterial aetiology was identified in 41 patients (41.8%), a viral aetiology in 27 (27.6%), and no pathogen was identified in the remainder. Median ferritin was 387 µg/L (IQR 210–610) in the bacterial group versus 198 µg/L (IQR 115–320) in the viral group (p=0.004). Procalcitonin discriminated bacterial aetiology better (AUC 0.79) than ferritin alone (AUC 0.68), but a combined score incorporating both markers reached AUC 0.84. Ferritin above 300 µg/L was independently associated with bacterial trigger after adjustment for prior antibiotic use and spirometric severity. The study was limited by the inability to confirm viral aetiology in all cases.

title: Industrial Wasteland or Urban Resource? Mapping Derelict Riverfront Land along the Danube between Novi Sad and Vukovar
abstract: This study presents a systematic cartographic survey of derelict and underused riverfront parcels along a 140-kilometre Danube corridor between Novi Sad and Vukovar, conducted between 1993 and 1995. Aerial photograph interpretation was combined with municipal cadastral records and field visits to classify 87 distinct sites by former industrial use, current contamination indicator, and degree of hydrological exposure. Results showed that 61 percent of mapped parcels had direct flood-plain contact, and 34 percent exhibited surface evidence of hydrocarbon or heavy-metal contamination. The study established a five-category typology—active industrial, recently abandoned, long-term derelict, informally occupied, and partially remediated—that informed subsequent regional planning discussions. The paper argues that standard land-use surveys consistently undercount riverfront brownfields because administrative boundaries follow property lines rather than hydrological units. The typology and base maps produced were adopted as reference materials in subsequent cross-border planning workshops organised under early Phare CBC programmes.

title: Soil Contamination Profiles at Four Former Shipyard Sites in the Vojvodina Danube Reach: Implications for Vegetation-Based Remediation
abstract: Soil samples were collected at 0.5-metre depth intervals to 3 metres at four former shipyard locations in Vojvodina, totalling 216 samples analysed for lead, zinc, copper, and total petroleum hydrocarbon (TPH) concentrations. All sites exceeded Serbian provisional soil quality thresholds for at least two contaminants in the upper 1.5 metres, with one site recording TPH values of 4,800 mg/kg in the intertidal zone. The study then tested phytoremediation potential under controlled greenhouse conditions using three locally available plant species—common reed (Phragmites australis), black poplar (Populus nigra), and smooth cordgrass (Spartina alterniflora)—over an 18-month period. Phragmites australis achieved the highest TPH uptake rates under simulated seasonal flooding cycles. The findings suggest that phytoremediation can serve as a low-cost first-stage treatment compatible with later landscape design interventions, but only where contaminant concentrations fall below a site-specific threshold established in the study. Regulatory implications for Serbian brownfield ordinances are discussed.

title: Landscape Urbanism and the Post-Industrial Waterfront: Adapting North American Frameworks to Pannonian Conditions
abstract: During the late 1990s and early 2000s, landscape urbanism emerged as a distinct theoretical position in North American and British planning discourse, foregrounding ecological process, infrastructural logistics, and temporal phasing over fixed spatial composition. This book chapter critically evaluates the transferability of key landscape urbanism propositions—particularly those developed for former industrial port and rail-yard sites in Chicago, Toronto, and London—to the very different legal, climatic, and ownership conditions of medium-sized post-socialist cities along the Danube and Tisza rivers. The chapter argues that the emphasis on process and indeterminacy translates poorly to contexts where municipal planning capacity is limited, land ownership is fragmented among multiple state successor entities, and EU Structural Fund timelines impose rigid delivery schedules. A modified framework is proposed that preserves the ecological process logic of landscape urbanism while accommodating the project-delivery constraints common in Serbian and Hungarian municipal planning practice. The chapter draws on three planning case studies and workshop material from a 2006 bilateral academic exchange.

title: Blue-Green Infrastructure as Flood Buffer: Performance Monitoring at the Šodrošpark Brownfield Pilot, Novi Sad, 2005–2009
abstract: A 4.2-hectare former gravel-processing yard on the Danube south bank in Novi Sad was partially remediated and replanted between 2003 and 2005 as a pilot blue-green infrastructure intervention. This paper reports monitoring data collected across four complete hydrological years (2005–2009) covering surface runoff volume, infiltration rates, inundation extent during three moderate flood events, and vegetation establishment. An automated water-level gauge network of seven stations recorded peak flood-wave attenuation of 8–14 percent relative to an adjacent unmodified embankment section. Infiltration rates in the restored wetland fringe reached 42 mm/hour by year three, compared with 6 mm/hour on compacted fill areas. Vegetation transects recorded 23 spontaneous colonising species supplementing the 11 planted species, indicating successful ecological integration. Cost data show that the intervention cost approximately 40 percent less per square metre than conventional hard-engineering bank stabilisation applied at a comparable site upstream. Limitations of the before-after control-impact design are discussed.

title: Revisiting the Šodrošpark Pilot Twenty Years On: Long-Term Vegetation Dynamics and Infrastructure Performance under Intensified Flood Cycles
abstract: A follow-up survey of the Šodrošpark blue-green infrastructure pilot site (first monitored 2005–2009; see Lačoková et al. 2010) was conducted in 2023–2024 to assess long-term performance under the altered hydrological regime of the intervening two decades, which included the exceptional Danube flood of 2013 and three further moderate events. Vegetation surveys using the same transect locations as the original study recorded 54 species, up from 34 in 2009, with canopy closure now averaging 68 percent in the wetland fringe zone. Soil carbon content in restored areas had increased to 3.1 percent compared with 0.8 percent at monitoring inception. However, two infiltration trenches installed in 2003 had partially blocked with fine sediment deposited during the 2013 flood, reducing local infiltration rates to below design values. The 2013 flood also redistributed residual hydrocarbon contamination into a previously clean sector of the site. The paper discusses implications for maintenance protocols and for the design life assumptions embedded in Serbian technical standards for blue-green urban infrastructure.

title: Velocity distribution and Manning roughness coefficient in channels with emergent rigid cylinder arrays at varying densities
abstract: Laboratory experiments were performed in a 12 m long, 0.60 m wide recirculating tilting flume to examine how stem density affects depth-averaged velocity profiles and the bulk Manning roughness coefficient in flow with emergent rigid cylinders. Cylinder diameters of 8 mm and 16 mm were arranged in staggered patterns at solid volume fractions ranging from 0.005 to 0.045. Acoustic Doppler velocimetry measurements were taken at 45 cross-sectional points per run, and Manning's n was back-calculated from measured water surface slopes and cross-sectional mean velocities. Results showed that Manning's n increased from 0.018 to 0.071 as solid volume fraction increased from 0.005 to 0.045 for the 8 mm cylinders, with slightly higher values for the 16 mm arrays at equivalent densities. A regression equation relating n to solid volume fraction and stem diameter is proposed, calibrated against 72 individual experimental runs. The relationship departs from existing empirical formulas at high densities, suggesting that wake interference between stems becomes the dominant flow resistance mechanism above a solid volume fraction of approximately 0.030.

title: Effect of flexible stem deflection on energy head loss in submerged aquatic vegetation: a flume study
abstract: Flexible aquatic vegetation bends under current, altering its projected area and therefore the drag force it exerts on the flow. This study quantified energy head loss across a 1.8 m long vegetation patch of polyethylene strips mimicking submerged flexible macrophytes at three stem heights (0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 m) and four Froude numbers (0.08–0.28). Water surface elevations were recorded with a point gauge and a laser distance sensor at 0.05 m intervals along the flume centreline. Stem deflection angles were measured from video frames captured at 60 frames per second. Head loss across the patch ranged from 4 mm to 31 mm depending on stem height and discharge, and was consistently 18–34 % lower than predicted by rigid-stem formulas at equivalent densities. A modified drag coefficient accounting for reconfiguration number (Vogel exponent ≈ −0.28) reproduced measured head losses with a mean absolute error of 2.1 mm. The findings suggest that rigid-stem assumptions lead to measurable overestimates of energy dissipation in channels with flexible vegetation, with practical implications for flood routing models.

title: RANS simulation of turbulent flow through emergent vegetation patches using the k–ε and k–ω SST models: comparison with laboratory measurements
abstract: Two Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes turbulence closure models, standard k–ε and k–ω SST, were applied to simulate three-dimensional flow through a staggered array of 8 mm diameter emergent cylinders in a 0.60 m wide channel at solid volume fractions of 0.010 and 0.030. The computational domain discretised the individual cylinders explicitly, with a mesh of approximately 4.2 million hexahedral cells. Inflow boundary conditions and bulk discharge values were set to match six previously published flume runs from the authors' earlier work. Depth-averaged velocity fields and turbulent kinetic energy distributions from both models were compared against ADV measurements at 45 points per cross-section. The k–ω SST model reproduced depth-averaged velocities with a root-mean-square error of 0.018 m/s compared with 0.031 m/s for k–ε, and better captured the lateral shear layer at the patch edge. Both models underpredicted turbulent kinetic energy in the near-wake region by 15–25 %. Computational cost of the k–ω SST runs was approximately 40 % higher. Results indicate that k–ω SST is preferable for patch-scale resistance modelling while k–ε remains acceptable for channel-reach scale simulations where computational economy is a priority.

title: Parameterisation of bulk drag in two-dimensional flood inundation models for channels with emergent vegetation: sensitivity analysis and calibration guidelines
abstract: Two-dimensional shallow-water flood models typically represent vegetation resistance through a bulk drag source term, but guidance on appropriate parameter ranges for emergent vegetation in Serbian lowland channels is limited. This study used a 2D finite-volume model applied to a 400 m reach of a drainage canal in the Vojvodina plain, with vegetation survey data collected along 18 cross-sections in summer 2024. Drag coefficients were varied from 0.5 to 2.5 and stem density from 5 to 80 stems/m² in a factorial sensitivity analysis comprising 256 model runs. Simulated water surface elevations were compared with staff gauge records from four flood events between 2020 and 2024. Sensitivity analysis showed that stem density had roughly twice the influence of drag coefficient on simulated water surface slope. A calibration procedure based on reach-averaged vegetation density maps derived from drone imagery reduced the root-mean-square error of simulated peak water levels from 0.18 m to 0.07 m. Practical guidelines for parameter selection in routine flood studies are outlined, together with uncertainty bounds derived from Monte Carlo resampling of the vegetation survey data.

title: Diffusion coefficients of di(2-ethylhexyl) adipate from PVC-based monolayer films into iso-octane at 20–60 °C
abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) adipate (DEHA) is a common plasticiser in flexible PVC wraps used for fatty cheese and cured meats. This study measured specific migration of DEHA into iso-octane as a fatty food simulant at 20, 40, and 60 °C over contact periods of 2, 6, 24, and 72 hours using GC-MS. Partition and diffusion coefficients were derived by fitting a Fickian one-layer model to the experimental data. At 60 °C and 72 h, DEHA migration reached 14.3 mg/dm², exceeding the specific migration limit set by EU Regulation No 10/2011. An Arrhenius relationship was confirmed for the temperature dependence of the diffusion coefficient, with an activation energy of 68.4 kJ/mol. The results indicate that storage temperature management is a more critical control point than contact time at ambient conditions. Practical implications for retail display of fatty fresh cheeses wrapped in PVC stretch film are discussed.

title: Effect of polyethylene layer thickness on migration of Irganox-type phenolic antioxidants in coextruded PE/PA/PE films
abstract: Phenolic antioxidants such as 3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-hydroxytoluene (BHT) and octadecyl-3-(3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-hydroxyphenyl)propionate (AO-1076) are routinely added to polyethylene layers in coextruded polyamide barrier films for vacuum packaging. Migration of both compounds into ethanol 95% v/v simulant was measured at 40 °C over 10 days using HPLC-DAD with a C18 reversed-phase column. Three film architectures were compared: 30, 50, and 80 µm outer PE layers. Migration of BHT increased from 0.8 to 4.1 mg/kg with layer thickness, while AO-1076 migration remained below 0.3 mg/kg across all variants, consistent with its high molecular weight limiting mobility. A two-layer diffusion model incorporating the polyamide as a functional barrier reproduced experimental profiles with a root-mean-square deviation below 8%. These findings provide direct evidence that AO-1076 represents a safer antioxidant choice in functional-barrier film designs for high-fat simulant contact.

title: Comparative migration of dibutyl sebacate and dioctyl sebacate from regenerated cellulose film coatings into sunflower oil simulant
abstract: Regenerated cellulose films coated with nitrocellulose-based lacquers containing sebacate plasticisers are used in European smoked meat packaging. This study compared specific migration of dibutyl sebacate (DBS) and dioctyl sebacate (DOS) from commercially sourced coated cellulose films into refined sunflower oil as a fatty food simulant at 23 and 40 °C. Extraction and HPLC-DAD quantification were performed at 0.5, 1, 3, 7, and 14 days. DBS migrated 3.2 to 4.8 times faster than DOS at both temperatures, reaching 6.7 mg/dm² at 40 °C after 14 days. Total migration measured gravimetrically did not predict individual additive release reliably (R² = 0.41), underscoring the need for compound-specific analysis. A surface plot of migration as a function of temperature and time was constructed to aid shelf-life modelling. Results are compared with published values for PVC-derived sebacates and differences in polymer matrix solubility are discussed.

title: Modelling plasticiser migration across three-layer PET/adhesive/PE structures using a variable diffusivity approach
abstract: Standard Fickian models assume concentration-independent diffusivity, an assumption that breaks down at high plasticiser loadings in semi-crystalline polymers. This work developed a numerical finite-difference scheme allowing concentration-dependent diffusion coefficients to describe acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) migration from the PE sealant layer of PET/adhesive/PE laminates into olive oil simulant (HB307 isooctane surrogate) at 70 °C, representing hot-fill conditions. Diffusivity was expressed as D(c) = D₀·exp(βc) with β determined by least-squares optimisation against measured migration profiles. The variable-diffusivity model reduced prediction error from 23% to 9% relative to the constant-diffusivity baseline at plasticiser loadings above 4% w/w. Sensitivity analysis showed that adhesive layer resistance was negligible above 50 °C. The modelling framework is implemented in a freely distributed MATLAB script. These results are relevant for hot-fill olive oil and ready-meal tray applications.

title: Migration of epoxidised soybean oil from PVC gaskets into vegetable oil-based foodstuffs: influence of fat content and contact geometry
abstract: Epoxidised soybean oil (ESBO) serves as both a plasticiser and a heat stabiliser in PVC lid gaskets for glass jars. This study examined ESBO migration into three fat simulants (sunflower oil, 50% ethanol in sunflower oil emulsion, and Tenax solid simulant) at 40 °C for 30 days, replicating commercial jar storage conditions. Contact geometry was varied: full-immersion strips versus gasket-against-simulant headspace. Full-immersion yielded ESBO transfer 2.7–4.1 times higher than gasket-contact geometry, demonstrating that coupon-based laboratory tests overestimate real-world migration. ESBO concentrations in sunflower oil reached 42 mg/kg under full-immersion but only 11 mg/kg under realistic gasket-contact at 30 days. The specific migration limit of 60 mg/kg was not exceeded under either geometry. ATR-FTIR analysis of gaskets before and after migration confirmed measurable loss of the epoxide carbonyl peak at 822 cm⁻¹. The data support a geometry correction factor for regulatory compliance assessments.

title: Migration kinetics and packaging material interactions
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of mass-transfer theory applied to food-contact plastics, with emphasis on multilayer structures used in chilled and ambient fatty food packaging. Topics covered include derivation of the one-layer and bilayer Fickian models, experimental design for migration testing in compliance with EU Regulation No 10/2011, selection of fatty food simulants, and worked examples using ATBC, DEHA, and BHT as model compounds. Practical guidance is given on fitting diffusion and partition coefficients using non-linear least squares in common software environments. A section on temperature scaling via the Piringer estimation model discusses its applicability to semi-crystalline versus amorphous polymers. Case studies draw on published data for PVC, PE, PP, and PA-based laminates. The chapter closes with an overview of regulatory trends affecting the use of phthalate and adipate plasticisers in European markets.
venue: Handbook of Polymer Packaging for Food Applications, edited volume, TechPress Academic, Zagreb

title: Influence of repeated freeze-thaw cycling on plasticiser migration from low-density polyethylene films into fatty food simulants
abstract: Frozen ready-meal trays sealed with LDPE-based lidding films are subjected to repeated freeze-thaw cycles during distribution and consumer re-freezing. This study investigated how 0, 3, 6, and 10 freeze-thaw cycles (−18 °C to +20 °C, 12 h per half-cycle) affect migration of ATBC and DEHA from commercially supplied LDPE lidding films into HB307 fatty simulant. ATR-FTIR crystallinity indices and DSC thermograms were recorded after each cycle set to track polymer structural changes. Crystallinity increased by 6–9% after 10 cycles, correlating with a 15–22% reduction in plasticiser migration relative to uncycled controls. GC-MS quantification confirmed that cumulative migration after 10 cycles remained well below SML values. The mechanism is attributed to densification of amorphous regions reducing additive mobility. These findings suggest that conservative worst-case migration assessments based on isothermal tests at 20 °C may overestimate actual exposure for frozen food packaging.

title: Effect of enzymatic pre-treatment with pepsin on mechanical properties and permeability of ovine casings intended for dry-fermented sausage production
abstract: Ovine casings were treated with pepsin solutions at 0.02%, 0.05%, and 0.10% (w/v) for 30, 60, and 90 minutes at 37 °C prior to salting. Tensile properties, bursting pressure, and water vapour permeability were measured after treatment and after a standard 21-day salting period. The 0.05% pepsin treatment for 60 minutes increased WVTR by 22% and reduced breaking strength by only 8%, compared to untreated controls. Higher pepsin concentrations (0.10%) degraded mechanical integrity excessively, reducing breaking strength by 34%. Histological sections confirmed partial dissolution of the serosal collagen layer at the two higher concentrations. For dry-fermented sausage applications where accelerated drying is desired without casing rupture, the 0.05%/60 min combination was identified as technically practical.

title: Influence of pH adjustment between 4.5 and 7.0 on protein–starch interaction strength and gel mechanical properties in whey protein–wheat starch systems
abstract: The role of pH in governing interaction strength between wheat starch and whey protein isolate (WPI) was examined in mixed gels prepared at pH 4.5, 5.5, 6.0, 6.5, and 7.0. Total biopolymer content was fixed at 14 % (w/w) with a 10:4 starch-to-WPI ratio. Electrostatic interaction potential was estimated using zeta-potential measurements at each pH prior to gel formation. Maximum electrostatic attraction between starch granule surfaces and WPI occurred near pH 5.5 (zeta potential difference ≈ 28 mV). Gels formed at pH 5.5 showed the highest G′ (5 820 Pa) and the lowest syneresis after three freeze–thaw cycles (9.8 %). At pH 7.0, G′ was 3 410 Pa and syneresis reached 19.2 %. Dynamic mechanical spectra showed a crossover from predominantly elastic to viscoelastic behaviour at angular frequencies above 60 rad/s only for pH 7.0 gels. These results indicate that pH optimisation alone, without additional stabilisers, can meaningfully extend freeze–thaw textural performance.

title: A cost-allocation framework for waste-stream exchanges between co-located firms in a Vojvodina industrial zone
abstract: This paper develops a cost-allocation framework for evaluating bilateral waste-exchange agreements between co-located manufacturers. Using data from three pairs of firms operating within the Inđija industrial zone — a food-processing plant, a packaging manufacturer, and a chemical blending facility — the framework assigns avoided disposal costs and avoided raw-material procurement costs to each participant using a Shapley-value approach. Annual material flows were metered for 18 months; organic sludge, solvent residues, and cardboard off-cuts were the three principal streams. Results show that the packaging–food-processing dyad achieves cost neutrality within 2.1 years under conservative price assumptions, while the chemical–food-processing dyad requires a minimum exchange volume of 340 tonnes per year to break even. Sensitivity analysis over energy and transport price corridors indicates that payback periods range from 1.8 to 4.6 years depending on diesel costs. The framework is implemented as a parameterised Excel workbook made available to practitioners.

title: Material flow analysis of a greenfield agro-food processing cluster: baseline data and methodological constraints
abstract: Establishing reliable baseline material flow accounts for newly formed industrial clusters presents data challenges that are rarely discussed in the symbiosis literature. This study constructs a mass-balance model for a planned agro-food processing cluster in southern Vojvodina comprising seven facilities at different stages of construction. Input data were drawn from environmental impact statements, equipment vendor specifications, and analogues from four comparable clusters in Hungary and Romania. Uncertainty was propagated using Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations. Results indicate that organic waste generation is underestimated by 15–40% in pre-construction impact statements relative to analogues, and that steam demand peaks create a 6-hour daily window during which inter-firm heat exchange would be technically feasible. The paper argues that feasibility studies conducted before cluster occupancy should incorporate a mandatory revision step triggered by the first 12 months of operational metering data.

title: Payback period sensitivity to energy price volatility in steam-sharing networks: a case from a Serbian petrochemical park
abstract: Steam-sharing networks are among the most capital-intensive forms of industrial symbiosis, requiring dedicated pipeline infrastructure whose payback period is highly sensitive to energy price fluctuations. This study models a proposed steam-sharing configuration at a petrochemical manufacturing park near Pančevo involving four firms. Infrastructure investment was estimated at EUR 2.3 million based on engineering quotes obtained in 2014. Using historical natural gas price series from 2004 to 2014 and three forward scenarios constructed from Serbian Energy Agency forecasts, payback periods were calculated under deterministic and stochastic conditions. Under the base scenario the payback period is 6.4 years; under the high-volatility scenario it extends to 11.2 years. The analysis identifies the minimum guaranteed off-take volume — 18,500 GJ per year — below which the configuration is not financially viable without subsidy. Contractual structures that could reduce exposure to price risk are discussed.

title: Inter-firm water recycling in textile dyeing clusters: economic feasibility under variable effluent compositions
abstract: Textile dyeing facilities generate effluent streams whose composition varies substantially with production scheduling, complicating the design of shared treatment and recycling infrastructure. This chapter reviews published techno-economic assessments of water recycling schemes in textile clusters and proposes a generalised feasibility model that accounts for composition variability explicitly. The model separates capital costs (treatment plant, pipework, monitoring) from operating costs (chemicals, energy, labour) and evaluates net present value over a 15-year horizon. Drawing on data from six clusters in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria reviewed under a bilateral research collaboration, the chapter reports that NPV is positive in four of six cases when a pollution levy of at least EUR 1.2 per cubic metre is in force, and negative in all six cases without such a levy. Policy implications for regional industrial water governance are discussed.

title: Accounting for transaction costs in industrial symbiosis feasibility models: evidence from four Serbian manufacturing parks
abstract: Feasibility models for industrial symbiosis routinely omit transaction costs — negotiation, contracting, monitoring, and enforcement — which can materially alter project viability assessments. This study adds an explicit transaction cost module to a standard techno-economic model and calibrates it using interview data from managers at four manufacturing parks in Serbia: two in Vojvodina and two in central Serbia. Transaction costs were quantified through structured interviews using an adapted Delphi protocol with 34 respondents. Findings show that transaction costs add between 8% and 23% to total project costs depending on the number of participants and the novelty of the exchange type. In three of sixteen symbiosis links examined, inclusion of transaction costs shifted the feasibility verdict from positive to negative NPV. The paper provides a parameterised transaction cost module that can be appended to existing feasibility spreadsheet models.

title: A stepwise screening method for identifying economically viable symbiosis pairs in mixed-use industrial estates
abstract: Mixed-use industrial estates with heterogeneous tenants pose a combinatorial challenge for symbiosis identification: the number of potential exchange pairs grows rapidly with estate size, while most pairs are not economically viable. This paper presents a three-stage screening method designed to reduce the candidate space before full feasibility modelling is applied. Stage one uses mass-balance data to filter pairs by minimum flow volume thresholds. Stage two applies a transport-cost heuristic to eliminate geographically distant pairs. Stage three performs a rapid payback calculation using unit cost benchmarks. The method is applied to a 43-firm industrial estate in Subotica. Starting from 903 candidate pairs, stages one, two, and three reduce the set to 87, 34, and 11 pairs respectively. Full feasibility modelling of the 11 remaining pairs confirms economic viability for 7. Computation time for the full screening is under four hours using standard spreadsheet tools.

title: Heat integration potential between a food-processing facility and a district heating network: a techno-economic assessment
abstract: Food-processing plants generate substantial low-grade waste heat that is typically dissipated through cooling towers. This study evaluates the techno-economic feasibility of connecting a large dairy processing facility in Zrenjanin to the municipal district heating network as a supplemental heat source during the October–March heating season. Process measurements over two consecutive heating seasons established a usable waste heat output of 4.1 MW at 65–72°C. Capital investment for the heat exchanger substation, pipeline connection, and control systems was estimated at EUR 870,000 based on three contractor quotes. The calculated simple payback period is 5.1 years at current heat tariff rates, falling to 3.7 years if the plant avoids a planned cooling-tower upgrade. The assessment identifies regulatory ambiguities in Serbian district heating legislation that currently prevent formal heat purchase agreements between industrial producers and municipal utilities, and proposes a draft contract structure.

title: Carbon cost internalisation and its effect on industrial symbiosis project payback periods in Serbia
abstract: Serbia's prospective alignment with EU carbon pricing mechanisms raises questions about how carbon cost internalisation would affect the financial viability of industrial symbiosis investments. This paper models the payback period impact of hypothetical carbon prices of EUR 15, 30, 50, and 80 per tonne CO₂ equivalent for a portfolio of 19 symbiosis configurations previously assessed under the RESINPARK project. Emission factors were derived from plant-level metering data and IPCC Tier 2 defaults where primary data were unavailable. Results show that at EUR 30/tonne, 14 of 19 configurations shift from marginal to clearly viable (payback under 7 years); at EUR 50/tonne, all 19 become viable. The analysis disaggregates effects by exchange type: energy exchanges benefit most from carbon pricing, while material exchanges show smaller but still significant improvements. The paper discusses implications for policy design and for the sequencing of symbiosis investments in anticipation of carbon market entry.

title: Inter-firm nitrogen flow accounting in a co-located fertiliser and plastics manufacturing park
abstract: Nitrogen-containing by-products arise in both fertiliser production and certain plastics manufacturing processes, creating potential for closed-loop exchange that is underexplored in the symbiosis literature. This study constructs a nitrogen flow account for a co-located park in northern Serbia comprising a nitrogen fertiliser producer, a polyamide compounding facility, and a wastewater treatment operator. Flow data covering 24 months were collected from plant logbooks and verified against statutory environmental reports. The nitrogen balance reveals a recoverable ammonium stream of 210 tonnes per year from polyamide process washwater that currently enters the wastewater treatment system at net disposal cost. Techno-economic modelling of a proposed struvite recovery unit indicates a payback period of 4.3 years at current ammonium sulphate market prices. A secondary finding is that inter-firm nitrogen accounting exposed a systematic underreporting of approximately 18% in the facility's statutory environmental returns.

title: Feasibility boundaries for industrial symbiosis under supply chain disruption conditions: a scenario analysis
abstract: Industrial symbiosis configurations depend on continuous material and energy flows between partner firms; supply chain disruptions that interrupt one partner's operations propagate financial losses to others. This paper examines how disruption risk affects the techno-economic feasibility of six symbiosis configurations in two manufacturing parks in Vojvodina, drawing on production interruption records from 2015 to 2022. A disruption penalty term is incorporated into the standard NPV model, calibrated using observed downtime frequencies and durations. Results show that for configurations with fewer than three redundant exchange partners, disruption risk increases effective payback periods by 0.8 to 2.9 years. Configurations involving just two firms and capital-intensive shared infrastructure cross the infeasibility threshold (NPV < 0) when annual disruption probability exceeds 12%. The paper proposes minimum redundancy requirements and contractual penalty structures to maintain feasibility under realistic disruption frequencies.

title: A dynamic payback model for industrial symbiosis investments subject to tenant turnover in manufacturing parks
abstract: Manufacturing parks experience tenant turnover — firms leaving or entering — that can alter the economic basis of symbiosis configurations mid-project. Standard static payback models do not capture this dynamic. This paper proposes a discrete-event simulation model in which tenant arrivals and departures are modelled as stochastic processes calibrated to observed turnover rates in 12 Serbian and Hungarian manufacturing parks over a 10-year period. The simulation generates distributions of payback periods under different turnover rate assumptions and contract length scenarios. Median payback periods under observed turnover rates are 1.4 to 2.8 years longer than static model estimates. The model identifies a critical contract length — the minimum binding term required to maintain positive NPV in 90% of simulated scenarios — which ranges from 5 to 9 years depending on the exchange type and number of participating firms. Practical guidance for park management on lease structuring is provided.

title: A genetic algorithm for mixed-model sequencing with stochastic task times and sequence-dependent inventory costs
abstract: This paper combines stochastic task duration modelling with sequence-dependent inventory cost estimation in a mixed-model sequencing framework solved by a steady-state genetic algorithm (GA). Chromosome representation encodes the production sequence of 180 units across 5 model types in a single shift. Fitness evaluation uses a Monte Carlo approximation with 50 replications per candidate sequence to estimate expected cycle time violations and WIP holding costs simultaneously. The GA is run with a population of 100, tournament selection of size 3, order crossover (OX), and swap mutation over 500 generations. Tests on 30 instances derived from real demand data of a diagnostic kit assembly line show that the GA consistently finds sequences within 3.2% of a lower bound obtained from a Lagrangian relaxation. Convergence behaviour across random seeds is stable; the coefficient of variation of final fitness values is below 2% across 20 independent runs.

title: A maintenance maturity assessment instrument for food and beverage plants: development and pilot testing
abstract: Maintenance maturity models provide a structured means of benchmarking organisational maintenance capability, but existing instruments were largely developed for discrete manufacturing and petrochemical contexts. This paper describes the development of a 52-item Likert-scale questionnaire instrument tailored to food and beverage plants, drawing on the asset management maturity framework of PAS 55 and the eight TPM pillars as theoretical foundations. Item generation followed a three-round Delphi process involving 14 maintenance engineers from plants across Serbia, Slovenia, and Hungary. The instrument was pilot-tested in 19 food and beverage plants; exploratory factor analysis extracted five factors—maintenance planning, workforce competency, equipment care, data management, and continuous improvement culture—explaining 63 % of total variance. Cronbach's alpha for the full scale was 0.88. Plants scored lowest on the data management and continuous improvement factors, suggesting these are systemic weak points in the regional sector. The instrument is proposed as a pre-assessment tool before launching a full TPM programme.

title: Iterative closest point variants for aligning sequential terrestrial LiDAR scans of wheat plots
abstract: Repeated terrestrial LiDAR scanning of cereal plots produces a time series of point clouds that must be accurately co-registered to extract growth information. This study evaluated five ICP-based alignment strategies on twelve wheat plots scanned every three days over a 30-day period from tillering to anthesis. Scans were acquired with a FARO Focus 3D at 6 mm point spacing at 10 m range. Ground control points placed at plot corners provided reference transformations. Mean alignment error across variants ranged from 4.2 mm to 18.7 mm at canopy height. A plane-to-point variant using normal estimation over 15-cm neighbourhoods achieved the lowest error and proved most stable when canopy density exceeded 80% projected cover. Runtime on a single GPU was under 90 seconds per scan pair at 4 million points. The findings set baseline alignment tolerances for organ-tracking pipelines in dense cereal stands.

title: Segmentation of individual wheat tillers from dense LiDAR point clouds using Euclidean clustering with adaptive radius
abstract: Isolating individual tillers from a full-plot scan is a prerequisite for organ-level growth tracking. This paper proposes an adaptive-radius Euclidean clustering approach in which the search radius scales linearly with estimated local point density, computed over a 5 cm voxel grid. Experiments were conducted on 48 scans of a winter wheat trial comprising six cultivars at two nitrogen levels. Ground points were removed with a height threshold tuned per scan, and the remaining cloud was clustered at five candidate radius schedules. Cluster count matched manual tiller counts (conducted on destructive samples from adjacent sub-plots) with a mean absolute error of 3.1 tillers per 0.25 m² quadrat across growth stages, dropping to 1.4 tillers at Zadoks stage 30–39. The method was faster than graph-cut alternatives by a factor of 7.3 and required no training data, making it suitable for iterative use across large time-series datasets.

title: Estimating leaf area index in barley from repeated mobile LiDAR scans: a comparison with destructive measurements
abstract: Leaf area index (LAI) is a critical canopy descriptor but destructive measurement is labour-intensive and terminal. This study estimated LAI in spring barley from mobile ground-robot LiDAR scans at weekly intervals across a full growing season on a 1.2 ha trial. A gap-fraction inversion approach was applied to vertical profiles of voxel occupancy at 2 cm resolution. Fourteen destructive LAI samples per week served as reference. Pearson r between scan-derived and destructive LAI was 0.91 across all growth stages, with root-mean-square error of 0.34 m² m⁻². Accuracy degraded at LAI above 5.5, attributed to self-occlusion in the lower canopy. Adjusting scan angle to ±20° from nadir reduced RMSE by 18% at high LAI. The robot platform traversed 12 plot rows in 8 minutes, allowing same-day repeat measurements unfeasible with stationary scanners.

title: Point cloud normals as features for classifying wheat organs at Zadoks stages 30 through 60
abstract: Distinguishing leaves, stems, and heads in LiDAR point clouds of dense wheat canopies is complicated by overlap and occlusion. This work tested whether local surface normals, combined with height and return intensity, could drive a random forest classifier to separate three organ classes across six Zadoks growth stages. Training data were 22,000 manually labelled points extracted from destructively sampled plants scanned in isolation, then projected onto in-field scans via nearest-neighbour transfer. The classifier achieved overall accuracy of 84.7% on held-out in-field scans, with head classification accuracy rising from 61% at Zadoks 37 to 96% at Zadoks 59, when heads became geometrically distinct. Leaf–stem confusion was the main error source (12.4% misclassification rate) in the lower canopy below 15 cm. Feature importance analysis confirmed that normal-vector inclination and inter-return spacing contributed more than intensity alone, informing sensor selection for future platforms.

title: A ground robot platform for sub-daily LiDAR phenotyping of cereal plots: mechanical design and field evaluation
abstract: This paper describes the mechanical and electronic design of a ground-based phenotyping robot, designated AgriTrack-1, built for sub-daily LiDAR scanning of cereal breeding plots. The platform uses a differential-drive chassis with 180 mm pneumatic wheels and a central rotating LiDAR mast adjustable between 0.3 m and 1.8 m. Navigation relies on RTK-GNSS with 2 cm horizontal accuracy, supplemented by wheel odometry. Field tests over two seasons covered 320 km of cumulative travel on clay-loam soil at water contents between 12% and 38%. Mean lateral deviation from programmed row centrelines was 3.1 cm. Crop contact per pass was negligible: post-season manual assessment found no measurable stem lodging attributable to robot traversal. Battery endurance was 4.2 hours per charge, sufficient to scan a 60-plot nursery twice per day. The platform has since been adopted as the primary data-collection tool for the group's time-series phenotyping work.

title: Tracking flag leaf elongation in field-grown wheat using time-series point cloud differencing
abstract: Flag leaf length is a heritable trait correlated with photosynthetic capacity but measuring it non-destructively in the field at high throughput remains difficult. This study applied a point cloud differencing method to 14 consecutive daily scans of 36 wheat genotypes from flag leaf emergence to full extension. After rigid co-registration, per-plant point clouds were subtracted between consecutive days, and the change volume attributed to the flag leaf was extracted by masking the apical region above the penultimate leaf insertion height. Derived elongation curves were compared against daily manual measurements on 10 tagged plants per genotype. Mean absolute error of daily increment was 3.8 mm. Time to full extension, estimated from logistic curve fitting, agreed with manual assessment to within 0.7 days on average. Heritability of scan-derived final flag leaf length was 0.74, comparable to 0.77 from manual data, confirming that the method captures genotypic signal.

title: Multiview registration of LiDAR and structured-light scans for resolving occlusion in dense wheat canopies
abstract: Single-pass LiDAR scanning leaves large occlusion zones in dense wheat canopies, particularly below the third leaf node. This study combined data from a mobile LiDAR scan along the row and two flanking structured-light cameras to reduce occluded volume. Registration used a joint target-based and surface-based approach, with residual error below 2.1 mm across 20 trial runs. Occluded volume per plant, measured as the fraction of convex hull not covered by any scan, fell from 41% for LiDAR-only to 18% for the fused configuration. Stem diameter estimates derived from the fused cloud agreed with calliper measurements (n = 240) with RMSE of 0.8 mm, compared to 2.3 mm for LiDAR alone. Processing time per 10-plant section was 4.7 minutes on a workstation with an NVIDIA RTX card. The workflow is described as a reusable module compatible with the AgriTrack-1 platform.

title: Growth rate heterogeneity among tillers of individual wheat plants quantified by daily LiDAR scanning
abstract: Within-plant tiller heterogeneity in growth rate is known from controlled experiments but has rarely been characterised under open-field conditions across many genotypes. Using the AgriTrack-1 robot and the tiller segmentation pipeline developed in earlier work, this study tracked 1,840 individual tillers across 92 plants from 14 genotypes over 21 consecutive days in the stem elongation phase. For each tiller, height velocity was computed from the daily co-registered point clouds. Coefficient of variation in height velocity among tillers of the same plant ranged from 9% to 34%, with significant genotype effect (p < 0.001) and a smaller but significant nitrogen-level effect (p = 0.02). Primary tillers grew 12% faster on average than secondary tillers during early elongation, converging by Zadoks 45. These measurements provide quantitative baselines for computational models of within-canopy resource competition and for selecting stable phenotyping targets in breeding.

title: 3D point cloud phenotyping pipelines for cereal breeding programmes: data formats, metadata standards, and integration with LIMS
abstract: As point cloud phenotyping moves from research prototypes toward routine use in breeding, the lack of agreed data formats and metadata standards hampers reproducibility and cross-site comparison. This book chapter reviews current practices across nine European groups conducting repeated LiDAR scanning of cereals, summarising file format choices, coordinate reference system conventions, per-scan metadata fields, and linkage strategies to laboratory information management systems. A recommended minimum metadata schema is proposed, covering scanner model, beam divergence, angular step width, temperature, wind speed at scan time, crop growth stage, and registration method. The chapter also discusses size implications: a season-long daily scan series of a 200-plot trial produces roughly 4.2 TB of raw data, and best-practice compression and thinning strategies are outlined. Two case studies from wheat breeding programmes in Serbia and Germany illustrate practical implementation.

title: Estimating internode length dynamics in barley from time-series 3D scans without destructive sampling
abstract: Internode length sequence is a determinant of lodging resistance and harvest index in barley, but non-destructive measurement in the field is constrained by canopy occlusion. This study applied a skeleton-extraction approach to time-series LiDAR point clouds of 48 barley plots scanned at 48-hour intervals from Zadoks 31 to Zadoks 69. Skeletons were extracted using a Laplacian contraction algorithm adapted for noisy outdoor scans, and internode boundaries were identified from local minima in the skeletal curvature profile. Length estimates were validated against 216 destructively sampled plants across three time points. Mean absolute error for the second and third internodes was 4.2 mm and 6.0 mm respectively; the first internode was poorly resolved below 8 cm canopy height, with error of 11.4 mm. Longitudinal growth curves fitted per plot showed plastochron intervals consistent with independently recorded thermal time accumulations, providing an indirect quality check.

title: Sensitivity of organ growth rate estimates to LiDAR point density and scan repeat interval in wheat
abstract: Choosing scan frequency and point density involves trade-offs between data volume, robot deployment time, and the temporal resolution of detected growth events. This paper presents a sensitivity analysis using a dense reference dataset (10 million points per plot, daily scans) progressively subsampled in both dimensions to simulate lower-cost acquisition scenarios. Organ growth rate error, measured as deviation from the reference daily increment, was below 5% for point densities above 150 points cm⁻² and scan intervals up to 48 hours during active elongation. At 72-hour intervals, error rose sharply during the rapid elongation window around Zadoks 39–45, reaching 18% for stem height velocity. Below 60 points cm⁻² the skeleton-based internode method became unstable regardless of interval. These thresholds translate to practical instrument and scheduling specifications for breeding organisations planning to adopt the methodology at scale.

title: Sensor fusion of ethylene and four-channel VOC signals for real-time ripeness index estimation in plums: a regression approach
abstract: This paper describes a sensor fusion methodology combining a single-channel electrochemical ethylene sensor with a four-channel MOS VOC array to estimate a continuous ripeness index (RI) for two plum cultivars ('Čačanska Lepotica' and 'Stanley') measured on-tree. Sensors were mounted on a purpose-built sampling hood attached to a collaborative robotic arm (6 DOF, 3 kg payload). Measurements were collected from 480 individual fruits across 8 orchard rows over the 2024 growing season. Ground-truth RI was defined as a weighted composite of destructive firmness (Magness–Taylor penetrometer), soluble solid content (Brix), and skin colour (CIE L*a*b* from image), calibrated against a trained human assessor panel. Multivariate linear regression, random forest, and a 3-layer feedforward neural network were compared; the neural network achieved the lowest cross-validated RMSE of 0.11 RI units on a 0–1 scale. Latency from sensor sampling to RI output was 41 s on the onboard Raspberry Pi CM4 compute module. The system correctly identified the optimal picking window (RI > 0.72) in 91% of trials, compared to 76% using ethylene alone. Sensor drift over the 6-week season was partially mitigated by weekly single-point recalibration.

title: Life-Cycle Inventory Data Quality for Cement Production in the Western Balkans: A Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: This study examined how data quality choices in life-cycle inventory (LCI) modelling affect the global warming potential (GWP) of Portland cement produced in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Primary gate-to-gate data were collected from three clinker kilns over a 12-month period, covering fuel consumption, raw material inputs, and direct CO2 emissions from calcination. Background datasets from ecoinvent 3.3 were adapted to reflect local electricity grid mixes using national energy balance statistics. Sensitivity analysis was performed by substituting background electricity, transport, and quarrying modules one at a time. Results showed that GWP varied by ±9% depending on the background electricity mix selected, and by ±4% when regional transport distances were adjusted within ±50 km. Calcination-related CO2 consistently accounted for 58–62% of the cradle-to-gate GWP regardless of background assumptions. The findings indicate that primary data collection at the kiln level is more influential than background dataset choice for this product category, and provide guidance for EPD practitioners working in data-scarce regional contexts.

title: Cradle-to-Gate Environmental Profile of Autoclaved Aerated Concrete Blocks Produced in Vojvodina
abstract: Autoclaved aerated concrete (AAC) is widely used for residential construction in northern Serbia, yet no region-specific life-cycle data existed prior to this work. Primary inventory data were collected at a single AAC manufacturing plant in Vojvodina over one production year, covering quartz sand quarrying, quicklime calcination, aluminium powder addition, autoclave curing energy, and wastewater generation. The system boundary followed EN 15804:2012 modules A1–A3. Nine impact categories were calculated using the CML-IA characterisation method, with GWP100 as the main indicator. Results gave a GWP of 312 kg CO2-eq per tonne of product, with lime production contributing 47% and autoclave steam generation 31%. Acidification and eutrophication potentials were dominated by SO2 and NOx emissions from the on-site gas boiler. A mass allocation approach was applied for co-produced slurry recycled back into the process; allocation sensitivity was tested against system expansion. The study provides a dataset suitable for future EPD registration with a Serbian certification body.

title: System Boundary Definition in EN 15804-Compliant EPDs: A Comparative Review of 42 Declarations for Structural Concrete Products
abstract: Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) for structural concrete prepared under EN 15804 vary substantially in how cradle-to-gate system boundaries are drawn, which limits the comparability of declared values across manufacturers and countries. This paper reviewed 42 EPDs for ready-mix concrete and precast concrete elements published between 2012 and 2017 by programme operators in Germany, Sweden, France, and Serbia. For each EPD, the treatment of recycled aggregate input, waste concrete slurry, on-site diesel machinery, and co-product allocation was recorded and classified. Results showed that 61% of EPDs excluded on-site diesel machinery, 45% applied cut-off rules for minor additives without documentation, and only 29% reported a sensitivity analysis. Serbian declarations showed the highest rate of omission for transport sub-modules. A checklist of 14 critical system boundary decisions is proposed to support EPD verifiers and LCA practitioners in ensuring consistent declarations. The checklist is tested against three new declarations prepared in the course of this study.

title: Life-Cycle Assessment of Fired Clay Brick: Comparison of Tunnel Kiln and Hoffman Kiln Production Routes
abstract: Fired clay brick remains a dominant walling material in Serbian residential construction, yet production technology varies considerably between modern tunnel kilns and older Hoffman kilns still in operation. Primary data were collected from two brick factories in the Vojvodina region, one using a natural-gas-fired tunnel kiln and one using a coal-fired Hoffman kiln. The functional unit was defined as one tonne of fired clay brick meeting Serbian standard SRPS B.D1.010. Inventory data covered clay extraction, drying, firing, packaging, and internal transport. The EN 15804 module A1–A3 boundary was applied. GWP for the tunnel kiln route was 178 kg CO2-eq per tonne and for the Hoffman kiln 241 kg CO2-eq per tonne, a 35% difference driven by coal combustion emissions and lower thermal efficiency. Particulate matter formation was substantially higher for the Hoffman kiln due to uncontrolled stack emissions. The analysis supports prioritisation of kiln modernisation programmes as a climate and air quality measure in the regional brick industry.

title: Environmental Impact Quantification for a Prefabricated Timber Frame Panel System: Modules A1–A5
abstract: Cross-laminated timber and prefabricated timber frame panels have gained market share in Serbian residential construction since 2015, but LCA data for locally produced systems remain limited. This study quantified nine EN 15804 impact categories for a prefabricated timber frame wall panel manufactured in the Šumadija region, extending the system boundary from A1 (raw material supply) through A5 (installation on site) to enable comparison with masonry alternatives. Primary inventory data were collected over six months of panel production, including roundwood sourcing from certified forestry operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, kiln drying, finger-jointing, oriented strand board sheathing, and transport to a reference construction site in Novi Sad. Carbon storage in the wood fraction was reported separately following EN 15804:2019+A2. The GWP excluding biogenic carbon was 28.6 kg CO2-eq per square metre of finished wall at 200 mm thickness, compared to 87.4 kg CO2-eq/m² for an equivalent AAC block wall assessed using the same boundary in a companion study. Biogenic carbon uptake offset 31.2 kg CO2-eq/m² when included.

title: Quantifying the Contribution of Transport Logistics to Cradle-to-Gate GWP in Precast Concrete Element Manufacturing: A Case Study from Northern Serbia
abstract: Transport of raw materials to precast concrete factories is frequently treated as a minor contributor to cradle-to-gate GWP in EPD studies, with default distances often assumed rather than measured. This study collected primary transport data from a precast structural element manufacturer in Novi Sad over a 12-month period, covering 23 input materials delivered by road freight. Actual tonne-kilometre values were compared against EN 15804 default assumptions and the assumptions made in three published EPDs for comparable precast elements. Actual transport contributed 6.8% of total GWP, compared to 2.1–3.4% in the published EPDs, a discrepancy attributable to longer haul distances for aggregates and admixtures specific to the Pannonian Plain geography. The sensitivity of GWP, acidification potential, and fine particulate matter formation to transport distance was mapped across a ±100 km range. Results indicate that the EN 15804 default transport scenario underestimates transport-related GWP for inland Central and Southeast European factory locations and that site-specific transport data collection is warranted for manufacturers seeking verified EPDs.

title: Spatial distribution of plum orchards in Srem between 1890 and 1941 based on Austro-Hungarian cadastral records
abstract: This study reconstructs the extent and spatial pattern of plum orchard plots in the Srem district using 47 cadastral parcel sheets from the Austro-Hungarian land survey of 1896–1912, supplemented by corrective data from the first Yugoslav cadastral revision of 1928–1932. Sheets were digitised at 600 dpi and georeferenced to the ETRS89/UTM zone 34N coordinate system using tie points extracted from surviving trigonometric stations. A total of 6,840 parcels classified as 'voćnjak' or 'šljivik' were digitised and their areas computed. Results show a maximum orchard coverage of approximately 18,400 hectares in the study region around 1910, with pronounced clustering in a band 12–18 km east of the Fruška Gora ridge. Comparison with the 1932 revision indicates a net loss of roughly 2,100 hectares attributable to phylloxera-related land abandonment and conversion to arable. The dataset is made available as a shapefile archive. Methodological challenges related to coordinate drift in cadastral originals and the ambiguity of parcel classification terminology are discussed in detail.

title: Decline of apricot cultivation zones in Bačka: evidence from sequential aerial photography, 1953–1980
abstract: Yugoslav military and civilian aerial survey missions produced a largely unstudied sequence of panchromatic aerial photographs covering Bačka at scales ranging from 1:10,000 to 1:25,000 between 1953 and 1980. This paper uses 214 flight strips from three survey epochs (1953, 1967, 1979) to map the spatial contraction of apricot cultivation in 22 cadastral municipalities. Photographs were scanned and subjected to analogue stereophotogrammetric interpretation using a Zeiss stereoscope before digital vectorisation. Orchard polygons were distinguished from arable and vineyard land by canopy texture, row spacing signatures, and shadow geometry. The total mapped apricot area declined from 9,340 hectares in 1953 to 4,810 hectares in 1979, a reduction of 48.5 percent. Largest absolute losses occurred in municipalities adjacent to newly established socialist cooperative farms, where orchard parcels were frequently amalgamated into field crops. The temporal sequence also reveals a northward contraction of the cultivation zone consistent with documented cold-air pooling patterns in the lower Bačka plain.

title: Orchard mosaics as components of traditional agricultural landscapes in central Vojvodina: a comparative landscape metrics approach
abstract: Traditional orchard parcels in Vojvodina were rarely monospecific; smallholder plots typically contained mixtures of plum, apricot, quince, and pear trees arranged in irregular patterns reflecting family subsistence strategies rather than commercial logic. This paper applies landscape metrics (patch density, mean shape index, aggregation index) to digitised orchard polygons from 1930s cadastral sheets covering four contrasting subregions of central Vojvodina: the Titel loess plateau, the Deliblato sandy terrain, the Tisa riverside strip, and the Fruška Gora foothill zone. The analysis uses FRAGSTATS 4.2 applied to rasterised polygon layers at 5-metre resolution. Results show significantly higher shape complexity and lower aggregation in foothill orchards compared to riverside and plateau zones, interpreted as reflecting topographic constraints on parcel geometry. Patch density across the four subregions ranged from 1.8 to 7.4 patches per 100 hectares. The paper argues that landscape metrics, typically applied to present-day satellite imagery, can be meaningfully extended to historical cartographic sources provided georeferencing accuracy is systematically reported.

title: Documentation of lost local pear and quince cultivar names in Vojvodina notarial records, 1880–1945
abstract: Cadastral and aerial photographic sources record orchard extent but not species or cultivar composition. This paper explores an alternative primary source: notarial inheritance inventories and estate valuations deposited in the Archive of Vojvodina, which occasionally itemised orchard contents by locally used cultivar names. A systematic search of 1,240 notarial files from 18 municipalities yielded 312 documents containing orchard itemisations. From these, 67 distinct vernacular pear cultivar names and 19 quince names were extracted. Cross-referencing with surviving pomological literature of the interwar period (principally the catalogues of Aleksandar Berić and Stanko Novaković, published 1924–1938) allows tentative identification of 38 of the pear names with described morphotypes. The remaining 29 names appear to correspond to locally selected material not captured in published catalogues, suggesting a higher level of on-farm diversity than previously acknowledged in regional pomological histories. The paper does not claim cultivar survival; it reconstructs the names as evidence of former diversity.

title: Reconstructing vineyard and orchard boundaries in the Fruška Gora piedmont using the 1869 Franciscan Cadastre and 1960s aerial surveys
abstract: The Franciscan Cadastre of 1869, prepared under Austro-Hungarian administrative authority, provides one of the earliest large-scale cartographic records of land use in the Fruška Gora piedmont. This conference paper presents interim results from an ongoing georeferencing project covering 31 cadastral sheets at original scale 1:2,880. Sheets were photographed under controlled lighting, rectified using affine and thin-plate spline transformations, and co-registered with 1967 aerial survey mosaics and contemporary orthophotos derived from drone surveys conducted in 2018. Preliminary comparison of vineyard and orchard boundaries across the three epochs reveals that approximately 34 percent of 1869 orchard parcels remained in orchard use in 1967, while only 11 percent retain orchard or vineyard use today. Parcel boundary persistence is highest on south-facing slopes between 160 and 260 metres elevation. The paper focuses on methodological issues of multi-epoch co-registration at different scales and discusses the propagation of georeferencing uncertainty into area-change estimates.

title: Orchard landscapes of Vojvodina: historical extent, spatial patterns, and twentieth-century transformation
abstract: This book chapter synthesises findings from a decade of cadastral and aerial photographic research into the historical orchard landscapes of Vojvodina. It is structured around three periods: the late Austro-Hungarian cadastral era (1880–1918), the interwar Yugoslav period (1919–1941), and the socialist collectivisation period (1945–1980). Quantitative estimates of orchard area are assembled for each period from digitised sources covering approximately 60 percent of the province's cadastral municipalities. The chapter presents maps of orchard distribution at regional scale for each period, discusses the principal drivers of change (phylloxera and frost damage, land reform policies, cooperative farm expansion, urban growth), and situates Vojvodina trends within broader Danubian basin comparisons drawing on published data from Hungary and Romania. A concluding section addresses limitations of cadastral data for agroecological reconstruction, including the lag between actual land-use change and cadastral record update, estimated at four to twelve years in the interwar period based on cross-referencing with aerial sources.

title: Persistence of field boundary and orchard parcel structures across administrative reorganisations in Vojvodina, 1948–1971
abstract: Yugoslav administrative reorganisation reduced the number of cadastral municipalities in Vojvodina by consolidation in three distinct waves (1948, 1955, and 1963), creating opportunities to test whether administrative boundary changes affected the physical persistence of orchard parcel structures on the ground. This paper uses matched pairs of aerial photographs taken before and after each reorganisation event for 14 selected municipalities, covering an area of approximately 340 square kilometres. Orchard polygon boundaries were digitised from both epochs and overlaid to compute a boundary persistence index defined as the proportion of 1948 boundary length surviving within a 10-metre tolerance buffer in the post-reorganisation epoch. Mean persistence index was 0.71 for the 1948–1955 transition and 0.54 for the 1955–1971 interval, indicating that administrative consolidation accelerated physical landscape change in the second period coinciding with mechanisation of cooperative agriculture. Parcels smaller than 0.15 hectares showed disproportionately low persistence across all transition periods.

title: Chilling models compared: Dynamic Model vs. Chilling Hours in predicting sweet cherry bud burst in the northern Pannonian Basin
abstract: The choice of chilling model affects the accuracy of dormancy predictions and crop management decisions. We compared the predictive performance of the Dynamic Model (chill portions), the Chilling Hours Model (hours below 7.2°C), and the Utah Model for sweet cherry bud burst at four Vojvodina locations over 15 seasons (2009–2024). Observed bud burst dates for 'Hedelfingen', 'Regina', and 'Kordia' were regressed against accumulated chilling from each model using linear models with location and cultivar as factors. The Dynamic Model produced the lowest root mean square error (RMSE = 3.2 days) compared with the Chilling Hours Model (RMSE = 5.8 days) and the Utah Model (RMSE = 4.9 days). Model performance diverged most in the seven seasons that recorded more than five days above 15°C during December, when negative chilling hour contributions in the Utah Model introduced instability. The Dynamic Model is recommended for operational use in Vojvodina agrometeorological services.

title: Rootstock influence on graft-union anatomy and mineral element concentrations at the graft interface in apple
abstract: The graft union is a potential bottleneck for mineral element translocation between rootstock and scion, yet anatomical and chemical characterisation of this zone is rarely combined in apple studies. Graft-union segments from five rootstock–scion combinations ('Golden Delicious Reinders' on M.9, M.27, MM.111, Geneva 41, and NS-D2) were collected at two years after grafting and prepared for light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) to map Ca, K, and Mg distribution. Cross-sections revealed incomplete vascular continuity in M.27 unions, with a discontinuous cambial zone in 14 of 30 samples. EDX mapping showed Ca accumulation at parenchymatous graft interface tissue in M.27 and Geneva 41, suggesting restricted apoplastic Ca flow. Correlative field data from the same trial confirmed lower fruit Ca in M.27 trees. The findings point to anatomical filtering as a mechanism partly responsible for rootstock-dependent mineral partitioning.

title: Aromatic Profile of Neoplanta White Wine Produced by Spontaneous Fermentation: A Comparison with Commercial Yeast Inoculation
abstract: This study compared the volatile composition of wines produced from the autochthonous Serbian white variety Neoplanta (Vitis vinifera L.) under spontaneous fermentation versus inoculation with two commercial Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains. Grapes were harvested from a single vineyard in the Fruška Gora subregion in two consecutive vintages (2013 and 2014). Volatile compounds were extracted by solid-phase microextraction and analysed by GC-MS; 54 individual compounds were identified and quantified across the three treatments. Spontaneously fermented wines showed significantly higher concentrations of ethyl esters associated with floral and fruity descriptors, including ethyl hexanoate (mean 312 µg/L) and ethyl octanoate (mean 287 µg/L), while commercial yeast wines exhibited elevated higher alcohol content. A trained panel of nine assessors evaluated aroma intensity, freshness, and overall quality using a structured 10-point scale. Spontaneous fermentation wines received higher median scores for complexity (7.4 vs. 6.1) across both vintages. Vintage had a significant effect on total ester content (p < 0.05), but treatment effects were consistent across years.

title: Influence of Rectangular Coil Aspect Ratio on Coupling Coefficient in Static Inductive Power Transfer Systems
abstract: This paper investigates how the aspect ratio of rectangular transmitter and receiver coils affects the coupling coefficient in a static inductive power transfer (IPT) configuration intended for passenger electric vehicles. A parametric sweep of length-to-width ratios ranging from 1:1 to 3:1 was performed using finite element method (FEM) simulations in ANSYS Maxwell, with air-gap distances set at 100 mm, 150 mm, and 200 mm. Fifteen coil geometry combinations were fabricated using Litz wire and tested on a bench setup with a Keysight E4990A impedance analyser. Results show that a 2:1 aspect ratio consistently achieves coupling coefficients 8–12% higher than square coils at a 150 mm gap and zero lateral offset. The findings provide quantitative geometry guidance for early-stage IPT coupler design without resorting to full system optimisation at the outset. Ferrite shielding configurations were kept constant across all prototypes to isolate geometry effects.

title: Lateral Misalignment Effects on Transfer Efficiency in a DD-Coil Wireless Charging Pad
abstract: The double-D (DD) coil topology is widely studied for its reduced sensitivity to lateral misalignment compared to circular pads, but published efficiency data under combined lateral and angular misalignment remain sparse for operating frequencies near 85 kHz. This work presents measured and simulated efficiency curves for a DD transmitter pad (300 mm × 200 mm) paired with a DD receiver of identical size over a 130 mm air gap. Lateral offsets of 0–120 mm in both the x and y directions were tested in 20 mm increments, and angular rotations of 0°, 15°, and 30° were superimposed. A series–series resonant compensation topology was used throughout. Measured efficiency dropped from 91.3% at zero offset to 74.6% at 100 mm lateral offset with no angular tilt, and to 61.2% under combined 80 mm offset and 30° rotation. FEM predictions agreed with measurements within 2.5 percentage points across all configurations. The data set is made available as supplementary material.

title: Thermal Behaviour of Ferrite Core Assemblies Under Repeated Short-Duration Coupling Events Simulating Dynamic Charging
abstract: During dynamic wireless charging, a stationary road-embedded transmitter coil is energised for only the brief interval a vehicle passes over it. This paper examines the cumulative thermal loading on ferrite core assemblies in a transmitter pad subjected to repeated coupling pulses of 0.8 s duration at a 20% duty cycle, representative of a low-speed urban zone at 10 km/h with 5 m pad spacing. Three ferrite grades (N87, N95, PC90) were tested in a climate chamber at ambient temperatures of 20 °C and 40 °C. Surface temperatures were logged via embedded thermocouples and compared against analytical loss estimates derived from Steinmetz parameters. After 90 minutes of continuous operation, N87 assemblies reached 78 °C at 40 °C ambient, while PC90 remained below 61 °C under the same conditions. Core loss measurements at 85 kHz and 70 mT flux density are tabulated. The results inform material selection criteria for road-embedded transmitter pads in warm-climate deployments.

title: Segmented Transmitter Track Architecture for Low-Speed Dynamic EV Wireless Charging: Segment Length Trade-offs
abstract: In a segmented dynamic wireless charging track, individual transmitter pads are switched on only when a vehicle receiver is directly above them, reducing reactive power losses and electromagnetic emissions during idle intervals. This paper analyses how transmitter segment length affects three performance metrics—peak coupling coefficient, transition smoothness between segments, and total track-switching frequency—for a vehicle travelling at speeds between 5 and 20 km/h. A 6 m laboratory track with six interchangeable segment lengths (0.3 m, 0.5 m, 0.7 m, 1.0 m, 1.2 m, and 1.5 m) was constructed. Receiver position was detected using a low-latency Hall-effect array. Measured power delivery continuity, defined as time fraction above 90% of rated power, peaked at 94.7% for 0.7 m segments at 10 km/h. Shorter segments improved continuity at very low speeds but imposed higher switching frequencies on the inverter stage. Empirical transition overlap curves are provided as design charts.

title: Position Estimation Accuracy Requirements for Reliable Segment Switching in a 10 km/h Dynamic Charging Corridor
abstract: Reliable segment switching in a dynamic wireless charging lane requires accurate real-time knowledge of the receiver coil position relative to the transmitter grid. This paper quantifies how position estimation error translates into power delivery loss and unnecessary switching events for vehicle speeds in the 5–15 km/h range. Three receiver localisation methods were implemented on the same experimental track: a Hall-effect array, an ultrasonic time-of-flight system, and a model-based estimator using measured coupling coefficient gradient. Position estimation errors of 10 mm, 30 mm, and 60 mm were emulated by introducing calibrated delays. Results show that errors below 25 mm cause less than 3% reduction in energy delivery per pass, while 60 mm errors increase spurious switching events by a factor of 2.8. The Hall-effect array achieved 18 mm RMS error under laboratory conditions; the coupling-based estimator achieved 22 mm RMS without additional sensing hardware, making it attractive for retrofit installations.
