title: Comparative Evaluation of Bipolar and DDQ Receiver Pads for Combined Lateral and Longitudinal Misalignment in Urban Low-Speed Dynamic Charging
abstract: Urban low-speed electric vehicles, including campus shuttles and automated guided vehicles, operate on paths with both lateral and longitudinal positional variance relative to road-embedded transmitter tracks. This paper compares bipolar and DDQ receiver pad topologies across a two-dimensional misalignment grid covering ±120 mm laterally and ±200 mm longitudinally, measured at an 80 mm air gap and 85 kHz operating frequency. Twelve prototype receivers were fabricated and tested over a single-layer transmitter track 4.8 m long. Transfer efficiency and induced voltage uniformity are reported on a 20 mm grid mesh. The DDQ topology delivered higher mean efficiency (88.1% versus 84.6%) but exhibited localised efficiency dips near pad corners under diagonal misalignment combinations. Bipolar pads showed more uniform spatial performance. Normalised coupling maps are provided as MATLAB data files. The results are intended to support pad topology selection at the system design stage for guided urban vehicles.

title: A Pareto-Based Genetic Algorithm for Scheduling on Heterogeneous Processor Grids
abstract: This paper addresses static task scheduling on heterogeneous multiprocessor systems using a Pareto-based genetic algorithm that simultaneously minimises makespan and energy consumption. The representation encodes task-to-processor assignments as integer strings; crossover and mutation operators are tailored to preserve precedence constraints. Experiments were conducted on a benchmark suite of 120 synthetic task graphs with 50–500 nodes and on two real signal-processing workflows extracted from embedded automotive applications. The proposed algorithm consistently identifies hypervolume-competitive Pareto front approximations compared to NSGA-II and a weighted-sum baseline across all tested graph sizes. On the largest instances the average hypervolume improvement over NSGA-II reached 4.8 percent with comparable wall-clock time. The paper also analyses sensitivity to population size and crossover rate, identifying stable configurations for practical deployment. Results suggest the approach scales reasonably up to 500-node graphs without excessive computational overhead.

title: Decomposition-Based Multi-Objective Optimisation for Combinatorial Problems with Variable Interaction
abstract: MOEA/D and its variants decompose a multi-objective problem into a set of scalar subproblems solved cooperatively. This work investigates how variable interaction structure affects the performance of decomposition-based algorithms on three classes of combinatorial problems: the bi-objective knapsack, the graph colouring extension, and a routing variant. Interaction graphs are estimated using a fitness landscape analysis over 40 independently generated instances per class. The study shows that neighbourhood sizes in MOEA/D should be adapted to the interaction density: sparse interaction graphs benefit from small neighbourhoods, while dense graphs require larger ones. A lightweight adaptive neighbourhood scheme is proposed and validated against fixed-neighbourhood MOEA/D and NSGA-III on all instance classes. The adaptive version reduces the spread metric by an average of 6.1 percent on dense-interaction instances. The paper provides practical guidance for practitioners selecting decomposition parameters without prior knowledge of instance structure.

title: Surrogate Models in Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimisation: A Comparative Study on Expensive Black-Box Functions
abstract: When objective evaluations are computationally expensive, surrogate models are commonly embedded within the evolutionary loop to reduce the number of exact evaluations required. This study compares Gaussian process regression, radial basis function networks, and polynomial response surfaces as surrogates within an NSGA-II framework on six standard multi-objective test functions (DTLZ1–DTLZ6) scaled to expensive regimes by artificially enforcing an evaluation budget of 500 calls. Accuracy of the Pareto front approximation is measured via hypervolume, generational distance, and spread. Results show that Gaussian process surrogates outperform the others on unimodal functions but degrade on multi-modal landscapes where radial basis functions prove more robust. A simple switching criterion based on estimated model error is tested and yields consistent improvements of 3–9 percent in hypervolume across all six functions. The paper discusses practical criteria for surrogate selection in real engineering design contexts.

title: Three-Objective Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search Targeting ARM Cortex-M Microcontrollers
abstract: Deploying neural networks on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers requires simultaneous control of model accuracy, flash memory footprint, and peak RAM usage during inference. This paper presents a three-objective evolutionary NAS framework that treats all three quantities as objectives to be minimised subject to a classification accuracy floor. The search space consists of stacked blocks parameterised by filter counts, kernel sizes, and depthwise-separable vs. standard convolution choices. NSGA-III drives the search over 300 generations with a population of 80 individuals; each candidate is evaluated on the STM32F746 board using a subset of the Kvasir-v1 gastrointestinal image dataset (8 classes, 4000 images) resized to 48×48. The Pareto front reveals a family of models fitting within 256 KB flash and 64 KB RAM with top-1 accuracy between 78.3 and 84.1 percent. The most accurate model within the memory budget outperforms a hand-tuned MobileNet-v1 configuration by 2.4 percentage points in this setting.

title: Benchmarking Multi-Objective NAS Algorithms on a Unified Tabular Search Space
abstract: Reproducible comparison of neural architecture search algorithms is hampered by inconsistent search spaces, training protocols, and hardware targets. This paper introduces a tabular benchmark—MONAS-Tab—covering 18 650 architectures from a fixed cell-based space evaluated on three datasets (CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, and a 10-class subset of TINYML-Sound) with pre-recorded accuracy, parameter count, multiply-accumulate operations, and inference latency on two embedded targets. Using MONAS-Tab, five multi-objective search strategies are compared: NSGA-II, NSGA-III, MOEA/D, random search with Pareto filtering, and a Bayesian multi-objective baseline. Evaluation uses hypervolume, Pareto front coverage, and rank correlation between predicted and true objectives. Random search with Pareto filtering performs surprisingly competitively on small budgets (under 200 evaluations), while NSGA-II leads at larger budgets. The dataset and evaluation code are released publicly to encourage standardised comparison.

title: Warm-Starting Evolutionary NAS with Transfer of Pareto Front Approximations across Datasets
abstract: Evolutionary neural architecture search restarts from scratch for each new dataset, discarding knowledge accumulated in earlier runs. This paper investigates warm-starting: the Pareto front approximation obtained on a source dataset is used to initialise the population for a target dataset search, rather than sampling uniformly from the search space. Transferability is measured as the reduction in evaluations needed to reach a target hypervolume value on CIFAR-100 and three medical imaging datasets when warm-starting from CIFAR-10 solutions. Across all target datasets, warm-starting reduces the evaluation budget by 31–47 percent relative to cold-start NSGA-II at equivalent Pareto front quality. Performance degrades when source and target datasets are semantically distant, as measured by a simple feature distribution divergence metric. The paper provides a practical selection criterion for when transfer is likely to be beneficial, validated on eight source–target dataset pairs.

title: Mixed-Precision Quantisation as an Objective in Multi-Objective Neural Architecture Search
abstract: Mixed-precision quantisation assigns different bit-widths to different layers of a neural network, offering finer control over the accuracy–compression trade-off than uniform quantisation. This work incorporates bit-width assignment directly into the NAS genotype, extending the search space to include per-layer precision choices from {4, 6, 8} bits alongside architectural decisions. A four-objective evolutionary search minimises validation error, model size in bytes, inference latency on a Cortex-M55 target, and a proxy for energy consumption based on operation counts weighted by bit-width. The search is conducted over ResNet-style and plain convolutional cells on the HAR-70+ activity recognition dataset. Pareto-optimal solutions achieve up to 3.1× size reduction compared to 8-bit uniform quantisation at equivalent accuracy. The paper analyses which layers are most frequently assigned lower precision across Pareto-optimal solutions, identifying a consistent pattern of reduced precision in early spatial downsampling layers.

title: FPGA Prototyping of NAS-Derived Architectures: From Pareto Front to Bitstream
abstract: Translating multi-objective NAS results into running FPGA implementations requires hardware-aware evaluation during the search and a reliable post-search implementation flow. This paper presents an end-to-end workflow connecting an NSGA-II NAS backend to a high-level synthesis (HLS) toolchain targeting a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA. Latency and resource utilisation (LUT, BRAM, DSP) estimates from an HLS profiling run are fed back into the NAS loop as surrogate objective values, replacing slower board-level measurements. Three image classification tasks with 96×96 input resolution are used as benchmarks. The surrogate estimates correlate with measured values at r=0.91 for latency and r=0.87 for LUT count, validating their use in the search. The best NAS-derived architecture on the object detection proxy task achieves 19 ms inference latency at 93.4 percent accuracy, compared to 31 ms for a manually designed reference. The workflow is described in sufficient detail to replicate on comparable mid-range FPGAs.

title: Constraint Handling in Multi-Objective NAS: Penalty vs. Repair vs. Separation
abstract: Enforcing resource constraints—memory, latency, energy—during neural architecture search can be handled by adding penalty terms to objectives, repairing infeasible candidates to the nearest feasible point, or maintaining a separate infeasible population. This study provides a controlled comparison of these three strategies within a common NSGA-II framework across four constraint tightness levels on NAS-Bench-201. Metrics include final hypervolume of the feasible Pareto front, the rate of constraint violations in the final population, and computational overhead. Repair strategies based on greedy channel reduction consistently produce the most constraint-feasible Pareto fronts under tight budgets, but incur 15–20 percent additional computation per generation. Penalty-based approaches are fastest but produce 12–34 percent infeasible solutions at the tightest constraint levels. Separation methods balance these extremes. Practical recommendations are drawn for three deployment contexts: strict real-time, best-effort, and offline post-hoc filtering.

title: Multi-Objective NAS for Anomaly Detection on Industrial Sensor Streams under Memory Constraints
abstract: Anomaly detection on raw sensor data from industrial machinery is increasingly expected to run on the same low-power embedded controllers that manage the machinery itself. This paper applies multi-objective evolutionary NAS to design recurrent and convolutional-recurrent architectures for time-series anomaly detection within a 128 KB RAM and 512 KB flash budget on an ARM Cortex-M33 target. The search optimises three objectives: reconstruction error on nominal data, RAM usage during inference, and flash footprint. Training and evaluation use a 14-channel vibration dataset collected from rotating machinery in a manufacturing context, comprising 800 hours of nominal operation and 120 annotated fault events across five fault types. The best Pareto solution achieves an F1 score of 0.883 on the held-out fault set while fitting within the memory budget, compared to 0.901 for an unconstrained LSTM baseline that exceeds the budget by a factor of 6. The search also surfaces several compact purely convolutional architectures competitive with recurrent solutions.

title: Mapping Hansen solubility spheres for common pharmaceutical intermediates using a turbidimetric microplate method
abstract: Accurate determination of Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) for solid solutes typically requires testing 20–40 solvents individually, which is time-consuming and generates significant solvent waste. This study adapted a 96-well microplate turbidimetric protocol to measure partial miscibility of six pharmaceutical intermediates—including two sulfonamide precursors and three heterocyclic amines—against a library of 48 solvents, completing each HSP sphere in under 8 hours of bench time. Experimental Ra values were compared with estimates from the HSPiP group-contribution method; mean absolute deviations ranged from 0.4 to 1.1 MPa^0.5, with the largest discrepancy observed for a hydroxyl-dense substrate. Solvent consumption per data point was reduced by approximately 85% relative to conventional vial methods. The resulting spheres correctly predicted solubility class in an independent validation set of 12 solvents with 83% accuracy. The microplate approach is directly transferable to early-phase process chemistry workflows where material availability is constrained.

title: Solvent selection for liquid–liquid extraction of flavonoids from Sambucus nigra flowers: a Hansen parameter approach
abstract: Elderflower extracts are commercially relevant sources of rutin and quercetin glycosides, but existing extraction protocols rely heavily on methanol and ethyl acetate, both of which carry regulatory and safety concerns for food applications. This work applied Hansen solubility parameter (HSP) analysis to identify alternative extraction solvents with Ra ≤ 4 MPa^0.5 relative to the target flavonoid cluster. Ethyl lactate, dimethyl isosorbide, and a 70:30 v/v glycerol/water mixture were identified as candidates. Batch extraction yields at 40 °C were compared against a methanol reference: ethyl lactate achieved 91% of the reference rutin yield, while dimethyl isosorbide co-extracted 35% fewer chlorophyll pigments, simplifying downstream purification. The E-factor for the ethyl lactate route was 18, compared with 29 for the methanol route when accounting for solvent recovery losses. Preliminary toxicity screening using ECOSAR indicated lower aquatic hazard for all three alternatives.

title: Life-cycle solvent assessment for Fischer indole synthesis: comparing toluene, 2-methyltetrahydrofuran, and cyclopentyl methyl ether
abstract: Fischer indole synthesis remains a core reaction in the manufacture of pharmaceutical actives and agrochemical intermediates, and toluene is the dominant industrial solvent despite its classification as a substance of very high concern under REACH. This study compared toluene with 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF) and cyclopentyl methyl ether (CPME) across three metrics: reaction yield and selectivity at preparative scale (10 mmol), process mass intensity (PMI), and a condensed life-cycle assessment covering solvent production, use, and end-of-life. Yields were 87%, 84%, and 82% respectively; PMI values were 32, 28, and 31. The LCA showed that 2-MeTHF, when sourced from bio-based furfural, achieved a 41% reduction in cumulative energy demand relative to toluene, with a 27% reduction in the ReCiPe Midpoint human toxicity score. CPME offered comparable environmental performance with superior chemical stability under acidic reaction conditions. Both alternatives are considered viable drop-in replacements for this reaction class.

title: Process redesign of a batch recrystallisation step for an amine-containing active using deep eutectic solvent–antisolvent systems
abstract: A batch recrystallisation step in the synthesis of a secondary amine pharmaceutical active relied on a 4:1 isopropanol/water mixture that generated approximately 120 L of solvent waste per kilogram of product at pilot scale. Deep eutectic solvents (DES) composed of choline chloride and urea (1:2 molar ratio) or choline chloride and oxalic acid (1:1 molar ratio) were evaluated as primary solvents, with water as antisolvent. Solubility of the active in both DES systems was measured by gravimetry at 20, 40, and 60 °C; the choline chloride/urea system gave a solubility of 112 mg/mL at 60 °C, compared to 98 mg/mL in the isopropanol/water reference at the same temperature. Crystal habit was characterised by optical microscopy and PXRD; the DES route yielded equidimensional crystals with a smaller aspect ratio, improving filtration throughput by 22%. Solvent waste per kilogram of product was reduced to 38 L using aqueous DES recycle.

abstract: Phthalate plasticisers are being phased out of food-contact polymer applications across the European Union, creating demand for bio-based alternatives produced through greener routes. This study benchmarked four synthetic pathways to 1,4-butanediol diisononanoate from succinic acid and isononanol: Fischer esterification with sulfuric acid, enzymatic catalysis with a commercial lipase immobilised on silica, heteropolyacid catalysis, and solvent-free mechanochemical activation. Reaction conversion, yield, and selectivity were measured in parallel 50 mL reactors. Process mass intensity ranged from 8.4 (solvent-free mechanochemical) to 47.3 (Fischer/toluene). E-factors, including aqueous workup waste, followed the same order. Enzyme stability under repeated use was tracked over ten batch cycles; lipase activity dropped to 68% of initial after cycle 8. A simplified economic analysis indicated that mechanochemical and enzymatic routes have comparable reagent costs but different capital and maintenance profiles, suggesting context-dependent selection criteria for industrial implementation.

title: Prediction of binary solvent mixture HSP coordinates from pure-component parameters: validation against 120 experimental miscibility points
abstract: Binary solvent blends are routinely used to fine-tune solvation power in synthesis and extraction, yet their composite HSP coordinates are most often estimated by volume-fraction-weighted averaging of pure-component values—an approach that neglects preferential solvation and specific interactions. This study compiled 120 experimental solubility binary outcomes for three solid model compounds (a flavone, a sulfonamide, and a dicarboxylic acid) across 40 binary solvent pairs. Four estimation models were compared: volume-fraction averaging, mole-fraction averaging, the Flory–Huggins lattice correction, and an empirical correction factor fitted to a 60-point training subset. On the 60-point test set, the Flory–Huggins model achieved the lowest misclassification rate (11%), compared with 21% for simple volume-fraction averaging. The fitted empirical correction performed well (13% error) but required a solute-specific parameter. Practical lookup tables of corrected HSP coordinates are provided for 15 binary pairs commonly used in pharmaceutical processing.

title: Replacing N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone in polyimide membrane casting: a structured solvent selection workflow
abstract: N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) is widely used in polyimide membrane casting for gas separation applications but is subject to restriction under REACH due to reproductive toxicity. This study presents a structured workflow combining HSP sphere analysis, CHEM21 solvent selection guide scoring, and a practical castability screen to identify replacements. From an initial list of 52 solvents, the HSP filter (Ra ≤ 5.5 MPa^0.5 relative to the polyimide repeat unit) reduced candidates to 14; the CHEM21 step eliminated 6 on safety and environmental grounds; the castability screen—measuring film flatness, defect density by scanning electron microscopy, and membrane thickness uniformity—shortlisted 3 candidates: gamma-valerolactone, N-formylmorpholine, and dimethyl sulfoxide/glycerol 85:15 v/v. Gas permeance for CO2 and N2 was within 12% of NMP-cast reference membranes for all three. Gamma-valerolactone showed the most reproducible film morphology and is recommended for scale-up trials.

title: Life-cycle solvent assessment in the synthesis of agrochemical triazole intermediates: a case study from a Serbian fine-chemical context
abstract: Triazole-containing agrochemicals represent a significant share of the Central European fungicide market, and their synthesis intermediates are typically prepared using dichloromethane-intensive routes. This case study, conducted in collaboration with an anonymised Serbian fine-chemical producer, assessed the environmental burden of the existing DCM-based extraction step using a gate-to-gate LCA and compared it with three alternatives: ethyl acetate, 2-MeTHF, and isopropyl acetate. LCA boundaries included solvent production, transport to Novi Sad, use at 200 L reactor scale, distillative recovery, and incineration of residues. Across all five midpoint categories assessed (climate change, human toxicity, freshwater ecotoxicity, photochemical ozone formation, resource depletion), 2-MeTHF from bio-based furfural showed the lowest aggregate burden. Yield parity (within 2%) was confirmed at pilot scale. Implementation was estimated to reduce annual DCM purchase by 3.4 tonnes for the studied product line.

title: Automated Hansen solubility parameter determination using a cloud-controlled liquid-handling robot and turbidity sensing
abstract: Manual determination of HSP spheres is reproducible but labour-intensive. This work describes the construction and validation of an automated HSP mapping station built around a commercial 8-channel liquid-handling robot, a multi-cuvette turbidity detector, and custom control software. The system prepares and measures 48 solvent–solute vials in a single run of approximately 3 hours with less than 0.5% volumetric dispensing error. Three validation compounds—naphthalene, a commercial epoxy resin, and a hydroxypropylmethylcellulose grade—were characterised and their HSP spheres compared with published reference values. Ra deviations from reference were 0.3, 0.7, and 1.2 MPa^0.5 respectively, all within expected experimental scatter. Solvent consumption per full 48-point screen was 96 mL, roughly 60% less than a standard manual protocol. The station is maintained as shared infrastructure at the Faculty of Technology and is available to external users under a standard access agreement.

title: Solvent selection for continuous flow extraction of carotenoids from dried tomato pomace: HSP screening combined with environmental scoring
abstract: Tomato pomace, a by-product of juice and sauce production, contains 200–600 mg/kg lycopene and beta-carotene on a dry mass basis and represents a low-cost feedstock for natural pigment recovery. Continuous flow extraction offers higher throughput than batch methods but intensifies solvent consumption per unit time if solvent choice is not optimised. This study first applied HSP analysis to shortlist solvents with Ra ≤ 3.5 MPa^0.5 relative to lycopene, producing a candidate list of 11 solvents. These were scored using the GSK solvent sustainability guide and CHEM21 metrics. The top four—ethyl acetate, isopropyl acetate, ethanol/hexane 1:1 v/v, and 2-MeTHF—were tested in a 10 mL/min tubular flow extractor at 40 °C using 50 g batches of dried pomace. Lycopene recovery was 88%, 81%, 92%, and 86% respectively; the ethanol/hexane blend was excluded on safety grounds at scale. 2-MeTHF was selected for further optimisation based on combined yield and sustainability scores.

title: Selenium and chromium speciation in Chlorella vulgaris dietary supplements: method development and uncertainty estimation
abstract: Selenium and chromium species were simultaneously determined in twelve commercial Chlorella vulgaris tablet and powder products by HPLC-ICP-MS following microwave-assisted extraction with 0.1 M HCl at 70 °C for 20 min. Selenium species (selenate, selenite, selenomethionine, methylselenocysteine) were resolved on a reversed-phase C18 column with 0.1% formic acid/methanol gradient; chromium species (Cr(III), Cr(VI)) were separated on a cation-exchange resin with oxalate buffer. Recovery of spiked selenomethionine was 96 ± 4% and of Cr(VI) was 101 ± 6%. Measurement uncertainty was estimated following GUM guidelines, with combined relative uncertainties of 6–9% for Se species and 8–12% for Cr species. Selenomethionine constituted 55–78% of total selenium in all samples. Cr(VI) was detected above the LOQ (0.002 mg/kg) in only two products from non-EU suppliers, at 0.008 and 0.014 mg/kg. The validated procedure is proposed as a suitable candidate method for routine quality control of microalgal food supplements.

title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone levels and carotid intima-media thickness in perimenopausal women: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: Subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) is prevalent in perimenopausal women and may accelerate early atherosclerosis. We performed a cross-sectional study in 148 women aged 45–55 years attending a gynaecology outpatient clinic in Novi Sad; 51 had SCH (TSH 4.5–10 mIU/L, free T4 normal) and 97 were euthyroid controls. Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) was measured bilaterally using high-resolution B-mode ultrasound. Mean CIMT was significantly greater in the SCH group (0.82 ± 0.11 mm vs. 0.71 ± 0.09 mm, p < 0.001) after adjustment for age, body mass index, smoking, and lipid levels. Multivariate linear regression identified TSH as an independent predictor of CIMT (β = 0.031, 95% CI 0.014–0.048). The association was strongest in women with TSH above 7 mIU/L. These findings suggest that even mildly elevated TSH values may contribute to structural vascular changes before overt hypothyroidism develops.

title: Arterial stiffness measured by pulse-wave velocity in subclinical hypothyroidism: results from a Serbian cohort of postmenopausal women
abstract: Arterial stiffness is an independent cardiovascular risk marker. We measured carotid-femoral pulse-wave velocity (cfPWV) using applanation tonometry in 67 postmenopausal women with subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH; TSH 4.5–10 mIU/L) and 74 euthyroid postmenopausal controls recruited from the Endocrinology Outpatient Department of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2011 and 2013. Mean cfPWV was 9.4 ± 1.3 m/s in the SCH group versus 8.5 ± 1.2 m/s in controls (p < 0.001). After adjustment for mean arterial pressure, age, lipids, and HbA1c, SCH remained a significant independent determinant of elevated cfPWV (β = 0.72, 95% CI 0.29–1.15). There was no significant interaction with duration of menopause. This cross-sectional observation supports routine cfPWV assessment in postmenopausal women found to have elevated TSH during metabolic screening.

title: Prevalence of subclinical hypothyroidism and its overlap with metabolic syndrome in a primary-care population of postmenopausal women in Vojvodina
abstract: Epidemiological data on the co-occurrence of subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) and metabolic syndrome (MetS) in postmenopausal women from South-East Europe remain scarce. We analysed data from 1,204 postmenopausal women (mean age 61.4 ± 7.2 years) registered at 14 primary-care centres in the Vojvodina region. SCH was defined as TSH 4.5–10 mIU/L with normal free T4 on two separate measurements. MetS was defined using IDF/AHA criteria. SCH prevalence was 12.7% (153/1,204). Among women with SCH, 48.4% also met MetS criteria, compared with 31.2% in euthyroid women (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.44–2.98). Waist circumference and triglyceride levels were the MetS components most strongly associated with SCH. These population-level data from primary care suggest that thyroid screening could be incorporated into routine metabolic risk assessment programmes for postmenopausal women in the region.

title: Effect of levothyroxine therapy on arterial stiffness and diastolic function in postmenopausal women with subclinical hypothyroidism: a 12-month open-label trial
abstract: Whether levothyroxine (LT4) treatment reverses cardiovascular changes in subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) is debated. We conducted a 12-month open-label trial in 58 postmenopausal women with TSH 5.5–10 mIU/L randomised 1:1 to LT4 (starting dose 25 µg/day, titrated to achieve TSH 0.5–2.5 mIU/L) or observation. Carotid-femoral pulse-wave velocity (cfPWV) and echocardiographic E/e' ratio were the primary endpoints. At 12 months, cfPWV decreased by 0.61 m/s (95% CI −1.02 to −0.20, p = 0.004) in the treatment arm with no significant change in controls (−0.12 m/s, p = 0.41). E/e' ratio improved from 9.8 to 8.7 in the LT4 arm (p = 0.03) versus no change in controls. TSH normalisation was achieved in 83% of treated participants. No serious adverse events were recorded. These data suggest a modest but measurable cardiovascular benefit of LT4 over 12 months in this subgroup, warranting larger confirmatory trials.

title: Subclinical hypothyroidism as a risk factor for incident atrial fibrillation in postmenopausal women: findings from a five-year follow-up study
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) risk in subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) is understudied relative to overt thyroid disease. We followed 341 postmenopausal women (121 with baseline SCH, 220 euthyroid) for a median of 5.2 years, using 12-lead ECG and 24-hour Holter monitoring at annual visits. Incident AF was identified in 14 women with SCH (11.6%) versus 11 euthyroid women (5.0%; log-rank p = 0.02). Cox proportional hazards analysis adjusted for age, hypertension, diabetes, BMI, and left atrial diameter yielded an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.31 (95% CI 1.04–5.13) for SCH. Left atrial diameter at baseline was the strongest single predictor (HR per mm: 1.24, 95% CI 1.11–1.39). The absolute event numbers are modest and the study was not powered for definitive conclusions; nonetheless the direction and magnitude of association justify a prospective multicentre replication.

title: Cardiovascular sequelae of subclinical hypothyroidism in postmenopausal women
abstract: This book chapter reviews the pathophysiological mechanisms linking mildly elevated TSH to cardiovascular disease in the postmenopausal context. The chapter covers thyroid hormone action on vascular smooth muscle tone and endothelial function, the contribution of dyslipidaemia and low-grade inflammation to atherogenesis in SCH, and the evidence from observational studies and small intervention trials. Special attention is paid to the heterogeneity of TSH thresholds used across studies (ranging from 2.5 to 5.0 mIU/L as the upper limit of normal) and how this complicates risk estimation. The chapter also discusses the interaction between menopause-related oestrogen deficiency and thyroid hormone insufficiency at the level of the cardiomyocyte and vascular wall. Clinical guidance on when to consider echocardiographic and vascular assessment is offered, alongside a critical appraisal of current treatment guidelines in this subpopulation.

title: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide as a marker of subclinical cardiac dysfunction in euthyroid versus hypothyroid postmenopausal women: a cross-sectional comparison
abstract: NT-proBNP is secreted in response to myocardial wall stress and elevated filling pressures. We measured serum NT-proBNP in 184 postmenopausal women grouped as euthyroid (n = 74), subclinical hypothyroid (TSH 4.5–10 mIU/L, n = 63), and overtly hypothyroid (TSH > 10 mIU/L, n = 47). All participants had no history of heart failure or coronary artery disease. Median NT-proBNP was 68 pg/mL (IQR 44–98) in euthyroid, 97 pg/mL (IQR 62–144) in SCH, and 142 pg/mL (IQR 88–211) in overt hypothyroid women (Kruskal–Wallis p < 0.001). Pairwise comparisons showed a significant step-up between euthyroid and SCH groups (p = 0.003). NT-proBNP correlated positively with E/e' (r = 0.44) and negatively with lateral e' velocity (r = −0.39). Receiver-operating characteristic analysis suggested NT-proBNP > 85 pg/mL as a candidate threshold to prompt echocardiographic evaluation, with sensitivity 61% and specificity 72% for grade I or higher diastolic dysfunction.

title: Subclinical hypothyroidism and impaired heart rate variability in postmenopausal women: a time- and frequency-domain analysis
abstract: Reduced heart rate variability (HRV) reflects impaired autonomic modulation and predicts adverse cardiac outcomes. We analysed 24-hour Holter recordings in 88 postmenopausal women: 44 with SCH (TSH 4.5–10 mIU/L) and 44 matched euthyroid controls. Standard time-domain indices (SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50) and frequency-domain indices (LF, HF, LF/HF ratio) were computed. SDNN was 98 ± 22 ms in SCH versus 112 ± 24 ms in controls (p = 0.002). RMSSD and pNN50 were similarly reduced in SCH. Spectral analysis showed a significant reduction in HF power (0.41 ± 0.19 vs. 0.57 ± 0.24 ms²×10³, p = 0.001) and an elevated LF/HF ratio (3.1 ± 1.1 vs. 2.4 ± 0.9, p = 0.003), indicating relative sympathetic predominance. TSH was independently and inversely associated with SDNN in multivariate regression (β = −3.8, 95% CI −6.1 to −1.5). Autonomic dysfunction may partly mediate the increased arrhythmia susceptibility observed in SCH.

title: Left atrial strain measured by speckle-tracking echocardiography in postmenopausal women with subclinical hypothyroidism: a pilot observational study
abstract: Left atrial (LA) strain assessed by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) is a sensitive marker of atrial myopathy preceding overt dysfunction. We performed 2D-STE in 62 postmenopausal women (31 SCH, TSH 4.5–10 mIU/L; 31 euthyroid controls) using a high-end ultrasound platform and commercially available speckle-tracking software. LA reservoir strain (LASr), conduit strain (LAScd), and contractile strain (LASct) were measured offline from three-beat averaged apical four- and two-chamber views. LASr was significantly lower in SCH (31.4 ± 5.2%) than in controls (36.1 ± 5.8%, p < 0.001). LASct was also reduced (−11.8 ± 3.1% vs. −14.2 ± 3.4%, p = 0.002). LASr correlated inversely with TSH (r = −0.45, p < 0.001) and positively with lateral e' velocity (r = 0.52, p < 0.001). These preliminary data suggest that LA mechanical dysfunction detectable by STE may precede the onset of arrhythmia in postmenopausal SCH. Larger studies with incident AF as an endpoint are warranted.

title: Praxis Philosophy and Pedagogy: The Korčula Summer School as a Site of Educational Critique, 1964–1974
abstract: Drawing on published proceedings, correspondence archived at the Institute of Social Sciences in Belgrade, and interviews with three surviving participants, this paper reconstructs the pedagogical dimension of the Korčula Summer School, which operated from 1964 to 1974 as an international Marxist humanist forum. While the School is well studied as a philosophical event, its explicit engagements with educational theory have received little attention. The paper documents how Praxis-affiliated thinkers—chiefly from Zagreb and Sarajevo—developed a critique of instrumentalised schooling that challenged dominant Yugoslav Party pedagogy from within a socialist framework. Twelve participant memoirs and 34 published texts were coded using thematic analysis. The study argues that the Praxis critique constituted a minor but epistemologically significant counter-tradition that later supplied intellectual resources for post-1990 curriculum liberalisation discourses in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. The paper situates these findings within broader debates on critical pedagogy in Cold War Europe.

title: Discontinuity as Policy: The Rewriting of Pedagogical Foundations in Serbian Education Law, 1990–2004
abstract: This article analyses five successive education framework laws enacted in Serbia between 1990 and 2004 to trace how socialist pedagogical language was progressively displaced, retained, or reframed within post-transition legislative text. The study uses critical discourse analysis on the full legislative texts alongside parliamentary transcripts from 23 committee sessions sourced from the National Assembly of Serbia archives. Findings show three distinct phases: a reactive de-ideologisation (1990–1993), a period of rhetorical ambiguity (1994–2000), and a structured alignment with Council of Europe competence-based frameworks (2001–2004). Contrary to dominant transition narratives, large segments of socialist-era normative language persisted in operative clauses through all three phases, often recontextualised rather than replaced. The article identifies specific actors—former pedagogy professors serving as ministry advisors—who mediated this continuity. The results contribute to comparative post-socialist education law scholarship and to debates on path dependency in institutional reform.

title: Remembering the School of the Past: Oral History and Generational Memory of Yugoslav Classroom Practice among Teachers Trained before 1990
abstract: This paper reports findings from 38 semi-structured interviews conducted between 2017 and 2019 with retired and active teachers in Vojvodina who completed their initial teacher education before 1990. The study investigates how these educators narrate and evaluate the pedagogical principles they were trained in, and how they position those principles relative to current practice. Interviews were transcribed, translated where necessary (six respondents spoke in Hungarian), and analysed using constructivist grounded theory. Four dominant memory frames emerged: nostalgic coherence, critical retrospection, pragmatic continuity, and silence around politically sensitive practices such as mandatory ideological ceremonies. The paper argues that generational professional memory constitutes an underexamined vector through which socialist pedagogical epistemology persists in present classroom cultures, distinct from but intersecting with formal curriculum and policy channels. Methodological reflections on oral history in post-socialist educational research are included.

title: Between Belgrade and Ljubljana: Comparative Epistemological Divergence in Yugoslav Pedagogical Science, 1970–1988
abstract: This conference paper maps the divergence between dominant pedagogical research paradigms at the University of Belgrade and the University of Ljubljana during the final two decades of Yugoslav socialism. Using bibliometric analysis of 214 articles published in the two leading republic-level pedagogy journals over this period, the study quantifies differences in citation networks, methodological preferences, and theoretical reference points. Ljubljana-based researchers showed significantly higher engagement with West German and Austrian empirical educational science and with phenomenological approaches, while Belgrade research remained more oriented toward Soviet-influenced collective pedagogy and, increasingly, American sociological frameworks. The paper uses correspondence analysis to visualise the citation space and argues that these divergences reflected not simply different intellectual traditions but also deliberate institutional choices shaped by republic-level cultural policy. Implications for understanding post-Yugoslav educational fragmentation are discussed.

title: The Epistemological Status of 'Socialist Upbringing' (socijalističko vaspitanje) in Yugoslav Pedagogy Handbooks: A Concept History
abstract: This article undertakes a concept history (Begriffsgeschichte) of the term socijalističko vaspitanje ('socialist upbringing') as it appeared in the seven most widely used Yugoslav pedagogy university handbooks published between 1948 and 1988. The corpus of approximately 2,400 pages was subjected to both close reading and frequency-weighted keyword-in-context analysis using AntConc software. The study tracks how the concept's epistemic grounding shifted from explicit Marxist-Leninist doctrinal authority in early texts to a hybridised appeal to humanist developmental psychology and self-management theory in later ones. It further examines how the concept was assigned different disciplinary locations—sometimes subsumed under general didactics, sometimes treated as a branch of social pedagogy—reflecting ongoing boundary disputes within Yugoslav pedagogical science. The article contributes to the historiography of socialist education by demonstrating that even a core normative concept was epistemologically unstable across the period.

title: Post-Yugoslav Curriculum Convergence and the European Qualifications Framework: A Comparative Policy Analysis of Serbia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro, 2005–2023
abstract: This study analyses the adoption and domestic adaptation of European Qualifications Framework (EQF) principles in the curriculum policies of Serbia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro between 2005 and 2023. The analysis draws on 89 policy documents—national qualifications frameworks, ministerial strategies, and EU-funded reform reports—collected through systematic document search and supplemented by eleven expert interviews with officials from national qualifications agencies. Using policy borrowing theory, the paper examines which EQF elements were adopted instrumentally for EU integration purposes, which were substantively internalised, and which were formally endorsed but operationally resisted. Results indicate that all three states followed broadly similar adoption timelines driven by European integration incentives, but that the internal resistance of inherited socialist-era vocational pedagogy traditions produced distinct implementation gaps in each country. The comparative framing highlights how the post-Yugoslav epistemological legacy continues to mediate externally driven reform agendas.

title: Comparison of pixel-based and object-based classification approaches for maize row detection from airborne multispectral imagery
abstract: This study evaluated pixel-based maximum likelihood classification against multiresolution object-based image analysis (OBIA) for delineating individual maize rows in airborne multispectral imagery acquired at 8 cm ground sampling distance over three fields in Vojvodina, Serbia. Imagery was collected with a six-band camera covering 450–850 nm. Segmentation scale parameters were systematically varied from 10 to 80 using the Estimation of Scale Parameter 2 (ESP2) tool. OBIA achieved an overall accuracy of 91.3% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.88, compared to 78.6% and 0.71 for pixel-based classification. Results showed that incorporating shape and compactness features in addition to spectral bands improved row delineation particularly in areas with partial canopy closure. Field validation was conducted using 120 reference points across three growth stages (V4, V8, VT). The study concluded that scale parameter selection is the dominant source of variability in OBIA outcomes for row-crop scenes.

title: Spectral separability of sunflower and soybean canopies under varying nitrogen treatments using ground-based hyperspectral measurements
abstract: Controlled-plot experiments were established at the Rimski Šančevi agricultural research station near Novi Sad to assess whether hyperspectral reflectance measured with an ASD FieldSpec 4 spectrometer (350–2500 nm) could separate sunflower and soybean canopies under four nitrogen fertilisation levels (0, 60, 120, 180 kg N/ha). Measurements were taken at nadir from 1.2 m height at four phenological stages across two growing seasons (2015 and 2016), yielding 864 spectra. Spectral separability was quantified using Jeffries–Matusita distance and transformed divergence across all pairwise class combinations. Red-edge chlorophyll index (CIre) and the ratio of reflectance at 750 nm to 710 nm showed the highest separability scores. A linear discriminant analysis using 12 selected wavebands achieved 87% correct classification across crop-by-treatment combinations. Practical implications for UAV sensor band selection are discussed.

title: Automated delineation of soybean rows in UAV multispectral imagery using morphological profile analysis
abstract: This paper presents an automated method for soybean row delineation that uses morphological profiles computed from the near-infrared band of a five-band multispectral UAV image (MicaSense Altum, 8 cm GSD). The method applies a sequence of opening-by-reconstruction operations at varying structuring element sizes to extract elongated canopy structures corresponding to crop rows. A Hough transform-based regularisation step then fits row orientation and spacing parameters. The method was tested on 14 flights over seven fields in the 2020 and 2021 growing seasons, covering V3 to R5 growth stages. Row detection completeness ranged from 88% to 97% depending on canopy closure stage. Processing time per hectare was approximately 40 seconds on a standard workstation. The method requires no training data and is transferable across row spacings between 40 and 75 cm without parameter adjustment.

title: Influence of flight altitude and sun angle on within-field reflectance variability in UAV hyperspectral maize surveys
abstract: Consistent radiometric quality is a prerequisite for time-series analysis in precision agriculture, yet the combined effect of flight altitude and solar elevation angle on measured canopy reflectance has received limited systematic study in operational UAV surveys. Flights over a single maize field were conducted at 40 m, 70 m, and 100 m altitudes and at three times of day (08:00, 11:00, 14:00 local time) for three dates in the 2021 growing season. Reflectance was recorded with a Headwall Nano-Hyperspec sensor (270 bands, 400–1000 nm). Coefficient of variation of reflectance across the field increased by up to 18% at low altitudes, partly attributable to BRDF effects and pixel-level mixing at high altitude. An empirical line calibration using calibrated Spectralon panels reduced inter-flight variability from 12.4% to 4.1% for the red-edge band. Results provide practical guidelines for survey design.

title: Row-crop canopy segmentation across multiple crops using a transferable OBIA ruleset: a case study in Vojvodina
abstract: Object-based image analysis rulesets developed for one crop type often fail when applied to another without re-parameterisation. This study tested a single transferable OBIA ruleset, calibrated on maize imagery, on UAV multispectral datasets covering maize, sunflower, sugar beet, and soybean acquired across 22 fields and three growing seasons. The ruleset relied on NDVI thresholding combined with shape-index constraints and was recalibrated using only ten reference objects per new crop. Segmentation quality was assessed using the oversegmentation and undersegmentation indices. Across all crops and growth stages the mean F1 score for canopy objects was 0.86 (SD 0.07). Failures were concentrated in early vegetative stages (V2–V3) where canopy objects were smaller than 120 cm². The study provides a baseline for further machine-learning-based adaptation approaches and makes the ruleset parameters publicly available.

title: Detection of lodged maize zones from post-storm UAV hyperspectral imagery using spectral and textural features
abstract: Lodging caused by convective storms in Vojvodina can reduce harvestable yield by 15–40% in affected fields. This study investigated whether lodged maize zones could be identified from UAV hyperspectral imagery (128 bands, 4 cm GSD) acquired 48 hours after a major storm event in August 2022. Spectral angle mapper classification combined with grey-level co-occurrence matrix texture features (contrast, homogeneity, correlation at 0°, 45°, 90°, 135°) was applied to four fields totalling 68 ha. Producer's accuracy for lodged zones was 89% and user's accuracy was 84%. The normalised difference between bands at 531 nm and 570 nm (PRI) was the single most discriminating spectral feature, reflecting altered canopy architecture rather than stress-induced pigment changes. The approach was operationalised as a semi-automated processing script taking approximately 12 minutes per 10-hectare field.

title: Estimation of row-level leaf area index in sunflower using instance segmentation and structure-from-motion point clouds
abstract: Estimating leaf area index (LAI) at the individual row level requires combining three-dimensional canopy structure information with spectral data. This study combined UAV-derived structure-from-motion (SfM) point clouds with concurrent hyperspectral orthomosaics to estimate row-level LAI in sunflower across four fields during the 2025 growing season near Bečej, Serbia. A Mask R-CNN model, fine-tuned on 340 manually labelled canopy instances, was used to delineate individual row segments in the multispectral orthomosaic. Height metrics extracted from the SfM point cloud for each delineated row segment, combined with the NDRE index, were input to a Gaussian process regression model predicting LAI. Cross-validation RMSE was 0.31 m² m⁻² against 88 destructive LAI measurements. The method produced row-level LAI maps at 10 cm GSD, a spatial resolution relevant for intra-field management decisions.

title: High-Resolution Frost Risk Index for Vineyards in the Srem and Fruška Gora Wine Region
abstract: Late spring frost events (April–May) are a primary yield-limiting factor for viticulture in the Srem and Fruška Gora region. A spatial frost risk index (FRI) was developed by combining downscaled minimum temperature grids at 250 m resolution, topographic cold-air drainage indices derived from a 25 m DEM, and 22 years of phenological records from 14 commercial vineyards. Minimum temperature was downscaled from a 2 km gridded product using a local lapse-rate correction and a cold-air-pooling factor estimated from nighttime MODIS LST anomalies. FRI was defined as the probability that minimum temperature falls below −1 °C during the period 15 April–20 May. Maps produced at the parcel scale (0.5 ha) showed risk differentiation of up to 35 percentage points across elevation bands as narrow as 40 m, consistent with growers' empirical observations. The index was validated against three independent frost event records with an accuracy of 81 %.

title: Comparison of UAV photogrammetry and terrestrial LiDAR for façade geometry capture in a historic city block
abstract: Urban solar modelling requires accurate representation not only of rooftops but also of vertical façades, which receive direct irradiance in winter. This paper compared a nadir-plus-oblique UAV photogrammetric survey (Sony RX1R-II sensor, 42 Mpx) and a phase-based terrestrial laser scanner (Leica RTC360) for capturing façade geometry on a 14-building block in the historic core of Sremski Karlovci, Serbia. Point cloud density, planimetric completeness, and geometric accuracy were assessed. The UAV survey produced 480 points/m² on rooftops but only 62 points/m² on lower-storey façades due to occlusion. The laser scanner yielded 1 100 points/m² on accessible façades but left shadow gaps exceeding 15% on narrow street-facing walls. A merged product combining both sources achieved completeness of 91% and mean surface deviation of 8 mm relative to 42 check targets. Implications for winter façade solar calculations are discussed.

title: Background Removal Techniques for GPR B-Scan Data: A Comparative Evaluation on Field Measurements
abstract: Effective clutter suppression is a prerequisite for automated target detection in ground-penetrating radar surveys. This study systematically compared five background removal methods — mean subtraction, median subtraction, singular value decomposition filtering, frequency–wavenumber filtering, and a Wiener-filter-based approach — applied to 24 field B-scan profiles collected over known buried pipes and cables in urban test sites near Novi Sad. Profiles were acquired with a 500 MHz antenna at 0.02 m trace spacing. Performance was assessed using signal-to-clutter ratio and hyperbola apex visibility scores assigned by two independent annotators. SVD-based filtering achieved the highest mean signal-to-clutter ratio (14.3 dB) but introduced geometric distortions in shallow targets above 0.15 m depth. Median subtraction performed consistently across all depth ranges. The dataset and annotation labels are made publicly available to support reproducibility. Results provide practical guidance for selecting preprocessing pipelines prior to automated detection.

title: Anchor-Free Object Detection Applied to Hyperbola Localisation in GPR Imagery
abstract: Anchor-based detectors require careful tuning of anchor aspect ratios, which is non-trivial for GPR hyperbolas whose shape varies with depth, antenna frequency, and soil permittivity. This study adapted the CenterNet anchor-free framework to detect and localise hyperbola apices in B-scan images treated as single-channel 2D images. The model predicted a heatmap of apex locations alongside offset and size regression heads. Training used 6,200 annotated hyperbola instances from 83 profiles acquired at 250 MHz and 700 MHz. The model reached a mean average precision at IoU 0.5 of 0.893, outperforming a Faster R-CNN baseline (0.871 mAP) while running 1.7× faster. Qualitative analysis showed that apex localisation errors under 3 pixels (corresponding to roughly 0.03 m depth error) occurred in 91% of detected targets. The approach is less sensitive to antenna frequency than the anchor-based baseline when tested across frequencies unseen during training.

title: Accuracy Assessment of Low-Cost UAV LiDAR for Road Surface Profiling on Rural Highways
abstract: This study evaluates the geometric accuracy of a lightweight rotary-wing UAV equipped with a 16-channel scanning LiDAR for road surface profiling on a 4.2 km rural highway segment in Vojvodina, Serbia. Flight missions were conducted at 50 m and 80 m above ground level, and the resulting point clouds were compared against reference measurements from a terrestrial laser scanner mounted on a survey vehicle. Point cloud density averaged 42 pts/m² at 50 m altitude. Vertical RMSE values were 4.1 cm and 6.8 cm for the two altitudes respectively, with horizontal RMSE below 7 cm in both cases. The study identifies systematic roll-angle bias as the dominant error source and proposes a strip-adjustment procedure that reduces vertical RMSE by 38 % without ground control points. Results suggest that low-cost UAV LiDAR is adequate for detecting pavement deterioration features larger than approximately 15 cm in plan extent, while finer cracking requires supplementary photogrammetric texture data.

title: Bitemporal Registration of Airborne LiDAR Strips for Road Pavement Change Detection
abstract: Registering LiDAR strips acquired in different seasons and by different sensor platforms is a prerequisite for reliable change detection in road infrastructure. This paper presents a registration workflow based on planar road surface patches extracted as stable primitives and used as tie features in an iterative closest-plane algorithm. The method was tested on two LiDAR datasets covering a 28 km national road corridor in northern Serbia, acquired 18 months apart by different contractors using sensors of different point densities (8 pts/m² and 31 pts/m²). After registration, the mean surface discrepancy on unchanged asphalt areas dropped from 9.3 cm to 1.8 cm RMSE. Change masks generated from the registered clouds detected 94 % of verified pavement failures larger than 0.5 m², with a false-positive rate of 6.1 %. The proposed tie-feature extraction is fully automated and processes the full corridor in under 12 minutes on a standard workstation.

title: Lane Marking Extraction from Mobile and UAV LiDAR Data: A Comparative Study
abstract: Lane markings are a primary feature in high-definition maps for autonomous driving. This paper compares two acquisition strategies for lane marking extraction: a ground-based mobile laser scanning system mounted on a survey van, and a UAV-borne LiDAR flown at 30 m altitude. Both datasets cover a 3.1 km urban arterial road in Novi Sad, acquired on the same day. Intensity-based segmentation followed by connected-component labelling was applied to both datasets. The mobile system produced intensity RMSE of 0.04 (normalised) and extracted 97.3 % of visible lane markings with a positional accuracy of 2.8 cm. The UAV system extracted 89.6 % with positional accuracy of 5.4 cm. Processing time per kilometre was approximately 4 minutes for both pipelines. The paper discusses the trade-off between acquisition cost, coverage rate, and mapping accuracy, and identifies road geometry (curvature, gradient) as a key factor affecting UAV performance.

title: Detecting Road Widening and New Construction from Multitemporal Sentinel-2 and Archival Topographic Data
abstract: Road network changes at the regional scale are often monitored through periodic resurveys, which are costly and infrequent. This study proposes a workflow combining bi-yearly Sentinel-2 time series with raster topographic map data at 1:25 000 scale to flag candidate change areas for field verification or UAV follow-up. A spectral change index derived from NDVI and bare-soil band ratios was used to isolate linear construction corridors, followed by morphological filtering to suppress agricultural and urban clutter. The method was applied to 1 240 km of classified road network in Vojvodina over the period 2017–2022. Of 47 confirmed new or widened road segments (validated against official road authority records), 39 were correctly flagged (83 % recall). False-positive rate per 10 km road segment was 0.18. Sentinel-2 temporal resolution proved sufficient for detecting construction phases lasting more than three months. The workflow runs as an automated monthly batch job and outputs GeoJSON candidate polygons for review.

title: Automated Road Furniture Inventory from UAV Point Clouds Using Shape Primitive Fitting
abstract: Road furniture — signs, guardrails, lighting poles, and delineators — must be accurately recorded in both topographic databases and HD maps. This paper presents a processing chain for automated detection and classification of road furniture objects from UAV LiDAR point clouds. The chain applies ground filtering and above-ground segmentation, then fits geometric primitives (cylinders, planar patches, and curved sheets) to candidate clusters using RANSAC. Each cluster is assigned to one of seven furniture categories based on primitive type, dimension ratios, and height above road surface. The method was validated on 5.7 km of motorway near Novi Sad, where 412 objects were manually inventoried as reference. Detection recall was 91 % for vertical pole-like objects and 84 % for guardrail sections; classification accuracy over detected objects was 88.3 %. Processing time was 22 minutes for the full corridor. The paper also reports on a small trial of the same chain applied to mobile LiDAR data, yielding consistently higher recall due to superior point density.

title: Map Update Workflows for Lane-Level HD Maps: A Review of Data Sources, Change Triggers, and Validation Strategies
abstract: High-definition lane-level maps for autonomous and assisted driving require update cycles that are fundamentally different from those of conventional road databases. This book chapter reviews the data acquisition sources currently used or proposed for HD map updating, covering mobile LiDAR, UAV LiDAR, satellite very-high-resolution imagery, crowd-sourced probe vehicle data, and hybrid combinations. For each source, the chapter discusses achievable positional accuracy, typical update latency, cost per kilometre, and the change categories that each source can realistically detect. Particular attention is given to the distinction between geometric change (road surface, lane geometry) and semantic change (marking degradation, sign replacement, furniture addition). Validation strategies reviewed include ground truth survey comparison, map-to-map consistency checking, and driver-in-the-loop simulation testing. The chapter concludes with a discussion of standardisation efforts and the gap between research prototypes and operational map maintenance pipelines, drawing on examples from central and southeastern European infrastructure projects.

title: LiDAR-to-Satellite Image Co-Registration for Road Infrastructure Change Detection in Mixed Urban–Rural Corridors
abstract: Combining UAV LiDAR point clouds with very high-resolution (VHR) satellite imagery enables change detection across spatial scales, but requires robust co-registration between the two data modalities. This study develops a co-registration procedure based on road centreline and kerb-edge features extracted independently from both datasets and matched via a modified iterative closest-point algorithm operating in 2D plan view. The procedure was tested on a 12 km urban–rural transitional corridor in Novi Sad using UAV LiDAR (40 pts/m²) and a 0.5 m resolution tri-stereo satellite image acquired within 11 days of the LiDAR flight. Planimetric co-registration error after the procedure was 0.31 m RMSE, compared to 1.87 m before. Change areas identified jointly by both data sources showed 91 % agreement with field-verified change records. The study found that satellite imagery contributed most to detecting large-scale structural changes (new buildings encroaching on road reserves), while LiDAR was more sensitive to surface-level changes such as kerb displacement and lane-marking refresh.

title: Temporal Consistency of Extracted Lane Boundaries Across Repeated UAV LiDAR Surveys: A Six-Campaign Study
abstract: Reliable HD map maintenance requires that automatically extracted lane boundaries remain consistent across repeated surveys conducted under varying conditions. This paper reports on six UAV LiDAR surveys of a 2.4 km test road segment near Novi Sad, conducted between April 2022 and November 2024 at irregular intervals of two to eight months, with varying leaf cover, road moisture conditions, and two different UAV sensor configurations. Lane boundaries were extracted using the pipeline described in earlier work by the same group. The key metric tracked was the inter-survey standard deviation of extracted boundary positions on road sections confirmed as geometrically unchanged. Median inter-survey standard deviation was 3.7 cm in the along-road direction and 4.2 cm in the cross-road direction. Outlier surveys correlated with wet pavement conditions that suppressed LiDAR return intensity from faded markings. A moisture flag based on spectral auxiliary imagery is proposed as a quality gate for operational workflows. The dataset from all six campaigns has been made publicly available.

title: Estimating Road Shoulder Erosion Volumes from Bitemporal UAV LiDAR Using Differenced Digital Terrain Models
abstract: Shoulder erosion on unpaved and lightly paved rural roads is a maintenance concern that is rarely quantified systematically due to the cost of conventional surveying. This preprint presents a workflow for estimating eroded and deposited volumes along road shoulders using differenced digital terrain models (dDTMs) derived from repeated UAV LiDAR surveys. The workflow includes point cloud normalisation, adaptive ground filtering tuned for shoulder geometry, and uncertainty-weighted volume integration that accounts for spatially variable registration error. The method was applied to 6.8 km of unpaved agricultural-access road surveyed in spring 2024 and spring 2025 following one winter season. Total net erosion volume was estimated at 138 m³, distributed across 23 discrete erosion zones. The largest single zone measured 18.4 m³. Volume estimation uncertainty was ±12 % at 95 % confidence, dominated by ground filtering error in vegetated shoulder areas. The authors note that the workflow requires no special ground control beyond a minimal set of five flat targets per kilometre.

title: Propagation of Coordinate Uncertainty through Cadastral Parcel Chain Traversals in Rural Vojvodina
abstract: Cadastral parcels in Vojvodina were digitised in the 1970s and 1980s from analogue maps at scales between 1:2500 and 1:5000. The accumulated positional uncertainty along boundary chains connecting common corners can reach several decimetres in areas where the original survey control was sparse. This paper models uncertainty propagation through a sequence of 38 connected parcel boundaries in three cadastral municipalities near Zrenjanin using variance–covariance component estimation. Observed GNSS coordinates were assigned 2 cm standard deviations, while digitised boundary corners were assigned 25–40 cm depending on map scale. The resulting uncertainty ellipses at terminal parcels ranged from 0.28 m to 0.61 m semi-major axis. A weighting strategy that down-weights the digitised observations relative to GNSS-derived constraints is shown to reduce terminal uncertainty by 35–52 %. The methodology provides an audit trail compatible with the requirements of the Serbian cadastral legal framework.

title: Influence of curing temperature on reaction products and mechanical performance of alkali-activated slag from a Vojvodina steelwork
abstract: Granulated blast furnace slag sourced from the Sremska Mitrovica steel processing facility was activated with NaOH solutions of 4, 6 and 8 M concentration. Pastes were cured at 20, 40 and 60 °C for up to 90 days. 29Si and 27Al MAS-NMR spectroscopy, conducted at a partner laboratory, revealed that Q4(1Al) and Q4(2Al) environments dominated at all temperatures, with mean chain length of C-A-S-H increasing from 4.2 to 6.8 silicon units as temperature rose from 20 to 60 °C. Compressive strength at 8 M and 40 °C reached 68 MPa at 28 days, the highest value in the matrix. Elevated temperature combined with 8 M NaOH produced visible microcracking attributed to rapid desiccation and non-uniform gel shrinkage. The study recommends 40 °C pre-curing for 24 hours as a practical compromise for precast applications using this slag.

title: Resistance of alkali-activated fly ash mortars to decalcification in soft water: leaching kinetics and gel repolymerisation
abstract: Mortar prisms were immersed in continuously refreshed deionised water for up to 18 months to simulate aggressive soft-water environments relevant to hydraulic infrastructure in the Pannonian lowland. Cumulative calcium leached per unit surface area was measured by ICP-OES at monthly intervals and reached 42 mg cm−2 at 18 months, compared with 78 mg cm−2 for a reference Portland cement mortar of equivalent water-to-binder ratio. SEM-EDS line scans across the surface-to-core direction showed calcium depletion to a depth of 0.6 mm at 18 months in the alkali-activated specimens versus 1.4 mm in the Portland cement reference. 29Si MAS-NMR spectra collected on leached and unleached specimens indicated partial repolymerisation of aluminosilicate gel in the depleted zone, which may contribute to self-sealing behaviour. Compressive strength of leached alkali-activated specimens was 94% of unleached controls, suggesting that leaching alone has limited structural consequence at this exposure duration.

title: Plasma and milk pharmacokinetics of enrofloxacin and its metabolite ciprofloxacin following single subcutaneous administration in lactating dairy cows
abstract: A two-period crossover study was conducted in 12 healthy Holstein-Friesian cows administered enrofloxacin at 7.5 mg/kg BW subcutaneously. Serial blood and milk samples were collected over 120 hours and analysed by HPLC with fluorescence detection (LOQ 5 µg/L). Non-compartmental analysis yielded a plasma elimination half-life of 11.4 ± 1.9 h and milk-to-plasma AUC ratio of 2.1 ± 0.4, consistent with ion-trapping in acidic milk. Ciprofloxacin accounted for approximately 18% of the total milk residue burden at 24 h post-dose. Mean maximum milk concentrations of 312 µg/L were observed at 6 h. Individual variability in Cmax was substantial (CV 38%), suggesting that a fixed withdrawal period derived from mean data may underestimate the time required for all animals to fall below the EU MRL of 100 µg/kg. Data were used to parameterise a one-compartment model incorporating a milk-transfer compartment, yielding satisfactory goodness-of-fit diagnostics.

title: Comparative tissue depletion of enrofloxacin in muscle, liver, kidney and fat of beef cattle following a five-day intramuscular dosing regimen
abstract: Sixty Simmental steers were allocated to six slaughter groups (n = 10 each) at 1, 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days after the last of five daily intramuscular injections of enrofloxacin at 5 mg/kg BW. Edible tissues were analysed by validated HPLC-MS/MS (LOQ 10 µg/kg). Combined enrofloxacin plus ciprofloxacin concentrations in kidney were highest at slaughter day 1 (mean 2,840 µg/kg) and declined with an apparent half-life of 55 h. Muscle residues fell below the EU MRL of 100 µg/kg in all 10 animals at day 14, while kidney remained the marker tissue and did not universally reach MRL compliance until day 21. Fat residues were consistently low (< 50 µg/kg from day 7 onward). Log-linear regression with tolerance interval analysis predicted a withdrawal period of 22 days for kidney with 95% confidence at the 95th percentile, aligning with the licensed withdrawal period.

title: Pharmacokinetics of marbofloxacin after intravenous and intramuscular administration in healthy adult sheep
abstract: Eight Merinolandschaf ewes received marbofloxacin at 2 mg/kg BW intravenously and, after a 14-day washout, the same dose intramuscularly. Plasma samples were analysed by HPLC-MS/MS. Two-compartment modelling after IV dosing gave a distribution volume at steady state of 1.62 ± 0.21 L/kg and a systemic clearance of 0.18 ± 0.03 L/h/kg. Intramuscular bioavailability was 93 ± 8%. The absorption half-life was 0.35 h and elimination half-life 6.9 ± 0.8 h. The AUC/MIC ratio calculated against a target Mannheimia haemolytica MIC of 0.125 mg/L was 224 h, well above the commonly cited breakpoint of 125 h for fluoroquinolones. These data suggest that a single daily dose achieves PK/PD targets for common respiratory pathogens in sheep, and provide the kinetic parameters required for physiologically based residue modelling in this species.

title: Effect of subclinical mastitis on the milk pharmacokinetics of danofloxacin in dairy goats
abstract: Twelve Saanen does were divided into two groups: six with naturally occurring subclinical mastitis (California Mastitis Test score 2+, SCC > 500,000 cells/mL) and six healthy controls. All animals received danofloxacin 1.25 mg/kg BW subcutaneously. Milk and plasma were sampled over 72 h and analysed by HPLC-MS/MS. In mastitic animals, milk pH rose from a baseline of 6.53 to 6.74, reducing the ion-trap effect. Milk AUC of danofloxacin was 28% lower in mastitic quarters (P = 0.031) compared with healthy controls, while plasma kinetics did not differ significantly between groups. Milk-to-plasma ratio dropped from 3.8 ± 0.6 in healthy animals to 2.7 ± 0.5 in mastitic animals. These findings indicate that residue depletion may proceed faster in mastitic milk, but therapeutic concentration targets may also be harder to maintain, a consideration relevant to both efficacy and withdrawal period compliance.

title: Population pharmacokinetic modelling of enrofloxacin in beef cattle: identifying covariates for withdrawal period refinement
abstract: A population PK analysis was performed in NONMEM 7.4 using a pooled dataset from three field studies comprising 94 Simmental and Holstein-Friesian steers and heifers receiving enrofloxacin 7.5 mg/kg SC once daily for three days. A two-compartment model with first-order absorption best described the data. Body weight was a significant covariate on clearance (allometric exponent 0.71, 95% CI 0.59–0.83) and central volume (exponent 0.95). Breed had no significant effect on any structural parameter. Between-animal variability on clearance was 34% CV. A Monte Carlo simulation (n = 10,000) was used to derive a population-level withdrawal period using the EU Regulation 2017/880 tolerance interval method, yielding 18 days for muscle compared with the 15-day label claim, suggesting the label may be marginally non-conservative for heavy-weight animals. Body weight at time of treatment is proposed as a practical flag for extended withdrawal in feedlot management.

title: Fluoroquinolone residues in bovine tissues collected at routine slaughter in Vojvodina: a one-year monitoring study
abstract: A field surveillance study was conducted from January to December 2016 at three abattoirs in the Vojvodina region. Muscle, liver, and kidney samples were collected from 340 cattle carcasses selected by systematic random sampling. Residues of enrofloxacin, ciprofloxacin, marbofloxacin, and danofloxacin were determined by HPLC-MS/MS with EU Reference Laboratory-accredited methods (LOQ 10 µg/kg). Non-compliant results (above MRL) were detected in 4.4% of kidney samples and 1.2% of muscle samples. Enrofloxacin plus ciprofloxacin accounted for all non-compliant kidney samples. Traceability records where available indicated non-compliance was associated predominantly with animals from smaller, mixed-use farms rather than larger commercial cattle operations. Seasonal variation was not statistically significant. These data provide baseline residue occurrence figures for regulatory risk assessment in Serbia and highlight the continued relevance of farmer education on withdrawal period observance.

title: Influence of concurrent flunixin meglumine administration on the pharmacokinetics of enrofloxacin in cattle: a potential drug interaction study
abstract: Twelve healthy Simmental bulls received enrofloxacin 7.5 mg/kg BW SC alone (period 1) and in combination with flunixin meglumine 2.2 mg/kg BW IV (period 2) in a crossover design with 21-day washout. Serial plasma samples over 96 h were analysed by HPLC-MS/MS. Co-administration of flunixin did not significantly alter enrofloxacin Cmax (1,520 vs. 1,490 µg/L, P = 0.78) or AUC0–∞ (17,240 vs. 16,890 µg·h/L, P = 0.65). Terminal half-life and Vd were likewise unaffected. Protein binding displacement was measured in vitro at clinically relevant concentrations and showed < 3% change in free fraction. These findings suggest that the common clinical combination of an NSAID and a fluoroquinolone for treatment of bovine respiratory disease does not produce a pharmacokinetically meaningful interaction, and that separate withdrawal period calculations for each drug remain appropriate.

title: Tissue residue depletion of marbofloxacin in suckling lambs following subcutaneous treatment for respiratory infection under field conditions
abstract: This study addressed the data gap for marbofloxacin residues in lambs, a category not covered by the licensed species data used for EU MRL setting. Forty-eight Merinolandschaf lambs aged 4–6 weeks and weighing 8–14 kg were treated with marbofloxacin 2 mg/kg BW SC for three consecutive days on two commercial farms in southern Serbia. Animals were slaughtered in groups of eight at days 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, and 14 after the last dose. Muscle, liver, kidney, and fat were analysed by HPLC-MS/MS. Residues in kidney were highest (mean 1,156 µg/kg on day 1) and fell below 150 µg/kg (EU MRL) in all animals by day 10. Log-linear regression with tolerance interval analysis predicted a 12-day withdrawal period at 95/95. Liver was marker tissue throughout the study. Residue concentrations were approximately 40% higher than previously published data from adult sheep at equivalent doses, indicating age-related PK differences.

title: Pharmacokinetics and ex vivo PK/PD of danofloxacin against Pasteurella multocida isolates from Serbian sheep flocks
abstract: Danofloxacin was administered to 10 adult Württemberg sheep at 1.25 mg/kg BW SC, and plasma pharmacokinetics were determined over 72 h by HPLC-MS/MS. MIC distributions were determined by broth microdilution for 47 Pasteurella multocida isolates collected from respiratory disease cases on sheep farms across Vojvodina and Šumadija. MIC50 and MIC90 were 0.03 and 0.06 mg/L, respectively; epidemiological cut-off (ECOFF) was 0.25 mg/L. Using Monte Carlo simulation (n = 10,000) with the population PK parameter distributions from this study, AUC24/MIC target attainment at a PD target of 125 h was ≥ 96% for isolates at or below the ECOFF. One isolate with MIC 1 mg/L carried a parC point mutation (Ser80Phe) and was considered resistant. These data support the efficacy of danofloxacin at the licensed dose for respiratory pasteurellosis in Serbian sheep populations and do not reveal evidence of widespread acquired resistance.

title: Residue depletion of fluoroquinolones in bovine milk: a systematic review and meta-analysis of published depletion studies
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis summarised published milk depletion data for four fluoroquinolones authorised in cattle within the EU (enrofloxacin, marbofloxacin, danofloxacin, difloxacin) to estimate pooled depletion rate constants and assess between-study heterogeneity. A total of 28 studies published between 1993 and 2021 were included after screening 314 records against pre-specified eligibility criteria (PRISMA-Vet guidelines). Pooled first-order apparent milk elimination half-lives were 9.2 h (enrofloxacin, 95% CI 7.8–10.6), 7.1 h (marbofloxacin, 95% CI 5.9–8.3), 7.6 h (danofloxacin, 95% CI 6.5–8.7), and 8.8 h (difloxacin, 95% CI 6.4–11.2). I² values ranged from 62% to 84%, indicating substantial heterogeneity, largely attributable to dose, formulation, and baseline SCC. Studies using higher doses and oil-based formulations consistently showed longer half-lives. These pooled estimates are suitable for informing first-tier risk assessments when species-specific depletion data are unavailable.

title: Pharmacokinetics and tissue residue depletion of enrofloxacin in water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) following subcutaneous administration: a pilot study
abstract: Water buffalo are kept on approximately 30 farms in northern Serbia and are treated with cattle-licensed products off-label. No published PK or tissue residue data exist for fluoroquinolones in this species. Six adult Murrah buffalo cows received enrofloxacin 7.5 mg/kg BW SC. Plasma and milk samples were collected over 96 h; four animals were slaughtered at day 14 for tissue residue analysis. Plasma PK was broadly comparable to cattle, with a terminal half-life of 10.1 ± 1.4 h and AUC0–∞ of 15,600 µg·h/L. Milk peak concentrations (mean 280 µg/L at 8 h) were approximately 10% lower than published cattle values. All four slaughtered animals showed muscle and kidney residues below EU MRL at day 14. Although limited by sample size, these preliminary data suggest that the cattle withdrawal period of 14 days may be adequate for buffalo muscle, but further work with larger numbers is needed before regulatory extrapolation can be recommended.
