title: Withdrawal period modelling approaches for veterinary drug residues: a practical comparison of EMA CVMP, US FDA-CVM and Codex Alimentarius methods using a common cattle enrofloxacin depletion dataset
abstract: Three regulatory methods for withdrawal period calculation—the EMA CVMP Guideline EMEA/CVMP/473/98 tolerance interval regression, the US FDA-CVM statistical approach, and the Codex Alimentarius Commission Veterinary Drug Residues in Food (CCRVDF) guideline—were applied to an identical pooled cattle dataset of 96 animals slaughtered at eight time points after enrofloxacin treatment. Results were compared for muscle, liver, kidney, and fat using the combined enrofloxacin + ciprofloxacin marker residue. The EMA method yielded the most conservative estimates (kidney 22 days), followed by the Codex method (21 days) and FDA (19 days). Differences narrowed when datasets were balanced across slaughter times. The sensitivity of each method to unequal group sizes and to log-normality assumptions was explored by parametric bootstrap (1,000 replicates). The analysis provides a quantitative basis for understanding divergences in label withdrawal periods for the same product across different regulatory jurisdictions and is intended as a teaching resource for postgraduate students in veterinary pharmacology.

title: Effect of body condition score on marbofloxacin pharmacokinetics and predicted tissue residue depletion in beef cattle at slaughter weight
abstract: Lipophilicity of fluoroquinolones suggests that body composition may affect distribution and depletion, yet most PK studies use animals of average condition. Twenty-four Simmental steers were classified as lean (BCS 2.0–2.5, n = 8), moderate (BCS 3.0–3.5, n = 8), or over-conditioned (BCS 4.0–4.5, n = 8) and each received marbofloxacin 2 mg/kg BW SC as a single dose. Serial blood samples were taken over 96 h; animals were slaughtered at day 12 for muscle and kidney residues. Vd/F increased with BCS (1.41, 1.68, and 1.94 L/kg for lean, moderate, and over-conditioned groups respectively; P = 0.009), while clearance did not differ significantly. Terminal plasma half-life was prolonged in over-conditioned animals (9.2 vs. 6.8 h in lean; P = 0.014). Muscle residues at day 12 exceeded the EU MRL in 2 of 8 over-conditioned animals but in none of the other groups. Body condition score at treatment is proposed as a practical covariate that should be considered when assigning withdrawal periods on farm.

title: Spatial distribution of Toxoplasma gondii seroprevalence in backyard pigs across Vojvodina: a geographic information system analysis
abstract: GPS coordinates and seroprevalence data from 621 pigs on 89 farms sampled between 2009 and 2018 were integrated into a geographic information system to examine spatial clustering of T. gondii infection. Kernel density estimation and spatial scan statistics (SaTScan, Bernoulli model) identified two significant high-prevalence clusters: one in the Srem district along a river corridor (prevalence ratio 1.74, p = 0.002) and a secondary cluster in the northern Bačka district (prevalence ratio 1.52, p = 0.018). Land cover data from the Vojvodina geoportal were overlaid, revealing that farms within 500 m of forested parcels had significantly higher seroprevalence (35.6%) than farms in open agricultural landscapes (22.1%). Cat population density estimated from municipal registration records correlated positively with cluster membership. These spatial findings can inform targeted veterinary advisory programmes and prioritise farms for educational outreach.

title: Vokalski inventar šokačkih govora u okolini Sombora: preliminarni akustički nalaz
abstract: U radu se predstavlja akustička analiza vokalskog inventara govornika šokačkog vernakula iz tri sela u somborskoj opštini (Bački Breg, Gajić, Karapandža). Snimljeno je ukupno 34 govornika (18 žena, 16 muškaraca) različitih starosnih grupa, od kojih su svi aktivni dvojezičnici srpsko-mađarskog kontaktnog pojasa. Formantske vrednosti F1 i F2 ekstrahovane su programom Praat za 1.240 vokalskih tokena u akcentovanim slogovima. Rezultati pokazuju statistički značajno sužavanje vokalskog prostora kod govornika mlađih od 45 godina u poređenju sa najstarijim informatorima: prosečna F1 vrednost za /a/ snižena je za 18 Hz, dok /e/ i /o/ pokazuju tendenciju centralizacije prema šva. Diskutuje se o mogućoj interferentnoj ulozi mađarskog vokalskog sistema kao okidača za ove promene, uz napomenu da je unutardijalekatska varijacija unutar samog šokačkog korpusa i dalje znatna.

title: Bunjevački govor Subotice u drugoj deceniji 21. veka: stanje i perspektive
abstract: Rada se bavi aktuelnim stanjem bunjevačkog vernakula u Subotici, zasnovanim na korpusu od 47 sociolingvistički stratifikovanih intervjua sprovedenih između 2013. i 2015. godine. Analizira se distribucija specifičnih bunjevačkih fonetskih obeležja — ikavskog refleksa jata, posebnog tretmana sekundarnog jata, i karakteristične intonacione konture — u govoru različitih generacija. Podaci ukazuju na ubrzano nestajanje ikavizama u govoru govornika mlađih od 35 godina, dok je intonaciona kontura nešto stabilnija. Diskutuju se socijalni faktori koji ubrzavaju ili usporavaju atricion: mestimično snažan lokalni identitet vezan za bunjevačku tradiciju deluje kao faktor usporavanja promene, dok visoko obrazovanje i geografska mobilnost ubrzavaju konvergenciju prema standardnom novoštokavskom. Rad doprinosi razumevanju mehanizama jeziŽke promene u urbanim manjinskim sredinama.

title: Vowel Reduction in Contact: Evidence from Hungarian-Serbian Bilinguals in Bačka
abstract: Using a forced-choice auditory perception experiment alongside production data, this study investigates whether vowel reduction patterns in Šokac and Bunjevac vernaculars are perceptually salient to both community members and external listeners. Sixty-four participants—divided into four groups based on vernacular background and Hungarian-Serbian bilingualism—listened to 96 stimuli drawn from spontaneous speech recordings. Stimuli contrasted reduced versus full realizations of /e/ and /o/ in unstressed syllables. Results from signal detection theory analysis show that community-internal listeners exhibit significantly higher sensitivity (d′ = 2.18) to the reduced variants than external Serbian monolingual listeners (d′ = 0.83), suggesting that reduced vowels carry sociolinguistic meaning within the community. Production data from a subset of 28 speakers confirm that reduction correlates positively with Hungarian language dominance (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). The findings are discussed in terms of perceptual learning and the role of social evaluation in maintaining or reversing contact-induced reduction.

title: Contact-Induced Vowel Centralization in Endangered Pannonian Vernaculars: A Cross-Community Comparison
abstract: This paper compares vowel centralization tendencies in three communities along the Hungarian-Serbian linguistic border in Bačka: a Šokac-speaking village, a Bunjevac-speaking peri-urban neighborhood in Subotica, and a mixed Serbian-Hungarian village with no inherited Šokac or Bunjevac substrate. Ultrasound tongue imaging (UTI) was used alongside acoustic analysis for a subset of 18 speakers to verify articulatory correlates of formant changes. The data show a gradient pattern: centralization is strongest in the mixed community (mean Euclidean distance from cardinal vowel targets reduced by 31%), intermediate in the peri-urban Bunjevac group (19%), and weakest in the rural Šokac community (9%). Acoustic and articulatory data converge, confirming that the formant shifts correspond to genuine reduction of tongue body movement rather than to laryngeal adjustments. The cross-community comparison supports an intensity-of-contact model over a speaker-age model: contact frequency predicts centralization better than generation (β = 0.54 vs. β = 0.31 in mixed-effects regression).

title: Stavovi govornika prema bunjevačkom i šokačkom vernakulu: sociolingvistička anketa u Bačkoj
abstract: Istraživanje ispituje jezičke stavove prema bunjevačkom i šokačkom vernakulu kod 183 ispitanika iz pet bačkih opština, anketiranih u periodu od 2020. do 2022. godine. Primenjen je standardizovani upitnik tipa Likertove skale koji pokriva dimenzije prestiža, korisnosti, etničke autentičnosti i estetske vrednosti vernakula. Faktorska analiza identifikuje dva robusna faktora: 'lokalni identitet' i 'institucionalni prestiž'. Govornici starijih generacija konzistentno pripisuju vernakulu visoke vrednosti na dimenziji etničke autentičnosti, dok mlađi ispitanici s višim obrazovanjem vrednost vernakula ocenjuju niže na skali prestiža. Poređenje stavova između bunjevačke i šokačke zajednice pokazuje statistički značajnu razliku na dimenziji 'institucionalni prestiž' (p = 0,003), što se dovodi u vezu s razlikama u statusu ove dve zajednice u okviru vojvođanskog manjinskog zakonodavstva.

title: Automatic Forced Alignment of Bačka Šokac Speech: Challenges and Interim Results
abstract: Forced alignment of spontaneous dialect speech poses well-known difficulties due to phonological divergence from the standard language variety on which most alignment models are trained. This paper reports on an ongoing effort to adapt an existing Serbian forced aligner (based on a Kaldi acoustic model trained on broadcast news) to Šokac vernacular speech from the NovSadDialCorpus archive. A manually aligned reference set of 4.8 hours was prepared by two trained phoneticians (inter-annotator agreement κ = 0.81 for vowel boundaries). Alignment accuracy of the baseline model was 52% of segment boundaries within 20 ms of the manual reference. After fine-tuning on 1.2 hours of manually annotated Šokac data, accuracy rose to 71%. Key remaining challenges include the reduced vowels specific to the dialect, which the model systematically merges with adjacent consonant closures. The paper proposes a set of pronunciation dictionary modifications that could improve performance without full retraining.

title: Generational Transmission of Phonological Features in Šokac Families: A Panel Study
abstract: Intergenerational transmission of dialect features is one of the key mechanisms through which contact-induced change either persists or is reversed. This paper presents results from a panel study of 14 three-generation Šokac families in four villages in the Apatin and Sombor municipalities. Each family contributed recordings from a grandparent (mean age 74), a parent (mean age 49), and an adult grandchild (mean age 24), collected in 2015 and re-recorded in 2023. We track six phonological variables: three vowel quality targets, word-initial accent placement, the realization of final /l/, and yat reflexes. Generational attrition is clearest for word-initial accent placement and yat reflexes, while final /l/ vocalization and one vowel quality variable show stable transmission. The panel design reveals several cases of apparent reversal between the 2015 and 2023 recordings, interpreted as stylistic indexing of vernacular identity in interaction with the researcher rather than genuine phonological change.

title: Leksičke pozajmljenice mađarskog porekla u šokačkim i bunjevačkim govorima: fonetska adaptacija i stepen udomaćenosti
abstract: Rad analizira 340 leksičkih pozajmljenica mađarskog porekla ekstrahovanih iz dijalekatskog korpusa Katedre za srpski jezik i lingvistiku, s ciljem da utvrdi obrasce fonetske adaptacije i stepen njihove udomaćenosti u govornom repertoaru savremenih govornika. Pozajmljenice su klasifikovane prema fonetskim zonama adaptacije: vokalska harmonizacija, deaspiracija inicijalnih okluziva, i supstitucija mađarskih glasova koji nemaju korespondenta u srpskom fonološkom sistemu. Analiza pokazuje da mlađi govornici u proseku zadržavaju 47% izvornih mađarskih fonetskih obeležja u datim leksemama, dok stariji govornici zadržavaju svega 28%, što se tumači kao pokazatelj povećane fonetske kompetencije u mađarskom kod mlađih govornika, a ne kao fonetski konzervativizam. Detaljna lista od 120 najfrekventnijih pozajmljenica priložena je u vidu rečničkog aneksa.

title: Class Imbalance in Serbian Administrative Court Decisions: A Baseline Study
abstract: Administrative court rulings in Serbia exhibit a pronounced class imbalance: approximately 78% of decisions in a collected corpus of 3,400 documents belong to a single outcome category. This paper documents the construction of that corpus, covering rulings from 2005 to 2012, and evaluates five standard classifiers—naive Bayes, logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, and SVM—under original class distributions. F1-scores for minority classes fall below 0.21 across all methods when no resampling is applied. The paper analyses the linguistic and structural features most predictive of outcome, including citation patterns and procedural section length. Results serve as a reproducible baseline for subsequent resampling and augmentation experiments. All preprocessing code and anonymised metadata are released alongside the paper. The study intentionally avoids resampling or cost-sensitive learning so that future work can quantify gains relative to a clean reference point.

title: Back-Translation as Data Augmentation for Low-Resource Legal Sentence Classification
abstract: Legal sentence classification in low-resource Slavic languages is constrained by the scarcity of annotated data and the domain specificity of vocabulary. This paper investigates back-translation—translating Serbian sentences to English and back—as an augmentation strategy for a sentence-level dataset of 1,120 annotated clauses from civil procedure documents. Three translation pipelines are tested using freely available neural machine translation models, and the round-trip fidelity of legal terminology is measured against a manually curated glossary of 340 terms. Back-translation preserves legal term identity in 74% of cases for the best pipeline. Augmented training sets are used with a fine-tuned multilingual BERT model, yielding a macro F1 of 0.68 compared to 0.59 on the original data. Error analysis reveals that procedural verbs suffer the highest mistranslation rate, suggesting domain-adaptive fine-tuning of the translation component as a future direction. The dataset and annotation guidelines are publicly available.

title: Transfer Learning from General Croatian–Serbian Legal Texts to a Specialised Serbian Labour-Law Corpus
abstract: Transformer-based language models pretrained on large general corpora require substantial fine-tuning data to adapt to specialised legal domains. This paper examines whether intermediate pretraining on a moderately sized Croatian–Serbian legal text collection (approximately 120,000 sentences from publicly accessible legislation and court decisions) improves downstream performance on a Serbian labour-law classification task with only 640 training examples. Four model variants are compared: multilingual BERT with no intermediate pretraining, the same model with intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus, and two models pretrained on each national subset separately. Intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus achieves the best macro F1 (0.72) on a held-out test set of 160 examples, surpassing the no-pretraining baseline by 0.11. Differences between the Croatian-only and Serbian-only intermediate pretraining conditions are modest, suggesting that vocabulary overlap rather than syntactic similarity drives the gain. Computational cost and practical guidance for reproducing the pipeline on limited hardware are discussed.

title: Predicting Sequences of Procedural Outcomes in Serbian Civil Litigation Using Recurrent Models
abstract: Civil litigation in Serbia often involves multiple procedural stages, and the outcome of each stage influences the distribution of subsequent outcomes. This paper frames judicial decision sequences as a temporal classification problem and evaluates three recurrent architectures—vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU—on a dataset of 2,180 complete case trajectories spanning first instance, appeal, and revision stages. Each stage is represented by a combination of extracted text features and structured metadata (case type, duration, court tier). The dataset is severely imbalanced at the revision stage, where case types eligible for revision constitute only 9% of trajectories. Weighted cross-entropy and focal loss are compared as training objectives. The GRU with focal loss achieves a macro F1 of 0.61 at the revision stage, compared to 0.43 for weighted cross-entropy. Sequence length and court tier are identified as the strongest non-textual predictors via ablation. Limitations related to data availability outside the University's legal informatics collaboration are discussed.

title: A Survey of Synthetic Data Generation Methods for Small Legal Datasets
abstract: The application of machine learning to legal tasks is frequently limited by small annotated corpora and ethical constraints on data sharing. This chapter surveys methods for generating synthetic legal data, covering rule-based paraphrasing, conditional language model generation, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks adapted to text. For each method the chapter describes the underlying mechanism, summarises reported performance on legal benchmarks from the literature, and lists known failure modes, such as hallucinated case citations and vocabulary drift in conditional generation. Special attention is given to evaluation protocols, since standard NLP metrics such as BLEU and perplexity do not capture the legal validity of generated texts. The chapter concludes with a decision framework helping practitioners choose a generation strategy based on available corpus size, annotation type, and downstream task. Thirty-seven papers published between 2015 and 2022 are reviewed.

title: Cost-Sensitive Learning vs. Resampling: A Controlled Comparison on Four Serbian Legal Classification Tasks
abstract: Practitioners addressing class imbalance must choose between modifying the training objective and modifying the training set, but systematic comparisons on legal text data are rare. This paper applies seven resampling strategies (random oversampling, random undersampling, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, and two hybrid methods) and four cost-sensitive objectives (weighted cross-entropy, focal loss, asymmetric loss, and class-balanced softmax) to four Serbian legal classification tasks drawn from administrative, civil, criminal, and labour law subdomains. Corpus sizes range from 412 to 2,180 documents and imbalance ratios from 1:4 to 1:19. Results show no single strategy dominates across tasks; cost-sensitive objectives outperform resampling on the two smallest datasets, while hybrid resampling performs better on the two larger corpora. Statistical significance is assessed with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across cross-validation folds. The paper provides a reproducible experimental framework and releases all task-specific evaluation scripts.

title: Annotated corpus of Serbian electrical maintenance texts: construction methodology and baseline statistics
abstract: Reliable named entity recognition and relation extraction in the power-systems maintenance domain require annotated corpora that reflect the vocabulary and writing style of field personnel. This paper describes the construction of a 9,800-sentence corpus drawn from work orders, inspection reports, and incident summaries produced by two Serbian electricity distribution companies between 2008 and 2014. Annotation guidelines were defined to cover four entity types—equipment identifier, fault descriptor, location reference, and repair action—and two relation types: fault-equipment and action-equipment. A team of four annotators, including two electrical engineers and two computational linguists, performed the labelling using the BRAT annotation tool. Final inter-annotator kappa values ranged from 0.68 to 0.79 depending on entity type. The corpus contains 47,000 entity mentions and 31,000 labelled relation instances. Baseline results using a CRF tagger are reported, with an F1 of 0.73 for fault descriptors, which proved the most variable category. The corpus is released under a restricted-access licence pending operator approval.

title: Correlation between return voltage central time constant and moisture content in oil-impregnated pressboard specimens
abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between the central time constant extracted from return voltage measurements (RVM) and the water content in pressboard samples impregnated with mineral transformer oil. Fourteen laboratory specimens with moisture levels ranging from 0.5 % to 5.2 % by dry weight were prepared under controlled temperature conditions (20 °C ± 0.5 °C) and subjected to RVM using charging voltages of 500 V and 1000 V with charge times of 30 s, 100 s, and 300 s. The central time constant showed a monotonic increase with moisture content up to approximately 3.8 %, above which the relationship became less distinct, likely due to changes in oil conductivity at higher water concentrations. Karl Fischer titration of paper samples provided independent moisture reference values. The results confirm that the central time constant is a useful but moisture-range-limited indicator, and that systematic variation of charge-to-discharge time ratio improves discriminability between ageing-related and moisture-related polarisation mechanisms. Repeatability across three measurement series was within 4 %.

title: Frequency-domain dielectric spectroscopy of naturally aged transformer pressboard: a laboratory study
abstract: Pressboard strips were thermally aged at 110 °C, 130 °C, and 150 °C in sealed glass vessels containing new mineral oil, with ageing periods extending from 250 h to 3000 h. After ageing, the complex permittivity of each specimen was measured in the frequency range 0.1 mHz to 1 kHz using an impedance analyser. The degree of polymerisation (DP) of the cellulose was determined by viscometry as an independent ageing reference; DP values ranged from 1100 (unaged) down to 185 (most severely aged specimens). The imaginary part of permittivity at frequencies below 1 mHz exhibited a systematic increase with decreasing DP, while the real part changes were smaller in relative terms. A power-law fit to the low-frequency dispersion slope yielded an exponent that correlated with DP with a Pearson coefficient of −0.86 across the 42-specimen dataset. Oil conductivity was measured at each ageing stage and included as a covariate in the regression. The findings indicate that low-frequency loss angle is a more sensitive ageing marker than permittivity magnitude for pressboard at moisture contents below 2 %.

title: Effect of oil conductivity on the interpretation of polarisation and depolarisation current measurements in transformer insulation
abstract: Polarisation and depolarisation current (PDC) measurements were performed on oil-paper insulation models consisting of pressboard barriers immersed in mineral oils with three different conductivities: 0.3 pS/m, 2.1 pS/m, and 8.7 pS/m. Moisture content of the pressboard was held at three fixed levels (1 %, 2.5 %, and 4 % by dry weight). The experiment followed a full factorial design, yielding 27 test objects measured at 1000 V applied for 10 000 s. The oil conductivity was found to dominate the depolarisation current tail at times longer than 1000 s, which can mask the cellulose moisture signature in that time window. A correction procedure based on an iterative oil-conductivity extraction from the long-time polarisation current is proposed and validated against independent oil conductivity measurements. Application of the correction reduced the moisture estimation error from ±1.2 % to ±0.4 % absolute in the 1–4 % range. The study underlines the necessity of measuring oil conductivity separately before attempting moisture estimation from PDC data alone.

title: Dielectric response modelling of oil-paper insulation using a distributed RC ladder network with moisture-dependent parameters
abstract: A distributed RC ladder network model is developed to represent the dielectric response of oil-paper insulation over the frequency range 0.1 mHz to 1 kHz. Each cell of the ladder is assigned RC parameters derived from the measured complex permittivity of pressed cellulose boards at moisture contents between 0.5 % and 6 % at 20 °C. The model accounts for the separate contributions of oil conductivity, interfacial polarisation at oil-paper boundaries, and bulk relaxation within the cellulose matrix. Fitting of the model to measured frequency-domain spectra was performed using a nonlinear least-squares algorithm. The fitted parameters reproduced the measured spectra with a mean relative error below 3 % in the real part and 6 % in the imaginary part of permittivity. The same model was then transformed into the time domain and compared against independent polarisation current measurements on the same specimens, yielding agreement within experimental uncertainty. The model contains eight free parameters, which is fewer than competing multi-Debye approaches reported in the literature, while maintaining comparable fitting quality.

title: Field measurement campaign on distribution transformers: dielectric spectroscopy results versus maintenance records
abstract: Twelve oil-filled distribution transformers (10/0.4 kV, 250 kVA to 1000 kVA) operated by a regional electricity distributor in Vojvodina were subjected to frequency-domain dielectric spectroscopy measurements during scheduled outages between 2015 and 2016. Transformer ages ranged from 8 to 37 years. Measurements were carried out at 20 °C ± 3 °C with three temperature correction attempts based on Arrhenius-type shift factors. Oil samples were collected simultaneously and analysed for dissolved water content by Karl Fischer titration, dissolved gas content by gas chromatography, and acidity. For seven transformers, historical maintenance records including oil regeneration dates and previous dissolved gas analyses were available. The dielectric loss angle at 0.1 Hz correlated with transformer age (r = 0.74), but showed a weaker correlation with oil acidity (r = 0.51), suggesting that cellulose degradation and oil degradation do not necessarily progress in tandem in field units. Two transformers flagged as problematic by the model showed elevated furan compound concentrations in their oil, providing supplementary evidence of advanced cellulose ageing. Limitations of temperature correction in field conditions are discussed.

title: Comparison of XRD-derived crystallinity and dielectric relaxation parameters in thermally aged cellulose insulation
abstract: X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements were used to quantify the crystallinity index of cellulose paper samples aged at 120 °C for durations between 0 and 4000 h in the presence of uninhibited mineral oil. The crystallinity index, computed using the Segal method, increased from 0.68 in unaged paper to 0.81 after 4000 h, indicating progressive depolymerisation and recrystallisation of the amorphous regions. Frequency-domain dielectric spectra of the same samples were measured from 1 mHz to 10 kHz. The relaxation frequency of the dominant low-frequency dispersion peak shifted from approximately 0.8 mHz to 3.2 mHz over the same ageing range. A linear correlation between relaxation frequency and crystallinity index was established (r² = 0.91) across 36 specimens. The findings suggest that the shift in relaxation frequency may serve as a proxy for structural changes in the cellulose matrix. This study was motivated by the absence of direct structural data in most dielectric-only ageing studies and provides a physical basis for interpreting spectroscopic ageing indicators.

title: Insulation diagnostics of power transformers: dielectric methods and their practical application
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic account of time-domain and frequency-domain dielectric measurement methods applied to the condition assessment of oil-paper insulation in power transformers. The methods covered include capacitance and dissipation factor (tan δ) measurement at power frequency, polarisation and depolarisation current analysis, return voltage measurement, and broadband dielectric spectroscopy. For each method, the underlying polarisation mechanisms are described, the measurement protocol is outlined, and representative data from laboratory specimens and field transformers are presented. The chapter devotes particular attention to the problem of moisture and temperature cross-sensitivity, reviewing correction approaches from the literature and discussing their applicability ranges. A worked example using data from a 40 MVA, 110/35 kV autotransformer is included. The chapter is intended as an introduction for practising engineers and graduate students, and does not assume prior knowledge of dielectric physics beyond basic circuit theory.

title: Influence of winding geometry on the measured dielectric spectrum of power transformer insulation: a finite-element parametric study
abstract: The geometry of the insulation system in a power transformer—including oil duct widths, pressboard barrier thickness ratios, and electrode curvature—affects the measured dielectric spectrum in ways that are not always accounted for when using material-property-based interpretation models. A finite-element model of a simplified concentric winding arrangement was implemented, parameterised with frequency-dependent permittivity data measured on pressboard specimens at three moisture levels (1 %, 2 %, and 3.5 % by dry weight) and on mineral oil at three conductivity levels. The model geometry was varied across 16 configurations representing typical distribution and medium-power transformer designs. Simulated capacitance and loss angle spectra were computed at each geometry-material combination. The low-frequency loss angle was found to vary by up to 18 % between the most compact and most open geometries at identical material properties, a variation comparable to the moisture-induced shift in the 1–3.5 % moisture range. The implications for moisture estimation accuracy in field measurements are discussed, and a geometry correction factor expressed as a function of oil-duct fraction is proposed.

title: Moisture redistribution dynamics between oil and paper in transformer insulation during thermal cycling
abstract: The partitioning of water between mineral transformer oil and oil-impregnated pressboard changes with temperature because the equilibrium constant of the Fessler–Clark relation is temperature-dependent. This study tracked the dynamic redistribution experimentally using a sealed insulation model cell containing 150 g of oil and four pressboard specimens totalling 48 g dry weight. The cell was subjected to four thermal cycles between 20 °C and 80 °C with a ramp rate of 3 °C/h. At each of 11 temperature steps, oil samples were withdrawn and analysed for water content by Karl Fischer titration, and the complex permittivity of the pressboard specimens was measured in situ using embedded electrodes connected to the impedance analyser via feed-throughs. The measured permittivity at 1 mHz tracked the expected moisture content curve with a mean error of 0.18 % absolute moisture, based on recalculation using the equilibrium isotherm of Oommen. The results demonstrate that broadband dielectric spectroscopy can follow moisture redistribution over time scales of hours without disturbing the system, which is relevant to the interpretation of spectroscopic measurements performed at different ambient temperatures in the field.

title: Assessment of thermally upgraded paper insulation using frequency-domain dielectric spectroscopy: comparison with standard kraft paper
abstract: Thermally upgraded insulation paper (TUP), chemically modified by partial cyanoethylation to improve thermal stability, is increasingly used in new power transformers but its dielectric response differs from that of standard kraft paper. This study compares the frequency-domain dielectric spectra of TUP and kraft paper specimens aged in parallel under identical conditions: 130 °C in sealed vessels with new mineral oil, for ageing durations of 500 h, 1500 h, and 3000 h. At each ageing stage, moisture content was adjusted to 1 % and 3 % by controlled drying and re-humidification before spectroscopic measurement. TUP exhibited a higher real permittivity at low frequencies by 12–18 % compared with kraft paper at the same DP and moisture level. The imaginary part of permittivity, used for ageing assessment, showed a similar trend with DP for both paper types, but the absolute values for TUP were systematically lower by approximately 20 % in the 0.1–10 mHz range. The findings indicate that interpretation models calibrated on kraft paper will underestimate ageing severity when applied to TUP without recalibration. Separate calibration curves for each paper type are recommended.

title: Temperature-dependent dielectric spectroscopy of ester-oil-impregnated pressboard: implications for moisture assessment in ester-filled transformers
abstract: The adoption of natural and synthetic ester fluids in distribution transformers is increasing due to their higher fire point and biodegradability compared with mineral oil. Because ester fluids have higher inherent conductivity and water solubility than mineral oil, the dielectric response of ester-impregnated pressboard differs significantly from that of the mineral-oil-impregnated system. This study presents frequency-domain dielectric spectra of pressboard specimens impregnated with a commercial natural ester fluid (based on refined sunflower oil) and a pentaerythritol synthetic ester, measured at 10 °C, 20 °C, 40 °C, and 60 °C, at moisture levels of 1 %, 2 %, and 4 % by dry weight. Activation energies for the main relaxation process were determined from Arrhenius fits to the shift factors; values for ester-impregnated specimens were 0.72–0.81 eV, compared with 0.61–0.69 eV for mineral-oil-impregnated specimens at the same moisture levels. Existing temperature correction procedures calibrated for mineral oil were found to introduce errors of up to 0.8 % absolute moisture when applied to ester-impregnated systems. A revised set of activation energies specific to the two ester types is proposed and validated on a separate test set of 12 specimens.

title: Tractable Model for Millimeter-Wave Backhaul Links in Heterogeneous Networks with Random Blockage
abstract: This paper presents a stochastic geometry-based framework for evaluating the performance of millimeter-wave backhaul links in a two-tier network where small-cell base stations relay traffic to macro-cell donors over a 60 GHz channel. Building blockages are modeled using a random rectangular obstacle process with parameters derived from OpenStreetMap building footprint data for the central district of Novi Sad. A Boolean model is used to characterize blockage probability as a function of link distance. The paper derives a coverage probability expression for the backhaul tier that accounts for directional beamforming with sector antenna patterns, blockage-induced path-loss transitions, and co-tier interference from other small cells. Simulation results for blockage densities between 200 and 600 buildings per square kilometer show that the blockage process reduces effective backhaul capacity by 30–55% relative to an unobstructed scenario. The model is parameterized for three building density regimes corresponding to city center, suburban, and industrial zones.

title: Bias Analysis of MUSIC-Based DOA Estimation for Small Uniform Linear Arrays in Correlated Noise Fields
abstract: This work investigates the statistical bias of the MUSIC (Multiple Signal Classification) algorithm when applied to uniform linear arrays of four to eight elements under spatially correlated noise. Correlated noise is modelled using an exponential covariance structure with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.1 to 0.9. Theoretical bias expressions are derived using first-order perturbation analysis of the noise subspace and are validated through Monte Carlo simulations comprising 10 000 independent trials per scenario. Results show that even moderate correlation (coefficient 0.4) causes a mean angular bias of 1.2° to 3.7° depending on source separation and snapshot count, which is significant for arrays with apertures below 0.5 m at 2.4 GHz. The paper identifies the snapshot-to-element ratio as the dominant factor controlling bias growth and proposes a simple diagnostic criterion for determining when standard MUSIC results are unreliable without applying corrections.

title: Resolution Probability of Root-MUSIC for Two Closely Spaced Sources on a Four-Element Array
abstract: Root-MUSIC places the DOA estimation problem in the complex polynomial domain and can offer resolution improvements over spectral MUSIC for small arrays, but its behaviour with very few elements under correlated noise is not thoroughly characterised. This study derives an expression for the probability of resolution as a function of source separation, SNR, snapshot count, and noise correlation coefficient for a four-element array receiving two uncorrelated and correlated sources. Resolution is defined by the criterion that both polynomial roots closer to the unit circle are within 1° of the true angles. Analytical predictions are compared with simulation results over 20 000 trials. For the uncorrelated case, analytical and simulated resolution probabilities agree within 3 percentage points. Under noise correlation 0.6, resolution probability drops by 18–25 percentage points relative to the uncorrelated case at separations below 8°. Practical guidelines for array designers are derived from the results.

title: Measuring Unaided Brand Recall Among Spectators at Amateur Volleyball Tournaments: A Pilot Survey in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper reports on a pilot study examining unaided brand recall among 214 spectators attending four amateur volleyball club matches in Vojvodina during the 2011–2012 season. No television coverage was associated with any of the events. A structured post-match questionnaire adapted from established memory-measurement instruments was administered to attendees aged 18–55. Results indicate that unaided recall rates for pitch-side banner sponsors averaged 18.4 percent, with meaningful variation depending on banner placement zone and sponsor category. Local food and beverage brands were recalled at roughly twice the rate of financial services sponsors. The study establishes baseline recall benchmarks for low-media sports contexts in the region and highlights methodological challenges in conducting fieldwork at venues with no formal spectator registration. Findings suggest that product–event category fit modulates recall even when media amplification is absent.

title: Sponsor–Event Congruence and Its Effect on Recognition Memory: Evidence from a Regional Handball League
abstract: Using a 2×2 between-subjects experiment embedded in a post-match survey (n = 312), this study tests whether perceived fit between a sponsor's product category and a handball event influences recognition memory for sponsor brand names one week after attendance. Participants were spectators at six matches in the Vojvodina Regional Handball League during the 2013 spring season; none of the matches received television or paid online streaming coverage. Sponsors were real local brands whose identities were known to the researcher but masked for analytical purposes using fictitious labels. High-congruence sponsors showed a 23-percentage-point advantage in delayed recognition over low-congruence sponsors. Involvement with handball moderated the congruence effect, with high-involvement attendees showing smaller congruence benefits, consistent with elaboration arguments in the sponsorship literature. Practical implications for small clubs seeking locally relevant sponsors are discussed.

title: Does Sponsor Prominence Compensate for Poor Congruence? A Field Study at Domestic Athletics Meetings
abstract: Previous laboratory research suggests that high banner prominence can offset low sponsor–event fit on recall measures, but field evidence from non-televised events remains scarce. This study reports data collected at eight athletics meetings held in Serbia and northern Croatia between May and September 2014 (total n = 487 spectators). Prominence was operationalised through banner size, repetition count, and positioning relative to the finish line. A hierarchical regression framework was used, controlling for event involvement, prior brand familiarity, and attendance frequency. Neither size nor repetition compensated for perceived fit mismatches on unaided recall measured immediately after each event. Prominence did improve aided recognition but only modestly and primarily for sponsors already rated as moderately congruent. The results caution against over-reliance on size and frequency as proxies for sponsorship effectiveness in low-coverage sports contexts.

title: Congruence Cues in Low-Budget Sponsorship: A Qualitative Study of Club Managers and Local Sponsors in Serbia
abstract: Quantitative recall studies leave open the question of how sponsorship partnerships are actually selected and communicated in resource-constrained environments. This paper presents findings from 22 semi-structured interviews conducted in 2015 with club marketing managers and company representatives from small and medium-sized enterprises sponsoring non-televised sports clubs in Serbia. Thematic analysis reveals that congruence is rarely evaluated formally; partnerships are typically initiated through personal networks and ratified by goodwill considerations rather than strategic fit assessments. Club managers describe congruence primarily in geographic terms—local companies sponsoring local clubs—rather than product–activity terms. Sponsors express difficulty verifying any recall or awareness effects given the absence of media coverage. The paper proposes a simplified congruence assessment checklist tailored to clubs operating outside mainstream broadcast markets, intended as a practical complement to existing theoretical frameworks.

title: Memory Encoding for Sponsor Brands Among Occasional versus Regular Attendees: A Study Across Three Sports
abstract: This paper reports the doctoral-stage empirical work examining how attendance frequency shapes the encoding of sponsor brand information at live sports events with no media coverage. Data were collected from 641 spectators across handball, basketball, and rowing events in Vojvodina and the Banat region during the 2015–2016 season. Participants were classified as occasional (fewer than four events per season), regular (four to twelve), or frequent (more than twelve) attendees using self-report. A multivariate analysis of covariance controlling for sponsor familiarity and event involvement showed a significant attendance frequency × congruence interaction: regular attendees benefited most from high-congruence placements, while frequent attendees showed ceiling effects on both aided and unaided recall regardless of congruence level. Occasional attendees showed no significant congruence advantage. Implications for sponsor targeting and contract structuring are discussed.

title: Sponsorship Congruence in Online-Streamed Amateur Sport: Does Low-Budget Digital Coverage Change the Recall Picture?
abstract: Between 2017 and 2019, a growing number of Serbian amateur sports clubs began streaming matches on free video platforms using smartphones and basic cameras. This study compares brand recall among 198 live attendees and 211 online viewers of the same eight handball and futsal matches during the 2018–2019 season. Both groups completed identical post-event recall questionnaires. Unaided recall rates for in-venue sponsors were lower among online viewers (11.2%) than live attendees (19.8%), but sponsor congruence predicted recall significantly in both groups. The congruence advantage was proportionally larger for online viewers, suggesting that fit may serve as a stronger encoding cue when visual clarity is limited. Duration of viewing and device type (mobile vs. desktop) did not moderate results. The paper discusses implications for clubs considering low-cost streaming as a complementary sponsorship channel.

title: Sponsor Recall Decay Over a 30-Day Window Following a Non-Televised Sports Event
abstract: Most sponsorship recall research measures memory immediately after exposure or within a few days. This study tracks recall decay over a 30-day period using a panel of 168 spectators recruited at three water polo matches in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin in September 2020. Participants completed unaided and aided recall questionnaires at day 0, day 7, day 14, and day 30 via an online survey system, with a 74.4 percent retention rate at day 30. Unaided recall dropped from a mean of 22.1 percent at day 0 to 9.4 percent at day 30; aided recognition fell from 61.3 percent to 38.7 percent over the same window. High-congruence sponsors showed significantly slower decay on both measures. Regression analyses indicate that congruence explains an additional 11 percent of variance in day-30 unaided recall beyond day-0 recall, event involvement, and brand familiarity. Findings suggest that congruence may have a protective effect on longer-term memory traces.

title: Perceived Authenticity of Local Sponsors and Its Interaction with Congruence on Brand Attitude Formation
abstract: This study examines whether sponsor authenticity perceptions—defined as the extent to which a sponsor is seen as genuinely committed to a local community—moderate the relationship between sponsor–event congruence and post-event brand attitude. A survey of 388 spectators attending rowing, cycling, and athletics club events across Vojvodina in 2022 measured congruence perceptions, authenticity, and brand attitude using adapted Likert scales. Structural equation modelling with a latent interaction term indicates that authenticity strengthens the positive effect of congruence on brand attitude (standardised interaction coefficient = 0.21, p < 0.01). When authenticity perceptions are low, even high-congruence sponsors achieve only modest attitude gains. The effect size is comparable across the three sports. The paper connects sponsorship congruence theory to place-based identity literature and discusses how clubs might communicate sponsor authenticity to attendees through pre-event channels.

title: Cross-Category Sponsorship Portfolios in Regional Sport: Do Multiple Low-Congruence Sponsors Collectively Impair Brand Recall?
abstract: Many small sports clubs in Serbia carry between eight and fifteen sponsors simultaneously, often with inconsistent product–event fit across the portfolio. This paper investigates whether portfolio-level congruence—operationalised as the mean and variance of individual sponsor congruence ratings—predicts overall recall performance better than any single sponsor's congruence score. Data were gathered from 502 spectators at 14 matches across four sports (handball, basketball, futsal, volleyball) in Vojvodina during the 2023–2024 season. Multilevel modelling with sponsors nested within events and events nested within clubs reveals that high variance in portfolio congruence significantly depresses recall for all sponsors in the portfolio, including those individually rated as high-congruence. Mean portfolio congruence has an independent positive effect. Results suggest that adding a poorly fitting sponsor can damage recall for already-established sponsors. A practical scoring instrument for portfolio congruence assessment is proposed and described.

title: Naming Rights in Amateur Facilities: Recall and Attitude Effects When the Arena Name Changes for a Local Sponsor
abstract: Facility naming rights are typically studied in the context of professional sport and large arenas. This preprint presents a quasi-experimental study tracking recall and brand attitude before and after a naming rights deal was signed between a regional food manufacturer and an indoor sports hall used by amateur basketball and volleyball clubs in a mid-sized Vojvodina town. Surveys were administered to 273 regular attendees at baseline (six months before renaming), and again at three and nine months post-renaming. Unaided recall for the sponsor brand rose from 14.1 percent at baseline to 39.4 percent at nine months. Brand attitude improved modestly (mean shift of 0.38 on a 7-point scale). Subgroup analysis indicates that attendees who rated the sponsor as locally authentic showed approximately twice the attitude gain of those with lower authenticity perceptions. Congruence ratings remained stable across waves, suggesting naming rights alone do not change fit perceptions.

title: Salesperson Autonomy, CRM Mandate Strength, and Adaptive Selling: A Multi-Level Study Across Industrial Sectors in Serbia
abstract: This study investigated how firm-level CRM mandate strength moderates the individual-level relationship between salesperson autonomy and adaptive selling behaviour, using multi-level modelling on data from 267 sales representatives nested within 34 industrial firms in Serbia. CRM mandate strength was operationalised as a composite of managerial enforcement frequency, CRM activity KPIs in performance reviews, and IT access restrictions. Salesperson autonomy was measured with an adapted 5-item scale. At the individual level, autonomy was positively associated with adaptive selling (γ = 0.31, p < 0.001). This relationship was significantly attenuated in firms with high CRM mandate strength (cross-level interaction γ = −0.18, p < 0.05), suggesting that prescriptive CRM governance partially constrains the adaptive flexibility typically enabled by autonomy. Sector-level differences were observed, with the attenuation effect largest in logistics and smallest in machinery sales. The paper contributes to debates about whether CRM systems support or constrain sales force adaptiveness.

title: Fatigue stress spectra in angle-section members of a 110 kV transmission tower under simulated turbulent wind
abstract: Steel lattice transmission towers carry repetitive wind-induced loads throughout their service lives, yet most design codes treat fatigue only implicitly. This paper presents a simulation-based methodology for deriving fatigue stress spectra at critical bracing joints of a 110 kV single-circuit tower typical of the Vojvodina plain. A three-dimensional finite-element model was loaded with a 10-minute stationary turbulent wind time series generated by the spectral representation method using a Kaimal power spectral density and a mean wind speed of 18 m/s at the tower tip. Dynamic analysis by modal superposition retained the first eight modes. Rainflow cycle counting was applied to stress histories at 24 cross-section locations identified by preliminary static analysis as hotspots. The resulting stress-range histograms showed that 94 % of cycles fell below 20 MPa, but a tail of high-amplitude cycles above 60 MPa contributed disproportionately to Miner's damage sum. The accumulated damage index for a 40-year exposure period was estimated at 0.31 for the governing joint, indicating adequate design margin under current loading. Sensitivity to terrain roughness category is also discussed.

title: Effect of joint eccentricity on hot-spot stress concentration in bolted lattice tower connections
abstract: Angle-section members in transmission towers are routinely connected with a single bolt row, introducing eccentricity and secondary bending moments that elevate local stresses at hole edges. Finite-element sub-models of three representative bolted lap joints taken from a 220 kV double-circuit tower were analysed using three-dimensional solid elements with mesh refinement at hole boundaries. Stress concentration factors (SCFs) were extracted following the surface extrapolation procedure of IIW recommendations. Eccentricity increased the SCF at the net-section by 1.28 to 1.61 depending on the leg length ratio and number of bolts. An analytical correction formula dependent on slenderness and eccentricity ratio was fitted to the parametric numerical data with a root-mean-square error of 4.2 %. Application of the corrected SCFs in a fatigue assessment following EN 1993-1-9 detail category 71 reduced the estimated remaining life of an in-service tower from 52 to 34 years. The study recommends that design standards explicitly account for eccentric load transfer in lattice tower fatigue checks.

title: Comparison of wind load models for fatigue assessment of tall lattice structures in flat terrain
abstract: Regulatory wind load models for transmission towers in Serbia and neighbouring countries differ in their turbulence intensity profiles, gust factors, and spatial coherence assumptions. This conference paper compares fatigue damage estimates obtained with three models: the quasi-static gust-factor approach of SRPS EN 1991-1-4, a frequency-domain buffeting model following Davenport's formulation, and time-domain Monte Carlo simulation using a digital filtering technique. A 35 m guyed lattice tower in open flat terrain with a 50-year mean wind of 26 m/s was chosen as the reference structure. For the governing leg member, the 50-year fatigue damage index differed by a factor of 2.4 between the quasi-static and time-domain approaches, the former being unconservative relative to the latter. The frequency-domain method gave results within 12 % of the time-domain benchmark. The quasi-static approach is deemed unsuitable for fatigue calculations even in flat terrain because it does not resolve cycle amplitude distributions correctly.

title: Rainflow counting under non-stationary wind: a moving-window approach applied to measured tower strains
abstract: Standard rainflow counting assumes stationary load histories, an assumption violated during thunderstorm downburst or passage of a frontal system. Strain gauge records collected over 18 months on an operational 110 kV lattice tower in the Bačka region showed 23 episodes with clearly non-stationary characteristics identified by a Priestley evolutionary spectral test. A moving-window rainflow procedure was implemented in which the window length was adapted to local stationarity intervals estimated by the Augmented Dickey–Fuller test. Fatigue damage accumulations were compared between the standard and adaptive methods. For stationary wind episodes the two methods agreed within 3 %. For non-stationary episodes the adaptive method gave damage values up to 38 % higher than the standard approach, suggesting that simple long-record counting underestimates damage from transient high-amplitude bursts. The paper proposes a correction factor table indexed by turbulence intensity and non-stationarity indicator for use when full adaptive processing is not available.

title: Fracture mechanics-based remaining life prediction for a cracked diagonal brace in a lattice tower
abstract: A diagonal brace member in a 40-year-old 110 kV tower on a wind-exposed site in western Vojvodina was found during routine inspection to carry a surface crack 4.2 mm deep at a gusset plate weld toe. This paper applies linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM) to estimate the remaining service life from the detected crack size to a critical size determined by net-section yielding. The Paris–Erdogan crack growth law was calibrated using literature data for S235 structural steel. The stress intensity factor range ΔK was computed by weight function integration over the measured stress spectra from a companion monitoring campaign. Three inspection scenarios were analysed: no further action, repair at 6 mm crack depth, and immediate repair. Predicted remaining lives were 4.1, 9.7, and full life restoration, respectively. Sensitivity analysis showed that the Paris exponent m was the dominant uncertainty source, contributing 61 % of total variance in the remaining life estimate by a first-order reliability method. The results were used to prioritise a maintenance schedule for the operator's tower portfolio.

title: Fatigue assessment of transmission towers: methods, data needs, and code gaps
abstract: This book chapter surveys the state of practice in fatigue assessment of steel lattice transmission towers, with emphasis on the gap between what structural standards require and what is needed for a realistic remaining-life estimate. The chapter covers the load characterisation problem including wind climatology, turbulence modelling, and the treatment of correlated loading from conductor galloping and ice shedding. Structural modelling aspects are addressed: member buckling interaction effects, joint flexibility, and conductor–tower coupling. Damage accumulation methods are reviewed from simple linear Miner summation through non-linear damage models to probabilistic approaches. A critical comparison of the relevant provisions of EN 1993-1-9, IEC 60826, and the CIGRÉ TB 328 guide is included. The chapter concludes with a discussion of monitoring-informed assessment and identifies specific gaps in current codes regarding hot-spot classification for angle-section joints and the statistical treatment of inspection findings. The intended audience is practising engineers and researchers involved in asset management of aging transmission infrastructure.

title: Influence of conductor bundling configuration on wind-induced dynamic response and fatigue loading of a 400 kV lattice tower
abstract: High-voltage transmission towers increasingly carry bundled conductors to reduce corona losses, but the aerodynamic interaction between conductor bundles and tower members under turbulent wind is not well characterised in design guidelines. This paper develops a coupled conductor–tower model for a 400 kV suspension tower with twin-bundle conductors using a co-simulation approach: conductor motion is computed by a geometrically nonlinear cable dynamics module, and the resulting time-varying attachment-point forces are fed as input to the tower finite-element model. Wind speed series at conductor attachment points were generated with spatial coherence based on measured values from a wind mast at the site. Results show that twin-bundle configurations introduce a 15–22 % increase in stress-range amplitude at the crossarm-to-leg connection compared with an equivalent single-conductor model, and fatigue damage at this location increased by a factor of 1.31 over a simulated 30-year exposure. The finding suggests that bundle configuration should be explicitly included in the fatigue input for crossarm design.

title: Probabilistic fatigue life assessment using Bayesian updating of Paris law parameters from periodic inspections
abstract: Periodic visual and magnetic particle inspections of steel lattice towers yield crack depth data at discrete time points. This paper demonstrates how those inspection records can be used to update prior distributions of Paris–Erdogan crack growth parameters within a Bayesian framework, progressively narrowing the uncertainty in remaining life predictions. The methodology is applied to a portfolio of 17 towers of the same design operated by a regional electricity company in Vojvodina, with inspection data spanning 12 years and four inspection rounds. A Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm (Metropolis–Hastings) with 200 000 samples was used for posterior sampling. After the fourth inspection round, the coefficient of variation on predicted remaining life decreased from 0.61 to 0.29 for the tower sub-fleet with the most complete records. The posterior mean remaining life for the governing joint in the most damaged tower was 7.2 years, leading the operator to advance the planned replacement of six towers. The approach is computationally modest and can be implemented with standard statistical software.

title: Low-cost accelerometer-based system for fatigue-relevant dynamic monitoring of transmission towers: field validation
abstract: Continuous strain monitoring of transmission towers at many locations is cost-prohibitive for routine asset management. This paper describes a low-cost monitoring system built around MEMS accelerometers and a Raspberry Pi data logger that estimates fatigue-relevant stress ranges at uninstrumented cross-sections via a modal expansion technique. Six MEMS nodes were deployed on a 35 m lattice tower in the Srem district for a period of eight months. Modal parameters were identified by the Stochastic Subspace Identification method applied to 10-minute ambient vibration records. A calibration matrix relating accelerometer signals to stress ranges at seven previously strain-gauged hotspots was derived by regression against a two-week overlap period when both sensor types operated simultaneously. The reconstructed stress ranges agreed with strain-gauge reference values within 9 % for the five most-excited modes. Estimated fatigue damage accumulated over the eight-month period differed by less than 14 % from the direct strain-gauge baseline. Hardware cost per node was approximately 85 EUR, making dense deployment realistic for portfolio-level monitoring.

title: Effect of corrosion-induced cross-section loss on fatigue crack initiation life in angle members of aging towers
abstract: Corrosion reduces the net cross-section of angle members and roughens the surface, both of which affect fatigue performance, yet most remaining-life assessments treat corrosion and fatigue as independent processes. This paper presents a combined model in which annual thickness loss follows a power-law corrosion model calibrated to gravimetric measurements on 42 coupons retrieved from decommissioned towers across Vojvodina with exposure ages of 20 to 48 years. The evolving net section and elevated surface roughness were used to update both the applied stress range and the fatigue notch factor at each year of a simulated 60-year service life. Crack initiation life, defined as a 0.5 mm surface crack, was computed by the strain-life (ε-N) approach with Morrow mean-stress correction. Compared with a no-corrosion baseline, corrosion at the median measured rate reduced the crack initiation life by 31 %. At the 90th-percentile corrosion rate, the reduction reached 52 %. The results indicate that corrosion protection maintenance intervals have a first-order effect on fatigue performance in high-humidity micro-climates near waterways.

title: Wind climate change projections and their implications for the residual fatigue life of the Vojvodina transmission network
abstract: Regional climate projections for the Pannonian Basin under RCP 8.5 suggest a modest increase in extreme wind speeds and a shift in the seasonal distribution of storm events by mid-century. This preprint translates three downscaled wind climate datasets from the EURO-CORDEX ensemble into fatigue loading time series for a representative 110 kV tower. For each of twelve regional climate model runs, 30-year synthetic wind records were generated for the periods 2020–2049 and 2050–2079 and compared with a historical baseline from 1990–2019 derived from ERA5 reanalysis. Fatigue damage accumulation was computed by the frequency-domain buffeting method. The multi-model median showed an increase in annual fatigue damage of 8 % for 2050–2079 relative to the historical period, with a 5–95 percentile spread of −4 % to +23 %. The spread was dominated by inter-model variability in the frequency of westerly storm tracks rather than changes in mean wind speed. The results are preliminary and the full study incorporating updated conductor loading is in preparation for journal submission.

title: Bayesian updating of creep model parameters using bridge monitoring data
abstract: Structural health monitoring generates time series of strain and deflection that can be used to progressively update prior estimates of material model parameters. This study demonstrates Bayesian updating of the two principal parameters of the EC2 creep compliance function — β_H and φ_RH — using deflection data from an instrumented prestressed concrete bridge in Sremska Mitrovica monitored over 48 months. A Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm with 100 000 samples was implemented in Python. Prior distributions were set according to the EC2 model's nominal parameter ranges. After incorporating the first 12 months of monitoring data the posterior mean of φ_RH was 8 % lower than the EC2 default for the relevant humidity class. After 48 months the posterior 95 % credible interval had narrowed by a factor of 2.6 relative to the prior. The updated parameters were used to project deflections 10 years ahead, yielding predictions with 22 % tighter confidence bounds than EC2 default calculations.

title: Thermal gradient effects on apparent creep measurements in instrumented bridge girders
abstract: Vibrating-wire strain gauges embedded in concrete bridge girders record composite deformations that include mechanical strain, temperature-dependent strain, and instrument thermal output error. Failure to properly separate these components introduces systematic bias into apparent creep measurements. This paper quantifies the bias by analysing data from a simply supported prestressed concrete girder bridge monitored continuously from 2016 to 2020. The structure crosses a floodplain and experiences seasonal temperature gradients of up to 14 °C through the girder depth. Three separation schemes of increasing sophistication — a single-temperature correction, a gradient-corrected scheme, and a full thermoelastic finite element correction — are compared. The thermoelastic correction reduced the apparent creep coefficient at 48 months from 2.14 to 1.87, a 13 % reduction. The simpler single-temperature correction achieved only a 6 % reduction. The findings indicate that thermal gradient corrections are essential for any monitoring programme used to calibrate creep models.

title: Probabilistic Assessment of Punching Shear Capacity in Flat Slabs: Combining Core Sample Statistics with CSCT-Based Resistance Models
abstract: Structural assessment of existing flat slabs involves material properties characterised by limited and spatially variable data. This paper develops a probabilistic framework that combines material parameters derived from core sampling campaigns—concrete compressive strength, aggregate maximum size, and effective depth—with the CSCT resistance model to produce column-level capacity distributions. Monte Carlo simulation with 100,000 samples per column location was used, with input distributions calibrated from 63 cores extracted from three Vojvodina car parks (also described in a 2021 companion study). The probability of punching capacity being below the factored applied shear was computed for each of 63 column locations; seven locations exceeded a reference failure probability of 10⁻³, compared with only three flagged by a deterministic assessment using mean material properties. Sensitivity analysis identified concrete compressive strength and effective depth as the dominant uncertainty sources, jointly accounting for 74 % of output variance. The framework is compatible with standard structural reliability formats and can be implemented in spreadsheet tools without specialist software.

title: Critical weed-free period in sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.) under two nitrogen fertilisation levels
abstract: A two-year field experiment (2010–2011) at Rimski Šančevi evaluated how nitrogen rate (80 and 160 kg N ha⁻¹) modifies the critical weed-free period (CWFP) in sunflower. Weed interference was imposed and terminated at V2, V4, V6, V8, and R1 growth stages using hand weeding. The Gompertz model was fitted to yield-loss data from 12 treatment combinations per year. Under standard nitrogen application (80 kg ha⁻¹) the CWFP spanned V3 to V7; at 160 kg N ha⁻¹ it narrowed to V4–V6, indicating that higher nitrogen supply partially compensates for early weed competition. The economically acceptable yield loss threshold of 5% was maintained when fields remained weed-free from V3 through sunflower bud formation at both nitrogen levels. Practical implications for timing of inter-row cultivation are discussed.

title: Changes in weed flora composition in sunflower–soybean rotations over a 15-year monitoring period in Vojvodina
abstract: Weed emergence surveys were carried out annually from 2000 to 2014 on eight commercial fields in the Bačka region maintained in a sunflower–soybean two-year rotation. Species composition and relative abundance were recorded at three phenological stages per season using permanent quadrats (0.5 m², ten per field). Multivariate ordination and nonparametric tests detected a shift toward grass weed dominance from 2006 onward, coinciding with widespread adoption of imidazolinone-tolerant sunflower hybrids. Echinochloa crus-galli and Sorghum halepense increased in relative abundance by 28 and 19 percentage points respectively. Broadleaf weed diversity (Shannon index) declined significantly (p < 0.01) during the same period. The findings indicate that reliance on a single herbicide mode of action over consecutive seasons restructures the weed community within approximately eight years, with implications for resistance management planning.

title: Inter-row mechanical cultivation timing and frequency effects on weed biomass and soybean yield
abstract: This study quantified how the number and timing of inter-row cultivations affected weed suppression and seed yield in soybean over three growing seasons (2013–2015). Treatments included no cultivation (control), one early cultivation (V2), one late cultivation (V4), two cultivations (V2 + V4), and three cultivations (V2 + V4 + V6). Weed biomass was measured at R1. Two cultivations reduced weed biomass by 61–74% relative to the control, while three cultivations provided no additional benefit. Seed yield increased by an average of 0.41 t ha⁻¹ with two cultivations versus the untreated control. Late single cultivation was less effective than early single cultivation (44 vs. 52% biomass reduction). Soil compaction measurements indicated no significant increase in cone penetration resistance attributable to the three-cultivation treatment. Results support a two-cultivation standard as a herbicide-reduction strategy in conventional soybean systems.

title: Herbicide efficacy and weed control spectrum under half-rate and full-rate applications in soybean: a meta-analysis of Serbian trial data
abstract: Forty-three herbicide efficacy trials conducted between 2004 and 2016 in Vojvodina were compiled and subjected to meta-analysis to assess whether half-rate applications provided acceptable weed control when combined with mechanical cultivation. Trials included post-emergence treatments with bentazon, imazethapyr, and thifensulfuron-methyl in soybean. Across all active ingredients, half-rate application reduced weed density control efficacy from a mean of 83% (full rate) to 68%, but the combination of half-rate herbicide with one inter-row cultivation raised efficacy to 79%, within an acceptable margin for commercial production. Yield losses under the combined strategy averaged 1.8% relative to full-rate herbicide alone. Sub-group analysis indicated that half-rate efficacy was most variable for mixed grass–broadleaf weed populations, and least variable for predominantly broadleaf-dominated fields. The analysis provides a data-driven basis for integrated dose reduction programmes.

title: Influence of cover crop mulch on weed emergence and early-season competition in no-till soybean
abstract: A three-year experiment (2018–2020) examined how cereal rye (Secale cereale) cover crop residue at three mulch levels (0, 2, and 4 t dry matter ha⁻¹) affected weed emergence density and early-season biomass accumulation in no-till soybean. Weed counts were taken weekly for six weeks after soybean emergence. At 4 t ha⁻¹ mulch, total weed emergence was suppressed by 54–67% across years, with the greatest suppression observed for small-seeded species (Chenopodium album, Amaranthus retroflexus). Larger-seeded species (Xanthium strumarium, Datura stramonium) were not consistently affected by mulch level. Soybean emergence was delayed by 1.2 days per tonne of mulch. Final soybean yield under 4 t ha⁻¹ mulch without herbicide was 4–12% lower than under 4 t ha⁻¹ mulch plus a single reduced-rate herbicide treatment. Mulch alone did not fully substitute for chemical control in high-pressure years.

title: Integrated weed management in sunflower–soybean rotations: a review of threshold-based decision frameworks
abstract: This chapter synthesises published economic threshold studies for the major weed species in sunflower and soybean produced in the Pannonian Plain, covering the period 1990–2020. Static economic thresholds derived from density–yield loss models are compared with dynamic threshold approaches that incorporate weed seedbank feedback. Sources reviewed include 62 peer-reviewed studies and extension trial reports from Serbia, Hungary, Croatia, Slovakia, and Romania. The chapter discusses discrepancies between laboratory-derived and field-validated thresholds, the impact of rotation on threshold stability, and constraints on adopting dynamic thresholds under typical farm advisory conditions. A simplified decision tree for practical integrated weed management planning in two-crop rotations is proposed. Gaps in data for grass weed species under conservation tillage are identified as priority research needs.

title: Sorghum halepense rhizome depth and emergence dynamics under contrasting autumn tillage treatments in Vojvodina
abstract: Johnsongrass (Sorghum halepense) is increasingly problematic in sunflower–soybean fields across Vojvodina, but rhizome ecology under field conditions is poorly documented. Rhizome samples were excavated at harvest and the following spring from plots under deep mouldboard ploughing (28 cm), shallow disc tillage (12 cm), and no-till over two seasons (2021–2022). Deep ploughing relocated 68% of rhizome biomass below 20 cm, from which emergence was negligible. In disc-tilled plots, the majority of rhizomes remained in the 5–15 cm layer and emergence density averaged 18.4 shoots m⁻². Emergence in no-till was highest (26.1 shoots m⁻²), concentrated in the top 5 cm. A degree-day model (base 10°C) fitted to emergence timing data (R² = 0.84) allowed prediction of first emergence within ±4 days. These data support targeted timing of post-emergence grass herbicide applications in no-till systems.

title: Short-term seedbank depletion rates under contrasting weed management intensities in soybean: a two-rotation study
abstract: Reducing weed seedbank size is a long-term goal of integrated weed management but empirical depletion data from field rotations remain scarce in southeastern Europe. Seedbank density was quantified before and after each of four consecutive growing seasons (2020–2023) on twelve experimental plots managed under three regimes: standard herbicide programme, reduced herbicide plus mechanical cultivation, and herbicide-free mechanical cultivation only. Initial seedbank density averaged 6 120 seeds m⁻². Annual depletion rates estimated from the difference between measured seedbanks and modelled seed inputs differed significantly among management regimes (p < 0.001): 28% under standard herbicide, 22% under reduced herbicide plus cultivation, and 14% under mechanical cultivation only. Species-specific depletion rates varied widely; Amaranthus retroflexus depleted fastest (31–38% yr⁻¹) and Polygonum aviculare slowest (9–14% yr⁻¹). Predicted time to reach a management-target threshold of 2 000 seeds m⁻² ranged from 6 to 18 years depending on regime and starting composition.

title: An Integer Programming Formulation for Cyclical Nurse Rostering with Minimum Rest-Period Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for generating cyclical rosters in hospital nursing departments, explicitly encoding Serbian labour-law minimum rest periods of eleven consecutive hours between shifts. The formulation introduces a compact set of binary variables indexed by employee, shift type, and week, reducing the model size by approximately 34 percent compared with a standard day-indexed formulation on a dataset of 120 nurses across four wards. Computational experiments were conducted using CPLEX 9.0 on instances derived from two public hospitals in Vojvodina. Optimal solutions were found within one hour for instances with up to 60 nurses; for larger instances a two-phase approach combining LP relaxation with branch-and-bound obtained solutions within 2.8 percent of the lower bound. The model was validated against hand-crafted rosters produced by head nurses, yielding a 12 percent reduction in overtime costs.

title: Tabu Search for the Multi-Skill Shift Scheduling Problem in Call Centres
abstract: We study a multi-skill shift scheduling problem arising in a medium-sized call centre with 210 agents grouped into seven skill clusters. The objective minimises total staffing cost subject to hourly demand forecasts, agent availability windows, and contractual shift-length bounds. A tabu search procedure is developed in which the neighbourhood is defined by single-agent shift reassignments and inter-day swaps; the tabu tenure is adaptive, lengthening when the search stagnates. The algorithm is benchmarked against a commercial workforce management system on 30 weekly planning instances. On instances of industrial size the tabu search finds solutions within 4.1 percent of a computed MILP lower bound in under four minutes of CPU time, while the commercial system exceeds the lower bound by 9.7 percent on average. Sensitivity analysis examines the effect of varying demand-forecast error on solution quality.

title: Constraint Programming Models for the Employee Timetabling Problem: A Comparative Study
abstract: This paper compares four constraint programming (CP) models for a general employee timetabling problem drawn from the literature benchmark set ETP-Bench, which contains 45 instances ranging from 20 to 300 employees. Models differ in how they propagate shift-coverage constraints and how they handle soft preferences for weekends off. Experiments use OR-Tools CP-SAT solver version 6.4 with a time limit of 3600 seconds per instance. The model that combines cumulative constraints for shift coverage with a weighted violation objective solves all small instances to optimality and achieves the best known solutions on 31 of the 45 instances, improving four previously reported best solutions. Runtimes are analysed and the impact of symmetry-breaking constraints on search tree size is quantified. A discussion of modelling trade-offs is included for practitioners.
