title: Labour-Law Compliance in Automated Shift Scheduling: A Survey of Modelling Approaches
abstract: Personnel scheduling systems deployed across the European Union must encode a growing body of labour-law requirements at both EU directive and national statute levels. This survey reviews how such requirements—maximum weekly working hours, minimum daily rest, mandatory break durations, night-shift frequency limits, and public-holiday entitlements—are translated into constraints within integer programming, constraint programming, and metaheuristic frameworks. We categorise 68 papers published between 1990 and 2011 according to constraint type, solution method, and application sector. The survey identifies a persistent gap between academic models, which typically encode at most five constraint categories, and industrial implementations, which routinely enforce fifteen or more. We propose a unified constraint taxonomy with 22 categories and discuss which categories remain computationally intractable under standard solver technology. Directions for future research are outlined, including hybrid exact-heuristic approaches and parameterised complexity analysis.

title: A Branch-and-Price Algorithm for the Multi-Site Rostering Problem
abstract: Large retail and logistics companies operate workers across dozens of locations under shared employment contracts, creating a multi-site rostering problem in which assignments must respect both site-level staffing quotas and company-wide labour agreements. We develop a branch-and-price algorithm in which the master problem allocates weekly patterns to employees and a set of column-generation subproblems—one per employee—generate feasible pattern columns by solving shortest-path problems on a duty-sequence graph. Dual stabilisation using a boxstep method reduces oscillation during column generation. Tests on 20 generated instances (50–400 employees, 5–20 sites) show that the algorithm proves optimality or near-optimality (gap below 0.5 percent) on instances with up to 200 employees and heuristically terminates within 1 percent gap on larger instances within two hours. Comparison with a rolling-horizon heuristic shows a 7 percent cost saving.

title: Modelling Irregular Shift Patterns in Public Bus Transport Rostering
abstract: Bus driver scheduling in mid-sized Serbian cities is characterised by split shifts, irregular duty lengths, and a requirement that each driver complete a full route cycle. We model this as a set-partitioning problem over a duty network constructed from timetable data from the public transport operator in Novi Sad. The network contains approximately 14 000 duty arcs for a weekday timetable covering 18 lines and 340 drivers. A column-generation approach solves the LP relaxation, and integer solutions are obtained by a rounding heuristic followed by a fix-and-optimise procedure. The resulting rosters reduce total paid idle time by 8.3 percent relative to manually constructed rosters. The approach is validated over twelve weekly timetable instances spanning summer and winter service patterns. Implementation aspects relevant to practical deployment—driver preference representation and disruption recovery—are also discussed.

title: Exact and Heuristic Approaches to Shift Scheduling
abstract: This book chapter surveys the landscape of exact and heuristic methods for shift scheduling problems, targeting an audience of graduate students and practitioners without a deep background in mathematical programming. It covers MILP formulations, Lagrangian relaxation, constraint programming, genetic algorithms, tabu search, and large neighbourhood search, illustrating each with worked examples drawn from hospital, retail, and manufacturing domains. Emphasis is placed on how different problem features—demand uncertainty, multi-skill requirements, contractual variety—affect the choice of solution method. Computational complexity results are summarised without proof, and a guide to publicly available benchmark instances and solver software is included. The chapter concludes with a discussion of practical deployment issues including data integration, user acceptance, and re-optimisation after disruptions.

title: Large Neighbourhood Search for the Generalised Employee Rostering Problem with On-Call Duties
abstract: On-call duties—periods during which an employee must be reachable but not necessarily present at the workplace—are common in healthcare yet rarely modelled explicitly in academic rostering literature. We extend the generalised employee rostering problem to include on-call duty types and formulate associated activation costs and transition constraints. A large neighbourhood search (LNS) is implemented with five destroy operators (random, shift-type, ward-cluster, overload-repair, and preference-repair) and an OR-Tools CP-SAT repair phase. The method is tested on synthetic instances generated from anonymised data of a hospital in Subotica, Serbia, ranging from 40 to 250 nurses and one to three months of planning horizon. LNS consistently outperforms a greedy construction heuristic by 14–22 percent on weighted penalty and closes 80 percent of the gap to the MILP lower bound on small instances. Ablation experiments quantify the contribution of each destroy operator.

title: Robust Rostering Under Demand Uncertainty: A Scenario-Based Integer Programming Approach
abstract: Demand forecasts for personnel scheduling are inherently uncertain; rosters that are optimal under point forecasts may perform poorly when actual demand differs. This paper models demand uncertainty through a discrete scenario set and formulates a two-stage robust MILP in which the first stage fixes long-horizon pattern assignments and the second stage adjusts daily assignments within contractual bounds for each scenario. The model is applied to a set of 15 weekly instances from a warehouse logistics operator employing 320 pickers across two shifts. A scenario set of 20 demand realisations is constructed via historical simulation. A Benders decomposition scheme solves the robust model; subproblem dual information drives the generation of feasibility cuts. Resulting rosters exhibit a 6 percent cost premium over deterministic rosters but reduce expected under-staffing events by 43 percent across out-of-sample test scenarios.
venue: International Journal of Production Economics

title: Evaluating CP-SAT and Gurobi for Medium-Scale Nurse Rostering: A Computational Comparison
abstract: With the maturation of general-purpose MILP and CP-SAT solvers, practitioners often face a choice between them without clear guidance for specific problem classes. This paper presents a controlled comparison of OR-Tools CP-SAT (version 9.2) and Gurobi (version 9.5) on a set of 60 nurse rostering instances stratified by size (30–200 nurses) and planning horizon (4 and 8 weeks). Both solvers are given the same mathematical model—a standard MILP formulation with soft constraints penalised in the objective—and a uniform time limit of one hour. CP-SAT finds better solutions on 38 of 60 instances; Gurobi provides tighter lower bounds on 41 instances. For instances with 80 or fewer nurses and a 4-week horizon, CP-SAT proves optimality on 17 of 20 instances versus 11 for Gurobi. Differences in default parallelism, presolve, and linearisation are identified as contributing factors.

title: Decomposition Methods for Multi-Depot Driver Rostering in Regional Rail Services
abstract: Regional rail operators assign drivers to depots, and the rostering problem must simultaneously respect depot-level coverage requirements and network-wide contractual obligations. We model this as a multi-depot driver rostering problem and develop a Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition where subproblems correspond to individual depots. Each depot subproblem is solved by a CP-SAT model with a limit of 120 seconds; the master problem is solved by a cutting-plane method augmented with cover inequalities. The approach is tested on instances derived from the timetable of a regional rail operator in the Western Balkans, encompassing five depots and 280 drivers across monthly planning horizons. Decomposition solves all instances within 45 minutes, achieving gaps below 1.8 percent. A direct MILP formulation times out on instances with more than three depots. Sensitivity to depot size imbalance is analysed.

title: An Adaptive R-Tree Variant for Dynamic Insertion of Large Vector Polygon Datasets
abstract: This paper examines the performance of a modified R-tree structure, termed the AR-tree, designed to handle high-frequency dynamic insertions of polygon geometries typical in land-parcel cadastral databases. The AR-tree introduces a heuristic split policy based on minimum bounding rectangle overlap area rather than perimeter, reducing query time by an average of 18% compared to the standard Guttman R-tree across three benchmark polygon datasets totalling 4.2 million features. Experiments were conducted using synthetic urban cadastral data generated from OpenStreetMap extracts for the Vojvodina region. The structure was implemented in C++ and evaluated against PostgreSQL/PostGIS bulk-loaded equivalents. Results show consistent improvement for mixed insert-query workloads but marginal gains for read-heavy scenarios. The paper provides formal proofs for worst-case node utilisation bounds and discusses applicability to streaming sensor data ingestion pipelines.

title: Phytoseiid mite assemblages in conventionally managed apple orchards of Vojvodina: species composition and seasonal abundance
abstract: A two-year survey was conducted in eight commercially managed apple orchards across Vojvodina to characterise phytoseiid mite assemblages and document their seasonal fluctuation relative to Panonychus ulmi populations. Leaf and soil litter samples were collected at biweekly intervals from April to October in both years, yielding 3,840 individual leaf samples and 480 litter cores. Seventeen phytoseiid species were identified, of which Typhlodromus pyri and Kampimodromus aberrans accounted for 68% of all adult females recovered from foliage. Peak predator-to-prey ratios on leaves rarely exceeded 1:12 in conventionally treated blocks, and Panonychus ulmi populations exceeded the economic threshold of five mobile stages per leaf in five of the eight orchards during June–July. Cluster analysis separated orchards primarily by pesticide spray frequency rather than region or cultivar, suggesting that input intensity is the dominant structuring force for phytoseiid diversity under current management. The data provide baseline values for designing reduced-spray monitoring programmes in the region.

title: Effect of kaolin particle film on Panonychus ulmi and its phytoseiid predators in an apple orchard trial
abstract: A three-season field experiment assessed whether kaolin particle film (applied at 30 kg ha⁻¹ per application, four times per season) altered European red mite density and phytoseiid abundance compared with an untreated control and a standard acaricide programme. Treatments were replicated in four blocks of 12 trees each. Panonychus ulmi cumulative mite-days were 38% lower in the kaolin treatment than in the control but 22% higher than in the acaricide treatment. Predator populations, assessed as adult females per 25 leaves, were significantly higher in the kaolin plots (mean 4.7 per 25 leaves at midsummer) than in acaricide plots (0.9 per 25 leaves), and not significantly different from the control. Kampimodromus aberrans was the most abundant predator in kaolin plots, while Typhlodromus pyri dominated in control plots. Fruit russeting attributable to kaolin residue was evaluated visually at harvest and remained below 3% in all treated replicates. Results suggest kaolin can partially substitute acaricide applications while preserving predator communities.

title: Influence of ground cover management on phytoseiid mite dispersal from orchard floor to canopy in apple
abstract: Mite dispersal from herbaceous ground covers into the tree canopy was quantified in a split-plot experiment comparing permanent grass sward, mown clover-grass mixture, bare-soil tillage, and herbicide strip treatments across three growing seasons. Sticky-band traps placed at 50 cm height on trunks intercepted ascending mites weekly from May to September. Total phytoseiid catches were 3.1-fold higher in clover-grass plots (annual mean 68 mites per trap per week) than in bare-soil plots (22 mites per trap per week), with intermediate values in permanent sward. Panonychus ulmi was almost absent from ground-level catches. Morphological identification confirmed that Neoseiulus cucumeris and Typhlodromus pyri were the principal ascending species. Canopy phytoseiid densities in clover-grass plots were significantly elevated by mid-June compared with herbicide-strip controls. The study provides field evidence that orchard floor vegetation serves as a seasonal reservoir supporting early-season canopy colonisation by phytoseiid predators.

title: Overwintering survival of Typhlodromus pyri under different bark and ground cover conditions in Vojvodina apple orchards
abstract: The overwintering biology of Typhlodromus pyri was investigated by sampling rough-bark cores, wooden lath traps, and ground litter at monthly intervals from October to March across two winters in four orchards. Bark cores (5 cm² per sample, n = 960 total) yielded mean densities of 14.3 females per core in orchards with permanent grass cover and 6.8 females per core in bare-soil orchards. Survival to spring as estimated by mark-recapture with fluorescent dust was 61% in grass-covered orchards and 44% in bare-soil orchards. Temperature data loggers placed at the soil-litter interface recorded minimum temperatures 2.1–3.4 °C warmer under grass mulch than in bare soil during frost events, which correlated with survival differences. Wooden lath traps attached to trunks captured significantly more females than bark cores in October, suggesting active trunk migration preceding winter. Results indicate that maintaining ground vegetation improves thermal refugia for overwintering predatory mites.

title: Predator-prey ratio dynamics along a pesticide reduction gradient in apple: a four-year mesocosm study
abstract: A mesocosm experiment with 48 semi-isolated apple trees at Rimski Šančevi was used to test how stepwise reductions in acaricide application frequency (four, two, one, and zero applications per season) affected predator-prey dynamics over four consecutive seasons. Panonychus ulmi and phytoseiid counts were made on 25 leaves per tree at ten-day intervals. In zero-spray mesocosms, Panonychus ulmi populations peaked at 31.4 mobile stages per leaf in year one but declined to 7.2 in year four as phytoseiid populations established. Typhlodromus pyri dominated in low-spray treatments; Kampimodromus aberrans was most abundant in the zero-spray treatment by year three. A predator-prey ratio of approximately 1:6 consistently preceded suppression of Panonychus ulmi below the economic threshold in years three and four. The study documents a multi-year lag before biological control stabilises and suggests that a two-season bridge period of one acaricide application per year may reduce economic risk during transition to spray-free management.

title: Interspecific competition between Typhlodromus pyri and Kampimodromus aberrans: arena experiments under controlled temperature
abstract: Competitive interactions between Typhlodromus pyri and Kampimodromus aberrans were examined in arena trials at 20, 25, and 30 °C using Panonychus ulmi eggs as the sole prey source at two density levels (10 and 25 eggs per arena). Predation rates, oviposition, and survival were recorded over seven-day intervals for single-species and two-species arenas, each replicated 30 times per combination. At 20 °C, T. pyri consumed significantly more Panonychus ulmi eggs per female per day (mean 4.8) than K. aberrans (mean 3.1). At 30 °C, the difference was reversed (K. aberrans 6.3 vs T. pyri 5.1). In mixed arenas, K. aberrans oviposition declined by 29% at 25 °C, while T. pyri oviposition was unaffected. No direct intraguild predation was recorded. The results imply temperature-mediated competitive dominance shifts and suggest that orchard location and microclimate may partly explain field observations of varying species dominance.

title: Mite community response to strip-intercropping with Phacelia tanacetifolia in an organic apple orchard
abstract: Strips of Phacelia tanacetifolia were sown between alternate tree rows in a certified organic apple orchard and compared with mown grass control strips in a paired-block design over two seasons. Phytoseiid densities on foliage were 1.8-fold higher in Phacelia-strip trees than in grass-strip trees at the first midsummer census, and Panonychus ulmi cumulative mite-days were reduced by 41% in Phacelia strips in year two. Arthropod diversity in the ground layer was significantly greater in Phacelia strips (Shannon H' 2.34 vs 1.67 for grass controls). Pollen analysis of Phacelia flower heads confirmed the presence of Neoseiulus cucumeris and Typhlodromus pyri feeding directly on pollen, providing supplemental nutrition when prey was scarce. Phacelia senescence by late July led to partial predator emigration from strips, recorded via trunk traps. The study supports Phacelia intercropping as an inexpensive tool for augmenting resident predator populations in organic systems.

title: Baseline susceptibility of Panonychus ulmi populations from Vojvodina orchards to abamectin and bifenazate
abstract: Resistance monitoring of Panonychus ulmi is important for managing acaricide rotation in reduced-spray programmes. Leaf disc bioassays were used to establish concentration-response relationships for abamectin and bifenazate using five Panonychus ulmi populations collected from commercial orchards with varying treatment histories and two reference laboratory strains. LC₅₀ values for abamectin ranged from 0.008 mg L⁻¹ (susceptible reference) to 0.041 mg L⁻¹ across field populations, with resistance ratios of 1.2–5.1, indicating moderate but not alarming shifts. Bifenazate LC₅₀ values ranged from 0.015 to 0.019 mg L⁻¹ with resistance ratios of 1.0–1.3, suggesting uniform susceptibility. Orchards with longer continuous acaricide use histories showed the highest resistance ratios for abamectin. Results suggest that abamectin resistance monitoring should be incorporated into regional IPM advisory systems, and that bifenazate retains consistent efficacy as a rotation partner.

title: Soil mite communities as indicators of ground cover quality in apple orchards: an oribatid-phytoseiid co-occurrence analysis
abstract: Soil samples were taken from a paired comparison of twelve permanent grass-covered and twelve bare-soil apple orchard plots to investigate co-occurrence patterns between oribatid and phytoseiid mites across a gradient of organic matter content. Samples (n = 288 total, collected in spring and autumn over two years) were extracted by Berlese-Tullgren funnels. Oribatid richness was positively correlated with soil organic matter content (r = 0.71, p < 0.001) and with phytoseiid abundance in litter (r = 0.58, p < 0.001). A co-occurrence null model analysis detected significant positive associations between Scheloribates laevigatus and Typhlodromus pyri, possibly reflecting shared microhabitat preferences. Bare-soil plots had mean oribatid richness of 8.3 species versus 17.6 species in grass-covered plots. The results suggest that soil mite community indices could serve as rapid assessment tools for orchard floor ecosystem quality, relevant to certification criteria in regional agri-environment schemes.

title: Decision support thresholds for phytoseiid-based biological control of Panonychus ulmi: validation under Vojvodina field conditions
abstract: Action thresholds for initiating acaricide intervention when phytoseiid predators are present were tested against historical datasets from 14 orchard seasons accumulated between 2009 and 2020 at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station. Three threshold rules were evaluated: (i) spray when Panonychus ulmi exceeds 7.5 mobile stages per leaf regardless of predators; (ii) spray when Panonychus ulmi exceeds 7.5 per leaf and predator-to-prey ratio is below 1:10; (iii) spray when Panonychus ulmi exceeds 12 per leaf irrespective of predators. Rule (ii) reduced acaricide applications by 35% compared with rule (i) while keeping cumulative mite-days below the fruit quality damage threshold in 11 of 14 seasons. Rule (iii) led to yield losses exceeding 5% in three seasons. A simple spreadsheet decision tool implementing rule (ii) was developed and tested with three cooperating growers in 2021, who reported satisfactory outcomes. The thresholds and the tool are described for potential use in regional advisory services.

title: Functional response of Kampimodromus aberrans to Panonychus ulmi eggs at varying temperatures: implications for predictive modelling
abstract: The functional response of Kampimodromus aberrans adult females to Panonychus ulmi egg densities (0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 eggs per arena) was characterised at 18, 22, 26, and 30 °C in laboratory experiments with 20 replicates per combination. A type II functional response was confirmed at all temperatures. Attack rate a increased from 0.21 h⁻¹ at 18 °C to 0.49 h⁻¹ at 26 °C before declining slightly at 30 °C. Handling time T_h decreased monotonically from 0.43 h at 18 °C to 0.19 h at 30 °C. Maximum daily consumption estimated from the Rogers random predator equation ranged from 31 to 56 eggs per female per day across the temperature range. Parameter estimates were incorporated into a stage-structured simulation model for Panonychus ulmi suppression over a 90-day season. Model predictions matched mesocosm field data from 2019–2020 with a mean absolute error of 1.8 mites per leaf, suggesting the parameterisation is adequate for regional use.

title: Phytoseiid predator responses to insect growth regulator applications in an integrated apple programme: two-year field data from Serbia and Romania
abstract: Side-effect evaluation of three insect growth regulators (chlorantraniliprole, methoxyfenozide, and spirodiclofen) on phytoseiid mite populations was conducted in coordinated field trials at two sites in Vojvodina and one site in Dolj County, Romania, over the 2022–2023 seasons. Each trial used a randomised complete block design with four replicates per treatment. Phytoseiid density, species composition, and egg viability were assessed at 7, 14, and 28 days post-application. Chlorantraniliprole caused no significant reduction in phytoseiid abundance or fecundity at any time point. Methoxyfenozide reduced phytoseiid density by 22–27% at 14 days in both years but showed recovery by day 28. Spirodiclofen, applied as a miticide control, reduced phytoseiid densities by 78–85% and required six weeks for partial recovery. Side-effect ratings for integration into Vojvodina IPM guidelines are proposed on the basis of the combined dataset, following the IOBC/WPRS scoring protocol.

title: Early-season phytoseiid colonisation dynamics in young apple plantings established with different ground cover regimes: first results
abstract: Young apple plantings (year one and year two after establishment) typically lack the bark structure and ground cover complexity that support phytoseiid populations in mature orchards. This study reports preliminary data from a split-plot trial at two sites in Vojvodina comparing bare-soil, permanent meadow grass, and legume-grass mixture ground cover regimes established at planting time. Phytoseiid colonisation was tracked via weekly leaf and trunk sticky-trap samples from April to August in 2024 and 2025. In year one, no phytoseiid mites were detected in bare-soil plots before July, whereas meadow grass and legume plots showed first detections in late May. By August of year two, legume-grass plots had mean canopy densities of 2.3 phytoseiid females per 25 leaves, compared with 0.7 in bare-soil plots. Panonychus ulmi populations were low and below threshold at all sites in both years, possibly reflecting low initial inoculum pressure. A full analysis including molecular identification and mark-recapture dispersal data will be reported in a subsequent publication.

title: Soil bulk density and penetration resistance under conventional and reduced tillage in a soybean–maize rotation
abstract: Soil physical properties were monitored over four growing seasons on a silt-loam chernozem at two sites in Vojvodina under three tillage systems: conventional deep ploughing (30 cm), shallow disc tillage (15 cm), and no-till. Bulk density and cone index were measured at 0–10, 10–20, and 20–30 cm depth increments at sowing, flowering, and harvest. No-till plots showed significantly higher bulk density in the 10–20 cm layer (mean 1.38 g/cm³) compared with ploughed plots (1.21 g/cm³), while the surface layer (0–10 cm) displayed lower bulk density under no-till (1.18 g/cm³) than under conventional tillage (1.29 g/cm³). Cone index exceeded the critical threshold of 2 MPa more frequently under no-till during dry summers. Soybean yield was reduced by 8–14% under no-till relative to conventional tillage in years with below-average July rainfall, but differences were negligible in wetter seasons. The study highlights the importance of seasonal rainfall distribution when evaluating conservation tillage viability in the region.

title: Молекуларна идентификација и морфолошка карактеризација Trichoderma spp. изолованих из рипаријских земљишта у Банату

Изолати су идентификовани комбинованом применом морфолошких кључева и молекуларних маркера (ITS1, ITS2 и tef1 регион). Утврђено је присуство седам врста: T. harzianum, T. viride, T. koningii, T. asperellum, T. longibrachiatum, T. atroviride и T. hamatum. Доминантна врста у свим узорцима земљишта под шумарским и травним покривачем була је T. harzianum (34,2% изолата). title: Virulence variation among Fusarium solani isolates causing crown and root rot in greenhouse pepper in Serbia
abstract: Crown and root rot of pepper caused by Fusarium solani is increasingly reported in Vojvodina's greenhouse sector. Nineteen F. solani isolates obtained from symptomatic pepper crowns and roots at eight commercial greenhouses were characterised for virulence by inoculating three-week-old pepper seedlings (cv. Kurtovska kapija) under controlled conditions. Disease severity was rated on a 0–4 scale at 21 and 35 days post-inoculation. Significant variation in virulence was observed among isolates: disease severity index ranged from 0.8 to 3.6 at 35 days. Pathogenicity was confirmed by re-isolation. AFLP fingerprinting differentiated the isolates into four genetic groups that did not correlate strictly with geographic origin. Virulence was negatively correlated with the growth rate at 30 °C (r = −0.61, p < 0.01), suggesting that thermal tolerance may partly modulate aggressiveness. These findings have implications for selecting representative challenge strains in biocontrol screening.

title: Silicon supply affects resistance of winter wheat to Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici under field conditions in northern Serbia
abstract: The interaction between silicon nutrition and powdery mildew (Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici) incidence was examined in a three-cultivar field experiment over two seasons (2022–2024) at Rimski Šančevi. Soil calcium silicate (0 and 300 kg ha⁻¹) was combined with two fungicide programmes (full-programme and reduced by one application). Disease severity was assessed as percentage leaf area affected at GS47 and GS65 using a standardised decimal scale. Silicon amendment reduced powdery mildew severity by 19–31 % at GS47 across cultivars and seasons; susceptible cv. Dragana showed the largest response. The combination of silicon and reduced fungicide achieved disease severity statistically equivalent to the full fungicide programme without silicon in two of four season-cultivar combinations. Grain yield penalty from mildew in the untreated control was partially recovered by silicon (mean recovery 4.2 %, range 1.8–6.7 %). These results indicate silicon may support fungicide reduction strategies in wheat, though cultivar and seasonal variability require further characterisation.

title: Lay comprehension of conditional probability statements in cancer screening leaflets: a think-aloud study
abstract: This study examined how adults with no medical background interpret conditional probability expressions (e.g., '1 in 10 women with a positive result actually has cancer') in cervical screening information leaflets distributed by Serbian public health centres. Thirty-two participants aged 22–58 were recruited from a general-population sample in Novi Sad. Think-aloud protocols were recorded during reading and subsequently coded for interpretation errors, emotional reactions, and decision intentions. Results showed that 68% of participants misread positive predictive value as diagnostic certainty, and 41% expressed intention to avoid further screening after misunderstanding a false-positive rate. Frequency formats ('3 out of every 100') produced significantly fewer errors than percentage formats (p < .01). Qualitative analysis identified four dominant lay mental models of screening accuracy. Findings suggest that current Serbian screening leaflets require substantial revision of probability language and recommend adoption of frequency-based icon arrays as a supplement to text.

title: Measuring readability of Serbian-language patient information leaflets: adaptation of the Flesch–Kincaid index for South Slavic morphology
abstract: Standard readability formulas derived from English are poorly suited to morphologically rich languages where syllable counts and sentence boundaries behave differently. This paper reports the systematic adaptation of a Flesch–Kincaid-style index for Serbian, drawing on a corpus of 180 patient information leaflets collected from pharmacies and outpatient clinics in Vojvodina between 2008 and 2010. The corpus was manually segmented and syllabified, and comprehension was tested with 96 participants using a validated cloze procedure. Regression analysis identified an optimal formula weighting average syllables per word (β = 0.61) and average words per sentence (β = 0.29) against cloze scores (R² = 0.74). The resulting Serbian Readability Index (SRI) is compared with a naive transliteration of the original Flesch–Kincaid formula; the SRI shows significantly better predictive validity (F-change p < .001). Normative data for six text-type categories are provided, along with a scoring spreadsheet distributed as supplementary material.

title: Does plain-language rewriting of hospital discharge summaries affect patient recall? A randomised experiment
abstract: Hospital discharge summaries are frequently used as the primary written handover document between specialists and primary care, yet their accessibility for patients is rarely assessed. This randomised experiment compared recall and comprehension of standard discharge summaries against plain-language rewritten versions in a sample of 120 patients recently discharged from the internal medicine ward of a regional hospital in Vojvodina. Participants were randomised to receive either the standard institutional text or a version rewritten according to Serbian Ministry of Health plain-language guidelines (average SRI score 58 vs. 34). Immediate free recall (number of correctly recalled propositions) was significantly higher for the plain-language condition (M = 7.4 vs. 4.1, Cohen's d = 0.89). A two-week follow-up telephone interview showed that medication adherence intent did not differ significantly between groups. The study concludes that readability improvements substantially help patients understand their immediate care instructions but that additional behavioural supports are needed to sustain adherence intentions over time.

title: Numeracy moderates the effect of visual aids on genetic risk understanding: evidence from a 2×2 experiment
abstract: Visual aids such as icon arrays and bar charts are widely recommended to support comprehension of probabilistic genetic risk information, but the degree to which benefits depend on users' numeracy levels is not well established. This study recruited 160 adults from the general population in Novi Sad and Subotica and randomised them to receive information about a hypothetical autosomal-recessive condition in one of four conditions: text-only, text plus icon array, text plus bar chart, or text plus family pedigree diagram. Objective numeracy was measured with the eight-item Lipkus Numeracy Scale. A 4 (format) × 2 (numeracy: low/high) mixed ANOVA on risk comprehension scores showed a significant interaction (F(3,152) = 5.4, p = .001). Low-numeracy participants benefited most from icon arrays, whereas high-numeracy participants performed equally across all formats. Pedigree diagrams produced the most heterogeneous outcomes. These findings support targeted rather than uniform use of visual aids in genetic counselling settings.

title: Readability and structural clarity of informed consent forms in clinical trials conducted in Serbia: a corpus analysis
abstract: Informed consent forms (ICFs) are legally and ethically mandated documents, yet their readability is frequently criticised as inadequate for lay readers. This study analysed a corpus of 63 ICFs submitted to Serbian ethics committees between 2014 and 2018, covering oncology, cardiology, and psychiatric trials. Each document was scored using the SRI readability index and a newly developed Structural Clarity Index (SCI) that assesses organisation, use of headings, definition of technical terms, and legibility of typography. Mean SRI score across the corpus was 29.4 (SD = 7.1), corresponding to university-level reading demands, while SCI scores were low (mean 2.1 out of 5) for 71% of documents. Oncology ICFs were significantly harder to read than psychiatric trial ICFs (t(42) = 3.2, p = .002). Multiple regression showed that word count was the strongest predictor of low SCI scores (β = −0.49). A checklist derived from findings is appended for use by ethics committees and trial sponsors.

title: How adults update genetic risk beliefs after receiving carrier test results: a longitudinal interview study
abstract: This qualitative longitudinal study followed 38 adults who underwent carrier testing for cystic fibrosis or spinal muscular atrophy at a genetics clinic in Vojvodina over a period of twelve months. Participants were interviewed at three time points: one week before receiving results, two weeks after, and six months after. Interviews were analysed using interpretive phenomenological analysis, focusing on how mental models of inheritance and personal risk shifted in response to test results. At the pre-test stage, most participants held binary illness models rather than carrier concepts. Post-result interviews revealed three updating trajectories: assimilation (incorporating results into prior binary models with minimal conceptual change), accommodation (revising mental models toward probabilistic thinking), and non-integration (compartmentalising results as irrelevant). Accommodation was more common among participants who recalled having received a diagram-based explanation from a counsellor. The findings highlight the importance of visual explanatory tools during result disclosure.

title: Adapting the European Health Literacy Questionnaire (HLS-EU-Q47) for use in Vojvodina's multilingual population: Serbian and Hungarian parallel versions
abstract: Vojvodina is a multilingual region where Hungarian is an official regional language alongside Serbian, yet health literacy instruments validated for Serbian-speaking populations have not been systematically adapted for Hungarian-speaking Vojvodinian residents. This paper reports the cross-cultural adaptation of the 47-item European Health Literacy Survey questionnaire into both standard Serbian and the Vojvodinian Hungarian variety. The adaptation process followed a five-step forward-backward translation protocol with cognitive debriefing interviews conducted on 16 Serbian-speaking and 14 Hungarian-speaking participants. Pilot testing with 210 participants (105 per language version) confirmed acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.87 and 0.85 respectively) and a three-factor structure consistent with the original instrument. Differential item functioning analysis identified two items requiring further revision in the Hungarian version due to cultural differences in describing medical consultations. The validated instruments are made available for regional health surveys.

title: Designing accessible digital health content for adults with low literacy: participatory evaluation of a mobile app for hypertension self-management
abstract: This study used a participatory design and evaluation approach to assess the cognitive accessibility of a mobile application for hypertension self-management intended for use by patients with low health literacy. Thirty adults attending a hypertension clinic were recruited; 60% had primary or lower-secondary education and scored in the lowest two quintiles of the SRI-based health literacy screener. Three participatory workshops were conducted in which participants attempted core app tasks (recording blood pressure, interpreting trend graphs, reading medication reminders) with a researcher observing and probing. Usability problems were classified using a structured error taxonomy. Trend graph interpretation was the most problematic feature, with 73% of low-literacy participants misreading directionality on inverted axes. Written medication reminders averaging 24 words per notification produced substantially higher error rates than reminders of 10 words or fewer. A revised prototype incorporating plain-text notifications and simplified graphs was tested in a second round with 18 participants and showed a 44% reduction in task-error rate.

title: Does the framing of polygenic score results affect perceived susceptibility and health behaviour intentions? An online experiment
abstract: Polygenic scores (PGS) for common diseases are increasingly offered by direct-to-consumer genetic testing services, yet the communicative framing of results remains understudied. This pre-registered online experiment (n = 312 adults recruited via a Serbian online panel) tested three PGS result frames for a hypothetical elevated-risk scenario for type 2 diabetes: percentile rank ('you are in the top 20%'), relative risk multiplier ('your risk is 1.7 times the average'), and absolute lifetime risk ('your lifetime risk is 34%'). Perceived susceptibility, worry, and intentions to change diet and physical activity were assessed immediately after exposure and at a two-week follow-up. Absolute lifetime risk framing produced the highest perceived susceptibility (F(2,309) = 9.3, p < .001) and the strongest dietary change intentions at follow-up, but also the highest worry scores. Relative risk multipliers were least well understood; 38% of participants could not correctly rank their risk relative to average. Pre-registration, materials, and data are openly available.

title: Evaluation of a plain-language standard for Serbian pharmaceutical regulatory submissions: inter-rater reliability and stakeholder acceptability
abstract: The Serbian Medicines and Medical Devices Agency has been developing a plain-language standard for summary of product characteristics documents since 2021. This study reports the formal evaluation of a draft standard applied to 40 test documents (20 prescription, 20 over-the-counter medicines). Eight raters from different professional backgrounds (pharmacists, medical writers, patient representatives, and psychologists) scored each document on a 30-item adherence checklist based on the draft standard. Intraclass correlation coefficients for the total adherence score were ICC(2,1) = 0.81, indicating good inter-rater reliability. Stakeholder focus groups (n = 24 participants across three groups) identified that the provisions on numerical risk expression were considered the most beneficial by patient representatives but the most burdensome to implement by regulatory affairs professionals. Revisions to two sections of the draft standard are recommended based on combined quantitative and qualitative findings.

title: Perceived Information Quality in Small Manufacturing Firms: A Preliminary Scale Development
abstract: This paper reports the construction and initial validation of a multi-item scale designed to capture perceived information quality (PIQ) within accounting information systems used by small manufacturing enterprises in Vojvodina. Drawing on a convenience sample of 94 owner-managers and accounting staff collected through structured questionnaires in 2011, the study adapts established information quality taxonomies—accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and consistency—to the specific operational context of batch-production workshops. Exploratory factor analysis in SPSS 18 produced a four-factor solution accounting for 61.3% of variance. Item loadings and internal consistency coefficients (Cronbach's alpha ranging from 0.71 to 0.83) supported the provisional reliability of the scale. The paper discusses measurement artifacts arising from dual respondent roles in small family firms, where the same person often both inputs and interprets accounting data. Limitations include the lack of confirmatory analysis and geographic restriction to a single region. The scale is offered as a starting point for longitudinal or comparative research.

title: AIS Implementation Barriers in Family-Owned Enterprises: Evidence from the Serbian Wood-Processing Sector
abstract: Using semi-structured interviews with 28 owner-managers of family-owned wood-processing firms registered in the Vojvodina and Šumadija regions, this study identifies the principal organizational and technical barriers preventing or delaying the adoption of structured accounting information systems. Thematic coding of interview transcripts revealed five recurring barrier clusters: resistance to data transparency within the family hierarchy, perceived cost relative to firm size, absence of in-house IT competence, distrust of external software vendors, and uncertainty about regulatory compliance requirements. The findings complement prior survey-based research by illuminating the relational dynamics specific to family governance structures, where informal bookkeeping practices are embedded in long-standing trust relationships between founders and accountants. The paper recommends that AIS vendors targeting this segment develop modular, low-cost entry configurations and provide hands-on onboarding rather than documentation-only support. Policy implications for the Serbian Ministry of Economy's SME digitalization program are noted.

title: Do Accounting Report Characteristics Influence Manager Confidence? A Structural Equation Model for Serbian SMEs
abstract: This study tests a structural model linking four accounting report characteristics—accuracy, format clarity, update frequency, and traceability—to self-reported decision confidence among managers in Serbian small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 187 managers across 14 industry subsectors; respondents were recruited through the Regional Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 3.0 was used to estimate path coefficients and assess model fit. Update frequency (β = 0.31, p < 0.01) and accuracy (β = 0.28, p < 0.01) showed the strongest positive associations with decision confidence, while format clarity contributed modestly (β = 0.14, p < 0.05). Traceability did not reach significance in this sample. The explained variance in decision confidence (R² = 0.43) was moderate, indicating that system-level characteristics account for a substantial but not dominant share of confidence formation. The paper concludes by proposing refinements to the measurement model for replication in larger samples.

title: Information Quality Dimensions and Their Relevance for Owner-Managers in Family Manufacturing Firms: A Conceptual Reassessment
abstract: This book chapter revisits the standard Wang and Strong (1996) information quality framework and examines its applicability to the governance conditions typical of family-owned manufacturing firms. The chapter argues that the framework's four categories—intrinsic, contextual, representational, and accessibility quality—carry different weights depending on whether the decision-maker is also the principal owner, because ownership concentration compresses the feedback loop between information producer and consumer. A re-weighting is proposed on the basis of 12 in-depth case studies conducted in Serbian, Croatian, and Slovenian furniture and plastics manufacturers between 2015 and 2016. The chapter further introduces the concept of 'ownership-filtered interpretation bias,' describing systematic distortions in how owner-managers evaluate the completeness of reports they themselves commission. Practical implications are drawn for ERP configurators and management accountants advising family businesses. The chapter is part of an edited volume on accounting and governance in Southeast European SMEs.

title: Measuring AIS Output Quality in Vojvodina's Food-Processing Family Firms: Scale Refinement and Confirmatory Analysis
abstract: Building on the preliminary scale published in 2012, this paper reports a full confirmatory factor analysis of the AIS output quality instrument using data from 214 respondents employed in family-owned food-processing companies registered in Vojvodina. Respondents included both managerial and accounting staff to test for rater-role measurement invariance. Confirmatory factor analysis in AMOS 24 confirmed the hypothesized four-factor structure (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.061), and multigroup analysis revealed partial scalar invariance across rater roles: intercepts for the timeliness subscale differed significantly between managers and accountants, suggesting divergent reference standards. Convergent validity was supported by average variance extracted values exceeding 0.50 for all factors; discriminant validity was confirmed by the Fornell–Larcker criterion. The refined 18-item instrument is presented in full for use in subsequent research. An online administration protocol is described to facilitate replication in other agro-industrial regions of Serbia.

title: ERP System Upgrade Events and Short-Term Changes in Managerial Decision Confidence: A Longitudinal Panel Study
abstract: This paper uses a longitudinal panel design to track changes in self-reported managerial decision confidence before and after planned ERP upgrade events in 31 family-owned manufacturing firms in Serbia. Data were collected at three time points: six weeks before upgrade, one month after go-live, and five months after go-live. Mixed-effects regression models estimated in R (lme4 package) controlled for firm size, manager tenure, and upgrade scope. Decision confidence dropped significantly in the immediate post-upgrade period (mean decrease 0.41 points on a 7-point scale, p < 0.01), recovering to above baseline at the five-month observation point in 23 of 31 firms. Firms that provided structured user training before go-live showed a smaller confidence dip (mean decrease 0.19 points) and faster recovery. The paper draws attention to the transition window as a period of elevated decision risk and recommends staged upgrade rollouts as a practical mitigation strategy for family-managed operations.

title: Cognitive Overload and Report Format in Family Firm Management Accounting: An Experimental Study
abstract: This laboratory-style experiment examined whether the visual format of management accounting reports—tabular versus graphical—moderates the relationship between data volume and perceived cognitive overload among owner-managers of family firms. Forty-eight participants recruited from the Serbian Family Business Association were randomly assigned to one of four conditions varying format (table/graph) and data density (low/high). Dependent variables were self-reported cognitive load (NASA-TLX scale), decision time in seconds, and decision accuracy on a standardized inventory-replenishment task. A 2×2 ANOVA showed a significant interaction: graphical formats reduced cognitive load under high data density (F(1,44) = 7.21, p = 0.010, η² = 0.14), but the two formats did not differ under low data density. Decision accuracy was unaffected by format, suggesting that format effects manifest primarily in subjective experience rather than objective performance in this task type. Implications for AIS report template design in SME-oriented accounting software are discussed.

title: Linking AIS Output Quality to Inventory Decision Accuracy in Family-Owned Batch Manufacturers: A Multi-Site Field Study
abstract: This preprint presents results from an ongoing field study examining the direct relationship between objectively measured AIS output quality and the accuracy of inventory replenishment decisions in 19 family-owned batch manufacturers in Serbia and northern Croatia. AIS quality was assessed using auditor-reviewed records rather than self-report, producing an objective quality index for each participating firm across four quarters. Inventory decision accuracy was operationalized as the absolute percentage deviation of actual order quantities from the theoretically optimal order calculated from the firm's own demand and holding cost data. Multi-level modeling with firm as the grouping variable showed that a one-unit improvement in the objective AIS quality index was associated with a 2.1 percentage point reduction in order deviation (95% CI: 1.3–2.9 pp). The effect was moderated by the manager's years of experience with the current system, attenuating at higher experience levels. The study is the first in this literature to use an objective rather than perceptual quality measure linked to a quantifiable decision outcome.

title: Municipal-level variation in colorectal cancer incidence in Vojvodina, 1995–2003: a descriptive analysis using cancer registry records
abstract: This study examined geographic variation in colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence across the 45 municipalities of Vojvodina using records from the Vojvodina Cancer Registry for the period 1995–2003. A total of 6,842 incident cases were included. Age-standardised incidence rates were calculated using the European standard population. Crude mapping revealed substantial differences between municipalities, with rates ranging from 18.4 to 61.7 per 100,000 person-years in men and 14.2 to 44.9 in women. Analysis of registry completeness indicated that approximately 22% of records lacked a full street-level address, relying instead on municipality of residence only. Spatial autocorrelation assessed by Moran's I statistic was statistically significant for men (I = 0.31, p = 0.003) but not for women (I = 0.11, p = 0.18). The findings suggest that observed heterogeneity partly reflects genuine geographic clustering and partly differential case ascertainment across districts. The study provides a baseline description motivating subsequent methodological work on estimation under incomplete spatial information.

title: Comparative performance of deterministic and probabilistic geocoding strategies for Serbian residential address data
abstract: Geocoding of patient addresses in Serbia is complicated by inconsistent street naming conventions, transliteration variants, and the absence of a comprehensive national address gazetteer. This study compared four geocoding strategies applied to 5,012 colorectal cancer patient addresses drawn from the Vojvodina Cancer Registry: (1) exact string matching against a municipal gazetteer, (2) phonetic normalisation with fuzzy matching, (3) reverse-geocoding from postal codes, and (4) a probabilistic ensemble combining all three. Match rates at the street-segment level were 54%, 66%, 59%, and 72%, respectively. The ensemble approach also produced positional accuracy estimates; median offset from field-verified coordinates was 148 m for urban addresses and 540 m for rural addresses. Unmatched records fell disproportionately in municipalities with older housing stock and pre-1990 address formats. These results provide practical guidance for registry data managers and supply match-rate parameters used in subsequent estimation models.

title: Small-area estimation of colorectal cancer incidence: a methodological review with emphasis on incomplete spatial data
abstract: Reliable small-area estimates of cancer incidence are needed to allocate screening resources and identify high-risk communities, yet many European registries — particularly in Central and Eastern Europe — operate with substantial proportions of records geocoded only to administrative units larger than the area of interest. This chapter reviews the statistical literature on small-area estimation as applied to cancer registries, covering empirical Bayes and fully Bayesian smoothing methods, multiple imputation of spatial location, and composite estimators that combine survey and registry information. Special attention is given to the assumptions underlying each approach and their sensitivity to the pattern of missingness in address data. An illustrative comparison uses simulated data with realistic missingness fractions ranging from 10% to 50%. The chapter concludes with practical recommendations for registries operating in data-sparse environments and identifies open methodological problems, including the handling of population denominator uncertainty at small-area level.

title: Sensitivity of small-area colorectal cancer rate estimates to the choice of spatial scale: census tract versus settlement level in Vojvodina
abstract: Small-area health statistics are sensitive to the modifiable areal unit problem (MAUP): estimates at one geographic scale may differ substantially from those at another, complicating policy use. This study examined how CRC incidence estimates from the same registry dataset (Vojvodina, 2005–2014, n = 14,820) changed when the analysis unit was switched between census tracts (n = 312) and administrative settlements (n = 467). Bayesian CAR models were fitted separately at each scale and posterior medians were compared after areal interpolation. Correlation between scale-specific estimates was 0.74 for urban areas and 0.52 for rural areas, indicating meaningful scale dependence in sparsely populated zones. Variance components attributable to structured spatial effects were larger at settlement level. The paper quantifies the practical impact of scale choice and recommends census-tract level as a default for Vojvodina given the alignment with population denominator data from the Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia.

title: Concordance between colorectal cancer incidence estimates from the Vojvodina registry and hospital discharge data: implications for registry completeness assessment
abstract: Independent validation of cancer registry completeness is rarely straightforward in settings without multiple high-quality data sources. This study used hospital discharge records from the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina (2010–2018) and the Vojvodina Cancer Registry over the same period to assess concordance and identify gaps. Probabilistic record linkage was performed using name, date of birth, sex, and municipality of residence. Of 9,247 discharge records with a primary CRC diagnosis, 87.3% could be linked to a registry record. Non-linked cases were more often rural residents and older women. Registry-to-discharge ratio varied by municipality from 0.74 to 1.12, with ratios below 0.85 concentrated in three southern municipalities. These results indicate that registry underreporting is geographically patterned, which, if unaddressed, would bias small-area incidence estimates in a spatially correlated manner. The study proposes a completeness correction factor for use in subsequent estimation models.

title: Cross-border small-area cancer incidence estimation in the Hungary–Serbia border region using jointly modelled registry data
abstract: Administrative borders interrupt spatial continuity of cancer risk surfaces, making cross-border incidence mapping methodologically challenging. This study jointly modelled colorectal cancer incidence data from the Vojvodina Cancer Registry (Serbia) and the South Transdanubia Cancer Registry (Hungary) for the period 2012–2019, covering 58 administrative units on the Serbian side and 44 on the Hungarian side. A shared CAR model on a unified adjacency graph that spans the border was compared to two country-specific models. The joint model produced lower DIC and revealed a continuous north–south gradient that was obscured when each country's registry was modelled alone. Geocoding completeness differed substantially between registries (74% full-address in Hungary versus 63% in Serbia), and the reallocation prior was adapted to each system's address structure. Cross-border areas showed moderately elevated posterior incidence rate ratios (median 1.22, 95% CrI 1.07–1.41) relative to the pooled mean.

title: A multiple imputation framework for registry address data with hierarchical geographic uncertainty
abstract: Most multiple imputation (MI) procedures assume that the variable to be imputed is continuous or unordered categorical. Geographic location, however, has a hierarchical structure: a missing street address is known to lie within a settlement, which lies within a municipality. Ignoring this hierarchy in MI leads to implausible imputations. This paper develops a sequential MI procedure that first draws a settlement conditional on municipality using population-weighted multinomial sampling, then draws a street segment within the settlement using kernel density estimates from geocoded cases in the same municipality–year–sex stratum. The procedure was implemented in R and validated on the Vojvodina CRC registry (2008–2018, n = 18,032; 29% incompletely geocoded). Compared to single-imputation alternatives, the MI approach produced correctly calibrated confidence intervals for tract-level rate estimates and was robust to deviations from the assumed spatial density model. Code is provided as a supplementary R package.

title: Probabilistic reallocation versus spatial interpolation for incomplete registry geocoding: a head-to-head comparison using leave-one-out validation
abstract: Two broad families of methods address incomplete geocoding in registry-based small-area estimation: probabilistic reallocation, which assigns ungeocoded cases to sub-areas using prior distributions, and spatial interpolation, which smooths rate surfaces using neighbouring area information without explicit case relocation. This paper compares four specific implementations — weighted probabilistic reallocation, areal interpolation, kriging of standardised rates, and Bayesian CAR smoothing — using leave-one-out cross-validation on Vojvodina CRC data (2010–2022, n = 22,517). A random 30% of geocoded cases were masked to simulate the incomplete-geocoding scenario. Predictive performance was evaluated by mean absolute error and interval coverage at tract level. Bayesian CAR smoothing performed best overall (MAE 3.1 per 100,000), followed by weighted probabilistic reallocation (MAE 3.4). Kriging performed worst in sparsely populated rural tracts. Results provide a structured comparison to guide method selection by registry analysts.

title: Glycaemic trajectory patterns and incident hypertension in a multigenerational Vojvodinian cohort: a joint modelling approach
abstract: We applied joint group-based trajectory modelling to fasting glucose measurements and incident hypertension events in 791 non-diabetic participants from the Vojvodinian household registry followed for 18 years. Three fasting glucose trajectory groups were identified: stable low-normal (44%), gradually rising (38%), and accelerated rise crossing the impaired fasting glucose threshold (18%). The accelerated-rise group had a hazard ratio of 2.31 (95% CI: 1.62–3.29) for incident hypertension compared with the stable group, after adjustment for BMI trajectory class, LDL, sex, age, and smoking. Co-occurrence of the accelerated glucose rise and late-onset high-BMI trajectory substantially increased absolute hypertension risk. These findings contribute to understanding the sequence in which cardiometabolic risk factors accumulate in an ageing, economically transitioning community, and suggest that fasting glucose surveillance may be a useful early signal for cardiovascular risk escalation.

title: Modelling Bid-Ask Spread Persistence in a Thin Agricultural Spot Market: An Agent-Based Approach
abstract: This paper develops an agent-based model of a stylised grain spot market populated by heterogeneous traders — fundamentalists, chartists, and noise traders — to study the persistence of bid-ask spreads under varying liquidity conditions. The model is calibrated against weekly wheat price data from the Vojvodina grain exchange spanning 2004–2010, comprising 312 weekly observations. Simulations with 150 active agents reproduce the observed autocorrelation structure of spreads (Ljung-Box Q-statistic p < 0.01) and fat-tailed return distributions (excess kurtosis 4.7 vs. empirical 5.1). Sensitivity analysis shows that the ratio of noise traders to fundamentalists is the single strongest driver of spread persistence, accounting for roughly 60 percent of variance in simulated spread duration. The results suggest that in thin markets with fewer than 40 regular participants, even modest changes in trader composition can shift equilibrium spread levels by 15–20 percent. The model is implemented in NetLogo 6.1 and all code is made available for replication.

title: Order Flow Toxicity in Illiquid Spot Markets: Adapting VPIN to Low-Frequency Agricultural Data
abstract: Volume-synchronised probability of informed trading (VPIN) was developed for high-frequency equity markets and its applicability to low-frequency agricultural spot markets has not been systematically examined. This paper adapts the VPIN estimator to daily transaction data from three Balkan grain exchanges (sunflower, maize, and wheat) over the period 2008–2015, comprising approximately 1,800 trading days per commodity. To handle extended periods with zero trades — common in thin markets — a modified bulk-classification rule is proposed that assigns volume buckets based on weekly rather than tick-level aggregation. Back-tested against nine documented price spike episodes, the adapted VPIN correctly flags elevated toxicity conditions in seven cases with a three-day lead time. An agent-based simulation is used to validate the estimator's behaviour under controlled conditions, confirming that the modification preserves the theoretical relationship between informed trading intensity and VPIN values. The adjusted estimator may serve commodity exchange operators as a low-cost early warning indicator.

title: Agent-Based Simulation of Commodity Markets Under Microstructure Constraints
abstract: This book chapter surveys agent-based modelling approaches applicable to commodity spot markets characterised by structural thinness — defined here as fewer than 100 unique counterparties per month — and contrasts them with models designed for liquid equity markets. Five modelling frameworks are reviewed: Gode-Sunder zero-intelligence markets, Santa Fe artificial stock market variants, order-book models with strategic queuing, network-based models with bilateral search, and hybrid fundamentalist-chartist architectures. For each framework, the chapter details how the core assumptions must be relaxed or extended to remain plausible in a thin market context. Particular attention is given to the treatment of storage costs, seasonal supply shocks, and the absence of short-selling — features that distinguish physical commodity trading from financial asset trading. The chapter concludes with a set of ten modelling recommendations and identifies empirical regularities from Balkan and Central European grain data that any adequate model must reproduce.

title: Liquidity Cycles and Inventory Behaviour of Intermediaries in Seasonal Commodity Markets: Agent-Based Evidence
abstract: Physical commodity markets exhibit strong seasonality in both supply and liquidity. This paper incorporates explicit inventory dynamics into an agent-based model of a grain spot market, allowing intermediary agents to accumulate and draw down stocks in response to seasonal price signals and storage cost schedules. The model is parameterised using publicly available warehouse receipt data from three Serbian agri-food warehouses covering 2015–2021. Simulation results across 800 runs reproduce the empirically documented pattern whereby bid-ask spreads widen by 30–40 percent during harvest months relative to inter-seasonal periods. Intermediaries with larger inventory buffers are found to stabilise prices during supply gluts but amplify price spikes when stocks are depleted, contributing to a sawtooth volatility pattern that matches the observed autocorrelation structure in maize prices (r = 0.61 simulated vs. 0.58 empirical at a four-week lag). The findings suggest that warehouse capacity constraints have a first-order effect on market microstructure dynamics in thin seasonal markets.

title: Do Algorithmic Market Makers Stabilise or Destabilise Thin Spot Markets? Simulation Evidence from a Parametric Study
abstract: The adoption of simple algorithmic market-making strategies is beginning to reach regional commodity exchanges that have historically operated through bilateral negotiation. This paper evaluates the stabilising and destabilising properties of three algorithmic market-maker designs — symmetric quote update, inventory-adjusted quoting, and momentum-reactive quoting — within a calibrated agent-based model of a thin spot market. Each design is tested across a grid of 36 parameter combinations (quote width, inventory limit, update frequency) for 600 simulation runs per cell. Symmetric quote-update algorithms reduce price impact costs by 8–14 percent relative to a no-algorithm baseline under normal conditions, but under a simulated supply shock of 20 percent below expected harvest they amplify the maximum price drawdown by up to 31 percent compared with the baseline, because rapid quote withdrawal removes liquidity precisely when it is most needed. Inventory-adjusted designs show better shock resilience at the cost of higher normal-period spreads. The results provide a concrete parameter guidance for exchange operators considering algorithm licensing rules.

title: Integrating AHP and Goal Programming for Resource Allocation in Serbian Secondary Education: A Multi-Period Model
abstract: The paper presents a two-phase decision support model that combines AHP-derived criterion weights with goal programming to allocate teaching staff and equipment budgets across departments in six Serbian secondary schools over a three-year planning horizon. In the first phase, AHP was used to derive priority weights for five allocation criteria—curriculum coverage, student-to-teacher ratio compliance, equipment utilisation, extracurricular programme support, and administrative overhead minimisation—from pairwise comparisons provided by school principals and regional education inspectors. These weights were then embedded as penalty coefficients in a goal programming formulation solved using the LINGO 17 solver. The model was tested on actual budget and staffing data from schools in the South Bačka district for 2016–2018. Compared to the allocations actually made, the model solutions reduced deviation from minimum staffing targets by 14% and reduced total budget overshoot by 9.3%. Computational results and model limitations are discussed in detail.

title: Biorelevant dissolution testing of carvedilol solid dispersions prepared by hot-melt extrusion: effect of polymer carrier and drug loading on supersaturation kinetics
abstract: Carvedilol, a BCS Class II antihypertensive, exhibits low and variable oral bioavailability attributable to poor aqueous solubility. Solid dispersions of carvedilol were prepared by hot-melt extrusion using polyvinylpyrrolidone-vinyl acetate (PVP-VA 64) and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMC-AS) as carriers at drug loadings of 10, 20, and 30% w/w. Dissolution experiments were conducted in FaSSIF-V2 and FeSSIF at 37 °C using a µDiss Profiler UV system with continuous fibre-optic monitoring, enabling real-time supersaturation profiling. Extrudates with 20% carvedilol in HPMC-AS achieved a maximum supersaturation ratio of 8.3 relative to the crystalline reference after 15 minutes, maintained for over 90 minutes before precipitation. PVP-VA 64 formulations at the same loading showed earlier and more pronounced precipitation, with supersaturation collapsing to baseline within 45 minutes. Differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray powder diffraction confirmed complete amorphisation up to 20% loading for both carriers. Precipitation kinetics were parameterised using a two-compartment supersaturation model and the fitted rate constants are reported for subsequent use in PBPK absorption modelling. Results suggest HPMC-AS provides superior in vitro inhibition of precipitation, with implications for in vivo performance prediction.

title: Building a mechanistic absorption model for carvedilol HPMC-AS extrudates in GastroPlus: sensitivity of predicted Cmax to precipitation rate constants
abstract: This study describes the construction and local sensitivity analysis of a physiologically based pharmacokinetic model for carvedilol formulated as an amorphous solid dispersion in HPMC-AS, using GastroPlus version 9.8. Dissolution input was taken from FaSSIF-V2 experiments reported separately; precipitation rate constants (kppt) measured in the dissolution vessel were incorporated directly into the Advanced Compartmental Absorption and Transit (ACAT) model. A fasted-state virtual population of 20 subjects was simulated using human physiology with default GastroPlus parameters for the fasted small intestine. The model was first calibrated against published intravenous pharmacokinetic data for crystalline carvedilol to establish systemic disposition parameters (Vd 115 L/kg, CL 9.3 L/h/kg). Simulated Cmax for the HPMC-AS extrudate at 20% loading was 48.2 ng/mL (geometric mean), compared to a crystalline reference simulation of 19.7 ng/mL, representing a 2.45-fold enhancement. One-at-a-time sensitivity analysis revealed that kppt exerted the strongest influence on predicted Cmax, followed by intestinal permeability, whereas gastric emptying rate had negligible effect within physiological ranges. The results underscore the importance of accurate experimental precipitation kinetics as model input rather than default database values. Model files are deposited as supplementary material.

title: Coupling mechanistic dissolution models to PBPK frameworks for BCS Class II compounds: a practical guide for formulation scientists
abstract: Linking mechanistic in vitro dissolution data to physiologically based pharmacokinetic models is an increasingly applied strategy for reducing in vivo studies during early formulation development of BCS Class II compounds. This book chapter provides a step-by-step account of the workflow, covering biorelevant dissolution experiment design, data preprocessing, parameterisation of supersaturation-precipitation kinetics, and import of dissolution profiles into GastroPlus and PK-Sim. Emphasis is placed on practical decisions: choice of dissolution apparatus, media composition, sampling frequency, and the treatment of particle size and effective permeability as calibration variables. Case examples draw on experimental data for fenofibrate and carvedilol solid dispersion systems studied in the authors' laboratory. The chapter discusses common sources of model uncertainty including in vitro–in vivo differences in bile salt concentrations and gastrointestinal transit times. Verification strategies using retrospective clinical data are outlined, alongside a discussion of regulatory guidance documents from the EMA and FDA that support model-informed submissions. The chapter is intended for postgraduate students and early-career scientists entering the field, and includes annotated worked examples using publicly available software.

title: Effect of gastrointestinal pH variability on simulated plasma exposure of fenofibrate amorphous solid dispersions: a PBPK modelling study with Monte Carlo sampling
abstract: Gastrointestinal pH is a key source of inter-individual variability in the oral absorption of ionisable and pH-sensitive BCS Class II drugs. Fenofibrate, although non-ionisable, displays strong pH-dependent solubility when formulated as an amorphous solid dispersion due to ionisation of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate, which alters polymer dissolution rates. This study used PK-Sim 11.0 to construct a PBPK model for fenofibrate in an HPMC-AS solid dispersion matrix, incorporating experimentally derived dissolution profiles obtained across a pH range of 5.5–7.4 in FaSSIF buffers. Monte Carlo sampling (n = 500 virtual subjects) was applied to fasted gastric pH (log-normal distribution, mean 1.8, SD 0.6) and small intestinal pH (normal distribution, mean 6.5, SD 0.35) to generate predicted AUC0–24 and Cmax distributions. Simulated geometric mean AUC0–24 was 4 210 ng·h/mL with a coefficient of variation of 38%, compared to 52% for the crystalline reference formulation, suggesting that amorphisation partially reduces exposure variability driven by pH. Sensitivity analysis identified the dissolution rate constant at pH 6.8 as the parameter most strongly correlated with predicted AUC. Experimental validation against three published single-dose crossover datasets showed adequate predictive performance (predicted/observed ratio within 0.8–1.25 for all three studies).

title: Liquid-to-solid ratio as a dominant process variable governing porosity and dissolution rate of granules produced by continuous wet granulation
abstract: The relationship between liquid-to-solid ratio (L/S), internal granule porosity, and the in vitro dissolution rate of a model BCS Class II drug (ketoprofen, 20% w/w loading) was investigated systematically on a continuous twin-screw granulation platform. L/S was varied from 0.18 to 0.35 w/w in seven steps; barrel temperature, screw speed, and feed rate were held constant at 30 °C, 300 rpm, and 1.5 kg/h respectively. Granule porosity was quantified by mercury intrusion porosimetry and correlated with both laser diffraction size data and tablet dissolution profiles obtained under USP Apparatus 2 conditions at 75 rpm in pH 6.8 phosphate buffer. Porosity decreased from 41% to 22% as L/S increased from 0.18 to 0.35, while t80 (time to 80% drug release) increased from 18 to 47 minutes. A two-parameter power-law model fitted porosity–dissolution data with R² = 0.93. The findings support using L/S as a primary quality control handle when a specific dissolution target must be met without reformulation.

title: Effect of water activity on lipase-catalysed phospholipid acylation in microaqueous systems
abstract: Water activity (aw) is a critical parameter in enzymatic acylation reactions carried out under low-water conditions. This study examined how controlled aw (0.11–0.75, set by saturated salt solutions) affected the regioselectivity and yield of sn-2 acylation of lysophosphatidylcholine using immobilised Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase. Reactions were performed in tert-amyl alcohol at 50 °C. At aw 0.33, sn-2 selectivity reached 84% as determined by 13C-NMR positional analysis, compared with 61% at aw 0.75. Total conversion dropped from 78% to 54% as aw increased from 0.11 to 0.75. Residual solvent content in the product was below 5 ppm by GC headspace analysis after vacuum evaporation. The data indicate that maintaining aw between 0.22 and 0.33 provides the best balance of selectivity and conversion for pharmaceutical-grade synthesis, and this window was used as a specification in subsequent scale-up work.

Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na uzorcima od PLA materijala štampanim na kućnom FDM štampaču modifikovanom za prihvat kamere. Prikupljeno je 840 slika slojeva, od kojih je 23% sadržalo vidljive greške odvajanja. Rezultati su pokazali da pragovi intenziteta u sivim tonovima postižu tačnost od svega 61% pri detekciji grešaka, što ukazuje na nedovoljnost prostih metoda segmentacije u uslovima varijabilnog osvetljenja i refleksije filamenata. Rad definiše referentni skup podataka i metodologiju anotacije koji su korišćeni u kasnijim studijama grupe, te identifikuje ključne izvore lažno pozitivnih i lažno negativnih rezultata kao što su senke usled glave štampača i nejednoličan sjaj materijala.

title: Comparison of edge-detection filters for surface texture analysis in FDM-printed thermoplastic layers
abstract: This study systematically evaluates five classical edge-detection filters—Sobel, Prewitt, Laplacian of Gaussian, Canny, and Scharr—for characterising surface texture in thermoplastic layers produced by fused deposition modelling. A controlled dataset of 1,200 grayscale images was acquired under three lighting configurations (diffuse, directional, and co-axial) using a monochrome camera mounted perpendicular to the build platform. Ground truth labels were assigned by two independent operators and reconciled through majority vote. Canny filtering under co-axial illumination yielded the highest F1 score of 0.74 for delamination boundary localisation, outperforming the next best method (Scharr, F1 = 0.69) by a statistically significant margin (p < 0.01, paired t-test). Directional lighting consistently degraded all methods by introducing asymmetric shadow artefacts. The findings provide practical guidance for illumination setup in in-situ monitoring rigs and establish a reproducible baseline for subsequent machine-learning approaches.

abstract: Rad istražuje primenu konvolucionih neuronskih mreža (CNN) za klasifikaciju četiri kategorije grešaka u slojevima FDM štampe: potpuna adhezija, parcijalno odvajanje, warpingа i void. Skup podataka obuhvata 3.200 označenih isečaka slika dimenzija 64×64 piksela prikupljenih in-situ tokom štampe 18 različitih geometrija. Ispitane su tri arhitekture: plitka CNN sa tri konvoluciona sloja, prilagođena LeNet varijanta i jednostavna rezidijalna mreža. Obuka je sprovedena na 70% podataka, validacija na 15% i testiranje na 15%. Rezidualna mreža je dostigla tačnost od 88,4% na testnom skupu, a plitka CNN svega 74,1%. Analiza konfuzione matrice pokazuje da su greške tipa void najtežje za detekciju zbog vizuelne sličnosti sa senkom ekstrudera. Rad naglašava važnost augmentacije podataka rotacijom i horizontalnim preslikavanjem pri radu s ograničenim skupovima.
