title: Transfer learning from optical inspection datasets to FDM layer monitoring: a feasibility study
abstract: Publicly available image datasets from printed circuit board (PCB) and textile defect inspection contain large numbers of labelled anomaly images and share certain visual characteristics with surface defects in FDM-printed layers. This study investigates whether CNN models pre-trained on such heterogeneous inspection data can be fine-tuned effectively for FDM layer-adhesion defect detection. Six source dataset configurations were tested, ranging from single-domain PCB data to a mixed corpus of 42,000 images. Fine-tuning was performed on an FDM-specific set of 2,800 images using three frozen-layer strategies. The best configuration—pre-training on a mixed corpus with the first four convolutional blocks frozen—achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.91 on held-out FDM data, compared to 0.83 for training from scratch on the same data. Inference time per layer image was 14 ms on a GPU and 210 ms on CPU, both compatible with real-time monitoring at standard FDM print speeds. The study demonstrates the practical value of cross-domain transfer even when source and target visual domains are only loosely related.

title: Embedded single-board-computer platform for real-time CNN inference in FDM printer monitoring
abstract: Deploying convolutional neural network inference on embedded hardware is essential for cost-effective in-situ monitoring in industrial FDM printers. This paper describes the design, implementation, and evaluation of a monitoring module based on a single-board computer (SBC) with an attached neural processing unit. A ResNet-18 architecture, quantised to 8-bit integer weights, was deployed on the module and evaluated on a stream of 416×416 pixel images captured at one frame per completed layer. On a test sequence of 6,400 layer images, the embedded system achieved 91.2% accuracy for the binary delamination/no-delamination task at a throughput of 4.3 frames per second, within the latency budget imposed by typical layer completion times. Power consumption during inference was 3.8 W. The module communicates defect alerts to the printer controller via a serial interface, enabling automatic pause-and-notify behaviour. Bill-of-materials cost is estimated at €47 per unit at low-volume production.

title: Anomaly detection in FDM using autoencoder networks trained exclusively on defect-free layer images
abstract: Standard supervised defect classifiers require large labelled datasets of both normal and anomalous samples. In many production settings, defective prints are rare and costly to produce intentionally. This paper proposes an unsupervised approach using a convolutional autoencoder trained exclusively on 9,600 images of defect-free FDM layers from four different printer models. During inference, reconstruction error is computed per image patch; patches exceeding a threshold calibrated on a held-out normal validation set are flagged as anomalous. On an independent test set of 1,200 images containing five defect categories, the method achieved a detection rate of 84.7% at a false positive rate of 6.3%. Performance degraded by less than 2 percentage points when the model trained on one printer was applied to a different printer of the same manufacturer, suggesting acceptable cross-printer generalisation. The approach reduces annotation burden substantially while maintaining practically useful detection performance.

title: Closed-loop extrusion-rate correction driven by in-situ CNN defect signals in FDM
abstract: This study presents and evaluates a feedback control strategy that adjusts the extrusion multiplier of an FDM printer in response to defect signals generated by a deployed CNN monitor. The controller reduces the extrusion rate by 2% increments when delamination is detected on two or more consecutive layers, and restores the nominal rate when three consecutive clean layers are observed. Experiments were conducted on an open-architecture FDM platform with firmware modified to accept serial commands from the monitoring module. Sixty-four multi-layer prints of standardised tensile-test coupons in PETG were produced under the closed-loop condition and compared with 64 prints at fixed nominal settings. The closed-loop group showed a 31% reduction in measured delamination area assessed by post-print cross-section imaging and a 9% improvement in mean tensile strength at break. No statistically significant difference in total print time was observed. The work demonstrates the viability of CNN-driven closed-loop process control without requiring a detailed process model.

title: Višemodalni pristup praćenju kvaliteta FDM štampe: kombinovanje vizuelnih i akustičnih signala
abstract: Ovaj rad istražuje da li se akustična emisija, snimana mikrofonom postavljenim na okvir štampača, može kombinovati s vizuelnim signalima kamere kako bi se povećala tačnost detekcije grešaka u odnosu na pristup koji se oslanja samo na jedan modalitet. Prikupljeni su simultani audio i video podaci tokom 120 višeslojnih štampi uz namerno unošenje četiri vrste grešaka. Akustični signal je segmentiran na prozore od 0,5 s i opisan melodičnim koeficijentima kepstra (MFCC). Vizuelne karakteristike su dobijene iz prethodno opisane CNN arhitekture. Srednje i kasno spajanje oba modaliteta ispitano je u poređenju s jednomodalnim baznim linijama. Kasno spajanje s naučenim vektorom težina postiglo je makro F1 od 0,89 u poređenju s 0,82 (samo vizuelno) i 0,71 (samo akustično). Rezultati sugerišu da akustični modalitet doprinosi naročito pri detekciji klizanja filamenata, koje je teško vizuelno razlikovati od normalnog površinskog sjaja.

title: Benchmark dataset for in-situ FDM layer defect detection: acquisition protocol, annotation guidelines, and baseline results
abstract: The absence of a standardised, publicly available image dataset has hampered reproducible comparison of in-situ monitoring methods for fused deposition modelling. This paper describes FDMLayerBench, a dataset of 18,400 annotated layer images collected across six printer models, four thermoplastic materials, and twelve print geometries, under three controlled illumination conditions. Defect categories follow a taxonomy of seven types defined in consultation with manufacturing quality engineers. Inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss' kappa, reached 0.81 for major categories and 0.63 for subcategories. Baseline results are reported for five published CNN architectures evaluated under a standardised five-fold cross-validation protocol. The best-performing baseline (a lightweight ResNet variant) achieved a mean average precision of 0.79 across all defect categories. The dataset, annotation tool, and evaluation scripts are released under an open licence to support community benchmarking. Known limitations include an over-representation of PLA material and limited variation in printer manufacturers.

title: Lightweight attention-augmented CNN for on-device FDM defect localisation with limited labelled data
abstract: Industrial FDM monitoring deployments often face constraints in labelled data volume and computational resources simultaneously. This paper proposes a CNN architecture with a lightweight channel-and-spatial attention module inserted after the third convolutional block, designed to run on embedded hardware while matching the localisation accuracy of heavier models. The architecture has 1.4 million parameters, compared to 11.2 million for the ResNet-18 baseline. Training used a semi-supervised strategy combining 600 labelled and 4,800 unlabelled images via consistency regularisation. On the FDMLayerBench test partition, the proposed model achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.73 for defect region localisation, one point below ResNet-18 (0.74), while reducing inference time from 14 ms to 6 ms on the same embedded hardware. Ablation experiments confirm that the attention module contributes 3.1 points of mean IoU over an equivalent model without attention. Failure cases are concentrated in defect boundaries and thin delamination lines narrower than four pixels.

title: Fault Isolation in Multi-Stage Centrifugal Compressors Using Sparse Sensor Placement and Lasso Regression on Spectral Features
abstract: Centrifugal compressors in natural gas processing are monitored at multiple measurement points, but sensor infrastructure is expensive to retrofit. This paper addresses fault isolation using a reduced sensor set selected by a greedy algorithm that maximises fault-class separability while minimising sensor count. Spectral features from 12 candidate accelerometer positions were computed on data from a three-stage compressor test rig under five fault conditions: surge margin reduction, impeller blade wear, seal gas leakage, misalignment, and bearing outer-race damage. A Lasso logistic regression model identified 4 sensor positions sufficient for 88.7% correct fault isolation across 480 test cases, compared with 91.3% using all 12 positions. Installation cost savings are estimated at 38% relative to full instrumentation. Sensitivity analysis shows that the selected four positions remain effective across the tested operating range of 60–100% rated speed. The generalisation of the sensor selection to other compressor geometries is discussed as a limitation.

title: Compressive behaviour of PA12 specimens with uniform lattice infill produced by selective laser sintering
abstract: This study characterises the compressive response of polyamide 12 test coupons with BCC and TPMS-gyroid unit-cell lattice infills fabricated on an EOS Formiga P 110 system. Relative densities of 20 %, 30 %, and 40 % were examined across three build orientations (0°, 45°, 90° to the powder bed). Thirty-six specimens were manufactured and tested on an Instron 5967 at a crosshead speed of 2 mm/min. Load–displacement curves were recorded and elastic moduli, peak stresses, and energy absorption values were extracted. The TPMS-gyroid infill showed 12–18 % higher energy absorption than BCC at equivalent relative density. Build orientation had a statistically significant effect on peak compressive stress (ANOVA, p < 0.01) only for BCC structures. Fractographic analysis by optical microscopy revealed partial powder fusion at strut nodes as the primary failure origin for both topologies. The results provide experimental benchmarks for validating finite element homogenisation models used in subsequent optimisation workflows.

title: A Skill Ontology for Parameterised Pick-and-Place Operations in Flexible Assembly Cells
abstract: This paper presents a formal ontology for describing pick-and-place robot skills at a level of abstraction that is independent of specific robot controllers. The ontology, built in OWL 2, defines 34 skill classes, 18 object properties, and 112 individuals derived from a corpus of 47 existing industrial cell configurations. A reasoner-based consistency checker detects parameter conflicts before code generation. The approach was validated on a KUKA KR6 R900 workcell executing 12 distinct pick-and-place task variants. Correct executable programs were synthesised for 11 of the 12 variants without manual editing; the remaining case required a single parameter correction identified automatically by the reasoner. Average program generation time was 4.3 seconds on a standard workstation. The ontology is serialised in Turtle format and made available as a supplementary file. Results indicate that a structured skill vocabulary reduces workcell setup time by approximately 35 percent compared to manual teach-pendant programming measured across six repeated reconfiguration cycles.

title: Ontology Alignment for Cross-Platform Robot Skill Transfer Between KUKA and Universal Robots Controllers
abstract: Different robot vendors use proprietary data models for describing robot capabilities, which prevents direct reuse of skill descriptions across platforms. This work addresses the alignment of two vendor-specific capability ontologies—one developed for KUKA KRC4 and one for Universal Robots Polyscope—using a semi-automatic alignment procedure based on string similarity, structural analysis, and a small set of manually defined bridge axioms. Alignment quality was evaluated against a gold-standard mapping of 68 concept pairs constructed by two independent domain experts. The resulting alignment achieved precision of 0.87 and recall of 0.81. After applying the alignment, 14 of 17 skill descriptions originally authored for the KUKA platform were executed correctly on the UR5e without further manual editing. The three failing cases involved hardware-specific torque limit parameters that have no direct counterpart in Polyscope and required minor manual intervention. The paper discusses limitations related to semantic heterogeneity and proposes extensions to the alignment procedure for handling numerical parameter ranges.

title: A Constraint-Based Planner for Automatic Sequencing of Welding Skills in Small-Batch Production
abstract: Welding sequence planning in small-batch production is typically done manually by experienced process engineers, a bottleneck when batch sizes fall to single digits and product variants change frequently. This paper describes a constraint satisfaction approach in which weld bead skills drawn from a reusable library are sequenced automatically given a geometric model of the workpiece and a set of quality constraints encoded as OWL restrictions. The planner uses arc-consistency propagation followed by backtracking search. Tests were conducted on a dataset of 30 weld plans for structural steel brackets of varying complexity, ranging from 4 to 19 beads. The planner found valid sequences for 27 of the 30 cases within a 60-second time limit; for the remaining three, it identified and reported conflicting constraints rather than failing silently. Compared to a baseline greedy heuristic, the constraint-based planner produced sequences with 18 percent fewer torch repositioning moves on average, reducing estimated non-productive cycle time. Execution of four selected plans on the KUKA KR6 cell confirmed geometric correctness.

title: Rapid Workcell Reconfiguration Support Using a Semantic Description of Fixtures and End-Effectors
abstract: Physical reconfiguration of a robot workcell—swapping fixtures, grippers, or tool changers—normally requires a programmer to manually update all affected robot programs. This paper proposes a semantic layer in which fixtures and end-effectors are described by OWL individuals linked to their geometric and functional properties. When a reconfiguration event is logged, a rule engine implemented in SWRL propagates changes through dependent skill instances and flags programs requiring regeneration. A simulation study using 120 synthetic reconfiguration scenarios showed that the system correctly identified all affected programs in 117 cases and proposed updated parameter values that passed a geometric feasibility check in 104 of those cases. The remaining 13 cases involved tool-change combinations outside the training scope of the feasibility model. Reconfiguration support was also tested in a live cell over six weeks during a semester-long student project, during which instructors performed 23 actual reconfigurations; 20 resulted in immediately executable regenerated programs. Mean time from reconfiguration logging to regenerated program availability was 8.7 seconds.

title: Comparing Ontology-Based and Behaviour-Tree-Based Approaches to Robot Task Specification in a Shared Human-Robot Assembly Station
abstract: Behaviour trees have become a widely used alternative to classical finite-state machines for specifying robot tasks, and they can also serve as a competitor to ontology-based skill composition. This paper presents a controlled experiment in which four assembly tasks of increasing complexity were implemented using both approaches in a shared human-robot station equipped with a UR5e cobot and a proximity safety system. Implementation effort was measured in person-hours logged by six graduate students who implemented each task in both representations after equivalent training. Execution reliability was assessed over 200 runs per task per representation. Behaviour trees required less initial implementation time on three of four tasks (average 31 percent less) but showed greater maintenance effort when task parameters changed (average 44 percent more time for three representative modifications). Ontology-based programs showed more consistent execution reliability across task complexity levels, with failure rates between 1.5 and 3.0 percent versus 1.2 and 6.8 percent for behaviour trees on the most complex task. The paper discusses conditions under which each approach is preferable.

title: Extracting Reusable Skills from Existing Robot Programs Using Static Analysis and Pattern Matching
abstract: Many manufacturing companies possess large archives of robot programs written in proprietary languages such as KRL or URScript. Migrating these to a skill-based representation manually is labour-intensive. This paper describes a tool that parses KRL and URScript programs, builds abstract syntax trees, and applies a library of 18 pattern templates to identify candidate skill instances. Candidate instances are clustered by structural similarity using a tree-edit-distance metric, and cluster representatives are proposed to the user as new skill library entries. The tool was applied to a corpus of 214 KRL programs obtained from two regional manufacturing companies under a research agreement. It proposed 41 skill candidates, of which domain experts accepted 33 (80 percent acceptance rate) with minor manual adjustments. Rejected candidates were either too hardware-specific or represented one-off operations unlikely to recur. Integration of the 33 accepted skills into an existing library increased its coverage of the source corpus from 54 to 79 percent as measured by fraction of programs fully expressible through library composition.

title: A Benchmark Dataset and Evaluation Protocol for Robot Skill Library Coverage in Assembly Domains
abstract: Progress in robot skill library research is difficult to compare across studies because each group uses different tasks, metrics, and evaluation procedures. This preprint proposes a benchmark consisting of 60 assembly tasks drawn from publicly documented furniture and electronics assembly procedures, annotated with ground-truth skill decompositions agreed upon by five researchers through a structured consensus process. Three coverage metrics are defined: strict coverage (program fully expressible from library), partial coverage (fraction of steps covered), and adaptation coverage (steps coverable after bounded parameter adjustment). The paper reports baseline measurements for four skill libraries described in the literature, including the authors' own, re-evaluated on the benchmark. Strict coverage ranges from 23 to 61 percent across the four libraries on the full 60-task set. The benchmark files, annotation guidelines, and evaluation scripts are deposited in a public repository. The authors invite community feedback on the task selection and metric definitions before submitting a revised version to a journal.

title: Integrating a Robot Skill Ontology with a Manufacturing Execution System via a Lightweight REST API
abstract: Skill-based robot programming tools are typically developed as standalone research prototypes with no direct connection to the production IT infrastructure of a factory. This paper describes the design and implementation of a REST API layer that exposes the skill library and program synthesis engine developed by the authors to a commercial manufacturing execution system used at a regional automotive supplier. The API provides endpoints for querying available skills, requesting program synthesis given a task description in JSON-LD, and submitting the generated program to a robot controller via OPC UA. End-to-end latency from task request to program upload was measured at 6.1 seconds median across 300 requests in a staging environment. A pilot deployment over eight weeks at the partner company involved 47 production orders, of which 41 triggered automatic program synthesis; the remaining six involved task types outside the current library scope and fell back to manual programming. The paper reports observed failure modes and discusses architectural decisions relevant to similar integration efforts.

title: Interval-Censored Survival Analysis for Absenteeism Episodes Recorded at Weekly Resolution
abstract: HR information systems in many organisations record absence start and end dates only at weekly granularity, yielding interval-censored event times rather than exact durations. Standard survival methods assuming exact times underestimate variance and may produce biased covariate effects in this setting. This paper applies interval-censored maximum likelihood estimation via the NPMLE Turnbull algorithm and a parametric interval-censored Weibull model to a dataset of 5,100 absence episodes from four public-sector organisations in Serbia. Simulation experiments with known parameters confirm that the interval-censored Weibull recovers scale and shape parameters within 5% bias when the interval width is up to two weeks. Covariate effects of employee age group, absence spell history, and organisational unit size are estimated under both models and compared. The practical consequence of ignoring interval censoring is a 12–18% underestimate of median absence duration across the studied covariate profiles. Recommendations for HR data collection practices are included.

title: Automatsko mapiranje fonema u vizeme za srpski jezik primenom skrivenih Markovljevih modela
abstract: Rad predstavlja metod automatskog mapiranja fonema srpskog jezika u odgovarajuće vizeme korišćenjem skrivenih Markovljevih modela treniranih na korpusu od 4.200 rečenica izgovorenih od strane 18 govornika. Fonemski skup srpskog jezika sveden je na 14 vizem klasa na osnovu vizuelne sličnosti položaja usana i čeljusti, pri čemu je kategorizacija potvrđena perceptivnim testom sa 32 ispitanika. Eksperimenti su pokazali da model postiže prosečnu preciznost mapiranja od 87,4% u poređenju sa ručno anotiranim referentnim skupom. Greške su najizraženije na afrikativama i nazalima koji dele slične vizuelne karakteristike. Rezultati su evaluirani na dva nezavisna govornika čiji glasovi nisu bili deo skupa za trening, čime je potvrđena generalizabilnost pristupa. Rad postavlja osnovu za automatsku izradu animacija lica za srpski jezik bez potrebe za skupim ručnim anotiranjem.

title: Source-free domain adaptation for human pose estimation using self-supervised skeleton consistency
abstract: Source-free domain adaptation addresses the scenario where the source training dataset cannot be accessed during adaptation, which is practically important when training data contains sensitive imagery. We propose a self-supervised adaptation objective that exploits left-right skeletal symmetry and temporal smoothness as pseudo-supervision signals, requiring only unlabelled target-domain video. The method iteratively updates the model by minimising asymmetry in predicted left- and right-side joint positions and penalising frame-to-frame velocity inconsistencies beyond a learned motion envelope. Evaluated on three target domains — a sports hall, an outdoor construction site, and a care-home corridor — the approach improved mean PCK@0.2 by 6.3 points on average relative to no adaptation, and performed within 2.1 points of a supervised upper bound that uses 200 labelled target frames. Ablations isolate the contribution of symmetry and temporal terms.

title: Extracting Lane-Level Connectivity Graphs from OpenStreetMap Data for Urban Road Networks
abstract: This paper presents a rule-based pipeline for deriving lane-level directed graphs from OpenStreetMap (OSM) vector data in urban environments. The method parses OSM way attributes and relation tags to infer per-lane directionality, turn restrictions, and connectivity at junctions. A total of 14 urban districts in Novi Sad and Subotica were processed, producing graphs with between 800 and 4,200 lane segments each. Topological correctness was evaluated against manually annotated reference graphs: the pipeline achieved a node F1-score of 0.91 and an edge F1-score of 0.87 averaged across all districts. The main failure modes were incomplete tagging of dual-carriageway medians and missing turn-restriction relations. Runtimes ranged from 12 to 47 seconds per district on a single CPU core. The output format is compatible with standard graph libraries and can serve as input for simulation pre-processing. The study also proposes a set of five data-quality indicators that can be computed automatically to flag OSM input regions likely to produce reconstruction errors.

title: Scene Graph Generation as Abductive Logic Programming
abstract: We cast scene-graph generation as an abductive inference problem over a background theory that encodes spatial, semantic, and commonsense constraints. A Faster R-CNN detector provides bounding boxes and object-class scores for 150 categories; these scores are thresholded and asserted as probabilistic facts. An abductive logic programming engine then infers the most consistent assignment of predicates (object identity, spatial relation, action) subject to integrity constraints derived from a handcrafted ontology of 42 spatial and 28 action predicates. The system is evaluated on a synthetic indoor-scene dataset of 8,200 images with ground-truth scene graphs. Triplet recall at 50 IoU reaches 58.3%, outperforming a pure neural baseline (52.7%) and matching a graph-neural-network approach (58.9%) while producing explanations in a form directly readable by downstream planners. Ablation experiments show that commonsense constraints contribute 4.1 recall points; removing spatial constraints reduces recall by 6.8 points.

title: An adaptive large neighbourhood search for routing with time windows and split deliveries
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive large neighbourhood search (ALNS) algorithm tailored for the vehicle routing problem with time windows and split deliveries (VRPTW-SD). In classical routing formulations, each customer must be served by exactly one vehicle; however, in many real-world logistics settings — particularly in urban freight distribution — allowing deliveries to be split across multiple vehicles can substantially reduce total travel distance and improve fleet utilisation. We propose a destroy-and-repair framework in which a portfolio of destroy operators (random, worst, related) and repair operators (greedy, regret-based) are adaptively selected using a roulette-wheel mechanism that rewards recently successful operators. The algorithm incorporates a split-delivery feasibility check embedded directly within the repair phase to avoid infeasible reconstructions. Computational experiments on benchmark instances derived from the Solomon dataset, augmented with split-delivery parameters, demonstrate that the proposed ALNS consistently outperforms a tabu search baseline and a standard genetic algorithm across instances of varying size. For large instances with more than 150 customers, average improvements in total distance of 4.7% are observed. A sensitivity analysis of the adaptive weight update scheme confirms the robustness of the parameter settings. The results suggest that the adaptive mechanism is particularly beneficial for dense urban instances with tight time windows.

title: Same-day delivery with dynamic orders: a rolling-horizon approach
abstract: Same-day delivery (SDD) services require dispatching vehicles for orders that arrive dynamically throughout the operational day, making static routing plans quickly obsolete. This paper proposes a rolling-horizon optimisation framework for SDD in which the planning horizon is partitioned into short decision epochs. At each epoch, a mixed-integer programme is solved to route currently unassigned orders while reserving vehicle capacity for anticipated future demand. Demand forecasts are generated using a simple exponential smoothing model calibrated on historical order patterns. To keep computation tractable within each epoch, we embed an iterated local search heuristic as a warm-start procedure for the optimiser. Experiments conducted on a synthetic dataset modelling a mid-sized European city with 200–600 daily orders show that the rolling-horizon approach reduces average late-delivery rates by 18% compared with a batch-dispatching baseline and by 11% compared with a greedy nearest-neighbour policy. We further analyse the trade-off between epoch length and solution quality, finding that epochs of 20–30 minutes offer the best balance between computational effort and delivery punctuality. The framework is designed to be carrier-agnostic and can be integrated with real-time order management systems.

title: Scheduling with machine availability constraints
abstract: This paper investigates scheduling problems on parallel machines subject to availability constraints, a practically relevant setting in which machines may be unavailable during certain time intervals due to maintenance, breakdowns, or shared resource conflicts. We consider both the non-resumable case, where a job interrupted by a machine unavailability must be restarted from scratch, and the resumable case, where processing can continue after the unavailability window closes. Complexity results are established for single- and parallel-machine variants under makespan and total weighted completion time objectives. For the NP-hard variants, we develop constructive heuristics and a variable neighbourhood search metaheuristic. The variable neighbourhood search explores neighbourhoods defined by job-to-machine reassignment and insertion moves, guided by a shaking procedure that perturbs the current solution by randomly relocating a subset of jobs. Benchmark instances of up to 200 jobs and 10 machines are used to evaluate the algorithms. The variable neighbourhood search achieves solutions within 2.1% of a lower bound on average and significantly outperforms the constructive heuristics on larger instances. Practical implications for production planning in manufacturing environments with predictable maintenance schedules are discussed.

title: A hybrid genetic algorithm for the multi-depot vehicle routing problem with time windows
abstract: The multi-depot vehicle routing problem with time windows (MDVRPTW) extends the classical VRPTW by allowing vehicles to originate from and return to multiple depots, a configuration common in regional distribution networks. This paper proposes a hybrid genetic algorithm (HGA) that combines order-crossover and partially mapped crossover operators with a local search improvement phase based on 2-opt and Or-opt moves. A depot-assignment preprocessing step reduces the solution space by probabilistically assigning customers to depots based on proximity and time-window compatibility before the genetic search begins. The chromosome representation encodes both depot assignment and customer sequencing, and a penalty function handles time-window violations during fitness evaluation to allow controlled infeasibility during evolution. The algorithm is tested on the Cordeau MDVRPTW benchmark set and on a newly constructed instance set representing the logistics geography of the Vojvodina plain. On the Cordeau instances, the HGA matches or improves upon the best-known solutions for 14 out of 23 instances. On the Vojvodina instances, routing cost savings of up to 9.3% over a nearest-depot greedy construction are demonstrated. The study highlights the importance of depot assignment as a pre-optimisation lever and offers guidance on parameter tuning for practitioners deploying multi-depot fleet management systems.

title: Crowdsourced last-mile delivery: routing models and optimisation under uncertain courier availability
abstract: Crowdsourced delivery platforms engage occasional, non-professional couriers to fulfil last-mile shipments, offering flexibility and reduced fixed costs compared with dedicated fleets. However, courier availability is inherently stochastic, creating routing challenges absent from classical vehicle routing models. This paper formulates the crowdsourced last-mile delivery problem as a two-stage stochastic programme in which first-stage decisions assign packages to couriers and second-stage recourse decisions re-route undelivered packages using a backup dedicated fleet. A sample average approximation scheme is used to handle the stochastic availability, and a large neighbourhood search heuristic is developed to solve the resulting integer programme efficiently. Numerical experiments on instances derived from actual parcel-demand data collected during the LASTMILE-NS project in Novi Sad demonstrate that the stochastic model reduces expected total cost by 12.4% compared with a deterministic model that ignores courier dropout risk. We also quantify the value of the stochastic solution and analyse how it varies with courier reliability, package time-sensitivity, and backup fleet size. The findings provide actionable insights for platform operators balancing cost efficiency and service reliability in urban crowdsourced logistics.

title: Green vehicle routing with heterogeneous electric fleets and charging scheduling
abstract: The electrification of urban delivery fleets introduces new constraints into vehicle routing: limited battery range, discrete charging decisions, and time spent at charging stations must all be modelled explicitly. This paper addresses the green vehicle routing problem with a heterogeneous electric fleet (HGVRP-EV), where vehicles differ in load capacity, battery capacity, and energy consumption rate. A mixed-integer linear programming formulation is presented, incorporating partial recharging decisions and multiple charging station types with different power levels. Because exact solvers cannot handle instances of realistic size within practical time limits, we develop an iterated greedy metaheuristic augmented with a charge-scheduling subroutine that optimally allocates charging time at each visited station given the remaining tour. The algorithm is benchmarked on adapted instances from the E-VRP literature and on a new Novi Sad urban network instance with 12 charging stations. Results show that allowing partial recharging reduces total route duration by up to 15% compared with full-recharge-only policies. A sensitivity analysis examines the impact of charging infrastructure density on fleet size requirements, offering practical guidance for city planners and fleet operators transitioning to electric vehicles.

title: Time-indexed formulations and cutting planes for parallel machine scheduling with sequence-dependent setup times
abstract: Sequence-dependent setup times arise in many manufacturing and service scheduling environments where the time required to prepare a machine for a new job depends on the identity of the preceding job. This paper studies the parallel machine scheduling problem with sequence-dependent setup times (PMSDST) under the objective of minimising total weighted tardiness. We propose a time-indexed integer programming formulation that, while large in size, admits a tight linear programming relaxation. A branch-and-cut algorithm is developed in which valid inequalities — including precedence cuts, clique inequalities derived from incompatibility graphs, and novel setup-chain cuts — are separated and added dynamically. The algorithm is implemented using a commercial branch-and-bound solver with a callback interface. For instances with up to 40 jobs on 4 machines, the branch-and-cut closes the optimality gap to within 0.5% in under one hour of computation. For larger instances, we compare with a simulated annealing heuristic and demonstrate that the cutting plane bounds serve as effective quality certificates for heuristic solutions. The paper contributes both to the theoretical understanding of PMSDST polyhedral structure and to practical algorithm engineering for production scheduling applications.

title: Metaheuristic comparison for the capacitated vehicle routing problem: a unified computational study
abstract: A large number of metaheuristic algorithms have been proposed for the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) over the past three decades, yet systematic comparisons under controlled experimental conditions remain scarce. This paper presents a unified computational study that evaluates seven prominent metaheuristics — simulated annealing, tabu search, genetic algorithm, ant colony optimisation, particle swarm optimisation, large neighbourhood search, and iterated local search — on a common set of 120 CVRP benchmark instances ranging from 50 to 500 customers. All algorithms are implemented within the same software framework to eliminate implementation bias, and hyperparameters are tuned using a factorial experimental design. Performance is assessed across three dimensions: solution quality relative to best-known solutions, computational time, and robustness across instance classes. Large neighbourhood search and iterated local search emerge as the most competitive methods overall, with tabu search performing best on small dense instances. The study also examines the correlation between instance structural features (customer density, demand variability, depot centrality) and algorithm performance, providing guidance for algorithm selection in practice. All code and instance data are made publicly available to support reproducibility.

title: Urban consolidation centres and their impact on last-mile routing efficiency: a simulation-optimisation study
abstract: Urban consolidation centres (UCCs) are intermediate logistics facilities where shipments from multiple carriers are consolidated before final delivery, with the goal of reducing the number of vehicles operating in congested city centres. This paper integrates a discrete-event simulation model of urban freight flows with a vehicle routing optimisation engine to evaluate the cost and emission impacts of UCC deployment in a medium-sized city. The simulation captures stochastic demand arrival, consolidation delays, and time-varying road congestion, while the optimisation layer solves a time-window-constrained routing problem for outbound UCC vehicles at each simulated day. A simulation-optimisation loop iterates between the two components using a response surface methodology. Experiments are conducted using a calibrated model of freight demand in Novi Sad, drawing on parcel volume data collected under the LASTMILE-NS project. Results indicate that a single well-located UCC can reduce total vehicle kilometres travelled by 22% and CO2 emissions by 19% compared with decentralised direct delivery, though these benefits depend critically on UCC location and carrier participation rates. Policy scenarios exploring mandatory versus voluntary carrier participation are also analysed.

title: A matheuristic for the periodic vehicle routing problem with service choice
abstract: The periodic vehicle routing problem (PVRP) extends the classical VRP to a multi-day planning horizon, requiring each customer to be visited a specified number of times per period while respecting day-assignment and routing constraints. In the variant considered here, customers may choose from a menu of service frequency options (e.g., once versus twice per week), and the carrier must optimise both the day-assignment and routing decisions jointly with the customer service-choice recommendations to maximise profit. We develop a matheuristic that alternates between a column-generation procedure — which optimises day assignments and service choice for a fixed set of routes — and a large neighbourhood search that improves the routing for a fixed assignment. The column-generation subproblem is solved as a shortest-path problem with resource constraints using dynamic programming. On standard PVRP benchmark instances the matheuristic matches best-known solutions in 80% of cases within five minutes. On new instances with service choice, the joint optimisation yields profit improvements of 7–14% over sequential approaches that first fix service choices and then optimise routing. The algorithm is directly applicable to subscription-based delivery services and pharmaceutical distribution.

title: Sparse Keypoint Tracking for Monocular Visual Odometry on Resource-Constrained Platforms
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of real-time monocular visual odometry on embedded processors with limited arithmetic throughput. We adapt a FAST-based keypoint detector combined with a binary descriptor to operate within a 40 ms per-frame budget on an ARM Cortex-A9 running at 800 MHz. Experiments were conducted on three indoor sequences totalling 1.2 km of trajectory length, collected with a custom wheeled robot in the Faculty of Technical Sciences building. Relative translation error averaged 1.8% and relative rotation error 0.9 deg/m across all sequences. We further analyse the sensitivity of tracking quality to scene texture density and propose a simple texture-adaptive threshold that reduces track loss by 23% compared to a fixed threshold baseline. The system was implemented entirely in C++ without GPU acceleration, making it suitable for small autonomous vehicles.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Feature Descriptors for Indoor Visual Localization Under Varying Illumination
abstract: Robust localization in indoor environments requires feature descriptors that tolerate significant illumination changes between map-building and localization phases. We evaluate six binary and two floating-point descriptors — including ORB, BRISK, BRIEF, FREAK, SIFT, and SURF — across a dataset of 14 indoor rooms photographed under three controlled illumination levels (500 lux, 150 lux, and 30 lux). Images were acquired with a calibrated industrial camera mounted on a motorised pan-tilt head. Matching recall at a fixed precision of 0.9 is used as the primary metric. BRISK achieves the best recall–speed trade-off in low-light conditions, while SIFT retains higher absolute recall under extreme illumination reduction. We also report matching latency on both desktop and embedded hardware and discuss implications for SLAM back-end map reuse. The dataset is released publicly under a Creative Commons licence.

title: First Steps with Event Cameras: Asynchronous Feature Detection for Low-Latency Ego-Velocity Estimation
abstract: Event cameras generate asynchronous streams of per-pixel brightness change events at microsecond resolution, but most existing feature detectors assume synchronous frame data. This paper adapts a corner-like event surface representation — the surface of active events (SAE) — to detect stable tracking features from asynchronous event streams. We extract Harris-like corner scores from the SAE and show that stable features can be identified with median latency of 0.9 ms from the triggering event cluster on a Prophesee Gen3 sensor. Ego-velocity estimation is performed by fitting a six-parameter event-plane model to spatiotemporal event clusters using RANSAC. On a laboratory turntable dataset with ground-truth angular velocity from a calibrated servo motor, mean angular velocity error is 0.31 deg/s. This work establishes the processing pipeline used in subsequent studies from our group.

title: Calibration of Event Camera–IMU Systems: Temporal and Spatial Extrinsics
abstract: Accurate extrinsic and temporal calibration between event cameras and inertial measurement units is a prerequisite for tight fusion in visual-inertial odometry. Existing calibration toolboxes designed for frame cameras produce biased results when applied directly to event cameras because the noise model and timing assumptions differ substantially. We present a calibration procedure that uses a blinking LED pattern at known frequencies to excite the event sensor while simultaneously exciting the IMU with structured motion. Spatial extrinsics are estimated via a nonlinear optimisation minimising the reprojection of 3D LED positions derived from event-based reconstruction. Time offset estimation achieves a standard deviation of 47 µs across ten repeated calibration runs on a DAVIS 346 sensor paired with a Bosch BMI085 IMU. The calibration software is released as an open-source ROS package.

title: High-Dynamic-Range Scene Reconstruction from Event Streams: A Gradient Integration Approach
abstract: Standard frame cameras saturate in high-dynamic-range scenes, corrupting SLAM front-end tracking. Event cameras respond to logarithmic brightness changes and tolerate dynamic ranges exceeding 120 dB, but dense intensity reconstruction from events remains an open problem. We present a gradient integration method that accumulates event-stream polarity and magnitude into a per-pixel gradient field and solves a screened Poisson equation to recover absolute intensity. On an outdoor dataset collected in Novi Sad city centre under direct sunlight and deep shadow within the same frame, our method reconstructs scenes with mean absolute error of 4.2% relative to a HDR reference captured with exposure bracketing. Integration with a downstream SLAM pipeline reduces front-end tracking loss rate from 18% per 100 m to 3% compared to using a standard CMOS frame camera.

title: Event-Driven Visual-Inertial Odometry on a Microaerial Vehicle in Cluttered Indoor Environments
abstract: Microaerial vehicles (MAVs) operating in cluttered indoor spaces require state estimation with latency well below 10 ms to maintain stability. We implement a tightly coupled event-camera–IMU odometry system on a custom quadrotor with a Prophesee Metavision M event camera and a VectorNav VN-100 IMU. The estimator uses an event-driven extended Kalman filter (EKF) updated asynchronously on each event cluster of 500 events, with IMU propagation between clusters. In 12 indoor flight trials averaging 90 s duration each, the system achieves mean drift of 1.4% of path length with no loop closure. IMU-propagated latency is 0.7 ms and event-update latency is 2.3 ms, both measured end-to-end on the onboard Jetson Orin NX. We characterise failure cases caused by vibration-induced noise and propose a spectral filter that reduces false-positive events by 40%.

title: Benchmarking Event-Based SLAM Algorithms on a Controlled Outdoor Testbed
abstract: A reliable comparison of event-based SLAM algorithms requires datasets with precisely known ground truth and controlled environmental conditions. We describe a benchmarking testbed built around a linear motion stage and a motorised turntable instrumented with sub-millimetre encoders, capable of executing repeatable six-DoF trajectories at speeds up to 3 m/s. Four event-based odometry algorithms are evaluated on 48 sequences spanning three lighting conditions (overcast, direct sun, artificial night lighting) and two scene types (textured facade, low-texture wall). Results show that continuous-time methods outperform discrete-time methods by 22–35% in translational RMSE under direct sunlight, while discrete-time methods are 1.8× faster in computation. The dataset and evaluation scripts are made available for the community. We discuss systematic sources of error specific to event-camera benchmarking not present in frame-camera evaluations.

title: Event Cameras for Autonomous Ground Vehicles: Opportunities and Open Problems
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of event cameras to autonomous ground vehicle perception, covering sensor physics, available hardware platforms, ego-motion estimation methods, and integration into full autonomy stacks. We categorise the literature into model-based and learning-based approaches and identify three open problems: (1) reliable performance on wet road surfaces where reflections generate spurious events, (2) robust semantic segmentation from event streams, and (3) standardised calibration and synchronisation protocols for multi-sensor rigs that include event cameras. The chapter draws on the authors' practical experience operating event-camera-equipped vehicles in urban environments in Serbia and Austria and includes an annotated bibliography of 87 primary sources covering work published up to mid-2022.

title: Asynchronous Depth Estimation from Stereo Event Cameras Using Semi-Global Matching
abstract: Stereo event cameras can in principle provide dense depth maps at sub-millisecond latency, but the asynchronous and sparse nature of events makes classical stereo matching algorithms ill-suited. We adapt semi-global matching (SGM) to operate on event-accumulated disparity volumes constructed from time-surface representations of the left and right camera event streams. Disparity volumes are constructed over sliding windows of 5 ms and updated incrementally. On a newly recorded stereo event dataset of an industrial warehouse environment with a 15 cm stereo baseline, our method achieves median absolute disparity error of 1.2 pixels at 24 Hz effective frame rate, compared to 2.7 pixels for a single-frame SGM baseline using accumulated frames. We also evaluate depth accuracy against a LiDAR reference and report mean absolute depth error of 4.3 cm at 2 m range.

title: Spiking Neural Network Front-End for Event-Based Corner Detection with On-Chip Learning
abstract: Conventional event-camera processing pipelines run on GPUs or CPUs, introducing memory transfer overhead that limits achievable latency. We investigate whether a small spiking neural network (SNN) implemented on an Intel Loihi 2 neuromorphic chip can replace the SAE-based corner detector used in our visual odometry pipeline. The SNN is trained offline using surrogate-gradient backpropagation on a labelled corner event dataset of 120,000 event frames and then mapped to Loihi 2 cores. On-chip inference latency is 0.18 ms per 1,000-event batch, compared to 1.1 ms for the SAE baseline on an ARM Cortex-A78 core. Corner detection F1-score is 0.81 against a frame-camera ground truth annotation, slightly below the SAE baseline at 0.85 but acceptable for downstream odometry, which shows a 6% increase in translational RMSE relative to the SAE-based system. Power consumption on Loihi 2 is 310 mW versus 1.9 W for the CPU baseline.

title: Dot Height Retention in UV-Cured Relief Braille on Coated Folding Boxboard After Accelerated Ageing
abstract: Braille dots produced by UV-cured inkjet relief printing on 300 g/m² coated folding boxboard were subjected to accelerated ageing cycles simulating 12 months of ambient warehouse storage (40 °C, 75 % RH, 1 000 h). Dot height, dome radius, and base diameter were measured with a Mitutoyo SJ-410 profilometer at 0, 250, 500, and 1 000 h. A total of 480 individual dots across six commercial ink formulations were assessed. Mean dot height declined by 11–23 % depending on formulation, with the lowest-viscosity ink showing the greatest loss. Cell-C grade readability according to EN ISO 17351 was maintained by four of the six inks at the 1 000 h endpoint. Statistical analysis used repeated-measures ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc correction. Results indicate that ink elastic modulus, measured by nano-indentation, predicts long-term height retention better than initial viscosity. Recommendations are given for specifying minimum initial dot height margins to guarantee compliance after shelf life.

title: Effect of Embossing Pressure and Die Temperature on Braille Dot Geometry in Recycled Cartonboard
abstract: Recycled cartonboard (RC) grades with post-consumer fibre contents of 30 %, 60 %, and 100 % were embossed under a systematic design-of-experiments matrix varying die temperature (60–120 °C) and line pressure (80–160 N/cm). Dot height, inter-dot spacing, and springback ratio were recorded immediately after embossing and after 48 h conditioning at 23 °C and 50 % RH. A total of 216 test sheets were produced on a Billhöfer laboratory embossing press. Springback in the 100 % RC grade reached 28 % compared with 14 % in virgin board under identical conditions. Optimal process windows achieving EN ISO 17351 Grade B compliance were identified for each grade. The study provides a practical decision matrix for packaging converters transitioning to recycled substrates without compromising Braille legibility. Microscopic cross-sections confirmed that higher fibre heterogeneity in RC grades contributed to dot-base irregularity.

title: Tactile Reading Speed and Error Rate as a Function of Braille Dot Diameter: A User Study with 32 Participants
abstract: Thirty-two experienced Braille readers (18–67 years, 19 women) recruited through a regional blind association evaluated five test cards bearing standardised pharmaceutical text encoded in Braille with dot diameters ranging from 1.2 mm to 1.8 mm in 0.15 mm increments, produced on a calibrated embossing press. Reading speed (characters per minute) and error rate (misidentified cells per 100 characters) were recorded under two lighting conditions (irrelevant to tactile task, included as a distractor control). Mixed-effects regression models showed that a 1.5 mm dot diameter maximised reading speed (mean 68 cpm) while maintaining error rate below 3 %. Participants over 50 years showed a statistically significant preference for 1.6 mm diameter (p = 0.031). Results are discussed in the context of current EN ISO 17351 tolerances, which permit a wider range than the optimal window identified here. Implications for pharmaceutical packaging standards revision are outlined.

title: Thermoforming Depth and Wall Angle Influence on Tactile Symbol Legibility in PETG Blister Packaging
abstract: Tactile warning symbols intended for medication blister packs were vacuum-thermoformed into PETG film (250 µm) over aluminium moulds at draw depths of 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 mm and wall angles of 5°, 10°, and 15°. A full factorial design yielded 27 combinations; each was replicated three times. Symbol sharpness was quantified by edge-slope angle measured via optical profilometry, and legibility was rated on a four-point scale by 24 sighted participants wearing blindfold masks. Deeper draws combined with steeper wall angles produced the sharpest tactile edges but also the highest incidence of surface micro-crazing, assessed by SEM. A draw depth of 0.6 mm with a 10° wall angle offered the most consistent combination of legibility and surface integrity. Material thickness reduction at symbol walls ranged from 8 % to 31 % and correlated linearly with draw depth (R² = 0.91). Guidance is provided for mould design in pharmaceutical blister production.

title: Comparative Assessment of Four Braille Embossing Methods on Corrugated Microflute Board
abstract: Four embossing methods—dry embossing, wet embossing, counter die embossing, and heat-assisted embossing—were applied to E-flute and F-flute corrugated microflute board used in secondary pharmaceutical packaging. Dot height, dot density uniformity, and substrate damage (delamination, flute crush) were quantified across 120 samples per method-substrate combination. Wet embossing on F-flute achieved the highest mean dot height (0.52 mm) with lowest flute crush index, while dry embossing on E-flute produced the most uniform dot array (coefficient of variation 4.2 %) but at a reduced mean height of 0.38 mm. All methods except dry embossing on E-flute met the EN ISO 17351 minimum height threshold of 0.48 mm. Cross-sectional micrographs confirmed that flute deformation contributed to within-cell dot height variation. Practical guidance for selecting method–substrate combinations in secondary packaging lines is provided.

title: Surface Topography Metrics for Predicting Braille Dot Detectability: Correlation with Psychophysical Threshold Data
abstract: Surface topography parameters Sa, Sz, Ssk, and Sku extracted from white-light interferometry scans of embossed Braille dots were correlated with tactile detection thresholds measured in a two-alternative forced-choice experiment with 18 participants who were congenitally blind. Detection thresholds were determined using a staircase method at reading-fingertip locations (index finger, dominant hand). Among the parameters tested, Sz (maximum height of the scale-limited surface) showed the strongest correlation with detection threshold (Pearson r = −0.78, p < 0.001), outperforming the conventional dot height measurement used in EN ISO 17351. A regression model based on Sz and Ssk predicted detection probability with a root-mean-square error of 0.07. The findings suggest that multi-parameter surface topography assessment could supplement or replace single-dimensional dot height as a conformity criterion. Implications for standard revision and quality-control instrumentation in packaging plants are discussed.

title: Dimensional Tolerances of Commercial Pharmaceutical Packaging Braille: Audit of 200 Products on the Serbian Market
abstract: Two hundred commercially available pharmaceutical secondary packs bearing Braille were purchased from pharmacies in Novi Sad and Belgrade. Dot height, diameter, inter-dot spacing, and inter-cell spacing were measured with a profilometer on three replicate cells per pack. Conformity with EN ISO 17351 was assessed. Of 200 packs, 61 % met all four dimensional criteria simultaneously; 24 % failed on dot height alone; 9 % failed on inter-dot spacing. Imported products from Western European manufacturers showed a non-compliance rate of 18 %, while domestically packed products showed 47 % non-compliance. Packs embossed into aluminium foil laminate underperformed those on solid cartonboard (mean height 0.31 mm vs. 0.51 mm). The audit provides baseline data for regulatory enforcement discussions and identifies foil laminate as a substrate category requiring targeted technical guidance. Data were collected in 2013–2014.

title: Tactile Map Reproduction Quality on Vacuum-Thermoformed ABS Sheets for Educational Use
abstract: Raised-line tactile maps for school-age students with visual impairments were produced by vacuum thermoforming of 1.5 mm ABS sheet over master moulds generated by FDM 3D printing at three resolution settings (0.1, 0.2, and 0.4 mm layer height). Line width, line height, and edge definition were measured by laser profilometry on 45 test maps. The 0.1 mm master produced tactile lines with mean height 0.61 mm and edge slope 72°, rated as legible by all 10 student evaluators in a structured haptic task. The 0.4 mm master introduced staircase artefacts perceptible as roughness rather than line edges, reducing task completion rate from 94 % to 61 %. Thermoforming temperature (140–180 °C) had minimal effect on line geometry within the range tested. The findings support use of FDM masters at ≤0.2 mm layer height for educationally adequate tactile map reproduction.

title: Inter-Laboratory Reproducibility of EN ISO 17351 Dot Height Measurement: Round Robin Study Across Seven Laboratories
abstract: Seven laboratories in five countries (Serbia, Hungary, Croatia, Slovenia, and Germany) each received identical sets of 30 embossed cartonboard test specimens and measured dot height using their own profilometry or contact-measurement equipment following EN ISO 17351 procedures. Measurement uncertainty was calculated per ISO/IEC Guide 98-3 (GUM). Between-laboratory standard deviation was 0.041 mm for dot height and 0.028 mm for dot diameter. Four laboratories using stylus profilometry showed tighter inter-instrument agreement (σ = 0.022 mm) than three using optical methods (σ = 0.049 mm). Laboratories applying a 0.8 mm cut-off wavelength filter produced systematically lower height values than those using no filter, with a mean bias of 0.038 mm. The findings expose a measurement gap in the current standard text, which does not specify filter parameters. A draft amendment recommendation is formulated.

title: Print Relief Height Achieved by Multiple UV Inkjet Passes: Parametric Study on Glass and Cartonboard Substrates
abstract: UV inkjet relief printing was performed with a modified flatbed printer at 1 to 8 overprint passes on two substrates: standard glass (for controlled surface energy reference) and 300 g/m² coated cartonboard. Dot height, diameter, and sidewall angle were recorded after each pass by stylus profilometry. On glass, height increased linearly up to six passes (R² = 0.98), yielding 0.61 mm at pass 8. On cartonboard, ink absorption and substrate compressibility caused height growth to plateau after four passes at 0.44 mm, falling just below the EN ISO 17351 threshold. Adding a UV-opaque primer layer before the first Braille pass raised the four-pass height on cartonboard to 0.51 mm. Sidewall angle on glass reached 68° at pass 6, declining to 54° at pass 8 due to ink spread. The study provides a practical pass-count optimisation tool for flatbed UV Braille printing operations.

title: Teaching Accessible Packaging Design: Curriculum Integration of Tactile Print Standards in Undergraduate Graphic Engineering Education
abstract: This paper reports on a curriculum intervention introduced at the Department of Graphic Engineering and Design, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in which EN ISO 17351 and tactile print production were integrated into a fourth-year Packaging Design course over three academic years (2016–2019). Student learning outcomes were assessed before and after the intervention using a validated knowledge test (24 items) and a practical embossing assignment graded against standard conformity criteria. Mean test scores rose from 41 % (pre) to 74 % (post) over the three cohorts (n = 112 students total). The proportion of practical assignments achieving EN ISO 17351 Grade B or better increased from 28 % in 2016–17 to 61 % in 2018–19. Student feedback indicated that hands-on evaluation with visually impaired volunteer readers was the most valued component. The curriculum model is described in sufficient detail to support adoption at comparable institutions.

title: Influence of post-print lamination on spectrophotometric measurements and ICC profile validity
abstract: Lamination films applied over printed sheets alter the spectral reflectance of the underlying print by introducing a gloss or matte surface layer with a distinct refractive index. This study quantified those changes for three lamination types — gloss, matte, and soft-touch — applied to offset-printed coated paper characterised with an ECI2002 ICC profile prior to lamination. Spectrophotometric measurements were taken before and after lamination using both 45°/0° and integrating-sphere geometries, and the resulting CIELAB shifts were mapped across the printed gamut. Gloss lamination produced systematic CIELAB lightness reductions of 1.5–3.2 ΔL* in shadows, matte lamination reduced chromatic saturation by ΔC*ab 2.0–4.8 in mid-tones, and soft-touch lamination combined both effects. The pre-lamination ICC profile was found to be inadequate for post-lamination proofing; a correction LUT derived from the spectral shift data reduced mean ΔE2000 from 3.3 to 0.9 without requiring a full re-characterisation. The correction approach is applicable as a one-time calibration per lamination film type and press substrate combination.

title: Perceived Usefulness or Fear of Job Loss? Disentangling Employee Motives for Resisting ERP Implementation in Serbian SMEs
abstract: Enterprise resource planning systems are increasingly adopted by small and medium-sized enterprises across the Western Balkans, yet implementation failure rates remain high. This study investigates whether resistance is driven primarily by usability concerns, anticipated workload changes, or fears about employment security. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 214 employees across 31 manufacturing and retail SMEs in Vojvodina during 2023. Structural equation modelling with partial least squares (SmartPLS 4) was applied to test a model combining the Technology Acceptance Model with job-insecurity theory. Results indicate that perceived threat to employment explains a significantly larger portion of resistance variance (β = 0.41, p < 0.001) than perceived ease of use (β = 0.18, p < 0.05). Moderating effects of organisational tenure were found: employees with more than seven years at the same firm showed stronger fear-based resistance. Trust in direct management partially mediates the relationship between job insecurity and resistance intention. The findings suggest that communication strategies addressing job security concerns should precede usability training during ERP rollout in this context.

title: Middle Managers as Gatekeepers: Qualitative Evidence on Digital Change Mediation in Serbian Family-Owned Firms
abstract: Family-owned small enterprises represent a large share of the Serbian private sector, yet their internal dynamics during digital transformation programmes are rarely studied qualitatively. This paper presents findings from semi-structured interviews with 19 middle managers employed in family-owned service and trade businesses in Novi Sad and Subotica, conducted between October 2024 and February 2025. Using thematic analysis in ATLAS.ti, the study identifies three recurring roles that middle managers assume during digital initiatives: loyal implementers, selective filters, and covert saboteurs. The selective-filter role was most frequently observed and was associated with middle managers who perceived a mismatch between the digital tool introduced and existing informal workflows. Owner-family involvement was found to both accelerate adoption when owners championed the technology and to deepen resistance when ownership authority was perceived as bypassing middle management. Participatory decision-making during tool selection was cited by fourteen of the nineteen respondents as the single most important factor that would have increased their engagement. Findings contribute to research on middle management agency in organisational change and carry practical implications for consultants advising owner-managed firms on digital transition strategies.

title: Using O*NET Task Data as a Starting Point for Local Job Analysis: Adaptation Challenges in a Transition Economy Context
abstract: O*NET, the United States occupational information network, provides detailed task and competency data that researchers worldwide use as a convenient reference point. This methodological paper examines the practical and conceptual challenges that arise when O*NET task data are adapted for job analysis work in a transition economy manufacturing context, drawing on experience from three adaptation projects conducted in Serbia between 2015 and 2022. Challenges identified include: the granularity mismatch between O*NET standardised occupational codes and Serbian occupation classification categories; differences in technology vintage meaning that O*NET task statements describe equipment not present in regional plants; cultural differences in task ownership norms leading to boundary disagreements; and translation ambiguities in technical terminology. For each challenge, adaptation strategies are documented and their effectiveness evaluated through post-adaptation validity checks. The paper provides a structured checklist for practitioners undertaking similar adaptations in comparable contexts.

title: Integrating Event-Calendar Features into Short-Term Hotel Demand Forecasting Models
abstract: City hotels in mid-size European markets are strongly affected by recurring local events—congresses, fairs, sports tournaments—yet most off-the-shelf demand forecasting modules treat event effects as unpredictable noise. This preprint describes a forecasting framework that augments a SARIMA baseline with a structured event-calendar feature matrix compiled from public sources for Novi Sad over 2016–2023. Three event categories are coded: large-scale music festivals (e.g., multi-day outdoor events drawing 40,000+ daily visitors), regional trade fairs, and major sporting fixtures. A gradient-boosted tree model incorporating these features reduces mean absolute percentage error on a held-out test set by 11.4 percentage points relative to the calendar-blind baseline. Revenue simulations suggest that timely rate adjustments triggered by the improved forecasts would have added approximately 6.1% to annual RevPAR for the median hotel in the validation sample.

title: Integrating Market and Non-Market Strategies: Evidence from Regulated Industries in the Western Balkans
abstract: This paper examines how firms in three heavily regulated industries—electricity retail, private healthcare, and commercial banking—coordinate their market and non-market strategies in the Western Balkans. A fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is applied to a dataset of 41 firms coded on nine conditions derived from resource-dependence and institutional theory. Two sufficient configurations for high integration of market and non-market strategies are identified: one centred on state partial-ownership combined with high regulatory density, and another centred on foreign parent ownership combined with active industry-association participation. The absence of either configuration correlates strongly with reactive rather than anticipatory non-market positioning. The paper also addresses methodological considerations in applying fsQCA to strategy research in data-scarce institutional environments. Results replicate and extend findings from earlier Western European studies while highlighting the distinctive role of partial state ownership as a non-market resource in Balkan contexts.

title: Diverzitet arbuskularnih mikoriza u vinogradima Fruške gore: preliminarni pregled morfotipova

title: Seasonal shifts in arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal communities in a conventionally managed Graševina vineyard on Fruška Gora
abstract: We monitored AMF community composition at monthly intervals across a full growing season (April–October 2011) in a single-cultivar Graševina vineyard near Sremski Karlovci. Root samples were collected from twelve marked vines and assessed for colonisation rate using the gridline-intersect method. Spore suspensions were prepared by wet sieving. Fungal communities were characterised by cloning and Sanger sequencing of the SSU rRNA gene (n = 312 clones). Colonisation peaked in July at 74 % and dropped to 31 % after harvest. Community composition shifted from Rhizophagus irregularis-dominated assemblages in spring toward more diverse communities including Claroideoglomus and Diversispora taxa in midsummer. Shannon diversity index ranged from 1.1 in April to 2.4 in August. Soil moisture and root sugar content were the best predictors of both colonisation intensity and community turnover in a partial RDA framework (R² = 0.61). These findings establish a seasonal baseline relevant for timing inoculation practices.

title: Uticaj prelaska sa konvencionalnog na organski sistem gajenja vinove loze na zajednice Glomeromycota u zemljištu
abstract: U cilju praćenja promena u zajednicama arbuskularnih mikoriza nakon konverzije u organsku proizvodnju, odabrana su tri para susednih parcela na Fruškoj gori kod kojih je jedna parcela prešla na organsku proizvodnju 2010. godine, dok je susedna zadržala konvencionalne prakse. Uzorkovanje je vršeno godišnje tokom trogodišnjeg perioda (2011–2013), sa po 24 uzorka po parceli svake jeseni. Fragmenti rDNA amplifikovani su prajmerima AM1/NS31 i klonisani. Analiza OTU-ova pokazala je statistički značajno povećanje bogatstva vrsta na organskim parcelama treće godine (p < 0,05), sa porastom indeksa raznovrsnosti sa 1,8 na 2,6. Zastupljenost Paraglomus vrsta bila je veća na organskim parcelama, što se poklapa sa smanjenjem dostupnog fosfora u zemljištu. Organska agrotehhika je pokazala merljiv uticaj na sastav AMF zajednice već nakon tri sezone, naročito u pogledu retkih taksona.

title: Root colonisation intensity and spore density as proxies for AMF community health in Fruška Gora organic vineyards
abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal colonisation intensity and spore density are widely used indicators of AMF activity but their relationship to community composition remains unclear. We sampled fifteen organic vineyards distributed across the Fruška Gora foothills in autumn 2014, collecting 180 root and soil samples. Colonisation was scored by the Trouvelot scale, and spore density was determined by wet sieving. Community composition was assessed using 454 pyrosequencing targeting the ITS2 region, yielding 41,200 quality-filtered reads assigned to 38 VT (virtual taxa). Colonisation intensity and spore density were only weakly correlated (r = 0.32). Spore density was a better predictor of community richness (R² = 0.48) than colonisation intensity (R² = 0.21). The two most abundant VTs, affiliated with Rhizophagus and Septoglomus, dominated across all sites regardless of proxy values. We conclude that neither metric alone adequately represents community diversity and recommend their combined use alongside molecular characterisation.

title: Ectomycorrhizal fungi associated with oak windbreaks bordering vineyards on Fruška Gora: potential reservoirs of inoculum
abstract: Oak hedgerows and windbreaks bordering vineyards on Fruška Gora support diverse ectomycorrhizal (ECM) fungal communities that may serve as inoculum sources for adjacent agricultural soils. We sampled ECM root tips from 28 Quercus cerris trees along windbreak strips flanking seven organic vineyards in autumn 2015 and spring 2016. Morphotyping was followed by ITS1-5.8S-ITS2 Sanger sequencing (n = 224 tips). Forty-one ECM taxa were recorded, dominated by Tomentella and Inocybe s.l. genera. Soil hyphal ingrowth bags placed at distances of 0.5, 1.5, and 3.0 m from windbreak edges showed declining ECM hyphal biomass with distance (16.4, 7.1, and 1.8 mg NLFA 16:1ω5 per g soil, respectively). AMF taxa were found at all distances. Although ECM fungi are not typical vineyard mutualists, the proximity gradient suggests that mixed-fungal inoculum pools exist within at least 1.5 m of windbreak edges.

title: Procena metoda inokulacije komercijalnim AMF preparatima u rasadnicima vinove loze u Vojvodini
abstract: Komercijalni preparati koji sadrže arbuskularne mikorize sve se više koriste u rasadničarskoj praksi, ali podaci o njihovoj efikasnosti u lokalnim uslovima Vojvodine su oskudni. U ovom istraživanju testirani su tri komercijalna preparata (označena kao P1, P2 i P3) i neinokulisana kontrola na sadnicama Cabernet Sauvignon tokom rasadničke sezone 2016–2017. Primenjena su dva načina inokulacije: zamakanje žila i primena na supstrat. Parametri rasta (visina, masa suvih žila, ukupna masa), stopa kolonizacije i morfotipi identifikovani su na kraju sezone. Preparati P1 i P3 statistički su značajno povećali masu suvih žila (za 28 % i 31 % redom), dok P2 nije pokazao statistički značajan efekat. Zamakanje žila bilo je efikasnije od primene na supstrat (p < 0,01). Kolonizacija endogenim gljivicama bila je prisutna u svim tretmanima uključujući kontrolu, što upućuje na aktivnu mikoriznu zajednicu u supstratu. Preporučuje se obavezno testiranje lokalnih sojeva pre uvođenja komercijalnih preparata.

title: High-throughput amplicon sequencing reveals distinct AMF communities under different cover crop regimes in Fruška Gora vineyards
abstract: Cover crops are increasingly adopted in Serbian viticulture as a soil management strategy, yet their effect on AMF communities is poorly documented in this region. We established a replicated field trial in 2017 across three organic vineyards on Fruška Gora, comparing four cover crop treatments (ryegrass monoculture, phacelia monoculture, mixed legume–grass, bare soil control). Soil samples collected in spring and autumn 2018 and 2019 (n = 288 total) were processed for Illumina MiSeq amplicon sequencing targeting the SSU rRNA gene. A total of 1,240,500 quality-filtered reads were assigned to 62 VTs. Mixed legume–grass cover significantly increased AMF richness relative to bare soil control (ANOVA, p < 0.01) in both seasons and both years. Rhizophagus irregularis VT113 was dominant across all treatments. Diversispora VTs were enriched under legume–grass cover. Bare soil plots showed the lowest diversity and highest within-plot beta diversity, suggesting community instability. Cover crop type explained 18 % of community variance in a permanova framework.
venue: Soil Biology and Biochemical Interactions

title: Phosphorus and nitrogen gradients shape AMF community turnover across a Fruška Gora toposequence
abstract: Nutrient gradients along hillslope toposequences may drive spatial turnover in AMF communities independently of management practices. We sampled soils from ridge, midslope, and footslope positions in nine organic vineyards distributed across a 14 km transect on Fruška Gora in 2020. Soil chemistry (pH, Olsen-P, total N, organic C) was determined at each of 81 plots. AMF communities were characterised by Illumina MiSeq SSU amplicon sequencing. Olsen-P was highest at footslope positions (mean 18.4 mg kg⁻¹) and lowest at ridges (7.1 mg kg⁻¹). Community dissimilarity (Bray-Curtis) between ridge and footslope within the same vineyard was comparable to dissimilarity between different vineyards at the same topographic position. Olsen-P and total N jointly explained 24 % of community variance (db-RDA). Archaeospora VTs were disproportionately enriched at low-P ridge positions. These results indicate that nutrient redistribution along slopes represents an underappreciated driver of intra-vineyard AMF heterogeneity.
venue: Plant and Soil Ecology

title: Uticaj suše na kolonizaciju mikorize i razmenu fosfora u vinogradima sa smanjenim navodnjavanjem
abstract: Suša kao faktor stresa menja ravnotežu u mikoriznim simbiozama jer biljke redistribuiraju ugljenik od simbionata prema sopstvenoj odbrani. U ovom radu pratili smo 24 Prokupac čokota u organskom vinogradu tokom sušne sezone 2021. godine, koristeći sistem delimičnog sušenja rizosfere (PRD) naspram potpunog navodnjvanja i prirodnog padavinskog tretmana. Stopa kolonizacije merena je na svake tri nedelje; fosfor u ksilemu uzorkovan je punkcijom. Pregled AMF zajednice obavljen je amplikon sekvenciranjem na kraju sezone. Kolonizacija je bila najviša u tretmanu bez navodnjavanja (68 %) ali je prenos fosfora u ksilem bio statistički značajno niži nego u PRD tretmanu (p < 0,05). Shannon indeks AMF raznovrsnosti nije se statistički razlikovao između tretmana, ali se taksonomski sastav promenio u korist Claroideoglomus-dominantnih zajednica u sušnom tretmanu. Nalaze treba razmatrati u kontekstu predviđenog povećanja učestalosti suše u Panonskom regionu.
