title: Mycorrhizal network connectivity estimates in organic vineyard blocks using quantitative PCR species-specific assays
abstract: Common mycelial networks (CMNs) potentially redistribute carbon and water between neighbouring grapevines but their extent under field conditions is poorly quantified. We developed qPCR assays targeting three dominant AMF VTs (affiliated with Rhizophagus irregularis, Funneliformis mosseae, and Claroideoglomus claroideum) in a single 0.4 ha organic Riesling block on Fruška Gora. In 2022 and 2023, root and hyphal ingrowth core samples were collected at 1 m intervals along three parallel transects. Assay efficiency ranged from 93 to 98 % (R² > 0.99). Gene copy numbers for all three VTs were spatially autocorrelated (Moran's I > 0.4) at scales up to 3 m, suggesting continuous hyphal networks across at least a single vine interrow. Network connectivity was higher in spring than autumn and declined following copper-based fungicide application in both years. The qPCR approach provides a resolution not achievable with community-level sequencing alone.

title: Pedološki i klimatski faktori koji određuju AMF sastav u Fruškogorskim vinogradima: metaanaliza setova podataka 2010–2023
abstract: Sistematska istraživanja sprovođena od 2010. do 2023. godine na vinogradima Fruške gore akumulirala su obimne skupove podataka o zajednicama AMF, hemiji zemljišta i klimatskim parametrima. U ovom radu sprovedena je metaanaliza ovih skupova podataka (n = 1.140 uzoraka, 31 lokalitet, 14 sezona uzorkovanja) korišćenjem jedinstvenog protocola ponovnog mapiranja svih sekvenci na referentnu MaarjAM bazu podataka. Identifikovano je ukupno 84 VT u analiziranom skupu podataka. Ograničena analiza permanova sa deset pedoloških i klimatskih kovariata pokazala je da pH, Olsen-P i letnja suma padavina zajedno objašnjavaju 31 % varijanse zajednice. VT bogatstvo značajno je opalo na parcelama sa pH < 5,8 i Olsen-P > 25 mg kg⁻¹. Detekcija retkih taksona (zastupljenost < 0,1 %) bila je konzistentna između godina samo na parcelama bez fumigacije. Rezultati ukazuju na potrebu harmonizovanog dugoročnog monitoringa AMF zajednica u vinogradima jugoistočne Evrope.

title: Seasonal dynamics of leaf mineral status in 'Braeburn' apple across a rootstock series: a two-year field study
abstract: Leaf mineral composition in apple is routinely interpreted using single-point sampling norms, yet the seasonal trajectory of mineral accumulation may differ by rootstock. This study tracked weekly leaf concentrations of N, P, K, Ca, Mg, Fe, Mn, Zn, and Cu in 'Braeburn' grafted on M.9 NAKB T337, M.26, Jork 9, and a dwarfing seedling selection from Novi Sad (NS-D2) from leaf emergence to post-harvest leaf fall over 2015 and 2016. ICP-OES data from 1,104 individual leaf samples revealed that the timing of the mid-season Ca plateau differed by up to 18 days among rootstocks, with M.26 reaching plateau earliest. Jork 9 produced significantly higher midsummer leaf Mn (62.4 vs. 38.1 mg kg⁻¹ dry weight on M.9). The data challenge the common practice of applying a single sampling date for diagnostic leaf analysis across rootstock types and provide corrected reference windows for each rootstock examined.
venue: Journal of Pomology and Small Fruits

title: Rehabilitacija riparijalnih zelenih koridora uklanjanjem Amorpha fruticosa: trogodišnji monitoring autohtonih vrsta
abstract: Prikazani su rezultati trogodišnjeg monitoringa (2020–2022) na 10 lokaliteta duž kanala Begej i DTD, gde su 2019. godine sprovedene mere mehaničkog uklanjanja Amorpha fruticosa u kombinaciji sa sadnjom autohtonih žbunova (Cornus sanguinea, Sambucus nigra, Viburnum opulus). Kontrolne parcele su ostavljene bez intervencije. Na tretiranim parcelama praćeni su preživljavanje sadnica, pokrivenost autohtonih vrsta, rekolonizacija A. fruticosa i diverzitet herbasnog sloja. Nakon tri godine, preživljavanje sadnica kretalo se od 61% (V. opulus) do 79% (C. sanguinea). Pokrivenost autohtonih žbunova u tretiranim parcelama bila je statistički značajno veća nego u kontrolama (Mann–Whitney U test, p < 0.01). Rekolonizacija A. fruticosa bila je primetan problem na 7 od 10 lokaliteta, što ukazuje na neophodnost višegodišnjeg naknadnog održavanja. Rad daje konkretne preporuke za protokole restauracije.

title: Side-Channel Leakage in AES Implementations on 8-Bit AVR Microcontrollers: A Comparative Power Analysis Study
abstract: This paper evaluates the susceptibility of three publicly available AES-128 software implementations to simple and differential power analysis on an 8-bit AVR ATmega328P microcontroller. We collected 50,000 power traces per implementation using a 1 GHz digital oscilloscope and a 1-ohm shunt resistor, then applied standard DPA with a Hamming-weight model. All three implementations leaked the full 128-bit key within 10,000 traces; the fastest implementation (executing in 4,112 clock cycles) proved most vulnerable, with a signal-to-noise ratio 2.3 times higher than the most compact one. Countermeasures including boolean masking and shuffled S-box lookups were applied and re-evaluated; masking reduced the distinguishability metric by 87% at the cost of a 34% increase in execution time. The results provide a quantitative baseline for hardening AES on severely constrained nodes, directly informing subsequent work on post-quantum primitives for similar platforms.
venue: Journal of Embedded Systems and Security Research

title: Benchmarking SHA-3 Candidates on ARM Cortex-M3: Cycle Counts, Stack Usage, and Energy Consumption
abstract: We ported and benchmarked five finalist and alternate candidates from the NIST SHA-3 competition—Keccak, Skein-512, Grøstl, BLAKE, and JH—on an ARM Cortex-M3 running at 72 MHz with 20 kB of SRAM. For each candidate we measured clock cycles per byte for message lengths of 64, 256, and 4096 bytes, peak stack consumption, and energy drawn from a 3.3 V supply using a precision current sensor. Keccak achieved the lowest energy per byte (1.14 µJ for 256-byte messages) but consumed the most stack (3,584 bytes). BLAKE offered the best throughput at 15.2 cycles/byte for long messages. Grøstl was slowest on this architecture due to poor utilisation of 32-bit word operations. The dataset is publicly archived and intended to serve as a reference for designers selecting hash functions for sensor node firmware, and as a comparison point for future post-quantum scheme evaluations that rely on these primitives.

title: Memory-Efficient Polynomial Multiplication for NTRU on a 32-Bit Microcontroller
abstract: NTRU encryption requires repeated polynomial multiplication in truncated polynomial rings, and naïve convolution is prohibitively slow on constrained hardware. This work implements and compares three multiplication strategies—schoolbook convolution, Karatsuba decomposition, and a Number Theoretic Transform adapted to NTRU parameters—on an STM32F103 Cortex-M3 running at 72 MHz with 20 kB RAM. The NTT approach requires 512 bytes of working memory for degree-509 polynomials and achieves 148,000 clock cycles per multiplication, compared to 1.92 million for schoolbook convolution. Karatsuba occupies a middle ground at 340,000 cycles with minimal stack overhead. Code size across all three variants was kept below 8 kB of flash. We profile the full NTRU-HPS key-generation and encapsulation routines and show that NTT-based multiplication reduces total encapsulation time from 28.4 ms to 4.1 ms at 72 MHz. The implementation is validated against known test vectors from the NTRU reference package.

title: Practical Fault Injection Attacks Against a Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism on a Smart Card
abstract: We investigate the fault resilience of a software implementation of Kyber-512 running on a Java Card 3.0.4 smart card with an ARM SC300 security core. Using a voltage glitching station with sub-microsecond pulse resolution, we injected faults during the decapsulation procedure and collected 6,800 faulty ciphertexts over three days of automated testing. By applying a variant of the decryption failure attack, we recovered 128-bit session keys from 42% of successful fault injections within a single-bit error model. We further show that a simple instruction-count check at the end of the decapsulation loop detects 91% of our glitch attempts with zero false positives in 5,000 benign runs. The results indicate that Kyber implementations on real smart card hardware need explicit fault countermeasures beyond those assumed in the formal security proofs, and we propose a concrete software hardening checklist derived from our observations.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography on Constrained Devices: Implementation Strategies and Open Challenges
abstract: This book chapter surveys the state of post-quantum cryptographic implementations on microcontrollers, smart cards, and IoT gateways as of 2017. We categorise the main algorithm families—lattice-based, code-based, hash-based, and multivariate—by their suitability for constrained platforms, defining 'constrained' as under 64 kB RAM and under 256 kB flash. For each family we summarise published benchmarks, identify the primary performance bottlenecks (arithmetic units, memory bus width, absence of hardware multipliers), and discuss known implementation pitfalls such as non-constant-time modular reduction. A comparative table covers 14 schemes across seven hardware platforms. We also discuss the implications of NIST's post-quantum standardisation process for industry adoption timelines and the specific gap between academic proof-of-concept implementations and production-grade secure firmware. The chapter concludes with a prioritised list of open engineering problems, including the need for unified benchmarking methodology and hardware-assisted arithmetic support.

title: Comparing CRYSTALS-Dilithium and Falcon Signature Verification Speed on ARM Cortex-M4
abstract: We implement the NIST post-quantum signature finalists CRYSTALS-Dilithium (security levels 2 and 3) and Falcon-512 in C with platform-specific assembly optimisations for the ARM Cortex-M4 FPU on an STM32F407 board running at 168 MHz. Dilithium-2 verification takes 1.37 ms and requires 13.2 kB of stack; Dilithium-3 requires 1.89 ms and 16.8 kB. Falcon-512 verification takes 2.11 ms but requires only 7.4 kB of stack, making it preferable for devices with less than 10 kB SRAM. Signing is substantially more expensive for Falcon due to the discrete Gaussian sampler: 14.8 ms versus 3.2 ms for Dilithium-2. We also measure flash footprint and provide a side-by-side energy profile collected with a USB power monitor. All source code and raw trace data are released under a permissive open-source licence. The findings inform a practical selection guide for firmware engineers choosing between the two schemes.

title: A Hardware Security Module Architecture Supporting Hybrid Classical/Post-Quantum Key Exchange for Industrial Controllers
abstract: This paper describes the design and prototyping of a hardware security module intended for attachment to programmable logic controllers in industrial automation environments. The HSM combines an Infineon SLE97 secure microcontroller for classical ECDH key agreement with a separate FPGA fabric (Lattice iCE40UP5K) dedicated to Kyber-768 key encapsulation. The hybrid design ensures backward compatibility while adding quantum resistance. We detail the inter-chip communication protocol, a SPI-based command interface with authenticated encryption, and the key storage layout. Full key exchange (hybrid ECDH + Kyber-768) completes in 38 ms end-to-end. The FPGA implementation of Kyber uses 3,200 LUTs and 12 kB of embedded block RAM. Power consumption during key exchange peaks at 210 mW and averages 42 mW at idle. We evaluate the design against the IEC 62443-4-2 security level 2 requirements and identify three areas requiring further hardening before production deployment.

title: Stack and Heap Memory Profiling of SPHINCS+ on RISC-V RV32IMC Without Hardware Multiplier
abstract: SPHINCS+ is a stateless hash-based signature scheme selected for standardisation by NIST, but its relatively large signature sizes and tree traversal operations raise questions about feasibility on severely memory-constrained RISC-V cores lacking the M (multiply) extension. We port all three SPHINCS+-SHA2 and SPHINCS+-SHAKE parameter sets to bare-metal RISC-V RV32I (without M extension) on a 32 kB RAM, 256 kB flash target and measure peak stack depth, heap allocation, code size, and cycle counts. Without a multiplier, SHA-256 compression function throughput drops by 6.1x compared to RV32IM. Signing with SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s (the smallest parameter set) requires 28.4 kB of stack and 1.84 billion cycles, which is infeasible for latency-sensitive applications at typical MHz clock rates but acceptable for infrequent firmware update signing. We propose a streaming tree-node computation that reduces peak stack to 11.2 kB at a 9% cycle overhead, and validate correctness against the NIST Known Answer Tests.

title: Timing Variability in Constant-Time Dilithium Implementations Across Different Compiler Optimisation Levels
abstract: Lattice-based signature schemes such as CRYSTALS-Dilithium are typically written to be constant-time, but compiler optimisations can inadvertently introduce data-dependent timing variation by reordering or eliminating branchless constructs. We compile a reference Dilithium-2 implementation using GCC 11 and Clang 14 at optimisation levels O0 through O3 and Os on ARM Cortex-M4 and x86-64, then measure timing distributions for 100,000 signing operations with message inputs sampled uniformly at random. At O3 with GCC on x86-64, we observe a 14-cycle bimodal spread in the rejection sampling loop that correlates weakly (Pearson r = 0.19) with the norm of the signing randomness. Leakage detection using Welch's t-test and TVLA methodology crosses the threshold of |t| = 4.5 in three of eight compiler/architecture combinations. We trace each instance to specific compiler transformations visible in the generated assembly and propose source-level annotations (using the volatile barrier idiom) that suppress the leakage in all tested configurations.

title: Towards a Standardised Benchmarking Suite for Post-Quantum Cryptography on Embedded Targets
abstract: Comparing published implementation results for post-quantum schemes is difficult because researchers use different clock frequencies, compiler flags, measurement methods, and reporting conventions. This paper proposes a minimal benchmarking suite—PQBench-Embed—that specifies four representative hardware targets (ARM Cortex-M0+, Cortex-M4, RISC-V RV32IMC, and ESP32), a fixed GCC toolchain version and flag set, a cycle-counting harness based on hardware performance counters, and a structured JSON output format for result reporting. We validate the suite by collecting results for Kyber-512, Dilithium-2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and Classic McEliece 348864 across all four targets. Results show that cross-architecture speedup ratios for the same algorithm vary by up to 3.1x depending on benchmarking methodology, confirming the need for standardisation. The suite and all collected data are released as a public repository. We also provide a discussion of what metrics matter most for different deployment scenarios such as TLS handshake, firmware signing, and device attestation.

title: Cache-Timing Attacks on ML-KEM (FIPS 203) in a Shared-Memory Embedded RTOS Environment
abstract: Embedded real-time operating systems increasingly run multiple isolated tasks sharing a common data cache, creating conditions for cache-timing side channels even on microcontrollers. We study ML-KEM (FIPS 203, formerly Kyber) running as a FreeRTOS task on an STM32H743 Cortex-M7 with a 16 kB 4-way set-associative L1 data cache and a co-resident adversarial task with unprivileged access. Using a Prime+Probe variant adapted for the Cortex-M7 cache geometry, the adversary task collects 250,000 cache access measurements and applies a correlation distinguisher to the modular reduction tables. We recover 4 bits of the decapsulation secret with probability greater than 0.8, demonstrating a practical (though partial) leakage channel. We then evaluate three mitigations: cache-line aligned constant-time modular arithmetic, OS-level cache flushing between task switches, and disabling the data cache entirely. The last option increases ML-KEM decapsulation time from 0.31 ms to 1.87 ms and is impractical for most deployments, while aligned arithmetic eliminates the observed leakage with a 4% cycle overhead.

title: Traceability Between Requirements and ARXML Artefacts in AUTOSAR Development
abstract: Establishing traceable links between functional requirements and AUTOSAR model artefacts is required by ISO 26262 for software at ASIL B and above, yet toolchain support for this is fragmented. This paper reports on a traceability framework, TraceAR, that stores bidirectional links between requirement identifiers in a ReqIF document and elements in one or more ARXML files, using a trace metamodel serialised as a lightweight XML sidecar. The framework was implemented as an Eclipse plug-in with a matrix view and impact analysis function. It was evaluated in a 12-week study with four engineers working on a powertrain control ECU with 284 functional requirements and a corresponding AUTOSAR model containing 1 140 traceable elements. Coverage analysis showed 91% of requirements linked after the study period; initial linkage completeness before tool adoption had been estimated at 47% based on project documentation. Engineers rated the impact analysis function as the most practically valuable feature in post-study interviews.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Joint Offloading and Beam Selection in mmWave-Assisted IoT Edge Nodes
abstract: This paper investigates the use of a deep Q-network to simultaneously select beam directions and offloading fractions at mmWave-equipped edge nodes serving dense IoT clusters. A custom simulation environment is constructed in Python using ray tracing channel models parameterised for an indoor factory scenario at 28 GHz with 64-element ULA antennas. The agent observes local queue length, residual energy, and a coarse channel quality indicator quantised to four levels. Training uses 200,000 environment steps with an experience replay buffer of 10,000 transitions. The learned policy achieves a 28% reduction in energy-per-bit compared to a heuristic that handles beam selection and offloading independently, and maintains queue stability at arrival rates up to 85% of channel capacity. Ablation experiments show that joint optimisation accounts for most of the gain over independent control.

title: Subspace Identification of Multizone Thermal Dynamics in a Renovated School Building
abstract: Thermal coupling between adjacent zones complicates single-zone modelling approaches and motivates multivariate state-space identification. This paper applies a subspace identification algorithm (N4SID) to estimate a coupled three-zone state-space model for a renovated primary school in Zrenjanin, Serbia, heated by a central hot-water system with zone-level thermostatic valves. Input variables were valve opening signals and outdoor temperature; outputs were zone air temperatures sampled at 15-minute intervals over one full heating season. The estimated 6th-order state-space model captured inter-zone heat transfer through internal partitions and achieved a simulation RMSE below 0.35 °C in all three zones over a 30-day validation window. Model order reduction via balanced truncation yielded a 4th-order approximation with less than 5% increase in validation error, suitable for real-time model predictive control implementation on an embedded Linux platform. Energy simulations using the reduced model indicated that coordinated multizone control could reduce heating energy use by 14–17% relative to independent thermostat operation.

title: Loop Nest Optimisation for Sparse Tensor Contractions on an Out-of-Order Accelerator with Prefetch Buffers
abstract: Sparse tensor contractions involve loop nests whose iteration spaces are implicitly defined by the sparsity pattern of one or more operands. Standard loop transformations such as tiling and interchange assume dense rectangular iteration spaces and do not directly apply. This paper reformulates loop tiling for sparse iteration spaces by treating the compressed index arrays as first-class objects during the transformation and deriving tile boundaries from statistical properties of the non-zero structure. Prefetch buffer allocation is handled by a separate pass that inserts prefetch instructions at tile entry points, guided by a cost model calibrated on the target accelerator. Experiments on an RTL-level simulation of a six-stage out-of-order accelerator show 19–27% reduction in stall cycles for eight tensor contraction benchmarks from quantum chemistry. The paper reports sensitivity to tile size and discusses interaction with register allocation.

title: Contact-angle hysteresis on corona-treated recycled kraftliner: effect of treatment intensity and shelf-life
abstract: Corona treatment of recycled kraftliner at four power densities (5, 10, 15, and 20 W·min/m²) was studied by advancing and receding contact-angle measurements using distilled water, diiodomethane, and formamide as probe liquids. The Owens–Wendt–Rabel–Kaelble method was applied to resolve polar and dispersive surface-energy components. Immediately after treatment at 15 W·min/m², total surface energy rose from 31 to 54 mJ/m²; the polar component accounted for 18 mJ/m² of the gain. Ageing at 23 °C and 50 % RH showed a 40 % decline in polar component within 72 hours, attributed to reorientation of oxidised functional groups. Attenuated total-reflectance FTIR confirmed the disappearance of carbonyl and hydroxyl bands correlated with this decay. The data suggest a practical reprocessing window of no more than 48 hours for wet-flexo operations on this substrate class.

title: Peel strength of water-based flexographic inks on old corrugated container board: role of recycled-fibre content
abstract: Four corrugated medium grades with recycled-fibre content ranging from 50 % to 100 % were corona-treated and printed with a commercial cyan water-based flexographic ink on a laboratory proofer at a constant anilox volume of 6.5 cm³/m². Peel adhesion was measured at 90° after 24-hour cure at 23 °C/50 % RH. Boards with higher recycled content exhibited rougher surfaces (Ra 3.8–6.2 µm versus 1.9 µm for virgin stock) and greater ink spread, yet peel force was 15–22 % lower compared with virgin fibre boards. Mercury intrusion porosimetry indicated that excessive ink penetration into the porous recycled substrate reduced the cohesive film thickness available for adhesive bonding. A regression model relating surface roughness, ink penetration depth, and peel force is proposed, explaining 81 % of variance in the dataset.

title: Influence of starch surface sizing on corona-treatment effectiveness of recycled testliner
abstract: Starch surface sizing is widely applied to recycled testliner to improve surface strength, but its interaction with corona-treatment outcomes is poorly documented. This study compared unsized and starch-sized recycled testliner (oxidised maize starch, 2.5 g/m² coat weight) treated at 0–20 W·min/m². Contact-angle measurements using the OWRK protocol showed that the sized board achieved a maximum surface energy of 49 mJ/m² at 15 W·min/m², compared with 54 mJ/m² for the unsized reference. Scanning electron microscopy showed that the starch film partially sealed surface pores, limiting oxidised-group density achievable by corona. Despite lower absolute surface energy, sized boards showed superior ink-holdout and print gloss, indicating that porosity reduction compensates for reduced surface energy in practical printing. Ink-set time was reduced by 28 % on the sized variant.

title: Water-based flexographic ink performance on recycled board at temperatures from −20 °C to +23 °C
abstract: Cold-chain packaging for frozen goods must maintain print integrity at sub-zero temperatures, yet the low-temperature behaviour of water-based flexographic inks on recycled board has received little systematic attention. Four commercial water-based inks (two acrylic-resin, two styrene–acrylic-resin binders) were printed on recycled kraftliner, conditioned for 24 h, then evaluated at −20, −10, 0, and +23 °C for tape adhesion (ASTM D3359), scratch resistance (Elcometer 3092), and blocking tendency. Tape-adhesion scores declined from 4B at +23 °C to 2B at −20 °C for acrylic-binder inks; styrene–acrylic binders retained 4B down to −10 °C. Dynamic mechanical analysis of free ink films indicated that the glass-transition temperature of acrylic binders (Tg ≈ +4 °C) was responsible for embrittlement below 0 °C. A minimum Tg ≤ −15 °C is recommended for consistent cold-chain performance.

title: Comparative evaluation of surface energy measurement protocols for porous recycled fibre substrates
abstract: Four wettability-based surface-energy protocols—OWRK, Wu harmonic-mean, van Oss–Chaudhury–Good (vOCG), and Zisman critical surface tension—were applied to eight recycled and mixed fibre board grades. Reproducibility (coefficient of variation across three operators) and agreement with measured ink-adhesion peel force were used as performance criteria. The vOCG method showed the highest reproducibility (CV < 5 %) but required a third polar probe liquid, making it more time-consuming. OWRK and Wu methods produced comparable results for non-absorbing reference surfaces but diverged by up to 9 mJ/m² on highly porous recycled boards, attributed to rapid imbibition of polar probe liquids. Correlation with 90° peel force was strongest for OWRK (r² = 0.77). Recommendations for standardising measurements on porous substrates are provided, including a maximum measurement delay of 3 s after droplet deposition.

title: Optimising corona-discharge parameters for heterogeneous recycled packaging boards using a response-surface approach
abstract: Recycled packaging boards sourced from three European mills exhibited substantial variability in initial surface energy (28–37 mJ/m²) due to differing furnish compositions and coating histories. A central composite response-surface design with four factors (electrode gap 1–3 mm, line speed 50–150 m/min, power density 5–20 W·min/m², ambient humidity 30–65 % RH) was used to model total surface energy and polar component as responses. Forty-three experimental runs were performed. The quadratic model explained 88 % of variance in total surface energy; power density and electrode gap were the dominant factors, with a statistically significant interaction. A validated optimal treatment window (gap 1.5 mm, 12 W·min/m², 40–55 % RH) yielded total surface energy ≥ 50 mJ/m² across all three board grades, reducing within-batch variability in ink adhesion peel force from ± 0.9 N/cm to ± 0.3 N/cm.

title: Effect of bio-based additives on cold-temperature flexibility of water-based flexographic inks
abstract: Rosin ester and sorbitol-based plasticisers derived from bio-based feedstocks were incorporated into a styrene–acrylic water-based flexographic ink formulation at 2, 4, and 6 phr. Free ink films were cast and characterised by differential scanning calorimetry, dynamic mechanical analysis, and tensile testing at −20, 0, and +23 °C. Rosin ester at 4 phr reduced Tg from −8 °C to −22 °C without significant loss of blocking resistance. Elongation at break at −20 °C improved from 3 % to 14 % at the same loading. Printed samples on recycled kraftliner subjected to a 180° mandrel bend at −20 °C showed no cracking at 4 phr rosin ester, compared with visible cracking in the unmodified reference. Migration of plasticiser to the substrate surface, assessed by XPS after 30-day storage, was below detection limits at 4 phr.

title: Moisture absorption cycling and its effect on surface energy and ink adhesion of recycled packaging boards
abstract: Recycled packaging boards used in humid distribution environments undergo repeated wetting and drying cycles that alter fibre network topology and surface chemistry. Six board grades were subjected to 0, 3, 6, and 10 moisture-cycling events (65 % RH / 23 °C for 12 h followed by 10 % RH / 23 °C for 12 h). Surface energy was measured by OWRK after each cycle. Total surface energy declined monotonically with cycling, with the polar component falling by up to 35 % after 10 cycles, attributed to progressive hornification of surface fibres confirmed by solid-state ¹³C NMR. Corona treatment applied after 10 cycles restored surface energy to levels comparable with once-cycled boards, though peel adhesion recovery was partial (recovery ratio 0.78 ± 0.06). The results have implications for the timing of corona treatment in converting operations handling previously warehoused recycled board.

title: Ink–substrate interaction in cold-environment flexographic printing: a review of measurement approaches and influencing factors
abstract: This chapter reviews published methods and findings concerning the interaction between water-based flexographic inks and fibre-based substrates under cold or thermally varying conditions, with emphasis on adhesion measurement, rheological characterisation, and binder selection. The chapter covers contact-angle and surface-energy measurement protocols, peel and tape-adhesion tests, scratch and abrasion resistance assays, and their applicability to cold-chain packaging certification. Key influencing factors discussed include binder glass-transition temperature, ink viscosity–temperature relationships, substrate porosity and surface sizing, corona-treatment stability, and the effect of cold condensation on ink–substrate contact. The literature spans work published between 2000 and 2019. Gaps identified include a lack of standardised cold-temperature adhesion test protocols, limited data on bio-based ink systems, and absence of long-term field studies correlating laboratory results with distribution-chain print failure rates.

title: XPS depth profiling of corona-oxidised surfaces on 100 % recycled containerboard: distribution of functional groups across the fibre network
abstract: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy was used to profile the depth distribution of oxygen-containing functional groups introduced by corona treatment on 100 % recycled containerboard. Ar⁺ cluster-ion sputtering enabled sequential sampling to a depth of approximately 600 nm. The O/C ratio reached a maximum of 0.42 at the outermost 0–20 nm layer and fell to 0.18 at 300 nm, indicating that oxidation is concentrated near the surface. Carbon 1s peak deconvolution revealed that C–O and C=O groups account for 38 % and 12 % of total carbon signal, respectively, in the outermost layer, compared with 18 % and 4 % in untreated board. Mapping across a 500 µm × 500 µm area showed inhomogeneous group distribution correlated with local fibre orientation and filler particle clusters, which may explain variability in ink adhesion across the print area. Data support a surface-specific rather than bulk mechanism of corona activation.

title: Performance retention of water-based flexographic prints on recycled board after simulated frozen-food distribution: vibration, cold-shock, and condensation cycling
abstract: Printed corrugated cases destined for frozen-food distribution face a combination of mechanical vibration, cold shock, and condensation exposure not captured by any single standard test. Recycled kraftliner printed with a commercial four-colour water-based flexographic ink set was subjected to a sequence of: (i) random vibration at 0.5 g rms for 60 min at −18 °C, (ii) thermal shock from −18 °C to +8 °C over 30 min, and (iii) 90 % RH exposure at +8 °C for 2 h, repeated for 5 cycles. Print quality (optical density, ΔE, ink-film cracking) and adhesion (tape peel, cross-cut) were assessed after each cycle. Ink cracking was first observed after cycle 3 on acrylic-binder inks; styrene–acrylic binders showed no cracking through cycle 5. Optical density loss was below 5 % for all systems. Tape adhesion declined by one ASTM class for acrylic binders after the combined exposure. The combined test protocol is proposed as a basis for industry acceptance criteria.

title: Rheological characterisation of water-based flexographic inks at temperatures between −5 °C and +40 °C relevant to cold-chain printing operations
abstract: Ink rheology at the temperatures encountered during cold-chain converting is rarely reported but influences transfer and levelling behaviour. Seven commercial water-based flexographic inks (viscosities 18–65 mPa·s at 23 °C) were characterised by rotational and oscillatory rheometry between −5 °C and +40 °C. All inks showed Newtonian behaviour at shear rates above 1000 s⁻¹ across the full temperature range. Apparent viscosity at 0 °C was 1.4–2.1-fold higher than at 23 °C; at −5 °C, two inks exhibited a partial gel structure (loss tangent < 1 at 1 Hz). Temperature–viscosity data were fitted to the Williams–Landel–Ferry equation for the range 0–40 °C (r² > 0.98). Print mottle on recycled board increased significantly below 5 °C for inks with viscosities exceeding 50 mPa·s at 23 °C. A practical guideline recommending substrate and ink temperature conditioning above 10 °C prior to printing is supported by the data.

title: Effect of post-print UV-C exposure on adhesion and barrier properties of water-based flexographic coatings on recycled board
abstract: UV-C irradiation (254 nm, dose 0.5–3.0 J/cm²) applied to water-based flexographic over-print varnishes on recycled board was investigated as a means of improving crosslink density without transitioning to UV-curable systems. Three varnish formulations (polyurethane dispersion, styrene–acrylic, and a polyurethane–acrylic hybrid) were evaluated for tape-adhesion retention, water-vapour transmission rate, and surface gloss after UV-C doses of 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0 J/cm². The polyurethane–acrylic hybrid at 2.0 J/cm² showed a 22 % improvement in tape-adhesion score and a 31 % reduction in water-vapour transmission rate compared with untreated controls. FTIR analysis confirmed formation of additional urethane linkages post-irradiation. Over-exposure at 3.0 J/cm² caused surface yellowing (ΔE > 3) and a 15 % gloss reduction. The data indicate a usable UV-C dose window of 1.5–2.5 J/cm² for the polyurethane–acrylic system.

title: Residence time effects on fixed-bed pyrolysis of corn stover: product distribution and energy balance
abstract: A parametric study was conducted in a bench-scale fixed-bed reactor using milled corn stover (particle size 0.5–1.0 mm, moisture 8.3 wt%) at 500 °C with residence times of 15, 30, 60, and 120 minutes. Gas, liquid (bio-oil), and solid (biochar) product fractions were gravimetrically quantified. At 15 min, biochar yield was 32.4% and bio-oil 38.1%; extending residence time to 120 min reduced biochar yield marginally to 29.6% while increasing non-condensable gas fraction from 18.2 to 24.5 wt%. Bio-oil higher heating value ranged from 16.8 to 18.3 MJ kg⁻¹. An energy balance across the reactor showed that the char fraction retained 38–44% of feedstock energy regardless of residence time, whereas extended holding increased secondary cracking of bio-oil vapours. Recommendations for process optimisation targeting simultaneous biochar and syngas valorisation are presented.

title: Bounded reachability for piecewise-affine hybrid automata using delta-satisfiability
abstract: This paper addresses the bounded reachability problem for hybrid automata whose continuous dynamics are described by piecewise-affine differential equations, a class that covers many embedded control scenarios. The approach encodes the reachability query as a satisfiability problem over the reals and applies the dReal solver with a delta-relaxation parameter set to 10^-6. Experiments are conducted on four benchmark control loops drawn from automotive throttle and braking models, each with state spaces of dimension four to seven. For all benchmarks, the tool either certifies safety within a horizon of 50 discrete steps or produces a concrete counterexample trace. Computation times range from 8 seconds to 14 minutes on a standard workstation, depending on the number of mode transitions allowed. The paper also characterises the completeness threshold beyond which spurious counterexamples begin to appear as a function of the Lipschitz constant of the dynamics. The results suggest that delta-satisfiability scales acceptably for systems with up to three continuous state variables per mode but degrades sharply beyond that.
venue: Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Formal Verification and Synthesis (CEWFVS)

title: Abstraction refinement for safety verification of sampled-data control loops modelled as hybrid automata
abstract: Sampled-data controllers introduce a periodic discrete transition at every sampling instant, and this regularity can be exploited to construct coarser abstractions without sacrificing soundness. This paper presents a counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR) procedure tailored to sampled-data hybrid automata. The abstraction partitions the continuous state space into polyhedral cells using support-function computations, and the refinement step splits cells whose spurious transitions violate a simple Lyapunov-based separation criterion. The procedure is implemented as an extension to the SpaceEx reachability platform. Evaluation covers three proportional-integral controllers embedded in thermal management and DC motor drive case studies, with sampling periods between 1 ms and 10 ms. In all cases, the refined abstraction certifies a safety invariant within at most five refinement iterations. The paper reports the number of polyhedral cells at each iteration and the associated memory footprint, showing that growth is sub-linear in the number of refinement steps for the tested benchmarks.

title: Encoding guard conditions with floating-point semantics in timed automata for microcontroller verification
abstract: Guard conditions in timed automata are conventionally assumed to involve exact real arithmetic, yet microcontroller firmware computes in 32-bit floating-point. This discrepancy can cause verified models to disagree with deployed implementations. The paper investigates how to faithfully encode IEEE 754 single-precision arithmetic into timed automata guards so that the model and the C firmware share the same rounding behaviour. A small-step operational semantics for the floating-point guard evaluation is defined, and a translation procedure converts it into a network of timed automata components that can be analysed with Uppaal. The approach is validated against two industrial-style control tasks: a PID speed regulator and a bang-bang temperature controller, each implemented on an ARM Cortex-M3 board. Discrepancies found in three guard transitions of the PID regulator would have been missed by a purely real-arithmetic model. The paper quantifies the state space overhead introduced by the floating-point encoding, finding an average three-fold increase in the number of symbolic states.

title: Compositional verification of a distributed battery management system using assume-guarantee reasoning
abstract: Battery management systems in electric vehicles consist of several interacting controllers running on separate microcontrollers, making monolithic verification computationally prohibitive. This paper applies assume-guarantee reasoning to decompose the verification problem into per-component checks, each involving a single controller modelled as a hybrid automaton and an assumption automaton encoding the expected behaviour of its neighbours. The assumptions are synthesised iteratively using an L*-based learning algorithm adapted to continuous observation alphabets. The case study involves a four-cell lithium-ion management system with overvoltage, undervoltage, and thermal cutoff safety properties. Each property is expressed as a reachability constraint and checked with a combination of dReal and a custom interval arithmetic propagator. The compositional approach reduces peak memory usage from 18 GB (monolithic) to under 2 GB per component, and reduces total verification time from timeout (over 24 hours) to approximately 40 minutes. The paper discusses how the quality of initial assumptions affects convergence and proposes a heuristic based on controller coupling coefficients.
venue: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Formal Methods for Embedded Systems (ISFMES)

title: Interval-arithmetic-based invariant generation for nonlinear hybrid automata with polynomial guards
abstract: Generating inductive invariants for hybrid automata with polynomial guards and nonlinear continuous dynamics is a hard problem in general. This paper proposes a template-based approach in which candidate invariants are parameterised polynomials of fixed degree and the unknown coefficients are solved for using interval arithmetic over the Bernstein basis representation of the polynomial dynamics. The method avoids explicit computation of flow pipes: instead, it checks that the template polynomial decreases along all trajectories within a candidate invariant set by bounding the Lie derivative using a subdivision-based interval evaluator. Three benchmarks are studied: a nonlinear pendulum controller, a chemical reactor with cooling jacket, and a quadrotor hover controller discretised at 20 ms. For each, invariants of degree two and three are computed and compared against overapproximations obtained from SpaceEx. The proposed method produces tighter invariants in two of the three cases and requires less computation time in all three. Limitations relating to the quality of the initial template guess are discussed.

title: Formal analysis of priority inversion in RTOS-scheduled control loops using hybrid automata with discrete urgency
abstract: Real-time operating system schedulers introduce discrete preemption events that interact with continuous plant dynamics in embedded control loops. Priority inversion, where a high-priority control task is delayed because a lower-priority task holds a shared resource, can cause safety violations that are invisible to purely timing-based analyses. This paper models the scheduler, the resource lock protocol, and the continuous plant together as a single hybrid automaton with urgency constraints, and encodes the combined system in Uppaal Timed Automata with cost variables. Two schedulers are analysed: rate-monotonic and earliest-deadline-first, applied to a three-task DC motor control scenario. The analysis finds a class of priority inversion traces of length seven or more discrete steps that cause the motor position error to exceed a 0.05 radian safety bound. A Priority Ceiling Protocol variant is formally verified to eliminate these traces. Verification times for the corrected model are under three minutes on the experimental setup described.

title: Specification patterns for safety requirements in hybrid automata control models: a catalogue with verification outcomes
abstract: Specifying safety requirements precisely enough for formal verification is often a bottleneck in applying formal methods in practice. This paper documents sixteen specification patterns for safety requirements that arise recurrently in embedded control loop verification, including bounded-error tracking, forbidden-region avoidance, finite-time convergence, and mode-dwell constraints. Each pattern is given a parameterised hybrid automaton template, a corresponding reachability or timed CTL formula, and notes on which verification backends handle it efficiently. The catalogue is assembled from the authors' own case studies and from a structured review of thirty case studies in the formal verification literature. For each pattern, at least one worked example is included, using a control loop from one of three application domains: process automation, mobile robotics, and power electronics. The paper targets engineers who are familiar with control design but have limited prior exposure to formal specification languages. A companion repository contains all model files and verification scripts.

title: Checking conformance between C firmware and hybrid automaton specifications using symbolic execution and reachability intersection
abstract: After a hybrid automaton model of an embedded controller has been formally verified, it is not guaranteed that the deployed C firmware actually implements the model faithfully. This preprint presents a conformance checking procedure that runs symbolic execution on the compiled firmware binary using the KLEE-derived tool SymCtrl and intersects the resulting path condition set with the reachable state sets from the verified automaton model. A mismatch between any path condition and the corresponding automaton guard or invariant is flagged as a conformance violation. The procedure is demonstrated on two firmware files of approximately 4000 and 9000 lines of C respectively, obtained from open-source motor and thermal controller projects. Six conformance violations are found, all related to fixed-point arithmetic rounding in guard evaluation. The preprint discusses the scalability boundary and notes that the approach currently handles only control-flow conformance, leaving data-path conformance to future work.

title: Entropy production in active Brownian particles confined to a channel: dependence on self-propulsion speed and channel width
abstract: We compute the steady-state entropy production rate (EPR) of self-propelled Brownian particles confined between two parallel hard walls as a function of self-propulsion speed v0 and channel half-width L. The model uses the active Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process for the orientation angle with rotational diffusion coefficient Dr. EPR is evaluated both via the Harada–Sasa relation applied to particle velocity correlations and via direct integration of the steady-state probability current in the (x, y, θ) phase space discretised on a 200×200×36 grid. For v0L Dr / (kT) < 1 the two methods agree to within 3%; discrepancies grow at higher Péclet numbers due to grid resolution. EPR grows approximately as v0^1.8 for fixed L and saturates as L increases beyond the persistence length v0/Dr. Accumulation of particles near walls is quantified by the contact density ratio relative to bulk, reaching values up to 4.5 at Pe = 30. The results are relevant to understanding the metabolic cost of active confinement in microfluidic geometries.

title: Effect of laser energy density on the density and tensile properties of SLS-processed PA12 parts
abstract: Process parameter optimisation for selective laser sintering of PA12 was carried out by varying laser power (5–14 W), scan speed (1500–3000 mm/s), and layer thickness (0.10 and 0.12 mm) in a full-factorial design. Volumetric energy density ranged from 0.018 to 0.062 J/mm³. Archimedes densitometry and tensile testing according to ISO 527-2 were performed on 72 dog-bone specimens. Density increased monotonically with energy density up to 0.042 J/mm³, plateauing and showing surface degradation beyond that value. Ultimate tensile strength peaked at 46.3 MPa and Young's modulus at 1 710 MPa within the plateau region. A second-order response-surface model was fitted to predict density (R² = 0.91) and UTS (R² = 0.87) as functions of the three process inputs. The recommended processing window for structural applications is identified, providing a calibrated material card for use in finite element simulations of optimised components.

title: Topology optimisation of a PA12 SLS bracket using the SIMP method with manufacturing constraints
abstract: A cantilever aerospace-style mounting bracket was topology-optimised using the Solid Isotropic Material with Penalisation (SIMP) method implemented in MATLAB. Material properties were taken from the calibrated PA12 card established in prior experimental work. Three constraint scenarios were evaluated: minimum compliance only, minimum compliance with a 30 % volume fraction limit, and minimum compliance with volume fraction and a minimum member size filter of 1.5 mm to suppress features too fine for reliable SLS fabrication. The optimised geometries were exported as STL meshes via a marching-cubes algorithm, manufactured on an EOS Formiga P 110, and loaded to failure in a three-point bending fixture. Measured failure loads were 2–11 % below FEA predictions, with the discrepancy attributed to as-built surface roughness reducing effective cross-sections. The member-size-filtered design achieved the most consistent agreement between simulation and experiment and is recommended as a default workflow for SLS bracket design.

title: Fatigue life of topology-optimised PA12 SLS parts under cyclic tensile loading
abstract: S-N curves were generated for topology-optimised PA12 specimens produced by selective laser sintering, tested in load-controlled cyclic tension at stress ratios R = 0.1 and R = 0.3, at five stress levels between 25 % and 75 % of quasi-static UTS. A total of 90 specimens in three geometric configurations (solid, 30 %-dense TPMS, and topology-optimised with 40 % volume fraction) were tested on an Instron 8801 servo-hydraulic frame at 5 Hz. Run-out was defined at 10⁶ cycles. The solid specimens reached a fatigue limit of approximately 16.8 MPa at R = 0.1; the TPMS and topology-optimised configurations showed fatigue limits of 9.4 MPa and 12.1 MPa respectively, reflecting stress concentrations at lattice nodes and optimised-geometry re-entrant corners. Fracture surface analysis by SEM revealed crack initiation at partially sintered powder agglomerates in all configurations. A Basquin power-law fit is reported for each configuration to support fatigue-safe design workflows.

title: Graded-density lattice infill generation for SLS polymer components based on stress field mapping
abstract: A workflow for generating graded-density lattice infills in SLS PA12 components is described, in which the local relative density of a TPMS-Schwartz-P unit cell is varied continuously from 15 % to 55 % according to the von Mises stress field obtained from a linear FEA of the solid baseline design. The mapping uses a normalised stress metric and a piecewise linear transfer function with user-defined density bounds. The workflow was implemented as a Python script interfacing nTopology Element and Abaqus. Three bracket designs were fabricated and tested: a uniform 30 %-density reference, a binary solid-lattice partition, and the graded infill. The graded design reduced part mass by 23 % compared with solid and 9 % compared with the uniform lattice while maintaining failure load within 5 % of the solid reference. Build time differences were less than 4 % across all lattice variants owing to SLS's layer-by-layer nature.

title: Benchmarking topology optimisation solvers for PA12 SLS components: SIMP, BESO, and level-set compared
abstract: Three topology optimisation formulations — SIMP with MMA update, Bi-directional Evolutionary Structural Optimisation (BESO), and a level-set method based on the Hamilton–Jacobi equation — were applied to a common set of five benchmark problems representative of load-bearing SLS polymer components (cantilever, MBB beam, L-bracket, torsion box, and compliant gripper). All solvers were implemented in Python with identical finite element discretisations (64 000–250 000 four-node quadrilateral elements per problem) and a 40 % volume constraint. Convergence behaviour, final compliance, and computational time were recorded. Resulting geometries were manufactured in PA12 by SLS and mechanically tested. Level-set designs showed the smoothest boundaries and the lowest experimental scatter in failure load (CV = 4.2 %); BESO designs were consistently 7–12 % stiffer than SIMP designs at equal volume fraction in simulation but showed more variability in testing. The study provides a practical guide for selecting a solver for different component classes in a PA12 SLS workflow.

title: Thermal history effects on the mechanical anisotropy of SLS PA12: implications for topology optimisation material models
abstract: Selective laser sintering produces a spatially variable thermal history within a powder bed, resulting in material property gradients that isotropic material models used in topology optimisation do not capture. This work quantifies the variation in tensile modulus, yield stress, and elongation at break across six positions within a 250 × 250 × 330 mm build volume of an EOS Formiga P 110. Five specimens per position per orientation (X, Y, Z) were tested according to ISO 527-2, giving 270 specimens in total. Modulus varied by up to 14 % and yield stress by up to 11 % across build positions. A position- and orientation-dependent correction map was constructed and incorporated into the SIMP material model as a spatially varying stiffness tensor. Brackets optimised with the corrected model showed a 6 % improvement in agreement between predicted and measured stiffness compared with a homogeneous isotropic model. The correction has negligible computational overhead once the map is precomputed.

title: Influence of refresh ratio on the mechanical properties of recycled PA12 SLS powder and topology-optimised part performance
abstract: Selective laser sintering of PA12 generates significant quantities of unsintered powder. This study examines how blending aged and virgin powder at refresh ratios of 0 %, 30 %, 50 %, and 70 % aged powder affects the melt flow index, crystallisation temperature measured by DSC, and the tensile and fatigue properties of both dog-bone specimens and topology-optimised bracket specimens. A set of 48 tensile and 60 fatigue specimens was produced for each refresh ratio level. Tensile modulus and UTS decreased linearly with increasing aged fraction, with UTS dropping from 46.1 MPa (0 % aged) to 40.7 MPa (70 % aged). Fatigue life at a fixed stress amplitude of 14 MPa was reduced by 35 % between the 0 % and 70 % aged conditions. For topology-optimised components, failure loads in static testing showed greater sensitivity to refresh ratio than for solid specimens, attributed to stress concentration at thin optimised members where material degradation is more critical. A conservative refresh ratio of ≤ 40 % is recommended for structural SLS applications.

title: Concurrent topology and infill optimisation of SLS PA12 components using a two-scale density formulation
abstract: A two-scale optimisation framework is presented in which macroscale material density (governing topology) and mesoscale lattice relative density (governing infill) are updated simultaneously within a single SIMP-based iteration loop. The macro- and meso-density fields are linked through an analytical homogenisation model calibrated against the compressive test data reported in earlier work. The framework was tested on a simplified automotive seat-bracket problem with a 500 N vertical load and a 45 % total volume constraint. Convergence was reached in 180 iterations on a 200 × 100 × 60 voxel grid. The concurrent approach reduced compliance by 8.3 % compared with sequential topology-then-infill optimisation at equal mass. Four bracket variants were manufactured in PA12 by SLS and tested under the design load. Measured stiffness matched FEA predictions within 7 % for all variants. The computational overhead relative to standard SIMP is approximately 2.4× per iteration, which is manageable on a workstation-class CPU.

title: Benchmarking Seven Spectral Classifiers for Six-Class Polymer Sorting Under Industrial Noise Conditions
abstract: Published accuracy figures for NIR polymer classifiers are often obtained under controlled laboratory conditions that do not reflect industrial environments. This paper presents a systematic benchmark of seven classifiers — LDA, k-NN, SVM with RBF kernel, random forest, gradient boosting, a 1-D CNN, and a transformer with 4 attention heads — evaluated on a dataset of 72 000 spectra collected on an operational pilot line with realistic noise sources: vibration, conveyor belt reflectance variation, ambient temperature cycling (18–34 °C), and 6% label noise. Data were split by acquisition day to prevent information leakage. Under these conditions, the 1-D CNN achieved the highest macro F1 of 0.944, followed by the transformer at 0.938 and SVM at 0.931. LDA dropped to 0.871. Training time, inference latency, and memory footprint are reported alongside accuracy. The dataset and evaluation scripts are released under an open licence.

title: Fault Detection Rate Degradation in Flying-Probe Testers After Extended Use Under Thermal Stress Environments
abstract: Flying-probe test systems used in production lines adjacent to reflow ovens experience elevated ambient temperatures that gradually degrade probe tip geometry and contact repeatability. This study tracked the fault detection rate of a four-probe flying-probe tester over 18 months of production use in a facility where ambient tester temperature regularly reached 38 °C. Detection rate was assessed monthly by running a standardised reference board carrying 44 planted defects. Detection rate declined from 97.7 % at month zero to 93.1 % at month 18, with the sharpest decline observed for resistor opens below 5 Ω nominal. Probe contact resistance increased on average by 12 mΩ per six months, measured by four-wire probing on a calibration coupon. A predictive maintenance model based on contact resistance trend monitoring is proposed; simulations indicate it would have flagged maintenance need at month 12, preventing three months of degraded test performance.

title: Towards Integrated Sensing and Shape Estimation in Pneumatic Grippers for Agri-Food Sorting Lines
abstract: This preprint describes preliminary work on embedding resistive flex sensors within the wall of a pneumatic bending finger to provide in-situ curvature estimates without external cameras. Three sensor placement strategies—proximal, distal, and dual-location—are compared for their ability to reconstruct finger shape when combined with the reduced-order FE surrogate described in earlier work. Calibration data were collected over 600 pressure–angle combinations. Dual-location placement reduced shape reconstruction error to 3.2 mm mean tip position error compared with 6.8 mm for single proximal placement. A simple Kalman filter fusing sensor readings with surrogate predictions further reduced error to 2.5 mm. Integration into a sorting-line mockup running at 20 items per minute is described qualitatively; quantitative throughput and damage-rate experiments are planned for the next phase. Limitations including sensor drift over 500 actuation cycles and lead routing inside the finger wall are discussed openly.

title: Ionic composition of PM2.5 at an urban background site in Novi Sad during winter heating season 2020–2021
abstract: PM2.5 samples were collected daily over 90 consecutive days (November 2020–February 2021) at a rooftop urban background station in Novi Sad using a Partisol 2000 sequential sampler. Water-soluble inorganic ions (SO4²⁻, NO3⁻, Cl⁻, NH4⁺, Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺) were quantified by dual-channel ion chromatography. Mean PM2.5 mass concentration was 42.3 µg m⁻³, exceeding the EU annual limit on 61% of sampling days. Secondary inorganic aerosol (SIA) species—SO4²⁻, NO3⁻, and NH4⁺—contributed on average 38% of PM2.5 mass. Elevated K⁺ and Cl⁻ concentrations in January pointed to residential biomass and coal combustion as dominant sources. The SO4²⁻/NO3⁻ molar ratio was 0.91, indicating comparable contributions from stationary combustion and vehicular NOx precursors. Neutralisation ratio calculations showed aerosol was predominantly neutralised by ammonia. Results are compared with contemporaneous data from Budapest and Belgrade monitoring networks, and implications for local heating policy are discussed.

title: Chloride depletion in coarse and fine aerosol fractions over Novi Sad: evidence from size-segregated sampling
abstract: Chloride depletion from sea-salt and anthropogenic Cl⁻ carriers by reaction with gaseous HNO3 and H2SO4 was investigated using a five-stage Berner impactor deployed at an urban rooftop site in Novi Sad across four two-week campaigns in 2022 (one per season). Ion chromatographic analysis of size-segregated samples (0.14–10 µm aerodynamic diameter) showed strong Cl⁻ depletion in the accumulation mode (0.14–0.42 µm) during summer, with depletion fractions reaching 78%. In contrast, depletion in the coarse mode was moderate (mean 31%) and consistent across seasons. The coarse Cl⁻ deficit correlated with total NO3⁻ (r = 0.72, p < 0.01), supporting acid displacement as the primary mechanism. Non-sea-salt Cl⁻ in winter showed a strong co-variation with K⁺, confirming coal combustion as the dominant Cl source in that season. These findings refine understanding of HCl release pathways relevant to regional photochemical modelling.

title: Diurnal and seasonal patterns of water-soluble nitrogen species in PM2.5 at a suburban site in northern Serbia
abstract: To resolve diurnal variability in PM2.5 nitrate and ammonium, a six-hour sequential sampler was deployed at a suburban site on the outskirts of Novi Sad for eight weeks spread across winter 2023 and summer 2024. Ion chromatographic analysis yielded 224 short-interval samples. In winter, NO3⁻ concentrations peaked in the early morning (06:00–12:00 local time), averaging 8.4 µg m⁻³, and declined through the afternoon as temperature-driven volatilisation dissociated NH4NO3. In summer, NO3⁻ remained below 1.2 µg m⁻³ throughout the day, while NH4⁺ showed a broader mid-day plateau possibly linked to agricultural ammonia emissions from surrounding fields. The NH4⁺/NO3⁻ equivalent ratio was consistently above 1.1 in winter (excess ammonia) but fell to 0.8 in summer afternoons. Back-trajectory cluster analysis indicated that elevated nitrate episodes in winter were associated with air mass origins over the Pannonian interior rather than long-range transport. Data are consistent with thermodynamic equilibrium calculations using the E-AIM model.

title: Influence of ascorbic acid addition on polyphenol oxidation and colour stability in pasteurised pepper paste
abstract: The antioxidant effect of added ascorbic acid (0, 100, 200, and 400 mg/kg) on polyphenol oxidation and colour stability in pasteurised red pepper paste was studied over a 12-week storage period at 4 °C and 20 °C. Polyphenol content, PPO activity, browning index, and colour parameters were monitored at three-week intervals. At 20 °C, ascorbic acid at 400 mg/kg reduced browning index by 41% at week 12 compared to the unsupplemented control. HPLC analysis showed that chlorogenic acid degradation was slowed at all tested concentrations but not fully inhibited. Total colour difference (ΔE*) was reduced from 9.2 to 4.1 units in the best-performing treatment. The practical implication is that ascorbic acid supplementation can extend acceptable colour shelf life but requires pairing with low-temperature storage for full effect.

title: Dissolution rate of calcite crusts formed on soap surfaces in water of varying hardness and temperature
abstract: Calcite crusts scraped from aged sodium soap bars and pressed into 15 mm discs were immersed in synthetic waters covering a hardness range of 0–400 mg L⁻¹ as CaCO₃ at temperatures of 15, 25, and 40 °C. Dissolution rates were measured by tracking Ca²⁺ concentration by AAS at 5 min intervals over 120 min. In deionised water at 25 °C the initial dissolution rate was 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ mol cm⁻² s⁻¹, decreasing to 4.1 × 10⁻⁹ mol cm⁻² s⁻¹ in 400 mg L⁻¹ hard water due to the common ion effect. Increasing temperature from 15 to 40 °C raised dissolution rates by approximately 35% in soft water but only 12% in hard water. Comparison with dissolution rates of pure reagent calcite showed that soap-matrix calcite dissolved 15–20% faster, attributed to organic coatings reducing surface passivation. The data are relevant to understanding curd deposits formed when soap-containing wastewater meets hard water.

title: Correction of humic substance interference in stripping voltammetric determination of Pb(II) using absorbance ratio at 254 and 365 nm as a surrogate parameter
abstract: The ultraviolet absorbance ratio A₂₅₄/A₃₆₅ (specific UV absorbance ratio, SUVAR) was evaluated as a low-cost proxy for the aromaticity of dissolved organic matter in pore water, and its relationship to the suppression factor (SF) observed in SW-ASV of Pb(II) at a bismuth-film carbon paste electrode was characterised using 62 pore water samples from six sites across Vojvodina. A linear relationship was established between SF and SUVAR over the range 2.1–8.7 (r² = 0.87, n = 62), enabling a simple spectrophotometric pre-screen to estimate the correction factor required before stripping analysis. A two-step protocol—UV measurement in a microcuvette followed by corrected ASV—was tested in a quasi-blind validation set (n = 20) against ICP-MS reference values; mean absolute deviation was 6.3 µg L⁻¹ for Pb concentrations spanning 1.2–68 µg L⁻¹. The protocol requires no additional reagents beyond those used in standard pore water characterisation and adds less than 5 min to the overall procedure.

title: A Preparative HPLC Protocol for the Milligram-Scale Purification of Bidesmosidic Saponins from Complex Caryophyllaceae Extracts Using pH-Adjusted Mobile Phases
abstract: Large-scale purification of bidesmosidic saponins from Caryophyllaceae extracts is impeded by their structural similarity and co-elution on standard C18 phases. A preparative HPLC method was developed and validated on a 250 × 21.2 mm C18 column (5 µm, 100 Å) using acetonitrile–ammonium formate buffer (pH 3.5) gradient. The pH adjustment improved peak symmetry (asymmetry factor < 1.3 for all six test compounds) and resolved two previously inseparable pairs in Gypsophila and Dianthus extracts. Method parameters assessed include linearity (r² > 0.998 over 0.1–2.0 mg/mL), repeatability (RSD < 3.1% for peak area, n = 6), and recovery (87–97% for six isolated compounds). Total processing time per injection was 42 min. The protocol was applied to three different crude saponin fractions from the group's archive, yielding 12–38 mg of each target compound per run from 1 g crude input. Step-by-step operating conditions are provided to facilitate replication.

title: Effect of monochloramine concentration on nitrification onset kinetics in pilot-scale pipe loops: a mesocosm approach
abstract: Four parallel closed-loop pipe mesocosms (total pipe volume 120 L each, PVC and ductile iron variants) were operated for 280 days at four monochloramine residuals: 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 mg/L as Cl₂. Bulk water was sampled twice weekly for nitrite, nitrate, ammonia, heterotrophic plate count and qPCR-based enumeration of Nitrosomonas-related amoA gene copies. Nitrification onset, defined as nitrite accumulation exceeding 0.05 mg/L for three consecutive samples, occurred at days 114, 87, 61 and did not occur in the 3.0 mg/L arm by day 280. Total inorganic nitrogen mass balance confirmed that the observed nitrite originated from ammonia released by chloramine autodecomposition. Biofilm on iron pipe coupons established nitrification 12–18 days earlier than the PVC equivalent at the same residual, attributable to higher biofilm biomass as measured by ATP luminometry. These results quantify the threshold chloramine residual required to prevent biological nitrification in Vojvodina source water chemistry.

title: Microbial community dynamics following a chloramine-to-chlorine conversion event in a medium-sized distribution network
abstract: A controlled disinfectant conversion from monochloramine (average residual 1.4 mg/L) to free chlorine (0.5 mg/L) was carried out in a district metering area of the Sremska Mitrovica network serving approximately 18,000 people. Biofilm coupon devices and bulk water samplers were deployed at eight network nodes. 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing (Illumina MiSeq, V4 region) was performed on samples collected 2 weeks before, and 2, 4, 8 and 16 weeks after conversion. Shannon diversity in bulk water decreased from 3.8 ± 0.2 to 2.7 ± 0.3 within four weeks of conversion, driven by collapse of chloramine-tolerant Sphingomonadales. Nitrospira and Nitrosomonas relative abundances dropped below detection (< 0.1%) by week 8. Heterotrophic plate counts temporarily increased during week 2, consistent with biofilm sloughing triggered by the disinfectant shift. By week 16, community composition had not returned to pre-conversion structure, indicating a persistent reorganisation. Water quality parameters remained within regulatory limits throughout.

title: Immobilisation of Candida rugosa lipase onto aminopropyl-functionalised mesoporous silica: effect of surface chemistry on enzyme loading and initial ester synthesis activity
abstract: Mesoporous silica with three surface functionalisations—bare silanol, aminopropyl, and glycidoxypropyl—was prepared by post-grafting and characterised by BET, FTIR, and elemental analysis. Candida rugosa lipase was adsorbed or covalently attached under phosphate buffer at pH 7.0. Protein loading ranged from 18 to 74 mg g⁻¹ support, with covalent attachment on glycidoxypropyl silica giving the highest loading but lowest specific activity. Aminopropyl-functionalised material retained 68% of free-enzyme specific activity in the synthesis of ethyl oleate in n-hexane at 40 °C. Esterification yield reached 81% after 6 h under optimised water activity conditions (aw = 0.11). The study demonstrates that moderate ionic interactions between enzyme and support preserve catalytic conformation better than covalent bonding under these conditions, providing a straightforward criterion for support selection in batch ester synthesis.

title: Solvent polarity and water activity as co-determinants of lipase enantioselectivity in ester synthesis: a systematic screening across twelve solvents
abstract: Twelve solvents spanning log P from −1.4 (acetonitrile) to 4.5 (n-decane) were evaluated as reaction media for the esterification of (R,S)-2-phenylpropionic acid with ethanol catalysed by immobilised Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase. Water activity was controlled by molecular sieve addition at three levels (aw = 0.06, 0.11, 0.33). Enantioselectivity (E) and initial rate were measured for each combination. E values ranged from 6 in acetonitrile to 51 in n-hexane; within any solvent, lower aw consistently increased both E and reaction rate up to a plateau. Multivariate regression identified log P and aw as independent significant predictors of E (R² = 0.81, p < 0.001). Solvent viscosity did not correlate significantly with E after controlling for log P. These data support the hypothesis that non-polar solvents restrict enzyme conformational dynamics, favouring a more discriminating transition state geometry.

title: Operational stability of Rhizomucor miehei lipase covalently bound to epoxy-activated polymethacrylate beads in repeated batch transesterification of sunflower oil
abstract: Rhizomucor miehei lipase was covalently immobilised on epoxy-polymethacrylate beads (Lifetech ECR8285) and applied to the transesterification of sunflower oil with methanol in a solvent-free system. Catalyst was reused for 20 consecutive 8-hour batches at 40 °C. Fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) yield per batch, residual activity, and protein leaching were monitored. Yield dropped from 92% in batch 1 to 74% by batch 20, with a pronounced decline between batches 8 and 12 attributed to methanol-induced inactivation confirmed by differential scanning calorimetry. Stepwise methanol addition (three portions) partially mitigated this: yield after 20 batches recovered to 84%. Leached protein was below 0.4 mg g⁻¹ support across all batches. The carrier maintained its macroporous structure as confirmed by post-use SEM, suggesting inactivation is chemical rather than mechanical.

title: Comparison of sol-gel entrapment and adsorption methods for Candida antarctica lipase B in the synthesis of flavour esters
abstract: Candida antarctica lipase B (CalB) was immobilised by two methods: adsorption onto octyl-modified silica and entrapment in a tetraethoxysilane/methyltriethoxysilane (TEOS/MTEOS) sol-gel matrix. Both preparations were characterised for protein content, hydrolytic activity, and textural properties. Synthesis of geranyl acetate (geraniol + acetic acid) and citronellyl butyrate (citronellol + butyric acid) was conducted in toluene at 45 °C. Sol-gel CalB gave higher initial rates for both esters (1.8- and 1.4-fold, respectively) but lost 35% activity after six reuse cycles, while adsorbed CalB lost only 18% under the same conditions. Thin-film FTIR showed that the sol-gel matrix compresses slightly during drying, potentially restricting enzyme flexibility and explaining the activity loss pattern. Water produced during synthesis accumulated differently within the two matrices, measured by Karl Fischer titration of supernatants, and correlated with deactivation rate.

title: Influence of silica pore diameter on the activity and thermal stability of immobilised Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase
abstract: Commercial mesoporous silica grades with average pore diameters of 6, 10, 15, 22, and 30 nm were functionalized with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane and used as carriers for Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase. Protein loading, hydrolytic activity (p-nitrophenyl palmitate assay), and thermal stability (half-life at 60 °C in n-hexane) were measured. Maximum loading occurred on 10 nm pores (62 mg g⁻¹), but maximal specific activity and thermal stability were observed on 22 nm pores (specific activity 1,840 U mg⁻¹ protein; half-life 48 h). Circular dichroism spectra of solubilised enzyme recovered from each carrier suggested greater secondary structure preservation with larger pores. Kinetic parameters (Km, Vmax) were determined in olive oil hydrolysis and showed a 2.3-fold increase in Vmax moving from 6 to 22 nm pores. These results indicate that pore diameter must exceed approximately the hydrodynamic diameter of the enzyme dimer to avoid confinement-induced denaturation.

title: Enzymatic transesterification for biodiesel production: process intensification with immobilised lipase in a packed-bed mini-reactor
abstract: A packed-bed mini-reactor (10 mL bed volume) was loaded with Rhizomucor miehei lipase immobilised on macroporous acrylic resin and operated continuously for transesterification of refined rapeseed oil with ethanol in a solvent-free system at 40 °C. Three feed ratios (ethanol:oil 3:1, 4.5:1, 6:1 molar) and three residence times (30, 60, 90 min) were tested in a full factorial design. Maximum FAEE yield of 89.3% was achieved at 4.5:1 molar ratio and 60 min residence time. Steady-state performance was maintained over 200 hours of continuous operation with less than 8% yield decline. Pressure drop across the bed remained below 0.15 bar. The mini-reactor data were used to estimate scale-up parameters for a hypothetical 5 L pilot unit, projecting a volumetric productivity of 0.31 kg FAEE L⁻¹ h⁻¹. The study was presented at a regional biotechnology engineering meeting.

title: Effect of ionic liquid co-solvents on the enantioselectivity and stability of Burkholderia cepacia lipase in the resolution of secondary alcohols
abstract: Four imidazolium-based ionic liquids ([BMIM][PF6], [BMIM][BF4], [EMIM][NTf2], and [OMIM][PF6]) were added at 5–20% v/v to isooctane in which Burkholderia cepacia lipase on Celite resolved (R,S)-1-phenylethanol via transesterification with vinyl acetate. E values and half-lives were determined at each ionic liquid concentration. [BMIM][PF6] at 5% v/v increased E from 34 (pure isooctane) to 61 while reducing half-life from 120 h to 80 h; [OMIM][PF6] at 10% raised E to 74 with half-life 95 h. Anion hydrophilicity, assessed by logP analogy, correlated negatively with E. Fluorescence spectra of the enzyme in each medium showed quenching consistent with partial unfolding at ionic liquid concentrations above 15%. The results suggest a practical window of 5–10% [OMIM][PF6] that improves enantioselectivity without unacceptable stability loss.

title: Cross-linked enzyme aggregates (CLEAs) of Candida antarctica lipase B: preparation variables and performance in wax ester synthesis
abstract: CLEAs of Candida antarctica lipase B were prepared by precipitation with ammonium sulfate at three saturation levels (60%, 75%, 90%) followed by cross-linking with glutaraldehyde (10, 25, 50 mM) for 1–4 h. A 3² factorial design identified 75% saturation and 25 mM glutaraldehyde for 2 h as optimal, yielding CLEAs with 88% activity recovery and an E value of 29 in the resolution of (R,S)-2-octanol. These CLEAs were then tested for wax ester synthesis using cetyl alcohol and oleic acid in n-hexane. Yield reached 95% after 8 h with a substrate loading of 100 mM each. CLEAs were reused 15 times with 91% yield retention. SEM showed spherical aggregates of 3–8 µm. The relationship between aggregate particle size, determined by laser diffraction, and mass-transfer limitations is discussed in the context of a simple effectiveness factor calculation.

title: Immobilised lipase catalysis in deep eutectic solvent–water mixtures: activity, selectivity, and structural integrity
abstract: Three deep eutectic solvents (DESs)—choline chloride:glycerol (1:2), choline chloride:urea (1:2), and betaine:glycerol (1:3)—were prepared and added at 10–40% v/v to phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) as co-solvent systems for hydrolysis and transesterification catalysed by Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase immobilised on aminopropyl silica. Hydrolytic activity was measured with p-nitrophenyl laurate; transesterification activity with ethyl acetate as acyl donor for (R,S)-1-phenylethanol. At 20% v/v choline chloride:glycerol, transesterification E increased from 31 to 44 relative to pure buffer, while hydrolytic activity dropped 22%. Structural analysis by CD and intrinsic fluorescence indicated partial surface helix disruption at DES concentrations above 30% v/v. Water activity in the mixtures was determined by headspace measurement and found to be a confounding variable. The dataset was used to build a partial least-squares model relating DES composition to both activity and enantioselectivity outcomes.

title: Lipase-catalysed synthesis of ascorbyl oleate in acetone: optimisation by response surface methodology and antioxidant evaluation
abstract: Ascorbyl oleate was synthesised by direct esterification of L-ascorbic acid and oleic acid in anhydrous acetone using Rhizomucor miehei lipase immobilised on macroporous resin. A Box–Behnken design with four factors (temperature 35–55 °C, substrate molar ratio 1:1–1:5, enzyme loading 5–20% w/w substrate, molecular sieve mass 10–50 mg mL⁻¹) was applied. The predicted optimum (48 °C, 1:3 ratio, 14% enzyme, 38 mg mL⁻¹ sieves) was validated experimentally, giving 76.4 ± 2.1% conversion confirmed by RP-HPLC. The product was characterised by ¹H NMR and MS. Antioxidant capacity measured by DPPH and FRAP assays showed that ascorbyl oleate retained 82% of the radical scavenging activity of free ascorbic acid at equimolar concentrations. Emulsifying properties were assessed by turbidimetry; the product acted as an oil-in-water emulsifier at 0.3% w/w in a model system, suggesting food application potential.
