title: Support surface hydrophobicity controls the enantioselectivity of Candida rugosa lipase isoforms in the resolution of (R,S)-naproxen
abstract: Candida rugosa lipase contains multiple isoforms (Lip1–Lip3) with differing substrate preferences. Three carriers—bare silica, octyl-silica, and aminopropyl-silica—were loaded with a commercial Lip1-enriched preparation and the mixed isoform preparation, and tested for enantioselective esterification of (R,S)-naproxen with n-butanol in hexane. On octyl-silica, the Lip1-enriched preparation gave E = 52 and ee_p (S-ester) = 96% at 40% conversion; the mixed preparation gave E = 31 on the same carrier. Hydrophobic interaction between Lip1 and the octyl surface apparently stabilises the open-lid conformation, confirmed by limited proteolysis experiments showing 1.8-fold reduced tryptic susceptibility. Thermodynamic analysis (Eyring plots, 25–50 °C) gave ΔΔG‡ of 4.1 kJ mol⁻¹ favouring S-naproxen on octyl-silica, compared to 2.1 kJ mol⁻¹ on bare silica. The findings argue for deliberate matching of isoform composition with support hydrophobicity in pharmaceutical resolution processes.

title: Effect of potassium hydroxide excess on the surface roughness and wettability of potassium palmitate films
abstract: Potassium palmitate films cast from aqueous solution at KOH-to-acid molar ratios ranging from 1.00 to 1.25 were dried at 40 °C and characterised by contact angle goniometry, atomic force microscopy, and BET nitrogen adsorption. Increasing KOH excess from 0 to 25 mol% raised the BET specific surface area from 1.1 to 6.8 m² g⁻¹ and reduced the water contact angle from 84° to 31°. AFM revealed micron-scale pitting attributed to hygroscopic KOH domains. Films with excess alkali showed a 40% faster CO2 absorption rate measured by in situ mass gain in a closed vessel at 25 °C and 50% RH. The work provides a quantitative link between manufacturing alkali excess and the susceptibility of soap products to atmospheric carbonation. Practical implications for shelf-life estimation of soap bars are discussed.

title: Stability Constants of La(III), Gd(III) and Lu(III) Complexes with DO3A and Its Phosphonate Analogue DO3AP
abstract: Stability constants of La³⁺, Gd³⁺, and Lu³⁺ with 1,4,7,10-tetraazacyclododecane-1,4,7-triacetic acid (DO3A) and its monophosphonate analogue DO3AP were determined by potentiometry at 25 °C in 0.15 mol dm⁻³ NaCl, chosen to approximate physiological ionic strength. HYPERQUAD2013 fitting of potentiometric data converged with σ < 0.005 for all systems. Log β(GdDO3A) = 21.04 ± 0.05 and log β(GdDO3AP) = 22.57 ± 0.06; the phosphonate substitution increases stability by approximately 1.5 log units across all three metals. DO3AP shows a higher protonated complex fraction at physiological pH compared to DO3A. Selectivity coefficients derived from competition experiments with Zn²⁺ and Ca²⁺ indicate that lanthanide selectivity is maintained even for DO3A but is significantly enhanced for DO3AP. The data contribute to understanding the conditional stability relevant to potential use of macrocyclic ligands in radiopharmaceutical contexts.

title: Effect of roasting temperature on Maillard reaction products in ground paprika: a kinetic approach
abstract: Ground sweet paprika obtained by roasting Capsicum annuum pericarp at five temperatures (120, 140, 160, 180, and 200 °C) was analysed for Maillard reaction intermediates using colorimetry, fluorescence spectroscopy, and GC-MS. Formation rate constants for pyrazines increased nonlinearly above 160 °C, following apparent first-order kinetics with activation energies in the range 68–82 kJ/mol for individual alkylpyrazines. Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) accumulation was quantified by HPLC-UV and reached 420 mg/kg at 200 °C. Loss of free lysine and arginine was monitored by ion-exchange chromatography. Colour parameters (L*, a*, b*) correlated significantly (r = −0.91) with total pyrazine content. Results indicate that roasting above 170 °C rapidly shifts the flavour balance towards bitter and toasty notes at the expense of characteristic carotenoid-linked aroma.

title: Polyphenol composition of Capsicum annuum pericarp before and after industrial hot-break processing determined by HPLC-DAD
abstract: HPLC with diode array detection was applied to quantify phenolic acids, flavonoids, and capsaicinoids in fresh and hot-break processed Capsicum annuum pericarp. Seven varieties commonly grown in Serbia were sampled before and after industrial heating at 85 °C for 15 min. Chlorogenic acid, luteolin-7-glucoside, and quercetin-3-rutinoside were the dominant polyphenols in fresh material, ranging from 12 to 47 mg/100 g dry weight depending on variety. Hot-break processing reduced total polyphenol content by 22–38%, with the largest losses in hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives. Polyphenol oxidase (PPO) activity was measured spectrophotometrically and correlated inversely with residual chlorogenic acid (r = −0.87). The data support a PPO-mediated oxidation pathway contributing to brown off-colour and astringent off-notes in processed pepper products.
venue: European Journal of Food Composition

title: Formation of acrolein and other α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds during thermal degradation of capsaicin
abstract: Capsaicin and dihydrocapsaicin standards were subjected to controlled thermal degradation at 150, 175, and 200 °C for periods of 5–60 minutes in a sealed reactor system. Degradation products were trapped on Tenax TA sorbent tubes and analysed by thermodesorption GC-MS. Acrolein formation was confirmed at all temperatures, with maximum yields at 200 °C/30 min reaching 1.8 µmol/mg starting material. Methacrolein, crotonaldehyde, and 4-vinylguaiacol were also identified. Acrolein yield increased with temperature following an Arrhenius relationship (Ea ≈ 74 kJ/mol). The findings are relevant to occupational exposure assessments in paprika processing facilities and to understanding pungency-related off-notes generated during frying of hot pepper-containing products.

title: Thermal behaviour of quercetin-3-rutinoside and luteolin-7-glucoside in aqueous pepper extract: degradation products identified by HPLC-MS/MS
abstract: Aqueous extracts prepared from freeze-dried Capsicum annuum pericarp were heated at 80, 100, and 121 °C for up to 60 minutes in sealed vials. Quercetin-3-rutinoside and luteolin-7-glucoside degradation was followed by HPLC with electrospray ionisation tandem mass spectrometry. Both compounds followed pseudo-first-order degradation kinetics. Half-lives at 121 °C were 14.2 min (quercetin-3-rutinoside) and 22.7 min (luteolin-7-glucoside). Seven degradation products were tentatively identified, including protocatechuic acid, caffeic acid, and phloroglucinol carboxaldehyde. The aldehyde degradation products were detected at levels sufficient to contribute to bitter and phenolic off-notes based on comparison with reported threshold values. Results are applicable to autoclaving and retort processing conditions used in industrial production of shelf-stable pepper products.

title: Comparative volatile fingerprinting of smoked and unsmoked dried Capsicum annuum by GC-MS combined with multivariate classification
abstract: Smoked (wood-fired kiln) and unsmoked (hot-air-dried) Capsicum annuum products from twelve Serbian producers were analysed by HS-SPME-GC-MS to develop discriminant models for authentication. A total of 89 volatile compounds were detected; 34 were selected as discriminating variables by ANOVA followed by stepwise linear discriminant analysis. Phenolic smoke markers (guaiacol, 4-methylguaiacol, syringol) correctly classified 94.4% of smoked samples in cross-validation. Partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) on the full dataset achieved 91.7% correct classification. Guaiacol/β-ionone ratios above 3.1 were diagnostic for smoked origin. The method is intended as an analytical reference for certification schemes for traditionally smoked Serbian paprika products.

title: Quantitative structure–odour activity relationships for alkylpyrazines formed in heated Capsicum annuum: experimental thresholds and molecular descriptor modelling
abstract: Orthonasal detection thresholds were determined in water for twelve alkylpyrazines identified in GC-MS profiles of roasted Capsicum annuum, using a three-alternative forced-choice method with a trained panel of 16 assessors. Thresholds ranged from 0.04 µg/L (2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine) to 18.3 µg/L (pyrazine) in water matrix. Pepper paste matrix shifted thresholds upward by a factor of 1.7–4.2 depending on compound hydrophobicity. Partial least squares regression using eight molecular descriptors (log P, molar refractivity, molecular volume, polar surface area, and four topological indices) explained 81% of variance in threshold values (r² = 0.81, RMSECV = 0.31 log units). Odour activity values (OAVs) calculated from GC-MS quantification data identified 2-ethyl-3,5-dimethylpyrazine and 2-acetylpyrazine as the principal contributors to roasted notes in paprika with OAVs of 340 and 89, respectively.

title: Influence of carrier speed variation on gear-mesh harmonic amplitudes in a single-stage planetary gearbox
abstract: The relationship between carrier rotational speed and the amplitude envelope of gear-mesh harmonics is investigated experimentally and analytically for a single-stage planetary gearbox with four planet gears. A dedicated test rig was constructed with a magnetic brake providing programmable load profiles. Carrier speed was varied from 120 to 480 rpm in twelve discrete steps while the ring gear was held stationary. Vibration was acquired at 51.2 kHz on the ring gear housing. Analytical expressions derived from Fourier series representation of the meshing stiffness were used to predict harmonic amplitudes as a function of carrier speed. Predicted and measured amplitudes agreed within 8% for the first five harmonics at all tested speeds. The work identifies speed ranges in which second and third mesh harmonics temporarily coincide with structural resonances of the housing, causing transient amplitude peaks that may be misinterpreted as fault indicators if carrier speed is not accounted for in the diagnostic index computation.

title: Multi-body torsional dynamics model for pitting fault simulation in a planetary gearbox sun gear
abstract: A six-degree-of-freedom multi-body torsional dynamics model of a planetary gearbox is developed to simulate the vibrational signature of progressive pitting damage on the sun gear tooth flanks. Pitting is represented as a time-varying stiffness reduction localised to a fraction of the meshing period, with pit area parameterised from 0.5 mm² to 12 mm² based on measured pit geometries from accelerated fatigue tests on case-hardened 18CrNiMo7-6 steel gears. Equations of motion are integrated using a variable-step Runge–Kutta solver. Simulated acceleration signals are compared with measured signals from a physical gearbox with artificially introduced pitting. The model reproduces the characteristic amplitude modulation sidebands observed in measured spectra with a frequency error below 1.2% and an amplitude ratio error below 15% for the first four sidebands. The sensitivity of the model to damping ratio uncertainty is quantified through a parameter sweep, showing that a ±20% variation in mesh damping ratio affects sideband amplitude predictions by at most 9%.

title: Pitting severity index based on weighted sideband summation around gear-mesh harmonics in planetary stages
abstract: A scalar pitting severity index (PSI) is defined as a weighted sum of sideband amplitudes around the first four gear-mesh harmonics, with weights derived empirically from the torsional dynamics model published by the same group in 2017. The index is validated on two physical planetary gearboxes: a laboratory unit run to controlled pitting failure under accelerated fatigue at 1.8 times rated torque, and a repaired unit from a field-returned industrial conveyor drive. Vibration data were collected at 65.5 kHz. The PSI increased monotonically with measured pit area in the laboratory unit, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.94 across 11 damage stages from healthy to 35 mm² total pit area. On the field unit, the PSI correctly ranked five gearboxes of differing service history relative to their disassembly condition grades assigned by a maintenance engineer. False alarm rate at a threshold set to three standard deviations above the healthy mean was 4% across a 48-hour continuous monitoring run.

title: Effect of gear tooth profile errors on torsional dynamics and diagnostic index reliability in planetary gearboxes
abstract: Manufacturing tolerances in tooth profile geometry introduce systematic variations in mesh stiffness that can mask or mimic early-stage pitting signatures. This study uses coordinate measuring machine data from twelve planetary gear sets to characterise profile deviation distributions for ISO quality grades 6, 7, and 8. The measured deviations are introduced into the multi-body torsional dynamics model as deterministic stiffness perturbations. Monte Carlo simulation with 500 realisations per quality grade quantifies the spread in the pitting severity index under healthy conditions. For grade 8 gears, the healthy-state PSI variance is 2.4 times larger than for grade 6, reducing the effective detection margin for pitting areas below 5 mm². Recommendations are formulated for adjusting detection thresholds based on the nominal manufacturing quality grade of a given gearbox, which can be retrieved from component documentation without disassembly.

title: Real-time pitting detection prototype using FPGA-based gear-mesh harmonic extraction on a planetary gearbox test rig
abstract: A real-time condition monitoring prototype is described in which gear-mesh harmonic extraction and pitting severity index computation are implemented on an FPGA development board (Xilinx Kria KV260) connected directly to a 24-bit delta-sigma accelerometer. The harmonic extraction algorithm performs synchronous resampling using a phase-locked loop driven by an encoder pulse train, followed by a 1024-point FFT executed on-chip at a latency of 1.1 ms per shaft revolution. The computed PSI is streamed over Ethernet to a monitoring dashboard at 10 Hz update rate. The prototype was tested on the department's planetary gearbox test rig with three implanted pitting fault levels (2 mm², 8 mm², and 20 mm² total pit area). Detection latency from fault presence to threshold crossing was below 4 shaft revolutions at all tested speeds between 300 and 900 rpm carrier speed. Power consumption of the FPGA module was 4.2 W during continuous operation.

title: Threshold setting strategies for gear-mesh harmonic diagnostic indices under varying operating conditions: a survey of methods and a comparative study
abstract: Diagnostic indices derived from gear-mesh harmonic spectra require operating-condition-dependent thresholds to maintain acceptable false alarm and missed detection rates. This preprint surveys twelve threshold-setting strategies reported in the literature between 2005 and 2025 and applies six of them to a common dataset collected on a planetary gearbox test rig under four load levels and three temperature conditions. Strategies include fixed statistical thresholds, sliding window percentile methods, Gaussian mixture model fitting, control chart approaches, and two machine learning classifiers trained on healthy-condition data. Performance is evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves and F1 scores for five pitting severity levels. No single strategy dominates across all conditions; fixed statistical thresholds show the highest false alarm rates at partial load, while the sliding window percentile method performs most consistently but requires a longer initialisation window. The dataset used in the study is made available as a supplementary file.

title: Frequency and Pattern of Principal Diagnosis Coding Errors in a Tertiary Hospital in Vojvodina: A Retrospective Audit
abstract: This study examined 4,820 inpatient discharge records from a tertiary care hospital in Vojvodina over a twelve-month period to characterise the frequency and typology of principal diagnosis coding errors under ICD-10. Two trained clinical coders independently reviewed each record, with discrepancies resolved by a senior physician. Errors were classified into four categories: wrong chapter assignment, specificity failure, sequencing error, and omission of a relevant secondary diagnosis. An overall error rate of 18.4% was found, with specificity failures comprising the largest share (41% of errors). Cardiovascular and metabolic disease chapters showed the highest absolute error counts. The study further identified that records coded by physicians with less than two years of documentation experience had a statistically significantly higher error rate compared to more experienced staff (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.7–3.1). Findings were used to design a targeted continuing education module for the hospital's clinical documentation office.

title: Agreement Between Physician-Assigned and Retrospective Expert-Assigned ICD-10 Codes in Internal Medicine Wards: A Kappa Analysis
abstract: Inter-rater agreement between bedside physician-assigned ICD-10 codes and codes assigned retrospectively by a certified clinical coding specialist was measured for 1,210 closed internal medicine episodes across three hospitals in Serbia. Agreement was calculated using Cohen's kappa at the three-character category level and at the full code level. Overall kappa at the category level was 0.61 (substantial agreement), dropping to 0.44 at the full four-character code level. The lowest agreement was observed for codes in the range E10–E14 (diabetes mellitus subtypes, kappa 0.38) and J40–J47 (chronic lower respiratory diseases, kappa 0.41). The study discusses structural reasons for disagreement, including ambiguous clinical documentation and physician unfamiliarity with hierarchical specificity requirements. No significant association was found between hospital size and agreement level. Recommendations focus on structured discharge summary templates as a practical intervention.

title: Rule-Based Detection of Diagnostic-Therapeutic Inconsistencies in Coded Hospital Records
abstract: A set of 214 deterministic rules was constructed to flag logical inconsistencies between ICD-10 principal diagnosis codes and recorded therapeutic procedures in a hospital information system. Rules were derived from Serbian national clinical guidelines and peer-reviewed treatment protocols for the fifty most common discharge diagnoses in internal medicine. The rule set was applied to 22,400 discharge episodes from a regional hospital over three years. Flagged records were reviewed by a panel of internists to classify each flag as a genuine inconsistency, a documentation artefact, or an acceptable clinical exception. Precision of the rule set was 71%, with a recall of 64% against the panel-verified ground truth. The most productive rules concerned anticoagulant therapy absence in coded atrial fibrillation and insulin prescription absence in coded type 1 diabetes. The paper discusses the limitations of rule-based systems compared to probabilistic approaches and outlines a hybrid extension.

title: Mapping ICD-10 Coded Discharge Data to ICD-11: Feasibility and Ambiguity in an Internal Medicine Dataset
abstract: This study assessed the feasibility of algorithmically mapping existing ICD-10 coded discharge records to ICD-11 using the World Health Organization's published crosswalk tables, applied to a dataset of 9,600 internal medicine episodes from two hospitals in Serbia. For each episode the principal diagnosis and up to three secondary diagnoses were mapped. Full, unambiguous one-to-one mapping was achieved in 58% of codes. Partial or one-to-many mappings accounted for 29%, and unmappable codes—primarily local Serbian extensions to ICD-10—represented 13%. Ambiguity was highest in the mental and behavioural disorders chapter and in the chapter covering symptoms and signs. A sample of 400 ambiguous mappings was manually resolved by two physicians to produce a reference set. The study concludes that automated migration to ICD-11 in Serbian hospitals would require substantial pre-processing of local code extensions and structured supplementary clinical data not routinely recorded.

title: Clinical Coding in Serbian Hospitals: A Survey of Physician Knowledge, Attitudes and Institutional Support
abstract: A cross-sectional survey was administered to 312 physicians across seven hospitals in Serbia to characterise self-reported familiarity with ICD-10 coding principles, perceived adequacy of institutional training, and attitudes toward clinical documentation as a professional responsibility. The response rate was 74%. Only 31% of respondents correctly identified the ICD-10 coding rule for sequencing a principal diagnosis when two conditions equally meet the definition. Physicians working in teaching hospitals reported significantly higher confidence in coding than those in general district hospitals (p < 0.01), but this did not translate into higher accuracy on a ten-item coding knowledge test embedded in the survey. Fewer than 20% of respondents reported ever attending a formal coding training event. The paper discusses implications for health data quality in a system where physicians are the primary coders and argues for mandatory structured coding education in medical school curricula.

title: Secondary Diagnosis Undercoding in Comorbid Type 2 Diabetes Patients: Magnitude and Financial Implications Under the DRG Payment System
abstract: Using a matched record review design, this study quantified the extent to which comorbid type 2 diabetes was omitted from secondary diagnosis fields in hospital discharge records for patients whose clinical notes documented active diabetes management during the admission. A total of 870 records were reviewed from two hospitals participating in Serbia's diagnosis-related group pilot reimbursement programme. Diabetes was undercoded in 34% of eligible episodes. A financial impact simulation based on published DRG weight tables estimated a mean reimbursement shortfall of approximately 1,240 EUR per affected episode under the pilot tariff structure. Multivariate logistic regression showed that short length of stay (≤2 days) and admission via emergency pathway were independent predictors of undercoding. The paper recommends that DRG-based funding systems include automated secondary diagnosis plausibility checks triggered by pharmacy dispensing data.

title: Automated Auditing of Diagnostic Pathway Compliance Using Coded Administrative Data: A Pilot in Heart Failure Management
abstract: Heart failure (ICD-10 I50) was selected as a test case for an automated pathway compliance audit system applied to administrative discharge data from three hospitals in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina. The audit algorithm compared recorded diagnostic procedures and medication codes against a simplified, computable version of the Serbian heart failure management guideline, covering eleven mandatory and eight recommended process indicators. Records for 1,580 heart failure episodes over two calendar years were processed. Compliance with mandatory indicators was 63% on average, with echocardiography recording (indicator: echo performed and coded) showing the lowest compliance at 41%. The system produced episode-level compliance reports that were shared with each hospital's quality committee. A before-after comparison at a six-month follow-up showed a statistically non-significant improvement trend. The study identifies coding completeness, rather than actual clinical omission, as a likely contributor to apparent non-compliance.

title: Transition Barriers to ICD-11 in Low- and Middle-Income European Health Systems: A Comparative Analysis of Serbia, North Macedonia and Moldova
abstract: This comparative study collected structured data through key informant interviews and document analysis to characterise institutional, technical and workforce barriers to ICD-11 adoption in three non-EU European health systems. Fourteen informants per country were interviewed, including health ministry officials, hospital information system managers, clinical coders and physicians. Analysis identified five barrier domains: software infrastructure readiness, coder workforce size and training capacity, legal-regulatory framework, multilingual terminology coverage (Serbian, Macedonian and Romanian were assessed), and budgetary allocation. Serbia showed the most advanced software preparedness but the weakest regulatory mandate for transition. A composite barrier score was constructed and validated through member checking. The paper does not advocate a single transition timeline but instead proposes a modular readiness assessment tool adaptable to each system's constraints. Implications for WHO technical assistance programmes are discussed.

title: A Logistic Regression Model for Predicting Coding Specificity Failure in Routine Internal Medicine Discharge Records
abstract: Specificity failure—the selection of an ICD code at insufficient hierarchical depth when a more specific code is both clinically justified and available—is one of the most common coding error types but the least addressed by existing audit tools. Using 14,300 discharge records from internal medicine departments in four Vojvodina hospitals over four years, a logistic regression model was trained on episode-level covariates (admission urgency, length of stay, primary physician specialty, ward type, number of secondary diagnoses) to predict whether the principal diagnosis code would be flagged as a specificity failure by a reference reviewer. The model achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.72 on a held-out test set. The highest-weight predictors were short length of stay, admission via emergency, and ward type (general versus specialised). The model is intended as a triage tool to prioritise which records should receive human audit review, rather than as a standalone classifier.

title: Serum adiponectin and leptin ratio as a predictor of lobular inflammation in NAFLD: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Adipokine imbalance is implicated in the progression of NAFLD, but the combined predictive value of the leptin-to-adiponectin ratio (LAR) for histological inflammation has been less studied relative to Eastern European or Balkan populations. We analysed fasting serum leptin and adiponectin in 87 biopsy-confirmed NAFLD patients and 40 age- and sex-matched controls recruited from a hepatology outpatient clinic. Leptin was measured by ELISA and adiponectin by multiplex immunoassay. LAR was significantly higher in patients with lobular inflammation grade ≥1 compared with grade 0 (11.4±3.2 vs 5.7±2.1, p<0.001). ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.79 (95% CI 0.71–0.87) for LAR in discriminating histological inflammation, with an optimal cut-off of 8.2 (sensitivity 74%, specificity 76%). LAR remained independently associated with inflammation after multivariate adjustment for BMI, triglycerides, and ALT. LAR may serve as a low-cost adjunct in clinical risk stratification of NAFLD patients when liver biopsy is not immediately available.

title: Prevalence of polypharmacy among hospitalised patients over 65 years in a tertiary care centre in Vojvodina: a cross-sectional study
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence of polypharmacy (defined as concurrent use of five or more medications) among patients aged 65 and over admitted to the internal medicine wards of a tertiary care centre in Novi Sad over a 12-month period (2009–2010). Data were extracted from discharge summaries and pharmacy dispensing records for 612 patients. Polypharmacy was identified in 67.3% of the sample, with hyperpolypharmacy (ten or more medications) present in 21.4%. The most common drug combinations involved antihypertensives, proton pump inhibitors, antidiabetics, and anticoagulants. Clinically significant potential drug interactions were detected in 43.8% of polypharmacy cases using the Micromedex interaction database. Comorbidity burden, quantified by the Charlson Comorbidity Index, was the strongest predictor of hyperpolypharmacy (OR 2.34, 95% CI 1.71–3.19). The findings provide a baseline estimate for the region and highlight the need for systematic medication review protocols at hospital admission.

title: Consistency Checking of Road Geometry in Parametric Map Formats: A Case Study with OpenDRIVE
abstract: OpenDRIVE encodes road geometry as sequences of parametric cubic polynomials (clothoids, arcs, and lines). Small numerical errors introduced during authoring or format conversion can produce curvature discontinuities, overlapping road surfaces, or misaligned lane boundaries that cause simulation instability. This paper defines eleven geometric consistency rules for OpenDRIVE files and implements them as a standalone checker tool written in Python. The checker was applied to 23 OpenDRIVE maps obtained from public repositories and from two automotive simulation projects, with file sizes ranging from 0.3 MB to 41 MB. In total, 1,847 distinct violations were detected across all files. The most frequent class was tangent-direction mismatch at geometry segment boundaries, accounting for 38 percent of all violations. Proposed automatic repair strategies are described for seven of the eleven rule classes, and their success rate is reported on the test corpus. The tool is released as open-source software and integrated with a Python-based map processing library.

title: A Comparative Study of Road Network Format Translators for ADAS Simulation Workflows
abstract: Several map formats are used across the ADAS simulation ecosystem, including OpenDRIVE, SUMO's network XML, Lanelet2, and proprietary formats used by commercial simulators. Translating between these formats without losing semantic content or introducing topological errors is a known practical problem. This paper evaluates five existing open-source and commercial translation tools on a benchmark suite of 30 test maps spanning urban intersections, motorway junctions, and rural roads. Evaluation criteria include preservation of lane connectivity, sign and signal associations, elevation profile accuracy, and round-trip fidelity. No single tool passed all criteria on all map types. Round-trip translation (OpenDRIVE → Lanelet2 → OpenDRIVE) introduced measurable lane-width errors in 21 of 30 maps. The paper also identifies three systematic ambiguities in the OpenDRIVE 1.5 specification that are the root cause of divergent translator behaviour, and proposes clarifications with example XML fragments.

title: Graph-Based Modelling of Signalised Intersections for Microscopic Traffic Simulation
abstract: Signalised intersections require precise representation of signal phases, protected and permitted turn movements, and conflicting path sets to support microscopic traffic simulation. This paper proposes a directed multigraph model in which nodes represent stop lines and conflict points, edges represent lane segments and pedestrian crossings, and signal phases are encoded as time-indexed edge activation sets. The model is formally specified and then instantiated for fifteen signalised intersections in Novi Sad city centre using a combination of field measurement data and OSM geometries. Simulations were run in SUMO with the generated graphs and validated against 90-minute vehicle count recordings at each intersection. The mean absolute percentage error in throughput estimates was 8.3 percent. Comparison with a manually built SUMO network for the same intersections shows that the automated graph construction reduces preparation time from an average of 4.1 hours to 22 minutes per intersection. Limitations with respect to overlapping pedestrian phases are discussed.

title: Handling Elevation and Superelevation in Automated OpenDRIVE Generation from Survey Data
abstract: Road elevation profiles and cross-slope (superelevation) are critical for realistic vehicle dynamics in ADAS simulation but are frequently omitted or approximated poorly in automatically generated maps. This paper addresses the fitting of OpenDRIVE elevation records and superelevation polynomials to GNSS trajectory data and cross-sectional tilt measurements acquired during standard road surveys. A cubic spline fitting procedure is adapted to enforce the OpenDRIVE constraint that each record covers exactly one road geometry segment. The method is evaluated on 42 km of two-lane rural roads in Vojvodina. Fitting residuals for elevation were below 5 cm RMS on 94 percent of segments; superelevation residuals were below 0.3 degrees RMS. The generated OpenDRIVE files were imported into two commercial vehicle dynamics simulators and lateral acceleration profiles from simulated runs were compared with reference measurements from an instrumented vehicle, yielding mean absolute differences of 0.08 g over the test routes.

title: A Taxonomy of Topology Errors in Converted Road Maps and Their Impact on ADAS Scenario Testing
abstract: Road maps used in ADAS scenario testing frequently originate from conversion pipelines rather than being authored natively in the target format, and the resulting topology errors can invalidate test results. This book chapter reviews the literature and author experience to produce a structured taxonomy of topology error classes, covering missing connections, spurious connections, incorrect lane count propagation, erroneous road object placement, and signal association failures. For each class, the chapter provides a formal definition, a representative example drawn from real converted files, and a description of the simulation artefact it produces. The chapter also discusses which error classes are detectable by automated checkers and which require human review, and proposes a severity classification scheme tied to functional safety considerations under ISO 26262. The taxonomy is intended as a reference for map quality assurance engineers and researchers developing automated validation tools.

title: Incremental Updating of OpenDRIVE Road Networks from Repeated Mobile Surveys
abstract: Road networks change over time due to construction, lane reconfigurations, and traffic management measures. Maintaining ADAS simulation maps in sync with the physical road requires an update workflow that is less expensive than full resurvey and reconstruction. This paper proposes a change-detection algorithm that compares lane marking polylines extracted from two temporally separated mobile LiDAR surveys of the same route. Differences above a spatial threshold of 0.5 m are classified as additions, deletions, or geometric shifts of lane boundaries. The algorithm then generates a minimal set of edits to an existing OpenDRIVE file that brings it into agreement with the updated survey data, leaving unchanged road segments untouched. The method is tested on a 3.1 km corridor in Novi Sad surveyed in March 2020 and again in October 2022, during which period two intersections were reconfigured. All reconfigured intersection topologies were correctly updated; no false positives were detected on unchanged segments. Edit generation took under 90 seconds.

title: Resolving Ambiguous Junction Configurations in OSM-to-OpenDRIVE Conversion Using Turn-Count Data
abstract: Many urban junctions in OpenStreetMap are mapped at the road centreline level without explicit lane topology, making it difficult to infer the correct connection geometry required by OpenDRIVE. This paper proposes a data-fusion approach that incorporates anonymised intersection turn-count matrices—available from municipal traffic management systems or estimated from GPS probe data—as a constraint during junction topology inference. A probabilistic graph-matching formulation is used, where candidate connection topologies are scored against observed turn proportions. The method is evaluated on 38 junctions in Novi Sad for which both OSM data and ground-truth turn counts were available. Compared to a baseline that uses only OSM tags, the turn-count-guided method reduced incorrect connection assignments from 34 percent to 9 percent of junctions. Runtime overhead relative to the baseline was under 2 seconds per junction. The paper also discusses privacy implications of using GPS probe data and describes the anonymisation procedure applied.

title: Cross-Validation of Road Topology Graphs Derived from Three Independent Sources: OSM, LiDAR Survey, and Cadastral Data
abstract: Road topology graphs derived from different source data types—crowdsourced maps, mobile LiDAR surveys, and cadastral land registers—exhibit different error profiles and coverage characteristics. This preprint reports a systematic cross-validation study in which topology graphs for a 47 km² area of Novi Sad were independently derived from all three sources and then compared pairwise. Geometric matching was performed at the road segment level using a 1.0 m buffer tolerance; topological matching used node degree sequences and connectivity signatures at junctions. Agreement rates at the road segment level were 94 percent (OSM–LiDAR), 81 percent (OSM–cadastral), and 79 percent (LiDAR–cadastral). Discrepancies were categorised and mapped spatially; the highest disagreement density occurred in recently developed residential areas and around major construction sites. The study highlights which source is most reliable for each road class and provides guidance for weighted fusion strategies.

title: Margin-Based Query Selection for Document Classification with Small Initial Label Sets
abstract: Early active learning experiments on document corpora frequently assume large seed sets, which is impractical in domain-specific settings where expert time is scarce. This paper examines margin sampling applied to a legal document collection of 4,200 items with an initial labelled pool of only 50 instances. A logistic regression classifier with TF-IDF features is retrained after each batch of 20 queries. We compare margin, entropy, and random baselines across 15 query rounds and report macro-F1 on a fixed held-out test set of 800 documents. Margin sampling reaches the passive-learning ceiling at round 9, using roughly 230 labelled examples, compared with round 14 for random selection. We also analyse annotation time per round using think-aloud sessions with two legal experts, finding that cognitive load peaks at round 5 when the decision boundary is most ambiguous. The results suggest that early rounds benefit from diversity-augmented queries rather than pure uncertainty.

title: Test-time adaptation for pose estimation under gradual illumination drift
abstract: Illumination conditions in real deployments often change gradually throughout the day rather than abruptly, yet most adaptation methods are benchmarked on sharp distribution shifts. We study the scenario of gradual illumination drift in long-duration video and propose a test-time adaptation strategy that updates only the batch normalisation statistics of a frozen backbone using an exponential moving average over recent frames. The approach is evaluated on a 6-hour video sequence recorded in a gymnasium with natural light, during which illumination intensity varied from 320 lux to 1,800 lux. PCK@0.2 degraded from 0.83 to 0.72 without adaptation and was maintained at 0.80 with adaptation. The method requires no labels at test time and adds 2 ms per frame on a mid-range GPU. We also characterise the sensitivity of the approach to the smoothing coefficient and window size.

title: Enforceability of Sukuk Covenants under Slovenian and Serbian Civil Law: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: This paper examines whether the contractual architecture of sukuk—specifically asset-transfer clauses and profit-distribution mechanisms—can be rendered enforceable under the civil-law frameworks of Slovenia and Serbia without statutory amendment. Using a doctrinal method, the study analyses forty-three sukuk prospectuses issued between 2004 and 2009 and maps each structural element to existing contract and property law provisions in both jurisdictions. Findings indicate that asset-backed sukuk structures face the most significant obstacles in Serbian law due to restrictions on beneficial ownership, while Slovenian fiduciary transfer provisions offer a partial functional equivalent. The paper identifies three legislative lacunae in each jurisdiction and proposes minimal textual amendments to existing civil codes that would accommodate sukuk issuance without creating a parallel regulatory regime. The study contributes to the emerging literature on Islamic finance transplantation into non-common-law environments and is among the first to address the Serbian context specifically.

title: Murabaha as a Lending Substitute: Regulatory Treatment under the EU Consumer Credit Directive
abstract: Murabaha—a cost-plus-profit sale used as an alternative to interest-bearing loans—is increasingly marketed to Muslim retail clients in EU member states. This paper investigates whether murabaha products offered by institutions in Austria, Germany, and the United Kingdom prior to Brexit satisfy the disclosure, APR-calculation, and cooling-off requirements of Directive 2008/48/EC. The analysis draws on product documentation collected from eight financial institutions and two legal opinions issued by national regulators. The study finds that standard murabaha documentation systematically fails to express the profit margin as an annual percentage rate, creating compliance risk under the Directive. It further argues that the Directive's definition of 'total cost of credit' is broad enough to capture murabaha profit without amendment, provided national supervisors issue interpretive guidance. Three supervisory approaches adopted in the UK, Luxembourg, and Ireland are benchmarked as regulatory templates for continental jurisdictions.

title: Capital Treatment of Ijara Contracts under Basel III: Lease or Loan?
abstract: Ijara, an Islamic leasing instrument, presents classification difficulties for prudential supervisors because it shares economic characteristics with both operating leases and secured lending. This paper analyses how ijara should be treated under the Basel III capital adequacy framework, with particular focus on risk-weighted asset computation and the leverage ratio. Using a sample of sixteen ijara agreements from Gulf Cooperation Council institutions operating in European markets, the paper applies the Basel Committee's criteria for on- and off-balance-sheet treatment and compares results with accounting classifications under IFRS 16. The study finds that identical ijara structures receive divergent capital charges depending on national supervisor interpretation, producing competitive distortions between Islamic and conventional banks. A proposed classification decision tree is developed and tested against the sample agreements. The paper also discusses the relevance of the EBA's 2016 discussion paper on proportionality in regulatory treatment of alternative finance products.

title: Islamic Finance in the Western Balkans: Demand-Side Survey Evidence from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, and North Macedonia
abstract: This study reports findings from a structured questionnaire survey of 1,240 adult respondents in three Western Balkan states, conducted in 2013, examining awareness of and stated preferences for Islamic financial products. The survey instrument covered savings accounts, home-purchase financing, and small-business lending. Results indicate that awareness of Islamic finance products is highest in Bosnia and Herzegovina (62% of Muslim respondents), moderate in North Macedonia (38%), and low in Serbia (19%), while stated willingness to use such products if available exceeds awareness in all three markets, suggesting latent demand. Multivariate logistic regression identifies age, religiosity index, and prior banking experience as significant predictors of stated preference. The paper discusses regulatory preconditions for market entry and estimates minimum viable market size for a standalone Islamic retail banking unit in each jurisdiction, drawing on population data and deposit statistics from national central banks.

title: Shariah Supervisory Boards and Corporate Governance: Accountability Gaps in European Subsidiaries of Islamic Banks
abstract: Islamic financial institutions operating in Europe typically maintain shariah supervisory boards (SSBs) to certify product compliance, yet European company law provides no statutory recognition of such bodies. This paper examines the governance implications of SSBs in fourteen Islamic financial institutions that held banking licences in EU or EEA jurisdictions as of 2015. Document analysis of annual reports, articles of association, and regulatory submissions reveals that SSB mandates are legally subordinated to supervisory board instructions in all fourteen cases, creating a potential conflict between religious and prudential oversight. The paper considers whether SSB members can be held liable under EU Directive 2013/36/EU fitness-and-properness requirements and concludes that the current framework contains a regulatory gap. Three governance models from the UK, Luxembourg, and Malaysia are reviewed and adapted to fit the one-tier and two-tier board structures prevalent in continental Europe.

title: Regulatory Barriers to Islamic Finance in Central and Eastern Europe: A Policy Comparison
abstract: This book chapter surveys the legislative and regulatory landscape for Islamic finance in eight Central and Eastern European states: Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, and Serbia. Drawing on interviews with fourteen central bank officials and regulators conducted in 2016–2017, alongside a structured review of banking laws, tax codes, and securities regulations, the chapter maps specific legal provisions that create obstacles for Islamic finance products. The analysis finds that double-taxation of asset transfers in murabaha and ijara transactions represents the most uniformly cited barrier across jurisdictions, followed by the absence of a legal concept of beneficial ownership. The chapter also identifies Hungary and Serbia as having made the most substantive preliminary enquiries into enabling legislation, and discusses the political economy of reform in each case. The chapter concludes with a standardised reform checklist for policymakers.

title: Musharaka Venture Financing and the EU Prospectus Regulation: A Structural Compatibility Assessment
abstract: Musharaka is a partnership-based financing structure in which profits and losses are shared according to a pre-agreed ratio, functioning as an approximate equivalent to equity co-investment. This paper assesses whether musharaka instruments issued to retail investors in the EU require a prospectus under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, focusing on the transferability criterion and the definition of 'securities' under Article 2(a). The study analyses twelve musharaka instruments marketed in Germany, France, and the Netherlands between 2012 and 2018, classifying each according to the four-part transferability test derived from ESMA guidance. Results indicate that seven of the twelve instruments meet the transferability threshold and should have been accompanied by a prospectus; in five cases, issuers relied on crowdfunding exemptions that the paper argues were inapplicable. The paper proposes a disclosure template adapted from the Key Information Document format specified in the PRIIPs Regulation that would be suitable for retail musharaka offerings.

title: Zakat and Tax Deductibility: Lessons for Serbian Fiscal Law from Malaysian and UK Precedents
abstract: Zakat—a mandatory charitable contribution under Islamic law—creates a dual-payment burden for Muslim taxpayers in jurisdictions that do not recognise it as a tax-deductible expenditure. This paper examines the fiscal treatment of zakat in Serbian income and corporate tax law and compares it with the treatment in Malaysia (where zakat offsets income tax liability directly) and the United Kingdom (where zakat qualifies as a charitable donation for Gift Aid purposes). The study uses a hypothetical taxpayer model to calculate the effective tax burden difference across the three systems for individuals at three income levels and one corporate entity. It finds that Serbian taxpayers face a de facto additional tax burden of between 10% and 15% of total tax liability if they fulfil zakat obligations, compared to a zero additional burden in Malaysia. The paper argues that a modest amendment to the Serbian Law on Income Tax could resolve the asymmetry without creating broader fiscal risks.

title: Green Sukuk and EU Sustainable Finance Taxonomy: Alignment and Gaps
abstract: Green sukuk—sukuk whose proceeds are restricted to environmentally beneficial projects—have been issued in Malaysia, Indonesia, and several Gulf states since 2017. This paper examines whether the asset eligibility criteria and reporting requirements of green sukuk frameworks published by the Securities Commission Malaysia and the AAOIFI align with the technical screening criteria of the EU Taxonomy Regulation (EU) 2020/852. The study compares eligibility criteria across six environmental objectives, applying the Do No Significant Harm and minimum social safeguard tests to a sample of seventeen green sukuk issued between 2017 and 2021. Results indicate partial alignment for climate change mitigation (approximately 70% of criteria matched) but significant gaps in biodiversity, water, and circular economy objectives. The paper also notes that the AAOIFI green sukuk standard lacks a forward-looking science-based target requirement, which is implicit in the EU Taxonomy's trajectory approach. Practical implications for European issuers seeking dual Islamic-and-green certification are discussed.

title: The Serbian National Bank's Prudential Framework and the Accommodation of Profit-and-Loss Sharing Deposits
abstract: Serbian banking regulation, based on the Law on Banks of 2005 as amended, defines deposits exclusively in terms of contractual interest obligations, leaving no explicit room for profit-and-loss sharing (PLS) deposit accounts, which are the retail funding instrument of Islamic banks. This paper analyses the statutory definition of 'deposit' and 'credit institution' under Serbian law and explores whether a domestic bank could offer PLS accounts under existing licence conditions or whether a dedicated licence category is required. The study interviews seven officials at the National Bank of Serbia (anonymised) and reviews regulatory correspondence obtained through freedom-of-information requests. The paper concludes that a PLS account with a guaranteed minimum principal—a common hybrid structure—would be legally classifiable as a deposit under current Serbian law, while a fully loss-bearing PLS account would not, and proposes a regulatory sandbox mechanism as an interim solution. Comparison is made with the Hungarian MNB's 2019 exploratory exercise.

title: Towards an Islamic Finance Window Regulation in Serbia: Drafting Principles and Comparative Benchmarks
abstract: A finance 'window' is a dedicated unit within a conventional bank licensed to offer shariah-compliant products, subject to ring-fencing requirements. This paper develops a set of drafting principles for a hypothetical Serbian Islamic finance window regulation, benchmarked against window frameworks in Turkey, Malaysia, Oman, and the United Kingdom. The study identifies eleven structural elements that any enabling regulation must address: licensing criteria, capital ring-fencing, shariah governance, product approval, liquidity management, deposit insurance, consumer protection, tax neutrality, resolution planning, supervisory reporting, and public disclosure. For each element, the paper compares the four benchmark jurisdictions, scores them on a six-point adequacy scale developed by the author, and derives a recommended approach for the Serbian context. The paper is intended as a direct input into ongoing consultations between the University of Novi Sad and the National Bank of Serbia on alternative finance.

title: AAOIFI vs. IFSB Standards: Practical Divergences for European Supervisors
abstract: The Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI) and the Islamic Financial Services Board (IFSB) are the two principal international standard-setters for Islamic finance, but their standards overlap in scope and sometimes conflict in detail. This paper catalogues divergences between AAOIFI Financial Accounting Standards and IFSB Prudential Standards as they apply to three instrument classes—sukuk, murabaha, and takaful—and assesses the practical implications for European national supervisors who must decide which standards to reference in domestic regulation or supervisory guidance. Using a structured comparison matrix applied to the most recent versions of relevant standards as of 2024, the paper identifies twenty-three material divergences, of which nine concern measurement or classification in ways that affect capital calculations. The paper also surveys how five European jurisdictions (Luxembourg, UK, France, Germany, Ireland) have referenced or ignored these standards in their existing guidance and identifies a pattern of selective borrowing that creates cross-border regulatory inconsistency.

title: Packet-Loss Concealment for MPEG-4 Video Streams Using Error-Weighted Temporal Interpolation
abstract: This paper addresses the degradation of MPEG-4 video quality under random packet loss on IP wide-area links. A temporal-interpolation concealment algorithm is proposed that weights candidate reference frames by a combination of motion-vector coherence and per-macroblock error estimates derived from the decoded bitstream. Experiments were conducted by injecting uniform random losses at rates from 1% to 12% into 15 pre-encoded CIF-resolution test sequences at 512 kbit/s. PSNR improvements of 1.8–4.3 dB were observed relative to zero-motion concealment, and SSIM scores improved by 0.03–0.09 across the loss range. Subjective MOS tests with 24 participants confirmed statistically significant perceptual improvements at loss rates above 4%. Computational overhead of the proposed scheme adds approximately 7% to decoder processing time on a 1.2 GHz ARM reference platform, which is considered acceptable for set-top-box deployment. The method does not require any encoder-side modifications or additional signalling.

title: Comparison of H.264 and Dirac Codec Performance Under Simulated DSL Link Impairments
abstract: This study compares the rate-distortion and error-resilience behaviour of H.264 Baseline Profile and the Dirac wavelet codec under DSL-representative link conditions, including variable delay, jitter up to 40 ms, and correlated burst losses modelled with a two-state Markov chain. Twelve standard test sequences at resolutions from QCIF to 720p were encoded at four target bitrates between 256 kbit/s and 4 Mbit/s. H.264 achieved higher PSNR at low bitrates, but Dirac's lack of inter-frame dependency propagation resulted in measurably lower degradation under burst-loss conditions at rates exceeding 3% contiguous-packet loss. At 720p and 2 Mbit/s, the mean SSIM deficit after a five-packet burst was 0.07 for H.264 versus 0.03 for Dirac. The paper discusses practical implications for codec selection in residential broadband videoconferencing services and identifies bitrate thresholds at which the quality ordering between codecs reverses.

title: A Lightweight RTCP-Extension Mechanism for Per-Flow QoS Feedback in Multipoint Video Conferences
abstract: Real-time Transport Control Protocol (RTCP) provides only aggregate feedback, which is insufficient when individual flows in a multipoint video conference traverse links with heterogeneous quality. This paper specifies a compact extension to RTCP receiver reports that carries per-flow loss rate, one-way delay, and jitter estimates in an 8-byte overhead appended to standard RTCP RR packets. The extension is designed to remain compatible with existing RTCP parsers that ignore unknown fields. A prototype was implemented in a SIP-based videoconferencing client and tested in a six-node emulated WAN topology with independently configurable per-link loss and delay. The extension enabled a session controller to identify degraded flows within two RTCP reporting intervals rather than the five intervals required when relying on aggregate statistics. Bandwidth overhead of the mechanism is 3.1% relative to a typical H.264 stream at 512 kbit/s. Backward compatibility and deployment considerations are discussed.

title: Rate Adaptation Strategies for HTTP Adaptive Streaming Over Mobile LTE Networks
abstract: HTTP Adaptive Streaming (HAS) systems such as MPEG-DASH rely on throughput or buffer-occupancy signals to select quality representations. Mobile LTE networks introduce rapid, correlated fluctuations that cause standard throughput-estimation algorithms to either over-adapt, producing frequent quality switches, or under-adapt, wasting available capacity. This paper evaluates four published ABR algorithms—BBA-2, BOLA, Pensieve-derived heuristic, and a proprietary algorithm from a commercial CDN—on traces collected from 210 real LTE handover events in an urban area around Novi Sad. Switching frequency, startup delay, stall duration, and average received quality level were measured. BBA-2 produced the fewest quality switches (mean 1.4 per 60-second viewing session) but sacrificed 18% average bitrate relative to the best-performing algorithm. BOLA achieved the best average bitrate with acceptable stall rates. The paper derives threshold conditions under which buffer-based control outperforms throughput-based control and quantifies the influence of segment duration, tested at 2 s and 6 s.
venue: Proceedings of the European Wireless Conference (EWC)

title: Adaptive Codec Selection for Heterogeneous Video Conferencing Endpoints: A Decision-Tree Approach
abstract: In multipoint video conferences connecting endpoints with diverse hardware capabilities, a common codec must be negotiated or transcoding must be applied at a media server. This paper proposes a decision-tree classifier that selects the most efficient codec—from a candidate set including H.264, H.265, VP9, and AV1—for each participating endpoint pair based on six observable features: available uplink bandwidth, measured round-trip time, estimated CPU headroom, display resolution, declared battery status, and link type. The classifier was trained on 4 800 labeled session samples collected from a campus video-conferencing deployment over 14 months, with ground-truth quality labels derived from VMAF scores measured at the receiving endpoint. Cross-validation accuracy reached 83.7%. In a 60-session live trial, the decision-tree selection reduced mean transcoding server load by 22% compared to a fixed H.264-fallback policy while maintaining mean VMAF above 72. The feature importance analysis identifies available bandwidth and CPU headroom as the dominant selection drivers.

title: QoS Differentiation for Real-Time Video Using DSCP Marking in Campus SD-WAN Deployments
abstract: Software-Defined WAN architectures offer programmable traffic management but their interaction with Differentiated Services Code Point marking for real-time video is not well understood in campus-scale deployments. This paper reports a measurement study conducted on a 14-node SD-WAN testbed spanning three buildings of the Faculty of Technical Sciences, carrying synthetic H.264 video flows alongside background TCP bulk transfers. Four DSCP marking schemes were compared, including the EF per-hop behaviour and two institutional policies from Croatian and Romanian campus networks. Under 70% link utilisation, EF-marked video flows experienced mean one-way delay of 8.3 ms and zero packet loss, while best-effort video suffered 3.1% loss and 47 ms mean delay. At 90% utilisation, EF marking maintained loss below 0.5% whereas best-effort loss exceeded 11%. Interaction effects between SD-WAN path-selection algorithms and DSCP priority queuing are identified and quantified, and configuration recommendations for campus network operators are provided.

title: Temporal and Spatial Error Propagation in AV1 Under Packet Loss: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: AV1 is increasingly deployed for web-based real-time communication but its error-resilience characteristics are less studied than those of H.264 or H.265. This paper presents an empirical analysis of temporal and spatial error propagation in AV1 encoded with libaom 2.0 under uniform random and burst packet-loss conditions ranging from 0.5% to 15%. Ten test sequences at 1080p and five at 360p were encoded at 500 kbit/s and 1.5 Mbit/s with keyframe intervals of 30, 60, and 120 frames. Propagation was quantified using per-frame PSNR-Y degradation relative to a loss-free reference. AV1's compound prediction modes were found to extend spatial error propagation beyond the boundaries observed in H.264, affecting up to 34% more macroblocks per corrupted frame at 120-frame keyframe intervals. A reduced keyframe interval of 30 frames constrained mean propagation duration to 1.1 s at 5% loss without exceeding a 12% bitrate increase. Implications for WebRTC deployments are discussed.

title: Real-Time Video Streaming in Vehicular Networks: Codec and Protocol Trade-offs on the Novi Sad Urban Corridor
abstract: Vehicular networks based on IEEE 802.11p and LTE-V2X exhibit rapid link-quality transitions that challenge real-time video streaming. This study characterises video streaming performance along a 12 km urban test route in Novi Sad using a dedicated instrumented vehicle. Measurements span 80 driving passes over four months, capturing throughput, handover frequency, and loss statistics. Four codec-transport combinations were tested: H.264 over RTP/UDP, H.265 over RTP/UDP, AV1 over QUIC, and VP9 over QUIC. AV1 over QUIC achieved the highest mean VMAF score (68.4) despite lower raw throughput on 802.11p segments, attributed to QUIC's connection migration reducing re-establishment latency after handovers by a median of 310 ms. H.264 over UDP produced the lowest startup delay (0.9 s) but highest stall rate (6.3%). The paper provides a selection matrix mapping link-type and speed combinations to preferred codec-transport pairings based on measured performance distributions.

title: Bandwidth Estimation Accuracy Under Competing Traffic: Implications for Adaptive Video Rate Control
abstract: Adaptive video controllers rely on accurate bandwidth estimates to select appropriate encoding bitrates, yet most estimators are calibrated in isolation from competing background flows. This paper evaluates seven bandwidth estimators—including GCC, NADA, SCReAM, and four research implementations—under six competing traffic profiles (file transfer, video-on-demand, gaming, VoIP mix, cloud backup, and idle) on a controlled 50 Mbit/s WAN emulation testbed. Estimation error, measured as the ratio of estimated to actual available bandwidth, is characterised across 1 350 thirty-second test runs. All estimators overshoot available bandwidth during cloud-backup background flows by 15–38%, a condition caused by the bursty inter-packet gaps produced by backup software. NADA showed the smallest overshoot at 15% but also the highest variance under gaming traffic. A correction factor derived from passive traffic classification is proposed and reduces overshoot to below 8% across all profiles. The data set is made available for reproducibility.

title: Learned Packet-Loss Concealment for Real-Time Video Using Lightweight Convolutional Frame Synthesis
abstract: Deep-learning approaches to packet-loss concealment have shown promise in offline video restoration but their applicability in real-time decoders is limited by computational cost. This paper investigates a lightweight convolutional frame-synthesis network trained to reconstruct lost macroblocks using two preceding and one subsequent decoded frame, constrained to run within 8 ms on a mid-range GPU. The network uses a three-stage encoder-decoder architecture with 1.2 million parameters, trained on 48 000 synthetic loss events applied to sequences from the UHD-1 dataset. At a loss rate of 5%, mean PSNR improvement over motion-compensated temporal interpolation is 2.1 dB and mean SSIM improvement is 0.04, measured on a held-out test set of 6 000 frames. At 10% loss, improvements grow to 3.4 dB and 0.07. Processing latency on an NVIDIA embedded GPU representative of a video-gateway appliance is 5.3 ms per frame, fitting within a 60 fps real-time constraint. Failure modes at scene cuts and under high spatial complexity are characterised.

title: Sex-dependent differences in AgRP and POMC neuronal activation following acute caloric restriction in rats
abstract: Agouti-related peptide (AgRP) and pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons in the arcuate nucleus exert opposing actions on energy intake. We compared Fos immunoreactivity co-localised with AgRP and POMC in male and female Sprague-Dawley rats after 24-hour fasting versus free feeding. Brains from six animals per sex per condition were sectioned coronally and processed for double immunofluorescence. Fasted males showed a 3.1-fold increase in AgRP-Fos co-labelled cells compared with fed males; fasted females showed a 1.7-fold increase. POMC-Fos co-labelling declined similarly in both sexes during fasting. Circulating oestradiol correlated negatively with AgRP neuronal activation in females (r = −0.71, p = 0.009). These results indicate that oestradiol may attenuate orexigenic AgRP responses to energy deficit, providing a mechanistic basis for reported sex differences in meal patterning and refeeding behaviour.

title: Orexin-A immunoreactivity in the lateral hypothalamus of obese Zucker rats compared with lean littermates
abstract: Orexin-A (hypocretin-1) produced in the lateral hypothalamic area modulates arousal and feeding behaviour. We used immunohistochemistry to quantify orexin-A-positive neurons and optical density of orexin-A staining in the lateral hypothalamus of obese (fa/fa) and lean Zucker rats at 12 and 20 weeks of age (n = 6 per group). At 12 weeks, neuron counts did not differ between genotypes. At 20 weeks, obese rats showed 22% fewer orexin-A-positive neurons than lean controls (p = 0.018) and a 31% reduction in mean optical density (p = 0.004). Correlation analysis revealed that orexin-A cell count correlated negatively with body weight at 20 weeks (r = −0.62). These morphological data suggest progressive attrition of orexin signalling in advanced obesity, which may paradoxically facilitate hyperphagia through loss of satiety-promoting orexin effects on the melanocortin pathway.

title: Indirect calorimetry reveals reduced dark-phase energy expenditure in diet-induced obese male rats without changes in locomotor activity
abstract: We characterised the metabolic phenotype of male Wistar rats fed a high-fat diet (45% kcal fat) for 12 weeks using a four-chamber indirect calorimetry system. Respiratory exchange ratio (RER), oxygen consumption (VO₂), and spontaneous locomotor activity were recorded continuously over 72-hour periods at weeks 4, 8, and 12 (n = 10 per group). High-fat-fed rats showed a progressive decline in dark-phase VO₂ from week 8 onward; by week 12, dark-phase VO₂ was 11% lower than in chow controls (p = 0.003). RER was also reduced (0.79 ± 0.02 vs. 0.86 ± 0.02; p < 0.001), reflecting increased fat oxidation. Locomotor activity counts were not significantly different between groups at any time point. Caloric intake was 18% higher in high-fat animals across the study. These data indicate that reduced metabolic rate during the active phase, rather than decreased activity, is an early contributor to positive energy balance in this model.

title: Circadian variation in hypothalamic NPY and AgRP mRNA in lean and diet-induced obese rats
abstract: Hypothalamic orexigenic neuropeptide expression follows circadian rhythms that may be disrupted in obesity. We sacrificed lean and diet-induced obese (DIO) male Wistar rats at six time points across a 24-hour light-dark cycle (Zeitgeber times ZT0, ZT4, ZT8, ZT12, ZT16, ZT20; n = 6 per time point per group) and measured arcuate NPY and AgRP mRNA by quantitative RT-PCR. In lean animals, NPY expression peaked at ZT12 (onset of dark phase) and was lowest at ZT4. This rhythm was markedly blunted in DIO rats: the ZT12-to-ZT4 fold-change fell from 2.8 in lean to 1.4 in obese animals. AgRP showed a similar attenuation. The amplitude of the melatonin rhythm, measured by plasma RIA, was also reduced in DIO rats, suggesting upstream disruption of circadian entrainment. Loss of neuropeptide rhythmicity may contribute to impaired meal timing and sustained hyperphagia in obesity.

title: Ghrelin receptor mRNA in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus decreases after prolonged high-fat feeding
abstract: Ghrelin acts on growth hormone secretagogue receptors (GHSR1a) distributed across multiple hypothalamic nuclei to stimulate food intake. We quantified GHSR1a mRNA in the arcuate, paraventricular (PVN), dorsomedial, and ventromedial hypothalamic nuclei of male rats after 4 and 16 weeks on a high-fat diet using radioactive in situ hybridisation. Plasma acyl-ghrelin and des-acyl-ghrelin were measured by RIA. After 4 weeks, GHSR1a mRNA was unchanged across all nuclei. After 16 weeks, PVN expression was 40% lower in high-fat than in chow-fed rats (p = 0.011), while other nuclei showed no significant change. Plasma acyl-ghrelin was reduced in DIO animals at both time points. The selective downregulation of PVN GHSR1a may reflect adaptive desensitisation or altered neuronal composition and could contribute to disrupted meal termination signalling in prolonged obesity.

title: Hypothalamic neuropeptides in rodent models of diet-induced obesity: methods and pitfalls
abstract: Rodent models of diet-induced obesity are widely used to study hypothalamic appetite regulation, but methodological inconsistencies across laboratories make results difficult to compare. This chapter surveys the most common approaches—high-fat diet formulations, duration of feeding, choice of rat or mouse strain, methods of tissue collection, and quantification of neuropeptide mRNA versus peptide protein levels—and discusses how each affects reproducibility. We cover NPY, AgRP, POMC, orexin, and melanin-concentrating hormone as the main targets of study, and compare radioimmunometric assays with ELISA platforms for peptide quantification in microdissected hypothalamic punches. We also address statistical power considerations specific to between-group designs in this literature, noting that many published studies use sample sizes that provide less than 80% power to detect effects of the magnitude typically reported. Practical recommendations are provided for tissue preservation, punch coordinates, and normalisation strategies in gene expression studies.

title: Intermittent caloric restriction normalises arcuate AgRP expression and reduces fat mass in female diet-induced obese rats more effectively than continuous restriction
abstract: We compared two caloric restriction protocols in female Wistar rats with established diet-induced obesity (16 weeks on 45% fat diet): continuous 30% caloric restriction (CR, n = 12), intermittent restriction (alternate-day 50% restriction, iCR, n = 12), and an ad libitum obese control (n = 12) over eight weeks. Body composition was measured by DEXA. Arcuate AgRP and POMC mRNA were quantified at sacrifice. Both restriction protocols reduced body weight and fat mass significantly relative to obese controls. iCR animals lost 18% more fat mass than CR animals (p = 0.031) despite similar total caloric deficits. AgRP mRNA returned to levels not significantly different from lean reference animals only in the iCR group. Insulin sensitivity (HOMA-IR) improved in both groups, but the improvement was greater in iCR. These findings suggest that the temporal pattern of caloric restriction influences hypothalamic neuropeptide responses independently of total energy deficit.

title: Plasma nesfatin-1 correlates with hypothalamic NUCB2 mRNA and meal size in rats across a range of adiposities
abstract: Nesfatin-1, cleaved from nucleobindin-2 (NUCB2), is produced in hypothalamic nuclei and acts as an anorexigenic signal. Its relationship with adiposity and meal structure has not been systematically characterised across a graded range of body fatness. We assembled four groups of male Wistar rats differing in adiposity index (lean, mildly overweight, moderately obese, severely obese; n = 10 per group) created by varying diet fat content and duration. Plasma nesfatin-1 was measured by ELISA; hypothalamic NUCB2 mRNA by RT-PCR; meal size and intermeal interval were recorded by automated monitoring over 72 hours. Plasma nesfatin-1 correlated positively with adiposity index (r = 0.68, p < 0.001) and negatively with meal size (r = −0.54, p < 0.001). Hypothalamic NUCB2 mRNA showed a weaker positive correlation with adiposity. The data support a tonic role for nesfatin-1 in meal size limitation that is preserved across varying degrees of obesity.

title: High-fat diet during adolescence programmes arcuate nucleus neuropeptide expression and increases obesity susceptibility in adult rats
abstract: Exposure to dietary excess during critical developmental windows may persistently alter hypothalamic circuitry. Male and female Wistar rats were fed a 45% fat diet from postnatal day 21 to 60 (adolescent HFD group), then switched to standard chow until day 150. Controls received chow throughout. At day 150, all animals were challenged with a six-week high-fat diet. Body weight, fat mass, arcuate NPY and POMC mRNA, and plasma leptin were assessed at day 60, day 150, and after the challenge. Adolescent HFD females, but not males, showed persistently elevated NPY mRNA at day 150 despite normal body weight at that time point. Both sexes from the adolescent HFD group accumulated more fat during the adult challenge than controls (females: +24%; males: +17%; p < 0.05). These data suggest a sex-differentiated programming effect of adolescent dietary fat excess on hypothalamic orexigenic tone.

title: Melanin-concentrating hormone receptor 1 binding in the hypothalamus is reduced in rats with severe diet-induced obesity: an autoradiographic study
abstract: Melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH) signals through MCHR1 in the hypothalamus to promote positive energy balance. Whether MCHR1 availability changes with obesity severity has not been examined with quantitative receptor autoradiography. We used [¹²⁵I]-MCH radioligand binding on coronal hypothalamic sections from lean, moderately obese, and severely obese male Wistar rats (n = 8 per group). Specific binding was quantified in the lateral hypothalamic area, zona incerta, and ventromedial hypothalamus using image analysis. Severely obese rats showed 29% lower MCHR1 binding density in the lateral hypothalamus compared with lean controls (p = 0.006); moderately obese rats showed an intermediate, non-significant reduction. Binding in the zona incerta and ventromedial hypothalamus was not significantly affected. MCH peptide content, measured by RIA in hypothalamic extracts, was unchanged across groups. Reduced MCHR1 availability in severe obesity may represent receptor downregulation following chronic ligand exposure.

title: Orexin-B and prepro-orexin mRNA across the oestrous cycle in lean and diet-induced obese female rats
abstract: Orexin signalling intersects with reproductive neuroendocrinology, yet how the oestrous cycle modulates lateral hypothalamic orexin expression in obese females is unclear. We characterised prepro-orexin mRNA and orexin-B immunoreactivity in the lateral hypothalamus across the four phases of the oestrous cycle (proestrus, oestrus, metoestrus, dioestrus; n = 6 per phase per group) in lean and DIO female Wistar rats. Oestrous phase was confirmed by vaginal cytology. Lean rats showed significantly higher prepro-orexin mRNA at proestrus compared with dioestrus (1.8-fold; p = 0.017), consistent with an LH-surge-associated increase. This cyclical variation was absent in DIO rats, which also showed irregular cycle length (mean 5.8 ± 1.1 days vs. 4.1 ± 0.4 days in lean; p = 0.002). Orexin-B immunoreactive cell counts paralleled the mRNA pattern. The loss of oestrous-cycle-dependent orexin fluctuation in obese females may relate to disrupted GnRH pulsatility and altered energy sensing.

title: Ćutanje uprave u srpskom Zakonu o opštem upravnom postupku: analiza normativnog okvira i sudske prakse Upravnog suda
abstract: Rad istražuje institut ćutanja uprave u Zakonu o opštem upravnom postupku Republike Srbije iz 2016. godine, poređenjem sa ranijim zakonom iz 1997. Metodom analize 214 odluka Upravnog suda donetih u periodu 2017–2020. utvrđuje se koliko često podnosioci zahteva pribegavaju fikciji odbijanja i u kojim upravnim oblastima se ćutanje javlja najčešće. Rezultati pokazuju da su oblasti građevinarstva, urbanizma i inspekcijskog nadzora odgovorne za 61% evidentiranih slučajeva. Analiza otkriva da sudovi pretežno odbacuju tužbe zbog procesnih propusta stranaka, a ne zbog nepostojanja pasivnosti organa. Rad zaključuje da rok od 60 dana propisan zakonom nije dovoljan podsticaj za aktivnost uprave te predlaže uvođenje administrativnih kazni kao dopunskog mehanizma.

title: Administrative Silence in Comparative European Law: Typologies and Remedial Mechanisms across Ten EU Member States
abstract: This article surveys legislative and judicial responses to administrative silence in ten EU member states — Germany, France, Poland, Hungary, Croatia, Slovenia, Austria, Italy, Spain and Portugal — drawing on official statutory texts, supreme administrative court databases and secondary literature. Two principal typologies are identified: positive silence regimes (where non-response equals tacit approval) and negative silence regimes (deemed refusal). The study codes 78 distinct statutory provisions and classifies them according to six variables including the applicable time limit, the scope of exclusions, available remedies and the existence of disciplinary consequences for responsible officials. Data indicate that the median statutory response deadline has shortened from 90 to 30 days over the 2000–2020 period across the sample. The article argues that positive silence provisions tend to reduce backlog in permitting procedures but carry rule-of-law risks in areas involving third-party rights.

Rad ukazuje na nedovoljnu koordinaciju između ombudsmana i upravnih sudova kao sistemski nedostatak, te predlaže formalizovani mehanizam informisanja koji bi premostio taj jaz.
