title: The ReNEUAL Model Rules on Administrative Procedure and the Treatment of Silence: Implications for Western Balkan Accession Candidates
abstract: The article examines provisions relating to inaction and silence in the ReNEUAL Model Rules on EU Administrative Procedure (2014), focusing on Books III and IV concerning single-case decision-making and contracts. It evaluates the extent to which these provisions are consistent with the case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union and the European Court of Human Rights on the right to a decision within a reasonable time. The article then assesses alignment between the ReNEUAL standards and the current administrative procedure codes of Serbia, North Macedonia and Montenegro, using a structured gap analysis covering 24 criteria. Findings reveal that all three states lack explicit provisions on positive silence and that none provides a court-enforceable time limit for first-instance decisions outside the general procedural code. The article recommends targeted amendments ahead of Chapter 23 screening reviews.

title: Pravo na donošenje odluke u razumnom roku u srpskom upravnom sporu: između zakonskog ideala i sudske realnosti
abstract: Rad analizira garancije prava na suđenje u razumnom roku iz člana 6 Evropske konvencije za zaštitu ljudskih prava u kontekstu srpskog upravnog spora regulisanog Zakonom o upravnim sporovima iz 2009. godine. Kroz pregled 96 presuda Evropskog suda za ljudska prava donetih u predmetima protiv Srbije u periodu 2010–2022, autor utvrđuje da se 34% pronađenih povreda tiče trajanja i ishoda postupaka pred Upravnim sudom. Posebna pažnja posvećena je slučajevima u kojima pasivnost prvostepenog organa prethodi sudskom postupku, čime se efektivno udvostručuje period neizvesnosti za stranku. Analiza pokazuje da domaći sudovi retko koriste institut privremene mere radi obezbeđenja hitnog postupanja uprave. Predlažu se izmene sudskog poslovnika kojima bi se uvelo automatsko praćenje predmeta po isteku 18 meseci od podnošenja tužbe.

title: Tacit Approval as a Facilitation Tool in Business Licensing: Lessons from Slovenia and Croatia for Serbia
abstract: Using semi-structured interviews with 23 senior civil servants and a review of licensing files across three economic sectors (food safety, construction, and environmental permits), this study assesses the practical effects of positive administrative silence regimes introduced in Slovenia in 2004 and Croatia in 2009. The research recorded outcomes in 380 licensing cases in each country over five years post-reform. Positive silence reduced average licensing time by 31 days in construction but had no statistically significant effect in environmental permitting, where third-party consultation requirements created exceptions. The study identifies implementation bottlenecks attributable to the absence of electronic dossier management and unclear rules on the documentary evidence required to trigger the silence clock. Recommendations are addressed specifically to the Serbian Ministry of Public Administration, which was consulting on a regulatory reform package at the time of writing.

title: Sudska zaštita u slučaju ćutanja uprave: uporednopravna analiza procesnih modela Austrije, Nemačke i Srbije
abstract: Rad polazi od hipoteze da se efikasnost sudske zaštite od ćutanja uprave ne može svesti na pitanje propisanog roka, već zavisi od sveukupnog dizajna procesnog modela — uključujući distribuciju tereta dokazivanja, ovlašćenja suda da zameni upravu u donošenju meritornog rešenja, kao i troškove iniciranja spora. Komparativnom metodom ispituju se procesni okviri Austrije (Bundesverwaltungsgericht), Nemačke (Verpflichtungsklage) i Srbije (upravni spor zbog ćutanja). Austrijskim modelom direktnog preuzimanja nadležnosti od strane suda postiže se najbrža zaštita u proseku, ali uz rizik preuranjenih odluka u tehničko-složenim predmetima. Srpski model, koji obavezuje sud da vrati predmet organu, prolongira zaštitu u proseku za 14 meseci po nalazima empirijskog dela rada zasnovanog na 60 predmeta. Predlažu se izmene Zakona o upravnim sporovima kojima bi se sudu dala opcija meritorne odluke u jasno definisanim kategorijama predmeta.

title: Liability of Public Bodies for Damage Caused by Administrative Inaction: A Comparative Survey
abstract: Administrative silence may generate not only a procedural claim but also a tort claim for damage suffered during the period of unlawful inaction. This article surveys the conditions under which five legal systems — France, Germany, Austria, Croatia and Serbia — allow recovery for harm caused by delayed or omitted administrative decisions. Drawing on court databases and statutory provisions collected between 2010 and 2024, the study records 142 reported tort claims attributable to administrative inaction and analyses outcomes, damages awarded and the causal link requirements applied by courts. French administrative courts showed the highest rate of successful claims (54%), while Serbian courts granted damages in fewer than 10% of relevant cases, largely because claimants could not demonstrate that earlier action would have produced a positive decision. The article identifies harmonisation opportunities in the context of Serbia's EU accession Chapter 32 negotiations.

title: Elektronska uprava i rokovi u odlučivanju: da li digitalizacija smanjuje učestalost ćutanja uprave?
abstract: Istraživanje ispituje vezu između uvođenja sistema e-uprave i učestalosti ćutanja uprave u osam opština Vojvodine u periodu 2015–2021. Korišćenjem panel podataka iz Registra pružalaca usluga eUprave i godišnjih statističkih izveštaja Ministarstva državne uprave i lokalne samouprave, rad primenjuje metod fiksnih efekata kako bi kontrolisao opštinsku heterogenost. Rezultati pokazuju da uvođenje elektronskog portala za podnošenje zahteva smanjuje registrovane slučajeve ćutanja u proseku za 18%, ali je taj efekt statistički značajan samo u opštinama koje su istovremeno uvele unutrašnji sistem za praćenje rokova. Tehničko rešenje bez prateće reorganizacije procedura ne dovodi do merljivog poboljšanja. Rad doprinosi debati o e-upravi kao instrumentu vladavine prava, a ne samo tehničke efikasnosti.

title: Silence as a Systemic Problem: Organisational and Staffing Correlates of Administrative Non-Response in Serbian Municipalities
abstract: This mixed-methods study investigates organisational factors associated with systematically high rates of administrative silence in Serbian local governments. Survey data were collected from 74 municipal administrative services in 2020, supplemented by in-depth interviews with 18 heads of administrative departments. Descriptive statistics show that municipalities with fewer than three administrative staff per 1,000 residents have a non-response rate three times higher than larger units, while staff turnover above 15% per annum is the strongest single predictor of delayed decision-making (β = 0.42, p < 0.01). Organisational culture indicators — specifically the absence of internal complaint tracking and the non-application of disciplinary proceedings for missed deadlines — also correlate with elevated silence rates. The article recommends a national minimum-capacity standard for local administrative units and proposes integrating silence metrics into the existing local government performance assessment framework operated by the Standing Conference of Towns and Municipalities.

title: Ćutanje uprave i zaštita ranjivih grupa: poseban osvrt na lica sa invaliditetom i socijalno ugrožene porodice
abstract: Ovaj rad sagledava asimetričan teret koji ćutanje uprave nameće ranjivim grupama, posebno licima sa invaliditetom i korisnicima prava iz sistema socijalne zaštite. Analizom 312 predmeta centara za socijalni rad u Srbiji u periodu 2016–2020. i intervjuima sa 14 socijalnih radnika, utvrđeno je da pasivnost organa dovodi do prosečnog kašnjenja od 91 dan u isplatama naknada, uz posebno izražen problem u slučajevima iniciranja postupka za sticanje pravnog statusa u cilju ostvarivanja prava na smeštaj. Pravni okvir koji predviđa jednak tretman svih stranaka u slučaju ćutanja ne uvažava disproporcionalnu štetu po grupe koje ne raspolažu resursima za pokretanje upravnog spora. Predlažu se procesne olakšice poput besplatnog pravnog zastupanja ex lege i skraćenih sudskih rokova za ove kategorije predmeta.

title: The Right to Good Administration under Article 41 of the EU Charter and Its Horizontal Effects on Candidate State Administration
abstract: Article 41 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union codifies a right to have affairs handled impartially, fairly and within a reasonable time, but its direct applicability is confined to EU institutions and bodies. This chapter examines the extent to which the right to good administration nonetheless shapes administrative law reform in EU candidate states through the conditionality mechanism, case law of the Court of Justice, and the European Ombudsman's standards. The analysis draws on accession progress reports for Serbia, North Macedonia and Albania for the period 2014–2024 and codes 47 Commission recommendations relating to administrative procedure modernisation. The chapter argues that Article 41 functions as a soft constitutional template even where it lacks binding force, and that its influence on candidate state procedural reform is most visible in the area of time limits and the obligation to state reasons — with administrative silence representing a residual gap in transposition.

title: Procesne pretpostavke za tužbu zbog ćutanja uprave pred Upravnim sudom Srbije: teorija i praksa
abstract: Rad se bavi procesnim uslovima prihvatljivosti tužbe zbog ćutanja uprave prema Zakonu o upravnim sporovima iz 2009. godine — aktivnom i pasivnom legitimacijom, rokovima, prethodnim izjavljivanjem žalbe organu drugog stepena i izuzetkom hitnog postupka. Analizom 180 rešenja Upravnog suda o odbacivanju tužbe zbog ćutanja u periodu 2017–2022. utvrđeno je da se 44% odbacivanja zasniva na propustu stranke da podnese prethodnu žalbu drugostepenom organu, iako je organ bio obavezan da postupa po samoj sili zakona. Diskrepancija između teorijskog modela i sudske prakse ukazuje na nerazumevanje procesne logike ćutanja unutar same sudske institucije. Rad sugeriše izmene zakonske odredbe kojom bi se jednoznačno razgraničila polja primene hierarhijskog i direktnog sudskog nadzora.

title: Transposing EU Directives into National Labour Law: Monitoring Compliance Gaps in Serbia's Alignment Process
abstract: Serbia's progress reports under the EU accession process contain formal assessments of directive transposition, but these reports rarely identify compliance gaps at the operational level—that is, whether transposed norms are actually applied by inspection and enforcement bodies. This study examines the transposition and operational implementation of four EU labour directives transposed into Serbian law between 2013 and 2018: directives on working time, parental leave, temporary agency work, and information and consultation of workers. For each directive, the transposing legislation was compared to the source directive, and inspection activity data for 2016–2018 were analysed to determine whether inspectors applied the transposed provisions. Findings show transposition fidelity of 84 to 96 percent at the textual level, but operational application rates ranging from 41 to 79 percent depending on the directive. The article identifies the factors—training gaps, resource constraints, and ambiguous enforcement mandates—that explain the implementation shortfall, and proposes a compliance-gap monitoring protocol for use during accession negotiations.

title: Reading Regulatory Text: An Empirical Study of How Labour Inspectors Interpret Ambiguous Statutory Provisions
abstract: Empirical studies of how street-level officials interpret statutory text are rare in administrative law scholarship. This article reports findings from a structured vignette study involving 94 active labour inspectors in Serbia, presented with twelve ambiguous statutory provisions drawn from real legislation, each accompanied by a factual scenario. For each vignette, inspectors recorded their interpretive conclusion, rated their confidence, and described their reasoning in a short free-text field. Responses were coded for interpretive method using a scheme with five categories. Literal interpretation dominated (47 percent of responses), followed by reference to prior ministry guidance (31 percent). Purposive reasoning appeared in only 8 percent of responses, and comparative reference to European practice in 3 percent. Confidence ratings were highest when ministry guidance existed and lowest for provisions enacted in the three years before the study. The article discusses the implications for regulatory design—specifically, the finding that ministry guidance circulars are more influential than legislative intent materials for inspector behaviour—and argues for a more systematic guidance publication programme.

title: Transfer of State-Owned Real Property to Local Self-Government Units in Serbia: Procedural Gaps and Practice
abstract: The 2011 Law on Public Property established a framework for transferring real estate from the Republic of Serbia to municipalities and cities, yet implementation has proceeded unevenly across local self-government units. This paper analyses the transfer procedure as regulated in Articles 19–27 of the Law, maps the procedural requirements against a dataset of 112 transfer decisions published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbia between 2012 and 2022, and identifies the most frequent grounds for rejection or suspension of transfer requests. Approximately 29 percent of reviewed decisions were contested before the administrative court due to unresolved cadastral discrepancies, and a further 14 percent were delayed by competing claims from public enterprises. The paper also surveys the analogous Hungarian and Croatian models for comparative reference. The authors argue that the Serbian legislator should introduce a mandatory pre-transfer cadastral rectification procedure to reduce litigation and accelerate the consolidation of local property bases.

title: Teaching Administrative Law History in the Western Balkans: Curriculum Practices and Archival Resources
abstract: This short communication reports on a survey of administrative law curricula at 14 law faculties across six Western Balkan states, conducted in 2024, examining the extent to which the historical development of administrative jurisdiction is treated as a distinct subject or integrated into general administrative law courses. Responses from 29 faculty members show that historical content is present in all curricula but occupies fewer than 15 percent of contact hours in 11 of the 14 institutions surveyed. The paper also inventories available archival resources for teaching and research in the field, including digitised court registers from the Austrian State Archive, partially digitised files of the Yugoslav State Council held in Belgrade, and the as-yet undigitised administrative court records of the Banovinas held in regional archives in Novi Sad, Sarajevo, and Zagreb. The note proposes a minimum set of primary sources suitable for a regionally shared open-access teaching repository and calls for coordinated digitisation efforts.

title: Načelo određenosti pravne norme u podzakonskom normiranju: nemačka doktrina i mogućnosti recepcije u srpskom pravu
abstract: Rad ispituje mogućnost recepcije nemačke doktrine Bestimmtheitsgrundsatz u srpski ustavni i upravni poredak kao instrumenta ograničavanja diskrecionarnih normativnih ovlašćenja regulatornih tela. Nakon prikaza razvoja ove doktrine u nemačkoj ustavnosudskoj i upravnosudskoj praksi od 1949. do 2019. godine, autor analizira srpski Ustav i Zakon o državnoj upravi u svetlosti iste doktrine, identifikujući terminološke i sistemske razlike koje otežavaju direktnu recepciju. Posebno se razmatraju presude Saveznog ustavnog suda Nemačke u predmetima koji se tiču emisione dozvole za nuklearne elektrane i prehrambenih standarda, kao paradigmatski primeri primene načela. Zaključuje se da srpska pravna tradicija poseduje dovoljno receptivnih mehanizama za usvajanje suštine ove doktrine kroz izmenu sudske prakse, bez potrebe za formalnom ustavnom revizijom.

title: Vertical price transmission in the Serbian pork chain: evidence from farm-gate and retail monthly data, 2000–2008
abstract: This paper examines vertical price transmission between farm-gate pig prices and retail pork prices in Serbia using monthly data covering 2000–2008. The Engle–Granger two-step cointegration procedure confirms a long-run relationship between the two price series. An asymmetric error correction model is estimated to test whether positive and negative deviations from the long-run equilibrium are corrected at different speeds. Results indicate that retail prices respond faster to farm-gate price increases than to decreases, with adjustment half-lives of approximately 1.8 months and 3.5 months, respectively. The asymmetry is statistically significant at the 5 percent level and is interpreted as evidence of imperfect competition at the processing and retail stages. The finding that price increases are transmitted more quickly than decreases is consistent with markup pricing behavior observed in concentrated retail environments. Policy implications for monitoring retail margins and strengthening producer bargaining power are discussed.

title: Marketing margins along the Serbian pig meat chain: a seasonal decomposition approach
abstract: This study quantifies marketing margins between farm, slaughterhouse, and retail stages in the Serbian pork supply chain using weekly price data from 2005 to 2011 collected by the Serbian Ministry of Agriculture price monitoring programme. Seasonal decomposition using X-12-ARIMA separates trend, seasonal, and irregular components of each margin series. The analysis reveals that farm-to-slaughterhouse margins show pronounced seasonality peaking in late autumn, coinciding with the traditional pig-slaughtering season, while slaughterhouse-to-retail margins remain comparatively stable across seasons. On average, the farm stage captures 38 percent of the final retail price, slaughterhouses 27 percent, and retailers 35 percent, with considerable inter-annual variation. Granger causality tests confirm that retail price movements lead farm-gate adjustments with a lag of roughly four weeks. The paper discusses implications for contract arrangements between farmers and processors.

title: Threshold effects in farm-to-retail price transmission: the case of pork in the Western Balkans
abstract: Using a threshold autoregressive (TAR) model and a momentum-TAR specification, this paper tests for regime-dependent price adjustment in the pork chains of Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina over 2003–2012. Monthly farm-gate and retail price series were sourced from national statistical offices. The threshold values estimated for the Serbian chain imply that deviations from long-run equilibrium smaller than approximately 4 percent are not systematically corrected, consistent with menu cost or renegotiation cost explanations. For deviations above the threshold, upward shocks are absorbed within two months at retail, while downward shocks take on average five months. Croatian and Bosnian chains display similar asymmetric patterns, though thresholds differ. The results suggest that transaction costs and retailer market power interact to generate asymmetric adjustment across the region.

title: Do food retail concentration indices predict asymmetric price transmission? Cross-country evidence from Southeast Europe
abstract: This paper links structural indicators of grocery retail concentration—four-firm concentration ratio (CR4) and the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index—to the degree of price transmission asymmetry estimated from threshold error correction models across seven Southeast European countries for the period 2007–2014. Pork and poultry chains are examined. Country-level retail concentration data were compiled from trade association reports and national competition authority publications. Regression analysis of asymmetry coefficients on concentration indices shows a statistically significant positive association: a 10-percentage-point increase in CR4 is associated with an increase in the asymmetry ratio of approximately 0.18 (p < 0.05). The relationship is stronger for pork than for poultry. Results are robust to inclusion of GDP per capita, urbanization rate, and cold-chain infrastructure proxies as controls. The findings support the market-power hypothesis of price transmission asymmetry but do not rule out supply-side adjustment cost explanations.

title: Price transmission under trade policy uncertainty: Serbian pork markets during the 2014–2015 Russian import ban
abstract: Russia's 2014 import ban on EU agri-food products created a temporary supply surplus in several European pork markets that propagated through the Western Balkan region via trade linkages. This paper estimates how the external shock affected vertical price transmission dynamics within the Serbian pork chain using an autoregressive distributed lag model with a structural break test applied to monthly data from January 2013 to December 2015. The Zivot-Andrews test identifies a structural break in the cointegrating relationship around September 2014. Post-break adjustment speeds at farm level roughly doubled compared to the pre-ban period, indicating heightened price transmission during the surplus phase. Retail margins widened by an average of 12 percent in the four quarters following the ban onset. The case illustrates how external trade policy shocks can temporarily alter domestic transmission regimes even in countries not directly subject to the policy.

title: Asymmetric price pass-through along the Serbian pork value chain: a practitioners' workshop summary
abstract: This conference paper reports findings presented at a joint workshop of researchers and meat industry practitioners in Novi Sad in May 2016. Drawing on updated price transmission estimates for 2010–2016, the presentation showed that the degree of asymmetry at the farm-to-processor stage remained stable over the period, while asymmetry at the processor-to-retailer stage increased after 2013, a period coinciding with market entry of several large-format retail chains. Participants from the processing industry contested the interpretation that retail concentration drives asymmetry, citing logistics cost volatility and energy price pass-through as alternative explanations. The discussion highlighted data gaps, including the absence of a publicly available weekly wholesale price series for processed pork cuts, and recommended establishment of a coordinated price monitoring system modeled on EU price reporting obligations.

title: Feed-to-pork price transmission: how input cost shocks travel through the Serbian value chain
abstract: Rising feed grain prices triggered by drought in 2012 and again in 2017 created input cost shocks that propagated upstream in the Serbian pork value chain. This paper traces the pass-through of corn and soybean meal price increases to pig live-weight prices and subsequently to retail pork cuts using a structural VAR model estimated on monthly data from 2005 to 2019. Impulse response functions show that a 10 percent increase in feed costs leads to a statistically significant 4.2 percent increase in farm-gate live pig prices within three months and a 2.1 percent increase in retail pork prices within six months, with the remainder absorbed as margin compression at intermediary stages. The asymmetric pass-through of input cost increases is confirmed using sign-restricted VARs; retailers absorb downward feed cost shocks entirely rather than passing them on to consumers. The results suggest that the feed-to-pork transmission channel is considerably attenuated by retailer pricing behavior.

title: Retail price rigidity for pork products in Serbia: evidence from scanner data, 2016–2020
abstract: Using a dataset of approximately 2.1 million weekly price observations for 34 standardized pork stock-keeping units obtained from the electronic point-of-sale system of a major Serbian grocery retailer under a confidentiality agreement, this paper estimates the frequency and magnitude of retail price changes at the product level. On average, a pork product price changes once every 7.4 weeks, which is substantially less frequent than comparable estimates for German and Polish retailers. Downward price changes are significantly less frequent than upward changes (ratio 0.61), corroborating asymmetry found in aggregate time-series studies. Hazard model estimates show that the probability of a price change is sharply elevated in the two weeks following a farm-gate price spike. The granular data allow us to separate genuine price stickiness from product substitution and assortment rotation effects that confound aggregate price indices.

title: Pork value chain margins under inflation: Serbia 2021–2023
abstract: Serbia experienced a sustained period of high food price inflation between late 2021 and mid-2023, with retail pork prices rising by approximately 38 percent in nominal terms over 22 months. This preprint analyzes how the inflationary episode was distributed across value chain stages using biweekly price data collected by the authors from producer associations, wholesale markets, and a panel of 18 retail outlets in four Serbian cities. Gross marketing margins at the slaughterhouse stage contracted by about 4 percentage points relative to the 2019–2020 baseline, while retail margins expanded by approximately 7 percentage points. Error correction model estimates confirm that the speed of upward price transmission from farm to retail accelerated further relative to the pre-2021 period, with half-lives falling below six weeks. The analysis is limited by the short post-inflation time span and uses a working paper specification pending peer review.

title: Benchmarking Serbian pork price monitoring against EU mandatory reporting frameworks: gaps and options
abstract: The EU Market Transparency Regulation requires member states to report weekly slaughterhouse and retail prices for specified pork cuts through a standardised EU price notification system. Serbia, as an EU candidate country, is under advisory pressure to align its agricultural market reporting with these standards. This paper benchmarks current Serbian price data collection practices—conducted by the Statistical Office and the Ministry of Agriculture through separate, partially overlapping systems—against EU requirements. The comparison reveals that Serbia lacks weekly wholesale price data for eight of the twelve pork cuts specified in the EU framework, and that farm-gate price collection relies on voluntary reporting by a shrinking panel of reference farms. The paper proposes a phased alignment roadmap, estimates administrative costs based on analogous implementation experiences in Romania and Bulgaria, and discusses how improved data would enable more precise price transmission analysis and strengthen early-warning mechanisms for market imbalances.

title: Drought risk perception and insurance uptake among Vojvodina farmers: a behavioural survey
abstract: Despite increasing drought frequency in the Pannonian Plain, agricultural insurance penetration in Serbia remains low. This study investigates drought risk perception, subjective probability assessments, and crop insurance uptake decisions among 196 farm operators in Vojvodina, surveyed in 2018. The analytical framework draws on prospect theory and applies a double-hurdle model to distinguish between the decision to purchase insurance at all and the level of coverage chosen. Variables capturing past drought experience, loss framing, trust in government compensation, and financial literacy are included. Results show that past compensation through ad hoc state support significantly reduces insurance demand, consistent with a moral hazard interpretation. Risk perception scores are generally high, but translate into insurance purchase in only 19% of the sample. The paper identifies financial literacy and simplified premium structures as the most actionable policy levers.

title: Return Migration to Rural Areas of Serbia After COVID-19: Scope, Motivations and Durability
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted a widely discussed but empirically underexamined wave of urban-to-rural residential moves in many European countries. This study investigates the extent and durability of such moves in Serbia through a telephone survey of 1 104 working-age adults who changed their registered residence from an urban to a rural municipality between March 2020 and December 2021, supplemented by administrative population register data. Results show that 61 percent of movers had prior family ties to the destination rural settlement. Only 29 percent described the move as permanent at the time of interview (conducted in late 2022), while 44 percent had already returned to an urban location. Logistic regression indicates that permanent rural return is significantly more likely among households with children under 10, remote-work employment, and ownership of a house in the rural destination. The findings suggest that pandemic-era return migration offers limited demographic relief for depopulating villages without complementary changes in employment and service access.

title: Exergy Destruction Mapping in a Recuperated ORC Cycle: Influence of Pinch Point Temperature Difference
abstract: An exergy-based analysis is applied to a recuperated subcritical ORC operating with R245fa, with source temperatures between 130 °C and 160 °C. The cycle model tracks exergy destruction in each component—evaporator, expander, condenser, recuperator, and pump—as a function of pinch point temperature difference (PPTD) varied from 3 K to 20 K. Results show that the evaporator accounts for 38–54% of total exergy destruction depending on PPTD, and that reducing PPTD below 6 K yields diminishing returns in second-law efficiency while substantially increasing required heat transfer area. A simple cost-exergy trade-off index is introduced to identify economically rational PPTD values for different heat source flow rates. The analysis uses a modified Grassmann diagram to visualise exergy flows. Data were generated using an iterative EES-based simulation and cross-checked with the MATLAB model used in earlier work. Practical guidelines for heat exchanger sizing are provided for system designers.

title: ORC System Integration with a Ceramic Tile Plant in Northern Serbia: A Case Study of Heat Source Characterisation and Cycle Sizing
abstract: This paper documents the field measurement campaign and thermodynamic sizing study conducted at a ceramic tile manufacturing facility near Zrenjanin, where tunnel kiln exhaust gases are available at approximately 155 °C with a flow rate of 14 kg/s. Temperature and composition measurements were taken at six points along the flue gas duct over a 72-hour continuous period to characterise variability. A subcritical ORC with isopentane as the working fluid was sized to recover approximately 420 kW of thermal power, yielding a projected net electrical output of 38 kWe at design point. Partial-load behaviour was modelled for the measured variability range, showing net power drops of up to 22% during weekend low-production periods. Capital cost was estimated using a scaling factor approach and compared against a simple payback calculation based on local electricity prices in 2014. The study concludes that a net payback period of 6.4 years is achievable under conservative assumptions.

title: Modelling of a Kalina Cycle for Geothermal and Industrial Waste Heat Sources in the 90–130 °C Range
abstract: The Kalina cycle, which uses an ammonia–water mixture as the working fluid, is compared with a baseline subcritical ORC (R245fa) for heat sources in the 90–130 °C temperature range. A steady-state thermodynamic model is developed in EES, incorporating the full ammonia–water mixture property routines. Three Kalina cycle configurations—KCS-11, KCS-34, and a modified KCS-34 with an internal heat exchanger—are evaluated across ammonia mass fractions from 0.60 to 0.90 and condensation temperatures of 30 °C and 40 °C. KCS-34 outperforms the baseline ORC in thermal efficiency by 1.8–3.2 percentage points at source temperatures above 115 °C, primarily due to better temperature glide matching in the boiler. At 95 °C source temperature the advantage is marginal and the greater mechanical complexity of the Kalina cycle is less justified. The paper provides decision criteria for technology selection as a function of source temperature, cooling water availability, and plant scale.

title: Sensitivity of ORC Net Power Output to Expander Isentropic Efficiency: A Monte Carlo Approach
abstract: Expander isentropic efficiency is the single most influential parameter in determining the net electrical output of small-scale ORC units, yet it is subject to significant uncertainty during design-phase modelling. This study applies Monte Carlo simulation with 10 000 samples to propagate uncertainty in expander isentropic efficiency (mean 0.72, standard deviation 0.06, based on a survey of published scroll and screw expander test data) through a thermodynamic ORC model. Three working fluids—R245fa, R1233zd(E), and isopentane—and two heat source temperatures (120 °C and 150 °C) are examined. Results show that the 90th-percentile net power output differs from the 10th-percentile value by 18–26% depending on conditions, indicating that deterministic point estimates routinely used in feasibility studies can misrepresent system potential. Tornado diagrams are provided for each configuration. Recommendations are made for how expander performance specifications should be communicated in tender documents for small ORC equipment.

title: Heat Integration of an ORC Unit into a Continuous Pasta Drying Line: Pinch Analysis and Simulation
abstract: The integration of an ORC unit into a food processing facility presents constraints not present in heavy industry: strict hygiene requirements, variable production schedules, and relatively modest heat source temperatures (85–110 °C from dryer exhaust air). This paper applies pinch analysis to a continuous industrial pasta dryer with a throughput of 2 t/h to identify heat recovery potential and to position an ORC evaporator within the heat exchanger network without violating minimum approach temperature constraints. A composite curve analysis identifies 310 kW of recoverable heat above a minimum approach temperature of 8 K. A subcritical ORC with R1233zd(E) is sized for this duty, producing 22 kWe net. The pinch analysis is performed in Aspen Energy Analyzer and the ORC cycle simulation in MATLAB/REFPROP. The paper discusses the trade-off between heat recovery fraction and dryer energy balance, showing that recovery above 68% of available heat degrades product drying quality.

title: Low-Grade Waste Heat Recovery in the Serbian Manufacturing Sector: A Survey of Source Temperatures, Flow Rates, and Recovery Potential
abstract: This chapter reviews the landscape of low-grade industrial waste heat in Serbian manufacturing, drawing on publicly available energy audit reports, official energy statistics, and data collected during site visits to fifteen facilities across Vojvodina and Central Serbia between 2017 and 2020. Industry sectors covered include food and beverage processing, ceramics, brick manufacturing, plastics, and light metals. Source temperatures are catalogued into three bins: below 100 °C, 100–150 °C, and 150–200 °C. The aggregate technical waste heat recovery potential in the surveyed facilities is estimated at 14–22 MW of thermal power in the ORC-relevant temperature range, translating to 1.2–2.0 MWe of electrical generation potential. Barriers to adoption—including small facility size, financing constraints, lack of technical expertise, and grid connection difficulties—are discussed. The chapter concludes with a prioritisation matrix for technology deployment based on source temperature, availability factor, and proximity to district heating networks.

title: Experimental Validation of a Scroll Expander Model on the Laboratory ORC Test Rig at Technical Faculty Zrenjanin
abstract: A small-scale ORC test rig at the Thermal Measurements Laboratory of Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin', powered by a 12 kW electric heater simulating a waste heat source, was used to characterise a 1.2 kWe oil-free scroll expander operating with R245fa. Steady-state measurements were made at evaporation pressures between 8 and 14 bar and condensation temperatures of 28–40 °C. Expander isentropic efficiency ranged from 0.61 at low pressure ratio to 0.74 at the design pressure ratio of 4.5, with a filling factor between 0.92 and 1.08. A semi-empirical scroll expander model with six fitting parameters was calibrated to the experimental data; the calibrated model reproduced measured shaft power with a root-mean-square error of 34 W over 47 operating points. The calibrated model was then embedded in the cycle-level MATLAB simulation, reducing net power prediction error from 11.4% to 3.8% compared with the default isentropic assumption. Measurement uncertainties for all key sensors are reported in accordance with GUM.

title: Techno-Economic Optimisation of ORC Systems for Waste Heat Recovery in Small and Medium Enterprises: Effect of Heat Source Intermittency
abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) represent the dominant industrial structure in Vojvodina, but their waste heat sources are typically intermittent, with operating schedules of 1–2 shifts per day and significant weekend downtime. This paper develops an optimisation framework that combines a steady-state thermodynamic ORC model with an annual simulation based on a synthetic production schedule representing a 240-day operating year with variable daily hours. Three ORC configurations—basic subcritical, recuperated subcritical, and transcritical with R1234yf—are compared across a range of SME-relevant heat source magnitudes (50–400 kW thermal) and temperatures (100–160 °C). Levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) is the primary objective function, computed with capital cost correlations from equipment vendor quotations and O&M estimates. The recuperated subcritical configuration with R245fa shows the lowest LCOE (0.068–0.091 EUR/kWh) across the 150–300 kW source range. The transcritical configuration becomes competitive only above 350 kW source power. A design chart is provided for ORC technology selection as a function of source power and intermittency factor.

title: Dynamic Simulation of ORC Start-Up and Shut-Down Transients Using a Moving Boundary Evaporator Model
abstract: Most published ORC models assume steady-state operation, but start-up and shut-down transients can account for a significant fraction of annual energy losses in SME applications with daily cycling. This preprint presents a dynamic ORC model in which the evaporator is represented using a three-zone moving boundary formulation, capturing the transitions between subcooled, two-phase, and superheated regions as heat source flow ramps up or down. The condenser and recuperator use a lumped-capacitance approach. The full model is implemented in Modelica and co-simulated with a PI controller for superheat regulation via the expander bypass valve. Simulated start-up from cold to rated conditions takes 12.4 minutes and dissipates approximately 18% of the energy that would have been generated if the system had operated at rated output throughout the same period. Sensitivity to controller tuning parameters and thermal mass of heat exchangers is analysed. Validation against the Zrenjanin test rig transient data is ongoing.

title: Influence of Residual Stress on the Natural Frequencies of Welded Steel Frame Members
abstract: Residual stresses induced by welding alter geometric stiffness and thereby affect natural frequencies of frame members. This study quantifies the relationship using a combined experimental and finite-element approach. Residual stress profiles in twelve S355 steel beam specimens were measured by the hole-drilling method at five cross-sections per specimen; specimens were then tested for natural frequencies using impact hammer excitation before and after stress-relief annealing at 600 °C for two hours. Frequency increases of 0.8–2.3% were observed after annealing, depending on weld sequence and heat input. A 3D FE model incorporating measured residual stress fields as initial conditions reproduced the pre-annealing frequencies with a mean error of 1.1%. Parametric sensitivity analysis showed that longitudinal compressive residual stress near the weld toe exerted the strongest influence on the first bending frequency. The results imply that residual stress state should be accounted for when establishing SHM baselines for newly fabricated or repaired steel structures.

title: Experimental validation of a tractor multibody model using a wheel force transducer on structured test courses
abstract: Validation of simulation models against experimental data from field tests is rarely straightforward because terrain inputs are difficult to reproduce exactly. This paper describes a validation methodology based on structured test courses of known geometry: a sinusoidal asphalt strip (wavelength 2 m, amplitude 40 mm) and a cleat array (height 60 mm, spacing 1.5 m) constructed at the faculty proving ground. A six-component wheel force transducer was fitted to the front axle of a 75 kW MFWD tractor, and runs at three speeds (4, 6, 8 km/h) were recorded. A full-vehicle multibody model built in MSC Adams included a four-link rear axle suspension, a lumped-parameter tyre model (Fiala formulation with measured tyre stiffness), and the TPH in the raised position. RMS agreement between measured and simulated vertical wheel forces was within 8% for the sinusoidal course and within 13% for the cleat course across all speeds. Discrepancies are attributed to tyre damping coefficient uncertainty.

title: Benchmarking hole-drilling, XRD, and contour method for residual stress measurement in 3 mm MIG-welded aluminium sheet
abstract: Three established residual stress measurement techniques were applied to identical MIG-welded AA5083 specimens to assess their agreement and practical suitability for thin-wall sections. Incremental hole-drilling (ASTM E837), laboratory XRD with CrKα radiation, and the contour method using wire EDM sectioning were performed on specimens from the same weld batch. Each technique was applied at a minimum of three repeat specimens. Longitudinal residual stress profiles across the weld showed consistent tensile peaks near the fusion line (75–110 MPa), but the contour method revealed a bimodal stress distribution not resolved by the surface-sensitive XRD measurements. Hole-drilling underestimated peak stresses by 10–18% relative to the contour method, consistent with the known plasticity effect near the weld. XRD and the contour method agreed within 15 MPa in the base material. Practical considerations including specimen preparation time, equipment cost, and spatial resolution are discussed for each method to guide selection in an industrial inspection context.

title: Constraint Propagation in Rule-Based Page Layout: A Framework for Variable-Data Catalogues
abstract: Variable-data catalogue production requires that layout rules remain consistent across thousands of page instances while accommodating record-level content variation. This paper describes a constraint propagation framework implemented on top of an extended document object model, in which geometric and typographic constraints are expressed as bidirectional relations rather than fixed measurements. A prototype system was tested on a synthetic dataset of 4 800 catalogue pages derived from a retail product database, with content strings ranging from 12 to 340 characters per field. Constraint resolution time averaged 38 milliseconds per page on commodity hardware. Visual evaluation by five professional graphic designers rated layout acceptability at 81 percent for fully automated output, rising to 94 percent after a single manual override pass. The paper also reports failure modes—chiefly orphaned headlines and overlapping images—and proposes priority hierarchies that reduce their frequency by 67 percent in the tested dataset.

title: Measuring Typographic Legibility Under Automated Point-Size Scaling in Bilingual Print Documents
abstract: Automated scaling of body text across Latin and Cyrillic script versions of the same document introduces legibility risks that fixed typographic rules do not adequately address. This study used a two-alternative forced-choice reading-speed task with 48 participants to measure legibility thresholds at seven scaled point sizes between 7 pt and 13 pt, for three typeface families and two line-length conditions. Results show that Cyrillic paragraphs tolerate approximately 0.6 pt less reduction than equivalent Latin text before legibility scores decline significantly, a difference attributable to mean character complexity rather than x-height ratio. A lookup table derived from these results was integrated into a template engine and validated on a sample of 120 bilingual product-information leaflets. Post-integration designer correction rates dropped from 22 percent to 9 percent compared with a baseline scaling algorithm.

title: Automated Adaptation of Print Layouts for Reflowable Digital Output: A Comparative Study of Three Conversion Strategies
abstract: Publishing workflows frequently require simultaneous delivery of a document in a fixed-page print format and a reflowable digital format such as EPUB. This study evaluates three conversion strategies—direct export, semantic re-tagging, and parametric re-composition—using a corpus of 96 technical data sheets drawn from industrial suppliers. Quality was assessed on four dimensions: text reflow correctness, image–caption association, table fidelity, and reading-order accuracy, scored by six trained evaluators on a five-point rubric. Parametric re-composition scored highest overall (mean 3.91) but required the most authoring overhead, averaging 4.2 additional hours per document template. Direct export produced frequent reading-order errors (34 percent of pages affected). Semantic re-tagging offered the best balance for documents with stable grid structures. Recommendations for workflow selection based on document complexity indices are provided.

title: Colour Token Systems in Parametric Brand Templates: Consistency Under Substrate and Illuminant Variation
abstract: Brand colour consistency across substrates and viewing conditions is a practical problem when parametric templates are deployed without colour-managed pipelines. This chapter reviews token-based colour specification systems and assesses their behaviour when rendered to coated offset, uncoated offset, and inkjet substrates under D50 and D65 illuminants. Spectrophotometric measurements were collected from 18 paper–ink combinations for five brand colour tokens representing primary, secondary, and neutral roles. Delta E 2000 deviations between target and measured values ranged from 1.2 to 6.8. The chapter discusses soft-proofing integration within template engines and proposes a colour-token schema that embeds ICC profile references alongside hexadecimal fallback values, enabling runtime selection of the most appropriate colour definition for the output condition.

title: Grid Parameterization for Responsive Print: Adapting Modular Grids Across Five Standard Paper Formats
abstract: Modular grid systems developed for a primary paper format—commonly A4 or A3—often require manual redesign when repurposed for other standard formats, creating redundant work in high-volume print design operations. This paper defines a parametric grid model in which column count, gutter width, and margin ratios are expressed as functions of the page aspect ratio and a single base-unit value. The model was implemented as a scripting extension for a commercial page-layout application and tested across A6, A5, A4, A3, and A2 formats using 30 representative document types including reports, brochures, and posters. Designer evaluation of auto-adapted grids compared to manually designed grids found no statistically significant preference difference (paired t-test, p = 0.14) for 22 of 30 document types. The eight remaining types, primarily posters with complex image hierarchies, showed measurable preference for manual grids.

title: Readability of Automatically Condensed Typefaces in Packaging Copy: An Eye-Tracking Study
abstract: Pharmaceutical and food packaging frequently requires long mandatory text to fit within small fixed areas, leading designers to apply horizontal condensing to body typefaces using software scaling rather than optically designed condensed cuts. This study used remote eye-tracking with 36 participants to measure fixation duration, regression rate, and comprehension scores for text condensed at 100 percent, 90 percent, 85 percent, and 75 percent of normal width, at 8 pt and 6 pt, across two typeface families. At 85 percent condensing, mean fixation duration increased by 12 percent relative to 100 percent at 8 pt, and comprehension scores remained within measurement error. At 75 percent condensing, regression rate doubled and comprehension fell by 18 percentage points at 6 pt. Results suggest a practical condensing limit of approximately 87 percent for packaging copy at 8 pt, with tighter tolerances at smaller sizes. Implications for automated text-fitting algorithms in packaging template systems are discussed.

title: Version Diffing for Document Templates: Detecting Structural and Typographic Changes Across Brand Refresh Cycles
abstract: When a brand undergoes a refresh, template maintainers need to identify what has changed between old and new template versions in a structured, auditable way. Existing version-control tools designed for source code do not handle the hierarchical, mixed-content structure of document templates adequately. This paper presents a diffing algorithm operating on a normalised template tree representation that distinguishes four change categories: token substitution, structural insertion or deletion, constraint modification, and style inheritance changes. The algorithm was applied to 14 real brand-refresh scenarios reconstructed from anonymised project archives at a Serbian packaging design agency, with template pairs containing between 120 and 3 400 nodes. Mean diff computation time was under 200 milliseconds per pair. The change report format produced was evaluated by template engineers who rated it as substantially more useful than line-based text diffs for eight of the fourteen cases.

title: Towards a Declarative Language for Multi-Channel Document Composition: Design Principles and a Reference Grammar
abstract: Existing document description languages conflate content, structure, and output-channel concerns, making it difficult to maintain a single source that can be rendered faithfully to print PDF, screen-optimised PDF, and HTML simultaneously. This preprint sketches the design of a declarative language—provisionally named ComposeLang—that separates these three concerns into distinct declaration blocks linked by resolution rules. The proposed grammar draws on stylesheet cascade models, constraint-satisfaction semantics, and a token vocabulary for typographic and spatial properties. A reference interpreter prototype was implemented in Python and tested on 22 document templates covering report, leaflet, and form genres. All 22 templates rendered correctly to PDF; HTML rendering passed automated accessibility checks in 19 of 22 cases. The paper describes open questions around bidirectional text, mathematical content, and figure captioning that remain unresolved in the current grammar version.

title: Secondary dendrite arm spacing in Al–4.5Cu alloy as a function of local solidification time: directional solidification experiments and empirical correlation
abstract: Directional solidification experiments were conducted on Al–4.5 wt% Cu rods in a Bridgman furnace at withdrawal rates of 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, and 10.0 mm/min under a fixed temperature gradient of 12 K/mm. Local solidification times were calculated from thermocouple data and ranged from 28 s to 560 s. Secondary dendrite arm spacing (SDAS) was measured on longitudinal polished sections using image-analysis software on a minimum of 80 dendrite cells per specimen. SDAS values ranged from 14 µm at the highest withdrawal rate to 89 µm at the lowest. A power-law correlation SDAS = 8.1 · t_f^0.36 was fitted, where t_f is local solidification time in seconds; the exponent is consistent with coarsening-dominated ripening theory. The ripening rate constant was 5.4 × 10⁻¹⁸ m³/s, in agreement with literature values for the Al–Cu binary system within 12%.

title: Permeability of dendritic mushy zones in Al–Si alloys: comparison of Kozeny–Carman, Heinrich–Poirier, and lattice-Boltzmann estimates
abstract: Three approaches to estimating mushy-zone permeability were compared for Al–7Si and Al–12Si alloys at solid fractions between 0.3 and 0.85. The Kozeny–Carman (KC) equation, the Heinrich–Poirier tortuosity-corrected model, and two-dimensional lattice-Boltzmann (LB) simulations on dendrite cross-sections reconstructed from optical micrographs were evaluated. Micrographs were binarised at seven solid fractions prepared by partial remelting of DC-cast samples quenched into water. LB simulations were performed on 400 × 400 pixel domains using the BGK collision operator at Re < 0.01. At solid fraction 0.6, KC overestimated permeability by 47% relative to LB, while the Heinrich–Poirier model agreed within 18%. The discrepancy with KC was attributed to the tortuous, non-circular character of interdendritic channels, which the simpler model does not capture. Practical implications for macrosegregation modelling are discussed, with recommended permeability constants for each alloy.

title: Coupling a microsegregation model with a two-dimensional macrosegregation solver for Al–Mg–Si ternary alloy billets
abstract: A modular numerical framework was developed in which a back-diffusion microsegregation model (Clyne–Kurz scheme) was coupled to a two-dimensional finite-volume macrosegregation solver for DC casting of an Al–0.7Mg–0.4Si (wt%) ternary alloy billet of 150 mm diameter. The coupling was achieved through a lookup table of solid fraction versus temperature computed offline for a range of cooling rates from 0.1 to 50 K/s. The macroscopic solver handled interdendritic Darcy flow, thermosolutal buoyancy, and solidification shrinkage. Steady-state simulations required approximately 4.2 hours on a single-core desktop at a mesh resolution of 2 mm. Predicted Mg distribution matched electron probe microanalysis data on 10 cross-sections to within ±1.8% relative error. Si predictions were less accurate near the periphery, with errors up to ±4.1%, attributed to uncertain back-diffusion coefficients for Si in the α-Al matrix.

title: Influence of secondary cooling water flow rate on surface quality and subsurface microstructure in DC-cast aluminium extrusion billets
abstract: The effect of secondary cooling water flow rate on the surface quality and near-surface microstructure of 152 mm diameter AA6060 extrusion billets was studied at three flow rates: 80, 120, and 160 L/min per unit circumference. Surface roughness was measured by profilometry on 200 mm axial sections; Ra values decreased from 14.2 µm at 80 L/min to 8.9 µm at 160 L/min. The depth of the as-cast segregation band, visible in acid-etched cross-sections, ranged from 3.2 to 6.8 mm and was inversely correlated with flow rate (Pearson r = −0.94). Secondary dendrite arm spacing in the subsurface zone (0–5 mm) decreased from 38 µm to 22 µm as flow rate increased, consistent with higher local cooling rates estimated from an inverse heat-transfer calculation. Hardness profiles showed a 12% increase in Vickers hardness in the refined subsurface layer at the highest flow rate.

title: Validation of a volume-averaged two-phase solidification model against radiographic measurements of macrosegregation in Al–4Cu laboratory ingots
abstract: A volume-averaged two-phase solidification model, implemented in an open-source finite-volume framework, was validated against X-ray fluorescence (XRF) mappings of copper distribution in laboratory-scale Al–4 wt% Cu ingots of 80 × 80 × 200 mm cast under controlled conditions. Three pouring temperatures (680, 700, and 720 °C) and two mould materials (sand and cast iron) were tested. XRF maps were acquired on longitudinal mid-plane slices at a step size of 2 mm, yielding concentration fields with a spatial resolution of approximately 3 mm. The volume-averaged model used a Scheil-based solid fraction function and a permeability field derived from the SDAS measurements reported in the same specimens. Predicted positive centreline segregation ranged from +6.1% to +9.8% relative to nominal, compared with measured values of +5.7% to +10.4%. The root-mean-square error of the predicted Cu field across all specimens was 0.18 wt%.

title: Heat transfer coefficients at the billet–mould interface during DC casting: extraction from inverse analysis of thermocouple data
abstract: Interfacial heat transfer coefficients (IHTC) at the billet–mould interface were extracted from measured temperature histories using a sequential function specification inverse method for DC casting of AA3003 alloy at casting speeds of 55 and 80 mm/min. Thermocouples were embedded in the copper mould wall at three axial positions within the primary cooling zone. The inverse solver minimised the sum of squared residuals between measured and predicted temperatures, with the IHTC discretised into 0.5 s time intervals. Extracted IHTC profiles peaked at 8200 W/(m²·K) within the first 0.8 s of contact and decayed to a plateau of approximately 1100 W/(m²·K) as an air gap formed. The sensitivity of macrosegregation predictions to IHTC uncertainty was assessed by a ±25% perturbation study; centreline Mn segregation changed by less than 0.9% relative to the base case, while mushy-zone depth varied by 6 mm.

title: Porosity formation mechanisms in the mushy zone of aluminium alloy billets: a comparative study using X-ray micro-computed tomography
abstract: X-ray micro-computed tomography (µCT) at a voxel size of 4.3 µm was used to characterise porosity in samples extracted from three radial positions (centre, mid-radius, subsurface) in DC-cast AA2024 and AA6082 billets. For each alloy and position, five cylindrical specimens of 8 mm diameter were scanned. Total pore volume fraction, mean pore equivalent diameter, and pore shape factor were extracted from segmented three-dimensional reconstructions. In AA2024, centreline pore volume fraction was 0.61% with a mean equivalent diameter of 38 µm, compared to 0.18% and 22 µm in the subsurface zone. In AA6082 the corresponding values were substantially lower (0.21% and 16 µm at the centreline). A shrinkage-dominated mechanism was inferred for the centreline pores based on their elongated morphology (mean shape factor 0.41), while near-surface pores were more spherical (shape factor 0.72), consistent with gas-bubble entrapment. Correlations between SDAS measured in the same specimens and mean pore diameter yielded an R² of 0.87.

title: Data-driven surrogate model for SDAS prediction in DC-cast aluminium billets using gradient-boosted regression trees
abstract: A gradient-boosted regression tree (GBRT) surrogate was trained on a dataset of 1840 SDAS measurements compiled from DC-casting experiments conducted in the authors' laboratory between 2011 and 2022, covering alloys AA2024, AA3003, AA6060, AA6082, and AA7050 across billet diameters of 120 to 280 mm. Input features included casting speed, cooling water flow rate, billet diameter, alloy group (encoded as integer), and radial position normalised to billet radius. The dataset was split 75/25 into training and test sets with stratification by alloy. The GBRT model (200 estimators, maximum depth 5) achieved a test-set RMSE of 4.1 µm and R² of 0.93. Feature importance analysis identified local solidification time (derived from casting speed and diameter) as the dominant predictor, accounting for 51% of variance, followed by radial position at 23%. The surrogate is intended to support rapid parameter screening in industrial process design without requiring a full solidification simulation.

title: Quantitative SEM image analysis for pore size distribution mapping across the casting direction in flat-sheet membranes
abstract: A semi-automated image analysis workflow was developed in ImageJ to extract pore size and spatial distribution data from SEM micrographs of flat-sheet polysulfone and polyethersulfone membranes. Cross-sections prepared by cryo-fracture were imaged at five evenly spaced positions along the 200 mm casting direction of laboratory-scale hand-cast films, and at three magnifications (×500, ×2000, ×10 000). The method detected statistically significant gradients in mean pore diameter along the casting direction of up to 18% when ambient humidity varied by more than 15% RH during casting. Repeatability studies involving three operators showed inter-operator coefficients of variation below 6% for mean pore area after threshold calibration. The workflow was validated against mercury intrusion porosimetry on the same samples, showing agreement within 9% for median pore diameter. The paper provides the analysis script and threshold-selection protocol as supplementary material.

title: Comparative WVTR performance of wax, polyethylene, and starch-blend coatings on virgin kraft liner at three temperature levels
abstract: Water vapour transmission rates of three coating systems — paraffin wax, low-density polyethylene (LDPE) dispersion, and a commercially supplied starch-blend dispersion — were measured on virgin kraft liner (120 g/m²) at 10 °C, 23 °C, and 38 °C, each at 90 % relative humidity, following a modified ISO 2528 cup method. Coating add-on weights were standardised at 8 g/m² (±0.3 g/m²) across all systems. LDPE dispersion delivered the lowest WVTR at all temperatures (0.8–2.1 g/m²·24h), while the starch-blend performed comparably to wax at 10 °C but deteriorated sharply above 23 °C, reaching 18.4 g/m²·24h at 38 °C. Activation energies derived from Arrhenius plots were 31.2, 14.7, and 22.8 kJ/mol for starch-blend, LDPE, and wax, respectively. These values suggest that bio-based starch coatings carry a significant thermal sensitivity penalty under warm distribution chain conditions.

title: Reflectance Characteristics of Common Thermoplastics in the 1000–2200 nm Range Under Conveyor Illumination Conditions
abstract: This study characterises the diffuse reflectance spectra of six common thermoplastics — HDPE, LDPE, PP, PET, PVC, and PS — measured on a laboratory conveyor rig under halogen line illumination at belt speeds of 0.5–2.0 m/s. A line-scan InGaAs camera with a spectral resolution of 10 nm was used to acquire 1200 spectra per material class under controlled and variable soiling conditions. Spectral preprocessing included standard normal variate correction and Savitzky–Golay smoothing. Principal component analysis showed that the first three components captured 94.7% of interclass variance for clean samples, dropping to 81.3% for samples with 3% surface contamination by mass. A linear discriminant classifier trained on clean data achieved 97.1% accuracy on clean test samples and 88.4% on contaminated ones. The results establish baseline spectral signatures and identify the 1650–1750 nm window as most discriminating for polyolefin separation, providing a practical reference dataset for subsequent classifier development.

title: Effect of Belt Speed on Spectral Data Quality in Line-Scan NIR Imaging of Mixed Plastic Flakes
abstract: Increasing throughput on automated sorting lines requires higher belt speeds, which reduce per-pixel integration time and degrade signal-to-noise ratio in line-scan NIR systems. This work quantifies the relationship between belt speed (0.3–3.5 m/s), integration time (0.1–2.0 ms), and classification accuracy for a binary PET/PP discrimination task using a 256-element InGaAs array. At 2.5 m/s with 0.4 ms integration, SNR fell by 38% relative to the 0.5 m/s reference, and classification accuracy dropped from 96.8% to 89.1% using a fixed LDA model. Adaptive gain scheduling and dark-current correction recovered accuracy to 94.3%. Experiments were conducted with 2 400 flake samples across three size classes (20–50 mm, 50–80 mm, 80–120 mm). The paper provides empirical guidelines for integration-time selection as a function of belt velocity and flake geometry, directly applicable to industrial line design.

title: Partial Least Squares Regression for Additive Content Estimation in Recycled Polyolefin Streams
abstract: Recycled polyolefin batches often contain unknown quantities of flame retardants, plasticisers, and colorants that alter NIR absorption profiles and reduce sorting purity. This study applies partial least squares regression (PLSR) to estimate the concentration of two common additives — decabromodiphenyl ether (0–3% w/w) and dioctyl phthalate (0–5% w/w) — from NIR spectra of HDPE pellet samples. A calibration set of 320 samples with laboratory-verified additive concentrations was used to build PLSR models with 8 and 6 latent variables, respectively. Cross-validated RMSECV values were 0.18% for the brominated additive and 0.31% for the plasticiser. Prediction on an independent set of 80 samples gave RMSEP of 0.22% and 0.38%. The models were robust to pellet colour variation after scatter correction but degraded when carbon-black-pigmented samples exceeded 5% of the batch. Practical implications for quality-control integration in recycling facilities are discussed.

title: GPU-Accelerated Spectral Angle Mapping for Real-Time Polymer Classification at 2 m/s Belt Speed
abstract: Spectral angle mapping (SAM) is computationally straightforward but rarely benchmarked on embedded GPU hardware for industrial conveyor timing constraints. This paper implements SAM on an NVIDIA Jetson TX1 platform connected to a 320-pixel line-scan NIR camera operating at 1 000 lines/s. The processing pipeline — dark subtraction, flat-field correction, spectral angle computation against a 9-class reference library, and binary ejector trigger generation — was profiled for latency on batches of 1, 4, and 16 simultaneous spectral lines. End-to-end latency from line capture to trigger output was 1.8 ms for single-line mode and 4.1 ms for 16-line batch mode, both within the 8 ms actuation window at 2 m/s. Classification accuracy on 4 500 test flakes across six polymer types was 93.7%. Power consumption was 9.2 W, compatible with 24 V cabinet installation. The implementation is described with enough detail to enable replication.

title: Discriminating Black Plastics by Short-Wave NIR Spectroscopy: Carbon Black Interference and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Carbon-black-pigmented plastics present a persistent challenge in NIR-based sorting because carbon black strongly absorbs across the entire NIR range, masking polymer-specific overtone bands. This study evaluates three mitigation strategies: (1) extension of the measurement window into the 2200–2500 nm long-wave NIR region where carbon black absorption is relatively lower, (2) photoacoustic excitation at 1064 nm with NIR emission detection, and (3) time-resolved reflectance using a pulsed laser to isolate subsurface signal. Experiments used 180 black-pigmented samples spanning PP, ABS, PA6, and PC with carbon black concentrations of 0.5–4.0% w/w. Long-wave NIR extension improved classification accuracy from 61.3% to 79.4% for the four-class task; photoacoustic detection reached 86.1% but required a 120 ms dwell time, incompatible with high-speed lines. Time-resolved reflectance achieved 82.7% at 12 ms dwell. Practical trade-offs between accuracy and throughput are quantified, and a hybrid sensor layout is proposed.

title: Spatial Calibration of Line-Scan NIR Systems for Variable-Thickness Polymer Flakes on Moving Belts
abstract: Line-scan NIR cameras acquire spectra along a single spatial axis perpendicular to belt motion. When flakes vary in thickness (1–12 mm), the focal plane offset shifts the effective pixel pitch and introduces geometric distortion in reconstructed hyperspectral images, degrading spatial segmentation prior to per-pixel classification. This paper proposes a structured-light height measurement module mounted upstream of the NIR camera to estimate per-flake thickness and apply a perspective correction to the spectral image in real time. A dataset of 600 flakes with ground-truth thickness measured by contact gauge was used to evaluate calibration accuracy; mean thickness error after correction was 0.4 mm. Integration with a SAM classifier improved segmentation IoU from 0.74 to 0.89 for flakes thicker than 6 mm. The additional processing latency introduced by the correction step was 0.9 ms on the Jetson Xavier platform.

title: Online Drift Compensation in NIR Polymer Classifiers Using Unlabelled Production Data
abstract: Spectral classifiers deployed on industrial sorting lines experience performance drift over weeks to months due to lamp ageing, lens fouling, and seasonal temperature variation. Periodic manual recalibration is costly and requires line downtime. This paper proposes an unsupervised drift compensation procedure based on kernel mean matching between batches of unlabelled in-production spectra and the original training distribution, updating the classifier's normalisation parameters without requiring new labelled samples. Experiments were conducted on a six-month operational log from a pilot sorting line processing post-consumer packaging, comprising 1.4 million spectra. Without compensation, macro-averaged F1 declined from 0.953 to 0.891 over 24 weeks. With monthly drift compensation triggered automatically when a distribution shift detector exceeded a threshold, F1 was maintained above 0.941 throughout. Computational overhead of the compensation step was less than 2 minutes on a standard industrial PC.

title: Identification of PVC in Mixed Post-Consumer Rigids Using a Two-Stage NIR-Raman Decision Fusion Approach
abstract: PVC contamination in polyolefin recycling streams causes hydrogen chloride emissions during reprocessing and must be removed to below 50 ppm. NIR sorting alone misclassifies PVC as PE at rates up to 4.2% due to spectral overlap near 1730 nm. This paper evaluates a two-stage approach in which a fast NIR pre-screen flags suspect objects for secondary laser Raman interrogation at 785 nm. The NIR stage operated at 2 m/s on a full-width belt; Raman interrogation was triggered only for the 8–12% of items flagged as ambiguous, with a 40 ms dwell. On a test set of 3 200 PVC and 4 800 polyolefin items, the two-stage system achieved PVC recall of 99.2% and precision of 97.8%, compared to 94.3% recall and 96.1% precision for NIR alone. Throughput reduction from Raman dwell was 6.3% at the tested PVC concentration. Cost implications of the additional sensor are discussed.

title: Estimating Recycled Content Fraction in Polymer Blends from NIR Spectra Using Conformal Prediction Intervals
abstract: Quantifying the recycled content fraction in a polymer blend is commercially relevant for compliance with EU recycled content targets. This preprint presents a regression approach combining PLSR baseline estimates with conformal prediction to produce statistically valid prediction intervals rather than point estimates. A dataset of 480 HDPE/rHDPE blend samples with recycled content varying from 0 to 100% in 5% increments was prepared gravimetrically. The conformal prediction wrapper, calibrated on 96 samples, produced 90% prediction intervals with empirical coverage of 91.2% on the 120-sample test set. Interval width averaged 8.4 percentage points at 90% confidence. The method is model-agnostic and adds negligible computational cost. Preliminary results suggest that NIR alone can certify recycled content to ±5% only for blends below 30% or above 70% recycled material; intermediate fractions require supplementary measurement. Full data and code are available on the university repository.

title: Multi-Line NIR Sensing for Orientation-Independent Classification of Elongated Plastic Profiles on High-Speed Conveyors
abstract: Elongated polymer profiles such as window frame sections and pipe offcuts arrive on sorting conveyors at arbitrary orientations, causing single-line NIR measurements to sample only a narrow cross-section of the object and increasing misclassification for materials with spatially heterogeneous surface coatings. This study evaluates a sensor array of five parallel line-scan NIR cameras spaced 40 mm apart, with their outputs fused by a majority-vote scheme operating on per-object spectra aggregated across all five lines. Experiments used 1 100 elongated profiles across PVC, PP, and fibre-reinforced PA6, arriving at 1.8 m/s with randomised in-plane orientations. The five-line fusion system achieved 96.3% three-class accuracy, compared to 87.1% for the best single-line configuration. False-positive PVC detection rate fell from 3.8% to 0.7%, which is relevant given PVC removal targets. Hardware synchronisation, spatial co-registration of the five cameras, and the added cost relative to accuracy gain are analysed.

title: Effect of Rotor Guard Geometry on Thrust Loss in Lateral Wind: Experiments at Wind Speeds Up to 16 m/s
abstract: Propeller guards are increasingly fitted to agricultural and inspection UAVs for safety compliance, but their aerodynamic cost under wind is poorly quantified. This paper presents thrust and torque measurements for four guard geometries—open-ring, half-duct, full-duct, and lattice cage—tested on a single-rotor test stand in a closed-return wind tunnel at wind speeds of 0–16 m/s and wind angles of 0°–90° in 15° steps. Rotor diameter was 0.33 m and rotational speed was held constant at 5200 RPM. Thrust loss at 90° sideslip and 12 m/s reached 9% for the open-ring guard versus 21% for the full-duct geometry. The full-duct design also generated a pitching moment 3.4 times larger than the open-ring at 8 m/s sideslip. A simple analytical model based on actuator disk theory with an empirical blockage correction reproduced the measured thrust losses with a mean absolute error of 1.8 percentage points. Recommendations for guard selection in wind-exposed agricultural applications are summarised.
venue: Aerospace Science and Technology

title: Interpretable Health State Classification for Induction Motor Bearings Using Shapelet-Based Time-Series Features
abstract: Black-box classifiers for bearing health state estimation are often difficult to validate for deployment in safety-relevant applications. This paper develops an interpretable classification approach based on time-series shapelets—short subsequences whose presence discriminates between health states—extracted from raw vibration waveforms recorded from induction motor bearings under four health states: healthy, early outer-race damage, advanced outer-race damage, and inner-race damage. Shapelet discovery was performed on a training set of 2,400 labelled 0.5-second waveforms. The five most discriminative shapelets achieved 91.3% five-fold cross-validation accuracy using a nearest-shapelet distance classifier. Each shapelet was linked back to physical signal morphology (impacts, modulation patterns) and confirmed by domain-expert inspection. Comparisons with a support vector machine operating on 24 handcrafted spectral features showed equivalent accuracy (91.8%) but the shapelet approach required no manual feature engineering. Shapelet visualisation is shown to facilitate explanation of individual classifications to maintenance technicians.
venue: Journal of Intelligent Maintenance Systems

title: Residual stress distribution in injection-moulded PA66/GF30 tensile specimens: measurement and simulation
abstract: Injection-moulded dog-bone specimens of 30 wt% glass-fibre-reinforced polyamide 66 were produced at three mould temperatures (40, 60, and 80 °C) and three injection speeds. Residual stresses through the wall thickness were measured by layer-removal and hole-drilling methods and compared with predictions from a coupled mould-flow and structural simulation performed in Autodesk Moldflow linked to ANSYS. Fibre orientation tensors from the flow analysis were transferred directly to the structural model using a mapping script. Measured residual stresses in the skin layer reached up to 18 MPa compressive, while the core showed tensile values up to 9 MPa; simulation reproduced these trends within 12% on average. Mould temperature had the strongest single effect on residual stress magnitude. The study provides a validated simulation workflow that can be used to guide mould design for stress-sensitive structural applications.

title: Creep behaviour of unreinforced polypropylene under constant stress at elevated temperature: experimental characterisation and model comparison
abstract: Uniaxial creep tests on injection-moulded polypropylene bars were performed at temperatures of 23, 50, and 70 °C and at stress levels corresponding to 10, 20, and 30% of the respective yield stress. Tests ran for up to 1000 hours and strain was recorded with a clip-on extensometer. Three rheological models—the power-law creep model, the Burgers four-element model, and a modified Findley model—were fitted to the experimental data. The Findley model gave the best agreement across all temperature–stress combinations, with root-mean-square errors below 4% for strains up to 3%. At 70 °C and 30% yield stress, specimen deflection accelerated after approximately 600 hours, indicating onset of tertiary creep. Parameter maps as a function of temperature and stress are provided and can be used directly in finite element creep analyses.

title: Effect of weld-line position on fatigue life of injection-moulded ABS components under cyclic bending
abstract: Weld lines in injection-moulded acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS) parts are known stress concentrators, but their influence under fatigue loading at different thermal conditions is less documented. Rectangular beam specimens were moulded with a controlled weld line at three positions along the beam length (centre, quarter-span, and near-gate). Four-point bending fatigue tests were carried out at 23 and 60 °C at three stress amplitudes. Specimens with weld lines at the centre showed fatigue life reductions of 35–52% compared to weld-line-free reference specimens, depending on temperature and stress amplitude. Scanning electron microscopy of fracture surfaces confirmed crack initiation at weld-line boundaries in all cases. A simple knockdown factor approach, calibrated on the experimental dataset, is proposed for preliminary design assessments when weld-line location cannot be avoided.
