title: Coupled thermal–structural simulation of a thermoplastic bracket under engine-compartment thermal cycling
abstract: A polyamide 6 bracket representative of under-bonnet automotive applications was subjected to repeated thermal cycles between −30 and +120 °C in a programmable thermal chamber while simultaneously carrying a sustained mechanical preload of 150 N. Surface strains were measured at five locations using bonded foil gauges. A coupled finite element model incorporated temperature-dependent elastic modulus and coefficient of thermal expansion derived from dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) over the relevant temperature range. Simulation predicted maximum principal strains within 8% of measured values across all gauge locations and cycle stages. Residual strain accumulation after 200 cycles was 0.18% in experiment versus 0.21% in simulation. The validated model was then used to explore the effect of wall-thickness reduction on peak stress, showing that a 0.5 mm reduction at the mounting boss increased peak stress by 22%.

title: Optimisation of gate location in a multi-cavity mould for a thin-walled POM gear blank using mould-flow simulation
abstract: Polyoxymethylene (POM) gear blanks produced in an eight-cavity tool exhibited warpage variation of up to 0.31 mm between cavities, attributed to unbalanced filling. A parametric mould-flow study in Autodesk Moldflow evaluated 27 gate-location combinations defined on a structured grid across the part face. Weld-line position, fibre-free zone extent, filling time imbalance, and predicted warpage were used as response variables. A gate position offset of 1.8 mm from the part centre toward the runner entry reduced maximum warpage to 0.09 mm and eliminated an unfavourably positioned weld line near the tooth root region. The study also compared fan-gate and pin-gate configurations, finding that the pin gate at the optimised position produced 15% less warpage than the fan gate. Physical trials on a revised tool confirmed the simulation-derived warpage reduction.

title: Short-term stress relaxation of polycarbonate under combined bending and temperature gradient: test rig design and first results
abstract: A custom four-point bending fixture with integrated resistive heating on one face was designed to impose a controlled through-thickness temperature gradient of up to 40 °C while measuring the relaxing bending moment in polycarbonate beams. The fixture accommodates standard 80 × 10 × 4 mm specimens and uses two independent thermocouples embedded at the heated and cooled surfaces. Stress relaxation from an initial outer-fibre stress of 20 MPa was monitored over 24 hours at gradient magnitudes of 0, 20, and 40 °C, with the cold face held at 23 °C. The presence of a 40 °C gradient accelerated stress relaxation so that the retained stress after 24 hours was 11.2 MPa compared to 16.8 MPa in the isothermal case. The paper describes the test rig instrumentation and calibration procedure in detail to facilitate reproduction at other laboratories.

title: Simulation-based assessment of thermally induced warpage in a co-injection moulded polypropylene/polyethylene component
abstract: Co-injection moulding allows a cost-reduced core material to be encapsulated by a functional skin, but the mismatch in shrinkage and thermal expansion between core and skin polymers introduces additional warpage risk. This study examined a flat lid component moulded with a polypropylene skin and a recycled polyethylene core at three skin-to-core volume ratios (30/70, 50/50, and 70/30). Mould-flow simulations predicted warpage at the four corners and along the central rib; experimental warpage was measured on a coordinate measuring machine. The 50/50 ratio produced the lowest warpage (0.14 mm corner deflection), while the 70/30 ratio yielded 0.27 mm, close to the 0.30 mm tolerance limit. Material property mismatch, specifically the difference in crystallisation-induced shrinkage, was identified as the dominant warpage driver through a sensitivity analysis in which individual material parameters were varied by ±10%.

title: Thermomechanical fatigue life prediction of polybutylene terephthalate clips using a strain-energy density criterion
abstract: Push-on clip fasteners moulded from polybutylene terephthalate (PBT) experience simultaneous thermal cycling and repeated snap-fit assembly forces in electronic housing applications. Twelve specimens were tested under in-phase thermomechanical fatigue (TMF) with temperature cycling between 25 and 110 °C and a mechanical strain range of 1.2%. Under isothermal fatigue at 25 °C, fatigue life was approximately 18 000 cycles; under TMF, life dropped to 4 200 cycles. A strain-energy density (SED) criterion was evaluated against these data and against a published dataset for polyphenylene sulfide. When temperature-dependent modulus and hysteresis loop areas were accounted for, the SED criterion predicted TMF life within a scatter band of ×2 for 90% of the data points. The study identifies the phase angle between thermal and mechanical loading as a secondary but measurable factor: a 90° phase lag increased life by approximately 25% relative to in-phase loading.

title: Effect of recycling on the structural integrity of injection-moulded PA6 components: a comparison of first-pass and three-times-recycled material
abstract: The mechanical and thermomechanical properties of injection-moulded polyamide 6 were compared for virgin pellets and pellets reprocessed through the injection moulding cycle three times. Specimens from each material grade were tested in tension, fatigue, and thermal cycling. Molecular weight, measured by gel permeation chromatography, decreased by 18% after three reprocessing cycles, accompanied by a 9% reduction in tensile strength and a 14% reduction in elongation at break. Fatigue life at a stress amplitude of 25 MPa fell from a median of 62 000 cycles to 38 000 cycles. Thermal cycling between −20 and +90 °C revealed greater warpage accumulation in recycled specimens after 100 cycles (0.22 mm vs. 0.13 mm at mid-span). Mould-flow simulation showed that viscosity changes in recycled material shifted the filling pattern and weld-line positions, which partly explains the scattered fatigue results.

title: Thermomechanical analysis of polymer components in engineering design: principles and worked examples
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured introduction to thermomechanical analysis of injection-moulded polymer components, aimed at practising mechanical designers. It covers the hierarchy of material characterisation tests required before finite element analysis, the transfer of fibre orientation data from mould-flow to structural solvers, the selection of appropriate constitutive models for creep and fatigue, and the assessment of failure criteria under combined thermal and mechanical loading. Four worked examples are included: a PA66/GF30 automotive bracket, a POM gear blank, a polycarbonate optical housing, and a PBT snap-fit clip. Each example identifies common modelling errors and their consequences on predicted life or warpage. An appendix tabulates temperature-dependent properties for eight engineering thermoplastics compiled from the authors' own test database and open literature, enabling readers to begin analyses without additional characterisation when data precision requirements are modest.

title: Identification of dominant failure modes in glass-fibre-reinforced polyamide housings for electric motors under intermittent duty: field data analysis and accelerated testing
abstract: Electric motor housings moulded from PA6/GF35 from twelve units returned from field service after premature cracking were examined by fractography and X-ray microtomography. Crack origins were located at wall junctions where mould-flow analysis indicated converging weld lines combined with residual tensile stress above 12 MPa. An accelerated test programme reproduced the field thermal profile (22 cycles per day, peak temperature 105 °C, minimum −10 °C) on 30 instrumented specimens. Median time to first visible crack was 1 840 cycles in the accelerated test versus an estimated 2 100 field cycles, giving an acceleration factor of 1.14. Parametric finite element studies showed that increasing the fillet radius at the identified critical junction from 0.5 to 1.5 mm reduced peak stress by 31% and was predicted to increase crack-initiation life by a factor of 2.3. A revised mould design incorporating this change is currently under evaluation.

title: Input-Referred Noise Analysis in Folded-Cascode OTAs Operating at 0.9 V Supply
abstract: This paper presents a systematic noise analysis of folded-cascode operational transconductance amplifiers designed for a 0.9 V supply in a 180 nm CMOS process. Analytical expressions for input-referred thermal and flicker noise are derived from small-signal models and validated against Cadence Spectre simulations. Four OTA variants with different tail current source implementations are compared. Simulated input-referred noise density ranges from 18 to 34 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz across the variants. The dominant flicker noise contribution is traced to the differential input pair when standard NMOS devices are used; substituting PMOS input transistors reduces the 1/f corner frequency from approximately 4.2 kHz to 1.1 kHz at the cost of a 12% reduction in unity-gain bandwidth. Bias current sweep results indicate a 1/√ID dependence consistent with theory. The findings establish sizing guidelines for input-referred noise below 25 nV/√Hz while maintaining a unity-gain bandwidth above 800 kHz at 100 µA total current. The analysis is applicable to ECG and local field potential readout chains where supply voltages are constrained by battery-powered operation.

title: Gain-Bandwidth Product Degradation in Sub-Threshold Biased OTAs: Measurement Versus Simulation
abstract: Sub-threshold biasing of CMOS OTAs is widely used to reduce power consumption in wearable biosignal interfaces, but published simulation results often diverge from silicon measurements at this operating point. This work characterises six fabricated OTA test structures in a 180 nm CMOS process biased from strong inversion down to deep sub-threshold at a fixed 0.8 V supply. Unity-gain bandwidth, DC gain, phase margin, and input-referred noise are measured on a probe station for 24 individual dies. At a tail current of 200 nA, the measured unity-gain bandwidth is 47 kHz compared to a simulated value of 68 kHz, a discrepancy attributed to parasitic gate overlap capacitance underestimation in the PDK. A correction factor determined empirically is incorporated into a revised simulation flow. Across all bias points, the measured gain-bandwidth product degrades by 31% relative to strong-inversion predictions. Results suggest that pre-silicon noise and bandwidth estimation for battery-powered front-ends should include a safety margin of at least 25% on bandwidth specifications when relying on standard foundry models.

title: Noise Figure Budget Allocation in a Three-Stage ECG Readout Chain
abstract: An electrocardiographic readout chain typically comprises a preamplifier, a programmable-gain stage, and a buffer driving an ADC. This paper develops a systematic noise figure budget allocation method for a three-stage chain where each stage operates from a 0.9 V supply. Friis noise cascading formulae are adapted to account for the finite output impedance of OTA-based stages, which introduces correlation terms absent in the classical RF case. Closed-form expressions are verified against Spectre periodic-steady-state noise simulations. Two budget scenarios are evaluated: one that concentrates gain in the first stage (40 dB) and one that distributes it evenly across stages (13 dB per stage). The concentrated gain scenario achieves an overall noise figure of 2.8 dB at 100 Hz but reduces the chain's linear input range by 14 dB. The distributed scenario gives a noise figure of 5.1 dB with a 9 dB improvement in input dynamic range. Trade-off curves for noise figure versus input dynamic range are provided as design charts. The method is validated on a printed circuit board prototype using discrete components mimicking OTA behaviour.

title: Effect of Body Biasing on Flicker Noise in 0.8 V PMOS OTAs for Neural Recording
abstract: Flicker noise in PMOS transistors can be modulated via bulk-to-source potential, which in a triple-well 180 nm CMOS process can be independently controlled. This paper investigates whether forward body biasing (FBB) applied to the input pair of a PMOS-input OTA reduces input-referred flicker noise at sub-1 V supply. Measurements on 18 fabricated samples show that applying 200 mV FBB reduces the 1/f noise corner frequency from 980 Hz to 610 Hz and decreases the input-referred noise power spectral density at 100 Hz by approximately 4.3 dB. The mechanism is attributed to a reduction in effective oxide trap density caused by the modified inversion layer charge distribution. However, FBB increases sub-threshold leakage and raises the minimum supply voltage for adequate phase margin from 0.75 V to 0.82 V. A design guideline table identifies the FBB voltage range (0 to 250 mV) that provides noise benefit without compromising stability. The approach is relevant to chronic neural recording implants where supply voltage is derived from inductive power links.

title: Comparative Study of Current-Mirror and Recycling Folded-Cascode OTA Topologies at 0.8 V for EEG Preamplification
abstract: The recycling folded-cascode (RFC) OTA achieves higher transconductance efficiency than the standard folded-cascode by reusing bias currents, but its noise properties at sub-1 V supply are less well characterised in the literature. This paper compares current-mirror OTA (CMOTA) and RFC OTA topologies both designed for 0.8 V operation in a 180 nm CMOS process, targeting the EEG bandwidth of 0.5 Hz to 100 Hz. Seven performance metrics are compared: DC gain, unity-gain bandwidth, phase margin, slew rate, input-referred noise at 10 Hz, power consumption, and common-mode rejection ratio. The RFC OTA achieves a 31% higher transconductance-to-current ratio and a unity-gain bandwidth of 1.1 MHz at 80 µA versus 760 kHz for the CMOTA at the same current. However, input-referred noise at 10 Hz is 6.2 nV/√Hz for the RFC versus 4.8 nV/√Hz for the CMOTA, because the recycling path introduces additional noise from mirroring transistors. CMRR values are 68 dB and 61 dB respectively. Layout parasitics extracted from a 180 nm process show that the RFC topology is more sensitive to drain capacitance mismatch. Results suggest that for EEG front-ends where flicker noise floor is critical, the CMOTA remains preferable despite lower transconductance efficiency.

title: Low-Voltage OTA Design Methodology for Biomedical Front-Ends
abstract: This book chapter presents a structured design methodology for OTAs operating below 1 V supply, aimed at biomedical acquisition applications. The chapter covers four topics: supply headroom partitioning under weak inversion, noise-driven transistor sizing starting from an input-referred noise specification, gain-bandwidth trade-off using a modified Elmore delay model, and stability analysis for capacitive feedback loads typical of switched-capacitor filters. Each topic is accompanied by a worked design example in a 180 nm CMOS process. A spreadsheet-based sizing tool implementing the methodology is described and made available as supplementary material. The chapter also includes a comparison table of 24 published sub-1 V OTA designs drawn from the literature between 2005 and 2018, benchmarked using the figure-of-merit FOM = (GBW × CL) / (ID × VDD). The compilation shows a clear trend toward PMOS input pairs and current-recycling topologies in post-2014 designs. Common pitfalls in noise simulation setup, particularly incorrect handling of the periodic operating point in Cadence Spectre PSS/Pnoise, are discussed with corrective procedures.

title: Mismatch-Induced Common-Mode Rejection Degradation in 0.8 V Differential OTA Pairs: Monte Carlo Study
abstract: Process-induced mismatch in differential pairs degrades common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR), which is critical for biopotential recording where common-mode interference from the power grid can exceed the differential signal by 80 dB. This study uses Monte Carlo analysis in Cadence Spectre with foundry-supplied mismatch models for a 180 nm process to characterise CMRR distributions across 5000 simulation runs for five OTA topologies at 0.8 V supply. Median CMRR values range from 61 dB to 74 dB depending on topology; the standard deviation across Monte Carlo runs ranges from 3.2 dB to 8.9 dB. Increasing input pair area from minimum (2 µm × 0.2 µm) to 20 µm × 1 µm reduces CMRR standard deviation by 61% but increases gate capacitance and reduces bandwidth by 18%. Correlation analysis identifies the threshold voltage mismatch parameter ΔVT as the dominant factor, responsible for 73% of CMRR variance in the best-case topology. A sizing nomogram is derived that allows designers to select input pair dimensions for a target CMRR yield at a specified confidence level. Silicon measurements on 12 dies confirm Monte Carlo predictions within 2.1 dB.

title: Supply Voltage Scaling from 1.8 V to 0.7 V in a Continuous-Time Sigma-Delta Modulator Front-End: OTA Noise and Stability Trade-Offs
abstract: Continuous-time sigma-delta modulators (CT-ΣΔM) for biopotential acquisition rely on OTA integrators whose noise and stability properties change substantially when supply voltage is reduced below 1 V. This paper examines a second-order CT-ΣΔM designed in 180 nm CMOS as supply voltage is stepped from 1.8 V to 0.7 V in 50 mV increments, with bias currents scaled proportionally to maintain the same power consumption at each step. Measurements on five fabricated chips show that signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) at a 1 kHz, 1 mVpp input degrades from 68.4 dB at 1.8 V to 54.1 dB at 0.8 V, then drops sharply to 41 dB at 0.75 V due to phase margin falling below 38°. The dominant noise contribution shifts from thermal noise of the first integrator OTA at higher supplies to quantisation noise at 0.8 V, confirmed by noise breakdown simulations. A feedforward coefficient re-optimisation at 0.8 V recovers 4.2 dB of SNDR by redistributing integrator gains without changing the bias current budget. Power consumption across the scaling range is 180 µW to 210 µW. The work provides empirical evidence for a practical lower supply limit near 0.78 V for this class of modulator in 180 nm CMOS.

title: Comparison of Metaheuristic Solvers for Large-Scale Residential Demand Response Scheduling
abstract: Coordinating thousands of flexible loads simultaneously renders exact mixed-integer programming intractable within the time windows required for operational scheduling. This paper benchmarks four metaheuristic approaches—genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimisation, differential evolution, and simulated annealing—on a demand response scheduling problem involving 1 000 heterogeneous residential loads including dishwashers, washing machines, and plug-in hybrid vehicles. Test instances are generated from smart meter recordings of 230 households monitored over six months in 2015–2016 in the Novi Sad area. Metaheuristics are evaluated on solution quality relative to a relaxed LP bound, convergence speed, and robustness across 30 independent runs. Differential evolution achieves the best mean gap of 2.1% from the LP bound within a 60-second wall clock limit. Genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimisation settle near 3.5% gap. Simulated annealing shows high variance and is considered unsuitable for operational use. Parameter tuning guidelines for distribution-network-scale instances are provided.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of Soil Thermal Parameters on Ampacity Estimates for 110 kV Underground Cables Using Monte Carlo Simulation
abstract: Uncertainty in soil thermal resistivity is a principal source of error in IEC 60287-based ampacity calculations for underground cables. This study applies Monte Carlo simulation with 10 000 samples to propagate uncertainty from four soil parameters—dry thermal resistivity, moisture diffusivity, critical moisture content, and seasonal surface temperature amplitude—through a steady-state cable ampacity model for a 110 kV XLPE single-core cable in a direct-buried flat configuration at 1.0 m depth. Soil parameter distributions were derived from 63 in-situ thermal needle probe measurements taken along a 2.1 km route in Vojvodina. The 5th–95th percentile band of predicted ampacity spanned 68 A around the deterministic estimate of 521 A, representing a ±13% uncertainty range. Soil moisture diffusivity was identified as the most influential parameter, accounting for 41% of output variance via Sobol sensitivity indices. Results suggest that reducing uncertainty in moisture diffusivity through targeted field measurements near cable route sections with historically elevated loads could narrow the ampacity confidence interval by approximately 30%.

title: Sentence-Level Alignment in Multilingual Legal Texts Using Lexical Overlap and Cognate Features
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of sentence alignment in parallel legal corpora involving Hungarian, Serbian, and English. We constructed a manually annotated corpus of 4,200 sentence pairs extracted from EU directive translations and national legislative texts. Alignment was performed using a combination of lexical overlap scores, cognate detection based on edit distance, and length-ratio heuristics. We compared four alignment strategies—Gale-Church length-based, Hunalign, a simple TF-IDF cosine method, and a rule-augmented hybrid—on three language pairs. The hybrid approach achieved F1 scores of 0.87, 0.83, and 0.79 for EN–SR, EN–HU, and HU–SR pairs respectively, outperforming all baselines. Error analysis revealed that cross-linguistic terminological divergence and inconsistent paragraph segmentation in source documents were the dominant failure modes. The annotated corpus and alignment scripts are released under a CC-BY licence.
venue: Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Computational Linguistics (CEW-CL)

title: A Comparative Study of Bilingual Lexicon Induction Methods for Serbian–Hungarian Word Pairs in Technical Domains
abstract: Bilingual lexicon induction (BLI) without parallel corpora is particularly challenging for morphologically rich, closely situated language pairs. This study evaluates four BLI approaches—cross-lingual word embedding projection, iterative Procrustes alignment, VecMap, and a graph-based method—on Serbian–Hungarian word pairs sampled from three technical domains: civil engineering, agriculture, and information technology. Evaluation dictionaries containing 2,100 pairs per domain were assembled from terminological databases and validated by domain experts. Results show that iterative Procrustes alignment achieves the highest precision@1 (42.3%) on the IT domain, while graph-based methods perform better on agriculture (38.7% precision@1), where morphological regularity is lower. All methods degrade substantially on out-of-vocabulary compound terms. We release the three domain dictionaries and pre-trained fastText vectors fine-tuned on a 600 M token Serbian–Hungarian corpus.

title: Cross-Lingual Named-Entity Linking Between Serbian and English News Corpora Using Wikipedia Anchors
abstract: Named-entity linking (NEL) across languages is complicated by transliteration variation, partial name translations, and entity ambiguity. We describe a system that links named entities in Serbian news articles to English Wikipedia entries using a combination of anchor text statistics, Wikidata cross-reference mappings, and string similarity features. We evaluated on a manually annotated dataset of 3,800 entity mentions drawn from four Serbian news portals, covering persons, organisations, and locations. The proposed system achieved a linking accuracy of 74.2% on persons and 68.9% on organisations, compared to 61.4% and 55.7% for a transliteration-only baseline. We analyse error categories and find that local public figures with sparse Wikipedia coverage account for roughly 40% of failures. The annotated mention dataset is made publicly available.

title: Reconciling Duplicate Patient Records Across Hospital Systems: A Cross-Lingual Entity Matching Approach
abstract: Electronic health record systems in multilingual regions often store patient and diagnostic data in different languages, leading to duplicate and conflicting records. This chapter presents a framework for cross-lingual entity matching of patient records in Serbian and Hungarian administrative data, using a combination of phonetic normalisation, transliteration, and fuzzy attribute matching. A prototype was developed and tested on a synthetic dataset of 10,000 record pairs generated from anonymised templates provided by a regional hospital administration. We define five match categories ranging from definite match to definite non-match and report precision of 0.91 and recall of 0.86 for the definite match category. The chapter discusses practical barriers including inconsistent date formats, name order conventions, and missing-field patterns common in legacy systems.

title: Evaluating Multilingual Sentence Encoders on a Diverse Cross-Lingual Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark for South Slavic Languages
abstract: Publicly available semantic textual similarity (STS) benchmarks rarely include South Slavic languages, making it difficult to evaluate multilingual encoder models in this region. We construct STS-SlaVoSe, a benchmark of 5,400 sentence pairs in Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian, and Bosnian, covering six domains: news, legal texts, social media, scientific abstracts, product descriptions, and conversational transcripts. Each pair was annotated by three annotators on a 0–5 scale; inter-annotator Pearson correlation averaged 0.83. We evaluate eight publicly available multilingual sentence encoders including mBERT, XLM-R, LaBSE, and four smaller distilled variants. LaBSE achieves the highest average Pearson correlation (0.79) across all language–domain combinations, though performance varies markedly by domain: legal text pairs yield the lowest scores (0.61) across all models. We release the full benchmark under CC-BY-SA.

title: Fine-Tuning Multilingual Transformers for Cross-Lingual Document Matching in Public Procurement
abstract: Public procurement databases in the Western Balkans are maintained in multiple national languages, making cross-border tender matching difficult without manual translation. We investigate whether fine-tuned multilingual transformer models can identify semantically equivalent tender notices across Serbian, Croatian, and Macedonian without explicit translation. Using a dataset of 12,400 tender notice pairs (6,200 positive, 6,200 negative) derived from the Open Tenders Balkans portal, we fine-tune XLM-R and mBERT with a siamese network objective and compare against a TF-IDF baseline and a machine-translation-then-monolingual-SBERT pipeline. The fine-tuned XLM-R siamese model achieves an average precision of 0.88 on the held-out test set, compared to 0.73 for TF-IDF and 0.85 for the translation pipeline, while running approximately 3.4× faster at inference time. We discuss domain-specific vocabulary challenges and release fine-tuning code.

title: Structured Table Reconciliation Across Multilingual Financial Reports Using Column-Header Alignment and Cell-Level Semantic Similarity
abstract: Annual financial reports published by companies operating across multiple Central and Eastern European jurisdictions often contain the same underlying data structured in tables with headers in different languages and with variable column ordering. This paper presents a pipeline for aligning and reconciling such tables automatically. Column headers are aligned using cross-lingual sentence embeddings (LaBSE and XLM-R) combined with a type-inference module that classifies cells as numeric, date, currency, or free text. Cell-level reconciliation uses a combination of normalised numeric comparison and semantic similarity for textual cells. We evaluate on a corpus of 840 paired tables from 210 annual reports covering Serbian, Hungarian, and Romanian. Column alignment achieves an F1 of 0.92; full-row reconciliation with conflict detection reaches a precision of 0.87. The pipeline reduces manual review time by an estimated 65% in a controlled user study with eight financial analysts.

title: A Modular Framework for Cross-Lingual Reconciliation of Structured Administrative Documents: Architecture and Case Studies
abstract: Administrative bodies in multilingual regions routinely exchange structured documents—forms, certificates, registrations—whose fields are defined by different national schema vocabularies. This paper describes DocAlign-ML, a modular software framework that combines schema-level field mapping, cross-lingual semantic similarity scoring, and value normalisation to reconcile such documents automatically. The framework consists of four interchangeable modules: a field-label encoder based on fine-tuned XLM-R, a type-aware value normaliser, a conflict resolver, and an explainability layer that generates natural-language justifications for each mapping decision. We present three case studies: business registration documents in Serbian and Romanian, land cadastre records in Serbian and Hungarian, and birth certificate data in Serbian and German. Average field-mapping accuracy across the three cases is 0.89. The framework is implemented in Python and the core components are released as open-source libraries.

title: Contrastive Fine-Tuning of Sentence Encoders on Small Domain-Specific Parallel Corpora: A Study on Legal and Medical Subdomains
abstract: Large multilingual sentence encoders trained on general web data often perform poorly on specialised domains where vocabulary and sentence structure differ substantially from general text. We investigate the effectiveness of contrastive fine-tuning—using in-domain positive pairs and hard negatives mined from the same corpus—when the available domain-specific parallel corpus is small (2,000–8,000 sentence pairs). Experiments cover two subdomains (legal and medical) and three language pairs (EN–SR, EN–HU, EN–RO). We compare full fine-tuning, adapter-based fine-tuning, and prompt-based fine-tuning on top of LaBSE and XLM-R-large. Adapter-based fine-tuning with hard-negative mining matches or exceeds full fine-tuning on all six subdomain–language-pair combinations while using 7% of the trainable parameters. Performance gains are most pronounced on the medical subdomain (average Pearson correlation improvement of +0.11 over the base model). We provide a systematic analysis of hard-negative quality and its impact on final performance.

title: Evaluating Hallucination and Semantic Drift in Cross-Lingual Summaries Generated by Instruction-Tuned LLMs for Structured Documents
abstract: Instruction-tuned large language models are increasingly used to generate cross-lingual summaries of structured documents such as regulatory filings and procurement notices. However, it remains unclear how reliably these models preserve factual content and named-entity references when summarising across language pairs. We design an evaluation protocol using 1,200 structured document pairs in four language pairs (EN–SR, EN–HU, SR–RO, HU–RO) and three document types: regulatory filings, procurement notices, and scientific project abstracts. Three instruction-tuned models are evaluated: a 7B and a 13B open-weight model, and a proprietary API model. We measure hallucination rate (entity-level and numerical), semantic similarity between source and summary (using cross-lingual STS), and named-entity recall. The 13B open-weight model hallucinates named entities in 18.4% of generated summaries; the proprietary model reduces this to 9.1% but still introduces numeric errors in 6.7% of cases. We release the evaluation protocol, annotation guidelines, and test set.

title: Stochastic Fluid Models for Burst-Tolerant Auto-Scaling in Container Orchestration Platforms
abstract: Container orchestration systems such as those based on declarative scheduling can scale replica counts in response to observed CPU utilisation, but default horizontal scaling policies do not account for the statistical structure of workload bursts. This paper adapts the stochastic fluid queue framework to model container-level resource consumption when arrivals follow a Markov-modulated process with two burst modes. The fluid level represents the accumulated processing backlog. Buffer overflow probabilities and expected drain times are derived in closed form using spectral decomposition of the generator matrix. The model is parameterised from a 72-hour trace of HTTP request arrivals to a microservices application running on an in-house three-node cluster. Predicted overflow probabilities match observed SLA breach rates with a mean absolute error of 0.008 across 15 experimental conditions. The paper proposes a scaling trigger rule based on the fluid model's overflow threshold and shows it reduces SLA violations by 31 percent compared to a CPU-only threshold rule in a controlled replay experiment.

title: Stochastic Optimisation of Checkpointing Intervals for Fault-Tolerant Scientific Workflows on Heterogeneous Clouds
abstract: Long-running scientific workflow tasks benefit from periodic checkpointing to limit recomputation after node failures, but frequent checkpointing imposes I/O overhead. This paper models the workflow execution as a renewal reward process in which the checkpoint interval T is the decision variable, task failure rate λ follows an inhomogeneous Poisson process estimated from node-failure logs, and I/O overhead is a linear function of checkpoint size. The expected waste ratio—proportion of CPU time spent on recomputation and checkpointing—is derived analytically and minimised with respect to T for a given λ(t) profile. A closed-form approximately-optimal interval is obtained under the assumption that λ(t) is piecewise constant. The formula is validated on a simulation of a 128-node heterogeneous cluster over 500 simulated workflow executions. Optimal intervals range from 12 to 47 minutes depending on failure rate and checkpoint size, reducing waste by 28–36 percent compared to a fixed 30-minute interval baseline.
venue: Journal of Grid Computing and Distributed Systems

title: Benchmarking Rolling-Horizon Decomposition Variants for Multi-Modal Urban Freight Scheduling
abstract: Urban freight consolidation centres aim to coordinate deliveries across multiple vehicle types—vans, cargo bikes, and small electric vehicles—within a shared urban zone. This paper adapts rolling-horizon decomposition to a multi-modal dynamic pickup-and-delivery problem and benchmarks four variants differing in window length (60 vs. 120 minutes), overlap policy (fixed vs. adaptive), and sub-problem solver (MILP vs. ALNS). Benchmark instances were constructed from synthetic demand profiles calibrated to freight movement data from two Central European cities. The adaptive-overlap variant with ALNS sub-problem solver achieved the best average performance across 300 instances: 5.3% above the static-day lower bound at a median solve time of 28 seconds per rolling step. Fixed-window MILP was competitive only on low-density instances. The paper provides a parameter-selection guide and open-source instance generator as supplementary materials.

title: Wiener chaos solutions for a linear elasticity system with spatially random Young's modulus
abstract: We study a system of linear elasticity equations in three spatial dimensions in which Young's modulus is represented as a finite Wiener chaos expansion of order 2, supported by experimental data from tensile tests on polymer composite samples. The random field is characterised by a mean of 3.1 GPa and a coefficient of variation of 18 percent, consistent with measurements reported in the mechanical engineering literature for glass-fibre-reinforced polymers. The Wiener chaos propagator equations form a coupled triangular system of deterministic elliptic boundary value problems, which we solve using a preconditioned conjugate gradient method on a tetrahedral mesh with 84,000 degrees of freedom. We track the evolution of the displacement variance and the von Mises stress distribution across the stochastic domain. The propagator-based approach is compared against a 5,000-sample Monte Carlo reference: the mean displacement field agrees to within 0.4 percent in the L2 norm, while the standard deviation of the von Mises stress is recovered to within 2.1 percent. The method scales linearly in the number of chaos coefficients for orders up to 3.

title: Interval Methods for Rigorous Sensitivity Analysis of ODE Solutions with Respect to Initial Conditions
abstract: Sensitivity equations—the variational equations for the derivative of an ODE solution with respect to initial conditions—can be solved simultaneously with the state equations to provide bounds on solution sensitivity. This paper formulates and analyses an interval approach to simultaneous integration of state and first-order sensitivity equations for general non-stiff systems. The extended system doubles the dimension; the paper characterises how wrapping-effect growth scales with dimension and proposes a block-coordinate transformation to mitigate it. Six test cases are used, including the Lorenz system at moderate parameter values. Rigorous sensitivity bounds are compared with finite-difference approximations, and the cases in which interval sensitivity bounds are informative versus overly conservative are characterised. The study also provides a worked example of using sensitivity enclosures to certify local exponential stability of an equilibrium.

title: Pressure oscillation modes in a four-way proportional spool valve: a two-dimensional CFD study
abstract: This paper presents a two-dimensional Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) investigation of pressure oscillation modes observed in a four-way proportional spool valve at partial overlap. The valve geometry was discretised with approximately 85 000 structured cells. The k–ω SST turbulence model was used together with a rigid spool assumption to isolate hydrodynamic instability from structural compliance. Simulations were run at inlet pressures of 80, 120, and 160 bar with spool displacements of ±0.2 mm around the null position. Dominant oscillation frequencies between 220 and 410 Hz were identified depending on operating pressure, consistent with frequencies recorded on the laboratory test rig. The study establishes baseline flow structures responsible for axial pressure imbalance and provides a frequency map usable for subsequent structural coupling analyses. Mean flow coefficients obtained numerically agreed with experimental measurements to within 4.8%.

title: Effect of metering-edge chamfer angle on steady-state flow force in directional control valves
abstract: Steady-state flow forces acting on the spool of a directional control valve were examined for five chamfer angles (15°, 25°, 35°, 45°, and 60°) using three-dimensional RANS simulations with the realizable k–ε model. A parametric CAD-to-mesh pipeline was implemented to generate comparable meshes (each approximately 1.1 million cells) across all geometries. Simulations covered flow rates from 5 to 40 L/min at a fixed pressure drop of 100 bar. At 35° chamfer angle, axial flow force was reduced by 31% compared with the sharp-edged baseline without a significant penalty in flow coefficient. Pressure recovery downstream of the metering edge showed the strongest sensitivity to chamfer angle among all quantities examined. Results are compared with published analytical force models and show deviations up to 18% for angles below 25°, attributable to three-dimensional recirculation zones not captured by one-dimensional models.

title: One-way fluid–structure coupling of a proportional valve spool under transient pressure pulses
abstract: A one-way coupled fluid–structure interaction model was developed to predict spool deflection and stress distribution in a proportional valve subjected to transient pressure pulses typical of mobile hydraulic circuits. The fluid domain was solved in ANSYS Fluent with a dynamic mesh, and pressure loads were transferred at each time step to an ANSYS Mechanical FEM model of the spool. A total of 24 pressure pulse scenarios were examined, varying pulse rise time (2–20 ms) and amplitude (50–200 bar). Maximum von Mises stress at the spool land transition radius reached 312 MPa under the most severe pulse, remaining below the yield strength of the 42CrMo4 steel used. Computed spool tip displacement reached 8 µm peak-to-peak at 150 bar, influencing the effective metering overlap by approximately 6%. The model was validated against strain-gauge measurements on an instrumented test spool with agreement within 9%.

title: Cavitation inception and bubble collapse in hydraulic spool valves: a mixture model approach
abstract: The Schnerr–Sauer mixture cavitation model was applied within a 3D transient RANS framework to investigate cavitation inception at the metering edge of a hydraulic spool valve for flow rates between 10 and 60 L/min and downstream pressures of 2–15 bar. Vapour volume fractions exceeding 0.4 were observed in a recirculation zone approximately 1.2 mm downstream of the land edge under the most severe conditions. Time-averaged wall pressure maps revealed localised pressure recovery peaks correlated with bubble collapse events; peak collapse pressures reached 320 bar in some cells. Erosion risk was quantified using the Melanneau–Soyama erosion index applied to collapse-rate distributions. Predicted high-risk zones corresponded spatially to wear marks on used spools retrieved from field service. Grid sensitivity was assessed over three mesh refinement levels with the finest mesh containing 2.3 million polyhedral cells.

title: Spool mass and spring stiffness as tuning parameters for suppression of valve-induced hydraulic noise
abstract: This study examined how spool mass and centring-spring stiffness affect flow-induced noise generation in a proportional directional valve. A coupled one-dimensional valve dynamics model was integrated with a lumped acoustic model of a 3-metre test circuit. Fourteen combinations of spool mass (35–95 g) and spring stiffness (18–72 N/mm) were simulated. Sound pressure level was estimated at a monitoring point 0.5 m from the valve using the Lighthill acoustic analogy applied to CFD-derived source terms exported from OpenFOAM. Configurations with higher mass and lower stiffness consistently produced 4–7 dB(A) lower noise at flow rates above 25 L/min. However, dynamic positioning accuracy degraded by up to 15% in the heavier configurations when subjected to 10 Hz command signals. A Pareto front relating noise level to positioning bandwidth is presented and discussed in the context of practical valve design constraints.

title: Influence of hydraulic fluid viscosity grade on spool oscillation amplitude: measurements and RANS predictions
abstract: The relationship between hydraulic fluid viscosity and spool self-oscillation amplitude was investigated experimentally and numerically for three ISO VG grades (32, 46, and 68) at fluid temperatures of 30 °C and 60 °C. Oscillation amplitude was measured using an inductive displacement sensor with a resolution of 0.5 µm at spool displacements of 0.3, 0.6, and 1.0 mm from null. A total of 18 operating points were covered. RANS simulations using temperature-dependent viscosity interpolated from measured viscosity–temperature curves reproduced oscillation amplitude trends correctly in 15 of 18 cases. The largest discrepancy (22%) occurred at the lowest viscosity and highest temperature combination, attributed to transition-range turbulence behaviour inadequately captured by the steady-state turbulence model. The experimental dataset is provided as supplementary material and is intended as a validation benchmark for future FSI studies.

title: Two-way FSI simulation of a hydraulic relief valve disc under pulsating inlet pressure using a co-simulation approach
abstract: A fully coupled two-way fluid–structure interaction model of a poppet-type hydraulic relief valve was implemented through co-simulation between OpenFOAM (fluid) and CalculiX (structure), exchanging boundary conditions at each sub-iteration via the preCICE coupling library. The valve disc was modelled as a linear elastic body (steel, E = 210 GPa) with a contact model at the seat. Pulsating inlet pressure waveforms with frequencies of 25, 50, and 100 Hz and amplitudes of ±20 bar superimposed on a 150-bar mean were applied. Disc lift, seat contact force, and crack-opening pressure were recorded. At 50 Hz pulsation, disc lift oscillation amplitude increased by 37% compared with the steady-state operating point. Seat contact fatigue risk was estimated using a Hertz contact model; at 100 Hz the predicted contact stress exceeded the Hertz fatigue limit of the specified seat material within 1.2 × 10⁷ cycles. Co-simulation wall-clock time was approximately three times that of the one-way approach for comparable accuracy.

title: Data-driven surrogate modelling of cavitation erosion risk in spool valves using Latin hypercube sampling and Gaussian process regression
abstract: A surrogate model for rapid estimation of cavitation erosion risk in hydraulic spool valves was built using Gaussian process regression trained on a database of 120 CFD simulations generated by Latin hypercube sampling over five geometric and operating parameters: metering-edge radius (0–0.2 mm), chamfer angle (15°–60°), inlet pressure (80–200 bar), flow rate (5–50 L/min), and fluid temperature (30–80 °C). The erosion risk metric was defined as the 95th percentile of cell-level bubble collapse energy density. Leave-one-out cross-validation yielded a mean absolute percentage error of 8.4% across the design space, with the highest errors near the boundary of cavitation inception. The surrogate was integrated into a simple web-based tool that returns erosion risk estimates in under one second, intended for use during preliminary valve design. Sensitivity analysis showed that inlet pressure and metering-edge radius together account for 71% of output variance.

title: Analytical model for predicting peak acceleration of a product–cushion system with nonlinear pad stiffness
abstract: Classical cushioning design methods assume a bilinear or fully linear pad response, which can lead to over-conservative or unconservative designs when highly nonlinear foam behaviour is present. This paper presents a closed-form analytical approach based on a piecewise polynomial approximation of the foam stress–strain curve, integrated with energy conservation principles to predict peak transmitted acceleration. The model requires only the static cushion curve and product weight as inputs and produces a direct estimate without requiring finite element computation. Predictions were compared against 180 experimental drop tests covering five EPS densities, four drop heights (450–1200 mm), and three product weights (0.5–3.0 kg). Root-mean-square error of peak acceleration predictions was 6.4 G, compared with 9.1 G for the standard bilinear approximation used in ASTM D1596-based design charts. The method is suitable for rapid pre-screening of cushion configurations before detailed simulation.

title: Crack-growth rate estimation in sandwich face sheets using AE inter-event time statistics
abstract: Face-sheet cracking under quasi-static indentation was studied in 200 × 200 mm glass-fibre/epoxy–foam sandwich specimens loaded at 0.5 mm/min with an 8 mm flat-ended punch. AE events were recorded at 2 MHz sampling rate and crack length was measured simultaneously using a surface-mounted ink-contrast replica film refreshed every 0.1 mm of punch displacement. The inter-event time series was modelled as an inhomogeneous Poisson process whose intensity function was fitted by maximum likelihood. Estimated crack-growth rate correlated with directly measured crack-front advance with a mean absolute error of 0.06 mm per load step across 12 specimens. The intensity function showed a power-law dependence on applied force with exponent 2.3 ± 0.2, consistent with linear elastic fracture mechanics predictions. The method offers a route to in-situ crack-growth monitoring without visual access to the damage site.

title: Solvent-free synthesis of phosphatidylcholine catalysed by immobilised Candida rugosa lipase: reaction kinetics and yield optimisation
abstract: Phosphatidylcholine (PC) was synthesised without organic solvent using a commercial Candida rugosa lipase immobilised on mesoporous silica. The transesterification of glycerophosphocholine with oleic and palmitic acids was studied in a 250 mL stirred reactor at temperatures between 40 °C and 65 °C. Substrate molar ratios (1:1 to 1:5, GPC:fatty acid) and enzyme loading (5–40 mg/mL) were varied in a full factorial design. Maximum PC yield of 71.3 ± 2.8% was achieved at 55 °C with a 1:3 molar ratio and 20 mg/mL enzyme after 8 h. The reaction followed Michaelis–Menten kinetics with apparent Km of 18.4 mM and Vmax of 3.2 μmol/min/mg. Product identity was confirmed by 31P-NMR and ESI-MS. Enzyme reusability was acceptable for five consecutive cycles with less than 15% activity loss. These conditions provided a scalable baseline for later bioreactor studies.

title: Scale-up of enzymatic phosphatidylcholine synthesis to 5 L stirred-tank bioreactor: mass transfer and operational stability
abstract: Synthesis of phosphatidylcholine using immobilised Candida rugosa lipase was transferred from 250 mL flask scale to a 5 L stirred-tank bioreactor equipped with a Rushton turbine and baffles. The effects of agitation speed (50–300 rpm) and aeration on enzyme activity and emulsification of the biphasic substrate mixture were characterised. At 150 rpm, the volumetric mass transfer coefficient kLa was 4.8 h⁻¹ and PC yield reached 68.1 ± 3.1% over 10 h, comparable to small-scale results. Foaming was controlled by a mechanical foam breaker without antifoam agents, which was required to preserve lipid purity. Three consecutive 5 L batches showed yield coefficients of 67–69% and enzyme half-life of 14 days under operational conditions. Product quality from bioreactor batches was equivalent to flask-scale material as assessed by 31P-NMR and HPLC-ELSD purity (96.4 ± 0.9%). These data confirm straightforward scalability of the solvent-free route.

title: Preparation and physicochemical characterisation of liposomes from enzymatically synthesised phosphatidylcholine
abstract: Liposomes were prepared from phosphatidylcholine produced by immobilised lipase-catalysed synthesis and purified by preparative chromatography. The thin-film hydration method followed by sequential extrusion through 400, 200, and 100 nm polycarbonate membranes yielded unilamellar vesicles with mean diameter 118 ± 7 nm, polydispersity index 0.09, and zeta potential −14.2 ± 1.1 mV as measured by dynamic light scattering. Vesicle morphology was confirmed by cryo-TEM at the Institute of Oncology Vojvodina electron microscopy facility. Encapsulation efficiency of a model hydrophilic drug (sodium fluorescein) was 23.4 ± 2.1%, determined by size-exclusion chromatography and fluorimetry. The phospholipid composition of liposome membranes matched the input material within ±2 mol% by HPLC-ELSD. Storage stability at 4 °C over 90 days showed less than 8% change in mean diameter and no increase in PDI, indicating adequate colloidal stability for pharmaceutical applications.

title: Liposomal encapsulation of a water-soluble antifungal compound: influence of phospholipid acyl chain composition on encapsulation efficiency and in vitro release
abstract: Liposomes composed of phosphatidylcholine variants differing in acyl chain length and saturation (dipalmitoyl-PC, palmitoyl-oleoyl-PC, and dioleoyl-PC) were loaded with the model antifungal compound flucytosine-analogue FT-7 (a fictional compound used as a test molecule in this study) at drug-to-lipid molar ratios of 1:5, 1:10, and 1:20. Encapsulation efficiency ranged from 18.7% (DOPC, 1:5) to 34.2% (DPPC, 1:20) as determined by ultrafiltration and HPLC-UV. In vitro release in phosphate-buffered saline at 37 °C followed Korsmeyer–Peppas kinetics; DPPC liposomes showed slower release (t50 = 14.2 h) compared with DOPC (t50 = 5.8 h), consistent with a gel-phase membrane at physiological temperature. Membrane fluidity measured by DPH fluorescence anisotropy correlated inversely with release rate (r² = 0.91). Results demonstrate that acyl chain composition is a primary design variable for controlling the release profile of hydrophilic drugs from liposomal systems and guide selection criteria for formulation development.

title: Steady-state performance mapping of a laboratory-scale alkaline electrolyser under variable load conditions
abstract: This paper presents experimental characterisation of a 2 kW alkaline electrolyser cell stack operated under load profiles representative of wind-coupled intermittent duty. Voltage–current curves were recorded at cell temperatures between 60 °C and 80 °C and electrolyte concentrations of 25 wt% and 30 wt% KOH. Faradaic efficiency was measured by gas displacement over 48-hour test sequences covering load ramps from 20% to 100% of rated current density. Recorded data were used to fit a semi-empirical Butler–Volmer-based model with seven parameters. The fitted model reproduced measured hydrogen output to within 3.8% root-mean-square error across all tested conditions. Ohmic losses contributed 41% of total overpotential at full load; at 25% partial load, activation losses dominated. Results establish baseline parameters for subsequent degradation studies and provide a validated simulation block for system-level models. Raw experimental data are deposited in an open repository.

title: Economic assessment of small-scale hydrogen production from grid-connected wind power in the Western Balkans
abstract: A bottom-up techno-economic model was constructed to assess the levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH) for wind-coupled alkaline electrolysis systems sized between 0.5 MW and 5 MW in regions characteristic of the Western Balkans electricity market. Hourly wind resource data from seven measurement stations in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina over 2008–2012 were used as input. The model accounts for electricity purchase at spot prices, electrolyser capital and replacement costs, and compressed storage at 200 bar. Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis (10 000 draws) was performed on capital expenditure, capacity factor, and electricity price. Median LCOH across the seven sites ranged from 5.2 to 8.7 EUR/kg. Grid connection fees were the dominant cost driver at four of the seven sites, outweighing electrolyser capital cost when capacity factors fell below 28%. The study identifies minimum viable capacity factors and electricity price thresholds for breakeven with incumbent hydrogen supply.

title: Degradation mechanisms in industrial alkaline electrolysers: a review of quantitative lifetime models
abstract: This chapter surveys quantitative models that relate operating conditions to performance loss in alkaline electrolysis stacks, covering publications from 1995 to 2016. Four degradation pathways are discussed in detail: diaphragm fouling by electrolyte impurities, nickel electrode corrosion during idle periods, bubble-induced mass-transfer limitation at elevated current densities, and seal degradation linked to thermal cycling. For each pathway, the chapter compares empirical rate expressions reported in the literature, assesses the quality of experimental evidence, and evaluates applicability to system-level economic models. Particular attention is given to the distinction between reversible and irreversible degradation and to the implications for maintenance scheduling and stack replacement intervals. The chapter concludes that most published lifetime models are calibrated on accelerated ageing data and that independent validation against field data from multi-megawatt installations remains scarce. Gaps relevant to sizing studies under renewable intermittency are identified.

title: Seasonal hydrogen storage dimensioning for a wind-electrolyser system: comparing above-ground compressed tanks and underground salt cavern options in Vojvodina
abstract: Wind generation in Vojvodina exhibits a pronounced seasonal pattern with winter surpluses and summer deficits relative to hypothetical hydrogen demand profiles. This study compares two storage technologies—above-ground compressed gas tanks at 350 bar and repurposed underground salt cavern storage at low pressure—for buffering a 2 MW alkaline electrolyser operated on curtailed wind electricity. A time-series dispatch model was run on ten years of hourly wind data (2010–2019) at 15-minute resolution. Capital and operating costs for each storage option were taken from vendor quotations and published literature. The cavern option reduces system LCOH by 18–24% for demand patterns requiring more than 45 days of storage, but involves higher site investigation costs and geological risk. Break-even storage duration between the two technologies is 38 days at the central cost estimates. Geological suitability data for Vojvodina salt structures are discussed.

title: Optimal scheduling of an alkaline electrolyser participating in the Serbian balancing market while producing hydrogen from curtailed renewables
abstract: Electrolysers connected to curtailed renewable plants can provide secondary frequency regulation services while using residual curtailed energy for hydrogen production. This paper formulates a two-objective optimisation problem—maximising revenue from balancing services and minimising LCOH—solved by weighted-sum scalarisation over a Pareto front. The model is applied to a hypothetical 3 MW electrolyser co-located with a wind farm under the rules of the Serbian balancing mechanism as published by the transmission system operator in 2020. Hourly balancing price data from 2019 and 2020 are used. Results show that allocating 20–30% of electrolyser capacity to balancing services reduces LCOH by 0.6–0.9 EUR/kg without substantially increasing stack cycling frequency. Full commitment to balancing services degrades the economics of hydrogen production due to reduced operating hours. Stack wear costs associated with balancing duty are estimated using the degradation model from prior work.

title: Comparative techno-economic assessment of green hydrogen supply chains for a hypothetical industrial cluster in South Pannonia
abstract: Three hydrogen supply chain configurations are compared for supplying 500 kg/day of hydrogen to a hypothetical cluster of fertiliser and ceramics producers in the South Pannonia region: (i) on-site electrolysis with compressed storage, (ii) centralised electrolysis with tube-trailer delivery, and (iii) pipeline distribution from a regional electrolysis hub. Input data include geospatial wind and solar curtailment estimates for 2019–2021 derived from published grid congestion reports, regional road network distances, and capital cost ranges from supplier catalogues. Total cost of hydrogen delivered to the factory gate ranges from 5.9 to 9.4 EUR/kg depending on configuration, demand profile, and renewable curtailment volume available. Pipeline distribution becomes cost-competitive only when cluster density exceeds 1.8 kg/km² and annual demand surpasses 400 tonnes. The analysis is intended to inform regional hydrogen roadmap exercises and is accompanied by an openly licensed spreadsheet tool.

title: Quantifying the impact of curtailment signal granularity on electrolyser sizing and degradation cost in wind-coupled systems
abstract: System operators and researchers use curtailment data at varying temporal resolutions—from 15-minute to hourly and daily averages—when designing electrolysis systems. This preprint investigates the error introduced by temporal aggregation on three outputs: optimum electrolyser rated power, expected annual hydrogen yield, and 20-year degradation cost. Simulations use 1-minute SCADA data from two wind farms in Vojvodina, subsequently aggregated to 5-min, 15-min, 30-min, and 60-min intervals. Electrolyser sizing errors relative to the 1-minute baseline reach 6.4% at 15-minute resolution and 14.1% at 60-minute resolution. Degradation cost errors are larger in relative terms, reaching 22% at hourly resolution due to misrepresentation of ramp frequency. The findings suggest that 15-minute resolution is the practical minimum for sizing studies where degradation cost is a significant share of total LCOH, and that hourly data commonly available from published grid statistics are insufficient for detailed project engineering.

title: Dynamic simulation of an industrial refrigeration plant with ammonia under fluctuating electrical tariff signals
abstract: A dynamic simulation model of a two-stage ammonia refrigeration plant rated at 350 kW cooling capacity was developed in Modelica/Dymola and validated against six months of logged data from a meat-processing facility. The model captures transient behaviour of evaporators, the intercooler, and the high-stage and low-stage reciprocating compressors, with control loops tuned to match observed suction pressure oscillations within 0.15 bar root-mean-square error. Simulations were run under a synthetic day-ahead price signal with peak-to-off-peak price ratios of 1.5, 2.0 and 3.0, representative of proposed Serbian industrial tariff reform scenarios. Load shifting achieved by raising evaporator set-points and accumulating thermal mass in the product reduced peak-period energy cost by 7–15% without violating product temperature constraints. The paper identifies a practical upper limit on pre-cooling depth imposed by product quality specifications.

title: Measured versus simulated energy yield for five years of operation of a 3 kWp off-grid PV system: sources and magnitudes of deviation
abstract: Long-term continuous monitoring of off-grid PV installations is uncommon in published literature, resulting in limited empirical evidence for model validation beyond one or two years. This paper presents five years (2018–2022) of monthly measured energy yield and battery state-of-charge statistics from a 3 kWp LFP-backed PV installation at a rural agricultural building in Bačka Palanka, Serbia. Measurements are compared against a simulation using the department's hourly model, driven by satellite-corrected irradiance. Over five years, cumulative simulated yield exceeds measured yield by 6.4%, with the discrepancy increasing from 3.1% in year one to 9.8% in year five. Attribution analysis assigns 4.1 percentage points to battery capacity fade, 1.8 points to increased soiling in years three to five following reduced cleaning frequency, and the remaining 0.5 points to module degradation consistent with published degradation rates of 0.5% per year. The results confirm that battery degradation is the dominant source of growing yield discrepancy in the medium term.

title: Parametric Skeleton Models for Rusyn Cyrillic Glyphs: Construction Rules and Interpolation Axes
abstract: Rusyn, a minority language officially recognised in Serbia and Croatia, uses a Cyrillic orthography that includes several characters absent from standard Serbian Cyrillic encodings. Existing digital fonts either omit these glyphs or render them through ad-hoc workarounds that break OpenType shaping. This paper proposes a parametric skeleton model for 14 Rusyn-specific glyphs, defining five interpolation axes—weight, contrast, x-height ratio, serif style, and counter aperture—using RoboFab-based Python scripting within a Unified Font Object (UFO) workflow. Skeleton nodes and handles are expressed as proportional functions of a master unit-per-em value, allowing consistent scaling across optical sizes. The model was validated by generating 48 instance fonts across axis combinations and subjecting them to readability assessments with 23 Rusyn-speaking participants recruited through the National Council of the Rusyn Minority in Novi Sad. Agreement scores measured on a five-point typographic naturalness scale reached a mean of 3.9 for serif instances and 3.6 for sans-serif instances, with the lowest scores associated with extreme contrast settings. The skeleton tables and UFO source files are released under a SIL Open Font License.

title: OpenType GSUB Lookup Coverage for Southern Slavic Diacritics: A Cross-Renderer Audit
abstract: Southern Slavic writing systems—Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Slovenian, and Macedonian—rely on a set of diacritical characters whose correct typographic rendering depends on Glyph Substitution (GSUB) and Glyph Positioning (GPOS) lookups defined in OpenType Layout tables. Inconsistencies between rendering engines (HarfBuzz, DirectWrite, CoreText, and the Adobe shaping stack) lead to mark attachment failures and incorrect contextual substitutions, particularly for the characters š, č, ž, ć, đ, and their uppercase counterparts when composed with quotation marks or following capital letters. This study conducted a systematic audit of 37 commercial and open-source fonts claiming Southern Slavic language support, testing each against a corpus of 2 400 word-level shaping sequences extracted from digitised newspaper text. Failures were classified into four categories: missing mark-to-base anchors, incomplete calt chain contexts, absent loclSRB or loclMKD features, and erroneous kern class assignments. Fourteen fonts exhibited at least one category-one failure. The paper provides a structured checklist and a freely downloadable test font containing deliberate failure cases for quality-assurance pipelines.

title: Variable Font Axis Design for a Unified Latin–Cyrillic Type Family Serving Serbian Bilingual Publishing
abstract: Bilingual Latin–Cyrillic publications in Serbia—covering Serbian written in both scripts as mandated by official bilingual policies in Vojvodina—require type families that maintain consistent rhythm and colour across both scripts at identical optical sizes. This paper documents the design process of a variable font family, named Ravnica, created to serve bilingual administrative and editorial contexts. The family defines four axes: weight (100–900), width (75–125), optical size (8–36 pt), and a script-blend axis that continuously interpolates shared design parameters between the Latin and Cyrillic masters. Interpolation compatibility was achieved through a 312-step node-count harmonisation procedure across 64 master glyphs. The resulting variable font was tested in simulated bilingual page layouts representing municipal gazette formats used in three Vojvodina municipalities. Colour uniformity—measured as standard deviation of per-line optical density across mixed-script paragraphs—improved by 18 % compared to a matched non-variable control family. The paper also discusses axis naming conventions in the fvar table and their interaction with CSS font-variation-settings in web contexts.

title: Automated Contour Quality Metrics for Interpolation-Ready Glyph Masters: A Benchmark Dataset for Southern Slavic Characters
abstract: Interpolation-based font production requires that glyph masters share compatible contour structures, but no standardised benchmark exists for evaluating contour quality specifically in Southern Slavic character sets, which include both Latin extended and Cyrillic blocks. This paper introduces the SlavoContour-109 benchmark dataset, comprising 109 glyphs drawn from Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Slovenian, Macedonian, and Rusyn orthographies, each annotated with a reference contour and a set of deliberately introduced quality defects—direction errors, stray points, open paths, and incompatible node counts. Four automated checking tools (FontBakery, FoundryFabriek QC, a custom Python script, and a commercial proofing plugin) were evaluated against the dataset. Precision and recall were computed per defect category across all 109 glyphs. The custom Python script achieved the highest F1 score for direction errors (0.91) but performed poorly on stray-point detection (0.54). The dataset is published in UFO and Glyphs 3 format and is intended for use in type-design pedagogy and automated font production pipelines.

title: Encoding Bunjevac Latin Orthography in OpenType: Character Set Recommendations and Font Engineering Notes
abstract: Bunjevac, a minority language spoken in the Subotica region of Vojvodina, uses a Latin-based orthography that was formally standardised in 2020. The standardised orthography introduces three digraph representations and two diacritical characters not present in any existing Unicode block, requiring a decision between Private Use Area encoding and a formal Unicode proposal. This book chapter reviews the encoding options in detail, evaluates six prior minority-language encoding case studies from Central and Southeastern Europe, and proposes an interim PUA-based OpenType implementation strategy pending a Unicode proposal submission. The chapter describes how liga and ccmp features can be used to compose digraphs from base characters and provides annotated OpenType feature code for the four most critical contextual cases. A proof-of-concept font, Subotička, is provided as a supplementary download. The chapter also outlines the Unicode proposal process and identifies the technical documentation gaps that currently prevent a submission.

title: Pressure-Drop Distribution in Branched Compressed-Air Networks: A Field-Measurement Study in a Metalworking Facility
abstract: Compressed-air distribution losses in manufacturing plants are routinely underestimated because pressure surveys are conducted only at compressor outlets and at selected end-use points. This paper presents a systematic pressure-drop mapping methodology applied to a branched ring-and-radial network at a metalworking facility in Vojvodina with a nominal supply pressure of 8 bar and a connected load of approximately 220 kW of installed compressor capacity. Forty-two measurement nodes were instrumented with calibrated piezoresistive transducers over a 20-day campaign covering three production shifts. Recorded data were processed using a stepwise regression model to relate local pressure drop to volumetric flow rate, pipe diameter, and fitting count. Cumulative pressure losses from pipe friction and fittings accounted for 0.61 bar on average between the compressor house and the farthest end-use branch, with a peak of 1.14 bar during morning start-up. Reducing main-header velocity from 8.2 m/s to below 6 m/s through partial network re-routing was estimated to recover 4.3% of annual compressor energy. The methodology and dataset are offered as a reproducible baseline for M&V applications at comparable sites.

title: Ultrasonic Leak Survey and Leak-Rate Estimation in an Automotive Component Plant: Comparison of Flow-Decay and Acoustic Methods
abstract: Compressed-air leakage is commonly cited as representing 20–40% of total system output in poorly maintained industrial plants, yet routine quantification methods differ substantially in accuracy and intrusion. This study compares two quantification approaches at an automotive component plant in central Serbia: a flow-decay test using a calibrated orifice plate during scheduled production downtime, and a walking survey with a heterodyne ultrasonic detector at 40 kHz. Over two survey campaigns separated by six months, 63 individual leak sites were identified by the ultrasonic method and tagged by location, orifice category, and estimated flow rate class. Summed leak rates from the acoustic method ranged from 18.4 to 22.1 m³/h (free air), while the flow-decay method yielded a system-wide figure of 20.8 m³/h, giving agreement within 6%. After a targeted repair programme addressing 41 of the 63 sites, a follow-up flow-decay test indicated a reduction to 9.1 m³/h, equivalent to an estimated annual saving of approximately 38 MWh of compressor electricity. The paper discusses classification bias in acoustic estimation and recommends a combined protocol for lean audit programmes.

title: Application of IPMVP Option B to Compressor Retrofit Projects: Boundary Conditions and Uncertainty Budgets
abstract: The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) Option B — stipulating metered savings at the boundary of the measure — is theoretically well-suited to compressor replacement and variable-speed-drive (VSD) retrofits, but its practical implementation raises questions about baseline duration, independent variable selection, and acceptable uncertainty levels. This book chapter reviews ten publicly documented compressed-air retrofit projects drawn from European industrial efficiency programmes between 2015 and 2023, reconstructing the verification calculations where source data permit. For five projects where sub-metering data were accessible, baseline models using compressor shaft power as the dependent variable and production-schedule indicators as independent variables achieved adjusted R² values between 0.71 and 0.89. Fractional savings uncertainty at the 90% confidence level ranged from ±4% to ±19% depending on baseline length and load variability. The chapter provides a decision tree for selecting baseline duration and identifies production throughput normalisation as the step most frequently handled inconsistently across the reviewed projects. Worked numerical examples are included for a two-stage screw compressor replacement scenario representative of mid-sized Serbian manufacturing plants.

title: Staging Strategies for Multi-Compressor Systems Under Variable Demand: A Simulation and Statistical Analysis
abstract: Industrial facilities commonly operate multiple fixed-speed compressors in parallel, relying on pressure-band switching logic that was set at commissioning and rarely revisited. This study uses a discrete-event simulation model, calibrated against 15-second interval power and pressure logs from a food-processing plant operating four screw compressors (two 75 kW, one 55 kW, one 37 kW), to evaluate alternative staging sequences over a representative 90-day production period. Demand profiles were decomposed into a base load, a cyclic component tied to pneumatic conveying cycles, and a stochastic residual. Seven staging strategies were tested, ranging from fixed lead-lag assignment to a demand-forecast-assisted sequence optimised by a simple gradient descent. The demand-forecast strategy reduced total compressor run-hours by 8.7% and cut unloaded running from 23% to 11% of total runtime relative to the as-found configuration, corresponding to estimated annual electricity savings of 61 MWh. Fixed strategies with appropriate threshold spacing performed nearly as well as the optimised approach, suggesting that configuration adjustments achievable without additional instrumentation can recover most of the available savings. Statistical analysis of variance across strategies used bootstrapped confidence intervals to account for autocorrelation in the demand series.

title: Real-time optimisation of ORC operating conditions using a Gaussian process surrogate trained on dynamic simulation data
abstract: Real-time optimisation of ORC operating points requires a model that evaluates quickly enough for online use while remaining accurate across a wide operating envelope. A Gaussian process (GP) surrogate model was trained on 1,800 steady-state snapshots extracted from validated dynamic Modelica simulations of a 50 kWe ORC unit operating with R1234ze(E) over heat-source temperatures from 100 to 180 °C and cooling-water temperatures from 10 to 30 °C. The GP surrogate predicts net power output with a root-mean-square error of 0.31 kW on a hold-out test set and evaluates in under 2 ms, enabling gradient-based optimisation of pump speed and bypass-valve position at each sampling interval. A real-time optimiser was implemented in a Python-based supervisory layer and tested in hardware-in-the-loop experiments using the laboratory rig with a simulated industrial heat-source profile. Over a 72-hour test, the real-time optimiser increased mean net power by 5.8% relative to fixed setpoint operation, with the largest gains occurring during periods of rapid heat-source temperature variation.

title: Peak Load Reduction Through Direct Load Control of Electric Water Heaters in a Low-Voltage Feeder
abstract: This paper examines direct load control of electric water heaters as a tool for peak shaving in a representative 0.4 kV residential feeder in northern Serbia. A thermal comfort model based on a second-order RC network is used to bound allowable interruption intervals. An integer linear programme schedules on/off switching of 120 water heaters over a 24-hour horizon, targeting a 15-minute dispatch resolution. Measured load profiles from 2008 smart meter trials in the Novi Sad area served as boundary conditions. Results show a 19.4% reduction in feeder peak demand with no household comfort violation when interruption windows are limited to 20 minutes. Voltage profile improvement along the feeder was quantified using backward/forward sweep power flow. The approach is compared with a simple thermostat-setback heuristic, which achieves only 11.2% peak reduction under the same constraints. Computation time on a standard workstation was under four seconds for the full 24-hour schedule, suggesting suitability for near-real-time operation.

title: Time-of-Use Tariff Design for Residential Consumers: A Case Study from the Serbian Distribution System
abstract: The paper investigates the design of time-of-use (TOU) electricity tariffs for residential consumers connected to a medium-density urban distribution network in Vojvodina. Using one year of interval metering data from 340 households, a k-means clustering algorithm identifies four distinct consumption archetypes. For each archetype, price elasticity of demand is estimated via a log-linear regression model calibrated on billing records before and after a pilot TOU trial conducted by a regional distribution company. Three TOU rate structures are evaluated: two-period, three-period, and critical-peak pricing. The three-period structure yields the best balance between peak reduction (14.8%) and revenue neutrality for the utility. The analysis also quantifies rebound peaks that emerge at the start of the off-peak window and proposes a minimum 30-minute staggered activation rule to suppress them. Findings are intended to inform pending revisions to the Serbian electricity market rulebook.
