title: Stochastic Scheduling of Thermostatically Controlled Loads Under Uncertain Outdoor Temperature Forecasts
abstract: Thermostatically controlled loads such as air conditioners and heat pumps introduce forecast uncertainty into demand response programmes because their flexibility depends on ambient temperature. This paper formulates a two-stage stochastic integer programme in which first-stage decisions commit a population of 200 simulated residential heat pumps to an hourly schedule one day ahead, while second-stage recourse actions correct deviations as temperature scenarios are realised. Fifty temperature scenarios are generated by a first-order autoregressive model fitted to ten years of meteorological data from Novi Sad. The stochastic model is compared with a deterministic benchmark that uses point forecasts. The stochastic approach reduces expected energy cost by 6.3% and decreases the frequency of comfort bound violations by 44% relative to the deterministic schedule. Scenario reduction via fast-forward selection is applied to keep the problem tractable; the reduced 12-scenario model retains 94% of the value of the full 50-scenario problem. The model is solved with a branch-and-bound solver within 90 seconds.

title: Aggregator-Mediated Demand Response: Modelling the Relationship Between a Residential Aggregator and the Distribution System Operator
abstract: This book chapter reviews regulatory and technical frameworks for aggregator-mediated demand response in southeastern Europe, with a focus on the emerging Serbian market structure. The chapter first outlines the principal–agent relationship between the aggregator and enrolled households, deriving an incentive-compatible contract that compensates consumers for flexibility provision while allowing the aggregator to bid in a day-ahead flexibility market. A stylised bilevel optimisation model is presented in which the aggregator's profit maximisation problem forms the upper level and individual household comfort-constrained scheduling problems form the lower level. Numerical examples use parameters representative of a 500-household portfolio in the Vojvodina region. The chapter discusses barriers to aggregator entry in markets dominated by a single vertically integrated utility and compares the Serbian situation with Croatian and Romanian counterparts. Policy recommendations emphasise the need for standardised communication protocols and metering data access rules.

title: Day-Ahead Optimal Charging Schedules for a Fleet of Private Electric Vehicles Under Real-Time Pricing Signals
abstract: This paper presents an optimisation framework for scheduling overnight charging of a fleet of 80 private electric vehicles connected to a residential distribution feeder. Vehicle availability windows and required state-of-charge targets are treated as deterministic inputs derived from a travel survey of commuters in Novi Sad conducted in 2015. The objective minimises total charging cost under an hourly real-time price signal modelled on the day-ahead market prices from the regional power exchange. A mixed-integer quadratic programme enforces feeder capacity constraints, transformer thermal limits, and individual charger ratings of 3.7 kW and 7.4 kW. Compared with uncontrolled charging, the optimised schedule reduces peak feeder load by 28.7% and lowers total charging cost by 11.3%. The model is also solved under a simplified convex relaxation, which yields a cost within 0.4% of the exact solution at one-tenth of the computation time. Sensitivity analysis shows that results are robust to ±10% variation in vehicle arrival times.

title: Quantifying Demand Flexibility in Aggregated Residential Portfolios Using a Virtual Battery Model
abstract: The virtual battery abstraction represents the aggregate flexibility of a population of deferrable loads as a single storage device characterised by equivalent capacity, charge/discharge rate limits, and efficiency. This paper derives virtual battery parameters analytically for three load classes—electric vehicle chargers, heat pumps, and washing machines—and validates the model against detailed appliance-level simulations of a 500-household portfolio. Validation data are drawn from a monitoring campaign conducted in three residential estates in Novi Sad in 2016–2017. The virtual battery model achieves demand tracking errors below 4.2% for time steps of 15 minutes or longer, but errors exceed 9% at 5-minute resolution due to unmodelled switching transients. An extension handles heterogeneous fleets by compositing individual virtual batteries. The model is lightweight enough to be embedded in distribution management system software and is demonstrated in a receding-horizon control scenario over a 48-hour test period. Comparison with the appliance-level model shows a computational speed-up of three orders of magnitude.

title: Distributed Model Predictive Control for Coordinated EV Charging in Multi-Feeder Residential Networks
abstract: Centralised optimisation of electric vehicle charging across multiple feeders sharing a medium-voltage/low-voltage substation raises scalability and data privacy concerns. This paper proposes a distributed model predictive control (DMPC) scheme in which each feeder-level controller optimises local EV charging over a rolling two-hour horizon and exchanges only aggregated power setpoints with a substation coordinator via an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) decomposition. The test network comprises four radial feeders with 60 EVs each, totalling 240 vehicles, parameterised from field measurements at a residential estate in Petrovaradin. Real-time price signals are taken from synthetic hourly price sequences calibrated to SEEPEX market data. After 15 ADMM iterations the substation transformer overload constraint is satisfied with a residual primal infeasibility of 0.3%. Total charging cost is within 1.8% of the centralised optimum. The DMPC scheme is also evaluated under 20% communication packet loss, showing graceful performance degradation without instability.

title: Impact of Photovoltaic Self-Consumption on Optimal EV Charging Schedules in Distribution Networks with High Residential PV Penetration
abstract: Residential rooftop photovoltaic systems alter the net load profiles that drive EV charging optimisation. This paper extends a day-ahead scheduling model to jointly optimise EV charging and PV self-consumption in a 200-node low-voltage network with 35% PV penetration, representative of newer housing developments in the Vojvodina region. PV generation forecasts are produced by a persistence model corrected with a sky-camera irradiance estimate; forecast errors are characterised empirically over 14 months of monitoring data. The optimisation minimises grid electricity cost minus self-consumption revenue under real-time pricing, subject to feeder voltage limits enforced via a linearised DistFlow formulation. Compared with EV scheduling without self-consumption awareness, the joint approach increases self-consumed PV energy by 18.6% and reduces grid import cost by 9.1%. A parametric study varying PV penetration from 10% to 60% shows that joint scheduling benefits grow monotonically up to 50% penetration, beyond which grid export curtailment becomes binding.

title: Coordinated Scheduling of Heat Pumps and EV Chargers in a Residential Microgrid with Battery Storage Under Dynamic Tariffs
abstract: This paper addresses the joint day-ahead scheduling of heat pumps, EV chargers, and a 100 kWh lithium-ion battery storage unit in a residential microgrid serving 40 dwellings in Novi Sad. A mixed-integer linear programme minimises electricity procurement cost under an hourly dynamic tariff while respecting thermal comfort bounds, battery cycle-life constraints modelled via a throughput counter, and a 160 kVA grid connection limit. Demand-side flexibility from heat pumps and EVs is represented using the validated virtual battery model from prior work. The scheduling problem is solved for all 365 days of 2019 using actual hourly temperature, occupancy, and price data. Annual electricity cost is reduced by 22.4% compared with uncontrolled operation. Battery degradation is limited to 1.8% capacity loss per year by capping daily throughput at 1.2 cycles. The interaction between heat pump and EV flexibility is analysed: scheduling them jointly rather than sequentially reduces cost by an additional 4.1% by exploiting temporal complementarity in their flexibility windows.

title: Assessing the Capacity of Demand Response Aggregators to Provide Balancing Services in the Serbian Electricity Market
abstract: Since 2021, Serbian market rules permit aggregators to offer secondary frequency regulation capacity on behalf of residential flexible loads. This paper quantifies how much regulation capacity a demand response aggregator managing 3 000 households in Novi Sad could reliably bid in the balancing market. A Monte Carlo simulation draws 1 000 portfolio realisations from empirical distributions of appliance flexibility, vehicle state of charge at grid connection, and occupancy patterns collected during a 2021 smart meter pilot. For each realisation, the maximum symmetric regulation bandwidth achievable without comfort violations is computed analytically. The 10th percentile bandwidth, used as the conservative bid quantity, equals 420 kW upward and 380 kW downward at a 95% reliability level. Revenue estimates under published Serbian ancillary service tariffs indicate that balancing service revenue could cover 60–70% of aggregator operational costs, making business viability conditional on combining balancing with energy arbitrage. Policy implications for market rule revisions are discussed.

title: Data-Driven Estimation of EV Charging Flexibility Envelopes from Smart Meter Records
abstract: Accurate characterisation of EV charging flexibility requires knowledge of vehicle departure times and required state-of-charge, which are rarely directly observable by a grid operator. This paper develops a data-driven method to infer charging flexibility envelopes from smart meter current measurements at 1-minute resolution without explicit vehicle telemetry. A hidden Markov model detects charging session boundaries and estimates session energy demand from the measured current integral. Departure time is predicted by a gradient-boosted regression tree trained on 14 months of session records from 65 private EV owners participating in a monitoring trial in Novi Sad. The predicted flexibility envelope—defined as the set of feasible charging power trajectories from session start to predicted departure—is compared against ground-truth GPS-derived departure times. Envelope feasibility rate is 89.3% at a 95% confidence level. The method enables aggregators to construct flexibility bids without requiring direct vehicle communication and is computationally suitable for deployment on a distribution management server handling up to 5 000 concurrent sessions.

title: Volt/VAR Optimisation Coupled with Flexible Load Scheduling in Low-Voltage Networks with High EV Penetration
abstract: High EV penetration raises both active power demand and reactive power fluctuations in low-voltage distribution networks. This paper integrates Volt/VAR optimisation (VVO) with flexible load scheduling in a joint AC optimal power flow formulation applied to a 94-node test feeder representative of a mixed residential–commercial area near Novi Sad. EV chargers are modelled as controllable complex power injections, exploiting the ability of modern off-board chargers to operate at adjustable power factor. A second-order cone relaxation of the AC OPF is solved hourly over a 24-hour horizon. The joint VVO–scheduling approach reduces total active power losses by 11.8% and keeps all bus voltages within ±5% of nominal throughout the day, compared with 7.2% loss reduction and three voltage violations under active-power-only EV scheduling. Reactive power support from EV chargers contributes 34% of total reactive compensation, reducing on-load tap changer operations by 40%. The formulation scales to 200-node feeders within a two-minute solve time.

title: Rolling-Horizon Scheduling of Aggregated Residential Loads Under Intraday Price Revisions: A Receding-Horizon MPC Benchmark Study
abstract: Day-ahead EV and flexible load schedules must be revised intraday as electricity prices, vehicle arrivals, and weather conditions deviate from forecasts. This paper benchmarks four receding-horizon model predictive control (MPC) strategies—open-loop optimal, closed-loop robust, scenario-based stochastic MPC, and a lightweight rule-based corrector—on a 15-minute-resolution intraday scheduling problem for a 150-household residential portfolio with 60 EVs. Intraday price revisions are modelled using an ARIMA process fitted to 18 months of regional day-ahead and intraday price differences. Stochastic MPC achieves the lowest mean daily cost (within 2.3% of a clairvoyant oracle) but requires 8× more computation than open-loop optimal. The rule-based corrector, requiring less than one second per revision cycle, achieves costs within 5.1% of the oracle and is considered the practical default for resource-constrained controllers. All four strategies are evaluated on a hardware-in-the-loop testbed using the laboratory's RTDS simulator interfaced with a physical 7.4 kW EV charger, confirming simulation results within measurement uncertainty.

title: Impedance Matching Network Design for 433 MHz Short-Range Transceivers Using LC Ladder Topologies
abstract: This paper examines the design and measured performance of three LC ladder impedance matching topologies applied to a 433 MHz short-range transceiver antenna port. Prototype networks were fabricated on FR-4 substrate and characterised with a two-port vector network analyser. Return loss better than 18 dB was achieved across a 2 MHz bandwidth for all three topologies under nominal load conditions. The sensitivity of each topology to component tolerance was evaluated by Monte Carlo simulation using 5 % resistor and 2 % capacitor tolerance distributions over 10 000 runs. Results show that the L-network topology maintains the tightest impedance bandwidth variance, while the pi-network offers a 3 dB improvement in insertion loss at the expense of greater sensitivity to stray inductance. Measurements in a temperature range of −10 °C to +60 °C revealed a centre frequency drift of up to 480 kHz for the pi-network. Practical guidelines for component placement to minimise parasitic effects on 50 mm × 30 mm board layouts are derived from the measurement data.

title: Comparison of time-domain EMG features for knee joint torque prediction during isometric contraction
abstract: This study evaluated six time-domain surface electromyography features—root mean square, mean absolute value, waveform length, zero-crossing rate, slope sign change, and integrated EMG—for their ability to predict knee extension and flexion torques during isometric tasks in 14 healthy male subjects. Signals were recorded from the rectus femoris, vastus medialis, vastus lateralis, and biceps femoris using a 4-channel Biopac system at 2 kHz. A linear regression model was trained on a 60/40 train-test split for each feature individually and in concatenated vectors. Waveform length combined with RMS achieved the lowest normalised root mean square error of 8.3% across subjects. Inter-subject variability was high, with individual model errors ranging from 5.1% to 14.7%, motivating subject-specific calibration procedures. These results provided a baseline for subsequent nonlinear modelling approaches in the group's research programme.

title: A subject-specific musculoskeletal model of the lower limb for inverse dynamics torque estimation during gait
abstract: A scaled musculoskeletal model of the lower limb was constructed for ten healthy subjects (five male, five female, mean age 26 ± 3 years) using anthropometric measurements and OpenSim 3.3. Ground reaction forces were recorded with two AMTI force plates and kinematic data were captured at 120 Hz using a six-camera Vicon motion capture system. Inverse dynamics analyses were performed for level walking at self-selected speed and at 1.2 m/s. Model-predicted knee joint torques were compared with those derived from the force plate and motion capture pipeline alone, yielding mean absolute errors below 4.1 Nm across the gait cycle. Sensitivity analysis revealed that errors in segment mass estimates of ±5% produced torque deviations under 1.8 Nm. The validated pipeline was subsequently used as a reference for EMG-driven torque estimation studies.

title: EMG-driven torque estimation for a knee exoskeleton: Hill-type muscle model calibration and real-time implementation
abstract: This paper describes the calibration and real-time implementation of a Hill-type muscle model for estimating knee joint torque from surface EMG signals in a powered knee exoskeleton context. Four muscle groups were instrumented on eight subjects during a series of isometric ramp contractions at 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% of maximum voluntary contraction. Hill model parameters—activation dynamics time constants, optimal fibre length, and pennation angle—were personalised using a gradient-descent optimisation minimising torque RMSE against force plate reference measurements. The calibrated model achieved mean RMSE of 6.8 Nm (9.2% of peak torque) during validation contractions not seen during calibration. Real-time computation ran at 100 Hz on an embedded ARM Cortex-A9 board with 7.3 ms average latency. The calibration required approximately 15 minutes per subject, which is considered feasible for clinical deployment.

title: Electrode placement variability and its effect on sEMG-based torque prediction at the knee
abstract: Inconsistent electrode placement between sessions is a recognised source of error in surface EMG-based torque estimation systems. This study quantified the effect of deliberate electrode displacement of 1 cm, 2 cm, and 3 cm in the proximal, distal, and lateral directions on torque prediction accuracy for the quadriceps and hamstring muscle groups in twelve healthy subjects. A support vector regression model trained on day-one recordings was evaluated on day-two recordings with controlled misplacements. Torque RMSE increased from a baseline of 7.1 Nm to 11.4 Nm for 2 cm distal displacement on vastus medialis and to 14.8 Nm for 3 cm lateral displacement on biceps femoris. A feature normalisation strategy using the centroid frequency shift reduced the sensitivity to lateral displacement by approximately 35%. Results suggest that clinical protocols requiring day-to-day consistency should enforce placement landmarks photographically.

title: Blind source separation approaches for decomposing high-density sEMG into motor unit spike trains
abstract: High-density surface EMG recorded with a 64-electrode grid over the vastus lateralis was decomposed into individual motor unit spike trains using three algorithms: fast independent component analysis, convolutive kernel compensation, and a sparse Bayesian framework adapted for surface recordings. Data were collected from ten subjects during trapezoid isometric contractions at force levels of 10%, 30%, and 50% of maximum voluntary contraction. Ground truth was not available, but cross-algorithm agreement and pulse-to-noise ratio were used as quality metrics. FastICA identified a mean of 9.3 motor units per recording; convolutive kernel compensation identified 17.6; the sparse Bayesian method identified 14.2. Reconstruction accuracy of aggregate force from identified motor units correlated with force level and was highest for the convolutive method at 50% MVC (r² = 0.91). Computational time for the convolutive method was 38 s per 30-second contraction on a desktop workstation.

title: Influence of muscle co-contraction on sEMG-based torque estimation accuracy during dynamic knee flexion-extension
abstract: Antagonist co-contraction introduces estimation error in EMG-driven torque models because net joint torque reflects the balance of agonist and antagonist contributions. This study systematically varied co-contraction levels in eight healthy subjects by instructing them to perform knee flexion-extension cycles under three verbal instruction conditions: relaxed antagonist, moderate co-contraction, and high co-contraction, confirmed by normalised hamstring EMG thresholds. A two-compartment Hill model that included both quadriceps and hamstrings as independent inputs was compared with a quadriceps-only model. The dual-compartment model reduced mean absolute torque error from 10.4 Nm to 6.7 Nm during high co-contraction trials. Joint stiffness estimated from the model increased monotonically with co-contraction level (Pearson r = 0.83), validating the physiological plausibility of the approach. These findings support the inclusion of antagonist EMG channels in clinical exoskeleton applications.

title: Recurrent neural network torque estimation from decomposed motor unit discharge rates: a comparison with envelope-based methods
abstract: Cumulative spike train signals reconstructed from decomposed motor unit discharge rates were used as inputs to a long short-term memory network for knee torque estimation and compared against standard linear envelope and RMS-based approaches. Recordings from a 32-channel electrode grid over the quadriceps were acquired from eleven subjects during ramp and sinusoidal isometric contractions. Decomposition was performed offline using a validated convolutive kernel compensation algorithm that identified between 12 and 24 motor units per recording. The LSTM trained on cumulative spike trains achieved a mean R² of 0.96 and RMSE of 5.1 Nm, compared to 0.91 and 8.6 Nm for RMS-based linear regression. Performance advantage was most pronounced in the low-force range (0–20% MVC), where spike-train inputs yielded 41% lower RMSE. Offline processing time was 180 ms per 1-second window, identifying a gap for real-time optimisation.

title: Exoskeleton-assisted gait rehabilitation after spinal cord injury: torque control strategies and clinical outcomes — a scoping review
abstract: This scoping review synthesised evidence on torque control strategies used in lower-limb exoskeleton-assisted gait rehabilitation for individuals with incomplete spinal cord injury, covering publications from 2010 to 2022. Forty-three studies were included after screening 612 records using PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Control strategies were categorised as predefined trajectory tracking (23 studies), EMG-driven assist-as-needed (11 studies), impedance/admittance control without EMG (7 studies), and hybrid approaches (2 studies). EMG-driven AAN strategies showed statistically greater improvements in 10-metre walk test scores (mean difference 0.09 m/s, 95% CI 0.02–0.17) compared to trajectory-tracking approaches across the included trials, though heterogeneity was high (I² = 64%). Reporting of adverse events was inconsistent across studies. Key methodological gaps identified include small sample sizes, absence of long-term follow-up beyond three months, and inconsistent torque control parameter reporting. Recommendations for standardised reporting are provided.

title: Real-time motor unit decomposition on an embedded GPU for closed-loop exoskeleton control
abstract: Moving high-density EMG decomposition from offline workstations to embedded hardware is a prerequisite for clinical deployment of spike-train-driven exoskeleton controllers. This paper presents an implementation of a modified convolutive kernel compensation algorithm on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module. The algorithm was optimised for parallel execution using CUDA, reducing per-iteration computation time from 34 ms on a desktop CPU to 4.1 ms on the embedded GPU for a 32-channel input stream. Online decomposition was validated against offline reference decomposition on pre-recorded datasets from nine subjects, yielding a mean motor unit identification rate agreement of 87.3%. A closed-loop knee exoskeleton experiment with three healthy subjects demonstrated that spike-train-derived torque estimates could drive impedance control at 200 Hz with stable joint angle tracking (RMSE < 3.1°). Power consumption of the embedded module was 12.4 W during peak processing.

title: Fatigue-adaptive torque estimation during prolonged exoskeleton-assisted rehabilitation sessions
abstract: Muscle fatigue progressively alters EMG amplitude and spectral characteristics, causing static Hill model calibrations to accumulate torque estimation errors over time. This study examined how a median frequency shift-based fatigue index could be used to update Hill model activation dynamics coefficients online during 30-minute exoskeleton-assisted knee exercise sessions in ten subjects, five of whom were healthy controls and five were individuals with chronic stroke. The adaptive update rule used a first-order recursive estimator triggered when the median frequency of vastus lateralis EMG fell by more than 8% from the session baseline. With adaptation enabled, torque RMSE increased from 6.4 Nm at the start of sessions to only 7.9 Nm at the 30-minute mark, compared to 6.3 Nm to 13.1 Nm without adaptation. The stroke group showed faster fatigue onset (median frequency drop of 8% reached at 12 minutes vs. 21 minutes for controls).

title: Towards intent detection for upper-limb exoskeletons: elbow torque estimation from sparse sEMG during activities of daily living
abstract: Extending EMG-driven torque estimation to the elbow joint during unconstrained activities of daily living presents challenges not present in controlled isometric laboratory protocols. This work used a sparse four-electrode setup over biceps brachii, brachioradialis, triceps brachii long head, and anconeus to estimate elbow flexion-extension torques during ten standardised ADL tasks including pouring, lifting a 0.5 kg bottle, and reaching overhead. Sixteen subjects without neurological impairment participated. A Gaussian process regression model with automatic relevance determination was compared against a calibrated Hill model. The Gaussian process model achieved mean RMSE of 1.9 Nm across ADL tasks versus 2.7 Nm for the Hill model, with greatest improvement during the pouring task (1.4 vs. 2.9 Nm). The sparse electrode configuration is motivated by the commercial wearable constraint of minimising setup time in a clinical or home setting.

title: Feedforward Wind Compensation in PID-Controlled Quadrotor Hover Using a Pitot-Static Probe Array
abstract: The study investigates whether a compact three-probe Pitot-static array attached to a quadrotor landing gear can supply sufficient wind velocity information to improve hover position accuracy under low-frequency wind gusts. A 450 mm quadrotor was flown in a 5 × 5 m outdoor test area instrumented with a sonic anemometer reference mast. Wind speeds ranged from 1.5 to 7 m/s with gust frequencies below 0.4 Hz. Probe readings were fused with IMU data through a complementary filter with a crossover frequency of 0.8 Hz. The resulting wind estimate fed a feedforward roll and pitch compensation term added to a standard PID position loop. Root-mean-square horizontal position error fell from 0.41 m to 0.23 m in the 5–7 m/s regime compared to pure PID flight. Probe flow distortion from rotor downwash was characterised and partially corrected by a static lookup table. The paper discusses residual errors attributable to vertical wind components not captured by the horizontal probe array.

title: Anchor position optimisation for a reconfigurable CDPR serving multiple sequential positioning tasks
abstract: When a CDPR must serve a sequence of spatially distributed positioning tasks without manual re-anchoring, a fixed anchor layout must balance workspace coverage and tension feasibility across all tasks simultaneously. This paper formulates anchor placement as a mixed-integer nonlinear program, minimising the largest tension-to-limit ratio over all tasks and all cables in the sequence. A set of 15 representative industrial task sequences is used as a benchmark, each comprising between 8 and 24 target poses. The optimisation is solved using a genetic algorithm initialised from geometric heuristics, with a local interior-point refinement stage. For the benchmark set, optimised layouts achieve full wrench feasibility in 93% of tasks versus 61% for empirically chosen layouts. Computation times range from 4 to 28 minutes on a 16-core workstation. Sensitivity of the solution to ±10 mm anchor placement errors is evaluated and found to reduce feasibility coverage by at most 4 percentage points.

title: Energy-optimal rest-to-rest trajectories for CDPRs under variable regenerative braking efficiency
abstract: Motor drives in cable-driven parallel robots can recover energy during deceleration phases, but regenerative efficiency varies with speed and load current, affecting the true energy optimum. This paper incorporates a piecewise-linear regenerative efficiency model, fitted from drive datasheet measurements and confirmed by 40 braking experiments, into the direct collocation energy optimisation framework. Three drive configurations are tested: no regeneration, fixed 70% regeneration efficiency assumption, and the piecewise model. Across 24 test trajectories, using the piecewise model reduces predicted energy consumption error from 11.2% (fixed efficiency assumption) to 2.8% compared to measured values. Optimal trajectories shift peak velocity earlier in the motion profile to exploit higher regenerative efficiency at moderate deceleration currents. Total measured energy savings relative to trapezoidal profiles reach 38% for long-distance tasks and 14% for short-distance tasks under the piecewise model.

title: SMT-Based Feasibility Analysis for Fixed-Priority Scheduling on Single-Core Processors
abstract: This paper presents a formulation of fixed-priority preemptive scheduling feasibility as a satisfiability modulo theories problem over the theory of linear arithmetic. A set of periodic tasks with implicit deadlines is encoded as a conjunction of utilisation constraints and worst-case response-time inequalities. The encoding is fed to the Z3 solver, version 4.3, and compared against classical rate-monotonic analysis on a benchmark suite of 1 200 synthetically generated task sets, spanning utilisation levels from 0.5 to 0.98. The SMT approach correctly classifies all schedulable sets accepted by the classical test and additionally resolves 14.7 % of the indeterminate cases that the classical sufficient condition cannot decide. Solving time remains under 80 ms for task sets of up to 20 tasks on a standard desktop processor. The work establishes a baseline encoding that subsequent papers in this line of research extend to multiprocessor and mixed-criticality settings.

title: Constraint-Based Allocation of Mixed-Criticality Tasks to Partitioned Multiprocessors
abstract: Mixed-criticality task sets assign distinct levels of worst-case execution time (WCET) budgets to tasks depending on their assurance level. Allocating such tasks to a partitioned multiprocessor while preserving schedulability at each criticality mode transition is a combinatorial problem that grows intractable with naive enumeration. This paper models the allocation problem as a finite-domain constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) and solves it with a branch-and-bound search using arc-consistency propagation. Experiments use the WATERS 2015 automotive benchmark adapted to a dual-mode criticality model with two processors. For task sets of 40 tasks and four processors, the CSP approach finds valid allocations in under 3 seconds in 89 % of instances where an allocation exists, compared to a first-fit heuristic that fails to find allocations in 22 % of solvable instances. The paper also proves that the proposed constraint model is complete with respect to the adopted schedulability test.

title: Automated Synthesis of EDF-VD Scheduling Policies via Quantifier-Free Linear Arithmetic
abstract: Earliest-Deadline-First with Virtual Deadlines (EDF-VD) is a well-known scheduling policy for mixed-criticality systems that assigns tightened virtual deadlines to high-criticality tasks during low-criticality mode operation. Choosing the virtual deadline scaling factor has so far been done analytically for simple cases. This paper formulates the selection of per-task virtual deadline factors as a satisfiability query in quantifier-free linear arithmetic (QF-LIA), automatically synthesising a valid policy or reporting infeasibility. The approach handles arbitrary numbers of criticality levels and per-task deadline constraints. On a test suite of 600 task sets derived from the Emberson random task generator, the synthesis procedure yields valid scaling factors in 94 % of feasible instances within a two-second timeout per instance. A proof-of-concept implementation wraps the Z3 Python API and is released as an open-source repository. Synthesised policies are verified against a discrete-event simulation model written in SimPy.

title: Encoding Sporadic Task Models in SMT: Handling Minimum Inter-Arrival Times and Jitter
abstract: Most SMT-based schedulability analyses in the literature restrict attention to strictly periodic tasks. This paper extends the QF-LIA encoding to sporadic task models characterised by minimum inter-arrival times and bounded release jitter. The key technical contribution is a bounded hyperperiod unrolling technique that constructs a finite but sufficient task arrival sequence within an SMT instance. Correctness of the truncation bound is shown formally. The extended encoding is evaluated on a benchmark combining synthetic sporadic task sets with traces extracted from a CAN-bus communication log captured in a laboratory automotive gateway prototype running on an NXP S32K144 microcontroller. Results show that the extended encoding adds on average 37 % more SMT variables compared to the periodic model but still solves within a 500 ms budget for task sets of up to 30 tasks. The paper discusses the tradeoff between unrolling depth and completeness guarantees.

title: A Survey of Formal Methods for Scheduling in Mixed-Criticality Systems
abstract: This book chapter surveys formal and semi-formal methods applied to the scheduling and allocation problems in mixed-criticality systems from roughly 2010 to 2019. It organises the literature along three axes: the formalisms employed (SMT, timed automata, constraint programming, integer linear programming), the system models addressed (uniprocessor, partitioned multiprocessor, global multiprocessor, distributed), and the properties verified or synthesised (feasibility, policy parameters, allocation, mode-switch correctness). For each category, representative results are summarised with attention to scalability limits and tool support. The chapter identifies recurring patterns in how researchers encode criticality-level assumptions into formal models and highlights divergences in the treatment of mode-switch overhead, which is handled inconsistently across the literature. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems, particularly the lack of formal methods support for mixed-criticality systems with aperiodic server mechanisms and the challenge of integrating formal scheduling analysis with AUTOSAR configuration tools.

title: MaxSMT-Driven Optimisation of Worst-Case Response Times in Fixed-Priority Mixed-Criticality Scheduling
abstract: Beyond feasibility checking, system designers often want to minimise the maximum worst-case response time across a task set subject to schedulability constraints. This paper formulates that objective as a maximum satisfiability modulo theories (MaxSMT) problem, using soft clauses to encode the minimisation target alongside hard schedulability constraints in QF-LIA. The Z3 MaxSMT interface is used as the backend solver. On a benchmark of 400 mixed-criticality task sets generated at utilisation levels between 0.6 and 0.9, the MaxSMT approach reduces the maximum worst-case response time by 11 % on average compared to deadline-monotonic priority assignment, with solving times under 10 seconds for 25-task instances. The paper also evaluates partial MaxSMT relaxations that trade solution optimality for speed, obtaining near-optimal results in under 1 second for 80 % of instances. A case study on a simulated flight management data concentrator illustrates applicability.

title: Incremental SMT Solving for Online Admission Control in Mixed-Criticality Real-Time Systems
abstract: Offline synthesis of scheduling policies does not handle dynamic task arrival in mixed-criticality systems where aperiodic jobs must be admitted at runtime. This paper investigates whether incremental SMT solving can be used for online admission control, exploiting the ability of SMT solvers to add and retract assertions without full re-solving. A prototype admission controller is built on top of Z3's incremental API and evaluated on a soft real-time server model. Experiments run on an ARM Cortex-A53 embedded board with a preemptive Linux kernel patched with PREEMPT_RT. For task sets of up to 20 background periodic tasks and aperiodic job arrival rates up to 50 jobs per second, the incremental solver makes admission decisions within 2 ms in 97 % of cases. Comparison against a table-driven acceptance test shows that the SMT-based controller admits 8 % more jobs while maintaining zero deadline misses for high-criticality tasks across a 30-minute stress test.

title: Constraint Programming Models for Time-Triggered Schedule Synthesis with Mixed-Criticality Constraints
abstract: Time-triggered schedules assign each task a fixed dispatch time within a hyperperiod, eliminating runtime scheduling overhead at the cost of reduced flexibility. Synthesising such schedules under mixed-criticality requirements means finding dispatch times that satisfy both low-criticality and high-criticality timing requirements simultaneously, without mode switching. This paper models the problem as a constraint optimisation problem (COP) in MiniZinc, using global constraints including cumulative and all-different to prune the search space. The model is evaluated using the Chuffed and OR-Tools backends on a dataset of 300 task sets representative of automotive body-control module configurations, with hyperperiods up to 500 ms and 32 tasks. Chuffed finds optimal schedules for 81 % of instances within a 60-second limit. The paper analyses failure modes and shows that hyperperiod length, not task count, is the dominant factor in solver difficulty. Integration with a hardware-in-the-loop bench confirms that synthesised schedules execute correctly on target hardware.

title: Towards SMT-Based Synthesis of Mixed-Criticality Schedules for Multi-Core Automotive SoCs with Shared Memory Contention
abstract: Modern automotive system-on-chips expose multi-core processors sharing last-level cache and DRAM, introducing memory access latency variability that invalidates WCETs derived for isolated cores. This preprint extends the SMT-based scheduling synthesis framework from prior work to account for memory contention by incorporating contention-aware WCET inflation factors derived from measurement-based analysis on a Renesas RH850-class evaluation board. The inflated WCETs are parameterised by a contention coefficient modelled as a real-valued SMT variable bounded by empirical measurements. The solver then synthesises priority assignments and core affinities simultaneously. Preliminary results on 50 task sets show that ignoring contention leads to deadline misses in high-criticality tasks in 18 % of cases at 85 % utilisation, whereas contention-aware synthesis avoids such misses at the cost of a 6 % utilisation reduction. The work is ongoing; a full evaluation with formal correctness arguments is in preparation.

title: Integracija animacije lica pokretane govorom u sistem za e-učenje sa virtuelnim asistentom
abstract: Ovaj rad opisuje tehničku integraciju sistema za animaciju lica pokretanog govorom u platformu za e-učenje sa virtuelnim nastavničkim asistentom. Arhitektura sistema sastoji se od TTS modula, fonetskog alaignera, seq2seq modela za generisanje vizem trajektorija i WebGL renderera koji prikazuje animiranog lika u pregledaču bez dodatnih dodataka. Merenja na mreži od 40 Mbit/s pokazala su prosečno kašnjenje od 180 ms od unosa teksta do početka animacije na stranici, što je ispod praga koji korisnici percipiraju kao neprihvatljiv (>300 ms prema literaturnim izvorima). Sistem je testiran u pilot studiji sa 94 studenta na Fakultetu tehničkih nauka tokom jednog semestra. Anketni upitnik pokazao je da 78% studenata smatra da animirani asistent poboljšava razumevanje materijala u poređenju sa tekstualnim ili audio-samo modalitetom. Tehničke poteškoće vezane za sinhronizaciju audio-vizuelnih kanala, posebno na mobilnim uređajima, detaljno su opisane.

title: Soiling Rate Estimation on Utility-Scale PV Panels via Piecewise Linear Segmentation of Cleaned Irradiance-Normalised Output
abstract: Soiling of photovoltaic panels reduces energy yield in a gradual, weather-dependent manner that is difficult to separate from other sources of degradation. This study applies piecewise linear segmentation to daily cleaned irradiance-normalised DC output records from a 1.1 MWp park monitored over 27 months. Rain events identified in co-located meteorological station data were used as natural cleaning markers, enabling segment-wise soiling rate estimation. Rates ranged from 0.04 % to 0.31 % per day depending on season and prevailing wind direction, consistent with dust transport patterns documented for the Pannonian plain. The method requires no additional soiling sensors and can be applied retrospectively to existing SCADA archives. Comparison with a reference clean-string approach showed mean absolute error below 0.09 % per day, demonstrating suitability for operational use.

title: Scheduling Dependent Task Graphs with Shared Peripherals on Multi-Core Microcontrollers: An ILP Approach
abstract: Many embedded control applications express their computation as directed acyclic task graphs (DAGs) where nodes represent computation phases and edges encode data dependencies and shared peripheral access sequences (SPI, I2C, UART). This paper formulates the problem of scheduling such DAGs on a dual-core STM32H7 microcontroller as a mixed-integer linear programme that jointly models core assignment, execution order, and peripheral arbitration. A symmetry-breaking constraint set reduces solution space by a factor of up to 4.8 on symmetric DAGs. Experiments used 12 control application DAGs collected from open-source embedded projects, ranging from 8 to 47 nodes. The ILP produced valid schedules with average hyperperiod makespan 11% below a list-scheduling baseline. Peripheral contention accounted for 19–34% of total schedule length, motivating the joint treatment of computation and peripheral arbitration. The paper discusses how the formulation extends to three or more cores.

title: Calcium carbonate nucleation on sodium stearate surfaces during exposure to humid CO2-enriched atmosphere
abstract: Pressed sodium stearate pellets with controlled residual NaOH content (0.5–3.0 wt%) were exposed to atmospheres containing 0.04–5.0 vol% CO2 at relative humidities between 40 and 85% in a custom flow-through chamber. Surface carbonate accumulation was monitored gravimetrically and by FTIR at 12 h intervals over 30 days. Calcite was identified as the dominant polymorph by XRD at all CO2 concentrations tested; vaterite appeared as a transient phase only at humidity above 75% and CO2 above 2 vol%. Nucleation induction periods ranged from 18 h at high NaOH and high humidity to over 120 h at the lowest alkali loading. SEM images showed rhombohedral calcite crystals with mean diameter 4.2 µm after 30 days under standard conditions. A first-order rate expression with respect to dissolved carbonate ion activity described the growth data with R² = 0.94. The results indicate that residual alkali content is the principal factor controlling induction time, while humidity governs crystal habit.

title: Magnesium carbonate formation in potassium soap systems containing dolomitic hard water residues
abstract: Laboratory saponification of palm kernel oil was carried out using KOH solutions prepared from deionised water and from synthetic hard water containing 180 mg L⁻¹ Ca²⁺ and 95 mg L⁻¹ Mg²⁺ representative of Vojvodina tap water composition. Finished soap samples were stored at 25 °C and 65% RH for 90 days. XRD and SEM-EDS characterisation of surface precipitates showed that hard-water-derived soaps accumulated both calcite and hydromagnesite (Mg₅(CO₃)₄(OH)₂·4H₂O) in a 3:1 molar ratio, while deionised-water soaps produced only calcite. Hydromagnesite crystals appeared as rosette-shaped aggregates 8–15 µm in diameter. Total carbonate on hard-water soap surfaces was 37% higher after 90 days. Titration of remaining Mg in the bulk soap phase indicated 82% incorporation efficiency into surface precipitates. The results highlight a regional water quality factor relevant to soap manufacturers operating in carbonate-rich aquifer areas.

title: Surface chemistry of fatty acid salts: a chapter on alkali–CO2 interactions and ageing phenomena
abstract: This book chapter reviews the physical chemistry of sodium and potassium fatty acid salt surfaces from synthesis through storage, with emphasis on the reactions of residual alkaline phases with atmospheric carbon dioxide. Coverage includes thermodynamic stability fields for carbonate polymorphs relevant to soap matrices, kinetic data from the literature and from the author's laboratory spanning 2003–2015, the influence of humidity and temperature on reaction rates, and analytical methods used to characterise carbonate deposits. Particular attention is given to the distinction between surface carbonation, bulk carbonation, and rancidity as competing ageing pathways. The chapter also addresses implications for product quality standards (ISO 685 free alkali determination) and suggests approaches for extending shelf stability without altering the fatty acid composition of the final product.

title: Raman spectroscopic mapping of carbonate polymorph distribution across a soap bar cross-section
abstract: Cross-sections of sodium soap bars with 1.5 wt% excess NaOH, aged for 6, 12, and 24 months under 60% RH and 20 °C, were examined by confocal Raman mapping at 2 µm spatial resolution using a 532 nm laser. Maps of 500 × 500 µm areas at three depths (0–50, 200–250, and 500–550 µm) showed calcite as the exclusive carbonate phase at the surface layer, with the ν₁ band centred at 1085 cm⁻¹. At 200–250 µm depth, vaterite (characteristic doublet at 1074 and 1090 cm⁻¹) constituted up to 18% of carbonate signal at 24 months. No carbonate signal was detected below 400 µm even after 24 months. Carbonate area fraction at 0–50 µm rose from 3% at 6 months to 31% at 24 months. The Raman mapping approach provides spatially resolved polymorph information not accessible by bulk XRD and clarifies the layered carbonation mechanism in commercial soap matrices.

title: CO2 partial pressure and temperature coupling in controlling vaterite-to-calcite transformation in soap film systems
abstract: Thin films of sodium oleate–stearate mixed soap (40:60 molar ratio) containing 2 wt% excess NaOH were cast on glass substrates and aged in environmental chambers with CO2 partial pressures of 0.04, 0.2, 0.5, and 1.0 kPa and temperatures of 10, 25, and 40 °C. Phase identification by XRD at 24 h intervals over 21 days tracked vaterite and calcite proportions. At 25 °C and 0.04 kPa CO2, vaterite persisted for 14 days before transforming to calcite; at 1.0 kPa CO2 and 40 °C the transformation was complete within 48 h. A kinetic phase diagram constructed from the transition half-times shows a clear boundary between vaterite-persistence and calcite-dominant regions. The Avrami exponent derived from isothermal transformation curves ranged from 1.8 to 2.4, consistent with a surface-nucleation-controlled mechanism. The findings help explain batch-to-batch polymorph variability in industrial soap powders stored at different altitudes or in climate-controlled warehouses.

title: Quantifying free alkali gradients in soap bars by micro-titration of sequential surface layers
abstract: A micro-titration protocol was developed to determine free NaOH concentration at controlled depth increments of 100 µm in soap bar cross-sections. Material was removed by a precision lathe fitted with a collection hood; each 100 µm layer was dissolved in ethanol–water (50:50 v/v) and titrated against 0.01 M HCl with potentiometric endpoint detection. Applied to bars with nominal 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 wt% total free alkali stored for 0, 6, and 12 months at 60% RH, the method revealed steep alkali gradients with surface depletion reaching 400 µm depth after 12 months. Surface-layer alkali declined by 70–90% due to carbonation, while bulk alkali dropped by only 10–15%. Repeatability expressed as RSD was below 4% for all layers except the outermost, where surface roughness contributed higher variability. The protocol offers a straightforward quality-control tool requiring only standard laboratory equipment.

title: Interaction of biogenic amine contaminants from rancidity with carbonate precipitate surfaces in aged soap
abstract: Soap bars prepared from partially oxidised tallow (peroxide value 12 meq kg⁻¹) and fresh tallow (peroxide value 0.4 meq kg⁻¹) were saponified identically and aged for 24 months. GC-MS headspace analysis showed putrescine and cadaverine in oxidised-tallow bars at 0.8 and 0.4 µg g⁻¹ respectively, absent in fresh-tallow bars. FTIR of carbonate crusts from oxidised-tallow bars showed N–H deformation bands at 1540 cm⁻¹ not present in control bars, suggesting amine adsorption onto carbonate crystal surfaces. BET surface area of carbonate material from oxidised bars was 20% lower, consistent with partial pore blocking by adsorbed organics. Amine loading on carbonate surfaces estimated by TGA was 0.9 mg g⁻¹. Although this interaction does not alter carbonate polymorph, it affects the sensory properties of the crust and may complicate titrimetric free-alkali determination by neutralising a fraction of the surface acid.

title: Carbonate precipitation inhibition by citrate and tartrate additives in sodium soap formulations: a comparison of inhibition mechanisms
abstract: Sodium stearate formulations containing 0, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 wt% sodium citrate or sodium tartrate were cast as standard bars with 1.5 wt% free NaOH and aged at 25 °C, 65% RH for 120 days. Carbonate accumulation measured by periodic acid digestion showed 60% reduction in total carbonate at 2 wt% citrate and 42% reduction at 2 wt% tartrate relative to additive-free controls. Zeta potential measurements of nucleated carbonate particles in aqueous suspension indicated stronger negative charge with citrate (−38 mV) than with tartrate (−27 mV) at equivalent loadings, consistent with greater adsorption of citrate onto calcite growth sites. AFM force curves on calcite cleavage surfaces in citrate solution showed a repulsive steric layer of 3.2 nm not observed with tartrate. Crystal size distributions by laser diffraction were broader and mean size larger with both additives compared with controls, consistent with nucleation inhibition rather than growth inhibition as the dominant mechanism for citrate, and growth rate reduction for tartrate.

title: Scale-up of a visible-light photocatalytic reactor for azo dye treatment: from 0.5 L batch to 10 L recirculating annular design
abstract: A 10 L recirculating annular photoreactor was designed, constructed, and evaluated using 30 wt% BiVO₄/TiO₂ immobilised on borosilicate glass rings as the catalyst support. Catalyst immobilisation was achieved by dip-coating followed by calcination at 350 °C, yielding a film thickness of approximately 3.2 µm confirmed by SEM cross-section. Light source comprised four 24 W visible-LED strips (peak emission 460 nm) arranged around the annulus. For Reactive Red 195 at 30 mg L⁻¹ and a flow rate of 2 L min⁻¹, 80% colour removal was achieved after 4 hours of recirculation, compared to 95% in the 0.5 L batch system under equivalent photon flux. Pressure drop across the packed bed was 0.8 kPa. Energy consumption analysis gave 42 kWh per kg COD removed, which is discussed in comparison with published figures for UV-based advanced oxidation processes.

title: Fine-tuning Multilingual BERT Variants for Disease Named Entity Recognition in Serbian Biomedical Text
abstract: Transformer-based language models pre-trained on multilingual corpora have shown strong transfer performance to low-resource languages, but their behaviour on morphologically rich South Slavic languages in the biomedical domain remains understudied. This study systematically compares four publicly available multilingual transformer models—including a generic multilingual checkpoint and two models with partial Serbian training data—on disease named entity recognition using the SerbioNER corpus introduced in prior work. Models were fine-tuned with five random seeds and evaluated using strict and partial span-matching F1. The best-performing model, a multilingual model with continued pre-training on a 2.1-billion-token Serbian web corpus, achieved a strict F1 of 0.79 on the disease category, representing a gain of ten percentage points over the CRF baseline. Error analysis showed that the majority of remaining errors involve entity boundaries at morphological suffixes and multi-word expressions denoting disease subtypes. Experiments also tested zero-shot transfer to a small Bosnian test set, where F1 dropped to 0.61, indicating that cross-lingual transfer within the South Slavic cluster is non-trivial without further adaptation. All fine-tuned model weights are made available through a public model repository.

title: Cross-lingual Weak Supervision for Gene Mention Detection Across South Slavic Languages
abstract: Gene mention detection in biomedical text is challenging in South Slavic languages because annotated training data are scarce and gene nomenclature is frequently borrowed from English without consistent morphological adaptation. This paper investigates whether weak supervision derived from automatic translation of English gold-standard gene mention datasets can improve a Serbian and Croatian gene detection model. We translate three English gene mention datasets using a neural machine translation system and project entity labels via word alignment, producing weakly labelled training sets of approximately 18,000 sentences per language. A sequence labelling model trained on this weakly labelled data and fine-tuned on 500 manually annotated Serbian sentences achieves an F1 of 0.71 on a Serbian test set, compared to 0.58 for the same model trained only on manual annotations. We additionally evaluate on a Croatian test set of 300 sentences collected from open-access veterinary journals, obtaining F1 of 0.65 without any Croatian-specific fine-tuning. Analysis of projection errors shows that inflected gene name forms account for 38% of alignment failures. The results suggest that projection-based weak supervision is a viable low-cost strategy for expanding gene NER to related languages in this cluster.

title: A Lightweight Pipeline for Extracting Drug–Disease Relations from Serbian Clinical Case Reports
abstract: Relation extraction between biomedical entities in low-resource languages is typically approached by adapting English-trained models, but direct adaptation is complicated by the absence of parallel corpora and the syntactic differences of inflected languages. This preprint describes a lightweight relation extraction pipeline applied to a set of 620 Serbian clinical case reports collected from three open-access Serbian medical journals between 2015 and 2025. The pipeline uses the disease and gene named entity recogniser developed in prior work, extended here with a drug entity module trained on a manually annotated set of 300 sentences. Candidate drug–disease pairs are classified using a support vector machine over typed dependency features extracted from a Serbian dependency parser. The approach avoids large model fine-tuning and can run on CPU hardware. On a held-out set of 80 case reports, the pipeline identifies drug–disease treatment relations with a precision of 0.72 and recall of 0.61. Error analysis indicates that the main precision losses arise from non-treatment drug mentions such as contraindications mentioned in passing. The code and evaluation data are shared as a preprint to invite community feedback before journal submission.

title: Change-point detection in engine load profiles of field sprayers using BOCPD
abstract: Bayesian online change-point detection (BOCPD) is applied to univariate and multivariate engine load time-series recorded from self-propelled field sprayers during pesticide application campaigns. Fourteen sprayers from five farms in Serbia and Hungary contributed 880 hours of CAN-bus logs over one growing season. A hazard rate of 1/200 time steps and a Student-t predictive distribution were used; hyperparameters were estimated from a held-out calibration set. The algorithm identified 94% of manually annotated load-regime transitions with a median detection lag of 2.3 seconds. A secondary analysis assessed whether abrupt load changes correlate with approaching pump cavitation events: of 23 documented cavitation incidents, 17 were preceded by a statistically significant change point in the pump pressure channel within a 90-second window. The remaining 6 incidents showed only gradual pressure decay captured better by drift detectors. These results suggest that BOCPD is well suited to segmenting operational regimes, while complementary drift-detection layers are needed for slowly evolving faults.

title: Combining mRNA Expression and DNA Methylation for Prognosis in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Using Regularised Multi-Block Cox Models
abstract: mRNA expression (Illumina HiSeq, 20,531 genes) and 450K DNA methylation data from 478 NSCLC patients were integrated within a multi-block elastic net Cox framework. Three data-fusion strategies were compared: early concatenation, a two-step filtering-then-concatenation approach, and a block-weighted penalisation scheme. The primary endpoint was overall survival; competing cause of death was modelled separately. After 50-iteration Monte Carlo cross-validation, the block-weighted scheme achieved the best C-index (0.69 ± 0.03) and the lowest calibration error at 2 years. The expression block contributed 27 retained features versus 14 from the methylation block. Methylation sites near the CDKN2A promoter appeared in over 90% of cross-validation folds, suggesting consistent prognostic relevance. The study used publicly available TCGA NSCLC data supplemented with a 96-patient validation set from the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina.

title: Comparative assessment of spray drying and extrusion for microencapsulation of a mixed Lactobacillus culture: survival and release behaviour in simulated intestinal fluid

Spray-dried powders had a mean particle size of 18.4 µm and water activity of 0.22; extrusion capsules averaged 1.6 mm diameter. Encapsulation efficiencies were 87% and 95%, respectively. Both products were subjected to sequential exposure at pH 2.0 for 2 hours then pH 6.8 with pancreatin for 2 hours. Extruded capsules released 78% of viable cells in intestinal phase, compared with 61% for spray-dried powders. However, spray-dried powders showed superior storage stability at 4 °C over 16 weeks (loss of 0.8 log CFU/g versus 1.4 log CFU/g). Trade-offs between scalability, release profile, and storage stability are discussed with reference to potential product applications.

title: Influence of cold-chain interruption cycles on the viability of encapsulated Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus in commercial-style yoghurt

Products were subjected to simulated cold-chain interruptions consisting of repeated temperature excursions from 4 °C to 15 °C for 4 hours, applied every 48 hours over a 28-day shelf life. Viable counts were determined by fluorescence in situ hybridisation combined with flow cytometry to distinguish live from membrane-compromised cells. After four interruption cycles, encapsulated cells maintained 7.2 log CFU/g, while free cells in an identical yoghurt matrix dropped to 5.8 log CFU/g. Texture profile analysis and syneresis measurements confirmed that capsule addition did not negatively affect gel strength (p > 0.05). pH evolution profiles were similar across treatments, indicating that capsule presence did not alter fermentation dynamics during the storage period.

title: Effect of sucrose and trehalose as cryoprotectants on survival of freeze-dried Lactobacillus fermentum during storage at two temperatures
abstract: Lactobacillus fermentum NRRL B-1932 was freeze-dried with 5% and 10% (w/v) sucrose or trehalose added prior to freezing at −80 °C. Residual moisture content after lyophilisation ranged from 1.8% to 3.4% across treatments. Samples were stored in sealed foil pouches at 4 °C and 25 °C for up to 24 weeks. Survival was assessed by plate counting on MRS agar every 4 weeks. At 4 °C, trehalose at 10% w/v provided the best protection, with 89% survival at 24 weeks; sucrose at 10% gave 76% survival. At 25 °C, all treatments showed more pronounced decline, with trehalose 10% retaining only 54% viability at 24 weeks. Differential scanning calorimetry indicated glass transition temperatures (Tg) of 47–53 °C for trehalose formulations and 41–46 °C for sucrose, consistent with the observed stability differences. Practical recommendations are made for dried probiotic ingredient storage logistics.

title: Microencapsulation of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum in whey protein–inulin double-layer coatings prepared by fluidised-bed coating
abstract: A fluidised-bed coating process was used to apply a two-layer shell comprising an inner whey protein isolate layer and an outer inulin layer onto spray-dried L. plantarum powder particles. Process parameters evaluated included coating temperature (30 and 40 °C), airflow rate (30 and 45 m³/h), and spray rate (5 and 10 g/min). Particle size distribution (D50 = 28 µm) and moisture content (2.1% w/w) were characterised by laser diffraction and Karl Fischer titration, respectively. Encapsulation efficiency reached 91% under optimal conditions. Coated particles stored at 4 °C for 20 weeks showed a mean loss of 0.6 log CFU/g compared with 1.9 log CFU/g for uncoated spray-dried powder. Exposure to pH 2.5 for 120 minutes resulted in 6.3 log CFU/g survival for double-coated particles versus 4.1 log CFU/g for uncoated controls. The synbiotic character of the inulin-containing shell is discussed briefly in the context of potential functional food applications.

title: pH-dependent survival modelling of encapsulated probiotic blends using modified Weibull and biphasic linear inactivation models
abstract: Survival data for three commercial probiotic strains (L. acidophilus, L. rhamnosus, B. animalis) encapsulated in alginate–pectin matrices were collected over a pH range of 1.8 to 5.0 in citrate–phosphate buffer at 37 °C over 180 minutes. Survival curves were fitted to the Weibull model, the biphasic linear inactivation model, and a log-linear model with shoulder. Goodness of fit was assessed by root mean square error and the Akaike information criterion. The Weibull model provided the best fit for all three strains across most pH levels, with shape parameters (β) below 1.0 at pH values under 2.5, indicating concave survival curves typical of non-log-linear inactivation. Encapsulation consistently shifted D-values upward by a factor of 1.8 to 3.4 relative to free cells. Model parameters are presented as functions of pH to enable incorporation into predictive inactivation frameworks for product formulation. Limitations of extrapolating buffer-based models to complex food matrices are discussed.

title: Survival of encapsulated Bifidobacterium animalis in plant-based fermented beverages under refrigerated storage: comparison of oat and soy matrices
abstract: Oat-base and soy-base fermented beverages were prepared using a standardised fermentation protocol with Streptococcus thermophilus as primary fermenter. Bifidobacterium animalis Bb-12 encapsulated in alginate–carrageenan beads (2.0 mm mean diameter) was added post-fermentation at approximately 8.5 log CFU/mL. Products were stored at 4 °C for 21 days. Viable counts of B. animalis were monitored every 3 days by selective enumeration on MRS-NNLP agar. In the oat matrix, viable counts declined from 8.4 to 7.1 log CFU/mL; in the soy matrix the decline was from 8.5 to 6.6 log CFU/mL. pH profiles, titratable acidity, and dissolved oxygen were measured in parallel. Higher residual dissolved oxygen in the soy matrix (0.8 mg/L versus 0.3 mg/L in oat) was identified as a likely contributing factor to greater B. animalis loss. Sensory evaluation by a trained panel of twelve found no significant difference in texture or flavour attributable to bead presence.

title: Metabolic footprint analysis of Aspergillus niger during protease yield decline in repeated-batch submerged fermentation
abstract: A repeated-batch fermentation process for alkaline protease production using Aspergillus niger was operated over 12 consecutive batches in 5 L stirred-tank bioreactors. Protease activity in the harvest broth fell from 342 U/mL in batch 1 to 198 U/mL in batch 12, representing a 42% decline. Spent broth samples from each batch were profiled by HPLC-DAD for organic acids, amino acids, and sugar alcohols. Principal component analysis separated batches 1–4, 5–8, and 9–12 into distinct metabolic groups. Accumulation of gluconic acid (rising from 0.8 g/L to 4.1 g/L across batches) and concurrent depletion of free glutamate were the strongest discriminating variables. Spore morphology by light microscopy showed progressive conidiophore shortening correlating with gluconic acid concentration. The data suggest that acid accumulation combined with nitrogen recycling inefficiency drives the observed yield trajectory.

title: Seasonal variability of sunflower head silage quality and its consequences for biogas reactor stability: a one-year monitoring study
abstract: Sunflower heads harvested at four points across two growing seasons in Vojvodina were ensiled and characterised for dry matter, crude protein, neutral detergent fibre, and fermentation acids. VS content varied from 88.2% to 94.7% DM and crude protein from 7.1% to 11.4% DM, producing C/N ratios between 24 and 39 across batches. BMP tests per batch showed methane yields ranging from 221 to 298 mL CH4/g VS. A 2 L fed-batch reactor operated continuously for 12 months at constant OLR using seasonally alternating batches exhibited three periods of pH instability (pH drops to 6.6–6.8) coinciding with transitions to high-fibre batches. Real-time VFA:alkalinity monitoring successfully predicted two out of three instability events 4–6 days in advance. The study provides a practical substrate characterisation protocol for farm-scale biogas plants relying on sunflower by-products in the region.

title: Gastric emptying rate as a determinant of metformin peak plasma concentration in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetic patients
abstract: Metformin absorption is confined largely to the proximal small intestine, making gastric emptying a potential rate-limiting step. In this cross-sectional study, 38 patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes (mean HbA1c 7.4%) underwent a standardised 13C-octanoic acid breath test to estimate gastric half-emptying time (t½GE) and received a single 500 mg metformin dose under fasting conditions. Serial venous samples were collected over 10 hours. Non-compartmental analysis yielded Cmax values ranging from 0.41 to 1.87 µg/mL. Pearson correlation between t½GE and Cmax was −0.62 (p < 0.001), and t½GE explained 36% of Cmax variance in linear regression after adjusting for body mass index and creatinine clearance. AUC0–10 h showed a weaker but significant negative correlation (r = −0.44, p = 0.006). These results suggest that slowed gastric emptying, even before clinically overt gastroparesis, meaningfully reduces metformin peak exposure and may partly explain early treatment failures.

title: Comparison of two population pharmacokinetic models for gliclazide modified-release in patients with and without diabetic autonomic neuropathy
abstract: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy (DAN) affects gastrointestinal transit and may alter the release and absorption of modified-release (MR) oral formulations. We developed and compared two population pharmacokinetic models for gliclazide 60 mg MR tablets using NONMEM v7.3 in 52 type 2 diabetic patients (26 with confirmed DAN by cardiovascular reflex tests, 26 controls matched for age, sex and eGFR). A one-compartment model with a lag-time absorption function and a transit-compartment absorption model were evaluated. The transit-compartment model provided a significantly better fit (ΔOFV = −18.4, p < 0.001). In the DAN subgroup, the mean transit time was 1.8-fold longer (3.4 vs. 1.9 h) and estimated ka was 34% lower. Inter-individual variability in ka was 61% in DAN patients versus 38% in controls. Simulations indicated that 22% of DAN patients would not achieve target plasma concentrations above 0.8 µg/mL for the first 4 hours post-dose, compared with 6% of controls.

title: Variability in oral sitagliptin pharmacokinetics in type 2 diabetic patients undergoing Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy
abstract: Helicobacter pylori eradication regimens combining a proton pump inhibitor with two antibiotics can transiently alter gastric acid secretion and intestinal motility. We investigated whether a standard 14-day triple-therapy regimen (omeprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin 1 g, clarithromycin 500 mg, twice daily) modified sitagliptin 100 mg/day pharmacokinetics in 24 type 2 diabetic patients in an open-label, two-period pharmacokinetic study (treatment vs. 6-week washout). AUC0–24 h for sitagliptin increased by a mean of 18% during eradication (95% CI: 9–28%; p = 0.002), attributable largely to clarithromycin-mediated inhibition of intestinal CYP3A4 and P-gp. Renal clearance of sitagliptin was unaffected. Gastric half-emptying time measured by scintigraphy shortened by 14 min on average during the eradication period, a change that correlated positively with Cmax increase (r = 0.48). No serious hypoglycaemic events were recorded, but three patients exhibited glucose levels below 4.0 mmol/L. Dose adjustment guidance during H. pylori eradication in diabetic patients is discussed.

title: Effect of acute hyperglycaemia on intestinal permeability and oral bioavailability of atenolol in healthy volunteers: a pilot study
abstract: Hyperglycaemia acutely modifies gastrointestinal motility and may affect the absorption of drugs that are transported by intestinal epithelial mechanisms. Atenolol, a hydrophilic beta-blocker largely absorbed by paracellular transport, was selected as a model compound. Twelve healthy male volunteers (aged 22–35 years) participated in a randomised crossover experiment: a euglycaemic clamp (blood glucose ~5 mmol/L) and a hyperglycaemic clamp (~12 mmol/L), each followed by a single 50 mg oral atenolol dose. Plasma samples were collected over 24 hours and quantified by validated LC-MS/MS. Under hyperglycaemia, atenolol Cmax fell by 21% (p = 0.03) and tmax was prolonged by 40 minutes on average. AUC0–∞ was reduced by 15% (p = 0.06, borderline). Lactulose/mannitol ratio measured in 6-hour urine collections did not differ between conditions, suggesting paracellular tight-junction permeability was not the primary mechanism. Concurrent gastric scintigraphy indicated delayed gastric emptying under hyperglycaemia as the more likely explanation. Sample size limitations preclude firm conclusions.

title: Oral absorption of rosuvastatin in type 2 diabetic patients with different degrees of gastroparesis assessed by wireless motility capsule
abstract: Statins are commonly prescribed alongside antidiabetics, yet the interaction between diabetic gastroparesis severity and statin absorption is poorly characterised. Sixty type 2 diabetic patients were stratified by wireless motility capsule (WMC) into no gastroparesis (n = 22), mild gastroparesis (gastric residence time 5–8 h; n = 21), and moderate gastroparesis (>8 h; n = 17). Each patient received a single 20 mg rosuvastatin dose under standardised low-fat breakfast conditions; plasma rosuvastatin and the active metabolite N-desmethyl rosuvastatin were quantified by LC-MS/MS at 12 time points over 24 hours. Cmax decreased progressively across gastroparesis categories (geometric means: 7.8, 5.9, 4.2 ng/mL; ANOVA p < 0.001). AUC0–24 h differences were smaller and not statistically significant across categories (p = 0.11). OATP1B1 genotyping (SLCO1B1 c.521T>C) was performed; the effect of gastroparesis on Cmax was present in both genotype groups. LDL-C response at 4 weeks showed a trend toward attenuation in moderate gastroparesis, though the study was not powered for clinical endpoints. This dataset supports further investigation of dose-timing strategies in this population.

title: Dietary fibre composition and its short-term effect on GLP-1 receptor agonist subcutaneous absorption: a secondary pharmacokinetic analysis
abstract: Although GLP-1 receptor agonists are administered subcutaneously, their pharmacodynamic action on gastric emptying indirectly modulates the absorption of co-administered oral medications. This secondary analysis used pharmacokinetic data collected within a 12-week dietary intervention trial comparing high-soluble-fibre (HSF) and standard diets in 44 type 2 diabetic patients on stable semaglutide 0.5 mg/week. Oral pharmacokinetics of concomitant metformin 1000 mg and linagliptin 5 mg were assessed at weeks 0, 6, and 12. In the HSF group, metformin AUC0–8 h increased by 12% from baseline to week 6 (p = 0.04) while linagliptin Cmax decreased by 9% (p = 0.09, not significant). Changes in gastric half-emptying time estimated by the 13C-breath test correlated inversely with metformin Cmax changes (r = −0.51). The HSF diet also altered gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), and bacterial richness index correlated with tmax changes for both drugs, though causality cannot be established from these data. Findings highlight the pharmacokinetic relevance of dietary context in patients receiving GLP-1 receptor agonists.

title: A Double-Auction Clearing Mechanism for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading in Low-Voltage Residential Microgrids
abstract: This paper proposes a sealed-bid double-auction mechanism for clearing energy trades among prosumers connected to a single low-voltage feeder. The mechanism operates in fifteen-minute intervals and uses a uniform-price clearing rule derived from aggregate supply and demand curves constructed from individual prosumer bids. Individual rationality, budget balance, and incentive compatibility under quasi-linear preferences are analysed formally. Simulations are performed on a synthetic neighbourhood of 48 residential prosumers—each modelled with rooftop photovoltaic generation between 3 and 8 kWp, a battery storage unit of 5–10 kWh, and a flexible load profile drawn from a publicly available Austrian household dataset. The clearing algorithm runs in O(n log n) time. Results show that average prosumer surplus increases by 18.4% relative to a net-metering baseline, while the distribution network operator's congestion event frequency drops by 31% over a simulated 90-day period. The mechanism is implemented in Python and validated against a DIgSILENT PowerFactory network model of the test feeder.

title: Strategic Bidding Behaviour of Battery-Owning Prosumers in a Local Energy Market: A Simulation Study
abstract: Prosumers who own battery storage systems can time-shift energy to manipulate clearing prices in local auction markets. This paper investigates the extent of such strategic behaviour using an agent-based simulation in which a subset of prosumers follows best-response bidding strategies while others bid truthfully. The test case consists of 60 prosumers on a simulated feeder in northern Serbia, parameterised with load and generation profiles collected from a pilot project at an industrial park in Subotica. Three market formats are compared: pay-as-bid, uniform-price, and McAfee's double auction. Convergence to Nash equilibrium is tracked over 500 repeated auction rounds using fictitious play. The uniform-price format is found to be most robust to strategic manipulation, with price deviation from the competitive equilibrium remaining below 4.2% even when 30% of agents play strategically. Pay-as-bid shows the largest welfare loss under the same conditions, approximately 11.7% relative to the social optimum. Implications for market rule design at the distribution level are discussed.

title: Incentive-Compatible Demand Response Contracts for Aggregators in Distribution Grids: A Mechanism Design Perspective
abstract: Aggregators coordinating groups of flexible residential loads face an adverse selection problem: consumers have private information about their true flexibility cost. This paper models the aggregator–consumer relationship as a principal–agent mechanism design problem and derives a family of direct revelation mechanisms that are incentive-compatible and individually rational. The theoretical framework builds on Myerson's optimal mechanism, adapted to the discrete flexibility levels typical of residential appliances such as heat pumps and electric vehicle chargers. A stylised numerical example calibrated to data from a 120-apartment building in Novi Sad illustrates the trade-off between aggregator revenue and consumer participation rate as a function of the assumed distribution of flexibility costs. Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis over 10,000 parameter draws shows that the optimal mechanism achieves 89–94% of the first-best welfare surplus across the tested parameter space. The paper also discusses implementation constraints arising from European regulatory requirements on consumer data access and contract transparency under the Clean Energy for All Europeans package.
