title: Comparison of Bilateral and Auction-Based Trading Protocols for Prosumer Microgrids Under Communication Delay
abstract: Real-time energy trading platforms in low-voltage microgrids must account for communication latency between smart meters, edge controllers, and the market clearing server. This paper evaluates three trading protocols—continuous double auction, periodic call auction, and bilateral contract negotiation—under varying communication delay scenarios ranging from 50 ms to 2 s, using a hardware-in-the-loop testbed built around a Raspberry Pi cluster at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. A microgrid of 24 prosumers is emulated with real-time power flow computed in MATLAB/Simulink. Key metrics are clearing efficiency, price volatility, and the frequency of physically infeasible cleared trades that would require curtailment. Results indicate that the periodic call auction with a fifteen-minute clearing window is the least sensitive to communication delay, maintaining clearing efficiency above 95% across all tested delay levels. The continuous double auction degrades substantially above 500 ms delay, dropping to 81% clearing efficiency and producing a threefold increase in curtailment events. Bilateral negotiation shows intermediate performance but higher implementation complexity.

title: Truthfulness and Efficiency in Multi-Unit Auctions for Local Flexibility Markets: A Preliminary Analysis
abstract: This preprint examines multi-unit auction formats applicable to local flexibility markets where distribution system operators procure upward and downward flexibility from aggregated prosumer pools. The focus is on the tension between computational tractability and theoretical properties such as truthfulness and allocative efficiency in the multi-unit setting. The VCG mechanism and several approximation variants are benchmarked on randomly generated flexibility request instances of size 10 to 200 units using both exact integer programming and a greedy heuristic. For instances with up to 50 units, the exact VCG implementation runs in under 200 ms on a standard desktop, which is within the window of practical use for fifteen-minute markets. The greedy heuristic achieves 96.3% of optimal social welfare on average across 1,000 random instances while running two orders of magnitude faster. The paper frames open questions regarding combinatorial bids and network constraints as directions for the author's ongoing PhD work.

title: Graph-Neural-Network-Assisted VNF Migration Scheduling in SD-WAN with Dynamic Link Failures
abstract: Scheduling VNF migrations in an SD-WAN where links fail and recover dynamically requires fast decisions that classical optimisation cannot deliver within operational time windows. This paper trains a graph neural network (GNN) on synthetic SD-WAN topologies with 10–80 nodes and failure traces modelled as a Markov renewal process calibrated to a European research network fault log. The GNN learns a scoring function over migration candidates that is used inside a greedy scheduler. The scheduler is evaluated in an emulated SD-WAN of 40 nodes built with Containernet and a custom failure injector. Against an ILP oracle with full future knowledge the GNN scheduler achieves 91% of optimal chain availability while reducing scheduling compute time from 4.2 seconds to 38 milliseconds per decision epoch. Generalisation is tested on two held-out real topologies. The paper also quantifies the effect of stale topology information on scheduling quality.

title: Granular resynthesis of crowd noise: a corpus-based approach for interactive environments
abstract: This paper describes a corpus-based granular resynthesis system designed to generate plausible crowd ambience in real time for interactive media applications. A corpus of 4.2 hours of field recordings from sporting events, public squares, and indoor market halls was collected across four cities in Serbia and Slovenia. Recordings were segmented into grains of 80–320 ms, annotated with spectral centroid, loudness, and roughness descriptors, and stored in a searchable database. A matching algorithm retrieves and concatenates grains at runtime based on three high-level control parameters: density, arousal, and directional distribution. Listening tests with 34 participants showed that synthesised output was rated statistically indistinguishable from edited reference recordings on the dimensions of realism and appropriateness (p > 0.05, Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Latency from parameter change to audible response measured under 12 ms on a standard gaming workstation. The system is implemented as a plugin for a widely used game audio middleware platform.

title: Procedural audio for architectural simulation: mapping spatial occupancy to real-time soundscape synthesis
abstract: This chapter examines the use of procedural audio techniques in architectural acoustics simulation tools, where the goal is to give architects and urban planners an audible preview of a space's acoustic character during the design phase. The authors describe a pipeline that takes occupancy data—expressed as agent count, movement speed, and room geometry—and maps it to a layered granular synthesis engine producing footstep textures, diffuse speech, and HVAC noise. Room impulse responses are computed at low resolution using an image-source method and convolved with the granular output at runtime. Two case studies are presented: a university atrium in Novi Sad and a planned pedestrian underpass in Zagreb. Informal evaluation sessions with architecture students indicated that the audio feedback was considered useful for intuiting acoustic comfort, though precise quantitative validation against measured impulse responses is noted as outstanding future work.

title: A dataset of annotated urban ambient sound for procedural audio research
abstract: This paper introduces UrbAmbNS-1, a freely available annotated dataset of urban ambient sound recordings collected in Novi Sad between 2014 and 2016. The dataset comprises 11.4 hours of binaural and mid-side recordings captured at 24-bit 96 kHz across 18 locations including a central market, a tram stop, a sports stadium exterior, parks, and residential courtyards. Each file is annotated with time-stamped labels for 22 sound event categories, measured A-weighted equivalent sound pressure levels, weather conditions, time of day, and estimated crowd density derived from concurrent video footage. Inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) across three annotators reached 0.74 on average. The paper describes the recording methodology, annotation protocol, and baseline statistics. The dataset is intended to support reproducible research in procedural audio, soundscape design, and machine listening applied to urban contexts.

title: Real-time spatialisation of procedurally generated crowd sound over a first-order ambisonics system
abstract: The spatial distribution of crowd sound sources is an important perceptual cue for presence and immersion in virtual environments, yet most procedural crowd audio systems treat ambience as a non-directional texture. This paper describes an approach in which individual virtual crowd agents, each assigned a granular voice synthesising breathing, speech fragments, and movement noise, are spatialised using first-order ambisonics encoding and decoded for a 12-channel loudspeaker array. Tests were conducted in the Spatial Audio and Interaction Laboratory at the Academy of Arts, Novi Sad. A localisation experiment with 19 listeners compared agent positions rendered by the procedural system against equivalent positions rendered from dry anechoic recordings. Mean absolute localisation error was 8.3° for the procedural system versus 6.1° for the reference, a difference not found significant (Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.11). CPU load with 64 simultaneous agents reached 34% on a standard workstation.

title: Granular modelling of footstep textures on heterogeneous surfaces for walkthrough simulations
abstract: Footstep sound synthesis is a recurring challenge in walkthrough and virtual reality applications because surface material, walker gait, and shoe type interact in complex ways that prerecorded libraries handle poorly. This paper presents a granular synthesis model of footstep textures parameterised by surface hardness, grain size, walking tempo, and heel-toe weight ratio. A corpus of 840 single footstep recordings across seven surface types was segmented into attack, sustain, and release grains. A regression model trained on measured surface properties predicts grain selection weights and envelope parameters; cross-validation RMSE for predicted spectral centroid was 0.41 Bark. In a two-alternative forced-choice test, 31 participants preferred synthesised footsteps over unmatched library sounds in 71% of trials (binomial test, p < 0.001) but showed no significant preference over matched library sounds (p = 0.38), suggesting the synthesis model approaches library quality for known surfaces.

title: Soundscape design guidelines for outdoor public VR experiences: practitioner perspectives from a survey study
abstract: This study surveyed 68 audio professionals—including sound designers, game audio directors, and immersive installation artists—across 14 European countries regarding their practices and challenges in designing soundscapes for outdoor public virtual reality installations. An online survey included Likert-scale items and three open-ended questions. Thematic analysis of qualitative responses identified five recurrent challenge categories: environmental noise interference, headphone bleed in shared spaces, mismatch between visual and acoustic scales, limited platform support for real-time procedural audio, and absence of standardised loudness targets for VR contexts. Quantitative results showed that 61% of respondents used some form of procedural or generative audio in their last project, yet only 23% reported using dedicated procedural audio tools as opposed to prerecorded layers. The paper discusses implications for tool development and proposes a draft checklist for soundscape design in outdoor VR deployments.

title: Concatenative synthesis versus parametric models for indoor atrium ambience: a comparative evaluation
abstract: Indoor atria with glass roofs and hard reflective surfaces produce complex ambient textures that are difficult to model parametrically. This paper compares three synthesis strategies—corpus-based concatenative synthesis, a physical parameter model based on statistical room acoustics, and a hybrid approach—for generating atrium ambience under varying occupancy levels (10, 50, 150, and 300 simulated occupants). Synthesis was driven by the UrbAmbNS-1 dataset and supplementary recordings from a university atrium. Evaluation combined objective spectral similarity measures against held-out reference recordings and a listening test (n = 26). The hybrid approach achieved the highest similarity scores (mean spectral distance 1.8 dB vs. 2.9 dB for parametric alone) and the highest listener preference ratings (mean score 6.4 on a 9-point scale). Computational cost of the hybrid approach was approximately 1.9× that of concatenative synthesis alone.

title: Reinforcement learning for adaptive parameter control in real-time procedural soundscapes
abstract: This paper investigates whether a reinforcement learning (RL) agent can learn to adjust procedural audio synthesis parameters—grain density, pitch scatter, spatial spread—in response to evolving game state variables, replacing manually authored control curves. A proximal policy optimisation agent was trained in a simulated game environment with a reward signal derived from a learned perceptual model trained on listener preference data from earlier studies. After 1.2 million environment steps the agent converged to policies that matched hand-authored curves in 83% of game state scenarios as rated by five experienced sound designers in a blind comparison. In the remaining 17% of scenarios the agent produced solutions rated as equally or more appropriate by at least three of five raters. Training and inference infrastructure, parameter spaces, and reward function design are described in full. The policy was tested in a prototype mobile game with 15 playtesters who reported no perceived audio quality degradation.

title: Auditory display of pedestrian flow data in urban planning decision support: a prototype evaluation
abstract: Urban planners routinely work with pedestrian flow models but almost always interact with them through visual displays. This paper describes and evaluates an auditory display prototype that maps pedestrian density, speed variance, and directional flow from a simulated Novi Sad city-centre block to a procedural soundscape generated by a granular synthesis engine. Three mapping strategies were designed: iconic (crowd sounds scaled to density), symbolic (abstract tones encoding flow direction), and hybrid. Twelve urban planning professionals participated in a task-based evaluation requiring them to identify congestion events in animated flow datasets using the auditory display alone, the visual display alone, and both combined. Combined display produced the fastest correct identification times (mean 4.3 s vs. 6.8 s visual alone). The hybrid auditory mapping was preferred over iconic and symbolic by 9 of 12 participants in a post-task ranking.

title: Perceptual effects of latency in adaptive soundscape parameter updates: implications for mobile game audio
abstract: Mobile game audio pipelines introduce variable latency between game state changes and audible synthesis output due to hardware audio buffer constraints, operating system scheduling, and middleware overhead. This paper quantifies the perceptual impact of such latency on player experience in a controlled study. Thirty participants played a short mobile game prototype under five latency conditions (0, 40, 80, 160, and 320 ms) with a within-subjects design. Dependent measures were self-reported immersion (IEQ-9 scale), detection rate of state-mismatch events (where audio lagged a visible gameplay event), and game performance score. Detection rate rose significantly above chance at 80 ms and reached ceiling at 160 ms. Self-reported immersion dropped significantly between 80 and 160 ms conditions (p = 0.003, paired t-test). Game performance was unaffected across conditions. Results suggest 80 ms as a practical upper latency budget for adaptive soundscape systems on mobile platforms.

title: Accuracy Assessment of GPR Depth Estimation for Buried PVC Water Pipes in Sandy Loam Soils
abstract: Ground-penetrating radar depth estimates for buried polyvinyl chloride water pipes depend strongly on the dielectric permittivity of the surrounding soil, which varies with moisture content and texture. This study presents controlled-trench experiments carried out at two test sites in Vojvodina, where 110 mm and 160 mm diameter PVC pipes were buried at known depths between 0.6 m and 1.8 m in sandy loam. A 400 MHz antenna was used with a GSSI SIR-3000 system. Permittivity was estimated by the common-midpoint method and cross-validated against time-domain reflectometry probes inserted at five depths per trench. Depth errors for the 400 MHz antenna ranged from 2.1% to 8.7%, with the largest errors occurring when volumetric water content exceeded 28%. A correction procedure based on a two-layer dielectric model reduced mean absolute depth error from 6.3 cm to 2.1 cm. Results indicate that routine moisture monitoring at GPR survey sites can substantially improve cadastral positioning accuracy for utility pipes.

title: A GIS Data Model for Urban Utility Cadastre Compliant with the Serbian Technical Regulation on Underground Installations
abstract: Serbia's technical regulation on underground installations, enacted in 2010, specifies minimum positional accuracy requirements and mandatory attribute sets for utility cadastres but provides no standardised data model. This paper proposes a relational GIS schema implemented in PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension that maps regulation requirements to feature classes, topology rules and attribute domains. The schema covers six utility categories: water supply, sewerage, gas, district heating, electricity and telecommunications. Topology constraints enforce minimum pipe separation rules and flag intersections lacking documented crossing agreements. The model was populated with survey data for a 1.2 km² pilot area in Subotica municipality and validated against 1:500 municipal plans. Completeness ratio reached 94% for water and 71% for telecommunications, reflecting the poorer documentation state of the latter. The schema is published as an open-source QGIS plugin accompanying this paper.

title: Subsurface Utility Engineering for a 22 kV Underground Cable Replacement Project: Methodology and Lessons Learned
abstract: This book chapter describes the subsurface utility engineering process applied to a 3.4 km urban corridor in Zrenjanin, Serbia, where an ageing overhead 22 kV line was replaced by an underground cable. The chapter covers the full SUE quality level sequence from desk study through geophysical detection to test-hole verification. Desk-study sources included 1:2500 municipal cadastre sheets, utility operator records and historical aerial photographs from 1973 and 1988. GPR surveys with 250 MHz and 500 MHz antennas were conducted prior to open-cut construction; results were overlaid with cable route design drawings to identify conflict points. Seventeen previously unknown utility segments were discovered, triggering four route design revisions. The chapter discusses root causes of documentation gaps, including informal network extensions during the 1980s and post-war reconstruction, and proposes a project-phase checklist for Serbian distribution grid operators undertaking similar cable burial programmes.

title: Comparison of 3D GPR Migration Algorithms for Resolving Closely Spaced Parallel Pipes at Shallow Depth
abstract: When two pipes run in parallel at separation distances below the Rayleigh resolution limit of the antenna in use, standard B-scan interpretation underestimates pipe count and misestimates lateral positions. This study compared Kirchhoff migration, frequency-wavenumber migration and reverse-time migration applied to synthetic C-scan volumes and to field data collected over a test trench containing three 63 mm PE pipes at 0.7 m depth with 120 mm centre-to-centre spacing. The 900 MHz antenna was traversed in a 0.05 m × 0.05 m grid pattern over a 2 m × 2 m aperture. Kirchhoff migration separated the two outer pipes in 78% of synthetic realisations but failed to resolve the central pipe. Frequency-wavenumber migration resolved all three pipes in 91% of realisations and produced lateral position errors below 25 mm. Field validation using a reference frame showed mean lateral positioning error of 21 mm for frequency-wavenumber versus 54 mm for Kirchhoff. Processing time remained tractable on standard desktop hardware at under 90 seconds per C-scan volume.

title: Updating an Existing Utility Cadastre Using Mobile LiDAR and GPR: Workflow and Cost Analysis for a Peri-Urban Gas Distribution Area
abstract: Periodic cadastre updates are required when network extensions or repairs alter buried asset positions. This paper presents a workflow that couples a vehicle-mounted LiDAR scanner for above-ground reference frame acquisition with GPR for subsurface detection, tested on 18 km of peri-urban gas distribution network in Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia. LiDAR point clouds were georeferenced using GNSS/INS at 5 cm absolute accuracy and served as the spatial backbone onto which GPR detections were registered. Change detection between the updated cadastre and the prior 2011 record identified 64 newly installed segments, 11 relocated segments and 3 abandoned segments not recorded in any documentation. Cost comparison against a conventional resurvey using walking GPR and RTK-GNSS on the same corridor showed a 34% reduction in field time per kilometre, partially offset by higher data processing costs. The workflow is applicable to annual update cycles for medium-density distribution grids.

title: Quality Level Attribution of Existing Utility Records in Four Serbian Municipalities: A Systematic Audit
abstract: A reliable subsurface utility engineering programme requires knowing the quality level of existing records before planning intrusive works. This paper presents a systematic audit of utility documentation held by four Serbian municipalities covering a combined urban area of approximately 38 km². Records for water, sewerage, gas and electricity were evaluated against a four-tier quality framework adapted from the American CI/ASCE 38-02 standard and calibrated to Serbian regulatory requirements. Auditors reviewed 1,847 plan sheets and 423 digitised GIS layers, assessing completeness, positional accuracy, attribute richness and update frequency. Overall, 31% of reviewed records met quality level B or above; sewerage documentation was the weakest category, with 61% at quality level D. Municipalities with GIS-based cadastres introduced after 2010 performed significantly better than those retaining paper-only systems. The audit protocol is offered as a transferable tool for municipal geodetic services and utility operators preparing investment programmes.

title: GPR Signature Classification for Common Pipe Materials in Vojvodina Soils: A Laboratory and Field Study
abstract: Distinguishing pipe material from GPR reflections alone is commercially useful because material type determines corrosion risk and replacement priority. This laboratory and field study characterised GPR reflections from steel, cast iron, ductile iron, PVC and high-density polyethylene pipes of 63–315 mm diameter buried in reconstructed Vojvodina soil columns at 0.5–2.0 m depth. Four antenna frequencies (250, 500, 900 and 1600 MHz) were evaluated. Amplitude-versus-offset behaviour, reflection polarity and hyperbola apex sharpness were extracted as discriminating features and fed into a random forest classifier. In controlled conditions the classifier separated metallic from non-metallic pipes with 96% accuracy; distinguishing PVC from HDPE remained unreliable at all frequencies tested. Field trials over 12.1 km of surveyed distribution network in Ruma and Inđija showed that metallic versus non-metallic classification transferred to field conditions with 89% accuracy when soil moisture was below 20% volumetric content, degrading to 74% under wet conditions.

title: INSPIRE Compliance in Municipal Utility Cadastres: Mapping Serbian Practice to the Utility Networks Data Specification
abstract: The INSPIRE Directive's Utility Networks theme specifies a comprehensive data model for cross-border interoperability of network infrastructure data, but implementation among smaller European municipalities remains patchy. This paper examines the degree to which nine Serbian municipal utility cadastres produced between 2015 and 2024 conform to the INSPIRE Utility Networks Data Specification v3.0. Conformance was assessed across four dimensions: feature-type completeness, attribute population, coordinate reference system compliance, and metadata provision. Mean feature-type completeness was 58%; attribute population averaged 44% of mandatory attributes. Coordinate reference system compliance was universal, as EPSG:32634 is standard in Serbian cadastral practice. Metadata provision was the weakest dimension, with only two of nine cadastres supplying INSPIRE-compliant metadata records. A lightweight transformation toolkit implemented as a QGIS processing algorithm is described that maps the most common Serbian cadastre schemas to INSPIRE GML, reducing manual intervention required for cross-border data exchange.

title: Evaluating the fitness for purpose of the Serbian cadastral base map for use as a reference layer in municipal urban planning GIS
abstract: Municipal urban planning in Serbia relies on the cadastral base map as a primary spatial reference, yet no systematic assessment of its fitness for planning-specific purposes has been conducted at a national scale. This paper develops a fitness-for-purpose assessment framework based on six criteria—positional accuracy, completeness, topological correctness, attribute currency, semantic alignment with planning ontology, and access and licensing constraints—and applies it to the cadastral datasets of eight municipalities of varying size and development pressure in the Vojvodina and Šumadija regions. Data were obtained directly from municipal cadastral offices under a research agreement. Positional accuracy (assessed by GNSS check survey, n=2 400 points) varied from 0.3 m to 2.1 m RMSE across municipalities. Topological correctness was below 95% in six of eight municipalities. Attribute currency was rated adequate in three municipalities. The paper concludes with a scoring matrix and identifies the principal bottlenecks for routine planning use.

title: Stable carbon and nitrogen isotope ratios in primary feathers of Reed Warblers (Acrocephalus scirpaceus) reflect breeding latitude across the Central European flyway
abstract: We collected primary feathers from 214 Reed Warblers captured at five ringing stations spanning a north–south gradient from Slovakia to northern Serbia during autumn migration (2010–2011). Feathers synthesised at the breeding grounds retain isotopic signatures of local food webs, enabling origin assignment. Carbon isotope ratios (δ13C) ranged from −23.4‰ to −19.1‰ and nitrogen ratios (δ15N) from 5.8‰ to 10.3‰. Latitudinal regression explained 41% of δ15N variance and 29% of δ13C variance, consistent with documented gradients in baseline δ15N across European freshwater invertebrate communities. A two-isotope Bayesian mixing model (MixSIAR) placed 68% of individuals with breeding origin uncertainty within a 3-degree latitudinal band. Results confirm that feather isotopes provide a viable, cost-effective complement to direct tracking for population-level studies of this species across the flyway.

title: Trophic niche partitioning between sympatric Acrocephalus warblers at a Vojvodina reed-bed stopover inferred from stable isotopes
abstract: Reed-bed habitats in Vojvodina host multiple Acrocephalus species during autumn migration. We tested whether Great Reed Warbler (A. arundinaceus) and Sedge Warbler (A. schoenobaenus) partition trophic niche at a shared stopover, using δ13C and δ15N from blood samples collected at Carska bara nature reserve in 2014 and 2015 (n = 96 and n = 88 individuals, respectively). Bayesian standard ellipse areas (SIBER) indicated significantly larger isotopic niche width in Sedge Warbler (SEAc = 3.21‰²) compared with Great Reed Warbler (SEAc = 1.87‰²; posterior probability of overlap < 0.05). Mixing models indicated that Great Reed Warbler relied more heavily on aquatic invertebrates (estimated contribution 58–72%), whereas Sedge Warbler showed broader use of terrestrial arthropods. These differences may reduce interspecific competition during the energetically demanding stopover phase.

title: Sulphur isotopes (δ34S) improve geographic assignment of migratory warblers in Central Europe: a multi-tissue evaluation
abstract: Sulphur stable isotopes have been proposed as a third axis for improving geographic assignment of migratory birds because δ34S gradients are driven by geology and distance from marine sources, largely independently of latitude. We measured δ34S alongside δ13C and δ15N in feathers, blood and claw tips of 130 Blackcap (Sylvia atricapilla) and 95 Garden Warbler (Sylvia borin) captured at ringing stations in Austria, Hungary and Serbia during 2015 and 2016. Adding δ34S to a two-isotope discriminant model improved correct population assignment from 58% to 71% for Blackcap and from 52% to 67% for Garden Warbler, using a reference dataset of 61 known-origin individuals. Claw tips and feathers showed consistent δ34S values within individuals (ICC = 0.82), supporting their joint use. We provide an updated isoscape calibration for Central European passerines.

title: Isotopic turnover rates in blood fractions of three European passerine species: captive study implications for field dietary reconstruction
abstract: Accurate dietary reconstruction from stable isotopes requires species- and tissue-specific isotopic turnover rates and diet-to-tissue discrimination factors (DTDFs). We conducted a controlled captive feeding experiment using 45 individuals of three species — Chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs), Blackcap (Sylvia atricapilla) and Willow Warbler (Phylloscopus trochilus) — maintained at the University of Novi Sad animal facility. Birds were switched from a standard invertebrate diet to an isotopically distinct plant-based diet, and whole blood, red blood cells and plasma were sampled at nine time points over 60 days. Half-lives estimated by non-linear regression ranged from 8.2 days (plasma δ13C) to 24.6 days (red blood cells δ15N). Mean DTDFs for δ13C were 0.8–1.4‰ and for δ15N 2.1–3.2‰, values somewhat lower than commonly applied passerine averages. These species-specific parameters are provided as a reference for field studies using these taxa.

title: Stable isotope evidence for population-specific wintering strategies in Barn Swallow (Hirundo rustica) populations breeding in Serbia
abstract: We used feathers moulted on African wintering grounds to infer isotopic differentiation among Barn Swallow populations breeding at three sites in Serbia (northern Vojvodina, Fruška Gora foothills, southern Serbia). Feathers were collected from 162 adults recaptured at breeding sites in 2018 and 2019. A three-isotope mixing model combining δ13C, δ15N and δ34S suggested partial segregation of isotopic clusters consistent with differential use of Sahel vs. Guinea savanna wintering habitats: birds from northern breeding sites showed significantly lower δ15N (mean 10.6‰) than those from southern Serbia (mean 12.4‰; Welch t-test, p < 0.005). Individuals with higher winter δ15N arrived on average 3.1 days earlier to Serbian breeding sites (linear regression, R² = 0.18, p = 0.01), suggesting a fitness-relevant link between wintering habitat quality and migratory timing.

title: Stable isotopes in ecology: principles and applications for animal migration studies
abstract: This book chapter provides a methodological overview of stable isotope techniques used in wildlife ecology with an emphasis on applications to migrating birds. It covers the physical basis of isotope fractionation, tissue selection criteria, analytical procedures (EA-IRMS), sources of measurement error, mixing model frameworks (MixSIAR, simmr), and geographic assignment approaches. Case studies drawn from Central European passerine research illustrate decisions around sampling design and statistical treatment. A section on quality control discusses reference material selection, instrument calibration, and inter-laboratory comparison protocols relevant to small research groups with limited budgets. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and researchers planning to integrate stable isotope methods into field ornithology programmes, and includes worked examples with R code for basic mixing model runs.

title: Combined stable isotope and geolocator analysis reveals differential routing of Eurasian Reed Warbler along the Central European and Adriatic flyways
abstract: We deployed light-level geolocators on 38 Eurasian Reed Warblers (Acrocephalus scirpaceus) breeding at two sites in Serbia and Hungary, recovering 19 devices the following season. Geolocator-inferred autumn routes were compared with feather δ13C, δ15N, and δ34S profiles to evaluate how well isotopes proxy routing behaviour independently. Birds using the Central European route (n = 11) showed significantly lower feather δ34S (mean 4.2‰) than Adriatic-route birds (n = 8; mean 7.9‰; p = 0.003), consistent with exposure to marine-influenced precipitation during Adriatic coastal travel. A cross-validation using leave-one-out classification assigned route correctly for 15 of 19 individuals using the three-isotope model. The study demonstrates that routing differences can leave detectable isotopic traces and that isotopes may substitute for geolocators for population-level route inference where device deployment is logistically constrained.

title: Arthropod prey isotopic baselines at Vojvodina wetland stopover sites: a resource for passerine dietary mixing models
abstract: Reliable mixing models depend on accurate isotopic baselines for dietary sources. We sampled 18 arthropod orders from four wetland stopover sites in Vojvodina (Carska bara, Obedska bara, Koviljsko-petrovaradinski rit, and a Danube island site) in spring and autumn 2023 and 2024, yielding 412 composite samples analysed for δ13C, δ15N, and δ34S. Aquatic invertebrate orders showed higher δ15N (mean 7.8 ± 1.6‰) and lower δ13C (mean −25.3 ± 1.9‰) than terrestrial groups (δ15N 5.1 ± 1.4‰; δ13C −23.8 ± 1.5‰). Within-site seasonal variation in δ15N was up to 1.9‰ for some Diptera families, highlighting the importance of temporally matched source sampling. A publicly archived dataset and site-specific source libraries formatted for direct use in MixSIAR and simmr are provided alongside this paper, intended to serve as a regional reference for future isotope-based dietary studies of migratory passerines.
venue: Isotopes in Ecology and Environmental Studies

title: Citizen-science records correct distributional gaps in atlas data for Pannonian amphibians
abstract: Historical atlas data for seven amphibian species in the Pannonian Basin were compared against 14,200 georeferenced photographic records submitted to a regional citizen-science platform between 2010 and 2014. Species distribution models were fitted using MaxEnt for both data sources separately and in combination. For three species, citizen-science records filled distributional gaps exceeding 80 km from the nearest atlas point, substantially shifting predicted range boundaries northward. Temporal overlap analysis showed that citizen contributions peaked during spring breeding migrations and covered phenological windows missed by systematic surveys. Photograph-based taxonomic validation was performed by two expert reviewers; misidentification rates were 6.4% overall, dropping to 2.1% for distinctive species. The combined dataset improved model AUC scores by a mean of 0.07 relative to atlas data alone, demonstrating practical value of vetted citizen observations for regional biodiversity monitoring.

title: Integrating eDNA metabarcoding and image-based monitoring for macroinvertebrate assessment in Pannonian lowland streams
abstract: Macroinvertebrate communities were assessed in 16 lowland stream reaches in Vojvodina using three parallel methods: Surber sampling with morphological identification, underwater macro-photography with CNN-assisted identification, and eDNA metabarcoding targeting the COI barcode region. Morphological identification recorded 67 taxa across all sites; eDNA detected 84 taxa including 22 not found by netting; image-based identification retrieved 51 taxa from 9,400 reviewed image frames. Concordance between methods was highest for EPT taxa (Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, Trichoptera) and lowest for chironomid midges. ANOSIM comparing community matrices from morphological and eDNA approaches yielded R = 0.43 (p = 0.002), indicating moderate but significant dissimilarity attributable partly to differential detection of rare taxa. Biotic index scores derived from morphological identification correlated well with eDNA-derived scores (Pearson r = 0.81, p < 0.001) across the water quality gradient represented by study sites. Methodological strengths and field cost comparisons are discussed.

title: Nematode-based soil health scoring for arable farms in Serbia: a pilot protocol and field validation
abstract: A pilot protocol for nematode-based soil health scoring was developed and tested on 24 arable farms across three Vojvodina districts during 2024–2025. The scoring system integrates four nematode indices (MI, EI, SI, PPI/MI) into a composite Nematode Soil Health Score (NSHS) scaled 0–100, with weighting coefficients derived from a literature meta-analysis of 63 European arable soil datasets. The NSHS was validated against independent measurements of aggregate stability, earthworm density, and microbial biomass carbon collected from the same farms. Pearson correlations between NSHS and these reference indicators ranged from 0.61 to 0.78. Farm managers were surveyed regarding willingness to use nematode-based reporting; 62% expressed interest if sampling costs could be reduced below EUR 80 per farm. The protocol is available as an open-access spreadsheet tool. Limitations regarding seasonal timing of a single annual sample are discussed.

title: Penalised Cox Regression for Gene Expression-Based Survival Prediction in Early-Stage Colorectal Cancer
abstract: This study evaluated the predictive performance of LASSO-penalised Cox regression applied to microarray gene expression data from 312 patients with stage II–III colorectal cancer from the Ljubljana University Medical Centre. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival; secondary endpoints included overall survival. Cross-validated concordance indices (C-index) were computed across ten repeated fivefold splits. The final regularised model retained 38 of 18,432 probes and achieved a C-index of 0.71 on held-out data, outperforming a clinical-variable-only baseline (C-index 0.62). Calibration was assessed using Brier scores at 3 and 5 years. Gene ontology enrichment of the retained features pointed to cell-cycle regulation pathways. The analysis demonstrated that even modest penalisation substantially reduced overfitting compared to stepwise Cox methods, and that cross-validation must account for the full modelling pipeline, including variable pre-filtering, to obtain unbiased performance estimates.

title: Elastic Net Regularisation in Competing-Risks Models: A Simulation Study
abstract: Cause-specific and subdistribution (Fine–Gray) hazard models were compared under elastic net penalisation in a comprehensive simulation study. Data were generated under five competing-risks scenarios varying the number of events, censoring fraction (10–60%), number of covariates (100–5000), and degree of predictor correlation. Performance was measured by the cause-specific C-index, integrated Brier score, and empirical false-discovery rate of selected variables. Results showed that the Fine–Gray subdistribution model with elastic net achieved lower integrated Brier scores than cause-specific penalised models when the cumulative incidence function was the primary target, but was more sensitive to high predictor correlation. Penalty ratio α was found to matter most when covariates clustered into blocks with intra-block Pearson correlations above 0.7. Practical guidance for selecting α and the penalty strength λ via nested cross-validation is provided, with accompanying R code released under an MIT licence.

title: Time-Varying Covariate Effects in Penalised Cox Models: Application to Breast Cancer Recurrence
abstract: The proportional hazards assumption is routinely violated in breast cancer recurrence data, yet most regularised Cox implementations do not accommodate time-varying effects. This paper adapted the Breslow partial likelihood to allow time-varying log-hazard ratio estimates through B-spline interactions between penalised covariate effects and log-time. The method was implemented as an extension to the CoxBoost R package and applied to a cohort of 601 hormone receptor-positive breast cancer patients from three Balkan oncology centres. Follow-up extended to 12 years. Genomic predictors derived from a 50-gene prognostic signature showed strong early effects that attenuated after 5 years, consistent with clinical knowledge about late recurrence. The integrated time-varying C-index exceeded fixed-effects models by 0.04 points at the 8-year horizon. Computational overhead was manageable: fitting required under 4 minutes per cross-validation fold on a standard server.

title: A Competing-Risks Framework for Predicting Death from Disease Versus Treatment Toxicity in Head-and-Neck Cancer
abstract: Patients with locally advanced head-and-neck squamous cell carcinoma face two distinct hazards after radiochemotherapy: locoregional relapse and treatment-induced organ failure. A cause-specific hazard model and a Fine–Gray subdistribution model were each fitted with elastic net penalisation to clinical and RNA-seq data from 284 patients treated at three regional oncology centres (2008–2018). A 25-gene expression panel was jointly derived for both competing endpoints. The Fine–Gray model's cumulative incidence predictions were better calibrated for treatment-related mortality (IBS 0.09 vs. 0.14), whereas cause-specific models were superior for relapse prediction at 3 years (C-index 0.73 vs. 0.69). Decision curve analysis demonstrated net clinical benefit for the combined panel over clinical variables alone across threshold probabilities of 10–40%. The article also discusses identifiability issues when the two competing events share many predictors.

title: Proteomics-Augmented Survival Models in Ovarian Cancer: Feasibility and Benchmarking
abstract: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics (LC-MS/MS, 3,812 quantified proteins) was combined with RNA-seq and clinical data for 118 high-grade serous ovarian cancer patients. Three integration strategies were benchmarked: stacked ensembling, DIABLO (multi-block sparse discriminant analysis adapted for survival), and penalised multi-omics Cox regression. Given the modest sample size, three-way block elastic net Cox regression was fitted with strict nested cross-validation and permutation-based performance testing. The proteomics block provided incremental C-index gain (0.03) over RNA-seq alone, statistically non-significant at the 5% level (permutation p = 0.11). Proteins involved in DNA mismatch repair were among the most consistently selected features. The study concludes that proteomics data are informative but that sample sizes below approximately 150 are unlikely to yield reliably detectable incremental performance gains when added atop transcriptomics in penalised frameworks.

title: Regularised Cause-Specific Cox Models with Missing Omics Blocks: Multiple Imputation Versus Available-Case Analysis
abstract: Incomplete multi-omics data are common in retrospective cancer studies when not all assays were ordered for every patient. This paper compared multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE), single-block available-case analysis, and a missing-indicator approach within competing-risks Cox models penalised by elastic net, using a colorectal cancer cohort (n = 394) in which 22% of patients lacked methylation data and 31% lacked proteomic measurements. The estimands of interest were cause-specific cumulative incidence functions for cancer-specific death and cardiovascular death. MICE followed by elastic net Cox fitting under Rubin's rules produced the lowest Monte Carlo prediction error (integrated Brier score 0.148 vs. 0.167 for available-case), but required careful pooling of penalty parameters across imputed datasets. An R workflow is described and made available as a GitHub repository. Bootstrapped confidence intervals for C-index differences are reported.

title: Benchmarking Deep Survival Models Against Penalised Cox Regression on Multi-Omics Cancer Data
abstract: Deep learning approaches to survival analysis (DeepSurv, Cox-nnet, SurvivalNet) were systematically compared against LASSO and elastic net Cox regression on six multi-omics cancer datasets (n ranging from 116 to 621) covering lung, breast, glioblastoma, bladder, kidney, and ovarian cancer. Evaluation used nested cross-validation with 100 Monte Carlo repetitions; endpoints included overall survival and progression-free survival. Across all datasets, elastic net Cox outperformed or matched deep survival models in C-index on five of six datasets; the exception was the glioblastoma set (n = 515), where Cox-nnet achieved C-index 0.72 vs. 0.68 for elastic net. Deep models showed considerably higher variance across folds. The study does not advocate against deep survival models but highlights the requirement for substantially larger datasets and more careful hyperparameter tuning before they replace well-regularised Cox models in the multi-omics context.
venue: Computational and Statistical Approaches in Oncology

title: Dynamic Prediction of Pancreatic Cancer Survival Using Landmark Models with Multi-Omics Covariates
abstract: Landmark modelling was used to generate dynamic survival predictions that update as patients accumulate post-diagnosis follow-up information. A series of landmark Cox models, each fitted at a different landmark time (3, 6, 12, 18 months), incorporated baseline clinical variables and RNA-seq features selected by elastic net from a discovery cohort of 203 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients. An independent validation cohort of 87 patients from two Serbian oncology centres was used for external validation. The 12-month landmark model achieved the highest C-index for prediction at the 2-year horizon (0.74), reflecting the increasing predictive value of post-surgery CA19-9 trajectories captured as time-varying covariates. Dynamic pseudo-observation plots illustrated how patient-specific survival probability estimates shifted meaningfully with each landmark update. The work also quantifies the information lost when omics data are measured only at baseline.

title: A Graph-Grammar Formalism for Indoor Architectural Space Synthesis
abstract: We propose a typed graph-grammar framework for generating indoor floor plans that respect both topological adjacency requirements and metric area constraints. Grammars are defined over a node-labelled attributed graph where nodes represent rooms and edges encode doorway, wall-sharing, or service-corridor relationships. Production rules carry pre-conditions expressed as linear inequalities over node attributes such as floor area and natural-light exposure. We validate the formalism against a manually annotated dataset of 310 floor plans from public Serbian residential building archives dating from 1980 to 2005. The grammar reproduces 84% of the recorded adjacency patterns and generates structurally valid plans for 91% of randomly sampled area-budget inputs. Derivation trees are stored and can be replayed, providing a lightweight versioning mechanism for generated content. Limitations regarding non-planar adjacency graphs and staircase placement are discussed in detail.

title: Comparing Stochastic Local Search and Systematic CSP Solving for Real-Time Level Generation
abstract: Real-time applications such as roguelike games require procedural level generators that complete within strict frame-budget windows, typically under 33 milliseconds. We compare four approaches—min-conflicts local search, simulated annealing, DPLL-based systematic search, and a hybrid restarter—on a benchmark of 1,200 level specifications varying in corridor density, obstacle ratio, and required item placement. Experiments run on a single CPU core at 3.2 GHz. The hybrid restarter met the 33 ms budget for 97% of easy instances and 71% of hard instances, outperforming pure local search by 14 percentage points on hard instances. Solution quality, measured as deviation from target room-count and connectivity-degree distributions, was statistically equivalent across methods when solutions were found. We release the benchmark suite and solver wrappers as an open dataset.

title: Playability Metrics as Soft Constraints in Puzzle Level Generation
abstract: We treat playability properties—solvability, estimated solution length, and cognitive load proxy—as weighted soft constraints within a partial constraint satisfaction problem formulation for grid-based puzzle level generation. A constraint hierarchy assigns hard constraints to structural validity (no isolated cells, reachable goal state) and soft constraints to playability targets supplied by a designer profile. We generate sets of 200 puzzle levels per profile and evaluate them with a human study involving 38 participants who rated difficulty, fairness, and enjoyment on Likert scales. Levels generated with soft-constraint playability targets scored statistically higher on fairness (p < 0.01, Wilcoxon test) than levels generated without them, with no significant difference in enjoyment. Solution-length deviation from targets averaged 1.8 steps across 600 generated levels. We discuss how constraint weight calibration can substitute for extensive hand-tuning of generator parameters.

title: Rule Conflict Detection in Attributed Graph Grammars for Urban Layout Synthesis
abstract: When graph-grammar production rules are authored independently by multiple designers, conflicting rules can cause derivation deadlocks or generate structurally inconsistent urban blocks. We formalise three classes of rule conflict—attribute range overlap, precondition negation, and topological exclusion—and present a static analysis algorithm that detects all three classes in polynomial time relative to rule-set size. The algorithm is evaluated on four grammar collections for urban block generation totalling 247 rules, finding 31 previously undetected conflicts. Resolving detected conflicts reduced deadlock rate during stochastic derivation from 12% to under 1% of generation attempts on a test suite of 400 city-block scenarios. Run-time of the analysis over the largest grammar (89 rules) was under 2 seconds. The tool is implemented as a plugin for an existing open-source graph-transformation workbench.

title: Constraint-Driven Road Network Generation for Open-World Game Environments
abstract: Road networks in open-world games must satisfy geometric constraints (curvature limits, grade limits) and topological constraints (connectivity, absence of isolated districts) simultaneously. We model this as a weighted CSP over a planar graph whose edges carry road-segment variables and whose nodes represent junctions. The solver combines arc consistency with a greedy heuristic seeded by a minimum spanning tree of mandatory waypoints. We test generation on five reference maps of sizes between 2 km² and 25 km² derived from anonymised urban planning sketches provided by a Serbian municipal authority. The solver produces valid road networks for all inputs, with mean generation time of 8.7 seconds for the largest map. Expert evaluators from a transportation-planning office rated network plausibility at 3.9 out of 5 on average, noting realistic district connectivity but occasional over-regular intersection spacing.

title: Formal Verification of Safety Properties in Procedurally Generated Training Scenarios
abstract: Training simulations used in emergency-response drills must guarantee that generated scenarios are escapable and do not place agents in unwinnable states. We apply bounded model checking to verify two safety properties—agent reachability to exit nodes and absence of resource starvation—over procedurally generated scenario graphs. Scenario generation uses a constraint-satisfaction pipeline that outputs a finite transition graph; a lightweight SMT encoding is then checked with an off-the-shelf solver. Over a corpus of 1,500 generated scenarios of complexity between 20 and 80 state nodes, model checking confirmed both properties for 98.3% of instances within a 10-second per-instance timeout. The 1.7% failures corresponded to edge cases in the stochastic rule selector that were subsequently fixed. We report on integration into a pilot training tool developed for a regional civil-protection organisation.

title: Interoperability Between CSP Solvers and Graph-Transformation Engines for Spatial Synthesis
abstract: CSP solvers and graph-transformation engines are typically used in isolation for content generation, yet their strengths are complementary: CSP solvers handle metric and quantitative constraints efficiently while graph-transformation engines manage topological structure. We define a synchronisation protocol in which a CSP solver and a graph-transformation engine exchange partial solutions through a shared attribute blackboard. The protocol specifies when each subsystem may commit a partial assignment and how conflicts are signalled and resolved. We implement the protocol using an open-source CP solver and an existing graph-transformation workbench, requiring 1,200 lines of adapter code. Benchmarks on three spatial-synthesis tasks—floor-plan generation, dungeon tiling, and settlement layout—show that the combined system finds solutions that neither subsystem finds alone in 18–35% of hard instances, at a cost of 1.5–3× longer median generation time.

title: Incrementally Updatable Procedural Layouts Under Evolving Constraint Sets
abstract: In live-service game contexts and iterative urban-planning tools, a previously generated layout must be updated when constraints change without discarding and regenerating the entire structure. We model this as a dynamic constraint satisfaction problem where a change event specifies which constraints are added, removed, or tightened. We adapt an existing chronological backtracking solver with a dependency graph that identifies the minimal subgraph of the layout affected by each change event. Across 900 change events applied to three base layout types of sizes 64, 256, and 1,024 tiles, the incremental approach required modifying a mean of 12.4% of tile assignments compared to full regeneration, reducing mean update time by 61%. Layout validity was maintained in all cases. We discuss how this approach interacts with artist-authored manual overrides that must be preserved across updates.

title: Grammar-Based Generation of Accessible Public Space Layouts Satisfying Accessibility Standards
abstract: Public space design must comply with accessibility regulations specifying minimum corridor widths, turning radii for wheelchair users, and maximum cross-slope values. We encode Serbian and EU accessibility standards as hard constraints within a graph-grammar-based generator for public plaza and pedestrian-zone layouts. The grammar contains 54 production rules; 19 are annotated with accessibility preconditions derived directly from regulatory text. We test generation on 12 reference plaza configurations drawn from urban-planning tenders published by three Serbian municipalities. The generator produces fully compliant layouts for all 12 configurations, with a mean of 2.1 derivation attempts required per layout. A validation step using a separate rule checker confirms compliance independently. Practitioners from two municipal planning offices reviewed outputs and noted that 9 of 12 generated layouts required no manual adjustment for submission.

title: Discretionary Accruals in Serbian Listed Firms: An Initial Assessment Using the Modified Jones Model
abstract: This paper provides an early empirical mapping of discretionary accruals among companies listed on the Belgrade Stock Exchange over the period 2005–2010. Using annual financial statements for 84 non-financial firms, we estimate total and current accruals through the modified Jones (1991) model adapted for a thin-trading, low-liquidity context. Cross-sectional OLS regressions are run separately for each two-digit industry classification. Median absolute discretionary accruals reach 6.3 percent of lagged total assets, substantially higher than benchmarks reported for developed European exchanges. The incidence of income-increasing manipulation is more pronounced among smaller firms approaching debt covenant thresholds. Robustness checks using the Dechow–Dichev model confirm the direction of findings, though magnitudes differ. The paper concludes that institutional weaknesses in auditing oversight and thin analyst coverage amplify reporting discretion, and it proposes a baseline dataset for longitudinal monitoring of Serbian capital market reporting quality.

title: Real Activities Manipulation Around Initial Public Offerings on the Zagreb and Ljubljana Exchanges
abstract: We examine whether firms conducting initial public offerings on the Zagreb Stock Exchange and the Ljubljana Stock Exchange engage in real activities manipulation in the year preceding and the year of listing, covering 61 IPO events between 2004 and 2011. Following Roychowdhury (2006), we construct benchmarks for abnormal cash flows from operations, abnormal discretionary expenditures, and abnormal production costs using industry-year matched control firms. Findings indicate statistically significant reductions in discretionary expenditures (advertising, R&D, and SG&A) in the pre-IPO year, averaging 4.1 percent of lagged assets, consistent with upward earnings management through cost cuts rather than accrual inflation. Abnormal production costs show a marginally significant increase in the IPO year. Accrual-based tests run in parallel do not yield comparable significance, suggesting that real manipulation is the preferred tool under stricter local audit scrutiny. Results are robust to size and leverage matching and to alternative definitions of the event window.

title: Audit Quality and Earnings Management Containment: Evidence from Central European Frontier Markets
abstract: This study investigates whether Big Four audit engagement is associated with lower levels of discretionary accruals among listed firms in four Central European frontier markets: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. The sample includes 312 firm-year observations over 2008–2013. We estimate discretionary accruals using the performance-adjusted Jones model proposed by Kothari et al. (2005) and regress the absolute value of estimated accruals on an indicator for Big Four auditor, controlling for firm size, leverage, return on assets, and growth. OLS and quantile regression (at the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile of accrual distribution) are employed. The Big Four dummy is negatively and significantly associated with absolute discretionary accruals in OLS and at upper quantiles, with coefficient magnitudes implying a reduction of approximately 2.8 percentage points of lagged assets. Results suggest that audit quality does exert a constraining effect even where enforcement capacity is limited, though the effect is concentrated among the highest accrual reporters.

title: Income Smoothing Behaviour of Commercial Banks in the Western Balkans: Loan Loss Provision Evidence
abstract: Banks employ loan loss provisions (LLP) as a primary vehicle for income smoothing, yet this practice is understudied in Western Balkan banking systems. Using consolidated annual data for 47 commercial banks from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina over 2009–2014, we estimate a LLP model that decomposes provisions into a non-discretionary component (driven by non-performing loan ratio, loan growth, and GDP growth) and a discretionary residual. Panel regressions with bank and year fixed effects show a significant negative relationship between pre-provision earnings and discretionary LLP, consistent with income smoothing. The coefficient on pre-provision earnings implies that for each one-unit increase in earnings, banks adjust provisions downward by approximately 0.18 units, dampening reported income volatility. Smoothing intensity is higher for state-owned banks and for institutions with lower capital adequacy ratios. Results have implications for supervisory stress-testing frameworks and IFRS 9 adoption assessments in the region.

title: Benchmarking Earnings Quality Across Frontier European Stock Exchanges: Methodological Challenges and Data Constraints
abstract: This book chapter surveys the methodological difficulties of applying standard US-derived earnings management models to frontier European stock exchanges, drawing on the authors' accumulated experience with Serbian, Macedonian, Romanian, and Hungarian datasets. We discuss three recurring problems: thin cross-sectional samples that undermine industry-year regressions, pervasive related-party transactions that inflate accrual noise, and the co-occurrence of IFRS adoption with privatisation waves that confounds time-series comparisons. We propose practical adaptations including pooled cross-border industry groupings, winsorisation thresholds calibrated to local return distributions, and the use of rolling three-year estimation windows in lieu of annual cross-sectional regressions. A worked example using 2010–2015 data from the Bucharest Stock Exchange illustrates each adjustment. The chapter is intended as a methodological reference for researchers entering this empirical domain and for practitioners assessing the reliability of published earnings quality estimates for regional companies.

title: Do Political Connections Amplify Earnings Management? Evidence from Privatised Firms on the Belgrade Stock Exchange
abstract: We test whether state-residual ownership and board-level political connections are associated with elevated earnings management among former state-owned enterprises listed on the Belgrade Stock Exchange. The sample comprises 68 firms that underwent partial privatisation between 1997 and 2007, observed annually from 2008 to 2015. Political connections are proxied by the number of board members with documented positions in national or local government, drawn from public corporate disclosures and official gazette announcements. Discretionary accruals are estimated using the modified Jones model and the Dechow–Dichev accrual quality measure. Tobit regressions indicate that each additional politically connected director is associated with an increase of 1.1 percentage points in absolute discretionary accruals. The effect is stronger in years preceding parliamentary elections, consistent with a political business cycle interpretation. Findings suggest that corporate governance reforms targeting board composition may be more effective than audit regulation for constraining reporting manipulation in post-privatisation settings.

title: Accrual Reversals and Persistence of Earnings in Small-Cap Companies on the Budapest Stock Exchange
abstract: Accrual reversals provide a clean identification of prior-period manipulation, as artificially inflated accruals must partially reverse in subsequent periods. We exploit this property with a sample of 93 small-cap firms listed on the Budapest Stock Exchange over 2011–2017. Estimating accrual components following the Sloan (1996) decomposition, we test whether the persistence coefficient on accruals is lower for firms with high prior-year discretionary accruals, controlling for firm size, book-to-market ratio, and industry. Panel regressions confirm that earnings persistence is significantly lower for firms in the top accrual quartile, with the interaction term between lagged accruals and the high-accrual indicator yielding a coefficient of −0.31, compared to a base persistence of 0.58. A supplementary portfolio test shows that a long-short strategy exploiting this reversal earns a mean annual return of 5.2 percent on a risk-adjusted basis over the sample horizon, though liquidity constraints would limit practical implementation.

title: IFRS 15 Adoption and Revenue-Based Earnings Management in Listed Croatian and Slovenian Retailers
abstract: The transition to IFRS 15 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) altered the timing and pattern of revenue recognition, with potential consequences for earnings management through revenue manipulation. We study 34 retail-sector firms listed in Croatia and Slovenia before (2014–2017) and after (2018–2021) mandatory IFRS 15 adoption, focusing on abnormal revenue as a proxy for real-side earnings management following McNichols and Stubben (2008). Difference-in-differences analysis, with a matched control group of unlisted firms applying the same standard, shows a statistically significant reduction in abnormal revenue post-adoption, averaging 3.4 percent of lagged total revenue. This reduction is concentrated in firms that previously reported large contract liability balances, suggesting the standard's clarified recognition criteria constrained a specific manipulation pathway. Accrual-based tests show no parallel reduction, indicating that management shifted rather than eliminated earnings management activity. Implications for standard-setters considering enforcement capacity in small open economies are discussed.

title: Earnings Management and the Cost of Debt: Evidence from Bond-Issuing Non-Financial Firms in Romania and Hungary
abstract: We examine whether creditors price earnings management risk into bond yield spreads for non-financial firms issuing corporate bonds on the Bucharest and Budapest exchanges between 2014 and 2021. The sample comprises 148 bond issuances by 62 unique firms. Earnings management is measured using three proxies: absolute discretionary accruals from the Kothari et al. model, the accrual quality factor from Dechow and Dichev, and an indicator for suspected real activities manipulation based on simultaneous abnormal values across at least two Roychowdhury benchmarks. OLS regressions of yield spread at issuance on each proxy, controlling for credit rating, maturity, issue size, and macroeconomic conditions, show positive and significant coefficients for all three earnings management measures. The effect is economically meaningful: a one-standard-deviation increase in absolute discretionary accruals is associated with a 28-basis-point increase in yield spread. Results hold under IV estimation using lagged industry-level accruals as an instrument.

title: Detecting Earnings Management Through Machine Learning Classification: A Comparative Exercise on Balkan Exchange Data
abstract: This conference paper reports a comparative exercise in which we apply three supervised machine learning classifiers — random forest, gradient boosting, and a regularised logistic regression — to distinguish firm-years with high earnings management from clean reporters, using a labelled sample constructed from enforcement actions and qualified audit opinions for firms listed on Balkan frontier exchanges (Serbia, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina) between 2012 and 2020. Feature sets include traditional accrual-based and real-activities metrics alongside balance sheet ratios, auditor characteristics, and governance indicators. Out-of-sample classification accuracy ranges from 71 to 79 percent across models, with gradient boosting performing best. Variable importance rankings consistently place the ratio of receivables growth to revenue growth and abnormal discretionary expenditure among the top five predictors. We discuss the limitations of using enforcement actions as ground-truth labels given heterogeneous regulatory capacity across jurisdictions.

title: Real Earnings Management in Loss-Avoidance Contexts: Micro-Cap Firms at the Zero-Earnings Threshold on the Belgrade Stock Exchange
abstract: Firms with pre-managed earnings just below zero have strong incentives to cross the zero threshold through manipulation. We test for real activities management around the zero-earnings discontinuity for micro-cap firms on the Belgrade Stock Exchange, using all non-financial non-utility firm-year observations with available cash flow data from 2015 to 2022, yielding 1,104 observations. Following the distribution-based approach of Burgstahler and Dichev (1997) augmented with Roychowdhury real-activities benchmarks, we first document an excess mass of observations just above zero earnings and a deficit just below, consistent with threshold management. Among suspected threshold managers (firms in the [0, 0.01] interval of earnings scaled by assets), we find significantly higher abnormal production costs and lower abnormal discretionary expenditures relative to firms far from the threshold. The magnitude of real-activities adjustment averages 2.9 percent of lagged assets. We find limited evidence of concurrent accrual manipulation, suggesting real tools dominate at this threshold in this market.

title: Sustainability Reporting and Accrual-Based Earnings Management: Is There a Trade-Off in CEE Listed Companies?
abstract: The relationship between voluntary sustainability reporting and financial reporting quality is theoretically ambiguous: transparency motives may reduce earnings manipulation, while impression management motives may allow it to persist beneath ESG disclosures. We test these competing hypotheses using a panel of 224 non-financial firms listed on six Central and Eastern European exchanges that published standalone sustainability or integrated reports at least once between 2017 and 2024. Sustainability reporting adoption is treated as endogenous, instrumented by industry-level peer adoption rates and a country-level ESG regulatory index. IV-2SLS estimates show a negative and significant association between sustainability reporting adoption and absolute discretionary accruals, with a point estimate of −0.031 (standard error 0.009), consistent with a complementarity interpretation. The effect is not significant for real activities manipulation proxies, suggesting that sustainability commitments constrain accrual opportunism more than operational manipulation. The result is robust to the exclusion of firms subject to mandatory non-financial reporting under domestic transpositions of the EU NFRD.

title: Intra-Group Pricing Distortions in Serbian Manufacturing: Evidence from Customs and Balance Sheet Data, 2003–2006
abstract: This paper examines whether foreign-owned manufacturing subsidiaries in Serbia systematically mispriced intra-group goods transactions relative to arm's-length benchmarks in the period 2003–2006. The study matches customs declaration microdata with audited balance sheet records for 214 subsidiaries controlled by parent companies registered in the European Union. An arm's-length price range is constructed for each HS-6 product category using contemporaneous third-party transaction prices from the same customs database. Results indicate that 38 percent of the sampled subsidiaries reported export prices to affiliated parties that fell more than 15 percent below the interquartile arm's-length range, a pattern consistent with deliberate underpricing of outbound shipments to shift taxable income to lower-tax jurisdictions. The average estimated tax revenue loss per firm amounts to approximately 1.2 million Serbian dinars annually. The analysis controls for firm size, industry concentration, and the bilateral effective tax rate differential between Serbia and the parent-country jurisdiction. The findings provide early quantitative documentation of base erosion through goods transfer pricing in a Western Balkans economy with limited tax administration capacity.

title: Suspended sediment concentration gradients during spring floods on the lower Tisa reach near Titel: a two-year field campaign
abstract: Continuous turbidity and water-stage records were collected at two cross-sections on the lower Tisa River over the flood seasons of 2009 and 2010 using optical backscatter sensors calibrated against filtered water samples. A total of 847 discrete samples were analysed for total suspended solids and grain-size distribution. Rating curves were fitted separately for rising and falling limbs, revealing a consistent hysteresis index averaging +0.34, indicating higher sediment concentrations on the rising limb. Peak suspended sediment concentration during the April 2010 event reached 2 340 mg/L, roughly 2.8 times the mean annual value. Fine silt fractions dominated the suspended load throughout, accounting for 71–84 % of mass. The results challenge the assumption of a single power-law rating curve commonly applied in regional flood-damage assessments and suggest that event-based hysteresis correction reduces annual load estimates by up to 18 %.

title: Longitudinal bedform migration during a single flood pulse on a sand-bed reach of the Danube upstream of Novi Sad
abstract: Repeated multibeam echo-sounder surveys were conducted before, during, and after a bankfull flood event in March 2012 on a 4.2 km reach of the Middle Danube. Six survey runs captured the full hydrograph at roughly 36-hour intervals. Dune celerity was estimated by cross-correlation of successive longitudinal bed profiles extracted along the thalweg. Mean dune heights ranged from 0.38 m to 1.24 m and wavelengths from 9 to 47 m; celerity peaked at 11.2 m/day near discharge maximum. Net volumetric change across the reach was a deposition of 18 400 m³, concentrated in two distinct mid-channel bars. The ratio of bedload flux estimated from dune tracking to that from the Meyer-Peter and Müller formula was 0.61, consistent with prior studies on regulated lowland channels. Hysteresis in dune height was weaker than in bedload transport, suggesting lagged morphological adjustment.

title: Grain-size segregation at channel bifurcations in the Vojvodina canal network under unsteady flow
abstract: The Danube–Tisa–Danube canal system in Vojvodina presents a network of engineered bifurcations whose sediment partitioning behaviour under unsteady conditions is poorly documented. Bedload traps and pumped-sampling equipment were deployed at three bifurcation nodes during four regulated discharge pulses in 2013. Grain-size distributions in both tributary channels were measured at 2-hour intervals. At discharge ratios above 0.65, the finer channel consistently received a disproportionate fraction of suspended fines (D50 < 0.063 mm), while coarser fractions (D50 0.2–0.5 mm) were preferentially routed into the dominant branch. A simple bifurcation routing model, calibrated to these data, reproduced observed downstream D50 values within ±12 %. The results carry practical implications for maintenance dredging schedules, as disproportionate fine deposition in secondary branches reduces conveyance capacity roughly four times faster than predicted by uniform-sediment models.

title: Calibration of Delft3D-FLOW for morphodynamic simulation of a Tisa floodplain reach: sensitivity to sediment-transport formula choice
abstract: A reach-scale Delft3D-FLOW coupled morphodynamic model was set up for a 12 km segment of the lower Tisa between Kanjiža and Adorján. Bathymetric data from a 2015 survey served as the initial bed condition, and the model was forced with observed discharge and water-level boundary conditions from five flood events in 2015–2016. Four sediment-transport formulae—van Rijn (1984), Engelund–Hansen, Ackers–White, and Wu–Wang–Jia—were evaluated against post-event bathymetric surveys. The Brier Skill Score for bed-elevation change ranged from −0.12 (Ackers–White) to +0.41 (van Rijn), the latter performing best when the hiding-exposure correction was applied. Model skill was most sensitive to the choice of critical Shields parameter; a value of 0.047 rather than the standard 0.056 reduced bed-elevation RMSE by 22 %. Suspended-sediment output matched measured concentrations within one standard deviation for three of the five events.

title: Riverbed scour at bridge piers during the 2016 Tisa flood: combining UAV photogrammetry with acoustic profiling
abstract: The May 2016 flood on the Tisa produced the third-highest peak stage since 1972 at the Senta gauging station and offered an opportunity to quantify scour at three bridge structures. Acoustic Doppler surveys were conducted 48 hours before, during peak discharge, and 14 days after the event. UAV-mounted photogrammetric surveys captured exposed pier geometry and scour hole morphology during the falling limb. Maximum observed scour depth at the deepest pier nose reached 2.7 m, compared to 1.9 m predicted by the HEC-18 formula using peak velocity alone. Scour hole volumes correlated more closely with cumulative stream power above a threshold of 320 W/m² than with peak discharge alone (R² = 0.87 vs 0.61). Post-flood backfilling was substantial: within 14 days, 60–75 % of scour volume was refilled. The study argues that current design standards may underestimate scour duration risk in lowland floods with wide, flat hydrographs.

title: Long-term thalweg incision and its relationship to gravel extraction on the Sava River between Sremska Mitrovica and Jamena, 1980–2017
abstract: Cross-sectional survey data collected by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia at nine permanent stations on the lower Sava were digitised and standardised to compare thalweg elevations from 1980 to 2017 at five-year intervals. Permitted gravel extraction volumes for the same period were obtained from provincial records. Mean thalweg incision over 37 years was 1.43 m, with the most pronounced lowering (up to 2.8 m) occurring downstream of two former licensed extraction sites. A piecewise linear regression with a breakpoint at 1997 (when extraction permits became more restrictive) showed a statistically significant reduction in incision rate from 0.07 m/yr to 0.03 m/yr. The analysis also found a downstream propagation of the incision signal at an estimated rate of 0.8–1.2 km/yr. Implications for levee stability, floodplain drainage, and riparian groundwater tables are discussed.

title: Sediment dynamics in an embanked floodplain reconnected to the main channel: a controlled inundation experiment on the Tisa oxbow near Padej
abstract: A pilot reconnection project on a 3.4 km² abandoned oxbow floodplain near Padej allowed controlled inundation for 22 days in spring 2019 through a temporary notch in the flood levee. Continuous turbidity logging at the inlet and outlet, combined with gridded sediment trap arrays (n = 48) distributed across the floodplain, quantified deposition patterns during filling and draining phases. Total suspended sediment input was 8 700 t, of which 63 % was retained on the floodplain. Spatial deposition was highest within 200 m of the inlet (average 12 mm thickness) and decreased exponentially with distance. Fine clay and organic matter fractions were disproportionately retained relative to inlet load. The experiment also recorded a measurable reduction in flood-peak level (–0.11 m at a downstream gauge), consistent with detention-storage attenuation. Findings support the case for managed floodplain reconnection as a sediment management tool.

title: Bedload transport estimation using passive acoustic monitoring: a field validation on a sand-gravel bed reach of the Bosut River
abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) using hydrophone arrays was tested as a proxy for bedload flux on a 180 m reach of the Bosut River at Sremska Mitrovica over three consecutive flood seasons (2018–2020). A broadband hydrophone was installed at mid-depth and sampled continuously at 44 kHz. Acoustic power in the 5–16 kHz band was correlated against co-located Helley-Smith sampler measurements (n = 112 hauls). A power-law relationship between acoustic power spectral density and unit bedload transport rate yielded R² = 0.79. Calibration was season-dependent, with coefficients varying by up to 31 % between years, partly attributable to changes in bed surface grain size assessed by pebble counts each season. The method successfully detected the onset of bedload motion at discharges within ±6 % of the threshold estimated from bed shear stress. Recommendations for hydrophone placement and calibration frequency are provided.
