title: Impact of consecutive dry years on bedform geometry and grain sorting on the Middle Danube: evidence from annual repeat surveys 2017–2022
abstract: Six annual multibeam echo-sounder surveys were conducted on a 6.8 km reach of the Middle Danube downstream of Novi Sad to track changes in dune geometry and surface sediment texture during a period of below-average discharge (2017–2022). Dune heights decreased progressively from a mean of 0.91 m in 2017 to 0.52 m in 2022, while dune wavelength shortened by 19 %. Surface sediment D50 coarsened from 0.41 mm to 0.63 mm, indicating armour layer development. The number of active bedform crests per kilometre dropped by 34 %. Low-flow exposure of gravel bars, mapped from satellite imagery, increased from 1.2 km² in 2017 to 3.8 km² in 2022. These observations are contextualised against a 40-year discharge record and compared with the morphological response documented after the 2003 low-flow period. The results highlight the asymmetric recovery time of dune fields following flood and drought cycles.

title: Phosphorus and heavy-metal partitioning between bedload and suspended sediment fractions during flood events: implications for water quality modelling
abstract: Paired bedload (Helley-Smith) and suspended sediment (depth-integrated) samples were collected during five flood events on the lower Tisa in 2021–2023. Samples were analysed for total phosphorus, extractable phosphorus, lead, cadmium, and zinc concentrations at a certified laboratory. Phosphorus concentrations in suspended sediment were 3.1–5.4 times higher than in bedload samples from the same cross-section and event. Lead and cadmium showed similar enrichment in fines, while zinc was more uniformly distributed. During the largest event (April 2022), the suspended fraction carried 94 % of the total phosphorus load despite representing only 78 % of total sediment mass. A simple partitioning coefficient approach integrated into a one-dimensional water-quality model reduced simulated downstream phosphorus concentration error from 38 % to 14 % compared to a sediment-uniform assumption. These findings have direct relevance to nutrient load estimates submitted under EU Water Framework Directive reporting obligations.

title: Predicting morphological response of a regulated lowland channel to managed flood releases: a HEC-RAS 2D morphodynamic assessment for the Tisa between Kanjiža and Senta
abstract: Water management plans for the Tisa in Serbia include provisions for controlled flood releases through auxiliary spillways to relieve dyke pressure during extreme events. This study uses HEC-RAS 2D with the sediment transport module to simulate morphological change for three release scenarios (5 000, 7 500, and 10 000 m³/s) over a 14.2 km regulated reach. The model was validated against the 2016 flood bathymetric record, achieving a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.72 for bed-elevation change. Under the 10 000 m³/s scenario, simulated maximum scour at the outer bend of the main meander exceeded 3.1 m, posing a risk to the armour protection of the Kanjiža revetment. Deposition in the downstream cross-section was predicted to reduce conveyance capacity by 8 % within 72 hours. Sensitivity tests showed that an uncertainty of ±20 % in the incoming sediment supply boundary condition shifted peak scour depth by ±0.4 m. Results are presented in a form intended to support decision-making by the Vojvodina Water Management Authority.

title: Influence of solvent composition and temperature on anthocyanin yield from Cabernet Sauvignon pomace
abstract: This study examined how ethanol concentration (20–80% v/v) and extraction temperature (25–60 °C) affect total anthocyanin content (TAC) and individual anthocyanin profiles in extracts from Cabernet Sauvignon grape pomace sourced from a winery in the Fruška Gora region. A 3×4 full factorial design was applied across 12 solvent–temperature combinations. TAC was determined by the pH differential method and ranged from 1.8 to 6.4 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside equivalents per gram of dry pomace. HPLC-DAD analysis identified malvidin-3-glucoside as the dominant pigment across all conditions, representing 38–52% of total anthocyanin area. Increasing ethanol from 40% to 60% at 40 °C produced the highest TAC. Temperatures above 50 °C caused measurable degradation of acylated anthocyanins, reducing their proportion by approximately 18% compared with extractions at 25 °C. Antioxidant capacity measured by DPPH and ABTS assays correlated positively with TAC (r = 0.91 and r = 0.88, respectively). Results suggest that 60% ethanol at 40 °C represents an appropriate starting point for further optimisation.

title: Ultrasound-assisted extraction of anthocyanins from dried grape skin: optimisation by response surface methodology
abstract: Ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) was evaluated as an alternative to conventional stirring for recovering anthocyanins from dried Prokupac grape skin, a variety grown predominantly in southern Serbia. A Box-Behnken design was applied to three independent variables: ultrasound power (100–300 W), extraction time (10–40 min), and liquid-to-solid ratio (15–45 mL g⁻¹). Total monomeric anthocyanin content served as the response variable and was determined spectrophotometrically. The optimal conditions predicted by the fitted quadratic model were 220 W, 28 min, and 35 mL g⁻¹, yielding a predicted TAC of 7.9 mg CGE g⁻¹ dry weight, which was confirmed experimentally at 7.7 ± 0.3 mg CGE g⁻¹. Compared with conventional extraction under the same solvent conditions (60% ethanol, 40 °C, 60 min), UAE reduced extraction time by 53% while increasing TAC by approximately 21%. Colour measurements (CIE L*a*b*) indicated more vivid red hues in UAE extracts, with higher a* values (mean 18.4 vs. 14.2). Energy consumption calculations showed a modest increase per batch but a clear advantage when expressed per milligram of pigment recovered.

title: Photodegradation kinetics of grape pomace anthocyanins under fluorescent, LED, and UV-A illumination
abstract: Purified anthocyanin fractions from Cabernet Sauvignon pomace were exposed to three light sources: cool-white fluorescent tubes (1500 lux), white LED panels (1500 lux), and UV-A lamps (365 nm, 15 W m⁻²) for up to 72 hours at pH 3.5 and 20 °C. Degradation was monitored hourly for the first 12 h and then at 24, 48, and 72 h by measuring absorbance at 520 nm. All treatments followed pseudo-first-order kinetics. Rate constants were 0.0031 h⁻¹ (fluorescent), 0.0019 h⁻¹ (LED), and 0.0412 h⁻¹ (UV-A). LED illumination caused the lowest pigment loss (12.8% over 72 h), while UV-A caused near-complete degradation (94.3%) within the same period. Addition of ascorbic acid (0.1%) accelerated fluorescent-light degradation by approximately 35%, consistent with pro-oxidant synergy. Individual anthocyanin profiles by HPLC-DAD revealed that acylated species degraded faster than non-acylated ones under UV-A. Findings are relevant for packaging decisions and storage recommendations when grape pomace colorants are used in food products displayed under retail lighting.

title: Spray-drying encapsulation of anthocyanin-rich grape pomace extracts using maltodextrin and gum arabic carriers
abstract: Anthocyanin-rich extracts from Frankovka grape pomace were microencapsulated by spray drying using three wall material formulations: maltodextrin alone (MD, DE 18), gum arabic alone (GA), and a 1:1 blend (MD-GA). Inlet temperature was fixed at 160 °C; feed concentration was 5% total solids. Encapsulation efficiency ranged from 71.4% (MD) to 88.2% (MD-GA blend). Moisture content, bulk density, solubility, and hygroscopicity were measured for each powder. Stability testing was conducted over 60 days at 25 °C and 45% RH. TAC retention after 60 days was 61.3% (MD), 72.8% (GA), and 81.5% (MD-GA). Scanning electron microscopy showed spherical morphology with few visible surface cracks for all formulations, with smaller mean particle diameter for MD-GA (9.3 µm) compared with MD alone (14.7 µm). Release profiles in simulated gastric and intestinal fluids indicated faster release at pH 1.2 than at pH 6.8 for all carriers. The MD-GA blend was identified as the most suitable formulation based on combined stability and flow properties, with potential application in powdered beverage mixes.

title: Stability of encapsulated and unencapsulated grape pomace anthocyanins in a model carbonated soft drink at pH 3.2
abstract: A model carbonated beverage at pH 3.2, composed of water, sucrose (10% w/v), citric acid, and CO₂ (3.5 vol), was used to compare the stability of spray-dried MD-GA encapsulated anthocyanin powder against unencapsulated liquid extract from Cabernet Sauvignon pomace. Both preparations were added at equivalent TAC concentrations (50 mg L⁻¹ CGE). Samples in amber and transparent PET bottles (250 mL) were stored at 20 °C under fluorescent light (1200 lux, 12 h/day) and in the dark for 30 days. In transparent bottles under light, unencapsulated anthocyanin TAC fell to 38% of initial value by day 30, while encapsulated retained 61%. In dark storage, both preparations retained above 85% TAC regardless of packaging. Colour difference (ΔE*) values in transparent–light conditions were 12.1 (unencapsulated) and 6.4 (encapsulated) after 30 days. Sensory evaluation by a 12-member trained panel detected no off-flavours attributable to the encapsulant material at the tested concentration. The results confirm that encapsulation provides a measurable but incomplete protection against light-induced degradation in a realistic beverage matrix.

title: Comparative extraction performance of deep eutectic solvents and hydroalcoholic mixtures for anthocyanins from pressed grape skin waste
abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DES) were evaluated against conventional hydroalcoholic solvents for anthocyanin extraction from pressed grape skin waste (Pinot Noir variety). Six DES systems were prepared from choline chloride paired with oxalic acid, lactic acid, glycerol, fructose, glucose, and citric acid at molar ratios determined by differential scanning calorimetry. Extraction conditions were standardised at 50 °C, 30 min agitation, and 1:20 solid-to-liquid ratio. TAC, individual anthocyanin profile (HPLC-DAD), and antioxidant capacity were determined. The choline chloride–lactic acid DES (1:2 molar ratio, 20% added water) yielded 8.6 mg CGE g⁻¹ dry skin, outperforming 60% ethanol (7.1 mg CGE g⁻¹) under identical conditions. HPLC profiling showed similar anthocyanin profiles across DES systems with differences mainly in total yield rather than selectivity. Viscosity of DES at 50 °C ranged from 18 to 47 mPa·s, affecting mass transfer; lower viscosity systems correlated with higher TAC (r = −0.81). Cytotoxicity screening of selected DES on a Caco-2 cell line at concentrations up to 1 mg mL⁻¹ showed no significant reduction in cell viability, suggesting preliminary food-grade applicability.

title: Quantification of refined sunflower oil adulteration in cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil using partial least squares regression on NIR spectra
abstract: Adulteration of premium cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil with cheaper refined sunflower oil is a documented food fraud concern in Central and Eastern Europe. Binary mixtures of authenticated pumpkin seed oil and refined sunflower oil were prepared at ten concentration levels (2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 70, and 100% w/w sunflower oil) using three independent oil batches each, yielding 90 mixture samples in total. NIR spectra (1000–2498 nm) were acquired in duplicate. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) models were built on SNV-preprocessed spectra using a 10-fold cross-validation scheme. The optimised model with six latent variables achieved a root mean square error of cross-validation (RMSECV) of 1.83% w/w and an RMSEP of 2.11% w/w on an independent validation set. The model showed acceptable linearity (R² = 0.981) across the full adulteration range. These detection limits are practically relevant given that commercial fraud typically involves substitutions above 5%. A portable NIR instrument was also tested on a subset of 30 samples, showing moderately higher errors (RMSEP 3.6% w/w), suggesting scope for transfer calibration improvements.

title: Preoperative hyperalgesia as a predictor of chronic groin pain after Lichtenstein hernioplasty: a prospective cohort study
abstract: This prospective cohort study enrolled 148 male patients scheduled for elective open Lichtenstein inguinal hernia repair at a single tertiary centre in Novi Sad. Quantitative sensory testing (QST) was performed on the contralateral forearm at baseline to assess pressure pain thresholds (PPT) and temporal summation. Patients were followed at 3 and 12 months postoperatively using the Inguinal Pain Questionnaire and NRS scores. Thirty-one patients (20.9%) met criteria for chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP) at 12 months. Preoperative PPT below 210 kPa was associated with a 2.8-fold increased risk of CPIP (OR 2.82, 95% CI 1.41–5.63, p = 0.003), independent of mesh type and anaesthetic technique. High temporal summation scores were also significantly associated with CPIP (p = 0.011). These findings suggest that generalised pain sensitivity, measured preoperatively by simple bedside QST, may help identify patients at elevated risk for persistent pain and guide perioperative analgesic planning.

title: Учесталост и карактеристике хроничног постоперативног бола у препони код пацијената оперисаних методом по Лихтенштајну – анализа пресека
abstract: Циљ овог истраживања bio је да се процени учесталост, интензитет и сензорни карактер хроничног бола у препони у популацији пацијената опериних методом по Лихтенштајну у КЦВ у периоду 2010–2012. године. Анкетирано је укупно 203 пацијента у периоду 14–36 месеци од операције. Упитник је садржао НРС скалу бола, критеријуме за неуропатски бол (DN4) и процену утицаја на свакодневне активности. Хронични бол интензитета ≥3/10 пријавило је 18,2% испитаника, при чему je DN4 резултат ≥4 забележен код 41% тих пацијената, указујући на неуропатску компоненту. Бол у мировању bio је ређи (6,9%) него бол при оптерећењу (14,3%). Старосна доб и трајање операције нису значајно корелирали с присуством хроничног бола, ali je претходна болна анамнеза bila значајан фактор ризика (p=0,018).

title: Effect of pre-emptive gabapentin on postoperative pain intensity and opioid consumption following open inguinal hernia repair: a randomised controlled trial
abstract: Pre-emptive use of gabapentinoids before surgery has been proposed to reduce acute postoperative pain and the risk of chronification. This double-blind RCT randomised 120 patients scheduled for elective open inguinal hernia repair (Lichtenstein technique) to a single oral dose of gabapentin 600 mg or matching placebo administered two hours before induction. Primary outcomes were NRS pain scores at rest and on movement at 6, 12, and 24 hours postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included total morphine equivalent consumption in the first 24 hours, time to first analgesic request, and nausea/vomiting incidence. The gabapentin group showed significantly lower NRS scores on movement at 6 hours (3.1 ± 1.4 vs 4.3 ± 1.6, p = 0.001) but not at later time points. Opioid consumption was reduced by 24% in the gabapentin arm (p = 0.03). No significant difference was observed in sedation scores. Pre-emptive gabapentin provided modest short-term analgesic benefit without clear impact on early functional recovery.

title: Nerve identification and preservation during Lichtenstein repair: does intraoperative ilioinguinal nerve handling affect chronic pain outcomes?
abstract: Three strategies for managing the ilioinguinal nerve during Lichtenstein hernioplasty have been proposed: preservation, division, or resection. This retrospective study reviewed operative reports and 12-month pain follow-up data for 241 consecutive patients operated by four surgeons at a single centre between 2015 and 2018. Nerve handling was categorised post-hoc from video recordings and operative notes. Chronic pain rates were 19.8% in the preservation group (n = 106), 15.9% in the division group (n = 88), and 12.8% in the resection group (n = 47), with no statistically significant intergroup difference (p = 0.42). Neuropathic pain quality (DN4 ≥4) was more frequent in the preservation group (38.1% vs 21.4% in resection, p = 0.09). Methodological limitations include non-randomised design and variable follow-up compliance. Results are consistent with published meta-analytic trends but underscore the need for a prospective trial in this population.

title: Psychological factors and pain catastrophising as mediators of chronic post-herniorrhaphy pain: a structural equation modelling approach
abstract: Pain catastrophising and psychological distress are established modulators of acute-to-chronic pain transition across surgical contexts. This study applied structural equation modelling (SEM) to data from 178 patients followed prospectively for 12 months after inguinal hernia repair. Instruments included the Pain Catastrophising Scale (PCS), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), Pain Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, and validated inguinal pain assessment tools at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Catastrophising fully mediated the relationship between preoperative anxiety and 12-month pain intensity (standardised indirect effect β = 0.31, 95% bootstrap CI 0.14–0.49). Self-efficacy exerted a significant protective direct effect (β = −0.27, p < 0.001). Depression was independently associated with pain-related disability but not with pain intensity per se. The SEM model accounted for 41% of variance in 12-month pain outcomes. These results highlight the value of preoperative psychological screening as part of hernia repair workup.

title: Thermal detection and pain thresholds in the inguinal region before and after hernioplasty: a longitudinal QST study
abstract: Quantitative sensory testing of the inguinal region itself is technically demanding and rarely reported longitudinally. This study applied a standardised QST battery (thermal detection thresholds, cold and heat pain thresholds, vibration detection threshold, mechanical pain threshold) at the operative site and the matched contralateral site in 64 patients at three time points: preoperatively, and at 6 weeks and 6 months postoperatively. Patients developing CPIP (n = 14) showed significantly reduced heat pain thresholds at the operative site at 6 months compared to pain-free patients (38.4 ± 3.1°C vs 43.2 ± 2.8°C, p < 0.001), consistent with peripheral sensitisation. Cold allodynia was detected in 7 of 14 CPIP patients at 6 months and in none of the pain-free patients. Longitudinal changes in contralateral site thresholds were small and non-significant, suggesting predominantly peripheral rather than centralised mechanisms in this sample.

title: Variation in chronic pain outcomes across three mesh fixation techniques in laparoscopic totally extraperitoneal inguinal hernia repair: a multicentre observational study
abstract: Laparoscopic totally extraperitoneal (TEP) repair is increasingly preferred in specialised hernia centres, but comparative data on long-term pain outcomes across mesh fixation methods remain limited in Southeast European cohorts. This observational multicentre study collected prospective data from four surgical units in Serbia and Croatia on 312 patients undergoing TEP repair with tacker fixation, fibrin glue fixation, or self-gripping mesh. Twelve-month CPIP rates (NRS ≥3) were 11.4%, 8.7%, and 9.2% respectively (p = 0.61 across groups). Neuropathic features were uncommon (<5%) in all groups. Operative time was shortest in the tacker group (mean 41.2 min) and longest in the glue group (53.7 min, p < 0.001). Recurrence at 12 months did not differ significantly (1.9–3.2%). The study was limited by non-randomised design and centre-level variation in surgical experience. Data support the view that fixation technique per se has limited impact on chronic pain in experienced TEP centres.

title: Serum neurofilament light chain concentration in patients with and without chronic post-herniorrhaphy pain: a pilot biomarker study
abstract: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is a marker of neuroaxonal injury detectable in serum and has been explored in neuropathic pain conditions. This pilot cross-sectional study measured serum NfL by single-molecule array (Simoa) in 38 patients with established CPIP and 40 post-herniorrhaphy patients without pain, recruited from the Novi Sad hernia clinic database. Median serum NfL was 9.8 pg/mL (IQR 6.2–14.4) in the CPIP group and 7.1 pg/mL (IQR 5.0–10.3) in controls (Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.04). Within the CPIP group, NfL correlated weakly with DN4 score (Spearman ρ = 0.31, p = 0.06) but not with pain intensity. Given the small sample and cross-sectional design, these results should be interpreted with caution. A prospective longitudinal design is needed to determine whether perioperative NfL rise predicts CPIP development.

title: Patient-reported functional disability at two years after inguinal hernia repair: which preoperative factors matter?
abstract: Functional outcomes at two years after inguinal hernia repair are less studied than pain outcomes, and the relationship between pain and disability is not straightforward. This prospective study followed 194 patients operated electively for primary unilateral inguinal hernia and administered the Hernia-Specific Functional Disability Index (HSFDI), NRS pain scales, and the EuroQol EQ-5D-3L at baseline, 6 months, and 24 months postoperatively. At 24 months, 13.4% of patients reported moderate-to-severe functional disability. Multivariable regression identified preoperative disability (β = 0.41), CPIP at 6 months (β = 0.33), and baseline catastrophising score (β = 0.19) as significant independent predictors of 24-month HSFDI. Surgical approach (open vs laparoscopic) was not independently associated with disability. EQ-5D utility scores improved from 0.74 ± 0.14 preoperatively to 0.88 ± 0.11 at 24 months in the no-CPIP group, versus 0.76 ± 0.16 in CPIP patients.

title: Preoperative pain education and expectation-setting before inguinal hernia repair: a feasibility randomised trial
abstract: Expectations about postoperative pain are known to shape outcomes, yet structured preoperative education is rarely tested in hernia surgery. This feasibility RCT randomised 80 patients to either a single 30-minute structured education session (covering normal recovery trajectories, pain management options, and realistic expectations for return to activity) or standard written information. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment rate, completion of outcome measures at 3 months, and fidelity of education delivery. Recruitment rate was 74% of eligible patients; follow-up completion was 88% at 3 months. Pain scores at 3 months were 1.8 ± 1.3 in the education arm versus 2.4 ± 1.7 in controls (difference −0.6, 95% CI −1.3 to 0.1, p = 0.09). Catastrophising scores at 6 weeks were significantly lower in the education group (PCS 8.4 vs 11.7, p = 0.03). These pilot data support the feasibility of a larger powered trial.

title: Laparoscopic management of Mirizzi syndrome: classification, technical considerations and outcomes in 23 cases
abstract: Mirizzi syndrome is a rare but technically demanding biliary complication of gallstone disease. This retrospective case series reviewed 23 patients with preoperatively or intraoperatively diagnosed Mirizzi syndrome managed laparoscopically at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2012 and 2022. Csendes classification: type I in 10, type II in 8, type III in 4, type IV in 1. Type I cases were treated with laparoscopic cholecystectomy alone. Types II–III required partial cholecystectomy with suture repair of the fistula in 9 cases; 3 required conversion to open hepaticojejunostomy for types III–IV. Laparoscopic completion was achieved in 87.0% of cases. Mean operating time was 114 minutes. Postoperative bile leak occurred in 2 patients, managed endoscopically. There was no mortality. Adequate preoperative imaging and liberal use of IOC were associated with reduced conversion rates. The series contributes to the limited laparoscopic literature on Mirizzi syndrome from the region.

title: Safe Harbour Provisions and Consumer Redress in Cross-Border Online Sales: A Comparative Analysis of Serbian and EU Law
abstract: This article examines whether the safe harbour provisions inherited from the 2000 E-Commerce Directive adequately protect consumers in cross-border B2C transactions involving Serbian-registered platforms. Using doctrinal analysis and a comparative survey of case law from four EU member states and Serbia covering the period 2008–2012, the study identifies three recurring gaps: the absence of a duty-of-care standard for hosting providers, the limited reach of Serbian consumer-protection remedies against foreign sellers, and ambiguity in jurisdiction clauses embedded in standard terms. The article argues that Serbian law, at that time, lacked coherent secondary legislation to fill those gaps and that courts applied conflict-of-laws rules inconsistently in fourteen traced decisions. Recommendations are offered for statutory clarification ahead of anticipated EU approximation obligations. The analysis draws on primary legislative sources from Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia, and on academic commentary published in German, English, and Serbian.

title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and Its Transposition in Serbia: Outstanding Discrepancies
abstract: The paper maps the state of Serbian transposition of the EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC) as of 2014, five years after the relevant domestic legislation entered into force. Through a clause-by-clause comparison of the Serbian Consumer Protection Act 2010 and the directive, the authors identify eleven provisions that diverge substantively from EU requirements, focusing on digital and remote-selling contexts. Particular attention is given to the black-list practices in Annex I and their partial reproduction in domestic law. An analysis of 23 decisions issued by the Serbian Commission for Consumer Protection between 2011 and 2013 reveals that enforcement was concentrated on offline practices; only two decisions addressed online advertising. The paper concludes that legislative alignment is formally close but practical enforcement in digital settings remains weak, partly because of understaffing in the supervisory body and partly because of definitional gaps in the national statute.

title: Liability of Online Marketplaces for Third-Party Seller Misconduct: Lessons from German and French Jurisprudence for Balkan Legislators
abstract: This book chapter surveys approximately 40 German and French court decisions issued between 2010 and 2016 concerning marketplace platform liability for defective goods and misleading product descriptions posted by third-party sellers. It traces the doctrinal evolution from strict hosting-provider immunity toward an emerging due-diligence obligation triggered by notice-and-action procedures. The chapter then asks whether this jurisprudential shift offers normative guidance for legislators in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbia, and North Macedonia, who had not yet enacted platform-specific rules. The author argues that the German model of proactive monitoring obligations, cautiously applied by courts, is better suited to the institutional capacity of Western Balkan enforcement bodies than the French administrative notice system. The chapter closes with a model provision suitable for incorporation into existing consumer protection statutes, drafted in terms compatible with prospective EU accession obligations.

title: Standard Terms in Cross-Border Consumer Contracts on Serbian-Operated Platforms: Fairness Assessment under the OCA and EU Acquis
abstract: The article applies the unfair terms test from the Serbian Law on Obligations and the EU Directive 93/13/EEC to a corpus of 18 standard contracts published by Serbian-registered e-commerce platforms during 2016–2017. Each contract was coded for 47 clauses across nine categories, including limitation-of-liability clauses, dispute-resolution clauses requiring arbitration abroad, and unilateral modification rights. The fairness analysis finds that 14 of the 18 contracts contained at least one clause likely to be regarded as unfair under the EU grey list, and 9 contained provisions that closely matched the black-list categories. The article discusses how Serbian courts have approached analogous clauses in a set of 11 first-instance judgments between 2014 and 2017, noting that courts rarely invoke the fairness doctrine sua sponte. Policy implications for disclosure obligations and judicial training are outlined.

title: Algorithmic Pricing and Transparency Obligations in B2C Online Sales: Regulatory Options for Pre-Accession States
abstract: This paper examines price transparency obligations applicable to algorithmic pricing by online platforms, focusing on the gap between what the EU Omnibus Directive (2019/2161) requires of member states and what pre-accession states like Serbia and Montenegro are expected to do under Stabilisation and Association Agreements. The methodology combines a doctrinal review of the relevant EU secondary law with semi-structured interviews with eight legal practitioners and compliance officers at Serbian and Montenegrin e-commerce companies conducted in 2019. The findings indicate that practitioners are largely unaware of forthcoming EU requirements and that current national rules do not mandate disclosure of personalised pricing based on profiling. The paper proposes a two-stage approach: an immediate administrative guidance measure, followed by statutory amendment timed to EU accession milestones. It also identifies specific provisions of the Omnibus Directive that may require adaptation for jurisdictions without fully harmonised contract law.

title: Trader Identification Obligations Under the DSA and the Problem of 'Seller Verification' in Serbian Cross-Border E-Commerce
abstract: Article 30 DSA requires online marketplaces to collect, verify, and publish certain trader information before allowing sellers to address consumers in the EU. This article examines how that obligation interacts with Serbian data protection law, company registration rules, and e-signature legislation, creating a cluster of compliance problems for Serbian platforms seeking to serve EU consumers. The analysis proceeds in three steps: a doctrinal reading of Art. 30 DSA and its recitals; a comparison of the Serbian Business Registers Agency's data-disclosure framework with the verification standard implied by Art. 30(2); and a review of five anonymised compliance assessments provided by Serbian platforms under a research agreement. The article finds two areas of direct tension—business-registry data accessibility and the identity-verification standard for natural-person traders—and proposes targeted legislative amendments and administrative-guidance measures that Serbia could adopt in advance of prospective DSA approximation.

title: Liability of Drop-Shipping Intermediaries for Consumer Claims Under Serbian Law and the DSA Regime
abstract: Drop-shipping arrangements, in which a platform operator or reseller takes orders from consumers but contracts fulfilment to an overseas supplier, create particular difficulties for attributing liability when goods are defective, not delivered, or misrepresented. This paper analyses how Serbian sales and consumer-protection law currently allocates liability among drop-shipper, platform, and supplier, and compares that allocation with the liability framework implied by DSA Art. 6 and Art. 30, as well as the Product Liability Directive reform proposal circulating at the time of writing. The study is informed by an analysis of 21 consumer complaint decisions issued by the Serbian consumer-protection authority between 2020 and 2023 involving international drop-shipping sellers. The paper finds that Serbian enforcement practice defaults to treating the domestic intermediary as the seller of record, but that this approach is challenged when the intermediary is also non-resident, leaving consumers without an effective domestic defendant. Amendments to the Serbian Consumer Protection Act and clarification of the Postal Services Act's application to fulfilment are recommended.

title: Enforcing DSA Obligations Against Non-EU Platforms in Western Balkan Markets: Jurisdictional Mechanisms and Practical Constraints
abstract: The Digital Services Act designates the Digital Services Coordinator (DSC) as the primary national enforcer and envisions cooperation between EU member-state DSCs for platforms established outside the EU. This paper examines the structural problem that Western Balkan states face: they are neither EU members nor parties to any formal enforcement-cooperation agreement with EU DSCs, yet their consumers regularly use platforms subject to DSA regulation. The paper first maps the formal enforcement channels available under the DSA for complaints originating in non-EU countries, drawing on the legislative text and Commission implementing acts adopted through early 2025. It then analyses the conflict-of-laws and mutual-recognition gaps that arise when Serbian consumers attempt to invoke DSA-derived rights—such as complaint acknowledgment under Art. 20 or recommender-system transparency under Art. 27—against platforms with no Serbian establishment. Three enforcement scenarios are modelled, and the paper argues that Serbia should seek an observer status in the European Board for Digital Services and pursue bilateral cooperation protocols with at least two EU member-state DSCs as an interim measure.

title: Cross-Border Workforce Data Flows in the Western Balkans: Mapping Transfer Mechanisms and Supervisory Capacity
abstract: This article provides a systematic mapping of the legal mechanisms available under the data protection laws of Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania, and Kosovo for transferring personal data of employees and job applicants to third countries. For each jurisdiction, the article identifies which transfer tools have been formally implemented (adequacy decisions, standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules, derogations), which supervisory authority guidance documents are publicly available, and what enforcement activity has occurred in the employment context as of the end of 2024. The mapping is based on a review of national legislation, official supervisory authority websites, and correspondence with practising data protection lawyers in each jurisdiction conducted between September and November 2024. The article finds that standard contractual clauses are the de facto universal mechanism but that no Western Balkan supervisory authority has issued jurisdiction-specific guidance on supplementary measures, leaving companies to rely entirely on EDPB documents that were not drafted with these legal systems in mind.

title: Prinudni otkup akcija manjinskih akcionara u srpskom pravu: normativni okvir i prva sudska praksa
abstract: Rad analizira institut prinudnog otkupa akcija (squeeze-out) kako je uređen Zakonom o privrednim društvima Republike Srbije iz 2011. godine, s posebnim osvrtom na izmjene iz 2015. Metodom normativne analize i pregledom dostupnih odluka Privrednog apelacionog suda od 2012. do 2015. godine (ukupno 23 predmeta), autor istražuje kako su sudovi tumačili odredbe o pragu od 90% i mehanizmu utvrđivanja pravične cijene. Rezultati pokazuju da je sudska praksa u posmatranom periodu bila nekonzistentna u pitanju tereta dokazivanja nepravičnosti ponuđene cijene te da ni u jednom predmetu sud nije naložio angažovanje neovisnog procjenitelja po vlastitoj inicijativi. Rad identifikuje četiri tipska scenarija u kojima je manjinski akcionar ostao bez djelotvorne zaštite i predlaže de lege ferenda izmjene inspirisane austrijskim Gesellschafter-Ausschlussgesetz modelom.

title: Few-shot surface defect detection on reflective metal parts
abstract: Detecting surface defects on highly reflective metal components remains a significant challenge for automated visual inspection systems, primarily because specular reflections obscure subtle anomalies and corrupt standard feature representations. This paper presents a few-shot learning framework tailored specifically to reflective surfaces, combining a reflection-aware preprocessing pipeline with a prototypical network backbone trained on a curated set of metallic defect categories. A novel data augmentation strategy simulates varying illumination angles and reflection intensities, substantially increasing intra-class diversity without requiring large annotated datasets. The proposed method is evaluated on a newly introduced benchmark—ReflectDefect-M—comprising five metallic material types and twelve defect classes, collected in cooperation with regional SME manufacturing partners. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves a mean average precision of 87.3% using only five support examples per defect class, outperforming seven competitive baselines by margins ranging from 4.1 to 11.6 percentage points. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each pipeline stage. The work establishes a practical pathway for deploying few-shot defect detectors in small-batch production settings where collecting large labeled datasets is economically infeasible.

title: Quantized detectors for real-time inspection on edge devices
abstract: Real-time visual inspection on embedded and edge hardware demands detectors that are simultaneously accurate and computationally lean. This paper investigates the application of post-training and quantization-aware training techniques to a family of convolutional defect detectors intended for deployment on low-power edge devices used in industrial conveyor-line inspection. We evaluate INT8 and mixed-precision INT4/INT8 quantization strategies across four detector architectures, measuring the trade-off between inference latency, memory footprint, and detection accuracy on three public industrial defect benchmarks. A structured pruning step preceding quantization is shown to recover accuracy losses for the most aggressive quantization settings. On a representative ARM Cortex-M55 target platform, the best-performing quantized detector achieves 34 frames per second with less than 2% mAP degradation relative to the full-precision baseline, satisfying the real-time constraint of most conveyor inspection scenarios. We further provide deployment guidelines and an open-source model-conversion toolkit compatible with common edge inference runtimes, lowering the barrier for practitioners in small and medium manufacturing enterprises to adopt AI-based inspection.

title: Synthetic defect generation for visual quality control
abstract: The scarcity of labeled defect images is a persistent bottleneck in training robust visual quality control models, particularly for rare or newly introduced defect types. This paper explores procedural and generative approaches to synthetic defect generation, proposing a unified pipeline that combines physically based rendering (PBR) with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) fine-tuned on a small set of real defect exemplars. The pipeline produces photorealistic defect images across six categories—scratches, pits, cracks, stains, delamination, and inclusion—on both metallic and polymer substrates. A systematic evaluation protocol measures the downstream impact of synthetic augmentation on detection model performance using three standard industrial datasets. Models trained with a 70% synthetic / 30% real mixture achieve accuracy within 3.2% of fully supervised baselines trained on complete real datasets, while reducing annotation effort by approximately 80%. The study also benchmarks the realism of generated images using FID and a domain-expert perceptual rating study. The findings support synthetic data generation as a cost-effective strategy for bootstrapping quality control systems in low-data manufacturing environments.

title: Adaptive anomaly detection for multi-product assembly lines using one-class contrastive learning
abstract: Modern assembly lines frequently switch between product variants, requiring inspection systems that adapt rapidly to new normal-appearance distributions without collecting defect examples in advance. This paper presents an adaptive one-class contrastive learning framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in multi-product settings. The approach uses a momentum-updated reference encoder and an online memory bank of normal embeddings that is refreshed at product changeover events, enabling the model to track appearance shifts without full retraining. A self-supervised pretext task based on synthetic local masking strengthens the encoder's sensitivity to subtle textural and structural anomalies. The framework is evaluated on a novel multi-variant industrial benchmark—PolyAssembly-7—covering seven polymer component types across four product families. It achieves an average AUROC of 93.1% across all variants and demonstrates adaptation in fewer than 50 unlabeled normal samples per changeover, outperforming five established one-class detection baselines. Inference runs at 28 fps on an NVIDIA Jetson edge module. The results highlight the viability of continual anomaly detection for flexible manufacturing without persistent human annotation effort.

title: Knowledge distillation for lightweight surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware
abstract: Deploying high-accuracy surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware—spanning microcontrollers, FPGAs, and GPU-equipped single-board computers—requires models that balance computational cost with detection performance across very different hardware profiles. This paper proposes a hardware-aware knowledge distillation pipeline in which a large teacher network transfers representational knowledge to a suite of student architectures of varying capacities, each targeting a specific hardware tier. A novel attention-alignment distillation loss aligns intermediate feature maps at multiple scales, preserving fine-grained defect discriminability in the student networks. Experiments on three industrial surface inspection datasets show that the distilled lightweight students retain 95–98% of teacher mAP while reducing multiply-accumulate operations by 4× to 11× depending on the target hardware. We further present a hardware profiling methodology that automates student architecture selection given user-defined latency and accuracy constraints. The complete pipeline is released as an open-source toolkit, enabling non-expert practitioners to generate inspection-ready models for their specific edge deployment targets.

title: Domain randomization strategies for cross-industry transfer in visual defect detection
abstract: Visual defect detection models trained on one industrial domain often fail to generalize when transferred to a different material type, surface finish, or manufacturing process. This paper systematically investigates domain randomization as a transfer-enabling strategy, examining how randomization of texture, illumination, background clutter, and camera parameters during synthetic training data generation affects cross-domain transferability. A large-scale factorial experiment is conducted across six source-target domain pairs spanning metallic, ceramic, and textile substrates. Results show that targeted randomization of illumination direction and surface reflectance parameters yields the largest gains in target-domain detection accuracy, while excessive geometric randomization can degrade performance. Building on these findings, we propose an adaptive randomization curriculum that progressively increases domain diversity during training, guided by a domain-gap estimator computed from unlabeled target samples. The curriculum approach achieves a 6.8% average mAP improvement over static randomization across all transfer pairs, demonstrating a principled path toward generalizable industrial vision systems that require minimal target-domain labeling.

title: Temporal consistency regularization for video-based industrial anomaly detection
abstract: Frame-level anomaly detectors applied to industrial video streams often produce temporally inconsistent predictions, flagging and clearing the same defect region across successive frames due to minor illumination or motion changes. This paper introduces a temporal consistency regularization scheme that enforces smooth anomaly score trajectories across video frames without requiring ground-truth temporal annotations. A recurrent scoring head aggregates frame-level embeddings over a short sliding window, and a consistency loss penalizes abrupt score oscillations that are inconsistent with the physical persistence of genuine defects. The approach is evaluated on a new video inspection dataset—ConveyorVID—capturing three product types under realistic factory floor conditions including vibration, partial occlusion, and varying conveyor speed. The regularized model reduces the false-positive rate by 31% and improves temporal F1 score by 8.4 points compared to a strong frame-level baseline, with a negligible increase in computational overhead. Qualitative results confirm that the detector maintains stable anomaly localization across frames, a property that is critical for downstream alarm-triggering logic in automated quality control systems.

title: Federated learning for privacy-preserving collaborative defect model training across SME factories
abstract: Small and medium enterprises in manufacturing are often reluctant to share proprietary defect imagery due to intellectual property and competitive concerns, yet individually they lack the data volume needed to train robust inspection models. This paper presents a federated learning framework designed specifically for collaborative defect detection across multiple SME factories, where each factory trains a local model on its own data and only gradient updates are communicated to a central aggregation server. A defect-class-aware aggregation strategy weights participant contributions proportionally to their class coverage, mitigating the class imbalance that arises when different factories produce different defect types. Communication efficiency is improved through structured gradient sparsification tailored to convolutional inspection model architectures. The framework is validated in a simulated federation of six virtual factories instantiated from three public industrial datasets partitioned to mimic realistic cross-factory data heterogeneity. Federated models match the accuracy of centrally trained counterparts within 4% mAP while transmitting less than 12% of the raw gradient volume, demonstrating practical feasibility for bandwidth-constrained industrial networks.

title: Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines
abstract: Labeling defect images in industrial settings is expensive and requires domain expertise, making the efficient allocation of annotation effort a critical practical concern. This paper proposes an active learning framework for industrial defect detection that uses ensemble-based model uncertainty to prioritize the most informative unlabeled samples for expert annotation. A Monte Carlo dropout ensemble estimates epistemic uncertainty at the instance and region levels, and a diversity-aware sampling strategy prevents the selection of redundant near-duplicate crops from the same production batch. The framework is integrated into a realistic annotation pipeline validated with two industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-molded plastic components. Across both domains, the active learning approach achieves 90% of fully supervised baseline performance using only 35% of the total available labeled data, reducing annotation cost by an estimated 58% in practitioner time. A user study with three quality control engineers confirms that the uncertainty-guided sample ordering significantly reduces the cognitive load of the labeling process compared to random sample presentation.

title: Edge-cloud collaborative inference for latency-constrained industrial visual inspection
abstract: Industrial visual inspection scenarios impose strict latency requirements that may not be met by cloud-only inference, yet edge devices alone cannot always host the most accurate detection models. This paper proposes an edge-cloud collaborative inference architecture that dynamically partitions model execution between an on-premise edge node and a remote cloud server based on real-time estimates of network latency, sample difficulty, and inspection urgency. An early-exit mechanism on the edge node resolves easy, high-confidence samples locally while routing ambiguous samples to the cloud for processing by a more powerful model. A difficulty estimator trained with self-supervised pretext tasks predicts inference complexity before full forward-pass execution, enabling proactive routing decisions with negligible overhead. Experiments on two industrial conveyor-line inspection scenarios show that the collaborative architecture achieves 96.3% of full cloud accuracy while reducing average end-to-end latency by 47% and cloud compute cost by 38% under typical factory network conditions. Ablation experiments isolate the contributions of the early-exit mechanism and the proactive difficulty estimator, confirming that both components are necessary for the performance-latency trade-off.

title: Diurnal and seasonal variation of fair-weather atmospheric electric field at a lowland site in northern Serbia
abstract: Fair-weather atmospheric electric field (AEF) measurements collected over 28 months at the Rimski Šančevi field station using a JCI 131 field mill are analysed. The dataset covers 2012–2014 after strict fair-weather filtering based on aerosol optical depth and cloud-cover criteria. A pronounced diurnal cycle peaking near 18–19 UTC, consistent with the Carnegie curve, is identified, with a mean daily amplitude of 32 V/m. Seasonal modulation shows higher mean values in autumn (148 V/m) relative to summer (112 V/m), attributed partly to regional aerosol loading. Spectral analysis reveals a secondary 8-hour harmonic not commonly reported at continental European sites. The results are compared with simultaneous measurements at the Stará Lesná observatory in Slovakia, showing broadly coherent patterns with a phase lag of approximately 40 minutes. The study provides a baseline characterisation of AEF behaviour at lowland Pannonian sites and identifies local boundary-layer influence as a significant source of inter-annual variability.

title: Electric field evolution during an isolated supercell over the middle Danube basin on 5 June 2015
abstract: A detailed case study documents the atmospheric electric field signature of a well-observed isolated supercell that crossed the Bačka plain on 5 June 2015. Surface electric field mill data at 1 Hz resolution are combined with C-band Doppler radar reflectivity and radiosonde profiles to reconstruct the charge structure evolution. The prestorm fair-weather field of +120 V/m reversed to negative values approximately 40 minutes before the first lightning, associated with the leading anvil overhead. Three distinct charge-reversal events correspond to stages of updraft intensification identified in the radar data. Peak negative fields of −4800 V/m were recorded during the mature stage. A simple two-layer charge model is inferred using the method of moments, yielding a positive charge centre near 8.5 km and a main negative charge at 5.2 km altitude. Hail signature at the surface coincided with a secondary field minimum. The study illustrates the diagnostic potential of a single-station field mill when supplemented with independent storm observations.

title: Calibration and long-term stability assessment of field mill sensors in a continental humid climate
abstract: The operational reliability of three JCI 131 electric field mill units deployed across northern Serbia is evaluated over a five-year period (2014–2019). Sensor offset drift, rotor contamination, and connector corrosion are identified as the dominant maintenance issues at continental lowland sites with high summer humidity. A field-portable calibration apparatus consisting of a parallel-plate capacitor driven by a stable DC source is constructed and described in detail, allowing in-situ calibration without removal of the sensor. Repeated calibrations at 6-month intervals show mean sensitivity drift rates of 0.8 % per year across the fleet. Temperature dependence of the preamplifier gain is characterised over −15 °C to +45 °C. A correction procedure based on simultaneously recorded ambient temperature and relative humidity reduces residual scatter in fair-weather baseline records by 18 %. Maintenance recommendations adapted to the regional climate are outlined. The calibration protocol described here has since been adopted by two partner institutions in Hungary and Romania.

title: Influence of Saharan dust intrusions on fair-weather atmospheric electric field over the Pannonian Basin
abstract: Four Saharan dust intrusion episodes recorded in spring and early summer over 2018–2021 are examined for their effect on near-surface atmospheric electric field at two Serbian monitoring sites. Aerosol optical depth data from a CIMEL photometer and back-trajectory analyses from the HYSPLIT model are used to identify and time dust episodes. During confirmed intrusion days, mean AEF values were elevated by 22–38 % compared to aerosol-free fair-weather days at the same sites. The correlation between columnar aerosol optical depth at 500 nm and AEF is statistically significant (r = 0.61, p < 0.01, n = 47 days). A simple columnar resistance model is applied; the inferred increase in column resistance during dust events is consistent with the observed field enhancement under the global circuit framework. The findings suggest that episodic mineral aerosol loading is a non-negligible source of variability in long-term AEF records at southern Pannonian sites.

title: Surface electric field as a short-range proxy for convective initiation: statistical evaluation over a five-year dataset
abstract: The potential of near-surface electric field observations to supplement standard meteorological triggers for convective initiation warnings is assessed using five years (2018–2022) of 1 Hz field mill data from three Vojvodina stations combined with operational radar data and SYNOP reports. A total of 312 convective events are classified by storm type (single-cell, multi-cell, supercell, organised squall line). Receiver operating characteristic analysis is used to determine threshold crossing criteria. A threshold of −500 V/m at any station, sustained for at least 4 consecutive minutes, yields a probability of detection of 0.73 with a false alarm ratio of 0.31 for events within 25 km of the station. Performance degrades substantially beyond 40 km. Supercells are detected earlier (median lead time 22 min) than single-cell convection (median 8 min). The results indicate that electric field monitoring is useful as a supplementary indicator but insufficient as a standalone warning tool at the current network density. Recommendations for minimum network spacing are derived.

title: Atmospheric electricity monitoring networks: instrumentation, siting criteria, and data quality
abstract: This chapter provides a practical treatment of the design and operation of ground-based atmospheric electric field monitoring networks, with particular emphasis on temperate continental environments. Topics covered include field mill operating principles, siting requirements to avoid local electrode effect distortions, cabling and shielding best practices, data acquisition configurations, and common failure modes encountered in field deployments. Quality control procedures including automated fair-weather filtering, spike removal, and baseline drift correction are described with worked examples drawn from the Vojvodina network. The chapter also addresses the integration of electric field data streams with lightning location and meteorological sensor data. A section on network expansion considerations discusses cost–benefit trade-offs for sparse versus dense network geometries. The chapter is aimed at researchers and technical staff planning new installations or expanding existing regional networks in southeastern and central Europe.

title: Effect of pH on lycopene stability and emulsion droplet charge in whey protein-stabilised oil-in-water systems
abstract: Lycopene-loaded emulsions stabilised with whey protein isolate (1.5 % w/v) were prepared at pH 3.0, 5.0, 7.0, and 8.5 to map the relationship between interfacial charge, droplet aggregation behaviour, and pigment retention over 14 days at 25 °C in the dark. Zeta potential shifted from +28 mV at pH 3.0 to −38 mV at pH 7.0 and became less negative at pH 8.5 (−22 mV). Lycopene loss was greatest at pH 5.0 (46 % over 14 days), coinciding with the protein isoelectric point and maximum droplet aggregation (d₄₃ rising to 1.8 µm). Retention was highest at pH 3.0 (18 % loss). Fluorescence spectroscopy confirmed conformational changes in adsorbed whey protein near the isoelectric point. Results suggest that protein structural rearrangement at pH 5.0 exposes lycopene to prooxidants more readily than at acidic or alkaline conditions.

title: Photo-oxidative degradation of lutein in oil-in-water nanoemulsions under fluorescent and UV-A irradiation: a comparative kinetic study
abstract: Lutein-loaded nanoemulsions (mean droplet diameter 148 ± 9 nm, prepared by high-pressure homogenisation at 800 bar) were exposed to fluorescent light (1200 lux) and UV-A radiation (365 nm, 4 W m⁻²) for up to 72 h. Lutein content, peroxide value, and malondialdehyde concentration were measured at 6 h intervals. Under UV-A, lutein half-life was 11.3 h compared to 38.7 h under fluorescent light. Peroxide value increased sixfold faster under UV-A. Addition of 0.05 % tocopherol to the oil phase extended UV-A half-life to 19.1 h and suppressed malondialdehyde formation by 34 %. Degradation products were tentatively identified by LC-MS as 5,6-epoxylutein and lutein endoperoxide. The data indicate that lipid co-oxidation substantially accelerates lutein loss under UV-A and that even modest antioxidant supplementation provides meaningful protection.

title: Combined thermal and UV-A stress on astaxanthin nanoemulsions: degradation modelling using the Weibull function
abstract: The adequacy of first-order and Weibull models for describing astaxanthin loss under simultaneous thermal (55 °C) and UV-A (4 W m⁻²) stress was evaluated in lecithin-stabilised nanoemulsions over 48 h. Astaxanthin was quantified by HPLC-DAD at 476 nm. The Weibull model provided a significantly better fit (mean RMSE 0.031 vs. 0.058 for first-order) and described an initial acceleration phase (shape factor β = 1.41) followed by a slower tail, interpreted as depletion of the most accessible pigment fraction. Droplet size increased from 162 nm to 289 nm over 48 h, and oxidative markers (conjugated dienes, TBARS) showed a non-linear accumulation pattern consistent with the Weibull shape. Lecithin concentration (0.5 vs. 1.0 %) had no significant effect on kinetic parameters, suggesting that interfacial coverage above a threshold does not further retard combined stressors.

title: Influence of carrier oil composition on β-carotene photodegradation rate in oil-in-water nanoemulsions: sunflower, medium-chain triglyceride and hemp seed oil compared
abstract: Three carrier oils differing in fatty acid profile—refined sunflower oil (high linoleic), medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) oil (saturated), and cold-pressed hemp seed oil (ω-3/ω-6 balance 1:3)—were evaluated as lipid phases in β-carotene nanoemulsions (1 % oil, 0.5 % lecithin) under 12 h fluorescent light exposure (1200 lux). Mean initial droplet diameters were comparable across formulations (145–168 nm). β-Carotene photodegradation rate constants were 0.031, 0.012, and 0.049 h⁻¹ for sunflower, MCT, and hemp seed oil emulsions, respectively. The markedly higher rate in hemp seed emulsions correlated with faster peroxide value increases (r = 0.94) attributed to the high polyunsaturated fatty acid content. MCT emulsions showed the lowest lipid oxidation and the best pigment retention, supporting their use where oxidative stability is prioritised over nutritional fatty acid profile.

title: Encapsulation of zeaxanthin in Maillard-conjugate-stabilised nanoemulsions: preparation conditions and storage stability at 4 °C and 25 °C
abstract: Maillard conjugates were prepared from pea protein isolate and maltodextrin (DE 10) by dry heating at 60 °C, 79 % relative humidity, for 48 h, then used as emulsifiers at 1.5 % w/v to produce zeaxanthin-loaded nanoemulsions by ultrasound emulsification (400 W, 8 min). Mean droplet diameter was 178 ± 11 nm; encapsulation efficiency was 94.2 ± 1.1 %. Emulsions were stored at 4 °C and 25 °C for 60 days in the dark. At 4 °C, zeaxanthin retention was 89 % and droplet size increase was negligible (Δd < 20 nm). At 25 °C, retention fell to 71 % and d₄₃ reached 390 nm by day 60, indicating gradual coalescence. Glycation degree (OPA assay) was 38 %, and conjugates with higher glycation provided marginally better emulsion stability. The data support refrigerated storage as a practical condition for zeaxanthin-fortified dairy-analog products.

title: Non-REM sleep staging and interictal spike frequency in temporal lobe epilepsy: a polysomnographic study
abstract: We performed overnight polysomnography combined with full 19-channel EEG in 28 patients with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy confirmed by MRI and video-EEG telemetry. Sleep was staged according to AASM 2007 criteria. Interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) rate was computed per epoch for N1, N2, N3, and REM stages. IED density was highest in N2 (mean 4.7 discharges/min, SD 2.1) compared with N3 (2.1/min) and REM (0.8/min). N3 sleep percentage was significantly reduced relative to age-matched controls (12.4% vs 19.8%, p=0.003). We found a negative correlation between N3 proportion and total IED count per night (r=−0.52, p=0.004). These findings suggest that IED accumulation in N2 may actively suppress slow-wave sleep entry. Arousals indexed by EEG were more frequent in patients with IED density above the median. The study provides quantitative baseline data for future intervention trials targeting sleep quality in this population.

title: Sleep spindle characteristics in patients with mesial temporal sclerosis and drug-resistant epilepsy
abstract: Sleep spindles are generated by thalamocortical circuits that overlap anatomically with seizure propagation pathways in mesial temporal sclerosis (MTS). We analysed automatic spindle detection output from overnight polysomnography recordings of 22 MTS patients and 22 healthy volunteers matched for age and sex. Spindle density (spindles per minute of N2 sleep), amplitude, and duration were compared between groups and between spindle-rich and spindle-poor hemispheres estimated from referential EEG derivations. MTS patients showed reduced spindle density (8.3 vs 12.7/min, p<0.001) and shorter mean spindle duration (0.61 vs 0.74 s, p=0.002). Ipsilateral derivations over the affected temporal lobe displayed 31% fewer spindles than contralateral derivations within the same patient. Spindle amplitude was not significantly different between groups. The asymmetry index correlated moderately with hippocampal volume loss on volumetric MRI (r=0.44, p=0.038). Results are discussed in terms of thalamic relay dysfunction secondary to hippocampal damage.

title: Subjective and objective sleep quality in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: discordance between questionnaire data and polysomnography
abstract: We examined whether self-reported sleep quality in drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients accurately reflects polysomnographic findings. Sixty-one consecutive patients completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) before undergoing standard overnight polysomnography. PSQI global scores indicated poor sleep in 74% of participants, but only 49% met polysomnographic criteria for sleep efficiency below 85%. Conversely, 18 patients with PSQI scores in the normal range showed significant polysomnographic abnormalities including elevated arousal index and reduced REM percentage. Agreement between ESS and mean sleep latency on polysomnography was poor (kappa=0.19). Patients on enzyme-inducing antiseizure medications reported worse subjective quality but showed less objective slow-wave suppression than those on sodium channel blockers. These discordances suggest that questionnaire instruments alone are insufficient for sleep assessment in this population and that objective polysomnography should accompany self-report measures in clinical and research protocols.

title: Effect of perampanel add-on therapy on sleep architecture in focal epilepsy: a prospective observational study
abstract: Perampanel, an AMPA receptor antagonist, is used as add-on therapy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Its sedative properties raise questions about effects on sleep architecture. We prospectively enrolled 34 patients commencing perampanel at 2 mg/day titrated to 8 mg/day over 12 weeks and performed polysomnography at baseline and after titration completion. Primary endpoints were changes in total sleep time, sleep efficiency, N3 percentage, and REM latency. Total sleep time increased by a mean of 28 min (95% CI 11–45, p=0.002). N3 percentage increased from 13.6% to 17.1% (p=0.018). REM latency increased from 94 to 126 min (p=0.009). Sleep efficiency improved modestly (81.4% to 84.9%, p=0.04). IED density in N2 showed a non-significant reduction (−0.9/min, p=0.12). Patient-reported sleepiness on ESS worsened in nine participants despite objective improvements. These findings suggest perampanel modifies slow-wave sleep positively but delays REM onset, with mixed subjective impact.

title: Ictal and postictal respiratory patterns detected by polysomnography in frontal lobe epilepsy: implications for nocturnal monitoring
abstract: Frontal lobe seizures frequently occur during sleep and can be mistaken for parasomnias or obstructive sleep apnoea events. We reviewed polysomnographic recordings from 19 patients with video-EEG confirmed frontal lobe epilepsy who underwent split-night polysomnography during inpatient monitoring. Respiratory channels, pulse oximetry, and electromyography were analysed in relation to electrographically confirmed ictal and postictal periods. Desaturation below 90% occurred in 68% of captured nocturnal seizures; mean nadir SpO2 was 84% (range 71–92%). Postictal central apnoea lasting more than 10 seconds was documented in 11 of 19 patients. Nasal airflow attenuation preceded EEG seizure onset by a mean of 4.1 seconds in seven patients, representing a potential early biomarker. Leg EMG artifact obscured seizure onset in 37% of events. These observations suggest that polysomnographic respiratory channels add clinically meaningful information beyond scalp EEG in nocturnal frontal lobe epilepsy management.

title: Cyclic alternating pattern analysis in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: relationship with interictal discharge burden
abstract: The cyclic alternating pattern (CAP) is a marker of NREM sleep instability quantified by alternating A-phase subtypes (A1, A2, A3) and intervening B-phases. We applied CAP scoring to polysomnographic recordings of 40 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. CAP rate was significantly higher in patients (56.3% vs 38.7%, p<0.001). The A2 and A3 subtypes, reflecting cortical arousal, were disproportionately elevated in patients relative to A1 subtypes, yielding a higher A2+A3 to A1 ratio (1.8 vs 0.9, p<0.001). Within the patient group, nights with IED density above the group median showed higher CAP rate (60.1% vs 51.4%, p=0.014) and longer mean A-phase duration. Structural equation modelling indicated that IED density, CAP rate, and next-day attention performance were related in a chain pathway (χ²/df=1.7, RMSEA=0.048). CAP analysis may provide a sensitive index of epilepsy-related sleep fragmentation beyond conventional macroarchitecture scoring.

title: Sleep architecture in focal cortical dysplasia subtypes: MRI-confirmed type I versus type II lesions
abstract: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is a leading cause of drug-resistant epilepsy, yet differences in sleep architecture between FCD subtypes remain poorly characterised. We compared overnight polysomnography in 17 patients with histologically or radiologically classified FCD type I and 14 with FCD type II, all with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. FCD type II patients exhibited higher IED density across all NREM stages (N2: 6.2 vs 3.9/min, p=0.007) and more severe suppression of N3 sleep (8.7% vs 14.4%, p=0.012). REM percentage did not differ significantly between subtypes. High-frequency oscillations visible on polysomnographic EEG derivations overlying the lesion were more prevalent in type II (detected in 10/14 patients vs 5/17, p=0.038). Daytime sleepiness scores were worse in type II patients. These differences suggest that FCD subtype should be considered when interpreting sleep studies and designing sleep-targeted adjunct interventions in this population.

title: Sleep and epilepsy: a practical guide to polysomnographic assessment in adult neurology
abstract: This book chapter provides a practical framework for neurologists performing or interpreting polysomnography in adult patients with epilepsy. The chapter covers electrode placement considerations when epilepsy monitoring is integrated with polysomnography, AASM sleep staging as applied to epilepsy patients with diffuse interictal activity, and the distinction between parasomnias and nocturnal seizures using combined video, EEG, and respiratory channel review. Specific sections address artefact recognition in epilepsy patients on multiple antiseizure medications, scoring guidance for nights containing electrographic seizures, and interpretation caveats for patients with encephalopathy. Case examples drawn from the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina sleep laboratory illustrate common diagnostic dilemmas. The chapter also reviews current evidence on how seizure frequency and antiseizure drug class differentially affect sleep staging outcomes, providing summary tables for clinical reference. The intended audience is neurology residents and practising neurologists without formal sleep medicine training.

title: Automated IED detection during polysomnography: validation of a convolutional neural network pipeline against expert annotation in 60 recordings
abstract: Manual annotation of interictal epileptiform discharges in overnight polysomnographic recordings is time-consuming and prone to inter-rater variability. We developed and validated a convolutional neural network (CNN) pipeline trained on 140 annotated overnight recordings from the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina sleep laboratory and tested it on an independent validation set of 60 recordings (30 temporal lobe, 30 frontal lobe epilepsy). The model achieved sensitivity of 88.3% and specificity of 91.6% at the epoch level for IED detection compared with consensus annotation by two senior neurophysiologists. False-positive rates were highest in N1 sleep due to vertex waves and K-complex morphology overlap. Processing time per full overnight recording was 4.2 minutes on standard laboratory hardware. Per-stage IED density computed by the model correlated strongly with manual counts (r=0.91). The pipeline is intended as a research tool to reduce annotation burden in sleep–epilepsy studies and does not replace clinical review.

title: Impact of lacosamide versus levetiracetam add-on therapy on sleep macroarchitecture: a randomised crossover polysomnographic study
abstract: Lacosamide and levetiracetam are both used as add-on therapies in focal epilepsy, but their differential effects on sleep architecture have not been compared in a controlled setting. We conducted a randomised, open-label crossover study in 38 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy who were assigned to lacosamide or levetiracetam add-on for 12 weeks before crossing over after a four-week washout. Overnight polysomnography was performed at baseline, after each treatment period, and after washout. Lacosamide treatment was associated with a modest increase in N2 percentage (+4.1%) and reduction in REM percentage (−3.2%, p=0.027) relative to baseline. Levetiracetam showed no significant macroarchitecture changes. IED density in N2 was marginally lower under lacosamide (−1.1/min, p=0.06). Behavioural adverse effects (irritability, rated on a standardised scale) were higher under levetiracetam and correlated with poorer subjective sleep scores. Neither drug significantly altered total sleep time or sleep efficiency. The results inform drug selection for patients who also report sleep complaints.

title: High-density EEG polysomnography as a presurgical tool in drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy: concordance with intracranial EEG source estimates
abstract: In a subset of presurgical candidates, it remains unclear whether non-invasive source localisation during sleep IEDs can approximate findings from intracranial EEG (iEEG). We prospectively enrolled 21 patients with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy undergoing stereo-EEG (SEEG) evaluation and performed 64-channel overnight polysomnography within two weeks before electrode implantation. IED clusters identified during N2 sleep were submitted to equivalent current dipole modelling and standardised low-resolution electromagnetic tomography. Source estimates were compared with the clinically designated seizure onset zone from SEEG. Agreement within one gyrus was achieved in 15 of 21 patients (71%). Source estimates were closer to the SEEG onset zone for IEDs occurring during N2 sleep relative to those in N1 (mean Euclidean distance 14.2 mm vs 21.8 mm, p=0.018). These preliminary data suggest that sleep-state selection matters for non-invasive source analysis and that N2-restricted IED averaging improves localisation accuracy without requiring additional awake monitoring sessions.

title: Mass spectrometry-based quantification of tau phosphopeptides in CSF: comparison with immunoassay in a regional dementia cohort
abstract: Immunoassays for phospho-tau rely on antibody specificity that may vary across lots and manufacturers. We developed and validated a targeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method for simultaneous quantification of tau phosphopeptides spanning residues 173–184 (pT181) and 212–221 (pT217) in CSF, using stable isotope-labelled internal standards. The method was applied to 95 CSF samples from Vojvodina (35 AD, 30 MCI, 30 controls). Calibration curves were linear from 5 to 500 pg/mL (R²>0.998); inter-day CV was <9% for both peptides. Spearman correlations with the respective immunoassays were r=0.86 for pT181 and r=0.81 for pT217. MS-based quantification confirmed the diagnostic superiority of pT217 (AUC 0.93 vs 0.88 for pT181). Two samples showing immunoassay outlier values were confirmed normal by MS, suggesting matrix interference in the immunoassay. This method provides a reference platform for regional immunoassay calibration.
venue: Journal of Proteomics and Neurochemistry

title: Thermal detection thresholds in type 2 diabetic patients with and without painful neuropathy: a cross-sectional study
abstract: We applied a standardised quantitative sensory testing (QST) protocol derived from the German Research Network on Neuropathic Pain (DFNS) to 64 patients with type 2 diabetes recruited from the endocrinology outpatient service of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Patients were divided into painful neuropathy (n=31) and painless neuropathy (n=33) groups on the basis of structured interview and the Douleur Neuropathique 4 questionnaire. Both groups showed significantly elevated warm detection thresholds at the dorsum of the foot compared with healthy controls (n=40), consistent with small-fibre dysfunction. The painful group additionally demonstrated paradoxical heat sensation at a higher rate (48% vs 18%, p=0.012) and lower mechanical pain thresholds at the hand, suggesting a pattern of preserved or enhanced central sensitisation alongside peripheral deafferentation. Cooling detection thresholds did not differ significantly between pain groups. These results support a loss-of-function phenotype with superimposed gain-of-function features in the painful subgroup and underscore the need to characterise sensory profiles rather than treating neuropathic pain as a single entity.

title: Automatska klasifikacija sudskih odluka korišćenjem SVM klasifikatora i TF-IDF reprezentacije
abstract: Rad predstavlja sistem za automatsku klasifikaciju sudskih odluka Vrhovnog kasacionog suda Republike Srbije u 12 pravnih oblasti. Korpus se sastoji od 4.200 anonimizovanih odluka prikupljenih između 2003. i 2008. godine. Primenjen je SVM klasifikator sa linearnim jezgrom na TF-IDF vektorizovanim tekstovima, uz eksperimentisanje sa različitim veličinama n-grama (unigrami, bigrami i trigrami). Evaluacija je sprovedena petostukim unakrsnim validiranjem. Najbolji rezultat postignut je kombinacijom unigrama i bigrama: makro F1 mera iznosila je 0,81. Analiza grešaka pokazuje da su kategorije sa malim brojem primera i dvosmislenom terminologijom (npr. radno pravo u odnosu na privredno pravo) najtežie za razlikovanje. Rad takođe opisuje postupak anotacije i metriku inter-anotatorne saglasnosti (Koen kapa = 0,79).
venue: Journal of Information and Organizational Sciences

title: Building a Manually Annotated Corpus of Serbian Legal Texts for NLP Benchmarking
abstract: This paper describes the construction and release of SerbLex-1.0, a manually annotated corpus of 8,500 Serbian legal documents spanning legislation, court rulings, and administrative decisions from 1995 to 2010. Annotation covers sentence boundaries, named entities (persons, organisations, locations, dates), and thematic categories across 18 legal domains. Inter-annotator agreement was measured on a 1,200-document subset, yielding a Cohen's kappa of 0.76 for named entity spans and 0.83 for thematic labels. The paper reports baseline performance figures for three established classifiers—Naive Bayes, maximum entropy, and SVM—alongside a rule-based tokeniser adapted for Serbian legal orthography. Corpus statistics reveal significant class imbalance, with commercial law and civil procedure accounting for over 40% of documents. The corpus is made available under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence.
