title: Polu-nadgledano učenje za kategorizaciju zakonodavnih izmena u srpskom pravnom sistemu
abstract: Ovaj rad istražuje primenu polu-nadgledanih metoda klasifikacije na problem automatskog prepoznavanja vrsta izmena u zakonodavnim tekstovima (dopune, brisanja, supstitucije i terminološke promene). Polazni skup označenih primera obuhvata 620 ručno obeleženih paragrafa iz Službenog glasnika RS za period 2008–2012, dok se polu-nadgledana komponenta oslanja na 14.000 neobeleženih paragrafa. Testirana su tri pristupa: samo-učenje (self-training), ko-učenje (co-training) sa dva pogleda (leksički i sintaksički) i grafovski zasnovano širenje oznaka (label propagation). Ko-učenje postiže makro F1 od 0,74 u odnosu na 0,68 kod čisto nadgledanog modela pri istoj količini označenih podataka. Rad analizira uticaj veličine inicijalnog labeled skupa (50, 200 i 620 primera) na stabilnost rezultata i predlaže heuristiku za odabir pouzdanih samoobeleženih primera.

title: Semantic Similarity Measures for Matching Legal Clauses Across Jurisdictions
abstract: Identifying equivalent or near-equivalent clauses in contract law documents from different national jurisdictions is an important task for comparative legal research and cross-border compliance. This study evaluates six semantic similarity measures—cosine similarity over TF-IDF vectors, BM25, word mover's distance, averaged word2vec embeddings, Doc2Vec, and a fine-tuned multilingual sentence encoder—on a manually constructed parallel dataset of 1,840 clause pairs drawn from Serbian, Croatian, and Austrian commercial contracts. Each pair was labelled by two legal experts as equivalent, partially equivalent, or non-equivalent. Spearman correlation between model scores and expert ratings is reported for each method. The fine-tuned sentence encoder achieves ρ = 0.71, substantially outperforming the TF-IDF baseline (ρ = 0.48). Error analysis shows that domain-specific terminology and negation patterns are the main sources of failure across all methods.
venue: International Journal of Legal Information Technology

title: Detekcija anomalija u javnim nabavkama primenom metoda obrade teksta i statističkog modeliranja
abstract: Rad opisuje sistem za automatsku detekciju potencijalno neregularnih tender dokumenata u bazi javnih nabavki Republike Srbije. Korišćen je skup od 23.400 tenderskih specifikacija objavljenih između 2013. i 2016. godine. Anomalije su definisane u tri kategorije: neuobičajeni tehnički uslovi koji ograničavaju konkurenciju, nekonzistentna upotreba merne jedinice i vrednosti, i kopiranje teksta između naizgled nepovezanih ponuda. Za detekciju prve kategorije primenjen je one-class SVM na TF-IDF vektorima; za drugu je korišćena statistička kontrolna karta zasnovana na z-skoru numerički ekstrahovanih vrednosti; za treću fuzzy heširanje (MinHash LSH). Sistem je validiran na 200 ručno pregledanih primera od strane revizora Državne revizorske institucije, pri čemu je postignut recall od 0,83 i precision od 0,61. Rad diskutuje ograničenja uzrokovana kvalitetom izvornih OCR dokumenata.

title: Domain Adaptation of Pre-trained Word Embeddings for South Slavic Legal Text
abstract: General-purpose word embedding models trained on news and web corpora perform poorly on legal text due to the divergent distribution of technical and archaic terminology. This paper investigates three domain adaptation strategies—continued training, vocabulary extension, and retrofitting with a legal synonym lexicon—applied to publicly available fastText models for Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian. Adaptation uses a 120-million-token corpus assembled from national gazettes and court databases. Intrinsic evaluation uses a newly constructed legal word analogy set (3,200 quadruples) and a legal similarity judgement set (480 pairs). The retrofitting approach yields the largest gains on similarity judgements, improving Spearman correlation from 0.38 to 0.57 for Serbian. Downstream evaluation on two classification tasks (document type and legal domain) shows improvements of 2–4 F1 points over unadapted embeddings. All adapted models and evaluation sets are released publicly.

title: Fine-Tuning BERT for Regulatory Compliance Classification in the Energy Sector
abstract: This study examines the performance of fine-tuned BERT-based models for classifying technical regulatory documents from the Serbian and European energy sector according to a compliance taxonomy with 24 leaf categories. A domain-specific corpus of 9,800 labelled documents was constructed from the regulatory archive of the Energy Agency of the Republic of Serbia and publicly available EU energy directives, with labels assigned by two certified compliance officers. Four model variants were compared: multilingual BERT, Serbian-only BERT, a legal-domain BERT pre-trained on EU legislative text (LegalBERT-EU), and a baseline TF-IDF+SVM pipeline. LegalBERT-EU achieved the highest macro F1 of 0.86, followed by Serbian BERT at 0.83. The SVM baseline reached 0.74. Attention analysis reveals that the transformer models rely heavily on modal verbs and obligation phrases as classification signals. Training and inference times are reported for a mid-range GPU server.

title: Detecting Contradictory Obligations in Contract Drafts Using Sentence-Level Entailment Models
abstract: Contracts drafted by multiple parties over successive revisions sometimes contain clauses that create contradictory obligations. This paper addresses automated detection of such contradictions using natural language inference (NLI) models adapted to contractual text. A dataset of 2,640 clause pairs was annotated by contract lawyers as entailment, neutral, or contradiction, drawn from 480 service-level agreements and supply contracts in Serbian and English. Cross-lingual zero-shot transfer from an English-trained NLI model achieves an F1 of 0.61 on the Serbian subset, while a fine-tuned multilingual model reaches 0.78. A rule-augmented hybrid system combining the NLI model with a hand-crafted deontic logic pattern library achieves 0.82 F1. Ablation experiments show the pattern library contributes most to recall on negation-based contradictions. The annotated dataset will be released upon acceptance.

title: Merenje semantičke sličnosti između srpskih zakonskih normi i korporativnih politika: pristup zasnovan na kontrastivnom učenju
abstract: Ovaj rad razmatra problem automatskog uparivanja zakonskih normi iz domaćeg zakonodavstva sa internim korporativnim politikama radi provere usklađenosti. Predložen je pristup zasnovan na kontrastivnom učenju gde su pozitivni parovi ručno definisani od strane compliance konsultanata, a negativni parovi uzorkovani iz različitih zakonskih oblasti. Model koristi dvotokový enkoder sa srpskim RoBERTa inicijalizacijom, finajtuiran na 3.200 anotiranih parova. Evaluacija obuhvata i standardnu preciznost na test skupu (mAP = 0,79) i praktičnu metriku odbranjenu pred poslovnim korisnicima: udeo slučajeva gde je tačan zakon rangiran unutar prvih tri rezultata (Recall@3 = 0,88). Poređenje sa BM25 i standardnim kosinus similaritetom na SBERT vektorima ukazuje na napredak od 9, odnosno 5 procentnih poena za Recall@3. Model je integrisan u prototip alata za compliance koji je testiran u dve kompanije iz finansijskog sektora.

title: Evaluacija velikih jezičkih modela na zadacima pravnog rezonovanja u srpskom jeziku
abstract: Rad sistematski procenjuje sposobnost četiri velika jezička modela (LLM) – GPT-4o, Llama 3 70B, Mistral Large i srpski prilagođen model SrbGPT-7B – na skupu zadataka pravnog rezonovanja u srpskom jeziku. Definisano je pet zadataka: identifikacija relevantnog zakonskog osnova, detekcija kršenja proceduralnih normi, ekstrakcija strana u sporu, summarizacija presude u propisanom formatu i klasifikacija u pravnu oblast. Svaki zadatak pokriva 200 primera, ručno proverenih od strane pravnih stručnjaka. GPT-4o postiže najvišu tačnost u četiri od pet zadataka (73–89%), dok SrbGPT-7B, uprkos mnogo manjem broju parametara, postiže konkurentne rezultate na morfološki zahtevnijim zadacima ekstrakcije. Rad identifikuje sistematske greške u razumevanju negacije i upućivanja na prethodne stavove (anaphora resolution) kao zajednički problem svih modela. Zaključci su relevantni za procenu praktične primenljivosti LLM-ova u pravosudnom kontekstu.

title: Continual Learning for Evolving Legal Taxonomies: Preventing Catastrophic Forgetting in Serbian Statutory Classification
abstract: Legal classification systems face a practical challenge: national legislatures periodically restructure statutory categories, requiring models to learn new classes without forgetting old ones. This paper applies five continual learning strategies—fine-tuning, elastic weight consolidation (EWC), progressive neural networks, experience replay, and a generative replay variant using a lightweight language model—to a Serbian statutory classification task spanning three taxonomy versions issued between 2018 and 2024. Each taxonomy update introduces between two and seven new categories and retires one to three existing ones. Performance is measured using backward transfer, forward transfer, and average accuracy across all versions. EWC and generative replay show the smallest backward transfer (0.04 and 0.03 average F1 drop respectively) while maintaining competitive forward transfer. Naive fine-tuning exhibits catastrophic forgetting with a backward transfer of −0.19. The study provides practical guidance on update schedules and replay buffer sizing for operational legal NLP systems.

title: Bulk Density and Pore Size Distribution in Conventionally Tilled vs. No-Till Chernozem After Five Years of Continuous Maize Cropping
abstract: A five-year field trial on two adjacent plots under conventional mouldboard ploughing and no-till management was established in 2007 on a Haplic Chernozem near Srbobran, Vojvodina. Undisturbed soil cores were sampled at 0–10, 10–20, and 20–40 cm depths in autumn of each year. Bulk density was determined gravimetrically and pore size distribution was derived from water retention curves measured with a pressure plate apparatus at matric potentials of −0.01, −0.033, −0.1, −0.3, and −1.5 MPa. After five years, bulk density in the 0–10 cm layer under no-till was 1.41 Mg m⁻³ compared with 1.28 Mg m⁻³ under conventional tillage. Macroporosity (pores >30 µm) decreased by 18% in no-till topsoil, while mesopore volume (0.2–30 µm) increased by 11%, suggesting a redistribution rather than a net loss of pore space. No significant differences were found below 20 cm depth. Results indicate that short-term no-till adoption shifts the pore network toward finer pores, with implications for infiltration capacity and seedbed preparation for sunflower and soybean rotations.

title: Seasonal Variation in Soil Water Retention Parameters Under Strip-Till and No-Till Sugar Beet Production in Northern Vojvodina
abstract: Sugar beet fields on silty clay loam soils in the Subotica–Horgoš region were monitored over two growing seasons (2012–2013) to compare soil water retention under strip-till and full-width no-till treatments. Soil moisture was recorded continuously at 10, 30, and 60 cm depths using TDR probes installed in four replicate plots per treatment. Retention curve parameters (van Genuchten α and n) were fitted from weekly sampled cores and laboratory drainage measurements. Under strip-till, the van Genuchten n parameter at 10 cm depth averaged 1.38 compared with 1.22 under no-till, reflecting a broader pore size distribution in the loosened strips. Plant-available water capacity across the 0–60 cm profile was approximately 7 mm higher in strip-till plots during the driest July period. These differences translated to a 4.2% higher sugar beet fresh root yield in strip-till, though inter-annual variability was substantial and confounded by rainfall distribution. The study argues for further multi-year replication before firm agronomic recommendations can be made.
venue: Journal of Central European Soil and Crop Research

title: Cone Penetration Resistance Profiles Across a Tillage Intensity Gradient on Vojvodina Loam Soils
abstract: Cone penetration resistance (CPR) was measured on four commercial farms in Vojvodina representing a gradient from deep subsoil loosening to continuous no-till, each with at least eight years of documented management history. Measurements were taken in spring and autumn of 2015 using a hand-pushed electronic cone penetrometer at 5 cm depth intervals to 70 cm. At least 20 insertions per plot were averaged per sampling date. No-till plots showed a distinct compaction peak between 12 and 22 cm depth, with CPR values reaching 2.8–3.3 MPa in spring under dry conditions, exceeding the commonly cited 2.0 MPa root restriction threshold. Subsoil-loosened plots showed peak CPR below 40 cm and lower resistance throughout the upper horizon. Gravimetric soil moisture at sampling was co-recorded to allow partial normalisation. The data support the conclusion that no-till systems on these medium-texture soils develop a tillage-pan analogue within a decade without periodic intervention, with potential consequences for deep-rooted crops such as sunflower.

title: Long-Term No-Till Effects on Saturated and Unsaturated Hydraulic Conductivity of a Calcic Chernozem: A 12-Year Dataset
abstract: This study presents hydraulic conductivity data collected annually from 2005 to 2016 on a long-term field experiment maintained by the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops in Rimski Šančevi. Saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ks) was determined in situ with a tension infiltrometer at matric potential heads of 0, −20, and −60 mm H₂O, allowing simultaneous estimation of the macropore-flow contribution. No-till plots exhibited Ks values at the soil surface approximately 35% higher than ploughed controls in 2016, up from negligible differences in 2007, attributed to a progressive development of continuous biopores from earthworm activity and root channels. Unsaturated conductivity at −60 mm head showed little difference between treatments across all years. Earthworm density counts, conducted in parallel on a subset of years, correlated positively with macropore Ks (r = 0.71, p < 0.01). The findings highlight a temporal trajectory in which biological macropore formation compensates for reduced tillage-induced aeration in established no-till systems, though this benefit appears restricted to the surface 15 cm.

title: Shrink–Swell Behaviour and Crack Formation in No-Till Clay Loam Soils of the South Bačka Region During Summer Drought
abstract: Soils with moderate clay content (28–34% clay fraction) in the South Bačka administrative district were monitored during the drought summer of 2017 for desiccation crack development under no-till management with a soybean–maize rotation and under conventional tillage. Crack width, depth, and areal density were mapped using a grid-frame photographic method at two-week intervals from late June to early September. Volumetric moisture content was monitored with TDR probes at 10 and 30 cm. Cracks first appeared in no-till plots at a mean volumetric moisture content of 0.22 m³ m⁻³ compared with 0.19 m³ m⁻³ in tilled plots, suggesting an earlier onset of shrinkage possibly linked to higher organic matter in the surface horizon. Maximum crack depth reached 41 cm in no-till versus 29 cm in tilled plots. Crack volume represented up to 6.8% of total soil volume at peak drought. The paper discusses implications for preferential flow, topsoil drying feedback, and re-wetting dynamics in autumn rainfall events, noting that rapid crack closure was observed after the first 20 mm rain event in early September.

title: Soil Physical Quality Indices Under Three Decades of Contrasting Tillage on Vojvodina Chernozem: A Comparison of S-Index, Air Capacity, and LLWR
abstract: Three integrated soil physical quality indices — the S-index (slope of the log–log water retention curve at the inflection point), air-filled porosity at field capacity, and the least limiting water range (LLWR) — were evaluated on archived soil cores and current field samples from a long-term experiment initiated in 1991 at Rimski Šančevi. Three treatments were compared: mouldboard ploughing to 30 cm, chisel ploughing to 25 cm, and continuous no-till. By 2021, the no-till treatment showed S-index values of 0.041 in the 0–5 cm layer (above the 0.035 critical threshold) but declined to 0.028 at 10–20 cm, indicating degraded structure at the critical transition depth. The LLWR was 0.09 m³ m⁻³ under no-till versus 0.13 m³ m⁻³ under mouldboard ploughing at the same depth, implying a narrower range of conditions suitable for field operations and root growth. Air capacity at field capacity was adequate (>0.10 m³ m⁻³) only in the surface 5 cm of no-till. Results are interpreted in the context of maize and wheat yield records from the same experiment, showing a moderate but consistent yield penalty for no-till in wetter-than-average years.

title: Effect of Tractor Wheel Traffic Frequency on Subsoil Compaction Persistence in a No-Till Maize System: Two-Year Recovery Monitoring
abstract: A controlled wheel-traffic experiment was conducted in 2022–2023 on a no-till field in Temerin municipality. Four traffic intensity levels (0, 2, 4, and 8 tractor passes of a 9-tonne axle load) were applied in spring 2022 to 6 × 40 m plots. Cone penetration resistance and bulk density at 5 cm intervals to 60 cm were measured immediately after trafficking, and then in autumn 2022, spring 2023, and autumn 2023. Immediately after trafficking, CPR at 30–40 cm exceeded 3.5 MPa for the 8-pass treatment. After two full growing seasons with no further disturbance, CPR at 30–40 cm remained at 2.9 MPa, indicating limited natural recovery at depth. The 0–10 cm layer showed partial recovery, reaching pre-treatment CPR values by autumn 2022, likely driven by freeze–thaw cycles and biological activity. A simple linear model explained 68% of variance in CPR recovery using initial compaction magnitude and depth as predictors. The results suggest that a single severe trafficking event causes subsoil compaction that persists well beyond the measurement period under no-till, reinforcing the agronomic value of controlled traffic farming.

title: Mapping Topsoil Compaction Risk Across Vojvodina Using Terrain Attributes, Soil Texture, and Traffic Load Data
abstract: A spatial compaction risk model was developed for the Vojvodina region using a 25 m digital elevation model, provincial soil survey texture data (clay and silt fractions), reported machinery axle loads from a farm survey conducted in 2023 (n = 114 farms), and long-term cropping system data from the agricultural census. Risk scores were computed by combining normalised layers for soil susceptibility (derived from texture and organic matter content), traffic frequency (workload index per ha), and topographic wetness index as a proxy for antecedent moisture. Validation was performed against 88 field CPR measurements taken across 22 sites in spring 2024. The model correctly classified compaction risk level (low/medium/high) in 74% of validation points. High-risk zones were concentrated in the flat, low-permeability soils of southern Bačka and along major crop production corridors. The study provides a reproducible, low-cost framework for prioritising on-farm compaction monitoring and for informing municipal land use planning in the context of heavy machinery use.

title: Magnetic structure determination of the pyrochlore oxide Yb2Zr2O7 by neutron powder diffraction
abstract: The magnetic structure of the pyrochlore oxide Yb2Zr2O7 was investigated using neutron powder diffraction at temperatures between 0.05 K and 10 K on the D20 high-flux diffractometer at the Institut Laue-Langevin. Rietveld refinement of the diffraction patterns collected at 0.08 K revealed an all-in–all-out spin arrangement on the Yb3+ pyrochlore sublattice, with an ordered moment of 1.24(3) μB per Yb site. No long-range order was detectable above 0.4 K, consistent with a broad heat-capacity anomaly centred near 0.25 K measured on a polycrystalline pellet using a quasi-adiabatic calorimeter. Magnetic diffuse scattering persisting well below the heat-capacity feature indicates short-range correlated spin clusters. Symmetry analysis using the BASIREPS program identified the Γ5 irreducible representation as best fitting the data. The results place Yb2Zr2O7 in the family of quantum spin ices rather than classical dipolar spin ices, in agreement with susceptibility measurements showing a negative Curie-Weiss temperature of −0.31(4) K.

title: Spin dynamics in the Tb2Ti2O7 pyrochlore from inelastic neutron scattering on a powder sample
abstract: Inelastic neutron scattering measurements on a polycrystalline sample of Tb2Ti2O7 were carried out on the IN4C time-of-flight spectrometer at ILL using incident energies of 3.5 meV and 8 meV at temperatures from 0.06 K to 50 K. The spectra show crystal-field excitations at 1.7 meV and 4.3 meV at 5 K, in good agreement with point-charge model calculations employing a trigonally distorted D3d environment. A quasielastic component persisting to the lowest measured temperature is consistent with persistent spin fluctuations and rules out static order in this compound above 60 mK. The integrated quasielastic intensity follows a Curie-like temperature dependence between 0.5 K and 10 K, with a characteristic fluctuation rate of approximately 2 × 10^9 s−1 extracted from a Lorentzian lineshape fit. Comparison with previous μSR data on this compound shows good quantitative consistency. The absence of any resolution-limited elastic magnetic Bragg peaks at the lowest temperatures confirms the spin-liquid ground state of Tb2Ti2O7.

title: Muon spin relaxation study of spin freezing in the spinel oxide NiCr2O4 under applied pressure
abstract: Zero-field and longitudinal-field muon spin relaxation (μSR) measurements were performed on the GPS instrument at the Paul Scherrer Institut on a polycrystalline NiCr2O4 sample enclosed in a copper–beryllium pressure cell delivering up to 12 kbar at temperatures from 2 K to 120 K. At ambient pressure, a sharp transition to a ferrimagnetically ordered phase at 74 K is followed by a spin-reorientation transition near 31 K, both visible as step-like increases in the early-time asymmetry. Under 9 kbar, the ferrimagnetic transition shifts to 69 K and the low-temperature reorientation broadens considerably, suggesting a distribution of local exchange parameters. The Kubo-Toyabe relaxation function fitted to the paramagnetic-phase data yields a static second moment Δ2 that increases by approximately 18% between ambient pressure and 12 kbar, interpreted as enhanced orbital overlap among Cr3+ ions on the B-site. These findings are discussed in the context of competing double-exchange and superexchange interactions in the normal-spinel geometry.

title: Neutron single-crystal diffraction on Ho2Sn2O7: mapping diffuse scattering in the spin-ice phase
abstract: Single-crystal neutron diffraction measurements on a flux-grown Ho2Sn2O7 crystal (mass 38 mg) were performed on the D10 diffractometer at ILL with a wavelength of 2.36 Å at 0.07 K, 0.5 K, 2 K, and 10 K. Within the (hhl) scattering plane, pinch-point diffuse scattering features were observed at the zone boundaries of the pyrochlore Brillouin zone at temperatures above 0.3 K, in the classical spin-ice phase. The pinch points sharpen and their transverse width decreases from 0.12(1) Å−1 at 2 K to 0.06(1) Å−1 at 0.5 K, consistent with the diverging correlation length of the emergent Coulomb phase. Below 0.3 K the diffuse scattering is replaced by resolution-limited Bragg peaks corresponding to an ordered all-in–all-out structure with propagation vector k = 0. Monte Carlo simulations using nearest-neighbour and dipolar interactions reproduce the experimental pinch-point maps to within 8% integrated intensity. The data provide direct real-space evidence that Ho2Sn2O7 undergoes a field-free ordering transition at low temperature, in contrast to the closely related Ho2Ti2O7.

title: Magnetic frustration in the breathing pyrochlore LiGaCr4O8 studied by neutron powder diffraction and heat capacity
abstract: The breathing pyrochlore LiGaCr4O8, in which Cr3+ ions form alternating large and small tetrahedra, was studied by neutron powder diffraction on the D2B instrument at ILL and by specific heat measurements from 0.35 K to 300 K. No long-range magnetic order was detected down to 0.35 K despite a Curie-Weiss temperature of −53(2) K, yielding a frustration index f ≈ 152. Diffuse magnetic scattering centred on the (111) and (002) positions is present below 5 K, indicating short-range correlations with a characteristic length of approximately 8 Å. The magnetic specific heat shows a broad maximum at 2.3 K and releases approximately 70% of the expected R ln(2S+1) entropy by 30 K. A linear-in-temperature electronic contribution to the specific heat is absent, ruling out a gapless spin-liquid state at the measured temperatures. Crystal-field analysis from the paramagnetic neutron cross-section above 30 K yields consistent g-factors with earlier ESR data.

title: Low-temperature magnetometry and AC susceptibility of frustrated Er2Ge2O7: comparison with neutron diffraction results
abstract: DC magnetisation and AC susceptibility measurements on a polycrystalline Er2Ge2O7 sample were performed in a SQUID magnetometer between 1.8 K and 300 K in applied fields up to 5 T. The zero-field-cooled and field-cooled DC curves diverge below 1.2 K, and the real part of the AC susceptibility shows a frequency-dependent peak near 0.9 K (at 100 Hz) with a shift of 0.04 per decade of frequency, characteristic of a spin-glass-like freezing. Complementary neutron powder diffraction at 0.08 K (D20, ILL) shows no magnetic Bragg peaks, confirming the absence of long-range order. The isothermal magnetisation at 0.08 K saturates at 4.7(1) μB per Er site, below the free-ion value of 9 μB, consistent with a strongly anisotropic crystal-field ground state. The Curie-Weiss fit above 50 K yields an effective moment of 9.4(2) μB and θCW = −0.68(5) K. These results establish Er2Ge2O7 as an XY pyrochlore antiferromagnet with a disordered ground state, relevant for theories of quantum order-by-disorder.

title: Frustrated magnetism in oxide thin films: potential and limitations of neutron reflectometry
abstract: This chapter reviews the application of polarised neutron reflectometry (PNR) to thin-film systems hosting geometrically frustrated magnetic lattices. PNR provides depth-resolved magnetisation profiles with sub-nanometre resolution and sensitivity to in-plane moments of the order of 0.1 μB per formula unit, making it complementary to bulk neutron diffraction. The chapter discusses the structural prerequisites for growing epitaxial pyrochlore and spinel films on perovskite substrates by pulsed-laser deposition, with representative examples from the literature covering film thicknesses from 10 nm to 200 nm. Particular attention is given to strain effects: biaxial strain of ±1.5% applied through substrate choice shifts the Curie-Weiss temperature by up to 12 K in model Cr-spinel films. Experimental challenges including incoherent background from hydrogen-containing substrates, limited in-plane momentum transfer, and beam-time constraints are discussed, along with strategies to mitigate them. The chapter closes with an outlook on combining PNR with time-of-flight inelastic techniques for studying spin dynamics in films.

title: Structural and magnetic characterisation of the spinel ZnFe2O4 nanoparticles prepared by solution combustion synthesis
abstract: ZnFe2O4 nanoparticles with mean diameters of 8, 14, and 22 nm were synthesised by solution combustion using urea as fuel and characterised by neutron powder diffraction, X-ray diffraction, and SQUID magnetometry. Neutron diffraction was essential for determining Fe/Zn site occupancies, revealing that 18(2)% of Fe3+ ions migrate to the A-site in the 8 nm sample, compared to 6(1)% in the bulk reference, indicating inversion disorder that increases with decreasing particle size. The magnetic moment extracted from Rietveld refinement of the 1.5 K neutron data is 3.6(1) μB per formula unit for the 8 nm particles, significantly above the near-zero value expected for normal-spinel ZnFe2O4. AC susceptibility shows a superparamagnetic blocking temperature of 38 K (at 100 Hz) for the 8 nm sample, rising to 62 K for 22 nm. The results are discussed in terms of size-dependent inversion and its effect on the competing superexchange interactions within the spinel B-sublattice.

title: Spin correlations in the kagome-like compound BaNi3(VO4)2(OH)2 from neutron total scattering and pair distribution function analysis
abstract: The local and average magnetic structure of BaNi3(VO4)2(OH)2, a compound with Ni2+ ions forming distorted kagome planes, was investigated using neutron total scattering on the GEM diffractometer at the ISIS Neutron and Muon Source, Harwell. Data were collected at 1.5 K, 10 K, and 50 K over a Q range of 0.3–40 Å−1. The magnetic pair distribution function (mPDF) extracted after subtraction of the nuclear contribution shows strong nearest-neighbour correlations decaying to noise within approximately 12 Å at all measured temperatures, with no transition to long-range order down to 1.5 K despite θCW = −28(1) K. The nearest-neighbour Ni–Ni correlation length grows from 3.1(2) Å at 50 K to 5.8(3) Å at 1.5 K. Reverse Monte Carlo modelling of the mPDF at 1.5 K is consistent with short-range order of the q = 0 type but cannot discriminate between it and a √3 × √3 configuration. Heat capacity measured from 0.35 K to 50 K releases 62% of R ln 3 below 10 K, consistent with substantial residual entropy at low temperatures.

title: Temperature-dependent crystal-field excitations in the frustrated oxide Pr2Hf2O7 from time-of-flight inelastic neutron scattering
abstract: Inelastic neutron scattering spectra of polycrystalline Pr2Hf2O7 were recorded on the PANTHER time-of-flight spectrometer at ILL at incident energies of 12 meV and 25 meV, covering temperatures from 0.06 K to 100 K. Seven crystal-field transitions were identified below 20 meV at 5 K; their energies and intensities were fitted simultaneously using a D3d point-group Hamiltonian with five independent parameters. The ground state is found to be a non-Kramers doublet with predominantly |±4⟩ character, separated from the first excited singlet by 1.9(1) meV. On cooling below 0.8 K, the elastic line acquires a magnetic component that grows monotonically without any sudden increase, inconsistent with a single sharp ordering transition. A quasielastic contribution broadens significantly below 2 K and narrows again below 0.3 K, suggesting a crossover in spin dynamics. These data are compared with published heat capacity and μSR results on Pr2Hf2O7, and the crystal-field parameters are used to estimate exchange anisotropy ratios relevant for quantum spin-ice model Hamiltonians.

title: Second-law efficiency of chemically powered microswimmer propulsion: a stochastic thermodynamics perspective
abstract: We define and compute the second-law efficiency of chemical-to-mechanical energy conversion in model phoretic microswimmers using a minimal three-state chemical network coupled to a Langevin equation for translational motion. The chemical driving force is parameterised by the free-energy drop per catalytic cycle, varied between 1 kT and 20 kT. Mechanical output power is calculated from the mean squared displacement after subtracting thermal contributions. Maximum efficiency does not coincide with maximum speed: it occurs at intermediate driving where the ratio of useful mechanical power to total dissipated power reaches a peak of about 3.5% for the parameter set considered. We show that efficiency is bounded above by a quantity analogous to the Carnot bound that depends on the ratio of the chemical relaxation time to the mechanical persistence time. Numerical results for 10⁴ simulated trajectories confirm the analytical bound is tight within 2%. These findings are relevant for comparing the performance of synthetic microswimmers with biological molecular motors.

title: Spectral properties of the time-fractional diffusion operator on bounded domains with mixed boundary conditions
abstract: This work examines the eigenvalue structure of the Caputo time-fractional diffusion operator defined on one- and two-dimensional bounded domains subject to mixed Dirichlet–Neumann boundary conditions. Using a Galerkin projection onto a Legendre polynomial basis, we derive a system of fractional ordinary differential equations and establish bounds on the real parts of the discrete spectrum for fractional orders α ∈ (0.5, 1.0). Numerical experiments on square and L-shaped domains with grid refinements from 32×32 to 256×256 nodes confirm that spectral abscissa decreases monotonically with α and that the first fifteen eigenvalues converge with order approximately 1.8 in the L² norm. The results suggest that for α below 0.7 the slowest-decaying mode dominates the long-time behaviour significantly more than in the classical parabolic case. Implications for analytic approximations used in tissue diffusion modelling are discussed.

title: A finite-difference scheme for the two-dimensional Riesz–Caputo diffusion equation with application to porous media
abstract: We construct and analyse an implicit finite-difference scheme for a two-dimensional diffusion equation involving both Riesz spatial and Caputo temporal fractional derivatives of orders β ∈ (1, 2) and α ∈ (0, 1) respectively. Consistency, stability via von Neumann analysis, and convergence of order O(τ^(2−α) + h²) are proved rigorously. The scheme is applied to simulate tracer transport in a synthetic porous medium whose void geometry is generated from micro-CT images of sandstone at 10 μm resolution. Comparison with particle-tracking Monte Carlo simulations over 500 realisations shows that the fractional PDE reproduces the anomalous scaling exponents of the displacement variance within 3% for times beyond the transient regime. CPU times on a single workstation range from 14 s (64×64 grid) to 22 min (512×512 grid) for 1000 time steps.

title: Estimating fractional-order parameters from impedance spectroscopy data of ex vivo liver tissue
abstract: Electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements were performed on twelve samples of freshly excised porcine liver tissue at frequencies between 1 Hz and 1 MHz using a four-electrode cell. The complex impedance data were fitted to a Cole–Cole model whose exponent α is directly related to the order of the underlying fractional diffusion equation. A nonlinear least-squares procedure using the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm was applied; confidence intervals were obtained by bootstrap resampling with 2000 iterations. The estimated α values ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 across samples, with the interquartile range 0.75–0.81. Temperature dependence between 4 °C and 37 °C was quantified: α decreased by approximately 0.04 per 10 °C increase. These empirical ranges constrain the fractional order to be used in subsequent tissue diffusion simulations and show that ignoring the temperature shift introduces systematic error in predicted diffusion coefficients of up to 18%.

title: Subdiffusion in heterogeneous brain white matter: a fractional Fokker–Planck approach
abstract: Diffusion-weighted MRI data acquired on a 1.5 T scanner for fifteen healthy volunteers were used to test whether a fractional Fokker–Planck equation with spatially varying diffusivity D(x) and order α(x) fits apparent diffusion coefficient maps better than the standard monoexponential model. Voxel-wise parameter maps were reconstructed from 32-direction diffusion-encoding data at b-values of 500, 1000, and 2000 s/mm². Fitting the fractional model reduced the mean squared residual by 23% in white matter and 11% in grey matter relative to the monoexponential baseline. Spatial maps of α showed consistent localised reductions (α ≈ 0.78) in the corpus callosum and internal capsule, regions known to have restricted diffusion. A cross-validation experiment on five additional subjects confirmed that the fractional model generalises without overfitting despite two extra free parameters per voxel. The code and anonymised parameter maps are made publicly available.

title: Mittag-Leffler stability analysis for a class of fractional reaction–diffusion systems
abstract: We study a coupled system of fractional-order reaction–diffusion equations arising from a two-species model of metabolite transport in tumour tissue. Existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in a weighted L² space are established using semigroup theory adapted to the Caputo derivative. Mittag-Leffler stability of the spatially homogeneous steady state is proved via a fractional Lyapunov function constructed from the sum of squared species concentrations. The decay rate constant is shown to scale as (reaction rate)^(1/α), recovering the classical exponential rate when α → 1. Numerical simulations on a 1D domain of length 5 mm with Dirichlet boundary conditions confirm the theoretical decay exponent to within 1.5% relative error for α ∈ {0.6, 0.75, 0.9}. The analysis provides a rigorous foundation for fitting such systems to in vitro diffusion chamber experiments.

title: Anomalous diffusion models in biological tissues: a comparative review
abstract: This book chapter surveys mathematical models of anomalous diffusion developed for biological tissues over the period 2000–2016, with emphasis on the interplay between fractional-order differential equations, continuous-time random walk theory, and empirical data from MRI and EIS experiments. Four model families are compared: time-fractional, space-fractional, distributed-order, and variable-order formulations. For each family the chapter summarises the governing equation, known analytical solutions, common numerical discretisations, and the experimental observables to which the free parameters can be connected. A unified table lists 34 published parameter estimation studies, including tissue type, measurement modality, reported fractional orders, and goodness-of-fit metrics. The chapter concludes with a discussion of identifiability: which combinations of fractional parameters can in principle be distinguished from a finite dataset, and how many measurements are required in practice given typical signal-to-noise ratios in MRI and EIS.

title: Numerical inversion of the Laplace transform for distributed-order diffusion equations via Gauss–Laguerre quadrature
abstract: Distributed-order diffusion equations require numerical evaluation of integrals over fractional orders, which complicates both forward simulation and inverse problems. We propose a method that transforms the distributed-order equation to Laplace space, applies Gauss–Laguerre quadrature with N_q nodes to approximate the order integral, and then inverts the resulting rational Laplace transform using a contour integration approach on a Hankel path. Error analysis shows convergence of order O(N_q^{−N_q}) in the quadrature step and O(N_t^{−2}) in the time inversion step for smooth weight distributions. Benchmarks against known analytic solutions for uniform and bimodal weight functions demonstrate relative errors below 10⁻⁵ using N_q = 16 and N_t = 64. Computation times are compared with a direct finite-difference solver; the Laplace-domain approach is 7–12 times faster for long-time simulations on grids up to 256 nodes.

title: Identification of anomalous diffusion exponents in tumour spheroid cultures from fluorescence recovery after photobleaching
abstract: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) experiments were performed on multicellular tumour spheroids of a human colorectal carcinoma line grown to diameters of 300–450 μm. Recovery curves for a 10 μm bleach spot were recorded at 0.5 s intervals over 120 s for n = 40 spheroids. A fractional-order diffusion model was fitted to each recovery curve using a Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler with 10⁴ samples after a 2×10³ burn-in period. The posterior median fractional order was α = 0.72 (95% credible interval 0.67–0.78), significantly below unity, confirming subdiffusion. Effective diffusivity estimates ranged from 0.8 to 1.4 μm²/s depending on spheroid size, consistent with geometric obstruction models. The Bayesian approach allowed uncertainty propagation into the recovered diffusivity maps, which is not straightforward with deterministic fitting.

title: A Grünwald–Letnikov scheme with nonuniform time steps for anomalous diffusion in tissue with memory
abstract: Standard Grünwald–Letnikov discretisations of the Caputo derivative use uniform time grids, which can be wasteful when the solution varies rapidly at early times and slowly later—the typical profile in subdiffusion problems. We derive a modified Grünwald–Letnikov formula on a geometric time grid with ratio r ∈ (1, 2] and prove that it retains first-order convergence in time. For r = 1.3 and 256 time levels, the geometric grid achieves comparable accuracy to a uniform grid of 1024 levels on three test problems including a tissue diffusion benchmark with published MRI data. Memory requirements are reduced by a factor of 3.6 and wall-clock time by a factor of 4.1 on the benchmark. The scheme is validated on the ex vivo cartilage data from the 2018 study, confirming that parameter estimates change by less than 1.2% when switching to the nonuniform grid.

title: Sensitivity analysis of fractional diffusion parameters to MRI acquisition protocol in white matter phantoms
abstract: The reliability of estimated fractional diffusion parameters depends on how MRI data are acquired, yet this dependence is rarely quantified systematically. Using a polyacrylamide gel phantom with a calibrated pore-size distribution (mean pore diameter 8.5 μm, coefficient of variation 0.22), we acquired diffusion MRI datasets under 24 different acquisition protocols varying the number of b-values (3–12), maximum b-value (800–3000 s/mm²), number of diffusion directions (6–64), and voxel size (1.5–3 mm isotropic). For each dataset the fractional order α and effective diffusivity D_eff were estimated by nonlinear least squares. The variance of α estimates increased by a factor of 2.8 when the number of b-values was reduced from 12 to 3. Maximum b-value had the largest single effect on α bias: using b_max = 800 s/mm² systematically overestimated α by 0.09 ± 0.02 compared to b_max = 3000 s/mm². Recommendations for minimum protocol requirements are derived from these data.

title: Modified atmosphere packaging extends raspberry shelf life for export
abstract: This study investigated the effect of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) on the postharvest quality and shelf life of Serbian-grown raspberries intended for export markets. Three gas compositions — 5% O₂/15% CO₂/80% N₂, 10% O₂/10% CO₂/80% N₂, and ambient air control — were evaluated at 2 °C storage over a 14-day period. Quality parameters including firmness, color (L*, a*, b*), soluble solids content, titratable acidity, and visual mold incidence were monitored at two-day intervals. Microbiological analyses targeted total aerobic counts and Botrytis cinerea colony formation. Results demonstrated that the 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to control and maintained firmness above commercial acceptability thresholds for 12 days compared to 6 days in ambient conditions. Sensory panel scores for color and texture confirmed marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP conditions. The findings provide actionable gas-mix specifications for exporters shipping raspberries to Central European markets, and establish a data foundation for integrating MAP parameters into predictive shelf-life models. Practical recommendations for film permeability selection and pallet-level gas management are discussed.

title: Antagonistic activity of indigenous Trichoderma isolates from Serbian greenhouse soils against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. radicis-lycopersici
abstract: Forty-seven Trichoderma isolates were collected from greenhouse rhizosphere soils at five locations in Vojvodina and screened for antagonistic activity against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. radicis-lycopersici (FORL) using dual-culture plate assays. Inhibition of mycelial growth was measured after seven days at 25 °C. Fifteen isolates exhibited more than 60% inhibition. The three most active isolates were identified by ITS rDNA sequencing as T. atroviride (two isolates) and T. harzianum (one isolate). Secondary screening under controlled greenhouse conditions using artificially infested rockwool substrate showed that root rot severity index was reduced by 42–57% compared to untreated controls. Plant height, fresh shoot weight and root dry weight were significantly higher in Trichoderma-treated tomato seedlings. Results indicate that locally sourced isolates hold practical potential for integration into tomato propagation systems.

title: Integration of Trichoderma-based biocontrol with reduced doses of fluazinam in pepper crown rot management
abstract: A two-year greenhouse trial assessed the compatibility and combined efficacy of a T. atroviride isolate (TA-22) applied as a root drench with three reduced doses (25%, 50% and 75% of the standard label rate) of the fungicide fluazinam against Fusarium solani crown and root rot on pepper. Treatments were arranged as a 4 × 3 factorial with untreated and full-rate fungicide controls. Crown rot incidence, disease severity index and marketable fruit yield were recorded across two pepper growing cycles. The combination of TA-22 with 50% fluazinam achieved disease incidence comparable to the full fungicide rate (23.4% vs. 19.8%) while maintaining significantly higher yield than fungicide-only treatments. In vitro compatibility tests showed that TA-22 germination was reduced by only 12% at the 50% dose, confirming acceptable tolerance. Results support the use of combination strategies for resistance management and reduction of fungicide load.

title: Formulation and shelf-life stability of a wettable powder based on Trichoderma harzianum conidia for greenhouse use
abstract: Development of stable Trichoderma-based formulations remains a limiting step in commercialisation of biocontrol agents. A wettable powder (WP) formulation was prepared by mixing spray-dried conidia of T. harzianum isolate TH-07 with talc, kaolin and a hydroxypropyl methylcellulose adjuvant. Conidial viability was assessed monthly over twelve months of storage at 4 °C, 20 °C and 35 °C using propidium iodide staining and flow cytometry. At 4 °C, viability remained above 78% after twelve months. At 20 °C, a significant decline occurred after month six (from 85% to 51%). Storage at 35 °C resulted in viability below 30% after three months. The WP formulation demonstrated stable water dispersibility (settling index < 5% after 30 min) across all storage temperatures. Greenhouse bioassays confirmed that efficacy against Fusarium crown rot on tomato was preserved in formulations stored for up to nine months at 4 °C. These data define practical storage and logistics parameters.

title: Trichoderma colonisation dynamics in pepper roots under repeated drench application assessed by quantitative PCR
abstract: Quantitative PCR using species-specific primers targeting the tef1 locus was used to monitor root colonisation by T. atroviride (TA-22) following single, double and triple drench applications at 14-day intervals in a commercial pepper greenhouse trial. Root samples were taken at 7, 14, 28 and 42 days post-first application. Target DNA concentration was expressed as conidial equivalents per gram of fresh root tissue. Peak colonisation was reached at day 14 after the first application (3.2 × 10⁵ conidial equivalents g⁻¹ FW) and declined in single-treatment plants to 8.4 × 10³ g⁻¹ FW by day 42. Repeated application maintained colonisation levels above 5.0 × 10⁴ g⁻¹ FW throughout the monitoring period. Crown rot severity was inversely correlated with root colonisation density (r = −0.74). Soil type and organic matter content had no significant effect on colonisation at the three sampling sites. Findings inform practical application schedules in commercial greenhouse production.

title: Biological control of Fusarium crown and root rot in Mediterranean greenhouse systems: a review of isolate selection and application strategies
abstract: This book chapter synthesises literature published between 2000 and 2018 on the use of Trichoderma spp. for biological control of Fusarium crown and root rot in solanaceous crops under protected cultivation in the Mediterranean and Pannonian zone. Coverage includes criteria for isolate selection, mechanisms of action (mycoparasitism, antibiosis, induced resistance), compatibility with standard growing substrates and irrigation management, and factors influencing application efficacy. Particular attention is given to differences between soil-based and soilless production systems, where colonisation dynamics differ substantially. The chapter also addresses regulatory frameworks for registration of microbial plant protection products in Serbia and the EU, identifying gaps between research outputs and commercially available products. Case studies from research conducted in Serbia, Hungary, Romania and Greece are included. The chapter aims to serve as a practical reference for researchers and extension specialists.

title: Effect of substrate composition on Trichoderma establishment and Fusarium root rot suppression in tomato transplant production
abstract: Transplant production in peat-based, coir-based and bark-based substrates was compared for capacity to support T. harzianum (TH-07) establishment and subsequent suppression of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. radicis-lycopersici. Trichoderma was applied as a WP formulation at sowing. Conidial populations were enumerated from substrate cores at 10, 20 and 30 days using dilution plating on Trichoderma Selective Medium. At day 30, colonisation was highest in bark-based substrate (4.1 × 10⁶ CFU g⁻¹ dry substrate) and lowest in coir (1.3 × 10⁶ CFU g⁻¹). Disease incidence in FORL-challenged transplants at the end of the trial was 14.2% (bark), 21.6% (coir) and 18.9% (peat), compared to 61.4% in uninoculated FORL controls. The fungal community composition determined by ITS amplicon sequencing differed among substrates and appeared to interact with Trichoderma performance. Substrate selection is therefore a practical management lever in biocontrol programmes for tomato transplants.

title: Systemic defence gene expression in pepper following root treatment with Trichoderma atroviride TA-22 and subsequent Fusarium solani challenge
abstract: Expression of genes encoding pathogenesis-related proteins (PR-1, PR-2, PR-5) and jasmonate-responsive proteinase inhibitor II (pin2) was monitored by RT-qPCR in pepper leaves and crowns at 3, 7 and 14 days after root drench with T. atroviride TA-22, with or without subsequent F. solani inoculation. TA-22 alone induced a transient 4.2-fold upregulation of PR-1 in crowns at day 7, which returned to baseline by day 14. Upon F. solani challenge, plants pre-treated with TA-22 maintained 3.1–4.8-fold higher expression of PR-2 and PR-5 in crown tissue relative to untreated challenged plants throughout the 14-day monitoring period. Induction of pin2 was observed only in challenged plants regardless of TA-22 treatment. Hydrogen peroxide accumulation in crown tissue, measured histochemically, was lower in TA-22 pre-treated challenged plants, consistent with reduced oxidative stress. Data support an induced systemic resistance mechanism contributing to TA-22 biocontrol activity.

title: Учесталост и заступљеност врста рода Fusarium на корену паприке у стакленичкој производњи Војводине: трогодишња студија
abstract: Током три производне сезоне (2019–2021) са 22 газдинства у Војводини прикупљено је 348 узорака ткива корена и круне паприке са симптомима трулежи. Изолација гљива вршена је на селективној подлози Nash-Snyder. Идентификовано је укупно 286 Fusarium изолата. Специјесна структура обухватала је F. solani (48,6%), F. oxysporum (27,1%), F. proliferatum (14,3%) и F. redolens (10,0%). Учесталост F. proliferatum порасла је са 8,2% у 2019. на 19,5% у 2021. години, у односу на укупан број изолата. Тест патогености на паприци потврдио је агресивност свих четири утврђених врста, с тим да је F. solani изазвао најтежа оштећења (просечни индекс болести 3,1 на скали 0–4). Подаци указују на постепену промену специјесне структуре и наглашавају потребу за широкоспектарним биоконтролним агенсима.

title: Volatile organic compounds produced by Trichoderma atroviride TA-22 inhibit Fusarium solani mycelial growth and spore germination in closed container assays
abstract: The role of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the biocontrol activity of T. atroviride TA-22 was investigated using sealed inverted-plate assays in which pathogen colonies were exposed to Trichoderma volatiles without direct contact. Fusarium solani mycelial growth was reduced by 38–52% after six days, and macroconidial germination was inhibited by 61% compared to controls. GC-MS analysis of TA-22 headspace identified 23 compounds, of which 6-pentyl-2H-pyran-2-one (6-PP), 1-octen-3-ol and isoamyl alcohol were present in the highest relative abundance. Synthetic 6-PP at concentrations of 50 and 100 µg ml⁻¹ reduced pathogen growth by 27% and 49% respectively, confirming its contribution to VOC-mediated inhibition. Tomato seedling growth was significantly stimulated by exposure to TA-22 VOCs at both concentrations, indicating a plant-growth-promoting secondary effect. These findings open perspectives for encapsulated VOC-releasing formulations, though practical translation faces challenges related to confinement and dose delivery.

title: Trichoderma-based biocontrol efficacy against Fusarium crown rot in tomato at elevated substrate temperatures: implications for climate scenarios
abstract: Greenhouse substrate temperatures in Vojvodina can exceed 32 °C during summer months, which may compromise Trichoderma biocontrol activity. Five T. harzianum and T. atroviride isolates were assessed for thermal tolerance (growth at 28, 32 and 36 °C) and retention of antagonistic activity against FORL at elevated temperatures. Two isolates retained growth rates above 65% of the 25 °C benchmark at 32 °C; none grew appreciably at 36 °C. Greenhouse microplot experiments with substrate heating cables simulating 28 °C and 32 °C mean substrate temperatures showed that biocontrol efficacy of the most thermotolerant isolate (TA-31) declined from 55% disease reduction at 25 °C to 34% at 28 °C and 18% at 32 °C, while the least tolerant isolate lost all detectable efficacy above 28 °C. Application timing in relation to daily temperature peaks is discussed as a practical mitigation measure. Results highlight the need to include thermal screening in early selection stages.

title: Comparative performance of three Trichoderma-based commercial products and two indigenous isolates in suppression of Fusarium crown and root rot in pepper: a multi-site greenhouse trial
abstract: Three commercial Trichoderma-based plant protection products registered in Serbia (designated CP-1, CP-2 and CP-3 to maintain anonymity with respect to ongoing regulatory review) were evaluated against T. atroviride TA-22 and T. harzianum TH-07 at four commercial pepper greenhouse sites over a single production cycle. All products and isolates were applied as root drenches at label or equivalent rates. Primary outcomes were crown rot disease incidence, disease severity index and marketable pepper yield. CP-1 achieved 40% reduction in disease incidence across sites; TA-22 achieved 51% reduction. TH-07 and CP-3 performed comparably (36–38% reduction). Under high disease pressure (incidence above 40% in control plots), differences between treatments were more pronounced. Yield increases attributable to Trichoderma treatment ranged from 8% to 23% depending on site and treatment. Multi-site analysis indicated significant site × treatment interactions, underlining the importance of local isolate selection. Cost-benefit estimates based on current market prices favour indigenous isolate formulations under the production conditions assessed.

title: Wild bee species richness and abundance in sunflower fields of Vojvodina: influence of field margin width and crop variety
abstract: We surveyed wild bee communities across 18 sunflower fields in Vojvodina during two consecutive flowering seasons (2010–2011) using pan-trap arrays placed at three distances from the field edge (5 m, 50 m, and 150 m). A total of 2,847 wild bee specimens belonging to 34 species were collected. Species richness and total abundance declined significantly with distance from field margins, dropping by approximately 60% between 5 m and 150 m. Halictidae dominated the catch at all distances, while Apidae were concentrated near margins. Wider margins (>3 m) supported roughly 30% more species than narrow margins (<1 m). Crop variety had no significant effect on total bee abundance, though one confectionery sunflower cultivar attracted a higher proportion of Bombus individuals than hybrid varieties in both years. Results indicate that maintaining wide, unmanaged margins is a practical measure for supporting wild bee visitation in large-scale sunflower production landscapes typical of the Pannonian Plain.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns of solitary bee nesting in arable landscapes: evidence from soil-dwelling species at the Rimski Šančevi experimental farm
abstract: Ground-nesting solitary bees were monitored over three seasons (2013–2015) at the Rimski Šančevi experimental farm using a combination of emergence traps (n = 40 traps, 1 m² each) placed along transects spanning crop fields, field roads, and grassland remnants. A total of 19 ground-nesting bee species were identified, dominated by Lasioglossum and Andrena genera. Nesting density at uncompacted field road verges was 4.7 times higher than within actively cultivated plots. Tillage frequency was the strongest negative predictor of nesting density among all site-level variables measured (β = −0.62). Seasonal emergence peaked in early May for Andrena species and mid-June for Lasioglossum, corresponding to different crop flowering windows. Soil texture and bare ground cover together explained 58% of variance in total nesting density. The findings identify field road verges as disproportionately important nesting resources that are rarely considered in agri-environment scheme design.

title: Buckwheat as a pollen and nectar resource for wild bees in cereal-dominated landscapes: a cage exclusion experiment
abstract: A cage pollinator exclusion experiment was conducted across six buckwheat plots in Vojvodina (2015) to separate wind and insect pollination contributions to grain yield. Caged plots (insect-excluded) produced 38% fewer seeds per plant compared to open plots, confirming a strong dependence on insect pollination. Pan traps and timed observations identified 28 wild bee species visiting buckwheat flowers, with Halictus rubicundus and Lasioglossum calceatum most frequent. Pollen analysis of pan-trap specimens confirmed buckwheat as the primary pollen source for 71% of individuals collected during the flowering window. Yield penalties from insect exclusion were larger in plots further from grassland edges (>200 m), suggesting that proximity to semi-natural vegetation supports pollinator density. The experiment provides a quantitative estimate of the pollination service value of wild bees specifically in buckwheat, a minor but commercially relevant crop in the region with no previous controlled pollination data from Serbia.

title: Landscape-scale effects on wild bee communities in sunflower: a gradient analysis across 40 farms in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: We investigated how landscape composition at three spatial scales (500 m, 1 km, 2 km radius) affects wild bee species richness, functional group composition, and sunflower seed set across 40 farms in Vojvodina and adjacent Hungarian territory. Landscape variables were derived from CORINE Land Cover and high-resolution orthophotos. Bee sampling combined pan traps and 15-minute transect counts at each farm during peak sunflower anthesis. Mixed-effects models showed that proportion of SNH at the 1 km scale best explained wild bee species richness (R² = 0.51) and abundance of solitary bees (R² = 0.44). Sunflower seed set was positively related to solitary bee abundance (β = 0.38, p < 0.001) but not to bumblebee abundance after controlling for landscape context. Farms in landscapes with >8% SNH had significantly higher estimated yield gains attributable to wild bee pollination (mean 6.1% over the landscape average) compared to farms with <4% SNH (mean 1.8%). These results support targeted SNH restoration at the 1 km scale as a cost-effective pollination management strategy.

title: Pollinator visitation in field-grown vegetables: a comparison of open-pollinated and hybrid cultivars of squash (Cucurbita pepo) under farmland bee community structure
abstract: Cucurbita pepo (pumpkin and zucchini types) requires insect pollination for fruit set, yet pollinator visitation in vegetable production systems is rarely quantified separately from managed honeybee contributions. We monitored pollinator visits to male and female flowers of two open-pollinated and two hybrid squash cultivars at five farms over two seasons (2017–2018). Cumulative observation effort was 320 h. The dominant visitors were bumblebees (Bombus terrestris aggregate, 44% of visits), squash bees were absent from all farms, and wild solitary bees comprised 18% of visits. Fruit set was complete (>92%) in open flowers at all farms regardless of cultivar type. However, fruit weight was 11–14% higher when bumblebee visitation rates exceeded six visits per flower per day. Honeybee visits were recorded at only two farms with nearby managed hives and contributed <8% of total visits overall. The study provides baseline visitation data for squash in temperate continental agroecosystems where squash bee distributions are absent.

title: Decline in sampling efficiency of standard pan-trap colours across a ten-year time series in Vojvodina: implications for long-term pollinator monitoring
abstract: Long-term monitoring of wild bee communities with standardised pan traps relies on consistent trap efficiency, but colour reflectance and UV properties of polypropylene traps change with weathering. We compared catch composition and per-trap abundance from newly purchased and five-year-old pan traps (yellow, white, and blue) operated simultaneously at four fixed monitoring sites at Rimski Šančevi between 2019 and 2021. UV reflectance measurements confirmed significant degradation of blue and yellow traps after approximately 3–4 seasons of outdoor use. Old blue traps caught 29% fewer bees per trap-day than new traps; old yellow traps caught 22% fewer. Taxonomic composition differences were small but statistically detectable for rare species with narrow UV sensitivity ranges. The data are presented alongside a ten-year catch archive (2011–2021) from the same monitoring sites to illustrate how undetected trap degradation could produce spurious abundance decline trends of 1–3% annually. We recommend trap replacement intervals and calibration protocols for ongoing monitoring programmes.

title: Bee diversity and pollination in sunflower: landscape and local management interactions
abstract: This book chapter reviews the current state of knowledge on how landscape configuration and on-farm management jointly determine wild bee diversity and pollination service reliability in sunflower, the most economically important entomophilous crop of the Pannonian Plain. Drawing on 15 published datasets including three generated by our group in Vojvodina, we synthesise effect sizes of semi-natural habitat proportion, crop rotation diversity, pesticide application frequency, and field size on bee abundance and species richness. A meta-analytic summary (k = 32 effect sizes) shows that landscape-level SNH proportion has the largest and most consistent effect across studies (mean Hedges' g = 0.71), followed by field margin management. Local pesticide reduction showed variable results strongly modulated by landscape context. The chapter includes a decision framework for farmers seeking to improve pollination service reliability and discusses practical constraints in large-scale intensive farming regions. It is directed at agronomists, ecologists, and agricultural extension practitioners.

title: Interannual variation in wild bee phenology and its consequences for pollination synchrony with oilseed rape flowering in Vojvodina (2016–2022)
abstract: Mismatch between bee emergence phenology and crop flowering can reduce pollination service reliability, particularly under variable spring temperatures. We used a seven-year dataset (2016–2022) of pan-trap catches at six oilseed rape farms combined with daily temperature records and crop development scoring to evaluate temporal overlap between Andrena and Halictus emergence and crop bloom onset. Degree-day accumulation from 1 January was a better predictor of first-emergence date for Andrena fulva (R² = 0.84) than calendar date alone. In three years with early warm periods followed by late frosts, bee emergence preceded crop bloom by 8–12 days, reducing estimated pollinator density during peak bloom by 23–34% relative to well-synchronised years. Seed set was 9% lower on average in mismatched compared to synchronised years. The degree of mismatch was uncorrelated with landscape SNH proportion, suggesting that phenological risk is partly independent of landscape-level habitat management and requires separate consideration in adaptation strategies.

title: Evaluating flower strip mixes for wild bee support in sunflower-dominated Vojvodina farmland: a two-year field trial with eight seed mixtures
abstract: Flower strips are widely promoted as a habitat management tool for pollinators in agroecosystems, but the composition of seed mixtures varies greatly and their effectiveness under continental climatic conditions is poorly tested. We established eight commercially available or custom-designed seed mixtures as two-metre flower strips alongside sunflower fields at a single 45-hectare experimental farm in Vojvodina across 2022 and 2023, monitoring wild bee abundance, species richness, and functional group composition using weekly pan-trap collections and timed transect walks throughout the growing season. Mixtures including Phacelia tanacetifolia, Borago officinalis, and native Centaurea species consistently attracted the highest total bee abundance (up to 4.2 individuals per metre of strip per hour). Mixtures dominated by grasses and composites with small florets had low attractiveness regardless of bloom duration. Strip establishment cost per hectare and weed suppression capacity were also evaluated as secondary metrics. These results identify combinations of flowering plant species adapted to continental climate conditions that maximise wild bee attraction during the critical sunflower pollination window.

title: Remote sensing-derived landscape metrics as predictors of wild bee abundance in Vojvodina: testing Sentinel-2 classifications against field-mapped land cover
abstract: Landscape ecology studies of pollinators typically rely on manual or semi-manual mapping of land cover, which limits spatial and temporal scalability. We evaluated whether landscape metrics derived from automated Sentinel-2 multispectral classifications could substitute for field-verified land cover maps in predicting wild bee abundance at 22 study sites across Vojvodina. Classifications were produced with a random forest algorithm trained on 1,240 ground-truth points and achieved an overall accuracy of 84% for eight land cover classes including arable land, SNH, tree rows, and water bodies. Wild bee abundance models built with Sentinel-2-derived SNH area at the 1 km scale explained 61% of variance, compared to 67% explained by field-mapped SNH, a non-significant difference (ΔAIC < 2). Agreement was lower for narrow linear features such as field margins below 2 m width, which Sentinel-2 systematically underestimated. We provide a calibration function for adjusting Sentinel-2 SNH estimates at the 1 km scale for use in pollinator modelling in Pannonian agricultural landscapes.

title: Quantifying the economic value of wild bee pollination in sunflower across farm size categories in Vojvodina: a damage function approach
abstract: Although wild bees deliver measurable pollination services to sunflower, the monetary value of that service is rarely translated for farm-level economic decision-making. We applied a damage function approach, combining empirical pollinator exclusion data from 14 farms in Vojvodina with sunflower market prices and yield response coefficients from our long-term dataset (2012–2024), to estimate the annual economic contribution of wild bees across three farm size categories: small (<50 ha sunflower), medium (50–200 ha), and large (>200 ha). Estimated wild bee service value averaged 48 EUR/ha on small farms with diverse surrounding landscapes, 29 EUR/ha on medium farms, and 14 EUR/ha on large intensive farms in species-poor landscapes. Sensitivity analysis showed results were most responsive to assumptions about baseline wild bee exclusion yield penalty and current sunflower market price. We discuss how these estimates can be incorporated into cost-benefit analyses of agri-environment scheme participation by Vojvodina farmers, and identify data gaps that most constrain estimate precision.

title: Comparative evaluation of resampling strategies for binary classification on skewed industrial fault logs
abstract: This study compared seven resampling approaches—including SMOTE, ADASYN, random undersampling, and two hybrid variants—on four binary classification tasks derived from fault detection logs collected at a regional manufacturing facility. Each dataset contained between 12,000 and 48,000 records with minority-class ratios ranging from 1:9 to 1:47. Classifiers evaluated included decision trees, random forests, and gradient-boosted trees. Performance was measured using the geometric mean, F1 score on the minority class, and area under the precision-recall curve. Results showed that hybrid methods combining cluster-based undersampling with borderline oversampling outperformed pure oversampling in 11 of 16 dataset-classifier combinations, but that the gains diminished when the imbalance ratio exceeded 1:30. Random forests paired with random undersampling provided the most consistent baseline across all conditions. The paper provides a reproducible benchmark pipeline and discusses the sensitivity of each metric to threshold selection.

title: Effect of feature scaling and missing-value imputation on ensemble performance with imbalanced tabular data
abstract: Preprocessing choices that are often treated as secondary—scaling strategy, imputation method, and the order in which they are applied relative to resampling—can substantially alter classifier performance when class distributions are skewed. This paper reports a factorial experiment across three preprocessing factors, four imputation strategies, and five ensemble classifiers on eight publicly available imbalanced datasets augmented with two proprietary operational datasets from the energy sector. Outcome metrics included AUC, G-mean, and Brier score. Min-max scaling combined with k-nearest-neighbour imputation consistently produced better-calibrated probability estimates than mean imputation across all ensemble types. Applying imputation after oversampling rather than before reduced artificial variance inflation in synthetic minority samples. The findings suggest that preprocessing pipelines for imbalanced data should be validated as a whole rather than component by component, and a recommended default ordering is proposed.

title: Cost-sensitive random forests with asymmetric misclassification penalties: a case study in credit default prediction
abstract: Standard random forests minimise overall error without accounting for the different costs associated with false positives and false negatives. This paper implements and evaluates three mechanisms for incorporating asymmetric costs into random forest training: weighted Gini impurity at splits, class-weighted bootstrapping, and post-hoc threshold shifting. Experiments were conducted on a credit default dataset of 31,000 loan applications with a default rate of 6.4 %, supplemented by two synthetic benchmarks at 3 % and 10 % minority frequency. Cost matrices were varied systematically with false-negative penalties set at 3, 5, and 10 times the false-positive penalty. Weighted impurity modification achieved the best expected cost reduction at penalty ratios of 5 and 10, while threshold shifting performed comparably at a ratio of 3 with lower computational overhead. The interaction between training-time cost weighting and resampling is examined, and practical guidance for cost matrix specification is provided.

title: Temporal drift in behavioural feature distributions: detection and retraining schedules for production classifiers
abstract: Classifiers trained on historical behavioural logs degrade in production as user patterns shift over time, a phenomenon that is more pronounced when the training set was already imbalanced. This paper quantifies distributional drift using the population stability index and the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic applied monthly to engineered features derived from a 36-month log of user interactions with a digital banking platform, covering 210,000 accounts. Six classifiers trained at different points in the observation window were evaluated on each subsequent month. AUC degradation of more than 5 percentage points occurred within 4 to 7 months for all models, with feature groups related to device usage patterns drifting fastest. A simple schedule that triggers retraining when the average PSI across the top-20 features exceeds 0.2 recovered most of the performance loss with 40 % fewer retraining cycles than a fixed monthly schedule. Implications for monitoring pipelines in regulated financial environments are discussed.

title: Ensemble pruning under class-imbalance constraints using diversity and minority-class recall jointly
abstract: Large ensembles are often pruned to reduce inference latency and memory use. Standard pruning criteria based on overall accuracy or AUC are biased toward majority-class performance when training distributions are skewed. This paper proposes a pruning criterion that combines pairwise Q-diversity with minority-class recall estimated on a validation fold, selecting subsets of size k from a pool of 200 trained trees using a greedy forward selection procedure. The criterion is evaluated on twelve benchmark datasets with imbalance ratios between 1:10 and 1:99, alongside three criteria from prior literature. The joint criterion consistently produced smaller ensembles (median k = 23 versus pool size of 200) while maintaining G-mean within 2 percentage points of the full ensemble. Experiments also examine the sensitivity of the selected subset to validation fold size and stratification strategy.

title: Calibrating probability outputs of gradient-boosted classifiers trained on imbalanced data
abstract: Gradient-boosted classifiers trained on imbalanced data are known to produce poorly calibrated probability estimates, with systematic underestimation of minority-class probabilities. This paper investigates the effectiveness of Platt scaling, isotonic regression, and beta calibration as post-processing steps applied after training on seven datasets with minority-class proportions between 2 % and 15 %. Each calibration method was evaluated using the expected calibration error, maximum calibration error, and the Brier skill score relative to a no-skill baseline. Beta calibration reduced expected calibration error by a median of 34 % across datasets compared with uncalibrated outputs, outperforming the other methods in five of seven cases. However, calibration methods trained on the imbalanced validation set yielded worse results than those trained on a class-balanced calibration subset, suggesting that the resampling strategy used during calibration matters as much as the choice of calibration algorithm.

title: Feature selection stability under class imbalance: a bootstrap-based assessment across filter and wrapper methods
abstract: Feature selection is a standard step in tabular machine learning pipelines, but the stability of selected subsets—their tendency to change when training data are resampled—has received little attention in imbalanced settings. This paper applies a bootstrap-based stability index to five filter methods (mutual information, chi-squared, Relief-F, and two correlation-based variants) and two wrapper methods (sequential forward selection with logistic regression and with random forest) across ten datasets with minority-class proportions from 3 % to 20 %. Stability is reported separately for the full feature ranking and for the top-10 and top-20 subsets. Filter methods based on Relief-F showed the highest stability across imbalance levels. Wrapper methods achieved competitive predictive performance but exhibited substantially lower subset stability, particularly when the minority class was below 5 %. The paper provides recommendations for practitioners who need reproducible feature subsets in regulated or auditable applications.

title: Generating minority-class samples for tabular data using a conditional variational autoencoder: comparison with SMOTE variants on operational datasets
abstract: Synthetic oversampling for tabular imbalanced data is dominated by SMOTE and its descendants, which rely on linear interpolation in feature space. This paper evaluates a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) as an alternative generative model for minority-class augmentation, comparing it against SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and SVM-SMOTE on six operational datasets from logistics and telecommunications domains. The CVAE was implemented with a three-layer encoder and decoder, trained for 200 epochs with early stopping on a minority-class validation split. Downstream classifiers were random forest, XGBoost, and a support vector machine. The CVAE improved G-mean relative to the best SMOTE variant in four of six datasets, with the largest gains on datasets containing mixed continuous and low-cardinality categorical features. On purely continuous datasets the differences were within noise. Training time for the CVAE was 8–15 times higher than for SMOTE, which is relevant for production retraining schedules.
