title: Coordination Geometry of Yb(III) Complexes with DTPA-BMA Probed by Near-Infrared Luminescence
abstract: The coordination geometry of Yb³⁺ complexed by the bisamide derivative DTPA-BMA was investigated by near-infrared (NIR) luminescence spectroscopy between 900 and 1100 nm using a Horiba Fluorolog-QM instrument equipped with a NIR-sensitive InGaAs detector. Emission spectra at pH 6.0–8.5 in 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaClO4 at 25 °C showed a single 2F5/2 → 2F7/2 transition with three resolved Stark components, indicative of low-symmetry coordination. Luminescence lifetime τ(H2O) = 8.7 ± 0.3 μs and τ(D2O) = 58.2 ± 1.1 μs gave q = 1.8 ± 0.2 water molecules, higher than the q ≈ 1 found for [YbDTPA]²⁻ under identical conditions, suggesting reduced denticity of the bisamide ligand. The pH dependence of emission intensity showed no spectral changes attributable to deprotonation below pH 8.5. The results indicate that DTPA-BMA does not provide full occlusion of the inner coordination sphere in Yb(III).

title: Complexation of Ce(IV) with DTPA Under Mildly Acidic Conditions: Potentiometry and Redox Considerations
abstract: The formation of Ce⁴⁺–DTPA complexes under mildly acidic conditions (pH 2.0–5.0) was investigated by potentiometry and UV–Vis spectrophotometry in 0.5 mol dm⁻³ NaClO4 at 25 °C. Control of the Ce(IV)/Ce(III) redox equilibrium was achieved by adjusting solution Eh with dilute ceric ammonium nitrate and monitoring with a Pt–calomel electrode pair. A conditional stability constant log β'(CeDTPA) = 18.4 ± 0.1 at pH 3.5 was extracted from competition titrations with Ce³⁺. Species distribution modelling showed that the Ce(IV)–DTPA complex is stable below pH 4.5 but undergoes ligand oxidation above pH 5, consistent with reported cerium-mediated oxidation of aminocarboxylates. The measurement approach using competitive potentiometry provides a practical method for characterising tetravalent lanthanide complexes that are inaccessible by direct alkalimetric titration. Implications for separation of Ce(IV) from trivalent lanthanides are discussed.

title: Enthalpy–Entropy Compensation in Lanthanide–Polyaminocarboxylate Complexation: A Systematic Analysis Across the Full Series
abstract: Thermodynamic data (ΔG°, ΔH°, ΔS°) for the complexation of all fourteen trivalent lanthanides (La–Lu, excluding Pm) with EDTA, DTPA, and DOTA were compiled from measurements carried out in this laboratory over fifteen years and supplemented with critically selected literature data, all at 25 °C, I = 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaClO4. For each ligand a linear enthalpy–entropy compensation plot (ΔH° vs. TΔS°) was obtained with slopes β_c of 0.87 ± 0.04 (EDTA), 0.91 ± 0.03 (DTPA), and 0.83 ± 0.05 (DOTA); compensation temperatures T_c were 290, 302, and 278 K respectively. The compensation behaviour suggests a common mechanistic origin in inner-sphere water reorganisation regardless of ligand structure. Deviations from the compensation line at Gd and Tb correlate with published solution-phase structural data indicating the onset of the tetrahedral-cap coordination motif. The dataset, provided as supplementary material, is intended to serve as a reference for computational modelling of lanthanide speciation.

title: Rule-based ¹H NMR chemical shift prediction for substituted cyclohexanones using incremental parameters
abstract: Chemical shift prediction in flexible aliphatic ketones remains problematic for purely empirical approaches. This work presents an incremental parameter set derived from a curated training corpus of 312 cyclohexanone derivatives whose ¹H NMR spectra were recorded at 300 and 400 MHz in CDCl₃. Substituent effects at positions 2 through 6 were treated with a least-squares regression model incorporating steric correction terms derived from molecular mechanics geometries. Cross-validation on a held-out set of 58 compounds yielded a mean absolute error of 0.07 ppm for ring methylene protons and 0.12 ppm for protons adjacent to the carbonyl. The rule set was encoded in a portable XML schema compatible with the in-house spectral interpreter SPECINT-1. The work demonstrates that systematic parameter harvesting from a moderately sized, curated dataset outperforms two widely used commercial predictors on this compound class, and offers a reproducible baseline for future neural-network refinements.

title: Mechanochemical preparation of BiVO₄/TiO₂ composites: a solvent-free alternative and its photocatalytic evaluation
abstract: Mechanochemical preparation of BiVO₄/TiO₂ composites (10–50 wt% BiVO₄) was carried out in a planetary ball mill at 400 rpm for milling times of 1–6 hours, without solvents or calcination. XRD analysis revealed progressive amorphisation of TiO₂ and broadening of BiVO₄ reflections with extended milling; 3 hours was identified as optimal. BET surface areas increased from 7 m² g⁻¹ (1 h) to 21 m² g⁻¹ (3 h) before declining. UV-Vis DRS showed visible-light absorption onset consistent with heterojunction formation. Under visible-light irradiation, the 30 wt% BiVO₄ composite milled for 3 hours degraded Reactive Red 195 (20 mg L⁻¹) with k = 0.019 min⁻¹, compared to 0.021 min⁻¹ for the equivalent sol-gel sample, demonstrating near-equivalent performance with a substantially reduced environmental footprint. Life cycle inventory data for solvent and energy use are reported for both routes.

title: Selective Harmonic Elimination PWM for a Three-Level Neutral-Point-Clamped Inverter Using Newton–Raphson Iteration
abstract: This paper addresses the computation of switching angles for selective harmonic elimination pulse-width modulation (SHE-PWM) applied to a three-level neutral-point-clamped (NPC) inverter. The transcendental equations governing harmonic cancellation were solved using the Newton–Raphson iterative method initialised with angles derived from Fourier series analysis of the target waveform. Solutions were obtained for modulation indices ranging from 0.5 to 1.15 in steps of 0.05, targeting elimination of the 5th, 7th, 11th, and 13th harmonics while controlling the fundamental output. Simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink showed that the 5th and 7th harmonic magnitudes were reduced to below 0.3% of the fundamental for all tested modulation indices. Laboratory validation on a 2 kVA NPC prototype confirmed simulation predictions, with measured total harmonic distortion (THD) at the inverter output below 4.1% across the full modulation index range. The paper also discusses convergence sensitivity to initial angle estimates and provides pre-computed angle look-up tables for practical implementation on embedded control hardware.

title: Comparison of Carrier-Based and Space-Vector PWM Strategies for Five-Level Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters in Variable-Speed Induction Motor Drives
abstract: A systematic comparison of phase-disposition carrier-based PWM (PD-CBPWM), phase-opposition-disposition PWM (POD-CBPWM), and space-vector PWM (SVPWM) is presented for a five-level cascaded H-bridge (CHB) inverter supplying a 15 kW induction motor. Each modulation strategy was implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and validated on a scaled laboratory prototype. Performance was evaluated across switching frequencies of 450 Hz, 900 Hz, and 1350 Hz and load conditions from 25% to 100% rated torque. Key metrics included output voltage THD, current ripple, DC-link capacitor voltage balance, and inverter losses estimated via a Plexim PLECS thermal model using IGBT datasheet parameters. PD-CBPWM achieved the lowest voltage THD (3.8% at 1350 Hz, full load) but exhibited a 6% DC-link voltage imbalance at light loads. SVPWM showed the best voltage balance across all conditions. The paper provides a decision framework linking switching frequency constraints typical of medium-voltage industrial drives to the preferred modulation strategy.

title: Genetic Algorithm Optimisation of Switching Angles for Selective Harmonic Elimination in a Seven-Level CHB Inverter
abstract: Selective harmonic elimination for a seven-level cascaded H-bridge inverter requires solving a system of twelve nonlinear transcendental equations per modulation index. Classical iterative solvers are sensitive to initial conditions and frequently fail to find all solution families. This paper presents a real-coded genetic algorithm (GA) approach with tournament selection, arithmetic crossover, and adaptive mutation rate to compute globally optimal switching angle sets. The GA was run 200 times per modulation index point on a grid of 61 values from 0.4 to 1.2. Solutions targeting simultaneous elimination of the 5th, 7th, 11th, 13th, 17th, and 19th harmonics were obtained with convergence reliability above 97%. Experimental tests were conducted on a 5-level downscaled prototype (due to laboratory constraints) with the switching angles scaled accordingly. Measured output voltage spectra confirmed harmonic cancellation consistent with computed results. Computation time per modulation index point averaged 14 seconds on a standard desktop, making the GA suitable for offline look-up table generation but not real-time recalculation.

title: Thermal Stress Estimation in IGBT Modules of Medium-Voltage CHB Inverters Under Non-Sinusoidal Load Conditions
abstract: Medium-voltage cascaded H-bridge inverters driving motors with significant harmonic content in the load current experience uneven thermal cycling across IGBT modules. This paper combines a PLECS-based electrothermal simulation with analytical loss models derived from manufacturer datasheets for 3.3 kV IGBT modules to estimate junction temperature swing and mean junction temperature across a full operating cycle representing a variable-speed compressor profile. The load profile covers start-up, ramp to 60% speed, steady-state operation, and deceleration over 180 seconds. Simulations show that outer phase modules in a seven-level CHB topology exhibit peak junction temperature swings 12–18°C higher than inner modules due to unbalanced harmonic currents. A simple balancing strategy based on rotating the switching angle assignment among modules is proposed and evaluated, reducing the maximum inter-module junction temperature difference from 21°C to under 7°C. The approach requires no additional sensors and is compatible with standard dSPACE-based control implementations.

title: Harmonic Distortion Limits Compliance for Variable-Speed Pump Drives: A Case Study in the Water Treatment Sector
abstract: This paper analyses total harmonic distortion levels produced by a medium-voltage multi-level inverter-fed pump drive installation at a water treatment facility in northern Serbia and evaluates compliance with the IEC 61000-3-6 harmonic emission limits for medium-voltage networks. Measurements were performed over seven consecutive days using a class A power quality analyser at the point of common coupling (PCC) of the 6 kV distribution network. The measured 95th percentile of voltage THD reached 4.7%, exceeding the 4% indicative planning level. Passive harmonic filters were designed for the 5th and 7th harmonic frequencies and evaluated through network simulations built in PSCAD. The proposed filter configuration reduced 95th percentile voltage THD at the PCC to 2.9%. Filter sizing, cost, and physical footprint constraints specific to pump station installations are discussed. The paper provides a practical procedure applicable to other industrial motor drive installations connected to medium-voltage networks with limited short-circuit power.

title: Deadband Compensation Methods for Multi-Level Inverters and Their Effect on Output Voltage Distortion at Low Modulation Index
abstract: Deadband intervals inserted to prevent IGBT shoot-through cause systematic output voltage errors that become proportionally more significant at low modulation indices. In three-level and five-level NPC inverters, the polarity of the phase current determines the direction of the voltage error, complicating compensation compared to the two-level case. This paper analyses deadband-induced distortion patterns for three-level and five-level NPC topologies and derives compensation formulas applicable to both SVPWM and SHE-PWM modulation. Four compensation strategies are compared: feed-forward voltage injection, current polarity detection with average voltage correction, observer-based estimation using a discrete Luenberger observer, and no compensation (baseline). Tests were conducted on a 400 V laboratory prototype across modulation indices from 0.15 to 0.55 at deadband times of 2 µs, 4 µs, and 6 µs. Observer-based compensation reduced low-order harmonic content (3rd, 5th, 7th) by 60–75% compared to baseline at a 4 µs deadband, with similar accuracy to the feed-forward method but without requiring explicit current polarity sensors.

title: Multi-Level Inverters in Industrial Drive Applications: Modulation, Harmonic Control, and Practical Constraints
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of multi-level inverter topologies—diode-clamped, flying capacitor, and cascaded H-bridge—from the perspective of their deployment in medium-voltage industrial motor drive systems. The chapter covers the theoretical foundations of carrier-based and space-vector PWM methods adapted for levels three through nine, selective harmonic elimination formulations and solution strategies, and capacitor voltage balancing requirements for clamped topologies. A section is dedicated to practical constraints encountered in industrial environments, including thermal management of power modules, electromagnetic compatibility requirements under IEC standards, and commissioning considerations for retrofit installations. Numerical examples are drawn from documented laboratory results obtained on a 5-level CHB testbed. The chapter also discusses trade-offs between switching frequency, output harmonic performance, and semiconductor stress that arise when selecting modulation strategies for specific load profiles such as fans, compressors, and conveyors.

title: Embedded Implementation of SHE-PWM Angle Look-Up Tables on a Low-Cost FPGA for Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters
abstract: Pre-computed switching angle tables for selective harmonic elimination pulse-width modulation occupy significant memory when resolution over modulation index is fine and the number of target harmonics is large. This paper describes the implementation of a compressed look-up table on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA, using piecewise linear interpolation between stored angle sets to reduce memory footprint while maintaining angular accuracy within 0.02°. The implementation targets a five-level cascaded H-bridge inverter eliminating the 5th, 7th, 11th, and 13th output voltage harmonics. Resource utilisation, interpolation latency (measured at 1.4 µs from modulation index update to angle output), and sensitivity of harmonic cancellation quality to interpolation error are reported. Hardware testing on a 2 kVA laboratory inverter confirmed that output voltage THD with the interpolated table differed by at most 0.15 percentage points from the THD achieved using the full-resolution table, across 61 modulation index points from 0.5 to 1.1. The design targets inverter control cards in cost-sensitive retrofit applications.

title: Selective Harmonic Elimination Under Unbalanced DC-Link Voltages in Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters: Reformulation and Experimental Validation
abstract: Standard SHE-PWM formulations assume equal DC-link voltages across all H-bridge cells. In practice, unequal charging of isolated DC sources—common in photovoltaic-fed or battery-buffered CHB drives—distorts the output voltage spectrum and invalidates pre-computed angle tables. This paper reformulates the SHE-PWM equations to account for arbitrary, known DC-link voltage imbalances across a seven-level (three-cell) CHB inverter. The reformulated system is solved using a trust-region algorithm with multiple random starting points to locate all physically meaningful solution branches. Angle correction maps were constructed for DC-link voltage deviations of up to ±15% relative to nominal. Experimental tests on a laboratory CHB prototype with deliberately unbalanced DC supplies (220 V, 208 V, 234 V nominal 220 V per cell) showed that corrected angles reduced the 5th harmonic from 4.1% to below 0.5% of the fundamental and the 7th harmonic from 3.7% to below 0.6%. The paper discusses update latency requirements if the correction is applied dynamically during operation.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Lifetime Estimation Methods for Primary Lithium Cells in Static IoT Sensors
abstract: Four lifetime estimation methods are benchmarked against each other using a common dataset of 60 Li/MnO₂ and 60 Li/SOCl₂ cells discharged under eight realistic IoT sensor profiles. The methods compared are: (i) Peukert-based capacity scaling, (ii) a lookup-table approach derived from manufacturer pulse-discharge curves, (iii) a two-RC equivalent-circuit model updated by EIS, and (iv) a Gaussian process regression model trained on early-discharge features. All methods are evaluated on prediction error at 80 % and 100 % cell depletion. The Gaussian process method achieves the lowest median absolute error (6.2 % at end-of-life) but requires 11 input features extracted during the first 5 % of discharge. The EIS-based model achieves 8.7 % median error with fewer inputs. The Peukert method is least accurate at 22 % median error. A decision flowchart is provided to help practitioners choose a method based on available hardware and tolerable error. All data and model code are published under a CC-BY licence.

title: Power–Quality Trade-offs in Approximate Adder Trees for DCT-Based JPEG Encoding
abstract: This work examines the use of speculative adder designs inside the butterfly stages of an 8-point 1-D discrete cosine transform intended for JPEG baseline encoding. Four speculative adder families—carry-select with reduced lookahead, almost correct adder, error-tolerant adder type I, and a locally approximate variant—are inserted into a synthesised RTL pipeline and evaluated on a corpus of 1200 colour images compressed at quality factor 80. Metrics collected include mean absolute error in DCT coefficients, structural similarity index of reconstructed images, gate count, and estimated switching energy at 100 MHz in 130 nm CMOS. The locally approximate adder achieves the best energy–quality ratio, reducing toggle-weighted power by 27% relative to a reference ripple-carry baseline while maintaining SSIM above 0.97 on all test images. Timing closure is verified with static timing analysis at the target frequency, and no timing violations are introduced by the approximate stages.

title: Fitting two-parameter Weibull distributions to pump failure data from a Serbian petrochemical facility: a censored-data maximum-likelihood approach
abstract: Centrifugal pumps in continuous-process industries are among the most frequently replaced components, yet field failure records are almost always incomplete due to preventive replacements and planned shutdowns. This paper applies maximum-likelihood estimation with right-censored and interval-censored data to a set of 214 pump failure events collected over eight years at a petrochemical plant in Pančevo, Serbia. Shape and scale parameters are estimated for eight pump subtypes grouped by duty class. Goodness-of-fit is evaluated with the Anderson–Darling statistic. Results indicate that mechanical seal failures follow a shape parameter β between 1.8 and 2.4, confirming wear-out behaviour, while bearing failures cluster around β ≈ 1.1, closer to a random-failure regime. The fitted distributions are used to derive mean time between failures and B10 life estimates. Confidence intervals are constructed via likelihood profiling. The study highlights biases introduced when censoring is ignored and provides a practical data-cleaning procedure applicable to other Serbian heavy-industry datasets.

title: Age-replacement policies for rotating machinery under Weibull wear-out: cost-rate optimisation with incomplete maintenance histories
abstract: Age-replacement models prescribe an optimal replacement age that balances planned-replacement costs against the higher costs of run-to-failure. In industrial practice, however, the age of a component at the moment it enters the maintenance record is often unknown, introducing left-truncation into the failure history. This paper extends the classical Barlow–Proschan age-replacement cost-rate formulation to handle left-truncated failure times using a weighted likelihood correction. A numerical optimisation routine based on golden-section search is applied to data from 47 gearboxes in a sugar-processing plant in Vojvodina. For the dominant failure mode, the optimal replacement age decreases by 12% relative to the naive estimate that ignores truncation. Sensitivity analysis shows that cost-rate results are more sensitive to the ratio of planned-to-unplanned replacement costs than to uncertainty in the Weibull shape parameter. The paper concludes with a decision table for maintenance planners.

title: Spare-parts provisioning under stochastic demand driven by equipment failure processes: a renewal-theory framework
abstract: Spare-parts inventory for capital-intensive equipment differs from standard retail inventory because demand is generated by an underlying failure or replacement process rather than by independent customer orders. This book chapter reviews the connection between renewal theory and spare-parts demand modelling, covering the ordinary renewal process, the stationary renewal process, and the compound Poisson approximation for long-lead-time items. For each model the chapter derives the expected number of demands over a finite horizon and the associated variance, which together parameterise a negative-binomial approximation used to set reorder points. Numerical examples draw on maintenance records from cement-production and food-processing facilities in the Western Balkans. The chapter also discusses how to account for non-stationary failure intensities arising from infant mortality or seasonal loading, and gives worked procedures for practitioners who have access to a spreadsheet but not specialised reliability software. It closes with a comparison of safety-stock formulas from the reliability-driven model against those from classical demand forecasting.

title: Condition-based maintenance triggers derived from vibration trend data: integrating proportional hazards modelling with inventory replenishment
abstract: Condition-based maintenance (CBM) systems generate variable and hard-to-predict replacement demands that complicate spare-parts inventory control. This paper proposes a procedure that links a proportional hazards model (PHM), fitted to vibration root-mean-square trend data from 62 rolling-element bearings on paper-machine rolls, with a modified (s, Q) inventory policy whose reorder point is updated at each condition-monitoring inspection. The PHM covariate is the ratio of the current vibration level to the baseline level at commissioning. Posterior failure-time distributions conditional on the latest covariate observation are used to compute expected demand over the replenishment lead time. The adaptive policy is compared against a static policy calibrated on historical mean demand. Over a two-year test period, stockout events fell from 14 to 5 and average inventory dropped by 18%. The paper also discusses the practical challenge of missing vibration readings and proposes a last-observation-carried-forward imputation strategy.

title: Estimating remaining useful life distributions for slow-speed bearings using mixture Weibull models and bootstrap confidence bands
abstract: Slow-speed bearings in sugar-mill roller drives and similar equipment present a data-scarcity problem: failure events are infrequent, vibration signatures are masked by low signal-to-noise ratios, and each machine may contribute only one or two observed failures over a decade of operation. This paper examines whether mixture Weibull models with two sub-populations—reflecting manufacturing-defect early failures and wear-out failures—provide better remaining-useful-life (RUL) estimates than single-distribution fits given samples of 20–60 failure times. Monte Carlo experiments show that when the true mixture weight of the early-failure sub-population exceeds 0.15, the two-component mixture reduces RUL mean-squared error by 30–45% relative to a single Weibull. For smaller mixing weights the improvement is negligible and the simpler model is preferred by AIC. Parametric bootstrap confidence bands for the RUL distribution are also derived and their coverage properties assessed. Practical guidance on minimum sample sizes needed to distinguish mixtures is given for maintenance engineers.

title: Life-cycle cost comparison of corrective, time-based, and condition-based maintenance strategies for hydraulic presses: a Balkan manufacturing case study
abstract: Hydraulic presses used in metal-forming operations have high acquisition costs and long service lives, making maintenance strategy selection economically significant. This paper constructs life-cycle cost models for three maintenance strategies—corrective maintenance only, fixed-interval preventive replacement, and condition-based maintenance triggered by oil-contamination particle counts—for a fleet of 18 hydraulic presses at two manufacturing plants in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Failure time data spanning 2009–2022 are analysed using Weibull regression with plant and press-tonnage covariates. The condition-based strategy yields the lowest expected life-cycle cost per press (estimated at 11% below time-based preventive maintenance) but requires an oil-analysis programme whose setup cost is amortised over approximately 2.4 years for fleets larger than ten presses. Cost uncertainty is characterised using a Latin hypercube sampling approach with 5,000 replications. Results are sensitive to the assumed cost of unplanned downtime, with corrective maintenance becoming competitive only when downtime costs are below €180 per hour.

title: Stochastic inventory models for long-lead-time rotary kiln components: accounting for imperfect repair and partial replenishment
abstract: Rotary kilns in cement and lime production rely on a small number of high-cost, long-lead-time components—notably riding rings, thrust rollers, and kiln shells—whose procurement lead times can reach 16–28 weeks. This paper models the inventory of such components under a periodic-review policy where replenishment quantities may arrive partially if a supplier cannot fill the full order. Component lifetimes after an imperfect repair are described by the arithmetic reduction of age model, with repair effectiveness estimated from plant maintenance logs. The stochastic demand process is derived from the renewal-reward theorem applied to the imperfect-repair sequence. Reorder points and order quantities are optimised for a service-level constraint of no more than 0.5 stockouts per year per component type. The model is applied to data from a lime-production facility in Kovin, Serbia, covering four kiln component types over 15 years. Accounting for imperfect repair reduces estimated reorder points by one unit for three of the four components compared to a perfect-repair assumption.

title: Tool-wear monitoring in interrupted turning using spindle-current signals from standard CNC drives
abstract: Retrofit force dynamometers and AE sensors add cost and complexity that prevents their adoption in most production environments. Spindle motor current, already available on modern CNC drives as a standard output, is examined here as a low-cost proxy for cutting force in interrupted turning. Tests were conducted on a production turning centre without hardware modification; motor-current data were logged via the drive's serial interface at 200 Hz sampling. Workpiece material was EN 1.4301 austenitic stainless steel, known for high tool demands. Over 56 tool-life trials, a CUSUM chart on a 10 s windowed mean of spindle current detected VB > 0.20 mm in 87% of cases with a median detection lag of 3.2 windows. The false-alarm rate was 3.6%. The signal was noisier than a dynamometer (SNR approximately 14 dB vs. 28 dB) but sufficient for reliable end-of-life detection under the test conditions. The approach requires only a one-time calibration run per insert grade.

title: Farmers' Market Participation and Household Income in Vojvodina: Evidence from a Survey of Vegetable Producers
abstract: This study examines the relationship between participation in urban farmers' markets and total household income among small-scale vegetable producers in Vojvodina. Data were collected through structured interviews with 148 farm households across four municipalities in 2010. Descriptive statistics and OLS regression were used to assess income contributions from direct sales relative to wholesale and intermediary channels. Results indicate that households selling at farmers' markets derived, on average, 34% of their agricultural income from this channel, compared with 18% for households relying exclusively on wholesale buyers. Market participation was positively associated with proximity to Novi Sad and the availability of family labour. The paper highlights infrastructure and certification barriers that limit participation by more remote producers and recommends targeted support through municipal market development programmes.

title: Trust and Repeat Purchasing in Direct Farm Sales: A Case Study of Two Novi Sad Green Markets
abstract: Using exit surveys administered to 312 customers at two municipal green markets in Novi Sad over eight weeks in spring 2013, this study investigates the determinants of repeat purchasing from identified small-farm stalls. A binary logistic regression model relates repeat-purchase behaviour to perceived product freshness, vendor familiarity, price transparency, and traceability information provided at the point of sale. Results show that vendor familiarity (odds ratio 2.7) and verbal traceability claims (odds ratio 2.1) are the strongest predictors of stated repeat-purchase intent, while price differences relative to supermarkets were not statistically significant. The findings suggest that relationship quality between producer and buyer is a more robust driver of loyalty than price competition alone, with implications for how producers and market managers might invest their promotional efforts.

title: Women's Labour and Decision-Making in Short Supply Chain Enterprises on Family Farms in Central Serbia
abstract: This paper draws on qualitative fieldwork conducted in 2014 in the Šumadija and Morava districts, comprising 31 in-depth interviews with women on family farms engaged in direct or near-direct sales of processed and fresh products. The analysis applies a gender-disaggregated livelihood framework to examine how women's contributions to SFSC activities—processing, packaging, market attendance, and customer communication—are recognised in household decision-making around investment and income allocation. Findings reveal that women carry the majority of daily SFSC labour on most surveyed farms yet retain formal control over proceeds in fewer than one-third of cases. The paper connects these dynamics to broader patterns of rural gender inequality in Serbia and argues that agricultural extension services should explicitly address intra-household bargaining when promoting direct-sales strategies to family farms.

title: Economic Margins in Farm-to-Restaurant Sales: Evidence from Organic Vegetable Producers in Vojvodina
abstract: This study analyses the economic margins achieved by certified organic vegetable producers in Vojvodina who supply restaurants directly, comparing them with producers selling through wholesale intermediaries. Data were gathered from financial records and structured interviews with 46 organic producers and 18 restaurant buyers in 2015–2016. Gross margin analysis shows that direct farm-to-restaurant sales yielded average margins 28 percentage points higher than wholesale channels for the same crop categories, though transaction costs associated with small-batch delivery and relationship management partially offset this advantage. Multivariate analysis identifies contract length and producer proximity to Novi Sad as significant moderating variables. The paper discusses implications for extension advice on channel selection and calls for standardised cost accounting tools adapted to small organic operations.

title: Barriers to SFSC Expansion Among Elderly Farmers in Rural Vojvodina
abstract: Ageing of the farm workforce is a documented trend in Serbia, yet its intersection with short food supply chain (SFSC) participation has received limited attention. This paper reports findings from a mixed-methods study combining a postal survey of 203 farmers aged 60 and above in Vojvodina and 14 follow-up semi-structured interviews conducted in 2017. Quantitative analysis identifies physical mobility constraints, limited digital literacy, and lack of a designated successor as the primary barriers to SFSC adoption or expansion. Qualitative data add nuance by revealing that social isolation and reduced bargaining confidence also play a role. The paper argues that rural development instruments targeting SFSCs need age-sensitive design elements, including mobile market access schemes and mentorship pairings with younger farmers, to avoid excluding a significant segment of the existing smallholder population.

title: Mapping Short Food Supply Chain Density Across the Danube–Tisza–Danube Region: A GIS-Based Approach
abstract: This study uses geographic information system methods to map and classify SFSC outlets—farmers' markets, farm shops, box-scheme pick-up points, and direct-delivery arrangements—across the DTD (Danube–Tisza–Danube) canal region of Vojvodina. Data were assembled from municipal registries, field verification visits to 87 sites in 2020, and georeferenced consumer survey data from 641 respondents. Kernel density estimation identifies two high-density clusters around Novi Sad and Zrenjanin, with significant spatial gaps in the northwestern and northeastern parts of the region. Logistic accessibility modelling shows that approximately 38% of the rural population lives more than 15 km from any verified SFSC outlet. The resulting maps have been shared with Provincial Secretariat staff and provide a baseline for evaluating future rural development interventions targeting market access.

title: Price Premium Realisation and Its Variability Among Direct-Selling Fruit Producers in Serbia
abstract: This paper investigates whether small-scale fruit producers in Serbia consistently realise the price premiums commonly attributed to direct sales, and what accounts for variability in premium levels across producers and crops. Using production and sales records voluntarily provided by 88 producers in Vojvodina and Western Serbia, combined with matched wholesale price data from the Republican Institute of Statistics for 2019–2021, a panel regression approach is applied. Results show high variability: the median direct-sales premium across all producers and years is 22% above wholesale prices, but the interquartile range spans from 4% to 51%. Product category, proximity to a city of over 50 000 inhabitants, and frequency of market attendance explain approximately 41% of this variance. The paper cautions against treating the price premium as a guaranteed benefit and identifies producer characteristics associated with consistently above-median premiums.

title: Institutional Support Schemes for Short Food Supply Chains in EU Candidate Countries: Lessons for Serbian Policy Design
abstract: This book chapter reviews the design and outcomes of public support schemes for short food supply chains in three EU candidate and recent accession countries—Slovenia, Croatia, and Romania—drawing on programme evaluation reports, budget data, and eight expert interviews conducted in 2022. The chapter identifies four recurring design elements in more effective schemes: clear legal definitions of SFSCs, dedicated funding lines within rural development programmes, producer training components, and municipal co-investment requirements. It then assesses the extent to which current Serbian IPARD III programming reflects these elements, finding partial adoption of definitional clarity but limited dedicated funding. Recommendations are offered for the next IPARD cycle and for complementary measures that could be implemented through the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture without awaiting full EU accession.

title: Livelihood Portfolios of Near-Exit Farmers: When Direct Sales Delay or Prevent Farm Abandonment
abstract: Drawing on longitudinal qualitative data from 22 farm households in Vojvodina revisited over three interview rounds between 2016 and 2024, this paper examines the role of SFSC income in decisions about whether to continue farming. Using a livelihood portfolio framework, the analysis traces how SFSC revenues, particularly from farmers' markets and community-supported agriculture box schemes, interact with off-farm employment, pension income, and land-lease revenues to shape continuation or exit decisions. In twelve of the twenty-two households, SFSC income was identified as the decisive factor in the decision to continue farming past a point at which wholesale margins alone would have prompted cessation. The paper contributes qualitative texture to debates about structural change in Serbian agriculture, where average farm size and the pace of land consolidation remain contested policy issues.

title: Γ-konvergencija perimeterskih funkcionala sa kapilarnom korekcijom na domenu sa glatkom granicom
abstract: U ovom radu proučavamo niz varijacionih funkcionala oblika koji kombinuju klasični perimeterski funkcionalni sa površinskim energijskim termom duž zadatog dela granice domene. Koristeći aparat Γ-konvergencije u smislu De Giorgia, dokazujemo da odgovarajući fazni-polski funkcionali, parametrizovani sa ε → 0, konvergiraju ka sharp-interface limitu koji se poklapa sa kapilarnim energijskim funkcionalnim. Analiza se oslanja na ocenu donje granice putem sečenja i refleksije, kao i na konstrukciju oporavne sekvence zasnovane na optimalnim prelaznim profilima. Razmatramo slučaj domene čija je granica C^{2,α} glatka i pokazujemo da dodatan rubni doprinos precizno reprodukuje energiju kvašenja kosim uglom između 30° i 150°. Rezultati su verifikovani poređenjem sa poznatim rešenjima za sferne kapice na ravnim podlogama.

title: A finite element scheme for axisymmetric capillary surfaces with pinned and free contact lines
abstract: We develop and analyse a finite element method for computing equilibrium shapes of axisymmetric capillary surfaces governed by the Young–Laplace equation under both pinned-contact-line and free-contact-line boundary conditions. The weak formulation is posed on a one-dimensional meridional domain, discretised with piecewise linear elements on a graded mesh near the contact points. We prove a priori error estimates in H^1 showing convergence of order O(h) for the free-contact-line case and O(h^{3/2}) for the pinned case, the difference arising from a corner singularity. Numerical experiments on a cylindrical capillary of radius 1 mm with water (surface tension 72.8 mN/m) confirm the theoretical rates. We also compare computed drop volumes at incipient detachment against experimental data from the literature for four liquids, finding relative errors below 2.1% in all cases. The implementation is released as an open-source Python module built on FEniCS.

title: Stabilnost kapilarnih površi pod perturbacijom ugla kvašenja: spektralna analiza drugog varijacionog funkcionala
abstract: Razmatramo pitanje stabilnosti ravnotežnih kapilarnih površi kada se ugao kvašenja podloge menja za mali parametar δ. Drugi varijacioni funkcionali oko ravnotežne konfiguracije formulišu se kao kvadratne forme na odgovarajućim Soboljevljevim prostorima. Koristimo teoriju samopridrugih operatora i spektralnu teoriju kompaktnih perturbacija da bismo pokazali da stabilna ravnoteža ostaje stabilna za |δ| < δ_0, gde δ_0 zavisi eksplicitno od geometrije površi i Bondovog broja. Izvodimo eksplicitne formule za promenu najnižih sopstvenih vrednosti Jakobijevog operatora pod ovom perturbacijom. Rezultati su primenjeni na tri kanonske geometrije: sferna kapica, kapljica na cilindru i meniskus u kapilari, gde numerički rezultati potvrđuju analitičke ocene sa relativnom greškom ispod 3%.

title: Numerička aproksimacija slobodnih granica u trodimenzionalnim kapilarnim sistemima metodom Level-Set
abstract: Razvijamo Level-Set metod prilagođen za praćenje slobodnih granica u trodimenzionalnim kapilarnim sistemima sa promenljivim uglom kvašenja. Numerička shema kombinuje standardnu Level-Set advektivnu jednačinu sa geometrijskom korekcijom normale na granici računskog domena kako bi se osiguralo ispunjenje kapilarnog rubnog uslova. Prostorna diskretizacija zasnovana je na mrežama prvog i drugog reda tačnosti u L^2-normi. Testiramo metod na četiri referentna primera: statička kapljica na ravnoj podlozi, kapljica na kosom zidu, kapilarni uspon u pravougaonoj prizmi i trostruka kontaktna linija na heterogenoj podlozi. Za svaki primer poredimo dobijene profile sa analitičkim ili numerički referentnim rešenjima i beležimo grešku oblika ispod 1.4% u svim slučajevima. Posebna pažnja posvećena je stabilnosti metoda pri Bondovim brojevima u opsegu 0.05–10.

title: Isoperimetric-type inequalities for capillary drops under gravity: a geometric measure theory approach
abstract: We prove a sharp isoperimetric inequality for liquid drops in a half-space subject to gravitational body force, where the drop adheres to the bounding hyperplane with a prescribed contact angle θ ∈ (0°, 90°]. The inequality bounds the surface energy of any admissible drop from below in terms of its volume and θ, with equality characterised by spherical caps. The proof proceeds by a symmetrisation argument in the framework of sets of finite perimeter, using the Steiner symmetrisation adapted to the half-space geometry and a careful analysis of how the wetting energy transforms under symmetrisation. We also derive a stability version: any drop whose energy is within ε of the minimum satisfies a deficit estimate in terms of the Fraenkel asymmetry with constant depending only on θ and the Bond number. The constant is computed explicitly for θ = 30°, 60°, 90° and found to be of order 10^{−1} to 10^{0}.

title: Kapilarni efekti u mikrofluidnim kanalima nepravilnog preseka: varijacioni model i eksperimentalna validacija
abstract: Kombinujemo varijacioni pristup za modelovanje ravnotežnih meniskusa u mikrofluidnim kanalima čiji poprečni presek nije standardnog oblika (trapezni, poligonalni i hibridni profili koji odgovaraju realnim PDMS kanalima) sa skupom merenja dobijenih saradnjom sa jednim startup preduzećem iz Naučno-tehnološkog parka. Varijacioni problem minimizacije ukupne kapilarno-gravitacione energije formulišemo na skupu skupova konačnog perimetra unutar zadatog kanala i dokazujemo egzistenciju rešenja. Numeričku aproksimaciju vršimo prilagođenom Surface Evolver procedurom uz triangulacione mreže sa 8 000–40 000 trouglova. Eksperimentalni podaci obuhvataju 36 konfiguracija kanala sa hidrofobnim i hidrofilnim oblogama i tri radna fluida (voda, etanol, izopropanol). Srednje kvadratno odstupanje između simuliranih i merenih visina meniskusa iznosi 4.7 μm, što odgovara relativnoj grešci ispod 6% u svim ispitanim slučajevima.

title: Pinning and depinning transitions for contact lines on chemically heterogeneous substrates: a variational energy landscape analysis
abstract: We study pinning and depinning of the contact line of a sessile drop on a substrate with a periodic chemical pattern, modelled as a two-phase wettability distribution with contact angles θ_1 = 40° and θ_2 = 110° and stripe width ratios ranging from 1:1 to 1:9. The total energy is expressed as a functional on the space of Caccioppoli sets, and we identify local and global minimisers using a mountain-pass argument adapted to the BV setting. The energy barriers separating locally stable pinned states are estimated analytically and compared with results from a direct numerical minimisation using a gradient-flow discretisation with time step τ = 10^{−4}. We find that the barrier height scales as the product of the wettability contrast, the stripe width, and the line tension, and we derive a closed-form approximation valid when the stripe width is much smaller than the drop radius. Implications for hysteresis in contact angle measurements are discussed.

title: Comparing SMOTE variants for minority-class oversampling in multivariate haematology data
abstract: Synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) and its derivatives are widely applied to imbalanced tabular datasets, but their comparative behaviour on clinical haematology data has received limited systematic attention. We evaluated six SMOTE variants—original SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE 1 and 2, SVM-SMOTE, ADASYN, and k-means SMOTE—across four binary classification tasks drawn from a haematology laboratory database of 11,340 samples spanning anaemia subtype discrimination, thrombocytopenia grading, and lymphocyte subset classification. Each variant was paired with a random forest classifier trained under five-fold stratified cross-validation. Primary metrics were AUPRC, geometric mean, and Brier score. k-means SMOTE produced the highest geometric mean in three of four tasks, while original SMOTE and ADASYN performed comparably on the remaining task. Computational overhead of k-means SMOTE was 2.4 times that of original SMOTE on the largest dataset. Absolute differences in AUPRC across variants rarely exceeded 0.03, suggesting that classifier choice may matter more than oversampling variant for these data sizes.

title: Adaptive Tile Cache Replacement Policies for Spatially Correlated Web Map Access Patterns
abstract: Tile caching is critical for web map performance, but standard LRU and LFU cache replacement policies do not account for the spatial correlation of user pan and zoom behaviour. This paper introduces two spatially aware cache replacement policies, SpatialLRU and ZoomWeightedLFU, that prioritise retention of tiles spatially adjacent to recently requested tiles and tiles at frequently revisited zoom levels. The policies are evaluated using access logs from a regional geoportal serving 1.8 million tile requests per day over a six-month period. SpatialLRU achieves a 12% improvement in cache hit rate over standard LRU at equal cache sizes, and ZoomWeightedLFU achieves 9% improvement, both statistically significant at p < 0.01. A combined policy yields 15% improvement. Implications for CDN edge node sizing and tile server load balancing are discussed, including a cost model for estimating infrastructure savings.

title: A Rule-Based Framework for Detecting Structural Inconsistencies in REST API Responses
abstract: Web service APIs frequently change their response schemas without formal versioning, causing downstream data consumers to silently ingest malformed or incomplete records. This paper presents a lightweight rule-based framework that continuously inspects JSON payloads returned by REST endpoints and flags deviations from a registered baseline schema. The framework encodes expected field types, cardinality constraints, and value-range rules in a declarative specification file. Violations are classified into four severity tiers and surfaced through an alerting interface. The approach was evaluated against a corpus of 14 publicly accessible APIs monitored over six months, capturing 38 distinct schema-change events. Detection latency averaged 1.4 seconds from the first non-conforming response. False-positive rates remained below 2.1% across all monitored endpoints. The paper also discusses how rule sets can be partially auto-generated from historical response samples using frequency-based field inference. The implementation is provided as a self-contained Java library with a configuration-file interface.

title: Cross-Source Consistency Validation for Event-Triggered Business Logic in Distributed Retail Systems
abstract: When a single business event—such as a purchase confirmation—must be reflected consistently across inventory, billing, and logistics APIs, inconsistencies arising from partial failures or race conditions can corrupt downstream decision logic. This paper formalises a consistency validation model that reconciles event records from multiple independent API sources by aligning them on a shared transaction identifier and a configurable time window. A conflict detection module compares field-level values across sources and produces a structured discrepancy report. The approach was tested on a synthetic dataset of 500,000 simulated purchase events with injected inconsistencies at rates of 0.5%, 2%, and 5%. Precision exceeded 97% in all three scenarios; recall dropped to 91% at 0.5% injection rate due to borderline timestamp ambiguities. The paper proposes a tie-breaking heuristic based on source-reliability weights that partially recovers recall in low-rate conditions. Runtime overhead on a four-core commodity server was under 8% of total pipeline throughput.

title: Schema Drift in Production API Pipelines: A Classification and Empirical Frequency Study
abstract: Schema drift—the unannounced alteration of data structures returned by APIs—is a recurring but poorly documented source of pipeline failures in practice. This paper presents a taxonomy of drift types encountered in production environments, distinguishing field addition, field removal, type coercion, key renaming, and structural nesting changes. An automated monitoring agent was deployed against 31 internal API endpoints operated by four partner organisations over 12 months, logging all response payloads in a versioned data store. Analysis of 9.7 million captured responses identified 74 drift events. Field addition was the most frequent type (41%), followed by type coercion (27%). Drift events clustered around software release dates, with 68% occurring within 48 hours of a detected version tag change in response headers. The paper derives practical design guidelines for pipeline engineers and discusses the feasibility of proactive drift prediction using release-calendar metadata.

title: Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry
abstract: High-frequency telemetry streams produced by IoT gateways and industrial APIs exhibit multivariate numeric patterns that rule-based detectors handle poorly when anomalies involve correlated deviations across several fields simultaneously. This paper investigates the use of the Isolation Forest algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection in such streams, focusing on tuning the contamination parameter and the number of estimators under streaming constraints. Experiments used telemetry data from a factory automation pilot comprising six sensor channels sampled at 10 Hz over 30 days, yielding approximately 15.5 million records. Isolation Forest outperformed a univariate z-score baseline by 18 percentage points in F1 score on held-out labelled anomaly windows. The paper also reports the effect of sub-sampling strategies on detection quality when full-stream processing is not feasible, and provides a reference configuration table for practitioners operating within defined memory budgets. No labelled training data was required beyond the held-out evaluation set.

title: Data Quality Monitoring in Apache Kafka Pipelines: Design Patterns and Operational Trade-offs
abstract: Apache Kafka has become a standard backbone for real-time data integration, yet integrating data quality checks directly into Kafka-based pipelines introduces non-trivial design decisions around consumer group placement, serialisation overhead, and back-pressure handling. This book chapter surveys and categorises design patterns for embedding schema validation, completeness checks, and anomaly scoring into Kafka consumer and Kafka Streams topologies. Four patterns are described in detail: inline validator consumers, side-car quality topics, quality-aware stream processors, and batch reconciliation jobs reading from compacted topics. Each pattern is evaluated against five criteria: latency impact, fault isolation, replayability, operational complexity, and suitability for schema drift detection. The chapter draws on deployment experience from three pilot integrations and provides worked configuration examples for each pattern using the Confluent Schema Registry and custom Avro schemas. Intended audience is data engineers and architects with working Kafka experience.

title: Detecting Silent Data Corruption Caused by API Middleware Caching in Event-Driven Microservices
abstract: Middleware caching layers in microservice architectures can serve stale data to downstream consumers long after the source record has been updated, producing a form of silent data corruption that is difficult to detect because individual responses remain schema-valid. This paper describes a consistency audit mechanism that periodically issues cache-bypass probe requests and compares their payloads against the most recently cached versions stored in a pipeline audit log. Discrepancies are scored by field-level severity weights reflecting business criticality. The mechanism was deployed in a logistics integration scenario comprising 11 microservices and approximately 200,000 event transactions per day. Over a four-week observation window, 312 stale-cache discrepancy instances were identified, of which 29 affected fields classified as high-criticality. The paper analyses the relationship between cache TTL settings and discrepancy frequency and proposes an adaptive TTL reduction policy triggered by elevated discrepancy scores. End-to-end detection latency averaged 3.1 seconds.

title: Benchmarking Schema-Drift Detectors Under Controlled Injection: A Reproducible Evaluation Protocol
abstract: Comparing schema-drift detection methods across published papers is hampered by incompatible datasets, inconsistent drift injection procedures, and unreported hyperparameter choices. This paper proposes a reproducible benchmarking protocol for schema-drift detectors operating on JSON API streams. The protocol defines six canonical drift injection categories, each with three severity levels, applied to a synthetic baseline dataset generated by a configurable data generator released alongside the paper. Five existing detection approaches—including two rule-based and three statistical methods—were re-implemented and evaluated under the protocol. Results show that rule-based methods achieve higher precision on structural drift (type coercion, key removal) but fail entirely on distributional value drift, whereas statistical detectors show the inverse pattern. No single evaluated method scored above 0.80 F1 across all six categories simultaneously. The paper concludes with a discussion of hybrid architectures and releases all code and datasets under an open licence to facilitate future comparisons.

title: Incremental Schema Inference for Long-Running API Integrations Using Probabilistic Field Tracking
abstract: Maintaining accurate schema documentation for APIs that evolve continuously over years is impractical when done manually. This paper presents an incremental schema inference engine that updates a probabilistic field model after each observed API response, tracking field presence probability, dominant type, value entropy, and co-occurrence correlations with other fields. The engine distinguishes transient field appearances (sparse presence below a configurable threshold) from stable schema additions, reducing noise in drift alerts. It was evaluated on a 26-month archive of responses from seven APIs in a supply chain integration platform, comprising 31 million records. The inferred schemas at month 26 matched manually audited ground-truth schemas with 94.2% field-level precision and 96.8% recall. Incremental update cost per response averaged 0.9 milliseconds on a mid-range server. The paper discusses integration with existing Kafka-based pipeline monitoring and provides configuration guidance for organisations with limited schema governance resources.

title: One-Class SVM for Detection of Scripted Clients in a Massively Multiplayer Online Environment
abstract: Scripted clients—programs that automate repetitive in-game actions—undermine economy balance in online games and are difficult to identify using rule-based filters alone. This paper applies one-class support vector machines (OC-SVM) to a labelled telemetry dataset of 48,000 sessions drawn from a game server log archive, of which 3,200 sessions were confirmed scripted via ban records. Training used only the majority legitimate-player class. Feature vectors were constructed from 22 behavioural metrics including action entropy, movement path straightness, click interval coefficient of variation, and resource acquisition rate. Radial basis function kernel parameters were tuned via cross-validation on a held-out clean subset. The resulting model achieved an F1 score of 0.81 on the contaminated test split, with a false-positive rate of 4.3%. Results were compared against isolation forest and local outlier factor baselines. The paper also discusses the effect of class contamination levels during training on downstream detection performance.

title: Knowledge distillation from transformer-based activity recognisers to microcontroller-deployable CNNs
abstract: Transformer architectures operating on raw IMU sequences achieve high recognition accuracy but are impractical for wearable hardware due to their parameter count and memory footprint. This paper applies offline knowledge distillation to transfer prediction behaviour from a six-layer temporal self-attention teacher (1.4 M parameters, F1 = 0.927 on the benchmark set) to a student 1-D CNN with 45 000 parameters. Training uses the standard KL-divergence soft-target loss with temperature sweeping from 2 to 8 on a combined dataset drawn from three public wrist-IMU corpora totalling 112 hours. The distilled student achieves F1 = 0.911, narrowing the gap from direct-training F1 = 0.893 by 18 percentage points of the teacher–student gap. Deployment on a Cortex-M33 device at 64 MHz consumes 8.4 mW during inference on a 1 s window, measured with a hardware power monitor. Flash footprint after quantisation is 182 KB.

title: Enriched Kleisli Categories and the Semantics of Call-by-Push-Value
abstract: We give a semantics for Levy's call-by-push-value calculus using enriched Kleisli categories. Starting from a V-enriched monad T on a V-category C, where V is a complete and cocomplete symmetric monoidal closed category, we construct an enriched Kleisli category Kl_V(T) and show that it carries the structure required to interpret the value and computation types of call-by-push-value. The adjunction between values and computations is recovered as an enriched adjunction between C and Kl_V(T). We work out three concrete instances: Set-enrichment recovering the standard model, poset-enrichment giving an order-theoretic model suitable for fixed-point induction, and metric-space enrichment giving a quantitative model. For each instance we verify the relevant equations of the calculus. The metric instance is new and yields a model in which computational cost is tracked by a real-valued distance on terms.

title: Comonadic Semantics of Contextual Modalities
abstract: We study a type theory with contextual modalities, motivated by staged computation and coeffect systems, and provide its denotational semantics in terms of comonads on a symmetric monoidal closed category. For each modality in the type theory we associate a comonad whose co-Kleisli category models the modal fragment. The central technical contribution is a coherence result: when two comonads C and D commute up to a distributive law, the corresponding modal type constructors can be combined consistently. We formalize the semantics in Coq, producing a proof term for the soundness theorem that amounts to approximately 2,400 lines of tactic script. The development identifies a gap in an earlier treatment by Brunel et al., and we provide a corrected statement and proof of their main lemma. We also give a small-step operational semantics and prove computational adequacy with respect to the denotational model.

title: Towards a Categorical Semantics of Gradual Typing
abstract: Gradual type systems combine static and dynamic typing along a precision lattice. We propose a categorical framework for their denotational semantics based on the notion of an embedding-retraction pair between types, organized into a category Grad. We show that the naive function space does not form an embedding-retraction pair in general, and characterize precisely when it does in terms of a universal property of the precision order. The paper defines a notion of gradual Cartesian closed category and shows that the semantics of the gradually typed lambda calculus can be given in any such category. As a concrete model we construct a gradual CCC from Scott domains, recovering a domain-theoretic semantics compatible with the existing operational theory. The framework unifies two earlier categorical proposals by Lennon-Bertrand and by New and Licata, clarifying which axioms each implicitly assumes.

title: A Quantitative Denotational Semantics for Recursive Types via Metric Enrichment
abstract: We construct a denotational model for a higher-order language with recursive types in which every type is interpreted as a 1-Lipschitz metric space and every term as a non-expansive function. Recursive types are handled by solving domain equations in the category of complete ultrametric spaces and non-expansive maps, exploiting the fact that this category has a terminal object and that the functor corresponding to recursive type formation is locally contractive in the sense of Birkedal et al. We show that the distance between two programs in the model corresponds to a differential sensitivity property: programs at distance ε behave indistinguishably on inputs that are ε-close. As an application, we derive a quantitative logical relation for proving differential privacy of programs typed in a linear type discipline with graded modalities, recovering a known result by a uniform semantic argument. All constructions are presented at the level of enriched category theory.

title: Graded Monads and Resource-Sensitive Type Systems: A Uniform Treatment
abstract: Graded monads, indexed by a monoid of resource annotations, provide a fine-grained account of computational effects in which the resource usage of a computation is tracked in its type. We give a uniform categorical treatment of graded monads and their morphisms, defining a 2-category GrMnd(C) for any monoidal category C of grades and any category C of types. We characterize when GrMnd(C) is fibered over the category of grade monoids and use this structure to systematically derive the typing rules of several resource-sensitive type systems from the literature—including bounded linear logic, graded modal types, and sensitivity types for differential privacy—as instances of a single template. We prove a general soundness theorem at the level of 2-cells. As a secondary contribution we identify a previously unnoticed condition, which we call grade-commutativity, that is necessary and sufficient for graded function types to be closed under composition.

title: Operational and Denotational Adequacy for a Probabilistic Higher-Order Language with Continuous Distributions
abstract: We establish full abstraction between an operational and a denotational semantics for a simply typed higher-order language with continuous probabilistic choice. The operational semantics is given by a Markov kernel small-step reduction relation, while the denotational semantics interprets types as quasi-Borel spaces and terms as morphisms in the category QBS. The main result is that two terms are contextually equivalent in the operational semantics if and only if they are identified by the denotational model. The proof proceeds by constructing a logical relation between QBS morphisms and distributions over closed terms, using compactness of the type structure in an essential way. We also characterize the definable elements of each type and show that the model contains non-definable elements at base type, confirming that the language is not fully complete. The paper includes a mechanized verification of the base cases of the adequacy argument in Lean 4.

title: Effect Handlers Have a Categorical Semantics in Eilenberg–Moore Algebras: A Corrected Account
abstract: Several papers in the literature claim that the semantics of algebraic effect handlers can be modeled entirely within the Eilenberg–Moore category of a monad. We revisit these claims, identify two errors in the published proofs—one concerning the handling of forwarding and one concerning the composition of handlers—and provide corrected statements. The correction to the forwarding lemma requires strengthening the hypothesis from a commutative to a separable monad; we show by counterexample that the original hypothesis is insufficient. We also provide a positive result: for the class of finitary effects defined by a Lawvere theory, the corrected theorem holds unconditionally, and we give a new proof using a coequalizer construction in the category of algebras. All counterexamples are finite and are verified by exhaustive computation in a Python script provided in the supplementary material.

title: A Matheuristic for the Integrated Shift Design and Rostering Problem
abstract: Most personnel scheduling approaches treat shift design (selecting the set of shifts to offer) and rostering (assigning employees to shifts) as sequential problems, which can lead to suboptimal overall solutions. This paper presents a matheuristic that interleaves an ILP shift-design phase with a CP rostering phase through a feedback mechanism: the rostering phase reports hard-to-cover periods back to the shift-design phase, which adjusts shift lengths and start times accordingly. The integrated method is applied to a logistics warehouse operating around the clock with 130 employees across five job families. Over ten iterations of the feedback loop, the total staffing cost decreases by an average of 8.4% relative to the sequential baseline across 25 test instances. The method also reduces the average number of distinct shift types used by 3.1 per instance, which is operationally significant. Detailed convergence profiles and sensitivity to feedback parameters are reported.

title: Density-Based Grouping of Mouse-Movement Trajectories in Web Form Interactions
abstract: This paper applies a modified DBSCAN procedure to two-dimensional mouse-movement trajectories recorded during web form completion tasks. A corpus of 18,400 sessions collected from a public e-government portal over three months was preprocessed by segmenting continuous cursor paths at velocity inflection points, yielding approximately 210,000 sub-trajectories. Spatial proximity was defined using the Fréchet distance rather than Euclidean point distance, and epsilon and min-samples parameters were tuned by inspecting the sorted k-distance graph. The resulting clusters mapped onto four dominant interaction styles: direct field targeting, hesitant scanning, backtracking, and idle hovering. Cluster membership showed statistically significant association (chi-squared, p < 0.001) with form-completion success rates. The study demonstrates that trajectory-level density clustering is feasible on modest hardware when combined with aggressive sub-sampling and provides behavioural segmentations that are interpretable without any labelled ground truth.

title: Sequential Pattern Frequencies in Desktop Application Logs: A Baseline Study
abstract: Desktop application event logs from a suite of office productivity tools were mined for frequent sequential patterns using the PrefixSpan algorithm. The dataset comprised 6.2 million timestamped events recorded from 340 volunteer users over eight weeks. Minimum support thresholds were swept from 0.5% to 5% in steps of 0.5%, producing between 88 and 4,300 patterns depending on the threshold and a maximum pattern length of eight events. Results were evaluated against an independent validation set gathered two months later from the same user pool. The top-100 patterns by support were stable across the two collection periods with a Jaccard similarity of 0.81, suggesting that dominant interaction sequences are relatively consistent over time for this software category. The paper also reports the proportion of users who generate at least one rare pattern per session, which averaged 63%, motivating subsequent work on outlier detection in log streams.

title: Spatial Co-occurrence of UI Events: Constructing Interaction Heatmaps from Sparse Log Data
abstract: Many interaction logs record only discrete widget-activation events rather than continuous pointer coordinates, making standard kernel density estimation difficult. This paper proposes a spatial co-occurrence matrix approach in which each screen region is treated as a node and simultaneous or near-simultaneous activations within a 400 ms window contribute edge weights. Non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) with rank selected by the cophenetic correlation coefficient then decomposes the matrix into a small set of spatial basis patterns. The method is validated on logs from two legacy enterprise applications, each with approximately 120 widgets and 28,000 recorded sessions. NMF with rank 6 explained 87% of variance and recovered patterns that aligned with known task workflows verified against internal documentation. Runtime on a standard workstation was under four minutes per application. The approach generalises to any application for which only event-type and widget-ID are logged.

title: Detecting Anomalous Interaction Sessions in Industrial Control Panel Logs Using Isolation Forest
abstract: Industrial human–machine interface panels generate structured event logs whose anomaly detection has safety implications. This study applies Isolation Forest to session-level feature vectors extracted from twelve months of logs collected from a simulated control-room environment operated by technician volunteers. Eighty-three features were derived per session including inter-event timing statistics, action-reversal rate, and screen-region entropy. A controlled experiment injected 420 synthetic anomalous sessions representing three fault scenarios: misnavigation, repeated erroneous input, and unusually short sessions. At a contamination parameter of 0.02, Isolation Forest achieved a recall of 0.89 and precision of 0.76 across the three fault types without any labelled training data. Comparison with one-class SVM showed comparable recall but substantially lower training time. The paper discusses feature sensitivity and the effect of operator experience level on the false-positive rate.

title: Temporal Drift in User Interaction Patterns: A Longitudinal Clustering Study Over 24 Months
abstract: User behaviour in software applications changes as users gain experience or as the software is updated. This paper tracks cluster membership of 210 longitudinal users across a 24-month event-log dataset from a desktop geographic information tool. Each month's data was independently clustered with HDBSCAN, and cluster alignment across months was achieved using the Hungarian algorithm on a Jaccard-similarity matrix of cluster memberships. Three trajectory types were identified: stable users who remained in the same cluster for at least 20 of 24 months (38% of users), gradual shifters who moved monotonically across adjacent clusters (29%), and oscillators whose cluster membership showed no persistent trend (33%). Update events in the software correlated with a sharp increase in oscillator proportion during the two months following release. These findings suggest that static one-shot clustering is insufficient for longitudinal interaction log analysis.

title: Grid-Based Spatial Aggregation of Cursor Dwell Events for Low-Resource Clustering Pipelines
abstract: Processing high-frequency cursor-position logs at scale is computationally demanding. This paper proposes a grid-based aggregation step that maps raw cursor coordinates onto configurable rectangular cells before clustering, drastically reducing data volume while retaining spatial structure. The method is evaluated on four publicly documented interaction datasets totalling 2.3 million cursor-dwell events. Grid resolutions of 20×15, 40×30, and 80×60 cells were tested in combination with k-means, DBSCAN, and agglomerative clustering. At 40×30 resolution, cluster structure recovery (measured by normalised mutual information against full-resolution clustering output) exceeded 0.91 for all three algorithms, while processing time dropped by factors of 18 to 34. Memory usage fell below 200 MB for all configurations, making the pipeline suitable for deployment on modest server hardware. An open-source Python implementation is released alongside the paper.

title: Evaluating Cluster Validity Indices for Interaction-Log Data: An Empirical Comparison on Seven Datasets
abstract: Choosing the number of clusters in unsupervised interaction-log analysis typically relies on internal validity indices, but little systematic evidence exists on which indices perform best for this data type. This study gathers seven interaction-log datasets ranging from 4,000 to 130,000 sessions, constructs labelled ground truth through expert annotation of randomly sampled subsets, and evaluates eleven internal indices — including silhouette, Calinski–Harabasz, Davies–Bouldin, CDbw, and S_Dbw — against the ground truth using rank-order correlation and top-k accuracy. Experiments are run with k-means (k from 2 to 15) and HDBSCAN. The Calinski–Harabasz index most reliably identified the annotator-preferred partition for k-means across datasets, while S_Dbw performed best for HDBSCAN. No single index dominated across both algorithms. The paper provides a decision table and a reproducible benchmark pipeline intended to assist practitioners selecting indices for specific log-analysis contexts.

title: Subspace Clustering of Multi-Application Interaction Logs for Cross-Tool User Profiling
abstract: Users who work with several software tools in the same organisation leave interaction traces across multiple applications, but logs are typically analysed per-application. This preprint proposes a subspace clustering framework that jointly analyses per-application session feature vectors and recovers user profiles that are coherent across tools. Projected-clustering is applied to a synthetic-but-realistic dataset generated from a validated log simulator calibrated on 18 months of real enterprise logs (anonymised and aggregated before release). The simulator produces data for 500 virtual users across four tools. Subspace clusters of dimension 4–7 (out of 40 total features) were more stable under bootstrap resampling than full-space clusters, with an average Jaccard stability of 0.79 versus 0.61. Three cross-tool profiles were consistently recovered and matched qualitatively with role descriptions provided by domain experts. A validation study on a second simulated cohort is in preparation.

title: Feature selection stability under bootstrap resampling for small clinical datasets with high feature-to-sample ratios
abstract: Many clinical laboratory studies involve datasets in which the number of measured analytes or derived features approaches or exceeds the number of patient records. In such settings, feature selection outcomes vary substantially across bootstrap samples of the training data, threatening reproducibility. We examined selection stability for five filter and three wrapper methods applied to six datasets with 80 to 340 samples and 30 to 210 features, all drawn from clinical biochemistry and immunology laboratory records. Stability was quantified with the Nogueira–Brown stability index. Mutual information filtering showed the highest stability index across five of six datasets. Wrapper methods based on recursive feature elimination with support vector machines showed strong predictive performance but low stability indices, with mean index values below 0.45. A two-stage procedure—filter pre-selection followed by wrapper refinement—improved both stability and cross-validated AUC in four datasets. Practical guidelines are provided for laboratories operating under sample-size constraints.

title: Formal Verification Methods for Concurrent Software: An Introductory Perspective
abstract: This book chapter surveys model checking, deductive verification, and type-based approaches to concurrent software correctness, aimed at graduate students and practitioners unfamiliar with formal methods. The chapter covers the theoretical foundations of Kripke structures, LTL and CTL semantics, and Büchi automata, then walks through worked examples in SPIN and NuSMV with annotated Promela and SMV code fragments. A section on scalability discusses the state-space explosion problem and mitigation strategies: symmetry reduction, abstraction, and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR). The chapter closes with a structured comparison of tool capabilities and a guide to selecting an approach based on system size, property type, and available expertise. The text draws on material developed for a master's-level course at the University of Novi Sad over three academic years and has been classroom-tested with approximately 90 students.

title: Signature Kernels for Detecting Structural Change in Non-Stationary Multivariate Time Series
abstract: Detecting change points in non-stationary multivariate time series is complicated when the change manifests in higher-order cross-channel dependencies rather than in marginal distributions. We explore the use of the signature kernel — a positive-definite kernel on path space derived from the inner product of truncated signatures — as the basis for a kernel change-point detection procedure applied to sliding windows. The method is tested on three settings: simulated regime-switching vector autoregressive processes, daily river flow measurements from five gauging stations in the Danube basin spanning 1990–2020, and a collection of 38 annotated accelerometer recordings from a wearable device capturing transitions between physical activities. On the simulated data, the signature kernel detector achieves an F1 score of 0.87 for identifying change points, versus 0.79 for an energy-distance baseline. On the river flow data it recovers 11 of 14 labelled hydrological regime transitions. We discuss computational cost and provide an approximation strategy based on random Fourier features for the signature kernel that reduces wall-clock time by a factor of roughly 3 on the longest series.
