title: Germination inhibition of Sinapis arvensis and Chenopodium album by aqueous leaf extracts of Ambrosia artemisiifolia at graduated concentrations
abstract: Aqueous extracts prepared from freshly collected Ambrosia artemisiifolia leaves at five concentrations (0, 10, 25, 50, and 100 g dry weight per litre) were applied to filter-paper bioassays with seeds of Sinapis arvensis and Chenopodium album. Germination percentage, radicle length, and hypocotyl length were recorded after seven days at 22 °C in the dark. At 50 g/L, germination of S. arvensis was reduced by 61% and radicle elongation by 74% relative to the water control; C. album showed lower sensitivity, with a 38% germination reduction at the same concentration. Dose-response curves were fitted with a four-parameter log-logistic model; ED50 values were 31.4 g/L for S. arvensis and 58.7 g/L for C. album. Total phenolic content of extracts, determined by the Folin-Ciocalteu method, correlated positively with phytotoxic intensity (r = 0.91). Results suggest that phenolic acids are important contributors to allelopathic activity, though the identity of individual compounds requires further chromatographic investigation.

title: HPLC-DAD profiling of phenolic acids in root exudates of Ambrosia artemisiifolia collected from three habitat types in Vojvodina
abstract: Root exudate samples were collected by hydroponic trap method from A. artemisiifolia plants grown from seeds originating in ruderal, field-margin, and soybean-field populations in Vojvodina province (n = 15 per habitat type). Extracts were analysed by HPLC-DAD at 280 and 320 nm. Twelve phenolic acids were tentatively identified and six quantified against external standards: chlorogenic, caffeic, ferulic, p-coumaric, vanillic, and syringic acids. Ferulic acid was consistently the most abundant, ranging from 18.4 to 34.2 µg g⁻¹ root dry weight depending on habitat origin. Field-margin plants produced significantly higher total phenolic acid content (mean 89.1 µg g⁻¹) than ruderal plants (mean 56.3 µg g⁻¹; p < 0.05, one-way ANOVA). Caffeic acid showed the widest variation among individuals within each group. Habitat-associated differences in metabolite composition suggest that soil nutrient status and interspecific competition pressure influence constitutive secondary metabolism in this invasive species.

title: Sesquiterpene lactone content of Ambrosia artemisiifolia across phenological stages and its relation to phytotoxic activity on Lactuca sativa root growth
abstract: Leaf samples of A. artemisiifolia were harvested at vegetative (V4), early flowering (R1), and seed-set (R3) stages from a single field population near Temerin, Serbia, over two consecutive growing seasons (2015–2016). Sesquiterpene lactones were extracted with ethyl acetate and quantified by GC-MS using parthenin and coronopilin as reference standards. Total sesquiterpene lactone content peaked at R1 (3.8 ± 0.4 mg g⁻¹ dry weight) and declined at R3 (2.1 ± 0.3 mg g⁻¹). Phytotoxic potency was assessed against Lactuca sativa radicle elongation using a 96-well plate bioassay; extracts corresponding to R1 showed the greatest inhibition (IC50 = 0.18 mg/mL). There was a strong linear relationship between sesquiterpene lactone concentration and inhibition magnitude (R² = 0.88). Season-to-season differences in absolute concentrations were modest (< 12%) but statistically significant for parthenin. These findings indicate that the allelopathic potential of ragweed shoot material is greatest during flowering, which has practical implications for timing of mowing-based management interventions.

title: Differential sensitivity of common arable species to ferulic and caffeic acids: a comparative dose-response study
abstract: Pure ferulic acid and caffeic acid solutions were prepared at six concentrations (0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mM) and applied in Petri-dish bioassays to seeds of eight arable species: Galium aparine, Veronica persica, Polygonum aviculare, Setaria viridis, Echinochloa crus-galli, Amaranthus retroflexus, Matricaria chamomilla, and Vicia villosa. Endpoints were final germination percentage and radicle dry weight after ten days. A three-parameter Weibull model provided best fit for most species-compound combinations. Ferulic acid was consistently more inhibitory than caffeic acid at equivalent molar concentrations; ED50 values for ferulic acid ranged from 0.19 mM (G. aparine) to 1.43 mM (E. crus-galli). Monocot species tended to be less sensitive than dicots. Vicia villosa was the least sensitive species overall, showing less than 20% radicle weight reduction at 2.0 mM ferulic acid. Interaction experiments with binary mixtures indicated additive effects rather than synergy between the two acids at equimolar concentrations. Results provide a ranked sensitivity table useful for predicting community-level allelopathic impacts in mixed arable stands.

title: Influence of Ambrosia artemisiifolia litter decomposition on soil phenolic acid dynamics and subsequent emergence of sunflower seedlings
abstract: A mesocosm experiment was established in which dried and milled A. artemisiifolia shoot litter was incorporated into loamy agricultural soil at rates of 0, 2, 5, and 10 t/ha (dry weight equivalent). Soils were incubated at field capacity and 20 °C for 0, 14, 28, and 56 days before phenolic acid extraction with 0.1 M NaOH and HPLC quantification. Sunflower (Helianthus annuus cv. Bačvanin) was sown at each time point and seedling emergence and early biomass measured at 14 days after sowing. Soil ferulic and p-coumaric acid concentrations peaked at 14 days post-incorporation (up to 4.2 and 2.9 µg g⁻¹ dry soil, respectively, at 10 t/ha), then declined to background levels by day 56. Sunflower emergence was reduced by 22% at the highest litter rate when sowing occurred at the 14-day peak but was unaffected when sowing was delayed to day 56. Soil pH and microbial biomass carbon were also monitored; rapid microbial degradation of phenolic acids accounted for the temporal decline. The results suggest that timing of crop establishment relative to ragweed residue incorporation affects allelopathic risk.

title: Volatile terpene emissions from Ambrosia artemisiifolia and their inhibitory effect on seed germination in a selection of native grassland forbs
abstract: Dynamic headspace sampling over intact rosette-stage A. artemisiifolia plants was used to collect volatile organic compounds, which were identified by GC-MS. Fourteen terpenes were detected, with α-pinene, β-caryophyllene, and germacrene D accounting for 68% of total emission. A sealed-chamber bioassay was designed to expose seeds of Plantago lanceolata, Leucanthemum vulgare, and Achillea millefolium to standardised concentrations of synthetic α-pinene and β-caryophyllene vapour (0.05, 0.1, and 0.2 µL/L air) for 72 hours before transfer to germination conditions. α-Pinene at 0.2 µL/L reduced germination of P. lanceolata by 44% and radicle length by 31%; L. vulgare was less affected (18% and 21%, respectively). β-Caryophyllene showed weak inhibitory effects at all concentrations tested. A. millefolium was largely insensitive to both compounds. The study demonstrates that airborne terpene exposure can contribute to allelopathic effects on neighbouring grassland species, though field-relevant concentrations require further determination through open-air emission modelling.

title: Population-level variation in sesquiterpene lactone profiles of Ambrosia artemisiifolia along an agricultural intensification gradient in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Leaf material from twelve A. artemisiifolia populations was collected from sites representing a gradient of agricultural intensity: extensively managed meadow margins, field edges of cereal fields, and intensively cultivated maize fields, spanning parts of Vojvodina (Serbia), Baranya (Hungary), and Timiș county (Romania). Sesquiterpene lactones were extracted and quantified by GC-MS. Parthenin concentration ranged from 1.2 mg g⁻¹ to 5.1 mg g⁻¹ dry weight across populations; coronopilin showed a narrower range (0.8–2.3 mg g⁻¹). Populations from intensively cultivated sites had statistically higher parthenin content than meadow-margin populations (p = 0.009, Kruskal-Wallis with post-hoc Dunn test). Genetic differentiation between populations was assessed using six microsatellite markers; FST values were low (mean 0.04), suggesting gene flow does not explain metabolic differences. Canonical correspondence analysis showed that soil nitrogen availability was the strongest environmental predictor of parthenin content (eigenvalue 0.41). Results support the hypothesis that nitrogen-rich agricultural soils enhance constitutive sesquiterpene lactone biosynthesis in ragweed.

title: Phytotoxic fractions of Ambrosia artemisiifolia leaf extract: bioassay-guided fractionation and identification of active components
abstract: Crude ethyl acetate extract of A. artemisiifolia leaves was fractionated by sequential liquid-liquid partitioning and preparative reversed-phase HPLC into eight fractions, each tested against L. sativa radicle elongation at a standardised dry-weight concentration of 0.5 mg/mL. Two fractions, designated F4 and F6, accounted for 83% of the total inhibitory activity. LC-MS/MS analysis of F4 identified parthenin as the dominant compound (purity > 90% by peak area), while F6 contained predominantly chlorogenic acid and a tentatively assigned dihydroxycinnamic acid derivative. Pure parthenin inhibited radicle elongation with an IC50 of 0.09 mg/mL; pure chlorogenic acid required 0.62 mg/mL for equivalent effect. Re-combination experiments showed that mixing F4 and F6 at their natural ratio produced inhibition statistically equivalent to the unfractionated extract, indicating these two fractions capture the majority of phytotoxic activity. Minor fractions showed no significant effect individually. This work establishes parthenin and chlorogenic acid as the primary allelopathic agents in leaf tissue of Vojvodinian ragweed populations.

title: Mapping the temporal dynamics of Ambrosia artemisiifolia allelopathic pressure in no-till soybean fields using soil bioassay monitoring
abstract: A field monitoring programme was established on four no-till soybean plots in Vojvodina where A. artemisiifolia was the dominant volunteer weed. Soil samples (0–10 cm) were taken biweekly from weed-infested and manually weeded control strips from sowing to harvest over the 2024 season. Phytotoxic activity was quantified with a standardised L. sativa root elongation bioassay using aqueous soil extracts. Parallel HPLC analysis tracked ferulic acid and parthenin concentrations. Peak bioassay inhibition (mean 54% root reduction relative to control soil) occurred at ragweed early flowering (calendar weeks 29–31). Parthenin was detected at quantifiable levels only in plots with densities above 8 plants m⁻². Ferulic acid was detectable throughout the season at all densities (range 0.3–3.1 µg g⁻¹ dry soil). Weed density at V4 ragweed stage was the strongest predictor of cumulative phytotoxic index (R² = 0.79). The data suggest a threshold-like relationship between ragweed density and meaningful soil allelopathic activity, with practical implications for economic threshold calculations.

title: In-situ exposure of Gammarus roeselii in drainage ditches adjacent to maize fields during the spring sowing period
abstract: Transplanted in-situ bioassays using caged Gammarus roeselii were deployed at eight drainage ditch sites adjacent to seed-treated maize fields and four reference sites during spring 2023 in the Srem district. Cages containing 20 individuals each were exposed for seven days, coinciding with post-emergence rainfall events. Survival, feeding rate (pre-conditioned alder leaf discs), and acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity were measured at cage retrieval. Mean survival at treatment sites was 71% compared to 96% at reference sites (Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.008). Feeding rate was reduced by 39% at treatment sites. AChE activity was inhibited by 28–45% at six of eight treatment sites. Concurrent water sampling confirmed imidacloprid concentrations of 0.11–0.44 µg/L at treatment sites during exposure. Regression analysis showed that AChE inhibition was significantly predicted by time-weighted average imidacloprid concentration (r² = 0.68). The in-situ approach confirmed laboratory-derived effect thresholds under realistic hydrological variability conditions.

title: AMPA accumulation in long-term glyphosate-treated maize soils: concentrations, depth distribution, and association with microbial functional diversity
abstract: Aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA), the primary glyphosate metabolite, is more persistent than the parent compound yet receives less regulatory attention. Soil profiles (0–10, 10–30, 30–60 cm) from twelve commercial maize fields with at least eight years of annual glyphosate application (0.9–1.8 kg a.i. ha⁻¹) in Vojvodina were sampled in autumn 2014 and analysed for AMPA and glyphosate by LC-MS/MS. AMPA was detected in all surface samples (mean 0.31 mg kg⁻¹, range 0.07–0.89 mg kg⁻¹) and in 8 of 12 fields at 10–30 cm depth. PLFA profiling of surface samples from all 12 fields was correlated with AMPA concentration by partial least squares regression (PLS-R), with AMPA explaining 29% of total community variation after partialling out soil texture and pH. Fungal indicators were consistently negatively associated with AMPA in the PLS-R loadings. The results suggest that AMPA accumulation may contribute independently to the observed microbial community shifts in repeatedly treated soils, distinct from any transient glyphosate effect.

title: Gradient-based illumination normalisation for indoor human body keypoint detection
abstract: We investigate the effect of structured illumination variation on 2D skeletal keypoint detectors trained on balanced studio datasets and tested in office and warehouse environments with fluorescent, mixed, and low-level lighting. Twelve video sequences totalling 4,800 frames were recorded with a single consumer-grade RGB camera. A gradient-based pre-processing stage that estimates and partially inverts illumination gradients across limb regions was incorporated ahead of a standard stacked-hourglass detector. On the internal test split the approach reduced mean per-joint position error from 18.4 px to 14.1 px without retraining the backbone. Experiments on a separate publicly available benchmark showed a consistent reduction of roughly 12% in PCK at threshold 0.2. The method adds negligible latency and requires no ground-truth illumination data. Failure cases concentrated on hand and foot keypoints occluded by cast shadows remain an open problem.

title: Comparing heat-map regression architectures for single-image human pose estimation on low-resolution inputs
abstract: Pose estimation from images with spatial resolution below 128×128 pixels is practically relevant for surveillance and embedded platforms but underexplored. This paper benchmarks five convolutional heat-map regression architectures, including variants of stacked hourglass and feature pyramid designs, on a dataset of 9,200 downsampled frames derived from a motion-capture studio dataset. We deliberately down-scaled images using bicubic interpolation to simulate constrained sensor conditions and measured PCK and OKS at several thresholds. A two-stage approach combining super-resolution pre-processing with a lightweight hourglass backbone achieved the best OKS of 0.61, compared with 0.54 for the strongest single-stage baseline. Training time and parameter counts are reported for each architecture. The study provides a structured comparison that informs architecture selection for embedded deployment, avoiding claims about any single method's overall superiority.

title: Anatomical constraint regularisation for 3D joint angle estimation from a single RGB image
abstract: We formulate joint angle estimation as a constrained optimisation problem where a learned kinematic model provides soft anatomical bounds on each degree of freedom. A small feed-forward network predicts unconstrained angle vectors, which are projected onto a feasibility manifold defined by bone-length ratios and per-joint range-of-motion limits derived from biomechanical literature covering 24 joint types. The projection is differentiable and integrated into end-to-end training. Evaluated on an in-lab dataset of 40 participants performing six activities, the constrained model reduced the rate of anatomically implausible configurations from 11.3% to 2.1% compared with an unconstrained baseline. Mean angle error across all joints decreased from 8.7° to 7.2°. The method is sensitive to bone-length initialisation errors when subjects deviate substantially from the average skeleton and requires per-subject calibration in precision applications.

title: Domain shift in human pose estimation: a taxonomy and empirical study across four environment types
abstract: This paper provides a structured taxonomy of domain-shift sources relevant to monocular pose estimation and conducts controlled experiments across four distinct deployment environments: a laboratory studio, an outdoor sports field, a factory floor, and a hospital corridor. A single model trained on studio data is evaluated without adaptation, with feature-level adversarial alignment, and with pseudo-label self-training. Across 28 test conditions, adversarial alignment improved average PCK by 5.1 percentage points over no adaptation, while self-training yielded 7.4 points improvement when pseudo-label confidence thresholds were tuned per environment. The paper documents failure modes specific to each environment type and quantifies the contribution of background clutter, occlusion, and lighting variation separately using ablation experiments on artificially generated image composites. The code and all collected annotations are released publicly.

title: Temporal smoothing of monocular 3D pose sequences using learned motion priors
abstract: Single-frame monocular 3D pose estimators produce temporally inconsistent joint trajectories when applied to video, because no inter-frame information is used during inference. We train a recurrent motion prior on a large corpus of motion-capture sequences covering locomotion, reaching, and manipulation tasks and use it as a post-processing filter that penalises physically implausible accelerations. The prior is parameterised as a variational recurrent model and is applied at test time without fine-tuning on target sequences. On three video sequences recorded in an uncontrolled factory setting with 30 fps cameras, median jitter (defined as mean absolute second difference of joint positions) decreased by 38% relative to a Savitzky–Golay baseline with matched window length. Joint position accuracy simultaneously improved by 4 mm in mean per-joint position error, suggesting that temporal coherence and spatial accuracy are not in conflict for the tested sequences. Limitations include higher error on fast ballistic movements.

title: Ergonomic risk assessment from monocular video in assembly workplaces: a pilot study
abstract: RULA-based ergonomic risk scoring typically requires wearable sensors or multi-camera setups that are impractical in production environments. This pilot study tests whether a monocular pose estimator, combined with the kinematic constraint model from our earlier work, can produce RULA scores sufficiently accurate for screening purposes. Ten participants performed 12 assembly tasks representative of automotive sub-assembly lines. Pose was estimated from a single ceiling-mounted camera at 1280×720 px. Estimated RULA scores were compared with scores from a concurrent optical motion-capture reference system. Weighted kappa between estimated and reference RULA categories was 0.61, interpreted as substantial agreement. Shoulder and neck joint angles showed the highest discrepancy, primarily due to self-occlusion. The study is explicitly framed as a feasibility assessment; the approach is not proposed as a replacement for clinical ergonomic evaluation.

title: Bone-length consistency loss for multi-person 3D pose estimation from a single camera
abstract: In multi-person scenes, per-person pose estimators are applied independently, producing skeletons whose inferred bone lengths vary across frames and individuals in physically implausible ways. We introduce a bone-length consistency loss that penalises per-sequence variance in estimated bone lengths during training and can optionally be applied as a differentiable post-processing step at inference time. The loss is parameter-free aside from a single weighting scalar. Evaluated on a purpose-collected dataset of 18 two-person interaction sequences and on a public benchmark of crowd scenes, the loss reduced mean bone-length variance by 44% without statistically significant degradation in MPJPE. Interactions involving close physical proximity showed smaller improvement due to depth ambiguity. The dataset and annotations are made available for research use.

title: Pose estimation under partial occlusion in warehouse environments: a dataset and benchmark
abstract: Partial occlusion caused by shelving units, pallets, and forklift equipment is a frequent failure mode for monocular pose estimators deployed in logistics warehouses, yet no benchmark specifically addresses this scenario. We present WarePose, a dataset of 14,600 annotated frames collected at two warehouse facilities in Vojvodina, Serbia, covering 22 workers performing eight task categories. Annotation was performed by projecting concurrent measurements from a body-worn inertial sensor suit onto the monocular frames and correcting outliers manually. Five representative pose estimators are benchmarked, with PCK@0.2 scores ranging from 0.55 to 0.71 under moderate occlusion and from 0.38 to 0.52 under severe occlusion. The benchmark reveals that limb keypoints on the occluded side are consistently underperforming regardless of architecture, and that heat-map confidence scores are poorly calibrated under occlusion. The dataset is released under a research licence.

title: Calibration-free depth estimation for 2D-to-3D pose lifting using scene context cues
abstract: Most 2D-to-3D pose lifting methods assume a known or estimated camera intrinsic matrix, which is unavailable in many deployed systems. We investigate whether scene context cues — specifically, floor plane detection and object size priors derived from semantic segmentation — can provide a sufficient depth reference to enable metric-scale 3D pose estimation without explicit calibration. A two-branch architecture first segments the scene to identify floor regions and objects of known approximate size, then uses estimated distance ratios as weak supervision for the lifting network. On 11 video sequences recorded with four different uncalibrated consumer cameras, mean per-joint position error in metric scale was 78 mm, compared with 61 mm for a calibrated baseline. Error increased most sharply when the floor was occluded or when the subject moved to the image periphery.

title: Survival Analysis Methods for Predicting Long-Term Employee Retention: A Comparative Study
abstract: Employee voluntary turnover is modelled as a time-to-event outcome using a cohort of 3,200 employees tracked over 8 years at a Central European financial services group. Four survival methods are compared: the Cox proportional hazards model, random survival forests, a DeepSurv neural network, and a competing-risks Fine–Gray model that treats involuntary separation as a competing event. Discrimination is measured by the time-dependent AUC at 12, 24, and 36 months. Random survival forests achieve the highest 24-month AUC of 0.76, compared with 0.72 for Cox and 0.74 for DeepSurv, but require more careful hyperparameter tuning in small organisational subgroups. The proportional hazards assumption is tested for the Cox model using Schoenfeld residuals and found to be violated for two of nine covariates, motivating time-varying coefficient extensions. Results suggest that the accuracy advantage of more complex methods diminishes when training data fall below approximately 500 observed events.

title: Measuring Annotator Cognitive Load During Active Learning Sessions: A Physiological Study
abstract: Annotation quality in active learning is assumed to degrade with annotator fatigue, but direct physiological measurements are rarely collected. We recruited 18 participants with domain knowledge in environmental science to annotate satellite image patches (binary land-use label) over 90-minute sessions while wearing a wrist-worn galvanic skin response sensor and an eye-tracking headset. Active learning selected batches of 20 images every five minutes using entropy sampling from a ResNet-50 model. GSR amplitude and pupil dilation both increased significantly after minute 50 (paired t-test, p < 0.01), coinciding with a measurable drop in inter-annotator agreement from κ = 0.83 to κ = 0.71 in the final 30 minutes. Label quality partially recovers after a five-minute break. We propose a fatigue index derived from GSR slope and show it predicts agreement drop with AUC 0.74. These findings support the inclusion of mandatory break triggers in annotation platform design.
venue: ACM Workshop on Human Factors in Machine Learning Systems

title: Dynamic modelling of a small-scale ORC system using a scroll expander driven by low-temperature flue gas
abstract: A dynamic model of a 5 kWe organic Rankine cycle unit equipped with a scroll expander was developed in Modelica and validated against experimental data collected from a laboratory test rig operating with R245fa as the working fluid. The heat source was a synthetic flue-gas flow at 130–160 °C, representative of light manufacturing exhaust. The model comprises component-level sub-models for the evaporator, condenser, scroll expander, and pump, with thermal capacitance terms retained to capture transient behaviour during heat-source fluctuations. Validation was performed over twelve steady-state operating points and four step-change experiments. Predicted expander outlet temperature matched measurements within ±3.2 °C and predicted electrical power output within ±4.5%. The model was subsequently used to analyse the system response to ±20% ramp changes in heat-source mass flow rate, revealing that the evaporating pressure stabilises within approximately 90 seconds under proportional–integral pump-speed control. The work provides a calibrated simulation platform for further control strategy studies.

title: Comparative steady-state performance of five low-GWP working fluids in an ORC designed for 120 °C industrial waste water
abstract: Five low-GWP organic fluids — R1234ze(E), R1233zd(E), butane, isobutane, and cyclopentane — were evaluated as replacements for R245fa in an ORC unit recovering heat from 120 °C industrial process water at a nominal flow of 8 kg/s. A thermodynamic optimisation was performed for each fluid using a simulated-annealing algorithm, with net power output as the objective function under fixed heat exchanger area constraints derived from an existing installation. Results show that R1233zd(E) achieves the highest net power at 6.3 kWe, approximately 8% above R245fa under the same boundary conditions, owing to a more favourable saturation curve and lower pump work. Cyclopentane yields the highest thermal efficiency (9.1%) but requires a higher expander inlet temperature that approaches the heat-source limit. Fluid flammability and compatibility with elastomer seals used in the test rig were also tabulated. The study provides a basis for a planned retrofit of the laboratory unit.

title: Off-design characterisation of a radial turbine expander for ORC applications using reduced-order maps
abstract: Off-design performance of a 10 kWe-class radial inflow turbine intended for ORC service was characterised using a combination of 1-D meanline calculation and a limited set of experimental measurements at four rotational speeds (1800, 2400, 3000, and 3600 rpm) and three pressure-ratio levels. A reduced-order performance map was derived by fitting the meanline predictions to the measured shaft power and isentropic efficiency data, which covered efficiencies from 0.61 at the lowest pressure ratio and speed to 0.78 near the design point. The map was implemented as a look-up table within a Modelica ORC system model, replacing the fixed isentropic efficiency assumption used in earlier work. Simulations with the map showed that off-design operation at 60% of rated heat input reduces cycle efficiency by 2.8 percentage points compared to the fixed-efficiency assumption, a difference with practical significance for control strategy design. The characterisation methodology is general and applicable to other turboexpander types.

title: Proportional–integral versus model predictive control for superheat regulation in a waste-heat ORC: a simulation and experimental comparison
abstract: Superheat regulation at the scroll expander inlet is critical for safe ORC operation; excessive superheat wastes available enthalpy while insufficient superheat risks liquid ingestion. This paper compares a tuned PI controller and a linear model predictive controller (MPC) designed from a step-response identified model of the laboratory ORC rig, operated with R245fa and a 140 °C hot-oil heat source. The MPC prediction horizon was set to 15 sample intervals of 2 seconds each, with superheat bounds enforced as hard constraints. In step-change experiments of ±15 °C in heat-source temperature, MPC reduced the peak superheat deviation by 38% and settling time by 22% compared to the PI benchmark, at the cost of a more complex implementation. Both controllers were tested over a 4-hour continuous run with a recorded real industrial load profile reproduced on the heat-source circuit. MPC maintained superheat within the ±3 °C target band 91% of the time versus 74% for PI. The hardware platform and identified model are described in sufficient detail for reproduction.

title: Screening of siloxane working fluids for high-temperature ORC units recovering heat above 200 °C
abstract: Siloxane compounds (MM, MDM, D4, and D5) were screened for suitability in an ORC unit designed to recover heat from a 220 °C ceramic-kiln exhaust stream at a Serbian brick manufacturer. Fluid stability, saturation-curve shape, and cycle performance were assessed at turbine inlet conditions from 180 to 210 °C. Thermodynamic cycle calculations using REFPROP-based fluid properties were combined with turbine sizing constraints limiting tip-speed Mach number to below 0.85. MDM emerged as the preferred fluid, achieving a net cycle efficiency of 14.2% at the design point with an estimated turbine size factor within common manufacturing limits. A preliminary techno-economic estimate suggests a payback period of 7–9 years at Serbian industrial electricity prices as of the analysis year. Fluid thermal decomposition at 210 °C was evaluated against published stability data, with MDM showing no reported decomposition products below 260 °C according to available literature. The analysis is intended to support a feasibility study for an industrial installation.

title: Start-up trajectory optimisation for an ORC unit subject to limited thermal mass in the evaporator
abstract: Rapid start-up of ORC units after cold shut-down can cause evaporator thermal stress and two-phase expander ingestion if the heat-up trajectory is not managed. This paper formulates start-up as a finite-horizon optimal control problem, minimising the time to reach rated superheat while keeping tube-wall temperature gradients below a 3 °C/min metallurgical limit. The dynamic ORC model (validated in earlier work) was linearised around three operating points to form a switched linear system. Open-loop optimal pump-speed and bypass-valve trajectories were computed using a sequential quadratic programming solver. Experiments on the 5 kWe laboratory rig confirmed that the optimised trajectory reduces start-up time from 18.4 minutes (operator-guided ramp) to 11.7 minutes while keeping measured wall gradients below the limit in all trials. A simplified version of the trajectory, parameterised by two scalars, was also tested and achieved a start-up time of 13.1 minutes, offering a practical compromise for field implementation without on-line optimisation capability.

title: Dynamic simulation of a cascade ORC–heat pump system for simultaneous power generation and process heating from a single waste heat source
abstract: A cascade system combining a top ORC cycle (working fluid: cyclopentane, heat source: 210 °C) and a bottom heat pump cycle (working fluid: R134a) was modelled in Modelica to evaluate simultaneous electricity generation and 60 °C hot-water delivery for a food-drying application. The condenser of the ORC serves as the evaporator of the heat pump. Dynamic behaviour was studied for step changes in the drying-process heat demand (±30 kW) and heat-source flow rate (±15%). Interaction between the two subsystems was characterised by a 2×2 relative-gain array analysis of the coupled system, revealing strong interaction between ORC pump speed and heat-pump compressor speed. A decentralised PI control structure with a steady-state decoupler was designed and tested in simulation: it reduced interaction-induced power oscillations by 61% compared to independent single-loop control. Peak ORC net power in the coupled configuration was 22.4 kWe and average heat-pump COP over a simulated 24-hour production cycle was 3.7.

title: Organic Rankine cycles for industrial waste heat recovery: system design and operational aspects
abstract: This book chapter provides a technically detailed treatment of ORC system design for practitioners working in industrial energy efficiency. Topics covered include thermodynamic cycle configurations (basic, regenerative, cascade), working-fluid selection criteria for source temperatures from 80 to 300 °C, expander types and their part-load characteristics, heat exchanger sizing under fouling allowances, and control strategies appropriate for intermittent or variable industrial heat sources. A design procedure is presented as a series of numbered steps, from initial heat-source characterisation through component sizing to controller specification, illustrated with two worked examples: a 90 °C geothermal brine source and a 190 °C metal-casting furnace exhaust. The chapter also discusses operational aspects including start-up sequencing, fluid maintenance, and integration with existing plant energy management systems. It is aimed at mechanical and process engineers involved in industrial energy audits and retrofit projects rather than at readers primarily interested in theoretical cycle analysis.

title: Fault detection for ORC units using a moving-horizon estimator applied to measured process data from a ceramics plant
abstract: Early fault detection in ORC units operating in unattended industrial settings can prevent damage and unplanned downtime. A moving-horizon state and parameter estimator was formulated using the validated dynamic ORC model, with working-fluid charge level, overall evaporator heat transfer coefficient, and expander isentropic efficiency treated as slowly varying parameters. The estimator was applied to 11 months of process data logged at 30-second intervals from a 35 kWe ORC unit installed at a ceramics plant in southern Serbia. Five fault events recorded in the plant maintenance log (two partial refrigerant leaks, two pump bearing degradations, and one condenser blockage) were used to assess detection capability. The estimator flagged all five events before visible performance degradation occurred in net-power trends, with lead times ranging from 3 to 19 days. One false positive was recorded during a planned heat-source shutdown misread as a charge fault. The approach requires no additional instrumentation beyond the standard ORC sensor set.

title: Comparative assessment of zeotropic mixtures as ORC working fluids for a steel mill recuperator heat source
abstract: Zeotropic working-fluid mixtures exploit the temperature glide during phase change to improve thermal match with non-isothermal heat sources and sinks, potentially reducing irreversibility in heat exchangers. This study evaluates six binary mixtures — R1234ze(E)/R245fa at three compositions, pentane/isopentane at two compositions, and R1233zd(E)/cyclopentane — against their pure-component counterparts for an ORC recovering heat from a steel-mill recuperator exhaust at 185 °C, 4.2 kg/s. Temperature glide in the condenser was constrained to match a cooling tower water flow available at 25 °C. Pinch-point analysis in Modelica was used to size heat exchangers for each mixture. The R1233zd(E)/cyclopentane mixture at a 0.6/0.4 molar ratio achieved the best net efficiency (13.6%) compared to 12.1% for pure R1233zd(E) and 11.8% for pure cyclopentane, at the cost of a 14% larger heat exchanger area. Dynamic simulations of the preferred mixture showed that composition shift due to differential leakage at a rate of 0.2% per month would reduce efficiency by 0.4 percentage points per year, a manageable degradation.

title: Characterisation of global horizontal irradiance variability at a lowland mid-latitude site using hourly ground measurements
abstract: This study analyses ten years (2000–2009) of hourly global horizontal irradiance (GHI) measurements collected at a meteorological station near Novi Sad to characterise intra-annual and inter-annual variability relevant to PV system design. Clearness index distributions were computed on monthly and seasonal bases, and fitted to beta probability distributions. The study finds that the coefficient of variation of daily GHI ranges from 18% in July to 47% in December, with a mean annual GHI of 1 382 kWh/m². Persistence of low-irradiance sequences exceeding five consecutive days was identified as the primary driver of storage requirements for stand-alone systems in the region. Autocorrelation structure of daily clearness index sequences was also quantified. Results are compared against two satellite-derived irradiance databases; systematic biases of 3–7% were found during winter months. The dataset and fitted distribution parameters are made available as supplementary material for use in system sizing studies.

title: Capacity sizing of a PV–battery system for a remote water quality monitoring station: methodology and case study on the Danube
abstract: Remote environmental monitoring stations must maintain continuous operation with minimal maintenance access, making reliable power supply critical. This paper documents the full sizing workflow applied to a water quality monitoring station installed on a Danube riverbank approximately 40 km downstream of Novi Sad, powered entirely by a PV–battery system. Load characterisation yielded an average daily demand of 18.6 Wh with a peak draw of 4.2 W from sensors, data logger, and cellular modem. The PV array and LFP battery bank were sized using a monthly simulation approach with LOLP ≤ 0.005 as constraint, resulting in a 60 Wp panel at 40° tilt and a 120 Wh usable battery capacity. Twelve months of post-installation monitoring confirmed zero loss-of-load events and a measured annual energy surplus of 34%, suggesting moderate conservatism in the applied safety factors. Lessons learned regarding connector corrosion, bird-related soiling, and seasonal load variation are discussed for designers of similar installations.

title: A zone-based model for fuel-NOx formation in small pellet burners: derivation and validation against experimental data
abstract: This paper presents a zone-based semi-empirical model for predicting fuel-NOx formation in small pellet burners operating between 30 % and 100 % rated load. The combustion chamber was divided into four zones—devolatilisation, primary flame, burnout, and post-flame—each characterised by time-averaged temperature and species concentrations derived from the in-flame measurements reported previously. Fuel-nitrogen content of the pellet batch was measured as 0.11 % by dry weight using a CHNS elemental analyser. NOx conversion efficiency from fuel-N was modelled using modified De Soete kinetics with empirically adjusted pre-exponential factors. Predicted NOx at the stack ranged from 71 to 138 mg/Nm³ across the load range tested; measured values were 69 to 143 mg/Nm³. Mean absolute error was 6.3 mg/Nm³. The model also captured the reversal in CO–NOx slope that occurs below 50 % load, where incomplete combustion zones expand and locally reduce NO to N₂. The zone approach requires only standard fuel analysis and burner geometry as inputs, making it applicable without CFD.

title: Measured reverberation times in primary school classrooms in Novi Sad: a baseline survey
abstract: This paper reports measured reverberation times (T20 and T30) in 24 standard classrooms across eight primary schools in Novi Sad, recorded under unoccupied and occupied conditions using an omni-directional dodecahedral loudspeaker and Brüel & Kjær 2250 sound level meter. Frequencies from 125 Hz to 4 kHz were examined. Mean unoccupied T20 at 500 Hz was 1.14 s, well above the 0.6 s ceiling recommended by ISO 3382-1 for classrooms used for speech. Occupied conditions reduced mean T20 to 0.83 s, still non-compliant in 19 of 24 rooms. Concrete block walls, terrazzo floors, and glazed tile ceilings dominated the surface inventory. The paper documents the construction typology of each building and correlates surface material composition with measured values, providing a reference data set for future retrofit planning and regulatory review in the region.

title: Effect of suspended mineral-wool ceiling panels on speech transmission index in rectangular classrooms
abstract: A series of scale-model and full-scale measurements was conducted to evaluate how partial suspended mineral-wool ceiling panels affect the Speech Transmission Index (STI) in a 65 m² rectangular classroom with a 3.1 m ceiling height. Three panel configurations were tested: full ceiling coverage, a central 40% strip, and two lateral 20% strips. STI was measured at nine student positions using a calibrated artificial mouth source. Full coverage raised mean STI from 0.52 to 0.68 across all positions, while the central-strip arrangement achieved a mean of 0.65, offering a cost-effective intermediate solution. Lateral strips produced negligible improvement beyond 4 m source distance. Background noise was held constant at NC-35 during tests. The study concludes that panel placement geometry matters as much as total absorption area, and offers a simple placement guideline applicable to standard Yugoslav-era school construction.

title: Airborne sound insulation of lightweight partition walls between adjacent classrooms: field measurements in four schools
abstract: This study presents field measurements of airborne sound insulation (R'w) between 38 pairs of adjacent classrooms in four primary schools in the Vojvodina region, conducted according to ISO 16283-1. Partitions ranged from 12 cm hollow-brick walls (R'w = 38 dB) to 25 cm reinforced concrete (R'w = 52 dB). Flanking transmission through floor slabs was estimated using a simplified EN 12354-1 approach and found to reduce effective insulation by 4–8 dB in most cases. Background noise levels in receiving rooms during school hours regularly exceeded 45 dB(A), meaning that even compliant partitions were insufficient when source rooms hosted music or physical education activities. Spectral deficiency at low frequencies (63–250 Hz) was identified as the primary compliance gap. The paper discusses the adequacy of Serbian national standard SRPS EN ISO 717-1 thresholds for educational occupancy.

title: Listening effort in English-as-a-foreign-language instruction: how reverberation time affects comprehension scores in Serbian primary school students
abstract: Forty-eight Serbian primary school students (age 10–11) participated in a listening experiment conducted in a reverberation-adjustable test classroom at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Three conditions were created by varying curtain absorption: T20 ≈ 0.4 s, 0.7 s, and 1.1 s. Students listened to standardised English-language sentence lists recorded by a native British-English speaker and a Serbian-accented speaker, and answered comprehension questions. Background noise was fixed at 38 dB(A). Mean comprehension scores fell from 78% at 0.4 s to 61% at 1.1 s for the native speaker and from 71% to 49% for the accented speaker. The performance gap between conditions was statistically significant (ANOVA, p < 0.01). The results confirm that recommended reverberation thresholds set for native listeners are insufficient for non-native language instruction and support adoption of a 0.5 s upper limit for English-language classrooms.

title: Comparative acoustic performance of three prefabricated classroom modules used in post-earthquake temporary schools in the region
abstract: Following several seismic events in the Western Balkans that prompted rapid deployment of prefabricated classroom modules, this study evaluated the acoustic performance of three proprietary module types used in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia between 2010 and 2015. In-situ measurements of T20 (250 Hz – 4 kHz) and R'w between modules were taken in 18 installed units. All three types exhibited T20 values between 0.9 s and 1.4 s at 500 Hz due to minimal absorption in the lightweight envelopes. Partition R'w between adjacent modules ranged from 32 to 39 dB, with significant low-frequency flanking through shared steel base frames. The paper proposes a set of minimum acoustic specifications for procurement of prefabricated educational structures and provides absorption coefficient data for the wall and ceiling composite panels used in each type.

title: Relationship between furniture arrangement and low-frequency room modes in primary school classrooms: a finite-element study
abstract: Low-frequency room modes in classrooms below 150 Hz are poorly addressed by standard porous absorbers, yet they contribute to uneven sound fields and reduced speech clarity. This finite-element study examined how the placement and mass of typical classroom furniture — rows of desks, bookshelves, and teacher's desk — affects modal frequency distribution in a 7.2 m × 9.6 m × 3.2 m shoebox classroom modelled in COMSOL Multiphysics. Eight furniture arrangements were evaluated. Results show that displacing dense furniture clusters from axial reflection planes shifts several problematic modes by up to 12 Hz, reducing maximum sound pressure level variance at student positions from ±9 dB to ±5 dB at 80 Hz. The study identifies three furniture layouts with consistently better low-frequency uniformity and provides simple layout rules derivable without FEM software.

title: Teachers' vocal load in high-reverberation classrooms: a field study using ambulatory dosimetry
abstract: This field study monitored the vocal output of 22 primary school teachers over a full school week using ambulatory electroglottograph dosimeters. Classrooms were grouped into three reverberation categories based on prior T20 measurements: low (T20 < 0.6 s, n = 7 teachers), medium (0.6–0.9 s, n = 8), and high (> 0.9 s, n = 7). Fundamental frequency, sound pressure level at 30 cm, and phonation time were logged continuously. Teachers in high-reverberation rooms sustained a mean equivalent voice level of 67.4 dB(A), compared with 63.1 dB(A) in low-reverberation rooms, consistent with a Lombard-effect mechanism. Phonation time differed by a mean of 18 minutes per day between groups. Teachers in high-reverberation classrooms reported significantly higher end-of-day vocal fatigue on the Voice Fatigue Index. The data argue for acoustic quality standards to be framed partly in terms of occupational health outcomes.

title: Impact noise insulation between floors in primary schools: measured L'n,w values in Vojvodina and comparison with design standards
abstract: Impact sound insulation between storeys in school buildings has received less regulatory attention than airborne insulation, yet footfall and chair-scraping noise from upper floors are among the most commonly cited disturbances by teachers and students. This study presents field measurements of weighted normalised impact sound pressure level (L'n,w) on 29 inter-storey floor constructions in primary schools across Vojvodina. Constructions ranged from unreinforced hollow-pot slabs (mean L'n,w = 74 dB) to reinforced concrete slabs with floating screed (mean L'n,w = 58 dB). Seven buildings met the Serbian national threshold of L'n,w ≤ 58 dB; none met the more stringent Finnish guideline of 53 dB. Spectral analysis identifies a consistent deficiency in the 63–250 Hz range attributable to absence of resilient layers. Retrofitting options for occupied school buildings are discussed, including dry floating screed systems feasible during summer maintenance breaks.

title: Acoustic conditions in newly built primary schools in Serbia: do current design guidelines ensure compliance?
abstract: Serbia's national technical regulation for primary school construction was updated in 2017 to include acoustic performance criteria for the first time. This paper evaluates compliance in 11 primary schools completed between 2018 and 2022 in Serbia, measuring T20, STI, R'w, and L'n,w in a representative set of classrooms, corridors, and gymnasiums. Results show that 8 of 11 buildings satisfied the T20 criterion of ≤ 0.8 s at 500 Hz in standard classrooms, but only 3 of 11 met the less common stricter criterion of ≤ 0.6 s now referenced in EU guidance documents. Sound insulation compliance rates were lower: 6 of 11 for airborne partitions between classrooms, 4 of 11 for impact floors. Design documentation review revealed that acoustic consultants were appointed in only 4 projects. The paper recommends mandatory acoustic consultancy as a project deliverable for publicly funded school buildings.
venue: Journal of Applied Architectural Research

title: Acoustic conditions in outdoor covered walkways connecting school buildings: measured levels and children's exposure during breaks
abstract: Outdoor covered walkways (colonnades, pergolas, and enclosed passages) between school buildings are rarely considered in acoustic design, yet children spend up to 25 minutes per day in these transitional spaces during breaks and class changes. This study characterises ambient noise levels and reverberation in 14 covered walkways at seven primary schools in Novi Sad, measuring equivalent A-weighted levels (LAeq) during occupied breaks and impulse response decay curves (EDT and T20) at 500 Hz and 1 kHz. Mean LAeq during breaks was 79 dB(A), with a maximum recorded value of 88 dB(A). Measured EDT ranged from 0.8 to 3.4 s depending on geometry and surface hardness. Children's estimated noise dose during a full school day including walkway exposure approached 80 dB(A) LEX,8h in two of the schools studied. The paper discusses implications for design and proposes absorptive ceiling treatments compatible with outdoor exposure.
venue: Proceedings of the European Conference on Architectural Acoustics

title: Subjective rating of classroom acoustics by Serbian primary school children using an adapted questionnaire: development and pilot testing
abstract: Most classroom acoustic research relies on physical measurements or adult self-report. This paper describes the development and pilot testing of a questionnaire instrument adapted for use with children aged 8–12 in Serbian primary schools. A 16-item instrument was created by simplifying and translating the CLACE adult classroom acoustic experience scale, replacing abstract terminology with concrete scenario descriptions verified through cognitive interviews with 24 children. Pilot testing was conducted in 12 classrooms in four schools in Novi Sad (n = 247 students). Internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.74) and test-retest reliability (r = 0.71 over two weeks) were acceptable. Factor analysis identified three subscales: perceived noisiness, listening effort, and teacher audibility. Questionnaire scores correlated moderately with measured STI (r = 0.58) and T20 (r = −0.47), suggesting the instrument captures acoustic experience not fully predicted by physical metrics. The instrument is provided in full as supplementary material.

title: A Framework for Classifying Spatial Mutations in Listed Rural Buildings of Vojvodina: Proposal and Pilot Application to 40 Structures
abstract: This paper proposes a classification framework for categorising spatially significant changes to listed rural buildings in Vojvodina, derived from examination of conservation files held at the Provincial Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments. The framework distinguishes five mutation types: subdivision, extension, subtraction, material substitution, and use-change without physical alteration. Each type is defined with measurable criteria and illustrated with drawn diagrams. The framework was piloted on a stratified sample of 40 listed structures across four spatial planning zones in Vojvodina, using condition reports, photographic records, and available measured drawings from the institute's archive. The pilot identified subdivision as the most frequent mutation type (found in 21 of 40 cases), followed by material substitution (17 cases). Extension and subtraction were less frequent but associated with greater loss of spatial integrity. The paper discusses how the framework could inform triage decisions in contexts where conservation staff capacity is limited relative to the number of protected structures requiring periodic monitoring.

title: Mean radiant temperature estimation from low-cost sensor arrays: accuracy assessment under clear-sky summer conditions
abstract: Mean Radiant Temperature (MRT) is central to outdoor thermal comfort indices but its direct measurement requires a globe thermometer, which limits large-scale spatial surveys. This paper evaluated three indirect estimation methods — the six-directional method using silicon photodiode sensors, a Tmrt model based on ENVI-met radiation outputs, and an empirical regression against air temperature and global radiation — against globe thermometer measurements at eight outdoor locations in Novi Sad during August 2019. Measurements were taken between 09:00 and 18:00 on three clear-sky days at pedestrian height (1.1 m). The six-directional sensor array achieved the lowest RMSE (1.9 °C), while the regression approach showed acceptable accuracy (RMSE 4.3 °C) during midday but deteriorated in shaded conditions. The ENVI-met-derived Tmrt overestimated MRT by a systematic 3.1 °C under direct sun, consistent with findings in prior European studies. Cost and deployment complexity for each method are discussed in the context of urban design practice.
venue: Building and Environment Measurement Studies

title: Freeze-thaw induced rutting in granular-base rural roads: field measurements and empirical correlations in the Vojvodina region
abstract: Rural roads with granular or thin bituminous surface layers in the Vojvodina lowland are subjected to repeated freeze-thaw cycles each winter, causing accelerated permanent deformation. This study presents results from a two-year field monitoring campaign on 14 road sections in Južnobačka and Sremska districts, where frost depth, soil moisture, and rut depth were recorded at weekly intervals between November and April. Frost penetration depths ranged from 18 cm to 64 cm across the observation period. A multiple linear regression model was fitted to relate rut increment per thaw event to antecedent frost depth, subgrade moisture content, and cumulative equivalent axle load. The model achieved an R² of 0.71 on the calibration dataset and 0.66 on a held-out validation subset. Results confirm that moisture content at the time of thaw is the single strongest predictor of rut depth increment, outweighing traffic load on roads with annual average daily traffic below 150 vehicles. Findings are intended to support maintenance scheduling decisions for municipal road administrations.
venue: Journal of Road and Pavement Research

title: Transition probability matrices for pavement condition states on unpaved and surface-dressed rural roads under seasonal climate loading
abstract: Markov chain models have been applied to pavement management for decades, yet their calibration for low-volume roads in continental climates with pronounced frost seasons remains limited. This study develops transition probability matrices (TPMs) for four pavement condition states—good, fair, poor, and very poor—using historical condition survey data from 87 km of municipal roads in three Serbian municipalities collected between 2015 and 2022. Data were sourced from local road administration records and supplemented by visual surveys conducted in 2021 and 2022. TPMs were estimated separately for spring post-thaw periods and summer–autumn periods, revealing substantially higher deterioration rates in the March–May window. Stationary distribution analysis indicates that without intervention, approximately 48% of the network reaches the poor or very poor state within eight years under current traffic and climate conditions. Sensitivity analysis shows that the assumed initial condition state has negligible effect on the stationary distribution beyond a five-year horizon. The calibrated matrices are directly applicable in standard pavement management software.

title: Mechanistic-empirical estimation of residual structural capacity after repeated freeze-thaw loading in thin asphalt pavements
abstract: Thin asphalt surface layers, typically 4–6 cm, are common on low-volume rural roads in Serbia and across the western Balkans. Their structural capacity after a winter season with multiple freeze-thaw events is not well characterised by existing mechanistic-empirical (ME) frameworks, which were largely calibrated on primary road networks with thicker structures. This study applies a modified ME procedure to estimate the residual structural number of 22 monitored pavement cross-sections following winters with 8 to 31 freeze-thaw cycles. Falling weight deflectometer (FWD) measurements were taken in late autumn and again in early spring at each site. Back-calculated subgrade moduli dropped by 18–43% between autumn and spring measurements, with the largest reductions observed on sections underlain by high-plasticity silty clay. A correction factor applied to the standard AASHTO structural layer coefficient for granular bases under frost-affected conditions is proposed based on the dataset. Limitations related to the small sample size and single-region calibration are discussed, and a validation study covering additional climate zones is recommended.
venue: European Journal of Pavement and Road Technology

title: Frost susceptibility classification of road subgrade soils in the Pannonian lowland using index properties and laboratory freeze-thaw tests
abstract: Accurate frost susceptibility classification of subgrade soils is a prerequisite for reliable pavement deterioration modelling in regions with seasonal frost. Standard classification schemes such as the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers criteria and the German ZTV system were developed under specific soil conditions and may not translate directly to the silty and silty-clay soils predominant in the Pannonian lowland. This paper reports results from laboratory freeze-thaw tests on 34 remoulded soil specimens sampled from rural road subgrades across Vojvodina, tested in a custom-built frost column apparatus with controlled temperature gradients. Heave rates, segregation potential, and post-thaw bearing capacity loss were measured and correlated with Atterberg limits, grain size distribution, and hydraulic conductivity. A discriminant analysis correctly classified frost susceptibility group membership in 82% of cases using only liquid limit and percentage finer than 0.02 mm as predictors. The simplified classification criterion is proposed as a practical field tool for municipal engineers without access to full laboratory testing.

title: Warm-Starting Metaheuristics Using Machine-Learning Predictions of Near-Optimal Depot Assignments
abstract: Metaheuristic solvers for multi-depot VRP instances often spend a significant fraction of their runtime escaping poor initial solutions. This paper investigates whether a gradient-boosted classifier trained on instance features can predict near-optimal depot assignments for individual tasks, thereby warm-starting the metaheuristic. A dataset of 4,800 solved MDVRPTW instances was used for training; features included task spatial coordinates, time-window midpoints, inter-depot distances, and task service durations. The classifier achieved a task-level assignment accuracy of 71.3% on held-out instances compared to optimal solutions. When used to initialise a tabu search, the ML-warm-started variants reached equivalent solution quality 38% faster than random initialisation and 19% faster than nearest-depot initialisation. Gains were largest on instances with high depot load imbalance. The paper also reports results on the public Cordeau MDVRP benchmark for comparability with existing literature.

title: Spatial variability of exchangeable sodium percentage in solonetz soils of the Bačka lowland: a geostatistical survey
abstract: A geostatistical study was conducted across 1,240 ha of Vojvodina solonetz soils to characterise spatial variability of exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP) and electrical conductivity (ECe) at three depth intervals (0–30, 30–60, 60–100 cm). A total of 312 soil cores were collected on a stratified random grid during spring 2008 and autumn 2009. Ordinary kriging with exponential variogram models (range 420–680 m) reproduced ESP patterns with cross-validation RMSE below 3.1 percentage points. Hotspots of ESP > 25% occupied 18% of the surveyed area, concentrated in micro-depressions with restricted drainage. ECe correlated weakly with ESP (r = 0.38) in the upper 30 cm but strongly (r = 0.71) below 60 cm, suggesting leaching of surface horizons by precipitation while subsoil alkalisation persisted. Results provide a baseline map for prioritising reclamation interventions and illustrate that single-depth sampling protocols underestimate subsurface alkalisation extent by 30–40% in this landscape.

title: Effect of gypsum application rate on saturated hydraulic conductivity of a Vertisol under furrow irrigation in Vojvodina
abstract: A three-year field experiment (2007–2009) evaluated four gypsum rates (0, 5, 10, and 20 t ha⁻¹) on saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ksat) of a Vertisol near Srbobran. Gypsum was surface-applied and incorporated to 30 cm in spring 2007. Ksat was measured in situ using the Guelph permeameter at 20, 60, and 90 cm depths after each growing season. At the 10 t ha⁻¹ rate, Ksat at 20 cm depth increased from 0.04 to 0.19 m day⁻¹ after three seasons, while the 20 t ha⁻¹ rate produced only marginally higher values (0.22 m day⁻¹), suggesting diminishing returns above 10 t ha⁻¹. Changes at 60 cm and 90 cm depths were smaller and non-significant after the first season. Exchangeable sodium percentage declined from 31% to 14% in the 0–30 cm layer under the optimal rate. These results support using 10 t ha⁻¹ as a practical threshold under current gypsum market prices in Serbia.

title: Tile drainage performance on alkaline heavy clay: monitoring discharge and ionic composition over four cropping seasons
abstract: Continuous discharge monitoring and bi-weekly water sampling were carried out at a 48-ha tile drainage system (drain spacing 15 m, depth 1.2 m) on an alkaline heavy clay near Zrenjanin from 2009 to 2012. Annual drainage volumes ranged from 82 mm (dry 2011) to 241 mm (wet 2010). Na⁺ export was highest in the first season (38 kg ha⁻¹) and declined to 17 kg ha⁻¹ by the fourth, while Ca²⁺ export remained below 8 kg ha⁻¹ throughout, indicating preferential Na removal but limited Ca mobilisation from the subsoil. Soil profile EC measurements showed that leaching was largely confined to the 0–80 cm layer despite drain depth. A simple one-dimensional leaching fraction model overpredicted Na export by 55% in the wet year due to preferential flow through shrinkage cracks. The data suggest that crack-flow pathways must be parameterised separately to improve prediction accuracy for heavy clay reclamation drainage.

title: Calibration of the SALTMOD model for solonetz reclamation planning under Vojvodina irrigation conditions
abstract: The steady-state SALTMOD water and salt balance model was calibrated and validated for two contrasting solonetz sites in Vojvodina (Bečej and Novi Bečej districts) using datasets spanning 1998–2011. Input data included monthly evapotranspiration (FAO-56 method), irrigation volumes from canal intake records, groundwater depth from 24 piezometers, and seasonal soil ECe profiles. After calibration, simulated root-zone ECe matched observed values with RMSE of 0.38 dS m⁻¹ and R² of 0.83 at Bečej and 0.79 at Novi Bečej. Sensitivity analysis identified capillary rise flux as the dominant source of uncertainty, accounting for 41% of output variance. Scenarios for drain spacing reduction from 20 m to 12 m combined with 15 t ha⁻¹ gypsum application predicted root-zone ESP below 15% within eight years. The calibrated parameter sets are made available to support regional reclamation planning by provincial water management authorities.

title: Monitoring secondary salinisation under drip irrigation in a maize production system on Vojvodina clay
abstract: Secondary salinisation risk was assessed in a three-year drip-irrigated maize trial (2013–2015) on a heavy clay at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station. Soil ECe and ESP were measured at 0–20, 20–50, and 50–100 cm depths before planting and after harvest each year. Irrigation water electrical conductivity was 0.9 dS m⁻¹. After three seasons, ECe in the 20–50 cm layer increased by 1.4 dS m⁻¹ relative to the non-irrigated control, while surface accumulation was modest (0.4 dS m⁻¹). Exchangeable sodium percentage did not change significantly in any layer, attributed to moderate sodium adsorption ratio (SAR < 6) in the irrigation source. The observed sub-surface ECe rise coincided with restricted lateral drainage and correlated with wetter-than-average seasons. Findings indicate that current irrigation practice at this site does not induce alkalisation over a three-year horizon but warrants continued ECe monitoring given the low initial soil permeability.

title: Reclamation drainage design criteria for slotted pipe systems in Vojvodina solonetz: comparison of three hydraulic calculation methods
abstract: Three analytical methods for pipe hydraulic design—the Hooghoudt equivalent depth method, the Ernst composite formula, and a numerical finite-element approach implemented in SEEP/W—were compared for 11 solonetz drainage projects in Vojvodina executed between 2000 and 2014. Project reports provided design drain spacing, installed depth, observed water table drawdown, and measured Ksat profiles. The Ernst formula most closely reproduced observed water table drawdown, with a mean absolute error of 0.09 m versus 0.17 m for Hooghoudt and 0.11 m for SEEP/W under dry-weather conditions. Under wet conditions following crack closure, all methods overestimated drainage rate by 25–60% due to clay swelling reducing effective pore volume. Practical guidance is provided for selecting calculation method based on available Ksat data quality and soil shrink-swell characterisation, with specific recommendations for the expansive clays predominant in the Bačka and Banat regions.

title: Long-term changes in soil alkalinity following combined gypsum and organic matter amendments on reclaimed solonetz in the Banat plain
abstract: A 15-year monitoring dataset (2001–2015) from a reclaimed solonetz site near Zrenjanin was used to analyse trajectories of pH, ESP, and aggregate stability following three amendment treatments: gypsum alone (10 t ha⁻¹), gypsum combined with green manure (5 t ha⁻¹ dry matter), and untreated control. Soil was sampled every three years at six depths to 120 cm. In the gypsum-only treatment, surface ESP declined from 28% to 11% by year six and stabilised near 14% at year fifteen, suggesting partial re-alkalisation from capillary Na ascent. The combined treatment maintained ESP below 12% throughout and yielded mean aggregate stability (wet sieving, MWD) 40% higher than gypsum alone after year nine. pH in the 60–90 cm layer remained above 9.2 in all treatments, confirming that single surface applications do not reclaim the subsoil alkalinity horizon within a 15-year window. Annual organic carbon inputs from crop residues were identified as the principal factor in sustaining surface-layer improvements.

title: Gypsum dose optimisation model for alkaline Vertisols: integrating soil ESP, crop tolerance and gypsum price
abstract: An Excel-based decision support model was developed to calculate economically optimal gypsum doses for alkaline Vertisol reclamation in Vojvodina. The model couples a three-layer salt balance routine with crop-specific salt tolerance thresholds (from FAO bulletin 29 values updated with local field data for sugar beet, sunflower, and wheat) and current Serbian gypsum market prices. Input data requirements are ESP profile, cation exchange capacity, target crop, irrigation water SAR, and expected yields under reference conditions. Calibration used data from 18 field trials conducted between 1998 and 2016 across Bačka and Banat. For sugar beet, optimal doses ranged from 7.5 to 14 t ha⁻¹ depending on initial ESP (15–35%) and cation exchange capacity (35–55 cmol kg⁻¹). Sensitivity runs showed that a 20% increase in gypsum price shifts the economic optimum downward by 1.2–2.4 t ha⁻¹. The model was validated against three independent trials not used in calibration, reproducing observed yield responses within ±8%.

title: Electromagnetic induction mapping of solonetz areas in the Tamiš–Bega interfluve: comparison with laboratory ECe measurement
abstract: EM38 and EM31 electromagnetic induction instruments were used to map apparent soil electrical conductivity (ECa) across 2,300 ha of the Tamiš–Bega interfluve in autumn 2017. A total of 61 calibration points were sampled for laboratory ECe, pH, and clay content to derive pedotransfer functions relating ECa to ECe at two depths. The EM38 vertical dipole configuration correlated best with 0–80 cm ECe (R² = 0.77), while EM31 was more informative below 1 m depth. Predicted ECe maps delineated three salinisation classes covering 8%, 31%, and 61% of the area. Cross-validation showed mean absolute errors of 0.44 dS m⁻¹ in the 0–30 cm layer and 0.61 dS m⁻¹ in the 30–80 cm layer. Temporal repeat surveys in spring and autumn 2018 detected seasonal ECa differences of up to 0.18 S m⁻¹ linked to drainage status. The maps are being used by the provincial water authority to prioritise areas for targeted reclamation funding.

title: Influence of drain depth and spacing on groundwater salinity dynamics in a Vojvodina solonetz: a lysimeter study
abstract: Twelve monolith lysimeters (1.5 m diameter × 1.8 m depth) containing undisturbed solonetz cores from Bačka were equipped with artificial drainage at two depths (0.9 m and 1.2 m) and irrigated over two seasons with water of two SAR values (5 and 12). Drainage effluent and pore water from suction cups at 0.4, 0.8, and 1.3 m were sampled weekly. Shallow drainage (0.9 m) removed 23% more Na⁺ per unit water volume applied than deep drainage in the first season under SAR-5 irrigation. Under SAR-12 irrigation, percolate SAR exceeded 8 in lysimeters with shallow drainage within six weeks, indicating re-sodification of the upper layer. Pore water data showed that the 0.8 m depth acted as a Na accumulation zone regardless of drain depth, attributed to upward capillary flux from the clay substratum during drying periods. These findings support the use of deeper drainage combined with low-SAR water as the minimum viable reclamation strategy.

title: Soil salinisation risk under projected climate change in the Vojvodina region: scenarios for 2050 and 2080
abstract: Salt accumulation risk for Vojvodina irrigated soils was assessed under two CMIP6 climate scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) using bias-corrected regional climate model output from the CORDEX-EUR-11 ensemble (six model chains). A one-dimensional unsaturated flow and salt transport model (HYDRUS-1D) was run for three representative soil profiles (solonetz, calcaric Chernozem, and stagnosol) at 24 virtual monitoring sites. Under SSP5-8.5, potential evapotranspiration is projected to increase by 14–18% by 2080 relative to 1990–2020, driving a simulated 28–42% rise in root-zone ECe under current irrigation management. Solonetz soils showed the highest sensitivity due to lower leaching efficiency. Switching from furrow to drip irrigation reduced projected ECe increase by 9–15 percentage points. The results suggest that without adaptation in irrigation scheduling and drainage infrastructure, roughly 65,000 ha of currently borderline alkaline soils in the region may cross the 15% ESP threshold by 2080.

title: Assessment of phosphogypsum as a substitute for natural gypsum in solonetz reclamation: chemical purity, heavy metal load, and short-term soil response
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG) sourced from a Serbian fertiliser plant was evaluated as an alternative amendment to natural mined gypsum (MG) in a two-year pot experiment with alkaline clay soil. Chemical analysis showed PG contained 82.4% CaSO₄·2H₂O with residual phosphoric acid (0.3%), fluoride (0.8 g kg⁻¹), and trace cadmium (1.1 mg kg⁻¹). Three rates (5, 10, 15 t ha⁻¹ equivalent) of both PG and MG were applied to 25 kg soil-filled containers planted with sunflower. After two seasons, ESP reduction was statistically indistinguishable between PG and MG at matching rates (mean difference 1.4 percentage points, p = 0.18). Soil fluoride levels increased significantly only at 15 t ha⁻¹ PG, reaching 11.2 mg kg⁻¹ extractable F, which remained below Serbian regulatory thresholds. Cadmium accumulation was negligible at all rates. PG appears technically viable for solonetz reclamation, but regulatory approval for agricultural use on food-crop land has not yet been obtained in Serbia as of the study date.
venue: Applied Soil Ecology

title: Irrigation water quality index for solonetz-prone soils in the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal system: 2015–2023 trends
abstract: Water quality data from 14 sampling stations on the Danube–Tisa–Danube (DTD) canal network were compiled for the period 2015–2023 from monthly monitoring records of the Provincial Directorate for Water Management. Parameters analysed included EC, Na⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, HCO₃⁻, Cl⁻, and SAR. A weighted irrigation water quality index (IWQI) was computed following the FAO guidelines approach, adapted with local soil texture weights for heavy clay. Mean annual SAR across stations ranged from 3.8 to 9.4, with highest values recorded in late summer (July–August) when low flows concentrate dissolved solids. Three stations exceeded SAR 8.5 in at least three of eight years, posing a moderate alkalisation hazard for clay soils. Trend analysis using Mann–Kendall tests detected a statistically significant increasing SAR trend (τ = 0.41, p < 0.05) at two stations downstream of intensive irrigation return flow discharge points. These results inform canal management scheduling to reduce peak-season hazard.

title: Machine learning classification of solonetz reclamation readiness from proximal and remote sensing covariates
abstract: Random forest and gradient boosting classifiers were trained to predict whether individual 1-ha parcels in the Bačka lowland met agronomic criteria for immediate reclamation (ESP < 20%, Ksat > 0.05 m day⁻¹, water table depth > 1.2 m) using a combination of Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, EM38-derived ECa maps, and 1:50,000 soil map polygons. A labelled dataset of 810 parcels with full profile measurements assembled between 2010 and 2023 was split 70/30 for training and testing. Random forest achieved an overall accuracy of 79% and F1 score of 0.76 for the reclamation-ready class; gradient boosting reached 81% accuracy and F1 of 0.78. The most informative predictors were ECa at 0.75 m integration depth, autumn NDVI, and soil map unit. A confusion analysis showed that misclassified parcels were disproportionately located at the solonetz–chernozem transition zone. The approach provides a scalable screening tool for provincial land reclamation planning without requiring exhaustive field campaigns.

title: Impact of inter-annual rainfall variability on rainfed maize water stress in Vojvodina: a 30-year simulation study
abstract: Long-term records from four synoptic stations in Vojvodina (1986–2015) were used to drive the AquaCrop model for rainfed maize in order to quantify inter-annual variability in crop water stress. The 30-year simulation showed that water stress during silking (growth stage GS-2) occurred in more than 60% of years at the most southern station (Sombor), compared to 42% at the northern station (Subotica). Mean simulated yield under rainfed conditions ranged from 5.9 t/ha (Sombor, dry years) to 9.4 t/ha (Subotica, wet years). The relationship between the standardised precipitation-evapotranspiration index (SPEI-3 for June–August) and simulated relative yield loss was statistically significant (r = −0.71, p < 0.001), confirming the utility of SPEI as a proxy indicator for irrigation need assessments at the planning level. Results suggest that supplemental irrigation of 60–80 mm applied at silking would reduce yield losses by approximately 35% in dry years.

title: Pollen germination capacity in selected pepper lines under contrasting temperature regimes during anthesis
abstract: Pollen viability was evaluated in five inbred pepper lines (Capsicum annuum L.) grown under three day/night temperature regimes (22/16 °C, 28/22 °C, 35/28 °C) in growth chambers at the Faculty of Agriculture, Novi Sad. Pollen was collected at full anthesis on three consecutive days per treatment and assessed by the fluorochromatic reaction (FCR) assay and in vitro germination on agar medium supplemented with 10% sucrose and 100 mg L⁻¹ boric acid. At 35/28 °C, FCR scores fell by 31–47% relative to the optimal 28/22 °C regime, while in vitro germination rates declined 22–38%. Pollen tube elongation was significantly reduced at high temperatures in all five lines, with the strongest effect observed in line NS-P3. Correlations between FCR score and in vitro tube length were positive (r = 0.74–0.89) across lines. Results suggest that FCR provides a reliable proxy for thermal tolerance screening at early breeding stages.
