title: Stigma receptivity in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) as influenced by flower position and developmental stage
abstract: Stigma receptivity in three tomato cultivars was assessed by peroxidase activity staining and pollen tube growth following hand-pollination at four developmental stages: early bud, late bud, day-0 anthesis, and day-2 post-anthesis. Flowers were sampled from the first, second, and third truss positions in a greenhouse experiment replicated over two seasons at Novi Sad (2010 and 2011). Peroxidase activity was highest at day-0 anthesis in all cultivars and declined sharply by day-2 post-anthesis. First-truss flowers showed slightly earlier onset of receptivity and shorter effective pollination periods (3.2 ± 0.4 days) compared to second-truss flowers (4.1 ± 0.6 days). Hand-pollination at day-0 produced the highest fruit set (88–94%) and seed number per fruit across cultivars. These data establish a practical timing guide for controlled crosses in tomato breeding programmes operating under greenhouse conditions.

title: Effect of relative humidity on pollen viability and fertilisation rate in open-field hybrid pepper seed production
abstract: Hybrid pepper seed production relies on reliable pollen transfer and fertilisation in open-field plots where ambient conditions vary considerably. This study quantified the relationship between relative humidity (RH) at time of anthesis and subsequent fertilisation success across two growing seasons (2012–2013) in the Bačka region of Vojvodina. Pollen viability (FCR assay) and fruit set were recorded daily at RH levels ranging from 28% to 87%. Viability declined at both extremes: below 40% RH, viability dropped to 54 ± 8%, while above 80% RH it fell to 61 ± 7%, compared with 82 ± 5% at 55–70% RH. Fruit set showed a parallel pattern, decreasing by 18–27% outside the optimal humidity range. Regression analysis explained 68% of the variance in fruit set using RH and maximum daily temperature as predictors. Supplemental irrigation to raise canopy humidity during low-RH periods improved fruit set by 11% in the drier season.

title: Pollen storage conditions and viability retention in male-fertile pepper lines used in F1 hybrid production
abstract: Reliable access to viable pollen is critical when synchronising flowering between parental lines in pepper hybrid seed programmes. Pollen from four male-fertile lines was harvested at full anthesis, dried to two moisture levels (approximately 6% and 10% dry weight basis), and stored at −20 °C, 4 °C, and 22 °C for periods of 1, 2, 4, and 8 weeks. Viability was assessed by FCR assay and confirmed by germination tests. Pollen stored at −20 °C with 6% moisture retained FCR scores above 70% for up to 8 weeks in three of four lines. Storage at 22 °C caused viability to drop below 50% within two weeks regardless of moisture level. Fruit set following hand-pollination with stored pollen corresponded closely to FCR scores (r = 0.83). Practical recommendations for short-term (≤4 weeks, 4 °C) and medium-term (≤8 weeks, −20 °C) pollen banking in breeding programmes are provided.

title: Diurnal variation in stigma exudate composition and pollen capture efficiency in pepper under greenhouse conditions
abstract: Stigma exudate in pepper flowers undergoes compositional changes throughout the day that may influence pollen adhesion and hydration. Stigma exudates from male-sterile pepper plants were collected at 06:00, 09:00, 12:00, 15:00, and 18:00 over five consecutive days and analysed for total soluble protein, soluble sugar content, and esterase activity. Pollen capture efficiency was assessed by recording the number of grains retained 30 min after standardised deposition at each time point. Soluble protein peaked between 09:00 and 12:00 (1.8–2.1 mg mL⁻¹) and declined through the afternoon. Esterase activity paralleled this pattern. Pollen capture efficiency was highest at 09:00–11:00 (77 ± 6 grains per stigma) and dropped to 41 ± 9 by 15:00. These findings suggest that pollination operations in hybrid seed greenhouses should be scheduled in the mid-morning hours to maximise fertilisation success.

title: Seed set variability in hybrid pepper production under elevated CO₂ and temperature: a controlled-environment study
abstract: Projected changes in atmospheric CO₂ concentration and seasonal temperatures in the Pannonian Plain prompted this experiment testing two CO₂ levels (400 and 700 µmol mol⁻¹) and two temperature regimes (ambient and +3 °C above ambient) in a two-by-two factorial arrangement in controlled-environment chambers. Two male-fertile pepper lines and one male-sterile line were grown through flowering and seed set. Elevated CO₂ alone had little effect on pollen viability or fruit set. Elevated temperature (+3 °C) reduced FCR-based pollen viability from 79% to 58% and fruit set from 81% to 62%. The combination of elevated CO₂ and elevated temperature produced an intermediate outcome: fruit set at 69%, possibly due to partial metabolic compensation under elevated carbon supply. Seed weight per fruit was unaffected by CO₂ but declined by 8% under elevated temperature. These results inform adaptation strategies for hybrid seed production in a changing regional climate.

title: Pollinator visitation and fertilisation success in open-field pepper hybrid seed production: implications for managed bee colony placement
abstract: Hybrid pepper seed production in uncaged open-field plots depends partly on insect-mediated pollen transfer. Pollinators were monitored by timed counts at the plot perimeter and interior over three seasons (2018–2020) in Vojvodina. The dominant visitor was Apis mellifera L. (62% of visits), followed by Bombus terrestris L. (21%) and solitary bees (17%). Fruit set was positively correlated with Bombus visitation rate (r = 0.71) but only weakly correlated with Apis visitation (r = 0.38), likely because A. mellifera preferentially collected nectar without contacting anthers. Placement of bumble bee colonies at a density of one colony per 800 m² increased fruit set by 14–19% relative to plots without managed colonies. Seed number per fruit was not significantly different across placement densities. These data support the targeted use of Bombus colonies to supplement natural pollinator communities in commercial hybrid pepper seed plots.

title: Image analysis as a tool for automated pollen viability scoring in pepper: comparison with FCR and in vitro germination
abstract: Manual FCR scoring and in vitro germination tests are time-consuming when processing large numbers of pepper breeding samples. This study evaluated an image-analysis pipeline applied to brightfield micrographs of pollen preparations stained with acetocarmine as an alternative. Pollen from 30 inbred pepper lines was assessed by all three methods across two seasons. The image-analysis approach classified each grain as viable or non-viable based on size, circularity, and stain intensity using a threshold trained on 2,400 manually annotated grains. Agreement between image analysis and FCR was 91.4% at the grain level and 0.93 in Pearson correlation of viability percentages across lines. Compared with in vitro germination, image analysis showed r = 0.87. Processing time per sample was reduced from approximately 25 min (FCR manual) to 4 min (image analysis). The pipeline code is described and the training dataset is deposited in a public repository. Limitations at extreme viability values (<20% and >95%) are discussed.

title: Intraspecific variation in the effective pollination period of tomato cultivars grown under low-light winter greenhouse conditions
abstract: Low light intensity during winter greenhouse production in the Pannonian region restricts photosynthetic output and may shorten the effective pollination period (EPP) of tomato flowers. EPP was measured in eight indeterminate tomato cultivars by pollinating flowers at one-day intervals from bud stage through five days post-anthesis and recording fruit set and seed number under natural light supplemented to either 150 or 250 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ PPFD. Mean EPP ranged from 2.9 to 5.2 days across cultivars at 150 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ and from 3.4 to 5.8 days at 250 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Two cultivars showed EPP extension of more than one day under higher light, while three showed no significant change. Stigma peroxidase activity scores aligned with EPP length in six of eight cultivars. The results indicate that supplemental lighting strategies should account for cultivar-specific EPP responses rather than applying uniform timing protocols.

title: Fertilisation outcomes in thermosensitive male-sterile pepper accessions under field heat episodes: a two-location trial
abstract: Thermosensitive male sterility (TSMS) is used commercially in pepper hybrid seed production but its stability under field heat episodes in Vojvodina has not been well characterised. This study evaluated five TSMS accessions and their corresponding restorer lines at two locations in Vojvodina (Rimski Šančevi and Bečej) across the 2023 and 2024 seasons. Fertility restoration percentage was scored by counting pollen-bearing anthers per flower (minimum 30 flowers per plot, three times per season). During documented heat episodes (≥3 consecutive days with maximum temperature ≥37 °C), two of five TSMS accessions showed partial fertility restoration (15–33%), compromising seed purity estimates. Pollen viability in restored plants was lower than in fully fertile controls (42% vs 79% FCR). Seed purity indices derived from morphological markers confirmed that contamination events occurred in both affected accessions during heat episodes. The findings have direct implications for roguing protocols and selection of TSMS lines for Vojvodina conditions.

title: Incorporating legacy soil survey data into prescription modelling: a harmonisation workflow for 1:50 000 soil maps and contemporary point observations in Serbia
abstract: Serbia's 1:50 000 legacy soil survey polygons represent decades of field work but were not designed for precision agriculture applications. This paper describes a harmonisation workflow that merges polygon-level soil attribute estimates from digitised legacy maps with contemporary point observations (grid sampling at 2–4 ha density) using a regression-kriging approach. The workflow was applied across 38 fields (total 4 200 ha) in three municipalities of Vojvodina. Incorporating legacy data as soft constraints in the regression-kriging covariance structure reduced the required contemporary sample density for achieving a target organic-matter prediction error (RMSE < 2 g kg⁻¹) from 2 ha to 3.5 ha per sample, representing a 43% reduction in sampling cost. Prescription maps produced with harmonised inputs deviated from the full-sampling benchmark by a mean of 9 kg N ha⁻¹, within operationally acceptable limits. The workflow is implemented as an open R script distributed with the paper.

title: Imidacloprid runoff losses from maize fields into adjacent drainage ditches in the Vojvodina lowlands
abstract: Concentrations of imidacloprid were monitored over two growing seasons (2009–2010) in surface runoff water collected from paired drainage ditches alongside conventionally treated maize plots in the Vojvodina lowlands. Thirty-six water samples were taken at weekly intervals from April through September and analysed by LC-MS/MS with a detection limit of 0.01 µg/L. Peak concentrations of 0.38 µg/L were recorded during the first post-sowing rainfall event, declining to below 0.05 µg/L within four weeks. Total seasonal export was estimated at 0.12–0.19 g active ingredient per hectare, accounting for approximately 0.08% of the applied seed-coating dose. Soil texture and rainfall intensity were identified as primary drivers of runoff magnitude. Results suggest that even under moderate rainfall, imidacloprid concentrations in receiving ditches may transiently exceed threshold values associated with acute effects on sensitive non-target invertebrates such as Gammarus fossarum.

title: Acute toxicity of clothianidin to Chironomus riparius under static and semi-static exposure conditions
abstract: Standard 48-hour and 96-hour acute immobility tests were conducted on fourth-instar larvae of Chironomus riparius exposed to clothianidin concentrations ranging from 0.05 to 10 µg/L, in both static and semi-static renewal regimes. Tests followed OECD Guideline 235 with minor adaptations for semi-static exposure. The 48-hour EC50 in the static system was 1.74 µg/L (95% CI: 1.31–2.18 µg/L), while semi-static renewal reduced the EC50 to 0.93 µg/L, reflecting compound degradation in the static vessels. No mortality was recorded at the lowest test concentration in either regime. These findings indicate that clothianidin poses moderate acute risk to midge larvae at field-relevant concentrations and that static tests may underestimate risk compared to flowing-water scenarios. Data are discussed in the context of existing regulatory trigger values for surface water protection.

title: Influence of vegetated riparian buffer width on neonicotinoid attenuation in shallow overland flow
abstract: A plot-scale field experiment was established at an agricultural research station near Sremska Mitrovica to test whether buffer strip width (0, 5, 10, and 20 m of mixed grass–forb vegetation) affects the attenuation of imidacloprid and thiamethoxam in simulated overland flow events. Three artificial rainfall events of 25 mm/h were applied to 4 m × 20 m plots. Water samples collected at the lower edge of each buffer were analysed by LC-MS/MS. The 5 m buffer reduced imidacloprid concentrations by 38% relative to the control, the 10 m buffer by 61%, and the 20 m buffer by 84%. Thiamethoxam showed consistently lower attenuation (maximum 71% at 20 m), attributed to its higher water solubility. Infiltration into the buffer soil accounted for 55–70% of the total mass reduction. Results support a minimum 10 m buffer recommendation but highlight that thiamethoxam may require wider zones or additional management practices.

title: Macroinvertebrate community responses to neonicotinoid contamination gradients along drainage canals in northern Serbia
abstract: Benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages were surveyed at 18 sites along a 120 km network of drainage canals in northern Vojvodina during spring and summer of 2014. At each site, surface water was sampled simultaneously for neonicotinoid residues. Imidacloprid was detected at 83% of sites (range: 0.01–0.47 µg/L), clothianidin at 61% of sites (range: <LOD–0.29 µg/L), and thiamethoxam at 44% of sites. Multivariate ordination (RDA) explained 34% of variance in community composition. EPT (Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, Trichoptera) taxon richness declined significantly with increasing imidacloprid concentration (Spearman r = −0.62, p < 0.01). Diptera and Oligochaeta showed relative increases at higher concentrations, suggesting community simplification. Canonical partitioning separated neonicotinoid effects from co-varying nutrients and flow velocity, accounting for approximately 12% of unique community variance. The results corroborate mesocosm-derived thresholds for chronic invertebrate effects in a real-world canal context.

title: Sorption characteristics of imidacloprid and clothianidin in alluvial and chernozem soils from the Sava riparian corridor
abstract: Batch equilibrium sorption experiments were performed on five soils collected from riparian and upland agricultural positions along the Sava River corridor in Serbia. Freundlich sorption coefficients (Kf) for imidacloprid ranged from 1.8 L/kg in a sandy alluvial soil (organic carbon 0.9%) to 8.4 L/kg in a chernozem (organic carbon 3.2%). Clothianidin showed systematically lower sorption (Kf range: 0.9–4.1 L/kg), consistent with its higher polarity. Positive linear correlations between Koc and soil organic carbon content were confirmed (r² = 0.87 for imidacloprid, r² = 0.79 for clothianidin). Desorption hysteresis was moderate (hysteresis index 0.12–0.21), suggesting partial irreversible binding in humic-rich soils. These data were incorporated into PELMO fate modelling runs to predict leaching potential under Vojvodina rainfall regimes, with results indicating higher leaching risk from sandy buffer soils at field margins.

title: Outdoor mesocosm study on chronic effects of imidacloprid on Gammarus fossarum feeding rate and survival
abstract: Twelve outdoor flow-through mesocosms were used to expose Gammarus fossarum to nominal imidacloprid concentrations of 0 (control), 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 µg/L for 28 days during the 2016 growing season. Measured water concentrations were within 15% of nominal values throughout. Leaf litter (alder discs) was added as a feeding substrate, and consumption rates were measured gravimetrically every four days. Survival was recorded daily. No significant mortality was observed at or below 0.1 µg/L. At 0.5 µg/L, survival at day 28 was 72% compared to 94% in controls (p = 0.03). Feeding rate was significantly reduced from 0.1 µg/L onwards, with a 46% reduction at 1.0 µg/L. The chronic NOEC for feeding inhibition was set at 0.05 µg/L. Environmentally measured concentrations in Vojvodina drainage ditches overlap substantially with this range during post-sowing periods, indicating ecological relevance of the observed effects.

title: Assessment of neonicotinoid risk to aquatic invertebrates in Pannonian lowland agricultural landscapes: a weight-of-evidence approach
abstract: A weight-of-evidence (WoE) framework was applied to integrate field monitoring data, laboratory toxicity data, and in-situ bioassay results for neonicotinoid risk assessment in 22 catchments across the Pannonian agricultural zone of Serbia and southern Hungary. Evidence was scored across four lines: measured environmental concentrations, species sensitivity distributions (SSDs), in-situ Hyalella azteca survival tests, and macroinvertebrate field community metrics. SSDs constructed from 34 acute EC50 values yielded HC5 estimates of 0.06 µg/L for imidacloprid and 0.12 µg/L for clothianidin. Risk quotients exceeded 1 at 68% of monitored sites for imidacloprid during peak periods. WoE scores classified 11 of 22 catchments as high risk. The framework produced consistent risk classifications with lower uncertainty than single-line assessments. Spatial analysis identified proximity to seed-treated maize as the dominant landscape predictor of high-risk classification.
venue: Science of the Total Environment

title: Buffer zone plant community composition alters imidacloprid dissipation rates through differential microbial activity
abstract: Laboratory microcosms containing intact soil cores from riparian buffer zones under three vegetation types—bare soil, grass monoculture (Festuca arundinacea), and mixed grass–forb assemblage—were spiked with imidacloprid at 500 µg/kg and incubated at 20°C for 90 days. Subsamples were taken at 0, 7, 14, 28, 60, and 90 days and analysed by LC-MS/MS. Dissipation followed first-order kinetics in all treatments. DT50 values were 87 days (bare soil), 54 days (grass monoculture), and 38 days (mixed assemblage). Microbial biomass carbon, measured by chloroform fumigation-extraction, was significantly higher in mixed-assemblage soils (383 µg C/g vs. 218 µg C/g in bare soil). Structural equation modelling indicated that microbial biomass partially mediated the vegetation effect on dissipation rate (indirect effect path coefficient = 0.44). The hydroxyl-imidacloprid metabolite was detected in all treatments but at concentrations below 12% of parent compound. Results suggest that enhancing plant diversity in buffer strips may accelerate neonicotinoid attenuation.

title: Neonicotinoid residues in riparian buffer zones: a synthesis of Central and South-Eastern European monitoring studies
abstract: This chapter synthesises published and grey-literature monitoring data from fourteen studies conducted across Central and South-Eastern European agricultural catchments between 2010 and 2022, covering Austria, Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania, and Serbia. Data for imidacloprid, clothianidin, thiamethoxam, and acetamiprid were harmonised to common units and screened against regulatory environmental quality standards. Imidacloprid exceedances were reported in 58% of compiled datasets, most frequently in countries with continued seed-coating use. Country-level differences in exceedance frequency were associated with soil drainage class and maize production area, rather than differences in monitoring methodology. The chapter also reviews proposed buffer zone management strategies, including width regulations, vegetation type requirements, and timing restrictions on soil tillage. Key data gaps identified include long-term monitoring of metabolite accumulation, ecotoxicological studies on local invertebrate species, and economic cost–benefit analyses of buffer strip management.

title: Combined effects of imidacloprid and temperature increase on Baetis rhodani nymph survival and emergence timing
abstract: Laboratory experiments assessed whether elevated temperature (ambient +3°C) interacted with sublethal imidacloprid exposure (0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5 µg/L) to alter survival and adult emergence timing of Baetis rhodani nymphs. A full factorial design with four temperature × four concentration combinations was replicated six times. Temperature alone at +3°C above ambient (16°C base) did not significantly reduce survival but advanced median emergence by 4.1 days. Imidacloprid at 0.5 µg/L reduced survival to 61% at ambient temperature and to 48% at elevated temperature, indicating a statistically significant but less-than-additive interaction (ANOVA interaction term F = 4.2, p = 0.04). Emergence timing was disrupted most severely in the combined treatment, with 23% of individuals failing to emerge within the observation window. Sublethal feeding inhibition was recorded at 0.1 µg/L in both temperature conditions. Results suggest climate warming may modestly amplify neonicotinoid toxicity to mayfly nymphs, with potential consequences for adult population synchrony.

title: Combined effects of repeated glyphosate and acetochlor applications on soil dehydrogenase and urease activities in a long-term maize monoculture
abstract: Soil enzyme activities were monitored over six years (2000–2005) in a replicated block trial at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station, where continuous maize was grown under four herbicide regimes: no herbicide, glyphosate only (0.9 kg a.i. ha⁻¹), acetochlor only (2.0 kg a.i. ha⁻¹), and a glyphosate–acetochlor tank mix. Dehydrogenase activity (TTC reduction method) and urease activity (urea hydrolysis colorimetric assay) were measured in early spring and at mid-season (BBCH 32–35 of maize). By year four, dehydrogenase activity in the combined treatment was 18–31% lower than the no-herbicide control in mid-season samples, while the glyphosate-only treatment showed a 12–19% reduction. Urease showed smaller and less consistent effects. Year-to-year variability was high, partly explained by annual precipitation differences (r² = 0.41 for dehydrogenase vs. May–June rainfall). Principal component analysis of the full enzyme dataset separated the combined-treatment plots from controls along PC1 (explaining 38% of variance) in years 5 and 6.

title: Phytoestrogen content of red clover-dominant hay rations and plasma 17β-estradiol concentrations in cycling Holstein cows
abstract: Red clover (Trifolium pratense) is widely used in Central European cattle rations but contains substantial quantities of formononetin and biochanin A, both precursors to the potent phytoestrogen equol. This study measured phytoestrogen concentrations in 24 hay samples collected from farms in Vojvodina and correlated them with plasma 17β-estradiol, LH, and progesterone measured by radioimmunoassay in 48 Holstein cows across two consecutive oestrous cycles. Hay samples contained formononetin at 2.1–18.4 mg/kg DM. Cows consuming rations with formononetin above 10 mg/kg DM showed a 23% reduction in peak LH amplitude at the preovulatory surge (p < 0.01) and a tendency toward lengthened inter-oestrous intervals (mean 22.4 vs. 20.8 days; p = 0.07). Progesterone profiles in the mid-luteal phase were not significantly affected. Results indicate that even moderate dietary phytoestrogen loads can blunt the gonadotropin surge without abolishing cyclicity, which has practical implications for insemination timing on farms relying heavily on legume-rich forage.

title: Zearalenone contamination of maize silage in northern Serbia: occurrence, seasonal variation, and estimated daily intake by dairy cows
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEN) is a Fusarium-derived mycotoxin with well-documented estrogenic activity. This survey assessed ZEN occurrence in 112 maize silage samples collected quarterly over two years (2009–2010) from 28 commercial dairy farms across Vojvodina. HPLC-FLD analysis detected ZEN in 74% of samples, with concentrations ranging from below the limit of quantification (0.05 mg/kg DM) to 3.8 mg/kg DM. Mean contamination was highest in samples collected after the wet autumn of 2009 (0.91 mg/kg DM) compared with the drier season (0.31 mg/kg DM). Estimated daily ZEN intake exceeded the provisional EU guidance value for dairy cows (0.5 mg/day) in 31% of farm–season combinations, assuming a silage inclusion of 20 kg/day. Farm size, silo type, and compaction method were identified as significant predictors of contamination level using logistic regression. The data provide a regional baseline for risk assessment and suggest that aerobic spoilage during feedout is a primary contamination driver.

title: Effects of sub-chronic dietary zearalenone exposure on progesterone and estradiol profiles in prepubertal heifers
abstract: The sensitivity of prepubertal animals to estrogenic mycotoxins may exceed that of adult cows because of lower endogenous estradiol concentrations. Twelve prepubertal Simmental heifers (7–8 months old, mean BW 195 kg) were allocated to control and ZEN-exposed groups (n = 6 each) in a 70-day feeding trial. The ZEN group received maize grain spiked to achieve a daily intake of 1.2 mg ZEN/animal. Blood was collected twice weekly for progesterone and estradiol-17β by ELISA, and vaginal cytology was assessed weekly. ZEN-exposed heifers showed earlier onset of vaginal cornification (mean 38 vs. 52 days post-trial start; p < 0.05) and had elevated estradiol concentrations throughout weeks 3–8 (mean 14.2 vs. 9.1 pg/mL; p < 0.01). Progesterone profiles suggested premature luteal activity in 4 of 6 ZEN heifers. Vulvar swelling was observed in 3 animals. Results confirm that 1.2 mg/day ZEN is sufficient to advance pseudo-puberty indicators in Simmental heifers.

title: Field survey of α-zearalenol and β-zearalenol in urine of dairy cows on farms with documented zearalenone-contaminated silage
abstract: Alpha-zearalenol (α-ZOL) is the primary hepatic metabolite of ZEN in cattle and possesses higher uterotrophic potency than the parent compound. This field study recruited 14 dairy farms in Vojvodina where silage ZEN had been confirmed above 0.5 mg/kg DM in the preceding survey season. Spot urine samples were collected from 168 cows (12 per farm) during mid-lactation and analysed for ZEN, α-ZOL, and β-ZOL by LC-MS/MS. α-ZOL was the predominant urinary form (median 4.7 ng/mL), detected in 91% of samples. β-ZOL was detected in 64% of samples at lower concentrations (median 1.1 ng/mL). Free ZEN was detected in only 28% of samples, confirming efficient hepatic conversion. Urinary α-ZOL concentration was positively correlated with silage ZEN content (r = 0.61; p < 0.001) and inversely correlated with milk yield of the previous 30 days (r = –0.29; p = 0.02). These data validate urinary α-ZOL as a practical biomarker for ZEN exposure in field settings.

title: Thyroid hormone status in dairy cows chronically exposed to combined zearalenone and phytoestrogen loads: a cross-sectional farm study
abstract: Endocrine disruption in cattle is rarely limited to the reproductive axis; thyroid function may also be perturbed by estrogenic compounds through feedback interference at the pituitary. In a cross-sectional study conducted on 20 commercial farms in Vojvodina, 200 Holstein-Friesian cows in their second or third lactation were sampled for total T3, total T4, TSH, estradiol-17β, and urinary α-ZOL. Feed samples were analysed for ZEN and total isoflavone content. Farms were categorised as low-exposure (ZEN < 0.3 mg/kg DM and isoflavones < 100 mg/kg DM; n = 10) or high-exposure (both above threshold; n = 10). Cows on high-exposure farms had lower total T4 (mean 42.3 vs. 55.8 nmol/L; p < 0.001) and higher TSH (mean 3.1 vs. 2.2 mIU/L; p < 0.01), consistent with subclinical hypothyroid tendency. Total T3 was not significantly different. Estradiol and α-ZOL concentrations mediated the TSH association in path analysis (standardised indirect effect = 0.41). Thyroid monitoring may be a valuable adjunct to reproductive assessment in high-risk herds.

title: Endocrine-disrupting compounds in bovine reproduction: feed sources, metabolism, and hormone pathway interactions
abstract: This book chapter reviews the major classes of endocrine-disrupting compounds (EDCs) encountered in European cattle feeding systems—mycotoxins, phytoestrogens, and agrochemical residues—and synthesises current knowledge on their uptake, hepatic biotransformation, and effects on the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal and hypothalamo-pituitary-thyroid axes. Special attention is given to Fusarium mycotoxins (zearalenone and its metabolites) and the Trifolium and Medicago phytoestrogen families because they consistently reach biologically relevant concentrations in commercially realistic diets. The chapter discusses epidemiological evidence from field surveys alongside experimental feeding trial data, evaluates biomonitoring approaches (blood, urine, milk), and identifies gaps in dose-response relationships at sub-regulatory exposure levels. The authors conclude that additive estrogenic burden—not single-compound exceedances—most reliably predicts reproductive impairment in field populations and call for cumulative risk assessment frameworks adapted to ruminant physiology.

title: Modelling fermentation kinetics in maize silage using logistic equations fitted to organic acid accumulation data
abstract: Fermentation kinetics of lactic and acetic acid accumulation in maize silage were described using modified logistic models fitted to time-series data (days 1, 3, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90) from a four-treatment experiment combining two DM levels (28%, 35%) and two inoculant regimes (uninoculated, L. buchneri). The modified Richards growth function provided superior fit over simple logistic equations for lactic acid in heterofermentative-inoculated treatments (R²≥0.987 vs. 0.961). Rate constants for lactic acid accumulation were highest in the first 7 days regardless of treatment; acetic acid accumulation rate constants were greater under heterofermentative inoculation particularly between days 14 and 60. Maximum asymptote estimates differed by DM level for acetic acid but not for lactic acid. Residual standard errors were below 1.8 g kg⁻¹ DM for all models. The study provides parameter estimates that can seed simulation tools for on-farm fermentation prediction.

title: Residence Time Distribution Analysis in a Packed-Bed Microreactor Loaded with Sulfonated SBA-15 for Oleic Acid Esterification
abstract: Accurate characterisation of flow behaviour in packed-bed microreactors is a prerequisite for reliable kinetic modelling, yet residence time distribution (RTD) data for catalyst-packed capillary systems at industrially relevant flow rates are sparse. In this study, a borosilicate capillary microreactor (inner diameter 1.0 mm, bed length 12 cm) packed with sulfonated SBA-15 was characterised using a pulse injection of tracer dye monitored by inline UV-Vis absorbance at three volumetric flow rates (0.05, 0.20, and 0.50 mL/min) and two temperatures (60 °C and 80 °C). Axial dispersion coefficients were extracted by fitting the axial dispersion model to the E-curves, yielding Péclet numbers between 18 and 47 across the tested conditions. Conversion of oleic acid with methanol (molar ratio 1:5) reached 91.4 % at 80 °C and 0.05 mL/min after 4 h on-stream. Comparison of the experimental RTD data with an ideal plug-flow assumption showed that neglecting dispersion overestimates conversion by up to 6.2 percentage points at the highest flow rate, emphasising the need for RTD-corrected kinetic evaluation in microreactor studies.

title: Deactivation Kinetics of a Zeolite-Beta Solid Acid Catalyst During Continuous Transesterification of Sunflower Oil in a Microreactor
abstract: Zeolite-Beta in its proton form (H-BEA, Si/Al = 25) was evaluated as a solid acid catalyst for the transesterification of refined sunflower oil with methanol at 150 °C and 10 bar in a stainless-steel tubular microreactor (0.8 mm i.d., 20 cm length). Experiments were conducted at a fixed methanol-to-oil molar ratio of 12:1 over a 72-hour continuous run to capture deactivation behaviour. Fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) yield declined from an initial 84.3 % to 51.7 % by the end of the run. Characterisation of spent catalyst by N₂ physisorption, NH₃-TPD, and TGA identified progressive pore blocking by glycerol oligomers and partial dealumination as co-responsible deactivation mechanisms, accounting for approximately 60 % and 40 % of Brønsted acid site loss, respectively. A power-law deactivation model with an order of 1.4 fitted the on-stream activity data with R² = 0.97. A partial regeneration protocol (calcination at 450 °C, 3 h) restored FAME yield to 76 % of the fresh-catalyst value after one cycle. The results provide quantitative parameters useful for scheduling regeneration intervals in scaled-up continuous processes.

title: Effect of Water Content on the Activity and Stability of a Sulfated Zirconia Catalyst in the Esterification of Acetic Acid with n-Butanol Under Continuous-Flow Conditions
abstract: Water generated in situ during esterification is widely cited as a catalyst inhibitor for solid acids, but the quantitative relationship between water concentration, reaction rate, and long-term catalyst stability in continuous-flow systems has not been well documented for sulfated zirconia. This study systematically varied the initial water content of the feed (0, 2, 5, and 10 wt%) in the esterification of acetic acid with n-butanol over sulfated zirconia (S-ZrO₂, 210 m² g⁻¹) in a PTFE capillary microreactor at 100 °C and atmospheric pressure. At 0 wt% added water and a residence time of 8 min, n-butyl acetate yield was 73.1 %. Introducing 5 wt% water reduced initial yield to 58.4 % and accelerated the rate of deactivation by a factor of 2.3 compared to the dry feed case over a 24-hour run. Langmuir–Hinshelwood kinetic parameters incorporating competitive water adsorption were estimated and are reported. ICP-OES analysis of the reactor effluent confirmed sulfate leaching rates below 0.3 mg L⁻¹ under all conditions tested, indicating that leaching was not the primary cause of deactivation at the timescales studied.

title: Characterisation of compressible cakes formed from cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil wax precipitates
abstract: Cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil from Styrian varieties contains 0.6–1.4 % w/w wax precipitate after winterisation at 4 °C for 48 h. Dead-end filtration of the wax suspension through a 5-µm polypropylene membrane at 0.05–0.40 MPa was performed to characterise cake compressibility. The compressibility exponent was 0.74, substantially higher than values reported for mineral bleaching-earth cakes, reflecting the soft, deformable nature of wax crystals. Addition of 0.5 % w/w perlite as a filter body reduced the compressibility exponent to 0.52 and increased throughput per unit area by 35 % at 0.2 MPa. Particle size and morphology of wax crystals before and after perlite addition were characterised by laser diffraction and optical microscopy. Temperature sensitivity of the wax cake was pronounced; a 3 °C rise from the target holding temperature roughly halved the cake resistance. Practical recommendations for winterisation–filtration coupling in small-scale pumpkin oil production are discussed.

title: Safety Stock Calculation Under Demand Variance Shifts: A Markov-Modulated Approach
abstract: This paper examines safety stock dimensioning when demand variance shifts between regimes, a situation common in consumer goods distribution. A discrete-time inventory model is formulated in which the demand process is governed by a two-state Markov chain, with empirically estimated transition probabilities derived from four years of weekly sales data for a regional food distributor in Vojvodina. The model computes reorder points that limit stockout probability to at most 2% per replenishment cycle in each regime. Numerical experiments compare the Markov-modulated policy against three stationary benchmarks: the square-root formula, the normal approximation, and a bootstrap method. The Markov-modulated approach reduces average on-hand inventory by 11–18% relative to the most conservative benchmark while maintaining the target service level. Sensitivity analysis shows that the gain is largest when inter-regime transition is infrequent and demand coefficient of variation exceeds 0.4. The paper also quantifies the cost of misspecifying the regime transition probability and identifies a robust parameter range.

title: Decomposition Heuristics for Multi-Echelon Inventory Networks with Stochastic Lead Times
abstract: Multi-echelon inventory systems with stochastic lead times are difficult to optimise jointly because the state space grows exponentially with the number of echelons. This study proposes a decomposition heuristic that treats each echelon as an approximately independent (s, S) system and propagates demand statistics downstream using moment-matching. The heuristic is tested on a set of 120 artificially generated three-echelon networks with 4–12 stocking locations per echelon and lead time coefficients of variation between 0.1 and 0.6. Optimal solutions obtained by exhaustive dynamic programming on small instances serve as a benchmark; the heuristic achieves costs within 4.3% of optimum on average and requires less than 0.8 seconds of CPU time per instance. Two real distribution networks from the Central European food sector are used as illustrative cases. The decomposition structure is shown to remain effective when downstream demand is negatively autocorrelated, which is frequently observed in retail data.

title: Estimating Non-Stationary Demand Distributions for Seasonal Products Using State-Space Models
abstract: Accurate demand distribution estimation is a prerequisite for any inventory optimisation procedure when seasonality is pronounced. This paper applies a local-level state-space model with time-varying variance to weekly point-of-sale data covering 36 seasonal SKUs from a pharmaceutical wholesaler operating across Serbia and Croatia, spanning 2009–2012. The Kalman filter is used for online parameter updating, and the resulting predictive distributions are compared to three alternatives: Holt-Winters exponential smoothing with fixed variance, a SARIMA model, and a kernel density estimator applied to a rolling window. Forecast accuracy is evaluated by continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) and by empirical coverage of 80% and 95% prediction intervals. The state-space model achieves CRPS reductions of 8–14% over the next-best method for high-seasonality SKUs. Inventory simulations driven by the estimated distributions show that state-space-based reorder points produce 15% lower average holding costs than Holt-Winters-based points for the same 95% cycle service level target.

title: Reorder Point Policies for Intermittent Demand: Comparison of Croston's Method, TSB, and Bootstrapping in a Spare-Parts Warehouse
abstract: Spare-parts management is complicated by intermittent demand, in which many periods record zero demand and occasional large orders occur irregularly. This study benchmarks three demand modelling approaches—Croston's method, the Teunter–Syntetos–Babai (TSB) modification, and empirical bootstrapping—for setting reorder points in a (R, s, Q) periodic review system. Data come from a machinery-repair workshop in Novi Sad covering 214 active spare-part SKUs over a 48-month observation window. Service level targets are set at 90% and 95% fill rate per replenishment cycle. Bootstrap-based policies produce fill rates closest to their targets, overshooting by on average 0.8 percentage points compared to 2.1 for TSB and 3.4 for Croston. However, bootstrapping requires substantially larger safety stocks, resulting in 22% higher average holding costs than TSB. A segmentation rule based on coefficient of variation of inter-demand intervals is proposed to guide practitioners in selecting the appropriate method by SKU category.

title: Warehouse Location and Safety Stock Joint Optimisation in a Two-Echelon Distribution Network
abstract: Decisions on warehouse location and safety stock levels interact because the number and placement of stocking locations affects demand pooling and thus the variance seen at each node. This paper formulates a mixed-integer nonlinear programme (MINLP) that simultaneously selects warehouse locations from a candidate set and assigns safety stocks to minimise total expected cost—comprising holding, shortage, and facility fixed costs—subject to a target aggregate fill rate across all retail customers. The demand at each retail node is modelled as an independent normal process with estimated mean and variance. A Lagrangian relaxation procedure is developed to obtain lower bounds, and a greedy improvement heuristic provides feasible upper bounds; the optimality gap is below 3% for all 60 test instances. Applied to a hypothetical three-warehouse reconfiguration scenario for a consumer electronics distributor in the Western Balkans, the method identifies a layout that reduces total annual cost by approximately €140,000 relative to the existing network while maintaining a 97% fill rate.
venue: Logistics and Operations Management Quarterly

title: Simulation-Based Evaluation of Demand-Driven Replenishment in a Regional Pharmaceutical Supply Chain
abstract: Demand-driven replenishment (DDR) uses actual downstream consumption signals rather than forecasts to trigger restocking. This paper implements a discrete-event simulation model in AnyLogic to compare DDR against a forecast-based (s, Q) policy in a three-tier pharmaceutical distribution chain comprising one central warehouse, two regional depots, and 18 pharmacies in the Vojvodina region. The simulation is calibrated using 24 months of transaction data provided by a distribution operator. Under DDR, stockouts at pharmacy level decrease from 3.7% to 1.4% of demand cycles, and total system inventory drops by 19% on average across all modelled SKUs. These gains are most pronounced for slow-moving drugs with high demand variability. The paper also tests the sensitivity of DDR performance to upstream replenishment lead-time variability, finding that DDR advantages erode when central-warehouse lead times exceed 10 days with a coefficient of variation above 0.5. Model validation is performed against a held-out six-month period.

title: Stochastic Modelling of Perishable Inventory with Age-Dependent Demand Rates
abstract: Perishable products pose an additional complexity for inventory models because unsold units deteriorate and must eventually be discarded, creating a trade-off between freshness, holding cost, and waste. This paper extends the classic continuous-review perishable inventory model by making the customer demand rate a function of remaining shelf life, motivated by empirical observations from a fresh food retailer showing that demand for a product drops sharply in the final 20% of its shelf life. The model is formulated as a continuous-time Markov chain with a finite state space defined by stock age. Stationary distributions are derived analytically for small state spaces and numerically via matrix-geometric methods for larger ones. Comparative experiments using scanner data from a supermarket in Novi Sad covering 11 fresh-produce SKUs over 52 weeks show that age-dependent policies reduce waste by 26% and improve net margin by 4.1 percentage points relative to age-independent reorder policies, at equivalent service levels.

title: Demand-Driven Replenishment Under Non-Stationary Demand: A Rolling-Horizon Optimisation Framework
abstract: In environments where demand distributions change over the planning horizon—due to product lifecycle effects, economic cycles, or market entry of substitutes—static replenishment parameters become suboptimal. This paper proposes a rolling-horizon framework that re-estimates demand distribution parameters at each review epoch using a sliding data window and recomputes reorder points and order quantities by solving a single-period stochastic programme. The approach is implemented and tested on simulation models of a five-echelon consumer goods network. Three window lengths (4, 8, and 16 weeks) and two update frequencies (weekly and biweekly) are compared across 500 Monte Carlo replications per configuration. Results show that an 8-week window with weekly updates achieves the best balance between responsiveness and parameter stability, reducing inventory investment by 13% relative to a fixed-parameter baseline while keeping backorder rates below 2%. The framework is particularly effective when demand trends shift more than once per quarter.

title: Inventory Positioning in a Cross-Docking Network Under Stochastic Demand and Uncertain Consolidation Times
abstract: Cross-docking reduces handling costs but shifts uncertainty from storage to consolidation timing, creating inventory positioning problems that standard warehouse models do not capture. This paper analyses a hub-and-spoke cross-docking network with four consolidation hubs and 32 destination routes. Consolidation time is modelled as a random variable with an empirically fitted log-normal distribution, estimated from GPS tracking records of a logistics provider operating in the Pannonian region. A stochastic programming model determines the quantity to hold as pre-positioned buffer stock at each hub to meet a given delivery reliability target under joint demand and consolidation-time uncertainty. The model is solved by sample average approximation using 1,000 demand-time scenarios. Results indicate that pre-positioning 15–20% of average daily volume as buffer stock achieves 97% on-time delivery, compared to 89% without pre-positioning under identical operating conditions. The effect of hub count on required buffer levels is also characterised.

title: Adaptive (s, S) Policies for Slow-Moving Industrial Spare Parts Under Compound Poisson Demand
abstract: Slow-moving spare parts with lumpy demand are frequently managed with fixed (s, S) policies calibrated at installation, but machinery usage patterns and failure rates drift over time, making static calibration increasingly inaccurate. This paper proposes an adaptive variant in which the reorder point s and order-up-to level S are updated periodically using a Bayesian model that treats the Poisson arrival rate and compounding distribution parameters as random variables with conjugate priors. The updating procedure uses warranty claim records and maintenance logs as auxiliary information alongside stockroom transaction data. The method is validated on 63 SKUs from two manufacturing firms in the Novi Sad industrial zone, covering a 36-month period. Adaptive policies reduce holding costs by 17% and emergency procurement events by 42% compared to a fixed (s, S) baseline recalibrated only annually. Computational requirements are modest enough for implementation on a standard ERP platform without specialised hardware.

title: Sensitivity of Multi-Echelon Inventory Costs to Demand Distribution Misspecification: A Simulation Study
abstract: Practitioners often assume normal or Poisson demand distributions for tractability, but real demand data frequently exhibit heavier tails, bimodality, or zero inflation. This paper investigates the cost consequences of such misspecification in a three-echelon distribution network through a systematic simulation experiment. Six true generating distributions—normal, log-normal, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson, Student-t with 4 degrees of freedom, and a two-component mixture normal—are paired with three assumed distributions used for policy computation: normal, Poisson, and empirical bootstrap. Each combination is replicated 2,000 times over a 52-week horizon. Total system cost inflation due to misspecification ranges from negligible (under 1%) for log-normal true demand assumed normal, to over 34% for Student-t true demand assumed Poisson, primarily through unplanned backorders. Bootstrap-based policy computation is the most robust across all true distributions, with maximum cost inflation of 8.2%. Recommendations for distribution selection based on readily observable demand statistics (kurtosis, zero fraction) are provided.

title: Prevalence and serotype distribution of Listeria monocytogenes in ready-to-eat fermented sausages from retail outlets in Vojvodina
abstract: A cross-sectional survey was conducted across 18 retail outlets in the Vojvodina region between 2012 and 2013 to determine the prevalence and serotype distribution of Listeria monocytogenes in ready-to-eat fermented sausages. A total of 214 product samples were collected and analysed according to ISO 11290-1. L. monocytogenes was detected in 27 samples (12.6%), with serotype 1/2a accounting for 59% of isolates and serotype 4b for 22%. Water activity and pH were measured for each product; no significant correlation was found between water activity in the range 0.87–0.93 and contamination probability. Isolates were further typed by PFGE using AscI and ApaI restriction enzymes, yielding 14 distinct pulsotypes. Clustering analysis identified two dominant pulsotype groups potentially linked to a shared upstream supplier. The findings indicate that serotype 1/2a strains circulating in this region show considerable genotypic diversity, complicating source attribution from retail data alone. Results were compared with surveillance data from Croatia and Hungary to assess regional patterns.

title: Environmental monitoring for Listeria spp. in two small-scale cooked meat processing plants: sampling site selection and detection frequency
abstract: Environmental monitoring programmes (EMPs) were established over a 12-month period in two small-scale cooked meat processing facilities in northern Serbia. A total of 680 environmental swab samples were collected from 34 defined sampling sites, including drains, slicer surfaces, conveyor belts, wall–floor junctions, and refrigeration units. Listeria spp. were detected at a frequency of 18.4% across all sites; L. monocytogenes was confirmed in 6.9% of samples. Drain and slicer niches exhibited the highest positivity rates (41% and 29%, respectively). Seasonal variation was assessed, and a statistically significant increase in positive findings was observed during summer months in one facility (p < 0.05, Fisher's exact test). The study demonstrates that generic EMP designs commonly used by small processors may underrepresent harborage sites located in drainage infrastructure. Recommended minimum sampling frequencies and site categories are discussed in the context of Serbian national food safety legislation.

title: Biofilm-forming capacity and sanitiser tolerance of Listeria monocytogenes isolates recovered from processing environments: phenotypic characterisation
abstract: Fifty-two L. monocytogenes isolates recovered from two Serbian ready-to-eat meat processing environments between 2015 and 2016 were assessed for biofilm-forming capacity using the microtitre plate crystal violet assay at 20 °C and 37 °C. Isolates were classified as strong, moderate, or weak biofilm formers; 34.6% were strong formers at 20 °C. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) and minimum bactericidal concentrations (MBCs) were determined for benzalkonium chloride (BAC) and sodium hypochlorite. Reduced susceptibility to BAC (MIC ≥ 10 µg/mL) was observed in 28.8% of isolates. A significant positive association was found between strong biofilm formation and reduced BAC susceptibility (OR 4.2; 95% CI 1.3–13.6). Tolerance to hypochlorite was not associated with biofilm-forming capacity. The data suggest that phenotypic sanitiser tolerance may contribute to persistence independent of harborage physical structure alone, and that BAC-based sanitisers require periodic rotation in facilities where tolerant strains have been detected.

title: Genomic determinants of harborage persistence in Listeria monocytogenes: a comparative analysis of environmental and product isolates from ready-to-eat meat facilities
abstract: This study compared the genomic content of 74 L. monocytogenes isolates from processing environments (n = 48) and finished product samples (n = 26) collected across three Serbian ready-to-eat meat facilities over three years. Pan-genome analysis identified 47 accessory genes significantly enriched in environmental isolates (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05), including stress-response loci associated with osmotolerance (opuCA cluster), cold adaptation (cspD), and biofilm matrix production (epsB-epsE). Product isolates were genetically more diverse and less likely to belong to persistent environmental clonal clusters. Isolates from persistent clusters (defined as ≤ 10 core-genome SNPs over ≥ 18 months) were more likely to carry the full inlA allele than non-persistent isolates (p = 0.02). No plasmid-encoded resistance determinants were found. Results indicate that a subset of accessory genetic content distinguishes isolates adapted to processing environments from transient contaminants, which has practical implications for risk-based prioritisation during root-cause investigation.

title: Evaluation of ATP bioluminescence and conventional swabbing for real-time verification of cleaning and disinfection efficacy against Listeria monocytogenes in a slicing environment
abstract: A paired comparison study was carried out in a controlled pilot slicing room at FINS over eight weeks to evaluate the diagnostic agreement between ATP bioluminescence measurements and conventional culture-based swabbing for verification of cleaning and disinfection procedures targeting L. monocytogenes. Surfaces were inoculated with a three-strain cocktail (ST1, ST9, ST121) at a target level of approximately 4 log CFU/cm² and subjected to three cleaning-and-disinfection protocols: hypochlorite-based (1000 ppm), peracetic acid-based (0.2%), and a sequential foam-and-rinse procedure. A total of 320 paired samples were collected. ATP thresholds at ≤ 10 RLU and ≤ 25 RLU were evaluated against culture-confirmed positivity; sensitivity was 61% and 48%, specificity 84% and 91%, respectively. No single ATP threshold reliably excluded L. monocytogenes contamination across all surface types tested. Results indicate that ATP bioluminescence is insufficient as a standalone verification tool for listerial contamination in slicing environments and should be used in conjunction with culture-based microbiological testing.

title: Harmonised sampling strategies for Listeria monocytogenes environmental monitoring in small and medium-sized ready-to-eat meat processors: a framework for Southeastern Europe
abstract: Ready-to-eat meat processors in Southeastern Europe are predominantly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with limited in-house microbiological capacity, making standardised environmental monitoring frameworks particularly valuable. This book chapter reviews published environmental monitoring data from Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, drawing on studies published between 2010 and 2023. The authors synthesise guidance on minimum sampling site categories, sampling frequencies stratified by facility type and risk tier, corrective action triggers, and documentation requirements compatible with existing HACCP obligations under regional food safety legislation. Special attention is given to drain monitoring, the use of sponge versus swab collection methods, and the integration of WGS data into trend analysis for SME contexts. Practical decision trees are provided for corrective action when L. monocytogenes is detected at indicator sites versus post-lethality exposed product contact surfaces. The chapter is intended as a technical reference for both food safety practitioners and competent authority inspectors.

title: Temporal dynamics of Listeria monocytogenes clonal diversity in a single ready-to-eat meat facility over ten years: WGS surveillance dataset and phylogenetic overview
abstract: A longitudinal WGS dataset is presented for 112 L. monocytogenes isolates collected from a single Serbian ready-to-eat cooked meat processing facility between 2015 and 2024, representing the most extensive single-site time series for the species in the Western Balkans region to date. Isolates span five sequence types (ST1, ST9, ST121, ST204, ST388) and show a pattern of successive clonal replacement interspersed with multi-year persistence events. The dominant ST9 harborage clone persisted from 2015 to 2019 before being displaced following facility remediation; an ST121 clone emerged in 2021 and persisted until 2023. Recombination analysis using ClonalFrameML identified six chromosomal regions under elevated substitution rates within the persistent ST9 clone, including regions overlapping stress response and cell wall biosynthesis loci. This preprint presents the raw phylogenetic analysis and annotated genome assemblies as a community resource. Full manuscript submission is planned for 2026.

title: Seroprevalence of Toxoplasma gondii in backyard pigs in the South Bačka and Srem districts of Vojvodina
abstract: A cross-sectional serological survey was conducted on 312 backyard pigs from 47 family farms in the South Bačka and Srem districts during the autumn slaughter season of 2009. Blood samples were tested using a commercial ELISA kit validated for porcine serum. Overall seroprevalence was 28.5% (95% CI: 23.5–34.0%), with significantly higher rates on farms keeping outdoor animals (34.1%) compared with fully confined systems (12.7%). Logistic regression identified access to outdoor areas (OR 3.6), presence of cats on the farm (OR 4.1), and farm size fewer than five pigs (OR 2.2) as statistically significant risk factors. Age of the animal was a strong predictor, with pigs older than 12 months showing seroprevalence of 41.3% versus 14.8% in younger animals. The findings suggest that backyard production systems common in Vojvodina present a relevant source of T. gondii-infected pork for direct household consumption.

title: Serological evidence of Toxoplasma gondii infection in sheep and goats on smallholder farms in northern Vojvodina
abstract: Between March and November 2011, serum samples were collected from 218 sheep and 94 goats on 38 smallholder farms across northern Vojvodina. The modified agglutination test (MAT) was employed with a cut-off titre of 1:25. Seroprevalence in sheep was 39.4% and in goats 31.9%. Multivariable logistic regression showed that access to shared pasture (OR 2.9), presence of free-roaming cats (OR 3.4), and sourcing replacement animals from multiple origins (OR 2.1) were independently associated with seropositivity. No statistically significant difference between breeds was detected after controlling for management system. The relatively high prevalence in sheep confirms this species as a significant reservoir in the region, with implications for human infection via undercooked meat and raw milk products. These data constitute a baseline for future longitudinal monitoring in small ruminant populations in the autonomous province.

title: Comparison of ELISA and modified agglutination test for detection of Toxoplasma gondii antibodies in pig serum: agreement and discordance analysis
abstract: Serum samples from 195 backyard pigs were tested in parallel by a commercial indirect ELISA and by MAT at dilutions of 1:25 and 1:50 to evaluate agreement between the two methods under field conditions typical of routine Vojvodina farm sampling. Sensitivity and specificity were estimated using Bayesian latent class analysis with no gold standard assumption. ELISA sensitivity was estimated at 91.4% (95% CI: 84.2–96.1%) and specificity at 96.8% (93.1–99.0%). MAT at 1:25 showed higher sensitivity (95.3%) but lower specificity (90.7%). Cohen's kappa between methods was 0.81. Discordant results (n = 24) were predominantly ELISA-negative, MAT-positive at low titres, suggesting that ELISA may miss low-titre chronic infections. Overall, both tests are appropriate for population-level surveys, but parallel testing is advisable for individual farm certification purposes given the economic implications of false negatives in pork traded locally.

title: Toxoplasma gondii in backyard livestock: epidemiological patterns and public health relevance in the Pannonian plain
abstract: This invited book chapter reviews epidemiological data on T. gondii in backyard pigs, sheep, and goats in the wider Pannonian plain region, synthesising published studies from Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia through 2017. The chapter covers seroprevalence estimates, predominant genotypes, risk factor profiles, and transmission pathways to human populations in rural settings. Particular attention is given to the role of home slaughter practices, the informal pork and cheese economy, and the absence of mandatory ante-mortem T. gondii testing for backyard-slaughtered animals under current Serbian and EU veterinary legislation. The chapter discusses gaps in surveillance infrastructure and argues for harmonised seromonitoring protocols across the region. Data tables compile 34 published surveys and 12 unpublished institutional reports obtained through personal communication with regional veterinary authorities.

title: Seroprevalence of Toxoplasma gondii in goats on organic and conventional smallholder farms: a comparative cross-sectional study from Vojvodina
abstract: Ninety-four goats from 18 certified organic farms and 112 goats from 21 matched conventional farms were sampled during the 2020 grazing season to compare T. gondii seroprevalence between production systems. All sera were tested by MAT at 1:25 and 1:50. Seroprevalence on organic farms (44.7%) was significantly higher than on conventional farms (27.7%, chi-square p = 0.006), a finding consistent with obligatory outdoor access and pasture-based feeding requirements of organic certification. Within organic farms, presence of wild felids documented in camera-trap records supplied by the operators was associated with further elevated odds of seropositivity (OR 2.6). Milk T. gondii DNA was tested by nested PCR in bulk tank samples from eight organic farms; two were positive, raising food safety questions about raw goat milk products, which are sold directly to consumers at local markets without heat treatment.

title: Awareness and behaviour of backyard pig farmers in Vojvodina regarding Toxoplasma gondii: results of a cross-sectional knowledge, attitude and practice survey
abstract: A face-to-face knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) survey was administered to 186 operators of backyard pig farms across six municipalities in Vojvodina in spring 2021. Respondents were predominantly male (71%), over 50 years old (58%), and operated farms with fewer than ten pigs. Correct identification of T. gondii as a zoonotic parasite was achieved by only 14.5% of respondents. Awareness of transmission via undercooked pork was low (22%), while 68% reported regular consumption of home-cured or raw pork products. Willingness to adopt recommended preventive measures was generally high (78%) once risk was explained, but correlated negatively with farm size and age of operator. Education level was the strongest positive predictor of correct knowledge (OR 4.3 per step increase in educational attainment). Findings highlight the need for targeted extension services and point-of-care informational materials delivered through local veterinary practitioners.

title: Longitudinal monitoring of Toxoplasma gondii seroconversion in a cohort of backyard pigs in Vojvodina: an 18-month follow-up study
abstract: A cohort of 124 seronegative weaned piglets from 22 backyard farms in Vojvodina was followed at six-month intervals over 18 months, with blood sampling and concurrent farm inspection at each visit. MAT was used at a 1:25 cut-off. Cumulative incidence of seroconversion was 29.0% by month 12 and 38.7% by month 18. Time-to-event analysis using a Cox proportional hazards model identified presence of more than one outdoor cat as the strongest predictor of early seroconversion (HR 3.1, 95% CI: 1.8–5.3), followed by feeding of kitchen waste containing raw meat (HR 2.4, 95% CI: 1.3–4.4). Seroconversion events clustered seasonally, with the highest incidence in April–June, coinciding with peak felid oocyst shedding documented through concurrent cat faecal sampling on the same farms. This is the first prospective cohort study of T. gondii seroconversion dynamics in backyard pigs in Serbia.

title: Seroprevalence and genotypic diversity of Toxoplasma gondii in Romanov and Merinolandschaf crossbred sheep in Vojvodina: preliminary data from an ongoing survey
abstract: Preliminary results are reported from an ongoing seroprevalence and genotyping survey targeting two commercially relevant sheep breeds introduced to Vojvodina farms in the past decade: Romanov crossbreeds (n = 89) and Merinolandschaf crossbreeds (n = 76). Blood samples collected between September 2024 and March 2026 were tested by MAT and ELISA. Seroprevalence was 42.7% in Romanov crosses and 36.8% in Merinolandschaf crosses, with no statistically significant breed effect after controlling for farm-level management. From seropositive animals available for slaughter inspection (n = 38), brain tissue was archived for ongoing PCR-RFLP genotyping; 21 samples have been processed to date, all yielding Type II genotype. These data extend the spatial and breed coverage of the existing Vojvodina T. gondii dataset. Full analysis including multilocus sequencing typing of divergent isolates is in progress.

title: Measurement Uncertainty in Radiated Emissions Testing of Class 1 Short-Range Devices Below 1 GHz
abstract: Quantifying measurement uncertainty in radiated emissions tests is essential for reproducible compliance assessment under the Radio Equipment Directive. This study applies the CISPR 16-4-2 framework to a set of twelve 868 MHz short-range devices tested on a 3 m open-area test site and a semi-anechoic chamber. Six uncertainty contributors are evaluated: antenna factor calibration, receiver bandwidth, cable impedance mismatch, site imperfections expressed as normalised site attenuation deviation, ambient noise floor, and device positioning repeatability. The combined expanded uncertainty (k=2) ranged from 3.8 dB to 6.1 dB depending on frequency and device category. Comparison of results between the two test environments showed systematic differences of up to 2.3 dB for horizontally polarised emissions, consistent with ground-plane reflection variations. A simplified uncertainty budget worksheet suited to laboratory accreditation audits is presented. The findings suggest that the standard 6 dB margin applied in many pre-compliance workflows is insufficient for devices operating near the regulatory limit.

title: Effect of Ground Plane Size on the Resonant Frequency of Planar Inverted-F Antennas for 2.4 GHz ISM Band Modules
abstract: Planar inverted-F antennas (PIFAs) are widely used in compact radio modules, yet the influence of finite ground plane dimensions on resonant frequency is often handled empirically. This study presents a systematic measurement campaign in which PIFA prototypes with a fixed radiating element geometry were soldered onto ground planes ranging from 20 mm × 20 mm to 100 mm × 60 mm in steps of 10 mm. Resonant frequency and bandwidth were extracted from S11 measurements using a calibrated vector network analyser. A shift of 84 MHz in resonant frequency was observed across the range of ground plane sizes studied. Three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation results using a finite integration technique solver showed agreement with measured resonant frequency within 1.5 % across all configurations. A dimensionless correction factor relating ground plane perimeter to resonant frequency offset is proposed and validated against an independent set of eight commercial module footprints. The results provide practical guidance for module integration engineers working with pre-certified radio subsystems.

title: Pre-Compliance Radiated Emissions Screening Using Near-Field Probe Arrays: Correlation with Far-Field OATS Measurements
abstract: This paper investigates the degree to which near-field emission maps acquired with a planar probe array can predict far-field radiated emissions measured at a 3 m open-area test site (OATS). Forty-eight printed circuit board assemblies representing five product categories were characterised using a custom 64-element magnetic probe array with 5 mm probe pitch at heights of 3 mm and 8 mm above the board surface. Near-field data were processed with an equivalent dipole model to extrapolate far-field values. The mean absolute error between predicted and measured peak emissions was 4.2 dB, with 90 % of predictions falling within ±7 dB of OATS reference measurements in the 30–300 MHz range. Accuracy degraded above 500 MHz, where near-field spatial aliasing became significant at the chosen probe pitch. The method reduced test preparation time by approximately 60 % compared to full OATS campaigns in an iterative design cycle. Limitations related to enclosure shielding effects and cable routing variability are discussed.

title: EMC Testing of LoRa End-Nodes Under the Radio Equipment Directive: A Practical Assessment of EN 301 489-1 Procedures
abstract: LoRa devices operating in the 868 MHz European sub-GHz band are subject to harmonised standard EN 301 489-1 under the Radio Equipment Directive. This paper documents a structured compliance assessment of fifteen commercial and prototype LoRa end-node designs tested for radiated emissions, radiated immunity, and conducted disturbances. Testing was conducted in a semi-anechoic chamber accredited to EN ISO/IEC 17025. Nine of fifteen devices exhibited radiated emissions exceeding the limit in the range 500–1000 MHz under worst-case payload and spreading factor combinations. A correlation between PCB layout quality metrics—specifically, return current path continuity and decoupling capacitor placement—and margin to the emission limit was observed. Immunity tests at 3 V/m field strength revealed functional degradation in four devices manifested as packet loss rates exceeding 10 %. The paper discusses how LoRa duty cycle restrictions interact with the quasi-peak detector integration time specified in the standard, a point of ambiguity that affects reproducibility across laboratories.

title: Characterisation of Ferrite Bead Impedance Under DC Bias and Signal Amplitude Conditions Relevant to Automotive EMC
abstract: Ferrite beads are routinely used on power supply lines to suppress conducted emissions, but their impedance characteristics are nonlinear functions of DC bias current and signal amplitude, factors that are often neglected in circuit simulation models. This study characterises twelve surface-mount ferrite bead types from four manufacturers across the frequency range 1 MHz–1 GHz under DC bias from 0 to 3 A and signal amplitudes from −20 dBm to +10 dBm. Measurements were performed with a four-port VNA using a custom bias tee fixture. At 2 A DC bias, resistive impedance at 100 MHz was reduced by 55–80 % relative to the zero-bias datasheet value depending on bead type. A Jiles–Atherton based macro-model is fitted to the measurement data and validated in SPICE simulation against measured insertion loss of a representative power supply EMC filter. The model predicts insertion loss within 2 dB across the measured frequency range under all bias conditions tested. Implications for automotive 12 V rail filter design are discussed.

title: Antenna Impedance Matching Optimisation for Bluetooth Low Energy Modules Integrated in Plastic Consumer Enclosures
abstract: Consumer electronic devices with Bluetooth Low Energy radios are commonly housed in plastic enclosures whose geometry and material dielectric properties influence the antenna impedance seen during product-level testing. This study examines how enclosure wall thickness (1–4 mm), material permittivity (εr = 2.6–4.1), and proximity to metallic internal components affect the impedance of a ceramic chip antenna at 2.44 GHz. Measurements were obtained for 48 enclosure and component proximity combinations using a fixture that reproduced defined internal layouts. Impedance magnitude varied by up to 28 Ω and phase by up to 41° across the configurations studied. A two-stage matching optimisation procedure is proposed: coarse adjustment using a fixed pi-network selected from a lookup table indexed by enclosure wall thickness and material class, followed by fine adjustment via a single tunable capacitor. Application of the procedure to four commercial product designs reduced mean reflection coefficient from −4.1 dB to −17.6 dB measured at the antenna port during standard regulatory testing.

title: Repeatability of Radiated Emissions Measurements in Small Semi-Anechoic Chambers: A Multi-Laboratory Study
abstract: Semi-anechoic chambers of 3 m and 5 m class are widely used in Serbian and regional accredited testing laboratories, yet systematic multi-laboratory repeatability data for these facilities remain scarce. This study organised a proficiency test involving five laboratories in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, each measuring radiated emissions from two identical reference radiators—a broadband comb generator and a stabilised 868 MHz transmitter—over the range 30 MHz to 1 GHz. Between-laboratory standard deviation ranged from 1.9 dB to 4.7 dB depending on frequency and polarisation, with the largest deviations observed below 80 MHz where chamber resonances are most significant. Within-laboratory repeatability standard deviation remained below 1.2 dB for all participants. The 5 m chambers showed a systematic 1.3 dB lower variability index than 3 m chambers across the full frequency range. The paper discusses causes of between-laboratory dispersion and proposes a standardised reference radiator procedure for routine verification of chamber performance between formal ISO 17025 audits.

title: Impact of USB 3.2 Spread-Spectrum Clocking on Radiated Emissions of 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Receivers in Collocated Radio Equipment
abstract: Spread-spectrum clocking is applied in USB 3.2 controllers to reduce peak radiated emissions, but the resulting broadened spectral skirt can raise the noise floor experienced by collocated 2.4 GHz radio receivers. This paper quantifies the degradation in Wi-Fi receive sensitivity caused by USB 3.2 conducted and radiated interference in a laptop-class platform where the USB controller and Wi-Fi module share a common ground plane. Receiver sensitivity degradation was measured as a function of USB cable routing, ground plane slot geometry, and spread-spectrum modulation depth (0.5 %, 1.0 %, 2.0 %). At 0.5 % modulation depth, sensitivity degradation at the most affected Wi-Fi channel was 3.8 dB. Increasing modulation depth to 2.0 % reduced peak emission levels by 6.1 dB but increased the noise floor across the full 2.4–2.484 GHz band by 2.3 dB, resulting in a net degradation of 1.1 dB in worst-case channel sensitivity. Mitigation measures assessed include USB cable ferrite sleeve impedance, common-mode choke placement, and via stitching around the USB differential pair routing.

title: Verification of Antenna Efficiency Extraction Methods for Electrically Small Antennas Using Reverberation Chamber and Wheeler Cap Techniques
abstract: Radiation efficiency is a key parameter for compact antennas in short-range devices, but measurement methods vary in accuracy and practical difficulty. This paper compares three efficiency extraction methods—Wheeler cap, reverberation chamber averaging, and gain-transfer with a reference antenna in a semi-anechoic chamber—applied to a set of ten electrically small antennas with maximum dimensions between 15 mm and 40 mm, covering frequencies from 433 MHz to 2.4 GHz. For each antenna, efficiency was extracted independently by all three methods. Mean absolute deviation between the reverberation chamber method and the Wheeler cap method was 1.4 dB, while both methods deviated from the gain-transfer reference by a mean of 2.1 dB and 2.8 dB respectively. Systematic overestimation by the Wheeler cap method in the presence of dielectric loading was identified as a primary source of discrepancy. Correction factors derived from the dataset are presented for each antenna class. The study provides quantitative guidance for laboratories that must select an efficiency measurement method based on available equipment.

title: Influence of Regulatory Interpretation Differences on Radio Equipment Directive Compliance Margins for Short-Range Devices: A Survey of Testing Practice in South-East Europe
abstract: The Radio Equipment Directive requires manufacturers to demonstrate compliance with essential requirements for radio spectrum use, but the harmonised standards and notified body interpretations leave room for procedural variation among testing laboratories. This paper reports findings from a structured survey of 22 accredited testing and notified body organisations in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, Croatia, and Bulgaria, covering procedures for worst-case test mode selection, antenna substitution, and declaration of conformity for multi-band devices. Significant procedural divergence was identified in three areas: selection of modulation scheme for peak emission tests (16 of 22 laboratories used a different default), treatment of antenna gain in equivalent isotropic radiated power calculations, and scope of immunity testing for devices combining active RFID with a secondary radio function. A summary of where regional interpretation differences create compliance margin uncertainty is provided, together with a set of recommended procedure clarifications submitted to the relevant standardisation working group. This work draws on test records from approximately 340 device assessments conducted between 2019 and 2024.
