title: Penetration Loss of Agricultural Greenhouse Structures at Sub-GHz Frequencies
abstract: Precision agriculture IoT systems often require radio links to pass through greenhouse structures whose aluminium frames, polycarbonate panels, and elevated humidity create attenuation conditions not well characterised in existing standards. Penetration loss was measured at 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz for three representative greenhouse wall and roof construction types: single-wall polycarbonate, double-wall polycarbonate, and glass with aluminium framing. Measurements were taken at 30 incidence angles between 0° and 70° in dry and wet surface conditions. Single-wall polycarbonate showed low penetration loss (2–4 dB) largely independent of frequency, while aluminium-framed glass panels exhibited 9–14 dB depending on frame density and incidence angle. Wet surfaces added 0.5–2.5 dB across all materials. A simple table of incidence-angle-dependent correction factors is derived for use in existing path-loss models, and its accuracy is validated against measurements from a commercial greenhouse IoT installation with 12 sensor nodes.

title: Sizing of lead-acid battery banks for rural off-grid PV installations in northern Serbia: a loss-of-load probability approach
abstract: The paper presents a deterministic iterative sizing procedure for lead-acid battery storage in stand-alone PV systems powering small rural loads in Vojvodina. Simulations were performed using hourly synthetic irradiance sequences generated from the clearness index distributions previously established for the Novi Sad site, combined with representative load profiles for three building categories: residential, irrigation pump shed, and livestock monitoring. The loss-of-load probability (LOLP) was used as the primary reliability index, with a design target of LOLP ≤ 0.01. Results show that required battery capacity varies between 2.1 and 4.8 days of average load, depending on season and load profile shape. Sensitivity analysis on battery depth-of-discharge limits (0.5–0.8) demonstrates a 15–30% spread in required nameplate capacity. The method is validated against twelve months of monitored data from three demonstration installations in the Bačka region. Discrepancies between simulated and measured LOLP are within 0.003 across all sites.

title: Comparison of diffuse irradiance decomposition models for a continental European lowland climate
abstract: Accurate separation of diffuse and beam irradiance components is essential for PV tilt-plane calculations. This work evaluates five widely referenced decomposition models — Erbs, Reindl, Skartveit-Olseth, Perez, and a locally recalibrated Orgill-Hollands variant — against a three-year dataset of simultaneous GHI and diffuse horizontal irradiance measurements from the department's outdoor station in Novi Sad, using a shading ring setup. Model performance is assessed via RMSE, MBE, and the 90th percentile of absolute error on an hourly basis. The locally recalibrated Orgill-Hollands model achieves the lowest RMSE of 28.4 W/m² and a near-zero MBE of −1.2 W/m². The Perez model performs comparably in summer but overestimates diffuse fraction by 8% under overcast winter conditions. The study recommends site-specific recalibration of correlation coefficients for the kt range 0.3–0.6, which is the most frequent regime in the region during autumn and spring. Recalibrated coefficients for the Pannonian Plain are provided.

title: Energy yield prediction for fixed-tilt PV arrays using temperature-corrected performance ratio: a 24-month field validation
abstract: This paper reports on a 24-month outdoor measurement campaign conducted at the Faculty of Technical Sciences test field to validate an energy yield prediction model that incorporates a temperature-corrected performance ratio (PR) rather than a fixed PR value. The test array consists of 3 kWp of polycrystalline silicon modules at 35° fixed tilt facing south. Module backsheet temperature was logged every five minutes alongside plane-of-array irradiance, AC output, and ambient temperature. The temperature correction reduces the mean absolute percentage error in monthly energy yield prediction from 6.8% (fixed PR = 0.78) to 2.9% (temperature-corrected PR). Shading and soiling losses were separately quantified: shading contributes 1.1% annual yield loss, and soiling contributes between 0.4% in rainy months and 2.3% in July–August. The study also compares three transposition models for converting GHI to plane-of-array irradiance and recommends the Hay-Davies model for the specific site geometry. Practical guidelines for designers are summarised in a design aid table.

title: Optimal tilt angle determination for off-grid PV panels under varying load seasonality in southern Pannonian conditions
abstract: The optimal tilt angle for a fixed PV panel depends on both the local solar resource and the temporal distribution of the load. This study formalises the relationship between load seasonality index and optimal tilt angle for stand-alone PV systems at a representative Pannonian Plain latitude of 45.3° N. Using twenty years of reconstructed hourly irradiance data derived from ERA5 reanalysis corrected with ground measurements, annual energy collection was simulated across tilt angles from 10° to 70° for four load archetypes: flat annual profile, summer-dominated irrigation, winter-dominated heating monitoring, and a bimodal agricultural load. The flat-profile optimum is 33°, consistent with the latitude-minus-12° rule, but winter-dominated loads shift the optimum to 52°, increasing winter energy collection by 11% relative to the flat-profile optimum at the cost of a 7% reduction in summer. A lookup table and a simple selection diagram are provided for practical use by installers without simulation tools.

title: Lithium iron phosphate versus absorbent glass mat lead-acid batteries for small stand-alone PV systems: a lifecycle cost comparison under Serbian grid-tariff conditions
abstract: The choice of battery technology for small off-grid PV systems (1–5 kWp) is increasingly contested between mature lead-acid variants and emerging lithium chemistries. This study performs a lifecycle cost analysis comparing absorbent glass mat (AGM) lead-acid and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries over a 20-year system horizon under Serbian conditions. Battery degradation was modelled using cycle-counting with depth-of-discharge correction for AGM and a capacity fade model calibrated to 500-cycle laboratory test data for LFP cells sourced from a European supplier. Replacement scheduling was derived from degradation models. At current procurement prices (2018 survey of Serbian and regional distributors), AGM achieves a lower levelised cost of stored energy (LCSE) of 0.19 EUR/kWh versus 0.24 EUR/kWh for LFP. Sensitivity analysis shows crossover occurs when LFP procurement prices fall below 280 EUR/kWh, a threshold projected to be reached within 4–6 years based on observed price trends. The study is accompanied by a spreadsheet tool for site-specific analysis.

title: Reliability metrics for stand-alone PV systems: a critical review of LOLP, LPSP, and EUE formulations in published sizing methodologies
abstract: Three reliability indices are predominantly used in stand-alone PV system sizing literature: loss-of-load probability (LOLP), loss of power supply probability (LPSP), and expected unmet energy (EUE). Despite widespread use, these indices are defined inconsistently across publications, leading to sizing outcomes that are not directly comparable. This review systematically collects 61 journal papers published between 2005 and 2021 and analyses the exact mathematical formulations employed. It finds that LOLP is computed at hourly time steps in 38 papers and at daily time steps in 19 papers, with the remainder using mixed or unstated resolutions; this alone produces sizing discrepancies of 10–25% in equivalent test cases. LPSP and EUE are frequently conflated. The paper proposes a harmonised set of definitions tied to a consistent temporal resolution and demonstrates their application using a common simulation dataset. Adoption of the proposed definitions is advocated to enable cross-study comparison.

title: Effect of battery state-of-health degradation on long-term LOLP in modelled off-grid PV systems
abstract: Most published sizing procedures for off-grid PV–battery systems treat battery capacity as fixed throughout the system lifetime, ignoring progressive capacity fade. This paper quantifies the error introduced by this assumption over a 10-year simulation horizon. An empirical capacity fade model, validated against laboratory cycling data for a commercially available LFP module, is integrated into an hourly stand-alone PV system simulator. Three sizing scenarios are compared: no-degradation assumption, end-of-life capacity assumption, and year-by-year degradation tracking. Results for a 200 Wh/day residential load profile show that the no-degradation design underestimates the required initial battery capacity by 18% to meet LOLP ≤ 0.01 over the full 10-year period. Conversely, the end-of-life assumption oversizes by 12%. The year-by-year approach provides the most accurate trajectory and is recommended for systems expected to operate more than five years without battery replacement. A correction factor chart is derived for designers who cannot run dynamic simulations.

title: Sizing sensitivity to irradiance dataset choice for small stand-alone PV systems: ERA5, PVGIS, and ground measurements compared
abstract: Designers of small off-grid PV systems in Serbia and surrounding countries commonly rely on publicly available irradiance datasets in the absence of local measurements. This paper quantifies how the choice between ERA5 reanalysis data, the PVGIS-SARAH2 product, and a ten-year local ground measurement series affects the resulting battery and PV array sizing for three representative loads at two sites in Vojvodina. Sizing is performed using the harmonised LOLP methodology proposed in earlier work by the first author. ERA5 data leads to undersizing of battery capacity by 8–14% relative to the ground-measurement baseline, while PVGIS-SARAH2 undersizes by 3–7%. Differences are most pronounced for winter-dominated loads. Applying the regional bias-correction factors previously published by the group reduces PVGIS-SARAH2 sizing error to below 2% and ERA5 sizing error to 4–6%. The paper concludes that uncorrected ERA5 data carries meaningful reliability risk for sizing exercises in the Pannonian region and recommends using PVGIS-SARAH2 with regional correction when ground data are unavailable.

title: A Tabu Search Approach for the Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing Problem with Hard Time Windows on Road Maintenance Networks
abstract: This paper presents a tabu search (TS) heuristic for scheduling maintenance crews across multiple depots on a regional road network. The test instances were derived from publicly available road segment data for Vojvodina, comprising 214 maintenance tasks distributed across six depot locations. Time windows were specified as four-hour intervals corresponding to low-traffic periods. The TS algorithm used a move-evaluation scheme based on segment-reinsertion and depot-reassignment operators, with a tenure list of 12 moves. Over 30 independent runs, the heuristic achieved solutions within 4.2% of a known lower bound obtained via LP relaxation. Total fleet travel distance was reduced by 18.3% compared to a nearest-neighbour baseline, while constraint violations fell to zero in all feasible instances. Computation times averaged 47 seconds on standard desktop hardware. The results suggest that moderate tabu tenure values outperform both short and long tenures in this problem class.

title: Modelling Maintenance Task Clustering for Geographically Dispersed Utility Networks Using K-Medoids Initialisation
abstract: Effective partitioning of maintenance tasks among depots is a prerequisite for tractable routing in large instances. This study evaluates three initialisation strategies—random assignment, nearest-depot assignment, and K-medoids clustering—as starting points for a variable neighbourhood search (VNS) on a synthetic benchmark set of 500 tasks across eight depots. Instances were generated using a spatial Poisson process calibrated to road density data from a 12,000 km² region in northern Serbia. K-medoids initialisation consistently produced better final solutions than the other two strategies, reducing total route cost by 9.1% on average across 15 benchmark groups. The paper also investigates how task density heterogeneity affects depot load balance, finding that uniform spatial distributions allow tighter workload constraints without significant cost penalties. Sensitivity analyses on time-window width (two to six hours) show a near-linear trade-off between fleet utilisation and feasibility rates.

title: Incorporating Skill Heterogeneity into Multi-Depot Routing for Road Infrastructure Repair Crews
abstract: Standard vehicle routing models assume homogeneous service capability across all vehicles. This paper extends the multi-depot VRP with time windows to account for crew skill levels, where each maintenance task requires one of three competence categories. The model was formulated as a mixed-integer linear programme (MILP) and solved with a branch-and-price algorithm for instances with up to 80 tasks and four depots. For larger instances (up to 320 tasks, six depots), a large neighbourhood search (LNS) heuristic was applied. Test data were drawn from maintenance records provided by a regional road authority in Serbia under a non-disclosure agreement. Results show that ignoring skill constraints leads to infeasible assignments in 23% of real-world instances examined; integrating skill matching increased total travel distance by only 6.8% compared to the unconstrained optimum. The LNS heuristic found solutions within 3.5% of the MILP optimum for instances where both were solvable.

title: Benchmark Set for Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing with Infrastructure Maintenance Constraints: Design and Baseline Results
abstract: Public benchmark libraries for VRP variants rarely capture characteristics specific to infrastructure maintenance: irregular task distribution along linear assets, mandatory service-window compliance, and multi-depot topology. This paper describes a benchmark set of 120 instances in four size tiers (50, 100, 200, and 400 tasks) constructed from a procedural generator that mimics road-network geometry. Each instance specifies depot locations, task positions, time windows, service durations, and vehicle capacities. Baseline results are reported for four algorithms: nearest-neighbour construction, Clarke–Wright savings, tabu search, and a genetic algorithm. Across all tiers, tabu search achieved the lowest average cost, but the genetic algorithm was more consistent on the largest tier. All instances and source code are published under a permissive open licence on an institutional repository. The benchmark is intended to support reproducible comparison of future algorithms addressing this problem class.

title: Real-Time Replanning of Maintenance Routes Under Unexpected Task Insertions: A Rolling-Horizon Framework
abstract: Infrastructure maintenance operations are frequently disrupted by urgent repair tasks that arise outside the original schedule. This paper proposes a rolling-horizon replanning framework in which the current routing solution is partially frozen and a reduced optimisation problem is solved over a look-ahead window of four to eight hours. The framework was implemented using a truncated branch-and-bound solver with a 30-second time limit per replanning cycle. Simulation experiments over a synthetic 12-hour workday with Poisson-distributed urgent task arrivals (mean rate 0.5 per hour) showed that the rolling-horizon approach reduced total overtime by 31% and task delay by 44% compared to a no-replanning baseline. Freezing 60% of already-committed vehicle assignments in each cycle provided the best balance between solution quality and computational feasibility. The paper also evaluates how the arrival rate of urgent tasks affects the benefit of shorter look-ahead windows.

title: GIS-Integrated Route Optimisation for Power Distribution Network Inspection in the Pannonian Region
abstract: Power distribution utilities operate geographically dispersed inspection fleets with strict scheduling requirements tied to grid load cycles. This study integrates a GIS data pipeline with a multi-depot routing solver to optimise inspection tours for 17 substations across a 9,400 km² service area in northern Serbia and southern Hungary. Road network travel times were extracted from a customised OpenStreetMap export, updated with seasonal speed profiles derived from traffic count data at 42 monitoring stations. A simulated annealing algorithm produced inspection schedules respecting both time-window and crew rest-period regulations. The optimised schedules reduced total vehicle-kilometres by 14.7% and eliminated all time-window violations present in the manually planned baseline. A sensitivity analysis demonstrates that a 15% increase in crew rest requirements raises total distance by only 3.2%, suggesting that regulatory tightening would have a modest operational impact for this operator.

title: Column Generation for Multi-Depot Maintenance Routing with Staggered Shift Starts
abstract: Many maintenance organisations stagger crew departure times to reduce peak depot congestion and improve service coverage. This paper incorporates staggered shift starts into a multi-depot VRP formulation by introducing a set of permissible departure time slots at each depot. The problem is solved via column generation, where the pricing subproblem is a shortest-path problem with time-window and capacity constraints solved by a bi-directional label-setting algorithm. The master problem was implemented in CPLEX 20.1. Tests on 40 instances derived from the benchmark set introduced in the authors' earlier work show that incorporating staggered starts reduces peak congestion indicators by up to 27% with an average cost increase of only 4.1%. The column generation approach solved instances of up to 150 tasks to optimality within 10 minutes; beyond 200 tasks a heuristic column selection strategy was necessary, yielding solutions within 5% of lower bounds.

title: Optimisation of Winter Road Maintenance Fleets Across Multiple Depots: A Case Study in Vojvodina
abstract: Winter maintenance of regional roads imposes tight response-time requirements and spatially concentrated demand during precipitation events. This chapter examines how multi-depot VRP models can be calibrated to winter maintenance operations by combining meteorological forecast data with pavement condition indices. Historical weather data from 11 automatic stations in Vojvodina covering five winter seasons (2017–2022) were used to construct probabilistic task arrival models. A scenario-based robust optimisation approach generated depot staffing and pre-positioning recommendations that performed within 8% of the deterministic optimum across 80% of simulated weather scenarios. The chapter discusses practical barriers to implementation, including dispatcher acceptance of algorithm-generated plans and the absence of real-time vehicle telemetry in most Serbian public road companies. Recommendations for phased adoption are outlined, with cost-benefit estimates for a medium-sized regional operator managing 22 vehicles from three depots.

title: Fleet Electrification and Route Feasibility in Multi-Depot Maintenance Operations: Range Constraints and Charging Stop Integration
abstract: Replacing diesel maintenance vehicles with battery-electric equivalents introduces range and charging constraints that interact with existing time-window requirements. This preprint formulates the multi-depot electric VRP with time windows and partial charging stops (MDEVRPTW-PC) and proposes an adaptive large neighbourhood search (ALNS) to solve it. Charging infrastructure is modelled using publicly available data on fast-charging stations in Serbia and Hungary. Experiments compare the all-diesel baseline, a partial electrification scenario (50% of fleet), and a full electrification scenario across 30 real-derived instances. Full electrification increases total route cost by 22–35% depending on task distribution and available charging density, while a 50% partial scenario increases cost by 8–13%. The paper identifies geographic corridors where charging gaps would require route redesign even with moderate task density, providing input for charging infrastructure placement planning.

title: Downlink Coverage Analysis of Two-Tier Cellular Networks Using Poisson Point Processes
abstract: This paper derives closed-form expressions for downlink coverage probability in a two-tier heterogeneous network where macro base stations and small cells are modeled as independent homogeneous Poisson point processes on the plane. The standard path-loss model with Rayleigh fading is adopted. Using tools from stochastic geometry, the Laplace functional of the interference is computed, yielding a tractable expression for the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio distribution. Numerical results are validated against Monte Carlo simulations conducted over 10,000 network realizations. The analysis covers a range of small-cell deployment densities from 1 to 100 nodes per square kilometer and examines the effect of the tier association bias on coverage. Results show that aggressive offloading to the small-cell tier improves median coverage probability by up to 18 percentage points when the small-cell density exceeds 20 per square kilometer, but creates a coverage hole region for users at tier boundaries under certain bias configurations.

title: Effect of Line-of-Sight Probability on Coverage in Dense Urban Small-Cell Deployments
abstract: Dense urban small-cell networks experience significant variation in propagation conditions because line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight links coexist. This paper incorporates an exponential line-of-sight probability function, calibrated against ITU-R P.1411 building entry loss data for a mid-European urban canyon environment, into a stochastic geometry framework for a single-tier network. Base stations are distributed as a homogeneous Poisson point process with density ranging from 10 to 500 per square kilometer. Separate path-loss exponents and Nakagami-m fading parameters are assigned to each propagation state. The resulting SINR distribution is expressed as a mixture involving two Laplace transforms, evaluated numerically. Coverage probability is shown to decline non-monotonically with network density beyond approximately 150 nodes per square kilometer in line-of-sight-dominated scenarios, contrary to the prediction of models that assume a single path-loss exponent. The model is further used to estimate area spectral efficiency as a function of transmit power.

title: Handover Rate and Sojourn Time Analysis in Multi-Tier Networks Under User Mobility
abstract: The integration of stochastic geometry with a spatial mobility model allows analytical characterization of handover rates and cell sojourn times in heterogeneous networks. This paper models user trajectories as linear paths with uniformly distributed orientations and derives the crossing rate of Voronoi cell boundaries for a marked Poisson point process representing a two-tier deployment. Results are expressed as functions of tier densities, user speed, and association policy. For a typical urban pedestrian scenario at 1.4 m/s, the predicted handover rate in the small-cell tier increases from 0.8 to 4.2 events per minute as small-cell density grows from 5 to 50 per square kilometer. The analytical predictions are within 6% of event-driven simulations. The framework is extended to estimate the signaling overhead caused by handover procedures, quantified in terms of control plane load per unit area. Results indicate a trade-off between coverage gain and signaling cost at densities above 30 small cells per square kilometer.

title: Stochastic Geometry Models for Heterogeneous Wireless Networks: A Survey of Analytical Tools and Results
abstract: This book chapter reviews the application of stochastic geometry to the performance analysis of heterogeneous wireless networks, with emphasis on coverage probability, rate distribution, and energy efficiency. The chapter covers foundational results based on homogeneous Poisson point processes and then discusses extensions to clustered processes, determinantal point processes, and Matérn hard-core processes, commenting on the trade-off between analytical tractability and spatial realism. A section is dedicated to multi-tier association policies, including maximum received power, maximum SINR, and range-expansion bias. Millimeter-wave specifics—beam alignment, blockage, and the dual LOS/NLOS path-loss model—are treated in a separate section. The chapter concludes with open problems including non-stationary deployments, correlated shadowing fields, and the interaction between physical-layer models and higher-layer protocols. Illustrative numerical examples use parameters representative of Central European urban environments.

title: Energy Efficiency of Dense mmWave Networks with Partial Sleeping Strategies Under Spatially Varying Traffic
abstract: This paper examines how base station sleeping policies affect energy efficiency in dense millimeter-wave networks when traffic demand is spatially inhomogeneous. A non-homogeneous Poisson point process with a log-Gaussian intensity function is used to model the spatial distribution of traffic demand, with parameters estimated from anonymized cellular measurement data collected in a mid-sized Central European city. Active base stations follow an independent thinning rule based on local traffic load. The energy efficiency metric, defined as bits per joule delivered to active users, is derived analytically using the Palm calculus framework. Results show that a threshold-based sleeping policy with load threshold set to 15% of peak capacity achieves 62% of the theoretical maximum energy efficiency while maintaining coverage probability above 0.80 for 95% of simulated demand realizations. The analysis also quantifies the coverage penalty introduced by sleeping for users at the boundary of sleeping zones, found to be up to 9 dB in received SINR under worst-case spatial correlation.

title: Analytical Framework for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Assisted mmWave Backhaul in Non-Line-of-Sight Conditions
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces offer a passive relay mechanism for millimeter-wave backhaul links blocked by buildings, but their integration into stochastic network models raises non-trivial questions about surface placement and phase configuration. This paper models RIS-assisted backhaul links in a two-tier heterogeneous network where each blocked small-cell base station is assigned the nearest available surface according to a separate independent Poisson point process. The cascaded channel through the RIS is approximated using a product of Nakagami-m random variables, and an achievable rate expression is derived as a function of surface element count and surface density. For a surface density of 10 per square kilometer and 64-element surfaces, the framework predicts a 7.4 dB median SINR improvement relative to no-surface baseline in a scenario where 40% of backhaul links are blocked. The sensitivity of this gain to imperfect phase control modeled by a uniform phase error is quantified, showing less than 1.2 dB degradation for phase errors up to 15 degrees.

title: Joint Coverage and Fronthaul Capacity Analysis for Cloud Radio Access Networks with Correlated Small-Cell Clusters
abstract: Cloud radio access network architectures require distributed remote radio heads to be connected to a central baseband unit via fronthaul links with bounded latency and capacity. This paper studies a C-RAN deployment where remote radio heads are distributed as a Matérn cluster process with parent macro-cell locations following a Poisson point process, capturing the tendency for small cells to be deployed in clusters near traffic hotspots. Fronthaul links are modeled as shared fiber segments with capacity drawn from a bounded distribution. The joint probability that a user simultaneously achieves a target downlink SINR and that the serving cluster's fronthaul is not saturated is derived. Numerical results for a cluster radius of 50 m and mean cluster size of 4 nodes show that fronthaul saturation reduces effective coverage by 11–19 percentage points depending on the fronthaul capacity distribution, an effect not captured by access-only coverage models. The model is further used to dimension fronthaul capacity for a given joint coverage target.

title: Stochastic Geometry Analysis of Uplink Performance in Heterogeneous Networks with Partial Zero-Forcing Receivers
abstract: Uplink analysis in heterogeneous networks is more involved than downlink because inter-cell interference originates from users scattered across multiple tiers. This paper derives the uplink SINR distribution for a two-tier network where macro-cell base stations employ partial zero-forcing receivers that cancel interference from the strongest K interferers while treating residual interference as noise. Users and base stations are modeled as independent Poisson point processes, and the analysis leverages the displacement theorem and Campbell's theorem to obtain expressions for the conditional Laplace transform of interference as a function of K and the number of receive antennas. For K=2 and 4 receive antennas, median uplink SINR improves by 5.8 dB over the single-antenna matched-filter baseline at a macro-cell load of 10 users per cell. The framework also provides a tractable lower bound on uplink spectral efficiency that tightens as antenna count increases and is within 4% of simulation at 8 antennas.

title: Bin picking with a collaborative robot and a depth camera
abstract: This paper presents a complete pipeline for bin picking using a collaborative robot equipped with a structured-light depth camera. The proposed system integrates 3D point cloud processing with a ROS 2-based control architecture to enable robust object detection, pose estimation, and grasp planning for randomly oriented parts inside industrial bins. A custom segmentation module isolates individual objects from cluttered scenes, while a grasp quality metric ranks candidate picks based on reachability and collision avoidance constraints. Experiments were conducted on a six-degree-of-freedom collaborative robot manipulator using a set of metallic and plastic components representative of small-batch manufacturing. The system achieved a grasp success rate of 91.4% across 500 trials, with an average cycle time competitive with existing industrial solutions. A comparative evaluation against two baseline methods demonstrates the advantages of the proposed approach in terms of both accuracy and adaptability to novel part geometries. The results suggest that off-the-shelf collaborative robots, when paired with appropriate perception and planning software, are viable candidates for flexible bin picking in small and medium enterprises.

title: ROS 2 Architecture for Real-Time Motion Planning in Collaborative Robot Cells
abstract: Collaborative robots operating in shared human-robot workspaces demand motion planning systems that are both computationally efficient and deterministically safe. This paper introduces a modular ROS 2-based software architecture designed to support real-time motion planning in dynamic collaborative robot cells. The architecture decouples perception, planning, and execution layers through a set of well-defined ROS 2 action and service interfaces, enabling hot-swappable algorithmic components without system downtime. A sampling-based planner augmented with workspace obstacle maps is implemented as a lifecycle-managed node, allowing graceful startup and shutdown during runtime reconfiguration. Benchmarks performed on a seven-degree-of-freedom collaborative manipulator show that the architecture sustains planning loop rates exceeding 50 Hz under realistic obstacle densities. Safety monitoring is integrated directly into the executor layer, enforcing speed and separation monitoring compliant with ISO/TS 15066. The paper further discusses lessons learned from deploying the architecture in a pilot production cell at a partner facility, highlighting engineering trade-offs between generality and determinism. The open-source release of the architecture is intended to accelerate adoption of ROS 2 in industrial collaborative robotics.

title: Sampling-Based Motion Planners for Cluttered Industrial Workspaces: A Comparative Study
abstract: Choosing an appropriate motion planning algorithm is critical for collaborative robots deployed in densely cluttered industrial environments. This paper presents a systematic comparative study of five sampling-based planners — RRT, RRT*, RRT-Connect, BiEST, and LBKPIECE — evaluated under conditions representative of assembly and bin picking workspaces. Each planner is benchmarked across three workspace configurations of increasing obstacle density using a standardized ROS 2 MoveIt 2 interface, with metrics including planning time, path length, success rate, and smoothness of the resulting trajectory. Results indicate that RRT-Connect consistently achieves the best balance between planning speed and path quality in high-density scenarios, while RRT* produces shorter paths at the cost of significantly longer computation times. The study also evaluates the sensitivity of each algorithm to hyperparameter settings, providing practical tuning guidelines for practitioners. A post-processing smoothing stage based on B-spline fitting is proposed and shown to reduce joint jerk by up to 38% without compromising safety clearances. The findings offer actionable recommendations for robotics engineers selecting planners for collaborative robot deployments in small and medium manufacturing enterprises.

title: Force-Torque Sensor Integration for Contact-Rich Assembly with Collaborative Robots
abstract: Peg-in-hole and snap-fit assembly tasks require robots to reliably detect and respond to contact forces during insertion operations. This paper describes the integration of a six-axis force-torque sensor into a ROS 2 control pipeline for a collaborative robot performing contact-rich assembly. A compliant motion controller based on impedance control is developed, with stiffness and damping parameters tuned online using a model-free adaptive scheme. The controller monitors force and torque readings in real time and adjusts the robot's end-effector trajectory to accommodate positional misalignments of up to 4 mm without hard-coded search patterns. Experimental validation covers three representative assembly tasks drawn from an electronics manufacturing scenario: circular peg insertion, rectangular prism fitting, and cable connector mating. The system achieves assembly success rates above 95% across all tasks at cycle times comparable to manual assembly. A failure recovery module is also presented, which classifies stuck states from force signatures and executes corrective motions autonomously. The work demonstrates that force-reactive control is both practically deployable and cost-effective on commercial collaborative robot platforms.

title: Point Cloud Preprocessing Strategies for Robust Pose Estimation in Industrial Bin Picking
abstract: Accurate pose estimation of partially occluded objects in cluttered bins remains one of the central challenges in industrial bin picking. This paper systematically investigates the impact of point cloud preprocessing choices — including voxel downsampling, statistical outlier removal, normal estimation neighborhood size, and surface reconstruction method — on the downstream performance of a correspondence-based pose estimation algorithm. Experiments are conducted using a structured-light depth camera mounted in eye-in-hand configuration on a collaborative robot, with three categories of target objects: simple prismatic parts, freeform cast components, and thin sheet-metal pieces. Results show that the choice of normal estimation strategy has a disproportionate effect on pose estimation accuracy compared with other preprocessing steps, and that adaptive neighborhood sizing outperforms fixed-radius approaches by an average of 2.3° in rotational error. A lightweight preprocessing pipeline incorporating the identified best practices is proposed and validated end-to-end in a live bin picking system under factory lighting conditions. Processing latency remains below 120 ms per frame on embedded hardware, confirming suitability for real-time deployment.

title: Safety-Aware Trajectory Replanning for Human-Robot Collaborative Workspaces
abstract: Ensuring human safety in shared workspaces is a fundamental requirement for deploying collaborative robots in real manufacturing environments. This paper proposes a safety-aware trajectory replanning framework that continuously monitors human pose estimates from an overhead RGB-D sensor and triggers local replanning when predicted human-robot minimum distances fall below configurable thresholds. Human poses are tracked using a skeleton estimation module running as a dedicated ROS 2 node, and predicted future positions are computed via a constant-velocity kinematic model over a short horizon. The replanner modifies the robot's active trajectory in real time using a dynamic programming approach that minimizes path deviation while enforcing a safety buffer surface. The framework is validated in a series of trials in which a human operator works alongside a collaborative robot performing pick-and-place tasks, with intentional incursions into the robot's workspace. The system reduces speed-separation monitoring violations by 84% compared with a static speed-reduction baseline, while maintaining a task completion rate above 97%. Integration effort is kept low by packaging all components as composable ROS 2 nodes compatible with standard MoveIt 2 deployments.

title: Calibration of Eye-in-Hand Depth Cameras for Collaborative Robot Manipulation: Methods and Industrial Considerations
abstract: Reliable hand-eye calibration is a prerequisite for accurate robot-sensor fusion in manipulation tasks such as bin picking, inspection, and assembly guidance. This paper provides a comprehensive review and experimental comparison of four hand-eye calibration methods — Tsai-Lenz, Park-Martin, dual quaternion, and nonlinear optimization — applied to an eye-in-hand depth camera mounted on a collaborative robot. Calibration targets of three types (checkerboard, ArUco grid, and spherical target) are also evaluated in combination with each method. Accuracy is assessed using a standardized pick-and-place benchmark in which the absolute position error of grasp attempts on known targets is measured. Results demonstrate that nonlinear optimization with an ArUco grid target achieves the lowest median position error of 0.8 mm, while classical algebraic methods remain competitive when calibration time is constrained. The paper further discusses practical factors specific to industrial deployment, including lens distortion compensation for structured-light sensors, temperature-induced drift, and re-calibration scheduling. A step-by-step calibration workflow compatible with the ROS 2 ecosystem is provided as a supplementary resource to lower the barrier for practitioners.

title: Grasp Planning Under Uncertainty for Deformable Objects in Collaborative Robot Applications
abstract: Grasping deformable objects such as flexible plastic components, packaged goods, and textile elements poses unique challenges for collaborative robot bin picking systems, as rigid-body assumptions underlying most grasp planners break down. This paper proposes a grasp planning framework that models object deformation uncertainty using a probabilistic shape representation derived from multiple depth camera observations collected prior to grasping. A Monte Carlo sampling procedure generates candidate grasp configurations and evaluates their robustness by simulating grasp outcomes over sampled shape instances, selecting the configuration with the highest expected success probability. The framework is implemented within a ROS 2 pipeline and tested on a set of five deformable object categories in a lab-scale bin environment. Compared with a deterministic baseline planner, the proposed approach improves grasp success rates by 17 percentage points on average across deformable categories while incurring only a modest 340 ms increase in planning latency. The paper discusses the trade-off between shape sample count and planning time, and presents an adaptive sampling schedule that maintains performance across varying levels of object deformability. Directions for extending the approach to fully closed-loop tactile feedback are outlined.

title: Energy-Constrained Lawnmower Coverage Planning for a Single Fixed-Wing UAV Over Irregular Terrain
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of planning a complete coverage trajectory for a fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle operating over an irregularly shaped agricultural field with elevation changes. The field boundary is represented as a polygon with up to 24 vertices extracted from cadastral GIS data. A boustrophedon decomposition is applied to partition the field into parallel strips, and a travelling-salesman-style ordering of strip endpoints is solved with a nearest-neighbour heuristic followed by 2-opt local search. An energy model based on aerodynamic drag and climb work is integrated into the planner to ensure the mission fits within a 90 Wh battery budget. Experiments on five synthetic terrain datasets derived from a 1:5000 topographic map of Vojvodina show that the proposed planner reduces uncovered area to below 1.2% on all test cases while keeping estimated energy consumption within 94% of capacity. Computation times remain under 8 seconds on a laptop-class processor. The work establishes a baseline for subsequent multi-vehicle extensions.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Polygon Decomposition Methods for UAV Area Coverage Under Wind Disturbance
abstract: Four polygon decomposition strategies—boustrophedon, Morse-based cell decomposition, trapezoidal decomposition, and a grid-raster approach—are evaluated for suitability in UAV area coverage tasks when a constant horizontal wind is present. Wind disturbance introduces asymmetric turn costs and modifies effective strip width due to drift, both of which are incorporated into a simulation framework built on top of a kinematic fixed-wing model. Test scenarios comprise 30 randomly generated convex and non-convex polygons with areas ranging from 0.4 to 12 km². Results show that boustrophedon decomposition with strips aligned perpendicular to the wind direction yields the lowest total path length in 22 of 30 cases, while the grid-raster approach produces the most robust coverage completeness across wind speeds of 3–9 m/s. The trapezoidal method performs poorly for non-convex shapes. Findings are intended to guide planner selection for precision agriculture and infrastructure inspection applications.

title: Task Allocation in a Two-UAV System for Parallel Strip Coverage With Heterogeneous Battery Capacities
abstract: The paper formulates a strip allocation problem for a team of two quadrotors with different battery capacities tasked with jointly covering a rectangular survey area. Each strip is modelled as an indivisible task with an energy cost computed from hover and cruise power measurements collected on DJI F450-class platforms. The allocation problem is cast as a variant of the bin-packing problem and solved exactly using branch-and-bound for areas up to 1.5 km², and approximately using a greedy longest-processing-time heuristic for larger areas. Seventeen flight experiments were conducted in a 60×40 m outdoor field; actual energy consumption deviated from the model by a mean of 6.3%. The greedy heuristic achieves within 4% of the optimal makespan in all tested instances while running in under 0.3 seconds. A sensitivity analysis shows that model accuracy degrades noticeably at wind speeds above 5 m/s, motivating future onboard adaptive re-planning work.

title: Incorporating Cylindrical No-Fly Zones Into Waypoint-Based UAV Mission Planning Using Penalty-Augmented A*
abstract: This study presents a waypoint graph planner that respects cylindrical no-fly zone exclusions defined in compliance with ICAO Doc 9861 conventions. No-fly zones are modelled as vertical cylinders with radius and altitude band parameters; the planner constructs a visibility graph over waypoints and zone boundaries in the horizontal plane and extends it to a 3-D layered graph to handle altitude bands. A penalty term proportional to zone penetration depth is added to the heuristic of A* to produce near-feasible initial solutions that are then repaired by a local search post-processor. Tests on 200 randomly generated mission instances with 3–12 no-fly zones and 5–20 waypoints show that the planner finds fully feasible paths in 97.5% of cases with a mean path-length overhead of 11.4% compared to unconstrained optimal paths. Average planning time is 140 ms. The method is integrated into a ground station prototype running on a standard laptop.

title: Multi-UAV Coverage Path Planning as a Vehicle Routing Problem With Time Windows and Energy Constraints
abstract: The multi-UAV coverage problem is reformulated as a capacitated vehicle routing problem with time windows (CVRPTW), where each strip segment is a customer node, vehicle capacity corresponds to battery energy, and time windows encode a desired synchronisation schedule for simultaneous coverage of adjacent strips. A Solomon-type construction heuristic is used to generate initial routes, followed by a large neighbourhood search with strip-swap and strip-reinsertion operators. Benchmark tests use a set of 40 instances derived from real Vojvodina agricultural parcel maps ranging from 2 to 18 km² with fleets of 2–6 UAVs. The LNS-based solver reduces total flight time by 19% on average compared to the construction heuristic alone. Constraint satisfaction rates for energy limits reach 100%; time window violations drop to below 2% in 38 of 40 instances after post-processing. Computation time stays below 45 seconds for all tested instances.

title: Battery Endurance Modelling for Multirotor UAVs Under Variable Payload and Ambient Temperature
abstract: Accurate endurance prediction is a prerequisite for safe multi-UAV mission planning. This work develops a physics-informed endurance model that accounts for payload mass variation (0.1–0.8 kg additional payload on a 1.2 kg platform), ambient temperature (−5 to 35 °C), and state-of-health of lithium polymer cells. Discharge curves were recorded under 42 combinations of payload and temperature in a laboratory climate chamber. A nonlinear regression model with 11 parameters achieves a mean absolute error of 38 seconds on a nominal 18-minute endurance, outperforming a widely used linear baseline by 31%. The model is embedded as a constraint oracle in the mission planner described in prior work. Field validation across 24 outdoor flights confirms that planned energy budgets are respected with a safety margin variance of less than 5% in 21 of 24 cases. Temperature effects account for up to 14% endurance reduction at −5 °C.

title: Conflict-Free Routing for Multi-UAV Missions in Urban Airspace With Overlapping Geofences
abstract: Urban UAV operations must contend with multiple overlapping geofence volumes issued by different authorities, creating logical conflicts in which no compliant path may exist. This paper first formalises the geofence consistency problem and gives an NP-hardness proof for the general case. A preprocessing algorithm identifies and resolves pairwise conflicts by computing minimum-volume corridor relaxations, reducing the problem to a consistent set before path planning begins. The conflict-resolution step uses a linear programming relaxation of a set cover formulation. After preprocessing, paths are computed with a 3-D probabilistic roadmap planner. Experiments on a synthetic model of a 2×2 km urban district with 8–20 overlapping geofence volumes show that preprocessing reduces planning failures from 43% to 3%. Mean additional path length introduced by relaxation is 14%. The framework is evaluated for 2- and 4-UAV teams with a shared airspace allocation scheme.

title: Adaptive Strip-Width Selection for UAV Coverage Under Sensor Footprint Uncertainty
abstract: Camera footprint width in UAV photogrammetric surveys depends on altitude, lens calibration, and terrain relief, all of which carry uncertainty. Fixed strip widths therefore lead to either gaps or redundant overlap. This paper formulates strip-width selection as a chance-constrained optimisation problem: given probability distributions over footprint width derived from sensor calibration data and a digital elevation model, find the set of strip widths that guarantees a user-specified coverage probability (95% or 99%) at minimum total flight distance. A sample average approximation method is used to solve the resulting stochastic programme. Tests on four agricultural parcels in the Bačka region with area 0.5–6 km² show that adaptive widths reduce total flight distance by 7–13% compared to a conservative fixed-width baseline at the 95% coverage level, while maintaining the coverage guarantee. The planner runs in under 20 seconds for all test parcels.

title: A Benchmark Suite for Multi-UAV Coverage Planning With Geofence and Energy Constraints
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of multi-UAV coverage planners is hampered by the absence of standardised benchmark instances. This paper introduces a benchmark suite of 120 instances derived from publicly available land-use and airspace data for the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina. Instances are parameterised by area size (0.5–20 km²), fleet size (1–8 UAVs), number of no-fly zones (0–10), geofence complexity, and battery capacity class. For each instance, optimal or best-known solution values are provided via exhaustive search (small instances) or a portfolio of state-of-the-art solvers run for 24 CPU hours (large instances). Baseline results from six existing planners drawn from the literature are reported. The suite is released as an open dataset alongside a Python evaluation harness. Preliminary results indicate that no single planner dominates across all instance classes, motivating algorithm selection or portfolio approaches. The benchmark is intended to facilitate fair cross-paper comparisons.

title: Latency Profiling of Multi-Source Data Reconciliation Pipelines Across WAN-Linked Data Centres
abstract: Organisations that operate data centres in multiple cities face non-trivial latency when reconciling data streams that originate in geographically separate locations. We deployed a five-source reconciliation pipeline across three data centres separated by WAN links with measured round-trip times of 8 ms, 47 ms, and 112 ms, reflecting intra-regional and cross-border scenarios relevant to European deployments. The pipeline reconciled structured records from simulated ERP, MES, and sensor historian systems at a combined rate of 35 000 events per second. We profiled latency contributions from network transfer, deserialization, entity matching, join state lookup, and sink write across 14 operator stages. Network transfer accounted for 61% of end-to-end latency on the 112 ms link but only 18% on the 8 ms link, shifting the optimisation priority from algorithmic to infrastructure concerns. Co-locating matching-heavy operators with the highest-volume source reduced median end-to-end latency by 29% without altering join semantics.

title: Consistency Checking Between ARXML System Descriptions and Deployment Configurations
abstract: AUTOSAR system descriptions and their corresponding deployment configurations are maintained as separate ARXML files and can diverge during iterative development. This paper describes a rule-based consistency checker implemented as an Eclipse plug-in that operates on a merged in-memory model assembled from multiple ARXML artefacts. Forty-three consistency rules derived from the AUTOSAR 4.1 specification were encoded as OCL constraints. The checker was applied to six industrial-style test configurations provided by a regional automotive supplier, ranging from 12 to 78 ECUs per configuration. It detected an average of 8.4 rule violations per configuration that were not flagged by the supplier's existing tooling, most relating to signal mapping mismatches and unresolved component prototype references. False positive rate was 2.1% after a calibration phase involving two domain experts. The tool reduced manual configuration review time by approximately 40% in a two-week pilot.

title: Uporedna analiza metaheurističkih pristupa za dinamički problem rutiranja vozila sa vremenskim prozorima
abstract: Rad predstavlja sistematičnu poređenje četiri metaheuristička algoritma — simuliranog kaljenja, tabu pretrage, genetskog algoritma i algoritma kolonije mrava — primenjenih na dinamički problem rutiranja vozila sa vremenskim prozorima (DVRPTW). Testni skup obuhvata 60 instanci generisanih iz realnih podataka o dostavi u Novom Sadu, sa 50 do 200 klijenata i stopom dinamičnosti između 10 i 40 posto. Evaluacija obuhvata ukupnu pređenu distancu, broj angažovanih vozila, vreme replanninga i stabilnost ruta između uzastopnih iteracija. Rezultati pokazuju da tabu pretraga sa adaptivnom dužinom liste postignutih rešenja daje najmanji prosečni odmak od 4,7 posto u odnosu na statički optimum, dok algoritam kolonije mrava pokazuje najveću osetljivost na visoke stope dinamičnosti. Analizira se i uticaj frekvencije pristizanja novih narudžbina na stabilnost finalnih ruta.

title: Inductance Setting as a Secondary Control Variable for Spatter Reduction in Inverter-Based Short-Arc MIG Welding
abstract: Modern inverter MIG/MAG power sources expose an inductance or arc-dynamics parameter that alters the current rise rate during short-circuit clearing. This paper reports a systematic variation of the inductance index (0–9 on a Varkon VT-350 inverter, corresponding to measured dI/dt values of 42–210 A/ms) at three fixed voltage–wire-speed operating points for 1.5 mm and 2.0 mm S235JR sheet. Spatter count and mass were recorded per 200 mm weld run. High-speed imaging at 3000 fps was used to classify spatter origin as short-circuit explosion or free-flight droplet. At low inductance (dI/dt > 180 A/ms), short-circuit-origin spatter dominated and constituted 72 % of total spatter mass on 1.5 mm sheet. Increasing the inductance index to 6–7 reduced total spatter mass by 29 % while maintaining adequate fusion at the 1.5 mm thickness. These findings confirm inductance tuning as a practical, parameter-free-of-cost improvement available to production line operators.

title: Residual Oil Film Thickness on Cold-Rolled Steel Strip and Its Influence on MIG Weld Pool Stability
abstract: Stamped automotive-grade cold-rolled mild-steel blanks typically carry residual drawing oil films in the range of 0.3–2.5 g/m². This study quantifies the relationship between oil film thickness, measured gravimetrically after solvent extraction, and arc stability indicators during MIG welding. Twenty-four coupons with controlled oil loads (0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.5 g/m², applied by roller coating with a SAE 10W reference oil) were welded under a fixed parameter set optimised for zero-oil conditions. Arc voltage and current waveforms were sampled at 50 kHz and analysed for short-circuit frequency, arc-on time fraction, and standard deviation of voltage. At 1.5 g/m² and above, arc-on time fraction dropped from 0.81 to 0.67 and short-circuit frequency increased by 34 %, accompanied by a 51 % rise in spatter mass. Bead porosity, assessed by X-ray radiography per EN ISO 5817, remained within level C limits up to 1.0 g/m² but exceeded them at higher loads. The results suggest a practical cleanliness threshold of ≤ 1.0 g/m² for production lines without degreasing pre-treatment.

title: Weld Process Parameter Optimisation for Low-Spatter MIG/MAG Joining of Thin Mild-Steel Sheet
abstract: This doctoral thesis presents a systematic investigation of process variable interactions governing spatter formation in short-arc and globular-to-spray-transition MIG/MAG welding of S235JR and DC01 sheet in thicknesses of 1.0–2.5 mm. Response surface methodology with a central composite design covering five factors — arc voltage, wire feed speed, travel speed, contact-tip-to-work distance, and shielding gas composition (Ar/CO₂ ratio 75/25 to 92/8) — was used to build regression models for spatter mass rate, bead width deviation, and tensile efficiency. Optimised conditions were validated on 120 weld specimens; spatter mass rates below 0.08 g/m were achieved on 1.2 mm sheet with a mixed gas of Ar/CO₂ 82/18 at 17.8 V, 5.8 m/min, and 45 cm/min travel speed. Mechanical testing confirmed all welds met EN ISO 15614-1 requirements. A simplified decision chart translating sheet thickness and joint configuration into parameter windows is provided as a practical outcome for production engineers.

title: Alkaline Degreasing Bath Concentration and Temperature Effects on Residual Carbon and Wettability of Mild-Steel Sheet Before Powder Coating
abstract: Alkaline spray degreasing is the first stage in most powder coating pre-treatment lines. This study investigates how bath concentration (10–40 g/L of a commercial alkaline degreaser, Alkoclean 720) and temperature (45–70 °C) affect the residual total organic carbon (TOC) on the sheet surface and the resulting water contact angle. A 3² factorial design was applied to DC01 cold-rolled panels (100 × 150 mm) at a fixed spray pressure of 1.2 bar and 60 s exposure. Residual TOC was measured by combustion analysis of surface swabs. Contact angle was measured by sessile drop with deionised water. Bath concentration was the more influential factor: raising concentration from 10 to 40 g/L reduced median TOC from 48 to 9 µg/dm² and contact angle from 62° to 14°. Temperature above 60 °C provided marginal additional improvement. Cross-cut adhesion testing (EN ISO 2409) of subsequently phosphated and powder-coated panels showed a direct correlation between contact angle after degreasing and final coating adhesion class, with all panels degreased at ≥ 20 g/L achieving class 0.

title: Measurement Uncertainty in Contact Angle Determination as a Process Control Indicator in Powder Coating Pre-Treatment
abstract: Contact angle measurement by the sessile drop method is increasingly used as an inline or near-line indicator of surface cleanliness in powder coating pre-treatment lines. However, its measurement uncertainty under industrial conditions has not been systematically characterised. This study applies the GUM framework to quantify uncertainty contributions from drop volume (1–5 µL), image acquisition angle, baseline detection algorithm, and surface roughness for DC01 panels at various stages of a five-stage pre-treatment line (degrease, rinse, zinc phosphate, rinse, passivation). Expanded uncertainty (k = 2) ranged from ±1.8° on smooth panels after rinsing to ±6.4° on phosphated panels with Ra ≈ 1.8 µm. Operator-to-operator reproducibility, evaluated across four operators on identical panels, contributed 18–31 % of total variance depending on stage. Practical control limits accounting for these uncertainties are proposed for each pre-treatment stage, offering a statistically defensible accept/reject criterion for production quality control.

title: Phosphate Coat Weight Uniformity Across a Conveyor-Fed Spray Phosphating Line: A Multi-Point Sampling Study
abstract: Zinc phosphate pre-treatment is critical to adhesion and corrosion resistance in electrostatic powder coating. This paper reports a multi-point sampling campaign at a medium-sized contract coating shop operating a seven-stage spray line with a throughput of 1800 m²/day. Coat weight was determined gravimetrically (strip-and-weigh per EN ISO 9717) at nine positions across the conveyor width and three longitudinal positions per batch, over 14 production days. Mean coat weight was 2.4 g/m² with a within-batch coefficient of variation of 11–19 % and a between-day coefficient of variation of 8 %. Edge zones (within 80 mm of conveyor rail) showed systematically 22 % lower coat weights, attributable to spray shadow effects characterised by flow visualisation with tracer dye. Bath chemistry (Zn²⁺, total acid, free acid, accelerator concentration) was logged concurrently; free acid point emerged as the strongest predictor of coat weight in a multiple regression model (R² = 0.71). Adjusting free acid set-point from 0.8 to 1.1 points reduced between-position variance by 31 % over a two-week trial.

title: Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input
abstract: Very thin mild-steel sheet (1.0 mm DC01) presents a narrow operating window in MIG welding because heat input must be minimised to avoid burn-through while maintaining fusion. This paper reports the effect of Ar/CO₂ mixture ratios (75/25, 82/18, 90/10, and 97/3 vol%) on spatter mass, bead width, dilution, and distortion in bead-on-plate welds at a fixed heat input of 85 J/mm. Forty-eight specimens were welded and measured. Ar/CO₂ 90/10 produced the lowest spatter mass (0.06 g/m) and the most consistent bead width (coefficient of variation 4.2 %), while 75/25 produced 0.21 g/m spatter. Hardness traverses across the heat-affected zone showed a maximum of 198 HV1 for all gas compositions, indicating no detrimental microstructural change. Distortion, measured by three-point deflection, was lowest at 97/3 but accompanied by an irregular bead profile with 14 % of runs showing incomplete fusion. The 90/10 ratio is recommended as the practical optimum for this thickness.

title: Statistical Process Control Implementation for a Four-Stage Pre-Treatment Line Feeding an Electrostatic Powder Coating Operation
abstract: This paper describes the design and pilot implementation of a statistical process control (SPC) scheme for a four-stage pre-treatment line (alkaline degrease, rinse, iron phosphate, rinse) at a small powder coating contractor in Novi Sad. Control variables selected for Shewhart chart monitoring were degreaser bath concentration, bath temperature, phosphate bath conductivity, and rinse-water conductivity at the final rinse stage. A three-month baseline data collection phase (n = 312 shift-level observations) established control limits. Capability indices (Cpk) were computed for each variable against supplier-specified bath chemistry windows; initial Cpk values ranged from 0.71 to 1.18. After operator training and the introduction of twice-daily titration checks replacing the previous once-daily practice, Cpk for degreaser concentration improved to 1.41 and phosphate conductivity to 1.29 over the subsequent three months. Coating adhesion cross-cut failures dropped from 4.1 % to 1.2 % of panels in the same period. The paper discusses the practical barriers to SPC adoption in small coating shops and proposes a minimal-instrument monitoring protocol.

title: Pulsed MIG Welding of 1.2 mm Mild-Steel Sheet: Parameter Window Mapping for Spatter-Free Operation at 150–300 A Mean Current
abstract: Pulsed MIG welding offers the potential for spatter-free operation across a wider thickness range than conventional short-arc transfer, but the interaction between peak current, pulse duration, background current, and frequency creates a large parameter space. This study applies a D-optimal design with 41 experimental runs to map the spatter-free operating window for 1.2 mm S235JR sheet using an inverter source with independent pulse parameter control (Varkon PulseMaster 400). Spatter was classified as zero, low (< 0.03 g/m), or unacceptable (≥ 0.03 g/m) based on production-line cleanliness targets. The response surface model identified a feasible zero-spatter region centred on peak current 320 A, pulse duration 2.1 ms, background current 42 A, and frequency 95 Hz for Ar/CO₂ 90/10 shielding gas. Travel speed and contact-tip-to-work distance were fixed at 48 cm/min and 14 mm respectively. Bead-on-plate and T-fillet specimens welded at the optimum point showed tensile shear strengths of 390–408 MPa and no radiographic indications above EN ISO 5817 level B. The mapped window boundaries are presented as a contour chart suitable for direct use in parameter card preparation.

title: Trace-level determination of N-nitrosodimethylamine in metformin hydrochloride tablets using GC-TEA after headspace extraction
abstract: A headspace gas chromatography method coupled to thermal energy analysis (GC-TEA) was developed and validated for the determination of N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) in metformin hydrochloride tablets. Extraction conditions including headspace equilibration temperature (80–120 °C), incubation time (20–60 min), and salt addition were systematically optimised using a central composite design. The validated method achieved a limit of detection of 0.004 µg g⁻¹ and a limit of quantification of 0.012 µg g⁻¹, well below the EMA-recommended acceptable daily intake of 0.0959 µg for NDMA. Recovery across three concentration levels ranged from 96.4% to 103.2% with relative standard deviations below 4.1%. Thirteen commercial metformin products purchased on the Serbian and Slovenian markets were analysed; two products exceeded the acceptable intake threshold when projected to the maximum daily dose. The method was compared with a published LC-MS/MS procedure, showing good agreement (Pearson r = 0.991). Practical considerations for routine quality-control laboratory implementation are discussed.

title: Kinetics of N-nitrosamine formation in ranitidine solutions under accelerated thermal stress conditions
abstract: Ranitidine has been reported to generate NDMA through an intramolecular rearrangement rather than classical nitrosation chemistry. This study monitored the time-dependent accumulation of NDMA in ranitidine hydrochloride solutions (pH 1, 4, and 7 phosphate buffers) held at 40, 50, and 60 °C over 90 days. NDMA concentrations were quantified by LC-MS/MS at nine time points per condition. First-order rate constants ranged from 2.1 × 10⁻⁴ day⁻¹ at 40 °C (pH 7) to 8.7 × 10⁻³ day⁻¹ at 60 °C (pH 1). An Arrhenius analysis gave an activation energy of 68.4 kJ mol⁻¹, consistent with a thermally driven decomposition mechanism. At pH 1 and 60 °C, NDMA exceeded the 0.0959 µg acceptable daily intake limit within 12 days when projected to the labelled dose. The data support the hypothesis that acidic gastric conditions can generate clinically relevant NDMA from ingested ranitidine. Implications for shelf-life specifications and storage temperature labelling are discussed.

title: Role of dimethylamine residues and nitrite contamination in NDMA formation during sartan synthesis: a process chemistry perspective
abstract: Sartans containing a tetrazole ring are manufactured through palladium-catalysed coupling steps in dimethylformamide (DMF) or dimethylacetamide (DMA) solvents. Both solvents can degrade to dimethylamine under acidic or basic conditions, providing a precursor for N-nitrosodimethylamine formation when nitrite-bearing reagents or excipients are present. This paper examines the reaction pathways leading to NDMA and structurally related nitrosamines (NMBA, NDEA, NIPEA) across five simulated synthetic routes for valsartan, irbesartan, and losartan analogues using spiking experiments. Reaction mixtures were sampled at each synthetic step and analysed by LC-HRMS. NDMA was consistently detected at the DMF hydrolysis step when sodium azide was used in a nitrite-contaminated aqueous workup. NMBA formation required the simultaneous presence of n-butyl intermediates and nitrous acid. The study maps specific unit operations to nitrosamine risk scores and recommends stage-specific controls, including in-process monitoring specifications for dimethylamine at ≤ 10 ppm and nitrite at ≤ 0.5 ppm.

title: Comparison of derivatisation strategies for GC-MS/MS quantification of volatile nitrosamines at sub-ppb concentrations in solid oral dosage forms
abstract: Volatile nitrosamines (NDMA, NDEA, NMEA, NDBA, NDIPA, NDPA) in solid dosage forms are commonly extracted by solvent and analysed by GC-MS/MS. This study evaluated four extraction and derivatisation approaches: direct solvent extraction in ethyl acetate, alkaline hydrolysis followed by dichloromethane extraction, headspace SPME with PDMS fibre, and headspace SPME with CAR/PDMS fibre. Each was assessed for recovery, matrix effects, and analytical figures of merit using spiked placebo tablets containing microcrystalline cellulose and magnesium stearate. CAR/PDMS SPME provided the best sensitivity (LODs 0.001–0.003 µg g⁻¹) and lowest matrix suppression (< 8% across six analytes). Method applicability was confirmed on ten commercial losartan and amlodipine tablets. Retention time reproducibility (RSD < 0.3%) and isotopic dilution accuracy (98.2–104.6%) confirmed suitability for routine use. The paper provides a practical comparison to guide quality-control laboratories in method selection.

title: ICH M7 compliant probabilistic risk assessment of nitrosamines in API manufacturing: a worked example for a multi-step synthetic route
abstract: ICH M7 requires that genotoxic impurities be controlled to acceptable intake limits, but the guideline does not specify how to handle compounds with incomplete carcinogenicity datasets. This paper presents a probabilistic framework for assessing nitrosamine risk across a ten-step synthetic route for a hypothetical angiotensin receptor blocker. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 iterations) propagated uncertainty in reaction yields, precursor concentrations, and purification efficiencies to estimate the 95th-percentile nitrosamine level in the final API. Inputs were drawn from laboratory-scale experiments (n = 3 independent batches) and published formation kinetic constants. The simulated 95th-percentile NDMA level in the final API was 0.041 ppm, compared with a measured value of 0.038 ± 0.007 ppm in validation batches, demonstrating adequate predictive accuracy. The framework was used to rank the four synthesis steps contributing most to nitrosamine load and to size in-process controls accordingly. A sensitivity analysis identified nitrite purity specifications as the dominant risk driver.

title: Regulatory frameworks for nitrosamine impurity limits: a comparative analysis of EMA, FDA, and ICH M7 approaches with implications for non-EU markets
abstract: Between 2018 and 2022, EMA, FDA, and the ICH M7 expert working group issued overlapping but not fully consistent guidance on acceptable intake limits, substance-specific limits, and analytical thresholds for nitrosamine impurities in drug products. This book chapter systematically compares the three frameworks across six dimensions: scope of applicability, analytical method requirements, risk assessment methodology, compound-specific versus class-based limits, timelines for compliance, and provisions for post-market surveillance. A tabular summary of 22 nitrosamines lists the limit values specified under each framework and highlights 11 cases where discrepancies exceed a factor of two. The chapter discusses the practical consequences for generic manufacturers in Serbia and other Western Balkan states seeking simultaneous compliance with European and US market requirements, and outlines a harmonised documentation strategy. Particular attention is given to the recently introduced concept of nitrosamine drug substance-related impurities (NDSRIs).

title: Rapid screening of ten nitrosamines in API batches using direct injection LC-MS/MS without sample preconcentration
abstract: Sample preparation for nitrosamine analysis in APIs typically involves liquid–liquid extraction, solid-phase extraction, or headspace concentration, all of which introduce analyst time and potential contamination. This paper describes a direct injection LC-MS/MS method for simultaneous quantification of ten nitrosamines (NDMA, NDEA, NMBA, NDBA, NDIPA, NDPA, NMPA, NIPEA, NDEA-d6 as internal standard reference, and NMPA-d6) in aqueous API solutions at concentrations as low as 0.005 ppm. Chromatographic separation was achieved on a C18 column (2.1 × 100 mm, 1.8 µm) with a 7-min gradient using 0.1% formic acid in water and methanol. Matrix effects were below 12% for all analytes in five representative API matrices. The throughput of 60 samples per eight-hour shift enables use in incoming material testing. The method was cross-validated against two published extraction-based procedures using 30 blind API samples, with mean bias below 7% for all analytes.

title: Quantitative structure–activity relationship models for predicting TD50 values of N-nitrosamines: training set composition and applicability domain considerations
abstract: Acceptable daily intake limits for nitrosamines under ICH M7 are derived from rodent TD50 values, but carcinogenicity data exist for fewer than 40 of the hundreds of structurally possible N-nitrosamines. QSAR models offer a route to estimate TD50 for data-poor compounds. This study trained four regression models (random forest, support vector regression, gradient boosted trees, and a 3-layer neural network) on the CPDB database restricted to N-nitroso compounds (n = 87 with rat TD50 data). Molecular descriptors included constitutional, topological, electrotopological, and quantum-chemical features. Cross-validated R² ranged from 0.61 (support vector regression) to 0.74 (gradient boosted trees) on the held-out test set (n = 18). Applicability domain was defined by a Euclidean distance threshold in descriptor space; 23% of structures drawn from recent EMA NDSRI communications fell outside the applicability domain. The paper provides an openly accessible descriptor set and model coefficients, and discusses how to report TD50 predictions and their uncertainties in ICH M7 risk assessment dossiers.

title: Nitrosamine formation in probiotics and probiotic-containing drug products: a risk assessment based on nitrite content of enteric coatings
abstract: Probiotic-containing pharmaceutical products increasingly use enteric coatings based on cellulose acetate phthalate or hypromellose phthalate, which may carry nitrite residues from raw material synthesis. When secondary amines derived from excipient degradation or probiotic metabolites are present, conditions for nitrosamine formation may arise during manufacturing or storage. Nitrite was measured in six commercial enteric coating polymers by ion chromatography; values ranged from 0.6 to 11.4 ppm. The nitrosation potential of the most concentrated polymer was assessed in spiked binary mixtures with nine secondary amines at pH 3–5 over 30 days at 40 °C. Three structurally distinct nitrosamines were detected above the 2 ng threshold for LC-HRMS confirmation. Risk characterisation using compound-specific ICH M7 limits showed one combination exceeded thresholds at the 90th-percentile daily dose assumption. The paper recommends nitrite specification limits for enteric coating polymers and outlines a testing protocol for early formulation development.

title: Threshold of toxicological concern as a tiered risk assessment tool for uncharacterised nitrosamines: an evaluation against empirical carcinogenicity data
abstract: When a nitrosamine structure lacks experimental carcinogenicity data and falls outside the applicability domain of validated QSAR models, ICH M7 allows application of the threshold of toxicological concern (TTC) concept, setting a default acceptable intake of 18 ng day⁻¹ for high-potency genotoxicants. This paper evaluates the conservatism of the 18 ng day⁻¹ TTC threshold against empirical TD50 data for 87 N-nitroso compounds in the CPDB. Using the linear extrapolation model, the compound-specific acceptable daily intake was compared with the TTC default; in 71 of 87 cases (82%) the TTC was more conservative than the data-derived limit, providing a safety margin. However, for 16 compounds (18%), the TTC was less conservative by a median factor of 3.2-fold. The structural features characterising the higher-risk outliers are described; they predominantly involve α-hydroxylation activation without competing detoxification pathways. The analysis supports selective use of TTC while flagging structural classes requiring data generation.

title: Application of principal component analysis to fault detection in fluid-bed coating: a case study with enteric polymer dispersions
abstract: This study examined the use of principal component analysis (PCA) applied to routinely collected process variables—inlet air temperature, exhaust air temperature, product temperature, spray rate, atomisation air pressure, and pan speed—for fault detection during enteric coating of 5 mm acetaminophen tablets in a 3-litre Glatt GPCG-1 fluidised-bed coater. Reference batches (n = 18) were used to build a PCA model, and Hotelling's T² and Q-statistic control charts were computed for 24 additional batches including six deliberately perturbed runs with introduced deviations in spray rate (±25%) and atomisation air pressure (±15%). The T² chart detected all six perturbed batches, with out-of-control signals appearing within 3–7 minutes of the perturbation onset. False alarm rates on normal batches were 4.2% at the 95% confidence limit. Results support the use of standard process variable PCA monitoring as a complementary tool to spectroscopic methods in resource-limited production environments.

title: Box–Behnken design optimisation of coating suspension composition and process parameters for sustained-release pellet coating
abstract: A Box–Behnken design with 15 experimental runs was used to optimise three formulation variables—ethylcellulose-to-hydroxypropyl methylcellulose ratio (70:30–90:10), plasticiser level (5–15% w/w relative to polymer), and coating level (5–15% weight gain)—alongside two process variables: inlet air temperature (35–55 °C) and spray rate (5–15 g/min), for sustained-release coating of 500–600 µm theophylline pellets. Drug release at 1 h, 4 h, and 8 h in phosphate buffer pH 6.8 was used as the response. Response surface models showed significant main effects of coating level and polymer ratio on the 1 h release (R² = 0.94), with a strong interaction between plasticiser level and inlet air temperature at 4 h. Optimised conditions predicted 18.7% release at 1 h, 52.3% at 4 h, and 89.1% at 8 h; experimental verification batches (n = 3) yielded values within 3.4% of predictions. Desirability function composite optimisation was used for multi-response optimisation.
