title: Extrusion–spheronisation of microcrystalline cellulose–calcium hydrogen phosphate pellets: influence of wet mass consistency on pellet size distribution and drug loading uniformity
abstract: Pellets intended as multiparticulate drug carriers were manufactured by extrusion–spheronisation using binary MCC–CaHPO4 blends (MCC fraction 40–80% w/w). A 3% w/v hydroxypropyl cellulose solution was used as binder. Wet mass water content was varied between 28 and 44% to modulate extrudate plasticity. Pellet size distributions were characterised by laser diffraction (n = 3 batches per condition), and drug loading uniformity of theophylline was assessed by assaying 10 individual pellets per batch by HPLC. MCC fraction of 60% and water content of 36% yielded the narrowest size distribution (D10/D90 ratio = 0.64) and highest uniformity (RSD < 3.2% for theophylline content). Increasing CaHPO4 content beyond 40% resulted in bimodal size distributions attributable to incomplete plasticity. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed smooth, near-spherical morphology under optimal conditions. The data provide quantitative guidance for binder selection and water addition in pellet manufacturing.

title: Supercritical CO₂ extraction of tocopherols from sunflower press cake: optimisation and comparison with conventional solvent extraction
abstract: Sunflower press cake is produced in large quantities as a by-product of cold-press oil production in Serbia and the wider region. This study compared supercritical CO₂ extraction (SCE) with n-hexane Soxhlet extraction for recovery of total tocopherols, with particular attention to α- and γ-tocopherol. SCE conditions were optimised over a pressure range of 200–400 bar and temperature of 40–70 °C using a Box-Behnken design. Tocopherols were quantified by normal-phase HPLC with fluorescence detection. Under optimal SCE conditions (380 bar, 60 °C, 120 min), total tocopherol yield reached 312 mg/100 g dry cake, representing 89% of the reference Soxhlet yield. Critically, SCE-derived extracts contained 27% less co-extracted triacylglycerols, producing a more concentrated tocopherol fraction. The ratio of α- to γ-tocopherol was 2.3:1 under both methods, indicating no selective fractionation between homologues at these conditions. Thermal stability of tocopherols during SCE was confirmed by comparing fresh and stored extracts by peroxide value measurement. The data support SCE as an industrially feasible alternative for tocopherol-enriched nutraceutical ingredient production.

title: Logistic regression with class-weighted loss for sepsis early warning in emergency laboratory panels
abstract: Early identification of sepsis from routine admission blood panels remains difficult because sepsis cases represent fewer than 8% of emergency admissions in most central European hospitals. This study applied class-weighted logistic regression to a retrospective dataset of 4,812 adult admissions collected at a regional hospital in Vojvodina between 2015 and 2018. Predictors included 22 haematological and biochemical markers. Model performance was assessed using the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) and F1 score at a range of classification thresholds. The optimal threshold, selected by maximising the F-beta score with beta equal to 2 to penalise false negatives, achieved sensitivity of 0.81 and specificity of 0.74 on a held-out test set of 962 patients. Comparison with a cost-insensitive baseline showed a 14-percentage-point improvement in recall with a 6-point drop in precision. Feature importance analysis identified lactate, procalcitonin, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as the three strongest predictors. The findings suggest that threshold tuning alone recovers a substantial fraction of missed cases without resampling the training data.

title: Decision tree ensembles for automated urine sediment classification in high-throughput workflows
abstract: Automated urine sediment analysers generate per-patient feature vectors of 18 morphological counts and fluorescence intensity values. Manual review remains necessary for ambiguous samples, but the criteria for flagging samples for review vary between laboratories. This study trained gradient-boosted decision trees on 9,240 labelled samples from two laboratories operating the same analyser model to learn a consistent flagging rule. The primary objective was to minimise unnecessary manual reviews while maintaining sensitivity above 0.95 for clinically significant findings including casts, dysmorphic erythrocytes, and bacteria above threshold. Bayesian hyperparameter search identified tree depth 5, learning rate 0.05, and 400 estimators as the best configuration. On a prospective validation set of 1,102 samples collected over three months, the model reduced manual review volume by 31% compared with the manufacturer default threshold, while achieving sensitivity of 0.96. Calibration was assessed with reliability diagrams; the ensemble required isotonic regression post-hoc calibration to bring expected calibration error below 0.04.

title: Threshold optimisation under asymmetric misclassification costs: a review and empirical comparison on clinical tabular datasets
abstract: Classification thresholds are routinely left at the default 0.5 in many applied clinical studies despite well-established evidence that asymmetric misclassification costs make this choice suboptimal. This paper reviews threshold selection methods including cost-minimisation, F-beta maximisation, utility-maximisation, and the Youden index, and provides an empirical comparison across twelve publicly deposited and in-house clinical tabular datasets ranging from 500 to 28,000 samples. Datasets cover six disease areas including cardiovascular risk, diabetes complications, and haematological malignancy. The comparison uses nested cross-validation to avoid threshold selection bias. Results show that cost-minimisation and F-beta methods are broadly equivalent when cost ratios are specified accurately, but that the Youden index consistently underperforms in high-imbalance settings with imbalance ratios above 1:15. The paper also provides guidance on eliciting cost ratios from clinical stakeholders and documents a structured interview protocol used with six clinicians at a teaching hospital in Novi Sad.

title: Kernel support vector machines for multiclass thyroid function classification from biochemical panels
abstract: Thyroid function is routinely assessed through a panel of three to five serum markers. Clinical guidelines define five functional categories—overt hypothyroidism, subclinical hypothyroidism, euthyroid, subclinical hyperthyroidism, and overt hyperthyroidism—but borderline cases generate significant inter-clinician disagreement. We trained one-vs-one kernel SVMs with radial basis function kernels on 6,730 labelled thyroid panels collected between 2012 and 2017 at two endocrinology outpatient clinics. Multiclass probability calibration used Platt scaling extended to the one-vs-one scheme. Overall accuracy on a stratified test split of 1,346 samples reached 88.3%. The two subclinical categories were most often confused, with confusion concentrated in samples where TSH differed from the midpoint of the reference range by less than 0.8 mIU/L. A confidence threshold was set such that panels with posterior probability below 0.65 for any predicted class were flagged for clinical review; this threshold captured 94% of misclassified cases at a flag rate of 21%.

title: An introduction to cost-sensitive classification methods in clinical laboratory informatics
abstract: This book chapter provides a self-contained introduction to cost-sensitive classification intended for laboratory informaticians and biostatisticians with limited background in machine learning. It covers the formulation of asymmetric loss functions, the construction of cost matrices from clinical outcome data, threshold-moving as a post-hoc strategy, and direct cost-minimising training through modified learning objectives. Each concept is illustrated with worked examples drawn from haematology, microbiology, and clinical chemistry laboratory settings. The chapter also discusses common pitfalls, including the use of accuracy as a performance metric when classes are imbalanced, the conflation of probabilistic calibration with discrimination, and the failure to propagate cost assumptions into cross-validation. Pseudocode is provided for the main algorithms. The target audience is practitioners who need to communicate method choices to clinical colleagues and regulatory reviewers.

title: Bayesian network classifiers for differential diagnosis support in autoimmune liver disease
abstract: Autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis present with overlapping serological and biochemical profiles. Differential diagnosis relies on combinations of antibody titres, liver enzyme ratios, and imaging findings that are difficult to integrate without computational assistance. We constructed naive Bayes and tree-augmented naive Bayes (TAN) classifiers using 38 clinical variables recorded for 872 patients diagnosed at hepatology units in Novi Sad and Zagreb between 2009 and 2016. Class sizes were 311, 349, and 212 for the three conditions. TAN outperformed naive Bayes on macro-averaged F1 (0.79 vs 0.73) and was more robust to missing values introduced by simulating real-world data gaps at rates of 10%, 20%, and 30%. Sensitivity analysis over prior distributions for the Bayesian parameter estimates showed stable rankings across all three missingness levels. The model's conditional probability tables were made interpretable for clinicians by displaying the five most influential variable combinations per class.

title: Performance evaluation metrics for binary classifiers in laboratory medicine: a structured comparison
abstract: Numerous metrics are available for evaluating binary classifiers, yet laboratory medicine publications disproportionately report sensitivity and specificity to the exclusion of metrics that account for prevalence and cost structure. This methodological paper examines twelve metrics—including accuracy, balanced accuracy, F1, F-beta, Matthew's correlation coefficient (MCC), AUROC, AUPRC, geometric mean, Cohen's kappa, net benefit, and two cost-weighted variants—across a simulation study spanning five prevalence levels (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%) and three classifier quality levels. Results show MCC and net benefit are the most informative single-metric summaries across the prevalence range examined. The paper provides a decision guide mapping clinical question type to metric selection. A secondary analysis applied the framework to fourteen published laboratory classification studies, finding that 11 of 14 would have drawn different conclusions about classifier superiority had they used prevalence-adjusted metrics. Recommendations are made for reporting standards in laboratory informatics publications.

title: Combining laboratory and patient history data for 72-hour prediction of hypoglycaemic episodes in insulin-treated type 2 diabetes
abstract: Hypoglycaemic episodes in insulin-treated type 2 diabetes patients are associated with significant morbidity but are difficult to predict from laboratory data alone. We constructed a two-source feature set combining 14 routine biochemical markers with 9 patient-history variables including insulin dose, meal regularity score, and prior episode count, recorded for 2,640 outpatients over 36 months. Prediction targets were hypoglycaemic episodes confirmed by glucose monitor readings below 3.9 mmol/L within a 72-hour horizon. Random forests, logistic regression, and naive Bayes were trained on 80% of the data and evaluated on the remaining 20%. The combined feature set improved F1 from 0.48 (laboratory-only) to 0.61 (combined) for random forests. Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) values identified prior episode count, HbA1c, and insulin dose as the three highest-magnitude contributors. Threshold was set at 0.38 rather than 0.5 to increase sensitivity, following the cost analysis agreed with the clinical partner.

title: Evaluating active learning strategies for iterative labelling of ambiguous laboratory records
abstract: Obtaining expert labels for clinical laboratory records is expensive. Active learning reduces annotation cost by querying an oracle for the most informative unlabelled instances. This study evaluated four active learning strategies—uncertainty sampling, query-by-committee, expected model change, and core-set selection—in a simulation of iterative label acquisition for a coagulation disorder classification task with an initial labelled pool of 200 records out of 5,500 total. Queries were simulated using a held-out label set as the oracle. Uncertainty sampling and query-by-committee reached 90% of fully supervised F1 after approximately 700 and 750 labels respectively, while random sampling required 1,100 labels to reach the same level. Core-set selection underperformed on this dataset, likely due to the relatively low dimensionality (16 features). Practical considerations for deploying active learning in a real laboratory workflow, including oracle fatigue and label noise, are discussed.
venue: Proceedings of the BioMedData Workshop at ECML-PKDD 2026

title: Early work on rule extraction from trained neural classifiers applied to clinical biochemistry data
abstract: Neural classifiers trained on clinical laboratory data are difficult to inspect, yet clinical adoption depends on the ability to articulate decision logic. This early study explored three rule extraction methods—TREPAN, pedagogical rule extraction, and decompositional extraction—applied to a three-layer feedforward network trained on 1,840 samples from a clinical biochemistry dataset covering 17 analytes and four diagnostic classes related to hepatic function. Networks were trained with early stopping using 15% validation hold-out. TREPAN produced the most compact rule sets (median 12 rules per class) while maintaining fidelity above 0.88 against network predictions on test data. Decompositional methods produced more rules but captured local network structure more faithfully. Human-readable rule sets were presented to two hepatologists who rated them for clinical plausibility; TREPAN rules received higher plausibility ratings. The study is limited by the modest dataset size and the relatively simple network architecture used.

title: Preprint: Conformal prediction intervals for clinical laboratory classification under distributional shift
abstract: Trained classifiers deployed in clinical laboratories may encounter distributional shift caused by reagent lot changes, analyser recalibration, or seasonal variation in patient population. Conformal prediction offers a framework for attaching valid marginal coverage guarantees to classifier outputs without retraining, under the assumption of exchangeability. This preprint investigates the coverage and efficiency of split conformal prediction sets applied to four laboratory classification tasks when calibration and test data are drawn from different six-month periods spanning up to two years. Coverage guarantees were maintained at the nominal 90% level in all within-year comparisons but degraded to 82–85% for the largest temporal gaps. Adaptive conformal methods that reweight the calibration set by estimated density ratio partially restored coverage. Prediction set sizes increased substantially under shift, which can serve as a diagnostic signal for laboratory staff that recalibration of the model may be warranted. All code and anonymised summary statistics are deposited in the institutional repository.

title: Queuing Models for Spot-Instance Markets: Bidding Strategies Under Preemption Risk
abstract: Cloud providers offer preemptible compute instances at discounted prices, but tasks running on such instances may be interrupted when market demand rises above supply. This paper models a batch-processing workload that uses a mix of on-demand and preemptible instances as an M[X]/M/c queue with unreliable servers, where server failures correspond to preemption events governed by an exogenous price process modelled as a two-state continuous-time Markov chain. The stationary distribution is derived numerically using truncated state-space methods. A bidding strategy that sets the maximum acceptable spot price as a function of the remaining job deadline and estimated preemption rate is derived from the first-passage time distribution. Experiments use preemption rate estimates from a 30-day synthetic price series generated with parameters drawn from published empirical studies of spot markets. The bidding strategy achieves a 22 percent cost reduction over a fixed-bid baseline while maintaining deadline miss probability below 5 percent.

title: Competency Outcome Modelling in Mathematics Education: A Mixed-Effects Survival Analysis of Time-to-Mastery
abstract: This paper frames competency attainment in undergraduate mathematics as a time-to-event outcome and applies mixed-effects parametric survival models to longitudinal assessment data. Records from 2,240 students completing a multi-module calculus sequence over five academic years were analysed. The outcome was defined as the week in which a student first demonstrated sustained mastery on adaptive quizzes, operationalised as three consecutive passing scores above 80 %. A log-logistic accelerated failure time model with random student and instructor intercepts provided the best fit (log-likelihood ratio test against Weibull, p < 0.001). Time-to-mastery was significantly shortened by higher prior achievement scores and by weekly formative quiz completion, and was lengthened by patterns of concentrated last-minute access. The paper contributes a reusable feature engineering pipeline for Moodle log data and provides worked R code as a supplementary appendix.

title: Estimation of Helmert Transformation Parameters between the Yugoslav State Coordinate System and ETRS89 for the Vojvodina Region
abstract: The Yugoslav state coordinate system (Gauss–Krüger projection, Bessel ellipsoid) remains embedded in cadastral records across the Vojvodina lowland plain. This study estimated a seven-parameter Helmert transformation linking that legacy system to ETRS89 using 114 identical points distributed across Vojvodina, observed with dual-frequency GNSS receivers and coordinated in both systems. Residual analysis showed that a single regional set of transformation parameters is insufficient at the sub-decimetre level because of systematic distortions inherited from the original triangulation network. A piecewise affine correction grid was fitted to the residuals on a 10 km × 10 km tile scheme, reducing the RMS positional discrepancy from 0.18 m to 0.04 m. The resulting correction surface was encoded as a NTv2-format grid shift file compatible with standard geodetic software. The approach was validated on an independent set of 22 check points not used in the fitting. Practical implications for cadastral boundary restitution are discussed.

title: Constrained Least-Squares Adjustment for Cadastral Boundary Networks with Legal Holdback Conditions
abstract: When modernising cadastral maps in areas with recorded boundary disputes or legal holdbacks, certain boundary segments must be held fixed while adjacent coordinates are adjusted freely. This paper presents a constrained least-squares formulation that accommodates mixed fixing conditions, derived from observations collected during a pilot re-survey of three cadastral sheets in the municipality of Sremska Mitrovica. The network comprised 1 247 boundary corners, of which 84 carried legal holdback constraints. The constraint matrix was sparse, and an efficient block-sparse Cholesky solver was adapted to handle it without dense matrix inversion. Adjusted coordinates for the free corners showed average displacement of 0.31 m relative to the original digitised positions, with a maximum of 1.72 m in areas of accumulated digitising error. Post-adjustment residuals satisfied a chi-squared goodness-of-fit test at the 95 % confidence level. The procedure was implemented as a prototype module within the national cadastral update workflow.

title: Assessment of CORS Network Geometry in Vojvodina and Its Effect on Single-Epoch RTK Positioning Accuracy
abstract: A continuously operating reference station (CORS) network provides the backbone for RTK positioning in cadastral and engineering surveys. This study assessed how the geometric configuration of seven CORS stations distributed across Vojvodina affects single-epoch horizontal and vertical accuracy for rover positions within the network polygon. Using data collected over 90 days in 2013, single-epoch solutions were computed at 224 test locations and compared to static post-processed references. Horizontal 95th-percentile accuracy ranged from 1.4 cm near network centres to 4.8 cm near the network boundary. Vertical accuracy was 1.5–3.0 times worse than horizontal at all test locations. The dilution of precision (DOP) values and ionospheric gradient estimates correlated with accuracy degradation during geomagnetically disturbed periods, identified using Kp-index data. Recommendations are given for the placement of two additional stations to reduce the maximum horizontal uncertainty to below 2.5 cm across the entire province.

title: Adjustment of a Mixed GNSS–Total Station Network for Cadastral Re-survey in Peri-Urban Zones
abstract: Peri-urban land parcels in Serbian municipalities undergoing rezoning frequently require re-survey because historical boundary coordinates carry decimetric errors that are unacceptable for subdivision applications. This paper presents an adjustment strategy for a mixed network combining GNSS static baselines and total-station traverse observations, applied to a 47-parcel re-survey in a peri-urban zone of Novi Sad. The combined adjustment was performed using a Gauss–Markov model with 214 observations and 89 unknowns. Stochastic modelling of total-station distance and direction measurements used manufacturer-specified standard deviations augmented by temperature-correction factors measured on site. The final adjusted coordinates showed a maximum internal closure error of 6 mm. Comparison with independently acquired RTK check points confirmed agreement within 1.2 cm (2D RMS). The paper discusses practical criteria for selecting which boundary corners warrant GNSS versus total-station observation in similar urban fringe settings.

title: Evaluating the Suitability of Publicly Available Digital Elevation Models for Orthometric Height Transfer in Flat Terrain
abstract: Cadastral surveys in the Pannonian lowland require orthometric heights for drainage and infrastructure planning. Acquiring spirit-levelled heights across large flat areas is expensive, prompting interest in substituting digital elevation model (DEM) data for coarse height transfer. This study compared three publicly available DEMs—a radar-based 30 m resolution product, a 12.5 m radar product, and a LiDAR-derived 1 m DEM produced by a regional mapping agency—against 512 precise spirit-levelled benchmarks distributed across the municipality of Vrbas. The LiDAR DEM reproduced benchmark heights with a standard deviation of 0.08 m, compared to 0.31 m and 0.44 m for the two radar products. Systematic height biases of 0.12–0.22 m were detected in the radar DEMs, likely caused by vegetation signal penetration. The results suggest that LiDAR DEMs can substitute for levelling in non-engineering cadastral work where height accuracy requirements are 0.15 m or coarser.

title: Transformation Grid Densification Using Additional Trigonometric Points from the Second-Order National Network
abstract: The NTv2 correction grid estimated in earlier work for Vojvodina relied exclusively on GPS-observed first-order trigonometric points. This follow-up study investigates whether incorporating 278 second-order trigonometric points, re-observed with static GNSS over two field campaigns in 2015 and 2016, reduces the interpolation error of the correction grid. Densification reduced the mean grid spacing from 10 km to approximately 4.5 km over the populated part of Vojvodina. Cross-validation using leave-one-out tests showed that the densified grid reduced the RMS transformation residual from 4.1 cm to 2.6 cm. In areas with historically dense triangulation coverage, the improvement was marginal (less than 3 mm), whereas in the poorly controlled southern Bačka corridor, improvement exceeded 2 cm. The densified grid file and its quality assessment layer are made available through a publicly accessible repository maintained by the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

title: Boundary Reconstruction from Destroyed Monuments: A Least-Squares Restoration Procedure Using Deed Measurements and Photogrammetric Evidence
abstract: In areas affected by construction disturbance or agricultural machinery damage, physical boundary monuments are frequently displaced or destroyed. Legal re-establishment of boundaries in Serbian cadastral law requires reconciling deed distances and angles with any surviving physical evidence. This paper proposes a formal least-squares restoration procedure that treats deed measurements as stochastic observations with scale-dependent standard deviations estimated from measurement-era instrument specifications. The procedure was tested on 14 boundary reconstruction cases drawn from legal disputes in the Novi Sad municipal area between 2012 and 2018, in which ground-truth was available from contemporaneous GNSS surveys conducted before disturbance. The restored positions agreed with the pre-disturbance GNSS positions with a 2D RMS of 0.09 m, compared to 0.34 m for the standard administrative procedure currently in use. Photogrammetric evidence from archival aerial photographs contributed useful tie constraints in six of the fourteen cases.

title: Integrating UAV-Derived Orthophotos into Cadastral Parcel Update Workflows: Geometric Accuracy and Procedural Considerations
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry produces sub-10 cm orthophotos at low cost, making it attractive for updating cadastral records in areas where last survey dates exceed 20 years. This study assessed the integration of UAV-derived orthophotos into the parcel update workflow of two cadastral municipalities in Srem, covering 3 800 parcels over a combined area of 18 km². Ground control points were established using RTK GNSS at a density of one per 4 hectares. The orthophotos achieved a horizontal RMSE of 0.06 m relative to independent check points. Parcel boundaries digitised from the orthophotos were compared to simultaneously collected RTK boundary surveys: 87 % of boundaries matched within 0.15 m, while 6 % required field verification due to vegetation obscuring corners. The procedural requirements under the Serbian Cadastre Act for accepting UAV-derived coordinates as legal survey documents are reviewed, and a compliant workflow is outlined.

title: Cross-Border Cadastral Data Harmonisation along the Serbian–Hungarian Boundary Strip
abstract: Land parcels on opposite sides of international boundaries are maintained in separate cadastral systems with different reference frames, projection systems, and attribute schemas. This paper presents a harmonisation exercise for a 6 km wide strip on both sides of the Serbian–Hungarian boundary, covering approximately 1 100 parcels, undertaken as part of a cross-border cooperation programme. Coordinate transformation between ETRS89/EOV (Hungarian national grid) and ETRS89/Serbian TM was performed using validated parameters, reducing boundary crossing discrepancies from a median of 0.92 m to 0.07 m. Attribute harmonisation required mapping 34 Hungarian land-use codes to 27 Serbian equivalents, with 8 % of parcels flagged as ambiguous. The study identified 19 parcels where both national cadastres claimed ownership, constituting potential boundary anomalies forwarded to the respective authorities. Lessons for future cross-border cadastral integration are summarised.

title: Quality Indicators for Digital Cadastral Maps: A Framework Applied to Five Cadastral Municipalities in Serbia
abstract: Digital cadastral maps in Serbia originate from diverse sources—analogue scans, photogrammetric restitution, GNSS surveys and computerised total-station traverses—leading to highly variable positional quality. This paper proposes a set of seven measurable quality indicators covering positional accuracy, topological completeness, temporal currency, attribute consistency, boundary closure, monument availability and datum traceability. Each indicator is assigned a scoring function and the indicators are aggregated into a composite quality index. The framework was applied to five cadastral municipalities in Serbia spanning urban, peri-urban and rural contexts, using data from the national cadastral information system and from independent field checks at 1 450 boundary corners. Composite index scores ranged from 0.41 (a rural municipality with 1970s-era analogue surveys) to 0.83 (an urban municipality recently re-surveyed with GNSS). The framework is proposed as a decision support tool for prioritising cadastral renewal investment.

title: Stochastic Modelling of GNSS Multipath in Agricultural Settings and Its Effect on Cadastral Boundary Determination
abstract: Cadastral re-surveys in Vojvodina's agricultural landscape are conducted year-round, including during periods when tall maize or sunflower crops are present. Multipath signals reflected from crop canopies degrade GNSS positioning accuracy in ways not captured by standard elevation-dependent weighting models. This study collected 48 hours of GPS and GLONASS observations at five test points in a maize field near Temerin using geodetic dual-frequency receivers, spanning crop heights from 0.4 m to 2.4 m. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) data were used to derive site-specific stochastic models following a carrier-smoothed pseudorange approach. Applying the SNR-based stochastic model instead of the standard elevation-dependent model reduced the 3D RMS error from 2.8 cm to 1.4 cm for the tallest crop condition. For boundary determination, this improvement is most consequential for corners located within 5 m of dense canopy edges. Practical guidance for field survey scheduling and receiver placement is provided.

title: Automated Detection of Inconsistent Parcel Geometries in Large Cadastral Databases Using Graph-Based Topology Analysis
abstract: National cadastral databases in the Western Balkans contain tens of millions of parcel records accumulated over decades, with topology errors introduced during successive digitisation and update campaigns. Manual inspection is infeasible at scale. This paper describes a graph-based topology analysis pipeline in which parcel boundaries are represented as a planar graph and geometric inconsistencies—overlaps, gaps, slivers, dangling edges, and non-manifold nodes—are detected using efficient traversal algorithms. The pipeline was run on the full cadastral database of the Vojvodina province, comprising approximately 4.3 million parcels. Processing time on a standard server was under 3.5 hours. The analysis identified 61 400 parcels (1.43 % of total) with at least one reportable inconsistency, classified into five severity levels. Spatial clustering of errors revealed three zones where systematic digitisation errors from a 1988 aerial mapping campaign had propagated across municipal boundaries. The pipeline output is formatted as a GeoPackage layer compatible with the national cadastral information system.

title: Ground filtering in airborne LiDAR data over flat agricultural terrain using an adaptive TIN densification algorithm
abstract: Accurate ground point extraction is a prerequisite for generating reliable digital terrain models in lowland regions with sparse vertical relief. This study evaluates an adaptive triangulated irregular network densification algorithm applied to airborne LiDAR strips acquired over three test sites in the Vojvodina plain covering approximately 180 km². The algorithm iteratively classifies points as ground or non-ground by comparing each candidate point's distance to the current TIN surface against an angle threshold. Threshold sensitivity was assessed across tile sizes of 250 m, 500 m, and 1000 m. Results show that a tile size of 500 m with an angle threshold of 8° minimises root mean square error against 420 reference survey points, yielding an RMSE of 0.09 m. The method outperforms a fixed-window progressive morphological filter on sites with abrupt dyke structures, reducing commission errors by 14 percentage points. Processing time for the full 180 km² dataset on a four-core workstation was 38 minutes. The study concludes that tile size has greater influence on accuracy than angle threshold for flat terrain, and recommends parameter ranges for similar lowland environments in Central Europe.

title: Transfer learning for point cloud classification across sensor configurations and flight altitudes
abstract: Models trained on airborne LiDAR data from one sensor and flight configuration frequently degrade when applied to data from a different setup, limiting operational reuse. This study investigates transfer learning strategies for a random forest and a graph convolutional network trained on data acquired at 800 m altitude with a pushbroom scanner, then evaluated on data acquired at 1500 m with a discrete-return scanner over the same geographic area. Without adaptation, overall accuracy dropped by 18 percentage points for the graph convolutional network and 11 points for the random forest. Three adaptation strategies were compared: feature standardisation, fine-tuning on 5% target-domain labelled data, and domain-adversarial training. Fine-tuning with 5% labelled data recovered accuracy to within 3 percentage points of the source-domain baseline for both models. Feature standardisation alone recovered 6 percentage points but was insufficient for building and vegetation classes where point density differences are most pronounced. Domain-adversarial training showed marginal improvement over feature standardisation at substantially higher computational cost. Practical recommendations for survey operators seeking to reuse existing classification models are provided.

title: Monument Thermal Expansion Effects on Short-Period Vertical GNSS Signals at Forced-Centered Pillar Stations
abstract: Forced-centring pillars made of reinforced concrete are widely used for permanent GNSS stations in the Western Balkans. This study quantified thermally induced vertical displacements at four such monuments using co-located high-resolution temperature sensors and a tiltmeter installed at the base of each pillar. Continuous observations spanning 18 months were processed with Precise Point Positioning using final IGS products. Apparent vertical velocities extracted before and after applying a temperature-dependent correction differed by up to 0.4 mm/yr at south-facing monuments. A simple two-parameter thermal-expansion model, calibrated per monument, reduced the diurnal vertical scatter from 1.8 mm to 0.6 mm RMS. The findings suggest that uncorrected thermal monument motion introduces a detectable bias in long-term velocity estimates in continental climates with strong annual temperature amplitude, and that monument-level instrumentation is a cost-effective mitigation strategy.

title: Uticaj sadržaja grafita na tribološko ponašanje PA6 kompozita u uslovima suvog klizanja
abstract: U radu su ispitivana tribološka svojstva poliamida 6 (PA6) punjenog grafitom u masenim udelima od 2, 5, 10 i 15 %. Uzorci su izrađeni postupkom mešanja u rastopljenom stanju i kompresionog presovanja. Tribološka ispitivanja sprovedena su na pin-on-disc tribometru pri normalnim silama od 5 N i 10 N i kliznoj brzini od 0,1 m/s, u suvim uslovima na vazduhu pri sobnoj temperaturi. Specifična stopa habanja i koeficijent trenja mereni su u intervalima od 500 m kliznog puta do ukupno 3000 m. Rezultati su pokazali da dodatak grafita od 10 mas. % dovodi do smanjenja koeficijenta trenja sa 0,41 na 0,19 u poređenju sa čistim PA6, dok je specifična stopa habanja opala za oko 62 %. SEM analizom površina habanja utvrđeno je formiranje kontinualnog transfernog filma na čeličnoj ploči pri udelima grafita iznad 5 mas. %. Prekomerni udeo od 15 mas. % uzrokovao je krtost matrice i porast stope habanja. Rezultati ukazuju da PA6 sa 10 mas. % grafita predstavlja pogodan materijal za klizne elemente koji rade bez podmazivanja.

title: Friction and Wear Characteristics of PTFE-Based Composites Filled with MoS2 and h-BN Under Dry Sliding Conditions Relevant to Food-Contact Applications
abstract: This study examined the tribological performance of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) composites containing molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), and their hybrid mixtures at total filler loadings of 5 wt% and 10 wt%. Composite specimens were prepared by cold isostatic pressing followed by sintering at 375 °C. Sliding tests were conducted on a pin-on-disc apparatus against a 316L stainless steel counterface, using applied loads of 10 N and 20 N at a constant sliding speed of 0.05 m/s, in ambient air at 23 °C and 45 % relative humidity. Total sliding distance was set at 5000 m. The hybrid filler (equal parts MoS2 and h-BN, 10 wt% total) yielded the lowest steady-state coefficient of friction (0.09 ± 0.01) and a specific wear rate of 2.8 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/(N·m), compared to 4.1 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/(N·m) for pure PTFE. Profilometric analysis of worn surfaces confirmed shallower scratch grooves for hybrid composites. Migration behaviour of filler particles was assessed by EDX mapping of the transfer film. The results support the use of PTFE–MoS2–h-BN composites in unpowered sliding guides within food conveyors, where lubricant contamination of the product is inadmissible.

title: Primena SEM/EDX analize u identifikaciji mehanizama habanja samopodmazujućih polimernih kliznih umetaka za konvejere u prehrambenoj industriji
abstract: Rad prikazuje metodologiju skenirajuće elektronske mikroskopije (SEM) i energijsko-disperzivne spektroskopije X-zraka (EDX) u analizi površina habanja polimernih umetaka nakon eksploatacionih testova na simulatoru lančanog konvejera za prehrambenu industriju. Ispitivani su uzorci od PA6 punjenog PTFE (10 mas. %) i čistog PA6 koji su radili 200 sati pri opterećenju 50 N i kliznoj brzini 0,08 m/s uz intermitentno zaustavljanje radi simulacije radnog ciklusa. SEM analizom utvrđeni su dominantni mehanizmi abrazije i adhezije kod čistog PA6, dok je kod PA6/PTFE kompozita registrovano pretežno koheziono habanje sa jednolikim transfernim filmom na čeličnoj šini. EDX mapiranjem detektovano je prisustvo fluora u transfernom filmu, što potvrđuje aktivnu ulogu PTFE čestica u smanjenju adhezionih sila. Merenja hrapavosti Ra umetaka pre i posle testa pokazala su da PA6/PTFE umetci zadržavaju Ra ispod 0,8 µm tokom celog trajanja testa. Rezultati upućuju da SEM/EDX analiza može poslužiti kao rutinska metoda procene podobnosti materijala u postupcima kvalifikacije kliznih elemenata.

title: Effect of Sliding Speed and Contact Pressure on the Tribological Performance of PEEK–PTFE Composite Guides in Simulated Poultry Processing Conditions
abstract: Polyether ether ketone (PEEK) filled with 15 wt% PTFE was evaluated as a candidate material for chain guide strips in poultry slaughtering and deboning lines, where intermittent water exposure and stringent hygiene requirements restrict conventional lubrication. A reciprocating tribometer was used to replicate the sliding kinematics of a typical chain link running over a guide strip. Three contact pressures (0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 MPa) and two sliding speeds (0.06 and 0.12 m/s) were tested, each for a sliding distance of 2000 m. Tests were run under dry conditions and in the presence of a thin condensation water film (relative humidity 95 %) to approximate actual processing environment humidity. Under dry conditions, increasing contact pressure from 0.5 to 1.5 MPa raised the coefficient of friction from 0.11 to 0.17 and increased the specific wear rate by a factor of 2.4. The presence of surface moisture reduced friction by approximately 18 % at all pressure levels but accelerated subsurface fatigue cracking as revealed by cross-sectional SEM. PEEK–PTFE outperformed standard ultrahigh-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) guides at higher contact pressures, with a wear rate 3.1 times lower at 1.5 MPa. The data suggest that PEEK–PTFE is suitable for high-load chain guide applications in humid food processing environments, provided that maintenance intervals account for the increased subsurface damage observed under wet contact.
venue: Journal of Polymer Engineering and Tribology

title: Bacterial community composition in a municipal drinking water distribution network in northern Serbia assessed by DGGE fingerprinting
abstract: Denaturing gradient gel electrophoresis (DGGE) of 16S rRNA gene fragments was used to characterise bacterial communities at twelve sampling points along a mid-sized municipal distribution network in Vojvodina. Samples were collected across four seasons over one calendar year, yielding 48 profiles. Dominant bands were excised, cloned, and sequenced. Proteobacteria accounted for approximately 61 % of recovered sequences, with Sphingomonadales and Burkholderiales most frequently detected. Seasonal shifts were statistically significant (ANOSIM R = 0.41, p < 0.01), with higher community richness observed in summer months correlating with elevated water temperature and longer hydraulic residence times. Opportunistic pathogens of the genus Acinetobacter were detected at four points during summer sampling. The study established a community baseline for the network and identified two hydraulically stagnant dead-end zones as consistent hotspots for microbial diversity, informing subsequent flushing protocol recommendations to the utility operator.

title: Occurrence and amplification risk of Legionella pneumophila in hot water systems of student dormitories
abstract: Hot water systems of eight student dormitory buildings at two universities in Vojvodina were surveyed for Legionella pneumophila over two consecutive winters. Culture on BCYE agar and quantitative PCR targeting the mip gene were used in parallel. Legionella pneumophila was detected by qPCR in 34 of 112 samples (30 %), while culture confirmation was obtained from 11 samples (10 %). Concentrations in positive samples ranged from 100 to 8 400 CFU/L by culture and from 200 to 52 000 gene copies/L by qPCR. Thermal profiling showed that distal outlets had water temperatures below 50 °C in 78 % of measurements, falling into the proliferation-permissive range. Buildings with thermostatic mixing valves set below manufacturer guidelines showed the highest detection rates. The discrepancy between culture and qPCR results is discussed in relation to viable but non-culturable states. Corrective temperature management recommendations were communicated to facility managers.

title: Amplicon sequencing of 16S rRNA hypervariable regions V3–V4 reveals stratified microbial communities along a drinking water distribution gradient
abstract: Illumina MiSeq sequencing of 16S rRNA V3–V4 amplicons was applied to 36 water samples and 18 pipe biofilm swab samples collected along a 22-kilometre distribution network segment in Vojvodina. Sampling covered source water, post-treatment effluent, mid-network, and consumer-end points. Alpha diversity increased significantly from treatment plant effluent to consumer-end samples (Shannon index: mean 2.1 vs. 3.8; Wilcoxon p < 0.001). Beta diversity analysis (unweighted UniFrac) separated samples into four statistically distinct clusters corresponding to distance from treatment. Nitrifying bacteria, particularly Nitrospira, increased in relative abundance with network distance. Biofilm communities were substantially less diverse than planktonic counterparts (mean richness 112 vs. 289 OTUs) but enriched in Proteobacteria and Bacteroidota. Network distance and pipe material (PVC vs. ductile iron) were the strongest predictors of community composition in a PERMANOVA model (combined R² = 0.44). Raw sequence data were deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive.

title: Microbial community shifts in a recirculating cooling water system following transition from chlorine-based to UV-based disinfection
abstract: A controlled before-after study was conducted at a plastic manufacturing facility in Sremska Mitrovica that replaced continuous chlorination with medium-pressure UV disinfection in its cooling circuit. Water samples were collected six times before and eight times after transition over a total of 18 months. 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (V4 region, MiSeq) and HPC were used alongside physicochemical monitoring. After transition, HPC counts increased moderately (median 1.4 × 10³ vs. 3.1 × 10³ CFU/mL), while alpha diversity declined and community composition shifted significantly (PERMANOVA R² = 0.29, p < 0.01). Chlorine-resistant Mycobacterium-affiliated reads, comprising 7 % of reads before transition, were undetectable post-transition; Sphingomonadales increased from 9 % to 21 % of reads. Biofilm visual scoring of heat exchanger plates showed no significant difference between regimes over the study period. The study provides operational community dynamics data relevant to facilities evaluating disinfection alternatives.

title: Evaluation of polyphosphate and silicate-based scale and corrosion inhibitors on biofilm development in simulated drinking water pipes
abstract: Polyphosphate and silicate corrosion inhibitors are widely dosed into drinking water networks, yet their effects on biofilm community development are poorly characterised at the molecular level. A laboratory pipe-loop system using polyethylene tubing was operated under controlled conditions (temperature 18 °C, flow velocity 0.3 m/s, residence time 8 h) for 90 days. Four treatment arms were run in triplicate: chlorinated control, polyphosphate-dosed, silicate-dosed, and combined dose. Biofilm coupons were harvested at days 30, 60, and 90. 16S rRNA sequencing showed that polyphosphate dosing consistently elevated the relative abundance of Betaproteobacteriales compared to controls, consistent with increased phosphorus availability. Total biofilm protein was significantly higher in polyphosphate arms at day 60 (p = 0.03, Kruskal–Wallis with post-hoc Dunn). Silicate dosing had no significant effect on community composition or biomass at the concentrations tested. Results suggest that polyphosphate dosing practices deserve consideration alongside corrosion control objectives when optimising water treatment.

title: Short-term effects of pipe material replacement on drinking water biofilm composition: a case study from a distribution network rehabilitation project
abstract: During a scheduled pipeline rehabilitation programme in a Vojvodina municipality, six sections of cast iron mains (in service for 35–50 years) were replaced with high-density polyethylene pipes. Biofilm and bulk water samples were collected two weeks before replacement and at 1, 4, 12, and 24 weeks after commissioning of the new pipes. 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing was combined with ATP bioluminescence measurements as a proxy for total active biomass. ATP levels in water leaving new HDPE sections were elevated during the first four weeks (mean 42 ng/L vs. 11 ng/L baseline) before declining. Community composition on new pipe surfaces at week 4 was dominated by Betaproteobacteria and differed markedly from the established cast iron biofilm community (Bray–Curtis dissimilarity > 0.75). By week 24 the community had partially converged towards the reference network composition. The study provides field-derived timescales for biofilm re-establishment useful for managing water quality during network rehabilitation.

title: Swelling and erosion behaviour of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose matrix tablets: effect of polymer viscosity grade and drug solubility
abstract: Hydrophilic matrix tablets prepared with three HPMC viscosity grades (K4M, K15M, K100M) and two model drugs of contrasting aqueous solubility (metoprolol succinate and ibuprofen) were characterised with respect to tablet swelling, gel layer thickness and erosion rate using digital image analysis at 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 h time points in USP Apparatus II at 50 rpm, 900 mL of pH 6.8 phosphate buffer. Gel front and erosion front positions were quantified for 12 formulation variants (n = 6 per variant). HPMC K100M produced the thickest gel layer (up to 2.8 mm at 6 h) and slowest erosion for both drugs. Drug solubility significantly modulated the contribution of diffusion versus erosion: for metoprolol succinate, erosion accounted for approximately 65% of total release at 8 h, compared with 38% for ibuprofen under identical polymer loading. A combined diffusion–erosion model fitted the experimental profiles with mean absolute percentage errors below 8% in all cases. The results confirm that polymer viscosity grade and drug solubility must be considered simultaneously when predicting mechanism-dominant release.

title: Примена Box-Behnken дизајна у оптимизацији хидрофилних матрикс таблета с контролисаним ослобађањем метформин хидрохлорида
abstract: У раду је приказана примена Box-Behnken експерименталног дизајна за оптимизацију формулације матрикс таблета с контролисаним ослобађањем метформин хидрохлорида. Независне варијабле биле су удео HPMC K15M (10–30% m/m), удео карбопола 971P (1–5% m/m) и сила компресије (8–16 kN). Зависне варијабле обухватале су: проценат ослобађања лека за 1, 4 и 8 часова (USP апарат II, 0,1 М HCl / pH 6,8 фосфатни пуфер), тврдоћу таблете и фриабилитет. Добијени резултати обрађени су методом одзивне površine, а оптимална формулација предвиђена моделом потврђена је експериментом (одступање < 5%). Оптималне вредности независних варијабли износиле су 22% HPMC, 3% карбопола и 12 kN. Профил ослобађања оптималне формулације задовољио је критеријум f2 ≥ 50 у поређењу са референтним препаратом.

title: Mechanistic dissolution modelling of HPMC matrix tablets using a moving-boundary diffusion–erosion framework: parameter estimation and predictive validation
abstract: A one-dimensional moving-boundary model describing simultaneous gel swelling, drug diffusion through the hydrated layer, and polymer erosion was implemented in MATLAB and fitted to in vitro dissolution datasets for six HPMC K15M matrix formulations containing drugs spanning a 500-fold solubility range (0.04–20 mg/mL). Model parameters—effective diffusivity, erosion rate constant, and gel–solvent interface velocity—were estimated by nonlinear least-squares optimisation against USP Apparatus II profiles collected at three pH values (1.2, 4.5, 6.8). Leave-one-out cross-validation demonstrated that the model predicts withheld dissolution profiles with root-mean-square error ≤ 6.2% across all tested conditions. Sensitivity analysis identified gel-layer diffusivity and erosion rate constant as the parameters with highest influence on the 50% dissolution time (t50), accounting collectively for over 80% of variance in a Sobol first-order analysis. The parameterised model was subsequently used in forward simulations to screen 120 virtual formulation variants, identifying compositions predicted to achieve 12-h sustained release targets, thereby illustrating its utility as a formulation design tool.

title: Ethylcellulose film coating of theophylline pellets in a laboratory-scale fluidised bed: coating thickness, porosity and in vitro release
abstract: Theophylline pellets (250–355 µm fraction) produced by extrusion–spheronisation were coated with ethylcellulose (Surelease dispersion, 15% w/w solids) in a Wurster fluidised-bed coater at coating level targets of 5, 10, 15, and 20% w/w. Coating thickness was measured by cross-sectional SEM image analysis (20 pellets per batch). Membrane porosity was assessed by mercury intrusion porosimetry. In vitro release was carried out in USP Apparatus III (dip speed 10 dpm) in pH 1.2 HCl for 2 h followed by pH 6.8 phosphate buffer for 10 h. Coating level of 15% produced a mean membrane thickness of 14.2 µm and sustained release over 12 h with zero-order kinetics (R² = 0.997). At 20% coating, pore closure was evident (porosity 0.8% vs 4.1% at 10%) and release slowed unacceptably to 58% at 12 h. A permeability model relating porosity to release rate constant was developed and validated against independent batches with mean prediction error of 9.3%.

title: In vitro–in vivo correlation (IVIVC) for sustained-release HPMC matrix tablets: a Level A correlation using deconvolution and absorption modelling
abstract: A Level A IVIVC was developed for sustained-release metoprolol succinate HPMC K100M matrix tablets using in vitro dissolution data from USP Apparatus II (pH 6.8, 75 rpm) and published in vivo plasma concentration–time profiles from an open-label crossover study in 12 healthy volunteers. Numerical deconvolution (Wagner–Nelson method) was used to estimate in vivo drug input rates, and a one-compartment absorption model was applied to parameterise the in vivo dissolution process. The in vitro–in vivo time scaling factor was 1.18, indicating moderately faster in vitro release. The resulting IVIVC demonstrated R² = 0.963 between predicted and observed Cmax and AUC0–12h across five formulation variants differing in HPMC content (15–35% w/w). Internal predictability was assessed: mean prediction errors were 7.8% for Cmax and 5.4% for AUC, within FDA Guidance thresholds. The established correlation was used to set dissolution specifications bracketing the in vivo-relevant release window.

title: Dissolution model-informed design space definition for HPMC matrix tablets: a Quality by Design case study
abstract: A mechanistic dissolution model, previously validated for HPMC K15M matrices, was integrated into a QbD design space definition exercise for a once-daily sustained-release tablet containing a BCS Class II drug (simulated solubility 0.12 mg/mL at pH 6.8). Critical material attributes (HPMC viscosity grade, drug particle size d50) and critical process parameters (compaction pressure, granulation endpoint) were propagated through the model to predict their combined effect on the dissolution design space. Monte Carlo simulations (10,000 runs) were used to map the probability of meeting the dissolution acceptance criteria (Q ≥ 70% at 12 h) across the factor space. A proven acceptable range was identified where HPMC K15M content between 20–28%, drug d50 between 25–60 µm, and compaction force between 10–15 kN yielded > 95% probability of compliance. The approach was prospectively confirmed by manufacturing and testing 18 verification batches; 17 met specifications. The study illustrates how mechanistic modelling can reduce the experimental burden in early formulation development.

title: Comparative dissolution behaviour of generic and reference sustained-release doxazosin mesylate matrix tablets marketed in the Western Balkans: f2 analysis and mechanistic interpretation
abstract: Seven sustained-release doxazosin mesylate 4 mg matrix tablet products available on pharmacy markets in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia were subjected to comparative dissolution testing using USP Apparatus II (50 rpm, 900 mL, pH 6.8 phosphate buffer, 37 °C) at 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 h (n = 12 per product). Similarity factors (f2) were calculated against the reference product. Three generics failed the f2 ≥ 50 similarity criterion, releasing ≥ 85% drug within 6 h compared with 62% for the reference. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy of tablet cross-sections revealed differences in polymer distribution and particle morphology consistent with varying HPMC grades. Application of the mechanistic diffusion–erosion model to the failing generics indicated that erosion rate constants two- to threefold higher than the reference product explained the accelerated release. The findings highlight the need for mechanistic dissolution testing protocols in generic approval processes in the region.

title: Predicting the effect of pellet size and coating thickness on in vitro dissolution from multiparticulate capsules using a distributed-parameter model
abstract: A distributed-parameter mathematical model was developed to describe drug release from a population of coated pellets enclosed in a hard gelatin capsule, accounting for variability in pellet diameter (log-normal distribution, σ = 0.08–0.22) and ethylcellulose membrane thickness (CV = 5–18%). The model treated each pellet as an independent diffusion cell and summed contributions weighted by the respective size and thickness distributions, which were characterised experimentally by laser diffraction and confocal microscopy on three independent batches of diclofenac sodium pellets. Model predictions were compared with USP Apparatus III dissolution profiles (10 dpm, pH 6.8, 37 °C). The model reproduced the dissolution curves with RMSE < 5.4% across all batches without re-fitting. Sensitivity analysis showed that membrane thickness CV was the dominant source of dissolution variability: reducing CV from 18 to 8% narrowed the predicted 80% dissolution time interval from ±1.8 to ±0.6 h. These findings support tighter process control targets for coating uniformity in pellet manufacturing.

title: Fractionation of pumpkin seed oil phospholipids using supercritical CO₂ modified with ethanol as co-solvent
abstract: Phospholipids in pumpkin seed oil represent a minor but functionally important fraction with relevance for liposomal drug delivery systems. Crude pumpkin seed oil, obtained by cold pressing, was subjected to supercritical CO₂ fractionation at pressures between 200 and 350 bar and temperatures between 45 and 65 °C, with ethanol added as co-solvent at 2, 5, and 8 mol%. Phospholipid content in the fractions was quantified by HPLC-DAD after derivatisation, and thin-layer chromatography was used for class identification. At 250 bar, 55 °C, and 5 mol% ethanol, phosphatidylcholine concentration in the enriched fraction reached 42.3 mg/g, compared to 11.7 mg/g in the starting oil. Increasing co-solvent concentration beyond 5 mol% led to co-extraction of neutral lipids, reducing selectivity. The study provides a solvent-free route to phospholipid-enriched fractions without the use of hexane or acetone, which is relevant for nutraceutical and cosmeceutical applications requiring clean-label ingredients.

title: Mathematical modelling of supercritical CO₂ extraction of fixed oil from grape seeds: broken-and-intact cell model applied to pilot-scale data
abstract: Scale-up from laboratory to pilot extraction requires reliable mathematical models to predict extraction kinetics and design operating schedules. This work applied the broken-and-intact cell (BIC) model to describe the supercritical CO₂ extraction of grape seed oil at pilot scale (5 L vessel, 2.5 kg charge, 350 bar, 50 °C). Extraction curves were obtained at three CO₂ flow rates (10, 20, and 30 kg/h) and the BIC model was fitted using nonlinear least-squares regression. Model parameters—broken cell fraction, mass transfer coefficient in intact cells, and axial dispersion coefficient—were estimated with 95% confidence intervals. Predicted extraction curves matched experimental data with root mean square errors below 4.2% across all flow rates. The fitted model was used to simulate optimal extraction time for 95% yield recovery, predicting a minimum solvent-to-feed ratio of 28 kg CO₂/kg feed. Grape seed oil fatty acid composition (predominantly linoleic acid, 68–71%) was consistent across scales. The validated model is intended as a tool for process design at industrial scale.

title: Redundant on-screen text in introductory chemistry screencasts: a retention study with vocational high school students
abstract: This study examined whether displaying verbatim captions alongside narrated chemistry screencasts improved or impaired knowledge retention among 87 first-year students enrolled in a vocational chemistry programme in Novi Sad. Participants were randomly assigned to three conditions: narration only, narration with verbatim on-screen text, and narration with summary keywords. Immediate recall tests and a delayed posttest administered one week later served as dependent measures. Students in the keyword condition outperformed both other groups on the delayed posttest (d = 0.54), while the verbatim caption condition showed a small but consistent decrement relative to narration-only on immediate recall (d = 0.21). Eye-tracking data collected from a subsample of 24 participants revealed longer fixation durations on text regions in the verbatim condition, consistent with attentional competition between modalities. The findings suggest that full-text redundancy is not inherently facilitative and that text density and placement interact with prior knowledge levels.

title: Pacing control in screencasts: learner-controlled versus system-controlled segmentation in automotive technology courses
abstract: Ninety-six students from an automotive technology vocational school in Subotica participated in a two-by-two experiment crossing segmentation type (learner-controlled pause points vs. fixed system-paced segments) with narration style (conversational vs. formal). Outcome measures included a 20-item procedural knowledge test, a transfer task requiring diagnosis of a simulated engine fault, and a subjective cognitive load rating scale. Learner-controlled segmentation produced significantly higher transfer scores than system-controlled pacing (F(1,92) = 7.31, p = .008, η² = .07), while narration style had no significant main effect. An interaction indicated that formal narration with learner-controlled pacing was the least effective combination. Post-session interviews suggested that students found formal language combined with self-pacing cognitively taxing because they allocated more working memory to linguistic parsing. Implications for screencast authoring tools used in Serbian vocational programmes are discussed.

title: Discourse markers in instructional screencasts and their effect on structural comprehension
abstract: Discourse markers such as 'first', 'consequently', and 'in contrast' signal logical and sequential relationships in spoken instruction. This study coded 60 screencasts used in secondary vocational programmes across three Serbian cities for discourse marker density and type, then linked these features to student comprehension scores obtained from 218 students. Screencasts were segmented into episodes of comparable duration, and discourse marker density was calculated per minute of speech. A multilevel regression model controlling for student prior knowledge and screen complexity showed that signalling markers (indicating structure) accounted for unique variance in comprehension (β = 0.29, p < .001), while framing markers did not. The visual complexity of slides moderated this relationship: in high-complexity screens, marker density mattered more. The study provides a coding framework adaptable for screencast quality evaluation in vocational curricula.

title: Does on-screen instructor presence affect engagement in vocational screencasts? An eye-tracking investigation
abstract: The picture-in-picture (PIP) format—showing a small video of the instructor alongside a screen recording—is widely used in online vocational training, but its effect on student attention distribution is poorly understood. In this study, 44 secondary vocational students watched screencasts in either standard or PIP format covering electrical wiring procedures. Eye-tracking recorded fixation counts and dwell time on three areas of interest: instructional content area, cursor movement area, and instructor face (PIP only). Students in the PIP condition spent 14.3% of total dwell time on the instructor face, and their fixation counts on the instructional content area were significantly lower than in the standard condition (t(42) = 2.18, p = .035). However, retention test scores did not differ significantly between conditions, suggesting that moderate face-viewing did not impair learning despite redistributing attention. Affective engagement ratings were higher in the PIP condition.

title: Multimodal coherence in screencasts for healthcare assistant training: a discourse-analytic framework
abstract: This book chapter develops a multimodal discourse-analytic framework for evaluating coherence in screencasts designed for healthcare assistant programmes. Drawing on systemic functional multimodal discourse analysis and applying it to a corpus of 34 screencasts from Serbian and Croatian vocational health training providers, the framework identifies four coherence dimensions: ideational alignment (correspondence between verbal and visual informational content), interpersonal positioning (how tone and layout construct learner relationships), compositional integration (layout logic and temporal flow), and intermodal bridging (use of arrows, highlights, and cursor movement to link modes). The chapter illustrates each dimension with annotated screencast excerpts and discusses reliability of the coding scheme (Cohen's κ = 0.71–0.84 across dimensions). The framework is intended for curriculum developers and instructional designers working in allied health vocational training.

title: Caption position and split attention in screencasts: top vs. bottom placement in IT vocational training
abstract: Split attention occurs when learners must mentally integrate spatially separated but mutually referential information. This experiment compared bottom-placed captions (conventional) with top-placed captions in screencasts used in an IT vocational programme, targeting 102 third-year students aged 16–18 in Novi Sad. The screencasts covered database query construction over five ten-minute episodes. A counterbalanced within-subjects design allowed each student to experience both conditions across non-overlapping content blocks. Mental effort ratings after each episode and a knowledge test at the session end served as measures. Top-placed captions yielded lower mental effort ratings when instructional content was concentrated in the lower two-thirds of the screen (the typical position for command-line interfaces), reducing mean effort by 0.8 points on a 9-point scale. Knowledge test scores did not differ significantly, suggesting an efficiency rather than an effectiveness advantage.

title: Temporal contiguity and redundancy interact in chemistry screencasts: a 2×2 experiment
abstract: The redundancy effect and the temporal contiguity principle are both derived from cognitive load theory but have rarely been examined together in authentic vocational screencast settings. This study used a two-by-two factorial design crossing redundancy level (verbatim captions vs. keywords-only captions) with temporal contiguity (synchronised vs. 3-second delayed caption onset) in 118 second-year vocational students studying organic chemistry. A 24-item knowledge test and a near-transfer task were administered immediately after viewing. Results showed a significant interaction: verbatim captions combined with delayed onset produced the lowest transfer scores (M = 11.4, SD = 3.1), while keyword captions with synchronised onset produced the highest (M = 15.7, SD = 2.8). Main effects were significant for both factors. The study quantifies the additive cost of combining two suboptimal design choices common in teacher-produced screencasts.

title: How teachers in Serbian vocational schools design screencasts: a survey of practices and stated rationales
abstract: Despite the growing use of teacher-produced screencasts in Serbian secondary vocational education, little is known about how teachers make design decisions. This study surveyed 214 vocational teachers across 37 schools in Vojvodina regarding their screencast production practices, tools used, awareness of multimedia learning principles, and self-reported rationales for design choices. Eighty-one per cent used default settings in their recording software without consulting instructional design guidelines. Awareness of the redundancy effect was low (14% correct identification on a scenario-based item). Teachers with prior ICT training were more likely to use segmentation and to limit on-screen text. Open-ended responses revealed that perceived student preference drove many decisions, including the widespread inclusion of full narration transcripts as captions. The findings indicate a gap between research-derived guidance and classroom practice, informing the design of teacher professional development programmes.

title: Annotation overlays in screencasts and their effect on spatial attention: an eye-tracking study in automotive diagnostics training
abstract: Annotation overlays—highlights, arrows, and text boxes added to screen-recorded content—are intended to direct learner attention to relevant areas. This experiment examined whether three overlay types (static highlight, animated arrow, pulsing text box) differentially affected fixation patterns and learning outcomes in 66 vocational students watching screencasts on automotive diagnostic software. Areas of interest were defined a priori for each of twelve target events. Animated arrows produced the fastest time-to-first fixation on target areas (M = 0.61 s) compared with static highlights (M = 1.02 s) and pulsing text boxes (M = 0.83 s). Knowledge test scores favoured animated arrows for procedural items (d = 0.48 vs. static highlight) but not for declarative items. Extraneous fixations on non-target areas were fewest in the animated arrow condition, suggesting reduced distraction. Design recommendations for annotation use in vocational screencasts are derived from the data.

title: Prior knowledge moderates the redundancy effect in screencasts: evidence from electrical engineering vocational students
abstract: Cognitive load theory predicts that the redundancy effect—the impairment caused by adding redundant information—should be reduced or reversed for learners with low prior knowledge, who may benefit from additional textual support. This study tested this prediction with 144 first- and third-year electrical engineering vocational students, treating year of study as a proxy for prior knowledge. Half of each cohort watched screencasts with verbatim captions; the other half watched narration-only versions. For third-year students, verbatim captions impaired retention (d = 0.41); for first-year students, captions provided a small but non-significant benefit (d = 0.14). Expertise reversal was therefore partial: the cost of redundancy was clearly present for more knowledgeable learners but no clear benefit emerged for novices. The results suggest that adaptive removal of captions as learner expertise grows is a more defensible strategy than universal caption inclusion.

title: Cursor movement as a visual guide in screencasts: effects on attention and learning in a pharmacy assistant training context
abstract: In screencasts of software-based tasks, cursor movement is an ever-present dynamic visual element that instructors typically leave unrehearsed. This study coded cursor movement patterns—purposeful pointing, idle wandering, and tracing—in 48 screencasts used in pharmacy assistant training, then examined associations with learner outcomes in a sample of 96 students. Screencasts with a higher proportion of purposeful pointing movements were associated with higher procedural knowledge scores (r = 0.41, p = .004 at screencast level after controlling for video length and topic). In a subsequent experiment, 68 students were randomised to watch re-edited versions of six screencasts with wandering cursor motion replaced by purposeful pointing or left unchanged; the edited versions produced modestly higher posttest scores (d = 0.33). Eye-tracking data showed that purposeful cursor movement reduced the variance in fixation distribution, indicating more uniform attention. Practical guidance for screencast narrators is outlined.

title: Multimodal redundancy in auto-generated versus human-authored captions: a comparative analysis of 120 vocational screencasts
abstract: Automatic speech recognition tools now generate captions for instructional video with high accuracy, but auto-generated captions reproduce the full spoken narration verbatim, potentially maximising redundancy. This study compared verbatim auto-generated captions, human-edited keyword captions, and no captions across 120 screencasts drawn from six vocational subject areas (mechanical engineering, IT, healthcare, gastronomy, electrical installation, and construction). Three hundred and twelve students were assigned to one caption condition within their subject area. A multilevel model treating students as nested within screencasts showed a significant disadvantage for verbatim auto-generated captions relative to keyword captions on knowledge retention (β = −1.82, SE = 0.54, p = .001) and no significant difference between keyword captions and no captions for higher prior-knowledge learners. Subject area moderated the effect: gastronomy and healthcare students showed smaller redundancy penalties, possibly due to lower screen visual complexity in those subjects.

title: Screencast viewing on smartphones versus desktops in vocational education: differences in fixation patterns and retention
abstract: Secondary vocational students increasingly access instructional screencasts on smartphones, yet most screencasts are designed for larger desktop displays. This preprint reports data from 88 students in construction and gastronomy vocational programmes who watched identical screencasts on either a 15-inch laptop display or a standard smartphone (6.1-inch screen) under naturalistic viewing conditions. Eye-tracking was conducted using remote equipment for desktop viewers and a mobile eye-tracker worn as glasses for smartphone viewers. Smartphone viewers showed significantly more revisiting behaviour (returning to previously viewed screen areas) and shorter mean fixation durations on text regions, consistent with increased visual search effort due to smaller rendered text. Retention test scores were equivalent across devices for declarative items but significantly lower for smartphone viewers on procedural tasks requiring reading of on-screen labels (d = 0.44). The results have direct implications for caption sizing and layout in mobile-first screencast design.

title: Does Physical Manipulation Add Value to Digital Math Games? A Comparative Study in Grades Four and Five
abstract: A between-subjects experiment compared three conditions: purely digital tablet-based number games, physical manipulative tasks, and a hybrid condition combining both within the same activity. Participants were 127 students in grades four and five from three schools in Novi Sad. Each condition ran for six weeks with two 30-minute sessions per week. Outcome measures included a curriculum-aligned arithmetic test, a near-transfer task involving number patterns, and a far-transfer task involving measurement word problems. On the arithmetic test, all three conditions improved significantly from pre- to post-test; however, the hybrid condition outperformed the digital-only condition on the near-transfer task (p = 0.03, d = 0.48) but not on the far-transfer task. Physical-only students scored lower than hybrid students on the digital post-test, suggesting interface familiarity effects. Findings support hybrid designs for near-transfer benefits while questioning claims of broad cognitive transfer.

title: Designing Assessments Embedded in Educational Card Games: Challenges and a Proposed Framework
abstract: Assessing learning within a game without disrupting gameplay is a persistent design challenge. This book chapter reviews 22 published studies on embedded assessment in card and board games used for mathematics instruction at primary level and proposes a three-layer framework distinguishing performance indicators (observable in-game actions), inferential indicators (patterns requiring data aggregation), and post-game probes (brief structured questions administered after a session). The chapter argues that most existing designs rely exclusively on post-game probes, leaving real-time performance data unused. A worked example applying the framework to a fraction card game is provided, showing how rule-compliance errors, self-correction frequency, and help-seeking behaviour can serve as performance indicators without interrupting game flow. Limitations of the framework in low-technology settings and in classrooms without trained observers are discussed. The chapter concludes with a checklist for practitioners developing embedded assessment in game-based math instruction.

title: Instrument validation: the Serbian Metacognitive Regulation Scale for adult distance learners
abstract: This paper reports the development and psychometric validation of the Serbian Metacognitive Regulation Scale (SMRS), a 24-item instrument designed for use with adult distance learners. Item generation drew on existing frameworks and qualitative pilot data from 38 adult learners. The instrument was administered to 312 distance students across four universities in Serbia. Exploratory factor analysis on a random split-half (n = 156) yielded a three-factor structure corresponding to planning, monitoring, and evaluation, accounting for 54 % of total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis on the second half showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.061, SRMR = 0.057). Internal consistency was satisfactory for all three sub-scales (α = 0.81, 0.78, 0.76 respectively). Test-retest reliability over six weeks was r = 0.74. Convergent validity with the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire monitoring sub-scale was r = 0.63. The instrument is freely available in Serbian and English and is intended for use in research and programme evaluation.

title: Mapping within-field nitrogen variability using ground-based multispectral reflectance on winter wheat
abstract: This study evaluated the capacity of a four-band ground-based multispectral sensor mounted on a tractor toolbar to generate within-field nitrogen variability maps for winter wheat in Vojvodina. Measurements were collected across 14 commercial fields totalling 340 ha during the stem elongation stage over two growing seasons (2009–2010). Canopy reflectance in red-edge and near-infrared bands was recorded at 2 m spatial resolution and compared against 480 destructive biomass and Kjeldahl nitrogen samples. Partial least squares regression models explained 71–76% of the variance in leaf nitrogen content (RMSE 3.1 kg N ha⁻¹). Prescription maps generated from the sensor data were compared with uniform-rate applications, showing a mean absolute deviation in recommended dose of 18 kg N ha⁻¹ across blocks. The results supported the use of reflectance-based sensing for tractor-mounted variable-rate control but highlighted strong sensitivity to solar irradiance variation requiring active illumination correction.
