title: Evaluation of closed-loop spray pressure regulation for tractor boom applicators on heterogeneous canopies
abstract: Conventional variable-rate boom sprayers adjust flow by modulating section valves according to pre-loaded prescription maps, without feedback from actual deposition. This paper describes a prototype closed-loop pressure regulation system in which nozzle flow sensors provided real-time deposition estimates that were compared against target rates at 10 Hz. A PID controller adjusted the hydraulic pump outlet pressure to compensate for deviations caused by terrain slope, travel speed fluctuations, and clogging events. Field trials on sunflower and maize in 2012 across 6 experimental plots (total 22 ha) showed that the closed-loop system reduced application rate deviation from target by 34% compared with open-loop operation (mean absolute error 4.2 L ha⁻¹ versus 6.4 L ha⁻¹). Clogging detection latency was reduced to under 0.8 s. The system demonstrated practical applicability but required re-tuning of PID gains for fluids with different viscosities.

title: Canopy height estimation from low-altitude UAV photogrammetry for variable-rate input management
abstract: Structure-from-motion photogrammetry applied to images acquired by a fixed-wing UAV at 60 m AGL was used to derive canopy height models (CHM) for six maize fields in Bačka during the 2014 growing season. A total of 4 200 ground check points validated the CHM against RTK GNSS measurements. Mean height errors ranged from 6 to 14 cm depending on field surface roughness and plant density, with overall RMSE of 9 cm. Canopy height zones correlated moderately with yield monitor data collected at harvest (Pearson r = 0.58–0.67), confirming its utility as a proxy for biomass variability. Zonal prescription maps for late-season side-dress nitrogen were generated from the CHM and compared against farmer-uniform practice. The study quantified flight time and ground control point requirements to achieve sub-10 cm accuracy and discussed integration of the resulting prescription layers into variable-rate spreader controllers.

title: Real-time NDVI streaming from a multispectral camera payload on a rotary-wing UAV: latency and calibration constraints
abstract: This paper characterises the data pipeline required for real-time NDVI computation and transmission from a four-band multispectral camera mounted on an octocopter UAV. An embedded single-board computer processed raw image tiles at 4 Hz and streamed calibrated NDVI values over a 900 MHz radio link to a ground station. Radiometric calibration relied on a downwelling light sensor integrated on the UAV frame; calibration stability was evaluated across 42 flights in varying cloud cover during the 2016 field season over soybean and sugar beet. End-to-end latency from sensor integration to ground-station display averaged 310 ms (σ = 45 ms). Comparison of real-time streaming NDVI against post-processed full-resolution NDVI showed a mean absolute difference of 0.021 NDVI units, deemed acceptable for within-flight actuator triggering. The main performance bottleneck was the JPEG compression step, which consumed 61% of onboard processing time.

title: A variable-rate nozzle actuation system for UAV-mounted spray payloads driven by in-flight multispectral indices
abstract: A prototype UAV spray system was designed in which solenoid nozzle valves were actuated in real time based on NDVI thresholds computed from an onboard multispectral camera during herbicide application over maize. The actuation logic used a two-class decision boundary (NDVI < 0.35 triggering spray; NDVI ≥ 0.35 suppressing spray) intended to target weed patches. The UAV flew at 3 m s⁻¹ and 2 m AGL over experimental plots containing artificial weed targets. Actuation latency introduced a positional error of 14 cm at operational speed, representing 1.1% area misapplication relative to target patches 1 m in diameter. Total spray volume was reduced by 37% compared with broadcast application over the same plots. Nozzle wear tests showed consistent flow rates over 120 actuation cycles per flight. The paper discusses the signal-to-noise limitations of low-altitude multispectral sensing under variable irradiance and proposes a moving-average filter to reduce false actuation events.

title: Hardware-in-the-loop testing of UAV variable-rate spray controllers under simulated canopy sensing inputs
abstract: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation was used to evaluate three candidate variable-rate spray controllers before field deployment. The HIL bench combined a physical pump-nozzle assembly with simulated multispectral sensor feeds generated from 2019 orchard flights replayed at 1×, 2× and 4× speed. Three controller architectures were compared: rule-based threshold switching, a proportional controller with dead-band, and a model-predictive controller with a 200 ms horizon. Metrics included tracking error relative to a reference prescription, actuator duty cycle, and total volume dispensed. The model-predictive controller achieved the lowest mean tracking error (2.1 L ha⁻¹) but required 18% longer initialisation time. At 4× replay speed, all controllers degraded; the proportional controller maintained stability while MPC diverged when sensor latency exceeded 150 ms. The HIL framework reduced field testing iterations by an estimated factor of three and is described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Simultaneous LiDAR and multispectral sensing from a single UAV platform: sensor fusion approach for vineyard canopy characterisation
abstract: A co-aligned payload carrying a 16-channel LiDAR and a five-band multispectral camera was flown over 11 vineyard blocks in the Fruška Gora wine region during three phenological stages in 2021. Temporal registration of the two streams required a novel extrinsic calibration target yielding angular alignment errors below 0.3°. Fused point clouds that combined geometric canopy density with spectral NDVI values were segmented into canopy, post, and gap classes using a random forest classifier (overall accuracy 93.4%). Canopy volume and chlorophyll-proxy index were jointly used to generate dual-variable prescription maps specifying both spray volume and concentration. Compared with single-sensor prescriptions, the fused approach reduced over-application in dense low-vigour zones by 19% and under-application in sparse high-vigour zones by 12% as validated against reference hand-sprayer applications. Sensor synchronisation drift was identified as the primary remaining technical challenge.

title: Actuator response characterisation of variable-rate UAV nozzles under flight-representative vibration and pressure conditions
abstract: This bench study characterised the dynamic response of three commercially available solenoid nozzle valves proposed for UAV variable-rate spray payloads. Valves were tested on a vibration table reproducing accelerometer-recorded UAV flight profiles (0.5–80 Hz, up to 6 g). Actuation response times (open and close) were measured at line pressures of 1, 2, and 3 bar using high-speed pressure transducers at 5 kHz. All three valves showed statistically significant increases in close-delay at 2 g lateral vibration: mean close-delay increased from 18 ms to 31 ms for the worst performer. Flow rate non-linearity at partial duty cycles exceeded 8% in two of the three designs. A fourth prototype valve with a mechanical anti-vibration sleeve reduced vibration-induced delay to 4 ms. The study provided empirically grounded specifications for UAV spray controller designers and recommended test protocol standardisation across manufacturers.

title: Closed-loop altitude and spray rate co-control for UAV application over row crops with variable canopy height
abstract: Variable canopy height in row crops causes UAV sprayers to operate at non-constant nozzle-to-target distances, leading to deposit pattern distortion and variable droplet size. This study implemented a coupled controller where a downward-facing LiDAR altimeter fed a flight controller maintaining constant nozzle-to-canopy distance, while the same range signal concurrently adjusted pump duty cycle to maintain constant deposit density. Experiments were conducted over sunflower fields with measured canopy height variance of 0.38 m² across plots during the 2023 season. The coupled controller held nozzle-to-canopy distance within ±6 cm (σ = 3.1 cm) and application rate within ±4.7% of target across six flights totalling 8.4 ha. Uncoupled baseline flights showed ±22% rate deviation over the same terrain. Wind interaction at 3 m s⁻¹ cross-wind degraded altitude tracking; a feed-forward wind compensation term reduced the effect by 55%.

title: Regulatory and operational constraints on autonomous UAV spray applications in Serbian and Hungarian agriculture: a practitioner survey
abstract: Despite technical advances in UAV variable-rate spraying, deployment in commercial farming remains limited. This paper reports results of a structured survey of 78 agricultural practitioners (farmers, agronomists, and UAV service operators) across Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád county (Hungary) conducted in late 2024. Respondents rated barriers to adoption on a five-point Likert scale across regulatory, economic, technical, and agronomic dimensions. Regulatory uncertainty was the most frequently cited critical barrier (68% of respondents), followed by high equipment cost (54%) and lack of certified operators (47%). Technical reliability concerns were rated lower than expected, suggesting that early adopters have had broadly positive experiences with equipment performance. Cross-border differences in civil aviation authority interpretation of spray UAV rules were reported by all cross-border service operators interviewed (n = 11). The paper maps current national regulatory frameworks and identifies specific points of divergence that could inform harmonisation efforts.

title: Onboard edge inference of crop stress indicators from compressed multispectral imagery for real-time UAV actuation
abstract: Running full-resolution multispectral processing on UAV payloads is constrained by compute power and thermal limits. This preprint describes deployment of a quantised convolutional neural network (5.2 M parameters, INT8) on a low-power system-on-chip to infer three-class crop stress labels (healthy, nitrogen-deficient, water-stressed) from 320×240 multispectral tiles at 9 Hz during flight. Training used 14 800 labelled tiles collected from soybean and maize fields during the 2024 season. Inference accuracy on the held-out test set was 84.7% (F1 macro), degrading to 78.2% under high solar angle variation without downwelling correction. Actuation commands derived from the edge model were compared against post-flight reference commands from full-resolution offline analysis: agreement was 91.3% at the spray-zone level. Power consumption averaged 3.4 W, compatible with a 6 Ah UAV battery budget. The model weights and training pipeline are released openly.

title: Gradient-based edge detection performance on low-contrast food packaging under variable conveyor illumination
abstract: This paper evaluates four gradient-based edge detectors—Sobel, Prewitt, Scharr and a tuned Canny implementation—applied to grey-scale images of plastic food containers acquired on a laboratory conveyor belt running at speeds between 0.3 and 1.2 m/s. Illumination was varied systematically using diffuse dome lighting, coaxial lighting and combined side-plus-coaxial setups. A dataset of 4 200 images was collected across six packaging types. Edge continuity, F1 score against manually annotated ground truth, and processing latency on an ARM Cortex-A9 processor were measured. The Scharr operator combined with adaptive histogram equalisation achieved the highest mean F1 of 0.83 at 1.0 m/s under coaxial illumination, at a frame throughput of 47 fps. Diffuse dome lighting reduced F1 variance across packaging colours by 18% compared with single-source setups. The results provide practical guidance for lighting selection in low-budget inline inspection cells without dedicated machine-vision controllers.

title: Pose estimation accuracy for randomly oriented small metallic parts on a moving belt using structured-light depth sensing
abstract: This study assesses the suitability of a low-cost structured-light depth sensor for estimating the 6-DOF pose of small metallic workpieces on a conveyor belt moving at 0.4 m/s. Eighty part instances across four geometry classes were tested; each class included reflective surfaces that are known to produce depth artefacts in time-of-flight and structured-light sensors. A preprocessing step using infrared-band filtering and surface normal smoothing reduced invalid pixel ratios from 31% to 9%. Pose estimation used a point-pair feature algorithm with a RANSAC verification stage. Mean position error was 1.8 mm and mean orientation error was 2.3° over 2 400 trials. A downstream six-axis collaborative arm successfully grasped parts in 91.4% of trials at the given belt speed. The paper quantifies the dependence of pose error on part shininess measured by a calibrated reflectance standard and discusses the minimum acceptable surface roughness for reliable sensing.

title: Synchronisation of image acquisition and robot trajectory planning in a dual-arm pick-and-place cell
abstract: Coordinating two six-axis arms sharing a single conveyor pick zone requires tight synchronisation between the vision system's object-position updates and each arm's trajectory planner. This paper presents a time-stamped message-passing architecture implemented over EtherCAT that allows position corrections to be injected into a running trajectory up to 35 ms before the arm reaches the pick point. Experiments were conducted with 12 object types of varying size and aspect ratio at conveyor speeds of 0.5 and 0.9 m/s. The dual-arm cell achieved a combined throughput of 58 picks per minute with a collision-free rate of 99.7% over 10 000 continuous operating cycles. Cycle time improved by 22% compared with a token-passing arbitration baseline. Latency budgets for each pipeline stage—capture, classification, coordinate transform, trajectory update—are reported individually. The architecture was implemented on a ROS 2-based controller running on a real-time Linux kernel.

title: Comparison of lightweight CNN architectures for real-time object sorting on an NVIDIA Jetson platform
abstract: This paper benchmarks five lightweight convolutional architectures—MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, SqueezeNet 1.1, ShuffleNetV2 and a custom four-block network designed for the task—on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX module used as an embedded sorter controller. The test scenario involves classifying thirteen categories of mixed municipal recyclables on a conveyor running at 0.7 m/s, where objects may overlap partially. A dataset of 26 000 labelled single-object images and 8 400 partially occluded multi-object frames was assembled in-house. TensorRT-optimised INT8 models were compared on throughput, top-1 accuracy and power draw. EfficientNet-B0 achieved 88.4% top-1 accuracy at 68 fps and 9.1 W; the custom network reached 85.1% at 94 fps and 7.4 W. Occlusion degraded accuracy by 8–14 percentage points depending on architecture. The paper discusses trade-offs relevant to selecting a model for battery-powered or thermally constrained inspection units.

title: Dataset and baseline results for curved-surface 2D code detection under industrial lighting conditions
abstract: Publicly available datasets for 2D code (QR and DataMatrix) detection on curved surfaces are scarce, and those that exist rarely include the range of industrial lighting conditions encountered in practice. This preprint describes a dataset of 11 400 images collected on cylindrical, conical and saddle-shaped surfaces under eight distinct lighting configurations, including high-pressure sodium emulation, LED ring, telecentric backlight and mixed ambient. Images were captured at three conveyor speeds (0, 0.6 and 1.1 m/s) with two camera models. Each image is annotated with code location polygons, surface curvature class, lighting type and belt speed. Baseline detection results are reported for four open-source pipelines. ZXing-C++ achieved the highest overall decode rate of 81.3%, dropping to 64.7% on saddle surfaces. The dataset is released under a CC BY 4.0 licence and is intended to support reproducible comparison of detection methods in this under-studied setting.

title: Model Predictive Control of a Hexarotor UAV Sprayer with Explicit Wind State Prediction
abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) is applied to the trajectory-tracking problem for a hexarotor UAV sprayer, with wind state incorporated as an explicitly predicted exogenous input over a horizon of 0.5 s. Wind prediction is generated by a 12-tap autoregressive model fitted online to a rolling buffer of wind estimates derived from the motor current method. The MPC is formulated as a quadratic programme with a prediction horizon of 25 steps at 20 ms sample time, enforcing constraints on roll/pitch angles (±15°), thrust (5–42 N per rotor), and velocity (maximum 8 m/s). Real-time solution on a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 achieved a median solve time of 7.3 ms, within the 10 ms constraint budget. Field trials on a 4.2 ha soybean field under measured winds of 1.8–5.6 m/s showed swath lateral RMSE of 0.13 m, compared to 0.22 m for the DOB-PID baseline. Power consumption increased by 6.2% relative to baseline.

title: Real-Time Parametric Model Updating for Overhead Crane Digital Twins: Architecture and Latency Constraints
abstract: This paper describes a software and hardware architecture for synchronising a parametric digital twin of an overhead crane with its physical counterpart in real time. The twin runs on a dSPACE MicroLabBox executing a fourth-order state-space model at a 2 ms update cycle. Parameter updating uses a recursive least-squares algorithm with exponential forgetting (forgetting factor 0.995) driven by encoder velocity and rope-tension residuals. Four parameters are updated online: effective rope stiffness, damping coefficient, payload mass, and trolley friction coefficient. On the laboratory testbed, end-to-end synchronisation latency is measured at 3.8 ms (95th percentile over 10 000 cycles), and mean parameter tracking error is below 3% during standardised motion sequences. The paper discusses how sensor noise, update-rate mismatches, and actuator delays constrain achievable synchronisation fidelity, and identifies rope-tension signal bandwidth as the dominant bottleneck. A comparison of update rates from 1 ms to 20 ms quantifies the trade-off between computational load and state estimate accuracy.

title: Tracking Consumer Perceptions of Local Food Brands: A Three-Year Panel Study in Northern Serbia
abstract: This study reports the first wave of a multi-year brand equity tracking project covering 14 family-owned food producers in Vojvodina. A structured questionnaire adapted from Yoo and Donthu's brand equity scale was administered to 420 households at twelve-month intervals across three waves (2010–2012). Constructs measured included brand awareness, perceived quality, brand associations and brand loyalty. Confirmatory factor analysis confirmed scale stability across waves; longitudinal invariance was tested using configural, metric and scalar models. Results showed that perceived quality scores remained the most stable dimension, while brand loyalty exhibited significant seasonal fluctuation linked to purchasing of fresh and processed meat products. Smaller producers with direct-sales channels showed higher loyalty scores than those selling exclusively through retail intermediaries. The paper concludes that annual measurement intervals are adequate for tracking structural shifts but may miss short-term promotional effects.

title: Mixed-Methods Panel Design for SME Brand Equity: Methodological Considerations and a Pilot Application
abstract: Longitudinal brand equity research in small firm contexts faces recurring challenges: sample attrition, limited respondent pools, and the difficulty of capturing managerial intent alongside consumer perception. This book chapter presents a structured mixed-methods panel design developed and piloted with eight agri-food SMEs in Vojvodina between 2011 and 2014. The design integrates annual consumer surveys (n ≈ 350 per wave), biennial owner-manager interviews, and yearly review of publicly available distribution and labelling data. Procedures for managing attrition through partial invariance corrections and for integrating qualitative updates into quantitative interpretation are described in detail. The pilot application across four waves demonstrated that the design is feasible with a two-person research team and modest funding. Practical constraints, including survey fatigue among rural respondents and reluctance among some owners to share financial data, are discussed along with mitigation strategies adopted in the field.

title: Retail Channel Choice and Brand Equity Outcomes in Small-Scale Dairy Producers: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: Small dairy producers in Vojvodina operate across heterogeneous distribution channels—farm-gate direct sales, open markets, independent grocers, and regional supermarket chains—each offering different levels of brand visibility and price control. This paper examines whether channel configuration predicts brand equity scores, using consumer data from 11 dairy SMEs collected across two waves (2016 and 2018), yielding a balanced panel of 614 respondents. OLS regression with firm fixed effects and heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors was used. Producers relying primarily on farm-gate and open-market channels showed significantly higher perceived quality and brand loyalty scores than those selling mainly through supermarkets, even after controlling for firm age, geographic scope and price positioning. Interaction terms indicated that the effect is stronger for firms with fewer than five full-time employees. Implications for regional food policy supporting short supply chains are discussed.

title: Measuring Brand Equity Across Languages: Instrument Equivalence in a Bilingual Serbian-Hungarian Consumer Panel
abstract: Vojvodina's ethnic composition makes consumer research methodologically complex: a significant share of respondents prefer to complete surveys in Hungarian rather than Serbian. This paper investigates whether a seven-item brand equity instrument administered in Serbian and Hungarian versions yields equivalent factor structures, using data from 830 respondents recruited in Subotica, Senta and Bačka Topola in 2019. Multi-group confirmatory factor analysis tested configural, metric and scalar invariance. Full scalar invariance was not achieved for two items in the brand awareness subscale; partial invariance corrections were applied and cross-linguistic comparisons were adjusted accordingly. The practical implication is that researchers working in multilingual panels should routinely test for measurement equivalence rather than assuming it, and that item-level wording differences between translated instruments can produce non-trivial bias in brand equity estimates. Recommendations for instrument revision are provided.

title: Does Geographic Indication Certification Affect Brand Equity Trajectories? A Pre–Post Comparison in Vojvodina Food SMEs
abstract: Geographic indication (GI) labels such as Protected Designation of Origin are expected to enhance perceived quality and brand associations, but empirical evidence from small Central and Eastern European producers is limited. This study compares brand equity trajectories for six Vojvodina agri-food SMEs that received GI certification between 2017 and 2019 with a matched comparison group of seven non-certified firms, using four waves of consumer panel data (2017–2021, n = 389 balanced respondents). A difference-in-differences approach was applied, supplemented by follow-up qualitative interviews with 18 owner-managers to interpret quantitative patterns. GI certification was associated with a significant increase in perceived quality scores (average treatment effect = 0.31 points on a five-point scale, p < 0.05) sustained across two post-certification waves. Brand associations showed a smaller, statistically marginal increase. Qualitative data suggested that the quality effect was partly mediated by increased press coverage and in-store shelf placement rather than the label alone.

title: Long-Run Brand Equity Dynamics in Family Agri-food SMEs: Twelve-Year Panel Evidence from Vojvodina
abstract: This paper presents findings from the longest continuous brand equity panel conducted among family-owned agri-food firms in the Western Balkans, covering 12 annual waves (2010–2022) across a core sample of nine firms and approximately 310 balanced respondents per wave. Growth curve modelling in a multilevel framework was used to estimate firm-specific trajectories for four brand equity dimensions. Average trajectories showed modest positive drift in perceived quality (+0.18 points per five years) and near-stagnation in brand awareness, reflecting the limited marketing investment typical of micro-enterprises. Substantial between-firm variance was found in loyalty trajectories, explained partly by succession events, channel changes and GI certification. Qualitative data from nine owner-manager interview rounds were used to annotate trajectory inflection points. The paper also reflects on practical lessons from sustaining a twelve-year panel: the importance of maintaining a stable core respondent pool, managing interviewer effects, and adapting instruments incrementally without breaking longitudinal comparability.

title: Integrating Social Media Sentiment into Brand Equity Panels: A Feasibility Study with Vojvodina Food Producers
abstract: Customer-based brand equity panels rely on survey self-reports, which are resource-intensive and subject to attrition. This preprint reports a feasibility study examining whether social media sentiment scores can serve as a cost-efficient supplementary indicator between survey waves. Text data were collected from four Serbian-language social media platforms and two food-specific review sites for 11 agri-food SMEs over 24 months (2023–2024), yielding 4,820 posts after filtering for relevance. Sentiment was scored using a fine-tuned Serbian-language BERT variant. Pearson correlations between quarterly sentiment aggregates and the most recent survey-wave brand association scores ranged from 0.29 to 0.58 across firms, with higher correlations for firms with larger social media followings. The results suggest moderate concurrent validity. Major limitations include the small absolute volume of posts for micro-producers, language mixing between Serbian and Hungarian, and the inability to verify poster identity or purchase status.

title: Environmental Concern and Purchase Reluctance: An Exploratory Survey of Young Consumers in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper reports on an exploratory cross-sectional survey conducted in 2012 among 214 undergraduate students at two faculties of the University of Novi Sad. Participants completed a 38-item questionnaire measuring environmental concern, perceived consumer effectiveness, and self-reported frequency of green product purchases. Descriptive statistics and bivariate correlation analysis revealed a moderate positive association between environmental concern scores and stated purchasing intentions (r = 0.41, p < 0.001), but a weaker link between intentions and reported actual purchases (r = 0.22, p < 0.01). Qualitative open-ended responses suggested that price premium and limited retail availability were the most frequently cited barriers. The findings provide an early empirical baseline for the attitude–behaviour gap in this underrepresented regional context and point toward structural rather than purely motivational explanations for the gap. The study calls for longitudinal designs to track whether the gap narrows as green product ranges expand in Serbian retail markets.

title: Motility-induced phase separation and the thermodynamic arrow in two-dimensional active Brownian disks
abstract: We perform overdamped Langevin simulations of up to 40000 active Brownian disks on a periodic two-dimensional domain to study how motility-induced phase separation (MIPS) affects global entropy production. Péclet numbers between 1 and 200 and packing fractions between 0.1 and 0.7 are surveyed. Entropy production rate per particle is computed using a direct estimator based on the steady-state probability current. In the homogeneous phase, entropy production scales quadratically with Péclet number. At the MIPS transition, we observe a non-monotonic signature: entropy production rate drops by 12–18% upon entering the dense cluster phase before recovering at higher Péclet numbers. This dip correlates with the appearance of large immobile aggregates that effectively quench fluctuations. We characterise the spatial distribution of entropy production and find it concentrated in the interfacial region between dense and dilute phases. A phenomenological model based on interfacial area density reproduces the drop quantitatively within 5%.

title: Calibration-free estimation of entropy production from short trajectory segments using neural network time-reversal classifiers
abstract: Direct experimental estimation of entropy production from particle trajectories is hampered by the need for large datasets and sensitivity to measurement noise. We train a convolutional neural network to classify short trajectory segments (length 10–50 steps) as forward or time-reversed, and use the resulting log-odds scores as entropy production estimators following the Kolchinsky–Wolpert framework. Training uses synthetic trajectories from active Brownian particle simulations; the trained network is then applied without retraining to experimental trajectories of Janus microswimmers in water and to published datasets of motile algal cells. On synthetic data the estimator recovers 85–93% of the true entropy production at 50-step segment length; on experimental Janus data agreement with the thermodynamic uncertainty bound is within 18%. The method requires no knowledge of the force field or particle model and is robust to Gaussian positional noise up to 10% of the mean step size. Code and training datasets are made publicly available.

title: Entropy production and rheological signatures in dense active suspensions under oscillatory shear
abstract: We combine Langevin dynamics simulations with oscillatory shear boundary conditions to study how activity affects the linear and nonlinear rheology of dense active Brownian particle suspensions at packing fractions between 0.50 and 0.68. Strain amplitude is varied from 0.01 to 1.0 at angular frequencies between 0.1 and 100 rad s⁻¹. Active forces are parameterised by self-propulsion speed from 0 to 5 times the thermal velocity. In the linear regime, activity reduces the elastic storage modulus by up to 45% relative to the passive suspension at the same packing fraction, while the viscous loss modulus shows a non-monotonic dependence on self-propulsion speed with a minimum near speed ratio 2. Entropy production under shear can be cleanly decomposed into a shear-driven part and an activity-driven part; these two contributions are not additive and interfere constructively near the glass transition, enhancing total dissipation by 20–60%. We propose dimensionless ratios that could be measured in microfluidic rheometers.

title: Urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin as an early marker of tubular injury in cats with IRIS stage 1 and 2 chronic kidney disease
abstract: Urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (uNGAL) has been proposed as a sensitive indicator of tubular damage preceding rises in serum creatinine. This cross-sectional study measured uNGAL by sandwich ELISA in morning urine samples from 48 client-owned cats: 16 classified as IRIS stage 1, 16 as IRIS stage 2, and 16 healthy controls matched for age and body weight. Urine creatinine was measured simultaneously and uNGAL expressed as a ratio to urine creatinine (uNGAL:Cr). IRIS stage 1 cats showed a median uNGAL:Cr of 4.2 µg/g (IQR 2.8–6.1), significantly elevated compared to controls (median 1.7 µg/g, IQR 1.1–2.4; p < 0.01, Mann–Whitney U). IRIS stage 2 cats had a median of 9.8 µg/g (IQR 6.3–14.2). Symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) was correlated with uNGAL:Cr (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Urine protein:creatinine ratio did not differ significantly between stage 1 cats and controls. Results suggest uNGAL:Cr may detect tubular injury before proteinuria becomes apparent. Limitations include the single time-point design and absence of histopathological confirmation. A longitudinal follow-up study is under preparation.

title: Effect of a low-phosphorus renal diet on serum phosphorus, FGF-23 and parathyroid hormone in dogs with IRIS stage 2 and 3 chronic kidney disease: a 12-week observational study
abstract: Hyperphosphataemia accelerates CKD progression through renal secondary hyperparathyroidism and elevated fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF-23). This prospective observational study enrolled 34 client-owned dogs diagnosed with IRIS stage 2 (n = 19) or stage 3 (n = 15) CKD at a university veterinary clinic. Dogs were transitioned to a commercial low-phosphorus renal diet (phosphorus content 0.13% DM) and monitored at baseline, week 6, and week 12. Serum phosphorus, FGF-23 (ELISA), intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine were measured at each visit. By week 12, serum phosphorus decreased by a mean of 0.41 mmol/L in stage 2 dogs (95% CI 0.18–0.64, p < 0.01) and 0.58 mmol/L in stage 3 dogs (95% CI 0.29–0.87, p < 0.01). FGF-23 showed a statistically significant decline in stage 3 dogs only (p = 0.03). iPTH trends were in the expected direction but did not reach significance at this sample size. Owner-reported diet compliance was 85%. The study was limited by absence of a control group and variability in baseline diet histories.

title: Relationship between body condition score at calving and postpartum hepatic lipid accumulation in multiparous dairy cows
abstract: Data from 211 multiparous Holstein cows on five farms in Vojvodina were analysed retrospectively. Body condition scores (BCS) were recorded at dry-off (approximately 60 days before calving) and again at calving. Liver fat content was estimated by ultrasound echogenicity scoring at days 5 and 14 postpartum using a four-grade scale validated against biopsy data in a previous study. Cows calving with BCS above 3.5 were 2.8 times more likely to reach ultrasound grade III or IV hepatic lipidosis than cows with BCS 2.75–3.25 (odds ratio 2.83, 95% CI 1.61–4.97). BCS loss of more than 0.75 units in the first two weeks postpartum was independently associated with higher hepatic lipid score after adjustment for parity, milk yield, and farm. These findings reinforce recommendations to manage cows below 3.5 at calving and highlight BCS dynamics as an inexpensive monitoring variable.

title: Hepatic oxidative stress markers in dairy cows with subclinical fatty liver: malondialdehyde, superoxide dismutase, and glutathione peroxidase profiles
abstract: Blood and liver biopsy samples were obtained from 38 cows at 10 days in milk. Animals were classified into three groups: no lipidosis (triglyceride < 30 mg/g; n = 14), moderate lipidosis (30–100 mg/g; n = 13), and severe lipidosis (> 100 mg/g; n = 11). Plasma malondialdehyde (MDA) was measured by TBARS assay; erythrocyte superoxide dismutase (SOD) and whole-blood glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activities were determined spectrophotometrically. Plasma MDA was significantly elevated in the severe lipidosis group compared with no-lipidosis controls (mean 5.8 vs. 3.1 nmol/mL, p < 0.001). SOD activity was significantly reduced in both moderate and severe groups. GPx activity showed a non-significant trend toward reduction. Correlations between hepatic triglyceride content and MDA (rs = 0.71) and SOD activity (rs = −0.64) were statistically significant. These data support the view that oxidative stress is a quantitatively meaningful component of fatty liver pathophysiology in cattle, not merely a secondary finding.

title: Effect of pre-loading fasting duration on feather corticosterone and meat quality traits in Ross 308 broilers
abstract: Broilers are routinely feed-withdrawn before transport to reduce contamination risk during slaughter. The welfare consequences of extended fasting periods remain incompletely characterised. Four fasting durations (4, 8, 12, and 18 hours) were applied to groups of 60 birds each before simulated transport of 60 minutes and 1-hour lairage. Feather corticosterone was assayed from breast feathers collected at slaughter. Breast muscle yield, drip loss, shear force, and colour (CIE L*a*b*) were also measured. Feather corticosterone did not differ significantly between 4- and 8-hour groups but increased 38% in the 18-hour group (p < 0.01). Drip loss was highest in the 18-hour group (3.8% vs. 2.1% in the 4-hour group). Shear force and colour were not significantly affected by fasting duration. The 8-hour withdrawal period appeared to represent a reasonable compromise between welfare and processing hygiene within this experimental context.

title: Discourse of Responsibility: How Hungarian and Serbian Language Media Frame Ethical Consumption
abstract: Using critical discourse analysis applied to a corpus of 180 newspaper and magazine articles published between 2010 and 2013 in Hungarian- and Serbian-language print media circulating in Vojvodina, this study examines how ethical and sustainable consumption is framed for readers. Articles were coded inductively along dimensions of individual responsibility, collective action, market failure, and governmental obligation. Hungarian-language outlets disproportionately foregrounded individual consumer responsibility (62% of coded segments), whereas Serbian-language outlets more frequently invoked state and regulatory actors (48%). The analysis suggests that the dominant discourse encountered by bilingual millennial consumers in the region constructs ethical purchasing as a personal moral obligation, potentially intensifying guilt without providing structural pathways to action. These discursive patterns are discussed in relation to broader post-socialist media legacies and their consequences for green marketing messaging strategies in the region.

title: Green Claims and Scepticism: Millennial Reactions to Environmental Labels on Fast-Moving Consumer Goods in Serbia
abstract: This mixed-methods study combined an online survey (n = 389, ages 22–35, Serbia) with eight focus group sessions (total 52 participants) to investigate how millennials evaluate environmental claims on product packaging. Survey data were analysed using exploratory factor analysis, yielding three interpretable factors: label comprehension, institutional trust, and personal relevance. Regression analysis showed that institutional trust was the strongest predictor of purchase likelihood (β = 0.38), while label comprehension alone did not significantly predict purchase intentions when controlling for scepticism. Focus group transcripts, coded thematically in MAXQDA, revealed that participants frequently distinguished between 'genuine' and 'cosmetic' environmental claims, using heuristics such as brand country of origin and packaging material as proxy credibility cues. The results suggest that greenwashing perceptions are already well-developed among Serbian millennials and that trust-building, rather than information provision, should be the primary lever for green marketing in this segment.

title: The Value–Action Gap in Green Purchasing: A Cross-National Comparison of Millennials in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania
abstract: This chapter contributes a three-country empirical comparison to a volume on sustainable consumption in post-transition economies. Standardised online surveys were administered to millennials (born 1981–1996) in Serbia (n = 312), Hungary (n = 298), and Romania (n = 305) using parallel translated questionnaires. Core constructs included environmental values (adapted NEP scale), purchase intentions (six green product categories), and recalled recent purchases. Across all three samples, bivariate gaps between intention and behaviour scores were statistically significant (paired t-tests, p < 0.001), but effect sizes varied: Serbia showed the largest gap (Cohen's d = 0.71), Hungary an intermediate gap (d = 0.54), and Romania the smallest (d = 0.48). Moderation analysis indicated that perceived income sufficiency significantly attenuated the gap in all three countries, while environmental identity moderated the gap only in the Hungarian sample. The chapter discusses implications for regionally tailored green marketing strategies.

title: Willingness to Pay for Eco-Certified Food Among Urban Millennials in Novi Sad: A Discrete Choice Experiment
abstract: A discrete choice experiment was conducted with 241 millennial respondents recruited from the Novi Sad urban area to estimate willingness to pay (WTP) for eco-certification, local origin labelling, and reduced plastic packaging on a standardised grocery basket. Twelve choice sets were constructed using an orthogonal design, each presenting three product bundles varying on these three attributes and price. Mixed logit models estimated in R (mlogit package) revealed that respondents placed highest marginal utility on local origin (WTP premium: 18.4% over baseline price), followed by reduced plastic packaging (12.1%), with eco-certification generating a modest but significant premium (7.3%). Latent class analysis identified two consumer segments: a 'values-driven' class (38% of sample) showing strong premiums across all attributes, and a 'price-sensitive' class (62%) whose eco-certification premium was statistically indistinguishable from zero. Findings indicate that eco-labels alone are insufficient triggers for purchase conversion among the majority of urban Serbian millennials.

title: Social Norms and Green Purchasing: Does Perceived Neighbourhood Behaviour Predict Individual Choices?
abstract: Drawing on norm activation theory and social comparison processes, this study tested whether perceptions of neighbourhood-level green behaviour predict self-reported green purchasing intentions and actual purchases, over and above personal environmental attitudes. An online survey was administered to 478 residents of four mid-sized Serbian cities (Novi Sad, Subotica, Zrenjanin, Sombor). Structural equation modelling (SEM, AMOS 26) showed that perceived injunctive norms (what neighbours think one should do) had a direct effect on intentions (β = 0.29) but not on reported purchases, whereas perceived descriptive norms (what neighbours actually do) predicted purchases directly (β = 0.21) even after controlling for intentions. The indirect path from personal environmental attitudes to purchases via intentions was partially mediated by descriptive norms. Age and city size did not moderate these relationships significantly. Results suggest that green marketing communications emphasising local community behaviour may be more effective than messaging focused on abstract environmental values.

title: Ethical Consumption Talk vs. Ethical Consumption Walk: Qualitative Evidence from Millennial Consumer Diaries in Vojvodina
abstract: This study employed a consumer diary methodology to capture the daily gap between ethical consumption intentions and purchasing decisions over a four-week period. Sixteen millennial participants (ages 26–36, recruited from Novi Sad and Subotica) kept structured written diaries documenting each purchase occasion, their stated intention beforehand, the actual decision made, and a free-text reflection. Diaries generated 1,847 purchase records, of which 34.2% involved products where an environmentally preferable alternative was available. In 61% of those cases, participants chose the non-green option despite prior stated intentions. Thematic analysis of free-text reflections identified five recurring rationalisations: convenience, price, habit, doubts about product efficacy, and symbolic social risk. Notably, symbolic social risk—fear of being seen as performative or elitist by peers—emerged as a category not prominently theorised in Western European literature on the attitude–behaviour gap, suggesting a culturally specific barrier in post-socialist consumer contexts.

title: Can Framing Effects Narrow the Green Purchasing Gap? A Survey Experiment with Millennial Consumers in Serbia and Croatia
abstract: A between-subjects survey experiment (n = 614, roughly equal split between Serbia and Croatia, millennials only) tested four message framing conditions for a hypothetical eco-certified household cleaning product: gain frame, loss frame, collective gain frame, and a control (product features only). Participants were randomly assigned to one condition and reported purchase intentions on a seven-point scale. ANCOVA controlling for prior environmental attitudes found a significant main effect of framing (F(3, 606) = 8.31, p < 0.001, η² = 0.04). The collective gain frame produced the highest mean intention scores in both country subsamples (Serbia: M = 4.81; Croatia: M = 4.93), with individual gain frames performing comparably in Croatia but significantly lower in Serbia. Loss frames performed no better than the control in either country. Moderated analysis showed that environmental identity amplified responses to the collective frame but not to others. The findings have direct implications for copywriting in green advertising campaigns targeting post-Yugoslav markets.

title: Sustainability Signalling on Social Media and Its Effect on Green Purchase Intentions: Evidence from Instagram Usage Patterns of Serbian Millennials
abstract: This study investigates how exposure to sustainability-related content on Instagram influences green purchase intentions among Serbian millennials, distinguishing between passive exposure (scrolling), active engagement (liking, saving), and content creation (posting). An online survey of 502 Instagram users aged 25–38 in Serbia measured weekly sustainability content interactions, environmental self-identity, perceived authenticity of brand sustainability posts, and intentions to purchase green products. Multiple regression analysis revealed that active engagement with sustainability content was a significant predictor of green purchase intentions (β = 0.31, p < 0.001), while passive exposure was not (β = 0.07, p = 0.19) after controlling for covariates. Perceived authenticity of brand posts moderated the relationship between active engagement and intentions, with high-authenticity perceptions amplifying the positive effect. Content creation was associated with stronger environmental self-identity but did not independently predict purchase intentions. Results suggest that brands should prioritise content that invites active interaction rather than maximising impressions.

title: Measuring the Attitude–Behaviour Gap Longitudinally: Preliminary Findings from a Two-Wave Panel Study of Millennial Green Consumers in Northern Serbia
abstract: This preprint reports first-wave and second-wave results from an ongoing panel study tracking the same cohort of 281 millennial respondents in Vojvodina over an 18-month interval (Wave 1: autumn 2023; Wave 2: spring 2025). The panel examines whether attitude–behaviour gaps in green purchasing are stable individual-level traits or fluctuate with contextual factors such as income changes, retail environment changes, and media exposure. Cross-lagged panel models estimated in lavaan (R) show that Wave 1 intentions predicted Wave 2 purchases (β = 0.18, p = 0.003), while Wave 1 purchases also predicted Wave 2 intentions (β = 0.23, p < 0.001), suggesting bidirectional reinforcement. The gap index (intention minus behaviour score) showed moderate rank-order stability (r = 0.44) but substantial within-person variability correlated with reported income satisfaction changes. A third wave is planned for late 2026. Full panel results will be submitted to a peer-reviewed outlet upon completion.

title: Atmospheric intervention toolkit for traditional market managers: developing and piloting a low-cost sensory audit instrument
abstract: Existing atmospheric audit tools are designed for enclosed retail formats and are poorly suited to outdoor markets with variable infrastructure. This paper reports the development and pilot testing of the Market Atmospheric Audit Instrument (MAAI), a structured observation and rating tool tailored to open-air settings. Item generation drew on interviews with fourteen market managers across Vojvodina and a review of atmospheric literature. The resulting 34-item instrument covers five dimensions: olfactory ambience, auditory environment, visual merchandising, spatial navigation, and social atmosphere. Pilot application at six markets over eight observation days (two trained raters per visit) yielded inter-rater reliability coefficients ranging from 0.71 to 0.88 (Cohen's κ). Concurrent validity was assessed by correlating MAAI dimension scores with exit-survey atmospheric satisfaction ratings (r ranging from 0.54 to 0.69). The instrument is made freely available for use by market authorities and researchers.

title: Regional Flood Frequency Analysis of Small Ungauged Catchments in the Bačka Plain Using L-Moments
abstract: Flood frequency estimation for ungauged basins in the flat agricultural landscape of Vojvodina is constrained by sparse gauging networks and short record lengths. This study applies L-moment-based regional frequency analysis to 34 small catchments (areas 15–320 km²) across the Bačka plain, grouping them into homogeneous regions through a combination of cluster analysis on catchment physiographic descriptors and the Hosking–Wallis discordancy test. The generalised logistic (GL) distribution was selected as the regional parent distribution based on L-kurtosis diagrams and Z-statistics. Regional growth curves were derived and validated against annual maximum instantaneous peak discharges from 1971 to 2008. The index-flood method was used to scale regional curves to individual sites via drainage area and mean annual precipitation regressions. For 100-year return periods, the regional estimates showed coefficient of variation reductions of 18–31% relative to at-site fitting. Uncertainty bounds were quantified by a 5000-iteration bootstrap procedure. The approach provides a transferable framework for ungauged design flood estimation in lowland agricultural drainage systems.

title: Detection of Trends in Annual Maximum Flows at Selected Gauging Stations in the Srem Region, 1960–2012
abstract: Hydrological stationarity is commonly assumed in flood frequency analysis, yet climate variability and land drainage works may induce trends in flood series. This paper applies a suite of non-parametric trend tests—Mann–Kendall, Spearman's rho, and the Pettitt change-point test—to annual maximum discharge series at 11 stations in the Srem region of Vojvodina over the period 1960–2012. Significant increasing trends at the 5% level were detected at four stations, all located in extensively tile-drained agricultural sub-catchments where drainage density increased markedly after 1975. Two stations showed statistically significant step changes around 1980, coinciding with large-scale drainage improvement works. No significant trend was found at stations with stable land cover and minimal drainage infrastructure change. The findings suggest that drainage intensification, rather than precipitation change, is the dominant non-stationarity driver in these catchments. Consequences for the reliability of stationary flood quantile estimates are evaluated using split-sample validation.

title: Non-Stationary Flood Frequency Analysis Using Time-Varying GEV Parameters: A Case Study on the Krivaja Sub-Catchment
abstract: Accounting for non-stationarity in flood frequency analysis requires models in which distribution parameters are allowed to vary with time or climatic covariates. This study applies the time-varying GEV framework to a 54-year annual maximum discharge record (1961–2014) from the Krivaja sub-catchment, a 1 430 km² lowland watershed in central Vojvodina. Location and scale parameters are modelled as linear and log-linear functions of time, large-scale atmospheric indices (North Atlantic Oscillation, standardised precipitation evapotranspiration index), and local drainage area expansions. Models are fitted by maximum likelihood and compared via AIC and BIC. The best-fitting model incorporates a log-linear trend in the location parameter driven by SPEI-12. At the 100-year return level, non-stationary estimates for the period 2000–2014 are 14–22% higher than those from a stationary GEV fitted to the full record. Confidence intervals for non-stationary quantiles are derived by parametric bootstrap. The results illustrate both the promise and the sensitivity of covariate-driven non-stationary models to covariate selection in data-limited lowland settings.

title: Regionalisation of Design Rainfall Extremes in Vojvodina Using Spatial Interpolation and At-Site Frequency Analysis
abstract: Design rainfall is the primary input to flood estimation in ungauged basins and directly affects drainage design standards. This study combines at-site GEV fitting at 42 daily precipitation stations in Vojvodina with three spatial interpolation methods—ordinary kriging, kriging with external drift using elevation and distance from Danube as secondary variables, and radial basis function interpolation—to produce gridded 1-, 10-, 50-, and 100-year return period rainfall maps at 1 km resolution. Cross-validation retained 20% of stations; the kriging with external drift approach yielded the lowest mean absolute error (MAE = 4.7 mm for the 100-year event). Uncertainty maps were derived from kriging variance. The resulting rainfall frequency atlas provides input data for design flood estimation in the approximately 400 ungauged sub-catchments of the Vojvodina drainage network. Comparisons with the existing 1980 national rainfall atlas indicate increases of 8–15% in 100-year daily rainfall totals across most of the province, consistent with observed increases in convective rainfall intensity.

title: Bayesian Inference for GEV Flood Quantiles Under Non-Stationarity: Informative Priors from Regional Data
abstract: Bayesian approaches to flood frequency analysis allow incorporation of regional information through prior distributions, which is particularly valuable for short records. This paper presents a Bayesian GEV framework in which informative priors for shape and scale parameters are derived from regional L-moment estimates pooled across 28 stations in Vojvodina with records of 25–68 years. Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling (Metropolis–Hastings algorithm, 100 000 iterations after 20 000 burn-in) is used to obtain posterior parameter distributions at 12 target sites. The non-stationary extension allows the location parameter to vary linearly with a 30-year running mean of April–June precipitation totals. Posterior predictive distributions for 50- and 100-year quantiles are compared with maximum likelihood GEV estimates and regional growth curve scaling. The Bayesian non-stationary model reduces 100-year quantile uncertainty by 19–27% relative to at-site ML fitting for records shorter than 30 years. The sensitivity of posteriors to prior specification is evaluated with a weakly informative Cauchy prior alternative.

title: Sensitivity of Flood Frequency Estimates to Catchment Delineation Errors in Flat Terrain: Vojvodina Lowlands
abstract: Catchment delineation in flat terrain is prone to error because small differences in DEM resolution and depression-filling algorithms propagate into significant changes in drainage area and shape descriptors. This study systematically evaluates how delineation uncertainty translates into uncertainty in index-flood estimates for 16 ungauged sub-catchments in Vojvodina. Four DEM sources are compared: SRTM 30 m, Copernicus DEM 10 m, national 5 m lidar-derived DEM, and a 2 m drone-survey DEM over a 180 km² test area. Drainage area discrepancies between SRTM and lidar delineations range from 4% to 31%, with largest errors in catchments smaller than 50 km². These area differences translate to 6–24% changes in index-flood estimates under the regional regression equation derived from 34 gauged catchments. The lidar-derived DEM reduces mean delineation error to below 3% relative to field-surveyed boundaries. Practical recommendations are given for DEM selection in drainage planning studies under Serbian regulatory frameworks.

title: Climate Change Projections for Extreme Precipitation and Flood Frequencies in Vojvodina: Ensemble Downscaling from EURO-CORDEX
abstract: Credible projections of future flood frequencies require downscaled climate model output that preserves the tail behaviour of precipitation distributions. This study uses a 12-member EURO-CORDEX ensemble (EUR-11, RCP4.5 and RCP8.5) to drive a semi-distributed rainfall–runoff model (HBV-light) calibrated for five representative Vojvodina catchments covering the range of soil types and drainage densities in the province. Bias correction is applied using quantile delta mapping, which preserves projected changes in extreme quantiles better than standard quantile mapping. For the period 2071–2100, ensemble median 100-year flood quantiles increase by 11–28% under RCP8.5 relative to a 1971–2000 baseline, with inter-model spread spanning −5% to +46%. Under RCP4.5, the median increase is 6–17%. Changes are smallest in the northern Bačka sub-catchments with high groundwater influence and largest in the tile-drained Srem catchments. Uncertainty decomposition attributes approximately 55% of total spread to model structure, 30% to internal variability, and 15% to scenario choice at the 2080s horizon.

title: Stochastic Simulation of Synthetic Flood Event Series for Drainage Infrastructure Stress-Testing in Vojvodina
abstract: Drainage infrastructure design in Vojvodina conventionally relies on a single design flood derived from frequency analysis. This study develops a stochastic event-based generator that produces long synthetic annual maximum series (10 000 years) preserving observed first and second moments, L-skewness, and inter-annual autocorrelation structure. The generator couples a Gaussian copula to marginal GEV distributions fitted individually to 22 catchments, thus reproducing spatial dependence in concurrent flood peaks across the drainage network. The synthetic series are used to stress-test a 14-node drainage canal network under current design capacity and two upgrade scenarios. Results show that the 1% annual exceedance probability event causes capacity exceedance at 6 of 14 nodes under current infrastructure, rising to 9 nodes if 100-year quantiles increase by 20% as projected under RCP8.5. Upgrade scenario 2, which enlarges the three highest-flow bottleneck reaches, reduces exceedance nodes to 2 under the climate-adjusted series. The framework provides a transparent basis for probabilistic infrastructure investment prioritisation.

title: Flood Frequency Analysis Methods for Agricultural Drainage Systems: A Comparative Review for Practitioners in the Pannonian Basin
abstract: Practitioners in the Pannonian Basin face practical choices between stationary and non-stationary methods, at-site and regional approaches, and classical and Bayesian estimation when conducting flood frequency analysis for drainage design. This book chapter provides a structured comparison of seven methods with respect to data requirements, computational burden, regulatory compatibility, and performance under short records and non-stationarity. Methods are illustrated using worked examples from Vojvodina and Hungarian drainage case studies. The discussion addresses the gap between research advances and the methods permitted under current Serbian and Hungarian design standards, which still require stationary GEV or Pearson III fitting in most regulatory contexts. Guidance is given on when non-stationary or regional methods are justified by record length and detected non-stationarity, and how their outputs can be presented to regulators. The chapter concludes with a decision flowchart intended for engineers without specialist statistical training.

title: Record-Length Effects on L-Moment Ratio Diagrams for Identifying Flood Frequency Distributions: A Simulation Study
abstract: L-moment ratio diagrams are widely used to identify the best-fitting parent distribution for annual maximum flood series, but their reliability degrades for short records. This simulation study quantifies sampling variability on L-skewness–L-kurtosis diagrams for five candidate distributions (GL, GEV, GNO, PE3, Wakeby) across record lengths of 15, 25, 40, and 60 years using 20 000 Monte Carlo replicates per combination. For n = 15, the 90% confidence ellipses of all five distributions overlap substantially, making unambiguous selection impractical. At n = 40, GL and GEV can be distinguished with about 70% power when the true distribution is GL with shape parameter k = −0.15. Practical implications for the 18–35-year records typical of Vojvodina drainage stations are evaluated: at these lengths, regional pooling of L-moment ratios across homogeneous groups is more reliable than at-site diagram fitting. Recommended minimum homogeneous-region sizes as a function of target discrimination power are tabulated.

title: Towards a Continuous Probability Framework for Agricultural Drainage Failure Risk in Vojvodina Under Changing Flood Regimes
abstract: Agricultural drainage failure causes direct crop losses and soil saturation damage that accumulate over multiple flood seasons. This preprint proposes a continuous risk framework in which annual drainage exceedance probability is treated as a time-varying quantity driven by non-stationary flood frequency estimates and projected shifts in the seasonal distribution of peak flows under climate change. A Poisson arrival model with non-stationary rate parameter is coupled to a crop loss function calibrated from reported drainage failure events in Vojvodina between 1990 and 2022. Three damage metrics are computed: expected annual damage (EAD), probability of at least one drainage exceedance in a 10-year planning horizon, and value-at-risk at the 95th percentile of annual loss. Under RCP8.5 mid-century conditions, EAD increases by 31–44% relative to the stationary baseline. The framework is implemented in a publicly available R package (PannonDrainRisk) with documented functions for non-stationary rate estimation, copula-based spatial dependence, and damage aggregation across network nodes. Results are preliminary pending peer review.

title: Calibration of the AquaCrop model for sunflower under deficit irrigation conditions in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: AquaCrop (FAO version 6.1) was calibrated and validated for sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.) using three seasons of field trial data (2012–2014) collected at the experimental station in Rimski Šančevi, Serbia. Four deficit irrigation treatments (100%, 75%, 50%, and 25% of full irrigation dose) were applied in a randomised block design across twelve plots. Canopy cover, soil water content (measured with FDR probes at 20, 40, and 60 cm depth), and final biomass and seed yield were used for model calibration. After calibration, the model reproduced observed yield with a root mean square error of 0.31 t/ha and an index of agreement of 0.94 across validation treatments. Simulated soil water depletion at the 0–60 cm layer matched gravimetric measurements within ±12 mm. The calibrated parameter set is suitable for seasonal scheduling exercises in the northern Serbian lowlands and is provided in full as supplementary material.

title: Comparison of two low-cost soil moisture sensor networks for irrigation scheduling support in sugar beet production
abstract: Two commercially available low-cost capacitance sensor systems (FieldSens-200 and AgroMoist Pro, both fictional) were evaluated against a gravimetric reference and a calibrated FDR system over one full sugar beet growing season (April–October 2022) on a Calcic Chernozem soil in Bačka. Each system was installed in three plots with six sensors per plot at depths of 20, 40, and 60 cm. Sensor readings were logged at 30-minute intervals and transmitted via GSM to a cloud platform. Against the gravimetric reference, the FieldSens-200 yielded a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.028 m³/m³, while AgroMoist Pro showed MAE of 0.041 m³/m³. Both systems tracked depletion dynamics sufficiently to trigger irrigation at the 50% allowable depletion threshold within ±1 day of the reference schedule in 78% and 64% of cases, respectively. Sensor drift of up to 0.015 m³/m³ was observed after 90 days for AgroMoist Pro, requiring periodic re-calibration. The results provide a practical basis for cost–benefit selection of sensor technology for precision irrigation management on medium-sized farms.

title: Long-term phosphorus accumulation in sediments of a constructed wetland treating tile drainage: implications for system renewal
abstract: Sediment cores were extracted from a 12-year-old HSSF-CW at the Rimski Šančevi station to characterise phosphorus fractionation and estimate residual sorption capacity. Sequential extraction following the Psenner–Bostrom procedure distinguished loosely bound, iron-associated, aluminium-associated, and calcium-associated phosphorus fractions. Total sediment phosphorus increased from an initial value of 180 mg P kg⁻¹ (fresh gravel reference) to 2,340 mg P kg⁻¹ in the most loaded inlet zone. Iron-associated fractions dominated (52–61% of total P) in the upper 10 cm. Residual sorption capacity estimated from Freundlich isotherms on intact sediment samples was less than 15% of original in the inlet third of the bed, compared with 63% in the outlet third. Annual phosphorus mass balance indicated the wetland had entered a net phosphorus release phase in years 10–12 under elevated summer temperatures. These results indicate a need to define substrate renewal intervals and point to inlet-zone hot-spots as priority targets for partial media replacement.

title: Comparative Governance of Irrigation Water-User Associations in Post-Yugoslav States: Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia 1995–2003
abstract: Drawing on a parallel dataset collected between 1999 and 2003 across Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia, this book chapter situates the development of WUAs within the distinct agrarian reform trajectories of three post-Yugoslav successor states. Each country inherited fragments of the same federal hydraulic infrastructure yet pursued divergent institutional models: Slovenia moved rapidly toward voluntary associations aligned with EU water framework expectations; Croatia created hybrid state–cooperative entities; Serbia retained quasi-administrative associations with limited financial autonomy. Governance performance is assessed across fourteen indicators grouped into four dimensions: financial viability, maintenance standard, user inclusion, and conflict resolution capacity. Slovenian associations scored highest on all four dimensions by 2002, though starting from a more favorable economic baseline. Serbian associations exhibited the widest internal variance. The chapter draws on 78 key-informant interviews, documentary analysis, and field visits to 21 schemes, and argues that EU accession pressure functioned as a critical external driver of institutional consolidation.

title: Attachment kinetics of Pseudomonas fluorescens isolates from fresh-cut lettuce processing lines at 4 °C and 8 °C on stainless steel and polypropylene coupons
abstract: Twelve Pseudomonas fluorescens strains isolated from commercial fresh-cut lettuce processing lines in Vojvodina were characterised for surface attachment under refrigerated conditions. Stainless steel (AISI 304) and polypropylene coupons were inoculated at initial densities of 10^3–10^5 CFU/cm² and incubated for 2, 6, 12, and 24 hours at 4 °C and 8 °C. Attached cell counts were determined by plate counting and scanning electron microscopy was used to assess surface coverage. At 8 °C, mean attached cell densities on polypropylene were 1.8-fold higher than on stainless steel at 12 hours (p < 0.05), while differences were less pronounced at 4 °C. Hydrophobicity measured by the BATH method correlated positively with attachment efficiency on polypropylene (r = 0.71). Three strains showed markedly faster attachment regardless of surface material and temperature, suggesting strain-level variation of practical relevance for hygiene management. These findings indicate that surface material selection and temperature control interact in determining early colonisation risk in fresh-cut vegetable lines.

title: Expression of las-type quorum-sensing genes in Pseudomonas fluorescens biofilms formed on fresh-cut carrot surfaces during simulated cold storage
abstract: This study examined whether quorum-sensing (QS) signalling contributes to biofilm development by Pseudomonas fluorescens on shredded carrot surfaces stored at 4 °C and 8 °C over seven days. A single model strain isolated from a Vojvodina processing facility was used. Acyl-homoserine lactone (AHL) concentrations in carrot exudate were quantified by LC-MS/MS, and relative expression of lasI and lasR homologues was tracked by RT-qPCR at 24-hour intervals. Biofilm biomass was assessed by confocal laser scanning microscopy with SYTO 9 staining. AHL concentrations exceeded the estimated QS threshold of 0.5 µM between days 3 and 4 at 8 °C, coinciding with a statistically significant increase in biofilm thickness (from 12 ± 2 µm to 28 ± 5 µm). At 4 °C, AHL accumulation was delayed by approximately 48 hours and peak biofilm thickness was 35% lower. lasI expression correlated strongly with AHL levels (r = 0.84). Results suggest that temperature management within the cold chain may delay QS-regulated biofilm maturation and that carrot matrix components support sufficient AHL accumulation to trigger population-level responses.

title: Effect of chlorine-based and peracetic acid sanitisers on established Pseudomonas fluorescens biofilms in fresh-cut vegetable processing: biomass reduction and regrowth kinetics
abstract: Established biofilms of Pseudomonas fluorescens are substantially more resistant to sanitisers than planktonic cells. This study compared sodium hypochlorite (200 ppm free chlorine) and peracetic acid (PAA, 80 ppm) treatments on 48-hour-old and 120-hour-old biofilms grown on stainless steel coupons at 6 °C. Immediate log reductions, residual viable cell counts (epifluorescence with propidium iodide/SYTO 9), and regrowth at 6 °C over 48 hours post-treatment were measured. PAA achieved 2.4 ± 0.3 log CFU/cm² reduction on 48-hour biofilms compared with 1.8 ± 0.4 log for hypochlorite (p < 0.05). For 120-hour biofilms, both sanitisers were less effective, with log reductions of 1.6 and 1.1 respectively. Regrowth was faster after hypochlorite treatment in both biofilm ages. Extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) dry weight correlated negatively with sanitiser efficacy (r = −0.68 for PAA). Findings suggest that PAA offers a modest but consistent advantage and that biofilm age and EPS accumulation should be considered when setting sanitisation intervals.

title: Effect of spectral preprocessing strategies on PLS-DA model performance for geographic origin classification of cold-pressed flaxseed oil
abstract: Geographic origin labelling of flaxseed oil carries marketing and regulatory significance in the Western Balkans. This work investigated whether NIR spectral fingerprints, combined with partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), can separate flaxseed oil samples by region of production (Vojvodina, Slavonia, and Pannonian Hungary). Sixty-nine oil samples were collected over one harvest season from verified smallholder producers. Twelve preprocessing combinations were systematically compared: raw spectra, SNV, multiplicative scatter correction (MSC), first and second Savitzky-Golay derivatives, and their combinations. Model performance was evaluated by sensitivity, specificity, and area under the ROC curve in stratified 5-fold cross-validation. MSC combined with first derivative gave the best overall performance (mean AUC 0.89 across three classes), while raw spectra models showed systematic baseline drift artefacts. Vojvodina samples were classified with higher sensitivity (0.91) than the other two regions (0.82–0.85), likely due to better within-class sample homogeneity. The study underlines the importance of preprocessing selection as a modelling decision with substantive accuracy consequences rather than a purely technical step.

title: Strain elastography of thyroid nodules: initial experience at a single tertiary centre in Vojvodina
abstract: This prospective study evaluated real-time strain elastography (SE) as a supplement to conventional B-mode ultrasound for characterising thyroid nodules in 87 consecutive patients referred for fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) between 2009 and 2011. Each nodule was scored on a five-point Asteria elasticity scale and categorised independently by two radiologists blinded to cytological results. Histopathological or cytological diagnosis served as the reference standard. Among 94 evaluated nodules, 23 were confirmed malignant on histopathology. SE achieved a sensitivity of 78.3% and specificity of 84.3% at an Asteria score threshold of ≥3, with an area under the ROC curve of 0.86. Inter-observer agreement was moderate (κ = 0.61). Nodules smaller than 8 mm and those with marked calcification showed lower diagnostic accuracy, reducing sensitivity to 58% in this subgroup. The results suggest SE is a useful adjunct but should not replace cytological sampling for indeterminate nodules. Limitations include the single-centre design and relatively small malignant cohort.

title: Comparison of elasticity score and strain ratio in predicting thyroid nodule malignancy
abstract: Strain ratio (SR), computed as the ratio of adipose tissue stiffness to nodule stiffness, has been proposed as a more reproducible elastographic measure than qualitative scoring alone. This retrospective analysis of 141 nodules from 128 patients compared the Asteria five-point score with SR derived from a standardised reference region in the adjacent strap muscle. Cytological or histological confirmation was available for all nodules. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis showed the SR threshold of 2.05 yielded sensitivity 81.5% and specificity 79.4% (AUC 0.87), compared with sensitivity 76.3% and specificity 82.1% for the Asteria score (AUC 0.84). The difference between AUC values was not statistically significant (p = 0.31, DeLong test). SR showed slightly lower intra-observer variability (CV 9.2% vs 14.7% for qualitative scoring). These findings indicate that both methods perform comparably, and the choice may depend on operator experience and equipment software availability.

title: Influence of nodule size and composition on elastographic assessment of thyroid lesions
abstract: Sonographic characteristics such as nodule size, cystic component fraction, and coarse calcification are known to affect the technical reliability of ultrasound elastography. This prospective study enrolled 210 nodules in 187 patients and stratified results by nodule diameter (<10 mm, 10–20 mm, >20 mm) and composition (solid, predominantly solid, mixed, predominantly cystic). Technically adequate strain elastography images were obtainable in 91.4% of solid and predominantly solid nodules but only 53.7% of predominantly cystic lesions. For solid nodules over 10 mm, sensitivity and specificity for malignancy were 83% and 88% respectively. Elastography added incremental diagnostic value (net reclassification improvement 12.4%) over B-mode alone when restricted to solid nodules. Cystic or spongiform nodules should be excluded from routine elastographic scoring protocols. Practical cut-off criteria for patient selection are proposed.

title: Inter-observer agreement in thyroid strain elastography among radiologists with different experience levels
abstract: Elastography interpretation depends on operator training, yet the impact of experience level on agreement has been insufficiently quantified for thyroid applications. Three radiologists—one senior (>8 years of thyroid ultrasound), one intermediate (3–5 years), and one junior (<1 year)—independently scored 96 solid thyroid nodules using the five-point Asteria system. Images were acquired by a single senior sonographer to isolate scoring variability from acquisition variability. Weighted kappa between senior and intermediate was 0.68; between senior and junior 0.47; between intermediate and junior 0.52. Disagreements clustered at scores 2 and 3, the clinically most consequential zone. After a two-hour structured training session, junior observer kappa with the senior improved to 0.63 on a separate 40-nodule validation set. Structured training meaningfully reduces disagreement and should be incorporated into residency programmes before independent elastographic reporting is permitted.

title: Shear-wave elastography of thyroid nodules: quantitative stiffness values and malignancy prediction in a prospective cohort
abstract: Shear-wave elastography (SWE) provides quantitative tissue stiffness in kilopascals and is less operator-dependent than strain methods. This prospective study measured mean, maximum, and minimum SWE values in 163 nodules confirmed by post-surgical histopathology (54 malignant, 109 benign). Measurements used a 5 mm circular region of interest placed centrally in the nodule and repeated three times. Mean stiffness in malignant nodules was 58.4 ± 21.3 kPa versus 22.7 ± 9.1 kPa in benign nodules (p < 0.001). At an optimal threshold of 34 kPa, sensitivity was 85.2% and specificity 82.6% (AUC 0.91). Maximum SWE showed marginally higher AUC (0.93) but greater measurement variance. SWE outperformed concurrent strain elastography scoring (AUC 0.86) in the same cohort. Subgroup analysis showed that follicular carcinoma had lower stiffness than papillary carcinoma (41.2 vs 67.8 kPa, p = 0.003), which may affect diagnostic thresholds by histotype.
