title: Combined B-mode TIRADS scoring and shear-wave elastography for reducing unnecessary fine-needle aspiration biopsies of thyroid nodules
abstract: Fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) rates for thyroid nodules are high, and many yield benign or non-diagnostic results. This retrospective study assessed whether a combined decision rule—EU-TIRADS category plus SWE stiffness threshold—could safely reduce FNAB referrals. Among 248 nodules categorised as EU-TIRADS 3 or 4 (intermediate risk), adding a stiffness cut-off of <28 kPa as a criterion to defer biopsy reclassified 71 nodules to observation. Of these, five-year follow-up ultrasound was available for 63 nodules; two proved malignant (both low-risk papillary microcarcinomas < 5 mm managed conservatively). The combined rule reduced FNAB rate by 28.6% with a miss rate of 3.2% for clinically relevant malignancies. Sensitivity for detection of high-risk malignancies was maintained at 97.8%. A prospective validation study is warranted before clinical implementation of this protocol.

title: Thyroid elastography in pregnancy: normative stiffness values and influence of gestational age
abstract: Thyroid volume and perfusion change during pregnancy, potentially affecting elastographic stiffness measurements. This cross-sectional study enrolled 80 healthy pregnant women at gestational weeks 10–12, 20–22, and 30–32, and 30 age-matched non-pregnant controls. SWE was used to measure parenchymal stiffness in three regions of each lobe. Mean parenchymal stiffness was 12.3 ± 3.1 kPa in controls, 11.8 ± 3.4 kPa in the first trimester, 13.2 ± 3.9 kPa in the second, and 14.7 ± 4.2 kPa in the third trimester. ANOVA showed a significant increase across trimesters (p = 0.008) but all values remained well below published malignancy thresholds. Thyroid volume correlated weakly but significantly with stiffness in the third trimester (r = 0.31, p = 0.04). These normative data suggest that standard malignancy thresholds can be applied in pregnancy without trimester-specific adjustment, though the modest stiffness increase should be noted when interpreting borderline values.

title: Elastography of Hashimoto thyroiditis: parenchymal stiffness as a marker of fibrotic transformation
abstract: Hashimoto thyroiditis causes progressive fibrosis that may alter parenchymal stiffness, yet the relationship between histological fibrosis grade and elastographic values is not well characterised. Forty-one patients with biopsy-confirmed Hashimoto thyroiditis were graded for fibrosis (mild, moderate, severe) and compared with 40 controls with normal thyroid histology. SWE parenchymal stiffness was measured in four standardised positions per lobe. Mean stiffness increased significantly across fibrosis grades: 13.1 kPa (mild), 19.4 kPa (moderate), 28.6 kPa (severe) versus 11.9 kPa in controls (p < 0.001, Kruskal–Wallis). Spearman correlation between fibrosis grade and stiffness was 0.72 (p < 0.001). Anti-TPO antibody titre correlated weakly with stiffness (r = 0.28, p = 0.07). These results indicate that SWE may track fibrotic progression in Hashimoto thyroiditis, but stiffness elevations from fibrosis could complicate malignancy detection in co-existing nodules, where adjusted thresholds may be needed.

title: Reproducibility of shear-wave elastography measurements across three ultrasound platforms in thyroid nodule assessment
abstract: SWE stiffness values are known to vary between ultrasound systems due to differences in push-pulse sequences and reconstruction algorithms. This multicentre cross-platform study enrolled 55 patients with solid thyroid nodules who underwent SWE measurement on three systems (Siemens Acuson S3000, Canon Aplio i800, Esaote MyLab Twice X) on the same day in randomised order. Each system provided three repeated measurements per nodule. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) for within-system repeatability were 0.91–0.94. Between-system ICC was 0.74, indicating moderate cross-platform agreement. Bland-Altman analysis showed systematic stiffness offsets: Canon measurements were on average 6.8 kPa higher than Siemens (limits of agreement −4.1 to 17.7 kPa), and Esaote was 3.4 kPa higher than Siemens (limits −6.2 to 13.0 kPa). These offsets are clinically relevant and suggest that malignancy thresholds derived on one platform cannot be directly applied to another without recalibration. Platform-specific reference intervals are recommended.

title: Reproducibility of liver ADC measurements across two field strengths in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
abstract: Quantitative MRI metrics must be reproducible across scanners to be clinically useful. This study assessed the reproducibility of ADC measurements obtained at 1.5 T and 3 T in 42 patients diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Each patient underwent both examinations within seven days. ADC was measured in three standardised hepatic segments by two independent readers. The coefficient of variation across field strengths was 8.3% for reader 1 and 9.1% for reader 2. Intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.82 (1.5 T) and 0.79 (3 T) for inter-reader agreement. ADC values at 3 T were systematically 6% lower than at 1.5 T, a difference attributable to T2 shine-through effects at higher field. Correction factors are proposed. The findings support standardisation efforts needed before ADC enters routine clinical staging workflows.

title: Time-domain simulation of conducted disturbances generated by single-phase rectifiers in low-voltage residential networks
abstract: A time-domain simulation framework is developed to predict conducted emissions from single-phase uncontrolled rectifiers connected to a simplified residential low-voltage network. The network is represented by a ladder model with frequency-dependent line parameters derived from measurements on a 230 V, 50 Hz test feeder of approximately 120 m length. Rectifier loads ranging from 100 W to 2 kW are modelled as nonlinear voltage-dependent current sources parameterised from laboratory measurements. Simulated disturbance voltages at the mains terminal are compared against LISN-based measurements following CISPR 16-1-1 procedures over the 9 kHz to 30 MHz range. Agreement within 4 dB is achieved across the 150 kHz to 2 MHz sub-band, with larger deviations at higher frequencies attributed to parasitic capacitances not included in the ladder model. The study identifies the 450 kHz to 600 kHz interval as the most sensitive to load power level, with peak quasi-peak levels increasing by up to 11 dB when aggregate load increases from 500 W to 2 kW. The results suggest that existing CISPR limits may be approached under dense residential loading conditions.

title: Frequency-dependent impedance characterisation of low-voltage cable types used in Serbian urban distribution networks
abstract: The per-unit-length impedance and admittance parameters of four cable types commonly deployed in Serbian urban low-voltage distribution networks are characterised over the 10 kHz to 30 MHz frequency range using a two-port vector network analyser. Cable lengths between 10 m and 80 m are measured in open-circuit and short-circuit configurations, and results are fitted to a standard transmission-line model augmented with a skin-effect correction term. Measured propagation constants are compared to values predicted by IEC 60228-based geometric calculations, revealing deviations of up to 18% in the attenuation constant above 1 MHz for flat-conductor aluminium cables. The characterised parameters are incorporated into a SPICE-compatible model library intended for conducted emission simulations. Sensitivity analysis shows that uncertainty in conductor geometry translates to a maximum 6 dB uncertainty in predicted disturbance voltage at a 30 m cable termination at 10 MHz. The data set covers NYY, NAYY, NYM and NYFGbY cable types in cross-sections from 1.5 mm² to 25 mm².

title: Impact of variable-speed drives on harmonic voltage distortion in industrial low-voltage busbars
abstract: Harmonic voltage measurements are carried out on three low-voltage industrial busbars (400 V, 50 Hz) in a metalworking facility over a seven-day continuous recording period using a class A power quality analyser. Variable-speed drives of 5.5 kW to 90 kW nameplate ratings account for between 40% and 70% of connected load depending on the shift schedule. Total harmonic distortion of voltage (THDV) consistently exceeds the EN 50160 indicative limit of 8% during peak production hours, reaching up to 12.3%. The fifth and seventh voltage harmonics dominate, with average magnitudes of 4.1% and 3.6% of fundamental respectively. Measured current spectra from individual drives are used to construct aggregated injection models following IEC 61000-3-6 guidelines, and harmonic load flow calculations are performed on a network model validated against field measurements. Simulations reproduce measured THDV values within 1.5 percentage points. Mitigation options including passive fifth-harmonic filters and increased feeder conductor cross-section are evaluated, with the former reducing THDV to below 6% under peak load.

title: Conducted emission test reproducibility for switch-mode power supplies: influence of LISN topology and mains impedance variation
abstract: Switch-mode power supplies (SMPS) are tested for conducted emissions according to CISPR 32 using three commercially available line impedance stabilisation networks (LISNs) of nominally identical 50 Ω/50 µH topology but from different manufacturers. Tests are performed on five SMPS samples with rated power between 30 W and 250 W. Measured quasi-peak levels at the same SMPS unit differ by up to 7.2 dB across LISNs in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band, exceeding the 3 dB reproducibility figure often cited in the literature. The observed discrepancies are traced to differences in the LISN high-frequency impedance characteristic, particularly a self-resonance near 1.4 MHz in one unit. An additional test campaign varies the mains source impedance from 0.05 Ω to 0.8 Ω at 50 Hz by inserting series inductors, demonstrating that SMPS peak emission levels shift by up to 5 dB due to changes in rectifier operating point. These findings have implications for compliance margins and for the interpretation of borderline-pass test results.

title: Interference between ripple control signals and supraharmonic emissions in distribution networks: a time-domain case study
abstract: Ripple control systems operating at 316.7 Hz and 750 Hz are widely used by distribution system operators in central Europe for remote load switching. This study investigates the extent to which supraharmonic emissions from switch-mode loads corrupt ripple control telegram reception in a 400 V test feeder modelled from parameters measured in a suburban distribution area near Novi Sad. A full time-domain model is built in MATLAB/Simulink incorporating a ripple control transmitter, feeder impedance, and four classes of switching loads: SMPS, LED drivers, PV micro-inverters, and EV on-board chargers. At 15% feeder loading with mixed loads, signal-to-interference ratio at the receiver input drops below the 20 dB design threshold assumed in EN 61000-5-1 for ripple control. Worst-case degradation of 28 dB is observed when multiple PV micro-inverters synchronise their switching near the ripple control frequency. Temporal correlation between load power cycles and interference bursts is demonstrated. The model is validated against a 4-hour measurement record from the test feeder with 4.5% mean absolute error in receiver input voltage.

title: Common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions: measurement method comparison and uncertainty analysis
abstract: Four methods for separating common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) conducted emissions from single-phase equipment are compared: a commercial CM/DM separator, a home-built balun-based separator, a two-LISN simultaneous measurement approach, and a post-processing technique applied to standard LISN recordings. Measurements are performed on five reference loads including a 100 W SMPS, a 40 W LED driver array, and a 1.5 kW motor controller in the 150 kHz to 30 MHz band. Separator insertion loss and balance-to-unbalance conversion ratio are characterised by network analyser, revealing that the commercial unit maintains 40 dB mode separation only below 5 MHz. Uncertainty budgets are constructed according to JCGM 100:2008 for each method. Total standard uncertainty ranges from 1.1 dB to 3.8 dB depending on method and frequency, with the two-LISN method providing the lowest uncertainty above 10 MHz. Practical guidance is provided on method selection depending on available equipment and required accuracy.

title: Electromagnetic compatibility in low-voltage distribution systems: measurement methods, modelling, and regulatory framework
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of EMC problems specific to low-voltage distribution systems, intended for practising engineers and postgraduate students. The presentation proceeds from the physical mechanisms of conducted disturbance generation in power electronic equipment through to network propagation, coupling to sensitive loads, and measurement practice. The regulatory framework covering CISPR 11, CISPR 32, IEC 61000-3-2, IEC 61000-3-12 and EN 50160 is described with attention to applicability conditions and current revision status as of 2020. Frequency-domain and time-domain modelling approaches are compared for three representative scenarios: aggregated residential loading, industrial bus with variable-speed drives, and mixed-use low-voltage feeders with embedded generation. Common measurement pitfalls including grounding, LISN placement, and ambient noise subtraction are discussed with illustrative examples drawn from the authors' laboratory experience. The chapter concludes with an outline of open research questions including the standardisation of supraharmonic measurement methods and probabilistic compliance assessment.

title: Conducted disturbance propagation from EV on-board chargers: network impedance dependency and phase-to-phase coupling
abstract: Three-phase low-voltage feeders serving residential parking areas with electric vehicle charging infrastructure are studied using a combination of laboratory measurements and network simulation. On-board chargers of 3.3 kW, 7.4 kW and 11 kW rated power are characterised individually on a LISN test bench, and their emission spectra exported as Norton equivalent sources. A three-phase feeder model of 60 m length is parameterised from field impedance measurements and loaded with up to 12 simultaneous charger connections distributed across phases. Phase-to-phase coupling via the neutral conductor and earth return path is analysed and shown to introduce cross-phase disturbance voltages up to 8 dB below the directly driven phase in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band. Feeder impedance variation due to the connection of reactive compensation capacitors shifts dominant emission peaks by up to 40 kHz. Compliance margins relative to EN 61000-3-11 group emission limits shrink by 6 dB when six or more chargers of the same type operate simultaneously. Results are discussed in the context of planned charging hub deployments.

title: Statistical characterisation of supraharmonic emission levels in a low-voltage feeder over a 12-month monitoring campaign
abstract: Continuous monitoring of supraharmonic current and voltage emissions at the 400 V low-voltage busbar of a suburban distribution substation near Novi Sad is carried out over twelve consecutive months using a purpose-built acquisition system with 1 MS/s sampling and 90 dB dynamic range. The feeder supplies a mixture of residential and small commercial loads. Emission spectra are computed in 200 Hz bins from 2 kHz to 150 kHz on a ten-minute aggregation basis in accordance with the draft measurement protocol of IEC/TR 61000-2-1-2 Ed.2. Statistical distributions of emission levels are fitted to lognormal models at selected spectral bins; the 95th percentile levels at 16 kHz and 40 kHz are 12.1% and 6.3% of the fundamental current respectively. Clear diurnal and weekly patterns are observed, with evening peaks 4 to 9 dB above overnight minima. Seasonal variation is modest (less than 2 dB) except at 16 kHz, where a 5 dB increase in winter is attributed to increased LED and SMPS loading. The data set is made available as a supplementary repository and is intended for validation of aggregation models.

title: Apparent digestibility of dry matter and crude protein in pelleted diets for common carp (Cyprinus carpio) under semi-intensive pond conditions
abstract: This study established baseline apparent digestibility coefficients (ADCs) for dry matter and crude protein in pelleted compound diets fed to common carp held in earthen ponds at the University of Novi Sad experimental farm. Six dietary treatments differing in fishmeal inclusion level (0–18%) were evaluated over a 56-day trial using yttrium oxide as an inert marker. Faecal samples were collected by stripping from 30 fish per treatment replicated across three ponds. Dry matter ADC ranged from 61.4% to 69.8% and crude protein ADC from 78.2% to 87.6%, with higher values associated with greater fishmeal inclusion. Water temperature was maintained between 22 and 26°C throughout the trial. Feed conversion ratios ranged from 1.91 to 2.34. Results indicate that marker recovery was consistent above 91% across all treatments, validating the stripping methodology for carp under pond conditions. The data provide reference values for subsequent comparisons with extruded feed forms.

title: Comparative growth and feed utilisation of juvenile European catfish (Silurus glanis) offered extruded versus pelleted diets in pond trials
abstract: European catfish juveniles (mean initial weight 32 g) were allocated to earthen ponds and fed either a cold-pelleted or a steam-extruded diet of identical ingredient composition over 70 days during the summer season. Each treatment was replicated in three ponds (n = 150 fish per pond). Specific growth rate was 1.61% per day for extruded-fed fish compared to 1.38% for pelleted-fed fish. Feed conversion ratio was 1.74 and 2.11 for extruded and pelleted groups, respectively. Whole-body proximate composition was determined at trial start and end; protein retention was 8.4 percentage points higher in the extruded group. No significant differences in hepatosomatic index or condition factor were detected. Water quality parameters (dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH, ammonia) were recorded daily and remained within acceptable ranges throughout. Observations on feed rejection at the surface suggested pelleted feed produced greater post-feeding turbidity, potentially indicating mechanical breakdown. The data support a digestibility advantage for extruded feeds in catfish production.

title: Apparent digestibility coefficients for energy and lipid fractions in extruded and pelleted feeds for common carp: a direct comparison under pond conditions
abstract: A two-year field experiment was conducted at three commercial carp farms in Vojvodina to compare apparent digestibility coefficients for gross energy, ether extract, and nitrogen-free extractives between steam-extruded and cold-pelleted diets. Chromic oxide was incorporated at 0.5% in both feed types, and rectal stripping was performed on samples of 20 fish per farm per period at four time points spanning water temperatures from 18 to 28°C. Extruded diets showed consistently higher energy ADC (mean 74.6% vs. 67.3%) and ether extract ADC (mean 91.2% vs. 84.5%). The digestibility advantage of extrusion was larger at lower water temperatures, suggesting a temperature–feed form interaction affecting enzymatic capacity. Nitrogen-free extractive ADC was 88.1% for extruded versus 71.4% for pelleted diets. Inter-farm variability was moderate (CV 6–11%), attributed to differences in ambient plankton load and stocking density. These field-based coefficients are intended to support least-cost diet formulation for pond carp producers in the region.

title: Influence of feed form and feeding rate on nitrogen excretion and water quality in carp pond mesocosms
abstract: The environmental footprint of feed form was assessed in 12 mesocosm ponds (each 200 m²) stocked with common carp at 500 kg/ha and assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design (pelleted vs. extruded × maintenance vs. satiation feeding rate). Total ammonia nitrogen, nitrite, nitrate, total phosphorus, and biochemical oxygen demand were measured twice weekly over 60 days. Extruded-fed fish at satiation produced 14.8% less total ammonia nitrogen per kilogram of biomass gained than pelleted-fed fish at satiation, and total phosphorus accumulation in pond water was 11.2% lower. Satiation feeding increased all waste parameters relative to maintenance feeding regardless of feed form. Extruded feed at maintenance feeding produced the lowest measured environmental load. Sediment total nitrogen and phosphorus at trial end reflected the water column differences. Results suggest that feed form choice interacts with feeding management in determining pond nutrient loading, with implications for regulatory compliance under the EU Nitrates Directive.

title: Seasonal variation in apparent digestibility of extruded carp diets: data from two consecutive production seasons in Vojvodina
abstract: Seasonal fluctuations in digestibility were tracked over two full production seasons (April–October 2018 and 2019) at a single semi-intensive carp farm in central Vojvodina. Sampling was performed monthly, with rectal stripping of 25 fish per month. Water temperature ranged from 14.2°C in early April to 29.8°C in late July. Crude protein ADC of the extruded test diet ranged from 79.8% in April to 88.9% in July, declining to 83.1% by October. Dry matter ADC followed a similar pattern. Regression analysis indicated that water temperature explained 61% of the variance in crude protein ADC across both seasons (R² = 0.61, p < 0.001). Inter-annual repeatability was high (mean coefficient of variation 3.8% for monthly paired observations). The study provides empirical guidance for season-specific feed allocation and formulation adjustments, particularly for spring and autumn when temperature-related digestibility reductions are most pronounced.

title: Feed form effects on digestive enzyme activity in the pyloric region of common carp and European catfish
abstract: Digestive enzyme activity was compared in common carp and European catfish fed extruded or pelleted diets for 35 days in indoor tanks. Proteases (trypsin, chymotrypsin, leucine aminopeptidase), amylase, and lipase activities were measured spectrophotometrically in mucosal scrapings from the pyloric region and the mid-intestine. In carp, amylase activity was 38% higher in extruded-fed fish, consistent with greater starch gelatinisation in extruded products. Trypsin activity did not differ significantly between feed forms in either species. European catfish showed higher lipase activity in extruded-fed individuals (by 22%), correlating with improved ether extract ADC observed in parallel digestibility trials. Species differences were more pronounced for amylase and lipase than for proteases, reflecting the omnivorous versus carnivorous digestive strategy. Section histology confirmed normal villus morphology in all groups. These mechanistic data partially explain the performance advantages of extruded feeds observed in field trials.

title: Nutritional value of insect meal (Hermetia illucens prepupae) in extruded diets for common carp: digestibility and growth trial
abstract: Black soldier fly prepupae meal was produced under a controlled rearing protocol and incorporated at 0, 10, 20, and 30% into steam-extruded diets for common carp, replacing fishmeal on an isonitrogenous basis. Fish averaged 72 g at stocking and were held in mesocosm ponds over 63 days. Apparent digestibility of crude protein in insect-meal-based extruded diets ranged from 85.7% at 10% inclusion to 82.1% at 30% inclusion, values comparable to fishmeal-based extruded diets (86.4%). Specific growth rate declined marginally at 30% inclusion (1.51 vs. 1.59% per day at 0%). Fat content of whole-body increased at higher insect meal inclusion levels, consistent with the higher lipid content of insect meal. Feed conversion ratios were acceptable across all inclusion levels (1.82–2.03). Chitin content of dietary treatments was quantified and showed a moderate negative correlation with dry matter ADC. Results indicate that insect meal at up to 20% can replace fishmeal in extruded carp diets without meaningful production loss.

title: Pellet durability and water stability as predictors of nutrient leaching and apparent digestibility in carp and catfish feeds
abstract: Physical quality parameters of 14 commercial and experimental feeds (eight extruded, six pelleted) were evaluated using the Tumbling Can method for pellet durability index (PDI) and a 30-minute water immersion test for water stability index (WSI). Leachate samples from the water stability test were analysed for dry matter, crude protein, and total phosphorus. PDI ranged from 87.3% to 99.1% across feed types. Extruded feeds showed higher WSI (mean 88.4%) than pelleted feeds (mean 71.6%). Correlation analysis across 126 fish-feed combinations (carp and catfish fed each diet in tank trials) showed that WSI was a significant predictor of in vivo dry matter ADC (r = 0.63, p < 0.01) and crude protein ADC (r = 0.59, p < 0.01). PDI was a weaker predictor. Phosphorus leaching losses at low WSI were substantial (up to 18.4% of total phosphorus content per 30 minutes), reinforcing the relevance of feed form for environmental management. The results support adoption of WSI as a routine quality criterion in feed procurement specifications.

title: Digestibility and body composition responses of European catfish to graded dietary lipid levels in extruded versus pelleted diets at two rearing temperatures
abstract: European catfish (mean 95 g) were assigned to a 2 × 2 × 3 factorial design crossing feed form (extruded, pelleted), rearing temperature (22°C, 28°C), and dietary lipid level (8, 14, 20% crude fat) in recirculating aquaculture system tanks over 56 days. Ether extract ADC was highest in extruded feeds at 28°C and 14% inclusion (93.8%), and lowest in pelleted feeds at 22°C and 20% inclusion (79.4%). A significant three-way interaction (p < 0.05) indicated that the advantage of extrusion over pelleting was most pronounced at lower temperature and high lipid inclusion. Whole-body fat content increased linearly with dietary lipid level regardless of feed form, but the slope was steeper in extruded-fed fish, reflecting higher lipid digestibility. Specific growth rate peaked at 14% dietary lipid for both feed forms and temperatures. Liver lipid content did not exceed 11% in any treatment, suggesting no pathological lipid accumulation. Practical implications for catfish diets formulated for spring and autumn rearing conditions are discussed.

title: In vitro digestibility screening methods for aquafeeds: a calibration against in vivo ADC data from carp and catfish pond trials
abstract: Rapid in vitro digestibility assays were calibrated against an existing database of in vivo apparent digestibility coefficients accumulated over ten years of pond and tank trials with common carp and European catfish. Three in vitro methods were compared: two-step pepsin–pancreatin digestion, pH-stat titration, and a multi-enzyme cocktail assay. The database comprised 214 individual feed-species-temperature observations for crude protein ADC and 187 for dry matter ADC. Pearson correlations between in vitro and in vivo crude protein digestibility ranged from r = 0.71 (two-step method) to r = 0.84 (pH-stat). Predictive accuracy was higher for extruded feeds than for pelleted feeds across all three methods, possibly due to greater homogeneity of the extrudate matrix. Temperature at which in vivo trials were conducted moderated predictive accuracy: correlations dropped by 0.07–0.12 units for trials conducted below 20°C. The pH-stat method is recommended as a screening tool for ingredient evaluation prior to in vivo validation, with species-specific correction factors provided.

title: Dissident Interfaces: Net.Art Collectives and Anti-Institutional Practice in Post-Yugoslav Online Spaces, 1995–2001
abstract: This article examines three net.art collectives operating in the former Yugoslav republics between 1995 and 2001, focusing on their deployment of browser-based interventions and mock-institutional websites as critique of both state cultural bureaucracies and emergent commercial web design. Drawing on fourteen semi-structured interviews with surviving collective members, archived HTML files recovered from Wayback Machine snapshots, and correspondence held at the Museum of Contemporary Art Vojvodina, the study reconstructs the technical and conceptual decisions behind these works. Analysis applies Hakim Bey's concept of temporary autonomous zones alongside Chantal Mouffe's agonistic pluralism to interpret how the collectives simultaneously mimicked and subverted institutional aesthetics. The article argues that these practices constituted a regionally specific variation of tactical media that differed from Western European counterparts in its explicit engagement with post-war informational precarity and limited bandwidth infrastructure. Findings challenge accounts that treat Eastern European net.art as derivative of Western models.

title: Server Autonomy as Political Act: The Case of the Novi Sad Free Networks Initiative, 1999–2004
abstract: This case study investigates the Novi Sad Free Networks Initiative (NSFNI), an informal collective that maintained an autonomous server during and after the NATO bombing campaign of 1999, distributing independent news and hosting artistic projects censored by state broadcasters. Using server logs donated by former members, contemporaneous print journalism from Vojvodina regional newspapers, and oral history interviews with eight participants, the paper reconstructs the technical architecture and editorial decisions of the initiative. The analysis draws on Critical Infrastructure Studies and Geert Lovink's writings on tactical media to situate NSFNI within broader European autonomous media networks of the period. The study documents that the server hosted forty-three distinct art and activist projects over its operational life and that its physical location changed six times due to institutional pressure. The paper contributes a granular local case to historiographies of autonomous networking that have concentrated on Western European and North American examples.

title: Culture Jamming Between East and West: Comparing Détournement Practices in Hungarian and Serbian Net.Art, 2000–2008
abstract: This comparative study examines culture jamming and détournement as practiced by net.art communities in Hungary and Serbia across 2000–2008, periods that coincide in both countries with significant institutional restructuring of cultural funding. The article draws on a corpus of eighty-seven documented online artworks gathered from national media art archives, institutional acquisition records, and artist-maintained repositories. A close-reading methodology informed by Situationist theory and Brian Holmes's writings on artistic research is applied to works involving corporate logo manipulation, fake governmental portals, and hijacked advertising formats. The study identifies fourteen recurring visual and procedural strategies and maps their distribution across the two national contexts. The results indicate considerable formal overlap but divergent political targets: Hungarian works addressed European Union accession discourse, while Serbian works more frequently targeted domestic media monopolies. The article argues that regional comparison reveals how a shared tactical vocabulary acquired locally differentiated critical purposes.

title: Preserving the Unmaintainable: Methodological Challenges in Archiving Browser-Dependent Net.Art
abstract: This methodological article addresses the practical and theoretical problems that arise when attempting to archive interactive net.art works dependent on deprecated browser plugins, Java applets, and early Flash implementations. The paper reports on a two-year archiving project conducted at the Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad, during which the Media Tactics Research Group documented thirty-one works from Vojvodina-based artists created between 1997 and 2005. Three archival strategies were tested: static screenshot documentation, emulation via browser virtualisation environments, and artist-assisted recreation. Each strategy is evaluated against criteria of fidelity, accessibility, and sustainability. Results show that emulation preserved interactive behaviour in twenty-two of thirty-one cases but introduced anachronistic rendering artefacts that altered aesthetic experience. Artist-assisted recreation raised authorship questions that the group resolved through a co-authorship protocol now offered to other institutions. The article proposes a decision matrix for selecting archival strategies based on artwork type and available metadata.

title: Fake Institutions and Real Critique: Mock Museums in Central European Net.Art
abstract: This article analyses a cluster of mock-institutional websites created by artists in Poland, Czech Republic, Slovenia, and Serbia between 2001 and 2012 that simulate the online presence of fictitious cultural institutions. Eleven works are examined in depth through iconographic analysis, source code reading, and interviews with seven artists. The study identifies a consistent formal grammar: official typography, bureaucratic navigation structures, and deadpan exhibition text, deployed to expose the aestheticisation of institutional authority. The article situates these works in relation to canonical institutional critique by Michael Asher and Andrea Fraser while arguing that the Central European examples add a specifically post-socialist irony toward state cultural legitimacy. Quantitative content analysis of eighty-nine user comments archived from three of the works demonstrates that audiences frequently failed to identify the works as art during initial encounters, a misreading the artists often deliberately cultivated. This ambiguity is read as a structural feature, not a failure of communication.

title: Between Bandwidth and Barricades: Infrastructure Constraints and Aesthetic Form in Balkan Net.Art
abstract: This paper argues that material constraints of internet infrastructure in the Western Balkans during the late 1990s and 2000s—low bandwidth, unreliable connectivity, high access costs—shaped aesthetic choices in net.art produced in the region in ways that remain undertheorised. The study correlates technical infrastructure data drawn from ITU reports and national telecommunications authority archives with formal properties of 104 documented net artworks from Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and North Macedonia. Statistical analysis using logistic regression identifies significant associations between bandwidth availability by year and the prevalence of text-heavy or low-resolution image works. Qualitative close-reading of selected works then interprets these formal features as both pragmatic adaptation and deliberate aesthetic position, drawing on Wolfgang Ernst's media archaeology and Susan Buck-Morss's writing on peripheral modernisms. The paper contributes an infrastructural materialism to net.art historiography.

title: Net.Art in the Age of Social Platforms: Continuity and Rupture in Post-2010 Eastern European Practice
abstract: This article maps the relationship between the net.art practices that emerged in the 1990s and those of artists working on or against commercial social platforms after 2010 in Eastern Europe. It poses the question of whether platform-based art activism constitutes an extension of tactical media logic or a qualitatively different phenomenon shaped by algorithmic governance, data commodification, and platform terms of service. The article analyses twenty-two projects documented through artist statements, screen-capture archives, and press coverage, selected from artists based in Serbia, Romania, Croatia, and Slovakia. Drawing on Tiziana Terranova's concept of free labour and Ulises Mejias and Nick Couldry's data colonialism framework, the article identifies three modes of engagement: mimicry of platform aesthetics, systematic violation of community guidelines as performance, and platform refusal combined with mirror hosting. The conclusion argues that tactical media's emphasis on temporality has been radicalised by platform volatility, making the ephemeral even less controllable than the early practitioners anticipated.

title: Cataloguing the Uncatalogued: Towards a Regional Database of Central and Eastern European Net.Art, 1993–2010
abstract: This conference paper presents the design rationale and preliminary results of a multi-institutional effort to construct a shared database of net.art works produced in Central and Eastern Europe between 1993 and 2010. Eighteen institutions from nine countries participated in the first data-gathering phase, contributing records for 634 distinct works. The paper describes the metadata schema developed for the database, which extends Dublin Core with fields specific to browser-dependent interactive works, and discusses the negotiation required to reconcile divergent national cataloguing conventions. It reports on data quality audits conducted on the first 634 records, finding that complete technical metadata was available for only 31% of entries. The paper reflects on the political economy of cultural memory work: which works were institutionally acquired and thus documented, and which remained in informal circulation. A public-facing beta version of the database is described, along with a community annotation interface.

title: Tactical Media and the Infrastructures of Solidarity: Cross-Border Art Activism Between Serbia and Hungary, 2015–2022
abstract: This article examines collaborative tactical media projects undertaken by artists and collectives working across the Serbian-Hungarian border during the refugee crisis of 2015 and its aftermath through 2022. It focuses on four projects that used combinations of live-streaming, counter-mapping, and social media intervention to document and contest border enforcement practices. Research methods include participatory observation at two project events, analysis of project documentation held by the participating groups, and twenty-one semi-structured interviews with artists, activists, and participants. The article applies Doreen Massey's relational geography and Nicole Phelps's recent work on border aesthetics to argue that these projects produced a form of tactical solidarity that was geographically specific but deliberately designed for cross-border circulation. It also discusses how state pressure on civil society organisations in both countries constrained the projects' institutional affiliations and public communication strategies.

title: From Mailing Lists to Encrypted Channels: Communication Infrastructure in Eastern European Art Activism Across Three Decades
abstract: This historical overview traces how Eastern European art activist networks shifted their communication infrastructure from mailing lists and web forums in the 1990s to encrypted messaging platforms and decentralised federated networks in the 2020s, examining what changed and what remained continuous in practice. The study is based on archival analysis of three mailing list archives totalling approximately 47,000 messages, interviews with twenty-six practitioners active across multiple periods, and comparative analysis of current platform choices documented through a survey of forty-one active groups in eight countries. The article tracks shifts in the rhetoric of security, anonymity, and collective authorship across these communication contexts and argues that while the technical substrate changed dramatically, a consistent concern with infrastructure autonomy links practitioners across generations. It also identifies new tensions introduced by the usability demands of encrypted tools and the partial commodification of privacy-oriented platforms.

title: Net.Art After Net.Art: Retrospective Exhibitions and the Problem of Institutional Assimilation
abstract: This article critically examines a wave of retrospective exhibitions of 1990s net.art held in European institutions between 2018 and 2025, asking how the process of museum display transforms works that were constitutively anti-institutional and browser-dependent. Five exhibitions are examined in depth, including two held at institutions in the region: the retrospective at the Museum of Contemporary Art Vojvodina in 2022 and a touring exhibition organised from Vienna in 2023–2024. Methods include curatorial document analysis, exhibition reviews, and interviews with eight curators and twelve artists whose works were included. The article identifies three modes of institutional accommodation: the works are displayed as historical documents, as interactive reconstructions, or as conceptual scripts authorising new realisations. It argues that each mode entails a different theory of what a net.art work is, and that these theories are rarely made explicit by exhibiting institutions. The article closes with reflections on what a critically self-aware retrospective practice might look like.

title: Icon Comprehension Across Age Groups in a Municipal e-Services Portal: A Think-Aloud Study
abstract: Icon-based navigation is standard in public-sector web portals, yet comprehension rates among older adults or users with limited web experience are rarely measured during procurement. This study applied think-aloud protocol and post-task icon-labelling tasks with 60 participants stratified into three age brackets (18–35, 36–55, 56–72) recruited via community centres in Novi Sad. The portal under examination was a fictional prototype modelled on the structure of a typical Serbian municipal e-services site. Overall icon comprehension rate was 74 percent, with the 56–72 group achieving 58 percent compared to 84 percent in the youngest group. Metaphor transparency—whether the depicted object is culturally familiar—was the strongest predictor of comprehension (β = 0.51, p < 0.001). Abstract icons representing bureaucratic procedures (permit renewal, tax filing) showed the lowest comprehension across all groups. The study provides a ranked list of 22 icon types by comprehension and proposes a supplementary label requirement for icons below a 70 percent threshold.

title: Evaluating Tree Map vs. Force-Directed Graph Layouts for Displaying Patent Citation Networks to Technology Transfer Professionals
abstract: Technology transfer offices must help researchers and industry partners interpret patent citation landscapes without specialist bibliometric training. This study compared tree map and force-directed graph visualisations of the same citation dataset (1,240 patents in three technical domains) in a between-subjects study with 36 technology transfer professionals from Serbian and Croatian universities. Participants performed cluster identification, gap-spotting, and trend-reading tasks. Tree map users completed cluster identification tasks 18 percent faster; force-directed graph users performed better on gap-spotting tasks where spatial proximity conveyed citation distance (accuracy 67 percent vs. 51 percent). No significant difference appeared on trend-reading tasks. Post-task questionnaire responses indicated strong individual variation in visualisation preference correlated with self-reported prior exposure to network graphs. The results support offering both layout options rather than a single default and suggest that brief onboarding tutorials differentially benefit force-directed graph novices.

title: Spatial Metaphor in Data Dashboards: How Layout Grammar Affects Inference in Non-Expert Agricultural Advisors
abstract: Agricultural extension advisors in rural Serbia rely on digital dashboards provided by regional development agencies to communicate soil-health and yield-forecast data to farmers. Many advisors have formal agricultural education but limited experience with abstract data graphics. Through semi-structured contextual inquiry at six regional offices and a follow-up card-sorting study with 22 advisors, this research examined which spatial metaphors—geographic maps, bar charts, radial layouts, and tabular grids—were most intuitively mapped to specific inferential tasks (comparison, trend detection, anomaly spotting, and regional aggregation). Geographic map layouts were strongly preferred and more accurately used for regional aggregation regardless of whether spatial distribution was actually the most relevant dimension. Radial layouts produced the highest error rates across all task types. The paper proposes a task-metaphor alignment matrix for dashboard designers in agricultural and rural-development contexts and reports inter-rater reliability for a proposed annotation scheme (κ = 0.74).

title: Vinegar Syndrome Progression in Yugoslav Acetate Prints: A Longitudinal Assessment of 1960s Feature Film Collections
abstract: This study examines the rate of acetic acid off-gassing in a sample of 214 acetate film prints produced in Yugoslav studios between 1958 and 1972, held across three regional archives in Serbia and Slovenia. Prints were subjected to A-D strip testing at twelve-month intervals over a five-year period and cross-referenced with storage temperature and humidity records. Results indicate that approximately 38 percent of the sampled reels had progressed beyond A-D level 2 by the end of the observation window, with prints stored above 18°C showing statistically significant acceleration in decomposition rate. Shrinkage measurements obtained using a modified Kodak shrinkage gauge ranged from 0.4 to 1.1 percent across the degraded subset. The paper proposes a triage protocol that prioritises digitisation based on combined shrinkage and pH thresholds rather than production date alone, offering a practical framework for archives with limited scanning capacity.

title: Grid Erosion: How Photocomposition and Early Desktop Publishing Changed Letter Spacing in Serbian Newspaper Mastheads, 1978–1998
abstract: The shift from hot-metal composition to photocomposition and then to desktop publishing software brought measurable changes to the typography of Serbian newspaper mastheads that have not been systematically studied. This paper uses 412 masthead specimens collected from the library holdings of the Matica srpska and the archives of three regional newspapers to track changes in letter spacing, weight, and x-height in Cyrillic display settings across three distinct technological periods: 1978–1985 (late hot-metal and early phototype), 1986–1991 (dominant phototypesetting), and 1992–1998 (desktop publishing). Optical character recognition was adapted to measure inter-letter gaps in scanned specimens, with manual correction. The analysis shows that mean letter spacing in Cyrillic mastheads widened by an average of 18 percent between the first and third periods, a change associated with the default tracking values of early desktop publishing software rather than editorial decisions. The paper contributes to the broader history of how software defaults shape typographic culture.

title: Effect of Decoupling Capacitor Placement on Power-Bus Noise in a Four-Layer Mixed-Signal PCB
abstract: Power delivery network (PDN) impedance management in mixed-signal boards is examined through a combined measurement and simulation campaign. A test vehicle carrying an FPGA and two 12-bit ADC devices was designed with three decoupling capacitor placement strategies: bulk capacitors only, distributed 100 nF ceramic capacitors at 5 mm spacing, and a co-planar interdigitated capacitance structure formed by alternating power and ground copper pours. PDN impedance was measured from 100 kHz to 1 GHz using a one-port shunt method with a vector network analyser. Simultaneously, conducted noise on the 3.3 V rail was recorded with a 1 GHz oscilloscope probe during switching activity driven by a test pattern generator. The distributed ceramic strategy reduced peak PDN impedance from 840 mΩ to 210 mΩ at 480 MHz. Radiated emissions pre-compliance scans at 3 m confirmed a corresponding 4.8 dB reduction in broadband noise floor between 400 and 600 MHz. A compact circuit model of the PDN, fitted to measurement data, reproduces impedance to within 8% across the full bandwidth.

title: Pre-Compliance Near-Field Scanning as a Substitute for Preliminary Open-Area Test Site Measurements: Correlation Study on Consumer Electronics Enclosures
abstract: This paper investigates whether automated near-field scan data acquired at 3 mm standoff can reliably predict far-field radiated emission rankings before a product undergoes formal OATS testing. Seven commercial-grade consumer electronics boards were scanned on a 150 mm × 150 mm grid with 2 mm step resolution at frequencies from 30 MHz to 1 GHz. Far-field transformation was applied using a planar near-to-far-field algorithm. Results were compared against 3 m OATS measurements performed at an accredited external laboratory. Rank-ordering agreement between pre-compliance near-field predictions and OATS results was 85% at the frequency of maximum emission for each board. Absolute amplitude agreement was within ±4.5 dB in 74% of cases, degrading to ±9 dB at frequencies above 700 MHz where enclosure resonances are significant. The findings suggest the methodology is reliable for early design triage but not as a substitute for final certification. Practical recommendations for scan grid density and probe calibration are provided.

title: Frequency-Domain Characterisation of Intra-Board Power Supply Noise Coupling Through Shared Voltage Regulators in FPGA-Based Measurement Instruments
abstract: In FPGA-based instruments, multiple voltage domains are frequently derived from a single synchronous buck converter, and the resulting switching ripple can couple between domains through regulator output impedance. This paper characterises coupling using two-port frequency-domain measurements on a purpose-built test board hosting a single DC–DC controller powering three regulated rails: 1.0 V core, 1.8 V I/O, and 3.3 V auxiliary. Transfer impedance between rails was measured from 100 kHz to 500 MHz. A noise injection port was implemented as a calibrated current source realised with a transformer-coupled MOSFET stage. Results show that coupling from the 1.0 V rail to the 3.3 V rail peaks at 47 dBΩ near the converter switching frequency (400 kHz) and at a second peak near 85 MHz associated with a shared bulk capacitor resonance. Adding a series ferrite bead on the 1.8 V branch reduced the secondary resonance peak by 14 dB. The measurements were reproduced by a lumped circuit model with mean error below 1.5 dB from 100 kHz to 200 MHz.

title: A Probabilistic Framework for Minimum Protective Distance Estimation in Human-Robot Shared Workspaces
abstract: This paper addresses the estimation of minimum protective distances between human operators and collaborative robots under dynamic operating conditions. A probabilistic occupancy model was constructed using data from 14 healthy adult participants performing standardised pick-and-place tasks alongside a six-axis cobot in a laboratory cell. Human body segments were tracked using a stereo time-of-flight camera at 30 Hz, and a Kalman-filter-based predictor was applied to forecast limb positions over a 200 ms horizon. Protective distances were derived following the kinematic model prescribed in ISO/TS 15066 Annex A, with uncertainty margins computed from the 95th-percentile prediction error across all participants. Results showed that the proposed predictor reduced required separation distance by approximately 18% compared to worst-case static models, while maintaining zero unsafe contacts across all 2 800 task repetitions. The framework was validated on three cobot configurations differing in payload and maximum joint speed.

title: Experimental Evaluation of Time-of-Flight Sensors for Human Limb Detection in Industrial Robot Cells
abstract: Reliable detection of human body parts is a prerequisite for safe dynamic speed-and-separation monitoring. This study benchmarks four commercially available time-of-flight depth sensors under conditions representative of a light-assembly manufacturing cell, including variable ambient lighting, specular metal surfaces, and partial occlusion by tooling fixtures. Each sensor was tested on a calibrated grid at distances between 0.4 m and 3.2 m, and detection latency, depth noise, and missed-detection rate were measured using a robotic arm sweeping a foam limb proxy at speeds between 0.1 and 1.5 m/s. The Mesa SR4000 equivalent configuration produced the lowest missed-detection rate at 0.3% for speeds below 0.8 m/s, rising to 2.1% at 1.5 m/s. Practical installation recommendations regarding sensor placement angles and inter-sensor spacing to minimise blind zones are derived from the experimental data and expressed as concrete geometric constraints for cell designers.

title: Real-Time Speed Scaling of a Collaborative Manipulator Based on Measured Human-Robot Separation Distance
abstract: Speed-and-separation monitoring requires that robot velocity be continuously adjusted to the instantaneous distance between the nearest human body part and any moving robot component. This work implements a closed-loop speed-scaling controller on a six-axis collaborative arm with a 5 kg payload, using a depth-image pipeline running at 25 Hz on an embedded GPU board. The controller maps measured separation distance to a scalar velocity limit applied multiplicatively to all joint velocity references. Experiments with five experienced operators performing co-manipulation tasks over 120-minute sessions demonstrated that the robot completed the target cycle in a mean time of 38.4 s, compared to 29.1 s under full-speed operation, representing a 32% cycle-time penalty attributable to human proximity. No unexpected stops were triggered in 3 600 cycles. The paper also analyses latency contributions from sensor acquisition, segmentation, and command transmission, totalling 67 ms end-to-end.

title: Mapping ISO/TS 15066 Compliance Requirements to Formal Verification Conditions for Cobot Control Software
abstract: ISO/TS 15066 specifies requirements for collaborative robot systems but does so in natural language, making automated compliance checking difficult. This paper proposes a methodology for translating a subset of those requirements—specifically the speed-and-separation monitoring and power-and-force limiting subclauses—into formal temporal logic specifications that can be model-checked against a software implementation. The control logic of a commercially available collaborative arm was modelled as a timed automaton in UPPAAL, and nineteen compliance conditions were expressed as TCTL properties. The model checker verified all nineteen conditions in under 40 seconds on a standard workstation, and two latent timing violations were identified that had not been detected during manual review. The paper discusses the limits of the approach, particularly the difficulty of modelling continuous sensor noise in discrete symbolic models, and proposes abstraction strategies to manage this gap.
venue: Safety Science

title: Influence of Operator Fatigue on Trajectory Predictability in Human-Robot Collaborative Assembly
abstract: Dynamic separation monitoring relies on predictions of human motion; prediction accuracy may degrade when operators are fatigued. This study recruited 22 assembly workers from a partner manufacturing facility and measured wrist and elbow trajectories using an inertial measurement unit suit during four-hour shifts with a collaborative robot assisting on a simulated engine-component assembly task. Fatigue was indexed using perceived exertion ratings and electromyographic amplitude. Trajectory variability, measured as standard deviation of hand position at 100 ms and 300 ms prediction horizons, increased by 23% and 41% respectively in the final hour compared to the first hour. The paper models this variability increase as a time-dependent inflation of the safety distance margin and proposes a shift-duration-aware parameter to be included in speed-and-separation monitoring controllers, with numerical guidelines for four task types.
venue: Human Factors and Ergonomics in Manufacturing

title: Sensor Fusion Architecture for Simultaneous Occupancy and Velocity Estimation in a Shared Robot Workspace
abstract: Accurate estimation of human limb velocity, not only position, is required to compute compliant robot speed limits under ISO/TS 15066 Annex A. This paper describes a sensor fusion system combining a time-of-flight depth camera and a 2D lidar scanner mounted at orthogonal angles in a ceiling-floor arrangement above a 2 m × 2 m collaborative workspace. An unscented Kalman filter fuses the two data streams, providing 3D position and velocity estimates for up to three tracked body segments at 20 Hz with a measured RMS velocity error of 0.04 m/s at human walking speed. Comparative tests against a Vicon optical motion capture reference system across 800 motion sequences showed 91% agreement in worst-case velocity classification into the four ISO/TS 15066 speed bands. A prototype fusion board consuming 18 W was implemented on a Xilinx Zynq SoC.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics

title: Safety Region Decomposition for Multi-Cobot Cells with Overlapping Workspaces
abstract: When two or more collaborative robots share overlapping reachable workspaces alongside human operators, the standard single-robot speed-and-separation monitoring framework must be extended to account for robot-robot proximity as well as human-robot proximity. This paper formalises a safety region decomposition approach in which the shared workspace is partitioned into convex sub-regions at runtime using a Voronoi-based algorithm seeded by current end-effector positions. Within each sub-region, an independent speed-and-separation controller governs the corresponding cobot. Experiments on a two-cobot testbed performing interleaved pick-and-place tasks showed that the decomposition algorithm executes in under 3 ms per cycle on a standard industrial PC, and that cycle-time efficiency was 6% higher than a conservative joint-slowdown baseline, with safety compliance maintained across 10 000 consecutive cycles.

title: A Software Tool for Offline ISO/TS 15066 Compliance Auditing of Recorded Cobot Operation Logs
abstract: Manufacturing quality systems increasingly require documented evidence that cobot deployments were operated in conformance with ISO/TS 15066 during specific production periods. This paper describes CobotAudit, a desktop software tool that ingests timestamped logs of robot joint states, end-effector poses, and sensor-derived human position estimates, and retrospectively evaluates whether speed-and-separation monitoring constraints were respected at each logged timestep. The tool implements the kinematic distance model from ISO/TS 15066 Annex A and produces a PDF compliance report itemising any violations with duration, severity, and context. Tested on logs from three industrial deployments totalling 280 hours of operation, CobotAudit processed one hour of log data in approximately 4 minutes on a mid-range laptop. Across the three deployments, 14 minor and two moderate constraint violations were identified that had not been flagged by the onboard safety controller.

title: Human-Robot Collaboration Safety
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of the safety engineering methods applicable to collaborative robot deployments in industrial settings. It covers the evolution from traditional safeguarded-space approaches to collaborative operation modes as codified in ISO 10218 and ISO/TS 15066, with particular emphasis on speed-and-separation monitoring and power-and-force limiting. Analytical methods for computing protective distances and maximum allowable speeds are presented with worked numerical examples for six representative cobot configurations. The chapter also addresses the practical challenges of sensor selection, calibration, and failure-mode analysis for occupancy-detection systems, and closes with a summary of open research problems including multi-robot workspace sharing and adaptive safety parameters for fatigued operators. Intended for graduate students and practising engineers entering collaborative robotics deployment roles.
venue: Handbook of Industrial Robotics Safety, edited volume, Springer

title: Effect of Depth Camera Frame Rate on Minimum Protective Distance Estimation Error Under ISO/TS 15066
abstract: The ISO/TS 15066 kinematic model for minimum protective distance includes a reaction-time term that depends on sensor latency. As depth cameras are available at frame rates ranging from 15 Hz to 90 Hz, understanding the relationship between frame rate and distance-estimation error is practically important for system specification. This paper derives an analytical expression for the additional uncertainty introduced by discretised sampling and validates it against Monte Carlo simulations of human arm motion using motion-capture trajectories from 30 participants. At 15 Hz the additional protective distance margin was 84 mm at the 99th percentile, declining to 21 mm at 60 Hz with no further significant reduction beyond that rate. The results suggest that specifying sensors above 60 Hz provides diminishing safety returns under the current standard's model assumptions, while reducing system cost and computational load.

title: Runtime Monitoring of ISO/TS 15066 Constraints Using a Dedicated Safety Co-processor
abstract: Integrating compliance verification directly into the cobot control loop, rather than performing it offline, would allow protective actions to be triggered when constraints are about to be violated rather than after the fact. This paper presents a hardware-software architecture in which a dedicated ARM Cortex-M7 co-processor monitors six ISO/TS 15066 speed-and-separation constraints in parallel, running at 1 kHz independently of the main robot controller. The co-processor receives pre-processed human-position data from a fusion module and robot state data from the controller EtherCAT bus, evaluates all constraints, and asserts a safety-rated digital output with a worst-case latency of 0.8 ms. A performance-in-degraded-mode analysis shows that the monitor remains correct under single sensor failure. The architecture was integrated into the laboratory testbed and tested over 50 hours of continuous operation without spurious trips.

title: Quantifying the Productivity Cost of ISO/TS 15066 Speed-and-Separation Monitoring in Five Industrial Assembly Scenarios
abstract: Adopting speed-and-separation monitoring in a cobot cell is expected to reduce cycle speed relative to fully automated operation, but the magnitude of this reduction depends on task structure, workspace geometry, and human dwell patterns. This study measured cycle-time data across five assembly scenarios at two partner manufacturing sites in Vojvodina, covering electronics sub-assembly, automotive cable routing, pump valve assembly, light-fixture wiring, and medical-device inspection assistance. For each scenario, the cobot was operated first at maximum programmed speed with operators standing clear, then under active speed-and-separation monitoring with operators working at their natural pace. Mean cycle-time increase ranged from 11% (medical-device inspection) to 47% (automotive cable routing), with the variation explained primarily by the fraction of cycle time during which the operator was within 0.8 m of the robot end-effector. The data support task-level redesign guidelines aimed at minimising proximity overlap.

title: Intraoperative neuromonitoring of the recurrent laryngeal nerve during thyroidectomy: initial single-centre experience
abstract: This prospective observational study reports the introduction of intermittent intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) for the recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) at a single tertiary surgical centre in northern Serbia. Over a 24-month period, 118 patients undergoing total or hemithyroidectomy were enrolled. Electromyographic signals were recorded using surface electrodes integrated into the endotracheal tube. RLN was identified by stimulation at 1 mA prior to and after dissection. Postoperative laryngoscopy was performed in all patients at 48 hours and at six weeks. Transient RLN palsy was observed in 4 of 118 patients (3.4%); no permanent palsy was recorded. Signal loss was detected intraoperatively in 6 cases, of which 4 corresponded to postoperative voice change. Sensitivity of IONM for predicting postoperative palsy was 75% and specificity was 96.8%. The study establishes baseline IONM performance data for this centre and identifies operator learning curve as a contributing factor to early signal artefacts.

title: Факторы ризика повреде рекурентног ларингеалног живца код реоперација штитне жлезде: ретроспективна анализа
abstract: Ретроспективна студија анализирала је ризик-факторе повреде рекурентног ларингеалног живца (РЛЖ) код 64 пацијента подвргнутих реоперацији штитне жлезде у Клиничком центру Војводине у периоду 2008–2013. Примарне операције укључивале су хемитиреоидектомију (41 случај) и тоталну тиреоидектомију (23 случаја). Интраоперативни неуромониторинг примењен је у свих 64 пацијента. Анализирани су: претходна хируршка техника, патолошка дијагноза, искуство хирурга и интраоперативни EMG налаз. Пролазна парализа РЛЖ забележена је у 9,4% случајева (6/64), а трајна у 3,1% (2/64). Вишеструка логистичка регресија показала је да је претходна радикална хируршка дисекција најзначајнији предиктор повреде (OR 4,8; 95% CI 1,3–17,6). Налаз потврђује вредност IONM у контексту ревизијске хирургије и указује на потребу стандардизације протокола за реоперације.

title: Comparison of intermittent and continuous intraoperative neuromonitoring for recurrent laryngeal nerve preservation in total thyroidectomy
abstract: This prospective randomised study compared intermittent (I-IONM) and continuous intraoperative neuromonitoring (C-IONM) in 160 patients undergoing total thyroidectomy for multinodular goitre or differentiated thyroid carcinoma. Patients were allocated 1:1 to I-IONM (n=80) or C-IONM (n=80). C-IONM was performed using a vagal nerve stimulation cuff electrode with automated EMG sampling every 5 seconds. Primary endpoint was postoperative RLN function assessed by flexible laryngoscopy at 72 hours and 3 months. Transient palsy occurred in 3 patients in the C-IONM group and 7 in the I-IONM group (3.75% vs 8.75%; p=0.18). C-IONM detected 5 imminent injury signals enabling corrective surgical manoeuvres, all followed by signal recovery. No statistically significant difference in final palsy rate was demonstrated, likely due to sample size. The study provides effect size estimates suitable for planning a larger multicentre trial.

title: Laryngeal electromyography in the assessment of RLN recovery after intraoperative injury: a prospective follow-up study
abstract: Twenty-two patients who sustained electromyographically confirmed intraoperative RLN injury during thyroid surgery were followed prospectively for 12 months using serial laryngeal electromyography (LEMG) and flexible laryngoscopy. LEMG was performed at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months postoperatively. At baseline, all patients had absent or markedly reduced EMG amplitude at the vocalis muscle. By 12 months, 17 patients (77.3%) had regained normal or near-normal vocal cord mobility confirmed by laryngoscopy. LEMG findings at 6 weeks, specifically the presence of nascent motor unit potentials, correctly predicted full recovery in 14 of 17 cases (sensitivity 82.4%). Three patients with persistent paralysis showed fibrillation potentials and absence of voluntary recruitment at all time points. The data support early LEMG as a prognostic tool for counselling patients and planning voice rehabilitation interventions.

title: Intraoperative neuromonitoring findings in substernal goitre: a retrospective case series
abstract: Substernal goitre presents particular challenges for RLN identification due to displaced anatomy. We retrospectively reviewed IONM records and clinical outcomes for 38 patients who underwent thyroid surgery for substernal extension (Shin grade II or III) between 2013 and 2018. All procedures were performed via cervical approach; 3 required partial sternotomy. Mean operative time was 97 minutes (range 62–184). EMG stimulation was applied at the entry point into the thoracic inlet and at the cricothyroid junction. Baseline signal amplitude was significantly lower compared to a matched cohort of non-substernal cases (mean 412 µV vs 548 µV; p=0.04). Transient RLN palsy occurred in 4 patients (10.5%), and permanent injury in 1 (2.6%). Intraoperative signal loss preceded postoperative palsy in 4 of 5 affected cases. The series highlights anatomical variability as a source of reduced baseline amplitude and recommends contralateral vagal stimulation as a reference standard.

title: Effect of hypocalcaemia on intraoperative EMG signal quality during parathyroid surgery
abstract: Hypocalcaemia occurring during prolonged parathyroid operations may theoretically alter neuromuscular electromyographic signal quality and confound IONM interpretation. This prospective observational study enrolled 54 patients undergoing four-gland exploration for primary hyperparathyroidism. Serial intraoperative serum ionised calcium was measured at 30-minute intervals. EMG baseline amplitude and latency were recorded from the vocalis muscle at each time point. No patient developed symptomatic hypocalcaemia intraoperatively; minimum ionised calcium recorded was 0.92 mmol/L. No significant correlation was found between ionised calcium concentration and EMG amplitude (Pearson r = 0.11; p = 0.43) or latency (r = −0.07; p = 0.62). These findings suggest that, within the range of calcium values observed in standard parathyroid surgery, metabolic interference with RLN EMG monitoring is unlikely to be clinically relevant. The study provides reassurance for centres applying IONM during complex parathyroid re-explorations.

title: Patient-reported voice outcomes at one year following thyroidectomy with routine IONM: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: Objective laryngoscopic findings do not always correlate with patient experience of voice change following thyroid surgery. This cross-sectional survey assessed voice-related quality of life in 143 patients who had undergone total thyroidectomy with IONM between 2020 and 2022, at a median follow-up of 14 months. The Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10) was administered by telephone. Mean VHI-10 score was 6.2 (SD 7.8), indicating mild overall impact. Clinically significant voice handicap (VHI-10 ≥ 11) was reported by 23 patients (16.1%), of whom only 9 had an abnormal laryngoscopy finding on record. Multivariate analysis identified female sex (OR 2.4), preoperative dysphonia (OR 3.1), and diagnosis of thyroid carcinoma (OR 2.0) as independent predictors of significant VHI-10 score. Findings highlight a discordance between objective and subjective voice outcomes and support integration of patient-reported measures into routine post-thyroidectomy follow-up protocols.

title: Perfusion-guided vs. standard intraoperative decision-making in colorectal anastomosis: design of a multicentre randomised controlled trial (PERCO-RCT)
abstract: Anastomotic leak after colorectal resection affects 5–15% of patients and carries significant mortality. Whether systematic use of intraoperative perfusion assessment with ICG fluorescence angiography to guide the level of bowel transection reduces leak rates compared with standard surgeon judgement has not been evaluated in a properly powered randomised trial within the Balkan and Central European setting. This paper describes the rationale and protocol of PERCO-RCT, a multicentre open-label randomised controlled trial planned across five surgical units in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. Patients undergoing elective sigmoid or rectal resection with primary anastomosis are randomised 1:1 to perfusion-guided or standard arm. The primary outcome is grade B/C anastomotic leak within 30 days. Secondary outcomes include proximal resection margin revision rate, operative time, and 90-day major morbidity. The planned sample size is 340 patients per arm to detect a reduction in leak rate from 10% to 5.5% (80% power, α = 0.05). The protocol was registered and ethically approved at all participating sites before enrolment began.
venue: Trials in Digestive and Colorectal Surgery

title: Estimating Wright's Law Parameters from Sparse Early-Production Data in Contract Electronics Assembly
abstract: Reliable learning-rate estimation during the initial weeks of a new product introduction is difficult because production volumes are low and output quality is highly variable. This paper proposes a Bayesian updating procedure that incorporates prior distributions derived from historical ramp-up records of structurally similar products assembled at the same facility. The method was validated on a dataset of 14 distinct product introductions collected from a contract electronics assembler operating in the Vojvodina region over a five-year period. Each ramp-up sequence contained between 18 and 60 weekly cumulative unit observations. The Bayesian estimates converged to within 4 percentage points of the asymptotic ordinary-least-squares estimate after approximately six weeks of production, compared to eleven weeks required by the standard log-linear regression approach. Sensitivity analysis showed that prior width had a stronger effect on convergence speed than prior mean placement, suggesting that even loosely informed priors accelerate reliable estimation. The results provide a practical basis for production planners to set realistic delivery schedules and cost targets earlier in the ramp-up phase.

title: Cross-Product Knowledge Transfer Coefficients: A Regression-Based Approach Using Bill-of-Materials Similarity Metrics
abstract: When a manufacturer introduces a product that shares components, tooling, or assembly sequences with previously produced items, workers carry over some accumulated knowledge, which effectively shifts the starting point of the new product's learning curve. This study develops a method for quantifying that transferred knowledge by constructing a similarity index from bill-of-materials overlap, shared fixtures, and common supplier parts. Using production records from three contract manufacturers in Serbia and one in Hungary, covering 31 product transitions between 2017 and 2022, ordinary least squares regression was used to relate the similarity index to the observed effective first-unit cost reduction relative to a cold-start baseline. The resulting transfer coefficient ranged from 0.08 to 0.61 across the sample, with bill-of-materials component overlap explaining approximately 47 percent of the variance. The paper discusses how the coefficient can be inserted directly into the standard Wright's law formulation as an initial cumulative equivalent units adjustment, making it compatible with existing production planning tools without requiring software modification.

title: Comparing Plateau-Modified and Standard Log-Linear Learning Curves for High-Mix Low-Volume Assembly Environments
abstract: Standard Wright's law assumes that cumulative average unit cost declines indefinitely as a power function of cumulative output, but in high-mix low-volume contract manufacturing the workforce frequently switches between product types, limiting the depth of learning achievable before a product is discontinued. This paper tests whether a plateau-modified learning curve, which introduces an asymptotic cost floor parameter, fits ramp-up data better than the standard two-parameter model in such environments. A dataset of 22 product ramp-ups from a medical device sub-assembly contractor was used. Model comparison was performed using corrected Akaike information criterion. The plateau model produced a lower AICc in 16 of 22 cases, with the improvement being statistically meaningful in 11 cases based on a likelihood-ratio test at the 0.05 level. The estimated plateau was reached on average at 340 cumulative units, which in this factory corresponded to roughly eight to twelve weeks of production. The paper concludes that the plateau model is preferable when typical production runs are short, and provides a simple heuristic for practitioners to choose between the two formulations based on expected run length.

title: Data Requirements for Accurate Ramp-Up Forecasting: A Simulation Study Under Different Sampling Frequencies
abstract: Production planners rarely have the luxury of waiting for sufficient historical data before they must commit to cost and schedule targets. This simulation study examines how the frequency and timing of early production observations affect the accuracy of learning-rate estimates and downstream ramp-up duration forecasts. Synthetic ramp-up datasets were generated under Wright's law with learning rates uniformly drawn from the interval 0.72 to 0.92, representing the range commonly observed in light assembly manufacturing. Estimation was then performed using daily, weekly, and bi-weekly cumulative output snapshots, with the first observation available after 5, 10, or 20 units. Root mean squared error of the forecast total ramp-up duration to a target efficiency of 85 percent was used as the performance criterion across 2,000 simulation replications per scenario. Weekly sampling starting after 10 units was found to be a practical minimum for keeping forecast error below 15 percent of true ramp-up duration, a threshold considered acceptable by the production managers interviewed during the study design phase. Daily sampling beyond that point yielded diminishing accuracy improvements. The findings provide concrete guidance on data collection design for manufacturers preparing new product introduction procedures.
