title: Worst-Case Response Time Bounds for Fixed-Priority Tasks Sharing a Mutex on Dual-Core Microcontrollers
abstract: This paper derives closed-form worst-case response time (WCRT) bounds for sporadic task sets executing under fixed-priority preemptive scheduling on dual-core ARM Cortex-M3 microcontrollers when tasks share a single mutex-protected resource. The analysis extends the classic response-time recurrence by accounting for inter-core blocking intervals that arise from spin-wait implementations in the absence of an RTOS priority-ceiling protocol. A test suite of 240 synthetically generated task sets with utilisation ranging from 0.3 to 0.9 was constructed using the UUnifast-Discard algorithm. Computed bounds were compared against cycle-accurate simulation on an STM32F205 target. The analytical bounds overestimated measured WCRT by at most 8.2% across all schedulable sets. The paper identifies the conditions under which the overestimation collapses to zero and discusses the impact of cache-line contention on measured versus analytical gaps. The results suggest that the proposed extension is sufficiently tight for acceptance testing in small industrial controllers.

title: A Constraint Programming Model for Static Task-to-Core Assignment in Hard Real-Time Distributed Control Networks
abstract: Static assignment of periodic real-time tasks to processing nodes in a CAN-bus-connected distributed control network is formulated as a constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) over finite domains. The model encodes schedulability constraints per node using a sufficient utilisation bound, end-to-end deadline constraints along message chains, and memory footprint limits per node. A branch-and-bound solver augmented with arc-consistency propagation was implemented in MiniZinc 2.1. Benchmark instances were derived from three automotive-inspired control topologies with 4, 8, and 16 nodes and task counts ranging from 32 to 128. For the 4-node topology, optimal solutions were found in under 4 seconds on a standard workstation; for the 16-node topology, the solver found feasible solutions within a 60-second timeout in 91% of instances. The paper compares the CSP approach against a greedy first-fit decreasing heuristic; the CSP model reduced average processor utilisation imbalance by 14 percentage points.

title: Energy-Aware Scheduling of Aperiodic Tasks on Battery-Powered Embedded Controllers Using Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling
abstract: Aperiodic task scheduling under energy constraints is studied for a battery-powered ARM Cortex-M4 controller with four discrete voltage-frequency operating points. A modified earliest-deadline-first policy is combined with a look-ahead energy budget estimator that selects the lowest operating point guaranteeing deadline satisfaction for the current ready queue. A penalty function for missed deadlines is incorporated to allow graceful degradation when energy reserves fall below a configurable threshold. Experiments used a data-logging workload recorded from a flood-monitoring sensor node deployed on the Danube near Novi Sad, comprising 18 hours of real arrival traces. Compared to a static maximum-frequency baseline, the proposed scheduler reduced energy consumption by 31% while missing fewer than 0.3% of soft deadlines. A formal bound on the maximum deadline miss ratio under worst-case arrival bursts is derived and validated against the trace data.

title: Schedulability Analysis for Mixed-Criticality Task Sets on Single-Core Microcontrollers: A Survey and Classification
abstract: This book chapter surveys schedulability analysis techniques for mixed-criticality (MC) task sets running on single-core microcontrollers, covering the period 2007 to 2017. The chapter classifies existing approaches along four axes: the underlying scheduling algorithm (fixed-priority versus EDF variants), the criticality mode-switch trigger (utilisation-based versus budget-exhaustion), the type of WCET estimate used (safe versus measured), and the hardware platform assumptions (cache presence, memory bus contention). For each class, the chapter summarises key results, identifies assumptions that limit applicability to microcontroller-class hardware—particularly the absence of memory management units and restricted interrupt latency budgets—and tabulates the benchmark task sets used in original publications. The chapter concludes with a gap analysis identifying open problems in MC scheduling for constrained embedded controllers, including the interaction between interrupt service routines and high-criticality task budgets.

title: Integer Linear Programming Formulation for Message Scheduling over FlexRay Static Segments in Distributed Automotive Controllers
abstract: The assignment of periodic messages to slots in the static segment of a FlexRay bus is modelled as an integer linear programme (ILP). Decision variables encode slot and cycle-multiplexing assignments; constraints enforce slot capacity, bandwidth utilisation below 90%, and end-to-end latency requirements for signal chains derived from a brake-by-wire reference architecture. The ILP was solved with CPLEX 12.8 on instances with 20 to 80 messages and bus cycle lengths of 1 ms, 2 ms, and 5 ms. Optimal schedules were obtained for all instances with up to 40 messages within 30 seconds. For larger instances, a column-generation relaxation found solutions within 4% of the ILP lower bound. The paper reports sensitivity of slot utilisation to cycle-length selection and derives a rule of thumb for minimum slot count as a function of message count and period distribution.

title: Tight Utilisation Bounds for Non-Preemptive Fixed-Priority Scheduling on Memory-Constrained Microcontrollers
abstract: Non-preemptive fixed-priority scheduling is common on low-cost 8-bit and 16-bit microcontrollers where context-switch overhead and stack RAM are prohibitive. Existing schedulability tests for the non-preemptive case assume unbounded stack memory; this paper derives a utilisation bound that simultaneously respects a configurable maximum stack depth per task. The derivation uses a combinatorial argument over critical instants adjusted for blocking by the longest non-preemptive task. The resulting bound is a function of task count, period ratio, and per-task stack sizes. Experimental evaluation on an AVR ATmega2560 platform used 400 randomly generated task sets; the new bound correctly classified 97.3% of sets as schedulable or unschedulable, compared to 88.1% for the classic Liu-and-Layland bound applied without memory adjustment. The paper also reports a lightweight O(n log n) test procedure suitable for on-chip admission control.

title: Mapping Periodic Control Tasks onto Heterogeneous Sensor-Actuator Node Clusters Using Simulated Annealing
abstract: A heterogeneous cluster of sensor-actuator nodes—comprising three node types differing in processor speed, available RAM, and communication interface—is used as the target platform for distributing periodic control tasks in a water-treatment monitoring application. The mapping problem, which is NP-hard, is addressed with a simulated annealing (SA) metaheuristic. The objective function combines weighted processor utilisation imbalance, total inter-node communication volume, and a feasibility penalty for violated deadline constraints. Cooling schedule parameters were tuned using a Latin hypercube design-of-experiment on a set of 50 training instances; the final configuration used an initial temperature of 500, geometric cooling ratio 0.995, and 5000 inner-loop iterations per temperature step. On 100 test instances with 64 to 256 tasks, SA found solutions with total cost within 6.3% of a lower bound from LP relaxation. The paper compares SA against tabu search and a greedy list-scheduling baseline.

title: A Benchmark Suite for Constraint-Based Resource Allocation in Embedded Distributed Real-Time Systems
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of resource allocation algorithms for embedded distributed real-time systems is hampered by the absence of standardised benchmarks. This paper describes a benchmark suite comprising 600 problem instances generated according to a parameterised model that controls task period distribution, utilisation level, memory footprint distribution, network topology, and message deadline tightness. Instance parameters are calibrated against three real-world reference systems: a programmable logic controller for conveyor automation, a CAN-based engine management prototype, and a wireless sensor network for structural health monitoring. The suite is released with a Python generator script, a result-verification tool, and a set of reference solutions obtained with exact ILP for small instances. Baseline results are reported for five published algorithms. The paper documents the generation methodology, defines comparison metrics, and discusses corner cases that expose weaknesses in existing schedulability tests.

title: Online Admission Control for Sporadic Tasks Under Memory Budget Constraints on ARM Cortex-M7
abstract: An online admission controller for sporadic real-time tasks is implemented and evaluated on an ARM Cortex-M7 microcontroller with 512 KB SRAM. The controller must decide within 50 µs whether to accept an arriving task, enforcing both a processor utilisation ceiling and a per-region memory budget partitioned into stack, heap, and static data segments. A three-phase decision procedure first checks utilisation via the hyperbolic bound, then verifies memory region availability using a compact interval representation, and finally confirms schedulability with a reduced-complexity response-time check. Admission latency was measured at 8.4 µs mean and 43 µs worst-case across 10 000 arrival events. Compared to a full O(n²) response-time analysis invoked on each arrival, the proposed procedure reduced admission latency by 79% with no reduction in admission accuracy on the tested workloads. The paper includes a formal proof that the three-phase procedure is never less conservative than the full analysis.

title: Evaluating Constraint Propagation Strategies for Real-Time Task Allocation in Networks of Microcontrollers
abstract: The effectiveness of four constraint propagation strategies—arc consistency (AC-3), singleton arc consistency (SAC), bound consistency (BC), and a domain-reduction heuristic specific to utilisation constraints—is compared for CSP models of real-time task allocation on networks of 4 to 32 microcontroller nodes. Each strategy is paired with the same branch-and-bound search and tested on 480 instances drawn from the benchmark suite described in a prior work. Metrics collected include number of backtracks, constraint-check count, and wall-clock time to first feasible solution. BC combined with the utilisation-specific domain reduction consistently reached a first feasible solution using 38% fewer backtracks than AC-3 on instances with more than 16 nodes. The paper also reports that SAC incurred propagation overhead that outweighed its pruning benefit for instances where task utilisation variance was low. Recommendations for propagation strategy selection as a function of instance characteristics are provided.

title: Interval-Based Feasibility Filtering for Large-Scale Real-Time Task Allocation on Embedded Controller Networks
abstract: Large-scale instances of the real-time task allocation problem—those with more than 200 tasks and 20 nodes—remain difficult for exact CSP and ILP solvers within engineering time budgets. This paper proposes a preprocessing filter based on interval arithmetic applied to utilisation and memory constraints; the filter eliminates provably infeasible node–task assignments before search begins, reducing the effective variable-domain sizes by 51% on average across 200 large test instances. The filtered instances are then solved with a two-phase procedure: a greedy constructive heuristic followed by a local-search phase limited to five minutes. Combined, the approach found solutions matching or improving ILP-derived lower bounds in 84% of instances with 200 tasks, compared to 41% for unfiltered local search alone. Run time was under three minutes for 94% of instances. The paper includes a correctness proof for the interval filter and a discussion of its applicability to heterogeneous node types.

title: Constraint-based page imposition for variable-format print runs: a graph-theoretic formulation
abstract: Commercial print workflows frequently require imposition schemes that accommodate multiple page formats on a single press sheet while satisfying bleed, gutter, and trim constraints. This paper formulates the imposition problem as a bin-packing variant on a weighted constraint graph, where nodes represent pages and edges encode spatial and colorimetric dependencies. An integer linear programming solver was applied to a test set of 120 real-world job tickets sourced from a regional print service provider. Compared to the operator-defined reference layouts, the automated system reduced paper waste by 8.3% on average and decreased manual setup time from approximately 22 minutes to under 3 minutes per job. The solver found provably optimal solutions for 74% of jobs within a 60-second time budget; the remainder were solved to within 2% of optimality. Sensitivity analysis showed that bleed width and press-sheet aspect ratio were the dominant constraint parameters affecting solution quality.

title: Registration error accumulation in multi-pass flexographic printing on extensible substrates
abstract: Flexographic printing on polyethylene film introduces registration errors that compound across successive color stations due to substrate elongation under web tension. This study developed a forward-simulation model that predicts cumulative misregistration as a function of material elastic modulus, web tension profile, and print speed. Tensile properties of five commercial PE film grades were measured using a universal testing machine; web tension was logged at 100 Hz during live production runs on an eight-color narrow-web press. The simulation model was fitted to 46 production runs and predicted final misregistration within ±18 µm RMS across 90% of cases. A corrective pre-distortion look-up table was derived from the model and implemented in the RIP stage, reducing visible misregistration artifacts in consumer packaging trials from 6.1% to 0.8% of printed meters.

title: Parametric dieline generation for tuck-end folding cartons using feature-based CAD primitives
abstract: Structural packaging designers typically construct folding-carton dielines by manually placing and mirroring geometric primitives in vector drawing environments, a process prone to dimensional inconsistency when carton dimensions change. This chapter describes a parametric dieline engine implemented as a scripted extension for a commercial vector graphics application. The system represents carton geometry as a directed acyclic graph of dimensioned features—panels, score lines, glue flaps, and tuck tongues—each linked by algebraic dependency rules. When a single master dimension (e.g., internal depth) is updated, the full dieline recalculates in under 0.4 seconds. The engine was validated against 18 carton families from two regional packaging converters; 94% of regenerated dielines matched the reference drawings within ±0.05 mm. The chapter also discusses integration with a barcode placement module that respects quiet-zone requirements automatically.

title: Spectral prediction of overprint colors in offset lithography using a modified Yule–Nielsen model with ink-film thickness correction
abstract: Accurate prediction of overprint colors is essential for digital proofing and ink-saving formulation in offset lithography. The standard Yule–Nielsen spectral prediction model assumes uniform ink-film thickness, an assumption that breaks down with high ink coverage or uncoated substrates. This work introduces a correction term derived from in-line densitometric measurements of ink-film thickness variation across the print zone, obtained using a scanning densitometer traversing the press sheet transversally at 2 mm intervals. Predictions were evaluated on 320 two-color overprint patches printed on coated and uncoated stocks at three ink-film thicknesses. The corrected model reduced mean CIEDE2000 prediction error from 2.14 to 1.07 ΔE on coated stock and from 3.61 to 1.89 ΔE on uncoated stock. No additional calibration targets beyond a standard IT8.7/4 chart were required.

title: Automated PDF/X compliance verification for packaging artwork using rule-based document analysis
abstract: Packaging artwork submitted to prepress departments frequently contains PDF/X conformance errors that are not caught until late in the production cycle. This paper describes a rule-based verification engine that parses the PDF object tree to detect 23 categories of non-conformance including embedded font subsets, out-of-gamut spot colors, overprint mode conflicts, and missing bleed regions. The engine was written in Python using the pdfminer library and tested on a corpus of 1,240 artwork files collected from four packaging converters over 18 months. Of these, 38% contained at least one conformance error; the engine detected 96.3% of manually confirmed errors with a false-positive rate of 1.8%. The most common error category was incorrect overprint settings on white knockout objects, accounting for 31% of all detected issues. Integration into a hot-folder workflow is described.

title: Optical distortion mapping for artwork placement on curved and tapered labels
abstract: Labels applied to tapered cylindrical containers (e.g., conical bottles, truncated-cone tubs) exhibit predictable barrel or pincushion distortion that designers must compensate for during artwork origination. This study established an empirical distortion map by printing a reference grid on pressure-sensitive label stock, applying it to 12 container geometries with known taper angles between 2° and 18°, and measuring grid-node displacements using a calibrated flat-bed scanner at 600 dpi. A polynomial warp model was fitted to the displacement data per container geometry (R² > 0.97 in all cases). A pre-warp transformation derived from the model was applied to artwork in PDF form via a custom PostScript transform; after application, residual positional error was below 0.3 mm across all label zones. The approach requires only container geometry as input and no physical prototype.

title: Dimensional tolerance propagation in multi-component secondary packaging: an interval arithmetic approach
abstract: Secondary packaging assemblies consisting of a folding carton, a blister tray, and an inner leaflet must fit together within tight dimensional tolerances established by pharmaceutical clients. Manufacturing tolerances on each component accumulate and can cause assembly failures. This paper applies interval arithmetic to propagate dimensional tolerances through an assembly model of a blister-pack carton, representing each nominal dimension as a bounded interval derived from process capability data (Cpk values between 0.87 and 1.41 measured across 14 production lines). The model predicted worst-case assembly interference in 3 of 9 studied carton families; physical assembly trials confirmed interference in those same families. After adjusting nominal dimensions using the model, interference rate dropped from 2.3% to 0.4% in a 10,000-unit validation run. The approach requires only standard process capability statistics, not Monte Carlo simulation.

title: Comparison of ICC-based and spectral gamut mapping strategies for brand color reproduction across offset and digital printing
abstract: Brand identity guidelines typically specify spot colors that must be reproduced consistently across offset and digital printing processes with substantially different color gamuts. This study compared three gamut mapping strategies—ICC perceptual rendering intent, relative colorimetric clipping, and a spectral optimization approach that minimizes CIEDE2000 under the target illuminant—for reproducing 48 Pantone-equivalent brand colors on four substrates (coated offset, uncoated offset, electrophotographic coated, and inkjet coated). Color accuracy was evaluated using ΔE00 under D50 illumination and a secondary metamerism index under A illuminant. The spectral optimization strategy achieved the lowest ΔE00 mean (1.34) and lowest metamerism index (0.41) across all substrate–process combinations, but required 2.3 minutes of solver time per color versus under 1 second for ICC methods. Trade-offs between accuracy, metamerism, and computational cost are discussed.

title: Machine learning classification of prepress preflight errors from PDF structural features
abstract: Preflight error classification in prepress workflows typically relies on hard-coded rule sets that require expert maintenance as standards evolve. This paper investigates whether machine learning classifiers trained on features extracted from the PDF object tree can identify error categories without explicit rule authoring. A dataset of 3,847 packaging artwork PDFs, each manually annotated with up to five error categories, was assembled from three prepress bureaus. Forty-one structural and colorimetric features were extracted per file. Random forest, gradient boosting, and a small fully connected neural network were evaluated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Gradient boosting achieved the highest macro F1 score of 0.83 across 11 error categories. Performance was lowest for the 'insufficient bleed' category (F1 = 0.61) due to ambiguity in page-box definitions. Feature importance analysis confirmed that colorspace object count and overprint flag frequency were the most discriminative features.

title: Dieline-to-printed-artwork registration accuracy under varying die-cutting pressure and board caliper
abstract: Die-cutting pressure and board caliper variation affect the dimensional accuracy of cut and creased folding cartons, which in turn determines how well pre-positioned artwork aligns with structural features such as windows, tear-strips, and edge-to-edge bleeds. This work designed a full-factorial experiment with three levels of die-cutting pressure (80%, 100%, 120% of nominal) and three commercial board calipers (280, 350, 410 g/m²) across four carton dieline families. Cut-dimension deviations and crease-position deviations were measured on 30 samples per condition using a digital image analysis system. Board caliper had a larger effect on crease position than die-cutting pressure (η² = 0.41 vs. 0.19). A correction table mapping caliper to artwork pre-offset values was derived; applying it reduced crease-to-artwork misregistration from a mean of 0.54 mm to 0.21 mm without press adjustments.

title: Substrate-aware PDF rendering: adjusting halftone geometry for measured surface roughness in inkjet printing on corrugated board
abstract: Direct inkjet printing on corrugated board produces halftone dot gain that varies with flute type and liner roughness, causing calibrated ICC profiles to underperform relative to smoother substrates. This study measured Ra surface roughness across three corrugated board grades (B-flute, E-flute, EB-flute) using a contact profilometer and correlated roughness at 16 measurement points per sheet with dot gain at those locations. A locally adaptive halftone screening strategy was developed that modifies screen frequency and dot shape as a function of locally predicted dot gain, estimated from a roughness lookup table built from 240 calibration patches. On B-flute board, mean tonal error (ΔL* across a 51-step wedge) fell from 3.8 to 1.9; on E-flute it fell from 2.6 to 1.4. The approach is implemented as a pre-RIP filter requiring only a roughness scan of the substrate batch.

title: Ink-film optical density and gloss as indirect indicators of surface energy adequacy in flexographic printing on polyolefin films
abstract: Direct surface energy measurement is not feasible during high-speed printing, so indirect print-quality indicators that correlate with surface activation level would be practically useful. This study examined whether optical density (measured by reflection densitometry) and 60° specular gloss of cyan flexographic ink prints on corona-treated BOPP and LDPE films correlate sufficiently well with independently measured surface free energy values to serve as on-press proxies. Films were prepared at seven discrete corona dose levels (0.5–4.5 W·min/m²) and printed on a laboratory flexographic proofer at 100 m/min with a fixed anilox volume of 4.0 cm³/m². Pearson correlation coefficients between surface energy and optical density were r = 0.91 (BOPP) and r = 0.88 (LDPE); between surface energy and gloss, r = 0.85 and r = 0.79, respectively. A threshold surface energy of approximately 38 mN/m corresponded to an optical density plateau, below which density dropped sharply. These correlations are strong enough to support a simple two-point calibration chart for press operators to estimate surface activation status from routine densitometry.

title: Factorial structure of a Serbian-language matrix reasoning battery in primary school children
abstract: This study examined the latent factor structure of a newly constructed matrix reasoning battery administered to 412 children aged 8–11 from eight primary schools in Novi Sad and Subotica. Exploratory factor analysis followed by confirmatory factor analysis indicated a single dominant general factor accounting for 54% of common variance, with two residual group factors corresponding to item set complexity. Item response theory Rasch modelling showed adequate fit for 38 of 48 items; 10 items were removed due to local dependence or misfit. Differential item functioning by gender was absent for all retained items. The battery demonstrated good internal consistency (α = .88) and four-week test–retest reliability (r = .82, n = 94). Age-differentiated raw-to-standard-score conversion tables are provided. The results support the battery's use as a screening instrument within the Serbian educational context, pending broader national norming.

title: Standardisation of working memory span tasks for Serbian children aged 7–15: percentile norms and reliability estimates
abstract: Normative data are reported for three working memory tasks—digit span forward, digit span backward, and a newly developed sentence span task—administered to a stratified sample of 1,186 Serbian children from Vojvodina. Stratification variables included age (seven one-year bands), school type, settlement size, and parental education. Digit span forward and backward showed monotonic age-related increases through age 13, with a plateau thereafter. The sentence span task showed a steeper developmental trajectory and higher correlation with reading comprehension (r = .46) than either digit span measure. Internal consistency ranged from .73 to .84 across tasks and age bands. Split-half reliability corrected by the Spearman–Brown formula ranged from .70 to .80. Age- and task-specific percentile tables are provided alongside standard scores (M = 10, SD = 3). Implications for clinical assessment of children with suspected working memory difficulties are discussed.

title: Comparing classical test theory and two-parameter logistic IRT estimates in a short vocabulary test for school-age children
abstract: The study compared item parameter estimates derived from classical test theory (CTT) and a two-parameter logistic item response theory (2PL IRT) model for a 40-item multiple-choice vocabulary test administered to 784 children aged 9–12. CTT item difficulty correlated .95 with IRT b-parameters and CTT item-total correlations correlated .88 with IRT a-parameters, replicating findings from Western language contexts. However, the rank ordering of items by discrimination diverged notably (Kendall's τ = .61) in the upper range of difficulty, suggesting that CTT discrimination indices underestimate differentiation for hard items in this sample. Information functions showed that the test measured most precisely at ability levels slightly below the sample mean (θ ≈ −0.4), indicating the test is better suited for identifying below-average vocabulary than for differentiating high performers. Recommendations for item revision and adaptive test construction are outlined.

title: Cross-cultural measurement equivalence of a non-verbal cognitive battery between Serbian and Hungarian primary school children in Vojvodina
abstract: Vojvodina hosts a substantial Hungarian-speaking minority whose assessment in Serbian-language instruments may introduce cultural measurement bias. This study applied multi-group confirmatory factor analysis to test measurement invariance of a five-subtest non-verbal cognitive battery across Serbian-speaking (n = 511) and Hungarian-speaking (n = 248) primary school children in grades 3–5. Configural, metric, and scalar invariance models were estimated, with the Satorra–Bentler scaled chi-square difference test used to compare nested models. Metric invariance held for all five subtests (ΔCFI = .006), but scalar invariance failed for one block design subtest (modification indices > 10 for two intercepts), suggesting partial scalar invariance. Latent mean comparisons corrected for non-invariant intercepts indicated no statistically significant group differences in general non-verbal ability (d = 0.09, p = .41). These findings support cautious use of the battery across both groups with appropriate intercept corrections.

title: A pilot study of computerised adaptive testing for general cognitive ability in Serbian secondary school students
abstract: Computerised adaptive testing (CAT) offers efficiency gains over fixed-form paper tests by selecting items calibrated to the examinee's estimated ability level after each response. This pilot evaluated a CAT implementation for general cognitive ability using a bank of 96 items previously calibrated with a 3PL IRT model in a sample of 1,340 Serbian secondary school students. Forty students aged 15–17 completed both a fixed 40-item form and the CAT version on separate occasions. The CAT reached comparable precision (mean standard error of measurement 0.31) using on average 18.4 items compared with 40 items for the fixed form. Ability estimates correlated .92 across administrations. Administration time was reduced by approximately 43%. Students' self-reported engagement ratings were higher for the CAT format (M = 4.1 vs. 3.6 on a 5-point scale). Limitations related to item bank depth and exposure control are discussed.

title: Item exposure control strategies in adaptive cognitive testing: a simulation study using Serbian item bank parameters
abstract: Uncontrolled item exposure in computerised adaptive testing inflates the risk of item compromise and score inflation over repeated administrations. This simulation study evaluated five exposure control methods—maximum information, randomesque, Sympson–Hetter, Stocking–Lewis, and a modified fade-away algorithm—using real item parameters from a calibrated 96-item Serbian cognitive ability bank. Simulations were conducted with 10,000 simulated examinees drawn from a standard normal ability distribution. Outcome criteria were measurement precision (RMSE of ability estimates), test overlap rate, and item pool usage. Maximum information yielded the lowest RMSE (0.29) but the highest overlap rate (61%). The modified fade-away algorithm achieved a balance, with RMSE of 0.33 and overlap rate of 28% while using 89% of the item pool. Sympson–Hetter performed comparably but required lengthy constraint calibration. Practical recommendations for adaptive test administration in Serbian educational settings are provided.

title: Psychometric properties of a short fluid intelligence scale for preschool children aged 5–7
abstract: Cognitive assessment of preschool-aged children is complicated by short attention spans, verbal demands, and examiner–child rapport factors. This study reports the development and initial validation of a 24-item picture-based fluid intelligence scale for Serbian children aged 5–7 (n = 318, recruited from kindergartens in Novi Sad, Zrenjanin, and Sombor). Items required analogical reasoning using pictorial stimuli with no verbal response required. Rasch analysis indicated acceptable fit (infit MNSQ 0.82–1.21) for 21 items; three items were revised. Test–retest reliability over three weeks was r = .78 (n = 62). Convergent validity with an established non-verbal reasoning measure was r = .64. Normative data stratified by age in six-month bands are presented. Results confirm that analogical reasoning at an age-appropriate level can be assessed reliably without verbal mediation, supporting use in multilingual and low-verbal populations.

title: Test norming with continuous norming methods: an application to a Serbian reading speed and comprehension battery
abstract: Traditional normative approaches group scores by discrete age bands, discarding information on age as a continuous predictor. This paper applies continuous norming using the cNORM method to a reading speed and comprehension battery administered to 1,842 Serbian children aged 7–14. The battery comprised three timed passages and 30 comprehension questions. Using Taylor polynomial regression within the cNORM framework, smooth percentile trajectories were estimated across the full age range. Compared with conventional norming, continuous norming reduced standard error of score estimates by 12–18% at age boundaries and eliminated the step artefacts observable when adjacent norm groups were compared. Cross-validation using a 20% hold-out sample confirmed predictive accuracy (R² = .91 for reading speed, .87 for comprehension). Normalised T-score and percentile tables derived from the continuous model are provided, along with the R code and anonymised dataset as supplementary materials.

title: Psychometric assessment in Serbian schools: a review of available instruments, norming quality, and gaps in coverage
abstract: This chapter reviews cognitive and scholastic ability instruments available in Serbian for school-age populations, evaluating each against criteria of norming sample adequacy, publication date, standardisation transparency, and psychometric reporting quality. Forty-one instruments were identified through database searches and publisher catalogues; 19 had been normed on Serbian samples, of which only 11 reported sample stratification procedures. Norms older than 15 years were flagged as likely outdated given documented Flynn effect trends in neighbouring Balkan countries. Critical gaps identified include the absence of nationally representative adaptive testing platforms, limited instruments for children under age 6, and scant coverage of children with hearing impairment. The chapter summarises recommendations for test publishers and policymakers, including minimum reporting standards, mandatory restandardisation cycles, and investment in digital test delivery infrastructure for schools.

title: Differential item functioning by socioeconomic status in a national cognitive screening battery: findings from a Vojvodina stratified sample
abstract: Cognitive screening batteries used for educational placement may carry systematic item bias against children from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. Using ordinal logistic regression DIF analysis, this study examined 54 items from a cognitive screening battery administered to 2,106 children in grades 1–4 across Vojvodina schools. Socioeconomic status (SES) was operationalised as a composite of parental education and occupational prestige. Fifteen items showed non-negligible DIF (effect size Δ > 0.43 on the McFadden scale), with 12 favouring high-SES children. Item content analysis revealed that SES-biased items more frequently included culturally loaded vocabulary in instructions or relied on familiarity with printed books and library materials. After removal of these 15 items, latent mean differences by SES were reduced by 31% compared with the full battery, suggesting that part of the observed group difference was attributable to item bias rather than true ability differences.

title: Short-form derivation and validation of the Vojvodina Cognitive Battery for Children using automated item selection algorithms
abstract: Long cognitive test batteries are impractical in school and clinical settings with limited testing time. This study derived short forms of the Vojvodina Cognitive Battery for Children (VCBC), a 90-item instrument normed on 2,106 children, using three automated selection algorithms: maximum battery reliability, maximum validity against an external criterion, and a combined information–coverage algorithm. The full calibration dataset (n = 2,106, grades 1–4) was split into derivation (n = 1,404) and validation (n = 702) halves. A 25-item short form selected by the combined algorithm achieved composite reliability of .84 and correlated .91 with the full battery score in the validation sample. External validity against teacher ratings of academic performance was r = .47 for the short form versus r = .50 for the full battery. Administration time was reduced from approximately 65 to 22 minutes. Norm tables for the short form are provided.

title: Test–retest stability and practice effects in repeated cognitive testing of Serbian children: a six-month longitudinal study
abstract: Reliable interpretation of cognitive re-assessment requires knowledge of expected score changes attributable to practice rather than genuine ability development. This study administered the Vojvodina Cognitive Battery for Children short form twice, six months apart, to 381 children aged 8–12 from four Novi Sad primary schools. Practice effect magnitudes (Cohen's d) ranged from 0.14 (block design) to 0.38 (matrix reasoning) across subtests. A regression-based reliable change index was computed for each subtest and the composite, enabling clinicians to identify changes exceeding practice effects at 80%, 90%, and 95% confidence thresholds. Younger children (ages 8–9) showed larger practice effects than older children (ages 11–12) for three of five subtests. Intraclass correlation coefficients for test–retest reliability ranged from .76 to .84 across subtests. Tables of reliable change indices are provided for clinical and school psychologists.

title: Attitudes of school psychologists in Serbia toward computerised and adaptive assessment: a survey study
abstract: Uptake of computerised and adaptive cognitive testing in Serbian schools has been slow despite the availability of calibrated item banks. This study investigated attitudes, perceived barriers, and training needs among school psychologists (n = 203) across Serbia using an online questionnaire developed for this purpose. Exploratory factor analysis of 28 attitude items yielded four factors: perceived test fairness, technical confidence, institutional readiness, and concern about relationship loss with the child. Technical confidence was the strongest negative predictor of resistance to adoption (β = −.41). Fewer than 18% of respondents reported having used any form of computerised cognitive assessment in the past year, and 64% cited lack of institutional hardware as a practical barrier. Regression analysis explained 47% of variance in adoption intention. The findings highlight the need for targeted training and infrastructure investment before adaptive assessment can be implemented at scale in Serbian schools.

title: Updating norms for a Serbian general ability screening test: secular score changes over 15 years and implications for the Flynn effect in Serbia
abstract: National cognitive test norms become outdated as population ability distributions shift over time. This study restandardised a general ability screening test originally normed in 2007–2009 using a new stratified sample of 1,614 Serbian children aged 7–14 collected in 2022–2024. Mean IQ-equivalent scores in the current sample exceeded the original normative sample by 3.1 points (95% CI: 2.3–3.9), corresponding to a rate of gain of approximately 0.21 points per year, consistent with the lower end of Flynn effect estimates from comparable European countries. Gains were larger for matrix reasoning (d = 0.29) than for vocabulary (d = 0.08), a pattern matching the predominantly abstract reasoning component of the Flynn effect. Regression discontinuity analyses ruled out school curriculum changes as the main explanation. Updated norm tables rendering 2007–2009 norms obsolete are presented alongside the original tables for historical comparison.

title: Constraint-Based Syntactic Parsing with Inductive Logic Programming over Treebank Corpora
abstract: This paper investigates the use of inductive logic programming (ILP) to learn syntactic constraints directly from annotated treebank data. We apply the Progol system extended with background predicates encoding morphosyntactic features to a 45,000-sentence corpus of Serbian news text annotated according to the Prague dependency guidelines. The learning procedure induces 312 Horn clauses that collectively capture agreement and government relations. On held-out data, the induced grammar achieves a labeled attachment score of 81.4%, compared with 78.9% for a hand-crafted baseline grammar of similar coverage. Analysis of the learned clauses shows that the system recovers most standard agreement constraints without human guidance, while also identifying three constructions not previously encoded in the manual grammar. Computational cost scales quadratically with clause length; we discuss pruning strategies that reduce training time by 38% with less than 0.5 percentage-point loss in accuracy. The work establishes a reproducible baseline for data-driven Slavic dependency parsing within the ILP paradigm.

title: Answer Set Programming for Temporal Constraint Satisfaction in Planning Domains
abstract: We examine answer set programming (ASP) as a substrate for encoding and solving temporal constraint satisfaction problems arising in logistics planning. A benchmark suite of 180 problem instances is derived from real delivery-route data provided by a regional transport company and anonymised for publication. Problems are encoded in ASP using event calculus axioms; the gringo/clasp toolchain solves instances with up to 400 events and 1,200 constraints within a 60-second time limit. We compare this approach with a mixed-integer linear programming solver and a constraint programming solver on the same suite. ASP finds optimal or provably near-optimal solutions on 91% of instances, while MIP and CP succeed on 86% and 88% respectively. More importantly, the ASP encoding is inspectable: a domain expert correctly interpreted 94% of answer sets in a structured interview, compared with 31% for MIP solutions. The paper discusses encoding choices that affect grounding size and proposes a modular axiom structure that reduces grounding time by a factor of 2.7.

title: Learning Object-Part Ontologies from Segmented Imagery Using ILP
abstract: This study addresses the automatic construction of part-whole ontologies from segmented natural images. We use a superpixel segmentation pipeline followed by a feature extraction step producing 47 geometric and chromatic attributes per region. These attributes serve as background knowledge for an ILP learner tasked with inducing part-of and adjacent-to predicates for six object categories (vehicles, furniture, animals, tools, buildings, vessels) sampled from a publicly available segmentation dataset containing 12,400 images. The induced ontology is evaluated against a gold-standard annotation created by three domain experts: precision is 0.79 and recall is 0.71 at the predicate level. A secondary experiment shows the ontology transfers with only minor revision to a related robotics grasping dataset, reducing manual annotation effort by approximately 55%. We document failure cases, mostly involving transparent objects and heavy occlusion, and argue for tighter integration between the segmentation quality metric and the ILP search heuristic.

title: Hybrid Architectures for Rule Extraction from Convolutional Feature Maps
abstract: We investigate whether symbolic rules can be reliably extracted from the intermediate feature representations of a convolutional neural network trained for object recognition. A ResNet-18 backbone is trained on a 60,000-image industrial-inspection dataset, achieving 93.1% top-1 accuracy. Activation patterns at three intermediate layers are discretised using k-means clustering and then supplied as extensional facts to an ILP system. The system attempts to induce rules that predict the network's class decisions. Fidelity—the proportion of test images on which the induced rules agree with the network—reaches 87% for the final layer features and 72% for mid-level features, with rules averaging 4.2 literals in length. A user study with 12 engineers reveals that 8 of them could identify the physical defect described by a rule within 90 seconds on average, suggesting the extracted rules are practically interpretable. Failure cases cluster around texturally ambiguous classes, motivating future work on attention-guided discretisation.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Grounding of Spatial Prepositions in Robot Manipulation Tasks
abstract: Spatial prepositions such as 'on', 'behind', and 'between' are grounded differently depending on viewing angle, object size, and task context. This paper proposes a grounding model consisting of a small convolutional encoder that maps RGB-D image patches to a 32-dimensional embedding, combined with an ASP theory that maps embeddings to preposition assignments via learned threshold parameters. Training uses 3,400 annotated robot-manipulation frames collected in a tabletop setting with six object classes and seven prepositions. The model achieves 88.6% accuracy on a held-out test split, compared with 83.1% for a purely neural classifier and 79.4% for a purely geometric rule system. In an online robot-arm control loop, command-following success rate increases from 71% (neural-only) to 84% when the neuro-symbolic grounding module is active. The learned thresholds are interpretable: they correlate with human judgements collected in a 40-participant norming study (Spearman ρ = 0.81).

title: Differentiable Forward Chaining over Neural Concept Embeddings
abstract: We describe a differentiable forward-chaining layer that can be inserted into a standard deep learning pipeline and trained end-to-end. The layer represents a Horn clause rule base as a set of soft implication matrices; at inference time, it performs up to K = 5 rounds of modus ponens over concept-level embeddings produced by an upstream encoder. The approach is evaluated on three tasks: family-tree relation prediction, a visual analogy benchmark with 15,000 items, and a subset of a scene understanding dataset. On the family-tree task, the differentiable layer matches the accuracy of a discrete Prolog solver (99.1% vs. 99.4%) while remaining end-to-end differentiable. On the visual analogy task, combining the layer with a ResNet encoder improves accuracy by 7.3 points over the encoder alone. Training requires approximately 40% more wall-clock time per epoch than a plain neural baseline but converges in fewer epochs for rule-governed tasks. We release all code and dataset splits.

title: Interpretable Visual Question Answering via Scene Graphs and Answer Set Programs
abstract: Visual question answering systems typically produce answers without explicit intermediate reasoning traces. We present a pipeline that first generates a scene graph using a trained relation-detection network, serialises the graph as ASP facts, and then uses a question-parsing module to convert natural-language questions into ASP queries. The ASP solver returns both the answer and the subset of scene-graph atoms that support it, forming a human-readable proof. The pipeline is evaluated on two benchmark VQA datasets totalling 94,000 question–image pairs filtered for questions answerable from scene graphs alone (approximately 61% of the full sets). Accuracy is 73.4% and 69.8% on the two benchmarks, below the best end-to-end neural systems by 4–6 points, but a panel of 20 domain experts rated the proof traces as 'sufficiently informative to audit' in 81% of correct answers. We discuss the main accuracy loss: errors in the upstream scene graph propagate irreversibly to the logic layer.

title: Probabilistic Logic Networks for Uncertain Scene-Graph Inference
abstract: Scene graphs derived from noisy detectors contain uncertain predicate assignments that deterministic logic programs handle poorly. We extend a standard Datalog engine with weighted rules whose weights are learned from data using a maximum-likelihood objective approximated by expectation-maximisation. The extended system, termed Weighted Scene-Graph Datalog (WSGD), is trained and evaluated on 22,000 images drawn from an annotated autonomous-driving perception dataset, using 85 object categories and 30 relational predicates. WSGD achieves a mean recall at 100 (mR@100) of 61.2%, compared with 57.8% for a deterministic ASP baseline and 63.1% for a graph-neural-network comparator. Inference time is 140 ms per image on a single GPU, making the system plausible for near-real-time use. The probabilistic weights are visualised as calibration curves; the model is well-calibrated for high-confidence predictions but underestimates uncertainty for rare predicates, particularly directional spatial relations at long range.

title: Compositional Generalisation in Scene-Graph Reasoning: A Benchmark and Baseline Study
abstract: Existing scene-graph benchmarks do not test whether a model can answer queries about object combinations unseen during training. We construct CompScene-SR, a benchmark of 40,000 synthetic images generated with a parametric 3D renderer, with scene graphs labelled for 60 object types and 25 relations. The benchmark is split so that the test set contains only predicate–object combinations absent from training. Five systems are evaluated: two end-to-end graph neural networks, a neuro-symbolic pipeline using WSGD (from earlier work), a modular network, and a large vision-language model (VLM) used zero-shot. The VLM achieves the highest overall accuracy (71.3%) but drops to 52.1% on compositionally novel queries; the neuro-symbolic pipeline drops by only 6.4 points (from 68.9% to 62.5%), suggesting stronger systematic generalisation. We release the renderer, scene graphs, and evaluation scripts under an open licence.

title: Auditable Industrial Inspection with Neuro-Symbolic Scene Graphs
abstract: Manufacturing quality control requires not only accurate defect detection but also records of the reasoning behind each rejection decision to satisfy regulatory requirements. We adapt the neuro-symbolic scene-graph pipeline developed in earlier work to a printed-circuit-board inspection task. A YOLOv8 backbone detects 14 component classes and 9 defect categories with 94.7% mAP on an in-house dataset of 18,500 images collected from a production line. Scene graphs are generated per board; an ASP-based inspection policy encodes IPC-A-610 acceptance criteria as 78 rules, producing a structured rejection report citing specific rule firings for each defect. Rejection accuracy matches the trained neural detector alone (93.1% vs. 92.8% at equal false-positive rate), while the audit trail is accepted by the quality manager as sufficient documentation in 97% of sampled cases. The paper discusses the process of translating the standard into ASP rules, including ambiguities that required domain-expert clarification.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Rule Revision in Deployed Neuro-Symbolic Systems
abstract: After deployment, a neuro-symbolic system may encounter data distributions that differ from training, causing rules that were accurate in-distribution to produce systematic errors. We propose an online rule-revision procedure: Bayesian tracking of per-rule fidelity over a sliding window of 500 recent examples triggers a revision search using a lightweight ILP subroutine when fidelity drops below a configurable threshold. The procedure is evaluated in a simulated deployment scenario built on the CompScene-SR benchmark augmented with four gradually introduced distributional shifts (lighting, viewpoint, new object textures, and sensor noise). Rule revision recovers 78–91% of the fidelity loss attributable to each shift within 2,000 adaptation examples, compared with 43–67% for periodic full retraining. Revision episodes average 14 seconds on a laptop CPU, making them plausible without interrupting inference. We discuss failure modes, including cases where the upstream neural perception degrades faster than rule revision can compensate.

title: CYP2D6 allele frequencies in a healthy volunteer cohort from Vojvodina: a preliminary population survey
abstract: CYP2D6 genotype data were collected from 124 healthy unrelated volunteers recruited at the University Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 1993 and 1995. Participants were genotyped by PCR-RFLP targeting the CYP2D6*3, *4, *5, and *6 alleles, the four variants most commonly associated with poor metaboliser (PM) status in European populations. The PM phenotype frequency in this Vojvodina sample was 7.3%, consistent with reported Western European rates of 5–10%, while heterozygous extensive metabolisers carrying one non-functional allele accounted for 38.7% of the sample. No ultrarapid metaboliser duplications were identified in this initial cohort. The results suggested that the Serbian population of Vojvodina follows a typical Central/Eastern European distribution for the major loss-of-function alleles, though the sample size precluded definitive conclusions for rarer variants. These baseline data were intended to provide a reference for later clinical pharmacokinetic studies of CYP2D6 substrate drugs in the same geographic region.

title: Plasma nortriptyline concentrations and CYP2D6 genotype in Serbian patients receiving fixed-dose tricyclic antidepressant therapy
abstract: Forty-eight psychiatric inpatients at the Clinic for Psychiatry, Novi Sad, receiving nortriptyline 75 mg/day were enrolled in a pharmacokinetic–pharmacogenomic correlation study. Steady-state plasma nortriptyline concentrations were measured by HPLC with UV detection. CYP2D6 genotyping was performed using a five-allele PCR-RFLP panel (*3, *4, *5, *6, *41). Patients classified as poor metabolisers (n=4) had mean steady-state concentrations of 318 ng/mL, roughly 4.2-fold higher than extensive metabolisers (n=31, mean 76 ng/mL). Three poor metaboliser patients had plasma levels exceeding the accepted therapeutic ceiling of 150 ng/mL and reported anticholinergic adverse effects of moderate severity. Intermediate metabolisers (n=13) showed intermediate concentrations (mean 141 ng/mL). No duplicated-gene ultrarapid metabolisers were identified. Logistic regression indicated that PM genotype significantly predicted supratherapeutic concentration (OR 18.4, 95% CI 2.1–161, p=0.008). The findings support pre-treatment CYP2D6 genotyping to guide nortriptyline dosing in routine psychiatric practice.

title: CYP2C19 poor metaboliser prevalence and escitalopram exposure in a Novi Sad outpatient cohort
abstract: The CYP2C19 enzyme is the primary determinant of escitalopram clearance. This study determined CYP2C19*2 and *3 allele frequencies in 211 outpatients initiating escitalopram therapy at a community psychiatric centre in Novi Sad, and correlated genotype with steady-state plasma drug concentration measured at four weeks. Genotyping was performed by real-time PCR using TaqMan allelic discrimination assays. CYP2C19 poor metaboliser prevalence was 3.3% (n=7), lower than the *2 carrier frequency of 26.5% might predict due to the rarity of *3 in European-ancestry populations. Among poor metabolisers, mean steady-state escitalopram Cmax was 2.8-fold higher than in normal metabolisers, and three of seven experienced QTc prolongation exceeding 470 ms on ECG monitoring. Rapid metabolisers (*17/*17, n=19) showed escitalopram concentrations approximately 40% below the normal metaboliser mean. The data indicate that CYP2C19 genetic status has clinically meaningful effects on escitalopram exposure in this population and warrant attention in prescribing guidelines adapted for South-Eastern European patients.

title: Comparison of CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 metaboliser phenotype distributions across four former Yugoslav successor states
abstract: Population pharmacogenomic surveys from Serbia (n=310), Croatia (n=287), Bosnia and Herzegovina (n=204), and Slovenia (n=198) were pooled to compare CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 metaboliser phenotype distributions across geographically proximate but administratively separate populations. Genotyping methods across centres were harmonised retrospectively using a shared allele panel (CYP2C19 *2, *3, *17; CYP2D6 *3, *4, *5, *6, *41, duplication). Chi-square testing revealed no statistically significant differences in CYP2C19 poor metaboliser frequencies across the four cohorts (range 2.9–4.4%, p=0.61). CYP2D6 poor metaboliser frequencies likewise showed homogeneity (range 6.8–8.1%, p=0.74). CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolisers, detectable only by gene-copy-number assay, ranged from 1.5% (Slovenia) to 3.2% (Bosnia and Herzegovina). The data argue against the use of country-specific reference ranges for these metaboliser phenotypes in the former Yugoslav region, and support development of shared regional prescribing recommendations for CYP substrate drugs.

title: Population pharmacokinetic modelling of sertraline in CYP2C19-genotyped Serbian patients: a NONMEM analysis
abstract: A population pharmacokinetic model for sertraline was developed using data from 89 Serbian patients with major depressive disorder, all of whom had been CYP2C19 genotyped. Plasma samples (2–4 per patient) were collected at weeks 2 and 6 of treatment and analysed by validated LC-MS/MS. NONMEM version VI was used for nonlinear mixed-effects modelling. A one-compartment model with first-order absorption best described the data. CYP2C19 metaboliser status was identified as a statistically significant covariate on apparent oral clearance (CL/F): CL/F estimates were 28.4, 19.7, and 9.3 L/h for normal, intermediate, and poor metabolisers respectively. Weight was a significant covariate on volume of distribution. Bootstrap validation (500 runs) and visual predictive checks confirmed model stability. Simulations demonstrated that a 50% dose reduction achieves therapeutic-range concentrations in poor metabolisers without exposing them to supratherapeutic levels. The model is offered as a basis for Bayesian therapeutic drug monitoring of sertraline in clinical practice.

title: CYP2D6 copy number variation and venlafaxine non-response in treatment-resistant depression: a case series from Vojvodina
abstract: Seven patients referred to the University Clinical Centre of Vojvodina for treatment-resistant depression were found by long-range PCR and quantitative real-time PCR to carry three or more functional CYP2D6 gene copies, classifying them as ultrarapid metabolisers (UM). All had received standard-dose venlafaxine (150–225 mg/day) without adequate response after at least eight weeks of treatment. Measured steady-state plasma venlafaxine concentrations in the UM patients ranged from 18 to 47 ng/mL, substantially below the therapeutic reference range of 100–400 ng/mL established for extensive metabolisers. Following dose escalation guided by plasma concentration monitoring in four patients, three achieved plasma levels in the therapeutic range and two of those showed clinical response by week 16 as measured by the Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale. This case series illustrates that unrecognised CYP2D6 ultrarapid metaboliser status is a tractable cause of apparent venlafaxine treatment resistance, and advocates plasma concentration monitoring as a complement to genotyping in refractory cases.

title: Genotype-guided versus standard dosing of escitalopram and sertraline in Serbian primary care: one-year outcomes from a registry linkage study
abstract: Using a linkage between a pharmacogenomic registry established at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, and electronic prescribing records from 14 primary care practices in the South Bačka District, this retrospective cohort study compared one-year treatment outcomes in patients whose antidepressant dose was adjusted following CYP2C19 genotyping (guided cohort, n=113) against patients receiving standard doses without genotype data (standard cohort, n=247). Primary outcomes were treatment discontinuation due to adverse effects and psychiatric hospitalisation within 12 months. CYP2C19 poor and rapid metabolisers in the guided cohort had significantly lower rates of discontinuation due to adverse effects (8.0% vs 19.3%, OR 0.37, 95% CI 0.16–0.85). Hospitalisation rates did not differ significantly between cohorts overall, but were numerically lower in guided poor metabolisers. The retrospective design limits causal inference; residual confounding by prescriber practice style and unmeasured clinical variables cannot be excluded. These data are offered as hypothesis-generating for a prospective trial.

title: Twenty-five years of CYP pharmacogenomics research in Vojvodina: dataset summary and allele frequency tables for regional reference use
abstract: This data report aggregates genotyping records accumulated by the pharmacogenomics group at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, between 1993 and 2020, covering 1,847 individuals genotyped for CYP2C19 and 1,614 for CYP2D6. Allele frequency tables are provided for the complete set of variants assayed across the study period: CYP2C19 *2, *3, *17 and CYP2D6 *3, *4, *5, *6, *41, plus functional copy-number status. The dataset spans healthy volunteers, psychiatric outpatients and inpatients, and primary care patients. Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium was confirmed for all alleles in the healthy volunteer subset. Observed genotype frequencies are tabulated by sex, decade of birth, and self-reported ethnicity where available. The data are placed in the context of European reference populations from the gnomAD database and published surveys from neighbouring countries. The aggregated tables are intended to serve as a regional reference for clinical pharmacogenomics interpretation in South-Eastern European practice and for calibration of commercial genotyping panels.

title: Characterisation of aqueous droplet generation in PDMS flow-focusing devices across a range of capillary numbers and oil-phase viscosities
abstract: Droplet size and generation frequency in flow-focusing microfluidic junctions depend on the balance between interfacial tension and viscous forces, yet published correlations often disagree because device geometry and surface conditions vary between laboratories. This work characterises droplet formation in PDMS channels with a 100 µm × 80 µm rectangular cross-section using three continuous-phase fluids: mineral oil, hexadecane, and a silicone oil with dynamic viscosity 50 mPa·s, each without added surfactant and with 1% (v/v) Span 80. Dispersed-phase flow rates ranged from 0.05 to 2.0 µL/min and continuous-phase rates from 0.5 to 10 µL/min, giving capillary numbers Ca between 4 × 10⁻³ and 0.18. High-speed imaging at 5 000 frames per second captured the squeezing-to-dripping transition. Droplet diameter scaled with (Qd/Qc)^0.33 in the squeezing regime, consistent with earlier scaling laws, but the prefactor differed by up to 22% between surfactant-free and surfactant-containing conditions. Generation frequency reached 1 240 Hz at the highest Ca tested. A dimensionless correlation is proposed that unifies data from all three oil phases within ±8% error. The dataset is provided as supplementary material to facilitate direct comparison by other groups.

title: Passive analyte preconcentration in a dead-end PDMS microchannel array exploiting evaporation-driven flow
abstract: Point-of-care assays for low-abundance biomarkers require preconcentration steps that are difficult to implement without external pumps or electrokinetic equipment. This paper describes a passive approach in which a dead-end array of 24 parallel PDMS microchannels (width 80 µm, depth 60 µm, length 12 mm) concentrates fluorescent model analytes through evaporation-driven convective flow at the open terminus. Device operation at 37 °C and 40% relative humidity was characterised using fluorescein sodium salt as a tracer at initial concentrations from 50 nM to 5 µM. Confocal fluorescence measurements at the closed end showed a 14- to 18-fold concentration increase within 25 min under optimised conditions. PDMS oxygen-plasma treatment time was found to influence evaporation rate: channels treated for 60 s showed 1.6-fold higher evaporation flux than untreated controls, attributed to increased hydrophilicity reducing the contact angle at the meniscus from 108° to 31°. Salt accumulation at the terminus was quantified by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, showing sodium enrichment consistent with the fluorescence measurements. The device requires no external power and is fabricated entirely by standard replica moulding, making it directly applicable to resource-limited diagnostic settings.

title: Integration of a porous PMMA membrane into a PDMS chip for combined droplet generation and size-based cell filtration
abstract: Combining droplet encapsulation with upstream cell filtering on a single chip reduces the number of manual handling steps in single-cell assays. This conference contribution reports on the bonding and characterisation of a 8 µm pore-size porous poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) membrane sandwiched between two PDMS layers at the inlet of a flow-focusing droplet generator. Membrane integration was achieved by oxygen-plasma activation followed by isopropanol-assisted alignment and 80 °C thermal bonding; burst pressure testing confirmed leak-free seals up to 65 kPa. Filtration efficiency for 15 µm polystyrene beads (used as cell surrogates) was 96.4 ± 1.8% at flow rates up to 5 µL/min, with no observable deformation of the downstream droplet junction geometry. Droplet size uniformity downstream of the filter was 4.1% CV, compared with 3.8% CV for an equivalent device without a membrane, indicating negligible disturbance to the flow-focusing regime. Pressure drop across the membrane was measured at 1.2 kPa at 2 µL/min and modelled with a Darcy permeability of 3.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ m². The fabrication protocol is described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Effect of channel wall ageing on droplet size variability in PDMS microfluidic devices stored up to 12 months
abstract: PDMS microfluidic devices are often fabricated well in advance of use, yet the effect of storage time on droplet generation performance is rarely quantified. This study tracks the wettability and droplet size coefficient of variation of oxygen-plasma-bonded PDMS flow-focusing chips stored under three conditions: sealed in nitrogen, sealed in air, and unsealed in air, over 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Water contact angle was measured by sessile drop goniometry at each time point; devices were then used for droplet generation with a mineral oil–water system at fixed flow rates. Contact angle recovery from the post-plasma value of 8° proceeded rapidly in all storage conditions, reaching near-native values (~108°) within 72 hours, consistent with surface hydrophobic recovery reported in the literature. Droplet size CV increased from 1.9% for freshly activated devices to 4.8% for 12-month air-stored devices. Nitrogen-sealed storage reduced this increase to 3.1% CV at 12 months. Attenuated total reflectance FTIR spectra showed progressive oxidation of surface methyl groups regardless of storage condition. The results suggest that nitrogen sealing meaningfully slows, but does not prevent, performance degradation, which has implications for pre-packaged point-of-care chip manufacturing.

title: Thermal gradient mapping inside refrigerated road trailers using a 16-node wireless mesh
abstract: Spatial temperature heterogeneity inside refrigerated semi-trailers was characterised using a 16-node ZigBee mesh network mounted at three heights and four longitudinal positions. Measurements were conducted over 22 journeys between Novi Sad and Vienna covering a total of 14,300 km under summer and winter conditions. Nodes sampled at 1-minute intervals, producing approximately 1.1 million temperature records. Analysis identified a persistent warm zone near the rear doors, averaging 2.1 °C above the set-point of +4 °C during door-open events lasting more than 90 seconds. A principal component decomposition of the spatial profiles revealed that the first two components explain 81% of within-trailer variance. These findings were used to propose three alternative sensor placement strategies that reduce the probability of undetected warm zones by a factor of 2.4 compared to the single-probe standard practice currently mandated by ATP regulations.

title: Time-of-arrival localisation of reefer unit fault events using distributed acoustic emission sensors: a feasibility study
abstract: Reefer unit compressor faults produce transient acoustic emission bursts that propagate through the vehicle frame. This feasibility study examines whether four piezoelectric AE sensors distributed across a trailer chassis can localise fault event origin using time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) estimation. Controlled fault events were simulated by mechanically exciting the chassis at 18 known positions during static trials. TDOA was estimated using generalised cross-correlation with phase transform (GCC-PHAT). Localisation error in two dimensions was below 0.35 m for 80% of events under low ambient vibration and below 0.9 m under motorway vibration. Frame-propagated wave speed varied between 2,100 and 2,850 m/s depending on structural member, requiring individual calibration. While the current implementation requires wired data acquisition for the high-sample-rate AE signals, the study identifies conditions under which a compressed-sensing approach could reduce the required sample rate by a factor of 6, making wireless transmission feasible.

title: Heart rate variability indices in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis: a cross-sectional comparison with healthy controls
abstract: Autonomic dysfunction in multiple sclerosis is increasingly recognized but remains incompletely characterized in early relapsing-remitting disease. We recruited 42 patients with clinically definite relapsing-remitting MS (median EDSS 2.0, disease duration 3.1 years) and 42 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Five-minute resting electrocardiographic recordings were analysed for time-domain (SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50) and frequency-domain (LF, HF, LF/HF ratio) heart rate variability parameters. Patients showed significantly reduced RMSSD (mean 28.4 ms vs. 41.7 ms, p=0.003) and HF power (p=0.009) compared with controls, indicating parasympathetic withdrawal. SDNN was borderline reduced (p=0.048). LF/HF ratio did not differ significantly between groups. No correlation was found between HRV indices and current relapse activity or steroid treatment within the preceding three months. Lesion load on cervical spinal MRI correlated weakly with RMSSD reduction (r=−0.31, p=0.04). These results suggest measurable parasympathetic impairment even at early disease stages.

title: Quantitative sudomotor axon reflex testing in multiple sclerosis: pilot observations in 18 patients
abstract: Small fiber autonomic axons are vulnerable to the neurodegenerative process in MS, yet sweat function is rarely tested systematically. We applied a standardized quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test (QSART) protocol at four anatomical sites (forearm, proximal and distal leg, foot) in 18 MS patients (10 relapsing-remitting, 8 secondary progressive) and 18 healthy controls matched for age and sex. Sweat output was measured volumetrically after iontophoresis of 10% acetylcholine. Secondary progressive patients showed markedly reduced sweat volumes at all four sites compared with controls (p<0.01 at each site); reductions in the relapsing-remitting group were present only at the distal leg and foot (p=0.02 and 0.03 respectively). A distal-to-proximal gradient of sudomotor impairment was observed in the progressive subgroup, consistent with length-dependent axonal dysfunction. Correlation with intraepidermal nerve fiber density from previously published skin punch biopsy data is discussed. This pilot series supports QSART as a candidate surrogate measure of axonal burden in MS.

title: Orthostatic hypotension and tilt-table responses in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis: frequency and clinical correlates
abstract: Symptomatic orthostatic hypotension is a source of morbidity in advanced MS but its prevalence in a secondary progressive cohort has not been prospectively described in our region. We enrolled 55 patients with secondary progressive MS (median EDSS 5.5, range 4.0–7.5) and performed a standardized 70-degree head-up tilt-table test with continuous non-invasive beat-to-beat blood pressure monitoring. Orthostatic hypotension (defined as a drop ≥20 mmHg systolic or ≥10 mmHg diastolic within three minutes) was documented in 27 patients (49%). Among those, 15 (55%) were asymptomatic at rest. Tilt-induced heart rate increment was blunted compared with a healthy reference group (mean 7.1 vs. 18.6 bpm, p<0.001), consistent with combined sympathetic and parasympathetic impairment. Regression analysis identified higher EDSS and longer disease duration as independent predictors of orthostatic hypotension. Bladder dysfunction and fatigue scores were significantly worse in patients with orthostatic hypotension, suggesting shared autonomic pathway involvement.

title: Autonomic dysfunction in multiple sclerosis: heart rate variability and sudomotor function as surrogate markers of axonal injury in secondary progressive disease
abstract: This doctoral thesis examined autonomic nervous system impairment in a cross-sectional cohort of 80 patients with secondary progressive MS and 40 age-matched controls, integrating spectral heart rate variability, 24-hour Holter analysis, tilt-table testing, and four-site QSART. Principal component analysis of eleven autonomic variables identified two independent factors accounting for 61% of total variance: a cardiovagal factor (loaded by RMSSD, HF power, and tilt heart rate increment) and a sudomotor factor (loaded by QSART volumes at all four sites). Both factor scores correlated independently with EDSS (r=−0.44 and −0.52 respectively, p<0.001) and with cervical cord cross-sectional area on MRI (r=0.38 and 0.41, p<0.01). Longitudinal data in a subset of 28 patients followed over 24 months showed a mean annual decline of 8.3% in distal foot QSART volume and 6.1% in RMSSD, rates comparable to concurrent atrophy measures. The findings support combined autonomic testing as a candidate composite outcome for neuroprotection trials in secondary progressive MS.

title: Twenty-four-hour heart rate variability monitoring reveals diurnal autonomic dysregulation in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis
abstract: Standard short-term HRV recordings may underestimate autonomic burden by missing nocturnal and circadian variation. We analysed 24-hour Holter ECG recordings from 38 secondary progressive MS patients and 38 controls, extracting time- and frequency-domain HRV parameters in six consecutive four-hour epochs. Patients showed significantly lower SDNN across all epochs (overall group effect p<0.001). The normal nocturnal augmentation of HF power was attenuated in the MS group: mean nocturnal HF increase relative to daytime was 14% in patients versus 47% in controls (p=0.001). Daytime LF/HF ratio was elevated in patients, suggesting relative sympathetic predominance. Hierarchical linear modelling confirmed that group membership and time-of-day interacted significantly (p=0.006), indicating disrupted diurnal autonomic rhythm. Nocturnal HF augmentation correlated with self-reported sleep quality (r=0.41, p=0.01). These data suggest that ambulatory 24-hour HRV monitoring captures autonomic dysfunction not visible in short-term resting recordings and may be informative for assessing disease severity.

title: Agreement between QSART and the sympathetic skin response in detecting sudomotor failure in multiple sclerosis
abstract: QSART and the sympathetic skin response (SSR) both assess postganglionic sudomotor function but differ substantially in cost, technical demands, and sensitivity. We compared both methods in 50 MS patients (25 relapsing-remitting, 25 secondary progressive) and 30 controls. QSART was performed at four standard sites; SSR was elicited by electrical stimulation at the wrist, recorded from the palm and sole. Absent or prolonged SSR was found in 16 of 50 patients (32%); abnormal QSART (any site below the 5th percentile of controls) was found in 31 of 50 (62%). Agreement between the two tests was moderate (Cohen's κ=0.41). QSART detected sudomotor failure in 15 patients with normal SSR. Discordant cases had shorter disease duration and lower EDSS, suggesting QSART detects earlier or milder impairment. ROC analysis showed QSART area under the curve of 0.81 versus 0.67 for SSR in the secondary progressive subgroup. Results support QSART as the more sensitive option for clinical research purposes.

title: Autonomic testing in a secondary progressive MS cohort: reproducibility of QSART and short-term HRV over a six-month interval
abstract: Surrogate markers are only useful in longitudinal trials if they are reproducible within a stable disease period. We assessed test–retest reproducibility of four-site QSART and five-minute resting HRV in 30 secondary progressive MS patients who were neurologically stable (no relapse, no steroid use, EDSS unchanged ±0.5) over six months. Intraclass correlation coefficients for QSART volumes ranged from 0.79 (forearm) to 0.86 (foot). For HRV time-domain indices, ICC was 0.73 for RMSSD and 0.78 for SDNN; frequency-domain indices were less reproducible (ICC 0.59–0.67). Bland-Altman plots showed acceptable limits of agreement for QSART foot volume (bias −0.04 µL, LoA ±0.62 µL) and RMSSD (bias −0.8 ms, LoA ±9.4 ms). The smallest detectable change for foot QSART was estimated at 0.88 µL, providing a reference for sample size calculations in interventional studies. These data indicate that QSART and time-domain HRV are sufficiently reproducible for use as secondary outcomes in neuroprotection trials of 12 months or longer.
