title: Permeation kinetics of acetaldehyde through porous ZnO thin-film membranes: a time-lag analysis
abstract: Time-lag permeation measurements were applied to polycrystalline ZnO films of 100–600 nm thickness to extract effective diffusion coefficients and solubility coefficients for acetaldehyde at concentrations of 0.2–5 ppm. Films were deposited on anodic alumina substrates with controlled 20 nm pore size to decouple substrate from film contributions. Diffusion coefficients ranged from 3.1 × 10⁻¹² to 8.7 × 10⁻¹² m² s⁻¹ and showed a clear dependence on grain boundary area per unit volume as determined from plan-view TEM. Activation energy for permeation was 0.53 eV, close to the previously reported migration barrier for oxygen at ZnO grain boundaries. The ratio of boundary diffusivity to bulk grain diffusivity was estimated at approximately 40:1. These values provide direct input parameters for finite-element models of sensor response dynamics. No photocatalytic pre-treatment was applied, ensuring measurements reflect the native polycrystalline state.

title: Grain boundary engineering in WO₃ films for selective ppb-level detection of nitrogen dioxide
abstract: Tungsten trioxide films were fabricated by reactive sputtering at varying oxygen partial pressures and subsequently annealed in the range 400–600 °C to tune grain boundary density. The number density of grain boundaries along a 1 µm cross-section was counted from HRTEM micrographs and varied between 6 and 22 µm⁻¹. Sensor response to NO₂ at 100–800 ppb was measured in a flow-through cell at 200 °C. Films with 18–22 grain boundaries µm⁻¹ exhibited a response factor of 310 ± 25 at 200 ppb NO₂ with a detection limit of approximately 15 ppb (signal-to-noise ratio 3). Cross-sensitivity to 1 ppm CO, 1 ppm H₂S, and 50% RH humidity was below 8% in all cases. Post-exposure XPS confirmed no irreversible surface nitration. The grain boundary density parameter is proposed as a practical optimisation handle for WO₃-based NO₂ sensors without the need for noble-metal surface decoration.

title: Sub-ppm formaldehyde detection with In₂O₃ thin films: role of film porosity and operating temperature
abstract: Indium oxide films were deposited by pulsed DC sputtering at substrate temperatures of 25–300 °C, producing a range of columnar-to-equiaxed microstructures quantified by image analysis of cross-sectional SEM micrographs. Open porosity fraction varied from 3.1% to 19.4% as substrate temperature decreased. Formaldehyde response was characterised at 0.1–2 ppm in synthetic air at 45% RH and operating temperatures of 250–400 °C. The highest response to 0.5 ppm HCHO (response factor 6.8) was observed for the most porous film at 300 °C operating temperature, with a calculated detection limit of 80 ppb. Impedance spectroscopy in the frequency range 1 Hz–1 MHz was used to separate bulk grain, grain boundary, and electrode contributions to total resistance. Grain boundary resistance accounted for 71–83% of total sensor resistance in all samples, confirming its dominant role in transduction. Response time was below 20 s at 300 °C.

title: Quantifying the contribution of grain boundaries to VOC chemiresistive response using focused ion beam tomography
abstract: Focused ion beam serial sectioning combined with scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM tomography) was applied to SnO₂ films to reconstruct three-dimensional grain boundary networks in volumes of approximately 1 µm³. Five samples with systematically varied annealing temperatures (300–700 °C) were analysed, yielding grain boundary area densities between 0.6 and 4.1 µm⁻¹. The three-dimensional grain boundary network was correlated with steady-state chemiresistive response to 0.5 ppm acetone measured at 350 °C. A linear relationship (R² = 0.94) was found between grain boundary area density and log(Ra/Rg), supporting a parallel-conduction pathway model. Additionally, the tortuosity of the conduction percolation path through grain interiors was estimated from the tomographic data and showed no significant correlation with response, indicating boundary rather than bulk transport controls sensitivity at this analyte concentration. The FIB-SEM approach is proposed as a routine characterisation tool for sensor microstructure optimisation.

title: Drift characterisation of metal-oxide sensors under continuous operation: a 14-month field study in a grain storage facility
abstract: Four chemiresistive sensor nodes, each containing SnO₂ and WO₃ elements, were deployed in a wheat storage facility near Novi Sad and logged continuously from April 2020 to June 2021. Baseline resistance drift and sensitivity change were tracked against temperature and humidity co-variates recorded at 10-minute intervals. Mean annual baseline drift was +12.4% for SnO₂ and +7.1% for WO₃ elements. Sensitivity loss to ethanol (periodically injected at 1 ppm for calibration) was 18% over the 14-month period for SnO₂ and 9% for WO₃. Post-deployment XPS analysis of harvested sensor elements showed an increase in sulphate and carbonate surface species consistent with adsorption of SO₂ and CO₂ from the storage atmosphere. A drift-compensation algorithm based on baseline resistance ratio between co-located sensors reduced residual ethanol reading error from ±23% to ±7%. The study provides field-realistic numbers for sensor lifetime modelling in agri-food environments.

title: Effect of grain boundary passivation by low-dose fluorine implantation on the cross-sensitivity of SnO₂ to water vapour
abstract: Fluorine ions were implanted into polycrystalline SnO₂ films at doses of 1 × 10¹³ to 5 × 10¹⁵ cm⁻² at 30 keV, followed by recovery annealing at 300 °C. Secondary ion mass spectrometry profiles confirmed fluorine accumulation at grain boundary regions at all doses. Impedance spectroscopy before and after implantation showed a selective increase in grain boundary capacitance consistent with partial passivation of surface hydroxyl sites. Cross-sensitivity to water vapour at 30–70% RH was reduced by 44% at the optimal dose (5 × 10¹⁴ cm⁻²) with only a 12% reduction in ethanol response factor at 1 ppm. High-dose samples (5 × 10¹⁵ cm⁻²) showed structural damage evidenced by increased X-ray diffraction peak broadening and a 60% drop in ethanol sensitivity, indicating an upper limit for this approach. The results suggest selective grain boundary surface modification as a route to improve humidity rejection without a physical barrier layer.

title: Finite element simulation of gas diffusion through polycrystalline SnO₂ films: sensitivity of steady-state response to grain boundary diffusivity ratio
abstract: A two-dimensional finite element model of gas permeation and surface reaction in polycrystalline SnO₂ was implemented in open-source software to examine how the ratio of grain boundary diffusivity to bulk grain diffusivity (DB/DG) affects predicted steady-state chemiresistive response at analyte concentrations of 0.1–5 ppm. Microstructure input was derived from experimentally measured grain size distributions (log-normal, mean diameter 14 nm, σ = 3.1 nm). Simulations were run for DB/DG ratios of 1, 10, 25, 50, and 100 at three operating temperatures (300, 350, 400 °C). Predicted response factors for ethanol differed by up to a factor of 4.2 across the DB/DG range, demonstrating that this parameter dominates uncertainty in model predictions more than grain size polydispersity. The 25:1 ratio gave best agreement with experimentally measured response-concentration curves obtained on the same film batch. Sensitivity analysis also showed that the grain size standard deviation had a secondary effect, contributing less than 15% to response variance across the studied range.

title: Correlation between grain boundary character distribution and VOC sensitivity across a combinatorial SnO₂–TiO₂ thin-film library
abstract: A combinatorial co-sputtering approach was used to deposit a 64-point SnO₂–TiO₂ composition gradient library across a 100 mm wafer, spanning 0–100 at.% TiO₂. Composition was mapped by wavelength-dispersive X-ray fluorescence; crystal structure by microfocused XRD. Grain boundary character distribution was characterised by electron backscatter diffraction at 16 representative compositions. VOC sensitivity was measured in a custom addressable array test cell at 1 ppm isopropanol and 1 ppm hexanal at 350 °C. The highest isopropanol response (factor 9.3) was found near 15 at.% TiO₂ and correlated with a high fraction (38%) of low-angle grain boundaries (misorientation < 15°). Hexanal response showed a less systematic trend but peaked near 30 at.% TiO₂. Rutile TiO₂-rich compositions above 70 at.% showed negligible response. The dataset is provided as supplementary material and is intended to serve as a microstructure–property reference for mixed-oxide sensor design.

title: Synchronisation error accumulation in multi-hop sensor networks for perishable goods tracking
abstract: Clock drift in multi-hop wireless sensor networks causes timestamp misalignment that complicates post-hoc attribution of thermal excursions to specific logistics events such as loading, unloading, or border crossings. This paper quantifies drift accumulation in a five-hop 802.15.4 network over 72-hour transport trials. Forty trials were conducted using nodes with 16 MHz crystal oscillators, and drift was measured against a GPS-disciplined reference. Without resynchronisation, median timestamp error reached 4.3 seconds per hop per 24 hours, producing attribution errors of up to 22 seconds for five-hop paths. A lightweight flooding-based resynchronisation protocol executed every 30 minutes reduced median error to 0.18 seconds. The protocol adds 1.2% to total radio-on time. The paper discusses implications for traceability records submitted under EU Regulation 37/2005 on continuous temperature monitoring of frozen foods.

title: Aerosol-jet printing of bismuth film electrodes for differential pulse anodic stripping voltammetry of heavy metals in water
abstract: Bismuth film electrodes were fabricated by aerosol-jet printing of a bismuth oxide nanoparticle ink followed by electrochemical reduction in 0.1 M acetate buffer. Printed bismuth loading was varied between 8 and 45 µg·cm⁻² by adjusting the number of overprinted layers. Differential pulse anodic stripping voltammetry was used to determine cadmium(II) and lead(II) simultaneously in river water samples spiked at 10–200 µg·L⁻¹. The optimum film (28 µg·cm⁻² Bi) yielded detection limits of 1.2 µg·L⁻¹ for Cd²⁺ and 0.9 µg·L⁻¹ for Pb²⁺, with recoveries of 97–103% in Danube water matrix. Interferent screening showed no significant signal suppression at 10-fold excess of Cu²⁺, Fe³⁺, or Zn²⁺. The electrode produced 220 scans before performance degradation exceeded 5%, supporting its use as a quasi-disposable device.

title: Dielectric ink selection for inkjet-printed electrode insulation layers: compatibility with water-based conductive inks and mechanical flexibility
abstract: Four commercial UV-curable dielectric inks (designated D1–D4) were evaluated as insulation layers over inkjet-printed silver tracks on PET foil. Adhesion (cross-cut, ISO 2409), dielectric breakdown voltage, crack onset strain during bending (5–40 mm mandrel diameter), and ion permeability (EIS in 0.1 M NaCl) were measured. D2 and D3 exhibited breakdown voltages above 40 V·µm⁻¹ and withstood 1000 bending cycles at 10 mm radius without cracking. Ion permeability at 1 kHz was below 10 nS for both, qualifying them for electrochemical sensor encapsulation. Silver migration through the dielectric was tracked by XPS depth profiling after 72 h immersion in artificial sweat; D3 showed no detectable silver in the outermost 50 nm. The study provides a selection protocol directly applicable to roll-to-roll fabrication lines.

title: Aerosol-jet printing of semiconducting metal oxide layers for chemiresistive gas sensors on flexible substrates
abstract: Tin oxide (SnO₂) and zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticle inks were formulated and deposited by aerosol-jet printing on alumina and flexible polyimide substrates carrying interdigitated gold electrodes. Layer thickness (100–900 nm, controlled by number of passes) and post-deposition annealing temperature (200–450 °C on alumina; 200–300 °C on polyimide) were systematically varied. Chemiresistive response to ethanol, acetone, and NO₂ was measured at sensor operating temperatures of 200–350 °C achieved by an integrated printed heater. On alumina, SnO₂ at 300 °C operating temperature gave response ratios (R_air/R_gas) of 18 for 50 ppm ethanol and 4.2 for 5 ppm NO₂. On polyimide, maximum operating temperature was limited to 250 °C, reducing ethanol response to 7 but maintaining sensor function through 200 thermal cycles without delamination. The work demonstrates that aerosol-jet printed metal oxide layers are viable for flexible gas sensing, albeit with reduced sensitivity compared to high-temperature-sintered counterparts.

title: Piecewise Linear Approximation for Sensor Data Reduction on 8-bit Microcontrollers
abstract: This paper presents a piecewise linear approximation (PLA) scheme implemented on an ATmega328P microcontroller targeting temperature and humidity sensor streams in building automation scenarios. The algorithm segments incoming data into variable-length intervals whose endpoints are stored, discarding intermediate samples when the reconstruction error stays below a user-defined threshold. We evaluated performance on 72 hours of real sensor logs sampled at 1 Hz, achieving compression ratios between 8:1 and 14:1 at a maximum absolute reconstruction error of 0.4 °C. Flash footprint was kept below 3.2 kB and average processing time per sample was 11 µs at 16 MHz. The scheme is compared against a fixed-rate decimation baseline and a simple dead-band filter; PLA consistently produces smaller payloads while maintaining tighter error bounds. Energy consumption during the compression stage was measured at 1.7 µJ per sample using a shunt-resistor current monitor. The results suggest that PLA is a practical first-stage compression step before MQTT transmission in low-power mesh networks.

title: A Comparative Study of Delta Encoding Variants for Industrial Vibration Signals on ARM Cortex-M3
abstract: Industrial vibration monitoring generates high-rate accelerometer data that must often be stored or transmitted by nodes with limited SRAM. We implemented five delta-encoding variants — first-order delta, second-order delta, delta with Golomb-Rice coding, delta with run-length extension, and an adaptive-threshold delta — on an STM32F103 microcontroller and tested them against a 48-hour dataset of bearing vibration signals sampled at 4 kHz from a conveyor drive unit. Each algorithm was profiled for compression ratio, signal-to-noise ratio of reconstructed waveforms, processing cycles per sample, and peak SRAM usage. Adaptive-threshold delta achieved the best compression ratio of 3.8:1 while retaining impact-event peaks within 2.1 dB SNR of the original. SRAM overhead across all variants ranged from 128 bytes to 640 bytes. Cycle counts varied from 6 to 41 per sample. The paper provides decision guidelines for selecting a variant based on spectral content and memory budget.

title: Adaptive Nyquist-Rate Reduction Using Signal Variance Tracking for Low-Power Acoustic Sensors
abstract: This work addresses the energy cost of continuous acoustic sensing in wildlife monitoring nodes powered by solar-harvesting supercapacitors. We propose a variance-tracking scheduler that estimates short-time variance in 20 ms windows and dynamically reduces the effective sampling rate from 16 kHz to as low as 2 kHz during low-activity periods, restoring full rate when variance exceeds a learned threshold. The threshold is updated via an exponential moving average with a decay constant tuned to avoid false rate reductions during transient silence. Experiments were conducted with a custom node based on an MSP430FR5969 microcontroller and a MEMS microphone deployed in a mixed forest environment for 14 days. Compared to continuous 16 kHz sampling, the adaptive scheme reduced flash write volume by 73% and cut average current draw from 4.1 mA to 1.4 mA, extending estimated node lifetime from 11 days to 31 days without missing a single detected bird call event. Spectral fidelity during active periods was indistinguishable from the full-rate baseline.

title: Anomaly-Preserving Lossy Compression: Retaining Fault Signatures Under High Compression Ratios
abstract: Standard rate-distortion optimisation treats all signal samples equally, which can erase rare fault-indicative spikes at high compression ratios. This paper formalises the concept of anomaly-preserving compression (APC) for industrial sensor streams and proposes a two-stage pipeline: an online anomaly scorer based on a lightweight CUSUM detector flags candidate segments, and a segment-aware bit allocator assigns additional bits to flagged regions. The allocator operates within a fixed total bit budget so that overall compression ratio is unchanged. We tested APC on synthetic bearing-fault accelerometer traces (1000 trials per fault type) and on 60 hours of real motor current signals from a pump station. At a 12:1 target compression ratio, standard DPCM missed 31% of injected fault events, whereas APC missed 4.2% under identical bit constraints. The computational overhead of the anomaly scorer was 9 CPU cycles per sample on a Cortex-M4 at 168 MHz. The paper also provides an analytical bound relating CUSUM detection lag to false-anomaly rate.

title: Fixed-Point FFT Optimisation for Spectral Feature Extraction on Cortex-M4 Without FPU
abstract: Many mid-range microcontrollers include an FPU-equipped Cortex-M4, yet FPU use in battery-constrained nodes is often disabled to save power. This paper details the design of a 256-point radix-2 Cooley-Tukey FFT using Q15 fixed-point arithmetic without FPU instructions. We compare three twiddle-factor storage strategies — full table, quarter-wave compression, and on-the-fly CORDIC — for their trade-offs between SRAM, ROM, and cycle count. Full-table FFT executes in 4,912 cycles at negligible numerical error (SNR 78 dB); CORDIC reduces ROM by 2 kB but costs 9,340 cycles. The implementation was used in a vibration-based tool-wear classifier where six spectral band energies serve as features. Classification accuracy on a 400-sample dataset of milling operations was 91.3% using a lookup-table nearest-centroid classifier consuming 1.2 kB RAM. Total feature extraction and classification latency was 0.31 ms, making real-time 1 kHz inference feasible.

title: Lightweight Dictionary Coding for Repetitive Telemetry Payloads in LPWAN Networks
abstract: Low-power wide-area networks such as LoRaWAN impose strict payload size limits (typically 51 bytes in Europe at SF12) that force aggressive data reduction. Many agricultural IoT deployments generate highly repetitive soil-sensor payloads where values change slowly. We exploit this repetitiveness by implementing an LZ78-inspired dictionary coder with a bounded dictionary of 64 entries stored in 512 bytes of SRAM on an ATtiny3217. Across a 90-day deployment monitoring soil moisture, temperature, and electrical conductivity at four depths in a maize field, the coder achieved a mean payload reduction of 58% relative to raw quantised integers, enabling SF9 transmission and reducing time-on-air from 1.48 s to 0.62 s per burst. Monthly energy consumption fell by 34% compared to uncompressed transmission, extending estimated battery life from 14 months to 21 months. Decoding is performed server-side with negligible latency. The paper includes a simulation study covering payload entropy conditions where the scheme degrades gracefully to near-uncompressed size.

title: Resource Budget Modelling for Co-located Compression and Inference Tasks on RISC-V MCUs
abstract: When a sensor node must run both a data compressor and a machine-learning inference engine simultaneously, their memory and compute demands interact in non-obvious ways. This paper proposes a static resource budget model that takes as inputs the compressor's working-set size, the inference model's layer dimensions, and the microcontroller's SRAM/flash/cycle budget, and outputs a Pareto frontier of achievable compression ratio versus inference accuracy trade-offs. We instantiate the model for four compressor types (DPCM, PLA, Haar, dictionary) and three classifier sizes (16, 64, 256 parameters) on two RISC-V targets: GD32VF103 and ESP32-C3. Empirical validation on an air-quality monitoring workload (6 sensors, 1 Hz) shows the model predicts achieved compression ratio within ±7% and classification accuracy within ±2 percentage points across 48 configuration combinations. The paper also discusses memory-bank partitioning strategies that reduce SRAM contention between the two tasks by 23% without hardware modification.

title: Quantisation Error Propagation in Cascaded Lossy Compression Stages for Multi-Hop IoT Pipelines
abstract: In multi-hop sensor networks, data may be compressed at the originating node, partially decompressed and re-compressed at relay nodes, and finally decoded at a gateway. This paper analyses quantisation error accumulation across up to five cascade stages for three compressor families: scalar quantisation, vector quantisation, and transform coding. We derive recurrence relations for mean-square error under additive quantisation noise assumptions and validate these analytically against Monte Carlo simulations (10 000 runs per configuration) using synthetic AR(2) sensor traces. For scalar quantisation with uniform step size, error after five stages reaches 4.7 times the single-stage distortion; the proposed stage-aware bit-rate allocation, which front-loads precision to early hops, caps the same metric at 2.1 times. Practical guidelines are given for selecting per-hop quantisation step sizes given a gateway reconstruction target and a network energy budget. The paper includes a worked example for a three-hop soil moisture network consistent with LoRa hardware constraints.

title: TENT: A Tiny Entropy-Coded Transform for Ultra-Low-Power Sub-Threshold Microcontrollers
abstract: Sub-threshold microcontrollers operating at supply voltages below 0.5 V achieve pico-joule-per-cycle energy figures but impose extreme constraints on code size and arithmetic complexity. This paper introduces TENT, a lightweight integer transform followed by a two-symbol static Huffman coder, implemented entirely within 1.4 kB of flash and 256 bytes of SRAM on a custom ASIC test chip fabricated in 65 nm CMOS running at 50 kHz and 0.4 V. TENT applies a 4-point integer approximation to a discrete cosine transform using only additions and one-bit shifts, quantises coefficients with a three-level dead-zone quantiser, and encodes symbols using a precomputed 16-entry Huffman table stored in ROM. On temperature, pressure, and light sensor streams sampled at 0.1 Hz, TENT achieves compression ratios of 3.1:1 to 5.8:1 at per-sample energy of 48 pJ. The paper presents silicon measurement results alongside a software reference implementation validated on an ARM Cortex-M0+.

title: Effect of root branching morphology on extraction torque in robotic selective harvesting of parsnip
abstract: Parsnip roots exhibit pronounced lateral branching compared to carrot, and the additional anchorage provided by branch roots substantially increases resistance to rotational extraction strategies. This conference paper reports an experimental investigation into the relationship between branch root architecture and the torque required to rotate-and-pull a parsnip root free from sandy loam soil. Forty-eight parsnip specimens were CT-scanned prior to harvesting to quantify branch root count, mean branch angle, and total lateral root volume. Extraction was performed by a 6-DOF collaborative robot arm fitted with a compliant jaw gripper and a wrist-mounted ATI Gamma force/torque sensor. Three extraction trajectories were compared: pure axial pull, combined 30° helical rotation, and combined 60° helical rotation. Mean peak torques during 30° and 60° helical extraction were 0.38 N·m and 0.52 N·m respectively, compared with negligible torque in the axial condition. Linear regression showed that total lateral root volume was the strongest predictor of peak torque (R² = 0.71). The 30° helical trajectory achieved the best trade-off between reduced axial peak force and acceptable torque loading on the gripper mechanism.

title: Calibration of DEM contact parameters for wheat grain using a bulk angle-of-repose test
abstract: Accurate discrete-element modelling of grain assemblies requires well-calibrated contact parameters. This study presents a systematic calibration procedure for wheat grain using a hollow-cylinder collapse test to measure bulk angle of repose. Grain samples of three wheat cultivars (NS Renesansa, Pobeda, and Simonida) were characterised for size, shape, and surface properties using image analysis and friction measurement rigs. A factorial design varied the static friction coefficient (0.20–0.55), rolling friction coefficient (0.01–0.08), and coefficient of restitution (0.50–0.85) in EDEM 2018 simulations with 12 000 spherical and clumped-sphere grain proxies. Response surface regression identified static friction 0.38, rolling friction 0.04, and restitution 0.62 as the parameter set minimising the deviation between simulated (34.1°) and measured (33.8°) repose angles. Sensitivity analysis showed that rolling friction had the strongest influence on repose angle among the three parameters tested. The calibrated parameter set was validated against a separate inclined-plane sliding test, yielding less than 2% error. Results provide a baseline parameter database for subsequent combine harvester simulations using Serbian winter wheat varieties.

title: Simulation of grain separation on a flat oscillating sieve using the discrete element method
abstract: Grain cleaning units in combine harvesters rely on oscillating flat sieves to separate cleaned grain from chaff and short straw. This paper presents a two-dimensional DEM model of a flat sieve (800 mm × 450 mm, wire mesh, 8 mm aperture) oscillating at amplitudes of 40–80 mm and frequencies of 3.5–5.5 Hz. Particle assemblies of 5 000 spheres representing grain, chaff, and straw segments were simulated using LIGGGHTS with calibrated parameters from earlier laboratory work. Sieve throughput, stratification index, and grain loss below the sieve were recorded for each parameter combination. Increasing frequency from 3.5 to 5.5 Hz raised throughput by 18% but increased grain loss by 6.3 percentage points. An amplitude of 60 mm at 4.5 Hz yielded the best compromise, with a stratification index of 0.71 and grain loss under 1.5%. Predictions were compared against mass-balance measurements on a laboratory sieve rig, showing agreement within 4.2% for throughput and 8.1% for loss. The model provides a foundation for multi-sieve combine cleaner optimisation.

title: Effect of cylinder speed and concave clearance on threshing efficiency: a DEM parametric study
abstract: Threshing performance in a rasp-bar cylinder–concave unit is controlled primarily by peripheral cylinder speed and the clearance between the cylinder and the concave. A DEM model of a simplified rasp-bar threshing unit (cylinder diameter 600 mm, concave wrap angle 115°, 9 concave bars) was constructed in EDEM 2019. Wheat ear assemblies were represented by linked-sphere clusters connected with bonded particles to capture ear breakage. A total of 27 simulation cases combined cylinder speeds of 900, 1 100, and 1 300 rpm with concave clearances of 8, 12, and 18 mm and feed rates of 3, 5, and 7 kg/s. Threshing efficiency, grain damage rate, and power consumption were evaluated. Efficiency exceeded 98% at 1 300 rpm and 8 mm clearance but grain damage reached 4.1%. At 1 100 rpm and 12 mm clearance, efficiency was 96.8% and grain damage was 1.6%. Power consumption scaled approximately with the square of cylinder speed. Results agreed with field measurements from a commercial combine to within 5% for efficiency and 12% for damage, supporting use of the model for preliminary design studies.

title: Particle segregation in a grain elevator leg: measurements and DEM predictions
abstract: Bucket elevators used in grain storage facilities produce segregation patterns that affect sampling accuracy and blend uniformity. This study combined physical measurements in a pilot-scale elevator leg (height 3.2 m, bucket pitch 300 mm, belt speed 1.8 m/s) with DEM simulations to quantify size-induced segregation. A binary mixture of wheat grain (equivalent diameter 6.1 mm) and broken grain (diameter 3.2 mm) at mass fractions of 10%, 20%, and 30% broken was tested. Broken-grain concentration was measured at the spout discharge using sieve analysis of samples collected at 30-second intervals over 10-minute runs. DEM simulations used 25 000 particles and replicated belt geometry, bucket geometry, and discharge trajectory. The simulated discharge concentration of broken grain at the spout edge exceeded the inlet concentration by a factor of 1.7–2.1 depending on feed fraction, matching experimental ratios within 9%. The model correctly predicted that broken grain accumulated at the periphery of the discharge arc. These findings have direct implications for representative grain sampling at elevator discharge points.

title: Airflow–particle coupling in combine harvester cleaning units: a CFD–DEM approach
abstract: The combine harvester cleaning shoe uses an air blast from a fan to remove chaff from the grain–chaff mixture on the sieves. Capturing this process requires coupling computational fluid dynamics with DEM. A coupled CFD–DEM model was developed in OpenFOAM 4.1 and LIGGGHTS, representing a cleaning unit 1 200 mm long with upper and lower sieves and a centrifugal fan producing 0.9 m/s mean air velocity at the sieve inlet. Particle types included wheat grain, oat-hull proxies for chaff, and cylindrical segments for straw. The fan air velocity was varied from 0.6 to 1.4 m/s. At 0.9 m/s, 93% of chaff was entrained and discharged over the rear of the unit while grain loss was 0.8%. Increasing velocity to 1.2 m/s removed 99% of chaff but raised grain loss to 3.5%. Spatial maps of particle velocity and air–particle drag force distribution over the sieve surface were generated, showing a stagnation zone in the forward third of the lower sieve that accumulated dense chaff clumps. Validation against mass-fraction measurements at the shoe exit gave errors below 7% for all particle types.

title: DEM-based shape sensitivity analysis for soybean grain in auger conveyor simulations
abstract: Soybean grain differs from wheat in size, surface properties, and shape, requiring separate DEM characterisation. This paper examines how the choice of particle shape representation—single sphere, two-sphere clump, and four-sphere clump—affects predictions of auger conveyor throughput, power draw, and grain stress distributions. A horizontal auger conveyor (screw diameter 100 mm, pitch 95 mm, length 1 000 mm, rotational speed 400–700 rpm) was simulated with each shape model using EDEM 2021. Reference throughput and power measurements were collected on a laboratory conveyor with soybean of known moisture content (12–14% w.b.). The four-sphere clump representation reproduced throughput within 5% and power within 8% across all speeds, whereas the single-sphere model overestimated throughput by up to 19% and underestimated power by 21%. Grain stress distributions differed markedly: peak compressive stress in the single-sphere model was 38 kPa versus 62 kPa for the four-sphere model. The four-sphere clump was deemed the minimum adequate shape fidelity for soybean simulations, while single spheres may suffice for coarse throughput estimates where computational cost is a constraint.

title: High-speed imaging of grain trajectories in a rasp-bar threshing unit and comparison with DEM predictions
abstract: Validating DEM models of threshing units requires spatially resolved grain trajectory data. This study used two synchronised high-speed cameras (2 000 fps, 2 Mpx) installed behind a transparent polycarbonate side wall of a laboratory threshing unit to track individual grain centroids using blob-detection image analysis. A batch of 300 wheat grains dyed with fluorescent pigment was introduced at controlled feed rates of 1 and 3 kg/s at cylinder speeds of 900 and 1 200 rpm. Grain centroid positions were extracted at 0.5 ms intervals and converted to trajectories in the cylinder–concave gap. Corresponding EDEM 2021 simulations with 300 labelled particles reproduced the experimental setup. Trajectory matching was quantified using mean absolute deviation in position (1.8–4.3 mm at the 50th percentile) and residence time (simulated mean 87 ms vs. measured 91 ms at 1 100 rpm, 3 kg/s). Larger deviations occurred near rasp-bar impact events, suggesting that the rigid-bonded cluster model underestimates the rotational impulse transferred to the grain. Recommended model improvements include polyhedral bar geometry and a compliant rasp surface.

title: Size segregation of maize grain mixtures on combine harvester sieves: DEM study with polydisperse assemblies
abstract: Maize grain harvested from multi-variety plots or with uneven kernel fill presents a polydisperse particle assembly on the cleaning sieve. This study used DEM to investigate how coefficient of variation (CV) in grain size affects stratification and loss on a two-sieve cleaning unit. Log-normal size distributions with CVs of 5%, 15%, and 25% were generated for assemblies of 15 000 maize grain proxies (mean equivalent diameter 9.8 mm) and simulated on upper and lower sieves oscillating at 4.8 Hz, 55 mm amplitude. Particle tracking across five consecutive oscillation cycles revealed that large grains migrated to the top layer two cycles earlier when CV was 25% compared with 5%, with a stratification index increasing from 0.64 to 0.81. Grain loss through the sieve decreased paradoxically from 2.4% at CV 5% to 1.1% at CV 25% because large grains blocked apertures. Mean residence time on the upper sieve decreased by 14% at high CV. These findings suggest that combine harvester cleaning settings should be adjusted when harvesting seeds with non-uniform size distributions to avoid plugging of sieve apertures.

title: Wear prediction in concave bars of a combine harvester threshing unit using DEM-derived contact force maps
abstract: Concave bar wear limits the service life of threshing units and alters the gap geometry over time, affecting threshing efficiency. This paper describes a methodology in which DEM simulation of a full-scale axial threshing unit (rotor diameter 460 mm, concave wrap angle 130°, rotor length 1 550 mm) was used to generate contact force density maps on each concave bar. Simulations were run for wheat at 1 050 rpm rotor speed, 12 mm concave clearance, and 5 kg/s feed rate over a virtual duration of 2 s, producing 4 200 concave bar contact events per second. A Archard wear model was applied post-processing to the force maps to estimate local material removal rate, using a wear coefficient measured in a pin-on-disk tribometer for a St52 steel–wheat grain pair (k = 3.1 × 10−14 m² N−1). Predicted wear profiles after 500 operating hours showed maximum depth of 2.3 mm at the leading edge of the third concave bar, consistent with the pattern found by measuring worn bars taken from a commercial combine. The approach enables estimation of component replacement intervals without instrumented field trials.

title: Reducing grain losses in combine harvester cleaning units through sieve geometry optimisation: a DEM-based parametric study
abstract: Grain loss over the rear of the cleaning sieve accounts for a significant fraction of total combine harvester field losses. This paper reports a DEM-based design study aimed at reducing rear grain loss by varying three sieve geometry parameters: aperture size (7–11 mm), louver angle (15°–35° from horizontal), and sieve length (800–1 200 mm). A full factorial design with three levels per factor (27 combinations) was simulated using a coupled CFD–DEM model with 18 000 wheat grain and 9 000 chaff particles at constant fan speed (1 450 rpm) and oscillation parameters. Grain loss was defined as the mass fraction of grain exiting over the rear edge. The lowest grain loss (0.6%) was obtained with 9 mm aperture, 25° louver angle, and 1 100 mm sieve length. Analysis of variance confirmed that aperture size was the dominant factor (52% of total variance), followed by sieve length (28%). A quadratic response surface model fitted R² = 0.94 for grain loss, enabling rapid evaluation of intermediate design points. The study provides a practical framework for sieve geometry selection without recourse to costly prototype testing.

title: Towards real-time DEM-based monitoring of threshing quality: a reduced-order model approach
abstract: Full-scale DEM simulations of combine harvester threshing units require hours of computation time on multi-core workstations, precluding real-time use in machine monitoring or adaptive control. This preprint describes a reduced-order modelling approach in which a database of 216 full DEM simulations spanning the design space of cylinder speed (800–1 400 rpm), concave clearance (8–20 mm), and feed rate (3–9 kg/s) was used to train a Gaussian process regression surrogate. The surrogate predicts threshing efficiency, grain damage rate, and specific energy consumption with leave-one-out cross-validation errors of 0.9%, 0.7 percentage points, and 4.2%, respectively. Inference time per query is under 2 ms on a laptop CPU, making the surrogate feasible for embedding in a combine harvester controller. A prototype integration with a simulated CAN bus feed from virtual cylinder speed and feed-rate sensors is described. The approach is validated against 18 additional DEM simulations not included in the training set, achieving maximum absolute error of 2.3% for efficiency and 1.1 percentage points for damage. Limitations related to crop variety variation and out-of-distribution operating conditions are discussed.

title: Friction coefficient measurement at the soil–steel interface: a method comparison using pin-on-disk and linear-reciprocating geometries
abstract: Standardised measurement of soil–steel friction is hindered by the absence of agreed test geometry and soil preparation protocols. This study compared friction coefficients obtained using a pin-on-disk configuration (20 mm diameter steel pin, 90 mm soil-filled disk, 60 rpm) and a linear-reciprocating tribometer (flat coupon, 30 mm stroke, 0.05 m/s) for three steels (mild steel, 28MnB5, and WC-CoCr coated) against three repacked soil specimens (sand, loam, clay-loam) at two compaction levels (1.3 and 1.6 g/cm³ bulk density). Friction coefficients from pin-on-disk were systematically 0.04–0.11 higher than from reciprocating tests for the same steel–soil pair, with the largest discrepancy in clay-loam. The effect of bulk density was larger in sand (Δµ ≈ 0.08) than in clay-loam (Δµ ≈ 0.02). Repeatability (CV < 8% within-geometry) was acceptable for both setups. The paper proposes a minimum reporting checklist — soil moisture, bulk density, particle-size distribution, compaction procedure — to improve inter-laboratory comparability.

title: Comparison of Hazen–Williams and Darcy–Weisbach friction equations for small-diameter polyethylene drip laterals
abstract: The choice of friction-loss equation affects the accuracy of hydraulic design calculations for small-diameter polyethylene laterals commonly used in drip irrigation. This paper reports laboratory measurements of head loss in 16 mm and 20 mm nominal polyethylene tubes at flow velocities between 0.1 and 1.8 m/s, covering the transition and turbulent regimes. Roughness values were estimated by fitting Colebrook–White solutions to measured friction factors. The Darcy–Weisbach equation with a fitted roughness of 0.0015 mm reproduced measured head losses within 2.1% across the full velocity range. The Hazen–Williams equation with C = 150 underestimated losses by up to 9.4% at velocities above 1.2 m/s and overestimated by 6.1% below 0.3 m/s. The commonly used 150 C-factor is therefore not uniformly conservative for drip lateral design. Revised C-factor recommendations are proposed for three velocity sub-ranges to allow continued use of the simpler Hazen–Williams framework without excessive error.

title: Praćenje prirodnog slabljenja tetrahloretilena u nezasićenoj zoni aluvijalnog sedimenta: trogodišnja terenska studija
abstract: U radu su prikazani rezultati trogodišnjeg monitoringa prirodnog slabljenja tetrahloretilena (PCE) na industrijskom lokalitetu u blizini Novog Sada, sa aluvijalnim sedimentom kao dominantnim geološkim okruženjem. Na mreži od 24 monitorska bunara i 6 profilnih tačaka u nezasićenoj zoni praćene su koncentracije PCE, trikloretilena (TCE), cis-1,2-dihloretilena (cDCE) i vinil-hlorida (VC) u parnoj fazi i kapilarnoj vodi. Tokom posmatranog perioda zabeleženo je smanjenje masene bilanse PCE od 38% uz istovremeno povećanje udela cDCE, što ukazuje na biostimulisanu reduktivnu dihloraciju. Vrednosti δ¹³C merene metodom CSIA porasle su od −27,4‰ do −19,1‰ duž transportnog puta, konzistentne sa faktorom obogaćenja ε = −5,8‰ za TCE. Rezultati su upoređeni sa laboratorijskim mikrokosmos eksperimentima koji su potvrdili aktivnost dihlorisposobivih bakterija Dehalococcoides spp. Studija demonstrira primenjivost CSIA kao kvantitativnog alata za procenu napretka MNA na lokalitetima sa složenom stratigrafijom.

title: Zero-valent iron permeable reactive barriers for TCE reduction in shallow unsaturated profiles: column experiments
abstract: Laboratory column experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of zero-valent iron (ZVI) granules (particle size 0.5–2 mm, surface area 1.8 m² g⁻¹) for reductive dechlorination of trichloroethylene (TCE) under partially saturated conditions mimicking a shallow vadose zone. Columns of 80 cm length were packed with a 15 cm ZVI reactive zone embedded in sandy loam. Influent TCE concentrations ranged from 50 to 400 µg L⁻¹ in aqueous phase; gas-phase flux was maintained at 2.0 L h⁻¹ to simulate seasonal soil-gas advection. TCE removal efficiencies of 87–93% were achieved at hydraulic retention times of 4 h, producing primarily ethylene (64%) and ethane (21%) with minor cis-DCE (8%). Carbon isotope enrichment factors measured by CSIA were −14.2 ± 0.9‰, consistent with a β-elimination mechanism. Reactivity declined by approximately 22% over 180 days, attributed to surface passivation by carbonate precipitation confirmed by SEM-EDX. Results indicate that ZVI barriers can be effective even under fluctuating moisture content, though long-term performance requires periodic geochemical management.

title: Procena rizika od isparavanja hlorovanih rastvarača iz nezasićene zone ka unutrašnjim prostorijama na lokalitetima hemijske industrije u Vojvodini
abstract: Rad prikazuje metodologiju i rezultate procene rizika od migracije para hlorovanih rastvarača (uglavnom TCE i PCE) iz kontaminirane nezasićene zone ka unutrašnjim prostorijama na tri industrijska lokaliteta u Vojvodini. Primenjen je kombinovani pristup koji podrazumeva terensko merenje koncentracija u parnoj fazi (0,3–4,5 m dubine), modelovanje transporta u vadoznoj zoni pomoću programa VaporPro v2.1 i poređenje sa referentnim vrednostima za inhalacioni rizik prema EPA RSL tabelama. Na dva od tri lokaliteta izmerene koncentracije u unutrašnjem vazduhu premašivale su ciljne vrednosti za TCE (2,7 µg m⁻³), s vrednostima od 4,1 i 6,8 µg m⁻³ respektivno. Analiza osetljivosti pokazala je da debljina kapilarne zone i propusnost poda objekata dominantno kontrolišu prenos mase. Preporučene su mere aktivne remedijacije vadozne zone i ugradnja pasivnih ventilacionih sistema u skladu sa srpskim propisima (Uredba o programu sistematskog praćenja kvaliteta zemljišta, Sl. glasnik RS 88/2010). Rezultati su prikazani i resornom ministarstvu u okviru stručne saradnje.

title: Primena emulzifikovanog nula-valentnog gvožđa za in situ hemijsku redukciju TCE u nezasićenoj zoni: pilot test na vojvođanskom lokalitetu
abstract: Pilot test primene emulzifikovanog nula-valentnog gvožđa (EZVI) za in situ hemijsku redukciju (ISCR) TCE sproveden je na lokalitetu bivše hemijske fabrike u okolini Zrenjanina. Injektovano je 340 kg EZVI suspenzije kroz šest injekcionih tačaka raspoređenih na mreži 3×3 m, u dubinskom opsegu 1,5–4,5 m. Monitoring je uključivao merenje koncentracija hloretilena u parnoj fazi, redoks potencijala i temperature, kao i CSIA analizu δ¹³C. Dvanaest meseci nakon injektovanja, prosečne koncentracije TCE smanjene su za 74%, dok je povećanje udela vinil-hlorida (do 15 µg m⁻³) ukazivalo na nepotpunu dihloraciju u perifernim zonama. Vrednosti δ¹³C TCE porasle su za 6,2‰ u centru tretiranog volumena, potvrđujući hemijsko-biološku razgradnju. Uočena je heterogenost distribucije EZVI uslovljena promenljivom teksturom sedimenta. Preporučena je dopunska bioaugmentacija Dehalococcoides kultura za neutralizaciju vinil-hloridnog intermedijera.

title: Geochemical controls on reductive dechlorination efficiency across textural gradients in the unsaturated zone
abstract: This study examined how lithological heterogeneity within a multi-layered vadose zone affects the efficiency of reductive dechlorination of PCE and TCE at a contaminated site in the Pannonian Basin. Undisturbed core samples from silty clay, loamy sand, and fine sand horizons were used to set up 18 anaerobic microcosm incubations. Dechlorination rates were fastest in fine sand (first-order rate constant k = 0.042 d⁻¹) and slowest in silty clay (k = 0.007 d⁻¹). Organic carbon content (0.4–3.1%) and pH (6.8–7.6) were the strongest predictors of rate variability in a multiple regression model (R² = 0.81). Correlation of rate constants with ε¹³C values showed that isotope fractionation was suppressed under diffusion-limited conditions in clay-dominated layers, complicating field-scale CSIA mass balance calculations. A correction factor based on effective diffusivity was proposed and validated against field data from two monitoring transects. The findings have direct implications for the design of isotope-based monitoring programs at heterogeneous vadose zone sites.

title: Monitoring and natural attenuation of vinyl chloride in vadose zone gas: a field and laboratory study from three Central European sites
abstract: Vinyl chloride (VC) is a carcinogenic terminal product of incomplete PCE/TCE dechlorination and is frequently under-monitored in unsaturated zone remediation programs. This paper presents integrated field and laboratory results from three contaminated industrial sites in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania where VC accumulation in soil gas was documented. Soil gas surveys at depths of 0.5–5 m recorded VC concentrations between 12 and 310 µg m⁻³. Microcosm experiments conducted under aerobic conditions using site soils demonstrated rapid VC biodegradation (k = 0.18–0.31 d⁻¹) attributable to ethene-oxidising bacteria identified by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Carbon isotope enrichment factors for aerobic VC oxidation ranged from −8.3 to −9.7‰ across the three soil types. A simplified mass balance model combining field gas flux measurements, microcosm rate data, and CSIA enrichment factors estimated natural attenuation capacity sufficient to prevent indoor air guideline exceedance at two of the three sites under current boundary conditions. The third site required supplementary active ventilation of the vadose zone.

title: Odabir reagensa za in situ hemijsku redukciju hlorovanih rastvarača: komparativna laboratorijska studija EZVI, nanočestičnog ZVI i kalcijum-polisulfida
abstract: Komparativna laboratorijska studija evaluirala je efikasnost tri komercijalna reagensa za in situ hemijsku redukciju (ISCR) hlorovanih rastvarača: emulzifikovanog nula-valentnog gvožđa (EZVI), nanočestičnog ZVI (nZVI) i kalcijum-polisulfida (CPS), pri primeni u peskovito-ilovastom tlu kontaminiranom smešom PCE i TCE (inicijalne koncentracije 480 i 620 µg kg⁻¹, respektivno). Batch eksperimenti sa 200 g uzoraka tla sprovođeni su 90 dana pri 15°C. Uklanjanje PCE iznosilo je 91% (nZVI), 85% (EZVI) i 43% (CPS), a TCE 88% (nZVI), 82% (EZVI) i 38% (CPS). Nasuprot tome, nZVI je izazvao najizraženije povećanje pH (do 9,4) i smanjenje mikrobiološke aktivnosti za 67%, merene dehydrogenaza testom. EZVI je postigao bolji balans između hemijske efikasnosti i očuvanja mikrobiočke zajednice, što je od značaja za kombinirane ISCR–MNA pristupe. CPS se pokazao nedovoljno efikasnim pri ispitanim uslovima vlažnosti tla (Θ = 0,22 cm³ cm⁻³).

title: Influence of soil moisture fluctuations on carbon isotope fractionation during TCE vapour-phase transport in the vadose zone
abstract: The effect of periodic wetting and drying cycles on carbon isotope fractionation of trichloroethylene (TCE) during vapour-phase transport was investigated using laboratory soil columns (1.2 m length, sandy loam texture) subjected to four simulated rainfall events over 120 days. Wetting front advancement was tracked with time-domain reflectometry probes and tensiometers; TCE vapour flux and δ¹³C were measured at the top boundary by GC-IRMS. During drainage phases, δ¹³C values in the exiting vapour were lighter by 1.0–1.6‰ relative to source values, consistent with partial re-dissolution into mobile capillary water. During drying phases, isotopically heavier vapour was mobilised as residual NAPL volatilised. A reactive transport model incorporating moisture-dependent Henry's law partitioning reproduced the observed δ¹³C variability with a root mean square error of 0.9‰. These results indicate that moisture dynamics must be accounted for when interpreting field CSIA data in shallow vadose zones subject to seasonal recharge.

title: Razvoj protokola za terenska merenja CSIA u parnoj fazi nezasićene zone: upoređivanje pasivnog uzorkovanja i aktivnog pumpanja
abstract: Rad razmatra metodološke aspekte terenske primene izotopske analize specifičnih jedinjenja (CSIA) u parnoj fazi nezasićene zone, poređenjem dve tehnike uzorkovanja: pasivnih difuzionih uzorkivača (GORE-Sorb tip) i aktivnog pumpanja sa Tenax TA adsorbentima. Na sedam monitorskih lokacija na kontaminiranom industrijskom terenu u centralnoj Srbiji, uzorkovanje je sprovedeno u tri navrata tokom jedne godine. Pasivna metoda pokazala je sistematsko potcenjivanje δ¹³C vrednosti za 0,8–1,4‰ u poređenju sa aktivnim pumpanjem, najverovatnije usled izotopskog efekta pri adsorpciji na difuzionim membranama. Preciznost ponovnog uzorkovanja bila je bolja kod aktivnog pumpanja (σ = 0,3‰ nasuprot 0,7‰). Utvrđene su preporuke za minimalne zapremine uzorka (≥4 L za aktivno pumpanje) i trajanje ekspozicije (≥14 dana za pasivno uzorkovanje) kojima se postiže pouzdana CSIA merenja pri koncentracijama TCE ispod 50 µg m⁻³. Protokol je prilagođen za rutinsku primenu u okviru srpskog regulatornog okvira.

title: Combined ISCR and monitored natural attenuation for PCE source zone treatment: five-year performance assessment at a textile industry site
abstract: A five-year post-treatment assessment of a combined in-situ chemical reduction (ISCR) and monitored natural attenuation (MNA) strategy is reported for a PCE source zone at a decommissioned textile dyeing facility in Vojvodina. ISCR was implemented in 2016 using emulsified zero-valent iron injected across 220 m² of the vadose zone source area. Performance verification employed quarterly soil gas sampling for chlorinated ethene concentrations and CSIA (δ¹³C, δ³⁷Cl). Over five years, PCE mass in the vadose zone decreased from an estimated 38 kg to 9 kg based on soil gas concentration mapping and vapour flux modelling. The δ¹³C of TCE, the primary daughter product, increased from −26.1‰ to −17.8‰ longitudinally, confirming active degradation rather than dilution. Microbial community profiling by qPCR showed a ten-fold increase in Dehalococcoides cell counts in the lower vadose zone by year two, sustained through year five. A simple analytical model combining first-order decay rates derived from CSIA and mass balance estimates projected asymptotic cleanup to target concentrations within 12–15 additional years under MNA alone.

title: Bioaugmentation with Dehalococcoides-containing consortia as a complement to ISCR in chlorinated-solvent-impacted vadose zones: laboratory feasibility study
abstract: Laboratory feasibility experiments were conducted to assess whether bioaugmentation with a Dehalococcoides-enriched anaerobic consortium (designated DHC-NS22, isolated from a contaminated site in Serbia) could complement ISCR treatment and prevent vinyl chloride accumulation in the vadose zone. Soil columns (80 cm, silty sand, Θ = 0.28) were pre-treated with EZVI and then inoculated with DHC-NS22 at a density of 10⁷ cells g⁻¹ dry soil. After 60 days, VC concentrations in column effluent gas were 78% lower compared to ISCR-only controls, and ethylene production confirmed complete dechlorination. Cell survival under the partial saturation conditions was confirmed by qPCR targeting the vcrA gene. Temperature sensitivity tests showed that metabolic activity was preserved down to 8°C, relevant for shallow vadose zones in continental climates. Carbon isotope data for VC showed enrichment (ε¹³C = −22.3 ± 1.4‰) consistent with reductive dechlorination rather than aerobic oxidation. The results support field-scale bioaugmentation trials at sites where ISCR alone does not achieve complete dechlorination.

title: Primena trodimenzionalnog modela transporta para za optimizaciju mreže monitoringa u nezasićenoj zoni: studija slučaja sa vojvođanskog lokaliteta
abstract: Rad opisuje primenu numeričkog modela transporta para hlorovanih jedinjenja u tri dimenzije (programski paket VadoseSim 3.0) radi optimizacije prostornog rasporeda monitorske mreže na kompleksnom industrijskom lokalitetu. Model je kalibrisan na osnovu dvogodišnjih terenskih podataka o koncentracijama PCE i TCE u parnoj fazi i vrednostima δ¹³C iz 32 monitorske tačke. Kalibrisani model korišćen je za simulaciju 48 alternativnih konfiguracija monitorske mreže sa brojem tačaka od 8 do 24. Evaluacija je sprovedena upotrebom kriterijuma D-optimalnosti i maksimalne prediktivne greške. Optimizovana mreža od 14 tačaka postigla je isti nivo informacionog sadržaja kao polazna mreža od 32 tačke, uz smanjenje troškova monitoringa za 54%. Verifikacija na nezavisnom setu terenskih podataka pokazala je da optimizovana mreža pravilno klasifikuje trend remedijacije u 91% slučajeva. Pristup je prenosiv na lokalitete sa sličnom geološkom građom u Panonskom basenu.

title: Chlorine and carbon dual-isotope fractionation during abiotic PCE degradation by calcium polysulfide: implications for field monitoring
abstract: Dual-element isotope fractionation (δ¹³C and δ³⁷Cl) was measured during abiotic reductive dechlorination of PCE by calcium polysulfide (CPS) in controlled batch experiments at pH 7.5 and 9.0, temperatures of 12 and 20°C, and two CPS concentrations (0.5 and 2.0 g L⁻¹). Carbon enrichment factors ranged from −2.1 to −3.4‰ depending on conditions, with higher values at elevated pH and temperature. Chlorine enrichment factors were consistently small (−0.7 to −1.1‰), yielding dual-isotope slopes (Λ) of 2.8–3.6. This range overlaps partially with values reported for microbial hydrogenolysis, complicating process attribution in the field when both mechanisms coexist. A sensitivity analysis using a reactive transport model showed that dual-isotope monitoring at a minimum of three depth intervals is required to discriminate CPS-driven from biotic degradation with 90% confidence when source δ¹³C values are known. The dataset provides reference values for interpretation of CSIA data at CPS-treated sites, which currently lack published isotope benchmarks.

title: Spatial autocorrelation of bacterial community composition along a crop rotation transect in northern Vojvodina
abstract: We investigated whether bacterial community composition in agricultural topsoil exhibits detectable spatial autocorrelation along a 12-km transect crossing four rotation systems in northern Vojvodina. Soil cores were collected at 48 evenly spaced points in spring 2014. After DNA extraction and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (V3–V4 region, Illumina MiSeq, mean depth 28 400 reads per sample), OTU tables were constructed using QIIME 1.9. Empirical variograms were computed for three alpha-diversity indices (Shannon, Chao1, Faith's PD) and for the first two axes of a Bray–Curtis PCoA. Spherical variogram models fitted the Shannon and Chao1 series well, with range estimates of 1.8 km and 2.3 km respectively. Ordinary kriging maps showed a consistent diversity depression in a zone associated with intensive maize monoculture. Mantel tests confirmed significant isolation-by-distance effects (r = 0.41, p < 0.001). These results indicate that microbial diversity in Vojvodina croplands is structured at sub-kilometre scales relevant to precision agriculture management.

title: Comparison of kriging interpolators for predicting soil fungal richness from sparse sampling grids
abstract: Soil fungal richness is highly variable at field scales, and choosing an appropriate interpolation method strongly influences map quality when sampling density is limited. We used a dataset of 96 ITS1 amplicon samples collected on a 200 × 200 m grid across a 4 ha experimental wheat field at the Rimski Šančevi research station to benchmark four kriging variants: ordinary kriging, simple kriging, indicator kriging, and universal kriging with elevation as an external drift variable. Leave-one-out cross-validation was performed for each method using root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) as criteria. Universal kriging with elevation drift achieved the lowest RMSE (14.2 OTUs) compared to ordinary kriging (18.7 OTUs). Indicator kriging performed best for mapping the probability that richness exceeded a threshold of 120 OTUs. The study also assessed the sensitivity of results to variogram model choice (spherical, exponential, Matérn). Results suggest that even simple topographic covariates substantially improve fungal diversity maps and that variogram model choice matters more for fungi than for bacteria in this soil type.

title: Dirichlet-multinomial regression for modelling phylum-level microbiome shifts along a salinity gradient in Pannonian solonetz soils
abstract: Solonetz soils in the Pannonian Plain present pronounced salinity gradients over short distances, providing a natural laboratory for studying microbiome composition change. We collected 72 samples across a 6-km transect in the Deliblato area, measured soil electrical conductivity (EC) and pH at each point, and performed 16S rRNA sequencing (mean 32 100 reads per sample). Because compositional data violate ordinary regression assumptions, we fitted Dirichlet-multinomial (DM) regression models with EC and pH as continuous predictors and geographic coordinates as spatial random effects implemented via a Gaussian process prior. The DM model identified significant negative associations between EC and the relative abundance of Acidobacteria (posterior mean β = −0.38, 95% CrI: −0.51 to −0.25) and a positive association with Proteobacteria. Spatial random effects explained approximately 22% of residual variance after accounting for the measured covariates, indicating unmeasured soil properties cluster spatially. These findings suggest that salinity-driven compositional shifts are detectable even at the phylum level and that ignoring spatial dependence inflates false-positive rates in microbiome–environment association studies.

title: Sensitivity of microbiome spatial models to sequencing depth rarefaction: a simulation study using Vojvodina soil data
abstract: Rarefaction to a common sequencing depth is a standard preprocessing step in microbiome studies, yet its effect on downstream spatial models has not been systematically evaluated. We used a real dataset of 120 soil samples from Vojvodina croplands (mean depth 41 500 reads, range 9 800–68 200) to construct a simulation framework in which reads were downsampled to five target depths (5 000, 10 000, 20 000, 30 000, and 40 000 reads) with 50 replicates each. For each replicate we fitted ordinary kriging to Shannon diversity and DM regression to phylum compositions. Variogram range estimates were stable (coefficient of variation < 8%) across depths above 10 000 reads but deteriorated sharply at 5 000. DM regression coefficients for the dominant phyla were recoverable at all depths tested, but credible intervals widened approximately 35% at 5 000 reads compared to 40 000. We conclude that for spatial modelling applications a minimum depth of around 15 000 reads per sample provides a reasonable balance between statistical reliability and sequencing cost.

title: Spatial modelling of microbiome beta-diversity along sunflower–soybean intercrop boundaries using multivariate geostatistics
abstract: Intercropping creates sharp edaphic transitions at crop boundaries that may influence local microbiome assembly. We sampled soils at 88 points along five replicated transects crossing sunflower–soybean intercrop interfaces at a commercial farm in Bačka Palanka, collecting samples at 0–10 cm and 10–30 cm depths. 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing yielded a mean of 35 200 reads per sample. Beta-diversity was quantified by Aitchison distance and the first three PCoA axes were treated as co-regionalised variables in a linear model of coregionalisation (LMC) framework. Fitted LMC models revealed two spatial structures: a nugget component attributable to micro-scale variability and a spherical structure with range approximately 3.1 m centred on the crop interface. Co-kriging of the three PCoA axes improved prediction accuracy by 14% over independent kriging of each axis. Depth had a stronger effect on composition than proximity to the interface, but interface effects remained significant after depth was controlled. Results have practical implications for precision placement of soil amendments in intercropping systems.

title: A geostatistical workflow for microbiome diversity mapping in precision agriculture: a practical guide with R code
abstract: Applying geostatistical methods to microbiome datasets requires bridging methodological traditions in spatial statistics and microbial ecology that have largely developed independently. This book chapter outlines a step-by-step analytical workflow covering: sample design for spatial surveys (including variogram-informed minimum sample sizes), compositional data preprocessing (centred log-ratio and Aitchison isometric transforms), empirical variogram estimation and model fitting in R using the gstat package, ordinary and universal kriging prediction, and cross-validation. Supplementary sections address the Dirichlet-multinomial regression with spatial random effects using the INLA-SPDE approach. All steps are illustrated with a worked example from a 96-point survey of a maize field near Zrenjanin. Annotated R scripts are provided throughout. The chapter concludes with a discussion of common pitfalls, including pseudo-replication from dense sampling, the choice between kriging and spline-based interpolation, and the handling of zero-inflated taxa. The material is aimed at microbial ecologists with basic R literacy who wish to incorporate spatial structure into their analyses.

title: Disassembly Time Estimation for Small Household Appliances Using Liaison Graph Decomposition
abstract: This paper presents a graph-based method for estimating disassembly time of small household appliances, specifically hand-held vacuum cleaners and electric kettles. Liaison graphs were constructed for 14 product variants from three Serbian and Central European manufacturers, encoding joint types, access constraints, and tool requirements as edge attributes. A weighted traversal algorithm generated disassembly sequences that were compared against timed manual disassembly trials conducted with six technicians across two proficiency levels. The predicted disassembly times deviated from measured values by a mean absolute error of 8.4% across 112 sequences. Sensitivity analysis showed that snap-fit connections contributed disproportionately to total disassembly time—accounting for up to 34% of task duration while representing only 12% of joint count. Results are used to derive a time-normalised disassembly index suitable for early-stage design benchmarking. The method requires only information available at the detailed design stage and is independent of any specific CAD platform.

title: Comparative Life-Cycle Assessment of Electric Hand Dryers: Scenarios for Repair, Remanufacture, and Landfill
abstract: A cradle-to-grave life-cycle assessment was carried out for a mid-range electric hand dryer (motor unit, housing, and control board) under four end-of-life scenarios: landfill, mechanical recycling, component remanufacture, and full product repair. Primary data were collected from one Central European manufacturer covering material composition, production energy, and logistics distances. The functional unit was defined as 10,000 drying cycles. Climate change, resource depletion, and cumulative energy demand were the impact categories assessed using an in-house adapted Ecoinvent 3.8 background database. The repair scenario reduced global warming potential by 38% compared with landfill when the repaired unit substituted a new unit in the market. Remanufacture of the motor subassembly alone yielded a 22% reduction. Breakeven carbon analysis showed that repair remains beneficial up to three transport round-trips of 600 km. Uncertainty was assessed by Monte Carlo simulation (n = 1000). Results are sensitive to the grid electricity mix assumed for the use phase.

title: Towards a Standardised Repairability Index for Electromechanical Consumer Goods: Methodology Proposal and Validation
abstract: The paper proposes a quantitative repairability index (RI) for electromechanical consumer products, structured around five sub-indices: physical accessibility of components, availability of spare parts, availability of service documentation, tool standardisation, and disassembly reversibility. Each sub-index is scored on an ordinal scale derived from 48 product teardowns covering cordless drills, hair dryers, and robot vacuum cleaners. Aggregate RI values are computed using weights elicited from eleven design engineers and seven repair technicians via an analytic hierarchy process. The resulting index showed strong rank correlation (Spearman ρ = 0.81) with independently measured mean time to repair in controlled workshop trials. The proposal is benchmarked against the French ADEME repairability score introduced in 2021 and identifies three dimensions inadequately captured by that scheme, particularly fastener standardisation and subassembly modularity. A worked example for a cordless drill demonstrates application at early design review stages.

title: Material Flow Modelling of Printed Circuit Boards Recovered from Disassembled Household Appliances in Serbia
abstract: This study presents a static material flow analysis of printed circuit boards (PCBs) recovered from end-of-life small household appliances collected through the Serbian WEEE take-back system between 2015 and 2017. Collection data from three urban centres were combined with composition measurements from 220 PCB samples to estimate annual flows of copper, tin, lead, and selected rare earth elements. Results indicate that approximately 34 tonnes of copper-bearing PCB material entered formal collection annually in the study region, of which 61% was processed domestically and 39% exported for precious metal recovery. The model was structured according to the STAN material flow analysis framework and calibrated against national statistics on appliance sales. Transfer coefficients for sorting and preprocessing steps were estimated by interval analysis due to data scarcity. The analysis identifies PCB pre-processing capacity as the primary bottleneck limiting domestic value recovery. Policy implications for extended producer responsibility scheme design are discussed.

title: Design-for-Disassembly Guidelines for Electromechanical Products: A Structured Review and Gap Analysis
abstract: This book chapter reviews design-for-disassembly (DfD) guidelines published between 1990 and 2020 for electromechanical consumer products, cataloguing 61 guidelines from 34 sources covering academic literature, industrial standards, and regulatory documentation. Guidelines are classified along four dimensions: scope (fastening, material marking, access, documentation), lifecycle stage of applicability, quantitative versus qualitative formulation, and evidence base. The review finds that 43% of guidelines lack quantitative backing from product teardown data, and that joint-type recommendations are overwhelmingly derived from automotive rather than consumer electronics contexts, which differ substantially in scale, assembly force, and material combinations. Gaps are identified in: guidance for multi-material polymer-metal interfaces, disassembly under aged adhesive bonds, and integration with digital product passport requirements. The chapter concludes with a prioritised research agenda and a consolidated checklist of 18 evidence-supported guidelines suitable for use in design reviews of small electromechanical appliances.

title: Quantifying Repairability Loss Over Product Service Life: Degradation of Fastener and Connector Accessibility in Cordless Power Tools
abstract: Repairability is typically assessed for new products, but accessibility of fasteners and connectors changes as products age due to corrosion, adhesive creep, wear, and contamination. This paper presents a longitudinal measurement study of disassembly accessibility in 96 cordless drills at three service-life stages: new, two years in-service, and four years in-service, sourced through a co-operation with two Serbian appliance repair networks. Accessibility was measured as applied torque to disengage fasteners, force to release snap-fit elements, and time to expose the battery subassembly. Mean torque for self-tapping screws increased by 31% after four years. Snap-fit release force showed higher variance, with 18% of connectors requiring destructive disassembly at four years. A degradation factor is proposed for incorporation into repairability index calculations to produce time-adjusted scores. Implications for extended warranty and circular economy policy design are discussed in relation to current European Union regulatory proposals.

title: Integration of End-of-Life Scenario Analysis into Early-Stage Product Development: A Decision Support Framework
abstract: End-of-life (EoL) considerations are rarely integrated into product development before the detailed design stage, by which point 70–80% of lifecycle impacts are already determined. This paper presents a decision support framework that introduces EoL scenario analysis at the concept selection phase through a structured set of screening metrics computable from bill-of-materials sketches and architecture diagrams alone. The framework draws on a database of 140 EoL scenarios constructed from four product categories: angle grinders, hair dryers, electric fans, and water pumps. Metrics include a simplified embodied carbon proxy, a disassembly feasibility score, and a spare-part criticality flag. The framework was piloted in two product design courses at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad, involving 34 student teams, and was evaluated against expert LCA outcomes for the same concepts. Agreement at concept rank level was 74%. Limitations of using proxy metrics and conditions under which full LCA is still warranted are discussed.

title: Carbon Accounting for Informal Repair Activity: Estimating Emissions Avoided Through Small Appliance Repair in the Western Balkans
abstract: Informal and semi-formal repair of small household appliances represents a substantial but poorly quantified contribution to extending product lifespans and avoiding manufacturing emissions. This preprint estimates the greenhouse gas emissions avoided by repair activity across five Western Balkan countries using a combination of national appliance sales statistics, repair shop density data from business registry records, and a parametric LCA model covering 12 product types. The avoided emission factor per repair event was estimated at 3.1–8.7 kg CO₂-equivalent depending on product category, with washing machine motors and refrigeration compressors at the high end. Scaled to the estimated annual repair volume of 2.1 million events across the region, total annual avoided emissions are estimated at 9,400–18,300 tonnes CO₂-equivalent. Key uncertainties include repair success rates, counterfactual replacement behaviour, and grid emission factors. The study provides baseline data for potential carbon crediting mechanisms applicable to informal repair sectors.

title: Disassembly Sequence Planning Under Uncertainty: A Stochastic Optimisation Approach for Mixed End-of-Life Targets
abstract: Optimal disassembly sequences for electromechanical products depend on the economic value and recovery rate of targeted subassemblies, both of which are uncertain at planning time. This paper formulates disassembly sequence planning as a two-stage stochastic programme in which the second stage accounts for uncertainty in component condition, secondary material prices, and available processing capacity. The model is applied to a dataset of 320 end-of-life washing machine drum-drive assemblies processed at a Serbian remanufacturing facility over an 18-month period. Stochastic sequences reduced total disassembly cost by 11% compared with deterministic sequences planned on expected values, primarily by deferring destructive steps until condition inspection outcomes were known. Computational tractability was maintained using a sample average approximation with 200 scenarios. The model is parameterised for three levels of labour cost, allowing application across different regional economic contexts in Southeast Europe.

title: Influence of tyre pressure asymmetry on the lateral stability of a reach truck during high-reach operations
abstract: Reach trucks operating at lift heights above 8 m are sensitive to deviations in tyre inflation pressure because the effective contact stiffness directly affects the lateral stability margin. This paper quantifies the effect of asymmetric tyre pressure—one drive tyre underinflated by 15%, 25%, or 40% relative to the nominal 9 bar—on the stability triangle geometry and load-capacity reduction for lift heights of 6 m, 8 m, and 10 m. A rigid multibody model incorporates pneumatic tyre contact compliance using a linear spring–damper formulation at each wheel contact patch. Static and low-speed dynamic (0.4 m/s) simulations are conducted for load masses of 800 kg and 1200 kg. A 40% underinflation at the loaded side reduces the effective stability base width by 41 mm and decreases the allowable load mass by up to 7.8% at 10 m lift height. Field measurements on a rented reach truck with pressure-controlled tyres verify the model predictions with a mean discrepancy of 3.6% in lateral ground-reaction force.

title: Gravimetric measurement of water vapour permeability in EPDM and silicone gasket materials at temperatures from 5 °C to 50 °C
abstract: Vapour permeability of two commercially representative gasket elastomers—EPDM and silicone—was measured using a modified dry-cup gravimetric method over a temperature range of 5 °C to 50 °C at 50 % and 80 % relative humidity differentials. Twelve specimens per material were conditioned for 96 hours before testing. Results show that silicone permeability increases by a factor of 2.3 between 5 °C and 50 °C, while EPDM exhibits a weaker temperature dependence with a factor of 1.6. Activation energies derived from Arrhenius fits are 18.4 kJ/mol for EPDM and 22.1 kJ/mol for silicone. The datasets are incorporated into a one-dimensional diffusion model and used to compute steady-state vapour flux as a function of gasket cross-section width between 4 mm and 16 mm. Predicted internal humidity rise over a 30-day period agrees with chamber experiments to within 6 %. The data provide material constants suitable for use in finite-element hygrothermal models of sealed enclosures.

title: Effect of pH and temperature on acid-catalysed hydrolysis of wheat starch slurries at varying dry-matter concentrations
abstract: Acid hydrolysis of wheat starch was carried out in a stirred batch reactor over a dry-matter range of 30–42% (w/w), with hydrochloric acid concentrations of 0.05–0.20 M, temperatures of 120–145 °C, and reaction times of 10–60 minutes. Dextrose equivalent (DE) values were monitored at 10-minute intervals using the Lane–Eynon titration method and confirmed by HPLC sugar profiling. At 140 °C and 0.10 M HCl, DE values of 15–22 were consistently achieved within 20–30 minutes across all dry-matter levels tested, with maltose representing 8–12% of the total soluble carbohydrate fraction. Increasing dry-matter content above 38% led to a measurable increase in colour (absorbance at 420 nm), attributed to enhanced Maillard and caramelisation side reactions. A simple first-order kinetic model fitted the DE–time data with R² > 0.96 for all conditions. The results suggest that acid hydrolysis can serve as a cost-effective pre-treatment for subsequent enzymatic saccharification steps targeting glucose syrups with DE above 60.

title: Liquefaction of corn starch with a thermostable alpha-amylase: influence of enzyme dosage and calcium ion concentration on dextrose equivalent and viscosity profiles
abstract: Thermostable alpha-amylase from a commercial bacterial preparation was used to liquefy jet-cooked corn starch suspensions (35% dry matter) at 95 °C and pH 6.2. Enzyme dosages ranged from 0.3 to 1.2 KNU/g starch and calcium chloride was added at 0, 25, 50, and 100 ppm to assess its stabilising effect on enzyme activity. Apparent viscosity was measured at 5-minute intervals using a rotational viscometer throughout the 60-minute liquefaction period. DE values at the end of liquefaction ranged from 8 to 19 depending on enzyme dose. Calcium supplementation at 50 ppm maintained enzyme activity significantly longer than calcium-free conditions, reducing residual insoluble material by approximately 18% at low enzyme doses. Sugar oligomer distributions determined by HPLC indicated a predominance of malto-oligosaccharides in the DP3–DP7 range at DE 10–14, which is the typical target range for food-grade maltodextrins. The dataset was used to calibrate a Michaelis–Menten-based kinetic model for starch liquefaction under industrial-like conditions.
