title: Two-stage enzymatic hydrolysis of wheat starch for production of glucose syrups: optimisation of saccharification conditions using response surface methodology
abstract: A two-stage enzymatic process consisting of alpha-amylase liquefaction followed by glucoamylase saccharification was applied to wheat starch at 30% dry matter. Liquefaction was carried out at 95 °C, pH 6.2, for 90 minutes to a target DE of 10–12. Saccharification variables—glucoamylase dose (0.3–1.0 AGU/g starch), temperature (58–65 °C), pH (4.0–4.8), and reaction time (24–72 hours)—were optimised using a central composite design with DE and glucose content as responses. Under optimal conditions (0.7 AGU/g, 60 °C, pH 4.3, 60 hours), glucose content reached 94.8% of total sugars and DE was 97.4. Pullulanase debranching co-supplementation at the saccharification stage increased glucose yield by an additional 1.8 percentage points while reducing saccharification time by approximately 8 hours. Byproduct streams, primarily residual oligosaccharides recovered from simulated mother liquor after glucose crystallisation, were characterised for potential use as fermentation substrates.

title: Recovery and fermentative potential of oligosaccharide-rich streams from starch hydrolysis processes
abstract: Residual oligosaccharide fractions were collected from pilot-scale glucose syrup production by membrane ultrafiltration (10 kDa cut-off) of the saccharification liquor after primary glucose separation. The permeate, containing predominantly DP2–DP5 malto-oligosaccharides at total solid concentrations of 18–24 g/L, was evaluated as a carbon source for lactic acid fermentation using two laboratory strains of Lactobacillus amylophilus sourced from the culture collection of the Department of Biotechnology, Faculty of Technology Novi Sad. Fermentation trials at 37 °C and pH 6.0 showed lactic acid yields of 0.71–0.78 g/g consumed carbohydrate over 48 hours, comparable to yields obtained on pure glucose medium. Chemical oxygen demand of the fermented stream was reduced by 74% relative to the unfermented oligosaccharide permeate, supporting its use as a route to reduce the environmental load of starch processing effluents. These results demonstrate a straightforward valorisation pathway requiring minimal upstream modification of existing plant operations.

title: Influence of starch granule size distribution on the efficiency of alpha-amylase liquefaction in wheat flour slurries
abstract: Wheat flour fractions enriched in small (A-type, > 10 µm) and large (B-type, < 10 µm) starch granules were separated by wet sieving and elutriation, and their susceptibility to thermostable alpha-amylase liquefaction was compared at identical dry-matter and enzyme-dose conditions. Granule size distributions were confirmed by laser diffraction. The B-type fraction, despite representing only 25–30% of total starch mass, exhibited approximately 35% lower initial hydrolysis rates at 90 °C and pH 6.0, attributed to lower surface area per unit mass and higher amylopectin branch density as determined by isoamylase debranching followed by HPAEC-PAD chain length analysis. Gelatinisation enthalpies measured by DSC differed by less than 1.2 J/g between fractions, confirming that the observed kinetic differences were not primarily due to gelatinisation extent. Mixing A- and B-type fractions in their native flour ratio restored normal liquefaction kinetics, suggesting that industrial whole-flour processes are not meaningfully impaired by granule heterogeneity under standard operating conditions.

title: Partial acid pre-hydrolysis as a means to reduce enzyme consumption in the production of high-DE glucose syrups from corn starch
abstract: A combined acid-enzyme process was evaluated as a strategy to reduce glucoamylase consumption in glucose syrup production. Corn starch suspensions (35% dry matter) were subjected to mild acid pre-hydrolysis (0.05 M HCl, 130 °C, 15 min) to a DE of 5–8 before standard alpha-amylase liquefaction and glucoamylase saccharification. Glucoamylase doses were reduced incrementally from a baseline of 0.8 AGU/g to 0.4 AGU/g in 0.1-unit steps. Final glucose purity and DE after 60-hour saccharification were compared between acid pre-treated and untreated controls at each enzyme dose. Acid pre-treatment allowed a 25–30% reduction in glucoamylase dose while maintaining final glucose content above 93% of total sugars and DE above 95. Colour development in the pre-treated samples was higher by 0.04–0.08 absorbance units at 420 nm but remained within acceptable limits for standard glucose syrup grades. An economic estimate based on current enzyme contract pricing in the region indicated a potential reduction in enzyme costs of 18–22% for a 50 t/day plant.

title: Kinetic modelling of colour development in wheat flour extrudates: application of the zero-order and Weibull models
abstract: CIE L*a*b* colour parameters were monitored in wheat flour extrudates produced over a barrel temperature range of 130–190 °C and at screw speeds of 200, 300 and 400 rpm. Samples were collected every 15 minutes during continuous runs lasting 90 minutes. Colour change ΔE* was calculated relative to unextruded flour. Both zero-order and Weibull kinetic models were fitted to the ΔE* data using nonlinear regression. The Weibull model provided a better fit (R² 0.96–0.98) compared with zero-order kinetics (R² 0.88–0.93) across all temperature levels. The activation energy estimated from the Arrhenius equation was 42.3 kJ/mol for the L* decrease. Screw speed had a secondary but statistically significant effect on browning rate at temperatures above 170 °C, likely linked to increased specific mechanical energy input. The fitted parameters are discussed in the context of on-line colour control for continuous extruder operation.

title: Maillard reaction in extruded snack foods: mechanisms, process variables, and health-related reaction products
abstract: This chapter reviews the state of knowledge regarding Maillard reaction pathways relevant to low-moisture, thermally processed cereal extrudates. The mechanistic discussion covers the Amadori rearrangement, Strecker degradation, and the competing routes leading to acrylamide, HMF, and melanoidins. The influence of key process variables—barrel temperature, screw speed, moisture content, and residence time—on the distribution of Maillard products is discussed with reference to experimental data from twin-screw extrusion studies. Particular attention is given to the duality of melanoidins as both health-relevant antioxidants and potential indicators of excessive browning. Regulatory frameworks for acrylamide in cereal snacks in the EU context are summarised. The chapter also discusses analytical methods used to quantify Maillard reaction products in extrudates, including LC-MS/MS for acrylamide, fluorescence spectroscopy for melanoidins, and colorimetry. Gaps in the literature on the interaction between substrate amino acid profile and extrusion process design are identified.

title: The Right to an Explanation in Administrative Decision-Making: Lessons from French and German Practice for Serbian Reform
abstract: Drawing on the administrative procedure reforms introduced in France (2015 Loi pour une République numérique) and Germany (amendments to the Verwaltungsverfahrensgesetz), this book chapter analyses what a statutory duty to explain automated decisions would require in the Serbian legal context. The chapter proceeds in three parts: first, a doctrinal reconstruction of the explanation requirement as it has developed in French and German administrative law and case-law; second, an assessment of whether existing Serbian administrative procedure law contains latent equivalents; third, a legislative drafting exercise producing a model provision. The chapter concludes that Serbian law already contains a general duty to state reasons for administrative acts that could be extended by analogy, but that this extension requires an explicit legislative signal to be reliable in practice. Particular attention is paid to the tension between the duty to explain and trade secret protections invoked by private technology vendors supplying software to public bodies.

title: Profiling in Public Administration: Data Protection Law Meets Administrative Procedure in the Western Balkans
abstract: This article examines the intersection between personal data protection rules derived from the Council of Europe Convention 108 and the GDPR, and administrative procedure obligations, in the context of profiling practices used by social welfare and tax authorities in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The empirical basis consists of 22 semi-structured interviews with public officials in the three countries conducted in 2016, supplemented by freedom-of-information requests yielding internal policy documents. The study finds that none of the three jurisdictions had produced formal internal guidance on how profiling-based risk scores should be integrated into decision workflows in a manner consistent with individual procedural rights. The article maps the specific normative gaps and argues that the EU GDPR Article 22 framework, although not directly applicable in the Western Balkans, provides a useful template for national legislators.

title: Technical Documentation as a Legal Instrument: What the GDPR Record-Keeping Obligation Tells Us About Future AI Regulation
abstract: Article 30 of the GDPR requires controllers to maintain records of processing activities, and supervisory authority guidance has gradually expanded the substantive content those records must contain. This article analyses decisions and guidance issued by ten European data protection authorities between 2018 and 2020 to determine what a mature technical documentation obligation looks like in practice. Using content analysis of 87 enforcement decisions and 34 guidance documents, the study codes the types of information authorities consistently demand, the format requirements they impose, and the evidentiary use they make of records in proceedings. The results identify eight recurring documentation elements—including data flows, retention schedules, processor contracts, and security measures—that appear in at least 70 per cent of the sampled materials. The article argues that this established GDPR practice constitutes a model for the technical documentation requirements later incorporated into the EU Artificial Intelligence Act for high-risk systems, and evaluates the continuities and divergences between the two regimes.

title: High-Risk AI Systems in Public Administration: Mapping the Operators' Obligations Under the Proposed EU AI Act
abstract: Presented at the 2021 International Conference on Administrative Law and Digital Technologies in Ljubljana, this paper provides a systematic mapping of the compliance obligations that the then-proposed EU Artificial Intelligence Act would impose on public bodies acting as operators of high-risk AI systems. The analysis focuses on the obligations in Articles 29 and 30 of the Commission's April 2021 proposal, examining: the duty to follow the supplier's instructions of use; the duty to monitor system performance; the duty to suspend the system in case of serious incident; and the duty to cooperate with national supervisory authorities. For each obligation the paper identifies the corresponding administrative law doctrine—duty of care, proportionality, good administration—and assesses whether existing administrative procedure laws in Serbia and the EU Member States adequately operationalise them. The paper concludes by identifying three obligations that require new procedural instruments not currently present in most national legal systems.

title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment for Algorithmic Systems: Designing a Procedural Model for Public Bodies
abstract: This article develops a procedural model for fundamental rights impact assessments (FRIA) as required under Article 29a of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act as amended by the European Parliament in 2023. The model is constructed by synthesising three existing assessment frameworks: the data protection impact assessment procedure under GDPR Article 35, the equality impact assessment practice developed in the United Kingdom, and the human rights due diligence methodology promoted by the Council of Europe. The article identifies seven procedural steps—scoping, stakeholder mapping, rights inventory, likelihood and severity scoring, mitigation design, residual risk acceptance, and periodic review—and evaluates each against the specific requirements of the AI Act text and the fundamental rights protected under the EU Charter. A draft template is provided as an appendix, calibrated to the resources available to medium-sized public bodies. The article does not assert that the proposed model satisfies all future regulatory guidance, which remains to be issued.

title: Conformity Assessment Procedures Under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act: An Administrative Law Reading
abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act establishes conformity assessment procedures that must be completed before a high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service. This book chapter examines those procedures through the lens of administrative law, treating them as a form of preventive administrative authorisation. The chapter proceeds in four parts. First, it situates conformity assessment within the broader tradition of pre-market authorisation in EU product safety law. Second, it analyses the internal conformity assessment procedure applicable to most high-risk systems under Annex VI, identifying its evidentiary and documentary requirements. Third, it examines the third-party notified body procedure applicable to biometric and critical infrastructure systems. Fourth, it considers the enforcement consequences of non-compliance, including market withdrawal and prohibition orders issued by national market surveillance authorities. The chapter argues that the notified body procedure creates a hybrid public-private regulatory arrangement without adequate public law accountability mechanisms.

title: Post-Market Monitoring Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems: Compliance Costs and Legal Uncertainty for Small Public Bodies
abstract: Article 72 of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act requires operators of high-risk AI systems to implement post-market monitoring plans and report serious incidents to national authorities. This article evaluates the practical compliance burden of these obligations for small and medium-sized public bodies—defined here as municipal administrations and social welfare agencies with fewer than 200 staff. The study is based on a survey administered in 2023 to 64 such bodies in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, supplemented by 15 in-depth interviews with heads of legal and IT departments. Results show that 81 per cent of respondents lacked dedicated staff capable of drafting a monitoring plan compliant with the Act's requirements, and 74 per cent were unaware of the incident-reporting timelines. The article identifies three structural causes of under-preparedness—resource constraints, cross-functional coordination failures, and lack of regulatory guidance—and proposes differentiated compliance pathways for bodies below a defined resource threshold.

title: The Role of National Competent Authorities Under the EU AI Act: Institutional Design Choices for Western Balkan Candidates
abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act requires each Member State to designate one or more national competent authorities responsible for implementation and enforcement. This article examines the institutional design choices made by five EU Member States that published their designation decisions in 2024—Austria, the Netherlands, Portugal, Finland, and Estonia—and draws lessons for Western Balkan candidate countries preparing alignment legislation. The comparison covers: the choice between a dedicated AI authority, an expanded data protection authority, and a sectoral regulator model; the scope of investigative and sanctioning powers; coordination mechanisms with the European AI Office; and resource allocation. Serbia is used as the primary case study for the candidate-country analysis, given its advanced EU integration status and the existence of a draft AI alignment strategy published by the government in 2023. The article argues that Serbia should opt for an expanded mandate within the existing Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection rather than creating a new body.

title: Human Oversight Requirements in the EU AI Act: Between Formal Compliance and Effective Control
abstract: Articles 14 and 29 of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act impose human oversight requirements on providers and operators of high-risk AI systems, but the Act provides little guidance on what effective oversight entails in operational settings. This article analyses the human oversight requirement by drawing on organisational theory, administrative law doctrine, and empirical case studies of three public-sector deployments of algorithmic systems: a child welfare risk assessment tool used by a regional social services agency in Germany, a benefits eligibility screening tool used by a national social insurance fund in a Central European country, and a document classification system used by a European customs authority. For each case, the article reconstructs the oversight arrangements actually in place and evaluates them against the Act's text and recitals. The analysis finds a recurrent pattern in which oversight is nominally present but operationally ineffective because reviewers lack both the time and the technical literacy to meaningfully assess system outputs.

title: Liability for Automated Administrative Decisions Under Serbian Law: Current Framework and the Case for Statutory Reform
abstract: This article examines the state liability framework applicable when automated or AI-assisted administrative decisions cause harm to individuals under Serbian law. The doctrinal analysis covers the constitutional basis for state liability (Article 35 of the Constitution), the general tort provisions of the Law on Obligations, and the specific administrative liability rules in the Law on General Administrative Procedure. The article identifies two scenarios that the current framework handles poorly: harm caused by a technically correct decision that nonetheless produces disproportionate effects on an individual due to reliance on an inaccurate training dataset, and harm caused by a decision that would have been revised had a human reviewer actually examined the AI system's output rather than accepting it automatically. For each scenario, the article assesses whether existing fault, unlawfulness, and causation doctrines can accommodate the claim, concluding that the causation analysis is the most problematic element in both cases. Legislative reform options are presented and evaluated.

title: Regulatory Sandboxes for AI Under the EU AI Act: Public Law Constraints and Opportunities for Candidate Countries
abstract: Articles 57 to 63 of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act establish a framework for national regulatory sandboxes in which AI systems can be developed and tested under relaxed compliance conditions. This article analyses the public law constraints that apply to such sandboxes—legality, equal treatment, proportionality, and accountability—and assesses whether the Act's framework adequately respects those constraints. The analysis then considers the specific position of EU candidate countries, which are encouraged under the Act's recitals to establish compatible sandbox regimes in preparation for accession. Using Serbia as the central example, the article examines whether the existing Serbian legal framework for administrative experimentation—sparse as it is—provides a sufficient basis for establishing a compliant sandbox, or whether primary legislation is required. The article concludes that a sandbox ordinance adopted by the Government under existing enabling legislation would be legally sufficient but institutionally fragile, and that a dedicated statutory instrument would be preferable.

title: Sub-legislative Rulemaking and the EU Approximation Agenda: Constitutional Tensions in Western Balkan Candidate States
abstract: European Union accession requires candidate states to transpose a large body of technical acquis, much of which is implemented not through primary legislation but through agency rulebooks and adopted European standards. This book chapter examines how this external normative pressure interacts with constitutional norms on delegated legislation in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. Based on a review of 118 transposition instruments across the three states covering the period 2012–2018, the chapter identifies a structural tension: EU-driven technical rulemaking expands agency norm-production at a pace that domestic constitutional frameworks, designed for a different scale of regulation, struggle to accommodate. The chapter maps the gap between formal constitutional requirements and actual legislative practice, and surveys judicial responses where they exist. Recommendations are addressed to both domestic legislators and EU technical assistance programmes.

title: Potentiometric determination of protonation constants of citric acid at 25 °C and ionic strengths 0.01–0.5 M NaClO₄
abstract: Accurate protonation constants of citric acid are prerequisites for calculating metal–citrate conditional stability constants in environmental matrices. This study used a glass-electrode potentiometric cell calibrated in terms of hydrogen-ion concentration (Gran procedure) to measure pKa values of citric acid at five ionic strengths (0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50 M NaClO₄) and 25 °C. Titration data were processed with the HYPERQUAD2006 software package. The three successive pKa values at I = 0.10 M were 3.09 ± 0.01, 4.56 ± 0.01 and 5.98 ± 0.02, in close agreement with literature data obtained by different methods. Activity corrections following SIT (Specific Ion interaction Theory) formalism yielded thermodynamic pKa values of 3.13, 4.76 and 6.40. The dependence of all three pKa values on ionic strength was adequately described by SIT with interaction coefficients consistent with published values for related carboxylate systems. The dataset provides a self-consistent basis for subsequent determination of Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ stability constants under soil-relevant conditions.

title: Complexation of zinc(II) with oxalate in aqueous solutions at pH 5.0–8.5: relevance to zinc mobility in acid and calcareous soils
abstract: Zinc deficiency is widespread in calcareous soils across the Pannonian Plain, and zinc–organic acid complexation critically governs Zn solubility and root uptake. Stability constants for Zn²⁺–oxalate (ZnL⁰, ZnL₂²⁻ and ZnHL⁺) were measured by potentiometry and UV-Vis spectrophotometry at 25 °C, I = 0.10 M (KNO₃). Measurements were performed over 44 independent titration curves covering metal-to-ligand ratios from 1:1 to 1:10. HYPERQUAD refinement gave log K(ZnL⁰) = 4.89 ± 0.02, log K(ZnL₂²⁻) = 7.98 ± 0.05, and log K(ZnHL⁺) = 2.10 ± 0.08. Speciation modelling using MINEQL+ version 4.6 was applied to three Vojvodina soil pore-water compositions (measured total oxalate 8–45 µM). At pH 8.0, ZnL⁰ accounts for less than 4% of total dissolved Zn, indicating that oxalate alone is insufficient to explain observed Zn mobilisation in these alkaline soils.

title: Calorimetric determination of enthalpy changes for Mg²⁺–succinate and Mg²⁺–gluconate complexation at 25 °C
abstract: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) was employed to measure the enthalpy of complexation (ΔH) for 1:1 Mg²⁺–succinate and Mg²⁺–gluconate systems at 25 °C and I = 0.10 M (NaNO₃). Stability constants obtained by parallel potentiometric experiments at the same conditions served as fixed input parameters for ITC curve fitting using a one-set-of-sites model. For Mg–succinate, ΔH = −3.4 ± 0.3 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔG = −8.9 kJ mol⁻¹ and TΔS = +5.5 kJ mol⁻¹, indicating an entropically driven association. For Mg–gluconate, ΔH = −6.1 ± 0.4 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔG = −10.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and TΔS = +4.1 kJ mol⁻¹. The relatively small exothermic contributions and positive entropy terms are consistent with partial dehydration of Mg²⁺ upon outer-sphere or semi-chelate coordination. These thermodynamic data are discussed in the context of temperature dependence of micronutrient speciation in surface soils subject to seasonal thermal fluctuations.

title: Copper(II) and cadmium(II) complexes with citrate in synthetic calcareous soil solutions: speciation at pH 7.5–8.5
abstract: Copper and cadmium speciation in calcareous soil pore water controls phytoavailability and transfer into the food chain. Stability constants for Cu²⁺ and Cd²⁺ with citrate were redetermined at three ionic strengths (0.01, 0.05 and 0.10 M NaClO₄) and at 25 °C using potentiometry. For Cu–citrate, log K(CuL⁻) = 6.10 ± 0.03 and a minor binuclear species Cu₂L was detected at Cu:citrate ratios above 2:1. For Cd–citrate, log K(CdL⁻) = 3.75 ± 0.04. Synthetic soil solutions were prepared from dissolution data for three Vojvodina calcareous soils (CaCO₃ content 12–28%), with dissolved organic acid concentrations estimated from published rhizosphere measurements. In solutions representing the rhizosphere near maize roots, 38–52% of dissolved Cu²⁺ is complexed with citrate at pH 8.0, compared with only 8–14% of Cd²⁺. Implications for differential phytoavailability of Cu versus Cd in calcareous Chernozem soils are discussed.

title: Comparative potentiometric study of Pb²⁺ and Zn²⁺ complexes with malate, succinate and fumarate at I = 0.10 M
abstract: Lead contamination from historical agricultural use of Pb-based pesticides remains a concern in some Vojvodina orchard soils. This study compares the complexation behaviour of Pb²⁺ and Zn²⁺ with three dicarboxylate ligands—malate, succinate and fumarate—by glass-electrode potentiometry at 25 °C and I = 0.10 M NaNO₃. For Pb²⁺, stability constants (log K₁₁) are: malate 3.48 ± 0.03, succinate 3.02 ± 0.04, fumarate 3.18 ± 0.03. For Zn²⁺: malate 2.93 ± 0.03, succinate 2.44 ± 0.04, fumarate 2.35 ± 0.05. The α-hydroxy group in malate consistently enhances stability for both metals relative to the saturated succinate. Ternary mixed-ligand models with malate and citrate together did not improve fit statistics, suggesting independent binding. These results feed into a soil speciation database for Vojvodina orchard soils being compiled in collaboration with the provincial agricultural extension service.

title: Thermodynamic stability constants for Cd²⁺ and Pb²⁺ complexes with gluconate: potentiometric measurements from 15 to 37 °C
abstract: Temperature-dependent stability constants allow prediction of metal speciation in soils subject to seasonal temperature variation (typically 5–35 °C in the Pannonian Plain). Stability constants for Cd²⁺–gluconate and Pb²⁺–gluconate were measured potentiometrically at five temperatures (15, 20, 25, 30 and 37 °C) at I = 0.10 M NaClO₄. For Cd–gluconate, log K₁₁ decreases from 2.51 at 15 °C to 2.38 at 37 °C; for Pb–gluconate, log K₁₁ decreases from 3.16 to 2.94 over the same range. Van't Hoff analysis gives ΔH = −7.2 ± 0.6 kJ mol⁻¹ for Cd–gluconate and −9.5 ± 0.8 kJ mol⁻¹ for Pb–gluconate, confirming exothermic complexation. The temperature dependence implies that Cd²⁺ and Pb²⁺ speciation by gluconate in topsoil shifts measurably between cold spring and hot summer conditions, with free metal ion activity increasing by 8–12% from 15 to 37 °C for representative soil pore-water compositions.

title: Compilation and critical evaluation of stability constants for divalent metal–citrate systems: a database for calcareous soil speciation modelling
abstract: No single peer-reviewed compilation focuses on metal–citrate stability constants specifically evaluated for use in calcareous soil speciation models. This book chapter presents a critical review and selection of log K values for the citrate complexes of Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Zn²⁺, Cu²⁺, Mn²⁺, Fe²⁺, Cd²⁺ and Pb²⁺ from publications between 1970 and 2021. Selection criteria include: ionic medium, temperature control, electrode calibration procedure, fitting software and number of independent titrations. For each metal, recommended values at I = 0.10 M and 25 °C are given with assigned uncertainties. Where fewer than three independent determinations exist, gaps are noted explicitly. The chapter also tabulates SIT interaction coefficients needed for correcting constants to lower ionic strengths representative of dilute soil solutions (I < 0.02 M). The recommended dataset is provided as a formatted input file for MINEQL+ and MINTEQ A2. Entries from the authors' own work constitute 11 of the 34 recommended constant values.

title: Conditional stability constants for Fe³⁺–citrate at pH 7.0–8.5: implications for iron solubility in calcareous soils
abstract: Iron deficiency (chlorosis) in grapevines and stone fruits grown on calcareous soils is economically significant in southern Pannonia. Although Fe³⁺–citrate chemistry is more complex than that of divalent metals, reliable conditional stability constants at alkaline pH are sparse. Measurements were carried out at I = 0.10 M NaClO₄, 25 °C, using a combined potentiometric–spectrophotometric approach. The ligand-to-metal ratio was held at 10:1 or higher to suppress Fe(OH)₃ precipitation. Three solution species were identified: FeHL (log K = 11.40 ± 0.10), FeL (log K = 10.08 ± 0.08) and FeL₂³⁻ (log K = 16.90 ± 0.15). At pH 8.0 and total citrate of 15 µM (median rhizosphere value from the authors' 2021 field study), modelled soluble Fe³⁺ activity is 3.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ M, about 40-fold above the minimum threshold estimated for Strategy I plant uptake. The data support the hypothesis that citrate exudation can partially substitute for phytosiderophore production in citrus and grapevine rootstocks under low-Fe conditions.

title: Mixed-ligand complexes of Zn²⁺ with citrate and malate in ternary solution systems: potentiometric evidence and speciation modelling at pH 6.5–8.5
abstract: Soil pore water contains multiple organic ligands simultaneously, yet most stability constant measurements consider binary metal–ligand systems. This study investigates the formation of ternary Zn²⁺–citrate–malate complexes at 25 °C and I = 0.10 M NaClO₄ by potentiometry over a wide pH range (4.5–9.5). Binary constants for Zn–citrate and Zn–malate, determined independently in the same medium, were used as fixed parameters during ternary system refinement with HYPERQUAD2013. A ternary species ZnCitMal³⁻ (log K_mixed = 8.71 ± 0.09) was identified; no binuclear ternary species were statistically supported. Speciation diagrams in a synthetic soil solution containing 10 µM citrate and 15 µM malate at pH 8.0 show that the mixed-ligand species accounts for 9–14% of total dissolved Zn, depending on Ca²⁺ competition. While modest, this fraction is non-negligible in mass-balance calculations for plant-available Zn fractions and should be included in updated speciation codes for calcareous soils.

title: Fluoride uptake profiles in artificially demineralised human enamel measured by electron probe microanalysis: effect of exposure time and concentration
abstract: Early enamel carious lesions were created in extracted human premolars using a 0.1 M acetic acid buffer at pH 4.5 over 96 hours, producing lesions with a mean mineral loss of 1 840 vol% μm as determined by transverse microradiography. Specimens were then treated with sodium fluoride solutions at 226, 450, or 900 ppm F for intervals of 1, 5, and 10 minutes. Fluoride concentration gradients across the enamel cross-section were measured by electron probe microanalysis at 2 μm steps. At 900 ppm F and 10-minute exposure, fluoride levels at the lesion surface reached 2 340 ppm, declining steeply beyond 20 μm depth. Increasing concentration produced significantly greater surface fluoride (p < 0.01) but not proportional subsurface penetration. Exposure time beyond 5 minutes yielded diminishing returns for subsurface uptake at all concentrations tested. These results suggest that short, higher-concentration applications may be preferable for surface hardening of incipient lesions, though subsurface remineralisation requires repeated cycling.

title: Comparison of remineralisation efficacy of CPP-ACP paste and 1 100 ppm fluoride dentifrice using a five-day pH cycling model in vitro
abstract: Bovine enamel blocks carrying standardised artificial lesions (mean integrated mineral loss 2 110 vol% μm by TMR) were randomly allocated to four treatment groups: CPP-ACP paste (10% Recalden-P, a fictional ingredient), 1 100 ppm fluoride dentifrice, a combination of both agents applied sequentially, and a negative control receiving only the remineralisation solution. A five-day pH cycling protocol alternated 6-hour demineralisation phases (pH 4.8, 0.1 M acetate) with 17-hour remineralisation phases. Mineral gain was measured by TMR after cycles 1, 3, and 5. The combination group showed the greatest mineral gain at day 5 (mean Δ∆Z = −640 vol% μm, indicating net recovery of 30% of initial mineral loss), compared with CPP-ACP alone (18%) and fluoride alone (22%). The negative control showed continued net mineral loss throughout. Lesion body mineral density recovered more slowly than the surface layer in all treatment groups. Differences between CPP-ACP alone and fluoride alone were not statistically significant (p = 0.14).

title: Quantitative light-induced fluorescence as a monitoring tool for incipient enamel lesion progression under sucrose challenge: a 12-week clinical pilot study
abstract: Thirty-two adult patients with at least one buccal white spot lesion on a permanent premolar or molar were recruited and divided into a high-sucrose-challenge group and a low-sucrose-challenge group based on dietary recall and Streptococcus mutans salivary counts. QLF measurements (ΔF fluorescence loss and lesion area) were recorded at baseline, 4, 8, and 12 weeks without any active remineralisation intervention, to establish natural progression data. At 12 weeks, the high-challenge group showed a mean ΔF change of −2.3 percentage units (95% CI −3.1 to −1.5), indicating lesion progression, while the low-challenge group showed a mean change of −0.4 units (95% CI −1.0 to +0.2), consistent with stability. Intraoperator reproducibility of QLF measurements was high (ICC = 0.91). Lesion area correlated moderately with ΔF (r = 0.67). The pilot confirmed QLF sensitivity to short-term progression and provided baseline variance estimates for future powered intervention trials.

title: Effect of CPP-ACP and fluoride toothpaste on white spot lesions adjacent to fixed orthodontic brackets: a 16-week randomised controlled trial
abstract: Patients undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment were randomised to three groups (n = 27 per group): CPP-ACP mousse applied nightly, fluoride toothpaste (1 450 ppm F) twice daily, or both combined. White spot lesions present at baseline or newly developed during treatment were measured by QLF at 0, 4, 8, 12, and 16 weeks. Primary outcome was ΔF change. Lesion area and lesion fluorescence recovery index (LFRI) were secondary outcomes. At 16 weeks, the combined group showed a mean ΔF improvement of +3.9 percentage units (SD 1.7), the fluoride-only group +2.8 units (SD 1.9), and the CPP-ACP-only group +2.3 units (SD 2.1). Pairwise comparisons showed a significant advantage for the combined group over CPP-ACP alone (p = 0.008) but not over fluoride alone (p = 0.08). No lesion showed complete resolution in any group. Patient-reported compliance was monitored by weekly SMS diaries and was above 85% in all groups.

title: Modeliranje gubitka kompetencija inženjera u uslovima organizacione tranzicije: preliminarna studija
abstract: U radu se istražuje kako organizaciona tranzicija – posebno spajanje dva proizvodna preduzeća – utiče na individualne kompetencije inženjera u prvim mesecima integracije. Korišćenjem upitnika sprovedenog u jednom metaloprerađivačkom preduzeću u Vojvodini (n=47 zaposlenih), identifikovane su tri dimenzije kompetencijskog pada: tehničke veštine, međutimska koordinacija i eksplicitno dokumentovano znanje. Podaci su analizirani metodom klaster analize, pri čemu su definisana dva tipična profila zaposlenih – 'otporni' i 'podložni' kompetencijskom padu. Rezultati pokazuju da zaposleni u međufunkcionalnim timovima pokazuju statistički značajno veće stope pada kompetencija u prvih šest meseci nakon spajanja (p < 0,05). Rad ukazuje na potrebu za dinamičkim modeliranjem ovih procesa kao osnove za buduće simulacione studije.

title: Dinamika prenosa znanja u međufunkcionalnim inženjerskim timovima: agent-baziran pristup
abstract: Ovaj rad razmatra specifičnosti prenosa znanja unutar međufunkcionalnih inženjerskih timova formiranih kao posledica postmerger reorganizacije u prerađivačkoj industriji. Razvijen je agent-baziran model u platformi NetLogo 5.3, koji simulira 30 agenata raspoređenih u dve fusionisane organizacione jedinice tokom perioda od 24 meseca. Svaki agent karakteriše se skupom atributa: stepen specijalističkog znanja, socijalna mreža kontakata, motivacija i kapacitet učenja. Model uključuje mehanizme zaboravljanja (forgetting) bazirane na Ebbinghausovoj krivoj i mehanizme reaktivacije znanja kroz formalne treninge. Simulacioni eksperimenti pokazuju da timovi sa izbalansiranom zastupljenošću oba prethodno odvojena preduzeća prenose znanje efikasnije za 31% u poređenju sa timovima koji su dominantno sastavljeni od zaposlenih jednog preduzeća. Ograničenje modela je odsustvo validacije na longitudinalnim empirijskim podacima.

title: Calibrating Forgetting Rates in Organisational ABMs: A Sensitivity Analysis Using Empirical Data from Two Serbian Manufacturing Mergers
abstract: Forgetting rate is one of the least empirically grounded parameters in agent-based models of organisational knowledge. This study addresses the calibration problem by fitting forgetting rate parameters against longitudinal skill-assessment records collected from two Serbian manufacturing companies that underwent merger integration between 2010 and 2014 (combined n=112 employees, 18-month observation window, quarterly assessments). Six candidate forgetting functions – including linear decay, exponential decay, and a step-function variant tied to role changes – were compared using root mean squared error against observed competency scores. The exponential decay function with a half-life of 8.4 months provided the best fit (RMSE = 0.17 on a normalised scale). The calibrated parameters were then embedded in an AnyLogic simulation and used to compare four integration timeline scenarios. Findings indicate that the choice of forgetting function substantially alters policy-relevant predictions, with linear and exponential models diverging by up to 28% in projected competency levels at the 24-month mark.

title: Simulaciono modeliranje postmerger integracije kao alat za upravljanje ljudskim resursima: pregled literature i istraživački okvir
abstract: Rad daje sistematski pregled literature objavljene između 2000. i 2017. godine koja se bavi primenom simulacionih metoda – posebno agent-baziranih modela i sistemske dinamike – u kontekstu postmerger upravljanja ljudskim resursima u manufacturing sektoru. Analizirano je 68 radova identifikovanih pretragom baza Scopus i Web of Science. Rezultati pokazuju da dominantni pristup u literaturi zanemaruje kompetencijski pad kao zasebnu varijablu i uglavnom modelira samo tok zaposlenih, a ne kvalitet njihovog znanja. Predložen je integrativni istraživački okvir koji kombinuje teoriju organizacionog učenja, model kompetencijskog pada i mrežne teorije prenosa znanja. Okvir služi kao osnova za razvoj simulacionih alata prilagođenih potrebama HR menadžera u spajajućim prerađivačkim preduzećima. Identifikovane su četiri prioritetne oblasti za buduća istraživanja.

title: Cross-Functional Team Composition and Knowledge Retention After Merger: Evidence from a Discrete-Event and Agent-Based Hybrid Model
abstract: We present a hybrid simulation model combining discrete-event and agent-based components to investigate how cross-functional team composition affects knowledge retention in the 36 months following a manufacturing firm merger. The discrete-event layer models project workflows and task allocation, while the agent-based layer represents individual knowledge states and interpersonal learning interactions. The hybrid architecture is implemented in AnyLogic 8.4 and parameterised using HR records and skill assessments from a longitudinal dataset collected at an automotive-component supplier in northern Serbia (n=89 employees). Four team composition strategies are evaluated: random reassignment, competency-matching, social-network-preserving assignment, and a hybrid heuristic developed in consultation with the company's HR department. Social-network-preserving assignment yields the highest aggregate knowledge retention (12.4% above the random baseline at month 36) but underperforms on project throughput in the first twelve months. The hybrid heuristic balances both objectives with a 7.1% knowledge retention gain and no statistically significant throughput reduction.

title: Representing Informal Mentoring in Agent-Based Models of Post-Merger Knowledge Transfer
abstract: Informal mentoring relationships are frequently cited as a primary channel for tacit knowledge transfer following organisational mergers, yet they are rarely represented explicitly in simulation models. This paper proposes and evaluates three mechanisms for encoding informal mentoring in an ABM: (1) a random-encounter mechanism with proximity weighting, (2) a directed preferential attachment mechanism based on competency gap, and (3) an empirically derived network seeded from sociometric survey data. The three mechanisms are implemented in AnyLogic 8.7 and tested against a 12-month observational dataset from a Vojvodina food-processing company that merged two production sites in 2019 (n=61 employees). Validation against held-out quarterly competency assessments shows that the empirically derived network mechanism produces the closest match to observed outcomes (RMSE = 0.13), while the random-encounter mechanism systematically underestimates knowledge transfer rates in the first four months post-merger. The paper provides open model documentation to support replication.

title: Workforce Simulation as a Decision-Support Tool for HR Managers in Manufacturing Mergers: A Prototype and Usability Assessment
abstract: This paper describes the design, implementation, and usability evaluation of a decision-support prototype that wraps an agent-based simulation model in a graphical interface intended for use by HR managers without modelling expertise. The underlying ABM, calibrated on data from three completed mergers in the Serbian manufacturing sector, simulates knowledge transfer and competency decay across a 36-month integration horizon. The interface allows users to specify integration timeline, team reassignment policy, and training budget, and returns visualised projections of aggregate competency levels and estimated productivity impact. Usability was assessed through a think-aloud study with eight HR managers from companies at the Novi Sad Science and Technology Park and affiliated firms. Participants rated the tool positively on task completion and output clarity (SUS score 74.5) but identified model parameter transparency as a limitation. The paper discusses implications for deploying simulation tools in practitioner contexts and outlines planned improvements based on the usability findings.

title: Decay Asymmetry in Merged Engineering Teams: Do Employees from the Acquired Firm Lose Competencies Faster?
abstract: This preprint reports preliminary findings from an ongoing study examining whether employees from the acquired firm in a manufacturing merger experience systematically faster competency decay than employees from the acquiring firm. Using anonymised longitudinal skill-assessment records from four mergers completed in Serbia and Hungary between 2018 and 2023 (combined n=204 employees, 24-month observation per merger), we fit individual competency trajectories using mixed-effects models with firm-of-origin as a grouping variable. Results indicate a statistically significant decay asymmetry: acquired-firm employees show a mean annual competency decline of 14.2% versus 8.7% for acquiring-firm employees (difference 5.5 percentage points, 95% CI [3.1, 7.9]), controlling for role change, age, and pre-merger competency level. The asymmetry is most pronounced in technical skills and weakest in process knowledge. We discuss alternative explanations including social marginalisation, reduced access to informal knowledge networks, and differential exposure to training resources. An agent-based model encoding the asymmetry mechanism is under development.

title: Verification of Combined Heat and Power Savings Under IPMVP Option C: Complicating Factors and Case Evidence
abstract: Combined heat and power installations in industrial facilities create verification challenges for Option C protocols because total facility electricity import decreases while on-site generation increases, requiring metering of both streams. This paper analyses three CHP projects in Vojvodina where Option C was applied at the utility boundary. The baseline model must account for CHP dispatch decisions that vary with energy prices, adding a dispatch variable to the regression. Results show that failing to account for dispatch introduces a downward bias of 9–14% in estimated electricity savings. The paper also addresses the allocation of savings between the CHP measure and complementary efficiency measures implemented concurrently, proposing an attribution procedure based on partial regression coefficients. Estimated savings across the three sites ranged from 1,100 to 4,800 MWh/year with relative uncertainties of 6–11% at the 90% confidence level.

title: Applying value-stream mapping to identify waste in a precast hollow-core slab facility
abstract: Value-stream mapping (VSM) was applied to the full production sequence of a hollow-core slab facility with an annual output of approximately 28,000 square metres. Current-state maps were constructed through three weeks of floor-level observation and timed walks, capturing 11 distinct process steps from raw material receipt to dispatch yard staging. The analysis identified waiting and over-processing as the dominant waste categories, accounting together for 39% of total lead time. Transport loops between the curing yard and the finishing area were measured at a combined daily distance of 1.2 km per operator. Future-state maps were developed under two scenarios—one preserving existing equipment layout, one incorporating a partial cell redesign—projecting lead-time reductions of 22% and 34% respectively. The paper provides a step-by-step mapping template adapted to the physical constraints of long-line prestressed concrete production.

title: Moral Arguments and Technical Solutions: Framing Online Pornography Regulation in EU Policy Documents, 2000–2010
abstract: This article examines how European Union institutions framed the question of online pornography regulation during the first decade of widespread broadband access. Drawing on a corpus of 47 policy documents, parliamentary debates, and commission communications published between 2000 and 2010, the study applies Fairclough's critical discourse analysis framework to trace shifts in argumentative patterns. The analysis identifies three dominant rhetorical formations: child protection imperatives, technical-neutrality frames, and free expression counter-arguments. Findings indicate that child protection rhetoric was invoked in 83 percent of legislative proposals but was consistently decoupled from empirical evidence about harm incidence. The article argues that this decoupling allowed regulatory advocates to maintain moral urgency while avoiding rigorous impact assessment requirements. The study contributes to scholarly understanding of how normative and technical discourses interact in EU digital policymaking and offers a baseline for comparison with later age-verification debates.

title: Between Censorship and Consent: Serbian Media Legislation and the Regulation of Sexual Content Online
abstract: This chapter examines how Serbian media law has addressed sexually explicit online content since the adoption of the Electronic Communications Law in 2010. The author reviews legislative texts, regulatory guidance issued by the Regulatory Authority for Electronic Media, and parliamentary hearing transcripts collected through a freedom of information request. The analysis shows that Serbian legislators imported conceptual categories from EU directives without adapting them to the domestic institutional context, producing ambiguities that regulators have handled inconsistently. Three case studies are presented involving administrative proceedings against domestic video-sharing platforms between 2011 and 2014. The chapter situates these findings within broader scholarship on post-socialist media law transplantation, arguing that the adoption of Western regulatory vocabulary has not been accompanied by equivalent enforcement capacity or deliberative tradition. Implications for Serbia's EU accession negotiations in the digital policy chapter are discussed.

title: Age Verification as a Governance Technology: Comparing Legislative Proposals in the United Kingdom, France, and Germany
abstract: This comparative study analyses age-verification legislative proposals in the United Kingdom, France, and Germany between 2014 and 2018, examining how each national context shaped the technical and procedural requirements placed on platforms hosting adult content. Document analysis was combined with 18 semi-structured interviews with policy advisors, civil liberties advocates, and platform representatives conducted in 2017. The study finds that while all three proposals invoked child protection as primary justification, they differed substantially in their treatment of privacy risks, liability allocation, and third-party verification infrastructure. German proposals showed the strongest engagement with data minimisation principles, reflecting established constitutional privacy norms, whereas the UK proposal prioritised implementation speed over privacy safeguards. The French case occupied an intermediate position, influenced by ongoing debates within the Conseil Supérieur de l'Audiovisuel. The article draws on governmentality theory to argue that age verification functions as a technology for redistributing responsibility from states to platforms and individuals.

title: Protecting Children or Governing Sexuality? Discourse Analysis of Parliamentary Debates on Internet Pornography in Serbia, 2012–2017
abstract: This article presents a systematic discourse analysis of Serbian parliamentary debates containing references to internet pornography between 2012 and 2017. A corpus of 214 parliamentary sessions was searched using keyword queries, yielding 38 relevant debate segments involving 61 individual speakers from across the political spectrum. The study codes argumentative moves along three dimensions: the construction of harm, the construction of the subject requiring protection, and the articulation of state responsibility. Results show that speakers predominantly constructed harm in developmental and psychological terms, drawing on popular psychology rather than peer-reviewed evidence. Minority voices raised free expression and governmental overreach objections but were systematically marginalised in debate structure. The article also documents cross-party consensus on the need for age barriers while revealing fundamental disagreement on implementation, which has prevented any legislation from passing. The findings extend existing European research on parliamentary pornography debates into a post-socialist democratic context.

title: Platform Self-Regulation and Adult Content: Terms of Service as Quasi-Legislation
abstract: This paper examines the terms of service and community standards of ten major platforms that host or have hosted significant volumes of adult content, analysing how these documents function as a form of private regulation that substitutes for or anticipates public legislation. The corpus covers document versions published between 2015 and 2020, totalling 340 distinct document snapshots retrieved from web archives. The analysis focuses on definitional strategies — how platforms define prohibited content — and on enforcement mechanisms and appeals procedures. Findings indicate substantial convergence in prohibition language despite differences in platform type and jurisdiction, suggesting coordinated drafting or common legal advisory influence. The paper argues that this convergence has normalised a restrictive and vague regulatory standard that affects legitimate adult content producers, sex workers' safety information, and LGBTQ+ health content as collateral casualties. The study contributes to scholarship on platform power and the democratic deficit of private content governance.

title: Problematising Age Verification: Technical Feasibility and Civil Liberties in the European Digital Services Act Debate
abstract: This conference paper, presented at the 2021 European Communication Research Association annual conference, examines how age verification was discussed during the drafting and negotiation of the Digital Services Act between 2020 and 2021. The paper draws on a document corpus of 92 items including European Commission working papers, European Parliament committee amendments, and lobbying submissions obtained via the EU Transparency Register. It traces how technical feasibility arguments were used strategically both by advocates of mandatory age verification and by civil liberties organisations opposed to it. The paper finds that technical complexity was frequently invoked as a reason to defer specific requirements to delegated acts, effectively postponing hard political choices. The role of age estimation technology providers as expert witnesses in committee hearings is examined in detail, revealing a pattern in which commercial interests shaped the apparent technical consensus. The paper situates these findings within scholarship on regulatory capture in EU digital governance.

title: The Absent Beneficiary: Children in Age-Verification Policy Texts
abstract: This article examines how children are constructed as policy subjects in European and national age-verification legislation and regulatory guidance published between 2018 and 2023. Drawing on ten documents across five jurisdictions — France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and the European Union — the study applies membership categorisation analysis to identify how regulatory texts invoke childhood as a legitimating category while abstracting actual children from view. The analysis finds that children function primarily as rhetorical resources — invoked in preambles and objectives clauses but absent from implementation and monitoring provisions, where questions of technical design dominate. The paper argues that this structural absence enables policymakers to claim protective intent while designing systems whose primary effects concern platform liability and state surveillance capacity rather than children's experiential welfare. The discussion draws on sociological scholarship on children as social actors and proposes evaluation criteria that centre children's documented information-seeking behaviours.

title: Regulating Pornography Through Infrastructure: DNS Blocking, Payment Processor Policies, and App Store Rules
abstract: This preprint examines three infrastructural mechanisms through which access to pornographic content is regulated without direct legislative mandate: DNS-level blocking by internet service providers, payment processor acceptable use policies, and app store distribution rules. The study compiles a dataset of 61 documented cases of infrastructural restriction affecting adult content platforms between 2019 and 2024, drawn from news sources, regulatory filings, and platform communications. For each mechanism, the paper analyses the decision-making process, the extent of procedural transparency, and available evidence on collateral effects on non-prohibited content. The analysis finds that payment processor policies have become the most consequential single mechanism, able to effectively demonetise entire categories of content without any adjudicative process. The paper argues that infrastructural regulation constitutes a distinct regulatory mode that operates largely outside democratic accountability frameworks and warrants separate scholarly and policy attention.

title: Serbia and the Digital Services Act: Alignment Pressures, Regulatory Capacity, and the Question of Adult Content Platforms
abstract: This article assesses the implications of the EU Digital Services Act for Serbian digital media regulation as part of the accession process, with specific attention to provisions applicable to platforms hosting adult content. The study is based on analysis of Serbian government alignment reports submitted to the European Commission between 2021 and 2025, supplemented by interviews with six officials from the Regulatory Authority for Electronic Media and two representatives of domestic hosting providers conducted in 2025. The analysis identifies a significant gap between the procedural requirements of the DSA — particularly around transparent content moderation and complaint mechanisms — and current Serbian regulatory practice, which relies heavily on discretionary administrative authority. The article traces how adult content provisions, politically sensitive domestically, have been systematically downplayed in official alignment communications. It argues that EU accession conditionality, while creating external pressure for formal change, is insufficient to address underlying institutional capacity deficits.

title: Does Fact-Checking Coverage Change Trust? A Quasi-Experiment Using a Natural Variation in Exposure
abstract: This study exploits a naturally occurring variation in the regional distribution of a fact-checking column published in a Vojvodina weekly newspaper to assess whether regular exposure to fact-checking content affects readers' overall trust in media. Readers in municipalities where the paper had more than 15 percent household penetration were compared with readers in matched low-penetration municipalities using propensity score matching (N = 512 matched pairs drawn from the 2017 panel wave). Respondents in high-penetration areas scored 0.41 points higher on a composite media literacy scale (p = 0.003) but did not differ significantly on a general media trust scale. A separate item asking about trust in fact-checking as a practice showed a positive association with exposure (OR = 1.67, 95% CI 1.21–2.31). The results suggest that fact-checking exposure builds selective genre-level trust without necessarily transferring to trust in media institutions broadly.

title: Digitalisation and Workforce Restructuring in Serbian Commercial Television, 2010–2017
abstract: This article traces workforce changes at Serbian commercial television broadcasters across the period of mandatory digital switchover, completed in 2015, using data from the national broadcasting regulator's annual licence reports combined with 41 interviews with production managers and technical staff. Total permanent employment in television production fell by 26 percent between 2010 and 2017 at the nine largest commercial broadcasters surveyed. Technical staff experienced the sharpest contraction, losing 38 percent of positions, while on-screen presenting roles were more stable. The article examines how digitalisation was used rhetorically by management as justification for redundancies that respondents attributed primarily to revenue pressures and ownership rationalisation strategies unrelated to technical change. It contributes to debates about technological determinism in media labour studies by showing that digitalisation functioned more as an enabling condition for restructuring than as its direct cause.

title: A stochastic Galerkin finite element scheme for the Darcy flow equation with log-normal permeability field
abstract: This paper develops and analyses a stochastic Galerkin finite element method for the steady-state Darcy flow equation in a two-dimensional bounded domain, where the permeability is modelled as a log-normal random field parameterised by a truncated Karhunen–Loève expansion with 12 terms. The variational formulation is posed in a tensor-product space combining piecewise linear finite elements on a uniform triangular mesh with polynomial chaos basis functions of total degree up to 4. Existence and uniqueness of the Galerkin solution are established via an inf-sup argument adapted to the stochastic setting. A priori error estimates are derived showing algebraic convergence in both the physical mesh parameter h and the polynomial degree p. Numerical experiments on benchmark permeability fields with correlation lengths 0.1 and 0.3 confirm the theoretical rates, with the mean and variance of the pressure head converging at rates consistent with O(h^2) and O(p^{-1.8}) respectively. The computational cost is compared against a standard Monte Carlo estimator using 10,000 samples, showing a factor-of-6 reduction in work for comparable accuracy.

title: Convergence of a sparse collocation scheme for parabolic SPDEs modelling heat conduction in heterogeneous media
abstract: This work examines sparse grid stochastic collocation for a parabolic equation modelling transient heat conduction in a two-dimensional domain with a spatially varying, uncertain thermal conductivity. The conductivity field is parameterised by 20 Karhunen–Loève modes, and Clenshaw–Curtis abscissae on a Smolyak sparse grid of level 5 are used in the stochastic domain, yielding 2,001 collocation points. Each deterministic subproblem is discretised with piecewise quadratic finite elements on a mesh with 6,400 elements and integrated in time with the implicit Euler scheme at timestep 0.01 over the interval [0, 1]. We prove convergence in the mean-square sense under standard regularity assumptions and derive convergence rates that depend on the decay of the Karhunen–Loève eigenvalues. For an exponential covariance kernel with correlation length 0.25, the total error reaches 3.7 × 10^{−4} in the H1 seminorm at the final time, compared with 8.2 × 10^{−4} for an equivalent-cost isotropic full-tensor grid. The study also includes a sensitivity analysis isolating the contribution of individual stochastic modes to the output variance.

title: Monte Carlo versus stochastic Galerkin for fluid–structure interaction under random loading: a practical comparison
abstract: A fluid–structure interaction problem in which a thin elastic plate is immersed in a viscous flow with an uncertain inlet velocity profile is treated as a testbed for comparing Monte Carlo and stochastic Galerkin solvers. The inlet velocity uncertainty is described by a truncated Gaussian random variable with standard deviation equal to 15 percent of the mean, and the plate's bending stiffness is modelled as a uniform random variable on [0.8D, 1.2D]. Monte Carlo simulations use 50,000 samples generated by a Sobol quasi-random sequence, while the stochastic Galerkin formulation employs Legendre polynomial bases of degree 3 in each stochastic dimension. Both approaches are implemented within a partitioned iterative coupling scheme using OpenFOAM for the fluid and an in-house FEM code for the structure. For quantities of interest such as maximum plate deflection and drag coefficient, the stochastic Galerkin method achieves comparable accuracy to quasi-Monte Carlo at roughly one-quarter of the computational cost. However, the Galerkin approach requires substantially more implementation effort and shows sensitivity to the coupling iteration tolerance.

title: Regularity of solutions to the stochastic Navier–Stokes equations with multiplicative noise in weighted Sobolev spaces
abstract: This paper addresses the theoretical regularity of weak solutions to the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations driven by multiplicative Gaussian noise, in a two-dimensional periodic domain. The noise acts through a bounded linear operator in L2 with a Hilbert–Schmidt norm bounded by 0.3 in appropriate units. Using an energy-estimate approach combined with a stopping-time argument, we establish that the unique local strong solution belongs to L^4(Ω; L^∞([0,T]; H^1)) ∩ L^2(Ω; L^2([0,T]; H^2)) for T up to a stopping time τ_R that is positive almost surely for each truncation level R. The main technical contribution is a weighted Gronwall lemma that accommodates the multiplicative noise term without invoking global Lipschitz assumptions on the noise coefficient. These regularity results provide the analytic foundation for constructing convergent numerical schemes of the type developed in companion papers. No numerical experiments are included; the work is purely analytical.

title: Uncertainty propagation in linear viscoelasticity: a polynomial chaos approach with application to polymer creep
abstract: Creep behaviour of a viscoelastic polymer bar under constant axial load is modelled using a Boltzmann integral constitutive law in which the relaxation modulus is treated as a random process with a Matérn covariance function. A Karhunen–Loève expansion truncated at 8 terms captures 94 percent of the total variance. Polynomial chaos expansions of total degree 3 are constructed for the time-dependent displacement field, resulting in a system of 165 coupled deterministic integral equations. These are solved by a Gauss–Legendre quadrature rule on the time interval [0, 1000] s with 200 integration points per equation. The mean creep compliance curve and its 90 percent confidence band are extracted from the chaos coefficients and compared against 20,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Relative error in the mean curve is below 0.6 percent throughout the time interval; the 90 percent confidence band width is recovered within 1.8 percent. The effect of truncation order is studied systematically, showing diminishing returns beyond degree 3 for this covariance structure.

title: An adaptive stochastic finite element method for elasticity problems with random voids: local error indicators and refinement strategy
abstract: We develop an adaptive stochastic finite element procedure for a two-dimensional plane-stress elasticity problem in which a random number of elliptical voids is embedded in the domain, each with random position, size, and orientation. The void geometry is parameterised via a marked point process with Poisson intensity 0.05 per unit area and log-normal size distribution. The physical mesh is adapted using a residual-based a posteriori error indicator computed from the deterministic part of the Galerkin solution, while the stochastic polynomial degree is refined independently based on a stochastic residual estimator. Starting from a coarse mesh of 512 elements and polynomial degree 1, the adaptive loop terminates after 9 refinement cycles with a final mesh of 3,840 elements and mixed polynomial degrees ranging from 1 to 4. The total error in the energy norm is reduced by a factor of 11 compared to the uniform-refinement baseline at the same number of degrees of freedom. Applications to structural reliability estimation under microstructural uncertainty are discussed.

title: Quasi-Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification in compressible flow simulations with uncertain boundary conditions
abstract: This study applies randomised quasi-Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in a one-dimensional compressible Euler flow problem in which the upstream Mach number and total temperature are jointly uncertain. The joint distribution is modelled as a bivariate normal with means 0.4 and 420 K, standard deviations 0.03 and 12 K, and correlation 0.35, calibrated from wind-tunnel measurement records. Scrambled Sobol sequences of size 2^{14} are used as the primary estimator, with a 32-sample pilot study for variance estimation. The quantities of interest are the downstream pressure ratio and the shock position. Randomised quasi-Monte Carlo achieves a root-mean-square error of 1.2 × 10^{−4} for the pressure ratio at 2^{12} samples, compared with 4.8 × 10^{−4} for plain Monte Carlo at the same sample size. A first-order Sobol sensitivity analysis shows that the upstream Mach number accounts for 71 percent of the output variance in the pressure ratio, while total temperature contributes 22 percent.

title: Stochastic collocation for diffusion-dominated transport in porous media with uncertain porosity fields: implementation notes and benchmark results
abstract: This book chapter provides a self-contained treatment of stochastic collocation for a convection-diffusion equation modelling solute transport in a saturated porous medium, intended as a reference for practitioners. The porosity field is parameterised by a beta-distributed random variable with shape parameters 4 and 6, and the diffusion-to-convection ratio (Péclet number) ranges from 0.5 to 50 across the benchmark suite. Gauss–Jacobi quadrature points matching the beta distribution are used at collocation levels 3, 5, and 7. Spatial discretisation uses the streamline-upwind Petrov–Galerkin stabilisation on structured meshes. The chapter documents implementation pitfalls encountered with high-Péclet-number cases, including spurious oscillations in variance estimates, and proposes a simple variance-based clipping strategy that reduces these artefacts by approximately 80 percent. Reference output statistics for five benchmark configurations are tabulated to three significant figures, allowing straightforward comparison with other solvers. Source code snippets in Python are included.

title: Pressure–volume relationships for sunflower oil filter cakes formed from bleaching-earth suspensions
abstract: Compressibility of filter cakes formed during batch pressure filtration of sunflower oil bleaching-earth suspensions was studied using a laboratory dead-end cell operating between 0.05 and 0.5 MPa at 60 °C. Specific cake resistance was determined by Ruth's filtration theory applied to constant-pressure runs. The compressibility coefficient α ranged from 0.41 to 0.68 depending on bleaching-earth grade and oil moisture content (0.05–0.20 % w/w). At 0.3 MPa the resistance reached 2.1 × 10¹¹ m/kg for the finest earth fraction (d₅₀ = 8 µm). A power-law model fitted the resistance–pressure data with R² > 0.97 across all grades tested. Moisture content above 0.12 % significantly increased compressibility, suggesting that pre-drying the oil feed reduces long-term pressure-drop build-up in industrial leaf filters. Results provide baseline compressibility parameters for process simulation of industrial filtration steps in refined sunflower oil production.

title: Fouling behaviour of tubular ceramic membranes during cross-flow microfiltration of degummed sunflower oil
abstract: Cross-flow microfiltration of degummed sunflower oil was examined using α-alumina tubular membranes with pore sizes of 0.2 and 0.5 µm at cross-flow velocities of 1.0, 2.5, and 4.0 m/s and transmembrane pressures of 0.05–0.35 MPa. Permeate flux declined by 65–80 % within the first 30 min of operation regardless of operating condition, indicating rapid pore constriction by phospholipid aggregates. The 0.5-µm membrane at 3.5 m/s and 0.15 MPa gave the highest steady-state flux of 38 L/(m²·h) with filtrate turbidity below 3 NTU. Resistance-in-series analysis attributed 55 % of total resistance to reversible concentration polarisation and 45 % to irreversible fouling at these conditions. Alkaline cleaning (0.5 % NaOH, 50 °C, 20 min) restored 88 % of initial water permeability. The critical flux concept was applied to map stable operating windows for this oil type.

title: Dead-end filtration of corn germ oil miscella: influence of solvent-to-oil ratio on cake structure and resistance
abstract: Corn germ oil miscella at hexane-to-oil ratios of 4:1, 7:1, and 10:1 (v/v) was filtered through precoated leaf filters in a laboratory dead-end configuration to study how solvent content alters cake porosity and resistance. Reducing the ratio from 10:1 to 4:1 raised crude oil viscosity from 0.6 to 1.9 mPa·s at 25 °C and decreased filter cake permeability by 40 %. However, cake moisture (solvent retention) fell from 38 % to 22 % at the lower ratio, reducing downstream solvent-recovery load. An optimal ratio of 6:1 was identified where pressure drop remained below 0.25 MPa for 4 h of continuous operation with a 1 % w/w diatomite precoat of 2 kg/m². Cake washing efficiency with fresh hexane was also tested; three wash stages at a wash ratio of 1.5 recovered 96 % of residual oil. The study provides sizing data applicable to continuous rotary vacuum filters in solvent-extraction plants.

title: Solid–liquid separation in vegetable oil processing: filtration fundamentals and industrial practice
abstract: This chapter reviews the theoretical foundations and industrial applications of solid–liquid separation in edible-oil refining. Coverage begins with the governing equations for constant-pressure and constant-rate dead-end filtration, including compressible cake theory and the role of filter aids. Cross-flow microfiltration of crude and partially refined oils is discussed with reference to fouling mechanisms, critical flux, and membrane selection. Industrial filter types encountered in oil processing—plate-and-frame, vertical leaf, rotary vacuum drum, and tubular membrane systems—are described with emphasis on scale-up parameters and maintenance considerations. A section on filter-aid sustainability addresses diatomite supply concerns and emerging alternatives such as cellulose-based and rice-hull-ash materials. Case data from sunflower, rapeseed, and soybean processing are used throughout to illustrate design calculations. The chapter closes with a worked example for sizing a leaf filter for a 200 t/day crude sunflower oil plant.

title: Rice hull ash as an alternative filter aid in dead-end filtration of crude sunflower oil: performance and food-safety assessment
abstract: Amorphous silica derived from controlled combustion of rice hull at 600 °C was evaluated as a diatomite substitute in dead-end pressure filtration of crude sunflower oil at 0.2 MPa and 60 °C. Four rice hull ash (RHA) preparations with BET surface areas of 120–310 m²/g were screened against a reference food-grade diatomite. At equal precoat loading (1.5 kg/m²), the RHA preparation with 210 m²/g surface area matched diatomite in turbidity removal (final filtrate < 4 NTU) and gave 12 % lower cake resistance. Heavy-metal leaching tests showed arsenic and lead concentrations in filtrate below EC food contact limits. Phosphorus content of the filtrate decreased by 22 % relative to unfiltered oil, suggesting partial degumming action by the alkaline surface of RHA. Economic estimates indicate that RHA produced from local rice processing waste could reduce filter-aid material cost by 30–40 % for regional oil mills. Regulatory status under EU additive legislation is discussed.

title: Pilot-scale cross-flow ultrafiltration of crude sunflower oil: operating window determination and membrane cleaning protocol
abstract: A 0.8-m² spiral-wound polyethersulfone ultrafiltration module (molecular weight cut-off 50 kDa) was tested for clarification and partial degumming of crude sunflower oil at pilot scale. Operating pressure was varied from 0.1 to 0.6 MPa at cross-flow velocities of 0.5–3.0 m/s and oil temperatures of 40–70 °C. Steady-state permeate flux peaked at 22 L/(m²·h) at 0.25 MPa, 2.5 m/s, and 60 °C. Above 0.35 MPa, flux plateaued due to concentration polarisation, confirmed by flux–velocity experiments. Phospholipid retention exceeded 95 % at all conditions, reducing phosphorus from 320 to below 15 mg/kg in the permeate. Irreversible fouling after 8 h was quantified at 18 % flux loss; a two-step cleaning sequence (0.3 % citric acid, then 0.5 % NaOH) restored 94 % of clean-water flux. Energy consumption was estimated at 0.9–1.4 kWh per litre of clarified oil, providing a comparison point with conventional filtration and centrifugation.

title: Modelling pressure-drop build-up in continuous rotary vacuum drum filters processing bleached sunflower oil
abstract: A semi-empirical model for predicting pressure-drop evolution over an operating cycle of a rotary vacuum drum filter was developed and validated against measurements from a 4 m² pilot drum operating at a reference edible-oil plant in Vojvodina. The model couples Ruth's cake-growth equation with a time-varying compressibility parameter that accounts for gradual pore plugging by sub-micron phospholipid fragments. Fitted compressibility exponents showed a systematic increase from 0.44 at cycle start to 0.61 after 6 h, attributed to progressive migration of fines into the cake interior. Simulations reproduced measured pressure drop within ±8 % across six production batches. Sensitivity analysis indicated that reducing feed turbidity from 150 to 60 NTU extended time-to-maximum-pressure by 38 %. The model is implemented as a spreadsheet tool intended for use by plant engineers to schedule filter-cloth replacement and precoat re-application intervals.

title: Hydrodynamic similarity analysis of a 150 L pilot bioreactor for lactic acid production: geometric, kinematic and dynamic approaches
abstract: A 150 L stainless-steel stirred-tank bioreactor was characterised using three classical hydrodynamic similarity frameworks—geometric, kinematic and dynamic—to assess its equivalence to a validated 10 L bench unit. Geometric similarity was confirmed (D/T = 0.36, C/T = 0.25, four standard baffles). Kinematic similarity was evaluated by mapping dimensionless velocity profiles via PIV at matched Reynolds numbers (Re = 4.2 × 10⁴). Power number (Np = 1.81) agreed with the bench-scale value within 4%. Dynamic similarity was assessed through impeller-to-vessel-volume power dissipation maps; volumetric energy dissipation rate (ε) was 0.18 W/kg at the design operating point (250 rpm, 150 L), compared with 0.21 W/kg at 10 L under equivalent P/V conditions. The 14% discrepancy in local ε near the impeller discharge stream was attributed to wall proximity effects and was reduced to 6% after impeller repositioning. Practical recommendations for maintaining hydrodynamic similarity during equipment procurement are provided.
