title: A Piecewise-Linear Approximation for the Backlash Nonlinearity and Its Effect on Bifurcation Structure
abstract: Gear-rattle simulations commonly represent the backlash clearance with a piecewise-smooth restoring force that is zero inside the gap and linearly elastic outside. This book chapter reviews the mathematical structure of such models, discusses smooth approximations including hyperbolic tangent and cubic spline regularisations, and assesses their accuracy against exact piecewise solutions for representative parameter sets. Numerical experiments with three regularisation schemes show that the hyperbolic tangent approximation with a steepness parameter κ ≥ 50 reproduces Poincaré sections within 1.5 % mean point distance of the exact model for periodic orbits, but overestimates the width of chaotic windows by up to 18 % near co-dimension-two bifurcation points. The chapter also discusses implications for continuation software that requires smooth right-hand sides. Practical recommendations are given for selecting regularisation parameters when using commercial multibody codes that do not natively support non-smooth dynamics.
venue: Advances in Nonlinear Mechanical Systems – Selected Topics (Springer-Verlag regional series)

title: Effect of Gear-Mesh Stiffness Fluctuation on Rattle Intensity in a Three-Speed Automated Manual Transmission
abstract: Most gear-rattle studies treat the mesh stiffness of loaded pairs as constant, ignoring the parametric excitation arising from tooth-contact stiffness variation. This paper includes time-varying mesh stiffness as a second parametric excitation alongside engine torque fluctuation in a three-DOF model of a three-speed automated manual transmission. The stiffness variation is approximated as a rectangular wave with amplitude ratio 1.6 and tooth-pass frequency derived from gear geometry. Time–frequency analysis via short-time Fourier transform of simulated impact force signals reveals that stiffness fluctuation creates sideband components around the tooth-pass frequency that can lock the rattling gear pair into stable periodic orbits at otherwise chaotic operating points. Rattle intensity, defined as the RMS of normalised impact force, decreases by 12–31 % when stiffness fluctuation is included, depending on idle speed. The finding suggests that intentional mesh-stiffness tuning could be exploited as a passive rattle-mitigation strategy.

title: Numerical and Experimental Comparison of Impact Force Spectra in a Gear-Rattle Test Rig with Adjustable Backlash
abstract: A custom gear-rattle test rig is described in which backlash between a spur gear pair is set with shim-adjustable centre distance, allowing values from 0.05 mm to 0.40 mm in steps of 0.05 mm. A servo motor replicates measured engine torque irregularity signals from a four-cylinder passenger-car engine at 700 rpm and 850 rpm idle. Impact forces are inferred from acceleration signals on the gear body using calibrated frequency-response functions. Predicted impact force spectra from a three-DOF model show agreement with measurements within 3 dB across the 20–500 Hz range for backlash values up to 0.25 mm; discrepancies grow to 7 dB at the largest backlash, attributed to housing flexibility not captured in the lumped model. Coherence between input torque signal and impact response exceeds 0.85 below 200 Hz, confirming that the rig reproduces automotive idle conditions with adequate fidelity for model validation purposes.

title: Codimension-Two Bifurcations in a Gear-Rattle Oscillator with Both Backlash and Preload Nonlinearities
abstract: Preloaded gear pairs, found in anti-backlash mechanisms and certain CVT-adjacent transmissions, exhibit a dual nonlinearity: a dead-zone backlash region flanked by two linear stiffness zones of different magnitude due to the preload spring. This paper analyses the codimension-two bifurcation structure of such a system using the MATCONT continuation toolbox. The parameter plane spanned by excitation amplitude and preload force reveals cusp points, Bogdanov–Takens points, and a region of co-existing stable attractors bounded by fold-of-limit-cycles curves. At a preload of 0.8 N·m, the rattle-free operating region expands by a factor of 2.3 in excitation amplitude compared to the zero-preload case. However, within a narrow parameter strip near the Bogdanov–Takens point, sub-harmonic rattle of order three persists even at preload levels that eliminate the conventional impact rattle. Phase portraits and basin-of-attraction maps are presented for six representative parameter combinations.

title: Sensitivity of Gear-Rattle Onset to Manufacturing Tolerance Stack-Up in a Four-Speed Gearbox Assembly
abstract: Gear-rattle propensity in production gearboxes varies between nominally identical units due to tolerance stack-up in centre distances, shaft runout, and bearing clearances. This paper presents a Monte Carlo study in which 5 000 random realisations of a four-speed gearbox are generated by sampling six geometric tolerances from uniform distributions consistent with ISO 1328-1 quality grade 7. For each realisation, the effective backlash of four gear pairs is computed and inserted into a lumped rattle model driven by a measured idle torque signal. The fraction of assemblies predicted to rattle at 750 rpm idle is 34 % when all tolerances are at nominal; this rises to 61 % when centre-distance tolerance alone is increased to grade 8. The sensitivity ranking shows that centre-distance variation contributes 55 % of the variance in rattle intensity, followed by shaft runout at 23 %. Implications for tightening tolerance specifications are discussed with reference to manufacturing cost trade-offs.

title: Data-Driven Surrogate Model for Gear-Rattle Intensity Prediction Across Idle Operating Points
abstract: Physics-based rattle models are computationally expensive when used for design-space exploration involving many parameter combinations. This paper constructs a surrogate model using Gaussian process regression trained on 420 simulation runs of a validated six-DOF rattle model covering idle speeds from 650 to 950 rpm, backlash from 0.05 to 0.35 mm, drag torque from 0.04 to 0.25 N·m, and oil temperature from −5 °C to 90 °C. The surrogate predicts dimensionless rattle intensity with a leave-one-out cross-validation RMSE of 0.031 and R² of 0.974. Prediction intervals derived from the posterior variance correctly bracket the true model output in 93.2 % of 80 test points. The surrogate is integrated into a simple web interface for rapid rattle assessment. Training data and the fitted model are made available as supplementary material. Limitations at the boundaries of the training domain and for configurations with strong modal coupling are discussed.
venue: Transactions on Mechanical Systems – Dynamics and Acoustics

title: Effect of shoulder geometry on material flow and surface finish in friction stir welded 5xxx series aluminium alloys
abstract: Three shoulder geometries — flat, concave (5° tilt), and scrolled — were evaluated for FSW of AA5754-H22 plates at 3 mm thickness. Welding was performed at a fixed rotation speed of 900 rpm and traverse speeds of 80, 120, and 160 mm/min. Flash formation, surface roughness (Ra), and cross-sectional void content were quantified. The scrolled shoulder produced the lowest average Ra of 2.3 µm across all traverse speeds and eliminated flash at 80 and 120 mm/min, while the flat shoulder generated consistent flash at all conditions. Internal void area fraction, measured by image analysis on polished cross-sections, was below 0.4% for the scrolled tool at all speeds. Microhardness profiles showed no significant difference between shoulder types in the nugget zone, suggesting that shoulder geometry primarily controls surface quality and material containment rather than nugget-zone thermal history under the tested parameter range. The findings provide guidance for tool selection when surface integrity is a functional requirement.

title: EBSD characterisation of grain structure and crystallographic texture in the nugget zone of FSW AA6082-T6/AA5083-H111 joints
abstract: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) was used to map grain orientation, misorientation angle distribution, and crystallographic texture in the nugget, thermomechanically affected zone (TMAZ), and heat-affected zone (HAZ) of dissimilar FSW joints produced at 800 and 1000 rpm. Step size was 0.3 µm over areas of 300 × 200 µm. The nugget exhibited predominantly equiaxed grains with average diameters of 5.2 µm (1000 rpm) and 3.9 µm (800 rpm), with high fractions of high-angle grain boundaries (>72% at both conditions). Texture analysis revealed a dominant B/B̄ shear texture component in the nugget, with C and A* components also present, consistent with simple shear deformation during stirring. The TMAZ on the retreating side showed a more diffuse texture and partial retention of the rolling fibre texture from the AA5083 base material. HAZ grains were coarser on the AA6082 side, reaching 28 µm, attributed to dissolution of β″ precipitates. These observations clarify the distinct deformation and recovery histories experienced by each microstructural zone.

title: Fatigue crack initiation sites in dissimilar AA6082/AA5083 friction stir welds under four-point bending
abstract: Fatigue behaviour of FSW AA6082-T6/AA5083-H111 joints was studied under four-point bending at stress ratios R = 0.1 and R = −1 over stress amplitude ranges of 60–140 MPa. S–N data were generated for 12 specimens per condition. Failure consistently initiated at the advancing-side TMAZ/HAZ boundary on the AA6082 face, coinciding with the hardness minimum (69–72 HV) identified in prior quasi-static testing. Fracture surface examination by SEM revealed fatigue striations with spacing of 0.2–0.8 µm at mid-life crack front positions. At R = −1, joint fatigue strength at 10⁷ cycles was 88 MPa, compared to 112 MPa for the AA5083 base metal tested in the same configuration. Cross-sections from interrupted tests at 50% of fatigue life showed secondary crack nucleation at kissing bond-type features near the root of the weld on the advancing side. The study establishes the relative importance of metallurgical softening versus geometric stress concentration as competing crack initiation drivers in this joint system.
venue: European Journal of Structural Integrity

title: Nugget zone defect classification in FSW aluminium joints: a systematic review of detection methods and process parameter thresholds
abstract: This chapter reviews published data on the formation, classification, and detection of internal defects in friction stir welded aluminium alloy joints, with emphasis on wormhole voids, kissing bonds, and lazy-S oxide lines. Detection methods covered include optical metallography, X-ray radiography, ultrasonic phased array, and computed tomography. The review compiles reported parameter windows for defect-free welding from 47 peer-reviewed studies involving 5xxx, 6xxx, and 7xxx series alloys, and identifies the heat index (ω²/v, where ω is rotation speed and v is traverse speed) as the most consistently reported single-variable discriminator between defective and sound welds, with a threshold range of 4.5–6.2 × 10³ rpm²·min/mm depending on alloy combination and joint thickness. Limitations of the heat index approach, including its insensitivity to tool geometry and tilt angle, are discussed. Practical recommendations are provided for inspection protocol selection based on joint geometry and required detection sensitivity. The chapter is intended as a reference for welding engineers selecting quality control procedures for structural aluminium fabrication.

title: Residual stress distribution in friction stir welded AA6061-T6/AA7075-T651 joints measured by X-ray diffraction
abstract: X-ray diffraction sin²ψ measurements were performed on cross-sections of FSW AA6061-T6/AA7075-T651 joints produced at traverse speeds of 80 and 120 mm/min and a rotation speed of 950 rpm. Measurements were taken at 2 mm intervals across the weld width from −20 mm to +20 mm relative to the weld centreline, on both the crown and root faces. Longitudinal residual stresses showed an M-shaped compressive-tensile distribution on the crown, with peak tensile values of +82 MPa on the AA7075 advancing side at 80 mm/min and +67 MPa at 120 mm/min, located approximately 4–5 mm from the centreline. Root-face stresses were uniformly lower, reaching +41 MPa maximum. On the AA6061 side, compressive residual stresses up to −55 MPa were measured within the nugget. The asymmetric stress profile correlates with the asymmetric hardness distribution previously reported for this alloy pair and has implications for the directionality of fatigue crack propagation observed in service-like loading conditions.

title: Influence of post-weld natural ageing on microhardness recovery in FSW AA6082-T6 joints
abstract: The evolution of microhardness in the heat-affected zone of FSW AA6082-T6 butt joints was tracked over a natural ageing period of 365 days after welding. Joints were produced at three heat inputs corresponding to tool rotation speeds of 800, 1000, and 1200 rpm at a constant traverse speed of 100 mm/min. Hardness was measured at 1, 7, 30, 90, 180, and 365 days post-welding along profiles at the mid-thickness plane. The initial hardness minimum in the HAZ on the advancing side recovered from 68–72 HV at day 1 to 81–89 HV at 365 days, representing a partial but not full recovery relative to the base material value of 105 HV. Recovery rate was fastest in the first 30 days and plateaued between 90 and 365 days. TEM examination of samples from the day-1 and day-365 conditions confirmed re-precipitation of fine β″ needles in the HAZ at 365 days, consistent with natural ageing kinetics of AA6082. The degree of recovery correlated negatively with heat input: the 1200 rpm joint showed the least recovery, likely due to greater precipitate dissolution during welding.

title: Comparative corrosion behaviour of FSW and MIG-welded AA5083/AA6082 joints in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution
abstract: Potentiodynamic polarisation and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) were used to compare the corrosion behaviour of friction stir welded and MIG-welded dissimilar AA5083-H111/AA6082-T6 joints in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 °C. FSW joints were produced at 1000 rpm and 100 mm/min; MIG joints were produced using ER5356 filler wire with direct current electrode positive. Three microstructural zones (nugget/weld metal, TMAZ/HAZ, and base material) were isolated using masked specimens and tested separately. The FSW nugget exhibited a corrosion current density (icorr) of 1.8 µA/cm², compared to 4.6 µA/cm² for the MIG weld metal. EIS Nyquist plots showed a single capacitive arc for all FSW zones, while MIG specimens showed a second time constant attributed to a porous oxide layer. Intergranular attack was observed in the AA5083 HAZ for both processes after 72-hour immersion, but pitting depth measured by confocal profilometry was 34% shallower in the FSW joint. The results suggest that grain refinement and reduced intermetallic segregation in FSW joints confer a measurable corrosion advantage over MIG welding for this alloy pair.

title: Effect of tool tilt angle on asymmetric material mixing and defect formation in FSW of 2 mm AA6061/AA5052 sheets
abstract: Thin-sheet FSW of 2 mm AA6061-T4/AA5052-H32 dissimilar joints was carried out at tilt angles of 0°, 1°, 2°, and 3° with a fixed rotation speed of 1100 rpm and traverse speed of 150 mm/min. The study addressed the heightened sensitivity of thin-sheet FSW to tilt angle compared to thicker plate configurations. Cross-sectional image analysis using optical microscopy with polarised light and EDX line scans quantified the degree of material mixing by tracking Mg content distribution across the nugget. At 0° tilt, an intermittent void was present along the advancing side root in 4 of 6 specimens; this defect was eliminated at 1° and 2° tilt. At 3° tilt, a surface groove appeared on the retreating side. Mixed-zone width, defined as the region where Mg content lay between 2 and 4 wt.%, increased monotonically from 0.8 mm at 0° to 1.4 mm at 3°. Tensile tests showed peak strength of 194 MPa at 2° tilt, corresponding to 91% efficiency relative to AA5052 base material. The results define a narrow tilt angle window of 1.5°–2.5° for defect-free, high-strength thin-sheet joining.

title: Membrane casting process control using real-time laser thickness monitoring: a pilot study on a 500 mm wide casting machine
abstract: A non-contact laser triangulation sensor was integrated into a pilot-scale flat-sheet casting machine (500 mm web width, casting speed 0.5–2.0 m min⁻¹) to provide real-time measurement of wet film thickness at three cross-web positions. Data were logged at 10 Hz and fed to an X̄ chart with 3σ control limits updated on a rolling 50-sample basis. Over 22 casting runs producing polysulfone membranes, the in-line sensor detected thickness deviations exceeding ±5 µm in real time in 8 runs; offline SEM cross-section measurements confirmed corresponding pore structure variations. A proportional–integral controller adjusting doctor-blade gap was tested in 6 runs and reduced the thickness standard deviation from 7.2 µm to 3.4 µm compared to manual operation. Energy consumption of the casting line was not significantly affected by controller action. The study establishes that closed-loop thickness control is technically feasible on sub-metre casting machines relevant to research-scale membrane producers.

title: Synthesis and rheological characterisation of hydrophobically modified hydroxyethyl cellulose with variable alkyl chain length
abstract: Hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) was modified by reaction with a series of alkyl glycidyl ethers bearing chain lengths of C8, C12, and C16 in aqueous alkaline medium. The degree of hydrophobic substitution was varied between 0.8 and 3.2 mol% by adjusting reagent stoichiometry. Reaction products were characterised by FTIR, 1H NMR, and SEC-MALS. Aqueous dispersions (1–4 wt%) were evaluated by steady-state and oscillatory shear rheometry at 25 °C. All derivatives exhibited shear-thinning flow behaviour; the C12 series showed the strongest network formation at 2 wt%, with a plateau elastic modulus G' of approximately 180 Pa and a cross-over frequency of 0.08 rad/s. The C16 series formed inhomogeneous, turbid gels attributed to hydrophobe aggregation above a critical concentration of 1.5 wt%. Temperature-dependent measurements (5–50 °C) revealed a moderate reduction in G' with heating, consistent with weakening of micellar junctions. The results establish chain length as the primary tuning parameter for network strength in this derivative class.

title: Viscoelastic properties of guar gum derivatives bearing short-chain hydrophobic substituents in emulsion carrier systems
abstract: Hydroxypropyl guar (HPG) was hydrophobically modified with C6 and C8 acyl chlorides to produce a set of derivatives with degrees of substitution between 0.5 and 2.8 mol%. Derivatives were evaluated as thickeners in oil-in-water emulsions prepared with 15 wt% sunflower oil, stabilised with a 2:1 blend of two non-ionic emulsifiers. Rheological characterisation included amplitude sweeps, frequency sweeps, and creep-recovery experiments. The C8-HPG series at 1 wt% produced emulsions with G' = 95–210 Pa, tan δ = 0.12–0.22, and recoverable strains above 78% after 300 s creep. Droplet size distributions measured by laser diffraction showed d43 values of 4.2–6.8 µm; no significant change was observed after 28 days of accelerated storage at 40 °C. The C6 analogues performed comparably only at concentrations above 1.5 wt%, suggesting a less efficient hydrophobic network at shorter chain length. Potential utility in leave-on skin formulations is discussed.

title: Associative thickeners from hydroxypropyl methylcellulose: effect of molecular weight on network formation and yield stress
abstract: A series of hydrophobically modified hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HMHPMC) samples spanning three molecular weight ranges (Mw 50, 150, and 320 kDa by SEC-MALS) were synthesised by stepwise etherification with C14 octadecyl isocyanate at a fixed hydrophobic substitution of 1.8 mol%. Aqueous dispersions at 0.5–3.0 wt% were characterised by steady-state flow, oscillatory shear, and stress-ramp experiments to obtain apparent yield stress values via the Herschel–Bulkley model. The 150 kDa series demonstrated the highest yield stresses (τy = 7–42 Pa across the concentration range) and the most developed elastic plateau, while the 320 kDa series formed heterogeneous gels with spatial variation in turbidity. Zero-shear viscosity scaled with Mw with an exponent of 2.1, consistent with entanglement-dominated behaviour below the critical overlap concentration c* but transitioning toward associative network control above it. Implications for formulation of suspension-stabilising systems in rinse-off personal-care products are outlined.

title: Frequency-dependent rheology of mixed thickener systems: HMHEC/xanthan gum blends at varying mass ratios
abstract: Binary blends of HMHEC-C12 (Mw 250 kDa) and xanthan gum were prepared at a fixed total polymer concentration of 1.5 wt% and HMHEC:xanthan mass ratios from 9:1 to 1:9. Frequency sweeps (0.01–100 rad/s) and strain-amplitude sweeps were conducted at 25 °C. At xanthan fractions above 0.4, frequency-independent G' dominated (G' > G'' across all frequencies examined), a behaviour absent in pure HMHEC dispersions at the same concentration. Synergistic enhancement of low-frequency G' up to a factor of 2.8 relative to the rule-of-mixtures prediction was observed at a 1:1 mass ratio, attributed to co-operative interpolymer hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions. Large-amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) experiments revealed that the 1:1 blend exhibited pronounced strain stiffening not seen in either component alone. Microscopy with Congo Red staining showed no phase separation at the optical scale. The blend showing the best combination of spreadability index and stability against dilution is identified as a candidate for gel-cream formulations.
venue: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Polysaccharides in Pharma, Food and Cosmetics (PPC-14), Vienna

title: Skin-feel attributes and tribological performance of cellulose ether gels as carrier systems for emollient actives
abstract: The tribological and sensory properties of five gel formulations based on HMHEC-C12, HMHEC-C16, HMHPMC-C14, hydroxypropyl guar, and a commercial carbomer reference were evaluated in the context of their use as carriers for 5 wt% dimethicone and 5 wt% caprylic/capric triglyceride actives. Micro-tribometry (ball-on-flat geometry, 37 °C, 1–100 mm/s) was used to construct Stribeck curves. Coefficient of friction in the mixed-lubrication regime ranged from 0.07 (HMHPMC-C14) to 0.28 (HPG). A panel of twelve trained sensory evaluators assessed tacky-feel, spread-ease, and after-feel using a structured ballot; HMHEC-C16 scored highest on spread-ease but lowest on after-feel due to residual tackiness. Correlation between sensory scores and the ratio G''/G' at 1 rad/s was statistically significant (Spearman ρ = 0.74, p < 0.01) for spread-ease but not for after-feel. The results provide quantitative guidance for selecting thickener type when targeting specific consumer sensory profiles.

title: Degradation of hydrophobically modified hydroxyethyl cellulose under alkaline oxidative conditions: rheological and structural consequences
abstract: HMHEC-C12 samples with three initial molecular weights (80, 160, and 280 kDa) were subjected to hydrogen peroxide treatment at pH 9.5, 40 °C for exposure times of 0, 2, 4, 8, and 24 hours to simulate aggressive alkaline formulation conditions. Molar mass loss was monitored by SEC-MALS, and zero-shear viscosity and G' at 1 rad/s were tracked as rheological indicators. All samples showed first-order-like decrease in Mw with time; the 80 kDa sample lost 55% of its initial Mw within 8 h, while the 280 kDa sample retained network connectivity until 16 h. Critical chain length for associative network formation was estimated at approximately 100 kDa. FTIR analysis confirmed oxidative cleavage of the anhydroglucose ring rather than hydrolysis of the hydrophobe ether linkage. The findings define minimum molecular weight stability thresholds relevant to product shelf-life in bleach-containing personal-care formulations.

title: Microrheology of associative polysaccharide networks probed by diffusing wave spectroscopy: comparison with bulk oscillatory data
abstract: Passive diffusing wave spectroscopy (DWS) was applied to 1 and 2 wt% aqueous dispersions of three associative thickeners — HMHEC-C12, HMHPMC-C14, and a C12-modified guar derivative — to obtain frequency-dependent G' and G'' in the range 1–10 000 rad/s, inaccessible by conventional bulk rheometry. Tracer particles (polystyrene beads, d = 500 nm) were incorporated at 0.05 wt%. At the microscale, all three systems showed higher G' than measured in bulk at equivalent frequencies, with discrepancies of 20–60%, interpreted as evidence for heterogeneous network topology at length scales below the mesh size. The mesh size estimated from DWS G' data (12–35 nm) agreed within 20% with estimates from blob-theory applied to bulk plateau moduli. The C12-guar derivative showed the largest micro–macro discrepancy, tentatively attributed to larger-scale structural heterogeneity. These results support the use of DWS as a complementary screening tool in thickener development.

title: Concentration-dependent microstructure of HMHEC gels studied by rheo-SAXS: junction zone geometry and strand connectivity
abstract: In situ small-angle X-ray scattering coupled to oscillatory shear (rheo-SAXS) was used to characterise the microstructure of HMHEC-C12 gels at 0.5, 1.5, and 3.0 wt% under quiescent and steady-shear conditions. Experiments were performed on the P12 BIOSAXS beamline (EMBL, Hamburg). Quiescent SAXS patterns showed a broad correlation peak at q* = 0.28–0.44 nm−1 shifting to higher q with concentration, corresponding to a characteristic spacing d* of 14–22 nm attributed to intermicellar junctions. Scattering data were fitted to a sticky hard-sphere model with polydisperse micelle cores. Upon shear at rates above 10 s−1, anisotropic scattering emerged, indicating partial alignment of polymer strands; the correlation peak broadened and shifted to lower q, consistent with network disruption under flow. Recovery of the quiescent peak position after cessation of shear occurred on a timescale of 40–120 s depending on concentration, matching macroscopic G' recovery kinetics measured simultaneously.

title: Hydraulic gradients and exchange fluxes along a channelized reach of the Middle Danube: a piezometer network study
abstract: This study presents two years of continuous hydraulic head data collected from a 14-piezometer transect installed along a 3.2 km regulated section of the Middle Danube upstream of Novi Sad. Measurements were taken at 15-minute intervals using pressure transducers calibrated against manual readings. River stage fluctuations of up to 4.7 m induced clearly identifiable losing and gaining phases in the aquifer, with lag times ranging from 6 to 41 hours depending on distance from the riverbank and local sediment heterogeneity. Specific exchange fluxes were estimated using Darcy calculations based on measured hydraulic gradients and grain-size-derived hydraulic conductivity values between 8 × 10⁻⁴ and 3 × 10⁻³ m/s. Results show that the regulated embankments suppress lateral connectivity during average flow conditions but enhance it during flood recession. The dataset provides baseline exchange flux estimates for this reach that are suitable for calibrating regional groundwater models.

title: Temperature as a natural tracer of vertical seepage through streambed sediments: field evidence from the Tisa alluvial plain
abstract: Vertical temperature profiles measured at seven streambed locations along a 9 km stretch of the Tisa River were used to quantify downward seepage fluxes during a prolonged low-flow period in summer 2012. Profiles were recorded with 1 cm resolution using a portable temperature lance at fortnightly intervals over 14 weeks. Flux magnitudes were derived by fitting analytical solutions for one-dimensional vertical heat transport to the observed temperature envelopes. Estimated downward fluxes ranged from 0.4 to 2.1 × 10⁻⁵ m/s, consistent with independent grain-size analyses of cored sediment samples. Spatial variability correlated strongly with the thickness of a fine-grained surface layer identified in cores, suggesting that clogging exerts primary control on seepage rates in this reach. The approach is low-cost and reproducible, making it suitable for baseline characterisation of ungauged alluvial systems in the Pannonian lowland.

title: Clogging dynamics of a riverbank filtration site: observations over a four-year operational period
abstract: A municipal bank filtration gallery on the left bank of the Danube near Bačka Palanka was monitored over 48 consecutive months to characterise changes in hydraulic conductivity and travel time between the river and abstraction wells located 55 m inland. Monthly slug tests conducted in three observation wells showed a statistically significant decline in hydraulic conductivity in the top 0.3 m of the aquifer, decreasing from a median of 2.1 × 10⁻³ m/s to 6.4 × 10⁻⁴ m/s over the study period, with partial seasonal recovery during high-discharge events. Particle-size analyses of sediment cores taken annually confirmed progressive accumulation of fine material in the uppermost layer. Fluorescent dye tracer experiments performed at the beginning and end of the period showed that median travel time from river to well increased from 18 to 34 days. These findings have direct implications for managing the pathogen attenuation capacity of the filtration system.

title: MODFLOW-based simulation of bank filtration response to flood embankment realignment on the Danube floodplain
abstract: This contribution describes a MODFLOW-NWT groundwater flow model built for a 12 km² domain on the right bank of the Danube near Apatin, calibrated against 18 months of observed heads in 11 piezometers. The model was used to evaluate three embankment realignment scenarios proposed within a floodplain restoration programme. Removing a 1.4 km section of the secondary embankment in scenario 3 increased calculated groundwater recharge from the river by 38% compared to the current configuration during the modelled median flood event. Scenario 1, involving only minor berm lowering, yielded a 9% increase. Simulated travel times from the river to existing abstraction points were shortened by 6 to 12 days under the most permissive scenario, which would require revision of wellhead protection zones. Sensitivity analyses indicated that uncertainty in hydraulic conductivity of the alluvial gravel unit is the dominant source of prediction uncertainty.

title: Hydrochemical evolution of bank filtrate along a transect from the Danube to inland production wells
abstract: Water samples collected monthly over one year at the Danube riverbank, at three observation wells positioned 20, 55, and 90 m from the river, and at two production wells were analysed for major ions, dissolved oxygen, dissolved organic carbon, nitrate, ammonium, iron, and manganese. The dataset encompasses 168 samples. A clear redox sequence was observed: oxic riverbank conditions transitioned to anoxic conditions by 20 m, accompanied by DOC reduction from a median of 4.8 mg/L at the bank to 1.1 mg/L at 90 m. Iron concentrations peaked at 55 m at a median of 1.4 mg/L, exceeding drinking water guidelines at this intermediate point. Principal component analysis identified two dominant hydrochemical gradients corresponding to an organic matter degradation axis and a dilution axis driven by seasonal river chemistry variability. Results suggest that aquifer residence time, rather than distance, is the controlling variable for iron mobilisation.

title: Effect of gravel extraction from an active floodplain on bank filtration travel times: a combined tracer and modelling approach
abstract: Aggregate extraction from a licensed gravel pit located 80 m from the Danube bank created a hydraulic shortcut between the river and downstream abstraction wells documented by this investigation. Before and after tracer tests using sodium bromide were conducted across two extraction phases during 2019 and 2020. Pre-extraction breakthrough curves at the nearest well (150 m from the river) showed a median travel time of 22 days. After a 1.2 m deepening of the extraction pit, this decreased to 11 days, with peak bromide concentrations arriving 35% earlier. A particle-tracking analysis using the calibrated MODFLOW model confirmed that flow paths had been diverted through the pit, bypassing 40–60 m of filtration pathway. The findings were submitted to the relevant water management authority and informed a revision of the extraction licence conditions.

title: Seasonal variability of the hyporheic exchange zone thickness in a gravel-bed section of the Tisa River
abstract: Hyporheic zone extent was characterised at four cross-sections of the Tisa River using vertical temperature gradient analysis and porewater electrical conductivity profiling over four seasons in 2021–2022. At each cross-section, a 1 m long drive-point sampler was deployed at 0.1 m depth increments to extract porewater for conductivity and dissolved oxygen measurement. The depth at which river water influence became undetectable ranged from 0.25 m during summer low flow to 0.65 m during spring snowmelt-driven high flow, with intermediate depths during autumn baseflow. Vertical Darcy flux estimates derived from paired temperature profiles ranged from −3.0 × 10⁻⁶ m/s (upwelling) to +8.5 × 10⁻⁶ m/s (downwelling). Temporal variability within seasons exceeded spatial variability across cross-sections, pointing to stage fluctuation as the primary driver of hyporheic exchange in this lowland reach. Data were deposited in the Serbian National Hydrological Data Repository.

title: Long-term trends in riverbed hydraulic conductivity at a Danube bank filtration site: 1995–2023
abstract: Slug test records from a monitoring network at a bank filtration facility near Novi Sad were compiled and reanalysed to assess multi-decadal changes in streambed and near-bank hydraulic conductivity. The dataset includes 312 slug tests performed in 8 wells between 1995 and 2023, supplemented by annual turbidity records from the river gauge station and engineering logs of periodic riverbed rehabilitation works. Analysis using the Bouwer-Rice method showed no statistically significant trend in wells located more than 30 m from the bank, while the two wells closest to the river exhibited a decreasing trend of approximately 15% per decade. Periods of accelerated conductivity decline corresponded with years of elevated suspended sediment load measured at the upstream gauge. Two rehabilitation events involving mechanical riverbed loosening temporarily restored conductivity to near-initial values. The record provides empirical evidence relevant to long-term operation planning for lowland bank filtration systems.

title: Detecting non-stationarity in annual maximum rainfall series at selected stations in Vojvodina using Mann–Kendall and GAMLSS approaches
abstract: Rainfall records from 14 synoptic and climatological stations across Vojvodina spanning 1961–2021 were examined for monotonic trends and distributional shifts in annual maximum 1-hour, 6-hour, and 24-hour totals. The Mann–Kendall test identified statistically significant upward trends (p < 0.05) in 1-hour maxima at six stations, predominantly in the northwestern part of the region. Generalised Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) with a GEV response distribution and time as a covariate were then fitted to quantify changes in the location and scale parameters. At the Subotica station, the estimated 100-year return-period 1-hour rainfall increased by approximately 12% between the sub-period 1961–1990 and 1991–2021 when a time-varying location parameter was used rather than a stationary GEV fit. These results suggest that design intensities derived under stationarity assumptions may underestimate current and future extremes for Vojvodina, with direct implications for drainage infrastructure sizing. The findings are discussed in the context of available regional climate projections.

title: Accrual-Based Earnings Management in Serbian Private Firms: An Initial Assessment
abstract: This study provides an early empirical examination of earnings management behaviour among private Serbian companies in the period 2005–2009. Using a modified Jones model applied to a sample of 412 firms drawn from the Serbian Business Registers Agency database, the paper estimates discretionary accruals as a proxy for earnings management. Results indicate statistically significant income-smoothing patterns, particularly among firms approaching debt covenant thresholds. Cross-sectional regressions reveal that leverage and firm size are the strongest determinants of accrual manipulation, while audit firm type shows no significant moderating effect in the private-firm context. The study contributes an early empirical baseline for a transition economy in which listed-company-focused methodologies had rarely been adapted to the private sector. Limitations regarding the reliability of historical Serbian accounting data are discussed, and robustness checks using the Dechow–Dichev model are reported.

title: Audit Quality and Earnings Management Constraint in Non-Listed Serbian Companies
abstract: The paper investigates whether auditor size and auditor industry specialisation reduce discretionary accruals in a sample of 610 non-listed Serbian companies audited between 2010 and 2014. Big-N audit firms are represented by only 7 percent of the sample, reflecting the structure of the Serbian audit market. Using a performance-matched modified Jones model and OLS with clustered standard errors at the industry level, the analysis finds that Big-N audited firms exhibit significantly lower absolute discretionary accruals, with a magnitude of approximately 2.4 percentage points of total assets. Industry-specialist auditors show a weaker and less consistent effect. Heteroscedasticity-robust quantile regressions confirm the finding is not driven by outliers. The paper argues that audit quality effects documented in capital-market-focused literature generalise, at least partially, to the private-company context of a developing European economy.

title: Financial Distress Prediction and Earnings Management: Are Distressed SMEs More Likely to Manipulate?
abstract: This paper examines whether financially distressed SMEs show higher levels of earnings management compared with healthy peers, and whether the direction of manipulation shifts as distress deepens. Using a sample of 3,100 Serbian and Croatian SMEs over 2012–2017, we estimate Altman Z-score variants calibrated for private firms and use these as a continuous distress measure in interaction models. Discretionary accruals are estimated via the performance-adjusted Jones model. Results show that moderately distressed firms engage in income-increasing accruals, while severely distressed firms switch to income-decreasing manipulation, consistent with a big-bath reporting incentive before expected restructuring or bankruptcy filings. The pattern is more pronounced in construction and retail sectors. These findings have implications for creditors and auditors who use financial statements of SMEs in credit assessments and going-concern evaluations.

title: Earnings Management Detection in SMEs: Practitioner Tools and Their Limitations
abstract: This book chapter reviews the state of practitioner-oriented tools for detecting earnings manipulation in small and medium enterprises, addressing the gap between academic accrual-model research and methods actually used by auditors and credit analysts in the Western Balkans. The chapter surveys six commercially distributed financial analysis platforms used in the region and evaluates the theoretical foundations of their manipulation-detection modules against the academic literature. A structured comparison shows that most tools rely on ratio-based heuristics rather than residual-based accrual models, and none incorporates real activity manipulation proxies. Case vignettes drawn from anonymised audit engagements in Serbia and North Macedonia illustrate common detection failures. The chapter concludes with a discussion of practical constraints—limited time series, missing notes disclosures, and irregular filing—that make direct transfer of academic models to practitioner settings non-trivial.

title: Real Earnings Management Detection Using Machine Learning: An Application to Vojvodina Agri-Food SMEs
abstract: Standard regression-based proxies for real activity manipulation have known power limitations under heterogeneous industry conditions. This paper explores whether supervised machine learning classifiers improve detection accuracy for a sample of 890 agri-food SMEs registered in the Vojvodina region of Serbia, observed over 2016–2022. Features are constructed from Roychowdhury-type abnormal accrual and operating metrics supplemented by cash-flow volatility and working capital ratios. Random forest and gradient boosting classifiers are trained on a labelled subsample identified through enforcement actions by the Serbian Audit Oversight Commission. Out-of-sample AUC values reach 0.74 for gradient boosting, compared with 0.61 for a logistic regression benchmark. Feature importance analysis confirms that abnormal production costs and abnormal cash flows from operations are the two most informative predictors. Limitations related to the small size of the labelled enforcement sample and potential selection bias in enforcement targets are discussed in detail.

title: Working Capital Management and Earnings Manipulation in SMEs: Separating Operational from Discretionary Accruals
abstract: Abnormal working capital changes are used as both a real activity manipulation proxy and as an accrual-quality indicator, creating a conceptual overlap that inflates estimated manipulation levels when firms face genuine operational shocks. This paper proposes a two-stage decomposition procedure to separate operational working capital fluctuations from discretionary components, using industry-level cash conversion cycle benchmarks as auxiliary instruments. The approach is validated on a sample of 2,600 manufacturing SMEs from Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia covering 2017–2023. Simulation exercises show the proposed decomposition reduces false-positive manipulation rates by 18 to 31 percentage points relative to unadjusted Roychowdhury measures across different levels of operational volatility. Application to the sample reveals that previously reported high manipulation rates in Balkan manufacturing SMEs are substantially overstated, largely reflecting supply chain disruptions in 2020–2021 rather than deliberate reporting choices.

title: Turn-on and turn-off energy losses in a 600 V GaN HEMT half-bridge: double-pulse test measurements at 400 V bus voltage
abstract: This paper presents a systematic measurement campaign of switching energies in a 600 V enhancement-mode GaN HEMT half-bridge using a double-pulse test fixture. Turn-on losses Eon and turn-off losses Eoff were measured across a gate-resistance range of 0–22 Ω, a drain current range of 2–25 A, and junction temperatures of 25 °C and 100 °C. At 15 A and 400 V with a 4.7 Ω gate resistance, Eon was 4.8 µJ and Eoff was 1.9 µJ, giving a total switching loss of 6.7 µJ per event. Parasitic common-source inductance of the PCB layout was extracted via network-analyser S-parameter measurements and ranged from 0.8 to 2.3 nH across three board variants. A piece-wise linear switching model was fitted to the experimental data with relative error below 6 % over the full test matrix. The calorimetric cross-validation agreed with the electrical integration method within 4 %. Results are compared with datasheet figures and discrepancies exceeding 20 % at high current are highlighted.

title: Isolated gate-driver supply with reinforced insulation for 650 V GaN half-bridge modules
abstract: An isolated gate-driver power supply achieving reinforced insulation per IEC 60950-1 is described for use with 650 V enhancement-mode GaN half-bridge modules. The design uses a 4 MHz resonant Royer oscillator driving a coreless PCB transformer with a creepage distance of 8 mm and a measured partial-discharge inception voltage of 4.2 kV. Under-voltage lockout thresholds are set at +5.4 V / −2.5 V for the high-side channel. Propagation delay mismatch between high- and low-side channels was measured at 3.8 ns over the full temperature range of −20 °C to 125 °C. The supply delivers 750 mW per channel with a peak efficiency of 82 %. Short-circuit protection using a desaturation-equivalent drain-voltage comparator trips within 120 ns. Prototype boards were subjected to a 1000-hour humidity-bias test at 85 °C / 85 % RH without insulation degradation. The design is intended for DC–DC converters switching at 1 MHz.
venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics

title: Effect of negative turn-off bias on switching losses in an enhancement-mode GaN transistor at 800 kHz
abstract: Negative gate turn-off bias is commonly recommended for enhancement-mode GaN HEMTs to suppress parasitic turn-on, yet its influence on total switching energy is rarely quantified across a realistic operating range. This paper measures Eon and Eoff at turn-off bias voltages of 0 V, −1 V, −2 V, and −3 V for a 100 V / 35 A GaN transistor operating in a 100 V, 800 kHz synchronous buck converter. At a load current of 20 A, applying −3 V reduced spurious turn-on drain current peaks by 78 % compared to 0 V bias, while Eon increased by 0.6 µJ due to the longer gate charge recovery time. A SPICE behavioural model incorporating the gate charge profile and Miller plateau voltage was validated against measured waveforms. The model reproduced peak turn-on dv/dt within 8 % and peak di/dt within 11 %. Thermal measurements using an infrared camera confirmed junction temperature reduction of 6 °C at maximum load.

title: PCB layout guidelines for minimising common-source inductance in GaN half-bridge circuits: a parametric study
abstract: Common-source inductance (CSI) introduced by PCB interconnects degrades switching-speed and increases switching energy in GaN half-bridge circuits. This paper presents a parametric finite-element study of CSI as a function of five geometric variables: via diameter, via pitch, power-loop width, source-sense routing length, and copper pour layer count. Seventeen PCB variants were fabricated and CSI was measured by the impedance-analyser short-circuit method at 1 MHz. CSI ranged from 0.4 nH for a four-layer optimised layout to 3.1 nH for a two-layer reference layout. Switching-energy experiments confirmed that each additional 1 nH of CSI increased Eon by approximately 0.35 µJ at 15 A / 400 V. A design flowchart consolidating the parametric results is provided. Recommended design rules include a maximum source-sense trace length of 5 mm and a minimum of four vias per source return path. The findings apply to GaN devices in TO-leadless packages with source-sense pins.

title: Comparison of switching losses in GaN and SiC transistors in a 400 V / 1 MHz hard-switched inverter
abstract: GaN enhancement-mode HEMTs and SiC MOSFETs are compared under identical hard-switching conditions in a single-phase full-bridge inverter operating at 400 V DC bus and 1 MHz PWM frequency. Four device types were tested: two GaN devices (80 V and 650 V rated) and two SiC MOSFETs (900 V and 1200 V rated). Device-level double-pulse tests were complemented by full-inverter calorimetric loss separation. At 10 A output current and 400 V, the 650 V GaN device exhibited total switching losses 34 % lower than the 900 V SiC MOSFET in a comparable RDS(on) class. Conduction losses favoured SiC at currents above 18 A. Reverse-recovery charge Qrr was negligible for GaN (<5 nC) but reached 180 nC for SiC, contributing 1.8 W additional turn-on loss at 1 MHz. Gate charge figures, thermal resistance, and package inductance are tabulated for all devices. The paper concludes with application boundaries for each device class.

title: Switching transient modelling of silicon carbide power MOSFETs using a physics-based threshold-charge approach
abstract: This paper presents a threshold-charge switching model for silicon carbide power MOSFETs intended for use in circuit simulators. The model requires nine parameters extractable from standard datasheet curves and a set of three short-circuit transient measurements. The threshold-charge concept partitions the gate charge characteristic into three segments corresponding to pre-Miller, Miller, and post-Miller phases, each described by a linear charge-voltage relationship. Model extraction was applied to a 1200 V / 20 A SiC MOSFET and validated against double-pulse test measurements at 600 V and 800 V bus voltages over a current range of 2–18 A. Peak dv/dt during turn-off was reproduced within 9 % and peak di/dt during turn-on within 12 %. The model executes in SPICE transient simulation 40 times faster than a published physics-based JFET model. Limitations at high temperature and under avalanche conditions are discussed and directions for extension are indicated.

title: Measurement of junction temperature in GaN HEMTs during switching transients using gate-threshold voltage shift
abstract: Junction temperature measurement in GaN HEMTs during active switching is complicated by the absence of a body diode forward voltage that is usable as a temperature-sensitive parameter in silicon MOSFETs. This paper exploits the gate threshold voltage Vth shift of enhancement-mode GaN HEMTs, which decreases by approximately −6 mV/°C, as an in-situ temperature indicator. A measurement protocol is described in which the device is briefly switched to linear region at the end of each switching period and a fast sampling circuit captures the drain current at a known Vgs to infer Vth. The method was validated against infrared thermography and a Pt100 temperature-controlled chuck. Agreement within ±3 °C was achieved over a junction temperature range of 25–150 °C. The technique was applied to a 200 W, 400 kHz hard-switched boost converter to measure cycle-by-cycle junction temperature ripple of 8 °C at rated power.

title: Interleaved totem-pole PFC rectifier at 500 kHz using GaN HEMTs: switching loss budget and efficiency analysis
abstract: A two-phase interleaved totem-pole power-factor-correction rectifier using 650 V GaN HEMTs is designed and characterised at 500 kHz switching frequency for a 230 V AC input and 400 V / 1 kW output. The switching loss budget is decomposed into turn-on, turn-off, body-diode reverse-recovery, and dead-time conduction components using the calorimetric bench described in earlier work. At rated power, turn-on losses account for 58 % of total switching losses while dead-time conduction accounts for 21 %. Interleaving reduced peak-to-peak input current ripple from 4.2 A to 1.7 A and allowed reduction of the differential-mode inductor by 55 % compared to a single-phase design. Measured efficiency at rated power was 98.2 % and power factor was 0.997 at full load. Thermal mapping by infrared camera confirmed that the high-frequency leg GaN devices reached 92 °C junction temperature at maximum ambient of 40 °C, within the 150 °C maximum rating.

title: Effect of gate-driver output impedance on drain voltage oscillation amplitude in hard-switched GaN circuits
abstract: Ringing on the drain node of a GaN transistor after hard switching is determined by the interaction between circuit parasitics and the gate-driver output impedance. This paper measures peak drain voltage overshoot and oscillation frequency as functions of gate-driver source and sink impedances (0.5–47 Ω) for a 650 V / 15 A GaN HEMT at 400 V / 15 A. A lumped-parameter resonant circuit model with four parasitics—loop inductance, drain capacitance, gate-to-drain capacitance, and common-source inductance—was fitted to each measurement. Peak overshoot ranged from 38 V at 47 Ω turn-off resistance to 119 V at 0.5 Ω, representing 9.5 % and 29.8 % of bus voltage respectively. The model predicts overshoot with a root-mean-square error of 4.1 V. A design curve relating maximum safe turn-off gate resistance to bus voltage and loop inductance is derived for overshoot-constrained applications.

title: Concurrent Dual-Band DPD Using Shared Observation Receiver with Sub-Band Decomposition
abstract: Concurrent dual-band transmission in 700 MHz and 3.5 GHz bands from a single PA requires linearisation across both bands simultaneously. A shared observation receiver based on sub-band decomposition using polyphase filter banks is proposed to reduce hardware cost relative to two dedicated observation paths. The sub-band outputs feed two independent GMP-based DPD cores that share coefficient update resources. Validation is performed on a broadband GaN PA with 3 dB compression point of 40 W, driven by simultaneous 10 MHz LTE at 703 MHz and 40 MHz 5G NR at 3.48 GHz. The dual-band DPD achieves ACPR values of −50.2 dBc and −48.7 dBc in the respective bands, compared to −31.4 dBc and −29.8 dBc without linearisation. Cross-band intermodulation products at harmonically related frequencies are characterised and shown to remain below −55 dBc after correction. Total observation receiver resource utilisation on a Xilinx evaluation FPGA board is 34% of available DSP slices.

title: Kinetic modelling of essential oil extraction from peppermint (Mentha × piperita L.) leaves by steam distillation
abstract: A mathematical model based on simultaneous washing and diffusion mechanisms was applied to describe the steam distillation kinetics of peppermint essential oil. Experiments were conducted in a pilot-scale steam distillation unit (20 L still) at three steam flow rates (0.8, 1.4, and 2.1 kg/h) and two moisture contents of the plant material (fresh, 78% w/w; air-dried, 12% w/w). Yield data were collected at 10-minute intervals over 180 minutes. The two-parameter model fitted the experimental data with R² values above 0.97 for all conditions. The washing rate constant kw ranged from 0.041 to 0.089 min⁻¹ and the diffusion coefficient De from 1.2×10⁻¹⁰ to 3.8×10⁻¹⁰ m²/s, both increasing with steam flow rate. Menthol content in oil fractions collected at successive time intervals decreased from 44.2% in the first fraction to 38.1% in the final fraction, indicating preferential early-stage removal of the more volatile components. The model provides a useful basis for scale-up calculations.

title: Optimizacija parametara vodeno-parne destilacije nane (Mentha spicata L.) primenom metode odzivnih površina
abstract: Metodom odzivnih površina (RSM) sa centralnim kompozitnim planom eksperimenta ispitivani su uticaji temperature vode (70–100°C), odnosa droga/voda (1:5 do 1:15 m/v) i trajanja destilacije (60–180 min) na prinos etarskog ulja nane u laboratorijskim uslovima (Clevenger aparat, 2 L). Ukupno je izvedeno 20 eksperimenata. Maksimalni prinos od 1,62% v/m postignut je pri temperaturi 96°C, odnosu droga/voda 1:10 i trajanju od 150 minuta. ANOVA analiza pokazala je da su sva tri faktora statistički značajna (p < 0,05), sa dominantnim efektom temperature. Kvadratni model sa zadovoljavajućom tačnošću predviđanja (R² = 0,954, prilagođeni R² = 0,912) prihvaćen je kao adekvatan. GC-FID analizom utvrđeno je da optimizovani uslovi ne utiču značajno na hemijski profil ulja, pri čemu karvon ostaje dominantna komponenta sa 58–63% ukupnog sadržaja.

title: Effect of pre-treatment methods on steam distillation efficiency of coriander (Coriandrum sativum L.) fruits
abstract: Four pre-treatment methods — intact fruit, coarsely crushed (2–4 mm), finely crushed (0.5–1 mm), and freeze-thawed intact — were compared with respect to essential oil yield and linalool content during steam distillation of coriander fruits. Distillations were performed in triplicate in a 5 L stainless steel still at a constant steam flow rate of 1.2 kg/h for 120 minutes. Finely crushed material gave the highest yield (0.71% v/m), approximately 2.4-fold greater than intact fruit (0.29% v/m), while freeze-thaw pre-treatment increased yield to 0.44% v/m without mechanical reduction of particle size. Linalool content, determined by GC-MS, was highest in oil from intact and freeze-thawed fruits (87–89%) and slightly lower in crushed fractions (83–85%), suggesting minor thermal or oxidative degradation in finer material. Energy consumption per unit mass of recovered oil was lowest for coarsely crushed material, making it the preferred option for large-scale processing when both yield and energy efficiency are considered.

title: Comparison of hydrodistillation and steam distillation for recovery of essential oil from dried chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla L.) flowers: yield, composition and energy demand
abstract: A systematic comparison of hydrodistillation (HD) and steam distillation (SD) was carried out for chamomile flowers at pilot scale (20 L still). Variables studied were distillation duration (60–240 min) and charge ratio (material-to-water ratio for HD; steam flow rate for SD). HD gave marginally higher total oil yield (0.58 ± 0.04% v/m at optimum) compared to SD (0.51 ± 0.03% v/m), but the difference was not statistically significant at the 95% confidence level. GC-MS analysis identified 34 compounds in HD oils and 31 in SD oils. The content of (−)-α-bisabolol oxide A was significantly higher in SD oils (31.2 ± 1.8% vs. 24.7 ± 2.1% in HD), while chamazulene content was comparable (4.5–5.2%). Specific energy consumption calculated from metered steam and electrical input was 1.8-fold higher for HD than for SD under equivalent conditions. Results indicate that SD is preferable from an energy standpoint when a chamazulene-rich product is not the primary target.

title: Influence of drying temperature on essential oil yield and terpene profile in oregano (Origanum vulgare L.) processed by steam distillation
abstract: Oregano herb was dried at five temperatures (30, 40, 50, 60, and 70°C) in a tray dryer to constant moisture content before steam distillation in a 20 L pilot still (steam flow rate 1.5 kg/h, 90 min). Essential oil yield ranged from 2.11% v/m (dried at 30°C) to 1.47% v/m (dried at 70°C), a statistically significant linear decrease (p < 0.01). GC-MS profiling identified carvacrol as the dominant component across all treatments (68.4–74.1%), with thymol as the second major constituent (8.2–11.7%). Drying temperature above 50°C caused a measurable reduction in p-cymene content (from 7.8% to 4.9%), attributed to its conversion to carvacrol during prolonged thermal treatment. Antioxidant activity assessed by DPPH assay was highest in oils from material dried at 30–40°C (IC₅₀ 6.8–7.4 µg/mL). The data support a maximum drying temperature of 45°C to preserve both yield and composition when steam distillation is the downstream processing step.

title: Uticaj starosti biljnog materijala tokom skladištenja na efikasnost parne destilacije žalfije (Salvia officinalis L.)
abstract: Ispitivan je uticaj dužine skladištenja sušenih listova žalfije (0, 3, 6, 9 i 12 meseci na 20°C, u tamnim uslovima) na prinos i hemijski sastav etarskog ulja dobijenog parnom destilacijom na pilot postrojenju (20 L, protok pare 1,5 kg/h, 120 min). Prinos je opadao sa produžetkom perioda skladištenja: sa 2,31% v/m sveže sušenog materijala na 1,47% v/m nakon 12 meseci. GC-MS analizom identifikovano je 42 jedinjenja; tujone (α+β) kao dominantna frakcija pokazali su nešto veću stabilnost od kamfora i 1,8-cineola koji su brže gubili. Sadržaj vlage materijala rastao je sa 9,2% na 14,8% tokom skladištenja u nekontrolisanim uslovima, što korelira sa padom prinosa (Pearsonov r = −0,91). Preporučuje se maksimalni period skladištenja od 6 meseci pri sadržaju vlage ispod 12% da bi se osigurali prinos iznad 1,9% i adekvatan hemijski profil za farmaceutsku primenu.

title: Energy and mass balance analysis of a semi-industrial steam distillation plant for lavender processing in Vojvodina
abstract: A complete energy and mass balance was performed on a 200 L steam distillation plant operated by a local cooperative in Vojvodina over three consecutive lavender harvests (2018–2020). Steam consumption, condensate temperature, distillation time, fresh biomass charge, and oil yield were logged continuously for 312 individual batches. Mean oil yield was 0.74% v/m (fresh weight basis), with a coefficient of variation of 18% attributable mainly to inter-harvest differences in maturation stage. Specific steam consumption averaged 4.6 kg steam per kg fresh biomass, with 31% of the thermal input lost through uninsulated pipework and the still body. Retrofitting with 40 mm mineral wool insulation was modelled to reduce specific steam consumption to approximately 3.2 kg/kg, with a payback period of 2.1 years at current energy prices. Cohobation of the distillation water reduced total process water discharge by 62% and recovered an additional 4.1% of oil mass relative to non-cohobation runs.

title: Hydrodistillation of Rosa damascena Mill. petals: effect of salt addition on oil yield and phenylethyl alcohol recovery
abstract: The effect of sodium chloride (NaCl) addition on hydrodistillation of Rosa damascena petals was investigated at three salt concentrations (0, 30, and 60 g/L in distillation water) using a 5 L Clevenger apparatus with cohobation. Salt addition at 60 g/L increased the total oil yield by 14.3% relative to unsalted control (0.041 vs. 0.036% v/m, p < 0.05) and raised the 2-phenylethyl alcohol (2-PEA) content in the oil from 51.3% to 62.8%, while reducing the 2-PEA fraction lost to the hydrolate. The effect is attributed to salting-out, which reduces the solubility of 2-PEA in the aqueous phase and drives partitioning toward the distillate. No statistically significant effect of salt concentration on citronellol or geraniol content was observed. The economic trade-off between increased oil yield and the cost of salt and wastewater treatment is discussed, and the 30 g/L level is identified as a practical compromise. Results are relevant for small-scale rose oil production facilities in the region.

title: Modelovanje prenosa mase pri parnoj destilaciji mešanog biljnog punjenja: studija na smeši lavande i žalfije
abstract: Ispitivana je kinetika parne destilacije u pilot postrojenju (20 L) pri preradi mešanog punjenja sušene lavande i žalfije u masenim udelima 1:1, 3:1 i 1:3 (lavanda:žalfija). Dvofazni kinetički model (pranje + difuzija) primenjen je na svaku biljku posebno, uz pretpostavku da su procesi prenosa mase nezavisni. Modifikovani efektivni difuzioni koeficijenti za terpenske komponente iz mešanog punjenja bili su statistički isti kao u slučaju monokomponentnog punjenja (p > 0,05), što ukazuje na odsutnost međusobne interferencije biljnih matrica pri prenosu mase. Prinos lavandulovog ulja iz mešanog punjenja bio je ekvivalentan prinosu iz monokomponentnog punjenja (1,02 ± 0,06% v/m), dok je prinos ulja žalfije neznatno manji (2,17 ± 0,09% vs. 2,31 ± 0,07% v/m). Rezultati otvaraju mogućnost istovremenе prerade kompatibilnih vrsta bez gubitka prinosa, što može smanjiti operativne troškove u malim prerađivačkim pogonima. Predstavljeni model može se koristiti za projektovanje destilacionih ciklusa kod mešanih punjenja.

title: Distillation water (hydrolat) characterisation and valorisation potential from pilot-scale oregano and peppermint steam distillation
abstract: Hydrolats collected during pilot-scale (20 L) steam distillation of oregano and peppermint were characterised for dissolved volatile organic content, total phenolic content (TPC), antioxidant activity (DPPH, ABTS), and microbial inhibition potential against four test organisms (Staphylococcus simulans, Escherichia coli ATCC 25922, Candida tropicalis, and Aspergillus brasiliensis). Oregano hydrolat contained carvacrol at 0.31 ± 0.03 g/L and thymol at 0.08 ± 0.01 g/L as determined by HPLC; peppermint hydrolat contained menthol at 0.84 ± 0.07 g/L and menthone at 0.21 ± 0.02 g/L. TPC values were 182 ± 14 mg GAE/L (oregano) and 96 ± 9 mg GAE/L (peppermint). Both hydrolats exhibited measurable inhibition of all test organisms, with MIC values of 12.5–50 mg/mL. The results support the potential use of hydrolats as functional water in cosmetic or food applications rather than as process wastewater. A simplified economic estimate suggests that selling hydrolat at conservative bulk prices could offset 8–15% of distillation operating costs.

title: Comparison of Differential Pressure Burst and 180° Peel Tests as Acceptance Criteria for Seal Quality in Pouch Packaging
abstract: Two standard seal-quality tests—the 180° peel test and the differential pressure burst test—were applied to heat-sealed pouches made from OPP/tie/mLLDPE films sealed across a jaw temperature range of 95–140 °C. For each jaw temperature, 20 pouches were prepared and tested by both methods. Peel force data and burst pressure data were analysed for correlation and for their ability to discriminate between adequate and inadequate seals. The two methods agreed in classifying seals above 110 °C as acceptable (peel ≥ 25 N/25 mm; burst ≥ 180 kPa), but diverged in the 100–109 °C zone, where 7 of 20 pouches passed the burst test but failed the peel criterion. Root-cause analysis by SEM cross-section showed incomplete interdiffusion at the seal interface in those pouches. Repeatability expressed as coefficient of variation was 5.8 % for peel and 9.2 % for burst across all jaw temperatures. The peel test is recommended as the more conservative acceptance criterion for VFFS applications handling liquid or particulate products.

title: Evapotranspiration-based irrigation scheduling for sugar beet on chernozem
abstract: Accurate irrigation scheduling is critical for maximising sugar beet yields while minimising water use on chernozem soils, which dominate the agricultural landscape of Vojvodina. This study evaluated a Penman–Monteith-based evapotranspiration (ET₀) model for generating irrigation recommendations across three growing seasons on experimental plots near Novi Sad. Reference evapotranspiration values were computed daily using meteorological data from an on-site automatic weather station and adjusted by crop coefficients (Kc) determined for local sugar beet cultivars at four distinct growth stages. Soil water status was monitored continuously using multi-depth capacitive probes to validate model outputs. Results demonstrated that ET-based scheduling reduced seasonal irrigation water application by 18–24% compared with calendar-based farmer practice, without a statistically significant reduction in root yield or sugar content. The irrigation scheduling algorithm was subsequently integrated into a web-based decision support tool accessible via mobile devices. The findings confirm that ET-driven scheduling is both technically feasible and economically advantageous for sugar beet production on chernozem, and provide locally calibrated Kc values that can be adopted directly by advisory services operating in the region.

title: Low-cost capacitive soil moisture probes: calibration across soil types
abstract: Capacitive soil moisture sensors offer a low-cost alternative to time-domain reflectometry (TDR) probes for continuous soil water monitoring, but their accuracy is strongly dependent on soil-specific calibration. This paper presents a systematic calibration procedure applied to a prototype capacitive probe across five soil types commonly encountered in Vojvodina: chernozem, humogley, sandy loam, silty clay loam, and saline solonetz. Laboratory calibration curves were developed by measuring probe output voltage against gravimetrically determined volumetric water content (VWC) across a range from air-dry to field saturation. Separate polynomial regression models were fitted for each soil type, and their coefficients of determination (R²) ranged from 0.94 to 0.98. Field validation was performed by co-locating calibrated capacitive probes with TDR probes in irrigated maize and sunflower plots. Mean absolute error across all soil types was below 0.024 m³ m⁻³, which is sufficient for practical irrigation scheduling applications. The study also assessed probe performance at three installation depths (15, 35, and 60 cm), confirming that calibration coefficients must be depth-specific in stratified soil profiles. The calibration methodology described here is directly applicable to the multi-depth probe array described in the authors' associated patent.

title: Deficit irrigation of vegetables in a changing climate
abstract: Deficit irrigation—deliberate application of water below full crop evapotranspiration demand—is increasingly proposed as a strategy for adapting vegetable production to reduced water availability under climate change scenarios. This conference paper synthesises three years of field trial data from pepper, tomato, and courgette crops grown under regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) in an open-field system in northern Serbia. Treatments ranged from 100% ET replacement (full irrigation) to 50% ET replacement applied at different phenological stages. Yield, water use efficiency (WUE), and selected quality parameters were measured for each combination. Results indicated that mild deficit (70–80% ET) applied during vegetative growth stages did not significantly reduce marketable yield of pepper or courgette, whereas tomato showed greater sensitivity, particularly during fruit set. WUE improved by up to 31% under the best-performing deficit regime relative to full irrigation. Climate projections for the Pannonian Plain suggest that summer precipitation deficits will intensify, making deficit irrigation protocols an essential component of future farm adaptation strategies. Practical guidelines for deficit scheduling using inexpensive sensor-based feedback are proposed.

title: A smartphone-based decision support application for real-time irrigation scheduling in smallholder vegetable production
abstract: Smallholder vegetable growers frequently lack access to reliable, timely irrigation advice, resulting in both over- and under-irrigation with associated yield and water losses. This paper describes the design, implementation, and on-farm evaluation of IrriAdvisor, a smartphone application that delivers real-time irrigation recommendations based on a combined ET-model and soil moisture feedback loop. The application retrieves daily meteorological data from a national weather service API and calculates crop-specific water demand using locally calibrated Penman–Monteith equations. Users can supplement model outputs with readings from low-cost capacitive soil moisture probes connected via Bluetooth to the mobile device. Recommendations are expressed as practical irrigation volumes and timing windows. Field evaluation was conducted across 14 smallholder farms in Vojvodina growing pepper, onion, and cucumber over a single growing season. Farmers using IrriAdvisor reduced water application by 21% on average compared with a control group, while marketable yields were statistically equivalent or higher. User acceptance surveys indicated high satisfaction with interface simplicity and notification reliability. The application architecture is described in sufficient detail to support replication and adaptation in other semi-arid regions with comparable data infrastructure.

title: Drip versus furrow irrigation of processing tomato: water productivity, yield components, and soil water distribution
abstract: Processing tomato is an economically significant crop in Vojvodina, yet comparative data on drip and furrow irrigation systems under local edaphoclimatic conditions remain limited. A two-season field experiment compared subsurface drip irrigation (SDI), surface drip irrigation (DI), and furrow irrigation (FI) at two water supply levels (100% and 80% ET replacement) on a chernozem soil. Soil water distribution was mapped weekly using a multi-depth capacitive probe array installed at representative locations within each treatment. Yield components—fruit number per plant, average fruit weight, and total marketable yield—as well as lycopene content and dry matter were measured at harvest. SDI achieved the highest water productivity (8.4 kg m⁻³) and uniform soil water distribution, while FI showed the highest deep percolation losses estimated from soil water balance calculations. Under the 80% ET treatment, SDI yield was not significantly different from full-irrigation SDI, suggesting strong potential for deficit management with this system. Energy requirements for pumping were also assessed and found to favour surface DI for small farm units. The results support a transition from furrow to drip systems as a water-saving strategy for the processing tomato sector.

title: Calibration and long-term stability of a multi-depth capacitive soil moisture probe array under field conditions
abstract: The long-term reliability of capacitive soil moisture probes is a critical concern for continuous irrigation monitoring systems. This paper reports an 18-month field stability assessment of the capacitive multi-depth probe array described in patent SYN-PAT-001, installed in a chernozem profile under irrigated sugar beet and winter wheat rotation. Probe output was compared monthly against gravimetric sampling at corresponding depths (15, 35, and 60 cm). Drift in probe response was quantified using a linear drift model fitted to paired datasets, and a simple field recalibration procedure requiring only three gravimetric reference measurements was developed and tested. Drift rates were below 0.003 m³ m⁻³ per month at the 15 and 35 cm depths, but reached 0.007 m³ m⁻³ per month at 60 cm, attributed to seasonal shrink-swell cycles in the subsoil. Temperature compensation using a co-located thermistor reduced residual drift by 62%. The recalibration procedure restored mean absolute error to below 0.020 m³ m⁻³ at all depths. These results demonstrate that the probe array is suitable for multi-season deployment with periodic recalibration and inform recommended maintenance protocols for commercial deployment of the sensor system.

title: Towards IoT-enabled irrigation management: integration of wireless soil moisture sensor networks with cloud-based decision support
abstract: The proliferation of low-cost wireless sensor nodes and cloud computing platforms creates new opportunities for scalable, automated irrigation management at the farm level. This paper presents an architecture for integrating a network of capacitive soil moisture sensor nodes with a cloud-based irrigation decision support engine. Each node transmits volumetric water content readings at configurable intervals over a LoRaWAN protocol to a gateway, from which data are forwarded to a cloud platform for storage, visualisation, and scheduling computation. The scheduling engine combines incoming sensor data with ET₀ forecasts derived from a regional numerical weather prediction model to issue valve-control commands to a drip irrigation controller via MQTT messaging. The system was deployed at a 4-hectare experimental plot at the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, and operated continuously for one full growing season of sugar beet. Automated scheduling reduced irrigation labour time by approximately 85% compared with manual sensor reading and scheduling. Water savings of 17% were achieved relative to a sensor-monitored manual scheduling control. Latency, packet loss, and battery consumption of sensor nodes are characterised, and design recommendations for scaling the architecture to larger farms are discussed.

title: Crop coefficient determination for sugar beet under drip irrigation in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Locally determined crop coefficients (Kc) are essential inputs for evapotranspiration-based irrigation scheduling, yet published FAO-56 values may not adequately represent cultivar performance and micro-climate in the Pannonian Plain. This study determined single and dual crop coefficients for four commercially grown sugar beet cultivars under drip-irrigated conditions across two experimental sites on chernozem in Vojvodina. Actual crop evapotranspiration (ETc) was measured using a soil water balance approach supported by continuous multi-depth soil moisture monitoring. Reference ET₀ was calculated from an automatic weather station. Kc values were derived for four growth stages: initial, development, mid-season, and late season. The locally determined mid-season Kc ranged from 1.17 to 1.23 across cultivars, exceeding the FAO-56 tabulated value of 1.05 by 11–17%. Using locally derived Kc values in the scheduling algorithm reduced irrigation over-application by 14% without yield penalty. The dual Kc approach, separating basal crop and soil evaporation components, provided additional accuracy during canopy development phases. A simple lookup table of locally calibrated Kc values by growth stage and cultivar group is provided for immediate use by agricultural advisors.

title: Effects of regulated deficit irrigation at critical growth stages on sunflower yield and oil content in semi-arid conditions
abstract: Sunflower is among the most drought-tolerant field crops cultivated in Vojvodina, yet supplemental irrigation during critical growth stages can substantially improve both yield and oil content. This paper investigates the effects of regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) applied selectively at four growth stages—vegetative, bud formation, flowering, and grain filling—on yield components and seed oil content of a mid-maturity sunflower hybrid. A split-plot factorial experiment was conducted over three growing seasons at an experimental station near Zrenjanin. Deficit levels of 100%, 75%, and 50% ET replacement were applied at each stage, while other stages received full irrigation. Water use efficiency and oil yield per unit area were used as primary performance indices. Deficit irrigation at the vegetative stage had the smallest yield penalty, while deficit at flowering caused a 19–27% reduction in achene yield regardless of the water level tested. Oil content showed greater resilience, declining significantly only under the most severe deficit at flowering. The study concludes that sunflower irrigation strategies should protect the flowering stage and may safely reduce water application during vegetative growth, providing practical guidance for farmers facing water allocation constraints.
