title: Precision irrigation in field crops: a review of sensor-based feedback systems and decision support frameworks applicable to Vojvodina
abstract: Precision irrigation represents a convergence of sensor technology, data analytics, and agronomy aimed at delivering the right amount of water to the right location at the right time. This review systematically examines published sensor-based feedback systems and decision support frameworks for field crop irrigation, with a focus on applicability to the Pannonian Plain agro-ecological context. Technologies reviewed include capacitive and TDR soil moisture sensors, electromagnetic induction soil mapping, UAV-mounted thermal cameras for crop water stress indices, and lysimeter-based evapotranspiration measurement. Decision support frameworks are evaluated across three categories: threshold-based scheduling, model-driven scheduling, and machine learning-assisted forecasting. Strengths and limitations of each approach are assessed in terms of data requirements, cost, scalability, and suitability for smallholder versus large commercial operations. A gap analysis identifies the limited availability of locally validated crop coefficient databases and the absence of standardised sensor calibration protocols for Vojvodina's diverse soil types as key barriers to adoption. The review concludes with a research agenda prioritising low-cost IoT sensor integration, open-access scheduling tools, and participatory co-design with farmers and advisory services.

title: A second-order finite difference scheme for the thin-film equation with variable surface energy on periodic microgrooved substrates
abstract: The thin-film equation in lubrication approximation is discretised on one-dimensional periodic microgrooved substrates using a second-order implicit finite difference scheme in space and a semi-implicit Crank–Nicolson stepping in time. The substrate geometry is encoded through a spatially varying disjoining pressure term whose amplitude and wavelength are matched to grooves of depth 5–20 µm and pitch 40 µm, representative of plasma-etched silicon samples. Mass conservation is verified numerically to within machine precision across all tested grid refinements. Convergence rates of 1.98 in the L2 norm are measured for smooth initial data, consistent with theoretical predictions. Simulations reveal that groove depth strongly modulates the onset of dewetting: for groove amplitudes exceeding a threshold of approximately 8 µm, a film of initial mean thickness 80 nm ruptures 30–40% earlier than on a flat substrate of equal wettability. The scheme is validated against published asymptotic solutions for weak substrate heterogeneity. Computational costs are compared for three linearisation strategies, and a modified Newton iteration is found to reduce wall-clock time by a factor of 2.3 relative to a fixed-point approach at equivalent accuracy.

title: Stability of thin viscous films on conical surfaces under partial wetting conditions
abstract: The linear stability of a thin viscous film coating the outer surface of a cone is examined analytically and numerically under partial wetting conditions. The base-state film thickness profile is derived from the lubrication equations in axisymmetric cone coordinates, accounting for the variation in surface curvature along the generator. A linearised eigenvalue problem is formulated and discretised using second-order finite differences on a non-uniform radial grid adapted to the base-state gradient. Growth rates are computed for cone half-angles between 5° and 45° and dimensionless film thicknesses from 0.01 to 0.1. Results show that increasing the cone angle stabilises the film against axisymmetric perturbations at all tested thicknesses, reducing the maximum growth rate by up to 47% compared to the flat-substrate limit. Non-axisymmetric modes are found to be subdominant for half-angles above 15°. Nonlinear time integration confirms the linear stability predictions up to perturbation amplitudes of 20% of the mean thickness, after which finite-amplitude effects introduce a 5–8% shift in the most dangerous wavenumber. The work extends available flat-substrate stability theory to a practically relevant curved geometry.

title: Goodness-of-fit testing for bivariate extreme value copulas via the Pickands dependence function
abstract: Bivariate extreme value copulas are characterised by their Pickands dependence function A, which must satisfy convexity and boundary constraints. Several nonparametric estimators of A have been proposed in the literature, but their use in formal goodness-of-fit testing has received limited attention. This paper derives a Cramér–von Mises test statistic based on the distance between a parametric estimate of A under the logistic, negative logistic and Hüsler–Reiss models and a boundary-corrected nonparametric estimate. The finite-sample distribution of the statistic under the null hypothesis is approximated by a parametric bootstrap procedure with B = 9999 replicates. A simulation study covering sample sizes n = 50, 100, 250 and 500 shows that the test achieves nominal size and competitive power against misspecified models. The procedure is applied to annual maximum daily precipitation and wind speed at three weather stations in the Western Balkans, where the Hüsler–Reiss model is selected at two of the three sites.

title: Estimating bivariate return periods for compound drought–heat events using an elliptical copula approach
abstract: Compound drought–heat events cause disproportionate impacts on agriculture and human health relative to either hazard individually. Using monthly standardised precipitation index (SPI-3) and maximum temperature anomaly data from 1960 to 2009 for 14 stations across the Pannonian Plain, this study fits Gaussian and Student-t copulas to model the dependence between drought severity and concurrent heat intensity. The Student-t copula with estimated degrees-of-freedom parameter ν̂ = 4.1 fits better than the Gaussian copula at the majority of stations, indicating heavier joint tail behaviour. Bivariate return periods in the Kendall sense and in the survival copula sense are computed and compared. Results indicate that Kendall return periods exceed univariate return periods by a factor of 1.3 to 2.1 for moderate events but converge toward univariate values for very rare events. A regionalisation using hierarchical clustering identifies three coherent zones across the domain.

title: Vine copula models for multivariate dependence in a network of Danube basin river gauges
abstract: Multivariate flood risk assessment requires joint models for discharge at several gauging stations simultaneously. Regular vine copulae (R-vines) decompose a multivariate distribution into a cascade of bivariate pair copulae and offer flexibility that no single parametric family can match. Discharge records from nine stations along the Danube corridor and its main tributaries within Serbia (1970–2010) were standardised to unit Fréchet margins. An R-vine structure was selected using the minimum spanning tree algorithm applied to pairwise empirical Kendall τ values. Each pair copula family was chosen from a candidate set of twelve families by the Akaike information criterion. Out-of-sample predictive performance was evaluated using a conditional probability scoring rule on withheld data from 2000–2010. The fitted vine model assigned non-negligible probability to simultaneous high-discharge events across all nine stations, whereas a meta-Gaussian model underestimated this probability by a factor of approximately three. Simulated 10 000-year realisations from the fitted vine are provided for use in hydraulic engineering design.

title: Extreme value copulas
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of the class of extreme value copulas arising as the limiting dependence structures of componentwise block maxima. The Pickands representation theorem is stated and proved, and its implications for the parametric subfamilies — logistic, asymmetric logistic, Galambos and Hüsler–Reiss — are derived. Estimation methods including maximum likelihood, the method of moments via Kendall's tau, and nonparametric estimators of the Pickands function are compared with respect to bias and variance in a comprehensive simulation study. The chapter includes a treatment of the connection between extreme value copulas and max-stable random fields, which is relevant for spatial modelling of environmental extremes. Three worked examples using Balkan precipitation and temperature data illustrate the methods. The chapter is intended for graduate students and researchers with a background in mathematical statistics.

title: Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of compound flood–wind events at the Serbian Danube reach
abstract: The peaks-over-threshold (POT) method requires selection of a threshold above which observations are modelled by the generalised Pareto distribution. In the bivariate context, both variables must exceed respective thresholds simultaneously or separately depending on the risk definition. This paper evaluates five threshold selection diagnostics — mean residual life plots, parameter stability plots, and three automated criteria based on goodness-of-fit — applied to concurrent records of river discharge and mean daily wind speed at five stations on the Serbian Danube reach (1980–2015). The copula of the bivariate exceedances is modelled with a censored-likelihood approach that accounts for observations exceeding only one threshold. Results show that the Galambos copula fits the bivariate extremes well (upper tail dependence coefficient 0.22–0.35) and that threshold choice materially affects estimated joint return levels: a 10 percent increase in threshold reduces the estimated 200-year joint quantile by up to 18 percent. Guidance for practitioners is provided.

title: Comparing parametric and nonparametric multivariate quantile contour estimation under copula misspecification
abstract: Multivariate quantile contours — level sets of a joint distribution at a given probability level — are central to multivariate return period analysis but sensitive to model misspecification. This simulation study compares five estimators: the Kendall quantile contour under three parametric copula families (Gaussian, Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard), the geometric quantile estimator of Chaudhuri and the depth-based Tukey median contour estimated by the Donoho–Gasko algorithm. Data are generated from six dependence structures at sample sizes n = 100, 300, 500, 1000, with standard Gumbel margins. Performance is measured by the integrated squared Hausdorff distance between estimated and true contours. Parametric estimators outperform nonparametric competitors when the model is correctly specified, but nonparametric depth-based contours exhibit substantially lower worst-case error across misspecified scenarios. A data-driven selection rule combining a copula goodness-of-fit test with a nonparametric fallback is proposed and evaluated on a subset of Serbian environmental monitoring data.

title: Modelling the joint distribution of extreme wildfire weather indices in Serbia using time-varying copulas
abstract: Climate change is shifting the distributional properties of wildfire weather indices, so static copula models fitted over long historical periods may be inadequate for current risk assessments. Daily records of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) components — Fine Fuel Moisture Code and Drought Code — from 18 stations in Serbia for 1961–2020 were used to investigate non-stationarity in both marginal distributions and dependence structure. Marginal parameters of the fitted GEV distributions were allowed to vary as smooth functions of a global temperature covariate using penalised spline regression. The copula dependence parameter was then estimated conditional on the same covariate using a local-likelihood approach with a Gaussian kernel. Estimated Kendall τ increased from approximately 0.31 in the 1960s to 0.48 in the 2010s, indicating strengthening co-occurrence of the two fire risk indicators. This trend implies that joint exceedance probabilities have roughly doubled over the observational record.

title: Sensitivity of infrastructure failure probability to tail dependence assumptions: a case study for bridge foundations on the Sava River
abstract: The structural reliability of bridge foundations in alluvial reaches depends jointly on peak discharge, scour depth and ice loading, three variables whose dependence in the extreme tails is poorly constrained by available data. This paper quantifies the sensitivity of estimated annual failure probability to the choice of tail dependence structure. A structural limit-state function for a simplified foundation model is combined with a joint hazard model in which the copula family is varied across six candidates spanning tail independence to strong upper tail dependence. The difference between the failure probability under the independence copula and under the upper-tail-dependent Gumbel–Hougaard copula with τ = 0.4 is approximately one order of magnitude at annual exceedance probability 10⁻⁴, a difference that is practically significant for design. A robust upper bound is obtained by taking the maximum over a class of copulas with matching Kendall τ.

title: Bayesian estimation of C-vine copula parameters for high-dimensional environmental hazard vectors
abstract: C-vine copulas reduce the dimensionality problem in multivariate dependence modelling by expressing the joint density as a product of bivariate pair copulas arranged in a tree structure. When the dimension is moderate to high (here d = 8), maximum likelihood estimation of the full parameter vector becomes computationally burdensome and confidence intervals are poorly calibrated. This preprint proposes a blocked Gibbs sampler for posterior inference over C-vine structures and bivariate copula family indicators jointly, using a reversible-jump extension. Experiments on simulated data with n = 500 show that credible intervals for tail dependence coefficients have nominal coverage 3 to 8 percentage points closer to 95 percent than profile likelihood intervals. The method is applied to an eight-dimensional vector of hydrometeorological hazard indicators — discharge, precipitation intensity, wind speed, temperature anomaly, and four soil moisture metrics — observed simultaneously at a single representative site in the Bačka subregion of Vojvodina.

title: A regional frequency analysis framework for multivariate compound events using spatial pooling and copula aggregation
abstract: Regional frequency analysis (RFA) extends the information base for rare event estimation by pooling data from hydrologically homogeneous stations. Classical RFA applies to univariate distributions; this paper extends the L-moments approach to multivariate compound events by fitting station-specific copulas and aggregating them into a regional dependence structure using a weighted Wasserstein barycenter. Sixty-three stations in the middle Danube basin (Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia) contribute 40 to 95 years of simultaneous discharge and precipitation records. Homogeneity is assessed using a multivariate extension of the Hosking–Wallis H statistic. The regional copula reduces estimation uncertainty for joint return levels at ungauged locations compared to at-site estimation; the reduction in root-mean-square error for the 100-year bivariate quantile ranges from 23 to 41 percent depending on the region. The method is implemented in an open-source R package deposited at the University of Novi Sad data repository.
venue: Water Resources Research

title: Quantile regression forests for marginal standardisation in nonparametric multivariate extreme value analysis
abstract: Transforming raw observations to uniform or Fréchet margins is a necessary preprocessing step in most copula-based extreme value analyses, and the quality of this transformation influences downstream inference. Standard empirical probability integral transforms perform poorly in sparse tails. This paper proposes using quantile regression forests to estimate marginal conditional distribution functions that adapt to covariate information — elevation, land use, catchment area — thereby improving tail standardisation at environmental monitoring stations. The approach is evaluated in a leave-one-out cross-validation on 44 discharge stations in Serbia and Croatia. After forest-based standardisation, the residual dependence structure is more stable across stations and seasons than after empirical-transform standardisation: the interquartile range of estimated pairwise Kendall τ values shrinks by 19 percent. The standardised residuals are then used as input to a Brown–Resnick max-stable model fitted by pairwise composite likelihood, which yields a 12 percent reduction in the composite likelihood information criterion relative to the baseline approach.

title: Skin conductance and self-reported affect after walks in a city park versus a commercial street: a pilot study
abstract: This pilot study compared electrodermal activity (EDA) and self-reported affect in 28 university students (mean age 21.4, SD 2.1) who completed two 20-minute walks—one through Štrand park and one along a busy commercial street in Novi Sad—in counterbalanced order. Portable EDA sensors recorded mean skin conductance level and number of non-specific skin conductance responses during each walk and a subsequent 5-minute seated recovery period. Participants also completed the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule and a single-item perceived stress scale immediately after each walk. EDA during the recovery period was significantly lower after the park walk than after the street walk (paired t-test, p = .03, d = 0.54). Self-reported negative affect showed a parallel pattern (p = .04, d = 0.50). The study is limited by small sample size and lack of baseline physiological recording, but the magnitude of differences is consistent with stress recovery theory and motivates a larger controlled design. Recruitment and ethical procedures are described in detail to support replication.

title: Trait anxiety as a moderator of physiological recovery in green versus built urban settings
abstract: Stress recovery theory predicts faster psychophysiological recovery in natural than in built environments, yet individual differences may attenuate or amplify this effect. This study tested whether trait anxiety (STAI-T) moderated heart rate variability (HRV) recovery following a validated laboratory stress induction (Trier Social Stress Test) when participants subsequently viewed a 10-minute video of either a riverside park or an urban commercial area. Seventy-two adults (38 women, mean age 27.6, SD 6.3) were randomly assigned to viewing condition. RMSSD was recorded continuously; self-reported stress and restorativeness were assessed post-viewing. A significant Condition × Trait Anxiety interaction emerged for RMSSD recovery slope (F(1,68) = 5.14, p = .027, η²p = .07): high-anxiety individuals showed blunted HRV recovery in both conditions but proportionally less blunting in the park video condition. Perceived restorativeness did not differ by trait anxiety. The findings suggest that high-trait-anxiety individuals may still benefit physiologically from green environments but require larger or more immersive exposures to reach the same recovery magnitude as low-anxiety individuals.

title: Comparing self-report restorativeness scales: psychometric properties of three instruments in a Serbian-speaking sample
abstract: Three widely used instruments for measuring perceived restorativeness—the Perceived Restorativeness Scale (PRS), the Restorative Components Scale (RCS), and a brief restorativeness adjective checklist translated for this study—were administered to 214 adults (131 women, mean age 33.1, SD 11.8) recruited through community centres in Novi Sad. Participants rated ten environment descriptions (five green, five built) and completed all three scales after each description. Confirmatory factor analysis replicated the four-factor structure of the PRS and three-factor structure of the RCS in this sample; model fit was acceptable for both (CFI > .92, RMSEA < .07). Convergent validity between PRS and RCS total scores was high (r = .81), but fascination subscales diverged in their loadings on descriptions of managed versus semi-wild green spaces. Internal consistency (Cronbach's α) ranged from .74 to .89 across subscales. The adjective checklist showed weaker fit but acceptable reliability. Normative data for the Serbian translations and inter-scale correlation matrices are reported and made available for regional researchers.

title: Does walking pace moderate physiological restoration in a linear park? A within-subjects field experiment
abstract: Laboratory and simulated-environment studies often impose sedentary viewing, leaving open whether walking pace interacts with green-space exposure to influence stress recovery. In a within-subjects design, 44 adults completed a standardised cognitive load task before each of three 15-minute walks along the same tree-lined canal path in Novi Sad at self-paced slow, medium, and brisk speeds on three separate days (order counterbalanced). Heart rate variability (SDNN, RMSSD), cortisol from saliva samples collected immediately post-walk, and the Stress Recovery Scale were measured. Mixed-effects models controlling for ambient temperature and time of day showed a significant effect of condition on RMSSD (F(2,84) = 4.31, p = .016) with slow walking associated with highest post-walk RMSSD. Salivary cortisol did not differ significantly across pace conditions (p = .22). Self-reported recovery was highest for slow walking (d = 0.41 vs. brisk). Results suggest that the pacing of green-space use, not only its duration or type, may matter for physiological outcomes.

title: Neighbourhood green space quantity and self-reported psychological restoration in Novi Sad residents: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: Using data from a structured telephone survey of 487 adult residents of Novi Sad (52% women, mean age 42.3, SD 14.6), this study examined associations between objective neighbourhood green space quantity—measured as the proportion of vegetated land cover within a 500-metre Euclidean buffer around each participant's home using municipal GIS data—and self-reported restoration, perceived stress (PSS-10), and restorative experience frequency (custom scale). After adjusting for age, gender, household income, and self-reported health, a 10-percentage-point increase in green cover was associated with a 0.18-point reduction in PSS-10 scores (95% CI: −0.31 to −0.05) and a 0.24-point increase in restorative experience frequency (95% CI: 0.09–0.39). Associations did not significantly differ by income group, contrary to hypotheses based on health equity literature. Perceived safety of local green spaces partially mediated the PSS-10 association (indirect effect proportion = 0.31). Limitations include reliance on self-reported outcome data and cross-sectional design.

title: Eye-tracking indicators of attentional engagement during viewing of urban park and street photographs
abstract: Attention restoration theory proposes that natural environments support effortless, involuntary attention, whereas built urban environments demand directed attention. This study used a portable eye-tracker to record fixation duration, saccade amplitude, and pupil diameter while 56 participants (31 women, mean age 24.8, SD 4.5) viewed 40 high-resolution photographs (20 park scenes, 20 commercial street scenes) each for 8 seconds. A pre-viewing arithmetic task served as a fatigue induction. Mean fixation duration was significantly longer for park photographs (248 ms vs. 211 ms, t(55) = 4.87, p < .001, d = 0.65), and pupil diameter was smaller (2.31 mm vs. 2.54 mm, p < .001), consistent with lower cognitive load. Saccade amplitudes did not differ significantly. Exploratory region-of-interest analyses showed that vegetation elements attracted first fixations more reliably than architectural elements attracted first fixations in the street scenes. Post-viewing ratings of restorativeness correlated positively with mean fixation duration (r = .38, p < .001). The relationship between oculomotor indices and self-report restoration warrants replication with more ecologically valid stimuli.

title: Age differences in self-reported and physiological restoration across green and built urban environments
abstract: Younger and older adults may differ in the degree to which green spaces support stress recovery, yet age is rarely examined as a primary moderator in restorative environment research. This study recruited three age groups—young adults (18–30, n = 41), middle-aged adults (40–55, n = 39), and older adults (65–75, n = 35)—who completed a structured 20-minute walk through a municipal park and a 20-minute walk along a commercial street in Novi Sad (order counterbalanced, one week apart). Heart rate variability (RMSSD), blood pressure, and self-reported restorativeness and mood were assessed pre- and post-walk. A significant Age Group × Environment interaction emerged for systolic blood pressure change (F(2,112) = 3.89, p = .023): older adults showed greater systolic blood pressure reduction in the park condition (mean Δ = −5.4 mmHg) than younger adults (mean Δ = −1.8 mmHg). RMSSD gains did not significantly interact with age. Self-reported restorativeness ratings were uniformly higher in the park condition across all groups. Implications for age-sensitive urban planning are discussed.

title: Effect of Weld Toe Geometry on Vibration Response of Rectangular Steel Frame Joints
abstract: Weld toe geometry influences local stress concentrations and, consequently, the dynamic stiffness of frame joints. This paper examines three weld toe profiles—as-welded, ground flush, and TIG-dressed—fabricated on identical S355 steel rectangular frame specimens. Each specimen was tested using impact hammer excitation at nine measurement points, and frequency response functions (FRFs) were computed from the averaged response over 20 impacts. The first four natural frequencies and corresponding mode shapes were extracted via the rational fraction polynomial method. Ground-flush specimens showed a mean increase of 0.6% in the first natural frequency relative to as-welded specimens, while TIG-dressed specimens showed 1.1%. Modal assurance criterion (MAC) values between all profile variants exceeded 0.97 for the first two modes, indicating negligible mode shape changes. The paper concludes that weld dressing has a measurable but small effect on global modal parameters, relevant when establishing baseline signatures for health monitoring.

title: Comparison of Frequency-Domain Decomposition and Stochastic Subspace Identification for Damage Localization in Multi-Bay Steel Frames
abstract: Two widely used OMA algorithms—frequency-domain decomposition (FDD) and stochastic subspace identification (SSI-COV)—are compared for their ability to localize damage in a three-bay, two-storey welded steel frame model. Damage was simulated by progressively cutting a weld in the lower right column-beam connection in three stages, reducing net throat area by 20%, 40%, and 60%. Ambient excitation was provided by pedestrian-like loading applied at the floor levels. Both algorithms identified natural frequencies within 0.15 Hz of each other for the first six modes. Damage localization was assessed via the modal strain energy damage index (MSEDI). SSI-COV achieved correct panel identification at 20% damage in 7 of 10 repeated trials, while FDD achieved correct localization in only 4 of 10 at the same damage level. At 40% and 60% damage, both methods localized correctly in all trials. The study recommends SSI-COV for early-stage damage detection when signal-to-noise conditions are moderate.

title: Temperature Effects on Modal Parameters of Welded Steel Frame Structures: A Seasonal Monitoring Study
abstract: Environmental temperature variation is a known source of false alarms in vibration-based structural health monitoring systems. This paper reports a 14-month continuous monitoring campaign on a full-scale welded steel storage rack structure at an industrial facility in Zrenjanin, during which ambient temperature ranged from −14 °C to +38 °C. Twelve accelerometers and four temperature sensors were installed. OMA was performed on 30-minute data windows using SSI-COV. The first natural frequency varied by up to 4.3% over the monitoring period, primarily correlated with temperature (Pearson r = −0.81). A linear regression model was fitted to remove temperature effects from frequency trends; residuals were examined for anomalies. No structural damage occurred during the campaign, confirming the temperature model captured the dominant environmental influence. The study provides a temperature-compensation baseline that can support future damage detection in similar industrial steel structures in the Pannonian climate zone.

title: Laser Vibrometry Measurements of Weld-Zone Mode Shapes in Thin-Walled Steel Box Sections
abstract: Conventional accelerometer grids cannot resolve high-spatial-resolution mode shapes in thin-walled welded box sections without adding significant mass. This paper uses a scanning laser Doppler vibrometer (SLDV) to measure operational deflection shapes at 320 scan points on three box-section specimens (wall thickness 4 mm, 6 mm, and 8 mm) under harmonic excitation at frequencies corresponding to the first five bending and torsional modes. Specimens were fabricated with identical nominal welds; one specimen per thickness group contained an artificial internal lack-of-fusion defect of 12 mm length introduced by inserting a 0.3 mm Teflon insert during fabrication. The SLDV measurements revealed localized amplitude anomalies of 8–23% at the defect location for the 4 mm and 6 mm specimens at modes 3 and 4, while the 8 mm specimen showed no detectable anomaly. Mass loading from a hypothetical 4-accelerometer grid would have shifted frequencies by up to 2.1%, justifying the non-contact approach. Fractional wavelet energy maps derived from the velocity fields improved defect contrast over raw mode shape images.

title: Vibration-Based Structural Health Monitoring of Steel Structures: Methods and Practical Considerations
abstract: This book chapter reviews the application of vibration-based SHM to steel civil and industrial structures, with emphasis on welded connections. The chapter covers the theoretical basis of modal analysis, sensor placement strategies, algorithm selection criteria, and the practical challenges of long-term monitoring including power supply, data transmission, and environmental compensation. Case studies drawn from laboratory and field experience in the Western Balkans region illustrate typical damage scenarios (weld cracking, corrosion-induced stiffness loss, fatigue-related loosening) and the sensitivity of common damage indices to each. Particular attention is given to structures with irregular geometry or asymmetric boundary conditions, where standard damage localization indices can give misleading results. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems, including the scarcity of labeled field damage datasets and the difficulty of transferring laboratory-calibrated models to field conditions.

title: Detection of Fatigue Crack Initiation in Fillet-Welded T-Joints Using Damping Ratio Tracking
abstract: Changes in damping ratio are hypothesized to be more sensitive to early-stage crack initiation than frequency shifts, but damping estimation is highly variable. This paper investigates the feasibility of tracking damping ratios as a damage indicator in fillet-welded T-joint specimens subjected to cyclic three-point bending fatigue loading. Eight specimens of S275 steel were cycled at 60% and 75% of their static failure load. OMA data were collected at intervals of 5,000 load cycles. Damping ratios for the first bending mode, estimated by the half-power bandwidth method and by SSI-COV, were compared. SSI-COV estimates showed standard deviations approximately 40% lower than half-power bandwidth estimates. Damping ratios increased detectably (>2σ above baseline) at approximately 35–40% of total fatigue life at 75% load, preceding a measurable frequency drop by roughly 8,000 cycles. At 60% load, no consistent damping increase was detected prior to visible crack formation. Results suggest that damping tracking may provide early warning in moderate-to-high stress fatigue scenarios.

title: Baseline-Free Damage Detection in Welded Steel Trusses Using Transmissibility Functions
abstract: Transmissibility-based methods do not require a pristine baseline measurement, making them attractive for structures where an undamaged reference state was never recorded. This paper evaluates a transmissibility-function damage indicator on three laboratory-scale welded Pratt-type steel truss specimens. Each truss had 11 joints; damage was introduced at single joints by partially cutting the weld of one diagonal member to depths of 1, 2, and 3 mm. Transmissibility functions were computed between all sensor-pair combinations (15 pairs from 6 accelerometers) under broadband random excitation. A transmissibility damage index (TDI) based on the Euclidean norm of transmissibility differences between two arbitrary operating conditions was computed. Correct damage localization was achieved in 18 of 21 test cases (86%) across all damage levels and joint positions. Failed cases were concentrated at joints near the support conditions. Comparison with the modal strain energy method showed similar localization accuracy but lower computational demand for TDI. The approach requires no FE model and no undamaged reference.

title: Low-Cost Wireless Sensor Network for Continuous Vibration Monitoring of a Welded Steel Overhead Crane Girder
abstract: Overhead crane girders in production halls undergo repetitive dynamic loading from hoisting operations and are susceptible to weld fatigue at rail attachment points. This paper describes the design, installation, and 18-month operation of a low-cost wireless accelerometer network (8 nodes, MEMS sensors, 1 kHz sampling) installed on a 22-metre span welded box-girder crane at a metalworking company in Zrenjanin. Data were transmitted to a local edge device and processed using automated SSI-COV at each hoisting event. Over 3,400 events were recorded. The first bending frequency showed a gradual decrease of 0.9% over the monitoring period; post-campaign visual inspection revealed a 28 mm weld fatigue crack at one rail attachment. Frequency changes tracked the estimated crack length progression using a fracture mechanics model calibrated to the geometry. System power consumption averaged 220 mW per node. The study demonstrates that MEMS-based wireless networks can detect slow-growing weld fatigue cracks in crane girders under purely operational loading.

title: Principal Component Analysis of Long-Term Modal Data for Anomaly Detection in an Industrial Steel Frame: Influence of Operational Load Patterns
abstract: Statistical process control methods applied to long-term SHM data must account not only for environmental variability but also for systematic changes in operational loads such as storage fill levels or production-line traffic. This paper applies principal component analysis (PCA) to a 22-month dataset of modal parameters (12 frequency and 8 damping estimates per measurement epoch) collected from a welded steel mezzanine frame in a logistics warehouse in the Novi Sad industrial zone. Ambient excitation was provided by forklift traffic. Temperature, humidity, and floor load (estimated from a weigh-bridge log) were recorded simultaneously. A PCA model trained on the first 6 months of data reduced the feature vector to 3 principal components explaining 87% of variance. Control charts on the residuals flagged three anomalous periods; two corresponded to planned maintenance (bolt retightening), and one corresponded to a previously unreported localized weld crack found during the subsequent annual inspection. False alarm rate over the remaining 16 months was 3.1%, comparable to the 5% control limit set.

title: Modal Testing Protocol for Welded Steel Frame Structures in Active Industrial Environments: Repeatability and Interference Assessment
abstract: Performing modal tests in operating industrial environments introduces variability from background machinery noise, temperature gradients, and measurement interruptions. This paper proposes and evaluates a standardized testing protocol designed to maximize repeatability under such conditions. The protocol specifies sensor placement rules based on effective independence (EFI) criteria, a minimum recording duration formula as a function of the target frequency resolution and lowest expected natural frequency, and a quality-control step using automated pole stabilization diagrams with human-review triggers. The protocol was validated on five distinct welded steel frame types at three industrial sites in Vojvodina over a period of two years, with two operators per site performing independent tests within 48 hours of each other. Inter-operator repeatability of estimated natural frequencies was within 0.4% for all structures and all modes up to the sixth. Damping ratio repeatability was within 12% of the mean value for 89% of identified modes. The protocol is described in sufficient detail to be reproducible without specialized training beyond standard OMA software familiarity.

title: Kinematic analysis of the standard three-point hitch under lateral slope conditions using a constrained multibody model
abstract: The three-point hitch (TPH) is the primary mechanical interface between an agricultural tractor and its implements. While its kinematics on flat ground are well documented, behaviour on lateral slopes up to 15° has received less attention. This paper presents a constrained planar-plus-tilt multibody model of a Category II TPH constructed in MSC Adams and validated against static measurements on a purpose-built test frame at the Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin'. Seventeen link positions were instrumented with string potentiometers. Model predictions of lower link angle deviated from measured values by at most 1.8° across the full slope range. Sensitivity analysis revealed that the top link length has the dominant influence on implement pitch angle on slopes, contributing 63% of variance in a Sobol decomposition. The results suggest that top-link adjustment protocols currently specified in ISO 730 are insufficient for slopes above 10° when using rigid-frame ploughs, and a revised adjustment envelope is proposed.

title: Oestrogen receptor alpha expression in canine mammary carcinomas: immunohistochemical evaluation and association with histological grade
abstract: Oestrogen receptor alpha (ERα) expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded sections from 78 canine mammary carcinomas graded according to the Elston–Ellis adapted scheme. Anti-human ERα antibody clone SP1 was applied after heat-induced epitope retrieval; positive controls were normal uterine tissue sections. An H-score was calculated combining staining intensity (0–3) and percentage of positive nuclei. ERα positivity was recorded in 38 of 78 tumours (49%). A statistically significant inverse relationship was found between ERα H-score and histological grade: grade I tumours had a median H-score of 142, grade II 87, and grade III 31 (Kruskal–Wallis p < 0.001). Tumours showing lymphovascular invasion were ERα-negative in 79% of cases. These findings mirror patterns described in human breast carcinoma and support the biological relevance of ERα profiling in the clinical assessment of canine mammary malignancies.

title: Progesterone receptor status in canine mammary tumours and its correlation with oestrogen receptor expression
abstract: Progesterone receptor (PR) immunoreactivity was assessed in 91 canine mammary tumours, including 67 malignant and 24 benign lesions, using clone 1E2 antibody on automated immunostainer platforms. Results were scored semi-quantitatively (Allred scale). PR positivity was detected in 54% of malignant and 83% of benign tumours. Among carcinomas, concordant ERα-positive/PR-positive cases accounted for 39%, while ERα-negative/PR-negative cases accounted for 31%, a distribution consistent with human luminal-A and triple-negative-like subtypes respectively. Simple carcinomas were more frequently PR-negative than complex carcinomas (p = 0.018, Fisher's exact test). No significant difference in PR status was found between grade II and grade III carcinomas. The Allred score correlated moderately with the H-score derived from parallel ERα staining (Spearman r = 0.58). Findings suggest that combined ER/PR profiling provides more stratification information than either marker alone in routine canine mammary tumour diagnostics.
venue: Journal of Comparative Veterinary Oncology

title: HER2 scoring in canine mammary carcinomas: comparison of three immunohistochemical antibody clones and fluorescence in situ hybridisation
abstract: HER2 protein overexpression was evaluated using three commercially available antibody clones (CB11, SP3, and 4B5) on tissue microarrays constructed from 55 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded canine mammary carcinoma blocks. Results were scored according to an adapted human scoring system (0, 1+, 2+, 3+). Cases scoring 2+ were further assessed by fluorescence in situ hybridisation (FISH) for HER2 gene amplification. Overall HER2 3+ positivity rates were 18%, 22%, and 16% for CB11, SP3, and 4B5 respectively. Inter-clone agreement was moderate to good (kappa 0.59–0.71). FISH amplification was confirmed in 6 of 12 cases scored 2+ by the majority clone, yielding an effective HER2-positive rate of 27% across the cohort. Tissue microarray scoring correlated well with full-section scoring in a 20-case validation subset (concordance 90%). These data support tissue microarray construction as a practical and resource-efficient approach for multi-marker studies in canine mammary pathology.

title: Survival analysis following surgical excision of canine mammary carcinomas: a cohort study of 84 bitches with two-year follow-up
abstract: Disease-free interval and overall survival were assessed in 84 bitches undergoing complete surgical excision of histologically confirmed mammary carcinomas between 2010 and 2014. Follow-up data were collected through structured telephone interviews with owners and attending veterinary practitioners at six-month intervals. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. Median disease-free interval was 18 months (95% CI: 14–23) and median overall survival 22 months (95% CI: 17–28). Histological grade was the strongest independent predictor of disease-free interval (grade III vs. I HR = 4.1; p < 0.001). Lymph node involvement at surgery reduced median overall survival to 9 months. Tumour size above 3 cm was associated with a 2.3-fold increase in hazard for local recurrence. ERα negativity correlated with shorter overall survival in multivariable analysis (HR = 2.6; p = 0.009). Loss to follow-up was 14%, predominantly in the final six-month interval.

title: Ki-67 proliferation index in canine mammary carcinomas: optimal cut-off determination and clinical relevance
abstract: Ki-67 immunoreactivity was evaluated in 66 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded sections of canine mammary carcinomas using anti-Ki-67 antibody clone MIB-1. The labelling index was calculated as the percentage of positively stained nuclei in five high-power fields counted by two independent observers using digital image analysis software (QuPath 0.3). The mean Ki-67 labelling index was 24.3% (range 2–71%). Receiver operating characteristic analysis against two-year survival yielded an optimal cut-off of 22%, with sensitivity 68% and specificity 74%. Cases with Ki-67 above the cut-off had significantly shorter overall survival (log-rank p = 0.003). In multivariable regression including grade and nodal status, Ki-67 retained independent prognostic significance (HR = 2.1; p = 0.04). Inter-observer variability was low (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.91). These results support the routine inclusion of Ki-67 index in canine mammary carcinoma pathology reports alongside histological grade.

title: Histopathological characterisation of inflammatory mammary carcinoma in bitches: a series of 14 cases
abstract: Inflammatory mammary carcinoma (IMC) in dogs is a rare and aggressive clinical entity. Fourteen cases with clinical signs consistent with IMC (erythema, oedema, peau d'orange appearance) confirmed by biopsy between 2014 and 2020 were characterised histologically and immunohistochemically. Dermal lymphatic emboli were present in all 14 cases. Tumour type was solid carcinoma in 9, tubular carcinoma in 3, and anaplastic carcinoma in 2. All cases were grade III. ER and PR positivity was recorded in only 2 cases each; HER2 3+ was identified in 4 cases; Ki-67 labelling index ranged from 41 to 78%. Median survival from diagnosis was 27 days (range 6–63 days), with no animal surviving beyond two months. Pathological features and receptor profile distinguished these cases clearly from non-inflammatory high-grade carcinomas in the same practice population, supporting IMC as a distinct biological entity warranting separate classification in canine tumour registries.

title: Digital image analysis versus manual scoring of HER2 immunohistochemistry in canine mammary tumours: a methodological comparison
abstract: Automated digital image analysis (DIA) for HER2 immunohistochemical scoring was compared with conventional manual scoring in 80 canine mammary carcinoma sections stained with clone 4B5. Whole-slide images were acquired at 40× equivalent resolution on a Pannoramic 250 scanner. DIA was performed using two algorithms: a threshold-based membrane segmentation tool and a machine-learning classifier trained on 20 annotated cases. Manual scoring was performed independently by two experienced pathologists. Agreement between manual consensus and threshold-based DIA was moderate (kappa 0.58); agreement between manual consensus and the machine-learning classifier was substantially higher (kappa 0.79). Discrepancies were most frequent in the 2+ category, where membrane continuity was difficult to assess algorithmically. Processing time per slide was 4.2 minutes for DIA versus 12.8 minutes for manual scoring. Both DIA methods showed acceptable reproducibility on repeat scanning sessions (ICC > 0.85). These results suggest the machine-learning DIA approach is suitable for high-throughput research applications but requires case-by-case review of equivocal 2+ scores.

title: Pathology of canine mammary tumours: a practical guide for veterinary diagnosticians
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of the macroscopic and microscopic pathology of mammary gland tumours in bitches, intended as a practical reference for veterinary diagnostic pathologists and clinicians. Topics covered include gross examination and sampling protocols for mastectomy specimens, application of the current WHO classification, criteria for histological grading, and interpretation of immunohistochemical panels including ERα, PR, HER2, and Ki-67. Illustrated examples are provided for each tumour type with annotated photomicrographs. A section on reporting standards addresses minimum data set requirements for clinical decision-making. The chapter also discusses diagnostic pitfalls, including pseudoinvasion artefacts, processing-related antigen loss affecting immunostaining, and the distinction between reactive and neoplastic spindle-cell proliferations. Practical tables summarise antibody dilutions, retrieval conditions, and scoring criteria validated in the authors' laboratory.

title: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte density in canine mammary carcinomas and its relationship with molecular subtype and survival
abstract: Stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (sTILs) were evaluated on routine haematoxylin and eosin sections from 95 canine mammary carcinomas following a scoring method adapted from human breast cancer guidelines. sTIL density was recorded in 10% increments. CD3 and CD20 immunostaining was performed to characterise T-cell and B-cell infiltration separately. Mean sTIL density was 18% (range 0–70%). Triple-negative-like tumours had significantly higher sTIL density (mean 34%) compared with luminal-A-like (mean 9%) and HER2-enriched-like (mean 22%) subtypes (ANOVA p < 0.001). High sTIL density (≥ 30%) was associated with improved two-year disease-free interval in triple-negative-like tumours (log-rank p = 0.027) but not in other subtypes. CD3-positive infiltrate predominated in all subtypes; CD20-positive density was highest in luminal-B-like carcinomas. These findings are consistent with the human literature on immune microenvironment variation across breast cancer subtypes and support sTIL assessment as a potentially informative pathological variable in canine mammary carcinoma prognosis.

title: Concordance between fine-needle aspiration cytology and histopathology in the preoperative assessment of canine mammary masses
abstract: The diagnostic accuracy of fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) for predicting histopathological outcome was evaluated in 110 canine mammary masses for which both preoperative cytology and postoperative histopathology were available. FNAC was performed under mild sedation; slides were stained with May–Grünwald–Giemsa and Papanicolaou stains. Histopathological diagnosis served as the reference standard. Overall agreement for malignant versus benign classification was 78%, with sensitivity of 81% and specificity of 74%. Positive predictive value was 79% and negative predictive value 76%. The most common cytological misclassification was false-negative assignment of low-grade tubular carcinomas as benign. Cellularity was rated as adequate in 89% of aspirates; cystic lesions and fibroadenomatous changes were associated with the highest inadequate sample rates. These data indicate that FNAC is a useful but imperfect triage tool, and that histopathological examination of excised tissue remains necessary for definitive diagnosis and grading.

title: Solute inclusion modelling in progressive freeze-concentration of lactic acid fermentation broth
abstract: Progressive freeze-concentration was applied to a lactic acid fermentation broth containing 38–55 g/L lactic acid, residual sugars, proteins, and pigment compounds. A static tube crystalliser was operated at wall temperatures between −4 and −10 °C, and ice layers of 5–25 mm thickness were grown over periods of 30–180 minutes. Solute inclusion in the ice phase was quantified by ion chromatography for lactic acid and HPLC for residual glucose and fructose. An effective distribution coefficient (K_eff) was calculated for each solute as a function of growth velocity, determined by optical measurement of the ice–liquid interface position. K_eff for lactic acid ranged from 0.021 at 0.8 µm/s to 0.12 at 4.1 µm/s, in reasonable agreement with the Burton–Prim–Slichter framework when a boundary layer thickness of 210 µm was assumed. Protein inclusion was low (< 1.2 % of broth protein in the ice phase) across all conditions, confirming the suitability of the method for bioprocess streams sensitive to thermal denaturation. A semi-empirical inclusion model fitted to the data predicted K_eff within ±15 % over the tested range.

title: Energy consumption and concentration efficiency in a falling-film cryoconcentrator: comparison of single- and two-stage configurations for elderflower extract
abstract: A custom-built falling-film cryoconcentrator was evaluated for concentrating elderflower aqueous extract, a stream rich in flavonoids and volatile aroma compounds that degrades rapidly under conventional evaporative conditions. Single-stage and two-stage configurations were compared across feed flow rates of 20–80 L/h and refrigerant temperatures of −6 and −10 °C. Specific energy consumption was measured by inline power metering and normalised per kilogram of water removed. The two-stage configuration achieved a concentration factor of 4.1 with a specific energy consumption of 310 kJ/kg water removed, compared to 420 kJ/kg for a single stage at equivalent concentration factor, owing to improved ice wash efficiency. Retention of total flavonoids, expressed as rutin equivalents, was 96.3 ± 1.1 % in the concentrate. Ice wash column separation efficiency was characterised as a function of wash water volume-to-ice mass ratio, with 95 % solute recovery achieved at ratios above 0.35. A simple steady-state process model accounting for heat transfer in the falling film and wash column hydraulics reproduced measured concentration profiles with a mean absolute error below 8 %.

title: Cryomicroscopic observation of dendritic ice formation in high-fructose fermentation media and implications for unit operation design
abstract: Cryomicroscopy was used to directly image ice crystal nucleation and subsequent dendritic growth in synthetic fermentation media containing fructose (50–200 g/L), ethanol (0–8 % v/v), and yeast extract (2–10 g/L). A Peltier-controlled cryostage maintained cooling rates between 0.1 and 5 °C/min, and time-lapse images were recorded at 2-second intervals. Dendritic arm spacing was measured by image analysis and correlated with cooling rate using a power-law relationship (arm spacing ∝ cooling rate^−0.38). Ethanol at concentrations above 4 % v/v caused a pronounced shift toward finer, more irregular dendrite morphology, which was linked to increased solute inclusion during subsequent centrifugal separation tests. Yeast extract proteins above 6 g/L further suppressed crystal growth anisotropy without significantly altering nucleation temperature. The observations were used to define practical operating windows—specifically, cooling rates below 0.5 °C/min and ethanol below 3 % v/v—for achieving coarse, washable ice crystals in a scraped-surface crystalliser. These findings are discussed in the context of retrofitting existing fermentation post-processing lines with freeze-concentration steps.

title: Freeze-concentration as a downstream step for thermolabile fermentation broths: process principles, equipment options, and current limitations
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of freeze-concentration unit operations as applied to fermentation downstream processing, addressing tubular progressive crystallisers, falling-film systems, and suspension crystallisers. Thermodynamic fundamentals of the aqueous ice–solution equilibrium are presented alongside practical heat transfer correlations relevant to equipment sizing. The chapter discusses solute inclusion mechanisms and the role of crystal growth velocity, hydrodynamics, and multi-component interactions in determining separation efficiency. Equipment options are compared on the basis of published concentration factors, energy intensity (typically 150–500 kJ per kg water removed), and suitability for viscous or protein-containing streams. Particular attention is given to wash column design as the primary determinant of final product purity. Current limitations are identified, including scale-up uncertainty for suspension crystallisers beyond pilot scale, the scarcity of validated inclusion models for multicomponent fermentation media, and the limited availability of long-term fouling data from industrial trials. The chapter is written for graduate students and process engineers considering freeze-concentration as an alternative to vacuum evaporation for heat-sensitive products.

title: Comparative CFD and experimental study of flow patterns in pilot-scale lactic acid bioreactors
abstract: Computational fluid dynamics simulations using the k–ε turbulence model were carried out for a 50 L stirred-tank bioreactor equipped with a PBT impeller and four baffles, and compared with experimental particle image velocimetry (PIV) data collected at three horizontal planes. Simulated radial velocity profiles agreed with PIV measurements within 8–14% relative error across the range 150–450 rpm. Dead-zone volume fraction, defined as regions with local velocity below 5% of tip speed, was 6.2% at 150 rpm and decreased to 1.8% at 350 rpm. Simulated mixing times matched tracer-based experimental values with a mean absolute deviation of 3.1 s over 12 test conditions. The validated model was used to predict flow fields at 150 L scale prior to physical construction of the vessel, identifying an unfavourable recirculation zone near the bottom head that was eliminated by shifting the impeller clearance from D/3 to D/4.

title: Mechanical recycling of starch–protein extruded packaging: changes in rheology and film properties over five extrusion cycles
abstract: The reprocessability of corn starch–pea protein (80:20) extruded sheets was evaluated by subjecting granulated extrudate to five consecutive extrusion cycles under identical processing conditions (145 °C, 150 rpm, 24 wt% moisture). After each cycle, in-line viscosity, tensile properties of compression-moulded films, DSC gelatinisation degree, and molecular weight distribution by gel permeation chromatography were measured. Melt viscosity at 100 s⁻¹ decreased monotonically from 2 900 Pa·s (cycle 1) to 1 750 Pa·s (cycle 5), indicating progressive chain degradation. GPC showed reduction of weight-average molecular weight from 2.1 × 10⁶ to 1.3 × 10⁶ g/mol over five cycles. Tensile strength decreased from 14.2 to 9.8 MPa and elongation at break from 33 to 19%. Colour darkening (ΔE* = 6.2 after cycle 5 versus cycle 1) was attributed to Maillard-type reactions. Gelatinisation degree remained above 94% throughout, indicating structural conversion was maintained. The data suggest that at most two reprocessing cycles are acceptable before mechanical property degradation becomes significant for packaging applications.

title: Uticaj poluprechnika horizontalne krivine na operativne brzine putničkih vozila na dvotračnim putevima van naselja u Srbiji
abstract: Istraživanje analizira vezu između poluprechnika horizontalne krivine i izmerenih operativnih brzina (V85) na dvotračnim ruralnim putevima u Vojvodini. Terenska merenja sprovedena su na 34 horizontalne krivine sa poluprechnicima u rasponu od 90 m do 780 m, korišćenjem pneumatskih cevnih brojača i laser-brzinomera. Ukupno je prikupljeno više od 18 000 individualnih merenja brzina za laka motorna vozila u slobodnom saobraćajnom toku, pri suvom kolovozu i dnevnoj vidljivosti. Rezultati pokazuju statistički značajnu logaritamsku vezu između poluprechnika i V85, sa koeficijentom determinacije R² = 0,81. Razvijena je regresiona jednačina prilagođena lokalnim uslovima puta, koja se razlikuje od nemačkih i španskih modela iz literature zbog specifičnih karakteristika mreže regionalnih puteva u Srbiji. Nalaze je moguće primeniti u fazi projektne provjere konzistentnosti brzine prema kriterijumima koji se koriste u revizijama bezbednosti puteva.

title: Operating Speed Prediction on Two-Lane Rural Highways: Comparison of Regression and Artificial Neural Network Models
abstract: This paper compares the predictive accuracy of multiple linear regression and feed-forward artificial neural network (ANN) models for estimating the 85th-percentile operating speed (V85) on two-lane rural highways in northern Serbia. Input variables included horizontal curve radius, curve length, tangent length preceding the curve, posted speed limit, and annual average daily traffic (AADT). Field data were collected at 47 sites across three regional road corridors during 2014 and 2015, yielding 24 600 individual speed observations under free-flow, dry-pavement conditions. The ANN model with one hidden layer of eight neurons achieved a mean absolute error of 3.1 km/h and R² = 0.87 on a held-out test set, outperforming the best regression model (R² = 0.79, MAE = 4.3 km/h). Sensitivity analysis indicated that horizontal curve radius and preceding tangent length were the two most influential predictors in both modelling approaches. Practical implications for the application of speed-profile consistency checks during geometric design audits are discussed.

title: Naturalističko prikupljanje podataka o brzinama vozača pomoću GPS uređaja na ruralnoj putnoj mreži – metodološka razmatranja
abstract: Rad opisuje metodologiju terenskog istraživanja zasnovanu na naturalističkom praćenju brzina individualnih vozača pomoću GPS data-logera postavljenih u 42 privatna vozila koja su učestvovala u istraživanju tokom perioda od šest meseci na putevima Južnobačkog okruga. Ukupno je zabeleženo 1 240 prolazaka kroz instrumented deonice sa horizontalnim krivinama. Analiza obuhvata poređenje V85 vrednosti dobijenih naturalističkim posmatranjem sa vrednostima iz konvencionalnih spot-merenja na istim lokacijama. Razlike između metoda kreću se u rasponu od −2,4 do +5,8 km/h, pri čemu su naturalistički podaci konzistentno pokazali nešto niže V85 vrednosti na krivinama manjeg poluprechnika. Rad identifikuje ograničenja uzorkovanja uzrokovana selektivnošću vozačkog panela i predlaže korekcione faktore. Rezultati potvrđuju primenljivost GPS-baziranog naturalističkog pristupa za profilisanje operativnih brzina, ali ukazuju na potrebu pažljivog odabira učesnika i dužeg perioda praćenja.

title: Geometric Design Consistency of Horizontal Curves on Two-Lane Rural Roads: Application of Operating Speed Difference Criteria
abstract: Design consistency along two-lane rural roads is commonly evaluated using differences in operating speed between successive geometric elements (ΔV85). This study applies two widely referenced threshold criteria (ΔV85 ≥ 10 km/h for poor consistency; ΔV85 ≥ 20 km/h for very poor consistency) to a corridor of 68 km of regional road in the Fruška Gora foothill area of Serbia. Operating speed profiles were constructed from field-measured V85 values at 52 curve and tangent sections. Of the 61 curve–tangent transitions examined, 26% were classified as poor consistency and 11% as very poor consistency. Sections with very poor consistency ratings showed a statistically higher frequency of reported injury accidents over a five-year observation period (OR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.4–5.6), after controlling for AADT and road width. The analysis highlights specific alignment sections where geometric redesign or speed management measures should be prioritised.

abstract: Roadside environment characteristics such as tree density, embankment height, and the presence of roadside obstacles are known to influence perceived risk and speed selection at horizontal curves. This study uses video footage from dashboard cameras installed in instrumented vehicles during naturalistic driving sessions on 18 horizontal curves in rural Serbia, combined with simultaneously recorded GPS speed data, to examine whether roadside opennes affects V85 and speed reduction through the curve. For each curve, roadside enclosure was quantified using a lateral clearance index measured from aerial imagery. Statistical analysis using mixed-effects models, with driver and curve as random effects (n = 1 080 traversals), showed that an increase in the lateral clearance index from 0 to 1 was associated with a 4.7 km/h increase in mid-curve speed (95% CI: 3.1–6.3 km/h), independently of curve radius and tangent length. The findings suggest that roadside management and planting design are relevant considerations in the safety assessment of rural road alignments.

title: Speed Profile Continuity at Successive Horizontal Curves: Field Evidence from a Hilly Terrain Corridor in Serbia
abstract: Speed carryover between successive horizontal curves—where a driver's exit speed from one curve becomes the approach speed for the next—can substantially affect the magnitude of ΔV85 values used in consistency evaluation. This paper quantifies carryover effects on a 34 km hilly-terrain corridor in central Serbia containing 38 horizontal curves, using speed measurements at curve entry, apex, and exit points collected with inductive-loop detectors and supplemented with 620 instrumented-vehicle traversals. Results show that when the inter-curve tangent is shorter than 300 m, the approach speed at the following curve is on average 6.9 km/h higher than the predicted tangent free-speed, inflating the apparent ΔV85 by a corresponding margin. A correction procedure is proposed for adjusting ΔV85 calculations when inter-curve tangent length falls below 300 m. Application of the correction reduced the number of curve transitions classified as poor consistency from 34% to 22% on the studied corridor.

title: Uticaj vremenskih uslova na operativne brzine u horizontalnim krivinama: analiza naturalističkih podataka sa ruralnih puteva u Vojvodini
abstract: Rad istražuje kako mokri kolovoz i smanjena vidljivost zbog kiše i magle utiču na V85 vrednosti izmerene u 24 horizontalne krivine na ruralnim putevima u Vojvodini. Podaci su prikupljani tokom 14 meseci korišćenjem kombinacije pneumatskih cevnih detektora i meteoroloških senzora postavljenih uz cestu, uz sinhronizovano beleženje vremenskih uslova. Ukupno je analizirano 61 400 individualnih prolazaka raspoređenih prema kategorijama vremenskih uslova: suvo, mokro, kiša, magla. Rezultati pokazuju statistički značajno smanjenje V85 za mokre uslove u poređenju sa suvim na krivinama sa poluprechnicima manjim od 200 m (prosečno smanjenje: 5,3 km/h), dok na krivinama većeg poluprechnika razlika nije statistički značajna. Modelovanje vremenskog faktora u profilima operativnih brzina može poboljšati tačnost sezonskih procena konzistentnosti i informisati upravljanje varijabilnim ograničenjima brzine.

title: Evaluating the Sensitivity of Design Consistency Outcomes to Operating Speed Model Choice on Two-Lane Rural Roads
abstract: Several operating speed prediction models published in the literature differ substantially in their functional form and calibration datasets. This study assesses how the choice of model affects the proportion of horizontal curve transitions classified as consistent, poor, or very poor on a common test corridor of 52 km in northern Serbia, using six models sourced from German, Spanish, Italian, and local Serbian research. Applying the six models to 67 curve–tangent transitions yielded poor-consistency rates ranging from 17% to 41% and very-poor-consistency rates from 6% to 19%, indicating that model choice can change consistency classifications at more than one in five transitions. The disparity is largest at curves with radii between 150 m and 350 m, where model predictions diverge most. Sensitivity of accident-prediction calibration to model choice is also quantified using a negative binomial regression framework with five years of police-reported accident data. Recommendations are given for the selection and local recalibration of operating speed models before their use in mandatory design consistency checks.

title: Extraction and characterisation of water-extractable arabinoxylan from buckwheat bran using sequential alkaline fractionation
abstract: Arabinoxylan (AX) fractions were isolated from hulled buckwheat bran by sequential water and alkaline extraction at pH 8, 10, and 12. Fractions were characterised by arabinose-to-xylose (A/X) ratios determined by HPAEC-PAD, molecular weight distributions via SEC-MALLS, and degree of ferulic acid esterification by alkaline saponification followed by HPLC-UV. Water-extractable AX accounted for 4.1 g per 100 g dry bran, with an A/X ratio of 0.62. Alkaline extraction at pH 12 yielded the highest total AX (9.8 g per 100 g dry bran) but reduced ferulic acid content by 38% relative to the pH 10 fraction. Molecular weight of the water-extractable fraction was 285 kDa. Gel-forming capacity, assessed by small-amplitude oscillatory rheology, was positively correlated with ferulic acid content (r = 0.84). Results indicate that pH 10 alkaline extraction represents the best compromise between yield and functional integrity for subsequent use in food formulations.

title: Effect of particle size reduction of buckwheat flour on the rheological properties of gluten-free dough
abstract: Buckwheat flour was milled to four particle size classes (d50 = 320, 220, 140, and 85 µm) by stone milling followed by air classification. Gluten-free dough formulations were prepared at 55% water absorption, and rheological properties were measured by small-amplitude oscillatory shear and creep-recovery tests. Reducing d50 from 320 to 85 µm increased storage modulus G' from 1,840 to 4,210 Pa at 1 Hz and reduced tan δ from 0.41 to 0.28, indicating greater elastic character. Extensibility measured by a Kieffer dough and gluten extensibility rig decreased by 24% at the finest fraction. Water absorption capacity of flour increased from 1.8 to 2.7 g water per g flour as particle size decreased. Specific loaf volume of baked breads followed a non-linear response, peaking at d50 = 140 µm (2.31 cm³ g⁻¹) and declining at 85 µm. Results confirm that fine milling improves dough cohesiveness at the cost of gas retention capacity.

title: In vitro fermentability of beta-glucan fractions from oat and amaranth flour by human faecal microbiota
abstract: Beta-glucan was isolated from oat flour (Avena sativa) and amaranth flour (Amaranthus hypochondriacus) by hot-water extraction and ethanol precipitation, yielding purity levels of 78% and 61% respectively as determined by the Megazyme mixed-linkage beta-glucan assay. Molecular weights were 2,340 kDa (oat) and 890 kDa (amaranth) by SEC-MALLS. In vitro fermentation was conducted using batch cultures inoculated with pooled faecal slurry from four healthy adult donors, pH-controlled at 6.7 for 48 h. Short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles were determined by GC-FID at 8, 24, and 48 h. Total SCFA production was 42.3 mmol L⁻¹ for oat beta-glucan and 31.8 mmol L⁻¹ for amaranth beta-glucan at 48 h. Acetate predominated in both systems, but the propionate fraction was proportionally higher for oat (28% vs. 19%). Neither fraction promoted Bifidobacterium counts significantly above the inulin-negative control at 24 h, suggesting limited prebiotic selectivity in this model.

title: Psyllium husk arabinoxylan as a structuring agent in quinoa-based gluten-free bread
abstract: The influence of psyllium husk powder (PHP) addition (1, 2, 3, and 4 g per 100 g flour) on the quality of quinoa flour gluten-free bread was investigated. Dough consistency was evaluated by the Mixolab and moisture content after baking was measured gravimetrically. Crumb texture was assessed by texture profile analysis (TPA) at 24 and 72 h post-baking. Adding 2 g PHP per 100 g flour increased specific loaf volume from 1.87 to 2.54 cm³ g⁻¹ and reduced hardness at 72 h from 18.4 N to 9.7 N. Water activity of crumb at 72 h was 0.923 compared to 0.901 in the control. Crumb porosity analysed by image analysis showed 31% increase in mean cell area at the 2 g level. The arabinoxylan content of PHP was confirmed at 67% by HPAEC-PAD analysis. Higher PHP levels (3–4 g) produced a gummy texture and reduced springiness. Sensory evaluation by a trained panel of 12 confirmed 2 g PHP as the preferred addition level.

title: Dietary fibre composition of selected pseudocereal flours available on the Serbian market
abstract: Commercial flours of buckwheat, quinoa, amaranth, and teff purchased from five Serbian retailers were characterised for total dietary fibre (TDF), soluble dietary fibre (SDF), and insoluble dietary fibre (IDF) using the AOAC 2009.01 enzymatic-gravimetric method. Beta-glucan was quantified by the Megazyme assay and arabinoxylan by HPAEC-PAD. TDF ranged from 6.3 g per 100 g (quinoa) to 11.8 g per 100 g (teff). Buckwheat showed the highest SDF content (2.9 g per 100 g). Beta-glucan was detectable only in oat-containing reference samples and at trace levels in amaranth (0.14 g per 100 g). Arabinoxylan levels in teff flour were the highest (2.7 g per 100 g). Considerable batch-to-batch variation was observed, with coefficients of variation up to 22% for arabinose and xylose residues. These data provide a baseline for formulating gluten-free products with defined fibre fractions and are relevant for regulatory fibre content labelling under Serbian food standards.

title: Modelling water redistribution in gluten-free crumb enriched with arabinoxylan during storage using low-field NMR
abstract: Gluten-free bread formulated from a 70:30 blend of rice and buckwheat flour with added water-extractable arabinoxylan (WEAX, 0.5 and 1.0 g per 100 g flour) was stored at 22°C for 96 h. Low-field 1H NMR transverse relaxation measurements (T2) were performed at 0, 24, 48, and 96 h to monitor proton populations in crumb. Three T2 populations were resolved by non-negative least-squares fitting: tightly bound water (T2a ~ 1–5 ms), plasticised biopolymer water (T2b ~ 20–80 ms), and free water (T2c > 100 ms). Relative population of T2b decreased by 31% in the control over 96 h but only by 14% in the 1.0 g WEAX sample, indicating retardation of water migration. Firmness increase correlated with the decline of T2b (r = 0.91). Staling enthalpy, measured by DSC at 96 h, was reduced from 1.8 J g⁻¹ in the control to 1.1 J g⁻¹ in the 1.0 g WEAX treatment. Results suggest WEAX interacts with starch and prolongs crumb softness by limiting water redistribution during staling.

title: Influence of sourdough fermentation with selected lactic acid bacteria on arabinoxylan solubilisation in buckwheat–amaranth gluten-free bread
abstract: Three homofermentative lactic acid bacteria strains (Lactiplantibacillus vegetus NS-4, Levilactobacillus brevoides NS-7, and Ligilactobacillus alimentarius NS-11) isolated from traditional Serbian fermented grain products were used to prepare sourdoughs from 50:50 buckwheat–amaranth flour blends at 28°C for 16 h. AX solubilisation was quantified by HPAEC-PAD before and after fermentation. NS-7 produced the highest increase in water-extractable AX (+2.1 g per 100 g flour dry weight) associated with feruloyl esterase activity measured at 0.42 U mg⁻¹ protein. Bread produced with NS-7 sourdough had 12% higher specific volume, 21% lower hardness at 48 h, and a crumb with 9% greater mean cell area than the chemical leavening control. In vitro fermentation of AX-enriched crumb hydrolysate showed a 17% increase in total SCFA production relative to the control hydrolysate. The results indicate that selection of esterase-active LAB strains can simultaneously improve technological quality and potential gut health attributes of pseudocereal gluten-free bread.

title: Fermentation kinetics of mixed arabinoxylan and beta-glucan substrates: synergistic or additive effects on microbiota?
abstract: Mixed substrates consisting of water-extractable arabinoxylan (WEAX) from buckwheat and oat beta-glucan (OBG) were prepared at three mass ratios (WEAX:OBG = 3:1, 1:1, 1:3) and compared to single-substrate and inulin controls in a 48 h pH-stat batch fermentation system (n = 4 donors). Total SCFA, acetate, propionate, butyrate, and lactate were measured at 4, 8, 24, and 48 h by GC-FID and HPLC, respectively. Microbial diversity was assessed by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (V3–V4 region) at 0 and 24 h. Total SCFA in the 1:1 mixture (57.4 mmol L⁻¹) exceeded the additive prediction based on individual substrate values (49.1 mmol L⁻¹), a difference significant at p < 0.05. Butyrate proportion was highest in the 1:3 ratio (22% of total SCFA). Shannon diversity index at 24 h was higher for the 1:1 mixture (3.41) than for either single substrate. The finding supports the hypothesis that combining structurally distinct fibres from different pseudocereal sources may provide broader microbiota stimulation than single-fibre supplements.

title: Arabinoxylan fermentation profiles across six healthy adult donors: inter-individual variability and its implications for assessing prebiotic potential
abstract: Inter-individual variability in colonic fermentation response to water-unextractable arabinoxylan (WUAX) from buckwheat and teff was assessed using a pH-controlled in vitro batch model inoculated with individual faecal slurries from six healthy adults (three male, three female; age 26–44 years; no dietary fibre supplement use). SCFA profiles at 24 h showed coefficients of variation of 38–51% across donors for total SCFA, with butyrate showing the largest variation (CV = 58%). Cluster analysis of donor SCFA profiles identified two distinct responder groups: high-butyrate producers (n = 3, mean butyrate proportion 26%) and low-butyrate producers (n = 3, mean 11%). High-butyrate producers had higher baseline Roseburia and Eubacterium populations as identified by qPCR. Teff WUAX fermentation produced consistently higher butyrate proportions than buckwheat WUAX regardless of donor group. These data suggest that using pooled donor inocula, a common simplification in prebiotic screening, may mask clinically relevant variation and produce substrate rankings that differ substantially from individual-donor data.

title: Structural features of arabinoxylan from Vojvodina-grown amaranth and their relation to fermentability
abstract: Amaranth (Amaranthus cruentus) cultivated at two sites in the Vojvodina region was harvested at physiological maturity, and flour was produced by disc milling. Water-extractable arabinoxylan was isolated and characterised by methylation analysis, 1H and 13C NMR, and enzyme fingerprinting using GH10 and GH11 endoxylanases combined with MALDI-TOF-MS of the resulting oligosaccharide fragments. A/X ratio was 0.48–0.52 with 43% of xylose residues doubly substituted at O-2 and O-3. Degree of polymerisation of the main chain estimated by SEC was 920 (Mn). In vitro fermentation (pH-stat, 24 h, four donors) showed a 24 h lag phase before SCFA production, contrasting with the 4 h lag observed for teff AX of similar molecular weight. Enzyme fingerprinting suggested that double substitution density, not MW alone, reduces fermentation rate by limiting endo-xylanase cleavage accessibility. Butyrate proportion at 48 h was 18% of total SCFA, lower than teff AX (24%). Fine structural features are therefore a better predictor of fermentability than bulk MW measurements.
