title: Combined effect of sourdough fermentation and psyllium arabinoxylan addition on crumb microstructure and in vitro fibre fermentability of buckwheat bread
abstract: Buckwheat flour bread was prepared under four conditions: straight-dough with no fibre addition (control), straight-dough with 2 g psyllium AX per 100 g flour, sourdough (Lactiplantibacillus vegetus NS-4) with no added fibre, and sourdough with 2 g psyllium AX. Crumb microstructure was evaluated by confocal laser scanning microscopy after staining with Calcofluor White for fibre and Congo Red for starch. Fermentability of fibre hydrolysates recovered from simulated gastric and pancreatic digestion was assessed by pH-stat batch fermentation (48 h, n = 3 donors). Sourdough combined with psyllium AX produced the finest gas cell distribution (mean cell diameter 0.92 mm, porosity 68%) and the highest SCFA at 24 h (51.3 mmol L⁻¹) relative to all other conditions. Sourdough alone increased AX solubilisation by 1.8 g per 100 g flour dry weight without added psyllium. Combination of fermentation and added AX produced a butyrate proportion of 23% at 24 h, significantly above the straight-dough control (14%). The two interventions appear to act additively on fibre accessibility for colonic bacteria.

title: Prediction of short-chain fatty acid yield from pseudocereal arabinoxylan substrates using near-infrared spectroscopy combined with partial least squares regression
abstract: A rapid prediction model for 24 h total SCFA yield in in vitro colonic fermentation was developed using diffuse reflectance NIR spectra of 38 arabinoxylan preparations from buckwheat, amaranth, and teff processed under varying extraction and drying conditions. Reference SCFA values were obtained by GC-FID after pH-stat batch fermentation with a standard four-donor pooled inoculum. Spectra were collected at 1000–2500 nm with a resolution of 4 cm⁻¹. Partial least squares regression models were built and cross-validated using leave-one-out procedures. The best model (four latent variables) explained 88% of variance in calibration and showed RMSECV of 3.8 mmol L⁻¹ against total SCFA values ranging from 22 to 61 mmol L⁻¹. Important spectral regions were identified at 1450, 1930, and 2100 nm, associated with water, hydroxyl, and C–O–C stretching. The model was validated on an external set of 10 preparations (R²ext = 0.83). The approach could offer a non-destructive screening tool for fibre preparations before full fermentation assays, reducing the burden of the multi-day fermentation protocol.

title: Glycaemic response and arabinoxylan molecular weight in quinoa–teff gluten-free bread: a combined in vitro starch digestion and colonic fermentation study
abstract: Gluten-free breads were prepared from quinoa–teff flour blends (60:40) supplemented with WEAX fractions of three molecular weight classes (low: 85 kDa, medium: 320 kDa, high: 810 kDa) at 1 g per 100 g flour. In vitro starch digestion was performed by the Englyst method to estimate rapidly available glucose (RAG) and slowly available glucose (SAG) indices. The residue from digestion was subsequently used as substrate in pH-stat batch fermentation (24 h, n = 4 donors). High-MW AX reduced RAG from 61% (control) to 48% and increased SAG from 22% to 31% of total starch, consistent with viscosity-mediated diffusion restriction; low-MW AX had no significant effect on digestion kinetics (p = 0.18). In the fermentation phase, low-MW AX produced significantly higher total SCFA (46.1 mmol L⁻¹) than high-MW AX (33.4 mmol L⁻¹), as high-MW fractions remained partially entrapped in the digestion residue matrix and were less accessible. These findings suggest an intrinsic trade-off between glycaemic modulation and colonic fermentability when selecting WEAX fractions for gluten-free bread enrichment.

title: Determinants of Non-Performing Loans in Serbian Commercial Banks: A Panel Data Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the macro-financial and bank-level drivers of non-performing loan (NPL) ratios across twelve Serbian commercial banks over the period 2004–2012. Using a balanced panel fixed-effects model, the study decomposes NPL variation into a systematic component—captured by GDP growth, unemployment, and the real exchange rate—and a bank-specific component reflecting capitalization, loan growth, and return on assets. Hausman test results support the fixed-effects specification. Estimation yields a statistically significant negative relationship between GDP growth and NPLs (coefficient −0.41, p < 0.01) and a positive relationship with unemployment (coefficient 0.28, p < 0.05). Bank-level capitalization shows a significant negative association, consistent with moral hazard arguments. The systematic macro-financial factors account for approximately 58% of total NPL variance, with the remainder attributed to idiosyncratic bank behavior. Robustness checks using random effects and Prais–Winsten corrections for serial correlation confirm the core findings. Results provide actionable benchmarks for stress-testing exercises under National Bank of Serbia supervisory guidelines.

title: Systematic versus Idiosyncratic Credit Risk: Evidence from a Central European Corporate Loan Dataset
abstract: The paper applies a two-way error component panel model to a dataset of 1,840 corporate borrowers drawn from Czech, Hungarian, and Serbian bank records over 2006–2013. The goal is to quantify how much of the cross-sectional variation in one-year default probabilities is driven by common macro-financial shocks versus firm-level heterogeneity. Macro-financial regressors include short-term interest rates, credit-to-GDP gaps, and industrial production indices; firm-level controls include leverage, interest coverage, and firm size. A variance decomposition exercise shows that common factors explain 43–52% of default rate variance depending on the country subsample, with the Serbian subsample exhibiting the highest idiosyncratic share (57%). The finding suggests that microprudential monitoring of individual borrower quality is at least as important as macroprudential oversight for the region. Estimation is conducted in Stata using the Mundlak correction to address potential correlation between regressors and unobserved firm effects.

title: Stress Testing Retail Mortgage Portfolios Under Adverse Macro Scenarios: A Factor-Augmented Panel Approach
abstract: This study develops a stress-testing framework for retail mortgage default rates using a factor-augmented panel data model estimated on quarterly data from three Serbian banks, covering 2008–2015. Two common factors are extracted via principal component analysis from a set of fourteen macro-financial variables, including house price indices, disposable income, unemployment rates, and the EUR/RSD exchange rate. These factors are then embedded into a panel probit model to generate conditional default probabilities under baseline, adverse, and severely adverse macro scenarios calibrated to match historical downturn periods. Under the severely adverse scenario—a 4.2 percentage point rise in unemployment combined with a 15% nominal exchange rate depreciation—the aggregate mortgage default rate is projected to increase by 3.1 percentage points relative to baseline over an eight-quarter horizon. The framework is computationally tractable and aligned with European Banking Authority stress-testing methodology, making it applicable to smaller banks with limited internal modeling capacity.
venue: South-East European Journal of Finance and Accounting

title: Does Loan Officer Discretion Contribute to Idiosyncratic Default Risk? Micro-Level Evidence from a Serbian Savings Bank
abstract: Using a proprietary dataset of 6,200 consumer loans originated between 2011 and 2016 at a single mid-sized Serbian savings institution, this paper tests whether residual default risk—after controlling for observable borrower financials—is systematically related to the identity of the originating loan officer. A multilevel logistic regression model with loan officers treated as a random intercept reveals statistically significant officer-level heterogeneity in default outcomes (LR test χ² = 18.4, p < 0.001), accounting for approximately 9% of total residual variance. Officers with longer tenure show lower unexplained default rates, pointing to the role of informal borrower information gathered through repeated interactions. The result survives inclusion of branch fixed effects and controls for loan vintage and product type. The findings have implications for internal risk models: idiosyncratic risk is not fully captured by hard financial information and retains a human-judgment component that standard scoring models systematically ignore.

title: Decomposing the Rise in Non-Performing Loans During the COVID-19 Shock: Systematic and Idiosyncratic Drivers in Serbian Banking
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic produced a sharp but heterogeneous increase in non-performing loan ratios across Serbian commercial banks between 2019 Q4 and 2021 Q2. This paper applies a structural factor model to monthly bank-level balance sheet data combined with aggregate macro-financial indicators to decompose observed NPL movements. A two-stage estimation procedure is used: in the first stage, common factors are identified via dynamic factor analysis; in the second stage, idiosyncratic residuals are regressed on bank-specific variables including pre-crisis capital adequacy ratios and industry concentration of loan books. Results indicate that approximately 64% of the NPL increase is attributable to common macro-financial distress, with the remainder driven by bank heterogeneity. Banks with higher pre-crisis exposure to tourism and hospitality sectors exhibit significantly larger idiosyncratic NPL increases. The paper provides quantitative guidance for post-pandemic provisioning requirements and discusses interactions with government loan moratoria.

title: Panel Regression Approaches to Credit Risk Modeling in Transition Economies: A Methodological Survey
abstract: This book chapter surveys the econometric methods used to model credit default risk in Central and South-Eastern European transition economies from the mid-1990s through 2020. The chapter organizes the literature around three generations of panel approaches: static fixed- and random-effects models of NPL ratios, dynamic GMM specifications addressing default persistence, and factor-augmented models that integrate macro-financial common shocks. For each generation, the chapter discusses identification challenges, data requirements, and reported effect sizes, drawing on over eighty empirical studies. A comparative table presents variance decomposition results from sixteen studies, showing that the systematic share of default variation ranges from 38% to 71% depending on portfolio type and country context. The chapter also documents a gap in the literature regarding household credit portfolios and micro-enterprise lending, and outlines estimation strategies suitable for researchers working with small regional bank datasets characteristic of the Western Balkans context.

title: Interest Rate Pass-Through Heterogeneity and Borrower Default Risk: Evidence from Serbian Corporate Loan Data
abstract: Central bank policy rate changes do not translate uniformly into lending rates across bank–borrower relationships, and this heterogeneity may influence borrower default risk. This paper uses a matched loan-level panel dataset of 2,870 Serbian corporate loans observed quarterly from 2015 to 2022 to estimate how incomplete interest rate pass-through interacts with borrower-level financial fragility. A panel IV regression strategy instruments lending rate changes with the euro area policy rate, exploiting variation in bank funding structures to isolate exogenous pass-through variation. Firms receiving higher-than-average rate increases show a 2.3 percentage point higher annual default probability, with the effect concentrated among firms already in the third leverage quartile. Idiosyncratic components—measured as residuals from a cross-sectional factor model—are significantly amplified by high pass-through, suggesting that macro-financial policy shocks interact with firm-level vulnerability rather than simply adding to it.

title: Borrower-Level Stress Testing for Small Banks: A Simplified Factor Model with Macro Scenario Integration
abstract: Large-scale stress-testing infrastructures developed by the European Banking Authority are computationally and data-intensive, placing them out of reach for most smaller regional banks in South-Eastern Europe. This paper proposes a simplified borrower-level stress-testing methodology grounded in a one-factor Gaussian copula model augmented with an observable macro-financial index. The approach requires only standard loan-level data—probability of default estimates, exposure at default, and a sectoral classification—combined with publicly available macro forecasts. The framework is calibrated using data from two Serbian banks and validated against realized NPL outcomes over 2017–2023. Under a simulated recession scenario comparable to 2012, aggregate expected credit loss increases by 34% relative to baseline, with the construction and retail trade sectors accounting for 61% of incremental losses. The methodology is documented in sufficient detail to allow implementation in spreadsheet environments, making it accessible to compliance teams at smaller institutions without dedicated quantitative modeling staff.

title: Separating Macro and Micro Default Drivers in Retail Lending: A Latent Factor Approach Using Monthly Administrative Data
abstract: This preprint presents a latent factor decomposition of monthly retail loan default rates sourced from the Serbian Credit Bureau covering 2.1 million individual borrower records from 2018 to 2025. A dynamic latent factor model is estimated using the Kalman filter, extracting one common macro-financial factor and allowing for sector-specific loadings across five retail loan categories: personal unsecured, auto, credit card, overdraft, and mortgage. The idiosyncratic component for each category is then regressed on observable borrower-level characteristics available in the credit registry, including credit score at origination, debt-service-to-income ratio, and employment sector. The macro factor explains between 29% (credit card) and 54% (mortgage) of month-to-month default rate variation, while borrower-level observables account for 31–44% of idiosyncratic variance. Residual unexplained idiosyncratic variance is largest for overdraft facilities, suggesting that behavioral factors not captured in standard registry data play a material role. Full replication code in R is provided as supplementary material.

title: Uticaj kratkolančanih kationskih peptidnih derivata na formiranje biofilma Acinetobacter baumannii kliničkih izolata
abstract: Studija je ispitivala antibiofilm aktivnost serije od osam kratkolančanih kationskih peptidnih derivata (KCKP-01 do KCKP-08) sintetisanih modifikacijom lizin-leucinskog kostura, prema dvadeset i četiri klinička izolata Acinetobacter baumannii prikupljena iz jedinica intenzivne nege Kliničkog centra Vojvodine u periodu 2018–2019. Minimalne biofilm-inhibitorne koncentracije (MBIC50 i MBIC90) određene su metodom mikrodilucionog bujonskog testa u kombinaciji sa XTT-redukcionim testom za procenu vijabilnosti biofilma. Šest od osam ispitivanih jedinjenja pokazalo je MBIC50 vrednosti ispod 32 μg/mL prema svim izolatima, pri čemu je derivat KCKP-05 postigao MBIC90 od 16 μg/mL prema 19 od 24 izolata. Konfokalna laserska skening-mikroskopija sa SYTO-9/propidijum-jodidom potvrdila je dezintegraciju biofilm strukture pri subinhibitornim koncentracijama KCKP-05. Hemolizni test na eritrocitima humanog porekla pokazao je hemolizu manju od 5% za koncentracije do 128 μg/mL za pet vodećih jedinjenja. Rezultati ukazuju da modifikacije hidrofobone regije peptidnog molekula značajno utiču na antibiofilm selektivnost bez izrazite citotoksičnosti.

title: Sinteza i karakterizacija dikloro-supstituisanih benzimidazolnih peptidnih konjugata sa potencijalnom antibiofilm aktivnošću
abstract: Opisana je sinteza šest novih peptidnih konjugata u kojima je standardni N-terminalni alaninski ostatak zaменjen dikloro-supstituisanim benzimidazolskim fragmentom. Jedinjenja su pripremljena primenom Fmoc čvrste faze sinteze na Rink amidnoj smoli, a čistoća i strukturna potvrda izvršeni su metodama RP-HPLC i ESI-MS spektrometrije. Antibiofilm aktivnost ispitana je prema referentnom soju A. baumannii ATCC 19606 i prema pet kliničkih XDR izolata. Derivat BIZ-04 pokazao je najnižu MBIC50 vrednost od 8 μg/mL prema referentnom soju i 12–24 μg/mL prema kliničkim izolatima. Raman spektroskopija biofilmske mase pre i posle tretmana BIZ-04 ukazala je na smanjenje intenziteta traka karakterističnih za ekstracelularnu polisaharidnu matricu za 61 ± 7% u poređenju sa netretiranom kontrolom. Toksičnost prema HEK-293 ćelijama određena MTT testom bila je zanemarljiva do koncentracije od 64 μg/mL. Rezultati sugerišu da uvođenje halogenovanog heterocikličnog sistema poboljšava penetraciju kroz biofilm matricu.

title: In vitro model of catheter-associated biofilm: comparative evaluation of polypropylene and silicone surfaces for A. baumannii attachment and maturation
abstract: Catheter material properties significantly affect biofilm architecture and drug susceptibility. This study compared A. baumannii biofilm formation on polypropylene (PP) and medical-grade silicone (SI) catheter segments using quantitative colony counts, crystal violet staining, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) at 6 h, 24 h, and 72 h time points. Three reference strains (ATCC 19606, DSM 30007, and one in-house XDR clinical isolate) were studied at standardised inocula of 1×10⁶ CFU/mL. Crystal violet measurements showed that SI surfaces supported significantly greater biomass accumulation at 72 h (OD595 1.42 ± 0.11 vs. 0.89 ± 0.08 for PP; p < 0.01 by two-way ANOVA). SEM images revealed denser exopolysaccharide networks on SI for all three strains. Subsequent MBIC testing with KCKP-05 on mature 72-hour biofilms showed 2- to 4-fold higher MBIC50 values on SI relative to PP, underscoring the importance of surface material in preclinical antibiofilm assessments. The data advocate for surface-specific testing protocols in standardisation efforts.

title: Osnovna farmakološka pismenost studenata medicine prve godine: pilot istraživanje na uzorku iz Novog Sada
abstract: Sprovedena je poprečna (cross-sectional) studija na uzorku od 214 studenata prve godine Medicinskog fakulteta u Novom Sadu u akademskoj 2019/2020. godini sa ciljem procene ulaznog znanja iz farmakologije i stava prema antimikrobnoj rezistenciji. Korišćen je anonimni upitnik od 32 pitanja, validiran u prethodnim studijama na uzorcima sa Medicinskog fakulteta u Beogradu i prilagođen lokalnom kontekstu. Prosečan skup tačnih odgovora bio je 41,2 ± 9,7%. Svega 18,7% ispitanika tačno je odgovorilo na pitanja vezana za mehanizme rezistencije, dok je 61,4% iskazalo visoko samopouzdanje u procenu sopstvenog znanja. Utvrđena je statistički značajna pozitivna korelacija između prethodnog pohađanja nastave biologije u okviru srednje stručne medicinske škole i ukupnog skora (r = 0.38, p < 0.001). Nalazi ukazuju na potrebu za unapređenjem propedevtičkih sadržaja iz farmakologije i mikrobiologije pre početka kliničkih predmeta.

title: Automated COSY-based connectivity graph construction for molecular fragments up to ten heavy atoms
abstract: Extraction of connectivity information from two-dimensional COSY spectra is a prerequisite for computer-assisted structure elucidation but remains sensitive to noise and overlap in the aliphatic region. We describe an algorithm that converts a digitised COSY matrix into a weighted connectivity graph by applying adaptive threshold selection based on row-by-row signal-to-noise estimation. Fragment assembly is then performed with a depth-first search that respects valence constraints derived from molecular formula input. The procedure was benchmarked on 145 organic compounds with molecular weights between 120 and 350 Da, drawn from teaching collections and commercial standard libraries. Complete correct connectivity was recovered for 81% of compounds without manual intervention; a further 14% required selection among two or three candidate graphs. Processing time per spectrum was under four seconds on hardware available in 2005. The implementation was integrated into the SPECINT-1 platform and tested jointly with the University of Belgrade analytical chemistry group.

title: Mass spectral fragmentation trees for terpenoid skeletons: a database-guided approach
abstract: Terpenoids produce complex electron-ionisation mass spectra whose interpretation benefits from skeleton-specific fragmentation libraries rather than generic rules. We assembled a reference database of EI-MS spectra for 204 monoterpenes, sesquiterpenes, and diterpenes obtained from authenticated botanical extracts and commercial standards, recording spectra at 70 eV on a quadrupole instrument. For each compound, dominant fragmentation pathways were annotated manually and then used to train a decision-tree classifier operating on m/z ratios and relative intensities of the ten most abundant ions. Leave-one-out cross-validation gave correct skeleton-class assignment in 87% of cases. The database and classifier were made available as a downloadable module for the open-source spectral workbench ChemParse. A smaller validation set of 31 unknowns from essential-oil analysis confirmed an identification rate of 74% without retention-index information, rising to 91% when retention index was included as an additional feature.

title: Comparison of ¹³C shift prediction methods for nitrogen-containing heterocycles in a 600-compound benchmark
abstract: Accurate ¹³C chemical shift prediction for heterocyclic systems is essential for computational structure verification in pharmaceutical contexts. We assembled a benchmark set of 600 nitrogen heterocycles—pyridines, pyrimidines, indoles, quinolines, and related bicyclic systems—with experimental ¹³C shifts recorded in DMSO-d₆ and CDCl₃ from published spectra and in-house measurements. Four publicly accessible prediction methods were evaluated: two increment-based approaches, one neural network predictor, and one quantum-chemical method using DFT/B3LYP/6-31G* with GIAO formalism. The DFT approach gave the lowest overall RMSE of 2.1 ppm but required computation times two to three orders of magnitude longer than the empirical tools. A neural network predictor trained primarily on carbocyclic compounds showed systematic errors exceeding 5 ppm for carbon atoms directly bonded to ring nitrogen. The results argue for heterocycle-specific training sets and provide a publicly archived benchmark for future method development.

title: SPECINT-2: an open-architecture platform for integrated NMR and MS structure verification
abstract: We describe the second major version of the SPECINT software platform, which integrates ¹H, ¹³C, COSY, HSQC, and HMBC processing with EI and ESI mass spectral interpretation under a single workflow engine. The architecture separates spectral parsing, feature extraction, candidate generation, and scoring into discrete modules communicating through a JSON-based internal protocol, enabling independent replacement of individual components. Candidate structures are generated by fragment assembly from 2D NMR constraints and ranked by a composite scoring function combining predicted versus observed shift deviations, mass spectral match factors, and molecular formula consistency. Benchmarking on 320 synthetic intermediates provided by two university synthetic chemistry groups showed that the top-ranked candidate was correct in 76% of cases and appeared in the top three in 91%. The platform is distributed under an open-source licence and supports spectral data import from five common instrument vendor formats.

title: Dereplication of flavonoid glycosides in plant extracts using LC-MS/MS fragmentation libraries
abstract: Flavonoid glycosides generate characteristic neutral-loss and product-ion patterns in collision-induced dissociation that can be exploited for rapid dereplication without pure reference standards. We constructed an in-house MS/MS library of 88 flavonoid glycosides—including flavones, flavonols, and isoflavones bearing mono- and di-glycosidic substituents—using authenticated reference material and published spectra. A hierarchical scoring scheme first assigns the aglycone class from diagnostic product ions and then identifies the glycan portion from neutral-loss series. The method was applied to methanolic extracts of twelve Balkan medicinal plant species, tentatively identifying 143 glycoside signals; 37 were confirmed by co-injection of available standards. The library and scoring algorithm are packaged as a plugin for the ChemParse workbench. Processing time for a 30-minute LC-MS/MS run of 1400 spectra was approximately 90 seconds on a standard laptop.

title: Chemoinformatics approaches to structure elucidation: a chapter on spectral data integration
abstract: This book chapter reviews computational strategies for combining heterogeneous spectroscopic data—primarily NMR and mass spectrometry—into unified structure proposals for organic molecules with molecular weights below 600 Da. The discussion covers the evolution from rule-based expert systems of the 1980s through constraint-satisfaction graph algorithms to contemporary machine-learning approaches, with emphasis on the information content of each spectral technique and the practical difficulties of data fusion. Particular attention is given to the treatment of spectral ambiguity, overlap, and incomplete data, which remain the main obstacles to fully automated elucidation. Case studies drawn from natural product and pharmaceutical contexts illustrate the current state of the art and identify open problems including stereochemical determination and handling of complex mixtures. The chapter is intended for postgraduate students and researchers entering the field.

title: Evaluation of molecular formula generation from high-resolution ESI-MS data: effect of adduct type and mass accuracy on false positive rates
abstract: Molecular formula assignment from accurate mass measurements is routinely performed in metabolomics and natural product research, but false positive rates are rarely reported systematically. We evaluated three publicly available formula generators using a test set of 520 compounds with masses between 150 and 800 Da, simulating ESI data with [M+H]⁺, [M+Na]⁺, [M+NH₄]⁺, and [M–H]⁻ adducts at mass accuracies of 1, 2, and 5 ppm. At 1 ppm, the number of formula candidates per spectrum ranged from 1 to 14 with a median of 3; at 5 ppm the median rose to 11. Including nitrogen and oxygen element limits derived from the compound's drug-likeness class reduced the candidate list by 40% on average without excluding the correct formula in any test case. The study provides practical guidance for instrument calibration requirements and post-processing filter settings in untargeted metabolomics workflows.

title: Graph-neural-network prediction of HSQC cross-peak patterns from molecular structure
abstract: HSQC spectra provide direct one-bond C–H correlations whose predicted appearance can be compared against experimental data for rapid structure verification. We trained a graph neural network (GNN) on 4100 ¹H–¹³C HSQC datasets compiled from open spectral archives and in-house measurements, representing the molecular structure as a typed atom–bond graph with three-hop neighbourhood features. The model predicts both ¹H and ¹³C shifts simultaneously through a dual-output architecture with shared graph-convolutional layers. On a held-out test set of 420 compounds, median absolute errors were 0.09 ppm for ¹H and 1.8 ppm for ¹³C, comparable to or better than ensemble increment methods on the same set. The predicted cross-peak patterns were used within the SPECINT-2 scoring engine in place of tabular incremental predictions, improving top-1 structure identification rate from 76% to 82% on a 150-compound validation batch.

title: Automated detection of spectral artifacts in routine ¹H NMR quality-control workflows for pharmaceutical intermediates
abstract: Spectral artifacts—solvent residual peaks, spinning sidebands, and baseline distortions—frequently interfere with automated integration and shift-assignment routines applied to quality-control NMR spectra. We developed a detection pipeline that classifies spectral regions as signal, artifact, or noise using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 6800 manually annotated spectral segments recorded on 300 and 400 MHz instruments in four different solvents. On a held-out test set of 850 segments, the network achieved precision of 0.94 and recall of 0.91 for artifact detection. Integration of the pipeline into a QC workflow processing 40 spectra per day at a partner synthesis facility reduced the rate of manual re-inspection flags from 18% to 4% over a three-month trial period. The model weights and training code are available on the group's repository. This work was carried out in collaboration with the NTP Novi Sad tenant company SynthoCheck d.o.o. under a short-term industry contract.

title: Transfer learning for ¹³C chemical shift prediction across structural families with limited training data
abstract: Training deep models for ¹³C shift prediction in underrepresented compound families is constrained by the scarcity of curated spectral data. We explored transfer learning from a broadly trained transformer-based shift predictor (pretrained on 61 000 diverse structures) to three target families—steroidal compounds, macrolide-like rings, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons—each with fewer than 400 training examples. Fine-tuning required between 150 and 300 examples to match or exceed the performance of an increment-based method trained on the full available data for each family. On the macrolide test set, fine-tuned RMSE was 1.9 ppm compared to 4.1 ppm for the increment method. The study used only publicly archived spectra; no proprietary data were involved. Findings suggest that the main bottleneck for rare-scaffold prediction is not architecture but the absence of even modestly sized, well-curated family-specific datasets, pointing to a community data-collection priority.

title: Integrated NMR–MS elucidation of minor alkaloids from Balkan Fumaria species using automated spectral interpretation
abstract: Fumaria species native to the Balkan peninsula produce structurally diverse isoquinoline alkaloids, many of which occur in minor quantities insufficient for classical isolation-and-characterisation workflows. We applied an integrated automated elucidation pipeline combining high-field ¹H/¹³C/HMBC NMR and HR-ESI-MS/MS to enriched alkaloid fractions from three Fumaria species collected in Vojvodina, obtaining interpretable spectra at sub-milligram scale. The SPECINT-2 platform proposed structural candidates for 18 alkaloid signals; 11 were confirmed against the literature or authentic standards, four were assigned as known analogues, and three remain provisional. The provisional structures include two apparent N-methyl variants of known protoberberine scaffolds not previously reported from these species. HRESIMS data provided molecular formulas with mass errors below 2.2 ppm for all 18 signals. The study demonstrates that automated spectral interpretation can replace manual expert analysis for the majority of signals in a moderately complex alkaloid mixture when combined with appropriate reference databases.

title: Environmental fate descriptors as additional predictors in QSAR models for azole fungicides: logKow, bioconcentration factor, and soil sorption
abstract: The potential of azole-class fungicides to accumulate in aquatic compartments motivates inclusion of environmental fate parameters alongside biological activity descriptors. For a dataset of 40 commercial and experimental azole fungicides, measured or reliably estimated logKow, BCF, and Koc values were appended to standard topological and electronic descriptors within a PLS regression framework targeting ergosterol inhibition IC50. Models including environmental descriptors showed marginal improvement in external Q²ext (from 0.74 to 0.78) relative to structure-only models, while the BCF term carried a positive PLS weight indicating that lipophilicity and membrane permeability jointly contribute to target binding. Soil sorption (logKoc) was collinear with logKow (r = 0.89) and was removed to avoid redundancy. The exercise demonstrates that environmental fate data, routinely available from regulatory dossiers, can be reused as molecular features in biological activity QSAR, supporting integrated assessment workflows.

title: Determinants of Permanent Out-Migration from Rural Municipalities in the South Banat Region
abstract: Drawing on a structured household survey administered to 412 households across eight municipalities in the South Banat planning district in 2012, this paper examines individual and household-level drivers of permanent rural out-migration. Respondents were classified as stayers, seasonal migrants, or permanent migrants using a retrospective mobility calendar. Binary logit models show that young adults aged 18–35 with secondary or tertiary education, access to a vehicle, and at least one prior relative in an urban area are three to five times more likely to have permanently departed compared with otherwise equivalent peers. Land ownership and receipt of agricultural subsidies exhibit a modest but statistically significant retention effect. The analysis also documents a pronounced gender asymmetry: young women migrate at roughly 1.4 times the rate of young men, contributing to a skewed sex ratio in remaining rural populations. Policy implications for targeted retention incentives are discussed.

title: Land Abandonment as a Consequence of Rural Aging: Evidence from the Mačva District, Serbia
abstract: This paper quantifies the relationship between population aging and agricultural land abandonment in the Mačva district over the period 2000–2015 using cadastral records linked to census population data at the cadastral municipality level. A two-stage least squares model instruments for the share of population aged 65 and over using historical settlement patterns from the 1961 census to address endogeneity. Results indicate that a one-percentage-point increase in the elderly population share is associated with a 0.7 percent rise in the proportion of registered agricultural parcels with no recorded cultivation activity over a five-year interval. The effect is larger on parcels smaller than 0.5 hectares and on sloped terrain. Satellite-derived land cover data from Landsat imagery corroborate cadastral evidence for a subsample of 12 settlements. The study underscores the importance of land mobility measures that account for the limited physical capacity of elderly farm operators.

title: Service Provision Gaps in Demographically Depleted Municipalities of Vojvodina
abstract: As rural populations contract and age, local governments face rising per-capita costs for maintaining basic services. This chapter examines the fiscal and institutional consequences of depopulation in 22 municipalities in Vojvodina that lost more than 20 percent of their population between 1991 and 2011. Using a mixed-method design combining municipal budget data, administrative service records, and interviews with 31 local officials, the chapter documents the closure or consolidation of primary schools, general practice health posts, and postal branches since 2005. The most affected municipalities have an average of 1.8 remaining settlements with a functioning primary school, down from 4.3 in 2000. Interview analysis reveals that inter-municipal cooperation is rarely formalised, and decisions about service withdrawal are typically reactive rather than planned. The chapter proposes a framework for proactive territorial restructuring that could reduce per-capita service costs while minimising access deprivation for elderly residents.

title: Comparing Depopulation Rates Across Peripheral Rural Areas in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and North Macedonia, 2002–2018
abstract: This comparative study examines population trends in 187 rural municipalities classified as peripheral according to a composite accessibility index across three Western Balkan countries using harmonised census and inter-censal estimate data for the period 2002–2018. The natural rate of population change (births minus deaths) and net migration rate are decomposed for each country context. Serbia shows the most pronounced negative natural change (−6.2 per thousand annually on average), driven by a very low crude birth rate. Bosnia-Herzegovina records the highest net out-migration in absolute terms, partly linked to emigration to Western Europe. North Macedonia exhibits higher fertility in rural areas but significant internal redistribution toward Skopje. A multivariate panel model with country and period fixed effects identifies per-capita GDP, road network density, and regional unemployment as the primary correlates of net migration intensity. The results highlight the limits of uniform EU pre-accession rural development instruments when demographic contexts diverge substantially.

title: Spatial Patterns of Elderly Population Concentration in Rural Serbia: A GIS-Based Assessment
abstract: Using settlement-level population data from the 2011 Serbian census and geographic information system tools, this paper produces a fine-grained map of elderly population concentration for the approximately 4 700 rural settlements of Serbia. A spatial autocorrelation analysis (Moran's I = 0.61, p < 0.001) confirms strong clustering of high elderly shares in the eastern and southeastern parts of the country. Local Indicators of Spatial Association identify 312 settlements as high–high clusters, almost all located in the Šumadija–Western Serbia and Southern and Eastern Serbia planning regions. Kernel density estimation is applied to visualise the intensity of aging across continuous space, revealing a contiguous belt of demographic crisis extending from the Homolje highlands to the Pčinja river basin. The paper discusses how these spatial patterns should inform the geographic targeting of rural revitalisation measures and argues that current IPARD programme allocation criteria are poorly aligned with demographic vulnerability.

title: Population Projections for Rural Municipalities of Vojvodina Under Three Migration Scenarios, 2021–2041
abstract: This paper presents cohort-component population projections for 39 rural municipalities of Vojvodina under a baseline scenario (continuation of observed 2011–2021 trends), an optimistic scenario (50 percent reduction in net out-migration from the most recent five-year period), and a pessimistic scenario (acceleration of emigration to EU member states by 30 percent). Mortality rates are drawn from the latest Serbian life tables; fertility rates are parameterised separately for urban-origin and rural-origin cohorts using registered birth data. Under the baseline scenario, 26 of the 39 municipalities are projected to lose more than 25 percent of their 2021 population by 2041, with total rural population in the province falling from an estimated 296 000 to approximately 228 000. The optimistic scenario reduces this loss to around 14 percent. Sensitivity analysis highlights the disproportionate impact of female cohorts aged 20–34, whose emigration decisions drive projected declines in the crude birth rate more strongly than any other demographic parameter.

title: Demographic Decline and Agricultural Extensification in the Timočka Krajina Region: A Twenty-Year Retrospective
abstract: The Timočka Krajina region in eastern Serbia has experienced some of the most severe population losses in the country since the 1990s. This study integrates agricultural census data (2000, 2012, 2023), municipal population statistics, and satellite-derived Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) time series to trace the co-evolution of demographic contraction and shifts in land use intensity across 18 municipalities over two decades. The analysis documents a 34 percent reduction in the number of registered farms, a 41 percent fall in the agricultural labour force, and a measurable decrease in summertime NDVI variance consistent with reduced crop diversity. Panel regressions with municipality fixed effects confirm a robust negative association between population density change and the proportion of arable land under annual crops. The paper argues that extensification in this region is primarily driven by labour scarcity rather than deliberate policy or market signals, with implications for food production capacity and rural landscape management.

title: Informal Care Arrangements in Aging Rural Households of the Western Balkans: Evidence from Four Country Contexts
abstract: As formal elderly care infrastructure in rural areas declines alongside the populations that justify it, informal care arrangements within households and kin networks take on greater significance. This preprint reports preliminary findings from 284 structured diary-based interviews conducted in rural settlements of Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro between 2023 and 2025 as part of an ongoing cross-national project. Respondents are elderly individuals aged 70 and over living in settlements with fewer than 500 inhabitants. The analysis distinguishes three care provision modes: co-resident adult children (31 percent), non-resident kin visiting at least weekly (28 percent), and isolation with minimal regular support (41 percent). The isolated group is disproportionately composed of women over 80 living alone. Seasonal out-migration of potential caregivers amplifies care gaps during summer months. Cross-country variation in the share of isolated elderly correlates with the availability of public transport and the density of diaspora remittance flows. Full results will be published following field completion.

title: Agent heterogeneity in evacuation simulation: modelling mobility-impaired occupants in public spaces
abstract: Standard pedestrian evacuation models typically assume a homogeneous population with uniform walking speed and reaction time. This study extends an agent-based evacuation model to include three subpopulations: unimpaired adults, elderly individuals, and wheelchair users. Parameter values for walking speed, door-passing time, and response time were derived from a structured observational study conducted in a shopping centre in Novi Sad involving 210 volunteers. Agents were assigned stochastically to subpopulations according to census-based proportions for a mid-sized Serbian city. Simulations were run for a two-storey shopping centre floor plan with four exits, varying the proportion of mobility-impaired agents from 5 to 25 percent of total occupancy. Results indicate that a 20 percent share of mobility-impaired agents increases mean total evacuation time by 41 percent under peak occupancy conditions, and shifts the critical bottleneck from the main exit to interior ramp connections. Recommendations for signage placement and staff-assisted routing are discussed.

title: Integrating IFC building data with agent-based evacuation models: a workflow for fire safety assessment
abstract: Building Information Modelling (BIM) data in Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) format contains geometric and semantic information that is directly useful for populating evacuation simulations, but automated conversion workflows remain uncommon. This paper describes a Python-based parser that extracts room boundaries, door positions, stairwell connections, and occupancy capacities from IFC files and translates them into the input format required by the AnyLogic pedestrian library. The workflow was validated on three buildings: a university faculty building, a municipal administrative centre, and a hospital outpatient wing, all in the Vojvodina region. Parsing time for the largest model, containing 847 spaces, was under 90 seconds. Simulation results for evacuation scenarios were compared with manually constructed baseline models; total evacuation time differed by less than 5 percent across all three cases. The workflow reduces model setup time from approximately 14 hours to under 2 hours for a building of average complexity.

title: Behavioural response to alarm signals in school buildings: a survey-informed agent-based study
abstract: Pre-evacuation delay — the time between alarm activation and the start of movement — is a critical but poorly quantified factor in school building evacuations. This paper reports results from a questionnaire administered to 318 teachers and staff across 11 primary and secondary schools in Zrenjanin and Novi Sad, asking about their typical response to fire alarm signals. Responses revealed that 64 percent of respondents would first attempt to gather students before moving toward exits, and 23 percent reported they would seek confirmation from colleagues before acting. These behavioural modes were encoded as finite-state machines within an agent-based model. Simulation runs for a representative three-storey school building showed that including realistic pre-evacuation delay distributions increased mean evacuation time by 28 percent compared with a zero-delay baseline. The study also found that classroom location on upper floors correlated with longer teacher response delays, suggesting targeted training interventions.

title: Effect of exit sign visibility on evacuation efficiency: an agent-based sensitivity analysis under smoke conditions
abstract: Exit sign visibility degrades significantly under smoke conditions, yet most simulation studies assume full wayfinding capability for all agents. This paper introduces a visibility model in which each agent's awareness of available exits is a function of a simulated smoke density field and the photometric properties of LED exit signs at three luminance levels: 100, 300, and 500 cd/m². The smoke dispersion field was pre-computed using a simplified zone model and imported as a time-varying input to the agent simulation. Experiments were conducted on a 1,200 m² conference centre floor plan with 400 agents. Reducing exit sign luminance from 500 to 100 cd/m² under full smoke conditions increased mean evacuation time by 19 percent and raised the proportion of agents requiring more than 6 minutes to exit from 4 percent to 31 percent. Results suggest that current Serbian building regulations, which specify a minimum of 100 cd/m² for emergency signage, may be insufficient for high-occupancy venues.

title: Validation of pedestrian simulation models using motion capture data from controlled evacuation drills
abstract: Agent-based pedestrian models are rarely validated against spatially resolved empirical trajectory data because such data are expensive to collect. This paper describes a controlled evacuation experiment in a university corridor segment measuring 32 m × 2.4 m, involving 60 volunteer participants equipped with reflective markers tracked by a 12-camera motion capture system at 100 Hz. Three density conditions were tested by varying the number of active participants. Recorded trajectories were used to compute spacing, speed, and lateral deviation distributions, which were then compared against simulated trajectories produced by two calibrated agent-based models implemented in AnyLogic. The social force model reproduced mean speed profiles with a mean absolute error of 0.06 m/s, while a rule-based model produced errors of up to 0.19 m/s in high-density conditions. The dataset, comprising 1,840 individual trajectory segments, is released as an open dataset to support future model comparisons.

title: Evacuation modelling for heritage buildings: challenges and adaptations in a nineteenth-century municipal archive
abstract: Heritage buildings present particular difficulties for evacuation modelling: irregular floor plans, narrow historic doorways, restricted structural modifications, and mixed-use occupancy all deviate from assumptions embedded in standard simulation tools. This paper presents an evacuation study of a nineteenth-century municipal archive building in Sremski Karlovci, which houses both document storage areas accessed by archivists and a publicly accessible reading room. Field measurements of doorway widths, tread geometry, and visitor flow were conducted over four months. An agent-based model was constructed with custom geometry and door-flow parameters derived from the measurements. Simulations indicated that the single public staircase represents a critical bottleneck at visitor loads above 40 persons, with evacuation times exceeding 5 minutes. The study proposes three low-intervention modifications — repositioning a storage rack, adding directional signage, and revising the visitor entry protocol — that collectively reduce simulated evacuation time to under 3 minutes without structural alteration.

title: Towards a standardised benchmark suite for pedestrian evacuation simulation tools: a position paper
abstract: Reproducibility in pedestrian simulation research is hampered by the absence of agreed benchmark scenarios. Different studies use incompatible floor plan geometries, occupant parameter ranges, and performance metrics, making cross-tool comparisons unreliable. This paper reviews 42 published evacuation simulation studies from 2010 to 2024 and identifies recurring experimental configurations. Based on this review, the authors propose a set of five benchmark scenarios — a single-room egress, a corridor merge, a multi-storey stairwell, a mixed-mobility public hall, and a phased zone evacuation — each with specified geometry, occupant load, parameter ranges, and required output metrics. A reference implementation in AnyLogic and NetLogo accompanies the paper. The benchmarks are intended to be usable by academic researchers and by safety engineers in applied practice. The authors invite community feedback through an open repository prior to formal standardisation submission.

title: Effect of Base Station Clustering on Interference in Heterogeneous Cellular Networks
abstract: Practical base station deployments exhibit spatial clustering rather than complete spatial randomness. This study replaces the standard homogeneous Poisson model with a Thomas cluster process to capture the tendency of small cells to be deployed in groups around high-traffic venues such as shopping areas and transit hubs. Analytical expressions for the Laplace functional of interference are derived and used to obtain coverage probability bounds. Comparisons with a homogeneous Poisson model using calibrated parameters from a mid-size urban area in Vojvodina show that the clustered model predicts interference levels up to 3 dB higher in the fifth percentile of the SINR distribution. Field measurements collected at 12 locations are used to partially validate the spatial model selection. The results suggest that ignoring clustering leads to optimistic coverage estimates in dense indoor deployments.

title: Downlink Energy Efficiency in Dense Small-Cell Networks: A Stochastic Geometry Perspective
abstract: Energy efficiency, defined as the ratio of area spectral efficiency to total power consumption, is analyzed for a single-tier dense small-cell network modeled by a homogeneous Poisson point process. A power consumption model that accounts for static circuit power, dynamic transmit power, and sleep-mode savings is incorporated into the stochastic geometry framework. Closed-form approximations for energy efficiency as a function of small-cell density are derived and validated by simulation over a range of densities from 1 to 500 base stations per square kilometer. Results indicate a unimodal relationship between base station density and energy efficiency, with a peak at an intermediate density that depends on the load model and the sleep-mode activation threshold. The analysis quantifies the trade-off between coverage improvement and energy cost associated with network densification and offers deployment guidelines for operator planning.

title: Ironic Framing in Serbian Facebook Political Memes During the 2022 Parliamentary Campaign
abstract: This study examines how irony functions as a rhetorical device in political memes shared on Serbian Facebook groups in the lead-up to the April 2022 parliamentary elections. A corpus of 1,840 image-text memes was collected from fourteen publicly accessible political discussion groups between January and April 2022 using a custom scraping script. Memes were annotated for ironic register, visual composition type, and partisan orientation. Semiotic analysis drawing on Barthes's concepts of denotation and connotation was applied to a stratified subsample of 230 memes. Results indicate that irony appears in approximately 61 percent of opposition-aligned memes but in only 22 percent of pro-government material, suggesting a structural asymmetry in rhetorical strategy. The most frequent ironic device is incongruity between superimposed text and photographic source material, particularly in memes targeting incumbent officials. The article argues that irony in this context functions less as humour and more as a distancing mechanism that allows politically risky claims to circulate with reduced accountability. Implications for the study of vernacular political communication in hybrid-regime media environments are discussed.

title: From Screenshot to Share: Tracing Meme Mutation Across TikTok and Telegram in the Serbian Online Sphere
abstract: Political memes rarely remain static as they move between platforms; their visual and textual elements are cropped, captioned, or re-contextualised in ways that alter their semiotic load. This paper tracks the cross-platform mutation of twenty-three seed memes identified on TikTok and followed through Telegram channels between March and September 2023. Each seed was selected because it had attracted more than five hundred shares in its first week of circulation. Variant versions were collected manually and through keyword monitoring, yielding 614 distinct instances. For each variant, changes in image crop, added overlays, altered captions, and metadata were recorded. Semiotic comparison of variant chains shows that decontextualisation of photographic evidence and reattachment to new political actors is the most common transformation (occurring in 38 percent of chains). A secondary pattern involves the replacement of Serbian-language captions with regional language variants, suggesting cross-border circulation into Bosnian and Croatian online communities. The findings are discussed in relation to platform affordances that shape which semiotic elements are stable and which are easily modified.

title: Vernacular Resistance and Visual Satire: Political Memes as Counterpublic Practice in Serbia
abstract: This chapter situates Serbian political meme production within theories of counterpublics and vernacular creativity, drawing on ethnographic observation of three online communities between 2022 and 2023 and forty-five semi-structured interviews with active meme creators recruited through purposive sampling. Participants ranged in age from seventeen to thirty-four and described their meme-making primarily as a form of political commentary unavailable to them through institutional channels. Analysis focuses on how creators perceive the boundary between acceptable satire and actionable defamation, and how that perception shapes their choices of visual source material, caption tone, and distribution channel. The chapter argues that meme production in this context constitutes a form of low-cost political participation that compensates for perceived closure in formal public debate. However, the chapter also documents self-censorship practices—including face blurring and deliberate ambiguity—that creators adopt in response to earlier legal threats against online commentators. The tension between expressive ambition and anticipatory self-restraint is presented as a defining feature of politically engaged meme culture in a constrained media environment.

title: Multimodal Annotation Schemes for Political Internet Memes: A Comparative Review of Existing Frameworks and a Proposal for Serbian-Language Corpora
abstract: Annotating political memes for computational or discourse-analytic research requires decisions that existing multimodal annotation schemes do not always address satisfactorily, particularly for languages with limited digital NLP resources and for cultural contexts outside Western Europe or North America. This paper reviews eight annotation schemes published between 2017 and 2023, assessing them against four criteria: handling of embedded typography, treatment of photographic versus illustrated sources, provision for irony and sarcasm marking, and suitability for morphologically rich languages. Following this review, the paper proposes a layered annotation scheme tailored to Serbian-language political memes, with four tiers covering visual composition, textual surface, rhetorical register, and estimated partisan alignment. The scheme is piloted on a test set of 320 memes drawn from the corpus described in the authors' earlier work. Inter-annotator agreement is measured using Cohen's kappa; values above 0.72 are achieved for visual and textual tiers, while the rhetorical register tier yields a lower mean of 0.58, indicating that irony marking remains a persistent challenge. The scheme and the pilot annotations are made available as an open dataset.

title: Frames of Ethnic Otherness: A Content Analysis of Three Serbian Daily Newspapers, 1999–2003
abstract: This study examines how three high-circulation Serbian daily newspapers framed ethnic minority communities in the immediate post-conflict period. Using a deductive framing protocol applied to 1,847 news items sampled across four constructed weeks per year from 1999 to 2003, the analysis identifies five dominant frames: threat, victimhood, integration, folklorisation, and legal-administrative. Threat framing declined from 41 percent of coded items in 1999 to 18 percent in 2003, while integration frames rose from 9 percent to 27 percent over the same interval. Inter-coder reliability was established using Krippendorff's alpha (α = 0.81). The findings suggest a gradual normative reorientation in editorial practice rather than a sudden shift, and they are interpreted in relation to EU accession pressure on Serbian media institutions. The article contributes a baseline dataset that has since informed follow-up reception studies.

title: Editorial Autonomy in Small-Market Television: A Comparative Study of Serbia, Montenegro, Slovenia, and Slovakia
abstract: This monograph presents findings from a four-country comparative study of editorial autonomy in small-market commercial television conducted between 2018 and 2022. Using a mixed-methods design combining the adapted editorial autonomy instrument previously developed by the lead author, 112 in-depth interviews, and content analysis of 4,800 news segments across 24 broadcasters, the study provides the most extensive comparative evidence to date on the structural determinants of editorial independence in post-communist small markets. Key findings include: Slovenia shows substantially higher autonomy scores than the other three countries, associated with stronger public service broadcasting and more diverse ownership; Serbia and Montenegro show convergent patterns of low autonomy linked to politically affiliated ownership; Slovakia occupies an intermediate position. The monograph develops an explanatory model in which regulatory capacity, ownership diversity, and labour market conditions interact to produce distinct autonomy regimes, and concludes with policy recommendations for the Western Balkan media reform agenda.

title: Wet-Gate Telecine Scanning of Shrunk Nitrate Prints: Practical Parameters for Sub-1-Percent Shrinkage Material
abstract: Nitrate-base films from the early Yugoslav documentary corpus (1945–1952) present specific transport challenges when shrinkage falls between 0.6 and 0.9 percent. This paper documents a series of scanning trials conducted on seven short documentary prints held at the Vojvodina Regional Film Depository, using a Marconi-derived wet-gate telecine unit retrofitted with a variable-tension sprocket drive. Four immersion fluids—perchloroethylene, isoparaffin, a fluorocarbon blend, and a water-glycol mixture—were evaluated for scratch concealment efficiency, measured optically by comparing before-and-after RMS grain noise readings at 2K resolution. The fluorocarbon blend produced the most consistent scratch suppression (average reduction of 62 percent in visible surface noise) while introducing the least dimensional variability in the film path. Handling protocols and fluid recovery procedures are described in sufficient detail to allow replication in comparable archive laboratory settings.

title: Colour Fading Characterisation in Imbibition-Dyed Prints from the Yugoslav Colour Cinema Transition, 1955–1965
abstract: Between 1955 and 1965 several Yugoslav productions were printed using imbibition dye transfer processes, sourced primarily from Czech and East German laboratories. These prints exhibit characteristic cyan dye loss that produces a strongly magenta-shifted image after decades of storage. This paper describes a spectrophotometric survey of 31 surviving imbibition prints, measuring dye layer density in red, green, and blue channels using a calibrated transmission densitometer at ten representative frames per reel. A reference dataset was assembled from production-era grading records recovered from the Jadran Film technical archive in Zagreb. Digital restoration paths are evaluated using two commercial colour science tools and one open-source pipeline; the open-source route produced results within acceptable dE2000 tolerance of the reference when guided by the recovered grading records. Limitations arising from incomplete documentation for roughly half the surveyed titles are discussed.

title: Manual Stabilisation Techniques for Anamorphic Prints with Lateral Weave: A Case Study from a 1961 Serbian Feature
abstract: This paper presents restoration work carried out on the sole surviving print of a 1961 Serbian anamorphic feature held in deteriorated condition at a municipal archive in Zrenjanin. The print exhibited severe lateral weave due to asymmetric moisture absorption in the base layer, producing positional jitter of up to 14 pixels horizontally at 2K resolution after scanning. A combination of optical flow stabilisation and manually supervised point-tracking was applied across approximately 8,400 frames. Human supervisors overrode automatic tracking decisions in an estimated 9 percent of frames, primarily in scenes with low-contrast interiors and dissolve transitions. The paper evaluates the labour cost of the hybrid manual–automatic approach against a fully automated pass using two off-the-shelf stabilisation modules, finding that the hybrid method reduced residual jitter by an additional 34 percent at the cost of roughly 60 additional person-hours per reel. Archival and aesthetic justification for this expenditure is discussed.

title: Grain Structure Preservation in 4K Restorations of Black-and-White Yugoslav Films: A Comparison of Noise Reduction Approaches
abstract: The tension between noise reduction and grain preservation is a recurring problem in archival film restoration. This paper evaluates four noise reduction strategies—temporal averaging, spatial frequency filtering, learning-based single-frame denoising, and a hybrid temporal–spatial approach—applied to 4K scans of three 35 mm black-and-white Yugoslav feature films from the 1950s. Ground-truth grain structure was estimated from framestills scanned from undegraded leader sections of the same prints. Quantitative assessment used a grain texture similarity metric computed over matched image patches, supplemented by a structured expert viewing session involving seven film archivists who were unaware of the processing method applied to each clip. The learning-based method achieved the highest noise suppression but received the lowest grain-fidelity scores from expert viewers, suggesting that perceptual and metric-based criteria diverge significantly for this material. Practical recommendations are offered for archives operating within defined viewing-format constraints.

title: Documentation Standards for Hybrid Photochemical–Digital Restoration Projects: Lessons from Southeastern European Archive Practice
abstract: Hybrid restoration workflows—those combining physical photochemical interventions with digital processing—generate heterogeneous records that rarely conform to a single metadata schema. This chapter reviews documentation practices across seven restoration projects conducted at institutions in Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, and North Macedonia between 2009 and 2016, drawing on interviews with archive technicians and examination of project logbooks. The analysis identifies three categories of underdocumented decision points: chemical treatment choices, manual colour correction adjustments, and frame-level interpolation events. A minimum documentation template is proposed, compatible with both FIAF cataloguing guidelines and the EBU R99 technical metadata framework. The chapter also discusses the practical difficulty of retrospectively documenting decisions made during time-pressured restoration campaigns, and argues for embedding documentation checkpoints into project scheduling rather than treating documentation as a post-production task.

title: Acetic Acid Neutralisation Pre-Treatment Prior to Scanning: Effects on Base Transparency and Dimensional Stability in Moderate-Stage Vinegar Syndrome Prints
abstract: A controlled experiment was conducted to assess whether alkaline buffering pre-treatment—using a dilute magnesium bicarbonate solution applied by controlled humidity exposure—measurably improves base transparency and dimensional stability in acetate prints rated A-D level 2 to 3. Forty-eight reels drawn from a single production batch of a 1967 Yugoslav documentary series were divided into treated and untreated groups. Treated reels underwent a 72-hour humidity chamber exposure at 45 percent relative humidity with buffering agent, followed by a 48-hour drying phase. Transmission densitometry and shrinkage measurements were taken before treatment, immediately after drying, and at four weeks. Treated reels showed a mean improvement of 0.08 in base transmission density and a 0.12 percent reduction in shrinkage compared to controls. No statistically significant difference was observed in surface haze. These results suggest modest but consistent benefit for moderate-stage material, with the caveat that severely degraded reels (A-D level 4) showed no measurable improvement.

title: Reconstructing Missing Frames in Yugoslav Newsreels: Interpolation, Duplication, and the Ethics of Visual Completeness
abstract: Yugoslav weekly newsreels from the 1950s and 1960s frequently survive with physical frame loss caused by splice failures, perforation tears, and deliberate editorial cuts made during the socialist period. This paper examines three strategies for handling missing frame sequences during digital restoration: leaving gaps with visual markers, duplicating adjacent frames, and applying motion-interpolated synthetic frames. A sample of 18 newsreel segments with documented physical frame loss was used to test all three approaches. Viewer response data collected from 24 participants—drawn from archivists, film scholars, and general audiences—indicate that motion interpolation was preferred for sequences of one to three missing frames but was considered misleading in sequences of four or more. The paper argues for a tiered approach grounded in both technical feasibility and archival transparency, and proposes visible watermarking conventions for interpolated frames intended for public distribution.

title: Calibration of a 4K Wet-Gate Scanner for Non-Standard Aspect Ratios in Yugoslav Partisan Film Productions
abstract: A subset of Yugoslav partisan films produced between 1947 and 1955 were shot on 35 mm stock but framed for projection at non-standard aspect ratios—typically 1.33:1 with top-and-bottom aperture masking or 1.55:1 intermediate formats—due to equipment constraints and exhibition venue variability. Scanning these materials at standard aperture settings introduces systematic inclusion of unexposed rebate areas that distort automatic colour calibration and grain sampling routines. This paper describes a calibration procedure developed for the department's 4K wet-gate telecine unit that allows user-defined active aperture boundaries to be specified per reel, with automatic propagation of calibration targets derived from framestill samples within the defined boundary. Verification tests on 11 reels show that constrained-aperture calibration reduced mean colour channel deviation by 0.6 density units compared to full-aperture calibration and eliminated rebate-area artefacts in the delivered scan without requiring post-scan cropping.

title: Reflectance Transformation Imaging Applied to Damaged Film Leader and Title Cards from 1940s Yugoslav Documentary Material
abstract: Film leaders and intertitle cards from the earliest Yugoslav documentary productions often carry ink or stamp markings that are illegible under standard transmitted light due to fading, chemical staining, or physical abrasion. This paper describes an application of Reflectance Transformation Imaging (RTI), adapted from its conventional use in flat heritage objects, to physically extracted title frames from six documentary reels dating to 1945–1948. Frames were carefully removed from deteriorated sections and imaged under 24-position dome illumination using a purpose-built compact RTI rig. Post-processing using polynomial texture mapping recovered legible text in four of the six samples, including a previously unknown production credit and a distribution stamp indicating export to Hungary. Limits of the method—particularly with heavily lacquered or base-fogged frames—are discussed, and a reintegration workflow for returning digitised metadata to the reel record is described.

title: Hybrid Workflow Assessment for the Restoration of Scope Prints with Combined Base Shrinkage and Colour Fading: Preliminary Findings from the Vojvodina Regional Corpus
abstract: This preprint presents interim findings from an ongoing restoration campaign covering 34 CinemaScope prints produced at Vojvodina-based studios between 1963 and 1971. The prints exhibit simultaneous acetate base shrinkage (mean 0.71 percent) and dye layer fading affecting primarily the yellow and cyan channels. The paper documents a hybrid workflow in which physical pre-treatment—alkaline humidity buffering and controlled drying—precedes wet-gate scanning, followed by digital dye recovery guided by reference densitometry from surviving camera negatives held at a separate institution. Preliminary quantitative results from 11 completed reels indicate that the hybrid approach yields a 28 percent improvement in measured colour gamut coverage relative to digital-only processing from untreated scans. Remaining challenges include inconsistent negative access and variable photochemical pre-treatment response across reel batches. Full results are expected following completion of the remaining 23 reels in late 2026.

title: Adaptive Disclosure Levels in a Pharmacovigilance Reporting Interface: A Simulation Experiment
abstract: Pharmacovigilance adverse-event reporting systems are used by a heterogeneous population ranging from hospital pharmacists to general practitioners with minimal pharmacology training. This paper presents a simulation experiment in which 48 healthcare professionals from four institutions in Serbia and North Macedonia were assigned to either a fixed-disclosure or an adaptive-disclosure version of a prototype reporting interface. The adaptive version estimated user expertise from response latency and field-completion patterns during an onboarding task and adjusted the number of visible optional fields accordingly. Completion rate for voluntary narrative fields rose from 31 percent (fixed) to 54 percent (adaptive) without a significant increase in overall session time. However, expert pharmacists in the adaptive condition reported lower satisfaction, citing the system's occasional misclassification of their expertise level as patronising. The paper discusses calibration strategies and the trade-off between automation comfort and professional identity in expert-facing adaptive systems.

title: Attenuation of ibuprofen and carbamazepine during riverbank filtration along a Danube transect: field monitoring across two hydrological seasons
abstract: Riverbank filtration (RBF) is widely used as a pre-treatment step for drinking water production along the Danube, yet systematic data on pharmaceutical removal across contrasting hydrological conditions remain scarce. This study presents a 14-month field monitoring campaign at an RBF site near Novi Sad, combining weekly sampling from four multilevel piezometers positioned 8–120 m from the riverbank. Ibuprofen and carbamazepine were quantified in river water and bank filtrate by solid-phase extraction followed by LC-MS/MS, with method detection limits of 2 ng/L and 4 ng/L, respectively. Dissolved oxygen, redox potential, nitrate, iron(II), and manganese were measured as redox indicators. Ibuprofen concentrations decreased from a median of 310 ng/L in river water to below detection at 45 m travel distance under oxic conditions, but persisted at up to 85 ng/L at equivalent distances during anoxic winter periods. Carbamazepine showed consistently low removal (14–22%) regardless of redox status, consistent with its recalcitrance. Travel time estimates derived from bromide tracer injections ranged from 4 to 18 days across the piezometer transect. Results indicate that redox zonation, more than residence time alone, controls ibuprofen fate and should be considered in RBF vulnerability assessments.

title: Column experiment assessment of 17α-ethinylestradiol sorption and transformation in sediments representative of the Danube riverbank
abstract: The synthetic estrogen 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2) is frequently detected in surface waters at concentrations sufficient to cause endocrine disruption in fish, yet its behaviour during bank filtration is poorly constrained relative to non-steroidal pharmaceuticals. Bench-scale saturated column experiments were conducted using Danube alluvial sediments (coarse sand, organic carbon content 0.08–0.31% by mass) packed into 50 cm borosilicate columns operated under controlled oxic (dissolved oxygen 7–8 mg/L) and anoxic (sparged with N2, redox potential −120 to −160 mV) conditions at 12 °C. Influent EE2 concentration was set at 200 ng/L. Effluent samples were collected at pore-volume intervals and analysed by LC-MS/MS after online SPE. Under oxic conditions, EE2 removal reached 91% by 3.2 pore volumes, attributable to both sorption (Kd = 2.8 L/kg) and aerobic biodegradation evidenced by the appearance of the transformation product EE2-3-sulfate. Under anoxic conditions, removal was 47% at equivalent pore volumes and no sulfate conjugate was detected, suggesting biotransformation was suppressed. Sterilised controls confirmed abiotic sorption accounted for roughly 30% of total removal under both conditions. Results support the view that aerobic microbial activity is essential for effective EE2 attenuation during RBF.

title: Seasonal variability in the microbial community composition of Danube bank filtrate and its relationship to pharmaceutical transformation rates
abstract: Microbial communities in riverbank filtration systems catalyse the transformation of many organic micropollutants, but how their seasonal shifts translate to changes in attenuation capacity is rarely quantified directly. Groundwater samples from two piezometers at a Novi Sad RBF site were collected monthly over one calendar year (January–December 2023) for both pharmaceutical analysis and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing (V3–V4 region, Illumina MiSeq). Simultaneously, first-order biotransformation rate constants (kbio) were estimated for ibuprofen, diclofenac, and metoprolol from pore-water concentration profiles using an advection–dispersion–reaction model. Alpha diversity (Shannon index) was significantly lower in winter months (mean 3.1 ± 0.3) than in summer (mean 4.6 ± 0.4). Relative abundance of Proteobacteria correlated positively with kbio for ibuprofen (Pearson r = 0.74, p < 0.01). Metoprolol kbio showed no significant seasonal trend, consistent with its partial transformation under both oxic and mildly anoxic conditions. Diclofenac transformation was negligible (kbio < 0.02 d⁻¹) year-round. These findings suggest that seasonal microbial dynamics are a meaningful predictor of pharmaceutical fate for select compound classes and should be incorporated into predictive RBF models.

title: Occurrence of selected endocrine-disrupting compounds in drinking water supply wells fed by Danube bank filtration: a two-site comparison
abstract: Production wells at riverbank filtration schemes are considered a robust barrier against micropollutants, but systematic occurrence data from Serbian water supply infrastructure are limited. This study reports the concentrations of nine endocrine-disrupting compounds (EDCs) — including bisphenol A, four natural and synthetic estrogens, nonylphenol, and two phthalate metabolites — in raw river water, intermediate monitoring wells, and finished drinking water at two RBF-supplied waterworks in Vojvodina province, sampled quarterly over 12 months in 2024. All samples were extracted by solid-phase extraction and measured by LC-MS/MS. Estrone was the most frequently detected estrogen in river water (median 18 ng/L, maximum 67 ng/L) and was detected in 40% of production-well samples at concentrations of 2–9 ng/L. Bisphenol A was detected in 100% of river water samples (median 34 ng/L) but fell below the method quantification limit of 5 ng/L in 85% of production-well samples. Nonylphenol showed the lowest removal across both sites (mean 38%), correlated with shorter estimated travel times during high-flow events. Results indicate that current RBF operation provides adequate but not complete EDC removal, and that travel time reduction during floods represents the primary vulnerability for these supply systems.
