title: Effect of Carbonate Alkalinity on Absorbance Readings in the 1,10-Phenanthroline Iron(II) Method at Elevated pH
abstract: The 1,10-phenanthroline colorimetric procedure for dissolved iron(II) is routinely applied in field settings, yet its sensitivity to background alkalinity is poorly documented for samples from carbonate-rich aquifers. This study examined absorbance readings at 510 nm in synthetic solutions containing 0–600 mg/L total alkalinity (as CaCO3) with iron(II) concentrations between 0.05 and 2.0 mg/L. At alkalinity above 300 mg/L, apparent absorbance increased by 4–11% relative to low-alkalinity blanks, attributable to colloidal carbonate scattering forming within seconds of reagent addition. Three correction approaches were tested: matched-matrix blanks, a turbidity-subtraction step at 700 nm, and acidification pre-treatment to pH 2.0. Acidification reduced the bias to below 0.3% but introduced partial oxidation of Fe(II) to Fe(III) during transport when samples were not preserved immediately. The turbidity subtraction at 700 nm offered a practical compromise, reducing the alkalinity-related error to under 1.5% across the tested range without requiring pre-acidification. Limits of detection under corrected conditions were 0.018 mg/L. The findings are directly applicable to monitoring wells in the Vojvodina region, where groundwater alkalinity commonly exceeds 400 mg/L.

title: Calcium and Magnesium Cross-Sensitivity in the Molybdenum Blue Phosphate Method: A Systematic Evaluation
abstract: The molybdenum blue method for dissolved reactive phosphate (DRP) is widely used in portable water-quality kits, but interference from divalent cations at concentrations typical of hard groundwater has not been systematically quantified. Solutions containing 0–400 mg/L Ca2+ and 0–150 mg/L Mg2+ were prepared at three DRP levels (0.05, 0.50, and 2.00 mg/L) and analysed using the ammonium molybdate–ascorbic acid procedure at 880 nm. Calcium at 300 mg/L caused a suppression of 6–8% in absorbance relative to deionised water blanks, while magnesium at 120 mg/L caused 3–4% suppression. When both ions were present at levels representative of Pannonian Basin shallow aquifers (260 mg/L Ca2+, 85 mg/L Mg2+), total suppression reached 9.5% at low DRP concentrations. A simple correction factor derived from total hardness, measurable in the field with EDTA titration, reduced the combined error to below 2%. The approach was validated against ICP-OES measurements on 22 groundwater samples collected from monitoring wells in Bačka and Banat. The method is suitable for routine deployment without laboratory pre-treatment.

title: Field-Portable Photometric Determination of Ammonium in Groundwater Using the Indophenol Blue Reaction Under High-Salinity Conditions
abstract: The indophenol blue reaction is the standard colorimetric route to ammonium in natural waters, but its applicability in high-ionic-strength groundwater (electrical conductivity above 1500 µS/cm) has been questioned due to ionic-strength effects on reaction kinetics and dye stability. This work evaluated the method across a conductivity range of 200–3500 µS/cm using synthetic NaCl, Na2SO4, and NaHCO3 matrices at ammonium concentrations of 0.1–5.0 mg/L NH4-N. Ionic strength alone (controlled by NaCl) caused less than 2% deviation at conductivities up to 2500 µS/cm. However, bicarbonate at concentrations above 500 mg/L slowed colour development by approximately 18% at 20 min reaction time, requiring an extended 45-minute development period or mild acidification before reagent addition. Temperature during colour development (15–30 °C) interacted significantly with bicarbonate effects; a correction equation incorporating both temperature and alkalinity is presented and validated on 18 real groundwater samples from the Srem sub-region. Detection limit under optimised conditions was 0.04 mg/L NH4-N.

title: Turbidity Compensation Strategies for Portable Spectrophotometers Operating in Optically Complex Groundwater
abstract: Optically complex groundwater — containing suspended iron oxyhydroxides, colloidal silica, or humic substances — presents a persistent challenge for portable single-wavelength photometers. This study compared four turbidity compensation strategies across 12 field instruments from four manufacturers: (i) dual-wavelength subtraction using a non-absorbing reference wavelength, (ii) centrifugation of a field sub-sample, (iii) 0.45 µm syringe filtration, and (iv) mathematical blank correction using a reagent-free aliquot. Tests used synthetic suspensions of ferrihydrite (5–80 NTU) and humic acid (2–25 mg/L) added to certified standard solutions of iron, phosphate, and nitrite. Filtration and centrifugation removed turbidity effectively but altered analyte concentrations for iron by 15–40% depending on redox conditions. Dual-wavelength subtraction performed well for humic backgrounds (bias < 3%) but underperformed for ferrihydrite (bias 5–12%) due to wavelength-dependent scattering. Reagent-free blank correction was the most universally applicable approach, reducing error to below 2% in all tested matrices. Practical guidance for field use is provided.
venue: Journal of Field Analytical Chemistry and Environmental Monitoring

title: Nitrite Determination by the Griess Reaction in Groundwater Containing Elevated Sulfate and Chloride: Matrix Matching or Standard Addition?
abstract: The Griess diazotisation reaction is among the most sensitive colorimetric methods available for nitrite, yet anion matrix effects at elevated ionic strength are insufficiently characterised for practical guidance. Synthetic groundwater solutions were prepared to represent three ionic-strength scenarios encountered in Vojvodina wells: low (IS ≈ 8 mmol/L), moderate (IS ≈ 25 mmol/L), and high (IS ≈ 60 mmol/L), with sulfate ranging from 50 to 600 mg/L and chloride from 30 to 400 mg/L. Nitrite concentrations tested were 0.01–1.0 mg/L NO2-N. Sulfate at 600 mg/L caused no statistically significant bias (<1%). Chloride had a slight suppressive effect (2–4%) at 400 mg/L attributed to competition in the diazotisation step. Matrix matching using a synthetic background electrolyte reduced the chloride-related bias to below 0.5%. Standard addition gave equivalent accuracy but required three times the reagent volume and analysis time. Based on reproducibility and speed, matrix matching with a single representative synthetic blank is recommended for routine field campaigns in high-chloride groundwater.
venue: Water Analysis Letters

title: Comparative Assessment of Absorbance-Based and Reflectance-Based Portable Platforms for Manganese Determination in Drinking Water Sources
abstract: Portable manganese detection is important in regions where reducing aquifer conditions mobilise Mn(II) above drinking-water limits. This study compared three commercially available portable platforms — two absorbance-mode photometers and one reflectance-mode test-strip reader — for the determination of total dissolved manganese using the formaldoxime and periodate oxidation procedures. Calibrations were constructed in deionised water and in two synthetic groundwater matrices (low hardness: 150 mg/L as CaCO3; high hardness: 550 mg/L as CaCO3). In high-hardness matrix, the periodate procedure showed a positive bias of 7–13% on the absorbance platforms that was absent in low-hardness conditions, associated with partial precipitation of calcium periodate scattering at 525 nm. The formaldoxime procedure was unaffected by hardness up to 550 mg/L. The reflectance-based strip reader showed higher variability (RSD 8–15%) but was unaffected by solution turbidity. Thirty-two real samples from municipal well fields in the southern Bačka District were analysed; results from the formaldoxime absorbance method agreed with ICP-OES reference values within 4.5%.

title: Simultaneous Correction for Turbidity, Alkalinity, and Hardness in a Multi-Analyte Portable Photometric Protocol for Groundwater Quality Surveys
abstract: Field surveys requiring simultaneous measurement of iron, manganese, phosphate, and ammonium in a single sampling event are constrained by limited time and reagent volume. This work presents a sequential analytical protocol optimised for a single-operator field campaign using one portable eight-wavelength spectrophotometer. The protocol incorporates a unified pre-measurement correction step: (1) a 700 nm turbidity reading on each sample before reagent addition, (2) a rapid EDTA titration for total hardness, and (3) an alkalinity estimate from field pH and conductivity using an empirical calibration model developed for Vojvodina aquifer chemistry. Correction factors for each of the four analytes were parameterised using 144 synthetic matrices covering the relevant ranges of all three interferents. The corrected protocol was validated against laboratory ICP-OES and ion chromatography results for 46 groundwater samples from 12 monitoring well clusters. Median absolute percentage errors were 3.1% (Fe), 4.0% (Mn), 3.8% (PO4-P), and 2.9% (NH4-N). The protocol requires approximately 22 minutes per sample, a reasonable field rate for four-analyte work.

title: Influence of Dissolved Organic Carbon Character on the Molybdenum Blue Reaction: Humic Versus Fulvic Acid Fractions in Deep Alluvial Aquifer Samples
abstract: Deep alluvial aquifers in the Pannonian Basin frequently contain elevated dissolved organic carbon (DOC) of natural origin, primarily humic substances. The influence of humic versus fulvic acid fractions on the molybdenum blue phosphate determination has not been distinguished in prior work. Humic acid (HA) and fulvic acid (FA) standards were added at 1, 5, 10, and 25 mg/L DOC to synthetic matrices at two phosphate levels (0.1 and 1.0 mg/L PO4-P) with background alkalinity of 450 mg/L and hardness of 380 mg/L as CaCO3. HA at 10 mg/L suppressed the molybdenum blue signal by 11% at 880 nm, while FA at the same concentration suppressed it by only 4%. The suppression was partially reversed by UV-photooxidation (30-minute UV irradiation at 254 nm) before reagent addition, reducing HA interference to 2.5%. Sixty-three samples from deep monitoring wells (80–220 m depth) in the Banat region were analysed with and without UV pre-treatment; the pre-treatment affected results in 34% of samples by more than 5%, indicating meaningful DOC interference in that subset.

title: Arsenic Field Screening in High-Bicarbonate Groundwater: Evaluation of Four Portable Colorimetric Methods Against Hydride-Generation AAS Reference Values
abstract: Arsenic contamination in drinking water drawn from reducing alluvial aquifers is a documented public-health issue in southern Pannonia. Field screening methods for arsenic must function reliably in the same high-bicarbonate, high-hardness matrices that challenge other colorimetric procedures. This study evaluated four commercially marketed portable arsenic test kits — all based on variants of the silver diethyldithiocarbamate (SDDC) or arsine-generation colorimetric approaches — against reference measurements by hydride-generation atomic absorption spectrometry (HG-AAS) in 55 groundwater samples from arsenic-affected well fields in the Banat Plain. Samples were grouped by alkalinity (<300, 300–500, >500 mg/L CaCO3) and hardness (<200, 200–400, >400 mg/L CaCO3). At alkalinity above 500 mg/L, two of four kits showed false-negative rates exceeding 20% at 10 µg/L As, the WHO guideline value. Hydrogen sulfide co-interference, generated in reducing samples, caused additional positive bias in two kits. Recommendations for pre-treatment and result interpretation specific to the regional matrix are provided, including a bicarbonate pre-removal step using acidification and degassing.

title: Speciation-Aware Correction for Iron in Field Photometric Analysis: Accounting for Fe(II)/Fe(III) Partitioning Under Varying Redox and pH in High-Alkalinity Groundwater
abstract: Dissolved iron in groundwater is distributed between Fe(II) and Fe(III) in proportions governed by redox potential and pH. The 1,10-phenanthroline method measures only Fe(II); total iron requires prior reduction. In high-alkalinity samples, partial precipitation of Fe(III) as colloidal iron hydroxide occurs before and during analysis, causing negative bias in total iron results unless samples are immediately acidified. This study combined field Eh and pH measurements with laboratory Fe(II), Fe(III), and total iron determinations by ICP-OES and spectrophotometry to characterise the Fe speciation in 80 samples from 20 monitoring wells in the Bačka Palanka and Apatin areas. At pH above 7.5 and alkalinity above 350 mg/L, Fe(III) precipitation within 5 minutes of sampling accounted for losses of 12–38% of total iron from the dissolved fraction. A speciation correction algorithm taking field Eh, pH, alkalinity, and immediate Fe(II) measurement as inputs was developed; median agreement with ICP-OES total iron improved from 18.4% error to 4.7% error after correction. Practical implications for well-head sampling protocols are discussed.

title: Kriging-based nitrogen prescription maps for winter wheat on chernozem soils of Vojvodina: accuracy versus sampling density
abstract: Variable-rate nitrogen application requires spatially continuous estimates of soil mineral nitrogen from discrete point observations. This study evaluated ordinary kriging, co-kriging with apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) as a covariate, and inverse-distance weighting at four sampling densities (1, 2, 4, and 8 ha per sample) across three commercial fields totalling 340 ha on Vojvodina chernozem. Variogram parameters were fitted for each field and density level; cross-validation mean absolute error (MAE) and prescription rate deviation were used as criteria. Co-kriging with ECa reduced MAE by 18–31% relative to ordinary kriging at the 4 ha per sample density, allowing prescription maps of comparable quality to the 2 ha benchmark at substantially lower cost. The resulting variable-rate N prescriptions differed from uniform-rate recommendations by up to 38 kg N ha⁻¹ within individual fields. The study provides practical sampling guidelines for advisory services operating on Vojvodina chernozem.

title: Integrating historical yield maps into phosphorus prescription models: a five-year case study in sunflower production
abstract: Phosphorus prescription in intensive sunflower production typically relies on single-year soil test data, which may not capture the long-term spatial structure of yield response. This study used five consecutive yield maps (2008–2012) from four commercial sunflower fields (total 480 ha) in South Bačka to derive stable yield response zones. Temporal stability analysis identified consistently low-yielding (14% of area) and consistently high-yielding (22% of area) zones. These zones were overlaid with current Olsen-P maps to produce a two-factor phosphorus prescription: standard soil-test-based rates adjusted by a yield-stability coefficient ranging from 0.75 to 1.25. A randomised strip trial in year six showed a 6.4% improvement in economic return compared with uniform application at the field average. The study demonstrates a practical method for incorporating multi-year yield data into routine prescription generation.

title: Spatial modelling of herbicide prescription rates in maize based on soil organic matter and texture gradients
abstract: Pre-emergence herbicide efficacy depends on soil organic matter and clay content because both affect adsorption and bioavailability. This study developed a spatially explicit prescription algorithm for two pre-emergence herbicide active substances (acetochlor and atrazine) applied to maize across twelve fields (1 650 ha) in the Srem sub-region. Soil organic matter was estimated by near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy on 2 ha grid samples; clay content was predicted from ECa using field-calibrated transfer functions. A published adsorption model was parameterised with local soil data and used to compute spatially variable application rates that achieve a uniform herbicide concentration in soil solution. Rates varied by 28% and 34% across fields for the two active substances respectively. Post-emergence assessment at 35 days after application showed weed cover was statistically equivalent between variable-rate and the high-rate uniform standard, while active substance use was reduced by 19% on average.

title: Comparison of semivariogram model families for describing ECa spatial structure in heterogeneous Vojvodina fields
abstract: Choice of semivariogram model affects the quality of spatial interpolation and, downstream, the precision of prescription maps. Using ECa data collected with an EM38 sensor along parallel transects at 12 m spacing across 30 fields (ranging from 25 to 280 ha) in Vojvodina, this study fitted spherical, exponential, Gaussian, and Matérn (κ = 1.5 and 2.5) semivariogram models and compared them by leave-one-out cross-validation RMSE and by the resulting prescription map entropy. Range parameters varied from 54 m to 312 m across fields. The Matérn κ = 1.5 model produced the lowest cross-validation RMSE in 18 of 30 fields, closely followed by the exponential in 9 fields. Prescription map entropy differences between model families were small (< 4%) when the optimal model was selected per field, but using a fixed spherical model throughout increased mean prescription deviation by 7.2 kg N ha⁻¹ across the dataset. Practical guidance for model selection is provided.

title: Soil variability indices for parameterising prescription algorithms: a comparative assessment of ECa, gamma-ray spectrometry, and vis-NIR scanning
abstract: Three proximal soil sensing methods were compared as inputs for management-zone delineation and prescription map parameterisation on 15 fields (total 1 870 ha) in Vojvodina. Apparent electrical conductivity (EM38 dual-depth), vehicle-mounted gamma-ray spectrometry (total count, potassium, uranium, thorium channels), and vis-NIR scanning of intact cores (350–2 500 nm) were each used to predict clay content, organic matter, and Olsen-P by partial least-squares regression with leave-one-out cross-validation. Gamma-ray potassium channel alone achieved an R² of 0.74 for clay and 0.69 for organic matter prediction, competitive with EM38 dual-depth (0.77 and 0.66 respectively). Vis-NIR performed best overall for organic matter (R² 0.81) but was the most time-consuming. A cost-per-hectare analysis suggested that gamma-ray spectrometry offers the best trade-off for large commercial holdings (> 100 ha per field), while vis-NIR justifies its cost for high-value horticultural fields. Prescription maps generated from all three sensor inputs agreed within 12 kg N ha⁻¹ on 80% of the mapped area.

title: Steady-state modelling of a two-stage reciprocating air compressor under variable inlet conditions
abstract: This paper presents a steady-state thermodynamic model of a two-stage reciprocating air compressor intended for use in light manufacturing facilities. The model accounts for variable ambient temperature and humidity at the compressor inlet, heat exchanger effectiveness between stages, and mechanical losses estimated from catalogue data for four commercial units rated between 7.5 and 22 kW. Validation was carried out against 14 months of sub-hourly logged data from a metalworking plant near Novi Sad, comprising over 9 000 operating hours. The specific energy consumption predicted by the model agreed with measurements within 3.1% across the full load range. Sensitivity analysis showed that inlet temperature variation of ±10 °C produced specific energy deviations of up to 4.8%, which is practically significant for outdoor-air-cooled installations. The validated model is offered as a building block for larger system-level simulations of compressed-air utility networks.

title: Energy audit of a centralised compressed-air network in a food-processing facility: losses, leakage fraction and savings potential
abstract: A detailed energy audit of a centralised compressed-air system supplying a dairy processing plant with a peak demand of approximately 1 200 m³/h at 7 bar was conducted over six weeks during winter and summer operating periods. Ultrasonic leak detection identified 34 individual leak points accounting for an estimated 17% of total compressed-air generation. Pressure drop mapping across the distribution network revealed an additional 0.8 bar avoidable pressure loss attributable to undersized pipe sections installed during a capacity expansion. The audit protocol combined portable flow measurement, compressor electrical sub-metering and manual operating logs. The total identified saving potential was equivalent to 138 MWh per year, corresponding to roughly 11% of the system's annual electricity consumption. Proposed corrective measures are costed and prioritised according to simple payback period, with the leak-repair programme returning investment within five months.

title: Simulation of a small rooftop photovoltaic system coupled to a single-zone cold-storage room: annual energy balance
abstract: A TRNSYS-based simulation study examines the annual energy balance of a 12 kWp rooftop photovoltaic array directly coupled to a single-zone cold-storage room maintained at −18 °C and located in the continental climate of Vojvodina. Hourly irradiation and temperature data from the Rimski Šančevi meteorological station covering the years 2008–2012 were used as boundary conditions. The refrigeration system was modelled using a catalogue-fitted vapour-compression cycle with a variable-speed compressor. Results show that direct PV generation covers 31–38% of annual cooling electricity demand depending on year and operating schedule, with the highest offset occurring in July when peak irradiation coincides with peak refrigeration load. Grid interaction profiles are presented and the potential for demand-side shifting by pre-cooling is quantified at 8–14% additional PV utilisation without battery storage.

title: Characterisation of PV output variability and its effect on demand-peak coincidence in a small industrial park
abstract: Measured one-minute irradiance and PV output data from three rooftop arrays (7, 11 and 18 kWp) installed at an industrial park in Novi Sad were analysed over two full calendar years (2018–2019) to characterise output variability and its statistical relationship to afternoon demand peaks. The variability index, defined as the standard deviation of one-minute ramp rates normalised by rated capacity, averaged 0.031 min⁻¹ in summer and 0.058 min⁻¹ in winter. Cross-correlation between aggregated PV output and the grid demand peaks billed under the local distribution tariff showed that PV generation offset the dominant peak-demand interval on only 38% of weekdays in summer, because afternoon storms regularly suppress generation during peak hours. The findings suggest that demand-peak reduction through PV alone is unreliable without coordinated load-shifting of deferrable loads such as compressors and chillers.

title: Sizing photovoltaic generation and compressed-air storage for peak-demand capping in a medium-voltage industrial consumer
abstract: This work addresses the joint sizing problem for a rooftop PV array and an additional compressed-air storage vessel intended to cap the 15-minute demand peaks of a medium-voltage industrial consumer subject to capacity-based tariff charges. A mixed-integer linear programme is formulated with PV capacity (kWp), additional receiver volume (m³), and an hourly dispatch schedule as decision variables, minimising total annualised cost including capital and tariff charges over a 20-year horizon. Fourteen years of hourly irradiation data from PVGIS and five years of measured load data from a rubber-products factory in Sremska Mitrovica were used. Pareto-optimal solutions indicate that a 48 kWp array combined with 6 000 litres of additional receiver capacity reduces annual tariff expenditure by 22% at a net present value break-even of 8.3 years. Sensitivity to future electricity price trajectories is discussed.

title: Енергетски профил малих и средњих предузећа у Војводини: анализа структуре потрошње електричне енергије на узорку 42 предузећа
abstract: Истраживање представља резултате структуриране енергетске анализе спроведене на 42 мала и средња предузећа у Војводини у периоду 2020–2022. године. Подаци су прикупљени кроз стандардизовани упитник и верификовани увидом у рачуне за електричну енергију и, у 19 случајева, кроз мерење подоптерећења. Резултати показују да системи компримованог ваздуха чине у просеку 23% укупне потрошње електричне енергије у прерађивачким предузећима, а расхладна постројења додатних 18%. Удео трошкова обрачунске снаге у укупном рачуну варира између 12 и 31% у зависности од карактеристика оптерећења. Идентификовано је да свега 7 од 42 предузећа примењује неки облик управљања вршним оптерећењем. Резултати пружају статистичку основу за процену потенцијала примене аутоматизованих решења за управљање потрошњом у регионалном контексту.

title: Co-simulation framework for photovoltaic generation, compressed-air networks and refrigeration loads with shared electrical bus: methodology and case study
abstract: A co-simulation framework linking three specialist tools—PVsyst for photovoltaic generation, a custom compressed-air network solver written in Python, and a Modelica refrigeration model—via a shared electrical bus object is described and applied to a case study involving a beverage packaging plant. The bus object handles bi-directional power flows and enforces grid import constraints at five-minute resolution. The framework was used to evaluate 96 combinations of PV capacity (0–60 kWp), additional air receiver volume (0–8 000 litres), and chilled-water buffer tank volume (0–10 m³) against a two-part tariff with a coincident peak demand charge. The Pareto frontier of annualised cost versus peak demand reduction was mapped across all configurations. Key finding: chilled-water buffering contributed more to peak reduction per euro of capital than compressed-air buffering at the studied site, due to a stronger coincidence between refrigeration load and tariff peak windows.

title: Effect of groundwater flow on long-term borehole field thermal performance: a 3D finite-element study calibrated to Vojvodina aquifer conditions
abstract: Groundwater advection in aquifer layers can substantially alter the thermal plume around a borehole field, either flushing away accumulated cold (or heat) or distributing it along the flow direction. Standard g-function methods ignore advection. This paper presents a 3D finite-element model of a 16-borehole field embedded in a two-layer stratigraphy representative of shallow Vojvodina aquifer conditions: a low-permeability clay overburden underlain by a confined sandy aquifer with a measured hydraulic gradient of 0.0008 m/m and estimated pore velocity of 0.4 m/day. The model is implemented in a commercial finite-element solver and coupled to a borehole resistance network. Over a 20-year simulation with residential heating-dominated loads, groundwater advection reduces the mean borehole wall temperature depression by 35 % compared to the pure-conduction case, a significant effect that is poorly captured by any of the analytical correction methods tested. Sensitivity to hydraulic conductivity uncertainty is assessed by Monte Carlo sampling of a log-normal conductivity distribution.
venue: Geothermics

title: Synthesis and cytotoxic evaluation of aroylhydrazones derived from 2-acetylpyridine against HCT 116 colorectal carcinoma cells
abstract: A series of twelve 2-acetylpyridine-derived aroylhydrazones was prepared through condensation of 2-acetylpyridine with various aromatic acid hydrazides under reflux conditions in ethanol. Structures were confirmed by 1H and 13C NMR, IR spectroscopy, and elemental analysis. Cytotoxicity was assessed against the HCT 116 human colorectal carcinoma cell line and the non-malignant HEK-293 cell line using the MTT assay at 72-hour exposure. IC50 values ranged from 4.3 to 68.7 µM; the most active compound, bearing a 4-chloro substituent on the aroyl ring, showed IC50 = 4.3 µM against HCT 116 with approximately 6-fold selectivity over HEK-293. Selectivity indices across the series correlated with electron-withdrawing substituent character assessed by Hammett sigma constants. Lipophilicity calculated as logP ranged from 1.8 to 3.4. These preliminary results suggest that halogen substitution at the para position of the aroyl fragment is a productive direction for further structural optimisation targeting colorectal cancer.

title: Acid-catalysed condensation pathways for salicylaldehyde hydrazones: reaction optimisation and structural characterisation
abstract: Formation of salicylaldehyde-derived hydrazones was studied under varied acid catalysis conditions (HCl, AcOH, TFA) in aqueous ethanol to identify optimal protocols for E/Z isomer control. Ten derivatives were prepared from four hydrazide precursors. Reaction progress was monitored by TLC and in-line HPLC. 1H NMR integration of the imine proton region in DMSO-d6 confirmed predominant E-isomer formation (>92%) in all cases when glacial acetic acid was used as catalyst at 0.1 equiv loading and 60 °C. Crystal structures of two derivatives were obtained by X-ray diffraction, confirming intramolecular O–H···N hydrogen bonding that stabilises the E configuration. Melting points, logP values estimated by reversed-phase HPLC, and molar absorptivity data are tabulated. The work provides a reproducible synthetic protocol applicable to libraries intended for biological screening, with emphasis on isomeric purity as a prerequisite for meaningful structure–activity interpretation.

title: Comparative cytotoxicity of thiosemicarbazone and hydrazone analogues against SW480 and SW620 paired colorectal cancer lines
abstract: Matched pairs of thiosemicarbazone and hydrazone derivatives sharing identical acyl fragments were synthesised and tested in parallel against the isogenic SW480 (primary tumour) and SW620 (metastatic lymph node) human colorectal cell lines to assess both potency and model-specificity. Eighteen compounds were prepared; purity was confirmed at >98% by HPLC-UV. The MTT assay at 48 and 72 hours revealed that thiosemicarbazones were generally more active (mean IC50 at 72 h: 9.1 µM versus 18.4 µM for hydrazones against SW480), though three hydrazones bearing a 3,4-dichlorophenyl group showed IC50 values below 7 µM. SW620 displayed uniformly higher resistance; fold-resistance ranged from 1.2 to 3.8. Cell morphology changes consistent with early apoptosis were observed by phase-contrast microscopy at sub-IC50 concentrations for the two most active compounds. The findings support further mechanistic study of the dichlorophenyl hydrazone scaffold in metastatic models.

title: Flow cytometric analysis of apoptosis and cell cycle perturbation induced by a 3,4-dichlorophenyl hydrazone in HCT 116 cells
abstract: Following earlier cytotoxicity screening, the 3,4-dichlorophenyl hydrazone designated compound BÉ-14 was selected for mechanistic investigation. HCT 116 cells were treated at IC25, IC50, and IC75 concentrations (determined at 72 h) for 24 and 48 hours. Apoptosis was quantified by Annexin V/propidium iodide double staining and flow cytometry; cell cycle distribution was assessed by PI staining after RNase treatment. At IC50 and 48 hours, early apoptosis accounted for 21.4 ± 2.1% of the cell population versus 5.8 ± 0.7% in the vehicle control. Sub-G1 fraction increased from 3.1% to 14.7% at IC75. G2/M arrest was observed at the IC25 concentration at 24 hours (37.2% versus 18.9% in controls). Caspase-3 activity measured by colorimetric substrate cleavage was elevated 3.4-fold at IC50/48 h. These data indicate a caspase-dependent apoptotic mechanism with concurrent cell cycle interference for BÉ-14.

title: Hydrazone derivatives in anticancer drug discovery: synthetic strategies and biological profiles
abstract: This chapter surveys published synthetic routes to hydrazone-based cytotoxic agents reported between 2000 and 2015, with attention to condensation protocols, catalytic methods, and microwave-assisted procedures. Biological evaluation strategies discussed include MTT/MTS proliferation assays, flow cytometric apoptosis measurement, and xenograft mouse models. Structure–activity trends are analysed across compound classes grouped by the carbonyl component: aromatic aldehydes, heteroaromatic ketones, and acylhydrazides. Selectivity toward cancer versus non-malignant cell lines is discussed in relation to logP, planarity, and metal-chelating potential. The role of E/Z isomerism in biological variability is addressed as a methodological concern. Case studies from the authors' own data on colorectal cancer models are integrated throughout. The chapter is intended to serve as a practical reference for researchers entering the field, providing both reaction conditions and suggested assay workflows with quality benchmarks.

title: Interactions of hydrazone derivatives with bovine serum albumin studied by fluorescence spectroscopy and molecular docking
abstract: Binding of six cytotoxic hydrazone derivatives to bovine serum albumin (BSA) was characterised by steady-state fluorescence quenching at three temperatures (298, 304, 310 K). Static quenching was confirmed by the temperature dependence of Stern-Volmer constants (Ksv decreased with increasing temperature). Binding constants Ka ranged from 1.2 × 10^4 to 8.7 × 10^4 M−1, and the number of binding sites n was close to 1.0 for all compounds. Thermodynamic parameters calculated from van't Hoff plots indicated that binding was predominantly driven by hydrophobic interactions for five compounds (ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0) and by hydrogen bonding for one outlier. Molecular docking into BSA subdomain IIA (Sudlow site I) using an AutoDock-based protocol reproduced the experimental binding rank order (Spearman ρ = 0.83). These data support the utility of BSA fluorescence quenching as an early-stage predictor of plasma protein binding propensity in this compound class.

title: Quantitative structure–cytotoxicity relationships for a heterogeneous hydrazone dataset using random forest and multiple linear regression
abstract: A compiled dataset of 87 hydrazone derivatives tested against HCT 116 in the authors' laboratory over eight years was used to build QSAR models predicting pIC50. Molecular descriptors were calculated using PaDEL-Descriptor software (version 2.21); 1,444 descriptors were reduced to 22 informative features by recursive feature elimination. Random forest (RF) and multiple linear regression (MLR) models were built on a 70/30 train-test split with five-fold cross-validation. RF outperformed MLR on the test set (R2test = 0.76, RMSEtest = 0.41 versus R2test = 0.61, RMSEtest = 0.58). The five most important descriptors by mean decrease in impurity were related to topological surface area, ring count, and halogen electronegativity-weighted atom counts. Applicability domain was assessed by Williams plot; 11 compounds fell outside the domain. The validated RF model was used to virtually screen 320 commercial hydrazide precursors, nominating 18 as synthesis candidates with predicted IC50 < 5 µM.

title: Synthesis and antiproliferative activity of fluorinated benzaldehyde hydrazones predicted by QSAR virtual screening
abstract: Eighteen fluorinated benzaldehyde-derived hydrazones nominated by a random forest QSAR model were synthesised and evaluated against HCT 116, CRC SW480, and non-malignant CCD-18Co cells. All 18 compounds were prepared in 2–4 synthetic steps; purity exceeded 95% by HPLC for 16 of them. IC50 values against HCT 116 at 72 hours ranged from 2.1 to 41.4 µM; 11 compounds matched the model prediction within one log unit. The best compound (BÉ-F7, IC50 = 2.1 µM vs HCT 116) showed SI = 9.4 over CCD-18Co. QSAR predictions were less accurate for SW480 (R2 between predicted and observed pIC50 = 0.49), highlighting limits of cross-line model transfer. BÉ-F7 was further characterised by Annexin V staining, showing 31.8% early apoptosis at IC50 concentration after 48 hours. Reactive oxygen species generation measured by DCFH-DA fluorescence was elevated 2.9-fold versus vehicle, suggesting oxidative stress involvement.

title: 3D tumour spheroid models for cytotoxicity testing of hydrazone candidates: comparison with monolayer results for a reference compound set
abstract: Three-dimensional spheroid cultures of HCT 116 were established in ultra-low attachment 96-well plates and grown to mean diameters of 380–420 µm before treatment. Fifteen hydrazone compounds previously characterised in 2D monolayer assays were re-evaluated in the spheroid model at 72- and 120-hour endpoints using the ATP-based luminescence viability assay. IC50 values in spheroids were uniformly higher than in monolayer: the ratio ranged from 1.7- to 9.3-fold, with the largest resistance factors observed for the most hydrophilic compounds (logP < 1.5). BÉ-F7 showed a 2.4-fold spheroid-to-monolayer IC50 ratio, the most favourable in the set. Spheroid cross-sections stained with Ki-67 and cleaved caspase-3 antibodies confirmed a necrotic core and a proliferating outer rim in untreated controls, and BÉ-F7 treatment reduced Ki-67 area by 47% at IC50. This work identifies penetration-dependent resistance as a key variable for further optimisation.

title: Stress–strain characterisation of expanded polystyrene foam under quasi-static and dynamic compressive loading
abstract: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) specimens of three densities (15, 20, and 30 kg/m³) were tested under quasi-static compression at 10 mm/min and dynamic loading at strain rates between 10 and 200 s⁻¹ using a split Hopkinson pressure bar apparatus. Engineering stress–strain curves revealed a pronounced rate sensitivity: plateau stress increased by 35–55% across the tested density range when strain rate was raised from quasi-static to 200 s⁻¹. Volumetric energy absorption was computed for each condition. A piecewise constitutive model with three regions—linear elastic, plateau, and densification—was calibrated and implemented in Abaqus/Explicit. Simulation of a 600 g instrumented impactor dropped from 750 mm onto a 50 mm thick EPS pad matched measured peak acceleration within 8% for all three densities. The data set provides baseline material parameters for subsequent cushioning design work and is made available as supplementary material.

title: Finite element simulation of cushioning system performance for a fragile electronic product subjected to a standard drop sequence
abstract: A cushioning system for a 1.2 kg portable measurement instrument was designed analytically using classical fragility theory and then evaluated using a three-dimensional Abaqus/Explicit model. The product was idealised as a rigid body with a single fragile element represented by a linear spring–dashpot pair, with a critical acceleration threshold of 60 G established from component supplier data. The EPS cushion geometry was parameterised by pad thickness (40–80 mm) and density (20–25 kg/m³). Drop simulations at 900 mm onto a rigid surface reproduced the six-face, two-edge, and one-corner orientations required by ISTA 2A. Corner impacts consistently produced the highest transmitted accelerations—on average 18% above equivalent face drops—highlighting the need for corner geometry optimisation. Optimal pad thickness was identified as 65 mm at 22 kg/m³, reducing simulated peak acceleration below the 60 G threshold for all orientations. Prototype pads were manufactured and validated experimentally, with agreement within 12%.

title: Comparative evaluation of EPS, EPE, and moulded pulp as protective packaging materials under repeated drop loading
abstract: Three packaging materials—expanded polystyrene (EPS, 20 kg/m³), expanded polyethylene (EPE, 30 kg/m³), and moulded pulp (density 320 kg/m³, wall thickness 4 mm)—were subjected to repeated drop sequences of 30 impacts from 750 mm using a 1.5 kg guided impactor. Transmitted peak acceleration, dynamic cushioning curve, and dimensional recovery were recorded after every fifth drop. EPS showed the greatest degradation: plateau stress dropped by 22% and peak transmitted acceleration increased by 18 G over 30 drops, with visible cell crushing evident in cross-section images. EPE exhibited superior recovery, retaining 91% of initial energy absorption after 30 drops. Moulded pulp performed comparably to EPE in the first 15 drops but degraded rapidly thereafter due to fibre delamination. Scanning electron microscopy images are presented for each material at 0, 15, and 30 drops. The results have practical implications for reusable and returnable packaging system design.

title: Measurement and statistical characterisation of shock pulses occurring in road parcel distribution in Serbia and Romania
abstract: Field data on shock events experienced by parcels during road distribution were collected using tri-axial data loggers (sampling rate 3200 Hz, range ±200 G) deployed inside 60 instrumented test packages of 2 and 5 kg nominal weight, distributed over 48 routes across Serbia and Romania during autumn and winter seasons. A total of 14,720 shock events exceeding 3 G in any axis were recorded and analysed. Median peak acceleration was 8.4 G; the 95th percentile was 31.2 G, with a maximum recorded event of 78 G associated with a loading-dock impact. Vertical axis events dominated in frequency (61%) but horizontal impacts produced higher peak magnitudes on average. Extreme value analysis using the generalised extreme value distribution produced design shock levels for three packaging performance tiers. The data set supplements existing ISTA and ASTM reference distributions, which are predominantly derived from North American and Western European logistics chains.

title: Design and FE validation of a geometrically optimised EPS corner pad for consumer electronics packaging
abstract: Corner pads represent the most mechanically demanding component of a standard consumer electronics cushioning system because they must absorb energy from both face and edge drop orientations simultaneously. This paper describes the geometry optimisation of an EPS corner pad for a 1.8 kg tablet computer package using parametric finite element analysis in Abaqus/Explicit. Seven geometric parameters—including wall thickness, rib configuration, and fillet radii—were varied in a full factorial screening design with 128 simulations, followed by a gradient-based optimisation of the three most influential parameters identified by sensitivity analysis. The optimised geometry reduced peak transmitted acceleration in the 45° corner drop from 74 G to 52 G while reducing pad mass by 9% relative to the baseline design. The optimised pads were manufactured by a regional EPS moulding supplier and validated experimentally; peak accelerations agreed within 7% for all five drop orientations tested.

title: Material parameter identification for expanded polyurethane foam using inverse finite element analysis and drop-test data
abstract: Expanded polyurethane (EPU) foam used in automotive and electronics packaging is difficult to characterise through quasi-static testing alone because its response to high-rate shock loading differs substantially from low-rate behaviour. An inverse identification procedure was developed in which material parameters of a crushable foam plasticity model in Abaqus/Explicit were iteratively adjusted to minimise the discrepancy between simulated and experimentally measured acceleration–time histories from instrumented drop tests. Seventeen drop tests at four heights (300–1200 mm) and two impactor weights (0.8 and 2.2 kg) on three EPU densities (40, 60, and 80 kg/m³) were used as the calibration data set; nine additional tests formed the validation set. The optimised parameters reproduced validation peak accelerations within 9% and pulse duration within 11%. Sensitivity of identified parameters to measurement noise was assessed using bootstrap resampling, confirming robust convergence for all three densities.

title: Bio-based and recycled-content foams as EPS substitutes in protective packaging: mechanical performance comparison
abstract: Regulatory pressure and corporate sustainability targets are driving interest in bio-based and recycled-content foam alternatives to conventional EPS. This study characterises four candidate materials—mycelium composite foam (MCF), expanded starch–polylactic acid blend (sPLA), recycled EPS regrind at 85% content (rEPS), and expanded cork agglomerate—against a reference EPS grade (20 kg/m³) using quasi-static compression, dynamic Hopkinson bar testing, and drop-test validation. All four alternatives showed lower plateau stress than reference EPS at equivalent apparent density, requiring 15–40% greater pad thickness to achieve equivalent cushioning performance. MCF exhibited the most consistent energy absorption across strain rates but had the highest density (38 kg/m³), leading to a 55% mass penalty per pad. Cork agglomerate performed best in repeated-impact durability among alternatives, retaining 85% of initial energy absorption after 20 drops. A performance index combining cushioning efficiency, mass, and recyclability is proposed for comparative material selection.

title: Influence of ventilation holes on the cushioning performance of EPS pads: experimental and numerical study
abstract: Ventilation holes are routinely included in EPS cushioning pads to reduce internal air pressure build-up during dynamic compression, but their effect on peak transmitted acceleration and energy absorption is not well documented quantitatively. This study examined square arrays of circular holes (diameter 5–15 mm, pitch 20–40 mm) machined into 50 mm thick EPS pads (20 kg/m³) and tested under drop loading with a 1.2 kg impactor from 600 mm. Instrumented drop tests showed that hole areas exceeding 12% of pad face area reduced plateau stress by up to 17%, shifting the cushion curve upward and increasing peak transmitted acceleration. Abaqus/Explicit simulations incorporating a porous media gas flow model captured this trend with a mean absolute error of 2.1 G. Finite element results were used to generate a design chart relating hole area fraction, pad thickness, and peak acceleration for practical use by packaging engineers.

title: Predicting accumulated product damage over a multi-drop distribution cycle using a probabilistic fragility model
abstract: Standard cushioning qualification tests treat each drop event independently, ignoring accumulated damage to both product and packaging over a complete distribution cycle. This paper presents a probabilistic framework in which product fragility is modelled as a degrading threshold drawn from a log-normal distribution, and shock events over a simulated 500-package distribution cycle are sampled from the empirical field distribution measured in a prior study. Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 cycles was used to estimate the probability of product damage as a function of cushion design parameters. A two-parameter cushion design space (pad thickness and density) was mapped to iso-damage-probability contours, providing a direct tool for specifying packaging to target a defined damage rate. The framework was illustrated for a 2.0 kg medical diagnostic device with a critical acceleration of 45 G. Sensitivity analysis showed that uncertainty in the fragility threshold dominates overall damage probability uncertainty, motivating better experimental fragility characterisation.

title: Vapour permeability of aged elastomeric seals: comparison of EPDM, silicone, and thermoplastic polyurethane after thermal and UV ageing
abstract: Vapour permeability was measured for EPDM, silicone, and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) seal materials in unaged condition and after accelerated thermal ageing (100 °C, 1000 hours) and UV ageing (1.0 W/m² at 340 nm, 500 hours) in accordance with ISO 4892-2. Gravimetric cup tests at 23 °C and 85 % relative humidity differential were conducted on three specimens per material per ageing condition. EPDM permeability increased by 12 % after thermal ageing and by 8 % after UV ageing relative to the unaged baseline. Silicone showed no statistically significant change after thermal ageing but a 19 % increase after UV ageing. TPU exhibited the largest sensitivity, with permeability increasing by 34 % after thermal ageing and 27 % after UV ageing, accompanied by visible surface crazing and a 15 % reduction in hardness. Shore A hardness, tensile elongation at break, and infrared spectroscopy were used to characterise degradation mechanisms. The results indicate that TPU is not recommended for long-service-life outdoor enclosures exposed to solar radiation.

title: Workstation Layout Benchmarking for Printed Circuit Board Disassembly: A Time Study at Three Serbian Collection Centres
abstract: This study conducted structured time-and-motion observations at three end-of-life electronics collection centres in Vojvodina to benchmark current workstation layouts for manual printed circuit board disassembly. Using a combination of direct stopwatch study and predetermined motion time system (MTM-UAS) coding, 1 240 individual task cycles were recorded across 18 operators. Results showed that average cycle time varied by 34% between the best- and worst-performing stations, with non-value-adding reach and reposition motions accounting for 41% of total cycle time at poorly arranged benches. A revised workstation layout incorporating a fixed tool shadow board and a gravity-fed component tray was proposed and piloted at one site, reducing average cycle time by 18% and peak wrist deviation angle from 28° to 14°. The findings indicate that systematic layout analysis can simultaneously improve throughput and reduce musculoskeletal loading without capital investment in automation.

title: Applying the RULA Method to End-of-Life Appliance Disassembly Tasks: Posture Scoring Across Four Product Categories
abstract: Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) was applied to 64 disassembly tasks drawn from four product categories—washing machines, microwave ovens, desktop computers, and small power tools—at a certified reverse-logistics facility near Subotica, Serbia. Video recordings of 12 experienced operators were coded frame-by-frame using standardised RULA worksheets. Tasks were grouped by fastener type, component mass, and access geometry. Mean RULA scores ranged from 3.1 for small power-tool casings to 6.4 for washing-machine motor extraction, where sustained awkward shoulder abduction was predominant. Correlation analysis showed fastener access depth to be the strongest predictor of RULA score (r = 0.71, p < 0.01), ahead of component mass and operator height. The study provides a ranked risk register for six of the eleven task families examined, which was used to prioritise ergonomic redesign interventions. Recommendations include angled fixture holders and adjustable-height benches for the highest-risk tasks.

title: Disassembly Line Balancing Under Stochastic Task Times: A Comparison of Ranked Positional Weight and Simulated Annealing Heuristics
abstract: Disassembly line balancing differs from assembly balancing because task precedence is shaped by physical accessibility constraints and task times are more variable due to corrosion, fastener stripping, and operator experience differences. This paper examines 26 real task networks collected from an end-of-life mobile phone disassembly line operated by a Novi Sad-based reverse-logistics company. Task time distributions were fitted to lognormal models using maximum-likelihood estimation on 800 observations per task. Ranked positional weight (RPW) and simulated annealing (SA) heuristics were both applied under deterministic mean times and then re-evaluated via Monte Carlo simulation with 10 000 replications. SA produced workstation configurations with 12% lower variance in cycle time across simulations compared to RPW, though mean throughput differences were under 3%. The paper discusses how variability metrics, not only mean balance efficiency, should be used when selecting balancing heuristics for disassembly contexts with high task-time dispersion.

title: Ergonomics in Reverse Logistics: A Review of Workplace Design Practices in End-of-Life Facilities in Central and Eastern Europe
abstract: This chapter reviews published studies and grey literature on ergonomic workplace design practices in end-of-life processing and reverse-logistics facilities across Central and Eastern Europe, covering the period 2005–2022. Sources were identified through a structured literature search in three databases, yielding 54 papers and 12 industry reports after screening. The review finds that ergonomic interventions in this sector cluster around three themes: adjustable-height workstations, material presentation systems, and lighting standardisation. Evidence for systematic use of motion-time measurement methods remains sparse outside Western Europe. The chapter identifies a gap between ergonomic guidelines developed for assembly contexts and their application to disassembly, where force requirements, awkward postures, and contamination hazards create distinct risk profiles. The chapter concludes with a framework mapping intervention types to facility scale and product category, intended as a practical reference for facility planners.

title: Measuring Operator Learning Curves on a Smartphone Disassembly Line: A Longitudinal Study Over 16 Weeks
abstract: Learning curve effects in manual disassembly are less well characterised than in assembly, partly because worker tenure at end-of-life facilities tends to be short. This study tracked eight operators on a three-station smartphone disassembly line at a Serbian take-back facility over 16 consecutive working weeks, recording individual task times weekly using video-coded MTM-UAS analysis. A power-law model was fitted to mean task times for each operator and each station separately. Learning curve slopes (expressed as percentage reduction per doubling of cumulative output) ranged from 7% to 21% across operators and stations, with the highest learning rates observed at the display-removal station where tactile judgment is important. Plateau times ranged from 6 to 11 weeks. Inter-operator variability declined significantly after week 8 (F-test, p = 0.03), suggesting convergence toward a common method. Results support scheduling new operators at lower-complexity stations in the first four weeks and adjusting line-balance target times accordingly during the ramp-up period.

title: Integration of Value Stream Mapping and Ergonomic Risk Assessment in a Refrigerator Disassembly Facility: A Case Study
abstract: Value stream mapping (VSM) is a standard lean tool for identifying waste but does not capture ergonomic risk, while ergonomic assessment methods do not quantify time and flow losses. This case study presents a combined approach applied to a refrigerator end-of-life disassembly facility with a capacity of approximately 900 units per week. A current-state VSM was constructed from timed observations across seven workstations, and REBA scores were simultaneously recorded for each station. Four of seven stations showed REBA scores above 7 (action required), all coinciding with VSM-identified bottlenecks. The combined analysis revealed that awkward postures were partly caused by insufficient in-process buffer space forcing operators to reposition large components. A future-state VSM incorporating redesigned buffer zones and a scissor-lift tilt table at the compressor-removal station was simulated using discrete-event modelling. Predicted outcomes included a 14% throughput increase and a REBA score reduction from 9 to 5 at the highest-risk station.

title: Cycle Time Estimation for Mixed-Product Disassembly Lines Using a Feature-Based Time Standard
abstract: Standard pre-determined motion time systems require detailed task breakdown that is impractical when product mix changes frequently, as in take-back and remanufacturing contexts. This paper develops and validates a feature-based time standard for mixed-product disassembly that estimates station cycle times from six product-level features: unit mass, fastener count, fastener type diversity, housing material, contamination class, and number of separable subassemblies. Data were collected from 214 disassembly jobs across three product categories (laptops, power tools, and coffee machines) at two facilities in Serbia and one in Hungary. A multiple linear regression model trained on 70% of the dataset predicted cycle times within ±15% for 81% of held-out jobs, outperforming a simple weight-based estimator (63% within ±15%). The feature-based standard was implemented as a spreadsheet tool used during job intake to pre-assign products to stations and set piece-rate targets. Facility managers reported reduced replanning effort compared to their previous ad hoc approach.

title: Effect of Shift Duration and Rest Schedule on Perceived Exertion and Throughput in a Manual Battery-Pack Disassembly Line
abstract: With growing volumes of end-of-life lithium-ion battery packs entering reverse-logistics streams, understanding human factors in battery disassembly is increasingly relevant. This study examined how shift structure—specifically total shift duration (six versus eight hours) and rest schedule (two fixed breaks versus micro-break scheduling every 52 minutes)—affects perceived exertion (Borg CR10 scale) and hourly throughput at a pilot battery disassembly line established at the Faculty of Technical Sciences ergonomics laboratory. Fifteen volunteers participated in a within-subjects crossover design covering all four shift configurations over four days. Throughput was highest under the six-hour shift with micro-breaks (mean 23.4 packs per operator per hour), while perceived exertion at end of shift was lowest under the same condition (mean Borg 3.1). The eight-hour fixed-break condition produced the lowest throughput (20.1 packs per hour) and the highest end-of-shift exertion (Borg 5.6). Statistical differences between conditions were significant for both measures (p < 0.05). Limitations include the laboratory setting and volunteer sample, which likely underestimate fatigue effects in a full production context.

title: Integration of inventory holding costs into mixed-model line sequencing: a bi-criteria model
abstract: Standard mixed-model sequencing models minimise workload variation without accounting for the inventory consequences of producing certain model mixes early or late in a shift. This paper formulates a bi-criteria integer programme that simultaneously minimises peak station load deviation and total work-in-process (WIP) holding costs. Holding costs are approximated using a linear carrying charge based on standard component values obtained from a bill of materials of a surgical instrument tray assembly line operating in northern Serbia. The two objectives are combined through a weighted-sum scalarisation, and a Pareto frontier is traced by varying the weight parameter across 11 discrete values. The model is solved exactly for instances up to 6 model types with a daily demand horizon of 120 units and approximately for larger instances using a simulated annealing procedure. Results indicate a 7–14% increase in peak deviation is sufficient to achieve a 22% reduction in daily WIP costs on the tested instances.

title: Handling Structural Breaks in Industrial Energy Baselines Caused by Production Process Changes
abstract: Energy performance contracts in industrial settings frequently span periods during which production processes change in ways unrelated to the energy conservation measures being verified. This paper addresses the statistical treatment of such structural breaks in IPMVP Option C baseline models. Using Chow tests and CUSUM procedures, structural breaks are detected in baseline data from eight facilities undergoing EPC verification in Serbia and Romania. In six cases, the breaks correspond to documented events such as equipment replacement or product line changes. Two approaches to break handling are compared: truncating the baseline to the post-break segment versus introducing a dummy variable for the structural change. Truncation reduces model stability when the post-break period is short; dummy variable inclusion improves goodness of fit (mean CVRMSE improvement of 3.1 percentage points) but requires contractual agreement on break definition. A decision flowchart is provided for practitioners.

title: Estimating true availability on aseptic PET lines: accounting for micro-stops below SCADA detection threshold
abstract: SCADA-based availability reporting systematically omits micro-stops shorter than the system's event-capture threshold, which in most food-plant configurations is set between 30 and 60 seconds. On fast aseptic PET lines running at 36,000 bottles per hour, this threshold excludes a substantial fraction of stoppages. This study combined SCADA logs with video observation of 240 production hours on an aseptic PET line at a Serbian juice and nectar manufacturer to quantify the magnitude of sub-threshold micro-stops. Micro-stops contributed an additional 4.1 percentage-point reduction in actual availability beyond SCADA-reported figures. A correction factor model based on line speed and product viscosity group was fitted using ordinary least squares and validated on a hold-out month. The results imply that aseptic lines routinely overstate true OEE by 4–7 percentage points when relying exclusively on SCADA data. Recommendations for adjusting event-capture thresholds and supplementing SCADA with vibration-based stop detection are provided.

title: Field Measurement of Thermal Comfort Conditions in Early Twentieth-Century Primary School Buildings in Vojvodina During the Heating Season
abstract: This study presents results from a field measurement campaign conducted in three state-protected primary school buildings in the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia during the 2021–2022 heating season. Measurements of air temperature, relative humidity, mean radiant temperature, and CO₂ concentration were collected at 10-minute intervals across 14 classrooms over a period of 11 weeks using portable multi-sensor loggers. Occupancy was tracked through timetable records and passive infrared counters. Operative temperatures ranged from 17.4 °C to 24.1 °C, with 38 % of classroom-hours falling outside the EN 15251 Category II comfort band. CO₂ levels exceeded 1 200 ppm in 61 % of occupied periods, indicating inadequate air exchange. The data reveal a systematic mismatch between heating system operation schedules and actual occupancy patterns, particularly in buildings served by district heating with no local regulation. The findings establish a quantitative baseline for subsequent simulation work and highlight the need for occupancy-responsive ventilation interventions compatible with heritage constraints on facade modification.

title: Calibration of an EnergyPlus Model Against Monitored Data for a Masonry School Building in a Humid Continental Climate
abstract: Reliable building energy simulation of heritage masonry structures requires careful calibration against measured performance data, yet protocols suited to pre-1950 construction are rarely discussed in the literature. This paper describes the calibration process for an EnergyPlus 9.4 model of a 1927 brick-and-timber school building in Novi Sad. Measured hourly gas consumption and internal air temperatures from three representative classrooms collected over a full heating season (October 2021 to April 2022) were used as calibration targets. Initial model runs overestimated heating demand by 23 % due to assumed envelope air-tightness values. Calibration proceeded iteratively by adjusting infiltration rates, window U-values, and thermal mass parameters within uncertainty bounds derived from on-site blower-door testing and thermographic surveys. The calibrated model achieved a mean bias error of −1.8 % and a coefficient of variation of the root mean square error of 9.4 % for monthly energy use, satisfying ASHRAE Guideline 14 criteria. The calibrated model was subsequently used as the base case for ventilation strategy simulations.

title: Occupancy-Driven Ventilation Control Logic for Heritage Classrooms: Parametric Simulation Study Using Coupled EnergyPlus–Python Co-Simulation
abstract: Operating natural ventilation openings according to occupancy rather than fixed schedules can reduce heating energy penalties while maintaining acceptable indoor air quality. This paper develops and tests a rule-based control logic for transom window actuators in heritage classrooms, implemented through a co-simulation framework coupling EnergyPlus 22.2 with a Python controller via the Building Controls Virtual Test Bed middleware. The control logic uses CO₂ concentration as a proxy for occupancy and triggers window opening when CO₂ exceeds 900 ppm, subject to a wind-speed override above 3 m/s and a minimum indoor–outdoor temperature differential of 3 K. Parametric runs were performed for the calibrated Novi Sad school model across a 10-year Meteonorm weather file spanning 2012–2022. Compared with a fixed daily schedule, the occupancy-driven strategy reduced annual heating energy demand by 11–17 % depending on class timetable variability, while limiting the fraction of classroom-hours with CO₂ above 1 000 ppm to under 8 %. Thermal comfort hours within the adaptive comfort band (EN 16798-1, Category II) increased by 6 percentage points on average across the shoulder seasons.

title: Thermal Comfort and Energy Trade-offs in Pre-War School Buildings of the Pannonian Region: A Comparative Simulation Across Four Climate Scenarios
abstract: Central European heritage school buildings face compounding challenges as heating seasons shorten and cooling demand emerges in classrooms that were never mechanically cooled. This chapter situates simulation results from buildings in Novi Sad, Pécs, Subotica, and Timișoara within the broader context of Pannonian regional climate variability and building stock characteristics. Using calibrated EnergyPlus models for each case, the authors compare thermal comfort outcomes and heating plus cooling energy demands under a historical 1990–2020 baseline and three projected climate scenarios for 2050 derived from CORDEX-EUR-11 regional model outputs at RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Results show that natural ventilation strategies adequate for current conditions are insufficient to prevent overheating in classrooms above the first floor under the mid-range 2050 scenario, with discomfort hours during May–September increasing by 40–70 % relative to the baseline. The chapter discusses passive measures, including increased thermal mass exposure, external shading compatible with heritage designation, and night pre-cooling, concluding with a prioritisation framework for building managers operating under conservation constraints.

title: Chloroplast microsatellite instability in callus-derived regenerants of Hypericum perforatum L.
abstract: Callus cultures of Hypericum perforatum were initiated from leaf explants of a single donor clone and maintained for 8, 16, and 24 weeks before regeneration. Forty regenerants per time point were screened with 12 chloroplast microsatellite (cpSSR) primer pairs targeting the large single-copy and inverted repeat regions of the plastome. Gel scoring revealed length polymorphisms at three loci in regenerants from the 16-week and 24-week callus cohorts, with a polymorphism rate of 4.2% and 11.7% respectively. No polymorphisms were detected in regenerants from 8-week cultures or in the donor plant. Hypericin and pseudohypericin content, measured by HPLC, showed a statistically significant negative correlation (r = −0.61, p < 0.01) with the number of polymorphic loci per regenerant. The results indicate that extended callus maintenance increases plastid genome instability, which in turn compromises the consistency of naphthodianthrone biosynthesis in tissue-culture-derived plants.

title: Assessment of somaclonal variation in lavender (Lavandula angustifolia Mill.) micropropagated through axillary shoot proliferation versus direct organogenesis
abstract: Two micropropagation routes—axillary shoot proliferation (AP) and direct organogenesis from leaf disc explants (DO)—were compared across 60 Lavandula angustifolia regenerants each, derived from a single mother plant. Somaclonal variation was assessed using ISSR markers (15 primers, 214 scorable bands), cpSSR markers (10 loci), and flow cytometric ploidy estimation. ISSR polymorphism was detected in 3.3% of AP plants and 18.3% of DO plants. Ploidy anomalies (tetraploidy and mixoploidy) occurred exclusively in the DO group (5 of 60 plants). Chloroplast SSR profiles were stable across both groups. Essential oil yield and linalool percentage, quantified by GC-MS from second-season field-transplanted regenerants, did not differ significantly between the non-variant AP regenerants and donor plants. The findings support AP as the preferred route for commercial lavender multiplication when secondary metabolite consistency is required.

title: Structural rearrangements in the inverted repeat boundaries of the plastome in long-term callus cultures of Atropa belladonna
abstract: Atropa belladonna callus lines were maintained for up to 36 weeks under two auxin regimes (2,4-D at 1.0 and 2.5 mg/L). Plastome structure in bulked callus samples and individual regenerants was investigated by PCR amplification spanning the large single-copy/inverted repeat (LSC/IR) boundaries and the IR/small single-copy (SSC) junction. Sequencing of amplicons from 24 regenerants derived from 36-week cultures revealed insertion–deletion events of 12–47 bp in the rpl2–rpl23 intergenic spacer in 5 of 24 plants at the 2.5 mg/L auxin level, compared with 1 of 24 at 1.0 mg/L and 0 of 24 in the donor. Hyoscyamine content measured by HPLC in leaf tissue of greenhouse-grown regenerants was reduced by an average of 23% in plants carrying the indel compared with structurally intact counterparts. Auxin concentration during callus maintenance appears to influence the frequency of IR boundary instability.

title: Epigenetic and plastid marker concordance in detecting somaclonal variants among Salvia officinalis regenerants
abstract: Sixty regenerants of Salvia officinalis obtained via indirect shoot organogenesis were analysed using methylation-sensitive amplified polymorphism (MSAP) and cpSSR markers, and results were compared with morphological scoring and rosmarinic acid quantification. MSAP revealed cytosine methylation changes in 21.7% of regenerants, predominantly hypomethylation events affecting CG and CHG contexts. cpSSR profiling identified sequence-length variants in 6.7% of plants. Concordance between the two marker systems was low (Kappa = 0.18), suggesting they capture independent dimensions of genome instability. Plants showing both types of variation had the largest reductions in rosmarinic acid content (average −31% relative to donor). Morphological abnormalities were present in only 8.3% of regenerants and correlated poorly with molecular markers. The study highlights the complementarity of epigenetic and organellar markers for comprehensive somaclonal variation assessment in aromatic sage.

title: Influence of plant growth regulator combinations on shoot regeneration frequency and cpDNA stability in Valeriana officinalis callus cultures
abstract: Leaf-derived callus of Valeriana officinalis was cultured on Murashige and Skoog medium supplemented with four combinations of BAP (0.5 or 1.5 mg/L) and NAA (0.1 or 0.5 mg/L). Shoot regeneration frequencies ranged from 12% to 68% depending on the hormone combination. Chloroplast genome stability was assessed in 30 regenerants per treatment using 8 cpSSR markers and sequencing of the matK and rbcL coding regions. The lowest auxin/cytokinin ratio (BAP 1.5/NAA 0.1) gave the highest regeneration frequency (68%) and the lowest cpSSR instability rate (3.3%). High auxin levels (NAA 0.5) were associated with regeneration frequencies below 20% and cpSSR instability in up to 16.7% of surviving regenerants. Valerenic acid content in regenerant-derived root cultures did not differ significantly from the donor material in low-instability groups, suggesting that hormone-optimised protocols can preserve secondary metabolite capacity.

title: A comparative approach to cpDNA integrity assessment: whole-plastome sequencing versus targeted cpSSR genotyping in tissue-cultured regenerants
abstract: Whole-plastome Illumina sequencing (150 bp paired-end, mean coverage 120×) and cpSSR genotyping (12 loci) were performed in parallel on 20 Ocimum basilicum regenerants derived from 12-week callus cultures. Complete plastome assemblies were obtained for all samples using a reference-guided pipeline. Sequencing identified single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) and indels in 9 of 20 plants, distributed across non-coding intergenic spacers and tRNA genes. cpSSR genotyping detected length variation in 5 of those 9 plants, missing 4 cases of SNV-level change. Conversely, all cpSSR-detected variants were confirmed by whole-plastome data. Loci most prone to instability were located in the accD upstream region and the trnL-trnF spacer. The cost per sample for targeted cpSSR genotyping was approximately 8% of that for whole-plastome sequencing, suggesting a tiered screening strategy for routine quality control in medicinal plant micropropagation programmes.

title: Somaclonal variation frequency across five medicinal plant species subjected to identical indirect organogenesis protocols: a cross-species comparison
abstract: Five medicinal plant species—Melissa officinalis, Origanum vulgare, Mentha × piperita, Echinacea purpurea, and Matricaria chamomilla—were subjected to a standardised indirect organogenesis protocol (4-week callus phase, MS medium with BAP 1.0/NAA 0.2 mg/L) to allow cross-species comparison of somaclonal variation frequency. For each species, 40 regenerants were screened with ISSR (10 primers) and cpSSR (8 loci) markers. ISSR-based variation ranged from 2.5% in Mentha × piperita to 22.5% in Matricaria chamomilla. cpSSR variation ranged from 0% in Melissa officinalis to 12.5% in Matricaria chamomilla. Genome size estimated by flow cytometry was positively correlated with ISSR variation frequency (r = 0.83), while no significant correlation was found between genome size and cpSSR instability. Representative metabolites (essential oil yield, flavonoid content) were reduced in ISSR-variant plants of each species, confirming that nuclear somaclonal variation is the primary driver of metabolite inconsistency at this callus duration.

title: Plastid genome coverage and read-depth uniformity as indicators of organelle copy number variation in callus tissue of Catharanthus roseus
abstract: Catharanthus roseus callus cultures were established from cotyledon explants and maintained for 6, 12, and 24 weeks. Whole-genome sequencing (Illumina NovaSeq, 2 × 100 bp) was performed on pooled callus samples and on 15 individual regenerants per time point. Plastid-to-nuclear genome coverage ratios were calculated using mapped read counts. In 6-week callus, the plastid/nuclear ratio was 83 ± 12, consistent with the ratio in leaf tissue of donor plants (79 ± 9). At 24 weeks, the ratio dropped to 34 ± 21, with high variance among individual regenerants, indicating heteroplasmy and unequal organelle partitioning. Read-depth uniformity across the plastome (measured as coefficient of variation) increased significantly at 24 weeks (CV = 0.41 vs. 0.09 at 6 weeks). Vinblastine precursor accumulation assayed by HPLC in regenerant shoot cultures correlated positively with plastid/nuclear ratio (r = 0.72, p < 0.001), connecting organelle copy number maintenance to terpenoid indole alkaloid biosynthesis capacity.

title: Stability of phenylpropanoid pathway gene expression and chloroplast genome integrity in Hypericum perforatum regenerants across three subculture cycles
abstract: A set of 24 Hypericum perforatum regenerants previously characterised for cpSSR status (12 with detected instability, 12 without) was subcultured through three shoot multiplication cycles under identical conditions. At each cycle, cpSSR profiling was repeated, RT-qPCR was performed for PAL, CHS, and F3H transcripts (normalised to EF1α), and hypericin and emodin were quantified by HPLC from harvested shoot biomass. In regenerants that were cpSSR-stable at the outset, plastid marker profiles remained unchanged through three cycles. In initially unstable regenerants, two additional cpSSR variants emerged by cycle 3, suggesting ongoing instability. PAL and CHS expression was reduced by an average of 28% and 34% respectively in cpSSR-unstable plants relative to stable plants at cycle 1, with differences maintained but not amplified across cycles. The data indicate that cpDNA instability detected immediately after regeneration is a reliable predictor of long-term metabolite production capacity.

title: Rapid cpDNA screening protocol for quality certification of micropropagated aromatic plant material: workflow design and validation in three Lamiaceae species
abstract: A streamlined four-step cpDNA screening workflow was developed for routine certification of micropropagated aromatic plants at commercial scale. The protocol comprises CTAB-based DNA extraction adapted for small shoot explants (< 50 mg fresh weight), multiplexed PCR amplification of four plastid microsatellite loci selected for maximum informativeness across Lamiaceae, fluorescent capillary electrophoresis fragment sizing, and automated allele binning with a custom R script. Validation was performed on 120 Lavandula angustifolia, 90 Thymus vulgaris, and 90 Mentha × piperita regenerants, alongside their respective donor plants and artificially mutagenised positive controls generated by EMS treatment. Sensitivity (detection of known variants) was 94.7% and specificity was 100%. Turnaround time from tissue sampling to result was 2 working days. Per-sample reagent cost was calculated at approximately €3.20 under Serbian laboratory pricing conditions. The protocol is proposed as a practical tool for both academic research programmes and plant nursery quality control workflows.
