title: Cloning and sequence analysis of a laccase gene from a Trametes-like isolate and its comparison with publicly available basidiomycete sequences
abstract: The full-length laccase-encoding gene lcc1 was amplified from genomic DNA of a Trametes-like isolate using degenerate primers designed against conserved copper-binding domain regions. The open reading frame of 1,578 bp encoded a predicted protein of 525 amino acids including a 21-residue signal peptide. Intron positions were confirmed by cDNA sequencing from RNA extracted during peak activity cultures. Phylogenetic analysis using the neighbour-joining method placed the deduced protein sequence in a clade with laccases from Trametes versicolor and Cerrena unicolor with bootstrap support of 87. Predicted substrate-binding residues at positions 164, 265, and 458 were identical to those in structurally characterised members of the clade. The coding sequence was subcloned into the pPICZαA shuttle vector in preparation for Pichia pastoris expression. Sequence data were deposited in a regional bioinformatics repository. The analysis confirmed the presence of all four histidine-coordinated copper centres characteristic of multi-copper oxidases.

title: Recursive Least-Squares Identification of a Second-Order Thermal RC Model for a Lightweight Prefabricated Wall Panel
abstract: Accurate low-order models of wall thermal dynamics are needed to support real-time control of indoor climate. This paper presents a recursive least-squares identification procedure applied to a second-order resistor–capacitor (RC) analogy model representing a 120 mm expanded-polystyrene prefabricated panel. Outdoor air temperature, solar irradiance measured on a south-facing pyranometer, and interior surface heat flux data were collected over 21 consecutive days in a monitored test room at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad. The RC parameters were updated every 15 minutes using a forgetting factor of 0.98 to capture seasonal drift. The identified two-state model reproduced interior surface temperature with a root-mean-square error of 0.31 °C on a separate 7-day validation set. Sensitivity analysis showed that the effective thermal capacitance converged after approximately 72 hours of winter excitation. The work demonstrates that a simple forgetting-factor RLS scheme is sufficient for online parameter tracking in lightweight constructions without requiring persistent external excitation.

title: Grey-Box Identification of a Radiant Floor Heating System Using Continuous-Time State-Space Models
abstract: Radiant floor heating systems exhibit pronounced thermal inertia and nonlinear heat exchange at the floor surface, making them difficult to represent with standard discrete-time models. This paper proposes a continuous-time grey-box state-space formulation with three states—water temperature, floor slab temperature, and room air temperature—whose parameters are estimated by the expectation-maximisation (EM) algorithm applied to data from a 48 m² office room retrofitted with a hydronic floor system. Measurements included supply and return water temperatures, flow rate, and operative room temperature sampled at 5-minute intervals over 45 days. The nonlinear floor-to-air convection term was approximated by a first-order Taylor expansion around the operating point. The identified model produced a root-mean-square prediction error of 0.22 °C for operative temperature over a 14-day validation period. A simplified version of the model was implemented in a constrained model predictive controller, reducing energy consumption by 11% compared with a thermostat reference over a four-week pilot.

title: Nonlinear Thermal Model of a Phase-Change Material Composite Wall: Identification and Validation
abstract: Phase-change materials (PCMs) embedded in wall panels introduce strongly nonlinear enthalpy-temperature behaviour that standard linear RC models cannot capture. This paper presents a piecewise-linear grey-box state-space model with two switching regimes (solid and liquid phases) for a gypsum-PCM composite wall panel (25 mm, melting point 23 °C) tested in a guarded hot-box apparatus. The model parameters—effective conductance, solid-phase and liquid-phase capacitances, and latent heat fraction—were estimated by nonlinear least squares using trust-region reflective optimisation. Twelve charge–discharge cycles at three ambient temperature amplitudes (±4, ±6, ±8 °C around the melting point) produced 36 identification datasets. The switched model reduced validation RMSE from 0.61 °C (linear model) to 0.19 °C. The paper also discusses the numerical conditioning issues that arise when the PCM fraction exceeds 30% of wall cross-section, and proposes a reparameterisation that improves convergence.

title: Thermal Comfort Prediction Using a Low-Order PMV Proxy Model Integrated with Grey-Box State-Space Identification
abstract: The ISO 7730 predicted mean vote (PMV) index requires metabolic rate and clothing insulation estimates that are impractical in automated building control. This paper proposes a surrogate PMV proxy—a static nonlinear function of operative temperature, relative humidity, and mean radiant temperature estimated from surface thermocouples—calibrated against occupant comfort votes collected via a mobile application from 38 office workers over eight weeks in Novi Sad. The proxy was coupled with a two-state grey-box thermal model of the office zone to form a combined dynamic comfort predictor. Parameters of both layers were estimated jointly by penalised nonlinear least squares. Cross-validated against independent comfort vote sessions, the proxy predicted PMV category (cool/neutral/warm) with 81% accuracy, compared with 74% for an operative-temperature-only baseline. The integrated model was used as the objective function in a receding-horizon controller that maintained PMV within [−0.5, +0.5] while reducing active cooling energy by 9% over three summer weeks.

title: Effect of Airtightness Uncertainty on Identified Thermal Parameters in Passive-Standard Wall Assemblies
abstract: Infiltration-driven heat loss introduces an unmeasured disturbance that is systematically confounded with wall conductance estimates in thermal identification experiments. This paper quantifies the bias in identified RC parameters caused by airtightness uncertainty for three passive-standard wall assemblies—timber frame, autoclaved aerated concrete block, and prefabricated structural insulated panel—tested in a calibrated hot-box chamber. Blower-door tests at the start and end of each 30-day identification campaign showed airtightness variation of up to 12% due to gasket compression. Monte Carlo simulations propagated this uncertainty through the maximum-likelihood estimator, yielding 95% confidence intervals of ±8% on wall conductance and ±14% on effective capacitance. A correction procedure based on a co-estimated infiltration state reduced conductance bias below 3% in all three assemblies. The paper recommends that blower-door measurements be integrated into standard building identification protocols when airtightness class cannot be verified independently.

title: Structured State-Space Models for Thermal Identification: A Comparison of RC-Network and Koopman-Linear Representations
abstract: Koopman operator theory offers a way to represent nonlinear thermal dynamics as a linear system in a lifted state space, potentially avoiding the manual tuning of RC-network topology. This paper compares RC-network grey-box models with data-driven Koopman-linear representations (constructed via extended dynamic mode decomposition with polynomial lifting functions of degree 2 and 3) for four building zones with different construction types in Novi Sad. Both approaches were identified from one year of 15-minute monitoring data and validated on a held-out winter month. RC-network models outperformed Koopman representations in extrapolation to unseen setpoint trajectories (mean RMSE 0.24 °C vs. 0.41 °C), while Koopman models required less domain knowledge and converged to comparable accuracy during the central heating season. A hybrid scheme—initialising Koopman lifting functions from RC-network eigenvectors—reduced the Koopman extrapolation RMSE to 0.29 °C. The paper discusses conditions under which each approach is preferable in practice.

title: Closed-Loop Thermal Identification under Model Predictive Control: Persistent Excitation and Bias Considerations
abstract: When a building zone is already under model predictive control, the closed-loop feedback suppresses temperature variations, potentially violating the persistent excitation condition required for consistent parameter estimation. This paper analyses the severity of this effect for a two-state RC model under three MPC formulations—tracking, range control, and economic—using data from a 55 m² laboratory office controlled by a dSPACE rapid-prototyping unit at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Spectral analysis of closed-loop input–output data confirmed significant reduction of excitation below 0.2 mHz under tight tracking MPC. Bias in estimated conductance reached 22% under the tightest tracking formulation. Adding a small band-limited exploratory signal (amplitude 15 W, bandwidth 0.5 mHz) to the MPC output reduced conductance bias to below 5% with negligible impact on comfort (PMV deviation < 0.08). The paper provides design guidelines for dual-control strategies that balance comfort maintenance with identification accuracy during regular building operation.

title: Detecting Abrupt and Gradual Faults in Hydraulic Actuator Systems Using a Combined CUSUM–Autoencoder Approach
abstract: Hydraulic actuator faults manifest as either abrupt jumps in pressure or flow or as gradual drift in actuator efficiency. Standard CUSUM charts detect the former reliably but respond slowly to the latter, while autoencoder reconstruction error captures complex multivariate deviations but is insensitive to the direction of change. This paper proposes a two-stage detector: a shallow convolutional autoencoder generates a residual vector, and a sign-constrained CUSUM statistic accumulates this residual in the direction identified by an offline fault-mode analysis. The combined statistic is evaluated on the public Hydraulic System Condition dataset (2 205 cycles, 17 sensors, four fault types) and on a laboratory actuator testbed. For gradual efficiency-loss faults, the combined scheme reduced mean detection delay from 41 cycles (autoencoder alone) to 17 cycles at a matched false-alarm rate of 1%. No improvement over plain CUSUM was observed for abrupt pressure-drop faults, confirming complementary strengths.

title: Moment–Rotation Behaviour of Bolted Glulam Beam-to-Column Connections Under Monotonic Loading
abstract: Four configurations of bolted glulam beam-to-column joints with steel knife-plate inserts were fabricated from GL28c beech-spruce combination glulam and tested under monotonic bending. Bolt diameters of 12 and 16 mm and two bolt-row spacings were examined, yielding 32 specimens in total. Rotation was determined from LVDT readings at four points around each joint. Initial rotational stiffness ranged from 180 to 520 kNm/rad depending on configuration. Failure modes included bolt yielding in bending, timber splitting, and combined bearing-splitting; the latter dominated at the closer bolt spacing. A tri-linear moment–rotation model was fitted to the data, and its parameters are expressed as functions of bolt diameter and timber density. Predicted stiffness values using the Eurocode 5 slip-modulus approach underestimated measured stiffness by 20–35 %, suggesting the need for calibration factors in semi-rigid frame analysis.

title: Withdrawal Resistance of Self-Tapping Screws in Cross-Laminated Timber Edge Connections
abstract: Self-tapping screws (STS) are increasingly used to connect CLT panels at wall-to-floor interfaces. This paper presents 144 withdrawal tests on fully threaded STS (6 × 100 mm and 8 × 160 mm) inserted at 0°, 30°, and 45° angles into the narrow face of three-layer and five-layer CLT panels made from Norway spruce laminations. Withdrawal force was recorded at 1 mm/min displacement rate. Mean withdrawal capacities ranged from 4.1 kN (6 mm, 0°) to 14.8 kN (8 mm, 45°). Comparison with the ETA-assessed calculation model showed satisfactory agreement within ±10 % for angled insertion but a 15 % overestimate for perpendicular insertion into the narrow face, attributed to layer interface splitting. Characteristic values are tabulated for the three CLT grades tested and recommendations for minimum edge distances at narrow-face connections are proposed.

title: Load-Sharing in Multi-Fastener Glulam Connections: Effect of Stiffness Distribution on Characteristic Capacity
abstract: Eurocode 5 requires that the characteristic capacity of a multi-fastener connection be determined as the number of fasteners multiplied by the lowest individual capacity, implicitly assuming equal load-sharing. This assumption was evaluated by testing 60 glulam splice joints with 2, 4, 6, and 8 dowels in a single row, using digital image correlation (DIC) to measure individual fastener deformations under load. Results showed load distribution to be markedly unequal at serviceability loads, with the outermost fasteners carrying up to 1.6 times the mean load in 8-fastener groups. At ultimate load, redistribution reduced the peak ratio to 1.2 due to timber plasticity. A modified load-sharing factor depending on fastener-row count and fastener stiffness-to-timber-stiffness ratio is proposed, reducing characteristic group capacity by 4–12 % compared to the current Eurocode 5 formula.

title: Timber Connections in Seismic Regions: Design Principles and Code Comparisons
abstract: This book chapter provides a practitioner-oriented review of ductility requirements for timber connections in seismic design, drawing on EN 1998-1 and ÖNORM provisions alongside selected research results. The chapter covers the plastic rotation capacity of nailed, bolted, and screwed connections in glulam and CLT, with emphasis on ductility class M and H requirements. Design worked examples are included for a three-storey CLT shear wall building representative of residential construction in the Pannonian lowland seismic zone. The chapter also compares the effective number concept in Eurocode 5 with the US NDS overstrength approach, highlighting situations where the European approach may yield unconservative shear-wall base connection designs. Practical detailing guidance is given for platform-frame and balloon-frame CLT configurations.

title: Racking Resistance of CLT Wall Panels Connected with Angle Brackets Under Cyclic Loading
abstract: Twelve CLT wall specimens (3 × 3 m) connected to a rigid concrete foundation with paired L-shaped steel angle brackets and STS were subjected to ISO 16670 quasi-static cyclic loading protocols. Two bracket types (1.5 mm and 3 mm plate thickness) and two STS patterns (4×4 and 6×6 per bracket face) were tested. Hysteresis loops were analysed for equivalent viscous damping, ductility ratio, and secant stiffness degradation. Equivalent viscous damping ranged from 8.4 % to 14.2 % depending on configuration. Ductility ratios exceeded 4.0 in all cases. The 3 mm bracket with the denser STS pattern showed 38 % higher initial racking stiffness than the lightest configuration but similar displacement capacity. Results are compared to the q-factor provisions of EN 1998-1 for timber buildings and support a q = 3 assignment for the stiffer bracket type.

title: Numerical Modelling of Timber-to-Concrete Composite Beams with Notch Connections: Calibration Against Push-Out Tests
abstract: Timber-concrete composite (TCC) floors using glulam beams and concrete slabs joined by notch-and-screw connections are gaining traction in multi-storey mass timber buildings. A three-dimensional finite element model was developed in ABAQUS using a smeared crack model for concrete, orthotropic elastic-plastic constitutive law for glulam, and elasto-plastic spring elements for the connection interface. The model was calibrated against results from 24 push-out specimens tested at the Faculty's laboratory under monotonic and cyclic shear. Calibrated models reproduced peak shear force within ±7 % and stiffness within ±11 %. A parametric study varying notch depth (20–50 mm), slab thickness (80–120 mm), and screw inclination (0°, 45°) showed notch depth to be the dominant parameter governing stiffness. A simplified design formula for notch connection slip modulus is derived and compared with expressions in existing literature.

title: Effect of Moisture Cycling on the Stiffness and Strength of Screwed CLT Panel-to-Panel Connections
abstract: Moisture variations in exposed or partially exposed CLT structures cause cyclic swelling and shrinkage of laminations that may degrade connection performance over time. Forty half-lap CLT panel-to-panel connections secured with inclined STS pairs were subjected to 0, 5, 10, and 20 moisture cycles (alternating 12 % and 20 % MC) before monotonic shear testing. Stiffness was determined from the secant slope between 10 % and 40 % of ultimate load. After 20 cycles, mean stiffness decreased by 22 % and mean shear strength by 9 % relative to uncycled controls. Scanning electron microscopy of fractured surfaces showed progressive fibre detachment around fastener shanks beginning after 5 cycles. The results suggest that the Eurocode 5 kdef factor for service class 2 may need recalibration for STS connections in repeatedly wetted zones.

title: Shear Force Distribution at Glulam-Steel Composite Floor Interfaces: Experimental and Analytical Study
abstract: Glulam-steel composite beams with mechanical shear connectors are an alternative to timber-concrete composites in situations where floor depth is critical. This study tested 16 full-scale beams (5.4 m span) made from GL28h glulam bonded to cold-formed steel C-profiles with 10 mm coach screws at three spacing patterns (100, 150, and 200 mm). Bending stiffness, mid-span deflection, and longitudinal interface slip were recorded under four-point bending. Effective bending stiffness ranged from 68 % to 89 % of fully composite values depending on connector spacing. An analytical model based on the Möhler partial composite theory, adapted for the steel-timber interface, predicted mid-span deflection within 9 % for all beam types. Connector slip modulus values back-calculated from the beam tests were 14–22 % higher than those from standalone push-out tests, consistent with observations in timber-concrete literature.

title: Comparison of CEB-FIP MC90, EC2, and ACI 209R creep models for high-humidity continental environments
abstract: Three widely used creep prediction models — CEB-FIP MC90, Eurocode 2 Annex B, and ACI 209R-92 — are evaluated against an assembled dataset of 27 prestressed and reinforced concrete specimens tested at the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica between 1998 and 2011. Specimens were loaded at ages of 3, 7, and 28 days and monitored for periods of up to 10 years. The laboratory climate was maintained at 65–75 % relative humidity and 18–22 °C. The mean absolute percentage error over the full dataset was 22 % for CEB-FIP MC90, 28 % for EC2, and 34 % for ACI 209R. All models overestimated creep coefficients at loading ages beyond 14 days. The EC2 model showed the largest scatter at high sustained stress ratios (σ/fcm > 0.40). Revised partial correction factors for application in the regional context are proposed and validated against a withheld subset of 6 specimens.

title: Predicting distribution transformer failures from dissolved gas analysis and load history
abstract: This paper presents a machine-learning framework for predicting incipient failures in distribution transformers by combining dissolved gas analysis (DGA) measurements with historical load profiles. A dataset spanning seven years of operational records from a regional distribution system operator was used to train and validate gradient-boosted classification models. Seven key fault gases—hydrogen, methane, ethylene, ethane, acetylene, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide—were extracted at regular sampling intervals and correlated with thermal loading cycles derived from SCADA archives. The proposed model achieves a fault-prediction horizon of up to six months before confirmed failure, outperforming conventional Duval triangle and IEC ratio methods in both precision and recall. A risk-scoring output allows asset managers to prioritise field inspection schedules and defer or advance maintenance interventions. Sensitivity analyses confirm that ethylene concentration trends and cumulative overload hours are the most discriminative features. The methodology is validated against a hold-out test set of 214 transformer units, demonstrating a false-positive rate below 8 %. The results support integration into existing distribution management systems without requiring additional sensor hardware.

title: Health indices for ageing transformer fleets
abstract: Ageing transformer fleets represent a critical financial and reliability challenge for distribution system operators throughout Europe. This paper proposes a composite health index (HI) methodology that aggregates multiple condition indicators—including dissolved gas analysis results, oil quality parameters, insulation resistance measurements, and load history statistics—into a single scalar score suitable for portfolio-level asset management decisions. The HI framework is calibrated against end-of-life failure records from three distribution operators and benchmarked against two previously published scoring systems. Weighting coefficients are derived through an analytic hierarchy process informed by domain expert elicitation. Case studies involving transformer populations of more than 400 units demonstrate that the proposed index correctly identifies assets within two years of failure with 91 % accuracy. The paper also discusses how the HI can be embedded within a risk-based maintenance planning tool, enabling operators to optimise replacement budgets over a rolling five-year horizon. Limitations arising from inconsistent historical record quality are discussed, and guidelines for data governance are provided.

title: Thermal models of oil-immersed transformers under PV-driven reverse flow
abstract: The rapid uptake of rooftop photovoltaic generation in low- and medium-voltage networks creates reverse power flow conditions that fundamentally alter the thermal loading patterns of distribution transformers. This paper develops an enhanced thermal model for oil-immersed transformers that explicitly accounts for bidirectional load cycles, including periods of sustained reverse flow during peak PV generation hours. The model extends the IEC 60076-7 top-oil and hot-spot temperature framework by introducing asymmetric loss factors calibrated through laboratory measurements on two 630 kVA transformer units operated under controlled reverse-flow schedules. Field validation is performed using temperature loggers installed on twelve transformers in a suburban network with high PV penetration. Results show that conventional thermal models underestimate peak hot-spot temperatures by up to 14 °C during reverse-flow episodes, leading to non-conservative ageing estimates. The revised model is implemented as a real-time monitoring module and tested over a twelve-month period, demonstrating improved alignment with measured winding temperatures. Implications for asset lifetime recalculation and DGA interpretation under PV-driven operating regimes are discussed.

title: Accelerated ageing of cellulose insulation in power transformers: laboratory characterisation and field correlation
abstract: Cellulose-based insulation in oil-immersed power transformers undergoes thermally and hydrolytically driven degradation that ultimately limits transformer service life. This paper presents a systematic accelerated ageing study in which paper insulation samples were subjected to controlled thermal stress at temperatures ranging from 110 °C to 150 °C over periods of up to 3 000 hours. Degree of polymerisation, tensile strength, and moisture content were tracked at regular intervals and correlated with concurrent dissolved gas generation rates, with particular attention to carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide trends. The laboratory findings were subsequently matched against field data collected from 38 transformers with documented age and load histories provided by a regional distribution operator. A statistical correlation model is derived that allows field engineers to estimate remaining insulation life from routine DGA results and available thermal history without invasive paper sampling. Validation against units with post-mortem insulation analysis confirms that the model estimates degree of polymerisation within ±15 % for 85 % of the test population. The work contributes a practical diagnostic pathway applicable to ageing fleet management decisions.

title: Bayesian network model for multi-symptom fault classification in power transformers
abstract: Accurate fault classification in power transformers requires the integration of multiple, often uncertain, diagnostic signals. This paper proposes a Bayesian network (BN) model that combines dissolved gas analysis ratios, partial discharge measurements, oil quality indices, and operational history into a unified probabilistic fault classifier. The network topology is established through expert elicitation and refined using a training dataset of 312 confirmed fault cases drawn from post-mortem inspection records of distribution and sub-transmission transformers. The model distinguishes among five fault categories: thermal faults of low and high severity, partial discharge, cellulose degradation, and combined electro-thermal faults. Posterior probability outputs provide interpretable confidence levels for each diagnosis, enabling asset managers to make risk-informed decisions rather than relying on binary fault/no-fault thresholds. Comparative evaluation against three established DGA interpretation methods shows that the BN classifier achieves an overall accuracy of 88 % on a held-out test set, representing an improvement of 11–19 percentage points. Particular performance gains are observed in distinguishing co-occurring fault modes that produce overlapping gas signatures. The model is packaged as a stand-alone diagnostic module compatible with standard DGA laboratory data formats.

title: Online DGA sensor integration for real-time transformer condition monitoring: field deployment experience
abstract: This paper reports on a three-year field deployment of continuous online dissolved gas analysis sensors on a fleet of 24 medium-power distribution transformers operated by a Serbian distribution system operator. The deployment covers the installation methodology, communication architecture, data quality assurance protocols, and operational outcomes. Online sensors measuring hydrogen, acetylene, ethylene, and moisture content transmitted readings every 15 minutes to a central asset management platform. Alarm thresholds were set using rate-of-change criteria derived from the authors' prior statistical work on ageing fleets, enabling early warning notifications independently of scheduled laboratory DGA sampling. During the monitoring period, three incipient fault events were detected an average of 47 days ahead of the earliest sign observable through conventional periodic sampling. One unit was taken out of service before a catastrophic failure, avoiding an estimated outage cost of approximately €180 000. The paper discusses false-alarm management strategies, sensor fouling issues encountered in high-humidity substations, and communication resilience under grid disturbances. Lessons learned are synthesised into a deployment guideline for distribution operators considering wider rollout of online DGA monitoring.

title: Risk-based replacement prioritisation for distribution transformer fleets under budget constraints
abstract: Distribution system operators must allocate limited capital budgets across large transformer populations, making replacement prioritisation a critical and technically demanding task. This paper develops a risk-based optimisation framework that combines probabilistic failure modelling with economic impact assessment to generate replacement schedules that minimise expected total cost of ownership under defined budget envelopes. Failure probability is estimated using survival analysis applied to a dataset of 1 140 transformer unit-years from three distribution operators, incorporating health indices derived from DGA, oil quality, and load data as time-varying covariates. Consequence modelling accounts for direct replacement costs, outage duration costs, and secondary network reconfiguration expenses. A mixed-integer linear programme identifies the Pareto-optimal replacement portfolio for annual budgets ranging from 60 % to 120 % of the operator's historical average spend. Scenario analyses demonstrate that shifting from age-based to risk-based replacement reduces expected annual outage costs by 22–31 % for equivalent budget levels. The framework is validated in collaboration with two distribution operators and is designed for integration into existing enterprise asset management software environments without requiring proprietary extensions.

title: Partial discharge measurement techniques for condition assessment of high-voltage power transformers in service
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) activity within the insulation system of high-voltage power transformers is one of the most sensitive indicators of impending dielectric failure. This paper reviews and experimentally compares three on-site PD measurement techniques—high-frequency current transformer (HFCT) coupling, ultra-high frequency (UHF) sensing via drain valve-mounted antennas, and acoustic emission detection—applied to twelve in-service 110/20 kV transformers at substations in the Vojvodina region. Each technique is evaluated for sensitivity, susceptibility to electromagnetic interference, ease of field application, and ability to localise discharge sources. Simultaneous measurements with all three methods allow cross-validation of detected PD activity. The study finds that UHF and HFCT methods provide complementary coverage: HFCT is more sensitive to low-level discharges in the outer insulation structure while UHF better resolves internal winding defects. Acoustic emission localisation successfully identified the approximate source position in four out of six cases with confirmed internal PD activity. Practical guidance for measurement campaign design, interference rejection, and result interpretation in the context of IEC 60270 and IEC TS 62478 is provided for engineers performing routine condition assessments.

title: Effect of harmonic loading on dissolved gas generation rates in distribution transformers: experimental study
abstract: Non-linear loads connected to distribution networks generate harmonic currents that increase eddy-current and stray losses in transformer windings, leading to elevated localised temperatures and accelerated insulation ageing. This paper reports on a controlled experimental programme in which a 100 kVA oil-immersed distribution transformer was subjected to defined harmonic load spectra—including individual 5th, 7th, and 11th harmonics as well as a combined non-linear load profile representative of a commercial building feeder—at total harmonic distortion levels between 10 % and 40 %. Oil samples were withdrawn at weekly intervals and analysed for fault gas concentrations using gas chromatography. Results show that harmonic loading significantly accelerates hydrogen and methane generation relative to sinusoidal loading at equivalent fundamental-frequency current levels, with a near-linear relationship between total harmonic distortion and gas generation rate at moderate harmonic levels. Carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide production also increases, consistent with additional thermal degradation of the cellulose-paper insulation. The findings suggest that standard DGA alarm thresholds, which are calibrated for conventional sinusoidal loading, may require upward revision for transformers serving harmonic-rich loads. Revised threshold recommendations are proposed based on the experimental data.

title: Data quality and standardisation challenges in building transformer health databases from heterogeneous operator records
abstract: Effective data-driven asset management of power transformer fleets depends critically on access to high-quality, consistently formatted historical records. In practice, distribution system operators accumulate maintenance and test data across decades using different recording conventions, laboratory contractors, and enterprise software systems, resulting in heterogeneous datasets that are difficult to harmonise. This book chapter documents the data governance challenges encountered during the consolidation of transformer health records from four Serbian distribution operators for use in condition monitoring research. Issues addressed include: inconsistent DGA reporting units and gas extraction methods; missing load history fields; ambiguous fault classification codes; and temporal misalignment between oil sample dates and nearest load metering records. A standardised transformer health data schema is proposed, covering 47 fields across equipment identity, loading, oil diagnostics, electrical test results, and maintenance history. Mapping procedures for converting legacy records to the proposed schema are described, along with automated data quality scoring rules. The chapter concludes with recommendations for operators establishing new data collection processes and for researchers designing studies that rely on multi-operator datasets. The schema has been adopted as the data standard for the GRIDHEALTH project.

title: Boundary-Scan Controllability Metrics for Mixed-Signal Nets in Double-Sided PCB Assemblies
abstract: This paper presents a quantitative framework for evaluating boundary-scan controllability and observability on mixed-signal printed circuit board assemblies where analogue subcircuits interrupt digital scan chains. The method assigns a weighted coverage score to each net segment based on the ratio of scan-accessible driver–receiver pairs to the total number of electrical nodes. Experiments were conducted on three reference boards populated with 128, 256, and 512 component pins respectively, using a commercial JTAG controller operating at 10 MHz TCK. Coverage scores were compared against hand-calculated fault-injection results for twelve common defect classes including opens, shorts, and stuck-at faults. The framework identified a 14–22 % gap between nominal boundary-scan coverage estimates and empirically verified detection rates on nets that cross analogue power domains. A correction factor derived from net impedance profiles is proposed and validated on an automotive-grade sensor interface board. The approach requires no modifications to existing IEEE 1149.1 infrastructure.

title: Automated Generation of JTAG Test Vectors for Interconnect Verification on High-Density Connectors
abstract: High-density board-to-board connectors with pitches below 0.5 mm are difficult to access with flying-probe or bed-of-nails fixtures, making boundary-scan the only practical interconnect verification method. This work describes an algorithm that automatically generates optimised JTAG test vectors for connector nets by traversing the board netlist graph and selecting driver–receiver pairs that maximise fault coverage while minimising vector length. The algorithm was implemented in Python 3.8 and validated on four industrial backplane designs containing between 800 and 2400 connector pins. Generated vector sets achieved 97.3 % stuck-at coverage on average, compared to 89.1 % for vendor-supplied default vectors, while reducing vector count by 31 %. Runtime on a standard workstation was under 90 seconds for the largest design. The tool outputs vectors compatible with the SVF and STAPL formats used by common boundary-scan controllers.

title: Defect Classification in Mixed-Signal PCB Assemblies Using Decision-Tree Analysis of ICT Measurement Residuals
abstract: In-circuit testers produce rich measurement data during parametric component tests, yet most production systems discard residuals after a pass/fail decision. This paper exploits those residuals—voltage deviations, current waveform slopes, and impedance phase angles—as input features for a decision-tree classifier trained to distinguish among seven defect classes: component open, component short, wrong-value component, reversed polarity, solder bridge, cold joint, and lifted pin. A dataset of 4,812 labelled board test records was collected from a contract electronics manufacturer over six months. A C4.5 tree trained on 70 % of the data achieved 91.4 % correct classification on the held-out test set, outperforming a nearest-neighbour baseline by 8.3 percentage points. Feature importance analysis confirmed that impedance phase angle at 1 kHz and the slope of the transient current response were the two most discriminative features. Integration into an existing ICT workflow required only a post-processing module with no hardware changes.

title: Test Coverage Analysis for Analogue Subcircuits in IEEE 1149.4 Mixed-Signal Boundary-Scan Environments
abstract: IEEE 1149.4 extends boundary-scan to analogue pins, but its adoption in volume production has been limited by uncertainty about achievable fault coverage on practical board topologies. This study analyses test coverage attainable under the 1149.4 standard for five analogue subcircuit categories: RC filters, op-amp stages, ADC input conditioning networks, power management feedback loops, and sensor signal conditioning chains. Each category was represented by ten reference circuits implemented on test vehicles. Coverage was measured by fault injection: 1,240 resistor opens/shorts and 880 capacitor deviations spanning ±20 % to ±80 % of nominal value. Achieved coverage ranged from 73 % for power-management loops to 94 % for RC filter networks, with the main limitation being the bandwidth of the analogue test bus relative to circuit operating frequency. A set of design-for-test recommendations is derived from the results, targeting layouts that improve 1149.4 coverage by an average of 11 percentage points.

title: Impact of PCB Moisture Absorption on In-Circuit Test False-Failure Rates: A Controlled Study Under IPC-9691 Accelerated Conditioning
abstract: Moisture absorbed into FR-4 substrates increases leakage currents and shifts parasitic capacitance, both of which affect the accuracy of in-circuit measurements. This controlled study conditioned 90 identical boards at 30 °C/60 % RH, 40 °C/75 % RH, and 50 °C/85 % RH for durations of 24, 72, and 168 hours following IPC-9691 protocols. After each conditioning step, boards were tested with a flying-probe system targeting 320 passive components. False-failure call rates, measured as a percentage of total tests executed, rose from a baseline of 0.4 % to a maximum of 3.7 % at the most severe condition. Leakage resistance between adjacent nets dropped below 10 MΩ in 18 % of boards at 50 °C/85 % RH after 168 hours. A humidity-aware guard-band adjustment procedure is proposed that keeps false-failure rates below 0.8 % across all conditioning levels. The procedure adds approximately 4 % to total test time.

title: Functional Test Sequence Optimisation for Mixed-Signal Boards Using Integer Linear Programming
abstract: Functional test sequences for mixed-signal boards are often designed by hand, resulting in redundant measurements and long test times. This paper formulates functional test sequencing as an integer linear programming problem in which the objective is to minimise total test execution time subject to constraints on fault coverage, power sequencing dependencies, and signal settling times. The ILP model was solved with a branch-and-bound solver for six industrial board designs ranging from 18 to 64 functional test steps. Optimised sequences reduced mean test time by 27 % compared to original hand-crafted sequences while maintaining or improving fault coverage in five of the six cases. The largest board saw test time cut from 142 to 98 seconds. Constraint violation penalties were calibrated against data from 1,200 production test records to ensure that power sequencing margins were never violated. The method is board-agnostic and requires only a netlist and a test-step dependency graph as inputs.

title: Boundary-Scan Test Development for Safety-Relevant Automotive ECUs: A Process Description and Lessons Learned
abstract: This book chapter documents the practical process of developing boundary-scan test programmes for engine control units that must comply with ISO 26262 ASIL-B requirements. It covers the workflow from netlist import through BSDL file validation, cluster-based test step generation, and diagnostic coverage estimation. Particular attention is given to conflicts between scan-clock frequency requirements and EMC constraints on automotive boards, and to the documentation artefacts required for functional safety audits. The chapter draws on experience from three development cycles carried out in collaboration with a regional electronics manufacturer over four years. Quantitative data are provided on coverage achieved, defect escapes observed during pilot production, and rework costs attributed to test-strategy decisions. The chapter concludes with a checklist of 22 items for teams beginning boundary-scan development on safety-relevant ECUs.

title: Design-for-Testability Guidelines for Mixed-Signal PCBs Under Repeated Thermal Stress: Coverage, Access, and Reliability Trade-offs
abstract: Boards intended for environments with frequent thermal excursions require design-for-testability decisions that balance initial test coverage with the need to maintain that coverage throughout the product lifetime as solder joints and contact pads degrade. This preprint consolidates data from five years of thermal cycling experiments and production test monitoring at two electronics manufacturing partners to derive a set of quantitative DFT guidelines. For each of twelve layout and routing decisions—including test pad size, via-in-pad avoidance, and scan chain segmentation—the study reports the effect on initial boundary-scan coverage, estimated coverage at 1,000 thermal cycles, and the probability of a probe contact failure per 100,000 test operations. The guidelines are expressed as scoring criteria compatible with standard DFT review checklists. Validation on three new board designs showed that following the guidelines improved predicted 1,000-cycle coverage by an average of 9.4 percentage points relative to designs reviewed without the guidelines.

title: Condition Monitoring and Prognostics for Industrial Rotating Machinery
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of condition monitoring methods for rotating machinery in industrial settings, covering vibration signal acquisition hardware considerations, standard feature extraction techniques in the time, frequency, and time-frequency domains, and the principal classes of prognosis models including physics-based, data-driven, and hybrid approaches. Practical guidelines are given for sensor placement, sampling rate selection, and signal conditioning. Case studies drawn from pump, gearbox, and compressor applications illustrate the trade-offs between model complexity and the volume of historical data required for reliable remaining useful life estimation. The chapter concludes with a discussion of deployment constraints in legacy industrial environments, including communication bandwidth limitations and the suitability of embedded versus cloud-based computation.

title: Cycling infrastructure and local economic impact in the Fruška Gora foothill villages: a baseline survey
abstract: This study examined the relationship between existing cycling track density and local business turnover in nine villages along the southern slopes of Fruška Gora. Field surveys conducted in spring and autumn 2014 recorded 312 cyclist passages per week on the primary unpaved trail segment using manual counting sheets. Structured interviews were administered to 47 local service providers, including agritourism hosts, bakeries, and bicycle rental points. Results showed that settlements located within 500 m of a marked trail reported 18–23% higher seasonal revenue from tourist spending compared with control villages without trail access. The study also identified gaps in wayfinding signage and accommodation capacity as the main constraints on further visitor growth. Recommendations were made for a minimum viable infrastructure investment per village unit, estimated at approximately 4,200 EUR, primarily for signage and basic rest facilities. The findings fed into a municipal development discussion in Sremska Mitrovica.

title: Mapping slow tourism potential in the Banat plain: a multi-criteria GIS assessment
abstract: The paper presents a GIS-based multi-criteria evaluation of slow tourism suitability across 148 cadastral municipalities in the Serbian and Romanian parts of the Banat plain. Criteria layers included road and path density, proximity to heritage sites, landscape diversity index derived from CORINE land cover data, accommodation capacity, and public transport accessibility. Each criterion was weighted using an analytic hierarchy process informed by expert judgement from seven regional tourism practitioners. The resulting suitability map identified three high-priority corridor zones totalling approximately 620 km that could support continuous cycling and walking routes. Validation against visitor numbers from available tourism statistics for 2014–2016 showed moderate agreement (Spearman r = 0.61) between predicted suitability and actual visitor overnight stays at the municipal level. The study highlights the uneven spatial distribution of basic services along potential routes as a key planning challenge in the region.

title: Peripheral region identity and route branding: lessons from three Vojvodina cycling corridors
abstract: Three cycling corridors in Vojvodina that received route branding interventions between 2014 and 2017 were compared with three unbranded corridors of similar physical characteristics. Data were collected through intercept surveys of 214 cyclists, semi-structured interviews with 18 local tourism operators, and content analysis of regional tourism promotion materials. Branded corridors registered on average 34% more reported repeat visits and scored higher on visitor satisfaction scales related to orientation and sense of place. However, branding alone did not compensate for deficiencies in accommodation supply; operators on branded routes without sufficient overnight options reported that most visitors completed routes as day trips, limiting spending. The study draws on place identity theory and rural marketing literature to discuss conditions under which route branding is likely to translate into measurable economic benefit for peripheral communities. Practical guidance is offered for route managers in flat agricultural landscapes with dispersed heritage assets.

title: Slow tourism as a development pathway for depopulating rural areas: conceptual framework and Serbian case evidence
abstract: This book chapter situates slow tourism within broader debates on counter-urbanisation, rural shrinkage, and alternative development trajectories for peripheral areas of Central and Eastern Europe. Drawing on fieldwork in four depopulating municipalities in the Mačva district and two in the Bačka subregion, the chapter compiles demographic and economic indicators from 2002 to 2018 census and statistical data and triangulates these with interview evidence from local government representatives and tourism entrepreneurs. The argument advanced is that slow tourism is not a universal remedy but may function as a partial stabilising mechanism in places where natural and cultural assets exist alongside a minimum threshold of local entrepreneurial capacity. The chapter identifies five enabling conditions and three inhibiting conditions derived from cross-case comparison. It also reviews policy instruments at the provincial and national level in Serbia that intersect with slow tourism development, noting significant gaps in coordinated support.

title: Seasonality patterns and year-round viability of cycling tourism on the Danube corridor in Serbia
abstract: Using automated inductive loop counters installed at seven points along a 140 km section of the Serbian Danube cycling corridor, this study collected continuous hourly cyclist counts over 24 months (April 2019 to March 2021). Count data were combined with weather station records and a 180-respondent online survey of past users to model seasonality and identify barriers to off-peak use. The peak-to-trough ratio was 11:1, with July–August accounting for 58% of annual passages. Regression analysis identified temperature, precipitation, and daylight hours as the primary physical drivers of demand variation, while survey data highlighted inadequate winter maintenance of surfaces and closed service facilities as the main perceived barriers to shoulder-season cycling. Scenario modelling suggested that targeted investments in two strategic rest hubs could increase shoulder-season visits by an estimated 22–28% under a moderate behavioural response assumption. The corridor's dependence on foreign visitors (67% of surveyed cyclists) is discussed in the context of cross-border tourism policy.

title: Monitoring landscape change along cycling corridors using repeat photography and volunteered geographic information: a methodological assessment
abstract: Long-term monitoring of the landscape context of cycling routes is important for both tourism quality assurance and environmental assessment but is rarely conducted systematically. This paper evaluates a low-cost monitoring approach combining fixed-point repeat photography at 48 stations along two Vojvodina cycling corridors with volunteered photographs uploaded by users of a route application over a three-year period (2022–2024). Photographs were classified manually and by a convolutional neural network fine-tuned on a labelled dataset of 2,400 regional landscape images. Agreement between manual and automated classification reached 81% for seven landscape categories. Results showed detectable changes in vegetation height, agricultural land use at corridor edges, and condition of rest infrastructure across the monitoring period. The paper discusses the feasibility of scaling the approach to regional route networks with limited institutional resources and identifies systematic biases introduced by non-uniform smartphone camera characteristics in the volunteered dataset.

title: Collapse Potential and Hydrocompression Characteristics of Loess Samples from the Titel Loess Plateau: A Laboratory Study
abstract: Loess deposits in the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia cover large areas and underlie numerous existing and planned structures. This study characterises the collapse potential and hydrocompression behaviour of undisturbed loess samples retrieved from six boreholes at depths of 1.5 m to 6.0 m on the Titel Loess Plateau. Single and double oedometer tests were conducted on 72 specimens at vertical stresses ranging from 25 kPa to 400 kPa. Collapse potential values ranged from 0.8% to 6.4%, with specimens at 3.0 m depth showing the highest susceptibility. A clear stress threshold near 75 kPa was identified below which wetting-induced deformation was minor. Initial dry density averaged 1.41 g/cm³ and natural moisture content ranged from 8% to 13%. Hydrocompression strain was found to correlate strongly with initial void ratio (R² = 0.81). Results are discussed in relation to existing classification schemes for collapse susceptibility and provide a baseline dataset for future foundation design studies in similar loess environments of the Middle Danube Basin.
venue: Geotechnics and Engineering Geology – Central European Journal

title: Influence of Wetting Sequence on Bearing Capacity of a Strip Footing Model on Loess: Small-Scale Laboratory Experiments
abstract: The timing of wetting relative to load application has practical relevance for foundation performance on collapsible loess, yet controlled experimental data comparing different wetting sequences remain scarce for Vojvodina loess. This paper reports results from 18 small-scale strip footing model tests conducted in a 600 mm × 400 mm × 350 mm steel tank filled with remoulded loess compacted to 90% of standard Proctor density. Three wetting sequences were tested: pre-wetting before load application, wetting at 50% of estimated ultimate load, and post-wetting after sustained loading. Each sequence was replicated six times. Ultimate bearing capacity under pre-wetted conditions averaged 68 kPa, compared with 142 kPa for dry specimens. Settlements at failure for mid-load wetting exceeded those of both dry and pre-wetted series by 35% to 55%. Load-settlement curves exhibited a pronounced collapse-induced displacement increment that depended strongly on applied stress at the moment of inundation. Failure mechanisms observed through a transparent sidewall showed localised shear in dry tests and more diffuse bearing failure in wetted tests. Findings suggest that current simplified approaches to bearing capacity reduction for collapsible soils may underestimate settlements under partial inundation scenarios.

title: In-Situ Plate Load Tests on Collapsible Loess with Controlled Inundation: Stress–Settlement Response at a Site in Bačka
abstract: Field data on the load-settlement behaviour of collapsible loess under controlled wetting conditions are limited, particularly for sites in the Bačka sub-region of Vojvodina. This paper presents results from eight in-situ plate load tests (300 mm × 300 mm rigid steel plate) performed at a test site near Vrbas, Serbia, at a depth of 1.0 m below ground surface. Four tests followed a standard incremental loading procedure on natural-moisture loess; four were conducted with simultaneous ponded inundation around the plate. Natural moisture content at the site was 9.5% ± 1.2% and average dry density was 1.38 g/cm³. Ultimate bearing pressure for natural-moisture tests averaged 218 kPa, while inundated tests yielded 91 kPa, representing a reduction of approximately 58%. Settlement at a reference stress of 75 kPa increased from 3.1 mm to 8.7 mm upon wetting. Subgrade reaction modulus dropped from 38 MN/m³ to 14 MN/m³. Pore water pressure transducers installed at 0.5 m depth confirmed rapid wetting front propagation within 20 minutes of ponding. A simple correction factor framework for adjusting bearing capacity calculations to account for inundation probability is proposed for use in preliminary design.

title: Screen-printed electrodes for on-farm nitrate measurement
abstract: This study presents a fully screen-printed electrochemical sensor designed for quantitative nitrate measurement under on-farm conditions. Carbon-based working electrodes were fabricated on flexible polyester substrates using a custom nitrate-selective ink incorporating a quaternary ammonium ionophore. The sensor architecture was optimised for compatibility with portable potentiostats, enabling standalone field operation without laboratory infrastructure. Analytical performance was characterised in synthetic nitrate solutions across a concentration range of 0.5–200 mg L⁻¹, yielding a linear response with a limit of detection of 0.3 mg L⁻¹. Interference studies confirmed acceptable selectivity against common co-existing anions including chloride, sulphate, and phosphate. Field validation was conducted at two agricultural sites in Vojvodina, Serbia, where sensor readings correlated closely with ion chromatography reference measurements (R² = 0.97). The electrode fabrication process was demonstrated to be reproducible at batch scale with a relative standard deviation below 4.5%. The findings confirm the viability of screen-printed nitrate sensors as cost-effective tools for precision irrigation management and rapid soil-water quality screening.

title: Detecting somatic cells in milk with an impedance sensor
abstract: Somatic cell count (SCC) is a primary indicator of bovine mastitis and overall milk quality, yet conventional cytometric methods are impractical in on-farm settings. This paper describes an impedance-based electrochemical sensor capable of detecting elevated somatic cell concentrations directly in raw milk samples. Interdigitated microelectrode arrays were fabricated via screen printing on flexible substrates and functionalised with a thin bovine serum albumin blocking layer to minimise non-specific adsorption. Impedance spectra were recorded across a frequency range of 100 Hz to 1 MHz, and principal component analysis was applied to extract discriminatory features correlating with SCC. The sensor discriminated between milk samples with SCC below 200,000 cells mL⁻¹ and those exceeding 400,000 cells mL⁻¹ with an accuracy of 91% on a blinded validation set of 60 samples. Temperature compensation was implemented to maintain measurement stability across the 4–25 °C range typical of farm environments. The results support further development of this platform as a portable, disposable tool for rapid mastitis screening at the point of care.

title: Inkjet-printed silver reference electrodes for disposable electrochemical cells
abstract: Stable, miniaturised reference electrodes are a persistent bottleneck in the fabrication of fully printed electrochemical cells. This work investigates inkjet-printed silver/silver chloride (Ag/AgCl) reference electrodes produced on polyethylene terephthalate substrates using a commercially formulated Ag nanoparticle ink followed by electrochemical chloridisation. The electrode potential stability was evaluated over a 72-hour period in phosphate-buffered saline and in simulated milk ultrafiltrate, yielding a drift of less than 1.2 mV h⁻¹. The printed reference was integrated into a three-electrode cell alongside a screen-printed carbon working electrode and demonstrated performance comparable to a conventional Ag/AgCl reference in cyclic voltammetry and differential pulse voltammetry measurements. The effect of chloride concentration in the analyte matrix on reference stability was systematically characterised, and a Nafion coating was found to reduce matrix-dependent potential shifts by 65%. Batch-to-batch reproducibility across 80 electrodes showed a standard deviation of 2.1 mV. These results establish inkjet-printed Ag/AgCl electrodes as a viable component for fully printed, single-use sensor cards intended for point-of-care agri-food applications.

title: Electrochemical detection of phosphate in drainage water using a screen-printed cobalt-phthalocyanine sensor
abstract: Phosphate runoff from agricultural fields is a significant driver of eutrophication in freshwater ecosystems, yet real-time monitoring tools remain scarce. This study reports the development of a screen-printed electrochemical sensor incorporating cobalt phthalocyanine as a catalytic modifier within a carbon-paste working electrode for the amperometric detection of phosphate. The sensor was characterised by cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and chronoamperometry in phosphate-buffered solutions. A linear calibration range of 0.1–50 mg L⁻¹ phosphate was established with a detection limit of 0.08 mg L⁻¹, meeting EU regulatory thresholds for surface water. Selectivity was evaluated against nitrate, chloride, carbonate, and common heavy metal ions; minimal interference was recorded at physiologically and environmentally relevant concentrations. The sensor was tested on drainage water samples collected from tile-drained fields in the Vojvodina region, with results validated against spectrophotometric reference analysis (R² = 0.95). A single electrode exhibited stable performance over at least 30 repeated measurements before significant signal degradation. The platform is compatible with the same fabrication workflow used for the group's nitrate sensor, supporting multi-analyte card development.

title: Dual-analyte screen-printed sensor card for simultaneous nitrate and phosphate monitoring in irrigation water
abstract: Simultaneous monitoring of multiple nutrient ions in field water samples can provide more actionable information for precision agriculture than single-analyte devices. This paper describes a dual-channel screen-printed sensor card capable of simultaneous electrochemical determination of nitrate and phosphate in a single 50 µL sample aliquot. The card integrates two independently addressable working electrodes: a nitrate-selective polymeric membrane electrode and a cobalt-phthalocyanine-modified carbon electrode for phosphate, sharing a common Ag/AgCl reference and carbon counter electrode. Multiplexed measurements were performed using a custom two-channel miniaturised potentiostat. Cross-talk between the two channels was quantified at less than 3% under standard measurement conditions. The dynamic ranges covered 0.5–200 mg L⁻¹ for nitrate and 0.1–50 mg L⁻¹ for phosphate. Field performance was validated on irrigation canal samples in Vojvodina with results agreeing with laboratory reference methods within 8%. The card format is amenable to roll-to-roll production and estimated unit cost at manufacturing scale is below €0.35. This work demonstrates the feasibility of multi-parameter printed electrochemical platforms for low-cost, distributed water quality surveillance.

title: Aerosol-jet printing of conductive tracks for flexible biosensor substrates: process optimisation and electrical characterisation
abstract: Aerosol-jet printing offers sub-millimetre feature resolution and compatibility with a wide range of functional inks, making it attractive for fabricating biosensor electrodes on curved or flexible substrates. This study investigates the process window for aerosol-jet deposition of silver and carbon inks on polyimide and paper substrates, with the goal of producing tracks suitable for integration into electrochemical biosensor layouts. Key process parameters—carrier gas flow rate, sheath gas flow rate, substrate temperature, and print speed—were systematically varied and their effects on track width, resistivity, and adhesion were quantified using a design-of-experiments approach. Optimised silver tracks achieved a sheet resistance of 18 mΩ sq⁻¹ at a sintering temperature of 130 °C, compatible with heat-sensitive substrates. Carbon tracks showed stable electrochemical activity over 500 cyclic voltammetry scans in phosphate buffer. Bending tests confirmed maintained conductivity after 1000 bend cycles at a radius of 5 mm. The optimised process parameters were subsequently applied to fabricate nitrate-selective electrodes, which matched the analytical performance of conventionally screen-printed counterparts. This work provides a foundation for incorporating aerosol-jet printing into the group's biosensor manufacturing pipeline.

title: Towards a printed biosensor patch for real-time milk pH monitoring during cold-chain transport
abstract: pH is a sensitive indicator of microbial spoilage in raw and processed milk, and its continuous monitoring during transport could significantly reduce food waste and safety incidents. This study presents a flexible, printed potentiometric pH sensor patch designed for placement inside milk transport containers. The sensing element consists of a screen-printed iridium oxide (IrOx) film deposited on a polyester substrate, prepared by anodic electrodeposition from an iridium trichloride precursor solution. The IrOx electrode exhibited a super-Nernstian response of −68.4 mV pH⁻¹ across the pH range 4.0–8.5, covering the full spoilage trajectory of bovine milk. Response time to a unit pH step change was less than 8 seconds. The patch was evaluated in raw milk samples stored at 4 °C and 10 °C over 96 hours, with pH readings correlating with parallel titration measurements and bacterial colony counts. A printed Ag/AgCl reference electrode and NFC-enabled readout circuit were co-integrated on the patch, enabling wireless data logging to a smartphone. Shelf-life prediction accuracy reached 85% compared to culture-based methods. This work positions the printed pH patch as a practical cold-chain monitoring tool compatible with existing smart packaging ecosystems.

title: Impedance spectroscopy fingerprinting of adulterated milk using printed microelectrode arrays
abstract: Milk adulteration with water, whey, or foreign substances poses serious economic and public health risks. This conference paper presents an impedimetric fingerprinting approach using screen-printed interdigitated microelectrode arrays to discriminate between authentic and adulterated bovine milk samples without requiring chemical functionalisation. Impedance spectra were recorded between 100 Hz and 10 MHz for 120 milk samples encompassing authentic full-fat milk, diluted milk (5–30% water addition), and whey-adulterated milk. A data-driven analysis pipeline combining equivalent-circuit modelling and linear discriminant analysis achieved 94% correct classification across all three categories in leave-one-out cross-validation. The sensor array was fabricated using the group's existing screen-printing process, requiring no modifications to the standard carbon-Ag/AgCl electrode stack. Measurement time per sample was under 90 seconds using a portable impedance analyser. Sensor-to-sensor reproducibility was characterised across 40 arrays, showing consistent spectral features with inter-array coefficient of variation below 5%. These results suggest that label-free impedance fingerprinting on printed microelectrodes is a viable, low-cost alternative to mid-infrared spectroscopy for rapid milk adulteration screening at collection points.

title: Screen-printed biosensors for agri-food applications: materials, fabrication and field deployment
abstract: Screen printing has emerged as a dominant manufacturing paradigm for low-cost, disposable electrochemical sensors intended for deployment outside conventional laboratory settings. This book chapter provides a comprehensive overview of screen-printed biosensor technology with a focus on agri-food quality control and environmental monitoring. The chapter opens with an introduction to functional ink formulations—carbon, silver, conductive polymer, and ion-selective membrane inks—and discusses their rheological requirements for consistent screen-printing. Fabrication workflows are described in detail, covering substrate selection, mesh specifications, curing protocols, and quality control procedures. A central section reviews electrochemical sensing modalities suited to printed platforms, including amperometry, potentiometry, impedance spectroscopy, and voltammetric techniques, with worked examples from water nitrate monitoring, milk quality assessment, and soil nutrient analysis. The chapter also addresses the practical challenges of field deployment: packaging, sample introduction, calibration strategies, and integration with wireless readout electronics. Case studies drawn from the authors' own research programmes illustrate the translation pathway from laboratory prototype to field-validated device. The chapter concludes with an outlook on emerging trends including roll-to-roll manufacturing, multi-analyte cards, and AI-assisted data interpretation for distributed sensor networks.

title: Soundness Verification of Administrative Workflow Nets Using State-Space Reduction
abstract: This paper addresses the computational challenge of verifying soundness in large WF-nets derived from administrative processes, where full state-space enumeration is intractable. We apply a combination of place-invariant analysis and siphon-trap decomposition to reduce the verification search space. Experiments were conducted on a set of 18 synthetic and 4 real-world WF-net models collected from two Serbian municipal information systems, with token counts ranging from 12 to 340 places. The reduction technique decreased average verification time by 63% compared to a naive reachability analysis baseline implemented in ProM 6. Soundness violations were identified in 6 of the 22 models, with deadlock-prone structures concentrated in models representing multi-party approval workflows. The paper includes a complexity analysis showing that the combined technique remains polynomial for free-choice WF-nets while providing useful bounds for non-free-choice cases.

title: Otkrivanje modela procesa iz evidencija događaja informacionih sistema javne uprave
abstract: Rad predstavlja primjenu algoritma za otkrivanje procesa (Alpha algoritam i njegova proširena varijanta Alpha++) na evidencijama događaja izvezenim iz dva sistema elektronske uprave u Republici Srbiji. Evidencije sadrže ukupno 14.218 slučajeva i 87.340 događaja, zabilježenih u periodu od januara 2014. do juna 2015. Otkriveni modeli upoređeni su sa referentnim proceduralnim pravilnicima koji su usvojeni zakonskim aktima. Mjere kvaliteta (fit, precision, generalizacija) izračunate su koristeći ProM 6 okvir. Prosječna vrijednost fitness-a na skupu iznosi 0,81, dok su mjere preciznosti niže (0,67), što ukazuje na značajnu varijabilnost stvarnog ponašanja u odnosu na propisane tokove. Identifikovano je pet kategorija često prisutnih odstupanja, uključujući preskakanje obaveznih koraka ovjere i ponavljanje aktivnosti koje bi trebale biti jednokratne.

title: Alignment-Based Conformance Checking for Compliance Auditing: A Case Study in University Admissions
abstract: Alignment-based conformance checking computes an optimal correspondence between observed event sequences in a log and the traces permitted by a reference Petri-net model, minimising total move costs. This paper applies the technique to audit the student admissions process at a mid-sized Serbian public university over three enrolment cycles (2013–2015), using an event log of 6,042 cases extracted from the student information system. A reference WF-net was constructed from the official admissions rulebook. The cost function was calibrated with domain experts to reflect regulatory severity of deviations. Results show that 18.4% of cases contain at least one non-conforming move, with the most frequent deviation being the registration of a candidate's documents before the official application window opens. Deviations cluster in the first three days of each cycle. The paper discusses how identified deviation patterns can be fed back into process redesign and how cost calibration affects which violations surface first.

title: Petri-net semantike za modelovanje izuzetaka u administrativnim tokovima rada
abstract: Standardne WF-mreže pretpostavljaju da je svaki slučaj obrađen u skladu s unaprijed definisanim normalnim tokom, što ne odgovara realnosti administrativnih procesa u kojima su izuzeci (žalbe, vanredni zahtjevi, zakonski rokovi) česti i dobro dokumentovani. Ovaj rad predlaže proširenje WF-mreža koje uvodi posebnu klasu prelaza za izuzetke i odgovarajuće mehanizme poništavanja djelimično izvršenih tokova. Formalna semantika razrađena je kroz operacionu semantiku zasnivanu na oznakama (labeled transition systems), a prikazane su i transformacije kojima se prošireni model prevodi u standardni Coloured Petri Net radi analize u alatu CPN Tools. Primjena je ilustrovana na modelu žalbenog postupka u sistemu visokog obrazovanja s 9 tipova izuzetaka. Diskutovana su ograničenja pristupa kada je broj mogućih interakcija između izuzetaka eksponencijalan.

title: Token-Based Replay with Partial Synchronisation for Conformance Checking in Long-Running Cases
abstract: Token-based replay is a widely used technique for conformance checking but struggles with long-running process instances in which the model and log diverge substantially in the middle of a case, causing token accumulation artefacts that distort fitness measures. This paper proposes a partial-synchronisation extension of the standard replay procedure that introduces checkpoint markers derived from obligatory activities in the reference model. Replay resets at each successfully synchronised checkpoint, limiting error propagation across the full trace. The technique is evaluated on three event logs from Serbian healthcare administration (appointment scheduling, discharge documentation and referral management) comprising 8,900, 12,400 and 5,100 cases respectively. Compared to standard token-based replay, the proposed method reduces the median absolute error in fitness estimation from 0.09 to 0.03 on the same logs, as validated against manually labelled ground truth for a 500-case sample. Runtime overhead is less than 12% relative to the baseline.

title: Automated Generation of Audit Reports from Conformance Checking Results Using Rule-Based Templates
abstract: Conformance checking produces quantitative deviation metrics that are technically precise but not directly usable by compliance auditors without process-mining expertise. This paper describes a system that translates conformance checking output – specifically alignment diagnostics exported from ProM – into structured audit reports using a rule-based template engine. Rules encode mappings from deviation types (skipped activities, wrong ordering, repeated mandatory steps) to regulatory references drawn from Serbian administrative law. The system was piloted at a provincial government directorate processing 3,200 administrative cases over six months. Auditors evaluated 30 automatically generated reports against manually written reports for the same cases, rating completeness (mean 4.1/5), accuracy (mean 4.4/5) and readability (mean 3.7/5). The main shortcoming noted was insufficient contextualisation of deviations involving discretionary decisions. The paper discusses how the rule base can be maintained as regulations change and outlines integration with existing document management systems.

title: Uticaj kvaliteta evidencije događaja na pouzdanost provjere usklađenosti: empirijska studija
abstract: Provjera usklađenosti zasnovana na poravnavanju osjetljiva je na kvalitet ulaznih evidencija događaja: greške u oznakama aktivnosti, nedostajuće vremenske oznake i netačna dodjela slučajeva mogu dovesti do lažnih pozitiva i lažnih negativa u detekciji kršenja. Ova studija mjeri taj uticaj na kontrolisanom skupu evidencija s poznatim tačnim vrijednostima usklađenosti, u koji su programski ubačene greške različitih vrsta i intenziteta. Testirana su četiri scenarija: zamjena 1%, 5%, 10% i 20% oznaka aktivnosti slučajnim greškama. Za svaki scenario izračunate su vrijednosti preciznosti i odziva detekcije kršenja u odnosu na referentno stanje. Rezultati pokazuju da već 5% zamijenjenih oznaka smanjuje odziv detekcije za 0,14, dok preciznost ostaje relativno stabilna do praga od 10%. Rad predlaže metriku za procjenu pouzdanosti evidencije (Log Reliability Index) i pragove iznad kojih revizorske nalaze treba uzimati s oprezom.

title: Discovering Hierarchical Process Models from Aggregated Administrative Logs Using Decomposition-Based Mining
abstract: Administrative processes in large organisations are executed by multiple departments and recorded in separate information systems, producing event logs that are aggregated for analysis but retain heterogeneous granularity. Flat discovery algorithms applied to such logs produce spaghetti models with low precision. This paper applies a decomposition-based mining approach that partitions the log by activity clusters identified through Directly-Follows Graph community detection, mines a sub-model per cluster, and composes the results into a hierarchical Petri-net process model. The approach is applied to an integrated event log from a Serbian university's central administration, covering 11 departments, 44 activity types, 19,600 cases and spanning academic years 2017–2020. The hierarchical model achieves a precision of 0.74 and fitness of 0.83, compared to 0.48 precision and 0.86 fitness for a flat Inductive Miner baseline. Manual inspection by three domain experts rated the hierarchical model as substantially more interpretable (mean 4.2 vs. 2.6 on a 5-point scale).

title: Provjera usklađenosti u sistemima upravljanja dokumentima: integracija sa DMS platformom otvorenog koda
abstract: Sistemi za upravljanje dokumentima (DMS) generišu interne revizijske tragove koji su strukturno slični evidencijama događaja u upravljanju procesima, ali rijetko se koriste za formalnu provjeru usklađenosti. Ovaj rad opisuje arhitekturu i implementaciju modula koji se integriše sa DMS platformom otvorenog koda Alfresco Community Edition i automatski prevodi revizijski trag u XES format pogodan za provjeru usklađenosti pomoću ProM-a. Modul je konfigurisan da pokreće provjeru usklađenosti na kraju svakog radnog dana i generiše izvještaje o slučajevima koji odstupaju od referentnih WF-net modela. Testiran je u pilot primjeni u jednoj pravnoj firmi u Novom Sadu tokom šest mjeseci (4.800 slučajeva). Ukupno je identifikovano 312 slučajeva s kršenjem procedura, od kojih su 87% potvrđeni od strane menadžera kao stvarna kršenja. Rad diskutuje troškove integracije, performansna ograničenja i plan za proširenje na oblak okruženje.

title: Temporal Conformance Checking: Measuring Time-Constraint Violations in Administrative Processes
abstract: Standard conformance checking assesses whether activities occur in the correct order but does not directly evaluate whether they occur within prescribed time limits, which are central to administrative law in many jurisdictions. This paper extends alignment-based conformance checking with a temporal dimension by annotating the reference WF-net with time constraints expressed as intervals on transitions, drawn from statutory deadlines in Serbian administrative procedure law. The extended alignment algorithm assigns additional cost to moves that satisfy activity ordering but violate timing constraints. The method is validated on two event logs: case handling at a cadastral office (7,200 cases, 2019–2021) and permit processing at a municipal secretariat (3,100 cases, 2020–2022). Temporal violations account for 31% and 44% of total non-conformance cost respectively, a portion that would be invisible to order-only conformance checking. The paper discusses how statutory deadline changes propagate into model annotations and reports runtime performance on logs of varying size.
