title: Benchmarking Conformance Checking Tools on Real-World Public Sector Event Logs from the Western Balkans
abstract: The process-mining literature relies predominantly on benchmark datasets from Western European manufacturing and healthcare contexts, leaving open the question of whether tool performance generalises to public sector organisations in lower-resource environments with different regulatory structures. This paper assembles a benchmark corpus of nine event logs from Serbian, Bosnian and North Macedonian public institutions (total 148,000 cases), covering permit processing, social welfare case management and tax administration. Four conformance checking tools are evaluated: ProM 6 (alignment plug-in), PM4Py, Apromore and a standalone implementation of the token-based replay algorithm. Evaluation criteria include fitness, precision, runtime, memory consumption and robustness to missing data. PM4Py achieves the best runtime-to-quality trade-off for logs exceeding 50,000 cases; ProM produces the highest precision scores but with substantially higher memory demand. The corpus and evaluation scripts are released under an open licence to support reproducibility.

title: Integracija rudarenja procesa u internu reviziju javnih preduzeća: okvir i studija slučaja
abstract: Interna revizija u javnim preduzećima oslanja se pretežno na uzorkovanje i ručnu provjeru dokumentacije, što ograničava pokrivenost i povećava troškove. Ovaj rad predlaže okvir za integraciju rudarenja procesa u ciklus interne revizije koji se sastoji od četiri faze: ekstrakcija evidencije događaja, otkrivanje modela, provjera usklađenosti i interpretacija nalaza uz podršku revizora. Okvir je primjenjen u studiji slučaja u javnom komunalnom preduzeću iz Vojvodine s 340 zaposlenih, gdje su analizirani procesi nabavke i fakturisanja tokom 2023. godine (ukupno 2.100 slučajeva nabavke, 18.400 događaja). Provjera usklađenosti otkrila je 214 slučajeva nabavke u kojima je plaćanje evidentirano prije formalnog prijema robe, što predstavlja kršenje internih kontrolnih procedura. Nalaz je potvrđen ručnom verifikacijom uzorka od 40 slučajeva s tačnošću od 95%. Rad diskutuje organizacione i tehničke preduslove za uvođenje pristupa u javnim preduzećima s ograničenim IT kapacitetima.

title: Partition-Aware Inverted Index Construction for Heterogeneous Document Streams
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of building inverted indexes over document streams that vary widely in language, length, and encoding. We propose a partition-aware construction algorithm that assigns incoming documents to index shards based on a lightweight language-and-length feature hash, reducing cross-shard query fan-out by approximately 34% compared to round-robin partitioning on a corpus of 12 million news articles drawn from four Balkan-language feeds. Index build time on a six-node cluster decreased by 18% while median query latency fell from 47 ms to 31 ms at the 50th percentile. The approach requires no prior knowledge of the full corpus distribution and adapts incrementally as stream statistics shift. Experiments use Apache Lucene as the underlying segment engine, with a custom coordinator layer implemented in Java. Recall at rank 10 remains within 0.4% of a monolithic baseline.

title: Sleep duration and fasting glucose in healthcare shift workers: a cross-sectional analysis in a tertiary hospital in Vojvodina
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between objectively measured sleep duration and fasting plasma glucose in 187 healthcare workers (nurses and physicians) employed at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad. Participants wore wrist actigraphs for 14 consecutive days, and blood samples were collected on two separate mornings following both day and night shifts. Workers rotating between day and night shifts had a mean sleep duration of 5.8 hours on work days compared with 7.1 hours on days off. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and physical activity, each one-hour reduction in mean sleep duration was associated with a 0.18 mmol/L increase in fasting glucose (95% CI: 0.09–0.27). Workers on rotating shifts showed a 1.7-fold higher prevalence of impaired fasting glucose compared with fixed day workers. These findings suggest that even modest, chronic sleep curtailment associated with shift schedules may contribute to dysglycaemia independent of obesity.

title: Shift work duration as a cumulative exposure and prevalent type 2 diabetes: findings from a retrospective cohort in Serbian industrial workers
abstract: This retrospective cohort study used occupational health records from three large manufacturing companies in Vojvodina province to examine the association between cumulative years of shift work and prevalent type 2 diabetes. A total of 1,042 male workers were included, with a median follow-up of 16 years. Shift work history was reconstructed from employment records and self-reported questionnaires. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios after adjustment for BMI, smoking, alcohol use, and family history of diabetes. Workers with more than 10 years of rotating shift work had an odds ratio of 1.83 (95% CI: 1.31–2.55) for type 2 diabetes compared with permanent day workers. A dose-response pattern was observed across tertiles of cumulative shift work exposure. The association was stronger in workers who began shift schedules before age 35. These results support a role for prolonged circadian disruption in diabetes aetiology in an Eastern European occupational context.

title: Clock gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of shift workers with and without dysglycaemia
abstract: We investigated the expression of core clock genes BMAL1, CLOCK, PER1, PER2, and CRY1 in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) collected from 62 rotating-shift workers and 31 permanent day workers at a textile plant in southern Vojvodina. Blood was drawn at standardised times relative to individual melatonin onset to control for phase differences. Rotating-shift workers with impaired fasting glucose (n = 21) showed significantly attenuated amplitude of PER1 oscillation compared with normoglycaemic shift workers and day workers. BMAL1 expression was inversely correlated with HOMA-IR across the full sample (r = −0.41, p < 0.001). No significant differences were found in CLOCK expression. These molecular findings align with the hypothesis that circadian disruption in shift workers attenuates the peripheral clock, which may in turn impair transcriptional regulation of glucose-metabolising enzymes. The small sample size and cross-sectional design are acknowledged limitations requiring replication in longitudinal work.

title: Melatonin receptor gene variants (MTNR1B rs10830963) and differential diabetes risk in shift versus day workers: a candidate gene study
abstract: The MTNR1B rs10830963 G allele has been associated with impaired early insulin secretion in general population studies. We tested whether this variant modifies the relationship between shift work and incident type 2 diabetes in a prospective occupational cohort of 734 workers from four production facilities in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin, followed over a median of 6.2 years. Among G-allele carriers working rotating shifts, the incidence rate of type 2 diabetes was 12.4 per 1,000 person-years, compared with 5.7 in non-carriers on rotating shifts and 4.9 in G-allele carriers on day shifts. Cox proportional hazards models yielded a hazard ratio of 2.14 (95% CI: 1.42–3.22) for G-allele carriers on rotating shifts versus day-shift non-carriers, after adjusting for age, BMI, and family history. Interaction tests suggested a super-additive effect on the absolute scale. Findings indicate that individuals with compromised melatonin-mediated insulin secretion may be disproportionately harmed by shift work schedules.

title: Continuous glucose monitoring profiles across shift cycles: within-person variability in a small cohort of rotating-shift police officers
abstract: We used blinded continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) over two consecutive shift cycles—day week, night week—in 18 male police officers on a fixed rotation schedule in Novi Sad. Participants wore the CGM device continuously for 14 days and completed a dietary diary. Outcomes included mean glucose, coefficient of variation (CV), time above 7.8 mmol/L, and time in range (3.9–7.8 mmol/L). During the night-work week, mean 24-hour glucose was 5.9 mmol/L compared with 5.4 mmol/L during the day-work week (p = 0.04). Time above 7.8 mmol/L was approximately doubled during night weeks (mean 38 vs. 19 minutes/day). CV was higher in night weeks, indicating greater glycaemic instability. Dietary caloric intake did not differ significantly between conditions, though meal timing was shifted by approximately three hours during night weeks. This exploratory study demonstrates that CGM can reveal acute glycaemic consequences of circadian misalignment even in individuals not classified as diabetic.

title: Shift work and type 2 diabetes: epidemiology, mechanisms, and clinical considerations
abstract: This chapter reviews the epidemiological evidence linking shift work to type 2 diabetes risk, synthesising data from prospective cohort studies, meta-analyses, and mechanistic human experimental work published through 2021. The chapter covers four proposed pathways: (1) circadian misalignment reducing insulin sensitivity independently of sleep loss; (2) sleep curtailment impairing glucose tolerance through appetite hormone dysregulation and reduced physical activity; (3) disrupted clock gene expression in peripheral metabolic tissues; and (4) genetic susceptibility variants in melatonin signalling. Particular attention is given to heterogeneity across shift types, with evidence suggesting that rotating shifts confer greater risk than fixed night work. The chapter also addresses methodological challenges in shift work research, including inconsistent exposure definitions and confounding by socioeconomic status. Clinical implications for screening frequency and preventive intervention timing in occupational health settings are discussed, drawing on published guidelines from European diabetes societies.

title: Effect of a structured sleep extension intervention on insulin sensitivity in rotating-shift workers with prediabetes: a randomised pilot trial
abstract: We conducted a 12-week parallel-group randomised pilot trial in 54 rotating-shift workers at a food-processing plant who met criteria for prediabetes (fasting glucose 5.6–6.9 mmol/L or HbA1c 39–47 mmol/mol). Participants were allocated to a sleep extension protocol (target: one additional hour per sleep episode, supported by a brief behavioural session and written guidance) or usual care. Primary outcomes were HOMA-IR and fasting glucose at 12 weeks. Actigraph-verified sleep increased by a mean of 42 minutes in the intervention group and 4 minutes in controls. HOMA-IR improved by 0.31 units (95% CI: 0.08–0.54) in the intervention arm relative to controls, and fasting glucose decreased by 0.22 mmol/L (95% CI: 0.07–0.37). Adherence was moderate; 61% of intervention participants achieved the target on at least 5 of 7 nights per week. No serious adverse events were recorded. The trial was not powered for definitive conclusions but provides feasibility data for a larger confirmatory study.

title: Actigraphy-derived social jetlag and HbA1c trajectory over 3 years in a Vojvodina shift-worker cohort
abstract: Social jetlag—the discrepancy between circadian timing on work days versus free days—was quantified using actigraphy in 312 workers enrolled in an ongoing prospective cohort study in Vojvodina. HbA1c was measured at baseline, 18 months, and 36 months. At baseline, mean social jetlag was 1.6 hours (SD 0.9) in rotating-shift workers compared with 0.5 hours (SD 0.4) in permanent day workers. Mixed-effects linear models showed that each additional hour of social jetlag was associated with a 0.09% per-year increase in HbA1c (95% CI: 0.04–0.14) after adjustment for BMI trajectory, dietary quality score, and baseline HbA1c. This association was attenuated but remained significant after additional adjustment for total sleep time, suggesting that circadian phase misalignment contributes to glycaemic deterioration beyond sleep duration alone. Workers with social jetlag exceeding 2 hours and BMI above 27 kg/m² showed the steepest HbA1c trajectories. Formal mediation analyses are planned at the five-year follow-up.

title: Prevalence of metabolic syndrome components across shift categories in female textile workers: baseline data from the VojShift cohort
abstract: We report baseline metabolic characterisation of 489 female textile workers enrolled in the VojShift prospective cohort across four factories in Vojvodina. Participants were classified as permanent day workers (n = 162), fixed night workers (n = 89), or rotating shift workers (n = 238). Metabolic syndrome was defined using IDF criteria. Prevalence of metabolic syndrome was 18.5% in day workers, 26.9% in fixed night workers, and 31.1% in rotating shift workers. Waist circumference and triglycerides were the components that differed most markedly across groups. After adjustment for age, years of employment, and educational level, rotating shift work was associated with an odds ratio of 1.74 (95% CI: 1.09–2.77) for metabolic syndrome compared with day work. Sensitivity analyses excluding participants with self-reported prior diabetes diagnosis did not materially alter estimates. These baseline data establish the foundation for prospective incidence analyses in subsequent follow-up waves.

title: Steady-State Voltage Profile Analysis in Radial Low-Voltage Feeders with Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: This paper presents a steady-state power flow analysis of a 0.4 kV radial distribution feeder in an urban residential area of Novi Sad, incorporating measured generation profiles from twelve rooftop photovoltaic installations aggregating 48 kWp of installed capacity. A backward–forward sweep load flow algorithm was implemented and validated against one week of SCADA measurements. Voltage profiles were computed under three penetration scenarios: 20 %, 50 %, and 80 % of feeder customers operating as prosumers. Results indicate that reverse power flow emerges at penetration levels above 35 % under peak irradiance conditions, causing end-of-feeder voltage to exceed the EN 50160 upper limit of 1.10 p.u. for approximately 4.2 % of annual hours at 80 % penetration. The sensitivity of voltage rise to feeder impedance ratio X/R was quantified, showing that resistive-dominant cables characteristic of low-voltage grids amplify voltage deviations by a factor of 1.6 compared to equivalent medium-voltage lines. The study provides a benchmark dataset and simulation framework subsequently used in follow-up hosting capacity work.

title: Reactive Power Compensation Using Fixed Capacitor Banks in Distribution Feeders with Variable Generation: A Sensitivity Study
abstract: Fixed shunt capacitor banks remain common in Serbian low-voltage distribution infrastructure. This paper evaluates their effectiveness under variable photovoltaic generation using a sensitivity analysis approach applied to a representative 0.4 kV test feeder parameterised from field measurements in the Vojvodina region. Thirty-two daily generation profiles collected over two seasons were used as input. Power factor correction was assessed at three placement positions along the feeder, and the interaction between capacitor injection and reverse power flow was examined. The analysis shows that fixed capacitor banks installed at the mid-feeder position reduce reactive power import by 22 % on average but cause overvoltage exceedances of up to 0.04 p.u. during midday peak generation periods, a finding that is absent in purely passive feeder conditions. The paper quantifies the trade-off between power factor improvement and voltage constraint violation as a function of installed photovoltaic capacity, providing practical guidelines for distribution system operators considering retrofit compensation strategies without active voltage control.

title: Smart Inverter Volt–Var Control for Voltage Regulation in Prosumer-Integrated Low-Voltage Feeders
abstract: Grid-connected photovoltaic inverters with programmable Volt–VAr (Q(U)) characteristic functions can absorb or inject reactive power in response to local voltage measurements, providing a distributed voltage regulation mechanism without centralised communication. This paper implements and tests three Q(U) characteristic shapes—linear, piecewise linear with deadband, and cosφ(P)—on a hardware-in-the-loop test bench using an RTDS real-time simulator interfaced with a commercial 5 kW single-phase inverter. Feeder parameters replicate a 380 m urban cable section. Simulations and hardware experiments were conducted for 120 irradiance scenarios generated from one year of meteorological data for Novi Sad. The piecewise linear characteristic with a ±2 % voltage deadband reduces voltage violations at the feeder end by 87 % compared to unity power factor operation while increasing inverter reactive current by no more than 18 % of rated current. Additional reactive losses of 1.1 % of annual energy yield are recorded, representing the compensation cost. The experimental setup and parameter tuning procedure are described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Impact of Electric Vehicle Charging on Voltage Quality and Hosting Capacity in Residential Low-Voltage Feeders
abstract: The simultaneous rollout of rooftop photovoltaics and private electric vehicle (EV) charging in residential areas creates competing and sometimes complementary effects on feeder voltage profiles. This paper extends an existing hosting capacity framework to include EV load as a stochastic variable characterised by charging start time, state-of-charge on arrival, and rated charger power. Input distributions were estimated from a mobility survey of 340 respondents in the greater Novi Sad area conducted in 2019. Three charging strategies are compared: uncontrolled immediate charging, night-valley charging, and solar-matched daytime charging. Results on a 0.4 kV feeder model show that uncontrolled charging during evening hours reduces hosting capacity by up to 9 kWp relative to the no-EV baseline because voltage drop from EV load adds to end-of-feeder sag during low-generation periods, restricting the permissible generation envelope. Daytime solar-matched charging, by contrast, partially offsets voltage rise and increases median hosting capacity by 6 kWp. The paper identifies feeder impedance as the dominant factor moderating these interactions.

title: Feeder Reconfiguration as a Hosting Capacity Enhancement Tool in Meshed Low-Voltage Networks
abstract: Low-voltage distribution networks in newer urban developments in Serbia are built with a meshed cable topology but operated radially through normally-open points. Switching the normally-open point changes feeder lengths, impedance distributions, and load sharing, all of which affect hosting capacity for distributed generation. This study systematically evaluates feeder reconfiguration as a low-cost hosting capacity enhancement measure for a 0.4 kV meshed network of 84 nodes representing a residential district in Novi Sad. A brute-force enumeration of all 12 candidate normally-open point positions is combined with the stochastic hosting capacity assessment method from previous work. Results show that the optimal normally-open point configuration raises the network-wide hosting capacity by 23 % compared to the default as-built configuration, without any hardware investment. The improvement is driven primarily by impedance balancing across two parallel cable routes. The sensitivity of results to load growth assumptions of 1 % and 2 % annual increase is also reported, showing that reconfiguration benefits persist over a 10-year horizon under both scenarios.

title: Battery Storage Sizing for Voltage Support in Low-Voltage Feeders: A Cost–Benefit Approach
abstract: Behind-the-meter battery energy storage systems can flatten prosumer net load profiles and provide reactive power support to the local feeder. This paper addresses the problem of selecting storage capacity and power rating to maximise a combined economic and technical objective consisting of prosumer electricity bill reduction, avoided distribution system operator penalty costs for voltage violations, and degradation cost of the battery over a 10-year planning horizon. A mixed-integer linear programming formulation is developed and applied to four prosumer archetypes derived from clustering 18 months of smart meter data collected from 210 customers in Novi Sad. Storage sizes in the range 3–12 kWh are evaluated with lithium iron phosphate chemistry. Results indicate that economically optimal storage sizes for the studied archetypes fall between 4.5 kWh and 7 kWh, constrained primarily by battery degradation cost rather than voltage benefit. Sensitivity to electricity tariff structure shows that time-of-use tariffs with a peak-to-off-peak ratio above 2.4 significantly shift optimal sizes upward.

title: Probabilistic Hosting Capacity Maps for Low-Voltage Distribution Networks: A Methodology for Municipal-Scale Assessment
abstract: Distribution system operators and municipal planners require spatially aggregated information on available photovoltaic hosting capacity to guide permitting decisions and grid investment planning. This paper proposes a methodology for producing probabilistic hosting capacity maps at the level of an entire municipal distribution network by applying a stratified feeder sampling approach. Feeders are classified into six morphological types based on cable length, cross-section, and customer density. For each type, 500 stochastic hosting capacity assessments are performed. The resulting per-type distributions are spatially assigned to all 1 140 low-voltage feeders in a medium-sized municipality in the Vojvodina region, producing a rasterised map with 100 m resolution. The map is validated against 23 actual photovoltaic connection applications processed by the distribution system operator in 2022–2023, showing that 91 % of accepted connections fell within the predicted feasible range. Limitations of the stratification approach and data requirements from the distribution system operator are discussed in detail.

title: Wake-up receiver circuit for asynchronous event-driven body-area networks: design and measured sensitivity
abstract: Polling-based duty cycling requires a node to activate its main radio at fixed intervals regardless of whether data are ready, wasting energy between physiological events. A wake-up receiver (WuRx) circuit that remains continuously active at very low power can replace this periodic wakeup. This paper presents a WuRx designed in 130 nm CMOS consuming 4.2 µW from a 1.0 V supply. The circuit uses an envelope detector followed by a three-stage comparator with hysteresis to decode an amplitude-shift-keyed wake-up beacon at 868 MHz. Measured sensitivity was −62 dBm at a target false-alarm rate of one per hour. Selectivity to adjacent channels was verified in a shielded box with an interferer 3 MHz offset at levels up to −20 dBm. Die area was 0.19 mm². When integrated into a complete sensor node alongside a CC1310 main radio, the WuRx reduced mean idle-state current from 18.4 µA (timer-based duty cycle at 1% duty) to 6.7 µA under a traffic model representative of a cardiac event monitor with bursts averaging twice per hour.

title: Effect of mast flexibility on dynamic load distribution in counterbalance forklifts during acceleration
abstract: Counterbalance forklifts are typically modelled as rigid multibody systems for stability assessment, yet the mast exhibits measurable elastic deformation under combined vertical and inertial loads. This study incorporates a flexible mast beam—discretised into twelve Timoshenko beam elements—into an otherwise rigid vehicle model built in MSC Adams. The flexible model is parameterised using experimentally derived stiffness and damping values obtained from hammer-impact tests on a 2.5-tonne capacity forklift. Simulations are run for forward acceleration profiles of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 m/s², with fork heights ranging from 0.3 m to 3.6 m and pallet masses of 500 kg, 1000 kg, and 1500 kg. Mast tip deflection reaches 47 mm at maximum fork height under 1.5 m/s² acceleration, shifting the effective load centroid forward by 31 mm relative to the rigid-body prediction. This shift reduces the calculated rear-axle contact force by up to 9.3% and narrows the stability margin accordingly. The results highlight that rigid-body models may overestimate stability reserves when forks are elevated above 2.5 m.

title: Simulation of lateral load shift in automated guided vehicles carrying asymmetric pallets on ramp surfaces
abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) used in warehouse distribution centres increasingly traverse ramp transitions of 3–8° grade. This paper investigates lateral load shift experienced by a unit-load AGV carrying asymmetrically loaded pallets—mass offset up to 250 mm from the pallet centre—on ramp surfaces combined with crossfall angles of 0°, 1°, and 2°. A rigid multibody model with four-wheel contact is built in MATLAB/Simscape Multibody. Pallet–deck interaction is represented by a compliant contact layer with experimentally fitted stiffness of 4.2 kN/mm. A design-of-experiments matrix covering pallet offset, ramp grade, crossfall, and vehicle speed (0.3–1.2 m/s) produces 144 simulation runs. The lateral shift of the pallet centroid exceeds 18 mm in 23% of configurations, which breaches the aisle-clearance tolerance used by the logistics partner supplying real-world dimensional data. Sensitivity analysis identifies ramp grade as the dominant factor, contributing 51% of the total variance in centroid displacement. Recommendations for speed governor settings and ramp geometry limits are provided.

title: Dynamics of a bridge crane trolley subject to simultaneous hoisting and traversing motion
abstract: Bridge crane operations in heavy manufacturing facilities frequently involve simultaneous hoisting and traversal, producing coupled pendulum-like swing of the suspended load. This study develops a four-degree-of-freedom rigid-body model of a 10-tonne single-girder crane in which the rope is modelled as a rigid link with adjustable length. Equations of motion are derived analytically and integrated numerically using a fourth-order Runge–Kutta scheme with a 1 ms timestep. Three traversal velocity profiles—trapezoidal, S-curve, and step—are compared for rope lengths of 2 m, 4 m, and 8 m and hoisting rates of 0 m/min, 2 m/min, and 4 m/min. Peak load swing angle reaches 7.4° under the step profile at 8 m rope length, more than twice the value recorded under the S-curve profile. Simultaneous hoisting during traversal increases peak swing by 0.8–1.6° relative to traversal alone. The model is validated against measurements from a scaled laboratory gantry equipped with an inertial measurement unit attached to the load. Mean angular error across all validation runs is 0.31°.

title: Coupled rigid–flexible model of a telescopic crane boom during luffing with payload oscillation
abstract: Telescopic crane booms undergo significant elastic deformation during luffing at extended boom lengths, and this deformation couples with payload pendulum dynamics in ways that rigid-body models do not capture. A co-simulation framework is developed linking a rigid-body vehicle–slewing model in MSC Adams with a geometrically nonlinear beam finite-element model of the two-section telescopic boom in ANSYS Mechanical. The two solvers exchange generalised forces and displacements at the boom–vehicle interface at each 5 ms co-simulation step. Luffing from 20° to 60° is simulated over durations of 8 s, 12 s, and 20 s for boom extensions of 8 m, 12 m, and 16 m carrying a 1.5-tonne payload. Boom-tip deflection under fast luffing (8 s) at 16 m extension reaches 112 mm and generates payload swing amplitudes 2.3 times larger than the rigid-boom prediction. Structural stress at the boom root during these manoeuvres reaches 87% of the yield stress assumed for S355 steel, indicating that luffing speed limits in current operating manuals may be insufficient at maximum extension.

title: Tip-over risk index for warehouse forklifts traversing uneven floor surfaces: a simulation-based approach
abstract: Industrial floor surfaces in older warehouse buildings exhibit surface height deviations up to 15 mm per metre, which can dynamically alter the wheel-contact geometry of a counterbalance forklift and reduce tip-over safety margins. This paper defines a scalar Tip-Over Risk Index (TORI) derived from the instantaneous zero-moment-point displacement normalised by the current stability polygon area. A rigid multibody simulation model incorporates measured floor surface profiles from three warehouses in the Vojvodina region, digitised using a floor profiler at 50 mm longitudinal resolution. Simulations cover travel speeds of 2, 4, and 6 km/h, fork heights of 0.5 m and 2.0 m, and payload masses of 500 kg and 1500 kg. TORI exceeds 0.85 (a proposed alert threshold) in 11% of simulation timesteps at 6 km/h, 2.0 m fork height, and 1500 kg payload on the most uneven measured profile. A speed–height–mass threshold chart derived from the results is proposed as input to an onboard driver assistance system. The methodology is designed to be portable to other vehicle types with minimal re-parameterisation.

title: Long-term performance of foam-in-place gaskets in outdoor electrical cabinets: a comparative study with die-cut EPDM
abstract: Foam-in-place (FIP) polyurethane gaskets applied to twelve sheet-metal electrical cabinet covers were compared with die-cut EPDM strips on twelve matched cabinets over a 36-month outdoor exposure period in a semi-urban environment near Novi Sad. Both cabinet populations were inspected every six months for visual defects, and sample gaskets were removed annually for laboratory compression-set and Shore A testing. FIP gaskets maintained lower compression-set values (mean 17 % at 36 months) compared with EPDM strips (mean 29 %), and showed less dimensional variability across the bead cross-section. However, four FIP samples exhibited adhesion loss at corners after 24 months when substrate surface preparation was below the specified cleanliness grade. Internal humidity loggers showed that cabinets with FIP gaskets experienced 11 % fewer condensation events over the monitoring period. Cost-benefit analysis incorporating material, application labour, and seal replacement is also presented.

title: Secrecy Capacity of a Single-Relay Decode-and-Forward Network over Rayleigh Fading Channels
abstract: This paper derives closed-form expressions for the ergodic secrecy capacity of a three-node decode-and-forward relay network in which a single passive eavesdropper intercepts the relay-to-destination link. The source-relay and relay-destination channels are modelled as independent Rayleigh fading links, while the eavesdropper channel follows an independent Rayleigh distribution with a separately parameterised average SNR. Using moment-generating function techniques, the authors obtain tight closed-form bounds on the ergodic secrecy rate and validate these against 10^6-run Monte Carlo simulations. Results show that relay-assisted transmission improves the secrecy rate by up to 3.1 dB relative to a direct link at an average SNR of 20 dB when the eavesdropper is located midway between relay and destination. The impact of relay placement on secrecy is quantified through a parametric sweep over 21 discrete positions along the relay-to-destination path.

title: Outage-Based Secrecy Analysis for Amplify-and-Forward Relaying with an Uninformed Eavesdropper
abstract: The secrecy outage probability (SOP) is studied for an amplify-and-forward cooperative relay system in which neither the legitimate nodes nor the relay have access to instantaneous channel state information of the eavesdropper link. Both the main channel and the eavesdropper channel are subject to independent Nakagami-m fading with integer fading parameters. An exact analytical expression for the SOP is derived using incomplete gamma function identities, and an asymptotic expression valid at high SNR is obtained to characterise the secrecy diversity order. Numerical evaluation is performed for fading parameters m ∈ {1, 2, 3} and SNR values from 0 to 30 dB. The diversity order is shown to be min(m_sr, m_rd), independent of the eavesdropper's fading parameter. Monte Carlo simulations over 5×10^5 channel realisations confirm the analytical results to within 0.4% relative error across all scenarios tested.

title: Effect of Multiple Passive Eavesdroppers on Secrecy Capacity in Dual-Hop Relay Networks
abstract: This work extends single-eavesdropper secrecy analysis to scenarios with K colluding passive eavesdroppers distributed according to a homogeneous Poisson point process around the relay node. A dual-hop decode-and-forward architecture is assumed. The combined eavesdropper channel capacity is modelled using order statistics of exponential random variables, and the secrecy capacity is characterised through its cumulative distribution function for K ranging from 1 to 10. For K = 5 at an average main-channel SNR of 15 dB and an eavesdropper SNR 6 dB lower, the mean secrecy rate drops by approximately 1.8 bits/s/Hz compared to the single-eavesdropper case. The paper also quantifies the minimum main-channel SNR advantage required to maintain a target secrecy rate of 1 bit/s/Hz as a function of K, providing a practically useful design curve for relay-network planners.

title: Physical-Layer Security in Cooperative Networks: Models, Bounds and Open Problems
abstract: This book chapter surveys information-theoretic approaches to physical-layer security in multi-hop cooperative wireless networks. It covers the wiretap channel model from its origins, extensions to relay-assisted topologies, and the distinction between ergodic and outage-based secrecy metrics. The chapter systematically compares decode-and-forward, amplify-and-forward, and compress-and-forward relay protocols from a secrecy perspective, discussing the trade-offs in system complexity and achievable secrecy rate. Special attention is given to the role of fading channel statistics—Rayleigh, Rician, and Nakagami-m—and their influence on secrecy diversity order. The chapter concludes with a structured discussion of open problems including imperfect channel estimation at the eavesdropper, heterogeneous relay topologies, and the interaction between cooperative beamforming and secrecy constraints. The target audience is postgraduate students and researchers entering the field.

title: Secrecy Rate Analysis for a Two-Way Relay Network with Untrusted Relay Node
abstract: A two-way relay scenario is examined in which the relay node itself is treated as a potential passive eavesdropper. Two source nodes exchange information through an amplify-and-forward relay using a physical-layer network coding scheme based on XOR combining. The secrecy of each individual source's message against the relay is analysed using the conditional mutual information framework. Achievable secrecy rate regions are characterised for symmetric and asymmetric channel conditions. When the source-to-relay channels are balanced within 2 dB and the relay operates at 20 dB average received SNR, the per-source secrecy rate is shown to lie within 85% of the theoretical maximum. The analysis is extended to Rician fading with K-factor values of 0, 3, and 7 dB, showing that stronger line-of-sight components reduce secrecy against the untrusted relay by up to 1.2 bits/s/Hz.

title: Lower Bounds on Secrecy Capacity for Multi-Relay Parallel Networks under Individual Power Constraints
abstract: This paper addresses the secrecy capacity of a parallel multi-relay network in which N decode-and-forward relays operate simultaneously and independently over orthogonal sub-channels. A single passive eavesdropper observes all sub-channels. Under individual per-relay power constraints, the problem of maximising a lower bound on the secrecy capacity is formulated as a convex optimisation problem and solved using a projected sub-gradient algorithm. Simulations for N ∈ {2, 4, 8} show that the lower bound grows logarithmically with N when relay channels are i.i.d. Rayleigh, and that the sub-gradient algorithm converges within 40 iterations for N = 8. The gap between the derived lower bound and an upper bound obtained via a cut-set argument is quantified numerically and shown to be at most 0.6 bits/s/Hz for the considered SNR range of 5–25 dB.

title: Impact of Antenna Correlation on Secrecy in MIMO Amplify-and-Forward Relay Networks
abstract: MIMO extensions of the amplify-and-forward relay wiretap channel are studied under spatially correlated Rayleigh fading, using the Kronecker model with exponential correlation matrices at the relay and the eavesdropper. The secrecy capacity lower bound derived via the GSVD precoding strategy is evaluated for relay arrays of 2, 4, and 8 antennas and correlation coefficients ranging from 0 to 0.9. Results indicate that correlation at the eavesdropper antenna array is beneficial for secrecy: at a correlation coefficient of 0.7 and 4-antenna arrays, the lower bound improves by approximately 1.4 bits/s/Hz compared to the uncorrelated case. Conversely, relay-side correlation reduces the bound by up to 0.9 bits/s/Hz under the same conditions. Practical implications for relay antenna spacing in confined deployment environments are discussed using a 2.4 GHz carrier frequency reference scenario.

title: Secrecy Outage of Energy-Harvesting Decode-and-Forward Relay Networks with a Passive Eavesdropper
abstract: The secrecy outage probability is analysed for a decode-and-forward relay network in which the relay node harvests energy from the source signal using a power-splitting protocol before forwarding the message. The eavesdropper intercepts both the source-to-relay and relay-to-destination transmissions, and its combined received signal is processed using maximal-ratio combining. Closed-form expressions for the SOP are derived under Rayleigh fading for power-splitting ratios from 0.1 to 0.9. An optimal power-splitting ratio that minimises SOP is identified for each SNR setting. At a source transmit power of 100 mW and a target secrecy rate of 0.5 bits/s/Hz, the optimal ratio lies between 0.3 and 0.5 across the SNR range tested. The analytical expressions are verified by Monte Carlo simulation with 10^6 trials, yielding agreement to within 1% in all cases.

title: Achievable Secrecy Rates in Full-Duplex Relay Networks with Self-Interference Cancellation Errors
abstract: Full-duplex relaying improves spectral efficiency but introduces residual self-interference that affects achievable secrecy rates. This paper models the residual self-interference as an additive Gaussian term with variance proportional to the relay transmit power, and derives the ergodic secrecy rate for a decode-and-forward full-duplex relay network with one passive eavesdropper. The proportionality constant β, representing cancellation quality, is varied over the range 10^{-5} to 10^{-2} to represent current and near-future hardware. Results show that for β below 3×10^{-4}, full-duplex outperforms half-duplex relay operation in terms of secrecy rate at SNR values above 18 dB. For larger β values, the advantage disappears or reverses. The analysis is carried out under both perfect and statistical eavesdropper CSI assumptions, showing a secrecy rate penalty of up to 0.7 bits/s/Hz when only statistical CSI is available.

title: Secrecy Capacity Bounds for Cooperative Relay Networks with Correlated Eavesdropper Channels: A Copula-Based Approach
abstract: In practical deployments, a multi-antenna eavesdropper's sub-channel gains may be statistically dependent due to proximity or shared scattering environments. This paper applies Gaussian and Clayton copulas to model the dependence structure among K eavesdropper sub-channel gains and derives upper and lower bounds on the secrecy capacity of a decode-and-forward relay network. For K = 3 sub-channels with Kendall's τ correlation of 0.6, the gap between bounds under the Clayton copula is 0.3 bits/s/Hz smaller than under the independence assumption at 20 dB SNR, indicating that ignoring correlation leads to pessimistic secrecy predictions. The framework is validated against empirical channel data collected from a controlled indoor software-defined radio experiment at 900 MHz with two USRP B210 units acting as eavesdropper elements, recording 8,000 channel snapshots. Model fitting is assessed using the Cramér–von Mises criterion.

title: Finite-SNR Diversity-Multiplexing Tradeoff under Secrecy Constraints in Relay-Assisted Fading Networks
abstract: The diversity-multiplexing tradeoff (DMT) is a well-established tool for characterising MIMO system performance, but its extension to the secrecy setting at finite SNR is less studied. This paper derives finite-SNR DMT curves for a decode-and-forward relay network operating under a secrecy constraint, using the outage formulation introduced by Narasimhan for conventional channels. The analysis covers Rayleigh and Nakagami-m fading with m ∈ {1, 2, 4} and relay counts N ∈ {1, 2, 3}. A key finding is that the finite-SNR secrecy DMT curve lies strictly below the non-secrecy DMT and the gap widens with increasing multiplexing gain, converging to the asymptotic secrecy DMT only for SNR above approximately 25 dB in the Rayleigh case. The results offer quantitative guidance on choosing between spatial multiplexing and diversity modes when secrecy is a design criterion in relay deployment.

title: Secrecy in Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Assisted Relay Networks: Capacity Bounds and Phase-Shift Optimisation
abstract: This paper examines whether reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) inserted between a relay and a destination can improve secrecy capacity bounds when a passive eavesdropper is present in the same angular sector as the destination. The RIS is modelled as an N_r-element passive array with independent phase-shift control on each element. The source uses decode-and-forward relaying and the eavesdropper has no knowledge of the RIS configuration. Upper and lower secrecy capacity bounds are derived for N_r ∈ {16, 32, 64} under Rician fading with K = 5 dB. An alternating optimisation algorithm for phase-shift selection is proposed and shown to achieve within 0.5 bits/s/Hz of an exhaustive phase-sweep benchmark at N_r = 32 while reducing computational complexity from O(2^{N_r}) to O(N_r^2). The results suggest that RIS placement within 10 m of the legitimate destination provides the largest secrecy gain relative to relay-only operation.

title: Phase gradient modelling of passive reflective surfaces for indoor link budget calculations
abstract: This work introduces a simplified phase gradient model for flat passive reflective surfaces and assesses its applicability to indoor link budget predictions in the 2.4–5.8 GHz range. The model parameterises each surface tile by a local phase shift applied to an incident plane wave and derives far-field radiation patterns through a discrete aperture summation. Predictions were validated against full-wave FDTD simulations on 16×16 element surfaces and against over 300 measured path-loss points in a corridor environment with a prototype 8×8 element reflective panel. The model agreed with FDTD results within 1.5 dB across steering angles up to ±45°. Computational complexity was reduced by a factor of 90 relative to FDTD. The study identifies the far-field approximation breakdown distance as a function of surface size and carrier frequency, providing a practical design rule for deployment planning.

title: Characterisation of Reference-Spur Mechanisms in an Integer-N Charge-Pump PLL at 868 MHz
abstract: Reference spurs in integer-N charge-pump phase-locked loops arise from multiple concurrent mechanisms, including charge-pump current mismatch, loop-filter leakage, and substrate coupling of the reference clock. This work presents a measurement-based decomposition of spur contributions in a discrete-component 868 MHz integer-N PLL assembled on a four-layer PCB. Each mechanism is isolated by selectively modifying circuit parameters: charge-pump up/down currents are trimmed in 1 µA steps between 50 µA and 200 µA, and loop-filter capacitor leakage is swept by substituting capacitor types. Reference spurs measured with a signal analyser range from −42 dBc under worst-case mismatch to −74 dBc after trimming and layout optimisation. A simplified behavioural model that predicts spur level within 4 dB for charge-pump mismatch currents above 2 µA is derived and validated. The results provide design guidelines for narrow-band ISM-band transmitters where spurious emission limits are set at −36 dBm.

title: Applicability of Earned Value Metrics to Iterative Software Development: A Controlled Experiment
abstract: Earned value management (EVM) was designed for plan-driven projects, yet practitioners increasingly apply it to iterative processes. This paper reports a controlled experiment conducted with 24 student teams at the University of Novi Sad, each executing a four-sprint software project under identical scope constraints. Teams were randomly assigned to EVM-instrumented or traditional progress-tracking conditions. Schedule Performance Index (SPI) and Cost Performance Index (CPI) were computed at each sprint boundary and compared against final delivery accuracy. Results show that SPI computed over story-point estimates correlates with final schedule deviation at r = 0.61 (p < 0.01), while CPI correlates at r = 0.54. Accuracy degrades for sprints shorter than one week. The study identifies three systematic biases introduced when mapping agile artefacts onto EVM structures and proposes a lightweight mapping procedure that reduces the absolute percentage error of final-date forecasts from 18.3% to 11.7% in the experimental sample. Implications for industrial adoption are discussed.

title: Schedule Risk Estimation in Agile Projects Using Monte Carlo Simulation on Sprint Velocity Distributions
abstract: This paper presents a Monte Carlo framework for estimating schedule completion risk in Scrum-based projects. Velocity data from 38 software projects collected from two mid-sized Serbian software companies over a three-year period were used to fit statistical distributions to sprint velocity. Log-normal and gamma distributions were evaluated; the gamma distribution provided the best fit for 27 of the 38 projects (AIC comparison). The framework samples velocity sequences for remaining sprints and derives empirical probability distributions over completion dates. Backtesting on a held-out subset of 10 projects shows that 80% confidence intervals captured the actual completion date in 8 out of 10 cases. Compared to deterministic forecasting using average velocity, the probabilistic model reduces overconfident predictions and flags high-risk projects earlier in the lifecycle, on average 3.2 sprints before the deterministic method. The paper discusses calibration procedures and practical integration with standard project dashboards.

title: Hybrid EVM–Agile Performance Dashboards: Implementation Patterns in Central and Eastern European Software SMEs
abstract: A multi-case study examining how five small and medium-sized software enterprises in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania have integrated earned value metrics into agile toolchains. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 23 project managers and developers, supplemented by anonymised project records covering 112 completed sprints. Three implementation patterns emerged: (1) post-hoc EVM calculation on closed sprints, (2) real-time EVM overlay on backlog management tools, and (3) hybrid milestone-sprint structures with EVM applied only to milestone intervals. Pattern 2 produced the lowest administrative overhead and the highest uptake among development teams. A measurement instrument for assessing EVM integration maturity in agile SMEs is proposed and validated against the case data. The paper concludes with practical guidelines for organisations considering adoption, including estimates of the effort required to instrument an existing Jira-based workflow.

title: Quantifying the Effect of Team Composition Stability on Sprint Velocity Variance: Evidence from 94 Agile Teams
abstract: Frequent changes in team membership are often cited as a source of velocity instability, yet empirical evidence at scale is limited. This study assembles a longitudinal dataset covering 94 Scrum teams across 11 software organisations in Serbia and Slovenia, tracking team membership changes and sprint velocity over periods of 6 to 24 months. Team Composition Stability Index (TCSI) is operationalised as the proportion of team-members unchanged between consecutive sprints. Mixed-effects regression models show that a 10-percentage-point decrease in TCSI is associated with a 6.8% increase in velocity standard deviation (95% CI: 4.1–9.5%) and a statistically significant drop of 4.3 story points in the immediately following sprint. Effects are larger for teams of five or fewer members. The relationship plateaus for teams with TCSI above 85%, suggesting diminishing returns from strict stability policies. Findings are discussed in the context of hiring and staffing decisions in growing software companies.

title: An Earned Schedule Extension for Multi-Team Agile Programmes: Formulation and Simulation Validation
abstract: Earned Schedule (ES) theory extends traditional EVM by computing a time-based performance measure that avoids the anomalous behaviour of SPI(t) near project completion. Existing ES formulations assume a single project plan, but scaled agile programmes coordinate multiple interdependent teams. This paper derives a multi-team ES formulation that accounts for cross-team dependencies encoded in a programme-level dependency graph. The formulation is validated through discrete-event simulation using synthetic programme configurations spanning 3 to 12 teams, with dependency densities ranging from 10% to 40%. Simulated programmes with high dependency density (>30%) show that single-team ES systematically underestimates overall programme schedule delay by 12–21%, whereas the proposed multi-team formulation reduces this bias to below 4%. An illustrative application to a reconstructed programme from an anonymised telecommunications company is included. The paper provides worked calculation examples and pseudocode for implementation.

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Sprint Completion Forecasting: A Comparative Study
abstract: This study compares five machine learning models—gradient boosted trees, random forest, support vector regression, k-nearest neighbours, and a feedforward neural network—against a baseline deterministic velocity forecast for predicting the number of story points completed in the next sprint. The dataset comprises 4,217 individual sprints collected from 143 Scrum teams across seven organisations over five years. Features include rolling velocity statistics, team size, sprint duration, backlog refinement ratio, and number of mid-sprint scope changes. Models were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation with MAE and RMSE as primary metrics. Gradient boosted trees achieved the lowest MAE (3.1 story points) compared to 5.4 for the deterministic baseline. SHAP value analysis identifies rolling median velocity and mid-sprint scope change count as the two most influential features across all tree-based models. The study includes a runtime and interpretability comparison relevant to practitioners deploying predictions in live project dashboards.

title: Integrating Schedule Risk Indices into Agile Retrospectives: A Field Study at Three Software Companies
abstract: Retrospectives are the primary continuous-improvement mechanism in Scrum, yet they typically rely on qualitative team discussions rather than quantitative metrics. This field study embeds probabilistic schedule risk indices—derived from Monte Carlo velocity sampling—into the retrospective process at three Vojvodina-based software companies over nine months. Retrospective sessions were observed and recorded, and project performance data were tracked before and during the intervention. Teams that received risk index summaries before retrospectives identified a higher proportion of schedule-related impediments (mean 41% vs. 22% in control sessions) and implemented a larger share of process changes in the following sprint (58% vs. 37%). Self-reported meeting satisfaction scores did not decrease significantly, addressing a concern that metric-driven retrospectives reduce psychological safety. The paper describes the facilitation protocol, the dashboard tool used to present indices, and practical lessons from the deployment.

title: Calibrating Confidence Intervals for Agile Completion Date Forecasts Under Changing Team Contexts
abstract: Probabilistic completion date forecasts for agile projects are typically calibrated on historical velocity data, but calibration quality degrades when team context—such as size, domain, or tooling—changes significantly between the historical reference period and the active project. This paper proposes a contextual recalibration procedure that weights historical sprints by similarity to current context using a kernel function over a vector of five context features. The method is evaluated on a longitudinal dataset of 211 projects with documented context shifts. Compared to equal-weight historical calibration, contextual recalibration improves the coverage of 80% prediction intervals from 61% to 79% and reduces interval width by 14% on average. The improvement is largest when context shifts involve team size changes of two or more members or a domain switch. An open-source Python implementation is described and made available through the paper's supplementary material.

title: Work-Content Allocation Models for Project-Based Manufacturing: Relating Design Complexity to Labour Hours
abstract: In project-based manufacturing, the allocation of estimated total labour hours across project phases—engineering, procurement, fabrication, and commissioning—is rarely documented systematically. This paper examines historical labour-hour records from 49 completed projects at two ETO manufacturers in Serbia and analyses how the phase distribution varies with product complexity. Complexity was quantified using a scoring method based on number of unique components, number of interfaces, and degree of customer-specified tolerances. Regression analysis showed that engineering-phase share increases significantly with complexity score, while fabrication-phase share decreases. A linear allocation model with four parameters was fitted and validated on a separate dataset of 11 projects. The model enables project managers to generate phase-level labour budgets from a single early-estimate total and a complexity score, without requiring detailed work breakdown. The paper discusses how the scoring method can be operationalised from information typically available in bid documentation.

title: Geostatistical merging of rain-gauge and C-band radar data over the Pannonian Plain: a variogram-based approach
abstract: Accurate precipitation estimates over flat terrain such as the Pannonian Plain are constrained by the low density of surface rain-gauge networks and the range-dependent errors of single-polarisation C-band radars. This study applies ordinary kriging with external drift (KED) to merge hourly rain-gauge observations from 47 stations in Vojvodina with composited reflectivity data from the Serbian RHMSS radar network during the summer convective seasons of 2007–2009. Empirical variograms were fitted using an exponential model after systematic bias correction of the radar field via mean-field adjustment. Cross-validation against withheld gauge stations showed a reduction in root-mean-square error of 31% compared to radar-only estimates and 18% compared to gauge-only kriging. Spatial correlation ranges of 35–60 km were identified for convective events, substantially shorter than for stratiform precipitation. The merged product was tested against an independent flash-flood inventory for the Fruška Gora foothills, showing improved hit rates for events exceeding 20 mm h⁻¹. Results confirm that KED merging is viable operationally even with sparse station networks typical of the western Balkans.

title: Просторна варијабилност интензитета конвективних олуја у Војводини на основу мреже дистрометара
abstract: У раду је анализирана просторна варијабилност интензитета падавина током девет конвективних епизода у Војводини у периоду 2010–2011. на основу мреже од шеснаест оптичких дистрометара типа ОТТ Парсивел размештених на растојању 5–40 км. Измерени параметри расподеле капљица (DSD) коришћени су за проверу Z–R релација добијених за радарске снимке РХМЗС мреже. Утврђено је да стандардна Маршал–Палмерова релација потцењује акумулацију за 15–28% у највећим ћелијама организованих мезоскалних конвективних система. Предложена је регионално калибрисана релација Z = 270R¹·⁵², чијом применом је RMSE смањен на 2,4 mm у поређењу са 4,1 mm код стандардне релације. Резултати указују на значај регионалне калибрације за оперативну хидрологију.

title: Detection of hail-bearing convective cells using dual-polarisation radar signatures and MSG SEVIRI infrared channels
abstract: This study presents a cell-tracking algorithm that fuses dual-polarisation C-band radar parameters with Meteosat Second Generation SEVIRI brightness temperatures to identify hail-bearing convective cells over Serbia and northern Bosnia-Herzegovina. Radar-derived variables — differential reflectivity ZDR, co-polar correlation coefficient ρHV, and specific differential phase KDP — were combined with 10.8 µm and 6.2 µm channel data at 15-minute temporal resolution. A decision-tree classifier trained on 78 hail reports collected during 2011–2014 achieved a probability of detection of 0.81 and a false alarm ratio of 0.23 in leave-one-season-out validation. Detected cells were tracked using a modified TITAN algorithm over a 400 × 400 km domain. The resulting dataset of 312 hail-cell trajectories reveals a pronounced SW–NE advection corridor across the Pannonian sector, consistent with regional synoptic climatology. Cell life spans ranged from 18 to 94 minutes, with median maximum reflectivity of 58 dBZ. The fused approach outperformed single-source detection in both probability of detection and cell continuity.

title: High-resolution precipitation accumulation maps from X-band radar for urban flash-flood assessment in Novi Sad
abstract: A portable X-band polarimetric radar was deployed on the roof of the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad to capture fine-scale precipitation structure over the city's 290 km² urban area during ten events in summer 2015. Scan-to-scan attenuation correction was applied using a ZPHI algorithm, and the resulting specific differential phase KDP fields were converted to rain rate with a power-law estimator calibrated against a co-located Pluvio² weighing gauge. Sub-hourly accumulation grids at 100 m × 100 m resolution were produced and ingested into a 1D urban drainage model of the Kisač storm-sewer network. Comparison with seven observed pipe-overflow locations showed that the X-band-derived inputs correctly flagged six exceedance events, whereas the nearest operational S-band radar at 68 km range missed two due to overshooting of shallow convective cells. The study demonstrates that local X-band deployment significantly improves lead time estimates for urban flash-flood warnings in medium-sized Central European cities.

title: Spatio-temporal recurrence of extreme convective precipitation in the central Balkans derived from a 20-year radar climatology
abstract: A 20-year archive (1998–2017) of composited C-band radar reflectivity from three operational Serbian radars was processed to derive a spatially continuous climatology of convective precipitation extremes. Reflectivity fields were converted to rain rates using a seasonally varying Z–R relationship, bias-corrected against 112 rain gauges, and aggregated to daily extremes. Return periods for 1-hour accumulations exceeding 30, 50, and 80 mm were estimated cell-by-cell using a generalised extreme-value (GEV) distribution fitted with L-moments. Bootstrapped uncertainty bounds at the 90% confidence level were mapped across a 10 × 10 km grid. The analysis identifies a statistically robust hot-spot zone along the southern margins of the Pannonian Plain where 50-year return-period hourly accumulations reach 72 mm, substantially higher than in adjacent mountainous terrain. Orographic lift along the Fruška Gora and Vršački Breg massifs modulates cell initiation but not maximum intensities. The resulting hazard maps are compared with insurance loss data from hail and flood events, showing qualitative agreement in the highest-risk zones.

title: Fusion of multi-frequency passive microwave and infrared satellite retrievals for sub-daily precipitation estimation over the Dinaric–Pannonian transition zone
abstract: Passive microwave (PMW) precipitation retrievals from the GPM constellation provide physically meaningful rain-rate estimates but suffer from low revisit frequency (2–4 h) over mid-latitudes. This paper presents a weighted blending scheme that combines half-hourly IMERG Late Run precipitation fields with SEVIRI infrared-based motion-vector extrapolations to produce 15-minute precipitation estimates over a 600 × 600 km domain spanning the Dinaric–Pannonian transition. Blending weights were determined by a spatially varying skill score derived from three years of gauge verification data. Against an independent 2020 verification dataset, the blended product reduced false alarm rates for events above 10 mm h⁻¹ by 22% relative to IMERG alone, while maintaining the spatial coherence of large-scale precipitation features. Systematic underestimation of deep convective cores, documented in earlier IMERG studies, was partially corrected by incorporating column-maximum reflectivity from operational radars as a secondary predictor. Seasonal analysis shows the largest skill gains in June–August, when fast-evolving supercell storms constitute a majority of extreme events in the study domain.

title: Probabilistic hail hazard maps for agricultural insurance: a radar-based approach for Vojvodina
abstract: Agricultural losses from convective hail in Vojvodina represent a recurrent economic hazard affecting the region's dominant cereal and vegetable production. This study develops probabilistic hail hazard maps at 1 km resolution using a 15-year (2005–2019) archive of dual-polarisation radar data processed with the cell-tracking algorithm described in earlier work. For each identified hail trajectory, kinetic energy proxies were derived from maximum expected size of hail (MESH) estimates. Kernel density estimation was applied to produce continuous hail frequency surfaces. GEV distribution fitting at pixel level yielded 10-, 25-, and 50-year return-period MESH maps. The maps were validated against parcel-level crop loss reports provided by the insurance cooperative Vojvodina Agro-Protect covering 14,000 parcels over 2015–2019. Concordance between high-hazard zones and observed loss frequencies was evaluated with the Spearman rank correlation (ρ = 0.67, p < 0.001). Spatial clustering of high-hazard areas is statistically significant (Moran's I = 0.43), supporting the use of these maps for zone-based premium differentiation rather than uniform province-wide rates.

title: Evaluation of a random forest downscaling model for daily precipitation from ERA5 reanalysis over the Carpathian–Pannonian region
abstract: ERA5 reanalysis provides spatially complete precipitation fields at 31 km resolution, but this coarseness is insufficient for catchment-scale hazard assessment. This paper evaluates a random forest (RF) model that statistically downscales ERA5 daily precipitation to a 5 km grid using terrain elevation, land cover, distance to major water bodies, and upper-air predictors as features. Training used 780 station-days from a dense network in Hungary, Romania, and Serbia (2000–2015), with spatial cross-validation across five geographic blocks. In the validation period (2016–2020) the RF model achieved a continuous rank probability score 18% lower than bilinear interpolation and correctly reproduced 91% of the spatial pattern variance for events exceeding the 95th percentile. However, peak intensities in convective grid cells were systematically underestimated by 12–19%, a limitation attributed to the representativeness mismatch between point gauge observations and ERA5 large-scale fields. The model is made available as a Python package with pre-trained weights for the study domain.

title: Резултати примене производа мреже метеоролошких радара РХМЗС у систему за рано упозорење на поплаве у Сремском округу
abstract: У раду су приказани резултати двогодишњег тестирања система за рано упозорење на изненадне поплаве у Сремском округу заснованог на оперативним производима радарске мреже Републичког хидрометеоролошког завода Србије. Систем комбинује QPE (quantitative precipitation estimation) производе у реалном времену са хидролошким моделом ТОПМОДЕЛ прилагођеним за шест малих сливова брдске Посавине. Прагови упозорења дефинисани су на основу фреквентне анализе падавина из дугогодишњег архивског низа. У периоду тестирања (2021–2022) систем је генерисао 23 упозорења, од чега је 19 коресподирало са забележеним надлевањима водотокова или пријавама штете. Средње предупређујуће време износило је 47 минута. Лажне узбуне везују се претежно за рефлективност из прелетних конвективних ћелија ниске основе облака које нису дале значајне падавине на тлу. Предложено је увођење дополнске верификације путем мреже нисконошћних сензора влажности тла.

title: A benchmark dataset and baseline models for convective storm cell segmentation from composite radar reflectivity in South-East Europe
abstract: Automated segmentation of convective storm cells from composite radar reflectivity is a prerequisite for downstream hazard mapping workflows, yet no publicly available labelled dataset exists for the South-East European radar domain. This paper describes the construction of CONVBALK-2800, a dataset of 2,800 manually annotated composite reflectivity images from three operational C-band radars in Serbia covering 2010–2023, with polygonal labels for 14,620 individual convective cells. Three baseline segmentation approaches — watershed transform, U-Net, and an ensemble of watershed with a gradient-boosting cell-property classifier — are evaluated in five-fold cross-validation. The U-Net achieves the highest intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.74 for cells with equivalent radar reflectivity factor ≥ 45 dBZ but degrades to IoU = 0.51 for weak-cell fringe areas. Processing time per composite frame is 1.2 s on a single GPU, suitable for near-real-time use. The dataset and training scripts are released under an open licence to facilitate reproducible research. Known limitations include temporal clustering of labels and under-representation of nocturnal events.

title: Temporal trends in convective precipitation intensity over the Pannonian Basin inferred from a homogenised multi-radar archive, 1998–2023
abstract: Detection of long-term trends in convective precipitation intensity from radar archives is hampered by hardware upgrades, site relocations, and calibration discontinuities. This study applies a homogenisation procedure to the 25-year (1998–2023) Serbian composite radar archive using parallel rain-gauge records and reanalysis data as reference series. After correction for six identified inhomogeneity breaks, Mann–Kendall trend tests were applied to annual 99th-percentile hourly rain-rate series at each 4 × 4 km grid cell. Statistically significant increasing trends (p < 0.05) in hourly extremes are found over 34% of the Pannonian domain, concentrated in the northern and eastern sectors, with median Sen's slope of +0.18 mm h⁻¹ per decade. No significant trend was detected in event frequency, suggesting intensification rather than increased occurrence. Comparison with ERA5-derived convective available potential energy (CAPE) trends shows spatial correspondence (Pearson r = 0.61), supporting a thermodynamic interpretation. These findings have direct implications for updating the probabilistic hazard maps produced in earlier work.

title: Combining Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope imagery for fine-scale riparian habitat mapping in a braided gravel-bar reach
abstract: Braided river reaches with active gravel bars, pioneer herbaceous vegetation, and narrow willow scrub strips pose particular challenges for satellite-based habitat mapping because the relevant landscape elements are often narrower than 10–20 m. This study tested the feasibility of fusing 3 m PlanetScope SuperDove multispectral imagery with 10 m Sentinel-2 time-series composites to map seven riparian habitat classes in a 40 km reach of the upper Ibar River, which represents an unusual morphologically active corridor in the otherwise lowland-dominated Serbian river network. Fusion was performed through a spatial-temporal adaptive reflectance fusion model (STARFM) adapted for the 8-band PlanetScope configuration. An OBIA workflow using eCognition was applied to the fused product, yielding a map with overall accuracy of 91.3% verified against 320 independent field polygons collected in summer 2021. Pioneer herb communities on gravel bars, which were undetectable in Sentinel-2-only classifications, were correctly identified with a producer's accuracy of 79%. Processing time for the fusion step on the group's workstation cluster was approximately 4 hours per scene pair. The results support the use of commercial 3 m imagery for national-scale habitat monitoring programmes where budget allows targeted acquisitions.

title: L-band vs. C-band InSAR for deformation retrieval on vegetated loess slopes: a case study from the Srem region
abstract: Agricultural and orchard-covered loess slopes in the Srem region decorrelate rapidly at C-band, limiting persistent scatterer density to sparse built structures. This study compared 34 ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 Fine Beam Double acquisitions (L-band, 2015–2021) with 78 Sentinel-1 C-band acquisitions over the same area and period. L-band coherence exceeded 0.35 over 71 % of vegetated pixels compared to only 19 % for C-band in summer months. Distributed scatterer processing with MintPy using SqueeSAR-style covariance estimation yielded 4 800 measurement points ha⁻¹ from L-band against 620 from C-band across orchard parcels. Both datasets agreed within 1.5 mm/yr over bare-soil reference parcels. L-band detected a previously unreported creep zone of −4.3 mm/yr on a north-facing loess scarp, invisible in C-band products. The study quantifies the coherence benefit of L-band for vegetated loess and discusses practical constraints related to ALOS-2 data availability and cost.

title: Transfer of a convolutional feature extractor trained on Tehran informal settlements to European peri-urban contexts
abstract: A compact convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a labelled VHR dataset of informal settlements in Tehran (approximately 18,000 image patches at 0.5 m) was fine-tuned with 1,200 locally labelled patches from Novi Sad and tested on held-out scenes from Sofia and Niš. The pre-trained feature extractor, frozen except for the final two layers, achieved 85.7 % F1-score on the Novi Sad test set after fine-tuning with only 600 local samples, compared with 74.3 % when trained from scratch on the same 600 samples. Applying the fine-tuned model to the Sofia and Niš scenes without any additional local training yielded F1 scores of 81.2 % and 83.6 % respectively, suggesting reasonable cross-city transferability within the post-socialist built environment context. Domain shift was partially attributed to differences in rooftop colour conventions and parcel shape regularity. The paper quantifies the minimum local sample size required to exceed the from-scratch baseline at each target site.

title: Monitoring moisture content during aqueous pan coating of sugar spheres using near-infrared diffuse reflectance spectroscopy
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) diffuse reflectance spectroscopy was evaluated as an in-line tool for monitoring moisture content during aqueous hydroxypropyl methylcellulose coating of 700–850 µm sugar spheres in a 10-litre side-vented pan coater. Calibration models were developed using partial least squares regression on spectra collected at 30-second intervals throughout 12 coating runs at varying spray rates (4–12 g/min) and inlet air temperatures (40–60 °C). The final PLS model achieved a root mean square error of cross-validation of 0.18% w/w moisture, validated against Karl Fischer titration on pulled samples. Score plots from principal component analysis of the spectral data clearly separated runs with suboptimal drying from those operating within target ranges. The approach enabled detection of a moisture accumulation event in three of twelve runs approximately 8 minutes before visible tablet agglomeration occurred, demonstrating the utility of in-line NIR for early fault detection in pan coating.

title: Multivariate statistical process control applied to solid dosage film-coating: a review of methods and industrial case studies
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of multivariate statistical process control (MSPC) to film-coating unit operations in solid dosage manufacturing, covering the period 2000–2015. Methods reviewed include PCA-based monitoring charts, partial least squares discriminant analysis for batch end-point determination, and multi-way PCA for batch trajectory analysis. Industrial case studies drawn from the peer-reviewed literature are categorised by coating type (aqueous, organic solvent, hot-melt), equipment scale (laboratory to production), and the source of process data (online sensors, at-line spectroscopy, or historian process variables). The chapter discusses practical implementation challenges including the choice of reference batch set size, time-alignment of batch trajectories with dynamic time warping, and the interpretability of latent variable models for operators unfamiliar with multivariate methods. Gaps identified include limited published data on scale-up transitions and on coatings applied to non-spherical substrates.

title: Comparison of D-optimal and full factorial designs for characterising the effect of pan coating process variables on tablet weight gain variability
abstract: Weight gain variability across individual tablets is a critical quality attribute in film coating, yet the relative efficiency of different experimental designs for characterising its dependence on process parameters has received limited systematic attention. This study compared a 2⁴ full factorial design (16 runs) with a D-optimal design (12 runs) constructed in the same four-factor space—inlet air temperature (45–65 °C), pan speed (8–16 rpm), spray rate (6–14 g/min), and coating suspension solids content (10–20% w/w)—for aqueous HPMC coating of 300 mg placebo tablets in a 15-litre pan coater. Weight gain relative standard deviation (RSD) across 20 tablets per batch end-point was the response. Prediction variance maps and model coefficient confidence intervals from both designs were compared. The D-optimal design recovered 94% of the prediction accuracy of the full factorial at 75% of the experimental effort. Pan speed and spray rate showed the largest main effects on RSD (p < 0.01), and their interaction term was statistically significant in both designs.

title: Raman spectroscopy for in-line coating thickness estimation on film-coated tablets: calibration strategy and prediction uncertainty
abstract: In-line Raman spectroscopy was investigated as a non-destructive method for estimating mean coating thickness on film-coated 400 mg ibuprofen tablets during aqueous ethylcellulose coating in a side-vented pan coater at the 6-litre scale. Spectra were collected every 60 seconds using a PharmaScan PB-2 immersion probe (invented instrument). A PLS calibration model was trained on 220 spectra from 11 reference batches spanning coating thickness values of 30–180 µm (confirmed by cross-sectional optical microscopy on pulled samples). The RMSECV for coating thickness was 8.3 µm on a leave-one-batch-out cross-validation scheme. Prediction uncertainty was decomposed into contributions from model error, spectral noise, and batch-to-batch variability using a Monte Carlo resampling approach (5000 iterations). Results indicated that batch-to-batch variability in tablet core composition accounted for 38% of total prediction uncertainty, suggesting that incorporating core spectral pre-processing could further improve model robustness across manufacturing campaigns.

title: Batch trajectory analysis with multi-way PCA for monitoring scale-dependent coating dynamics in side-vented pan coaters
abstract: Scale-up of film-coating processes often introduces changes in batch trajectory shape that invalidate monitoring models built at smaller scale. This study applied multi-way principal component analysis (MPCA) to batch process data from aqueous HPMC coating runs conducted at three pan scales: 6-litre (n = 14 batches), 30-litre (n = 11 batches), and 120-litre (n = 9 batches). Time-alignment across batches was performed using indicator variable synchronisation based on cumulative spray volume. Five process variables were monitored per run. Score trajectories on PC1–PC2 showed systematic between-scale shifts attributable primarily to differences in exhaust air humidity dynamics, confirmed by contribution plots. A two-step monitoring strategy was proposed in which a scale-specific MPCA model is used for real-time fault detection and a cross-scale PLS model is used for end-point prediction. Cross-validated root mean square errors for weight gain prediction at the 120-litre scale were 0.43% using the cross-scale model, compared to 1.12% when the 6-litre model was applied directly.
