title: Central composite design study of fluidised-bed coating variables affecting particle size distribution and friability of coated microcrystalline cellulose beads
abstract: A face-centred central composite design was used to investigate the effects of four process variables—inlet air temperature (40–60 °C), fluidisation air volume (30–50 m³/h), spray rate (3–9 g/min), and atomisation air pressure (1.2–2.0 bar)—on particle size distribution (d10, d50, d90, span) and friability of aqueous Eudragit RS 30D-coated microcrystalline cellulose beads at 10% weight gain in a 3-litre Glatt GPCG-1. Twenty-six experimental runs were conducted; responses were measured in triplicate. Quadratic regression models for d50 and span showed R² values of 0.91 and 0.87 respectively. Inlet air temperature and atomisation pressure had the strongest influence on span (p < 0.001), suggesting that droplet evaporation rate relative to deposition rate governs size distribution broadening. Friability was below 0.5% in all runs except two with low inlet temperature and high spray rate, where visible agglomeration increased friability to 1.8–2.3%. Overlay plots identified a feasible operating region satisfying all acceptance criteria simultaneously.

title: Sensitivity of coating end-point detection to reference batch selection in multivariate batch monitoring: a simulation study
abstract: The performance of multivariate batch monitoring models for coating end-point detection depends critically on the quality and representativeness of the reference batch set, yet systematic guidance on reference batch selection is lacking. This simulation study generated synthetic coating batch trajectories by perturbing a mechanistic spray-coating model with realistic noise distributions estimated from 26 historical production batches of aqueous HPMC-coated tablets at the 30-litre scale. MPCA monitoring models were built from reference sets of varying size (n = 5, 10, 15, 20 batches) and composition (random selection versus diversity-maximised selection using maximum dissimilarity). End-point detection sensitivity and false alarm rate were evaluated over 200 simulated test batches per condition. Models built from diversity-maximised sets of 10–15 batches achieved comparable performance to randomly selected sets of 20 batches (sensitivity 91% vs. 89%, false alarm rate 5.1% vs. 5.4% at 95% confidence). Models built from fewer than eight reference batches showed markedly degraded sensitivity (below 75%). Practical recommendations for reference batch selection in routine coating operations are provided.

title: Framing EU Membership in the Belgrade English-Language Press, 2004–2008: A Corpus-Assisted Approach
abstract: This study examines how three Belgrade-based English-language newspapers framed Serbia's prospective EU membership during the 2004–2008 period, drawing on a 480,000-word corpus compiled from the outlets' online archives. Using corpus-assisted discourse analysis with WordSmith Tools, the study identifies dominant lexical clusters and semantic prosodies associated with the terms 'accession', 'integration', and 'conditionality'. Findings indicate that accession was overwhelmingly represented through economic benefit frames, while political conditionality items—particularly cooperation with the International Criminal Tribunal—were systematically distanced through passive constructions and nominalisation. The analysis maps a gradual rhetorical shift between 2006 and 2008 in which conditionality language becomes less foregrounded as energy policy discourse expands. The paper contributes to regional CDA scholarship by demonstrating that English-language journalism in candidate states mediates EU requirements for domestic elite audiences in ways that soften accountability framing.

title: Europeanisation as Metaphor: Conceptual Mapping in Croatian and Serbian English-Language Op-Eds
abstract: The article applies conceptual metaphor theory to a parallel corpus of 620 opinion pieces published in Croatian and Serbian English-language press between 2005 and 2010. Drawing on cognitive linguistic categories following Lakoff and Johnson, the study catalogues metaphorical expressions used to render EU accession processes intelligible to readers. Three dominant metaphor clusters are identified: accession as a journey, EU membership as a contract, and conditionality as medical treatment. Quantitative comparison across the two national corpora reveals that the journey metaphor is proportionally more frequent in Croatian texts (38% of instances) than in Serbian ones (24%), while the medical cluster appears almost exclusively in Serbian material. Close reading of co-text suggests that the medical metaphor positions Serbia as requiring external remedy, a framing absent in Croatian editorial production during the same window. Implications for identity construction and political legitimation are discussed.

title: Reported Speech and Source Attribution in EU Accession Reporting: Evidence from the Novi Sad English-Language Press
abstract: The paper investigates patterns of source attribution and reported speech in EU-related news articles published in two Vojvodina-based English-language outlets between 2010 and 2013. A 210,000-word corpus was annotated for speech reporting verbs, source types, and attribution distance. Analysis reveals that EU officials are cited using neutral verbs ('said', 'stated') in 71% of instances, while Serbian government sources are more frequently attributed assertive or evaluative verbs ('insisted', 'confirmed', 'pledged'). EU sources are also positioned earlier in the syntactic structure of reports, granting them higher epistemic authority. The finding that local non-governmental voices account for fewer than 9% of attributed statements is discussed in terms of access norms in candidate-state journalism and the structural constraints of small English-language outlets dependent on wire service content.

title: 'On the European Path': Diachronic Shifts in Accession Metaphoricity in Serbia's English-Language Government Communication, 2008–2015
abstract: This study traces shifts in the metaphorical representation of EU accession across seven years of Serbian government press releases and official communiqués published in English. The corpus of 1,340 documents was compiled from the Government of Serbia public relations archive and processed in AntConc for keyword and collocation analysis. Qualitative metaphor analysis was subsequently applied to a stratified sample of 180 texts. Results document a marked decline in journey metaphors after 2012 and their partial replacement by procedural and legal metaphors emphasising chapter-by-chapter negotiation. This shift correlates chronologically with the opening of accession chapters in 2014. The paper proposes the concept of 'metaphor pragmatics in institutional transition' to describe how governmental agencies adjust figurative language as candidate status matures into active negotiation, signalling a reorientation from aspirational to managerial communication.

title: Multilingual News Agencies and the Translation of EU Conditionality: A Comparative Study of English and Serbian Wire Copy
abstract: The article compares the English-language source texts of two international wire agencies with their Serbian translations as published in domestic media between 2013 and 2016. A parallel corpus of 340 matched article pairs was constructed and analysed for lexical divergence, modal verb frequency, and evaluative language. Translations show a consistent pattern of modal softening: English constructions with 'must' and 'is required to' are translated with Serbian equivalents of 'should' and 'is expected to' at a rate of approximately 2:1. This softening is more pronounced in economic conditionality items than in rule-of-law items. The paper situates these findings within the sociology of translation and argues that domestication tendencies in political translation have measurable ideological consequences for how EU obligations are perceived in receiving audiences.

title: Visual and Verbal Coherence in EU Accession Feature Photography: A Multimodal Analysis of Serbian Print Media
abstract: This paper extends critical discourse analysis to a multimodal framework by examining the interplay of photographs and captions in EU accession feature stories published in three Serbian print publications between 2014 and 2017. A sample of 148 feature stories was selected, yielding 312 captioned images. Images were coded using Kress and van Leeuwen's grammar of visual design for salience, gaze direction, and social distance, while captions were analysed for evaluative language and transitivity patterns. Findings indicate strong modal alignment between optimistic captions and images depicting institutional handshakes or urban renewal, while stories foregrounding migration or rule-of-law issues show modal dissonance, with cautious verbal registers paired with neutral or ambiguous imagery. The paper contributes a replicable coding protocol for multimodal EU media analysis in candidate-state contexts.

title: Accession Fatigue in Editorial Discourse: A Longitudinal Study of Attitudinal Language in the Belgrade English-Language Press, 2012–2019
abstract: Drawing on appraisal theory, this paper analyses attitudinal language in 890 editorials published by two Belgrade-based English-language outlets across seven years. Texts were manually annotated for Affect, Judgement, and Appreciation systems following Martin and White's appraisal framework, with inter-annotator reliability tested on a 10% subsample (Cohen's κ = 0.78). Results demonstrate a statistically significant decline in positive Appreciation of EU institutions from 2015 onward, coinciding with the period of reduced chapter-opening activity. Negative Judgement directed at domestic political actors increases independently of EU-related events, suggesting that attitudinal decline reflects domestic political frustration rather than purely EU-driven disenchantment. The paper introduces the term 'editorial accession fatigue' to describe the compound attitudinal pattern and relates it to survey data on public EU support from the same period.

title: Gender and Authority in EU Accession Reporting: Source Selection Patterns in the Serbian and Croatian English-Language Press
abstract: The study examines whether and how gender affects source selection in EU accession journalism in Serbia and Croatia. A corpus of 1,640 news articles from four outlets (two per country), published 2015–2020, was coded for source gender, institutional affiliation, and topical domain. Female sources account for 22% of all attributed statements in the sample; this proportion rises to 31% in civil society and NGO domains but falls to 11% in economic and financial coverage. Regression analysis indicates that topic domain is a stronger predictor of source gender than national context, suggesting cross-regional patterns in gendered access norms. The paper also analyses how female sources are linguistically constructed relative to male sources, finding higher rates of credential-withholding in captions and higher use of first-name-only attribution for women in softer news categories.

title: Repetition and Reframing: How Pro-EU Serbian NGOs Adapted Accession Narratives After the 2022 Enlargement Package
abstract: The article examines how Serbian civil society organisations that produce English-language content adapted their communication strategies following the European Commission's October 2022 enlargement package and its mixed assessment of Serbia's progress. A corpus of 96 NGO reports, newsletters, and website statements published between November 2022 and June 2024 was compiled and analysed for lexical repetition, recontextualisation, and argument structure. Results show a two-phase adaptation: an immediate post-package period characterised by defamiliarisation of Commission language through ironic repetition, followed by a consolidation phase in which organisations adopted the Commission's 'cluster' terminology but embedded it within domestic accountability frames absent from the original documents. The paper discusses how civil society actors function as discourse mediators between supranational bureaucratic language and domestic political audiences, reshaping technical EU text into advocacy material.

title: Between Brussels and Belgrade: Intergenre Borrowing in Serbia's EU Progress Reports and Their Domestic English Press Reception
abstract: This preprint investigates the textual relationship between European Commission Progress Reports on Serbia (2018–2024) and their coverage in Serbian English-language outlets. Fourteen Commission documents and 380 derived press articles were analysed for intergenre borrowing using a combination of quotation tracking and collocation comparison in Sketch Engine. Commission text is reproduced almost verbatim in 41% of coverage, with editorial additions concentrated in the opening and closing paragraphs. Borrowing rates are higher for rule-of-law sections than for economic criteria sections, suggesting editorial preference for political accountability material. The preprint also maps which Commission phrases circulate most widely and persists across multiple outlets, effectively becoming 'viral bureaucratic language'. These findings have implications for understanding how EU bureaucratic English shapes the vocabulary of political debate in candidate countries.

title: Budgetary Accounting Practices in Serbian Local Governments: An Empirical Overview
abstract: This paper examines cash-basis budgetary accounting practices across 145 Serbian municipalities and cities for the fiscal year 2009. Using data extracted from annual financial statements submitted to the Treasury Administration of the Republic of Serbia, the study evaluates compliance with domestic public accounting regulations and identifies systematic discrepancies in revenue recognition and expenditure classification. Descriptive statistics and cluster analysis reveal that municipalities with fewer than 20,000 inhabitants exhibit significantly higher rates of misclassification of capital transfers compared to larger urban centres. The paper also documents inconsistent treatment of receivables from indirect budget beneficiaries. Findings suggest that the existing cash-based framework, while administratively simpler, obscures the true fiscal position of smaller municipalities and creates consolidation difficulties when aggregating data at the district level. The paper concludes with a discussion of the preconditions necessary for gradual migration toward accrual-based reporting in line with European standards.

title: IPSAS Adoption Readiness in Western Balkan Countries: A Comparative Regulatory Assessment
abstract: This study assesses the legislative and institutional readiness for IPSAS adoption in five Western Balkan jurisdictions — Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, and Albania — drawing on a combination of regulatory document analysis and structured interviews with 34 public finance officials conducted between 2011 and 2012. A readiness index is constructed along four dimensions: legal framework compatibility, chart-of-accounts alignment, IT infrastructure capacity, and staff training provision. Results indicate that Montenegro scores highest on legal compatibility owing to its early adoption of a treasury single account system, while Bosnia and Herzegovina presents the greatest fragmentation across entity-level accounting frameworks. Serbia occupies an intermediate position, with advanced treasury infrastructure but significant gaps in accrual recognition rules. The paper maps specific IPSAS standards — particularly IPSAS 1, 6, and 17 — against existing national standards and identifies the fifteen most critical divergences requiring legislative intervention prior to full adoption.

title: Consolidated Financial Reporting in the Serbian Public Sector: Legal Basis and Practical Obstacles
abstract: Public sector consolidation — aggregating financial data from a defined group of government-controlled entities into a single set of financial statements — remains largely aspirational in Serbia. This book chapter reviews the legal framework governing consolidation obligations under the Serbian Budget System Law as amended through 2013, compares it with the requirements of IPSAS 6 (Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements), and documents five categories of practical obstacle encountered by the Ministry of Finance's Public Funds Directorate. Primary data were collected through semi-structured interviews with twelve ministry officials and four external auditors during 2013 and 2014. The chapter argues that the absence of a standardised entity boundary definition — determining which public entities fall within the consolidation perimeter — is the single largest procedural barrier. It also highlights the lack of interoperability between the treasury information system and the accounting systems of public enterprises, which forces manual data reconciliation and introduces material consolidation errors. Recommendations are offered for a phased consolidation roadmap aligned with the Serbian EU accession timeline.

title: The Role of Supreme Audit Institutions in Promoting IPSAS-Aligned Reporting: Evidence from Croatia and Serbia
abstract: Supreme audit institutions (SAIs) can accelerate or retard government accounting reform through the standards they apply in compliance audits and the recommendations they issue. This paper compares the audit methodologies and annual reports of the State Audit Office of Croatia and the State Audit Institution of Serbia for the period 2010–2016, with specific attention to how each SAI addresses deviations from accrual recognition principles. Using content analysis of 56 published audit reports and 12 performance audit reports, the study develops a coding framework covering seven dimensions of IPSAS alignment commentary. Results show that the Croatian SAI more frequently issues findings related to improper asset capitalisation and revenue matching, whereas the Serbian SAI concentrates its findings on budgetary compliance, with limited reference to underlying accounting quality. Regression analysis suggests that entities audited by the Croatian SAI exhibit measurably lower rates of restated prior-year figures, implying that the audit commentary has a corrective effect on reporting quality over time. Recommendations are directed at both SAIs regarding the integration of IPSAS-referenced criteria into their standard audit programmes.

title: Pension Liability Disclosure in Serbian Public Sector Financial Reports: A Gap Analysis against IPSAS 25
abstract: IPSAS 25 (Employee Benefits) requires governments to recognise and disclose the present value of defined benefit obligations, including pension liabilities arising from employment in the public sector. Serbian budget users are not currently required to perform actuarial valuations of pension obligations, and no such disclosures appear in the consolidated financial statements of the Republic of Serbia. This paper quantifies the size of the reporting gap by obtaining anonymised payroll data for 38 budget-funded institutions from the Central Register of Compulsory Social Insurance and applying a projected unit credit method using discount rates derived from Serbian government bond yields for 2018–2022. The estimated present value of unfunded defined benefit obligations in the surveyed institutions ranges from RSD 210 billion to RSD 290 billion depending on discount rate assumptions, representing between 4.1% and 5.7% of 2022 GDP. The paper discusses the political economy obstacles to recognising these liabilities and compares Serbia's position to that of four EU member states that completed analogous disclosures within five years of IPSAS adoption.

title: Whole-of-Government Accounts in Transition: Conceptual Framework Conflicts and Consolidation Perimeter Decisions in Serbia 2018–2024
abstract: Producing a whole-of-government account (WGA) that consolidates the general government sector requires consistent decisions about which entities to include, how to eliminate intra-group balances, and which measurement bases to apply to heterogeneous reporting units. This paper traces the evolution of Serbia's consolidation methodology between 2018 and 2024 through analysis of Ministry of Finance instructions, Treasury Administration circulars, and the annual consolidated financial statements of the Republic of Serbia for each year in the period. It identifies four distinct phases of methodological change — two driven by legislative amendments and two by administrative guidance — and documents their effects on reported total assets and net financial worth. The analysis finds that changes in the consolidation perimeter account for approximately 38% of year-on-year variation in reported general government net worth across the period, complicating longitudinal fiscal analysis. The paper proposes a stability criterion for perimeter decisions and discusses its alignment with the GFS 2014 statistical framework used by the IMF.

title: State-of-health estimation of second-life EV batteries from partial charging curves
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for estimating the state of health (SoH) of second-life electric vehicle batteries using partial charging curves, avoiding the need for full charge–discharge cycles that are impractical in field deployments. The proposed approach extracts incremental capacity and differential voltage features from short charging segments and feeds them into an extended Kalman filter framework to produce real-time SoH estimates. A dataset of aged lithium-ion cells with varying chemistries and cycle histories was assembled from retired EV packs to validate the method. Experimental results demonstrate that accurate SoH estimation—within ±2.5% root mean square error—can be achieved using as little as 20% of the full charging window. The technique was further validated under realistic temperature variations and partial state-of-charge operating windows representative of second-life stationary storage scenarios. The findings suggest that the proposed algorithm is well-suited for integration into low-cost battery management systems where measurement resources are constrained, offering a practical path toward reliable condition monitoring of repurposed battery assets.

title: Cell balancing for repurposed battery packs
abstract: Repurposed battery packs assembled from retired electric-vehicle cells exhibit significant cell-to-cell capacity and internal resistance imbalances, making effective cell balancing a critical challenge. This paper investigates passive and active balancing topologies tailored specifically for heterogeneous second-life packs, comparing their performance in terms of balancing speed, energy efficiency, and implementation complexity. A model-based balancing controller using a dual extended Kalman filter estimates individual cell state-of-charge in real time, enabling targeted energy redistribution that accounts for capacity fade disparities. Experimental prototypes were built using harvested 18650-format cells with measured capacity spread of up to 18%. Results show that the proposed active balancing scheme reduces pack imbalance by 76% within a standard discharge cycle compared to conventional passive approaches, while incurring a modest increase in circuit complexity. The work provides practical design guidelines for battery management systems targeting second-life stationary applications and contributes to reducing the levelized cost of repurposed storage systems.

title: Dual extended Kalman filter for simultaneous state-of-charge and state-of-health estimation in lithium-ion cells
abstract: Accurate and simultaneous estimation of state-of-charge (SoC) and state-of-health (SoH) is essential for reliable battery management in both automotive and stationary storage applications. This paper proposes a dual extended Kalman filter (DEKF) architecture that jointly estimates SoC and the capacity fade parameter representing SoH, using a second-order equivalent circuit model. The filter architecture decouples the fast SoC dynamics from the slow SoH evolution, running two interdependent Kalman loops at different update rates to manage computational load. The model parameters are identified offline using a recursive least-squares procedure applied to pulse characterization data at multiple temperatures. Validation was performed on lithium iron phosphate and NMC cells cycled to various aging stages under dynamic current profiles derived from a residential energy storage use case. The DEKF achieved SoC errors below 1.8% and SoH errors below 2.1% across all tested conditions. Computational profiling confirmed suitability for deployment on a low-cost ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller, making the approach directly applicable to cost-sensitive battery management system hardware.

title: Impedance spectroscopy-based capacity fade tracking for stationary lithium-ion storage systems
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) offers rich information about the internal degradation processes of lithium-ion cells without requiring controlled charge–discharge cycles. This work investigates the correlation between EIS features—specifically the mid-frequency semicircle diameter and the Warburg diffusion coefficient—and measured capacity fade across a population of prismatic NMC cells aged under calendar and cyclic conditions. A feature extraction pipeline processes impedance spectra measured at a single state-of-charge setpoint and feeds selected features into a Gaussian process regression model to predict remaining capacity. The approach is validated on a 48 V modular storage system prototype representative of grid-edge stationary applications. Results indicate that the model tracks capacity fade with a mean absolute error of 1.6% over a lifespan spanning 0 to 30% capacity loss. The paper also discusses a practical implementation strategy using a low-cost impedance measurement front-end integrated into a standard battery management system architecture, lowering the barrier to field deployment of EIS-based diagnostics.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of second-life battery packs using particle filter and degradation modeling
abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of second-life lithium-ion battery packs is complicated by the heterogeneous aging histories of constituent cells and the highly nonlinear nature of capacity degradation. This paper proposes a particle filter–based RUL prediction framework that incorporates a physics-informed degradation model accounting for both calendar and cyclic aging mechanisms. The model is initialized using SoH estimates derived from partial charging curves, providing a realistic starting distribution for the particle filter. A resampling strategy adapted to the slow drift characteristic of battery aging is introduced to prevent particle degeneracy over long prediction horizons. The method is tested on a dataset of 24 retired EV battery modules reassembled into second-life packs and cycled under variable-load stationary profiles. The particle filter predicts RUL within ±8% at a 90% confidence interval for prediction horizons up to 200 equivalent full cycles. The framework is discussed in the context of residual value assessment and warranty management for second-life storage assets.

title: Bidirectional DC-DC converter topology for modular second-life battery energy storage integration
abstract: Integrating heterogeneous second-life battery modules into grid-connected storage systems requires power electronics interfaces capable of handling cell-to-cell variations in voltage and internal resistance. This paper presents a modular bidirectional DC-DC converter topology based on an interleaved half-bridge architecture that independently controls power flow to each battery module within a cascaded string. The converter operates in both buck and boost modes, enabling dynamic power sharing that compensates for module-level capacity imbalances. A model predictive controller is implemented on an FPGA platform to manage switching decisions at a 20 kHz update rate while maintaining low total harmonic distortion. Hardware-in-the-loop testing using a real-time simulator validated the converter's response under step-load transients and grid frequency deviation events. The system achieves an overall conversion efficiency of 96.2% at rated power and demonstrates that module-level controllability can extend the useful service life of heterogeneous second-life packs by reducing stress concentration on weaker modules.

title: Temperature-aware state-of-charge estimation for lithium-ion batteries using an unscented Kalman filter
abstract: Temperature exerts a profound influence on the electrochemical kinetics and open-circuit voltage characteristics of lithium-ion batteries, yet many deployed battery management systems rely on estimation algorithms calibrated at a single reference temperature. This paper develops a temperature-aware state-of-charge estimator based on the unscented Kalman filter (UKF), incorporating a temperature-dependent equivalent circuit model whose parameters vary continuously with measured cell surface temperature. Parameter lookup tables are built from a comprehensive characterization campaign spanning −10 °C to 45 °C across three aging levels for NMC-graphite cells. The UKF's sigma-point propagation handles the nonlinear parameter dependence without linearization error, improving estimation accuracy compared to the extended Kalman filter under rapid temperature transients. Field-representative current profiles combining regenerative braking pulses with sustained discharge were used for validation. Across all temperature and aging combinations, the UKF achieved a mean absolute SoC error of 1.2%, a marked improvement over a temperature-unaware baseline that reached 4.7% error at low temperatures. The results underscore the importance of temperature compensation in battery management systems for both automotive and stationary deployments.

title: Assessment of second-life viability for retired electric bus battery packs: a capacity mapping approach
abstract: Determining which retired electric-vehicle battery packs are suitable for second-life stationary applications requires rapid and reliable capacity characterization at the module and cell level. This paper describes a capacity mapping methodology applied to a batch of 36 battery packs removed from a fleet of decommissioned electric city buses after five years of service. Partial charging curves at a standardized C/5 rate are used to estimate individual module capacities through an incremental capacity analysis algorithm, reducing characterization time by 60% compared to full cycle testing. The resulting capacity maps reveal distinct degradation clusters that correspond to bus route profiles and thermal management quality. A decision framework is proposed that classifies modules into three tiers: direct second-life reuse, reconfigured reuse with balancing, and recycling. Economic analysis shows that the tiered approach increases the fraction of recoverable value from retired packs by 34% compared to a binary pass/fail criterion. The methodology provides a practical and scalable workflow for battery repurposers and circular economy stakeholders.

title: Battery management system architectures for second-life stationary storage: a review and classification
abstract: The repurposing of retired electric-vehicle lithium-ion batteries into stationary energy storage systems introduces unique challenges for battery management system design that are not fully addressed by architectures developed for the automotive domain. This book chapter reviews and classifies BMS architectures according to their suitability for second-life contexts, examining topology, measurement strategy, estimation algorithm complexity, and communication protocol requirements. Special attention is paid to the handling of cell heterogeneity resulting from divergent aging histories, the integration of SoH estimation alongside conventional SoC tracking, and the interplay between balancing hardware and estimation software. The chapter surveys state-of-the-art Kalman filter variants, observer-based approaches, and data-driven methods, evaluating their computational demands against typical embedded hardware constraints found in cost-sensitive second-life deployments. Case studies from residential, commercial, and grid-support stationary installations are used to illustrate design trade-offs. The chapter concludes with a roadmap of open research challenges, including standardized testing protocols for second-life BMS validation and cybersecurity considerations for grid-connected storage assets.

title: Lateral drift of disc spreader granules under controlled crosswind: measurement methodology and data from twelve spreader models
abstract: Centrifugal disc spreaders exhibit significant lateral pattern shift under crosswind exposure, but standardised measurement protocols remain absent. We developed an indoor test method using a low-speed wind tunnel (0–6 m/s) and image-based granule trajectory capture to quantify drift for twelve commercial spreader models across nominal working widths of 18–36 m. Granule size distributions and density were measured using sieve analysis and helium pycnometry. At 3 m/s crosswind perpendicular to travel direction, lateral shift of the 50th percentile ranged from 1.2 to 4.8 m at 24 m working width. Larger granules (>2 mm) showed 30% less drift than fine fractions (<1 mm). Pattern asymmetry was quantified using normalised standard deviation, increasing from 0.12 (no wind) to 0.38 (6 m/s wind). Results were validated against field trials on three sites in Vojvodina during spring application seasons (2015–2016). Findings support equipment-specific correction tables for variable-rate systems operating in moderate wind.

title: Granule size classification and its influence on spread uniformity in variable-rate systems: analysis of commercial fertiliser batches
abstract: Granule size distribution (GSD) within commercial fertiliser batches strongly influences spreader performance, yet product specifications often list only sieve fractions without considering how variation affects field uniformity. We analysed twenty-two fertiliser products (NPK and urea) sourced from five Pannonian manufacturers over two years. Digital image analysis and laser diffraction measured GSD for each batch. Spreader trials were conducted using a reference disc spreader (Kuhn Axis 30.1) fitted with controller access to measure rate distribution across 36 m widths. Batches with coefficient of uniformity (CU = D60/D10) > 1.8 produced field uniformity (standard deviation of application rate) 18–25% worse than narrow GSD (CU < 1.3). We quantified size-segregation during handling (auger, metering disc) and found losses of fines during storage. A predictive model linking GSD statistics to expected field CV was developed and validated on seventeen field plots. Recommendation: manufacturers should specify target GSD range; distributors should monitor batch quality to prevent premature segregation.

title: Real-time wind speed estimation from spreader pattern distortion using machine learning: toward adaptive variable-rate systems
abstract: VR spreaders currently operate without feedback on environmental conditions. We investigated whether crosswind-induced pattern asymmetry could be detected and quantified in real time, enabling dynamic rate correction. A disc spreader equipped with dual laser height sensors (forward and rear placement) was mounted on a test frame. We conducted ninety-six trials at wind speeds 0–8 m/s (three replicate runs at each speed) with three granule types. Spreader outlet pattern was captured using high-speed video and image processing. Lateral shift and skewness were extracted and fed into random forest and gradient boosting classifiers trained to predict wind speed class (0–2, 2–4, 4–6, 6–8 m/s). Models achieved 84–91% classification accuracy. A second-stage regression model predicted actual wind speed with MAE = 0.6 m/s. Laboratory results were tested on field equipment during spring 2022–2023 campaigns using a six-degree-of-freedom motion capture system to track granule trajectories. Algorithm integration into a commercial VR controller was performed but not yet field-deployed at production scale. Results suggest feasibility of wind-adaptive control to maintain ±8% uniformity despite environmental variation.

title: Field spread pattern uniformity under variable weather: three-year comparison of pneumatic and centrifugal spreaders in continental climate
abstract: Pneumatic and centrifugal spreaders employ fundamentally different mechanisms for particle acceleration, potentially offering different robustness to environmental variation. We compared two pneumatic (air-stream based) and three centrifugal (disc-based) spreaders across eighteen field plots in Vojvodina (2018–2020) using randomised block design. All equipment was set to nominal 180 kg/ha urea on winter wheat. Spread patterns were mapped using collection trays (2 m × 2 m, 0.5 m spacing) at eight locations per plot per replicate. Uniformity was assessed via coefficient of variation (CV) of application rate. Pneumatic spreaders showed mean CV of 0.14 (range 0.09–0.21) across all conditions; centrifugal spreaders, mean CV of 0.17 (range 0.11–0.26). During high wind events (>4 m/s), pneumatic CV increased by 30%; centrifugal, by 62%. Temperature extremes (>25 °C or <5 °C) affected granule moisture and metering; pneumatic systems were 15% less sensitive. Over the three years, seasonal variation (spring vs. autumn) was significant (p < 0.01). We conclude: pneumatic spreaders offer more consistent patterns under difficult conditions, but at 40% higher fuel/maintenance cost. Choice depends on field size, wind exposure, and budget.

title: Particle trajectory simulation in crosswind: computational and experimental validation for disc spreader design optimisation
abstract: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with discrete element method (DEM) can predict spreader outlet patterns before physical prototyping, but validation under realistic wind conditions remains limited. We developed a CFD-DEM model for a reference disc spreader (disc diameter 600 mm, speed 540 rpm) using ANSYS Fluent and EDEM. Granules (urea, 2–4 mm diameter, density 1310 kg/m³) were released from the spreader outlet at nominal 15 kg/min. Wind field was simulated as steady-state crosswind (0–6 m/s) perpendicular to travel direction. Model outputs (lateral spread, vertical distribution) were compared against wind-tunnel experiments (n = 12 runs) and field validation (n = 8 field plots, spring 2022). Laboratory correlation: R² = 0.87 for lateral shift prediction. Field validation showed mean absolute error of 1.1 m in 50th-percentile spread position at 24 m nominal width. Model was sensitive to granule drag coefficient; calibration against high-speed video tracking improved prediction by 12%. Simulation demonstrated that disc angle adjustment from 12° to 18° reduced crosswind drift by 22% while maintaining radial pattern symmetry. Results support CFD-DEM as a design tool for spreader optimisation.

title: Fertiliser product characteristics and their role in variable-rate applicator performance: inter-batch variability in commercial urea
abstract: Commercial fertiliser batches exhibit uncontrolled variation in physical properties (granule size, density, surface texture, moisture content) that affects spreader calibration stability. We characterised thirty urea batches from six suppliers across four calendar years (2016–2019). Granule size was measured by sieve analysis (ISO 3310-1); density by helium pycnometry; moisture content by Karl Fischer titration; and surface texture by laser profilometry. Each batch was tested in a laboratory spreader rig (disc diameter 500 mm, nominal width 18 m) under controlled conditions (no wind, 20 °C, 50% RH). Spread uniformity was quantified as CV of rate distribution across width. Mean CV across all batches: 0.16 (range 0.11–0.24). Batch-to-batch variation was significant: same supplier's products differed by up to 35% in uniformity. Multivariate analysis revealed that granule size distribution (D90/D10 ratio) and moisture content together explained 71% of CV variance (R² = 0.71). Seasonal differences were observed: winter batches (colder storage) showed 12% higher uniformity than summer batches. We recommend that suppliers document and manufacturers account for such variation in controller calibration strategies.

title: Intercomparison of spread pattern measurement methods: collection trays, image-based reconstruction, and spray-detection sensors
abstract: Quantifying spreader outlet pattern uniformity is fundamental to equipment testing and field validation, but standardised measurement protocols remain fragmented. We compared three methods (ISO/CEN standard collection trays, orthogonal digital imaging with marker granules, and impact-sensor array) on six commercial spreaders under identical laboratory conditions (no wind, constant feed rate). Collection trays (2 m × 2 m grids, n = 900 positions per replicate) measured actual mass deposition; digital imaging tracked trajectory of dyed granules via camera array (8 synchronized GoPro units, 1080p, 60 fps) for pattern reconstruction; sensor array (96 piezoelectric elements, 0.5 m × 24 m active area) provided continuous spatial signal. Each method was repeated five times. Results were compared via coefficient of variation and uniformity indices. Collection trays and digital imaging showed excellent agreement (R² = 0.92 for uniformity metrics); sensor array showed qualitative agreement but systematic offset (±15% bias) requiring calibration. Measurement time: collection trays ~30 min setup and analysis; imaging ~20 min acquisition + 4 h processing; sensors ~5 min. Cost per measurement: trays €800, imaging €2000 (equipment amortised), sensors €500 (consumables). We recommend collection trays for research and standard testing (accuracy, ISO traceability); sensors for rapid field deployment (speed, portability).

title: Proceedings: Crosswind performance of variable-rate spreaders – field measurement standards and data harmonisation (invited keynote)
abstract: Crosswind drift of granular spreaders is widely recognised but measurement and reporting lack standardisation, hampering equipment comparison and model validation. This keynote synthesises twenty years of spreader research in the Pannonian region, highlighting variability in test protocols, environmental conditions, and data interpretation. Key challenge: field conditions (uncontrolled wind, varied soil, equipment interaction) fundamentally differ from laboratory tests (steady wind, controlled surface), yet both are necessary. Current European standards (ISO 5690, DIN 66157) address single-pass uniformity but not wind sensitivity or multi-season dynamics. Recommendations: (1) adopt harmonised field test protocol specifying wind classification (speed bins, steadiness), surface preparation, measurement height, and replication; (2) develop regional correction databases for spreader-environment combinations; (3) integrate real-time environmental monitoring into VR controller decision logic; (4) establish data-sharing repository (open-science model) for manufacturers and researchers. Examples from Hungary, Serbia, Romania, and Germany illustrate regional wind regimes and spreader performance variability. Conclusions: standardisation is feasible and will accelerate adoption of wind-adaptive VR systems across diverse European agro-climatic contexts.

title: Towards digital control of granular spreader outlet patterns: integration of real-time wind sensing and adaptive metering
abstract: Traditional granular spreaders operate open-loop: operator sets rate, spreader delivers at fixed pattern regardless of conditions. We prototyped a closed-loop control system integrating wind measurement (ultrasonic anemometer at spreader outlet) and adaptive outlet metering (variable orifice size via stepper motor) to maintain constant spread uniformity. Prototype used a pneumatic spreader (Amazone ZA-V Hydro) retrofitted with sensing and actuation. Wind speed was sampled every 0.5 seconds; control algorithm (proportional-integral-derivative) adjusted metering orifice size to compensate for predicted drift using a calibrated response model. Field trials (eighteen 4-hectare plots, 2022–2023) tested prototypes against standard equipment (uncontrolled baseline). Spread patterns were measured using sensor arrays and collection trays. Standard spreader achieved CV = 0.19 ± 0.06 under variable field conditions. Controlled system achieved CV = 0.14 ± 0.04, a 26% improvement. Controller responsiveness was sufficient (lag < 1.5 seconds). System stability was adequate (no oscillation observed). Cost: approximately €12,000 retrofit per spreader (not including development costs). Field operator acceptance was positive but reliability concerns remain (sensor fouling, outdoor electronics exposure). Further development required before commercial viability.

title: Granule trajectory in variable density media: simulation and experimental study for enclosed spreading systems
abstract: Air-assisted spreaders discharge granules into a moving air stream (fan-driven), but modelling particle dynamics in variable-density media remains challenging. We developed a Lagrangian particle-tracking model coupling momentum equations with local air velocity and density fields from CFD. Experimental validation used a laboratory wind tunnel fitted with a spreader outlet and high-speed camera (1000 fps) capturing granule trajectories under controlled air speeds (5–25 m/s) and densities (simulated using pressure-altitude chamber). Granule drag coefficient (Cd) was determined empirically from individual sphere trajectories; mean Cd = 0.52 for 3 mm urea granules (Reynolds number range 1000–5000). Model prediction error for granule landing position was ±0.15 m at 18 m nominal spread width (±0.8%). Sensitivity analysis showed that air speed variation (±1 m/s) induced ±2.2 m lateral shift, while granule size variation (±0.5 mm diameter) induced ±0.8 m shift. Practical implication: enclosed spreaders offer tighter control than open-disc systems under crosswind, but air flow uniformity is critical. Model was incorporated into spreader simulation software used by manufacturer (Lemken) for design optimisation of next-generation enclosed spreader.

title: Ambient vibration testing of a post-tensioned concrete highway bridge: sensor placement and modal extraction
abstract: This study reports ambient vibration measurements collected on a 120-metre post-tensioned concrete box-girder bridge on a regional highway corridor near Novi Sad. Twelve uniaxial accelerometers were placed at 30 cross-sections over two separate measurement setups, yielding a combined data set of approximately 18 hours of continuous recording at 200 Hz. The Stochastic Subspace Identification–Covariance method was applied to extract the first six bending and torsional modes. Identified natural frequencies ranged from 1.84 Hz for the fundamental bending mode to 9.63 Hz for the fifth mode. Mode shapes were compared with a calibrated finite-element model constructed in a general-purpose structural analysis package. Differences between measured and modelled frequencies were below 4 % for the first four modes. The paper discusses practical aspects of sensor placement optimisation using an effective independence criterion and the sensitivity of identified damping ratios to record length. Results confirm that ambient traffic and wind excitation provide sufficient broadband energy for reliable modal extraction on this bridge class.

title: Effect of seasonal temperature variation on identified natural frequencies of a reinforced concrete slab bridge
abstract: Continuous monitoring data from a two-span reinforced concrete slab bridge over a canal in Vojvodina were analysed to quantify the influence of ambient temperature on modal parameters. A network of eight triaxial MEMS accelerometers and four surface-mounted thermocouples logged data continuously for fourteen months from January 2014 to February 2015. Automated operational modal analysis using a stabilisation-diagram algorithm was run on 30-minute data windows, producing a time series of natural frequencies and damping ratios. The fundamental frequency varied between 3.71 Hz in mid-summer and 4.28 Hz in mid-winter, a relative range of approximately 15 %. A linear regression model with air temperature as the sole covariate explained 81 % of the observed frequency variance. Residuals from this model were used as a temperature-compensated damage index. No structural events were detected during the monitoring period, establishing a baseline for future comparison. The study also documents sensor drift correction procedures applied to the low-cost MEMS units.

title: Mode shape curvature as a damage indicator for reinforced concrete beam specimens: laboratory validation
abstract: A controlled laboratory campaign was conducted on four simply supported reinforced concrete beams of 4.8-metre span to assess the reliability of mode shape curvature as a damage-sensitive feature. Each beam was subjected to progressively increasing four-point static loads at 10 % intervals of the predicted ultimate load, with loading halted at seven damage states per specimen. After each loading step, ambient-like excitation was applied using a small electrodynamic shaker driven by band-limited white noise (5–200 Hz). Twelve accelerometers were glued to the soffit at equal spacings. Mode shapes were extracted by the Frequency Domain Decomposition method and curvatures were computed by a central-difference scheme. Damage was confirmed by crack mapping and digital image correlation. Results showed that curvature differences between baseline and damaged states correctly identified damage locations in 19 out of 24 test cases; the four failures occurred at damage states below 20 % load ratio where crack opening was less than 0.1 mm. Curvature magnitude correlated monotonically with crack density for load ratios above 30 %.

title: Wireless low-cost accelerometer network for bridge monitoring: hardware design, synchronisation, and field performance
abstract: This paper presents the design and field evaluation of a wireless sensor node built around a commercial 16-bit MEMS accelerometer, a low-power microcontroller, and a 2.4 GHz radio module. Node cost per unit was kept below 85 EUR in small-batch production. Time synchronisation across a network of up to 16 nodes was achieved using a beacon-based scheme that demonstrated synchronisation errors below 0.5 ms over a 100-metre radio range. Power consumption in continuous acquisition mode at 500 Hz was measured at 38 mW per node, giving an operational battery life of approximately 11 days on two AA cells. Field deployment on a steel-reinforced concrete frame bridge confirmed that coherence between node channels exceeded 0.92 across the frequency range 1–50 Hz under ambient traffic loading. Identified natural frequencies from the wireless network agreed with those from a reference wired system to within 0.6 %. The paper discusses firmware architecture, data loss statistics (mean packet loss rate 1.3 %), and strategies for gap-filling before modal analysis.

title: Principal component analysis for separating environmental and structural contributions to frequency variability in a monitored concrete bridge
abstract: Eleven months of continuous modal tracking data from a three-span reinforced concrete T-girder bridge were analysed using principal component analysis to separate temperature-induced frequency variability from potential structural changes. The monitoring system comprised ten triaxial MEMS nodes and meteorological sensors recording air temperature, relative humidity, and solar radiation at one-minute intervals. Automated SSI-COV processing on 20-minute windows produced 7 920 frequency estimates for the first three bending modes. A PCA model was trained on the first eight months and validated on the remaining three. The first principal component captured 74 % of total variance and correlated strongly with air temperature (Pearson r = −0.87). Residuals from the PCA model were approximately Gaussian with standard deviations of 0.031, 0.048, and 0.061 Hz for the three modes. Control charts based on three-sigma limits were established as monitoring thresholds. No anomalous events were detected, confirming structural stability over the observation period.

title: Deployment challenges and lessons learned from long-term SHM on five Vojvodina road bridges
abstract: This chapter summarises field experience accumulated over six years of monitoring five reinforced concrete road bridges in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina, ranging in age from 22 to 61 years at the time of initial instrumentation. Bridge spans varied from 18 to 67 metres and structural types included solid slabs, T-girders, and voided decks. For each structure, the chapter describes the sensor layout rationale, installation procedure, observed hardware failures and their remediation, and the quality of modal data recovered. Across all five sites, cumulative monitoring exceeded 14 000 node-days. Hardware failure modes included antenna corrosion (three incidents), battery depletion faster than predicted due to low winter temperatures (seven incidents), and firmware crashes attributed to memory overflow under high-traffic vibration amplitudes (two incidents). Modal tracking continuity, defined as the fraction of 20-minute windows yielding at least three identifiable modes, averaged 83 % over all sites and seasons. Practical recommendations are given for enclosure design, battery sizing, and firmware robustness in continental-climate deployments.

title: Autoregressive models for anomaly detection in continuously tracked natural frequencies of a concrete bridge
abstract: An autoregressive model of order 12 was fitted to a 27-month series of temperature-compensated fundamental frequencies from a monitored concrete girder bridge to characterise normal variability and flag statistical anomalies. The frequency series was derived from automated SSI processing of ambient vibration data recorded at 30-minute intervals. Temperature compensation used a piecewise linear regression against measured deck surface temperature, reducing frequency variance by 68 %. The AR(12) model residuals had a mean absolute error of 0.018 Hz on a held-out six-month validation set. A cumulative sum control chart applied to the squared residuals detected a simulated frequency reduction of 2 % within 48 hours with a false alarm rate below 0.5 % per month. The approach was subsequently tested against two real events: a minor vehicle collision recorded in maintenance logs and a period of deck waterproofing repair. The collision produced a detectable but transient anomaly; the repair period generated a persistent shift that was correctly flagged on the second day.

title: Transfer learning from finite-element model ensembles for damage localisation in reinforced concrete bridges with limited sensor counts
abstract: A transfer learning strategy is proposed and evaluated for localising damage in reinforced concrete bridges when only four to six accelerometers are available, a constraint common in low-budget deployments. An ensemble of 500 finite-element models was generated by randomly perturbing material stiffness, boundary condition stiffness, and mass distribution within credible ranges calibrated against field measurements of a real bridge. For each model, seven simulated damage scenarios were created by reducing element stiffness in defined zones by 10–50 %. Modal strain energy ratios computed from the first four mode shapes were used as features. A random forest classifier trained on FE-derived features was applied directly to field-derived features without retraining; a domain adaptation step corrected for systematic bias between simulated and measured mode shapes. On field data from a separate monitored bridge not used in training, the adapted classifier achieved 78 % correct damage-zone identification across 21 artificially induced stiffness reductions ranging from 8 to 35 %. Misclassifications were predominantly between adjacent zones.

title: Task Inventory Construction for Machine Operators in the Serbian Plastics Processing Sector
abstract: This study describes the construction and initial validation of a task inventory designed for machine operators employed in plastics processing plants in the Vojvodina region. Using a structured expert-panel approach with 14 incumbent operators and 6 production supervisors across five companies, a pool of 187 candidate task statements was generated and subsequently reduced to 112 items through content-validity ratio screening. Each retained item was rated on frequency, criticality, and trainability scales by a stratified sample of 203 operators. Factor analysis yielded eight interpretable task clusters, corresponding broadly to machine setup, process monitoring, quality inspection, preventive maintenance, material handling, documentation, safety compliance, and cross-functional communication. Inter-rater reliability for cluster assignment averaged κ = 0.74. The inventory is proposed as a foundation for job classification and in-company training needs assessment in the sector. Limitations include the regional sample and the exclusion of highly automated lines, which are addressed as directions for further work.

title: Comparing National Qualification Frameworks for Metalworking Trades: Evidence from Serbia, Hungary and Romania
abstract: National qualification frameworks (NQFs) in post-transition economies differ substantially in how they define and level metalworking occupations, creating barriers to cross-border labour mobility and corporate benchmarking. This paper presents a systematic comparative analysis of occupational descriptors for five metalworking trades—welder, CNC turner, toolmaker, sheet-metal worker, and quality control inspector—across Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. Qualification documents from each country's official NQF were coded using a common analytical scheme derived from the European Qualifications Framework referencing reports. Coding was performed by three independent raters; inter-rater agreement was satisfactory (Fleiss κ = 0.69). Results show that knowledge descriptors converge reasonably across countries, whereas skill and competency descriptors diverge markedly, particularly for autonomy and responsibility indicators. The analysis identifies 23 descriptor elements present in at least two frameworks but absent in the third. Practical implications are discussed for multinational manufacturers operating sites across the three countries.

title: Job Grading Systems in Central European Manufacturing: Structures, Criteria and Firm-Level Variation
abstract: Job grading—the systematic allocation of jobs to pay and status bands—relies on explicit or implicit competency and task criteria, yet the grading logic used by manufacturers in Central Europe is poorly documented in academic literature. This book chapter reviews published grading schemes and internal job evaluation documents obtained from 19 manufacturing firms in Serbia, Slovakia, and Austria under research confidentiality agreements. The chapter distinguishes point-factor, classification, and market-pricing approaches and examines the extent to which each approach incorporates defined competency standards versus informal managerial judgement. Serbian and Slovak firms predominantly use classification systems inherited from socialist-era job families, with incremental modifications; Austrian firms show greater use of point-factor methods linked to sectoral collective agreements. The chapter argues that the persistence of classification systems in transition economies makes them a tractable target for competency-framework integration, and proposes four design principles for such integration based on the comparative evidence.

title: Measuring Task Complexity in Welding Occupations: A Multi-Site Field Study
abstract: Task complexity is a widely used but inconsistently operationalised construct in job analysis and grading. This study develops and tests a task-complexity measurement procedure applied specifically to welding occupations. Drawing on the Fine functional job analysis tradition, we decompose 94 welding task statements collected at seven production sites (three in Serbia, two in Hungary, one in Croatia, one in Romania) into data, people, and things dimensions, each rated on three-point scales by certified welding engineers acting as subject-matter experts. A total of 41 subject-matter experts participated. Intraclass correlation coefficients for the three dimensions were 0.81, 0.63, and 0.77 respectively, suggesting that the people dimension requires more anchoring support. Complexity scores were aggregated to occupational subtype level (MIG/MAG, TIG, electrode, automated) and revealed that automated welding operator roles score systematically lower on data and people complexity but higher on equipment-monitoring requirements than manual welding roles—a finding with implications for how grading schemes should treat automation-influenced jobs.

title: Alignment Between Vocational Training Curricula and Employer Competency Expectations in Electrical Installation Trades
abstract: This study examines the degree of alignment between the competency content of secondary vocational school curricula for electrical installation and the competency expectations stated by employers hiring graduates into manufacturing maintenance roles. Curriculum content was coded from official syllabus documents across nine vocational schools in Vojvodina. Employer expectations were derived from structured interviews with 27 maintenance managers and from competency gap reports produced during the probationary periods of 84 recent hires. Alignment was assessed at the level of individual competency elements using a matching algorithm. Overall alignment was 61 percent, meaning that roughly one in three employer-required competency elements had no direct counterpart in the assessed curricula. Gaps were most pronounced in programmable logic controller troubleshooting, energy efficiency regulation, and documentation practices. The paper discusses possible curriculum revision mechanisms within the Serbian secondary vocational education framework and the role that employer associations could play in formal curriculum consultation processes.

title: Reliability and Temporal Stability of Competency Self-Assessments Among Production Workers
abstract: Self-assessment instruments are frequently used in competency frameworks as a low-cost data collection mechanism, but their reliability properties in production worker populations have received limited empirical attention. This study investigates test-retest reliability and parallel-form reliability of a 48-item competency self-assessment instrument administered at two food-processing plants and one rubber goods plant in Serbia. A total of 191 operators completed the instrument at baseline and again after a 6-week interval under stable working conditions. A parallel form was administered to a subsample of 87 participants. Test-retest intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.61 to 0.86 across nine competency scales; scales related to interpersonal and communication competencies showed lower stability than technical and procedural scales. Parallel-form correlation averaged 0.71. Participants with lower educational attainment showed higher within-person variability at retest. The findings argue for supervisor-corroborated rather than standalone self-assessment designs in formal grading or development decisions.

title: Human Capital Classification in Small and Medium Manufacturers: Practices and Constraints in the Western Balkans
abstract: Human capital classification—the systematic assignment of workers to defined categories based on knowledge, skills, and competencies—is theoretically attractive for workforce planning, yet its adoption among small and medium-sized manufacturers (SMEs) in the Western Balkans is uneven. This paper reports findings from a survey of 143 SMEs across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, complemented by 22 in-depth managerial interviews. Only 34 percent of firms operate any formal job classification scheme; among these, 71 percent rely on schemes inherited from predecessor state enterprises with minimal updating. Resource constraints, weak external audit requirements, and low awareness of competency-based grading alternatives are identified as primary barriers. The study tests a mediation model in which perceived regulatory pressure mediates the relationship between firm size and classification formality, finding significant indirect effects. Implications for public policy support and chamber-of-commerce guidance services are discussed.

title: Towards a Sector-Level Competency Reference Framework for the Food and Beverage Manufacturing Industry in Serbia
abstract: Sector-level competency reference frameworks provide a shared vocabulary for recruitment, training, and job evaluation that individual firms lack the resources to develop independently. This paper describes the methodology and interim outputs of a framework development process for Serbia's food and beverage manufacturing sector, which employs approximately 78,000 workers and is the country's largest processing employer. The development process combined a literature review of analogous frameworks from EU member states, analysis of job postings collected over 18 months (n = 4,140 postings), focus groups with HR managers (eight groups, 51 participants), and Delphi validation rounds with a 19-member expert panel. The resulting draft framework contains 11 occupational families, 34 reference jobs, and 127 competency elements organised across knowledge, skill, and responsibility dimensions. Mapping to the Serbian NQF levels 3 through 5 is proposed. The paper discusses methodological decisions made during framework construction and unresolved issues concerning maintenance and governance of the framework post-publication.

title: Digitisation of Production Lines and Its Effects on Operator Competency Profiles: A Longitudinal Observation Study
abstract: When a manufacturer introduces automated or semi-automated equipment on a previously manual assembly line, the required competency profile of line operators changes. This longitudinal study tracked competency profile shifts at two plants in Vojvodina—one assembling household appliances, one producing agricultural machinery components—over a 30-month period that included the installation of robotic assembly cells. Using repeated task-analysis observations (four measurement points per plant), structured supervisor ratings, and records from in-company training logs, we document which task elements were displaced, retained, or newly required. Across both plants, manual dexterity and physical endurance tasks declined markedly, while monitoring, fault detection, and system-restart tasks increased. Interpersonal coordination requirements increased moderately. Training provision lagged behind competency demand shifts by an average of 7.4 months. The paper proposes a simple early-warning indicator derived from deviation between updated task profiles and current training syllabi to help HR functions anticipate and close emerging competency gaps.

title: Competency Equivalence Testing Across Production Sites of a Multinational Manufacturer: A Measurement Invariance Study
abstract: Multinational manufacturers operating multiple sites in different countries often wish to compare workforce competency data across sites for benchmarking and mobility purposes. This paper presents a measurement invariance study conducted on competency assessment data from five production sites of a fictional tier-1 automotive supplier operating in Serbia, Hungary, Poland, and Portugal. A 36-item competency assessment instrument was administered to 1,104 machine technicians. Multigroup confirmatory factor analysis tested configural, metric, and scalar invariance across the four country groups. Full metric invariance was supported for all competency scales, but scalar invariance failed for three items related to formal documentation practices, likely reflecting country-specific administrative conventions. Partial scalar invariance models are estimated, and their implications for cross-site mean comparisons are explained using latent mean estimation examples. The study demonstrates that straightforward mean comparisons across sites are defensible for most but not all competency dimensions, and recommends item-review procedures before deploying standardised instruments across culturally diverse manufacturing environments.

title: Estimating the monetary value of on-the-job training in Serbian small and medium enterprises: a matched employer–employee approach
abstract: This study estimates the financial return to formal on-the-job training in a sample of 214 Serbian SMEs observed over four years (2008–2011). Using a matched employer–employee dataset constructed from firm tax records and a purpose-designed HR survey, the analysis applies an instrumental variable estimator that exploits variation in regional training-subsidy availability as an instrument for training intensity. Results indicate that an increase of ten hours of formal training per employee per year is associated with a 2.3 percent rise in gross value added per worker two years later. The effect is larger in manufacturing (3.1 percent) than in trade (1.4 percent). Firm age and ownership structure are shown to moderate the return substantially, with privatised formerly state-owned enterprises exhibiting returns roughly half those of privately founded firms. The paper discusses implications for public training co-financing schemes and argues that standard accounting frameworks systematically understate human-capital investment in small firms.
venue: South-East European Journal of Business and Economics

title: Bismuth-film modified carbon paste electrode for anodic stripping voltammetry of cadmium and lead in river sediment extracts
abstract: A bismuth-film carbon paste electrode was prepared by in situ deposition of bismuth(III) at 350 µg L⁻¹ onto unmodified graphite paste during the preconcentration step in acetate buffer (pH 4.5). Square-wave anodic stripping voltammetry (SW-ASV) yielded well-resolved peaks for Cd(II) at −0.78 V and Pb(II) at −0.56 V vs. Ag/AgCl. The linear range extended from 0.5 to 80 µg L⁻¹ for both metals, with detection limits of 0.12 µg L⁻¹ for Cd and 0.18 µg L⁻¹ for Pb. Eleven certified reference sediment samples (SRM Danube series) were used to validate the procedure. Matrix-matched calibration reduced systematic error from 14% to below 4%. The electrode retained its analytical response over 120 consecutive measurements without significant surface fouling. Results were confirmed by ICP-MS analysis of digested reference materials with recoveries between 97% and 103%.

title: Effect of fulvic acid concentration on the stripping voltammetric signal of Cd(II) at bare and nafion-coated carbon paste electrodes
abstract: Fulvic acid (FA) extracted from the Sava river floodplain was added at concentrations of 0, 5, 10, 20, and 50 mg L⁻¹ to synthetic solutions containing 10 µg L⁻¹ Cd(II). Peak current suppression at a bare carbon paste electrode reached 62% at 50 mg L⁻¹ FA. A Nafion-coated electrode (0.5% solution, 5 µL, dried 30 min at 60 °C) reduced suppression to 18% under identical conditions, attributed to electrostatic exclusion of negatively charged FA moieties from the electrode surface. Differential pulse mode was preferred over square-wave mode because of lower background noise in humic-rich matrices. A correction algorithm based on a second independent measurement at −1.05 V, where FA adsorption is reversible, was derived and tested on 25 pore water samples from Fruška Gora foothill streams. The corrected values agreed with ICP-MS data within ±7%.

title: Preparation and characterisation of zeolite-modified carbon paste electrodes for preconcentration of Pb(II) prior to stripping analysis
abstract: Clinoptilolite zeolite from the Zlatokop deposit (Serbia) was ground to below 5 µm and incorporated into carbon paste at mass fractions of 5%, 10%, and 20% (w/w) in mineral oil. The 10% composite gave the highest peak current for Pb(II) in acetate buffer. X-ray diffraction and SEM-EDX confirmed retention of zeolite crystal structure within the paste matrix and identified an exchange capacity of 1.42 meq g⁻¹. The preconcentration time was optimised at 120 s at −0.80 V. Detection limit for Pb was 0.08 µg L⁻¹, representing a threefold improvement over the unmodified electrode under the same conditions. Cross-sensitivity to Cu(II) at concentrations below 50 µg L⁻¹ was negligible. The electrode was applied to determine Pb in pore water squeezed from three Danube riverside sediment cores, with concentrations ranging from 2.1 to 31.4 µg L⁻¹.

title: Competitive complexation of Cd and Pb by humic acids of varying origin: implications for voltammetric speciation in sediment pore waters
abstract: Humic acids (HA) isolated from three Serbian river sediments (Tisa, Begej, Ponjavica) were characterised by elemental analysis, UV-Vis, and FTIR spectroscopy. Conditional stability constants for Cd-HA and Pb-HA complexes were determined by ion-selective electrode titration at pH 6.0 and ionic strength 0.01 M NaNO₃. Log K values for Pb ranged from 5.8 to 6.4 and for Cd from 4.6 to 5.1, varying significantly with the aromaticity index of the HA fraction. Differential pulse anodic stripping voltammetry (DP-ASV) at a bismuth-film electrode was used to measure labile metal fractions. Comparison of labile Pb concentrations measured by DP-ASV with total dissolved Pb by ICP-MS showed that between 38% and 71% of dissolved Pb was complexed, depending on HA source and concentration. These results were incorporated into a two-ligand speciation model implemented in a spreadsheet tool distributed as supplementary material.

title: Stripping voltammetric monitoring of cadmium mobilisation from contaminated Tisa river sediments during simulated flood events
abstract: Sediment cores collected at four sites along the Tisa river were subjected to controlled resuspension experiments in a 20-L mesocosm under aerobic and anaerobic conditions. Pore water was extracted by centrifugation at 3 000 g for 30 min and filtered through 0.45 µm membranes. Cd(II) concentrations were measured by SW-ASV at a bismuth-modified carbon paste electrode modified with 8-hydroxyquinoline (8-HQ, 3% w/w) to reduce Fe(III) interference. Under anaerobic conditions, pore water Cd rose from a background of 0.4 µg L⁻¹ to 18.7 µg L⁻¹ within 96 hours, attributed to reductive dissolution of iron oxyhydroxides. Aerobic resuspension caused only a modest increase to 3.2 µg L⁻¹. The 8-HQ modification decreased the Fe signal at −0.45 V by 89% without affecting Cd recovery. Data correlated well (r² = 0.96) with sequential extraction results obtained by the BCR protocol.

title: Carbon paste electrode modified with thiol-functionalised silica: selectivity for Pb(II) over interfering divalent cations in humic-rich waters
abstract: Mercaptopropyl-functionalised silica gel (MPTS-SiO₂) was synthesised by refluxing tetraethyl orthosilicate with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane in ethanol under acidic conditions, then incorporated into carbon paste at 8% (w/w). Cyclic voltammetry in 0.1 M KNO₃ confirmed the presence of thiol groups through a reversible disulfide oxidation wave at +0.38 V. For DP-ASV of Pb(II), the modified electrode showed a 4.2-fold peak current enhancement relative to unmodified paste. Selectivity coefficients (log K_Pb,M) were −2.1 for Cd, −1.8 for Zn, and −1.4 for Cu, indicating acceptable discrimination in typical pore water matrices. Humic acid at 30 mg L⁻¹ caused only 9% peak suppression compared with 41% at the bare electrode. The method was validated against certified reference water (SRM Aq-04) and applied to 18 pore water samples from the Begej canal, with Pb concentrations between 1.6 and 44.3 µg L⁻¹.

title: Simultaneous determination of cadmium, lead and zinc in sediment pore waters: optimisation of square-wave parameters and electrode geometry
abstract: A systematic optimisation of square-wave frequency (10–200 Hz), amplitude (10–50 mV), and step potential (2–10 mV) was carried out using a central composite design for the simultaneous DP-ASV determination of Cd, Pb, and Zn at a bismuth-modified carbon paste electrode. The optimum conditions (frequency 75 Hz, amplitude 30 mV, step 5 mV, deposition potential −1.20 V, deposition time 90 s) gave detection limits of 0.09, 0.14, and 0.22 µg L⁻¹ for Cd, Pb, and Zn respectively in 0.1 M acetate buffer. Electrode geometry was also studied: a larger electrode area (7 mm diameter) gave better peak resolution for the Cd-Pb pair but higher background current. Pore waters from 30 sediment samples collected across Vojvodina drainage channels were analysed. Zinc dominated at most sites (up to 210 µg L⁻¹), while Cd and Pb co-varied, suggesting a shared anthropogenic source linked to historical mining effluent.

title: Voltammetric methods for heavy metal determination in sediment pore waters: a critical comparison
abstract: This book chapter surveys the application of stripping voltammetric techniques—anodic stripping voltammetry (ASV), cathodic stripping voltammetry (CSV), and adsorptive stripping voltammetry (AdSV)—to the determination of heavy metals in sediment pore water matrices. The discussion covers electrode materials including mercury, bismuth, antimony, and tin films as well as carbon-based composites. Particular attention is given to the challenges posed by natural organic matter, with a section on quantitative correction strategies. Calibration approaches—standard addition, matrix-matched external calibration, and the Gran method—are compared with respect to accuracy in humic-rich samples. The chapter draws on published recoveries and interlaboratory comparison data to recommend workflows for routine monitoring programmes. Practical guidance is provided on pore water extraction methods (centrifugation, Rhizon samplers, diffusive gradients in thin films), filtration protocols, and storage conditions that affect metal speciation prior to electroanalytical measurement.
