title: Evaluation of reduced graphene oxide–carbon paste composite electrodes for trace Cd(II) determination: comparison with conventional graphite paste
abstract: Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was synthesised from graphite flakes using a modified Hummers procedure and subsequently reduced at 200 °C under N₂ for 2 h. Composites containing 2%, 5%, and 10% rGO in mineral oil paste were prepared and characterised by Raman spectroscopy (D/G band ratio 1.12), BET surface area (218 m² g⁻¹ for 5% composite), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. The 5% rGO composite showed charge transfer resistance of 34 Ω compared with 120 Ω for unmodified graphite paste, consistent with improved conductivity. Under optimised SW-ASV conditions, the detection limit for Cd(II) in acetate buffer was 0.04 µg L⁻¹, threefold lower than graphite paste. In synthetic pore water containing 20 mg L⁻¹ humic acid, peak current decreased by 22% for rGO composite versus 55% for graphite paste. Fifty consecutive measurements showed a relative standard deviation of 3.8%, indicating adequate stability for field monitoring applications.

title: Field-deployable stripping voltammetric cell for in-situ pore water sampling in riparian sediments: design, calibration, and pilot testing on the Danube bank near Novi Sad
abstract: A compact three-electrode flow cell was constructed from polyoxymethylene and fitted with a replaceable bismuth-film carbon paste working electrode (3 mm diameter), a Ag/AgCl reference, and a platinum counter electrode. The cell was integrated with a portable potentiostat (Torvec EA-200, single-channel) and a peristaltic pump drawing pore water through a 0.45 µm in-line filter at 0.8 mL min⁻¹. The total cell volume was 280 µL. On-site calibration used three standard additions prepared from a 1 000 µg L⁻¹ stock carried in the field kit. Pilot measurements at six riverbank locations on the Danube near Novi Sad gave Pb concentrations between 0.9 and 12.3 µg L⁻¹ and Cd between 0.1 and 1.7 µg L⁻¹. Comparison with laboratory ICP-MS analysis of split samples collected simultaneously showed mean relative deviations of 8% for Pb and 11% for Cd. Temperature correction (1.8% per °C for peak current) was implemented in firmware.

title: Seasonal variability of dissolved Cd and Pb speciation in sediment pore waters of the Begej canal: 18-month monitoring study
abstract: Pore water was extracted monthly from three fixed stations in the Begej canal (Vojvodina, Serbia) over 18 consecutive months using Rhizon SMS samplers inserted to depths of 5, 10, and 20 cm below the sediment surface. Total dissolved Cd and Pb were measured by ICP-MS; labile fractions were determined by DP-ASV at a thiol-silica carbon paste electrode with humic acid correction. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC), pH, Eh, Fe²⁺, and SO₄²⁻ were measured as auxiliary parameters. Labile Cd accounted for 55–88% of total dissolved Cd, showing a minimum in summer when DOC peaked at 18 mg L⁻¹. Labile Pb ranged from 22% to 64%, inversely correlated with DOC (r = −0.81, p < 0.001). Principal component analysis explained 73% of variance with two components dominated by redox potential and organic matter content. Results indicate that humic substance complexation, not simply redox cycling, is the primary control on seasonal Pb mobility at this site.

title: Antimony film electrode on carbon paste substrate: performance for Cd and Pb in the presence of high iron concentrations typical of reduced sediment porewaters
abstract: Antimony films deposited in situ from 500 µg L⁻¹ Sb(III) solutions were compared with bismuth films for the determination of Cd and Pb in synthetic pore water matrices containing up to 5 mg L⁻¹ Fe(II), representative of strongly reducing sediment environments. At a bismuth-film electrode, Fe(II) at 2 mg L⁻¹ caused a 34% suppression of the Cd peak, increasing to complete loss at 5 mg L⁻¹. The antimony film was less affected, showing 11% suppression at 5 mg L⁻¹ Fe(II). Linear ranges were 0.5–60 µg L⁻¹ for Cd and 0.5–80 µg L⁻¹ for Pb at the antimony electrode. Detection limits (3σ criterion) were 0.21 µg L⁻¹ for Cd and 0.27 µg L⁻¹ for Pb, somewhat higher than for bismuth. The antimony electrode was validated with spiked anaerobic pore water samples; recovery was 94–107% for Cd and 91–106% for Pb. A side-by-side comparison across 14 real samples from the Ponjavica floodplain confirmed acceptable agreement between the two film types after Fe masking.

title: Adsorptive stripping voltammetry of Cd and Pb complexes with 1-(2-pyridylazo)-2-naphthol at carbon paste electrodes: optimisation and application to industrially impacted sediment pore waters
abstract: 1-(2-Pyridylazo)-2-naphthol (PAN) was used as a complexing ligand for adsorptive stripping voltammetry (AdSV) of Cd(II) and Pb(II) at a bare carbon paste electrode in PIPES buffer (pH 7.0, 50 mM) containing 50 µmol L⁻¹ PAN. Adsorption at −0.30 V for 60 s concentrated the Cd-PAN and Pb-PAN complexes onto the electrode surface. Cathodic stripping produced peaks at −0.72 V (Cd) and −0.61 V (Pb). Detection limits were 0.06 µg L⁻¹ for Cd and 0.09 µg L⁻¹ for Pb, among the lowest reported for bare carbon paste. The method was applied to pore water samples from sediments adjacent to a former battery recycling facility in the Novi Sad industrial zone; Cd reached 94 µg L⁻¹ and Pb reached 380 µg L⁻¹ at the most impacted site. Humic acid at 25 mg L⁻¹ reduced peak currents by only 6% because PAN outcompetes HA for the metal centres under the conditions used.

title: Covariate Shift in Markov-Based Purchase Sequence Models: A Density-Ratio Approach
abstract: This paper examines covariate shift between training and deployment distributions in first- and second-order Markov chain models of retail purchase sequences. We use kernel mean matching to estimate density ratios between a labelled source dataset of 180,000 anonymised transaction records from a Serbian supermarket chain and an unlabelled target dataset of 47,000 records from a Slovenian retailer. Reweighting source training samples by the estimated ratios reduces one-step prediction error on the target by 14.3% compared to unweighted transfer, measured by cross-entropy on held-out target sequences. We provide a bias-variance analysis of the density-ratio estimator under varying source-target overlap and show that performance degrades gracefully as overlap decreases. The approach requires no labelled target data and adds negligible computational overhead at inference time. Results suggest that even shallow sequence models can benefit substantially from explicit shift correction when deployed across national retail markets with differing product assortments and shopping rhythms.

title: Importance-Weighted Hidden Markov Models for Cross-Regional Mobility Behaviour Transfer
abstract: We investigate the transfer of hidden Markov models (HMMs) trained on GPS-derived mobility sequences from one metropolitan region to another, where land-use patterns and transit infrastructure differ substantially. The source corpus contains 62,000 daily movement traces from Novi Sad and the target contains 21,000 traces from Pécs, Hungary. Importance weights are computed via logistic-regression-based density-ratio estimation on a set of trip-level features including departure time, trip duration, and activity-type distribution. Weighted Baum-Welch re-estimation of emission and transition parameters on source data followed by a short fine-tuning pass on 500 labelled target traces yields a 9.8-point improvement in activity-recognition accuracy over unweighted transfer and comes within 2.1 points of a fully supervised target model trained on 5,000 labelled traces. We also evaluate robustness under label noise in the small target supervision set. The method is computationally suitable for deployment on city-scale datasets without high-performance infrastructure.

title: Domain Adaptation for Recurrent Session-Based Recommendation Without Target Labels
abstract: Session-based recommendation systems trained on one user population often degrade when deployed for a demographically or geographically distinct population. We study unsupervised domain adaptation for GRU-based session encoders, adapting a model trained on an e-commerce session dataset of 1.2 million sessions from a Western European market to a dataset of 310,000 sessions from a Southeast European market with no available target labels. Adaptation is achieved by minimising the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between source and target hidden-state distributions in an adversarial training loop appended to the base GRU. On five standard next-item metrics (HR@10, NDCG@10, MRR, coverage, novelty), adapted models outperform direct transfer by margins of 6–12%. We conduct ablations separating the contributions of the encoder adversarial loss and a category-level alignment auxiliary objective. The study also reports how gains vary with session length distribution mismatch between domains, finding that the method is most beneficial when mean session lengths differ by more than 30%.

title: Transfer Learning for Sequential Models: Methods, Benchmarks, and Evaluation Pitfalls
abstract: This book chapter reviews the landscape of transfer learning techniques applied to discrete-event and behavioural sequence models, covering instance reweighting, feature-level alignment, parameter transfer, and meta-learning approaches. We organise methods along two axes: the degree of target supervision required and the structural assumptions made about the sequence-generating process. Particular attention is paid to evaluation design: we identify four recurring pitfalls in published benchmarks, including temporal leakage across domain boundaries, conflation of domain shift with concept drift, and the use of target validation data during hyper-parameter selection, which artificially inflates reported gains. For each pitfall we propose a concrete corrective protocol. The chapter includes case studies drawn from retail, mobility, and digital media consumption domains, using both public and proprietary datasets. Intended as a reference for practitioners deploying sequence models across heterogeneous populations, the chapter also points to open problems around privacy-constrained adaptation and low-resource target domains.

title: Subpopulation-Aware Adaptation: Clustering Source Users to Improve Target-Domain Sequence Predictions
abstract: When a source dataset contains multiple latent user subpopulations, treating it as a single homogeneous distribution can obscure the subsets most relevant to the target domain. We propose a two-stage pipeline: first, soft-cluster source users into K groups using a variational autoencoder over their purchase-sequence embeddings; second, weight each cluster's contribution to fine-tuning by its representational similarity to the target population, estimated via symmetric KL divergence on cluster-level feature distributions. Experiments on a grocery transaction dataset (source: 950,000 users; target: 120,000 users from a different regional chain) show that K=6 clusters with similarity-weighted fine-tuning achieves a 17% reduction in next-basket prediction error over flat transfer and 8% over standard importance-weighted transfer. Performance is stable for K between 4 and 10. We also examine the cluster structures recovered, finding they correspond loosely to interpretable shopping-pattern archetypes. The pipeline adds one offline clustering step with negligible cost relative to model training.

title: Quantifying Distributional Distance Between Consumer Datasets: A Practical Toolkit
abstract: Choosing the right distributional distance measure is a prerequisite for meaningful domain adaptation diagnostics, yet practitioners rarely examine this choice systematically. We compare nine distance and divergence measures—including MMD with RBF and polynomial kernels, Wasserstein-1 distance estimated via the Sinkhorn algorithm, total variation, Jensen–Shannon divergence, and two classifier-based proxy measures—applied to six pairs of real consumer-behaviour datasets spanning retail, streaming, and banking domains. Dataset sizes range from 15,000 to 2.1 million sessions or transactions. We evaluate each measure by its rank-correlation with actual post-transfer model performance degradation, finding that Wasserstein-1 with a learned cost metric and a gradient-boosting-based classifier proxy consistently produce the highest correlations (Spearman ρ ≈ 0.81 and 0.78 respectively). We release a documented Python library implementing all nine measures with a unified interface. The toolkit is intended to assist practitioners in auditing dataset compatibility before investing in full adaptation pipelines.

title: Federated Domain Adaptation for Behavioural Sequence Models Across Retail Partners
abstract: Sharing raw transaction data across competing retail organisations is legally and commercially infeasible, yet jointly improving a shared sequence model would benefit all parties. We frame this as a federated domain adaptation problem: each of four retail partners holds a private dataset (sizes ranging from 80,000 to 420,000 users) and a global GRU-based next-item model is adapted to each partner's distribution using only locally computed gradient updates and aggregated feature statistics. We introduce a federated MMD alignment term that operates on summary statistics transmitted to a central coordinator rather than raw embeddings. After 40 communication rounds, per-partner models achieve within 3.5% of a centralised adaptation baseline that would require full data pooling. Privacy guarantees are characterised under differential privacy with ε=4.2. The paper also reports wall-clock communication overhead, which is dominated by the summary-statistic exchange rather than gradient transmission. Experiments use synthetic and real datasets under a data-use agreement with a regional retail consortium.

title: Concept Drift Detection in Sequential Consumer Data Using Adaptive Windowing and Representation Shift Monitoring
abstract: Distribution shift in deployed sequence models can arise gradually (concept drift) or abruptly (data drift); conflating the two leads to unnecessary retraining or missed degradation events. We propose a monitoring framework that tracks two signals in parallel: an ADWIN-based drift detector operating on rolling prediction-error streams, and a representation-drift monitor comparing cosine similarity between rolling mean hidden-state vectors and a reference window. Applied to 18 months of daily transaction streams from a mid-sized Serbian e-commerce platform (approximately 9,000 daily active users), the combined framework correctly identifies 14 of 16 manually annotated drift events, with two false positives. Detection latency averages 4.2 days. We compare against four baseline drift detectors (DDM, EDDM, PHT, STEPD) and show that the representation-shift monitor provides complementary signal particularly for gradual seasonal drift. The monitoring overhead is less than 2% of inference cost. Integration with an automated retraining trigger reduces average post-drift performance recovery time from 11 days to 4 days.

title: Source Selection Under Budget Constraints for Multi-Source Transfer to Behavioural Sequence Targets
abstract: When multiple potential source datasets are available for transfer, selecting which sources to include is non-trivial, especially when labelling or licensing costs constrain how many sources can be used. We formalise source selection as a combinatorial optimisation problem and evaluate three tractable heuristics: greedy selection by pairwise Wasserstein distance to the target, a Shapley-value-based attribution method, and a regularised regression approach that estimates each source's marginal contribution on a small probe set. Experiments span 12 source datasets across three behavioural domains (streaming media consumption, ride-hailing, grocery retail) with a fixed target in each domain. Across 36 transfer scenarios, Shapley-value attribution selects the most effective source subsets in 28 cases using a probe set of only 200 target examples. We also study how gains degrade as probe set size shrinks to 50 examples, finding that Wasserstein-based greedy selection becomes competitive at this regime. The study provides practical guidance on source curation workflows for teams with limited data access.
venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics

title: Evaluating Cross-Domain Robustness of Temporal Purchase Pattern Models Under Assortment Heterogeneity
abstract: Retail datasets from different markets differ not only in user behaviour but also in the item catalogue, making direct feature-level comparison impossible. We study a constrained transfer setting in which source and target share only a partial item overlap of 15–60% and examine how catalogue heterogeneity interacts with population shift. Using a controlled data generation framework and three real retail datasets, we systematically vary overlap levels and measure their effect on the adaptation gains achievable by importance weighting, adversarial alignment, and catalogue-embedding alignment methods. Results show that below 25% item overlap, all three methods converge to near-chance performance on target-exclusive items, and that catalogue-embedding alignment—using pre-trained product category embeddings as a bridge—degrades most gracefully, retaining 58% of full-overlap adaptation gains at 20% overlap. We release the data generation framework and reproducibility scripts. Findings have direct implications for retailers considering model sharing or acquisition of analytics assets from other markets.

title: Test-Time Adaptation of Behavioural Sequence Models Using Unlabelled Target Batches
abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) updates model parameters using only the unlabelled batch of target inputs available at inference time, without access to source data or target labels. We adapt this paradigm to GRU-based sequence models by defining a self-supervised auxiliary objective—predicting masked sub-sequences—that can be minimised on each incoming target batch before generating recommendations or predictions. On three deployment scenarios involving shifts in user demographics, device type, and regional market, TTA with 100-sample target batches recovers 73–85% of supervised adaptation gains in under 30 seconds of update time on a single GPU. We analyse stability under small batch sizes (down to 20 samples), finding that a layer-normalisation-only update strategy avoids the divergence observed with full-parameter TTA at small batch sizes. The method is compatible with any pre-trained GRU model without architectural modification, requiring only an auxiliary masked-token prediction head added at adaptation time.

title: Drought trends in Vojvodina, 1961–2023
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of drought trends across the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia for the period 1961–2023, utilizing a network of 14 meteorological stations and monthly precipitation and temperature records obtained from the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. Three standardized drought indices—the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and the Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI)—were computed at multiple timescales to characterize drought frequency, duration, and intensity. Results indicate a statistically significant increase in the frequency of moderate-to-severe drought episodes since the mid-1980s, with the most pronounced drying trend observed during summer months. Spatial analysis conducted in a GIS environment reveals that the northeastern and eastern sub-regions of Vojvodina exhibit greater drought vulnerability compared to the western areas adjacent to the Danube floodplain. The study further identifies a decadal oscillation in drought recurrence linked to large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns over the Euro-Atlantic sector. These findings carry direct implications for agricultural planning and water resource management in one of Serbia's most economically significant farming regions.

title: Spatial interpolation of precipitation anomalies in the Pannonian Plain using geostatistical methods
abstract: Accurate spatial representation of precipitation anomalies is fundamental to regional climate assessments and agricultural risk modeling. This study evaluates the performance of five geostatistical interpolation techniques—ordinary kriging, universal kriging, co-kriging with elevation as a covariate, radial basis function interpolation, and inverse distance weighting—applied to monthly precipitation anomaly data from 27 meteorological stations distributed across the Pannonian Plain in Serbia and Croatia for the period 1971–2010. Cross-validation was employed to assess interpolation accuracy using root mean square error and mean absolute error metrics. Results demonstrate that ordinary kriging and co-kriging consistently outperform simpler deterministic methods, particularly in areas with complex microclimatic gradients near the Fruška Gora massif. Seasonal differences in interpolation performance are documented, with winter months showing markedly higher predictability than the convection-dominated summer season. All analyses were performed within an open-source GIS framework, and the resulting interpolated raster layers were integrated into a multi-temporal geodatabase for downstream drought and climate trend analysis. The methodology presented here is directly transferable to operational agro-meteorological monitoring systems.

title: Assessment of the SPEI drought index under projected climate scenarios for northern Serbia to 2050
abstract: This paper investigates projected changes in drought conditions across northern Serbia using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) derived from statistically downscaled outputs of three regional climate models participating in the EURO-CORDEX initiative under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 emission scenarios. Baseline statistics were established from observed station data for 1981–2010, and future projections were analyzed for two time horizons: 2021–2040 and 2041–2060. Spatial analysis in a GIS environment was used to map drought frequency, mean duration, and peak intensity across a 5 km resolution grid covering the Vojvodina administrative province. Results indicate that under the high-emission scenario, the probability of summer drought events exceeding SPEI −1.5 doubles by the 2041–2060 period relative to the baseline. Intermodel uncertainty is quantified and discussed in relation to regional teleconnections and model biases in simulating summer precipitation. The findings have direct relevance to climate adaptation strategies for the agricultural sector, particularly irrigated maize and sunflower cultivation in the Bačka and Banat plains. Recommendations for integrating these projections into spatial planning decision support tools are outlined.

title: GIS-based delineation of agro-climatic zones in Vojvodina using cluster analysis of drought and temperature indicators
abstract: The spatial delineation of agro-climatic zones is a prerequisite for precision agricultural management and land-use planning. This study proposes a GIS-based methodology for classifying the Vojvodina region into homogeneous agro-climatic zones by applying hierarchical and k-means cluster analysis to a composite dataset of drought indices (SPI-3, SPI-12, SPEI-3), mean growing-season temperature, thermal amplitude, and frequency of late spring frosts, computed from 18 meteorological stations over 1981–2020. Cluster solutions were evaluated using the silhouette coefficient and Calinski-Harabasz index to determine the optimal number of zones. Five distinct agro-climatic zones were identified, each characterized by a unique drought risk profile and thermal regime. The resulting zone map was produced in vector GIS format and overlaid with existing land-cover and soil-type data to assess zone-specific agricultural vulnerability. The methodology is reproducible and scalable, making it suitable for integration into regional agricultural information systems or decision support platforms operated by agri-tech companies. This work represents a contribution to the spatial planning literature for post-socialist transitional economies facing accelerated climate change.

title: Remote sensing integration with ground-based drought monitoring: a case study of the Bačka lowland
abstract: Ground-based drought monitoring networks in the Western Balkans suffer from sparse station coverage and data gaps, motivating the integration of satellite-derived vegetation and soil moisture indices as complementary observational sources. This paper presents a multi-source drought monitoring framework for the Bačka lowland in northern Serbia, combining the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) anomaly derived from MODIS Terra 16-day composites, and the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) Level-3 product for the period 2015–2022. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses were used to quantify the relationship between SPI timescales and satellite-derived stress indicators across four land-use classes: arable land, orchards, pastures, and wetlands. Results show that NDVI anomalies lag SPI-3 by approximately four to six weeks on arable land, while SMAP soil moisture correlates most strongly with SPI-1 and SPI-2. The integrated framework is implemented as a semi-automated workflow in an open-source GIS environment, enabling near-real-time drought condition mapping. Practical implications for operational early-warning systems are discussed, with reference to data requirements relevant to agri-tech and environmental monitoring enterprises.

title: Temporal variability of the SPI and PDSI over the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal network zone and implications for water management
abstract: The Danube–Tisa–Danube (DTD) hydro-amelioration system in Vojvodina is central to the region's agricultural water balance, yet its management is increasingly challenged by hydro-climatic variability. This study examines temporal variability in the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) for meteorological stations situated in the DTD zone over the period 1961–2020, using Mann-Kendall trend tests and Sen's slope estimator to detect monotonic changes in drought index time series. Wavelet coherence analysis is applied to identify cyclical signals and their evolution through time. Results reveal statistically significant drying trends in summer PDSI since the late 1990s, while SPI at the 12-month timescale indicates increasingly prolonged dry spells in the hydrological year. These trends are corroborated by independent streamflow records from DTD canal monitoring stations. The GIS visualization of trend magnitudes highlights spatial heterogeneity within the seemingly flat agricultural plain, pointing to the role of local soils and land cover in modulating drought expression. The study provides actionable inputs for revising canal operation protocols and dimensioning future irrigation infrastructure under climate change.

title: Climatological atlas of drought indices for the Balkans: methodology and pilot application
abstract: Standardized climatological atlases serve as foundational reference products for climate services, yet no comprehensive drought index atlas exists for the Balkan Peninsula at the national or regional scale. This book chapter describes the methodology developed for a pilot climatological atlas covering Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on the computation, validation, and cartographic representation of four drought indices: SPI, SPEI, PDSI, and the Reconnaissance Drought Index (RDI). Input data were sourced from national hydrometeorological services and subjected to quality control procedures including homogeneity testing using the standard normal homogeneity test (SNHT) and Pettitt test. All indices were computed for multiple reference periods and timescales using a harmonized Python-based processing pipeline. Results are represented as a series of GIS-derived thematic maps showing climatological means, percentile ranks, and trend directions at 10 km spatial resolution. The chapter discusses challenges specific to the Balkan data environment, including station network sparsity, political fragmentation of data archives, and diverging national data standards, and proposes a collaborative transboundary data-sharing framework as a prerequisite for operational regional climate services.

title: WebGIS prototype for real-time drought index visualization in the Vojvodina region
abstract: Effective dissemination of drought information to agricultural stakeholders requires interactive, web-accessible spatial tools that transcend the limitations of static map products. This paper presents the design, implementation, and user evaluation of a WebGIS prototype developed for near-real-time visualization of SPI and SPEI across the Vojvodina region. The system ingests daily precipitation and temperature data from 14 automated meteorological stations via an open API provided by the national hydrometeorological service, computes drought indices on a rolling basis using a server-side Python module, and renders output layers as Web Map Service (WMS) tiles accessible through a Leaflet.js front end. The database back end uses PostGIS for spatial querying and time-series storage. A user evaluation study involving 22 participants from the agricultural advisory service confirmed that the prototype significantly improved the perceived accessibility and timeliness of drought information compared to conventional bulletin-based delivery. Key challenges related to data latency, index uncertainty communication, and mobile responsiveness are discussed. The prototype architecture is documented in sufficient detail to facilitate adaptation by environmental technology companies or public agencies seeking to deploy operational versions. Directions for expanding the system to include forecast-based drought outlooks are outlined.

title: Field measurement of long-term camber loss in precast prestressed I-girders on two highway overpasses in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper presents deflection records collected over 36 months on twelve precast prestressed I-girders forming two highway overpasses near Novi Sad. Vibrating-wire strain gauges and precise levelling were installed immediately after erection in 2007. Midspan deflections were recorded at intervals of approximately one month. The measured downward deflection at 36 months averaged 18.4 mm, while EC2 Annex B predictions exceeded this by 31 % and CEB-FIP MC90 predictions exceeded it by 26 %. Relative humidity records from the nearest meteorological station were used as environmental input. Concrete composition parameters, including water-to-cement ratio and cement content, were obtained from bridge construction records. The discrepancy is attributed partly to conservative assumptions for notional size and partly to actual curing conditions that promoted earlier hydration than assumed. The dataset is offered as a calibration reference for regional concrete mixes typical of the Vojvodina plain.

title: Sensitivity of EC2 creep coefficient to input parameter uncertainty in post-tensioned box girder bridges
abstract: The EC2 Annex B creep model requires several input parameters—compressive strength at loading, relative humidity, notional member size, and age at first loading—each carrying measurement or estimation uncertainty. This study applies a variance-based global sensitivity analysis to quantify the contribution of each input to the uncertainty of the predicted creep coefficient φ(t, t₀) for a representative post-tensioned box girder cross-section. Monte Carlo sampling with 50 000 realisations was used, drawing inputs from distributions reflecting typical Serbian construction practice. The analysis shows that age at loading and relative humidity together account for approximately 68 % of output variance. Concrete strength contributes a further 19 %. Notional size, although deterministic in practice, contributes less than 5 % when cross-section dimensions are well controlled. These findings suggest that tighter specifications for casting schedule and site humidity recording would reduce prediction scatter more than tighter concrete mix control. Practical guidance for bridge specification documents is proposed.

title: Time-dependent deflection of a continuous post-tensioned concrete viaduct: 60-month monitoring report
abstract: A five-span continuous post-tensioned concrete viaduct with span lengths of 34.5–42.0 m was instrumented prior to deck casting in 2010 and monitored until 2015. Forty-two vibrating-wire strain gauges were embedded in the concrete at mid-span and quarter-span sections, and optical levelling surveys were conducted at approximately two-month intervals. Prestress losses attributable to creep and shrinkage were separated from elastic and thermal components using a temperature-compensated strain baseline established during the first 30 days after stressing. Measured long-term midspan deflections ranged from 12 to 27 mm depending on span length. EC2 predictions using as-built concrete properties overestimated the measured deflections by 14–38 %. A correction procedure using back-calculated effective creep coefficients φ_eff is demonstrated and yields residuals within ±8 % for all monitored sections. The procedure is directly applicable to the EC2 serviceability verification framework.

title: Effect of supplementary cementitious materials on creep of prestressed concrete under moderate sustained stress
abstract: Fly ash and ground-granulated blast-furnace slag are increasingly substituted for Portland cement in bridge construction to reduce carbon emissions, but their effect on creep under sustained prestress is incompletely captured by current code models. This study prepared eighteen 100 × 100 × 400 mm prisms in three concrete mixes: plain OPC, 30 % fly ash replacement, and 40 % GGBS replacement, all at a water-to-binder ratio of 0.42. Prisms were loaded to 30 % of 28-day compressive strength at ages of 7 and 28 days and monitored for 18 months. Fly ash concrete exhibited 12–18 % higher specific creep than OPC concrete when loaded at 7 days, converging toward OPC values by 12 months. GGBS concrete behaved similarly to OPC throughout. EC2 Annex B predictions based on equivalent 28-day strength did not capture the age-at-loading sensitivity of fly ash mixes. A modified age factor for use with the EC2 model is proposed.

title: Long-term performance assessment of prestressed concrete bridges in Vojvodina: a review of monitoring programmes 2000–2018
abstract: This book chapter summarises eighteen years of periodic bridge monitoring carried out under various institutional and contractual programmes in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina. Fourteen prestressed concrete bridges ranging from simple spans of 18 m to continuous viaducts of 130 m total length are reviewed. For each structure, the monitoring instrumentation, measurement frequency, data completeness, and primary observed behaviours are described. Common findings include systematic overestimation of long-term deflections by EC2 and CEB-FIP MC90, prestress losses 10–22 % below code predictions, and satisfactory crack performance in structures with water-to-cement ratios below 0.45. The chapter also discusses practical obstacles encountered in sustained monitoring programmes: sensor replacement after vandalism, data gaps due to winter access restrictions, and evolving ownership of bridge infrastructure. Recommendations are given for the design of future monitoring programmes on similar bridge stocks.

title: Calibration of the fib Model Code 2010 creep model against long-term deflection data from seven simply supported prestressed concrete bridges
abstract: The fib Model Code 2010 introduced a revised creep compliance function compared with CEB-FIP MC90, with changes to the basic creep and drying creep components. This study calibrates the fib MC2010 model against a seven-bridge dataset compiled from monitoring campaigns in northern Serbia and southern Hungary. The bridges span the period 2004–2022 and include 36 instrumented simply supported prestressed concrete spans with concrete compressive strengths at transfer ranging from 32 to 55 MPa. The calibration adjusts two dimensionless coefficients using weighted nonlinear least squares, minimising the sum of squared relative errors of predicted versus measured midspan deflection at 12, 24, 48, and 96 months after stressing. Calibrated coefficients reduce root-mean-square error from 3.7 mm to 1.9 mm across the dataset. The sensitivity of the calibration outcome to bridge selection and weighting scheme is tested by leave-one-out cross-validation.

title: Influence of variable traffic loading intensity on time-dependent deflections of prestressed concrete highway bridges
abstract: Most creep analyses for prestressed concrete bridges treat traffic loading as a constant equivalent sustained load, but actual traffic volumes vary seasonally and may increase over the service life due to route reclassification. This study investigates how a time-varying superimposed load, derived from weigh-in-motion data collected on an arterial highway in Vojvodina over five years, affects cumulative midspan deflections compared with a constant equivalent load assumption. The bridge analysed is a three-span continuous post-tensioned box girder of 31.5–42.0–31.5 m. Creep compliance was modelled using the EC2 Annex B function with calibrated coefficients from a prior study. Step-by-step time integration was applied with monthly load increments. The variable-load analysis produced deflections 4–9 % larger than the constant-load analysis at year 20, with the difference increasing with mean annual traffic growth rate. Implications for serviceability limit state checks at intermediate assessment intervals are discussed.

title: Prestress loss estimation in existing bridges without original construction records: an inverse analysis approach
abstract: Many older prestressed concrete bridges in Serbia lack reliable as-built documentation on concrete mix design, initial prestress, and construction sequence. Estimating residual prestress is nevertheless necessary for structural assessment and load rating. This paper proposes an inverse analysis procedure that uses current deflection measurements, concrete core test results, and assumed construction scenarios to back-calculate a plausible range of residual prestress force. The procedure is applied to a 1978-vintage prestressed concrete T-girder bridge with four 24 m spans. Cores drilled from two girders yielded compressive strengths of 38–43 MPa. Deflections measured by precise levelling showed 28–34 mm of midspan sag relative to theoretical camber. The inverse analysis, implemented through a grid search over prestress and creep coefficient combinations, identifies a residual prestress between 62 % and 71 % of the nominal jacking force, consistent with an independent tendon force measurement by lift-off test on one accessible anchor.

title: Monitoring-informed remaining service life estimation for a 40-year-old post-tensioned concrete overpass
abstract: Combining long-term structural monitoring data with probabilistic service life models allows more rational maintenance scheduling than prescriptive approaches based solely on construction age. This paper demonstrates the procedure for a post-tensioned concrete overpass on a secondary road in Bačka, constructed in 1983 and continuously monitored since 2018. Monitoring data include monthly deflection surveys, continuous strain records, and periodic carbonation depth and chloride penetration measurements. Creep-induced deflection accumulated at approximately 0.6 mm per year over the monitoring period. A time-dependent reliability analysis was conducted using a limit state function defined by midspan deflection exceeding L/400. Lognormal distributions were assigned to creep coefficient, sustained load intensity, and chloride diffusion rate. The probability of exceeding the deflection limit was 3 % at the current time and is estimated to reach 12 % within 15 years without intervention. Two intervention scenarios — tendon supplementation and traffic load restriction — are evaluated in terms of their effect on the reliability index.

title: Observed time-dependent behaviour of two external post-tensioned concrete girder bridges retrofitted with additional tendons: 30-month data
abstract: External post-tensioning is increasingly applied as a strengthening measure for prestressed concrete bridges whose tendons have deteriorated or whose load rating must be increased. This paper reports observations from two highway overpasses in Vojvodina that received external tendon retrofits in 2022. Both bridges had been monitored before retrofitting as part of an ongoing regional monitoring programme, providing baseline creep and deflection records. After tendon installation, additional vibrating-wire gauges were attached to the external tendon anchorage zones and the existing embedded gauges continued to record. Over the 30-month post-retrofit monitoring period, the retrofitted bridges exhibited camber recovery of 6.2 and 8.9 mm respectively, consistent with the elastic component of the additional prestress. Longer-term creep redistribution between original and new tendons is detectable in the differential strain records. The data are used to validate a step-by-step analysis in which the original and retrofit tendon systems are treated as discrete prestress increments with different ages at loading.

title: Effect of composite action degree on the serviceability vibration response of steel-concrete floor systems
abstract: The degree of shear connection between a steel joist and a concrete slab influences both the effective flexural stiffness and the predicted natural frequency of a composite floor panel. This study examines how partial composite action, ranging from 40% to 100% full connection in increments of 10%, alters the fundamental frequency and the peak acceleration response under a standardised walking excitation model. Analytical calculations following a modified transformed-section approach are combined with finite element simulations using a three-dimensional shell-beam model. Parametric results show that reducing composite action from 100% to 60% decreases the fundamental frequency by approximately 8% for a 6 m span panel with a 75 mm slab, and increases the predicted peak acceleration by 18–22% depending on modal damping assumed. The sensitivity of frequency to partial composite action is highest for shorter spans and thicker slabs. Implications for limit state assessment and inspection-based reliability updating are discussed.
venue: Steel and Composite Structures – An International Journal

title: Endogenous phytase activity in wholemeal wheat flour: effect of water activity and temperature on phytate degradation during dough resting
abstract: The study examined phytate hydrolysis driven by endogenous phytase in wholemeal wheat flour under varying water activity (0.90–0.98) and temperature (25–45 °C) conditions during a 60-minute dough resting period. Phytic acid was quantified by HPLC with UV detection after iron precipitation. Water activity of 0.96 combined with 35 °C yielded the greatest reduction in myo-inositol hexakisphosphate, reaching 68% degradation compared with 21% under the lowest water activity tested. First-order kinetic constants were calculated for each condition. Partial degradation to lower inositol phosphates (IP5 and IP4) was tracked and confirmed by anion-exchange chromatography. The molar ratio of phytate to zinc dropped from 28 to below 10 in optimised samples, suggesting a meaningful shift toward predicted zinc bioaccessibility. The results provide a practical basis for adjusting bread-making protocols without enzyme supplementation.

title: Phytate content and phytase activity across triticale varieties grown in Vojvodina: a screening study
abstract: Fourteen triticale varieties cultivated in the Vojvodina region were screened for total phytic acid content and endogenous phytase activity in wholegrain flour. Phytic acid ranged from 4.3 to 9.1 mg/g dry weight, while phytase activity measured at pH 5.0 and 37 °C varied between 38 and 147 nkat/g. A moderate negative correlation (r = −0.51) was observed between phytase activity and residual phytic acid after a 2-hour aqueous incubation. Grain protein content showed no significant association with phytase activity. Two varieties exhibited both relatively low initial phytate and high phytase activity and were identified as candidates for reduced-phytate flour production without additional processing steps. The data contribute to a regional anti-nutritional factor database for Vojvodina cereal varieties.

title: Mapping inositol phosphate profiles in lentil flour during lactic acid bacterial fermentation using ion-exchange HPLC
abstract: Lentil flour was fermented with three lactic acid bacterial strains (Lactobacillus plantarum NS-4, Lactiplantibacillus brevis 17M, and Leuconostoc mesenteroides L22) isolated from traditional Serbian fermented products. Inositol phosphate species IP6 through IP3 were quantified at 0, 4, 8, 12, and 24 hours using anion-exchange HPLC with suppressed conductivity detection. All three strains promoted phytate hydrolysis primarily via acidification-mediated activation of endogenous phytase; exogenous phytase secretion was not detected in cell-free supernatants. IP6 declined by 91–96% within 24 hours across strains, with transient accumulation of IP5 and IP4 peaking at 8 hours. Residual lower phosphates (IP3) at 24 hours were below 0.3 mg/g in all treatments. Iron and zinc solubility in fermented flour slurry, measured by centrifugation and AAS, increased by 3.1- and 2.8-fold respectively compared to unfermented controls.

title: Phytate reduction in whole-grain sorghum flour by sequential hydrothermal treatment: influence on in vitro iron and zinc bioaccessibility
abstract: Whole-grain sorghum flour was subjected to sequential hydrothermal treatment (steeping at 55 °C for 90 minutes followed by autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 minutes). The effect on phytic acid, polyphenol content, and in vitro mineral bioaccessibility was assessed. Phytic acid decreased by 61% after sequential treatment compared with 27% after steeping alone. Total polyphenols, determined by Folin–Ciocalteu, were reduced by 38%. Using a dialysability assay simulating gastrointestinal digestion, iron bioaccessibility rose from 2.4% to 7.8% and zinc bioaccessibility from 5.1% to 13.4% in processed versus raw flour. The simultaneous reduction in both phytate and polyphenols explains the additive improvement in mineral release. Sensory acceptability of experimental porridges prepared from treated flour, evaluated by a 12-member trained panel, was rated comparable to untreated controls.

title: Phytase thermostability engineering: a review of approaches applicable to bread-baking conditions
abstract: Phytases are inactivated at temperatures above 70 °C, which limits their effectiveness during bread baking where crumb temperatures exceed 90 °C. This chapter summarises published strategies for improving phytase thermostability, including directed evolution, rational mutagenesis at disulfide bridge positions, immobilisation on food-grade carriers, and encapsulation in alginate or resistant starch matrices. Reported improvements in half-life at 70 °C range from 2- to 18-fold depending on approach. The chapter evaluates each strategy against practicality criteria for industrial flour supplementation: regulatory status of the carrier material, cost of production, compatibility with bread texture, and labelling implications under European food law. Case studies from wheat, rye, and mixed-grain breads are discussed. Gaps in knowledge, particularly around the fate of encapsulated phytase during steam injection baking, are identified.

title: In vitro Caco-2 iron uptake from fermented lentil and chickpea flours: cell model protocol and sensitivity to residual phytate level
abstract: A standardised Caco-2 cell ferritin formation protocol was adapted for use with legume flour digesta and tested across a range of residual phytate concentrations (0.1–6.5 mg/g flour) obtained by varying fermentation duration. Cells were maintained under standard conditions and exposed to digesta from in vitro pepsin–pancreatin digestion. Ferritin mass per milligram cell protein increased non-linearly as residual phytate fell below 2 mg/g, with a plateau effect at very low phytate levels. A phytate-to-iron molar ratio of approximately 5 corresponded to 50% of maximum ferritin response in this model. The protocol was validated using FeSO4 standards and the inhibitory reference compound inositol hexakisphosphate. Between-run CVs for ferritin measurements were below 9%. The adapted protocol is offered as a reproducible tool for ranking flour treatments by their iron nutritional quality.

title: Pilot-scale fermentation of composite wheat–lentil flour: phytate reduction, dough rheology, and bread nutritional quality
abstract: Composite flours containing 20%, 30%, and 40% lentil flour were fermented at pilot scale (50 kg batch) using a Lactiplantibacillus plantarum starter culture at 30 °C for 16 hours before bread production. Phytic acid reduction relative to unfermented composite flours reached 82–88% across inclusion levels. Farinograph water absorption increased with lentil inclusion (from 60.2% for wheat control to 68.7% for 40% composite), while dough stability time decreased by 3.1 minutes at the highest inclusion level. Bread loaves were evaluated for specific volume, crumb porosity, crust colour (CIELAB), and in vitro iron bioaccessibility. Specific volume declined from 4.1 to 3.3 cm³/g as lentil inclusion rose, but in vitro iron bioaccessibility increased from 4.3% (wheat control) to 9.6% (fermented 30% composite). Sensory scores for flavour and overall acceptability were not significantly different between fermented composite and wheat control loaves at the 30% inclusion level.

title: Exogenous phytase supplementation of extruded chickpea snacks: enzyme survival through extrusion and effect on phytate in the extrudate
abstract: Chickpea flour was mixed with a thermally encapsulated microbial phytase preparation before extrusion at barrel temperatures of 120 and 140 °C using a co-rotating twin-screw extruder (screw speed 200 rpm, moisture content 16%). Enzyme recovery after extrusion was assessed by activity measurement in ground extrudate slurry at pH 5.0 and 37 °C. At 120 °C, 28% of initial activity was recovered; at 140 °C, recovery dropped to 9%. Post-extrusion incubation of ground extrudate at 37 °C for 4 hours at adjusted moisture content (60%) reduced phytic acid by 52% at 120 °C treatment and 19% at 140 °C, compared with 6% in enzyme-free controls. The results suggest that a post-extrusion enzyme activation step is feasible if product is intended for reconstitution or further cooking. Texturometer measurements confirmed that post-incubation did not significantly alter extrudate hardness or fracturability.

title: Exopolysaccharides from lactic acid bacteria as texture modifiers in plant-based fermented foods: structure–function relationships
abstract: This chapter reviews experimental evidence for relationships between the primary and secondary structure of lactic acid bacteria exopolysaccharides and their macroscopic functional behaviour in plant-based gel systems. Sections cover the main structural determinants—backbone stiffness, degree of branching, charge density, and molecular weight—and their quantitative links to intrinsic viscosity, critical entanglement concentration, and gel-forming capacity as measured by oscillatory rheology. The discussion emphasises that ropy EPS phenotypes characterised by high molecular weight (> 10⁶ Da) and low branching tend to produce stronger weak gels in soy and oat matrices compared to capsular EPS with higher branching density. Interaction of EPS with protein networks in fermented matrices is discussed with reference to published microscopy and turbidity data. The chapter also outlines practical constraints in scaling EPS production from laboratory to pilot scale, including losses during ethanol precipitation and the variable performance of commercial enzyme preparations used for deproteinisation. Over 90 primary sources are cited.

title: Creep and Temperature-Induced Drift in Piezoresistive Wheatstone Bridge Force Sensors Under Sustained Static Loading
abstract: Piezoresistive Wheatstone bridge sensors exposed to sustained loads exceeding 72 hours exhibit a measurable output drift that is distinct from thermal offset. This study characterises that drift by subjecting ten nominally identical sensors to constant compressive loads of 5 N, 15 N, and 30 N inside a temperature-stabilised chamber held at 25 ± 0.05 °C. Resistance values of all four bridge arms were sampled every 60 seconds over 96-hour cycles. Results show a non-linear drift curve with a fast component saturating within the first 8 hours (mean 0.31% of full-scale output) and a slow component accumulating at approximately 0.004% per hour thereafter. The fast component correlates with resistor geometry, while the slow component correlates with substrate adhesive thickness as measured by profilometry. An empirical two-exponential decay model was fitted with R² above 0.97 for all 30 sensor-load combinations. The findings provide a quantitative basis for scheduling in-situ recalibration events in wearable systems that cannot be returned to a laboratory.

title: Humidity Sensitivity of Screen-Printed Piezoresistive Pastes and Its Contribution to Baseline Drift in Wearable Force Measurement
abstract: Screen-printed piezoresistive thick-film resistors are a cost-effective alternative to thin-film bridges, but their hygroscopic binder matrix absorbs water vapour and alters apparent resistance. This paper reports a systematic study of three commercial conductive paste formulations printed on flexible polyimide substrates and characterised over a relative humidity range of 20–90 % RH at constant temperature. Resistance was recorded continuously during humidity ramp cycles and during three weeks of wear-like cycling between 40 % and 75 % RH. All three pastes showed hysteresis in their resistance-versus-humidity response, with peak-to-peak variations of 0.8 %, 1.4 %, and 2.1 % of the nominal resistance value. A simple humidity co-sensor embedded on the same substrate and fed into a software compensation routine reduced the apparent drift by 71–84 % depending on paste type. Cross-sensitivity to substrate bending radius was also assessed at radii between 30 mm and 80 mm. The study recommends paste selection criteria and a two-sensor correction architecture for integration into wearable insoles and knee-sleeve monitoring devices.

title: A Switched-Reference Architecture for Continuous In-Situ Gain Calibration of Capacitive Force Sensor Arrays
abstract: Capacitive force sensors in wearable arrays suffer from dielectric permittivity changes caused by temperature, sweat ingress, and mechanical fatigue of the dielectric layer. This paper presents a switched-reference circuit architecture that interleaves measurement cycles with reference-capacitor cycles at 20 Hz to track and correct gain variations without interrupting normal data acquisition. A 16-element sensor array fabricated on a silicone substrate was integrated into a plantar-pressure insole and worn by five participants during 30-minute treadmill sessions. With the calibration disabled, gain drift reached 4.7 % over the session; with the architecture active, residual drift was held below 0.6 %. The reference capacitors are sealed units on the same flex circuit, dimensionally stable to better than 0.05 % over the operating temperature range as verified by impedance spectroscopy at 1 kHz, 10 kHz, and 100 kHz. Power overhead of the switching circuitry is 1.8 mW from a 3.3 V supply. The architecture is described in sufficient detail for replication and the firmware is made publicly available.

title: Long-Term Stability Assessment of Piezoresistive Knee-Joint Force Sensors Over a Six-Month Outdoor Field Trial
abstract: Laboratory drift characterisation typically spans hours to days; this study reports a six-month uncontrolled field deployment of piezoresistive sensors embedded in textile knee sleeves worn by eight recreational runners. Sensors were based on a commercial 4-arm bridge chip encapsulated in medical-grade silicone and connected via a Bluetooth data logger to a smartphone app. Monthly laboratory reference measurements were made using a deadweight calibration rig. Over six months, seven of the eight sensors showed a monotonic upward offset drift averaging 1.9 % of full-scale per month, with individual variation between 0.8 % and 3.1 %. Two sensors experienced step-changes in offset coinciding with recorded incidents of high-impact falls. Principal-component analysis of the full time-series distinguished thermal drift, mechanical fatigue, and encapsulant delamination as separable drift sources. The results quantify realistic in-use degradation rates and provide a baseline against which self-calibration algorithms can be benchmarked under real-world conditions.

title: Comparison of Polynomial, Piecewise-Linear, and Neural-Network Correction Functions for Residual Nonlinearity in Capacitive Force Sensors After Gain Self-Calibration
abstract: After gain and offset are corrected by an in-situ calibration loop, a residual nonlinearity of up to 1.2 % of full-scale remains in the capacitive force sensor arrays studied here, arising from fringe-field geometry changes under load. This paper compares three post-calibration correction functions—a third-order polynomial, a seven-segment piecewise-linear map, and a shallow fully-connected neural network with one hidden layer of eight neurons—trained on data from 12 sensors across three fabrication batches. Evaluation used a leave-one-batch-out cross-validation protocol. The polynomial reduced residual nonlinearity to 0.41 %, the piecewise-linear map to 0.38 %, and the neural network to 0.29 %, but the neural network required 14 times more microcontroller RAM than the polynomial. On a Cortex-M4 target processor at 80 MHz the polynomial executes in 3.1 µs and the neural network in 47 µs per sample. The paper provides implementation guidelines for choosing among the three options depending on the available hardware and the tolerable nonlinearity budget.

title: In-Situ Reference Signal Generation Using a Micro-Fabricated Deadweight Cell on a Flexible Substrate
abstract: Most in-situ calibration schemes for wearable force sensors rely on electrical reference elements rather than mechanical ones, leaving the transduction chain from physical force to electrical signal uncalibrated end-to-end. This paper describes a micro-fabricated deadweight reference cell—a small sealed cavity containing a tungsten mass of known weight (23.4 ± 0.05 mg) attached via a thin-film spring to the same piezoresistive bridge used for measurement—that generates a repeatable 0.23 N reference force signal on command by enabling an electrostatic actuator. The cell is fabricated on a 125-µm polyimide substrate using a five-mask process. Reference signal repeatability over 500 actuation cycles was better than 0.15 % (1σ). Mechanical cross-coupling to adjacent sensor elements in a 4×4 array was below 0.08 %. Integration into a forearm-worn impact-measurement band demonstrated end-to-end offset correction of 2.3 % over a two-hour session. The approach eliminates the need for periodic removal of the device from the wearer for laboratory recalibration.

title: Effect of Cyclic Mechanical Fatigue on the Capacitance-Force Relationship of Silicone Dielectric Elastomer Sensors
abstract: Silicone dielectric elastomer capacitive sensors used in wearable force measurement undergo stiffness and permittivity changes after repeated compression cycles, which shift the nominal capacitance-force calibration curve. Specimens of three silicone formulations were subjected to 0–200 000 compression cycles at 2 Hz between 0 N and 20 N in a custom cyclic loading rig. Capacitance at zero load, capacitance at 10 N, and the slope of the capacitance-force curve were tracked at intervals of 10 000 cycles. After 200 000 cycles the softest formulation showed a 7.2 % reduction in slope and a 4.4 % increase in zero-load capacitance; the stiffest formulation showed 2.1 % and 1.8 % respectively. Scanning electron microscopy cross-sections at 0, 50 000, and 200 000 cycles revealed progressive microvoid formation in the softer matrices. A phenomenological aging model expressed as a function of cumulative strain energy was fitted and validated on a hold-out dataset of 40 000 additional cycles. The model can be embedded in firmware to schedule adaptive recalibration events based on estimated cumulative use.

title: Drift-Aware Data Fusion of Piezoresistive and Inertial Sensors for Continuous Wrist-Force Estimation During Manual Assembly Tasks
abstract: Combining a piezoresistive wrist-worn force sensor with a six-axis inertial measurement unit (IMU) can improve wrist-force estimates during dynamic manual assembly, but the two sensor modalities age at different rates, which can introduce systematic estimation errors over a shift-length deployment. This paper presents a drift-aware fusion filter based on an unscented Kalman filter in which the drift state of the force sensor is treated as an augmented slow-varying variable estimated jointly with the kinematic state from the IMU. Experiments used 11 participants performing a standardised 45-minute assembly task on a simulated production board. Ground-truth force was measured by a load cell embedded in the tool handle. Without drift correction, root-mean-square force estimation error grew from 0.21 N at the start to 0.74 N by 45 minutes. With drift-aware fusion the final error was 0.29 N, a reduction of 61 %. Computational load on a wrist-worn Cortex-M33 processor was 8.4 % at 100 Hz output rate.

title: Benchmarking Self-Calibration Strategies for Capacitive Plantar-Pressure Arrays Against Standardised Drift Injection Profiles
abstract: Evaluation of self-calibration algorithms for wearable sensors is hampered by the absence of shared benchmark protocols. This paper proposes a set of five standardised drift injection profiles—step offset, linear ramp, diurnal thermal cycle, impact-induced step, and slow permittivity drift—implemented in a hardware-in-the-loop test bench that injects synthetic drift into the analogue signal path of a real 16-element capacitive plantar-pressure array. Six self-calibration algorithms drawn from the literature were re-implemented and evaluated on all five profiles using root-mean-square error, latency to 90 % correction, and peak overshoot as metrics. The switched-reference gain method performs best on gain-ramp profiles (RMSE 0.18 N) but is slowest to recover from step disturbances (latency 3.4 s). An adaptive-rate polynomial correction introduced here offers a balanced trade-off across all five profiles. The test bench hardware description and all algorithm implementations are published under an open licence to encourage community adoption of the benchmark.

title: On the transferability of AOS nitrogen calibration models across years and fields in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: A recurring practical concern with active optical sensor applications is whether calibration equations developed in one year or location can be applied in another. This study tested the inter-annual and inter-site transferability of three regression models (linear, quadratic, and partial least squares) for predicting winter wheat LNC from red-edge reflectance indices. Model training data came from 2013–2015 field experiments (n = 380 calibration points), and validation was carried out on independently collected 2016 and 2017 datasets from fields not used during training. Transferring the PLS model without recalibration resulted in RMSE increases of 18–34% relative to within-dataset cross-validation. A gain-normalisation procedure using a small set of concurrent anchor measurements (n = 8–12 per field) reduced this RMSE penalty to 6–9%, making the calibration operationally viable. The study provides practical guidelines for the minimum number of destructive calibration samples needed each season to maintain acceptable prediction accuracy.

title: Aerosol-jet deposition of silver nanoparticle ink on PET: effect of substrate temperature on line morphology and sheet resistance
abstract: Silver nanoparticle inks (50 nm mean particle diameter, 40 wt% loading in ethylene glycol) were deposited on polyethylene terephthalate substrates using an aerosol-jet system at substrate temperatures ranging from 25 °C to 80 °C. Line width, edge roughness, and sheet resistance were characterised by profilometry, SEM, and four-point probe measurement. At 60 °C substrate temperature, the minimum sheet resistance of 28 mΩ/sq was achieved at a sintering temperature of 130 °C for 30 minutes, compared to 54 mΩ/sq for room-temperature deposition under identical sintering conditions. Adhesion was assessed by cross-cut tape test according to ISO 2409; samples deposited above 50 °C showed Grade 0 adhesion. The study identifies a processing window suitable for roll-to-roll integration and provides empirical correlations between deposition parameters and electrical performance. Substrate pre-treatment with oxygen plasma (60 W, 2 min) improved wetting but did not significantly alter final sheet resistance.

title: Printed carbon electrode arrays for multiplexed detection of nitrite and phosphate in irrigation water
abstract: A 4 × 4 array of inkjet-printed carbon electrodes on flexible PEN substrate was developed for simultaneous amperometric nitrite and potentiometric phosphate detection in irrigation water. Nitrite determination used differential pulse voltammetry at +0.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl in 0.1 M PBS; a phosphate-selective membrane doped with trioctylamine was cast on alternate electrodes for potentiometric measurement. The nitrite sensor showed a linear range of 5–500 µM (LOD 1.8 µM) with no interference from chloride or sulphate up to 5 mM. The phosphate electrode gave a near-Nernstian slope of −28.4 mV per decade over 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻² M. Arrays were tested with 24 irrigation water samples from the Vojvodina region; results agreed with reference ion chromatography within 8% relative error. The 16-electrode format allows eight replicate measurements per analyte from a single 4 cm × 6 cm strip.

title: Intraoperative laser Doppler flowmetry at the colonic anastomosis site: a pilot study of thirty patients undergoing left hemicolectomy
abstract: Anastomotic leak remains a major source of morbidity after colorectal resection, and impaired tissue perfusion at the anastomotic margins is considered a principal contributing factor. This prospective pilot study enrolled 30 consecutive patients undergoing elective left hemicolectomy at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2009 and 2011. Laser Doppler flowmetry probes were applied to the proximal and distal bowel margins immediately after bowel division and after anastomosis construction. Perfusion flux values were recorded and correlated with postoperative outcome over a 30-day follow-up period. Three patients (10%) developed anastomotic leak confirmed by CT or re-operation. In these three patients, intraoperative perfusion flux at the distal margin was below 45 perfusion units (PU), compared with a mean of 112 PU in the leak-free group (p = 0.04). Although the sample size precludes definitive conclusions, the findings indicate that a low distal-margin flux measurement may identify bowel segments with inadequate perfusion before anastomosis is completed. Limitations include the absence of a standardised probe placement protocol and the single-centre design. The study provides baseline data for a larger validation trial.

title: Risk factors for anastomotic leak following anterior resection for rectal cancer: a retrospective cohort analysis of 210 cases
abstract: This retrospective cohort study examined 210 patients who underwent anterior resection for rectal cancer at two colorectal surgery units in Vojvodina between 2006 and 2013. The primary outcome was clinically relevant anastomotic leak (grade B or C by the International Study Group of Rectal Cancer definition) within 30 days of surgery. Leak occurred in 24 patients (11.4%). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified male sex (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.1–7.1), anastomosis height below 6 cm from the anal verge (OR 4.1, 95% CI 1.7–10.0), operative time exceeding 210 minutes (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.0–5.3), and preoperative haemoglobin below 110 g/L (OR 2.6, 95% CI 1.1–6.4) as independent predictors. Body mass index, neoadjuvant therapy, and diverting stoma formation were not independently significant in this sample. The study confirms established demographic and technical risk factors in a regional patient population and highlights the need for objective intraoperative perfusion assessment tools to complement these predictors. Inter-centre variability in surgical technique is acknowledged as a limitation.

title: Agreement between laser Doppler flowmetry and indocyanine green fluorescence angiography in assessing bowel wall perfusion during colorectal resection
abstract: Two intraoperative perfusion assessment modalities—laser Doppler flowmetry (LDF) and indocyanine green near-infrared fluorescence angiography (ICG-NIF)—were compared in 28 patients undergoing sigmoid or rectal resection. After bowel division, both measurements were obtained at four standardised sites along the proximal margin before anastomosis formation. LDF provided continuous flux values in perfusion units; ICG-NIF provided time-to-peak fluorescence intensity derived from video analysis. Bland–Altman analysis showed acceptable agreement at three of four sites (mean bias below 8%), with wider limits of agreement at the most distal site (bias 14%, 95% limits −31% to +59%). Spearman correlation between LDF flux and ICG-NIF peak intensity was 0.71 (p < 0.001). The two methods disagreed in four cases; in two of these, the surgeon modified the anastomotic level based on fluorescence findings. No anastomotic leaks occurred at 30 days in this series. The study suggests that the two modalities capture overlapping but not identical aspects of perfusion and that combining them may improve information available to the surgeon.

title: Effect of vasopressor use during colorectal resection on intraoperative bowel wall perfusion measured by laser Doppler flowmetry
abstract: Vasopressor agents administered to maintain mean arterial pressure during surgery are known to cause peripheral vasoconstriction, potentially reducing intestinal wall perfusion. This prospective observational study included 52 patients who underwent elective colorectal resection under general anaesthesia with standardised fluid management. Norepinephrine infusion was required in 21 patients (40%) to maintain mean arterial pressure above 65 mmHg. Laser Doppler flowmetry measurements were taken at the proximal and distal bowel margins at three timepoints: before anastomosis, during peak vasopressor dose, and 10 minutes after vasopressor weaning. In the vasopressor group, mean distal margin flux was 34% lower than in the non-vasopressor group at the time of anastomosis construction (78 vs 118 PU, p = 0.008). Flux values partially recovered after vasopressor discontinuation. Anastomotic leak occurred in 3 of 21 vasopressor-exposed patients and in 1 of 31 non-exposed patients (p = 0.14). The study provides quantitative evidence that intraoperative haemodynamic management influences perfusion measurements and that this variable should be controlled for in future perfusion-based risk models.

title: Machine learning prediction of anastomotic leak using preoperative and intraoperative variables in 380 colorectal resections
abstract: Prediction models for anastomotic leak have largely relied on logistic regression with a limited number of predictors. This study applied gradient-boosted decision trees (XGBoost) to a prospectively collected dataset of 380 consecutive colorectal resections performed at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2015 and 2021. A total of 34 candidate features were included, spanning preoperative (age, sex, BMI, ASA class, albumin, haemoglobin, comorbidities, neoadjuvant treatment), intraoperative (anastomosis height, operative time, blood loss, vasopressor use, LDF distal flux, ICG Srise and Imax), and surgical-technical variables. The dataset was split 70/30 for training and internal validation. The XGBoost model achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.83 (95% CI 0.75–0.91) on the test set, outperforming logistic regression (AUC 0.71). SHAP analysis identified ICG Srise, anastomosis height, and distal LDF flux as the three most influential predictors. The model was externally validated on 89 cases from the General Hospital Sombor (AUC 0.79). Calibration plots showed modest overestimation of risk in the 10–20% probability range. Prospective validation before clinical deployment is warranted.

title: Impact of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy on anastomotic tissue perfusion in rectal cancer: an ICG fluorescence study
abstract: Neoadjuvant long-course chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) before anterior resection for rectal cancer may alter mesorectal vascularity and tissue perfusion, potentially increasing anastomotic leak risk. This prospective case-control study compared intraoperative ICG fluorescence parameters in 44 patients who received nCRT (50.4 Gy with concurrent capecitabine) against 44 matched controls who underwent primary surgery. Fluorescence Srise values at the distal margin were significantly lower in the nCRT group (mean 3.1 vs 4.8 units/s, p = 0.003). Tpeak was prolonged by a mean of 4.2 seconds in the nCRT group (p = 0.01). Imax did not differ significantly between groups. Anastomotic leak occurred in 7 of 44 nCRT patients (15.9%) and 4 of 44 controls (9.1%; p = 0.34). In the nCRT subgroup, patients who leaked had lower Srise than those who did not (1.9 vs 3.4 units/s, p = 0.02). The findings suggest that nCRT attenuates perfusion kinetics at the anastomotic site, and that fluorescence-based parameters may have particular prognostic relevance in this population.

title: Surgeon-level variability in ICG fluorescence image interpretation and its consequences for anastomotic decision-making
abstract: Fluorescence angiography with ICG is increasingly used to assess bowel perfusion before anastomosis, but the interpretation of fluorescence images relies substantially on subjective surgeon judgement. This study quantified inter-surgeon variability in interpreting 60 standardised fluorescence video clips from colorectal resection cases. Twelve colorectal surgeons from four institutions in Serbia and Hungary were each asked to classify perfusion at three bowel margin zones per clip as adequate, borderline, or inadequate, and to state whether they would revise the transection level. Overall inter-rater agreement was moderate (Fleiss κ = 0.42). Agreement was higher for clearly hypoperfused zones (κ = 0.61) than for borderline cases (κ = 0.28). Intended management differed between at least two surgeons in 41% of clips. More experienced surgeons (>200 colorectal resections) did not show significantly higher agreement than less experienced surgeons. The findings highlight the need for objective quantitative tools to reduce subjectivity in perfusion-guided surgical decisions and strengthen the case for standardised curve-analysis algorithms.

title: Wearable near-infrared spectroscopy for continuous postoperative anastomotic perfusion monitoring: a proof-of-concept study in pigs
abstract: Early detection of falling anastomotic perfusion in the postoperative period might allow preemptive intervention before clinically evident leak. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) has been used to monitor tissue oxygenation non-invasively in other surgical contexts. This proof-of-concept study evaluated a custom NIRS probe designed for transrectal placement adjacent to a colorectal anastomosis in an animal model. Twelve domestic pigs underwent anterior resection with low colorectal anastomosis under general anaesthesia. Six animals had an artificially induced partial devascularisation of the anastomotic segment; six served as controls. The NIRS probe was placed transrectally immediately after anastomosis construction and remained in place for 24 hours. StO2 values in devascularised anastomoses declined from 74% at baseline to 41% at 8 hours and to 28% at 24 hours, compared with stable values of 70–76% in controls (p < 0.001 at both timepoints). All devascularised anastomoses showed gross ischaemic changes on necropsy. Probe displacement occurred in one control animal. The findings support further development of continuous NIRS monitoring as a complement to intraoperative ICG assessment.

title: Automatic segmentation and perfusion zone classification in intraoperative ICG fluorescence video using a convolutional neural network
abstract: Manual analysis of ICG fluorescence video during colorectal surgery is time-consuming and subject to the inter-rater variability documented in our previous work. This study describes training and validation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) for automatic frame-by-frame bowel wall segmentation and classification of perfusion zones as well-perfused, borderline, or poorly-perfused in intraoperative fluorescence video. The training dataset comprised 4,200 annotated frames from 70 resection cases; annotation was performed by consensus between two experienced colorectal surgeons and served as the reference standard. A U-Net architecture with a ResNet-34 encoder was trained using fivefold cross-validation. On the held-out test set (18 cases, 1,080 frames), pixel-level segmentation Dice coefficient was 0.87. Zone classification accuracy was 84%, with sensitivity for the poorly-perfused class of 78% and specificity of 93%. Inference time per frame was 38 ms on standard hospital hardware, compatible with near-real-time use. Integration with the existing fluorescence laparoscopy platform at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina is currently underway.
