title: Retrofitting Legibility: Typographic Audit Methods for Legacy Wayfinding Systems in Post-Socialist Public Buildings
abstract: Many public buildings in Serbia retain wayfinding systems installed during the 1970s and 1980s that have been partially updated, producing typographic inconsistency across floors or wings. This preprint outlines an audit methodology developed during fieldwork in six public buildings in Novi Sad and two in Zrenjanin, conducted between 2023 and 2024. The methodology combines photographic inventory, a structured coding scheme covering typeface category, size, contrast, directionality marks, and script completeness, and a short comprehension task administered to building users. Pilot application of the audit in the eight buildings produced a comparative legibility score that correlated moderately (r = 0.54) with user task completion time. The paper argues that retrofit design interventions in such buildings are more likely to succeed when conducted with reference to a systematic baseline audit rather than ad hoc replacement of deteriorated signs. A draft audit form is appended.

title: Variable Fonts and Script Mixing: Technical Constraints and Design Considerations for Latin–Cyrillic Text in Low-Resource Print Environments
abstract: Variable font technology allows a single font file to encode a continuous range of weight, width, and other axes, reducing file overhead and potentially simplifying the management of multilingual typesetting workflows. This paper evaluates whether these advantages translate into practical benefits for organisations producing bilingual Latin–Cyrillic materials with limited technical staff and older printing infrastructure. Working with three non-governmental organisations in Serbia as case partners, we assessed existing workflows, conducted typeface selection exercises, and implemented test variable-font pipelines in each organisation's publishing software. Outcomes were measured by error rate in script-switching tasks, time per page for layout operators, and print quality on the partners' equipment. Results were mixed: variable fonts reduced file management errors but required software updates that two partners were unable to implement without external support. The paper concludes with a decision framework for organisations considering variable font adoption.

title: Participatory Sketching as a Requirements Elicitation Method for Data-Intensive Medical Interfaces
abstract: Requirements elicitation in medical informatics projects is complicated by clinical staff having limited time and variable ability to articulate interface needs in technical terms. This chapter reviews and evaluates participatory sketching—structured group sessions in which clinicians draw desired screen layouts on paper templates—as a complement to formal use-case modelling. Evidence is drawn from two case projects: a radiology workflow tool developed at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina and a general-practitioner scheduling system piloted in three primary care centres in Novi Sad. Across both projects, sketching sessions produced an average of 2.3 previously undocumented functional requirements per session that were later validated as implementation-relevant by project stakeholders. The chapter also identifies conditions under which the method fails, particularly when participants have had recent exposure to a specific commercial product whose conventions they default to reproducing rather than questioning.

title: Guest Satisfaction in Agrotourism: Evidence from Fruit-Farm Stays in the Šumadija Region
abstract: Fruit-farm agrotourism has expanded considerably in central Serbia, yet formal assessment of guest satisfaction in this sub-sector remained absent from the literature at the time of this study. Using structured exit questionnaires administered at 22 fruit farms during harvest-stay programmes in 2010 and 2011, the study collected 387 usable responses. Satisfaction was measured on a seven-point Likert scale across eight thematic dimensions derived from earlier qualitative fieldwork. Regression analysis identified host–guest interaction and authenticity of farm activities as the strongest predictors of overall satisfaction (standardised β = 0.41 and 0.37 respectively), while accommodation comfort had a comparatively modest effect (β = 0.19). Guests who participated in active farm tasks rated their stays 0.6 points higher on average than passive observers. The paper discusses how farm operators can design programmes that increase participatory contact without substantially increasing labour costs, and argues that Serbian national tourism statistics should collect activity-type data alongside accommodation data.

title: Repeat Visitation Intentions at Rural Guesthouses: The Mediating Role of Emotional Attachment
abstract: This paper investigates the pathway from perceived service quality through guest satisfaction to repeat visitation intention, testing emotional attachment as a mediator in the context of rural guesthouses. Data were collected from 496 guests at 31 guesthouses across three Serbian rural tourism zones (Fruška Gora, Zlatibor, and Stara Planina) in 2012. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to estimate the model. The indirect effect of service quality on revisit intention through satisfaction and attachment was significant (β = 0.28, 95% CI bootstrapped: 0.19–0.38). Emotional attachment mediated a larger share of the total effect than satisfaction alone, suggesting that building personal bonds—through personalised host communication and returning guests' recognition—can be a cost-effective strategy for small operators. Multigroup analysis showed no significant differences between first-time and repeat visitors in the structural model, which supports the generalisability of the findings across experience levels.

title: Measuring Tourist Expectations Before Rural Stays: A Pre-Trip Online Survey Approach
abstract: The classical gap model of service quality relies on expectation measurement at or after the point of service, which can introduce recall bias. This study tested a pre-trip online measurement protocol: guests booking rural accommodation through a regional portal completed an expectation questionnaire at booking, and a perception questionnaire within 72 hours of checkout. Matched pairs were obtained from 312 guests across 18 properties in the 2013 season. Pre-trip expectations were significantly higher for tangibles than post-booking expectations reported by a control group surveyed on arrival (t(310) = 3.14, p < 0.01), suggesting online imagery inflates tangible expectations. Satisfaction gaps were therefore wider under the pre-trip protocol for tangibles but not for other dimensions. The paper recommends that rural accommodation portals adopt photography guidelines that more accurately represent room and bathroom conditions, reducing expectation–perception mismatches and improving post-stay satisfaction scores.

title: Service Quality Perceptions in Vojvodina Agrotourism: A Cross-Seasonal Comparison
abstract: This conference paper reports preliminary findings from a multi-season data collection effort examining whether guest perceptions of service quality at Vojvodina agrotourism farms differ systematically between spring harvest visits and winter holiday stays. Surveys were administered during two spring (April–May 2014 and 2015) and two winter (December–January 2014/15 and 2015/16) periods at 16 farms, yielding 502 responses. MANOVA results indicated significant multivariate differences across seasons (Wilks' λ = 0.81, p < 0.001), driven primarily by the responsiveness and empathy dimensions. Winter guests rated personal attention from hosts considerably higher (mean difference = 0.9 on a 7-point scale), possibly reflecting lower farm activity levels allowing more host–guest contact. The paper argues that rural operators should consider season-specific service protocols and staffing rather than applying uniform service delivery scripts year-round.

title: User-Generated Reviews as a Proxy for Service Quality Scores: Comparison with Survey Data from Serbian Rural Accommodations
abstract: Online review platforms have become a primary channel through which rural accommodation guests express satisfaction, yet the relationship between platform scores and validated survey-based quality measurements has received little empirical attention for the Serbian rural context. This study matched platform review scores (aggregated from two major booking platforms) with RGS-19 survey scores collected at 24 rural properties between 2015 and 2016, producing 389 matched observations. Spearman correlation between the overall platform score and the composite RGS-19 score was ρ = 0.68 (p < 0.001), indicating moderate alignment. Dimension-level comparisons showed that cleanliness-related comments in text reviews aligned closely with tangibles scores, whereas responsiveness and empathy were systematically underrepresented in review text. Sentiment analysis of 2,140 review texts using a manually coded lexicon confirmed quantitative findings. The paper concludes that platform scores are useful screening tools but cannot substitute for structured quality measurement instruments.

title: Staff Behaviour as a Service Quality Driver in Rural Guesthouses: A Critical Incident Analysis
abstract: Critical incident technique (CIT) was used to identify staff behaviours that guests of rural Serbian guesthouses associate most strongly with service quality. Over 18 months of fieldwork ending in late 2019, 510 critical incidents were collected from 384 guests at 27 properties via follow-up telephone interviews conducted within two weeks of checkout. Incidents were coded into 11 behaviour categories by two independent coders (Cohen's κ = 0.79). Positive incidents clustered heavily around personalised problem solving (29.1% of positive incidents), while negative incidents were dominated by unavailability of staff during non-meal hours (34.8% of negative incidents). Regression confirmed that the frequency of personalised problem-solving incidents significantly predicted overall satisfaction scores (B = 1.23, SE = 0.19, p < 0.001) even when controlling for accommodation category and season. The paper discusses practical training implications for family-run properties where staff and owners often overlap.

title: Cross-Border Rural Tourism Quality Perceptions: Comparing Hungarian and Serbian Guests at Backa Guesthouses
abstract: The Hungary–Serbia cross-border region hosts a substantial flow of Hungarian day-trip and overnight rural tourists, yet comparative research on their service quality perceptions relative to domestic Serbian guests is sparse. This study collected parallel surveys in Serbian and Hungarian from 620 guests (315 Serbian nationals, 305 Hungarian nationals) at 21 licensed guesthouses in the Backa subregion during the 2020 and 2021 seasons. Multigroup PLS-SEM revealed that Hungarian guests placed significantly greater weight on food quality and regional culinary authenticity in predicting satisfaction, while Serbian guests weighted accommodation comfort more heavily. Both groups showed similar sensitivity to host responsiveness. The paper argues that guesthouses attracting cross-border guests should offer bilingual menus and expand traditional food offerings as a targeted quality investment. Limitations related to COVID-19 disruptions to visitor flows in 2020 are discussed.

title: A Longitudinal View of Service Quality Trends in Vojvodina Agrotourism: 2010–2020
abstract: Using a panel of 31 agrotourism facilities that participated in repeated RGS-19 surveys at three-year intervals between 2010 and 2019, this paper tracks changes in perceived service quality across a decade. In total, five data collection waves produced 2,847 guest responses. Linear mixed models accounting for facility-level random effects showed significant improvements in tangibles scores over the period (estimated annual trend: +0.09 scale points, p < 0.001), attributable in part to a regional subsidy programme for guesthouse renovation active between 2014 and 2017. Responsiveness and empathy scores remained stable throughout. Reliability scores declined modestly after 2016, coinciding with a period of rapid capacity expansion in the sector. The paper provides the first decade-spanning quantitative evidence of service quality trajectories in a post-socialist rural tourism region and discusses how subsidy design can be aligned with service quality outcomes rather than purely physical investment targets.

title: Willingness to Pay a Quality Premium at Rural Agrotourism Facilities: A Choice Experiment
abstract: This paper applies discrete choice modelling to estimate visitors' willingness to pay (WTP) for specific service quality improvements at Serbian agrotourism facilities. A labelled choice experiment was designed around four service attributes—host attentiveness, meal authenticity, room cleanliness standard, and availability of farm activities—with three levels each, and administered to 534 respondents recruited at nine regional tourism fairs and via an online panel in 2023. Mixed logit models estimated marginal WTP values for moving from a base to a high level of each attribute. Host attentiveness commanded the highest premium (approximately €14 per night), followed by farm activity richness (€11), meal authenticity (€8), and room cleanliness (€7). Latent class analysis identified two distinct preference segments: a 'relational' segment (58% of sample) driven by interpersonal experience, and a 'comfort-oriented' segment (42%) driven by physical standards. The paper provides pricing guidance for operators considering quality investments.

title: Digital Tools for Self-Assessment of Service Quality in Small Rural Accommodation: A Field Test in Three Serbian Regions
abstract: Small guesthouse and agrotourism operators frequently lack resources to commission professional quality audits. This paper reports the design and field test of a tablet-based self-assessment tool built around a shortened 12-item version of the RGS-19 scale, intended for use by operators without formal hospitality training. The tool was piloted with 63 rural accommodation businesses across Vojvodina, Šumadija, and Western Serbia during 2024. Operators completed the self-assessment, and their scores were compared with concurrently collected guest survey scores (n = 1,104). Intraclass correlation between operator self-assessment and aggregated guest scores was ICC = 0.61 (95% CI: 0.47–0.73), indicating moderate to good agreement. Operators systematically overestimated their tangibles scores (mean overestimation: 0.7 points) but underestimated their empathy scores. The paper discusses adjustments to tool design—including photographic anchors for tangibles items—that can reduce self-assessment bias and make the instrument useful for continuous improvement cycles.

title: Material Quantities and Embodied Energy in Low-Rise Timber-Frame Houses in Vojvodina: A Pilot Survey
abstract: This paper presents measured material quantity takeoffs from twelve completed single-family timber-frame houses built in Vojvodina between 2006 and 2011. On-site documentation and construction drawings were used to compile bill-of-materials data for structural elements, envelope assemblies, and foundations. Embodied energy was estimated using the Ecoinvent 2.2 database, with process datasets selected to approximate regional Central European supply chains where Serbian-specific data were unavailable. The twelve houses ranged from 98 to 147 m² of conditioned floor area. Mean embodied energy for the structural timber frame was found to be 412 MJ/m², while the concrete strip foundation contributed a further 290 MJ/m². The study identifies the envelope insulation layer—predominantly expanded polystyrene—as the third largest contributor at approximately 110 MJ/m². Limitations arising from the use of generic Western European inventory data in a Serbian context are discussed, and a roadmap for region-specific data collection is proposed. The results serve as a baseline for subsequent comparative studies.

title: Comparing Embodied Carbon of Timber-Frame and Reinforced Concrete Structural Systems for Two-Storey Residential Buildings: A Parametric Study
abstract: This study performs a parametric lifecycle assessment comparing embodied carbon of timber-frame and cast-in-situ reinforced concrete structural systems for a standardised two-storey residential building archetype of 120 m² floor area. The functional unit is the complete structural system including foundations, walls, floor decks, and roof structure. System boundaries follow the EN 15978 cradle-to-practical-completion scope, excluding operational energy. Three concrete mix variants (C25/30, C30/37, and a slag-blended C25/30) and two timber species sourcing scenarios (locally sawn Serbian spruce and imported Central European spruce) are compared across twelve parameter combinations. Using Ecoinvent 3.4 with adjusted transport distances, the timber-frame variants produce embodied carbon between 98 and 134 kg CO₂e/m², while the concrete variants range from 187 to 241 kg CO₂e/m². Sensitivity to concrete cement content and timber transport distance are the dominant variables. The slag-blended concrete closes roughly 22% of the gap with the timber baseline. Results are sensitive to the biogenic carbon accounting convention applied; a supplementary analysis tests both the GWP-fossil-only and GWP100 including biogenic approaches.

title: Embodied Carbon in the Foundation Systems of Low-Rise Residential Buildings on Soft Vojvodina Soils: Comparing Strip, Raft, and Driven-Pile Options
abstract: Foundation choice is frequently overlooked in building-level embodied carbon assessments but can represent 15–30% of a structure's total embodied carbon, particularly on weak cohesive soils typical of Vojvodina's alluvial plains. This paper models the embodied carbon of three foundation typologies—reinforced concrete strip, flat raft, and driven precast concrete pile with ground beam—for a 100 m² single-storey timber-frame house on three representative bearing-capacity conditions (soft clay at 40, 80, and 120 kN/m²). Structural design was carried out to the Eurocode 7 standard with local soil profiles derived from geotechnical reports for sites near Novi Sad, Zrenjanin, and Sombor. Results show that the strip foundation on the 120 kN/m² profile produces the lowest embodied carbon at 47 kg CO₂e/m² of floor area, while driven piles on the soft clay profile reach 91 kg CO₂e/m². Raft foundations occupy an intermediate position and show less variance across soil conditions. These findings suggest that geotechnical site selection can be a meaningful lever for reducing whole-building embodied carbon in low-rise construction.

title: Biogenic Carbon in Timber Buildings: How Accounting Convention Choice Shifts the Comparative Result Against Reinforced Concrete
abstract: The treatment of biogenic carbon stored in harvested wood products remains contested in lifecycle assessment practice. This paper examines how four accounting conventions—GWP100 fossil only (PAS 2050 approach), dynamic LCA with Moura-Costa crediting, the IPCC AR5 GWP100 including biogenic CO₂, and the Levasseur dynamic characterisation method—alter the comparative embodied carbon result for a matched pair of timber-frame and reinforced concrete residential archetypes designed to Serbian construction norms. The building pair consists of a 115 m² two-storey detached house with identical envelope performance. Under the fossil-only convention, the timber structure shows a 46% lower embodied GWP than the concrete structure over a 50-year reference service life. Applying the Levasseur dynamic method with a 100-year time horizon and assuming no end-of-life combustion reduces this advantage to 29%. If end-of-life incineration with energy recovery is assumed, all four methods converge toward a 35–38% advantage for timber. The paper recommends that Serbian building carbon reporting standards adopt a clearly stated biogenic carbon convention before embodied carbon limits are introduced into national regulations.

title: Embodied Carbon Benchmarks for Multi-Family Residential Buildings in Serbia: Deriving Reference Values from a Sample of Permit-Approved Projects
abstract: Nationally calibrated embodied carbon benchmarks are a precondition for setting regulatory limits and monitoring progress in the building sector. This paper derives preliminary benchmarks for multi-family residential construction in Serbia by performing lifecycle assessments of twenty permit-approved projects submitted to municipal planning authorities in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Niš between 2015 and 2020. All projects use cast-in-situ reinforced concrete structural frames with masonry infill, which constitutes the dominant typology in contemporary Serbian multi-family residential construction. Material quantities were extracted from structural drawings and submitted bills of materials. The median whole-structure embodied carbon (modules A1–A5) is 412 kg CO₂e/m² of gross floor area, with a 10th–90th percentile range of 348–501 kg CO₂e/m². Structural frame and foundations account for 61% of the median total. The paper compares these values to published benchmarks from the RICS 2023 Whole Life Carbon Assessment guidance and from Hungarian and Romanian studies using comparable methodology, finding Serbian values consistent with the Central European range. Limitations arising from exclusion of fit-out and MEP systems are noted.

title: Cross-Laminated Timber as a Structural Alternative in Serbian Multi-Family Housing: An Embodied Carbon and Cost Assessment
abstract: Cross-laminated timber (CLT) is increasingly used in multi-storey residential construction across Western and Central Europe, but its uptake in Serbia is negligible, partly due to the absence of domestic production and uncertainty about costs and environmental performance. This paper assesses the embodied carbon and approximate construction cost of a hypothetical six-storey CLT residential building of 2,400 m² gross floor area situated in Novi Sad, benchmarked against an equivalent cast-in-situ concrete frame building designed to the same spatial programme and fire resistance class. CLT panels are assumed to be imported from Austria or Slovenia based on current supply routes; two transport scenarios (road only and road plus rail) are modelled. Embodied carbon for the CLT structural system ranges from 102 to 119 kg CO₂e/m² depending on transport scenario and biogenic carbon convention, compared to 198 kg CO₂e/m² for the concrete frame. The estimated construction cost premium for CLT is 12–18% over the concrete baseline when using 2023 price data gathered from Serbian quantity surveying firms. A break-even carbon price of approximately 44 €/tonne CO₂e would be required to offset the cost premium through an embodied carbon levy, contextualising policy options for Serbian building regulations.

title: Towards a Serbian National Lifecycle Inventory for Structural Concrete: Cement Production Carbon Intensity and Regional Aggregate Transport
abstract: Reliable embodied carbon accounting for reinforced concrete construction in Serbia is constrained by the absence of a national lifecycle inventory. This paper reports primary data collected from two cement plants operating in Serbia during 2022–2023, covering clinker-to-cement conversion ratios, specific thermal energy consumption, fuel mix, and kiln dust recycling rates, supplemented by industry association aggregate production statistics. The resulting cradle-to-factory-gate carbon intensity for CEM II/A-S 42.5 cement produced in Serbia is estimated at 712 kg CO₂e per tonne of cement, compared to 740 kg CO₂e/t in the Ecoinvent 3.9 CH dataset typically used as a proxy. Regional aggregate supply is analysed using GPS-logged delivery records from three construction sites in Vojvodina, yielding mean transport distances of 38 km for gravel and 54 km for crushed stone. Incorporating these primary data into a concrete mix LCA for C25/30 reduces the cradle-to-gate concrete carbon intensity by approximately 4% relative to the Ecoinvent proxy. The paper provides adapted datasets formatted for direct import into SimaPro and recommends a pathway to formal inclusion in future versions of the Ecoinvent database.

title: Comparative Isochrone Mapping of Public Transport Accessibility in Four Serbian Cities
abstract: The study constructs 15-, 30-, and 45-minute isochrones from all residential centroids in Novi Sad, Kragujevac, Niš, and Subotica using timetable-based routing in OpenTripPlanner 0.13, fed with GTFS datasets assembled from operator schedules. Departure times were sampled at 08:00, 12:00, and 17:00 on a standard Tuesday in October 2013. The proportion of the population reachable within 30 minutes from the city hall was 61% in Novi Sad, 54% in Niš, 49% in Kragujevac, and 43% in Subotica. The paper documents the GTFS construction process in detail, as none of the four operators published feeds at the time, requiring manual digitisation of timetables. Inter-city differences are attributed primarily to network topology and headway rather than fleet size. The methodology is transferable to other cities in the Western Balkans where GTFS adoption remains limited.

title: Transit Deserts in Polycentric Mid-Size Cities: Definition and Identification Criteria
abstract: The concept of a transit desert, developed primarily for North American metropolitan areas, is adapted here for the conditions of polycentric mid-size European cities with populations between 100,000 and 500,000. The paper proposes a composite index combining three dimensions: (1) maximum walking time to the nearest stop with at least four departures per hour in peak periods, (2) ratio of transit travel time to car travel time for the ten nearest employment centres, and (3) share of car-dependent households in the census tract. The index is tested on Novi Sad using 2011 census microdata and a reconstructed GTFS feed. Fourteen census tracts out of 118 are classified as transit deserts under the proposed threshold. The paper discusses the limitations of applying North American desert typologies to cities where historical urban form is more compact and car ownership rates have risen rapidly only since the 1990s.

title: Accessibility to Healthcare by Public Transport in Vojvodina: A Multi-City Panel Study
abstract: This chapter contributes a case study of Vojvodina to a comparative volume on healthcare accessibility in post-socialist Central and Eastern Europe. Using GTFS feeds for seven cities (Novi Sad, Subotica, Zrenjanin, Sombor, Vršac, Kikinda, Pančevo) and a point dataset of 43 general hospitals and health centres, the study computes the share of population within 45 minutes by public transport of any health facility. The analysis is repeated for 2015 and 2020 to assess change over the period. Coverage in the region declined from 69% to 63% between those years, driven by service reductions in smaller cities rather than population redistribution. The chapter also maps zones where coverage is below 40% in both years, finding that these persist predominantly in peri-urban zones of Zrenjanin and Sombor. Policy implications for rural-urban feeder services are discussed in the regional context.

title: Constructing a Longitudinal GTFS Archive for Novi Sad Public Transport, 2012–2022
abstract: Retrospective accessibility analyses are constrained by the absence of archived GTFS data in cities that adopted the format late or inconsistently. This paper describes the construction of a ten-year GTFS archive for Novi Sad covering the period 2012–2022, assembled from operator timetable booklets, city council transport committee minutes, and scanned schedule boards digitised with a semi-automated OCR workflow. Each annual feed was validated against independent sources including newspaper notices of route changes and a subset of GPS traces donated by volunteer transit riders. The archive contains 11 annual snapshots with a median of 22 routes and 614 stop records per snapshot. Validation shows stop position accuracy within 8 m on average and schedule accuracy of 94.7% at the trip level. The archive is deposited at the University of Novi Sad institutional repository and released under an open data licence. Potential uses for longitudinal accessibility, ridership, and equity research are outlined.

title: Does New Tram Infrastructure Reduce Transit Deserts? A Pre–Post Study of the Subotica Light Rail Extension
abstract: A 4.2 km light rail extension opened in Subotica in late 2022, linking the city centre to two outer residential neighbourhoods built between 2005 and 2015. This study applies the transit desert index developed in earlier work (Đorđević & Stojanović, 2017) to Subotica census tracts before (June 2022) and after (June 2023) the extension, using GTFS feeds from both periods and 2021 census population data. The number of census tracts classified as transit deserts fell from nine to five. However, three of the four reclassified tracts had above-median car ownership, suggesting the new line primarily serves residents with transport alternatives already available. Two tracts with below-median car ownership in the western periphery remain classified as deserts. The paper argues that rail extensions in mid-size cities are not sufficient on their own to address transit desert problems without complementary bus feeder improvements.

title: Sensitivity of Transit Accessibility Metrics to GTFS Feed Quality: A Simulation-Based Assessment
abstract: GTFS feeds from smaller operators frequently contain errors: missing stop coordinates, incorrect trip sequences, or mismatched calendar entries. This paper quantifies how such errors propagate into accessibility metrics by introducing controlled perturbations into a validated Novi Sad GTFS feed and recomputing 30-minute isochrone areas for 120 origin points. Six error types are tested: stop displacement (10–200 m), schedule offset (1–10 min), missing trips (1–20% randomly removed), duplicated trips, incorrect shape references, and calendar boundary errors. Missing trips have the largest effect, reducing computed accessible population by up to 22% when 15% of trips are absent. Stop displacement errors below 50 m have negligible effect on area metrics but can cause misclassification of individual stops near network edges. The findings provide practical guidance for researchers deciding whether to pre-clean feeds before analysis and suggest minimum quality thresholds for comparative studies.

title: Downscaling Monthly Air Temperature Over the Vojvodina Plain Using MODIS Land Surface Temperature and Regression-Kriging
abstract: Monthly mean air temperature fields at 1 km resolution were produced for the Vojvodina plain by combining MODIS Terra LST composites (MOD11A2, 2003–2008) with ground observations from 34 meteorological stations operated by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. A regression-kriging framework was adopted in which daytime and night-time LST, elevation, and distance to water bodies served as covariates in an ordinary least-squares pre-regression step, with residuals subsequently interpolated by ordinary kriging. Leave-one-out cross-validation yielded a mean absolute error of 0.62 °C averaged across all months, improving on straight inverse-distance weighting by 31 %. Spatial patterns of cold air pooling in topographic depressions and urban heat islands around Novi Sad and Subotica were captured more faithfully than in the national 10 km gridded product. Seasonal decomposition showed the strongest LST-to-air-temperature coupling in July and weakest in December, a result attributed to soil moisture and snow cover masking effects.

title: Mapping Growing Degree Days at Sub-Kilometre Scale Across the Middle Danube Basin
abstract: Growing degree days (GDD, base 10 °C) were computed at 500 m resolution for the 2005–2010 growing seasons across a 180 000 km² domain spanning Hungary, Serbia, Croatia and Romania. Temperature surfaces were produced by spatially downscaling ERA-Interim reanalysis fields using a statistical transfer function fitted to surface station data and MODIS LST anomalies. The transfer function was a geographically weighted regression model, separately calibrated for spring and summer sub-periods to account for differing advection regimes. Validation against 51 held-out stations showed RMSE in cumulative GDD below 120 GDD-days for the April–September period. The resulting maps revealed consistent positive anomalies along the Fruška Gora slopes relative to flat Vojvodina, with implications for early-harvest crop variety selection. The dataset was made available as a 12-band GeoTIFF archive through a regional agrometeorological data portal.

title: Estimating Reference Evapotranspiration in Data-Sparse Regions by Fusing SEVIRI and MODIS Thermal Imagery
abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀, Penman–Monteith FAO-56) requires net radiation and humidity inputs that are often measured only at sparse synoptic stations. This study fused instantaneous surface radiation estimates from the MSG/SEVIRI satellite (3 km, 15-minute) with daytime MODIS LST (1 km, daily) to reconstruct diurnal temperature and radiation cycles at 1 km resolution over Serbia for 2008–2011. A temporal interpolation scheme based on sinusoidal fitting between two daily MODIS overpasses was applied to fill the radiometric gap left by SEVIRI's coarser spatial detail. Daily ET₀ estimated from the downscaled inputs agreed with FAO Penman–Monteith computed from station data to within 0.38 mm day⁻¹ (RMSE, n = 28 stations). Spatial maps revealed a systematic ET₀ gradient from the Pannonian lowland to the Šar Mountains exceeding 1.1 mm day⁻¹ in July, consistent with independent eddy covariance records at two sites.

title: Kriging Interpolation Variants for Daily Precipitation in Complex Terrain: A Comparative Assessment Over the Dinaric Alps Fringe
abstract: Four kriging variants — ordinary kriging (OK), kriging with external drift (KED), co-kriging with elevation, and indicator kriging of wet-day occurrence — were evaluated for daily precipitation interpolation using a 62-station network across a 55 000 km² domain covering the Dinaric fringe of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro. The 2009–2013 wet-season record was used, with 15 % of stations withheld for validation in each of 200 bootstrap iterations. KED using terrain-exposed elevation as the external drift variable outperformed OK in 73 % of daily cases, with mean RMSE reductions of 12 % in autumn and 8 % in spring. Indicator kriging proved most accurate for binary wet-day mapping, reducing false wet-cell fractions by 18 percentage points compared with deterministic methods. Variogram range parameters varied seasonally between 28 km in convective summer and 110 km in frontal winter regimes.

title: Spatiotemporal Drought Monitoring Over the Pannonian Basin Using the SPEI at Multiple Time Scales Derived from Downscaled Gridded Climate Data
abstract: The Standardised Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month accumulation periods was computed at 1 km resolution over the Pannonian Basin for 1991–2015 using monthly precipitation and ET₀ grids produced by the author's regression-kriging pipeline. The resulting 25-year, 288-layer dataset allowed continuous spatial tracking of drought onset, intensity and recovery without relying on station interpolation alone. Trend analysis using the Mann–Kendall test identified statistically significant (p < 0.05) drying trends in 34 % of the study area at the 12-month SPEI, concentrated in the eastern Hungarian and western Romanian sectors. Correlation of 3-month SPEI with satellite NDVI composites (MODIS MOD13Q1) reached 0.71 for rainfed maize areas, confirming utility for near-real-time agricultural drought early warning. Comparison with the European Drought Observatory CCI SM product showed spatial agreement of 78 % for severe drought flags.

title: Comparison of Machine Learning Regressors and Geostatistical Models for 1 km Daily Minimum Temperature Mapping Over Serbia
abstract: Random forest (RF), gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost), and artificial neural networks were compared against regression-kriging and co-kriging for the task of producing daily minimum temperature grids at 1 km over Serbia. Inputs common to all methods included MODIS LST, DEM-derived topographic variables, distance to major water bodies, and calendar-day encoding. Training used station data from 67 automatic weather stations for 2013–2017; testing was performed on 2018–2019 withheld data. Random forest achieved the lowest test RMSE (0.88 °C) compared with regression-kriging (0.97 °C), XGBoost (0.91 °C), and co-kriging (1.03 °C). However, regression-kriging produced better-calibrated prediction intervals and smoother spatial fields in data-sparse mountain regions. An ensemble blending RF predictions with kriging residuals achieved RMSE of 0.81 °C while retaining spatial coherence. Computational cost for the ensemble was approximately 4× that of standalone RF.

title: Reconstructing Pre-Satellite Agroclimatic Grids for the Carpathian–Pannonian Region Using Historical Station Records and Spatial Reanalysis
abstract: High-resolution gridded records of growing season length, heat accumulation, and aridity index were reconstructed for the 1961–2000 period over the Carpathian–Pannonian region by downscaling the ERA-20C centennial reanalysis to 2 km using transfer functions calibrated on the 2001–2015 overlap period with MODIS LST data. Station data from 148 surface synoptic stations in five countries were used to bias-correct the ERA-20C baseline. Trend testing showed a 14-day advance in start-of-growing-season dates between 1961 and 2000 in the lowland zone, consistent with independent phenological records for winter wheat. The reconstruction fills a critical gap for long-term impact assessments that require spatial data prior to the MODIS era. Uncertainty was quantified by propagating station observation errors and ERA-20C ensemble spread through the downscaling chain, yielding 90 % confidence intervals of ±3 days for growing season start.
venue: Climate Dynamics – Regional Studies

title: Agroclimatic Zoning of Soybean Cultivation Potential in the Western Balkans Under Present and Near-Term (2030–2040) Climate Projections
abstract: Soybean cultivation in the Western Balkans is expanding but spatially under-characterised. This study applied a set of agroclimatic indices — growing season length, sum of active temperatures above 10 °C, number of dry spells exceeding 10 days in July–August, and mean diurnal temperature range during pod fill — computed from high-resolution (1 km) historical grids and from dynamically downscaled EURO-CORDEX RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 projections for 2030–2040. Under RCP4.5, the area classified as highly suitable for soybean is projected to increase by 11 % relative to the 1991–2020 baseline, driven primarily by warming in the mountainous interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro. Under RCP8.5, suitability decreases in the Vojvodina core zone due to increased drought stress frequency. Results were delivered as Web Map Service layers and as 1 km GeoTIFF products.

title: Sensitivity of Spatial Downscaling Performance to Variogram Estimation Sample Size in Sparse Station Networks
abstract: Variogram estimation is a fundamental step in geostatistical downscaling, but its reliability degrades when fewer than 30–40 stations are available — a common situation in developing countries. Using a sub-sampling simulation study on the 72-station Serbian agrometeorological network, this work examined how kriging interpolation error grows as the estimation sample is reduced from 72 to 8 stations for monthly mean temperature, total precipitation, and reference ET₀. Variograms were estimated by the method-of-moments and by restricted maximum likelihood (REML). REML maintained acceptable nugget-to-sill ratios down to 15 stations where the method-of-moments failed, yielding 18 % lower RMSE on average. Below 12 stations, both estimators produced unreliable range parameters. The study provides practical guidance for selecting estimation method and minimum station density thresholds for each variable type, expressed as a function of spatial autocorrelation range.

title: Detecting inter-annual change in softwood floodplain forest extent using dense Sentinel-2 time-series and a change vector approach
abstract: Softwood gallery forests dominated by Salix alba and Populus nigra are among the most flood-disturbance-adapted habitats in Pannonian river floodplains, but their spatial extent can fluctuate substantially between years in response to flood frequency and timber harvesting. This study applied a change vector analysis framework to annual phenological composites derived from Sentinel-2 MSI 10 m imagery for the period 2016–2021 across a 210 km reach of the Sava River floodplain in Serbia. Annual composites were constructed using the 20th percentile NIR and the maximum NDRE over a 60-day spring window. Change magnitudes exceeding one standard deviation above the multi-year mean were flagged and attributed to four process categories (flood disturbance, harvest clearance, natural regeneration, encroachment) using auxiliary topographic wetness index and forest management registry data. Over the six-year period, 2,140 ha of softwood forest underwent detectable canopy-layer change, with flood-related losses concentrated in the 2019 and 2021 high-water years. Accuracy of change attribution reached 82% against independent field verification of 160 change patches. The approach requires no training data beyond the composite stack and is applicable at the scale of an entire national river network.

title: Bounded Model Checking for Mutual Exclusion Protocols: A Comparative Study of Four Classical Algorithms
abstract: This paper applies bounded model checking (BMC) to four classical mutual exclusion algorithms — Peterson's, Dekker's, Lamport's Bakery, and a ticket-based protocol — encoded in Promela and analysed with SPIN 6.2. The study systematically evaluates reachability of deadlock states and violation of the critical-section property under varying thread counts from 2 to 8. State spaces grow from roughly 10^4 to over 10^9 states, making exhaustive verification infeasible beyond five threads without abstraction. We apply partial-order reduction and bitstate hashing, documenting the precision loss and the corresponding reduction in memory consumption. Results confirm that Lamport's Bakery generates the largest state space but maintains the strongest fairness guarantees; the ticket protocol is most amenable to partial-order reduction, retaining full verification up to seven threads within 4 GB memory. The comparison provides quantitative guidance for choosing mutual exclusion mechanisms in resource-constrained embedded contexts.

title: Specifying Progress Properties of Multi-Threaded Java Programs with LTL Annotations
abstract: We describe a lightweight annotation framework that maps LTL progress properties onto Java bytecode, enabling automatic extraction of finite-state models suitable for SPIN-based verification. Annotations capture liveness constraints such as starvation-freedom and eventual consistency at the method level. The extracted Promela models are conservative abstractions that preserve counterexample traces traceable back to source locations. We evaluated the approach on six open-source Java libraries containing a total of 43 annotated thread interaction points. Of eleven liveness properties specified, SPIN confirmed eight and produced counterexample traces for three, two of which corresponded to genuine bugs subsequently patched upstream. Abstraction overhead was measured: on average, the extracted model is 97% smaller in state count than a naive direct encoding. The paper discusses soundness limits of the abstraction and outlines conditions under which the approach is both sound and complete for safety sub-properties.

title: Assume-Guarantee Reasoning for Lock-Free Data Structures
abstract: Lock-free data structures avoid mutual exclusion by exploiting hardware compare-and-swap (CAS) operations, but their correctness proofs are notoriously difficult. This work applies assume-guarantee compositional reasoning to verify linearisability of three lock-free queue implementations: Michael–Scott, Kogan–Petrank, and a single-producer single-consumer ring buffer. Each component (enqueue and dequeue operations) is modelled as a labelled transition system and verified in isolation against assumptions about its environment, then composed. We formalise the composition rule in CTL* and implement verification using NuSMV 2.6. The full parallel composition of Michael–Scott with four threads and a 32-entry queue has 2.1 × 10^7 states; the compositional approach reduces per-component verification to at most 1.4 × 10^5 states. All three structures were verified correct; one latent ABA-problem scenario in the ring buffer was exposed under relaxed memory model assumptions and documented as a known limitation.

title: Timed Automata Models for Real-Time Task Scheduling in Embedded Controllers
abstract: Real-time embedded controllers must satisfy hard deadlines whose violation can cause physical harm. This paper develops a library of timed automata templates for common scheduling policies — fixed-priority preemptive, earliest-deadline-first, and cyclic-executive — and verifies schedulability and absence of deadline misses using UPPAAL 4.1. We model a case study drawn from an automotive body-control module with 12 periodic tasks and three aperiodic interrupt handlers. UPPAAL's symbolic reachability analysis with difference-bound matrices completes within 180 seconds on a 16-core workstation. Properties checked include absence of deadline misses, mutual exclusion of shared-bus access, and bounded end-to-end latency. The templates are parameterised and distributed as an open UPPAAL library. We compare verification times with those of a direct Promela encoding and find a 3× speedup attributable to UPPAAL's native clock semantics.

title: Detecting Data Races in Rust Programs via Model Extraction and SPIN Verification
abstract: Although Rust's ownership type system prevents most data races at compile time, programs using unsafe blocks or foreign-function interfaces can still exhibit race conditions. This paper proposes a pipeline that extracts a Promela model from Rust's MIR (mid-level intermediate representation) for functions marked unsafe, preserving thread-interleaving semantics and shared-reference patterns. The extraction handles raw pointers and atomic intrinsics. We evaluate the approach on 27 crates from the Rust package registry that contain unsafe blocks and have known concurrency issues listed in public issue trackers. SPIN found confirmed race conditions in 9 of 27 crates; 4 were previously unreported. State spaces for individual crates range from 8 × 10^3 to 6 × 10^6 states. False-negative analysis shows that our MIR abstraction misses races mediated by interior mutability through reference-counted types in 6 additional crates, a limitation we characterise formally.

title: Verifying Distributed Consensus Protocols with Parameterised Model Checking
abstract: Distributed consensus protocols such as Paxos and Raft are difficult to verify because correctness must hold for an arbitrary number of participants. We apply parameterised model checking, using the indexed predicate abstraction technique implemented in the Cubicle tool, to a Promela-level encoding of single-decree Paxos and a simplified version of Raft's leader election phase. For Paxos with up to n proposers and n acceptors (n treated as a parameter), we verify agreement and validity automatically for all n ≥ 3; liveness under weak fairness is verified up to n = 6 before state-space limits are reached. For Raft leader election, safety is verified for arbitrary n but liveness requires a bound n ≤ 5. We additionally identify an abstraction gap between the Raft TLA+ specification and our Promela encoding and document which properties are preserved across the gap. Verification times on a 32-core server range from 4 minutes (n = 3) to 11 hours (n = 6).

title: Baseline VOC emission profiles of peach cultivars at five maturity stages under field conditions
abstract: Accurate ripeness staging of peaches prior to robotic picking requires a reliable understanding of how volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions evolve across the full maturation window. This study characterised VOC emission profiles of four peach cultivars ('Redhaven', 'Fayette', 'Tardibelle', and 'Elegant Lady') grown in the Rimski Šančevi experimental orchard, sampled at five discrete maturity stages from 14 days pre-harvest to commercial harvest. A portable proton-transfer-reaction mass spectrometer (PTR-MS) was used in headspace mode directly at the canopy, with measurements taken on 12 individual fruits per cultivar per stage over two growing seasons (2022 and 2023). A total of 27 VOC species were detected consistently; of these, hexyl acetate, (E)-2-hexenal, and linalool showed the strongest monotonic increase correlated with destructive firmness measurements (r = 0.81–0.93). Ethylene co-measurements confirmed coordinated climacteric onset. Principal component analysis separated maturity stages with 87% correct classification using only five VOC predictors. Cultivar-specific differences in emission intensity were marked, emphasising that sensor calibration models must be cultivar-aware. The dataset provides a reference for selecting target analytes when designing lightweight sensor arrays for robotic mounting.

title: Comparison of three MEMS metal-oxide sensor arrays for ethylene detection in the 0.1–10 ppm range under orchard humidity variability
abstract: Commercial metal-oxide semiconductor (MOS) MEMS sensors are attractive for on-robot gas sensing owing to their low mass and power consumption, but their cross-sensitivity to humidity and temperature must be characterised before deployment in outdoor orchards. This study compared three commercially available MEMS sensor arrays—designated SX-A, SX-B, and SX-C—across ethylene concentrations of 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, and 10 ppm in a controlled flow-through chamber, at relative humidity levels of 40%, 60%, and 85% and temperatures of 18 °C, 24 °C, and 32 °C. Each condition was replicated eight times. Sensor response was characterised using resistance ratio (Rs/R0), response time (T90), and recovery time. SX-B showed the lowest humidity-induced drift (mean ΔRs/R0 = 0.04 across humidity levels) and a T90 of 34 s at 1 ppm ethylene, making it the most suitable candidate for real-time field use. A temperature-compensation polynomial reduced root-mean-square error in ethylene estimation from 0.41 ppm to 0.12 ppm across the tested range. Findings directly inform sensor selection for the group's robotic arm-mounted sensing module.

title: Effect of micro-canopy airflow on ethylene concentration gradients around stone fruit: implications for sensor placement on harvesting robots
abstract: Ethylene-based ripeness sensing on robotic harvesters is complicated by the dilution and redistribution of ethylene emissions within the fruit canopy. This study used a combination of ultrasonic anemometry and electrochemical ethylene spot measurements at 16 positions within peach canopy cross-sections (3 trees, 2 training systems: open-centre and tatura trellis) to characterise spatial ethylene concentration gradients under low-wind (< 0.5 m/s) and moderate-wind (1.0–2.5 m/s) conditions. Gradients of up to 0.8 ppm were recorded between the fruit proximal zone (5 cm from fruit surface) and 25 cm distance under low-wind conditions; under moderate wind, gradients collapsed below 0.15 ppm. A simple advection–diffusion model parameterised from the measurements reproduced observed gradients with a mean absolute error of 0.09 ppm. Results suggest that sensor placement within 8 cm of the fruit surface, combined with a lightweight shroud to reduce local airflow, maximises ethylene signal-to-background ratio. Practical design constraints for shroud geometry on picking end-effectors are discussed. Data are made available as a supplementary dataset.

title: Towards standardised in-situ gas sensing protocols for tree fruit ripeness assessment: a review of methods and reporting practices
abstract: Gas-phase sensing of ethylene and volatile organic compounds as ripeness indicators for tree fruits has attracted considerable research attention over the past decade, yet reported results are rarely comparable across studies due to inconsistent measurement conditions, sensor types, calibration methods, and reporting conventions. This book chapter surveys 54 peer-reviewed studies published between 2013 and 2025 that describe in-situ or near-in-situ gas sensing for ripeness staging of stone fruits, pome fruits, and soft fruits on the tree or vine. The chapter identifies six major sources of inter-study incomparability: sampling geometry, humidity and temperature normalisation, calibration gas standards, ground-truth maturity metrics, data reporting granularity, and sensor lifespan documentation. For each source, current practices are tabulated and a minimum reporting checklist is proposed. The chapter also summarises evidence on which VOC species have been successfully used as ripeness markers across multiple independent research groups, finding ethylene, hexyl acetate, and (E)-2-hexenal as the most consistently replicated. The proposed checklist is intended as a starting point for community discussion toward a shared measurement standard.

title: Spectral separability of informal versus formal built-up structures in WorldView-2 eight-band imagery
abstract: Using a 2012 WorldView-2 scene (eight multispectral bands, 2 m) acquired over the north-western fringe of Belgrade, this study evaluated the spectral separability of informal and formal built-up classes using Jeffries–Matusita and transformed divergence metrics. Seventy-two reference sites per class were delineated by cross-referencing aerial orthophotos and urban cadastral data. Results showed that coastal blue (band 1) and red-edge (band 6) bands contributed most to class separation, with JM distances exceeding 1.8 for the informal versus formal pair. A support vector machine classifier using all eight bands achieved 91.1 % overall accuracy on a 30 % hold-out set. A baseline classifier using only the four standard bands (blue, green, red, NIR) dropped to 84.6 %, demonstrating the marginal but consistent benefit of the additional WorldView-2 bands for this application. Confusion between informal housing and low-density formal villa zones remained the principal error source.

title: Mapping rooftop material types in informal settlements as a proxy for construction quality: evidence from Pléiades imagery
abstract: Rooftop material was used as a proxy for dwelling construction quality and settlement age in informal zones on the periphery of Novi Sad and Pančevo, exploiting a 2015 Pléiades tri-stereo acquisition at 0.5 m pan-sharpened resolution. A supervised classification using a maximum likelihood approach identified five rooftop material classes—fibre cement, metal sheet, clay tile, asphalt felt, and concrete flat slab—with training samples collected via field survey in June 2015 (n = 412 roofs). Overall accuracy reached 79.4 %; confusion was highest between asphalt felt and metal sheet under variable illumination conditions. Spatial patterns indicated that older informal clusters (visible in 2003 imagery) had a higher proportion of clay tile and concrete flat-slab roofs compared with more recent encroachments, which predominantly showed metal sheet and asphalt felt. The approach is discussed as a low-cost complement to household survey data in settlements where cadastral records are incomplete.

title: Detecting incremental dwelling extensions in peri-urban areas through bitemporal Pléiades differencing
abstract: Incremental self-extension of existing dwellings is a less studied dimension of informal settlement growth than new construction. This paper presents a methodology for detecting floor-area additions to existing buildings using two Pléiades acquisitions over a 490 ha study area near Futog, Serbia, separated by 27 months (2014 and 2017). After orthorectification and co-registration, a normalised difference built-up index was computed per epoch and differenced at pixel level; the result was filtered with a 3×3 median kernel and thresholded to isolate candidate change patches. Of 1,840 residential parcels intersected, 214 (11.6 %) showed area additions of at least 12 m². Field verification of a stratified random sample (n = 80) confirmed additions in 71 cases (89 % detection rate) and returned 9 false positives, mostly attributable to temporary structure placement or vehicle shadows. The paper argues that this simple workflow is reproducible in data-scarce contexts where only two VHR acquisitions are available.

title: Annual change maps of informal construction using a Sentinel-2 and WorldView-3 data fusion approach, Novi Sad 2016–2021
abstract: Annual layers of new informal construction were generated for a 210 km² peri-urban study area around Novi Sad by fusing Sentinel-2 10 m time series with opportunistically acquired WorldView-3 30 cm pan-sharpened scenes. A two-stage workflow was employed: Sentinel-2 time-series harmonic modelling first flagged pixels with anomalous temporal trajectories; flagged pixels were then verified and delineated using the nearest available WorldView-3 acquisition. Over the six-year period, 512 ha of new built-up area was mapped with a per-year commission error of 4–9 % and omission error of 6–11 %, depending on acquisition density. Growth was fastest in 2018–2019, coinciding with a period of reduced municipal enforcement activity. The fusion strategy reduced required VHR acquisitions by approximately 70 % compared with a purely VHR-based annual monitoring approach, lowering data procurement costs substantially while maintaining mapping detail adequate for parcel-level analysis.

title: Uncertainty propagation in multi-date informal settlement classifications: a Monte Carlo approach
abstract: Change detection analyses that subtract two classification maps inherit errors from both epochs, but uncertainty propagation is rarely reported in the peri-urban remote sensing literature. This paper quantifies how input classification uncertainty propagates to change area estimates using a Monte Carlo simulation framework applied to three pairs of Pléiades classifications covering informal zones in Inđija, Ruma and Stara Pazova, Serbia. For each classification, per-class confusion matrices were used to parameterise Dirichlet distributions from which 1,000 realisations of alternative label assignments were drawn; the resulting distribution of change area estimates was summarised by 90 % credible intervals. Intervals for the informal class widened by a factor of 1.4–2.3 relative to the point estimate of changed area, depending on baseline classification accuracy. The analysis demonstrates that even modestly improving the producer accuracy of the informal class from 82 % to 88 % reduces uncertainty in the change area estimate by approximately 30 %. The Monte Carlo outputs are argued to be useful as inputs to municipal planning risk assessments.

title: Does regularisation of informal settlements reduce measurable physical change? Satellite evidence from three Serbian municipalities
abstract: Serbian legislation enacted in 2015 allowed owners of informally constructed dwellings to seek retroactive legalisation. This study tests whether legalisation, by formalising existing structures, measurably altered the pace of new construction or extension activity in three municipalities—Inđija, Sremska Mitrovica and Bačka Palanka—using annual VHR change maps derived from Pléiades and Spot-7 imagery for 2013–2020. A difference-in-differences design compared construction activity in parcels whose owners filed for legalisation (treatment group, n = 2,340 parcels) against parcels in the same zones whose owners did not (control group, n = 3,815 parcels). No statistically significant reduction in extension activity was detected in the treatment group post-2015, but a modest reduction in new ancillary structure construction (sheds, garages) was observed in 2017–2018. The results are interpreted in the context of continued uncertainty about legalisation outcome and the time lag between application and decision.

title: Near-real-time informal construction alerts using a lightweight change detection model and commercial satellite tasking
abstract: This paper describes a monitoring pipeline that pairs commercial satellite tasking for recurring Pléiades Neo acquisitions with a lightweight binary change detection model deployed on a cloud processing environment to generate informal construction alerts within 72 hours of image delivery. The model, a shallow encoder–decoder with 1.2 million parameters, was trained on a 5-year archive of Pléiades change pairs from Vojvodina and fine-tuned monthly on newly confirmed detections. Over a 10-month pilot (June 2024–March 2025) covering 55 km² of monitored peri-urban fringe in Novi Sad municipality, 74 alerts were issued; manual review confirmed 63 as genuine new construction events (85 % precision). Median time from ground event onset to alert issuance was estimated at 19 days, constrained primarily by revisit interval rather than processing latency. Alert data were delivered to municipal planning staff via a web map service. The paper discusses cost structure and the minimum monitoring area that makes commercial tasking economically viable relative to archive-based retrospective analysis.

title: Mapping gallery forest extent along the lower Tisa using Landsat ETM+ seasonal composites
abstract: Gallery forests along lowland rivers in the Pannonian Plain represent fragmented but ecologically significant habitats that are difficult to delineate with single-date imagery due to spectral confusion with adjacent agricultural land. This study used six Landsat ETM+ cloud-free scenes distributed across the growing season of 2009–2010 to construct a seasonal composite stack for a 120 km reach of the lower Tisa River in Serbia. A supervised maximum-likelihood classifier was trained on 340 field-verified reference polygons representing six land-cover classes including willow-dominated softwood forest, poplar plantation, reed beds, wet grassland, arable land, and open water. Overall classification accuracy was 81.4% with a kappa coefficient of 0.77. The resulting map showed gallery forest covering 4,820 ha along the study reach, with 38% assessed as structurally degraded based on canopy density indices derived from the red-edge and NIR bands. Results were compared against topographic map polygons from 1985, indicating a net loss of 610 ha of natural gallery forest over the 25-year period. The methodology is transferable to other reaches with similar data availability.
venue: Journal of Applied Remote Sensing in Central Europe

title: Four-bar linkage synthesis for a single-tendon underactuated finger: a dimensional analysis approach
abstract: This paper addresses the dimensional synthesis of a four-bar linkage intended as the proximal phalanx drive of a single-tendon underactuated prosthetic finger. Starting from a set of 47 measured cadaveric finger posture pairs from the literature, the authors formulate a least-squares Chebyshev approximation problem over three precision points per grasp type. Eleven candidate topologies are evaluated by comparing the transmission angle variation across the workspace. The selected topology achieves a minimum transmission angle of 38° throughout the full flexion arc of 85°. Physical prototypes were fabricated from polyamide and tested on a custom tendon-force bench; mean tendon force at full flexion was 14.3 N, within 6% of the analytical prediction. The study demonstrates that a simple planar four-bar drive can satisfy both kinematic and force-transmission constraints without requiring active joint control, providing a basis for low-cost myoelectric and body-powered finger modules.

title: Comparison of three underactuation schemes for prosthetic finger prehension: simulation and bench testing
abstract: Three mechanical underactuation schemes—differential pulley, proximal-phalanx spring return, and floating joint—are compared for their ability to conform to cylindrical, spherical, and lateral pinch grasps. A planar dynamic simulation model with contact stiffness of 0.8 N/mm was constructed in MSC Adams for each scheme. Contact force distributions were recorded at five object diameters ranging from 20 mm to 80 mm. The differential pulley scheme produced the most uniform contact distribution (coefficient of variation below 12%) across all object sizes but required 23% higher peak tendon force than the spring-return scheme. Bench tests using 3D-printed ABS prototypes confirmed the simulation rankings with mean force errors below 9%. The floating-joint scheme showed the lowest force requirements but failed to maintain stable grasp on objects smaller than 30 mm diameter. Results provide designers with a quantitative basis for scheme selection based on anticipated use-case profiles.

title: Pseudo-rigid-body modelling of monolithic flexure hinges for prosthetic finger joints printed in PLA
abstract: Compliant hinges produced by fused deposition modelling (FDM) in polylactic acid (PLA) exhibit non-linear stiffness behaviour that deviates from the standard pseudo-rigid-body (PRB) model due to anisotropic layer bonding. This work develops a modified PRB model in which the torsional spring constant is a quadratic function of deflection angle, identified from 120 load-deflection measurements on rectangular cross-section flexures with widths of 0.8, 1.2, and 1.6 mm and three infill orientations. The modified model reduces the root-mean-square prediction error from 18.4% (standard PRB) to 4.7% across the 0°–60° deflection range. Fatigue behaviour was assessed over 10 000 cycles at 45° deflection; stiffness degradation was below 8% for the 1.2 mm width and 0° infill orientation. The results are incorporated into a finger design spreadsheet tool distributed as supplementary material.

title: Optimisation of a three-phalanx compliant finger for whole-hand prostheses using a genetic algorithm
abstract: A three-phalanx monolithic compliant finger for a whole-hand prosthetic device is optimised using a real-coded genetic algorithm. The design variables are the widths, lengths, and out-of-plane depths of three serial flexure segments, totalling nine variables. Two objective functions are minimised simultaneously: the difference between the synthesised path and a target grasping trajectory derived from motion-capture data collected from eight non-disabled participants performing 12 grasp types, and the peak von Mises stress normalised by the PLA tensile yield strength. The Pareto front contains 31 non-dominated solutions; a selected design achieves a trajectory error of 3.1 mm RMS and a peak stress ratio of 0.61. Printed prototypes were attached to a wrist-mounted actuator block and grasped eleven everyday objects; successful grasp was achieved in 9 of 11 trials without slip. The approach reduces design iteration time compared to manual parameter studies.

title: Grasp stability margin for passively adaptive underactuated fingers: a wrench-space formulation
abstract: Passive grasp adaptation in underactuated fingers relies on spring preload and linkage geometry to maintain contact forces without sensor feedback. This paper proposes a wrench-space stability margin that quantifies the ability of a two-contact underactuated finger to resist disturbance wrenches applied at the fingertip. The margin is defined as the radius of the largest ball inscribed in the friction cone polytope formed by the two contact wrenches, computed using linear programming. The formulation is applied to a parametric family of four-bar finger designs varying in proximal-link length from 30 mm to 60 mm in 5 mm steps and spring preload from 0.2 N to 1.0 N. Results show that proximal-link length has a stronger effect on margin than spring preload for cylindrical grasps, while the reverse holds for pinch grasps. Experimental validation on a tendon-actuated testbed with a six-axis force sensor confirms the analytical ranking in 18 of 22 tested configurations.

title: Dimensional synthesis of a thumb opposition mechanism for a body-powered partial-hand prosthesis
abstract: Partial-hand amputees retaining the palm but lacking all five digits represent a clinically under-served group for whom commercially available prostheses are largely unavailable. This paper presents the kinematic synthesis of a two-degree-of-freedom thumb opposition mechanism driven by a single Bowden cable. The mechanism consists of a slider-crank converting cable displacement into palmar abduction, combined with a cam-follower producing coupled flexion of the first metacarpophalangeal joint. Thirty-five two-point precision conditions derived from clinical grasp taxonomy data were used to determine cam profile geometry. A printed prototype was evaluated on a one-week home trial by two partial-hand prosthesis users; participants reported improved pinch grasp performance on a standardised peg-transfer task, with completion time reduced by 34% and 29% respectively relative to their existing passive cosmetic devices. The design is fabricated in four components with a total mass of 48 g.

title: Stiffness tuning of FDM-printed flexure joints through infill pattern and layer orientation: application to prosthetic finger design
abstract: The stiffness of fused deposition modelled flexure joints can be adjusted without changing external geometry by varying the internal infill pattern and print orientation. This study tests five infill patterns (rectilinear, gyroid, honeycomb, grid, concentric) at three orientations (0°, 45°, 90° relative to the bending axis) and three infill densities (20%, 40%, 60%) on rectangular PETG specimens. Stiffness is measured by three-point bending at deflections up to 50°; 45 specimen groups of five are tested, yielding 225 specimens in total. Gyroid infill at 40% density and 45° orientation provides the most linear stiffness response (R² = 0.994 over the full deflection range) and the widest tunable stiffness range (0.9–6.2 N·mm/°) when density is varied. A design chart is produced that allows a finger designer to specify required joint stiffness and select the corresponding parameter combination. The chart is validated in a three-finger gripper prototype.

title: Compliant mechanisms in upper-limb prosthetics: a structured review of design methods and clinical outcomes, 2000–2022
abstract: This chapter surveys 118 publications from 2000 to 2022 addressing compliant mechanism design for upper-limb prosthetic components. The review is structured around four design method families: analytical beam-theory models, pseudo-rigid-body models, topology optimisation, and data-driven surrogate models. For each family the chapter describes the assumed loading conditions, material models, and fabrication constraints typically employed, and tabulates reported accuracy metrics and prototype test outcomes. Clinical outcome data are available for only 23 of the 118 studies; reported outcome measures are heterogeneous, with grip strength, range of motion, and task completion time being most common. Key gaps identified include the absence of long-term fatigue data for polymer compliant joints under realistic duty cycles, and a scarcity of studies addressing hygiene and cleaning requirements. The chapter provides a classification framework and a gap map intended to guide future research priorities in the field.

title: Simultaneous path and force synthesis for a two-phalanx underactuated finger using interval analysis
abstract: Kinematic synthesis problems for underactuated fingers are typically solved by separating path and force requirements, which can lead to designs that satisfy geometry but violate tendon force limits in part of the workspace. This paper formulates a unified synthesis problem in which both the fingertip path error and the tendon force envelope are treated as constraints, solved simultaneously using interval arithmetic. The design space covers six geometric parameters of a two-phalanx slider-crank mechanism. The interval solver is initialised with 5000 random boxes and refined using bisection with a width tolerance of 0.01 mm. Of 5000 initial boxes, 312 survive both constraints; the verified solution set is clustered into four families by k-means. Representatives from each family were 3D-printed and evaluated on a tendon force bench; all four achieved fingertip path errors below 2.8 mm RMS and remained within the 4–18 N tendon force band across the full 80° flexion arc. The interval approach guarantees no constraint violation within the certified solution boxes.

title: Towards modular low-cost finger modules for multi-grasp prosthetic hands: parametric design and assembly tolerance analysis
abstract: Low-cost prosthetic hands assembled from individually printable finger modules require that grasp performance be robust to the dimensional tolerances achievable on desktop FDM printers. This paper presents a parametric finger module design in which joint pivot diameters, link lengths, and flexure widths are expressed as tolerance intervals corresponding to ±0.3 mm positional accuracy and ±0.1 mm width accuracy, consistent with a mid-range FDM printer. Monte Carlo simulation with 50 000 samples propagates these tolerances through the kinematic model to yield distributions of fingertip path deviation and maximum contact force. The 90th-percentile fingertip path deviation is 4.1 mm, acceptable for power grasps but marginal for precision pinch. A design modification reducing the proximal link length by 4 mm lowers the 90th-percentile deviation to 2.6 mm with no increase in tendon force. Twenty assembled modules from a single batch of prints on three different printers are tested; measured path deviations are within the predicted 90th-percentile bounds in 18 of 20 cases.

title: Wrench-feasibility workspace computation for reconfigurable cable robots using interval arithmetic
abstract: Determining the wrench-feasible workspace (WFW) of a cable-driven parallel robot depends on anchor geometry, cable count, and tension bounds, all of which change when the robot is reconfigured for a new task. This work applies interval arithmetic to evaluate wrench feasibility at discrete pose samples over a 4 m × 4 m × 3 m operating volume. A bitset representation allows the WFW to be stored as a voxelised Boolean grid at 50 mm resolution, enabling fast Boolean intersection queries during motion planning. The method is validated against convex-polytope enumeration for three anchor configurations and three payloads, showing agreement within one voxel boundary for all cases. Computation time for a full workspace scan is reduced from 47 minutes with polytope enumeration to under 90 seconds on a standard workstation. The paper includes sensitivity analysis showing how anchor position uncertainty of ±5 mm affects WFW volume by up to 8%.

title: Comparison of Defuzzification Methods for Trapezoidal Type-2 Fuzzy Numbers in Decision Aggregation
abstract: Defuzzification of interval type-2 fuzzy sets involves a two-step reduction process whose outcome can vary substantially depending on the chosen method. This paper provides a systematic numerical comparison of four widely referenced defuzzification strategies—Karnik–Mendel iterative procedure, Wu–Mendel approximation, the enhanced centroid method, and a geometric centroid variant—applied to 48 trapezoidal type-2 fuzzy numbers drawn from published supplier evaluation datasets. For each fuzzy number, all four methods were computed and the resulting crisp values were compared in terms of absolute deviation, rank preservation, and computational time measured on a standard workstation. The Karnik–Mendel and Wu–Mendel approaches differed by less than 2.1% on average across the dataset, while the geometric centroid variant showed deviations exceeding 8% in 11 cases with highly asymmetric footprint-of-uncertainty regions. Rank reversals occurred in 6 out of 48 cases when switching between the geometric centroid and the Karnik–Mendel procedure, which has practical implications for decision support applications where rank stability is required. Recommendations for method selection based on footprint-of-uncertainty shape are provided.

title: A Type-2 Fuzzy AHP Model for Evaluating Software Quality Attributes in Enterprise Resource Planning Systems
abstract: Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems are evaluated along multiple qualitative dimensions whose relative importance is often expressed imprecisely by stakeholders. This study develops a pairwise comparison framework based on interval type-2 fuzzy AHP to assess six software quality attributes—functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability, and portability—as defined in ISO 25010. Judgements were elicited from 14 IT professionals at five mid-sized manufacturing companies in the Pannonian region. The consistency of each expert's interval type-2 fuzzy pairwise comparison matrix was verified using an adapted consistency ratio threshold of 0.10, and matrices failing this threshold were revised through a structured revision protocol until consistency was achieved. Priority weights derived from the type-2 fuzzy AHP were compared to weights obtained from a standard crisp AHP applied to the same data after defuzzification at the elicitation stage. Reliability and functionality received the highest aggregated weights (0.231 and 0.198 respectively). The type-2 model allocated noticeably more weight to maintainability than the crisp counterpart, attributed to higher expert disagreement on that criterion. Practical implications for ERP procurement decisions are discussed.
