title: Learned Sparse Retrieval for Low-Resource South Slavic Languages
abstract: Learned sparse retrieval models such as SPLADE expand query and document terms using transformer-derived weights, producing sparse vectors that are indexed in a standard inverted index. Their effectiveness on languages other than English is less studied. We fine-tune a multilingual base transformer on Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian document–query pairs assembled from publicly available court decisions and parliamentary records, producing a total of 280,000 training triples. The resulting model is evaluated on three held-out test sets. MRR@10 improves by 6.1, 4.8, and 5.3 points over BM25 on the Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian sets respectively. Index size is 2.1× that of BM25, and query latency at the 95th percentile is 38 ms on a CPU-only server. We also report the effect of training set size, showing useful gains above approximately 40,000 triples.

title: Tiered Vector Storage: Exploiting NVMe and DRAM Hierarchies for ANN Index Serving
abstract: Dense vector indexes for ANN search are memory-intensive; billion-scale deployments frequently exceed available DRAM. We design a tiered storage manager that partitions HNSW graph layers across DRAM and NVMe, keeping upper graph layers and frequently accessed vectors in DRAM while spilling lower layers to NVMe. Access patterns are tracked with a lightweight frequency counter and a decay factor that deprioritises temporally stale vectors. On a 1.5-billion-vector index (768 dimensions, float16) requiring 2.2 TB uncompressed, the tiered system achieves 89.1% recall@10 using 128 GB DRAM plus 2 TB NVMe, compared to 94.3% recall with full DRAM loading. Query throughput at this recall level is 1,340 queries per second, a 4.2× improvement over a pure NVMe baseline. The implementation builds on an open-source ANN library with a custom I/O scheduler.

title: Distributed Stream Processing: Architectures, Algorithms, and Deployment
abstract: This book chapter surveys the architectural space of distributed stream processing systems, covering foundational data models (data streams, continuous queries, operator graphs), core algorithmic challenges (join algorithms, windowing, state management, fault tolerance), and deployment considerations on both on-premises clusters and cloud-native infrastructure. The chapter is structured in three parts. The first part establishes formal definitions and a taxonomy of processing guarantees (at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once). The second part surveys algorithms for the main operator classes—filters, aggregations, joins, and enrichments—with emphasis on complexity trade-offs under varying data distributions. The third part addresses operational concerns: resource allocation, monitoring, schema management, and integration with batch systems. Representative open-source and commercial systems are discussed as illustrative examples without prescriptive endorsement. Annotated references guide readers toward primary literature for each subtopic. The chapter is intended for graduate students and practitioners with prior exposure to database systems and parallel computing.

title: Screening of white-rot fungi from Fruška Gora for laccase activity on guaiacol and syringaldazine substrates
abstract: Fourteen fungal isolates collected from beech and oak deadwood in the Fruška Gora nature reserve were screened for extracellular laccase activity using guaiacol and syringaldazine as colorimetric substrates. Isolates were cultivated in submerged liquid culture on malt extract medium supplemented with 0.5 mM CuSO4 as an inducer. Activity was measured spectrophotometrically at 470 nm and 525 nm, respectively, over a 12-day growth curve. Three isolates showed specific activities exceeding 180 U/L on syringaldazine at day eight. One isolate, tentatively assigned to the genus Trametes based on ITS sequencing, produced the highest titre of 310 U/L. Temperature optima ranged from 45 to 60 °C and pH optima from 4.5 to 5.5 across the active isolates. These strains were retained as candidates for subsequent gene cloning and heterologous expression work. The study provides a baseline activity dataset for laccase producers indigenous to the Pannonian forest ecosystem of northern Serbia.

title: Optimisation of methanol induction conditions for heterologous laccase production in Pichia pastoris X-33
abstract: The lcc1 gene under the control of the AOX1 promoter was expressed in Pichia pastoris X-33 using episomal and integrative configurations. A central composite design with five factors—methanol concentration (0.5–2%), induction temperature (20–30 °C), pH (5.0–7.0), CuSO4 supplementation (0.1–1.0 mM), and induction duration (48–120 h)—was used to maximise volumetric laccase activity. Response surface analysis identified 1% methanol, 22 °C, pH 5.5, 0.5 mM CuSO4, and 96 h as optimal conditions, yielding a volumetric activity of 1,840 U/L in shake-flask culture. This represented a 5.8-fold improvement over the unoptimised baseline. SDS-PAGE and zymographic analysis confirmed secretion of an active protein of approximately 66 kDa. Activity was fully abrogated by 1 mM NaN3, consistent with laccase identity. The optimised conditions were subsequently used as the baseline for directed evolution campaigns targeting improved thermostability.

title: Directed evolution of a fungal laccase for improved activity at alkaline pH using error-prone PCR and high-throughput colorimetric screening
abstract: Wild-type Lcc1 shows a sharp activity optimum at pH 4.5–5.0 with less than 15% residual activity at pH 7.5, limiting its utility in lignin oxidation processes coupled to alkaline pre-treatment steps. Three rounds of error-prone PCR mutagenesis followed by screening of approximately 2,400 colonies per round on ABTS-containing agar plates at pH 7.0 identified six variants with improved alkaline activity. The most active variant, carrying substitutions G208D and T423S, retained 68% of its maximum activity at pH 7.5 compared with 12% for the parent enzyme. Kinetic characterisation on ABTS showed a fourfold reduction in Km (from 480 µM to 118 µM) and a threefold increase in kcat at pH 7.0. Thermostability was marginally reduced, with T50 decreasing by 4 °C to 58 °C. The G208D substitution is located at the entrance to the substrate-binding pocket, suggesting electrostatic modulation of substrate approach at higher pH. This work provides a platform variant for further engineering.

title: Laccase-mediator oxidation of kraft and organosolv lignins derived from sunflower husk: product characterisation by GPC and 2D-NMR
abstract: Sunflower husks, a major agro-industrial by-product in Vojvodina, were subjected to kraft and ethanol-organosolv fractionation to isolate technical lignins with weight-average molecular masses of 8,400 and 3,200 Da, respectively. Both lignins were treated with the G208D/T423S Lcc1 variant (100 U/g lignin) in the presence of three redox mediators—ABTS, violuric acid, and 1-hydroxybenzotriazole—at pH 6.5 and 50 °C for 24 h. Gel permeation chromatography indicated depolymerisation of organosolv lignin by 28% (reduction in Mw from 3,200 to 2,300 Da) under ABTS mediation, whereas kraft lignin showed preferential repolymerisation. 2D HSQC NMR confirmed cleavage of β-O-4 linkages and an increase in phenolic hydroxyl content from 0.9 to 1.6 mmol/g in the organosolv fraction. No depolymerisation was observed with the wild-type enzyme under equivalent conditions at pH 6.5. The results suggest that alkaline-shifted variants are particularly suited to processing of readily soluble low-Mw organosolv lignins.

title: Semi-rational mutagenesis of substrate-binding residues in Lcc1 to broaden activity toward phenolic aldehydes relevant to lignin depolymerisation products
abstract: Lignin depolymerisation generates a mixture of phenolic monomers including vanillin, syringaldehyde, and p-hydroxybenzaldehyde. The capacity of laccases to oxidise and thereby detoxify or functionalise these aldehydes is relevant to downstream biorefinery steps. Using a homology model of Lcc1 built on the Trametes trogii laccase crystal structure (PDB 2HRG), residues within 5 Å of the docked aldehyde substrates were identified by computational docking with AutoDock Vina. Fourteen single-point variants at five positions (A163, D265, F332, I411, V458) were constructed by site-directed mutagenesis, expressed in Pichia pastoris, and assayed against a panel of eight phenolic aldehydes. Variant F332L showed a 2.3-fold increase in kcat/Km for syringaldehyde (rising from 12 to 28 mM⁻¹s⁻¹) with negligible change for ABTS. The double variant G208D/F332L combined alkaline-pH tolerance with enhanced aldehyde activity and is considered the most useful engineering product to date. Circular dichroism confirmed no gross secondary structure perturbation in the double variant.

title: Immobilisation of engineered Lcc1 variants on lignin-derived carbon particles for repeated-batch oxidation of wheat straw hydrolysate
abstract: Carbon microparticles derived from hydrothermal carbonisation of wheat straw lignin fraction were surface-functionalised with (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane and used as a support for covalent immobilisation of the G208D/F332L Lcc1 double variant via glutaraldehyde crosslinking. Immobilisation yield was 78% with retained activity of 61% relative to the soluble enzyme at equivalent loading. The immobilised preparation was used in ten consecutive 6-hour oxidation cycles on a dilute wheat straw enzymatic hydrolysate containing 320 mg/L residual aromatic compounds. Removal of total phenolics, monitored by Folin–Ciocalteu assay, averaged 74% per cycle in cycles 1–5 and declined to 48% by cycle 10, with activity loss attributed primarily to product inhibition rather than protein leaching as confirmed by Bradford assay of the spent reaction liquor. Reusability represents a practical advantage over soluble enzyme preparations at the intended process scale of 50–500 L. Storage stability at 4 °C over 30 days showed less than 15% activity loss.

title: Techno-economic considerations for integrating laccase-mediator delignification into an agro-industrial residue biorefinery at pilot scale: a process design perspective
abstract: A conceptual process design was developed for a 500 kg/day dry-matter biorefinery processing sunflower husks and corn stover in a 60:40 mass ratio. The process incorporates aqueous pre-treatment, organosolv fractionation, laccase-mediator delignification using immobilised G208D/F332L Lcc1, enzymatic saccharification, and fermentation to lactic acid as the primary product with functionalised lignin oligomers as a co-product stream. Mass and energy balances were estimated using Aspen Plus simulation with kinetic parameters drawn from laboratory data. The laccase step accounted for approximately 18% of total operating cost at an assumed enzyme price of 8 EUR/kU. Sensitivity analysis showed that reducing the mediator loading from 5 mM to 1 mM ABTS—feasible with the engineered enzyme variant—decreased overall operating cost by 6%. The co-product lignin stream, valued conservatively at 0.4 EUR/kg, improved the net present value of the plant by approximately 12% over a 15-year horizon. Key uncertainties are enzyme production cost at scale and market price of functionalised lignin.
venue: Bioresource Chemistry and Processing

title: Genomic drift in Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 during sequential subculturing: a comparison of plating-based and whole-genome sequencing approaches
abstract: Repeated subculturing of Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 over 50 transfers was monitored by colony morphology scoring, sporulation frequency counting, and Illumina short-read whole-genome sequencing at transfers 10, 25, and 50. Sporulation frequency declined from 91% at transfer 1 to 67% at transfer 50. Sequencing identified seven single-nucleotide variants accumulating progressively, five mapping within the spo0A regulatory network. Plating-based morphology scoring correlated poorly with variant accumulation until transfer 35, suggesting that phenotypic methods underestimate early genomic instability. Glycerol cryostocks prepared at transfer 5 fully recovered wild-type sporulation and variant profiles after revival, supporting early banking as the primary mitigation strategy. The study provides quantitative thresholds for acceptable transfer number in inoculum propagation protocols used in industrial enzyme production.

title: Influence of build orientation on support volume and surface roughness in LPBF-produced Ti-6Al-4V brackets
abstract: Fourteen orientations, sampled uniformly over the upper hemisphere, were evaluated for a topology-optimised titanium bracket produced by laser powder-bed fusion. For each orientation, support volume was calculated analytically using a 45-degree overhang threshold, and surface roughness Ra on functional contact faces was predicted with a regression model trained on 96 coupon measurements taken from a prior design-of-experiments campaign. The bracket had a final mass of 38 g and contained three M6 boss features. Minimum support volume (7.4 cm³) was achieved at an orientation 22 degrees from vertical, while minimum Ra on the primary mating face (3.1 µm) required a 67-degree tilt, increasing support volume to 19.1 cm³. A Pareto front with six non-dominated solutions was identified. The study suggests that functional surface requirements and support minimisation are frequently conflicting objectives and that designer intent must explicitly weight each criterion before build preparation.

title: Fatigue life of topology-optimised AlSi10Mg brackets in the as-built and shot-peened conditions
abstract: Ten topology-optimised brackets were produced from AlSi10Mg powder on an LPBF platform at standard process parameters (laser power 370 W, scan speed 1300 mm/s, layer thickness 30 µm) and tested under four-point bending at a load ratio of R = 0.1. Five specimens were tested in the as-built condition and five after shot peening to a coverage of 100 % with S110 steel shot. Fatigue life at a peak stress of 120 MPa increased from a median of 41 000 cycles in the as-built condition to 118 000 cycles after shot peening, primarily attributable to compressive residual stresses of −85 MPa measured at 0.1 mm depth by X-ray diffraction. Fractographic analysis showed crack initiation at surface pores in as-built specimens and at sub-surface pores after peening, with defect diameters in the range 40–90 µm. The findings suggest that topology-optimised geometries retain the same fatigue-improvement response to shot peening as simple coupon geometries.

title: A geometry-based heuristic for simultaneous build orientation selection and support minimisation in metal additive manufacturing
abstract: A heuristic algorithm is presented that jointly determines build orientation and support scaffold layout for arbitrary polyhedral geometries intended for laser powder-bed fusion. The approach discretises the orientation space into 480 candidate directions using a geodesic sphere and, for each candidate, computes overhang area, projected footprint, and a thermal distortion proxy based on cross-sectional area gradients. A weighted scoring function aggregates these metrics. Applied to a set of twelve industrial bracket geometries with masses ranging from 18 g to 210 g, the heuristic reduced support volume by a mean of 31 % relative to a vertical default orientation and by 18 % relative to an experienced operator's manual selection, with a computation time under 40 seconds on a standard workstation. The algorithm does not require simulation and is intended for integration into early-stage design workflows before detailed process simulation is warranted.

title: Integration of minimum member size and overhang constraints into SIMP topology optimisation for direct LPBF fabrication
abstract: This paper incorporates two fabrication constraints—minimum member size and maximum overhang angle—directly into the SIMP optimisation loop rather than applying them as post-processing corrections. Minimum member size is enforced via a projection filter with threshold radius r_min set to 1.5 mm, consistent with the LPBF machine's resolved feature capability. The overhang constraint is implemented as a pseudo-load acting on density gradients that exceed a 45-degree threshold from the build direction, with a penalty weight calibrated by a bisection procedure over five test cases. A titanium bracket of 52 g with six load attachment points was optimised under both unconstrained and constrained formulations. The constrained result required 8.4 % more material but produced a geometry that was self-supporting except for the base plate connection and required no design revision before fabrication. Both geometries were built and mechanically tested; stiffness reduction of the constrained design was 6.2 % relative to the unconstrained topology.

title: Post-process milling allowance estimation for LPBF brackets with functional mating surfaces: a regression approach
abstract: Laser powder-bed fusion produces characteristic surface textures whose roughness depends on local surface inclination relative to the build direction. For load-bearing brackets with bolted mating surfaces, post-process milling is often required to meet flatness and roughness tolerances. This study develops a regression model to predict the minimum material removal depth required on any planar face as a function of inclination angle, part height above the build plate, and local cross-sectional area. Training data were collected from 144 faces on 18 AlSi10Mg bracket specimens measured by contact profilometry. The resulting model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.04 mm on a held-out validation set of 36 faces. The model was integrated into a build-preparation script so that milling stock is automatically added to designated functional faces before slicing. Application to five production brackets reduced total post-process milling time by an estimated 22 % by enabling thinner, location-specific allowances rather than uniform stock addition.

title: Thermal residual stress distributions in topology-optimised Ti-6Al-4V brackets: finite element simulation versus neutron diffraction measurement
abstract: Residual stresses arising from the LPBF process can cause distortion and premature fatigue failure in load-bearing brackets, but their distribution in topologically complex geometries is not well characterised. This study applies a sequentially coupled thermo-mechanical finite element model, using an inherent-strain approach calibrated on simple coupons, to predict residual stress fields in two topology-optimised titanium brackets. Predictions are compared with neutron diffraction measurements performed at a national neutron source facility at 31 interior measurement points per bracket. Mean absolute deviation between predicted and measured von Mises residual stress was 48 MPa at a mean measured level of 310 MPa. Elevated stresses concentrated at re-entrant features and thin-wall junctions identified by the topology optimisation. The calibrated simulation was then used to assess stress relief from two heat treatment schedules, providing guidance for selecting annealing parameters without additional experiments.

title: Topology optimisation of a multi-axis fixture bracket under combined static and dynamic loading: design, fabrication, and experimental validation
abstract: A fixture bracket used in a five-axis machining centre was redesigned using topology optimisation targeting simultaneous minimisation of static compliance and first natural frequency maximisation, formulated as a weighted multi-objective problem. The design domain was an irregular 180 × 140 × 95 mm envelope in AlSi10Mg. The optimised geometry reduced mass by 44 % relative to the reference cast aluminium bracket while raising the first natural frequency from 610 Hz to 740 Hz and maintaining static stiffness within 4 % of the original. Three brackets were produced by LPBF and mounted in the machining centre for cutting force response tests using a dynamometer at spindle speeds between 4000 and 12 000 rpm. Vibration amplitude at the tool tip was reduced by 18 % on average across the tested speed range. The case study demonstrates that a combined structural-dynamic objective is practically realisable within typical LPBF material and process constraints.

title: Design for additive manufacturing guidelines for metallic load-bearing brackets: a structured review of constraint formulations
abstract: This review systematically collects and categorises constraint formulations reported in the topology optimisation literature that address fabrication requirements specific to laser powder-bed fusion of metallic brackets. Eighty-three publications from 2010 to 2024 were screened; forty-one met inclusion criteria covering overhang angle, minimum feature size, enclosed void avoidance, and thermal gradient control. Each formulation is classified by implementation stage (optimisation loop, post-processing, or build preparation), mathematical form, and reported effect on structural performance relative to an unconstrained baseline. Overhang constraints were the most frequently implemented (29 studies), with a median structural compliance penalty of 7 %. Minimum feature size constraints were second (18 studies), with a median penalty of 5 %. Only four studies addressed enclosed void constraints, and thermal gradient constraints appeared in seven studies, mostly after 2021. Gaps identified include limited validation on full bracket geometries and near-absence of combined constraint studies on materials other than Ti-6Al-4V and AlSi10Mg.

title: Influence of locator position on elastic deformation in milled thin-walled aluminium frames: an FE parametric study
abstract: Thin-walled aluminium frames used in aerospace and automotive sub-assemblies are susceptible to elastic deformation under clamping and cutting loads. This paper presents a parametric finite-element study in which six locator layout configurations were evaluated for a 320 × 180 × 12 mm prismatic aluminium frame with nominal wall thickness of 2.5 mm. Models were built in Abaqus 6.9 using 8-node linear brick elements, with mesh refinement at boss contact regions. Cutting forces were derived from Kienzle's specific cutting force model calibrated by slot-milling trials on an instrumented Hermle C 400 machining centre. Results showed that displacement of the primary locator cluster by 18 mm from the geometric centroid increased peak nodal displacement by up to 34 μm and raised positional error at the reference bore from 12 μm to 41 μm. A regression surface relating locator spacing to peak deformation was fitted with R² = 0.91, providing a design guideline for process planners. Experimental validation on three physical workpieces confirmed model predictions within 15%.

title: Lumbar Compressive Forces During Repetitive Box Lifting in a Simulated Automotive Parts Assembly Task
abstract: This study quantified lumbar compressive and shear forces in twelve male assembly workers performing a standardised box-lifting protocol simulating conditions observed on a passenger vehicle door-panel sub-assembly line. Participants lifted 8 kg and 14 kg loads from floor level to a conveyor height of 950 mm at a rate of six lifts per minute. A linked-segment biomechanical model was applied to kinematic data captured using an electrogoniometric suit, combined with simultaneous surface EMG recordings from the erector spinae and rectus abdominis. Peak L5/S1 compressive force exceeded the NIOSH action limit of 3400 N in 9 of 12 subjects when lifting the 14 kg load with a pronounced forward trunk lean. Shear forces at L5/S1 averaged 680 N under the same condition. Redesigning the origin height of the lift to 430 mm and introducing a tilt table reduced peak compression by 22 percent. The results provide specific force benchmarks for use in production planning decisions at automotive assembly facilities.

title: Postural Loading Assessment Using OWAS and RULA in a Transmission Component Sub-Assembly Cell
abstract: A comparative field study applied both the Ovako Working Posture Analysis System (OWAS) and the Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) method to seven workstations within a transmission component sub-assembly cell at an automotive supplier in Vojvodina. Continuous video observation over four-hour periods yielded 1,840 posture snapshots per worker across a two-week measurement campaign. OWAS classified 38 percent of observed postures in action category 3 or 4, indicating that corrective measures were required urgently at three of the seven stations. RULA grand scores of 6 or 7 were recorded at two stations involving overhead fastener tightening. Discrepancies between the two methods were most pronounced for asymmetric trunk postures combined with upper-limb loading, where RULA consistently indicated higher urgency. Station-specific redesign proposals—including height-adjustable benches and pneumatic torque tool balancers—were evaluated and estimated to reduce high-risk posture time by 44 percent. Observation reliability was tested with two trained raters giving Cohen's kappa of 0.81.

title: Shoulder Muscle Fatigue During Sustained Overhead Work in Automotive Underbody Assembly: An EMG-Based Analysis
abstract: Shoulder muscle fatigue was investigated in ten male workers performing sustained overhead fastener installation tasks representative of underbody vehicle assembly. Surface EMG signals were recorded bilaterally from the anterior deltoid, upper trapezius, and infraspinatus over continuous work cycles of 90 seconds at three simulated overhead heights (1900, 2050, and 2200 mm above floor). Median frequency shifts in the power spectrum of the upper trapezius signal indicated the onset of localised muscle fatigue within 45 seconds at the 2200 mm condition. Normalised root mean square amplitude for the anterior deltoid increased by 31 percent from the first to the tenth consecutive cycle. A perceived effort rating using the Borg CR-10 scale correlated strongly with EMG-derived fatigue indices (r = 0.87). The study provides time-to-fatigue estimates that can inform job rotation scheduling and overhead reach height limits in production layout planning. Recommendations include limiting continuous overhead work to cycles below 40 seconds and introducing mechanical lift aids for tasks above 2000 mm.

title: A Task-Based Exposure Index for Manual Materials Handling Risk in Small-Batch Automotive Sub-Assembly: Development and Pilot Validation
abstract: This paper describes the construction and pilot validation of a composite task-based exposure index (TBEI) intended for rapid risk screening of manual materials handling in small-batch automotive sub-assembly environments. The index combines four parameters—load weight, handling frequency, trunk inclination angle, and horizontal distance at origin—into a single dimensionless score weighted by regression coefficients derived from an earlier dataset of 96 biomechanical measurements collected in the authors' laboratory. TBEI scores were computed for 34 tasks sampled across two sub-assembly plants in Vojvodina. Concurrent validity was assessed by comparing TBEI classifications with NIOSH Revised Lifting Equation recommended weight limits and with expert ergonomist judgement; agreement was 79 percent with NIOSH and 82 percent with expert ratings. The index required an average of 8 minutes per task to apply, compared with 27 minutes for the full NIOSH procedure. Sensitivity to redesign interventions was tested at five stations before and after introducing height-adjustable trolleys. Limitations regarding asymmetric lifts and two-person tasks are discussed.

title: Influence of Workstation Height and Part Bin Location on Spinal Loading During Seated Assembly of Wiring Harnesses
abstract: Seated assembly of automotive wiring harnesses is associated with sustained neck flexion and asymmetric trunk postures. This laboratory study examined the effect of four workbench heights (650, 700, 750, and 800 mm) combined with three part bin horizontal positions (200, 400, and 600 mm from body midline) on spinal loading estimated by a static biomechanical model. Sixteen female participants assembled standardised connector sub-sets on an adjustable fixture while postural data were collected using an optoelectronic motion capture system sampling at 50 Hz. Head and neck flexion angle exceeded 25 degrees for 63 percent of the total assembly time at the 650 mm bench with the bin at 600 mm, compared with 18 percent at the optimal combination of 750 mm bench height and 200 mm bin distance. Predicted neck compressive force was reduced by 310 N (17 percent) at the optimal configuration. Participants' subjective discomfort ratings on a body map questionnaire aligned closely with the biomechanical predictions. Practical guidelines for seated wiring harness assembly stations are derived from the findings.

title: Ergonomics in Production Engineering: Workstation Design and Human Factors in Manufacturing
abstract: This textbook chapter provides a systematic treatment of ergonomic principles applied to manufacturing workstation design, with emphasis on automotive sub-assembly contexts. Topics covered include anthropometric data selection for Serbian and regional working populations, postural assessment methods (OWAS, RULA, REBA), the NIOSH Revised Lifting Equation, biomechanical modelling of the lumbar spine and upper extremity, and the use of electromyography in occupational settings. Case studies drawn from the authors' fieldwork in Vojvodina automotive supplier plants illustrate the application of each method. The chapter discusses the integration of ergonomic criteria into production layout planning and the economic justification of workstation redesign through reduced absenteeism and injury compensation costs. Worked examples include height-adjustable assembly bench specification, conveyor height selection, and push-pull force limit derivation. The chapter is intended as a reference for undergraduate and postgraduate students in production engineering as well as practicing industrial engineers.

title: Push and Pull Force Limits for Two-Wheeled Cart Operations on Inclined Surfaces in an Automotive Logistics Context
abstract: Push and pull tasks involving two-wheeled carts on inclined floor sections of automotive assembly logistics areas were analysed to establish acceptable force limits. Seventeen male and nine female participants pushed and pulled loaded carts (200, 350, and 500 kg gross load) across floor gradients of 0, 3, and 5 degrees. Initial and sustained hand forces were measured with a calibrated load cell attached to the cart handle. Predicted disc compressive forces at L4/L5 were computed using a biomechanical model parameterised with participant anthropometry and trunk EMG data. Initial push force for the 500 kg cart on the 5-degree slope averaged 312 N for male participants and 274 N for female participants, both exceeding the recommended initial force limits for occasional tasks proposed in the literature. Regression equations relating gross cart load and floor gradient to predicted spinal compressive force are presented. The results support adoption of a 350 kg maximum gross load for mixed-sex logistics workforces on gradients up to 3 degrees without powered assist.

title: Comparison of Static and Dynamic Biomechanical Models for Estimating L5/S1 Loading During Automotive Seat Installation Tasks
abstract: Automotive seat installation involves a sequence of carrying, lowering, and aligning manoeuvres that impose highly dynamic loads on the lumbar spine. This study compared predictions of L5/S1 compressive force from a conventional static biomechanical model and a two-dimensional dynamic model in fourteen workers performing a standardised seat installation task with a 28 kg front seat. Kinematic data were recorded at 100 Hz using an optoelectronic system; trunk and hip segment accelerations were included in the dynamic model as pseudo-static correction terms. The static model underestimated peak L5/S1 compressive force by an average of 18 percent (range 9–31 percent) relative to the dynamic model during the lowering phase, when trunk deceleration contributed substantial inertial loading. Both models agreed closely during the initial carry phase. The findings suggest that static modelling provides acceptable approximations for slow controlled tasks but may underestimate risk in rapid lowering operations. Implications for standard assessment methods applied to automotive seat installation are discussed.

title: Retrospective Exposure Assessment for Musculoskeletal Disorder Risk in a Closed Automotive Sub-Assembly Plant: Linking Archived Postural Data to Reported Injury Rates
abstract: Using archived postural observation records and injury report data from a Vojvodina automotive sub-assembly plant that operated between 1998 and 2011 before closure, this study examined associations between workstation-level ergonomic exposure indices and recorded musculoskeletal disorder (MSD) incidence rates. Postural data in OWAS format were available for 41 workstations covering 283 worker-years of exposure. MSD reports were obtained from occupational health records. Poisson regression was used to model MSD incidence as a function of time-weighted OWAS category distribution, adjusting for age, sex, and job tenure. The proportion of working time in OWAS category 3 or 4 was the strongest predictor of MSD incidence (IRR 2.14 per 10-percentage-point increase; 95% CI 1.68–2.73). Lumbar and shoulder disorders were the most prevalent MSD types, consistent with the task profile of the plant. The analysis is limited by reliance on official injury reports, which likely undercount MSD events. The dataset is made available to support future longitudinal ergonomic exposure modelling.

title: Ergonomic Risk Factors at Electromobility Sub-Assembly Workstations: A Preliminary Comparison with Conventional Drivetrain Assembly
abstract: The shift toward battery electric vehicle production alters the physical demands placed on assembly workers through changes in component weight, geometry, and handling sequence. This preliminary observational study applied RULA, REBA, and the key indicator method for manual handling operations (KIM-MHO) to twelve workstations at a newly commissioned electromobility sub-assembly line and compared results with a matched set of twelve conventional drivetrain assembly workstations at the same facility in Vojvodina. Battery module handling tasks generated REBA scores of 8–10 at four of the twelve electromobility stations, driven by the combination of high load weights (18–34 kg per module) and constrained postures required during tray insertion. By contrast, conventional drivetrain workstations showed higher scores for repetitive wrist deviation tasks. The KIM-MHO results indicated that electromobility stations had a higher proportion of high-risk ratings (42 percent vs. 25 percent) despite the use of vacuum lift assists. The findings suggest that standard ergonomic assessment tool portfolios remain applicable to electromobility lines but that battery module handling deserves targeted attention in production layout planning.

title: Ultrasound-assisted cleaning cuts membrane fouling in dairy wastewater
abstract: Membrane fouling remains a primary operational challenge in dairy wastewater treatment, leading to flux decline, increased energy consumption, and frequent membrane replacement. This study investigates the application of low-frequency ultrasound as an in-situ cleaning strategy to mitigate fouling in polymeric ultrafiltration membranes processing dairy effluents. Experiments were conducted at ultrasound frequencies of 25 kHz and 40 kHz under controlled transmembrane pressure and crossflow velocity conditions. Fouling layer composition was characterized by scanning electron microscopy, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, and hydraulic resistance analysis. Results demonstrated that ultrasound-assisted cleaning reduced irreversible fouling resistance by up to 62% compared to hydraulic backwashing alone, with the 25 kHz treatment yielding superior flux recovery rates. A reversibility index was introduced to quantify cleaning efficiency across repeated fouling–cleaning cycles. The findings further showed that ultrasound treatment did not compromise membrane integrity over ten operational cycles. The study concludes that ultrasound-assisted cleaning is a viable, energy-efficient method for extending membrane service life in dairy wastewater applications, offering practical guidance for industrial implementation.

title: Modelling fouling in ceramic membranes
abstract: Fouling of ceramic membranes in industrial wastewater streams represents a persistent obstacle to the broader adoption of membrane-based separation processes. This work presents a comprehensive mathematical modelling framework to describe fouling dynamics in ceramic microfiltration membranes under variable operating conditions. The model integrates standard blocking laws with a cake filtration sub-model extended to account for compressibility effects observed in particulate-rich food-industry effluents. Experimental validation was performed using synthetic suspensions of varying particle size distributions and real dairy effluents processed on tubular alumina membranes. The model accurately predicted flux decline profiles across a range of transmembrane pressures (0.5–2.5 bar) and temperatures (15–45 °C), with an average relative error below 8%. A sensitivity analysis identified initial particle concentration and membrane surface charge as the most influential parameters governing fouling rate. The proposed framework provides a predictive tool suitable for process design and operational optimisation of ceramic membrane filtration units in food and beverage processing environments.

title: Crossflow microfiltration of vegetable oil wastewater: flux behaviour and fouling indices
abstract: Vegetable oil processing generates large volumes of effluent rich in suspended solids, emulsified fats, and surface-active compounds that pose significant challenges for conventional wastewater treatment. This study examines the performance of polymeric polysulfone membranes in crossflow microfiltration of sunflower oil mill effluent, with emphasis on flux behaviour over extended operating periods. Fouling indices including the modified fouling index and resistance-in-series parameters were evaluated under systematically varied crossflow velocities and transmembrane pressures. Results indicated that emulsified oil droplets constitute the primary foulant, forming a compressible gel layer that dominates hydraulic resistance. Pre-screening of the feed stream through a 200 µm mesh reduced total fouling resistance by 34%. Chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal exceeded 85% after ultrafiltration polishing, indicating potential for effluent reuse in non-contact cooling circuits. An empirical correlation linking fouling index to feed oil concentration was derived and validated against three independent datasets. The findings provide actionable design criteria for membrane units treating vegetable oil processing wastewater in food industrial parks.

title: Process intensification via membrane-integrated evaporation for whey concentration
abstract: Whey, a major by-product of cheese manufacturing, contains valuable proteins and lactose yet is frequently discharged as effluent due to the high cost of conventional concentration technologies. This study proposes and evaluates a process-intensified hybrid system coupling nanofiltration membrane stages with mechanical vapour recompression evaporation for whey concentration. The integrated configuration was modelled using steady-state mass and energy balances, and the resulting process flowsheet was optimised using a multi-objective genetic algorithm minimising specific energy consumption and capital cost simultaneously. Simulation results showed that the hybrid process reduces specific energy demand by 41% relative to standalone evaporation while achieving a total solids concentration of 45% w/w. A laboratory-scale proof-of-concept trial confirmed model predictions within 7% deviation. Membrane fouling behaviour during whey nanofiltration was characterised, and a cleaning-in-place protocol optimised for caustic and enzymatic agents was established. The study demonstrates that process intensification through membrane–evaporation integration offers a technically and economically viable route for sustainable whey valorisation in small-to-medium dairy enterprises.

title: Effect of operating pH on fouling layer formation in ultrafiltration of fruit juice effluents
abstract: Fruit juice processing effluents contain pectin, polyphenols, and suspended pulp fragments that rapidly foul ultrafiltration membranes, curtailing process efficiency and product quality. This investigation systematically evaluates the influence of feed pH (3.0–7.5) on fouling layer composition, membrane flux, and rejection of target macromolecules during dead-end and crossflow ultrafiltration of apple and plum juice processing effluents. Regenerated cellulose membranes with molecular weight cut-offs of 10, 30, and 50 kDa were employed. At pH 4.5, pectin molecules were found to adopt a coil configuration that promoted dense cake layer formation, yielding the highest fouling resistance. Alkaline pre-adjustment to pH 7.0 shifted the dominant fouling mechanism from cake filtration to standard pore blocking, reducing irreversible resistance by 28%. Polyphenol adsorption onto membrane surfaces was characterised by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, revealing covalent bonding at acidic pH values. A fouling mechanism transition map as a function of pH and flux was constructed, providing practical operational guidance. These results directly inform pre-treatment protocol design for fruit processing wastewater membrane systems.

title: Pilot-scale assessment of forward osmosis for concentration of sugar beet molasses stillage
abstract: Sugar beet molasses stillage, generated as a by-product of bioethanol distillation, presents a high organic load that complicates conventional wastewater treatment. Forward osmosis (FO) is investigated here as an energy-efficient pre-concentration technology to reduce the hydraulic load prior to anaerobic digestion. Pilot-scale trials were conducted using cellulose triacetate flat-sheet FO membranes with sodium chloride and magnesium chloride draw solutions at varying concentrations. Water flux, reverse solute flux, and organic rejection were monitored over 72-hour continuous runs. Membrane orientation (active layer facing feed versus draw) was found to significantly influence internal concentration polarisation, with the active-layer-facing-draw configuration yielding 18% higher average water flux. Specific reverse solute flux values below 0.15 g L⁻¹ were achieved with MgCl₂ draw solution, minimising process losses. Organic matter rejection exceeded 92%, and the pre-concentrated stillage demonstrated improved biogas yield in subsequent bench-scale anaerobic digestion tests. The study provides a scale-up basis for integrating FO into sugar industry wastewater management chains.

title: Intensified reactive extraction coupled with membrane separation for lactic acid recovery from fermentation broth
abstract: Lactic acid is a platform chemical of growing industrial relevance, yet its recovery from complex fermentation broths remains costly and energy-intensive. This study presents a process-intensified approach combining reactive liquid–liquid extraction with continuous hollow-fibre membrane contactors for the selective separation and concentration of lactic acid. Tri-n-octylamine dissolved in a non-toxic diluent mixture was employed as the extractant, and the membrane contactor configuration eliminated phase dispersion and emulsification problems encountered in conventional mixer-settlers. Extraction efficiency exceeding 94% was achieved at feed pH 2.5, with a membrane mass transfer coefficient of 3.1 × 10⁻⁵ m s⁻¹. Fouling of the microporous polypropylene membranes by biomass and protein residues was characterised and substantially mitigated by inclusion of a tangential flow microfiltration pre-treatment step. A simplified techno-economic analysis indicated that the integrated process reduces operating costs by approximately 30% relative to a conventional ion-exchange recovery route at the 500 kg d⁻¹ scale. The results support further scale-up investigation within the framework of biorefinery process intensification.

title: Anti-fouling surface modification of polyethersulfone membranes using zwitterionic polymer grafting
abstract: Polyethersulfone (PES) ultrafiltration membranes are widely adopted in food and beverage wastewater treatment but suffer from rapid hydrophobic fouling that degrades long-term performance. This work investigates surface modification of PES membranes by grafting of a zwitterionic poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (PSBMA) brush layer via UV-initiated free radical polymerisation. Modification was confirmed by ATR-FTIR, contact angle goniometry, and atomic force microscopy. Water contact angle decreased from 68° for pristine PES to 14° after grafting, confirming substantial hydrophilicity enhancement. Fouling resistance was assessed using bovine serum albumin, sodium alginate, and humic acid as model foulants representative of food processing effluents. PSBMA-grafted membranes exhibited flux recovery ratios above 93% after simple hydraulic cleaning across all foulant types, compared to 51–67% for unmodified membranes. Protein rejection remained above 96%, confirming that modification did not compromise selectivity. Long-term stability tests over 30 days in simulated dairy effluent showed no significant loss of hydrophilicity. The modified membranes represent a promising platform for low-maintenance, high-throughput filtration in food industry wastewater applications.

title: Membrane separation processes in agro-industrial wastewater treatment: a systematic review
abstract: Agro-industrial wastewater presents one of the most complex challenges in environmental engineering due to its highly variable composition, high organic load, and seasonal discharge patterns. Membrane separation processes, including microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, and reverse osmosis, have emerged as versatile and efficient tools for the treatment and valorisation of such effluents. This systematic review synthesises findings from 180 peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2023, covering applications in dairy, fruit and vegetable processing, slaughterhouse, and fermentation industries. Key performance indicators including flux, rejection, fouling propensity, and energy consumption are compared across membrane materials, module geometries, and operating conditions. The review identifies fouling management as the predominant technical barrier, discusses advances in anti-fouling surface modification and enhanced cleaning protocols, and highlights process intensification strategies that integrate membrane stages with biological treatment or thermal concentration. Emerging trends including ceramic membrane adoption, membrane bioreactors, and digitally monitored autonomous cleaning cycles are discussed. Critical research gaps are identified, particularly regarding long-term pilot studies under real industrial conditions and standardised fouling characterisation protocols. The review concludes with recommendations for future research and development priorities relevant to sustainable agro-industrial water management.

title: Comparing ordinary kriging and inverse distance weighting for mapping exchangeable sodium percentage in Vojvodina sodic soils
abstract: Exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP) is a primary diagnostic criterion for classifying sodic soils, yet its spatial mapping is rarely performed at the within-field scale. This study compared ordinary kriging (OK) and inverse distance weighting (IDW) for predicting ESP from 88 topsoil samples (0–30 cm) collected across a 120-hectare trial site in the Zrenjanin municipality. Samples were analysed for cation exchange capacity and exchangeable cations by standard titrimetric and flame photometric methods. Omnidirectional variograms for ESP were fitted with an exponential model (range 134 m, nugget-to-sill ratio 0.24). Cross-validation showed that OK produced a lower RMSE (3.1 cmol/kg) than IDW with power 2 (RMSE 4.0 cmol/kg). Spatial maps generated by the two methods differed most in areas between sampling locations, where OK smoothing reduced the risk of artefacts. Areas exceeding the ESP threshold of 15% covered 38% of the field under OK interpolation and 41% under IDW, a difference relevant for lime and gypsum amendment planning.

title: Regression-kriging for delineating saline-sodic soil units using EM38 and pXRF auxiliary data
abstract: Regression-kriging (RK) was applied to delineate saline-sodic soil management zones at a commercial sunflower farm of 280 hectares in central Vojvodina. Apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) from an EM38 survey and total sodium content from pXRF scanning served as covariates in a multiple linear regression step predicting measured ECe and ESP from 66 calibration soil cores. Residuals from the regression were subsequently kriged with fitted spherical variogram models and added back to the regression predictions. Prediction performance was assessed by 10-fold cross-validation: RK achieved RMSE of 2.7 mS/m for ECe and 2.9 cmol/kg for ESP, compared with 3.8 and 4.2 for ordinary kriging without covariates. The resulting classification into non-saline-sodic, transitional, and saline-sodic zones covered 48%, 27%, and 25% of the field area respectively. Zone boundaries were consistent with field observations of sparse sunflower emergence and yellow chlorotic patches that historically corresponded to sodium-dominated spots. The study demonstrates that combining two proximal sensing methods as regression covariates reduces the number of expensive laboratory analyses needed for reliable soil unit mapping.

title: Geostatistical methods in precision soil survey: a practical guide for practitioners in Southeast Europe
abstract: This book chapter reviews the practical application of variogram modelling, ordinary kriging, kriging with external drift, and regression-kriging for soil property mapping, with examples drawn from surveys conducted in Serbia, Romania, and Hungary. It addresses common difficulties faced by practitioners in the region, including sparse sampling networks, non-stationarity of saline soil properties, and the choice between model-based and algorithm-based interpolators. Step-by-step guidance is provided on exploratory data analysis, normal score transformation, variogram fitting, and uncertainty quantification through conditional simulation. Case studies illustrate the mapping of pH, ECe, organic carbon, and particle size distribution at field and catchment scales. Software options including R packages gstat and automap, as well as QGIS plugins, are discussed with attention to reproducibility and open data formats. The chapter is aimed at soil scientists and agronomists who have basic statistical knowledge but limited prior experience with geostatistics, and it draws heavily on datasets from Vojvodina and the broader Pannonian region.

title: Temporal stability of ECa spatial patterns in a recurrently flooded saline field over five growing seasons
abstract: The temporal stability of apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) spatial patterns was examined in a 62-hectare field subject to periodic flooding in the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal zone of Vojvodina. EM38 surveys were repeated in May and October of each year from 2016 to 2020, producing ten maps per depth mode (vertical and horizontal dipoles). Spearman rank correlation coefficients between ECa maps from different years ranged from 0.74 to 0.93 for the vertical dipole mode, indicating moderate to strong temporal stability of high- and low-conductivity zones despite annual flooding events. Stable high-ECa zones coincided with fine-textured depressions identified by a 1-m LiDAR digital terrain model. Zones of lower stability were located on sloping transitions between microrelief elements. Temporal stability index maps were produced by calculating the coefficient of variation at each interpolated grid node across the ten survey dates. Results suggest that a single growing-season survey can adequately represent salt distribution for management purposes in stable zones, while transition zones require repeated measurement. The LiDAR terrain derivatives explained 58% of spatial variance in mean ECa across the ten surveys.

title: Mapping soil pH at 1:5000 scale combining ion-selective electrode rapid measurements and regression-kriging in alkaline agricultural land
abstract: A rapid ion-selective electrode (ISE) method for field measurement of soil pH was calibrated and used to densify a sparse laboratory sample network for regression-kriging in an alkaline agricultural area near Kikinda, Serbia. Laboratory pH values from 54 standard samples (1:2.5 water suspension, glass electrode) and 210 in-field ISE readings were collected across 95 hectares. The bias of ISE versus laboratory measurements averaged 0.12 pH units and was corrected by a linear calibration. Regression-kriging using ISE readings as a covariate reduced cross-validation RMSE for laboratory pH from 0.31 (ordinary kriging alone) to 0.18. The final 1:5000-scale map identified three zones: pH 7.4–7.8 (32% of area), pH 7.9–8.3 (51%), and pH above 8.3 (17%), the last corresponding closely to visible lime-encrusted surface patches and prior EM38 surveys. The approach substantially reduces laboratory costs per hectare while maintaining mapping accuracy sufficient for liming and micronutrient management decisions. Semivariogram parameters and calibration coefficients are reported to allow replication at similar alkaline sites in the Pannonian region.

title: Evaluation of sample size reduction strategies for regression-kriging of soil electrical conductivity using dense EM38 grids as covariates
abstract: Determining the minimum number of laboratory soil samples required for acceptable regression-kriging accuracy is practically important because laboratory analysis is the main cost driver in proximal-sensing-assisted surveys. Using a fully sampled reference dataset of 148 soil cores and a continuous EM38 grid from a 115-hectare saline field in Vojvodina, this study evaluated the effect of progressively reducing the calibration sample set to 100, 75, 50, 30, and 20 samples on regression-kriging predictions of ECe, ESP, and clay content. Sampling configurations were replicated 100 times using random, conditioned Latin hypercube, and spatial coverage designs. Cross-validation RMSE for ECe increased moderately from 1.9 mS/m (n=148) to 2.6 mS/m (n=30) under the conditioned Latin hypercube design, but rose sharply to 4.3 mS/m at n=20. For ESP and clay content, a threshold near n=40–50 was identified below which spatial coverage sampling outperformed random designs by 15–22% in RMSE. Nugget variance estimates became unstable below n=30, compromising kriging weights. Results indicate that for fields with strong covariate signals, conditioned Latin hypercube designs with 40–50 soil cores are a reasonable compromise between cost and mapping accuracy.

title: Radiation partitioning between maize and bean strips of contrasting widths under continental climate conditions
abstract: Strip widths of 0.75 m, 1.5 m, and 3.0 m were tested in a three-year field experiment near Novi Sad using paired quantum sensors placed at 10 cm intervals across canopy profiles. The fraction of photosynthetically active radiation intercepted by the shorter maize strips decreased by 18–24 % relative to sole-crop controls, with corresponding increases in transmitted radiation to the bean understorey. Biomass accumulation in bean rows adjacent to maize borders exceeded interior-row biomass by up to 31 % in the 0.75 m treatment, attributed to lateral light penetration. A simple geometric interception model parameterised from row height and azimuth reproduced observed PAR profiles with RMSE below 12 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ across 80 % of measurement positions. Results suggest that strip width is the dominant design variable for radiation management in this intercrop combination under temperate continental conditions.

title: Effect of potassium silicate foliar application on silicon deposition in the epidermis of winter wheat internodes
abstract: Foliar potassium silicate sprays were applied at three growth stages (tillering, stem elongation, flag-leaf emergence) to determine the timing that maximises silica body deposition in the epidermal cells of the second internode in winter wheat. Two cultivars (Renesansa and Simonida) and three concentration levels (0, 1.5 and 3.0 g Si L⁻¹) were tested in a split-plot field experiment at Novi Sad in 2012–2013. Cross-sections of the second internode were prepared at anthesis and imaged by scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) to map silicon distribution. Application at stem elongation (GS31–GS37) increased epidermal Si signal area by 47–62 % compared with the untreated control, while tillering applications showed no significant effect. The higher concentration did not outperform 1.5 g Si L⁻¹. Results indicate a narrow application window linked to rapid cell-wall lignification in the internode, and suggest that SEM-EDX is a reliable semi-quantitative tool for monitoring silicon deposition in field-grown wheat.

title: Mechanical properties of wheat culms following silicon soil amendment: a three-year field study
abstract: The relationship between soil-applied calcium silicate (0, 250 and 500 kg ha⁻¹) and the breaking strength and elastic modulus of winter wheat culms was investigated over three consecutive seasons (2013–2016) on a calcaric cambisol at Sremska Mitrovica. Culm breaking strength was measured with a modified three-point bending apparatus at GS65, and cross-sectional area, wall thickness and sclerenchyma ring width were determined from stained paraffin sections. The 500 kg ha⁻¹ treatment increased culm breaking strength by 18–27 % relative to the control across years, with the greatest response in the drier 2014/15 season. Wall thickness in the second internode increased significantly (p < 0.05) at 500 kg ha⁻¹ in all three seasons, while sclerenchyma ring width responded only in the two wetter seasons. Silicon content in straw increased from 2.1 to 3.8 mg g⁻¹ at the highest dose. The cost of calcium silicate at the effective rate is discussed in relation to achievable yield protection, suggesting economic viability only in high-yield, irrigation-supported systems.

title: Silicon and nitrogen interaction on lodging incidence and grain yield in high-input winter wheat systems
abstract: High nitrogen rates increase shoot biomass and lodging risk in winter wheat; silicon amendments are hypothesised to counteract this. A two-factor field experiment with four N rates (80, 120, 160 and 200 kg N ha⁻¹) and two silicon treatments (no silicon, 300 kg ha⁻¹ calcium silicate) was conducted at Rimski Šančevi over two seasons (2016–2018). Lodging was scored on a 0–9 scale at GS77. At 160 kg N ha⁻¹, silicon reduced mean lodging score from 4.3 to 2.1 and increased grain yield by 6.4 %. At 200 kg N ha⁻¹, yield response to silicon reached 9.1 % in the season with a late-July rain event. Silicon had no significant effect at 80 kg N ha⁻¹, where lodging was negligible. Harvest index improved by 3–5 percentage points with silicon at the two highest N rates. Results support targeted silicon use as a partial substitute for growth regulators under intensive nitrogen management, without altering protein content significantly.

title: Micro-CT imaging of wheat culm cross-sections for non-destructive assessment of silicon-induced anatomical changes
abstract: Scanning micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) was applied for the first time to quantify anatomical parameters of winter wheat culm cross-sections in silicon-treated and untreated plants. Internodes from 20 plants per treatment were scanned at 8 µm voxel resolution at the Centre for Non-Destructive Testing, University of Novi Sad. Parameters extracted included outer culm diameter, wall thickness, cross-sectional area of vascular bundles, and void fraction of the internode lumen. Silicon-treated plants (300 kg ha⁻¹ calcium silicate) showed a 12 % thicker culm wall and 9 % greater total vascular bundle area compared with controls. Void fraction did not differ significantly between treatments. Results were validated against conventional paraffin-section measurements (Pearson r = 0.88 for wall thickness). Micro-CT required no chemical fixation and permitted multiple cross-sections from a single internode segment, reducing preparation time by approximately 60 % relative to classical histological methods. The technique is proposed as a routine screening tool in silicon nutrition experiments.

title: Bioavailability of silicon from three commercially available amendments in Vojvodina soils: an incubation study
abstract: Calcium silicate slag, diatomite and rice-husk ash were compared as silicon sources in a 90-day incubation experiment using Vojvodina chernozem and calcaric cambisol. Amendments were applied at 200 and 400 kg SiO₂ ha⁻¹ equivalent rates. Plant-available silicon (0.5 M acetic acid extraction) was measured at 15-day intervals. Calcium silicate slag released plant-available silicon most rapidly, reaching plateau concentrations after 30 days. Diatomite released silicon slowly and reached only 55–62 % of the slag plateau at day 90. Rice-husk ash showed intermediate release but high variability across replicates (CV up to 34 %). Soil pH buffered the release rate: at pH 6.0, slag-derived Si availability was 22 % lower than at pH 7.4. Results inform amendment selection for practical field use and suggest diatomite is unsuitable as a sole Si source unless applied at very high rates or combined with acidulation.

title: Response of root architecture to silicon supply in hydroponically grown winter wheat seedlings
abstract: Root morphological responses to silicon were characterised in three winter wheat cultivars grown in hydroponic solution culture with 0, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 mM monosilicic acid for 21 days. Root images were captured with a flatbed scanner and analysed using WinRHIZO software. Total root length, specific root length, root tip count and average diameter were recorded. At 1.0 mM Si, total root length increased by 14–22 % and root tip count by 17–28 % compared with the Si-free control across all three cultivars, while average root diameter decreased slightly (3–6 %), indicating finer root proliferation. At 2.0 mM, responses plateaued or slightly declined relative to 1.0 mM. Silicon concentration in root tissue reached 3.2–4.1 mg g⁻¹ DW at 1.0 mM supply. These data suggest silicon contributes to root architecture modification at moderate concentrations, with potential implications for soil exploration and water uptake in field-grown wheat, though translation of hydroponic results to field conditions requires caution.

title: Editorial Independence and Ownership Structure in Serbian Commercial Television: A Case Study of Three Broadcasters
abstract: This article examines the relationship between ownership concentration and editorial decision-making in three Serbian commercial television stations during the period 2005–2009. Using semi-structured interviews with 34 editorial staff and producers, supplemented by analysis of broadcast schedules and regulatory filings with the Republic Broadcasting Agency, the study traces how ownership transitions altered news selection criteria and the frequency of self-censorship. Findings indicate that stations acquired by domestic holding companies experienced a measurable reduction in investigative segments — from an average of 4.2 per week to 1.7 per week — within eighteen months of acquisition. Editorially, producers described informal pressure as more determinative than formal editorial policy. The article situates these dynamics within comparative frameworks from small-market broadcasting literature and argues that regulatory design in Serbia has consistently underestimated the informal dimension of ownership influence.

title: Freelance Labour and Precarity in Post-Yugoslav Television Production
abstract: Drawing on 48 in-depth interviews conducted in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Zagreb between 2009 and 2010, this chapter maps the expansion of freelance and fixed-term contracting in television production across former Yugoslav successor states. The study documents the shift from permanent employment models, which predominated in public broadcasting through the 1990s, toward project-based contracts that became standard in commercial sectors by 2005. Interviewees reported average contract durations of under six months and described a pervasive reluctance to report workplace grievances due to fear of non-renewal. The chapter draws on labour sociology frameworks to argue that precarity in this context is not merely economic but functions as a disciplinary mechanism shaping editorial content. Comparative data from public and commercial sectors highlight how different ownership forms produce distinct labour regimes, with public broadcasters retaining somewhat stronger protections even under budget pressure.

title: Scheduling Power: How Prime-Time Decisions Are Made in Vojvodina's Regional Television Sector
abstract: This study investigates the internal scheduling processes of six regional television broadcasters licensed to operate in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina, Serbia. Through observation sessions totalling 210 hours across three stations and document analysis of internal programming memos obtained via institutional cooperation agreements, the research reconstructs how scheduling decisions are negotiated between commercial, editorial, and technical departments. Quantitative content analysis of 840 hours of broadcast output coded episodes by genre and origin. Results show that domestically produced information programming occupies 23 percent of peak hours on average, compared to 41 percent on the single public regional broadcaster. Interview data from 19 scheduling executives reveal that advertiser preferences — particularly the avoidance of politically contentious content adjacent to commercial breaks — function as implicit scheduling constraints rarely discussed in formal meetings.

title: Measuring Editorial Autonomy: Toward an Instrument for Small-Market Television Research
abstract: Existing instruments for measuring editorial autonomy in newsrooms were developed primarily in the context of large-market, nationally dominant broadcasters in Western Europe and North America. This article proposes an adapted measurement instrument suited to small-market television environments, defined as national or regional markets with fewer than three million households. The instrument comprises 34 Likert-scale items across five dimensions: formal policy, informal pressure, resource constraints, source relationships, and self-censorship. Items were derived through three rounds of expert consultation involving 12 media scholars and practising editors from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Slovenia, followed by cognitive pre-testing with 22 television journalists. Preliminary reliability data show Cronbach's alpha values above 0.78 for all five dimensions. The article discusses limitations arising from social desirability bias in sensitive professional contexts and proposes mitigation strategies including anonymised online administration.

title: Working Conditions in Serbian Television News: Survey Evidence from 2013
abstract: This paper presents findings from a structured survey of 187 television news workers employed at 22 licensed broadcasters in Serbia, conducted in autumn 2013. The survey gathered data on contract type, weekly working hours, access to professional development, perception of editorial freedom, and experience of pressure from management or ownership. Sixty-one percent of respondents held fixed-term or freelance contracts. Mean reported weekly hours were 48.3, with 29 percent reporting more than 55 hours per week. Respondents at privately owned commercial stations reported significantly lower perceived editorial autonomy than those at public service broadcasters on all five dimensions of the adapted instrument previously validated by the author. Logistic regression indicates that contract precarity and low perceived autonomy are positively associated even after controlling for station size and market position. The paper discusses implications for Serbian broadcasting regulation and compares results with similar surveys conducted in Hungary and Romania.

title: The Influence of Political Advertising Revenue on News Coverage: Evidence from Local Television in Serbia and North Macedonia
abstract: Local television broadcasters in Serbia and North Macedonia depend heavily on political advertising, particularly during election cycles, for a substantial share of annual revenue. This article examines whether dependence on political advertising revenue correlates with coverage patterns favourable to paying political parties. Using a combination of advertising expenditure data obtained from regulatory bodies in both countries and content analysis of 2,640 news segments broadcast during the 2016 Serbian parliamentary election, the study constructs a station-level index of revenue dependence and tests its association with sentiment coding of party-related segments. Stations in the top quartile of political advertising dependence gave 34 percent more airtime to coalition parties and coded significantly higher on positive sentiment toward those parties. The methodological limitations of inferring intent from correlational data are discussed, and the article recommends that advertising transparency requirements be extended to local broadcasters.

title: Production Studies as Method: Applying Ethnographic Approaches to Balkan Television Newsrooms
abstract: This book chapter surveys the methodological challenges of conducting production studies research in television newsrooms across the Western Balkans, based on fieldwork experience accumulated by the author and collaborators between 2008 and 2015. The chapter addresses three recurring difficulties: negotiating access when broadcasters perceive research as potentially exposing editorial misconduct, maintaining researcher positionality in politically polarised environments, and managing the gap between what participants say in interviews and what observation reveals about actual practice. Drawing on field notes from six newsrooms, the chapter provides concrete examples of how informal editorial decisions are made in practice, and how these diverge from stated editorial policies. The chapter also proposes a staged access protocol for newsroom ethnography in sensitive media environments, which has subsequently been adopted in graduate methods training at the authors' institution.

title: Editors Under Pressure: Qualitative Accounts of Ownership Interference in Vojvodinian Commercial Television
abstract: This article presents findings from 26 in-depth interviews with current and former editors-in-chief and senior producers at commercial television stations in Vojvodina conducted between 2017 and 2018. Interviewees described a range of ownership interference practices, from direct telephonic instruction during live broadcasts to systematic exclusion of specific topics from editorial meetings. The study uses thematic analysis to identify six distinct interference patterns, which are characterised along dimensions of frequency, directness, and the intermediaries involved. Three patterns — topic blacklisting, source recommendation, and timing pressure — were reported by more than half of participants. The article distinguishes between interference experienced as occasional and manageable and that experienced as structurally defining of daily editorial work. It argues that the latter form, present at four of the twelve stations represented, constitutes a systematic rather than incidental constraint on journalistic practice and cannot be adequately addressed by existing self-regulatory codes.

title: Cross-Border Comparisons in Small-Market Broadcasting Research: Methodological Notes from a Four-Country Study
abstract: Comparative media systems research frequently encounters difficulties when applying frameworks developed for large Western European markets to smaller post-communist contexts. This conference paper reflects on methodological lessons from a four-country comparative study of editorial autonomy conducted in Serbia, Montenegro, Slovenia, and Slovakia between 2018 and 2020. Key challenges included the non-equivalence of regulatory categories across national frameworks, variation in what counts as a commercial broadcaster, and the limited comparability of audience measurement data across markets of very different sizes. The paper proposes a set of tertium comparationis principles for small-market broadcasting research and illustrates these with data from pilot interviews conducted in all four countries. It also reports on initial quantitative comparisons of staff-to-output ratios, which range from 3.8 to 11.4 full-time equivalents per weekly broadcast hour across the sample, suggesting substantial structural variation warranting further investigation.

title: Streaming Platforms and the Changing Labour Market for Serbian Television Producers
abstract: The entry of international subscription video-on-demand platforms into the Serbian market between 2016 and 2022 created new commissioning opportunities for independent production companies while simultaneously intensifying competition for experienced production labour. This article examines labour market effects using data from 28 interviews with producers who had worked for both traditional broadcasters and platform-commissioned productions, combined with employment advertisement analysis covering 1,140 positions posted on Serbian media industry job boards between 2019 and 2023. Platform commissions offered higher per-episode budgets — averaging 2.3 times the comparable national broadcaster rate in reported figures — but introduced new forms of contractual control through non-disclosure agreements and content approval clauses uncommon in domestic television contracting. The article argues that the platform sector has created a segmented labour market in which a relatively small group of experienced producers circulates between well-resourced commissions while the broader workforce experiences unchanged or worsening conditions.

title: Who Owns Local Television in Serbia? A Mapping of Beneficial Ownership Structures, 2015–2024
abstract: Regulatory analysis of Serbian local television ownership has been hampered by the use of intermediary holding structures that obscure beneficial ownership. This article presents findings from a systematic review of commercial register filings, regulatory licence documentation, and investigative journalism sources for all 67 commercial local and regional television broadcasters licensed in Serbia as of December 2023. Using network analysis to map ownership chains, the study identifies 14 distinct beneficial ownership clusters, of which six are linked to individuals with documented involvement in political party financing. The average ownership chain length between the licensed entity and the beneficial owner is 3.2 corporate layers, compared to 1.4 layers in a reference sample of commercial broadcasters in Slovenia drawn from comparable sources. The article argues that current Serbian broadcasting legislation is structurally inadequate to enforce the ownership transparency provisions that formally exist and proposes specific amendments to disclosure requirements.

title: A tabu search heuristic for the vehicle routing problem with stochastic demand and late order insertion
abstract: This paper addresses a variant of the capacitated vehicle routing problem in which new customer orders arrive during the execution of routes, requiring immediate replanning. We model the problem as a two-stage stochastic program and solve it using a tabu search heuristic that maintains a pool of partial routes amenable to low-cost reinsertion. Experiments are conducted on a benchmark set derived from the Solomon instances, augmented with synthetic late-arrival events drawn from a Poisson process with mean inter-arrival times of 8, 15, and 25 minutes. On instances with up to 150 customers and an average late-order rate of 12 per cent, the heuristic finds solutions within 3.1 per cent of a post-hoc optimal computed by CPLEX 12.9 on average, while replanning decisions are delivered in under 400 milliseconds on a single-core 3 GHz machine. Solution degradation relative to the static optimum grows approximately linearly with the late-order rate up to 25 per cent insertion frequency, beyond which route fragmentation becomes a dominant cost driver.

title: Hybridising branch-and-price with large neighbourhood search for same-day delivery replanning
abstract: Same-day delivery services require route plans to be revised within seconds whenever a new order is accepted. We develop a hybrid algorithm that combines a branch-and-price exact framework for small residual sub-problems with a large neighbourhood search (LNS) procedure that handles the full dynamic instance. The branch-and-price component solves column generation sub-problems to optimality for sub-instances of up to 30 unserved customers, while LNS destroy-and-repair operators handle the broader neighbourhood. The algorithm is evaluated on 80 instances derived from publicly available courier data from a mid-sized Central European city, with fleet sizes of 5 to 20 vehicles and dynamic order rates of 20 to 50 per cent of total demand. The hybrid reduces average total travel distance by 6.8 per cent compared to a standalone LNS baseline and by 11.2 per cent compared to a greedy insertion benchmark, at median decision times of 1.2 seconds. Scaling behaviour is reported for instances up to 400 customers.

title: Modeli za vrednovanje stabilnosti rešenja pri dinamičkom rutiranju u distributivnoj logistici
abstract: Dinamičko rutiranje vozila obično se ocenjuje isključivo prema ukupnoj pređenoj distanci ili broju vozila, zanemarujući stabilnost plana — to jest, koliko se nova ruta razlikuje od prethodne sa stanovišta vozača i dispečera. Ovaj rad predlaže tri mere stabilnosti: prosečni Hammingov rastojanje između uzastopnih planova, indeks razdvajanja korisnika i stopu promene opterećenja vozila. Mere se primenjuju na skup od 120 instanci generisanih iz podataka o dostavi maloprodajnih pakata u Vojvodini, a analizira se korelacija između stabilnosti i efikasnosti pri različitim stopama dinamičnosti (10–50 posto). Utvrđeno je da povećanje stabilnosti za 15 posto prosečno povećava distancu za 2,4 posto, što ukazuje na merljiv kompromis. Rad dalje predlaže parametrizovanu objektivnu funkciju koja dozvoljava operateru da eksplicitno postavi preferenciju između stabilnosti i distancne efikasnosti.
