title: Real-time order acceptance and routing decisions under fleet capacity constraints: a rolling horizon approach
abstract: We study the joint order acceptance and vehicle routing problem in which a dispatcher must simultaneously decide whether to accept an incoming order and how to insert it into active routes, subject to hard vehicle capacity and time-window constraints. A rolling horizon framework is proposed in which the planning horizon is divided into 10-minute decision epochs; at each epoch, a mixed-integer programme is solved for a truncated lookahead window while a fast greedy policy handles arrivals within the epoch. The MIP is formulated with a set-partitioning structure and solved via CPLEX 20.1 with a time limit of 8 seconds per epoch. Tests on 40 instances with up to 250 customers and an acceptance rate decision threshold calibrated against a revenue model show that the rolling horizon policy accepts 94.1 per cent of profitable orders on average, compared to 88.3 per cent for a myopic greedy policy. Sensitivity analysis covers fleet size, time-window tightness, and order spatial clustering.

title: Primena adaptivne pretrage promenljivih okruženja na problem dinamičkog rutiranja hitnih vozila
abstract: Rad razmatra primenu adaptivne pretrage promenljivih okruženja (AVNS) na dinamički problem rutiranja hitnih vozila u urbanim sredinama. Modelovana je mreža Novog Sada sa 312 čvorova i podacima o saobraćajnim gustinama u različitim periodima dana. Simulirani su scenariji sa 20 do 80 simultanih hitnih poziva u vremenskom periodu od četiri sata, sa prosečnom stopom pristizanja od 18 poziva na sat. AVNS kombinuje tri operatora razmene, dva operatora reinseriranja i jedan operator segmentnog obrnutog rasporeda, sa dinamičkim odabirom operatora baziranim na istoriji poboljšanja. Prosečno vreme odgovora na poziv smanjeno je za 11,3 posto u poređenju sa aktuelnom procedurom dispečinga zasnovana na fiksnim sektorima, uz redukciju praznih kilometara od 8,6 posto. Rezultati su validirani kroz razgovore sa dispečerima Zavoda za hitnu medicinsku pomoć Novi Sad.

title: Benchmarking exact and metaheuristic solvers for dynamic insertion in time-critical VRP: a computational study
abstract: This paper provides a structured computational comparison of seven solution methods for the dynamic vehicle routing problem with time-critical order insertion: two exact approaches (branch-and-cut and column generation), three metaheuristics (iterated local search, simulated annealing, and memetic algorithm), and two hybrid schemes combining exact and heuristic components. All methods are evaluated on a common benchmark library of 200 instances spanning 50 to 500 customers, dynamic rates of 10 to 60 per cent, and three time-window tightness levels. Performance is measured by solution quality gap relative to an offline optimum, decision latency, and robustness across instance classes. Branch-and-cut becomes impractical beyond 120 customers under tight time limits, while the memetic–column generation hybrid achieves the best quality-latency trade-off at 200 customers. Raw results, instance files, and solver configurations are published in an open repository to support reproducibility.

title: Višekriterijumska optimizacija u dinamičkom rutiranju vozila za dostavu poslednje milje: ugljični otisak i vreme isporuke kao konkurentski ciljevi
abstract: Dostava poslednje milje u gradskim područjima podleže rastućem pritisku da se istovremeno smanje emisije CO₂ i zadrži kratak rok isporuke. Ovaj rad formuliše bićiljevni dinamički VRP u kome se minimiziraju ukupna emisija (modelovana funkcijom brzine i opterećenja vozila prema COPERT metodologiji) i maksimalno kašnjenje isporuke. Pareto front se aproksimira NSGA-II algoritmom adaptiranim za dinamičke uslove, uz reinicijalizaciju populacije pri svakom ubacivanju nove narudžbine. Testirano je na 30 instanci generisanih iz anonimizovanih podataka jedne distributivne kompanije u Vojvodini za period od 90 dana, sa flotom od 8 do 15 vozila. Dobijeni Pareto frontovi otkrivaju da smanjenje emisije za 10 posto zahteva prosečno povećanje maksimalnog kašnjenja za 4,2 minuta, dok smanjenje od 20 posto udvostručuje ovaj kompromis. Rad uključuje i analizu osetljivosti na različite politike prihvata novih narudžbina.

title: Warm-starting branch-and-price with learned dual variables for dynamic VRP re-optimisation
abstract: Re-optimisation in dynamic vehicle routing typically starts a branch-and-price solver from scratch at each replanning trigger, discarding dual variable information from previous solves. We investigate whether dual variables from the immediately preceding solve, adjusted by a learned correction model, can serve as a warm start to accelerate convergence. A gradient-boosted regression model is trained on 15,000 solve pairs drawn from simulated dynamic instances to predict the shift in column generation duals caused by a single order insertion or deletion. On a test set of 500 replanning events with 80 to 180 unserved customers, warm-starting reduces the number of column generation iterations by a median of 31 per cent and total solver wall-clock time by 24 per cent, with no statistically significant degradation in solution quality. The approach is solver-agnostic and is demonstrated on two open-source branch-and-price frameworks.

title: Demand Uncertainty Modelling in Supplier Contracts Using Scenario-Based Stochastic Programming
abstract: This study formulates a two-stage stochastic programming model for supplier order allocation when end-customer demand is uncertain. The first stage determines contract quantities with each of six candidate suppliers before demand is realised; the second stage adjusts order volumes after a demand scenario is observed. Fifty discrete demand scenarios are generated from three years of historical shipment data provided by a food processing company in Bačka Palanka, fitted to a mixture of normal distributions. The objective function minimises total expected procurement and penalty costs, including holding, shortage, and over-order costs. The model is implemented in Python using the PuLP library and solved with the CBC solver. Compared to a deterministic baseline using average demand, the stochastic solution reduces expected total cost by 8.3% and decreases the standard deviation of total cost by 22.1% across out-of-sample test scenarios. The paper also examines how varying the shortage-to-holding cost ratio shifts the optimal supplier mix, finding that above a ratio of 4:1, dual sourcing from the two top-ranked suppliers becomes consistently preferable to single sourcing.

title: Quantifying Supply Chain Disruption Risk with a Combined Failure Mode and Stochastic Simulation Framework
abstract: Supply chain disruption events such as supplier insolvency, transport delays, and quality failures are difficult to capture with deterministic risk scores alone. This paper presents a hybrid framework that combines a modified Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) with Monte Carlo simulation to estimate the distribution of annual disruption costs for a multi-tier supply network. The case study involves a plastics processing manufacturer in Novi Sad with 11 first-tier suppliers and three second-tier nodes. FMEA severity, occurrence, and detectability scores are collected from 12 supply chain managers using structured questionnaires. These scores seed the probability distributions for individual failure events, and 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations generate an empirical cost distribution. The 95th percentile of simulated annual disruption cost is 18.4% higher than the deterministic point estimate used in the company's existing risk register. The framework identifies three suppliers whose individual contribution to tail risk exceeds their share of purchase volume, suggesting targeted mitigation actions such as dual qualification and safety stock increases. Limitations regarding the subjective basis of FMEA scores and their correlation structure are discussed.

title: Robust Supplier Selection under Interval-Valued Criteria Weights: A Min-Max Regret Formulation
abstract: When decision-makers cannot precisely specify the relative importance of evaluation criteria, using exact weights in multi-criteria supplier selection models can lead to solutions that perform poorly under alternative weight settings. This paper proposes a min-max regret model for supplier selection in which criteria weights are only known to lie within specified intervals, derived from a group of eight procurement professionals via an interactive questioning protocol. The model selects the supplier portfolio that minimises the maximum deviation from the optimal solution across all weight vectors within the defined intervals. The approach is applied to a dataset of 10 candidate suppliers for an agri-food company in Sombor, evaluated across six criteria. The robust solution differs from the deterministic weighted-sum solution in two out of five selected suppliers. Computational experiments show that the min-max regret formulation can be solved exactly for problems of this size within a few seconds using standard mixed-integer programming solvers. The paper includes a comparison with a minimax regret approach based on sampled weight vectors and discusses conditions under which the exact and approximate solutions agree.

title: Integrating Carbon Emission Penalties into Stochastic Supplier Selection: Evidence from the Serbian Food Processing Sector
abstract: Growing regulatory pressure on greenhouse gas emissions is beginning to affect procurement decisions in Serbian manufacturing. This paper extends a two-stage stochastic supplier selection model to incorporate a carbon emission penalty cost term, allowing procurement planners to evaluate the trade-off between economic and emission-related objectives under demand uncertainty. Emission factors per unit shipped are estimated for each supplier based on transport distance, modal split, and energy intensity data gathered through supplier questionnaires. Demand scenarios are constructed from 24 months of sales data for a pasta production company based near Novi Sad. The extended model is solved for 30, 50, and 100 scenario sets to assess solution stability. Results indicate that including a carbon penalty equivalent to 25 EUR per tonne of CO2 changes the preferred supplier in one out of four sourcing categories and increases expected total procurement cost by 2.1%. The paper also presents a Pareto frontier between expected cost and expected total emissions, computed by parametric variation of the carbon penalty, and identifies a range of penalty values within which the supplier portfolio remains unchanged, providing guidance for sensitivity to future carbon pricing.

title: Evaluating buffer sizing policies in unbalanced mixed-model lines through designed simulation experiments
abstract: Buffer sizing is a key design decision in mixed-model assembly that is often addressed heuristically. This paper uses a full-factorial simulation experiment to quantify the effect of buffer capacity, line imbalance level, and product-mix ratio on throughput and work-in-process inventory simultaneously. Experiments were conducted on a parameterised simulation model representing a six-station line with configurable imbalance (coefficient of variation of station workloads ranging from 0.05 to 0.35) and three product-mix scenarios. In total, 648 experimental conditions were evaluated, each replicated 30 times to achieve 95% confidence intervals of width below 2% of mean throughput. The results show that for imbalance levels above 0.20, buffer insertion at the first identified bottleneck upstream neighbour delivers more than 80% of the throughput gain achievable with unconstrained buffering, with a WIP cost two to three times lower than full buffering.

title: Seasonal Demand Asymmetry and Room Rate Optimisation in Small Pannonian Spa Hotels
abstract: This paper examines how small spa hotels along the Pannonian thermal belt adjust room rates in response to asymmetric seasonal demand signals. Using a panel dataset of 38 properties collected across four years (2006–2009), the study estimates a two-regime threshold regression model that distinguishes high-demand and shoulder-season pricing behaviour. Results show that managers systematically under-price during early shoulder periods, leaving an estimated 7–12% of potential revenue unrealised. A simulation exercise based on calibrated demand functions suggests that a simple rule-triggered rate fence—activated when forward occupancy crosses 55%—recovers approximately 9% of that gap without increasing cancellation rates. The paper contributes an empirical baseline for dynamic pricing adoption in a sub-regional market where yield management practice lags behind Western European counterparts.

title: Price Dispersion in Adriatic Coastal Accommodation: Evidence from an Online Travel Agency Database
abstract: Online travel agencies have made price dispersion in tourism accommodation highly visible to consumers, yet its structural determinants remain understudied in South-East European contexts. This study draws on a scraped dataset of 4,200 daily rate observations from a single mid-size online travel agency covering 112 Dalmatian coastal hotels during the summer seasons of 2008 and 2009. Quantile regression estimates reveal that price dispersion at the upper tail is driven primarily by star-rating heterogeneity and last-minute inventory clearance, while dispersion at the lower tail reflects competitive pressure from unlicensed accommodation. A price-concentration index constructed for 14 micro-destinations shows significant variation even within the same coastal stretch. The findings suggest that revenue managers in the region treat promotional discounting and peak-period premiums as largely independent decisions, which limits overall yield performance.

title: Consumer Willingness to Accept Dynamic Fares in Serbian Bus Tourism: A Contingent Valuation Study
abstract: Although dynamic pricing is standard in air travel, its adoption in overland coach tourism remains limited in the Western Balkans. This paper reports a contingent valuation study conducted with 620 respondents recruited at three major Serbian bus terminals. Respondents were presented with hypothetical fare scenarios that varied discount depth (5%, 15%, 25%), advance purchase window (1 day to 3 weeks), and service quality attributes. Ordered logit estimates indicate that willingness to accept variable fares rises sharply when discounts exceed 15% and when the purchase window is at least seven days. Respondents with prior air-travel experience show significantly higher acceptance across all scenarios. The study provides practical guidance for intercity coach operators considering revenue management systems and fills a gap in the empirical literature on non-aviation surface transport pricing in transition economies.

title: Measuring the Revenue Impact of Early Check-In Upselling in City Hotels: A Quasi-Experiment
abstract: Hotels in Serbian cities began introducing early check-in upselling programmes around 2011–2013, yet evidence on their net revenue contribution is sparse. Exploiting a natural experiment created when a Novi Sad hotel chain introduced a structured upselling script for front-desk staff in mid-2013 while two comparable properties delayed implementation, this study applies a difference-in-differences estimator to daily revenue per available room (RevPAR) data for a 28-month period. The treated properties show a statistically significant increase in ancillary revenue of approximately 4.2 EUR per occupied room, with no detectable displacement of room revenue. Heterogeneity analysis shows the effect is concentrated in leisure segments and disappears for corporate accounts managed under contracted rates. The study illustrates how relatively low-cost operational changes can complement algorithmic pricing tools.

title: Asymmetric Loss Functions in Hotel Demand Forecasting: Does Under-Forecasting Cost More?
abstract: Standard demand forecasting models used in hotel revenue management minimise mean squared error, implicitly treating over- and under-forecasting as equally costly. This paper argues that under-forecasting is typically more costly in rack-rate environments because forgone full-price sales are not recoverable. Using daily occupancy data from 17 hotels in Vojvodina over a three-year period, we fit ARIMA, exponential smoothing, and gradient-boosted regression tree models under both symmetric and asymmetric (LINEX) loss functions. Forecasting accuracy is evaluated via a revenue-weighted scoring rule calibrated from each property's actual rate structure. Results show that asymmetric loss specifications reduce average revenue loss by 1.8–3.4% relative to symmetric benchmarks, with the largest gains in properties with higher rate dispersion. The paper argues for routine integration of property-specific loss calibration into commercial property management systems.

title: Overbooking Limits Under Uncertain No-Show Rates: A Stochastic Programming Approach for Mid-Size Hotels
abstract: Determining safe overbooking limits is a classical problem in hotel revenue management, but most published solutions assume stable no-show distributions. This paper relaxes that assumption by modelling no-show rates as scenario-dependent random variables influenced by local events, weather anomalies, and booking-channel mix. A two-stage stochastic programme is formulated and solved for a representative mid-size hotel with 80–150 rooms, using data from eight properties in Novi Sad and Subotica over five years. The first stage sets overbooking limits before demand is observed; the second stage computes expected walking costs and revenue under 200 sampled scenarios. The model recommends limits that are on average 1.2 rooms lower than current practice, yet reduce expected walking costs by 18% due to better alignment with scenario-specific outcomes. A sensitivity analysis examines how results change as booking-channel volatility increases.

title: Dynamic Pricing in Agritourism: Balancing Capacity Constraints and Rural Community Expectations
abstract: Agritourism properties in Vojvodina operate under capacity constraints far tighter than urban hotels and serve communities where visible price discrimination may carry social costs. This book chapter synthesises 14 semi-structured interviews with agritourism operators and a discrete-choice experiment with 380 potential guests to assess the acceptability and revenue potential of demand-responsive pricing in this segment. Interview analysis identifies three adoption barriers: lack of forecasting skills, fear of negative word-of-mouth, and perceived incompatibility with the 'authentic rural' brand. The discrete-choice experiment shows that guests tolerate price premiums of up to 18% during peak agritourism weekends but penalise perceived arbitrariness by switching to competitors at premiums above 25%. The chapter concludes with a practical tiered pricing framework calibrated to these tolerance thresholds and compatible with simple spreadsheet management.

title: Reference Price Effects and Perceived Fairness Under Algorithmic Hotel Pricing: An Experimental Study
abstract: Revenue management systems can generate rapid within-day rate changes that expose consumers to stark price anchoring effects. This paper reports two controlled online experiments (n = 410 and n = 385) in which Serbian and Hungarian participants evaluated hotel offers under manipulated sequences of displayed price histories. Experiment 1 tests whether an upward reference price trajectory increases willingness to book relative to a flat or declining sequence, holding the current price constant. Experiment 2 introduces a stated 'algorithm-based pricing' explanation and measures its effect on perceived fairness. Results confirm a significant reference price anchoring effect (Cohen's d = 0.41) but show that algorithm attribution reduces perceived fairness scores by 0.6 points on a 7-point scale. No significant moderation by hotel-booking experience is found. The study has implications for how revenue management systems should communicate price rationale to end consumers.

title: Revenue Management Adoption Among Small and Medium Hotels in Serbia: A Technology Acceptance Survey
abstract: Commercial revenue management systems are widely used by international hotel chains but their penetration among independently owned small and medium hotels in Serbia remains unclear. This paper reports findings from a structured postal and online survey of 214 hotel managers conducted in 2020, using an adapted technology acceptance model supplemented with dimensions for perceived complexity and data availability. Structural equation modelling confirms that perceived usefulness and top-management support are the two strongest predictors of adoption intention, together explaining 48% of variance. Perceived data complexity acts as a significant barrier, particularly for properties with fewer than 30 rooms. Only 19% of respondents currently use any systematic revenue management tool beyond manually adjusted rate sheets. The paper identifies targeted training needs and recommends a simplified diagnostic scorecard for hotels evaluating entry-level systems.

title: Personalised Pricing and GDPR Constraints: Revenue Management Implications for European Hotels
abstract: Personalised pricing—setting individual rates based on inferred consumer willingness to pay—offers revenue managers potentially large gains but conflicts with European data protection rules under the GDPR. This paper develops a formal model of constrained personalised pricing in which the hotel revenue manager maximises expected revenue subject to a data minimisation constraint that limits the number of consumer attributes usable in rate discrimination. The model is parameterised using conjoint survey data from 502 hotel guests in four countries (Serbia, Hungary, Romania, Austria) and solved numerically. Results show that even a two-attribute rate model (trip purpose, booking channel) recovers 61% of the theoretical full-information revenue gain, while satisfying a plausible interpretation of GDPR data minimisation. The study offers a practical framework that legal and revenue management departments can use jointly to design compliant personalisation strategies.

title: Competitive Price Monitoring via Web Scraping: Accuracy, Latency, and Ethical Boundaries for Revenue Managers
abstract: Automated competitive rate monitoring has become a standard component of hotel revenue management, yet the quality of scraped data and the ethical limits of scraping practice receive limited systematic attention in the hospitality literature. This paper conducts a controlled accuracy audit in which rates retrieved by a purpose-built scraping prototype are compared to rates confirmed through direct booking for 48 hotels in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Szeged over a 90-day window totalling 12,960 rate observations. Scraping latency—the delay between a price change and its detection—averages 4.2 hours across the sample, with tails exceeding 18 hours for properties using client-side rendering. Data accuracy is 94.7% at the headline rate level but falls to 81.3% when tax-inclusive rates are required. The paper also reviews applicable terms-of-service restrictions and Serbian and EU legal precedents relevant to automated data collection, providing a compliance checklist for revenue management practitioners.

title: Comparative LCA of On-Premises and Hosted E-Mail Service Delivery: A Case Study from Central Europe
abstract: This study applies attributional life-cycle assessment to compare the environmental burdens of operating an on-premises e-mail server infrastructure against a co-located hosted service at a regional data centre. System boundaries span hardware manufacture, operational energy consumption, cooling, and end-of-life treatment. Primary energy data were collected from two organisations in Vojvodina over a twelve-month measurement campaign; background processes were modelled with the ecoinvent 3.4 database. The functional unit was defined as delivery of one million e-mail transactions. Results indicate that the hosted scenario reduces global warming potential by 34% and cumulative energy demand by 28% relative to on-premises operation, driven principally by higher power usage effectiveness at the co-location facility. Eutrophication and land use impacts, however, are marginally higher in the hosted scenario due to longer hardware logistics chains. Sensitivity analyses on grid electricity mix show that results are robust across a ±15% variation in renewable energy share. The study provides empirical baseline data for regional ICT procurement policy.

title: End-of-Life Flows for Enterprise Networking Equipment in Serbia: A Material Flow Analysis Perspective
abstract: Enterprise networking hardware—routers, switches, and access points—represents a growing but poorly characterised component of national e-waste streams. This study combines material flow analysis with a targeted survey of 48 Serbian companies to quantify annual discards of networking equipment and to map current collection, refurbishment, and disposal pathways. Results estimate that approximately 1,200 tonnes of such equipment reached end-of-life in Serbia in 2015, of which roughly 38% entered informal recycling channels. Copper, aluminium, and printed circuit board fractions are quantified per equipment category. Linkage to life-cycle inventory data allows a preliminary estimate that informal processing generates 1.7 kg CO₂-equivalent per kilogram of equipment compared with 0.9 kg under formalised dismantling. The study highlights a gap between producer responsibility legislation and actual collection infrastructure and recommends harmonisation with EU Directive 2012/19/EU as a policy priority.

title: Carbon Accounting for a National Broadband Expansion Programme: Scope Boundaries and Data Quality Considerations
abstract: National broadband infrastructure investments are frequently justified on economic and social grounds, yet their life-cycle carbon costs remain poorly quantified. This conference paper presents a carbon accounting framework applied to a hypothetical 10,000 km fibre-optic network rollout representative of conditions in South-East Europe. The framework distinguishes capital emissions (cable manufacture, civil works, equipment production) from operational emissions (active node energy, cooling, maintenance) across a 20-year service life. Using regionalised electricity grid factors and construction activity data, capital emissions are estimated at 48,000 tCO₂e and annual operational emissions at 3,200 tCO₂e. The paper evaluates the sensitivity of results to functional unit choice—kilometre of fibre versus connected household versus gigabyte transported—demonstrating that the metric selected can shift the apparent emission intensity by a factor of four. Recommendations are provided for consistent scope definition in future national infrastructure environmental assessments.

title: Life-Cycle Environmental Assessment of a Hyperscale Data Centre Under Different Energy Scenarios for the Western Balkans
abstract: This paper models a hypothetical 20 MW hyperscale data centre facility under four electricity supply scenarios relevant to the Western Balkans region: current grid mix dominated by lignite, a 30% renewable penetration scenario, a 60% renewable scenario, and direct power purchase agreement with a solar photovoltaic park. LCA is conducted in accordance with ISO 14040/44 using SimaPro 9.1 and ecoinvent 3.7, covering ReCiPe 2016 midpoint categories. Hardware manufacturing contributes between 18% and 47% of life-cycle global warming potential depending on the scenario, illustrating that upstream embodied emissions become proportionally dominant as operational energy decarbonises. The analysis also quantifies water consumption at 1.4 litres per kWh of IT load under evaporative cooling. Results are compared with published data for Western European and Nordic facilities, showing a 2.1- to 3.4-fold higher operational emission intensity for current Balkan grid conditions. The study is intended to inform siting and energy procurement decisions for data centre operators entering the regional market.

title: Occupational Exposure Assessment in ICT Hardware Refurbishment Workshops: Particulate Matter and VOC Monitoring
abstract: Workers in informal and semi-formal ICT hardware refurbishment operations may be exposed to hazardous particulate matter and volatile organic compounds released during desoldering, cleaning, and component testing. This study reports results from a twelve-week monitoring campaign in four workshops in Novi Sad, measuring PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations alongside a VOC panel including benzene, toluene, and xylene isomers. Personal and stationary sampling methods were compared. Mean personal PM2.5 exposure was 68 µg/m³ across measured shifts, exceeding the Serbian occupational limit of 50 µg/m³ in two of four facilities. Benzene concentrations remained below occupational exposure limits in all cases, though toluene peaked at 1.8 times the limit during intensive desoldering tasks. The study recommends targeted local exhaust ventilation and procedural controls and discusses the relevance of findings to occupational safety frameworks under EU Directive 2017/164/EU, to which Serbian legislation is being aligned.

title: Scope 3 Emission Reporting in the Serbian ICT Sector: Current Practice and Methodological Gaps
abstract: This book chapter examines the state of corporate greenhouse gas reporting, with particular attention to Scope 3 categories, among ICT companies registered in Serbia. A content analysis was conducted on 31 sustainability and annual reports published between 2018 and 2022. Findings indicate that 19 companies report Scope 1 and 2 emissions, while only seven make any attempt to quantify Scope 3 categories; of these, purchased goods and services and use of sold products are the most frequently reported, yet methodological documentation is sparse in most cases. The chapter maps reported practices against the GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain Standard and identifies recurrent issues: inconsistent system boundary definitions, reliance on spend-based rather than activity-based factors, and absence of uncertainty quantification. The chapter concludes with a set of practical recommendations intended for practitioners and for national environmental agencies considering mandatory reporting frameworks.

title: Moisture sorption isotherms of fluting and liner grades commonly used in Southeast European corrugated board production
abstract: Moisture sorption isotherms were measured for five commercial fluting and liner grades supplied by mills in Serbia, Croatia, and Romania. Samples were conditioned at relative humidity levels of 20, 35, 50, 65, 75, and 90 % at 23 °C using a static saturated-salt method inside sealed desiccator chambers. Equilibrium moisture content was determined gravimetrically after 72-hour conditioning intervals. The data were fitted to the Guggenheim–Anderson–de Boer (GAB) model; fitted parameters showed that recycled fluting grades exhibited notably higher monolayer moisture contents (between 4.8 and 6.1 g per 100 g dry fibre) compared to virgin kraft liner (3.2–3.9 g per 100 g dry fibre). Hysteresis loops were pronounced for all grades at intermediate humidity, with adsorption-branch equilibrium moisture contents exceeding desorption values by 0.8–1.6 percentage points. The results provide grade-specific input data for subsequent mechanical performance models. The paper also discusses practical implications for storage conditions in corrugated board plants in continental climates with wide seasonal humidity variation.

title: Effect of relative humidity on the edge-crush resistance of single-wall corrugated board: a systematic study across four flute profiles
abstract: Edge-crush test (ECT) values were measured for A-, B-, C-, and E-flute single-wall corrugated boards conditioned at five relative humidity levels (33, 50, 65, 75, and 85 % RH) at 23 °C. For each flute type, three commercial board grades were tested, yielding 60 distinct board–humidity combinations. Conditioning was performed in a Klimatest KK-400 climate chamber for 48 hours prior to testing. ECT was performed in the machine direction and the cross-machine direction separately. Results indicated that ECT values declined monotonically with increasing RH for all grades and flute types; the steepest relative drop (42 % from 33 % to 85 % RH) was observed for B-flute boards with 100 % recycled furnish. A-flute boards with semi-chemical fluting showed the smallest relative decline (28 %). The relationship between RH and ECT was well described by a power-law expression for each grade with R² values exceeding 0.97. Interaction effects between flute geometry and furnish type were statistically significant at the 5 % level.

title: Crease depth and rule geometry as determinants of folding stiffness in moisture-conditioned solid bleached sulphate cartonboard
abstract: Folding stiffness of creased solid bleached sulphate (SBS) cartonboard was measured as a function of crease depth and male-rule tip radius across five RH levels (30–80 % RH). Boards of 300 and 350 g/m² were creased on a bench creasing machine equipped with interchangeable male rules with tip radii of 0.15, 0.25, and 0.40 mm; crease depths ranged from 0.05 to 0.25 mm in 0.05 mm steps. A purpose-built crease-stiffness rig recorded bending moment as a function of fold angle from 0 to 180°. At 50 % RH, peak bending moment increased by 18 % when tip radius was reduced from 0.40 to 0.15 mm at identical crease depth. At 80 % RH, moisture-plasticised fibres resulted in peak bending moments 31–37 % lower than at 50 % RH across all crease geometries. The interaction between crease depth and RH was non-linear: deeper creases provided proportionally more benefit at low RH than at high RH. Fractographic SEM images of cross-sections at selected conditions confirmed fibre-bundle fracture patterns consistent with the mechanical data.

title: Modelling Z-directional compression of corrugated board under controlled humidity using a sandwich-layer finite element approach
abstract: A finite element model of single-wall corrugated board in the Z-direction (flat-crush) loading configuration was developed and validated against laboratory flat-crush test data collected at 33, 50, 65, and 80 % RH. The model treated the fluting medium as a series of sinusoidal arch elements and the two liners as orthotropic shell elements. Elastic moduli and in-plane Poisson ratios for each layer were derived from RH-dependent tensile test data gathered during the experimental phase. Material stiffness functions were incorporated as polynomial RH-dependent scalar modifiers calibrated against 180 individual test specimens. Model predictions agreed with measured flat-crush values within ±6.5 % across all humidity levels. Sensitivity analysis indicated that the elastic modulus of the fluting medium in the Z-direction was the dominant parameter governing flat-crush resistance, accounting for 61 % of model variance. The model is implemented in open-source finite element software and the input scripts are made available for use by other researchers.

title: Seasonal humidity variation in corrugated board converting plants in the Pannonian region: field measurement and implications for box compression strength
abstract: Ambient relative humidity and temperature were logged continuously for 14 months at four corrugated board converting plants located in northern Serbia and southern Hungary. Loggers were placed at seven positions per plant: board storage, corrugator pre-heater zone, slitter–scorer area, flexo printer–slotter, flat-sheet stack, dispatch warehouse, and outdoors. Mean daily RH in board storage varied from 34 % in winter to 71 % in summer with peaks reaching 82 %. The temperature–humidity data were correlated with weekly box compression test (BCT) records provided by the plants. A statistically significant negative correlation (Pearson r = −0.74, p < 0.001) was observed between mean storage-area RH and BCT values aggregated weekly. Each 10-percentage-point increase in storage RH was associated with a 4.2 kN decline in mean BCT for a standard RSC box of 600 × 400 × 400 mm. The study quantifies a practically relevant seasonal variation that is rarely accounted for in box-design calculations used in the region.

title: Starch surface sizing and its effect on creasing performance under high-humidity conditions in recycled linerboard
abstract: The influence of oxidised starch surface sizing on the creasing and folding behaviour of recycled linerboard was examined at 50 and 80 % RH. Linerboard samples of 150 g/m² basis weight were produced on a pilot paper machine and surface-sized to five coat-weight levels (0, 1.5, 3.0, 4.5, and 6.0 g/m²). Crease quality was assessed using a line-scan optical profilometer to measure crease-channel depth uniformity and shoulder-crack density. Folding stiffness was measured as described in TAPPI T556. At 80 % RH, samples with 4.5 g/m² starch coating retained 82 % of their 50 % RH folding stiffness, compared to 67 % retention for unsized reference samples. Increasing coat weight beyond 4.5 g/m² yielded no further statistically significant improvement at either humidity level. Scanning electron microscopy of the crease shoulders showed that surface sizing reduced inter-fibre debonding by maintaining fibre-to-fibre bonding through the crease zone under humid conditions.

title: Anisotropy of tensile stiffness orientation angle in corrugated board liner as a function of ambient humidity
abstract: The tensile stiffness orientation (TSO) angle, which represents the alignment of dominant fibre orientation relative to the machine direction, was measured for four commercial kraft liner grades conditioned at 33, 50, 65, 75, and 85 % RH. TSO was determined using an ultrasonic stiffness measurement device at 15-degree intervals through 0–90 degrees. At 50 % RH, TSO angles ranged from 2.1° to 5.8° across the four grades, consistent with well-controlled papermaking. Conditioning at 85 % RH increased TSO angle variability across-web by a factor of 1.4–1.9 compared to 50 % RH, indicating humidity-induced differential swelling that skewed the effective fibre angle. Corrugated board produced from liner exhibiting higher TSO angle shifts showed measurably reduced ECT in the cross-machine direction, with losses of 6–11 % relative to 50 % RH reference boards. The findings suggest that TSO monitoring could serve as a practical incoming-goods quality indicator in humid climates.
venue: Packaging and Converting Science

title: Repeatability of crease geometry on an industrial rotary die-cutter: a 48-hour continuous monitoring study under varying plant humidity
abstract: Crease geometry repeatability was monitored on a rotary die-cutter running a standard 0201-style corrugated box blank over a 48-hour production shift at a converting plant in Novi Sad. Crease channel depth, width, and shoulder symmetry were measured on samples taken every 30 minutes using a contact profilometer; a total of 96 sample sets, each comprising 20 blanks, were collected. Ambient RH and temperature inside the plant were logged at 5-minute intervals. Analysis of variance showed that RH accounted for 38 % of the variance in crease channel depth and 44 % of the variance in shoulder asymmetry across the monitoring period. Machine-speed and substrate-thickness variations were secondary factors. Shoulder asymmetry increased markedly when RH exceeded 68 %, consistent with differential in-plane swelling of the two liners. The plant's existing die-cutting matrix degraded measurably over the 48 hours, and the interaction between matrix wear and humidity was statistically significant, suggesting that matrix replacement intervals should be shortened during high-humidity periods.

title: Water vapour transmission rate of corrugated board as a predictor of in-box equilibrium humidity and secondary packaging performance
abstract: The water vapour transmission rate (WVTR) of eight commercial corrugated board grades was measured using the cup method at 23 °C and 85/50 % RH gradient. WVTR values ranged from 420 to 1140 g/(m²·day), reflecting large differences in liner furnish and basis weight. Sealed RSC boxes assembled from each grade were placed in a climate-controlled room set to 85 % RH and the interior humidity was logged over 96 hours. Interior RH equilibration time was positively correlated with WVTR (Pearson r = 0.88); boards with WVTR below 550 g/(m²·day) maintained interior RH below 65 % for more than 72 hours. Secondary packaging performance was assessed by measuring BCT of the boxes after 24, 48, and 72 hours of 85 % RH exposure. BCT loss at 72 hours ranged from 19 % to 41 % across grades and was strongly correlated with time-integrated interior RH (r = 0.91). The results suggest WVTR measurement as a cost-effective screening parameter for selecting corrugated grades for humid distribution environments.

title: Influence of Emulsion Over Mesh Ratio on Edge Acuity and Sawtoothing in Screen-Printed Conductive Lines Below 200 µm Width
abstract: The emulsion over mesh (EOM) ratio — the thickness of emulsion above the mesh surface relative to the mesh thickness — affects both the seal quality during printing and the edge definition of fine printed lines. This work systematically varies EOM from 10% to 40% for a 150-thread/cm polyester mesh, printing a 60 wt% silver paste to produce nominal 100, 150, and 200 µm wide lines on FR4 substrates. Line edge profiles were extracted from optical microscope images at 200× magnification and analysed for mean sawtooth amplitude and spatial frequency. Lower EOM values (10–15%) produced higher sawtooth amplitude (mean 18 µm) but sharper mean edge position accuracy. Higher EOM (35–40%) reduced sawtooth amplitude to below 7 µm but introduced systematic line width broadening of 8–12 µm. Deposit thickness measured by profilometry was 10–15% greater at higher EOM due to the extended ink reservoir. A practical optimum at EOM 20–25% is identified, balancing edge acuity against thickness consistency for lines below 200 µm.

title: A watchdog-based self-recovery scheme for 802.15.4 sensor nodes in unattended deployments
abstract: Unattended wireless sensor nodes in field deployments frequently enter irrecoverable software states due to memory corruption, peripheral lockup, or stack overflow caused by transient power events. This paper presents a layered watchdog architecture implemented on an ATmega128RFA1 platform in which three independent timers supervise the operating system scheduler, the radio driver, and the analog front-end sequencer separately. When any tier detects a violation of its expected heartbeat window, a graduated recovery procedure is executed that avoids full device reset in roughly 74 percent of observed fault cases, thereby preserving the sensor's runtime context. The scheme was evaluated over a 90-day outdoor deployment of 18 nodes sampling soil moisture at 10-minute intervals. Mean time between unrecoverable resets increased from 11.3 days in the baseline configuration to 61.7 days with the proposed architecture. Current overhead introduced by the additional supervision circuitry was measured at 38 µA in active mode, representing less than 2 percent of total node consumption. The design is described in sufficient detail to be reproduced on comparable 8-bit and 16-bit microcontroller families.

title: On-node detection of resistive humidity sensor drift using recursive least-squares residual monitoring
abstract: Capacitive and resistive humidity sensors used in long-term field deployments exhibit systematic drift attributable to membrane contamination, mechanical stress, and UV degradation of the sensing polymer. This study examines drift detection using a recursive least-squares estimator running on a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M0+ microcontroller with 64 kB RAM. The estimator maintains a sliding 72-hour model of sensor behaviour and raises a diagnostic flag when the standardised prediction residual exceeds a threshold calibrated to yield a 5 percent false-alarm rate under clean operating conditions. The method was validated against a controlled ageing experiment in which 24 SHT31-compatible sensors were exposed to accelerated UV and humidity cycling; 21 of 22 drift events exceeding 3 percent RH offset were detected within 8 hours of onset. Computational cost was benchmarked at 1.2 ms per update cycle at 48 MHz, consuming negligible battery capacity relative to the radio subsystem. The paper includes a discussion of threshold sensitivity as a function of sampling interval and recommends a minimum of 15-minute sampling for reliable operation.

title: Energy-aware retransmission scheduling for IoT nodes operating on solar-harvested power under partial shading conditions
abstract: Solar energy harvesting for IoT nodes in temperate climates is complicated by persistent partial shading from vegetation, cloud cover, and seasonal sun angle variation. This chapter reviews energy buffering and transmission scheduling strategies applicable to nodes where the harvester output drops to 10–40 percent of rated capacity for multi-hour periods. A discrete-time predictive controller is presented that adjusts the uplink reporting interval and transmission power based on a rolling 24-hour energy budget estimated from a small supercapacitor voltage sensor. Simulations using one-year solar irradiance data from three sites in the Pannonian Plain show that the controller maintains the reporting duty cycle above 85 percent of the target rate throughout the year compared with 61 percent for a fixed-interval baseline. The chapter also covers hardware design guidelines for solar panel placement and MPPT circuit selection, and discusses the trade-off between supercapacitor capacity, leakage current, and cold-start reliability in sub-zero conditions.

title: Multi-metric data quality scoring at the gateway for heterogeneous agricultural IoT deployments
abstract: Aggregation gateways in agricultural IoT networks receive streams from sensors operating under different power regimes, communication protocols, and environmental exposures. This paper proposes a gateway-side data quality scoring framework that assigns each incoming measurement a composite score based on four sub-metrics: timeliness (elapsed time since last message relative to expected interval), signal plausibility (z-score against a rolling peer-group distribution), battery state estimate, and historical reliability index derived from 30-day uptime statistics. The framework was implemented in Python 3.9 on a Raspberry Pi 4 gateway serving 61 nodes in a test vineyard in Fruška Gora, processing approximately 8,700 messages per day. Over a 5-month evaluation period, the composite score correctly flagged 93 of 97 manually confirmed measurement anomalies and produced 11 false positives. Score computation added a mean latency of 4.1 ms per message at gateway level. The scoring metadata is forwarded alongside raw measurements to a central time-series database, enabling downstream analytics to weight observations accordingly. Integration steps for two commercial farm management platforms are documented.

title: Firmware update reliability over NB-IoT in low-signal rural environments: a field study
abstract: Over-the-air firmware updates (FOTA) are essential for maintaining security and functionality of deployed IoT nodes but are poorly characterised in weak-signal rural cellular conditions. This study documents 1,840 FOTA sessions conducted across 46 NB-IoT nodes installed at distances of 8–22 km from the nearest base station in the southern Bačka region of Serbia. Update payloads ranged from 48 to 192 kB and were delivered using a block-based transfer protocol with configurable block size and retry budget. Session success rate was 81.4 percent without adaptive configuration and rose to 94.6 percent when block size was reduced from 512 to 128 bytes and the retry budget was tripled. Failed sessions were traced primarily to receive-window mismatches during peak network load periods. Energy cost per successful update was measured between 0.9 and 3.4 mAh depending on retry overhead. The paper quantifies the dependency of success rate on RSRP and presents a simple heuristic for selecting block size based on a short link probe transmitted before each update session.

title: Characterising the interaction between cellular network congestion and duty-cycle regulation in dense IoT deployments: a simulation and measurement study
abstract: When hundreds of IoT nodes sharing a single NB-IoT cell simultaneously enter their reporting window, uplink congestion increases packet delay and loss in ways that interact nonlinearly with node-level duty-cycle power management. This preprint reports a combined simulation and measurement study: a system-level LTE-M/NB-IoT simulator was configured to match the topology of a 312-node crop monitoring network in Srem, and its congestion behaviour was cross-validated against 8 weeks of gateway-side timestamps showing mean delay growth from 1.2 s to 14.7 s during morning reporting peaks. The simulator was then used to evaluate four transmission-window randomisation strategies across node densities from 50 to 500 nodes per cell. A jitter-and-backoff strategy combining a randomised initial delay drawn from a 0–300 s uniform window with an exponential backoff on contention reduced 99th-percentile delay from 41 s to 8 s and cut failed transmissions by 63 percent at 400 nodes per cell. Interaction effects with solar harvesting schedules are discussed and a recommended configuration table is provided for deployment engineers.

title: Factor structure of the Maslach Burnout Inventory–General Survey in a Serbian healthcare sample
abstract: This study examined the factor structure of the Maslach Burnout Inventory–General Survey (MBI-GS) in a sample of 412 healthcare workers employed in two public hospitals in Vojvodina. Confirmatory factor analysis was used to compare four competing structural models: a one-factor model, a correlated three-factor model, a bifactor model, and a hierarchical model. Model fit was evaluated using CFI, RMSEA, and SRMR. The correlated three-factor model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.063, SRMR = 0.057), consistent with the original MBI-GS structure, though modification indices suggested correlated residuals between two exhaustion items. Internal consistency was satisfactory across all three subscales (α = 0.78–0.87). Convergent validity was supported through significant positive associations with emotional demands and negative associations with work engagement. The results suggest that the MBI-GS is a usable measure in Serbian healthcare contexts, with minor caveats for the exhaustion subscale.

title: Adapting the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale to Serbian: translation, factor structure, and initial norm data
abstract: The study describes the adaptation of the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-17) into Serbian and the examination of its psychometric properties across two independent samples totalling 684 employed adults recruited via workplace contacts in Novi Sad and Belgrade. Translation followed a forward–backward procedure with two bilingual psychologists and a reconciliation panel. Confirmatory factor analysis tested one-factor, two-factor, and three-factor solutions. The three-factor model (vigour, dedication, absorption) provided the best fit (CFI = 0.96, RMSEA = 0.055), replicating the original Dutch structure. Cronbach's alpha ranged from 0.81 to 0.88 across subscales. Preliminary norm data are reported by gender and occupational sector. Convergent validity was established against a Serbian version of the Job Satisfaction Scale (r = 0.41–0.58). Limitations include a convenience sampling strategy and restricted representation of manual occupations.

title: Measurement invariance of an occupational stress scale across gender and employment sector in Serbia
abstract: This study tested measurement invariance of a 20-item occupational stress questionnaire developed for Serbian-speaking populations across four groups defined by gender (women/men) and employment sector (public/private), using a sample of 891 employed adults. Multi-group confirmatory factor analysis proceeded through configural, metric, and scalar invariance steps following the Vandenberg and Lance protocol. Full metric invariance was supported for all four groups; however, scalar invariance was only partial, with two item intercepts differing significantly between public and private sector employees. Partial scalar invariance implies that latent mean comparisons between sectors require caution. Effect sizes for non-invariant intercepts were small (ΔCFI < 0.01). The two-factor structure of the instrument (demands and control) was confirmed in all groups. Implications for cross-group comparisons in organisational research using self-report stress measures are discussed, with particular attention to the public sector context in post-transition economies.

title: Psychometric properties of a brief perceived organisational support scale in ICT sector employees in Serbia
abstract: Perceived organisational support (POS) has been extensively studied internationally, but its measurement in the Serbian ICT sector remains unexamined. This study evaluated a 8-item short form of the Survey of Perceived Organizational Support in a sample of 267 software developers and project managers employed at technology companies in Novi Sad and Belgrade. Confirmatory factor analysis confirmed a one-factor structure (CFI = 0.97, RMSEA = 0.051). Internal consistency was high (α = 0.91; ω = 0.92). Significant positive correlations with job satisfaction (r = 0.52) and organisational commitment (r = 0.44) supported convergent validity. Discriminant validity from a turnover intentions measure was confirmed. Additionally, differential item functioning by remote versus on-site work arrangement was tested using the Mantel–Haenszel procedure; no statistically significant DIF was detected. The results support the use of this short POS form in applied HR assessment contexts within the Serbian ICT sector.

title: Response format effects on occupational wellbeing scale scores: comparing 5-point and 7-point Likert formats in a within-subjects design
abstract: The choice of response format is a practical measurement decision with potential consequences for scale reliability, factor structure, and score distributions, yet it is rarely examined systematically in occupational psychology. This study used a counterbalanced within-subjects design with 186 employed adults to compare 5-point and 7-point Likert formats on 24 items drawn from the OWI-SR occupational wellbeing inventory. Participants completed both formats two weeks apart. Confirmatory factor analyses in each condition replicated the four-factor structure of the OWI-SR in both formats. Reliability estimates were marginally higher for the 7-point format (average α difference = 0.03), but the difference was not statistically significant at p < 0.05. Score distributions showed slightly greater variance under the 7-point format. Latent means did not differ significantly between formats after accounting for carryover effects. Practical guidance for researchers choosing between formats in organisational survey research is provided, with emphasis on context and respondent literacy.

title: Psihodinamska formulacija slučaja u kontekstu graničnog poremećaja ličnosti: pregled pristupa strukturisanoj proceni
abstract: Ovaj pregledni rad sistematizuje metode strukturisane psihodinamske formulacije slučaja primenjene u istraživanjima graničnog poremećaja ličnosti (GPO) objavljenim između 2000. i 2018. godine. Analizirano je 34 relevantne studije pronađene pretragom baza PsycINFO, PubMed i CENTRAL. Utvrđeno je da se u većini studija koriste tri osnovna konstrukta — objektni odnosi, odbrambeni mehanizmi i identitetska difuzija — ali da su operacionalizacije ovih konstrukata međusobno nekonzistentne. Svega 14 od 34 studije izveštava o inter-rater pouzdanosti, što ograničava poređenje nalaza. Predlažu se minimalni standardi izveštavanja IRR vrednosti u budućim istraživanjima GPO, kao i smernice za harmonizaciju instrumenata u regionalnim multicentričnim studijama.

title: Effect of screw element configuration on granule size and friability in continuous twin-screw wet granulation of microcrystalline cellulose–lactose blends
abstract: This study examined how the number and angular offset of kneading elements in a Thermo Fisher Pharma 11 twin-screw granulator affect granule size distribution and friability of a 70:30 microcrystalline cellulose–lactose monohydrate blend. Six screw configurations were tested at a fixed feed rate of 2 kg/h, a barrel temperature of 25 °C, and liquid-to-solid ratios (L/S) of 0.20, 0.25, and 0.30 w/w. Granule size was characterised by laser diffraction (d10, d50, d90) and sieve analysis; friability was measured by a Roche friabilator at 100 rotations. Increasing the number of kneading zones from two to four reduced d50 from 412 µm to 278 µm at L/S 0.25, while friability decreased from 1.8% to 0.9%. Response surface modelling explained 87% of d50 variance. An interaction between kneading element stagger angle (30° vs. 60°) and L/S was statistically significant (p < 0.01), producing granules with notably broader size distributions at 60° stagger combined with L/S 0.30. The results indicate that kneading zone geometry is a primary lever for targeting a d50 between 250 and 350 µm without adjusting liquid addition rate.

title: Near-infrared spectroscopy calibration for in-line moisture monitoring during continuous twin-screw wet granulation
abstract: A partial least squares (PLS) calibration model was developed for real-time moisture content prediction of granules exiting a twin-screw granulator, using a fibre-optic NIR probe mounted at the barrel exit. Calibration samples (n = 84) were collected at moisture levels between 3.5% and 18.2% w/w, verified gravimetrically by loss on drying at 105 °C. Spectra were acquired in the 1100–2500 nm range at 2 nm resolution; pre-processing included standard normal variate transformation and first-derivative Savitzky–Golay smoothing (window 11, second polynomial order). The final four-latent-variable PLS model achieved a root mean square error of cross-validation (RMSECV) of 0.41% w/w and an RMSEP of 0.48% w/w on an independent test set (n = 21). Model performance was stable across two granule formulations (ibuprofen–MCC and paracetamol–MCC) and three screw speeds (200, 400, 600 rpm). Moisture predictions correlated well with downstream fluid-bed dryer inlet settings, suggesting that the model could support feed-forward dryer control in a future integrated line.

title: Potentially inappropriate medications in elderly outpatients attending general practice in the South Pannonian region: application of the Beers 2012 criteria
abstract: Applying the 2012 American Geriatrics Society Beers criteria to a prospective cohort of 389 community-dwelling patients aged 70 or older attending general practice clinics in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin, this study assessed the frequency and predictors of potentially inappropriate medication (PIM) prescribing. Medication data were collected through structured interviews and cross-checked against dispensing records over a six-week period in 2013. At least one PIM was identified in 38.6% of patients; benzodiazepines (prescribed in 19.4%) and first-generation antihistamines (11.3%) were the most prevalent. Polypharmacy status was significantly associated with PIM presence (adjusted OR 3.07, 95% CI 2.01–4.71). Patients with dementia or depression were at elevated risk. The study underlines the practical utility of Beers criteria in a primary care setting in the Western Balkans, where formal deprescribing programmes remain absent.

title: Drug interaction risk across the primary-to-secondary care interface: findings from a linked electronic health record study in Vojvodina
abstract: Using linked outpatient and inpatient electronic health record data from the Health Centre of Novi Sad and the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina for the period 2014–2016, this study quantified the change in clinically relevant drug interaction risk when elderly patients (≥65 years, n=1,043) were admitted to hospital or returned to community care. Interaction risk was scored using the SFINX interaction classification system adapted for the Serbian drug formulary. Mean interaction risk score increased significantly on admission (from 4.2 to 6.8, p<0.001) and remained elevated at discharge (6.1). Cardiac glycosides combined with loop diuretics and warfarin combined with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs represented the most prevalent high-severity pairs. Patients admitted via emergency pathways had 1.8 times higher interaction burden than elective admissions. The study demonstrates the feasibility of using linked routinely collected data for pharmacovigilance at a regional level in Serbia.

title: Polypharmacy and frailty in community-dwelling older adults: a cross-sectional analysis from the Vojvodina Aging and Health Study
abstract: This analysis used data from the Vojvodina Aging and Health Study, a multicentre cross-sectional survey of adults aged 70 and over living in the community (n=724, five municipalities in the Vojvodina region, data collected 2018–2019). Frailty was assessed using the Fried phenotype criteria; medication data were obtained from dispensing records. Polypharmacy was present in 61.2% of participants and was significantly associated with frailty after adjustment for age, sex, and comorbidity (adjusted OR 2.61, 95% CI 1.84–3.70). Hyperpolypharmacy was associated with an approximately threefold increase in frailty odds (OR 3.14, 95% CI 1.97–5.01). Among drug classes, anticholinergic agents and sedatives showed the strongest independent associations with frailty components, particularly exhaustion and low grip strength. The findings support integration of polypharmacy review into frailty screening programmes in primary care settings in the region.

title: Anticholinergic burden and cognitive decline in elderly patients transitioning from hospital to home: a six-month longitudinal study
abstract: Anticholinergic medications are frequently prescribed to elderly patients and have been associated with cognitive deterioration. This six-month prospective longitudinal study followed 211 patients aged 65 or older discharged from internal medicine wards to home care in Novi Sad (2020–2021). Anticholinergic burden was quantified at discharge and at one- and six-month follow-up using the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale. Cognitive function was assessed with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) at the same time points. Mean ACB score at discharge was 3.4 (SD 1.9); 44.1% of patients had an ACB score of 3 or higher. A one-unit increase in ACB score at discharge was associated with a 0.9-point decline in MoCA score at six months (β = −0.87, 95% CI −1.31 to −0.43, p<0.001), independent of baseline cognitive status and comorbidities. Bladder antimuscarinics and tricyclic antidepressants were the most common contributors to high ACB scores. The study provides quantitative support for prioritising anticholinergic deprescribing at discharge.

title: Structured medication review by clinical pharmacists at hospital admission: a pragmatic controlled trial in an internal medicine setting
abstract: This pragmatic controlled trial assessed whether structured medication review conducted by a clinical pharmacist at hospital admission reduces clinically significant drug interactions in elderly inpatients. Patients aged 65 or older admitted to two internal medicine wards at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina were allocated to intervention (pharmacist-led structured review with physician feedback, n=148) or usual care (n=152) according to admission day. The primary outcome was the number of clinically significant drug interaction pairs at 72 hours post-admission, classified using the SFINX system. At 72 hours, the intervention group had a mean of 1.9 interaction pairs compared with 3.4 in the control group (mean difference −1.5, 95% CI −2.1 to −0.9, p<0.001). Length of stay was not significantly different between groups. Physician acceptance of pharmacist recommendations was 71.3%. The trial provides evidence for integrating pharmacist review into routine admission workflows for elderly patients with polypharmacy.

title: Development and preliminary validation of a clinical decision support tool for polypharmacy risk stratification in elderly patients at care transitions in the Serbian healthcare system
abstract: This paper describes the development and preliminary validation of a risk stratification tool intended for use at care transition points (hospital admission, discharge, and first post-discharge primary care contact) to identify elderly patients at highest risk of adverse drug interactions. Item generation was based on a systematic review of existing tools (including STOPP/START, FORTA, and the GerontoNet score), expert consensus among seven clinicians from Serbia and Hungary, and retrospective analysis of 934 patient records from the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina (2018–2022). The resulting 14-item checklist was tested prospectively in a convenience sample of 120 patients. At a cut-off of 6 out of 14 points, the tool achieved a sensitivity of 76% and specificity of 71% for predicting at least one serious drug-related adverse event within 30 days of transition. Calibration was acceptable (Hosmer-Lemeshow p=0.34). External validation in a multicentre sample is planned.

title: Hepatic IRS-1 serine phosphorylation correlates with the degree of steatosis in biopsy-confirmed NAFLD patients
abstract: Insulin receptor substrate-1 (IRS-1) serine phosphorylation is a recognised mechanism of insulin resistance, yet its quantitative relationship with histological severity in NAFLD has not been well characterised in a Central European cohort. We collected liver biopsies from 54 patients undergoing bariatric surgery at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, graded steatosis, lobular inflammation, and ballooning by the NAFLD Activity Score (NAS), and quantified IRS-1 pSer307 by western blot normalised to total IRS-1. Patients were stratified into NAS 0–2 (n=18), NAS 3–4 (n=21), and NAS ≥5 (NASH, n=15). IRS-1 pSer307 increased progressively across groups (mean ratios 0.38, 0.71, and 1.14 respectively; p<0.001 by one-way ANOVA). Logistic regression showed that pSer307 ratio was independently associated with NASH after adjustment for BMI, fasting insulin, and ALT (OR 3.7, 95% CI 1.6–8.9). These data support IRS-1 serine phosphorylation as a tissue-level correlate of disease stage and suggest it may be informative alongside standard biochemical markers.

title: Farinographic and extensographic properties of mill streams from two soft wheat varieties grown in Vojvodina
abstract: Nineteen mill streams from two soft wheat varieties (Zvezdana and Kolubara) were isolated at a pilot-scale Bühler MLU-202 mill and characterised by farinograph water absorption, development time, stability, and softening index, together with extensograph energy, extensibility, and maximum resistance after 45, 90, and 135 min of rest. Zvezdana break and reduction streams differed significantly in water absorption (range 54.1–61.8 %) and stability (1.2–9.4 min), whereas Kolubara streams showed narrower variation in extensibility (138–176 mm). Principal component analysis separated streams into three clusters corresponding to anatomical origin. The data suggest that Zvezdana reduction flours with stability above 7 min and extensibility above 160 mm are suitable targets for blending into high-performance bread flour without the need for ascorbic acid supplementation. Regression models (R² = 0.84–0.91) relating protein content and wet gluten index to farinograph stability were derived for each variety, providing practical reference equations for mill operators.

title: DSC-based gelatinisation parameters of isolated wheat starch as a function of granule size fraction
abstract: Wheat starch was isolated from a commercial mill flour by alkaline steeping and fractionated by sequential centrifugation into A-type granules (>10 µm) and B-type granules (<10 µm). Differential scanning calorimetry was performed at 1:3 starch-to-water ratio, heating from 20 to 120 °C at 5 °C/min, on a Mettler Toledo DSC 3+. Onset temperature (To), peak temperature (Tp), conclusion temperature (Tc), and enthalpy (ΔH) were determined for each fraction across three consecutive seasons (2009–2011). A-type granules exhibited consistently higher ΔH values (10.2–11.8 J/g) than B-type granules (7.9–9.3 J/g), while Tp differed by 1.5–2.1 °C between fractions. Interannual variation in ΔH was significant (p < 0.05) for both fractions, correlated with grain protein content (r = −0.72). The results indicate that the A/B granule ratio in flour blends is a practical lever for targeting gelatinisation onset in starch-based industrial applications.

title: Effect of enzyme-active soya flour addition on gluten network mechanics and bread loaf volume in industrial baking streams
abstract: Enzyme-active soya flour (EASF) was incorporated at 0, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.8 % (flour weight basis) into three wheat mill streams differing in protein content (9.8, 11.4, and 13.1 %). Gluten network development was assessed by Mixolab 2 and dynamic oscillatory rheometry (frequency sweep 0.1–10 Hz, amplitude 0.1 %). EASF addition at 0.3 % increased storage modulus G' at 1 Hz by 12–18 % across streams without substantially altering loss tangent. Starch gelatinisation enthalpy measured by DSC decreased by 5–9 % at 0.5 % EASF, consistent with lipoxygenase-mediated starch-lipid disruption. Bread loaf volume increased from 685 to 740 mL (mid-protein stream, 0.3 % EASF) but declined at higher addition levels. Crumb texture analysis (TPA) showed increased hardness above 0.5 % EASF in all streams. Practical inclusion limits are proposed for each protein class.

title: Algorithmic reconstruction of target falling number from binary and ternary wheat flour blends
abstract: A quadratic programming (QP) model was formulated to identify blend proportions of up to five mill streams such that the resulting Hagberg–Perten falling number (FN) matched a specified target within ±5 s while simultaneously satisfying protein content, ash, and moisture constraints. Input data comprised 48 mill streams characterised over four milling campaigns. Blend optimisation was implemented in Python 3.9 using the CVXPY library with the ECOS solver. For binary blends, the QP model matched target FN (280 s) within tolerance in 91 % of tested stream pairs; for ternary blends the rate dropped to 76 % due to nonlinear enzyme–substrate interactions not captured by the linear starch degradation assumption. An empirical correction factor derived from α-amylase activity (Ceralpha assay) improved ternary blend accuracy to 86 %. The model is deployable as a stand-alone script integrated with laboratory information management systems.

title: Variability of wet gluten index and gluten aggregation energy across Pannonian basin wheat genotypes: a four-year survey
abstract: Wet gluten index (GI) and gluten aggregation energy (measured by Glutomatic and GlutoPeak, respectively) were determined on 204 flour samples representing 17 wheat genotypes grown at four locations in Serbia and Hungary between 2015 and 2018. GI ranged from 24 to 98 across the dataset; aggregation peak time (PT) ranged from 68 to 312 s. Genotype explained 41 % of total GI variance, environment 29 %, and genotype-by-environment interaction 18 %, with the remainder attributable to analytical error. GlutoPeak PT correlated with farinograph stability (r = 0.83, p < 0.001) but showed weaker correlation with extensograph energy (r = 0.61). High-GI genotypes grown under elevated temperature during grain filling showed markedly shorter PT, suggesting heat-induced glutenin polymerisation alteration. Cluster analysis identified four genotype groups with stable across-environment gluten quality suitable for blending targets in industrial milling specifications.

title: Thermal pasting profiles of reconstituted flour blends: sensitivity to bran particle size and pentosan content
abstract: Reconstituted flour blends were prepared from white flour (70 %), shorts (15 %), and bran fractions (15 %) in which bran was milled to three particle size classes (d50 = 412, 228, and 89 µm). Water-extractable and water-unextractable arabinoxylan (WEAX and WUAX) contents were determined by the phloroglucinol colorimetric method. Rapid Visco Analyser (RVA 4500) profiles showed that decreasing bran d50 from 412 to 89 µm increased peak viscosity by 310–430 cP and shifted pasting temperature down by 1.8–3.2 °C, effects attributable to increased WEAX release (from 0.41 to 0.89 g/100 g flour). Multiple linear regression relating RVA parameters to WEAX content, protein content, and damaged starch explained 78–85 % of viscosity variance. The findings have direct relevance for whole-wheat product developers targeting specific pasting behaviour without enzyme supplementation.

title: Starch retrogradation kinetics in stored bread: influence of initial blend composition and added exogenous amylase
abstract: Three flour blends with contrasting gelatinisation enthalpies (ΔH = 8.6, 10.1, and 11.3 J/g) were used to bake pan bread with or without added fungal α-amylase (20 FAU/kg flour). Retrogradation was monitored by DSC at 1, 3, and 7 days post-baking (retrogradation enthalpy ΔHret) and by crumb firmness (texture profile analysis, probe compression 40 %). Blends with lower initial ΔH showed faster retrogradation (ΔHret at day 7: 2.3, 2.7, and 3.4 J/g respectively), but amylase addition reduced day-7 ΔHret by 28–35 % uniformly across blend types. Crumb firmness at day 7 ranged from 6.1 to 9.8 N without amylase and from 3.8 to 5.9 N with amylase. The interaction between initial blend gelatinisation enthalpy and amylase dose on retrogradation rate was not statistically significant (p = 0.19), suggesting amylase dosage can be decoupled from blend thermal properties in commercial formulation.

title: Machine learning classification of wheat flour blend suitability for biscuit manufacturing using Mixolab and DSC descriptors
abstract: A dataset of 186 flour blends was assembled from archived Mixolab 2 profiles, DSC gelatinisation parameters, and farinograph indices. Each blend was labelled as suitable (1) or unsuitable (0) for short-dough biscuit manufacturing based on pilot-scale baking trials evaluated by spread ratio, surface crack score, and texture snap force. Four classifiers were tested: logistic regression, k-nearest neighbours, random forest, and gradient boosting. Gradient boosting achieved the highest cross-validated F1 score (0.87) and AUC (0.93). The five most important features by permutation importance were Mixolab C2 torque, DSC Tp, farinograph water absorption, damaged starch, and C3–C4 torque difference. Misclassified samples were concentrated in the protein content range 10.8–11.2 %, where biscuit spread ratio showed high experimental variance. The trained classifier is intended as a decision-support tool for mill laboratory staff to pre-screen blend candidates before physical baking trials.

title: Phytase, protease, and amylase activities in a malt–sourdough combined system for sprouted barley flatbread: influence of malt addition level (0–30%) on dough rheology and mineral bioaccessibility
abstract: Malted barley flour (72 h germination, 65 °C kilning) was substituted into a sourdough flatbread formulation at 0, 10, 20, and 30% (w/w flour basis). Dough enzyme activities, rheological parameters (small deformation oscillatory testing), and mineral bioaccessibility (in vitro dialysability for iron and zinc) were measured after 16 h fermentation at 28 °C. Phytase activity increased linearly with malt addition (R² = 0.96), reaching 174 nkat g⁻¹ at 30% substitution. Phytate reduction improved from 34% (0% malt) to 79% (30% malt). Dough storage modulus G′ decreased progressively with malt level, from 3,420 Pa at 0% to 1,180 Pa at 30%, consistent with increased proteolytic softening. Iron dialysability improved by 2.3-fold and zinc dialysability by 1.9-fold at 30% malt. Baked flatbread specific volume was optimal at 20% malt substitution, above which excessive softening reduced gas retention.

title: Viscosity-based rapid screening of oat hull beta-glucan molecular weight: calibration against SEC-MALS across a temperature and concentration matrix
abstract: A calibration framework was developed to estimate Mw of oat hull beta-glucan from apparent viscosity measurements without recourse to SEC, using 18 extracted fractions spanning Mw 98–512 kDa. Solutions were prepared at 0.25, 0.50, and 1.00% (w/v) and apparent viscosity was measured at 20, 37, and 50 °C using a Brookfield DV3T viscometer at 10 s⁻¹. Mark–Houwink–Sakurada parameters were determined as K = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ dL g⁻¹ and a = 0.72 in 50 mM NaOH at 25 °C, consistent with a semi-flexible random coil conformation. A simplified look-up approach using viscosity at 37 °C and 1% concentration predicted Mw with a mean absolute error of 31 kDa (11% relative) against SEC-MALS reference values across a validation set of 6 independent fractions. The approach provides a laboratory-accessible quality control tool applicable to production-scale extraction monitoring in industrial settings.

title: Comparison of inkjet-printed and screen-printed carbon working electrodes for amperometric glucose detection
abstract: Carbon paste electrodes were fabricated by inkjet printing (Dimatix DMP-2850) and conventional screen printing on cellulose acetate substrates and evaluated as working electrodes in a three-electrode electrochemical cell for amperometric glucose detection using glucose oxidase immobilised with glutaraldehyde cross-linking. Cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry were performed in phosphate-buffered saline (pH 7.4) with glucose concentrations from 1 mM to 20 mM. Inkjet-printed electrodes showed a sensitivity of 12.4 µA·mM⁻¹·cm⁻² and a detection limit of 0.18 mM, whereas screen-printed counterparts yielded 9.7 µA·mM⁻¹·cm⁻² and 0.31 mM, attributed to the smoother surface morphology and more uniform enzyme coverage achieved by inkjet printing. Electrode-to-electrode reproducibility (RSD of peak current, n=10) was 4.2% for inkjet versus 6.8% for screen-printed. Storage stability over 14 days at 4 °C showed less than 10% response decrease for both types.
