title: Appraisal Rights in Post-Yugoslav Company Laws: A Comparative Survey
abstract: This article compares appraisal right mechanisms across six successor-state legal systems — Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina (both entities), Slovenia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro — drawing on statutory texts, secondary literature, and a dataset of 61 reported court and arbitration decisions collected from publicly accessible judicial databases between 2011 and 2018. The comparison is structured around four variables: triggering events, valuation methodology, procedural standing, and costs allocation. The findings reveal a spectrum from Slovenia, where appraisal procedures closely follow the Austrian model with mandatory independent expert appointment, to Bosnia and Herzegovina (Federation), where statutory provisions are largely inoperative due to absent implementing regulations. Serbia occupies an intermediate position; its 2015 amendments improved procedural clarity but left valuation standards underspecified. The article argues that the divergence within the region creates forum-shopping risks in cross-border M&A transactions involving companies incorporated in multiple successor states.

title: Pravo na pobijanje odluke o squeeze-outu pred privrednim sudom: procesne pretpostavke i rokovi

Analizirani su svi objavljeni prvostepeni i drugostepeni sudski predmeti koji su autoru bili dostupni putem Informatora o radu privrednih sudova za period 2016–2020. (n = 31). Utvrđeno je da su u 48% predmeta tužbe odbačene zbog propuštanja roka od 30 dana, što ukazuje na sistemski problem informisanosti manjinskih akcionara. Posebna pažnja posvećena je pitanju da li se rok počinje računati od dana dostavljanja obavještenja ili od dana upisa u registar, gdje je uočena podjela u sudskoj praksi. Predložen je model izmjene zakonskog teksta koji rok vezuje za dan stvarnog prijema obavještenja.

title: Valuation Methodologies for Minority Shares in Closely-Held Serbian Companies: DCF Versus Book Value
abstract: The article examines the practical application of share valuation methodologies in Serbian squeeze-out proceedings, focusing on the tension between the discounted cash flow (DCF) method, which is dominant in financial practice, and the book value approach, which remains prevalent in expert reports submitted to Serbian courts. Using a sample of 18 court-appointed expert reports obtained through freedom of information requests to five Serbian commercial courts (2016–2021), the study codes each report for methodological choice, disclosure of assumptions, and whether a control or minority discount was applied. Book value or a simple earnings multiple was used in 14 of 18 reports, with no discount adjustments in any case. The article situates these findings within the broader literature on fair value standards, with reference to the Delaware appraisal statute and German Abfindungsrecht, and recommends that the Serbian court system adopt binding methodological guidelines analogous to the German IDW S 1 standard.

title: Freeze-Out Transactions and the Role of Independent Valuation Experts: Evidence from Croatian and Serbian Practice
abstract: Drawing on a combined dataset of 44 completed freeze-out transactions in Croatia (2015–2022) and Serbia (2015–2022), this study investigates whether mandatory appointment of an independent valuation expert, as required by Croatian law since 2013, yields measurably different outcomes for minority shareholders compared with the Serbian system, where expert appointment is discretionary. Transaction records were obtained from the Zagreb Stock Exchange regulatory filings and the Serbian Business Registers Agency. For each transaction, the announced consideration per share was compared with a reference value derived from a 90-day pre-announcement volume-weighted average price. Croatian transactions showed a mean premium of 8.3% over the reference price, while Serbian transactions showed a mean discount of 2.1%, a difference that is statistically significant at the 5% level (t-test, p = 0.031). Regression analysis controlling for firm size, sector, and majority shareholding concentration confirms the sign and significance of the country variable. The results support a causal role for mandatory expert appointment in improving minority outcomes.

title: Shareholder Oppression Doctrine in Serbian Law: Can Existing Remedies Fill the Gap?
abstract: Anglo-American company law has long recognised a distinct doctrine of shareholder oppression, empowering courts to grant relief when majority conduct is unfairly prejudicial to minorities. Serbian law contains no equivalent doctrine, relying instead on a set of fragmented statutory provisions. This article systematically maps the available remedies — including the squeeze-out challenge, derivative action, dissolution for cause, and breach of shareholders' agreement — and assesses their suitability as functional substitutes for oppression relief through doctrinal analysis and review of 28 published appellate decisions from 2014 to 2024. The analysis shows that dissolution for cause is rarely granted and practically requires proof of deadlock, while derivative actions face high procedural barriers. Shareholders' agreements provide the most effective private ordering solution but remain uncommon in Serbian practice. The article concludes that the remedial gap is real and proposes targeted amendments modelled on Section 994 of the UK Companies Act 2006, adapted to civil law procedural constraints.

title: Informaciona prava manjinskih akcionara u zatvorenim akcionarskim društvima: između zakonskog minimuma i korporativne prakse
abstract: Rad ispituje da li srpski zakonodavni okvir obezbeđuje manjinskim akcionarima zatvorenih akcionarskih društava dovoljno informacija za smisleno ostvarivanje prava glasa i za procenu da li su ugroženi. Istraživanje se zasniva na analizi 60 godišnjih izveštaja i statuta nasumično odabranih zatvorenih akcionarskih društava registrovanih u AP Vojvodini, dostupnih u registru Agencije za privredne registre za 2023. godinu. Kodirani su sledeći elementi: obim obelodanjivanja u godišnjim izveštajima, dostupnost statuta akcionarima po zahtevu, postojanje politike sukoba interesa i procedura za sazivanje vanredne skupštine. Rezultati pokazuju da 43 od 60 društava (71,7%) nije objavilo potpun finansijski izveštaj u zakonskom roku, a da svega 12 od 60 (20%) ima internu politiku o sukobima interesa. Rad predlaže uvođenje minimalnog standarda korporativnog izveštavanja za zatvorena akcionarska društva s više od 50 akcionara.

title: A Morphological Lexicon for Serbian Legal Texts: Construction and Evaluation
abstract: This paper describes the construction of a domain-specific morphological lexicon targeting legal Serbian, a register characterised by archaic inflectional forms, borrowings from Austro-Hungarian administrative vocabulary, and multi-word terminological units. The lexicon was built through semi-automatic extraction from a 4.2-million-token corpus of court decisions and legislative documents, followed by manual verification by two trained annotators. The extraction pipeline combined a pre-existing general-purpose morphological dictionary with a rule-based extension module handling productive suffixation patterns not attested in general resources. The resulting lexicon contains 87,400 lemma–paradigm pairs and 620,000 fully inflected word forms with part-of-speech and morphosyntactic feature tags conforming to the MULTEXT-East specification. Evaluation on a held-out set of 5,000 sentences yielded a lemmatisation accuracy of 96.4 % and a full morphosyntactic tagging accuracy of 91.7 %, compared to 88.1 % for the same tagger using the general-purpose lexicon only. The lexicon is released under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Annotating Named Entities in Serbian News Corpora: Guidelines and Inter-Annotator Agreement
abstract: We present annotation guidelines and an inter-annotator agreement study for named-entity recognition in Serbian newswire text. Seven entity categories were defined—person, organisation, location, geopolitical entity, product, event, and work of art—with sub-type distinctions motivated by downstream information extraction needs. Three annotator pairs independently labelled a 120,000-token sample drawn from the SrpNovine reference corpus. Cohen's kappa for the coarse-grained scheme reached 0.81 on boundaries and 0.78 on boundary-plus-type agreement, while the fine-grained scheme yielded 0.69. The most frequent disagreement source was the organisation–geopolitical entity boundary, accounting for 34 % of all conflicts. Analysis of morphological ambiguity showed that genitive and instrumental case forms of proper nouns caused a disproportionate share of boundary errors compared to nominative forms. Revised guidelines incorporating additional decision trees for these categories raised agreement by 0.05 kappa points in a follow-up round. The annotated sample and the guidelines are made publicly available.

title: Morphological Disambiguation of Serbian Using Conditional Random Fields with Lexical and Contextual Features
abstract: Morphological disambiguation in Serbian is complicated by a high degree of syncretism across the seven-case nominal paradigm and by frequent zero-marked verb forms. This paper reports experiments using Conditional Random Fields with feature sets combining lexical unigrams and bigrams, character n-grams up to length five, morphological dictionary lookup confidence scores, and syntactic head distance estimates derived from a dependency parser. Training data consisted of 1.1 million tokens from the SrpNovine and SrpWiki corpora, annotated with full MULTEXT-East morphosyntactic descriptions. On the standard SrpNovine test partition, the CRF model achieved a per-token accuracy of 94.2 % on full morphosyntactic description compared to 91.8 % for a maximum-entropy baseline. The largest gains were observed for case disambiguation of adjectives (from 87.3 % to 92.6 %) and for verb mood disambiguation (from 90.1 % to 93.7 %). Error analysis identified multiword proper nouns and technical compound adjectives as persistent problem classes.

title: SrpMed: A Corpus of Serbian Medical Discharge Summaries with Morphosyntactic and Named-Entity Annotation
abstract: Clinical text in Serbian poses specific challenges for natural language processing: heavy use of Latin-origin terminology, abundant abbreviations, non-standard orthography, and code-switching with English pharmacological names. This paper describes SrpMed, a corpus of 8,400 de-identified hospital discharge summaries comprising approximately 2.3 million tokens, collected from three clinical centres in Serbia under a data sharing agreement. Annotation covers sentence boundaries, tokenisation, lemmas, morphosyntactic tags, and a four-category named-entity scheme: medication, disease/disorder, anatomical location, and clinical procedure. A semi-automatic pipeline performed initial annotation; subsequent manual correction on a 200,000-token sample by two specialist annotators achieved Cohen's kappa of 0.84 for named entities. Baseline sequence labelling experiments using a BiLSTM-CRF architecture trained on the corrected sample attained an entity-level F1 of 79.3 % on a 20,000-token test set. Corpus statistics, annotation tools, and trained models are described.

title: Semantic Role Labelling for Serbian: Frame Inventory, Annotation, and Baseline Models
abstract: This paper presents the first systematic semantic role labelling resource for Serbian, covering 42 verbal frames drawn from a stratified sample of Serbian FrameNet-aligned predicates. Frame selection prioritised verbs frequent in journalistic and administrative registers. A 350,000-token corpus slice from SrpNovine was annotated with frame-evoking predicates and their semantic arguments following an adapted FrameNet methodology, with cross-validation of frame assignments against a Slovenian FrameNet resource to promote inter-language consistency. Annotation was carried out by four trained linguistics students supervised by two researchers; overall agreement on argument spans reached 0.76 kappa. Baseline models using a pipeline of dependency parsing followed by argument classification with an SVM achieved a labelled F1 of 66.4 % on core arguments and 54.1 % on peripheral arguments on the test partition. The work identifies subject–object ambiguity in passive constructions as the main error source. Frame definitions and annotated data are released.

title: Challenges in Annotating Financial Reports in Serbian: A Case Study in Domain Shift
abstract: Automatic language processing of Serbian financial and corporate reporting texts faces domain shift from general-purpose models due to numerical expressions, specialised nominal compounds, anglicisms, and non-standard sentence structures in translated source material. This paper reports annotation of a 600,000-token corpus of annual reports, prospectus summaries, and audit findings collected from publicly listed companies registered in Serbia. Three annotation layers are described: morphosyntactic tagging, multi-word expression identification, and a five-class named-entity scheme covering company names, persons, monetary values, dates, and regulatory instrument references. Morphosyntactic tagging accuracy using an existing general model dropped from 94.2 % on newswire to 89.3 % on this corpus. Fine-tuning on 80,000 tokens of in-domain annotated data recovered accuracy to 93.6 %. Multi-word expression identification posed additional difficulties; only 61 % of financial compound nouns were correctly identified by general-purpose tools. The paper discusses annotation decisions and provides corpus statistics.

title: A Valency Dictionary for Serbian Verbs: Structure, Coverage, and Computational Encoding
abstract: This chapter describes the design and computational encoding of a valency dictionary for Serbian verbs, covering 3,200 lexical entries with a total of 6,800 valency frames. Each entry specifies obligatory and optional argument slots, their syntactic realisation (nominative subject, accusative or genitive object, prepositional phrases, infinitival complements), and a representative set of corpus-attested example sentences. Syntactic annotations were linked to dependency trees from the Universal Dependencies Serbian treebank to allow automatic frame lookup by tree pattern matching. The dictionary was built through manual analysis by three lexicographers working from frequency-sorted verb lists extracted from a 90-million-token balanced corpus of Serbian. Completeness was assessed by comparing frame inventories against a subset of Serbian verbs present in VerbNet-like resources for related languages; 74 % of attested frames had equivalents in Croatian or Slovenian resources, while 26 % required language-specific frame definitions. Inter-lexicographer agreement on frame assignment reached 0.82 kappa. Potential applications in semantic role labelling and pedagogical grammar are discussed.

title: NERSrp 2.0: An Updated Named-Entity Recognition Benchmark for Serbian with Cross-Domain Test Sets
abstract: We release NERSrp 2.0, an updated benchmark for named-entity recognition in Serbian that extends the earlier NERSrp 1.0 release with three additional test sets covering medical, financial, and social media text. The benchmark retains the original eight-category newswire annotation scheme and provides domain-specific sub-type extensions for medical entities. Total annotated data amounts to 1.1 million tokens across five domains. We report results for four system classes: a rule-and-dictionary baseline, a CRF system, a fine-tuned BERTić model, and a fine-tuned SrpBERT model. On the newswire test set, SrpBERT reaches an entity-level F1 of 89.7 %, but performance drops to 76.4 % on social media and 81.2 % on medical text without domain-specific fine-tuning. Adding 10,000 in-domain annotated tokens per domain narrows the gap by 4–7 F1 points. The benchmark, annotation guidelines, and evaluation scripts are released under open licences to facilitate reproducibility.

title: Morphological Generation for Data Augmentation in Low-Resource Serbian NLP Tasks
abstract: For morphologically rich languages with limited annotated data, generating inflectional variants of training examples can improve model generalisation without requiring additional manual annotation. This paper evaluates a morphological generation strategy applied to three Serbian NLP tasks: relation extraction from legal text, aspect-level sentiment classification of product reviews, and semantic textual similarity scoring. Generation was performed using a finite-state morphological transducer applied to noun and verb lemmas identified in training sentences, producing between two and nine inflectional variants per sentence depending on the syntactic head category. Training set sizes ranged from 400 to 3,000 examples per task. Augmentation improved F1 by 2.1–4.8 points across tasks when target training sets contained fewer than 1,000 examples, with diminishing returns above 2,500 examples. Negative transfer was observed in the STS task when augmented sentences altered argument roles, leading to a 1.2-point decrease. Analysis of augmentation errors attributes most regressions to verb aspect mismatches in finite-state generation.

title: Term Extraction and Glossary Construction for the Serbian Language in the Domain of Renewable Energy Regulation
abstract: Consistent regulatory terminology for renewable energy is important for legislative drafting and public communication in Serbia, yet no comprehensive terminological resource exists. This paper describes a semi-automatic term extraction workflow applied to a 4.8-million-token corpus assembled from EU directive translations, national legislation, technical standards, and the proceedings of the Serbian Energy Agency. Candidate terms were extracted using a hybrid method combining statistical association measures (log-likelihood and PMI) for multi-word units with a morphological filter restricting candidates to nominal and adjectival groups. A total of 4,210 candidate terms were generated; expert review accepted 2,670 as valid domain terms. For each accepted term, the workflow automatically populated glossary fields including definition, source reference, part-of-speech, inflectional paradigm, and up to three corpus example sentences. Equivalents in English and German were semi-automatically linked via EU terminology databases. The resulting glossary is structured as a TEI-conformant XML resource and is intended for use in specialised dictionary compilation and legal translation support tools.

title: Wideband indoor channel measurements at 2.45 GHz in office environments using a switched-array sounder
abstract: This paper presents a wideband channel measurement campaign conducted in three office-type buildings at the University of Novi Sad campus at 2.45 GHz. A switched-array channel sounder with 8×8 virtual aperture and 200 MHz bandwidth was used to collect 1,440 channel impulse response snapshots across line-of-sight and obstructed line-of-sight links. Path loss exponents ranged from 1.9 to 3.2 depending on floor layout and partition type. Delay spread statistics were extracted and compared with empirical models from the literature. A log-normal shadowing model with standard deviation of 5.1 dB was fitted to the measured data. The influence of furniture density on small-scale fading characteristics was also assessed; Rician K-factors were found to decrease from 8.2 dB in sparsely furnished rooms to 2.1 dB in heavily cluttered corridors. The dataset is made available for further model validation.

title: Comparison of deterministic and stochastic indoor propagation models for the 5 GHz WLAN band
abstract: The paper evaluates the prediction accuracy of a 3-D ray-tracing tool against a log-distance stochastic model in four indoor test environments ranging from small offices to a university lecture hall. The ray-tracing engine accounted for up to four reflections and two diffractions per path, with material parameters calibrated from reflection coefficient measurements. Over 620 reference measurement points were collected using a calibrated spectrum analyser and omni-directional reference antenna. Ray tracing produced a mean absolute error of 3.8 dB, while the stochastic model yielded 6.2 dB, with the gap widening in highly reflective rooms with concrete walls. Computation time for ray tracing exceeded that of the stochastic approach by a factor of 340. The study provides guidance on when deterministic modelling justifies the additional computational overhead for network planning purposes.

title: Polarisation diversity gain in reverberation-chamber-validated indoor MIMO channels
abstract: Dual-polarised MIMO channel matrices were measured at 5.2 GHz in a purpose-built reverberation chamber and in three real indoor environments at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The chamber was used to generate Rayleigh-fading reference data with controlled mean excess delay. A 4×4 dual-polarised patch antenna array was designed and fabricated in-house with cross-polarisation isolation exceeding 28 dB. Measured channel capacity values in the real environments reached 18.3 bits/s/Hz at 20 dB SNR, compared with 14.7 bits/s/Hz for a co-polarised configuration of the same array. Envelope correlation coefficients remained below 0.15 for antenna separations beyond 0.4λ. The reverberation chamber results validated the fading statistics of the real measurements within a 1.8 dB capacity margin, supporting its use as a calibration reference for indoor MIMO evaluations.

title: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces: channel modelling approaches and open challenges — a survey
abstract: This survey reviews channel modelling methodologies for reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) in sub-6 GHz and millimetre-wave indoor environments, covering the period 2014–2018. Four categories of models are examined: free-space dyadic Green's function approaches, generalised sheet transition condition models, empirical path-loss extensions, and stochastic geometry frameworks. For each category the paper identifies assumptions, validated frequency ranges, and computational requirements. The survey compiles 78 experimental studies and 42 simulation-only works, evaluating the proportion that include real indoor measurement validation (29%). Key open challenges identified include near-field channel characterisation, mutual coupling effects in closely spaced RIS elements, and the absence of standardised measurement protocols. The paper also proposes a taxonomy of RIS deployment scenarios based on link geometry and discusses its implications for model selection.

title: Measured path loss and angular spread for a wall-mounted RIS panel at 3.5 GHz in a single-floor office building
abstract: A measurement campaign characterised the propagation channel between a transmitter, a 16×16 element wall-mounted RIS prototype and a receiver in a 450 m² single-floor office environment at 3.5 GHz. Fifty-four transmitter–receiver pairs were measured with the RIS in both active (with pre-loaded phase profile) and passive (uniform phase) configurations. Received power increased by 8.3 dB on average when the RIS phase profile was pre-computed using a geometric optics steering law, compared with the passive case. Angular spread at the receiver was reduced from 42° to 17° with the RIS active, indicating stronger specular behaviour. Path loss for the RIS-assisted link was found to follow an approximate R⁻²·⁴ law for transmitter–RIS distances up to 12 m. These results inform deployment guidelines for coverage extension in enterprise Wi-Fi environments.

title: Codebook-based passive beamforming for RIS-assisted indoor networks: design and over-the-air validation
abstract: This paper develops a codebook design method for passive beamforming at a 32×32 element RIS operating at 2.4 GHz. Codebook entries are generated by sampling the steering vector space with a hierarchical scheme that partitions the unit sphere into 512 sectors. The optimal codebook size balancing overhead and received signal-to-noise ratio gain was determined analytically and confirmed experimentally. Over-the-air validation used a software-defined radio platform with OFDM waveforms in a 12 m × 8 m laboratory room. With a 128-entry codebook, the measured SNR gain over a direct link reached 9.1 dB at a receiver located 6 m from the RIS, with beam selection latency of 14 ms using a binary tree search. The influence of human movement on codebook stability was evaluated over 30-minute observation periods, with beam mismatch occurring in fewer than 3.5% of frames.

title: Mutual coupling effects on RIS element radiation patterns: a measured and simulated comparison at 5.8 GHz
abstract: Mutual coupling between adjacent elements of a printed dipole RIS array at 5.8 GHz is investigated using both full-wave method-of-moments simulations and direct measurements on fabricated 4×4 and 8×8 sub-arrays. Coupling levels between nearest-neighbour elements at λ/2 spacing were measured at −17.3 dB on average, rising to −11.8 dB at λ/3 spacing. The resulting distortion of the individual element patterns was quantified by comparing active element patterns against isolated element patterns. Beamforming gain degradation due to mutual coupling reached 2.9 dB for a 16-element linear sub-array when coupling was ignored in the phase profile design. A post-processing correction based on the measured active element patterns recovered 2.1 dB of the lost gain. The findings suggest that coupling-aware design is necessary for RIS arrays with element spacing below 0.45λ.

title: Indoor RIS channel modelling
abstract: This chapter reviews physical-layer channel models for reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in indoor sub-6 GHz environments. It covers free-space cascade models, geometry-based stochastic models, and measurement-calibrated path-loss models, discussing the assumptions and validity limits of each. A particular focus is placed on the transition between near-field and far-field regimes as surface dimensions increase, with numerical examples for 0.5 m × 0.5 m and 1 m × 1 m surfaces at 3.5 GHz. The chapter also addresses RIS-specific phenomena including specular beamsteering gain, angle-of-incidence dependence of element phase response, and the impact of wall mounting on effective aperture. Practical modelling guidelines for system-level simulations are provided, together with a discussion of open problems in channel model standardisation. Exercises and annotated MATLAB code fragments accompany the chapter.

title: Optimisation of RIS phase profiles under partial channel state information using a projected gradient method
abstract: Passive beamforming optimisation for RIS-assisted indoor links is addressed under the constraint that only partial channel state information (P-CSI) is available at the controller. P-CSI is modelled as the mean angle-of-departure and angle-of-arrival with bounded uncertainty regions. A projected gradient algorithm is derived that maximises the worst-case received power over the uncertainty set, with the gradient projection enforcing the unit-modulus constraint on RIS phase shifts. For a 64-element RIS at 3.5 GHz in a simulated office floor plan with 18 scatterers, the algorithm converged in fewer than 40 iterations and achieved within 1.4 dB of the full-CSI optimum when the angular uncertainty half-width was below 8°. Computation time per update was 3.2 ms on a standard workstation. Monte Carlo results over 5,000 random room realisations confirmed robustness across diverse indoor geometries.

title: Frequency-selective behaviour of PIN-diode-tunable RIS elements: characterisation and compensation at 2.4 GHz
abstract: PIN-diode-based RIS elements exhibit frequency-selective phase and amplitude responses that are often neglected in narrowband system models. This paper characterises the frequency selectivity of a fabricated single-element cell over a 200 MHz bandwidth centred at 2.4 GHz across four discrete bias states. Measured insertion phase variation across the band reached 22° per 100 MHz in the forward-biased state, compared with 6° in the reverse-biased state. An equivalent circuit model with eight lumped parameters was fitted to the measured S-parameter data, achieving a fit error below 0.4 dB and 1.5° across the measurement band. A compensation scheme adjusting the phase profile as a function of subcarrier index in an OFDM system reduced wideband beamforming gain degradation from 3.1 dB to 0.7 dB in simulation. Experimental verification on a 16-element prototype confirmed a 2.2 dB improvement in received power at the band edges.

title: A geometry-based stochastic channel model for RIS-assisted corridors: parameterisation from 5.2 GHz measurements
abstract: A geometry-based stochastic channel model (GBSM) is developed and parameterised for RIS-assisted propagation in corridor environments at 5.2 GHz. The model decomposes the channel into a specular RIS-reflected component and a diffuse scattering component represented by a cluster of virtual scatterers distributed uniformly along the corridor walls. Model parameters — cluster angular spread, scatterer density, and specular-to-diffuse power ratio — were extracted from 96 measured channel realisations collected in two university building corridors. The specular-to-diffuse ratio varied from 6.8 dB near the RIS boresight to −2.3 dB at 40° off-boresight. A goodness-of-fit test based on the Cramér–von Mises statistic confirmed that the GBSM reproduced the measured delay–Doppler distribution more accurately than a two-ray model (p-value improvement from 0.04 to 0.31). The model is intended for use in system-level simulators.

title: Greedy Basis Pursuit for Sparse Spectrum Recovery in UHF Bands: A Simulation Study
abstract: This paper examines the application of greedy pursuit methods — specifically Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) and its stagewise variant StOMP — to the problem of recovering sparse frequency occupancy maps in the UHF television band (470–790 MHz). Synthetic occupancy scenarios with sparsity levels ranging from 5% to 30% were generated using a channel model parameterised from measurement campaigns in urban Novi Sad. Random Gaussian measurement matrices of size 128×512 were used to project wideband observations onto a low-dimensional space. Recovery accuracy was assessed by the normalised mean squared error (NMSE) and the probability of correct support identification over 1000 Monte Carlo trials. OMP achieved correct support recovery in 91% of trials at a sparsity level of 10% and a signal-to-noise ratio of 15 dB, while StOMP reduced computation time by 38% at a modest accuracy cost of 4 percentage points. The results suggest that greedy methods are viable for real-time spectrum monitoring when the occupied band fraction remains below 15%.

title: Structured Measurement Matrices for Sub-Nyquist Wideband Sensing: Toeplitz versus Circulant Designs
abstract: Random Gaussian measurement matrices guarantee recovery with high probability but are impractical to store and apply in hardware. This paper compares Toeplitz-structured and circulant-structured matrices as computationally efficient alternatives for wideband spectrum sensing spanning 200 MHz at a nominal Nyquist rate of 400 Msps. The restricted isometry property (RIP) constants are estimated numerically for matrix sizes from 64×256 to 256×1024. Reconstruction is performed with BPDN (Basis Pursuit De-Noising) solved via the ADMM algorithm. At a compression ratio of 4:1 and SNR of 10 dB, circulant matrices achieved an NMSE of −18.4 dB compared with −19.1 dB for Gaussian matrices and −17.6 dB for Toeplitz matrices. Circulant structure enables matrix-vector products via FFT, reducing per-iteration complexity from O(mn) to O(n log n). Simulation results are validated against a prototype sub-Nyquist sampler implemented on a Xilinx FPGA evaluation board sampling at 100 Msps.

title: Iterative Reweighted ℓ1 Minimisation for Recovery of Spectrally Sparse Signals Under Coloured Noise
abstract: Standard ℓ1 minimisation for compressed sensing implicitly assumes white Gaussian noise in the measurement model. In practical spectrum monitoring, interference from adjacent channels introduces coloured noise that degrades recovery if not accounted for. This paper adapts the iterative reweighted ℓ1 (IRL1) algorithm by incorporating a noise covariance estimate obtained from noise-only guard intervals flanking each monitored sub-band. The covariance is estimated using a 64-point pilot interval and updated every 200 ms. Tests use signals recorded with a USRP B210 receiver in a 100 MHz window around 750 MHz in an indoor laboratory environment, with WLAN interference injected from a separate transmitter. IRL1 with covariance weighting reduced the false alarm rate from 14.2% to 6.8% and the missed detection rate from 9.1% to 4.3% compared with standard BPDN, at a per-recovery computational overhead of 22%.

title: Compressed Sensing Reconstruction Benchmarks for Spectrum Monitoring: A Comparative Study of Eight Algorithms
abstract: A systematic comparison of eight compressed sensing reconstruction algorithms is presented for the specific task of wideband spectrum monitoring in the context of cognitive radio. The algorithms evaluated are OMP, CoSaMP, StOMP, SP (Subspace Pursuit), BPDN-ADMM, LASSO with coordinate descent, IRL1, and MUSIC-CS (a hybrid spectral estimation approach). Each algorithm is tested across three signal classes: narrowband carriers, OFDM multiplex signals, and frequency-hopping waveforms. Evaluation metrics include NMSE, probability of correct support recovery, execution time on a single CPU core (Intel Core i7-6700), and sensitivity to compression ratio. At a compression ratio of 8:1 and SNR of 15 dB, CoSaMP and SP achieve the best balance between accuracy (NMSE below −22 dB) and speed (under 3 ms per recovery for a 512-bin spectrum). BPDN-based methods are more robust at low SNR but 6–12× slower. Recommendations are provided for algorithm selection based on latency constraints.

title: Dictionary Learning for Adaptive Sparse Representations in Dynamic Spectrum Access Scenarios
abstract: Fixed analytical dictionaries such as the DFT basis may be suboptimal when monitored signals do not conform to the assumed model. This paper investigates K-SVD dictionary learning applied to a set of 3200 spectrum snapshots captured over 30 days by a USRP X310 receiver operating across 600–800 MHz in Novi Sad. A dictionary of 128 atoms of length 256 is learned and compared against DFT, DCT, and wavelet bases in terms of average sparsity (number of atoms required to represent a signal within 1% relative error). The learned dictionary achieved a mean sparsity of 7.3 atoms versus 19.1 for DFT and 14.8 for DCT. Downstream compressed sensing recovery using the learned dictionary reduced NMSE by 3.2 dB relative to DFT at a compression ratio of 6:1. Training and updating procedures are described, including an incremental update strategy that tracks spectral changes over time with a sliding window of 200 snapshots.

title: Real-Time FPGA Implementation of CoSaMP for Wideband Spectrum Sensing at 200 Msps
abstract: This paper describes the hardware implementation of the Compressive Sampling Matching Pursuit (CoSaMP) algorithm on a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA for real-time sparse spectrum recovery at an effective sampling rate of 200 Msps. The architecture processes 512-bin spectrum estimates from 128 compressed measurements within a latency budget of 500 μs, suitable for cognitive radio sensing cycles. Fixed-point arithmetic with 16-bit precision is used throughout; a precision loss analysis shows a 1.4 dB degradation in NMSE compared with double-precision floating-point. Resource utilisation amounts to 34% of available DSP slices and 41% of block RAM on the target device. A hardware-in-the-loop testbench using a USRP B210 as signal source confirms that the implementation correctly identifies active bands in 96.4% of test frames at SNR ≥ 10 dB. Power consumption during sensing cycles is measured at 4.1 W.

title: Sparse Recovery Under Quantisation Noise: Effect of ADC Resolution on Wideband Spectrum Reconstruction Accuracy
abstract: Sub-Nyquist compressed sensing receivers rely on analog-to-digital converters whose finite resolution introduces quantisation noise not captured by standard Gaussian measurement noise models. This study analyses the interaction between quantisation noise and ℓ1 reconstruction error as a function of ADC bit depth (4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 bits), compression ratio (2:1 to 10:1), and signal sparsity (5%, 10%, 20%). A theoretical bound on reconstruction error due to quantisation is derived under the assumption of uniform scalar quantisation and bounded measurement noise. Simulation results with BPDN-ADMM show that 8-bit quantisation introduces an NMSE floor of approximately −28 dB that cannot be lowered by increasing the number of measurements beyond a saturation point. For 6-bit ADCs the floor rises to −22 dB. Practical guidelines for ADC selection in compressed spectrum monitoring receivers are provided, with a worked example for a 200 MHz monitoring window.

title: Compressed Sensing-Based Spectrum Occupancy Prediction Using Temporal Correlation in Cognitive Radio Networks
abstract: Spectrum occupancy at a given frequency channel is not independent across time; primary user activity exhibits temporal autocorrelation that can be exploited to improve compressed sensing recovery. This paper models temporal occupancy as a hidden Markov chain with two states (occupied / idle) and estimated transition probabilities from the 14-day Novi Sad measurement dataset described in earlier work. The HMM occupancy prior is incorporated into a modified BPDN objective via a log-likelihood penalty term. At moderate SNR (10 dB) and a compression ratio of 6:1, the proposed approach reduces missed detection probability from 8.9% to 4.1% and false alarm probability from 7.3% to 3.6% compared with standard BPDN without temporal prior. The improvement is most pronounced for channels with high autocorrelation (television broadcast and LTE downlink). A discussion of applicability in fast-varying indoor environments is included.

title: Comparison of Sparse Recovery Algorithms for IoT Interference Detection in the 868 MHz Sub-GHz Band
abstract: The 868 MHz ISM band used by LoRaWAN, Sigfox, and other IoT protocols is increasingly congested, making real-time interference identification relevant for network management. This paper applies compressed sensing reconstruction to interference detection, treating the 868–870 MHz band sampled at 4 Msps as a sparse signal in the frequency domain. Four algorithms are compared: OMP, SP, BPDN-ADMM, and a proposed modified CoSaMP variant that incorporates known LoRaWAN chirp spreading factor as a structured prior. Measurements were performed with a USRP B205mini in an urban district of Novi Sad over a 48-hour period. The modified CoSaMP achieved a detection rate of 94.7% for LoRaWAN interference events at SNR = 8 dB, outperforming standard CoSaMP by 6.3 percentage points. False positive rates for all methods were below 5% for SNR ≥ 6 dB. Run time on an embedded ARM Cortex-A53 processor was 1.8 ms per frame.

title: Unrolled Iterative Algorithms for Compressed Spectrum Sensing: A Deep Unfolding Approach
abstract: Algorithm unrolling maps a fixed number of iterations of an iterative sparse recovery algorithm into a trainable neural network, allowing data-driven parameter learning while retaining interpretability. This paper applies deep unfolding to the Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm (ISTA), producing LISTA (Learned ISTA), and adapts it for compressed spectrum sensing in the 600–800 MHz band. A training set of 18000 spectrum snapshots with ground-truth occupancy labels is used; 2000 snapshots are reserved for testing. A 10-layer LISTA network trained with Adam (learning rate 10−3, 200 epochs) achieved an NMSE of −25.7 dB at a compression ratio of 8:1 and SNR of 10 dB, compared with −22.3 dB for standard ISTA at 50 iterations. Inference time on a GPU (NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX) was 0.31 ms per frame versus 4.7 ms for ISTA. Generalisation to unseen compression ratios and its degradation pattern are analysed.

title: Cramér-Rao Bounds for Compressive Delay-Doppler Estimation Under Structured Pilot Patterns in OFDM V2X
abstract: This paper derives analytical Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) for the joint estimation of delay, Doppler shift, and complex amplitude of individual multipath components from compressively observed OFDM pilot grids in V2X channels. The signal model accounts for inter-carrier interference arising from high mobility, treats the pilot selection matrix as a deterministic parameter, and assumes a Gaussian noise model. Closed-form expressions for the Fisher information matrix are derived for the single-component case and extended numerically to up to ten components. The resulting bounds are evaluated for pilot densities from 10 % to 50 % of the full grid and for vehicle speeds of 30, 90, and 140 km/h. Results show that the delay CRLB is largely insensitive to pilot density above 20 % while the Doppler CRLB degrades sharply below 15 %. The bounds are compared against the empirical performance of three published estimators—OMP, BSBL, and ANM—using Monte Carlo trials, and the gap to the bound at practical SNR (5–25 dB) is quantified.

title: Serum ferritin on admission as a predictor of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Acute exacerbations of COPD are associated with substantial in-hospital mortality, yet widely used severity scores do not incorporate iron-related markers. This retrospective cohort study analysed data from 214 patients admitted to the Clinic for Pulmonology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, between January 2020 and December 2021. Serum ferritin was measured on the day of admission alongside CRP, complete blood count, arterial blood gases, and spirometric data from the stable period. Patients were stratified into tertiles according to admission ferritin concentration. In-hospital mortality was 8.4% overall. After adjusting for age, sex, GOLD stage, and comorbidity index, patients in the highest ferritin tertile (>420 µg/L) had a significantly higher odds of in-hospital death compared with the lowest tertile (OR 3.7, 95% CI 1.4–9.8). Ferritin above 420 µg/L showed a sensitivity of 67% and specificity of 74% for predicting mortality. Ferritin correlated positively with CRP (r=0.51, p<0.001) and negatively with haemoglobin (r=−0.33, p<0.001). These findings suggest that serum ferritin, as a readily available laboratory parameter, carries independent prognostic information in this patient group.

title: Changes in serum ferritin from admission to discharge and their association with 90-day readmission after COPD exacerbation: a pilot study
abstract: Most biomarker studies in COPD exacerbation measure a single time point; little is known about whether the trajectory of ferritin during the hospital stay carries prognostic information. This pilot study followed 67 patients admitted for acute COPD exacerbation at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, measuring serum ferritin at admission, day 3, and at discharge. Ninety-day readmission data were obtained by medical record review and telephone contact. The readmission rate was 34.3%. Patients who were readmitted within 90 days had a smaller proportional decline in ferritin from admission to discharge (median −12%) compared with those not readmitted (median −31%, p=0.03). A decline of less than 20% at discharge was associated with readmission risk (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.1–7.8) after adjusting for prior exacerbation frequency. The sample size limits the strength of these conclusions, and a confirmatory study with at least 200 patients is being planned. This work was presented in preliminary form at the Balkan Congress of Internal Medicine.

title: Extending LoRaWAN node lifetime in sub-zero temperatures with adaptive duty cycling
abstract: This paper addresses the significant degradation in battery performance and radio frequency behaviour observed in LoRaWAN sensor nodes operating in sub-zero environmental conditions, a challenge critical for year-round agricultural monitoring in continental climates such as those found across the Pannonian Plain. We propose and evaluate an adaptive duty cycling algorithm that dynamically adjusts transmission intervals based on onboard temperature readings and real-time battery voltage measurements. The algorithm reduces unnecessary wake cycles during extreme cold, prioritising data integrity over raw reporting frequency. We validated the approach on a custom STM32-based node platform over a six-month winter deployment across three outdoor test sites in northern Serbia. Experimental results demonstrate a 38% extension in projected node lifetime compared to a static duty-cycle baseline, while maintaining acceptable data completeness rates above 91%. The paper further analyses the interplay between spreading factor selection and cold-induced current draw, offering practical guidelines for firmware designers targeting sub-zero deployments. These findings are directly applicable to precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and remote infrastructure sensing scenarios where battery replacement is logistically difficult and costly.

title: Solar energy harvesting for orchard sensor nodes: a two-year field study
abstract: Orchards present a demanding environment for solar energy harvesting due to variable canopy shading, seasonal irradiance shifts, and the need for continuous long-term sensor operation without manual maintenance. This paper reports a two-year field study conducted across four commercial apple and pear orchards in the Fruška Gora foothill region, in which solar-powered LoRaWAN sensor nodes were deployed to monitor soil moisture, microclimate temperature, and leaf wetness. Each node integrated a 2 W monocrystalline panel, a maximum power point tracking circuit, and a supercapacitor-buffered LiFePO4 battery pack designed to balance charge cycling longevity with burst transmission capability. We characterise harvested energy profiles across seasons, quantify shading losses attributable to tree canopy at different growth stages, and evaluate the performance of three panel tilt configurations. Results indicate that a 15° southward fixed tilt achieves the best annual energy balance in this latitude range. Node availability exceeded 97% across both deployment years, with only two hardware failures unrelated to the energy subsystem. The study provides empirically grounded sizing guidelines for orchard IoT deployments and identifies key design trade-offs between panel area, storage capacity, and node reporting duty cycle.

title: Packet loss in dense rural LoRa deployments
abstract: Dense deployments of LoRa-based sensor networks in rural agricultural settings introduce collision and interference patterns that differ substantially from those studied in urban or laboratory environments. This paper investigates packet loss mechanisms in a 120-node LoRaWAN deployment spread across 8 km² of mixed arable farmland in Vojvodina, Serbia. We characterise the contributions of intra-network collisions, near-far interference, and gateway saturation to overall packet delivery ratio degradation as node density increases. Field measurements reveal that naive single-spreading-factor deployments suffer packet loss rates exceeding 22% at peak reporting intervals during irrigation events, when many nodes transmit simultaneously. We evaluate three mitigation strategies: adaptive data rate assignment, time-slotted transmission scheduling, and multi-gateway spatial diversity. A hybrid approach combining adaptive data rate with dual-gateway coverage reduces peak packet loss to below 6% without requiring modifications to commercial LoRaWAN gateway hardware. The paper also presents a path-loss model calibrated to flat open farmland terrain, which outperforms standard log-distance models in this propagation environment. Our findings have direct implications for network planning tools and firmware design in precision agriculture IoT systems.

title: Supercapacitor-assisted power buffering for intermittent energy harvesting in agricultural sensor nodes
abstract: Agricultural IoT sensor nodes relying on intermittent energy sources such as solar panels or piezoelectric transducers face significant challenges in maintaining stable supply voltage during transmission bursts. This paper investigates the use of supercapacitors as primary power buffers in harvesting-enabled LoRaWAN nodes, focusing on charge-discharge cycling behaviour under realistic field conditions. We designed and fabricated a custom power management board incorporating a hybrid supercapacitor–LiFePO4 storage architecture and a programmable MPPT controller. The system was tested over eight months across two agricultural monitoring sites featuring different harvesting modalities: rooftop photovoltaic panels and soil-embedded vibration harvesters. We developed an analytical model predicting state-of-charge evolution as a function of harvesting intermittency and transmission scheduling, validated against measured data. Results show that supercapacitor buffering reduces peak battery discharge events by 64%, significantly extending projected cell calendar life. We further propose a firmware-level voltage-aware scheduling scheme that postpones non-critical transmissions when buffer charge falls below a configurable threshold. The combined hardware-firmware approach achieves continuous node operation through a 14-day low-irradiance winter period without external recharging. Design guidelines and component sizing equations are provided for practitioners deploying similar systems.

title: Embedded machine learning for anomaly detection in low-power soil sensor nodes
abstract: Deploying anomaly detection directly on resource-constrained embedded sensor nodes eliminates the need for continuous raw data transmission and reduces energy expenditure in wireless agricultural monitoring networks. This paper presents the design and field evaluation of a TinyML inference pipeline running on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller integrated into a LoRaWAN soil monitoring node. The pipeline targets detection of faulty sensor readings caused by probe degradation, soil air pockets, and connector corrosion — failure modes frequently observed in long-term outdoor deployments. We trained a lightweight one-class classification model on 14 months of reference sensor data and quantised it to 8-bit integer representation for on-device inference. Energy profiling shows that on-node inference consumes 1.8 mJ per inference cycle, representing less than 4% overhead relative to a standard sensing and transmission cycle. Field trials across five deployment sites demonstrated a fault detection recall of 89% with a false positive rate of 3.1%, substantially reducing spurious alert transmissions to the gateway. The paper analyses the trade-off between model complexity, inference energy, and detection accuracy, and provides a methodology for selecting quantisation depth appropriate to available SRAM constraints. These results support the viability of edge inference for data quality assurance in battery-powered agricultural IoT systems.

title: Comparative evaluation of LPWAN technologies for precision viticulture monitoring
abstract: Precision viticulture demands reliable, low-maintenance wireless connectivity across complex hilly terrain with dense vegetation, creating propagation challenges not well characterised in existing LPWAN literature. This paper presents a systematic comparative field evaluation of three LPWAN technologies — LoRaWAN, Sigfox, and NB-IoT — deployed simultaneously across two commercial vineyards in the Sremski Karlovci wine region of Serbia. We measured received signal strength, packet delivery ratio, latency, and per-message energy consumption for identical sensing payloads transmitted over a six-month growing season. LoRaWAN with adaptive data rate demonstrated the best overall energy efficiency and coverage reliability in the absence of cellular infrastructure, while NB-IoT provided superior data throughput at higher energy cost in areas with adequate 4G coverage. Sigfox showed competitive battery life figures but presented limitations in message frequency that conflicted with high-temporal-resolution frost-alert requirements. We further developed a site-suitability decision framework that maps terrain morphology and available infrastructure to the most appropriate LPWAN technology. The framework is validated against the field results and is intended as a practical planning tool for agricultural technology integrators. Our findings highlight that no single LPWAN solution universally dominates, and that hybrid deployments may be optimal for large, heterogeneous vineyard estates.

title: Hardware design guidelines for moisture-resilient PCB assemblies in outdoor sensor nodes
abstract: Long-term outdoor deployment of agricultural sensor nodes exposes printed circuit board assemblies to moisture ingress, condensation cycles, and corrosive agrochemical aerosols, leading to premature failure rates that undermine network reliability and increase maintenance costs. This paper provides empirically validated hardware design guidelines for improving the moisture resilience of low-cost embedded sensor node PCBs without resorting to hermetically sealed enclosures, which significantly increase unit cost and complicate firmware update procedures. We evaluated five conformal coating materials — acrylic, silicone, polyurethane, epoxy, and a UV-curable hybrid — applied to custom LoRaWAN node boards subjected to accelerated humidity cycling, salt spray, and fungal exposure tests aligned with IEC 60068-2 standards. Electrical performance metrics including quiescent current drift, RF transmission power stability, and ADC accuracy were tracked throughout a 2,000-hour stress protocol. Silicone-based coatings provided the best balance of moisture barrier performance and reworkability for field repairs. We additionally characterise connector selection criteria, soldermask specification choices, and via-in-pad avoidance strategies that collectively reduce ingress failure events. The guidelines are presented in a format directly usable by PCB designers and hardware engineers working on agricultural and environmental monitoring IoT products operating in humid continental climates.

title: Energy-neutral operation thresholds for LoRaWAN nodes with piezoelectric harvesting in wind-exposed farmland
abstract: Piezoelectric energy harvesting from wind-induced structural vibrations in agricultural infrastructure — fences, irrigation pipes, and support poles — offers an alternative to solar harvesting in conditions of persistent cloud cover or dense canopy shading. This paper derives and experimentally validates theoretical energy-neutral operation thresholds for LoRaWAN sensor nodes equipped with cantilever-beam piezoelectric transducers mounted on fence posts in open Vojvodina farmland. We characterised the wind speed probability distributions at three sites over 18 months and correlated them with harvested electrical power output measured at sub-hourly resolution. A duty-cycle optimisation model is developed that adjusts reporting frequency to match instantaneous energy income, ensuring storage buffer charge remains above a minimum operational threshold throughout low-wind periods. Hardware implementation on a custom RISC-V-based ultra-low-power microcontroller platform is described, including the impedance matching network between transducer and storage element. Results show that energy-neutral operation is achievable with average wind speeds exceeding 3.1 m/s at 2 m mounting height, a condition met for more than 71% of the annual deployment period at the tested locations. The study provides a replicable methodology for harvesting feasibility assessment applicable to other geographic contexts and structural mounting configurations.

title: FIELDNET architecture: scalable gateway placement for heterogeneous rural sensor deployments
abstract: Rural wireless sensor networks serving precision agriculture applications must accommodate heterogeneous node densities, varying terrain, and a mix of sensing modalities within a unified network architecture. This paper describes the gateway placement methodology and network architecture developed within the FIELDNET project, which deployed over 200 LoRaWAN nodes across 35 km² of mixed farmland in northern Serbia. We present a coverage optimisation algorithm based on a modified greedy set-cover formulation incorporating terrain elevation data, vegetation attenuation estimates, and node priority weighting derived from agronomic data value assessments. The algorithm is evaluated against a brute-force exhaustive placement baseline and a commercial network planning tool, achieving within 4% of optimal coverage with a fraction of the computation time. Network topology supports three tiers: battery-powered leaf nodes reporting infrequently, mains-powered relay aggregators providing local data buffering, and fibre-connected primary gateways feeding the cloud backend. We detail the protocol adaptations made to standard LoRaWAN Class A and Class B operation modes to support relay-assisted communication in areas of insufficient gateway signal strength. End-to-end latency and packet delivery measurements collected across all deployment phases are reported, demonstrating that the proposed architecture meets the data freshness requirements of irrigation scheduling and frost warning applications.

title: Low-power embedded systems for IoT: design patterns and energy optimisation
abstract: This book chapter provides a comprehensive treatment of design patterns and energy optimisation strategies for low-power embedded systems intended for IoT deployment, with an emphasis on agricultural and environmental monitoring applications. The chapter opens with a taxonomy of power consumption sources in a typical sensor node, decomposing energy expenditure across sensing, computation, communication, and sleep state management. Systematic methods for profiling and attributing current draw using both hardware instrumentation and software energy models are described. A catalogue of firmware design patterns is then presented, including event-driven wake scheduling, peripheral power gating, adaptive sampling, and voltage-scaling strategies applicable to ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V class microcontrollers. Each pattern is accompanied by illustrative pseudocode and quantitative energy savings figures drawn from real embedded deployments. The chapter subsequently addresses hardware-level optimisations including LDO versus switched-mode regulator selection, decoupling strategy for RF transceivers, and crystal oscillator start-up energy minimisation. A worked design example integrates multiple patterns into a complete LoRaWAN soil moisture node, tracing the iterative optimisation process from a 12 mA average current baseline to a final 38 µA operating average. The chapter concludes with a discussion of emerging ultra-low-power microcontroller architectures and their implications for next-generation batteryless sensor nodes.

title: Coverage Analysis in Two-Tier Cellular Networks Using Poisson Point Processes
abstract: This paper develops a tractable analytical framework for evaluating downlink coverage probability in a two-tier heterogeneous cellular network where macro base stations and pico base stations are modeled as independent homogeneous Poisson point processes on the plane. Using tools from stochastic geometry, closed-form expressions for the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) distribution are derived under Rayleigh fading assumptions. The analysis accounts for open and closed access policies at the pico tier. Numerical results show that deploying pico base stations at a density four times that of macros increases median coverage probability by approximately 18 percentage points relative to a single-tier deployment, provided that a sufficiently biased cell association rule is applied. Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000 network realizations confirm the analytical expressions. The framework provides a baseline for evaluating more complex tier configurations without site-specific deployment data.

title: Stochastic Geometry Models for Wireless Networks
abstract: This book chapter reviews the principal stochastic geometry tools used for modeling and analyzing wireless networks, with emphasis on spatial point process theory, the Campbell theorem, and the probability generating functional. The chapter covers homogeneous and inhomogeneous Poisson processes, hardcore processes, and cluster processes, and explains how each captures different aspects of real deployment data. Derivation procedures for coverage probability, average rate, and outage probability are presented in a unified notation. Case studies drawn from single-tier, two-tier, and millimeter-wave scenarios illustrate the scope of the methodology. The chapter also discusses limitations of the approach, including the assumption of independence between point processes and the difficulty of incorporating correlated shadowing. It is intended as a self-contained introduction for graduate students and researchers entering the field.

title: Coverage and Rate in Millimeter-Wave Heterogeneous Networks with Directional Antennas
abstract: The use of millimeter-wave frequencies in the 28–73 GHz range introduces blockage-dependent propagation that differs substantially from sub-6 GHz behavior. This paper models a millimeter-wave small-cell layer overlaid on a sub-6 GHz macro layer using a two-state line-of-sight/non-line-of-sight propagation model and a random Poisson point process for base station locations. Directional antenna patterns at both transmitter and receiver are incorporated using a sectored antenna model. Coverage probability and average achievable rate expressions are derived as functions of base station density, beamwidth, and blockage density. Results from a parameter sweep over building densities representative of four urban morphologies in Central Europe show that coverage probability is highly sensitive to blockage density, varying by up to 35 percentage points between open suburban and dense urban scenarios at the same base station density. Analytical results are cross-checked against ray-tracing-based simulations provided by a collaborating group.

title: Load-Aware Coverage Probability in Multi-Tier Networks Under Non-Poisson Traffic Distributions
abstract: Standard stochastic geometry results for heterogeneous networks assume that users are distributed as an independent Poisson point process. This paper examines the effect of spatially correlated user distributions, modeled as a Neyman-Scott process, on load-aware coverage probability. A nearest-neighbor load estimation heuristic is incorporated to approximate the conditional interference seen by a typical user under varying load at serving and interfering cells. Analytical bounds for coverage probability under high and low load regimes are derived and compared with simulations using a synthetic traffic trace generated from taxi GPS data scaled to a mid-size Serbian city. Results indicate that correlated traffic can cause the median SINR to differ from the independent-user prediction by 1.8 to 4.2 dB depending on cluster scale and macro-to-pico density ratio. The study highlights scenarios where the Poisson user model produces acceptable approximations and where it does not.

title: Joint Uplink-Downlink Analysis of Heterogeneous Networks Using Stochastic Geometry
abstract: Most stochastic geometry analyses of heterogeneous cellular networks consider only the downlink direction. This paper develops a unified framework covering both uplink and downlink coverage probability for a two-tier network where user equipment transmit powers are subject to open-loop fractional power control. The SINR distributions for both links are characterized under Nakagami-m fading with integer m, extending results previously limited to the Rayleigh case. The coupling between uplink interference from users served by neighboring cells and downlink interference from base stations is explicitly modeled. Numerical evaluation for m values of 1, 2, and 4 shows that the uplink coverage probability is substantially more sensitive to user density than downlink coverage in the pico tier. Results are validated against link-level simulations using a 3GPP Urban Micro channel model. The framework is intended to support joint uplink-downlink resource management studies.

title: Interference Characterization for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Assisted Heterogeneous Networks
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) alter the interference landscape in heterogeneous networks because reflected signals introduce additional coherent components whose spatial distribution depends on RIS placement and phase configuration. This paper derives expressions for the aggregate interference seen by a typical user in a Poisson-distributed small-cell network augmented by a single RIS panel of fixed size placed on a building facade. The analysis uses a product-of-distances path-loss model for the cascaded base-station-to-RIS-to-user link and treats RIS phase shifts as fixed. Coverage probability expressions are obtained for the case of a single dominant RIS contribution and verified via Monte Carlo simulation over 50,000 network drops. Results show that a 64-element RIS placed 30 meters from the user improves the fifth-percentile SINR by 4.1 dB on average but also increases interference at users in adjacent cells by 0.9 dB on average. The dependency on RIS orientation and proximity is quantified.

title: Spatial Outage Analysis for UAV-Assisted Coverage in Rural Heterogeneous Networks
abstract: Rural and peri-urban areas in Central and Eastern Europe are characterized by sparse terrestrial infrastructure, motivating the use of unmanned aerial vehicles as temporary aerial base stations. This paper models a ground macro network augmented by a single hovering UAV base station and analyzes the outage probability seen by ground users distributed as a homogeneous Poisson point process. The UAV altitude is treated as a deterministic parameter, and the probability of line-of-sight to the UAV is modeled as a logistic function of elevation angle calibrated to an ITU-R rural environment. Outage probability is minimized over UAV altitude and horizontal positioning using a gradient-based numerical procedure. Results for a 400 km² rural Vojvodina area show that the optimal UAV altitude ranges from 80 to 220 meters depending on terrestrial base station density, and that coverage holes exceeding 2 km in diameter can be fully served at the target SINR threshold. The analysis is validated against measurements from a commercial UAV platform borrowed from a partner institution.

title: Tractable Bounds for Coverage Probability in Networks with Correlated Shadowing via Shot-Noise Fields
abstract: The assumption of independent shadowing at different base stations is a standard simplification in stochastic geometry analyses that is violated in environments where large obstacles affect multiple links simultaneously. This paper models correlated shadowing through a shot-noise field driven by a Poisson process of obstacles, allowing for analytical tractability while capturing spatial correlation structure. Upper and lower bounds for downlink coverage probability are derived using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applied to the Laplace transform of the shot-noise interference field. The bounds are evaluated for a single-tier macrocell network and for a two-tier HetNet at a range of obstacle densities and heights consistent with a dense urban morphology. Compared with independent log-normal shadowing predictions, the correlated model reduces the median coverage probability estimate by 2.3 to 6.7 percentage points depending on obstacle density. The derivation methodology is self-contained and extendable to richer propagation scenarios.

title: A Multivariate CUSUM Scheme with Adaptive Estimation of Covariance Structure for Batch Chemical Processes
abstract: Classical multivariate CUSUM charts assume a fixed in-control covariance matrix, an assumption routinely violated in batch manufacturing where operating conditions shift between phases. This paper proposes replacing the static covariance estimate with a sliding-window estimator updated at each sampling instant, with the window length selected by minimising a penalised prediction error over a rolling validation segment. The scheme was evaluated on a publicly available benchmark dataset from a simulated batch reactor (50 process variables, 1 000 batches) as well as on data collected from a plastics-extrusion line at a partner facility. On the benchmark, the average run length to detection for mean-shift magnitudes between 0.5 and 2.0 standard deviations improved by 18–34% compared with the fixed-covariance baseline, at the cost of a 7% increase in false-alarm rate. Parameter sensitivity, computational cost per sample, and the practical question of selecting the penalty coefficient are discussed in detail. The method is implemented in a freely available R package accompanying the paper.

title: Comparison of Kernel Density and Parametric Approaches to Control-Chart Limit Setting Under Non-Normality
abstract: Control limits in Shewhart-type charts are almost always derived under a Gaussian assumption. When process measurements exhibit skewness or heavy tails, this leads to inflated false-alarm rates or missed detections. This paper compares five methods for setting control limits on individual measurements: standard ±3σ, Johnson transformation, Box–Cox transformation, Pearson-family fitting, and nonparametric kernel density estimation with reflection boundary correction. Simulations covered twelve non-normal distributions (skewness 0.5–4.0, kurtosis 3–12) at sample sizes of 100, 300, and 1 000 in-control observations. The kernel density method achieved the closest empirical false-alarm rates to the nominal 0.27% in 10 of 12 distributions at n = 300, but required careful bandwidth selection. A practical decision flowchart is provided. The findings are illustrated using vibration amplitude data from a rotating-machine testbed in the authors' laboratory.

title: Online Detection of Covariance Shifts in Industrial Sensor Arrays Using the Generalised Likelihood Ratio Test
abstract: Changes in the covariance structure of a multivariate sensor stream can signal developing faults before any univariate indicator crosses a threshold. This paper applies a sequential generalised likelihood ratio (GLR) test to detect covariance shifts in an online, computationally efficient manner. The test statistic is computed over a sliding dual-window: a reference window of fixed length and a test window that grows until a detection is declared. Theoretical bounds on average run length are derived under a Wishart distribution model and confirmed by Monte Carlo simulation for dimensions p = 5, 10, 20 with 10 000 replicates each. The method is applied to a 14-channel temperature and pressure dataset from a district-heating substation, where it detected three confirmed maintenance events 40–120 seconds earlier than the plant's existing alarm system. Computational complexity is O(p²) per new sample after initial setup.

title: Monitoring Nonlinear Process Dynamics with a Kernel Principal Component Analysis Control Chart: A Practical Assessment
abstract: Kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) projects nonlinear process data into a feature space where conventional Hotelling T² and Q statistics can be applied. Despite a substantial theoretical literature, practical guidance on kernel and hyperparameter selection for SPC purposes remains limited. This paper presents a systematic assessment of radial-basis-function and polynomial kernels across four industrial benchmark datasets (Tennessee Eastman process, simulated polymerisation reactor, rolling-mill dataset, and an in-house compressor dataset) using fault-detection rate and false-alarm rate as primary metrics. Cross-validation on in-control data was used to select the bandwidth parameter. Results show that RBF-KPCA outperforms linear PCA on three of four datasets, with the compressor data yielding the largest improvement (fault-detection rate 81% vs. 57% at a 1% false-alarm rate). The effect of the number of retained components is also analysed. An open-source Python implementation is included.

title: Bayesian Change-Point Models for Multivariate Non-Stationary Time Series in Continuous Manufacturing
abstract: Many continuous manufacturing processes operate under time-varying mean and variance due to raw-material variability and gradual equipment wear. Standard SPC methods tuned on historical data deteriorate in such environments. This paper formulates a Bayesian online change-point detection model (BOCPD) extended to multivariate observations under a Normal-Inverse-Wishart conjugate prior. The model simultaneously estimates the probability of a change and updates the predictive distribution after each new sample. Two variants are compared: one with a fixed hazard rate and one with a hazard rate estimated from past inter-change intervals using empirical Bayes. On simulated data with p = 8 variables, 500 change points, and signal-to-noise ratios between 0.5 and 3.0, the empirical-Bayes variant reduced the mean detection delay by 1.8 samples at a fixed false-alarm rate of 0.5%. The method was validated on accelerometer data from a CNC milling machine spindle over a six-month period.

title: Unsupervised Segmentation of Industrial Time Series via a Penalised Piecewise-Stationary Model
abstract: Long industrial time series collected from cyber-physical systems rarely satisfy stationarity over their full length. This paper treats segmentation as a model-selection problem: a piecewise-stationary multivariate Gaussian model is fitted, and the number and positions of segments are chosen by minimising a modified BIC penalising both the number of segments and their minimum length. Optimisation uses a dynamic programming algorithm with complexity O(n²) in the number of observations. The approach is compared with binary segmentation and wild binary segmentation on 24 synthetic scenarios (varying segment lengths 50–500 and p = 4–16 variables) and on three industrial datasets: a paper-machine headbox, a wastewater treatment blower, and a refrigeration compressor. BIC-guided dynamic programming achieved the lowest mean absolute error in estimated change-point locations on 19 of 24 synthetic scenarios and recovered all manually labelled regime changes in the wastewater dataset.

title: Statistical Process Control for Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey of Methods and Open Challenges
abstract: Cyber-physical systems produce streams of heterogeneous sensor data at high sampling rates, creating both opportunities and difficulties for statistical process control. This chapter surveys methods applicable to the monitoring of such systems, organising them along four dimensions: the stationarity assumption (static vs. adaptive), the observation structure (univariate vs. multivariate), the supervision level (supervised vs. unsupervised), and the computational setting (batch vs. online). For each combination, representative methods are described and their assumptions, strengths, and computational requirements are tabulated. Special attention is given to the interaction between control-chart theory and machine-learning approaches, including isolation forest, autoencoders, and one-class SVMs as anomaly scorers whose output feeds threshold-based alarms. Open challenges discussed include distribution shift under normal ageing, alarm rationalisation in dense sensor networks, and the absence of labelled fault data. The chapter concludes with a set of benchmark recommendations for the community.

title: One-Class SVM Anomaly Scores as Control-Chart Statistics: Calibration, Threshold Setting, and Recalibration Frequency
abstract: One-class support vector machines produce a real-valued decision score that can serve as a univariate control-chart statistic, enabling the combination of nonlinear pattern recognition with the interpretability of run rules and average-run-length guarantees. This paper addresses three practical questions: (1) how to calibrate raw SVM scores to approximate a false-alarm probability, (2) how to set the control limit given a desired in-control ARL, and (3) how frequently the SVM must be retrained to maintain calibration when the in-control distribution drifts slowly. Using a Platt-scaling calibration step and a bootstrap-based limit-setting procedure, the method achieves in-control ARLs within 5% of nominal across six simulated drift scenarios. Recalibration triggered by a secondary drift-detection statistic on residuals reduced worst-case ARL inflation from 43% to 9% on a simulated six-month conveyor-belt dataset with gradual load increase. The paper reports training times and discusses feasibility for edge deployment.

title: Federated Learning for Distributed Statistical Process Monitoring Across Multiple Production Lines
abstract: When identical or similar machines operate at multiple plants, it is attractive to pool monitoring knowledge across sites without centralising raw sensor data for privacy or bandwidth reasons. This paper adapts federated averaging to train a shared anomaly-detection model for multivariate SPC, with each plant training locally on its own data and contributing model updates to a central aggregator. Four federated aggregation strategies are compared against a centralised baseline and a local-only baseline on a network of five simulated production lines with heterogeneous fault-type distributions. Federated averaging with client-side control-limit adjustment achieved fault-detection rates within 4 percentage points of the centralised model on three of five sites, while local-only models lagged by 11–19 percentage points. Communication overhead, convergence speed, and the influence of data heterogeneity on model drift are quantified. Limitations regarding non-IID client data are discussed.
