title: Benchmarking Change-Point Detection Algorithms on Annotated Industrial Datasets: Methodology and Initial Results
abstract: Published evaluations of change-point detection algorithms are difficult to compare because they use different datasets, annotation conventions, and performance metrics. This paper proposes a reproducible benchmarking protocol and applies it to eight algorithms—including BOCPD, PELT, RUPTURES binary segmentation, wild binary segmentation, BOCD with student-t likelihood, L2-cost dynamic programming, a kernel change-point detector, and an LSTM-based method—on six annotated industrial datasets contributed by the authors and three collaborating groups. Annotations were produced by domain engineers and reviewed by a second engineer; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Metrics reported include F1 score at a tolerance of five samples, mean absolute error in change-point location, and computational time per 1 000 observations. No single algorithm dominated across all datasets. PELT performed best on datasets with large between-segment variance ratios, while the kernel method was most robust on datasets with covariance-only changes. The datasets and annotation files are deposited in a public repository.

title: Monitoring Concept Drift in Online Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial IoT Streams
abstract: Anomaly detection models deployed in industrial IoT environments face concept drift: the statistical properties of normal operation change over months due to seasonal variation, equipment ageing, or production-mix changes. This paper proposes a two-level monitoring architecture in which a primary anomaly detector (isolation forest trained offline) is supervised by a secondary drift monitor based on the Page–Hinkley test applied to the score distribution's empirical mean and variance. When drift is confirmed, a lightweight incremental update procedure re-weights the forest using recent in-control samples without full retraining. The architecture is evaluated on 18 months of data from three IoT-connected air-compressor units at a manufacturing plant, comprising approximately 4.7 million observations per unit. The drift monitor correctly identified seven of eight documented operating-regime transitions with one false trigger. Post-update fault-detection rates recovered to within 3% of the initial model's performance within 2 000 samples of each transition.

title: Adaptive Binarisation of Low-Contrast Scanned Documents Using Local Gradient Statistics
abstract: Binarisation is a critical pre-processing step for OCR pipelines operating on degraded paper documents. This paper evaluates three families of local thresholding algorithms—Sauvola, Niblack, and a modified Bradley–Roth variant—on a corpus of 480 scanned Serbian administrative forms from the 1990s, characterised by ink fade and uneven illumination. We propose a parameter selection scheme based on histogram skewness and local contrast variance that adapts the window size and correction factor without manual tuning. On the DIBCO 2011 benchmark the method achieves an F-measure of 88.3% and a pseudo-recall of 90.1%, comparable to supervised deep learning approaches while requiring no training data. Processing time on a single CPU core averages 1.4 seconds per A4 page at 300 dpi. The approach is integrated into an open-source preprocessing toolkit released alongside the paper.

title: Serum non-esterified fatty acid concentrations in the last week of pregnancy as predictors of postpartum ketosis in Holstein cows on commercial farms in Vojvodina
abstract: Blood samples were collected from 148 Holstein cows at seven, five, and two days before expected calving on four commercial dairy farms in Vojvodina. Serum non-esterified fatty acid (NEFA) concentrations were measured by enzymatic colorimetric assay. Cows were monitored for the first 21 days postpartum and classified as ketotic (blood BHB ≥ 1.2 mmol/L on at least two consecutive measurements) or healthy. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis identified a prepartum NEFA threshold of 0.42 mmol/L at seven days before calving, yielding a sensitivity of 74% and specificity of 81% for prediction of postpartum ketosis. Multiparous cows and animals with body condition score above 3.75 at dry-off had significantly higher prepartum NEFA values (p < 0.01). These findings support targeted surveillance of high-risk animals in the close-up dry period and suggest that a single NEFA measurement one week before parturition can be incorporated into practical herd health programmes without substantial labour costs.

title: Liver biopsy-based assessment of hepatic triglyceride content in early-lactation cows with varying degrees of negative energy balance
abstract: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous liver biopsy was performed on 62 Holstein cows at 7 and 21 days in milk across three farms. Biopsy samples were subjected to Soxhlet lipid extraction and histological staining with Oil Red O to quantify hepatic triglyceride content and assess hepatocyte vacuolation grade. Negative energy balance was estimated from daily feed intake records and milk energy output. Triglyceride content ranged from 8 mg/g wet tissue in cows with mild energy deficit to 147 mg/g in severely affected animals. Histological grade correlated strongly with biochemical triglyceride content (Spearman rs = 0.88, p < 0.001). Cows in the highest triglyceride quartile showed significantly elevated serum AST and GLDH activities from day 7 onward. The biopsy protocol was well tolerated, with no serious complications in 124 procedures. Results confirm that Oil Red O grading is a reliable semiquantitative proxy for biochemical lipid measurement in field conditions.

title: Diagnostic performance of a portable beta-hydroxybutyrate meter compared with laboratory analysis for on-farm detection of subclinical ketosis
abstract: A portable whole-blood BHB meter (Medivet BHB, a fictional device) was evaluated against a validated laboratory photometric method in 319 blood samples from cows at 3–21 days in milk collected on eight farms in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of −0.07 mmol/L (limits of agreement −0.41 to +0.27 mmol/L) across the diagnostic range 0.5–3.5 mmol/L. At the standard subclinical ketosis threshold of 1.2 mmol/L, the meter achieved sensitivity 88.2% and specificity 92.7% relative to laboratory reference. Agreement was slightly lower at extreme temperatures below 10°C, which is relevant for winter use in unheated barns. Repeatability (coefficient of variation 4.1%) was acceptable for clinical decision-making. The meter is suitable for weekly pen-level screening programmes and reduces the delay between sampling and treatment decision from 24 hours to under two minutes.

title: Cytokine and acute-phase protein responses in dairy cows with fatty liver at peak lactation: an exploratory study
abstract: Fourteen Holstein cows diagnosed with grade III hepatic lipidosis (liver biopsy triglyceride > 100 mg/g wet weight) at 7 days in milk were compared with fourteen healthy controls matched for parity and farm. Serum concentrations of haptoglobin, serum amyloid A, TNF-α, and IL-6 were measured by commercial bovine ELISA kits at days 7, 14, and 21 postpartum. Cows with fatty liver had significantly higher haptoglobin at all three time points (p < 0.01) and elevated IL-6 at day 7 only (p = 0.03). Serum amyloid A did not differ significantly between groups. Spearman correlation between haptoglobin at day 7 and hepatic triglyceride content was moderate (rs = 0.61). These preliminary data suggest that inflammatory activation accompanies severe hepatic lipidosis and that haptoglobin may supplement liver enzyme measurements in a diagnostic panel, though a larger study is needed to confirm specificity.

title: Seasonal variation in postpartum BHB concentrations in Vojvodina dairy herds: a two-year longitudinal analysis
abstract: Whole-blood BHB measurements from 1,847 cows at days 5 and 12 postpartum were collected over 24 months on six commercial farms in Vojvodina. The dataset was analysed using generalised linear mixed models with farm and cow as random effects, and calving month, parity, and milk yield at first test-day as fixed effects. Prevalence of subclinical ketosis (BHB ≥ 1.2 mmol/L) was highest in February–March (38.4%) and lowest in July–August (19.7%). After adjustment for parity and milk yield, winter calving remained a significant predictor (OR 2.11, 95% CI 1.54–2.89). Farms feeding maize silage with higher dry matter content showed lower seasonal fluctuation, pointing to feed quality as a modifiable risk factor. The results suggest that seasonal monitoring intensity should be increased in the January–April period on farms in continental climates with pronounced winter housing.

title: Effect of propylene glycol drenching in the first five days postpartum on BHB, liver enzymes, and reproductive outcomes in high-risk cows
abstract: A randomised controlled trial enrolled 84 multiparous Holstein cows identified as high-risk based on prepartum NEFA above 0.42 mmol/L. Cows were allocated to propylene glycol (PG) drench (300 mL once daily, days 1–5 postpartum; n = 42) or untreated control (n = 42). Blood was collected on days 1, 5, 10, and 21 postpartum. PG-treated cows showed significantly lower BHB on days 5 and 10 (p < 0.01) and a lower proportion exceeding the subclinical ketosis threshold on day 5 (29% vs. 52%, p = 0.03). AST and GLDH did not differ significantly between groups at any time point. Time to first detected oestrus was shorter in treated cows (mean 52 vs. 68 days, p = 0.04). First-service conception rate was numerically higher in the PG group (54% vs. 43%) but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.24). The findings support selective rather than blanket use of PG, targeted at cows with elevated prepartum NEFA.

title: Rumen microbiome composition in early-lactation cows with and without subclinical ketosis: a 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing study
abstract: Rumen fluid was collected by orogastric tube from 40 Holstein cows at 7 days in milk: 20 with subclinical ketosis (BHB 1.2–2.9 mmol/L) and 20 healthy controls matched for farm and parity. DNA was extracted and the V3–V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene was sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform. Alpha diversity (Shannon index) did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.18). Beta diversity analysis (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, PERMANOVA) showed significant separation between groups (p = 0.009, R² = 0.09). Ketotic cows had a higher relative abundance of Prevotella spp. and lower abundance of Ruminococcaceae. Volatile fatty acid profiles in rumen fluid showed higher acetate-to-propionate ratios in ketotic animals (mean 4.8 vs. 3.9, p = 0.006). The study is limited by sample size and cross-sectional design; causality between microbiome shifts and ketosis cannot be established. The data motivate a larger longitudinal investigation.

title: Ketosis and subclinical metabolic disorders in transition dairy cows: pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management
abstract: This book chapter provides a synthesis of current knowledge on energy metabolism in periparturient dairy cows, covering the physiological adaptations of lipolysis and hepatic gluconeogenesis, the mechanisms leading to excessive fat mobilisation and hepatic triglyceride accumulation, and the consequences for immune function, reproduction, and production longevity. Diagnostic approaches are reviewed, including blood BHB measurement, liver enzyme panels, milk-based indicators, and ultrasound liver assessment, with commentary on their practical applicability and thresholds validated in regional (Central and Eastern European) dairy herds. Management strategies discussed include dry cow nutrition, body condition control, transition group management, and metabolic profiling programmes. Special attention is given to subclinical forms of the disease, which are numerically dominant and economically important but often undetected. The chapter also reviews published evidence on pharmaceutical and nutritional interventions, noting where evidence from randomised trials is limited.

title: Point-of-care lactate measurement as a supplementary marker of metabolic acidosis severity in clinical ketosis cases
abstract: Forty-three Holstein cows presenting with clinical signs consistent with type-I or type-II ketosis were enrolled. Whole-blood lactate was measured using a handheld lactate analyser alongside routine BHB and blood gas parameters at initial examination and after 48 hours of treatment. Mean blood lactate at presentation was 2.4 mmol/L (range 0.8–6.1). Lactate correlated moderately with BHB (rs = 0.49, p < 0.001) and more strongly with base excess (rs = −0.68, p < 0.001). Cows with lactate above 3.0 mmol/L at presentation had significantly lower recovery rates at 48 hours (54% vs. 82%, p = 0.03). Lactate concentration above 3.5 mmol/L at presentation was associated with fourfold higher odds of culling within 30 days. The findings suggest that lactate adds prognostic information beyond BHB in clinical ketosis, particularly for identifying cows unlikely to respond to standard intravenous glucose therapy.

title: Machine learning classification of subclinical ketosis risk using routinely collected farm management data: a proof-of-concept analysis
abstract: Routinely collected records from 1,104 Holstein cows across nine Vojvodina farms—including calving data, dry-off BCS, parity, transition group feeding records, and first test-day milk composition—were used to train and evaluate random forest and logistic regression classifiers for prediction of subclinical ketosis (BHB ≥ 1.2 mmol/L at day 7 postpartum). The dataset was split 70/30 for training and testing with stratification by farm. The random forest model achieved area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.76 compared with 0.68 for logistic regression on the test set. The five most important features in the random forest were: BCS at dry-off, parity, days on transition ration, first test-day fat-to-protein ratio, and farm identity. Model calibration was acceptable (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.21). The analysis demonstrates that existing farm data have moderate predictive value and identifies data collection improvements—specifically standardised BCS recording protocols—that would likely increase model performance.

title: Longitudinal BHB and NEFA trajectories from two weeks prepartum to six weeks postpartum in Holstein and Simmental cows under commercial farming conditions
abstract: Blood samples were collected at standardised intervals (days −14, −7, +3, +7, +14, +21, +42 relative to calving) from 88 Holstein and 74 Simmental cows on four farms. BHB and NEFA were measured by enzymatic colorimetric methods. Mixed-effects modelling of the concentration-time trajectory showed that Holstein cows reached higher peak BHB values (mean 1.38 vs. 0.91 mmol/L, p < 0.001) and a later peak (day 7 vs. day 5). NEFA peaked sharply at day 3 in both breeds and declined more rapidly in Simmental animals. Prevalence of subclinical ketosis at any point in the first three weeks was 44% in Holstein versus 27% in Simmental cows. Breed × farm interaction was significant for BHB trajectory, indicating that farm management practices modify breed-associated differences. These data are relevant for farms transitioning between breeds and for calibrating breed-specific BHB thresholds in regional screening protocols.

title: Corticosterone deposition in feathers grown during transport and lairage: is a short-term acute stress event detectable?
abstract: Feather corticosterone is assumed to reflect stress experienced during feather growth, but whether a single acute stressor near the end of the growth period contributes measurably to feather corticosterone concentrations is debated. In this experiment, one group of broilers (n = 40) underwent commercial transport and two-hour lairage on day 40, while a control group (n = 40) remained undisturbed. Both groups were slaughtered on day 42. Feathers collected at slaughter were segmented into proximal and distal halves; corticosterone was extracted from each segment separately. No significant difference in distal-segment corticosterone was found between transported and control birds (p = 0.41), whereas proximal segments showed a non-significant trend toward higher concentrations in the transported group. The findings suggest that feather corticosterone at slaughter predominantly reflects rearing conditions rather than acute transport stress, reinforcing the interpretation of feather measures as chronic welfare indicators.

title: A simulated annealing approach to irregular polygon nesting with minimum bounding rectangle constraints
abstract: This paper addresses the two-dimensional irregular strip packing problem, in which a set of non-convex polygonal pieces must be arranged within a fixed-width strip so as to minimise total strip length. A simulated annealing (SA) metaheuristic is implemented using no-fit polygon (NFP) calculations to evaluate feasible placements. The cooling schedule follows a geometric reduction with an initial temperature calibrated on 200 random placement trials per instance. Benchmark instances from the ESICUP repository with 25 to 197 pieces are used; the algorithm achieves an average material utilisation of 83.4%, improving the best-known solutions on four out of twelve instances. Computational time on a single-core 2.4 GHz processor ranges from 18 to 340 seconds depending on instance size and polygon complexity. Sensitivity analysis shows that NFP pre-computation accounts for 62% of total runtime, motivating future work on approximate NFP methods. The implementation is validated against a commercial marker-making system on a real denim fabric dataset of 48 pattern pieces.

title: Comparative evaluation of bottom-left and skyline placement heuristics for non-convex piece nesting
abstract: Constructive placement heuristics are widely used in industrial nesting software because of their low computational cost. This study systematically compares the bottom-left (BL) and skyline-based heuristics across three industry-sourced datasets: upholstery fabric (31 distinct piece types), shoe upper leather (54 piece types), and automotive gasket sheet metal (19 piece types). Each dataset contains between 120 and 480 pieces per production order. The skyline heuristic is implemented with a variable beam width to handle re-entrant polygon boundaries. Results show that skyline placement yields 2.1 to 4.7 percentage points higher utilisation than BL across all datasets, at a computational overhead of less than 0.8 seconds per layout on a standard workstation. The study also quantifies the sensitivity of both heuristics to piece sequencing: sorting by decreasing bounding-box area improves skyline utilisation by an average of 1.3%. The findings support using skyline placement as the initialisation step for subsequent metaheuristic refinement.

title: Integer programming formulation for multi-roll cutting-plan scheduling in textile production
abstract: Cutting-plan scheduling in textile manufacturing requires allocating pattern-piece layouts to fabric rolls while respecting roll length, colour lot constraints, and due-date windows for garment assembly. This paper proposes a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that integrates roll assignment, layout sequencing, and spread-height decisions. The model is tested on data from a mid-sized Serbian garment manufacturer with 12-week planning horizons and up to 85 active orders simultaneously. A column generation approach decomposes the problem into a master scheduling problem and a subproblem equivalent to a weighted bin-packing instance. On instances with up to 40 orders, the column generation procedure closes 94% of the LP relaxation gap within 600 seconds. Material utilisation improved from 78.2% to 81.9% compared to the company's manual planning procedure, and roll inventory turnover increased by 11% over a three-month pilot. Limitations regarding shade-banding constraints are discussed.

title: Parallel computation of no-fit polygons using multi-core CPU architectures
abstract: No-fit polygon (NFP) computation is the dominant bottleneck in exact irregular nesting solvers. For non-convex polygons with 40 or more vertices, NFP generation via the orbital sliding method can require several seconds per pair. This paper investigates parallelisation of NFP pre-computation across piece-pair combinations using OpenMP on shared-memory systems with 4, 8, and 16 cores. Three polygon datasets from apparel and leather goods sectors are used, containing piece sets with 20 to 312 vertices per polygon. Speedup factors of 3.6, 6.9, and 11.2 are measured on 4-, 8-, and 16-core configurations respectively, with near-linear scaling on convex sub-problems and super-linear cache effects on concave pairs at 8 cores. Integration into a simulated annealing nesting loop reduces total solver wall-clock time by 58% on the largest test instance without changing solution quality. Memory overhead for storing the full NFP matrix grows as O(n²) and becomes a practical constraint above 250 pieces.

title: 2D Nesting Algorithms: Methods, Benchmarks, and Industrial Applications
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured review of computational methods for two-dimensional nesting of irregular shapes, covering exact, heuristic, and metaheuristic approaches developed between 1980 and 2015. The chapter begins with a formal problem taxonomy distinguishing strip packing, bin packing, and knapsack variants, then describes NFP- and direct-trigonometry-based overlap detection. Sections are devoted to constructive heuristics, local search, simulated annealing, genetic and evolutionary algorithms, and hybrid methods. Industrial application contexts covered include apparel, footwear, furniture upholstery, sheet metal, and glass cutting, with reported utilisation ranges and computation-time benchmarks from published literature. A summary table of 47 representative algorithms lists problem type, piece count, reported utilisation, and hardware context. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems including three-dimensional extensions, multi-material scheduling integration, and the handling of grain-direction constraints in fabric cutting.

title: Effect of piece rotation discretisation on material utilisation in apparel marker-making
abstract: Industrial marker-making systems typically restrict piece rotation to a discrete set of allowed angles—most commonly 0° and 180°, with some systems permitting 90° increments or finer steps. This paper quantifies the trade-off between rotation resolution and material utilisation on a dataset of 22 apparel style markers, each containing 35 to 112 pattern pieces. A simulated annealing nesting solver is run with rotation sets of {0°, 180°}, {0°, 90°, 180°, 270°}, {0°, 45°, …, 315°}, and a continuous interval [0°, 360°] sampled at 1° resolution. Across the 22 markers, moving from the binary set to the 8-direction set yields an average utilisation gain of 1.8 percentage points, while moving to continuous rotation yields an additional 0.9 points at three times the computation time. For styles with grain-direction constraints on at least 60% of pieces, the gain from continuous rotation drops to 0.3 points, making finer discretisation economically marginal in those cases. Fabric cost and throughput implications are estimated for a hypothetical production volume of 50,000 garments.

title: A beam search procedure for sequencing cutting plans to minimise fabric roll changeover
abstract: In garment production, adjacent cutting plans laid on the same spreading table ideally consume pieces from the same fabric roll to reduce changeover time and shade variation. This paper formulates roll-to-plan assignment and plan sequencing as a combined optimisation problem and solves it with a beam search procedure guided by a composite objective weighting material utilisation (70%) and roll changeover frequency (30%). The beam width is varied from 5 to 50 and evaluated on planning instances with 15 to 60 cutting plans drawn from production records of two Serbian garment manufacturers. At beam width 20, the procedure reduces average changeover frequency by 27% relative to first-fit sequencing while reducing material utilisation by only 0.4 percentage points. Solution time is under 4 seconds for all instances. The paper also reports a sensitivity analysis showing that the 70/30 objective weighting is robust within the range 60/40 to 80/20 for the tested instances.

title: Outer-boundary approximation of non-convex polygons for fast feasibility checking in nesting solvers
abstract: Exact NFP computation for highly concave polygons is expensive and sometimes numerically unstable when boundaries include near-parallel edges or very short segments. This paper proposes replacing exact NFPs with convex-hull-augmented outer-boundary approximations (OBA) for an initial placement phase, followed by exact NFP verification only for retained candidate positions. The OBA is constructed by iteratively merging convex components of each polygon. On a test set of 30 polygon pairs with 60 to 180 vertices, OBA generation is 8.3 times faster than exact NFP computation on average. Integrating OBA into a hybrid simulated annealing / local search nesting solver reduces total solve time by 31% on a 96-piece leather cutting instance while yielding placements within 0.6% of those obtained with full exact NFPs. The paper discusses error bounds on the approximation gap and conditions under which OBA-based placements are guaranteed to be feasible without exact verification.

title: Integrating nesting optimisation with production order batching in a make-to-order furniture manufacturer
abstract: Furniture upholstery cutting presents a combined order-batching and nesting problem: grouping production orders into cutting batches determines which piece sets must be nested together, directly affecting fabric utilisation. This paper studies a medium-sized furniture manufacturer in Vojvodina with 80 to 120 active orders per week and 14 fabric types. A two-stage optimisation framework is proposed: an order-batching model based on set-partitioning assigns orders to batches sharing the same fabric type and colour, and a simulated annealing nesting solver then generates the physical layouts. The interaction between batch size and nesting efficiency is characterised over eight weeks of production data: increasing average batch size from 6 to 14 orders raises nesting utilisation from 76.3% to 81.7% at the cost of an average order lateness increase of 0.8 days. A Pareto front illustrating this trade-off is presented, and a simple weighting rule for practitioners is proposed. The framework was piloted over four weeks, reducing average fabric waste from 22.1% to 17.4%.

title: Benchmark dataset for 2D irregular nesting from Central and Eastern European manufacturing: description and baseline results
abstract: Public benchmark datasets for 2D irregular nesting are dominated by instances from UK, Spanish, and Brazilian industry sources. This paper describes a new dataset of 34 nesting instances collected from seven manufacturing companies in Serbia, Croatia, and Romania, covering apparel (12 instances), leather goods (8 instances), automotive gaskets (7 instances), and foam-based furniture (7 instances). Each instance is provided as a set of DXF-format polygon files together with roll or sheet dimensions and allowed rotation sets. The paper reports baseline utilisation results obtained with three reference solvers: a bottom-left heuristic, a simulated annealing solver, and an open-source NFP-based local search. Baseline utilisation ranges from 71.2% to 88.6% across instances and solvers. Statistical comparison using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test shows that the regional dataset is significantly harder (p < 0.01) than the ESICUP suite on instances with more than 80 pieces, attributed to higher average polygon concavity. The dataset is made publicly available under a CC BY 4.0 licence.

title: Variable neighbourhood search for multi-objective nesting with concurrent minimisation of material waste and cutting-path length
abstract: CNC cutting machines incur tool travel cost that depends on both the positions and the sequencing of piece outlines on the cutting plan. This paper addresses a bi-objective nesting problem minimising material waste and total cutting-path length simultaneously. A variable neighbourhood search (VNS) algorithm alternates between three neighbourhood structures: piece translation, piece swap, and sequence reversal of a cutting-path segment. The two objectives are combined via an ε-constraint method to generate approximate Pareto fronts. Experiments on six instances from an automotive gasket manufacturer show that layouts optimised solely for material utilisation have cutting paths 18 to 34% longer than layouts optimised for path length alone. VNS generates Pareto fronts of 15 to 22 non-dominated solutions per instance in under 20 minutes. A sensitivity analysis indicates that cutting-path savings of 12% can typically be achieved with less than 1 percentage-point sacrifice in material utilisation by selecting solutions in the knee region of the Pareto front.

title: Learning-guided construction heuristics for 2D nesting using graph neural networks
abstract: Constructive nesting heuristics require hand-crafted placement rules whose performance varies substantially across polygon types. This paper investigates whether a graph neural network (GNN) can learn a placement policy from solved instances, replacing the manual rule. Each partial layout is represented as a graph in which nodes encode piece geometric features (area, perimeter, convexity ratio) and edges encode spatial relationships between already-placed pieces and the candidate piece. The GNN is trained on 4,800 solved instances generated from the CEE benchmark dataset using a supervised imitation-learning objective. On a held-out test set of 400 instances, the GNN-guided heuristic achieves average utilisation of 82.1% compared to 79.4% for the best constructive baseline, at comparable computation time. Generalisation experiments on ESICUP instances not seen during training show a 1.2 percentage-point improvement over baseline, suggesting transferability. The approach requires approximately 14 hours of training on a single GPU; inference time per placement decision is under 3 milliseconds.

title: Scheduling multi-layer fabric spreads with heterogeneous roll lengths: a set-covering model and Lagrangian relaxation
abstract: In high-volume garment production, fabric is spread in multiple layers before cutting, and rolls of different remaining lengths must be combined to cover the required spread length. Mis-matched roll combinations create tail-end fabric scraps that contribute significantly to total waste. This paper models the multi-layer spread scheduling problem as a set-covering integer program in which columns represent feasible roll combinations for a given required spread length. A Lagrangian relaxation of the coverage constraints is solved iteratively to obtain lower bounds; the relaxed subproblem decomposes into independent knapsack problems solvable in polynomial time. On instances with 20 to 60 active fabric rolls and 8 to 25 cutting orders, the Lagrangian bound closes 89% of the integrality gap on average, and an LP-rounding post-processing step produces near-optimal integer solutions. Applied to three months of production data from a Serbian shirt manufacturer, the method reduces tail-end waste by 14.3% relative to current manual planning.

title: Energy consumption mapping in precast concrete curing processes and its integration into activity-based cost models
abstract: Thermal curing of precast elements is one of the highest energy-cost activities in a concrete component facility, yet it is rarely disaggregated in standard costing systems. This study used data loggers on six steam-curing chambers at two production sites in Serbia over a combined 31-week period to record temperature profiles and energy draw at 15-minute intervals. Total measured energy consumption for curing averaged 38 kWh per cubic metre of finished product across both sites, with nighttime cycles consistently consuming 12–17% less energy due to ambient temperature effects. An energy cost sub-module was integrated into an existing TDABC framework, adding three time equations that capture chamber loading density, element geometry class, and season. The revised model reduced the unexplained cost variance in the heating resource pool from 18% to 6%. Recommendations are given for rescheduling curing cycles to off-peak tariff windows.

title: Stochastic demand modelling for shift scheduling: a scenario-based approach using historical order data from a contract electronics manufacturer
abstract: Deterministic demand forecasts used in shift scheduling ignore forecast uncertainty and can lead to under- or over-staffing when actual orders deviate from plan. This paper develops a scenario-based stochastic programme for a contract electronics assembly plant in Subotica with 310 employees. Fifty demand scenarios per week were generated from three years of historical order data using a bootstrap procedure stratified by product family. The two-stage stochastic programme determines a committed weekly shift structure in the first stage and allows limited worker reallocation across lines in the second stage. Solving with sample average approximation required an average of 22 minutes per weekly planning problem on a 16-core workstation. Out-of-sample evaluation over 52 test weeks showed a 6.1 percent reduction in total labour cost variance compared to deterministic scheduling, with mean cost within 1.4 percent of the deterministic optimum. Sensitivity to scenario count is reported for 10, 25, 50, and 100 scenarios.

title: Rumen bacterial community composition in heifers supplemented with wheat DDGS: a DGGE-based survey
abstract: Denaturing gradient gel electrophoresis (DGGE) was used to profile rumen bacterial communities in twelve Holstein heifers (8 months of age) randomly assigned to diets containing 0 or 15% wheat-based DDGS for 60 days. Rumen samples were collected via oro-ruminal probe on days 0, 30, and 60. After DNA extraction, the V3 region of the 16S rRNA gene was amplified and resolved by DGGE. Band richness and the Shannon diversity index were calculated from digitised gel images. Heifers on the DDGS diet showed a modest increase in band richness at day 30 (mean 18.4 vs. 16.1 bands, P = 0.048) that was not maintained at day 60. Principal component analysis of banding patterns indicated a partial separation between dietary groups at day 30. Specific bands were excised, sequenced, and tentatively assigned to Butyrivibrio and Ruminococcus genera. The findings indicate that wheat DDGS causes transient shifts in bacterial diversity that resolve as the rumen adapts over two months.

title: Sulphur intake and rumen hydrogen sulphide accumulation in heifers fed diets high in corn DDGS
abstract: Elevated sulphur content in corn DDGS is a recognised risk factor for polioencephalomalacia in ruminants, yet data from heifers fed diets typical of Central European production systems are scarce. Sixteen Holstein heifers were fed a basal total mixed ration supplemented with 0, 15, 25, or 35% corn DDGS (n = 4 per group) over 70 days. Total dietary sulphur was measured by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry. Rumen headspace hydrogen sulphide (H2S) was sampled two hours post-feeding using gas-tight syringes and quantified by gas chromatography. At 35% DDGS inclusion, mean dietary sulphur reached 0.48% DM and mean rumen headspace H2S was 1,840 ppm, both exceeding recommended thresholds. No clinical signs were observed, but the 35% group showed reduced dry matter intake during weeks 8–10. Results indicate that corn DDGS inclusion should be kept below 25% DM when sulphur content of the batch exceeds 0.6% DM.

title: 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing reveals diet-driven shifts in core rumen microbiome taxa of prepubertal dairy heifers fed DDGS
abstract: The rumen microbiome of prepubertal Holstein heifers (n = 24, aged 4–6 months) was profiled by Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene. Animals were assigned to three dietary groups: control (0% DDGS), low DDGS (12% DM), and high DDGS (24% DM) for 90 days. After quality filtering, a mean of 43,200 reads per sample were obtained and clustered into amplicon sequence variants (ASVs). At the phylum level, Bacteroidota and Bacillota dominated across all groups. The high DDGS group showed a significantly lower Bacillota:Bacteroidota ratio (1.31 vs. 1.67 in control, P = 0.03). At the genus level, relative abundance of Prevotella was higher in the high DDGS group (+4.2 percentage points, P = 0.01), while Ruminococcus was lower (−2.1 percentage points, P = 0.04). Alpha diversity metrics (Chao1, Faith PD) did not differ between groups. The study provides sequence-level evidence that moderate DDGS inclusion selectively modulates fibre-degrading and propionate-producing taxa.

title: Methane output and rumen fermentation parameters in heifers fed corn versus wheat DDGS at equal inclusion rates
abstract: Corn and wheat DDGS differ in fibre and sulphur content, yet their comparative effects on enteric methane emissions in young dairy stock have rarely been measured under the same experimental conditions. Twenty-four Holstein heifers (10 months) were allocated to three groups: control, 18% corn DDGS, or 18% wheat DDGS on a DM basis. After a 21-day adaptation period, methane output was estimated over four days using the SF6 tracer gas technique. Rumen fluid was sampled by oro-ruminal probe for VFA, pH, and ammonia nitrogen on days 21 and 42. Mean methane emission per kg DM intake was 21.3 g (control), 18.9 g (corn DDGS), and 20.1 g (wheat DDGS). The corn DDGS group emitted significantly less methane per kg DM intake (P = 0.04). Acetate-to-propionate ratio was lower in the corn DDGS group (2.8 vs. 3.3, P = 0.02). Wheat DDGS showed intermediate effects. These differences align with differences in rumen fibre degradability between the two co-product types.

title: Association between rumen microbiome composition at weaning and subsequent growth performance in heifers transitioned to DDGS-containing rations
abstract: Early microbial colonisation of the rumen may predispose calves to better or worse adaptation to fermentable feed co-products later in life. This prospective cohort study followed 36 Holstein heifer calves from weaning (age 10 weeks) through 6 months of age. At weaning, rumen microbiome profiles were obtained via oro-pharyngeal swab and 16S rRNA sequencing. At 14 weeks, animals were gradually transitioned to a ration containing 18% corn DDGS. Body weight, average daily gain, and rumen pH were recorded monthly. Hierarchical clustering of weaning-time microbiome profiles identified two distinct clusters differing in Fibrobacter and Butyrivibrio abundances. Animals in the Fibrobacter-enriched cluster showed a higher average daily gain over the trial period (0.88 vs. 0.79 kg/day, P = 0.03) and maintained a more stable rumen pH after DDGS introduction. The results suggest that weaning-time rumen microbiome composition partially predicts adaptability to DDGS-supplemented rations, though the mechanisms require further investigation.

title: Cyclical Properties of Remittance Inflows to Serbia: Evidence from Quarterly Balance-of-Payments Data 2000–2009
abstract: This paper examines whether remittance flows to Serbia behave counter-cyclically, pro-cyclically, or acyclically over the period 2000–2009 using quarterly balance-of-payments data from the National Bank of Serbia. A VAR framework with four lags is estimated, incorporating GDP growth, the unemployment rate, and the real effective exchange rate as conditioning variables. Remittance series are deflated using the CPI and seasonally adjusted via X-13-ARIMA. Results indicate a statistically significant counter-cyclical component: a one-percentage-point fall in domestic GDP growth is associated with a 0.34 percentage-point increase in the remittance-to-GDP ratio in the subsequent quarter. The effect weakens after 2004, coinciding with EU enlargement and shifts in migrant destination countries. The paper argues that the stabilising role of remittances in Serbia is real but contingent on origin-country labour market conditions, which limits policy reliance on this channel as an automatic fiscal stabiliser.

title: Remittances and Household Consumption Smoothing in Rural Vojvodina: A Micro-Survey Approach
abstract: Using a purpose-designed survey of 412 households in rural Vojvodina conducted in autumn 2012, this study investigates the extent to which remittance receipts buffer household consumption against income shocks. The survey targeted municipalities with above-average emigration rates, identified through municipal registry data. An instrumental variable approach is used, instrumenting remittance receipt with the share of close relatives abroad and bilateral migration stock data from OECD. Results show that households receiving remittances exhibit consumption variance roughly 28 percent lower than comparable non-receiving households, controlling for asset holdings, land ownership, and formal employment status. The stabilisation effect is concentrated in food and utility expenditure rather than durable goods investment. The findings suggest remittances operate primarily as insurance transfers rather than investment capital in this context, with implications for rural development policy in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina.

title: Remittances as a Fiscal Substitute: Public Revenue Shortfalls and Private Transfers in Post-Crisis Balkan Economies
abstract: This book chapter examines whether increased remittance inflows partially compensate for shortfalls in public revenue during fiscal stress episodes in Balkan labour-exporting economies. Drawing on an unbalanced panel of six countries over 2004–2015 and using a difference-in-differences design around crisis-episode years defined by IMF programme triggers, the analysis tests whether remittance-to-GDP ratios rise systematically in years of fiscal consolidation. Results indicate a modest but robust positive association: each percentage-point reduction in government consumption-to-GDP is associated with a 0.18 percentage-point rise in remittances-to-GDP in the following year. The chapter situates this finding within broader debates on the fungibility of diaspora resources and cautions against designing social protection systems that implicitly depend on private cross-border transfers, given the political fragility of migration corridors.

title: Determinants of Remittance Volatility: Evidence from a Cross-Country Dataset of 18 European Labour-Sending Countries
abstract: This paper constructs a novel measure of remittance volatility—the coefficient of variation of annual remittance inflows over rolling five-year windows—and models its determinants for 18 European labour-sending countries over 1995–2016. Independent variables include migrant stock concentration indices, the share of migrants in top-three destination countries, institutional quality scores from Worldwide Governance Indicators, financial inclusion indices, and bilateral trade openness. System GMM estimation is used to address endogeneity and dynamic persistence. Remittance concentration in a single destination country is the strongest positive predictor of volatility, with a one-standard-deviation increase in concentration associated with a 12 percent increase in the volatility measure. Institutional quality at home reduces volatility, consistent with a portfolio-rebalancing motive. The findings suggest that diversification of migration corridors reduces macroeconomic exposure to remittance shocks.

title: Mobile Money Adoption and Remittance Channel Choice Among the Serbian Diaspora in Germany
abstract: A survey of 286 Serbian-born migrants in Frankfurt, Stuttgart, and Munich conducted in 2019 investigates the determinants of channel choice for remittances—formal bank transfer, money transfer operator, or mobile application—and the effect of mobile application adoption on transfer frequency and cost. Multinomial logistic regression shows that respondents under 40, employed in the services sector, and with a smartphone-owning recipient in Serbia are significantly more likely to use mobile applications. Adopters report an average transfer fee of 1.9 percent compared with 4.7 percent for money transfer operators. Transfer frequency is 1.4 times higher among mobile adopters, and average transfer size is 23 percent smaller, suggesting a shift toward more frequent small transfers. The paper discusses the implications of this granularity for recipient household cash-flow management and for the measured volatility of aggregate remittance series.

title: Remittance Inflows During the COVID-19 Recession: Did the Balkan Pattern Differ from Global Trends?
abstract: Global remittance flows proved surprisingly resilient during the 2020 recession, defying initial World Bank projections of a 20 percent decline. This paper asks whether Western Balkan economies shared this pattern and attempts to identify mechanisms. Using monthly central bank data for Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia from January 2018 to December 2021, a counterfactual trend is constructed via synthetic control and compared with actual outcomes. Serbia and North Macedonia both recorded positive deviations from trend in 2020 Q2–Q3, while Bosnia and Herzegovina showed a brief but statistically significant trough in April–May 2020. Survey evidence from a follow-up of 180 Serbian diaspora households suggests that fiscal stimulus payments in host countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) temporarily inflated migrants' disposable incomes and supported transfers. The paper concludes that host-country fiscal policy was an important, if underexamined, driver of Balkan remittance resilience during the pandemic.

title: Remittances and Current Account Sustainability in Small Open Balkan Economies: A Long-Run Cointegration Approach
abstract: This paper examines the long-run relationship between remittance inflows and current account balances in Serbia, Albania, Kosovo, and Moldova over 1996–2021 using the Pesaran–Shin–Smith bounds testing approach to cointegration within an ARDL framework. Remittances are treated both as a current account credit item and as a potential driver of import demand through the income effect. In three of four countries, a statistically significant long-run equilibrium is confirmed between remittances, the trade balance, and the real exchange rate. In Serbia specifically, a one-percent permanent increase in remittances is associated with a 0.41 percent improvement in the current account balance in the long run, but this is partially offset by a 0.19 percent increase in import demand, implying a net improvement of approximately 0.22 percent. The error correction term is negative and significant across all specifications, confirming adjustment toward the long-run equilibrium. Policy implications for exchange rate and trade policy under high remittance dependence are discussed.

title: Measuring Diaspora Financial Literacy and Its Effect on Investment-Oriented Remittances: Survey Evidence from the Serbian Community in Austria
abstract: A structured survey of 341 Serbian migrants in Vienna and Graz assessed financial literacy using an adapted Lusardi-Mitchell instrument and linked scores to the declared purpose of remittances sent over the preceding twelve months. Respondents were categorised as sending primarily consumption-support, savings-support, or investment-oriented transfers. Higher financial literacy scores are positively associated with investment-oriented transfers (odds ratio 1.62, 95 percent CI 1.21–2.17), controlling for income level, length of stay, and intended return. Among respondents scoring in the top quartile, 34 percent directed at least part of their transfers toward business start-up or property investment in Serbia, compared with 11 percent in the bottom quartile. The paper estimates that a standardised financial literacy programme targeted at migrants could shift approximately 8–12 percent of consumption-support transfers into investment-oriented flows based on extrapolation of the regression coefficients, though the authors note the limits of such projections.

title: Brain Drain, Remittances, and Human Capital Accumulation: A General Equilibrium Perspective on Vojvodina
abstract: This paper presents a calibrated two-period overlapping-generations model of a small open region characterised by high emigration rates and significant remittance receipts, parameterised to match Vojvodina's demographic and financial data for 2010–2024. The model allows for both a direct human capital investment channel (remittance-financed education) and an indirect channel through reduced labour supply of recipient households. Simulations suggest that under current migration and remittance rates, remittance inflows finance approximately 7 percent of total private education expenditure in Vojvodina, partially offsetting the human capital loss from emigration. However, the model also identifies a crowding-out effect on female labour force participation among recipient households, consistent with empirical evidence from the household survey in Takács and Varga (2013). Policy experiments suggest that conditional transfer mechanisms tied to educational enrolment could increase the human capital return to remittances by 15–22 percent in the model environment.

title: Recursive Least-Squares Identification of PMSM Stator Resistance Under Step Load Variations
abstract: Accurate knowledge of stator resistance is essential for sensorless control and thermal monitoring of permanent-magnet synchronous motors. This paper presents a recursive least-squares (RLS) scheme for online identification of stator resistance in a surface-mounted PMSM rated at 2.2 kW. The identification model is derived in the stationary αβ reference frame, and a variable forgetting factor is introduced to improve tracking speed during abrupt load steps. Experiments were conducted on a test bench using a programmable eddy-current dynamometer capable of imposing load steps of 0–14 N·m within 80 ms. The forgetting factor was varied between 0.92 and 0.99 based on a residual error threshold. Compared to a fixed forgetting factor baseline, the proposed scheme reduced the resistance estimation error from 4.1% to 1.3% during 100% rated torque steps. Thermal effects were partially decoupled by incorporating a first-order temperature model fed by a PT100 sensor embedded in the stator winding. Results demonstrate that the approach is practical for integration into existing field-oriented control frameworks without additional computational overhead beyond standard DSP resources.

title: Comparison of EKF and UKF for Simultaneous Estimation of d- and q-Axis Inductances in Interior PMSM Drives
abstract: Interior permanent-magnet synchronous motors exhibit significant inductance variation due to magnetic saturation, complicating precise torque and speed control. This study compares the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and unscented Kalman filter (UKF) for simultaneous online estimation of d- and q-axis inductances in a 4 kW interior PMSM operating under variable speed and load profiles. The state vector is augmented with the two inductances, and both filters are implemented on a dSPACE DS1202 MicroLabBox running at a 10 kHz sampling rate. Test profiles include sinusoidal load torque at 0.5 Hz, 2 Hz, and 5 Hz with amplitudes up to 18 N·m. The UKF achieved a root-mean-square estimation error of 0.31 mH for Ld and 0.44 mH for Lq across all profiles, compared to 0.52 mH and 0.71 mH for the EKF. The computational cost of the UKF was approximately 2.4 times higher, but remained within the available cycle budget. Process and measurement noise covariance matrices were tuned systematically using a constrained optimisation routine, and sensitivity to initial covariance settings is discussed quantitatively.

title: Effect of Inverter Nonlinearity on Parameter Identification Accuracy in PMSM Drives at Low Speed
abstract: Inverter nonlinearities—including dead-time, forward voltage drop of switching devices, and blanking time—introduce harmonic distortions in the applied voltage that degrade the accuracy of model-based parameter identification algorithms at low rotational speeds. This paper quantifies the estimation error introduced by these effects on an RLS-based identification scheme for a 1.5 kW surface-mounted PMSM operating between 50 and 300 rpm. Voltage distortion was characterised experimentally by comparing reference voltage commands with terminal voltages measured using a calibrated high-bandwidth differential probe at 1 MHz sampling. A compensation lookup table indexed by phase current sign and magnitude was constructed and evaluated against an uncompensated baseline. With compensation active, the mean error in identified stator resistance dropped from 6.8% to 1.9% at 80 rpm and from 3.4% to 0.8% at 200 rpm. The analysis also shows that q-axis inductance estimation is more sensitive to dead-time distortion than d-axis inductance, which is attributed to the distribution of harmonic content relative to the rotor position. The findings are relevant for applications requiring reliable identification during start-up or low-speed operation.
venue: IET Power Electronics and Drives

title: Characterising Interference Patterns in Dense 2.4 GHz IoT Deployments: A Measurement Study
abstract: Dense IEEE 802.15.4 and IEEE 802.11 co-existence is studied through a structured measurement campaign conducted across three office floors totalling 1,200 square metres at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad. Forty-two sensor nodes and eight Wi-Fi access points were deployed simultaneously, and spectrum occupancy was logged over 72 hours using USRP B210 radios. Packet reception rates, channel busy times, and inter-arrival jitter are reported across 16 non-overlapping and overlapping channel configurations. Results show that the median packet loss rate in the densest configuration reaches 18% on channel 11 when Wi-Fi traffic exceeds 4 Mbps aggregate. A simple empirical interference model is fitted to the data and validated against a held-out 24-hour trace. The dataset and measurement scripts are released publicly. The model is intended as an input layer for scheduling algorithms in subsequent work.

title: Energy Neutral Operation Bounds for Solar-Harvesting Sensor Nodes With On-Board Inference Workloads
abstract: The paper derives analytical bounds on the maximum sustainable computation rate for sensor nodes powered exclusively by small-area photovoltaic panels under Central European solar irradiance profiles. A finite-capacity supercapacitor energy buffer is modelled, and the tradeoff between inference task complexity and buffer underflow probability is characterised using a Markov chain formulation. Irradiance traces from Novi Sad (2014–2018, hourly resolution) sourced from the national meteorological service are used as the stochastic input. Results show that a node with a 1 F supercapacitor and a 2 cm² panel can sustain a 30 ms inference task every 4.2 seconds at a 99% non-interruption probability in summer, falling to one task every 14.7 seconds in December. A lookup-table controller is designed and validated on STM32L4-based hardware. Code is made available as open source.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Offloading Granularity Strategies in Multi-Tier Edge Architectures
abstract: Three offloading granularity models—binary, fractional, and subtask-level—are compared in a simulated three-tier architecture consisting of end devices, a local edge server, and a regional cloudlet. Simulation is implemented in OMNeT++ 5.6 using the INET framework extended with a custom task queue module. Workload traces are derived from a smart-factory IoT pilot involving 120 temperature, vibration, and current sensors sampled at 100 Hz. Energy consumption, end-to-end latency, and server CPU utilisation are measured over simulated intervals of 3,600 seconds under low, medium, and high congestion conditions. Subtask-level offloading reduces 95th-percentile latency by 22% over binary offloading at the cost of a 9% increase in signalling overhead. Fractional offloading provides a middle ground with lower implementation complexity. Results suggest that subtask decomposition is worthwhile only when task graphs contain at least five parallelisable branches.

title: Scheduling Harvested-Energy Allocation Across Concurrent Sensing and Communication Tasks on a Single MCU
abstract: This work addresses the problem of allocating harvested energy between concurrent sensing and wireless transmission tasks executing on a single microcontroller. A priority-inversion-free earliest-deadline-first variant is adapted to account for a stochastically replenished energy budget. The scheduler is implemented on a Nordic nRF9160 system-in-package device. A hardware emulator injects synthetic energy traces derived from piezoelectric and RF energy harvesting measurements taken from a vibrating industrial pipe fixture. Over 48-hour continuous operation tests, the proposed scheduler reduces task deadline miss rate from 11.3% to 3.7% compared to an energy-oblivious EDF baseline, while maintaining average radio duty cycle below 4%. The paper also provides a worst-case energy consumption analysis that supports offline dimensioning of the storage element.

title: A Congestion Index for Heterogeneous IoT Access Networks and Its Use in Offloading Triggers
abstract: The paper proposes a lightweight congestion index computed from three observable quantities—channel busy ratio, queue occupancy at the edge node, and per-flow retransmission rate—that can be calculated on resource-constrained hardware without packet inspection. The index is calibrated against ground-truth throughput measurements on a 35-node testbed spanning IEEE 802.15.4, LoRaWAN, and NB-IoT access segments. Calibration uses a ridge regression fit on 48 hours of labelled traffic. The index is then embedded as a trigger condition in an offloading policy: offloading is initiated only when the index exceeds a threshold tuned per access technology. Field evaluation over 14 days shows that trigger-based offloading reduces unnecessary offload invocations by 41% compared to a fixed-interval policy, with negligible increase in peak latency. The index computation requires under 0.8 ms on a Cortex-M4 core.

title: Energy Harvesting for Mobile Edge Nodes: Survey of Sources, Storage Technologies, and Scheduling Approaches
abstract: This book chapter surveys energy harvesting modalities applicable to mobile and fixed edge computing nodes in IoT deployments, covering solar, vibration-based piezoelectric, RF ambient, and thermal gradient sources. Typical harvested power ranges and temporal variability are tabulated for each source based on literature values and the authors' own measurements. Storage technologies—lithium polymer batteries, supercapacitors, and hybrid cells—are compared on capacity, leakage rate, and cycle lifetime. The chapter then surveys scheduling frameworks published between 2012 and 2022, categorising them by optimisation objective (energy neutrality, latency minimisation, reliability) and solution method (Lyapunov, dynamic programming, reinforcement learning, heuristic). A comparison table of 34 reviewed systems is provided. Open research directions highlighted include multi-source harvesting coordination and predictive models trained on locally collected irradiance data.

title: Deadline-Aware Partial Offloading Under Shared Uplink Congestion: A Fluid Model Analysis
abstract: A fluid model is developed to analyse the interaction between multiple IoT devices sharing a single uplink channel when each device independently applies a partial offloading policy with hard task deadlines. The model captures the feedback loop in which individual offloading decisions increase aggregate channel load, which in turn degrades the transmission time for all devices. Fixed-point analysis yields conditions on device count and arrival rate under which deadline satisfaction probability exceeds 95%. Numerical results for populations of 10, 20, and 40 devices show that without coordination, deadline miss rate grows superlinearly beyond 28 devices for the tested parameter set. A simple token-bucket coordination mechanism is proposed that restores near-linear scaling. The analysis is validated against event-driven simulations in NS-3 with relative error below 6% across all tested configurations.

title: A Benchmark Dataset and Baseline Heuristics for the Dynamic Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time-Dependent Travel Times
abstract: The paper introduces a publicly available benchmark dataset constructed from GPS traces collected over six months in the Novi Sad metropolitan area. The dataset contains 120 problem instances at three demand scales (50, 100, and 200 delivery requests) with time-dependent arc costs derived from measured congestion profiles. Three classical constructive heuristics—nearest-neighbour insertion, savings algorithm, and time-oriented sweep—are evaluated as baselines. Results show that time-dependent arc costs increase average route length by 8–14 % compared to static cost assumptions, with the largest gap occurring in morning peak windows. The dataset and baseline implementations are released under an open licence to support reproducibility. The authors discuss instance generation methodology, anonymisation procedures, and known limitations arising from the urban street network in Vojvodina.

title: Adaptive Large Neighbourhood Search for the Multi-Depot Dynamic Vehicle Routing Problem
abstract: The paper applies adaptive large neighbourhood search (ALNS) to the multi-depot dynamic vehicle routing problem (MD-DVRP) in which new customer requests arrive throughout the planning horizon and vehicles may return to any of several depots. The algorithm is implemented with six destroy operators and four repair operators; operator selection probabilities are updated every 50 iterations using a score-based weight adjustment scheme. Tests on 90 benchmark instances with two to five depots and 100 to 400 customers show that ALNS reduces total distance by an average of 6.3 % relative to a greedy insertion baseline and finds solutions within 1 % of the best-known values for 74 % of static instances from the literature. Runtime on a standard workstation remains below 90 seconds for all tested instance sizes. Sensitivity analysis reveals that depot placement has a stronger influence on solution quality than fleet size within the tested ranges.

title: Integration of Real-Time Traffic State Estimates into Operational Dispatch for Multi-Depot Fleets
abstract: This chapter reviews approaches for coupling traffic state estimation systems with operational routing engines, with emphasis on multi-depot settings common in regional logistics. The review covers three estimation paradigms—loop detector aggregation, floating vehicle data, and model-based prediction—and discusses interface requirements for feeding updated arc cost matrices into a running optimisation loop without triggering full re-optimisation. A taxonomy of integration architectures is presented, distinguishing between loosely coupled systems where the estimator and router exchange data at fixed intervals, and tightly coupled systems where the router subscribes to event-driven traffic updates. Practical challenges including data latency, inconsistent coordinate systems, and partial network coverage are documented using case material from a logistics operator in southern Hungary and one in northern Serbia. The chapter concludes with a gap analysis identifying open research questions in partial re-optimisation under streaming data.

title: Sensitivity of Rolling-Horizon VRP Solutions to Demand Arrival Rate Estimation Errors
abstract: Accurate forecasting of customer request arrival rates is assumed by most rolling-horizon routing frameworks, yet real deployments routinely face estimation errors. This study quantifies how errors in the estimated arrival rate affect total route cost and service level in a rolling-horizon vehicle routing model. A controlled simulation experiment introduces multiplicative noise on the true arrival rate at levels of ±10 %, ±25 %, and ±50 %, across three demand patterns (uniform, morning-peak, and bimodal). Results across 360 simulation runs show that a 25 % underestimation of arrival rate increases late deliveries by 31 % on average, while overestimation by the same margin raises total distance by 9 % due to premature vehicle dispatch. The sensitivity is asymmetric: underestimation is more damaging to service level than overestimation. A simple correction heuristic that inflates the estimated rate by 15 % recovers most of the service level loss at a 4 % cost in total distance.

title: A Matheuristic for Real-Time Reoptimisation of Large-Scale Urban Delivery Fleets with En-Route Request Insertion
abstract: Urban delivery fleets with more than 80 vehicles and continuous request arrival present a computational challenge for exact methods in real-time settings. This paper proposes a matheuristic that decomposes the fleet into geographic clusters, solves a mixed-integer programme for each cluster independently, and applies a post-optimisation exchange phase across cluster boundaries. The en-route insertion subproblem is handled by a modified regret-based heuristic that accounts for remaining vehicle capacity and time window feasibility. Experiments on 30 large instances, each with 80–120 vehicles and 400–700 dynamically arriving requests, show that the matheuristic finds solutions within 2.8 % of a lower bound computed offline, with average reoptimisation times of 38 seconds. The method is validated against data from a Novi Sad-based logistics company operating a mixed fleet of vans and cargo bicycles over a three-month pilot.

title: Incorporating Driver Shift Constraints into Multi-Depot Dynamic Routing: Model and Computational Results
abstract: Labour regulations impose strict limits on continuous driving time, mandatory rest periods, and total shift duration, yet these constraints are rarely embedded directly into dynamic multi-depot routing models. This paper presents a mixed-integer model that explicitly represents driver shift state as a set of auxiliary variables and integrates shift feasibility checks into the ALNS repair operators. The model is tested on 54 instances derived from a cross-border distribution network operating between Serbia and Hungary, with two to four depots and 10 to 30 drivers per depot. Including shift constraints raises total route cost by 7–18 % compared to ignoring them, depending on demand volume and depot spacing. Violation rates when constraints are ignored post-hoc are found to exceed 30 % in high-volume scenarios, illustrating the practical importance of direct integration. A compact dataset suitable for future benchmarking is included as supplementary material.

title: Score-based Bayesian network structure learning on small-sample gene expression datasets from Arabidopsis cold-stress experiments
abstract: Inferring gene regulatory networks from observational transcriptomic data is complicated when sample sizes are small relative to the number of candidate variables. This study evaluated four score-based structure learning algorithms—BDe, BGe, BIC-penalised hill-climbing, and a tabu-search variant—on RNA-seq data from 18 Arabidopsis thaliana samples subjected to 4°C cold stress over 24 hours. We assessed edge recovery against a manually curated reference subnetwork of 42 known regulatory interactions. The BGe criterion with a conservative prior on graph complexity recovered 61% of true edges at a false discovery rate of 0.18, outperforming BIC-penalised search (52% recovery, FDR 0.24). We also examined sensitivity to prior specification by varying hyperparameters across a grid of 120 settings. Results indicate that informative priors derived from published protein–protein interaction data improve skeleton accuracy by approximately 9 percentage points in this low-n regime. Data and scoring code are deposited in a public repository.

title: Comparing constraint-based and hybrid structure learning for drought-responsive gene networks in maize
abstract: Maize (Zea mays) exhibits a coordinated transcriptional response to water deficit that involves hundreds of genes, yet comprehensive network maps constructed from observational field data remain scarce due to limited replication. We applied PC, FCI, and MMHC algorithms to a dataset of 31 RNA-seq profiles collected from maize leaf tissue at three time points during progressive drought imposed in a controlled greenhouse setting. Genes were pre-filtered to 210 drought-annotated candidates using a publicly available functional annotation. Structural Hamming distance to a reference DAG constructed from published ChIP-seq evidence was used as the primary accuracy metric. MMHC achieved the lowest SHD (148 ± 12) compared with PC (173 ± 15) and FCI (167 ± 14). Stability of learned edges was evaluated through a 100-iteration bootstrap, revealing that 38 edges were consistently present across more than 80% of bootstrap samples. We discuss how sparsity assumptions in each algorithm interact with the biological connectivity typical of stress-signalling modules.

title: Handling missing values in RNA-seq time-series before Bayesian network learning: a simulation study
abstract: Missing observations are common in plant transcriptomics experiments owing to sample degradation, sequencing failure, or design constraints. Yet most Bayesian network structure learning implementations assume complete data. We conducted a simulation study to compare the effect of five imputation strategies—mean substitution, k-NN imputation, SoftImpute, a Gaussian graphical model-based approach, and listwise deletion—on the accuracy of subsequently learned network structures. Synthetic datasets were generated by sampling from ten known DAGs of 50 and 100 nodes, with missingness rates of 10%, 20%, and 30% imposed under MCAR, MAR, and MNAR mechanisms. Each combination was repeated 500 times. SoftImpute followed by BGe-scored hill-climbing yielded the smallest average SHD under MAR conditions at all missingness rates tested, while listwise deletion performed worst under MNAR. Practical recommendations are provided for researchers working with small plant stress transcriptomic cohorts where missingness is likely non-random.

title: Bayesian network inference of heat-stress gene regulatory modules in sunflower using prior knowledge from orthologous species
abstract: Transferring regulatory prior knowledge from well-studied species to crops with sparser genomic resources can improve network inference quality. We constructed informative edge priors for Helianthus annuus heat-stress genes by mapping orthologous interactions from Arabidopsis and soybean databases, weighted by sequence similarity scores. These priors were incorporated into a Bayesian network structure learning pipeline using the BGe criterion with a custom prior distribution over graphs. The resulting networks were learned from 24 sunflower RNA-seq samples collected at 38°C and 42°C over a six-hour time course. Cross-validated predictive log-likelihood was used to compare models built with and without orthology-derived priors. Prior-informed models showed a mean improvement of 11.3% in held-out log-likelihood. We identified a subnetwork of seven transcription factors showing consistent regulatory connectivity across temperature conditions, three of which lack prior characterisation in sunflower. The pipeline is available as an R package.

title: Regularisation strategies for Gaussian Bayesian networks learned from high-dimensional, low-sample plant metabolomics data
abstract: Metabolomics profiles from stress-exposed plants routinely contain hundreds of features measured across few biological replicates, creating a p >> n scenario that is particularly challenging for Gaussian Bayesian network learning. We compared L1-penalised covariance estimation (graphical lasso), shrinkage-based approaches (Ledoit-Wolf, Oracle Approximating Shrinkage), and a Bayesian spike-and-slab prior on edge weights when used as starting-point estimates feeding into score-based structure search. Evaluation used LC-MS metabolomics data from 16 tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) plants under salt stress, alongside 500 synthetic datasets generated to match the observed data characteristics. Graphical lasso with cross-validated regularisation parameter provided the best trade-off between precision and recall for edges in the sparse reference network (F1 = 0.43), compared with Ledoit-Wolf (F1 = 0.37) and OAS (F1 = 0.38). We also quantified how edge orientation accuracy degrades as the feature-to-sample ratio increases beyond 10:1.

title: Dynamic Bayesian networks for modelling temporal gene expression cascades in wheat under combined heat and drought stress
abstract: Combined heat and drought stress causes yield losses in wheat that exceed those from either stress applied alone, yet the temporal regulatory dynamics underlying this interaction remain poorly characterised. We constructed dynamic Bayesian networks (DBNs) from a time-series RNA-seq experiment in bread wheat involving six time points across 48 hours of combined stress in 22 individual plants. A first-order DBN with BGe scoring and a tabu-search optimiser was applied to a filtered set of 180 stress-responsive genes. Edges in the learned DBN were compared with contemporaneous single-stress DBNs to identify interaction-specific regulatory links. Fourteen transition edges were present exclusively under combined stress, six of which connected known drought-responsive transcription factors to heat-shock protein genes. Stability of these cross-condition edges was validated using a leave-two-out resampling strategy. The work demonstrates a practical workflow for analysing combined abiotic stress responses within tight sample-size constraints common in greenhouse phenotyping.

title: Evaluating the effect of discretisation on Bayesian network structure recovery in RNA-seq gene expression data
abstract: Discrete Bayesian networks require continuous expression values to be binned before structure learning, yet the choice of discretisation method has received little systematic attention in the plant bioinformatics literature. We tested seven discretisation approaches—equal-width, equal-frequency, Hartemink's mutual information-preserving method, hierarchical clustering-based binning, and three variants of model-based clustering—on 60 RNA-seq datasets from stress experiments in rice, barley, and Arabidopsis, each with between 18 and 45 samples. Structure quality was evaluated against independently validated regulatory interactions from a plant-specific regulatory database. Hartemink's method achieved the highest mean edge precision (0.58) across datasets, though it was the most computationally expensive (mean 4.2× runtime increase relative to equal-frequency binning). Equal-frequency discretisation with three bins provided a reasonable compromise and is recommended as a default for researchers without access to substantial computing resources. Sensitivity to the number of bins was strongest in datasets with fewer than 25 samples.

title: Evaluating reproducibility of scRNA-seq clustering pipelines across five commonly used workflow managers
abstract: Reproducibility in single-cell RNA sequencing analyses depends not only on algorithmic choices but also on the computational environment, including workflow manager, container version, and execution platform. This study ran an identical scRNA-seq clustering pipeline—from raw count matrix to annotated UMAP—using Snakemake, Nextflow, WDL, CWL, and a custom Makefile-based approach across three computational environments: a local HPC cluster, a cloud instance, and a local workstation. The pipeline was applied to two datasets of 8,000 and 22,000 cells. Cell-type cluster assignments were identical across workflow managers within the same environment for deterministic steps but diverged by up to 4.1% of cells in stochastic steps when floating-point rounding behaviour differed between platforms. Conda environment pinning and container-based execution reduced inter-platform divergence to under 0.3% of cells. A minimum specification for reproducible scRNA-seq pipeline reporting was proposed, covering software versions, container hashes, and random seed logging.

title: Alkali extraction of arabinoxylan from wheat bran: effect of NaOH concentration and extraction time on yield and molecular weight distribution
abstract: Wheat bran arabinoxylan (AX) was extracted using aqueous NaOH at concentrations ranging from 0.5 to 4 M and extraction times of 1–6 hours at 30 °C. Yield of water-extractable AX increased from 8.4 % to 21.7 % (w/w dry bran) as NaOH concentration rose to 2 M, but levelled off above this point. Size-exclusion chromatography coupled with refractive index detection showed a bimodal molecular weight distribution at lower alkali concentrations, collapsing to a single population (Mw 280–320 kDa) at 2 M NaOH. The arabinose-to-xylose (A/X) ratio, determined by gas chromatography after acid methanolysis, remained within 0.55–0.62 across all conditions, suggesting limited side-chain cleavage. Phenolic acid content (ferulic and p-coumaric acids, measured by reversed-phase HPLC) decreased markedly above 1.5 M NaOH, indicating saponification of ester linkages. Optimal conditions for retaining molecular integrity while achieving acceptable yield were identified as 1.5 M NaOH, 3 hours, yielding 18.2 % AX with Mw 410 kDa. The extracted fraction was characterised as a suitable substrate for subsequent hydrolysis studies.

title: Partial hydrolysis of rye bran arabinoxylan by a commercial endo-xylanase: time-course changes in oligosaccharide profile
abstract: Rye bran arabinoxylan (Mw 520 kDa, A/X 0.71) was incubated with a commercial Thermomyces-derived endo-xylanase (GH10 family) at 50 °C and pH 5.5 over 0–240 minutes. Aliquots were taken at 12 time points and analysed by high-performance anion-exchange chromatography with pulsed amperometric detection (HPAEC-PAD). Hydrolysates at 30 min showed predominant accumulation of xylotetraose (X4) and xylopentaose (X5) together with branched arabinoxylooligosaccharides (AXOS) of degree of polymerisation (DP) 4–7. Extended hydrolysis beyond 120 min shifted the profile toward xylobiose (X2) and xylotriose (X3), with a corresponding drop in average DP from 5.1 to 2.8. Reducing sugar content (DNS method) increased linearly up to 60 min (r² = 0.98) then plateaued. The A/X ratio in the soluble fraction remained above 0.60 throughout, indicating preferential cleavage at unsubstituted backbone regions. Results indicate a hydrolysis window of 45–75 min for maximising DP 3–6 AXOS fraction yield (up to 38 % of initial AX mass).
