title: Dilute oxalic acid hydrolysis of wheat bran arabinoxylan: selectivity toward low-DP oligosaccharides and influence of temperature
abstract: Wheat bran arabinoxylan (18 % extract, Mw 310 kDa) was subjected to dilute oxalic acid hydrolysis (0.05–0.20 M, 80–120 °C, 10–60 min) in a factorial design experiment (three factors, three levels). Response variables were total AXOS yield, number-average DP of the soluble fraction (DPn), arabinose release, and furfural accumulation. Maximum AXOS yield of 44.3 % was obtained at 0.10 M oxalic acid, 100 °C, 30 min. Furfural, quantified by HPLC-UV, remained below 0.8 mg g⁻¹ substrate under these conditions, well below inhibitory thresholds for downstream fermentation. Temperature had the greatest effect on DPn reduction (partial η² = 0.61 in ANOVA), while acid concentration primarily governed arabinose side-chain removal. Correlation between arabinose release and A/X ratio drop (r = −0.89) confirmed glycosidic bond selectivity. Oxalic acid hydrolysis produced a DP 2–5 fraction purity of 72 % after membrane ultrafiltration (3 kDa cut-off), comparable to enzymatic approaches but at lower cost.

title: Comparison of GH10 and GH11 xylanases for production of prebiotic arabinoxylooligosaccharides from durum wheat bran
abstract: Two endoxylanase families—GH10 (Aspergillus-derived) and GH11 (Bacillus-derived)—were compared for their ability to generate defined AXOS fractions from durum wheat bran AX (A/X 0.48) under identical conditions (pH 5.0, 45 °C, 2 h, enzyme load 5 U g⁻¹ substrate). Oligosaccharide profiles were resolved by HPAEC-PAD and confirmed by ESI-MS. The GH10 enzyme produced a broader DP distribution (DP 2–9) and released more feruloylated AXOS, quantified by RP-HPLC (ferulic acid content 0.31 mg g⁻¹ AXOS). GH11 was more selective, generating predominantly DP 2–4 linear xylooligosaccharides with lower arabinose substitution (A/X 0.21 in product). Prebiotic potential was estimated in vitro using a pH-stat fermentation model with human faecal inoculum; the GH10 product gave significantly higher butyrate production (1.84 vs. 1.12 mmol L⁻¹ after 24 h, p < 0.05). Results support substrate-specific enzyme selection for targeted prebiotic synthesis.

title: Membrane-based fractionation of enzymatic wheat bran arabinoxylan hydrolysates: permeate composition and flux decline at different cut-offs
abstract: Enzymatic hydrolysates of wheat bran AX (GH10 xylanase, 60 min, 45 °C) were fractionated using flat-sheet ultrafiltration membranes with molecular weight cut-offs of 1, 3, and 10 kDa in a cross-flow cell at 25 °C. Feed total oligosaccharide content was 52 g L⁻¹. At 3 kDa cut-off and transmembrane pressure of 3 bar, permeate flux stabilised at 18 L m⁻² h⁻¹ after 60 min; flux decline (from 41 to 18 L m⁻² h⁻¹) followed a combined cake-pore blocking model (R² = 0.94). HPAEC-PAD analysis of permeates showed 1 kDa preferentially passed DP ≤ 3, while 3 kDa passed DP ≤ 6 with minor contamination by DP 7–9 (< 8 % area). The 10 kDa membrane retained selectivity at DP ≤ 12 but with high polymer passage. Mass balance showed 81 % recovery of DP 3–6 fraction in 3 kDa permeate after diafiltration. Data provide parameters for pilot-scale design.

title: Effect of feruloylation degree on the prebiotic index of arabinoxylan oligosaccharides in a mixed human faecal fermentation model
abstract: AXOS fractions with high (HF-AXOS, 1.8 µmol ferulic acid mg⁻¹) and low (LF-AXOS, 0.3 µmol mg⁻¹) feruloylation were produced from wheat bran by enzymatic hydrolysis followed by preparative RP-HPLC separation. Both fractions had comparable DP distributions (mean DP 4.6 vs. 4.8, assessed by HPAEC-PAD). Fermentation with pooled human faecal inocula (n = 6 donors) was conducted in batch vessels at 37 °C, pH-controlled at 6.8 for 48 h. Microbial community shifts were tracked by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (V3–V4 region). HF-AXOS selectively enriched Bifidobacterium and Roseburia genera to a greater extent than LF-AXOS (relative abundance increase 4.2× vs. 2.7× for Bifidobacterium). Butyrate production from HF-AXOS was significantly higher (2.31 mmol L⁻¹, p = 0.03). The prebiotic activity score (PAS) was 0.58 for HF-AXOS and 0.41 for LF-AXOS. Feruloylation appears to modulate both the fermentation kinetics and community selectivity.

title: Pilot-scale production of arabinoxylan oligosaccharides from wheat milling by-products: mass balance, energy consumption, and oligosaccharide purity
abstract: A process for AXOS production from wheat bran was scaled from laboratory (0.5 L) to pilot (50 L stirred-tank) level, comprising alkaline extraction, enzymatic hydrolysis (GH10 xylanase, 45 °C, 90 min), membrane ultrafiltration (3 kDa), and spray drying. Mass balance accounting tracked dry matter, oligosaccharide, and ferulic acid across all unit operations for three independent pilot runs using bran batches from a local flour mill. Overall AXOS recovery to dry powder was 31 ± 3 % (w/w starting AX). Spray-dried powder contained 74 % AXOS by mass (HPAEC-PAD quantification with xylooligosaccharide standards), with residual proteins 8 %, ash 6 %, and moisture 4 %. Energy consumption for the pilot batch was 14.2 MJ kg⁻¹ AXOS powder, with spray drying accounting for 61 % of the total. Product colour (CIELab) remained stable over 6 months storage at 20 °C and 55 % RH in sealed foil pouches. The data provide a basis for techno-economic analysis at industrial scale.

title: Arabinoxylan oligosaccharides as functional ingredients in rye crispbread: effect on texture, water activity, and in vitro prebiotic score after baking
abstract: AXOS powder produced from wheat bran (mean DP 4.8, purity 72 %) was incorporated into a rye crispbread formulation at 1, 2, and 4 % (w/w flour basis). Texture profile analysis (TPA) showed that AXOS addition at 2 % reduced crispness (fracture force decreased by 18 %) without significantly affecting hardness. Water activity (aw) at 2 % addition was 0.23, within the acceptable range for shelf-stable crackers. Maillard browning (measured as L* colour decrease) was not significantly different from control up to 2 % AXOS (p = 0.12). HPAEC-PAD analysis of crispbread aqueous extracts confirmed retention of intact AXOS oligosaccharide profile after baking at 200 °C for 12 min; total AXOS recovery was 88 % of added amount. In vitro prebiotic score (pH-stat batch fermentation, 24 h) of baked crispbread extracts was 0.52, compared with 0.58 for unheated AXOS solution, indicating minimal prebiotic function loss. Results suggest 2 % AXOS is a practical inclusion level.

title: Oat bran arabinoxylan versus wheat bran arabinoxylan as substrates for GH10 xylanase: differences in hydrolysis kinetics and oligosaccharide branching patterns
abstract: Arabinoxylan was extracted from oat bran and wheat bran under identical alkaline conditions (1.5 M NaOH, 3 h). Characterisation showed oat bran AX had a higher A/X ratio (0.82 vs. 0.55) and lower Mw (195 vs. 310 kDa). GH10 xylanase kinetics were measured by the initial-rate method at varying substrate concentrations (0.5–10 mg mL⁻¹); apparent Km was 3.1 mg mL⁻¹ for oat and 2.0 mg mL⁻¹ for wheat AX, while Vmax values were 28.4 and 41.7 µmol min⁻¹ mg⁻¹ enzyme respectively. HPAEC-PAD profiles of hydrolysates at matched reducing sugar release (1.2 mmol g⁻¹ substrate) differed substantially: oat hydrolysate was enriched in branched AXOS with DP 4–8 carrying two arabinose substituents per xylose residue, whereas wheat hydrolysate was dominated by monosubstituted and linear DP 2–5 species. ESI-MS confirmed the branching differences. The results have implications for targeting specific AXOS structures for defined prebiotic applications.

title: Influence of substrate A/X ratio on the inhibition kinetics of endo-xylanase during prolonged arabinoxylan hydrolysis
abstract: Product inhibition of a GH10 endo-xylanase was investigated during hydrolysis of three AX substrates differing in arabinose-to-xylose ratio (0.45, 0.62, 0.81), all normalised to Mw 300 kDa. Hydrolysis was monitored over 360 min at 45 °C, pH 5.0. Residual enzyme activity was measured by withdrawing aliquots, separating enzyme by 3 kDa ultrafiltration, and assaying against fresh high-Mw substrate. Activity loss followed first-order kinetics more closely for high-A/X substrate (k = 0.014 min⁻¹) than low-A/X (k = 0.007 min⁻¹). Dixon plots with xylobiose and xylotriose as model inhibitors gave Ki values of 4.2 and 11.8 mM respectively, suggesting competitive inhibition. Arabinose released into the medium showed no inhibitory effect up to 15 mM. A two-compartment kinetic model incorporating competitive inhibition by xylobiose fitted the experimental reducing sugar data (RMSE < 5 % across all three substrates). The model provides a basis for designing fed-batch enzyme dosing strategies to maintain hydrolysis efficiency.

title: Sequential enzymatic and mild acid treatment of corn bran glucuronoarabinoxylan: oligosaccharide yield, uronic acid retention, and antioxidant activity of feruloylated fractions
abstract: Corn bran glucuronoarabinoxylan (GAXOS) was treated sequentially: first with GH10 xylanase (45 °C, 60 min) to produce an initial oligosaccharide pool, then with 0.05 M oxalic acid (90 °C, 20 min) to further depolymerise remaining high-DP material. Fractions collected after each step were characterised by HPAEC-PAD, HPSEC-RI, and IC for uronic acid content. The enzymatic step yielded 38 % soluble oligosaccharides (DP 3–10); subsequent acid treatment added a further 21 % yield with DP shifting toward 2–5. Uronic acid (glucuronic acid and 4-O-methylglucuronic acid) was retained in the enzymatic fraction at 0.18 mmol g⁻¹ AXOS but dropped to 0.06 mmol g⁻¹ after acid treatment, indicating preferential hydrolysis of glucuronic acid-substituted regions by the acid. Feruloylated AXOS fractions from the enzymatic step exhibited DPPH radical scavenging activity of 42 % at 5 mg mL⁻¹. The sequential strategy yielded overall GAXOS conversion of 59 % with a tuneable DP profile.

title: Tocopherol and Phytosterol Co-extraction from Defatted Maize Germ under Pressurised Liquid Conditions
abstract: Simultaneous recovery of tocopherols and phytosterols from defatted maize germ was investigated using pressurised liquid extraction with three solvent systems: n-hexane, ethyl acetate, and a 7:3 (v/v) hexane–ethyl acetate mixture, at 80 and 120 °C and 100 bar. Tocopherols were quantified by HPLC-FLD and phytosterols by GC-FID after saponification and trimethylsilylation. The mixed solvent at 120 °C recovered 94% of tocopherols and 87% of phytosterols relative to exhaustive Soxhlet extraction, while individual pure solvents showed 15–25% lower co-extraction efficiency. Total tocopherol in optimised extracts was 1.84 mg/g and total phytosterol was 4.12 mg/g of dry germ. Extract purity was assessed by gravimetric co-extracted lipid measurement; mixed solvent extracts contained 8% less co-extracted triglycerides than hexane alone. The study demonstrates that a single pressurised liquid step can yield commercially relevant concentrations of both compound classes.

title: Termogravimetrijska analiza poliesterskih tkanina sa epoksidnim matricama pri različitim brzinama zagrevanja
abstract: U radu je ispitana termička stabilnost poliesterskih tkanina impregniranih epoksidnom matricom primenom termogravimetrijske analize (TGA) u opsegu temperatura od 30 do 600 °C, pri brzinama zagrevanja od 5, 10 i 20 °C/min u atmosferi azota i vazduha. Uzorci su pripremljeni sa masenim udelima epoksidne smole od 20%, 35% i 50%. Utvrđeno je da povećanje udela smole pomera početak razgradnje ka višim temperaturama (Tonset između 312 i 341 °C), dok atmosfera vazduha uvodi sekundarni egzotermni pik između 490 i 520 °C koji odgovara oksidaciji ostatka ugljenika. Kinetički parametri izračunati Kissinger-Akahira-Sunose metodom pokazuju da energija aktivacije razgradnje raste sa 148 na 174 kJ/mol povećanjem masenog udela smole. Rezultati ukazuju da optimalan sadržaj smole od oko 35% daje najpovoljniji odnos termičke stabilnosti i mehaničkih karakteristika za primene u zaštitnoj odeći.

title: Flammability screening of woven glass-fibre reinforced polyamide laminates using the limiting oxygen index and UL-94 vertical burn test
abstract: Woven glass-fibre reinforced polyamide 6 laminates with four different fibre volume fractions (30, 40, 50 and 60 vol%) were subjected to limiting oxygen index (LOI) measurements and UL-94 vertical burn testing. LOI values ranged from 21.4 to 26.7%, showing a roughly linear increase with fibre content. All samples with fibre volume fractions of 50% and above achieved a V-1 classification, while samples at 30% failed to self-extinguish within 30 s. Burning rate measured along the sample length was 28 mm/min at 30 vol% and dropped to 11 mm/min at 60 vol%. Post-burn residue was analysed by SEM-EDS, revealing partial delamination and glass bead formation at the surface. The results suggest that fibre volume fraction alone can shift the flammability classification by at least one UL-94 category in this material system, independent of any chemical flame retardant additive.

title: Cone calorimetry assessment of multilayer textile laminates for protective workwear: effect of adhesive interlayer chemistry
abstract: Three adhesive interlayer chemistries — polyurethane (PU), ethylene–vinyl acetate (EVA), and modified starch-based adhesive — were used to bond outer shell aramid fabric to a moisture-barrier membrane in a three-layer laminate structure intended for industrial protective workwear. Cone calorimetry at an incident heat flux of 35 kW/m² was used to measure peak heat release rate (pHRR), total heat release (THR), time to ignition (TTI) and smoke production. PU-bonded laminates showed the highest pHRR at 184 kW/m² but the longest TTI of 28 s. EVA-bonded samples ignited at 19 s with a pHRR of 211 kW/m². Starch-based adhesive laminates produced the lowest smoke specific extinction area (62 m²/kg) compared to 147 m²/kg for PU. Cross-section analysis after testing showed that PU interlayer acts as a partial thermal barrier, delaying flame front penetration to the inner membrane by approximately 4 s relative to EVA. The findings provide direct guidance for adhesive selection in EN ISO 11612-compliant garment design.

title: Uticaj površinske obrade aramidnih vlakana na adheziju u laminatnim sklopovima i termičku stabilnost međusloja
abstract: Ispitan je uticaj tri postupka površinske obrade aramidnih vlakana — plazma tretman, kisela hidroliza i silanizacija — na kvalitet adhezije i termičku stabilnost poliuretanskog međusloja u dvoslojnom laminatu. Čvrstoća na raslojavanje merena je T-peel testom pre i posle ubrzanog starenja (72 h pri 70 °C i 95% RH). Plazma tretman povećao je T-peel vrednost sa polaznih 3,1 N/cm na 6,8 N/cm, dok je silanizacija dala vrednost od 5,4 N/cm. Termogravimetrijska analiza međusloja izolovanog mehaničkim razdvajanjem pokazala je da silanizovani uzorci imaju Tonset viši za 18 °C u odnosu na netretirana vlakna, što se pripisuje ograničenoj mobilnosti polimernih lanaca na granici faza. Rezultati ukazuju da plazma tretman poboljšava adheziju bez značajnijeg uticaja na termičku stabilnost, dok silanizacija istovremeno poboljšava oba parametra, ali u manjoj meri nego plazma tretman.

title: Požarno ponašanje višeslojnih tekstilnih struktura primenjenih u javnom prevozu: ispitivanje konusnim kalorimetrom i toksičnost produkata sagorevanja
abstract: Sedam komercijalnih višeslojnih tekstilnih struktura koje se koriste za tapaciranje sedišta u autobusima ispitano je konusnom kalorimetrijom pri toplotnom fluksu od 25 i 50 kW/m² prema standardu ISO 5660-1. title: Comparative cone calorimetry and TGA of bio-based and petroleum-derived adhesive interlayers in woven carbon-fibre laminates
abstract: Four adhesive interlayer systems — two petroleum-derived (polyurethane and epoxy film) and two bio-based (polylactic acid film and a castor-oil-derived polyurethane) — were evaluated in woven carbon-fibre laminates intended for lightweight structural applications. Cone calorimetry at 50 kW/m² showed that the castor-oil PU interlayer produced the lowest pHRR (112 kW/m²) among all variants, compared to 164 kW/m² for conventional PU and 139 kW/m² for epoxy film. PLA-bonded samples exhibited the earliest ignition (TTI 14 s) and highest CO yield (0.046 g/g). TGA in nitrogen revealed that bio-based interlayers generally decompose in a narrower temperature window (30–40 °C FWHM) compared to 55–70 °C for petroleum-derived adhesives. Residual carbon-fibre fabric integrity after cone testing was assessed by tensile testing of post-burn coupons, showing that castor-oil PU laminates retained 38% of original tensile strength versus 21% for PLA-bonded equivalents. The study provides a quantitative comparison relevant to substitution decisions in automotive and aerospace component manufacturing.

title: Termička i mehanička karakterizacija recikliranih ugljičnih vlakana u epoksidnim kompozitima: uticaj stepena degradacije vlakna
abstract: Reciklirana ugljična vlakna dobijena solvolizom epoksidnih kompozita pri tri procesna uslova (250 °C/4 h, 280 °C/4 h i 280 °C/8 h u etanolnom rastvoru KOH) inkorporirana su u novu epoksidnu matricu i ispitana TGA, DSC i zateznim ispitivanjem. Zatezna čvrstoća kompozita opala je sa 487 MPa (devičanska vlakna) na 391 MPa (280 °C/8 h reciklirani uzorci), dok je modul elastičnosti ostao relativno stabilan (pad od 7%). Rezultati sugerišu da blaži uslovi solvolize (250 °C/4 h) daju reciklirana vlakna čije su termičke i mehaničke karakteristike kompozita prihvatljive za sekundarne strukturne primene.

title: Electrochemical and microbiological assessment of corrosion in stainless steel fittings after 15 years of service in a Vojvodina municipal network
abstract: Decommissioned AISI 316L fittings from a municipal water distribution network in Vojvodina, with 15 years of service history, were subjected to a comprehensive post-mortem analysis combining electrochemical reactivation tests, XRD, SEM-EDS, and culture-based microbial enumeration. Double-loop electrochemical potentiokinetic reactivation (DLEPR) tests indicated sensitisation in approximately 22% of fittings from zones with reported leaks, while unsensitised fittings from well-flushed zones showed DLEPR ratios below 0.01. Microbial counts from biofilm swabs revealed total heterotrophic plate counts of up to 5 × 10⁵ CFU/cm² and SRB counts of up to 1.8 × 10³ CFU/cm². Corrosion product phases included FeS, FeSO₄·7H₂O, and Cr₂O₃. Wall thickness measurements by ultrasound showed localised thinning of up to 0.35 mm in confirmed MIC zones. The study provides empirical reference data for infrastructure managers considering replacement schedules and material upgrading in comparable network conditions.
venue: Corrosion Engineering Science and Technology

title: Calibration of a fringe-projection system for sub-millimetre reconstruction of machined aluminium parts
abstract: Fringe-projection structured-light systems suffer from systematic calibration errors that become significant when measuring specular metallic surfaces. This paper describes a calibration procedure that jointly estimates the projector intrinsics, the camera intrinsics, and the phase-to-depth mapping using a coated ceramic calibration target with known geometry. The procedure was validated on thirty-two machined aluminium components with ground-truth dimensions measured by a coordinate-measuring machine. Root-mean-square depth error was reduced from 0.41 mm with the manufacturer's default calibration to 0.09 mm after applying the proposed approach. We also show that using a polarising filter on the camera reduces highlight saturation on polished surfaces by approximately 14 dB in pixel intensity variance, improving unwrapping reliability from 91 % to 98 % across the test set. The method is applicable to any binary-coded or phase-shift fringe projector operating in the 300–800 nm range and requires no modification to the projector hardware.
venue: Journal of Optical Measurement and Instrumentation

title: Recovering surface normals on translucent injection-moulded components using multi-spectral photometric stereo
abstract: Standard photometric stereo breaks down on translucent materials because subsurface scattering violates the Lambertian assumption. We recorded a multi-spectral dataset of forty-two translucent polypropylene and ABS components under illumination at 470 nm, 530 nm, 625 nm, and 850 nm using a dome with sixteen individually addressable LEDs. At longer wavelengths, subsurface scattering is weaker, and the angular error in recovered normals dropped from 11.3° at 470 nm to 4.8° at 850 nm, measured against a stylus profilometer reference. Combining near-infrared and red channels via a weighted least-squares estimator reduced the mean angular error further to 3.1° over the test set. Depth maps integrated from these normals using the Frankot–Chellappa algorithm showed a mean absolute height error of 0.18 mm on components with features as small as 1.2 mm. The dataset and calibration images are made available as a public benchmark.

title: A comparison of phase-shift and binary-coded structured light for real-time depth acquisition in cluttered bin environments
abstract: Bin-picking applications require depth maps acquired at frame rates compatible with robotic cycle times, typically under two seconds per scan. We evaluated four structured-light coding strategies—three-frequency heterodyne phase shift, Gray-code binary, Hamming-code binary, and single-shot Fourier transform profilometry—on a standardised bin filled with randomly placed metal brackets, plastic gears, and rubber seals. Evaluation metrics included reconstruction completeness, depth noise on occluded edges, and acquisition time. Gray-code binary achieved 97.1 % completeness at 1.8 s per scan but produced 0.6 mm higher edge noise than three-frequency heterodyne. Single-shot Fourier profilometry completed acquisition in 0.12 s but completeness fell to 82.4 % under partial occlusion. Results are reported for three lighting conditions: diffuse ambient, fluorescent workshop, and near-darkness. The paper provides a decision table mapping part geometry and cycle-time constraints to the most appropriate coding strategy.

title: Fusion of structured-light depth and photometric stereo normals for reconstruction of specular freeform surfaces
abstract: This paper presents the core contribution of the author's doctoral research: a pipeline that fuses coarse depth maps from a phase-shift structured-light scanner with high-resolution surface normals from a four-light photometric stereo unit to reconstruct specular freeform surfaces. Structured-light provides the low-frequency depth trend while photometric stereo supplies high-frequency normal detail; fusion is performed via a variational optimisation that minimises a combined data term weighted by per-pixel confidence estimates derived from highlight saturation maps. The method was validated on eleven freeform aluminium moulds measured independently with a Renishaw contact profilometer. Mean absolute surface error was 0.12 mm with a maximum of 0.31 mm across all parts. Processing time on a standard workstation was 38 seconds per part at 2 megapixel resolution. The pipeline required no hardware synchronisation between the two sensors, which were operated sequentially under the same static scene assumption.

title: Depth completion for robotic grasping of transparent laboratory glassware
abstract: RGB-D cameras based on structured infrared light fail on transparent glass objects because the material transmits and refracts the projection pattern. We address this by using a photometric stereo module to supply surface normal maps that are then passed through a lightweight convolutional encoder-decoder to infer depth completions for pixels where the RGB-D camera reports invalid readings. Training was performed on a synthetic dataset of 14 000 rendered glass vessels augmented with measured background clutter; the model was fine-tuned on 600 real scenes captured in a chemistry laboratory setting. On the real test split, the completed depth maps reduced the 6-DoF grasp pose angular error from 19.4° to 6.8° compared to using the raw RGB-D output, and the grasp success rate on a UR5-type manipulator rose from 41 % to 74 % across eighty trials. The network has 3.1 million parameters and runs at 12 Hz on a mid-range GPU.
venue: Journal of Robotic Systems and Perception

title: Online re-calibration of a photometric stereo dome under changing ambient light for factory-floor deployment
abstract: Photometric stereo systems deployed on factory floors experience gradual drift in recovered normals caused by changes in ambient illumination, dust accumulation on LEDs, and thermal expansion of the mounting frame. We propose an online re-calibration scheme that uses a small retroreflective reference sphere mounted at a fixed position in the scene to estimate updated light directions and intensities every sixty seconds without interrupting production. The reference sphere subtends 15 pixels in diameter and is excluded from the working volume. Experiments over an eight-hour production shift on a stamped-steel part inspection line showed that normal angular error drifted from 2.1° to 5.7° without re-calibration and remained below 2.6° with re-calibration active. False-rejection rate of a downstream defect classifier was 3.8 % without re-calibration versus 1.2 % with re-calibration across 4 800 inspected parts.

title: Estimating 6-DoF grasp poses for shiny metal fasteners using a structured-light and normal-map pipeline
abstract: Small shiny fasteners such as bolts, nuts, and washers are among the most difficult objects for vision-guided bin-picking because their geometry is compact, repetitive, and specular. We combined a structured-light depth scan with a photometric stereo normal map to generate enhanced point clouds and evaluated three grasp-pose estimation backends—point pair features, super4PCS global registration, and a learned PointNet-based estimator—on a bin containing mixed fastener types. The combined representation improved recall at 5 mm / 5° threshold from 58 % to 79 % for point pair features and from 67 % to 84 % for the PointNet backend compared to depth-only inputs. Physical grasp trials on a six-axis manipulator with a two-finger gripper achieved 88 % success over 240 picks, versus 64 % with the depth-only baseline. Processing pipeline latency was 2.3 seconds end-to-end.

title: Multi-modal 3D perception for robotic manipulation: sensor integration and scene representations
abstract: This book chapter surveys approaches to integrating complementary 3D sensing modalities—structured light, photometric stereo, time-of-flight, and passive stereo—for robotic manipulation tasks. The chapter is organised around three decision axes: the optical properties of target objects (diffuse, specular, translucent, transparent), the required spatial resolution and acquisition speed, and the computational budget available for downstream grasp planning. Each section reviews representative methods, discusses their failure modes, and provides quantitative comparisons where published benchmarks allow. The chapter also covers calibration strategies for multi-sensor rigs, confidence estimation, and the representation of fused measurements as point clouds, depth images, or implicit surfaces. A short section on learning-based approaches discusses how data from physical sensors can complement synthetic training data. The intended audience is graduate students and engineers beginning work on perception systems for manipulation.
venue: Advances in Robot Perception and Grasping, Springer Series on Advanced Robotics

title: Reconstructing partially occluded translucent objects in bin-picking scenarios using polarisation and near-infrared photometric stereo
abstract: Translucent objects in a bin-picking scenario present two compounded difficulties: subsurface scattering degrades normal estimation, and inter-object occlusion creates incomplete surface coverage. We address both with a pipeline that uses a polarisation camera to separate surface-reflected and volume-scattered radiance components, applies near-infrared photometric stereo to the separated surface-reflected component, and then performs shape completion of occluded regions with a variational method seeded by the structured-light depth prior. Experiments used a bin containing forty instances of three translucent food-grade plastic container types. Mean normal angular error on visible regions was 3.4° and on completed occluded regions 6.1°, compared to 9.7° and 14.3° respectively for a standard near-infrared photometric stereo baseline without polarisation separation. Grasp success on a physical manipulator reached 81 % over 160 trials, an improvement of 23 percentage points over the baseline.

title: Real-time structured-light and photometric stereo fusion on an embedded GPU for in-hand object re-identification
abstract: When a robot re-grasps an object mid-task, the changed contact geometry requires updated pose estimation. We present an embedded implementation of a fused structured-light and photometric stereo pipeline running on a Jetson-class GPU module mounted on the wrist of a six-axis manipulator, enabling in-hand re-identification at 3 Hz. The pipeline uses a single-shot Fourier profilometry pattern for structured-light acquisition and a four-LED ring for photometric stereo, both captured in under 80 ms. Fusion uses a GPU-parallelised version of the variational scheme adapted from earlier work, reduced to run within a 340 ms budget per frame. Tests on fourteen object types including metal clips, plastic shells, and rubber grommets showed pose estimation error below 4 mm / 4° in 87 % of frames under workshop lighting. Power consumption of the wrist module was 18 W during active scanning.

title: Nonlinear model predictive control for real-time cable tension regulation in a CDPR with elastic cables
abstract: Elastic cables introduce oscillatory disturbances that degrade positioning accuracy and increase energy consumption if not actively damped. This paper applies nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) to simultaneously regulate end-effector pose and suppress cable oscillations in a six-cable CDPR. The prediction model is the elastic lumped-mass formulation from earlier work, reduced to 18 states by retaining only the first vibrational mode per cable. The NMPC problem is solved at 200 Hz using the real-time iteration scheme implemented in ACADO Toolkit, running on an embedded PC with dSPACE I/O. Comparison against a baseline PD controller over 60 test trajectories shows 47% reduction in peak positioning error during aggressive manoeuvres and 19% reduction in total electrical energy per trajectory. The NMPC constraint on maximum cable tension is violated in fewer than 0.3% of control steps during testing, all occurring at trajectory start points with large initial pose errors.

title: Steady-State Analysis of a Two-Stage Tandem Queue with Markov-Modulated Input and Finite Buffers
abstract: This paper examines a tandem queuing model with two service stations, Markov-modulated Poisson arrivals, and finite intermediate buffers of capacity K. The authors derive the stationary distribution using matrix-analytic methods and obtain closed-form expressions for mean sojourn time and blocking probability as functions of K and the traffic intensity ρ. Numerical experiments are performed for phase-generator matrices calibrated to packet-switched network traces collected at the University of Novi Sad computing centre in 2011. Results show that blocking probability decreases by a factor of approximately 3 when K is increased from 5 to 20, while mean sojourn time increases by less than 8 percent, suggesting a practically useful buffer-sizing rule. The model is validated against a discrete-event simulation implemented in SimPy, with relative errors below 2 percent across all tested parameter combinations. The work provides a tractable basis for dimensioning two-tier storage or processing pipelines in early private cloud deployments.

title: Optimal Threshold Policies for Virtual Machine Provisioning in Elastic Cloud Clusters
abstract: The paper formulates virtual machine (VM) provisioning in an Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) environment as a discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP). The state space encodes the number of active VMs, the queue length of pending jobs, and a two-state workload signal. A threshold-based control policy is derived by value iteration over a finite horizon of T = 200 decision epochs, with per-step costs reflecting both VM rental fees and job latency penalties. The optimal threshold is shown to depend on the ratio of rental cost to latency penalty in a monotone, piecewise-linear fashion for the parameter ranges examined. Experiments use a synthetic workload trace generated by a compound Poisson process with burst parameters estimated from publicly available Google cluster usage traces. The derived threshold policy reduces total expected cost by 17–24 percent compared to static over-provisioning across five cost-ratio scenarios. The model is intentionally kept small enough for exact MDP solution without approximation.

title: Energy-Delay Trade-offs in Heterogeneous Server Farms: A Queuing-Theoretic Approach
abstract: This work studies a heterogeneous server farm composed of N fast servers with high power draw and M slow, energy-efficient servers, modelled as a mixed M/G/N+M queue with non-preemptive service and a join-the-shortest-queue routing discipline. Energy consumption is modelled as a convex function of server utilisation derived from SPECpower benchmark data for two classes of commodity hardware. The paper derives approximations for mean response time and mean power consumption under moderate-to-heavy traffic (ρ ∈ [0.5, 0.9]) using a decomposition method, and compares them against discrete-event simulation results. The relative error of the approximation is within 5 percent for mean response time and 3 percent for mean power in all tested configurations. A Pareto frontier of energy versus delay objectives is traced for different server-mix ratios, and it is found that a 40/60 fast-to-slow ratio achieves near-minimum delay at roughly 70 percent of the energy cost of an all-fast configuration at ρ = 0.75.

title: Approximate Dynamic Programming for Multi-Resource Scheduling in Multi-Tenant Cloud Environments
abstract: Multi-tenant cloud platforms require scheduling decisions that jointly allocate CPU, memory, and network bandwidth across competing tenant queues. This paper frames the problem as a continuous-time MDP with a product-form state space that grows exponentially in the number of tenants. Exact solution is tractable only for up to three tenants; for larger instances the paper applies a linear function approximation within an approximate policy iteration scheme, using basis functions derived from the single-resource optimal policies. Experiments are run on a simulated cluster with 6 tenants and 32 virtual CPU cores. The approximate policy achieves within 6 percent of a lower bound on average cost obtained by Lagrangian relaxation, and reduces mean job completion time by 19 percent relative to a first-come-first-served baseline. Sensitivity analysis shows the policy degrades gracefully as tenant arrival rate heterogeneity increases.

title: Workload Prediction for Proactive Scaling: A Comparison of Time-Series and Markov-Modulated Models
abstract: Reactive auto-scaling introduces lag that can cause transient SLA violations during rapid workload changes. This paper compares two classes of predictive models—SARIMA-based time-series forecasts and hidden Markov models (HMMs) with Gaussian emission distributions—for 15-minute-ahead prediction of CPU demand in a web-serving workload. Evaluation is performed on four one-month traces collected from a private cloud operated at the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad testbed. Prediction accuracy is measured by mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and by the downstream effect on scaling decisions, assessed via a queuing simulator. HMMs with three hidden states achieve lower MAPE (8.3 percent vs. 11.7 percent for SARIMA) on traces with clear regime-switching behaviour, but both methods perform comparably on smooth, diurnal traces. Proactive policies driven by either model reduce the frequency of under-provisioning events by 40–55 percent compared to a reactive CPU-threshold policy, at a cost of approximately 8 percent over-provisioning.

title: A Fluid-Queue Bound on Tail Latency for Serverless Function Invocations with Cold-Start Delays
abstract: Serverless computing platforms invoke functions on demand, incurring a cold-start initialisation delay when no warm instance is available. This paper models warm-pool management as a fluid queue driven by a background Markov chain with states representing high, medium, and low demand regimes. Cold-start events correspond to buffer underflow epochs. An upper bound on the tail probability of end-to-end latency exceeding a threshold d is derived analytically using the theory of Markov-modulated fluid queues. The bound is parameterised from invocation traces of three representative functions observed over a 48-hour period on an experimental serverless platform deployed at the University of Novi Sad. The bound is numerically tight within a factor of 1.4 across all tested thresholds d ∈ [50, 500] ms. A warm-pool sizing rule derived from the bound reduces empirical P99 latency by 18 percent relative to a heuristic rule based solely on mean invocation rate, with a 12 percent increase in idle-instance cost.

title: Numerical prediction of condensation onset inside consumer electronics housings under diurnal ambient cycling
abstract: A two-dimensional finite-volume model of moisture and heat transport was developed for a generic polycarbonate housing representative of handheld electronic devices. The domain included the polymer shell, an internal air cavity of 38 cm³, and a printed circuit board heat source. Boundary conditions followed a 24-hour ambient cycle between 5 °C and 35 °C at 60–90 % relative humidity, representative of coastal storage conditions. The dew-point margin at the coldest internal surface was tracked over 72 simulated hours. For a housing wall thickness of 2 mm with no desiccant, the dew-point margin dropped below zero during the cooling phase at hour 14, predicting condensation on the board. Adding a 0.5 g silica gel insert raised the margin to +1.8 °C at the same instant. Model sensitivity to polycarbonate vapour diffusivity was assessed over a ±30 % range; the condensation-onset time varied by ±2.1 hours. The numerical approach is validated against laboratory cycling tests using thermocouples and a miniature humidity probe placed inside the cavity.

title: Comparative assessment of flat gasket profiles for moisture control in outdoor junction boxes
abstract: Three flat gasket profiles—rectangular, trapezoidal, and tongue-and-groove—made from the same cellular EPDM formulation were evaluated for their ability to limit internal relative humidity in a standardised IP55-class outdoor junction box over a 6-month outdoor exposure period in Novi Sad. Internal humidity and temperature were logged at 15-minute intervals. The tongue-and-groove profile yielded the lowest mean internal relative humidity of 54 % compared with 63 % for the rectangular and 58 % for the trapezoidal cross-section under identical external conditions. Surface area exposed to the vapour gradient differed by up to 22 % between profiles at the nominal bolt torque of 4 N·m. A finite-element contact analysis confirmed that effective sealing length, defined as the region where contact pressure exceeded 0.3 MPa, was longest in the tongue-and-groove geometry. The study provides practical geometry recommendations for designers of weatherproof enclosures.

title: Moisture accumulation in sealed optical instrument housings: influence of residual air humidity at assembly
abstract: Optical devices assembled in factories at relative humidity levels of 30 %, 50 %, and 70 % were modelled and tested to quantify the long-term internal moisture level reached after hermetic sealing. A one-dimensional mass-balance model predicts that the asymptotic internal humidity is determined by the initial air charge, the internal surface sorption capacity of polymer components, and the slow permeation through glass-to-metal adhesive joints. For an assembly humidity of 70 %, the model predicts a post-sealing equilibrium internal relative humidity of 22 % at 20 °C; at 30 % assembly humidity this falls to 9 %. Twelve laboratory assemblies per condition, sealed with a tin-indium solder alloy joint, were placed in a climate chamber and monitored via a fibre-optic dew-point sensor for 18 months. Predictions and measurements agree within 4 percentage points. The study underpins a factory specification of maximum 45 % assembly-room humidity to maintain the internal level below 15 % over a 10-year service life.

title: Temperature distribution and natural convection patterns in a sealed rectangular enclosure with an off-centre heat source
abstract: Natural convection and temperature stratification were studied in a sealed rectangular aluminium enclosure (250 mm × 180 mm × 80 mm) with a single resistive heat source displaced 30 mm from the geometric centre. Three source power levels—5 W, 15 W, and 30 W—were tested in a still-air environment at 23 °C external temperature. Internal temperature was mapped with a 35-point thermocouple array and compared with three-dimensional CFD solutions computed using the Boussinesq approximation on a 1.2-million-cell structured mesh. At 30 W the maximum internal air temperature of 61 °C occurred at the top rear corner; the temperature non-uniformity across the enclosure was 23 °C. CFD predictions agreed with measurements within 1.8 °C on average. A dimensionless correlation relating the Nusselt number to the Rayleigh number and source eccentricity ratio is proposed and fits the present data with a maximum deviation of 7 %. The correlation assists in locating heat sources to minimise condensation-prone cold spots.

title: Hygrothermal modelling of enclosures with phase-change material inserts for condensation suppression
abstract: Paraffin-based phase-change material (PCM) inserts were evaluated as passive condensation suppressors inside sealed outdoor enclosures. A two-dimensional transient finite-element model coupling heat conduction with vapour diffusion in air was developed. The enthalpy method was used to represent the latent heat of the PCM at its melting temperature of 28 °C. Parametric simulations varied PCM mass from 20 g to 100 g and tested two ambient diurnal profiles: continental summer (15–38 °C) and continental autumn (4–18 °C). During the summer profile, a 60 g PCM insert reduced the peak internal temperature rise by 5.1 °C relative to the no-PCM case, delaying the internal dew-point crossing by 3.8 hours. During the autumn profile, the PCM effect was negligible because the ambient temperature remained below the melting point for over 80 % of the cycle. Laboratory validation with a 240 cm³ aluminium enclosure showed model predictions of internal surface temperature within 1.4 °C over 48-hour test runs.

title: Seal groove surface roughness as a determinant of effective vapour permeance in static metal-to-metal joints
abstract: The influence of metal groove surface roughness on the effective vapour permeance of compressed rubber seals was investigated experimentally and analytically. Aluminium groove surfaces were prepared at five arithmetic mean roughness values between Ra 0.4 µm and Ra 6.3 µm. NBR O-rings of 3.5 mm cross-section diameter were compressed to 20 % and exposed to a 1 kPa water vapour partial pressure differential. Steady-state permeance was measured gravimetrically over 240-hour intervals. Permeance increased from 1.8 × 10⁻¹² kg/(m²·s·Pa) at Ra 0.4 µm to 8.7 × 10⁻¹² kg/(m²·s·Pa) at Ra 6.3 µm, a factor of 4.8 increase. A model relating the open micro-channel area at the rubber–metal interface to permeance, using a Hertz contact pressure distribution modified for surface asperities, captures the trend within 15 %. The results quantify a minimum surface finish requirement of Ra ≤ 1.6 µm to keep vapour permeance within one order of magnitude of the bulk rubber value.
venue: Tribology and Sealing Technology

title: Condensation risk mapping in wall-mounted outdoor housings using coupled CFD and vapour diffusion simulations
abstract: A coupled simulation workflow was developed to map condensation risk on internal surfaces of wall-mounted outdoor plastic housings under winter conditions. A three-dimensional steady-state CFD model computed the internal temperature distribution accounting for natural convection and wall conduction; the resulting surface temperature field was then passed as a boundary condition to a vapour diffusion model that predicted local relative humidity and dew-point margin at each surface node. A 6-litre ABS housing with a 20 W internal heat source was simulated at external temperatures of −10 °C, 0 °C, and 10 °C at 90 % external relative humidity with a seal permeance of 3.5 × 10⁻¹² kg/(m²·s·Pa). At −10 °C, 14 % of the internal wall area showed a negative dew-point margin; this reduced to 3 % at 0 °C and to zero at 10 °C. A redesign placing the heat source at the geometric bottom of the housing eliminated the negative-margin area at −10 °C. The workflow is implemented in open-source tools and requires less than 4 hours of computation time on a workstation.

title: Hygrothermal analysis of sealed enclosures
abstract: This book chapter reviews the physical mechanisms governing moisture behaviour in mechanically sealed enclosures, covering vapour diffusion through seal materials, convective moisture transport in internal air volumes, and sorption on interior polymer surfaces. The chapter presents one-dimensional and two-dimensional analytical solutions for steady-state and transient vapour transport in simple geometries, followed by a discussion of finite-element and finite-volume implementations for complex enclosure shapes. A worked example demonstrates the prediction of condensation onset time for a 2-litre aluminium housing sealed with a silicone gasket subjected to a step change in external relative humidity from 50 % to 95 %. The chapter also addresses the coupling between thermal and hygric calculations, noting conditions under which decoupled analysis is acceptable (Biot number for vapour transfer below 0.1). Measurement techniques for validating hygrothermal models, including gravimetric permeability testing, capacitive sensing, and fibre-optic dew-point measurement, are described.

title: Effect of internal air volume on the time to condensation onset in hermetically sealed enclosures with a single cold spot
abstract: The relationship between enclosure free air volume and the time required for internal relative humidity to reach dew point at the coldest internal surface was investigated through a series of controlled laboratory experiments and complementary lumped-parameter modelling. Steel enclosures with free volumes of 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 litres were sealed with identical silicone gaskets at 20 % compression and subjected to an external humidity step from 40 % to 95 % at 20 °C, while a Peltier element maintained one internal wall face at 10 °C. Time to condensation onset ranged from 8.3 hours for the 0.2-litre enclosure to 49.1 hours for the 2.0-litre enclosure. The lumped model, which treats the air volume as a well-mixed reservoir and the gasket as a resistance in series with the Peltier surface, reproduced onset times with a mean absolute error of 1.4 hours across all four volumes. A dimensionless time-to-onset parameter normalised by gasket permeance and effective cold surface area collapses the data for all four volumes onto a single curve.

title: Sensitivity analysis of hygrothermal model parameters for sealed outdoor enclosures used in photovoltaic junction box applications
abstract: A hygrothermal model of a polyphthalamide (PPA) junction box used in crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules was subjected to a global sensitivity analysis using the Sobol variance decomposition method. Nine input parameters were varied: gasket vapour permeability, gasket cross-section width, groove surface roughness, internal air volume, internal polymer sorption isotherm slope, external temperature amplitude, external humidity amplitude, solar irradiance-driven temperature offset, and potting compound surface area. Each parameter was sampled over physically realistic ranges drawn from the literature and from in-house measurements. A total of 18 432 model evaluations were performed. The first-order Sobol index for the time to condensation onset was dominated by gasket vapour permeability (S₁ = 0.41) and external humidity amplitude (S₁ = 0.28). Grove surface roughness had a smaller but non-negligible contribution (S₁ = 0.09). The analysis identifies gasket material selection and installation surface finish as the most impactful design levers for extending the condensation-free service life of PV junction boxes.

title: Validated workflow for predicting dew-point margin in sealed outdoor enclosures under real climate boundary conditions from meteorological station data
abstract: A simulation workflow is described that takes hourly meteorological station data (dry-bulb temperature and relative humidity) as its sole external boundary condition and predicts the time-history of the dew-point margin on the coldest internal surface of a sealed outdoor enclosure. The workflow chains a thermal resistance–capacitance model of the enclosure wall with a lumped vapour mass-balance model and a local surface temperature correction derived from a short CFD pre-computation. It was applied to three years of hourly data (2021–2023) from the Rimski Šančevi meteorological station near Novi Sad for three enclosure configurations: unheated ABS 1-litre, unheated aluminium 4-litre, and aluminium 4-litre with 10 W anti-condensation heater. The workflow predicted that the unheated ABS enclosure experienced 312 condensation-onset events over three years; the unheated aluminium enclosure experienced 94, and the heated aluminium enclosure experienced zero. Predictions were validated against a 12-month data set from four instrumented enclosures deployed at the same station, with onset event counts matching to within 8 %.

title: Human-capital intensity ratios and credit-rating outcomes: evidence from Croatian and Serbian listed companies
abstract: Credit-rating agencies and lenders increasingly request non-financial information, yet human-capital data remain largely absent from standardised disclosure packages. This paper constructs a human-capital intensity ratio—defined as personnel expenditure divided by total assets—and examines whether this ratio predicts credit-rating downgrades in a panel of 87 listed companies from Croatia and Serbia between 2006 and 2012. Logistic regressions with firm fixed effects show that a one-standard-deviation increase in the ratio reduces the probability of a downgrade by 6.4 percentage points, conditional on leverage and profitability controls. The effect persists after excluding the crisis years 2008–2009. The paper concludes that human-capital intensity carries incremental predictive content beyond conventional financial ratios and recommends that national accounting standards bodies consider mandatory disclosure of training expenditure in annual reports.

title: Measuring organisational commitment and its short-run effect on labour productivity: a survey-based panel study in the Vojvodina food-processing sector
abstract: This paper examines the lag structure between organisational commitment—measured through a 22-item Likert survey administered annually to 1,840 employees across 31 food-processing firms in Vojvodina—and labour productivity recorded from company financial statements over three consecutive years (2013–2015). A dynamic panel model estimated by the Arellano–Bond GMM procedure controls for unobserved firm heterogeneity and reverse causality. Affective commitment shows the strongest positive association with productivity, with a coefficient implying roughly a 1.8 percent productivity gain per unit increase on the composite scale one year forward. Continuance commitment is statistically insignificant. Firm size negatively moderates the affective-commitment effect, suggesting that larger plants face coordination costs that attenuate individual-level motivation. The data collection instrument and full item wording are published as supplementary material.

title: Accounting for human capital under IFRS: a comparison of practice in five Western Balkan countries
abstract: This book chapter reviews how companies in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro and Albania treat human-capital expenditures under International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted locally. Drawing on a content analysis of 260 annual reports published between 2014 and 2017 and coded against a 34-item disclosure checklist, the chapter documents wide heterogeneity in the voluntary disclosure of training costs, employee competence valuations and workforce turnover data. Serbian firms in the sample disclose significantly more human-capital information than counterparts in the other four countries, a finding the authors attribute to SEC-Serbia listing requirements and the influence of foreign parent companies that mandate group-level HR reporting. The chapter also compares current practices with proposals in the IFRS Foundation's 2017 discussion paper on broader reporting and identifies gaps most amenable to regulatory intervention.

title: Does management training pay off? Quasi-experimental evidence from a subsidised leadership programme in Serbia
abstract: Between 2015 and 2018 the Serbian Development Agency co-financed a leadership training programme for middle managers in 78 manufacturing firms. The staggered rollout of the subsidy—driven by administrative processing delays rather than firm characteristics—provides a quasi-experimental setting exploited here through a difference-in-differences estimator with staggered treatment timing. Outcome variables include return on assets, operating cash-flow margin and voluntary employee turnover, all drawn from official financial statements and HR reports. Firms whose managers completed the programme show a statistically significant 1.9 percentage-point improvement in return on assets two years after programme completion relative to firms in the control group. The turnover rate falls by 3.2 percentage points in the same window. Effects on cash-flow margin are positive but imprecisely estimated. A heterogeneity analysis suggests that firms with fewer than 100 employees benefit more on all three dimensions.

title: Constructing a firm-level human-capital stock index for panel data: methodology and a Serbian application
abstract: Standard balance-sheet data record personnel costs as period expenses, making it impossible to track accumulated human capital across time at the firm level. This paper proposes a perpetual-inventory method adapted for human-capital stocks, using annual training expenditure as investment and applying depreciation rates estimated from wage-tenure profiles in the 2013 and 2018 waves of the Serbian Labour Force Survey. The method is applied to an unbalanced panel of 412 Serbian firms observed from 2012 to 2019. The resulting human-capital stock index has a cross-sectional standard deviation roughly twice that of physical capital intensity, indicating substantial dispersion. Firms in the information and communication sector maintain the highest index values; construction firms the lowest. The index correlates positively with total factor productivity at a coefficient of 0.31 (p < 0.001) after controlling for sector and year fixed effects. Replication code and anonymised panel data are archived in the University of Novi Sad institutional repository.

title: Linking employee engagement scores to quarterly revenue variance: a pilot study in two Serbian technology firms
abstract: This conference paper reports preliminary results from a collaboration with two medium-sized technology companies headquartered in Novi Sad. Both firms administered a 16-item employee engagement questionnaire quarterly over two years (Q1 2020–Q4 2021), yielding 1,104 individual responses matched to quarterly revenue and gross-margin data at the department level. Fixed-effects regressions at the department–quarter level show that a ten-point increase in the composite engagement score—measured on a 100-point scale—precedes a 2.7 percent revenue increase in the following quarter. The relationship is stronger in customer-facing departments than in back-office units. The paper discusses measurement limitations, including potential response bias and the short observation window, and outlines a planned extension to five additional firms. Ethics approval and data-sharing agreements are documented in the supplementary appendix.

title: Human-capital accounting practices in science and technology parks: a multi-case study of five Central and Eastern European parks
abstract: Science and technology parks house knowledge-intensive firms whose competitive advantage derives primarily from human capital, yet there is little empirical documentation of how such firms account for or manage that capital. This paper reports findings from structured interviews with finance and HR managers at 34 companies located in five science and technology parks in Hungary, Slovakia, Romania, Croatia and Serbia, conducted in 2023. Interview transcripts were coded using a framework adapted from the Danish Intellectual Capital Statement model. Three distinct accounting postures emerge: compliance-minimum, voluntary-narrative and quantified-stock approaches. Firms with foreign parent companies and those planning equity financing are significantly more likely to adopt quantified-stock approaches. The paper maps which organisational and financial characteristics predict each posture and discusses how park management bodies can design support services to help tenant firms develop more systematic human-capital accounts. Practical implications for park administrators and policy-makers are outlined.

title: Wage returns to employer-provided training across firm-size classes: microeconometric evidence from the Western Balkans
abstract: Using harmonised individual-level wage surveys from Serbia, North Macedonia and Bosnia and Herzegovina collected in 2019 and 2022, this paper estimates the private wage return to employer-provided training separately for micro, small, medium and large firms. A Mincerian earnings equation augmented with training incidence and intensity measures is estimated by OLS and by a control-function approach that instruments training with whether the respondent's immediate supervisor completed higher education. Pooled estimates put the return at 4.1 percent per training episode, but there is marked heterogeneity: workers in micro firms earn a 6.8 percent premium per episode while those in large firms earn 2.3 percent. The gap persists after controlling for occupation, sector, country and year. The authors argue that micro-firm workers face a steeper earnings trajectory because employer-provided training is rarer and less substitutable by self-directed learning in such settings. Policy implications for national training-fund design are discussed.

title: Genetic diversity of the Sjeničko sheep breed assessed by fifteen microsatellite markers
abstract: The Sjeničko sheep is an autochthonous breed from the Pešter plateau of southwestern Serbia, maintained by smallholder herds with limited recording. Blood samples were collected from 98 individuals across seven flocks. Fifteen FAO-recommended microsatellite loci were amplified, sized by capillary electrophoresis, and scored using GeneMapper software. Mean number of alleles per locus was 7.4, observed heterozygosity averaged 0.61, and expected heterozygosity 0.64. AMOVA revealed that 11.3 % of total genetic variation resided among flocks, suggesting moderate but meaningful differentiation. STRUCTURE analysis at K = 3 identified a subset of flocks with admixture consistent with recent introduction of Merino rams for wool improvement. FIS values were positive in five of seven flocks, pointing to mild inbreeding driven by small census sizes. Results are discussed in relation to breed registration criteria and the need for a coordinated mating programme to preserve allelic richness in this endangered population.

title: Comparative microsatellite profiling of four Serbian autochthonous sheep breeds
abstract: A panel of 18 microsatellite markers was used to characterise genetic relationships among four Serbian autochthonous sheep breeds: Sjeničko, Pirotska Oplemenjivana, Vlašićka, and Bardoka. A total of 312 animals (78 per breed) were genotyped. Allelic richness standardised to 60 individuals ranged from 4.8 in Bardoka to 6.2 in Vlašićka. Pairwise FST values ranged from 0.07 (Sjeničko vs. Vlašićka) to 0.19 (Bardoka vs. Pirotska), and a neighbour-joining tree based on DA distances placed Bardoka as an outgroup relative to the other three breeds. Principal coordinates analysis confirmed breed clustering, with some individual scatter between Sjeničko and Vlašićka flocks bordering Kosovo. Assignment tests using GeneClass2 correctly assigned 84 % of individuals to their source breed. The data provide a baseline for designing conservation priorities and highlight the distinctiveness of Bardoka as a candidate for special protection status.

title: Estimation of effective population size in the Vlašićka sheep using linkage disequilibrium and demographic records
abstract: Effective population size (Ne) is a central parameter for managing genetic erosion in small populations. For the Vlašićka breed, kept primarily in central Bosnia and Herzegovina, microsatellite-based linkage disequilibrium (LD-Ne) estimates were calculated from 156 individuals genotyped at 20 loci, yielding a current Ne of 43 (95 % CI: 31–58). Pedigree-based Ne derived from studbook records spanning 1995–2011 gave a comparable value of 49. Temporal estimates using two sampling cohorts (2004 and 2011) confirmed a declining trend. The rate of inbreeding per generation (ΔF) was estimated at 1.16 %, exceeding the 0.5 % threshold recommended by FAO for sustainable management. Monte Carlo simulations projected allele loss trajectories over 10 generations under current management versus two hypothetical rotational mating scenarios. Implementing a rotational scheme across five ram lines would be expected to reduce ΔF to approximately 0.6 %, halving projected heterozygosity loss over 50 years.

title: Population structure of sheep breeds across the Dinaric Arc: gene flow at the contact zones of Serbia, Bosnia, and Montenegro
abstract: The Dinaric Arc harbours several morphologically distinct sheep breeds whose genetic boundaries remain poorly defined. Tissue and blood samples from 487 animals representing six breeds across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro were genotyped at 22 microsatellite loci. Bayesian clustering in STRUCTURE and discriminant analysis of principal components (DAPC) consistently supported K = 5 clusters, with Sjeničko and Vlašićka forming one admixed cluster, reflecting extensive historical trade movement along the Via Dinarica transhumance routes. Isolation-by-distance analysis (Mantel test, r = 0.41, p = 0.002) explained part of the genetic differentiation, but residual structure remained after geographic distance was partialled out, suggesting breed management practices contribute independently. MIGRATE-N analyses indicated asymmetric gene flow from lowland to highland populations, consistent with past policies of upgrading local breeds with Merino rams. These findings argue for transboundary breed conservation planning.

title: Y-chromosome microsatellite haplotypes in Western Balkan sheep: paternal lineages and their geographic distribution
abstract: Maternal lineage data for Balkan sheep are well described through mitochondrial DNA, but paternal lineage diversity is understudied. This study characterised five Y-chromosome microsatellite markers (SRYM18, OarMS8, OarJMP8, INRA126, SR-crsp-8) in 198 rams from five autochthonous breeds across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. Fourteen distinct Y-haplotypes were identified. Haplotype H3 was the most frequent overall (34 %) and was found in all five breeds, whereas haplotypes H9–H14 appeared exclusively in Macedonian breeds. Network analysis revealed a star topology centred on H3, consistent with a recent expansion or founder effect. The geographic distribution of Y-haplotypes showed weaker differentiation (ΦST = 0.09) compared to autosomal microsatellite data (FST = 0.16), supporting male-mediated gene flow associated with historical ram trading. These data complement maternal lineage studies and contribute to a fuller picture of breed formation processes in the region.

title: Mitochondrial DNA control region diversity and maternal origins of the Pirotska Oplemenjivana sheep
abstract: The Pirotska Oplemenjivana is a mid-size breed developed in southeastern Serbia through crossing of the native Vlasinska with various fine-wool breeds during the twentieth century. To investigate its maternal genetic history, the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) D-loop control region (476 bp) was sequenced in 118 individuals. Forty-three haplotypes were identified, grouping into four major haplogroups: A (61 %), B (22 %), C (11 %), and E (6 %). The predominance of haplogroup A is consistent with central-European domestic sheep ancestry, while the presence of haplogroup E suggests a Near Eastern contribution uncommon in other Serbian breeds. Haplotype diversity was 0.91 and nucleotide diversity was 0.021. Bayesian skyline plots indicated a population bottleneck around 80–100 generations ago followed by moderate expansion, broadly coinciding with nineteenth-century breed development records. These results support a composite maternal origin for the breed and suggest that its genetic distinctiveness merits inclusion in regional breed conservation frameworks.

title: Genomic inbreeding estimates in Sjeničko sheep using runs of homozygosity on a medium-density SNP array
abstract: Runs of homozygosity (ROH) derived from SNP arrays provide a more accurate and biologically informative measure of inbreeding than pedigree-based coefficients. A medium-density ovine SNP array (OvineSNP50 BeadChip, 46,813 informative SNPs after quality control) was applied to 88 Sjeničko animals sampled from 11 flocks. Mean genomic inbreeding (FROH) was 0.134, considerably higher than pedigree-based estimates (Fped = 0.061), reflecting incomplete pedigree recording. ROH segments longer than 4 Mb were enriched on chromosomes 2, 6, and 14, regions harbouring quantitative trait loci for wool and body weight. Short ROH (<2 Mb) collectively contributed 62 % of total ROH length, indicating both ancient and recent autozygosity. Flock-level FROH ranged from 0.09 to 0.19, and the two flocks with the highest values had documented histories of brother–sister mating. These findings provide empirical support for revising the breed management strategy and highlight specific chromosomal segments for further investigation.

title: Detecting selection signatures in autochthonous Balkan sheep using integrated haplotype scores and FST outlier tests
abstract: Identifying genomic regions under selection can reveal adaptation to local environments and guide conservation of functional diversity. Genome-wide data from 210 animals across four Western Balkan breeds (Sjeničko, Vlašićka, Bardoka, Pirotska Oplemenjivana) genotyped on the OvineSNP50 array were analysed using iHS (integrated haplotype scores), XP-EHH (cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity), and FST outlier detection. After multiple-testing correction (FDR < 0.05), 34 genomic windows showed consistent signals across at least two methods. Candidate regions overlapped with genes associated with thermotolerance (HSPA1A), parasite resistance (DRB1 in the MHC region), and mountain adaptation-related metabolic traits. The strongest FST outlier on chromosome 6 spanned a window containing MSTN. Breed-specific signals were more numerous in Bardoka, potentially reflecting its more isolated geographic distribution and distinct morphology. The results suggest that even in endangered breeds, meaningful adaptive variation has been retained and should be factored into conservation and potential breeding decisions.

title: Conservation genetics of autochthonous sheep breeds in the Western Balkans: a review and management recommendations
abstract: This book chapter synthesises two decades of population genetic research on autochthonous sheep breeds from Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and North Macedonia. It covers the development of microsatellite characterisation studies, the transition to SNP-based approaches, and comparative results on diversity indices, population structure, and phylogenetic relationships across approximately 15 named breeds. Key recurring findings include: moderate to high within-breed heterozygosity in most breeds; significant differentiation at national and regional scales; evidence of historical admixture with cosmopolitan breeds; and consistent underestimation of inbreeding in official pedigree records. The chapter discusses institutional challenges in maintaining breed registers, the role of agri-environment schemes in incentivising traditional pastoral systems, and technical recommendations for minimum marker panel requirements for parentage and diversity monitoring. Practical guidance for establishing transboundary genetic resource networks among Western Balkan countries is outlined, drawing on analogous programmes in Central and Northern Europe.

title: Genome-wide assessment of relatedness and population stratification in the Bardoka breed for the purpose of gene bank sample selection
abstract: Gene bank collections are most useful when sampled individuals represent maximal genetic diversity at minimal redundancy. For the Bardoka breed, 64 candidate animals from 12 flocks in the Metohija and western North Macedonia were genotyped on the OvineSNP50 platform. A genomic relationship matrix was constructed and decomposed using principal component analysis. Two clear sub-clusters corresponded to geographic origin. Average pairwise genomic relatedness was 0.18, with 14 pairs exceeding 0.375 (equivalent to half-siblings or higher). Using an iterative selection algorithm to minimise mean pairwise relatedness while preserving allelic richness, an optimal panel of 40 individuals was identified from the 64 candidates, retaining 97.3 % of observed alleles and capturing both geographic sub-clusters. The selected panel was submitted to the cryopreservation programme coordinated by the Institute for Animal Husbandry, Belgrade. This study provides a practical workflow applicable to other small ruminant breeds undergoing gene bank sampling.

title: Temporal changes in allele frequencies and heterozygosity in the Vlašićka breed over a 15-year monitoring period
abstract: Long-term genetic monitoring is rare in Balkan autochthonous breeds due to discontinuous sampling efforts. This study capitalised on archived DNA and historical genotype data from Vlašićka sheep sampled in 2007, 2015, and 2023, allowing temporal analysis across three cohorts totalling 267 individuals genotyped at 18 microsatellite loci. Allelic richness declined significantly between 2007 and 2023 (from 6.1 to 5.3, p = 0.004), while expected heterozygosity showed a marginal non-significant decrease (0.672 to 0.651). Effective population size estimated from temporal allele frequency changes was Ne = 38, consistent with single-time-point LD-based estimates from earlier work. The number of private alleles dropped from 24 to 11 over the period, and three loci showed near-fixation of previously minor alleles in the youngest cohort, consistent with drift in a small population. The rate of change was faster in flocks without formal pedigree registration, underscoring the practical value of participation in the national breed register.

title: Floor cooling mats versus overhead misting systems: a comparative trial on milk yield, rectal temperature, and fatty acid changes in Holstein-Friesian cows during a natural heat wave
abstract: During an eight-day heat wave in late July 2022 (maximum daily temperature 38.4°C, mean THI 82.6), 36 Holstein-Friesian cows on a research farm were divided into three groups: rubber floor cooling mats supplied with chilled water (14°C), overhead intermittent misting with tap water, and untreated control. Rectal temperature was recorded twice daily. Milk was collected at each milking (twice daily) and pooled weekly for fatty acid analysis. Cows on floor cooling mats showed the smallest increase in rectal temperature above 38.6°C (mean peak 39.1°C vs. 39.6°C for misting and 39.9°C for control). Milk yield decline over the event was 2.1 kg/day in the mat group, 2.9 kg/day in the misting group, and 4.2 kg/day in control. Saturated fatty acid share increased by 2.1 pp in control, by 1.4 pp in the misting group, and by 0.9 pp in the mat group. Floor mats are technically simpler to retrofit in existing tie-stall barns, but higher capital cost per animal is a practical constraint.

title: Gas production kinetics during the first 14 days of maize ensiling as affected by inoculant type
abstract: Gaseous losses during the early phase of ensiling represent an underappreciated source of dry matter loss. This experiment monitored cumulative CO₂ and H₂ evolution from whole-plant maize (30% DM) treated with three inoculants: a homofermentative blend (Lactobacillus plantarum + Pediococcus acidilactici), a single-strain heterofermentative inoculant (L. buchneri), and an uninoculated control. Sealed glass fermenters (500 mL) fitted with water-displacement gas collectors were sampled every 24 h. Cumulative CO₂ at day 14 was 3.1, 4.8, and 2.6 L kg⁻¹ DM for heterofermentative, homofermentative, and control treatments, respectively. The homofermentative inoculant accelerated fermentation onset but generated greater total gas volume. Dry matter losses estimated from gas data corresponded closely with gravimetric measurements (r²=0.91). Headspace composition differed markedly between inoculant types after day 5. The method offers a practical, low-cost approach for screening inoculant candidates under laboratory conditions.

title: Myosin heavy chain isoform distribution in vastus lateralis of sedentary men aged 60–75 from Vojvodina: a histochemical survey
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined fibre-type composition in percutaneous needle biopsies of the vastus lateralis from 38 sedentary men aged 60–75 years recruited in Novi Sad and Subotica. Serial cryosections were stained for myosin ATPase at pH 9.4, 4.6, and 4.3, and fibre proportions were determined by point-counting morphometry on digitised micrographs. Type I fibres constituted a mean of 41.2 ± 8.3% of the fibre population, type IIa 34.6 ± 7.1%, and type IIx 24.2 ± 6.4%. Mean cross-sectional area was significantly lower for type IIx fibres (3 210 ± 480 µm²) compared with type I (3 890 ± 510 µm²), consistent with selective fast-fibre atrophy. No significant difference in type I proportion was found between the Novi Sad and Subotica sub-cohorts. These baseline data provide a regional reference for subsequent longitudinal and interventional studies targeting muscle ageing in the Pannonian population.

title: Capillary density and capillary-to-fibre ratio in ageing human skeletal muscle: comparison between sedentary and moderately active men from the southern Pannonian region
abstract: Capillary supply to skeletal muscle was assessed in 52 men (26 sedentary, 26 moderately active; age range 58–72 years) from Novi Sad, Sombor, and Pécs (Hungary). Cryosections were stained with Ulex europaeus agglutinin I lectin immunofluorescence to identify capillary endothelium, and laminin antibody was applied to delineate fibre boundaries. Capillary density (CD) and capillary-to-fibre ratio (C:F) were measured with semi-automated image analysis in ImageJ. Sedentary participants showed a mean CD of 287 ± 43 capillaries/mm² versus 341 ± 51 in the active group (p < 0.001). C:F ratio was 1.41 ± 0.22 versus 1.68 ± 0.24 respectively. Multiple regression indicated that daily step count, but not BMI, was a significant independent predictor of C:F. The data support the hypothesis that habitual physical inactivity contributes substantially to capillary rarefaction independent of body composition in this regional cohort.

title: Satellite cell frequency and myonuclear domain size in type I and type II fibres of sedentary elderly men: an immunofluorescence morphometry study
abstract: Satellite cell (SC) content and myonuclear domain (MND) size were quantified in needle biopsies from 30 sedentary men aged 65–78 years. Sections were co-labelled with antibodies against Pax7 (SC marker), laminin (basement membrane), and DAPI for nuclei. Confocal z-stacks were acquired and analysed using a semi-automated pipeline. Mean SC frequency was 3.8 ± 1.2 per 100 fibres in type I and 2.1 ± 0.9 per 100 fibres in type II compartments. MND was 18 300 ± 2 800 µm³ for type I and 22 600 ± 3 400 µm³ for type II. SC frequency correlated negatively with age (r = −0.54, p = 0.002). Comparison with published data from physically active age-matched men from the literature indicates that the sedentary Pannonian cohort presents with SC frequencies at the lower end of reported ranges. These findings suggest a diminished regenerative reserve in this population.

title: Slow-to-fast myosin heavy chain shift across the seventh decade: longitudinal evidence from a Vojvodina cohort
abstract: A 4-year follow-up was conducted on 22 initially sedentary men first examined at age 60–65 years. Repeat vastus lateralis biopsies were processed by immunofluorescence with antibodies against MHC-I (BA-D5), MHC-IIa (SC-71), and MHC-IIx (6H1), and fibre-type proportions were determined by automated thresholding. Over the follow-up interval, type I fibre proportion decreased from 42.3 ± 7.6% to 38.9 ± 8.1% (p = 0.031), while type IIx proportion increased from 22.8 ± 5.9% to 27.1 ± 6.7% (p = 0.014). Type IIa proportion did not change significantly. The mean cross-sectional area of type IIx fibres declined by 11.4% (p = 0.008). These changes align with a slow-to-fast transition accompanied by selective fast-fibre atrophy, consistent with denervation–reinnervation cycles reported in animal models. This is among the first longitudinal datasets documenting this transition within a defined regional population over a short interval.
