title: Methodological comparison of point-counting and automated image analysis for capillary morphometry in human skeletal muscle cryosections
abstract: Reliable measurement of capillary supply indices in skeletal muscle requires consistent methodology. This study compared traditional stereological point-counting with two automated approaches—threshold-based segmentation in ImageJ and a trainable pixel classifier in Fiji/Trainable Weka Segmentation—applied to the same set of 120 fluorescence micrographs from 20 volunteers. For capillary density, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) between point-counting and the Weka classifier was 0.96, while ICC between point-counting and threshold segmentation was 0.89. Analysis time was reduced by approximately 70% with the Weka approach. The automated classifier performed less well in sections with high background autofluorescence due to lipofuscin accumulation, a concern specific to aged muscle. A pre-processing step involving spectral unmixing markedly improved classifier accuracy in affected sections. Recommendations for standardised morphometric protocols in ageing muscle research are provided.

title: Regional variation in fibre-type composition and capillarisation among sedentary elderly from three Pannonian cities: Novi Sad, Subotica, and Szeged
abstract: Whether muscle morphological ageing differs between geographically proximate populations sharing similar lifestyles but differing in dietary traditions remains unexplored. Biopsies from 72 sedentary men (24 per city; mean age 67.4 ± 4.2 years) were processed by combined ATPase histochemistry and lectin immunofluorescence. Analysis of variance showed no statistically significant difference in type I fibre proportion (F = 1.43, p = 0.24) or capillary density (F = 1.11, p = 0.33) across city groups after adjustment for age and BMI. Mean capillary-to-fibre ratio was 1.38 ± 0.19 overall. The absence of inter-city differences supports pooling participants from these three centres in future studies and suggests that shared Pannonian dietary and lifestyle patterns are associated with homogeneous muscle morphology at this scale. The study was presented at the 14th Congress of the Central European Physiological Society.

title: Correlates of capillary rarefaction in sedentary elderly men: role of habitual sitting time, self-reported dietary protein intake, and circulating insulin-like growth factor 1
abstract: This cross-sectional analysis examined lifestyle and endocrine correlates of skeletal muscle capillarisation in 58 sedentary men aged 63–77 years. Capillary morphometry (C:F ratio and capillary density) was measured from lectinstained cryosections. Sitting time was estimated by accelerometry over 7 days; dietary protein intake was assessed by a 4-day food diary; serum IGF-1 was determined by ELISA. In multivariate linear regression, sitting time (β = −0.34, p = 0.006) and serum IGF-1 (β = 0.29, p = 0.018) were independent predictors of C:F ratio, while dietary protein intake was not significant after adjustment. Participants in the highest sitting-time tertile (>10 h/day) showed a mean C:F of 1.29 ± 0.17 compared with 1.52 ± 0.21 in the lowest tertile (p = 0.001). These findings point to prolonged sitting as a behavioural correlate of capillary rarefaction distinct from low physical activity volume.

title: Three-year change in satellite cell content and fibre-type composition after unsupervised walking programme in sedentary men aged 65–75: a pilot randomised trial
abstract: Forty sedentary men (65–75 years) were randomised to a 3-year unsupervised Nordic walking programme (n = 20; target 150 min/week) or a control group (n = 20; maintain habitual activity). Vastus lateralis biopsies at baseline and 36 months were processed for Pax7/laminin immunofluorescence and MHC isoform staining. The walking group showed a significant increase in type I fibre proportion (from 39.1 ± 7.4% to 44.3 ± 7.9%, p = 0.009) and in Pax7+ cell frequency (from 3.4 ± 1.0 to 4.9 ± 1.3 per 100 fibres, p = 0.003). Capillary-to-fibre ratio increased by 0.17 ± 0.08 in the walking group (p = 0.004) with no significant change in controls. Adherence averaged 61%. Intention-to-treat analysis attenuated but did not eliminate significant effects. These results suggest that a modest, unsupervised walking intervention can partially reverse fibre-type and capillary ageing changes over a 3-year horizon in this population.

title: Anytime Weighted A* with Adaptive Inflation for Motion Planning Under Sensor Noise
abstract: Weighted A* is a well-studied approach to trading solution quality for speed, but static inflation factors perform poorly when sensor noise causes the effective heuristic admissibility to vary across a search episode. This paper introduces an adaptive inflation scheme that adjusts the weight at each expansion step based on an online estimate of heuristic error variance derived from a particle-filter belief state. Experiments are conducted in a 2-D planar environment with a simulated differential-drive robot and Gaussian-corrupted range measurements at four noise levels. On 1,200 randomly generated problem instances, the adaptive variant finds solutions within 5% of optimal in 89% of cases while reducing planning time by a factor of 2.3 compared to a fixed-weight baseline at the same suboptimality bound. The method degrades gracefully as noise increases and requires no offline tuning of the inflation schedule.

title: A Comparison of Sampling Strategies for Probabilistic Roadmaps in Narrow-Passage Environments
abstract: Probabilistic roadmap methods (PRM) are widely used for high-dimensional motion planning, but their performance degrades sharply in environments with narrow passages due to the low probability of sampling valid configurations in those regions. This study evaluates six sampling strategies—uniform random, Gaussian bridge, obstacle-based, visibility-based, medial-axis-guided, and a hybrid of Gaussian bridge with uniform—across 48 benchmark environments in 3-D and 6-D configuration spaces. Metrics include roadmap build time, query time, and path quality measured as clearance ratio. Results show that medial-axis-guided sampling achieves the best query success rate (94.2% vs. 76.8% for uniform random) in 3-D narrow-passage scenarios but incurs a build-time penalty of approximately 3.4× compared to uniform sampling in open environments. The hybrid strategy offers the most consistent trade-off across all tested geometries.

title: Iterated Local Search for Multi-Robot Task Assignment with Precedence and Resource Constraints
abstract: Multi-robot task assignment problems combining precedence constraints, shared resource limits, and heterogeneous robot capabilities are NP-hard and resist exact solvers at scales relevant to warehouse and logistics applications. This paper formulates the problem as a constrained combinatorial optimisation instance and applies an iterated local search (ILS) metaheuristic with a custom perturbation operator designed to escape precedence-constraint violations efficiently. The perturbation selects a minimal infeasible subsequence and reorders it using a topological sort heuristic. Benchmarks are constructed from three real warehouse layouts with 12–40 robots and 60–300 tasks. ILS finds solutions within 8% of a lower bound (computed via LP relaxation) in under 4 seconds on all 240 instances tested, outperforming a genetic algorithm baseline by 11% in solution quality at equivalent runtime.

title: A Reactive Re-Planning Architecture for Robotic Arms Under Geometric Pose Uncertainty
abstract: Industrial robotic arms executing assembly tasks frequently encounter positioning errors introduced by part tolerances and gripper slip, requiring replanning at runtime. This paper describes a reactive architecture that monitors execution using wrist-mounted force-torque and vision sensors and triggers a lightweight local replanner when deviation from the reference trajectory exceeds a threshold. The local replanner uses a truncated RRT variant seeded from the current configuration and constrained to a reachability capsule around the nominal goal. In hardware experiments on a 6-DOF arm performing peg-in-hole and snap-fit assembly tasks over 500 trials each, the reactive architecture reduces failure rates from 23% to 4.7% compared to open-loop execution and from 11% to 3.1% compared to a global replan strategy, at an average additional cycle time cost of 0.38 seconds.

title: Online Replanning for Mobile Manipulators Using Monte Carlo Tree Search with Task-Level Macros
abstract: Mobile manipulators operating in partially observable environments must replan both at the navigation and manipulation level when observations invalidate prior assumptions. Full replanning from scratch is often too slow for real-time operation. This paper investigates the use of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with a library of task-level macros—precomputed parameterised subtask templates—to accelerate online replanning. Macros are extracted offline by clustering successful plan traces. During execution, MCTS selects and instantiates macros rather than primitive actions, reducing the effective branching factor from approximately 420 to 18 in the tested domain. In simulation experiments across 600 episodes in a tabletop manipulation scenario with occluded objects, macro-augmented MCTS achieves a 71% task completion rate versus 54% for flat MCTS and 48% for a reactive rule-based baseline, with a mean decision time of 210 ms per step.

title: Tight Lower Bounds for Geometric Multi-Robot Coordination via Combinatorial Packing Arguments
abstract: Lower bounds for multi-robot coordination problems in continuous geometric environments are rarely studied analytically; most work focuses on algorithms. This paper derives tight lower bounds for two coordination variants: makespan minimisation for disk robots on planar graphs and energy-optimal coordination for convex-body robots in a polygonal arena. The bounds are established through reductions from combinatorial packing problems—specifically, bin packing for the makespan case and strip packing for the energy case—and are shown to be tight by constructing matching upper-bound algorithm families. For disk robots of radius r on a planar graph with n nodes, the derived lower bound on makespan is Ω(n·r²/A) where A is the arena area. The results provide theoretical grounding for benchmarking heuristic methods and help identify problem regimes where approximation guarantees are achievable.

title: Lazy Evaluation Strategies in Conflict-Based Search for Large Multi-Agent Pathfinding Instances
abstract: Conflict-Based Search (CBS) scales poorly beyond 50 agents in dense environments because the number of constraints in the constraint tree grows rapidly and each node requires a costly low-level A* invocation. This paper systematically evaluates four lazy evaluation strategies—lazy A* re-expansion, deferred constraint validation, partial-conflict detection, and node subsumption—within the CBS framework and analyses their interactions. Experiments are conducted on 32×32 and 64×64 grid maps with agent counts from 30 to 150 drawn from standard MAPF benchmarks and three new logistics-motivated instances. The combination of deferred constraint validation and node subsumption reduces the number of low-level A* calls by 43% on average and allows CBS to solve instances with 100 agents in under 30 seconds on maps where the vanilla solver times out at 60 seconds. Trade-offs in memory consumption are documented.

title: A Covariance Matrix Tapered Reconstruction Scheme for DOA Estimation Under Non-Uniform Noise Power
abstract: Standard subspace DOA estimators assume that sensor noise powers are equal or known. In practice, receivers in compact arrays often show gain imbalances of 1–3 dB between channels. This paper proposes a reconstruction procedure in which the off-diagonal entries of the sample covariance matrix are retained while the diagonal is re-estimated using a least-squares fit to a parameterised noise model. The approach is evaluated on synthetic data from a six-element array with inter-element spacing of half a wavelength at 900 MHz, using 50 to 500 snapshots and signal-to-noise ratios between –5 and 15 dB. The proposed reconstruction reduces the root-mean-square error of estimated angles by 28–41% relative to uncorrected MUSIC across the tested conditions. Computational overhead compared with standard MUSIC is negligible, making the method suitable for real-time implementations on embedded processors.

title: Spatial Smoothing With Partial Covariance Reconstruction for Coherent Source Separation in Compact Arrays
abstract: Coherent sources arising from multipath propagation cause rank deficiency in the signal covariance matrix, defeating standard subspace estimators. Spatial smoothing restores rank but reduces effective aperture, which is especially costly for arrays with fewer than ten elements. This paper combines spatial smoothing with partial covariance reconstruction: after smoothing, off-diagonal entries at lags where the noise contribution is estimated to be dominant are replaced by model-predicted signal-only values derived from a preliminary single-snapshot spectral estimate. The combined method is tested on a simulated five-element uniform linear array receiving two coherent sources at 5° and 12° separation. At 200 snapshots and 5 dB SNR, the proposed scheme resolves the two sources in 91% of trials versus 63% for smoothing alone. Sensitivity to the noise model mismatch is analysed and shown to be mild for correlation errors below 15%.

title: Iterative Reweighted Subspace Fitting for DOA Estimation in Spatially Colored Noise
abstract: Weighted subspace fitting (WSF) offers asymptotically optimal DOA estimates but requires knowledge of the noise covariance matrix, which is rarely available in colored noise environments. This paper presents an iterative procedure in which an initial DOA estimate from MUSIC is used to form a signal-subspace projection, which in turn allows a structured noise covariance estimate via restricted maximum likelihood. The updated noise estimate is then fed back into the WSF criterion. The iteration is shown to converge in three to five steps for scenarios with two to four sources on a seven-element array. Across 5 000 Monte Carlo trials at SNRs from 0 to 20 dB and 100 to 1 000 snapshots, the iterative method closely approaches the Cramér-Rao bound derived for the unknown noise covariance case. The paper also reports results from a testbed experiment using software-defined radio hardware at 433 MHz.
venue: Acta Electrotechnica et Informatica

title: Array Signal Processing for Direction Finding: Methods, Limitations and Practical Considerations
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured treatment of subspace-based direction-of-arrival estimation methods relevant to compact arrays in real-world deployment conditions. It covers the signal model, properties of the sample covariance matrix, the MUSIC and ESPRIT families, root-finding variants, and weighted subspace fitting. Special attention is given to the conditions under which standard assumptions—white spatially uncorrelated noise, sufficient snapshots, well-separated sources—fail, and to practical remedies including covariance reconstruction, forward-backward averaging, and diagonal loading. Numerical examples throughout use arrays of four to eight elements at frequencies between 400 MHz and 2.4 GHz. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and practicing engineers who need a working understanding of the statistical underpinnings without requiring a full research-level treatment of asymptotic theory.

title: Structured Covariance Estimation Using Toeplitz Approximation for Correlated Noise in Uniform Linear Arrays
abstract: For a stationary uniform linear array in a spatially homogeneous noise field, the noise covariance matrix has Toeplitz structure. This paper exploits that structure to improve noise covariance estimation from a limited number of snapshots by projecting the sample noise covariance onto the set of Hermitian Toeplitz matrices using an alternating projections algorithm. The projection is seeded with an initial noise covariance estimate obtained after nulling estimated signal directions. The method is evaluated for arrays of six and eight elements, with 50 to 300 snapshots and spatial noise correlation coefficients between 0.2 and 0.8. MUSIC angular RMSE after Toeplitz-constrained reconstruction is on average 35% lower than with unconstrained sample noise subtraction and 18% lower than with simple diagonal loading. Results hold across SNRs from –2 to 15 dB. Convergence of the alternating projections is typically achieved in under 20 iterations.

title: Effect of Mutual Coupling on Covariance Matrix Reconstruction–Based DOA Estimation for a Five-Element Dipole Array
abstract: Mutual coupling among closely spaced dipole elements modifies both the signal steering vectors and the effective noise covariance, invalidating assumptions underlying standard covariance reconstruction procedures. This paper characterises the angular error introduced by neglected mutual coupling for a five-element half-wavelength dipole array with inter-element spacings of 0.3 to 0.5 wavelengths at 868 MHz. Coupling coefficients are obtained from a full-wave electromagnetic simulation using method-of-moments software. A calibration-based compensation scheme is then applied: the coupling matrix estimated from simulations is used to pre-correct the received data before subspace estimation. After compensation, MUSIC RMSE decreases from 4.1° to 0.9° at 10 dB SNR for 0.3-wavelength spacing. Residual errors after compensation are attributed to fabrication tolerances modelled as random perturbations with 2% standard deviation, and their statistical effect on final DOA estimates is quantified.

title: Comparison of Ray-Tracing and Semi-Empirical Propagation Models in a Greenhouse Metallic-Frame Environment at 868 MHz
abstract: Modern greenhouse complexes use aluminium or galvanised steel frame structures that generate complex multipath conditions relevant to in-greenhouse sensor deployments. This study compares predictions from a deterministic 3-D ray-tracing tool calibrated against greenhouse frame material parameters with those from three semi-empirical models (Okumura-Hata extended, COST 231 Walfish-Ikegami, and a locally derived regression model). Measurements were conducted in a 120 m × 40 m tomato greenhouse in Futog at 868 MHz, with 320 receiver positions on a 2 m grid and transmitter mounted at 3.5 m height near the central irrigation spine. The ray-tracer using up to third-order reflections achieved an RMSE of 5.8 dB; all three semi-empirical models exceeded 9 dB RMSE. The dominant error in semi-empirical models occurs within 25 m of the frame pillars, where specular reflection dominates. Practical guidance on ray-tracer configuration for greenhouse deployments is provided.

title: Relationship between temperature-humidity index and somatic cell count in Holstein-Friesian cows on commercial farms in Vojvodina
abstract: Elevated temperature-humidity index (THI) values during summer months are associated with immune suppression and increased mastitis incidence in dairy cattle. This study examined records from six commercial dairy farms in Vojvodina over three consecutive years (2009–2011), covering 1,240 lactation records. Monthly THI averages were calculated from regional meteorological data and correlated with bulk-tank and individual cow somatic cell counts (SCC). Results showed a significant positive correlation between THI exceeding 72 and SCC above 400,000 cells/mL (r = 0.61, p < 0.01). Farms with mechanical ventilation in free-stall barns displayed a weaker correlation compared to tie-stall systems without cooling infrastructure. Multiparous cows in their third or higher lactation exhibited the strongest THI–SCC relationship. These findings indicate that housing design and parity interact with ambient heat load in determining udder health outcomes, and that THI thresholds used in temperate Northern European contexts may underestimate risk in the Pannonian climate.

title: Effect of summer heat load on milk fatty acid profile in mid-lactation Holstein-Friesian cows in northern Serbia
abstract: Sixteen mid-lactation Holstein-Friesian cows were monitored across a full summer season (June–August 2012) on a single commercial farm in the Bačka region. Milk samples were collected biweekly and fatty acid composition was determined by gas chromatography–flame ionisation detection following direct methylation of extracted fat. Simultaneously, rectal temperatures, respiration rates, and barn THI were recorded. During periods when daily mean THI exceeded 75, the proportion of saturated fatty acids in milk fat increased by an average of 3.8 percentage points relative to the thermoneutral baseline, while conjugated linoleic acid (CLA, cis-9, trans-11 isomer) decreased by 0.18 percentage points of total fat. Unsaturated-to-saturated fatty acid ratio dropped from 0.71 to 0.63 under high heat load. Regression analysis indicated that rectal temperature explained 34% of variance in total saturated fatty acid content. These changes are consistent with reduced rumen biohydrogenation capacity and altered de novo synthesis under physiological heat stress.

title: Sprinkler and fan cooling systems in free-stall dairy barns: microclimate measurements and cow behaviour during peak summer heat
abstract: Microclimate conditions and cow behaviour were compared across two commercial free-stall barns in Vojvodina: one equipped with a combined sprinkler–fan system and one relying on natural ventilation alone. Sensors recording temperature, relative humidity, and airspeed were placed at shoulder height at 12 positions per barn. Behavioural observations of 40 focal animals per farm were conducted using scan sampling at 30-minute intervals across 21 consecutive days in July 2013. THI at cow level averaged 79.4 in the naturally ventilated barn compared to 73.1 in the cooled barn. Cows in the cooled barn spent on average 52 minutes more per day at the feed bunk and 38 minutes less standing in the loafing area. Dry matter intake estimated from refusal weights was 1.9 kg/day higher in the cooled group. These differences translated to a 1.4 kg/day milk yield advantage. The study provides farm-level evidence supporting investment in active cooling infrastructure in the Pannonian climate zone.

title: Heat stress mitigation strategies in dairy cattle: a review of dietary, management and housing approaches with emphasis on Southeastern European conditions
abstract: Dairy production in Southeastern Europe faces increasingly frequent summer heat events driven by the continental Pannonian climate, with THI values exceeding the stress threshold of 72 for 60–90 days per year in the region. This book chapter reviews published evidence on three categories of heat stress mitigation: dietary supplementation (antioxidants, niacin, rumen buffers, osmoregulatory additives), management interventions (milking frequency, turnout restriction, water provision), and housing modifications (ventilation, cooling systems, orientation, shading). For each category, the chapter summarises effect sizes on milk yield, composition, reproductive performance, and animal welfare indicators. Special attention is given to economic feasibility under typical farm sizes and investment conditions in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia. Gaps are identified in long-term controlled trials reflecting local genetics and feeding practices. The chapter is intended as a practical reference for extension services and farm advisors in the region.

title: Niacin supplementation at two doses during summer heat: rumen fermentation parameters and milk omega-3 to omega-6 ratio in dairy cows
abstract: Twenty-four multiparous Holstein-Friesian cows were allocated to three equal groups: control, low niacin (6 g/day), and high niacin (12 g/day) supplementation over a 45-day summer period (mean barn THI 77.8). Rumen fluid was collected via stomach tube on days 0, 22, and 45 for pH, volatile fatty acid (VFA) concentration, and ammonia nitrogen assay. Milk samples were collected weekly and fat was analysed by GC-FID. High niacin supplementation maintained rumen pH above 6.2 on all sampling days, while the control group showed mean rumen pH of 5.98 on day 22. Total VFA concentration was 12% higher in the high niacin group compared to control (p < 0.05). The omega-3 to omega-6 ratio in milk fat was 0.09 in control versus 0.12 in the high niacin group at day 45. Alpha-linolenic acid (C18:3n-3) increased significantly in supplemented groups. No effect on milk protein content was detected. The data indicate that niacin supplementation at 12 g/day has measurable benefits for rumen function and favourable fatty acid ratios under summer conditions.

title: Interannual variation in heat stress intensity on Vojvodina dairy farms 2015–2020 and predicted exposure under two climate scenarios
abstract: Daily maximum temperature and relative humidity records from six automated weather stations in Vojvodina were used to calculate THI for each day of the May–September period from 2015 to 2020. Cumulative heat stress load (HSL), defined as the integral of THI above 72 per season, ranged from 214 to 487 THI-hours across years and stations, indicating substantial interannual variability. A farm-survey component gathered data on current cooling infrastructure from 22 Holstein-Friesian operations. Using regional climate projections from the CORDEX-SEE ensemble under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, HSL was projected forward to the 2041–2060 window. Under RCP4.5 the median projected increase was 38% compared to the 2015–2020 mean; under RCP8.5 the projected increase reached 71%. Only 32% of surveyed farms had any mechanical cooling. The study quantifies the gap between current farm preparedness and projected future heat load and provides a baseline for economic assessment of cooling investment decisions.

title: Pressure distribution along drip irrigation laterals on uniform slopes: a comparison of analytical and numerical approaches
abstract: Pressure variation along drip laterals laid on sloped terrain is a central design problem because elevation changes modify the available pressure head at each emitter, directly affecting discharge uniformity. This study compared four analytical models (Christiansen, Wu–Gitlin, Keller–Karmeli, and a friction-gradient integration approach) against finite-difference numerical simulations for laterals of 50 m to 200 m in length on slopes between −15% and +15%. Field data were collected from two experimental plots at the University of Novi Sad research vineyard using 72 pressure transducers at 2 m intervals. The finite-difference model reproduced measured pressures with a root-mean-square error below 0.18 m for all tested configurations. Among the analytical models, the Wu–Gitlin approach had the smallest systematic bias on downhill slopes but overestimated end-pressure on uphill runs by up to 0.9 m. Practical design charts are presented for lateral diameters of 16 mm, 20 mm, and 25 mm at operational inlet pressures of 1.0 and 1.5 bar, enabling field engineers to select lateral length without iterative computation.

title: Effect of lateral inlet pressure and slope gradient on emission uniformity in gravity-fed drip systems for hillside vineyards
abstract: Gravity-fed drip irrigation is used in areas where energy costs are a constraint, but managing emission uniformity on sloped vineyards requires careful selection of operating pressure and lateral geometry. This study evaluated emission uniformity (EU) for three lateral lengths (60 m, 100 m, 140 m) at inlet pressures of 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0 bar across slope gradients of 5%, 10%, and 18% under both uphill and downhill lateral orientations. A total of 1 296 individual emitter-flow measurements were collected over two growing seasons. EU ranged from 61% in the worst-case scenario (140 m, 18% uphill, 0.6 bar) to 96% in the best case (60 m, 5% downhill, 1.0 bar). Multiple linear regression identified slope gradient and lateral length as the dominant factors, together explaining 74% of EU variance. Recommendations are made for maximum lateral lengths as a function of slope and available head, with an emphasis on maintaining EU above 85%.

title: Seasonal variation in emitter discharge coefficients under field conditions in the Fruška Gora wine region
abstract: Emitter manufacturers specify discharge coefficients under controlled laboratory conditions, but field performance can deviate substantially due to water quality, temperature fluctuations, and partial clogging. This study monitored 480 pressure-compensating emitters installed in four commercial vineyards on Fruška Gora over three consecutive seasons (2012–2014). Emitter flow was measured gravimetrically at monthly intervals; water samples were collected for iron, manganese, bicarbonate, and suspended-solids analysis. Mean discharge coefficients declined by 4–11% from spring to late summer and by a cumulative 7–19% over three seasons. Correlation analysis showed that iron concentration (range 0.12–0.84 mg/L) and total suspended solids (15–62 mg/L) were the strongest predictors of seasonal drift. Two emitter brands showed statistically significant discharge reduction after the first season while a third maintained performance within manufacturer tolerance. Results indicate that irrigation scheduling based on fixed nominal emitter flow may overestimate actual application by 8–14% by the third season without maintenance intervention.

title: Hydraulic design criteria for drip laterals on terraced parcels with variable inter-terrace slope
abstract: Terraced vineyard parcels present an irregular hydraulic boundary condition because each terrace platform is nearly level while the transition between terraces introduces a discrete elevation step. Conventional uniform-slope design equations do not adequately capture this geometry. This study developed a segmented hydraulic model in which each terrace segment is treated as a separate lateral section with its own inlet condition derived from the pressure at the end of the previous segment. The model was validated against field measurements on two terraced plots in the Vršac Hills district (terrace widths 4–8 m, inter-terrace slopes 30–55%). Simulated versus measured pressure profiles agreed within ±0.22 m across all 148 measurement points. The study then used the validated model to generate design charts showing maximum permissible lateral length per terrace tier as a function of header pressure, terrace width, and riser elevation difference. A worked design example is provided for a representative 2-ha terraced parcel.

title: Clogging of drip emitters by iron-oxidising bacteria in shallow groundwater-fed irrigation systems in Vojvodina
abstract: Shallow groundwater used for drip irrigation in the Vojvodina plain frequently contains elevated dissolved iron (0.5–3.2 mg/L) and supports populations of iron-oxidising bacteria (Gallionella and Leptothrix spp.) that can precipitate iron hydroxide deposits inside emitter flow paths. This study investigated clogging rates in 320 non-compensating button emitters (nominal flow 2 L/h and 4 L/h) over a single 120-day irrigation season. Emitters were divided into four treatment groups: untreated, intermittent chlorine injection (2 mg/L), continuous acid injection (pH 6.5), and combined chlorine plus acid. Discharge uniformity was measured bi-weekly. The untreated group showed a 23% mean reduction in discharge by day 90. Continuous acid injection maintained EU above 90% throughout the season. Bacterial plate counts on sacrificially removed emitters confirmed that acid injection reduced iron-oxidiser populations by 98% compared with the untreated control. Water pH reduction to 6.5 is recommended as the minimum management measure when groundwater iron exceeds 0.8 mg/L.

title: Hydraulic performance of subsurface drip irrigation laterals under vineyard row compaction conditions
abstract: Subsurface drip irrigation (SDI) is increasingly used in perennial crop systems to reduce surface evaporation, but soil compaction around buried laterals may alter pipe cross-section and thereby change friction losses compared with surface installation. This study examined 16 mm polyethylene laterals buried at 25 cm depth under vineyard rows after three, five, and seven years of operation, comparing measured internal diameter, ovality, and head-loss coefficients with newly installed controls. Laterals were excavated from two commercial vineyards in the Srem district. After seven years, mean internal diameter was reduced by 0.31 mm (1.9%) due to soil loading and pipe creep, leading to a 4.7% increase in head loss per unit length at a flow rate of 0.6 L/h per emitter. Emission uniformity decreased by 2.1 percentage points on a 100 m lateral. While practically modest, these changes should be accounted for in irrigation scheduling software after five or more years of SDI operation.

title: Irrigation uniformity and vine water status under two drip lateral spacings in a Chardonnay block on a 12% slope
abstract: The interaction between hydraulic design and agronomic outcome in sloped vineyards is rarely measured directly. This study established a replicated field trial in a Chardonnay block in the Vršac Hills comparing two lateral configurations: single lateral per two-row interspace (conventional) versus two laterals per interspace (paired). Both systems were designed to achieve EU ≥ 90% at the head of the block; the single-lateral system fell to EU = 83% at the lowest emitter row due to elevation effects, while the paired system maintained EU = 91% throughout. Vine water status was assessed using stem water potential at midday (Ψstem) at ten measurement dates over two seasons. On the driest measurement day, Ψstem was −1.08 MPa in the lower rows of the single-lateral treatment versus −0.92 MPa in the paired treatment, a statistically significant difference (p < 0.01) linked to hydraulic non-uniformity. Yield and berry weight were not significantly different between treatments, but berry sugar accumulation was 0.8 °Brix lower in the lower rows of the single-lateral block.

title: Measured and modelled flow uniformity in drip laterals: a synthesis of 15 years of field data from northern Serbia
abstract: This book chapter synthesises hydraulic field data collected between 2008 and 2022 from 34 drip-irrigated vineyard and orchard sites in northern Serbia, covering 112 individual lateral segments ranging in length from 28 m to 210 m and in slope from −22% to +22%. The dataset is used to evaluate the predictive accuracy of five hydraulic design models against measured emission uniformity values. Across all 112 segments, model predictions had a mean absolute error of 2.6–6.8 EU percentage points depending on the model. The segmented approach developed for terraced parcels consistently showed the smallest error (2.6 pp). A synthesis diagram is presented relating achievable EU to lateral length, slope category, and inlet pressure class, which can serve as a rapid field-assessment tool. Practical guidance is provided for incorporating local water quality factors, lateral age, and pipe diameter selection into routine design practice in the Pannonian Plain context.

title: Automated pressure monitoring for real-time detection of emitter clogging in vineyard drip systems
abstract: Early detection of localised emitter clogging is important for maintaining irrigation uniformity, but manual checking of large vineyard drip systems is time-consuming. This study describes and evaluates a low-cost monitoring system consisting of 12 datalogger-connected pressure transducers distributed along two 120 m laterals in a test vineyard. Pressure was logged at 10-minute intervals over a full irrigation season. A threshold-based alert algorithm was developed using pressure signature patterns observed during controlled partial-clogging experiments in the laboratory (25%, 50%, and 75% flow reduction in 2, 5, and 10 emitters). In the field, the algorithm correctly identified seven genuine clogging events out of eight that occurred, with two false positives triggered by air-pocket formation after system restart. Response time from clogging onset to alert generation averaged 3.2 hours. The system hardware cost was approximately 340 EUR per lateral, suggesting practical feasibility for medium to large commercial vineyards where water uniformity and crop value justify the investment.

title: Thermal response test analysis for shallow boreholes in the Pannonian Basin: measured ground thermal conductivity and comparison with lithological estimates
abstract: Thermal response tests (TRTs) were conducted on six single U-tube boreholes drilled to depths between 50 m and 80 m at sites in Vojvodina, northern Serbia. The Pannonian Basin sedimentary sequence at these locations is characterised by alternating sand and clay layers with measured bulk thermal conductivities ranging from 1.6 to 2.3 W/(m·K). Undisturbed ground temperatures at 10 m depth varied between 13.1 °C and 14.4 °C across the test sites. TRT data were analysed using the line-source approximation and a parameter estimation routine to extract effective thermal conductivity and borehole thermal resistance. Results were compared against conductivity values estimated from borehole lithological logs using a geometric-mean mixing rule. Agreement was generally within 12 %, but two sites with high silt content showed systematic underestimation by the lithological method. Borehole thermal resistance values ranged from 0.08 to 0.14 m·K/W, consistent with the grouting materials used. The dataset provides a regional reference for preliminary borehole field sizing in this geological setting.

title: A finite-line-source g-function model for inclined boreholes and its validation against distributed-temperature sensing data
abstract: Standard g-function tabulations assume perfectly vertical, equally spaced boreholes, an assumption that is routinely violated on constrained urban plots. This paper derives a semi-analytical finite-line-source g-function for arbitrarily inclined boreholes and implements it in a time-stepping simulation tool. The model accounts for borehole-to-borehole thermal interaction through superposition of point-source solutions integrated along each borehole axis. Validation used a five-borehole pilot field at the Faculty of Technical Sciences campus in Novi Sad, where distributed-temperature sensing fibre-optic cables had been installed in two boreholes. Simulated fluid temperatures matched measured profiles within ±0.35 °C over a two-year monitoring period covering both heating-dominated and nearly balanced seasonal cycles. Sensitivity analysis showed that a 10° inclination from vertical in a 6×6 m grid reduces the effective thermal resistance between adjacent boreholes by approximately 8 % compared with the vertical case, with modest consequences for long-term ground temperature drift predictions.

title: Long-term ground temperature drift in a residential borehole field: a ten-year simulation study for the Novi Sad climate
abstract: Asymmetric heating and cooling loads are common in continental European residential buildings, where winter heating demand dominates. Over multi-decade operation, net heat extraction causes progressive ground temperature depression that reduces heat pump evaporating temperatures and degrades the seasonal coefficient of performance (SCOP). This study simulates a 12-borehole field (80 m depth, 6 m spacing) supplying a 200 m² residential building in Novi Sad using a validated transient g-function model coupled to a building energy model calibrated against a two-year monitored dataset. Annual heat extraction exceeds heat rejection by a factor of 2.8. Over a 25-year simulation horizon, mean borehole wall temperature decreases by 4.1 K, and the SCOP of the water-to-water heat pump decreases from an initial 3.8 to 3.1, a reduction of 18 %. Three mitigation strategies are evaluated: solar thermal recharging, load balancing through a backup cooling circuit, and increased borehole spacing. Solar recharging at 5 m² collector area per borehole limits the temperature drop to 1.6 K and largely preserves SCOP.
venue: Applied Thermal Engineering

title: Seasonal COP measurements and uncertainty quantification for a ground-source heat pump installation in a school building in Subotica
abstract: Field measurement campaigns on operating ground-source heat pump systems in Serbian buildings are scarce, limiting the calibration of simulation models. This paper reports seasonal COP measurements from a water-to-water heat pump installed in a school building in Subotica, Vojvodina, over three consecutive heating seasons (2015–2018). The system comprises eight 75 m boreholes serving 1,200 m² of floor area. Measurement uncertainties in flow rate (±1.5 %), inlet and outlet temperatures (±0.1 K), and electrical power (±0.8 %) were propagated using a Monte Carlo approach to obtain SCOP uncertainty bands. Measured SCOP values were 3.54 ± 0.11, 3.47 ± 0.10, and 3.41 ± 0.11 for the three seasons, indicating a statistically significant year-on-year decline of approximately 0.06–0.07 per season consistent with ground cooling. A simplified linear regression model relating mean borehole inlet temperature to measured SCOP explains 91 % of the observed variance.

title: Comparison of short time-step models for vertical borehole heat exchangers: numerical vs. analytical approaches under intermittent heat pump operation
abstract: Ground-source heat pump systems cycle on and off on timescales of minutes to hours, producing short-term temperature fluctuations in the borehole that are not captured by standard g-function methods, which assume uniform radial heat flux. This study compares four short-time-step modelling approaches—the capacity resistance model, the numerical finite-difference borehole model, the duct ground heat storage (DST) model, and a composite cylindrical source analytical solution—against high-frequency temperature measurements collected at 30-second intervals in a monitored single borehole at the faculty campus in Novi Sad. All four models were compared over a two-week period in January 2019 with 847 on/off cycles. The finite-difference and composite cylindrical source models reproduced measured borehole wall temperatures within ±0.4 K. The capacity resistance model showed systematic over-prediction of peak temperatures by up to 1.8 K during the first 10 minutes after start-up. Results are used to select an appropriate sub-hourly model for subsequent coupled building-ground simulations.

title: Calibration of a transient borehole field model using Bayesian inference and monitoring data from a public building installation
abstract: Predictive models for borehole field thermal performance contain uncertain parameters—ground thermal conductivity, volumetric heat capacity, and borehole thermal resistance—that are commonly estimated from a single TRT at one representative borehole. This paper demonstrates a Bayesian calibration workflow applied to a 10-borehole field serving a municipal sports hall in Zrenjanin, where two years of sub-hourly heat pump power, source-side flow rate, and borehole inlet/outlet temperature data were available. The prior distributions for the three uncertain parameters were set using TRT results and regional geological data. A Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler updated the posteriors using the monitoring data, reducing parameter uncertainty substantially: the posterior standard deviation for ground thermal conductivity narrowed from 0.21 to 0.07 W/(m·K). Predictions of borehole mean fluid temperature over a subsequent 18-month validation period fell within the 90 % credible interval. The calibrated model was then used to project 15-year SCOP trajectories with quantified uncertainty bounds.

title: Borehole thermal energy storage for seasonal load shifting in a district heating micro-network: pre-feasibility modelling for a Novi Sad residential block
abstract: Seasonal borehole thermal energy storage (BTES) concentrates solar or waste heat injected in summer for extraction in winter, potentially eliminating the thermal imbalance problem that causes long-term SCOP degradation. This pre-feasibility study models a BTES array of 36 boreholes (60 m depth, 3 m spacing) coupled to 800 m² of flat-plate solar collectors serving a 1980s residential block of 48 apartments in Novi Sad. The simulation combines a transient g-function borehole model with a stratified storage temperature model and an hourly building demand profile derived from energy audits. After a four-year charging phase, the system reaches quasi-steady periodic operation with a storage efficiency of 52 % and a solar fraction for space heating of 68 %. The ground temperature in the BTES core stabilises around 38 °C, requiring a heat pump with a high source-side temperature capability. Economic analysis at current Serbian electricity and gas tariffs gives a simple payback period of 19 years, sensitive primarily to the assumed solar collector cost.

title: Influence of dissolved oxygen accumulation on biomass productivity in a pilot flat-panel photobioreactor
abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) accumulation is a well-known inhibitory factor in closed photobioreactor systems, yet quantitative data under variable outdoor light conditions remain scarce. This study tracked DO concentration, pH, and biomass dry weight every 30 minutes over 14 consecutive days in a 120-litre flat-panel unit cultivating Scenedesmus obliquus at the Faculty of Technical Sciences campus. Aeration rates were varied between 0.05 and 0.20 vvm in separate experimental blocks. At the lowest aeration rate, DO regularly exceeded 35 mg/L during peak afternoon hours and correlated with a 22 % reduction in daily biomass productivity compared to the 0.10 vvm baseline. A semi-empirical inhibition term was fitted to the productivity–DO relationship (R² = 0.87). Energy consumption of the blower was monitored and found to account for 18–26 % of total electrical input to the system depending on aeration rate. The results were used to define an aeration schedule that balances DO control against energy cost.

title: Comparison of measurement uncertainty in FTIR versus electrochemical cell methods for flue-gas NOx quantification in small biomass appliances
abstract: Both Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectrometry and electrochemical cells are used for NOx measurement in small combustion appliance testing, but their agreement under field-like conditions is not well characterised. This study ran both methods in parallel on a 20 kW pellet burner across six fuel types and three load levels, producing 54 paired measurement sets. The FTIR system used here resolved NO and NO₂ independently; the electrochemical cell reported NOx as a single channel after converter reduction. Mean relative difference between methods was −4.2 % (electrochemical lower), with a standard deviation of 6.8 %. Discrepancies widened at low NOx concentrations below 70 mg/Nm³, where electrochemical cross-sensitivity to water vapour contributed an estimated ±9 mg/Nm³ error. NO₂ fraction in total NOx varied between 4 % and 17 % depending on load and fuel; ignoring this split did not bias the electrochemical reading systematically. Recommendations are given for minimum instrument specifications in EN 303-5 compliance testing.

title: Eigenvalue Interlacing for Subgraph Perturbations in Regular Graphs
abstract: This paper examines how the addition or removal of a single edge in a k-regular graph perturbs the full spectrum of its adjacency matrix. Using the Cauchy interlacing theorem and rank-one update analysis, explicit bounds are derived on the displacement of each eigenvalue as a function of k and the local structure around the modified edge. The results are validated on a family of circulant graphs with vertex counts ranging from 20 to 500, generated with SageMath. Numerical experiments show that the spectral gap—the difference between the two largest eigenvalues—changes by at most 2/√k for edge insertions, confirming a conjecture stated informally in earlier literature. The paper also identifies extremal cases where the bound is tight, providing a graph-theoretic characterisation of these configurations. The findings have direct implications for sensitivity analysis of Laplacian-based synchronisation criteria in lightly perturbed network topologies.

title: On the Energy of Threshold Graphs and Related Constructions
abstract: Graph energy, defined as the sum of absolute values of adjacency eigenvalues, is investigated for the class of threshold graphs, which are built recursively by adding isolated or dominating vertices. Closed-form expressions for the energy of threshold graphs on up to 12 vertices are derived and tabulated; a recursive formula for the characteristic polynomial is established that reduces computation from O(n³) to O(n²) for this class. Using exhaustive enumeration via SageMath for graphs up to 16 vertices, we identify the threshold graph on n vertices that maximises energy for each n ≤ 16, and propose a conjecture about the extremal structure for general n. Comparisons with non-threshold graphs of equal order and size show that threshold graphs are generally not energy-extremal in the broader class, settling a question raised in a 2008 survey. The paper includes 14 figures illustrating spectral distributions.

title: Spectral Bounds on the Diameter of Distance-Regular Graphs
abstract: This work establishes improved spectral upper bounds on the diameter d of distance-regular graphs in terms of the number of distinct eigenvalues and the valency. The classical Bannai–Ito bound d ≤ (s−1)/2, where s is the number of distinct eigenvalues, is refined by incorporating information from the second-largest and smallest eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix. For a test collection of 47 known distance-regular graphs drawn from the literature, the new bound reduces the overestimate of diameter by an average of 1.3 compared with the Bannai–Ito bound. The proof technique combines polynomial approximation arguments with explicit evaluation of the minimal polynomial at the identity. A short section discusses applicability to sensor placement in communication networks where diameter constraints model worst-case latency.

title: Normalised Laplacian Spectra of Caterpillar Graphs and Diffusion Properties
abstract: Caterpillar graphs—trees obtained by attaching pendant vertices to a path—are parameterised by the spine length p and the pendant-degree sequence (d₁, …, d_p). The full normalised Laplacian spectrum is computed analytically for symmetric caterpillars (all d_i equal) and expressed in terms of p and the common pendant degree d. For asymmetric caterpillars, a numerical study covering 3 ≤ p ≤ 20 and 1 ≤ d_i ≤ 8 is performed with NetworkX and NumPy. The spectral gap λ₂ is shown to decrease monotonically with spine length and to increase with pendant degree, with an approximate formula λ₂ ≈ 1/(1 + p/(2d)) fitting the numerical data with R² = 0.97. Heat-kernel diffusion simulations quantify how these spectral properties control the mixing time on caterpillar topologies, relevant to modelling hierarchical communication trees.

title: Eigenvector Localisation in Sparse Random Graphs Near the Connectivity Threshold
abstract: For Erdős–Rényi random graphs G(n, c/n) with c slightly above 1, the eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix corresponding to eigenvalues outside the bulk semicircle are studied empirically using ensembles of size n = 2000, with 200 realisations per value of c ∈ {1.05, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0}. Participation ratio and inverse participation ratio are computed for each eigenvector. Results confirm that the leading eigenvector remains localised on the giant component's high-degree vertices for c < 2, with delocalisation occurring gradually as c increases beyond 2. A phase diagram in the (c, n) plane is sketched based on the numerical evidence. Additionally, implications for synchronisation are examined: localised leading eigenvectors correspond to configurations where synchronisation initiates locally around hubs rather than spreading uniformly, which can slow global synchronisation by up to 40% in simulated Kuramoto dynamics on these graphs.

title: A Comparison of Spectral Clustering Methods for Detecting Synchronisation Communities in Power-Grid-Like Networks
abstract: Four spectral clustering algorithms—unnormalised, normalised (Shi–Malik variant), ratio-cut, and Bethe Hessian—are benchmarked on synthetic power-grid-like networks generated from a planar random geometric graph model with 100 to 2000 nodes and average degree 2.7, matching statistics reported for European transmission networks. Ground-truth communities are defined by the planted partition structure used in generation. Clustering quality is assessed by normalised mutual information (NMI) and adjusted Rand index (ARI). The Bethe Hessian method achieves the highest NMI (0.83 ± 0.04) across all tested sizes, outperforming unnormalised spectral clustering (NMI 0.71 ± 0.07) at n = 500. Synchronisation robustness—measured as the minimum coupling strength needed for full phase-locking after a single node failure—correlates with intra-community algebraic connectivity (Pearson r = 0.79), suggesting a practical use of spectral community detection in network hardening.

title: Cheeger-Type Inequalities for Signed Graphs and Their Role in Anti-Phase Synchronisation
abstract: A Cheeger constant for signed graphs is defined by extending the classical edge-boundary ratio to account for negative edges, which represent inhibitory or repulsive couplings. An analogue of the Cheeger inequality is proved, relating the signed Cheeger constant h± to the smallest eigenvalue of the signed Laplacian: h±²/2Δ ≤ λ_min ≤ 2h±. The bound is compared with the classical result on a set of 30 signed graphs constructed from social-network datasets with artificial sign assignments and on random signed graphs with edge-sign probability p ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.5}. For systems of Stuart–Landau oscillators with inhibitory edges, numerical integration shows that λ_min predicts the onset of anti-phase synchronisation clusters more accurately than unsigned spectral gap measures, with prediction error below 5% for networks with up to 300 nodes. The result provides a computable criterion for designing networks that exhibit prescribed synchronisation patterns.

title: Spectral Graph Characterisation of Synchronisation Onset in Heterogeneous IoT Mesh Networks
abstract: Mesh network topologies used in low-power IoT deployments are modelled as random geometric graphs with non-uniform node densities reflecting building-interior deployment scenarios. Three real floorplan layouts from public building-information datasets are discretised into node configurations of 80 to 600 devices. For each layout, the normalised Laplacian spectrum is computed and its smallest non-zero eigenvalue λ₂ is used to predict the minimum broadcast repetition rate needed for time-synchronisation convergence below a 1 ms jitter target, as per IEEE 802.15.4 requirements. Predictions are validated against discrete-event simulations in the Cooja network simulator. The spectral predictor achieves a mean absolute error of 0.8 repetitions/second across all tested layouts and densities. The paper also proposes a greedy edge-addition algorithm, guided by incremental λ₂ updates, that adds the fewest edges to meet the synchronisation target, reducing median added edges by 18% compared with a random addition baseline.

title: Through-thickness residual stress profiles in MIG-welded AA5083 plates measured by X-ray diffraction and hole-drilling
abstract: Residual stresses in 4 mm thick AA5083 plates joined by single-pass MIG welding were characterised using both X-ray diffraction (XRD) and incremental hole-drilling. Specimens with three heat-input levels (80, 120, and 160 J/mm) were prepared under controlled fixturing conditions. XRD measurements were conducted at 11 cross-section positions spanning the weld centreline to 30 mm into the base material, using CrKα radiation with the sin²ψ method. Hole-drilling provided average through-thickness stress profiles at selected locations. Peak tensile longitudinal residual stresses of 85–120 MPa were recorded in the heat-affected zone, while the weld metal showed values near 60 MPa. Transverse stresses remained compressive at the plate edges. Increasing heat input shifted the peak stress location further from the fusion line. A good agreement between the two methods was observed at mid-thickness positions, with discrepancies below 12 MPa. The dataset forms a validation baseline for subsequent finite element modelling.

title: Influence of clamping sequence on angular distortion in MIG-welded aluminium T-joints
abstract: Angular distortion in thin-wall aluminium T-joint fillet welds is strongly affected by the sequence and number of clamps applied during welding. This study investigated six clamping configurations on 3 mm thick AA6061-T6 web and flange plates welded with a single-pass MIG process at 1.2 m/min travel speed. Distortion was quantified with a structured-light 3-D scanner before and after clamp release, capturing out-of-plane deformation maps over a 300 × 150 mm field. Maximum angular rotation ranged from 0.8° for the most constrained configuration to 3.1° for the unclamped reference. Symmetric clamping with four clamps placed 40 mm from the weld toe reduced distortion by 62% relative to the reference. Longitudinal bowing was less sensitive to clamping sequence, varying by less than 0.3 mm across configurations. Results suggest that optimising clamp placement is an effective low-cost distortion mitigation strategy for thin-wall assemblies without the need for post-weld correction.

title: Thermo-mechanical finite element model for residual stress prediction in multi-pass MIG welding of AA6061 extrusions
abstract: A sequentially coupled thermo-mechanical finite element model was developed in Abaqus to predict residual stresses and distortions in two-pass MIG-welded AA6061-T6 extruded profiles with a wall thickness of 2.5 mm. The thermal model used a double-ellipsoid heat source calibrated against 18 thermocouple measurements taken at distances of 5, 10, and 20 mm from the weld centreline. Material properties including temperature-dependent yield strength, thermal conductivity, and specific heat were taken from published data and supplemented by isothermal compression tests at 25, 150, 250, and 350 °C. Predicted peak temperatures matched measurements with a mean absolute error of 14 °C. Longitudinal residual stresses from the simulation agreed with XRD measurements within 18 MPa across 9 measurement points. Distortion predictions reproduced the experimentally observed saddle deformation mode with an error of less than 0.15 mm at mid-span. The model was used to evaluate the effect of interpass cooling time (30 s, 120 s, and 300 s) on stress redistribution.

title: Residual stress relaxation in MIG-welded AA5754 sheets during cyclic loading: an X-ray diffraction study
abstract: Welded aluminium structures in service are subject to cyclic mechanical loads that can redistribute welding residual stresses. This study examined stress relaxation in MIG-welded AA5754-H22 sheets (3 mm thick) under uniaxial fatigue loading at stress amplitudes of 40, 70, and 100 MPa with a load ratio R = 0.1. XRD measurements were performed in the longitudinal and transverse directions at the weld toe, heat-affected zone, and base material after 1, 10², 10³, 10⁴, and 10⁵ cycles. Initial tensile residual stresses at the weld toe of approximately 95 MPa relaxed by 35–55% after 10³ cycles at the highest amplitude. Below the fatigue limit, relaxation was below 10% even after 10⁵ cycles. Compressive residual stresses in the base material showed negligible relaxation in all conditions. The results indicate that as-welded residual stress fields should not be assumed stable in fatigue life assessment when operating stresses exceed 60% of the yield strength.

title: Distortion prediction in aluminium vehicle frame sections using an inherent strain approach
abstract: Full thermo-mechanical finite element simulations of large welded assemblies are computationally prohibitive in industrial practice. This chapter reviews the inherent strain method and its application to aluminium automotive sub-frame sections produced by MIG welding. Inherent strain tensors derived from detailed single-weld simulations of AA6061 and AA6082 joints are mapped onto coarse structural meshes representing a 1.2 m long frame assembly consisting of 14 individual welds. Computed distortions agreed with optical scan measurements on physical prototypes within 0.4 mm for vertical deflection. The chapter discusses calibration procedures, the sensitivity of inherent strain components to heat input variation (±15%), and the boundary conditions required for accurate assembly-level prediction. Limitations related to weld sequence interaction and fixture modelling are identified. The approach reduces computation time by a factor of roughly 40 compared to a full transient simulation while retaining adequate accuracy for early design evaluation.

title: Effect of wire feed rate and shielding gas composition on heat input distribution and residual stress in MIG-welded AA6082 butt joints
abstract: Process parameter selection in MIG welding directly controls heat input and consequently the residual stress state in the completed joint. This study varied wire feed rate (4, 6, and 8 m/min) and shielding gas composition (100% Ar versus Ar–5% He and Ar–30% He) across a factorial experiment on 3 mm thick AA6082-T6 butt joints. Thermal cycles were recorded with 12 embedded thermocouples per specimen. Residual stresses were measured by XRD at 15 positions per specimen. Adding 30% He to the shielding gas increased peak heat-affected zone temperature by approximately 40 °C at equivalent wire feed rate and raised longitudinal residual stress by 15–20 MPa. The 8 m/min wire feed rate combined with Ar–30% He produced the highest peak residual stresses (131 MPa) and also the widest softened HAZ as measured by Vickers microhardness mapping. The combination of 6 m/min with pure Ar offered the best compromise between fusion quality and residual stress level for the geometry tested.

title: Distortion control in MIG-welded aluminium battery enclosure panels through pre-set counter-deformation fixtures
abstract: Thin-wall aluminium enclosures for electric vehicle battery modules are prone to welding distortion that compromises sealing surface flatness. This study investigated pre-set counter-deformation fixturing as a passive distortion control strategy for 2.5 mm AA6061-T6 panels with partial-penetration fillet welds along all four edges. Finite element simulation was first used to predict the free distortion shape; a fixture introducing opposite pre-deformation of 0.6 mm camber was then designed and fabricated. Optical scan measurements on 10 production panels showed that mean post-weld flatness deviation was reduced from 1.8 mm (standard fixture) to 0.4 mm (counter-deformation fixture), with standard deviation dropping from 0.35 mm to 0.09 mm. Residual stresses measured by XRD were not significantly altered by the fixture change. The method was validated on panels welded at two heat input levels. Cost and cycle time implications of the approach are discussed relative to post-weld straightening.

title: Influence of post-weld ageing on residual stress redistribution in MIG-welded AA6061-T6 thin-wall profiles
abstract: Artificial ageing applied after welding is used industrially to restore precipitation-hardened properties in 6xxx aluminium alloys, but its effect on residual stress fields in thin-wall welded profiles has received limited attention. This study subjected MIG-welded AA6061-T6 extruded sections (wall thickness 3 mm) to post-weld artificial ageing at 175 °C for 8 h following standard T6 practice, as well as to a retrogression-and-re-ageing cycle. Residual stresses were measured by XRD before and after each treatment at 12 cross-section positions. Standard artificial ageing reduced peak tensile residual stresses at the weld toe from 108 MPa to 72 MPa on average, attributed to thermally activated creep relaxation at ageing temperature. The retrogression step produced additional relaxation, reaching 55 MPa, without fully eliminating the tensile stress zone. Vickers hardness profiles confirmed partial strength recovery. The findings are relevant for manufacturers using post-weld heat treatment as a combined distortion and stress management step.

title: Comparing the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Student Survey and the Oldenburg Burnout Inventory in a Balkan Sample
abstract: Both the MBI–SS and the OLBI have been applied to student populations with varying cross-cultural success. This study tested the measurement equivalence of adapted Serbian versions with a sample of 541 students across psychology, engineering, and law programmes at the University of Novi Sad. Confirmatory factor analysis was applied to both instruments separately, followed by multigroup tests across faculties. The MBI–SS three-factor model showed adequate fit (CFI = .91, RMSEA = .063) while the OLBI two-factor model fit was weaker (CFI = .87, RMSEA = .071). Partial scalar invariance was established for the MBI–SS across faculty groups, with two intercept non-invariances in the cynicism subscale. Latent mean comparisons indicated that engineering students scored higher on exhaustion than law students (d = 0.34). The paper recommends the MBI–SS with revised cynicism items for continued use in Serbian higher education research, with caution about cross-programme mean comparisons.

title: Self-Regulatory Strategies and Burnout Trajectories Across a Single Academic Semester
abstract: A prospective design tracked 203 first-year psychology students at four measurement points across one semester (weeks 2, 6, 10, and 14). At each wave, participants completed short-form burnout, goal-setting, and self-monitoring measures. Latent growth curve modelling was applied to assess change trajectories in exhaustion and cynicism. Exhaustion showed a significant linear increase across the semester (β = 0.18, p < .001), while cynicism trajectories were more heterogeneous. Latent class growth analysis identified three trajectory classes: stable-low (41%), gradual-increase (38%), and rapid-escalation (21%). Students in the rapid-escalation class reported significantly lower use of strategic planning and self-monitoring in week 2 compared with the stable-low class. The study suggests that early-semester self-regulatory behaviour may serve as a practical screening indicator for burnout risk. Sample attrition across waves (18.2%) is noted as a limitation.

title: Psychometric Properties of a Short-Form Academic Burnout Scale for Repeated-Measures Use
abstract: Frequent administration of full burnout instruments in longitudinal and experience-sampling designs is hampered by response fatigue. This paper developed and validated a nine-item Short Academic Burnout Scale (SABS-9) intended for repeated measurement at intervals of one to two weeks. Item selection drew on item response theory analyses of data from a prior 312-student sample; items with the highest discrimination parameters and lowest floor/ceiling rates were retained, three per dimension. The SABS-9 was then administered at three time points separated by two weeks to a new sample of 167 students. CFA at each wave supported the three-factor structure (CFI ≥ .94). Test–retest ICCs ranged from .68 to .74 across dimensions. Convergent correlations with the full MBI–SS administered at wave 1 ranged from r = .79 to .83. The instrument is released with normative data and scoring syntax as supplementary material.

title: Burnout and Dropout Intention in Engineering Versus Humanities Students: A Two-Wave Comparative Study
abstract: Dropout intention has been linked to burnout in multiple single-faculty studies, but cross-faculty comparisons using equivalent measures are scarce in the regional literature. This study used a two-wave design (four months apart) with 488 students from engineering faculties and 391 from humanities faculties at the University of Novi Sad. The SABS-9 and a four-item dropout intention scale were administered at both waves. Cross-lagged panel modelling showed that wave-1 exhaustion predicted wave-2 dropout intention in both groups (β = .27 engineering; β = .22 humanities), but the reverse path was significant only for humanities students (β = .19, p = .03). Cynicism was a stronger predictor of dropout intention in engineering (β = .31) than in humanities (β = .17). The results suggest that intervention timing and content may need to differ by faculty context. Sample non-equivalence in gender distribution is acknowledged as a limitation.

title: Experience Sampling of Academic Engagement and Disengagement: A Seven-Day Protocol Report
abstract: This methodological paper reports a seven-day experience-sampling study with 94 students at the University of Novi Sad who responded to six daily prompts via a smartphone survey app. Each prompt included three-item bursts assessing momentary engagement, distraction, and subjective task demand. Compliance averaged 74.3% of prompts; multilevel modelling was used to partition within-person and between-person variance. Within-person variability accounted for 58% of total variance in engagement scores, underscoring the limitations of trait-level snapshot measures. Momentary task demand was associated with reduced engagement in the same prompt occasion (b = −0.31, SE = 0.04) and with increased distraction in the following prompt (b = 0.18, SE = 0.05). Students who scored higher on the SABS-9 exhaustion dimension showed a steeper negative slope between demand and engagement. The paper discusses ESM protocol design considerations for future burnout research including prompt frequency, app attrition, and ecological validity.

title: Predicting End-of-Year Academic Outcomes from Mid-Year Burnout Profiles: A Cluster-Analytic Approach
abstract: This paper used person-centred analysis to identify burnout profile types at mid-year and tested whether profile membership predicted academic outcomes at year end. Data came from 601 students across five faculties at the University of Novi Sad who completed the SABS-9 at week 16 of the academic year; GPA, credit completion rate, and dropout status were extracted from the student registry six months later. K-means clustering on the three burnout dimensions at week 16 yielded four profiles: engaged (low on all dimensions, n = 198), overloaded (high exhaustion only, n = 156), disengaged-cynical (high cynicism and low efficacy, n = 142), and fully burnt-out (high on all dimensions, n = 105). ANCOVA controlling for prior GPA showed that the fully burnt-out profile was associated with the lowest credit completion rate (M = 61.3%) and highest dropout rate (14.3%), while the engaged profile showed 88.7% credit completion and 1.5% dropout. Profile membership explained 18% of variance in credit completion above prior GPA alone.

title: Validity of Behavioural Disengagement Indicators Against Self-Report Burnout Measures: A Registered Replication
abstract: A prior unpublished attempt to validate observable disengagement behaviours (assignment submission latency, attendance irregularity, and LMS inactivity) against the SABS-9 produced inconsistent results across two small samples. This registered replication with a pre-specified analysis plan used data from 714 students at two Serbian universities over two semesters. Administrative records provided behavioural data; SABS-9 was administered at mid-semester. Submission latency (days after deadline) correlated with exhaustion (r = .29) and cynicism (r = .33) but not with efficacy. Attendance irregularity showed the strongest association with cynicism (r = .38). LMS inactivity replicated earlier findings (r = .27 with exhaustion). Incremental validity of the combined behavioural composite over SABS-9 total score in predicting credit completion was small but significant (ΔR² = .04). The paper notes that behavioural indicators are observable without student cooperation and may therefore be useful in contexts where survey completion is low.

title: Automated Classification of Student Disengagement Risk Using Administrative and Behavioural Data: Psychologist Considerations for Model Deployment
abstract: Machine learning models for early identification of at-risk students are increasingly discussed in educational analytics, yet psychologists are rarely involved in their design or evaluation. This paper reports a collaboration between the first author and a software team at a Serbian higher education institution in which a logistic regression and a gradient boosting classifier were trained on administrative records (prior GPA, first-year credit completion, attendance, LMS activity) from 2,310 historical student records to predict burnout-risk status operationalised via SABS-9 tertile scores in a concurrent validation sample of 389 students. The gradient boosting model achieved AUC = .71 on the holdout set; recall for the high-risk class was 0.63 at a 0.40 probability threshold. The paper focuses primarily on measurement and conceptual issues: how the criterion variable was defined, thresholding implications for false positive rates, and the psychologist's role in interpreting and contextualising algorithmic outputs for institutional users. Ethical and data governance considerations are discussed at length.

title: Ink Penetration Depth and Its Effect on Edge Acuity of Flexographically Printed DataMatrix Symbols on Corrugated Liner Substrates
abstract: Ink penetration into porous corrugated liner substrates degrades the edge sharpness of printed DataMatrix cell boundaries, directly reducing the modulation transfer function available to industrial scanners. This study quantified ink penetration depth using cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy and correlated those measurements with edge-spread function profiles obtained from high-resolution flatbed scans at 1200 dpi. Twelve commercially produced liner grades with grammages from 90 to 175 g/m² were printed on a pilot flexographic press using two UV-curable ink formulations. Edge acuity was parameterised as the 10–90 % rise distance across cell boundaries. Results showed that penetration depth explained 71 % of the variance in rise distance (R² = 0.71, n = 144 symbol replicates). Symbols on substrates with penetration depths exceeding 28 µm consistently failed ISO/IEC 15415 grade thresholds at print contrast below 0.62. The findings provide quantitative substrate selection criteria for packaging lines where inline DataMatrix verification is mandatory.

title: Spectral Reflectance Matching of White Substrates for Predictable Print Contrast in Flexographic Label Production
abstract: Reliable machine-vision reading of printed codes on self-adhesive labels depends on the spectral relationship between substrate fluorescence and ink absorption in the near-infrared (NIR) range used by many industrial scanners. This paper reports measurements of diffuse spectral reflectance between 380 and 1000 nm for 34 self-adhesive facestock materials, including calendered papers, cast-coated papers, and white polypropylene films. Measurements were made with a double-beam spectrophotometer under D65/10° geometry. Fluorescence contributions were separated using a dual-monochromator method. Results showed that optical brightening agent (OBA) fluorescence elevated the 400–440 nm reflectance by up to 19 percentage points relative to non-OBA stocks. When black UV flexographic ink was overprinted, print contrast measured at 900 nm ranged from 0.58 to 0.89, with polypropylene films yielding the highest contrast. A simple reflectance-matching index is proposed to rank substrates before press trials, reducing failed verification runs.

title: Thermal Aging of UV-Flexographic Inks and Its Consequences for Machine-Readable Code Quality on Polyethylene Packaging
abstract: Polyethylene packaging for food products is routinely stored at elevated temperatures during transport, causing UV-cured flexographic inks to undergo post-crosslinking and yellowing that alter reflectance characteristics relevant to code verification. This study subjected 2D DataMatrix symbols printed with two commercial UV flexographic black inks to accelerated aging (70 °C, 40 % relative humidity, 0–28 days) and tracked changes in optical density, contrast ratio, and ISO/IEC 15415 decode grade at seven-day intervals. Optical density of the black modules decreased by 0.09–0.15 units over 28 days for one ink formulation, while remaining stable for the other. Decode grade degraded from B to C in 35 % of symbols for the unstable ink. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) spectra indicated continued photoinitiator fragment migration as the dominant mechanism. Results indicate that ink selection for high-temperature supply chains should include accelerated aging as part of the qualification protocol.

title: Resolution Requirements for Reliable Flexographic Printing of GS1 DataMatrix at 10 × 10 and 14 × 14 Module Configurations
abstract: Minimum module size for GS1 DataMatrix symbols used in pharmaceutical unit-dose labelling is constrained simultaneously by press resolution limits and by scanner optical resolution. This paper derives a resolution budget model that combines the press modulation transfer function (MTF), substrate roughness-induced dot gain, and the scanner pixel-to-module ratio. Experimental validation used a narrow-web UV flexographic press printing 10 × 10 and 14 × 14 DataMatrix configurations at X-dimensions of 0.25, 0.30, and 0.38 mm on three pharmaceutical label stocks. MTF was measured using a sinusoidal test target at spatial frequencies from 1 to 8 cycles/mm. First-read-rate was tested on five GS1-compliant imager models. At X = 0.25 mm, reliable decoding (first-read-rate ≥ 99 %) required an in-press MTF above 0.35 at 4 cycles/mm. The model predicts acceptable combinations and is presented as a practical lookup chart for prepress engineers.
