title: Comparison of Flatbed Scanner and Dedicated Verifier Outputs for ISO/IEC 15415 Grading of Flexographically Printed DataMatrix Symbols
abstract: Small and medium-sized label converters frequently use flatbed document scanners as a cost-saving substitute for dedicated ISO-compliant code verifiers. This study examined whether flatbed scanners calibrated to a reflectance standard could produce ISO/IEC 15415 grade assessments consistent with a dedicated verifier across a wide range of symbol qualities. Sixty DataMatrix symbols printed flexographically on five substrate types were graded independently using a Vericode M400 dedicated verifier and three flatbed scanners operating at 600, 1200, and 2400 dpi, all calibrated with an IT8.7/2 target. Agreement between the verifier and the 2400 dpi scanner was 80 % at the pass/fail boundary (grade C threshold), rising to 91 % when symbols grading A or F were excluded. Systematic underestimation of axial non-uniformity by flatbed scanners was identified as the main discrepancy source. Guidelines are given for when flatbed substitution is acceptable and when it is not.

title: Substrate Surface Texture Metrics as Predictors of DataMatrix Decode Failure Rate in High-Speed Inline Scanning
abstract: Surface texture of paper-based packaging substrates introduces local reflectance variation that can corrupt individual DataMatrix cell values when scanned at belt speeds above 1 m/s. This paper investigates which surface texture parameters measured by profilometry (Ra, Rz, Rsk, Rpk) best predict per-symbol decode failure rate in a simulated inline environment. A conveyor test rig with a fixed-mount area-scan camera and programmable belt speed was constructed and used to scan 480 DataMatrix symbols printed on eight paper substrates at belt speeds of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 m/s under three LED illumination intensities. Logistic regression identified Rz (ten-point mean roughness) and Rpk (reduced peak height) as the strongest predictors of failure (AUC = 0.84). Substrates with Rz > 9.4 µm showed failure rates above 3 % at 2 m/s regardless of illumination intensity. Threshold values for substrate qualification in high-speed lines are proposed.

title: Field Measurement of Ambient Illumination Variability in Serbian Food-Processing Facilities and Its Impact on Handheld DataMatrix Scanner Performance
abstract: Industrial handheld scanners for DataMatrix verification are often qualified under laboratory conditions that do not represent the ambient illumination encountered in production facilities. This paper reports illuminance and spectral irradiance measurements made at 18 workstations across five food-processing plants in Vojvodina using a calibrated spectroradiometer. Illuminance ranged from 180 to 2400 lux; colour temperature varied from 2850 K (incandescent retrofit zones) to 6500 K (LED daylight luminaires). At each workstation, first-read-rate was recorded for 100 GS1 DataMatrix symbols on PET and paper substrates using three commercial handheld scanners. First-read-rate dropped below 95 % at workstations with illuminances above 1800 lux combined with colour temperatures below 3200 K, a condition attributable to near-IR interference from halogen-replacement lamps. Scanner models differed in ambient-light rejection capability by up to 22 percentage points under the most adverse conditions. Workstation illumination specifications for reliable handheld scanning are derived.

title: Characterisation of Dot Gain Temporal Drift on Flexographic Printing Presses Over Multi-Hour Production Runs
abstract: Dot gain in flexographic printing is known to vary as press components reach thermal equilibrium, yet most quality control sampling happens after the press reaches steady state. This study tracked dot gain continuously over 5-hour production runs on two wide-web CI flexographic presses printing LDPE film with water-based inks. DataMatrix symbols and 50 % tone patches were printed at 10-minute intervals; dot gain and ISO/IEC 15415 symbol grades were measured for each interval. Mean dot gain increased by 4.1–6.8 percentage points during the first 40–60 minutes before stabilising. Over this warm-up period, the proportion of DataMatrix symbols achieving ISO grade B or better fell from 88 % to 67 % before recovering to 81 %. Temperature of the ink train correlated with dot gain (Pearson r = 0.82). A simple compensation strategy based on anilox volume adjustment during warm-up is evaluated and found to reduce grade-B failure incidence by 14 percentage points.

title: Minimum Illumination Threshold Maps for Camera-Based Inline DataMatrix Decoding: A Photometric Modelling Approach Validated on a Pilot Press
abstract: Camera-based inline code verification systems must be designed with illumination levels that guarantee sufficient signal-to-noise ratio across the full web width. This paper presents a photometric model that predicts the minimum illumination threshold at the camera sensor for reliable DataMatrix decoding as a function of web speed, substrate reflectance, camera pixel size, and lens aperture. The model was parameterised using bench-top measurements and validated on a pilot narrow-web flexographic press equipped with a custom LED bar illuminator and a GigE area-scan camera. Web widths of 200, 330, and 520 mm were tested at speeds of 50, 100, and 150 m/min. The model predicted required illuminance to within 12 % of measured values in 84 % of test configurations. Lookup tables derived from the model allow press engineers to specify LED power and lens f-number combinations for new installations without empirical trials, reducing commissioning time.

title: Benchmark of Open-Source and Commercial DataMatrix Decoding Libraries Under Degraded Print Conditions Typical of Flexographic Production
abstract: A range of open-source and proprietary software libraries are used by researchers and SME manufacturers to decode DataMatrix symbols, yet their comparative robustness under print degradation conditions typical of flexographic production is not systematically documented. This study compiled a test set of 840 DataMatrix symbol images sampled from flexographic press production across six substrate types, representing five ISO 15415 grade categories from A to F. Each image was passed through four open-source libraries (ZXing-C++, libdmtx, ZBar, and OpenMV) and two commercial SDKs (names anonymised as SDK-A and SDK-B). Decode success rates were recorded along with processing time per symbol. Commercial SDK-A achieved 91.4 % success on grade-C symbols versus 63.2 % for the best open-source library. All libraries failed below 20 % on grade-F symbols. Processing time ranged from 1.2 ms (ZXing-C++) to 48 ms (SDK-B) per symbol. Results inform library selection for embedded verification applications in resource-constrained industrial environments.

title: Hydrogen sulphide accumulation in sulphonate-type cation exchange beds during extended stagnation periods
abstract: Ion exchange resins used in municipal water softening occasionally produce hydrogen sulphide-tainted water after periods of low or zero service flow. This study quantified dissolved H2S concentrations in effluent from pilot-scale strong-acid cation resin columns after stagnation intervals of 12, 24, 48 and 96 hours at 15 °C. Dissolved H2S rose from below detection (< 0.005 mg L⁻¹) to 0.34 mg L⁻¹ after 96 hours in columns previously operated without biocidal treatment. MPN counts of sulphate-reducing bacteria (SRB) in resin bed samples reached 1.2 × 10⁴ cells g⁻¹ dry resin. Resin that had been chlorinated weekly showed no detectable SRB and produced no measurable H2S. The results establish a clear correlation between SRB colonisation density and odour-threshold H2S exceedance under realistic stagnation scenarios, providing a quantitative basis for recommending chlorination frequency in drinking-water softening installations.

title: Identification of dominant sulphur-cycling bacteria on spent strong-acid cation resins from a district heating circuit
abstract: Sulphonate-type cation exchange resins recovered from a district heating make-up water unit in Novi Sad were analysed by culture-based methods and 16S rRNA gene clone library sequencing. The resin had been in service for 14 months without biocidal regeneration. Dominant isolates belonged to Desulfovibrio and Desulfomicrobium genera, together accounting for 68% of clones. A secondary population of thiosulphate-oxidising Halothiobacillus-related sequences was also identified, suggesting a coupled sulphur cycle within the resin bed. Total organic carbon adsorbed to the resin surface was 11.4 mg C g⁻¹, indicating significant accumulation of organic electron donors. Fluorescence in situ hybridisation confirmed spatially structured biofilm layers up to 35 µm thick on resin bead surfaces. The study provides the first culture-independent community profile for an industrially operated cation exchange resin in a heating-circuit context in this region.

title: Effect of resin bead crosslink density on the rate of anaerobic microbial colonisation under batch conditions
abstract: Three commercially equivalent divinylbenzene-crosslinked sulphonate cation resins differing in nominal crosslinking (6%, 8% and 10% DVB) were inoculated with a mixed SRB consortium derived from a conditioned water-treatment unit. Colonisation kinetics were followed by ATP bioluminescence and plate counts over 30 days under strictly anaerobic batch conditions at 20 °C. Resins with 6% DVB crosslinking showed the highest colonised surface area after 30 days (estimated 2.1 × 10⁶ cells cm⁻²), compared with 1.4 × 10⁶ and 0.9 × 10⁶ cells cm⁻² for 8% and 10% DVB resins respectively. Mercury intrusion porosimetry confirmed that lower crosslinking correlated with higher macropore volume accessible to cells. H2S generation rates per gram of resin followed the same rank order. The findings suggest that resin microstructure is a significant, though often overlooked, determinant of biological fouling risk.

title: Sulphide generation in intermittently operated water softeners: a field survey of twenty installations in Vojvodina
abstract: Twenty domestic and small-commercial water softeners using sulphonate cation exchange resins were sampled across Vojvodina over one winter season. First-flush water samples were collected after overnight stagnation and analysed for H2S, total dissolved sulphide, sulphate, and heterotrophic plate counts. H2S exceeded the 0.05 mg L⁻¹ odour threshold in nine of the twenty units, all of which had not been sanitised in the preceding six months. Sulphate concentrations in source water above 120 mg L⁻¹ correlated with higher sulphide in effluent (Spearman ρ = 0.74, p < 0.01). Resin samples from four selected units were cultured and confirmed SRB presence at between 10² and 10⁵ MPN g⁻¹. Seasonal temperature had no statistically significant effect at the scale of this survey. The data support targeted sanitisation protocols for high-sulphate source water areas.

title: Carbon source availability as a controlling factor for SRB activity within exhausted sulphonate resin beds
abstract: Exhausted cation exchange resins accumulate organic matter during service, providing electron donors for sulphate-reducing bacteria. This laboratory study systematically varied acetate, lactate and formate concentrations in synthetic feed water at levels representative of treated surface water (0.1–5 mg C L⁻¹) and monitored H2S production rates in mini-column reactors over 21-day anaerobic incubation periods. Lactate at 2 mg C L⁻¹ produced the highest cumulative H2S (18.4 µmol g⁻¹ resin), followed by acetate (12.1 µmol g⁻¹) and formate (4.8 µmol g⁻¹). Elimination of all added carbon reduced but did not abolish H2S production (2.3 µmol g⁻¹), attributed to hydrolysis of adsorbed humic fractions. The results indicate that organic carbon control at the inlet of exchange units could reduce biogenic H2S by up to 75% without biocidal intervention, offering a practical management option for installations where chlorination is undesirable.
venue: Biofouling and Corrosion International

title: Scanning electron microscopy and EDS characterisation of biofilm architecture on sulphonate resin beads at different stages of fouling
abstract: Resin bead samples were collected from pilot columns at early (day 7), intermediate (day 30) and advanced (day 90) fouling stages under controlled anaerobic conditions. SEM imaging revealed a progression from sparse cell attachment with minimal extracellular matrix at day 7 to dense, multi-layered biofilm embedding cells in a fibrous EPS network by day 90. EDS mapping detected sulphur enrichment in the EPS layer at day 90 (mean atomic % S of 4.1 vs. 0.3 in fresh resin controls), consistent with elemental sulphur precipitation. Mean biofilm thickness estimated from cross-sectioned embedded beads was 8 µm at day 7, 29 µm at day 30, and 54 µm at day 90. Porosity measurements by nitrogen adsorption showed a 31% reduction in accessible pore volume between day 0 and day 90. The morphological dataset is freely available as a supplementary image library.

title: Comparison of sodium hypochlorite and peracetic acid regeneration protocols for suppressing SRB in water-softening resins
abstract: Two biocidal regeneration agents were evaluated in a controlled pilot study: sodium hypochlorite (10 mg L⁻¹ free Cl₂, 30 min contact) and peracetic acid (PAA, 80 mg L⁻¹, 30 min contact), each applied after established SRB biofilms had formed over 45 days. H2S generation was monitored for 14 days post-treatment. Hypochlorite reduced H2S production by 94% on day 1 post-treatment but showed rebound to 40% of pre-treatment levels by day 10. PAA reduced H2S by 89% on day 1 with a slower rebound, reaching only 22% of pre-treatment levels by day 14. Ion exchange capacity measurements showed a statistically significant loss of 3.1% capacity in hypochlorite-treated resins but no significant loss with PAA. The results support PAA as the preferred biocidal agent for installations where resin longevity is a primary concern, with the caveat that downstream PAA residuals require monitoring.

title: Metagenomic profiling of microbial communities in industrial demineralisation units: comparing anion and cation exchange stages
abstract: Shotgun metagenomics was applied to biofilm samples from both the cation exchange (sulphonate-type) and anion exchange (quaternary ammonium-type) stages of a three-bed demineralisation train serving a pharmaceutical water system in Serbia. Total DNA was extracted from 1 g resin aliquots and sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq platform, yielding 12–18 million paired-end reads per sample. Taxonomic binning revealed that the cation stage was dominated by Deltaproteobacteria (38%), with high relative abundance of Desulfovibrio vulgaris-related reads, while the anion stage harboured a more diverse community lacking classical SRB but enriched in Bacteroidetes (29%). Functional annotation of sulphur metabolism genes (dsrA, dsrB, aprA) was restricted almost entirely to cation stage metagenomes. The anion stage showed enrichment of genes for denitrification. Results confirm the cation exchange stage as the primary site of biogenic H2S risk in demineralisation trains.

title: Flow interruption frequency and its effect on sulphide accumulation in household water softener columns: a controlled mesocosm study
abstract: The relationship between service-flow interruption frequency and H2S accumulation was investigated using twelve mesocosm-scale softener columns operated in parallel over eight weeks. Four interruption regimes were applied: continuous flow, one interruption per day (8 h stagnation), two interruptions per day (2 × 4 h), and weekend-only operation (60 h stagnation). H2S in first-flush effluent was highest in weekend-only units (mean 0.41 mg L⁻¹) and lowest in continuously operated units (< 0.01 mg L⁻¹). Units with two short daily interruptions produced less H2S than units with a single longer interruption of equivalent total stagnation time, suggesting that partial oxygen ingress during brief interruptions partially suppresses SRB. SRB viable counts in resin samples correlated with accumulated stagnation time (r = 0.88). The study provides quantitative evidence that use-pattern data can improve risk stratification for household softener installations.

title: Stable isotope tracing (³⁵S) of sulphonate group degradation by SRB in cation exchange resin biofilms
abstract: A key unresolved question in resin biofouling is whether SRB directly utilise sulphonate groups as a sulphur source or rely entirely on dissolved sulphate. ³⁵S-labelled sulphonate resin was synthesised by sulphonation of divinylbenzene-styrene copolymer beads using ³⁵S-labelled chlorosulphonic acid. Labelled resins were inoculated with Desulfovibrio-dominated consortia and incubated under strictly anaerobic conditions for 28 days. Scintillation counting of gas-phase H₂³⁵S confirmed isotope incorporation from resin sulphonate groups, contributing 14 ± 3% of total H2S produced when dissolved sulphate was present at 50 mg L⁻¹. When dissolved sulphate was omitted, resin sulphonate became the dominant S source (73 ± 9% of H2S). The findings confirm that direct enzymatic desulphonation by SRB occurs within resin biofilms, with implications for understanding H2S generation in low-sulphate source waters.

title: Pilot-scale evaluation of UV disinfection as a preventive measure against SRB colonisation of water-softening resins
abstract: Ultraviolet disinfection was tested as a non-chemical pretreatment to reduce SRB inoculum entering cation exchange softener columns. A 254 nm medium-pressure UV unit was installed upstream of three pilot columns; three parallel columns received untreated feed. Influent SRB counts were reduced from 180–320 MPN 100 mL⁻¹ to below 5 MPN 100 mL⁻¹ by UV at a dose of 40 mJ cm⁻². Over 90 days of operation, UV-pretreated columns showed 82% lower resin-associated SRB counts and 76% lower cumulative H2S output in stagnation tests compared with untreated controls. However, SRB were never entirely absent from UV-pretreated columns, indicating that a small proportion of cells survived and established viable populations over time. The study concludes that UV is a useful supplementary measure but should not replace periodic sanitisation of the resin itself for installations with a documented sulphide problem.

title: Spatial heterogeneity of hydrogen sulphide gradients within large-diameter exchange resin columns: measurements and a one-dimensional diffusion-reaction model
abstract: Full-scale cation exchange columns (diameter 0.8 m, bed depth 2.1 m) at a municipal water utility were instrumented with twelve dissolved sulphide microsensors at three depths and four radial positions to capture spatial H2S distribution during 24 h stagnation events. Sulphide accumulated preferentially in the lower third of the bed, reaching 0.52 mg L⁻¹ at the base, compared with 0.07 mg L⁻¹ at the top. A one-dimensional diffusion-reaction model incorporating measured SRB activity distributions reproduced the observed gradients with a root mean square error of 0.04 mg L⁻¹. Sensitivity analysis identified local SRB density as the dominant controlling parameter, with dissolved sulphate concentration and temperature as secondary variables. The model is intended as a planning tool for utilities considering partial-bed replacement strategies and is provided as a freely downloadable spreadsheet.

title: Characterisation of carbonate-bearing industrial wastes from a cement plant: thermal behaviour and mineral content
abstract: Raw meal bypass dust and kiln dust collected at three sampling points along the rotary kiln of a cement plant were characterised by XRF, XRD, simultaneous TG-DSC-FTIR, and SEM-EDS. Total inorganic carbon ranged from 6.2 to 28.4 wt%, with calcite, dolomite, and traces of siderite identified by XRD. TG curves in nitrogen showed up to four partially overlapping decomposition events; Gaussian deconvolution of the DTG signal resolved contributions assignable to siderite (430–500 °C), dolomite stage 1 (660–720 °C), partial-pressure-stabilised dolomite (750–800 °C), and calcite (820–880 °C). Alkali chloride sublimation signals were detected by FTIR between 680 and 780 °C in the most alkali-rich sample. Total mass loss to 1000 °C ranged from 14.1 to 31.7 wt%. The study provides a thermal fingerprinting approach for rapid characterisation of cement kiln dust quality prior to recycling or disposal decisions.

title: Empirical Path-Loss Measurements at 868 MHz in a Multi-Floor Office Building
abstract: This paper presents a path-loss measurement campaign conducted across six floors of a reinforced-concrete office building in Novi Sad. A continuous-wave transmitter operating at 868 MHz was placed at three fixed positions on the ground floor, and received power was logged at 214 measurement points using a calibrated spectrum analyser mounted on a wheeled trolley. The collected data were compared against the ITU-R P.1238 indoor model and a dual-slope log-distance fit. The dual-slope model with breakpoint at 15 m showed a root-mean-square error of 4.1 dB, outperforming the ITU-R model by 2.3 dB on upper floors where inter-floor attenuation dominates. Floor attenuation factors extracted from the data ranged from 11 dB to 17 dB depending on floor construction type. The dataset and derived model coefficients are provided for direct use in LoRaWAN network planning tools.

title: Delay Spread Statistics in Warehouse Environments at 433 MHz and 868 MHz
abstract: Wideband channel impulse responses were measured in two logistics warehouses with steel shelving, concrete floors, and metallic roofing, using a vector network analyser with 801 frequency points spanning a 200 MHz band centred on each carrier frequency. Measurements were taken along 18 linear tracks of 20 m each under loaded and unloaded shelf conditions. RMS delay spread at 433 MHz ranged from 38 ns to 124 ns, while at 868 MHz values were 29 ns to 98 ns. Loaded shelves consistently reduced delay spread by 10–25 % compared to empty conditions, attributed to increased absorption. A lognormal fit adequately described the delay spread distribution at both frequencies with similar shape parameters. The results indicate that standard LoRa spreading factors provide sufficient guard intervals for these environments without additional equalisation, but gateway placement relative to shelf aisles significantly affects coverage uniformity.

title: Small Planar Inverted-F Antenna for 868 MHz LoRa End-Node Integration
abstract: A compact planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) was designed and fabricated for integration onto a 50 mm × 30 mm PCB intended for battery-powered LoRa sensor nodes. The antenna occupies a 25 mm × 8 mm footprint on an FR-4 substrate with 1.6 mm thickness. Matching was achieved through a shorting strip and a tuning slot, yielding a measured −10 dB bandwidth of 28 MHz centred at 868 MHz, covering the full European LoRa band. Measured gain was −0.8 dBi in free space and dropped by 1.4 dB when the PCB was placed inside an ABS plastic enclosure of 2 mm wall thickness. Radiation efficiency was 61 %. The sensitivity of the resonant frequency to hand proximity was characterised using a phantom limb fixture; detuning of up to 14 MHz was observed, which remains within the matched bandwidth. The design is compared against a monopole reference and a commercially available chip antenna.

title: Link Budget Tool for LoRaWAN Deployments in Mixed Indoor–Outdoor Industrial Sites
abstract: A deterministic link-budget calculation tool was developed to assist network planners in estimating coverage for LoRaWAN deployments that span both indoor factory halls and adjacent outdoor yard areas. The tool combines empirical path-loss exponents derived from dedicated measurement campaigns at three industrial sites in the Vojvodina region with a material-dependent wall-transmission loss database compiled from waveguide measurement data. Users specify building geometry, gateway positions, and target reliability thresholds; the tool outputs a coverage probability map and recommends spreading-factor assignments per zone. Validation was performed by comparing predicted received-signal strength indicator (RSSI) values with drive-test data from a 23-gateway pilot deployment; median prediction error was 3.8 dB with a standard deviation of 6.2 dB across 1 840 logged packets. The tool is implemented in Python and the source code is publicly available under a BSD licence.

title: Spatial Correlation of Received Signal Strength in LoRa Networks Inside Hospital Buildings
abstract: Hospital buildings present specific propagation challenges owing to a heterogeneous mix of construction materials, frequent metallic obstacles, and strict electromagnetic compatibility requirements. This paper analyses the spatial correlation structure of RSSI measurements from a static LoRaWAN testbed installed in a four-wing hospital building in Novi Sad, comprising three gateways and 47 fixed end-nodes over a monitoring period of four weeks. Semivariogram analysis was used to quantify spatial correlation lengths, which ranged from 6 m in densely furnished patient wards to 22 m in long straight corridors. Temporal variation of RSSI at fixed nodes showed a diurnal pattern with peak-to-peak variation of up to 4 dB, correlating with occupancy levels. The findings suggest that gateway placement optimisation based on static measurements may overestimate coverage reliability during peak occupancy, and a safety margin of at least 5 dB is recommended for healthcare IoT system planning.

title: Angle-of-Arrival Estimation Accuracy for Indoor Localisation at 868 MHz Using a Four-Element Switched Beam Array
abstract: A switched-beam array consisting of four printed Yagi elements arranged in a cross configuration was constructed and evaluated for angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation in indoor environments. The array aperture was 220 mm and operated at 868 MHz with a measured half-power beamwidth of 72° per sector. AoA estimation was performed using a maximum-likelihood algorithm applied to received signal strength differences between sectors. Laboratory tests in an anechoic enclosure yielded a mean absolute angular error of 4.2°. In a furnished office environment with rich multipath, the error increased to 11.7° for line-of-sight paths and 19.4° for non-line-of-sight paths at distances between 5 m and 30 m. The effect of antenna placement height (1 m vs. 2.5 m) on estimation accuracy was also evaluated; the higher placement reduced non-line-of-sight error by approximately 3°. Results are discussed in the context of asset-tracking accuracy requirements.

title: Scoring micro-enterprises with little credit history
abstract: Micro-enterprises represent a disproportionately large share of employment in transition economies yet remain systematically underserved by formal credit markets, largely because conventional scoring models require longitudinal repayment histories that these firms cannot provide. This paper proposes a scoring framework tailored to micro-enterprises with fewer than three years of banking relationship data, drawing on a dataset of 4,800 loan applications collected from three Serbian commercial banks between 2018 and 2022. The framework combines sparse financial statement ratios with owner-level psychometric indicators and payment behaviour data from non-bank sources such as utility and telecom providers. Gradient-boosted trees are benchmarked against logistic regression and a naïve Bayes baseline. Results show that the enriched feature set reduces the Gini coefficient gap between thin-file and thick-file applicants by 14 percentage points, while maintaining discriminatory power above 0.70 AUC across all tested segments. A post-hoc SHAP analysis confirms that telecom payment regularity and owner age are the two most influential non-traditional predictors. The paper concludes with policy recommendations for supervisors considering the adoption of alternative data in standardised internal ratings-based approaches under the revised Capital Requirements Regulation.

title: Explaining credit decisions to supervisors: a case study
abstract: Regulatory frameworks across the European Union increasingly require financial institutions to provide meaningful explanations of automated credit decisions, yet operationalising this requirement for complex statistical models remains an open challenge for both banks and their supervisors. This paper presents a case study conducted with a mid-sized bank operating in the Western Balkans, examining how SHAP-based and LIME-based explanation methods can be adapted to produce supervisor-readable model documentation. Through structured interviews with six risk officers and two national regulatory examiners, we identify a systematic gap between the granularity of machine-generated explanations and the narrative format expected by supervisory review teams. We propose a three-layer explanation architecture that separates model-level, portfolio-level, and individual-decision-level outputs, mapping each layer to a specific supervisory use case. A prototype implementation demonstrated that the middle portfolio layer, summarising feature contribution distributions across loan cohorts, received the highest usability ratings from regulatory staff. The findings have direct implications for banks seeking validation of internal models under the European Banking Authority's upcoming guidelines on model risk management and for vendors developing regulatory technology solutions in credit risk.

title: Alternative data in consumer credit scoring: evidence from a Serbian fintech lender
abstract: The proliferation of digital footprints has opened new possibilities for consumer credit assessment, particularly for individuals excluded from the traditional banking system. This study analyses a proprietary dataset of 12,400 loan applications processed by a Serbian fintech lender between 2019 and 2021, of which approximately 38 percent belong to borrowers with no prior bank credit record. We evaluate the incremental predictive lift obtained by appending seven categories of alternative data—including e-commerce transaction patterns, mobile recharge frequency, social network activity proxies, and geolocation stability—to a baseline logistic regression model trained solely on bureau data. Incremental AUC improvements range from 3.2 to 8.7 percentage points depending on the borrower segment, with the largest gains concentrated among self-employed individuals aged 25 to 40. Random forest and XGBoost models are also evaluated; XGBoost achieves the highest overall AUC of 0.81 on the holdout set. We further examine fairness metrics across gender and regional subgroups, finding no statistically significant disparate impact when SHAP-constrained feature selection is applied. Regulatory implications under the General Data Protection Regulation and the forthcoming EU Artificial Intelligence Act are discussed, with emphasis on consent management and the right to explanation.

title: Regulatory capital implications of machine learning credit models: a stress-testing perspective
abstract: Machine learning models now underpin a growing share of internal ratings-based credit risk systems at European banks, yet their behaviour under macroeconomic stress remains poorly understood. This paper examines how gradient-boosted and neural-network-based probability-of-default models respond to simulated recessionary shocks compared with traditional logistic regression scorecards, using a panel of SME loan portfolios from five Western Balkan banks spanning 2010 to 2022. We construct three stress scenarios calibrated to the 2008–2009 financial crisis, the 2020 pandemic shock, and a hypothetical sovereign debt episode, and we measure through-the-cycle versus point-in-time PD migration for each model class. Results indicate that complex models exhibit higher rank-order stability but produce more severe PD spikes under tail scenarios, potentially amplifying procyclicality in Pillar 1 capital requirements. We propose a model blending strategy that preserves discriminatory power in normal conditions while dampening stress-period volatility. The paper also evaluates how supervisory overlays recommended by the European Banking Authority interact with machine learning outputs, offering guidance for banks preparing internal model validation documentation.

title: Credit access barriers for women-owned SMEs in the Western Balkans
abstract: Gender disparities in small business credit access have been documented in developed economies, but evidence from transition markets in the Western Balkans remains scarce. This paper draws on a survey of 870 SME owners across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, combined with administrative loan outcome data obtained from three partner banks, to quantify the magnitude of gender-based credit gaps and identify their structural drivers. Decomposition analysis following the Blinder–Oaxaca method reveals that roughly 60 percent of the observed approval rate gap between male-owned and female-owned firms is attributable to differences in collateral endowments rather than business performance metrics, suggesting that collateral requirements serve as a structural barrier rather than a neutral risk-management instrument. We find that firms scoring above the median on a cash-flow-based alternative scorecard have near-identical default rates regardless of owner gender, supporting the case for collateral-light lending products targeted at women entrepreneurs. Policy recommendations address both regulatory incentives for banks and technical assistance programmes funded through EU pre-accession instruments. The paper contributes to the growing literature on inclusive finance and SME credit rationing.

title: Explainability requirements under the EU AI Act: implications for credit scoring vendors
abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act classifies credit scoring systems as high-risk AI applications, imposing stringent transparency and human oversight obligations on both developers and deployers. This paper systematically maps those obligations onto the technical architecture of contemporary scoring platforms, focusing on three widely adopted model families: gradient-boosted trees, neural networks, and scorecard ensembles. We identify eight distinct explainability requirements arising from the Act's Articles 13 and 14 and evaluate the degree to which current post-hoc explanation libraries—SHAP, LIME, DiCE, and Anchors—satisfy each requirement as interpreted by draft guidance from the European AI Office. Our analysis finds that no single library fully addresses all eight requirements and that the most underserved dimension is contrastive explanation for portfolio-level supervisory reporting. We propose a modular explanation stack architecture for credit vendors that combines global surrogate models, individual SHAP waterfalls, and counterfactual generators within a unified audit trail. Case studies drawn from two anonymised Serbian fintech deployments illustrate the practical implementation challenges. The paper has implications for regulatory technology firms developing compliance tooling and for banks seeking to achieve AI Act conformity assessments before the 2026 deadline.

title: Incorporating cash-flow volatility into SME credit scoring: a machine learning approach
abstract: Traditional SME credit scoring models rely heavily on balance-sheet snapshots that fail to capture the temporal dynamics of business cash flows. This paper proposes a scoring methodology that extracts volatility and trend features from monthly bank transaction records spanning at least twelve months, feeding these time-series features into a stacked ensemble model alongside conventional financial ratios and owner characteristics. The dataset comprises transaction histories and twelve-month loan outcomes for 6,200 Serbian SMEs obtained from a commercial bank under a data-sharing agreement. Feature engineering steps include rolling standard deviation of net cash flow, seasonal decomposition residuals, and autocorrelation-based regularity scores. The stacked ensemble combines a long short-term memory network for sequence features with gradient-boosted trees for tabular features, achieving an AUC of 0.83 on the holdout set compared with 0.74 for a bureau-only logistic regression baseline. SHAP values confirm that cash-flow regularity score and the ratio of peak-to-trough monthly receipts are among the top five predictors. The paper also discusses data governance considerations, including minimum transaction history requirements and the treatment of COVID-19 payment moratoria as structural breaks in the time series.

title: Open banking data for thin-file borrower assessment: opportunities and regulatory constraints
abstract: Open banking frameworks established under the revised Payment Services Directive have created legal pathways for lenders to access enriched transaction data with borrower consent, offering a potential solution to the thin-file problem that affects an estimated 30 percent of adult borrowers in Serbia and neighbouring markets. This book chapter reviews the current state of open banking adoption in the Western Balkans, evaluates the credit information value of Payment Initiation Service Provider and Account Information Service Provider data streams, and discusses the regulatory constraints that limit their use in automated scoring. Drawing on pilot studies conducted with two regional banks and one licensed fintech lender, we present empirical evidence that open banking features improve AUC by 6 to 11 percentage points for borrowers with fewer than two years of credit bureau history. The chapter also examines tensions between the General Data Protection Regulation's data minimisation principle and the feature richness required for accurate thin-file scoring, proposing a privacy-preserving feature aggregation protocol as a practical reconciliation. The chapter concludes with a framework for national regulators considering mandatory open banking data standards as a tool for financial inclusion.

title: Benchmarking scorecard interpretability metrics in credit risk practice
abstract: The credit risk literature has converged on SHAP values as the dominant post-hoc explanation tool, yet practitioners frequently report difficulty translating SHAP outputs into actionable underwriting narratives for loan officers and borrowers. This preprint introduces a benchmarking protocol for scorecard interpretability that evaluates five dimensions: local fidelity, global coherence, counterfactual proximity, regulatory legibility, and borrower comprehensibility. We apply the protocol to six model types—logistic regression scorecard, decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and a shallow neural network—using a unified dataset of 8,500 Serbian consumer and micro-business loan applications. Logistic regression scorecards dominate on regulatory legibility and borrower comprehensibility but lag on predictive performance, confirming the classic accuracy-interpretability trade-off. XGBoost with SHAP explanation achieves the best composite interpretability-performance score under our weighting scheme, which assigns equal weight to all five dimensions. We also show that LIME explanations exhibit lower cross-run stability than SHAP for tree-based models, raising concerns about their suitability for audit documentation. The benchmarking protocol is released as an open-source Python toolkit to support reproducibility and adoption by practitioners preparing model validation dossiers under Basel IV and the EU AI Act.

title: A Liveness-Based Register Coalescing Pass for Sparse Matrix–Vector Multiply on VLIW Processors
abstract: Register coalescing in VLIW architectures is complicated by the irregular memory access patterns that arise during sparse matrix–vector multiplication. This paper describes a liveness-based coalescing pass integrated into a custom VLIW back-end. The pass analyses def-use chains constructed from SSA form, identifies coalescing opportunities across basic-block boundaries, and applies an interference-graph pruning step that reduces the number of copy instructions by an average of 31% across six sparse benchmarks drawn from the SuiteSparse collection. Compilation time overhead relative to a baseline greedy allocator is 8%. The evaluation uses a cycle-accurate simulator of a four-issue VLIW core. Results show a 12–18% reduction in dynamic instruction count for matrices with densities between 0.1% and 2%. The pass is implemented as an LLVM 3.4 module pass and the source code is released under a permissive licence.

title: Encoding Compressed Sparse Row Layout in an SSA-Based Intermediate Representation
abstract: Standard SSA-based IRs represent memory accesses as load and store instructions with flat address arithmetic, which discards structural information present in compressed sparse formats. This work proposes an extension to a three-address SSA IR that introduces typed sparse-access nodes carrying row-pointer, column-index, and value streams as first-class operands. Thirty-two sparse kernels from graph analytics and scientific computing are re-expressed in the extended IR. A lowering pass translates the typed nodes to architecture-specific address sequences with a mean code-size increase of 4% compared to hand-written assembly. Static analysis on the extended IR detects 23 out of 25 injected out-of-bounds accesses at compile time. The paper reports compilation statistics for kernels compiled to a simulated 32-bit RISC-V target and discusses interaction with standard dataflow optimisations including constant propagation and dead-code elimination.

title: Register Pressure Reduction Through Sparsity-Specific Live-Range Splitting in an LLVM Back-End
abstract: Dense compiler back-ends handle live-range splitting by inserting spill code at points where register pressure exceeds the physical register count. For kernels operating on sparse tensors, spill patterns are strongly correlated with non-zero structure, and generic spill heuristics incur unnecessary memory traffic. This paper evaluates three live-range splitting strategies—interval halving, def-chain splitting, and density-guided breakpoint selection—on a set of sparse linear algebra kernels running on a simulated accelerator with 32 general-purpose registers. Density-guided splitting reduces spill instruction count by 22% and improves kernel execution time by 9% on average compared with the LLVM default spiller. The paper also reports on integration into a continuous integration pipeline used to track regression across nightly LLVM builds. Benchmarks cover matrices from the Florida Sparse Matrix Collection with non-zero counts between 10k and 40M.

title: A Taxonomy of Intermediate Representations for Domain-Specific Tensor Accelerators
abstract: This book chapter surveys IRs that have been proposed or deployed for tensor-processing hardware over the period 2008–2019, organising them along four axes: granularity (scalar, vector, tile, graph), sparsity awareness (none, hint-based, structural), target coupling (portable, vendor-specific, hybrid), and transformation support (limited, full algebraic, extensible). Thirty-one distinct IR designs are catalogued, drawn from academic papers, open-source compiler projects, and publicly disclosed industrial compiler documentation. The chapter identifies three recurring design tensions: expressiveness versus analysability, portability versus performance, and static shape information versus dynamic sparsity. Case studies are provided for three representative IRs, including compilation pipelines, supported hardware targets, and documented performance figures. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems in IR design for emerging sparse-dense mixed workloads.

title: Compile-Time Density Estimation for Guiding Sparse–Dense Format Selection in a Kernel Compiler
abstract: A kernel compiler targeting mixed sparse–dense workloads must decide at compile time whether a tensor operand should be stored in a sparse format (CSR, COO, BCSR) or a dense layout. Wrong choices lead to format-conversion overhead at runtime. This paper proposes a static analysis pass that propagates density bounds through an SSA-based IR using interval arithmetic. The pass is evaluated on a suite of 44 tensor kernels drawn from graph neural network training and scientific simulation. Static estimation selects the correct format for 38 of 44 kernels when compared with a profile-guided oracle. For the remaining six cases, a lightweight runtime fallback is triggered. End-to-end compilation including format inference takes under 400 ms per kernel on a standard laptop. The paper analyses false-positive rates for density over-estimation and their impact on memory allocation.

title: Seasonal variability of minimum discharges in the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal network: a long-record statistical analysis
abstract: Monthly minimum discharge records from eleven gauging stations along the DTD canal network, spanning the period 1971–2009, were analysed to characterise seasonal low-flow regimes. Flow duration curves and L-moment-based frequency analysis were applied to identify return-period thresholds for operationally critical low-flow states. Results indicate that Q90 values at interior junctions decreased by 12–18 % over the study period, with the steepest decline observed at the Vrbas–Savino Selo reach. Mann–Kendall trend tests confirmed statistically significant negative trends (p < 0.05) at seven of eleven stations. Spatial correlation structure was examined using a copula-based approach that revealed strong tail dependence between adjacent stations during summer droughts. The findings provide baseline statistics for irrigation scheduling and navigation depth management in the canal network.

title: Calibration of a one-dimensional unsteady flow model for a branching irrigation canal under low-water conditions
abstract: A HEC-RAS 1D unsteady-flow model was constructed for a 47 km branching reach of the DTD canal between Novi Sad and Zrenjanin. Bathymetric surveys conducted in 2010 provided cross-section geometry at 200 m intervals. Manning roughness coefficients were calibrated against 15 discharge–stage event pairs recorded between 2008 and 2011, achieving a Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.87 for water surface elevation and 0.81 for discharge at the downstream control point. The model was subsequently used to evaluate minimum operational depths under Q95 conditions, confirming that three gate structures require operational adjustments when daily mean discharge falls below 4.5 m³/s. Sensitivity analysis showed that uncertainty in roughness contributed more to prediction error than uncertainty in lateral inflow estimates. The calibrated model is used as a component in ensemble low-flow forecasting experiments described in subsequent work.

title: Stochastic simulation of daily inflows to the DTD canal system using a multisite weather generator
abstract: Synthetic daily precipitation and temperature series were generated for 23 sub-catchments feeding the DTD canal system using a Markov-chain-based weather generator conditioned on ERA-Interim reanalysis data for 1980–2012. Generated series were used to drive a lumped rainfall–runoff model (HBV-light) and lateral inflow estimates for the canal water-balance model. Ensembles of 500 synthetic years were generated, and resulting flow distributions at six canal nodes were compared with observed records. The generator reproduced observed interannual variability reasonably well, though it underestimated the frequency of multi-week dry spells in July–August by approximately 15 %. A bias-correction procedure based on quantile mapping reduced this discrepancy. The ensemble inflow distributions formed the stochastic forcing for a probabilistic low-flow forecast framework targeting 7- to 30-day lead times for navigation and irrigation operations.

title: Water-balance closure errors in a managed canal network: sources and quantification
abstract: Daily water-balance records for the entire DTD canal system covering 2005–2015 were used to evaluate the magnitude and spatial distribution of closure errors. The canal network encompasses approximately 930 km of main canals and handles both drainage and irrigation functions. Lumped water-balance equations were formulated for 14 sub-network segments, and residual terms were attributed to seepage loss, unmetered abstractions, and measurement uncertainty at flow-control structures. Seepage loss was estimated independently using soil permeability data from 112 borehole logs, yielding values between 0.3 and 1.1 mm/day across clay-lined and unlined sections. Unmetered abstractions from agricultural users were estimated at 8–22 % of total diverted volume during the irrigation season. Measurement uncertainty at gate structures, assessed through repeated calibration runs, contributed ±6 % systematic error. The analysis identified four sub-segments where closure errors exceeded 15 % and recommended metering upgrades.

title: Impact of regulated gate operations on dissolved oxygen dynamics in a slow-flow canal during summer low water
abstract: Dissolved oxygen concentrations were monitored at 30-minute intervals at five cross-sections of the DTD canal between Bečej and Zrenjanin during the summers of 2015 and 2016. During periods when flow velocity dropped below 0.05 m/s, DO fell to 3.1 mg/L or below at two mid-reach stations, approaching thresholds hazardous to fish. A one-dimensional water-quality module coupled to the calibrated HEC-RAS model was used to simulate reaeration, biochemical oxygen demand, and sediment oxygen demand. The model reproduced observed DO diurnal cycles with a root mean square error of 0.6 mg/L. Simulations showed that pulsed gate releases of 6 m³/s for periods of 4 hours every 48 hours during low-flow events could maintain DO above 4 mg/L throughout the monitored reach. Operational gate-scheduling recommendations were communicated to the water management authority.

title: Probabilistic low-flow forecasting at 14-day lead time using a Bayesian model averaging ensemble for the DTD canal system
abstract: Four hydrological models (HBV-light, GR4J, SAC-SMA, and a simple regression benchmark) were forced with ensemble numerical weather prediction outputs from ECMWF and ALADIN-Serbia to produce 14-day probabilistic discharge forecasts at three canal nodes. Forecasts from individual models were combined using Bayesian model averaging with weights estimated from a 10-year hindcast period (2006–2015). The BMA ensemble achieved a continuous ranked probability skill score of 0.31 relative to climatology at Bečej node for lead days 8–14, compared with 0.18 for the best single model. Reliability diagrams confirmed adequate probabilistic calibration across all three nodes. The framework was tested operationally during the 2019 summer low-flow period and issued four correctly verified low-flow alerts. Computational runtime allowed daily forecast updates on a standard workstation in under 12 minutes.

title: Intercomparison of gridded precipitation products over the Pannonian Plain and their suitability for canal catchment hydrology
abstract: Five gridded daily precipitation datasets—ERA5, MERRA-2, CHIRPS v2.0, a regional climate model output from RegCM4, and an interpolated station product from the Serbian meteorological network—were evaluated against observed records from 34 rain gauges distributed across the DTD catchment for 2000–2020. Evaluation metrics included Kling–Gupta efficiency, bias ratio, and hit rates for days exceeding the 90th percentile. ERA5 performed best overall, with KGE of 0.76 and a wet-day bias of +4 %, while CHIRPS v2.0 systematically underestimated convective summer events by 18 %. When used to drive the calibrated HBV model for the DTD catchment, ERA5 produced streamflow KGE values 0.11 higher than those from MERRA-2 at the Bečej station. Results are intended to guide the choice of historical forcing for water-balance and drought studies in the region.

title: Estimating canal seepage losses from remotely sensed soil moisture under variable antecedent conditions
abstract: Sentinel-1 SAR-derived surface soil moisture data were used to infer spatial seepage patterns along 210 km of unlined DTD canals during three contrasting low-flow periods in 2020 and 2021. A simplified vadose-zone model linked SAR-retrieved near-surface moisture to unsaturated hydraulic conductivity, enabling daily seepage flux estimates at 500 m intervals. Results were compared with previously published borehole-based estimates and with water-balance residuals. SAR-based estimates agreed with borehole values within ±0.2 mm/day for 78 % of reaches but diverged in areas with dense riparian vegetation. Total annual seepage loss for the study reach was estimated at 18.4 Mm³, consistent with the upper bound of earlier water-balance closure analyses. The approach offers a low-cost supplement to direct measurement where borehole data are unavailable.

title: Drought propagation from meteorological to hydrological deficit in the DTD canal catchment under two RCP scenarios
abstract: Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index values computed from EURO-CORDEX regional climate projections at five ensemble members were used to drive the calibrated HBV–canal water-balance model chain for the DTD system under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 for the period 2021–2060. Meteorological drought indices were compared with simulated hydrological drought indices at canal nodes to characterise propagation lags and attenuation factors. Results indicated median propagation lags of 2–3 months from SPEI-3 to canal discharge deficit, with attenuation factors between 0.55 and 0.72 depending on groundwater storage coefficients. Under RCP8.5, the frequency of days with discharge below Q90 at Bečej is projected to increase from a historical baseline of 36 days per year to 61 days by 2050. Uncertainty decomposition identified scenario uncertainty as dominant beyond 2040, with model uncertainty prevailing at shorter horizons.

title: Taint Propagation Across Remote Method Invocations in Distributed Java Applications
abstract: This paper describes a bytecode-instrumentation approach for tracking taint labels across remote method invocations in Java-based distributed applications. The instrumentation is performed at class-loading time using a custom Java agent, adding per-object label fields and propagating them through serialised message payloads. The evaluation covers four synthetic benchmarks and one medium-sized open-source application consisting of twelve communicating services. Label propagation overhead was measured at 4–11% throughput reduction on the benchmarks and 7% on the larger application. The study identifies three common coding patterns that cause label loss during serialisation and proposes wrapper types to preserve label integrity. The work also documents a set of false-positive flows arising from shared utility libraries and discusses suppression heuristics. Results confirm that bytecode-level instrumentation is feasible for moderate-size service graphs without requiring source-code access.

title: A Lattice-Based Label Model for Declassification in Multi-Party Web Services
abstract: The paper formalises a label model for multi-party web services where data owners may belong to overlapping trust groups. Labels are drawn from a finite security lattice whose structure is derived from organisational role hierarchies expressed in XACML policies. Declassification is permitted only at explicitly annotated service boundaries and requires a signed audit record. The model is implemented as a reference monitor sitting between an HTTP reverse proxy and the upstream service pool. Experiments use a synthetic banking workflow with five participants and three confidentiality levels. The monitor correctly enforced the policy in all 1,200 injected test transactions; it introduced a median latency of 2.3 ms per request, measured over 100,000 requests. The paper also proves that the model satisfies a termination-insensitive non-interference condition under the stated declassification rules.

title: Information-Flow Policies for Containerised Applications: A Taxonomy and Gap Analysis
abstract: This book chapter surveys policy languages and enforcement mechanisms proposed for containerised applications between 2010 and 2017. The taxonomy organises existing work along four axes: the granularity of the information-flow label (process, container, pod, namespace), the enforcement point (kernel, sidecar, orchestrator), the policy language expressiveness (lattice, role-based, attribute-based), and the runtime overhead class (negligible, moderate, prohibitive). Forty-three publications are categorised. The analysis identifies gaps: most proposals handle single-host deployments; fewer than ten address multi-host, multi-tenant scenarios; none formally verify policy composition when containers from different tenants share a pod network. The chapter concludes with a research agenda prioritising compositional policy verification and integration with orchestrator admission controllers. It is intended as background reading for graduate students and practitioners evaluating security tooling for Kubernetes-based platforms.

title: PolyFlow: Per-Request Information-Flow Tracking in a Kubernetes Service Mesh
abstract: PolyFlow is a system that attaches information-flow labels to individual HTTP requests and propagates them through a microservice application deployed on Kubernetes without modifying application source code. It instruments Envoy sidecar proxies using WebAssembly filter modules to extract and inject labels in request and response headers. A centralised policy server distributes compiled label-propagation rules to each sidecar at startup. The system is evaluated on a 16-service synthetic e-commerce benchmark and on a real internal workload with eight services, both running on a five-node cluster. Policy enforcement latency overhead was 1.8 ms median and 4.2 ms at the 99th percentile for the benchmark; policy compilation and distribution took under 3 seconds for a 40-rule policy. PolyFlow correctly identified 17 of 18 deliberately injected policy violations; the one missed violation involved an asynchronous message queue that bypassed HTTP headers.

title: Namespace Isolation Failures in Multi-Tenant Kubernetes Clusters: A Measurement Study
abstract: This paper reports a systematic measurement study of namespace isolation properties in Kubernetes 1.18–1.22 across three dimensions: network reachability, filesystem path exposure, and kernel resource visibility. A tenant simulation harness creates 50 pairs of tenant namespaces on a bare-metal cluster and runs 312 automated probe tests derived from known container-escape and cross-tenant information-leak CVEs. The study finds that default cluster configurations permit unintended network reachability in 34% of tested namespace pairs due to missing NetworkPolicy defaults, and that procfs entries expose cross-namespace process names in the absence of pid-namespace remapping. Filesystem exposure tests reveal shared tmpfs mounts accessible to adjacent namespaces in 8% of cases. The paper maps each finding to a specific Kubernetes configuration option or admission webhook that closes the gap, and provides a hardened baseline configuration validated against all 312 probes.

title: eBPF-Based Runtime Enforcement of Inter-Service Communication Policies
abstract: This paper presents an eBPF-based enforcement layer that intercepts socket operations inside container network namespaces and applies per-tenant communication policies expressed as allowlists of (source service identity, destination service identity, port, protocol) tuples. Service identities are derived from cryptographic certificates injected by the orchestrator at pod startup. The eBPF programs are compiled from a high-level policy DSL using a custom LLVM-based toolchain and loaded into the kernel via the BPF filesystem. The system is evaluated on a 24-service benchmark workload across a 10-node cluster. Policy enforcement adds a median of 210 µs to connection setup time and under 20 ns per packet on established flows. Compared with an equivalent iptables implementation, the eBPF approach reduces rule evaluation time by 78% at 1,000 active policies. The paper also characterises verifier complexity growth as policy size increases.

title: Side-Channel Leakage via Shared Kernel Resources in Co-Located Container Workloads
abstract: This paper investigates covert and side channels arising from shared kernel data structures in Linux when containers belonging to different tenants are co-located on the same host. Five channels are studied in detail: the dentry cache, the page cache, the per-CPU run-queue length, the TCP receive buffer pressure signal, and the inode number allocator. For each channel, the paper characterises bandwidth (measured in bits per second), reliability (bit error rate), and detectability by standard intrusion-detection tools. The dentry cache channel achieves 420 bits per second with a 3.1% bit error rate and is not detected by any of the four tested IDS tools. Proposed mitigations include per-namespace dentry partitioning and randomised inode allocation, evaluated on a patched 6.1 kernel. The mitigations reduce channel bandwidth by 94–99% with a filesystem operation overhead of 2–5%.

title: Continuous Policy Auditing for Long-Running Microservice Deployments Using Streaming Event Logs
abstract: Microservice deployments evolve continuously: services are redeployed, scaled, and reconfigured, which can silently invalidate previously verified information-flow policies. This paper proposes an online auditing architecture that ingests a stream of Kubernetes audit log events and service mesh access logs, maintains an up-to-date abstract model of the deployment, and re-checks the model against the tenant's policy after each structural change. The checker uses an incremental model-update algorithm that re-evaluates only the policy sub-graphs affected by each change, reducing re-verification time by a median of 67% compared with full re-verification across 500 simulated deployment-change sequences. The system is integrated with a Kubernetes operator and tested on three month-long deployment traces from a partner organisation. Fourteen unreported policy violations were identified in the traces, all caused by misconfigured new service versions introduced during rolling updates.

title: FlowGuard: A Policy Specification Language and Enforcement Runtime for Multi-Tenant Container Platforms
abstract: This paper presents FlowGuard, an integrated system comprising a domain-specific policy specification language and a corresponding enforcement runtime for information-flow security in multi-tenant container platforms. The language allows platform operators to define confidentiality and integrity labels, tenant-specific declassification rules, and cross-tenant boundary conditions using a syntax intentionally resembling YAML to lower the barrier for DevOps practitioners. The runtime compiles language constructs into eBPF programs for network enforcement and Kubernetes admission webhook rules for admission-time checks, and deploys them via a Kubernetes operator. FlowGuard is evaluated on a 10-tenant, 80-service synthetic workload and on a real deployment contributed by an industry partner with 6 tenants and 31 services. The system correctly enforces all 94 hand-authored policy rules in the synthetic workload and detects all 12 deliberately introduced violations in the industry deployment. Total runtime overhead relative to an unmonitored baseline is 3.1% for median latency and 6.4% at the 99th percentile.

title: Conflict-Free Replicated Counters in Edge Computing Scenarios with Intermittent Connectivity
abstract: Edge deployments frequently involve devices that disconnect from the core network for extended periods, making standard quorum-based replication impractical. We study the behaviour of grow-only counters and positive-negative counters under three intermittent connectivity models: periodic disconnection, random disconnection, and partition-triggered isolation. For each model we derive the expected delta between a device's local state and the globally merged state at reconnection time, as a function of operation rate and disconnection duration. We then propose a simple carry-forward delta-state protocol that reduces merge time at reconnection by pre-compressing accumulated increments. Experiments on a Raspberry Pi 4 cluster with emulated link failures show a 38% reduction in merge latency compared to a full-state sync for operation logs exceeding 50 000 entries. We discuss practical constraints imposed by limited flash write cycles on the compression frequency.

title: Identification of Cost Drivers in Engineer-to-Order Production: A Case Study in Welded Steel Structures
abstract: Engineer-to-order (ETO) production is characterised by high geometric variability and low repetition, which makes traditional cost estimation unreliable. This paper presents a systematic procedure for identifying and ranking cost drivers in the fabrication of welded steel structures based on 114 completed orders collected from a medium-sized manufacturer in Vojvodina over a five-year period. An initial pool of 31 candidate variables was reduced to 9 statistically significant cost drivers through stepwise regression. Weight, joint length, material grade, and surface preparation class emerged as the four variables explaining 78% of total production cost variance. The paper describes the data-collection protocol, discusses multicollinearity diagnostics, and evaluates the influence of order complexity indices. Results suggest that geometry-derived variables outperform weight alone as predictors when orders span multiple product families. The approach is intended as a structured input to parametric model development rather than a finished estimation tool.

title: Parametric Estimation Model for Pre-Tender Costing of Custom Hydraulic Cylinder Assemblies
abstract: Hydraulic cylinder manufacturers operating on an engineer-to-order basis often need reliable cost estimates before full technical specifications are available. This paper develops a parametric estimation model using geometric and performance parameters extractable from client enquiry documents. Input data comprising 86 completed cylinder orders were collected from a manufacturer in central Serbia. Ordinary least squares regression and a regression tree approach were both evaluated; the regression tree produced a mean absolute percentage error of 11.3% on a holdout sample of 17 orders, compared with 16.8% for the linear model. Key parameters were bore diameter, stroke length, operating pressure class, and seal configuration. The paper also discusses the estimation context, including which parameters are typically known at enquiry stage and which require assumption. Limitations related to material price volatility and subcontracted component inclusion are noted, and a correction procedure using a commodity-price index is proposed.

title: Structured Time Study for Non-Repetitive Assembly Tasks: Procedure and Pilot Application
abstract: Standard time study methods were developed primarily for repetitive, short-cycle operations and require adaptation when applied to assembly tasks that differ substantially from order to order. This paper proposes a structured procedure that disaggregates assembly work into a hierarchy of work elements defined by functional content rather than by product geometry. The procedure was piloted in a company producing custom switchgear panels, where 34 assembly jobs were observed over eight weeks, yielding 1,240 individual element-time observations. Inter-rater reliability between two trained observers was assessed using intraclass correlation, yielding ICC values above 0.91 for all major element categories. The resulting element-time database was used to construct synthetic basic time estimates for 12 recurring functional elements. The paper discusses the classification scheme, the rating procedure used, and the sensitivity of total job-time predictions to element boundary definitions. Applicability to other low-volume electrical assembly contexts is discussed.

title: Comparison of Estimation Methods for Early-Phase Cost Prediction in Custom Machine Tool Manufacturing
abstract: Four estimation approaches—analogical, parametric regression, feature-based, and expert judgement—were compared on a dataset of 62 completed orders for custom machine tools supplied by a manufacturer in northern Serbia. Each method was applied to the same set of 15 test orders using only information available at the end of the concept design phase. Accuracy was measured by mean absolute percentage error and bias. The parametric regression model achieved the lowest MAPE at 13.1%, while analogical estimation performed comparably at 14.6% when case retrieval used a weighted Euclidean distance over five technical attributes. Expert judgement showed the highest bias, systematically underestimating cost on geometrically complex orders. Feature-based estimation was most sensitive to the completeness of the conceptual design, limiting its reliability at the earliest project phase. The paper concludes with a discussion of which method is most appropriate depending on the information available and the acceptable risk of estimation error.

title: Standardisation of Work Instructions in ETO Manufacturing: A Framework Based on Reusable Work Packages
abstract: Engineer-to-order manufacturers frequently recreate work instructions from scratch for each order, leading to inconsistent time estimates and quality deviations. This paper presents a framework for constructing a library of reusable work packages that can be assembled into order-specific work instructions for mechanical assembly operations. Each work package covers a defined functional operation and includes a standard time, a list of required resources, and a set of applicability conditions. The framework was developed and trialled at a manufacturer of industrial mixing equipment in Serbia over a 14-month period. At the end of the trial, 63% of new order work instructions were assembled entirely from library packages, compared with 11% at baseline. Average instruction preparation time fell from 4.2 to 1.8 hours per order. Conformance rate between estimated and recorded work hours improved from 74% to 88%. The paper discusses the governance process for library maintenance and the criteria for retiring or splitting packages.

title: Machine Learning Approaches to Parametric Cost Estimation: Applicability Conditions and Data Requirements for ETO Manufacturers
abstract: Recent publications have proposed machine learning algorithms as replacements for regression-based parametric cost models. This paper evaluates that claim under the data conditions typical of small and medium ETO manufacturers, where historical order datasets rarely exceed 150 records. Using a synthetic dataset generated by Monte Carlo simulation, calibrated to match the distributional properties of four real ETO cost datasets, the performance of gradient boosted trees, random forests, support vector regression, and ordinary least squares regression was compared across dataset sizes ranging from 30 to 300 observations. At sample sizes below 80, OLS regression consistently matched or outperformed all machine learning methods on MAPE and on out-of-sample coverage. Gradient boosted trees showed advantages only above approximately 140 observations and when the relationship between cost drivers and cost was non-monotonic. The paper concludes with a decision table guiding practitioners in method selection based on dataset size, variable count, and available validation data.

title: Cost-to-Complete Forecasting Methods for Engineer-to-Order Projects: A Structured Review and Empirical Comparison
abstract: Cost-to-complete (CTC) forecasting during project execution receives less attention in the literature than pre-order estimation, despite its importance for cash-flow management and contract performance. This paper reviews 38 published methods and frameworks for CTC forecasting published between 2000 and 2024, classifying them by underlying technique, input data requirements, and intended application domain. Four representative methods were then empirically compared on a dataset of 22 completed ETO manufacturing projects, using data cut-offs at 25%, 50%, and 75% of project duration to simulate forecasting at different stages. The earned value management extension with a performance factor showed the lowest average absolute error across all cut-off points, but required accurate work breakdown and progress reporting. A simpler analogical method based on closest historical projects performed best at the 25% cut-off when progress reporting was sparse. The paper identifies gaps in coverage of multi-project environments and recommends directions for further empirical work.

title: A Practical Framework for ISO 14064-1 Organisational GHG Inventories in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
abstract: Small and medium-sized manufacturers in Serbia increasingly face requests from export customers and public procurement bodies to document greenhouse gas emissions at the organisational level. ISO 14064-1 provides a recognised framework, but its implementation guidance assumes resource levels not typical of Serbian SMEs. This paper develops and tests a simplified but standard-conformant procedure for Scope 1 and Scope 2 inventory compilation, applied to four manufacturing companies in the Novi Sad industrial zone with between 45 and 210 employees. The procedure uses default emission factors from the national energy balance supplemented by supplier-specific electricity grid data from EPS. Data collection time at each company was recorded; the full inventory was completed in an average of 14 working days per company. Verification readiness was assessed against ISO 14064-3 criteria. Two companies achieved documentation sufficient for third-party verification without additional consultancy. Barriers identified include inconsistent utility metering and lack of internal ownership of environmental data. The paper provides a checklist and data collection template adapted to Serbian regulatory and utility contexts.

title: Estimating Hidden Internal Failure Costs in Electronics Contract Manufacturing: A Structured Interview and Time-Study Approach
abstract: Visible failure costs—scrap, rework labour, and component replacement—represent only a portion of actual internal failure expenditure. This study develops a protocol for estimating hidden internal failure costs, defined here as managerial time, scheduling disruption, expediting, and re-inspection effort generated by defective assemblies. The protocol combines structured interviews with production supervisors and engineers, time-study observations on the shop floor, and activity-based allocation of indirect labour. Applied at two contract manufacturers in Serbia over a combined observation period of eight months, the method revealed that hidden costs averaged 1.8 times the visible internal failure costs. The ratio varied by product complexity: high-layer-count boards showed ratios up to 2.4, while simpler single-board assemblies showed ratios closer to 1.3. The paper discusses sources of estimation uncertainty, inter-rater reliability of the interview instrument (Cohen's κ = 0.74), and practical limits on data granularity in SME settings. A condensed version of the protocol suitable for self-assessment by quality managers is included as an appendix.

title: Criteria for Classifying Assets as Public Goods Under Serbian Law: A Doctrinal Analysis
abstract: This article examines the criteria applied by Serbian courts and administrative bodies to classify assets as public goods (opšta dobra) under the Law on Public Property of 2011 and related sectoral legislation. The analysis draws on a systematic review of 47 first-instance administrative court decisions issued between 2013 and 2021, as well as relevant opinions issued by the Republic Attorney's Office. The study identifies three recurring classification disputes: the boundary between natural watercourses and privately constructed channels, road infrastructure built on cadastrally private parcels, and publicly accessible green areas in peri-urban zones. Findings show that courts applied inconsistent criteria in approximately 38 percent of the reviewed cases, frequently conflating public use with public ownership. The article proposes a two-stage classification test grounded in the objective nature of the asset and the exclusivity of public use, and situates Serbian doctrine within the broader taxonomy developed in French and German administrative property law. No empirical field data were collected; the methodology is doctrinal and comparative.

title: Public Domain Assets in the Legal Systems of the Western Balkans: Between Socialist Legacy and European Standards
abstract: This book chapter provides a comparative overview of the legal regime for public domain assets (res in publico usu) in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, tracing the doctrinal lineage from the Yugoslav socially-owned property concept through post-1990 legislative reforms. The chapter draws on primary legislation, constitutional court decisions from all three jurisdictions, and a review of secondary literature in Serbian, Bosnian, and Macedonian legal scholarship. It identifies three divergent reform trajectories: Serbia's property dualism separating general public goods from public property stricto sensu; Bosnia and Herzegovina's entity-level fragmentation; and North Macedonia's relatively consolidated public domain catalogue introduced in 2010. The chapter concludes that all three systems retain structural ambiguities inherited from the socialist period, particularly regarding the legal personality of public domain assets and the conditions for their temporary private use, and recommends drawing on the acquis of the Council of Europe's Venice Commission recommendations on property reform.
