title: Municipal Land Management and Urban Planning Instruments: Legal Interfaces in the Context of Serbian Local Self-Government Reform
abstract: This conference paper examines the intersection of municipal property law and urban planning instruments in Serbian law, focusing specifically on the legal tools available to municipalities for managing building land under both the Law on Public Property and the Law on Planning and Construction. It analyses four case municipalities—Novi Sad, Sombor, Vranje, and Zaječar—selected to represent different population sizes and regional contexts. Data were collected through structured review of municipal property registers and publicly available urban plans adopted between 2015 and 2023. The paper finds that municipalities with consolidated cadastral bases deployed expropriation and land consolidation procedures significantly more effectively than those with fragmented records, and that the legal interface between the two statutory regimes produces overlapping competences for municipal administration bodies and the Republic Geodetic Authority. The paper was presented at the Regional Administrative Law Conference held in Sarajevo in May 2024.

title: The Concept of 'General Use' in Serbian Public Property Law: Origins, Current Application and Open Questions
abstract: This preprint offers a preliminary doctrinal analysis of the concept of general use (opšta upotreba) as a defining characteristic of public goods in Serbian law, tracing its legislative history from the 1980 Law on Basic Property Relations through the current 2011 framework. The analysis identifies the concept's Roman law origins as mediated through Austrian and Yugoslav civil law traditions, and examines how the Serbian legislator adapted it in the post-2000 reform period. The paper reviews 22 Constitutional Court and Supreme Court of Cassation decisions in which the scope of general use was at issue, finding that the courts have progressively narrowed the concept since 2015, with implications for municipal access to riverbanks, public squares, and unmarked paths. The author argues that this judicial narrowing is not adequately supported by the statutory text and risks producing inconsistencies with European Court of Human Rights case law on Protocol 1, Article 1.

title: Minimum Wage Enforcement and Compliance Monitoring: A Multi-Level Analysis of Municipal-Level Variation in Serbia
abstract: Despite a uniform national minimum wage, compliance rates in Serbia vary substantially across municipalities. This article investigates the sources of that variation using a dataset combining Labour Inspectorate inspection records for 2020–2024 with municipal-level economic and institutional variables for 145 municipalities. A multi-level logistic regression model was used to estimate the probability of a minimum-wage violation being detected and upheld, with random effects at the municipal level. After controlling for sector composition, firm size distribution, and unemployment rate, variation attributable to the municipal level accounted for 18 percent of total outcome variance. The strongest municipal-level predictors were the density of registered labour inspectors per thousand employees and the presence of an active local economic development office. The article argues that compliance monitoring for national labour standards cannot be evaluated solely at the national level and proposes a municipal compliance capacity index comprising four observable indicators that could be used to target inspection resources. Implications for the design of the new National Labour Inspectorate Strategy 2026–2030, currently in preparation, are discussed.

title: Discretion, Expertise, and Democratic Legitimacy in Serbian Energy Regulation
abstract: The Serbian Energy Agency (AERS) has been empowered since its establishment in 2004 to issue binding rulebooks on network tariffs and grid connection conditions. This paper examines whether the enabling statutes—the Energy Acts of 2004, 2011, and 2014—satisfy the constitutional requirement that essential regulatory choices be made by the legislature itself. Drawing on the Wesentlichkeitstheorie and the American non-delegation doctrine as analytical benchmarks, and reviewing twenty-two AERS rulebooks issued through 2015, the study finds that the 2014 Act leaves significant pricing discretion to the agency without specifying the criteria against which rates must be assessed. A comparison with regulatory enabling statutes in Slovenia and Croatia reveals that both neighbouring legal orders impose more explicit statutory constraints. The paper recommends legislative amendments to introduce intelligible-principle requirements in Serbian sector-specific legislation.

title: Excess air ratio effects on CO and NOx emissions from a 15 kW wood pellet burner under steady-state conditions
abstract: This study examined how varying excess air ratios (λ = 1.1 to 2.0) influence CO and NOx concentrations in the flue gas of a 15 kW fixed-grate wood pellet burner. Measurements were conducted over 90-minute stabilised runs at full rated load using a non-dispersive infrared CO analyser and a chemiluminescence NOx detector. Pellet feedstock from a single batch of spruce–fir blend (moisture content 8.2 %, ash content 0.4 %) was used throughout to minimise fuel variability. Results showed a clear trade-off: CO decreased monotonically from 420 mg/Nm³ at λ = 1.1 to below 30 mg/Nm³ at λ = 1.6, while NOx rose from 68 mg/Nm³ to 142 mg/Nm³ over the same range. A simple empirical correlation relating λ to both pollutants simultaneously was fitted with R² above 0.94. The findings suggest that λ = 1.35–1.45 represents a practical optimum for this burner geometry, keeping both pollutants below EN 303-5 Class 5 limits without efficiency penalties exceeding 1.8 percentage points.

title: In-flame temperature mapping in a 20 kW pellet burner using a suction pyrometer and thermocouple array
abstract: Accurate knowledge of in-flame temperature distribution is a prerequisite for validating combustion models. This paper reports temperature profiles measured at seventeen axial and radial positions inside a 20 kW downdraft pellet burner using a combination of a water-cooled suction pyrometer and sheathed K-type thermocouples. Measurements were performed at 100 % and 60 % thermal load, with the same spruce pellet batch used in earlier work. Peak temperatures reached 1 087 °C at full load near the primary air nozzle exit and dropped to 923 °C at partial load. Radial gradients were steeper than axial gradients in both cases. The thermocouple array systematically underread by 40–85 °C compared with the suction pyrometer due to radiation losses, and correction factors were derived as a function of local gas velocity. These corrected profiles were used to construct a two-dimensional temperature map suitable for input to a zone-based NOx formation model described in subsequent work.

title: Effect of staged primary-to-secondary air split on NOx and CO in a retrofit pellet burner head
abstract: Staged-air combustion was implemented on a commercial 20 kW pellet burner by dividing the original single primary air plenum into two independently controlled zones—lower (LZ) and upper (UZ)—using a welded baffle plate. Tests were run at 100 %, 75 %, and 50 % load across nine LZ/UZ split ratios from 70:30 to 30:70. Flue-gas composition was measured continuously over 120-minute stabilised runs. At full load, a 55:45 split reduced NOx by 22 % relative to the unstaged baseline (from 138 to 108 mg/Nm³) with CO remaining below 50 mg/Nm³. At 50 % load, the same split increased CO to 310 mg/Nm³ as the flame root lifted; a 65:35 ratio restored CO to 85 mg/Nm³ while still achieving 14 % NOx reduction. Combustion efficiency remained above 91 % in all compliant configurations. The study provides a practical load-dependent staging map applicable to burner manufacturers considering low-cost retrofit solutions.

title: Influence of pellet ash content and alkali metal concentration on particulate matter and NOx co-emission
abstract: Five commercial pellet grades with ash contents ranging from 0.3 % to 3.8 % and potassium concentrations from 420 to 3 100 mg/kg were combusted in the same 20 kW staged-air burner at 100 % load. Particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) was sampled gravimetrically on quartz fibre filters using an isokinetic probe at the stack. NOx was measured in parallel by chemiluminescence. High-alkali agricultural pellets (sunflower husk, 3.8 % ash) produced PM10 of 185 mg/Nm³, compared with 28 mg/Nm³ for low-ash spruce pellets, and also showed elevated NOx at 162 mg/Nm³ versus 108 mg/Nm³, attributed to additional fuel-N and catalytic effects of KCl on char oxidation. A linear regression of NOx on potassium concentration gave a slope of 0.031 mg NOx per mg/kg K, significant at p < 0.01. These results suggest that pellet quality specifications targeting alkali content could simultaneously benefit both NOx and PM performance, with implications for regional air-quality regulations in the Vojvodina plain.

title: Transient CO and NOx behaviour during load-change cycles in a modulating pellet burner
abstract: Most combustion appliance emission standards are evaluated at steady state, yet residential boilers regularly cycle between load levels. This study characterised the transient flue-gas response of a 20 kW modulating pellet burner during programmed step changes from 100 % to 50 % load and back, repeated 30 times over two test days. CO and NOx were logged at 1 Hz. Each downward step produced a CO spike averaging 1 140 mg/Nm³ lasting 38 seconds before settling to a new steady state, while NOx dropped immediately to the lower-load steady value within about 20 seconds. Upward steps caused a brief NOx transient peaking 18 % above the full-load steady value for roughly 15 seconds, with no appreciable CO excursion. Integrated over a 24-hour simulated residential heating cycle with six load changes, transient emissions increased total CO by 11 % and total NOx by 2 % compared to a purely steady-state calculation. These findings suggest that type-test protocols should include at least a standardised transient sequence.

title: Low-cost sensor array for continuous CO monitoring in small biomass boiler flue ducts: calibration and drift characterisation over a heating season
abstract: Electrochemical CO sensors are attractive for long-term monitoring of small biomass boilers but suffer from drift and cross-sensitivity. This paper describes the calibration and nine-month field deployment of a four-sensor array installed in the flue duct of a 20 kW pellet boiler in a private household in Novi Sad. Each sensor was cross-calibrated weekly against a reference NDIR instrument. Raw sensor readings drifted by up to 23 % over the season, but a simple two-point recalibration at intervals of four weeks reduced mean error to below 8 % across the 20–800 mg/Nm³ range. The array correctly identified all 47 transient CO spikes above 500 mg/Nm³ logged by the reference instrument during the season. Temperature compensation improved accuracy at flue temperatures above 160 °C. The system cost under 120 EUR in components and required no specialised installation. The paper discusses suitability as a low-cost compliance indicator and the data requirements for a future load-state classifier based on CO signature alone.

title: Accuracy Assessment of Split-Window and Single-Channel LST Retrieval Algorithms Applied to Landsat 8/9 TIRS Data over Novi Sad
abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) retrieved from Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS) imagery was evaluated using two widely applied retrieval approaches: the split-window algorithm and the single-channel algorithm. The study area covered the Novi Sad urban agglomeration and its peri-urban surroundings across four seasonal acquisitions in 2022–2023. Land surface emissivity was estimated from NDVI-based fractional vegetation cover. Retrieved LST values were validated against concurrent measurements from seven portable FLIR infrared radiometers deployed across land cover classes including dense residential fabric, industrial zones, parks, and bare agricultural soil. Root mean square errors ranged from 1.3 K to 2.1 K depending on algorithm and season, with the split-window approach performing consistently better over heterogeneous urban surfaces. Systematic warm biases were identified over low-emissivity industrial rooftops. Results suggest that algorithm choice and emissivity input quality interact strongly in urban contexts, and the paper provides land-cover-stratified accuracy statistics for the Pannonian lowland setting.

title: Spatial Downscaling of MODIS Land Surface Temperature to 30 m Resolution Using Random Forest Regression and Auxiliary Spectral Indices
abstract: MODIS Terra daily LST composites (MOD11A1, 1 km resolution) were downscaled to 30 m using a random forest regression model trained on predictor variables derived from coincident Landsat 8 OLI imagery. Predictor set included NDVI, NDBI, MNDWI, albedo, and sky-view factor estimated from a 1 m lidar-derived digital surface model. The model was trained and tested over the Novi Sad metropolitan area using 48 cloud-free Landsat–MODIS pairs from 2019 to 2022 distributed across all seasons. Cross-validated RMSE of the downscaled product was 1.7 K in summer and 2.4 K in winter. Spatial detail improved substantially in mixed-use transition zones between compact urban blocks and suburban gardens. The method was applied to produce a summer daytime LST climatology at 30 m, revealing intra-urban temperature gradients of up to 9.2 K within 500 m horizontal distance during heat-wave conditions in July 2021. Computational processing used a Python-based pipeline available as supplementary material.
venue: Proceedings of the 14th Symposium on Remote Sensing of Urban Areas (URBAN-RS 2024), Vienna, Austria

title: Comparing Daytime Urban Heat Island Intensity Across Seven Mid-Size Cities in the Pannonian Basin Using ECOSTRESS Thermal Data
abstract: ECOSTRESS Level-2 LST retrievals (70 m native resolution) from the International Space Station were used to characterise daytime urban heat island (UHI) intensity across seven mid-size cities in the Pannonian Basin: Novi Sad (Serbia), Subotica (Serbia), Szeged (Hungary), Pécs (Hungary), Timișoara (Romania), Osijek (Croatia), and Banja Luka (Bosnia and Herzegovina). A total of 214 overpass acquisitions from 2019 to 2023 were processed, retaining 89 scenes with cloud cover below 15 percent over the full study domain. UHI intensity was defined as the mean LST difference between pixels classified as urban by the ESA WorldCover 2021 product and surrounding rural pixels within a 10 km buffer. Mean summer daytime UHI intensities ranged from 2.4 K in Banja Luka to 4.1 K in Szeged. Correlation analysis showed that city compactness index and impervious surface fraction together explained 61 percent of variance in peak UHI intensity. The multi-city approach allowed controlling for regional meteorological drivers that otherwise confound single-city studies.
venue: International Journal of Urban Climate Research

title: Sensitivity of Downscaled LST Products to Input Emissivity Maps Derived from Different Classification Schemes
abstract: Downscaled land surface temperature estimates depend on the emissivity map used as input to the retrieval algorithm, yet emissivity is rarely treated as a source of uncertainty in urban downscaling workflows. This study systematically compared five emissivity assignment strategies over the Novi Sad study area: ASTER GED climatology, NDVI-threshold classification, random-forest-predicted emissivity, OpenStreetMap-guided material classification, and a constant emissivity assumption. For each strategy, LST was retrieved from six Landsat 9 TIRS scenes acquired in summer 2023 and validated against radiometer measurements at 21 sites. Mean absolute errors in the final downscaled 30 m LST product varied between 0.8 K and 2.9 K across strategies. The OpenStreetMap-guided approach performed best in dense urban cores while ASTER GED performed adequately in peri-urban vegetated areas. The study provides practical guidance on emissivity input selection for cities where high-resolution material maps are partially available through volunteered geographic information.
venue: Remote Sensing Letters

title: Individual tree segmentation in dense broadleaf canopies: comparison of watershed, region-growing and graph-cut approaches on UAV LiDAR data
abstract: Three established point cloud segmentation algorithms — normalised cut watershed, region-growing based on local maxima, and a min-cut/max-flow graph-cut method — were evaluated on UAV LiDAR data acquired over four broadleaf forest plots in the Vojvodina lowlands and Fruška Gora foothills, Serbia. Plot-level tree densities ranged from 280 to 640 stems per hectare. Point cloud density averaged 180 points m⁻² after trajectory processing. Accuracy was assessed against field-measured stem positions and crown projections for 412 reference trees. The graph-cut method achieved the highest F1 score (0.81) overall, outperforming watershed (0.74) and region-growing (0.77) particularly in plots with overlapping crowns and stem densities above 450 ha⁻¹. All three methods underperformed in the suppressed understorey layer, where detection rates fell below 0.55. Processing time for the graph-cut approach was approximately 4.2 times longer than watershed per plot. Results highlight trade-offs relevant to operational large-area forest inventory using UAV platforms.
venue: Proceedings of the Central European Remote Sensing Conference (CERSC)

title: Water absorption and density variability of recycled coarse aggregates sourced from demolished residential buildings in the Vojvodina region
abstract: Recycled coarse aggregates were collected from five demolition sites in the Vojvodina region between 2012 and 2013. A total of 180 individual aggregate samples were characterised for water absorption, bulk density, and crushing value following adapted EN 1097 procedures. Water absorption ranged from 3.1% to 8.7%, with a coefficient of variation of 31%, considerably higher than the 6–8% typically reported for natural aggregates in the same grain size fraction. Bulk density varied between 2,140 and 2,580 kg/m³. Statistical analysis indicated that the source building age and original concrete grade were the dominant factors explaining variance in absorption, together accounting for approximately 52% of variability in a two-way ANOVA. The dataset was used to develop preliminary quality classification criteria for recycled aggregates intended for structural concrete applications in the region. Findings support the need for batching-specific aggregate characterisation rather than reliance on single-source test certificates.

title: Probabilistic assessment of characteristic compressive strength for precast beams produced with partial recycled aggregate substitution
abstract: A probabilistic framework was developed to estimate the characteristic compressive strength of precast concrete beams incorporating 30% recycled coarse aggregate, targeting compliance with the EN 13369 requirements for precast elements. Production data from a regional precast manufacturer were collected over an eight-month period, yielding 214 in-plant cube test results. The data were fitted to normal, lognormal, and Weibull distributions; goodness-of-fit was assessed using the Kolmogorov–Smirnov and Anderson–Darling tests. The lognormal distribution provided the best fit. Monte Carlo simulation with 50,000 iterations was used to propagate aggregate quality variability, quantified from a parallel testing programme, into beam-level strength predictions. Results indicated that, under the identified variability conditions, a 28-day target mean strength of 43.5 MPa was required to reliably achieve a characteristic strength of 35 MPa, representing a 2.3 MPa increase over the equivalent all-natural-aggregate mix. The approach is adaptable to other replacement levels and mix classes.

title: Chloride diffusion coefficients in recycled aggregate concrete: experimental data and comparison with predictive models
abstract: Chloride diffusion was investigated in concrete mixes with 0%, 50%, and 100% recycled coarse aggregate replacement prepared at water-to-cement ratios of 0.45 and 0.55. Specimens were exposed to a 3% NaCl ponding solution for 90 days following initial curing. Chloride profiles were obtained by dry-grinding at five depth increments and potentiometric titration. Apparent diffusion coefficients were calculated by fitting Fick's second law to the measured profiles. At w/c = 0.45, apparent diffusion coefficient increased from 4.1 × 10⁻¹² m²/s at 0% replacement to 9.7 × 10⁻¹² m²/s at 100% replacement. At w/c = 0.55, corresponding values were 7.3 and 15.4 × 10⁻¹² m²/s. Existing predictive models from the literature underestimated the diffusion coefficient for high-replacement mixes by 25–40%, attributed to the additional porosity introduced by residual mortar on the recycled aggregate surface. A correction factor based on measured aggregate absorption was proposed to improve model predictions.

title: Effect of carbonation pre-treatment of recycled aggregate on ITZ porosity and chloride penetration resistance
abstract: Carbonation of recycled coarse aggregate was applied as a densification pre-treatment by exposing aggregate batches to a CO₂ concentration of 20% v/v for periods of 4, 8, and 24 hours under ambient pressure and 60% relative humidity. Treated and untreated aggregates were incorporated into concrete mixes at 50% replacement, and specimens were tested for compressive strength at 28 days, ITZ porosity by mercury intrusion porosimetry, and chloride migration by the rapid chloride migration test following NT BUILD 492. The 24-hour CO₂ treatment reduced average ITZ porosity from 18.2% to 11.4% and decreased the chloride migration coefficient from 14.3 × 10⁻¹² m²/s to 9.1 × 10⁻¹² m²/s. Compressive strength increased by 8% relative to untreated aggregate mixes. The treatment had no measurable effect on aggregate bulk density or particle shape. The results indicate that carbonation pre-treatment is a practically applicable method for durability improvement without significant changes to mix proportioning.

title: Plancherel Measure and Square-Integrability for a Class of Two-Step Nilpotent Lie Groups
abstract: We study the unitary dual and the Plancherel decomposition for a parametric family of two-step nilpotent Lie groups G_{m,n}, where the centre has dimension m and the quotient has dimension n. Using Kirillov's orbit method, we give an explicit formula for the Plancherel measure in terms of polynomial functions on the dual of the Lie algebra, valid for all m, n ≥ 1. For the case m = 1 (generalised Heisenberg groups), we recover classical results and extend them by computing the precise constants in the inversion formula. We verify square-integrability of a family of representations indexed by a co-adjoint orbit of maximal dimension and use this to construct admissible vectors whose existence had previously been established only for small values of n. The proofs combine direct integral decomposition theory with explicit matrix computations carried out in SageMath. Numerical checks are provided for groups of dimension up to 14.

title: Irregular Sampling on the Heisenberg Group via Weighted Beurling Densities
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of reconstructing functions in modulation spaces on the Heisenberg group H^n from samples taken at non-uniform sets of points. We introduce a weighted Beurling density adapted to the Haar measure on H^n and prove that any separated sampling set whose lower weighted Beurling density exceeds a critical threshold determined by the modulation space parameters admits a stable sampling inequality. The proof proceeds by constructing a frame of Gabor-type atoms localised around the sampling points and applying an abstract perturbation result for frames in Banach spaces. We test the reconstruction algorithm on synthetic signals in H^1 discretised on a 128×128 grid, achieving relative reconstruction errors below 0.4% at oversampling ratios of 1.15. The dependence of the threshold on the group's non-commutativity parameter is made quantitative.

title: Coorbit Spaces Associated with Exponential Solvable Lie Groups
abstract: Coorbit space theory, originally developed for square-integrable group representations, is here extended to a broader class of exponential solvable Lie groups whose irreducible representations need not be square-integrable in the classical sense. We introduce a modified notion of analysing vector based on an integrability condition for the wavelet transform defined via induced representations, and construct a scale of coorbit Banach spaces interpolating between known L^p-type spaces. Embeddings between coorbit spaces at different scales are characterised in terms of membership in weighted L^p spaces on the group. As a concrete example, the full construction is carried out for the affine group of the real line (ax+b group) and for a three-dimensional solvable group, with explicit descriptions of the resulting function spaces and their norms. Connections to classical Besov and Triebel–Lizorkin spaces are identified.

title: A Discrete Fourier Analysis Framework on Cayley Graphs of Finite Nilpotent Groups
abstract: We develop a self-contained discrete harmonic analysis on Cayley graphs of finite nilpotent groups, motivated by applications in graph signal processing. Defining convolution via the group multiplication, we prove a Plancherel identity relating the L^2 norm of a function to the Hilbert–Schmidt norms of its matrix-valued Fourier coefficients, indexed by the irreducible unitary representations of the group. For groups of order up to 2^8, all irreducible representations are computed explicitly using GAP software, and the resulting Fourier transform is implemented as a sparse matrix operation. We evaluate reconstruction accuracy for signals defined on the Cayley graphs of groups Z_4 × Z_4, D_8 (dihedral), and the quaternion group Q_8, comparing performance of the group Fourier transform against the standard graph Laplacian eigenbasis under 20% random missing-node scenarios. The group Fourier approach shows lower reconstruction error in all symmetric graph configurations tested.
venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Harmonic Analysis and Graph Signal Processing (HAGSP 2019), Budapest

title: Frame Bounds for Coherent States on Compact Quotients of the Upper Half-Plane
abstract: We consider the problem of constructing frames of coherent states for L^2(Γ\G), where G = SL(2,ℝ) and Γ is a co-compact lattice, by sampling the continuous wavelet transform at a discrete set of group elements. Using the theory of discrete series representations and the geometry of fundamental domains, we derive explicit lower and upper frame bounds as functions of the lattice parameter and the admissibility constant of the mother wavelet. For three specific lattices—including a surface of genus 2 and one of genus 3—we compute the optimal frame bounds numerically using a truncated Gram-matrix method on grids of up to 10^4 points, confirming tightness up to a ratio of 1.08 in the best case. We also show that the frame property fails for sampling densities below an explicit critical value tied to the area of the fundamental domain.

title: Quantitative Uncertainty Principles on Graded Lie Groups with Applications to Time-Frequency Concentration
abstract: We prove a sharp Heisenberg-type uncertainty inequality for the group Fourier transform on graded Lie groups G, expressing a lower bound on the product of the L^2-spread of a function and the L^2-spread of its Fourier transform in terms of the homogeneous dimension of G. The bound is shown to be attained by Gaussian-type functions adapted to the group's dilations. A second result establishes a Benedicks-type theorem: if both a non-zero function f ∈ L^2(G) and its Fourier transform have supports of finite Plancherel measure, then no such f can exist, extending the classical result to graded groups of step up to 3. For the Engel group (step 3, homogeneous dimension 7), explicit examples illustrating the tightness of the constant are constructed and verified numerically. Connections to time-frequency localisation in sub-Riemannian geometry are discussed.

title: Reconstruction of Graph Signals on Product Cayley Graphs from Partial Spectral Data
abstract: Let G = G_1 × G_2 be a direct product of two finite groups, and let Γ be the Cayley graph of G with respect to a generating set that decomposes as a union of generators from each factor. We study the minimum number of spectral coefficients (with respect to the group Fourier basis) sufficient to guarantee unique reconstruction of a graph signal from its restriction to a subset of vertices, under an energy compactness assumption. A sufficient condition expressed as a coherence bound on the Fourier basis restricted to the vertex subset is derived, and an L^1-minimisation recovery algorithm is analysed. For product groups of sizes 16 through 256, Monte Carlo trials over 10,000 random vertex masks at varying retention rates (30%–80%) show that L^1 recovery achieves exact reconstruction in over 96% of trials whenever the retention rate exceeds 1.4 times the theoretical coherence threshold. The method is compared against interpolation based on the graph Laplacian eigenbasis.

title: Non-Uniform Sampling for Sensor Placement on Curved Surfaces via Lie Group Geometry
abstract: We consider the problem of choosing sensor locations on a smooth Riemannian manifold M that admit stable reconstruction of signals in a Sobolev-type space H^s(M) from point evaluations. Treating the isometry group of M as a locally compact Lie group and using the spectral decomposition of the Laplace–Beltrami operator, we derive a sampling criterion in terms of the covering radius of the sensor set and the bandwidth parameter s. The criterion is computationally verified for two test manifolds—the two-sphere S^2 with 50 and 200 sensors, and the flat torus T^2 with 64 and 256 sensors—by computing condition numbers of the associated sampling matrices. Results show that the theoretical covering-radius threshold predicts stable sampling (condition number below 10) with 92% accuracy across 500 random sensor configurations. Potential applications to distributed acoustic sensing and environmental monitoring are outlined without implementation.

title: Empirical Path-Loss Characterisation for 868 MHz Signals in a Mixed Residential and Commercial District
abstract: This paper presents a measurement-based path-loss study conducted in the Liman district of Novi Sad at 868 MHz during autumn 2009. A total of 4 800 received signal strength indicator samples were collected along 22 transects using a calibrated test transmitter and a portable receiver mounted on a bicycle. The log-distance model with a dual-slope breakpoint at 120 m was fitted to the data, yielding path-loss exponents of 2.1 and 3.6 for the near and far zones, respectively. Shadowing standard deviation was estimated at 7.2 dB. Results are compared against the COST 231 Hata model, which overestimates median loss by 4.8 dB in this environment. The fitted model parameters are provided as a baseline for subsequent LoRa link budget calculations in the region. Measurement methodology, equipment calibration procedure, and statistical goodness-of-fit tests are described in detail.

title: Link Budget Margins for LoRa Deployments in Underground Utility Tunnels
abstract: Urban utility tunnels housing water, gas, and district-heating pipes present a challenging propagation environment for wireless sensor nodes due to metallic surfaces, bends, and varying cross-sections. This paper reports measurements at 868 MHz in a 380 m segment of a utility tunnel in Novi Sad, conducted in cooperation with the municipal infrastructure operator. Three antenna configurations were tested: omnidirectional whip, patch, and small Yagi. Path loss along straight tunnel sections followed a waveguide-like model with an attenuation constant of 0.08 dB/m beyond the first Fresnel zone breakpoint. At 90-degree bends, excess loss of 12–18 dB was measured depending on the bend radius. With a LoRa gateway placed at the tunnel entrance, spreading factor SF12 provided connectivity over the full 380 m with a link margin of approximately 6 dB. A simplified link budget worksheet is provided for practitioners planning similar deployments.

title: Effect of Seasonal Foliage on LoRa Received Signal Strength in a Suburban Environment
abstract: Vegetation attenuation is a well-known propagation impairment but its seasonal variability at 868 MHz has not been systematically quantified for LoRa links in a continental European climate. This study used a fixed LoRa testbed with five static end nodes deployed in a mixed residential and park area in Novi Sad to record RSSI and SNR continuously over a 14-month period from March 2015 to April 2016. Three nodes had line-of-sight paths through deciduous trees; two served as reference nodes with unobstructed paths. A mean additional attenuation of 8.4 dB was observed during full-leaf season (June–September) compared with the dormant season, with a standard deviation across links of 2.1 dB. The results suggest that link budget calculations for year-round deployments in this climate should incorporate a seasonal margin of at least 11 dB when tree-lined paths are unavoidable.

title: Spreading Factor Assignment Strategies for LoRaWAN Networks: Simulations and Field Validation
abstract: In LoRaWAN, the choice of spreading factor directly affects data rate, airtime, and battery lifetime. The standard adaptive data rate (ADR) algorithm assigns SF based solely on signal margin without considering co-SF interference from neighbouring nodes. This paper proposes a static assignment strategy derived from a coverage simulation of a 12-gateway network deployed over a 38 km² area of Novi Sad and its surrounding suburbs, combined with measured RSSI maps. Three assignment strategies are evaluated: default ADR, a distance-based SF zoning scheme, and a simulation-optimised assignment minimising expected packet collision rate. Network-level simulations using OMNeT++ with the FLoRa module show that the optimised assignment reduces packet loss from 14.3% to 7.8% under a 500-node traffic load compared with default ADR. Field validation with 45 physical nodes confirmed the simulation trend within 1.5 percentage points.

title: Gateway Placement Optimisation for LoRaWAN Coverage of a Mid-Size City Using a Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Determining the minimum number of gateways and their locations to achieve a target coverage probability is an NP-hard combinatorial problem. This paper applies a genetic algorithm (GA) to optimise gateway placement for a 60 km² urban area modelled using a 10 m resolution digital surface model of Novi Sad derived from aerial lidar data. Path loss was pre-computed for a grid of 800 candidate gateway positions using the ray-tracing model validated in earlier work. The GA was run with a population of 200 individuals over 500 generations, with the objective of covering 95% of the service area with RSSI above −120 dBm. The algorithm converged to a 7-gateway solution compared with the 10-gateway result from a baseline hexagonal grid plan, achieving the same coverage probability. Sensitivity of the result to gateway height (3 m, 6 m, and 15 m above rooftop) is analysed.

title: Characterisation of LoRa Signal Propagation in a Deep Basement Car Park
abstract: Underground car parks are increasingly equipped with occupancy sensors communicating over LoRaWAN, yet quantitative propagation data for multi-level below-grade reinforced concrete structures is scarce. This paper reports measurements in a three-level underground car park in Novi Sad (total depth 9.5 m) at 868 MHz. A single gateway was placed at street level near the entry ramp. RSSI and SNR were logged at 230 static points across the three levels using Semtech SX1276-based nodes. Median RSSI on the first sub-level was −101 dBm; on the third sub-level it dropped to −127 dBm, just above the SF12 sensitivity threshold of −137 dBm. Floor-to-floor attenuation through 25 cm post-tensioned concrete slabs averaged 22.4 dB. The paper recommends a repeater strategy for reliable coverage below the second sub-level and gives a parametric link budget model for similar structures.

title: LoRa Link Budget Analysis for Water Meter Telemetry in a Dense Urban Area: A Case Study
abstract: This chapter examines the practical link budget constraints encountered when deploying LoRaWAN-based automatic meter reading for water utilities in a densely built urban district. The case study is based on a pilot deployment of 340 end nodes in the Stari Grad neighbourhood of Novi Sad, where meter boxes are located in basement utility cupboards 1.5–2.5 m below street level. The chapter first derives an extended link budget model that accounts for: outdoor urban path loss (measured empirically), building wall penetration loss (14–28 dB depending on construction type), and meter-box cavity shielding (estimated 6–10 dB additional loss). The model is validated against measured delivery rates from the pilot. Results show that SF10 was sufficient for 87% of nodes, while the remaining 13% required SF12 and in some cases external antenna cables. Network dimensioning guidelines are provided for practitioners.

title: Interference Between Co-Located LoRaWAN Networks Operating on the Same Sub-Band: Measurements and Model
abstract: As LoRaWAN adoption grows, multiple independently operated networks increasingly share the same 868 MHz sub-band in urban areas. This paper quantifies the impact of inter-network interference on packet delivery ratio through a controlled experiment in which two separate LoRaWAN networks, each with one gateway and 30 nodes, were co-deployed in a 500 m radius area in Novi Sad. Traffic load was varied from 0.1% to 5% channel occupancy on each network. At 1% occupancy per network, packet delivery ratio degradation was below 2 percentage points; at 5% it reached 11 percentage points for SF7 nodes and 18 percentage points for SF12 nodes. An analytical collision probability model based on LoRa symbol timing and the duty-cycle constraint is presented and shown to match measurements within 2 percentage points across all tested conditions. Practical coexistence guidelines are derived.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications – Regional Workshop Edition

title: Three-Dimensional Ray-Tracing Validation Against Large-Scale LoRa RSSI Measurements in Novi Sad
abstract: Ray-tracing models require careful validation before use in network planning tools. This paper presents a systematic comparison of a 3-D ray-tracing simulator, developed in-house in C++, against 18 500 georeferenced RSSI measurements collected from a 12-gateway LoRaWAN network operating continuously over Novi Sad. Building data were obtained from the geodetic authority of the Republic of Serbia at a cadastral level, supplemented by height estimates derived from a 2020 aerial photogrammetry survey. The simulator considers up to four specular reflections and one diffraction per ray. Over the full dataset, the simulator achieved a root mean square error of 5.8 dB and a mean error of −0.4 dB. Errors were highest in areas with large construction sites where building models lagged physical reality by up to 18 months. A correction procedure using recent satellite imagery to flag stale geometry is described and shown to reduce RMSE by 0.9 dB in affected zones.

title: Dynamic Spreading Factor Reallocation in Multi-Gateway LoRaWAN Networks Under Variable Traffic Density
abstract: Static SF zoning plans become suboptimal when sensor traffic density varies spatially and temporally, as occurs in smart city deployments during events, market days, or emergency response. This preprint describes an iterative reallocation algorithm that runs at the network server, uses per-node delivery ratio statistics from a sliding 24-hour window, and reassigns SFs to minimise total airtime while maintaining delivery ratio above a configurable threshold. The algorithm is evaluated in simulation on a synthetic 600-node network calibrated to Novi Sad street geometry and in a limited field trial with 60 nodes. In simulation, total network airtime decreased by 19% relative to static zoning under uniform traffic and by 31% under a synthetic event scenario concentrating 40% of traffic in 10% of the area. The field trial confirmed an airtime reduction of 17% over a two-week period. Algorithm convergence, update interval sensitivity, and interaction with the 1% duty-cycle limit are discussed.

title: Correspondence between biomechanical upper limb symmetry indices and Fugl-Meyer Assessment scores in chronic stroke: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: The Fugl-Meyer Assessment – Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) is a widely used ordinal scale for post-stroke upper limb motor function, but its granularity may be insufficient for tracking small rehabilitative gains. This cross-sectional study recruited 56 chronic stroke patients (mean time post-stroke 14.3 months, SD 6.1) and simultaneously administered the FMA-UE and a three-dimensional motion capture protocol capturing elbow flexion–extension symmetry, reach velocity ratio, and grip force ratio during a standardised cup-lifting task. Spearman correlations between FMA-UE total score and each biomechanical index ranged from ρ = 0.61 to ρ = 0.74 (all p < 0.001). Ordinal logistic regression confirmed that reach velocity ratio independently predicted FMA-UE severity class (mild/moderate/severe) after controlling for lesion chronicity and handedness. Floor effects of the FMA-UE were observed in 14% of participants, a range where the biomechanical indices continued to differentiate patients. The study provides quantitative support for supplementing ordinal scales with continuous kinematic measures.

title: Comparing NIHSS-derived motor subscore and quantitative balance asymmetry as early predictors of walking independence at hospital discharge
abstract: Early prediction of walking independence at hospital discharge is important for planning post-acute care. This study compared the prognostic utility of the NIHSS motor leg subscore (NIHSS-ML) against a centre-of-pressure (CoP) mediolateral asymmetry index derived from a balance platform assessment in 91 consecutive acute stroke admissions. Both measures were taken within 72 hours of admission. Walking independence at discharge was defined as Functional Ambulation Category (FAC) ≥ 4. Area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.73 (95% CI 0.62–0.83) for NIHSS-ML and 0.80 (95% CI 0.70–0.89) for CoP asymmetry index. Combining both measures increased AUC to 0.85 (95% CI 0.76–0.93). A decision tree using both inputs reached 79% classification accuracy in 10-fold cross-validation. These data suggest that a brief balance platform assessment within the first three days augments the predictive value of the standard neurological examination for planning discharge rehabilitation pathways.

title: Quantitative motor outcome measures in post-stroke rehabilitation: current methods and measurement properties
abstract: This chapter reviews the measurement properties—validity, reliability, responsiveness, and interpretability—of quantitative motor outcome instruments used in post-stroke rehabilitation research and clinical practice. Instruments covered include instrumented walkway systems, force platforms, IMU-based gait analysis, three-dimensional motion capture, and handheld dynamometry. For each instrument category, the chapter summarises available evidence on concurrent validity against clinical scales (Barthel Index, FMA-UE, FAC), test–retest and inter-rater reliability, and minimum clinically important differences where established. Special attention is given to feasibility constraints in routine clinical settings, including cost, space, and operator training requirements. The chapter also addresses the persistent challenge of converting continuous biomechanical indices into clinically interpretable thresholds. Key gaps in the literature, particularly regarding applicability in lower-resourced rehabilitation environments and in patients with severe motor deficits, are identified. Practical recommendations are offered for selecting outcome instruments according to assessment purpose and clinical context.

title: Within-session variability of IMU-derived gait symmetry metrics in post-stroke patients: effect of walking speed and fatigue
abstract: Within-session variability in gait symmetry metrics can obscure genuine rehabilitation-related change. This study examined sources of within-session variability—specifically the effects of walking speed condition and trial order as a proxy for fatigue—in 45 post-stroke community ambulators wearing five IMUs (bilateral shanks, thighs, and lumbar spine) during a structured protocol of six two-minute walks at self-selected, slow, and fast speeds. Mixed-effects models showed that speed condition accounted for 31% of variance in step symmetry ratio (p < 0.001), while trial order (fatigue proxy) explained an additional 8% (p = 0.02). Coefficient of variation for SSR within a single speed condition across repeated trials was 6.4% (95% CI 5.1–7.7%). Standardising to self-selected speed and using the mean of trials two and three reduced within-session variability by 22% compared with a single-trial protocol. These findings have direct implications for standardising measurement protocols in clinical trials of stroke rehabilitation.

title: Responsiveness of gait symmetry indices versus the 10-metre walk test and Barthel Index in inpatient stroke rehabilitation: a longitudinal observational study
abstract: Responsiveness—the ability to detect genuine change—is a critical measurement property for rehabilitation outcome instruments. This longitudinal study measured 68 stroke inpatients at admission, two weeks, and four weeks using the 10-Metre Walk Test (10MWT), Barthel Index (BI), and an IMU-based step symmetry ratio (SSR). Standardised response means (SRM) at the two-to-four-week interval were 0.61 for 10MWT, 0.54 for BI, and 0.79 for SSR. Effect sizes followed a similar pattern. In a subgroup of 24 patients classified as plateau cases by physiotherapists (no visible functional change), SSR detected statistically significant within-group change at the four-week time point (mean ΔSSR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01–0.11, p = 0.03), whereas BI and 10MWT did not. These data suggest that continuous biomechanical symmetry metrics may be more responsive to rehabilitation-induced motor change than the currently most used ordinal and functional walk tests, particularly in patients with moderate deficits.

title: Agreement between patient-reported difficulty and biomechanical symmetry deficit during stair climbing in stroke survivors: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Patient-reported outcome measures and biomechanical assessments capture different aspects of post-stroke motor impairment, and their agreement is not well characterised for specific tasks such as stair climbing. This cross-sectional study enrolled 49 stroke survivors (mean 9.6 months post-stroke) who completed the Stroke-Specific Quality of Life mobility subscale (SS-QOL-M) and an instrumented stair-climbing protocol using bilateral pressure insoles and bilateral shank IMUs. Kinematic and kinetic symmetry indices for push-off impulse, step time, and knee flexion were computed. SS-QOL-M correlated moderately with push-off impulse symmetry (ρ = −0.53, p < 0.001) and step time symmetry (ρ = −0.49, p < 0.001), but weakly with knee flexion symmetry (ρ = −0.31, p = 0.03). Fourteen participants reported minimal difficulty despite substantial push-off asymmetry (>20%), representing a compensatory adaptation pattern. These divergences between subjective report and objective mechanics have implications for selecting endpoints in rehabilitation trials targeting stair-climbing independence.

title: Derivation and preliminary validation of a composite biomechanical motor symmetry score for post-stroke rehabilitation monitoring
abstract: Rehabilitation clinicians and researchers typically assess multiple biomechanical dimensions of motor recovery separately, limiting comparability across patients and studies. This study describes the derivation of a composite Biomechanical Motor Symmetry Score (BMSS) integrating four standardised, unit-normalised sub-scores: step time symmetry, push-off impulse symmetry, upper limb reach velocity symmetry, and postural sway symmetry. Sub-score weights were initially equal; calibration was performed in a derivation sample of 82 stroke patients using partial least squares regression against concurrent FMA-UE and BI scores. Cross-validation in a separate 41-patient sample showed BMSS correlated with FMA-UE at r = 0.72 and with BI at r = 0.68 (both p < 0.001). BMSS demonstrated greater sensitivity to change over a four-week inpatient programme (SRM 0.84) than any individual sub-score (range 0.61–0.79). The BMSS framework is intentionally sensor-agnostic, with the intent to support future standardisation across clinical sites and device types.

title: Feasibility of a home-based IMU gait monitoring protocol in stroke survivors: adherence, data quality, and patient experience
abstract: Extending biomechanical motor assessment beyond supervised clinical settings requires understanding whether stroke survivors can reliably use wearable sensors at home. This mixed-methods feasibility study provided 28 community-dwelling stroke survivors with a single lumbar-mounted IMU and a companion smartphone application for daily two-minute walks over six weeks. Primary feasibility outcomes were adherence (proportion of scheduled sessions completed), data quality (proportion of sessions yielding ≥90% valid strides), and patient-reported experience (structured interview). Mean adherence was 74% (SD 18%), and 81% of completed sessions yielded sufficient data quality. Interview analysis identified three main barriers: device donning difficulty, application interface complexity, and concern about walking safety without a companion. Step symmetry ratio showed longitudinal trajectories consistent with expected subacute recovery patterns. These results support the feasibility of home-based IMU monitoring while identifying specific design requirements for device and application development aimed at this population.

title: Minimum clinically important difference for the Biomechanical Motor Symmetry Score in subacute stroke inpatients: an anchor-based and distribution-based analysis
abstract: The Biomechanical Motor Symmetry Score (BMSS) has shown validity and responsiveness in prior work, but its minimum clinically important difference (MCID) has not been established. This study enrolled 96 subacute stroke inpatients and assessed them at admission and four-week discharge. MCID was estimated using two anchor-based methods—patient global impression of change (PGIC) and clinician-rated global change—and three distribution-based methods: half standard deviation, standard error of measurement, and one-third interquartile range. PGIC-anchored MCID was 0.12 BMSS units (95% CI 0.09–0.16); clinician-anchored MCID was 0.11 (95% CI 0.08–0.14). Distribution-based estimates ranged from 0.09 to 0.14. Convergence across methods supports an MCID of approximately 0.11–0.12 BMSS units as a practical threshold for interpreting individual patient change. This estimate can inform sample size calculations in future rehabilitation trials using BMSS as a primary or secondary endpoint.

title: Električna svojstva kortikalne šireće depresije indukovane kalijum hloridom kod pacova Wistar soja: pilot studija
abstract: Kortikalna šireća depresija (KŠD) indukovana je topikalnom primenom 1 M kalijum hlorida na parijetalni korteks 12 odraslih pacova Wistar soja pod uretanskom anestezijom. Višeelektrodnim zapisima DC potencijala praćena je brzina propagacije talasa negativnog jednosmernog pomaka duž fronto-okcipitalne ose. Izmerena srednja brzina iznosila je 3,1 ± 0,4 mm/min, što je konzistentno sa literaturnim podacima za ovaj soj, dok je amplituda negativnog DC pomaka u proseku iznosila −18,7 mV. Trajanje perioda supresije bioelektrične aktivnosti korikovalo je sa distancom od mesta indukcije (r = 0,67, p < 0,01). Rezultati potvrđuju pouzdanost primenjenog protokola za dalja ispitivanja farmakoloških modulatora KŠD u ovom laboratorijskom postavljanju.

title: Propagation asymmetry of cortical spreading depression across the homotopic callosal axis: evidence from bilateral multielectrode recordings in rats
abstract: Whether CSD crosses callosal fibres to initiate contralateral events has been debated for decades. We implanted bilateral six-electrode arrays spanning parietal and occipital cortex in eleven Sprague-Dawley rats and induced unilateral CSD by cortical pin-prick. Of 63 unilateral CSD episodes recorded, contralateral spread occurred in 12 (19%), exclusively when the ipsilateral episode was of high amplitude (DC shift > 22 mV) and long duration (> 70 s). In contrast, low-amplitude episodes never propagated contralaterally (0/31). When contralateral transfer occurred, it appeared on the contralateral array at a delay of 8.4 ± 2.1 s, suggesting a subcortical relay rather than direct transcallosal diffusion. Corpus callosum transection (n = 5) abolished contralateral events entirely, confirming callosal dependence. These findings may be relevant to the minority of migraine patients who report bilateral simultaneous aura.

title: Shoot elongation and leaf area responses of Potamogeton perfoliatus to turbidity gradients in a shallow Pannonian lake
abstract: We measured morphological traits of Potamogeton perfoliatus along naturally occurring turbidity gradients in Lake Palić, Serbia, during the growing seasons of 2009 and 2010. Shoot elongation, internode length, specific leaf area, and chlorophyll a:b ratios were quantified at 12 sites spanning Secchi depths of 0.3–1.8 m. Plants at low-light sites (Secchi depth < 0.6 m) showed 34% greater shoot elongation and 28% higher specific leaf area compared with high-transparency sites, consistent with shade-avoidance morphology. Chlorophyll a:b ratios declined significantly with increasing turbidity (R² = 0.71, p < 0.001). Total phosphorus and suspended solids explained 61% of variance in turbidity across sites. The results indicate that even moderate eutrophication-driven turbidity elicits measurable morphological adjustment in this species, with implications for biomass production estimates used in habitat assessment.

title: Pigment composition of Myriophyllum spicatum under experimentally elevated phosphorus loads: a mesocosm study
abstract: Using outdoor mesocosm tanks (1,000 L, n = 24), we exposed Myriophyllum spicatum to four phosphorus concentration treatments (20, 100, 300, and 600 µg TP L⁻¹) over eight weeks during summer 2012. Photosynthetic pigments were extracted and quantified by HPLC at two-week intervals. Total chlorophyll content decreased by 41% at the highest phosphorus treatment compared with the control, while carotenoid-to-chlorophyll ratios increased by 1.6-fold, suggesting oxidative stress. Zeaxanthin accumulated progressively in treatments above 100 µg TP L⁻¹, implying enhanced photoprotection. Neoxanthin and lutein concentrations were relatively stable across treatments. Plant dry mass was significantly reduced only in the 600 µg TP L⁻¹ treatment after week six. These findings demonstrate that pigment remodelling precedes detectable growth suppression and may serve as an early biochemical indicator of eutrophication stress in submerged macrophytes.

title: Seasonal dynamics of macrophyte community structure in relation to nutrient loading in three shallow lakes of Vojvodina
abstract: Submerged macrophyte communities were surveyed in Lakes Ludoš, Rusanda, and Okanj Bara (Vojvodina, Serbia) in spring, summer, and autumn of 2013 and 2014. Percent cover, species richness, and biomass were recorded at permanent transects; water chemistry was monitored monthly. Total phosphorus ranged from 78 µg L⁻¹ at Okanj Bara to 540 µg L⁻¹ at Rusanda. Species richness declined significantly with increasing TP (Spearman ρ = −0.82). Ceratophyllum demersum dominated the most eutrophic lake with near-monospecific stands by summer 2014. Canonical correspondence analysis identified TP, turbidity, and conductivity as primary drivers of community composition, collectively explaining 54% of variability. Seasonal biomass peaked in July across all lakes regardless of trophic state, but peak values varied threefold between the least and most eutrophic systems. The dataset contributes baseline information for conservation management of Pannonian lake habitats listed under Natura 2000.

title: Light-use efficiency and photoinhibition in Ceratophyllum demersum across a eutrophication gradient: rapid light curves and Fv/Fm measurements
abstract: Pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM) fluorometry was applied to Ceratophyllum demersum sampled from 18 sites in Vojvodina shallow lakes covering a total phosphorus range of 50–620 µg L⁻¹. Rapid light curves generated maximum electron transport rates (rETRmax) and light saturation coefficients (Ek). rETRmax declined from 98 µmol electrons m⁻² s⁻¹ at oligotrophic sites to 41 µmol electrons m⁻² s⁻¹ at hypereutrophic sites, while Ek decreased from 210 to 87 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹. Fv/Fm was significantly lower at hypereutrophic sites (mean 0.61 vs. 0.79, p < 0.001), indicating chronic photoinhibition despite low ambient light. Pre-dawn Fv/Fm recovery measurements suggested incomplete overnight repair at the most turbid sites. Non-photochemical quenching was paradoxically elevated in high-turbidity plants, possibly reflecting constitutive photoprotective upregulation. Results are discussed in the context of threshold TP concentrations beyond which photosynthetic performance collapses.

title: Transcriptome profiling of Najas marina under combined nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment: identification of differentially expressed genes involved in light harvesting and carbon fixation
abstract: We performed RNA-seq analysis on Najas marina plants exposed to ambient (control), N-enriched, P-enriched, and N+P-enriched mesocosm conditions for four weeks. Libraries were sequenced on an Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform (150 bp paired-end; ~45 million reads per sample, n = 4 biological replicates per treatment). De novo transcriptome assembly using Trinity yielded 98,412 unigenes, of which 61% were annotated against the UniProt database. Differential expression analysis (DESeq2, FDR < 0.05) identified 2,847 significantly differentially expressed genes between the N+P treatment and the control. Downregulated genes were enriched in light-harvesting complex II (LHCII) subunit transcripts and RuBisCO small subunit genes. Upregulated genes included multiple glutamine synthetase isoforms and heat-shock proteins. The combined N+P treatment produced a larger transcriptomic response than either nutrient alone. These results provide a gene-level framework for understanding macrophyte photosynthetic decline under eutrophication.

title: Morphometric variation in Potamogeton pectinatus leaf anatomy as a function of dissolved inorganic nitrogen concentration: a common-garden experiment
abstract: Potamogeton pectinatus plants clonally propagated from a single genotype were grown in controlled-environment tanks at five dissolved inorganic nitrogen (DIN) concentrations (0.1, 0.5, 2, 8, and 20 mg N L⁻¹) with phosphorus held constant at 50 µg L⁻¹. After six weeks, leaf cross-sections were prepared and imaged with light microscopy. Lacunal area fraction, epidermis cell thickness, mesophyll cell density, and bundle sheath cross-sectional area were measured on 20 leaves per treatment. Lacunal area fraction increased significantly at DIN above 2 mg L⁻¹ (ANOVA, p = 0.002), while epidermis cell thickness decreased by 18% from lowest to highest DIN treatment. Bundle sheath cross-sectional area showed a non-linear response peaking at 2 mg N L⁻¹. These results indicate that nitrogen availability modulates internal anatomy in P. pectinatus independently of light, with potential consequences for gas exchange capacity and plant buoyancy regulation.

title: Long-term trends in submerged macrophyte distribution in Lake Palić: a retrospective analysis using historical records and current surveys
abstract: Historical vegetation maps, aerial photographs (1952–2005), and survey data from 1978, 1991, and 2003 were digitised and compared with a systematic transect survey conducted in 2017. Total cover of submerged macrophytes declined from approximately 68% of lake area in 1978 to 9% in 2017. Regression against concurrent water quality records showed that the sharp decline after 1988 coincided with TP exceeding 200 µg L⁻¹. Charophyte meadows, documented extensively in 1978, had disappeared entirely by 2003 and were not detected in 2017. Potamogeton species declined from seven to two between 1991 and 2017. Partial recolonisation of marginal zones by Ceratophyllum demersum was observed near an inlet restored in 2013. The study quantifies a 49-year trajectory of macrophyte loss attributable to progressive eutrophication and offers spatially explicit reference conditions for lake restoration planning.

title: Comparative transcriptomics of three Potamogeton species with contrasting eutrophication tolerances
abstract: RNA-seq was performed on Potamogeton crispus, Potamogeton perfoliatus, and Potamogeton pusillus grown in identical mesocosm conditions at 400 µg TP L⁻¹ and 50 µg TP L⁻¹. Each species was sequenced with four biological replicates (~50 million 150 bp paired-end reads). Species-specific de novo assemblies were generated, and one-to-one orthologues were identified across the three transcriptomes using OrthoFinder. The number of differentially expressed orthologs at high TP differed substantially: P. crispus (most tolerant in field surveys) showed 891 DEGs; P. perfoliatus showed 1,843 DEGs; P. pusillus (least tolerant) showed 3,207 DEGs. Photosystem II repair genes were upregulated in all three species at high TP, but anthocyanin biosynthesis genes were uniquely upregulated in P. crispus. Antioxidant enzyme gene families showed species-specific copy number variation correlated with tolerance ranking. The comparative framework identifies candidate gene families for physiological tolerance to eutrophication in submerged macrophytes.

title: Interactions between epiphyte load and light acclimation in submerged macrophytes: evidence from reciprocal transplant experiments in Vojvodina lakes
abstract: Reciprocal transplant cages were deployed in paired high-epiphyte (HE) and low-epiphyte (LE) microsites at six shallow lakes in Vojvodina during summer 2021. Potamogeton perfoliatus shoots were transferred between HE and LE microsites and held for four weeks alongside controls left in their original microsite. At harvest, PAM fluorometry, shoot elongation, and specific leaf area were measured; epiphyte dry mass was quantified after scraping. Transplants moved to HE sites showed significant decreases in Fv/Fm (mean 0.07 reduction) and increases in shoot elongation (mean 12%) within two weeks. Transplants moved to LE sites partially reversed these responses within four weeks. Multiple regression confirmed that epiphyte-mediated light attenuation (measured as photosynthetically active radiation immediately above and below epiphyte layer) explained 68% of Fv/Fm variability, independent of water column turbidity. The study demonstrates that epiphyte-driven shading operates as a distinct and reversible driver of macrophyte photophysiology alongside eutrophication-driven turbidity.

title: Methodological considerations for RNA extraction from field-collected submerged macrophytes: a comparison of five protocols
abstract: RNA quality from field-collected macrophytes is frequently compromised by polysaccharides and polyphenolics that co-precipitate with nucleic acids. We tested five extraction protocols on Potamogeton perfoliatus and Najas marina collected from three lakes in Vojvodina, evaluating RNA integrity number (RIN), A260/A280 ratio, yield, and downstream RT-qPCR performance. Protocols tested included CTAB-based, LiCl-precipitation, silica-column commercial kits, and two modified CTAB variants differing in β-mercaptoethanol concentration. The modified CTAB protocol with 4% β-mercaptoethanol and a PVP-40 wash step yielded mean RIN values of 7.8 for both species, compared with 4.1–6.3 for the other protocols. RT-qPCR efficiency using reference genes (EF1α and UBQ10) was significantly higher from the modified CTAB protocol. We provide a detailed step-by-step protocol optimised for carbohydrate-rich aquatic macrophyte tissue and discuss its applicability to other submerged species. This technical note is intended to reduce a common bottleneck in macrophyte molecular ecology studies.

title: Diurnal variation in transcript abundance of light-harvesting and photoprotection genes in Potamogeton perfoliatus under turbid versus clear-water conditions
abstract: We sampled Potamogeton perfoliatus shoots at 06:00, 10:00, 14:00, 18:00, and 22:00 local time from a turbid (Secchi depth 0.35 m) and a clear-water (Secchi depth 1.65 m) site in Lake Palić during three cloudless days in July 2023. Total RNA was extracted immediately after sampling, and RT-qPCR was performed for 18 target genes including LHCII subunits, PsbA (D1 protein), zeaxanthin epoxidase, PsbS, and violaxanthin de-epoxidase. In clear-water plants, transcripts of PsbA and LHCII subunits peaked at 10:00 and declined by 14:00, consistent with photoinhibitory downregulation at midday. In turbid-site plants, PsbA transcripts remained elevated throughout daylight hours, and PsbS expression was constitutively high across all time points sampled. Zeaxanthin cycle gene expression showed reduced amplitude in turbid-site plants. These diurnal expression patterns suggest that chronic low-light stress from turbidity produces constitutive rather than dynamic regulation of photoprotective and repair machinery, adding a temporal dimension to previous comparative transcriptomic findings.

title: Macrophyte-based trophic state indices for Pannonian shallow lakes: calibration against measured water chemistry across 47 sites
abstract: We compiled macrophyte survey data from 47 shallow lake sites across Vojvodina and the adjacent Bačka and Banat regions, pairing species composition and abundance records with concurrent measurements of total phosphorus, total nitrogen, chlorophyll a, and Secchi depth. Four existing macrophyte-based trophic state indices developed for Central European lakes (MTI-CE, MPhyI, AMPI, and MAI-Danubian) were calculated for each site and evaluated against measured TP as a reference variable using Spearman rank correlation, RMSE, and the ability to distinguish Water Framework Directive ecological quality classes. MTI-CE performed best overall (ρ = 0.76), but misclassified 14 sites in the hypereutrophic range. A revised index calibrated specifically to Pannonian alkaline shallow lakes improved Spearman ρ to 0.83 and reduced RMSE by 22%. The revised index assigns higher indicator weight to Charophyte presence/absence and penalises Ceratophyllum-dominated sites more heavily than existing indices. Regional calibration data and scoring tables are provided as supplementary material.

title: Suture anchor pullout force in human cadaveric linea alba: effect of needle size and knot technique
abstract: Failure at the suture–fascia interface is a recognised mechanism of incisional hernia recurrence. We used eleven fresh-frozen human cadaveric abdominal wall specimens to measure the pullout force of interrupted sutures placed in the linea alba using three needle gauges (2-0, 0, and 1 Prolene) and two knot configurations (square and surgeon's knot). A materials testing machine applied load perpendicular to the fascial plane at 5 mm/min. Mean pullout force ranged from 34.7 N (2-0, square knot) to 61.2 N (1, surgeon's knot). Specimen age and fascial thickness correlated positively with pullout force (r = 0.61 and r = 0.74, respectively). No statistically significant difference was found between knot types at equivalent suture calibre after correction for fascial thickness. These findings support selecting larger-calibre sutures in patients with thin or atrophic linea alba.

title: Collagen type I to type III ratio in the scar tissue of recurrent versus primary incisional hernia: a case–control study
abstract: Altered collagen composition has been proposed as a factor predisposing patients to hernia recurrence. We obtained fascial biopsy specimens from 42 patients undergoing repair: 21 with a first recurrence after prior open repair and 21 undergoing primary repair. Immunohistochemistry with anti-collagen I and anti-collagen III antibodies was performed on paraffin-embedded sections; collagen ratios were calculated by digital image analysis. The mean collagen I/III ratio was 2.1 ± 0.4 in primary hernia scar versus 1.4 ± 0.3 in recurrent hernia scar (p < 0.001). Matrix metalloproteinase-1 immunoreactivity was significantly higher in the recurrent group (semi-quantitative score 2.3 vs. 1.1, p = 0.002). Patient age, BMI, and diabetes status did not differ between groups. These results indicate that excessive type III collagen deposition and elevated MMP-1 activity characterise the scar environment of recurrent incisional hernia and may contribute to mechanical insufficiency.

title: Finite element simulation of abdominal wall mechanics during coughing: effect of mesh size and overlap distance
abstract: Determining optimal mesh overlap in incisional hernia repair is largely empirical. We constructed a patient-specific finite element model of the anterior abdominal wall from CT data of one male volunteer, discretised with 18,400 hexahedral elements, and assigned hyperelastic material properties derived from published ex vivo tensile data. Simulated cough-induced intra-abdominal pressure of 120 mmHg was applied as a boundary condition. Three mesh sizes (5 × 5, 8 × 8, and 10 × 10 cm) with overlap distances of 2, 4, and 6 cm on a 4 cm fascial defect were compared. Peak von Mises stress at the mesh–tissue interface decreased by 42% when overlap increased from 2 to 4 cm but only by a further 9% from 4 to 6 cm, suggesting diminishing returns beyond 4 cm. Mesh size influenced stress distribution at the lateral margins, supporting selection of 10 × 10 cm mesh for defects wider than 3 cm.

title: Risk factors for incisional hernia recurrence within five years of open repair: a retrospective cohort of 318 patients
abstract: Recurrence after open incisional hernia repair remains a significant clinical problem with reported rates of 10–30% at five years. We reviewed records of 318 consecutive patients who underwent open repair with mesh at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2010 and 2016. Recurrence was confirmed by clinical examination or ultrasound. The five-year recurrence rate was 14.2% (n = 45). Multivariable Cox regression identified BMI > 30 (HR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3–4.4), fascial defect width > 6 cm (HR 3.1, 95% CI 1.7–5.7), and surgical site infection within 30 days (HR 4.6, 95% CI 2.5–8.5) as independent predictors. Mesh overlap of ≥ 4 cm was protective (HR 0.5, 95% CI 0.3–0.9). Suture material and fixation technique were not independently associated with recurrence after adjustment. These data support preoperative optimisation of BMI and strict infection prevention as priorities in reducing recurrence.

title: Abdominal wall mechanics after components separation: a cadaveric pressure–strain study
abstract: Components separation technique restores midline continuity in large incisional hernias but its effect on regional wall mechanics is poorly quantified. We used eight fresh cadaveric abdominal preparations to measure strain distribution across the anterior wall using digital image correlation (DIC) at intra-abdominal pressures of 0, 5, 15, and 30 mmHg before and after bilateral external oblique release. After release, peak principal strain in the lateral abdominal wall increased by 28% at 30 mmHg compared with the intact state, while midline strain decreased by 41%. Rectus abdominis displacement was reduced by a mean of 4.1 mm ± 0.9 per side at 30 mmHg following release. These mechanical changes indicate that external oblique release significantly redistributes wall tension and that strain concentration shifts laterally, which may be relevant for planning mesh reinforcement in large repairs.

title: Mesh pore architecture and its relation to fibrovascular ingrowth: a morphometric analysis of nine commercial meshes after implantation in rabbits
abstract: Pore geometry is considered a determinant of mesh integration quality. Nine commercially distributed polypropylene and polyester meshes with pore sizes ranging from 0.8 to 4.2 mm² were implanted in the abdominal wall of 54 New Zealand White rabbits (6 per mesh type). Explants at 90 days were stained with Masson's trichrome and haematoxylin-eosin; fibrovascular ingrowth fraction, inflammatory cell density, and bridging fibrosis index were quantified by morphometry. Meshes with pore areas between 2.0 and 3.5 mm² showed the highest fibrovascular ingrowth fractions (mean 61–68%) and the lowest bridging fibrosis scores. Meshes with pore areas below 1.0 mm² had significantly higher macrophage density (p < 0.01) and near-complete bridging fibrosis. Maximum mesh tensile retention correlated moderately with fibrovascular ingrowth fraction (r = 0.57). These data provide quantitative support for preferring large-pore meshes in open repair.

title: TGF-β1 and CTGF serum levels as candidate biomarkers of hernia recurrence after open mesh repair
abstract: Systemic markers of fibrotic activity might predict patients at high risk of recurrence after hernia repair. We measured serum TGF-β1 and connective tissue growth factor (CTGF) in 78 patients at baseline (preoperative) and at 1, 3, and 12 months after open sublay repair. Twenty-three patients developed recurrence within 36 months. Preoperative TGF-β1 did not differ between groups; however, CTGF at 3 months was significantly elevated in patients who subsequently recurred (median 312 pg/mL vs. 198 pg/mL, p = 0.008). A combined model using CTGF at 3 months and fascial defect width achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.78 (95% CI 0.67–0.89) for recurrence prediction at 36 months. These findings are preliminary and require validation in an independent cohort, but suggest that early postoperative CTGF monitoring may identify candidates for closer surveillance.

title: Passive drag estimation in recreational masters swimmers aged 40–70 years using an instrumented tow-line protocol
abstract: This study quantified passive drag forces in 48 masters swimmers (24 women, 24 men) distributed across four age decades (40–49, 50–59, 60–69 years) plus a young-adult control group (20–29 years). Participants were towed at three fixed speeds (1.0, 1.3, and 1.6 m/s) in a standardised streamlined position using a motorised tow-line system equipped with a calibrated inline load cell sampling at 200 Hz. Body morphology variables (body mass, height, frontal surface area estimated from digital photographs) were recorded. Passive drag increased significantly with age at all three speeds after controlling for body mass and frontal area. At 1.3 m/s, mean drag in the 60–69 group exceeded that of the young-adult group by 18.4 ± 5.1 N (p < 0.001). A multiple regression model including age, frontal area, and body mass index explained 64% of the variance in drag at 1.3 m/s. Results suggest age-related changes in resting body position and tissue distribution meaningfully increase hydrodynamic resistance independent of active propulsion.

title: Age-related changes in arm-leg coordination index during front crawl in masters swimmers: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: Inter-limb coordination in front crawl swimming was assessed using the Index of Coordination (IdC) in 62 masters swimmers (age range 40–74 years) and 18 competitive young adults (21–29 years). Participants completed two 25-metre trials at self-selected race pace. Stroke cycles were filmed with two synchronised underwater cameras at 50 Hz, and IdC was computed from hand entry and exit events for 10 consecutive stroke cycles per trial. Mean IdC decreased progressively with age group, shifting from a small catch-up pattern in younger masters toward a more pronounced catch-up coordination in the oldest group (60–74 years: mean IdC = −9.3 ± 3.7 compared to −3.1 ± 2.4 in the 40–49 group). Stroke rate declined and stroke length shortened with age. Intra-individual variability of IdC, measured as within-trial coefficient of variation, increased significantly in the oldest cohort. Findings indicate a progressive loss of coordination precision and a trend toward less propulsive overlap between arm strokes as masters swimmers age.

title: Shoulder and hip muscle activation asymmetry during continuous front crawl in masters swimmers: an sEMG pilot study
abstract: Surface electromyography was used to compare bilateral muscle activation patterns in 16 masters swimmers (50–65 years) and 10 young adult swimmers during a 4-minute continuous front crawl bout at moderate intensity. Eight muscles were monitored bilaterally: deltoid anterior, deltoid posterior, triceps brachii, biceps brachii, external oblique, erector spinae, gluteus medius, and rectus femoris. Signals were normalised to maximal voluntary contractions recorded prior to swimming. Asymmetry was quantified using a symmetry index. Masters swimmers exhibited significantly higher bilateral asymmetry indices in deltoid anterior (asymmetry index: 17.2 ± 6.3% vs 8.9 ± 3.1%, p = 0.003) and gluteus medius activation (21.4 ± 8.0% vs 11.3 ± 4.5%, p = 0.007). Asymmetry in shoulder muscles was moderately correlated with IdC variability (r = 0.54, p = 0.031). The pilot character of the study limits generalisation, and a larger sample is planned. These early results suggest that neuromuscular asymmetry may contribute to coordination instability observed in older swimmers.

title: Prospective injury surveillance in two Serbian sub-elite football leagues over one competitive season
abstract: Epidemiological data on injuries in Serbian sub-elite football are scarce. This prospective cohort study tracked 214 male outfield players across two regional leagues over a full 34-week competitive season using the UEFA injury report consensus methodology. Team medical staff recorded 178 time-loss injuries, yielding an overall incidence of 6.4 injuries per 1000 player-hours (match incidence 24.1, training incidence 3.2). Muscle injuries of the thigh were most common (31% of all injuries), followed by lateral ankle sprains (18%). Defenders and forwards showed higher match-injury incidence than midfielders. Players who had sustained a hamstring injury in the previous season had a 2.7-fold elevated risk of recurrence. The study provides baseline epidemiological data applicable to injury prevention programme planning in Serbian regional football and highlights the need for structured post-injury rehabilitation pathways in clubs with limited medical personnel.
