title: Encoding Product Attributes for Cold-Start Item Recommendation in a Grocery Context
abstract: When a new product enters a retail catalogue with no purchase history, collaborative signals are entirely absent. This study investigates how structured product attribute data—category hierarchy, price tier, packaging size, and supplier origin—can be encoded into feature vectors to support immediate recommendation of new items. Experiments are conducted on a dataset of 412 SKUs from a single independent grocery retailer in Vojvodina, with transactions spanning 14 months and covering 3,840 distinct customers. Attribute vectors are constructed using one-hot encoding for categorical fields and min-max normalisation for continuous fields. Cosine similarity between attribute vectors is used to rank candidate new items against items with established purchase histories. The approach achieves a mean reciprocal rank of 0.31 on a held-out set of 28 newly introduced products, compared to 0.19 for a random baseline and 0.27 for a frequency-only heuristic. Limitations related to attribute completeness and supplier data availability are discussed.

title: Matrix Factorization Under Extreme Sparsity: Behaviour and Failure Modes in Datasets Below 0.5% Density
abstract: Matrix factorization methods are widely applied in recommendation research but are understood to degrade under high sparsity. This paper systematically examines that degradation by constructing synthetic user–item matrices at densities from 5% down to 0.1%, seeded from a real transaction log of a home-goods retailer with 620 users and 380 products. Alternating least squares and stochastic gradient descent variants of non-negative matrix factorization are evaluated alongside a probabilistic latent semantic analysis baseline. Root mean squared error and hit rate at ten are tracked across density levels. Both factorization approaches show relatively stable performance down to approximately 1% density, after which error increases non-linearly and hit rate drops below the non-personalised popularity baseline at 0.3% density. The findings provide empirical thresholds useful for practitioners deciding when to fall back to content-based or hybrid alternatives rather than relying on collaborative decomposition.

title: Hybrid Recommendation for New Users in Small Retail: A Two-Stage Architecture Using Demographic Proxies and Early Purchase Signals
abstract: The new-user cold-start problem is addressed with a two-stage architecture. In the first stage, demographic proxy features collected at registration—age group, postal region, and loyalty card tier—are used to assign a new user to one of eight pre-computed customer segments derived by k-means clustering on historical purchasers. Segment-level popularity rankings initialise the recommendation list. In the second stage, as soon as the user completes at least two transactions, item-level collaborative signals begin to replace segment defaults through a blending function that shifts weight gradually over the first ten interactions. Experiments use a dataset from a regional pharmacy chain operating twelve outlets in Vojvodina, with 5,400 registered users and 14 months of transaction records. The two-stage model achieves a recall at five of 0.44 for users with two to five transactions, compared to 0.36 for pure segment-level recommendation and 0.28 for global popularity. Transition dynamics and sensitivity to segment granularity are analysed in detail.

title: Knowledge Graph Embeddings as Item Feature Representations in Cold-Start Retail Recommendation
abstract: This paper investigates whether knowledge graph embeddings constructed from a product ontology can substitute for hand-crafted attribute vectors in cold-start recommendation, with the goal of reducing reliance on manual feature engineering. A product knowledge graph is built for a mixed-category retailer covering 890 SKUs, linking items through category membership, brand relationships, compatible-use associations, and price tier proximity. TransE and RotatE embedding methods are applied to produce 64-dimensional item vectors. These embeddings replace the manually coded attribute vectors in a previously validated cosine similarity pipeline. On a held-out evaluation covering 55 items introduced during the study period, RotatE-derived embeddings achieve a precision at five of 0.41, compared to 0.39 for manual attribute vectors and 0.33 for TransE embeddings. The marginal gain is modest but the approach requires substantially less manual curation effort. Limitations related to ontology construction time and update frequency are considered.

title: Benchmarking Hybrid Recommender Architectures on a Shared Small-Retail Dataset: Protocol and Baseline Results
abstract: Reproducibility in small-retail recommendation research is hampered by the absence of shared, well-documented benchmark datasets. This paper describes the construction and release of a curated anonymised transaction dataset drawn from five independent retailers in Serbia and Hungary, covering a combined 21,000 baskets, 1,200 unique customers, and 2,100 products across grocery, household, and personal care categories. A preprocessing protocol is specified, including rules for temporal train-test split, treatment of single-purchase users, and handling of product discontinuations. Four baseline architectures are evaluated under this protocol: global popularity, pure content-based cosine similarity, item-based kNN collaborative filtering, and a simple linear hybrid of the latter two. Results are reported for precision, recall, and F1 at ranks three, five, and ten. The dataset and evaluation code are released under a permissive open data licence to facilitate comparison in future work.

title: Temporal Drift in Product Relevance: Adjusting Content-Behavioural Hybrid Weights Over a Seasonal Retail Cycle
abstract: Recommendation systems trained on annual data implicitly average over seasonal variation in purchase patterns. This paper examines how optimal hybrid weighting between content-based and collaborative signals shifts across the four quarters of a retail year in a small sports-equipment retailer. Monthly transaction snapshots are drawn from a 26-month log covering 780 customers and 510 SKUs. For each month, a grid search identifies the content-to-collaborative weight that maximises normalised discounted cumulative gain on a one-week-ahead evaluation window. Results show that content-based signals are most informative in months when new season products are introduced—typically March and September—when collaborative history for new items is absent. Collaborative signals recover predictive weight within six to eight weeks of product introduction as purchase history accumulates. A simple adaptive schedule that shifts weights by calendar quarter, rather than per month, captures most of this gain with lower implementation complexity.
venue: Central European Journal of Information Systems and Data Science

title: Cross-Retailer Transfer of Item Embeddings to Address Catalogue Cold-Start: Feasibility and Boundary Conditions
abstract: Training item embeddings from scratch requires a sufficient volume of interactions, which individual small retailers often cannot provide. This paper investigates whether item embeddings trained on a source retailer with denser transaction data can be transferred to a target retailer sharing a partial product catalogue overlap. Transfer is implemented by aligning shared SKU vectors from a source embedding space to the target space using a linear mapping estimated on the overlapping items. Experiments use two real retailer datasets sharing approximately 30% SKU overlap; source data contains 48,000 baskets, target data contains 6,200 baskets. Transferred embeddings are evaluated in a cold-start scenario where 20% of target items have no transactions. Transferred embeddings yield a precision at five of 0.36 compared to 0.28 for attribute-only content vectors and 0.40 for full in-domain training (where available as an oracle). Performance degrades when SKU overlap falls below 15%, establishing a practical lower bound for transfer applicability.

title: Kernel-Based Alignment of Heterogeneous Sensor Streams for Fault Classification in Continuous Casting
abstract: This work addresses the challenge of combining measurements from sensors with fundamentally different sampling rates in a continuous steel-casting environment. A composite kernel constructed from radial basis functions and string kernels over event logs was used to embed synchronized and asynchronous streams into a shared feature space. Experiments were conducted on a dataset of 14 months of operation from a plant in Vojvodina, comprising 37 sensors and 1,840 labelled fault episodes across six fault categories. A support vector machine trained on the composite kernel representation achieved a macro-averaged F1 of 0.81 on held-out data, compared with 0.67 for a baseline that simply forward-filled missing values before training a linear classifier. The study also evaluated sensitivity to kernel bandwidth hyperparameters and found the composite approach substantially more robust. Results suggest that explicit modelling of stream asynchrony at the representation stage is preferable to imputation-then-classify pipelines for industrial fault classification tasks.

title: Missing-Data Patterns in Wireless Sensor Networks on Production Floors: A Taxonomy and Statistical Characterisation
abstract: Wireless sensor deployments in manufacturing environments exhibit missing data that is structurally different from the missing-at-random assumption common in the statistical literature. This paper analyses logs from three production floor deployments in Serbia and one in Hungary, totalling 22 sensor nodes monitored over periods between four and eighteen months. Missing observations were categorised into six pattern types based on their temporal autocorrelation, burst length distribution, and correlation with operating-mode transitions. For each type, parametric families—including zero-inflated negative binomial and Markov-modulated Bernoulli processes—were fitted and assessed by Akaike information criterion. The resulting taxonomy provides a principled basis for selecting simulation models in benchmark studies and for designing imputation or masking strategies in downstream learning algorithms. Annotated datasets for two of the four deployments are released alongside the paper. The work does not propose a new imputation method but provides empirical grounding for future method development.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Interpolation Strategies for Irregularly Sampled Process Variables Prior to Neural Network Training
abstract: Training feedforward and recurrent neural networks on process sensor data typically requires a regular time grid, making the interpolation step a significant preprocessing decision. This paper benchmarks seven interpolation strategies—linear, cubic spline, Gaussian process regression with a squared-exponential kernel, shape-preserving piecewise Hermite interpolation, zero-order hold, and two data-adaptive methods—across six industrial datasets with irregular sampling ratios ranging from 8 % to 61 % missing per channel per day. Downstream task performance is measured by mean absolute error on a temperature prediction task and by F1 on a binary shutdown-prediction task. Results show that Gaussian process regression consistently provides the best downstream performance when irregularity is above 30 % but incurs a runtime cost two to three orders of magnitude higher than linear interpolation. Practical guidance for selecting interpolation strategy as a function of irregularity ratio and available compute budget is distilled into a decision flowchart.

title: Sparse Autoencoders for Unsupervised Feature Extraction from Low-Rate Industrial Sensor Logs
abstract: Many small and medium-sized manufacturers operate legacy SCADA systems that log process variables at intervals of one minute or longer, producing sparse, low-dimensional tabular snapshots rather than dense time series. This paper investigates whether sparse autoencoders, originally developed for natural-image data, can learn meaningful latent representations from such logs without any labelled examples. Experiments use six months of data from a food-processing line and eight months from a plastics extrusion facility, both in Serbia. Learned representations are evaluated by measuring the separation of known operational modes in the latent space using a Davies–Bouldin index and by the accuracy of a k-nearest-neighbour classifier trained with 1 % labelled samples. Sparsity penalties between 0.01 and 0.1 were swept; penalty 0.05 gave the best trade-off in both settings. The method outperformed PCA and raw-feature baselines on every metric, with a Davies–Bouldin improvement of 34 % on the extrusion dataset.

title: Augmentation Strategies for Contrastive Learning on Tabular Sensor Data: What Transfers from Vision?
abstract: Contrastive self-supervised methods in computer vision rely on image augmentations such as cropping and colour jitter to generate positive pairs. For tabular industrial sensor data, the appropriate analogues are not obvious. This paper systematically evaluates eleven candidate augmentation operations—including Gaussian noise injection, random channel dropout, temporal jitter, segment permutation, magnitude scaling, and mixup with temporal neighbours—using SimCLR-style training on three tabular datasets from chemical processing and machining environments. Representations are assessed by linear probing accuracy and by clustering quality on held-out operational-mode labels. Channel dropout and temporal jitter applied jointly produced the strongest representations across all three datasets, while segment permutation consistently degraded quality. The paper also examines how augmentation choice interacts with the degree of temporal irregularity, finding that datasets with higher irregularity benefit more from noise-based augmentations than from structural ones.

title: Temporal Contrastive Learning with Non-Uniform Sampling Windows for Multivariate Sensor Streams
abstract: Standard contrastive learning assumes that positive pairs can be drawn from a fixed temporal window around an anchor point. In industrial sensor streams where sampling is irregular, the semantic similarity between two snapshots depends on the actual elapsed time rather than on a fixed number of steps. This paper proposes a time-aware contrastive objective in which the target similarity between an anchor and a candidate positive is modulated by the inverse of the elapsed time between them, interpolating smoothly between strong positives and informative negatives. The method is implemented on top of a shallow MLP encoder and evaluated on four datasets spanning hydraulic systems, conveyor-belt drives, and HVAC units, all characterised by non-uniform sampling caused by event-driven logging. The time-aware objective improved downstream anomaly detection AUROC by an average of 4.3 percentage points over a standard fixed-window contrastive baseline and by 9.1 points over a non-contrastive autoencoder.

title: Evaluating Contrastive Representations for Cross-Domain Transfer Between Industrial Sensor Datasets
abstract: A key motivation for self-supervised pretraining is the ability to transfer representations across tasks and domains with minimal labelled data. This paper conducts a controlled transfer study using contrastive representations pretrained on one industrial domain—water treatment—and fine-tuned on three target domains: grain drying, compressed-air distribution, and injection moulding. All datasets share a tabular format with 8 to 24 channels but differ in process physics and sampling rates. Transfer is evaluated at five labelled-sample budgets from 10 to 500. The study finds that transfer is positive in all conditions relative to random initialisation at budgets below 100 labels, but that at budgets of 500 labels the gap narrows and sometimes reverses, suggesting that domain-specific structure eventually dominates general sensor statistics. Feature-space alignment using centred kernel alignment scores correlates moderately (r = 0.61) with transfer performance, offering a cheap proxy for estimating transferability without running the full fine-tuning pipeline.

title: Hard Negative Mining in Sensor Space: Selecting Informative Negatives for Contrastive Training on Process Data
abstract: Contrastive learning performance depends critically on the informativeness of negative pairs. In industrial sensor data, naive random negative sampling frequently selects negatives from operating regimes that are easily distinguishable from the anchor, reducing the gradient signal during training. This paper proposes a hard-negative mining strategy based on approximate nearest-neighbour search in a running estimate of the current embedding space, retrieving negatives that are close in representation but drawn from a different temporal neighbourhood. The approach is evaluated against uniform negative sampling and semi-hard mining (adapted from the metric-learning literature) on five tabular sensor datasets. Hard negatives constructed by the proposed strategy improved linear probe accuracy by 3.1 to 6.8 percentage points depending on dataset, and reduced the number of pretraining epochs required to reach a target accuracy by approximately 35 % on average. The computational overhead of the approximate nearest-neighbour index was less than 8 % of total training time.

title: TabSCL: A Contrastive Self-Supervised Framework for Sparse and Irregular Tabular Sensor Logs
abstract: This paper presents TabSCL, a contrastive self-supervised framework designed specifically for tabular industrial sensor data characterised by sparse and irregular temporal sampling. The framework combines three components: a missingness-aware feature tokeniser that encodes observed/unobserved status as part of the token embedding, a time-gap encoding that injects elapsed-time information into a shallow transformer, and a curriculum-based augmentation scheduler that increases augmentation strength as training progresses. TabSCL is evaluated on seven datasets from manufacturing and utilities sectors, with missing rates between 12 % and 58 % per channel, covering fault detection, anomaly scoring, and mode classification downstream tasks. Across 21 dataset–task combinations, TabSCL improves mean AUROC by 5.7 points and macro-F1 by 4.2 points relative to the strongest prior contrastive baseline. An ablation study shows that missingness encoding contributes the largest individual gain (2.9 AUROC points on average), followed by time-gap encoding (1.8 points) and the curriculum scheduler (1.0 points). Code and datasets are publicly available.

title: Sensor Dropout as a Structured Augmentation: Theoretical Grounding and Empirical Validation for Contrastive Tabular Pretraining
abstract: Channel dropout—randomly zeroing out entire sensor channels during contrastive pretraining—has been observed to improve representation quality in tabular sensor data, but the mechanism has not been formally analysed. This paper provides a theoretical perspective by framing sensor dropout as an approximation to marginalisation over missing-channel distributions, and derives conditions under which dropout-augmented contrastive training recovers representations that are predictive of downstream labels. The theoretical claims are validated on five industrial tabular datasets by comparing representations learned with sensor dropout, Gaussian noise, and no augmentation, using both linear probing and mutual information estimation between representations and labels. Sensor dropout consistently produced representations with higher estimated mutual information (average gain 0.31 nats) and better linear probing accuracy (average gain 3.8 percentage points) relative to the no-augmentation baseline. The theoretical analysis additionally reveals why the dropout probability interacts with the native missingness rate of the data, suggesting dataset-adaptive probability selection.

title: Fermentation profile of whole-plant maize silage inoculated with Lactobacillus buchneri at two dry matter levels
abstract: This study compared fermentation outcomes in whole-plant maize ensiled at 28% and 35% dry matter (DM) with and without a commercial strain of Lactobacillus buchneri applied at 1×10⁵ CFU g⁻¹ fresh weight. Mini-silos (1.5 kg capacity, triplicate) were opened after 30, 60, and 90 days. Inoculation significantly increased acetic acid concentration at both DM levels, with the greatest effect observed at 35% DM after 90 days (28.4 vs. 14.1 g kg⁻¹ DM in untreated controls). Lactic acid declined from peak values of 42 g kg⁻¹ DM at day 30 to 31 g kg⁻¹ DM at day 90 in inoculated 35% DM silage. Ethanol was lower in inoculated treatments at both DM levels. pH values were within acceptable range (3.7–4.1) across all treatments. Aerobic stability, measured by temperature rise above ambient over 120 h, was extended by 48 h on average in inoculated silages at 35% DM. Results indicate that inoculant efficacy in promoting acetate accumulation is modulated by substrate DM concentration.

title: Effect of wilting duration on fermentation quality of whole-plant maize ensiled with a heterofermentative inoculant
abstract: Wilting whole-plant maize before ensiling is not standard practice, but brief field-wilting sometimes occurs in practice due to harvesting delays. This experiment evaluated silage quality when maize was ensiled immediately after harvest (29% DM), or after 6 h (33% DM) or 12 h (37% DM) of field wilting, with or without L. buchneri at 1.5×10⁵ CFU g⁻¹. Twelve treatments in triplicate mini-silos were opened at 45 and 90 days. Wilting to 37% DM without inoculant produced silage with elevated butyric acid (3.8 g kg⁻¹ DM), reduced lactic acid (18 g kg⁻¹ DM), and high pH (4.6), indicating clostridial activity. Inoculant application at 37% DM suppressed butyric acid to below detection threshold and restored pH to 4.1. At 29 and 33% DM, inoculant effects were primarily on aerobic stability. Ammonia-N as a proportion of total nitrogen was below 80 g kg⁻¹ in all inoculated treatments. The findings highlight the value of heterofermentative inoculants when DM at ensiling is uncertain.

title: Bacterial community dynamics in whole-plant maize silage treated with heterofermentative inoculants: a 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing study
abstract: Amplicon sequencing of the V3–V4 hypervariable region of 16S rRNA genes was used to characterise bacterial community succession in maize silage (31% DM) over 90 days, comparing L. buchneri inoculation at 1×10⁵ and 5×10⁵ CFU g⁻¹ with an uninoculated control. Six time points were sampled per treatment in triplicate. Relative abundance of Lactobacillaceae increased from under 15% at day 1 to over 85% at day 14 in all treatments, but the composition within Lactobacillaceae shifted: L. buchneri-related amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) dominated inoculated silages from day 7 onward (54–67%), whereas Limosilactobacillus fermentum-related ASVs were most abundant in controls at day 14. Alpha diversity (Shannon index) declined sharply between days 1 and 7 in all treatments. Enterobacteriaceae became undetectable after day 7 in inoculated silages but persisted at low relative abundance in controls until day 14. Community composition at day 90 explained 38% of variance in acetic acid concentration (PERMANOVA, p<0.01).

title: Temperature during the ensiling period alters fermentation outcomes in L. buchneri-inoculated maize silage
abstract: Laboratory-scale ensiling experiments were conducted at three constant temperatures (10°C, 20°C, 30°C) to simulate cool, ambient, and warm seasonal conditions in Central and Southeast Europe. Maize (32% DM) was inoculated with L. buchneri at 1.5×10⁵ CFU g⁻¹ or left uninoculated. Silos were opened at 15, 45, and 90 days. At 10°C, fermentation was markedly retarded: pH remained above 5.0 until day 15 even with inoculant. Final lactic acid at day 90 was lower at 10°C (24 g kg⁻¹ DM) than at 20°C (38 g kg⁻¹ DM) or 30°C (41 g kg⁻¹ DM). Acetic acid response to inoculant was negligible at 10°C but substantial at 20°C (+9.4 g kg⁻¹ DM vs. control) and 30°C (+12.1 g kg⁻¹ DM). Aerobic stability was reduced at 30°C in uninoculated silage (52 h) compared with inoculated silage (>120 h). Results suggest that temperature-adjusted inoculant application rates may be warranted in autumn harvesting conditions in Vojvodina.

title: Comparative fermentation performance of four heterofermentative Lactobacillus strains isolated from spontaneously fermented maize silage in Vojvodina
abstract: Four strains of heterofermentative lactic acid bacteria (designated NVS-1 through NVS-4) were isolated from three-year-old spontaneously fermented maize silage at farms in Vojvodina and identified by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry and partial 16S rRNA sequencing as L. buchneri (NVS-1, NVS-3), Lacticaseibacillus parabuchneri (NVS-2), and L. fermentum (NVS-4). Strains were applied individually to whole-plant maize (30% DM) mini-silos at 1×10⁵ CFU g⁻¹ alongside a commercial L. buchneri reference. After 90 days, NVS-1 produced the highest acetic acid (31.2 g kg⁻¹ DM) and best aerobic stability (>168 h), comparable with the commercial reference. NVS-4 (L. fermentum) produced substantial ethanol (8.1 g kg⁻¹ DM), undesirable for silage quality. NVS-2 performance was intermediate. Strain NVS-1 was retained for further characterisation as a candidate indigenous inoculant. Isolate collections of locally adapted strains may complement commercial inoculant portfolios in the region.

title: Silage inoculants for maize: mechanisms, practical considerations, and regional evidence
abstract: This chapter reviews the biological basis of heterofermentative and homofermentative lactic acid bacteria inoculants used in maize silage production, with emphasis on evidence from Central and Southeast Europe. The chapter covers carbon flow pathways in homo- and heterofermentative metabolism, the relationship between acetate accumulation and resistance to aerobic deterioration, and factors modifying inoculant efficacy, including DM content at ensiling, temperature, compaction, and inoculant dose. A section reviews published data from field-scale trials in Hungary, Romania, Serbia, and Croatia, identifying consistent response patterns and sources of variability. Practical guidance on inoculant selection and application technology is discussed in light of farming conditions in the region. The chapter also examines gaps in knowledge, including the limited characterisation of indigenous lactic acid bacteria populations from Southeast European maize fields and the lack of multi-year, multi-site trials under local agronomic conditions.

title: Decomposing six big losses in continuous pasteurisation tunnels: methodology adaptation from discrete to flow-process contexts
abstract: The conventional six-big-losses taxonomy was developed primarily for discrete-part machining equipment and fits imperfectly onto continuous thermal-processing equipment such as pasteurisation tunnels. This paper proposes a modified loss taxonomy in which speed losses are replaced by a throughput-rate deviation metric referenced to the nominal Brix-corrected flow rate, and quality losses are stratified into in-process deviations and post-tunnel hold detections. The adapted framework was validated on pasteurisation tunnel data from three beverage plants in Serbia and Croatia, covering 14 months of operational records amounting to 38,640 operating hours across all three sites. Intra-class correlation analysis confirmed acceptable consistency of loss classification between sites (ICC = 0.81). A linear mixed-effects model showed that maintenance interval length was the strongest predictor of availability, explaining 34 % of variance. The paper concludes with a proposed reporting template aligned with ISO 22400-2 KPI definitions.

title: Sensitivity of OEE to boundary condition assumptions in semi-continuous brewing fermentation
abstract: OEE calculation in brewing fermentation vessels is complicated by the semi-continuous nature of batch filling and conditioning cycles, which makes the definition of planned production time ambiguous. This paper analyses the sensitivity of computed OEE values to four plausible boundary condition assumptions using operational data from a craft brewery in Novi Sad operating 24 fermentation tanks over 18 months. Under the most conservative assumption, mean OEE was 43.2 %; under the most permissive, it reached 67.8 %—a range that significantly affects maintenance investment decisions. A structured decision procedure for selecting boundary conditions based on plant scheduling practices and contractual delivery requirements is developed. Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations quantified uncertainty in monthly OEE estimates given typical data-quality imperfections. The results suggest that inter-plant OEE comparisons in brewing should always report the boundary convention used alongside the numeric value, and that a single-number OEE target without stated conventions is practically uninformative.

title: Failure mode and effects analysis for CIP systems in liquid food production: severity ranking using operational downtime data
abstract: Clean-in-place (CIP) circuit failures are a significant but often under-reported source of unplanned downtime in liquid food manufacturing because their consequences are frequently logged as product quality holds rather than equipment failures. This paper presents an FMEA for the CIP circuit serving three production lines in a Serbian fruit-juice plant, combining expert elicitation with 26 months of maintenance work-order records to calibrate severity, occurrence, and detection ratings numerically rather than relying solely on expert opinion. A total of 47 failure modes were identified; the top five by risk priority number accounted for 58 % of CIP-attributable downtime. Diaphragm valve seat erosion and conductivity sensor drift emerged as the highest-priority failure modes. Corrective actions introduced on the basis of the FMEA reduced mean CIP circuit downtime per month by 31 % over the following 12-month verification period. The paper discusses the practical challenges of retrospectively recategorising maintenance records to separate CIP-circuit failures from process-line failures.

title: OEE disaggregation at machine level versus line level: implications for maintenance priority setting in multi-stage filling systems
abstract: Most published OEE analyses report line-level aggregates, obscuring the contribution of individual machines to overall line losses. This study compared machine-level and line-level OEE disaggregation on a multi-stage glass-bottle filling system comprising rinser, filler, capper, labeller, and palletiser, using 12 months of automated event logs from a mineral water plant in Vojvodina. At line level, mean OEE was 71.4 %. Machine-level disaggregation revealed that the capper contributed 42 % of all availability loss events despite accounting for only 11 % of total downtime duration, indicating frequent short stops that aggregate analysis masked. A simulation model of the line was built in AnyLogic to evaluate maintenance prioritisation scenarios. Focusing planned maintenance resources on the capper and labeller yielded a simulated line OEE improvement of 5.8 percentage points, versus 2.1 points for strategies guided by aggregate duration data alone. The paper advocates mandatory machine-level instrumentation as a prerequisite for data-driven maintenance budgeting.

title: Condition-based maintenance intervals for centrifugal pumps in continuous-flow food processing: a cost-optimisation approach
abstract: Centrifugal pumps are among the most numerous and failure-prone items of rotating equipment in continuous-flow food processing facilities. This paper formulates a cost-optimisation model for condition-based maintenance interval selection for such pumps, incorporating vibration-based degradation signals, replacement part costs, hygienic downgrade risk penalties, and planned-maintenance labour costs. Model parameters were estimated using 34 months of vibration trending data and maintenance cost records from a sunflower oil refinery in Vojvodina covering 78 pump units. A two-state continuous-time Markov chain was fitted to the degradation data; transition rates were estimated by maximum likelihood. The optimal inspection interval under the cost model ranged from 18 to 31 days depending on pump duty class, compared with the fixed 30-day schedule then in use. Simulation showed the cost-optimal policy reduced total pump-related maintenance expenditure by 14.3 % annually while reducing unplanned failures by 22 %. The model is implemented in a spreadsheet tool distributed with the paper.

title: TPM self-assessment in small and medium food enterprises: adapting frameworks developed for large plants
abstract: The majority of TPM implementation guidance and published case studies originates from large, high-throughput manufacturing environments. Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the food sector face different resource constraints, less formalised maintenance departments, and greater production variety, all of which complicate direct adoption of standard TPM frameworks. This paper presents a qualitative multiple-case study of four food SMEs in Vojvodina—a fruit-preserve producer, a small brewery, a spice-processing company, and a poultry slaughterhouse—each employing between 45 and 120 production staff. Semi-structured interviews and document review were used to map current maintenance practices against a simplified four-pillar TPM framework. Across all four cases, the absence of structured maintenance data recording was the primary barrier to launching any evidence-based improvement programme. A lightweight TPM starter toolkit, consisting of a paper-based failure log, a basic OEE calculation sheet, and a 10-question autonomous maintenance checklist, is proposed and its piloting at two of the case companies is described. Early results show improved first-pass failure categorisation accuracy after four weeks of use.

title: Attribute-Based Valuation of Banner Advertising Placements: A Conjoint Study on Serbian Online News Portals
abstract: This study applies choice-based conjoint (CBC) analysis to estimate the implicit prices that media buyers attach to specific attributes of banner advertising placements on Serbian online news portals. A fractional factorial design with six attributes—placement position, page context, audience targeting option, animation type, ad size, and exclusivity—was administered to a purposive sample of 84 media planning professionals from agencies in Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Zagreb. Hierarchical Bayes estimation was used to recover individual-level part-worth utilities. Results show that placement position (above versus below the fold) and audience targeting capability together account for 61 percent of total attribute importance. Ad size contributes only 9 percent, a finding that diverges from practitioner assumptions documented in prior qualitative work. The estimated willingness-to-pay premium for above-fold targeted placements over run-of-site untargeted placements averaged €1.84 CPM in 2009 prices. The paper discusses implications for small-market digital publishers setting rate cards without access to large-scale auction data.

title: Hedonic Price Functions for Online Display Advertising: Evidence from a Regional Ad Network
abstract: Using transaction-level data from a regional Central European ad network covering approximately 120,000 impression-level records from 2008–2010, this paper estimates hedonic price functions for display advertising inventory. The dependent variable is the net CPM paid by advertisers; explanatory variables include page category, time-of-day, day-of-week, ad format dimensions, publisher audience size, geographic targeting precision, and frequency-cap setting. OLS and quantile regression specifications are compared. The hedonic model explains 54 percent of CPM variance in the OLS baseline. Quantile regression reveals significant heterogeneity: the price premium for geographic targeting is approximately twice as large at the 75th percentile of the CPM distribution as at the median, suggesting that premium advertisers value targeting more intensely than average-spend clients. The paper provides a methodological template for publishers in small advertising markets where auction-clearing mechanisms are absent or opaque, and discusses limitations arising from collinearity between publisher audience size and page category.

title: Measuring Viewer Preferences for Pre-Roll Video Advertising Formats: A Discrete Choice Experiment
abstract: Pre-roll video advertising had expanded rapidly on Balkan streaming platforms by 2012, yet little empirical evidence existed on viewer tolerance for specific format attributes. This discrete choice experiment recruited 312 internet users in Serbia aged 18–45 via an online panel and presented them with hypothetical video-viewing scenarios varying in pre-roll duration (5, 15, or 30 seconds), skip availability (skippable after 5 seconds, never skippable), content relevance (matched to viewed content or unrelated), and ad frequency per session (one, two, or three). Mixed logit estimation revealed strong preference heterogeneity around skip availability: the mean disutility attached to non-skippable 30-second ads was equivalent in willingness-to-endure terms to watching an additional 2.1 ads per session. Content relevance generated a statistically significant positive utility coefficient (p < 0.01) even among respondents who reported general dislike of advertising. Findings are interpreted in light of limited local inventory pricing data and compared against equivalent estimates from a concurrent German study.

title: Conjoint Analysis in Academic Marketing Research: A Methodological Review with Emphasis on Media Applications
abstract: This book chapter surveys the methodological development of conjoint analysis from its origins in psychological measurement in the 1960s through adaptive and choice-based variants dominant in commercial practice by the 2010s. The chapter is directed at researchers in post-Yugoslav academic contexts where access to Sawtooth Software or equivalent commercial platforms has been constrained. It covers full-profile, adaptive conjoint analysis (ACA), and CBC designs, discussing sample size requirements, attribute selection protocols, and estimation approaches ranging from ordinary least squares to hierarchical Bayes. A dedicated section reviews conjoint applications in media economics and advertising research published between 2000 and 2013, identifying 34 relevant studies and coding them by sector, attribute set used, and estimation method. The chapter also provides worked examples using synthetic data constructed to resemble digital advertising inventory problems. Practical guidance is given on translating part-worth utilities into pricing recommendations for publishers lacking econometric staff.

title: Price Sensitivity and Attribute Importance in Native Advertising Placements: A CBC Experiment with Media Buyers
abstract: Native advertising—paid content designed to blend with editorial presentation—was growing rapidly in the region by 2014, but formal pricing frameworks were largely absent from smaller markets. This study recruited 97 media buyers from Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia in a web-based CBC experiment. Stimuli described native placement packages varying in editorial integration level (labelled sponsored content, unlabelled integrated, or editorially independent), publication reach, content production responsibility (publisher-produced or client-produced), placement duration, and price. Latent class analysis identified three buyer segments: price-driven buyers (31%), reach-maximisers (44%), and transparency-sensitive buyers (25%). The transparency-sensitive segment attached a willingness-to-pay premium of €240 per placement for clearly labelled sponsored content relative to unlabelled integration, a finding with regulatory as well as commercial implications. Aggregate willingness-to-pay elasticities with respect to publication reach followed a concave pattern, suggesting diminishing returns to scale in reach for native formats.

title: Hedonic Decomposition of Programmatic Display CPMs: A Regression Analysis of Private Marketplace Transactions
abstract: Private marketplace (PMP) deals account for a growing share of programmatic advertising transactions, yet their price-determinant structure is rarely studied with transaction-level data outside the US and UK. A dataset of 47,300 PMP deal records from a Central and Eastern European supply-side platform (SSP), covering January–December 2015, was obtained under a research data agreement. Hedonic regression models—including log-linear OLS and a random forest benchmark—were estimated with CPM as the dependent variable. Independent variables included publisher vertical, deal type (preferred deal vs. private auction), audience segment depth, viewability score (IAB standard), brand safety category, ad format, and deal size. The OLS model achieved an adjusted R² of 0.61. Viewability score emerged as the strongest single predictor: moving from a 50 percent to a 70 percent viewability guarantee was associated with a 38 percent CPM premium, ceteris paribus. The random forest model improved fit marginally (R² = 0.66) but did not alter the substantive rank ordering of predictors. The paper discusses structural differences between PMP and open-auction pricing logic.

title: Willingness-to-Pay for Ad-Free Subscription Tiers: Evidence from a Conjoint Study Among Serbian Streaming Service Users
abstract: As streaming platforms in the Western Balkans began introducing hybrid subscription–advertising models in 2017–2018, the equilibrium between ad-supported free access and paid ad-free tiers became commercially significant. This paper reports a CBC experiment conducted with 428 adult streaming users in Serbia. The experimental design varied monthly subscription price (from 149 to 599 RSD), ad load in the free tier (zero, two, four, or six ads per hour), content library size relative to baseline, download-for-offline functionality, and simultaneous stream count. Hierarchical Bayes estimation yielded median willingness-to-pay for complete ad removal of 231 RSD per month (approximately €2.00 at 2018 exchange rates). Users under 30 showed a significantly higher premium (median 287 RSD). Interaction effects between ad load and content library size were statistically significant and practically large: users accepted higher ad loads when content libraries were expanded, at a rate of approximately 0.8 additional ads per hour per 10 percent library expansion. Implications for tiered pricing design are discussed.

title: Context Effects on Advertising Attribute Weights: A Within-Subject Conjoint Replication Across News and Entertainment Contexts
abstract: Conjoint studies of digital advertising typically administer stimuli in a single neutral context, yet advertising effectiveness literature suggests that editorial context moderates attribute valuation. This study tests whether part-worth utilities for key inventory attributes—audience targeting, viewability, ad format, and brand safety category—differ when the same respondents evaluate placements framed as news-site inventory versus entertainment-site inventory. A within-subject CBC design was administered to 201 media planners recruited through a Serbian advertising industry association. Each respondent completed two blocks of 12 choice tasks, one per context, in randomised order. Paired comparisons of individual-level Bayes estimates revealed statistically significant context effects for brand safety (larger weight in news context, Cohen's d = 0.44) and audience targeting (larger weight in entertainment context, d = 0.38). Viewability weights did not differ significantly between contexts. These findings suggest that single-context conjoint studies may produce biased attribute importance estimates when generalised across editorial environments.

title: Estimating the Value of First-Party Data Segments in Cookieless Programmatic Environments: A Conjoint Approach
abstract: The deprecation of third-party cookies has prompted a reassessment of first-party data value in digital advertising. This paper presents a conjoint study designed to estimate how media buyers price first-party audience segments relative to contextual and third-party segments under a hypothetical cookieless scenario. A between-subjects CBC experiment was conducted with two samples: 109 media buyers surveyed in late 2020 (cookie-present baseline condition) and 98 media buyers surveyed in early 2021 (cookieless scenario condition). Stimuli described programmatic deal packages varying in audience segment type, match rate, CPM, format, and viewability guarantee. Under the cookieless scenario, the willingness-to-pay premium for publisher first-party segments over contextual-only targeting rose by 67 percent relative to the baseline condition. Segment match rate—defined as the share of the publisher's audience matched to the advertiser's CRM data—emerged as a new significant predictor of deal preference only in the cookieless condition. The paper discusses limitations of between-subjects counterfactual designs and the feasibility of implementing similar studies at individual publisher level.

title: Advertiser Preferences for Attention-Based Buying Metrics: A Discrete Choice Study Comparing CPM, vCPM, and Cost-per-Second Metrics
abstract: The advertising industry has debated replacing the standard CPM metric with attention-based alternatives, including viewable CPM (vCPM) and cost-per-second (CPS) metrics. This paper reports a discrete choice experiment examining how media buyers trade off metric type, price level, verification method, and publisher reach when purchasing digital display inventory. A sample of 143 media buyers from agencies and in-house teams in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania completed a web-based CBC survey in early 2023. Latent class analysis identified four preference segments: traditional CPM buyers (27%), vCPM adopters (38%), attention-metric explorers open to CPS (19%), and price-dominant buyers (16%). The attention-metric explorer segment attached a willingness-to-pay premium for third-party verified CPS inventory of 42 percent over equivalent unverified CPM inventory. Verification method (independent third party vs. publisher self-reported) was the strongest single attribute across all segments. The study provides empirical grounding for publishers considering metric transitions in regional markets with limited liquidity.

title: Hedonic Valuation of AI-Generated Contextual Targeting Signals in Programmatic Advertising
abstract: Contextual targeting has regained commercial importance as cookie-based behavioural targeting has declined, and suppliers now offer AI-generated contextual signals of varying granularity and claimed accuracy. This paper applies hedonic regression to estimate the price premium associated with AI-generated contextual signals in programmatic transactions. Transaction data covering 63,000 programmatic impressions bought by 11 advertisers through a regional demand-side platform (DSP) during 2024 were obtained under a research agreement with the DSP operator. The hedonic model regresses log CPM on signal type (standard IAB category, AI-generated granular contextual segment, or no contextual signal), claimed accuracy score, publisher domain authority, viewability, ad format, and time of day. AI-generated granular contextual signals commanded a CPM premium of 22 percent over standard IAB category signals (p < 0.001) after controlling for all other attributes. Claimed accuracy score was positively associated with price only at accuracy levels above 85 percent, suggesting a threshold effect. Implications for contextual signal vendors and publishers are discussed alongside limitations from non-random data collection.

title: Conjoint-Based Pricing Audits for Small Digital Publishers: A Practical Framework and Pilot Application
abstract: Small and mid-sized digital publishers in less-liquid advertising markets—including most Western Balkan countries—rarely possess the transaction volume or internal analytical capacity to conduct rigorous inventory pricing audits. This paper proposes a four-step framework that uses conjoint analysis and hedonic benchmarking to audit and recalibrate publisher rate cards when transaction data are sparse. The framework involves: (1) attribute identification through structured interviews with media buyers, (2) CBC experiment design calibrated to the publisher's specific format portfolio, (3) estimation of buyer willingness-to-pay using publicly available R packages as a low-cost alternative to commercial conjoint software, and (4) comparison of estimated willingness-to-pay ranges against current rate card prices to identify under- and over-priced inventory positions. A pilot application is reported for a mid-sized Serbian regional news portal with a monthly unique visitor count of approximately 280,000. The audit identified three format-position combinations priced below the 25th percentile of estimated buyer willingness-to-pay and two above the 75th percentile. The paper discusses generalisability constraints and the minimum data requirements for reliable CBC estimation in small publisher contexts.

title: Vapour diffusion resistance factor of hemp-lime panels: effect of lime binder content and curing age
abstract: The water vapour diffusion resistance factor (μ) of hemp-lime panels was determined according to the dry-cup and wet-cup procedure described in EN ISO 12572, using five binder-to-aggregate ratios by volume (0.5:1 to 2:1) and three curing ages (28, 90, and 180 days). Panels of 100 mm thickness were cast in timber formwork and cured at 20 °C and 65 % RH. Measured μ values ranged from 3.1 to 7.6 across the test matrix. Higher binder content consistently raised μ, while curing age had a comparatively smaller effect beyond 90 days. Dry-cup values exceeded wet-cup values by 15–40 %, confirming the well-known moisture-dependent diffusivity of lime-bonded porous materials. The data were used to derive moisture-dependent diffusion coefficients for each panel variant. Scanning electron microscopy images of the binder–aggregate interface at selected ratios are included to interpret the microstructural basis of the trends. The results suggest that panels with binder ratios below 1:1 offer a favourable balance of vapour permeability and mechanical integrity for interior insulation applications.

title: Thermal conductivity of flax-fibre reinforced gypsum boards under varying moisture conditions
abstract: Gypsum boards reinforced with short flax fibres (3 % and 6 % fibre mass fraction, chopped to 20 mm) were produced by casting and tested for thermal conductivity using a guarded hot plate apparatus at mean temperatures of 10, 23, and 35 °C and equilibrium moisture contents ranging from oven-dry to 12 % by mass. Unreinforced reference boards were included for comparison. Thermal conductivity of reference boards at 23 °C increased from 0.29 W/(m·K) at oven-dry state to 0.41 W/(m·K) at 12 % moisture content. Flax reinforcement reduced conductivity at low moisture contents (by up to 0.04 W/(m·K) at 3 % fibre content) but the benefit diminished at higher moisture levels owing to preferential moisture accumulation along fibre-matrix interfaces, as evidenced by X-ray computed tomography. The study provides conductivity–moisture relations that can be implemented directly in building envelope simulation. Mechanical flexural strength data are also reported as a secondary outcome, showing that 6 % fibre content doubled the modulus of rupture relative to unreinforced gypsum.

title: Hygrothermal performance of hemp-lime wall assemblies in a continental climate: a two-year in-situ monitoring study
abstract: Two south-facing external wall assemblies — one 300 mm hemp-lime monolithic wall and one 150 mm hemp-lime slab attached to a masonry backup — were instrumented with paired temperature and relative humidity sensors at three depths and monitored continuously from January 2018 to December 2019 in a test house near Novi Sad. Monthly precipitation and outdoor climate data were recorded on-site. Both assemblies remained within safe moisture content limits throughout the monitoring period; peak relative humidity at the cold-side sensor did not exceed 85 % in any month. The monolithic wall showed a larger diurnal temperature swing at its exterior face (up to 18 K) and a correspondingly larger moisture buffering response. Measured interior surface temperatures were compared with DELPHIN 6 simulations using hygrothermal material properties characterised in earlier laboratory work; agreement within ±1.2 K and ±3 % RH was achieved after calibration of the exterior surface transfer coefficients. The dataset is made openly available to support validation exercises for hygrothermal simulation software.

title: Moisture buffer value of bio-based interior panels made from sunflower stalk aggregate and clay binder
abstract: Panels fabricated from chopped sunflower stalk aggregate (particle length 10–20 mm) and a kaolin-based clay binder were assessed for moisture buffering capacity using the Nordtest protocol. Four panel formulations were prepared, varying the binder content (20 % and 35 % by dry mass) and whether the exposed surface was left raw or coated with a single layer of lime wash. Specimens were subjected to alternating 8 h high-humidity (75 % RH) and 16 h low-humidity (33 % RH) cycles at 23 °C for eight consecutive days. Moisture buffer values (MBV) for uncoated panels ranged from 2.1 to 2.8 g/(m²·%RH), placing them in the 'good' category of the Nordtest classification. Lime-wash coating reduced MBV by approximately 20 %. Complementary sorption isotherm measurements confirmed that the sunflower aggregate contributed the dominant fraction of sorption capacity. The results indicate that these panels are suitable as interior lining boards where passive humidity regulation is desired, with the added advantage of using an agricultural by-product locally available in Vojvodina.

title: Capillary water absorption and redistribution in hemp-lime composites with varying aggregate gradation
abstract: Water absorption by capillarity and subsequent redistribution under gravity were studied for hemp-lime composite cylinders (diameter 100 mm, height 200 mm) prepared with three aggregate gradations: fine (2–4 mm), coarse (8–16 mm), and a 1:1 blended fraction. The A-value (capillary absorption coefficient) was determined from partial immersion tests at 23 °C; the coarse-aggregate variant showed the highest A-value of 1.8 kg/(m²·h⁰·⁵) versus 0.9 kg/(m²·h⁰·⁵) for the fine-aggregate variant. Moisture redistribution after 24 h free drainage was mapped by slicing specimens at 20 mm intervals and determining moisture content gravimetrically. Mercury intrusion porosimetry characterised pore-size distributions for each variant. The results show that coarse aggregate creates a higher proportion of macropores that dominate capillary pathways, while the fine aggregate blend produces a more homogeneous moisture profile post-drainage. These findings have direct implications for the detailing of hemp-lime walls at ground level and sill junctions, where capillary uptake poses the main durability risk.

title: Coupled heat-and-moisture simulation of a bio-based roof insulation layer under summer driving rain: sensitivity to material property uncertainty
abstract: A 200 mm layer of loose-fill flax insulation beneath a ventilated roof cladding was modelled in DELPHIN 6 to assess its hygrothermal response during a simulated ten-day driving-rain episode representative of summer conditions in the Pannonian lowland. Material properties (thermal conductivity, vapour diffusion resistance factor, and capillary absorption coefficient) were treated as uncertain inputs and varied within experimentally determined ranges using Latin hypercube sampling (200 runs). Output distributions for maximum moisture content and drying-out time were computed. The dominant source of output variance was the vapour diffusion resistance factor of the underlying timber deck boarding, which governed drying potential toward the interior. Flax insulation properties ranked second in influence, with the capillary coefficient contributing least. Peak moisture content in the flax layer exceeded 25 % by mass in 12 % of runs, suggesting that roof geometry and deck permeability deserve closer attention in risk assessments than is standard practice. The paper proposes a simplified screening criterion based on the ratio of exterior vapour resistance to total assembly vapour resistance.

title: Ageing effects on vapour permeability and thermal conductivity of hemp-lime panels after accelerated weathering
abstract: Hemp-lime panels (binder-to-aggregate ratio 1:1 by volume) were subjected to accelerated cyclic weathering in a programmable climate chamber: 200 cycles each consisting of 8 h at 80 % RH and 40 °C followed by 16 h at 30 % RH and 5 °C, intended to approximate twenty years of service in a central European climate based on a cycle equivalence analysis. Vapour diffusion resistance factor was re-measured by the dry-cup and wet-cup methods after 50, 100, and 200 cycles, and guarded hot plate measurements of thermal conductivity were repeated at the same intervals. After 200 cycles, μ increased by 14 % relative to the initial value and thermal conductivity increased by 0.018 W/(m·K), both attributed to progressive carbonation and densification of the lime matrix confirmed by thermogravimetric analysis. Compressive strength and modulus of elasticity were also measured and showed slight increases. No visible cracking or delamination was observed. The findings support the assumption that hemp-lime maintains or improves its hygrothermal performance over service life under temperate climatic loading.
venue: Construction and Building Physics Transactions

title: A comparative review of standard test methods for hygrothermal characterisation of bio-based building materials: scope, limitations and interlaboratory variability
abstract: This chapter reviews the principal standardised methods used to characterise the hygrothermal properties of bio-based building materials: sorption isotherm measurement (ISO 12571), vapour diffusion resistance by the cup method (ISO 12572), thermal conductivity by the guarded hot plate (ISO 8302) and heat flow meter (ISO 9869-1), capillary water absorption (EN 1015-18), and the Nordtest moisture buffer value protocol. For each method the chapter discusses the underlying assumptions, the range of materials to which they apply without modification, and the known sources of interlaboratory variability drawn from published round-robin exercises. Particular attention is given to fibrous and heterogeneous materials such as hemp-lime, straw-bale sections, and loose-fill plant fibre batts, for which standard specimen geometry and conditioning requirements sometimes need adaptation. The chapter also discusses how properties obtained from these methods are incorporated as inputs into hygrothermal simulation tools and highlights the propagation of measurement uncertainty into simulation outputs. Practical guidance for laboratory operators is offered throughout.

title: Envelope Spectrum Analysis for Early Bearing Fault Detection in Industrial Centrifugal Pumps
abstract: This paper examines the use of envelope spectrum analysis applied to accelerometer signals collected from the drive-end and non-drive-end bearings of three centrifugal pumps operating under variable load conditions in a food processing facility. Vibration data were recorded at 25.6 kHz over a six-month period, accumulating approximately 1,800 hours of run-time data per unit. Bandpass filter parameters were optimised using kurtosis maximisation across 48 sub-bands. The envelope spectra reliably identified outer-race defect frequencies at signal-to-noise ratios as low as 4 dB before any audible symptom appeared. Comparisons were made between healthy and seeded-fault bearings under three load levels (25%, 50%, 75% of rated capacity). Detection lead times ranged from 11 to 34 days ahead of functional failure, depending on load severity. The study provides practical filter-selection guidelines for practitioners without access to specialised diagnostic software, and discusses limitations imposed by variable shaft speed.

title: Comparison of Time-Domain Statistical Features for Gearbox Fault Classification Under Non-Stationary Load
abstract: A systematic comparison of eighteen time-domain statistical features—including RMS, crest factor, kurtosis, skewness, and several higher-order moments—is presented for the classification of four gearbox fault types: healthy, chipped tooth, missing tooth, and worn tooth. Experiments were conducted on a back-to-back gearbox test rig operating at shaft speeds between 600 and 1,800 rpm under stepwise torque profiles. Each condition was recorded over 30 independent trials of 60 seconds each. A linear discriminant analysis classifier was trained on 70% of trials and tested on 30%. Under stationary load, kurtosis and crest factor together achieved 94.2% classification accuracy. Under non-stationary load, accuracy degraded to 78.6% using the same feature set, with the most frequent confusion occurring between chipped and worn tooth conditions. The paper concludes with recommendations for feature normalisation strategies that partially recover accuracy under variable-speed operation.

title: Simultaneous Vibration and Surface Temperature Monitoring of Rolling Element Bearings: Correlation and Complementarity
abstract: Rolling element bearings in a 37 kW induction motor test stand were instrumented with both piezoelectric accelerometers and non-contact infrared thermometers to assess whether combining both signal modalities improves early fault detection compared with either modality alone. Four bearing failure modes were induced: outer-race spall, inner-race spall, ball defect, and lubrication starvation. Data were collected over 200-hour run-to-failure experiments for each condition. Correlation coefficients between vibration kurtosis and surface temperature rise were computed at 30-minute intervals. Temperature rise alone lagged vibration-based indicators by 6 to 18 hours depending on fault type. However, for lubrication starvation faults, thermal indicators reached statistically significant thresholds 4.2 hours earlier than vibration kurtosis. A simple fusion rule based on logical OR combination reduced missed detections from 12% to 3% across all fault types, with no increase in false alarm rate.

title: Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Gearbox Bearings Using Particle Filter Prognosis
abstract: This work presents a particle filter framework for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of gearbox output-shaft bearings. A state-space degradation model was constructed from experimental run-to-failure data obtained from 14 identical bearing specimens tested on an accelerated life test rig at 1,500 rpm and 110% of rated radial load. The RMS of the high-frequency band (8–16 kHz) served as the health index. Particle filter parameters—number of particles, process noise covariance, and measurement noise covariance—were tuned via cross-validation on six training runs. The model was evaluated on the remaining eight runs. Mean absolute error in RUL prediction at the 50% life-consumed point was 6.3 hours against a mean actual remaining life of 41.7 hours. Prediction uncertainty bounds narrowed progressively as fault progression advanced. The approach is compared with an extended Kalman filter baseline, which yielded a mean absolute error of 9.8 hours under the same evaluation protocol.

title: Thermal Imaging-Based Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Roller Bearings in Conveyor Systems
abstract: Slow-speed roller bearings (shaft speed 15–80 rpm) present particular challenges for vibration-based diagnostics because fault-related frequencies fall below 10 Hz and are easily masked by structural noise. This paper investigates whether infrared thermography can serve as a primary diagnostic tool in such applications. Fourteen roller bearings from operating conveyor systems in a Vojvodina grain handling facility were inspected quarterly over 18 months using a calibrated thermal camera with a 320×240 focal plane array and 0.05 °C thermal resolution. Temperature differentials between the bearing housing and ambient were logged alongside manually assessed visual condition grades. A threshold of 8 °C above ambient was found to coincide reliably with the onset of detectable surface pitting, while a 15 °C differential indicated advanced degradation requiring imminent replacement. The paper also discusses emissivity correction procedures for painted versus bare metal housings and quantifies the effect of ambient air movement on measurement repeatability.

title: Multivariate Statistical Process Control for Simultaneous Monitoring of Multiple Bearing Locations in Rotating Machinery
abstract: Industrial rotating machines are typically equipped with multiple bearing points whose health may degrade independently or in coupled fashion. This paper develops a multivariate statistical process control framework, based on Hotelling's T² and the Q-statistic derived from principal component analysis, applied simultaneously to vibration features extracted from four bearing positions on a two-stage gearbox test stand. Feature vectors comprising RMS, kurtosis, and spectral energy in four frequency bands were computed from 1-second data windows at 30-second intervals over 900 hours of monitored operation including 22 seeded fault events. The Hotelling T² chart detected 19 of the 22 events, with a mean detection lag of 1.4 hours and 2 false alarms during the healthy baseline period. The Q-statistic contributed complementary sensitivity for four events missed or delayed by T². The paper discusses the selection of the number of retained principal components and the impact of load variation on control limit stability.

title: Transfer Learning for Bearing Fault Diagnosis When Source and Target Domains Differ in Machine Size and Speed
abstract: Labelled run-to-failure data from small laboratory test rigs are abundant, while equivalent data from large industrial machines are scarce. This paper investigates domain adaptation via fine-tuning of a convolutional neural network pre-trained on laboratory bearing data (shaft diameter 30 mm, 1,500 rpm) and applied to a 250 kW industrial motor (shaft diameter 100 mm, 750 rpm). The source dataset comprised 3,200 labelled one-second vibration windows across four fault classes; the target domain provided only 80 labelled windows per class for fine-tuning. Without adaptation, accuracy on the target domain was 61.4%. Fine-tuning the last two convolutional blocks on the small target dataset raised accuracy to 83.9%. Further improvement to 87.2% was obtained by including adversarial domain alignment of intermediate feature representations. The paper analyses which convolutional layers encode transferable versus domain-specific features, finding that the first two layers consistently transferred well regardless of machine size ratio.

title: Edge-Deployable Anomaly Detection for Pump Monitoring Using Autoencoder Compression of Vibration Spectra
abstract: Deploying data-driven condition monitoring at the network edge requires models small enough to run on microcontroller-class hardware. This paper describes the design, training, and deployment of a sparse autoencoder that compresses 512-point FFT spectra from pump bearing accelerometers into 16-dimensional bottleneck representations. The autoencoder was trained exclusively on healthy operation data from six pumps over three months (approximately 4.7 million spectrum snapshots). Reconstruction error served as the anomaly score. The deployed model occupied 47 kB of flash memory on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller and executed inference in 2.3 ms per spectrum. Over a subsequent 14-month monitoring period covering three pump failures and one false alarm, the system detected all three failures between 8 and 31 days before shutdown, with a false alarm rate of 0.7 events per pump per year. Power consumption of the monitoring node averaged 210 mW, enabling battery-backed installation.

title: Quantifying Measurement Uncertainty in Vibration-Based Health Indicators and Its Propagation Into Remaining Useful Life Estimates
abstract: RUL predictions are often presented as point estimates without propagating the uncertainty arising from sensor noise, mounting variability, and feature computation choices. This paper applies a Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis to quantify how measurement uncertainty in accelerometer-derived RMS and kurtosis propagates through a particle filter RUL estimator. Accelerometer mounting experiments showed that torque variations in stud-mounted sensors caused RMS variability of ±2.1% and kurtosis variability of ±8.7% across five remounting repetitions on the same bearing. A parametric bootstrap procedure with 10,000 replications was used to construct 90% confidence intervals for RUL at three degradation stages across 12 run-to-failure experiments. Confidence interval widths at the 30% life-consumed stage spanned 60–80% of the actual remaining life, narrowing to 25–35% at the 70% life-consumed stage. The study recommends reporting RUL distributions rather than point estimates and provides an open-source Python implementation of the uncertainty propagation procedure.

title: Combined Vibration and Oil Debris Monitoring for Planetary Gearbox Prognostics in Wind Turbine Drivetrains
abstract: Planetary gearboxes in wind turbines are subject to variable and non-stationary loading that complicates both vibration signal interpretation and single-modality prognosis. This paper reports a 26-month field study on four 850 kW wind turbines in which accelerometers, oil debris sensors, and oil temperature loggers were installed on the main gearboxes. Vibration features were computed after order-tracking resampling to remove speed-induced non-stationarity. Oil debris particle counts above 200 µm were logged every 15 minutes. A random forest regressor trained on combined feature vectors from both modalities outperformed vibration-only (MAPE 18.4% versus 26.1%) and oil-debris-only (MAPE 29.7%) models for RUL prediction evaluated on held-out turbine data. Shapley value analysis identified oil debris count rate and vibration kurtosis at the ring-gear mesh frequency as the two highest-importance features. One turbine experienced a ring-gear failure that was correctly predicted 37 days in advance with a 90% probability interval spanning 22–49 days.

title: Calcium and boron distribution in vegetative and reproductive organs of 'Zlatni Delišes' apple grafted on four clonal rootstocks
abstract: Calcium and boron deficiency disorders remain a primary cause of fruit quality loss in intensive apple production across the Vojvodina region. This study examined the partitioning of Ca and B into leaves, shoot bark, and fruit flesh of 'Zlatni Delišes' scion grafted onto M.9, M.26, MM.106, and a local Vojvodina selection designated VNS-4, planted at 3,300 trees per hectare at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station. Over three consecutive growing seasons (2009–2011), leaf samples were collected at four phenological stages per season and digested by wet acid procedure prior to ICP-OES analysis. Fruit Ca concentrations in trees on M.9 averaged 42.3 mg kg⁻¹ fresh weight, significantly lower than on MM.106 (61.7 mg kg⁻¹), while B levels showed no rootstock-dependent difference at final harvest. Differences in Ca partitioning were associated with measured transpiration rates and stomatal conductance data. The results suggest that rootstock vigour class influences calcium mobility more strongly than boron transport in this cultivar-site combination.

title: Potassium–calcium antagonism in apple fruit as modified by rootstock and crop load
abstract: Antagonistic interactions between potassium and calcium in apple fruit are well documented but their dependence on rootstock identity and crop load level has not been systematically studied in the Pannonian climate zone. A two-factor experiment with 'Gala Schniga' on M.9 and Geneva 935 rootstocks at Rimski Šančevi compared three manually adjusted crop loads (40, 80, and 120 fruits per tree) over the 2014 and 2015 seasons. Fruit mineral concentrations at commercial harvest were determined by ICP-OES; K:Ca molar ratios were computed for cortex and core tissue separately. Fruit K:Ca ratio was 32% higher on Geneva 935 at heavy crop load, while on M.9 the ratio remained stable across crop loads. Bitter pit incidence at 60 days of controlled atmosphere storage reached 11.4% on Geneva 935 at heavy crop load versus 3.8% on M.9. The interaction between rootstock and crop load was statistically significant for fruit Ca (p < 0.01) but not for Mg or P. Practical thinning guidelines for each rootstock are proposed.

title: Response of foliar-applied calcium to rootstock-determined transpiration rates in high-density apple orchards
abstract: Foliar calcium sprays are widely recommended to reduce bitter pit but their efficacy may depend on canopy transpiration, which is partly rootstock-determined. A three-year trial (2017–2019) at two commercial orchards in Fruška Gora foothills compared the effect of five foliar CaCl₂ spray programmes (0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 applications at 0.5% concentration) in 'Šampion' apple on M.9 T337 and MM.106. Stomatal conductance was measured fortnightly by porometry on southern-facing shoots; fruit Ca at harvest and bitter pit incidence after 90 days of refrigerated storage were recorded. Fruit Ca response per spray application was 1.8 mg kg⁻¹ on M.9 versus 2.6 mg kg⁻¹ on MM.106, consistent with higher stomatal conductance on MM.106 (+23%). Bitter pit reduction followed the same pattern. Regression models suggest that rootstock selection alters the cost-effectiveness of foliar calcium programmes and should be accounted for in spray scheduling recommendations.

title: Rootstock-mediated changes in phloem sap mineral composition of apple during the fruit-filling period
abstract: Phloem transport is the dominant pathway for K and Mg delivery to developing apple fruit, but direct sampling of phloem sap in woody perennials is methodologically challenging. This study used the EDTA-facilitated exudate method on bark strips collected from current-year shoots of 'Topaz' apple on M.9 T337, B.9, and Supporter 4 rootstocks at 14-day intervals from petal fall to 30 days before harvest in 2020 and 2021. Exudate mineral concentrations were measured by ICP-OES and amino acid profiles by HPLC. Supporter 4 produced exudates with 28% higher K and 41% higher glutamine concentrations compared to M.9 at peak fruit-filling stage. Fruit K at harvest was positively correlated with mid-season phloem K (r = 0.73, p < 0.001). No significant difference in phloem Ca was detected, consistent with the established xylem-dominant pathway for Ca. The data provide direct evidence that rootstock modulates phloem mineral composition independently of canopy leaf area.

title: Zinc and manganese uptake efficiency in apple: rootstock ranking across three soil types in Vojvodina
abstract: Micronutrient deficiencies of Zn and Mn are increasingly reported in high-density apple orchards on calcareous soils of Vojvodina. This multi-site study compared leaf and fruit Zn and Mn concentrations in 'Granny Smith' and 'Idared' scions on six rootstocks (M.9, M.26, MM.106, Geneva 935, Geneva 202, and B.9) established on chernozem, meadow soil, and sandy soil at three locations in the Vojvodina plain. Sites were sampled over three growing seasons (2020–2022). Soil Zn and Mn fractions (exchangeable, reducible, oxidisable, residual) were extracted by BCR sequential extraction. On calcareous meadow soil (pH 7.9), leaf Zn in trees on M.26 was 23% lower than on Geneva 202. Rootstock ranking for Mn uptake was consistent across soil types, with MM.106 producing consistently higher leaf Mn, while Geneva 935 produced the lowest. No rootstock × cultivar interaction was significant for Zn. Results suggest rootstock selection is a viable agronomic tool for managing micronutrient supply on problem soils without additional foliar applications.

title: Nutrient partitioning strategies in biennial bearing apple: rootstock modulation of the crop-to-vegetative tissue mineral allocation ratio
abstract: Biennial bearing in apple results in large year-to-year variation in sink demand for minerals, yet whether rootstock identity modulates the allocation of nutrients between fruit and vegetative compartments during on- and off-years remains unresolved. 'Elstar' on M.9 NAKB T337 and Geneva 935 was monitored across four consecutive seasons (2020–2023) at Rimski Šančevi; trees exhibiting natural biennial bearing were identified by yield records and separated from regular bearers. Leaf, shoot, and fruit mineral data were collected at harvest and post-harvest defoliation. The fraction of total tree N and K allocated to fruit in on-years was 12 percentage points higher on Geneva 935 than on M.9, while Ca allocation to fruit did not differ between rootstocks in either bearing year. In off-years, M.9 stored proportionally more N in bark compared to Geneva 935. The data suggest rootstock-dependent differences in reserve nutrient dynamics that interact with the biennial bearing cycle and may influence the nitrogen fertilisation needs across years.

title: Standardising leaf sampling protocols for mineral diagnostics in apple orchards: effect of rootstock, leaf position, and time of day
abstract: Interpretation of apple leaf mineral analysis for nutritional diagnosis relies on standardised sampling, yet existing guidelines were largely developed without accounting for rootstock identity or intra-canopy variation. This study tested the interaction of rootstock (M.9, Geneva 202), leaf position (basal, mid, and terminal on current-year shoots), and sampling time (06:00, 12:00, 18:00 h) on leaf concentrations of N, Ca, K, Mg, Fe, and Zn in 'Fuji' apple at a commercial orchard in Sremski Karlovci over two seasons (2024–2025). Analysis of variance showed significant rootstock × leaf position interactions for Ca (p < 0.001) and K (p < 0.01) but not for N. Time-of-day effects were significant only for K on Geneva 202 (afternoon values 8% higher than morning). The study recommends mid-shoot, mid-morning sampling as the most reproducible protocol across rootstock types and provides revised diagnostic reference ranges based on a dataset of 2,640 leaf samples.
