title: Combining rootstock selection and fertigation composition to optimise calcium-to-potassium ratios in apple fruit: a two-rootstock fertigation trial
abstract: Fertigation offers precision control over ionic ratios in the root zone, but its effectiveness in improving fruit Ca:K balance may be conditioned by rootstock. A factorial trial at Rimski Šančevi (2024–2026 seasons, third season ongoing) tests two rootstocks (M.9 NAKB T337, Geneva 202) crossed with three fertigation Ca:K ionic ratio treatments (1:3, 1:5, and 1:8 Ca:K molar ratio, balanced for total ionic strength) in 'Gala Schniga'. Drip fertigation was managed with EC and pH-compensated injection. Preliminary data from 2024–2025 show that Geneva 202 trees under the 1:3 treatment achieved fruit Ca of 58.2 mg kg⁻¹ compared to 44.7 mg kg⁻¹ on M.9 under the same treatment. The K:Ca molar ratio in fruit cortex tissue showed a significant fertigation × rootstock interaction only on Geneva 202. Bitter pit incidence in storage and fruit firmness data from the third season are pending. This preprint presents the design and first two seasons of results.

title: Exogenous gibberellin application as a partial substitute for chilling in sweet cherry: hormonal and phenological outcomes
abstract: In years with low chill accumulation, growers sometimes apply hydrogen cyanamide to overcome dormancy, but this compound carries occupational health concerns. Exogenous gibberellins have been proposed as a less hazardous alternative. We treated potted 'Regina' sweet cherry trees that had received only 25 or 30 CP with single or double foliar sprays of GA₃ at 50 or 100 mg L⁻¹ and compared bud burst outcomes with untreated controls at the same chilling levels and a full-chill control (50 CP). Endogenous ABA was measured 7 days post-treatment by LC-MS/MS. The 100 mg L⁻¹ double-spray reduced endogenous ABA by 35% relative to untreated low-chill controls and advanced bud burst by 8–11 days, but synchrony remained lower than in the full-chill control (coefficient of variation 18% vs. 7%). Fruit set in the partially substituted treatment was 22% lower than in the full-chill control. Results indicate partial hormonal compensation but do not fully replicate the chilling-driven hormonal programme.

title: Phenolic characterisation of elderberry accessions from a Serbian field gene bank using LC-MS/MS: identification of minor compounds not detected by HPLC-DAD
abstract: A collection of 18 Sambucus nigra accessions maintained at the Serbian Plant Genetic Resources Centre was re-analysed using LC-MS/MS to complement earlier HPLC-DAD datasets generated between 1997 and 2013. Fourteen previously undetected or tentatively identified compounds were resolved, including three kaempferol glycosides, two quercetin derivatives, and feruloylquinic acid. Chrysanthemin (cyanidin-3-glucoside) remained the dominant anthocyanin across all accessions, but two accessions showed elevated concentrations of pelargonidin-3-glucoside (up to 0.8 mg g−1 DW), a compound not previously reported in Pannonian elderberry material. Total identified phenolic compounds ranged from 28 to 41 per accession. The revised compound list updates the reference chromatographic library held at the Faculty of Agriculture and provides a basis for chemotyping the gene bank collection. The study underscores the value of upgrading analytical platforms when revisiting archived plant material.

title: Pitting susceptibility of AISI 316L stainless steel in synthetic tap water with increasing chloride concentration
abstract: Potentiodynamic polarisation and scanning electron microscopy were used to examine pitting initiation on AISI 316L coupons immersed in synthetic tap water at chloride concentrations of 50, 150, 300, and 500 mg/L. Experiments were conducted at 22 °C and pH 7.4. Pitting potential shifted cathodically by approximately 180 mV as chloride concentration increased from 50 to 500 mg/L, while repassivation potential showed a less pronounced dependence. Cross-sectional SEM of corroded coupons revealed subsurface undercutting at MnS inclusion sites, with pit mouths averaging 12 µm in diameter at 300 mg/L chloride after 96-hour immersion. Energy-dispersive X-ray analysis confirmed sulphur enrichment at the pit base. The results indicate that inclusion density and chloride concentration together govern the statistical distribution of pit nucleation events, and that the standard 250 mg/L chloride threshold used in Serbian water quality regulation provides only marginal protection against pitting in aged 316L installations.

title: Electrochemical impedance characterisation of passive films formed on austenitic steels in low-mineralisation drinking water
abstract: Passive films grown on AISI 304 and AISI 316L in low-mineralisation drinking water (total dissolved solids 85 mg/L) were characterised by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy over a frequency range of 100 kHz to 10 mHz. Specimens were held at open-circuit potential for 1, 7, and 30 days before measurement. Equivalent circuit fitting using a two-layer model (outer hydroxide/inner oxide) showed that the inner-layer capacitance decreased from 38 µF/cm² to 21 µF/cm² for 316L over 30 days, indicating film thickening and increased barrier properties. The Mott–Schottky analysis revealed n-type semiconducting behaviour for both alloys, with donor densities of 1.4 × 10²¹ cm⁻³ and 9.8 × 10²⁰ cm⁻³ for 304 and 316L respectively at 30 days. Molybdenum content in 316L is identified as the primary factor governing the lower donor density and, consequently, the more stable passive film in this environment.

title: Sulphate-reducing bacteria isolation from corroded stainless steel pipe sections in a municipal water network in Vojvodina
abstract: Pipe sections of AISI 304 removed during maintenance of a municipal water distribution network in northern Vojvodina were examined for microbial colonisation. Biofilm swabs and corrosion product scrapings were cultured in modified Postgate B medium under strictly anaerobic conditions at 30 °C. Three distinct sulphate-reducing bacterial (SRB) strains were isolated and identified by 16S rRNA gene sequencing as belonging to the genera Desulfovibrio and Desulfomicrobium. Corrosion product analysis by XRD showed the presence of mackinawite (FeS), greigite (Fe₃S₄), and iron sulphate hydrate phases. Pitting density on the inner pipe surface reached 140 pits/cm² in areas with confirmed biofilm, compared to fewer than 10 pits/cm² on pipe sections with no detectable biofilm. The study provides the first documented characterisation of MIC-active SRB strains in a functioning potable water network in the Vojvodina region.

title: Combined effect of chloride and sulphate ions on the corrosion behaviour of AISI 316L in simulated potable water at 25 and 50 °C
abstract: The antagonistic and synergistic effects of chloride and sulphate ions on corrosion of AISI 316L were investigated by varying Cl⁻ from 0 to 400 mg/L and SO₄²⁻ from 0 to 300 mg/L at 25 and 50 °C in deaerated aqueous solutions at pH 7.4. Corrosion current density was measured by linear polarisation resistance at 24-hour intervals over 14 days. At 25 °C, sulphate up to 100 mg/L marginally inhibited pit initiation at low chloride concentrations (≤100 mg/L), consistent with competitive adsorption on the passive film surface. At chloride concentrations above 250 mg/L, sulphate provided no protective effect. At 50 °C, pitting potential was 95 mV lower on average than at 25 °C across all ion combinations, and passive current densities increased by a factor of 2.4. The results suggest that temperature elevation in summer months significantly aggravates corrosion risk in distribution networks with suboptimal water chemistry control.

title: Effect of Desulfovibrio sp. biofilm on electrochemical noise and pitting statistics of austenitic stainless steel
abstract: Electrochemical noise measurements in the time domain were used to monitor the activity of Desulfovibrio sp. biofilm on AISI 316L in a modified Postgate C medium containing 150 mg/L chloride over 21 days. Current and potential noise signals were recorded at 1 Hz sampling frequency. Noise resistance, computed from the ratio of potential noise standard deviation to current noise standard deviation, dropped from an initial 42 kΩ·cm² to 6.3 kΩ·cm² between days 7 and 14, coinciding with the exponential growth phase of the biofilm. Localisation index analysis indicated a transition from general to localised corrosion at this stage. Post-exposure SEM showed pit depths up to 45 µm in biofilm-covered areas. Control specimens in sterile medium at the same chloride concentration showed a maximum pit depth of 8 µm after 21 days. The difference confirms that SRB metabolic activity accelerates pit propagation beyond what is expected from the ionic environment alone.

title: Seasonal variation in biofilm composition and corrosion rate on stainless steel fittings in a cold-water distribution network
abstract: Removable AISI 316L coupons were installed at six monitoring points in a cold-water distribution network operated by a mid-sized Serbian municipality and retrieved quarterly over two years. Biofilm dry mass, cell counts, SRB fraction, and corrosion rate by mass loss were measured for each retrieval. Biofilm dry mass ranged from 0.3 µg/cm² in winter to 4.8 µg/cm² in late summer. SRB constituted between 2% and 18% of the culturable bacterial population, with peak values in August and September. Mean corrosion rates followed a seasonal pattern consistent with biofilm development, ranging from 0.8 µm/year in February to 6.7 µm/year in September. Linear regression indicated that SRB cell count per cm² was a stronger predictor of corrosion rate (R² = 0.74) than temperature alone (R² = 0.51). The dataset supports targeted monitoring campaigns during warmer months in distribution systems using austenitic steel components.

title: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy characterisation of passive films on AISI 304 corroded under MIC conditions
abstract: Passive films on AISI 304 specimens exposed to Desulfovibrio sp. biofilm in synthetic potable water (200 mg/L Cl⁻, pH 7.2, 30 °C) for 28 days were characterised by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Survey and high-resolution spectra were acquired for Fe 2p, Cr 2p, Ni 2p, Mo 3d, S 2p, and O 1s regions. The Cr/Fe atomic ratio in the outer film layer decreased from 1.4 in sterile controls to 0.9 in biofilm-exposed specimens, indicating preferential iron dissolution under MIC conditions. Sulphur was detected in the S²⁻ and S⁰ oxidation states at concentrations of up to 3.8 at.% in biofilm-exposed samples but was below detection in controls. Curve fitting of the Fe 2p₃/₂ envelope showed increased Fe²⁺ content (from 31% to 52% of total iron) in biofilm samples, confirming partial reduction of the protective Fe³⁺ oxide. These compositional changes are consistent with cathodic depolarisation by SRB and direct electron transfer mechanisms.

title: Modelling pitting induction time on austenitic steel under variable chloride and biofilm loading using a stochastic approach
abstract: A stochastic model for pitting induction time was developed and calibrated using experimental data from 180 individual AISI 316L specimens exposed to conditions spanning Cl⁻ concentrations of 50–450 mg/L and biofilm cell densities of 10³–10⁷ cells/cm². A Weibull distribution was fitted to pit initiation times at each condition. The shape parameter β ranged from 1.4 (low Cl⁻, no biofilm) to 3.1 (high Cl⁻, dense biofilm), indicating a transition from random to wear-out-like failure statistics. Scale parameter η decreased from 820 hours to 94 hours across the same range. The model was validated against an independent dataset from a separate laboratory in Kragujevac with good agreement (mean absolute error 9.3 hours). Sensitivity analysis showed that biofilm cell density above 10⁵ cells/cm² had a larger influence on η than a doubling of chloride concentration, underlining the importance of microbiological control in predictive maintenance frameworks.

title: Influence of residual chlorine concentration on SRB biofilm formation and associated corrosion of stainless steel in drinking water
abstract: The effect of free chlorine residual (0, 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 mg/L as Cl₂) on Desulfovibrio sp. biofilm development and corrosion of AISI 316L was investigated in a recirculating flow-loop system at 22 °C over 35 days. Chlorine was dosed continuously by a peristaltic pump and monitored with an amperometric online sensor. At 0.3 mg/L chlorine, biofilm dry mass was reduced by 74% relative to the uncharged control and SRB viable counts decreased by 2.6 log units. Corresponding corrosion rates fell from 5.4 µm/year (no chlorine) to 1.9 µm/year at 0.3 mg/L and 1.5 µm/year at 0.5 mg/L, suggesting diminishing returns above 0.3 mg/L. However, at 0.5 mg/L chlorine, general corrosion current density was 18% higher than at 0.3 mg/L, attributed to the oxidising action of hypochlorous acid on the passive film. These results suggest that the Serbian regulatory upper limit of 0.5 mg/L residual chlorine is appropriate from a corrosion perspective but that maintaining levels consistently above 0.3 mg/L is important for MIC suppression.

title: Comparative corrosion performance of AISI 304, 316L, and duplex 2205 steels in potable water with elevated sulphate at elevated temperature
abstract: Three stainless steel grades — AISI 304, AISI 316L, and duplex 2205 — were compared under potable water conditions with sulphate concentrations of 50, 150, and 250 mg/L at 40 °C and fixed chloride of 200 mg/L. Electrochemical measurements (potentiodynamic polarisation, EIS, and electrochemical noise) were supplemented by profilometry after 30-day immersion tests. Duplex 2205 showed no stable pitting below 250 mg/L SO₄²⁻, while 304 exhibited localised attack above 50 mg/L SO₄²⁻ combined with 200 mg/L Cl⁻. The pitting potential of 316L was intermediate, averaging −25 mV vs SCE at the harshest condition, compared to −130 mV for 304 and +220 mV for 2205. Maximum pit depths measured by confocal profilometry were 38, 21, and 4 µm for 304, 316L, and 2205 respectively. Cost-adjusted corrosion performance indices are calculated to inform material selection decisions for new drinking water infrastructure.

title: Accelerated ageing of coated duplex board under ISO 5630-3 conditions: changes in WVTR, stiffness, and colour over 168 hours
abstract: Duplex board samples (350 g/m²) coated with three systems — LDPE extrusion, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) dispersion, and an acrylic–wax hybrid — were aged under ISO 5630-3 conditions (90 °C, 50 % RH) for periods of 24, 72, 120, and 168 hours. After each interval, WVTR (ISO 2528, 38 °C/90 % RH), four-point bending stiffness, and CIE L*a*b* colour coordinates were measured. LDPE-coated samples showed negligible WVTR change (<5 %) across all ageing intervals. PVA coatings degraded most rapidly, with WVTR increasing by 210 % after 168 hours, accompanied by visible yellowing (ΔE* = 8.3). The acrylic–wax hybrid occupied an intermediate position. Bending stiffness declined for all samples, with the greatest loss (22 %) recorded for PVA-coated boards, consistent with plasticiser migration observed in FTIR spectra. The study provides reference degradation curves for shelf-life modelling of coated paperboard.

title: Influence of silicon content on bainitic transformation kinetics in low-alloy TRIP steels studied by quenching dilatometry
abstract: Four steel grades with silicon content varying from 0.8 to 2.0 wt% and constant carbon (0.22 wt%) and manganese (1.8 wt%) contents were studied. Quenching dilatometry experiments at isothermal temperatures of 340 °C, 380 °C, 420 °C, and 460 °C covered a range of 120 to 7200 s holding time. Transformation kinetics were modelled using the Avrami equation; the Avrami exponent n ranged from 1.4 to 2.2 depending on silicon content and temperature. Higher silicon delayed the onset of bainite formation and reduced the overall transformed fraction at all temperatures, consistent with silicon's role in retarding cementite precipitation. At 1.6–2.0 wt% Si, bainite transformation was incomplete even after 7200 s at 380 °C, with untransformed austenite fraction above 12 vol% confirmed by XRD. The results show that silicon content above 1.6 wt% provides a sufficiently wide isothermal processing window to retain mechanically stable austenite without forming carbides.

title: Steady-state temperature profiles in a horizontal tubular photobioreactor under Central European summer conditions
abstract: A one-dimensional steady-state thermal model was developed for a horizontal tubular photobioreactor operating under measured outdoor irradiance and air-temperature data collected near Novi Sad during July 2008. The model couples a Beer–Lambert light attenuation submodel with a convective heat balance along a 40-m polyethylene tube loop of 5 cm internal diameter. Predicted axial temperature profiles were compared against 24 thermocouple measurements spaced every 1.7 m. The mean absolute deviation between model and experiment was 1.3 °C across a diurnal cycle with peak irradiance reaching 920 W/m². Sensitivity analysis showed that wind speed was the dominant factor controlling maximum culture temperature, contributing roughly 60 % of total variance. The model correctly predicted peak temperatures exceeding 38 °C during afternoon hours, a range known to suppress Chlorella vulgaris growth rates by up to 30 %. The study provides a validated baseline for evaluating passive cooling strategies and was used to size a simple shade-net intervention that reduced peak temperature by 4.1 °C in a follow-up field test.

title: Radiation field heterogeneity in raceway ponds: measurements and CFD validation at laboratory and pilot scale
abstract: Accurate knowledge of the local photon flux density inside raceway ponds is needed to link hydrodynamic mixing with photosynthetic efficiency. This paper reports submersible quantum sensor measurements at 48 spatial positions in a 6 m² laboratory paddle-wheel raceway and a 42 m² pilot pond, both operating with Arthrospira platensis suspensions at optical densities between 0.4 and 2.1 at 680 nm. A RANS-based CFD model using the k–ε turbulence closure was coupled with a discrete-ordinates radiation solver. Simulated irradiance distributions agreed with measured data to within 12 % root-mean-square error at both scales. The model revealed that approximately 35 % of the pond volume experienced irradiance below the compensation point of the cultivated strain during overcast conditions at the pilot scale. Increasing paddle-wheel speed from 15 to 25 rpm reduced the fraction of light-limited volume by 8 percentage points but increased pumping energy by 31 %. The trade-off is quantified and discussed in the context of seasonal operation.

title: Seasonal variation in areal biomass productivity of a 200 m² outdoor raceway pond in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Twelve months of continuous operation data from a 200 m² outdoor raceway pond cultivating Chlorella vulgaris at a demonstration site near Novi Sad are analysed. Monthly mean areal productivities ranged from 3.1 g/m²/d in December to 18.7 g/m²/d in July, with a mean annual value of 10.4 g/m²/d. Culture temperature, incident photosynthetically active radiation, and mixing depth were identified as the principal controlling variables through partial correlation analysis. Growth rate declined sharply below 12 °C and was negligible during six days when temperature fell below 8 °C. An empirical seasonal production model fitted to the dataset reproduced observed monthly totals with a mean absolute error of 1.8 g/m²/d. The analysis suggests that a 30-day curtailment in winter would save approximately 14 % of annual pumping and CO₂ costs while sacrificing less than 7 % of annual biomass yield, informing operational scheduling decisions for commercial-scale facilities in continental climates.

title: Heat integration between microalgal cultivation and a biogas upgrading unit using pinch analysis
abstract: Microalgal cultivation and biogas CO₂ scrubbing can be thermally coupled to reduce net energy demand, but the extent of feasible integration has not been studied for small-scale facilities typical of Serbian agro-industrial settings. This paper applies sequential pinch analysis to a hypothetical 1-ha facility combining a flat-panel photobioreactor array, an anaerobic digester, and a water-scrubbing biogas upgrading unit. Stream data were extracted from measured operating parameters and literature sources. The minimum hot and cold utility targets at a ΔTmin of 10 °C were 28 kW and 41 kW respectively, compared to 67 kW and 80 kW in the non-integrated base case. A heat exchanger network with six units was synthesised to approach these targets. Capital cost of the network was estimated at approximately €18 000. Simple payback on the integration investment was estimated at 3.2 years under current Serbian natural gas prices. Sensitivity to gas price and cultivation season length was also assessed.

title: Effect of CO₂ feeding strategy on pH stability and carbon use efficiency in a tubular photobioreactor
abstract: Carbon dioxide supply influences both pH and carbon availability in closed photobioreactor systems, and the two effects are difficult to decouple experimentally. An on-demand pH-stat controller was compared against fixed-interval CO₂ injection in a 40-litre helical tubular photobioreactor over 21-day Nannochloropsis gaditana batch cultivations. Under the pH-stat strategy, pH was maintained within ±0.15 units of the setpoint (7.5) throughout the photoperiod, whereas fixed-interval injection caused pH swings up to 0.9 units. Carbon use efficiency, calculated from inlet and exhaust gas concentrations measured by non-dispersive infrared sensors, was 71 % under pH-stat control versus 52 % under the fixed-interval protocol. Biomass productivity was 8 % higher under pH-stat conditions. The CO₂ cost saving per kilogram of biomass produced was calculated at €0.11 based on industrial CO₂ prices. The study supports on-demand control as the preferred strategy even when the associated sensor and actuator costs are accounted for.

title: Techno-economic assessment of microalgae-to-biodiesel production at two scales in Serbia
abstract: A detailed techno-economic model was constructed for hypothetical microalgal biodiesel facilities at 10-ha and 50-ha scales operating under Serbian climatic and economic conditions. Mass and energy balances were built from first principles using Chlorella protothecoides as the reference organism with a lipid content of 38 % dry weight under nitrogen-limited conditions. Capital expenditure was estimated using factored cost estimation from vendor quotations and literature for major equipment items. At the 10-ha scale, the minimum selling price (MSP) of biodiesel was €9.20/L; at 50-ha scale it fell to €5.40/L owing to economies of scale in harvesting and extraction. Sensitivity analysis identified biomass productivity, lipid content, and harvesting cost as the three most influential parameters, together contributing 74 % of MSP variance. Co-product credits from glycerol and protein-rich residue reduced the MSP by approximately 18 % at 50-ha scale. The study concludes that profitability under current market conditions requires either a substantial premium for high-value co-products or significant reduction in harvesting energy consumption.

title: Light attenuation modelling in dense microalgal suspensions: comparison of exponential, hyperbolic and two-flux models
abstract: Three analytical light attenuation models—the Lambert–Beer exponential model, a hyperbolic correction accounting for scattering, and the Kubelka–Munk two-flux model—were evaluated against spectrophotometric and integrating-sphere measurements of photon fluence rate in Spirulina platensis suspensions across a biomass concentration range of 0.3–4.5 g/L and path lengths of 0.5–10 cm. Absorption and scattering coefficients were determined independently for each strain and concentration level. The two-flux model showed the lowest root-mean-square error (5.8 %) across all conditions, while the Lambert–Beer model was adequate only at concentrations below 1.0 g/L and path lengths below 3 cm. The hyperbolic correction offered intermediate accuracy (9.2 % RMSE) with lower parametric complexity. Recommendations are given for which model is appropriate at different operating points, with the aim of providing guidance for integration into photobioreactor CFD codes without unnecessary computational overhead.

title: Passive thermal regulation in open raceway ponds using underground heat exchange: a pilot-scale study
abstract: Maintaining culture temperatures within acceptable bounds during cold Pannonian autumn nights without active heating is challenging. This study tested a passive earth-tube heat exchanger buried at 2.5 m depth and connected to the recirculation loop of a 42 m² pilot raceway pond. The system extracted approximately 1.8 kW on average during October nights, raising overnight minimum culture temperature by 3.1 °C compared to an uninsulated control pond. Biomass productivity in October was 12.4 g/m²/d with the earth-tube system versus 9.6 g/m²/d in the control. Soil thermal conductivity was measured in situ using a line-source probe. A finite-element thermal model of the soil–tube system was calibrated against hourly soil and fluid temperature measurements and reproduced observed fluid outlet temperatures with a mean absolute error of 0.7 °C. Seasonal economic analysis suggests the earth-tube investment of approximately €3 200 for the pilot scale could be recovered within two growing seasons at commercial scale.

title: Life cycle energy analysis of microalgal biomass production in a hybrid photobioreactor–open-pond system in Serbia
abstract: A lifecycle energy analysis was conducted for a hybrid system in which a tubular photobioreactor produces inoculum that is then transferred to outdoor open ponds for bulk biomass growth, using Chlorella vulgaris under Serbian conditions. Inventory data were collected from a 0.5-ha pilot hybrid facility operated over two full growing seasons. Cumulative energy demand was calculated following ISO 14044 guidelines. Total on-site energy consumption was 14.3 MJ per kilogram of dry biomass. Harvesting by centrifugation was the single largest energy consumer at 38 % of the total, followed by CO₂ supply (22 %) and mixing (19 %). A scenario analysis examined replacing centrifugation with flocculation-based harvesting, which reduced total energy demand to 9.8 MJ/kg but introduced chemical material costs. The ratio of energy produced as biomass higher heating value to total energy input was 1.31 for the centrifugation scenario and 1.92 for the flocculation scenario, both based on complete combustion of ash-free biomass.

title: Multi-objective optimisation of operating conditions in flat-panel photobioreactors using surrogate-assisted genetic algorithms
abstract: Operating a flat-panel photobioreactor to simultaneously maximise biomass productivity and minimise energy consumption involves competing objectives that cannot be resolved by single-objective optimisation. This study applied a surrogate-assisted NSGA-II genetic algorithm to identify Pareto-optimal operating strategies for a 120-litre pilot unit cultivating Haematococcus lacustris. A kriging surrogate model was trained on 180 steady-state operating points generated through a Latin hypercube design covering aeration rate, dilution rate, harvesting interval, and CO₂ setpoint. The Pareto front contained 34 non-dominated solutions. Compared to the operator-defined baseline, solutions on the front achieved either a 19 % increase in biomass productivity at constant energy input or a 24 % reduction in energy consumption at constant productivity. Experimental validation of three selected Pareto solutions showed agreement with surrogate predictions within 8 %. The framework is computationally inexpensive enough to be re-run monthly to account for seasonal shifts in ambient conditions.

title: Sensitivity of optimal high-side pressure to ambient humidity in transcritical CO₂ systems with wet gas-cooler pre-cooling: a simulation study
abstract: Adiabatic pre-cooling pads reduce the effective inlet temperature to the gas cooler but introduce a dependence on ambient relative humidity that is seldom examined in isolation from temperature effects. This preprint investigates how the optimal high-side pressure and corresponding COP change as relative humidity varies from 30 % to 80 % at fixed dry-bulb temperatures of 32 °C, 36 °C, and 40 °C, conditions typical of humid anticyclone episodes in the Carpathian Basin. The simulation couples a psychrometric evaporative-cooling model with the validated transcritical booster cycle model. At 36 °C dry-bulb, moving from 30 % to 80 % relative humidity raises the optimal high-side pressure by 4.2 bar and reduces COP by 5.7 %. The results suggest that humidity-adaptive pressure control could partially compensate for this loss, and a simple proportional correction factor based on wet-bulb temperature is proposed. The analysis uses hourly MERRA-2 reanalysis data for Vojvodina (2015–2020) to estimate how many operating hours fall into humidity regimes where the correction would yield more than 1 % COP improvement.

title: Discharge Behaviour of Li/SOCl₂ Cells Under Periodic Pulsed Loads at Low Ambient Temperature
abstract: Primary lithium thionyl chloride cells are widely deployed in remote sensing applications where loads are intermittent and temperatures can fall below 0 °C. This study characterises the discharge behaviour of twelve commercially available Li/SOCl₂ cells subjected to pulse trains with duty cycles of 2 %, 5 %, and 10 % at temperatures of +25 °C, 0 °C, and −15 °C. Cell voltage recovery curves were logged at 100 ms resolution. A passivation-layer resistance term was extracted from each voltage dip using a two-RC equivalent-circuit model fitted by nonlinear least squares. Results show that at −15 °C and 10 % duty cycle, usable capacity drops by 34 % compared to room-temperature constant-current reference tests. The passivation resistance increases by a factor of 2.7 after the first 50 pulses and stabilises within 200 pulses. An empirical correction factor is derived that maps constant-current datasheet capacity to expected pulsed-load capacity as a function of temperature and duty cycle. The correction reduces capacity prediction error from 19 % to under 6 % across the tested conditions.

title: A Parametric Equivalent-Circuit Model for Estimating Remaining Useful Life of Primary Lithium Cells in WSN Deployments
abstract: This paper presents a parametric model for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of primary lithium cells powering wireless sensor nodes. The model is built on a two-branch RC equivalent circuit whose parameters—series resistance, charge-transfer resistance, double-layer capacitance, and open-circuit voltage—are updated periodically using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements taken at 1 kHz and 10 Hz. Calibration data were collected from 30 Li/MnO₂ cells cycled under traffic profiles derived from a real agricultural monitoring deployment in Vojvodina. A particle-filter-based state estimator updates model parameters every 72 hours and extrapolates the voltage trajectory to a 2.8 V cut-off. Across a 14-month accelerated ageing campaign, the model predicted end-of-life timing with a mean absolute error of 9.3 days against actual cell exhaustion, outperforming the datasheet Peukert approach, which gave a 41-day mean error. Computational cost of the on-host particle filter is under 80 ms on a Cortex-M3 microcontroller at 8 MHz.

title: Impedance Evolution of Li/SOCl₂ Cells Stored at Elevated Temperature: A Three-Year Longitudinal Study
abstract: Long shelf life is a principal selling point of primary lithium cells, yet systematic data on impedance evolution during storage at elevated temperature are scarce. This study tracks 24 Li/SOCl₂ cells stored continuously at 40 °C over 36 months, with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements at 0.1 Hz–100 kHz taken every three months. Equivalent-circuit fits reveal that the passivation-layer resistance grows approximately linearly at 1.8 Ω month⁻¹ during the first 18 months and then slows to 0.6 Ω month⁻¹. The double-layer capacitance decreases by 22 % over the full period. Pulse-load discharge tests performed at months 0, 12, 24, and 36 show a 17 % reduction in capacity delivered above the 2.8 V cut-off after 36 months. A simple Arrhenius extrapolation calibrated against these data predicts that cells stored at 25 °C retain over 90 % usable capacity after 10 years, consistent with manufacturer claims but now supported by mechanism-level impedance data. The dataset is provided as a supplementary CSV file.

title: Energy Budget Analysis for LoRaWAN End-Nodes Powered by Single Primary Cells: Field Measurements from a Flood-Warning Network
abstract: This paper reports measured energy consumption data from 18 LoRaWAN end-nodes deployed along the Tisa river basin for flood-level monitoring over a 20-month period. Each node is powered by a single AA-size Li/MnO₂ cell. Current waveforms were logged at 1 ms resolution using a shunt-based data logger co-located on the PCB. The study decomposes total energy into four phases: sensor acquisition (7 %), radio transmission (61 %), idle sleep (29 %), and microcontroller housekeeping (3 %). Radio transmission current peaks ranged from 38 mA to 124 mA depending on spreading factor. An empirical energy model calibrated on the first six months of data predicted total charge drawn over the remaining 14 months with a 4.1 % root-mean-square error. Cells in nodes with high spreading factors (SF12) showed 28 % lower delivered capacity than those using SF7, attributable to larger pulse amplitude stressing the passivation layer. These findings suggest that adaptive data-rate policies can meaningfully extend primary-cell lifetime in flood-monitoring deployments.

title: Effect of Duty Cycle and Inter-Pulse Interval on Voltage Recovery in Li/SOCl₂ Cells: Systematic Bench Tests
abstract: Voltage recovery after a current pulse is critical for reliable data transmission in intermittent wireless devices. This work examines how duty cycle (1 %–20 %) and inter-pulse interval (0.5 s–60 s) affect voltage recovery time and recovered terminal voltage in Li/SOCl₂ cells at three states of discharge (fresh, 50 % depleted, 80 % depleted). Tests were conducted on 45 cells across five lots from three manufacturers. Voltage recovery curves were fitted with a biexponential function; time constants τ₁ (fast, 0.1–0.9 s) and τ₂ (slow, 4–35 s) were extracted. τ₂ increases by a factor of 3.1 between fresh and 80 %-depleted states. At 20 % duty cycle and 0.5 s inter-pulse interval, recovered voltage at 80 % depletion falls 140 mV below the fresh-cell baseline—sufficient to cause transmission failure on 3.0 V-threshold radio modules. A simple lookup table parametrised on state-of-discharge and inter-pulse interval is proposed as a lightweight pre-transmission voltage check implementable on a Cortex-M0.

title: Low-Power Embedded Energy Meters for In-Situ Primary Cell Characterisation on Deployed Sensor Nodes
abstract: Characterising primary cells in situ on deployed sensor nodes is difficult because measurement hardware must not significantly perturb node energy consumption. This paper describes the design and validation of an embedded energy meter that draws under 9 µA average current from the measured cell and logs voltage, temperature, and accumulated charge to on-board flash at configurable intervals down to 100 ms. The meter uses a 24-bit sigma-delta ADC, a precision 10 mΩ current-sense resistor, and a Cortex-M0+ microcontroller in deep-sleep mode between samples. Calibration against a laboratory Keithley 2450 source-measure unit shows a current measurement error below 0.4 % over 0.1 mA–200 mA. The meter was validated on 12 nodes installed in a grain-silo humidity monitoring network. In-situ capacity estimates derived from logged data agreed with post-deployment laboratory capacity tests to within 3.8 % RMS. Board gerbers and firmware are published in an open repository.

title: Temperature-Dependent Capacity Loss in Primary Lithium Cells: Separating Passivation and Electrolyte Conductivity Contributions via Frequency-Resolved Impedance
abstract: At sub-zero temperatures, primary lithium cells lose usable capacity through two overlapping mechanisms: increased passivation-layer resistance and reduced electrolyte ionic conductivity. Disentangling these contributions is necessary for accurate cold-temperature lifetime models. This study applies distribution-of-relaxation-times (DRT) analysis to impedance spectra collected at nine temperatures between −20 °C and +45 °C on 36 Li/SOCl₂ cells at four states of discharge. DRT peaks are assigned to passivation, charge-transfer, and electrolyte processes using supporting DC polarisation data. The passivation contribution dominates the impedance increase below −5 °C, accounting for 68 % of total resistance rise at −20 °C, while the electrolyte contribution is dominant above +10 °C. An additive model combining both temperature functions fits the measured capacity-delivered data with an adjusted R² of 0.94 across all conditions. Implications for sensor-node deployment in unheated outdoor enclosures are discussed with reference to three case-study climatic zones in the western Balkans.

title: Summer thermal comfort in the main pedestrian zone of Zrenjanin: field measurements and PET assessment
abstract: This study examined outdoor thermal comfort conditions along the central pedestrian street of Zrenjanin during the summer of 2010. Field measurements were conducted on 18 clear-sky days in July and August using portable weather stations recording air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and globe temperature at 1.1 m height. Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET) was computed for each measurement point using RayMan software. Results showed that PET exceeded 41 °C during afternoon peak hours on 14 of the 18 measurement days, placing conditions in the 'very hot' stress category for more than five hours per day. Shading from building facades provided local PET reductions of 6–9 °C compared to fully exposed spots. Correlations between sky view factor and mean radiant temperature were statistically significant (r = 0.78, p < 0.01). The study provides a baseline dataset for future urban planning interventions in the city centre.

title: Seasonal variability of microclimate parameters in public squares of Sombor and Kikinda
abstract: Two mid-sized cities in Vojvodina, Sombor and Kikinda, were selected for a comparative microclimate survey spanning all four seasons between 2010 and 2011. Measurements were taken in the main public squares of each city on days representative of seasonal mean conditions, totalling 48 measurement campaigns. Air temperature, humidity, wind speed at two heights (1.1 m and 10 m mast), and mean radiant temperature were recorded at five fixed points per square. Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) was calculated using RayMan Pro. The results indicated that summer UTCI in both squares frequently exceeded 32 °C ('moderate heat stress') during midday and early afternoon. Winter UTCI dropped below −13 °C on nine measurement days in Kikinda. Differences between the two cities were attributable primarily to tree canopy coverage: Sombor's square, with 38% canopy cover, showed consistently lower summer MRT values than Kikinda's square at 11% coverage. The findings support tree planting as a cost-effective mitigation strategy.

title: Assessment of perceived thermal comfort among tourists in the historic core of Sremski Karlovci
abstract: Thermal comfort perception was investigated among 312 tourists visiting the historic pedestrian core of Sremski Karlovci during summer weekends in 2013. A structured questionnaire using the ASHRAE seven-point thermal sensation scale was administered simultaneously with meteorological field measurements. PET was used as the physical comfort index. Respondents were grouped by country of origin (Serbia, Hungary, Germany, Austria) and age cohort. Logistic regression revealed that tourists from northern European countries reported discomfort at lower PET values (neutral range 18–26 °C) compared to Serbian respondents (neutral range 22–31 °C), consistent with adaptation effects reported in the literature. Elderly tourists (>60 years) expressed heat discomfort at PET thresholds approximately 3 °C lower than younger age groups. The dataset contributes to establishing local thermal perception thresholds for tourism planning in the Fruška Gora area.

title: Urban morphology and mean radiant temperature in Novi Sad street canyons: a summer measurement campaign
abstract: Street canyon geometry was evaluated as a determinant of mean radiant temperature (MRT) in 12 street canyon transects across central Novi Sad during June–August 2015. Canyon aspect ratios (H/W) ranged from 0.4 to 2.3. Globe thermometer readings at 1.1 m height, sky view factor (SVF) derived from fish-eye photography, and simultaneous meteorological data were collected between 08:00 and 20:00 local time on 22 clear-sky days. Linear regression showed that SVF explained 64% of the variance in afternoon MRT values (R² = 0.64, p < 0.001). Deep canyons (H/W > 1.5) maintained MRT values 11–17 °C below open spaces during peak radiation hours. Shading from east–west oriented streets was more effective than north–south orientation in reducing cumulative daily thermal load. ENVI-met 4.3 simulations were validated against measurements with a root mean square error of 1.8 °C for air temperature and 3.1 °C for MRT.

title: Heatwave impacts on outdoor thermal comfort in Subotica: observations during the July 2017 event
abstract: The heatwave that affected northern Serbia between 17 and 28 July 2017 provided an opportunity to document extreme outdoor thermal stress in Subotica, the northernmost mid-sized city in Serbia. Continuous measurements were conducted at four urban sites differing in land cover and morphology: a park, a paved market square, a residential street, and an industrial periphery. UTCI was calculated at 30-minute intervals. During peak heatwave conditions, UTCI at the market square reached 53 °C ('very strong heat stress') on three consecutive afternoons, while the park site remained at 38–42 °C due to tree shading and evapotranspiration effects. The industrial peripheral site showed UTCI levels intermediate between the square and park, attributed to low albedo surface materials. Comparison with the 2015 baseline measurement period showed UTCI exceedance of the 32 °C threshold extended by an average of 3.2 hours per day during the heatwave. The results highlight differential urban vulnerability during extreme heat events.

title: Microclimate adaptation strategies in small Serbian city centres: a review of measurement studies 2005–2019
abstract: This chapter synthesises empirical microclimate and thermal comfort research conducted in Serbian city centres with populations between 30,000 and 300,000 inhabitants, covering the period 2005–2019. Forty-one peer-reviewed studies were identified through systematic database searches and manual screening of domestic journals. The review categorises findings by measurement methodology (fixed stations, mobile traverses, ENVI-met simulation), comfort index used (PET, UTCI, SET*), and adaptation measure evaluated (tree planting, pergolas, reflective pavements, water features, building reconfiguration). Tree planting consistently produced the largest MRT reductions (mean 8–14 °C in reviewed studies), while reflective pavements showed variable results depending on surrounding geometry. Only seven studies addressed pedestrian adaptation behaviour alongside physical measurements. Gaps identified include a near-absence of night-time microclimate studies and limited coverage of cities in central and southern Serbia. The chapter identifies priorities for future research and monitoring network development.

title: Evaluating ENVI-met performance for MRT and air temperature simulation in a flat-terrain Pannonian city: case study Zrenjanin
abstract: ENVI-met 4.4 was applied to simulate summer daytime microclimate conditions in a 400 m × 400 m grid covering the central area of Zrenjanin, a city characterised by flat terrain and a grid street layout. Model inputs included high-resolution urban morphology data derived from a cadastral database, vegetation parameters from field survey, and boundary meteorological conditions from the nearest synoptic station. Simulations were run for three clear-sky days in July 2019 and compared against field measurements at 11 validation points. For air temperature, mean absolute error was 0.9 °C and root mean square error was 1.2 °C. For MRT, MAE was 4.1 °C and RMSE was 5.3 °C, with the largest discrepancies occurring in narrow east–west canyons at midday. Sensitivity analysis showed that leaf area index specification had the greatest influence on simulated MRT in vegetated areas. Recommendations for model parameter calibration in Pannonian flatland contexts are provided.

title: Thermal comfort conditions along cycling routes in Novi Sad: implications for active mobility planning
abstract: The expansion of cycling infrastructure in Novi Sad provides a context for examining thermal comfort along established and proposed cycling corridors. Mobile microclimate traverses were conducted by bicycle along 14 route segments covering 47 km of the city's cycling network during summer 2022 and spring 2023. A measurement instrument package recording air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and globe temperature was mounted on a cargo bicycle at rider head height (1.6 m). UTCI was calculated for each 50 m segment. Summer afternoon UTCI along fully exposed riverside embankment routes averaged 39 °C, while tree-lined inland routes averaged 34 °C under comparable synoptic conditions. Segments passing through the Štrand beach area showed the lowest UTCI values, attributed to evaporative cooling from the Danube. Thermal conditions on spring measurement days were predominantly in the 'no stress' or 'slight cold stress' categories. Findings are presented as segment-level thermal comfort maps intended for use in infrastructure planning.

title: Surface albedo and land surface temperature patterns in Serbian city centres derived from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery
abstract: Remote sensing data from Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS and Sentinel-2 MSI were combined to map surface albedo and land surface temperature (LST) across the central areas of nine Serbian cities with populations between 40,000 and 250,000. A total of 36 cloud-free summer images (2019–2023) were processed using standard atmospheric correction and split-window algorithms. LST ranged from 28 °C over well-vegetated parks to 54 °C over dark asphalt parking areas. Surface albedo values for predominant urban surface types were catalogued: dark asphalt (0.04–0.07), light concrete (0.28–0.34), terracotta tiles (0.18–0.25), and grass (0.19–0.23). Regression of LST against normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI) yielded r = −0.71 across all cities, with somewhat weaker relationships in cities with high proportions of light-coloured paving. The resulting surface property database is being used to initialise ENVI-met simulations in ongoing fieldwork and is made publicly available as a supplementary dataset.

title: Heat stress exposure during outdoor festivals in Novi Sad: a multi-event thermal comfort assessment
abstract: Large outdoor music and cultural festivals attract several hundred thousand visitors to Novi Sad each summer. This study quantified heat stress exposure at three festival venues in Novi Sad during the 2024 summer season, covering eight event days in June and July. Portable meteorological stations were deployed at five locations per venue: main stage area, vendor zone, forested rest zone, parking perimeter, and entrance queue. UTCI was recorded at 15-minute intervals and combined with festival attendance data to estimate total person-hours of heat exposure by stress category. Across all venues, 38% of cumulative attendance-hours fell in the 'strong heat stress' category (UTCI 38–46 °C) during afternoon hours. The forested rest zone consistently showed UTCI values 7–11 °C lower than the main stage area. A simple heat exposure score integrating attendance density and UTCI duration is proposed as a practical tool for event safety planning. Comparisons with meteorological station data from Novi Sad airport show UTCI underestimation of 3–5 °C when using off-site reference data for festival contexts.

title: Dense stereo matching for generating urban digital surface models from aerial frame imagery
abstract: This study evaluated four semi-global matching (SGM) parameter configurations for producing digital surface models (DSMs) from overlapping aerial photographs acquired over a 4 km² district of Novi Sad at a ground sampling distance of 8 cm. Reference elevations were drawn from a concurrent airborne LiDAR campaign at 8 pts/m². The SGM variants were compared on normalised median absolute deviation, completeness in occluded street canyons, and processing time on a 16-core workstation. The best-performing configuration achieved a median absolute error of 6.1 cm against LiDAR and a completeness of 93.4% for pixels with a LiDAR reference. Building eave edges were reconstructed with a planimetric displacement below 12 cm. The study identified penalty parameter P2 as the dominant influence on smoothness in roof-edge regions and recommended an adaptive penalty approach for mixed urban–vegetated scenes. Runtime for the full 4 km² mosaic was 38 minutes.

title: Automated segmentation of photovoltaic-suitable roof planes from photogrammetric point clouds
abstract: Identifying geometrically suitable roof segments for photovoltaic installation is a prerequisite for large-scale solar cadastre production. This study developed an automated pipeline for segmenting flat and pitched roof planes from photogrammetric point clouds derived from trinocular aerial cameras over Novi Sad. The method combined a voxel-based normal estimation step with a RANSAC-guided region-growing algorithm. A post-processing filter removed dormers, chimneys, and HVAC units smaller than 1.5 m². The pipeline was tested on 3 240 buildings and validated against manual delineations for a 400-building subset. Segment-level precision reached 91.7% and recall 88.2%. Mean tilt angle error was 1.4° and mean azimuth error 3.2°. Processing the full dataset required 4.2 hours on a standard 32-core server. The segmented planes were then used as input to an hourly shadow-aware irradiance model, improving annual yield estimates for flat roofs by 6% compared with a uniform-tilt assumption.

title: Shadow frequency maps for urban rooftops derived from time-series cast-shadow simulation at 30-minute resolution
abstract: Cast shadows from adjacent buildings reduce annual solar yield on rooftops in dense urban settings. This work produced hourly shadow frequency maps for the central business district of Novi Sad (area 2.1 km²) by simulating sun position at every 30-minute timestep across a full calendar year. The input DSM was generated from a Pleiades-1B stereo pair (0.5 m GSD) processed with an image-matching pipeline calibrated against 210 ground control points (RMSE 0.18 m). Shadow polygons were cast geometrically from each DSM cell for all 17 520 timesteps and accumulated into a raster counting the percentage of daylight hours in shadow. The resulting frequency map was cross-checked against roof-mounted pyranometer measurements at six buildings over a 12-month period; mean absolute error in annual irradiation was 4.8%. The maps revealed that 31% of rooftop area receives fewer than 1 000 peak-sun-hours annually, primarily due to neighbouring high-rise structures built in the 1970s.

title: Accuracy of WorldView-3 stereo DSMs over mixed urban–industrial zones: a multi-site assessment
abstract: Very-high-resolution satellite stereo imagery is increasingly used as a cost-effective alternative to airborne surveys for urban 3-D reconstruction. This study assessed the geometric accuracy of DSMs produced from WorldView-3 stereo pairs at five sites across Serbia, Romania, and Hungary, covering a combined area of 48 km² and representing varied urban morphologies. Reference data comprised airborne LiDAR strips (4 pts/m²) and differential GNSS measurements at 620 check points. Median absolute height errors ranged from 0.41 m (flat industrial zone, Pančevo) to 1.23 m (dense historic core, Timișoara). Systematic offset patterns correlated with off-nadir acquisition angles above 20°. A rational polynomial coefficient refinement using 15 ground control points per tile reduced median error to below 0.55 m at all sites. The study provides practical accuracy expectations for solar resource assessors relying on commercial satellite archives without access to concurrent LiDAR.

title: Integration of photogrammetric DSMs and building energy simulation for district-scale PV yield forecasting
abstract: This study coupled a photogrammetric 3-D city model with an hourly building energy simulation engine to forecast photovoltaic yield at district scale. The 3-D model was derived from a nadir UAV survey (GSD 5 cm) over a 0.8 km² residential district in Zrenjanin and comprised 412 individual building objects. Roof planes were automatically segmented and attributed with tilt, azimuth, and a shadow-hour fraction computed from the same DSM. PV panel specifications matched a locally available 400 W monocrystalline module. Simulated annual yields were compared with metered generation from 14 rooftop systems already installed in the area; mean absolute percentage error was 6.1% at the system level and 4.3% at the district aggregate level. The workflow was implemented as a reproducible QGIS plugin distributed under an open-source licence. Computational time for the full district, including shadow simulation, was under 90 minutes on a laptop.

title: Seasonal variation of cast-shadow effects on building-integrated photovoltaics: evidence from a monitored test site
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems installed on south-facing façades are subject to strong seasonal variation in shadow obstruction from adjacent structures. This paper reports 18 months of irradiance measurements from 24 pyranometers mounted at three height levels on two instrumented façades in a Novi Sad university campus block, combined with concurrent shadow simulations driven by a DSM updated quarterly by UAV survey to capture vegetation growth. Measured irradiance at the lowest sensor row (1.2 m above ground) was on average 41% lower than at the top row (8.5 m) during December and January, narrowing to 12% in June. The simulation reproduced seasonal irradiance ratios with a root-mean-square error of 8.3 W/m² when using the quarterly-updated DSM, versus 14.7 W/m² with a static DSM ignoring deciduous tree foliage. The results highlight the importance of dynamic vegetation representation in urban solar models for façade applications.

title: Photogrammetric reconstruction of industrial rooftop geometry for large-scale flat-roof solar planning
abstract: Flat or near-flat industrial rooftops present different modelling challenges than residential pitched roofs: large unobstructed areas are interrupted by skylights, ventilation units, and raised parapet walls that create localised shading. This chapter reviews methods for capturing industrial rooftop geometry using oblique UAV photogrammetry, with particular attention to the representation of parapet shadows and their effect on ballasted PV rack placement. Three industrial estates in Vojvodina were surveyed; DSMs at 3 cm GSD were compared to total-station measurements at 180 check points (RMSE 2.8 cm). A workflow for automatically delineating obstacle-free installation zones and estimating annual shadow losses per zone is described. Case-study results showed that parapet walls reduced usable roof area by 8–19% depending on building height and orientation. The chapter also discusses licensing considerations when overlying commercial satellite base maps in public planning documents.

title: Evaluating Sentinel-2 reflectance time series as a proxy for rooftop condition in solar suitability assessments
abstract: Reflectance properties of rooftop surfaces affect the operating temperature and therefore the energy yield of photovoltaic modules. This study explored whether multitemporal Sentinel-2 imagery (10 m bands, 2017–2023) can discriminate rooftop material classes (bitumen felt, concrete screed, metal sheeting, clay tile) at the building level when combined with photogrammetric roof segment polygons. A random forest classifier was trained on 640 manually labelled roof segments from Novi Sad and tested on 280 segments from Subotica. Overall accuracy reached 74.3% (four classes), with metal sheeting achieving the highest producer accuracy (88%) and bitumen felt the lowest (61%) due to spectral similarity with concrete. Thermal band data from Landsat-8 improved classification accuracy by 4.1 percentage points. The output material map was incorporated into a PV temperature-loss correction layer, reducing district-level yield overestimation from 3.8% to 1.2% compared with an assumption of uniform albedo.

title: Spectral signatures of mineral dust on glass surfaces: a laboratory characterisation using a field spectroradiometer
abstract: To interpret satellite-detected reflectance anomalies on large photovoltaic installations, a controlled laboratory study was designed to characterise the bidirectional reflectance distribution of mineral dust deposited on borosilicate glass. Dust samples were collected from four sites across Vojvodina representing distinct agricultural and industrial source environments. Deposition density ranged from 0.5 to 8 g m⁻² in increments controlled by sieve mass weighing. Reflectance measurements were made with a Spectra Vista HR-1024 spectroradiometer under a calibrated tungsten-halogen source at view angles of 0°, 15°, and 30°. Spectral contrast between clean and soiled glass was greatest between 400 and 700 nm, with a reflectance increase of up to 0.12 at 8 g m⁻² normal incidence. Above 1300 nm, deposition-induced contrast fell below 0.02 and was not reliably separable from instrument noise. A power-law relationship between deposition density and integrated visible-band reflectance excess (R² = 0.91) is reported and proposed as a basis for remote inversion algorithms.

title: Integrating Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service AOD forecasts into day-ahead soiling risk maps for PV plant operators
abstract: PV plant operators benefit from advance warning of high-soiling-risk days to pre-position cleaning equipment. This paper describes an operational chain that ingests 24 h and 48 h CAMS ensemble AOD forecasts, combines them with a regional dust-transport model, and outputs gridded soiling risk maps at 1 km resolution covering Serbia and adjacent areas. The chain was run in hindcast mode for 2020–2022, and predicted soiling risk (classified as low/medium/high) was verified against satellite-derived NSI changes. The high-risk class correctly anticipated NSI increases above 0.006 day⁻¹ in 71% of cases; the false-alarm rate was 29%. Performance was lower during mixed mineral-and-biomass-burning episodes in summer, when CAMS aerosol type partitioning introduced additional uncertainty. A web API delivering the daily risk maps in GeoJSON format was piloted with one cooperating plant operator; preliminary feedback on forecast utility is presented. Forecast skill degraded at horizons beyond 36 h for dust events originating from the Hungarian plain.

title: Buyer Perceptions of Salesperson Adaptiveness in Industrial Procurement: Evidence from the Food Processing Sector
abstract: The study investigated how procurement officers in Serbian food processing companies perceive and respond to adaptive behaviour by supplier sales representatives. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 24 purchasing managers from firms located in Bačka and Srem regions. Interview transcripts were coded using thematic analysis guided by a buyer–seller interaction framework. Three dominant themes emerged: perceived authenticity of adaptation, concerns about information asymmetry, and the role of long-term relational norms in shaping tolerance for adaptive tactics. Buyers distinguished sharply between what they labelled 'honest adjustment' and 'manipulative flexibility', with the latter strongly associated with distrust and supplier switching intent. Relationship duration of more than five years was associated with higher tolerance for adaptive tactics across all respondent categories. The paper contributes a buyer-side perspective that complements the predominantly seller-side literature on adaptive selling and argues for incorporating dyadic data in future B2B sales studies.

title: CRM Implementation Outcomes in Small and Medium Enterprises: A Comparative Study of Serbia and Hungary
abstract: This article compared CRM implementation outcomes across 112 small and medium-sized enterprises in Serbia and 98 in Hungary, drawing on data collected through a structured postal and online survey administered between 2011 and 2012. Implementation outcome was operationalised along three dimensions: system utilisation rate, perceived data quality, and user-reported sales performance impact. Regression analyses indicated that top management commitment and IT infrastructure adequacy were significant positive predictors of all three outcome dimensions in both samples, explaining 38% and 34% of variance in utilisation rate respectively. Vendor training duration and the presence of an internal CRM champion emerged as significant only in the Hungarian sample, suggesting context-specific organisational factors. Serbian respondents reported substantially lower utilisation rates on average (mean = 3.1 on a 7-point scale versus 4.4 in Hungary), a gap attributed in part to weaker internal change management practices. Implications for CRM consultancy and policy support for SMEs in transition economies are discussed.

title: Technology Resistance Among Industrial Sales Forces: Extending the Innovation Resistance Theory to CRM Systems
abstract: Grounded in innovation resistance theory, this study developed and tested a model of CRM resistance among B2B sales personnel in industrial sectors in Serbia. A sample of 214 respondents from metal processing, chemical distribution, and construction materials firms was gathered through a convenience-purposive sampling procedure. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied using SmartPLS 2.0. The model included usage barrier, value barrier, risk barrier, tradition barrier, and image barrier as resistance antecedents, and passive and active resistance as outcome constructs. Usage barriers (path coefficient = 0.41) and tradition barriers (0.33) were the strongest drivers of passive resistance, while risk perceptions most strongly predicted active resistance (0.38). Salespeople with more than ten years of experience showed significantly higher tradition barrier scores. The model explained 52% of the variance in passive resistance. The paper proposes resistance profiling as a tool for staged CRM rollout in industrial companies.

title: Adaptive Selling and Relationship Quality in Key Account Management: A Longitudinal Perspective
abstract: This chapter reviews the relationship between adaptive selling behaviour and relationship quality constructs—trust, commitment, and satisfaction—in key account management contexts within industrial markets. Drawing on longitudinal data collected from 61 matched buyer–seller dyads in the machinery and equipment sector across three measurement points (2012, 2014, 2016), the chapter traces how the effect of salesperson adaptiveness on relationship quality evolves as relational tenure increases. Hierarchical linear modelling results indicate that the positive effect of adaptive selling on trust diminishes at higher levels of relational maturity, suggesting a 'familiarity plateau' effect. Commitment, however, continues to rise with adaptiveness regardless of tenure. The chapter also presents qualitative vignette data from eight key account managers that illustrates how adaptation strategies shift from product-focused to process-focused over the relationship lifecycle. Practical implications for key account programme design are discussed.

title: Sales Manager Coaching Behaviour and Its Effect on Salesperson CRM Compliance: Field Evidence from the Chemical Distribution Industry
abstract: This study examined whether and how sales manager coaching behaviour influences CRM compliance among field sales representatives in chemical distribution companies in the Western Balkans. Data were collected from 143 salesperson–manager dyads across eight firms operating in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Croatia. Compliance was measured by system login frequency and CRM activity completeness scores extracted from company databases, supplemented by self-report measures. Hierarchical regression revealed that directive coaching was significantly associated with compliance metrics (β = 0.34, p < 0.001), whereas developmental coaching showed no significant direct effect but interacted positively with perceived CRM usefulness (interaction term β = 0.22, p < 0.05). Manager tenure and firm size were included as controls. The paper highlights that compliance-focused outcomes may respond differently to coaching styles than performance-focused outcomes, and cautions against assuming that coaching generically improves CRM adoption in sales organisations.

title: Measuring Adaptive Selling in Post-Transition Markets: A Scale Validation Study
abstract: This paper reports the validation of a revised adaptive selling scale tailored to the institutional and relational context of post-transition economies in Southeast Europe. The original ADAPTS instrument was subjected to a series of validation steps: expert panel review (n = 9), cognitive interviews with 15 sales practitioners, an exploratory factor analysis on a pilot sample of 84 respondents, and confirmatory factor analysis on a main sample of 312 B2B sales personnel from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Romania. The resulting 14-item scale yielded a two-factor structure distinguishing communication adaptation from offer customisation, with acceptable fit indices (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.057). Both subscales demonstrated discriminant validity relative to customer orientation and selling orientation measures. Test–retest reliability over six weeks was satisfactory (ICC = 0.78). The paper provides the validated scale items in Serbian and Romanian for use in future regional studies.

title: Antecedents of CRM Adoption Resistance in B2B Firms: An Fsqca Approach
abstract: Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study identified configurations of organisational conditions sufficient for high CRM adoption resistance in 48 B2B firms from the industrial equipment and logistics sectors in Serbia. Conditions examined included IT infrastructure quality, change management capacity, sales force average tenure, top management digitisation commitment, and prior ERP experience. The analysis identified three configurations sufficient for high resistance, all involving the combination of weak change management capacity with either high average sales force tenure or low top management commitment. A single configuration—high IT infrastructure quality combined with strong change management capacity—was identified as sufficient for low resistance. The fsQCA results diverge from previous variable-oriented findings in highlighting that no single condition is necessary in isolation. The study adds to CRM research by applying a configurational lens that reflects the complex causality typical of organisational adoption decisions.

title: Salesperson Perceived Fairness in CRM Data Obligations and Its Link to System Circumvention Behaviour
abstract: This paper examined whether industrial salespeople's perceptions of procedural fairness in CRM data entry obligations predict circumvention behaviour, defined as deliberate omission, delay, or distortion of CRM records. An online survey was administered to 196 field sales representatives employed in B2B firms in Serbia across manufacturing, logistics, and professional services sectors. Circumvention was measured through a 6-item behavioural self-report scale developed and validated within the study (α = 0.79). Procedural fairness perceptions were assessed using an adapted organisational justice scale. Multiple regression analysis revealed that procedural fairness was the strongest negative predictor of circumvention (β = −0.44, p < 0.001), outperforming workload, monitoring intensity, and perceived CRM usefulness. Open-ended responses from 41 participants indicated that fairness concerns centred on data being used for performance surveillance rather than customer service improvement. The study suggests that framing CRM obligations as service tools rather than control mechanisms may reduce circumvention.

title: Integrating CRM Analytics into Adaptive Selling Decisions: Practices and Barriers in Industrial SMEs
abstract: Despite growing availability of CRM analytical features, their integration into daily adaptive selling decisions remains limited in practice. This study combined a cross-sectional survey of 158 sales representatives and semi-structured interviews with 19 sales managers in industrial SMEs across Vojvodina and Šumadija regions to explore current practices and barriers to CRM analytics-driven adaptation. Survey data were analysed using descriptive statistics and logistic regression; interviews were coded thematically. Only 21% of survey respondents reported using CRM-generated analytics at least weekly in preparing for customer interactions. Barriers most frequently cited were poor data completeness, interface complexity, and absence of managerial expectations. Logistic regression indicated that firms with dedicated inside sales support staff were 3.2 times more likely to report regular analytics use. Interview findings highlighted a persistent divide between what sales managers expected analytics to do and what the systems delivered given existing data entry quality. Recommendations for staged capability-building are offered.

title: Pressure drop correlation for single-phase flow in chevron-pattern brazed plate heat exchangers at low Reynolds numbers
abstract: Accurate pressure drop prediction in brazed plate heat exchangers (BPHEs) at low Reynolds numbers (Re < 400) is important for sizing refrigeration circuits operating with viscous secondary fluids. In this work, experimental pressure drop data were collected for water–glycol mixtures at three chevron angles (30°, 45°, 60°) across a Re range of 80–1200 using a laboratory BPHE test rig with 20 plates. A least-squares regression procedure was applied to fit a modified Fanning friction factor correlation to 360 steady-state data points. The proposed correlation reproduces measured values within ±8% for all tested chevron angles. Comparison with four published correlations from the literature showed that existing models systematically underpredict friction factors at Re below 200 by up to 22%. The sensitivity of the fitted coefficients to plate geometry was quantified, and the results suggest that a single universal correlation is insufficient for channels with chevron angles deviating more than 10° from 45°. The work provides a validated correlation suitable for integration into system-level simulation tools for industrial refrigeration design.

title: Experimental investigation of flow maldistribution in a ten-channel brazed plate heat exchanger during R-410A evaporation
abstract: Non-uniform refrigerant distribution among parallel channels of a BPHE during evaporation reduces effective heat transfer area and increases superheat variability at channel outlets. This study reports measurements of per-channel refrigerant quality and outlet temperature in a ten-channel BPHE evaporating R-410A at heat flux levels of 5–18 kW/m² and inlet vapour qualities of 0.05–0.20. Individual channel mass flow rates were inferred from energy balances using embedded thin-film resistance temperature detectors and a custom multichannel data acquisition system sampling at 10 Hz. Experiments showed that at low inlet quality (x < 0.10), the central channels carried up to 34% more refrigerant mass flux than edge channels. At inlet quality above 0.15, maldistribution reduced to within 12% of the mean. The inlet manifold geometry was found to be the primary driver of non-uniformity. Results are intended as a validation dataset for two-phase distribution models and highlight the inadequacy of assuming uniform inlet boundary conditions in BPHE simulations.

title: CFD modelling of two-phase refrigerant flow in the inlet manifold of a brazed plate heat exchanger
abstract: This paper describes a three-dimensional CFD study of R-410A two-phase flow in the inlet manifold of a BPHE with ten parallel channels, addressing how manifold internal geometry governs phase separation and maldistribution. The Volume of Fluid (VOF) method was used within a commercial finite-volume solver on a mesh of approximately 1.8 million hexahedral cells. Inlet conditions corresponded to mass fluxes of 20–60 kg/(m²·s) and vapour qualities of 0.05–0.25. Simulated per-channel liquid fractions agreed with the experimental data from a companion study within 15% relative error for most operating points. Gravitational orientation (horizontal vs. vertical manifold axis) had a strong effect: a vertically oriented inlet manifold reduced the peak channel-to-channel liquid fraction difference from 34% to 11% under the same inlet conditions. Mesh sensitivity was assessed over three refinement levels, and the VOF-based approach showed acceptable grid independence above 1.2 million cells. Limitations of the steady-state assumption are discussed, particularly for oscillatory flow regimes observed at low quality.

title: Reduced-order network model for two-phase flow distribution in multi-channel plate heat exchangers
abstract: Full CFD simulations of multi-channel BPHEs are computationally prohibitive for engineering design loops requiring hundreds of operating-point evaluations. This work presents a reduced-order network model in which each channel is represented as a one-dimensional two-phase flow element governed by a drift-flux formulation, with inter-channel coupling enforced via pressure-node balancing at inlet and outlet manifolds. The model was coded in Python and validated against published experimental data for R-134a and R-410A at channel counts of 8, 14, and 20, with 243 total operating points. Predicted maldistribution index values fell within ±18% of measurements in 89% of cases. Computational cost was under 0.4 seconds per steady-state solution on a standard laptop, compared to 6–12 hours for equivalent VOF CFD cases. Parametric studies using the network model revealed that manifold port diameter has a stronger influence on maldistribution than plate corrugation depth for inlet qualities above 0.15. The model is distributed as an open-source repository and is suitable for integration into heat pump and refrigeration system optimisation tools.

title: Numerical study of combined fouling and maldistribution effects on the thermal performance of a 20-channel BPHE
abstract: In industrial operation, BPHEs are subject to simultaneous fouling and refrigerant maldistribution, but these phenomena are almost always studied in isolation. This paper couples a spatially resolved fouling deposition submodel with the reduced-order network flow distribution model to predict overall heat transfer coefficient degradation over an operating period of 0–5000 hours. Fouling is modelled as a growing thermal resistance layer whose deposition rate depends on local wall temperature and flow velocity, with parameters fitted to the six-month industrial dataset from a companion study. Simulations were performed for three maldistribution severity levels (uniform, moderate, severe) and two fouling water chemistries. Results show that maldistribution accelerates fouling accumulation in low-flow channels by up to 40% relative to the uniform case, because lower local velocities reduce deposit re-entrainment. After 3000 hours, the combined model predicts an 18% greater reduction in overall heat transfer coefficient compared to a fouling-only model assuming uniform flow. The findings underscore the importance of accounting for both phenomena simultaneously when scheduling maintenance intervals.

title: Effect of low-GWP refrigerant substitution on flow distribution and heat transfer in an existing BPHE evaporator: a simulation study for R-1234yf and R-290
abstract: The phase-out of high-GWP refrigerants obliges operators to re-evaluate existing heat exchanger equipment when switching to low-GWP alternatives. This simulation study uses the validated network flow-distribution model to assess the impact of replacing R-410A with R-1234yf and R-290 in a 14-channel BPHE evaporator originally designed for R-410A service. Thermodynamic and transport property data for all three fluids were taken from the REFPROP 10 database. Simulations covered evaporating temperatures of −10 to +10 °C, inlet vapour quality 0.05–0.20, and total mass flow rates matched to equal cooling capacity. R-290 produced the most uniform channel distribution, with maldistribution index 22% lower than R-410A at the baseline condition, attributable to its higher liquid-to-vapour density ratio. R-1234yf showed nearly identical distribution to R-410A but with an average heat transfer coefficient 9% lower, requiring approximately 8% additional surface area to maintain design duty. Pressure drop penalties for both alternatives remained within 15% of the R-410A baseline. The study provides practical sizing guidance for operators considering refrigerant retrofit without manifold redesign.
