title: Experimental characterisation of boiling heat transfer coefficients for R-290 in a brazed plate heat exchanger at low mass flux
abstract: Propane (R-290) is being reconsidered for use in industrial heat pump evaporators where charge size regulations allow it, yet boiling heat transfer data in BPHEs for this fluid at low mass fluxes (below 30 kg/(m²·s)) are limited. This paper reports heat transfer coefficient measurements for R-290 boiling in a 10-plate BPHE at mass fluxes of 8–30 kg/(m²·s), heat fluxes of 4–16 kW/m², saturation temperatures of 0 and 10 °C, and inlet quality of 0.08–0.18. Local heat transfer coefficients were inferred using a modified Wilson plot technique with 96 steady-state test points. Nucleate boiling was found to dominate at heat fluxes above 9 kW/m², with the heat transfer coefficient increasing approximately as q⁰·⁶⁵. Convective contribution became relevant only above 25 kg/(m²·s). Comparison with five published boiling correlations showed that the Kandlikar–Balasubramanian model performed best, matching 78% of data points within ±20%. A simple correction factor dependent on plate corrugation angle is proposed to improve agreement to ±14%. The dataset is made publicly available as a benchmark for simulation validation.
venue: International Journal of Refrigeration and Thermal Sciences

title: Sensitivity of BPHE fouling model predictions to uncertainty in water chemistry parameters: a Monte Carlo analysis
abstract: Fouling models for plate heat exchangers require water chemistry inputs—calcium hardness, alkalinity, temperature, pH—that are subject to measurement uncertainty and temporal variation in industrial settings. This study applies a Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation analysis to the asymptotic fouling model calibrated in earlier work, propagating distributions for six water chemistry parameters through 10,000 model evaluations per scenario. Three industrial water sources representative of Vojvodina groundwater chemistry were considered. Results show that calcium hardness uncertainty dominates model output variance, accounting for 51–63% of total variance in predicted asymptotic fouling resistance across all scenarios, followed by pH at 18–24%. The 90% prediction interval for asymptotic fouling resistance spans a factor of 2.8 under realistic field uncertainty conditions, which has direct implications for maintenance interval scheduling. A simplified variance-based sensitivity index table is provided to assist plant engineers in prioritising water quality monitoring effort. The analysis also shows that reducing calcium hardness measurement uncertainty below ±15 mg/L CaCO₃ brings diminishing returns in model precision.
venue: Chemical Engineering and Process Simulation

title: Towards digital twin representations of industrial BPHE evaporators: coupling reduced-order flow models with real-time sensor data
abstract: Digital twins for heat exchanger systems require that reduced-order models be continuously updated with operational data to track performance drift due to fouling and changing process conditions. This paper describes a framework in which the reduced-order network model is coupled with a recursive least-squares parameter estimator that updates fouling resistance and flow distribution coefficients from temperature and pressure sensor streams sampled every five minutes. The framework was tested on 14 weeks of operational data from a chilled water system at an agri-food processing plant, comprising approximately 28,000 five-minute records. The online estimator tracked overall heat transfer coefficient within 5% of measured values throughout the monitoring period, compared to 21% drift observed with static model parameters. A threshold-based alarm for predicted fouling resistance exceeding 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²·K/W was implemented and triggered maintenance scheduling 9 days before the operator's fixed-interval cleaning date, potentially enabling condition-based maintenance. Computational latency of the update cycle was under 2 seconds on edge hardware. Limitations related to sensor calibration drift and abrupt process disturbances are discussed.

title: Simplification Error Bounds for Douglas-Peucker Applied to Projected Coordinate Systems
abstract: The Douglas-Peucker line simplification algorithm is widely used in cartographic generalisation, but its geometric error properties under non-Euclidean projected coordinate systems are rarely formalised. This study derives analytical error bounds for the algorithm when applied to polylines represented in three common map projections: Gauss-Krüger, Web Mercator, and Lambert Conformal Conic. Using a set of 310,000 road and river polylines from the topographic database of Serbia and Montenegro, the paper quantifies the divergence between simplified geometries computed in geographic versus projected coordinates. Results show that Web Mercator introduces up to 3.4 times larger simplification error at latitudes above 50° N compared to Gauss-Krüger for equivalent tolerance settings. Recommendations are given for tolerance adjustment formulas specific to each projection type, validated against ground-truth lidar-derived reference geometries.

title: Tile Pyramid Construction Strategies for Heterogeneous Vector-Raster Web Map Services
abstract: Web map tile services typically maintain separate pyramid structures for raster imagery and vector overlays, leading to redundant storage and inconsistent zoom-level transitions. This paper proposes a unified tile generation framework that co-renders vector features and raster base layers into a single JPEG/PNG tile pyramid while preserving per-layer selectivity for client-side queries. The framework is implemented using a C++/Python pipeline tested on a dataset comprising 12 administrative layers and a 10 cm orthophoto mosaic covering 4,800 km² of the Vojvodina plain. Tile generation time for zoom levels 0–18 was reduced by 31% compared to a sequential dual-pipeline baseline, primarily through shared spatial index lookups. Tile storage footprint decreased by 19% due to elimination of duplicate background rendering passes. The paper also addresses edge artefacts at tile boundaries introduced by anti-aliasing of vector strokes.

title: Progressive Transmission of Vector Map Tiles Using Geometry Delta Encoding
abstract: Bandwidth constraints in mobile web mapping motivate progressive transmission schemes that deliver coarse geometry first and refine on demand. This work introduces a delta encoding scheme for vector tile sequences across consecutive zoom levels, where each tile payload stores only the geometric difference relative to the scaled parent tile. The encoding is implemented within the Mapbox Vector Tile specification using a custom extension layer and tested on four datasets of varying feature density: urban street networks, cadastral parcels, hydrological networks, and administrative boundaries. Across all datasets, progressive delta tiles reduce total transmitted bytes by 38–52% for users who stop panning before reaching maximum zoom. Decoding overhead on a mid-range Android device adds 14 ms average latency per tile, which is acceptable for most interactive mapping applications. Formal bounds on encoding size relative to Hausdorff distance thresholds are derived.

title: GPU-Accelerated Polygon Clipping for Real-Time Web Map Rendering
abstract: Rendering large polygon layers in browser-based GIS applications requires clipping thousands of polygons to the current viewport on every pan and zoom event. This paper describes a GPU-based polygon clipping implementation using WebGL compute shaders, replacing the Sutherland-Hodgman algorithm traditionally executed on the CPU. The approach encodes polygon vertices as floating-point textures and performs clip plane intersection tests in parallel across all edges. Benchmarks on a dataset of 280,000 land-use polygons from a regional spatial planning database demonstrate a 7.4× throughput improvement over a CPU JavaScript implementation at zoom level 14, maintaining interactive frame rates (above 30 fps) for polygon counts that previously caused frame drops to below 5 fps. Memory transfer overhead between CPU and GPU is characterised, and a batching strategy that amortises transfer cost across multiple render frames is proposed and evaluated.

title: Topology-Preserving Map Generalisation for Multi-Scale Vector Tile Databases
abstract: Automated generalisation of vector datasets for multi-scale tile databases frequently introduces topological errors such as polygon overlap, gap creation, and edge crossing between features that share boundaries in the source data. This chapter reviews algorithms designed to prevent such errors, with particular attention to constraint-based generalisation using a planar straight-line graph framework. Case studies are drawn from cadastral and land-use databases at 1:5,000 and 1:50,000 target scales in Serbia. The chapter describes implementation trade-offs between exact topological consistency and approximate fast generalisation, discusses the role of spatial tolerance parameters, and benchmarks four open-source generalisation libraries against a set of 14 topological correctness metrics. Practical recommendations for database schema design that facilitates topology-preserving pipelines are included.

title: Spatial Join Acceleration Using Space-Filling Curve Ordering in Tile-Aligned Query Grids
abstract: Spatial joins between large polygon and point datasets are a bottleneck in server-side preprocessing of web map tiles. This study investigates whether preordering dataset features along a Hilbert space-filling curve, aligned to the tile grid at a chosen zoom level, reduces the effective search space for spatial join predicates. Experiments compare Hilbert-ordered joins against standard bounding-box-filtered nested-loop joins and sort-merge joins on three cross-joined dataset pairs of increasing cardinality (up to 8.1 million points against 1.2 million polygons). Hilbert ordering reduces join execution time by 22–41% in PostgreSQL with PostGIS extensions, with larger gains at finer tile alignments. The approach requires a one-time reordering pass whose cost is amortised over repeated joins. The paper provides a cost model estimating break-even thresholds between reordering cost and cumulative join savings.

title: Evaluating Coordinate Quantisation Precision in Compact Vector Tile Encoding
abstract: Vector tile formats such as Mapbox Vector Tiles quantise floating-point coordinates to integer grids, typically 4,096 or 8,192 units per tile. This quantisation introduces geometric error whose magnitude depends on zoom level and geographic extent. This paper provides a systematic empirical analysis of quantisation error across zoom levels 6–18 for five feature types: administrative boundaries, road centrelines, river polylines, building footprints, and parcel polygons. Errors are measured in metres using a 10 m reference DEM-derived ground truth. At zoom level 12 with 4,096-unit quantisation, median positional error for road centrelines is 0.87 m, rising to 4.3 m for administrative boundaries at zoom level 8. The paper proposes a zoom-adaptive quantisation grid selection heuristic that reduces mean error by 28% with no change to tile file format. Compatibility with existing tile server and client implementations is discussed.

title: Visibility-Based Level-of-Detail Selection for Dense Point Feature Layers in Web Maps
abstract: Web maps displaying dense point features such as photo locations, sensor stations, or business listings suffer from overplotting at low zoom levels. This paper proposes a visibility-based level-of-detail selection algorithm that assigns each point feature to the minimum zoom level at which it remains visually distinct from its k nearest neighbours, given a configurable pixel-distance separation threshold. The algorithm runs as a preprocessing step and produces a zoom-level attribute for each feature, which tile servers use to filter features per tile without spatial query overhead. Tested on a dataset of 2.3 million geotagged points over the Western Balkans, the algorithm reduces per-tile feature count by 60–85% at zoom levels 4–10 while maintaining perceptually representative spatial distributions, validated through a 24-participant user study. Runtime scales as O(n log n) using a k-d tree for neighbour lookups.

title: Incremental Delaunay Triangulation for Real-Time Terrain Mesh Updates in Browser-Based 3D GIS
abstract: Browser-based 3D terrain visualisation commonly uses static pre-triangulated meshes, preventing real-time incorporation of newly acquired elevation points such as drone survey data. This paper describes an incremental Delaunay triangulation algorithm implemented in WebAssembly (Wasm) that supports point insertion and deletion without full mesh recomputation. The algorithm maintains a constrained Delaunay triangulation using a DAG-based point location structure and achieves amortised O(log n) insertion time. Performance is evaluated on terrain patches ranging from 5,000 to 500,000 points representing areas from the Fruška Gora foothills, using elevation data sourced from a 1 m resolution LiDAR survey. At 100,000 points, single-point insertion completes in 2.1 ms median on a desktop browser, enabling real-time updates at drone data acquisition rates. Comparison with a static TINTIN-based pipeline shows negligible accuracy difference and 94% reduction in data retransmission volume.

title: Rendering Performance Comparison of Client-Side Vector Tile Renderers Under High Feature Density
abstract: Several open-source JavaScript libraries render vector map tiles in the browser, but systematic performance comparisons under high feature density are scarce. This paper benchmarks four renderers—MapLibre GL, VectorCanvas, GeoLeaflet, and TileRenderer.js (all fictional names used for consistency with the study scope)—across five standardised test scenes containing between 5,000 and 120,000 polygon and line features per viewport. Metrics collected include frame render time, JavaScript heap usage, GPU memory usage, and visual correctness score assessed by pixel-diff comparison against a reference SVG rendering. At 80,000 features, WebGL-based renderers maintain above 24 fps while canvas-based renderers drop below 8 fps. However, canvas renderers produce higher visual fidelity scores for thin line features due to sub-pixel antialiasing differences. The paper provides a decision matrix for renderer selection based on feature type, density, and target device class.

title: Geometry Compression Ratio Analysis for MVT-Encoded Urban Cadastral Layers Across European Cities
abstract: This study analyses compression ratios achieved by Mapbox Vector Tile geometry encoding applied to urban cadastral parcel layers from eight European cities with contrasting urban morphologies: a historic compact Balkan centre, a Haussmann-grid French arrondissement, a post-war socialist housing district, a Dutch polder agricultural zone, and four others. For each city, cadastral parcel layers were encoded at zoom levels 14–17 and compressed with gzip and Brotli. Brotli achieves 12–18% better compression than gzip across all cities, with the largest gains in regular grid morphologies. Compact irregular street networks show the lowest absolute compression ratios but the highest feature density per tile. Coordinate quantisation grid resolution has a larger effect on compressed size than ring vertex count for parcels with more than 12 vertices. The results inform tile server configuration choices for national cadastral web services.

title: Preprint: Dynamic Tile Subdivision Strategies for Variable-Density Feature Distributions in Vector Tile Servers
abstract: Standard vector tile grids use fixed 256×256 or 512×512 pixel tiles regardless of spatial feature density variation across the coverage area. This preprint investigates adaptive tile subdivision that splits tiles exceeding a configurable feature density threshold into quadrant sub-tiles during server-side generation, producing a variable-resolution tile pyramid. A prototype implementation in a Rust-based tile server was tested against cadastral and land-use datasets for the territory of Vojvodina province, where density varies from fewer than 10 features per km² in agricultural zones to over 2,400 per km² in central Novi Sad. Adaptive subdivision reduces maximum per-tile feature count by 78% in high-density zones while increasing tile count by only 31% overall, improving client rendering frame time by a median of 44 ms in affected zoom levels. Edge cases involving features crossing subdivision boundaries are handled by a clipping-and-flagging mechanism described in detail.

title: Integer Programming Formulations for the Multi-Skill Project Staffing Problem
abstract: This study examines three integer linear programming (ILP) formulations for a staffing variant of the multi-skill project scheduling problem in which staff must be allocated to project activities over a rolling horizon of up to 16 weeks. Each formulation differs in how it represents the assignment of employees to skill roles: a compact set-covering model, an extended column-generation model, and a time-indexed arc-flow model. Formulations were compared using a benchmark library of 60 instances constructed from publicly available project scheduling data supplemented with skill profiles drawn from HR records of a regional IT company. The arc-flow model produced the tightest linear programming relaxation bounds in 47 of 60 instances but was computationally more expensive. The column-generation approach solved instances with up to 200 employees and 15 concurrent projects to optimality within a two-hour time limit in 83% of cases. Sensitivity analysis shows that solution cost is most sensitive to the ratio of required skill combinations to available certified employees.

title: A Memetic Algorithm for the Multi-Depot Vehicle-and-Driver Scheduling Problem
abstract: This paper addresses a combined vehicle and driver scheduling problem for a regional public transport operator with three depots and 180 drivers holding different licence categories. Drivers must be matched to vehicle duties so that licence requirements are satisfied and driving time, split-shift, and spread-time regulations are respected. The memetic algorithm uses a genetic recombination operator on driver-duty assignments and a local search phase based on 2-opt duty swaps. Population diversity is maintained through a crowding-distance mechanism. Computational experiments use a dataset representing a week of operations, comprising 420 vehicle duties across the three depots. The algorithm finds solutions with total overtime 11% below a greedy construction heuristic baseline and within 4% of the best ILP lower bound achievable within a one-hour solver run. The approach scales to the full weekly problem, whereas the ILP solver failed to close the gap on the largest instances within the allotted time.

title: Decomposition Methods for Large-Scale Nurse Scheduling with Cross-Unit Skill Assignments
abstract: When nurses are permitted to work across ward units according to their competency profiles, the scheduling problem enlarges considerably because cross-unit assignments must be coordinated to avoid double-booking and to satisfy unit-level coverage targets simultaneously. This paper proposes a Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition in which each ward unit constitutes a sub-problem, solved by CP, and a master problem coordinates cross-unit assignments by pricing out columns corresponding to feasible partial rosters. The method is applied to a 10-ward hospital with 210 nurses over a four-week horizon. The decomposition converges within 15 iterations on average. Final integer solutions obtained by branch-and-price satisfy all hard constraints and achieve soft constraint scores 9% better than those produced by a commercially deployed scheduling system used at the same hospital. Detailed results are given for three skill tiers and two staff categories.

title: Constraint-Based Modelling of Collective Labour Agreements in Healthcare Rostering
abstract: Collective labour agreements (CLAs) in healthcare contain scheduling rules that are often intricate and sometimes mutually inconsistent. This paper documents and formalises 34 distinct CLA rules drawn from agreements in force at three Serbian public hospitals and two Croatian private clinics, and examines how each can be encoded as a hard or soft constraint in a CP model. Seven rules required the introduction of auxiliary counting variables; four rules were found to be mutually inconsistent in particular staffing configurations, and the paper characterises the conditions under which infeasibility arises. A solver based on Choco 4 was implemented and tested on 18 instances covering wards of 20 to 60 nurses. All instances with fewer than 40 nurses were solved to proven optimality; for larger instances, an LNS post-processing phase was applied. The study contributes a publicly available benchmark set of CLA-constrained rostering instances.

title: Solving the Exam Timetabling Problem at a Multi-Faculty University with Shared Room Pools
abstract: University exam timetabling at institutions with shared examination rooms across multiple faculties presents coordination difficulties that single-faculty models do not capture. This paper addresses the problem at a mid-sized Serbian university with seven faculties, 14,000 students, and a pool of 62 shared rooms of varying capacities. Constraints include conflict avoidance for students enrolled in multiple faculties, room capacity and type matching, invigilator availability, and institutional spreading requirements. A two-phase approach is used: a graph-colouring-based construction heuristic assigns exams to time slots, and a CP model then assigns rooms and invigilators. The method produced a complete feasible timetable for the winter examination period, reducing student conflicts compared with the manual solution by 31% and eliminating all room-capacity violations. The approach was implemented as a web-accessible scheduling tool and used operationally for two consecutive examination periods.

title: Benchmark Instances for the Skill-Constrained Personnel Scheduling Problem: Construction Methodology and Baseline Results
abstract: The lack of standardised benchmark instances has hindered direct comparison of methods for skill-constrained personnel scheduling. This paper describes a systematic methodology for generating benchmark instances that reflect realistic distributions of skill profiles, demand patterns, and contractual constraints observed in five industry sectors: healthcare, logistics, contact centres, manufacturing, and retail. A total of 120 instances are generated at four size levels (25, 50, 100, and 200 employees) and released under an open licence. Baseline results are reported for five established methods: a greedy construction heuristic, a tabu search, a genetic algorithm, a CP solver with LNS, and a commercial ILP solver. Results show that no single method dominates across all sectors and sizes; in particular, the CP–LNS hybrid performs best on healthcare instances while the ILP solver is competitive on small manufacturing instances. The benchmark set and instance generator code are publicly available.

title: A Hybrid CP–SAT Approach for Technician Routing and Scheduling with Certification Constraints
abstract: Field service operations require assigning certified technicians to geographically distributed jobs while respecting travel times, time windows, and certification requirements per job type. This paper formulates the problem as a combined vehicle routing and scheduling model and proposes a hybrid approach that uses the Google OR-Tools CP–SAT solver augmented with a custom branching strategy that prioritises certification feasibility before travel cost. Test instances are constructed from GPS and work-order data contributed by a telecommunications infrastructure company operating in the Vojvodina and Central Serbia regions, comprising 40 technicians with up to 6 certification types and daily job sets of 80 to 150 tasks. The hybrid obtains feasible solutions for all instances; the average travel time is 7.9% above a relaxed lower bound. On small instances solvable to optimality, the gap is 2.1%. The branching strategy reduces the number of backtracks by 52% compared to the default CP–SAT configuration on certification-constrained instances.

title: Preference Elicitation for Automated Scheduling: A Structured Interview Study with Nursing Staff
abstract: Automated scheduling systems frequently optimise against proxy objective functions that do not accurately reflect employee preferences, leading to dissatisfaction even when formal quality metrics improve. This paper reports a structured interview study with 78 nurses across four hospital departments in Novi Sad, aimed at eliciting and quantifying scheduling preferences. A card-sorting protocol was used to rank 22 scheduling attributes; responses were analysed using a weighted scoring model and cluster analysis to identify preference profiles. Four distinct preference clusters emerged, differing primarily in the relative importance assigned to weekend distribution, shift-type consistency, and advance notice. Incorporating cluster-specific weights into a CP rostering model improved self-reported acceptance scores by 27 percentage points on a five-point Likert scale in a follow-up evaluation with 40 nurses. The study highlights that a single global preference weight vector is insufficient for diverse nursing populations and provides a practical elicitation protocol.

title: Integrating Real-Time Traffic Data into Rolling-Horizon Bus Scheduling: A Case Study from Novi Sad
abstract: Planned bus schedules assume fixed travel times that diverge from reality during peak hours and incidents. This paper describes a system that feeds real-time GPS and loop-detector traffic data into a rolling-horizon scheduler operating on a 20-minute receding horizon, re-solving sub-problems every 5 minutes. The system was piloted on four bus lines in Novi Sad over a 6-week period in 2022 using historical data replay. Updated travel time estimates were obtained from a gradient-boosted regression model trained on 11 months of GPS traces. Compared to a static daily schedule, the rolling-horizon system reduced total accumulated delay by 18% and reduced the number of trips arriving more than 3 minutes late by 22%. Practical challenges encountered during deployment—data latency, GPS dropouts, and dispatcher override frequency—are documented. The paper concludes with a discussion of the gap between research prototype and operational deployment.

title: An Empirical Study of Statement- versus Branch-Level Coverage Criteria in Regression Test Selection
abstract: Regression test selection (RTS) identifies the subset of an existing test suite relevant to a given code change, thereby reducing CI feedback time. This study evaluates four RTS techniques—two static (file-level and method-level change impact analysis) and two dynamic (statement-coverage-based and branch-coverage-based)—across 18 months of commit history from three medium-sized industrial C# codebases totalling 1.2 million lines of code. Selection recall, defined as the fraction of failing tests included in the selected subset, and reduction ratio are reported for each commit. Branch-level dynamic RTS achieved 97.3 % recall and a 52 % average reduction, outperforming method-level static analysis (94.1 % recall, 61 % reduction) in recall at the cost of higher instrumentation overhead. The study also quantifies the frequency of over-approximation errors introduced by static analysis when methods are overloaded. Findings are intended to guide practitioners choosing RTS granularity in .NET CI environments.

title: Multi-Objective Test Case Prioritisation Using NSGA-II: Balancing Fault Detection Rate and Execution Time
abstract: Test case prioritisation (TCP) reorders a test suite so that faults are detected earlier in a run. Most TCP techniques optimise a single objective such as average percentage of faults detected (APFD). This paper formulates TCP as a bi-objective problem—maximising APFD while minimising total execution time—and applies NSGA-II to approximate the Pareto front. Experiments are conducted on four Python projects with between 320 and 1 750 test cases, using historical execution-time logs and seeded faults generated by the mutmut mutation tool. Pareto-optimal solutions show that a 20–30 % reduction in execution time can typically be achieved with less than a 5 % decrease in APFD compared to the single-objective optimum. The paper includes a sensitivity analysis of population size (50, 100, 200) and crossover rate, finding that population size has a stronger effect on solution quality than crossover rate for the problem sizes studied.

title: Flaky Test Detection in Continuous Integration: A Taxonomy and Dataset from 12 Open-Source Repositories
abstract: Flaky tests pass or fail non-deterministically without any change to the code under test, eroding developer trust in CI pipelines. This paper introduces a taxonomy of flakiness root causes derived by manually inspecting 430 confirmed flaky tests collected from 12 open-source repositories hosted on a self-managed GitLab instance. Root causes are grouped into seven categories: concurrency, test order dependency, resource leak, async wait, network dependency, time dependency, and uninitialized random seed. The resulting labelled dataset of 430 flaky and 430 matched non-flaky tests is used to evaluate five supervised classifiers—logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, an LSTM on token sequences, and a CodeBERT-based model—using leave-one-repository-out cross-validation. CodeBERT achieves the highest F1 of 0.81, while gradient boosting reaches 0.74 using only static features, making it more practical for resource-constrained environments. The dataset is released publicly.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test Case Prioritisation in CI Pipelines
abstract: Static and search-based test case prioritisation methods do not adapt as the codebase and test suite evolve. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning (RL) agent that reorders test cases before each CI build using a contextual bandit formulation. The state representation encodes per-test features: recent failure history, time since last execution, last execution duration, and static complexity metrics of the modified files. The agent is trained on-line using an epsilon-greedy policy with a reward signal derived from the time-to-first-failure metric. Evaluation uses a replay simulation over 14 months of CI build logs from two software companies in Novi Sad, comprising 48 000 builds in total. The RL agent improves average time-to-first-failure by 31 % compared to round-robin ordering and by 12 % compared to a history-based greedy baseline. Convergence of the learned policy is analysed and instabilities during high-churn periods are discussed.

title: Regression Test Selection and Prioritisation Under Resource Constraints: A Unified Framework
abstract: Regression test selection (RTS) and test case prioritisation (TCP) are often treated as independent steps in CI pipelines, but their interaction affects overall fault detection under time budgets. This paper formalises a unified optimisation model in which RTS and TCP decisions are made jointly, subject to a wall-clock budget constraint. The model is solved with a hybrid approach combining a static change-impact filter with a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. Experiments are conducted on five open-source projects instrumented with Jacoco, using real fault data from historical bug-fix commits. Under a 10-minute execution budget, the unified approach detects 17 % more injected faults than a sequential RTS-then-TCP pipeline and 9 % more than TCP alone without selection. The paper also studies the sensitivity of results to budget tightness, showing that gains are most pronounced when the available budget covers between 30 % and 60 % of the full suite runtime.

title: A bi-objective integer programme for balancing workload equity and staffing cost in automotive component assembly
abstract: Workload equity among workers is rarely treated as a first-class objective in industrial scheduling. This study formulates a bi-objective integer programme that simultaneously minimises total staffing cost and maximises the minimum weekly working-hour allocation across individual workers, reflecting both company cost concerns and collective-agreement fairness clauses. Data were collected from a Tier-2 automotive component supplier in Zrenjanin with 210 production employees and a demand pattern that varies by up to 35 percent between the lowest and highest demand weeks in a calendar year. The epsilon-constraint method was used to approximate the Pareto front, yielding 31 efficient solutions. Decision-makers at the company were presented with a structured interview to elicit preference weights, and the preferred solution reduced perceived unfairness complaints—as recorded in HR logs—by approximately 22 percent over a six-month pilot. Computational experiments on synthetic instances up to 500 workers confirm that the model scales acceptably up to that size with branch-and-cut in CPLEX 12.9.

title: Fatigue accumulation indices in continuous-process chemical plants: a review and comparative evaluation
abstract: Several fatigue-risk indices have been proposed for shift-schedule evaluation—among them the Rohmert curve-based approach, the three-process model, and various simplified scoring systems used by occupational health regulators. This paper systematically reviews 41 studies published between 1990 and 2012 and compares the indices on four criteria: physiological grounding, computational tractability, compatibility with optimisation models, and regulatory acceptance in EU member states and candidate countries. None of the reviewed indices satisfies all four criteria simultaneously. The paper proposes a simplified additive index derived from the three-process model that can be linearised and embedded directly into mixed-integer programming formulations without requiring simulation. Illustrative application to a petrochemical facility in Romania demonstrates that constraining the new index to a threshold equivalent to existing regulatory guidance eliminates all high-risk shift sequences while increasing total staffing requirement by only 4.1 percent relative to unconstrained schedules.

title: Demand-responsive shift scheduling using rolling-horizon decomposition: a case study in a cold-storage distribution centre
abstract: Cold-storage logistics centres face strongly seasonal demand, with weekly throughput varying by a factor of up to 2.8 between summer trough and pre-holiday peaks. Fixed cyclic rosters are poorly suited to such environments. This paper proposes a rolling-horizon mixed-integer programme in which the schedule is re-optimised every two weeks over a six-week look-ahead window, with workers classified as permanent staff, part-time contract employees, or temporary agency workers. The model minimises total labour cost subject to demand coverage, fatigue-risk, and contractual constraints. It was implemented and tested at a distribution centre near Novi Sad employing 85 workers. Over a 12-month live trial, total labour cost fell by 9.3 percent relative to the previous manual scheduling practice, and the number of last-minute agency-worker calls was reduced by 41 percent. The rolling decomposition solves each two-week subproblem in under four minutes on standard workstation hardware.

title: Embedding ergonomic shift-sequence rules into a metaheuristic solver: a simulated annealing framework for large-scale roster construction
abstract: Mixed-integer programming becomes impractical for workforce scheduling instances with more than roughly 600 workers and planning horizons beyond eight weeks. This paper describes a simulated annealing framework in which ergonomic shift-sequence rules—maximum number of consecutive night shifts, minimum forward-rotation requirement, and maximum early-morning start frequency—are encoded as hard constraints enforced through a repair operator rather than penalty terms. The framework is tested on 60 instances generated from production data of a Serbian sugar-processing company with workforces of 200 to 1,200 employees and planning horizons of 4 to 26 weeks. For instances solvable by CPLEX within one hour, the heuristic produces schedules within 2.8 percent of optimality on average. For large instances where CPLEX finds no feasible solution within one hour, the heuristic yields feasible schedules in under 12 minutes. Parameter tuning used a design-of-experiments approach across 15 annealing configurations.

title: Workforce scheduling in Serbian food industry: regulatory context and modelling challenges
abstract: This book chapter provides a practitioner-oriented overview of workforce scheduling problems in Serbian food-processing companies, situating them within the regulatory framework established by the Law on Labour, sector-level collective agreements, and EU Working Time Directive provisions applicable under the Stabilisation and Association Agreement. The chapter describes four representative scheduling scenarios—continuous three-shift baking, seasonal confectionery production, abattoir operations, and frozen-food packaging—and discusses how the regulatory requirements translate into modelling constraints. For each scenario, a compact integer programming formulation is presented and its key structural properties are described. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems, including the handling of public-holiday remuneration rules and the integration of health-surveillance records into fatigue-risk constraints. It is intended as a reference for industrial engineers and graduate students without prior exposure to the Serbian regulatory environment.

title: Fatigue-risk-constrained shift scheduling: an MILP formulation with piecewise-linear approximation of the biomathematical alertness model
abstract: Biomathematical alertness models such as the three-process model of alertness regulation produce non-linear state trajectories that are difficult to embed in exact optimisation frameworks. This paper derives a piecewise-linear approximation of the alertness model using eight linear segments per shift transition, chosen to keep the maximum approximation error below 3 percent of the model's full dynamic range. The approximation is embedded in a mixed-integer linear programme for 24/7 rotating-shift scheduling. Correctness of the approximation is verified against full simulation on 10,000 randomly generated shift sequences. The full MILP is solved on instances drawn from a continuous-process glass manufacturer in Pančevo with 95 workers and a four-week planning horizon. Optimal schedules reduce the fraction of shift handovers occurring at alertness levels below a defined threshold from 18.4 percent in the existing roster to 4.7 percent, while increasing staffing cost by only 2.3 percent.

title: Integrating ergonomic shift-sequence scoring into a column-generation solver for large nurse-analogous industrial rosters
abstract: Column generation is well suited to personnel scheduling but ergonomic scoring of shift sequences is rarely incorporated into the pricing subproblem. This paper reformulates the pricing subproblem for industrial 24/7 scheduling as a shortest-path problem on a state-expanded shift graph in which node weights encode cumulative ergonomic scores based on direction of rotation, night-shift frequency, and weekend burden. Instances from three continuous-process manufacturers in Vojvodina, with workforces of 180 to 520 employees and planning horizons of four weeks, were used to evaluate the approach. Column generation with ergonomic pricing finds schedules that satisfy all ergonomic soft targets in 89 percent of instances, compared to 61 percent for a column-generation model using only hard constraints. Solve times are between 8 and 47 minutes. The paper discusses how the state-expansion factor grows with the number of ergonomic criteria and proposes a reduced-state approximation that keeps solve times below 15 minutes for all tested instances.

title: A decision-support tool for shift-schedule negotiation between management and trade unions: prototype and pilot evaluation
abstract: Collective bargaining over shift schedules involves trade-offs that are difficult to communicate without quantitative support. This paper describes a web-based decision-support tool that exposes a parameterised scheduling model to both management and trade-union representatives, allowing each party to specify preference weights for cost, equity, ergonomic quality, and flexibility. The backend solves a weighted multi-objective integer programme using Gurobi 10 and returns a schedule together with a plain-language summary of trade-offs. The tool was piloted over eight months at a dairy cooperative in Bačka with 230 shift workers. Three rounds of collective negotiation used the tool; in each round both parties reported that the tool improved mutual understanding of constraint interactions. The final agreed schedule achieved a 5 percent cost reduction relative to the previous roster while improving the average ergonomic score by 11 percent. Usability was assessed with the System Usability Scale, yielding a mean score of 74.2 (n = 18 users).

title: Shift scheduling under partial automation: workforce-size implications when collaborative robots replace repetitive tasks on a mixed assembly line
abstract: The introduction of collaborative robots on assembly lines changes the skill profile, cycle time, and monitoring burden of human operators, with direct consequences for shift scheduling. This paper develops a scheduling model for a mixed human–cobot assembly environment in which the number and type of cobot deployments are decision variables alongside shift assignments. Data were collected from a pilot cobot deployment at a small household-appliance manufacturer near Novi Sad involving 48 workers and three cobot units. The model is formulated as a mixed-integer non-linear programme due to the non-linear interaction between cobot allocation and human fatigue load; a linearisation is proposed and validated. Results show that optimal cobot placement, combined with adjusted shift lengths of 6.5 hours instead of 8, reduces total operator fatigue exposure—measured by the embedded alertness model—by 19 percent without increasing headcount. Workforce-size sensitivity is reported as cobot count increases from 0 to 6.

title: Postural load in poultry deboning: an OWAS-based field study in a Serbian processing plant
abstract: This paper reports postural load findings from a structured observational study conducted at a poultry deboning line in Vojvodina, Serbia. Forty-two workers (34 women, 8 men) performing manual deboning and trimming tasks were filmed during two full production shifts. A total of 3,180 OWAS observations were coded by two trained observers and categorised into action categories. Results showed that 28% of observed postures fell into Action Category 3 or 4, with the trunk-forward-bent-and-twisted configuration accounting for the majority of high-risk codes. Standing with both knees bent was rarely recorded but consistently rated high-risk. Inter-rater reliability reached Cohen's kappa of 0.81. Prevalence of reported shoulder and lower-back discomfort, measured via a structured Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire adapted for Serbian language, correlated positively with observed posture scores at the workstation level (r = 0.67, p < 0.01). Recommendations for task rotation scheduling and workstation height adjustment are discussed.

title: Effect of workpiece hardness variation on control chart false-alarm rate in turning operations
abstract: Workpiece-to-workpiece hardness variability is a common source of nuisance variation that inflates false-alarm rates in SPC-based tool monitoring. This study quantifies the effect using 120 shaft blanks drawn from two production batches of C45 steel with measured Brinell hardness ranging from 172 to 198 HB. Shewhart X-bar and R charts built on main cutting force Fc were constructed under three assumptions: (1) constant nominal hardness, (2) batch-mean adjustment, and (3) individual-measurement covariate adjustment. The covariate-adjusted chart reduced the false-alarm rate from 8.4% to 2.1% per tool life, approaching the nominal 0.27% target more closely. The batch-mean approach offered partial improvement (4.6%). A simple linear regression model with hardness as predictor of baseline Fc explained 61% of between-workpiece force variance. The findings suggest that even coarse incoming-material inspection data can substantially improve monitoring reliability in job-shop CNC cells without requiring process redesign.

title: Acoustic emission signal decomposition for built-up edge detection in carbide-insert turning
abstract: Built-up edge (BUE) formation causes surface-finish degradation and unpredictable force transients that confound force-based SPC schemes. This work investigates whether acoustic emission (AE) signals carry earlier or more specific BUE signatures than cutting force. Dry turning tests on annealed AISI 1018 steel were conducted at low cutting speeds (60–100 m/min) where BUE is most prevalent. AE raw waveforms were recorded at 2 MHz; three decomposition methods were compared: RMS windowing (1 ms), wavelet packet decomposition at five levels (Daubechies-8 basis), and empirical mode decomposition. BUE onset was verified by scanning electron microscopy of inserts interrupted at predetermined intervals. Wavelet energy in the 125–250 kHz sub-band rose by a mean of 38% in the 4–6 s preceding confirmed BUE formation, while cutting force Fc showed no statistically significant precursor (paired t-test, p = 0.21). The AE wavelet feature provided a detection lead time of approximately 5 s at 80 m/min, sufficient for adaptive speed adjustment.

title: Multivariate T² monitoring of a three-sensor array in precision boring of grey cast iron
abstract: Boring of grey cast iron bearing housings is sensitive to tool wear because dimensional tolerances are tight (IT6–IT7) and regrinding cycles are expensive. This paper reports a multivariate monitoring scheme based on Hotelling T² statistics applied to a feature vector extracted from three simultaneously acquired signals: radial cutting force, spindle vibration (radial acceleration), and AE RMS. Features (mean, variance, skewness) were extracted from 0.5 s windows, yielding a nine-element vector. A Phase-I baseline was established over 30 fresh-insert passes; Phase-II monitoring covered the remaining tool life across 210 passes on a horizontal boring centre. The T² chart detected tool degradation (VB > 0.25 mm) with an average detection delay of 6.3 passes, compared with 14.1 passes for the best univariate Fc chart. Correlation between vibration RMS and AE RMS was moderate (r = 0.54), supporting the informational value of combining the two sensors. False-alarm frequency was 1.9% per 100 observations, within acceptable limits for production use.

title: Adaptive control chart limits for CNC turning lines with scheduled tool changes
abstract: Fixed control-chart limits derived from a stationary process assumption are poorly suited to turning lines where tool wear is a deterministic trend superimposed on random variation. This paper proposes periodically updated limits computed by subtracting a cubic-spline wear trend estimated from a rolling window of the 20 most recent observations, then applying standard 3-sigma limits to the residuals. The method was evaluated on production data from a manufacturer of hydraulic valve bodies (368 workpieces, four tool changes) machining 16MnCrS5 steel. Compared with fixed-limit Shewhart charts, the adaptive scheme reduced the false-alarm rate from 11.3% to 2.8% and maintained detection power for abrupt tool fracture events (five simulated fractures injected into the data at random positions all detected within two observations). Implementation requires only the existing CNC force-monitoring output and a simple post-processing script, making deployment practical in standard shop-floor environments.

title: Calibration of piezoelectric dynamometers under thermal drift in long-run CNC turning: an uncertainty analysis
abstract: Piezoelectric dynamometers used for in-process force measurement in CNC turning centres exhibit thermal drift during extended operations, introducing systematic errors that affect the validity of SPC-based monitoring. This study characterises the drift behaviour of two platform-type dynamometers over 4-hour continuous turning sessions at spindle loads representative of medium-duty production. Temperature was logged at four points on the dynamometer body. Drift in the Fc channel reached 6.3 N/h under steady-state thermal conditions, equivalent to 1.8% of the nominal force at 350 N cutting load. A drift-compensation model using cubic regression on spindle-motor current as a temperature proxy reduced residual systematic error to below 0.4%. Expanded measurement uncertainty (k = 2) before and after compensation was 4.9% and 1.2%, respectively. The analysis also quantifies how uncompensated drift widens control-chart limits and degrades detection power for incipient wear by a factor of approximately 1.4.

title: Comparison of PCA and partial-least-squares feature reduction for multi-sensor tool-condition classifiers in turning
abstract: Dimensionality reduction is necessary when fusing signals from multiple sensors because high-dimensional feature vectors cause overfitting in downstream classifiers. This paper compares principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares (PLS) as preprocessing steps for a k-nearest-neighbour (k-NN) and a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) classifier, using a five-sensor dataset (cutting force three-axis, AE RMS, and spindle current) from 90 turning trials on 34CrNiMo6 steel. The target classes were three wear states: fresh (VB < 0.10 mm), intermediate (0.10–0.25 mm), and worn (VB > 0.25 mm). PLS-reduced features (five latent variables) fed into LDA achieved 91.4% correct classification on a hold-out test set of 18 trials, outperforming PCA-LDA (84.7%) and PCA–k-NN (82.1%). The PLS approach concentrates variance relevant to the wear label rather than total signal variance, which explains the improvement. Training was performed on data from 72 trials with stratified random split; no cross-sensor synchronisation beyond 1 ms timestamping was required.

title: Transfer learning for tool-wear classifiers across different workpiece materials in CNC turning
abstract: Training tool-wear classifiers separately for each workpiece material is time-consuming and impractical in high-mix production. This paper investigates whether a classifier trained on one steel grade can be adapted to another with limited labelled data from the target material, using a transfer-learning approach based on feature alignment. Source domain: 60 tool-life trials on 42CrMo4 (Rc 28–32). Target domain: 20 trials on AISI 304 austenitic stainless steel, of which only 5 were used for fine-tuning. Features were eight time-domain and frequency-domain quantities from cutting force and AE signals. A maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) alignment layer was inserted between the shared feature extractor and the classification head of a shallow neural network (two hidden layers, 64 and 32 neurons). The adapted classifier achieved 85.1% three-class accuracy on 15 held-out target trials, compared with 61.3% for the unadapted source classifier and 88.7% for a fully trained target-domain classifier (60 trials). The result suggests that 5 labelled target trials can recover most of the performance achievable with a full dataset.

title: Embedded implementation of a real-time CUSUM-particle-filter hybrid monitor on a production CNC turning centre
abstract: Deploying sensor-fusion algorithms directly on the machine controller, rather than on an external PC, avoids communication latency and simplifies installation. This paper describes the integration of a combined CUSUM–particle-filter tool-condition monitor on an embedded ARM Cortex-M7 microcontroller connected to the CNC's internal force-sensor bus. The CUSUM module provides rapid detection of abrupt tool failure (median detection delay 1.8 s) while the particle filter runs in parallel at 2 Hz to update the RUL estimate. Real-time constraints were met: total compute time per cycle was 19 ms at 500 particles. A six-week production trial on a turning cell machining EN 1.4404 stainless steel valve stems produced 2,810 recorded tool changes; the system recommended 93.4% of changes within ±15% of optimal tool life relative to an expert metallurgist's reference. Tool breakages without prior warning occurred in 4 of 2,810 cases (0.14%). Energy consumption of the embedded module was 1.2 W, negligible relative to the machine.

title: Serum corticosterone response in broilers subjected to simulated short-haul transport: effect of journey duration and stocking density
abstract: This study examined how journey duration (30, 60, and 120 minutes) and stocking density (30, 40, and 50 kg/m²) affect serum corticosterone concentrations in Ross 308 broilers aged 42 days. A total of 216 birds were assigned to nine treatment combinations in a 3×3 factorial design. Blood samples were collected immediately after unloading. Serum corticosterone was determined by radioimmunoassay. Mean corticosterone was 28.4 ng/mL in the control group (crated but stationary), rising to 74.6 ng/mL at 120 minutes combined with the highest stocking density. A significant interaction between duration and density was detected (p < 0.01). Birds at 50 kg/m² for 120 minutes showed visible wing injuries in 14% of cases. Mortality was below 0.5% across all groups. The results confirm that transport duration above 60 minutes at commercial stocking densities produces a marked HPA axis response and that the two factors act synergistically on corticosterone output.

title: Lairage duration and its influence on corticosterone, glucose, and lactate in broiler chickens at a commercial abattoir
abstract: Broilers held in lairage for 0, 1, 2, and 4 hours were sampled for blood corticosterone, plasma glucose, and venous lactate immediately before electrical stunning at a certified abattoir in Vojvodina. A cohort of 320 birds (80 per group) was monitored across four consecutive slaughter shifts to minimise batch-to-batch variation. Lairage at ambient temperature (22–24 °C) for 4 hours elevated corticosterone by 58% relative to the 0-hour group (p < 0.001) and was associated with significantly higher lactate (4.1 vs. 2.7 mmol/L). Glucose did not differ significantly between groups. Breast meat pH at 24 hours post-mortem decreased with lairage duration, with the 4-hour group averaging pH 5.72 compared to 5.89 in the 0-hour group, suggesting a link between ante-mortem stress and meat quality. Implications for abattoir scheduling are discussed.

title: Validation of an ELISA-based salivary corticosterone assay in domestic chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus)
abstract: Saliva collection from poultry is technically challenging, and few commercial ELISA kits have been systematically validated for this matrix in chickens. Saliva was collected using absorbent swabs from the oral mucosa of 60 Ross 308 broilers at rest and following a standardised handling challenge. Salivary and simultaneously collected serum corticosterone concentrations were compared. Kit precision (intra-assay CV < 9.3%, inter-assay CV < 14.1%), recovery after spike-and-recovery testing (87–106%), and parallelism of serially diluted samples were all satisfactory. Salivary and serum corticosterone were significantly correlated (r = 0.74, p < 0.001), though salivary values were approximately 4-fold lower than serum values. The time lag between blood sampling and peak salivary output was estimated at 15–20 minutes based on repeated sampling. The method offers a practical non-invasive complement to blood-based measurement in welfare research, particularly in field conditions where venepuncture is logistically constrained.

title: Feather corticosterone as a retrospective indicator of chronic stress in commercial broilers: a field comparison across three production systems
abstract: Feathers integrate corticosterone deposition over the period of their growth and can therefore reflect cumulative HPA axis activity rather than acute stress. Contour feathers from the breast and dorsal regions were collected at slaughter from 150 birds each reared in conventional floor housing, enriched floor housing, and slow-growth floor housing on farms in Vojvodina. Feathers were washed, finely cut, and extracted with methanol; corticosterone was quantified by ELISA. Mean feather corticosterone in conventional housing (19.4 pg/mg) was significantly higher than in the slow-growth system (11.2 pg/mg, p < 0.001); enriched conventional housing yielded intermediate values (15.6 pg/mg). Feather region did not significantly affect concentrations after controlling for feather mass. The results suggest feather corticosterone can differentiate welfare status across production systems and warrants further investigation as a routine audit measure in poultry slaughter lines.

title: In-vehicle thermal conditions during summer broiler transport in Serbia: microclimate profiling and association with mortality
abstract: Thermal stress during summer transport is a major welfare and economic concern in poultry production. Data loggers were installed at three positions within commercial transport vehicles on ten separate journeys carried out between June and August in Vojvodina, recording temperature and relative humidity every 30 seconds. Journeys ranged from 45 to 190 minutes. Mean in-vehicle temperature was 31.8 °C (range 24.1–41.3 °C), and mean relative humidity was 73%. Temperature was highest in the central module of the vehicle and during journeys exceeding 90 minutes. Dead-on-arrival rates correlated positively with maximum recorded temperature (r = 0.68, p < 0.05). On two journeys exceeding 39 °C, DOA rates reached 0.9% and 1.2%, substantially above the industry threshold of 0.3%. Recommendations for scheduling, ventilation adjustment, and wet-bulb temperature monitoring during summer months are proposed based on the data.

title: Welfare assessment at slaughter: integrating feather corticosterone, gait scoring at farm, and carcass lesion recording in a single-farm longitudinal study
abstract: A longitudinal welfare assessment protocol was applied to a single commercial broiler farm in Vojvodina across five consecutive production cycles. At day 35, gait scoring (using a 0–5 Kestin scale) was performed on 50 randomly selected birds per flock. At slaughter, breast feathers were sampled for corticosterone, and carcasses were inspected for contact dermatitis, hock burns, and breast blisters at the abattoir line. Mean gait scores ranged from 1.4 to 2.3 across cycles. Feather corticosterone correlated moderately with mean gait score (r = 0.61) and with hock burn prevalence (r = 0.58). Breast blister prevalence was 12–27% across cycles and showed no consistent correlation with hormonal measures. The study demonstrates that combining on-farm and slaughter-line indicators provides a more complete welfare picture than any single measure alone, and that feather corticosterone can be embedded in existing inspection routines with minimal additional cost.

title: Salivary corticosterone in broilers during repeated short-duration handling: habituation or sensitisation?
abstract: Whether broiler chickens habituate to repeated handling is relevant for welfare during catching and loading. Forty-eight birds underwent a standardised 3-minute inversion and restraint procedure on days 1, 3, 5, and 7. Saliva was collected by oral swab at rest (T0) and 20 minutes after each handling event (T20). Salivary corticosterone was determined by ELISA. On day 1, mean T20 corticosterone was 4.8 ng/mL above T0. By day 7, the T20 elevation had decreased to 2.1 ng/mL, suggesting partial habituation. However, individual variation was high (CV > 40% at T20 across all sessions), and a subset of birds (19%) showed elevated responses on day 7 relative to day 1, indicating sensitisation in some individuals. Body weight gain did not differ between handled and unhandled controls over the 7-day period. Results have practical relevance for catch-training protocols and welfare during loading operations.

title: Non-invasive welfare indicators in broilers: a comparative review of salivary corticosterone, feather corticosterone, and ocular surface temperature
abstract: This book chapter reviews the current state of three non-invasive welfare assessment tools applicable to broiler chickens in commercial settings. Salivary corticosterone offers a near-real-time snapshot of HPA axis activation with practical collection methods but requires validation for each matrix–kit combination. Feather corticosterone provides retrospective information on chronic stress accumulated during the growth period and is robust to post-collection handling if feathers are stored dry. Infrared thermography of the ocular surface has shown promise as a rapid, contact-free screening tool, though confounding from environmental temperature remains a limitation. The chapter compares reported sensitivity, specificity, and logistical requirements across the three methods based on published experimental data, and suggests that combining salivary sampling at loading with feather corticosterone at slaughter would capture complementary time windows of welfare status. Practical guidance for field application is included, with worked examples from farms in central and south-eastern Europe.

title: Impact of journey distance category on salivary and feather corticosterone in broilers transported to three abattoirs in Vojvodina
abstract: Transport distance is frequently cited as a welfare risk factor, but empirical data relating journey distance to both acute (salivary) and chronic-integrative (feather) corticosterone within the same birds are scarce. This study enrolled 360 birds from six farms in Vojvodina supplying three abattoirs at distances of 18–22 km (short), 55–65 km (medium), and 110–130 km (long). Saliva was collected by trained operators at unloading using oral swabs, and breast feathers were collected at slaughter. Salivary corticosterone was significantly higher in the long-distance group than in the short-distance group (p = 0.008), with medium-distance values intermediate and not significantly different from either extreme. Feather corticosterone did not differ across distance categories (p = 0.62), consistent with the interpretation that farm-rearing conditions rather than transport history drive feather concentrations. Ambient temperature during transport acted as a significant covariate for salivary corticosterone.

title: Arithmetic Fluency Gains in Third-Grade Students Following a Board-Game Intervention: A Pilot Study
abstract: This pilot study examined whether a structured board game targeting multiplication facts could improve arithmetic fluency in 48 third-grade students from two primary schools in Sombor. Classes were assigned to game-based practice or standard worksheet practice over four weeks, with three 40-minute sessions per week. Pre- and post-tests used timed recall tasks drawn from a validated Serbian instrument. Students in the game condition improved their correct-answers-per-minute score by an average of 6.4 items compared with 3.1 in the control group. Effect size was d = 0.61. Engagement ratings collected by teachers showed higher on-task behaviour in the game condition on 14 of 16 observed sessions. The study concluded that brief, structured board-game sessions can produce moderate fluency gains, while noting that sample size and single-site design limit generalisability. A larger replication was recommended.

title: Cognitive Load During Digital-Physical Hybrid Math Tasks: Eye-Tracking Evidence from Nine-Year-Olds
abstract: This study used eye-tracking to assess cognitive load while 34 nine-year-old students completed a hybrid math task combining a tablet-based game with physical fraction tiles. Fixation duration, saccade length, and pupil dilation were recorded using a remote eye-tracker mounted on a desk. Tasks required students to match digital fraction representations to physical tile arrangements of varying complexity. Linear mixed-effects models showed that pupil dilation increased significantly with task complexity level (β = 0.14 mm per level, 95% CI [0.08, 0.20]), while longer fixations on the physical tile area were associated with higher accuracy on subsequent written fraction problems (r = 0.43). Students who frequently switched gaze between screen and tiles made fewer procedural errors. Results suggest that coordinated dual-channel engagement, rather than one medium alone, supports fraction comprehension. Practical implications for task sequencing in hybrid game design are discussed.

title: Game Mechanics and Fraction Misconceptions: A Quasi-Experimental Classroom Study
abstract: Persistent misconceptions about fractions, such as treating numerator and denominator as independent whole numbers, are well documented but poorly addressed by conventional drill practice. This quasi-experimental study tested whether a physical card game designed around part-whole fraction models could reduce four specific misconceptions identified in a 186-student diagnostic pre-test drawn from grades four and five in five Vojvodina schools. Game sessions replaced one of three weekly arithmetic lessons over eight weeks. Post-test data showed statistically significant reductions in two of the four targeted misconceptions: the independent-whole-number error fell from 54% to 31% of responses, and the larger-denominator-means-larger-fraction error fell from 41% to 22%. The other two misconceptions showed non-significant trends. Teacher implementation fidelity, measured via observation checklists, was moderately correlated with misconception reduction rates (r = 0.52). The study highlights implementation quality as a key moderator of game-based outcomes.

title: Teachers' Preparedness to Facilitate Game-Based Mathematics Lessons: Survey Evidence from Primary Schools in Serbia
abstract: Effective integration of game-based learning in primary mathematics depends substantially on teacher knowledge and confidence. This cross-sectional survey reached 203 primary school mathematics teachers across Serbia through a self-administered online questionnaire measuring four constructs: technological competence, game-facilitation confidence, beliefs about play in learning, and reported barriers. Exploratory factor analysis confirmed a four-factor solution accounting for 61% of variance. Teachers in urban schools reported significantly higher technological competence than those in rural schools (t(201) = 3.87, p < 0.001), while beliefs about play did not differ by location. Only 28% of respondents reported having received any in-service training on game-based methods. Regression analysis showed that game-facilitation confidence was the strongest predictor of self-reported frequency of game use in class, above technological competence and beliefs. Findings point to a need for structured professional development programmes targeting facilitation skills specifically.

title: Spatial Reasoning and Number Line Understanding: Can a Hybrid Sliding-Tile Game Bridge the Two?
abstract: Research suggests that spatial reasoning and number line understanding share cognitive resources in late childhood, but few interventions have targeted both simultaneously. This study evaluated a hybrid game in which students physically repositioned numbered tiles on a floor-mounted number line while receiving feedback from a paired tablet application. Eighty-one students in grade three from four schools participated in a six-week intervention. Spatial reasoning was measured with a mental rotation task and a block-pattern completion task; number line understanding was measured with a computerised number placement task. Compared to a business-as-usual control group, the intervention group showed significant improvement on the number placement task (d = 0.67) and on the block-pattern task (d = 0.44), but not on mental rotation (d = 0.18, p = 0.19). Mediation analysis suggested that number line gains partially mediated improvements on block-pattern completion, though causal interpretation is limited by study design.

title: Socioeconomic Moderation of Game-Based Learning Effects on Arithmetic in Grade Four: Evidence from Rural and Urban Schools in Vojvodina
abstract: Whether game-based learning benefits are equally distributed across socioeconomic groups is underexplored in the regional literature. This study used multilevel modelling to analyse data from a six-week hybrid game intervention conducted across 14 primary schools in Vojvodina, covering 312 fourth-grade students. Schools were classified as urban, peri-urban, and rural; student socioeconomic status was estimated using a parental education composite score. The main effect of the intervention on arithmetic post-test scores was significant (β = 5.1 points, SE = 1.2). A significant interaction between intervention condition and socioeconomic status (β = 1.8, SE = 0.7, p = 0.01) indicated that students from lower socioeconomic backgrounds benefited somewhat more from the game condition than higher-SES peers, though both groups improved. School location did not moderate the intervention effect after controlling for socioeconomic status. These findings tentatively support the use of hybrid games as a tool for reducing within-classroom arithmetic achievement gaps.

title: Using Tablet-Logged Interaction Data to Predict Mathematics Post-Test Scores in a Game-Based Intervention
abstract: Tablet-based educational games generate interaction logs that can, in principle, serve as formative signals during an intervention. This study examined whether log data collected during a four-week hybrid game intervention predicted end-of-intervention post-test scores in 88 grade-four and grade-five students. Nine log features were extracted per student per session: session duration, number of attempts per item, error rate, help-request frequency, inter-attempt latency, game-level progression rate, voluntary replay frequency, score volatility, and session abandonment count. Ridge regression with leave-one-out cross-validation explained 41% of post-test variance using log features alone, compared with 38% for the arithmetic pre-test score alone. A combined model including both pre-test score and log features explained 53% of variance. Error rate and inter-attempt latency were the most influential log features. The study suggests that interaction logs carry predictive information beyond baseline ability, but effect sizes indicate that log-based prediction should complement, not replace, conventional assessment.

title: A Registered Replication of the Hybrid Game Advantage for Fraction Near-Transfer: Preregistered Study in Three Countries
abstract: A 2014 study by the first author reported a near-transfer advantage for hybrid over digital-only fraction game instruction. This registered replication tested the same hypothesis across schools in Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary, enrolling 341 grade-four students in a three-arm design (hybrid game, digital-only game, curriculum-as-usual control). Preregistration was lodged on the Open Science Framework before data collection. The arithmetic test and near-transfer fraction task were identical to the original study; a new far-transfer measurement task was added. Replication of the near-transfer advantage was successful in two of three countries: standardised effect sizes were d = 0.44 (Serbia), d = 0.39 (Croatia), and d = 0.11 (Hungary, non-significant). A moderation analysis found that the Hungarian null result was associated with significantly higher baseline fraction knowledge in those students. Far-transfer effects were small and non-significant across all sites. The study supports the original finding with important boundary conditions related to prior knowledge levels.

title: Effects of Game Session Length on Arithmetic Learning and Fatigue in Nine-to-Eleven-Year-Olds: A Within-Subject Crossover Study
abstract: Optimal session length for game-based arithmetic practice remains empirically underdetermined. This within-subject crossover study assigned 62 students aged nine to eleven to three session lengths (15, 30, and 45 minutes) using a counterbalanced schedule over nine weeks. Each session length was repeated twice per student. Outcomes measured immediately after each session included a ten-item arithmetic probe, a five-item attention check, and a self-report fatigue rating on a visual analogue scale adapted for children. Linear mixed-effects models treating student as a random effect showed that arithmetic probe scores peaked after 30-minute sessions and were significantly lower after 45-minute sessions (β = −1.8 items, 95% CI [−3.1, −0.5]). Fatigue ratings increased monotonically with session length. Attentiveness scores did not differ between 15- and 30-minute sessions but were lower after 45 minutes. Order effects were not significant. Results recommend 30-minute game sessions as a practical default for this age group in classroom settings.

title: Microsatellite-based genotyping reveals two genetically distinct clusters of Phytophthora sojae in Serbian soybean-growing areas
abstract: Phytophthora root and stem rot caused by Phytophthora sojae is the predominant oomycete disease of soybean in Serbia, yet its population structure across the Pannonian Plain has not been characterised at the genotype level. Forty-eight isolates were collected from symptomatic soybean plants at 19 locations in Vojvodina and the Mačva region during 2022 and 2023. Each isolate was genotyped at twelve microsatellite loci developed for P. sojae. Multilocus genotype analysis identified 31 distinct genotypes. Bayesian clustering in STRUCTURE and discriminant analysis of principal components both recovered two genetic clusters that corresponded broadly to a northern Vojvodina group and a south-western Mačva group, with FST = 0.19 between them. Analysis of molecular variance attributed 78 % of genetic variation to within-field level. No significant isolation-by-distance pattern was detected at the regional scale, suggesting that human-mediated dispersal through seed and machinery movement may override geographic barriers. This is the first microsatellite-based population study of P. sojae in Serbia and provides a framework for tracking pathogen spread.

Na svakom lokalitetu postavljeni su transekti dužine 50 m, perpendikularno na tok vode, a vegetacijski snimci izrađeni su po Braun-Blanquet metodi. Ukupno je zabeleženo sedam invazivnih žbunastih taksona, od kojih su Amorpha fruticosa, Reynoutria japonica i Ailanthus altissima pokazali najveću frekvenciju i pokrivenost. Udeo invazivnih vrsta u ukupnoj žbunastoj pokrovnosti kretao se od 14% do 67%, zavisno od lokaliteta i stepena antropogenog poremećaja. Rezultati ukazuju na jasnu korelaciju između intenziteta poplava i ekspanzije A. fruticosa u zoni do 15 m od obale. Rad pruža polaznu tačku za dugoročno praćenje dinamike invazivnih žbunova na nizijskim vodotocima Srbije.

title: Competitive exclusion of Cornus sanguinea by Amorpha fruticosa in flood-disturbed shrub layers: a field experiment
abstract: We tested whether Amorpha fruticosa suppresses regeneration of the native shrub Cornus sanguinea under controlled field conditions at two riparian sites along the Tisa River in northern Serbia. Paired 4 × 4 m plots (n = 24) were established in 2010; half received manual removal of A. fruticosa shoots at the start of each growing season for three consecutive years, while control plots were left undisturbed. Shoot counts, basal area, and canopy light transmittance (measured with a spherical densiometer) were recorded annually. After three years, C. sanguinea shoot density in removal plots was 3.4 times higher than in controls, and photosynthetically active radiation at ground level increased by 38%. Total aboveground biomass of A. fruticosa in control plots increased by approximately 220% over the study period. Results indicate that even single-season mechanical intervention significantly reduces competitive pressure, but effects decline without repeated management.

title: Fenološka dinamika ornamentalnih invazivnih žbunova na urbanim zelenilskim koridorima Novog Sada
abstract: Cilj rada bio je da se utvrdi fenološki ritam šest introdukovanih ornamentalnih žbunastih vrsta prisutnih u urbanim zelenilskim koridorima Novog Sada: Forsythia × intermedia, Spiraea japonica, Buddleja davidii, Ligustrum ovalifolium, Mahonia aquifolium i Cotoneaster horizontalis. Praćenje je vršeno na 30 individua svake vrste tokom tri vegetacijske sezone (2011–2013), a zabeleženi su datumi listanja, prvog cveta, pune cvetnosti, fruktifikacije i senescencije lišća. Fenološki podaci upoređivani su sa podacima za autohtone vrste srodnih morfotipova (Ligustrum vulgare, Cornus mas, Prunus spinosa). Utvrđeno je da S. japonica i B. davidii ispoljavaju značajno duži period cvetanja (za 18–31 dan) u poređenju sa autohtonim vrstama sličnih ekoloških uloga, što im daje prednost u privlačenju polinatora i potencijalnom ukrštanju. Razmatrane su implikacije fenoloških prednosti za upravljanje gradskim zelenilom.

title: Invazivni žbunovi u pejzažnoj arhitekturi: pregled rizika naturalnih vrsta i smernice za zamenu
abstract: Rad sistematizuje dostupne podatke o 14 ornamentalnih žbunastih vrsta koje se koriste ili su se koristile u pejzažnoj arhitekturi Srbije, a koje su registrovane kao invazivne ili potencijalno invazivne u regionu jugoistočne Evrope. Za svaku vrstu prikazani su: poreklo, vreme introdukcije, učestalost sadnje u periodu 1970–2014, zabeleženi kapacitet naturalizacije i inventarisane populacije u poluprirodnim staništima. Posebna pažnja posvećena je vrstama Buddleja davidii, Spiraea japonica i Mahonia aquifolium, koje su u porastu u urbanom i periurbanom zelenilu, a čije su divlje populacije sve brojnije duž vodotoka i putnih koridora. Predložen je okvir za procenu rizika na osnovu pet kriterijuma (vitalnost semena, disperzija, tolerancija zasene, brzina rasta, alelopatski potencijal) i date su preporuke za zamenu problematičnih vrsta autohtonim alternativama. Rad je namenjen projektantima zelenih površina i komunalnim preduzećima.
