title: Interspecific root competition between Salix alba and Amorpha fruticosa at varying water-table depths: mesocosm study
abstract: Root competition between the native riparian tree Salix alba and the invasive shrub Amorpha fruticosa was examined in a mesocosm experiment (n = 60 containers, 80 L each) maintained at three simulated water-table depths (−10 cm, −40 cm, −80 cm from soil surface) over one growing season. Treatments included monocultures and mixed plantings. Biomass, root architecture, and fine-root length density were measured at harvest. At −10 cm water table, Salix alba allocated proportionally more biomass to fine roots in mixed versus monoculture conditions (ratio 1.6), while A. fruticosa showed no significant biomass reduction, suggesting asymmetric competition favouring the invasive. At −80 cm, competition effects were balanced. Root length density of A. fruticosa exceeded that of S. alba by a factor of 2.1 at intermediate water-table depth. Results are discussed in relation to management of young riparian plantations where both species co-occur.

title: Uticaj Reynoutria japonica na diverzitet autohtone prizemne flore u riparijanskim pojasevima nizvodno od urbanizovanih zona
abstract: Reynoutria japonica formira guste monodominantne sastojine koje značajno menjaju strukturu riparijalnih zajednica nizvodno od naselja. U ovom radu analizirani su podaci sa 36 pari parcela (invadiranih i kontrolnih) postavljenih duž pet vodotoka koji prolaze kroz ili pored urbanizovanih zona u Vojvodini i severnoj Šumadiji. Na svakoj parceli (5 × 5 m) snimane su sve vaskularne biljke, a određeni su bogatsvo vrsta, Shannon-ov indeks diverziteta i Simpsonov indeks dominantnosti. U invadiranim parcelama utvrđen je prosečan pad broja vrsta od 62% u poređenju sa kontrolama. Posebno su bile pogođene trajnice male visine i jednogodišnje biljke osetljive na zasenčenost. Rezultati su konzistentni sa ranijim istraživanjima iz zapadne Evrope, ali pokazuju nešto veću stopu gubitka vrsta, što se dovodi u vezu sa specifičnom klimom i hidrologijom istraživanog područja.

title: Mapping invasive shrub patches along the Danube greenway in Serbia using UAV-derived multispectral imagery
abstract: We report a workflow for detecting and delineating patches of Amorpha fruticosa and Fallopia japonica along a 47 km segment of the Danube riparian greenway in Serbia using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) surveys. Flights were conducted in June and September 2020 with a quadrotor platform carrying a five-band multispectral sensor (green, red, red-edge, near-infrared, thermal). Ground-truth data were collected at 180 validation points. A random-forest classifier trained on spectral indices (NDVI, CIre, NDWI) and texture features achieved overall accuracy of 87% (kappa 0.83) for a five-class land-cover scheme including the two focal invasive species, native shrub layer, reed beds, and open ground. Amorpha fruticosa occupied 34% of the total shrub-covered area in the corridor, while F. japonica patches were smaller and concentrated near infrastructure access points. The maps have been shared with the relevant public waterways authority for management planning.

title: Allelopathic effects of Amorpha fruticosa root exudates on germination and early growth of native riparian shrub seedlings under laboratory conditions
abstract: Root exudates of Amorpha fruticosa were collected by hydroponic trapping from 20 greenhouse-grown plants and used to prepare aqueous solutions at three concentrations (2.5%, 5%, 10% w/v equivalent dry root mass). Germination and radicle growth of seeds from five native riparian shrubs (Cornus sanguinea, Sambucus nigra, Viburnum opulus, Rosa canina, Prunus spinosa) were tested in Petri-dish bioassays (n = 30 per species per treatment). All five species showed statistically significant reductions in germination rate at the 10% concentration compared with distilled water controls, ranging from −19% (R. canina) to −47% (V. opulus). Radicle length was reduced more consistently than germination percentage across concentrations. High-performance liquid chromatography identified three phenolic compounds (isoflavone derivatives and a flavanone glycoside) as candidate allelopathic agents. Results suggest that allelopathy may partly explain the suppression of native shrub regeneration beneath established A. fruticosa stands observed in field studies.

title: Procena kapaciteta ugljeničnog ponora u gustim sastojinama invazivnog žbuna Amorpha fruticosa na aluvijalnim terenima Vojvodine
abstract: Cilj rada bio je da se izmeri nadzemna i podzemna biomasa i proceni kapacitet skladištenja ugljenika u monodominantnim sastojinama Amorpha fruticosa na šest aluvijalnih lokaliteta u Vojvodini. Na svakom lokalitetu postavljene su četiri probne plohe (25 m²), na kojima su izmereni prsni prečnici, visine i pokrivenost žbunova, a uzeti su uzorci korena (do 50 cm dubine). Primenjene su alometrijske jednačine razvijene za srodne leguminozne žbunove, a ugljenični ekvivalenti izračunati standardnom metodom (biomasa × 0,47). Ukupna nadzemna biomasa kretala se od 4,3 do 11,7 t s.m. ha⁻¹, a podzemna od 1,9 do 5,1 t s.m. ha⁻¹. Ove vrednosti su niže od onih kod autohtonih žbunastih zajednica sličnih starosnih profila, ali ne zanemarljive. Rad raspravlja o konfliktnim ciljevima između upravljanja invazivnim vrstama i kratkoročnog skladištenja ugljenika, sa preporukama za integrisan pristup.

title: Long-term population dynamics of Buddleja davidii in periurban riparian margins: evidence from repeat photographic surveys and demographic modelling
abstract: Buddleja davidii has expanded from ornamental plantings into semi-natural riparian margins across central Serbia since the early 2000s. We used a combination of repeat photographic surveys at 22 fixed stations (surveyed in 2011, 2016, 2021, and 2025), size-structured demographic censuses in 2021 and 2025, and integral projection models to quantify population growth rates and identify key demographic transitions. Photographic evidence documented patch expansion at 19 of 22 stations, with a mean annual radial spread of 0.8 m in unmanaged margins. Estimated finite population growth rate (λ) was 1.14 (95% CI: 1.08–1.21) across all censused patches. Sensitivity analysis identified seedling survival-to-juvenile transition as the stage most strongly affecting λ, suggesting that targeting juvenile plants in management programmes would be more cost-effective than removing adults alone. Comparison with European data suggests B. davidii performs less aggressively in Pannonian conditions than in Atlantic-influenced climates, possibly reflecting lower winter precipitation.

title: Convergence Analysis of P-Type Iterative Learning Control for a Single-Axis Belt-Driven Positioning Stage
abstract: This paper examines the convergence properties of proportional-type iterative learning control (ILC) applied to a single-axis belt-driven linear stage intended for repetitive point-to-point motion. A lumped-parameter model of the stage was derived, accounting for belt stiffness of approximately 4.2 kN/m and a carriage mass of 2.1 kg. Convergence conditions were established in the frequency domain using the standard norm-based criterion, and the influence of belt elasticity on the usable learning gain range was quantified. Experiments were conducted on a laboratory stage driven by a 400 W servo motor, with position measured by a 1 µm resolution linear encoder. Over 50 trial repetitions, the root-mean-square tracking error decreased from 0.48 mm on the first trial to 0.031 mm at convergence, a reduction of approximately 94%. The results confirm that neglecting belt compliance in the inversion-based learning filter leads to divergence above 18 Hz commanded trajectory bandwidth, while a compliance-aware filter maintains stable convergence up to 34 Hz.

title: Identification of Frequency-Dependent Stiffness in Synchronous Belt Drives for Control Design
abstract: Synchronous rubber belts used in linear gantry drives exhibit stiffness that varies with preload and excitation frequency, complicating model-based control design. This study presents an experimental identification procedure using swept-sine excitation over the range 1–200 Hz applied to a preloaded GT2 polyurethane belt with steel cord reinforcement. Three belt lengths (0.6 m, 1.1 m, and 1.8 m) and two preload levels (50 N and 120 N) were tested. Dynamic stiffness was extracted from force–displacement frequency response measurements using a non-contact laser vibrometer. Results show that apparent stiffness drops by up to 22% between 10 Hz and 80 Hz for the longest belt at low preload, a variation large enough to shift closed-loop resonance by 4.2 Hz. A piecewise linear model parameterised in belt length and preload is proposed as a practical substitute for full viscoelastic models in ILC filter design.

title: Effect of Gantry Frame Vibration on ILC Convergence in High-Speed Repetitive Positioning
abstract: When a belt-driven Cartesian gantry operates at cycle rates above approximately 60 cycles per minute, the frame itself exhibits measurable vibration at frequencies near structural resonance. This paper investigates how such frame motion degrades the measured position signal and thereby disrupts iterative learning control convergence. Accelerometers were mounted at four frame nodes on a steel-profile gantry of 1.4 m × 0.9 m working area, and the vibration spectrum was recorded during 100-trial ILC runs at three cycle rates: 40, 65, and 80 cycles per minute. At 80 cycles per minute a 47 Hz frame mode was excited, injecting noise into the encoder feedback with an amplitude of 6 µm RMS. A notch filter at 47 Hz inserted in the learning path reduced the error floor from 0.062 mm to 0.024 mm. Finite element predictions of frame resonances agreed with measured values to within 4%, confirming that simple static-frame models are insufficient for high-speed ILC design.

title: Comparison of D-type and Gradient-Descent ILC Algorithms on a Flexible-Transmission Gantry with Varying Friction
abstract: Friction in linear guideways of Cartesian gantry systems is not constant: it varies with velocity, temperature, and lubrication state over a working shift. This study compares the sensitivity of derivative-type (D-type) and gradient-descent ILC to such friction variations. A horizontal single-axis gantry was operated over a four-hour session during which guideway friction torque was estimated online using a disturbance observer. Friction varied between 1.8 N and 4.4 N over the session. D-type ILC showed steady-state RMS errors that increased from 0.027 mm at the start to 0.061 mm after two hours before a re-initialisation was needed. The gradient-descent variant, which re-estimates the system Markov parameters every 20 trials, maintained errors below 0.033 mm throughout. Computational overhead of the online identification step was 1.4 ms per sample on a 1 kHz control loop, compatible with real-time implementation on the dSPACE DS1007 target used in the experiment.

title: Iterative Learning Control in Motion Systems with Flexible Transmissions
abstract: This book chapter provides an account of ILC design for motion control systems in which a flexible element—belt, lead screw, or cable—couples the actuator to the load. After a short review of the ILC framework, the chapter develops plant models for three transmission types and discusses how compliance affects the lifted-system representation central to NOILC synthesis. Stability and monotone convergence conditions are derived in terms of belt stiffness and carriage inertia ratios. Design guidelines are given for choosing Q/R weighting and trial-varying update laws. Worked examples are drawn from Cartesian gantry experiments, with data on convergence rates and steady-state error floors. The chapter closes with a discussion of remaining open problems, including robust ILC under transmission wear and extension to three-axis systems.

title: Effect of cable mass distribution on natural frequencies and mode shapes of a spatial CDPR
abstract: For large-span CDPRs the assumption that cables are massless introduces non-negligible errors in predicted natural frequencies, particularly for cables exceeding 4 m in length. This study extends a standard rigid-body dynamic model to account for distributed cable mass using a catenary formulation, and compares predicted natural frequencies against experimental values obtained from accelerometer-based modal analysis on a 5 m × 4 m × 3 m CDPR. Eight cable segments are analysed with lengths between 1.2 m and 6.1 m at three tension levels. The catenary model predicts the first four natural frequencies to within 4% of measured values, while the massless model underestimates the first transverse frequency by up to 23% for the longest cables. Modal damping ratios, identified using the half-power bandwidth method, lie in the range 0.8–2.1% and are insensitive to tension level within the tested range. Implications for minimum sampling frequency in trajectory controllers are discussed.

title: Comparison of AHP and TOPSIS for Prioritising IT Infrastructure Investments in Serbian Public Hospitals
abstract: The study compares AHP and TOPSIS as decision support tools for prioritising IT infrastructure investments across 12 public hospitals in Serbia. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to hospital IT managers and financial directors between March and June 2014, yielding 36 usable responses. Nine evaluation criteria were identified, covering cost, interoperability, vendor support, staff training requirements, regulatory compliance, and projected efficiency gains. Both methods were applied to rank seven candidate investment packages under each criterion set. Rank correlations between the two methods (Spearman ρ = 0.81) indicated substantial agreement, with divergence concentrated in mid-ranked alternatives. Sensitivity analysis varying criterion weights by ±20% revealed that TOPSIS rankings were more stable than AHP rankings in this dataset. The paper concludes that TOPSIS may be preferable when criteria weights carry high uncertainty, while AHP is advantageous when stakeholder preference elicitation is a central process goal.

title: Group AHP with Consensus Measurement for Selecting Outsourcing Partners in Public Utilities
abstract: This conference paper examines the use of group AHP for outsourcing partner selection in two Serbian public utility companies responsible for water supply and waste management. The decision problem involved eight candidate suppliers evaluated against 11 criteria organised in a three-level hierarchy. A panel of seven decision-makers participated, each providing independent pairwise judgements. Individual priority vectors were aggregated using both the arithmetic mean of local priorities and the geometric mean of judgements; the two aggregation strategies produced rank reversals for two of eight alternatives. A consensus index based on Kendall's coefficient of concordance (W = 0.67 and W = 0.71 for the two companies) was used to measure and improve inter-judge agreement through a structured discussion protocol. The paper describes the facilitation process in detail and reports that a second round of judgements raised both W values above 0.80. Practical implications for procurement committees in Serbian public enterprises are discussed.

title: Fuzzy AHP for Evaluating E-Government Service Quality Criteria: Evidence from Local Governments in the Western Balkans
abstract: This paper applies fuzzy AHP to assess the relative importance of e-government service quality criteria as perceived by citizens and public administrators in four Western Balkan countries: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Triangular fuzzy numbers were used to capture linguistic uncertainty in pairwise comparisons, with data gathered through a web-based instrument completed by 94 respondents—47 civil servants and 47 members of the public. The criteria framework comprised five dimensions: accessibility, reliability, transparency, responsiveness, and data security, further decomposed into 19 sub-criteria. Defuzzification was performed using the centre-of-gravity method. Results indicated that transparency and data security received the highest fuzzy weights across all four country samples, while responsiveness showed the greatest cross-country variance. The study provides a weighted criteria template that e-government programme managers can use as a baseline for investment prioritisation without repeating the full elicitation procedure.

title: MCDM Methods in Public Procurement: A Systematic Review of Applications in Central and Eastern Europe, 2005–2019
abstract: This chapter reviews 74 peer-reviewed studies published between 2005 and 2019 that apply multi-criteria decision-making methods to public procurement problems in Central and Eastern European countries. Studies were identified through searches of Scopus and Web of Science using a pre-registered search protocol, screened by two independent reviewers, and coded for method used, procurement domain, country, data type, and reported performance outcomes. AHP was the most frequently applied method (41%), followed by TOPSIS (22%) and combined AHP-TOPSIS frameworks (18%). Infrastructure procurement dominated the application domain (38 studies). Critical appraisal identified recurring methodological weaknesses including insufficient reporting of consistency ratios, absence of sensitivity analysis, and failure to validate model outputs against actual procurement decisions. The chapter proposes a minimum reporting standard for MCDM studies in public procurement and identifies under-researched domains including social services procurement and IT services contracting in the region.

title: Combining BWM and VIKOR for Evaluating Smart City Project Proposals: Application to Novi Sad's Urban Development Fund
abstract: This paper reports on a decision support exercise conducted for the Urban Development Fund of Novi Sad, tasked with evaluating 16 smart city project proposals submitted in 2022. The Best-Worst Method (BWM) was used to elicit criterion weights from a panel of six evaluators drawn from the fund, the City of Novi Sad administration, and an academic advisory board, reducing the number of pairwise comparisons required relative to full AHP. Eight criteria were used: innovation potential, alignment with the city's 2030 strategy, financial sustainability, environmental impact, social inclusion, technical feasibility, scalability, and data privacy compliance. The VIKOR method was then applied to rank the 16 proposals, producing a compromise ranking and three separate rankings based on maximum group utility, individual regret, and compromise balance. The top-ranked three proposals under all VIKOR indices were consistent. Results were presented to the fund's decision committee, and the process and feedback from committee members are documented. A reflective section discusses the gap between formal model output and final committee decisions.

title: Consistency Thresholds in AHP: An Empirical Examination Using Data from 210 Real Decision Problems
abstract: The widely applied consistency ratio threshold of 0.10 in AHP, originally proposed by Thomas Saaty, has been criticised as insufficiently grounded in empirical evidence. This preprint reports an analysis of 210 real-world AHP applications collected from published studies and unpublished practitioner datasets covering public administration, healthcare, and infrastructure planning in South-East Europe, gathered between 2015 and 2024. For each dataset the consistency ratio, matrix order, and decision domain were recorded, and the relationship between consistency ratio and rank stability was assessed through a rank-order perturbation test. Results show that matrices with consistency ratios between 0.10 and 0.15 produced stable rankings (Spearman ρ > 0.90 after ±5% weight perturbation) in 73% of cases, suggesting the conventional threshold may be overly strict for certain matrix sizes and application domains. A domain-specific and matrix-order-adjusted threshold table is proposed as a working reference for practitioners. Full dataset available as supplementary material.

title: Bayesian estimation of the Bühlmann credibility factor under sparse claim records
abstract: Classical Bühlmann credibility assumes sufficient within-risk observations to reliably estimate the within-risk variance. When individual risk histories contain fewer than five annual observations—common in industrial liability and agricultural lines—the naive credibility weight is severely biased. This paper reformulates the Bühlmann parameter estimation problem as a hierarchical Bayesian model with weakly informative priors on the between- and within-risk variance components. Using a synthetic portfolio of 120 risks with histories of one to four years, generated from a shifted log-normal collective, we show that the posterior mean credibility factor reduces mean squared prediction error by 18–31 percent relative to the empirical Bühlmann estimate across three prior specifications. A leave-one-risk-out validation on a real agricultural hail portfolio from a regional insurer confirms a 22 percent improvement in out-of-sample squared loss. Computational implementation relies on Hamiltonian Monte Carlo via Stan.

title: Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of operational risk losses
abstract: The peaks-over-threshold (POT) method fits a generalised Pareto distribution (GPD) to exceedances above a chosen threshold. In operational risk datasets the effective sample above any reasonable threshold is small—often 30 to 80 events in a ten-year window—making threshold choice critical. We compare four automated threshold selection rules (mean residual life plot heuristic, Wadsworth's spacings estimator, the Northrop–Coleman profile likelihood, and a Bayes factor approach) on 16 publicly available operational loss event collections and six simulated GPD samples with shape parameters ranging from 0.1 to 0.7. The Bayes factor approach and the Northrop–Coleman rule give the lowest bias in tail quantile estimation when the true shape exceeds 0.3. For lighter tails the spacings estimator is competitive. We provide an open R implementation of all four methods.

title: Posterior predictive distributions for aggregate annual loss with few historical years
abstract: Many small insurance portfolios and corporate self-insurance programmes have at most three to seven years of aggregate annual loss experience, rendering frequentist collective risk model fitting unreliable. We construct a fully Bayesian collective risk model in which claim frequency follows a negative binomial and severity follows a log-normal, with conjugate-like prior elicitation guided by industry benchmark data from reinsurance market surveys. Posterior predictive distributions for next-year aggregate loss are derived by Markov chain Monte Carlo for three case studies: a Serbian municipal fleet programme, a regional hospital professional liability programme, and a crop hail programme in Vojvodina. Value-at-risk at the 99th percentile is estimated with credible intervals. Coverage probability of 95 percent posterior predictive intervals is assessed via a simulation study with 500 synthetic portfolios, yielding empirical coverage of 93.1 to 94.8 percent.

title: A credibility-weighted extreme-value estimator for heterogeneous risk groups
abstract: When an insurer groups risks by a covariate (e.g., region or industry class) and each group has a small extreme-loss history, neither a fully pooled GPD fit nor a group-specific fit is satisfactory. We propose a two-stage estimator in which group-level GPD shape parameters are shrunk toward a common mean via empirical Bayes, borrowing the formal structure of Bühlmann–Straub credibility. The shrinkage intensity is estimated by method of moments from the cross-sectional dispersion of group shape estimates. In a Monte Carlo study with 20 groups of 15 to 50 tail observations each, the credibility-weighted estimator reduces root mean squared error of 99.5th-percentile quantile estimates by 14 to 28 percent compared to separate group fits, across shape parameter values of 0.0, 0.2, and 0.4. An application to liability loss triangles from five Central European markets is presented.

title: Ruin probability approximations for compound Poisson risk processes with Pareto claim severities under small portfolio assumptions
abstract: Classical Cramér–Lundberg ruin probability bounds assume exponential or at most phase-type claim severity distributions. For heavy-tailed Pareto severities with shape parameter below 2, the classical adjustment coefficient does not exist. We examine three approximation approaches—the Pollaczek–Khinchine formula truncated to a finite number of convolutions, a saddlepoint approximation adapted for heavy tails, and a simulation-based estimator with importance sampling—applied to synthetic portfolios of 200 to 1000 annual claims. Relative errors against exact ruin probabilities (available for Pareto via integral equations) are reported for initial surpluses corresponding to 50th, 80th, and 95th percentile reserve levels. The saddlepoint approach performs well for shape parameters above 1.5; below 1.5 the simulation estimator is preferred. Results are relevant for capital adequacy assessment of small non-life insurers.

title: Bayesian updating of catastrophe loss models using sequential Monte Carlo
abstract: Catastrophe risk models for pricing and reserving are typically calibrated on datasets that are augmented by a new large event every several years. Re-running full MCMC after each such update is computationally costly. We adapt a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to propagate posterior distributions over GPD parameters as new catastrophe event observations arrive. Tempering schedules and resampling strategies are tuned for the low-event-count regime typical of natural catastrophe lines: 8 to 30 historical events. We apply the SMC scheme to a stylised hailstorm loss series for the Pannonian Plain region, simulating sequential arrival of one to three new events. Posterior contraction and shifts in 99th-percentile return-level estimates are documented. Computation time is compared with fresh MCMC runs. The approach is implemented in Stan with custom R wrappers.

title: Finite-sample performance of credibility-adjusted tail quantile estimators: a simulation study with implications for agricultural insurance
abstract: Agricultural insurance portfolios in South-East Europe frequently span fewer than fifteen seasons per region, making individual-region tail quantile estimation unreliable. We design a factorial simulation study varying four factors: true GPD shape (0.1, 0.3, 0.5), number of regions (5, 10, 20), observations per region (8, 15, 25), and strength of between-region heterogeneity (low, medium, high). Three credibility-adjusted estimators—empirical Bayes shrinkage on the shape parameter, full hierarchical Bayes, and a simple equal-weight pooled estimator—are compared against individual-region MLE on root mean squared error of the 99th-percentile quantile. Hierarchical Bayes is best in 74 percent of the 108 simulation cells; the gap over empirical Bayes shrinkage is modest (median 4 percent RMSE reduction). Both dominate MLE when within-region sample size is below 15. A brief application to grape hail losses in three Vojvodina districts is included.

title: Polifenolni profil i antioksidativna aktivnost ekstrakata nadzemnih delova vrste Centaurea derventana Vis. & Pančić
abstract: U ovom radu ispitivan je hemijski sastav metanolnih ekstrakata nadzemnih delova biljke Centaurea derventana, endemske vrste zabilježene na Fruškoj gori i pojedinim lokalitetima u Bosni i Hercegovini. Ekstrakcija je vršena maceracijom u 70% metanolu, a polifenolni profil određen je primenom HPLC-DAD metode uz identifikaciju jedanaest fenolnih jedinjenja, uključujući luteolin-7-O-glukozid, apigenin, hlorogenu kiselinu i kaftarnu kiselinu. Ukupni sadržaj polifenola iznosio je 42,3 ± 1,8 mg GAE/g suvog ekstrakta. Antioksidativna aktivnost procenjena je DPPH, ABTS i FRAP metodama. IC50 vrednost za DPPH test iznosila je 18,4 µg/mL, što je statistički značajno niže od vrednosti zabeleženih za ekstrakte srodnih vrsta iz iste sekcije. Rezultati ukazuju da je luteolin-7-O-glukozid dominantni nosač antioksidativnog potencijala ispitivanog ekstrakta, što je potvrđeno korelacionom analizom (r = 0,91, p < 0,01).

title: Optimizacija metode ekstrakcije flavonoida iz suve droge Hypericum rumeliacum Boiss. primenom metodologije površine odziva
abstract: Rad opisuje optimizaciju ultrazvučne ekstrakcije flavonoida iz suve droge Hypericum rumeliacum Boiss., balkanske endemske vrste iz familije Hypericaceae, korišćenjem metodologije površine odziva (RSM) zasnovane na Box-Behnken dizajnu. Ispitivani parametri obuhvatali su koncentraciju etanola (40–80%), vreme ekstrakcije (10–40 min), temperaturu (30–60 °C) i odnos biljke i rastvarača (1:10–1:30, w/v). Optimalni uslovi utvrđeni su pri 65% etanolu, 35 min, 50 °C i odnosu 1:25, pri čemu je prinos ukupnih flavonoida iznosio 31,6 ± 0,9 mg QE/g suvog ostatka. HPLC-DAD analizom identifikovano je pet flavonolnih glikozida, od kojih je hiperozid bio dominantni konstituent (11,2 mg/g). Proverom prediktivnog modela (R² = 0,978) potvrđena je visoka podudarnost između predviđenih i eksperimentalnih vrednosti. Rezultati pružaju osnovu za standardizovanu pripremu ekstrakata ove vrste za dalja biološka ispitivanja.

title: Comparative DPPH and FRAP antioxidant screening of endemic Dianthus species from the Balkan Peninsula
abstract: Five Dianthus species endemic to the Balkan Peninsula — D. giganteus subsp. banaticus, D. petraeus, D. kitaibelii, D. nardiformis, and D. viscidus — were evaluated for total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), and antioxidant capacity using DPPH and FRAP assays. Plant material was collected from confirmed natural habitats in Serbia, Montenegro, and North Macedonia, and 70% methanol extracts were prepared by maceration. TPC values ranged from 18.9 to 61.4 mg GAE/g dry extract, with D. petraeus showing the highest polyphenol load. FRAP values varied from 84 to 312 µmol Fe²⁺/g. HPLC fingerprinting revealed that kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside and vitexin were present across all five species, while saponarin was detected exclusively in D. nardiformis. Hierarchical cluster analysis based on the polyphenol profiles grouped the five taxa into two chemically distinct clusters that partially reflect their taxonomic sections. These results provide a phytochemical basis for the further selection of target species for isolation studies.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Distributed Hash Table Overlay Networks for Peer-to-Peer Certificate Distribution
abstract: This paper evaluates three DHT-based overlay architectures—Chord, Kademlia, and Pastry—as substrates for distributing X.509 certificates in academic networks without a central certificate authority. Using a testbed of 120 emulated nodes deployed on a cluster at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, we measured lookup latency, certificate retrieval success rate under node churn rates of 5%, 15%, and 30%, and storage overhead. Kademlia achieved the lowest average lookup latency of 38 ms and maintained a retrieval success rate above 93% even at 30% churn, outperforming the other two architectures. Chord exhibited the highest overhead per retrieval due to finger table maintenance. The study provides a quantitative baseline for selecting overlay substrates in decentralised public-key infrastructures for educational institutions. Limitations include the emulated rather than real-network conditions and the restriction to symmetric churn patterns.

title: Federated Identity for Inter-University Single Sign-On: A Deployment Case Study Using Shibboleth
abstract: This work reports a multi-year deployment of a Shibboleth-based federated identity system across six universities in Serbia and two in Croatia, covering approximately 84,000 student and staff accounts. We document the configuration process, metadata exchange procedures, attribute release policies, and the recurring failure modes observed over 30 months of operation. The study recorded 1.4 million authentication events, of which 2.3% resulted in errors attributable to attribute mapping inconsistencies between identity providers. We propose and evaluate a lightweight attribute normalisation middleware layer that reduced cross-institution attribute errors by 71% in a six-month controlled trial. The paper also discusses governance challenges—particularly the absence of a formally recognised national federation operator in Serbia at the time of deployment—and draws comparisons with the established GÉANT framework in Western Europe.

title: Tamper-Evidence in Academic Transcript Records Using Merkle Tree Commitments on a Permissioned Blockchain
abstract: We describe and evaluate a scheme in which academic transcript records from a university student information system are hashed leaf-by-leaf into a Merkle tree whose root is periodically committed to a Hyperledger Fabric channel shared among registrar offices. The system does not store personal data on-chain; only cryptographic commitments are recorded. We implemented the scheme for one faculty with approximately 3,200 enrolled students and measured commitment latency, verification time, and storage growth over one academic year. Commitment rounds completed in under 4 seconds for batches of up to 500 records. Third-party verification of a single transcript required fetching a Merkle proof of average depth 12 and completed in under 200 ms. We discuss data minimisation compliance with the then-current national personal data protection framework and identify residual risks related to long-term hash function security.

title: Revocation Mechanisms for Blockchain-Anchored Educational Credentials: Trade-offs Between Privacy and Auditability
abstract: Credential revocation is a frequently underspecified component of blockchain-based diploma and transcript systems. This chapter surveys five revocation approaches—revocation lists, accumulator-based schemes, status registries on smart contracts, OCSP-like on-chain responders, and epoch-based key rotation—and analyses each against four criteria: computational cost, privacy exposure for the credential holder, auditability for relying parties, and compatibility with offline verification. We instantiate each approach in a prototype built on a permissioned Ethereum-compatible network and report benchmark results for issuance, revocation, and verification operations at scale (10,000 credentials). The accumulator-based approach offered the best privacy properties but imposed a 340 ms overhead per verification due to witness updates. The chapter concludes with guidance on selecting revocation strategies depending on whether the deployment prioritises holder privacy or institutional audit trails.

title: Decentralised Identifiers as Persistent Academic Person Identifiers: Protocol Design and Pilot Evaluation
abstract: Persistent identifiers for researchers and students are increasingly required by funding agencies and repositories, yet existing schemes such as ORCID rely on centralised registries. This paper proposes using W3C Decentralised Identifiers (DIDs) anchored to a consortium DLT operated by a group of regional universities as persistent academic person identifiers. We specify a DID method tailored to Serbian higher education governance structures, implement a resolver, and run a six-month pilot with 420 volunteer participants across three universities. We measured DID creation latency (mean 1.8 s), resolution latency (mean 0.6 s), and participant-reported usability via a 28-item questionnaire. Adoption barriers identified include inconsistent student IT literacy, lack of integration with existing student information systems, and absence of legal recognition for DID-based signatures under current Serbian e-document law. The paper proposes integration patterns for gradual adoption without replacing existing systems.

title: Zero-Knowledge Selective Disclosure for University Degree Verification Without Revealing Grade Details
abstract: When a graduate shares a diploma with an employer, they typically reveal more information than required—full transcripts including grades, dates, and internal codes. This paper implements a selective disclosure scheme using BBS+ signatures on a Hyperledger Aries-compatible stack, allowing a holder to prove possession of a valid degree credential from a named institution in a specified field without disclosing individual course grades or the diploma serial number. We conducted a functional evaluation with 18 employer organisations in the Vojvodina region acting as verifiers in structured role-play sessions. Verification transactions completed in an average of 1.1 s on Android smartphones. Employers reported that the scheme met their practical verification needs in 15 of 18 cases; three organisations required full transcript disclosure for regulated professions, pointing to a residual use case for full disclosure. Implementation artefacts are publicly available.

title: Interoperability of Verifiable Credential Formats Across European Educational Credential Frameworks: A Mapping Study
abstract: The European digital credential landscape comprises at least four partially competing formats: Europass Digital Credentials Infrastructure (EDCI) XML, W3C VC JSON-LD, Open Badges v3, and ELMO XML. This paper systematically maps the data models of these four formats against the European Qualifications Framework (EQF) attribute set, identifying 23 shared fields, 11 fields present in at least two but not all formats, and 9 fields unique to a single format. We developed a schema transformation pipeline tested on 1,200 real-anonymised Erasmus+ transcript records provided under a data sharing agreement with the University of Novi Sad International Relations Office. The pipeline achieved lossless transformation for 89% of records and partial loss (affecting non-mandatory fields) for the remaining 11%. We release the transformation rules as an open schema registry. The study informs standardisation discussions within the European Student Card Initiative.

title: Trust Registry Governance Models for Cross-Border Academic Credential Verification in the Western Balkans
abstract: A verifiable credential ecosystem requires not only technical infrastructure but also a governance model specifying which issuers are trusted and by whom. This paper analyses three governance models—centralised national authority, federated consortium, and decentralised web-of-trust—and evaluates their feasibility for a Western Balkans regional credential verification network spanning Serbia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. We conducted 34 semi-structured interviews with representatives of ministries of education, accreditation agencies, and university registrar offices across the four countries between October 2020 and March 2021. The federated consortium model was most frequently endorsed by participants (21 of 34) as compatible with existing institutional structures. We draft a reference governance framework specifying roles, liability allocation, and a dispute resolution procedure, and cross-reference it with the EU eIDAS 2.0 trust framework to assess future alignment.

title: Performance Characterisation of DIDComm v2 Messaging for High-Volume Academic Credential Issuance
abstract: DIDComm v2 is the messaging protocol underlying most Hyperledger Aries-compatible verifiable credential wallets, but its performance under load during bulk issuance—such as graduation season when thousands of diplomas are issued within days—has not been studied systematically. We deployed a test environment consisting of an institutional issuer agent, a mediator, and 500 simulated holder agents on a private cloud infrastructure and measured end-to-end issuance throughput, message delivery latency at the 50th and 99th percentiles, and failure rates under three mediator configurations. At peak load of 200 concurrent issuance sessions, median delivery latency was 820 ms, 99th-percentile latency was 4.3 s, and the failure rate was 0.8%. Replacing the default SQLite credential store with PostgreSQL reduced 99th-percentile latency by 38%. We provide configuration recommendations and identify a backpressure handling deficiency in the reference mediator implementation.

title: Alignment of Serbian Higher Education Credential Data Structures with the European Learning Model (ELM) 3.0
abstract: The European Learning Model 3.0 is the semantic backbone of the Europass Digital Credentials Infrastructure. This preprint reports on ongoing work to map the data fields used in Serbian university diplomas, supplements to diplomas, and transcripts—as specified by the national accreditation framework—onto ELM 3.0 ontology classes and properties. We reviewed diploma templates from 14 public universities and identified 47 distinct data elements across institutions, of which 39 map cleanly to ELM 3.0 terms, 5 require extension properties, and 3 have no direct equivalent in ELM 3.0. We propose three extension terms submitted to the relevant W3C community group for consideration. The mapping is encoded as a SHACL validation schema and tested against 200 anonymised diploma records. This work is being conducted in collaboration with the Commission for Accreditation and Quality Assurance of the Republic of Serbia.

title: Offline Verification of Verifiable Credentials in Low-Connectivity Environments: A Protocol for Border Crossing and Remote Institutional Settings
abstract: Standard verifiable credential verification assumes reliable internet access to resolve DIDs and check revocation registries. In practice, Serbian–Hungarian and Serbian–Romanian border crossings and remote branch campuses in Serbia frequently experience connectivity gaps of 30 seconds to several minutes. This paper specifies and evaluates an offline verification protocol in which a short-lived offline verification token—containing a locally cached DID document, a revocation status snapshot, and a bound credential hash—is embedded in the credential QR code at issuance time. Verifiers can complete verification without network access during the token validity window (configurable, default 72 hours). We evaluate the scheme against five adversary models and show that it is resistant to replay and token-forging attacks assuming SHA-3-256 collision resistance. A prototype was tested at two Serbian universities with 63 administrative staff serving as verifiers; 91% completed verification without errors after a 20-minute training session.
venue: Computers and Security

title: Recurrent Neural Network Regression for Continuous Lip Shape Parameter Prediction from Acoustic Features
abstract: We investigate the use of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to predict a set of 12 continuous lip shape parameters directly from mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) feature vectors extracted from an acoustic speech signal. Training data consisted of 3.5 hours of synchronized audio and facial motion-capture recordings from four Serbian speakers, totalling approximately 11,000 utterances. The LSTM model with two hidden layers of 256 units each outperformed a feed-forward baseline by 18% in root mean squared error on the test partition. Predicted parameter trajectories were smoother and required less post-processing compared to frame-by-frame regression. Qualitative evaluation by 22 participants rated the LSTM-generated animations significantly higher in lip-sync accuracy than the baseline. The model ran at sub-real-time latency of 34 ms per frame on a standard workstation GPU, suggesting feasibility for interactive applications.

title: Effects of three-year crop rotation sequences on soybean grain yield in northern Vojvodina
abstract: A three-year field experiment was established on chernozem soil at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station to evaluate the effect of five rotation sequences—maize–maize–soybean, wheat–maize–soybean, wheat–sunflower–soybean, rapeseed–maize–soybean, and continuous soybean—on soybean grain yield and yield components. Each rotation was replicated four times in a randomised complete block design. Grain yield was recorded across three consecutive growing seasons (2008–2010), with means ranging from 2.84 t/ha under continuous soybean to 3.61 t/ha following the wheat–maize sequence. Number of pods per plant and 100-seed weight were the yield components most strongly influenced by preceding crops. Soil mineral nitrogen content measured at sowing was positively correlated with yield (r = 0.71). The results indicate that including small-grain cereals as preceding crops provides a measurable yield advantage for soybean under Vojvodina conditions, and that continuous soybean cropping consistently depresses productivity even on fertile chernozem soils.

title: Weed community dynamics in sunflower under different tillage intensities over a six-year period
abstract: Weed species composition and abundance were assessed in sunflower crops grown under three tillage systems—conventional ploughing, minimum tillage, and no-till—at the Rimski Šančevi long-term trial over six growing seasons (2007–2012). Weed density and dry biomass were recorded at three phenological stages of sunflower. No-till plots accumulated a persistent seed bank of Chenopodium album, Amaranthus retroflexus, and Setaria viridis, reaching total weed densities 2.3–3.8 times higher than in ploughed plots by year four. Principal coordinate analysis separated the weed communities of no-till from those of conventional tillage after the third year. Sunflower yield loss attributable to weed competition, estimated by regression against weed biomass at the six-leaf stage, ranged from 4% under conventional tillage to 19% under no-till without additional herbicide inputs. Minimum tillage maintained intermediate weed pressure and yield loss. Findings suggest that no-till sunflower production in Vojvodina requires adjusted weed management strategies.

title: Rotation-induced changes in soybean nodulation and biological nitrogen fixation on Vojvodina chernozem
abstract: Biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) capacity of soybean was compared across five rotation sequences differing in the identity and frequency of preceding crops in a four-year field experiment. Nodule number, nodule dry mass, and acetylene reduction activity (ARA) were measured at the R2 growth stage. Soybean following wheat showed nodule dry masses 22% higher than soybean grown after maize, and ARA values were correspondingly elevated. Continuous soybean plots showed progressive reductions in nodule dry mass (−18% by year three) and ARA (−25% by year four) compared with values recorded in year one, suggesting an adverse effect of self-succession on Bradyrhizobium japonicum populations or root health. Grain nitrogen content and protein percentage were positively correlated with ARA (r = 0.68 and 0.61 respectively). The data support designing rotation sequences that maximise the temporal gap between successive soybean crops to maintain BNF efficiency without additional nitrogen fertilisation.

title: Long-term tillage effects on organic matter fractions and aggregate stability in chernozem soil of northern Serbia
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) fractions and water-stable aggregate stability were compared after 12 years of conventional ploughing, subsoil tillage, and no-till management in a maize–soybean–wheat rotation at two sites in northern Serbia. At 0–5 cm depth, no-till plots had 38% higher SOC and 47% greater macroaggregate stability (>250 µm) compared with conventionally ploughed plots, consistent with published meta-analyses. Below 20 cm depth, differences between treatments were negligible. Particulate organic matter (POM) fractions were particularly sensitive to tillage, with POM carbon 2.1 times higher under no-till at the surface. Despite surface enrichment, total profile SOC (0–40 cm) did not differ significantly among tillage systems, with values of 52.4, 51.1, and 50.8 Mg C/ha for no-till, subsoil tillage, and conventional tillage respectively. These results caution against overstating the carbon sequestration benefits of conservation tillage in deep, fertile chernozem profiles without whole-profile accounting.

title: Comparative performance of early- and late-maturing soybean groups across rotation and tillage combinations in Vojvodina
abstract: Eight soybean cultivars spanning maturity groups 0 and I were evaluated across factorial combinations of three preceding crops (winter wheat, maize, sunflower) and two tillage systems (conventional ploughing and no-till) over three growing seasons at Rimski Šančevi. Yield, days to maturity, plant height, and lodging score were recorded. Analysis of variance showed that the main effect of maturity group accounted for the largest proportion of yield variance (31%), followed by preceding crop (18%) and tillage (9%). The rotation × tillage interaction was not significant, but the cultivar × tillage interaction was significant (P < 0.05) in two of the three seasons, indicating that certain group-0 cultivars were relatively tolerant of no-till conditions. Late-maturing group-I cultivars produced higher mean yields under conventional tillage but were more penalised by the early autumn moisture deficits associated with no-till surface compaction. Results are used to guide cultivar placement recommendations for Vojvodina producers.

title: Sunflower Sclerotinia basal rot incidence as influenced by crop rotation interval in Vojvodina fields: a five-year survey
abstract: A field survey was conducted from 2015 to 2019 across 47 production fields in Vojvodina to quantify the relationship between the frequency of sunflower in the rotation and the incidence of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum basal rot. Field histories were reconstructed from farmer records for a minimum of seven preceding years. Fields with a rotation interval shorter than four years between sunflower crops showed significantly higher basal rot incidence (mean 11.3%) compared with fields with intervals of four or more years (mean 4.1%), controlling for hybrid, sowing date, and soil texture. Logistic regression confirmed rotation interval as the strongest predictor of disease incidence (odds ratio 0.61 per additional rotation year, 95% CI 0.49–0.76). Soil clay content was a secondary predictor, with heavier soils showing higher incidence at any given rotation interval. The results quantify the protective value of extended sunflower rotations in reducing sclerotinia pressure without fungicide applications.

title: Strip-till as an intermediate option between no-till and conventional ploughing for soybean in Vojvodina: a four-season assessment
abstract: Strip-till, in which only the seed row zone (approximately 30 cm width) is tilled while inter-row soil remains undisturbed, was compared with conventional ploughing and full-width no-till over four seasons in a maize–soybean rotation on chernozem at two locations. Soybean emergence rate, stand establishment, rooting depth, grain yield, and protein content were measured. Strip-till delivered soybean yields statistically equivalent to conventional tillage in three of four seasons (mean 3.49 vs. 3.53 t/ha) while significantly exceeding no-till yields (mean 3.18 t/ha). Soil moisture in the untilled inter-row zones under strip-till was 9–14% higher than under conventional tillage at mid-season, suggesting a moisture conservation benefit. Fuel consumption estimated from GPS-logged tractor passes was 34% lower under strip-till than under conventional tillage. Strip-till appears to offer a practicable compromise for Vojvodina producers seeking to reduce tillage intensity without incurring the yield penalties associated with full no-till.

title: Cover crop residue management before soybean sowing: effects on soil moisture, weed emergence, and early stand establishment
abstract: A two-year experiment tested the effects of four winter cover crop treatments—hairy vetch, winter rye, hairy vetch–winter rye mixture, and bare fallow control—on soil moisture at sowing, weed seedling density at the V2 soybean stage, and soybean early stand parameters (emergence %, plant height at V4, leaf area index at V6). Cover crop residues were terminated 14 days before soybean sowing using a roller-crimper. Hairy vetch residue retained 12% more soil water at 0–30 cm at sowing compared with bare fallow. Weed density at V2 was 61% lower in roller-crimped vetch plots than in fallow. Soybean emergence rate and early leaf area index were not significantly different between cover crop and fallow treatments, indicating that roller-crimped residue did not impede crop establishment at standard population densities. The results support the use of hairy vetch as a cover crop in conservation tillage soybean systems in Vojvodina to suppress weeds and conserve early-season moisture.

title: Rotation and tillage effects on sunflower seed quality: oil content, fatty acid profile, and tocopherol concentration
abstract: Sunflower seed from a factorial rotation × tillage field experiment conducted over five seasons was analysed for crude oil content, fatty acid composition (oleic, linoleic, palmitic, stearic), and total tocopherol concentration to determine whether agronomic management influences end-use quality beyond yield. Oil content ranged from 44.1% to 48.7% across treatments and was highest in plots with a four-year rotation interval and conventional tillage. Oleic acid proportion was primarily influenced by the thermal sum during seed filling (r = 0.77) and showed no significant main effect of rotation or tillage. Linoleic acid showed a weak negative correlation with preceding-crop nitrogen mineralisation potential. Total tocopherol concentration was 12% higher in no-till than in conventionally tilled plots (P < 0.05), a finding tentatively linked to mild oxidative stress responses associated with compaction-related oxygen limitation. Rotation and tillage effects on seed quality parameters were generally smaller in magnitude than the effects of seasonal temperature and radiation, and are unlikely to affect market classification.

title: Simulating long-term rotation effects on soybean and sunflower yield under projected climate scenarios for Vojvodina using the DSSAT crop model
abstract: The DSSAT CROPGRO-Soybean and OILCROP-SUN modules were calibrated and validated against 12 years of observed yield data from the Rimski Šančevi long-term rotation trial. Calibrated models were then used to simulate yield outcomes under two CMIP6 climate scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) for the periods 2031–2050 and 2051–2070. Under SSP2-4.5, mean simulated soybean yield declined by 6–11% relative to the 2000–2020 baseline across rotation treatments, driven primarily by increased heat stress during pod set. Under SSP5-8.5, simulated declines reached 17–24% by mid-century. The protective yield advantage of including a cereal preceding crop persisted under both scenarios and was proportionally larger under hotter, drier projections. For sunflower, simulated yields declined less steeply (3–9% under SSP2-4.5; 8–16% under SSP5-8.5), consistent with sunflower's greater heat tolerance. The simulations suggest that optimising rotation sequences can partially, but not fully, offset climate-induced yield losses anticipated in the region.

title: Phytase activity distribution across the barley grain during early germination: a layer-by-layer dissection approach
abstract: The spatial distribution of phytase activity within germinating barley grains was quantified using a layer-by-layer dissection protocol applied to grains at 0, 24, 48, 72, and 96 hours of controlled germination at 15 °C. Four anatomical zones were isolated per grain: pericarp–testa, aleurone, sub-aleurone endosperm, and central endosperm. Phytase activity was measured spectrophotometrically using p-nitrophenyl phosphate substrate in sodium acetate buffer (pH 5.0). At 72 h, the aleurone layer showed peak phytase activity of 412 ± 23 nkat g⁻¹ dry weight, approximately 6.8-fold higher than the central endosperm fraction. Activity in the pericarp–testa declined after 48 h while aleurone activity continued to rise through 96 h. Phytic acid content, measured by the Wade reagent method, fell by 54% in the aleurone fraction over the full germination period but only by 18% in the central endosperm. The data suggest that phytate hydrolysis is strongly localised in the aleurone during early germination and that milling practices targeting aleurone retention may substantially improve mineral bioavailability in malted cereal products.

title: Alpha- and beta-amylase activity gradients in malting rye: effect of steeping moisture on endosperm modification
abstract: This study compared alpha- and beta-amylase activity gradients in rye grains malted under two steeping moisture regimes (42% and 48% moisture content) over a six-day malting programme at 14 °C. Grains were sectioned into three transverse zones using cryostat microtomy and zones were extracted separately for enzyme assay. Alpha-amylase was quantified by the Ceralpha method (AACC 22-02) and beta-amylase by the Betamyl-3 assay. At 48% moisture, alpha-amylase in the sub-aleurone endosperm reached 58.4 ± 4.1 U g⁻¹ on day four, compared to 34.7 ± 3.6 U g⁻¹ at 42% moisture on the same day. Beta-amylase distribution was less steep, with a central-to-aleurone ratio remaining near 0.6 across both regimes. Starch damage assessed by Evans blue staining confirmed greater modification depth at 48% moisture. The results support higher steeping moisture for rye malt intended for flatbread fermentation applications, where endosperm-wide amylolytic capacity is required.

title: Protease activation and protein solubilisation in germinating barley: correlation with nitrogen soluble index and gluten-like protein fractions
abstract: Endoproteolytic and exoproteolytic enzyme activities were tracked in germinating two-row spring barley (cv. Kairos) over 0–120 hours at 16 °C. Grain cross-sections were separated into aleurone, inner endosperm, and embryo-scutellum fractions by hand dissection under magnification. Total protease activity was measured by azocasein digestion and free amino nitrogen was determined by the ninhydrin method. Endoprotease activity in the scutellum fraction reached a maximum of 88 nkat mg⁻¹ protein at 72 h before declining; aleurone protease activity peaked later, at 96 h, with 64 nkat mg⁻¹ protein. Nitrogen soluble index (NSI) of whole-grain extracts increased from 22% to 61% over 120 h. SDS-PAGE profiles showed progressive reduction in bands corresponding to hordein B and D fractions, while low-molecular-weight peptide bands intensified. These enzymatic shifts are discussed in relation to dough extensibility and flavour precursor formation in malt-type flatbread processes.

title: Sourdough fermentation of malted rye flour: tracking lactic acid bacteria populations alongside residual phytase and amylase activities
abstract: Sourdough fermented with a back-slopping protocol (10% inoculum, 28 °C, 20 h fermentation cycles) was produced from rye flour milled from laboratory-malted grain (72 h germination at 15 °C). Over five consecutive refreshment cycles, heterofermentative lactobacilli counts stabilised at approximately 8.2 × 10⁸ CFU g⁻¹. Residual phytase activity in the dough was measured at each cycle endpoint; activity declined from 186 nkat g⁻¹ on cycle one to 103 nkat g⁻¹ on cycle five, tracking the progressive acidification (final pH 3.8). Alpha-amylase activity remained above 12 U g⁻¹ through all cycles, sufficient to support fermentable sugar supply. Flatbreads baked at 230 °C showed phytate reduction of 72% relative to unmalted rye flour controls (p < 0.01). The study quantifies the progressive loss of germination-derived enzyme activity under sourdough acidity and provides practical targets for malt incorporation rates.

title: Histochemical mapping of amylase activity in barley aleurone sections using 4-methylumbelliferyl substrates
abstract: A fluorescence-based histochemical method was adapted for semi-quantitative spatial mapping of alpha-amylase activity directly on cryostat sections (20 µm) of germinating barley grains. 4-Methylumbelliferyl-α-D-maltopentaoside was applied as a fluorogenic substrate at pH 6.9 and sections were imaged by confocal fluorescence microscopy at 24, 48, and 72 h germination time points. Fluorescence intensity profiles were extracted along radial transects from pericarp to grain centre using image analysis. The method resolved activity gradients at subcellular resolution and confirmed that enzyme release from protein storage vacuoles in the aleurone begins at the grain crease side and progresses laterally. Quantitative comparison with biochemical extraction data from parallel grain batches showed correlation coefficients of 0.87–0.91 for alpha-amylase, validating the histochemical approach as a reliable screening tool. The technique requires no specialised embedding media and is compatible with standard cryostat sectioning protocols available in most cereal research laboratories.

title: Effect of kilning temperature on residual enzyme activities in rye malt: comparison of 65 °C, 75 °C, and 85 °C final kilning temperatures
abstract: Rye malt prepared by standardised germination (72 h, 15 °C) was kilned to final temperatures of 65, 75, and 85 °C using a laboratory kiln with programmable ramping. Residual phytase, alpha-amylase, beta-amylase, and total protease activities were quantified immediately after kilning and after 30 days of ambient storage. At 65 °C, phytase retained 68% of green-malt activity; this fell to 31% at 75 °C and 8% at 85 °C. Alpha-amylase was most heat-stable, retaining 74% even at 85 °C. During 30-day storage, phytase activity declined by a further 22–35% across all temperature treatments regardless of kilning intensity, while amylase losses were below 10%. These data indicate that rye malt for sourdough flatbread applications—where phytase retention is a priority—should not exceed a final kilning temperature of 70 °C, whereas malt intended primarily for amylolytic activity can tolerate conventional kilning temperatures.

title: Comparative enzyme activity profiles in six central European barley varieties under identical controlled malting conditions
abstract: Six spring barley varieties grown in the Vojvodina region (Pannonian Plains, Serbia) under uniform agronomic conditions in 2017 and 2018 were malted identically (soak 48 h at 13 °C; germination 96 h at 15 °C; kiln to 65 °C). Phytase, alpha-amylase, beta-amylase, and total endoprotease activities were measured in whole-grain flour and in separated aleurone and endosperm fractions. Significant variety × fraction interactions were found for phytase (p < 0.001) and endoprotease (p = 0.004) activities, while amylase activities were less variety-dependent. Variety Ranko showed consistently highest phytase activity (497 nkat g⁻¹ aleurone fraction) while variety Galeb showed highest beta-amylase in the endosperm fraction (74 U g⁻¹). Thousand-kernel weight and protein content were measured as covariates; protein content explained 38% of variance in endoprotease activity. The dataset provides a selection basis for flatbread malt production targeting either phytate reduction or fermentable sugar generation.

title: Spatial protease activity heterogeneity in germinating rye measured by micro-scale extraction from sequential cross-sectional slices
abstract: A micro-scale extraction protocol was developed to quantify protease activity in sequential 200-µm transverse slices across the rye grain, enabling construction of continuous enzyme activity profiles from pericarp to grain centre. Grains germinated for 48, 72, and 96 h at 15 °C were embedded in low-gelling-temperature agarose, sectioned with a vibratome, and individual slices extracted in 50 µL of acetate buffer. Total protease activity was assayed by fluorescence using BODIPY-FL-casein substrate. Activity profiles showed a bimodal distribution at 72 h, with peaks at the aleurone layer (38 µm from surface) and at the scutellum interface, separated by a relatively inactive central endosperm zone of approximately 400 µm. The bimodal pattern was more pronounced in rye than in barley under identical conditions, suggesting differential protease gene expression timing between species. Inter-grain variability within a batch was low (CV < 9%), validating the method for comparative studies.

title: Effect of germination temperature (10 °C vs. 18 °C) on the ratio of phytase to amylase activity in barley and rye: implications for single-grain malt design
abstract: Barley and rye were germinated at 10 °C and 18 °C over 120 h to determine whether temperature differentially affects the development of phytase versus amylolytic activity, with the aim of identifying conditions that maximise one activity relative to the other. Enzyme activities were quantified at 24 h intervals in whole-grain extracts using established spectrophotometric assays. In barley, germination at 10 °C produced a phytase-to-amylase activity ratio 1.8-fold higher than at 18 °C at the 72 h timepoint, while amylase activity itself was not significantly lower. In rye, the difference was smaller (1.3-fold). The data suggest that low-temperature germination preferentially promotes phytase expression relative to amylase in barley, potentially allowing a single-temperature malting programme to be tuned toward mineral bioavailability goals without sacrificing fermentable sugar generation beyond acceptable limits. Starch gelatinisation onset temperatures were unaffected by germination temperature.

title: Enzyme activity retention in commercially ground versus laboratory-milled malt flours: effect of milling intensity on aleurone particle integrity
abstract: Laboratory-malted barley (72 h, 15 °C, 65 °C kiln) was milled using three procedures: hammer mill (coarse, d₅₀ = 480 µm), roller mill (medium, d₅₀ = 210 µm), and planetary ball mill (fine, d₅₀ = 75 µm). Phytase, alpha-amylase, and endoprotease activities were measured in water-extractable and residual fractions immediately after milling and after 14-day storage at 20 °C and 60% RH. Hammer-milled flour retained the highest total phytase activity (98% relative to whole-grain extract) but showed the slowest in-dough extraction rate due to intact aleurone cell walls. Fine-milled flour extracted fastest in dough (90% of activity released within 30 min) but lost 28% of phytase activity to oxidative inactivation during 14-day storage. Particle size analysis confirmed that aleurone layer disruption increased with milling intensity. Practical recommendations for malt flour milling targeting sourdough applications are presented based on the trade-off between extraction kinetics and storage stability.
venue: Journal of Cereal Science

title: Quantifying the enzyme activity gradient in barley grains: methodological review and cross-laboratory comparison of five dissection and assay protocols
abstract: Spatial quantification of enzymatic activities in cereal grains depends heavily on methodological choices—tissue separation technique, buffer composition, extraction time, and assay temperature—yet no standardised protocol exists for the field. This book chapter reviews five published grain dissection and enzyme assay protocols applicable to phytase, amylase, and protease measurement in barley cross-sections. A cross-laboratory comparison exercise was conducted with three participating laboratories (Novi Sad, Brno, Galați) using split samples of the same malted barley lot. Intra-laboratory repeatability was high (CV < 8% for all three enzymes); inter-laboratory reproducibility was moderate for phytase (CV = 19%) and protease (CV = 24%) but high for alpha-amylase (CV = 11%). Sources of systematic variation are discussed, including tissue hydration state at dissection and temperature fluctuations during extraction. Recommended minimum reporting standards for enzyme gradient studies in cereal grains are proposed. The chapter is intended as a practical reference for research groups entering this measurement area.

title: Estimating the Effect of Residential PM2.5 Exposure on Incident Hypertension Using a Wind Direction Instrumental Variable in a Serbian Cohort
abstract: Long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is associated with cardiovascular disease, but confounding by socioeconomic status and lifestyle factors complicates causal interpretation in observational studies. This study applied an instrumental variable (IV) approach, using seasonal wind direction as an instrument for residential PM2.5 concentration, to a cohort of 4,812 adults recruited across four municipalities in Vojvodina between 2010 and 2018. PM2.5 measurements were obtained from a network of 14 monitoring stations and interpolated to residential addresses using ordinary kriging. The primary outcome was incident hypertension, defined by first recorded clinical diagnosis or antihypertensive prescription. Two-stage least squares estimation yielded an IV estimate of 3.1 mmHg increase in systolic blood pressure per 10 µg/m³ increase in annual mean PM2.5 (95% CI: 1.4–4.8), substantially larger than the OLS estimate of 1.7 mmHg, consistent with attenuation bias in naive regression. Instrument validity was assessed through first-stage F-statistics (F = 24.3) and falsification tests against non-pollution-sensitive outcomes. Findings suggest a stronger causal effect than previously estimated from unadjusted associations in this population.

title: Protocol-induced variation in UMAP embeddings of 10x Chromium and Smart-seq2 single-cell data
abstract: UMAP has replaced t-SNE as the default visualisation method in many scRNA-seq workflows, yet differences in library preparation protocol introduce technical variance that can distort embeddings and cluster assignments. This study generated matched single-cell transcriptomic profiles of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells using 10x Chromium 3′ and Smart-seq2 protocols, resulting in 8,400 and 1,200 cells respectively from the same donor pool. UMAP embeddings computed separately for each dataset were compared using Procrustes analysis and earth mover's distance applied to cluster centroid positions. Protocol-associated batch effects shifted monocyte and NK cell clusters most strongly, with mean centroid displacement of 2.1 UMAP units before batch correction. Three batch correction methods—Harmony, ComBat-seq, and MNN—were evaluated, with Harmony achieving the highest cell-type mixing score while preserving within-cluster variance. The study recommended protocol reporting as a mandatory metadata field in public repositories.

title: Collagen fibril orientation in sheep small-intestine casings as a function of anatomical segment and animal age
abstract: Cross-sections of ovine small intestines from three age groups (6–8 months, 12–18 months, 24–30 months) were examined by polarised-light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Fibril angle relative to the longitudinal axis was measured on 240 samples distributed across three intestinal segments. Fibril orientation became progressively more oblique with age, shifting from a mean angle of 18° ± 3° in lambs to 29° ± 5° in older animals. Tensile modulus in the circumferential direction increased from 1.4 MPa to 2.1 MPa across the same age range. The data indicate that sourcing casings from animals younger than 14 months yields more consistent mechanical behaviour and lower inter-unit variability in elongation-at-break, which is directly relevant to automated stuffing lines operating at constant fill pressure.

title: Effect of salt concentration during preservation on the breaking strength of hog middles
abstract: Hog middles were preserved in NaCl brines of 15%, 20%, and 25% concentration for periods of 7, 14, and 28 days at 4 °C. Mechanical testing was performed on a uniaxial tensile frame with a 50 N load cell at a crosshead speed of 50 mm/min. Breaking strength and elongation-at-break were recorded for 30 specimens per treatment combination. The 25% brine at 28 days produced the highest breaking strength (3.8 ± 0.4 N/mm²) but the lowest elongation-at-break (38% ± 6%), suggesting progressive collagen cross-link density increase. A 20% brine with a 14-day soaking period provided the best compromise between strength and extensibility for industrial use. Moisture content of casing walls decreased monotonically with brine concentration, from 68% to 54% dry-weight basis.

title: Water vapour permeability of natural sheep casings relative to commercial collagen casings under controlled humidity gradients
abstract: Water vapour transmission rates (WVTR) were measured for natural sheep casings and three commercial extruded collagen casings using a cup method at 25 °C across relative humidity differentials of 20–80%, 40–80%, and 60–80%. Natural casings showed WVTR values ranging from 420 to 680 g/m²·day depending on the humidity gradient, while collagen casings ranged from 310 to 540 g/m²·day under identical conditions. The higher permeability of natural casings was attributed to a less densely cross-linked collagen matrix confirmed by differential scanning calorimetry, which showed a denaturation peak at 62 °C for natural versus 71 °C for extruded product. These differences translate to measurable effects on drying rate during the first 12 hours of a standard fermented sausage process.

title: Dimensional calibration consistency in natural hog casings: statistical analysis of diameter variation along casing length
abstract: One hundred hog casing bundles from five Serbian slaughterhouses were purchased over a single production season. Each bundle was inflated with air at 6 kPa and photographed at 10 cm intervals along the full length; internal diameter was extracted from 3,200 measurement points per bundle using image analysis. Coefficient of variation (CV) for diameter within a single bundle ranged from 4.2% to 18.7%, with substantial inter-slaughterhouse differences. Slaughterhouses applying grading by gut length prior to packing showed mean within-bundle CV of 6.1%, compared to 13.4% for those applying no grading. The data support introducing a maximum CV threshold of 8% as a procurement specification for modern continuous stuffing equipment where casing stretch is not adjustable in real time.

title: Microstructural changes in ovine casing collagen after repeated freeze–thaw cycles
abstract: Ovine casings were subjected to one, three, five, and seven freeze–thaw cycles (−18 °C / +4 °C, 24 h each phase) and compared to fresh non-frozen controls. Scanning electron microscopy, hydroxyproline content assay, and uniaxial tensile tests were performed in triplicate for each cycle count. Hydroxyproline content did not change significantly up to five cycles (mean 68 mg/g dry mass), but SEM revealed progressive fibril bundling and void formation after three cycles. Breaking strength declined by 12% after five cycles and 28% after seven cycles relative to controls. Elongation-at-break was more sensitive, dropping 18% after three cycles. The results suggest that a maximum of three freeze–thaw cycles can be tolerated without substantial mechanical degradation, provided freezing is rapid and storage temperature is stable.

title: Relationship between collagen solubility fractions and in-line bursting pressure in salted sheep casings
abstract: Collagen in salted sheep casings was fractionated into acid-soluble, pepsin-soluble, and insoluble fractions using sequential extraction. The insoluble fraction accounted for 78–91% of total collagen depending on sample origin. Bursting pressure was measured by inflating casing segments clamped in a water-filled pressure chamber; results ranged from 14 to 38 kPa across 80 samples. Multiple linear regression showed that the proportion of insoluble collagen was the single strongest predictor of bursting pressure (R² = 0.67, p < 0.001), while the acid-soluble fraction correlated negatively with bursting pressure (r = −0.54). The findings suggest that rapid collagen solubility profiling could serve as a non-destructive quality index for incoming casing batches in large-scale meat processing plants.

title: Influence of stuffing fill pressure on casing diameter uniformity and post-drying weight loss in wiener-type sausages
abstract: Wiener-type sausages were produced using sheep casings stuffed at three hydraulic fill pressures: 60, 90, and 120 kPa. Casing diameter was measured at stuffing, after clipping, and at 2 h intervals throughout a 12 h drying cycle at 55 °C and 35% relative humidity. Weight loss and diameter change were recorded for 120 sausages per pressure level. At 120 kPa, immediate post-stuffing diameter was 9.4% greater than nominal casing calibre, and weight loss after 12 h was 11.2%, compared to 8.7% at 60 kPa. Casing rupture rate was 4.2% at 120 kPa versus 0.3% at 60 kPa. A fill pressure of 80–90 kPa was identified as an optimum balancing diameter consistency (CV ≤ 5.5%) against rupture risk and acceptable weight loss.

title: Calibre mapping of natural sheep casings using automated image capture along inflated length: a comparison of four grading centres in the Western Balkans
abstract: An automated inline photographic system was constructed to capture casing diameter at 5 cm intervals during air inflation at constant 5 kPa pressure on a grading line. Four commercial casing grading centres in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia were visited, and 200 bundles per centre were measured, yielding 1,280,000 individual diameter readings. Centre-level mean diameters ranged from 18.3 to 21.6 mm and within-bundle CV ranged from 5.1 to 16.3%. One centre using laser-calibrated pre-sorting achieved substantially lower CV (mean 5.8%) and fewer splice points per metre (0.8 versus 2.1 at the least consistent centre). The automated system achieved throughput of 18 bundles per hour and agreed with manual calliper reference measurements to within ±0.3 mm (RMSE).

title: Collagen thermal stability in natural casings as influenced by species, casing type, and preservation method: a DSC study
abstract: Differential scanning calorimetry was used to determine denaturation onset temperature (T_onset), peak temperature (T_peak), and enthalpy (ΔH) of collagen in sheep small intestines, hog middles, hog rounds, and beef rounds preserved by salting, drying, and refrigeration without salt. A total of 144 specimens were analysed. Salted sheep casings showed the highest T_peak (65.3 ± 0.8 °C) and highest ΔH (14.2 ± 1.3 J/g), interpreted as greater cross-link density. Dried casings exhibited broader denaturation peaks (half-width 8–12 °C) compared to salted (4–7 °C), suggesting structural heterogeneity introduced by dehydration. Species differences were significant: bovine casings showed T_peak values 2–4 °C higher than porcine under the same preservation method. The data support using DSC as a routine quality control tool distinguishing species origin and preservation history.
