title: Diameter retention and surface crack formation in natural sheep casings during accelerated low-humidity drying of thin sausages
abstract: Thin lamb sausages (nominal diameter 22 mm) in sheep casings were dried at 55 °C under three relative humidity conditions: 25%, 35%, and 45%. Weight loss, casing diameter, and surface crack incidence were monitored over 18 hours in 120 sausages per humidity level. At 25% RH, weight loss reached 18.4% at 18 h, but surface cracking incidence was 31% of sausages, localised at calibre transitions identified during pre-drying calliper mapping. At 35% RH, cracking incidence dropped to 9% with a weight loss of 14.1%. Image analysis of crack morphology showed that crack initiation sites corresponded to zones where local casing wall thickness deviated by more than 15% from the segment mean. A thickness uniformity criterion is proposed as a basis for rejecting casing bundles prior to production of thin-format products.

title: Benchmarking collagen fibre crimp wavelength in natural versus extruded casings using confocal reflection microscopy and automated image analysis
abstract: Collagen fibre crimp wavelength and crimp amplitude were measured in natural sheep, hog, and bovine casings, and in three grades of commercial extruded collagen casing, using confocal reflection microscopy without staining. An automated ridge-detection algorithm processed 480 images (80 per casing type). Natural ovine casings showed mean crimp wavelengths of 28 ± 5 µm, natural bovine 41 ± 7 µm, and extruded collagen casings 12 ± 3 µm. The shorter crimp wavelength in extruded casings correlated with a steeper initial slope in the tensile stress–strain curve (toe region), consistent with earlier fibre recruitment. Longer crimp wavelengths in natural casings corresponded to a more extended toe region and therefore a softer initial mechanical response, which is favourable for conforming to product shape variation during stuffing. The image analysis pipeline achieved intra-operator repeatability of CV < 4%.

title: Scale-up of Supercritical CO₂ Extraction from 100 mL to 5 L: Maintaining Carotenoid Yield and Selectivity in Tomato Pomace Processing
abstract: A scale-up study was carried out transferring an optimised supercritical CO₂ extraction of lycopene and β-carotene from tomato pomace from a 100 mL laboratory vessel to a 5 L pilot vessel. Isobaric and isothermal conditions (420 bar, 65 °C, 5 vol% ethanol co-solvent) were maintained while CO₂ volumetric flow rate was scaled proportionally to vessel cross-section. Bed depth-to-diameter ratios (L/D) of 3, 5, and 8 were tested. At L/D = 5, lycopene yield was 8.3 mg/g dry pomace (96% of laboratory scale), and β-carotene yield was 1.4 mg/g (91% of laboratory scale). At L/D = 8, channelling caused yield reduction of 18%. Pressure drop across the bed was measured and correlated with a modified Ergun equation. Extract composition was characterised by LC-MS/MS, confirming that the all-trans/cis isomer ratio did not change significantly between scales (p > 0.05, Student's t-test). Energy consumption at pilot scale was 14% lower per kilogram of extract than at laboratory scale.

title: A Taxonomy of Structural Defects in Scientific Python Codebases
abstract: We present a structured taxonomy of defects observed in scientific Python code developed by domain scientists with limited software-engineering training. Starting from manual inspection of 1 200 scripts drawn from astrophysics, bioinformatics, and economics repositories on GitHub, two independent annotators labelled each defect with respect to its syntactic category, triggering condition, and observable consequence. Inter-annotator agreement reached Cohen's κ = 0.74. The resulting taxonomy contains 38 leaf categories grouped under six top-level classes: data-shape errors, silent numeric precision loss, incorrect statistical aggregation, broken file-path assumptions, hidden state in global variables, and missing random-seed control. Frequency analysis shows that data-shape errors account for 34 % of all identified defects and that silent precision-loss bugs are the hardest to detect through testing alone, being triggered only by specific input value ranges. The taxonomy is made available as a structured dataset to support tool evaluation. We also discuss how the taxonomy informed the design of two subsequent static analysis tools built in our group.

title: Static Detection of Leaky Pre-Processing Steps Between Training and Test Sets
abstract: Data leakage, where information from a test set influences a model's training phase, is a systematic error pattern in machine-learning pipelines that inflates reported accuracy. This paper presents LeakTrace, a static analysis tool for Python that models scikit-learn-style pipelines as annotated directed graphs in which nodes carry a taint attribute indicating whether data has passed through a fit or transform call. The taint propagation rules cover 41 transformer and estimator classes from scikit-learn 0.17. LeakTrace was evaluated on 2 300 Kaggle competition notebooks. It identified 317 notebooks with at least one leaky step, which corresponds to 13.8 % of the sample. The most common leak pattern was fitting a scaler on the concatenation of training and test features before splitting. For 70 of the flagged notebooks, re-running the pipeline on held-out data after manual repair produced accuracy drops between 2 % and 19 percentage points. The paper describes the graph construction algorithm, the taint rules, and the precision/recall trade-offs for three sensitivity configurations.

title: Automated Repair of Broken DataFrame Column References After Schema Changes
abstract: Machine-learning notebooks frequently break when upstream data sources are updated and column names or types change. We formulate this as a program repair problem: given a notebook that raises a KeyError or TypeError when run against a new schema, produce a minimal patch that restores correct execution. Our repair procedure, implemented in the tool SchemaFix, combines a column-reference extraction pass with a similarity-based name matching step using edit distance and token-level Jaccard similarity, followed by a constraint-based type coercion suggester. We generated a benchmark of 480 intentionally broken notebooks by applying realistic schema mutations—column renames, type promotions, and column deletions—to 120 original notebooks sourced from public repositories. SchemaFix produced fully executable repairs for 61 % of rename faults and 48 % of type-promotion faults, with an average patch size of 1.8 changed lines. The paper discusses failure cases, mostly involving derived column names computed at runtime, and proposes three heuristics to handle them.

title: Reproducibility Failures in Public Jupyter Notebooks: A Large-Scale Execution Study
abstract: We re-executed 9 712 Jupyter notebooks downloaded from GitHub in their stated dependency environment reconstructed from requirements files or conda environment specifications. Notebooks were executed cell by cell using nbconvert with a two-minute per-cell timeout. Only 38 % completed without any error. The most frequent failure modes were missing package imports (29 % of failures), broken relative file paths (22 %), and out-of-order cell execution assumptions (18 %). We define a reproducibility score that weights failures by the cell index at which they occur, penalising early failures more heavily, and report its distribution across twelve subject-area categories. Notebooks in the finance and economics categories had the lowest median score. We release the execution harness, the categorised failure log, and the reconstructed environments as an open dataset. This dataset has since been used as a benchmark in our subsequent repair tool evaluations. The study quantifies the scale of a known problem and provides concrete category-level breakdowns that inform where static analysis effort is best directed.

title: Type-Error Localisation in Pandas Method Chains Using Backwards Type Propagation
abstract: Method chains in the pandas library are a common idiom that allows concise data-transformation code but complicates error localisation because a TypeError raised by one method carries limited information about which prior transformation introduced the incompatible type. We present a backwards type propagation scheme that, given the output type constraint expected at the end of a chain and the sequence of method calls, computes the tightest input type precondition for each step. Implemented as a 2 800-line Python analyser named ChainTrace, the tool pinpoints the earliest method in a chain whose output type is inconsistent with its successor's required input. We evaluated ChainTrace on 680 chains extracted from our notebook corpus, seeding each with one randomly chosen type fault and measuring whether ChainTrace identified the correct method. Localisation accuracy was 78 % for chains of up to five methods and dropped to 61 % for chains of ten or more. The paper provides a formal semantics for fifteen pandas methods and discusses interaction with missing-value propagation.

title: Patch Generation for Silent Aggregation Errors in groupby–agg Pipelines
abstract: Silent aggregation errors occur when a pandas groupby–agg pipeline produces numerically plausible but semantically wrong results due to incorrect aggregation functions, wrong grouping keys, or unintended inclusion of NaN values in aggregates. We defined nine error patterns of this type through inspection of 3 000 data-science notebooks and implemented a fault-seeding framework that injects each pattern into correct pipelines. A repair engine, named AggFix, enumerates candidate repairs by substituting aggregation functions and grouping key subsets, ranks candidates by a score combining AST edit distance and statistical divergence between the original and repaired output distributions on a reference dataset, and returns the top-three suggestions. On a benchmark of 540 seeded pipelines, AggFix ranked the ground-truth repair first in 54 % of cases and in the top three in 71 % of cases. Mean repair time was 4.3 seconds. The paper discusses limitations when the reference dataset is small and provides an ablation study of the ranking components.

title: Cross-Notebook Data Dependency Analysis for Pipeline Decomposition
abstract: Large data-science projects often decompose computations across multiple notebooks that exchange data through shared files or databases, but the dependencies between these notebooks are rarely documented explicitly. We present a whole-project analysis, implemented in the tool NotebookMap, that reconstructs cross-notebook data-flow graphs by tracking file read and write operations at the level of variable-bound filenames. For ambiguous filename expressions, NotebookMap applies a conservative over-approximation. We applied NotebookMap to 80 multi-notebook projects on GitHub containing between 3 and 27 notebooks each. The tool correctly reconstructed 88 % of manually verified edges and detected 43 projects with circular dependencies that would prevent deterministic pipeline execution. NotebookMap also reports which notebooks are amenable to parallelisation given the dependency structure. A user study with 14 data-science practitioners showed that the generated dependency diagrams reduced the time to answer project comprehension questions by 38 % compared to manual inspection. The paper describes the file-reference extraction algorithm and the heuristics for resolving f-string filenames.

title: LLM-Assisted Repair of Data-Science Notebooks: Where Generative Suggestions Meet Static Verification
abstract: Large language models can suggest plausible-looking repairs to broken Python notebooks, but they frequently introduce new errors or fail to respect the surrounding dataflow context. We present a hybrid repair framework in which an LLM generates a ranked list of candidate patches for a failing cell and a lightweight static verifier, built on top of our earlier ChainTrace and LeakTrace analyses, filters and re-ranks candidates by checking type consistency, absence of new data-leakage paths, and preservation of the notebook dependency graph. We evaluated the framework on a benchmark of 310 notebooks with known ground-truth repairs across five fault categories. The hybrid system placed the correct repair in the top-one position for 61 % of faults, compared to 43 % for the LLM alone and 38 % for a purely search-based baseline. The verifier rejected on average 2.4 LLM-generated candidates per fault before accepting one. The paper analyses which fault categories benefit most from verification and identifies cases where LLM suggestions and static analysis are mutually complementary.

title: Comparison of support vector machines and convolutional neural networks for binary authentication of cold-pressed walnut oil from NIR spectra
abstract: This study compared support vector machine (SVM) classifiers and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) for authenticating cold-pressed walnut oil against blends containing 10% or more of refined corn oil, using NIR spectra of 144 samples. SVM models with radial basis function kernel were optimised by grid search over the C and gamma hyperparameters using nested cross-validation. The 1D-CNN was designed with two convolutional layers, global average pooling, and a single dense output layer, and was trained for 150 epochs with early stopping. On a held-out test set (n = 29), SVM achieved 93.1% accuracy and 1D-CNN achieved 91.4% accuracy; the difference was not statistically significant (McNemar test, p = 0.72). SVM training required substantially less computation time and produced more interpretable outputs through feature importance back-mapping. The study suggests that for datasets of this size, SVM remains a practical and competitive choice compared to deep learning approaches, and that NIR-based walnut oil authentication is technically feasible at adulteration levels relevant for commercial enforcement.

title: Kinematic parameter identification of a six-axis industrial robot using a ballbar instrument
abstract: This paper describes an identification procedure for the 24 Denavit–Hartenberg parameters of a six-axis articulated robot using circular test paths measured with a telescoping ballbar. A constrained nonlinear least-squares solver was applied to measurement sets recorded at three different tool orientations across the robot's reachable workspace. Experiments were conducted on a laboratory testbed at room temperature to isolate geometric errors from thermal contributions. The identified model reduced the mean positioning error from 1.47 mm to 0.18 mm over a 500-point validation set distributed across the full workspace envelope. Residual errors were attributed primarily to joint compliance and backlash, which are not captured by the rigid-body kinematic model. The study establishes a baseline calibration methodology that subsequent work extends to thermal and load-dependent conditions. Repeatability of the identification procedure across five successive calibration runs was within 0.03 mm, confirming numerical stability of the approach.

title: Thermal field characterisation of a servo-driven robot joint during continuous duty cycle operation
abstract: Thermal gradients in servo motors and gear units of industrial robot joints cause dimensional expansion that shifts joint zero positions and link lengths over time. This study characterises the transient and steady-state thermal fields of a single revolute joint assembly instrumented with 18 PT100 resistance temperature detectors mounted at locations identified by a prior finite-element sensitivity analysis. A FLIR infrared camera provided surface temperature maps for validation. Continuous duty cycles of 60, 120, and 180 minutes at 50% and 100% rated torque were examined. Temperature rise at the motor housing reached 38°C after 90 minutes at full torque, while the output flange of the harmonic drive rose by 22°C over the same interval. The correlation between temperature sensor readings and measured joint angular offset, recorded simultaneously with an encoder and an external rotary interferometer, exceeded 0.94 for all test conditions. These correlations form the empirical basis for a regression-based thermal error model developed in follow-on work.

title: Regression-based thermal error model for positional compensation of an articulated robot arm
abstract: Building on experimentally determined temperature–error correlations, this work presents a multiple linear regression model that maps readings from a reduced set of six strategically placed temperature sensors to three-dimensional tool-centre-point displacement. Sensor positions were selected using a stepwise regression procedure that minimised the number of sensors while keeping the root-mean-square prediction error below 0.10 mm. Training data comprised 2,400 measurement epochs collected over 40 working cycles on a six-axis testbed robot; validation used an independent 800-epoch dataset recorded two weeks later. The final model achieved an RMS prediction error of 0.087 mm on the validation set, compared with a raw thermal drift of up to 0.61 mm in the absence of compensation. Real-time compensation was implemented in a soft PLC layer that updated joint offset tables at 1 Hz. The approach does not require a geometric re-identification pass and can therefore operate during production without interruption.

title: Load-dependent joint deflection and its contribution to end-effector positioning error in payload-carrying robots
abstract: Articulated robots operating near their rated payload exhibit elastic deflections at gear units and link structures that are not corrected by factory kinematic calibration. This paper quantifies the contribution of joint stiffness to end-effector positioning error using a quasi-static compliance model derived from torque measurements at each joint and deflection measurements obtained with a laser tracker. Tests were performed with payloads of 0, 5, 10, and 15 kg attached to the tool flange of a six-axis robot with a 20 kg rated capacity. At 15 kg, the peak TCP displacement attributable to compliance reached 0.54 mm, exceeding the thermal component measured under identical duty cycles. A joint stiffness matrix was identified by applying known external wrenches and measuring the resulting deflections. Superposition of kinematic, thermal, and compliance models reduced peak TCP error to 0.19 mm at full payload, a 65% improvement over thermal compensation alone.

title: In-process geometric recalibration using sparse laser tracker measurements integrated into robot controller feedback
abstract: Periodic offline calibration cannot track the gradual geometric drift that accumulates during a production shift due to thermal and mechanical causes. This study proposes an in-process recalibration scheme in which a fixed laser tracker continuously monitors a set of three reflector targets mounted on the robot link structure, providing position updates at 10 Hz. An extended Kalman filter fuses these measurements with joint encoder readings to produce online corrections to the kinematic parameter set. The filter was tuned on simulated data generated from the previously identified error model and validated over 14 production-shift-length trials of 8 hours each. Mean TCP error over the shift dropped from 0.47 mm without recalibration to 0.11 mm with the filter active. Computational load on the controller PC remained below 4% of one CPU core, making integration into existing robot controllers feasible. The scheme was tested with measurement dropout rates of up to 30% due to target occlusion with no degradation exceeding 0.04 mm.

title: Comparison of thermal error modelling approaches for robot arms: regression, neural networks, and physics-based simulation
abstract: Three classes of thermal error model—multiple linear regression (MLR), a feedforward neural network (FNN), and a reduced-order finite-element thermal model—are compared on identical training and test datasets collected from a six-axis robot operated over 60 duty cycles. The MLR model used six sensors and was trained on 3,000 epochs; the FNN had two hidden layers with 12 and 8 neurons; the FE model was parameterised by four temperature boundary conditions derived from sensor readings. On a 1,200-epoch test set, the FNN achieved an RMS TCP error of 0.071 mm, the physics-based model 0.083 mm, and the MLR model 0.092 mm. However, the FNN required a retraining interval of approximately 120 hours of operation to remain within specification as robot wear progressed, while the physics-based model remained stable over 400 hours without retraining. The study recommends the physics-based approach for long-horizon deployment and the FNN for short production campaigns with stable conditions.

title: Transferability of thermal error models between kinematically identical robots in the same production cell
abstract: Industrial production cells often contain multiple copies of the same robot model. Identifying a full thermal error model for each unit is time-consuming. This study investigates how much of the thermal error model identified on a source robot can be transferred to a target robot of the same model without re-identification. Four nominally identical six-axis robots from the same manufacturing batch were instrumented and characterised individually. The source model, transferred without modification, achieved an RMS TCP error of 0.19 mm on the three target robots, compared with 0.09 mm for individually identified models. A lightweight adaptation procedure requiring only 60 measurement epochs per robot reduced the transferred model error to 0.11 mm, retaining 78% of the accuracy benefit of full identification at roughly 10% of the measurement effort. The adaptation exploits the fact that inter-unit geometric variation is small while thermal expansion coefficients differ by up to 8% due to manufacturing tolerances in harmonic drive assemblies. The method is directly applicable to multi-robot welding and assembly lines.

title: Combining structured-light scanning and kinematic recalibration for volumetric accuracy verification of robot-based machining cells
abstract: Robot-based machining relies on positional accuracy exceeding what standard factory calibration provides, particularly for aluminium aerospace components where dimensional tolerances are below 0.2 mm. This preprint presents a workflow in which a structured-light scanner mounted on an external tripod measures the workpiece after each machining pass and feeds dimensional deviations back to the recalibration module to update joint offset corrections before the next pass. The scanner, a Fotomess SL-300 with a stated point accuracy of 0.05 mm, was used on aluminium test pieces with pocket features milled by a six-axis robot. Over 20 parts, the mean dimensional deviation from nominal was reduced from 0.31 mm with static calibration to 0.12 mm with closed-loop recalibration. Cycle time overhead introduced by the scanning step averaged 47 seconds per pass for the test geometry. The paper discusses conditions under which the overhead is acceptable and identifies fixture drift as the remaining dominant error source at 0.06 mm.

title: Identification of Nonlinear Rope-Tension Characteristics in Bridge Cranes Using Stepped-Sine Excitation
abstract: Rope tension in bridge cranes exhibits amplitude-dependent stiffness due to wire lay geometry and inter-strand friction. This paper applies a stepped-sine excitation protocol to characterise this nonlinearity on a full-scale 5-tonne bridge crane at a metal fabrication facility. Excitation frequencies are swept from 0.2 Hz to 4 Hz in 0.05 Hz steps at three payload levels (500 kg, 1 500 kg, and 3 000 kg). Tension is measured by a calibrated shackle-type load cell with 0.1% full-scale accuracy. Backbone curves extracted from the frequency responses show effective stiffness varying by 18% between low-amplitude (below 5 mm rope displacement) and high-amplitude (above 20 mm) regimes. A Duffing-type single-degree-of-freedom model is fitted via nonlinear least squares, achieving a relative fit error below 4% across all load levels. The identified parameters provide a physically interpretable basis for model updating in digital twin frameworks.

title: Effect of relative humidity cycling frequency on sucrose nucleation induction times in model confectionery films
abstract: Sucrose solutions of 65–75 Brix were subjected to square-wave humidity cycles at frequencies of 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 cycles per hour in a controlled climate chamber. Nucleation induction times were measured optically using a temperature-controlled stage microscope for at least 30 replicate droplets per condition. At 0.5 cycles per hour the mean induction time dropped to 38 ± 6 min, approximately half the value observed under static conditions at equivalent water activity. Cycle frequency above 1.0 per hour produced no further reduction, suggesting a saturation effect linked to diffusion-limited solute redistribution at the droplet periphery. Crystal number density at the end of each experiment correlated negatively with induction time (r = −0.87). The data are interpreted using classical nucleation theory with a time-averaged supersaturation term, and fitted parameters suggest an interfacial free energy of approximately 6.8 mJ m⁻² for sucrose in these films. The findings are directly relevant to the uncontrolled graining observed in high-humidity confectionery storage.

title: Seed crystal size distribution controls final crystal habit in fondant manufacture: a quantitative image analysis study
abstract: Three narrow seed fractions of sucrose (d50 = 12, 28, and 55 µm) were prepared by sieving and wet classification, and incorporated at 0.5% w/w into a supersaturated sucrose syrup (Brix 78, temperature 40 °C) under controlled paddle stirring. Crystal habit was assessed after 24 h by scanning electron microscopy and automated image analysis of at least 500 crystals per batch, characterising aspect ratio, elongation index, and volume-weighted mean size. The 12 µm seed fraction produced the most equidimensional crystals (mean aspect ratio 1.21 ± 0.08) with a narrow size distribution (coefficient of variation 18%), whereas the 55 µm fraction yielded elongated, irregular crystals (aspect ratio 1.68 ± 0.14, CV 34%). Rheological measurements showed that batches seeded with fine fractions had 22% lower yield stress in the final fondant mass. The results suggest that seed preparation at d50 below 20 µm is necessary to achieve the smooth mouthfeel target in commercial fondant.

title: Amorphous lactose crystallisation in skim milk powder under controlled humidity: effect of storage temperature between 20 and 45 °C
abstract: Spray-dried skim milk powder samples with residual moisture of 3.2 ± 0.1% were equilibrated to water activities of 0.33, 0.44, and 0.54 at temperatures of 20, 30, and 45 °C in sealed chambers for up to 60 days. Crystallinity was quantified by X-ray powder diffraction using an external standard method with microcrystalline cellulose. At aw 0.44 and 45 °C, crystallinity reached 62 ± 4% after 14 days, while the equivalent sample at 20 °C required 42 days to reach the same degree. The dominant polymorph identified was α-lactose monohydrate at lower temperatures, whereas a mixture of α-monohydrate and anhydrous β-lactose occurred above 38 °C. Differential scanning calorimetry glass transition temperatures decreased from 52 °C at aw 0.33 to 28 °C at aw 0.54, consistent with plasticisation-driven mobility. The data were fitted to a modified Avrami model, yielding Avrami exponents between 1.1 and 1.8, indicative of predominantly surface nucleation with diffusion-limited growth.

title: Role of minor impurities in delaying sucrose crystal growth: a comparative study of raffinose, invertase hydrolysis products, and betaine
abstract: The effect of three common impurity types on sucrose crystal growth rate was studied in a laboratory crystalliser at constant supersaturation (σ = 0.10) and temperature (40 °C). Raffinose at 0.05% w/w reduced the linear face growth rate of the {100} face by 41% relative to pure sucrose, consistent with step-pinning mechanisms. Betaine at the same concentration caused a 17% reduction, while glucose–fructose mixtures from invertase action at 0.1% combined equivalent caused a 29% reduction. Face-specific growth rates measured by in situ optical microscopy showed that the {110} face was proportionally less affected by raffinose than the {100} face, leading to a measurable change in final aspect ratio. Growth rate isotherms were fitted to a Cabrera–Vermilyea pinning model; effective impurity spacing at the step was estimated at 18–35 nm depending on impurity type. The results quantify the relative potency of process-derived impurities in industrial sugar crystallisation.

title: Dynamic vapour sorption as a tool for early detection of sucrose crystallisation onset in chocolate model systems
abstract: Model dark chocolate systems were prepared with cocoa butter content varied between 28 and 36% and with added sucrose at 47% w/w. Samples of 10–15 mg were subjected to step-change humidity programs (10 to 75% RH in 5% steps, 60 min per step) in a dynamic vapour sorption gravimetric analyser. Crystallisation onset was identified as a reproducible mass decrease following an uptake peak, occurring at critical RH values between 48 and 63% depending on fat content. The method detected crystallisation onset approximately 72 h earlier than conventional penetration hardness testing in storage trials. Powder X-ray diffraction performed immediately after DVS experiments confirmed crystallinity of 8–14% at the point of mass decrease. The paper includes a worked calibration procedure and discusses sources of artefact such as surface condensation and instrument baseline drift. The DVS-based onset criterion correlated well (r² = 0.91) with final crystallinity measured after 30 days of accelerated storage at 33% RH.

title: Polymorphic transformations of α- and β-lactose in infant formula powder during simulated transport conditions
abstract: Commercial infant formula powder was subjected to three simulated transport protocols: isothermal storage at 38 °C, 50% RH (Protocol A); diurnal temperature cycling between 20 and 45 °C at 45% RH (Protocol B); and a combined humidity–temperature cycling protocol (Protocol C) designed to mimic sea container transport in Mediterranean summer conditions. Samples were withdrawn at 0, 7, 14, and 28 days and analysed by X-ray powder diffraction with Rietveld refinement and by differential scanning calorimetry. Under Protocol C, the α-lactose monohydrate fraction increased from 12 ± 2% at day 0 to 34 ± 3% at day 28, while anhydrous β-lactose decreased correspondingly. Protocols A and B produced smaller but detectable changes. Particle morphology assessed by scanning electron microscopy showed surface roughening and emergence of tomahawk-shaped crystallites in Protocol C samples. Sensory reconstitution tests showed longer dispersion times (from 42 to 78 s) correlating with increased α-monohydrate content. The data support the need for tighter humidity control in cold-chain breaks.

title: Ground beetle assemblages along a tillage intensity gradient in Vojvodina croplands
abstract: Pitfall trap surveys were conducted at 18 sites across the Vojvodina plain during two growing seasons (2006–2007) to characterise Carabidae assemblages under three tillage regimes: conventional ploughing, reduced tillage, and no-till. A total of 4,312 individuals belonging to 61 species were collected. Species richness and Shannon diversity were significantly higher under no-till management, with a mean of 22 species per site compared to 14 under conventional tillage. Ordination by non-metric multidimensional scaling revealed that soil moisture and bare ground coverage explained 38% of community variance. Dominant species shifted from large-bodied Carabus granulatus morphospecies equivalents under reduced tillage to smaller, seed-feeding Amara spp. equivalents under ploughed plots. Results support the use of ground beetles as rapid-assessment indicators of tillage disturbance in Pannonian arable systems and establish a baseline species list for the region.

title: A digitised reference collection of Pannonian Coleoptera: design, metadata standards, and first-release statistics
abstract: The paper describes the construction of a digitised image reference collection for Central European and Pannonian Coleoptera, assembled from museum holdings and field-collected material over three years. The first release comprises 8,740 specimen images representing 412 species from 23 families, each associated with georeferenced occurrence data, collection date, sex, and body-length measurement. Images were captured under standardised lighting conditions with a fixed macro-photography rig. Metadata were structured following Darwin Core standards with extensions for imaging parameters. The collection is hosted on an open-access institutional repository and cross-linked with the Global Biodiversity Information Facility aggregator. Quality-control procedures including duplicate detection, taxon-name reconciliation against the Catalogue of Life, and image resolution checks are described. The dataset is intended to support supervised machine learning experiments for automated species identification.

title: Convolutional neural network classification of ground beetle images: effects of training set size and taxonomic resolution
abstract: A convolutional neural network (VGG-16 architecture, transfer-learning from ImageNet weights) was trained to classify dorsal habitus photographs of Carabidae at three taxonomic levels: tribe, genus, and species. Training sets of 200, 500, 1,000, and 2,000 images per class were compared using five-fold cross-validation. At species level with 62 classes, top-1 accuracy reached 81.4% with 2,000 images per class but fell to 59.3% with 200 images, indicating strong dependence on training set size for morphologically similar groups. Genus-level classification achieved 91.7% top-1 accuracy with 500 images. Misclassification was concentrated in three species pairs with overlapping wing-pattern phenotypes. Grad-CAM visualisations confirmed that the network attended predominantly to elytral sculpturing and pronotal width, aligning with expert diagnostic regions. The study establishes minimum data requirements for reliable automated identification of Pannonian beetles.

title: Automated measurement of elytra shape from museum specimen images using active contour segmentation
abstract: A semi-automated pipeline was developed to extract elytral outline coordinates from flat-pinned beetle specimens photographed against standardised backgrounds. Active contour (snake) algorithms initialised by a coarse bounding-box detector were used to segment 3,800 specimens belonging to 95 Carabidae species from the reference collection established in 2014. Mean segmentation error relative to manual landmarks was 0.31 mm, acceptable for species-level morphometric work. Processing speed averaged 4.2 seconds per image on a standard workstation, compared with 8 minutes per specimen for fully manual digitisation. The pipeline failed on approximately 3.7% of images where specimen colour closely matched the background or where legs obscured elytral margins; flagging rules for manual review are described. Extracted outlines were subjected to elliptic Fourier descriptors and hierarchical clustering, recovering groupings broadly concordant with published tribal classifications.

title: Long-term shifts in carabid species composition in Pannonian steppe fragments: resurvey after 25 years
abstract: Twelve loess steppe remnants in Vojvodina originally surveyed in the early 1990s were resampled using standardised pitfall trapping in 2018 and 2019 to detect community change over approximately 25 years. A total of 6,841 individuals from 78 species were captured in the resurvey, compared with 71 species in historical records. Species occupancy modelling estimated four local extinctions and eleven colonisations at the site level. Thermophilous open-habitat specialists showed net range expansion while hygrophilous and forest-edge species declined. Community temperature index increased by a mean of 0.43°C equivalent units across sites. Fragment area and connectivity to other steppe patches were the strongest predictors of species retention. A subset of 22 species recorded in historical data could not be re-detected, though detection probability estimates suggest some may be present at low densities below trap threshold.

title: Semi-supervised learning for expanding labelled training data in taxonomically depauperate insect groups
abstract: Labelled image data are sparse for many taxonomic groups outside a few well-studied families. A semi-supervised learning framework combining a small labelled seed set with large unlabelled image pools was evaluated on three Pannonian insect orders: Dermaptera (8 species, 340 labelled images), Raphidioptera (5 species, 190 images), and Neuroptera (14 species, 520 images). Pseudo-labelling with confidence thresholds of 0.80, 0.85, and 0.90 was applied iteratively across three retraining cycles. Compared to a supervised baseline trained on labelled data alone, the semi-supervised models improved mean species-level F1 scores by 0.11, 0.09, and 0.14 respectively after two iterations at the 0.85 threshold. Gains were largest for species with distinct wing venation patterns and smallest for taxa where unlabelled images disproportionately represented common congeners. The framework is portable to other under-resourced regional faunas where expert annotation capacity is limited.
venue: Methods in Ecological and Evolutionary Computation

title: Phenological mismatch under recent warming: activity windows of carabid beetles and their avian predators in Vojvodina
abstract: Daily carabid activity data from image-trap time series at eight Vojvodina arable sites (2016–2022) were combined with breeding-bird census records from the same sites to test for phenological alignment between ground beetle peak activity and chick-rearing periods of three ground-foraging passerine species. Mean carabid spring emergence advanced by 4.2 days per decade over the study period, estimated from sigmoid curve fitting to cumulative seasonal activity curves. Mean chick-rearing onset advanced by 2.1 days per decade, yielding a divergence trend of approximately two days per decade. Logistic regression showed that years with above-average April temperatures produced the largest divergence values. Dietary analysis of nest-camera footage confirmed that carabids constituted 18–34% of chick provisioning events by biomass. The dataset is too short to draw strong conclusions about demographic consequences, but the directional mismatch warrants continued monitoring.

title: Acoustic emission response of glass-fibre/foam sandwich beams subjected to three-point bending
abstract: Sandwich beams consisting of woven glass-fibre/epoxy face sheets bonded to a closed-cell PVC foam core were tested in three-point bending at a crosshead speed of 2 mm/min. A two-channel AE system recorded hits continuously from loading onset to final fracture. Peak amplitude, rise time, and energy were logged at a sampling rate of 1 MHz. Three statistically separable amplitude clusters (40–55 dB, 56–70 dB, 71–95 dB) were identified using k-means clustering and associated with matrix micro-cracking, face-sheet delamination, and core shear fracture respectively, based on post-mortem SEM images. The cumulative AE energy curve showed a distinct inflection point at 62–68% of failure load, corresponding to first visible core crack. Load-displacement curves and AE event rates were found to be closely correlated (R² = 0.91). Results establish amplitude-domain thresholds usable in real-time monitoring without requiring prior wavelet decomposition.

title: Effect of impact velocity on AE hit rate and frequency content in carbon-fibre sandwich panels
abstract: Drop-weight impact tests were carried out on 300 × 300 mm carbon-fibre/epoxy–Nomex honeycomb panels at impact velocities of 1.5, 3.0, and 4.5 m/s, corresponding to impact energies of 5, 20, and 45 J. AE was recorded using four piezoelectric sensors in a planar array, allowing source location by arrival-time differences. Hit rate peaked within the first 2 ms of contact at 4.5 m/s and remained elevated for 15 ms, whereas the 5 J event produced a hit cluster confined to the first 4 ms. Peak frequency of recorded waveforms decreased from a median of 280 kHz at 5 J to 195 kHz at 45 J, suggesting a shift from matrix cracking to larger-scale delamination as the dominant mechanism. Source-location maps corresponded well with C-scan results obtained post-impact. The study provides a baseline frequency–energy relationship for honeycomb panels under controlled impact conditions.

title: Discrete wavelet transform decomposition of acoustic emission signals for delamination onset identification in GFRP sandwich panels
abstract: Acoustic emission waveforms recorded during low-velocity impact (10–40 J) on glass-fibre/epoxy–polyurethane foam sandwich panels were decomposed using a five-level discrete wavelet transform (DWT) with Daubechies-8 mother wavelet. Energy fractions in frequency sub-bands D1–D5 (12.5–400 kHz effective range) were computed for each waveform. A marked increase in D3 sub-band energy fraction (156–200 kHz) was observed at impact energies above 22 J and coincided spatially with delamination fronts mapped by ultrasonic C-scan. The ratio of D3 to D1 energy fractions, designated the Delamination Indicator (DI), showed a threshold transition from DI < 0.18 (no delamination) to DI > 0.31 (confirmed delamination) across 47 independent impact events. Receiver-operating-characteristic analysis gave an area under the curve of 0.94 for DI as a binary classifier. The approach requires no prior mechanical model and processes each waveform in under 3 ms on standard hardware.

title: Comparison of AE-based damage indicators in PVC-core and balsa-core sandwich panels under repeated low-velocity impacts
abstract: Two sandwich panel configurations—woven E-glass/epoxy face sheets with either PVC foam or end-grain balsa core, both 25 mm thick—were subjected to repeated impact sequences at 15 J with a 10 mm hemispherical impactor. Each specimen received up to ten successive impacts at the same site. AE cumulative energy, peak amplitude, and the wavelet-based Delamination Indicator (DI) were tracked across impact number. For PVC-core panels, cumulative AE energy grew approximately linearly with impact count (R² = 0.97), while balsa-core panels showed a step increase at the third impact coinciding with first core splitting observed in cross-sectional cuts. DI exceeded the 0.31 threshold at impact four for PVC and impact two for balsa panels. Residual dent depth, measured with a dial gauge, correlated more strongly with cumulative AE energy than with DI (Pearson r = 0.88 vs. 0.72). Results suggest that energy-based AE metrics are better suited for progressive damage tracking than frequency-ratio indicators under repeated impact.

title: Acoustic emission monitoring of sandwich panels with embedded fibre Bragg grating sensors: a comparative study
abstract: Sandwich panels (glass-fibre/epoxy, PVC core) instrumented with both piezoelectric AE sensors and embedded fibre Bragg grating (FBG) strain sensors were impacted at 10, 20, and 30 J. AE amplitude and frequency content were compared with dynamic strain pulses captured by the FBG network at 50 kHz interrogation rate. Both sensor types detected impact events reliably at all energies. AE source-location error was 4.1 mm on average (four-sensor array), while FBG-based location using wave arrival times gave 7.8 mm error. AE peak frequency distinguished matrix cracking from delamination in 83% of events classified post hoc by C-scan, whereas FBG strain amplitude alone provided no frequency discrimination. Combined use of both sensor types improved event classification accuracy to 91% in a leave-one-out cross-validation on 96 impact events. The study highlights complementary strengths of the two sensing modalities and their integration cost.

title: Influence of face-sheet layup sequence on acoustic emission signatures during low-velocity impact
abstract: Four layup sequences—[0/90]₂s, [±45]₂s, [0/±45/90]s, and quasi-isotropic [0/60/−60]s—were prepared as glass-fibre/epoxy face sheets on identical 20 mm PVC foam cores. Panels (250 × 250 mm) were impacted at 15 J and 30 J. AE hit counts, cumulative energy, and wavelet DI were recorded. The [±45]₂s configuration produced the highest cumulative AE energy at 15 J (1.8× the quasi-isotropic baseline) but showed the smallest C-scan damage area, indicating that fibre orientation governs wave propagation directionality rather than damage extent alone. Attenuation tests using pencil-lead breaks confirmed that AE wave speed varied from 2 850 m/s in the 0° direction to 2 210 m/s in the 45° direction for the [0/90]₂s layup, a difference large enough to introduce 0.4 mm location error if an isotropic speed is assumed. Anisotropy corrections improved source-location accuracy from 6.3 mm to 2.9 mm for the [±45]₂s panels.

title: Real-time delamination onset detection using a single-threshold wavelet energy criterion implemented on an embedded microcontroller
abstract: The wavelet-based Delamination Indicator developed in earlier work was re-implemented in C on a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller (168 MHz) to assess feasibility of on-board real-time classification. A five-level DWT with Daubechies-8 kernel was computed for each incoming AE waveform (1 024 samples at 2 MHz). Total processing latency per waveform was 1.6 ms, well below the 10 ms inter-impact interval at the highest tested impact rate (three events per second in a sequence test). The embedded classifier matched the offline MATLAB reference on 98.4% of 1 250 test waveforms from three panel types (glass-fibre/epoxy–PVC, carbon-fibre/epoxy–foam, glass-fibre/polypropylene–balsa). False-positive rate was 1.8% and false-negative rate was 2.3%. Power consumption during active classification was 220 mW, making the system candidate for battery-operated deployments. Firmware and calibration procedure are described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Temperature effects on acoustic emission signal attenuation and delamination detection threshold in sandwich panels between −20 °C and 60 °C
abstract: Panels of woven glass-fibre/epoxy face sheets bonded to PVC foam cores were conditioned at −20, 0, 23, and 60 °C in a climate chamber before impact testing at 20 J. Sensor-to-sensor attenuation of a pencil-lead-break reference signal increased from 8.5 dB/m at 23 °C to 12.7 dB/m at 60 °C and decreased to 6.1 dB/m at −20 °C, indicating temperature-dependent wave damping primarily in the polymer face sheet. The wavelet Delamination Indicator threshold of 0.31 established at room temperature remained valid at 0 °C but required upward adjustment to 0.36 at 60 °C and downward to 0.27 at −20 °C to maintain classification accuracy above 88%. A linear temperature-correction equation (three coefficients fitted per panel type) restored classification accuracy to 91–93% across all temperatures. These results are directly relevant to outdoor structural applications where diurnal temperature swings exceed 40 °C.

title: Acoustic emission monitoring during fatigue loading of repaired sandwich panels: patch adhesion and secondary delamination growth
abstract: Sandwich panels with pre-existing 30 J impact damage were repaired using a scarfed glass-fibre/epoxy patch bonded with a two-component structural adhesive, then subjected to tension-tension fatigue at R = 0.1 and maximum stress of 60% of the undamaged residual tensile strength. AE was recorded continuously throughout fatigue life. Two distinct emission phases were identified: an initial high-rate phase (cycles 1–500) attributed to adhesive micro-cracking at the patch boundary, and a lower-rate phase preceding final failure characterised by rising median peak frequency (from 145 to 210 kHz) and accelerating cumulative energy growth. Specimens that survived more than 10 000 cycles showed a secondary delamination growing at 0.12 mm per 1 000 cycles on average, tracked by periodic C-scan interruptions. AE-derived crack-growth estimates using the inter-event Poisson method agreed with C-scan measurements within 18% for 14 of 17 specimens. Two specimens failed prematurely due to repair patch edge peeling, which produced a distinctive burst-type AE signature not present in successful repairs.

title: Variational mode decomposition as an alternative to discrete wavelet transform for AE waveform analysis in composite sandwich panels
abstract: Variational mode decomposition (VMD) was applied to 840 AE waveforms collected during 10–40 J impacts on glass-fibre/epoxy–foam and carbon-fibre/epoxy–balsa panels and compared with the established five-level DWT approach. VMD was run with mode count K set to 4 and balancing parameter α = 2 000. The dominant mode frequency separated matrix-cracking events (median 245 kHz) from delamination events (median 168 kHz) with less inter-mode energy leakage than DWT in 78% of waveforms, as measured by a modal purity index. Classification of delamination versus no-delamination using the VMD-derived modal energy ratio achieved an F1 score of 0.93 compared with 0.89 for the DWT Delamination Indicator on the same dataset. Computational cost of VMD was 4.7× higher than DWT per waveform in a Python implementation, which constrains its use to offline or post-event analysis at present. VMD showed particular advantage for signals containing low-frequency core-crushing components superimposed on high-frequency face-sheet cracking.

title: Electrochemical behaviour of hot-dip galvanised steel in synthetic soil electrolyte at varying chloride concentrations
abstract: The corrosion behaviour of hot-dip galvanised steel was studied in a synthetic soil electrolyte prepared according to a standard recipe, with NaCl concentrations ranging from 0.01 to 0.5 mol/L. Potentiodynamic polarisation curves and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements were recorded at open-circuit potential after 1, 24, and 168 hours of immersion. Nyquist plots revealed a two-time-constant response at all chloride concentrations tested, attributed to a compact inner oxide layer and a porous outer zinc corrosion product layer. Increasing chloride content shifted the corrosion potential cathodically by up to 45 mV and raised the corrosion current density from 1.2 to 8.6 µA/cm². SEM-EDS analysis of the corroded surfaces confirmed formation of simonkolleite and zinc hydroxide as dominant corrosion products. The results provide baseline data for service-life estimation of galvanised earthing electrodes used in buried power infrastructure.

title: Impedance modelling of zinc dissolution in near-neutral sulphate-chloride solutions simulating waterlogged soil
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectra of pure zinc electrodes were collected over a frequency range of 100 kHz to 10 mHz in three synthetic electrolytes simulating waterlogged soils with sulphate-to-chloride molar ratios of 1:1, 5:1, and 10:1 at pH 6.8. Equivalent circuit fitting using a two-layer model with a constant phase element for the double layer gave chi-squared values below 5×10⁻⁴ for all conditions. The polarisation resistance Rp decreased from 1840 to 390 Ω·cm² as sulphate fraction increased, indicating accelerated dissolution under sulphate-dominated conditions. Inductive loops appearing below 1 Hz were attributed to adsorption of intermediate zinc hydroxide species. The study supports the use of impedance modelling over purely resistive approximations in soil corrosion assessments and provides fitted parameters that can be incorporated into service-life prediction models for buried zinc-coated structural elements.

title: Effect of soil organic matter content on the corrosion rate of carbon steel: a laboratory simulation study
abstract: Carbon steel coupons were exposed to synthetic electrolytes prepared with controlled additions of humic acid (0, 50, 200, and 500 mg/L) to reproduce the range of organic matter found in agricultural soils of the Vojvodina plain. Gravimetric mass loss after 30-day immersion, combined with potentiodynamic polarisation and linear polarisation resistance measurements recorded weekly, were used to track corrosion rate evolution. At 500 mg/L humic acid, the average corrosion rate measured gravimetrically was 0.18 mm/year, compared with 0.31 mm/year in the humic-acid-free electrolyte, indicating a mild inhibitive effect. Infrared spectroscopy of the corroded surfaces suggested preferential adsorption of humic acid carboxylate groups onto the steel surface, partially blocking active dissolution sites. The work offers guidance for corrosion allowance calculations on buried pipelines in organic-rich agricultural soils.

title: Phosphate conversion coating on carbon steel: formation kinetics and corrosion barrier properties in sulphate soil electrolyte
abstract: Zinc–manganese phosphate conversion coatings were deposited on carbon steel substrates from an acidic phosphating bath at temperatures of 50, 65, and 80 °C with immersion times between 2 and 20 minutes. Coating mass per unit area ranged from 4.8 to 18.2 g/m² depending on conditions; SEM imaging showed a characteristic hopeite crystal morphology with average crystal size decreasing from 22 to 9 µm as bath temperature increased. EIS measurements in 0.05 mol/L Na₂SO₄ demonstrated that coatings formed at 65 °C for 10 minutes provided the highest pore resistance (Rpore = 3.2 × 10⁴ Ω·cm²) after 24 hours of immersion. Salt spray testing (500 h) confirmed an approximately threefold reduction in blistering area relative to uncoated steel. The results identify optimal process parameters for phosphate pretreatment intended for pipeline fittings exposed to sulphate-rich soils.

title: Scanning Kelvin probe mapping of delamination fronts in epoxy-coated steel exposed to chloride soil electrolyte
abstract: Epoxy primer coatings of 40 µm dry film thickness were applied to sandblasted carbon steel panels and scribed with a 1 mm artificial defect. Panels were partially immersed in a 0.1 mol/L NaCl synthetic soil electrolyte, and the Volta potential distribution was mapped weekly by scanning Kelvin probe (SKP) over a 15 × 15 mm area centred on the defect. A cathodic delamination front advancing at an average rate of 0.18 mm/day was identified over a six-week observation period. The Volta potential in the delaminated zone dropped by approximately 280 mV relative to intact coating areas, consistent with oxygen-reduction-driven undercutting. EIS on companion samples without scribes confirmed gradual uptake of electrolyte into the coating, with the low-frequency impedance modulus declining from 2.1 × 10⁹ to 4.7 × 10⁷ Ω·cm² after 42 days. The SKP data are used to calibrate a diffusion-based delamination model.

title: Cerium-doped silane sol-gel coatings on aluminium alloy AA2024: inhibitor release and corrosion protection in aggressive chloride media
abstract: Hybrid organic–inorganic sol-gel coatings were prepared from 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane and tetraethoxysilane (molar ratio 3:1) with cerium nitrate added at 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 wt% as a corrosion inhibitor. Coatings were deposited on AA2024-T3 by dip coating and cured at 120 °C for 30 minutes, yielding dry film thicknesses of 3–5 µm. Accelerated release experiments showed that Ce³⁺ release rate followed a Fickian profile, with cumulative release reaching 42 µg/cm² after 72 hours in 0.05 mol/L NaCl. EIS measurements after 1, 3, and 7 days in 3.5 wt% NaCl indicated that coatings with 1.0 wt% Ce maintained a total impedance above 10⁷ Ω·cm² throughout the test period, whereas undoped coatings dropped below 10⁵ Ω·cm² after 48 hours. Neutral salt spray testing (168 h) showed no pitting on 1.0 wt% Ce samples, while pits of 0.3–0.8 mm diameter formed on undoped references.

title: Corrosion behaviour of copper grounding conductors in artificially prepared acid sulphate soils
abstract: Copper strip electrodes (99.9% purity, 2 cm²) were tested in three artificially prepared acid sulphate soil electrolytes with pH values of 3.1, 4.0, and 5.2 adjusted using H₂SO₄, reflecting conditions found in drained coastal and wetland soils. Potentiodynamic scans from −0.4 to +0.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl at 1 mV/s showed that corrosion potential shifted positively with pH decrease, and corrosion current density increased from 0.6 µA/cm² at pH 5.2 to 4.8 µA/cm² at pH 3.1. Chronoamperometric data collected at open-circuit over 30 days indicated formation of a mixed Cu₂O/CuSO₄·3Cu(OH)₂ product layer confirmed by XRD. The contact resistance of corroded copper-to-copper bolted joints increased by a factor of 3.2 at pH 3.1, with implications for the reliability of buried earthing systems in drained peat soils.

title: Long-term EIS monitoring of organic coating degradation on steel buried in sandy loam soil: a two-year field study
abstract: Carbon steel pipes coated with a commercial epoxy-polyamide system (nominal 120 µm DFT) were buried in sandy loam soil at a test site in the Vojvodina region. EIS measurements at open-circuit potential were taken using a portable instrument at 0, 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months. The coating capacitance, extracted from the high-frequency response, increased from 0.31 to 1.84 nF/cm² over two years, indicating progressive water uptake with a calculated volume fraction of absorbed water reaching 3.1% at 24 months using the Brasher–Kingsbury equation. The pore resistance declined from 4.5 × 10⁸ to 1.2 × 10⁶ Ω·cm² between months 12 and 18, coinciding with onset of visible underfilm corrosion on excavated reference specimens. Soil resistivity measured at the site ranged from 28 to 74 Ω·m depending on season, and a correlation between low soil resistivity periods and accelerated Rp decline was established. The dataset provides calibration points for coating degradation models used in pipeline integrity management.

title: Polypyrrole-modified zinc coatings electrodeposited from citrate bath: structure, adhesion, and corrosion performance in alkaline chloride electrolyte
abstract: Composite polypyrrole-zinc coatings were electrodeposited onto low-carbon steel substrates from a citrate-based electrolyte containing 0.1 mol/L ZnSO₄ and 0.05 mol/L pyrrole monomer. Deposition was carried out at current densities of 20, 40, and 60 mA/cm² at room temperature; at 40 mA/cm², the coating contained approximately 4.2 wt% polypyrrole as determined by infrared spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis. Cross-section SEM showed a compact, columnar grain structure with average thickness of 18 µm and no visible porosity at the substrate interface. Adhesion measured by the cross-hatch method yielded class 0 for all compositions. EIS in 0.5 mol/L NaCl (pH 9.0) after 96 hours gave total impedance values 2.4 times higher for the composite coating than for plain zinc deposited under identical conditions. Neutral salt spray tests (240 h) showed first rust appearance at 196 hours for the composite versus 112 hours for the zinc reference.

title: Influence of microstructure on the localised corrosion susceptibility of friction-stir-welded low-alloy steel in chloride-containing soil electrolyte
abstract: Friction-stir-welded joints in S355 low-alloy steel were characterised by EBSD, microhardness mapping, and potentiodynamic polarisation in 0.1 mol/L NaCl soil electrolyte. Three zones were identified: base metal (BM), thermomechanically affected zone (TMAZ), and nugget zone (NZ), with hardness values of 162, 195, and 218 HV respectively. Potentiodynamic scans showed that Ecorr was most negative in the TMAZ (−0.71 V vs. SCE) compared to BM (−0.62 V) and NZ (−0.65 V). Localised corrosion initiated preferentially at TMAZ grain boundaries as confirmed by optical microscopy after 72-hour immersion. EIS-derived Rp for TMAZ (820 Ω·cm²) was approximately 40% lower than for BM (1370 Ω·cm²). The findings suggest that weld qualification protocols for buried structural steel should include zone-resolved corrosion testing rather than bulk assessments of the welded coupon.

title: Waterborne polyurethane coatings loaded with zinc phosphate and calcium ion-exchange silica as dual-action inhibitor systems for corrosion protection of carbon steel in soil environments
abstract: Waterborne polyurethane (WPU) coatings were formulated with zinc phosphate (ZP) and calcium ion-exchange silica (CIS) as pigment inhibitors at total loadings of 5, 10, and 15 wt% in a 1:1 ZP:CIS mass ratio. Coatings were applied to carbon steel panels (60 µm DFT) and evaluated by EIS in 0.1 mol/L NaCl at 25 °C over 28 days. At 10 wt% total inhibitor content the coating maintained Rp above 10⁷ Ω·cm² throughout the test; higher loading (15 wt%) led to increased porosity and lower Rp after day 14. Release experiments in deionised water confirmed Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻ release at rates of 0.9 and 1.6 µg/(cm²·day) respectively. Scanning electron microscopy of artificially defected areas showed dense mixed hydroxide-phosphate deposits forming at the defect edges after 14 days, consistent with active barrier repair. The formulation at 10 wt% loading was identified as a candidate for pipeline girth weld coating applications.

title: Unsupervised Clustering of Player Session Logs for Identifying Atypical Gameplay Patterns
abstract: This paper examines the application of k-means and hierarchical agglomerative clustering to raw session logs collected from a mid-scale online role-playing game operated by a Serbian software studio. The dataset comprised approximately 1.2 million session records gathered over six months, each containing timestamped action events at a median resolution of 340 ms. Feature engineering focused on inter-event intervals, action-type frequency histograms, and session duration quartiles. Clustering configurations ranging from k=4 to k=20 were evaluated using the Davies–Bouldin index and silhouette scores. A configuration of k=9 yielded the most coherent separation, isolating three clusters with statistically elevated repetitive action rates and compressed inter-event intervals, consistent with macro-assisted or scripted play. Manual inspection of a 500-record sample from these clusters by domain experts confirmed atypical patterns in 87% of cases. The study establishes a baseline clustering pipeline suitable for downstream supervised labelling tasks and discusses the sensitivity of results to session length truncation strategies.

title: Behavioural Fingerprinting of Game Accounts Across Sessions Using Metric Learning
abstract: Account sharing and identity obfuscation complicate enforcement in competitive online games, where players may use multiple accounts or lend accounts to others to circumvent bans. This study frames cross-session behavioural fingerprinting as a metric learning problem. A Siamese network is trained on pairs of sessions from the same and different accounts to learn an embedding space in which intra-account distances are minimised and inter-account distances are maximised. Training data consisted of 320,000 session pairs derived from a server log archive covering 11,000 distinct accounts over 14 months. Input features include per-minute action-type histograms, movement statistics, and reaction time distributions. The network achieves an equal error rate of 6.1% on a held-out test set of account-pair verification tasks. A qualitative analysis identifies cases where legitimate account sharing causes false positives and discusses potential mitigations through temporal segmentation of account histories.

title: Anomaly Detection in Telemetry Streams: Methods and Applications in Interactive Software Systems
abstract: This book chapter surveys machine learning approaches to anomaly detection in high-frequency telemetry streams generated by interactive software systems, with a focus on game clients and simulation environments. The chapter covers statistical process control baselines, isolation forest variants, autoencoder-based reconstruction methods, and sequence models including RNNs and TCNs. For each method family, key assumptions, scalability properties, and sensitivity to concept drift are discussed. A unifying taxonomy of telemetry anomaly types is proposed, distinguishing between point anomalies, contextual anomalies, and collective anomalies in the specific context of action event logs. Practical considerations for real-world deployment, including labelling cost reduction through active learning and the handling of class imbalance, are addressed in the final sections. The chapter synthesises results from approximately 60 papers published between 2010 and 2021 and identifies open problems including cross-game generalisation and privacy-preserving telemetry analysis.

title: Concept Drift Detection in Player Behaviour Streams Using Adaptive Windowing
abstract: Player behaviour distributions in live online games shift over time due to meta-game evolution, patch updates, and seasonal events. Anomaly detectors trained on historical data degrade in precision as the underlying normal behaviour changes, a problem characterised here as concept drift in the telemetry domain. This paper evaluates three adaptive windowing strategies—ADWIN, Page–Hinkley test, and a sliding-window reconstruction loss monitor—for triggering model retraining in an online anomaly detection pipeline. Experiments are conducted on 18 months of telemetry data from a live game title, with ground-truth drift points identified from patch release dates and manual inspection of feature distribution shifts. ADWIN with a delta parameter of 0.002 achieves the best balance between false alarm rate (9%) and drift detection latency (median 4.1 days). The paper proposes a retraining scheduling protocol that reduces labelling overhead by approximately 35% compared to periodic fixed-interval retraining.

title: Federated Anomaly Detection Over Distributed Game Server Telemetry Without Raw Data Sharing
abstract: Game operators running distributed server infrastructure across jurisdictions face constraints on centralising raw telemetry due to data residency regulations. This paper implements a federated learning setup for anomaly detection where each game server node trains a local autoencoder on its own telemetry shard and contributes only model weight updates to a central aggregation server. FedAvg and FedProx aggregation strategies are compared across simulations of 4, 8, and 16 federated clients with heterogeneous session distributions. Using a held-out centralised evaluation set of 90,000 sessions, FedProx with a proximal term of μ=0.01 achieves an AUROC within 3.2 percentage points of a centralised baseline trained on all raw data. Communication overhead is measured over 50 aggregation rounds. The paper discusses the effect of statistical heterogeneity between server shards on model convergence and proposes a lightweight client-side drift signal to schedule selective participation in aggregation rounds.

title: A two-compartment population pharmacokinetic model for vancomycin in adult haemodialysis patients based on routine clinical data
abstract: Vancomycin dosing in haemodialysis patients is complicated by highly variable interdialytic clearance and residual renal function. This study developed a two-compartment population pharmacokinetic model using 312 trough and AUC-guided concentrations collected retrospectively from 78 adult patients receiving intermittent haemodialysis at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Data were analysed with NONMEM 7.4 using the FOCE-I estimation method. Dialysis clearance was modelled as a separate additive term to non-renal clearance, with dialyser membrane type (high-flux vs. low-flux) and session duration as covariates. The final model estimated a central volume of distribution of 38.1 L (RSE 8.4%), non-renal clearance of 1.2 L/h, and dialysis clearance of 3.6 L/h for high-flux membranes. Internal validation by visual predictive check and normalised prediction distribution errors demonstrated adequate predictive performance. Monte Carlo simulation of three dosing regimens indicated that post-dialysis redosing of 750 mg achieved AUC24 targets in 61% of virtual patients versus 38% with a fixed 500 mg regimen.

title: Bayesian maximum a posteriori estimation for vancomycin AUC monitoring: comparison of three prior population models in a Serbian cohort
abstract: Model-informed precision dosing of vancomycin increasingly relies on Bayesian estimation of the 24-hour AUC rather than trough concentration alone. However, the predictive accuracy of prior population PK models developed in Western European and North American cohorts when applied to Southeastern European patients is not well documented. We evaluated three published two-compartment priors using data from 106 adult general-ward patients treated at two hospitals in Novi Sad between 2019 and 2021. Predictive performance was assessed by mean prediction error (MPE) and root mean square error (RMSE) calculated against measured steady-state troughs (n = 247) and limited AUC estimates derived from two-sample draws. Prior A underestimated AUC by a mean of 12.3 mg·h/L (MPE −9.1%), while Prior C performed best with MPE of −2.8% and RMSE of 18.4 mg·h/L. Updating priors with locally collected data using an empirical Bayes step improved MPE to −1.1%. These findings support prospective Bayesian TDM implementation using locally calibrated models rather than direct adoption of externally derived priors.

title: Effect of residual renal function on tacrolimus dose requirements in kidney transplant recipients: a population PK analysis
abstract: Tacrolimus has a narrow therapeutic index and exhibits wide intraindividual and interindividual pharmacokinetic variability in renal transplant recipients, partly attributed to the progressive recovery of renal function post-transplantation. We analysed 1,840 whole-blood trough concentrations from 94 adult kidney transplant patients followed for 12 months post-transplant at a single centre in Novi Sad. A one-compartment model with first-order absorption was developed in Monolix 2021R1. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, CKD-EPI) at the time of sampling was identified as a statistically significant covariate on apparent oral clearance (CL/F), increasing CL/F by 0.31% per mL/min/1.73 m² unit increase in eGFR. CYP3A5*3 genotype explained an additional 34% of interindividual variability in CL/F. Simulations demonstrated that a CYP3A5 expressers group required a mean dose 1.7-fold higher than non-expressers to achieve equivalent 12-hour troughs of 8–12 ng/mL in the first month. The model provides a basis for proactive dose adjustment as renal function recovers.

title: A Bayesian dosing algorithm for levetiracetam in patients with stage 3–5 chronic kidney disease: development and preliminary prospective evaluation
abstract: Levetiracetam is renally excreted and requires dose adjustment in chronic kidney disease, yet formal PK-guided dosing in this population remains uncommon in clinical practice. We first built a population PK model from retrospective data (n = 61 patients, 183 plasma samples) using NONMEM, identifying eGFR and body weight as significant covariates on clearance and volume, respectively. A Bayesian maximum a posteriori feedback algorithm was subsequently coded in R and integrated into a simple web interface for bedside use. A prospective pilot evaluation enrolled 22 patients at the Neurology Clinic in Novi Sad over eight months. Clinicians received Bayesian dosing recommendations for 38 dosing decisions. Target concentration attainment (12–46 mg/L at trough) was 74% with algorithm-guided dosing compared with 52% in a historical control group managed by standard label-based adjustment. No serious adverse events were attributed to algorithm use. Larger controlled trials are needed before routine clinical implementation.

title: Simulation-based evaluation of vancomycin dosing nomograms for patients on continuous renal replacement therapy
abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) substantially alters vancomycin pharmacokinetics, but dosing nomograms published for CRRT patients vary widely in their target attainment predictions. We performed a simulation study using a validated two-compartment model parameterised with data from 44 ICU patients on CRRT at two Serbian tertiary centres. Monte Carlo simulations (5,000 virtual patients per scenario) evaluated six published nomograms across three CRRT effluent flow rates (20, 25, and 35 mL/kg/h). The primary endpoint was the proportion of simulated patients achieving AUC24/MIC ≥ 400 for an MIC of 1 mg/L. Attainment probabilities ranged from 31% to 78% across nomograms at 25 mL/kg/h. Two nomograms consistently overshot the AUC target ceiling of 600 mg·h/L, associated with toxicity risk in more than 20% of simulations. A modified loading dose of 25 mg/kg followed by maintenance guided by two-level Bayesian estimation achieved 71% attainment with only 7% exceeding the ceiling. The results argue against uncritical adoption of fixed nomograms in this setting.

title: Pharmacokinetic modelling in patients with renal impairment: a practical guide for biomedical engineers entering clinical collaborations
abstract: Biomedical engineers contributing to pharmacokinetic research in nephrology encounter methodological challenges that differ substantially from standard engineering problem-solving, including sparse and irregular sampling schedules, time-varying covariates, and regulatory considerations around clinical data use. This book chapter provides a structured introduction to population PK modelling workflow—data assembly, structural model selection, covariate analysis, and model evaluation—illustrated with case examples drawn from vancomycin and tacrolimus studies in patients with chronic kidney disease. Practical guidance is given on collaboration with clinical partners, ethics approval in Serbian institutional settings, and reporting standards aligned with current EMA guidelines on population PK. Software tools covered include NONMEM, Monolix, and R packages PKPDsim and mrgsolve. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and early-career researchers in biomedical engineering who are beginning clinical pharmacokinetic collaborations.

title: Greenhouse Gas Inventory for a 10 kV Distribution Network: Methodology and First Results
abstract: This study presents a structured GHG inventory for a 110/10 kV distribution network segment in Vojvodina covering approximately 340 km of overhead lines and 47 transformer substations. Emission sources were categorised following GHG Protocol Corporate Standard into Scope 1 (SF6 leakage from switchgear), Scope 2 (resistive and corona losses), and Scope 3 (embodied carbon in conductors and insulators). SF6 leakage rates were estimated from annual top-up records across 12 substations, yielding a mean annual release of 1.8 kg per substation, equivalent to 40.5 t CO2e. Technical energy losses were extracted from metered data for 2006–2008 and converted using the national grid emission factor of 0.721 kg CO2/kWh. Scope 3 contributions from conductor manufacturing were estimated using published aluminium and steel process LCA datasets. Total network emissions amounted to 6 470 t CO2e per year, with Scope 2 losses dominating at 71%. The paper discusses boundary-setting decisions and data quality issues particular to utility inventories in transition economies.

title: Comparison of Emission Factor Derivation Methods for the Serbian National Grid: Consequential vs. Attributional Approaches
abstract: National grid emission factors used in Scope 2 accounting vary substantially depending on whether an attributional (average) or consequential (marginal) approach is applied. This paper derives both types of factors for the Serbian electricity system using generation dispatch data from the national transmission operator for 2005–2009. The attributional factor ranges from 0.695 to 0.742 kg CO2/kWh over the period, driven primarily by the share of lignite-fired generation (58–64%). The marginal factor, estimated by identifying the load-following plant at each hour across a representative sample of 8 760 hourly dispatch records, averages 0.812 kg CO2/kWh because gas-fired combined heat and power plants typically set the margin during peak hours. Implications for distribution company Scope 2 reporting are discussed, showing that marginal-factor inventories exceed average-factor inventories by 9–17%. The paper also examines the treatment of pumped storage and cross-border import flows in factor derivation and recommends a dual-reporting convention aligned with the GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance published in 2015.

title: SF6 Leakage Detection and Quantification in Medium-Voltage Switchgear: Field Measurement Protocols
abstract: Sulphur hexafluoride used as an insulating and arc-quenching gas in gas-insulated switchgear has a global warming potential of 23 500 over 100 years, making even small leaks highly significant for GHG inventories. This conference paper reports on a two-year field campaign across 24 substations in Vojvodina, using portable infrared SF6 detectors and annual gas-weight mass balance records to cross-validate leakage estimates. Top-up method estimates averaged 2.1 kg/substation/year while infrared camera surveys detected leakage events at six flanged joints and four density-monitor cable penetrations, collectively accounting for 76% of identified losses. Discrepancies between methods at individual substations ranged from −40% to +110%, highlighting the uncertainty in inventory reporting when only one method is applied. The paper proposes a tiered measurement protocol: annual top-up records as the default, supplemented by at least biennial camera surveys, which together bring combined uncertainty below ±25% at 95% confidence.

title: Comparative LCA of Underground Cable versus Overhead Line for a 20 kV Feeder: Cradle-to-Grave Perspective
abstract: Underground XLPE cable feeders are increasingly deployed for aesthetic and reliability reasons in urban distribution networks, yet their environmental trade-offs relative to overhead lines are rarely quantified. This study conducts a cradle-to-grave LCA comparing a 5 km 20 kV overhead aluminium line with a functionally equivalent underground XLPE cable installation in an urban district of Novi Sad, with a reference service life of 45 years. Primary data were collected from a cable manufacturer in Serbia and from the municipal distribution utility. The underground option has 2.3 times the embodied carbon of the overhead option at manufacturing stage (210 vs. 91 t CO2e), owing to PVC and XLPE insulation and higher copper cross-section. However, lower resistive losses (3.8% vs. 5.2% annual energy loss) reduce operational Scope 2 emissions by 18 t CO2e/year. Break-even analysis shows that the underground cable achieves lower cumulative life-cycle emissions only after 37 years, close to the end of its design life. Sensitivity analysis on loss rates and grid emission factors strongly influences this threshold.
