title: Retention of Title Clauses in Serbian Commercial Sales: Legal Framework and Practical Gaps
abstract: Retention of title (RoT) clauses are widely used in cross-border commercial sales involving Serbian buyers, yet their legal treatment under Serbian law remains fragmented across the Law on Contracts and Torts, the Law on Pledge, and conflict-of-laws rules under the Private International Law Act of 2014. This article analyses the doctrinal basis on which Serbian courts have recognised or disregarded RoT clauses in twenty-three published decisions between 2010 and 2022, retrieved from the official Supreme Court of Cassation database and the Paragraf legal information system. The analysis finds that courts apply inconsistent standards when determining whether an RoT clause constitutes a security interest subject to registration requirements. The article argues that the absence of a unified security interest registry encompassing RoT arrangements creates practical uncertainty for foreign trade creditors and distorts risk pricing in commercial lending. Comparison with Slovenian and Hungarian law illustrates how explicit statutory recognition of RoT as a functional security interest reduces litigation rates. The article concludes with a draft provision suitable for integration into a prospective Serbian Secured Transactions Act.

title: Fiduciary Transfer of Ownership as a Security Device: Comparative Observations from the Western Balkans
abstract: This book chapter surveys the use of fiduciary transfer of ownership (fidučijarna predaja) as an extra-registration security mechanism in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro. Drawing on statutory texts, academic commentary, and a small selection of lower court decisions available through national court databases, the chapter describes how the device emerged in practice as a workaround to the formalities associated with registered pledges. The chapter documents three common transactional structures: full transfer with repurchase undertaking, transfer to a trustee entity, and transfer as collateral for a bank loan. It then assesses each structure against the transparency and priority rules recommended by the UNCITRAL Legislative Guide, finding that all three structures would require either statutory recognition or judicial recharacterisation under a fully functional secured transactions statute. The chapter contributes to an edited volume on private law reform in the post-Yugoslav legal space and includes a comparative table summarising the treatment of fiduciary security in nine jurisdictions.

title: Priority Rules for Competing Security Interests over Inventory: A Gap Analysis of Serbian Law
abstract: This preprint presents an in-progress chapter of the author's doctoral dissertation examining the rules governing priority among competing non-possessory security interests over inventory under Serbian law. The analysis focuses on three scenarios: a conflict between a registered pledge and an unperfected RoT clause, a conflict between two registered pledges with staggered registration dates, and a conflict between a pledge and a tax lien. Serbian law is assessed against Recommendations 78–95 of the UNCITRAL Legislative Guide on Secured Transactions. The study uses a structured gap-analysis matrix with forty-one binary criteria, revealing that Serbian law provides clear answers on only nineteen of them. Particular attention is given to the absence of a purchase-money security interest concept in Serbian law and its implications for inventory financing by small traders. The preprint also contains a short empirical section based on forty semi-structured interviews with commercial lawyers and bank credit officers in Novi Sad and Belgrade conducted in late 2024, indicating that practitioners frequently rely on contractual workarounds rather than statutory priority rules.

title: The Concept of 'Settlement' in Commodity Derivatives Under EU Financial Regulation and Its Transposition in Western Balkan Jurisdictions
abstract: This article compares the regulatory concept of settlement as defined in EU MiFID II and EMIR with its transposition across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Data were collected through a systematic review of national securities and derivatives legislation, regulatory guidance documents, and 12 semi-structured interviews with compliance officers at commodity brokerages. The study finds significant divergences in the definition of physical versus cash settlement, with three of the four jurisdictions failing to distinguish multi-leg netting arrangements consistently. The article argues that these definitional gaps create arbitrage opportunities and legal uncertainty for cross-border commodity trades. It further discusses the extent to which the EU accession process has driven convergence, noting that alignment has been procedural rather than substantive in most cases.

title: Wind pressure distribution on low-rise residential blocks in a flat Pannonian urban setting: a CFD parametric study
abstract: This study examined wind pressure coefficients on low-rise residential block typologies characteristic of flat Pannonian urban areas using Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes simulations in OpenFOAM 2.3. Sixteen block configurations were tested, varying height-to-width ratios from 0.3 to 1.2 and street orientations at 0°, 45°, and 90° relative to the prevailing north-west wind direction. Boundary conditions were derived from a ten-year wind rose dataset recorded at Novi Sad meteorological station. Grid sensitivity analysis confirmed mesh independence at approximately 2.1 million cells for each domain. Results showed that blocks with H/W ratios above 0.8 produced recirculation zones extending 1.4 block lengths downstream, reducing ground-level wind speeds by up to 62% compared to open conditions. Corner acceleration factors reached 1.31 for 45° approach angles. The findings were compared against wind tunnel data from a parallel Slovak study and showed deviations below 11% at equivalent measurement points. Implications for natural ventilation and pedestrian comfort zoning in masterplan documents are discussed.

title: Measured and simulated surface temperatures in a central Novi Sad street canyon during a July heat event
abstract: Field measurements of surface and air temperatures were conducted along a 340-metre east–west oriented street canyon in central Novi Sad during four consecutive days in July 2013, when maximum air temperatures exceeded 38 °C. Asphalt, concrete pavement, and plastered brick façade surfaces were monitored at 15-minute intervals using four calibrated infrared radiometers and two aspirated psychrometers. The ENVI-met 3.1 model was subsequently set up to replicate the canyon geometry from cadastral data and was run with initialisation conditions drawn from the measurements. Simulated surface temperatures reproduced measured values with RMSE values of 2.7 °C for asphalt and 3.4 °C for south-facing façades. Discrepancies were largest between 13:00 and 15:00 local time, attributed to specular reflection not captured by the Lambertian surface assumption in the model. Results confirm that ENVI-met is adequate for comparative morphological studies in this climate context but requires caution when absolute temperature accuracy is needed.

title: Outdoor thermal comfort in redesigned public squares: linking morphological variables to PET values in a continental climate
abstract: Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) was used to assess outdoor thermal comfort across twelve public square configurations in Serbian and Croatian cities with a continental climate classification (Köppen Dfb/Cfa boundary). Each square was documented through on-site surveys and geometric reconstruction in AutoCAD, then modelled in ENVI-met 3.5. Simulations were run for a representative summer day (10 July 2015) and a transitional spring day (15 April 2015). Sky View Factor (SVF) was computed from fish-eye projections and ranged from 0.31 to 0.89 across the sample. Statistical analysis showed SVF to be the strongest predictor of midday PET (R² = 0.74), followed by the fraction of albedo-adjusted hard surface. Squares with SVF below 0.50 maintained PET values below 41 °C throughout the afternoon under summer conditions, while open squares exceeded 48 °C. Tree canopy cover showed a weaker direct correlation with PET than SVF but became significant in regression models that controlled for wind speed. Practical design thresholds derived from the data are proposed.

title: Sensitivity of CFD-predicted pedestrian wind comfort to inlet turbulence intensity in an open suburban layout
abstract: Inlet boundary conditions for pedestrian-level wind comfort simulations in open suburban layouts are rarely derived from site-specific measurements, leading to uncertainty in predicted wind speeds. This study systematically varied turbulence intensity (TI) at the inlet of a steady-state k–ε RANS simulation built in OpenFOAM 4.1, testing TI values of 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% for a suburban residential layout in Novi Sad with building heights between 6 and 18 metres. The computational domain extended 5H upwind and 15H downwind of the development. Eighteen pedestrian-level probe points were evaluated against a reference dataset from a boundary-layer wind tunnel test conducted at the Politecnico di Milano. Results showed that TI variation between 5% and 20% produced differences of up to 19% in local wind speed ratios at corner acceleration zones but less than 7% in sheltered courtyard locations. Recommendations for default TI settings for flat-terrain suburban studies are given, and limitations of isotropic turbulence assumptions are identified.

title: Solar access mapping for rooftop photovoltaic potential in a medium-density European city: methodology and results for Novi Sad
abstract: Accurate solar access maps are a prerequisite for realistic estimates of rooftop photovoltaic potential in cities with varied building stock. This study applied a RADIANCE-based irradiance simulation to a 2.4 km² test area in central and inner suburban Novi Sad using a photogrammetric point cloud processed into a digital surface model at 0.5 m resolution. Annual global horizontal irradiance was disaggregated to roof surfaces using a cumulative sky matrix based on ten years of hourly radiation data from the Serbian Meteorological and Hydrometeorological Institute. Usable roof area was filtered by tilt (0–45°), shading fraction (below 30% annual), and structural suitability class derived from building permit records. The analysis identified 0.94 km² of technically viable roof surface, with a median annual irradiation of 1,387 kWh/m². Comparison with satellite-derived irradiance products (SARAH-2) showed deviations of ±6% at aggregated block level. The methodology is transferable to other medium-density Pannonian cities with comparable data availability.

title: Thermal comfort zoning as a tool for public space prioritisation in municipal heat action plans: a pilot application for three Serbian cities
abstract: Municipal heat action plans in Serbia typically rely on hospital admission data and aggregate temperature statistics rather than spatially explicit thermal comfort assessments. This paper proposes a GIS-based workflow that integrates ENVI-met simulation outputs, population density data from the 2022 census, and vulnerability indices (elderly population share, green space deficit) to produce thermal comfort priority zones for outdoor public spaces. The method was piloted in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin, covering 47 public spaces in total. Simulations were run for the 2023 summer design week using ERA5-derived boundary conditions. Priority scores combined thermal load (midday PET exceedance above 41 °C) with social exposure, yielding ranked intervention lists. In Novi Sad, six of the top ten priority spaces were in pre-1960 residential quarters lacking tree cover. The workflow was presented to municipal planners in all three cities and technical requirements for implementation within existing GIS infrastructure are described.

title: Transformation of Agricultural Courtyard Buildings into Residential Conversions in Novi Sad's Periurban Villages: Ten Cases, 1991–2020
abstract: Ten cases of former agricultural courtyard buildings (dvori) in periurban villages within the Novi Sad municipal boundary were documented through measured survey, photographic recording, and semi-structured interviews with current occupants. All ten buildings were originally built between 1880 and 1940 and converted to primarily residential use between 1991 and 2020 without formal heritage protection status. The documentation records original spatial configuration, structural system, and surviving fabric alongside the sequence and character of alterations made during conversion. Alterations are classified by reversibility and impact on spatial legibility using a four-category scheme. Results show that in seven of the ten cases the original plan organisation of the dwelling wing is substantially intact, while stable and storage wings have been more radically altered. The paper discusses the absence of a regulatory instrument suited to this building category and the gap between heritage listing thresholds and the practical need for conservation guidance at the level of the individual building owner.

title: Interstitial condensation risk mapping for internally insulated brick walls across the Pannonian climate gradient
abstract: Climate data from eleven meteorological stations along a northwest–southeast transect from Pécs (Hungary) to Niš (Serbia) were used to drive HAM simulations of a standardised internally insulated brick wall assembly (51 cm solid brick, 80 mm calcium silicate board). The Pannonian climate gradient produces a systematic increase in summer vapour pressure from northwest to southeast, which influences annual drying capacity. Simulated peak accumulated moisture at the insulation–masonry interface ranged from 0.04 kg/m² at the Pécs station to 0.11 kg/m² at the Niš station under identical indoor conditions. A condensation risk index, defined as the ratio of peak annual moisture load to safe moisture storage capacity of the board, exceeded unity at four of eleven stations under humidity class 3 indoor conditions, indicating that material selection must be climate-zone specific. Maps showing the risk index distribution across the Pannonian Basin are provided for use in regional design guidance.

title: Template-based spike sorting under gradual electrode displacement in chronic Utah array recordings
abstract: Chronic intracortical recording with Utah arrays is routinely complicated by slow mechanical displacement of electrode tips relative to neuronal somata, causing waveform morphology to drift over days to weeks. We present a spike-sorting pipeline that models template evolution as a low-rank trajectory in principal-component space and updates template centroids incrementally after each 30-minute recording block. The method was evaluated on six weeks of continuous multi-unit data obtained from three adult male Sprague-Dawley rats implanted in forelimb motor cortex, yielding 192 channels in total. Compared with static template matching (k-means initialised), the proposed tracker reduced unit-loss events by 41% and improved isolation quality score from 0.61 to 0.79 (median across units). Computational overhead was under 12% relative to offline Kilosort2 processing. Particular attention was paid to distinguishing true morphological drift from genuine population turnover, and a statistical test for distinguishing these two phenomena is included. The code is released under a permissive open-source licence.

title: A Kalman filter decoder for continuous hand trajectory estimation from motor cortex multi-unit activity during chronic drift
abstract: We describe and validate a Kalman filter decoder adapted for neuroprosthetic hand trajectory estimation in conditions where multi-unit activity statistics shift non-stationarily over recording sessions. The decoder incorporates a session-by-session covariance update step driven by a small set of calibration trials (mean: 18 trials, range: 12–25) collected at the start of each recording day. Evaluation used a dataset of 22 recording sessions spanning eleven weeks, collected from two Macaca fascicularis subjects performing a centre-out reaching task with 16 target directions. Across sessions, the adapted decoder achieved a mean correlation between decoded and actual hand velocity of r = 0.76 (SD 0.08), compared with r = 0.58 (SD 0.14) for a fixed decoder trained only on day-one data. The calibration overhead per session was approximately four minutes. Decoder failure modes related to multi-unit isolation quality are characterised quantitatively, providing practical thresholds for deciding when recalibration is insufficient and full re-training is warranted.

title: Recurrent neural network decoders for intracortical neuroprosthetics: sensitivity to training set size and session-to-session variability
abstract: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have shown strong performance on offline neural decoding benchmarks, yet their practical deployment in neuroprosthetics is constrained by the amount of labelled training data that can realistically be collected per session and by performance degradation when recording statistics shift between sessions. We trained long short-term memory (LSTM) decoders on simulated reaching data generated by a published motor cortex population model and on two real primate datasets from collaborating laboratories. Training set sizes were systematically varied from 2 to 120 minutes of labelled movement. Velocity reconstruction R² reached a plateau at approximately 35 minutes of training data, beyond which gains were marginal (less than 0.03 R² improvement per additional 10 minutes). A lightweight domain-adaptation layer, requiring only five calibration trials at the start of a new session, recovered 89% of within-session performance when tested across a simulated one-week gap. Results suggest that RNN decoders can be made practically viable with moderate per-session overhead.

title: Минимално инвазивна ЕКоГ решетка са флексибилним полимерним подлогама: карактеризација импедансе и механичке стабилности
abstract: Овај рад описује поступак израде и карактеризацију прототипа флексибилне електрокортикографске решетке са 32 канала, израђене на полиимидној подлози дебљине 12 µm. Решетка је пројектована за минимално инвазивну примену у истраживачком контексту. Мерења импедансе на 1 kHz показала су медијану 38 kΩ непосредно после израде, уз пораст на 54 kΩ након 30-дневног потапања у физиолошком раствору. Механичка стабилност проверена је испитивањем клизања електродних трака при цикличном савијању (полупречник 5 mm, 5000 циклуса); ниједна електрода није показала прекид. Снимања на моделу свиње (n = 3) потврдила су детекцију соматосензорних евоцираних потенцијала. Рад не укључује хронична in vivo мерења, већ поставља основу за будућа дугорочна испитивања.

title: Decoder recalibration frequency and user fatigue in simulated closed-loop neuroprosthetic control: a human factors study
abstract: Adaptive decoder recalibration extends the functional lifespan of intracortical neuroprosthetic systems but imposes periodic interruptions during which users perform structured calibration movements. We investigated how recalibration frequency affects subjective fatigue, task engagement and cursor-control performance in a 2D brain-computer interface simulation with 22 able-bodied participants who controlled a cursor via an electromyographic proxy signal designed to mimic neural decoder behaviour. Participants completed sessions under four recalibration schedules (every 5, 10, 20 or 40 minutes). Self-reported fatigue (NASA-TLX) was lowest at the 20-minute interval. Performance degradation between recalibrations was acceptable up to 20-minute intervals but increased sharply at 40 minutes. A 10-minute schedule produced the highest performance but also the highest mental demand scores. These behavioural findings suggest that recalibration intervals of 15–25 minutes may offer the best balance for prolonged daily use, a recommendation that should be re-examined in future studies with actual implanted users.
venue: Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation

title: Generative data augmentation for neural decoder training under limited calibration data
abstract: Training high-capacity decoders for intracortical neuroprosthetics typically requires tens of minutes of labelled neural activity, which is costly to collect in clinical settings. We evaluate whether synthetic neural firing patterns, generated by a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) trained on a small seed corpus, can augment decoder training sets and improve velocity-decoding accuracy when real data are scarce. The CVAE was trained on 10-minute seed sessions and conditioned on movement direction and speed labels. Synthetic data were mixed with real data at ratios from 1:1 to 8:1 synthetic-to-real. Across five held-out recording sessions from two primate subjects, augmentation at a 4:1 ratio improved mean R² from 0.49 to 0.64 relative to training on real data alone. Performance gains diminished at higher synthetic ratios, likely due to mode collapse artefacts. Ablation experiments isolate the contribution of the conditioning variables and confirm that unconditioned generation provides no meaningful benefit.

title: Parental Supervision Styles During Computer-Based Homework: A Typology Study in Vojvodina Households
abstract: This study developed a typology of parental supervision during computer-based homework among families in Vojvodina. Structured observations were conducted in 68 households with children aged 9–11 over four consecutive school evenings, supplemented by semi-structured interviews with primary caregivers. Three distinct supervision styles emerged from hierarchical cluster analysis: active co-engagement, periodic monitoring, and non-involvement. Active co-engagement was associated with significantly higher homework completion rates (82% versus 61% for non-involvement, p < 0.01) but also with greater time-on-task for parents, averaging 47 minutes per evening. Families with higher parental educational attainment were overrepresented in the active co-engagement cluster. The study argues that supervision typologies should inform how schools design and communicate digital homework assignments, and that blanket assumptions about parental digital competence are not warranted in regional Serbian contexts.

title: How Primary School Teachers in Serbia Perceive Parental Roles in Digital Homework Tasks
abstract: This questionnaire-based study examined how 214 primary school teachers across 18 schools in Serbia perceive and value parental involvement when children complete digitally delivered homework. A purpose-built instrument measured teacher attitudes toward active parental co-use, technical assistance, and content supervision on five-point Likert scales. Factor analysis yielded three interpretable subscales: technical support expectation, content oversight acceptance, and autonomy preference. Teachers in urban schools scored higher on autonomy preference compared to rural teachers (mean difference 0.6, 95% CI 0.3–0.9). Open-ended responses revealed widespread uncertainty about appropriate parental involvement norms. The findings point to a gap between official school communication about digital homework and the tacit expectations teachers hold, suggesting a need for more explicit school policies on parental digital mediation.

title: Screen Time Logging as a Research Tool in Home Learning Environments: Methodological Considerations
abstract: This methodological paper reports on the use of passive screen-time logging software installed on children's devices to collect homework engagement data in 42 Serbian households over a three-week period. The paper documents practical and ethical challenges encountered during deployment, including parental concerns about privacy, device heterogeneity across Android and Windows platforms, and data loss rates of approximately 14% due to parental deactivation. Comparison of logged data with parent-reported time estimates showed a systematic overestimation in self-reports by a mean of 22 minutes per session. The paper proposes a protocol for consent-embedded deployment that reduces attrition and discusses the legal standing of such data collection under relevant Serbian data protection regulations. Recommendations are made for researchers planning similar studies in low-resource school contexts.

title: Restrictive Versus Active Digital Mediation and Children's Self-Regulated Learning on E-Learning Platforms
abstract: This study examined how two broad parental mediation strategies — restrictive and active — relate to third- and fourth-grade children's self-regulated learning (SRL) behaviours on a school-mandated e-learning platform. A sample of 183 child–parent dyads was recruited from 11 primary schools in Novi Sad and Sombor. Parents completed the Parental Mediation of Internet Use Scale adapted for an e-learning context, while children's SRL was assessed through platform log data and the Children's Perceived Self-Efficacy Questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analyses showed that active mediation significantly predicted higher SRL scores (β = 0.34, p < 0.001), whereas restrictive mediation showed a negative relationship with SRL (β = −0.19, p = 0.02) after controlling for child age, gender, and parental education. The effect of active mediation was stronger for children who had been using the platform for less than one school year, suggesting a scaffolding role that diminishes with experience.

title: Digital Parenting in Low-Income Households: Mediation Practices When Devices Are Shared
abstract: This qualitative study focused on 24 low-income families in Vojvodina where a single shared device was used by multiple household members, including children completing e-learning assignments. In-depth interviews were conducted with parents and, separately, with children, and home visits included a 90-minute structured observation period. Three themes dominated parental accounts: negotiated scheduling of device access, partial supervision due to simultaneous adult use, and content unawareness arising from limited time-with-device. Children reported adapting their e-learning behaviour to the presence or absence of adults, sometimes shortening task time to free the device for others. The findings complicate standard mediation typologies, which assume dedicated child-device pairs, and call for school-level accommodation strategies including asynchronous task design and extended submission windows for families with shared-device constraints.

title: Platform Design Features and the Distribution of Parental Mediation Effort: A Comparative Log Study
abstract: This study compared parental mediation effort across two commercially available e-learning platforms used in Serbian primary schools — one with an integrated parent dashboard and automated progress notifications, and one without — using a within-subjects design involving 97 families over two successive school terms. Platform log data, parental time-diary entries, and end-of-term interviews provided a mixed-methods dataset. Parents using the dashboard-equipped platform reported on average 18 fewer minutes of active supervision per week (95% CI 12–24 minutes) and scored lower on perceived parental burden scales. However, interview data indicated that some parents interpreted automated notifications as a substitute for direct engagement, leading to reduced conversational involvement with the child about task content. The study discusses trade-offs between efficiency gains from platform automation and the educational value of direct parental co-engagement.

title: Gender Differences in Parental Mediation: Do Mothers and Fathers Mediate Children's E-Learning Differently?
abstract: This study examined whether mothers and fathers differ in their digital mediation practices during children's e-learning homework, using paired data from 138 two-parent households in Sombor and Novi Sad. Both parents independently completed the same adapted mediation scale, and 40 households also participated in dual-caregiver observations. Mothers reported significantly higher levels of active mediation (p = 0.003) and content co-engagement, whereas fathers more frequently provided technical troubleshooting assistance. Observational data corroborated these differences: mothers were present during 71% of observed sessions, fathers during 38%. Multilevel modelling showed that household division-of-labour attitudes moderated the gender gap, with more egalitarian households showing smaller differences. The study suggests that school-facing parental engagement strategies should account for gendered patterns of availability and competence perception.

title: Parental Mediation Practices Before and During COVID-19 School Closures: A Longitudinal Panel Study
abstract: This panel study tracked parental digital mediation practices in 211 Serbian families across three measurement points: autumn 2019 (pre-closure), spring 2020 (full school closure), and autumn 2020 (partial reopening). Parents completed comparable mediation, parental stress, and digital competence instruments at each wave, and children's e-learning platform logs were collected continuously. Active mediation increased markedly during the closure period (mean increase of 1.2 scale points, SD = 0.7), while restrictive mediation decreased, possibly reflecting the necessity of sustained device use. Parental stress moderated this effect: highly stressed parents showed smaller increases in active mediation and maintained restrictive practices. Platform engagement data showed that children whose parents increased active mediation sustained higher completion rates through the closure period. The results have implications for crisis-period school communication with families.

title: Digital Mediation and Children's Reading Comprehension Scores on an E-Learning Literacy Platform: An Analysis of 400 Dyads
abstract: This study used hierarchical linear modelling to examine whether parental digital mediation type predicted reading comprehension growth over one school year on a school-assigned literacy e-learning platform. Data from 400 child–parent dyads across 19 schools in the Vojvodina region included platform log measures of time-on-task, hint usage, and retry rates, combined with parental mediation questionnaire data and standardised reading comprehension pre- and post-test scores. Active mediation predicted end-of-year reading comprehension scores above and beyond pre-test scores (β = 0.21, p < 0.001), while restrictive mediation was non-significant after controlling for time-on-task. Hint usage on the platform mediated approximately 30% of the active mediation effect, suggesting that parent-accompanied scaffolding translates into more strategic use of built-in platform supports. Implications for platform design and parent training are discussed.

title: Parental Digital Mediation in Bilingual Households: The Case of Hungarian-Serbian Families in Vojvodina
abstract: This mixed-methods study examined digital mediation practices in 58 bilingual Hungarian-Serbian families with primary school children in Vojvodina, where children may use e-learning platforms in either or both official languages. Parents completed the adapted mediation scale in their preferred language, and follow-up interviews explored how language choice on the platform influenced parental ability to co-engage with content. Quantitative results showed no significant difference in overall mediation frequency between bilingual and monolingual Serbian households. However, interview data revealed that parents with dominant Hungarian proficiency reported qualitatively different co-engagement when platform content was in Serbian: assistance shifted from content discussion to translation and vocabulary support, reducing time spent on task comprehension. The study highlights the need for platform localisation and bilingual parent guidance materials in minority-language school settings.

title: Parent–Child Conversation During E-Learning Tasks: A Microanalysis of 60 Video-Recorded Sessions
abstract: This microanalytic study examined naturally occurring verbal interaction between parents and children aged 8–12 during e-learning homework sessions. Sixty video recordings were collected from 32 families, with each family contributing one to three sessions. Interaction was coded using an adapted version of the Joint Media Engagement coding scheme, capturing 12 turn-taking categories including directive prompts, elaborating questions, and metacognitive comments. Metacognitive comments from parents — such as asking the child to explain their reasoning before clicking an answer — were positively associated with longer task persistence (r = 0.39, p = 0.002) and with children seeking fewer system hints. Directive prompts were negatively associated with child-initiated elaboration. The analysis provides a fine-grained basis for designing parent guidance materials that emphasise questioning strategies over answer provision, and offers coding materials that can be adapted for teacher training.

title: Parental Digital Mediation, Homework Anxiety, and Perceived Competence in Children Aged 8–12: A Structural Equation Model
abstract: This study tested a structural equation model linking parental digital mediation practices to homework-related anxiety and perceived academic competence in 341 children aged 8–12 across 15 primary schools in Novi Sad and Sombor. Parent-reported mediation data were combined with child self-report measures of homework anxiety (Children's Homework Anxiety Scale) and perceived competence (domain-specific subscale of the Self-Description Questionnaire). The fitted model showed adequate fit (CFI = 0.95, RMSEA = 0.06). Active mediation was negatively associated with homework anxiety (β = −0.28) and positively with perceived competence (β = 0.31). Restrictive mediation showed a small positive association with anxiety (β = 0.14) but not with competence. Moderation analyses indicated that the anxiety-reducing effect of active mediation was larger for children with lower initial competence ratings, suggesting a buffering function for less confident learners.

title: Sensitivity of Savings Estimates to Baseline Period Length in IPMVP Option C Applications
abstract: The International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) recommends but does not strictly prescribe a baseline period length for Option C whole-facility analyses. This study investigates how varying the baseline period from 6 to 36 months affects estimated energy savings and their associated uncertainties in a sample of 12 energy performance contracts executed in Serbia and Hungary between 2005 and 2009. Synthetic datasets were generated by bootstrapping from metered records to simulate shorter baseline scenarios. Results show that savings uncertainty, expressed as a 90% confidence interval half-width relative to reported savings, increases sharply when baseline periods fall below 12 months, with median relative uncertainty rising from 7% at 24 months to 22% at 6 months. The paper recommends a 15-month minimum to capture seasonal cycles adequately, particularly for facilities with heating-dominated energy profiles.

title: Multivariate Regression Models for Energy Verification in Ceramic Tile Production
abstract: Ceramic tile kilns present a challenging verification environment because energy consumption depends simultaneously on firing temperature setpoints, tile format mix, and throughput. This case study applies multiple linear regression with three independent variables—daily tonnes fired, average kiln setpoint in degrees Celsius, and format complexity index—to a 30-month baseline dataset from a tile manufacturer in southern Serbia. Cross-validation using leave-one-month-out yielded an average CVRMSE of 6.8% and an R-squared of 0.94. Interaction terms between throughput and format complexity improved model fit moderately (ΔR² = 0.02) but were retained based on physical reasoning. Post-retrofit verification over 18 months estimated annual savings of 2,340 MWh with a 90% confidence interval of ±210 MWh. The paper documents the data collection protocol and discusses practical challenges in obtaining reliable format complexity data from production management systems.

title: Uncertainty Propagation in IPMVP Savings Calculations: A Monte Carlo Framework
abstract: This paper presents a structured Monte Carlo framework for propagating measurement uncertainty through IPMVP Option C savings calculations. Three uncertainty sources are modelled explicitly: meter precision (characterised by manufacturer calibration certificates), model parameter uncertainty (expressed as regression coefficient covariance matrices), and routine adjustment variable uncertainty (arising from production reporting errors). For each source, probability distributions are specified and 10,000 simulation runs are performed per facility. The framework is applied to five industrial sites in Vojvodina. Combined relative uncertainty at the 90% confidence level ranged from 4.9% to 18.7% of reported annual savings, with model parameter uncertainty being the dominant contributor in four of five cases. The paper argues that meter accuracy is frequently over-emphasised in contract negotiations relative to the larger contribution of regression model error, and proposes a standardised uncertainty budget table for use in EPC contracts.

title: Practical Data Quality Criteria for Sub-Metering in IPMVP Option C Industrial Contracts
abstract: Sub-metering infrastructure installed for energy performance contracts in industrial facilities often suffers from data gaps, sensor drift, and communication faults that compromise verification reliability. This book chapter reviews data quality criteria—completeness thresholds, outlier detection rules, gap-filling procedures—and evaluates their impact on savings uncertainty in a set of 14 contracts from Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary. A minimum completeness of 95% of half-hourly readings per month is found to be necessary but not sufficient; the temporal pattern of gaps matters substantially. Systematic gaps during production peaks introduce bias of up to 8% in savings estimates when gap-filling uses mean substitution. Interpolation-based gap-filling reduces this bias to below 1% for gaps under four hours. The chapter provides a practical checklist for metering system acceptance testing before baseline measurement begins.

title: Machine Learning Baselines and IPMVP Compatibility: An Assessment Using Random Forests on Industrial Metering Data
abstract: Random forest regression has been proposed as an alternative to linear regression for energy baseline modelling, offering flexibility in capturing non-linear relationships. This paper assesses whether random forest baselines are compatible with IPMVP Option C requirements, focusing on uncertainty quantification and interpretability. Using data from nine industrial facilities in Serbia and Romania, random forest models are compared with multiple linear regression on out-of-sample CVRMSE, prediction interval coverage, and computational reproducibility. Random forests improve CVRMSE by 1.2–3.8 percentage points in facilities with non-linear production–energy relationships, but standard prediction interval methods undercover at the 90% nominal level, achieving actual coverage of 74–83%. A conformal prediction wrapper improves coverage to 88–91%. The paper concludes that random forests are technically usable under IPMVP with appropriate uncertainty wrappers but require more documentation and auditor expertise than linear methods.

title: Baseline Adjustment for Seasonal Production Shifts: A Case Study in the Food Processing Industry
abstract: Food processing facilities exhibit pronounced seasonal production cycles driven by agricultural harvest schedules, complicating the construction of stable energy baselines. This paper reports on the verification of energy conservation measures at a sunflower oil processing plant in Vojvodina where production is concentrated in a 14-week autumn campaign and then drops to near zero. A simple annual regression model fails diagnostic tests (CVRMSE = 28.4%), while a two-regime model with a campaign indicator variable achieves CVRMSE of 9.1%. Savings from heat recovery retrofitting are estimated at 3,610 MWh/year with a 90% confidence interval of ±390 MWh. The study also evaluates whether shorter campaign-period-only baselines are preferable, finding that they reduce model error but amplify savings uncertainty due to the reduced number of observations. Contractual implications of regime-switching models are discussed with reference to dispute resolution clauses.

title: Standardised Reporting Templates for IPMVP Option C Measurement and Verification Reports in the Western Balkans
abstract: Energy performance contracting markets in the Western Balkans are hampered by the absence of standardised measurement and verification reporting formats, leading to disputes between ESCOs and clients over savings claims. This paper proposes a set of seven reporting templates covering baseline model specification, routine adjustment procedures, savings calculation, uncertainty budget, data quality record, anomaly log, and annual reconciliation. The templates are developed through a review of 41 verification reports from Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, identifying the most frequent sources of ambiguity. A draft template set was reviewed by 18 practitioners—ESCOs, facility managers, and financial auditors—through a structured consultation process. Feedback indicated strong acceptance of the uncertainty budget and data quality templates, while the anomaly log format required two revision rounds. The templates are offered as open-access documents and are aligned with IPMVP 2022 and ISO 50015.

title: Influence of Production Mix Variability on Savings Uncertainty in Multi-Product Industrial Facilities
abstract: Industrial facilities manufacturing multiple product types with differing specific energy intensities pose a measurement and verification challenge because production volume alone is an inadequate independent variable. This study develops a weighted production index (WPI) that aggregates multi-product output using specific energy intensity ratios estimated from historical data, and evaluates its performance as a regression independent variable against simple total-tonnage models. The WPI is tested on datasets from six facilities: two metalworking plants, two plastics extruders, and two textile operations, all in Serbia. Using WPI reduces mean CVRMSE from 17.3% to 9.8% compared with total-tonnage models and from 12.1% to 9.8% compared with product-specific dummy variable approaches. The savings uncertainty reduction (median 38% reduction in 90% CI half-width) is large enough to matter in contract terms for facilities where savings are close to the guaranteed minimum. A spreadsheet tool implementing the WPI calculation is described and made available as supplementary material.

title: Changes in melt flow index and tensile properties of isotactic polypropylene subjected to ten consecutive extrusion cycles
abstract: Isotactic polypropylene (iPP) pellets were extruded ten times under identical processing conditions (220 °C, 60 rpm) and samples were withdrawn after cycles 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 10. Melt flow index increased from 4.1 g/10 min in the virgin material to 18.7 g/10 min after the tenth cycle, indicating substantial chain scission. Gel permeation chromatography revealed a continuous shift of the number-average molecular weight from 87 000 to 41 000 g/mol over the same interval. Tensile strength dropped by 22 % and elongation at break by 61 % after ten cycles. DSC measurements showed a slight decrease in crystallinity from 43 % to 38 %, suggesting that chain scission partially disrupts the crystalline phase. The study establishes a quantitative baseline for acceptable reprocessing limits of iPP in packaging-grade applications and highlights cycle 3–5 as the range where mechanical property decline becomes practically significant.

title: Antioxidant consumption in high-density polyethylene during multi-pass injection moulding
abstract: The depletion of Irganox 1010-type hindered phenolic antioxidant in commercial-grade high-density polyethylene (HDPE) was quantified across five injection-moulding cycles using HPLC extraction and UV detection. Starting from a nominal 1000 ppm loading, residual antioxidant fell to approximately 340 ppm after the first cycle and to below 80 ppm after the fifth, tracking closely with increased carbonyl index values measured by ATR-FTIR. Oxidation induction time (OIT) measured by DSC under pure oxygen atmosphere decreased from 42 min to 6 min across the same processing sequence. Despite these stabiliser losses, impact strength showed less than 10 % reduction after five cycles, while colour (CIE L*a*b*) shifted measurably toward yellow. Results suggest that antioxidant depletion in HDPE proceeds faster than mechanical failure, making OIT a sensitive early indicator of recyclate quality.

title: Effect of paper and adhesive label contamination on the properties of recycled PET bottle flake
abstract: Post-industrial PET bottle flake was deliberately contaminated with finely ground paper and pressure-sensitive adhesive residues at concentrations of 0.1, 0.5 and 1.0 wt %. Contaminated and uncontaminated flakes were dried at 150 °C for 4 h and extruded into strands. Intrinsic viscosity of uncontaminated PET was 0.74 dL/g; at 1.0 wt % adhesive contamination it fell to 0.59 dL/g, consistent with acid-catalysed hydrolysis from adhesive components. Paper contamination at the same level caused visible specks and a 15 % reduction in tensile modulus without significant IV change. Colour b* (yellowness) increased sharply with both contaminant types. SEM of fracture surfaces of adhesive-contaminated samples showed cavities and phase boundaries absent in clean material. The data provide quantitative tolerance limits useful for sorting facility quality control.

title: Rheological characterisation of blended polypropylene recyclates with varying contamination levels of polyethylene
abstract: Binary blends of post-industrial polypropylene with 2, 5, 10 and 20 wt % high-density polyethylene were prepared by melt compounding and characterised by oscillatory shear rheometry at 200 °C and 220 °C. Storage modulus G′ and loss modulus G″ were measured over a frequency range of 0.01–100 rad/s. Phase separation morphology was assessed by optical microscopy of quenched films. At 5 wt % HDPE, rheological behaviour remained close to neat PP; at 10 wt % the crossover frequency shifted and a shoulder appeared in the G′ curve consistent with a dispersed phase relaxation. Notched Charpy impact strength exhibited a non-monotonic trend, peaking modestly at 2 wt % HDPE due to rubber-like energy absorption before decreasing at higher content. The study informs sorting tolerance thresholds for mixed polyolefin streams entering single-polymer recycling lines.

title: Thermal stability and gas evolution during pyrolysis of multi-cycle extruded ABS: a TGA–FTIR coupled study
abstract: Acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS) was extruded one, three and five times under standard conditions and subjected to thermogravimetric analysis coupled with FTIR gas analysis (TGA–FTIR). The temperature of maximum decomposition rate (Tmax) decreased from 415 °C for virgin ABS to 402 °C after five cycles, indicating reduced thermal stability. The gas phase spectra after three cycles showed increased nitrile and acrylate absorbances relative to virgin material, pointing to preferential oxidation of the butadiene phase. Residual mass at 600 °C remained near 2.5 % in all samples. Differential scanning calorimetry confirmed a decrease in the glass transition temperature of the SAN matrix from 108 °C to 102 °C after five cycles. The work is relevant to electronics and automotive sectors where ABS recyclate quality must be controlled.

title: Recycled thermoplastics in construction applications: a review of degradation-related performance limitations
abstract: This chapter surveys published literature on the use of post-industrial and post-consumer thermoplastic recyclates—primarily polyolefins, PVC and PET—in construction-related applications such as pipes, profiles, geomembranes and insulation boards. The chapter critically evaluates how accumulation of degradation products, molecular weight reduction and contaminant introduction during reprocessing affect long-term mechanical performance, UV resistance and creep behaviour. Data from creep rupture and accelerated ageing studies conducted on recyclate-containing profiles are compared across European and North American sources. The chapter identifies test protocols that are insufficiently standardised for recyclate-containing products and recommends characterisation metrics—particularly OIT, MFI and GPC dispersity index—that should become routine quality control parameters. The review covers publications from 2000 to 2016 and includes about 140 references.

title: Influence of colorant masterbatch accumulation on the mechanical and optical properties of multi-cycle polypropylene
abstract: Commercial polypropylene was compounded with a carbon-black pigment masterbatch at a nominal 2 wt % loading and subjected to five extrusion cycles. After each cycle, tensile properties, Charpy notched impact strength, yellowness index and MFI were measured. A parallel series with the same base polymer but no masterbatch served as a control. Carbon-black incorporation increased MFI increment per cycle by approximately 18 % relative to the unpigmented control, attributed to the pro-oxidant activity of trace metal impurities in the pigment. Tensile elongation at break decreased 48 % over five cycles compared to 32 % in the unpigmented series. Optical microscopy and image analysis quantified agglomerate size distribution of pigment particles, which coarsened from a median diameter of 2.1 µm to 4.8 µm after five cycles, correlating with observed stress concentration effects at fracture initiation sites.

title: Degradation behaviour of glass-fibre reinforced polypropylene after multiple injection-moulding cycles
abstract: Short-glass-fibre reinforced polypropylene (GF-PP, 20 wt % fibre) was injection-moulded five times and the evolution of fibre length distribution, matrix molecular weight, and composite mechanical properties was tracked. After the first cycle, weight-average fibre length decreased from 410 µm to 270 µm; after the fifth cycle it reached 155 µm. Tensile strength of the composite fell from 82 MPa to 61 MPa across five cycles, a decline larger than observed in unfilled PP under identical conditions. GPC of the extracted matrix showed Mn reduction of 35 % over five cycles, comparable to unfilled PP. Scanning electron microscopy of fracture surfaces revealed increased interfacial debonding and pull-out after three or more cycles. The combined effects of fibre attrition and matrix degradation are partially independent and additive in their influence on tensile modulus loss.

title: Detection of mineral oil hydrocarbon migration from recycled polypropylene packaging intended for non-food contact use
abstract: Post-industrial polypropylene recyclate, produced from mixed technical packaging streams known to include printed materials, was characterised for mineral oil hydrocarbon (MOH) contamination using GC–FID after silica-gel fractionation. Mineral oil saturated hydrocarbons (MOSH) in the range C10–C35 were detected at concentrations of 28–74 mg/kg depending on recyclate batch; mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons (MOAH) were below the detection limit of 0.5 mg/kg in all samples. Three cycles of thermal processing of contaminated pellets reduced MOSH content by approximately 12 % per cycle under vacuum venting conditions, demonstrating limited but measurable volatilisation. The findings are relevant to food-contact regulation compliance even for materials marketed as non-food-contact grades, given potential supply chain mixing. The study informs sorting specification requirements for PP entering closed-loop recycling schemes.

title: Accelerated weathering of polypropylene recyclate: combined effects of prior reprocessing cycles and UV exposure on surface and bulk degradation
abstract: Polypropylene samples subjected to one, three and five prior melt-extrusion cycles were exposed to accelerated UV weathering (Xenon arc, 0.35 W/m² at 340 nm) for 200, 500 and 1000 h. Surface carbonyl index measured by ATR-FTIR increased approximately 60 % faster in five-cycle samples than in one-cycle samples at equivalent UV doses, indicating that prior thermal degradation sensitises the material to photooxidation. Colour change (ΔE*) after 1000 h weathering was 8.4 for virgin PP, 12.1 for one-cycle and 19.7 for five-cycle recyclate. Tensile elongation at break fell to below 10 % in five-cycle samples after only 500 h UV exposure. Depth profiling by micro-ATR showed that oxidation penetrated to at least 200 µm in five-cycle samples versus 80 µm in one-cycle. The results suggest that outdoor durability specifications for recyclate-containing articles should account for prior processing history.

title: Quantifying variability in post-industrial polypropylene recyclate properties across multiple supplier batches: implications for quality specifications
abstract: Fifteen batches of nominally equivalent post-industrial polypropylene recyclate were sourced from four suppliers over a twelve-month period and characterised for MFI, intrinsic viscosity, GPC molecular weight parameters, antioxidant residual content (HPLC), tensile and impact properties, and ash content. Between-batch coefficient of variation for MFI was 31 %, for Mn 27 %, and for notched Charpy impact strength 38 %, values substantially larger than within-batch variability (typically below 5 %). Cluster analysis grouped the 15 batches into three distinct quality tiers primarily differentiated by antioxidant content and Mn. Ash content varied from 0.12 % to 0.89 %, reflecting inconsistent removal of inorganic fillers from source material. The study highlights that existing industry specifications based on MFI alone are insufficient to capture the property variability encountered in practice and suggests a minimum set of four complementary measurements.

title: Stabiliser re-dosing strategies for post-industrial polypropylene recyclate: comparison of phenolic, phosphite and combined antioxidant systems
abstract: Post-industrial polypropylene recyclate depleted of primary antioxidant (OIT below 5 min) was re-stabilised by addition of a hindered phenolic antioxidant (0.1 and 0.2 wt %), a phosphite co-stabiliser (0.05 and 0.1 wt %), and their combination, prior to a further three extrusion cycles. OIT recovery was most effective with the combined system at 0.2 + 0.1 wt %, restoring OIT to 29 min after the first re-stabilised cycle compared to 11 min for phenolic alone and 8 min for phosphite alone. Carbonyl index increase per cycle was reduced threefold with the combined system. MFI stabilisation was partial: MFI rose from 9.1 to 12.4 g/10 min over three cycles with combined re-stabilisation versus from 9.1 to 17.9 g/10 min without additives, indicating that chain scission control was improved but not eliminated. Colour recovery was negligible regardless of stabiliser strategy.

title: Effect of winter chilling accumulation on gibberellin GA₁ and GA₄ levels at bud break in three sweet cherry cultivars
abstract: Insufficient chilling during winter is increasingly reported in the Pannonian Basin and is suspected to delay or desynchronise bud burst in sweet cherry. This study quantified gibberellins GA₁ and GA₄ in dormant buds of 'Hedelfingen', 'Regina', and 'Kordia' sweet cherry trees at three experimental sites in Vojvodina across four seasons (2010–2014). Chilling was recorded as chill portions (CP) using the Dynamic Model. At bud break, GA₄ concentrations were positively correlated with accumulated CP (r = 0.81), while GA₁ showed weaker correlation (r = 0.58). Seasons with fewer than 40 CP produced bud break delays of 6–12 days and GA₄ values roughly 30% lower than in adequately chilled seasons. Hormone extraction used methanol-based protocols followed by immunoaffinity clean-up and LC-MS/MS quantification. The data indicate that GA₄, rather than GA₁, is the principal gibberellin associated with chilling-dependent dormancy release in these cultivars under Vojvodina conditions.

title: Cytokinin profiles in sweet cherry buds from endo- to ecodormancy: a seasonal study
abstract: Although cytokinins are implicated in meristematic reactivation, their seasonal dynamics in sweet cherry buds have received less attention than those of ABA and gibberellins. Bud samples from 'Kordia' trees at the University of Ljubljana experimental orchard were collected at fortnightly intervals between October and March over two seasons (2015–2016). Trans-zeatin (tZ), tZ riboside, isopentenyl adenine (iP), and iP riboside were separated and quantified using UPLC-MS/MS. Total cytokinin content dropped sharply in November (by approximately 60% relative to October) and began recovering only after the accumulation of 35–45 chill portions in both seasons. Immunolocalisation on bud sections confirmed cytokinin presence in procambial cells during ecodormancy. Free tZ was the dominant form throughout the season, comprising 55–65% of total cytokinin. These results are consistent with a model in which cytokinin recovery signals the shift from endo- to ecodormancy and may interact with GA signalling to enable bud burst.

title: Transcription factors associated with ABA catabolism during sweet cherry dormancy release: a candidate gene survey
abstract: The enzymatic degradation of ABA in Prunus avium buds is regulated in part by CYP707A-family cytochrome P450 genes, whose expression is poorly characterised in cherry. Using bud RNA extracted at four dormancy stages (para-, endo-, eco-dormancy, and bud burst) from 'Regina' trees over two field seasons, we assessed transcript abundance of PavCYP707A1 and PavCYP707A3 by RT-qPCR. Both transcripts were undetectable during paradormancy and early endodormancy. PavCYP707A1 expression rose 12-fold between deep endodormancy and ecodormancy (p < 0.001), while PavCYP707A3 peaked sharply at bud burst (18-fold induction). Correlation of PavCYP707A1 transcript level with measured ABA decline was r = 0.87 across time points. Co-expression analysis with gibberellin 20-oxidase genes suggested partial regulatory overlap. These results provide molecular evidence for the enzymatic basis of ABA removal during natural dormancy release and identify PavCYP707A1 as a marker candidate for early detection of dormancy progression.

title: Warming winters and sweet cherry phenology in Vojvodina: a 20-year observational dataset
abstract: Long-term phenological records are needed to assess how changing winter temperatures affect bud burst timing in perennial fruit crops. We compiled a 20-year dataset (2001–2021) of bud burst dates and meteorological variables for 'Hedelfingen' and 'Kordia' sweet cherry from five commercial orchards distributed across the Vojvodina plain. Bud burst advanced by an average of 5.3 days per decade in 'Kordia' and 4.1 days per decade in 'Hedelfingen', consistent with reduced chilling accumulation (mean CP decrease of 4.2 per decade). Seasons with fewer than 38 CP showed significantly higher incidence of frost damage after bud burst due to the mismatch between advanced flowering and unchanged late-frost probability. The dataset is made publicly available and includes daily maximum and minimum temperatures, precipitation, and chill portion accumulation calculated by the Dynamic Model. The analysis uses standard linear mixed models with orchard as a random effect.

title: Interaction between hydrogen cyanamide and endogenous ABA/GA balance during forced bud break in sweet cherry: a time-course analysis
abstract: Hydrogen cyanamide (HC) is used commercially to compensate for insufficient chilling in sweet cherry, yet the sequence of hormonal changes it triggers is incompletely described. This study followed ABA, GA₄, tZ, and hydrogen peroxide levels in 'Kordia' buds at 0, 24, 48, 72, and 120 hours after HC application (2% v/v) under field conditions at Rimski Šančevi during the low-chill winter of 2022–23. ABA concentrations fell significantly within 48 hours (mean decrease 42%), while GA₄ began rising only after 72 hours, suggesting ABA removal precedes gibberellin accumulation. Catalase and peroxidase activities increased within 24 hours, consistent with an oxidative intermediate step. Comparative untreated buds showed no significant ABA change over the same period. These data describe the hormonal sequence triggered by HC and may assist the development of safer substitutes that mimic the same sequence using non-toxic elicitors.

title: Pouzdanost između procenjivača u kodiranju odbrambenih mehanizama primenom Skale odbrambenog funkcionisanja: pilot studija na kliničkom uzorku iz Srbije
abstract: Studija je ispitivala pouzdanost između procenjivača (IRR) pri primeni adaptirane verzije Skale odbrambenog funkcionisanja (SDF) na kliničkom uzorku od 48 pacijenata psihijatrijske ambulante u Novom Sadu. Dva nezavisna procenjivača kodirala su transkripcije polustrukturisanih kliničkih intervjua. Primenom Cohenovog kapa koeficijenta i intraklasnih korelacionih koeficijenata (ICC), utvrđena je umerena do dobra saglasnost za kategorije neurotiočnih i grandioznih odbrana (κ = 0.54–0.68), dok je saglasnost za primitive odbrane bila niža (κ = 0.38). Analiza izvora neslaganja pokazala je da najznačajniji doprinos varijabilnosti ima nejednak nivo kliničkog iskustva procenjivača. Rezultati ukazuju na neophodnost standardizovanih trening protokola pre primene instrumenta u istraživačke svrhe. Implikacije za dalji razvoj kodnog priručnika diskutovane su u svetlu sličnih nalaza iz evropskog konteksta.

title: Operationalising Object Relations in Structured Case Formulation: A Comparison of Three Coding Systems
abstract: This study compared the psychometric properties of three structured coding systems for object relations constructs—the Social Cognition and Object Relations Scale (SCORS), the Object Relations Inventory (ORI), and the Bell Object Relations Inventory (BORI)—applied to a sample of 72 outpatients from two psychiatric centres in Serbia and Croatia. Independent raters (n = 6) coded verbatim interview transcripts and Thematic Apperception Test (TAT) narratives. Intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.42 to 0.79 across systems and subscales. SCORS showed the highest reliability for complexity of representations (ICC = 0.79) and affect tone (ICC = 0.73). Structural equation modelling indicated that the three instruments loaded onto a common latent factor of object relations maturity (CFI = 0.94, RMSEA = 0.06), but each retained unique variance. Practical guidance for choosing among systems in low-resource clinical research settings is provided.

abstract: U radu je opisan proces razvoja srpske verzije priručnika za kodiranje odbrambenih mehanizama u narativnim kliničkim intervjuima (PKODNI), uključujući prevod, adaptaciju i pilotiranje na uzorku od 30 intervjua sa pacijentima neurotiočnih i graničnih poremećaja ličnosti. Inter-rater reliability merena ICC-om iznosila je prosečno 0.64 za ukupni nivo odbrambenog funkcionisanja. title: Training Effects on Inter-Rater Agreement in Psychodynamic Case Formulation: A Controlled Study with Trainee Clinicians
abstract: This study examined whether a structured six-session training protocol improved inter-rater agreement (IRA) on psychodynamic case formulations among trainee clinicians. Forty-four master's-level psychology students were randomly assigned to a training group (n = 22) or a waiting-list control group (n = 22). Both groups rated eight standardised case vignettes at pre- and post-training time points using a formulation rating scale covering conflict themes, developmental history integration, and defence level. The training group showed statistically significant gains in ICC values from pre- to post-training (mean ICC increase: 0.24, p < 0.001), whereas the control group showed no significant change. Gains were largest for the conflict themes subscale (Δ ICC = 0.31) and smallest for the developmental integration subscale (Δ ICC = 0.14). These findings suggest that structured training meaningfully narrows rater variability and that formulation components vary in their trainability.

title: Defence Mechanism Profiles in Depressive versus Anxiety Disorders: Coding Reliability and Clinical Differentiation
abstract: The study investigated whether defence mechanism profiles reliably differentiate patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) from those with generalised anxiety disorder (GAD), using the Psychodynamic Defence Coding Manual (PDCM). A sample of 94 outpatients (MDD n = 48, GAD n = 46) from three Serbian psychiatric outpatient clinics was recruited. Two trained raters independently coded transcripts of 60-minute semi-structured clinical interviews. Inter-rater agreement was acceptable to good across all defence categories (ICC range: 0.61–0.81). Patients with MDD showed significantly higher rates of introjection and turning against the self compared to GAD patients (p < 0.01), while GAD patients showed more frequent use of intellectualisation and isolation of affect (p < 0.05). Discriminant function analysis correctly classified 74.5% of cases. These findings support the clinical discriminant validity of structured defence coding and its potential utility in differential diagnosis.

title: Factorial Structure of a Revised Object Relations Rating Scale Applied to Psychotherapy Session Transcripts
abstract: This paper reports the factorial structure of the revised Object Relations Clinical Rating Scale (ORCRS-R), a 28-item instrument designed for use with psychotherapy session transcripts. The scale was applied to 180 transcripts drawn from 40 ongoing psychodynamic psychotherapy cases at a university outpatient clinic in Novi Sad. Confirmatory factor analysis tested a four-factor model (quality of representations, affect regulation, interpersonal motivation, and boundary regulation) against an exploratory two-factor solution. The four-factor model provided an acceptable fit (CFI = 0.91, RMSEA = 0.07, SRMR = 0.08). Inter-rater reliability across all sessions (n = 36 randomly selected transcripts, two raters) yielded ICC values of 0.66–0.82. The affect regulation subscale showed the lowest internal consistency (α = 0.58), suggesting that further item revision is warranted. Normative data from the outpatient sample are provided.

title: Cross-Cultural Stability of Defence Mechanism Coding: A Comparison of Raters from Serbia, Austria, and the Netherlands
abstract: This multi-site study examined whether defence mechanism coding using the Psychodynamic Defence Coding Manual (PDCM) yields stable inter-rater agreement across raters trained in different cultural and clinical traditions. Eighteen raters (six per site: Novi Sad, Vienna, Amsterdam) independently coded 24 identical interview transcripts translated into each rater's working language and also in the original Serbian. All raters participated in a standardised three-day training workshop before coding. Mean ICC across all raters and all transcripts was 0.69 (range: 0.54–0.83). A two-way mixed ANOVA found no significant main effect of cultural site on overall IRA (F(2, 15) = 1.83, p = 0.19), but a significant interaction between site and defence level category was observed, driven by lower agreement among Dutch raters on splitting and projective identification (ICC = 0.54 vs. 0.71–0.74 for Serbian and Austrian raters). Possible explanations related to training emphasis and conceptual translation are discussed.

title: Pouzdanost strukturisane psihodinamske formulacije kod adolescenata: primena PKODNI na uzorku adolescentnih pacijenata psihijatrijske dnevne bolnice
abstract: Studija je ispitivala da li je Priručnik za kodiranje odbrambenih mehanizama u narativnim intervjuima (PKODNI), razvijen prvobitno za odraslu populaciju, pouzdan i validan pri primeni na adolescentnom kliničkom uzorku. Uzorkom je obuhvaćeno 56 adolescenata (uzrast 14–18 godina) koji su bili na tretmanu u dnevnoj bolnici psihijatrije Kliničkog centra Vojvodine. Dva procenjivača kodirala su polustrukturisane intervjue uz korekciju priručnika za razvojne norme. Inter-rater agreement merena ICC-om iznosila je prosečno 0.63 (raspon 0.47–0.76), što je neznatno niže nego u odraslim uzorcima. Najniža saglasnost utvrđena je za kodiranje sublimacije i humor odbrana, što autori dovode u vezu sa razvojno uslovljenom nejasnošću ekspresije ovih mehanizama u adolescenciji. Predlažu se modifikacije kodnog priručnika prilagođene razvojnom kontekstu.

title: Automated Text-Based Pre-Coding of Defence Mechanisms: Testing a Dictionary Approach Against Human Raters
abstract: This study tested whether a rule-based dictionary approach to automatic text coding could approximate human rater judgements of defence mechanism use in clinical interview transcripts. A lexical dictionary was constructed from the Psychodynamic Defence Coding Manual (PDCM), covering 22 defence mechanisms with associated linguistic markers. The dictionary was applied to 112 interview transcripts previously coded by trained human raters. Agreement between automated and human coding was evaluated using percentage agreement, Cohen's kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha. Automated coding achieved acceptable agreement for mature defences such as humour (κ = 0.61) and intellectualisation (κ = 0.58), but showed poor agreement for primitive defences such as splitting (κ = 0.27) and projective identification (κ = 0.19), which rely heavily on contextual and relational inference beyond the reach of dictionary methods. The findings delineate the boundary conditions of text-automated approaches and suggest that hybrid human-automated pipelines should focus automation on the more linguistically transparent defence categories.

title: Estimating above-ground biomass of European hornbeam (Carpinus betulus) using voxel-based structural metrics derived from airborne laser scanning
abstract: Above-ground biomass (AGB) of European hornbeam was estimated at the individual-tree level using structural metrics extracted from airborne LiDAR point clouds acquired over 1,840 ha of managed broadleaf forest on Fruška Gora, Serbia, in leaf-on conditions. After individual tree segmentation, 22 voxel-based metrics were computed per tree segment, including filled-voxel count, height percentiles, canopy relief ratio, and vertical complexity index. A random forest regression model was trained on a calibration dataset of 94 destructively sampled trees, for which dry biomass had been measured following standard allometric protocols. Cross-validated root mean square error was 38.4 kg per tree (relative RMSE 19.7%), and R² reached 0.83. Model performance degraded for trees with crown volumes below 15 m³, likely due to segmentation boundary errors. Spatial AGB maps at 10 m resolution were produced and compared with national forest inventory plot estimates, showing a mean relative difference of 12.1% at the stand level. The approach offers a scalable alternative to species-specific allometric equations where ground-truth biomass data are limited.

title: Hyperspectral identification of dust mineralogy on photovoltaic surfaces using airborne HyMap imagery
abstract: The spectral contrast between soiled and clean PV glass varies with dust mineralogy, which affects both the magnitude of reflectance increase and the wavelength of maximum contrast. HyMap airborne hyperspectral imagery (126 bands, 400–2500 nm, 4 m GSD) was acquired over a 5 MW test array in Srem during a dust event in June 2019. Panel-level spectra were extracted and decomposed by spectral mixture analysis using endmembers derived from the USGS spectral library augmented with locally collected samples. Three mineralogical classes were separable: carbonate-rich agricultural dust (dominant, covering 68% of panels), siliceous road dust (19%), and iron-oxide-bearing industrial particulates (13%). Panels dominated by iron-oxide dust showed 40% higher reflectance in the 650–750 nm range per unit deposition mass than carbonate-dominated panels. The classification explained 12 percentage points more variance in gravimetric soiling than a single-mineral assumption. Mineralogical maps produced from HyMap data could refine mass-to-reflectance conversion factors used in satellite-based soiling retrieval.

title: Soil Moisture Influence on GPR Hyperbola Geometry: A Controlled Field Experiment
abstract: Variations in soil moisture alter the effective dielectric permittivity and consequently change the curvature of hyperbolic reflections in GPR B-scans, complicating automated depth estimation. This paper reports a controlled experiment in which three PVC pipes and two steel pipes were buried at known depths (0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 m) in a 6 × 4 m test plot. GPR surveys at 500 MHz were conducted on 11 dates over nine months, spanning volumetric soil moisture values from 0.08 to 0.38 m³/m³ measured with TDR sensors. Hyperbola apex depth estimates derived from fitted curvature increased by a mean of 0.07 m as soil moisture rose from dry to saturated conditions when using a fixed assumed permittivity. A simple correction procedure using a single TDR measurement at 0.3 m depth reduced this bias to below 0.02 m. Implications for automated pipeline-depth estimation in operational surveys are discussed.

title: Spatial Typology of IMS and Large-Panel System Blocks in Novi Sad: A Morphological Survey
abstract: This paper presents a systematic morphological survey of 214 prefabricated residential blocks built in Novi Sad between 1960 and 1985, classified by construction system (IMS skeletal frame and three large-panel variants), storey count, and site layout. Field measurements and archival drawings from the City of Novi Sad Urban Planning Institute were cross-referenced to produce a georeferenced typology database. The survey identified seven recurring block types, of which two account for 61 percent of the total floor area. Courtyard configurations, entrance spacing, and ground-floor activation potential were recorded as variables relevant to future retrofit planning. The paper argues that any city-wide adaptive reuse strategy must begin with this kind of disaggregated physical inventory rather than treating the panel-block stock as a homogeneous category. The database has been made available to the Faculty of Technical Sciences GIS laboratory and is intended as a baseline for subsequent studies.

title: Post-Occupancy Conditions in Zrenjanin Panel Blocks: Structural Decay, Energy Loss, and Resident Perception
abstract: This study investigates post-occupancy conditions in a cluster of 38 residential blocks in the Bagljaševo settlement of Zrenjanin, constructed under the Jugomont large-panel system between 1968 and 1974. The research combined on-site structural inspection records obtained from the municipal housing authority, blower-door tests on 12 representative apartments, and a structured questionnaire administered to 203 resident households. Thermal bridging at panel joints and inadequate window replacement were identified as the primary sources of heat loss, with average measured U-values for external walls ranging from 1.4 to 1.9 W/m²K. Resident satisfaction scores correlated negatively with storey level and positively with length of residence, suggesting habituation effects. Eighty-two percent of respondents indicated willingness to contribute financially to envelope improvements if monthly savings could be demonstrated in advance. The paper draws on these findings to outline minimum-information requirements for community-facing retrofit communication.

title: Ground-Floor Activation as an Entry Point for Adaptive Reuse: Lessons from Three Vojvodinian Towns
abstract: Ground floors of socialist-era panel blocks in Vojvodina were commonly left as unheated storage or bicycle cellars, later informally colonised for small-scale commerce or sealed entirely. This paper examines ground-floor transformation trajectories in panel settlements in Sombor, Kikinda, and Vrbas through a combination of sequential aerial photograph analysis (1985–2018), on-site observation of 67 blocks, and 24 semi-structured interviews with local housing managers and shopkeepers. Three transformation pathways are described: organic informalisation, municipally directed conversion, and neglect-and-abandonment. Organic informalisation produced the widest variety of uses but also the highest rate of subsequent closure due to poor thermal and acoustic conditions. The paper argues that formalising and thermally upgrading ground-floor spaces offers a low-disruption first step toward broader adaptive reuse that can generate rental income to cross-subsidise upper-floor improvements. A simple area-based financial model is presented for each of the three towns.

title: Tenant Participation Models in Central European Panel-Block Retrofit Programmes: A Comparative Review
abstract: This chapter reviews tenant participation structures used in state-supported retrofit programmes for prefabricated residential blocks in Hungary, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic between 2002 and 2018, drawing on programme documentation, evaluation reports, and eight practitioner interviews conducted during research visits to Budapest, Bratislava, and Brno. The review focuses on decision thresholds (the share of resident consent required to initiate works), information provision formats, financial incentive structures, and complaint and opt-out mechanisms. Hungarian programmes required 75 percent owner consent; Slovak programmes initially set the threshold at 51 percent before raising it in 2011. The chapter assesses how these choices affected uptake speed, litigation rates, and resident satisfaction in post-completion surveys. Findings are framed against the institutional context of Serbian condominium law, which currently lacks a comparable mandatory consent mechanism, and implications for potential Serbian programme design are outlined.
