title: Evaluating a Deliberative Workshop Format for Retrofit Decision-Making in a Subotica Panel Block
abstract: This paper reports on the design and evaluation of a structured deliberative workshop process piloted in a single twelve-storey block in Subotica's Prozivka settlement. Forty-one of the building's 48 owner-households participated across three two-hour sessions held between October and December 2019. Sessions used scaled physical models, simplified energy-cost scenario cards, and a ranked-choice preference tool developed for the study. A trained facilitator guided discussions on four retrofit packages ranging from basic insulation to full envelope and stairwell redesign. Preference convergence was measured by comparing initial and post-session rankings. Agreement on the second-highest cost package was reached by 78 percent of participants after the third session, compared to an initial split across all four options. Facilitator observation notes and post-workshop questionnaires are analysed to identify the discussion dynamics that drove convergence. The paper identifies time constraints, tenure insecurity, and distrust of contractors as the main remaining barriers.

title: Prefabricated Block Demolition vs. Retrofit in Shrinking Mid-Sized Cities: A Cost-Effectiveness Comparison for Kikinda and Sombor
abstract: A subset of Vojvodinian cities with declining populations has begun to consider selective demolition of the worst-performing panel blocks rather than retrofit. This paper compares the life-cycle costs and social displacement consequences of demolition-and-replacement versus deep retrofit for matched pairs of blocks in Kikinda and Sombor, using a 40-year assessment period. Construction cost data were obtained from recent municipal tenders; energy baselines were established from utility billing records for 220 apartments. Under current Serbian energy prices, deep retrofit of blocks in adequate structural condition produces a lower net present cost than demolition and replacement in both cities, with payback periods of 17–22 years. Social cost estimates, based on temporary relocation expenses and household survey data on attachment to place, add 8–14 percent to demolition scenario costs. The paper notes that these results are sensitive to assumptions about future energy prices and subsidy availability and provides a scenario table for three price trajectories.

title: Accessibility Deficits in Panel-Block Staircases and Entry Sequences: Survey Results from Novi Sad and Vršac
abstract: Socialist-era panel blocks in Serbia were designed without provisions for wheelchair access or other mobility accommodations, and elevator retrofits have been installed in a small and geographically uneven fraction of the stock. This paper presents results of an accessibility audit of 89 blocks in Novi Sad and 34 in Vršac, using a 23-item checklist adapted from European standard EN 17210. Entry sequences, staircase geometry, lift availability, and approach path conditions were recorded. Elevators were present in only 14 percent of audited blocks in Vršac and 31 percent in Novi Sad. Step heights at building entries exceeded accessible thresholds in 78 percent of cases where no ramp was present. Cross-tabulation with municipal disability registration data suggests that approximately 340 registered mobility-impaired residents in the two cities live in blocks with no lift and an inaccessible entry. The paper discusses integration of accessibility works into broader adaptive reuse planning as a mechanism for accessing EU cohesion funding streams.

title: Digital Documentation Workflows for Panel-Block Retrofit Planning: Testing Photogrammetry and Low-Cost Thermal Imaging in Sremska Mitrovica
abstract: Accurate as-built documentation of panel blocks is often absent or outdated, complicating retrofit design. This paper reports on a documentation workflow tested on six blocks in the Staro Sajmište settlement in Sremska Mitrovica. The workflow combined close-range photogrammetry using a consumer-grade mirrorless camera, point-cloud processing in open-source software, and thermal imaging using a mid-range uncooled microbolometer camera borrowed from the Faculty's shared equipment pool. Photogrammetric point clouds achieved a mean deviation from manual tape measurements of 18 mm, sufficient for preliminary retrofit design but not for structural calculation. Thermal imaging was conducted over four nights in January 2024 under stable outdoor conditions and identified panel joint thermal bridges consistent with prior intrusive surveys. The paper provides a time-and-cost breakdown: the full six-block documentation required 38 person-hours and approximately 1,200 EUR in consumables and equipment rental. A comparison with conventional measured drawing methods for the same blocks, available from a 2019 municipal survey, shows a 44 percent reduction in time.

title: Mapping Informal Retrofit Interventions in Novi Sad Panel Settlements: Extent, Typology, and Planning Implications
abstract: Residents of panel blocks across Serbia routinely carry out unsanctioned physical interventions including window replacement, balcony enclosure, satellite dish mounting, and air-conditioning unit installation. This paper systematically maps such interventions across 156 blocks in four Novi Sad settlements (Detelinara, Grbavica, Liman III, and Telep) using street-level photography collected in 2024 and coded against a 14-category scheme. Balcony enclosure and window replacement were the most frequent interventions, present in 74 and 68 percent of blocks respectively. Installation density varied by settlement and by block age, with older blocks showing higher rates. The paper assesses the cumulative thermal and structural consequences of the most prevalent interventions using simplified calculation models. It argues that informal retrofit activity represents latent investment capacity that coordinated adaptive reuse programmes could channel toward structurally and thermally effective outcomes, and discusses regulatory reform options under Serbian construction law.

title: Parental Education and Gymnasium Entry in Novi Sad: A Logistic Regression Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between parental educational attainment and the probability of children enrolling in gymnasium-track secondary schools in Novi Sad. Using survey data collected from 412 eighth-grade students and their parents across six primary schools in the 2009–2010 school year, the analysis applies binary logistic regression to estimate the net effect of parental education after controlling for the child's primary school grade point average. Results indicate that children with at least one parent holding a university degree are 3.4 times more likely to apply to a gymnasium than children from households where neither parent completed secondary education, even when academic performance is held constant. The findings suggest that parental educational background exerts an independent influence on track choice beyond merit-based criteria, consistent with reproduction theory. The paper discusses implications for admissions policy in Serbian secondary schools.

title: Cultural Consumption Practices and Track Aspirations among Serbian Urban Adolescents
abstract: Drawing on Bourdieu's concept of cultural capital, this paper examines whether adolescents' participation in highbrow cultural activities—museum visits, classical music attendance, reading habits—predicts their aspiration to attend a gymnasium as opposed to a vocational school. The dataset consists of questionnaires administered to 638 seventh- and eighth-grade pupils in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin during 2011. A composite cultural capital index was constructed from eleven activity items, and ordinal logistic regression was used to model track aspiration. Higher cultural capital scores were associated with significantly elevated gymnasium aspirations (OR = 2.1, 95% CI: 1.6–2.8), net of academic grades and parental occupational class. The paper also reports that the cultural capital effect is stronger for girls than for boys, a pattern tentatively attributed to differential socialization within households. Policy implications for extracurricular provision in under-resourced urban schools are discussed.

title: Social Reproduction in Post-Socialist Serbia: Educational Pathways Across Three Cohorts
abstract: This book chapter situates Serbian secondary-track differentiation within the broader trajectory of post-socialist transformation. Comparing retrospective survey data from three birth cohorts (born 1960–1969, 1975–1984, and 1990–1999) collected in Novi Sad households, the chapter traces whether the strength of the association between parental social class and gymnasium attendance has changed across periods corresponding to late socialism, early transition, and consolidated market conditions. Results from log-linear modelling show that the class–track association weakened modestly during the 1990s but rebounded to near-socialist levels by the early 2000s. The chapter argues that the brief period of weakening reflects disruption of elite reproduction strategies during economic crisis rather than structural equalisation, and that the subsequent rebound followed the stabilisation of private tutoring markets and gymnasium admissions competition. The findings are compared with parallel analyses for Hungary and Croatia.

title: Private Tutoring as a Mechanism of Privilege Transmission: Evidence from Novi Sad Primary Schools
abstract: Private tutoring ahead of the secondary-school admissions examination has expanded markedly in Serbian cities since the early 2000s. This paper uses survey data from 501 families in Novi Sad collected in spring 2014 to estimate the prevalence, cost, and social distribution of pre-entry tutoring. Approximately 61 percent of gymnasium applicants in the sample received private tutoring, compared with 19 percent of vocational applicants. Multinomial logistic regression shows that tutoring uptake is strongly predicted by parental income and parental own gymnasium or university attendance, while controlling for the child's prior grades. A mediation analysis suggests that roughly 28 percent of the parental education effect on gymnasium placement operates through tutoring. The paper concludes that informal educational markets serve as a channel through which economically and culturally privileged families convert advantage into examination performance and selective school access.

title: Teachers' Track Recommendations and Family Social Position in Serbian Middle Schools
abstract: In many Serbian primary schools, class teachers informally advise families on secondary-school options before the formal admissions process begins. This qualitative-quantitative mixed-methods study explores whether teachers systematically recommend gymnasium to children from higher social strata. The quantitative component uses administrative records from four Novi Sad primary schools (N = 1,102 pupils completing eighth grade between 2012 and 2015), linking teacher recommendation codes to family background data obtained via parental survey. The qualitative component includes semi-structured interviews with 24 teachers. Analysis shows that children from professional-class families were 2.7 times more likely to receive gymnasium recommendations than children from working-class families with equivalent grade records. Interview data reveal that teachers make implicit judgements about family commitment and 'future orientation' that systematically favour middle-class families. The paper contributes to understanding how institutional actors reproduce stratification.

title: Ethnic and Class Intersections in Secondary-Track Placement: Hungarian-Minority Families in Vojvodina
abstract: This paper examines how ethnicity and social class jointly shape gymnasium enrolment among Hungarian-minority families in Vojvodina, using data from a two-wave panel survey of 348 families conducted in 2014 and 2017. Interaction-term regression models show that the class gradient in gymnasium placement is steeper among ethnic Hungarian families than among Serbian families in the same region, a pattern that persists after controlling for school district, parental cultural capital, and language of instruction preference. Qualitative interviews with 18 Hungarian-minority parents suggest that gymnasium enrolment in Hungarian-language sections is perceived as a strategy for maintaining ethnic identity alongside class mobility, motivating higher-than-average investment at all class levels. The paper argues for intersectional analytic frameworks in the study of educational stratification in multiethnic regions.

title: Does Track Placement at 14 Determine Occupational Outcomes at 30? A Retrospective Survey in Novi Sad
abstract: This paper uses a retrospective life-course survey administered to 620 adults aged 28–34 in Novi Sad in 2018 to trace the pathway from secondary-school track to labour market outcomes. Structural equation modelling links family background at age 14 to track placement, then to tertiary education attainment, and finally to occupational status measured by the ISEI scale at approximate age 30. Results show that gymnasium placement mediates approximately 44 percent of the parental class effect on adult ISEI scores. Direct effects of parental class on adult occupational status remain significant even after accounting for the gymnasium pathway, indicating multiple transmission channels. The paper also reports substantial gender differences: the mediation proportion through gymnasium is larger for women than for men, partly because women's occupational destinations are more tightly linked to tertiary credentials.

title: Comparing Track Allocation Systems in Serbia and Romania: Institutional Rules and Inequality Outcomes
abstract: Serbia and Romania both use a points-based centralised admissions system to allocate eighth-grade pupils to secondary-school tracks, yet the systems differ in weighting of school grades versus standardised examination scores. This comparative paper uses nationally representative survey data from Serbia (N = 2,140) and Romania (N = 1,980), both from national school surveys conducted around 2016–2017, to estimate social background effects on gymnasium placement under each system. Blinder–Oaxaca decomposition is applied to assess how much of the cross-country difference in the class–track gap is attributable to compositional versus institutional factors. Results suggest that the higher weight of standardised tests in Romania is associated with a modestly smaller parental education effect compared with Serbia, where school grades—more susceptible to teacher judgement—carry greater weight. The paper discusses implications for admissions reform.

title: Home Reading Environment and Early Literacy as Predictors of Later Track Placement: Longitudinal Evidence from Novi Sad
abstract: This paper presents findings from a prospective longitudinal design in which 310 children were first surveyed through their parents at age 7 (in 2010) and followed up at age 15 (in 2018) to assess secondary-school track. The home reading environment at age 7—measured by number of books in the household, frequency of parental reading aloud, and library membership—was used as an early indicator of embodied cultural capital. Logistic regression shows that each standard deviation increase in the home reading score at age 7 is associated with a 1.5 times higher odds of gymnasium placement at age 15, controlling for parental education and income. The association is partially but not fully mediated by fourth-grade literacy test scores collected at an intermediate wave. The longitudinal design allows stronger causal inference than cross-sectional studies and supports early intervention arguments.

title: Secondary-School Track Sorting and Neighbourhood Segregation in Novi Sad: A Spatial Analysis
abstract: This paper asks whether residential segregation by social class in Novi Sad reinforces educational stratification by concentrating disadvantaged pupils in catchment areas predominantly served by vocational schools. Using geocoded pupil administrative records for all eighth-grade completers in Novi Sad between 2015 and 2020 (N ≈ 8,400), combined with census block-level socioeconomic indicators, multilevel logistic regression models are estimated with pupils nested in census blocks and primary schools. Between-neighbourhood variance in gymnasium placement rates remains statistically significant (ICC = 0.11) after accounting for individual family background. Spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.38) confirms clustering of low gymnasium-placement primary schools in historically working-class and Roma-majority neighbourhoods in the southern and eastern parts of the city. The paper argues for policy attention to geographic dimensions of educational inequality alongside family-level interventions.

title: Parental Cultural Capital and Digital Learning Resources: Track Placement During and After the COVID-19 School Closures
abstract: School closures in Serbia from March to June 2020 shifted instruction to online platforms, creating conditions under which household digital resources and parental capacity to support learning became acutely relevant. This paper uses a survey of 487 Novi Sad families conducted in autumn 2020, shortly before pupils submitted gymnasium applications, to examine whether parental cultural capital moderated the effect of digital resource availability on subsequent track placement. Interaction models show that the gap in gymnasium placement between high- and low-cultural-capital families widened compared with a historical 2018 baseline cohort from the same schools. Families with low cultural capital and inadequate digital access had gymnasium placement rates roughly 14 percentage points below the pre-pandemic baseline. The paper contributes to emerging literature on pandemic-amplified inequalities in compulsory education.

title: Class Reproduction Through Extra-Curricular Activity: Piano Lessons, Sports Clubs, and Gymnasium Enrolment in Three Serbian Cities
abstract: This paper examines whether participation in structured extra-curricular activities—specifically music lessons and organised sports—functions as an institutionalised form of cultural capital investment that predicts gymnasium enrolment. Using a cross-sectional survey of 1,104 families in Novi Sad, Niš, and Kragujevac conducted in 2023, the study distinguishes between 'highbrow' activities (instrument lessons, classical dance, chess) and 'general' sports and crafts. After controlling for parental education, income, and the child's academic marks, participation in at least two highbrow extra-curricular activities is associated with a 1.9-fold increase in gymnasium enrolment odds. Mediation analysis attributes roughly one-third of this association to higher admissions examination scores among participants. Highbrow activity participation itself is strongly predicted by parental occupational class, with a clearly stepwise gradient. City-level differences are modest. The results are broadly consistent with concerted cultivation theory.

title: Viscosity and Yield Stress Characterisation of Silver-Flake Screen-Printing Pastes at Varying Shear Rates
abstract: This study examines the rheological behaviour of four commercially prepared silver-flake pastes used in screen-printed electrical contacts on glass substrates. Steady-state flow curves were collected using a cone-and-plate geometry at shear rates ranging from 0.01 to 1000 s⁻¹ on a Malvern Kinexus rotational rheometer. All pastes exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behaviour well described by the Herschel–Bulkley model, with yield stresses between 18 and 74 Pa and consistency indices between 12 and 63 Pa·sⁿ. Dynamic oscillatory sweeps identified a crossover from elastic to viscous-dominant response at angular frequencies between 1.2 and 4.5 rad/s. Correlation with printed line width and edge definition on FR4 boards showed that pastes with yield stresses above 45 Pa produced lines with a standard deviation in width below 12 µm, compared with 28 µm for the lowest-yield-stress paste. These results support a simple pre-selection criterion based on yield stress for achieving acceptable line definition in fine-pitch applications.

title: Thixotropic Recovery of Carbon-Black Functional Inks After High-Shear Printing Events
abstract: Carbon-black dispersions used as resistive elements in screen-printed heaters undergo intense shear during squeegee passage, followed by rapid deceleration. This work quantifies thixotropic recovery for three carbon-black inks at different pigment loadings (15, 25, and 35 wt%) using a three-interval thixotropy test on a rotational rheometer. High-shear intervals at 500 s⁻¹ for 30 s were followed by low-shear recovery intervals at 0.5 s⁻¹ for 180 s. Recovery half-times ranged from 8 to 47 s depending on loading, with the 35 wt% dispersion requiring over 60 s to reach 90% of its pre-shear complex modulus. On-press measurements using a laboratory screen printer with an inline laser profilometer confirmed that inks with recovery half-times below 15 s produced smoother deposit surfaces (Ra below 0.8 µm) compared with inks requiring longer recovery. The results identify recovery time as a critical parameter for multilayer printing where successive print passes are performed within short intervals.

title: Squeegee Shore Hardness and Attack Angle as Determinants of Paste Pressure Distribution in Screen Printing
abstract: This experimental study investigates how squeegee blade hardness (55, 70, and 85 Shore A polyurethane) and attack angle (60°, 75°, and 90°) jointly affect the hydrodynamic pressure built up ahead of the squeegee blade and the resulting deposit characteristics on soda-lime glass substrates. Pressure was estimated indirectly from deposit thickness maps obtained by white-light interferometry across a 50 × 50 mm print area. A full-factorial design with three replicate prints per condition was employed, yielding 27 experimental conditions. Statistical analysis using two-way ANOVA showed that Shore hardness had a larger main effect on cross-track thickness uniformity than attack angle (F = 28.4 vs. F = 11.2, p < 0.01 in both cases). The 70 Shore A blade at 75° produced the most uniform deposit across the print area, with a coefficient of variation in thickness of 4.1%. Interaction between hardness and angle was statistically significant, suggesting that optimisation of one parameter without fixing the other is unlikely to yield consistent improvements.

title: Deposit Thickness Uniformity in Screen-Printed Silver Electrodes for Organic Photovoltaic Substrates on Borosilicate Glass
abstract: Achieving reproducible electrode thickness below 20 µm dry film with uniformity better than ±1 µm across a 100 × 100 mm substrate area is demanding in research-scale screen printing. This work reports a systematic study varying paste solid content (78, 82, 86 wt% silver), squeegee speed (100–300 mm/s), and post-print drying temperature (100–140 °C) for a single-component silver paste on borosilicate glass. Deposit thickness after drying was measured at 25 fixed points using tactile profilometry. The lowest within-substrate standard deviation of 0.7 µm was achieved at 82 wt% solids, 150 mm/s squeegee speed, and 120 °C drying temperature. Sheet resistance across the electrodes was measured by four-point probe and ranged from 12 to 31 mΩ/sq depending on thickness. Principal component analysis of the 25-point thickness maps revealed a systematic edge-to-centre gradient attributable to the tension distribution in the mesh frame, which persisted across all paste formulations tested.

title: Comparison of Oscillatory and Steady-State Rheological Protocols for Predicting Screen-Printability of Dielectric Inks
abstract: Dielectric inks used between layers in multilayer printed circuits must exhibit sufficient pseudoplasticity for mesh passage while retaining enough elasticity post-deposition to prevent spreading. This paper compares the predictive value of four rheological protocols — steady shear flow curve, amplitude sweep, frequency sweep, and creep-recovery — applied to six commercially available dielectric inks with solid loadings between 40 and 65 wt%. Printability was assessed empirically on a laboratory flatbed printer using a 120-thread/cm mesh, scored against five criteria: fill completeness, edge definition, pin-hole density, surface Ra, and interlayer isolation resistance. Correlation coefficients between individual rheological parameters and composite print quality scores revealed that the loss tangent measured at 1 Hz in the linear viscoelastic region (mean tan δ = 0.38–1.12 across inks) was the single strongest predictor (Pearson r = −0.89). Steady-shear-only characterisation missed three inks that printed poorly despite acceptable viscosity at printing-representative shear rates. The findings support adopting oscillatory characterisation as a standard pre-screening step for dielectric ink qualification.

title: Stencil Aperture Aspect Ratio and Paste Release in Screen Printing of Thick-Film Resistors on Alumina Substrates
abstract: The ratio of aperture width to stencil thickness (aspect ratio) is known to govern paste release in solder paste printing but has been less studied for thick-film resistor pastes on ceramic substrates. This study examines paste transfer efficiency as a function of aperture widths from 100 to 600 µm at a fixed stencil thickness of 100 µm, using three ruthenium-oxide-based resistor pastes with differing rheological profiles. Volume transfer efficiency (VTE) was measured gravimetrically and confirmed by 3D profilometry for 200 printed deposits per condition. A threshold aspect ratio of 1.5 was observed for all three pastes below which VTE dropped sharply (from approximately 85% to below 50%). Above aspect ratio 2.0, VTE plateaued at 85–92% and was primarily determined by paste yield stress rather than aperture dimensions. Fired resistance values measured by a four-wire bridge method showed a 14% coefficient of variation for deposits below the threshold compared with 4% above it. These data are directly applicable to design rules for thick-film hybrid circuits.

title: Temperature Sensitivity of Viscosity in Silver Nanowire Inks Intended for Unheated Substrate Screen Printing
abstract: Silver nanowire (AgNW) inks are of interest for transparent electrodes on rigid glass but their rheological properties at ambient temperatures between 18 and 30 °C, which vary in non-climate-controlled production environments, have not been well characterised. This study measures apparent viscosity at a representative printing shear rate of 200 s⁻¹ for four AgNW inks (wire diameter 35–90 nm, length 10–30 µm, solid loading 0.5–2.0 wt%) across the 18–30 °C range. Viscosity showed a temperature coefficient of −2.1 to −4.8 mPa·s/°C depending on formulation, with the highest-loading ink showing the greatest sensitivity. Printed line resistance measured by four-point probe varied by up to 22% over this temperature range solely due to rheological change, with no modification of electrical sintering conditions. Activation energies calculated from an Arrhenius fit ranged from 14 to 31 kJ/mol. The study recommends temperature control within ±1 °C for quality-sensitive AgNW printing and provides correction factors for process windows.

title: Benchmarking Rheological Characterisation Methods for Conductive Pastes: A Practitioner's Guide for Printing Laboratories
abstract: Laboratories in printed electronics commonly measure paste viscosity with a single-point Brookfield measurement at one rotational speed, which captures neither the shear-rate dependence relevant to squeegee passage nor the elastic recovery relevant to post-print spreading. This book chapter provides a structured comparison of measurement approaches accessible to printing-oriented laboratories: single-point rotational viscometry, multi-point flow curves, amplitude and frequency sweeps, three-interval thixotropy tests, and creep-recovery protocols. For each method the chapter describes equipment requirements, typical measurement durations, data interpretation, and the specific printing phenomena each approach predicts or fails to predict. Representative datasets are provided for a commercial silver paste, a carbon-black resistive ink, and a dielectric paste, all measured on the same rotational rheometer platform. A decision flowchart is included to guide analysts in selecting the minimum characterisation set appropriate for their process control or paste development context. The chapter is aimed at engineers with basic rheological literacy rather than specialist researchers.

title: Spectral upwelling from fluorescent spot inks: measurement strategies and impact on ICC characterisation data
abstract: Fluorescent spot inks are used extensively in security printing, toy packaging, and promotional materials, but their emission component causes conventional spectrophotometers operating without UV excitation control to record anomalously high reflectance values that corrupt ICC characterisation data. This study examined four fluorescent ink formulations — two yellow, one orange, one pink — printed on coated board at nominal ink densities of 0.9, 1.2, and 1.5. Measurements were collected under three UV conditions: full UV, UV-cut, and bispectral measurement using an Optronic OL-750 scanning spectroradiometer. The fluorescent contribution was isolated as the difference between bispectral total radiance and the purely reflective component. Including fluorescent patches in a standard ECI2002 characterisation target without UV handling produced profile errors of up to ΔE2000 9.4 on fluorescent colours and degraded neutral grey accuracy by 1.8 ΔE2000 units through lookup table interpolation artefacts. A workflow isolating fluorescent patches for bespoke spot-colour treatment, while building the process profile from non-fluorescent patches only, is proposed and validated on two commercial packaging jobs.

title: Flavonoid composition of wild elderberry populations from the Vojvodina lowlands: a baseline survey
abstract: A survey of 14 wild-growing Sambucus nigra populations collected from riparian and field-margin sites across Vojvodina was conducted to establish a baseline flavonoid profile. Berry samples were harvested at full maturity over two consecutive seasons (1995–1996) and extracted with acidified methanol. HPLC-DAD analysis resolved seven major flavonoids, with cyanidin-3-glucoside and cyanidin-3-sambubioside accounting for 78–85% of total anthocyanin content across populations. Total polyphenol content ranged from 412 to 891 mg gallic acid equivalents per 100 g fresh weight, with significant inter-population variability. Rutin concentrations varied from 1.2 to 4.7 mg per g dry weight. The data suggested that edaphic factors—particularly soil organic matter and moisture retention—correlated more strongly with polyphenol accumulation than geographic distance between sites. These findings formed the reference dataset for subsequent stress physiology studies by the group.

title: Rutin accumulation in elderberry leaves and inflorescences as a function of altitude and continentality across a Pannonian–Dinaric transect
abstract: Leaves and fresh inflorescences were collected from 22 Sambucus nigra individuals distributed along an elevational and continentality gradient from 80 m a.s.l. in the Vojvodina plain to 780 m in the Fruška Gora foothills. Rutin was quantified by HPLC after enzymatic hydrolysis and direct injection methods. Rutin content in leaves ranged from 6.3 mg g−1 DW at lowland sites to 14.8 mg g−1 DW at foothill sites, while inflorescence rutin ranged from 3.1 to 9.4 mg g−1 DW. Multiple regression analysis attributed 51% of the variance in rutin to mean summer temperature and 22% to soil pH, with altitude itself explaining relatively little once climate variables were included. The study provides empirical data relevant to the sourcing of elderflower raw material for food and nutraceutical processing in the western Balkans region.

title: Proline and malondialdehyde dynamics in elderberry under progressive drought: links to polyphenol upregulation
abstract: To examine oxidative stress markers alongside polyphenol responses, potted plants of accession SN-PAN-04 were exposed to progressive withholding of irrigation until leaf water potential reached −1.2 MPa, then rewatered. Leaf proline content, malondialdehyde (MDA, as an index of lipid peroxidation), hydrogen peroxide, and total anthocyanin content were measured at five time points. Proline increased sixfold by day 14 of water withholding; MDA rose by 2.3-fold at day 14 but returned to near-baseline 72 hours after rewatering. Total anthocyanin in leaves peaked at day 10 (3.1-fold increase over controls) and remained elevated for five days post-rewatering, suggesting that anthocyanin accumulation precedes peak oxidative damage and may serve a photoprotective rather than purely reactive role. The temporal dissociation between MDA and anthocyanin peaks is discussed in relation to reactive oxygen species signalling.

title: Elderberry as a functional ingredient: agronomic and phytochemical requirements for raw material standardisation in the Pannonian region
abstract: This chapter reviews the agronomic management practices, harvest timing, and post-harvest handling procedures that influence the polyphenol content of Sambucus nigra berries destined for food and nutraceutical processing in the Pannonian Basin. Drawing on a decade of experimental data from the Rimski Šančevi common-garden trial and published literature, threshold values for TPC (≥600 mg GAE per 100 g FW) and TAC (≥6 mg CGE per g FW) are proposed as raw material quality criteria. The chapter addresses how irrigation deficit management (targeting −0.1 to −0.3 MPa) can enhance polyphenol accumulation without reducing commercial yield below economically viable thresholds. Considerations for small-scale growers in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania are included, alongside a brief discussion of traceability and certification schemes applicable to nutraceutical ingredients in the EU regulatory framework.

title: Seasonal dynamics of chlorogenic acid in the bark, leaves, and berries of Pannonian elderberry over the vegetative cycle
abstract: Chlorogenic acid (CGA) content was tracked monthly from budbreak to leaf senescence in bark, leaf lamina, and developing berries of accession SN-PAN-02, chosen for its high CGA titre established in earlier work. Samples were collected from 10 individuals at the Rimski Šančevi orchard across two complete vegetative seasons (2010–2011). HPLC quantification revealed that bark contained the highest CGA concentrations in early spring (up to 18.4 mg g−1 DW) and that levels declined progressively as the season advanced. Leaf CGA peaked in June–July (7.2–9.1 mg g−1 DW) and corresponded to periods of maximum irradiance. Berry CGA at full maturity was comparatively low (1.8–3.2 mg g−1 DW) relative to other tissues. The seasonal profile suggests that bark harvested at budbreak represents the most CGA-rich tissue, a finding relevant to valorisation of pruning waste from commercial plantations.

title: Stomatal conductance and polyphenol responses of elderberry to simulated late-summer drought typical of Vojvodina climate projections
abstract: Climate projections for Vojvodina indicate an increased frequency of late-summer (August–September) dry spells by mid-century. To evaluate elderberry's physiological response to this pattern, a controlled experiment subjected accession SN-PAN-04 plants to a 28-day drought imposed during fruit development, mimicking projected conditions (soil water potential reaching −0.45 MPa on day 28). Stomatal conductance measured by a portable porometer declined by 78% relative to irrigated controls by day 21. Despite severe stomatal closure, berry anthocyanin content increased by 27% and rutin by 19% compared with controls, while berry fresh weight fell by 31%. Harvest index modelling suggested that moderate water deficit imposed during the final 14 days of fruit development would optimise the polyphenol-to-yield trade-off. Results are discussed in the context of adapting irrigation scheduling in commercial elderberry cultivation to anticipated climate change in the region.

title: Comparing polyphenol retention in dried elderberry products prepared by three low-temperature methods: relevance for small-scale producers in Vojvodina
abstract: Berries of accession SN-PAN-04 harvested at full maturity were processed by freeze-drying, hot-air drying at 45 °C, and vacuum drying at 40 °C, then stored for 0, 3, 6, and 12 months at 4 °C and 20 °C. TPC, TAC, rutin, and chlorogenic acid were measured at each time point. Freeze-drying retained 91–94% of TPC immediately after drying, compared with 74–78% for hot-air and 83–86% for vacuum methods. After 12 months at 20 °C, anthocyanin retention dropped to 61% in freeze-dried material, 44% in hot-air dried, and 53% in vacuum-dried product. Storage temperature had a larger effect on anthocyanin stability than drying method. For small-scale producers without freeze-drying access, vacuum drying with refrigerated storage was identified as the most practical compromise. The data provide quantitative benchmarks for quality specifications in producer–processor contracts.

title: Linearised hydraulic models for district heating network simulation: accuracy versus computational load
abstract: Accurate simulation of district heating networks requires solving coupled nonlinear hydraulic and thermal equations, which is computationally demanding in real-time control contexts. This paper evaluates three degrees of linearisation applied to the governing flow equations of a benchmark 23-node meshed network representative of mid-sized Eastern European cities. Pipe pressure-drop models are linearised around seasonal operating points derived from one year of measured data from a district heating operator in northern Serbia. Steady-state temperature error, transient overshoot, and computation time are compared across methods using Monte Carlo simulation with 500 demand realisations. A piece-wise affine approximation reduces computation time by 74% relative to the full nonlinear model while keeping maximum nodal temperature error below 0.9 °C in 95% of scenarios. The linearised model is proposed as a suitable prediction model for model predictive control implementations where online re-linearisation can be triggered by a change-detection test on supply pressure. Limitations at very low partial-load operation are discussed.

title: Model predictive control of a district heating substation with time-varying supply temperature setpoints
abstract: District heating operators in continental climates routinely adjust supply water temperature according to outdoor air temperature curves, creating a time-varying input constraint for substation-level controllers. This paper formulates a finite-horizon linear MPC for a single residential substation served by a variable supply temperature network. The prediction model couples a second-order building thermal resistance-capacitance model with a plate heat exchanger model. Setpoint trajectories are treated as measured disturbances provided by the network operator over a two-hour horizon. The controller is tested against a conventional PI baseline on a hardware-in-the-loop rig with real measured disturbance sequences from January and March 2012. MPC reduces indoor temperature deviation from setpoint by 31% and heat consumption by 4.8% compared with PI across the January test sequence. Constraint satisfaction is maintained in 98.2% of sampling intervals. The paper also characterises the sensitivity of performance to prediction horizon length.

title: Chance-constrained model predictive control for district heating with uncertain heat demand
abstract: This paper presents the doctoral research core: a chance-constrained MPC formulation for district heating network operation under uncertain consumer heat demand. Demand uncertainty is characterised by a Gaussian mixture model fitted to three years of hourly consumption data from 41 metered buildings in Novi Sad. Chance constraints enforce supply temperature bounds at all network nodes with a specified probability level of 95%. The resulting optimisation problem is reformulated as a second-order cone programme and solved with an interior-point solver at each 15-minute sampling step. Closed-loop performance is evaluated by simulation over one heating season using out-of-sample demand realisations. The chance-constrained controller reduces constraint violations by 83% relative to a nominal MPC formulation while incurring a 6.1% increase in pump energy consumption. Computation times average 4.3 seconds on standard workstation hardware, which is acceptable for the 15-minute control interval. Sensitivity to the fitted demand model is analysed through a cross-validation study.

title: Scenario-based stochastic MPC for integrating solar thermal collectors into a district heating network
abstract: Solar thermal collectors introduce correlated, weather-dependent uncertainty into district heat supply that is difficult to capture with simple Gaussian models. This paper applies scenario-based stochastic MPC to a 12-node pilot network equipped with 800 m² of flat-plate solar collectors feeding a 150 m³ stratified buffer tank. Irradiance scenarios for a 6-hour horizon are generated by a persistent-error ensemble method using pyranometer measurements and a numerical weather prediction model. The optimiser selects pump and valve schedules that minimise expected fuel consumption subject to comfort and equipment constraints across 60 scenarios, using a sample average approximation approach. Case studies cover spring and autumn operation when solar contributions are most variable. Compared with a deterministic forecast-based MPC, expected gas consumption decreases by 9.3% and the 95th-percentile temperature-deficit index falls by 55% over 60 test days. Scenario count sensitivity is analysed; 40 scenarios are found sufficient for stable performance.

title: Demand-side flexibility quantification for residential buildings connected to district heating: a grey-box modelling approach
abstract: Quantifying how much heat load a residential building can shift without violating occupant comfort constraints is a prerequisite for network-level demand response programmes. This paper presents a systematic grey-box identification approach applied to 18 apartments in three blocks of flats in Novi Sad, using two winters of 10-minute interval indoor air temperature and heat meter data. Second- and third-order resistance-capacitance models are fitted by maximum likelihood estimation. The identified models are used to compute a flexibility potential index defined as the maximum energy shift achievable within a 2 °C comfort band over 1-hour windows. Results show that pre-heating potential averages 1.8 kWh per apartment-hour in February, with significant variance explained by building envelope U-value and window-to-wall ratio. The flexibility index correlates moderately with heating degree days (Pearson r = 0.62). Identified parameters are compared with those obtained from EN ISO 13790 calculations to assess the reliability of simplified audits.

title: Robust tube MPC for district heating with uncertain geothermal heat pump output
abstract: Geothermal heat pumps integrated into district heating networks face variability in ground-source temperature over the heating season, producing a bounded but uncertain heat output that complicates network scheduling. This paper formulates a robust tube MPC using a disturbance set characterised from one year of borehole measurements at a pilot site in Vojvodina. The nominal trajectory is computed by solving a deterministic MILP for a 19-node network model; tube invariant sets are computed offline using a polytopic approximation of the disturbance set. The ancillary controller keeps the system state within the pre-computed tube with minimal corrective action. Closed-loop simulations over 90 days show that all nodal temperature constraints are satisfied robustly, with maximum constraint tightening consuming 12% of the available supply-temperature margin. Peak boiler activation frequency decreases by 28% relative to a rule-based controller. Computational overhead of the online MILP is evaluated for different network sizes.

title: Coordinated stochastic MPC for heat and power sector coupling via large-scale heat pumps
abstract: Large heat pumps that couple electricity and district heat networks can provide grid balancing services while reducing carbon emissions, but they introduce strong cross-sector uncertainty coupling. This paper develops a two-layer stochastic MPC framework in which an upper layer optimises heat pump scheduling using day-ahead electricity price scenarios and a lower layer handles real-time network balancing. Price scenarios are drawn from a vine copula model estimated on two years of Hungarian day-ahead market data, applied as a proxy for the future Vojvodina regional market. A 27-node test network with a 4 MW heat pump and 200 m³ thermal storage is used. Over a 30-day winter simulation, expected daily operating cost decreases by 14.2% and CO₂ proxy emissions by 11.7% relative to a myopic price-following strategy. Inter-layer communication latency and its effect on closed-loop stability are analysed. The paper also discusses practical implementation constraints related to heat pump ramp rates.

title: Data-driven disturbance models for stochastic MPC in district heating: comparing parametric and non-parametric approaches
abstract: The quality of a stochastic MPC solution depends critically on the disturbance model used to generate scenarios or compute constraint back-offs. This paper benchmarks five disturbance modelling approaches—Gaussian, Gaussian mixture, kernel density estimation, quantile regression forests, and conformal prediction sets—for representing short-term heat demand forecast errors in a district heating context. Evaluation uses an eight-year dataset of hourly heat consumption from a utility serving approximately 12 000 apartments in the Vojvodina region, split into training, validation, and test portions. Each disturbance model is embedded into the same scenario-based stochastic MPC formulation and tested over identical closed-loop simulation runs. Performance metrics include constraint satisfaction rate, average cost, and scenario generation time. Conformal prediction sets achieve the best calibration on the test set (coverage 94.8% against a 95% target) but at higher computational cost than parametric alternatives. Gaussian mixture models offer the best cost–calibration trade-off for real-time applications with 15-minute intervals.

title: Online re-identification of building thermal parameters for adaptive demand response in district heating
abstract: Building thermal parameters drift over time due to occupancy changes, envelope degradation, and renovation works, reducing the accuracy of models used in demand response programmes. This paper presents a recursive expectation-maximisation algorithm for online re-identification of grey-box building thermal models, designed to run on standard smart heat meter hardware with limited memory. The algorithm is validated on synthetic data generated from a validated EnergyPlus model of a Vojvodina multi-family block, with injected parameter drift representing gradual insulation ageing at 2% per year. Over a 3-year simulated operation, the adaptive model maintains a normalised root-mean-square prediction error below 4.1%, compared with 11.7% for a static model. The re-identified parameters are fed into an MPC demand response controller; energy shift potential estimation error decreases from 23% to 8% relative to static identification. Computational requirements are profiled on an ARM Cortex-M7 microcontroller to confirm embedded suitability.

title: A Comparison of Property Graph and RDF Representations for Drug–Target Interaction Networks: Storage, Query, and Reasoning Trade-offs
abstract: Drug–target interaction data is distributed across databases that use both property graph and RDF models, and practitioners frequently debate which model better supports integration and reasoning. We conducted a systematic comparison using a curated drug–target interaction dataset of 48 000 interactions involving 3 200 compounds and 1 900 protein targets, sourced from three public databases and normalised to InChI and UniProt identifiers. We instantiated the same data in Neo4j (property graph) and in an RDF triplestore (GraphDB), and executed 15 query tasks covering path finding, subgraph matching, and RDFS-based inference. RDF with reasoning found 11% more indirect interactions through class subsumption than the property graph equivalent, while Neo4j was 3.4× faster on two-hop path queries. We also measured storage footprints and bulk-load times. The paper provides decision criteria for teams choosing between the two paradigms based on their primary use case.

title: Gray-level co-occurrence matrix features for MRI-based staging of liver fibrosis in a mixed-aetiology cohort
abstract: Gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) features characterise spatial intensity relationships and can capture texture heterogeneity beyond first-order statistics. This prospective study enrolled 143 adults with liver fibrosis of mixed aetiology (viral hepatitis B and C, alcohol-related, autoimmune) staged by biopsy within six weeks of MRI. Fourteen GLCM features were computed from T2-weighted images at four angular offsets. Feature stability across offsets was assessed using the concordance correlation coefficient. Angular second moment and correlation coefficient were the most stable (CCC > 0.92). A random forest classifier trained on ten GLCM features achieved accuracy 79% for four-class grading (F0, F1, F2, F3–F4 combined). Performance degraded when aetiology subgroups were not balanced in training data, indicating that aetiology influences texture independently of fibrosis severity. The study highlights a need for aetiology-stratified model development.

title: T1 mapping of liver parenchyma at 3 T: relationship to fibrosis stage and iron content
abstract: Native T1 relaxation time in liver parenchyma is sensitive to both fibrosis-associated collagen deposition and iron overload, which can confound staging. This cross-sectional study measured native T1 using a modified Look-Locker inversion recovery sequence in 86 patients and 20 healthy volunteers at 3 T. Simultaneous T2* mapping was used to estimate liver iron content. After correction for iron-related T1 shortening using a published relaxivity model, iron-corrected T1 correlated significantly with fibrosis stage (Spearman ρ = 0.72, p < 0.001). Native T1 without iron correction showed markedly weaker correlation (ρ = 0.49). The correction reduced staging misclassification by 18 percentage points in patients with elevated iron (T2* < 20 ms). Healthy volunteer T1 was 812 ± 34 ms, consistent with published reference values. These results support routine co-acquisition of T2* when T1 mapping is used for fibrosis staging.

title: Radiomics features from gadoxetate disodium-enhanced hepatobiliary phase MRI for distinguishing F2 from F3 hepatic fibrosis
abstract: Differentiating moderate (F2) from severe (F3) fibrosis is clinically important for treatment decisions in chronic liver disease, yet remains among the hardest tasks for imaging-based methods. This study extracted 107 radiomics features from the hepatobiliary phase (20-minute post-injection) of gadoxetate disodium-enhanced MRI in 95 patients with biopsy reference. Feature selection used minimum-redundancy maximum-relevance (mRMR) followed by LASSO regularisation, retaining eight features. The final support vector machine model achieved AUC 0.78 (95% CI 0.69–0.86) for F2 versus F3 discrimination in fivefold cross-validation. Enhancement ratio of the liver parenchyma and a second-order texture feature derived from the portal vein phase were the top contributors. Direct comparison with serum-based scoring systems (APRI, FIB-4) showed that the MRI model outperformed both, particularly in patients with borderline serum markers. Contrast agent dose and acquisition timing were standardised across all examinations.

title: Repeatability of T2* liver mapping at 1.5 T and 3 T: a test-retest study in patients with suspected iron overload
abstract: T2* mapping is routinely used to estimate hepatic iron concentration, but test-retest repeatability data from clinical scanners in the Western Balkans region are sparse. Forty patients with suspected hereditary haemochromatosis or transfusion-related iron overload underwent T2* mapping twice within 14 days on the same scanner and field strength (20 at 1.5 T, 20 at 3 T) without any intervening treatment. T2* values were measured in nine liver segments using a multi-echo gradient echo sequence. Bland-Altman analysis showed limits of agreement of ±4.1 ms at 1.5 T and ±2.8 ms at 3 T, corresponding to measurement uncertainty of approximately 12% and 9% relative to group mean T2* values respectively. Repeatability was better at 3 T across all segments. Segment 1 (caudate lobe) showed highest variability at both field strengths due to cardiac motion artefacts. Results support clinical confidence in longitudinal T2* monitoring for iron quantification.

title: Quantitative MRI fibrosis staging as an endpoint in clinical trials: current readiness and outstanding requirements
abstract: Liver biopsy is the accepted reference standard in clinical trials for chronic liver disease, but sampling error, procedural risk, and patient reluctance limit its use. This book chapter reviews the current evidence on quantitative MRI methods—DWI-ADC, T1 mapping, T2* mapping, and radiomics—as potential trial endpoints for fibrosis staging, focusing on published clinical studies from 2010 to 2022. Key requirements discussed include analytical validation (sensitivity, specificity, inter-reader agreement), biological validation (correlation with histological reference), metrological standardisation across scanner types, and regulatory qualification pathways through the European Medicines Agency. The chapter identifies the gap between technically achievable accuracy in single-centre studies and what multicentre validation trials have demonstrated. A table summarises AUC values by method and fibrosis transition (F0–F1 vs F2–F4; F2 vs F3; F3 vs F4) drawn from 31 published studies. Practical recommendations for trial design are provided.

title: Longitudinal changes in liver radiomics features during antiviral therapy for hepatitis C: a pilot study
abstract: Direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy achieves sustained virological response in over 95% of hepatitis C patients and is associated with histological fibrosis regression in some patients. This pilot study tracked 18 radiomics features extracted from T2-weighted MRI in 29 patients before, 12 weeks after completing DAA therapy, and at 52 weeks of follow-up. Liver stiffness measured by MR elastography was used as a secondary quantitative reference. Entropy and energy showed statistically significant changes between baseline and 52-week follow-up (paired t-test, p = 0.01 and 0.02 respectively), while changes at 12 weeks were non-significant. MR elastography stiffness decreased from median 7.4 kPa at baseline to 5.9 kPa at 52 weeks. The correlation between entropy change and stiffness change was moderate (r = 0.55). Despite small sample size, the results suggest that texture features may track slow post-treatment remodelling and warrant evaluation in larger longitudinal cohorts.

title: Synthetic MRI for simultaneous T1, T2, and proton density mapping in liver fibrosis staging: feasibility at 3 T
abstract: Synthetic MRI acquires a single multi-dynamic multi-echo sequence and reconstructs T1, T2, and proton density maps simultaneously, reducing total acquisition time. This feasibility study assessed whether synthetic MRI-derived quantitative maps provide consistent hepatic fibrosis staging information compared with conventional separately acquired T1 and T2 maps in 51 patients with biopsy reference. Synthetic T1 and T2 values showed good agreement with conventional maps (CCC 0.88 and 0.84 respectively). A combined model using synthetic T1, T2, and proton density with six GLCM features achieved AUC 0.87 for advanced fibrosis detection, comparable to the conventional protocol (AUC 0.85, p = 0.41). Total acquisition time for the synthetic protocol was 8 minutes compared with 22 minutes for the conventional multi-sequence approach. Motion artefacts were more frequent in the synthetic protocol (19% vs 7% of examinations). Feasibility is confirmed; motion robustness improvement is needed before routine clinical use.

title: Automated fibrosis staging from routine clinical liver MRI using an ensemble of handcrafted and deep radiomics features: a multicentre study
abstract: Translating MRI-based fibrosis staging from research to routine clinical practice requires pipelines that operate on protocol-heterogeneous images already stored in hospital PACS systems. This multicentre retrospective study collected T2-weighted liver MRI from four clinical centres in Serbia, Croatia, and Romania (total n = 318 patients, biopsy within eight weeks). An ensemble model combining 24 handcrafted texture features and 128 deep features extracted from a convolutional encoder pretrained on natural images was trained using fivefold cross-validation. After histogram normalisation for scanner harmonisation, the ensemble achieved macro-averaged AUC 0.83 across F0–F4 classes. Performance was notably lower at centre 4, which used a non-standard acquisition bandwidth, underscoring residual protocol sensitivity. Explainability analysis using SHAP values showed that deep features dominated predictions for F3 and F4, while handcrafted entropy and GLCM features were more influential for F0–F1. The pipeline runs in under three minutes per case on a standard clinical workstation.

title: Reference intervals for native T1 and T2* liver at 1.5 T and 3 T in a Serbian adult population: a multisite normative study
abstract: Population-specific reference intervals for quantitative MRI liver metrics are required before staging thresholds can be applied clinically. This multisite normative study recruited 148 healthy adult volunteers (72 women, 76 men, ages 20–68) from four cities in Serbia. Native T1 was measured using modified Look-Locker inversion recovery and T2* using a six-echo gradient echo sequence at both 1.5 T and 3 T. After exclusion of six volunteers with incidental hepatic steatosis on in-phase/out-of-phase imaging, reference intervals (2.5th–97.5th percentile) were: T1 at 1.5 T 754–876 ms, T1 at 3 T 798–934 ms, T2* at 1.5 T 22.1–38.6 ms, T2* at 3 T 18.4–31.7 ms. T1 was significantly higher in women than men at 3 T (p = 0.003). BMI correlated weakly with T1 at both field strengths (r = 0.29). These intervals provide locally validated thresholds for clinical implementation in the region.

title: Effect of fructose and glucose on acrylamide formation in extruded corn grits at different barrel temperatures
abstract: Acrylamide formation was studied in corn grit extrudates processed at barrel temperatures of 140, 160, 180 and 200 °C using a co-rotating twin-screw extruder. Fructose and glucose were added at 1, 2 and 4 g per 100 g dry grit. Acrylamide content was quantified by GC-MS with deuterated internal standard. Fructose-enriched samples produced acrylamide concentrations 35–58% higher than glucose-enriched samples at matched temperatures and concentrations, consistent with fructose's greater reactivity in the initial Maillard steps. At 200 °C and 4 g fructose per 100 g, acrylamide reached 620 µg/kg, whereas the corresponding glucose treatment yielded 395 µg/kg. Asparagine content in the raw grit was measured by RP-HPLC and confirmed as the limiting substrate at low sugar additions. The results suggest that selective control of the reducing sugar type offers a practical lever for reducing acrylamide in corn-based extrudate manufacture without reformulating the entire recipe.

title: Influence of lysine and asparagine supplementation on acrylamide and melanoidin formation in rice-based extrudates
abstract: Rice flour extrudates were produced with additions of 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 g/100 g of L-lysine or L-asparagine at barrel temperatures of 150 and 170 °C. The objective was to characterise the competing roles of these amino acids in Maillard reaction pathways leading to acrylamide versus high-molecular-weight melanoidin formation. Acrylamide was quantified by LC-MS/MS and melanoidin yield was estimated gravimetrically after dialysis. Lysine supplementation at 1.0 g/100 g reduced acrylamide by 28% at 170 °C compared to the control, while simultaneously increasing melanoidin yield by 19%. Asparagine supplementation at 2.0 g/100 g raised acrylamide by 74%. Browning index (BI) correlated positively with melanoidin yield (r = 0.91) but not with acrylamide concentration, confirming that colour and acrylamide formation proceed via partly distinct mechanistic routes in this system. Texture (breaking force, expansion ratio) was not significantly affected by amino acid additions at the levels tested.

title: Barrel temperature profiling in twin-screw extrusion: effect of temperature gradient direction on Maillard reaction products in triticale-based snacks
abstract: Two temperature gradient strategies were compared in triticale flour extrusion: a progressive profile (120 → 140 → 160 → 180 °C from feed to die) and a regressive profile (180 → 160 → 140 → 120 °C). A flat profile at 160 °C served as the control. Acrylamide, colour (L*, a*, b*), hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) and melanoidin yield were measured in the extrudate. The progressive profile produced the highest acrylamide (390 µg/kg) and highest browning (ΔE* = 18.4), whereas the regressive profile gave the lowest acrylamide (210 µg/kg) and intermediate browning (ΔE* = 13.1). HMF followed the same trend as acrylamide. Specific mechanical energy was higher for the regressive profile by approximately 12%, resulting in slightly lower bulk density. Melanoidin antioxidant capacity (FRAP) did not differ significantly between profiles, suggesting that melanoidin quality is more temperature-level-dependent than temperature-order-dependent. The data provide practical guidance for programming barrel temperature sequences in industrial extrusion lines.

title: Residence time distribution and its link to acrylamide heterogeneity along the extrudate strand in corn-wheat snack production
abstract: Residence time distribution (RTD) in a co-rotating twin-screw extruder was measured using a pulse injection of a red FD&C dye at throughputs of 5, 8 and 12 kg/h, screw speeds of 250 and 350 rpm, and barrel temperatures of 160 and 180 °C. RTD parameters (mean residence time t̄, variance σ², Peclet number Pe) were extracted by fitting a dispersion model to UV absorbance profiles at the die outlet. Samples collected at the die were cut into 5 cm segments and acrylamide was measured by LC-MS/MS in each segment independently. Mean residence time decreased from 68 s at 5 kg/h to 31 s at 12 kg/h. Acrylamide concentration along a single strand varied by up to 18% within one production run, correlating weakly with local RTD estimates. The variance in RTD was the parameter most predictive of acrylamide spread (r = 0.71). These results suggest that process conditions reducing RTD variance could improve product uniformity from an acrylamide standpoint.

title: Predictive model for simultaneous acrylamide and colour response surfaces in twin-screw extruded wheat-corn blends: a central composite design study
abstract: A central composite rotatable design (CCRD) was used to model acrylamide concentration and CIE ΔE* as simultaneous responses in wheat-corn (50:50) extrudates. The three process variables were barrel temperature (150–190 °C), feed moisture (13–18 g/100 g wet basis) and screw speed (200–400 rpm). Twenty experimental runs were conducted on a Brabender DSE 25 twin-screw extruder. Acrylamide ranged from 95 to 710 µg/kg across the design space. Second-order polynomial models for both responses showed R² values of 0.94 (acrylamide) and 0.97 (ΔE*). Barrel temperature had the largest main effect on both responses, while feed moisture showed a significant quadratic term for acrylamide. A constrained optimisation using desirability functions identified the combination of 160 °C, 16 g/100 g moisture and 350 rpm as minimising acrylamide below 200 µg/kg while keeping ΔE* above 10 for acceptable browning appearance. Validation runs at the optimum confirmed predictions within 9% relative error.

title: Determinants of Voluntary Tax Compliance Among Sole Traders in Vojvodina: Evidence from a Survey of 280 Micro-Businesses
abstract: This paper investigates the factors that shape voluntary tax compliance decisions among sole traders operating under the Serbian flat-rate presumptive tax system. A structured questionnaire was administered to 280 micro-business owners in Vojvodina between 2009 and 2010, covering perceived fairness, administrative burden, audit probability, and trust in tax authorities. Ordered logistic regression is used to relate these attitudinal and structural variables to self-reported compliance behaviour. Results indicate that perceived procedural fairness and trust in local government are the strongest positive predictors of compliance, while high presumptive tax brackets relative to actual income are associated with significantly lower compliance intentions. Businesses operating in service sectors report higher compliance rates than those in trade, possibly reflecting differences in cash-handling practices. The findings suggest that recalibrating bracket thresholds to better match actual earnings could improve aggregate compliance at relatively low administrative cost.

title: Estimating the Shadow Economy in Small Serbian Municipalities Using a MIMIC Approach
abstract: The paper applies a Multiple Indicators Multiple Causes (MIMIC) structural equation model to estimate the size of the shadow economy in 45 small municipalities in Serbia over the period 2005–2010. Causal variables include tax burden, regulatory intensity proxied by business registration costs, unemployment rate, and share of self-employment. Indicator variables are currency in circulation, electricity consumption, and labour force participation. Annual shadow economy estimates range between 22 and 31 percent of official GDP across the sample municipalities, with pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Municipalities with higher shares of agricultural self-employment exhibit systematically larger informal sectors. The results are compared with national estimates from Eurostat-affiliated studies and found to be broadly consistent. The paper also discusses methodological limitations of the MIMIC approach when applied to subnational administrative units with limited statistical capacity.

title: Administrative Burden and Compliance Costs of Flat-Rate Taxation for Serbian Micro-Enterprises: A Time-Use Study
abstract: This study quantifies the time and monetary compliance costs incurred by Serbian micro-enterprises subject to the flat-rate presumptive income tax. Using a time-use diary methodology administered to 165 owner-operators across three sectors—retail trade, catering, and personal services—compliance-related activities were tracked over a four-week period. Average annual compliance time was estimated at 38.4 hours per enterprise, translating to a monetary equivalent of approximately 3.2 percent of annual tax liability at median wage rates. Compliance costs are regressive with respect to turnover, with the smallest enterprises bearing costs equivalent to 6.8 percent of liability. Comparison with enterprises paying standard corporate income tax shows that flat-rate taxpayers spend 41 percent less time on bookkeeping but face greater uncertainty regarding bracket re-assignment. Policy implications for the design of simplified tax regimes are discussed.

title: Tax Morale and Institutional Trust in Transition Economies: A Cross-Country Comparison of Serbia, Hungary, and Romania
abstract: Drawing on data from the 2012 wave of a harmonised enterprise survey covering 890 micro and small enterprises in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, this paper analyses the relationship between institutional trust and tax morale. Tax morale is operationalised through a validated six-item Likert scale. Multilevel logistic regression is used to account for individual-level and country-level variance. Institutional trust—measured as confidence in courts, tax administration, and local government—explains approximately 18 percent of between-country variance in tax morale scores. Serbian respondents report the lowest average trust scores and the lowest tax morale, while Hungarian respondents show intermediate values. The analysis also reveals that perceived corruption in tax administration is a stronger negative predictor of morale than the level of the tax burden itself, pointing to governance quality as a key lever for compliance policy.

title: Bracket Creep and Misclassification Incentives Under Serbia's Presumptive Tax for Entrepreneurs
abstract: Serbia's presumptive tax assigns micro-enterprise owners to fixed annual tax brackets based on activity type and municipality. This paper examines whether the bracket structure creates incentives for misclassification of economic activity. Using administrative registration data from the Serbian Business Registers Agency for 2010–2015, matched to tax bracket assignments, a regression discontinuity design is applied around bracket thresholds. A statistically significant bunching pattern is observed just below bracket boundaries, consistent with strategic activity misreporting. The effect is concentrated in sectors with multiple closely spaced brackets, notably personal services and food catering. The magnitude of bunching implies that between 8 and 14 percent of enterprises in affected sectors may be misclassified in any given year. The paper discusses audit targeting implications and suggests bracket consolidation as a partial remedy.

title: Fiscal Decentralisation and Local Tax Compliance: Panel Evidence from Serbian Municipalities 2008–2016
abstract: This paper investigates whether fiscal decentralisation reforms in Serbia influenced tax compliance rates at the municipal level. A balanced panel of 145 municipalities over 2008–2016 is constructed using data from the Ministry of Finance and the Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia. The dependent variable is the ratio of collected to assessed local surtax revenue as a proxy for aggregate compliance. Fixed-effects panel regression results indicate that a ten-percentage-point increase in the share of own revenues in total municipal budget is associated with a 2.1-percentage-point increase in the compliance ratio, consistent with the hypothesis that higher fiscal autonomy improves revenue administration effort. The effect is stronger in municipalities with elected mayors from non-governing-coalition parties, suggesting a political economy dimension. Robustness checks using instrumental variables confirm the direction and approximate magnitude of the main findings.

title: Perceived Audit Probability and Compliance Under Presumptive Taxation: Experimental Evidence from Serbian Micro-Entrepreneurs
abstract: A laboratory-in-the-field experiment was conducted with 198 micro-entrepreneurs in Novi Sad and Subotica to test how varying the perceived probability of tax audit affects compliance decisions under a stylised presumptive tax game. Participants were assigned to three treatment conditions with announced audit probabilities of 5, 15, and 30 percent, and made allocation decisions across five rounds. Higher announced audit probability significantly increased reported income in the experiment, but the effect was non-linear: moving from 5 to 15 percent had a larger impact than moving from 15 to 30 percent. Participants with prior experience of real audits responded more strongly to audit probability changes than those without. Intrinsic tax morale, measured by a pre-experiment questionnaire, moderated the treatment effect, with high-morale participants showing less sensitivity to audit probability. Results are consistent with prospect theory predictions and have implications for audit policy design.

title: Informality as Rational Adaptation: Qualitative Evidence from Micro-Entrepreneurs in Southern Bačka
abstract: This paper presents findings from 34 semi-structured interviews with micro-entrepreneurs operating in Southern Bačka, focusing on how they perceive and rationalise partial informality under the presumptive tax system. Thematic analysis identifies three dominant rationalisations: the perception that the flat-rate tax is disconnected from actual ability to pay, distrust in the productive use of tax revenues, and normalisation of under-reporting based on peer behaviour. Entrepreneurs who had undergone formal bookkeeping training and those with banking relationships were substantially more likely to express full-compliance norms. The study uses a purposive sampling strategy stratified by sector and municipality size, and applies iterative coding with intercoder reliability checks. Findings complement quantitative compliance studies by mapping the cognitive and social mechanisms through which non-compliance is sustained, and suggest that peer communication channels may be effective vectors for compliance norm diffusion.

title: Presumptive Taxation Regimes in the Western Balkans: A Comparative Regulatory Survey
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured comparative overview of presumptive and flat-rate tax schemes for micro-enterprises across six Western Balkan jurisdictions: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Albania, Montenegro, and Kosovo. The analysis draws on legislative texts, official tax authority guidance documents, and OECD/IMF technical assistance reports collected through 2021. Each jurisdiction is assessed along five dimensions: coverage threshold, bracket structure, sectoral differentiation, transition mechanism to standard taxation, and audit procedures. Serbia is found to have the most granular bracket structure and the longest history of the scheme, while Albania and Kosovo have undergone the most significant recent reforms. The chapter concludes with a typology of design trade-offs between simplicity, revenue adequacy, and incentive compatibility, and identifies gaps in comparative empirical research on cross-border compliance spillovers in the region.

title: Gender Differences in Tax Compliance Among Self-Employed Micro-Entrepreneurs: Survey Evidence from Serbia
abstract: This paper examines whether gender is associated with tax compliance attitudes and self-reported compliance behaviour among self-employed micro-entrepreneurs subject to Serbia's presumptive income tax. Data come from a cross-sectional survey of 441 self-employed persons conducted in 2022, stratified by gender, sector, and region. Controlling for education, income level, sector, years in business, and prior audit experience, female respondents report higher tax morale scores and higher self-assessed compliance rates than male respondents. The gender compliance gap is largest in the personal services sector and smallest in construction-related trades, where female representation is low. Interaction analysis suggests that the gender effect on morale is partially mediated by differential trust in public institutions rather than by risk aversion alone. The findings align with patterns documented in Western European studies but the magnitude of the gender gap is somewhat smaller in the Serbian context.

title: Flat-Rate Tax Reform and Business Formalisation: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from Serbia's 2016 Threshold Revision
abstract: In 2016 Serbia raised the annual revenue ceiling for eligibility under the flat-rate presumptive income tax from 6 million to 8 million Serbian dinars. This paper exploits that policy change as a quasi-experiment to estimate its effect on the formalisation of previously informal micro-businesses. Using administrative data from the Business Registers Agency and the Tax Administration for 2014–2019, a difference-in-differences estimator compares enterprise registration rates and declared turnover in activity codes directly affected by the threshold change against unaffected codes. The threshold expansion is associated with a 7.3-percentage-point increase in new registrations in the two years following reform, concentrated in trade and personal services. There is no detectable effect on declared turnover conditional on registration, suggesting the new registrants were genuinely marginal rather than formerly registered enterprises restructuring. Results are robust to alternative control group definitions and to placebo tests using the preceding non-reform years.

title: Virtual Network Embedding with Link Stress Constraints in Carrier-Grade Testbeds
abstract: This paper addresses the virtual network embedding (VNE) problem in carrier-grade IP/MPLS testbeds subject to explicit link stress constraints. The authors model the physical substrate as a weighted multigraph where edge weights encode utilisation history sampled at 30-second intervals over a four-week period from a regional ISP backbone with 18 nodes and 31 links. The VNE formulation is cast as an integer linear program (ILP) and solved exactly for small instances and via a greedy split-ratio heuristic for larger ones. Experiments on both the real topology and three synthetic Waxman-generated graphs show that enforcing a 70% link-stress ceiling reduces request acceptance rate by 11% compared to unconstrained embedding but cuts mean path stretch from 2.4 to 1.7. The heuristic achieves solutions within 4% of the ILP optimum while reducing runtime by two orders of magnitude. The work provides a publicly available dataset of substrate topologies and arrival traces.

title: A Comparative Study of OpenFlow Controller Placement Strategies Under Asymmetric Propagation Delays
abstract: Controller placement in OpenFlow networks is known to affect both switch-to-controller latency and resilience to partitioning. This study evaluates five placement strategies—k-median, k-center, latency-balanced, failure-aware, and random baseline—on 14 real WAN topologies drawn from the Internet Topology Zoo, augmented with propagation-delay measurements collected over three months using active probing. The evaluation metric combines 95th-percentile switch-to-controller round-trip time, inter-controller synchronisation cost, and the fraction of switches that remain reachable after single-link failures. Results show that latency-balanced placement reduces the 95th-percentile RTT by 23% over k-median while increasing inter-controller traffic by 18%. Failure-aware placement dominates on resilience metrics at negligible latency cost on sparse topologies but degrades on dense topologies with diameter below four. The paper provides a placement benchmark tool released under an open-source licence.
