title: Topology Modelling for Service Function Chain Placement in Multi-Domain SD-WANs
abstract: Service function chaining in multi-domain software-defined WANs requires a topology abstraction that hides intra-domain details while preserving enough information for cross-domain path computation. This chapter reviews three abstraction families—star, spine, and distance-vector—and introduces a hybrid model called condensed-topology graph (CTG) that retains border-node pairs with their inter-domain latency distributions and available bandwidth envelopes. The chapter formalises the chain placement problem on a CTG as a constraint satisfaction problem and discusses how domain confidentiality requirements limit the precision of shared topology information. A case study using a 5-domain emulation with Mininet-based stubs and a BGP-LS information bus demonstrates that CTG-based placement achieves cross-domain path stretch within 8% of an omniscient baseline, compared to 31% for star abstraction. The chapter concludes with open problems around synchronisation frequency and partial-failure propagation.

title: Pre-Copy vs. Post-Copy Live Migration of Stateful VNFs: A Measurement Study on 10 GbE DPDK Hosts
abstract: Stateful VNFs such as deep packet inspection engines and stateful firewalls carry significant memory working sets that make live migration disruptive. This paper presents a controlled measurement study comparing pre-copy and post-copy migration strategies for three stateful VNF types running as DPDK-accelerated containers on a six-node cluster interconnected at 10 GbE. Migration events are triggered at four traffic load levels (20%, 40%, 60%, 80% of line rate). Metrics include total migration time, dirty-page rate, packet loss during cutover, and state consistency verified by replay of recorded traffic. Pre-copy outperforms post-copy at loads below 50% with a mean downtime of 14 ms versus 38 ms; at 80% load the relationship inverts due to unbounded dirtying in pre-copy. A memory-scan-rate model is fitted to the measurements and shown to predict downtime within 15% across workloads. The dataset and VNF images are made available for reproducibility.

title: Topology Fingerprinting for Fast Re-Placement After Simultaneous Multi-Link Failures in NFV Infrastructures
abstract: Simultaneous multi-link failures in NFV infrastructures invalidate existing VNF placements and require rapid re-computation. This paper introduces topology fingerprinting, a method that pre-computes a compact spectral descriptor of each possible failure pattern and maps it to a cached re-placement plan. Fingerprints are based on the first eight eigenvalues of the normalised Laplacian of the residual graph. At runtime, the current failure state is fingerprinted and the closest pre-computed plan is retrieved via approximate nearest-neighbour search. The method is evaluated on three real ISP topologies with failure sets enumerated up to triple simultaneous failures, giving 3,876 distinct scenarios. Cache hit rate reaches 94% for double failures and 81% for triple failures, with mean re-placement time of 22 ms versus 1.8 seconds for online ILP. Chain availability during recovery improves by 14 percentage points over reactive re-computation. Limitations in topology coverage are discussed.

title: Bandwidth-Delay Product as a Placement Signal for Bulk-Transfer VNFs in SD-WANs
abstract: Bulk-transfer VNFs such as WAN optimisation controllers and video-transcoding middleboxes are sensitive to bandwidth-delay product (BDP) rather than latency or bandwidth alone. This paper argues that BDP should be a first-class metric in placement objectives and formalises a BDP-aware placement problem on a weighted directed graph. A branch-and-bound solver is implemented for instances up to 30 nodes; a greedy constructive heuristic handles larger instances. The paper evaluates placement quality on nine SD-WAN topologies representing enterprise networks with 15–120 sites, using traffic matrices derived from a corporate WAN monitoring tool anonymised by a partner operator. BDP-aware placement reduces retransmission events observed in TCP bulk transfers by 31% compared to latency-only placement and by 18% compared to bandwidth-only placement in emulation experiments on a Mininet-WiFi extended fabric. The paper also derives an analytical bound on BDP improvement relative to shortest-path routing.

title: Migration Cost Models for Containerised VNFs Under Heterogeneous Memory Compression Rates
abstract: Accurate migration cost models are necessary for migration scheduling algorithms to make sound decisions. Existing models treat memory dirty rate as workload-dependent but ignore memory compression, which modern container runtimes apply at varying ratios depending on page content. This paper develops an extended pre-copy migration cost model that incorporates compression ratio as a function of VNF type and load, estimated online via a lightweight page-content sampler requiring less than 0.3% CPU overhead. The model is fitted to 1,240 controlled migration experiments across five VNF types on a testbed with three compression algorithms (LZ4, ZSTD, Snappy) enabled at the hypervisor level. The fitted model predicts migration downtime with a mean absolute percentage error of 8.2% versus 22.1% for the compression-unaware baseline model. A scheduler plug-in using the model is demonstrated to reduce unplanned chain outages by 17% in a 24-hour emulation run.

title: Characterisation of Truncated Multiplier Error Distributions in Fixed-Point Image Convolution
abstract: Truncated multipliers reduce hardware area and switching power by discarding the least significant partial products, but introduce a systematic positive bias in multiplication results. This paper develops an analytical model for the error distribution of an n×n truncated multiplier operating on unsigned fixed-point operands drawn from natural image statistics. The model is validated against gate-level simulation of 8-bit, 12-bit, and 16-bit multiplier variants synthesised in a 180 nm CMOS standard cell library. Applied to a 3×3 Gaussian blur kernel, the 12-bit truncated multiplier with four discarded columns achieves a 31% reduction in dynamic power while keeping peak signal-to-noise ratio degradation below 0.9 dB on a 500-image test corpus derived from a publicly available greyscale dataset. The analytical error bounds derived match simulation within 4% across all tested operand widths, providing a practical tool for pre-synthesis quality budgeting in image processing pipeline design.

title: A Unified Error Metric Framework for Approximate Arithmetic Operators in Multimedia Applications
abstract: Existing error metrics for approximate arithmetic—mean error distance, normalised mean error, error rate, and worst-case error—are often applied inconsistently across the literature, making comparisons between designs difficult. This chapter surveys seventeen approximate adder and multiplier designs published between 2005 and 2013 and recomputes their performance under a common metric suite applied to three application benchmarks: 2-D image convolution, histogram equalisation, and IDCT-based MPEG decoding. The chapter introduces a metric sensitivity index that quantifies how the ranking of competing designs changes depending on which error metric is chosen. Results show that the choice of metric alters the Pareto-optimal design in eleven of the seventeen cases examined. Practical guidance is offered for selecting metrics appropriate to perceptual quality requirements, with specific thresholds derived from subjective quality evaluations conducted with twenty human observers using a paired-comparison protocol.

title: Gate-Level Simulation of Mean Error Distance Propagation Through Multi-Stage Approximate Pipelines
abstract: When approximate arithmetic units are chained in a processing pipeline, individual stage errors accumulate in ways that simple additive models fail to capture accurately because error distributions at the output of one stage become the input distribution to the next. This paper presents a gate-level Monte Carlo simulation methodology that tracks the joint error distribution across up to eight cascaded approximate adder or multiplier stages. The methodology is implemented as a Python wrapper around a standard event-driven gate simulator and validated against exhaustive bit-true simulation for 8-bit operand widths. Applied to a five-stage Sobel edge detector pipeline on a 360×240 pixel test image set, the simulation predicts mean error distance at the final output within 6% of the exhaustive reference. Run time scales linearly with the number of stages and quadratically with operand width, remaining tractable for 16-bit designs.

title: FPGA Prototyping of an Approximate Bilinear Interpolation Core for Real-Time Image Scaling
abstract: Bilinear interpolation is a computationally intensive step in real-time image scaling for display and camera ISP pipelines. This paper describes the FPGA implementation of an approximate bilinear interpolation core in which the four surrounding pixel multiplications are replaced by a reduced-precision multiplier with a configurable truncation level. The design is implemented on a mid-range FPGA device from a commercially available development board and tested at 1280×720 to 1920×1080 upscaling at 30 fps. Three truncation levels are evaluated: removing 2, 4, and 6 least-significant partial product rows. The 4-row truncation variant reduces LUT usage by 19% and estimated dynamic power by 24% relative to the exact baseline, while keeping PSNR above 41 dB on a 200-frame natural video sequence. Timing is met at 148 MHz. Resource utilisation breakdowns and power estimation reports generated by the vendor toolchain are provided.

title: Automated Design Space Exploration for Approximate Arithmetic Operators Using Multi-Objective Evolutionary Optimisation
abstract: The space of possible approximate implementations of a fixed-width multiplier or adder is combinatorially large even when parameterised by a small set of structural modifications. This paper presents an automated exploration framework that uses the NSGA-II multi-objective evolutionary algorithm to search simultaneously for minimum gate count, minimum switching energy, and minimum mean squared error under worst-case input conditions. The framework interfaces with a commercial synthesis tool through a Tcl scripting layer and evaluates candidate circuits by running gate-level simulation on a fixed operand sample set. Applied to the 8-bit unsigned multiplier design space with five independent truncation and approximation parameters, the tool identifies a Pareto front of 34 distinct designs after 120 generations of population size 50, with a total wall-clock time of 14 hours on a 16-core workstation. Three designs from the front are selected for detailed characterisation in a Gaussian image blur benchmark.

title: Carry-Save Approximate Accumulator Design for Energy-Constrained Histogram-of-Oriented-Gradients Feature Extraction
abstract: The histogram-of-oriented-gradients feature descriptor requires repeated gradient magnitude accumulation across spatial cells, making the accumulator a significant contributor to overall energy consumption in embedded vision hardware. This paper presents a carry-save approximate accumulator in which the save–propagate decision for carry bits is taken probabilistically based on a configurable acceptance threshold. The design is specified in synthesisable RTL, mapped to a 65 nm standard cell library, and verified against a C reference model on the INRIA pedestrian dataset rescaled to 64×128 windows. At a threshold of 3 discarded carry bits per accumulation step, dynamic energy per HOG window drops by 33% compared to an exact ripple-carry accumulator, while the false-positive rate of a linear SVM classifier trained on approximate features increases by less than 0.4 percentage points relative to exact training. Area overhead of the control logic is 7% of the accumulator cell.

title: Error-Resilience Analysis of Approximate Fixed-Point Arithmetic in a Hardware H.264 Intra Prediction Engine
abstract: H.264 intra prediction computes residuals between predicted and actual pixel blocks using additions and subtractions that are amenable to approximation. This paper analyses the resilience of intra prediction quality to arithmetic errors introduced by four classes of approximate adder inserted into a synthesised H.264 intra prediction RTL core. The core is implemented on a Virtex FPGA and fed with 30-second clips from six standard-definition test sequences encoded at constant quantisation parameter 28. Error resilience is quantified by the increase in luma PSNR loss relative to exact hardware. Results show that prediction modes 0 through 4 tolerate approximate addition well, with PSNR loss below 0.5 dB for all tested adder families, while mode 8 (horizontal) is most sensitive and degrades by up to 2.1 dB with the most aggressive approximation. A mode-selective approximation scheme is proposed that confines approximation to the five most resilient modes, recovering 80% of the energy saving available from full approximation at only 0.3 dB average PSNR cost.

title: Sensitivity Profiling of Convolutional Neural Network Inference to Quantised Approximate Multiply-Accumulate Units
abstract: Quantised integer neural network inference replaces floating-point multiply-accumulate operations with fixed-point equivalents, and approximate MAC units can further reduce silicon area and energy. This paper profiles the sensitivity of five small CNN architectures—ranging from 4 to 18 layers—to approximate 8-bit MAC units by injecting gate-level error models derived from three approximate multiplier designs into a software CNN inference framework. Networks are evaluated on a 10-class image classification task using a subset of 10 000 images from a publicly available benchmark. Sensitivity profiles show that the first and last convolutional layers are consistently the most sensitive, with top-1 accuracy dropping by more than 3 percentage points when those layers use the most aggressive MAC variant, while middle layers tolerate the same approximation with less than 0.5 point loss. A mixed-precision assignment strategy guided by the sensitivity profile recovers full accuracy within 0.8 points while applying approximate MACs to 60% of multiply-accumulate operations by count.

title: Approximate Arithmetic for Bayer Demosaicing in Embedded Camera Pipelines: A Hardware-Software Co-Design Study
abstract: Bayer demosaicing converts a raw single-sensor colour image to a full RGB image through bilinear or gradient-corrected interpolation, and is executed at full frame rate in camera ISP hardware. This paper presents a co-design study in which the interpolation arithmetic is progressively approximated at three granularities—operator level, pipeline stage level, and full-pipeline level—and quality is assessed using both automatic metrics (PSNR, CPBD sharpness) and a 30-observer psychophysical experiment using printed test charts. Hardware is mapped to a Cyclone-family FPGA and energy is estimated from vendor power analysis at 60 fps on 12-megapixel raw frames. Full-pipeline approximation at the moderate level achieves 29% energy reduction with no statistically significant perceived quality difference versus the exact baseline in the psychophysical test at the 95% confidence level. The study identifies chroma interpolation as significantly more tolerant of approximation than luma.

title: Approximate Arithmetic in Hardware Optical Flow Estimation: Error Sensitivity Maps and Energy Budgets
abstract: Optical flow estimation by the Lucas–Kanade method requires iterative solution of a 2×2 spatial gradient matrix system, dominated in hardware by repeated fixed-point multiplications and accumulations. This paper constructs error sensitivity maps for each arithmetic operation in a hardware Lucas–Kanade pipeline by individually enabling approximate arithmetic at each node and measuring the resulting endpoint error in estimated flow vectors on the Middlebury optical flow benchmark at 320×240 resolution. Sensitivity maps identify that the spatial gradient product accumulations are three to five times more sensitive than the temporal gradient multiplications. An energy-optimal approximation assignment derived from the sensitivity maps and a power model calibrated against 65 nm synthesis results reduces estimated dynamic energy per frame by 38% while keeping average endpoint error increase below 0.12 pixels across the test sequences. The pipeline is validated at gate level using ModelSim with a test bench driven by pre-computed pixel streams.

title: Song structure divergence between sympatric Chorthippus montanus and C. parallelus in lowland meadows of the Pannonian Plain
abstract: Male calling songs of Chorthippus montanus and C. parallelus were recorded at twelve mixed-species meadow sites across Vojvodina and analysed for syllable duration, inter-syllable interval, chirp rate, and carrier frequency using custom scripts in R. A total of 1,840 song bouts from 312 individually marked males were included. Principal component analysis of song parameters separated the two species along the first two components explaining 68% of variance, and the degree of separation was significantly greater at sites of highest species overlap (PERMANOVA, p < 0.001). No intermediate song phenotypes indicative of hybrids were detected. The data suggest that acoustic divergence is maintained or reinforced at sympatric sites relative to allopatric populations, consistent with a character displacement scenario. Playback experiments testing female phonotaxis responses are recommended as a follow-up to establish perceptual boundaries corresponding to the observed signal divergence.

title: Mitochondrial phylogeography of Chorthippus biguttulus complex across the Carpathian Basin and adjacent mountain ranges
abstract: We sequenced the mitochondrial COI and cytochrome b genes (combined 1,347 bp) from 218 specimens collected at 34 localities spanning Hungary, Serbia, Romania, Slovakia, and Ukraine. Bayesian phylogenetic analysis recovered three well-supported clades corresponding broadly to Pannonian lowland, Transylvanian plateau, and Carpathian arc populations, with estimated divergence times between 0.9 and 2.4 Ma based on a standard arthropod molecular clock. Haplotype network analysis revealed a star-like pattern within the Pannonian clade consistent with post-glacial expansion. The Transylvanian clade showed markedly higher nucleotide diversity (π = 0.018 vs. 0.004 in Pannonian populations), suggesting a refugial role. Morphological measurements of the hind femur and pronotum did not fully track these genetic boundaries, cautioning against sole reliance on morphology for species delimitation in this complex. The results provide a biogeographic framework for subsequent nuclear genomic studies.

title: Female phonotaxis discrimination in Chorthippus montanus and C. parallelus under field and laboratory conditions
abstract: We conducted two-choice phonotaxis assays presenting females with synthesised male songs of conspecific and heterospecific templates at four amplitude levels. Experiments were run in both controlled acoustic chambers (n = 89 females per species) and open-field arenas at two sympatric field sites (n = 67 females per species). Females of both species showed strong preference for conspecific song in laboratory trials, with discrimination indices of 0.81 (C. montanus) and 0.76 (C. parallelus). In field arenas, discrimination remained significant but was reduced at low amplitude treatments, suggesting that signal degradation over distance may occasionally allow heterospecific acoustic contact. High-speed video confirmed that approach paths were initiated within the first 300 ms of song onset. Results quantify the strength of acoustic pre-mating isolation and identify conditions under which the barrier may be incomplete.

title: Hybrid viability and fertility in controlled crosses between Chorthippus montanus and C. parallelus from sympatric Vojvodina populations
abstract: Reciprocal crosses between C. montanus and C. parallelus individuals collected at two sympatric sites in Vojvodina produced F1 hybrids at a rate of 38% relative to conspecific cross hatch rates. F1 hybrids of both sexes survived to adulthood, but male hybrids showed a 62% reduction in sperm motility relative to parental means as assessed by light microscopy. Female hybrids produced eggs, but F2 hatch rate from hybrid × hybrid crosses was only 11%, compared with 74% for conspecific crosses. Microsatellite genotyping confirmed F1 hybrid status in all 44 individuals used in subsequent fertility tests. These results indicate that post-mating isolation operates primarily through male-biased hybrid sterility, consistent with Haldane's rule, and suggest that post-zygotic barriers supplement pre-mating acoustic isolation in maintaining species boundaries in sympatry.

title: RADseq-based population structure analysis reveals genomic islands of differentiation between sympatric Chorthippus species
abstract: We generated restriction-site-associated DNA sequencing (RADseq) libraries from 96 individuals (48 per species) sampled at three sympatric sites in Vojvodina. After quality filtering and alignment to a de novo reference assembly (scaffold N50 = 420 kb), we retained 14,382 SNPs for analysis. FST outlier scans identified 218 SNPs showing significantly elevated differentiation (FST > 0.6) clustered in 11 genomic regions averaging 180 kb in length, while genome-wide mean FST was 0.14. These differentiation islands colocated with regions of low recombination estimated from linkage disequilibrium decay. Gene annotation of homologs in Locusta migratoria suggested enrichment for ion channel and olfactory receptor genes within the outlier regions, though functional validation is lacking. Admixture analysis at K=2 assigned all individuals cleanly to their morphological species, with no evidence of recent introgression in the sampled cohorts.

title: Seasonal overlap and microhabitat partitioning in co-occurring Chorthippus species in Fruška Gora foothill meadows
abstract: We monitored adult activity of three co-occurring Chorthippus species (C. montanus, C. parallelus, C. brunneus) across a full season at six transects on the southern slopes of Fruška Gora using 15-minute point counts at two-week intervals from June through September over two consecutive years. Vegetation height, soil moisture, and bare ground cover were measured at each point. C. montanus adults peaked four weeks earlier than C. brunneus and two weeks earlier than C. parallelus, providing partial temporal isolation. Generalised linear mixed models indicated that soil moisture was the strongest predictor of C. montanus occurrence (β = 1.42, SE = 0.31) while bare ground cover predicted C. brunneus (β = 0.98, SE = 0.22). Microhabitat segregation was most pronounced at intermediate vegetation heights where all three species co-occurred. The temporal and spatial data suggest that ecological partitioning may reduce interspecific encounter rates and contribute indirectly to reproductive isolation.

title: Speciation genetics of sympatric grasshoppers: current progress and remaining questions in the Chorthippus model system
abstract: This chapter reviews research on reproductive isolation mechanisms in the Chorthippus biguttulus species group and its relatives, focusing on studies conducted in Central and Eastern Europe over the past two decades. We cover the hierarchy of isolation barriers from habitat preference and phenological divergence through acoustic signal discrimination to post-mating incompatibilities, and discuss how estimates of relative barrier strength have been obtained. The genomic basis of isolation is addressed in light of recent population genomic data, including the relevance of recombination landscape to the maintenance of differentiation islands under gene flow. We identify gaps including the near-absence of transcriptomic data from hybrid tissues, the limited geographic sampling in Southeastern Europe, and the lack of experimental evolution approaches. The chapter situates the Chorthippus system within broader theoretical frameworks for sympatric and parapatric speciation and argues that its tractability for both field and laboratory work makes it a useful complement to Drosophila and fish model systems.

title: Whole-genome sequencing of a contact zone population reveals ongoing low-level introgression between Chorthippus montanus and C. parallelus at a Vojvodina wetland margin
abstract: We sequenced whole genomes of 60 C. montanus and 58 C. parallelus individuals (mean coverage 14×) collected along a 1.2 km transect crossing a wet–dry vegetation boundary at a site near Sremska Mitrovica where both species breed in adjacent patches. STRUCTURE and ADMIXTURE analyses at K=2 identified six individuals (three per species) with admixture proportions between 0.08 and 0.23, indicating recent or ongoing introgression absent in our earlier RADseq dataset from inland sites. D-statistics (ABBA-BABA) confirmed significant introgression (Z = 4.8). Introgressed segments were non-randomly distributed: autosomal introgression was detectable, but the X-chromosome equivalent showed significantly reduced introgression (χ² = 22.1, p < 0.0001). Functional annotation of introgressed regions in the autosomal fraction revealed enrichment for genes associated with cuticular hydrocarbon synthesis, potentially contributing to a chemosensory dimension of species recognition not previously studied in this system.

title: Isothermal calorimetry as a tool for tracking reaction extent in NaOH-activated fly ash systems
abstract: The heat flow curves of NaOH-activated fly ash pastes were recorded continuously for 168 hours at temperatures of 20, 40 and 60 °C. Cumulative heat at 72 hours was 48, 97 and 164 J g−1 at the respective temperatures, confirming strong temperature sensitivity of the reaction. Degree of reaction estimated from selective dissolution and compared to a calorimetric conversion model showed agreement within ±6 percentage points at 40 °C but diverged at 60 °C, likely due to gel reorganisation masking exothermic events. The activation energy calculated from the initial dissolution stage using the Arrhenius approach was 62 kJ mol−1, consistent with glass dissolution kinetics reported for similar silico-aluminous systems. Paste microporosity measured by mercury intrusion porosimetry decreased from 24.3 to 11.8 vol% as curing temperature rose from 20 to 60 °C. The work provides a semi-quantitative framework for predicting early reaction progress without destructive testing.

title: Pore structure evolution in alkali-activated fly ash mortars during the first year of ambient curing
abstract: Fly ash mortars activated with a combined NaOH–sodium silicate solution were cast and stored at 20 °C and 65% relative humidity. Specimens were extracted at 7, 28, 90, 180 and 365 days for mercury intrusion porosimetry and nitrogen adsorption (BET) measurements. Total porosity declined from 29.4% at 7 days to 18.7% at 365 days, with the threshold pore diameter shifting from 0.21 to 0.07 µm. BET surface area increased from 11 to 38 m2 g−1 over the same period, indicating progressive gel densification. XRD confirmed that zeolite phase formation (analcime, sodalite) began between 90 and 180 days and contributed to pore refinement. A parallel set of sealed specimens showed less total porosity reduction, suggesting that moisture availability from the environment contributes to continued reaction at ambient temperature. Results have direct implications for durability prediction models that rely on transport parameters.

title: Sulphate resistance of alkali-activated slag–fly ash mortars exposed to sodium and magnesium sulphate solutions
abstract: Mortar prisms (40 × 40 × 160 mm) with slag–fly ash ratios of 30:70, 50:50 and 70:30 were immersed in 5 wt% Na2SO4 and 5 wt% MgSO4 solutions for up to 540 days. Mass change, flexural and compressive strength retention, and linear expansion were monitored at 60-day intervals. The 30:70 slag–fly ash blend showed the best performance in Na2SO4, retaining 91% of its reference compressive strength at 540 days, while the 70:30 blend retained only 74%. In MgSO4 exposure, all blends performed worse, with the 50:50 blend showing the most balanced response (83% strength retention). XRD and SEM-EDS analysis of degraded zones attributed the differences to gypsum and brucite formation in MgSO4 and to selective decalcification of C-A-S-H gel in high-slag blends. Results demonstrate that lower slag content improves sulphate resistance but reduces early strength, requiring a design trade-off.

title: Freeze-thaw resistance of alkali-activated fly ash concrete: the role of air-void parameters
abstract: Concrete mixes based on Class F fly ash activated with 8 M NaOH and sodium silicate (Ms = 1.0) were prepared with and without an air-entraining admixture adapted for alkaline environments. Air-void spacing factor and specific surface of hardened air-void systems were measured by optical microscopy on polished sections according to ASTM C457. Freeze-thaw exposure followed a modified version of EN 12390-9 (CIF test), with mass loss, dynamic modulus of elasticity and visual scaling documented after 14, 28, 42 and 56 cycles. Non-air-entrained specimens showed mass loss reaching 1.8 kg m−2 and relative dynamic modulus below 60% after 56 cycles. Air-entrained specimens with spacing factor ≤ 0.20 mm maintained mass loss below 0.5 kg m−2 and relative dynamic modulus above 80%. The admixture dosage required was approximately 1.8 times the dosage effective in Portland cement concrete with the same aggregate, attributed to reduced surface tension of the alkaline mixing solution.

title: Combined sulphate and freeze-thaw exposure of alkali-activated mortars: a sequential and simultaneous test programme
abstract: The interaction of sulphate attack and freeze-thaw cycling was investigated in a 2 × 2 experimental design: specimens were subjected to sulphate immersion (5% Na2SO4) only, freeze-thaw cycling only, sequential exposure (sulphate then freeze-thaw), and simultaneous exposure in a sulphate solution during each freeze-thaw cycle. Binder composition was fixed at 50:50 slag–fly ash activated with Ms = 1.0 sodium silicate. After 300 freeze-thaw cycles (with sulphate), the simultaneous exposure reduced compressive strength by 38% relative to reference, compared with 19% for sulphate alone and 24% for freeze-thaw alone. Mercury intrusion porosimetry showed that simultaneous exposure produced a bimodal pore size distribution absent in single-mechanism tests, with a new peak around 0.8 µm attributed to ettringite-like phase precipitation. The study highlights the inadequacy of single-stressor durability tests for materials intended for use in sub-zero continental climates.

title: Thermogravimetric analysis of reaction product assemblages in ternary alkali-activated systems containing calcined clay
abstract: Ternary binders were formulated by partially replacing fly ash (20 or 40 wt%) with calcined illitic clay sourced from a brick production facility near Subotica. Calcination temperatures of 650, 750 and 850 °C were tested; clay calcined at 750 °C showed the highest pozzolanic reactivity by the modified Chapelle test. Pastes activated with 6 wt% Na2O (Ms = 0.8) were cured at 40 °C for 28 days and analysed by TGA-DSC. The principal endotherms were assigned to gel water release (100–250 °C), structural dehydroxylation of N-A-S-H and C-A-S-H gel (250–600 °C), and residual carbonate decomposition (650–750 °C). Bound water content increased from 8.4 to 11.7 wt% as calcined clay replacement rose from 0 to 40%, consistent with higher degree of reaction measured by selective dissolution. Compressive strength peaked at 20 wt% replacement (47 MPa at 28 days), declining at 40 wt% due to dilution of the slag fraction.

title: Alkali-activated binders in the context of circular construction: a chapter on precursor availability and quality in the Danube–Tisza region
abstract: This book chapter reviews the material flows, chemical quality and spatial distribution of industrial by-products suitable for alkali activation in the Danube–Tisza interfluvial region, covering Serbia, Hungary and the northern part of Romania. Annual fly ash production at active thermal power stations is estimated at 2.1 million tonnes for Serbia and 4.6 million tonnes for Hungary, with chemical data compiled from publicly available monitoring reports and the authors' own XRF database of 47 samples collected between 2010 and 2020. Slag availability is more limited, concentrated around two steel processing sites. The chapter discusses variability in fly ash chemistry as a function of coal blending, seasonal demand fluctuations, and long-term phase-out trajectories of coal power. It concludes with a framework for precursor qualification that construction companies or precast producers could apply without specialised laboratory infrastructure, using only particle size, loss on ignition and strength activity index measurements.

title: Shrinkage and cracking behaviour of alkali-activated slag–fly ash pastes: restrained ring test and digital image correlation measurements
abstract: Autogenous and drying shrinkage of pastes with slag–fly ash ratios of 30:70, 50:50 and 70:30 were measured by corrugated tube method and by a 150 mm prismatic specimen method for up to 90 days. Restrained shrinkage was assessed using the ASTM C1581 ring test at 50% relative humidity. Digital image correlation was applied to the outer surface of ring specimens to track strain field evolution prior to first cracking. The 70:30 blend cracked at 22 days with a surface crack width of 0.12 mm; the 30:70 blend reached 58 days without cracking under the same conditions. Free autogenous shrinkage values at 28 days were 1240, 870 and 590 µε for 70:30, 50:50 and 30:70 respectively. XRD showed that hydrotalcite formation in high-slag blends correlated with higher autogenous shrinkage, consistent with internal chemical contraction during slag hydration. Results confirm that cracking risk is a primary design constraint for high-slag alkali-activated systems.

title: Chloride transport in alkali-activated slag–fly ash concretes after prolonged sulphate pre-exposure
abstract: Concrete cylinders (100 × 200 mm) based on 50:50 slag–fly ash binder were exposed to 5% Na2SO4 solution for 0, 90, 180 and 360 days, then subjected to rapid chloride migration testing (NT Build 492) and non-steady-state migration coefficient Dnssm was determined. Pre-exposure to sulphate for 90 days reduced Dnssm from 4.3 to 3.1 × 10−12 m2 s−1, attributed to pore-blocking by secondary reaction products. Beyond 180 days of sulphate pre-exposure, Dnssm increased to 5.8 × 10−12 m2 s−1, coinciding with visible surface scaling and a 12% loss of compressive strength. Synchrotron micro-CT scans on subsampled cores (conducted at ESRF, Grenoble) revealed a 1.5 mm thick degraded surface layer with 34% higher connected porosity than the interior after 360-day sulphate pre-exposure. The data suggest that service-life models based solely on chloride diffusion coefficients measured on undamaged specimens will overestimate durability in environments combining both stressors.

title: Graph-based segmentation of vegetation clusters in airborne LiDAR point clouds for riparian corridor mapping
abstract: Riparian vegetation corridors along drainage channels pose segmentation challenges for standard voxel or region-growing methods due to overlapping crown boundaries and variable stem density. This paper presents a graph-based segmentation workflow in which each point is a node and edges are established between k=10 nearest neighbours weighted by Euclidean distance and return intensity difference. Minimum-cut partitioning is used to isolate individual tree crowns, followed by a random forest classifier that assigns each crown to one of four structural classes: single tree, shrub cluster, reed bed, and woody debris. The workflow was applied to 34 km of riparian corridor along two Vojvodina watercourses scanned at 6 points per square metre. Crown delineation accuracy, assessed against 310 manually delineated reference crowns, yielded a detection rate of 83% and a mean position error of 0.6 m. Structural classification overall accuracy was 85%. Processing the 34 km corridor on the GPU cluster took 18 minutes. Results are discussed in the context of flood risk vegetation management and hydraulic roughness parameterisation.

title: GNSS-Derived Precipitable Water Vapour over the Danube River Corridor: Validation and Spatial Patterns
abstract: Integrated precipitable water vapour (IPW) was derived from ZTD estimates at 22 GNSS stations along the Danube corridor from Regensburg to the Danube Delta, using in-situ pressure and temperature from co-located sensors. The period covered 2013–2016. IPW was compared with ERA5 reanalysis output and with MODIS near-infrared retrievals on cloud-free days. Biases against ERA5 were below 1.0 kg/m² at all stations; RMS differences ranged from 1.4 to 2.8 kg/m². Seasonal IPW cycles showed higher amplitudes over the Pannonian Basin than over upstream Alpine sites. Diurnal IPW anomalies were examined during three heavy-precipitation events; in each case, a rapid IPW increase of 6–12 kg/m² preceded peak rainfall by 2–4 hours. The dataset has been archived in NetCDF format and is available for further atmospheric studies.

title: Procena perceptivnog realizma animiranih lica metodom skale srednje ocene: komparativna studija za srpski govor
abstract: Studija ispituje korelaciju između objektivnih metrika animacije lica — dinamičke vremenske deformacije (DTW) između generisanih i referentnih trajektorija blendshape koeficijenata, kao i RMSE pozicija ključnih tačaka — i subjektivnih ocena realizma koje daju ispitanici putem MOS skale. U eksperimentu je učestvovalo 58 ispitanika koji su ocenjivali 120 kratkih animiranih isečaka u trajanju od 3 do 7 sekundi, generisanih pomoću tri različite metode: HMM-zasnovane, regresionog stabla i interpolacione osnove. Utvrđena je umerena korelacija (Spirmanov ρ = 0,61) između DTW mere i MOS ocene za naturalnost, dok RMSE nije pokazao statistički značajnu vezu sa perceptivnim kvalitetom. Nalazi ukazuju da objektivne metrike mogu biti nepouzdane kao jedini pokazatelji kvaliteta animacije u situacijama kada postoje suptilne razlike u ekspresivnosti. Preporučena je kombinovana evaluaciona procedura koja uključuje i perceptivnu komponentu.

title: Uticaj ko-artikulacije na tačnost vizem sekvenci u animaciji lica: analiza trojke konsonat-vokal-konsonat u srpskom
abstract: Rad analizira uticaj ko-artikulacije u trojkama konsonat-vokal-konsonat (KVK) na preciznost vizem sekvenci generisanih automatskim sistemima za animaciju lica. Elektromagnetni artikulograf korišćen je za merenje pokreta usana, čeljusti i jezika 12 govornika srpskog tokom izgovora 540 KVK trojki odabranih da ravnomerno pokrivaju fonemski inventar. Rezultati pokazuju da trajanje vizema za medijalni vokal opada u proseku za 23% u kontekstu okluziva u okolnim slogovima, u poređenju sa izolovanim izgovorom. Sistemi zasnovani na fiksnim vizem trajanjima sistematski precenjuju dužinu medijalne vokalske faze u ovim kontekstima. Predložen je korekcioni faktor koji uvažava klase okružujućih konsonanata i koji smanjuje DTW grešku na testnom skupu za 11,4% bez dodatnog treninga modela. Nalaze je moguće primeniti i na druge jezike sa sličnim fonotaktičkim ograničenjima.

title: Sequence-to-Sequence Learning of Viseme Trajectories for Real-Time Speech-Driven Facial Animation
abstract: This work presents a sequence-to-sequence architecture with attention mechanism trained to map phoneme label sequences to continuous blendshape coefficient trajectories for facial animation. The encoder processes phoneme embeddings enriched with duration and stress features; the decoder outputs 46-dimensional blendshape vectors at 30 Hz. Training used 6.2 hours of paired speech and performance-capture data from two female and two male Serbian speakers. The attention mechanism was shown to focus on a window of two to three adjacent phonemes, consistent with the physiological range of co-articulation. At inference time the model achieves a mean per-frame latency of 11 ms on a consumer GPU. A forced-choice perceptual study with 50 participants comparing the proposed model against an LSTM baseline found a significant preference for the proposed system on naturalness (p < 0.01, Wilcoxon signed-rank test). No significant difference was found on intelligibility scores.

title: Benchmarking Transformer-Based Models for Speech-Driven Facial Animation on a Multilingual Corpus
abstract: We present a systematic comparison of four transformer-based architectures — a vanilla encoder-decoder, a conformer encoder with autoregressive decoder, a non-autoregressive parallel decoder, and a diffusion-based conditional model — trained on a multilingual corpus covering Serbian, Croatian, and Slovak speech totalling 18.4 hours of motion-capture-aligned data. Models are evaluated on three metrics: DTW error on blendshape coefficient trajectories, lip-sync accuracy assessed by an automated audio-visual correspondence classifier, and perceptual naturalness rated by 60 participants in a mean opinion score study. The non-autoregressive parallel decoder achieved the best real-time performance at 8 ms per frame while sacrificing 4% DTW accuracy relative to the conformer model. The diffusion model produced the highest MOS naturalness score (4.1/5) but required 340 ms per frame, excluding it from interactive use. Correlation between DTW and MOS across all conditions was moderate (r = 0.54), reaffirming the limited reliability of DTW as a standalone proxy for perceptual quality.

title: Generisanje micro-ekspresija u animaciji lica pokretanoj govorom primenom uslovnih generativnih mreža
abstract: Standardni sistemi za animaciju lica pokretanu govorom fokusiraju se isključivo na pokrete usana i čeljusti, zanemarujući suptilne neverbalne signale kao što su micro-ekspresije. Ovaj rad istražuje mogućnost uslovnog generisanja micro-ekspresija — minimalnih mišićnih pokreta u trajanju 80–250 ms — koje su statistički korelisane sa fonetskim i prozodijskim karakteristikama govornih iskaza. Korišćen je skup podataka od 2.800 video snimaka 24 govornika anotiranih Facsimile akcionim jedinicama (FACU), pri čemu su micro-ekspresije identifikovane poluautomatski. Uslovna generativna mreža trenirana je da predviđa verovatnoću pojave i intenzitet micro-ekspresija na osnovu kontekstualnog reprezentacionog vektora iz seq2seq animacionog modela. Objektivna evaluacija na testnom skupu pokazala je F1 meru od 0,68 za detekciju micro-ekspresija, dok je perceptivna studija sa 45 ispitanika pokazala da prisustvo generisanih micro-ekspresija poboljšava ocenu prirodnosti animacije za 0,4 MOS boda u proseku.

title: Lightweight Speech-Driven Facial Animation for Embedded and Mobile Platforms Using Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Deploying neural speech-driven facial animation on mobile or embedded devices is constrained by memory bandwidth and compute budgets. This work applies knowledge distillation to compress a 47-million-parameter conformer seq2seq teacher model into a 3.2-million-parameter student model targeting ARM Cortex-A78 and mobile GPU architectures. The student model is trained with a compound loss combining standard regression loss on blendshape outputs and a feature-level mimicry loss aligned to the teacher's attention states. On a benchmark smartphone (mid-range, 2023), the student achieves 28 ms end-to-end latency per frame compared to 210 ms for the teacher running on the same device. DTW error of the student is 12% higher than the teacher on the Serbian test set, and MOS naturalness drops by 0.3 points (from 3.9 to 3.6). Battery consumption measurements show the student uses 68% less energy per animated second, a relevant factor for wearable assistive applications.

title: Subjektivna evaluacija animacije lica generisane od strane malih jezičkih modela: metodološki okvir i pilot istraživanje
abstract: Jak porast malih jezičkih modela (SLM) otvara pitanje da li se seq2seq animacioni sistemi mogu upariti sa SLM-ovima za generisanje potpunih razgovornih avatara na uređajima bez oblaka. Ovaj rad predlaže metodološki okvir za subjektivnu evaluaciju animacija lica koje su izlaz takve integrisane arhitekture, razlikujući komponente: kvalitet govora, kvalitet animacije, audio-vizuelna sinhronizacija i globalni dojam koherentnosti. Pilot istraživanje sprovedeno je sa 38 ispitanika koji su ocenjivali animacije generisane u kombinaciji jednog SLM-a (1,3 milijarde parametara) i distilovanog animacionog modela opisanog u prethodnom radu. Intraklasni koeficijent korelacije između ocenjivača iznosio je 0,71 za sinhronizaciju i 0,63 za koherentnost, što ukazuje na prihvatljivu pouzdanost predloženih skala. Identifikovane su ključne tačke neslaganja između ocenjivača i predložene su revizije instrukcija za buduće studije.

title: Prebiotic dietary fibre consumption and plasma flavonoid kinetics: a crossover pilot study in healthy adults
abstract: Human intervention data linking prebiotic intake to flavonoid pharmacokinetics remain sparse. We conducted a randomised two-period crossover pilot study in 14 healthy adults (7 female, 7 male; mean age 28 ± 4 years). Participants consumed 10 g/day inulin or maltodextrin (control) for 21 days before a single oral dose of a standardised green tea extract standardised to 200 mg epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Blood was collected at 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 h post-dose; urine was collected over 24 h. Plasma EGCG and its microbial catabolites (5-(3,5-dihydroxyphenyl)-γ-valerolactone and 3,5-dihydroxyphenylpropionic acid) were quantified by LC-MS/MS. After inulin pretreatment, EGCG Cmax decreased by 18% (p = 0.041) whereas urinary catabolite excretion increased 2.1-fold, suggesting accelerated colonic catabolism. Gut microbiome composition (16S rRNA sequencing of faecal samples) showed significant Bifidobacterium enrichment following inulin. The trial was registered at the national clinical trial registry (ClinicalTrials.RS). Though limited by sample size, results provide quantitative support for prebiotic-mediated remodelling of flavonoid bioavailability.

title: Caco-2 monolayer permeability of microbial quercetin catabolites produced under fibre-modified fermentation conditions
abstract: Gut microbial catabolism converts quercetin into a spectrum of phenolic acids and valerolactones of varying polarity, potentially altering intestinal transport compared with the parent aglycone. We collected fermentation supernatants from pectin- and inulin-supplemented batch cultures (human faecal inoculum, n = 5) and applied them to Caco-2 cell monolayers (transepithelial electrical resistance > 400 Ω·cm²) in an apical-to-basolateral transport assay. Individual catabolites were identified and quantified by UHPLC-Orbitrap MS. Apparent permeability (Papp) values ranged from 0.4 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s for homovanillic acid to 9.8 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s for 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetic acid. Pectin-conditioned supernatants yielded a catabolite mixture with a higher mean Papp than inulin-conditioned or control supernatants (6.1 vs. 4.3 vs. 3.2 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s, respectively). Cell viability (MTT assay) was unaffected at the concentrations tested. The data indicate that prebiotic type influences not only the identity of flavonoid catabolites but also their expected intestinal absorptive capacity.

title: Prebiotic fibre supplementation and flavonoid metabolism: a scoping review of in vitro, animal, and human evidence (2000–2022)
abstract: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science using a predefined PICOS framework for studies investigating the interaction between dietary prebiotic fibres and flavonoid pharmacokinetics or biotransformation published between January 2000 and December 2022. Of 1,847 records screened, 68 met inclusion criteria: 31 in vitro, 22 animal, and 15 human studies. In vitro models consistently reported altered catabolite spectra when prebiotic fibres were co-fermented with flavonoids, but methodological heterogeneity (fibre dose, flavonoid concentration, inoculum source) was high. Animal studies generally showed increased urinary phenolic acid excretion (median increase 1.8-fold across studies); however, fibre type, dose, and duration varied widely. Human trials were limited to eight randomised controlled designs, all with fewer than 30 participants. Key gaps identified include absence of pharmacokinetic modelling integrating microbial activity, scarcity of data on flavonoid glycoside versus aglycone comparisons, and lack of studies in older adults. A standardised in vitro-to-in vivo translation framework is needed.

title: Arabinoxylan from wheat bran modulates caecal microbiota and increases plasma naringenin after orange peel extract gavage in Wistar rats
abstract: Arabinoxylan (AX) is an abundant cereal fibre with documented prebiotic activity, yet its interaction with flavanone absorption has not been characterised in vivo. Wistar rats (n = 40, male, 8 weeks) were randomised to receive either 5% (w/w) wheat bran AX diet or isocaloric control diet for four weeks, followed by a single gavage of a standardised orange peel extract (containing 50 mg/kg naringenin and 45 mg/kg hesperidin). Blood was collected at 1, 2, 4, 8, and 24 h post-gavage; caecal contents were harvested at 24 h. Plasma naringenin AUC₀₋₂₄ was 34% higher in AX-fed animals (p = 0.009, Mann–Whitney U). Caecal microbiome analysis (16S rRNA sequencing) showed enrichment of Prevotella and Roseburia in the AX group. Short-chain fatty acid concentrations in caecal contents were significantly elevated in AX animals (total SCFA 82.4 vs. 54.3 µmol/g wet weight, p = 0.003). Histological assessment of colonic mucosa revealed no treatment-related adverse changes. Results support AX as a fibre candidate for enhancing flavanone systemic exposure.

title: Development of a simplified two-compartment in silico model predicting plasma flavonoid exposure as a function of fibre-driven microbiome changes
abstract: Computational tools that link measurable microbiome outputs to flavonoid pharmacokinetics could reduce the need for costly human trials. We assembled a two-compartment ordinary differential equation (ODE) model parameterised from our own published fermentation and Caco-2 data alongside literature-derived absorption rate constants for six flavonoids (quercetin, luteolin, naringenin, apigenin, kaempferol, EGCG). Microbial catabolism was represented by first-order degradation terms whose rate constants were estimated from 16S rRNA-derived functional proxies (Bifidobacterium and Ruminococcaceae relative abundances as predictors of fibre breakdown capacity). The model was calibrated against our 2019 human crossover dataset (EGCG) and validated against two external human datasets from the literature. Predicted versus observed plasma AUC values fell within a 1.5-fold range for four of six flavonoids. Sensitivity analysis identified the colonic transit time and initial microbial Bifidobacterium fraction as the most influential parameters. The model code and parameter sets are deposited in an open repository. Limitations include neglect of enterohepatic recirculation and individual variability in gut pH.

title: Gut microbiome-mediated biotransformation of isoflavones under inulin and resistant starch supplementation: comparative fermentation data
abstract: Isoflavones share structural features with flavonoids but undergo distinct microbial transformations, most notably equol production from daidzein by a subset of human gut bacteria. We compared fermentation of a soy isoflavone mixture (daidzein 40 µM, genistein 30 µM, glycitein 10 µM) under supplementation with long-chain inulin (lcInulin), high-amylose maize resistant starch (RS2), or no added fibre using a single-stage batch model (n = 6 donors, 48 h). Equol producers were identified in four of six donors by 16S rRNA profiling. In equol-producing donors, lcInulin increased equol yield to 8.3 ± 1.4 µM compared with 4.9 ± 0.9 µM for RS2 and 3.1 ± 0.8 µM for control. In non-equol-producing donors, neither fibre induced equol formation. Genistein ring-fission was enhanced by RS2 (6-hydroxydaidzein yield 11.2 µM vs. 6.4 µM under inulin). The data highlight the donor-specific and fibre-dependent nature of isoflavone catabolism and have implications for soy-based dietary supplement design.

title: Thermal performance of lightweight green roof substrates under simulated summer heat in a continental climate
abstract: This study evaluated five substrate mixtures differing in pumice-to-compost ratios (ranging from 70:30 to 100:0 by volume) installed in 0.8 m² lysimeter trays on a south-facing test roof at the University of Novi Sad experimental station. Surface temperatures and substrate temperatures at 5 cm and 10 cm depths were logged at 15-minute intervals throughout July and August 2011. Reference bare-membrane trays served as controls. Mixtures containing at least 20% compost fraction reduced peak surface temperatures by 6.3–8.1 °C compared to controls on days exceeding 35 °C ambient temperature. Purely mineral substrates showed lower peak temperatures than the control but performed significantly worse than compost-amended variants during prolonged dry spells. Substrate moisture content, measured gravimetrically at weekly intervals, declined faster in high-pumice mixes. Results suggest that modest organic amendment improves thermal buffering without compromising drainage adequacy for extensive roof applications in the Vojvodina region.

title: Establishment success and canopy cover of seven Sedum species on extensive green roofs in Novi Sad: a two-year field trial
abstract: Seven Sedum species commonly available in the Serbian horticultural trade were planted at uniform density (36 plugs/m²) on six identical green roof test modules (1.2 m × 0.8 m, 8 cm substrate depth) installed on a flat-roofed residential building in the Liman district of Novi Sad. Canopy cover, plant height, and mortality rate were assessed monthly from April 2013 to October 2014. Sedum spurium and Sedum album achieved the highest two-year cover (84% and 79% respectively) and the lowest mortality. Sedum telephium showed poor establishment, with 41% mortality by the second summer. Thermal infrared photography conducted on five clear July days confirmed that plots with cover above 70% maintained canopy surface temperatures 9–13 °C below bare substrate plots. Species performance was correlated with measured substrate moisture at time of installation and with distance from drainage outlets. Recommendations for species selection in residential retrofit applications in the Vojvodina lowland are provided.

title: Effect of substrate depth (6, 10, and 15 cm) on soil temperature and Sedum album biomass accumulation across three growing seasons
abstract: Substrate depth is a primary determinant of both structural load and thermal mass in extensive green roofs. This paper reports results from a factorial experiment at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station using three substrate depths (6, 10, 15 cm) crossed with two substrate types (standard pumice-loam mix and a local brick-rubble recycled aggregate mix). Sedum album was used as the sole plant species. Soil temperature was recorded continuously at mid-depth; above-ground biomass was harvested at the end of each growing season (2013–2015) and oven-dried at 70 °C. The 15 cm depth reduced maximum mid-depth summer temperature by 4.7 °C relative to the 6 cm treatment. Biomass accumulation was 38% greater at 10 cm than at 6 cm but showed no significant further increase at 15 cm. The recycled aggregate substrate performed comparably to the standard mix in biomass terms but retained 12% less moisture at field capacity. Findings support the use of 10 cm as a pragmatic compromise for residential flat-roof retrofits where load constraints apply.

title: Urban heat island intensity in residential blocks of Novi Sad: a mobile transect survey across twelve neighbourhoods
abstract: Mobile air temperature measurements were conducted along 14 pre-defined transects crossing twelve residential districts of Novi Sad during the summers of 2016 and 2017. Measurements were taken at 1.5 m height using a calibrated thermohygrometer mounted on a bicycle, following the methodology described by Oke (1973) adapted for low-rise continental urban environments. Each transect was repeated on at least eight clear, low-wind evenings (wind speed < 2 m/s) between 22:00 and 00:00 local time. Maximum urban heat island intensity reached 4.8 °C in the densely built Grbavica district compared to a reference rural station at Rimski Šančevi. Districts with higher proportions of tree canopy and any vegetation showed attenuated heat island values. Green roof coverage was mapped using municipal GIS data for the same districts, revealing less than 0.4% of flat residential roof area was vegetated. The data provide a baseline for evaluating future green roof expansion scenarios and their expected contribution to heat island reduction.

title: Zeolite addition to green roof substrates: effects on water retention, plant growth, and surface cooling in a hot dry summer
abstract: Zeolite clinoptilolite, available as a by-product of regional mineral processing, was incorporated into a pumice-based green roof substrate at 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20% volumetric fractions. Each mixture was loaded into 0.5 m² experimental modules at 8 cm depth, planted with a Sedum spurium monoculture, and monitored during the summer of 2019 at the Faculty of Agriculture rooftop facility. Substrate volumetric water content was measured hourly using capacitance probes. Surface temperatures were logged with infrared sensors above each module. Modules with 10% zeolite addition retained substrate moisture approximately 1.4 days longer after irrigation events compared to the zeolite-free control, and showed peak surface temperatures 3.1 °C lower during the hottest recorded day (38.4 °C ambient). The 20% zeolite treatment showed no further improvement in cooling but reduced drainage rate by 22%, which may create waterlogging risks. Plant biomass was significantly higher in the 10% and 20% zeolite treatments (p < 0.05). The 10% addition rate is recommended for practical use.

title: Comparing native Pannonian succulent species with commercial Sedum cultivars on extensive green roofs: survival, cover, and thermal performance over 30 months
abstract: Commercial Sedum cultivars dominate European green roof practice, yet native Pannonian succulent and semi-succulent species may be better adapted to local continental drought stress. This study compared six commercial Sedum cultivars against four native taxa — Jovibarba hirta, Sempervivum marmoreum, Sedum maximum (native ecotype), and Phedimus hybridus — installed on nine replicated rooftop modules at three residential buildings in Novi Sad (Sajmište, Liman III, and Adice districts) from March 2020 to September 2022. Survival rate, projected canopy cover, and leaf chlorophyll index (SPAD) were measured bimonthly. Infrared temperature measurements were taken on ten clear days per summer. Jovibarba hirta and Sempervivum marmoreum showed survival rates of 91% and 88% after 30 months, comparable to the best commercial cultivar (Sedum album 'Coral Carpet', 93%). Cooling effect was similar across surviving species once cover exceeded 65%. Native taxa showed slower initial establishment but lower variability in summer SPAD values, suggesting more stable photosynthetic activity under heat stress. Cost data from nurseries indicate native taxa were 15–22% cheaper per plug at the volumes tested.

title: Modelling the district-scale cooling potential of green roof retrofits in Novi Sad using a simplified energy balance approach
abstract: This paper applies a simplified energy balance model to estimate the urban air temperature reduction achievable if flat-roofed residential buildings constructed between 1950 and 1985 in four Novi Sad districts (Grbavica, Sajmište, Liman I–II, and Novo Naselje) were retrofitted with extensive green roofs at varying coverage rates (25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of eligible roof area). Building footprint data were derived from a municipal cadastre dataset; eligible flat roof area was estimated at 2.14 km² across the four districts. Thermal parameters for the modelled green roof layers were calibrated from the authors' earlier field measurements. Simulations suggest that 50% retrofit coverage could reduce mean afternoon air temperature in street canyons by 0.6–1.1 °C on a typical hot summer day, with the largest effect in Grbavica where roof-to-ground-surface area ratio is highest. The model does not account for plant water stress under prolonged drought, which the authors identify as the primary source of uncertainty. Results are intended to inform municipal green infrastructure policy rather than serve as engineering design values.

title: Irrigation frequency and volume thresholds for drought-stressed Sedum and Jovibarba on extensive green roofs during a 47-day rainless period
abstract: The summer of 2024 produced a 47-consecutive-day rainless period in Novi Sad (June 12 – July 28), providing an opportunity to study the response of green roof plantings under extreme drought without artificial manipulation. Twelve instrumented modules planted with Sedum album, Sedum spurium, and Jovibarba hirta at the Faculty of Agriculture rooftop facility were divided into three irrigation regimes: no supplemental irrigation, single emergency irrigation at 15 mm when substrate VWC fell below 5%, and fortnightly irrigation at 10 mm. Surface temperature, canopy cover, SPAD, and electrolyte leakage (as a measure of membrane damage) were monitored weekly. By day 47, no-irrigation Sedum album plots had lost 58% cover and showed electrolyte leakage values indicative of severe stress; Jovibarba hirta retained 79% cover in the same treatment. Single emergency irrigation at the 5% VWC threshold prevented cover loss exceeding 20% in all three species. Results provide quantitative thresholds relevant for building owners deciding whether to install supplemental drip irrigation on residential green roofs in the Vojvodina region.

title: Rumination drops from collar sensors predict clinical mastitis two days early
abstract: Mastitis remains the most economically damaging disease in dairy production, and its early detection is critical for reducing antibiotic use and milk losses. This study evaluated the capacity of rumination time data, collected continuously via commercial activity collars fitted to 214 Holstein-Friesian cows on three Vojvodina dairy farms, to predict clinical mastitis onset up to 48 hours before veterinary confirmation. Rumination duration per two-hour interval was extracted and modelled using a mixed-effects change-point detection algorithm, accounting for parity, days in milk, and individual baseline variation. Cows subsequently diagnosed with clinical mastitis showed a statistically significant and progressive decline in rumination time beginning 46–52 hours prior to diagnosis (mean drop: 18.3 min/2 h block, p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.87 for the 48-hour predictive window, with a sensitivity of 81% and specificity of 84% at the optimal threshold. False-positive rates were highest in primiparous cows during the first 30 days in milk. These findings demonstrate that rumination collar data, processed through appropriate statistical models, can serve as a reliable, non-invasive early warning tool for mastitis, enabling timely intervention and supporting antimicrobial stewardship on commercial dairy farms.

title: Heat stress and milk yield on Vojvodina dairy farms
abstract: Heat stress is an increasingly pressing challenge for dairy cattle productivity in continental European climates, including the Vojvodina plain of northern Serbia, where summer temperatures regularly exceed thermal comfort thresholds. This conference study examined the relationship between temperature-humidity index (THI) and daily milk yield across six commercial dairy farms in Vojvodina over three consecutive summer seasons (2019–2021), comprising records from 1,847 Holstein-Friesian cows. Farm-level microclimate data were collected via on-site weather stations, and individual daily milk yields were extracted from automated milking and parlour management systems. A linear mixed model incorporating THI, parity, days in milk, farm identity, and year as covariates revealed that each unit increase in THI above the threshold of 68 was associated with a mean reduction of 0.41 kg milk per cow per day (95% CI: 0.36–0.46 kg). Cumulative losses were most pronounced during July, averaging 3.2 kg/cow/day at peak THI values. Farms with mechanical ventilation and evaporative cooling systems demonstrated significantly attenuated yield losses compared to unmodified facilities. These results underscore the urgency of implementing heat abatement strategies and integrating THI monitoring into farm decision-support systems to mitigate climate-driven production losses in the region.

title: Integrating accelerometer and rumination data from neck collars for subclinical ketosis detection in early-lactation dairy cows
abstract: Subclinical ketosis is a metabolic disorder affecting a substantial proportion of dairy cows in the first weeks of lactation, causing reduced milk yield, impaired fertility, and increased susceptibility to secondary diseases. This study investigated whether the combined analysis of accelerometer-derived activity patterns and rumination time from commercially available neck collars could provide a non-invasive screening tool for subclinical ketosis in early-lactation Holstein-Friesian cows. A total of 312 cows on four farms in Vojvodina were enrolled from calving through day 30 in milk. Blood beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) was measured three times per week as the diagnostic gold standard, with subclinical ketosis defined as BHB ≥ 1.2 mmol/L. Collar sensor variables were extracted in 24-hour blocks and analysed using a random forest classifier trained on the first 14 days post-calving. The model achieved a sensitivity of 78% and specificity of 82% for subclinical ketosis detection, outperforming single-variable rumination-only models. Feature importance analysis identified nighttime rumination variability and step-count asymmetry as the strongest predictors. These results suggest that multi-parameter collar data analysis holds significant promise for on-farm metabolic health surveillance without the need for repeated blood sampling.

title: Benchmarking commercial precision livestock farming sensor platforms for dairy health monitoring: a field evaluation in Vojvodina
abstract: The commercial market for precision livestock farming (PLF) sensor systems has expanded rapidly, yet independent, field-level comparisons of competing platforms under identical farming conditions remain scarce. This study benchmarked three commercial PLF collar-based systems—designated PlatformA, PlatformB, and PlatformC for blinding—across twelve dairy herds totalling 2,104 Holstein-Friesian cows in Vojvodina over a twelve-month period. Platforms were evaluated on their accuracy for detecting oestrus, clinical mastitis, lameness, and feed intake reduction, using veterinarian-confirmed diagnoses as the reference standard. Significant inter-platform differences were found for mastitis detection sensitivity (range: 67–84%) and oestrus detection specificity (range: 71–91%). Data completeness, defined as the proportion of sensor readings successfully transmitted and stored, varied from 91.2% to 97.8% across platforms and was influenced by herd size and barn construction type. User-reported ease of integration with existing farm management software differed substantially and was identified as a key adoption barrier by farm managers. This evaluation provides evidence-based guidance for farmers and advisors selecting PLF tools and highlights the need for standardised performance reporting protocols within the industry.

title: Machine learning models for predicting somatic cell count elevation from continuous sensor data in commercial dairy herds
abstract: Elevated somatic cell count (SCC) in raw milk is a primary indicator of udder inflammation and a key determinant of milk quality premiums in dairy value chains. This study developed and validated machine learning models for predicting SCC elevation events (defined as individual test-day SCC > 200,000 cells/mL) from continuous wearable sensor data collected in six commercial dairy herds in northern Serbia over 18 months. Collar-derived variables including rumination time, lying behaviour, step count, and eating duration were aggregated into 24-hour feature vectors for 1,640 cows. Four model architectures were compared: logistic regression, gradient boosting, long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, and a stacked ensemble. The LSTM model demonstrated the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.89) for SCC elevation in a seven-day forward window, capturing temporal dynamics that static models missed. Gradient boosting achieved comparable performance (AUC = 0.86) with substantially lower computational requirements, making it better suited for on-farm edge deployment. Rumination time decline and increased nighttime restlessness were identified as the most informative predictors across all models. These findings support the development of automated SCC alert systems integrated with existing farm data infrastructure.

title: Lying behaviour patterns measured by accelerometer collars as indicators of lameness in Holstein-Friesian dairy cows
abstract: Lameness is among the most prevalent welfare and productivity challenges in modern dairy systems, yet routine locomotion scoring is time-consuming and subject to observer variability. This study assessed whether automated analysis of lying behaviour parameters derived from neck-collar accelerometers could serve as a reliable lameness indicator in a commercial herd setting. Data were collected from 487 Holstein-Friesian cows on five farms in Vojvodina over a six-month period. Lying duration, lying bout frequency, and bout length were extracted in 48-hour rolling windows and compared against weekly locomotion scores performed by two trained observers using a five-point scale. Cows assigned locomotion scores of 3 or higher showed significantly reduced lying bout frequency (mean: 7.1 vs. 9.8 bouts/24 h, p < 0.001) and altered lying duration compared to sound cows, after controlling for parity and stage of lactation. A classification tree using three lying variables correctly identified lame cows with 76% sensitivity and 80% specificity. The results indicate that collar-based lying behaviour monitoring can augment or partially substitute periodic locomotion scoring, particularly on large farms where manual assessment of every cow is impractical.

title: Precision livestock farming in small and medium dairy enterprises: adoption barriers and enablers in the Western Balkans
abstract: Despite the demonstrated technical benefits of precision livestock farming (PLF) technologies, adoption rates among small and medium dairy enterprises (SMEs) in southeastern Europe remain low. This study employed a mixed-methods approach—combining a structured questionnaire survey of 184 dairy farm operators across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia with 24 in-depth interviews—to identify the primary barriers to and enablers of PLF sensor technology adoption. Financial constraints were cited as the most significant barrier by 71% of respondents, followed by insufficient technical support infrastructure (58%) and lack of perceived need (44%). Positive adoption predictors included farm size above 100 cows, membership in a dairy cooperative, and prior engagement with any digital farm management tool. Farmers who had received subsidised demonstration trials reported significantly higher intention-to-adopt scores than those who had not. Interview data revealed widespread scepticism about data ownership and willingness to share sensor data with commercial platform providers. The findings have direct implications for agricultural extension services, equipment vendors, and policy designers aiming to improve PLF uptake in transition economies, and suggest that co-investment models and farmer-controlled data governance frameworks may be decisive enablers.

title: Sensor-based monitoring of transition cow health: a review of wearable technologies and data integration approaches
abstract: The transition period—spanning three weeks before to three weeks after calving—is the interval of greatest metabolic and immunological vulnerability in the dairy cow's lactation cycle, with the majority of production diseases originating during this window. This review synthesises evidence from 78 peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2023 examining the use of wearable sensor technologies—including neck collars, ear tags, boluses, and leg bands—for monitoring transition cow health. Technologies are evaluated on their capacity to detect or predict ketosis, hypocalcaemia, retained placenta, metritis, and mastitis using behavioural, physiological, and rumination-derived variables. The review finds that collar-based rumination and activity monitoring is the best-validated modality, with multiple studies confirming predictive value for ketosis and mastitis in the early post-partum period. Bolus-based rumen temperature sensors show promise for hypocalcaemia detection but require further large-scale validation. A key gap identified across the literature is the absence of integrated multi-sensor data fusion frameworks capable of providing a unified health risk score during transition. Future research directions include standardised disease definition protocols, open data initiatives, and the development of real-time decision-support tools compatible with existing herd management software.

title: Effect of automated milking system adoption on udder health and mastitis incidence on family dairy farms in Vojvodina
abstract: Automated milking systems (AMS) alter milking frequency, teat condition, and human-animal interactions in ways that may influence udder health outcomes. This study examined changes in clinical mastitis incidence rate and quarter-level somatic cell count before and after AMS installation on eleven family-scale dairy farms in Vojvodina, using a two-year pre-installation and two-year post-installation observational design covering 638 Holstein-Friesian cows. Clinical mastitis incidence fell from a mean of 42.3 cases per 100 cow-years before AMS installation to 31.7 cases per 100 cow-years after (p = 0.018), while geometric mean SCC declined by 14.2% (p = 0.031). Improvements were most pronounced on farms that integrated AMS inline conductivity alerts with a veterinary response protocol. Farms lacking a structured mastitis management protocol showed no statistically significant improvement in either metric post-installation. Parity and breed were significant covariates. These findings suggest that AMS adoption can improve udder health on family dairy farms in the region, but only when accompanied by appropriate data interpretation and herd management protocols, pointing to the need for extension support alongside technology transfer.

title: Benchmarking gradient boosting and recurrent architectures on sparse monthly e-commerce revenue series
abstract: E-commerce platforms with short operating histories often have fewer than 24 monthly revenue observations available when a first forecasting model is needed. This paper benchmarks XGBoost, LightGBM, a vanilla LSTM, and a stacked GRU network on a collection of 312 individual product-category revenue series drawn from four Serbian online retailers, each series containing between 12 and 36 observations. Models are evaluated using a rolling-origin procedure with a one-step-ahead horizon. Results show that LightGBM with lag features and calendar dummies outperforms recurrent architectures on series shorter than 20 observations, while the stacked GRU performs better on series exceeding 28 observations. The paper also reports that standard hyperparameter tuning via random search is unreliable at these sample sizes and recommends fixed, data-informed hyperparameter ranges derived from a held-out meta-dataset. Reproducible code and the anonymised dataset are made publicly available.

title: Synthetic data generation for meta-learning in revenue forecasting: fidelity, diversity, and downstream accuracy
abstract: Meta-learning for financial time-series forecasting requires large collections of heterogeneous series for meta-training, which are often unavailable in practice. This preprint investigates three synthetic data generation approaches—parameterised structural time-series models, variational autoencoders trained on a small real corpus, and a diffusion model conditioned on summary statistics—evaluated along three axes: statistical fidelity to real data (via distributional distances), diversity of generated series (measured by coverage of the feature space), and downstream meta-learning accuracy on held-out real series. Experiments use a real corpus of 480 weekly e-commerce revenue series as the reference distribution. The VAE generator achieves the best balance of fidelity and diversity, while the diffusion model produces the highest fidelity at the cost of lower diversity. Downstream, models meta-trained on VAE-generated data reach 94 percent of the accuracy achieved with real meta-training data, compared with 88 percent for structural model-generated data. The preprint also proposes a simple diagnostic for detecting distributional mismatch between synthetic and real series before meta-training.

title: Comparing task construction strategies for meta-learning on financial time series: episode length, stride, and sampling distribution effects
abstract: The performance of gradient-based meta-learning algorithms such as MAML and Reptile on time-series tasks is sensitive to how training episodes are constructed, yet systematic guidance on episode design is sparse. This paper conducts a controlled ablation study varying three episode construction parameters—support set length (4, 8, 16 observations), query set horizon (1, 2, 4 steps ahead), and series sampling distribution (uniform, stratified by variance, curriculum by difficulty)—across a meta-training corpus of 3,600 weekly e-commerce revenue series. Each of 36 design combinations is evaluated on 120 held-out series from a different market. Curriculum sampling by increasing series difficulty reduces RMSE by 8 percent on average relative to uniform sampling. Support set length of 8 observations represents a practical optimum, with longer support sets improving performance only marginally while increasing computation by 40 percent. Results are consistent across MAML and Reptile and across two encoder architectures.
