title: Saccadic velocity as an indicator of mental fatigue during prolonged form-filling tasks
abstract: This study investigated whether saccadic peak velocity decreases reliably as a function of time-on-task in a standardised form-filling scenario. Twenty-two undergraduate volunteers completed a 75-minute data-entry session while their eye movements were recorded at 250 Hz using a remote eye tracker. Sessions were divided into five 15-minute blocks, and saccadic velocity was extracted for horizontal saccades between 5° and 15° in amplitude. A repeated-measures ANOVA showed a statistically significant linear decline in mean peak velocity across blocks (F(4,84) = 11.3, p < 0.001, η² = 0.35). Self-reported fatigue scores on a visual analogue scale correlated with velocity decline (r = −0.61, p < 0.01). The results replicate findings from aviation research in an office-computing context and suggest that saccadic velocity monitoring could serve as a passive, unobtrusive fatigue detector in workplace software. Practical implications for automatic break-suggestion systems are discussed.

title: Pupil dilation response latency under varying display luminance: implications for cognitive load measurement
abstract: Pupil dilation is a widely used proxy for cognitive load, but the light reflex constitutes a significant confound when display luminance varies during task execution. This paper reports a controlled experiment with 18 participants who performed arithmetic tasks of three difficulty levels on screens set to four luminance levels (50, 100, 200, and 350 cd/m²). A linear mixed-effects model was used to separate the luminance-driven and task-driven components of pupil response. Results indicate that the latency of the task-evoked dilation peak increases by approximately 80 ms per doubling of background luminance, and amplitude is attenuated by up to 22% at the highest luminance setting. A simple luminance-correction formula is proposed and validated on a held-out dataset of 12 additional participants, reducing residual luminance-related variance by 67%. The correction is implemented as an open-source Python script released alongside the paper.

title: EEG-based classification of low and high cognitive load during software debugging tasks using LDA and SVM
abstract: Fourteen experienced software developers performed code-debugging tasks of controlled complexity while a 32-channel EEG was recorded. Trials were labelled as low or high cognitive load based on a median split of NASA-TLX scores collected immediately after each trial. Features extracted from EEG included band power in delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands for frontal, parietal, and occipital electrode clusters, yielding 48 features per 2-second epoch. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) and a radial-basis-function SVM were compared in a 10-fold cross-validation scheme. The SVM achieved a mean accuracy of 74.3% (SD = 6.1%), outperforming LDA (68.8%, SD = 7.4%). Theta power at Fz and alpha suppression at Pz were the most discriminative individual features. Analysis of between-subject variance revealed that three participants showed near-chance classification, suggesting that individual calibration sessions lasting at least 8 minutes are necessary for practical deployment.

title: Fixation duration distributions during reading versus visual search: a comparison across age groups
abstract: Eye movement characteristics differ systematically between task types and participant age groups, yet these interactions are rarely examined together in HCI settings. This study recorded eye movements of 60 participants divided into three age groups (18–25, 36–45, 56–65 years) performing both a text-reading task and a visual search task on a standard desktop display. Fixation duration distributions were modelled using ex-Gaussian fitting. The mu parameter (capturing the normal component) was significantly larger in the older group during visual search (mean 312 ms vs. 241 ms for the youngest group, p < 0.001), while differences during reading were smaller and less consistent. Saccade amplitude decreased with age in both tasks. These results have direct relevance for interface designers targeting older user populations, as standard eye-tracking metrics calibrated on young adults may misrepresent cognitive load in older users.
venue: Journal of Applied Human Factors in Computing

title: Cognitive load estimation in adaptive e-learning systems: methods and open challenges
abstract: This book chapter reviews approaches to real-time cognitive load estimation suitable for integration into adaptive e-learning platforms. The authors survey physiological methods (EEG, pupillometry, galvanic skin response) alongside behavioural indicators (response time, error rate, mouse dynamics) and discuss their trade-offs with respect to measurement accuracy, equipment cost, user acceptance, and latency. A taxonomy of adaptation strategies is proposed, ranging from content pacing adjustments triggered by threshold crossings to fully model-based personalisation using Bayesian knowledge tracing extended with load estimates. The chapter also discusses the ethical and privacy dimensions of continuous psychophysiological monitoring in educational settings, including data minimisation strategies and the implications of GDPR for biometric data collected in schools and universities. Representative case studies from existing prototypes are summarised, and a set of open research questions is identified for future work.
venue: Adaptive Learning Environments: Signals, Models and Interfaces (ed. Radu Ionescu, Péter Vámos), Springer

title: Simultaneous eye-tracking and EEG during a multi-window monitoring task: synchronisation protocol and data quality assessment
abstract: Combining eye-tracking and EEG in the same experimental session requires careful hardware synchronisation and joint artefact management. This paper describes a synchronisation protocol based on shared TTL trigger pulses and a shared millisecond-precision clock, validated on a 300 Hz remote eye tracker and a 32-channel amplifier. A multi-window monitoring task was used as the ecological context, in which 20 operators watched four simultaneous data streams and responded to anomaly events. Synchronisation error was measured at the sample level using photodiode-confirmed event markers and found to be below 3 ms in 97.4% of trials. Blink-related EEG artefacts were reduced by ICA decomposition seeded with blink events identified from the eye-tracker signal, resulting in a 41% reduction in blink-component residual power. The dataset and preprocessing scripts are made publicly available to support reproducibility.

title: Transfer learning from motor-imagery EEG models to cognitive-load classification: a feasibility study
abstract: Large labelled EEG datasets exist for motor-imagery brain–computer interface research, but equivalent resources for cognitive load are scarce. This preprint reports a feasibility study on whether convolutional neural network models pretrained on a publicly available motor-imagery corpus (109 subjects, BCI Competition IV dataset 2a equivalent) can be fine-tuned for cognitive-load binary classification using only 8 minutes of calibration data per new subject. Five subjects participated in a digit-span working memory task at three load levels while 32-channel EEG was recorded. Fine-tuned models reached a mean accuracy of 71.2% compared to 63.8% for models trained from scratch on the same calibration data. Training time was reduced from approximately 40 minutes to 6 minutes on a mid-range GPU. Results are preliminary due to the small sample, but suggest that transfer learning may partially address the data scarcity problem in cognitive-load EEG research.

title: Eye movement and EEG correlates of cognitive load in industrial dashboard monitoring: a field-compatible protocol
abstract: Most cognitive load studies use highly controlled laboratory paradigms that are difficult to translate to industrial monitoring workstations. This study developed and tested a protocol using a lightweight, mobile-compatible 8-channel EEG headset and a screen-mounted eye tracker on a replica industrial SCADA-style dashboard. Twenty operators from a regional utility company participated in sessions lasting approximately 45 minutes, during which dashboard complexity was systematically varied across four conditions. Theta/alpha ratio at frontal channels and mean pupil diameter both increased with dashboard complexity (p < 0.05 for all pairwise comparisons between adjacent complexity levels). Inter-subject reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients: ICC(3,1) for theta/alpha ratio was 0.67, indicating moderate reliability adequate for group-level analysis. The protocol is described in sufficient operational detail for replication in similar industrial settings. Limitations related to the use of consumer-grade EEG equipment are discussed.

title: Gaze entropy measures as real-time proxies for situation awareness degradation in dashboard-based tasks
abstract: Situation awareness (SA) degradation in monitoring tasks can precede overt errors by tens of seconds, and real-time detection would allow adaptive interfaces to intervene. This paper evaluates stationary gaze entropy (SGE) and transition entropy (TE) as candidate real-time indicators of SA degradation, operationalised as a missed-event rate exceeding 20% in a rolling 60-second window. Eye movements were recorded from 28 participants performing a 90-minute SCADA-like monitoring task in which a subset of events was hidden to manipulate SA without participants' awareness. SGE showed a receiver-operating characteristic AUC of 0.71 for detecting degradation windows, while TE achieved 0.68. A combined logistic regression model using both entropy measures, gaze velocity, and blink rate reached AUC = 0.78. Update latency of the real-time classifier was 420 ms on average using a sliding 5-second window, meeting the sub-second requirement for practical adaptive triggering.
venue: Human Factors: The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society

title: Cyclic Burst-Error-Correcting Codes over GF(2^m) with Controlled Redundancy
abstract: This paper investigates cyclic codes over GF(2^m) designed to correct single bursts of length up to b bits while maintaining a redundancy overhead below 2b+1 check symbols. Starting from the Fire code construction, we derive a family of shortened cyclic codes parameterised by field extension degree m and generator polynomial degree. For m ranging from 4 to 10 and burst lengths from 4 to 32 bits, we tabulate minimum redundancy codes and their generator polynomials. Simulation results over a binary symmetric channel with burst-noise injection show that all constructed codes achieve the theoretical Reiger bound within one extra redundancy bit for m ≥ 6. Algebraic decoding runs in O(b^2) operations per codeword using a modified syndrome-based algorithm. The codes are compared against Reed-Solomon interleaved schemes; for short blocks below 256 bits the proposed codes reduce decoder latency by approximately 18%. Generator polynomial tables are provided for immediate hardware implementation.
venue: Journal of Algebraic Coding and Information Systems

title: Saponin Profile of Gypsophila rochelii Collected from Fruška Gora: Isolation and Structural Assignment of Four Bidesmosidic Triterpene Glycosides
abstract: Four bidesmosidic saponins were isolated from the aerial parts of Gypsophila rochelii Griseb. collected at two sites on Fruška Gora mountain. Dried plant material (320 g) was extracted with 70% aqueous ethanol; the crude saponin fraction was obtained by n-butanol partition and purified by sequential Diaion HP-20 chromatography, followed by preparative reversed-phase HPLC. Compound structures were established by a combination of 1H, 13C, COSY, HSQC, HMBC, and ROESY experiments at 400 MHz, complemented by ESI-HRMS. Two compounds were identified as gypsogenin 3,28-O-bisglycosides bearing glucuronic acid at C-3 and a branched trisaccharide at C-28; the other two contained oleanolic acid as the aglycone with arabinose at C-3. Acid hydrolysis confirmed monosaccharide composition by TLC comparison against authentic standards. DPPH radical-scavenging IC50 values ranged from 48 to 97 µg/mL, lower than the positive control ascorbic acid at 12 µg/mL. The study provides the first documented saponin characterisation for this endemic Pannonian taxon.

title: Comparison of Extractability and Saponin Yield in Three Drying Methods Applied to Silene sendtneri Aerial Parts
abstract: Silene sendtneri Boiss., a narrow endemic of the Dinaric karst, was subjected to freeze-drying, oven-drying at 40 °C, and air-drying in shade to assess the effect of drying procedure on saponin extractability. Each 200 g batch was extracted with 70% ethanol under identical conditions; crude saponin fractions were weighed gravimetrically after n-butanol partition. Semi-preparative HPLC on a C18 column with acetonitrile–water gradient yielded six peaks; peak areas were integrated and compared across treatments. Freeze-dried material consistently produced 12–18% higher total saponin yield compared to oven-dried samples, while air-dried samples were intermediate. Structural identity of isolated fractions across treatments was confirmed by 1H NMR fingerprinting: all spectra matched a previously reported oleanane-type glycoside backbone. DPPH IC50 values did not differ significantly between drying methods (p > 0.05, ANOVA). Findings support freeze-drying as the preferred pre-treatment for preparative work when sample quantity permits.

title: Triterpenoid Saponins from Dianthus giganteus subsp. banaticus: Isolation, NMR Assignment and Haemolytic Index
abstract: Dianthus giganteus d'Urv. subsp. banaticus, confined largely to sandy grasslands of the Banat region, was investigated for saponin content. Five compounds were isolated from 450 g dry root material by ethanol extraction, butanol partition, and preparative HPLC (C18, 250 × 21.2 mm, flow 8 mL/min). Molecular formulae were determined by HRMS (orbitrap, accuracy < 2 ppm). Extensive 2D NMR (HSQC-TOCSY, HMBC, ROESY at 600 MHz) assigned four compounds as oleanolic acid glycosides with varying numbers of arabinose, rhamnose, and xylose units, and one compound as a quillaic acid 3-O-glucuronide. Haemolytic indices (HD50) were determined against sheep erythrocytes: values spanned 28–155 µg/mL, with the quillaic acid derivative exhibiting the lowest HD50, consistent with the literature on structurally related saponins. Radical-scavenging capacity by ABTS decolourisation correlated moderately (r = 0.61) with the number of sugar residues.

title: Saponins of Caryophyllaceae: Distribution, Structural Diversity and Bioactivity – A Decade Review
abstract: This chapter covers literature published between 2005 and 2015 on triterpenoid and steroidal saponins isolated from the family Caryophyllaceae, with emphasis on genera Gypsophila, Saponaria, Silene, Dianthus, and Vaccaria. Structural features are classified according to aglycone type (oleanane, ursane, dammarane) and glycosylation pattern. Representative isolation procedures are evaluated comparatively, highlighting shifts from classical column chromatography on silica to preparative HPLC. Bioactivity data are tabulated for radical-scavenging (DPPH, ABTS), haemolytic, anti-inflammatory, and cytotoxic assays; heterogeneous experimental conditions are discussed as limiting inter-study comparability. Particular attention is given to Balkan and Carpathian endemic taxa with limited previous chemical investigation. Taxonomic implications of saponin chemotypes are briefly discussed in relation to phylogenetic groupings within the family. The chapter identifies Silene and Dianthus species from the Western Balkans as under-explored sources of structurally diverse bidesmosidic glycosides.

title: Isolation of Six Saponins from Silene otites (L.) Wibel Collected at Three Altitude Gradients on Kopaonik and Their Differential Antioxidant Activities
abstract: Aerial parts of Silene otites were collected at 900, 1300, and 1750 m a.s.l. on Kopaonik National Park during peak flowering in June. Per-site extractions (150 g dry weight each) were processed identically through Diaion HP-20, Sephadex LH-20, and preparative HPLC. Six saponins were purified; all contained an oleanolic acid core. Sugar chains at C-3 ranged from monosaccharide to tetrasaccharide; C-28 ester linkages were present in two compounds. Structure elucidation relied on complete 1H and 13C assignment via HSQC and HMBC at 600 MHz and ROESY for glycosidic linkage geometry. Quantitative comparison by HPLC-UV (203 nm) showed a statistically significant increase in total saponin content with altitude (p = 0.009, Kruskal-Wallis). DPPH IC50 values differed across altitude groups (38–76 µg/mL), correlating with the degree of glycosylation as assessed by number of sugar units. The data support the hypothesis of altitude-driven intraspecific chemical variability.

title: HPLC-HRMS-Based Screening of Crude Saponin Fractions from Eight Dianthus Species Endemic to the Balkan Peninsula
abstract: Eight Dianthus species with restricted Balkan distribution – D. petraeus, D. gracilis, D. microlepis, D. nardiformis, D. myrtinervius, D. viscidus, D. integer, and D. pinifolius – were screened for saponin diversity using HPLC coupled to a high-resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometer in negative ionisation mode. Crude butanol fractions were prepared from 50 g dried aerial parts per species. A targeted extraction ion chromatogram workflow flagged 47 putative saponin peaks across all extracts, of which 21 were tentatively assigned as oleanane glycosides based on aglycone fragment ions at m/z 455.35 and 453.33. Cluster analysis of relative peak areas separated the eight species into three chemical groups partly congruent with morphological section boundaries. Three species (D. microlepis, D. nardiformis, D. pinifolius) showed mass features absent from the others, warranting preparative isolation. The study provides a prioritisation map for targeted isolation campaigns and represents the broadest comparative saponin screen for Balkan Dianthus to date.

title: Complete 1H and 13C NMR Assignment of a Quillaic Acid 3,28-O-Bisdesmoside from Vaccaria hispanica Growing on Disturbed Habitats of Vojvodina
abstract: A bidesmosidic saponin was isolated from the seeds of Vaccaria hispanica (Mill.) Rauschert collected from arable margins in Vojvodina. Purification involved ethanol extraction of 200 g seed material, butanol partition, and two-step preparative HPLC: first on a C18 column, then on a phenyl-hexyl column to achieve baseline separation from a co-eluting impurity. The purified compound (18.4 mg) was subjected to full 2D NMR characterisation at 600 MHz in DMSO-d6 and D2O. The molecule was identified as quillaic acid bearing a glucuronic acid-glucopyranose disaccharide at C-3 and a rhamnosyl-xylopyranose disaccharide at C-28, totalling four sugar units. ROESY cross-peaks confirmed the β-configuration of all glycosidic linkages. Key 1H and 13C chemical shifts and interresidue HMBC correlations are tabulated as a reference dataset for other researchers working on quillaic acid glycosides in this family. DPPH IC50 was 63 µg/mL; ABTS IC50 was 41 µg/mL.

title: Triterpenoid Saponins from Dianthus microlepis Boiss.: Structure of Three Compounds and Their Interaction with DPPH, ABTS and FRAP Assay Systems
abstract: Three saponins isolated from aerial parts of Dianthus microlepis, a Balkan endemic restricted to calcareous rocks, were characterised using spectroscopic and spectrometric data. Material was collected from two Bulgarian sites with permission. Compound 1 was identified as 3-O-(β-D-xylopyranosyl-(1→2)-β-D-glucuronopyranosyl) oleanolic acid; Compound 2 as its 28-O-β-D-glucopyranosyl ester; Compound 3 as the corresponding arabinose variant at C-3. HRMS confirmed molecular formulae C48H76O18, C54H86O23, and C47H74O17 respectively (< 1.5 ppm error). Radical-scavenging activity was evaluated in DPPH, ABTS and FRAP assays in parallel, and results are compared with quercetin and trolox standards at equimolar concentrations. Compound 2, the bidesmosidic form, gave weaker DPPH activity (IC50 155 µM) than monodesmosidic Compound 1 (IC50 88 µM), consistent with the general pattern of aglycone accessibility. FRAP values were lower across all three compounds relative to the flavonoid reference, highlighting the moderate antioxidant capacity of this saponin class.

title: Saponins of Silene sendtneri Revisited: Additional Minor Compounds Detected by UHPLC-HRMS and Confirmed by Micro-Scale NMR
abstract: An earlier study on Silene sendtneri Boiss. reported four major saponins; the present work re-examines archived butanol fractions using UHPLC coupled to a high-field Orbitrap (120 000 resolution) in data-dependent acquisition mode. Twenty-two putative saponin masses were detected, of which eleven had not been observed previously. Six minor compounds were isolated by semi-preparative HPLC in quantities of 0.8–4.2 mg. Structure assignment relied on 1H and 13C NMR recorded in 1.7 mm cryoprobe tubes at 600 MHz to compensate for the small sample masses, together with HMBC and HSQC. Three compounds were identified as monodesmosidic glucuronides of gypsogenin with different degrees of acetylation at the terminal sugar; two were ursolic acid monodesnosides; one remained partially assigned due to overlapping NMR signals. DPPH scavenging of the acetylated derivatives was reduced relative to their non-acetylated analogues (IC50 ratio 1.6–2.1), suggesting steric hindrance around the hydroxyl groups.

title: Distribution of Oleanane-Type Saponins Across Vegetative Organs of Gypsophila fastigiata L. During the Growing Season
abstract: Gypsophila fastigiata L. was selected to investigate organ-specific and phenological saponin accumulation. Roots, stems, leaves, and inflorescences were harvested separately at vegetative, early-flowering, full-flowering, and post-flowering stages from a single Fruška Gora population. Extractions and HPLC-UV quantification followed an in-house validated protocol. Six previously isolated saponins were tracked; two additional compounds appeared exclusively in roots at the vegetative stage and were isolated in 3.1 and 2.7 mg quantities and partially characterised by HRMS and 1H NMR. Total saponin concentration was highest in roots at all stages (up to 6.2% DW) and lowest in stems (< 0.8% DW). In aerial organs, saponin content peaked at early flowering and declined post-flowering. The two root-specific minor saponins could not be detected in aerial parts at any stage, suggesting organ-specific biosynthetic regulation. These results inform collection strategies for both research and any prospective large-scale use of the species.

title: Decomposition behaviour of natural dolomite under non-isothermal conditions: a TG-DSC study
abstract: Natural dolomite samples from the Fruška Gora formation were subjected to non-isothermal thermogravimetric and differential scanning calorimetric analysis in flowing CO2-N2 atmospheres over the composition range 0–100 vol% CO2. Mass loss curves indicated a two-stage decomposition sequence with the MgCO3 component dissociating between 680 and 720 °C and the CaCO3 component between 820 and 870 °C under pure N2. Increasing CO2 partial pressure shifted both events to higher temperatures, with the CaCO3 event reaching 950 °C at pCO2 = 0.5 atm. The associated DSC peaks yielded reaction enthalpies of 118 ± 3 kJ mol−1 and 165 ± 4 kJ mol−1 for the two stages, respectively. Isoconversional kinetic analysis using the Friedman and Ozawa–Flynn–Wall methods gave activation energies of 205–230 kJ mol−1 for the first stage and 185–210 kJ mol−1 for the second. Results suggest that the dolomite lattice provides some stabilisation to the MgCO3 component relative to pure magnesite. Powder XRD of quenched intermediates confirmed the transient formation of a Ca–Mg oxide solid solution at intermediate temperatures.

title: Influence of particle size on the thermal decomposition of limestone from the Beočin quarry
abstract: Limestone powders from the Beočin deposit were sieved into five fractions spanning 38–500 µm and analysed by TG-DSC at heating rates of 5, 10, and 20 K min−1 in nitrogen atmosphere. The onset decomposition temperature increased systematically with particle diameter, from 775 °C for the finest fraction to 810 °C for the coarsest, an effect attributed to diffusion limitation of evolved CO2 within larger grains. Peak temperatures and DTG peak widths were used to compute apparent activation energies by the Kissinger method; values ranged from 192 kJ mol−1 (38–63 µm) to 231 kJ mol−1 (250–500 µm). Reaction enthalpy showed no statistically significant dependence on particle size, averaging 167 ± 5 kJ mol−1. SEM imaging of partially decomposed grains revealed a sharp reaction front advancing inward, consistent with a contracting-volume model. These findings provide practical guidance for scaling calcination reactor residence times when feed particle size distributions are broad.

title: Mixed potassium–calcium carbonate systems: phase behaviour and evolved gas profiles during thermal treatment
abstract: Binary mixtures of K2CO3 and CaCO3 at molar ratios from 1:9 to 9:1 were prepared by coprecipitation and characterised by simultaneous TG-DSC-FTIR from room temperature to 1000 °C at 10 K min−1 in nitrogen. FTIR gas cell spectra recorded at 2 cm−1 resolution allowed real-time tracking of CO2 release as a function of mixture composition. K2CO3-rich samples showed a broad CO2 evolution commencing near 700 °C, attributed to eutectic melt-assisted decomposition confirmed by a DSC endotherm at 740 °C corresponding to the K2CO3–CaCO3 eutectic. At equimolar composition a sharp anomaly at 870 °C coincided with formation of K2Ca(CO3)2 (syncalcite) identified by XRD of quenched samples. Total mass loss agreed to within 0.3% of stoichiometric CO2 yield across all compositions. Residues at K2CO3:CaCO3 = 1:1 contained K2CaO2 at 1000 °C, suggesting partial oxygen exchange. The study maps the compositional space relevant to alkali-contaminated limestone calcination in industrial kilns.

title: Thermal analysis of sodium–magnesium carbonate mixtures and identification of intermediate phases
abstract: Mixtures of Na2CO3 and MgCO3 at compositions from 10 to 90 mol% Na2CO3 were heated at 5–20 K min−1 in both inert and 50% CO2–N2 atmospheres using simultaneous TG-DSC with on-line FTIR and quadrupole mass spectrometry. In pure nitrogen, the MgCO3-rich compositions decomposed in a single step between 400 and 500 °C, while sodium-rich mixtures showed two separate events. DSC revealed an exothermic transition at 563 °C in the 50:50 mixture, followed by a broader endothermic CO2 release at 640 °C. XRD of samples quenched at 580 °C identified Na2Mg(CO3)2 (eitelite) as an intermediate. The eitelite-to-oxide decomposition enthalpy was measured at 142 ± 6 kJ mol−1. Under CO2 atmosphere, the eitelite phase was stable to 680 °C. Isoconversional analysis for the eitelite decomposition yielded an apparent activation energy of 178 kJ mol−1, consistent with a surface-nucleation mechanism. These results are relevant for soda-ash processing of magnesite-bearing ores.

title: Comparison of model-fitting and model-free kinetic methods for carbonate decomposition: a critical assessment using dolomite data
abstract: Four decades of TG data for natural dolomite decomposition (stage 1: MgCO3 moiety; stage 2: CaCO3 moiety) collected at seven heating rates from 1 to 50 K min−1 in nitrogen were analysed by six kinetic methods: Coats–Redfern model fitting (16 reaction models), Kissinger, Ozawa–Flynn–Wall, Friedman, Vyazovkin advanced isoconversional, and Málek method for g(α) identification. For stage 1, model-free methods converged on Eα = 214 ± 12 kJ mol−1, while model fitting with the D3 diffusion model gave 209 kJ mol−1, consistent agreement. Stage 2 showed greater spread: 188–237 kJ mol−1 depending on method and conversion range, attributed to sintering of the CaO product layer at higher temperatures altering the effective reaction geometry. Pre-exponential factors calculated from compensation plots spanned four orders of magnitude, illustrating the hazard of comparing A values across methods. Recommendations are offered for standardised reporting of kinetic parameters in the carbonate calcination literature.

title: Effect of calcination atmosphere on the porosity and reactivity of magnesia derived from magnesite
abstract: Magnesite samples were calcined at 700, 800, and 900 °C in pure N2, 20% CO2–N2, and static air using a tube furnace; BET surface areas, pore size distributions (N2 adsorption–desorption), and hydration reactivity (citric acid test, slaked-lime temperature rise) were measured on the resulting MgO products. TG-DSC confirmed complete decarbonation above 750 °C in N2 and above 830 °C in 20% CO2. BET surface area peaked at 800 °C/N2 (62 m2 g−1) and declined to 11 m2 g−1 at 900 °C/N2, consistent with sintering. Samples calcined in CO2-containing atmospheres showed 15–30% lower surface area at equivalent temperature but improved crystal size uniformity by XRD line broadening. Citric acid reactivity index correlated linearly with BET area (R2 = 0.93). The data suggest that a moderate CO2 partial pressure suppresses excessively rapid sintering without penalising activity unduly, which has direct implications for rotary-kiln atmosphere control.

title: Quantification of CO2 evolved during carbonate decomposition by on-line FTIR: calibration strategy and uncertainty budget
abstract: A systematic calibration procedure for quantifying CO2 concentrations in the carrier gas stream of a simultaneous TG-DSC-FTIR instrument (Netzsch STA 449F3 / Bruker Tensor 27) is presented and validated. Gravimetric CO2 standards were generated by decomposing high-purity CaCO3 (Merck Suprapur, 99.95%) at controlled heating rates in N2. Absorbance of the asymmetric stretching band at 2349 cm−1 was integrated over the range 2280–2400 cm−1 and calibrated against known CO2 flux calculated from simultaneously measured mass loss rate. Linearity was confirmed over 0.1–12.0 vol% CO2 (R2 = 0.9997). Combined measurement uncertainty for a single evolved-gas peak area was ±4.2% (k = 2), with dominant contributions from baseline selection and flow rate stability. The protocol was tested on a dolomite decomposition sequence; stoichiometric CO2 yields of 97.4 ± 4.1% and 98.8 ± 4.4% were recovered for the two stages. Practical recommendations for gas-cell temperature and scan-averaging settings are provided to analytical laboratories using similar instrument configurations.

title: Thermal decomposition of ternary Li–Na–K carbonate eutectic mixtures studied by simultaneous TG-DSC-FTIR
abstract: The ternary eutectic mixture of Li2CO3 (43.5 mol%), Na2CO3 (31.5 mol%), and K2CO3 (25.0 mol%) and three off-eutectic compositions were characterised from 400 to 900 °C at heating rates of 5, 10, and 20 K min−1 in nitrogen and in 50% CO2. The eutectic melt onset at 397 °C was confirmed by DSC; a specific melting enthalpy of 188 J g−1 was measured. In nitrogen, CO2 evolution detected by FTIR commenced at 560 °C for the eutectic and was complete by 780 °C. Off-eutectic compositions showed higher onset temperatures (590–640 °C) and sharper CO2 peaks. Kinetic analysis of the liquid-phase decomposition using a reaction-order model (n ≈ 0.8) gave activation energies of 155–170 kJ mol−1 across compositions. In 50% CO2 atmosphere, the eutectic remained stable to above 750 °C. The results are discussed in the context of molten carbonate fuel cell electrolyte stability and high-temperature CO2 capture loop design.

title: Impact of trace barium carbonate additions on the calcination kinetics of limestone: a TG-DSC-FTIR investigation
abstract: Pure CaCO3 doped with 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0 mol% BaCO3 was synthesised by coprecipitation and heated at 10 K min−1 in nitrogen. TG-DSC profiles showed that BaCO3 addition progressively raised the calcite decomposition peak temperature from 883 °C (undoped) to 912 °C at 5 mol% doping, while the integrated CO2 FTIR signal confirmed stoichiometric decarbonation. The BaCO3 decomposition event (normally at 1005 °C) was suppressed at low doping levels, suggesting Ba2+ incorporation into the calcite lattice stabilises the carbonate against thermal decomposition. XRD of quenched samples at 920 °C confirmed full decarbonation of the CaCO3 host while residual BaCO3 remained detectable up to 970 °C at the 5 mol% level. Activation energy for the host decomposition rose from 196 to 223 kJ mol−1 at 5 mol% Ba. These findings are relevant to the use of Ba-bearing mineral admixtures in lime production and to the interpretation of thermal analyses of barite-contaminated carbonate ores.

title: Thermal analysis methods for carbonate minerals: a laboratory manual for undergraduate and graduate students
abstract: This book chapter presents a structured set of laboratory exercises covering simultaneous TG-DSC-FTIR analysis of calcite, magnesite, dolomite, and siderite, intended for physical chemistry and analytical chemistry laboratory courses at university level. Each exercise specifies sample preparation protocols, instrument parameter selection (purge gas, crucible type, heating rate), data processing procedures, and worked examples of kinetic calculations using the Kissinger and Ozawa methods. Uncertainty estimation following GUM guidelines is introduced through the CaCO3 decomposition enthalpy experiment. Guidance is provided on identifying common artefacts: buoyancy correction, baseline drift, and gas-cell temperature gradients in FTIR coupling. The chapter also includes a comparative section in which students use DTG peak deconvolution to estimate calcite/dolomite ratios in unknown limestone samples, providing an analytical chemistry context. The exercises have been tested over three successive academic years with groups of 15–25 students and revised based on feedback.

title: Correlation between FTIR gas-phase band intensities and TG mass-loss rate during dolomite decomposition at variable heating rates
abstract: The relationship between the time-resolved integrated absorbance of the CO2 asymmetric stretch (2349 cm−1) and the simultaneously measured mass-loss rate (mg min−1) from TG was examined for dolomite decomposition at seven heating rates (1–40 K min−1) and three carrier-gas flow rates (40, 80, 120 mL min−1 N2). Transfer-line dead volume introduced a systematic time lag between TG and FTIR signals of 4–18 s depending on flow rate, which was corrected by cross-correlation of the derivative signals. After time correction, the linear correlation coefficient between FTIR integrated absorbance and mass-loss rate exceeded 0.998 at all conditions. A flow-rate-dependent sensitivity factor was derived and shown to be independent of heating rate, enabling post-hoc recalculation of gas concentrations from archived TG data when calibrated FTIR data are unavailable. The method was extended to SO2 detection (at 1362 cm−1) during decomposition of a mixed carbonate–sulfate sample, recovering known sulfate content to within 6%.

title: Decomposition kinetics of mixed lithium–calcium carbonate systems as a function of atmosphere and heating rate
abstract: Mechanically mixed and co-precipitated samples of Li2CO3 and CaCO3 at molar ratios 1:4, 1:2, 1:1, 2:1, and 4:1 were studied by simultaneous TG-DSC-FTIR at heating rates of 5, 10, and 20 K min−1 in nitrogen and in 30% CO2–N2. DSC detected the Li2CO3 melting endotherm at 723 °C in lithium-rich samples, and a eutectic-like event at 665 °C at the 1:1 composition. CO2 evolution profiles from FTIR showed a single broad peak in co-precipitated samples versus two resolved peaks in mechanical mixtures at equivalent compositions, indicating intimate contact promotes melt-flux-assisted decomposition of CaCO3. In nitrogen, the CaCO3 decomposition onset in the 1:1 co-precipitate was 58 °C lower than in pure calcite. Isoconversional activation energies for the CaCO3 moiety in the co-precipitate ranged from 155 to 180 kJ mol−1 (compared with 198 kJ mol−1 for pure calcite), consistent with a flux mechanism. In 30% CO2, the effect was attenuated by 25–35 °C but not eliminated. Residue XRD identified Li2CaO2 as the final product above 900 °C.

title: Consensus QSAR modelling of CYP51-inhibiting azoles using random forests and support vector regression alongside classical MLR
abstract: Inhibition of CYP51 (lanosterol 14α-demethylase) was used as the target endpoint for a dataset of 74 azole derivatives compiled from enzymatic assay data. Three modelling approaches were applied: multiple linear regression (MLR), support vector regression (SVR) with a radial basis function kernel, and random forests (RF) with 500 trees. All models were trained on 60 compounds and tested on 14 held-out compounds selected by a Kennard–Stone algorithm. RF achieved the lowest test RMSE (0.29 log units, R²ext = 0.86), followed by SVR (RMSE = 0.33, R²ext = 0.83) and MLR (RMSE = 0.41, R²ext = 0.77). A consensus prediction averaging RF and SVR outputs reduced RMSE to 0.27 log units. Variable importance from RF highlighted the electrophilicity index and two Burden eigenvalue descriptors as the most influential features, consistent with the electronic mechanism of CYP51 heme-iron coordination. Applicability domain was assessed by the RF out-of-bag proximity measure.

title: Phenological separability of riparian vegetation classes in a Pannonian floodplain: a multi-date SPOT-5 analysis
abstract: Accurate delineation of riparian vegetation communities in lowland floodplains requires imagery acquired at multiple phenological stages to exploit temporal variation in canopy reflectance. This study evaluated the spectral separability of seven riparian vegetation classes using eight SPOT-5 HRG scenes acquired monthly from April to October 2012 along a 75 km reach of the Sava River upstream of Sremska Mitrovica. Jeffries–Matusita distance matrices were computed for all class pairs at each acquisition date and for stacked multi-date configurations. Single-date separability peaked in mid-May for distinguishing softwood forest from hybrid poplar plantation (JM = 1.87), but remained below 1.60 for reed versus wet grassland at all single dates. The seven-date stacked configuration achieved mean pairwise JM distance of 1.94, with all class pairs exceeding 1.75. A random forest classifier applied to the stacked dataset yielded an overall accuracy of 87.2% on an independent validation set of 510 polygons. The study demonstrates that at least four strategically timed acquisitions are required for reliable community-level mapping in this landscape.

title: Object-based classification of floodplain habitats using WorldView-2 imagery: sensitivity to segmentation scale and training sample size
abstract: Object-based image analysis (OBIA) is widely used for high-resolution land-cover mapping, but practical guidance on segmentation scale and training sample requirements for heterogeneous floodplain environments remains limited. This study applied eCognition multiresolution segmentation at seven scale parameter values (10 to 70 in steps of 10) to a WorldView-2 image acquired in June 2014 over a 3,400 ha floodplain area along the Bosut River, a right-bank tributary of the Sava. Training sample sizes of 30, 60, 120, and 240 objects per class were tested in combination with a support vector machine classifier for nine habitat classes defined according to the EUNIS classification scheme. Classification accuracy increased substantially up to 120 training objects per class but plateaued thereafter. Optimal segmentation scale varied by class: coarser scales (40–50) produced better results for poplar stands and arable land, while finer scales (15–20) were required for shrub willow and riparian meadow. The best overall configuration reached 89.6% overall accuracy (kappa 0.87). Findings provide practical thresholds applicable to similar medium-scale floodplain mapping tasks.

title: Mapping invasive Amorpha fruticosa encroachment in riparian meadows from Sentinel-2 multitemporal data
abstract: Amorpha fruticosa (false indigo bush) is an aggressive woody invasive species expanding rapidly in riparian meadows and levee slopes throughout the middle Danube basin. Reliable area estimates of encroachment are needed for management prioritisation but field surveys are expensive over large networks. This study developed a Sentinel-2 multitemporal classification approach targeting the species' distinctive early leaf-flush phenology in late March to mid-April, which precedes native grass green-up by two to three weeks. Five Sentinel-2 Level-2A scenes from March–April 2020 and 2021, plus one late-summer scene per year, were composited into an eight-band feature stack. A random forest classifier trained on 485 reference polygons produced an overall accuracy of 84.7% (kappa 0.81) for a four-class scheme (Amorpha dense, Amorpha sparse, native riparian meadow, and other). Applied to the full Vojvodina river network buffer (10 m either side of mapped levee lines, total 18,400 ha), the model estimated 3,270 ha of dense and 2,850 ha of sparse Amorpha cover. Results were substantially higher than the most recent national inventory figure, suggesting significant underreporting. The classification outputs have been shared with the Provincial Secretariat for Environmental Protection.

title: Long-term trajectories of riparian vegetation cover along regulated Pannonian rivers: a 35-year Landsat archive analysis
abstract: River regulation through channelisation, levee construction, and flow regime alteration has profoundly changed riparian vegetation dynamics in Pannonian lowlands since the mid-twentieth century. This study analysed a 35-year archive of Landsat TM, ETM+, OLI, and OLI-2 imagery (1989–2024) to reconstruct annual vegetation cover trajectories for five river regulation classes along 870 km of navigable lowland river reaches in Serbia, covering the Danube, Sava, Tisa, Begej, and Tamiš. Annual peak-NDVI composites and a time-series breakpoint detection algorithm (BFAST adapted for dense stacks) were used to identify structural change points and directional trends. Regulated reaches with bank revetment showed a statistically significant declining trend in riparian woody cover density (mean Sen's slope −0.0018 NDVI units per year), while unregulated reference reaches showed no significant trend. Flood pulse interruption, inferred from gauge records, was the variable most strongly correlated with periods of accelerated NDVI decline (r = −0.61, p < 0.01). The 35-year dataset provides baseline information for ongoing national river basin management planning under the EU Water Framework Directive transposition in Serbian legislation.

title: Integration of InSAR displacement maps with electrical resistivity tomography for loess failure mechanism interpretation
abstract: Surface displacement fields derived from InSAR give kinematic information but provide limited insight into subsurface failure geometry. This study combined 2D electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) profiles with Sentinel-1 persistent scatterer velocity maps at a 1.6 ha loess flow lobe near Beočin to constrain the failure plane depth and geometry. ERT profiles totalling 840 m were acquired along and across the flow axis using a Wenner-Schlumberger array at 2 m electrode spacing. A resistivity contrast at 3.5–5.0 m depth correlated spatially with the boundary between the high-velocity scatterer cluster (mean −9.2 mm/yr) and the stable upslope area. A simple infinite-slope stability model parameterised with the ERT-derived failure depth and loess shear-strength literature values yielded a factor of safety of 0.97–1.04, consistent with the observed slow continuous movement. Integration of the two datasets reduced uncertainty in estimated failure volume from ±40 % (InSAR alone) to ±18 %.

title: Ion-pairing effects on the rate of SNAr displacement of fluoride from 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene by alkali-metal methoxides in methanol
abstract: Rate constants for the reaction of 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene with sodium, potassium, and caesium methoxides were determined in anhydrous methanol at 25 °C using stopped-flow spectrophotometry over the concentration range 1–50 mM. Conductometric measurements confirmed the degree of ion-pair formation in each salt solution. For sodium methoxide, k2 varied from 38 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ at low concentration to 12 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 50 mM, while the caesium salt showed far weaker concentration dependence (31 to 26 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹). The data were analysed using the Fuoss–Winstein ion-pair scheme; the ratio of the rate constant for the free methoxide ion to that of the contact ion pair was 4.8 for NaOMe and 1.6 for CsOMe. These results confirm that tight ion pairing with small cations markedly suppresses nucleophilic reactivity through electrostatic shielding of the oxygen lone pair. Activation enthalpies and entropies are reported for both free and paired nucleophiles.

title: Substituent effects on SNAr reactivity in 5-substituted-2-chloropyrimidines: a Hammett correlation study
abstract: A series of seven 5-substituted 2-chloropyrimidines bearing electron-withdrawing groups (NO2, CN, CF3, CO2Et) and moderately electron-donating groups (CH3, OCH3, H) were synthesised and their reactions with n-butylamine in acetonitrile at 25 °C studied by stopped-flow spectrophotometry. Second-order rate constants ranged over four orders of magnitude: from 0.003 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ for the methoxy derivative to 31 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ for the 5-nitro compound. A linear Hammett σp correlation yielded a reaction constant ρ = +3.84 (r² = 0.991), indicating strong demand for electron withdrawal at the 5-position. Activation parameters were measured for the four most reactive compounds; ΔH‡ ranged from 38 to 52 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS‡ from −62 to −44 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. The results are discussed in terms of ground-state stabilisation versus transition-state effects and compared with literature data on 4-substituted 2-chloropyridines.

title: Solvent reorganisation and the isokinetic relationship in SNAr reactions of chlorodiazines with aliphatic amines
abstract: The enthalpy–entropy compensation relationship was examined for a set of fifteen SNAr reactions between chlorodiazine substrates (2-chloropyrazine, 2-chloropyrimidine, 2-chloroquinoxaline) and four aliphatic amines in nine solvents. Activation enthalpies and entropies were obtained from Eyring plots constructed from stopped-flow measurements over 15–45 °C. A clear isokinetic relationship with β = 312 K was found for each substrate–amine pair across solvents, suggesting that solvent reorganisation at the transition state is a major contributor to the observed enthalpy–entropy compensation. Deviations from linearity were observed in strongly protic solvents (water, formamide), where hydrogen-bond restructuring introduces an additional enthalpic component. A simple two-parameter model partitioning ΔH‡ into an intrinsic chemical term and a solvation term reproduced the experimental data with a mean absolute error of 1.9 kJ mol⁻¹. The isokinetic temperature is invariant across the three substrates examined, implying a common mechanistic pathway.

title: Kinetic study of the hydrolysis of 4-chloro-7-nitrobenzofuroxan in buffered aqueous solution
abstract: The hydroxide-promoted hydrolysis of 4-chloro-7-nitrobenzofuroxan, a highly activated SNAr substrate, was investigated by stopped-flow spectrophotometry at 25 °C in aqueous NaOH solutions (0.001–0.5 M) and in buffers spanning pH 6–12. The pseudo-first-order rate constant kobs showed a first-order dependence on [OH⁻] up to 0.1 M, with a second-order rate constant k2 = (1.84 ± 0.06) × 10³ L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹, one of the highest values reported for this substrate class. At [OH⁻] > 0.15 M, a downward curvature indicative of an activity coefficient effect was corrected using the Debye–Hückel extended law. Meisenheimer complex accumulation was not detectable on the millisecond timescale, implying that leaving-group departure is faster than complex formation. Product identification by LC-MS and ¹H NMR confirmed exclusive formation of 4-hydroxy-7-nitrobenzofuroxan. Ionic-strength effects (0–0.5 M KCl) showed a small positive salt effect consistent with reaction between a neutral substrate and a singly charged nucleophile.

title: Reactivity of 2,4,6-trinitrophenyl ethers toward aliphatic amines: leaving-group effects and mechanistic changeover
abstract: Four 2,4,6-trinitrophenyl ethers (methoxy, ethoxy, n-butoxy, phenoxy) were reacted with morpholine, piperidine, and n-propylamine in acetonitrile at 25 °C. Rate constants were determined by stopped-flow spectrophotometry monitoring at the Meisenheimer band (520–540 nm) and at the product absorption. For the alkyl aryl ethers, the overall second-order rate constants were governed by the decomposition step (k2), and the ratio k1/k−1 remained roughly constant across the ether series. For 2,4,6-trinitrophenyl phenyl ether, the mechanism shifted: the leaving-group departure became fully rate-determining with k2 < k−1, as evidenced by a Brønsted βlg of −0.71 derived from reactions with substituted phenoxides. The Brønsted βnuc for the attack step was +0.41, measured using primary amines of varying pKa. These data, combined with the activation volume measured at 25–100 MPa in a high-pressure stopped-flow apparatus at the University of Pécs, indicate a synchronous rather than stepwise mechanism for the aryl ether series.

title: Influence of crown ether complexation on ion-pairing and SNAr rate constants in aprotic solvents
abstract: The role of crown ether complexation in modulating cation–nucleophile ion pairing was studied for reactions of 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene with potassium phenoxide in acetonitrile and THF in the presence of 18-crown-6 at 25 °C. Without crown ether, conductometric titrations confirmed that ≥ 85% of the phenoxide exists as ion pairs in both solvents at 5 mM. Addition of stoichiometric 18-crown-6 reduced ion-pair fractions to < 10% as determined by the same method. Stopped-flow measurements showed that k2 increased from 0.29 to 3.4 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ in acetonitrile and from 0.11 to 2.7 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ in THF upon full decomplexation. The enhancement factor (≈ 12–25) is larger in THF than in acetonitrile, consistent with the higher dielectric constant of acetonitrile providing partial electrostatic screening even for paired species. Activation parameters measured at 15–35 °C reveal that crown ether addition lowers ΔH‡ by 9 kJ mol⁻¹ and makes ΔS‡ more negative by 18 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, supporting a tighter, more organised transition state for the free phenoxide.

title: Stopped-flow kinetics and environmental fate estimation of chlorinated triazine herbicide analogues in alkaline aqueous media
abstract: Three structural analogues of commercially used chlorinated s-triazine herbicides were synthesised and their hydrolysis kinetics measured by stopped-flow spectrophotometry in aqueous NaOH (pH 9–13) at 15, 25, and 35 °C. Second-order rate constants for hydroxide-mediated dechlorination ranged from 0.04 to 2.3 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹, depending on the nature of the C-2 and C-4 substituents. Half-lives at pH 9 and 25 °C ranged from 28 minutes to 14 days across the series, relevant to environmental persistence in surface water. Activation energies (Ea = 48–67 kJ mol⁻¹) and pre-exponential factors were derived from Arrhenius plots. Quantitative structure–reactivity relationships based on Hammett σ values for the C-4 substituents gave a linear correlation (ρ = +2.9, r² = 0.984). The data were used to estimate environmental half-lives under European freshwater pH and temperature conditions according to OECD guidelines, providing input parameters for persistence modelling.
venue: Environmental Chemistry and Reaction Kinetics

title: Solvent effects on the reaction of 2-chloro-5-nitropyridine with hydroxide ion: Gutmann acceptor number and specific solvation
abstract: The reaction of 2-chloro-5-nitropyridine with NaOH was studied in twelve pure solvents and four water–co-solvent mixtures at 25 °C using stopped-flow UV/Vis spectrophotometry. Second-order rate constants varied by a factor of 180 across the solvent series (from 0.007 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ in ethylene glycol to 1.3 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ in NMP). Multiparameter linear solvation energy relationships using the Gutmann acceptor number (AN), Kamlet–Taft α, β, and π*, and the Reichardt ET(30) scale were systematically compared. The best four-parameter fit (r² = 0.975) included AN, β, and π* as significant terms, with AN carrying the largest coefficient. This indicates that hydrogen-bond-donor ability of the solvent, which solvates and stabilises the hydroxide nucleophile, is the dominant retarding factor. Solvents with high β (strong hydrogen-bond acceptors) retard the reaction by solvating the ground-state substrate. Application of a scaled solvent-effect model successfully predicted k2 within a factor of two for all solvents in the validation set.

title: Kinetics of SNAr reactions of electron-deficient diazines with thiolate nucleophiles: sulfur versus oxygen and nitrogen comparison
abstract: Rate constants for the reaction of 2-chloro-4,6-dimethylpyrimidine, 2-chloro-4-nitropyrimidine, and 2-chloro-5-nitropyridine with sodium benzenethiolate, sodium p-nitrobenzenethiolate, and potassium n-propylthiolate in aqueous ethanol (50:50 v/v) at 25 °C were determined by stopped-flow spectrophotometry. Thiolate nucleophiles were 1–3 orders of magnitude more reactive than the oxygen analogues (phenoxide and propoxide) and 2–4 orders of magnitude more reactive than the corresponding nitrogen nucleophiles (aniline, n-propylamine) at matched pKa. The Brønsted βnuc for sulfur nucleophiles was +0.52, significantly higher than the +0.34 obtained for oxygen nucleophiles in the same substrate–solvent system. Ion-pairing corrections, assessed by conductometry, were important only for sodium thiolates at concentrations above 20 mM. The intrinsic nucleophilicity ordering (S > O > N) is interpreted in terms of polarisability-driven stabilisation of the SNAr transition state and partial contribution from a synchronous displacement pathway for the softest nucleophile.

title: Pressure effects on nucleophilic aromatic substitution: volumes of activation for reactions of amines with nitropyridines and nitropyrimidines
abstract: Volumes of activation (ΔV‡) for seven SNAr reactions between aliphatic amines and electron-deficient nitroheteroarenes were measured in acetonitrile and aqueous ethanol using a high-pressure stopped-flow apparatus (5–150 MPa) at 25 °C, in collaboration with the kinetics laboratory at the University of Pécs. ΔV‡ values ranged from −12.4 to −21.7 cm³ mol⁻¹ across the series. The most negative ΔV‡ values were associated with reactions in which Meisenheimer complex accumulation had independently been confirmed, consistent with a large electrostriction contribution upon charge localisation in the σ-complex. Reactions proceeding without detectable intermediates gave less negative ΔV‡ (−12 to −14 cm³ mol⁻¹), suggesting a more dispersed charge in the transition state. A linear correlation was found between ΔV‡ and the previously reported ΔS‡ values (r² = 0.93), implying that both quantities reflect the same physical change in solvent structure. The results are compared with literature ΔV‡ data for aliphatic SN2 reactions.

title: Aqueous-phase SNAr hydrolysis of chlorinated pyrimidine building blocks used in pharmaceutical synthesis: kinetics, pH profiles, and stability windows
abstract: Four chlorinated pyrimidine intermediates encountered in synthetic routes to pharmaceutical actives were assessed for aqueous stability by measuring their hydrolysis rate constants over pH 1–13 at 25 °C using stopped-flow and conventional UV/Vis spectrophotometry. The compounds include 2,4-dichloropyrimidine, 2-chloro-4-methylpyrimidine, 2-chloro-4-aminopyrimidine, and 4-chloro-2-(methylthio)pyrimidine. pH–rate profiles for each compound were constructed from pseudo-first-order rate constants measured at constant ionic strength (0.1 M KCl). The profiles were fitted to a mechanistic model distinguishing H2O, H3O⁺, and OH⁻ pathways. For 2,4-dichloropyrimidine, kOH = 8.3 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ and t1/2 at pH 9 and 25 °C is 23 min, whereas 4-chloro-2-(methylthio)pyrimidine is substantially more stable (kOH = 0.014 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹, t1/2 ≈ 9 days). The stability window analysis identifies pH 4–7 as suitable for aqueous processing of all four intermediates, with implications for process chemistry in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Stopped-flow kinetic studies of SNAr reactions in deep eutectic solvents: choline chloride–urea and choline chloride–glycerol as reaction media
abstract: The reaction of piperidine and morpholine with 4-chloro-3,5-dinitropyridine was investigated in two deep eutectic solvents (DES): choline chloride–urea (1:2 molar ratio, reline) and choline chloride–glycerol (1:2, glyceline), in comparison with the reaction in acetonitrile and in water at 25 °C. Despite high viscosity (η = 37 cP for reline and 259 cP for glyceline at 25 °C), stopped-flow measurements yielded reproducible absorbance–time traces after dead-time corrections. Second-order rate constants in reline (k2 = 0.41 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ for piperidine) were lower than in acetonitrile (k2 = 2.9 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹) but higher than in water (k2 = 0.12 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹), consistent with intermediate hydrogen-bond-donor capacity. Meisenheimer intermediate absorbance was observed transiently in both DES media. Activation parameters in glyceline show an unusually large and negative ΔS‡ (−98 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), attributed to the structured hydrogen-bond network of the solvent. These findings are among the first quantitative stopped-flow data for SNAr reactions in DES media.

title: Morphology-aware tokenization for Serbian NLP pipelines
abstract: Serbian presents significant challenges for standard tokenization tools designed for English or other analytic languages, primarily because of its rich inflectional morphology and the coexistence of Cyrillic and Latin scripts. This paper describes a rule-augmented tokenizer that combines finite-state transducers with a small supervised component trained on 120,000 tokens drawn from news and legal texts. The tokenizer was evaluated against three existing tools on a held-out test set of 18,000 tokens. It achieved a token-boundary F1 of 98.4%, outperforming the next best baseline by 1.7 percentage points. An ablation study shows that the finite-state component accounts for most of the gain on clitics and hyphenated compounds. The system is released as an open-source module and has since been integrated into two downstream annotation pipelines used at the university. Limitations related to non-standard social media orthography are discussed, along with directions for extending coverage to Bosnian and Montenegrin varieties.

title: Cross-lingual projection of NER labels from English to Serbian using parallel corpora
abstract: Acquiring labelled data for sequence tagging in low-resource languages is expensive. This work investigates whether NER annotations can be projected from English onto Serbian via word-alignment in a parallel corpus of 210,000 sentence pairs drawn from EU legislative translations. Three alignment models—IBM Model 2, fast-align, and a neural attention alignment—are compared on projection quality, measured by comparing projected labels to a 3,000-sentence gold standard. Fast-align produced the highest projection precision at 74.1%, though recall suffered at 58.3% due to free-word-order divergences. A heuristic post-processing step based on morphological case filtering raised F1 from 62.7% to 68.4%. Models trained entirely on projected data reached 73.1% F1 on the SerbNER-News test set, roughly 8 points below the fully supervised baseline. The gap narrows to 4.2 points when 2,000 manually labelled sentences are added as a small supervised component. Results suggest projection is a viable complement but not a substitute for in-language annotation.

title: Identifying IP addresses and domain indicators of compromise in Serbian-language cybersecurity forums
abstract: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) practitioners rely on structured indicators of compromise (IOCs)—such as malicious IP addresses, domain names, and file hashes—extracted from unstructured text. Most existing extraction tools are designed for English. This study targets Serbian-language underground forums and security mailing lists, constructing a dataset of 8,200 posts manually labelled for five IOC categories. A CRF-based extractor trained on 6,000 posts achieves an F1 of 87.3% for IP addresses and 79.6% for domain names, but only 51.4% for file-hash mentions due to inconsistent formatting conventions. An error analysis identifies three recurring failure modes: obfuscated notation (e.g., hxxp), mixed-script entity names, and colloquial abbreviations. The paper also releases a regular-expression baseline that achieves competitive recall (85.1%) at the cost of lower precision (61.8%), which may be preferable in high-recall security workflows. Data collection and ethical considerations regarding forum scraping are discussed in detail.
venue: Journal of Information Security and Applied Research in Eastern Europe

title: Adapting multilingual BERT to Serbian cybersecurity text through domain-specific continued pre-training
abstract: Multilingual BERT (mBERT) provides useful representations for Serbian but was pre-trained predominantly on Wikipedia text, which differs substantially in vocabulary and style from cybersecurity discourse. This paper describes a continued pre-training experiment in which mBERT was further trained using masked language modelling on a 34-million-token corpus of Serbian IT security blog posts, vulnerability reports translated into Serbian, and captured forum data. The resulting model, SecBERT-SR, was fine-tuned on the IOC dataset from prior work and compared against mBERT, XLM-RoBERTa, and a BiLSTM-CRF baseline. SecBERT-SR achieved a macro F1 of 83.7% on IOC extraction, compared to 79.1% for XLM-RoBERTa and 74.4% for mBERT. Gains were largest for the file-hash and URL categories. The model adds approximately 11% inference latency compared to mBERT when run on a single GPU, which is relevant for near-real-time CTI pipelines. Model weights and pre-training scripts are available under an open licence.

title: A survey of named-entity recognition methods for morphologically rich languages with emphasis on South Slavic
abstract: This chapter reviews named-entity recognition research for morphologically rich languages published between 2005 and 2021, with particular focus on South Slavic languages (Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian, Bulgarian, Macedonian). The chapter is organised around three axes: the type of linguistic knowledge encoded (none, rule-based, statistical), the size and domain of training corpora, and the entity taxonomy used. Forty-seven systems are surveyed and compared on a unified scoring framework where original reported figures are recalculated where possible. Key findings include: (1) lack of standardised shared tasks is the main barrier to comparability; (2) neural approaches since 2018 consistently outperform earlier CRF systems, but often by smaller margins than on English; (3) domain mismatch between available corpora and target deployment contexts remains acute. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems, including handling of named entities in dialectal text and the scarcity of evaluation sets for specialised domains such as cybersecurity, healthcare, and legal documents.

title: Few-shot NER for Croatian cybersecurity text using prompting with large language models
abstract: Croatian shares substantial vocabulary and morphological structure with Serbian but lacks even the modest annotated NER resources available for Serbian. This study examines whether large language models (LLMs) accessible via API, specifically a 70-billion-parameter instruction-tuned model, can perform few-shot NER for Croatian IOC extraction without any gradient updates. Prompts were constructed using between zero and sixteen in-context examples drawn from a newly created 500-sentence Croatian CTI evaluation set annotated by two bilingual security analysts. At sixteen-shot prompting, the LLM achieved an F1 of 68.3% for person and organisation entities but only 44.7% for file hashes, comparable to a CRF trained on 1,200 Serbian sentences and transferred via cross-lingual methods. Error analysis reveals that the model frequently conflates domain names with organisation names. Prompt format sensitivity is measured systematically: JSON-structured output prompts outperform free-text prompts by 9.1 F1 points. The evaluation set is released for future benchmarking.

title: Benchmarking low-resource NER across five Slavic languages using a unified annotation schema for cybersecurity entities
abstract: Comparing NER systems across Slavic languages is hindered by inconsistent entity taxonomies and disjoint test sets. This paper introduces SlavCyberBench, a benchmark consisting of parallel 2,000-sentence evaluation sets in Serbian, Croatian, Bulgarian, Slovak, and Czech, all annotated for the same seven cybersecurity entity types: malware name, threat actor, vulnerability identifier, IP address, domain, URL, and file hash. Annotation was produced by one expert per language following shared guidelines, with a cross-language adjudication pass performed on a 200-sentence common subset. Six representative models are evaluated: mBERT, XLM-RoBERTa-base, XLM-RoBERTa-large, SecBERT-SR cross-lingually transferred, a CRF baseline, and a GPT-class LLM with 16-shot prompting. XLM-RoBERTa-large leads on four of five languages; SecBERT-SR transfer is competitive on Croatian and Bulgarian despite being trained only on Serbian. The benchmark and annotation guidelines are released under a CC-BY 4.0 licence to support reproducible comparisons.

title: A Tabu Search Heuristic for the Multi-Depot Vehicle Scheduling Problem with Time Windows
abstract: This paper addresses the multi-depot vehicle scheduling problem (MDVSP) with time windows arising in regional bus networks. A tabu search heuristic is designed in which the neighbourhood is defined by reassignment of service trips between depots and by time-window stretching moves. The method was tested on benchmark instances derived from the public transport network of Vojvodina, comprising up to 18 depots and 340 service trips. Computational experiments show that the heuristic reaches solutions within 2.1% of the best known lower bound on average, with running times under 90 seconds on a standard workstation. The paper also reports sensitivity of solution quality to fleet heterogeneity: introducing two vehicle types increases average cost by 6.4% compared to the homogeneous case, a gap that narrows when deadhead time penalties are relaxed. The results suggest that the proposed method scales acceptably to instances of practical size without requiring exact solver calls.

title: Decomposition Strategies for Large-Scale Crew-Vehicle Integrated Scheduling in Urban Transit
abstract: Integrated crew and vehicle scheduling in urban transit is a large mixed-integer program that is computationally intractable for city-scale instances. This work compares three decomposition strategies—sequential, Lagrangian relaxation-based, and rolling-horizon—on synthetic instances calibrated to the timetable structure of a medium-sized Central European city with 22 lines and approximately 600 daily duties. The rolling-horizon approach partitions the planning day into overlapping windows of 90 minutes with a 30-minute slide and solves each sub-problem with a branch-and-price procedure. On instances of up to 1 200 duties, rolling-horizon decomposition yields solutions 4.7% cheaper on average than the sequential approach and 1.9% more expensive than the Lagrangian lower bound, while running in under 15 minutes. Sensitivity to window width and overlap length is analysed systematically. Practical guidance is offered for selecting decomposition parameters based on network density.

title: Online Re-Optimisation of Bus Schedules Under Vehicle Breakdowns: A Simulation Study
abstract: Vehicle breakdowns during daily operations force dispatchers to reassign trips and reposition spare buses within tight time constraints. This paper formalises the online re-optimisation problem triggered by a single unexpected breakdown event and proposes an adaptive large neighbourhood search (ALNS) procedure that must return a feasible revised schedule within 60 seconds. The method was evaluated in a discrete-event simulation environment built around timetable and incident data collected from a regional bus operator in Serbia over 18 months, covering 143 recorded breakdown events. ALNS recovered feasible schedules in 97% of cases and reduced passenger delay compared to a greedy dispatcher rule by an average of 34%. The study identifies trip clustering around peak hours as the main factor increasing recovery difficulty. A regression model linking network topology features to expected recovery time is also provided as a practical diagnostic tool.

title: Real-Time Metaheuristics for Dynamic Dial-a-Ride Problems: A Comparative Review
abstract: The dynamic dial-a-ride problem (DARP) requires continuous reassignment of passengers to vehicles as new requests arrive during the service day. This chapter surveys metaheuristic approaches published between 2005 and 2019 that operate under real-time constraints, covering tabu search, simulated annealing, genetic algorithms, and large neighbourhood search variants. Each method is characterised along five dimensions: acceptance criterion, neighbourhood structure, re-optimisation trigger, computational budget, and benchmark used. The survey covers 47 papers and reveals that large neighbourhood search dominates recent work, appearing in 21 of 47 studies, while direct comparisons across papers remain difficult due to inconsistent benchmark use. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems including multi-objective formulations combining cost, waiting time, and emissions, and highlights the absence of standardised real-time benchmarks as a barrier to progress in the field.

title: A Rolling-Horizon Framework for Electric Bus Scheduling with Charging Constraints
abstract: Introducing electric buses into an existing fleet imposes charging constraints that couple vehicle scheduling decisions across time in a way that classical vehicle scheduling models do not capture. This paper extends the rolling-horizon decomposition framework to handle state-of-charge dynamics, modelling each sub-problem as a mixed-integer linear program with battery level as a side constraint. The framework was applied to a hypothetical electrification scenario for a city with 14 bus lines, constructed from publicly available timetable data, and tested for fleet sizes between 20 and 80 electric vehicles with three charging infrastructure configurations. Results show that a 120-minute window with 45-minute overlap balances solution quality and tractability; average deviation from a full-day MILP optimum is 3.8% with a maximum of 7.1%. The paper also quantifies the trade-off between number of installed fast chargers and deadhead mileage.

title: Sensitivity of Metaheuristic Performance to Disruption Frequency in Dynamic Vehicle Scheduling
abstract: Most computational studies of dynamic vehicle scheduling evaluate algorithms at a single disruption rate chosen for convenience. This paper systematically varies disruption frequency—measured as expected incidents per operating hour—from 0.05 to 2.0 across 480 randomly generated instances and measures the performance of three metaheuristics: reactive tabu search, ALNS, and iterated local search. Performance is evaluated on solution cost, number of unserviced trips, and computation time. The experiments show that ALNS maintains the lowest cost across the full frequency range, but its advantage over reactive tabu search diminishes above 1.2 incidents per hour, where rapid reheating in tabu search compensates for less structured neighbourhood selection. Iterated local search degrades sharply above 0.8 incidents per hour due to insufficient time for perturbation. The paper proposes a simple classifier, trained on instance features, that predicts which algorithm to deploy given an estimated disruption rate.

title: Assessment of Tropospheric Zenith Total Delay Estimates from a Dense CORS Network in the Pannonian Basin
abstract: Zenith total delay (ZTD) estimates derived from 14 continuously operating GNSS reference stations distributed across the Pannonian Basin were evaluated against radiosonde observations at three co-located sites over a four-year period (2007–2010). Processing was performed using a double-differencing strategy with elevation cut-off angles of 7° and the Vienna Mapping Function 1. Mean ZTD biases with respect to radiosonde-derived values ranged from −1.4 mm to +3.1 mm depending on season and station altitude. Root-mean-square differences were below 6 mm at all sites. The study examined how station spacing affects spatial interpolation of ZTD gradients and identified systematic biases attributable to multipath contamination at three stations with nearby reflective surfaces. Results confirm that the regional CORS infrastructure, despite having been installed primarily for cadastral positioning, provides ZTD estimates suitable for numerical weather model assimilation after bias correction. Recommendations for antenna environment audits are provided.

title: Seasonal Vertical Displacements Detected by GNSS at Sites over the Vojvodina Lowland and Their Hydrological Interpretation
abstract: Five years of daily PPP solutions at nine GNSS stations across the Vojvodina lowland were decomposed using least-squares harmonic estimation to separate long-term trend, annual, and semi-annual components from white and flicker noise. Vertical velocities ranged from −0.8 to −2.3 mm/yr, suggesting mild but spatially variable subsidence. Annual amplitudes of 4–8 mm peak-to-peak correlated spatially with the depth of the water table as monitored by the Provincial Hydrometeorological Service, pointing to elastic aquifer compaction and loading as dominant mechanisms. A simple loading model using GRACE-derived terrestrial water storage anomalies reproduced about 60 % of the observed annual signal amplitude. Residual discrepancies were largest at sites overlying Holocene clay-rich sediments, consistent with seasonal poroelastic deformation. The study provides a baseline vertical motion field that can be used for levelling datum maintenance in the region.

title: Comparison of Static PPP and Double-Differencing Strategies for Long-Term Vertical Velocity Estimation in a Regional GNSS Network
abstract: Long-term vertical velocities at 11 stations in northern Serbia were estimated independently using static Precise Point Positioning with ambiguity resolution (PPP-AR) and a network double-differencing (DD) approach over a common 8-year observation window (2006–2013). Both solutions relied on IGS final orbits and clock products; tropospheric delays were modelled with VMF1 gridded data. Vertical velocity agreement between strategies was within 0.15 mm/yr at nine stations and diverged by 0.3–0.5 mm/yr at two stations situated near the network perimeter, where the DD baseline geometry was less favourable. Formal uncertainties were comparable, but power-spectral analysis revealed slightly higher flicker noise floors in the DD solutions. The study concludes that PPP-AR offers equivalent or marginally superior performance for velocity estimation in a sparse regional context, simplifying data processing and reducing dependence on inter-station baseline selection.

title: Quantifying Noise in Continuous GNSS Vertical Time Series Using Maximum Likelihood Estimation: A Case Study from the Central Balkans
abstract: Noise characteristics of vertical daily position time series from 17 GNSS stations in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Montenegro were estimated using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) with five candidate noise models: white noise only, flicker noise only, power-law noise, white-plus-flicker, and white-plus-random-walk. The preferred model, selected by Akaike information criterion, was white-plus-flicker at 14 stations. Spectral indices ranged from −0.8 to −1.2, close to the canonical flicker value. Three stations near urban areas showed elevated white-noise floors consistent with multipath changes caused by construction activity. Including a realistic noise model increased formal velocity uncertainties by factors of 2.5 to 4.1 compared with assuming white noise only, with direct implications for the significance of detected subsidence trends. Tables of noise parameters and corrected velocity uncertainties are provided as a community resource for the region.

title: Performance of Real-Time PPP Services for Structural Deformation Monitoring: Tests on a Reinforced Concrete Frame Building
abstract: Three commercial real-time PPP correction services were evaluated for their suitability in quasi-continuous structural health monitoring of a four-storey reinforced concrete frame building on the Novi Sad campus. Dual-frequency receivers were installed at two roof corners and one ground reference point. Over a 90-day test period, static repeatability of hourly horizontal and vertical coordinate estimates was assessed. Vertical RMS scatter ranged from 3.1 to 6.8 mm across services, compared with 1.9 mm achieved by post-processed static PPP using IGS final products. Convergence time after signal interruption varied from 14 to 37 minutes. Temperature-correlated apparent vertical oscillations of ±2 mm were observed and attributed to the combination of monument thermal expansion and service-specific tropospheric correction latency. The study discusses minimum convergence and precision requirements for real-time deformation monitoring applications in civil engineering practice and identifies conditions under which real-time PPP currently remains insufficient.

title: Epoch-by-Epoch Tropospheric Gradient Estimation from a Local GNSS Cluster: Implications for Differential Vertical Positioning in Hilly Terrain
abstract: A cluster of seven GNSS stations with inter-station distances between 8 and 35 km was established across a transect from the Pannonian plain to the southern slopes of the Fruška Gora hills to study horizontal tropospheric gradients at local scale. Epoch-by-epoch north and east gradient components were estimated using the GRAD mapping function and validated against radiosonde profiles from Novi Sad and a dense rain gauge network. Over the 24-month observation period, mean gradient magnitudes were 0.4–0.9 mm in the north–south direction and 0.2–0.5 mm east–west, with peak values exceeding 3 mm during convective episodes. Ignoring gradients in differential positioning introduced apparent height biases of up to 4 mm on baselines crossing the orographic boundary. A spatial interpolation procedure using atmospheric reanalysis fields to predict gradient fields is tested and reduces differential height biases by approximately 50 %. Practical guidance is given for geodetic surveys in areas of moderate relief.
