title: Towards a Unified Vertical Reference Frame for the Western Balkan Countries: Contributions from GNSS Permanent Networks
abstract: Establishing a height datum consistent across the Western Balkan countries requires combining national levelling networks with GNSS-derived vertical velocities to account for differential land motion that has accumulated since the reference epochs of existing datums. This book chapter reviews the available continuous GNSS infrastructure in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro, evaluates the quality and coverage of existing velocity solutions, and outlines a strategy for integrating GNSS vertical velocities with geoid models and levelling observations into a kinematic vertical reference frame. Particular attention is paid to the treatment of correlated noise in GNSS velocity fields and to the propagation of velocity uncertainties into datum-transformation parameters. The chapter includes a worked numerical example using data from 19 stations and concludes with a prioritised list of additional monitoring sites needed to achieve 0.5 mm/yr velocity precision across the entire region. Practical constraints related to data-sharing agreements between national geodetic authorities are also discussed.

title: Humidity sensor calibration drift under condensation cycles in refrigerated transport: a 12-month field study
abstract: Capacitive humidity sensors mounted inside refrigerated containers experience repeated condensation cycles that cause progressive calibration drift. This study tracked drift in 30 SHT31-based nodes deployed across six commercial refrigerated trailers over 12 months and approximately 280,000 km of operation. Sensors were retrieved and recalibrated against a chilled mirror reference hygrometer at three-month intervals. Mean drift at 12 months was +4.7% RH at 90% RH reference points and +1.2% RH at 50% RH, with high variability between units (standard deviation 2.1% and 0.8% respectively). Drift correlated significantly with the number of door-open events per month (r = 0.71, p < 0.01). A piecewise correction function estimated from the first three-month recalibration reduced 12-month error to below 1.5% RH for 80% of nodes. The results suggest that annual recalibration intervals are insufficient for high-cycling deployments.

title: LoRa coverage characterisation in mixed urban-rural transport corridors of the Pannonian Plain
abstract: LoRa radio coverage along the road corridors between Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin was characterised through drive-test campaigns conducted across four seasons. A mobile transmitter node using LoRa 868 MHz with spreading factor SF10 was driven 3,800 km while a fixed gateway network of nine nodes recorded received signal strength and packet reception rate. Median coverage distance to 90% packet reception was 6.4 km in flat open terrain, 3.1 km in peri-urban zones, and 1.8 km in industrial estate environments. Seasonal foliage effects accounted for a 2.8 dB median signal reduction in summer versus winter on tree-lined corridors. Empirical path-loss exponents are reported for each environment class. The data support gateway spacing recommendations of 9 km in open rural areas and 4 km in mixed-use zones for transport monitoring applications requiring 95% packet delivery.

title: Multi-point vibration and temperature co-logging in pharmaceutical cold chain transport: sensor placement and data rate trade-offs
abstract: Pharmaceutical products subject to temperature and vibration restrictions during transport require simultaneous monitoring of both parameters, yet most deployed systems treat them independently. This paper evaluates sensor placement strategies and data rate configurations for combined MEMS accelerometer and thermistor nodes in two vehicle types: a light van and a 3.5-tonne box truck. Eleven nodes were placed at positions defined by a factorial design across three axes of the cargo compartment. Vibration power spectral density and temperature time series were logged at 100 Hz and 60-second intervals respectively over 38 trial journeys. Results show that a three-node arrangement at front-top, rear-bottom, and centre-mid positions captures 87% of the variance in both parameters across all journey profiles. Reducing accelerometer sampling to 25 Hz retains PSD features relevant to the 5–50 Hz regulatory range while cutting node energy consumption by 43%.

title: Edge anomaly detection on LoRaWAN sensor nodes using a lightweight threshold-regression filter for cold-chain excursion flagging
abstract: Processing thermal excursion flags at the sensor node rather than in a central server reduces upstream data volume and enables immediate local alerts when cellular or LoRaWAN uplink is unavailable. This paper implements and evaluates a two-stage filter running on an ARM Cortex-M0+ microcontroller: a static upper-threshold check followed by a linear regression test over a 10-minute sliding window to distinguish genuine sustained excursions from transient measurement noise. Evaluation used 14 months of labelled temperature records from 40 deployed nodes covering vegetable transport in Vojvodina. The filter achieved 96.3% true positive rate and 1.8% false positive rate on held-out data, with average detection latency of 4.2 minutes. Flash and RAM footprints are 3.1 kB and 420 bytes respectively, compatible with nodes carrying 32 kB flash. Energy overhead over a standard logging firmware is 0.7%.

title: Spatiotemporal attribution of cold-chain excursions to logistics events using fused sensor and TMS data: a case study from Serbian fruit exports
abstract: Attributing temperature excursions in export fruit shipments to specific logistics events—pre-cooling, loading, border waiting, and unloading—requires merging continuous sensor records with event timestamps from transport management systems that often carry positional and temporal uncertainty. This paper presents a fusion method based on a hidden Markov model whose states correspond to logistics phases, estimated from GPS position, vehicle speed, door-open sensor, and reefer set-point change events. The method was evaluated on 6 months of data from 88 raspberry export journeys from Vojvodina to Germany. Attribution agreement with manually verified ground-truth logs was 89.4% at event-level and 94.1% at excursion-level. The most common attribution error was confusion between extended border waiting and unscheduled stops (7.2% of cases). The approach reduces manual audit time by an estimated 70% per shipment.

title: Power consumption profiling of a LoRaWAN end-node across spreading factors under dynamic network server load
abstract: ADR (Adaptive Data Rate) algorithms implemented on LoRaWAN network servers change node spreading factors in response to link quality, but the resulting energy impact at the node is rarely quantified under realistic, variable network load conditions. This paper reports bench measurements of a custom LoRaWAN end-node based on the SX1276 transceiver across SF7–SF12 at 14 dBm transmit power, combined with 72-hour field trials on a test route in Novi Sad under a three-gateway network with simulated variable congestion. Under ADR with moderate congestion, nodes settled at SF9 on average and consumed 38% more energy per day than static SF7 nodes, but exhibited 12% fewer uplink failures. A modified ADR policy that imposes a hysteresis band of 3 dB before SF escalation reduced energy overhead to 19% while maintaining uplink reliability above 97%. The implications for node battery sizing in multi-year cold-chain deployments are discussed.

title: A comparison of LoRaWAN, NB-IoT, and Sigfox for multi-point temperature monitoring along 800-km intermodal transport routes
abstract: Three low-power wide-area network technologies—LoRaWAN, NB-IoT, and Sigfox—were compared for suitability in continuous multi-point temperature monitoring along an intermodal (road plus rail) route from Novi Sad to Trieste. Parallel test nodes were fitted to six refrigerated containers and logged over 30 roundtrips between May 2022 and February 2023. Metrics collected included end-to-end packet delivery rate, latency, power consumption per successful uplink, and monthly connectivity cost at production tariffs. LoRaWAN private network delivered 91.4% PDR within the Pannonian Plain but dropped to 57% across Alpine terrain. NB-IoT achieved 95.1% PDR overall with 3.8-second median latency. Sigfox showed 88.6% PDR and lowest hardware cost. Per-uplink energy was lowest for LoRaWAN (1.8 mJ) and highest for NB-IoT (6.3 mJ). The paper provides a decision matrix for operators selecting connectivity technology based on route profile, reporting interval, and cost constraint.

title: Day-ahead PV forecasting for distribution feeders with satellite cloud data
abstract: This paper presents a day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting methodology for distribution feeders that integrates high-resolution satellite cloud motion imagery with numerical weather prediction data. The proposed framework applies a hybrid convolutional–recurrent neural network architecture to extract spatiotemporal cloud patterns and translate them into irradiance estimates at feeder level. Case studies are conducted on five medium-voltage distribution feeders in Vojvodina, covering a cumulative installed PV capacity of approximately 18 MW. The model is benchmarked against persistence, smart persistence, and a standard multilayer perceptron baseline. Results demonstrate a reduction of 17–23% in normalised root mean square error compared with the best-performing baseline across all test feeders. Probabilistic forecast intervals derived via conformal prediction are also evaluated using coverage and sharpness metrics. The methodology is designed to support intraday dispatch decisions by distribution system operators (DSOs) seeking to accommodate high shares of behind-the-meter solar generation while maintaining voltage profiles within statutory limits.

title: Demand response potential of industrial consumers in Vojvodina
abstract: Industrial consumers represent a largely untapped source of demand-side flexibility in South-East European electricity systems. This paper quantifies the demand response (DR) potential of manufacturing and agri-food processing facilities located in the Vojvodina region of Serbia through a combination of on-site energy audits, smart meter time-series analysis, and structured interviews with energy managers. Flexible loads are categorised by response speed, duration, and recovery constraints, yielding a total dispatchable capacity of 47 MW across the surveyed sample. The analysis reveals that refrigeration systems, compressed-air networks, and irrigation pumps collectively account for more than 60% of the identified flexibility. Barriers to market participation are examined, including the absence of a formalised balancing market product compatible with small aggregators and limited metering infrastructure at sub-hourly resolution. Policy recommendations are offered for aligning Serbian regulatory frameworks with EU demand response directives, and a roadmap for pilot aggregator programmes is outlined. The findings are directly relevant to distribution system operators and the emerging flexibility procurement landscape in the Western Balkans.

title: Probabilistic short-term load forecasting with gradient boosting
abstract: Accurate probabilistic short-term load forecasting (STLF) is essential for efficient energy scheduling, reserve dimensioning, and distribution network planning. This paper proposes a probabilistic STLF framework based on gradient boosting regression trees augmented with quantile loss functions, enabling simultaneous estimation of multiple prediction intervals without parametric distributional assumptions. A comprehensive feature engineering pipeline incorporates lagged consumption values, calendar effects, temperature dew-point interactions, and holiday indicators derived from Serbian public calendars. The model is trained and validated on two years of hourly active power measurements from 12 distribution substations supplied by a regional DSO in northern Serbia. Probabilistic calibration is assessed using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) and reliability diagrams across 10%, 50%, and 90% quantiles. The gradient boosting approach outperforms Gaussian process regression and quantile random forests on CRPS by margins of 8–14%, while maintaining sub-second inference times suitable for operational deployment. Practical guidance for hyperparameter tuning and rolling-window retraining schedules is also discussed.

title: Intraday solar irradiance nowcasting using sky-imager optical flow for urban distribution networks
abstract: Very short-term solar irradiance nowcasting is critical for real-time balancing of distribution networks with high rooftop PV penetration. This paper introduces an optical-flow-based nowcasting method that processes sequences of ground-level sky images captured at one-minute intervals by a network of low-cost all-sky cameras installed across the city of Novi Sad. Cloud motion vectors are estimated using a pyramidal Lucas–Kanade algorithm and projected onto a ground irradiance map via a geometric sky-to-plane transformation. The resulting irradiance field is aggregated to feeder level and evaluated against pyranometer measurements and smart inverter telemetry. Forecast horizons of 5, 15, and 30 minutes are examined. The optical flow model reduces mean absolute error by 21% relative to a persistence baseline at the 15-minute horizon. Uncertainty quantification is incorporated through an ensemble of perturbed optical flow fields, producing calibrated prediction intervals. Results demonstrate that sky-imager networks can complement satellite-based products and provide actionable nowcasts for DSO control room operators managing curtailment and reactive power compensation in real time.

title: Flexibility aggregation framework for residential prosumers in Serbian distribution grids
abstract: The proliferation of rooftop solar panels, home battery storage, and smart appliances is creating a new category of residential prosumers capable of providing grid flexibility services. However, aggregating small distributed resources into market-ready products remains technically and contractually complex, particularly in regulatory environments that have not yet fully transposed EU Clean Energy Package provisions. This paper proposes a hierarchical aggregation framework tailored to the Serbian distribution context, in which a virtual power plant (VPP) operator coordinates prosumer flexibility bids submitted to a day-ahead local flexibility market operated by the DSO. A mixed-integer linear programming dispatch model accounts for prosumer comfort constraints, battery state-of-charge limits, and network congestion thresholds. The framework is validated through a simulation study on a realistic 34-bus low-voltage feeder parameterised with data from a pilot neighbourhood in Novi Sad. Results show that coordinated prosumer dispatch reduces peak feeder loading by 18% while delivering measurable economic benefits to participants. Regulatory gaps and recommended amendments to Serbian energy bylaws are discussed.

title: Transfer learning for PV power forecasting across climate zones in the Western Balkans
abstract: Building accurate machine learning forecasting models for photovoltaic installations typically requires extensive historical generation data, which is unavailable for newly commissioned plants. Transfer learning offers a principled approach to knowledge reuse across sites with differing climatic and topographic characteristics. This study investigates domain adaptation strategies for day-ahead PV power forecasting across seven sites spanning the Western Balkans, representing Mediterranean, continental, and highland climate zones. A source-domain model pre-trained on a data-rich coastal site is fine-tuned using limited target-domain data through three transfer protocols: full network fine-tuning, feature extraction with frozen convolutional layers, and adversarial domain adaptation. Performance is assessed using normalised RMSE and skill score relative to smart persistence. Adversarial domain adaptation achieves the best generalisation with as few as 30 days of target-site observations, reducing normalised RMSE by up to 19% compared with a model trained from scratch on the same limited dataset. The results have practical implications for DSOs and project developers commissioning new solar farms where historical data are scarce.

title: Congestion management in active distribution networks through DSO-operated local flexibility markets
abstract: Active distribution networks with significant renewable generation increasingly face congestion events that traditional grid reinforcement cannot address cost-effectively in the short term. Local flexibility markets (LFMs) operated by distribution system operators offer an alternative mechanism in which prosumers and aggregators submit bids to resolve specific network constraints. This paper presents an LFM clearing algorithm based on an optimal power flow formulation with linearised branch flow equations, designed to accommodate the computational constraints of DSO operational systems. The algorithm is embedded within a co-simulation platform coupling a distribution grid model with an agent-based market simulator. Three congestion scenarios are evaluated on a 69-bus synthetic network calibrated to reflect a peri-urban feeder topology typical of northern Serbia. Comparative analysis against classical curtailment orders demonstrates that the LFM approach reduces total flexibility procurement costs by 31% on average while maintaining voltage and thermal compliance. Scalability to real DSO systems and interoperability with national balancing market products are discussed in the context of forthcoming Serbian grid code revisions.

title: Ensemble methods for week-ahead renewable generation forecasting in island microgrids
abstract: Week-ahead forecasting of combined wind and solar generation is a particularly challenging task in island microgrids, where limited interconnection and storage capacity amplify the operational consequences of forecast errors. This paper evaluates an ensemble forecasting architecture that combines output from three base learners—gradient boosted trees, long short-term memory networks, and a physical clear-sky model with meteorological corrections—using a stacking meta-learner trained to minimise a weighted combination of RMSE and the 90th-percentile quantile loss. The methodology is applied to a hypothetical island microgrid in the Adriatic, parameterised with meteorological reanalysis data and synthetic generation profiles. Week-ahead aggregate generation forecasts are produced at one-hour resolution for a 52-week test period. The stacking ensemble reduces RMSE by 14% and 22% compared with the best individual base learner for solar and wind components respectively. Sensitivity analysis reveals that the meta-learner's performance degrades gracefully under reduced training set sizes, suggesting applicability in data-sparse island settings. The proposed architecture is directly transferable to similar microgrids in the Serbian river island and mountain plateau context.

title: Smart metering data analytics for non-technical loss detection in Serbian distribution feeders
abstract: Non-technical losses (NTL) arising from electricity theft and meter tampering represent a significant financial burden for distribution system operators in South-East Europe, with estimates suggesting NTL rates of 4–9% in parts of Serbia. Advanced metering infrastructure deployments are generating large volumes of smart meter data that, if properly analysed, can provide early detection signals for NTL events. This paper develops a supervised anomaly detection pipeline that combines feature extraction from half-hourly consumption profiles—including load shape indices, phase imbalance ratios, and night-time baseload metrics—with a random forest classifier trained on labelled NTL incidents documented by a regional DSO. The classifier is augmented with a SHAP-based explainability module to assist field inspection teams in prioritising investigation visits. A retrospective study on 4,200 metering points over 18 months demonstrates a true positive rate of 78% at a false positive rate of 5%, substantially outperforming the DSO's existing rule-based detection system. The approach is designed to integrate with standard DSO SCADA and meter data management architectures without requiring proprietary data formats.

title: Regulatory and market design challenges for demand response in the Western Balkans energy community
abstract: The Energy Community Treaty obliges Western Balkans contracting parties, including Serbia, to progressively align their energy legislation with EU directives that explicitly recognise demand response as a market resource. Despite formal commitments, implementation has been slow, and industrial and commercial consumers remain largely excluded from balancing and ancillary services markets. This book chapter provides a comparative assessment of demand response regulatory frameworks across six Western Balkans jurisdictions, identifying transposition gaps, institutional capacity constraints, and market design features that impede flexibility procurement. Drawing on interviews with national regulatory authorities, transmission system operators, and industrial consumer associations, the chapter maps the gap between stated policy objectives and operational reality. It then proposes a phased regulatory roadmap aligned with EU Electricity Directive 2019/944 principles and adapted to the institutional context of the region. Key recommendations include the introduction of standardised flexibility product definitions, the designation of aggregator licensing regimes, and the establishment of sandbox provisions for pilot flexibility market trials. The chapter situates Serbia's FLEXGRID-RS initiative within this regional policy landscape.

title: A sub-threshold OTA topology for ECG front-ends in 180 nm CMOS with 320 nA supply current
abstract: This paper describes an operational transconductance amplifier designed to operate entirely in the sub-threshold region for use in single-lead ECG acquisition systems. The circuit was implemented in a 180 nm standard CMOS process. Biasing was set to achieve a quiescent current of 320 nA from a 1.2 V supply while maintaining an input-referred noise of 42 nV/√Hz at 100 Hz, sufficient for R-wave detection. The common-mode rejection ratio measured 78 dB across 20 fabricated dies. Electrode offset cancellation was addressed with a pseudo-resistor network whose impedance exceeded 10 GΩ at dc. Bandwidth could be digitally trimmed between 0.5 Hz and 150 Hz using a 3-bit switched-capacitor load. Measured results from twelve prototype boards equipped with dry Ag/AgCl electrodes showed SNR of 51 dB for a resting adult subject. Power consumption of the complete analogue chain, including a first-order high-pass filter, was 890 nW. The design occupies 0.041 mm² of active silicon area.

title: Characterisation of packet collision statistics in IEEE 802.15.4 networks under periodic biomedical traffic patterns
abstract: Biomedical body-area networks impose deterministic, quasi-periodic traffic from multiple sensor nodes sampling at fixed physiological rates such as 250 Hz for EMG or 500 Hz for EEG. Standard CSMA/CA back-off procedures in IEEE 802.15.4 were evaluated through a combination of analytical modelling using a two-dimensional Markov chain and hardware experiments with fifteen custom nodes based on a CC2520 transceiver. Traffic was generated to emulate simultaneous ECG at 250 samples/s, SpO2 at 50 samples/s, and skin temperature at 1 sample/s. Packet delivery ratio dropped from 98.7% with a single node to 83.2% with six co-located nodes at the default back-off exponent settings. Adjusting the minimum back-off exponent from 3 to 5 and reducing the maximum number of back-offs from 5 to 3 recovered delivery ratio to 96.1% for six nodes, at the cost of a mean latency increase of 4.1 ms. The paper provides a lookup table of recommended parameter combinations for clinically relevant node counts.

title: Energy budget analysis of implantable glucose monitors: from sensing front-end to RF uplink
abstract: Continuous glucose monitors intended for subcutaneous implantation face a hard energy ceiling imposed by the volume available for primary cells or inductive charging coils. This work presents a structured energy budget partitioning the 50 µW mean power allocated in a hypothetical 1 cm³ implant across four subsystems: the amperometric sensing front-end (8 µW), the 8-bit ADC (3 µW), the microcontroller running a linearisation algorithm (12 µW), and the 2.4 GHz OOK transmitter (27 µW active, duty-cycled to 0.4%). A custom switched-capacitor potentiostat operating at 100 mV applied potential consumed 6.1 µW measured on bench. The ADC was a successive-approximation design clocked at 10 kHz with an effective number of bits of 7.6. End-to-end system simulation using measured component data predicted a node lifetime of 14 days from a 4 mAh primary lithium cell, which is consistent with reported values in the literature for comparable implant geometries. Identified bottlenecks and proposed architectural changes are discussed.

title: Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes
abstract: This work, developed as part of the author's doctoral research, proposes a beacon-enabled superframe structure derived from IEEE 802.15.4 in which guaranteed time slots are assigned according to each sensor stream's sampling deadline rather than priority class alone. The scheduler runs on a body hub modelled as a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M3 at 4 MHz and accepts registration messages carrying a sampling period, payload size, and maximum tolerable latency for each node. A first-fit decreasing bin-packing heuristic assigns contiguous slots within each superframe. Simulation across 10,000 randomly generated workloads with 2–8 nodes showed that deadline miss rates remained below 0.3% for workloads at up to 80% superframe utilisation. Radio duty cycle for a six-node ECG plus EMG scenario was reduced to 1.8% compared with 6.4% under a fixed-slot baseline, yielding a projected 3.5-fold increase in node battery lifetime. The protocol was prototyped on a Cortex-M0 hub with four slave nodes and validated against simulated data.

title: Low-power multi-electrode bioimpedance spectroscopy front-end for wearable fluid monitoring
abstract: Bioimpedance spectroscopy between 1 kHz and 1 MHz can track extracellular fluid shifts relevant to oedema management in heart failure patients. This paper describes a four-electrode analogue front-end implemented in discrete components on a flexible PCB targeting wrist-worn use. A current source based on a Howland pump injected 50 µA peak sinusoidal current; the driving waveform was generated by a DDS peripheral on a low-power ARM microcontroller. Voltage was sensed by an instrumentation amplifier with a gain-bandwidth product of 10 MHz and an input impedance exceeding 100 MΩ. Phase and magnitude were extracted by a hardware lock-in approach sampling at 50 kSa/s and performing 16-point coherent averaging on the microcontroller. Average system current consumption was 1.4 mA during a 200 ms measurement burst and 3.8 µA in sleep. Accuracy of extracted resistance and reactance was within 1.2% of values measured with a laboratory impedance analyser across a 30-sample tissue-equivalent phantom set covering the physiological range of 20–800 Ω.

title: Energy harvesting from body heat for wearable ECG patches: thermoelectric generator characterisation and power management circuit
abstract: Wearable ECG patches worn continuously on the thorax can harvest energy from the skin-to-air temperature gradient, which typically spans 3–8 K in indoor environments. This work characterises six commercial thermoelectric generator (TEG) modules with active areas of 10–40 mm² under a simulated skin load using a temperature-controlled copper plate and forced convection at 0.5 m/s. Open-circuit voltages ranged from 18 mV to 74 mV at a 5 K gradient. A boost converter based on the BQ25504 integrated circuit with an impedance-matching network achieved maximum power point tracking efficiency of 82% across the characterised voltage range. Harvested power delivered to a 4.7 µF storage capacitor reached 48 µW at 5 K gradient for the 30 mm² module. A duty-cycle controller using a comparator and a timer allowed the ECG front-end described in a previous paper to operate from the harvested supply alone when the gradient exceeded 4.2 K, as verified over 48-hour benchtop trials. Implications for electrode placement and garment integration are discussed.

title: Compressed sensing reconstruction for sparse EEG signals acquired by sub-mW wireless nodes: a comparison of three recovery algorithms
abstract: EEG signals exhibit sparsity in the wavelet domain; compressed sensing (CS) can therefore reduce the number of samples transmitted over a wireless link, cutting radio energy. This paper evaluates three recovery algorithms — basis pursuit denoising (BPDN), orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), and iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) — applied to EEG segments recorded from eight healthy subjects performing an eyes-open resting task. Compression ratios of 2×, 4×, and 8× were tested by randomly sub-sampling a 256 Hz, 16-channel stream at the sensor node simulated in MATLAB. At a 4× ratio, BPDN achieved a mean per-channel SNR of 28.3 dB, OMP 24.7 dB, and IRLS 27.9 dB. Clinical-grade feature detection for alpha-band power (8–13 Hz) was preserved with less than 5% relative error for BPDN and IRLS at 4× but degraded sharply at 8×. Transmission energy savings estimated from a Cortex-M0 radio model were 61% at 4× compression after accounting for the reconstruction overhead run on the hub.

title: A 0.6 V, 210 nW instrumentation amplifier with reconfigurable gain for multi-modal biopotential acquisition in 65 nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a capacitively-coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) fabricated in a 65 nm low-power CMOS process and intended to serve both ECG (gain 40 dB, bandwidth 0.5–150 Hz) and EEG (gain 52 dB, bandwidth 0.5–80 Hz) acquisition modes selectable at run time via a 1-bit digital input. Supply voltage is 0.6 V drawn from an energy-harvesting rail. Total quiescent current across both amplifier stages is 350 nA. Input-referred noise integrated over the ECG band is 0.41 µVrms, and over the EEG band is 0.37 µVrms. The mid-band CMRR measured 91 dB for ECG mode and 88 dB for EEG mode. Electrode offset rejection was verified with offsets up to ±300 mV applied via a dc servo loop consuming 18 nA. The circuit was characterised on 20 dies; gain spread across dies was ±0.4 dB. Post-layout simulations and measured data are compared and show less than 6% discrepancy in noise and 3% in bandwidth.

title: Cutting false atrial fibrillation alarms in patch ECG with motion-aware filtering
abstract: Patch-based ECG monitors are increasingly deployed for continuous ambulatory cardiac surveillance, yet their clinical utility is severely limited by high false-positive rates for atrial fibrillation (AF) alarms, largely attributable to motion artifacts. This paper presents a motion-aware filtering framework that fuses single-lead ECG signals with three-axis accelerometer data recorded simultaneously by the same wearable patch. The proposed method employs an adaptive notch filter whose coefficients are dynamically updated according to a motion-intensity index derived from accelerometer magnitude. A subsequent AF detector based on RR-interval irregularity metrics is applied to the cleaned signal. The system was evaluated on a dataset of 312 twenty-four-hour recordings collected from 89 volunteers performing standardized daily activities including walking, stair climbing, and cycling. Compared with a baseline detector operating on raw ECG, the proposed approach reduced false AF alarms by 61% while maintaining sensitivity above 94% on confirmed AF episodes verified by a board-certified cardiologist. Processing latency was benchmarked on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, confirming real-time feasibility. The results demonstrate that tightly coupled motion-aware signal conditioning is essential for trustworthy AF screening in free-living conditions.

title: Single-lead ECG arrhythmia classification on a microcontroller
abstract: Arrhythmia classification in wearable cardiac monitors demands algorithms compact enough to execute entirely on the sensor node, eliminating reliance on continuous cloud connectivity. This paper describes the design and validation of a single-lead ECG arrhythmia classifier implemented on a low-power 32-bit microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M0+, 48 MHz, 32 kB RAM). The classifier distinguishes five rhythm classes—normal sinus rhythm, atrial fibrillation, premature ventricular contractions, supraventricular tachycardia, and noise—using a lightweight feature set comprising RR-interval statistics, QRS morphology descriptors, and a three-stage decision-tree ensemble. Memory-efficient quantization reduces all floating-point parameters to 8-bit fixed-point representations without measurable accuracy loss. Evaluated on a held-out split of 4,200 annotated 30-second segments, the on-device model achieved a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.87 and consumed an average of 1.4 mW during inference, enabling operation for more than 72 hours on a 180 mAh coin cell. The work demonstrates a practical pathway toward fully autonomous, battery-powered cardiac monitors suitable for remote patient monitoring in resource-limited settings.

title: Activity recognition from chest-worn accelerometers
abstract: Accurate activity recognition from chest-worn inertial measurement units is a prerequisite for context-aware physiological monitoring, yet most published benchmarks rely on wrist or hip placements. This study investigates the suitability of a single chest-mounted accelerometer for recognizing twelve daily-life activities including rest, walking, jogging, stair ascent and descent, cycling, and six sedentary postures. Features extracted in the time and frequency domains from three-axis acceleration signals were used to train and compare a k-nearest neighbor classifier, a random forest, and a support vector machine with radial basis function kernel. Data were collected from 45 healthy adults across a structured protocol lasting approximately 90 minutes per participant. The random forest achieved the highest overall accuracy of 92.3% in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. A confusion analysis revealed that the chest location provides particularly strong discrimination between static postures, outperforming wrist placement on that sub-task. The findings support the integration of chest-worn accelerometers into ECG patch monitors for simultaneous cardiac and activity monitoring without additional sensor hardware.

title: Benchmark dataset for motion-corrupted patch ECG and simultaneous accelerometry in free-living adults
abstract: High-quality annotated datasets pairing ambulatory ECG recordings with synchronised inertial data from the same wearable patch remain scarce, hampering reproducible research on motion-artifact suppression and context-aware cardiac monitoring. This paper describes the NovaSAD-PatchECG dataset: 128 recordings of 48 hours each, collected from 64 healthy volunteers and 64 patients with known arrhythmia history. Each recording includes single-lead ECG sampled at 500 Hz, three-axis accelerometer data at 100 Hz, and ground-truth rhythm annotations produced by two independent cardiologists with inter-annotator agreement reported via Cohen's kappa. Participants performed a standardized protocol encompassing controlled laboratory activities and unrestricted daily life. The dataset captures a diverse range of motion intensities, electrode contact qualities, and arrhythmia types. Baseline performance figures for three published AF detectors are reported to facilitate fair future comparisons. The dataset is released under an open-access licence and accompanied by Python-based loading utilities. We anticipate that this resource will accelerate development and fair benchmarking of wearable cardiac monitoring algorithms, particularly those addressing false-alarm reduction and real-time on-device inference.

title: Federated learning for atrial fibrillation detection across heterogeneous wearable ECG devices
abstract: Training robust atrial fibrillation detectors on data pooled from multiple clinical sites raises significant patient privacy concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving alternative by training shared model parameters without centralizing raw recordings. This work presents a federated AF detection framework tailored to the heterogeneous signal characteristics encountered when aggregating data from four distinct wearable ECG patch platforms with differing sampling rates, electrode configurations, and noise profiles. A domain-adaptive normalization layer is inserted before each local model head to compensate for device-specific distributional shifts. Communication efficiency is improved through gradient sparsification with a threshold calibrated per round. Experiments conducted on data partitioned across five simulated client nodes demonstrate that the federated model achieves within 2.1 percentage points of a centrally trained oracle in terms of F1 score for AF detection, while keeping raw data entirely local. Convergence analysis shows stable training within 35 communication rounds. The proposed approach is directly applicable to collaborative model development between hospitals and medical device manufacturers operating under strict data governance constraints.

title: Energy-efficient QRS detection on ultra-low-power microcontrollers for long-term cardiac patches
abstract: Battery life is the dominant constraint for wearable cardiac patches intended for multi-week arrhythmia screening. This paper presents an ultra-low-power QRS detection algorithm specifically designed for deployment on a 16-bit microcontroller operating at 8 MHz with 4 kB of available SRAM. The algorithm adapts the classical Pan–Tompkins pipeline by replacing floating-point operations with integer arithmetic and replacing the bandpass filter with a computationally cheaper differentiator-squarer cascade whose coefficients are pre-quantized to powers of two, enabling shift-based multiplication. Threshold adaptation is reformulated as a recursive integer update requiring no division. The implementation is benchmarked on five publicly available ECG databases totalling over 120,000 annotated beats, achieving a detection sensitivity of 99.1% and positive predictivity of 98.9%. On the target microcontroller, the algorithm consumes 87 μW at 500 Hz input, extending projected patch lifetime from 9 to 21 days compared with a floating-point baseline at equivalent sampling rate. The source code is released openly to support reproducibility and adoption in resource-constrained medical device development.

title: Combining heart rate variability and accelerometer features for stress detection in free-living conditions
abstract: Continuous stress monitoring in everyday life has attracted growing interest as a tool for preventive mental health management, yet most validated methods require laboratory-controlled conditions. This paper investigates a multimodal approach that fuses heart rate variability (HRV) indices derived from a chest-worn ECG patch with accelerometer-based activity features to infer subjective stress levels in free-living adults. Thirty-six participants wore the sensor system continuously for five days while self-reporting stress events via a smartphone application. A total of 41 time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear HRV features were extracted over non-overlapping five-minute windows and combined with six activity context features capturing posture and movement intensity. A random forest classifier trained with leave-one-day-out cross-validation achieved a binary stress/non-stress accuracy of 76.4%, improving by 8.3 percentage points over HRV-only baselines. Analysis of feature importance revealed that low-frequency HRV power and accelerometer-derived posture class were the two most discriminative predictors. The study highlights that activity context is an important confound in wearable stress detection and should be accounted for in algorithm design.

title: Signal quality assessment for single-lead wearable ECG: a survey and comparative study
abstract: Reliable automatic interpretation of single-lead wearable ECG recordings is contingent upon accurate signal quality assessment (SQA), yet no consensus exists on the best methodology for this task. This survey reviews 38 SQA algorithms published between 2010 and 2022, categorizing them by feature type (statistical, spectral, template-based, and learned), classification strategy, and target application domain. We implement and comparatively evaluate nine representative approaches on two independent ECG datasets collected with chest-worn patches under both controlled and free-living conditions. Evaluation metrics include per-segment quality classification accuracy, computational cost on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, and downstream impact on AF detector performance when SQA-based segment rejection is applied as a pre-processing gate. Results show that lightweight spectral flatness combined with kurtosis achieves the best accuracy-to-cost trade-off for real-time embedded use, while deep-learning approaches yield superior accuracy at much higher computational expense. The survey concludes with a discussion of open challenges including cross-device generalization and labelling inconsistencies across public datasets.

title: Wearable biomedical systems: signal acquisition, processing and clinical translation
abstract: This book chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the engineering challenges involved in translating wearable biomedical sensing systems from laboratory prototypes to clinically validated devices. The chapter covers the full signal chain from electrode–skin interface physics and analog front-end design through digital signal processing pipelines to clinical validation methodology. Particular attention is paid to the interplay between hardware constraints—power budget, memory, communication bandwidth—and algorithm design choices for cardiac and motion signals. The ECG acquisition and arrhythmia detection pipeline is used as a running example throughout, illustrating how design decisions at each layer propagate to end-to-end system performance. A dedicated section addresses regulatory considerations under the European Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) relevant to software-as-a-medical-device classification of on-device diagnostic algorithms. The chapter concludes with a roadmap for future research directions including personalized adaptive algorithms, multi-sensor fusion, and privacy-preserving distributed learning. It is intended as a graduate-level reference for students and practitioners entering the field of wearable medical technology.

title: Personalized adaptive thresholds for arrhythmia detectors in long-term ECG monitoring
abstract: Fixed detection thresholds in ambulatory arrhythmia monitors fail to account for inter-individual variability in cardiac electrophysiology and body habitus, leading to systematically elevated false-positive rates in certain patient subgroups. This paper proposes a patient-adaptive threshold framework for wearable ECG arrhythmia detectors in which detection parameters are continuously updated using an online Bayesian update rule applied to a rolling window of high-confidence rhythm annotations from the preceding monitoring period. The method requires no pre-training on patient-specific data and is therefore directly applicable from the first hour of monitoring. Computational overhead is bounded to allow deployment alongside an existing QRS detector on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The framework is evaluated on long-term recordings from 58 patients with documented paroxysmal AF. Compared with fixed-threshold detectors, the adaptive approach reduces the per-patient median false-alarm rate by 47% while maintaining sensitivity above 91% across all subgroups stratified by age, sex, and body mass index. The results support patient-adaptive personalization as a practical and computationally tractable strategy for improving specificity in clinical-grade wearable cardiac monitors.

title: Thermal cycling-induced stress accumulation in bisphenol-A epoxy encapsulants: an experimental baseline study
abstract: This study establishes baseline thermomechanical behaviour of a commercially formulated bisphenol-A epoxy encapsulant subjected to thermal cycling between −40 °C and +125 °C. Specimens were prepared by casting into aluminium moulds and cured at 150 °C for 90 minutes. Thermal cycling was conducted in a programmable climate chamber with a ramp rate of 10 °C/min and dwell times of 10 minutes at each extreme. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) was carried out at 1 Hz after every 250 cycles up to 2000 cycles total. Results show a progressive decrease in storage modulus from 3.8 GPa at cycle zero to 2.9 GPa after 2000 cycles, accompanied by a shift in the glass transition temperature of approximately 6 °C downward. Scanning electron microscopy of fracture surfaces after 1000 cycles reveals the onset of microvoid coalescence near filler particle interfaces. These findings provide quantitative reference data for subsequent modelling work and accelerated life prediction protocols for encapsulant systems in electronic assemblies.

title: Comparative delamination resistance of silicone and epoxy encapsulants at copper lead-frame interfaces under isothermal ageing
abstract: Interfacial adhesion between polymer encapsulants and copper lead-frames was evaluated for two commercial systems: a room-temperature-vulcanising silicone and an anhydride-cured epoxy. Double-cantilever beam specimens with electropolished copper substrates were aged isothermally at 85 °C and 85% relative humidity for periods of 0, 250, 500 and 1000 hours. Mode-I fracture toughness (GIc) was measured by displacement-controlled peel tests at a crosshead speed of 0.5 mm/min. The silicone system retained 78% of its initial GIc after 1000 hours, whereas the epoxy retained only 41%, a reduction attributed to hydrolytic chain scission confirmed by FTIR spectroscopy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated copper oxide layer growth of approximately 3 nm at the interface after 500 hours in both systems. The results suggest that silicone formulations offer superior long-term adhesion stability under humid thermal conditions relevant to outdoor power module applications.

title: A two-dimensional finite-element model for predicting encapsulant crack initiation in surface-mount device packages
abstract: A plane-strain finite-element model was developed in Abaqus 6.12 to simulate stress distribution within a simplified surface-mount device package subjected to thermal cycling from −55 °C to +150 °C at a rate of 15 °C/min. The model comprised four material layers: a FR-4 substrate, solder mask, die-attach adhesive, and epoxy encapsulant, with temperature-dependent elastic moduli taken from experimental DMA data. Mesh refinement was applied at the encapsulant–substrate interface using 4-node bilinear plane-strain elements with a minimum element size of 5 µm. Von Mises stress peaks of 47 MPa were predicted at the package corner during the cold dwell phase, correlating spatially with delamination initiation sites observed in cross-sectioned samples. Parametric studies varying encapsulant elastic modulus between 2 and 5 GPa show that a reduction of 1 GPa reduces peak stress by approximately 12%. The model was validated against strain gauge measurements on test vehicles with a mean absolute error of 8%.

title: Accelerated ageing protocol development for epoxy encapsulants in automotive control units: temperature–humidity combinations
abstract: The study reports the development and validation of a combined temperature–humidity accelerated ageing protocol tailored for epoxy encapsulants used in automotive engine control modules. Four stress conditions (85 °C/85% RH; 85 °C/60% RH; 65 °C/85% RH; 65 °C/60% RH) were applied to standardised beam specimens for up to 2000 hours. Degradation was tracked by periodic measurement of flexural modulus, tensile strength, and water uptake by gravimetry. The 85 °C/85% RH condition produced a 34% reduction in tensile strength after 1000 hours, whereas the mildest condition produced only 9% reduction after 2000 hours. An Arrhenius–Eyring model was fitted to the data; the derived activation energy was 62 kJ/mol. Scanning acoustic microscopy was used after each test interval to detect internal void formation. The protocol was benchmarked against IEC 60749-4 requirements and found to accelerate equivalent field degradation by a factor of 12–18 relative to a nominal 10-year automotive service life at 55 °C average temperature.

title: Viscoelastic constitutive modelling of encapsulant creep under long-duration compressive loading: a three-parameter solid approach
abstract: Long-term creep behaviour of an anhydride-cured epoxy encapsulant was characterised under uniaxial compression at four stress levels (5, 10, 20 and 30 MPa) and three temperatures (25, 60 and 85 °C) for durations up to 1000 hours. Measured creep strains were fitted using a three-parameter generalised Maxwell solid model within an ABAQUS UMAT subroutine. At 85 °C and 30 MPa, total creep strain reached 1.8%, compared to 0.4% at 25 °C. Time–temperature superposition was applied to construct master curves with a reference temperature of 25 °C; the shift factor followed the WLF equation with constants C1 = 11.2 and C2 = 68.4 K. Model predictions agreed with independent relaxation tests to within 7% over the entire load–temperature space examined. The calibrated UMAT was subsequently incorporated into a full package-level finite-element model to assess creep-induced stress relaxation at bond-wire attachment points during solder reflow.

title: Delamination growth kinetics at the epoxy–silicon interface during thermal shock: an in-situ digital image correlation study
abstract: In-situ digital image correlation (DIC) was used to track delamination front propagation at an epoxy encapsulant–silicon die interface during rapid thermal shock cycling between −40 °C and +125 °C with transition times of approximately 30 seconds. Transparent package test structures were fabricated with a borosilicate glass die surrogate to allow optical access. Full-field surface displacement maps at 2 Hz acquisition rate revealed a discontinuous, stick-slip mode of delamination advance, with crack jumps of 50–150 µm occurring predominantly at the end of the cold dwell phase. The measured strain energy release rate at the crack front ranged from 85 to 210 J/m², which brackets the independently measured mode-II adhesive toughness (GIIc = 145 J/m²). Delamination velocity correlated with cooling rate above a threshold of 8 °C/min. The data set provides direct experimental evidence for rate-dependent adhesive failure and was used to calibrate cohesive zone model parameters for subsequent simulations.

title: Finite-element cohesive zone modelling of interfacial delamination in overmoulded semiconductor packages under thermal cycling
abstract: A three-dimensional finite-element model incorporating bilinear cohesive zone elements was built in Abaqus 2019 to simulate delamination at the epoxy moulding compound–leadframe interface in a standard SOIC-8 package. Cohesive zone parameters (peak traction 38 MPa, critical separation 4.2 µm, fracture energy 125 J/m²) were taken from DIC experiments on peel specimens. Thermal cycling loads ranged from −40 °C to +125 °C over 3000 cycles. The simulation predicted delamination onset at approximately 650 cycles, in agreement with acoustic emission measurements showing a significant event cluster beginning at 610 cycles. After 3000 cycles, predicted delaminated area covered 38% of the total interface, consistent with scanning acoustic microscopy images showing 34%. A sensitivity analysis over adhesion fracture energy in the range 80–180 J/m² showed that a ±30% variation shifts predicted onset by approximately ±220 cycles. The model demonstrates predictive utility for package qualification without requiring full thermal cycling campaigns.

title: Influence of underfill material selection on solder joint fatigue life in flip-chip assemblies: an experimental and modelling comparison
abstract: Three underfill formulations — a standard capillary epoxy, a reworkable thermoplastic-modified epoxy, and a no-flow epoxy — were evaluated for their effect on solder joint fatigue life in daisy-chain flip-chip test vehicles on FR-4 boards. Assemblies were subjected to ATC from 0 °C to +100 °C at a 10 °C/min ramp rate. Electrical resistance monitoring detected first failure events at 712, 487 and 893 cycles for the standard, reworkable, and no-flow formulations respectively, with 63% failure thresholds defined by Weibull analysis of 20 assemblies per group. Warpage measurements using shadow moiré interferometry at −40 °C and +125 °C showed maximum bow values of 48–92 µm depending on formulation. A 2.5D axisymmetric FE model with Anand viscoplastic solder constitutive parameters reproduced solder strain energy density trends to within 14% of experimental Weibull means. The results indicate that no-flow underfill provides the best fatigue performance under the test conditions examined, despite exhibiting the highest post-cure modulus.

title: Post-reflow void content and its effect on delamination resistance in capillary underfill systems: an X-ray tomography study
abstract: X-ray micro-computed tomography (µCT) at 5 µm voxel resolution was used to quantify void distribution in capillary underfill specimens cured under three different reflow profiles. Void volume fractions of 1.2%, 3.4% and 5.8% were measured for profiles with peak temperatures of 245, 260 and 275 °C respectively. Specimens were subsequently subjected to 1000 thermal shock cycles (−55 °C to +125 °C), and delamination area at the underfill–substrate interface was mapped by scanning acoustic microscopy before and after cycling. A linear correlation (R² = 0.91) was found between initial void volume fraction and post-cycling delaminated area fraction. Three-dimensional finite-element models incorporating void distributions imported directly from µCT reconstructions predicted local stress concentrations up to 2.3× the void-free baseline, explaining premature delamination initiation at void clusters located within 50 µm of the interface. The study supports the use of µCT as a non-destructive qualification screening tool prior to thermal cycling tests.

title: Thermomechanical fatigue behaviour of bio-based epoxy encapsulants derived from epoxidised soybean oil
abstract: Bio-based epoxy encapsulants synthesised from epoxidised soybean oil (ESO) blended with a cycloaliphatic anhydride hardener at three ESO–conventional epoxy weight ratios (25:75, 50:50 and 75:25) were evaluated for thermomechanical performance relative to a fully petroleum-derived reference. DMA measurements showed glass transition temperatures of 92, 71 and 48 °C for the three blends compared to 118 °C for the reference. Accelerated thermal cycling (−40 °C to +125 °C, 1000 cycles) resulted in 22% lower fatigue crack density in the 25:75 blend compared to the reference, attributed to increased toughness (plain-strain fracture toughness KIc = 0.91 MPa·m¹/² versus 0.74 MPa·m¹/² for the reference). However, the 75:25 blend exhibited unacceptable creep at 85 °C. Contact angle measurements after ageing showed reduced hydrophilicity in the ESO-rich blends. The 25:75 formulation is identified as a technically viable partial bio-based substitute, subject to glass-transition temperature limitations in high-temperature applications.

title: Seal integrity degradation in epoxy-encapsulated MEMS pressure sensors under combined mechanical vibration and thermal cycling
abstract: This study characterises the combined effect of random mechanical vibration and thermal cycling on the seal integrity of epoxy-encapsulated MEMS pressure sensors. Test vehicles were subjected simultaneously to broadband random vibration (20–2000 Hz, 5.4 Grms) and thermal cycling (−40 °C to +85 °C, 500 cycles) in a purpose-built combined loading fixture. Seal hermeticity was assessed by helium leak testing (threshold 1×10⁻⁸ mbar·L/s) at intervals of 100 cycles. Under combined loading, seal failure occurred at a mean of 280 cycles, compared to 440 cycles under thermal cycling alone and no failures under vibration alone up to 500 cycles. Finite-element simulations using a coupled thermomechanical solver with Rayleigh damping (α = 18.4 s⁻¹, β = 1.2×10⁻⁵ s) reproduced the trend of earlier failure onset under combined loading; predicted interface peel stress exceeded measured mode-I toughness by cycle 290. The results indicate a significant synergistic interaction between vibration-induced fatigue and thermal-cycling-driven delamination in MEMS sensor packages.

title: Moisture uptake kinetics in uncoated and clay-coated recycled paperboard under cyclic humidity conditions
abstract: Recycled paperboard samples with and without a commercial kaolin clay coating were subjected to cyclic humidity programmes alternating between 35 % and 85 % relative humidity at 23 °C over 72-hour periods. Mass gain and dimensional change were recorded at 30-minute intervals using a precision gravimetric rig. Clay-coated boards showed 38 % lower equilibrium moisture content compared to uncoated controls, with a retardation of the initial fast-sorption phase by approximately 2.5 hours. Fickian diffusion modelling provided adequate fits (R² > 0.96) for the first sorption cycle, but systematic deviations appeared in subsequent cycles, suggesting irreversible fibre swelling. Cross-sectional SEM imaging confirmed delamination at the clay–fibre interface after five humidity cycles. The results indicate that single-layer clay coatings offer limited long-term hygroscopic resistance and that interface adhesion must be considered alongside bulk WVTR values when specifying barrier performance.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid total tau and phospho-tau181 levels in a Serbian memory clinic population: reference intervals and diagnostic cut-offs
abstract: We established reference intervals for CSF total tau (t-tau) and phosphorylated tau at threonine 181 (p-tau181) in a memory clinic cohort of 218 participants recruited at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina between 2007 and 2009. Participants were classified as cognitively normal (n=74), mild cognitive impairment (MCI, n=89), and probable Alzheimer's disease (AD, n=55) according to NINCDS-ADRDA criteria. CSF was analysed by commercial sandwich ELISA. Median p-tau181 was 43 pg/mL in controls, 67 pg/mL in MCI, and 112 pg/mL in AD. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis yielded an AUC of 0.84 for discriminating AD from controls using a cut-off of 78 pg/mL (sensitivity 80%, specificity 82%). The t-tau/Aβ42 ratio added marginal discriminatory value over p-tau181 alone in this sample. These data provide the first locally derived diagnostic thresholds for a South-Eastern European population and suggest that cut-offs from Western European studies may require regional calibration.

title: Comparison of INNOTEST and in-house ELISA platforms for p-tau181 quantification in CSF: implications for interlaboratory standardisation
abstract: Interlaboratory variability in CSF phospho-tau measurement remains a practical barrier to multicentre studies. We compared the INNOTEST hTAU Ag commercial assay against an in-house sandwich ELISA developed using monoclonal antibody AT270 for capture and HT7 for detection, testing 120 CSF samples from patients with MCI or early AD. Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) between platforms was 0.91 (95% CI 0.87–0.94), with a mean absolute difference of 6.2 pg/mL. Bland–Altman analysis revealed proportional bias at higher concentrations (>100 pg/mL), with the in-house assay yielding systematically lower values. Calibrator choice accounted for approximately 40% of the observed bias when tested with external reference material. These findings support the feasibility of the in-house platform for research use but indicate recalibration is required before clinical deployment. Detailed protocol and calibration curve data are provided.

title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of abnormal CSF biomarker profiles in a community-based elderly cohort from Vojvodina
abstract: Population-based data on CSF Alzheimer's disease biomarker prevalence are scarce in Central and Eastern Europe. We performed lumbar puncture in 143 volunteers aged 65–80 years recruited from three primary care practices in Novi Sad and Sremska Mitrovica as part of a regional ageing study. Participants were screened with MMSE and CDR; those with CDR ≥1 were excluded. CSF Aβ42, t-tau, and p-tau181 were measured by ELISA. Using locally established cut-offs, 22% of cognitively normal participants had at least one abnormal biomarker value. The proportion rose to 34% in those with subjective cognitive complaints. Age (OR 1.12 per year, 95% CI 1.06–1.19) and APOE ε4 carriership (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.4–5.6) were independent predictors of abnormal p-tau181. These prevalence estimates align with Western European data after age adjustment.

title: Differential phosphorylation of tau at threonines 181 and 231 across the Alzheimer's disease clinical spectrum
abstract: Phosphorylation of tau at threonine 231 (p-tau231) has been proposed to reflect earlier pathological changes than p-tau181. We measured both isoforms by ELISA in CSF from 192 participants: 58 controls, 72 MCI, and 62 AD dementia patients, all from the Vojvodina memory clinic. The p-tau231/p-tau181 ratio was examined as a potential staging marker. Mean p-tau231 was 22.4 pg/mL in controls, 38.7 in MCI, and 54.1 in AD. The ratio p-tau231/p-tau181 was significantly higher in MCI compared with AD (1.09 vs 0.87, p=0.003), consistent with a steeper relative increase in p-tau231 at earlier stages. ROC analysis showed p-tau231 outperformed p-tau181 for MCI-versus-control discrimination (AUC 0.81 vs 0.74, p=0.04). Results support using p-tau231 as a primary marker for pre-dementia screening in clinical settings where lumbar puncture is feasible.

title: CSF biomarker profiling in Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia: a regional differential diagnosis cohort study
abstract: Distinguishing Alzheimer's disease from frontotemporal dementia (FTD) in clinical practice relies heavily on imaging, but CSF biomarkers offer complementary value. We recruited 241 patients from neurology centres in Novi Sad, Niš, and Zagreb: 98 AD, 61 FTD, and 82 other dementias or non-demented controls. CSF p-tau181, t-tau, and Aβ42 were measured by ELISA; neurofilament light chain (NfL) was measured by single-molecule array (Simoa) as an exploratory marker. The p-tau181/t-tau ratio discriminated AD from FTD with AUC 0.88 (sensitivity 82%, specificity 85% at cut-off 0.46). NfL was elevated in both AD and FTD relative to controls and did not improve discrimination. In multivariate logistic regression, p-tau181/t-tau and age were the only independent predictors. These data support the diagnostic utility of p-tau isoform ratios in a regional referral setting with limited imaging access.

title: Genetic modifiers of CSF p-tau levels in a Serbian AD cohort: associations with PICALM and BIN1 variants
abstract: Genome-wide association studies have implicated PICALM and BIN1 as late-onset AD susceptibility loci, but their influence on CSF biomarker concentrations is less characterised in Southern European populations. We genotyped 196 participants from the Vojvodina memory clinic cohort (114 AD, 82 controls) for rs3851179 (PICALM), rs744373 (BIN1), and APOE ε4. CSF p-tau181 and t-tau were measured by ELISA. APOE ε4 carriership was associated with higher p-tau181 (β=12.4 pg/mL, SE=3.1, p<0.001). The PICALM rs3851179 minor allele was nominally associated with lower t-tau (β=−8.7 pg/mL, SE=3.9, p=0.027), consistent with reports in Northern European cohorts, though this did not survive Bonferroni correction. BIN1 showed no significant association. These results argue for replication in larger regional samples and suggest that genetic architecture of biomarker variation is broadly conserved across European populations.

title: Multiplex CSF biomarker profiling using Luminex xMAP in a cohort of 300 Serbian dementia patients: assay performance and clinical concordance
abstract: Single-analyte ELISA has dominated CSF Alzheimer's diagnostics but multiplex platforms allow simultaneous quantification of multiple biomarkers from small sample volumes. We evaluated a six-plex Luminex xMAP panel measuring Aβ40, Aβ42, t-tau, p-tau181, p-tau231, and NfL in 300 CSF samples from the Vojvodina dementia registry. Technical performance included intra-assay CV <8% for all analytes and inter-assay CV <12%. Clinical concordance with single-plex ELISA was high for Aβ42 (ICC=0.93) and p-tau181 (ICC=0.89), but moderate for NfL (ICC=0.76). The Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio improved diagnostic accuracy for AD versus non-AD dementia compared with Aβ42 alone (AUC 0.91 vs 0.84). The platform reduced per-sample reagent cost by approximately 35% compared with running six individual ELISAs. These data support transitioning the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina's CSF laboratory to multiplex-based workflows for routine diagnostics.

title: Machine learning classification of Alzheimer's disease using combinations of CSF biomarkers: a pilot study in a Balkan cohort
abstract: We tested whether supervised machine learning algorithms could improve AD classification accuracy beyond individual CSF biomarkers. Using data from 210 participants (105 AD, 105 controls) from the Vojvodina cohort, we trained random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and logistic regression models on six CSF variables: Aβ42, Aβ40, t-tau, p-tau181, p-tau231, and the Aβ42/p-tau181 ratio. Models were evaluated by 5-fold cross-validation. RF achieved the highest AUC of 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.97), outperforming logistic regression (AUC 0.89) and SVM (AUC 0.91). Variable importance analysis identified p-tau231 and the Aβ42/p-tau181 ratio as the two most informative features. Calibration plots indicated moderate overconfidence for RF at high predicted probabilities. Given the small sample, external validation in independent regional cohorts is required before clinical application. Code and anonymised feature data are deposited in an open repository.

title: CSF p-tau217 measured by a research-grade immunoassay in a Serbian cohort: performance relative to p-tau181 and p-tau231
abstract: Phosphorylation of tau at threonine 217 (p-tau217) has shown high diagnostic accuracy in longitudinal cohorts from Northern Europe and North America, but data from Southern and Eastern Europe are limited. We measured p-tau217 using a research-grade ELISA (provided under material transfer agreement) alongside commercial p-tau181 and p-tau231 assays in 168 CSF samples from Vojvodina (60 AD, 52 MCI, 56 controls). P-tau217 discriminated AD from controls with AUC 0.95, outperforming p-tau181 (AUC 0.87) and p-tau231 (AUC 0.88) in this cohort. For MCI versus control discrimination, p-tau217 AUC was 0.83 compared with 0.76 for p-tau181. Correlation between p-tau217 and p-tau181 was r=0.88 (p<0.001). The Aβ42/p-tau217 ratio did not significantly improve over p-tau217 alone. These findings replicate the diagnostic superiority of p-tau217 in a Balkan population and support its integration into regional diagnostic algorithms.

title: Longitudinal stability of CSF tau biomarkers over 24 months in patients with stable mild cognitive impairment
abstract: The temporal dynamics of CSF tau biomarkers in non-progressing MCI are poorly characterised. We conducted a prospective 24-month follow-up of 88 patients with stable MCI (no progression to dementia by neuropsychological assessment) from Vojvodina, measuring CSF p-tau181, p-tau217, and t-tau at baseline, 12, and 24 months. Mixed-effects models showed no significant change in p-tau181 over time (β=0.31 pg/mL/year, 95% CI −0.4 to 1.0, p=0.38). P-tau217 showed a modest but statistically significant increase (β=0.54 pg/mL/year, 95% CI 0.12–0.96, p=0.012). APOE ε4 carriers showed faster p-tau217 increase than non-carriers (interaction p=0.03). Intraindividual coefficient of variation across the three time points was 9.2% for p-tau181 and 11.4% for p-tau217. These data suggest that p-tau217 may capture slow ongoing pathological change in stable MCI and has potential utility for monitoring in clinical trials.

title: Plasma p-tau217 as a non-invasive screening tool prior to lumbar puncture: validation in a South-Eastern European cohort
abstract: Blood-based biomarkers may triage patients toward or away from lumbar puncture, reducing procedural burden. We measured plasma p-tau217 by single-molecule array (Simoa) in 201 paired plasma and CSF samples from Vojvodina memory clinic patients (68 AD, 65 MCI, 68 controls). The correlation between plasma and CSF p-tau217 was r=0.79 (p<0.001). Plasma p-tau217 discriminated AD from controls with AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.85–0.95) and predicted abnormal CSF p-tau217 status (>60 pg/mL) with AUC 0.87. Setting a plasma cut-off of 0.18 pg/mL to rule out abnormal CSF yielded a negative predictive value of 91%. Kidney function (eGFR) was a significant confound; after adjustment, the predictive accuracy was stable. A two-threshold strategy (rule-out at 0.18 pg/mL, rule-in at 0.42 pg/mL) correctly classified 68% of patients without lumbar puncture, reserving puncture for the intermediate zone (32%). These findings support plasma p-tau217 as a first-line screening tool in regional clinical practice.

title: Dietary patterns and CSF Alzheimer's biomarker profiles in a Vojvodina elderly cohort: a cross-sectional exploratory analysis
abstract: The relationship between diet and CSF Alzheimer's biomarkers is rarely examined in populations with distinct dietary habits, such as the traditional Vojvodina diet characterised by high meat and lard consumption relative to Mediterranean norms. We assessed diet in 134 cognitively normal adults (aged 60–78) using a validated 110-item food frequency questionnaire and measured CSF Aβ42, p-tau181, and t-tau. A Mediterranean diet adherence score was calculated. After adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and APOE ε4, higher Mediterranean diet adherence was associated with higher CSF Aβ42 (β=3.1 pg/mL per score point, 95% CI 0.8–5.4, p=0.008) but not with p-tau181 or t-tau. The association was stronger in APOE ε4 non-carriers. Limitations include cross-sectional design, self-reported diet, and the relatively young-old age range. These exploratory results motivate longitudinal dietary intervention studies in this population.

title: Abrasive wear of boron-alloyed steel ploughshares in sandy-loam soils of Vojvodina: a field trial
abstract: This study quantified mass-loss wear rates of four commercially available boron-alloyed steel grades (28MnB5, 33MnCrB5, 39MnCrB6, and a low-cost unalloyed reference) used as ploughshare blades during spring tillage on a sandy-loam Chernozem near Rimski Šančevi. Six ploughs were instrumented with weigh-before/weigh-after protocols at 10-hectare intervals over a total working area of 120 ha per grade. Soil moisture content, bulk density, and particle-size distribution were recorded at three depths. Results showed that 33MnCrB5 exhibited the lowest cumulative mass loss (38 g per 100 ha), approximately 31% less than the unalloyed reference. Hardness profiling across worn cross-sections revealed a work-hardened surface layer of 0.3–0.5 mm in all boron grades. Wear surface morphology, examined by SEM, indicated predominantly micro-cutting with limited micro-ploughing. The findings suggest that boron content above 0.003 wt% provides diminishing returns in sandy-loam conditions at the moisture levels tested.

title: Influence of clay content on the wear mechanisms of ploughshare tool steels: a laboratory abrasion study
abstract: Controlled laboratory abrasion tests were performed using a custom-built linear-reciprocating tribometer in which compacted soil beds of varying clay content (5%, 15%, 25%, and 35% clay by mass) were prepared from a reference quartz sand base with added kaolinite. Specimens of three tool steel grades were slid against each soil bed at a constant normal load of 120 N and sliding speed of 0.08 m/s for 2000 cycles. Specific wear rates were determined gravimetrically and expressed in mm³/N·m. At 35% clay, wear rates for all grades dropped by 40–55% relative to the 5% clay baseline, suggesting a lubricating-film effect of fine clay particles. SEM and EDS analysis of worn surfaces confirmed a thin clay-mineral transfer film on specimens tested in high-clay beds. Surface roughness Ra increased monotonically with quartz content. The tribometer geometry and soil preparation protocol are described in sufficient detail to permit replication.

title: Thermal spray tungsten-carbide coatings on ploughshare blades: adhesion, microhardness, and preliminary field performance
abstract: High-velocity oxy-fuel (HVOF) sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr coatings were applied to flat coupons and to the leading-edge region of full-size ploughshare blades. Coating thickness was held at 250 ± 30 µm, confirmed by eddy-current measurement on 24 specimens. Rockwell superficial hardness (HR15N) and scratch-adhesion critical load were measured before field deployment. Twelve coated blades and twelve uncoated 400 HB reference blades were installed in matched pairs on six mouldboard ploughs operating on silty-clay-loam soil for 80 ha each. Coated blades showed 47% lower mean mass loss (21 g vs. 40 g per 80 ha). Post-trial SEM revealed that coating delamination at the cutting edge, observed in 4 of 12 coated blades, was the primary failure mode rather than bulk abrasion. Pull-off adhesion of delaminated regions was below 28 MPa compared to 48 MPa in intact zones. The result motivates further work on edge-geometry optimisation before HVOF coating deposition.

title: Comparative wear of plasma-nitrided and borided ploughshare coupons in three contrasting soil textures
abstract: Plasma nitriding (520 °C, 6 h) and pack boriding (900 °C, 4 h) were applied separately to flat coupons of 42CrMo4 steel. Surface layers were characterised by glow-discharge optical emission spectroscopy (GDOES), cross-section hardness, and XRD phase identification. Nitrided coupons showed a compound layer of ε-Fe₂₋₃N and γ′-Fe₄N to a depth of 18 µm; borided coupons showed an Fe₂B layer of 60–80 µm. Specimens were tested in the soil-bed tribometer under sandy, loamy, and clay-loam beds at identical load and speed. In sandy beds, borided coupons exhibited 28% lower specific wear rate than nitrided counterparts. In clay-loam beds, the difference was statistically insignificant (p > 0.12). Borided specimens showed brittle chipping at corners in all soil types, raising concern about edge integrity on real tool profiles. Results suggest that the appropriate surface treatment depends strongly on soil texture and tool geometry.

title: Wear of subsoiler tines in compacted Chernozem: comparison of four hardfacing weld deposits
abstract: Four flux-cored arc welding hardfacing alloys (two chromium-carbide grades, one complex carbide, one martensitic steel overlay) were deposited on the leading faces of subsoiler tine blanks by a certified welder following supplier procedures. Deposit microstructure and carbide volume fraction (CVF) were quantified by image analysis on etched metallographic sections: CVF ranged from 11% (martensitic) to 44% (Cr-carbide grade B). Tines were installed on a single-leg subsoiler and operated in compacted Chernozem at 45 cm depth across 60 ha of cumulative area in 10-ha intervals. Tine mass was recorded at each interval. The complex-carbide deposit showed the lowest total mass loss (54 g over 60 ha) and the most uniform wear profile. The martensitic overlay lost 118 g over the same area. Spalling of the high-CVF Cr-carbide deposits occurred between 20 and 30 ha, resulting in accelerating wear thereafter. Service life estimates and cost-per-hectare comparisons are provided for each deposit.

title: Laser cladding of TiC-reinforced steel matrix coatings on ploughshare blades: microstructure and first-season wear results
abstract: Laser cladding was used to deposit a TiC-reinforced (30 vol%) iron-based matrix coating onto the leading-edge bevel of standard mouldboard ploughshare blades using a 3 kW diode laser and a powder blend delivered by coaxial nozzle. Clad tracks were 4 mm wide, 1.2 mm high, and overlapped by 40%. Metallographic cross-sections showed a dilution zone of 0.15–0.22 mm and a crack-free coating with TiC particles of 2–8 µm distributed in a martensitic matrix. Vickers hardness in the clad zone averaged HV0.3 920, compared to HV0.3 450 in the substrate. Eight cladded blades and eight 400 HB reference blades were deployed on two farms in the Bačka region during autumn ploughing (loamy Chernozem, 80 ha each). Cladded blades lost on average 14 g per 80 ha, versus 43 g for the reference, a 67% reduction. No delamination or macrocracking was observed post-trial. Edge geometry retention was noticeably better in cladded blades on visual inspection.

title: Soil texture variability across Vojvodina and its implications for tillage tool wear: a regional dataset and preliminary wear-rate mapping
abstract: Soil texture data from 412 sampling sites across Vojvodina (sand, silt, clay fractions at 0–30 cm depth) were compiled from provincial land-registry surveys conducted between 2010 and 2022 and supplemented with 38 new samples taken by the authors. The dataset reveals strong spatial clustering: sandy soils dominate northern Bačka, silty-loam Chernozems cover most of central Vojvodina, and heavy clay Vertisols appear in distinct patches in Srem and southern Banat. Wear rates of 400 HB ploughshare steel, taken from published field trials and the authors' own data archive, were interpolated onto the texture map using a regression model with clay and sand percentage as predictors (R² = 0.61). The resulting preliminary wear-rate map suggests that a farmer in northern Bačka may expect two to three times higher ploughshare replacement frequency than a farmer on central Chernozem at the same tillage depth. The dataset and regression coefficients are provided as supplementary material.
