title: Wavelength-Division Multiplexed FBG Array for Distributed Strain Measurement on a Scaled Reinforced Concrete Beam
abstract: This paper describes the design and laboratory validation of a wavelength-division multiplexed fibre Bragg grating array intended for quasi-distributed strain measurement on structural concrete elements. Eight gratings with centre wavelengths spaced at 3 nm intervals across the 1530–1560 nm C-band window were inscribed using a phase-mask technique and embedded along the tensile face of a 1.2 m scaled reinforced concrete beam. A swept-laser interrogator operating at 1 kHz scan rate was used to track Bragg wavelength shifts during three-point bending tests carried out at incremental loads up to 12 kN. Measured strain distributions were compared against finite-element predictions generated in a commercial structural analysis package. Mean absolute error across all sensor positions remained below 6 µε at load steps up to 8 kN, increasing to 14 µε near the failure zone. Crosstalk between adjacent channels was assessed by selectively thermally perturbing individual gratings; inter-channel isolation exceeded 28 dB in all cases. The results confirm that the proposed multiplexing scheme provides adequate spatial resolution and measurement accuracy for service-load monitoring of short-span concrete beams, while the identified limitations at higher strain gradients suggest that tighter grating spacing warrants further investigation.

title: Comparison of Peak-Detection Algorithms for FBG Interrogation Under Low Signal-to-Noise Conditions
abstract: Reliable extraction of Bragg wavelength from noisy reflection spectra is a persistent challenge in low-cost and multiplexed FBG interrogation systems. This study benchmarks five peak-detection approaches—centroid computation, Gaussian curve fitting, polynomial fitting, threshold-based edge detection, and a Savitzky–Golay smoothed derivative method—under controlled signal-to-noise ratio conditions ranging from 5 dB to 30 dB. Artificial noise was added to spectra recorded from a single 1550 nm grating subjected to known step strains between 0 and 2000 µε. Each algorithm was evaluated on wavelength accuracy, computational time on an embedded ARM Cortex-M7 microcontroller, and robustness to spectral peak broadening caused by bending-induced birefringence. Gaussian fitting achieved the lowest RMS wavelength error of 0.8 pm at SNR above 20 dB but required 4.7 times the computation time of the centroid method. The Savitzky–Golay derivative approach offered a practical compromise, yielding RMS errors below 1.5 pm across all tested SNR levels with processing latency under 2 ms on the target hardware. Findings are discussed in the context of real-time multiplexed interrogation systems where processing budget is shared across many simultaneous sensor channels.

title: Group size and perceived anonymity as predictors of bystander inaction in moderated online discussion forums
abstract: This study examined how the number of visible co-witnesses and platform anonymity settings affect the likelihood of intervening when witnessing targeted insults in a controlled online forum. Participants (N = 187) were assigned to one of six conditions varying group size (3, 9, or 27 bystanders) and account visibility (named versus anonymous). A purpose-built forum interface delivered a scripted harassment exchange. Dependent measures included intervention frequency, latency, and self-reported inhibition. Larger groups reduced intervention rates significantly (F(2,181) = 14.3, p < .001), replicating a digital diffusion-of-responsibility effect. Anonymity interacted with group size only in mid-sized groups: anonymous accounts in 9-person conditions showed the lowest intervention rates overall. Post-session questionnaires indicated pluralistic ignorance as a partial mediator. Effect sizes were moderate (partial η² = .14). Findings suggest platform design choices about account visibility may meaningfully shift bystander dynamics in ways comparable to classic face-to-face paradigms.

title: Trait empathy and moral disengagement jointly predict passive bystanding in text-based cyberbullying episodes
abstract: This correlational study investigated whether individual differences in affective empathy, cognitive empathy, and moral disengagement predicted self-reported bystander passivity in recalled cyberbullying episodes. A community sample of young adults (N = 312, aged 18–29) completed the Interpersonal Reactivity Index, a moral disengagement scale adapted for online contexts, and a retrospective bystander behaviour inventory covering the previous six months. Structural equation modelling showed that moral disengagement fully mediated the negative association between affective empathy and passive bystanding (β = −.31, 95% CI [−.44, −.19]), whereas cognitive empathy showed only a direct effect. The model accounted for 27% of variance in passive bystanding. Age and gender were included as controls; women reported lower passivity scores. Results support a dual-pathway account in which emotional resonance with victims reduces passivity partly through suppressing rationalisations for non-intervention.

title: Bystander responses to gendered versus non-gendered online insults: evidence from a simulated microblogging environment
abstract: Two experiments examined whether observers respond differently to harassment that is overtly gendered (sexist slurs directed at women) compared with non-gendered insults of equivalent hostility. In Experiment 1 (N = 204, undergraduate sample), participants witnessed a harassment exchange on a custom microblogging interface and could respond by liking, replying supportively, reporting, or doing nothing. Gendered harassment elicited higher reporting rates (47% vs. 31%) but not higher direct reply rates. Experiment 2 (N = 198) added a condition making the victim's distress more salient through visible reaction indicators. Distress salience increased direct replies for gendered (Δ = 19 pp) but not non-gendered harassment. Moderation by participant gender was non-significant after Bonferroni correction. The findings indicate that intervention form—passive reporting versus active addressing—varies systematically with harassment type and victim cue visibility, and that intervention form should be treated as a multidimensional outcome.

title: Social cost perception as a situational barrier to intervention: a scenario study across three Balkan university samples
abstract: This multi-site scenario study assessed whether perceived social cost of intervening—fear of retaliation, ridicule, or reputational loss—predicts non-intervention independent of empathy and moral attitudes. Participants at universities in Novi Sad, Zagreb, and Skopje (total N = 547) read standardised vignettes describing online harassment incidents varying in perpetrator group size (lone vs. gang) and audience visibility (private vs. public thread). After each vignette, participants rated likelihood of intervening and completed a social cost measure developed for the study. Multi-level modelling confirmed that social cost perception was the strongest proximal predictor of non-intervention (β = −.42) across all three sites, with only minor site-level variation. Perpetrator gang condition increased social cost ratings substantially. Empathy predicted intervention intention only after accounting for social cost. Cross-cultural consistency in effect direction suggests social cost mechanisms may be relatively robust across regional contexts.

title: Bystander intervention in online spaces: situational and dispositional predictors
abstract: This book chapter reviews empirical literature on bystander intervention in online harassment contexts, with emphasis on identifying which predictors have been tested experimentally versus correlational-only and where evidence is contradictory. The chapter organises findings around four classes of variables: victim characteristics (identity, expressed distress), perpetrator characteristics (size, perceived status), situational affordances (anonymity, audience size, platform reporting features), and bystander dispositions (empathy, moral disengagement, social dominance orientation). For each class the chapter summarises effect sizes from available quantitative syntheses and identifies gaps, particularly the scarcity of longitudinal data and the over-reliance on Western European and North American samples. An integrated conceptual model is proposed that treats intervention as a sequential decision process with distinct barriers at each stage. The chapter concludes with practical implications for platform design and bystander-training programme evaluation.

title: Real-time chat versus asynchronous thread: intervention timing and form differ across platform formats in a controlled experiment
abstract: This within-subjects experiment (N = 163) exposed participants to identical harassment content in two formats: a synchronous real-time chat and an asynchronous threaded reply interface. Order was counterbalanced. In the synchronous condition, mean time to first intervention response was 42 seconds compared with 109 seconds in the asynchronous condition, though ultimate intervention rates did not differ significantly (44% vs. 40%). Active responses (direct replies to perpetrator) were more frequent in real-time chat; passive responses (reporting, liking victim's reply) predominated in threaded format. Exit interviews suggested that perceived urgency drove faster responses in chat and that threading increased evaluation of whether others had already responded. Results indicate that platform interaction format shapes the temporal structure and qualitative form of bystander behaviour even when content is held constant, with implications for how intervention outcomes are measured across studies.

title: Does framing harassment as 'hate speech' versus 'cyberbullying' affect bystander responsibility attribution and intervention intention?
abstract: Online harassment is labelled inconsistently across policy documents, media reports, and user interfaces. This experiment tested whether framing the same aggressive exchange as 'hate speech' versus 'cyberbullying' changes bystanders' sense of personal responsibility to intervene and their stated intentions. Participants (N = 241) read a scenario with the label manipulated between subjects; content was otherwise identical. Participants who read 'hate speech' framing attributed more responsibility to platform moderators and less to themselves (Δ = 0.61 on a 7-point scale, t(239) = 3.84, p < .001), and reported lower personal intervention intention (d = 0.38). Perceived severity did not differ between conditions. Mediation analysis indicated that the effect on intervention intention operated through responsibility attribution rather than severity judgements. Findings suggest label choice in educational campaigns and interface design may inadvertently suppress individual bystander motivation.

title: Passive bystander normalisation: repeated exposure to unaddressed harassment reduces future intervention rates in a longitudinal simulation study
abstract: Concern has grown that frequent exposure to unaddressed online harassment may normalise it and lower bystander motivation. This longitudinal experiment tracked participants (N = 148) across five simulation sessions over six weeks. In a normalisation condition, participants observed harassment going consistently unaddressed by others; in a control condition, at least one other actor always intervened. Intervention rates declined across sessions in the normalisation condition from 51% at session one to 29% at session five (linear trend: b = −5.2 pp per session, 95% CI [−7.1, −3.3]), whereas control-condition rates remained stable. Perceived injunctive norms about non-intervention strengthened across sessions in the normalisation condition only (d = 0.61 at follow-up). Trait moral disengagement moderated the rate of decline. The study provides experimental evidence for a gradual normalisation process and highlights norm perception as a target for counter-intervention design.

title: Mapping Heterogeneous Plant Phenotype Databases to a Common OWL Ontology: A Case Study with Three Balkan Agricultural Repositories
abstract: Agricultural research institutions in Southeast Europe maintain phenotype databases that use incompatible schemas, making cross-institutional queries impractical. This paper describes the construction of a shared OWL 2 DL ontology covering 214 plant traits drawn from three institutional databases in Serbia, Romania, and Bulgaria, collectively holding records for approximately 18 000 accessions. We applied a semi-automatic schema mapping procedure based on lexical similarity and structural heuristics, followed by manual curation of 31 ambiguous mappings. The resulting ontology was evaluated against a gold-standard alignment produced independently by two domain experts; F1 for automatic mappings reached 0.81 before curation. We deployed a federated SPARQL 1.1 endpoint and ran 12 benchmark queries comparing response times and completeness against direct SQL access. Federated queries retrieved on average 97.3% of expected results with a mean overhead of 340 ms. The ontology and mapping files are published under CC-BY on an institutional GitLab instance.

title: A Lightweight Vocabulary for Describing Provenance in Life-Science Linked Datasets
abstract: Provenance metadata in linked life-science datasets is inconsistently recorded, which limits reproducibility and audit trails. This work proposes PROVLife, a lightweight RDFS vocabulary that extends W3C PROV-O with 18 additional classes and 27 properties targeting experimental protocols, instrument calibration records, and sample chain-of-custody information. We evaluated PROVLife by retrospectively annotating 6 400 RDF triples from an existing plant genomics dataset and a clinical trial registry mirror. Annotation completeness rose from 34% to 89% against a defined provenance checklist. We also report on a user study with 14 data curators at two research institutes who rated PROVLife's expressiveness and learnability on a five-point Likert scale; mean scores were 4.1 and 3.9 respectively. The vocabulary is published as a resolvable namespace with full HTML documentation generated by Widoco.

title: Ontology Alignment Across Clinical Trial Registries: Evaluation of Four Automated Matchers on a Manually Curated Benchmark
abstract: Clinical trial registries published by different national health agencies use partially overlapping controlled vocabularies, complicating systematic reviews and meta-analyses. We assembled a benchmark consisting of 1 120 concept pairs drawn from four European registry schemas and asked three biomedical informaticians to independently classify each pair as equivalent, related, or disjoint, achieving a Fleiss' kappa of 0.74. We then evaluated four existing automated ontology alignment systems—AgreementMakerLight, LogMap, PARIS, and a local transformer-based matcher fine-tuned on MeSH synonyms—on this benchmark. AgreementMakerLight achieved the highest precision (0.88) while the transformer-based matcher achieved the highest recall (0.84). We analysed systematic error patterns and identified 67 pairs where all four systems disagreed with human judges, attributing most disagreements to ambiguous scope notes rather than lexical overlap failures. The benchmark dataset is made freely available for future comparisons.

title: Federated Knowledge Graph Construction from Distributed Environmental Monitoring Stations in the Pannonian Basin
abstract: Fourteen environmental monitoring stations operated by four institutions across Serbia and Hungary collect soil, water, and air quality measurements using different sensor models and data formats. This chapter describes the architecture of a federated knowledge graph built over these sources, covering approximately 2.3 million observations recorded between 2015 and 2020. We used R2RML mappings to virtualise relational sources as RDF, supplemented by a custom Python connector for CSV streams from legacy loggers. The core domain ontology reuses SSN/SOSA for sensor descriptions and extends it with 11 domain-specific classes for Pannonian ecological zones. We discuss challenges encountered when reconciling temporal granularities ranging from 10-minute intervals to monthly aggregates and describe a resampling strategy that preserves provenance. A persistent SPARQL endpoint serves the graph, and we report query performance across five representative analytical queries. The chapter concludes with lessons learned relevant to cross-border environmental data governance.

title: Automated Extraction of Gene–Disease Associations from Serbian-Language Clinical Reports Using NLP and RDF
abstract: Most named-entity recognition pipelines for biomedical knowledge graph population are designed for English text, with limited coverage of low-resource South Slavic languages. We built a pipeline that processes Serbian-language clinical case reports to extract gene–disease associations and represent them as RDF triples linked to Orphanet and OMIM identifiers. The training corpus comprised 380 manually annotated reports obtained from three clinical centres in Vojvodina, containing 2 840 annotated entity mentions. We fine-tuned a multilingual BERT model for NER, achieving an F1 of 0.77 on a held-out test set of 60 reports. The extraction pipeline produced 1 134 distinct gene–disease triples, of which 68% could be aligned to existing entries in Orphanet via exact or approximate string matching. We assessed alignment quality by manual review of a random sample of 100 triples, finding 82% correct. The resulting graph and annotated corpus are deposited in the faculty's institutional repository.

title: Evaluation of SPARQL Query Rewriting Strategies for Ontology-Mediated Access to Fragmented Biobanks
abstract: Biobanks that store biological samples across multiple physical sites often expose different database schemas even within the same institution, making unified data access difficult. This paper examines four SPARQL query rewriting strategies—GAV, LAV, GLAV, and a rule-based approach implemented in Apache Jena—applied to an ontology-mediated access layer over three biobank schemas containing records for 9 200 donors. We designed 20 representative competency queries covering donor demographics, sample metadata, and linked clinical measurements, and measured precision, recall, and execution time for each strategy and query combination. The rule-based Jena approach achieved the best balance, with a mean precision of 0.91 and recall of 0.88 at a median query execution time of 780 ms. We identify three query patterns where GAV rewrites produce spurious results due to closed-world assumptions in the source schemas. Recommendations for practitioners setting up similar access layers are provided.

title: Incremental Knowledge Graph Updating for Continuously Ingested Clinical Laboratory Results: A Pilot Implementation
abstract: Clinical laboratories generate results continuously, yet most knowledge graph pipelines are designed for batch ingestion, leading to graphs that lag real-time data by hours or days. This preprint describes a pilot implementation of an incremental update architecture for a hospital laboratory knowledge graph covering 14 analyte types and approximately 2 000 new results per day at a regional hospital in Vojvodina. We use an event-driven pipeline built on Apache Kafka, with an R2RML streaming extension that converts incoming JSON messages to RDF and merges them into the live graph using SPARQL Update operations. We evaluate consistency maintenance under concurrent writes and report that duplicate triple rates remained below 0.3% over a 90-day observation period. Latency from result generation to graph availability averaged 4.1 seconds. We also discuss mapping maintenance costs when source schemas change, which occurred three times during the pilot. The implementation is described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Mitochondrial lineage diversity in Pannonian stoneflies (Plecoptera: Nemouridae): evidence for multiple Pleistocene refugia
abstract: We sampled 312 individuals of Nemoura cinerea from 24 sites across the Pannonian Basin, the Dinaric foothills, and the Carpathian fringe. Sequencing of the COI and 16S rRNA genes revealed eight divergent mitochondrial haplotype groups, with pairwise distances of 2.1–6.8%. Bayesian phylogenetic analysis placed the root in the southern Carpathian–Dinaric contact zone, while two secondary clades radiated northward into the Hungarian plain following estimated glacial retreat ca. 12,000–15,000 years BP. Population differentiation (FST = 0.61) was highest between the Tisza and Sava catchments. These data are inconsistent with a single northern refugium model and instead support at least three distinct source populations that contributed to present-day genetic structure. The study provides a framework for interpreting macroinvertebrate diversity in large lowland rivers of the Pannonian region.

title: Microsatellite markers for population-level studies in Gammarus fossarum (Amphipoda) across Danubian tributaries
abstract: We developed and characterised 11 polymorphic microsatellite loci for Gammarus fossarum using an enriched genomic library approach. Loci were screened in 96 individuals from four populations spanning the Tisa, Begej, and Morava rivers. Number of alleles per locus ranged from 4 to 17. Observed heterozygosity (0.38–0.82) was broadly consistent with Hardy–Weinberg expectations after Bonferroni correction, with two loci showing significant heterozygote deficiency attributable to possible null alleles. Cross-amplification success in G. balcanicus was 73%. All 11 loci were polymorphic in at least three of the four target populations. These markers are suitable for fine-scale parentage, dispersal, and connectivity analyses in amphipod metapopulations of Pannonian lowland systems.

title: Post-glacial colonisation of the Tisza floodplain by aquatic Diptera (Chironomidae): a multi-locus perspective
abstract: We examined genetic structure in three chironomid species (Chironomus plumosus, Ch. riparius, and Procladius choreus) collected at 18 sites along the Tisza River and its backwaters in Serbia and Hungary. For each species, we sequenced COI, COII, and the ITS2 nuclear region (n = 348 individuals total). Median-joining haplotype networks showed star-shaped topologies in Ch. plumosus, consistent with rapid Holocene population expansion (Tajima's D = −1.81, p < 0.05), whereas Ch. riparius displayed more structured genealogies with two haplogroups separated by five mutational steps. Site-level diversity correlated positively with distance from the main channel (r = 0.62, p = 0.01), suggesting floodplain backwaters act as genetic reservoirs. Results are compared with previously published paleohydrological reconstructions for the Middle Tisza valley.

title: Isolation by distance versus isolation by environment in Gammarus balcanicus metapopulations of karst springs feeding the Pannonian fringe
abstract: We genotyped 486 individuals of G. balcanicus at 11 microsatellite loci from 20 karst spring sites at the interface of the Dinaric highlands and the Pannonian Plain. Partial Mantel tests distinguished the relative contributions of geographic distance and local environmental variables (conductivity, temperature, canopy cover, flow velocity) to genetic differentiation. After removing the effect of geographic distance, environmental dissimilarity explained an additional 14% of FST variance (p = 0.002). Genetic cluster analysis (STRUCTURE, K = 4) broadly corresponded to four drainage basins rather than strict geography. Gene flow estimates (Nm) were substantially lower between spring systems in different basins (Nm = 0.8) than within basins (Nm = 4.3). These findings suggest that drainage divides act as more effective barriers to dispersal than simple Euclidean distance would predict.

title: Whole-mitochondrial genome phylogeny of Baetis rhodani (Ephemeroptera) reveals cryptic lineages across the Carpathian–Pannonian transition
abstract: We assembled 42 complete mitochondrial genomes from Baetis rhodani specimens collected across a transect from the Tatra Mountains to the Pannonian lowlands, using Illumina MiSeq sequencing of long-range PCR amplicons. Maximum likelihood and Bayesian trees placed specimens into four well-supported clades corresponding to alpine, Carpathian, Dinaric, and lowland–floodplain geographic groupings. Mean inter-clade divergence across all 13 protein-coding genes was 3.9–7.6%, comparable to species-level divergence in other baetid genera. Bayesian divergence time estimates (using a relaxed clock calibrated against the baetid fossil record) placed clade splits between 1.1 and 2.8 million years ago, predating the last glacial maximum. Morphological examination of 120 specimens found no characters that reliably distinguished the genetic clades. We discuss implications for bioassessment, where B. rhodani is routinely used as a water quality indicator.

title: Environmental DNA metabarcoding detects amphipod species unrecorded in net-based surveys of Vojvodina canal network
abstract: We applied eDNA metabarcoding (COI gene, 313 bp amplicon; primers BF2/BR2) to 38 water samples collected from the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal system in Vojvodina during spring and autumn 2018. Bioinformatic processing against a curated amphipod reference database identified 11 amphipod OTUs, of which three (Dikerogammarus villosus, Echinogammarus trichiatus, and an undescribed Gammarus sp. matching a lineage known from Romanian records) were not detected in concurrent kick-net sampling. Total amphipod read abundance was higher in downstream canal reaches (median 6,820 reads per sample) than upstream agricultural sections (median 1,104 reads). Occupancy modelling estimated detection probability for rare species at 0.61 per sample. These results indicate the canal network functions as a dispersal corridor for invasive and range-expanding amphipod taxa.

title: Comparative phylogeography of four co-distributed stonefly species across the Pannonian floodplain: concordant and discordant breaks
abstract: We compiled and newly generated COI sequence datasets for Nemoura cinerea, Leuctra hippopus, Isoperla grammatica, and Amphinemura sulcicollis across 31 shared sampling sites in the Pannonian Basin (total n = 617 sequences). Geographic concordance among species in haplotype boundaries was assessed using CAOS and spatial principal components analysis (sPCA). A clear genetic break on the Danube at the Iron Gate gorge was concordant across all four species and separated Dinaric from Carpathian lineages. A secondary break in the Middle Tisza zone was concordant in three of four species; L. hippopus showed no corresponding differentiation, possibly reflecting its greater aerial dispersal capacity. Null model permutation tests confirmed that the level of multi-species concordance at the Iron Gate break was significantly greater than expected by chance (p = 0.003). This break coincides with a documented Pleistocene drainage reorganisation event.

title: Population structure of Dikerogammarus villosus in the Serbian stretch of the Danube seven years after first detection
abstract: Dikerogammarus villosus was first recorded in Serbia in 2015. We sampled 320 individuals at 12 sites between Bezdan and the Đerdap reservoir in 2021 and 2022, genotyping them at 10 microsatellite loci. Genetic diversity was moderate (mean AR = 4.8; mean HO = 0.54), consistent with values from established western European populations rather than recently invaded eastern range edges. Assignment tests grouped Serbian samples into two genetic clusters aligned with upstream Danube and downstream–Sava confluence source populations. Low FST values (mean 0.04) and high proportions of migrants (42% of individuals) indicated rapid mixing along the Serbian stretch. These data suggest Serbia was colonised from at least two independent upstream source populations and that within-country gene flow is currently unrestricted.

title: Sequencing of historical museum specimens of Pannonian mayflies: lessons for reference database construction
abstract: We extracted and sequenced DNA from 78 pinned and ethanol-preserved Baetidae specimens collected between 1937 and 1982 from four natural history collections in Belgrade, Budapest, Vienna, and Brno. Success rates for COI amplification depended strongly on preservation age and storage medium: ethanol-preserved specimens younger than 40 years yielded usable sequences at 81% success; pinned specimens older than 60 years succeeded at only 23%. After quality filtering, 51 sequences were incorporated into a regional reference database. In 14 cases, historical specimens represented populations from sites now degraded or drained, extending the documented range of three taxa by more than 150 km relative to living-specimen records. We provide a standardised workflow and report average index of damage (AID) scores for each collection to assist future sampling decisions.

title: Patterns of residential vacancy in small border towns of Vojvodina: a GIS-based land-use survey
abstract: This paper presents findings from a systematic land-use field survey and aerial imagery analysis conducted in eleven small towns (population 2,000–12,000) situated within 30 kilometres of the Serbian-Hungarian border. Residential parcels were classified into four vacancy categories—fully vacant, partially vacant, functionally vacant, and occupied—using a combination of 2011 census parcel data, municipal cadastral records, and high-resolution orthophotography. In total, 47,840 parcels were examined. Overall vacancy rates ranged from 8.4% in the most populous settlements to 23.1% in the smallest. Spatial autocorrelation analysis (Moran's I) confirmed significant clustering of vacant parcels in historic town cores and along peripheral agricultural margins. The study establishes a replicable mapping protocol suitable for municipalities with limited technical capacity and proposes a four-tier vacancy severity index for use in local planning documents. Results are compared with equivalent surveys from Hungarian border counties to contextualise cross-border shrinkage dynamics.

title: Demographic indicators of urban shrinkage: constructing a composite index for small Vojvodinian settlements
abstract: The paper proposes and tests a composite demographic shrinkage index (DSI) drawing on five indicators derived from the 2002 and 2011 Serbian census: total population change, natural growth rate, net migration balance, age dependency ratio, and share of the population aged 65 and above. The index was computed for 89 settlements in the Vojvodina region with populations below 20,000. Settlements were grouped into four shrinkage classes using k-means clustering. Forty-one settlements fell into the two most severe shrinkage classes, concentrated in the northern and north-eastern sub-regions close to the Hungarian and Romanian borders. The paper discusses the limitations of relying solely on decennial census data and proposes a supplementary annual monitoring procedure based on municipal birth, death, and migration registers. Policy implications for spatial planning at the provincial level are outlined, with reference to the Vojvodina Regional Spatial Plan 2020.

title: Planning responses to population decline in Serbian small towns: a review of local spatial plans 2005–2015
abstract: This study examines the extent to which local spatial plans (LSPs) adopted by 24 small Serbian municipalities between 2005 and 2015 acknowledge and address population decline and land-use vacancy. Each plan was coded against a 38-item analytical framework covering demographic projections, vacancy management provisions, infrastructure downsizing measures, and inter-municipal coordination mechanisms. Fewer than one-third of the reviewed plans contained explicit demographic decline scenarios; none included provisions for systematic demolition or land banking of vacant residential properties. Growth-oriented zoning remained the dominant planning mode despite documented population losses in 19 of the 24 municipalities. The paper argues that Serbian planning legislation and planning practice culture create structural incentives for over-optimistic projections. Recommendations are made for amendments to the Law on Planning and Construction to require shrinkage-adjusted demographic forecasting in local plans.

title: Cross-border shrinkage dynamics along the Tisza corridor: a comparative analysis of Hungarian and Serbian riverside settlements
abstract: Eight pairs of functionally related settlements on opposite banks of the Tisza river—four in Hungary, four in Serbia—were compared using parallel datasets from national censuses, land-use registries, and municipal administrative records covering the period 1991–2016. The analysis focuses on whether EU accession differentials between the two countries are reflected in diverging shrinkage trajectories after 2004. Population loss rates in the Serbian settlements averaged 18.3% over the study period, compared with 12.7% on the Hungarian side. Commercial vacancy and agricultural land abandonment were substantially higher in Serbian settlements. Qualitative interviews with eight municipal planners supplement the quantitative findings. The paper concludes that the border effect amplifies shrinkage on the Serbian side through restricted labour mobility, infrastructure investment gaps, and lower agricultural subsidy levels, and calls for coordinated cross-border planning instruments under future IPA programmes.

title: Measuring functional vacancy: combining remote sensing classification and municipal utility disconnect records
abstract: Standard land-use surveys categorise parcels as vacant based on visual observation or ownership records, but properties that are legally occupied may be functionally unused for extended periods. This paper develops and tests a method for identifying functional vacancy by cross-referencing utility (electricity and water) disconnect and non-consumption records held by municipal service providers with building footprint data extracted from Sentinel-2 and Pleiades satellite imagery. The method was piloted in three Vojvodinian towns with populations between 3,500 and 8,000. Buildings classified as structurally present but showing zero utility consumption for 24 consecutive months were designated functionally vacant. These accounted for between 5.1% and 9.7% of all building footprints, approximately doubling the vacancy rates recorded by conventional cadastral surveys. Spatial analysis shows functional vacancy concentrations in inner-core historic fabric and post-1980 socialist housing estates. Accuracy assessment against field verification gave an overall classification accuracy of 88.4%.

title: Land banking as a planning tool for shrinking towns: lessons from Central European practice for the Serbian context
abstract: Land banking—the systematic public acquisition and management of vacant or abandoned parcels pending future redevelopment or green-space conversion—has been applied in shrinking cities in Germany, the Czech Republic, and Hungary since the early 2000s. This book chapter reviews twelve documented land banking schemes in those three countries, extracting design parameters including legal basis, financing mechanisms, parcel selection criteria, and exit strategies. The review is then used to assess the feasibility of introducing comparable mechanisms under Serbian planning and property law. Key legal obstacles identified include the absence of a dedicated municipal land fund instrument, restrictions on below-market municipal acquisitions, and fragmented cadastral records. The chapter proposes a model amendment package for Serbian legislation and a pilot scheme framework suitable for Vojvodinian municipalities with fewer than 10,000 inhabitants.

title: Housing stock obsolescence and vacancy in ethnically mixed settlements of northern Vojvodina: a parcel-level typological survey
abstract: Northern Vojvodina contains a significant number of settlements with historically mixed Serbian, Hungarian, and Rusyn populations, many of which have experienced accelerated emigration since the 1990s. This paper reports results of a parcel-level field survey conducted in seven such settlements in Bačka and Banat sub-regions during 2019. Each residential parcel was classified by housing type, construction decade, structural condition, and occupancy status. Of 11,240 surveyed parcels, 2,870 (25.5%) contained at least one vacant dwelling. Agricultural outbuildings constituted 38% of vacant footprint area, pointing to the legacy of dispersed farmstead settlement patterns. Cross-tabulation with population register data shows that Hungarian-majority settlements had vacancy rates 6–9 percentage points higher than Serbian-majority settlements of comparable size, a difference the paper links to higher out-migration rates to Hungary following Hungary's EU accession.

title: Pilot evaluation of a shrinkage-responsive zoning instrument in three Serbian municipalities: process, outcomes, and barriers
abstract: Between 2021 and 2023 the author collaborated with planners in three Vojvodinian municipalities to pilot a shrinkage-responsive zoning instrument that replaces conventional growth-oriented residential zones with three adaptive zone types: managed consolidation zones, temporary agricultural holding zones, and demolition-eligible zones. This paper documents the planning process, stakeholder responses, and the extent to which the instrument was ultimately incorporated into formal plan amendments. In one municipality the full instrument was adopted; in a second, a modified version was accepted; in the third, resistance from landowners and local councillors resulted in abandonment. Qualitative data from 26 stakeholder interviews and meeting records are analysed alongside the spatial outcomes measured by parcel reclassification counts. The paper identifies the conditions under which shrinkage-responsive zoning is politically feasible under current Serbian planning legislation and practice norms.

title: Temperature-Dependent 1/f Noise Characterisation of a CMOS Integrated Hall Plate from −40 °C to 120 °C
abstract: This paper presents a systematic experimental characterisation of low-frequency noise in a cross-shaped Hall plate fabricated in a standard 0.18 µm CMOS process. Noise spectral density measurements were performed at 23 bias conditions between 10 Hz and 100 kHz using a low-noise transimpedance amplifier chain and an FFT analyser, while a temperature-controlled probe station maintained device temperature from −40 °C to 120 °C in 20 °C steps. The Hooge noise parameter αH was extracted at each temperature point using a least-squares fit to the 1/f slope. Results show that αH increases by approximately 2.4× across the full temperature range, with the steepest rise occurring between 60 °C and 100 °C. An empirical model relating αH to lattice temperature via a power-law expression is proposed and validated against a separate set of 12 test dies. The extracted model parameters are compared with values reported for bulk CMOS Hall plates in the literature. Residuals from the fit remain below 8% across all conditions. The findings provide a quantitative basis for noise budget allocation in precision magnetic measurement front-ends intended for automotive and industrial environments.

title: Residual Offset After Spinning-Current Cancellation in Hall Sensors Under Thermal Gradient Conditions
abstract: The spinning-current technique is widely used to suppress offset in Hall sensors, but residual offset after switching remains poorly understood when a temperature gradient exists across the device. This work investigates residual offset in a 0.35 µm CMOS four-contact Hall plate under deliberately imposed in-plane thermal gradients of up to 15 K/mm, achieved by driving a separate polysilicon heater integrated on the same die. Four-phase spinning-current commutation was implemented in an FPGA-based readout board. Residual offset was recorded for 48 gradient directions and magnitudes at room temperature and at 85 °C. Measurements show that residual offset scales linearly with the gradient magnitude, with a proportionality constant of 31 nT/(K/mm) at room temperature, rising to 47 nT/(K/mm) at 85 °C. A geometric mismatch model is developed to attribute this behaviour to asymmetric mobility modulation across the active area. Reducing the sensor footprint from 40 µm × 40 µm to 20 µm × 20 µm decreases the gradient-induced residual by a factor of 2.8, consistent with the model prediction. Results have direct implications for sensor placement in power electronics modules where thermal gradients are unavoidable.

title: Comparison of SPICE Noise Models for p-Well and n-Well CMOS Hall Plates at Varying Substrate Bias
abstract: Accurate SPICE-level noise models for Hall plates are needed to support mixed-signal front-end simulation before fabrication. This work benchmarks four flicker noise model formulations — BSIM4 unified flicker, empirical Hooge, van der Ziel bulk trapping, and a modified surface-state model — against measured noise data from p-well and n-well Hall plates in a 0.18 µm twin-well CMOS process. Measurements covered substrate bias values of 0 V, −1 V, and −2 V at temperatures of 27 °C, 50 °C, and 85 °C, yielding 18 operating points per device type. The van der Ziel bulk trapping model achieved the lowest mean absolute error (6.1%) for the n-well devices across all bias and temperature conditions, while the BSIM4 formulation performed best for the p-well variant (7.4% error). The empirical Hooge model showed the largest deviation at elevated substrate bias, exceeding 20% error in three cases. Extracted model parameters for each formulation are tabulated and their sensitivity to process corner variation is discussed. The recommended model choices are compatible with standard Cadence Spectre simulation flows, and the parameter extraction procedure is described in sufficient detail to be replicated with commercially available parameter analysers.
venue: Microelectronics and Reliability – European Symposium Proceedings (MRESP)

title: Effect of Chopper Stabilisation Clock Frequency on 1/f Noise Upconversion in a CMOS Hall Sensor Readout Chain
abstract: Chopper stabilisation shifts low-frequency noise away from the signal band but can reintroduce folded high-frequency noise and clock-synchronous artefacts if the chopping frequency is poorly chosen. This study examines how the chopping frequency fch, varied from 1 kHz to 200 kHz, affects the output noise floor and residual ripple in a readout chain consisting of a CMOS Hall plate, a three-stage instrumentation amplifier with embedded chopper switches, and a sinc3 decimation filter, all implemented in a 0.35 µm CMOS technology. A test chip was fabricated and characterised at temperatures of 25 °C and 100 °C. Noise spectra were recorded at 12 chopping frequencies per temperature. Results show a clear noise floor minimum at fch = 40 kHz at 25 °C, corresponding to a measured equivalent magnetic noise density of 8.3 nT/√Hz in the 10–100 Hz band. At 100 °C the optimum shifts to 55 kHz, and the minimum noise density rises to 12.1 nT/√Hz, consistent with the increased 1/f corner frequency observed at elevated temperature. The dependence of residual ripple amplitude on fch relative to the amplifier bandwidth is also quantified. Practical guidelines for selecting fch as a function of operating temperature range are derived from the experimental data.

title: Low-Frequency Noise Reduction in Integrated Hall Sensors: Techniques and Temperature Constraints
abstract: This book chapter reviews the principal circuit and device-level strategies for reducing low-frequency noise in CMOS-integrated Hall magnetic field sensors, with emphasis on the constraints imposed by temperature variation in practical operating environments. The chapter begins with a concise derivation of the relevant noise mechanisms — thermal Johnson noise, generation-recombination noise, and 1/f flicker noise — as they appear in Hall plate structures under bias. Subsequent sections describe offset-reduction techniques including spinning current, chopper stabilisation, auto-zeroing, and their combinations, discussing the residual noise contributions and practical implementation trade-offs at each. A dedicated section addresses how the 1/f noise corner frequency and the Hooge parameter shift with temperature in standard CMOS n-well and p-well Hall geometries, drawing on published data and the authors' own measurements. The chapter also covers trimming and calibration approaches for temperature-induced offset drift. Design examples illustrate noise budgeting for a target equivalent magnetic noise density of 10 nT/√Hz across the automotive temperature range. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and practising engineers entering the field of integrated magnetic sensing.

title: Shipper Attitudes Toward Inland Waterway Transport on the Danube: Results from a Stated Preference Survey in Serbia
abstract: This paper reports on a stated preference survey conducted with 214 shippers located within 50 km of the Serbian Danube reach. Respondents were presented with binary choice tasks contrasting road transport and river barge options described by transit time, price per tonne-kilometre, reliability expressed as on-time delivery probability, and port access distance. A conditional logit model and a mixed logit model with normally distributed coefficients for transit time and reliability were estimated. The mixed logit fit improved significantly over the conditional logit (rho-squared 0.31 vs. 0.22). The implied value of reliability—measured as willingness to pay per percentage point increase in on-time delivery—was approximately 0.18 EUR per tonne for bulk commodity shippers, rising to 0.41 EUR per tonne for general cargo shippers. Price sensitivity was higher among shippers with annual freight volumes below 50,000 tonnes. The findings suggest that moderate improvements in schedule reliability could substantially increase inland waterway modal share among mid-volume shippers.

title: Measuring the Effect of Low-Water Events on Shipper Mode Choice: A Before–After Survey Approach
abstract: Extreme low-water periods on the Danube have become more frequent since the early 2000s, intermittently restricting navigation and forcing shippers to use road haulage as an unplanned substitute. This study exploits a severe low-water event in summer 2022 to administer matched before and after surveys to 97 shippers who had previously participated in a 2021 stated preference study. The analysis compares self-reported actual mode use during the restriction period with choices predicted by the earlier models, and asks whether the forced experience of road haulage altered subsequent inland waterway willingness-to-pay estimates. Post-event stated preference tasks were administered six months after navigation resumed. Mixed logit re-estimation showed a statistically significant decrease in the inland waterway time coefficient among shippers who experienced delays exceeding 14 days, suggesting that prolonged disruption reduces perceived reliability of waterway options even after service restoration. The reliability coefficient showed no significant change, implying that disruption mainly affects time perception rather than overall reliability valuation.

title: Design of Stated Preference Experiments for Freight Mode Choice: Attribute Range Effects and Survey Fatigue in Shipper Samples
abstract: The quality of discrete choice experiment data in freight contexts depends heavily on experimental design choices, yet methodological guidance aimed specifically at shipper respondents is limited. This study reports results from a split-sample pilot conducted with 120 Serbian freight decision-makers. Three design variants were tested: a D-efficient fractional factorial design with 12 choice tasks, an adaptive design with 8 tasks, and a blocked design with 6 tasks per respondent. Error variance proxies, item non-response rates, and protest responses were compared across groups. The 12-task design produced significantly higher rates of lexicographic response patterns (19 percent) compared with the 8-task adaptive design (9 percent), suggesting fatigue effects. Attribute range widths were manipulated between subjects; wider price ranges inflated price coefficients by up to 23 percent relative to narrower ranges used in prior regional studies. Practical recommendations include limiting tasks to eight or fewer per shipper respondent and pre-testing attribute ranges against observed market tariffs.

title: Estimating Value of Transit Time for Road versus Barge in Serbian Bulk Freight: Pilot Survey Results
abstract: This conference paper reports preliminary results from a pilot discrete choice experiment administered to 48 shippers operating bulk agricultural and construction material flows in Vojvodina. The experiment used a simple orthogonal design with three attributes—transit time, freight rate, and unloading wait time at destination—each at three levels. A conditional logit model was estimated. The implied value of transit time was 0.09 EUR per tonne-hour for barge and 0.14 EUR per tonne-hour for road, consistent with the hypothesis that bulk shippers are less time-sensitive when using inland waterway modes. Unloading wait time had a statistically significant negative utility, with a marginal disutility comparable to roughly 0.6 times the transit time coefficient. The study was limited by the small convenience sample and absence of firm-level controls, and the authors discuss the planned full survey design informed by these pilot results.

title: Revealed Versus Stated Preference Estimates of Freight Mode Choice Parameters: A Comparison Using Danube Corridor Data
abstract: Concerns about hypothetical bias in stated preference freight surveys are long-standing but rarely tested against matched revealed preference data in the same study region. This paper uses a dataset of 143 shippers for whom both actual shipment records (obtained from a forwarding agency operating on the Danube corridor) and stated preference responses were available. Models fitted to revealed preference data produced transit time coefficients approximately 35 percent smaller in absolute value than mixed logit models fitted to stated preference data, while price coefficients were broadly comparable. The reliability attribute could only be identified from stated preference data due to near-zero variation in observed on-time rates in the revealed preference records. A joint RP–SP model using scale parameter constraints is estimated and produces intermediate coefficient values. Implications for benefit–cost analysis of waterway infrastructure investments are discussed, particularly the risk of overstating time savings benefits when relying on stated preference estimates alone.

title: Income sources and off-farm employment among smallholder households in Vojvodina: a survey-based analysis
abstract: This study examines income diversification strategies among 214 smallholder farm households in Vojvodina surveyed in 2010. Using multinomial logit regression, the analysis identifies determinants of off-farm labour market participation, including farm size, operator age, education level, and proximity to urban centres. Results indicate that approximately 58% of surveyed households derive more than one-third of total household income from non-agricultural sources, with off-farm wage employment being the dominant pathway. Farms with holdings below 5 hectares show significantly higher off-farm participation rates compared to medium-scale farms. The paper also documents a negative association between access to direct payment schemes and the propensity to diversify, suggesting that subsidy access partially substitutes for off-farm income search. The findings have implications for rural development programming in the region, particularly for policies targeting household poverty reduction in the post-accession context of the Western Balkans.

title: Agri-environmental scheme uptake in a transition economy: evidence from the Pannonian lowlands of Serbia
abstract: This paper investigates the determinants of voluntary participation in agri-environmental schemes (AES) among 312 farm operators in the South Pannonian region of Serbia, drawing on data collected in 2012. A bivariate probit model accounts for the joint decision to apply for AES and to comply with scheme conditions. Key explanatory variables include farm size, tenure security, operator risk aversion (elicited via a lottery framing task), advisory service access, and prior experience with subsidy administration. Participation rates in the surveyed area stood at only 11.4%, substantially below the EU-27 average at the time. Tenure insecurity and high administrative burden are identified as the most consistent barriers to participation. The study also finds that farms engaged in livestock production are significantly more likely to participate than arable-only farms. Policy implications for simplifying scheme design in pre-accession and transition contexts are discussed.

title: Financial vulnerability of family farms in Vojvodina under crop price volatility: a stress-testing approach
abstract: This chapter applies a farm-level stress-testing framework to assess financial vulnerability of family farms in Vojvodina under simulated crop price shocks. Using bookkeeping data from 89 farms participating in a regional FADN-compatible monitoring network over the period 2009–2013, the analysis constructs a vulnerability index based on liquidity ratios, debt service coverage, and net farm income margins. Three price shock scenarios are simulated: a 15% decline in wheat prices, a 25% decline in sunflower prices, and a combined shock derived from the 2012 drought season. Results show that 34% of farms in the sample fall below critical liquidity thresholds under the combined scenario. Smaller farms with limited off-farm income buffers are disproportionately affected. The chapter situates these findings within the broader literature on financial resilience in post-socialist agricultural systems and draws comparisons with Hungarian and Romanian FADN data.

title: Land fragmentation and farm economic performance in Vojvodina: evidence from a cross-sectional farm survey
abstract: Land fragmentation is a persistent structural problem in post-socialist agricultural systems. This paper uses data from a 2016 cross-sectional survey of 278 farms in Vojvodina to examine the relationship between land fragmentation indices and farm economic performance, measured by gross margin per hectare and total factor productivity. A Heckman selection model accounts for the potential non-random selection of farms into renting additional parcels. Fragmentation is quantified using the Simmons index and average parcel size. Results indicate that a one-unit increase in the Simmons fragmentation index is associated with a 7.2% decrease in gross margin per hectare, controlling for farm size, operator characteristics, and crop mix. The effect is stronger for vegetable and mixed farms than for arable specialists. The paper discusses consolidation policy instruments and their limited implementation in the Serbian context to date.

title: Policy shock and farm exit: the effect of abrupt subsidy redesign on structural change in Serbian agriculture
abstract: This paper examines whether a 2014 redesign of Serbia's direct payment system, which shifted resources from per-hectare area payments toward investment co-financing schemes, triggered measurable farm exit among smaller operators. An administrative dataset covering 41,200 registered farm operators in Vojvodina over 2012–2019 is used. A difference-in-differences design exploits variation in farm-type exposure to the policy change, using livestock-heavy farms as the control group less affected by the redesign. Results indicate a 6.4 percentage point increase in exit probability for arable farms smaller than 10 hectares in the three years following the reform, compared with the counterfactual trend. Exit is concentrated among older operators and farms with no household member employed off-farm. The findings contribute to the debate on unintended structural adjustment consequences of payment reform in accession-candidate agricultural systems.

title: Carbon farming incentives and smallholder willingness to participate: a choice experiment in the Pannonian Plain
abstract: This paper presents results of a discrete choice experiment conducted with 231 smallholder farmers across Vojvodina and the adjacent Hungarian–Serbian border region in 2022, designed to elicit willingness to participate in a hypothetical carbon farming scheme. Attributes tested include payment level per tonne of CO₂-equivalent sequestered, contract duration, monitoring intensity, and co-benefits framing (biodiversity vs. soil health). Mixed logit estimates reveal strong heterogeneity in preferences: median willingness to accept is 38 EUR per tonne CO₂e per year for five-year contracts, rising to 54 EUR for ten-year commitments. Contract duration and perceived monitoring intrusiveness are the dominant negative attributes. Farmers with prior AES experience show significantly lower reluctance toward longer contracts. The results inform the calibration of carbon payment levels and scheme design for the Western Balkans context, where carbon markets remain nascent.

title: Resilience indicators for family farms in transition regions: a methodological comparison using Vojvodina panel data
abstract: A growing literature proposes quantitative indicators of farm resilience, but there is little consensus on which indicator sets perform best in data-scarce transition-economy contexts. This paper compares five indicator frameworks—robustness, adaptability, transformability, engineering resilience, and ecological-economic resilience composites—applied to a balanced panel of 97 Vojvodina family farms observed annually from 2014 to 2022. Indicator sets are evaluated against observed farm survival and income recovery after two documented stress events: the 2017 spring frost and the 2020 COVID-19 supply chain disruption. Predictive accuracy is assessed via receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results show that a parsimonious four-indicator set combining liquidity ratio, crop diversity index, off-farm income share, and short-term debt exposure outperforms more complex composites. The paper recommends this simplified set for routine monitoring within regional agricultural advisory networks.

title: Workload smoothing in mixed-model assembly lines: a comparison of priority rules under deterministic demand
abstract: Workload smoothing aims to reduce the variance of station loads across production sequences in mixed-model lines. This study evaluates eight priority sequencing rules—including Largest Work Content First, Smallest Work Content First, and a modified COMSOAL variant—on a test bed of 120 randomly generated problem instances with 3 to 7 model types and 5 to 10 workstations. Performance is measured by the average peak workload deviation per cycle and by the mean number of line stoppages over a simulated shift of 480 minutes. Results show that the modified COMSOAL rule reduces peak deviation by up to 18% compared to standard rules on instances with high inter-model time variation (coefficient of variation above 0.35). Computational effort is modest; all rules terminate in under 0.4 seconds. Practical applicability is discussed for a two-shift electronics sub-assembly context with deterministic daily demand.

title: A tabu search heuristic for the multi-manned mixed-model assembly line balancing problem
abstract: Multi-manned workstations, where more than one operator works simultaneously on the same unit, are prevalent in the assembly of large medical equipment such as imaging system sub-frames. This paper addresses the multi-manned ALBP extended to mixed-model settings and proposes a tabu search heuristic with adaptive tenure length. The neighbourhood structure is based on task migration moves between stations and operator reassignment within stations. The heuristic is tested on 60 instances derived from a published benchmark set and on two industrial instances with 48 and 61 tasks, respectively. On published benchmarks the heuristic matches or improves known best solutions in 52 of 60 cases within a 120-second runtime. For the 61-task industrial instance the solution has four stations each staffed by two operators, reducing total idle time by 16.3% relative to a single-manned configuration solved independently.

title: Demand variability buffering strategies for short-lifecycle medical device lines: a cost comparison
abstract: Medical device manufacturers face regulatory approval constraints that limit rapid product redesign, making finished goods inventory and capacity buffering the primary tools for absorbing demand variability. This study compares four buffering strategies—safety stock only, overtime capacity, dedicated buffer stations, and a hybrid safety stock–overtime policy—using a simulation-optimisation framework applied to an infusion pump line producing three variants. Demand is modelled as a negative binomial process fitted to 36 months of shipment records from a contract medical manufacturer in the region. For each strategy, total annual cost is estimated including inventory carrying, overtime premium, and expediting costs. The hybrid policy reduces total cost by 11–17% relative to pure safety stock across five demand scenarios covering different coefficient of variation levels (0.28 to 0.61). The analysis also quantifies the interaction between lot sizing decisions and buffer effectiveness.

title: Lot sizing and production scheduling integration in a low-volume orthopaedic implant facility: a rolling horizon approach
abstract: Orthopaedic implant manufacturers typically operate make-to-stock with long sterilisation lead times, creating a need to jointly determine lot sizes and detailed production sequences. This paper formulates a mixed-integer programme (MIP) integrating the capacitated lot sizing problem (CLSP) with sequence-dependent changeover times on a single mixed-model assembly line. A rolling horizon procedure is implemented with a window of four weeks and a frozen period of one week. The model is solved using Gurobi 8.0 with a 600-second time limit per window. Data were collected from a five-product orthopaedic screw manufacturing cell operating two shifts per day. Over a 26-week simulation horizon the rolling horizon approach reduces average backorder frequency by 34% and total inventory cost by 19% compared to a fixed cyclic schedule currently in use. Sensitivity to changes in the frozen period length is examined through a fractional factorial experiment.

title: Ergonomic constraints in assembly line balancing: incorporating RULA scores as task assignment restrictions
abstract: Assembly line balancing models rarely incorporate ergonomic loading directly into the optimisation. This book chapter reviews methodological approaches for embedding ergonomic metrics—specifically Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) scores—as hard or soft constraints within ALBP formulations. Three integration strategies are discussed: RULA score thresholds as feasibility constraints, penalty terms in the objective function, and post-processing reassignment. The chapter illustrates each strategy with a 28-task wiring harness assembly example where eight tasks have RULA scores of 6 or 7. Introducing a hard threshold of RULA ≤ 5 per station increases the required number of workstations from 5 to 6 in the example instance. The trade-off between ergonomic compliance and economic efficiency is quantified using a cost-per-unit model. Practical guidance is offered for industrial engineers implementing ergonomic line balancing in regulated manufacturing environments, including medical device assembly.

title: Demand forecasting accuracy and its downstream effect on assembly line buffer sizing: an empirical study in medical device manufacturing
abstract: This study investigates the link between forecast error characteristics and the sizing of in-process buffers on mixed-model assembly lines in three small-to-medium medical device manufacturers operating in Serbia and Romania. Monthly demand data spanning 48 months for 12 product families are analysed; forecast error is characterised by MAE, MAPE, and the Theil U statistic using simple exponential smoothing, Holt-Winters, and ARIMA models. Buffer sizes are then computed using a simulation model parameterised with empirical error distributions for each forecasting method. Results indicate that switching from a naïve forecast to Holt-Winters reduces required buffer space by 14–23% across the studied product families, with the largest reductions occurring for seasonal products. The study also documents that companies consistently use naïve or simple moving average forecasting, leaving measurable efficiency gains unrealised.

title: Rebalancing mixed-model assembly lines after product mix changes: a restart heuristic using incumbent solutions
abstract: Product mix changes during a planning horizon require rapid rebalancing of existing line configurations without discarding the accumulated ergonomic and tooling investments of the current layout. This paper proposes a warm-start rebalancing heuristic that uses the incumbent station assignment as a starting point for a variable neighbourhood search (VNS) procedure. The heuristic is evaluated on 45 rebalancing scenarios derived from a base configuration of a 10-station respiratory device assembly line, where between 1 and 4 new model variants are introduced with differing task sets. The VNS with warm-start reduces mean rebalancing computation time by 61% compared to solving from scratch while achieving solutions within 1.8% of the cold-start best on average. The number of station assignment changes between old and new configurations—a practical measure of physical retooling cost—is also minimised as a secondary objective, with results showing an average of 3.2 task reassignments per rebalancing event.

title: Scheduling with operator skill heterogeneity on a mixed-model medical device line: a robust optimisation approach
abstract: Operator skill heterogeneity is a recognised but rarely modelled source of performance variability on certified medical device assembly lines, where only qualified operators may perform specific tasks. This paper formulates a robust scheduling model that assigns tasks to stations and operators to shifts under uncertainty in individual operator processing speeds. Skill levels are represented as multipliers drawn from an interval uncertainty set fitted to direct observation data from a 7-operator diagnostic device assembly team. The robust counterpart of the nominal MIP is derived and solved with CPLEX 22.1 for a 5-station, 4-model line over a two-week rolling horizon. Compared to the nominal solution, the robust schedule reduces worst-case overtime cost by 28% with a 4% increase in expected makespan. A computational study examines the effect of the uncertainty budget parameter on solution conservatism across 36 test instances of varying operator team sizes.

title: Generating Minimum-Size Covering Arrays for Constrained Parameter Spaces in Automotive Middleware
abstract: Automotive middleware stacks expose large parameter spaces whose valid combinations are restricted by physical and logical constraints. Unconstrained covering array construction tends to produce test suites containing infeasible configurations, inflating execution time and masking real faults. This paper formulates constrained t-way covering array generation as a weighted partial MAX-SAT problem and evaluates three solvers—Glucose, CryptoMiniSat and a custom greedy heuristic—on eight industrial parameter models taken from a CAN-based body-electronics platform. For strength t = 2 and t = 3, the SAT-based approach reduces suite size by 18–34% compared to the greedy baseline while keeping generation time below 90 seconds for models with up to 40 parameters and 120 constraint clauses. Fault detection rates were measured against a seeded mutation set of 480 faults; the constrained suites achieved 91.4% detection versus 89.7% for unconstrained suites of equal size.

title: Interface Contract Specification for Multi-Supplier CAN Node Integration: A Formal Framework
abstract: When ECUs from different suppliers share a CAN bus, integration failures frequently arise from incompatible assumptions about message timing, signal encoding and error-handling behaviour. This paper presents a contract language, CAN-CL, based on assume-guarantee reasoning extended with real-time guards and bounded-integer signal domains. Contracts are written per node and per message group; a static checker verifies pairwise consistency before any hardware is available. The framework was applied retrospectively to a 14-node powertrain network. Among 37 documented integration bugs from the project history, static contract checking would have flagged 22 prior to bench testing, covering timing violations, byte-order mismatches and unhandled error frames. The paper details the contract syntax, the consistency-checking algorithm and its complexity, and discusses the mapping to AUTOSAR ComStack configurations.

title: Evaluating Strength-3 Combinatorial Test Suites Against Real Field Faults in a CAN Stack Implementation
abstract: Most empirical studies of combinatorial interaction testing rely on seeded or synthetic faults. This study evaluates t = 2 and t = 3 covering arrays against a corpus of 214 confirmed field faults extracted from maintenance records of a commercial CAN protocol stack used in agricultural machinery. Faults were classified by interaction order using a backward-coverage analysis: each fault was mapped to the smallest parameter interaction that would expose it. Results show 71% of faults are covered at t = 2 and 89% at t = 3, with diminishing returns beyond t = 3 (91% at t = 4). Suite sizes at t = 3 were 38–62% larger than at t = 2 across six parameter models; we quantify this cost against detection gain and discuss which fault categories resist coverage at any practical strength.

title: Specification and Automated Checking of Timing Contracts for Multi-Frame CAN FD Messages
abstract: CAN FD allows payloads of up to 64 bytes, enabling protocol designers to split application data across multiple frames within a single bus cycle. This introduces ordering and timing dependencies that are absent in classical CAN and are not addressed by existing contract formalisms designed for single-frame messages. We extend CAN-CL with frame-sequence guards, specifying allowable inter-frame gaps, mandatory acknowledgement windows and abort conditions. An automated checker based on timed automata model checking (UPPAAL 4.1) is implemented and evaluated on four CAN FD configurations. Verification of a 12-message sequence contract with 6 participating nodes completes in under 4 minutes on standard hardware. Three previously undetected timing hazards were found in one of the supplied configurations when contracts were tightened from their original loose bounds.

title: A Benchmark Suite for Constrained Covering Array Generators: Construction, Characteristics and Baseline Results
abstract: Progress in constrained covering array generation is hindered by the lack of a shared, publicly documented benchmark collection. We describe the construction of CovBench-CAN, a suite of 52 parameter models derived from real CAN-based embedded configurations with constraints anonymised for public release. Each model is characterised by parameter count (4–61), domain sizes, constraint density and tightness, and the number of valid t-tuples at t = 2 and t = 3. Baseline results are reported for five generators: ACTS, TestCoverage, an in-house SAT-based tool and two metaheuristic approaches. Across the suite, solver performance varies substantially: no single generator dominates on all metrics. The benchmark and scripts are released under an open licence to facilitate reproducible comparisons. We discuss lessons learned about constraint encoding and the sensitivity of generator performance to domain ordering.

title: Cross-Layer Interaction Faults in Multi-Supplier Embedded Stacks: A Taxonomy and Detection Study
abstract: Multi-supplier embedded stacks combine hardware abstraction layers, communication drivers, protocol stacks and application components from different vendors. Faults that manifest at integration time often involve interactions spanning two or more layers, yet testing strategies typically treat layers independently. This paper presents a taxonomy of cross-layer interaction faults assembled from post-mortem analyses of 19 integration projects in the automotive and industrial automation sectors, covering 312 documented faults. The taxonomy comprises 11 fault categories grouped under three themes: resource aliasing, contract silences and emergent timing. For each category we assess detectability by unit testing, pairwise integration testing and t-way combinatorial testing at t ∈ {2, 3, 4}. Categories involving three or more layers require t ≥ 3 for reliable detection. The taxonomy is proposed as a basis for checklist-driven integration reviews.

title: Monitoring Overhead Profiles for CAN-CL Runtime Contracts Across Six Microcontroller Families
abstract: Earlier work demonstrated CAN-CL runtime monitoring on a single microcontroller target. This paper broadens the evaluation across six representative 32-bit microcontroller families (two ARM Cortex-M4 variants, one Cortex-M7, one RISC-V, one TriCore and one PowerPC e200) commonly used in automotive and industrial embedded systems. For each target, monitors were generated from the same set of 12 canonical contracts and instrumented into a reference CAN stack. CPU overhead, stack usage, code size and worst-case response time were measured. Overhead ranged from 1.8% to 5.6% CPU utilisation across targets, driven primarily by differences in interrupt latency and cache behaviour rather than core clock speed. Stack additions were uniformly below 320 bytes. The results inform compiler flag choices and memory allocation policies and are provided as a configuration guide for practitioners.

title: Error-Driven Quadric Simplification with Perceptual Weighting for Static Mesh Sequences
abstract: This paper revisits quadric error metric simplification by introducing a perceptual weighting term derived from the expected viewing distance and surface curvature. The method computes per-face importance scores from a saliency map estimated by a lightweight convolution over the mesh surface normal field. Experiments were conducted on fourteen benchmark models ranging from 80 000 to 2.4 million triangles. At a 90 % reduction ratio the proposed weighting retained salient features—creases, high-curvature ridges—with a Hausdorff error 18 % lower on average than the standard quadric approach across the test set. Processing time on a single CPU core was under 4 seconds for all models below one million triangles. The method is implemented as a standalone C++ library with a documented API. The study also provides a small perceptual user study with 34 participants who rated visual fidelity of simplified meshes, confirming a statistically significant preference for perceptually weighted output at all tested reduction levels.

title: Fine-tuning a multilingual transformer model for fault classification in low-resource maintenance corpora
abstract: Training effective text classifiers for specialised industrial domains is constrained when annotated data are scarce. This paper evaluates fine-tuning strategies for the XLM-R multilingual transformer on a fault classification task using corpora of different sizes drawn from Serbian electrical maintenance records. Three conditions were tested: full fine-tuning on 500, 1,500, and 4,500 labelled instances; layer-freezing strategies that update only the top two transformer layers; and domain-adaptive pre-training on 180,000 unlabelled maintenance sentences prior to fine-tuning. On the smallest labelled set (500 instances), domain-adaptive pre-training followed by full fine-tuning yielded a macro-F1 of 0.71, compared with 0.63 for direct fine-tuning of XLM-R and 0.59 for a TF-IDF plus logistic regression baseline. Performance gaps narrowed at 4,500 instances. The paper also reports zero-shot transfer experiments to a Romanian maintenance corpus of 2,800 records, where the domain-adapted model achieved an F1 of 0.58 without any Romanian labels, suggesting partial cross-lingual portability within the domain.

title: Flank wear progression in uncoated and TiN-coated cemented carbide inserts during dry turning of grey cast iron
abstract: This study compared flank wear development in uncoated WC-Co inserts and single-layer TiN PVD-coated inserts when turning grey cast iron (HB 210) at cutting speeds of 180, 240 and 300 m/min, feed 0.15 mm/rev, depth 1.5 mm. Wear land width was measured at 400, 800, 1200 and 1600 m cumulative cutting distance by optical profilometry. TiN-coated inserts showed a 38–47 % reduction in flank wear width relative to uncoated tools at all three speeds. SEM examination of worn flanks revealed abrasive grooves and scattered adhesion patches on uncoated inserts, while TiN-coated tools exhibited oxidation pitting beyond 1200 m at 300 m/min. EDS mapping confirmed iron-rich transfer layers on both insert types. Tool life, defined by VB = 0.3 mm, was extended by a mean factor of 1.6 for TiN-coated inserts. Results indicate that TiN coatings offer moderate life improvement at moderate speeds but are thermally limited above 280 m/min in grey cast iron turning.

title: Crater wear characterisation of TiAlN-coated carbide inserts in turning of AISI 4340 hardened steel
abstract: Crater wear on the rake face of TiAlN-coated WC-Co inserts was characterised during turning of AISI 4340 steel hardened to 52 HRC, at cutting speeds 120 and 160 m/min, feed 0.10 mm/rev, depth 0.5 mm, under strictly dry conditions. Crater depth and area were measured at intervals of 200 m by confocal laser scanning microscopy. At 160 m/min, crater depth reached 12 µm after 800 m, while at 120 m/min the same depth was not exceeded before 1400 m. Cross-sectional TEM foils prepared by FIB from the crater floor revealed a 40–80 nm amorphous tribolayer enriched in Fe and O. Raman spectroscopy identified alumina clusters in the tribolayer, suggesting partial oxidative transformation of the TiAlN coating. Abrasive wear dominated the crater floor, with diffusion wear becoming significant above 160 m/min. The data support a transition from predominantly mechanical to thermally assisted wear between 140 and 160 m/min for this coating–workpiece combination.
