title: Reliability of three inertial sensor placements for stride detection during football-specific running drills
abstract: Accurate stride detection from wearable inertial measurement units depends heavily on sensor placement, yet standardised protocols for football field testing are lacking. Twenty-two healthy male players performed a battery of sport-specific running drills—including linear sprints, shuttle runs, and curved runs—wearing Shimmer3 IMUs simultaneously on the lower back, right shank, and right shoe. A treadmill-mounted force plate provided reference gait events. Intraclass correlation coefficients for stride time were 0.91, 0.87, and 0.94 for the back, shank, and shoe placements respectively. The shoe-mounted sensor yielded the lowest mean absolute error for initial contact detection (11 ms) but was most sensitive to debris and moisture. Shank placement offered the best compromise between accuracy and practical durability for outdoor use. These findings inform sensor placement choices for longitudinal load-monitoring studies conducted in community football settings.

title: Lower-limb loading asymmetry quantified by inertial sensors in football players following ACL reconstruction: comparison with healthy controls
abstract: This study examined whether players who had undergone anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and been cleared for return to play still exhibited loading asymmetries detectable by trunk- and shank-mounted IMUs during football-specific tasks. Sixteen post-ACLR players (mean 8.2 months post-surgery) and 16 age- and position-matched healthy controls performed a standardised circuit including cutting, deceleration, and acceleration tasks on a natural grass surface. Peak resultant acceleration at the shank and a composite symmetry index derived from mid-stance accelerations were computed. Post-ACLR players showed a symmetry index of 82.4 ± 7.1% compared with 94.6 ± 5.2% in controls (p < 0.001). Cutting tasks produced larger inter-limb differences than straight-line running. IMU-based symmetry indices correlated moderately with single-leg hop symmetry scores (r = 0.61). The findings suggest that IMU-based field assessments can complement standard hop-battery protocols in return-to-play decision-making.

title: Estimating tibial shock during football training sessions using a single shank-mounted accelerometer
abstract: Tibial stress fractures are a recognised overuse injury in football, yet direct measurement of tibial shock during full training sessions is logistically demanding. This study assessed whether peak positive tibial acceleration (PPTA) measured with a single Shimmer3 unit on the right shank during 18 training sessions in 28 male sub-elite players correlated with session rating of perceived exertion (sRPE) and GPS-derived high-speed running distance. PPTA ranged from 4.1 to 11.8 g across sessions and players. Mixed-effects modelling showed that high-speed running distance was the strongest predictor of within-player PPTA variation (β = 0.047 g per 10 m, 95% CI 0.031–0.063), while sRPE contributed negligibly after accounting for speed metrics. Players with body mass index above 26 kg/m² showed systematically higher PPTA values. The protocol adds an accessible bone-loading proxy to existing external load frameworks used in semi-professional club settings.

title: Seasonal variation in movement asymmetry indices in sub-elite football players: a longitudinal IMU study
abstract: Training and competition loads fluctuate considerably across a football season, potentially influencing bilateral movement symmetry. Thirty-one male players from one regional Serbian club wore shank-mounted IMUs during five standardised test sessions distributed across pre-season, early, mid, and late season, and post-season. A composite lower-limb asymmetry index (LLAI) was computed from acceleration envelopes during a 10-repetition step-down task. LLAI was highest at mid-season (mean 13.1 ± 4.6%) and lowest post-season (8.4 ± 3.9%), with a statistically significant main effect of time-point (F(4,120) = 6.83, p < 0.001). Players who accumulated more than 1200 minutes of match play showed larger mid-season LLAI peaks than those with lower exposure. Injuries occurring within two weeks of testing were preceded by LLAI values at least 1.5 standard deviations above a player's personal mean in six of nine cases. These longitudinal patterns suggest that LLAI monitoring could flag individuals warranting load reduction.

title: Inter-rater and test–retest reliability of a field-based IMU screening protocol for lower-limb symmetry in football
abstract: Before IMU-based movement screening can be adopted in practitioner settings, its measurement properties must be established. This methodological study recruited 40 male football players who completed a six-task IMU screening battery on two occasions seven days apart, assessed by two independent evaluators. The battery included step-down, lateral hop, and 180° change-of-direction tasks. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC2,1) for the composite LLAI ranged from 0.82 to 0.91 across tasks, indicating good to excellent test–retest reliability. Inter-rater reliability was excellent for all tasks (ICC ≥ 0.88). Minimal detectable change values ranged from 2.8 to 5.3 percentage points depending on task, providing clinically meaningful thresholds for interpreting longitudinal change. Standard error of measurement was below 2.5% for four of six tasks. The protocol is described with sufficient procedural detail to enable replication in community club environments without laboratory infrastructure.

title: Hamstring injury biomechanics during high-speed running: IMU-derived proxies and their relationship to injury history in regional football players
abstract: Hamstring strain injuries are the most prevalent muscle injury in football, but direct neuromechanical assessment during maximal sprinting is rarely feasible outside laboratory environments. This study used pelvis- and thigh-mounted IMUs to derive late-swing angular velocity as a proxy for hamstring loading in 38 male players (20 with a history of unilateral hamstring strain, 18 injury-free controls) during a 40-metre maximal sprint on a natural grass pitch. Peak angular velocity at the thigh during late swing was 7.3% higher in the previously injured limb compared with the contralateral limb in the history group (p = 0.009) and did not differ significantly in controls (p = 0.41). Regression analysis indicated that late-swing angular velocity asymmetry explained 22% of the variance in Nordboard eccentric hamstring force asymmetry (R² = 0.22, p = 0.004). IMU-derived angular velocity metrics may therefore serve as a practical adjunct to force-based hamstring screening in field settings.

title: Seasonal decomposition as a preprocessing step for short-horizon retail revenue forecasting: a comparative study
abstract: This study evaluates four seasonal decomposition methods—classical additive, STL, X-11, and empirical mode decomposition—applied as preprocessing steps before training ARIMA and exponential smoothing models on weekly retail revenue data. The dataset comprises 48 months of transaction records from three mid-sized Serbian retail chains, totalling roughly 11,000 weekly observations across 230 product categories. Each decomposition method is assessed against direct (undecomposed) modelling on one- and four-week-ahead forecasts, using MAE, RMSE, and MASE as evaluation metrics. STL decomposition combined with exponential smoothing produced the lowest MASE values across 18 of 24 test configurations. The paper discusses practical constraints arising from irregular promotions and public holidays in the Serbian retail calendar, which reduce the effectiveness of classical additive decomposition. Results suggest that decomposition choice has a larger effect on forecast accuracy than the choice of the base forecasting model for horizons up to four weeks.

title: Does source domain size matter in transfer learning for time-series forecasting? An empirical study
abstract: When building transfer learning systems for revenue forecasting, practitioners must decide how much source-domain data to collect before initiating transfer. This paper examines the relationship between source domain size and target domain forecast accuracy through a controlled experiment using 480 weekly revenue series from the retail sector across Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. Source datasets are subsampled at five size levels (50, 100, 200, 400, and 800 series), and fine-tuned LSTM models are evaluated on 96 target series with 12 weeks of available data. Accuracy is measured at 1-, 2-, and 4-week horizons. Results show a logarithmic relationship between source size and accuracy improvement, with diminishing returns beyond approximately 200 source series for 1-week-ahead forecasts. The gains plateau earlier for 4-week horizons. The paper provides practical guidelines for data collection investment decisions and includes a cost-benefit analysis template for industry practitioners.

title: Prototypical networks for time-series classification in short e-commerce revenue sequences
abstract: This chapter reviews and evaluates prototypical network architectures, originally proposed for image classification, in the context of time-series classification for short e-commerce revenue sequences. The task is to assign a new revenue series with fewer than 20 observations to one of six trend-regime classes (stable growth, plateau, seasonal spike, irregular, declining, launch ramp), which in turn conditions the choice of a downstream forecasting model. The chapter covers the adaptation of the embedding network to univariate time-series inputs using both 1D convolutional and LSTM encoders, describes the episode construction procedure used during meta-training, and reports results on a dataset of 540 manually labelled series. The 1D-CNN encoder achieves 74 percent five-way classification accuracy with five support examples per class, compared with 61 percent for a nearest-centroid baseline using DTW distance. The chapter concludes with a discussion of practical integration into a two-stage forecasting pipeline.

title: Warm-starting forecasting models for newly launched online products using cross-platform meta-training
abstract: Online marketplaces frequently add new product listings that accumulate revenue data for only a few weeks before a reliable forecasting model is required for inventory and pricing decisions. This paper proposes a cross-platform meta-training strategy in which a MAML-based meta-learner is trained on series from three established e-commerce platforms operating in different Balkan markets and then adapted to a fourth, newly launched platform. The meta-training set contains 2,100 series; the new platform provides between 4 and 16 weeks of data for 210 products used in evaluation. Warm-started models reach accuracy parity with in-platform models trained on 52 weeks of data when only 10 weeks of target-platform data are available, measured by MASE at a 1-week horizon. The paper analyses the influence of platform-level covariates (traffic sources, promotional calendar structure, product category distribution) on adaptation speed and finds that promotional calendar similarity is the strongest predictor.

title: Comparison of Minimum-Phase and Linear-Phase IIR Parametric Filters for Steady-State Modal Equalisation
abstract: Parametric equalisers applied to modal correction in small rooms can be implemented with either minimum-phase or linear-phase infinite-impulse-response topologies. This paper evaluates both approaches through simulation and bench measurement on a digital signal processor platform. Forty-eight filter configurations were designed to attenuate a set of six synthetic modal resonances with Q values ranging from 8 to 45. Residual error at the target listening position, group-delay distortion, and computational load were the three evaluation criteria. Minimum-phase filters reduced peak SPL by a mean of 9.2 dB but introduced group-delay ripple of up to 18 ms in the 40–80 Hz band. Linear-phase implementations eliminated the delay artefact at a cost of 3.1 dB less attenuation efficiency and a factor of 2.4 greater DSP load. For the correction of modes above 80 Hz, both topologies produced equivalent perceptual outcomes in a blind listening test with twelve experienced audio engineers. Below 80 Hz, eight of the twelve listeners preferred the linear-phase condition. The results inform filter selection guidelines for studio calibration workflows.

title: Gradient-Descent Optimisation of Multi-Band Parametric Filter Banks for Listening Room Correction
abstract: This paper describes a constrained gradient-descent algorithm for automatic placement of parametric equaliser bands targeting modal resonances in small listening rooms. The algorithm operates on a smoothed 1/12-octave room transfer function measured at the principal listening position and seeks to minimise a cost function combining spectral flatness deviation and total filter gain magnitude. A secondary penalty term discourages overlapping filter bands. Simulations using 22 measured room transfer functions from studios in Serbia and Hungary demonstrated convergence in fewer than 400 iterations for a 16-band filter bank. The resulting equalisers reduced the standard deviation of the 30–200 Hz magnitude response from a mean of 8.7 dB to 3.1 dB. Compared with manually tuned equalisers produced by three experienced acousticians, the algorithm achieved statistically equivalent flatness (p = 0.09, Wilcoxon test) with 60% fewer filter bands on average. Computational cost on a 2002-era DSP was approximately 140 ms per full optimisation run, making the method suitable for semi-automated studio setup procedures.

title: Loudspeaker Placement Geometry as a Precondition for Parametric Modal Correction: A Systematic Study in Twelve Studio Rooms
abstract: Parametric equalisation of room modes is inherently position-dependent: a filter effective at one seat may amplify the problem at an adjacent position. This study examined whether optimising loudspeaker placement before applying any electronic correction reduces the spatial variance of residual modal error. Twelve professional and semi-professional studios in Vojvodina participated. In each room, a two-speaker stereo configuration was tested at three lateral positions and two depths within the practical mixing zone. Room transfer functions were measured at a 5×3 grid of listening positions in each configuration. Results showed that the loudspeaker position that minimised the spatial variance of the 40–120 Hz response prior to equalisation also yielded a 22% lower residual error after applying a fixed 12-band parametric equaliser, compared with the conventionally centred placement. The paper provides a two-step workflow: first optimise geometry using a variance criterion, then apply parametric filters. A simple measurement protocol implementable with consumer-grade microphones and a laptop is described.

title: Sensitivity of Parametric Equaliser Correction to Listener Head Movement in Small Control Rooms
abstract: Room correction equalisers are typically calibrated at a single measurement point. When a listener moves their head, the corrected response degrades. This study quantified that degradation in five control rooms (volumes 30–55 m³) whose low-frequency responses had been corrected with 10–14-band parametric filter banks optimised by the gradient-descent method described in earlier work. Room transfer functions were remeasured at 120 positions within a 30 cm radius sphere centred on the calibration point, representing natural head movement during a mixing session. The mean increase in 30–150 Hz spectral standard deviation was 2.4 dB at 10 cm displacement and 5.1 dB at 25 cm displacement. Rooms with high modal density showed lower sensitivity because no single mode dominated. A perceptual threshold experiment with 14 listeners suggested that deviations up to 3.2 dB were not reliably detected (d' < 1.0). The paper concludes that correction is robust for listeners who remain within approximately 15 cm of the calibration point, and proposes a multi-position average measurement strategy for rooms with lower modal density.

title: Parametric Equalisation of Tangential and Oblique Modes: Are They Worth Targeting?
abstract: Low-frequency room equalisation practice typically targets axial modes because they have the highest Q and are straightforwardly identified by frequency. Tangential and oblique modes are often ignored on the grounds that their pressure distributions are spatially diffuse and their Q values low. This paper examines whether including tangential and oblique modes in the optimisation target set improves correction outcomes in six rooms where the axial mode correction had already been applied. An extended measurement protocol (81 microphone positions per room) was used to map the three-dimensional pressure distribution of all identified modes below 200 Hz. Parametric filters targeting the 12 strongest tangential and oblique modes per room were added to existing axial correction filter banks. At the primary listening position, the additional filters produced a mean improvement of 0.8 dB in spectral standard deviation, with a maximum of 2.1 dB in one room. At off-axis positions the improvement was larger: mean 1.9 dB. The paper provides a decision criterion — based on the ratio of oblique to axial modal energy — for determining when targeting higher-order mode types is cost-effective.

title: A Measured Transfer-Function Database for Small Asymmetric Rooms in the Vojvodina Region and Its Use as a Benchmark for Equalisation Algorithms
abstract: Comparative evaluation of room correction algorithms is hampered by the use of different test rooms and measurement protocols across studies. This paper describes the construction and public release of a database of room transfer functions measured in 31 small asymmetric rooms in Vojvodina — primarily recording studios, rehearsal rooms, and control rooms at educational institutions — with volumes between 22 and 80 m³. Each room was measured at 27 microphone positions per room with 1/24-octave resolution from 20 Hz to 500 Hz, producing a dataset of 837 individual transfer functions. The database includes room geometry sketches, material absorption estimates, and RT60 values at each position. Three previously published equalisation algorithms — gradient-descent parametric, genetic algorithm parametric, and direct inverse filtering — were evaluated against the full database. The gradient-descent parametric method produced the best median performance (spectral standard deviation 2.9 dB at the primary position) and the most consistent results across room types. The database is intended as a community benchmark resource and is distributed under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Uticaj kvaliteta korisničkih oznaka na preciznost preporučivanja audio sadržaja
abstract: Rad analizira kako nepotpunost i nekonzistentnost korisničkih tagova utiče na preporučivanje audio sadržaja u sistemima zasnovanim na sadržaju. Korišćen je skup od 42 000 pesama sa tagovima prikupljenim sa javne platforme za striming, uz ručno kreiranu zlatnu referencu za 1 200 stavki. Uvedena je metrika zagađenosti oznaka (tag noise ratio) i ispitana korelacija sa padom preciznosti preporuke merene NDCG@10 merom. Eksperimenti pokazuju da porast zagađenosti sa 5% na 25% dovodi do pada NDCG@10 za prosečno 0,12 poena u četiri testirana modela. Rad predlaže strategiju prečišćavanja zasnovanu na klasterovanju rečničkih vektora i pokazuje da ona delimično kompenzuje efekte zagađenosti.

title: Word2Vec Embeddings for Multilingual Audio Metadata: A Comparative Study on Serbian and Hungarian Text
abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of Word2Vec skip-gram embeddings trained on bilingual corpora of Serbian and Hungarian audio metadata for downstream music genre and mood classification tasks. We collected a dataset of 31 000 tracks whose metadata fields were available in both languages, sourced from a regional content aggregator. Models were trained separately on each language corpus and on a concatenated bilingual corpus with cross-lingual alignment via a small bilingual dictionary of 4 200 entries. Classification experiments using logistic regression show that the bilingual model outperforms both monolingual baselines on Hungarian data by 4.3 F1 points while maintaining Serbian-language performance. Error analysis highlights morphological richness as a persistent challenge, particularly for Serbian due to inflectional variability in descriptive text. The findings suggest that joint training with modest alignment resources is viable for closely cooperating regional content markets.

title: Semantic Similarity Measures for Short Audio Descriptions: Benchmarking on a Regional Podcast Corpus
abstract: Short descriptive texts accompanying podcast episodes present a distinct NLP challenge due to their brevity and domain heterogeneity. We assembled a corpus of 9 600 podcast episode descriptions from three Serbian-language podcast platforms, annotated by three independent judges for pairwise semantic similarity on a 1–5 scale (inter-annotator agreement κ = 0.64). We benchmarked eight similarity methods ranging from cosine similarity over TF-IDF vectors to sentence-level embeddings produced by a fine-tuned multilingual BERT variant. The sentence embedding approach achieved the highest Spearman correlation with human judgements (ρ = 0.73), outperforming TF-IDF cosine by 0.18 points. We also report that methods relying on surface lexical overlap perform disproportionately poorly on this corpus due to high synonym usage in Serbian descriptive prose. The annotated corpus is publicly released under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Fine-Tuning Multilingual Sentence Transformers for Low-Resource Audio Metadata Classification
abstract: We examine the degree to which a multilingual sentence transformer pre-trained on 104 languages can be efficiently fine-tuned for audio metadata classification in Serbian and Romanian — two languages with limited labelled resources. Starting from a publicly available multilingual sentence transformer checkpoint, we fine-tune on three target tasks: genre classification, mood tagging, and content advisory labelling, using labelled datasets of 6 000, 4 200, and 2 800 examples respectively. Fine-tuning with as few as 500 task-specific examples per class yields macro F1 scores within 5 points of a fully supervised baseline trained on ten times more data. We compare three fine-tuning strategies: full model, last-layer only, and adapter modules, finding that adapter-based fine-tuning achieves the best trade-off between performance and training cost. Experiments are conducted on a shared GPU cluster and all code and model weights are released openly.

title: Semantičko pretraživanje audio arhiva radiodifuznih stanica korišćenjem gustih vektora upita
abstract: Rad opisuje primenu gustih vektora upita (dense retrieval) za semantičko pretraživanje digitalnih audio arhiva dve regionalne radiodifuzne stanice. Arhive sadrže ukupno 230 000 zapisa sa prateće tekstualnim metapodacima različitog kvaliteta i opsega. Sistem upotrebljava bi-enkoder arhitekturu: odvojeni enkoder za upite i enkoder za dokumente, trenirane na skupu od 18 000 ručno pariranih parova upit–relevantni zapis. Efikasno pretraživanje velikog indeksa omogućeno je FAISS bibliotekom za aproksimativno pretraživanje najbližih suseda. Evalucija na 500 testnih upita pokazuje MRR@10 = 0,61, što je poboljšanje od 22% u odnosu na BM25 osnivača. Poseban naglasak stavljen je na upite koji koriste govorni jezik i idiome koji se ne pojavljuju direktno u metapodacima.

title: Evaluacija vektorskih modela za automatsko tagovanje audio metapodataka u uslovima nedovoljno zastupljenih klasa
abstract: Automatsko tagovanje audio sadržaja u realnim industrijskim katalozima karakteriše se izrazitom neravnomernošću klasa: manji broj popularnih žanrova i raspoloženja daleko je zastupljeniji od dugog repa specifičnih kategorija. U ovom radu evaluiramo šest metoda balansiranja klasa — uključujući preuzorkovanje, potcenjivanje i sintetičke primere bazirane na SMOTE pristupu primenjenom na prostoru ugrađivanja — u kombinaciji sa tri tipa semantičkih vektora (Word2Vec, fastText i sentence-BERT). Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na internom katalog skupu od 61 000 zapisa sa 47 tag kategorija. Kombinacija sentence-BERT ugrađivanja i SMOTE u prostoru ugrađivanja daje best macro F1 = 0,68, poboljšavajući rezultat najjačeg osnivača za 9,4 poena. Analiza troškova pokazuje da metoda ostaje računski primenljiva za operativnu upotrebu na prosečnom serverskom hardveru.

title: Contrastive Learning of Audio Description Embeddings Using Weak Supervision from Listener Behaviour
abstract: We propose a contrastive training objective for learning audio description embeddings that incorporates weak supervision signals derived from listener co-engagement patterns — specifically, pairs of audio items listened to in the same session by the same user. A dataset of 4.2 million session records from a fictional regional streaming platform was provided under a data processing agreement. Positive pairs are defined by co-occurrence within a session window of ten consecutive plays; negatives are sampled from across the catalogue. The resulting embeddings are evaluated on three downstream tasks: genre classification, mood tagging, and nearest-neighbour retrieval as judged by human assessors. On retrieval, the contrastive model achieves NDCG@10 = 0.74, exceeding a supervised sentence-transformer baseline by 3.1 points. Ablation studies confirm that session-derived weak supervision contributes meaningfully beyond text-only training, particularly for instrumental and ambient content where descriptive text is sparse.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Metadata Enrichment for Legacy Audio Archives: A Case Study with a Serbian National Broadcaster
abstract: Legacy audio archives at broadcasting institutions often contain incomplete or absent textual metadata, limiting discoverability. We describe a retrieval-augmented enrichment pipeline applied to a 180 000-item archive of a Serbian national broadcaster, where 38% of records lacked genre or thematic tags. The pipeline retrieves semantically similar, fully annotated items using a dense retrieval index and uses their metadata to propose tags for the unlabelled item via a lightweight classifier applied to the concatenated candidate descriptions. Human curators validated a random sample of 2 000 enriched records, accepting 71% of proposed primary tags without modification and 83% after minor edit. Processing cost was estimated at 0.4 CPU-hours per 1 000 records on standard server hardware. The pipeline is now in trial deployment. This work was carried out in collaboration with the broadcaster's digital archive department.

title: Tracking of total cholesterol levels across three decades in a Vojvodinian semi-industrial cohort: baseline findings
abstract: This paper presents baseline descriptive findings from a longitudinal household registry established in 1983 in a mixed agricultural-industrial settlement east of Novi Sad. A cross-sectional analysis of 1,214 adults aged 30–65 enrolled between 2004 and 2007 was carried out to characterise the distribution of fasting total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, and triglycerides. Measurements were taken following standardised fasting protocols; smoking status, dietary recall, and occupational history were collected via structured interview. Mean total cholesterol was 5.84 mmol/L (SD 1.12), with 41.3% of participants exceeding the 6.2 mmol/L clinical threshold. Occupational exposure to heavy metals in the prior decade was associated with a 0.38 mmol/L elevation in LDL after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. The cohort profile is described in detail to facilitate future follow-up analyses. This baseline dataset forms the foundation of a planned 20-year tracking study.

title: Parental hypertension and offspring blood pressure levels in a three-generation Vojvodinian family registry
abstract: Using data from 487 parent–offspring trios extracted from a longitudinal household registry, we examined the intergenerational transmission of elevated blood pressure in a post-industrial Vojvodinian population. Resting systolic and diastolic blood pressure was measured on three occasions twelve months apart in both generations; a parental hypertension index was derived from recorded diagnoses and antihypertensive medication use. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for family clustering showed that offspring of two hypertensive parents had systolic blood pressure 8.2 mmHg higher on average than offspring of normotensive parents (95% CI: 6.1–10.3), independent of current BMI, smoking, and salt intake. The association was stronger in sons than daughters. Socioeconomic position partially mediated the relationship, explaining approximately 18% of the intergenerational effect. These findings support the relevance of family-level screening programmes in communities with elevated cardiovascular burden.

title: Group-based trajectory models of BMI from young adulthood to age 60 in a Vojvodinian community sample
abstract: Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) was applied to body mass index measurements collected at five time points over 22 years in 863 participants from a community cohort in Vojvodina. Four distinct BMI trajectory groups were identified: stable normal weight (28.4%), gradual increase (34.7%), early-onset high BMI (21.1%), and late-onset rapid gain (15.8%). Membership in the late-onset rapid gain group was associated with a two-fold higher odds of incident hypertension by age 55 (OR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.47–3.11) after adjustment for baseline socioeconomic status, smoking, and physical activity. Women were over-represented in the stable normal weight group at all ages. Sensitivity analyses using different numbers of trajectory groups confirmed the four-group solution as optimal by BIC criteria. These trajectory patterns have implications for the timing of preventive interventions.

title: Trends in cardiovascular polypharmacy and risk factor control in a Vojvodinian cohort, 2005–2023
abstract: Using pharmacy dispensing records linked to 843 cohort participants followed from 2005 to 2023, we characterised trends in the use of antihypertensives, statins, and antiplatelet agents, and assessed whether increased medication uptake corresponded to improved risk factor control. The proportion receiving at least one antihypertensive rose from 24.1% in 2005 to 41.7% in 2023; concurrent statin use increased from 8.3% to 27.4%. Despite this increase, the prevalence of controlled hypertension (systolic < 140 mmHg) improved only modestly, from 38.2% to 47.6% among treated individuals. Polypharmacy (≥ 4 medications) was present in 19.3% of participants aged 65 and older by 2023. Gaps in control were most pronounced in men, participants with lower educational attainment, and former industrial workers. The findings suggest that prescription trends alone are insufficient to close cardiovascular risk gaps in this population.

title: Nematode community structure in conventionally tilled and no-till chernozem plots of northern Vojvodina
abstract: Free-living nematode assemblages were sampled from twelve paired conventionally tilled and no-till maize plots across four localities in Bačka during autumn 2008. A total of 38 genera were identified using morphological keys. Shannon diversity, Maturity Index (MI), and the Plant Parasitic Index (PPI) were calculated for each plot. No-till plots showed significantly higher MI values (mean 2.61 vs. 2.14, p < 0.01) and greater bacterivore enrichment. Fungivore abundance was also elevated in no-till treatments, consistent with greater fungal biomass inferred from soil organic carbon measurements (average 2.8% vs. 2.1% in tilled plots). Bacterivore-to-fungivore ratios declined with increasing tillage intensity. PPI values did not differ significantly between tillage treatments, though Pratylenchus densities were slightly higher under conventional tillage. Results support the use of nematode-based indices as early-warning tools for monitoring structural degradation of soil food webs under intensive arable farming in the Vojvodina region.

title: Effects of mineral nitrogen fertilisation on nematode trophic groups in wheat-growing soils of the Srem district
abstract: Soil nematode assemblages were examined at six wheat-growing sites in Srem subjected to three nitrogen fertilisation levels (0, 80, and 160 kg N ha⁻¹). Samples were collected at three time points over a single growing season. A total of 1,847 individuals per 100 g dry soil were counted on average. Bacterivore abundance increased significantly with increasing N application, rising from 412 to 689 individuals per 100 g dry soil between the unfertilised and highest-N treatments. The Enrichment Index rose from 38 to 67 across the same gradient, indicating enriched, disturbed conditions at high N input. Fungivore and omnivore genera showed inverse responses. The Enrichment Index and Channel Index were sensitive to fertilisation rate differences and are proposed as complementary monitoring variables for nutrient management assessment in intensive wheat production. Soil mineral nitrogen and microbial biomass carbon were measured alongside nematode extractions to contextualise trophic-group responses.

title: Comparison of nematode extraction efficiency between modified Baermann funnel and centrifugal-flotation methods applied to Vojvodina loam soils
abstract: Methodological consistency is critical when comparing nematode community data across studies and laboratories. This paper compared two widely used extraction procedures — modified Baermann funnels (48-hour passive extraction) and sugar centrifugal flotation — applied to loam soils with varying organic matter content collected from three sites in Vojvodina. Ten replicate extractions were performed per method per site. Centrifugal flotation consistently recovered 18–34% more individuals than Baermann funnels depending on soil organic matter content, with the greatest discrepancy in soils exceeding 3% organic carbon. Genus-level community composition showed no significant difference between methods in canonical correspondence analysis ordinations, suggesting that relative community metrics (indices) are robust to extraction method choice, whereas absolute density estimates are not. The Baermann funnel approach nonetheless performed adequately for relative community comparisons and remains practical for laboratories with limited centrifuge capacity. Standardisation recommendations are discussed.

title: Plant-parasitic nematodes associated with sunflower production in Vojvodina: occurrence and community composition
abstract: A survey of plant-parasitic nematode (PPN) genera in sunflower-growing soils was conducted across 42 commercial fields distributed throughout the Vojvodina region during 2014. A total of 19 PPN genera were recorded, with Pratylenchus, Tylenchorhynchus, and Helicotylenchus being most prevalent. Pratylenchus was detected in 88% of sampled fields with densities ranging from 12 to 347 individuals per 100 g dry soil. Fields in Bačka had higher PPN richness than those in Banat, a pattern partially explained by soil texture differences. The PPI was positively correlated with preceding crop history involving soybean monoculture. Correlation analyses indicated no strong relationship between PPN abundance and current-season yield data, though fields exceeding 200 Pratylenchus individuals per 100 g showed a non-significant trend of lower head diameter. Management implications and threshold discussions are included.

title: Nematode community indices as soil quality indicators in agricultural systems of the Pannonian Plain: a review of regional studies
abstract: This book chapter synthesises findings from approximately 25 published and grey-literature studies on soil nematode communities conducted in the Pannonian Plain region — covering Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia — over the period 2000–2017. The chapter evaluates the performance of eight widely used nematode community indices (MI, PPI, EI, CI, SI, Shannon H′, Nematode Channel Ratio, and PPI/MI ratio) across contrasting land-use types including conventional arable farming, organic farming, pasture, and floodplain forest. Regional calibration data are presented for each index on chernozem and fluvisol soil types. Consistent patterns include: MI is highest in undisturbed or low-intensity systems; EI responds sensitively to nitrogen enrichment; and the CI correlates with soil organic carbon across multiple datasets. The chapter identifies gaps in seasonal sampling coverage and the scarcity of molecular-based studies in the region as priorities for future work.

title: Land-use intensity gradient structuring nematode assemblages across a Vojvodina landscape: from organic smallholdings to industrial monocultures
abstract: Sixteen sites were selected to represent a continuous gradient of land-use intensity (LUI) in the Bačka landscape, ranging from certified organic smallholdings through conventional mixed farms to large-scale maize monocultures. LUI was quantified using a composite index based on pesticide application frequency, mineral fertiliser nitrogen dose, tillage depth, and irrigation frequency. Nematode assemblages were sampled in two seasons. Redundancy analysis showed that LUI explained 41% of nematode community variance. Omnivore and predator proportions declined monotonically with increasing LUI (Spearman ρ = −0.84 and −0.79). The Structural Index showed a threshold response, declining sharply above LUI scores corresponding to more than 90 kg N ha⁻¹ and more than two pesticide applications per season. These threshold patterns could inform the design of agri-environment scheme criteria for rewarding practices that maintain complex soil food webs.

title: Temporal stability of nematode community indices under contrasting crop rotation systems in Vojvodina: a four-year monitoring dataset
abstract: Soil nematode assemblages were monitored over four consecutive years (2018–2021) in six experimental plots representing three crop rotation systems: maize monoculture, two-year maize–soybean rotation, and four-year maize–soybean–wheat–sunflower rotation. Samples were collected each autumn before harvest. The four-year rotation system showed the most stable MI values across years (coefficient of variation 8.4%), while monoculture plots showed greater interannual fluctuation (CV 19.7%). Shannon genus diversity was consistently highest in the four-year rotation by year three. Pratylenchus densities were significantly lower in both rotation treatments compared with monoculture from year two onward. Year-to-year variation in precipitation explained a significant proportion of abundance fluctuations across all treatments, underlining the importance of multi-year datasets for detecting management effects above climatic noise. Raw abundance data by genus are provided as supplementary tables.

title: Soil nematode communities under cover crops in Vojvodina winter wheat systems: effects of species selection and termination method
abstract: Cover crop trials were established at two sites in Srem to test whether cover crop species selection (phacelia, winter vetch, and oilseed radish) and termination method (mechanical incorporation vs. herbicide kill) influence soil nematode assemblages in subsequent winter wheat. Samples were collected at three points: pre-sowing, tillering, and post-harvest. Cover crop plots had higher total nematode abundance (+28% on average) and higher Channel Index values at the tillering stage compared with bare fallow controls, indicating greater fungal-pathway activity. Termination method had no significant effect on nematode community structure after three months, contrary to the hypothesis that herbicide residues would suppress bacterivores. Fungivore abundance was highest following oilseed radish, which produced the greatest aboveground biomass. Results from both sites were broadly consistent despite different soil textures (loam vs. sandy loam).

title: Flux-Linkage Characterisation of a 6/4 Switched Reluctance Motor Using Static Finite-Element Measurements
abstract: Accurate magnetic models are a prerequisite for current-profiling controllers designed to reduce torque ripple in switched reluctance motors (SRMs). This paper presents a systematic procedure for extracting the nonlinear flux-linkage versus rotor-position versus current surface of a three-phase 6/4 SRM rated at 1.5 kW. Two-dimensional transient finite-element simulations were performed in ANSYS Maxwell at 360 rotor positions and 15 current levels spanning 0–25 A, yielding a 5400-point data matrix. Simulated flux-linkage values were compared with locked-rotor measurements on a laboratory prototype; the mean absolute error across the full operating range was 2.7%. The resulting look-up table was compressed using a piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation scheme that reduced memory footprint by 63% while keeping reconstruction error below 1.5%. The calibrated model served as the basis for subsequent static torque profile extraction and is shared as supplementary data. The work also discusses sensitivity of the flux-linkage surface to lamination stack length tolerances observed in the manufactured core.

title: Effect of Switching Angle Variation on Torque Ripple in a 6/4 SRM Under Hysteresis Current Control
abstract: This study investigates how the selection of turn-on and turn-off angles affects the torque-ripple coefficient of a 6/4 switched reluctance motor operating under fixed-band hysteresis current control at speeds between 500 rpm and 2500 rpm. Experiments were conducted on a 1.5 kW test bench equipped with a torque transducer and a resolver, with a dSPACE DS1104 board implementing the controller. Turn-on angle was swept from 0° to 15° ahead of the unaligned position in steps of 1°, and turn-off angle was swept symmetrically. At 1000 rpm and a reference current of 18 A, optimal switching angles reduced peak-to-peak torque ripple from 87% to 41% of mean torque compared with the manufacturer's default angles. The improvement degraded above 2000 rpm as back-EMF limited current rise, and a speed-dependent angle scheduling table is proposed. Results are consistent with simulation predictions from the calibrated FE model reported in earlier work.

title: Current Profiling for Torque-Ripple Reduction in Switched Reluctance Drives: A Comparative Survey of Optimisation Methods
abstract: Current profiling—assigning a position-dependent reference current to each phase so that their individual torque contributions sum to a smooth total—has been pursued through a range of optimisation formulations since the late 1980s. This book chapter surveys and categorises these methods into three groups: analytic torque-sharing-function approaches, numeric constrained-optimisation approaches, and learning-based approaches. For each category the chapter discusses the mathematical formulation, the data requirements from the motor model, the computational cost at design time versus online, and the sensitivity to modelling errors. Representative numerical examples drawn from published literature and from the authors' own 6/4 and 8/6 SRM data illustrate trade-offs. Copper-loss penalty terms and their effect on efficiency across the torque-speed plane are examined separately. The chapter concludes with a discussion of implementation constraints on embedded processors and rapid-prototyping platforms, and identifies conditions under which simpler fixed torque-sharing functions remain competitive with numerically optimal profiles.

title: Influence of Current Controller Bandwidth on Torque-Ripple Reduction Effectiveness in Switched Reluctance Motor Drives
abstract: Current-profiling controllers rely on accurate tracking of position-dependent current references; if the current controller bandwidth is insufficient, reference tracking errors introduce additional torque ripple that partially or fully cancels the intended reduction. This paper quantifies the relationship between PI hysteresis-band settings, asymmetric H-bridge switching frequency, DC-link voltage, and the residual torque ripple when a TSF-based reference profile is applied to a 7.5 kW 8/6 SRM. A describing-function approach is used to estimate the effective bandwidth of the hysteresis current loop as a function of rotor speed, phase inductance, and hysteresis band width. Predictions were verified against dynamometer measurements at 600, 1200, and 1800 rpm. Results show that torque-ripple coefficient rises from 18% to 34% when bus voltage is halved from 540 V to 270 V at 1800 rpm, because current slew rate limitation prevents profile tracking near commutation. Practical guidelines for minimum DC-link voltage and maximum hysteresis band are derived as functions of speed and load torque.

title: Effect of Lamination Material Grade on Finite-Element-Predicted Torque Ripple in Switched Reluctance Motors: A Sensitivity Study
abstract: Finite-element models of switched reluctance motors are typically calibrated with the B–H curve supplied by the steel manufacturer, yet actual lamination properties vary between production batches. This paper quantifies how uncertainty in the B–H curve propagates to uncertainty in the predicted static torque surface and, consequently, to the torque-ripple coefficient achieved by an optimised torque-sharing function controller. Three lamination grades (M270-35A, M330-35A, and M400-50A) representing the spread commonly encountered in prototype manufacturing are modelled in ANSYS Maxwell for the 8/6 SRM geometry. Monte Carlo sampling (500 runs) with ±5% perturbation of the B–H curve at each of 20 field-strength points is used to build confidence intervals on the torque surface. Results show that a TSF designed for M270-35A degrades from a 19% to a 27% torque-ripple coefficient when the motor is actually wound with M400-50A laminations, without re-calibration. A practical re-calibration procedure requiring only three steady-state current measurements is proposed and validated experimentally.

title: A Fuzzy AHP Approach to Supplier Selection in the Serbian Flour Milling Industry
abstract: This paper applies a fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) to the problem of wheat supplier selection for flour milling companies in Vojvodina, Serbia. The study collected pairwise comparison judgements from procurement managers at four milling enterprises and structured the evaluation around seven criteria: price stability, delivery reliability, grain quality certification, proximity, financial stability, flexibility, and environmental compliance. Triangular fuzzy numbers were used to capture linguistic uncertainty in expert assessments. The model was validated by comparing its ranking output with the actual supplier choices made by the firms over a two-year period. Results showed that delivery reliability and quality certification were the dominant criteria, together accounting for approximately 48% of the aggregate weight. The fuzzy rankings matched historical choices in 14 out of 17 documented procurement decisions, suggesting reasonable predictive validity. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that the ranking of the top two suppliers was stable across a wide range of weight perturbations.

title: Integrating TOPSIS and Rough Set Theory for Sustainable Supplier Assessment in Dairy Supply Chains
abstract: The dairy sector in Central and Eastern Europe faces increasing pressure to incorporate sustainability metrics into procurement decisions, yet practical tools for doing so under uncertain data conditions remain scarce. This study combines rough set theory (RST) for attribute reduction with the TOPSIS method for final ranking, applied to a sample of nine milk collection suppliers serving two dairy cooperatives in Serbia and one in Hungary. The attribute set initially comprised 14 criteria spanning economic, environmental, and social dimensions; RST-based reduct computation reduced this to seven essential attributes without significant information loss, as measured by classification accuracy. The combined RST-TOPSIS approach was benchmarked against standalone TOPSIS on the full attribute set. Rankings diverged notably for middle-ranked suppliers, suggesting that attribute redundancy can distort assessments when criteria are not pre-filtered. The findings have practical implications for procurement officers working with heterogeneous and partially missing supplier datasets.

title: A Hesitant Fuzzy Linguistic VIKOR Model for Cold-Chain Supplier Selection in the Meat Processing Sector
abstract: Cold-chain integrity is a critical risk factor in meat supply chains, yet supplier selection models rarely incorporate cold-chain performance attributes explicitly. This paper proposes a decision model based on hesitant fuzzy linguistic term sets (HFLTS) and the VIKOR compromise-ranking method. The model was applied to a real procurement decision at a pork processing plant in Vojvodina, where a panel of five decision-makers evaluated six refrigerated transport providers against ten criteria, including pre-cooling time compliance, temperature exceedance frequency, vehicle hygiene audit scores, and response time to breakdown events. HFLTS accommodated disagreement among decision-makers without forcing artificial consensus. The VIKOR ranking identified one supplier as the best compromise solution with a Q-value of 0.08, well below the acceptable threshold. The paper further tests the model's robustness by varying the compromise coefficient ν from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.1 and reports that the top-two ranking remained stable throughout.

title: Evaluating the Traceability Capabilities of Agri-food Suppliers Using an Interval-Valued Intuitionistic Fuzzy MCDM Framework
abstract: Regulatory and consumer-driven demands for food traceability have made traceability capability an increasingly prominent criterion in supplier evaluation. However, it is a composite, hard-to-quantify attribute that resists simple numerical scoring. This paper develops a supplier assessment framework using interval-valued intuitionistic fuzzy sets (IVIFS) to represent the epistemic uncertainty associated with traceability scoring, combined with the EDAS (Evaluation based on Distance from Average Solution) method for final ranking. The framework is applied to ten fresh fruit and vegetable suppliers assessed by a procurement committee at a retail distribution cooperative in Vojvodina. Traceability was decomposed into five sub-criteria: lot identification coverage, recall response time, digital documentation availability, third-party audit frequency, and farm-level record completeness. The IVIFS-EDAS results are compared with a crisp weighted-sum benchmark. The model identified three suppliers with traceability profiles substantially below the portfolio average, a finding that the crisp model had partially masked through averaging effects.

title: Incorporating Carbon Footprint Constraints into Fuzzy Multi-Objective Supplier Selection for a Vegetable Processing Cooperative
abstract: This paper formulates a fuzzy multi-objective linear programming (FMOLP) model for supplier order allocation that simultaneously minimises total procurement cost, delivery lead time, and carbon footprint of inbound logistics, subject to demand fulfilment and capacity constraints. The model is applied to a vegetable processing cooperative in the Banat region that sources peppers, tomatoes, and cabbage from twelve regional growers. Carbon footprint estimates per tonne-kilometre were derived from transport mode data and distance records. Fuzzy goals and fuzzy constraints were handled using the Zimmermann max-min operator. The Pareto-optimal solution surface was mapped for cost versus carbon trade-offs, revealing that a 12% reduction in carbon footprint could be achieved at a cost increase of approximately 4.7% under the best-case logistics configuration. The model was implemented in MATLAB and run on historical procurement data from two consecutive seasons.

title: Dynamic Supplier Performance Monitoring in Agri-food Chains Using a Time-Series Extended MCDM Approach
abstract: Most MCDM-based supplier evaluation models produce a static snapshot ranking, which may be inadequate for agri-food procurement contexts where supplier performance fluctuates seasonally and in response to climate events. This paper proposes a time-extended MCDM framework that combines a dynamic weighting mechanism—updating criterion weights quarterly based on procurement manager re-assessments—with a rolling TOPSIS score computed over a twelve-quarter moving window. The method is demonstrated using longitudinal procurement data from a sunflower oil producer in Vojvodina, covering 2020–2024 and involving seven active suppliers. The rolling scores reveal that two suppliers whose static three-year average ranks appeared stable actually underwent pronounced but temporally offset performance cycles. The paper also proposes a supplier alert threshold based on the rate of change of TOPSIS scores, flagging suppliers whose rolling rank drops by more than two positions across two consecutive quarters.

title: Fiscal Consolidation Announcements and Short-Run Spread Responses: Event Study Evidence from Serbia 2009–2013
abstract: This paper applies event study methodology to seventeen discrete fiscal policy announcements made by Serbian government authorities between 2009 and 2013—including austerity packages, IMF Stand-By Agreement milestones, and budget revision disclosures—to estimate their short-run impact on the spread between Serbian government Eurobonds and equivalent-maturity German Bunds. Abnormal spread changes are computed over a three-day window around each event using a GARCH(1,1) baseline model estimated on the preceding 120 trading days. Consolidation announcements tied to IMF programme benchmarks reduce spreads by an average of 22 basis points within three days, while domestically initiated austerity announcements produce a smaller and less statistically reliable reduction of 9 basis points. Failed parliamentary votes on budget amendments are associated with spread increases of up to 45 basis points. The asymmetry between IMF-anchored and domestically anchored signals is interpreted as a fiscal credibility discount applied by investors to sovereign commitments lacking an external enforcement mechanism.

title: Long-Run Fiscal Sustainability and the Spread–Debt Nexus: Panel Cointegration Tests for Six Western Balkan Economies
abstract: This study tests for a long-run cointegrating relationship between sovereign yield spreads, public debt-to-GDP ratios, and primary fiscal balances in six Western Balkan economies using annual data from 1998 to 2014. Panel unit root tests (Im–Pesaran–Shin and LLC) confirm that all series are I(1). Pedroni and Westerlund panel cointegration tests are applied, and fully modified OLS (FMOLS) and dynamic OLS (DOLS) estimators provide long-run coefficients. Results show a cointegrating vector is present for the full panel, with the long-run semi-elasticity of spreads with respect to the debt ratio estimated at 4.1 basis points per percentage point of GDP. The primary balance enters with the expected negative sign and a coefficient roughly twice the size found in comparable Central European panels. Error correction speeds suggest deviations from the long-run equilibrium are corrected at a rate of approximately 28 percent per year, indicating that spread adjustments are sluggish and that short-term fiscal signals may be systematically underpriced.

title: Fiscal Rules and Credibility Signals in EU Accession Candidates: Do Formal Commitments Reduce Yield Premia?
abstract: This paper investigates whether the adoption and formal operationalisation of fiscal rules—balanced budget rules, debt brakes, and expenditure ceilings—by EU accession candidates in the Western Balkans reduces sovereign yield spreads beyond what macroeconomic fundamentals predict. A difference-in-differences design compares spread trajectories before and after fiscal rule adoption for Albania (2016), Serbia (2015 amendment to the Budget System Law), and North Macedonia (2014 fiscal responsibility law), using a control group of non-adopting comparators. The analysis uses monthly Bloomberg data on secondary market yields and a composite fiscal rule index constructed from IMF Fiscal Rules Dataset entries supplemented by national legislative texts. Results indicate a statistically significant average treatment effect of −31 basis points in the eighteen months following rule adoption, concentrated in medium-term maturities. The effect is larger for rules backed by independent monitoring bodies. Rules without enforcement mechanisms are not associated with significant spread reductions.

title: Investor Base Composition and Yield Volatility in Serbian Government Bond Auctions, 2010–2018
abstract: This paper examines how changes in the composition of the investor base at Serbian Ministry of Finance primary auctions affected yield volatility over the period 2010–2018. Auction-level data provided under a research agreement with the Public Debt Administration of Serbia record bid-to-cover ratios, accepted and marginal yields, and broad investor category shares (domestic banks, domestic non-banks, and foreign investors) for 186 auctions of two-, five-, and seven-year dinar-denominated bonds. A GARCH-X model incorporates investor share variables as exogenous regressors in the variance equation. A ten-percentage-point increase in the foreign investor share is associated with a statistically significant increase in yield volatility at the auction of 8.3 basis points, controlling for global risk proxies. Domestic bank participation, by contrast, exerts a stabilising effect on auction yields, consistent with the captive-buyer hypothesis. Implications for the debt management office's pre-auction communication strategy are discussed.

title: Euroisation and Sovereign Spread Dynamics in Montenegro: Before and After the 2006 Independence
abstract: Montenegro unilaterally adopted the euro in 2002, well before EU accession negotiations began, making it an unusual laboratory for studying how full dollarisation/euroisation affects sovereign borrowing costs in the absence of EU institutional membership. This paper assembles a quarterly dataset on Montenegrin sovereign and quasi-sovereign borrowing costs from 2002 to 2020, combining Ministry of Finance loan agreement records, Eurobond prospectuses, and EBRD project financing terms. A structural break test confirms a significant reduction in the risk premium following independence in 2006 and a second structural break during the 2008–2009 crisis. A VECM framework relates spreads to fiscal variables and a synthetic eurozone periphery stress index. The absence of monetary policy autonomy under euroisation constrains fiscal flexibility and amplifies spread responses to external shocks by an estimated 15–22 percent relative to a counterfactual managed float calibrated from comparator economies.

title: Green Bond Issuance Potential in Western Balkan Sovereigns: A Spread Premium or Discount?
abstract: This conference paper presents preliminary evidence on whether Western Balkan sovereign issuers could access a greenium—a yield discount relative to conventional bonds of equivalent maturity and credit quality—if they were to issue labelled green bonds. The analysis proceeds in two steps. First, the paper surveys the existing literature on sovereign greenium estimates for emerging and frontier markets, identifying a range of −2 to −14 basis points across 23 studies reviewed. Second, it constructs a structural model of the conditions under which a greenium is likely to materialise, applying the model's parameters to available fiscal, institutional, and capital market depth indicators for Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. The conclusion is that greenium access is plausible for Serbia given recent improvements in its public debt management framework, but that Albania and Bosnia and Herzegovina would require prior development of domestic institutional investor bases and credible green expenditure frameworks before a greenium would be achievable.

title: Does IMF Programme Compliance Reduce Sovereign Borrowing Costs? Micro-Evidence from Programme Reviews
abstract: This paper exploits the within-programme variation in IMF review outcomes—waivers, delays, and clean passes—across twelve Western Balkan programme episodes from 2000 to 2022 to estimate the causal effect of compliance signals on secondary market spreads. A high-frequency event study around the publication dates of completed review documents is combined with a panel local projection framework using monthly data. Clean completion of programme reviews reduces spreads by an average of 18 basis points in the month of publication, while waiver requests are associated with a statistically insignificant spread increase of 7 basis points. Review delays lasting more than ninety days are associated with a significant spread widening of 28–34 basis points. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the spread-reducing effect of clean reviews is three times larger for economies with debt-to-GDP above 60 percent, suggesting that IMF credibility substitution is most valuable precisely when fiscal space is most constrained.

title: Fiscal Credibility Under Coalition Governments: Political Fragmentation and Sovereign Risk Premia in the Western Balkans
abstract: This paper introduces a political fragmentation index constructed from parliamentary seat distributions to test whether government coalition breadth and durability affect sovereign yield spreads independently of fiscal outcomes. The dataset covers quarterly observations for six Western Balkan economies from 2002 to 2023. The fragmentation index, computed as the effective number of governing parties weighted by seat share, is added to a benchmark spread model that controls for debt, fiscal balance, growth, and external sector variables. A one-unit increase in the fragmentation index—roughly equivalent to moving from a two-party to a three-party coalition—is associated with a spread premium of 14 basis points after conditioning on fundamentals. The effect is stronger in election years and in countries with weaker fiscal rule frameworks. Robustness checks use alternative political risk proxies from the PRS Group's International Country Risk Guide and Polity V scores.

title: Spread Compression and Financial Integration: Are Western Balkan Sovereign Markets Converging Toward EU Benchmarks?
abstract: This paper tests for sigma and beta convergence in sovereign yield spreads between Western Balkan economies and a weighted EU benchmark constructed from spreads of Bulgaria, Croatia, and Romania in the years before their respective EU accessions. Monthly Bloomberg data from 2004 to 2025 are used for Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro. Sigma convergence is assessed through rolling cross-sectional standard deviation, which shows a general downward trend interrupted by the 2008–2009 crisis, the 2011–2012 Eurozone stress, and the 2020 COVID shock. Beta convergence regressions confirm that economies with initially high spreads converged faster over 2004–2015 but that convergence slowed markedly after 2016 and is no longer statistically detectable for Bosnia and Herzegovina. Decomposition using the Oaxaca–Blinder approach attributes roughly 60 percent of remaining spread differentials to institutional quality gaps rather than fiscal fundamentals.

title: Time study and cycle time variability in a precast concrete panel line: a case from a Serbian manufacturer
abstract: This paper presents a detailed time-study analysis conducted on a single precast concrete panel production line at a mid-sized Serbian manufacturer over a 14-week observation period. A structured work-sampling protocol captured 1,840 individual activity records covering mould preparation, reinforcement placement, casting, curing, and demoulding. Cycle time variability was found to be highest at the reinforcement stage, with a coefficient of variation of 0.41, compared to 0.12 for casting. Statistical process control charts identified three recurring assignable causes linked to mould wear and steel supply inconsistency. The study establishes baseline performance metrics—average takt time of 47 minutes per panel, overall equipment effectiveness of 64%—that form the input for subsequent value-stream and costing analyses. The results suggest that targeted standardisation at the reinforcement station could reduce average cycle time by approximately 18% without capital investment.

title: Time-driven activity-based costing in precast concrete manufacturing: model development and validation
abstract: This article describes the construction and empirical validation of a time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) model for a precast concrete manufacturer producing five product families—columns, beams, slabs, staircases, and wall panels. Capacity cost rates were derived from 26 resource pools using 18 months of payroll, energy, and maintenance records. Time equations were parameterised from 312 hours of direct observation across all five product lines. Model output was validated against actual job-costing records for 84 production orders; average deviation was 4.7%, with the largest discrepancy (9.2%) occurring for non-standard staircase geometries. Sensitivity analysis showed that casting-floor utilisation rate and reinforcement steel price are the two dominant cost drivers. The TDABC model correctly identified that wall panels, despite their high volume, carried a negative contribution margin under existing pricing, a finding confirmed by subsequent management review.

title: Bottleneck detection methods in batch-variable manufacturing: a comparative review with application to construction component lines
abstract: This book chapter reviews five quantitative bottleneck detection methods—active period method, utilisation-based identification, throughput degradation analysis, shifting bottleneck heuristic, and simulation-based sensitivity analysis—and evaluates their applicability to batch-variable production systems typical of the precast construction component industry. Unlike high-volume repetitive manufacturing, precast lines switch between product families with significantly different processing times and mould requirements, which causes the bottleneck resource to shift across families. The chapter first provides a structured taxonomy of the methods based on data requirements, computational complexity, and real-time applicability. It then applies three of the methods to an illustrative production dataset from a 12-week campaign at a concrete product manufacturer in Vojvodina, Serbia, and compares the resulting bottleneck diagnoses. Practical guidance is given for practitioners choosing among methods under data scarcity conditions common in small and medium manufacturing enterprises.

title: Discrete-event simulation of a precast concrete production line under demand variability
abstract: A discrete-event simulation model was built in Arena 15 to represent a three-line precast production facility producing beams and columns for civil infrastructure projects. The model incorporated stochastic inter-arrival demand patterns derived from 24 months of historical order data, fitted to a negative binomial distribution (p = 0.31, r = 4.2). Four operational policies—fixed batch sizes, demand-driven batching, overtime scheduling, and mould-pool expansion—were tested under low, medium, and high demand scenarios across 30 replications each. Simulation results showed that demand-driven batching reduced average work-in-process inventory by 28% relative to fixed batching under high-demand conditions, at the cost of a 6% increase in mould changeover frequency. Overtime scheduling outperformed mould-pool expansion in cost terms for demand surges lasting fewer than six consecutive weeks. The model is parameterised to allow direct import of production calendar data.

title: Lean implementation barriers in small precast concrete manufacturers in the Western Balkans: an exploratory survey
abstract: An online survey targeting production managers and owners of precast and prestressed concrete product companies was administered across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Croatia. Sixty-one usable responses were received from companies with 10–250 employees. Respondents rated 22 potential lean implementation barriers on a five-point Likert scale. Factor analysis with varimax rotation yielded four barrier constructs: workforce resistance and training gaps (factor loading 0.74–0.81), management commitment deficits (0.68–0.77), measurement system inadequacy (0.61–0.70), and seasonal demand volatility (0.58–0.65). Seasonal demand volatility was ranked most severely inhibiting by companies producing for open-market housing, while measurement system inadequacy dominated responses from companies supplying infrastructure contracts. The findings suggest that lean adoption programmes designed for high-volume repetitive industries need substantial adaptation before being applicable to the regional precast sector.

title: Mould utilisation rate as a production planning parameter in batch-variable precast lines
abstract: Mould availability is a principal capacity constraint in precast concrete manufacturing but is often managed by informal rules of thumb rather than quantitative planning. This paper formalises mould utilisation rate (MUR) as a planning parameter and derives analytical expressions for MUR as a function of batch size, changeover duration, curing time, and product mix. Data from production logs at three facilities covering 6,400 production orders over two years were used to calibrate the model and estimate distribution parameters for stochastic changeover times. Simulation experiments showed that MUR drops below 55% when product-mix entropy—measured by the Shannon index of order variety—exceeds 1.8 bits, identifying a practical threshold for triggering mould investment decisions. A spreadsheet decision-support tool implementing the model was developed and piloted at one facility, reducing planned mould idle time by 14% over a three-month trial.

title: Integrating value-stream mapping and simulation to evaluate changeover reduction in a precast staircase line
abstract: This paper combines VSM and discrete-event simulation to assess the effect of single-minute exchange of die (SMED) principles applied to adjustable-geometry staircase moulds at a precast manufacturer in Vojvodina. The current-state VSM recorded average changeover time of 94 minutes with a standard deviation of 31 minutes across 76 observed changeovers. SMED analysis separated internal from external activities and identified that 42% of changeover time involved tasks executable offline. A reduced-changeover scenario with a target of 55 minutes was modelled in simulation, and 1,000 replications estimated a throughput increase of 11.4% (95% CI: 9.8–13.1%) for the staircase family. Cost implications were evaluated using the site's TDABC model, showing a reduction of €4.20 per unit in changeover-allocated overhead. An implementation roadmap with 11 actions, estimated durations, and responsibility assignments was provided to the company.

title: Cost allocation accuracy in multi-product precast facilities: comparing traditional job costing, TDABC, and machine-learning cost prediction
abstract: Three cost allocation approaches were compared on a dataset of 2,114 completed production orders from a precast facility producing eight product families over three years. Traditional job costing used three cost pools; the TDABC model used 24 resource pools with 41 time equations; a gradient-boosted regression tree (GBRT) was trained on 38 operational features including order size, geometry class, reinforcement density, and scheduling position. Holdout test performance was assessed over the most recent six months of data. Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 12.4% for traditional costing, 5.1% for TDABC, and 3.8% for GBRT. However, GBRT offered no interpretable cost driver structure, limiting its use for managerial decision-making. A hybrid approach is proposed in which TDABC provides the structural model and GBRT residuals flag orders warranting manual cost review. The threshold rule reducing review workload by 67% while catching 89% of high-deviation orders is described.

title: Production flow analysis in a prefabricated modular building component factory: lessons from a greenfield case
abstract: As demand for modular off-site construction grows in Central and Eastern Europe, new factories are being designed from greenfield to produce volumetric concrete modules. This paper documents a production flow analysis conducted during the ramp-up phase of a newly established modular building component facility near Novi Sad, where the authors had access to design documents, equipment commissioning data, and eight months of operational records. Flow analysis using process activity mapping and load-distance charts revealed that the initial layout generated an unnecessary 340-metre average travel distance per module through the finishing and inspection zone. Three layout alternatives were evaluated using a weighted scoring model covering material flow distance, future expansion flexibility, and investment cost. The recommended alternative reduced travel distance by 44% and was implemented during a scheduled summer maintenance shutdown. Post-implementation measurement confirmed a 38% reduction, close to the projected figure.

title: Quantifying the cost of schedule disruptions in precast concrete supply chains caused by construction site delays
abstract: Precast manufacturers are particularly exposed to schedule disruptions because finished elements cannot be stored indefinitely without risk of damage and occupy significant yard space. This study quantifies the cost consequences of site-side delivery postponements using order-level data from two precast suppliers over 28 months. A total of 614 postponement events were recorded, with an average delay duration of 8.3 days and a maximum of 47 days. Costs were decomposed into yard storage, remobilisation of casting resources, and re-sequencing overhead using the existing TDABC models at each facility. Average disruption cost per postponed order was €1,140, equivalent to 9.3% of mean order revenue. Regression analysis showed that order volume, product family complexity, and seasonal period were significant predictors (R² = 0.61). The paper proposes a simple penalty-clause calibration framework for use in supply contracts between precast manufacturers and construction clients.

title: Moisture accumulation in nineteenth-century brick walls of Vojvodina manor houses: a field measurement campaign
abstract: Solid brick walls in late nineteenth-century manor houses of the Vojvodina plain were instrumented with embedded temperature and relative-humidity sensors at three depths to track seasonal moisture cycling over two consecutive heating seasons (2007–2009). Twelve wall cross-sections in six buildings were monitored, covering walls with and without existing lime-render internal finishes. Measured winter wall-core relative humidity regularly exceeded 85 % in unheated structures and reached condensation conditions at the inner render interface in four cases. Gravimetric samples taken in spring confirmed water content increases of 1.2–2.8 kg/m³ above summer baseline values. The data reveal that current national energy-code assumptions underestimate winter moisture loads in unheated or intermittently heated heritage structures by a factor of roughly 1.5. The study provides a baseline dataset for subsequent HAM model calibration and highlights the need for climate-appropriate envelope interventions that account for intermittent occupancy patterns typical of rural heritage buildings in the region.

title: Calibration of a one-dimensional HAM model against in-situ wall measurements in Vojvodina heritage buildings
abstract: A one-dimensional coupled heat, air, and moisture (HAM) transfer model was calibrated using the two-year field dataset collected in Vojvodina manor houses. Material property inputs—thermal conductivity, water vapour diffusion resistance factor (μ), and moisture storage function—were determined from laboratory specimens cut from original brickwork and lime mortar, using the dry-cup, wet-cup, and sorption isotherm methods respectively. The calibration procedure minimised root-mean-square errors between simulated and measured temperature and relative humidity at sensor depths; final RMSE values were 0.4 °C and 3.1 % RH for the best-performing wall cross-section. Sensitivity analysis showed that the moisture storage function of mortar joints, which represents roughly 18 % of the wall area, was the dominant source of simulation uncertainty. The calibrated model is used as a reference tool in subsequent parametric studies of internal insulation variants presented by the research group.

title: Comparative assessment of calcium silicate board and mineral wool slab as internal insulation for historic brick walls
abstract: Two widely used internal insulation systems—12 cm mineral wool slab with a polyethylene vapour barrier and 8 cm calcium silicate board bonded directly to the masonry—were evaluated using calibrated HAM simulation for a 51 cm solid brick wall representative of Vojvodina residential buildings. Simulations were run over ten consecutive climate years using a synthesised Novi Sad reference year based on 1981–2010 meteorological records. The mineral wool system kept the existing wall at lower moisture contents in steady state but showed condensation at the insulation–brick interface in six of ten simulated years, with peak accumulated moisture of 0.18 kg/m² in February. The calcium silicate board, acting as a moisture buffer without a discrete vapour barrier, redistributed moisture more evenly and showed no liquid condensation accumulation exceeding 0.05 kg/m² in any year. Drying potential in summer was adequate for both systems when indoor vapour production was held at typical residential levels. Results are presented as monthly moisture content profiles and annual balance plots.
