title: Template-Based Generation of AUTOSAR RTE Stubs from Port Interface Models
abstract: Runtime Environment (RTE) stub generation is a recurring manual effort in AUTOSAR development workflows. This work describes a model-to-text pipeline in which Xpand templates consume an Ecore-based port-interface model and produce syntactically correct RTE stub files for AUTOSAR Classic Platform 4.0. The pipeline was evaluated on three representative Electronic Control Unit (ECU) designs—a door-control unit, a seat-adjustment module, and a battery-management interface—together comprising 67 port interfaces and 112 runnables. Generation time averaged 1.4 seconds per ECU on a standard workstation. Generated stubs were compiled without modification using a commercial compiler suite and passed static analysis with no MISRA-C:2004 violations in 94% of cases; the remaining 6% required minor pointer-cast annotations. Manual effort for stub authoring was reduced from approximately four person-hours to under fifteen minutes per ECU, as measured in a controlled comparison with two experienced engineers.

title: A Comparative Study of ATL and QVT-O for AUTOSAR Model Transformations
abstract: Model transformation language choice affects both the maintainability and execution performance of AUTOSAR toolchains. This study provides a systematic comparison of ATL and QVT-O for five representative AUTOSAR transformation tasks: SWC flattening, port interface normalisation, timing-model extraction, signal grouping, and ECU topology migration. Each transformation was implemented independently in both languages by two engineers with comparable experience. Metrics collected include lines of code, transformation execution time on models of three size classes (small: up to 50 elements, medium: 50–500, large: 500–5 000), and the number of defects found during a structured review. ATL required 18% fewer lines of code on average across the five tasks, while QVT-O executed 23% faster on large models. Defect counts were statistically indistinguishable. The paper provides a decision framework that maps transformation characteristics to language choice and discusses tooling maturity considerations relevant to industrial adoption.

title: Integration of AUTOSAR Toolchains with Continuous Integration Pipelines Using ARXML Diffing
abstract: Applying continuous integration (CI) practices to AUTOSAR-based projects is hampered by the fact that ARXML files are large, schema-structured XML documents for which standard textual diff tools produce uninformative output. This paper presents an ARXML-aware diff and merge utility, ArxmlCI, that operates at the metamodel level, representing changes as typed edit operations on model elements rather than text lines. The utility was integrated into a Jenkins-based CI pipeline and evaluated on a series of 180 commits drawn from three development branches of an internal ECU project maintained over six months. ArxmlCI correctly attributed 97.2% of change operations to their originating model element; textual diff attributed 61.4% correctly for the same commits. Merge conflict rates dropped from 34% to 9% of multi-author commits after adoption. The paper also describes a lightweight conflict resolution protocol for common AUTOSAR-specific patterns such as concurrent SWC interface modifications.

title: Generating AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Service Instance Manifests from Service Architecture Models
abstract: AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform introduces Service Instance Manifests (SIMs) that describe deployment-time binding of services to network endpoints. Authoring SIMs manually is error-prone because their content must be consistent with service interface definitions spread across multiple ARXML packages. This paper proposes a model-driven workflow in which a lightweight service architecture model, defined using a purpose-built metamodel, drives the generation of SIMs via Acceleo templates. The metamodel captures service interfaces, required and provided ports, transport protocol bindings, and QoS parameters. A transformation validates referential consistency before generation. The workflow was tested on an experimental adaptive ECU cluster consisting of four Processing Units running AUTOSAR AP 18.10, with 11 service instances and three transport protocols. All 11 generated SIMs were accepted by the AP execution environment without manual correction. Generation added less than four seconds to the overall build cycle.

title: Model-Driven Engineering for Automotive Embedded Software: A Practitioner's Guide
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured treatment of MDE practice as applied to automotive embedded software, with AUTOSAR as the primary platform. It covers the spectrum from metamodel definition through transformation authoring to final artefact generation, and situates each activity within a typical automotive development V-model. The chapter draws on case material from three ECU development projects to illustrate how metamodel granularity choices affect toolchain complexity and traceability. It includes a worked example of a complete SWC-to-C code generation pipeline using Ecore, ATL, and Acceleo, with all intermediate artefacts described in detail. A section on toolchain validation discusses coverage criteria for transformation testing and introduces a mutation-based adequacy measure adapted to ATL rules. Intended for software engineers entering the automotive domain and for academics setting up MDE courses with industrial relevance.
venue: Advances in Embedded and Cyber-Physical Systems (edited volume, Springer Verlag Balkans)

title: A Transformation Chain for Migrating AUTOSAR Classic SWC Models to Adaptive Platform Service Skeletons
abstract: Migration from AUTOSAR Classic to Adaptive Platform is increasingly relevant as vehicle architectures shift toward high-performance compute nodes. This paper describes a three-step transformation chain that takes Classic SWC descriptions in ARXML 4.3 as input and produces Adaptive Platform service skeleton headers and SIMs conforming to AP 21.11. The first transformation normalises Classic port interfaces into a platform-independent intermediate model; the second maps the intermediate model to AP service interface definitions; the third generates C++ skeleton headers using Acceleo. Migration was applied to 38 SWCs from two body-domain ECU projects. Thirty-one SWCs migrated fully automatically; seven required manual completion of data type mappings that have no direct AP equivalent. The paper analyses the seven exceptions and proposes three extension points in the intermediate metamodel that would reduce manual effort in future migrations. Compilation of generated skeletons succeeded on an AP reference implementation without modifications.
venue: Proceedings of the European Conference on Software Architecture and Component Engineering

title: Measuring Transformation Coverage in ATL-Based AUTOSAR Toolchains
abstract: Testing ATL model transformations systematically is difficult because standard code-coverage criteria do not map directly onto ATL rule structures. This paper adapts four coverage criteria—rule coverage, binding coverage, lazy-rule invocation coverage, and guard predicate coverage—to ATL and implements them in a coverage measurement plug-in for Eclipse. The plug-in instruments transformation execution and produces coverage reports in a machine-readable format. The criteria were evaluated on five ATL transformations from an AUTOSAR toolchain ranging in size from 12 to 74 rules. A mutation testing experiment seeded 210 rule mutations across the five transformations; guard predicate coverage achieved the highest mutation detection rate at 78%, while rule coverage detected 49%. The paper also proposes a ranked test-suite augmentation procedure that adds model instances to improve coverage incrementally, and demonstrates its use on the largest of the five transformations.
venue: Journal of Systems and Software Engineering Practice

title: Integrating Large Language Model Assistance into ARXML Authoring: Scope and Limits
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed for various software engineering tasks, and practitioners have begun using them informally for ARXML editing. This paper reports an empirical study examining the practical limits of LLM assistance for three ARXML authoring tasks: SWC descriptor creation, communication matrix extension, and deployment configuration. Two open-weight models and one API-accessible proprietary model were evaluated using a structured prompt protocol on 30 task instances derived from an internal reference project. Correctness of generated ARXML was assessed against the AUTOSAR 4.4 schema and 43 semantic consistency rules. Schema validity rates ranged from 41% to 67% depending on model and task; semantic correctness rates were consistently lower, ranging from 28% to 54%. Errors concentrated in inter-file reference resolution and numeric constraint satisfaction. The paper concludes that LLM assistance is useful for scaffolding boilerplate but requires systematic post-generation validation, and proposes an integration architecture that wraps LLM output in the ArxmlCI consistency checker described in prior work.

title: Toolchain-Independent Representation of AUTOSAR Timing Constraints Using a Standardised Metamodel
abstract: Timing constraint specifications in AUTOSAR are expressed through the Timing Extensions (TIMEX) sub-schema, but the way authoring tools serialise TIMEX artefacts varies substantially, causing interoperability problems when exchanging models between organisations using different tools. This paper proposes a standardised intermediate metamodel for AUTOSAR timing constraints covering end-to-end latency constraints, synchronisation constraints, age constraints, and execution time annotations. Import adaptors were implemented for three commercial AUTOSAR authoring environments and validated on a set of 17 timing specifications of varying complexity collected from two automotive projects. The metamodel-normalised representations enabled automated comparison of semantically equivalent constraints authored in different tools; comparison detected four constraint semantics discrepancies that had gone unnoticed during manual review. An Acceleo-based exporter regenerates tool-specific ARXML from the normalised metamodel with measured round-trip fidelity of 98.6% across all constraint types.
venue: Embedded Systems Letters

title: Incremental Regeneration of AUTOSAR RTE Code Under Model Changes: A Change-Impact-Driven Approach
abstract: Full regeneration of AUTOSAR RTE code after each model change is time-consuming in large ECU projects; build cycles of 20–40 minutes are reported in practitioner surveys. This preprint presents an incremental regeneration strategy in which a change-impact analyser, operating on the AUTOSAR model graph, computes the minimal affected subset of RTE translation units before invoking code generators only for that subset. The impact analyser uses a dependency graph derived from the Ecore-based AUTOSAR metamodel and propagates change markers along typed dependency edges. The approach was prototyped for AUTOSAR 4.3 and evaluated on two ECU model snapshots with 54 and 121 SWCs respectively. For single-SWC modifications, regeneration time dropped from 23.4 minutes to 2.1 minutes (54-SWC case) and from 38.7 minutes to 3.6 minutes (121-SWC case). Full build correctness was confirmed by byte-level comparison of generated files with the results of reference full builds for all 90 tested change scenarios.

title: How Economic Crisis Coverage Shapes Audience Anxiety: A Framing Experiment with Serbian Television Viewers
abstract: This laboratory experiment exposed 180 undergraduate participants at the University of Novi Sad to three versions of a televised economic crisis report: a consequences frame, a responsibility frame, and a neutral procedural frame. Participants completed the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory before and after exposure, along with a media trust battery. The consequences frame produced the largest increase in state anxiety (Δ = 6.2 points on the STAI-S scale), while the responsibility frame led to the greatest drop in institutional trust scores (Δ = −0.8 on a five-point scale). A moderation analysis showed that participants who reported high baseline news consumption were less susceptible to anxiety induction. The experiment contributes to the framing effects literature by linking specific frame types to distinct affective and evaluative outcomes within a Central-South European context where crisis communication norms differ from Western European baselines.

title: Tabloidisation and Trust Decline: Longitudinal Evidence from Vojvodina, 2011–2014
abstract: Drawing on the first three annual waves of the Vojvodina Audience Panel (N = 897 respondents present in all three waves after attrition), this study tracks changes in perceived credibility of five regional and national outlets alongside independent coders' assessments of tabloidisation indicators in those same outlets. Tabloidisation was measured as the proportion of front-page coverage devoted to celebrities, crime, and sensational politics. A fixed-effects panel regression model shows that a 10-percentage-point increase in tabloidisation indicators in an outlet's front-page mix is associated with a 0.23-point decrease (p < 0.01) in mean credibility rating among readers who primarily rely on that outlet. The effect is stronger among respondents with university education. The article also documents a general trust decline across all outlets of 0.31 points on a five-point scale between 2011 and 2014, independent of tabloidisation, suggesting a broader delegitimation trend.

title: Framing the Refugee Crisis in Serbian Online Portals: A Comparative Study of Five News Sites, August–October 2015
abstract: This article applies entitlement framing theory to coverage of the 2015 refugee movements through Serbia on five major online news portals. A stratified random sample of 2,310 articles was drawn from the three-month period August through October 2015 and coded by four trained coders (Krippendorff's α = 0.78). Seven frames were identified inductively and validated deductively: humanitarian, security, economic burden, transit, legal, human-interest, and political-instrumental. Security and transit frames together accounted for 54 percent of all coded articles. Human-interest frames appeared in only 8 percent of coverage and were concentrated on two of the five portals. Temporal analysis reveals an intensification of the security frame in September 2015 coinciding with border closures in neighbouring countries. The findings are compared with parallel coding projects conducted on Hungarian and Croatian portals by partner teams.

title: Generational Differences in News Source Credibility: Cohort Analysis from Five Panel Waves, 2011–2016
abstract: Using five annual waves of the Vojvodina Audience Panel (balanced subsample N = 741), this article separates age effects from cohort effects in perceived media credibility through an age-period-cohort decomposition approach. The analysis distinguishes three cohorts: those who formed primary media habits before 1991, those who did so during the 1991–2000 transition period, and those who came of age after 2000. Credibility ratings for public television diverge significantly across cohorts (F(2, 738) = 14.3, p < 0.001), with the youngest cohort consistently rating it lower and commercial online news portals higher relative to the other cohorts. Period effects show a cross-cohort dip in all credibility ratings in 2014, coinciding with a major political media controversy. The chapter discusses implications for public service media strategy and for survey-based credibility measurement in contexts of rapid media system change.

title: Measuring Frame Salience in Automated Text Analysis: A Validation Study Against Human Coding in Serbian-Language News
abstract: This methodological paper tests whether three automated text-analysis approaches — dictionary-based classification, supervised machine learning (SVM), and topic modelling (LDA) — can reproduce human-coded frame assignments in a corpus of 4,200 Serbian-language news articles previously coded by trained coders. The human-coded gold standard was derived from two earlier studies on economic and migration coverage. Against this standard, SVM achieved the highest macro-averaged F1 score (0.69), while dictionary-based classification reached only 0.51 due to the ambiguity of Serbian morphological forms. LDA identified thematically coherent clusters but mapped poorly onto the theoretically derived frames (V = 0.28). The paper identifies specific frame categories where automation is most unreliable and recommends a hybrid protocol combining initial automated classification with targeted human review of borderline cases. Code and annotated dataset are deposited in the university repository.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Framing and Health-Information Trust: A Six-Month Longitudinal Survey in Serbia
abstract: This six-wave weekly panel survey (March–August 2020, N = 808 at wave 1, 634 at wave 6) tracked changes in health-information trust and self-reported media consumption during the first COVID-19 wave in Serbia. Each wave included a brief ten-item trust battery and five questions on media source use. A parallel fortnightly content analysis of three television channels and four online portals coded pandemic coverage for four frames: government-competence, scientific-authority, individual-responsibility, and fear-uncertainty. Multilevel growth-curve models show that exposure to the fear-uncertainty frame was associated with declining trust in health institutions over time (β = −0.14 per unit increase in exposure index, p = 0.007), while scientific-authority framing was associated with stable or slightly increasing trust. The study documents how rapidly trust trajectories can shift within a single crisis period and illustrates the added value of aligning content and reception data longitudinally.

title: Platform Migration and Credibility Transfer: Do Audiences Carry Trust from Legacy to Social Media News?
abstract: This article tests whether trust established in a legacy news brand transfers to the same brand's social media account, using an online experiment with 496 participants recruited from the Vojvodina Audience Panel in 2021. Participants were randomised to receive a news item attributed to a trusted outlet (defined by prior survey data), an untrusted outlet, or an unknown source, each delivered either via a simulated newspaper website or a simulated social media feed. A 2 × 3 factorial ANOVA shows a significant main effect of outlet trust (F(1, 490) = 38.4, p < 0.001) and a significant interaction between outlet trust and platform (F(2, 490) = 5.1, p = 0.006). Trust transfer is incomplete: items from trusted outlets on the social media platform received credibility ratings 0.6 points lower than the same items on the outlet's website. Implications for news brand strategy and audience segmentation are discussed.

title: Trust in Media Among Hungarian-Language Minority Audiences in Vojvodina: Comparing Minority and Majority Outlet Preferences
abstract: This survey study (N = 401, Hungarian-language residents of Vojvodina, 2022) examines whether ethnolinguistic minority status shapes patterns of media credibility and source preference. Respondents reported their habitual news sources and rated the credibility of six outlets on a seven-point scale: two Hungarian-language regional outlets, two Serbian-language national outlets, two Hungarian state-funded outlets broadcast into Serbia, and one pan-European outlet. Mixed-effects regression controlling for age, education, and urban-rural residence shows that Hungarian-language regional outlets receive significantly higher credibility ratings than Serbian-language national outlets (β = 1.12, p < 0.001), while the Hungarian state-funded outlets occupy an intermediate position. Younger respondents show greater openness to Serbian-language sources than older respondents. The findings are discussed in relation to theories of diasporic media use and minority audience autonomy.

title: Ten Years of the Vojvodina Audience Panel: Attrition, Refresh, and What the Data Show About Long-Term Trust Decline
abstract: This retrospective analysis documents ten annual waves (2011–2021) of the Vojvodina Audience Panel, covering a refreshed cumulative sample of 3,847 unique respondents. It presents a composite media trust index and traces its trajectory, showing a cumulative decline of 1.1 points on a seven-point scale over the decade, with the steepest drops in 2014 and 2020. The paper discusses attrition bias correction procedures applied across waves, the three panel refreshes conducted in 2015, 2018, and 2021, and comparisons between the balanced rotating panel and fresh cross-sections. Demographic disaggregation reveals that trust has declined most sharply among 18–35-year-olds and least among respondents over 65. The paper offers the panel as a resource for researchers and calls for methodological standardisation in longitudinal media studies across the Western Balkans.

title: Algorithmic Curation and Perceived Fairness: How Awareness of Recommendation Systems Affects Trust in News Feeds
abstract: A two-wave online experiment (wave 1 N = 544, wave 2 N = 489, interval four weeks) tested whether informing news consumers about algorithmic curation of their news feed changes their credibility assessments and perceived editorial fairness. Participants in the treatment condition were shown a brief explainer about how recommendation algorithms select content before their second exposure; controls received no explainer. At wave 2, treatment-group participants rated their feed as less editorially fair (Δ = −0.52, p = 0.001) but showed no significant change in item-level credibility. A subgroup analysis by digital literacy score found that high-literacy respondents reduced item-level credibility ratings more than low-literacy respondents after the algorithm explainer (interaction β = −0.19, p = 0.02). Results indicate that transparency about curation mechanisms activates scepticism selectively along existing competence lines rather than uniformly raising or lowering trust.

title: Framing AI-Generated News: Audience Detection, Credibility Attribution, and Trust Consequences in Serbian Online Readers
abstract: This preprint reports results of an experiment (N = 621 online participants, recruited December 2025) in which respondents read short news articles on three topics — local politics, public health, and sports — attributed to either a human journalist, an AI system, or an unspecified author. Credibility ratings, emotional valence, and sharing intentions were measured after each article. Articles attributed to AI were rated 0.9 points lower on credibility than identical content attributed to a human journalist (p < 0.001). The credibility penalty was largest for public health content and smallest for sports content. Respondents who correctly identified AI-generated stylistic features in a separate cloze task did not show a larger credibility penalty, suggesting the penalty is driven by label rather than detected quality differences. Moderation by age and prior attitudes toward AI technology is examined.

title: Structuring Moral Dilemma Stories for Children Aged Four to Six: Methodological Considerations
abstract: The paper addresses the practical and theoretical problems involved in adapting classic moral dilemma formats for use with preschool-aged children who lack the reading ability and abstract reasoning assumed by standard instruments. Drawing on pilot work with 18 children in Novi Sad, the authors propose a set of design criteria for picture-supported oral dilemma stories: narrative length should not exceed 90 seconds in spoken delivery, protagonists should be child-like figures rather than adults or animals, and the dilemma should involve a single clear conflict between two familiar values such as loyalty to a friend versus honesty. Three story versions were piloted and revised based on children's comprehension checks and spontaneous questions. Inter-rater reliability for coding children's justifications reached κ = 0.71 after two rounds of coder training. The paper provides the revised story texts and coding manual as appendices, intended as a reusable resource for researchers in the region.

title: Peer Disagreement as a Site for Moral Learning: Evidence from Preschool Dyads
abstract: This study investigated whether verbal disagreements between peer dyads during structured story-discussion tasks produce measurable change in children's moral reasoning quality within a single session. Forty-eight children aged 4.5–6 years were randomly assigned to dyad or individual conditions. All children heard the same three dilemma stories and were asked to explain what the protagonist should do and why. Dyad children discussed each story together before giving individual responses; solo children responded without discussion. Moral reasoning quality was rated on a four-level scale adapted from neo-Piagetian frameworks. Children in the dyad condition showed significantly higher reasoning scores on the post-discussion individual measure than solo children (mean difference 0.41 scale points, p = .018, d = 0.55). The effect was stronger in mixed-age dyads than same-age pairs. Discourse analysis of a subsample of 20 dyad sessions identified perspective-taking prompts and counter-argument as the most frequent precursors to upward reasoning shifts.

title: Moral Reasoning in Early Childhood
abstract: This book chapter provides a structured overview of theories and empirical findings relevant to moral reasoning in children from birth to age six, with particular attention to the transition from heteronomous to more autonomous moral judgment in the three-to-six window. The chapter reviews neo-Piagetian stage models, social domain theory, and narrative approaches, situating each within the broader developmental literature. A section is devoted to methodological issues specific to research with pre-literate children, including the limitations of hypothetical dilemma tasks and the advantages of naturalistic observation. The chapter concludes with a discussion of pedagogical implications for preschool practitioners, including suggestions for designing classroom activities that make moral reasoning visible and discussable.

title: Cross-Cultural Comparison of Preschool Children's Responses to Dilemma Stories: Serbia and Hungary
abstract: This study compared the moral reasoning responses of 58 children in Novi Sad and 54 children in Pécs, Hungary, all aged five to six, using parallel versions of the same four dilemma stories adapted into Serbian and Hungarian by bilingual research assistants. Adaptation fidelity was checked by independent back-translation and by cognitive interviewing with six children per language. Both groups showed similar distributions across moral reasoning levels, with no statistically significant between-country difference in mean level (t(110) = 0.84, p = .40). However, children in Novi Sad produced longer justifications on average (mean 41 words vs. 28 words, p = .003), a difference that may reflect classroom discussion norms rather than reasoning capacity per se. Within each group, the pattern of more complex reasoning in response to harm dilemmas compared to fairness dilemmas was replicated consistently. The study represents a first step toward a harmonised regional assessment tool.

title: Practitioner-Administered Dilemma Story Sessions: Fidelity, Feasibility, and Children's Engagement in Routine Preschool Settings
abstract: This implementation study examined whether preschool practitioners could deliver a structured eight-session dilemma storytelling curriculum with acceptable fidelity in ordinary classroom conditions. Twelve practitioners in six preschool institutions in Novi Sad received a one-day training and a written session guide. Sessions were video-recorded and scored for fidelity on 14 protocol items. Mean fidelity across all sessions was 71%, with the lowest scores on items requiring open-ended questioning without follow-up moral commentary. Children's engagement was coded from the same recordings using a five-point scale; mean engagement was 3.8 out of 5 and did not differ significantly between high- and low-fidelity sessions. Pre–post assessments of 89 children using the moral reasoning battery showed a mean gain of 0.31 scale points over eight weeks. Practitioners reported the curriculum as feasible but noted that session length of 20 minutes was close to the upper limit of group attention. Refinements to the training protocol are proposed.

title: Ustavni osnov podzakonskog normiranja u Republici Srbiji: teorijski okvir i praksa
abstract: Rad ispituje ustavnopravni osnov za donošenje podzakonskih akata izvršne vlasti u Republici Srbiji, s posebnim osvrtom na član 137. Ustava iz 2006. godine. Primenjujući dogmatičko-pravnu metodu i analizu odluka Ustavnog suda Srbije od 2007. do 2012. godine (ukupno 47 relevantnih odluka), autor identifikuje tri modela prenosa normativnih ovlašćenja koja su razvila sudska praksa i doktrina. Rezultati pokazuju da je Ustavni sud dosledno primenjivao test suštinske saglasnosti podzakonskog akta sa zakonom, ali bez jasno razrađenih kriterijuma za ocenu stepena konkretnosti zakonskog ovlašćenja. Rad zaključuje da odsustvo preciznog ustavnog standarda otvara prostor za diskrecionarno normiranje izvršnih organa širih razmera nego što to Ustav implicitno predviđa, i predlaže korektivne smernice de lege ferenda.

title: Regulatory Agencies and the Limits of Delegated Rulemaking: A Comparative Study of Germany, France, and Serbia
abstract: This article compares the constitutional frameworks governing the rulemaking powers of independent regulatory agencies in Germany, France, and Serbia, focusing on the mechanisms by which each legal order constrains agency discretion when issuing sub-legislative rules. Using doctrinal analysis and a structured comparison of sixty-three agency acts issued between 2008 and 2013 in the three jurisdictions, the study examines how courts review the scope of delegated authority. German administrative courts applied a stricter specificity doctrine than their French counterparts, while Serbian Ustavni sud decisions showed inconsistency in reviewing technical rulemaking by sector regulators. The article argues that Serbia's partial transplantation of the German Wesentlichkeitstheorie through academic commentary has not been matched by coherent judicial application. Three corrective criteria are proposed for adoption in Serbian administrative court practice.

title: Tehničke norme kao podzakonski akti: problem normativne forme u srpskom standardizacionom pravu
abstract: Rad analizira pravnu prirodu srpskih nacionalnih standarda koje donosi Institut za standardizaciju Srbije (ISS), razmatrajući da li oni mogu biti podvrgnuti ustavnosudskoj kontroli kao podzakonski akti u smislu člana 168. Ustava. Na osnovu analize 29 standarda u oblasti građevinarstva i elektroenergetike donetih između 2009. i 2013. godine, kao i komparativnog pregleda austrijskog i slovenačkog prava, autor tvrdi da privatnopravna forma tehničkih standarda ne sme biti prepreka za ispitivanje njihovog efektivnog pravnog dejstva. Posebna pažnja posvećena je standardima koji su inkorporisani u tehničke propise i na taj način stekli obaveznu snagu. Zaključuje se da nedostatak zakonske definicije granice između tehničkih propisa i standarda u Zakonu o tehničkim zahtevima za proizvode iz 2009. godine stvara praznine u ustavnoj zaštiti građana.

title: Granice regulatorne diskrecije u oblasti telekomunikacija: analiza akata Regulatorne agencije za elektronske komunikacije i poštanske usluge
abstract: Istraživanje se bavi aktima Regulatorne agencije za elektronske komunikacije i poštanske usluge (RATEL) iz perioda 2010–2016. godine, sa ciljem utvrđivanja da li su obim i sadržaj regulatornih ovlašćenja koja RATEL izvršava u skladu sa ustavnim standardima vladavine prava. Metodom normativne analize ispitana su 34 podzakonska akta, uz komparativni osvrt na praksu slovenačke AKOS i hrvatskog HAKOM. Rezultati pokazuju da je srpski zakonodavac u Zakonu o elektronskim komunikacijama iz 2010. godine na više mesta koristio neopravdano široke generalne klauzule kao osnov za normativno delovanje RATEL-a, posebno u pogledu utvrđivanja tehničkih uslova pristupa mreži. Predložena su četiri kriterijuma za zakonodavnu razradu granica agencijskog normiranja u sektoru elektronskih komunikacija, uz pregled odgovarajućih direktiva EU.

title: Ustavnosudska kontrola tehničkih propisa u Srbiji: deset godina prakse Ustavnog suda (2007–2017)
abstract: Rad sistematizuje i analizira sve dostupne odluke Ustavnog suda Srbije koje se tiču tehničkih propisa i standarda tehničke prirode donetih od strane izvršnih organa i regulatornih agencija u periodu od 2007. do 2017. godine. Od ukupno 612 odluka o kontroli podzakonskih akata, identifikovano je 38 slučajeva koji se eksplicitno tiču tehničkih normi ili tehničkih propisa. Analiza pokazuje da je Ustavni sud u svega sedam slučajeva meritorno ocenjivao stepen preciznosti zakonskog ovlašćenja, dok je u ostalima primenjivao formalni test saglasnosti sa zakonom. Posebno je analizirano pet predmeta iz oblasti bezbednosti hrane i građevinarstva. Rad zaključuje da Ustavni sud do sada nije razvio konzistentnu doktrinu za ocenu proporcionalnosti prenosa normativnih ovlašćenja u tehničkim oblastima, i predlaže moguće korake ka sistematizaciji sudskog pristupa.

title: Regulatory Impact Assessment as a Constraint on Agency Discretion: Evidence from Serbian Technical Rulemaking 2015–2022
abstract: Serbia introduced a formal regulatory impact assessment (RIA) obligation for sub-legislative acts in 2013, subsequently reinforced by the 2018 Public Administration Reform Strategy. This article investigates whether RIA procedures have in practice constrained the discretion of five Serbian regulatory agencies—covering energy, electronic communications, civil aviation, food safety, and environmental protection—when those agencies issue technical rules. Using a dataset of 204 technical rulebooks published between 2015 and 2022, together with the accompanying impact assessment documents where available, the study measures compliance rates, depth of quantitative analysis, and responsiveness to public consultation inputs. RIA documents were absent in 31 percent of cases and substantively thin in a further 44 percent. Agencies with more developed internal legal departments produced qualitatively better RIA documents, but no agency systematically connected impact findings to the scope of the rule ultimately adopted. The article discusses implications for constitutional oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Automated Standard-Setting: Constitutional Questions for Serbian Administrative Law
abstract: Several Serbian regulatory agencies have begun using algorithmic tools to calibrate technical parameters embedded in binding rulebooks, particularly in the domains of network tariffs, emission thresholds, and product safety coefficients. This preprint explores the constitutional questions that arise when normative choices with binding legal effect are, in whole or in part, the output of automated systems rather than human deliberation. Drawing on the Serbian constitutional framework and on administrative law scholarship from Austria, the Netherlands, and the EU level, the paper identifies three distinct scenarios: fully automated parameter-setting, human-confirmed algorithmic outputs, and algorithm-informed expert discretion. It argues that the first scenario is constitutionally impermissible under the current Serbian constitutional order and that the second requires legislative authorisation specifying criteria the algorithm must apply. A preliminary doctrinal framework is offered for each scenario.

title: Ustavna dimenzija harmonizacije tehničkih standarda sa pravom EU: analiza odabranih sektora srpskog zakonodavstva
abstract: Rad analizira ustavne aspekte procesa harmonizacije srpskog tehničkog zakonodavstva sa pravom Evropske unije u periodu 2016–2024. godine, s fokusom na tri sektora: bezbednost mašina, električna oprema niskog napona i materijali za kontakt sa hranom. Na osnovu analize 67 tehničkih propisa i standarda donetih u navedenom periodu, uz pregled Sporazuma o stabilizaciji i pridruživanju kao relevantnog međunarodnog pravnog okvira, ispituje se da li je srpski zakonodavac, prenoseći tehničko zakonodavstvo EU, adekvatno definisao granice podzakonskog normiranja ili je diskrecionarni prostor regulatornih tela prouzrokovao ustavnopravne praznine. Utvrđeno je da se u 22 od analiziranih 67 propisa zakonsko ovlašćenje može oceniti kao nedovoljno određeno. Rad predlaže model klauzula o ovlašćenjima koji bi bio primenjiv u srpskoj tehničkoj legislativi.

title: Draft force requirements of strip-till row units operating at variable working depths in Vertisol profiles of Vojvodina
abstract: Strip-till implements operating in heavy clay (Vertisol) soils of Vojvodina are known to exhibit highly variable draft demand depending on working depth and soil moisture content. This study measured draft force using a three-point-hitch-mounted strain-gauge dynamometer across three working depths (15, 20, and 25 cm) and two soil moisture regimes (near field capacity and 60% of field capacity) on a 2.4 ha experimental plot near Srbobran. A commercial six-row strip-till unit with fixed-geometry coulter assemblies was used. Draft force increased by 38% when depth was raised from 15 to 25 cm at field capacity, and by 61% at the drier condition. Specific soil resistance values ranged from 14.2 to 23.7 N cm⁻². Cone penetration resistance profiles were measured before and after each pass to characterise loosening efficiency. Results indicated that a 20 cm working depth achieved the best ratio of loosened soil volume to energy input at both moisture levels. Tractor fuel consumption was logged continuously via CAN-bus and averaged 8.4 L ha⁻¹ at the optimal depth. The data suggest that adapting working depth in real time to soil moisture could reduce seasonal draft energy by up to 18%.

title: Soil bin evaluation of paraplow and winged subsoiler geometry on disturbance cross-section and energy demand in clay loam
abstract: Subsoil loosening in compacted clay loam soils is energy-intensive and the implement geometry strongly influences both the shape of the loosened cross-section and the draft force required. This controlled soil bin experiment compared three implement configurations: a standard paraplow (30° leg inclination), a modified paraplow with an extended wing (100 mm horizontal extension), and a straight-leg winged subsoiler at 90° shank angle. All tools were tested at 35 cm working depth in a prepared clay loam sample (clay content 42%, bulk density 1.48 g cm⁻³) maintained at two moisture levels. Cross-sectional area of disturbance was mapped using a profile metre at 0.5 m intervals along each pass. The winged subsoiler produced the largest disturbed cross-section (412 cm²) but required 22% more draft than the standard paraplow (mean 8.9 kN versus 7.3 kN). The extended-wing paraplow achieved an intermediate disturbed area (371 cm²) with draft comparable to the standard version. Specific energy per unit disturbed volume was lowest for the extended-wing paraplow at 3.1 J cm⁻³. Results provide geometry selection criteria applicable to Vojvodina field conditions.

title: Effect of coulter blade profile on energy consumption and seedbed quality in strip-till systems on compacted clay soils
abstract: The geometry of the opening coulter in strip-till systems affects both the energy needed to cut the soil profile and the quality of the prepared seedbed strip. This field study compared three commercially available coulter profiles — a plain disc, a fluted disc, and a notched disc — mounted on otherwise identical strip-till row units. Trials were conducted on a 4.1 ha field with a clay content of 49% (Haplic Vertisol) at Bački Petrovac over two growing seasons (2023 and 2024). Draft per row unit was measured with calibrated load pins on individual toolbar shanks. Fuel consumption was recorded via tractor ECU logging. The notched disc showed the lowest mean draft per row (1.12 kN) compared to the plain disc (1.41 kN) under dry soil conditions, a difference of 21%. Under moist conditions the advantage narrowed to 9%. Seedbed strip width and aggregate size distribution were assessed by image analysis of 60 photographs per treatment. The fluted disc produced the narrowest and most uniform strip (mean width 83 mm, CV 7%), which was associated with better early maize emergence uniformity (Pearson r = 0.71). Energy savings with the notched coulter were estimated at 1.9 L ha⁻¹ across the full field.

title: Draft force prediction for subsoil loosening implements using cone index-based empirical models: a comparison of three pedotransfer approaches in Pannonian clay soils
abstract: Reliable pre-season estimation of draft force for subsoil loosening implements reduces the risk of under-powered tractor–implement pairings and supports precision energy planning. Three empirical pedotransfer models from the literature — the ASABE D497 approach, the Grisso–Kocher regression, and a locally calibrated model from Hungarian clay soils — were tested against a field-measured dataset of 186 draft observations collected across six fields in the South Bačka and South Banat districts. Cone penetration resistance (0–40 cm depth, 1 cm intervals) and soil texture served as primary inputs. Mean absolute percentage error was 19.4%, 24.1%, and 12.8% for the three models respectively, with the locally calibrated model performing best. However, this model's accuracy degraded markedly (MAPE 28.3%) when applied to soils with clay content above 55%, pointing to the need for a regionally specific calibration dataset for Vojvodina Vertisols. A provisional correction factor for high-clay conditions is proposed and validated on a hold-out subset of 31 observations. The analysis also identifies cone index measured at 25–30 cm depth as the single strongest predictor of peak draft (R² = 0.68).

title: Occurrence of Cryptosporidium oocysts in shallow dug wells in three rural municipalities of Vojvodina
abstract: Fifty-two shallow dug wells (depth 4–9 m) in three Vojvodina municipalities were sampled monthly over one hydrological year. Water samples of 10 L were processed by membrane filtration followed by immunomagnetic separation and direct immunofluorescence assay. Cryptosporidium oocysts were detected in 31% of wells during the spring sampling campaign, with concentrations ranging from below the detection limit to 4.2 oocysts per 10 L. Higher oocyst counts correlated positively with proximity to livestock operations (Spearman r = 0.61, p < 0.01) and with elevated turbidity following precipitation events. Seasonal variation was significant, with spring peaks coinciding with snowmelt. The results indicate that shallow alluvial wells in agricultural lowland settings carry measurable Cryptosporidium loads that are rarely monitored under current Serbian drinking water regulations. The study provides baseline occurrence data intended to support subsequent risk characterisation for household users who consume water without prior disinfection.

title: Campylobacter detection in alluvial groundwater adjacent to small-scale poultry farms in the Tisa River corridor
abstract: Groundwater samples from 28 monitoring points in the Tisa River alluvial zone were analysed for Campylobacter spp. over a 15-month period using membrane filtration and real-time PCR targeting the hipO and 16S rRNA genes. Campylobacter was confirmed in 19 of 28 sites at least once; Campylobacter jejuni accounted for 74% of positive detections. Concentrations estimated by most probable number (MPN) ranged from 0.3 to 28 MPN per 100 mL at contaminated sites. A logistic regression model showed that distance from the nearest poultry farm boundary and seasonal temperature were the strongest predictors of detection probability. Sampling during summer months yielded the highest prevalence. The findings suggest that lateral infiltration from surface drainage near poultry operations contributes to episodic bacterial contamination of alluvial aquifers used for domestic supply in this corridor.

title: Dose–response analysis for Cryptosporidium parvum in sensitive population subgroups: implications for risk targets in rural Serbia
abstract: This paper revisits the exponential and beta-Poisson dose–response models for Cryptosporidium parvum infection, fitting them to pooled human feeding trial data from published literature (n = 7 trials, 374 subjects). Maximum likelihood estimation and bootstrap confidence intervals (10 000 iterations) were used to derive parameter distributions. The best-fitting model was the exponential with r = 0.0042 (95% CI: 0.0031–0.0057). Infection risk was then calculated for ingestion scenarios representative of unfiltered, unchlorinated shallow well water consumed by children under 5 and immunocompromised adults, using oocyst concentrations measured in previous field studies in Vojvodina. At a mean ingestion volume of 1 L per day and a median oocyst concentration of 0.8 oocysts per 10 L, estimated annual infection risk for children exceeded the WHO benchmark of 10⁻⁴ per person-year. The analysis quantifies the gap between current exposure conditions and acceptable risk targets and provides parameters for subsequent full QMRA frameworks in the regional context.

title: Effect of well casing material and depth on faecal indicator bacteria counts in alluvial wells: a field comparison study
abstract: Forty-eight operational drinking water wells in the Bačka region were classified by casing material (concrete rings, brick, unlined) and depth (< 5 m, 5–9 m, > 9 m). Escherichia coli and enterococci were enumerated monthly for 12 months using Colilert-18 and membrane filtration, respectively. Concrete-cased wells had significantly lower median E. coli counts (< 1 CFU per 100 mL) compared with unlined wells (median 18 CFU per 100 mL; Mann–Whitney U, p < 0.001). Depth showed a weaker protective effect that was significant only for wells deeper than 9 m. Multivariate linear regression confirmed that casing material and a constructed drainage apron each independently predicted log-transformed E. coli counts after controlling for season and land use within a 100 m radius. The findings support prioritisation of well casing improvements in rural sanitation programmes and suggest simple indicators suitable for rapid field assessment by local public health officers.

title: Seasonal dynamics of Giardia cysts and Cryptosporidium oocysts in a shallow unconfined aquifer recharged by an oxbow lake in the Danube floodplain
abstract: Over 24 consecutive months, water samples from seven monitoring boreholes positioned along a transect between an oxbow lake and the main alluvial aquifer were analysed for Giardia cysts and Cryptosporidium oocysts using US EPA Method 1623.1. Giardia cysts were detected more frequently (48% of samples) than Cryptosporidium oocysts (22%), with highest concentrations immediately after spring flood events when lake water infiltrated rapidly into the aquifer. Time-lagged cross-correlation analysis indicated a 3–7 day travel time from the oxbow lake margin to the nearest monitoring borehole. Oocyst viability, assessed by DAPI/PI staining and differential interference contrast microscopy, averaged 41% across positive samples. The data suggest that transient hydraulic connection during flood pulses constitutes the primary contamination pathway rather than persistent diffuse leakage. Results are discussed in terms of vulnerability mapping and source protection zone delineation for nearby community intakes.

title: Water safety plan implementation in four small settlements in Srem: microbial baseline assessment and risk ranking of hazards
abstract: Water safety plans (WSPs) were developed and partially implemented in four settlements in the Srem district (population 420–1 800 each), all relying on shallow alluvial wells as their primary supply. The study documents the microbial baseline assessment phase: 180 samples collected at source, treatment (where present), storage, and point of use were analysed for E. coli, total coliforms, enterococci, Clostridium perfringens spores, and somatic coliphages. Hazard identification and semi-quantitative risk ranking followed WHO WSP guidance. Point-of-use samples exceeded the Serbian drinking water standard for E. coli in 42% of households; the proportion was highest in settlements without any centralised distribution (67%). Treatment barrier assessment showed that simple household boiling, practised by 38% of surveyed residents, reduced risk scores substantially. The results are used to prioritise corrective actions and to provide a reproducible monitoring protocol for municipal public utility operators with limited laboratory capacity.

title: Climate variability and its effect on faecal pathogen concentrations in alluvial aquifers: analysis of a 10-year monitoring dataset from northern Serbia
abstract: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a 10-year monitoring dataset (2011–2020) covering 14 alluvial groundwater monitoring stations in northern Serbia, combining E. coli counts, Cryptosporidium oocyst concentrations (available for 8 stations from 2015 onward), and daily hydrometeorological records. Mixed-effects regression models with station as a random effect were fitted to assess relationships between antecedent precipitation index (API-7), water table depth, air temperature, and microbial concentrations. Each 10 mm increase in API-7 was associated with a 0.19 log increase in E. coli concentration (95% CI: 0.11–0.27). The relationship was stronger for Cryptosporidium (0.31 log per 10 mm API-7). Notably, the effect of temperature on Cryptosporidium was not statistically significant after controlling for precipitation, while air temperature independently predicted Campylobacter frequency at two stations. Projections based on two regional climate scenarios (RCP4.5 and RCP8.5) suggest that risk exceedance events could increase by 15–35% by 2050 at most monitored sites.

title: Comparing rapid concentration methods for Cryptosporidium and Campylobacter in low-turbidity groundwater samples: recovery efficiency and false-negative rates
abstract: Four concentration and detection protocols were compared for their recovery efficiency and false-negative rates when applied to groundwater samples with turbidity below 1 NTU: (1) hollow-fibre ultrafiltration followed by IMS-DFA, (2) membrane filtration with 1 μm cellulose nitrate filters followed by IMS-DFA, (3) continuous-flow centrifugation followed by PCR, and (4) positively charged membrane filtration followed by culture-PCR. Spiking experiments used 10 L tap water seeded with known concentrations of C. parvum oocysts (Iowa isolate) and C. jejuni cells at three concentration levels (low: 1–2 organisms per 10 L; medium: 10–20; high: 100–200). Mean Cryptosporidium recovery ranged from 18% (membrane filtration) to 54% (hollow-fibre UF). Campylobacter recovery was highest for continuous-flow centrifugation combined with culture-PCR (mean 61%). False-negative rates were highest at low seeding levels, reaching 40–70% depending on method. The study recommends hollow-fibre UF as the preferred method for Cryptosporidium in low-turbidity alluvial groundwater and provides recovery correction factors for use in QMRA exposure calculations.

title: Stochastic QMRA for Cryptosporidium in a proposed managed aquifer recharge scheme using treated wastewater in Bačka: risk quantification under varying recharge rates
abstract: A stochastic QMRA was conducted to evaluate the infection risk posed by Cryptosporidium parvum if a planned managed aquifer recharge (MAR) facility in the Bačka region were to operate using secondary-treated municipal wastewater. Effluent oocyst concentration distributions were derived from 36 weekly measurements at the Vrbas wastewater treatment plant. Unsaturated zone travel time was modelled using a one-dimensional advection-dispersion equation calibrated against a bromide tracer test. Monte Carlo simulation (50 000 iterations) was used to propagate uncertainty through the log-removal credit attributed to soil passage, varying from 1.5 to 4.0 log₁₀ depending on travel time. At a recharge rate of 500 m³/day, median annual infection risk at the nearest abstraction well was 3.1 × 10⁻⁵ per person-year with a 95th percentile of 2.2 × 10⁻⁴, marginally exceeding the WHO guideline at the upper bound. Scenarios with a minimum 60-day retention time consistently met the guideline. The analysis supports design of the required buffer zone around recharge ponds.

title: Cultivable heterotrophic bacteria isolated from corroded cast-iron pipes in the Novi Sad distribution network
abstract: Pipe wall scrapings were collected from six sections of cast-iron mains (diameter 100–200 mm, age 30–55 years) in the Novi Sad municipal distribution network during planned maintenance shutdowns. Surface-spread and pour-plate methods on R2A, nutrient agar and iron-amended minimal media yielded 214 isolates. Representative strains were identified by partial 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Pseudomonas and Sphingomonas species dominated on R2A (combined 38% of isolates), whereas iron-amended plates enriched for Gallionella-like and Sideroxydans-like morphotypes that could not be maintained in pure culture beyond two transfers. Resistance to free chlorine (0.2 mg/L) was tested using suspension assays; 61 isolates (28.5%) survived a 30-minute contact time. Pipe corrosion products (goethite, magnetite confirmed by XRD) appeared to afford partial protection. Results establish a baseline cultivable community profile and highlight the numerical underrepresentation of obligate iron oxidisers on standard media.

title: Seasonal variation in Nitrospira population density in a chloraminated distribution system inferred from quantitative PCR
abstract: Quantitative PCR targeting the Nitrospira-specific nxrB gene was applied to DNA extracted from bulk water (2 L grab samples) and loose pipe deposits collected monthly over 18 months from a chloraminated zone of the Subotica municipal network. Water temperature ranged from 7 °C in winter to 22 °C in summer. Nitrospira gene copy numbers in bulk water showed a significant positive correlation with temperature (Spearman r = 0.71, p < 0.001), peaking at 3.4 × 10³ copies/mL in July. Pipe deposit fractions consistently carried two to three orders of magnitude higher copy numbers than the corresponding bulk water samples, confirming that the distribution system interior surface rather than the bulk phase is the primary Nitrospira reservoir. Nitrite concentrations in the network correlated inversely with Nitrospira abundance, consistent with active nitrite oxidation. Free ammonia released by chloramine decay was identified as the principal driver of summer population growth using multiple linear regression.

title: Haloacetic acid formation potential in chloraminated systems undergoing nitrification: laboratory batch tests with biofilm leachate
abstract: Nitrification in chloramine-treated networks can alter the organic carbon pool and thereby affect disinfection by-product (DBP) formation. Biofilm leachate was collected from pilot-loop coupons after 120 days of nitrifying conditions (confirmed by nitrite accumulation) and subjected to chlorine and chloramine demand tests followed by headspace GC-ECD analysis of trihalomethanes (THMs) and ion chromatographic quantification of haloacetic acids (HAAs). Leachate from nitrifying biofilms showed a 23% higher HAA5 formation potential compared with non-nitrifying controls, while THM formation potential did not differ significantly between conditions. Dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) in nitrifying leachate was elevated (0.8 vs. 0.3 mg/L), and the increase in HAA yield correlated with DON concentration (r² = 0.84). Parallel LC-OCD fractionation identified hydrophilic acids and low-molecular-weight neutrals as the fractions contributing most to excess HAA formation. Findings suggest that nitrification suppression confers a co-benefit of reduced HAA precursor release.

title: Functional gene catalogue of nitrifying biofilm communities in Vojvodina drinking water networks derived from shotgun metagenomics
abstract: Shotgun metagenomes (Illumina HiSeq 2500, 2 × 150 bp paired-end) were generated from biofilm DNA pooled from 24 coupon devices deployed at six sites across three Vojvodina drinking water utilities operating under chloramine disinfection. Total sequencing yield was 312 Gbp after quality trimming. Assembly with MEGAHIT produced 2.1 million contigs; binning with MetaBAT2 recovered 38 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) with completeness > 70% and contamination < 5%. MAGs affiliated with Nitrospira (n = 6), Nitrosomonas (n = 4) and Sideroxydans (n = 3) were reconstructed. The Nitrospira MAGs encoded complete pathways for nitrite oxidation and carbon fixation via the reductive tricarboxylic acid cycle; two also harboured amoA genes, providing genomic evidence for complete ammonia oxidation (comammox) in this system. Functional annotations revealed high prevalence of chloramine tolerance determinants including glutathione S-transferase and methionine sulphoxide reductase genes across multiple lineages. This catalogue provides a reference for future monitoring studies in the region.

title: Spatial heterogeneity of biofilm community composition along a chloramine gradient in a branched distribution network
abstract: Chloramine residual in the Novi Sad network decays from approximately 2.1 mg/L at the reservoir outlet to < 0.3 mg/L at distal dead-end nodes. We exploited this natural gradient by deploying 48 biofilm coupon devices at 12 network locations stratified by chloramine residual class (high: > 1.5 mg/L; medium: 0.5–1.5 mg/L; low: < 0.5 mg/L). After 60 days of exposure, coupon biofilms were profiled by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and ATP measurements. Total biofilm ATP increased 3.1-fold from high to low residual zones. Ordination analysis (NMDS, Bray–Curtis distances) showed significant separation of community composition among residual classes (PERMANOVA R² = 0.41, p = 0.001). Comammox Nitrospira and Sideroxydans-related phylotypes were significantly enriched in low-residual sites; Methylobacterium and Sphingomonas dominated high-residual biofilms. Co-occurrence network analysis identified a Nitrospira–Sideroxydans positive association suggesting metabolic coupling between nitrogen and iron cycling at low disinfectant levels.

title: Metatranscriptomic evidence for active nitrification in low-biomass bulk water of a chloraminated network
abstract: Whether nitrification in drinking water distribution systems is primarily a biofilm-associated or bulk water process has been debated. We addressed this by applying metatranscriptomics to RNA extracted directly from 10 L bulk water samples collected at night (minimal hydraulic disturbance) from three chloraminated network zones in Novi Sad. RNA was stabilised with RNAlater, ribosomal RNA was depleted using a Ribo-Zero kit, and sequencing was performed on a NovaSeq 6000 (2 × 100 bp). Mapping against the reference gene catalogue from the 2020 Vojvodina metagenome revealed active transcription of amoA, amoB and hao genes (Nitrosomonas-affiliated) and nxrA, nxrB (Nitrospira-affiliated) in all three bulk water samples, with transcript abundances 18–42 times lower than in matched biofilm RNA. Transcripts for Sideroxydans cyc2 were also detected. Results confirm that bulk water harbours metabolically active nitrifiers, albeit at much lower activity than biofilm, with implications for chloramine demand modelling.

title: Long-read metagenomic assembly resolves complete genomes of comammox Nitrospira from drinking water biofilm
abstract: Short-read metagenomic assemblies commonly fragment genomic regions encoding repeat-containing operons, including the amo gene cluster in comammox Nitrospira. We applied Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) PromethION long-read sequencing to high-molecular-weight DNA extracted from pooled biofilm material from six low-residual network sites in Novi Sad. After Guppy basecalling and quality filtering, 28.4 Gbp of reads were available. Hybrid assembly using Flye followed by Illumina short-read polishing yielded three circularised comammox Nitrospira genomes (3.4–4.1 Mbp, completeness > 98%, contamination < 1%). Comparison with reference Nitrospira inopinata revealed expansions in transporter gene families (ABC-type phosphate and sulphate transporters), a full ure operon suggesting urea utilisation as an alternative ammonia source, and a type IV pili locus potentially involved in biofilm attachment. Phylogenomic placement confirmed all three genomes belong to comammox Nitrospira clade A. These are the first complete comammox genomes recovered from a Balkan drinking water system.

title: Distribution system microbiome and regulatory compliance: bridging metagenomic data and drinking water quality indicators
abstract: Chapter reviews the relationship between metagenomic community descriptors—alpha diversity indices, relative abundance of nitrifier guilds, iron-oxidiser guild richness—and conventional regulatory water quality indicators prescribed under EU Drinking Water Directive 2020/2184 (total coliforms, E. coli, colony counts at 22 °C and 37 °C, nitrite). Drawing on data from six Balkan utilities and a literature survey of 31 published distribution system metagenome datasets, the chapter evaluates whether any metagenomic metric can serve as an early warning indicator for regulatory threshold exceedances. Nitrospira relative abundance above 2% of the 16S rRNA community profile preceded nitrite exceedance events (> 0.1 mg/L) by a median of 23 days across the six utilities examined. Iron-oxidiser richness correlated with colour complaints (r = 0.62) but not with coliform counts. The chapter concludes with recommended sampling protocols for integrating sequence-based monitoring into utility operational practice, noting data infrastructure requirements and cost per sample in Vojvodina context.

title: Multiple linear regression QSAR models for triazole antifungal activity against Candida albicans: descriptor selection and cross-validation
abstract: A dataset of 48 triazole derivatives with experimentally determined MIC values against Candida albicans was compiled from the literature. Constitutional, topological, and geometrical descriptors were calculated using Dragon 5.5, yielding an initial pool of 412 variables. Forward stepwise multiple linear regression combined with leave-one-out cross-validation identified a four-descriptor model (R² = 0.87, Q²LOO = 0.83) in which the Wiener index, the molecular electronegativity distance vector MEDV-13, and two Randić connectivity indices carried the dominant predictive weight. An external test set of 12 compounds not used during model building gave R²ext = 0.81. Residual analysis revealed two structural outliers attributable to bulky halogenated substituents at the 4-position of the phenyl ring. The study emphasises that LOO cross-validation alone overstates model robustness and that a separate test set drawn before any descriptor selection is mandatory for reliable performance assessment.

title: Hedging in Serbian Scientific Prose: A Preliminary Survey of Medical and Technical Journals
abstract: This study presents a preliminary corpus-based examination of hedging devices in Serbian-language scientific prose, drawing on 120 journal articles published between 1988 and 1994 in two medical and two technical periodicals. Using a taxonomy adapted from earlier English-language hedging research, the analysis identifies modal verbs, epistemic adverbials, and approximators as the three most frequent hedging categories. Medical articles show a higher density of modal hedges per 1,000 words (mean 14.3) compared with technical articles (mean 9.7). The paper further distinguishes author-oriented from reader-oriented hedges and finds that the former predominate in both disciplines. Results suggest that Serbian scientific writers had already developed stable hedging conventions by the early 1990s, broadly parallel to those documented in English academic prose, though with distinctive lexical realisations tied to the morphological properties of Serbian. Implications for the description of Serbian academic style are discussed.

title: Introductory Moves in Serbian Law Review Articles: A Genre-Analytic Approach
abstract: Applying a moves-based genre analysis to 80 introduction sections drawn from four Serbian legal periodicals (1985–1997), this article examines how authors of law review articles establish a research territory, identify a gap, and announce their contribution. Each introduction was segmented into rhetorical moves and steps following an established analytical framework. The analysis finds that the three-move structure widely described for anglophone research articles is present in Serbian law review introductions, but that gap identification is frequently implicit rather than explicit, appearing in only 41 per cent of texts as a discrete step. Territorial establishment is achieved predominantly through citation of domestic statutory sources rather than prior scholarship, a pattern that distinguishes legal from natural-science introductions in Serbian academic writing. The study contributes to an emerging comparative description of genre conventions in Central and South-East European academic traditions.

title: Disciplinary Variation in Metadiscourse: Evidence from a 200-Text Serbian Academic Corpus
abstract: This paper reports findings from a systematic analysis of interpersonal and textual metadiscourse markers across a balanced corpus of 200 Serbian journal articles from four disciplines: biochemistry, history, civil engineering, and literary studies. Texts were drawn from nationally categorised journals published between 1995 and 2002. Metadiscourse categories were coded using a two-tier taxonomy distinguishing interactive markers (frame markers, code glosses, evidentials, endophoric markers, transitions) from interactional markers (hedges, boosters, attitude markers, self-mentions, engagement markers). Results show significant disciplinary differences: literary studies articles contain the highest density of attitude markers and self-mentions, while biochemistry articles rely heavily on evidentials and code glosses. Hedging density is highest in history (mean 18.1 per 1,000 words). The paper argues that these patterns reflect epistemological differences between disciplines and discusses their implications for teaching academic writing at Serbian universities.

title: Boosting and Self-Promotion in Serbian Natural-Science Abstracts, 1980–2000
abstract: Using a corpus of 300 abstracts from Serbian natural-science journals published across two decades (1980–2000), this study traces diachronic change in the use of boosters and evaluative language. Abstracts were sampled from biology, chemistry, and geology periodicals and coded for booster frequency, claim strength, and the presence of explicit result-highlighting phrases. The data show a moderate but consistent increase in booster density over the period, from a mean of 4.1 occurrences per abstract in 1980–1989 to 6.8 in 1991–2000, which the author associates with growing exposure to anglophone publication norms following increased international journal access in the 1990s. Boosters are most frequent in result and conclusion clauses. The study raises questions about whether the observed shift represents genuine rhetorical change or surface adaptation to translated anglophone conventions.

title: Academic Prose in Transition: Genre Conventions in Serbian Scholarly Journals Before and After 2000
abstract: This book chapter examines shifts in the organisational and rhetorical properties of Serbian scholarly journal articles across the transition period of the late 1990s and early 2000s, when Serbian universities began aligning with European publication standards. Drawing on a corpus of 160 articles sampled at five-year intervals from 1990 to 2005, the chapter traces changes in article structure, section labelling practices, abstract length and content, and the frequency of explicit signposting language. Findings indicate that section standardisation (IMRD structure) increased markedly in natural-science and biomedical journals but remained inconsistent in humanities disciplines throughout the period. Abstract length grew on average from 78 words in 1990 to 142 words in 2005. The chapter situates these changes in the broader context of Serbian higher education reform and discusses the tension between international genre norms and local disciplinary traditions.

title: Hedging Norms in Serbian Medical Writing: A Comparison with Croatian and Slovenian Counterparts
abstract: This comparative study examines hedging conventions in medical research articles written in Serbian, Croatian, and Slovenian, three closely related South Slavic standard languages with overlapping but distinct academic writing traditions. A parallel corpus of 180 articles (60 per language) was drawn from nationally indexed cardiology and internal medicine journals published between 2005 and 2012. Hedges were identified and classified using a revised taxonomy covering modal verbs, approximators, epistemic adverbials, and conditional constructions. Serbian texts show a mean hedging density of 16.4 per 1,000 words, slightly higher than Croatian (15.1) and Slovenian (14.7). Qualitative analysis reveals differences in preferred hedging lexemes that reflect each language's literary and academic register histories. The study argues for greater methodological attention to intra-regional variation when making generalisations about Slavic academic prose.

title: Seasonal patterns of fungal biomass and enzyme activity during oak leaf litter decomposition on Fruška Gora
abstract: Litter decomposition was monitored over two full years in a mixed oak-hornbeam stand on the southern slopes of Fruška Gora using a litterbag array of 480 nylon mesh bags (1 mm and 0.04 mm mesh) placed in three replicate plots. Fungal biomass was estimated by ergosterol extraction with HPLC quantification, and activities of laccase, Mn-peroxidase, and cellulase were measured monthly. Ergosterol concentrations peaked in late autumn (mean 312 µg g⁻¹ dry mass) and again in early spring, coinciding with maximum laccase activity (mean 4.8 nmol min⁻¹ g⁻¹). Mass loss reached 38% after 12 months and 61% after 24 months. Coarse mesh bags consistently showed higher fungal biomass and enzyme activity than fine mesh bags, indicating a significant contribution of mesofaunal fragmentation to fungal colonisation. Moisture content of the litter layer explained 54% of the variance in ergosterol concentration across sampling dates. These results confirm the dominant role of ligninolytic fungi in the early decay phase under the continental climate conditions of the southern Pannonian region.

title: Fungal community succession on Quercus robur and Carpinus betulus leaf litter: a comparative multiseason study
abstract: This study compared saprotrophic fungal succession on single-species litter of pedunculate oak (Quercus robur) and European hornbeam (Carpinus betulus) over three decomposition seasons in a mixed stand near Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia. Litterbags (n = 360) were retrieved at six time points. Fungal communities were characterised by direct plating on modified Hagem agar and by morphological identification of sporulating structures observed in situ. A total of 67 fungal taxa were recorded; species richness was higher on Q. robur litter (52 taxa) than on C. betulus litter (44 taxa). Succession proceeded from cellulolytic species such as Chaetomium spp. and Humicola spp. in the first four months toward basidiomycete white-rot taxa including Mycena spp. and Marasmius spp. after six months. Mass loss rates differed significantly between litter types (k = 0.48 yr⁻¹ for Q. robur versus k = 0.61 yr⁻¹ for C. betulus), attributable to the lower lignin-to-nitrogen ratio of hornbeam litter (23.1 versus 31.7). Redundancy analysis showed that litter lignin content and C:N ratio together explained 61% of community compositional variance.

title: Soil mesofauna and fungal biomass interact to regulate nitrogen release from hornbeam litter in a continental oak forest
abstract: The relative contributions of mesofauna and fungi to nitrogen mineralisation from C. betulus litter were investigated using a factorial litterbag experiment in which mesh size (1 mm versus 0.04 mm) was crossed with biocide treatment (cycloheximide versus untreated control) across 320 bags deployed for 15 months. Total nitrogen in litter residues and mineral nitrogen in underlying soil (0–5 cm) were measured at four time points. Biocide treatment reduced ergosterol concentrations by 76% and slowed net nitrogen release by 34% relative to untreated coarse-mesh bags. Mesofauna exclusion (fine mesh) reduced nitrogen release by 22% independent of biocide treatment. A significant interaction (p = 0.012) indicated that mesofaunal fragmentation amplified fungal nitrogen release rather than acting independently. These findings suggest that decomposer food-web structure moderates nitrogen cycling rates under the specific litter chemistry of hornbeam-dominated forests. Implications for forest floor nitrogen budgets in the Pannonian lowlands are discussed in relation to stand management practices.

title: Lignocellulolytic enzyme profiles of dominant saprotrophic fungi isolated from Quercus robur litter on Fruška Gora
abstract: Fifteen fungal isolates obtained from decomposing Q. robur litter at three moisture-contrasting microsites on Fruška Gora were screened for laccase, Mn-peroxidase, lignin peroxidase, CMCase, and xylanase activity under standardised liquid culture conditions. Isolates were identified by morphological characters supplemented by ITS1-5.8S-ITS2 rDNA sequencing. The basidiomycete Trametes hirsuta accounted for the highest laccase activity (mean 18.4 U ml⁻¹ on day 14) among white-rot taxa, whereas Phanerochaete chrysosporium-like isolates showed the highest Mn-peroxidase activity (11.2 U ml⁻¹). Soft-rot ascomycetes, including Chaetomium globosum and Humicola insolens isolates, exhibited high CMCase activity (up to 9.6 U ml⁻¹) but negligible laccase. Isolates from the driest microsite generally showed lower laccase and higher xylanase activities than their counterparts from moist microsites, suggesting physiological adaptation to substrate chemistry differences associated with drier conditions. These patterns are consistent with field enzyme activity data reported previously from the same sites and support the view that moisture regime shapes the functional diversity of the decomposer fungal community.

title: Long-term litter accumulation and fungal diversity in managed versus unmanaged oak-hornbeam stands in northern Serbia
abstract: Litter accumulation, mass loss rates, and macrofungal diversity were compared across six managed (periodically thinned) and six unmanaged oak-hornbeam stands in the Fruška Gora National Park over a five-year period (2007–2011). Forest floor organic horizon depth, litter bulk density, and total organic carbon were measured annually. Macrofungal fruiting bodies were inventoried on 20 × 20 m permanent plots in each stand each autumn. Managed stands had significantly thinner forest floors (mean 3.1 cm versus 5.4 cm in unmanaged stands, p < 0.001) and higher annual mass loss rates (k = 0.54 versus k = 0.41 yr⁻¹). Macrofungal species richness was 12% higher in unmanaged stands (mean 38 versus 34 species per stand per year), and community composition differed significantly (PERMANOVA, R² = 0.21, p = 0.002), with unmanaged stands supporting more late-succession saprotrophic basidiomycetes. These findings indicate that management history influences both the rate and pathway of organic matter turnover through its effects on microclimate and litter substrate availability.

title: Interannual variability in decomposition and saprotrophic fungal activity across a moisture gradient in Pannonian oak forests
abstract: Five years of litter decomposition data (2009–2013) were compiled from a network of eight permanent sites spanning a moisture gradient from xeric ridge-top to mesic valley-bottom positions in oak-hornbeam forests of Fruška Gora. At each site, annual mass loss, ergosterol concentration, and laccase activity were monitored using standardised litterbag and litter-core protocols. The Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) for the region showed substantial interannual variation, ranging from −3.1 (severe drought, 2012) to +1.8 (wet year, 2010). Mass loss rates varied from 0.29 yr⁻¹ at xeric sites in the drought year to 0.68 yr⁻¹ at mesic sites in the wet year. Ergosterol concentration correlated more strongly with site moisture class (r = 0.71) than with interannual PDSI variation (r = 0.48), suggesting that topographic position buffered year-to-year climatic fluctuations. A generalised linear mixed model explained 74% of total variance in annual mass loss using site moisture class, PDSI, and litter lignin content as predictors.

title: Saprotrophic fungal succession on woody debris of Quercus robur: a ten-year field study in Fruška Gora
abstract: Decomposition of naturally fallen Q. robur logs (diameter 15–35 cm, n = 24) was monitored from 2004 to 2014 on three replicate plots in the Fruška Gora National Park. Decay class, wood density, moisture content, and fruiting body inventories were recorded annually. Fungal communities shifted from initial colonisation by bark saprobes (Hypoxylon spp., Daldinia concentrica) in decay classes I–II to white-rot basidiomycetes (Ganoderma lipsiense, Bjerkandera adusta) dominating classes III–IV, and finally to predominantly brown-rot taxa (Coniophora puteana) in class V. Wood density declined from 0.64 g cm⁻³ in decay class I to 0.11 g cm⁻³ in class V. Annual mass loss rate was highest in decay class III (0.19 yr⁻¹) and lowest in class V (0.06 yr⁻¹). A significant negative relationship was found between annual precipitation during the preceding winter and the time to reach decay class III, suggesting that seasonal moisture availability accelerates the transition to the most active decay phase. Saprotrophic species richness peaked in decay classes III–IV with a mean of 11.4 species per log.
